en: Thereupon being bathed in blood that son of Vasava, fell senseless on the ground, in the conflict like to a blossoming Asoka growing on a hill and Sakra's banner struck down on the earth.

sn: ततः शरोणाभिहतो रामेण रणकर्कशः। पपात सहसा वाली निकृत्त इव पादपः॥
en: Thereupon Vāli, adept in warfare, wounded by Rāma's shaft, fell down to the ground like to a felled tree.

sn: स भूमौ न्यस्तसर्वाङ्गस्तप्तकाञ्चनभूषणः। अपतद् देवराजस्य मुक्तरश्मिरिव ध्वजः॥
en: Ornamented with burning gold, he stretched the whole length of his person on the ground like to the banner of the Lord of celestials, loosened and thrown (off the chariot).

sn: अस्मिन् निपतिते भूमौ हपृक्षाणां गणेश्वरे। नष्टचन्द्रमिव व्योम न व्यराजत मेदिनी॥
en: That lord of monkeys being levelled to the ground, his kingdom appeared like to the sky, shorn of the Moon.

sn: भूमौ निपतितस्यापि तस्य देहं महात्मनः। न श्रीर्जहाति न प्राणा न तेजो न पराक्रमः॥
en: Though struck down to the earth, neither vitality, effulgence nor prowess did renounce the body of that high-souled one.

sn: शक्रदत्ता वरा माला काञ्चनी रत्नभूषिता। दधार हरिमुख्यस्य प्राणास्तेजः श्रियं च सा॥
en: That excellent gold and jewel-crested garland conferred on him by Sakra maintained the vitality, effulgence and prowess of that lord of monkeys.

sn: स तया मालया वीरो हैमया हरियूथपः। संध्यानुगतपर्यन्तः पयोधर इवाभवत्॥
en: Being adorned with that golden garland, that heroic lord, of monkey-herds, appeared like to an evening cloud.

sn: तस्य माला च देहश्च मर्मघाती च यः शरः। त्रिधेव रचिता लक्ष्मीः पतितस्यापि शोभते॥
en: Though felled to the ground, his beauty appeared as if divided into three, namely, his garland, his body and the shaft piercing his heart.

sn: तदस्त्रं तस्य वीरस्य स्वर्गमार्गप्रभावनम्। रामबाणासनक्षिप्तमावहत् परमां गतिम्॥
en: The arrow thrown off Răma's bow pointing out to him the way to the celestial region, became an excellent means to that hero.

sn: तं तथा पतितं संख्ये गतार्चिषमिवानलम्। ययातिमिव पुण्यान्ते देवलोकादिह च्युतम्॥ आदित्यमिव कालेन युगान्ते भुवि पातितम्। महेन्द्रमिव दुर्धर्षमुपेन्द्रमिव दुःसहम्॥ महेन्द्रपुत्रं पतितं वालिनं हेममालिनम्। व्यूढोरस्कं महाबाहुं दीप्तास्यं हरिलोचनम् ॥ लक्ष्मणानुचरो रामो ददर्शोपससर्प च। तं तथा पतितं वीरं गतार्चिषमिवानलम्॥ बहुमान्य च तं वीरं वीक्षमाणं शनैरिव। उपयातौ महावीयौं भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ॥
en: Beholding the broad-chested and mightyarmed Vali, Mahendra's son, wearing a golden garland and having a flaming countenance and yellow eyes, thus struck down to the earth, resembling a flameless fire in the field of battle, like to Yayāti, slipped from the abode of the celestials on the wane of his piety, like to a tree falling down to the earth at the time of Dissolution, hard to repress as Mahendra himself, incapable to withstand like Upendra, Rāma, followed by Lakşmaņa, approached and beheld him. And paying respects to that hero falling on the earth like to a flameless fire and eyeing him again and again those two highly powerful brothers, Rāma and Laksmana neared him.

sn: तं दृष्ट्वा राघवं वाली लक्ष्मणं च महाबलम्। अब्रवीत् परुषं वाक्यं प्रश्रितं धर्मसंहितम्॥
en: And beholding that highly powerful Rāghava and Laksmana, Vāli addressed them with the following bold and pious words.

sn: स भूमावल्पतेजोऽसुर्निहतो नष्टचेतनः। अर्थसंहितया वाचा गर्वितं रणगर्वितम्॥
en: And thereupon Vāli, of mitigated prowess, waning vitality, motionless and stretched on the ground, spoke to Rāma, proud of warfare, saying these pregnant words.

sn: पराङ्मुखवधं कृत्वा कोऽत्र प्राप्तस्त्वया गुणः। यदहं युद्धसंरब्धस्त्वत्कृते निधनं गतः॥
en: What merit have you reaped by destroying me, who was not engaged in fight with you? I was exercised with ire, being engaged in conflict (with another person) and for you I have met with destruction.

sn: कुलीनः सत्त्वसम्पन्नस्तेजस्वी चरितव्रतः। रामः करुणवेदी च प्रजानां च हिते रतः॥ सानुक्रोशो महोत्साहः समयज्ञो दृढव्रतः। इत्येतत् सर्वभूतानि कथयन्ति यशो भुवि ॥
en: People speak highly of you, O Rāma, on this earth, describing you as coming of a high family, gifted with manliness and prowess, ever engaged in the welfare of your subjects, compassionate, energetic, of firm resolution and knowing time.

sn: दमः शमः क्षमा धर्मो धृतिः सत्यं पराक्रमः। पार्थिवाणां गुणा राजन् दण्डश्चाप्यपकारिषु॥
en: Punishment, control of passions, forgiveness, piety, firmness, truth, prowess and suppression of the wicked-these all are the royal virtues.

sn: तान् गुणान् सम्प्रधाहमग्र्यं चाभिजनं तव। तारया प्रतिषिद्धः सन् सुग्रीवेण समागतः॥
en: And knowing your high pedigree, and all these your accomplishments I approached Sugrīva with a hostile intention, albeit prevented by Tārā.

sn: न मामन्येन संरब्धं प्रमत्तं वेद्भुमर्हसि। इति मे बुद्धिरुत्पन्ना बभूवार्दशने तव॥
en: Before I saw you I had thought within myself:-'Forsooth Rāma shall not destroy me, engaged as I am with another person and hence not prepared to fight with him.'

sn: स त्वां विनिहतात्मानं धर्मध्वजमधार्मिकम्। जाने पापसमाचारं तृणैः कूपमिवावृतम्॥ सतां वेषधरं पापं प्रच्छन्नमिव पावकम्। नाहं त्वामभिजानामि धर्मच्छद्माभिसंवृतम्॥
en: I do now know you as one who has spoliated his soul through impious actions, feigning religion while in truth an irreligious person, resorting to all vicious deeds, like to a well crusted with grass, unrighteous while passing under the clock of honesty and religion like to a hidden fire.

sn: विषये वा पुरे वा ते यदा पापं करोम्यहम्। न च त्वामवजानेऽहं कस्मात्त्वं हंस्यकिल्विषम्॥ फलमूलाशनं नित्यं वानरं वनगोचरम्। मामिहाप्रतियुध्यन्तमन्येन च समागतम्॥ त्वं नराधिपतेः पुत्रः प्रतीतः प्रियदर्शनः। लिङ्गमप्यस्ति ते राजन् दृश्यते धर्मसंहितम्॥
en: I have not done you any wrong either in your kingdom or in your city. Nor have I passed by you. Why have you then destroyed me, who am a monkey ranging always in the woods, living on fruits and roots and who have come here to fight with another person? It appears that you are of a kingly father and of a graceful countenance. And, O king, there are marks of piety on your person.

sn: कः क्षत्रियकुले जातः श्रुतवान् नष्टसंशयः। धर्मलिङ्गप्रतिच्छन्नः क्रूरं कर्म समाचरेत् ॥
en: Who, born in the race of Kșatriyas, versed in religious lore, having his doubts removed and marks of piety on his person, perpetrates such an iniquitous deed?

sn: त्वं राघवकुले जातो धर्मवानिति विश्रुतः। अभव्यो भव्यरूपेण किमर्थं परिधावसे ॥
en: You are born in the family of Raghus and known all over the world as being pious. Being clothed in righteousness why did you commit such an unrighteous act?

sn: साम दानं क्षमा धर्मः सत्यं धृतिपराक्रमौ। पार्थिवानां गुणा राजन् दण्डश्चाप्यपकारिषु ।।२९ । ।
en: Chastisement, charity, forgiveness, piety, truthfulness firmness, prowess and the punishment of the iniquitous are the virtues of a king, O prince.

sn: वयं वनचरा राम मृगा मूलफलाशिनः। एषा प्रकृतिरस्माकं पुरुषस्त्वं नरेश्वर ॥
en: We are, O Rama, wild beasts ranging in the forest and living on roots and fruits-our nature is such—but you are a man, O king.

sn: भूमिर्हिरण्यं रूपं च निग्रहे कारणानि च । तत्र कस्ते वने लोभो मदीयेषु फलेषु वा ॥
en: Land, gold and silver are the causes of dissension. But who is there who is avaricious enough to get by our forest habitations and fruits?

sn: नयश्च विनयश्चोभौ निग्रहानुग्रहावपि। राजवृत्तिरसंकीर्णा न नृपाः कामवृत्तयः॥
en: The royal virtue consists in humbly and freely administering discipline, favour and punishment. Kings by no means, should follow their whims.

sn: त्वं तु कामप्रधानश्च कोपनश्चानवस्थितः। राजवृत्तेषु संकीर्णः शरासनपरायणः॥
en: But you are angry and unsteady by nature, capricious, perfectly narrow-minded in the discharge of your royal duties and did use your bow and shaft: (any where and every time).

sn: न तेऽस्त्यपचितिधर्मे नार्थे बुद्धिरवस्थिता। इन्द्रियैः कामवृत्तः सन् कृष्यसे मनुजेश्वर ॥
en: You have no attachment for virtue, no comprehension of right things and are always guided by your passions albeit you are a lord of men.

sn: हत्वा बाणेन काकुत्स्थ मामिहानपराधिनम्। किं वक्ष्यसि सतां मद्ये कर्म कृत्वा जुगुप्सितम्॥
en: O Kākutstha, destroying me sinless, with your shaft and perpetrating such a disgraceful act, how shall you relate it to the pious.

sn: राजहा ब्रह्महा गोघ्नश्चोरः प्राणिवधे रतः। नास्तिकः परिवेत्ता च सर्वे निरयगामिनः॥
en: Those, who commit treason, destroy Brahmins and kine, who are thieves and always engaged in the destruction of animals, and who are atheists and marry before their elder brothers are married, do all go to hell.

sn: सूचकश्च कदर्यश्च मित्रघ्नो गुरुतल्पगः। लोकं पापात्मनामेते गच्छन्ते नात्र संशयः॥
en: The villainous, the avaricious, those who kill their friends and elope with their preceptor's wives, do always visit the land of the vicious.

sn: अधार्यं चर्म मे सद्भी रोमाण्यस्ति च वर्जितम्। अभक्ष्याणि च मांसानि त्वद्विधैर्धर्मचारिभिः॥
en: And there is not the least doubt about it. My skin is not worthy of your touch and my bones and hairs should always be avoided by the virtuous. And my flesh is not worthy of being eaten by persons of your piety.

sn: पञ्च पञ्चनखा भक्ष्या ब्रह्मक्षत्रेण राघव। शल्यकः श्वाविधो गोधा शशः कूर्मश्च पञ्चमः॥
en: A hedge-hog a porcupine, an iguana, a hare and a tortoise these five animals only, having five toes, are worthy of being eaten by the Ks atryas and Brahmins, O Rāghava.

sn: चर्म चास्थि च मे राम न स्पृश्यन्ति मनीषिणः। अभक्ष्याणि च मांसानि सोऽहं पञ्चनखो हतः॥
en: The wise, O Rāma, do not touch my skin and bones and my flesh is not worthy of being taken-I am that (monkey) having five toes who have been killed by you.

sn: तारया वाक्यमुक्तोऽहं सत्यं सर्वज्ञया हितम्। तदतिक्रम्य मोहेन कालस्य वशमागतः॥
en: Alas! disregarding the well meaning and truthful words of Tārā, I have placed myself under the control of Kāla (Death).

sn: त्वया नाथेन काकुत्स्थ न सनाथा वसुंधरा। प्रमदा शीलसम्पूर्णा पत्येव च विधर्मणा ।॥
en: O Kākutstha, the Earth has got you as her husband like to a good natured damsel being wedded to a husband who has forsaken his own religion.

sn: शठो नैकृतिकः क्षुद्रो मिथ्याप्रश्रितमानसः। कथं दशरथेन त्वं जातः पापो महात्मना ॥
en: How are you, who are wicked, narrowminded, a liar and ever intent upon bringing about others' misfortune, born of the loins of the high-souled Dasaratha?

sn: छिन्नचारित्र्यकक्ष्येण सतां धर्मातिवर्तिना। त्यक्तधर्माङ्कुशेनाहं निहतो रामहस्तिना॥
en: I have been killed by an elephant-Rāma, disregarding the virtue of the pious, breaking the chord of character, and neglecting the goad of religion.

sn: अशुभं चाप्ययुक्तं च सतां चैव विगर्हितम्। वक्ष्यसे चेदृशं कृत्वा सद्भिः सह समागतः॥
en: Perpetrating this inauspicious, and improper act, blamed of the worthy what shall you speak to the pious when you shall return in their company?

sn: उदासीनेषु योऽस्मासु विक्रमोऽयं प्रकाशितः। अपकारिषु ते राम नैवं पश्यामि विक्रमम्॥
en: The prowess, you had displayed towards me, careless, O Rāma you did never employ for the suppression of the iniquitous.

sn: दृश्यमानस्तु युध्येथा मया युधि नृपात्मज। अद्य वैवस्वतं देवं पश्येस्त्वं निहतो मया॥
en: O son of a king, hadst you fought with me openly you wouldst have, forsooth, seen the abode of Death being killed by me.

sn: त्वयादृश्येन तु रणे निहतोऽहं दुरासदः। प्रसुप्तः पन्नगेनेव नरः पापवशं गतः॥
en: O Rāma, like to a serpent destroying persons asleep, you, that are under the control of vice, have killed me, who am hard to repress, keeping yourself out of my sight in the battle.

sn: सुग्रीवप्रियकामेन यदहं निहतस्त्वया। मामेव यदि पूर्वं त्वमेतदर्थमचोदयः। मैथिलीमहमेकाह्वा तव चानीतवान्भवः ॥ राक्षसं च दुरात्मानं तव भार्यापहारिणम्। कण्ठे बद्ध्वा प्रदद्यां तेऽनिहतं रावणं रणे।।५०
en: I have been killed by you, desirous of encompassing Sugrīva's well being. Hadst you apprized me of your object before, I would have got you your Maithili in the course of a day, and brought, by the neck, that vicious-souled Raks asa-Rāvaņa, the ravisher of your spouse with out putting an end to his life in the battle.

sn: न्यस्ता सागरतोये वा पाताले वापि मैथिलीम्। आनयेयं तवादेशाच्छेतामश्वतरीमिव॥
en: Whether in the deep ocean or in the region under the earth, I shall bring your Maithili like to an Asyatar* Here is an allusion. A prince of Daityas, named Hayagriva, stole the Vedas at the end of Kalpa; in the recovery of them he was slain by Vişnu after his descent as Matshya.

sn: युक्तं यत्प्राप्नुयाद् राज्यं सुग्रीवः स्वर्गते मयि। अयुक्तं यदधर्मेण त्वयाऽहं निहतो रणे॥
en: It is perfectly proper that Sugrīva shall inherit my kingdom on my ascension to heaven. And it is equally improper that I have been viciously killed by you in the battle.

sn: काममेवंविधो लोकः कालेन विनियुज्यते। क्षमं चेद्भवता प्राप्तमुत्तरं साधु चिन्त्यताम्॥
en: Every one in time meets with death and hence there is nothing to be sorry for me. But do you think of a proper reply you shall give to the people (when asked about the cause of my destruction).

sn: इत्येवमुक्त्वा परिशुष्कवक्त्रः शराभिघाताद् व्यथितो महात्मा। समीक्ष्य रामं रविसंनिकाशं तूष्णीं बभौ वानरराजसूनुः॥
en: Having said this, that high-souled Son of monkey-chief, greatly distressed being wounded by (Rāma's) shaft and having his countenance dried up, became silent, fixing his look upon Rāma, resembling the sun.

sn: इत्युक्तः प्रश्रितं वाक्यं धर्मार्थसहितं हितम्। परुषं वालिना रामो निहतेन विचेतसा॥ तं निष्प्रभमिवादित्यं मुक्ततोयमिवाम्बुदम्। उक्तवाक्यं हरिश्रेष्ठमुपशान्तमिवानलम्॥ धर्मार्थगुणसम्पन्नं हरीश्वरमनुत्तमम् । अधिक्षिप्तस्तदा रामः पश्चाद् वालिनमब्रवीत्॥
en: And thus Rāma was addressed by Vāli, wounded and senseless, with those modest, pious and auspicious words. And being thus reproached he spoke to that excellent lord of monkeys, gifted with virtue and other accomplishments, resembling the Sun shorn of its lustre, a cloud which has already discharged its waters and fire extinguished.

sn: धर्ममर्थं च कामं च समयं चापि लौकिकम्। अविज्ञाय कथं बाल्यान्मामिहाद्य विगर्हसे॥
en: Not cognizant of virtue, knowledge, passion and custom, why did you blame me like a child?

sn: अपृष्ट्वा बुद्धिसम्पन्नान् वृद्धानाचार्यसम्मतान्। सौम्य वानरचापल्यात् त्वं मां वक्तुमिहेच्छसि ॥
en: Why did you purpose to address me thus out of fickleness, consequent upon your monkeyhood not asking your wise elders recognized by the preceptors?

sn: इक्ष्वाकूणामियं भूमिः सशैलबनकानना। मृगपक्षिमनुष्याणां निग्रहानुग्रहेष्वपि॥
en: This land, abounding in hills and woods, belongs to the lkşwakus. Along with it was conferred on them the power of administering favour and chastisement to beasts, birds and human beings.

sn: तां पालयति धर्मात्मा भरतः सत्यवानृजुः। धर्मकामार्थतत्त्वज्ञो निग्रहानुग्रहे रतः॥
en: The upright, virtuous and truthful king Bharata, cognizant of virtue, knowledge and passion and ever engaged in administering favour and punisl.ment, governs this kingdom.

sn: नयश्च विनयश्चोभौ यस्मिन् सत्यं च सुस्थितम्। विक्रमश्च यथा दृष्टः स राजा देशकालवित्॥
en: That king is said to be cognizant of time and place; in him dwelleth modesty, truthfulness, prowess and a love for discipline.

sn: तस्य धर्मकृतादेशा वयमन्ये च पार्थिवाः। चरामो वसुधां कृत्स्नां धर्मसंतानमिच्छवः॥
en: Ourselves and other kings, being commanded by him to practise piety, have been journeying in this wide world desirous of multiplying virtue.

sn: तस्मिन् नृपतिशार्दूले भरते धर्मवत्सले। पालयत्यखिलां पृथ्वी कश्चरेद् धर्मविप्रियम्॥
en: That foremost of monarchs, Bharatalover of virtue, governing this entire earth, who dares perpetrate an iniquity.?

sn: ते वयं मार्गविभ्रष्ट स्वधर्मे परमे स्थिताः। भरताज्ञा पुरस्कृत्य चिन्तयामो यथाविधि ॥
en: Stationed in the excellent virtue of our own and placing Bharata's commandments on our heads, we shall consider how we shall punish them who go astray (from the path of virtue).

sn: त्वं तु संक्लिष्टधर्मश्च कर्मणा च विगर्हितः। कामतन्त्रप्रधानश्च न स्थितो राजवर्त्मनि॥
en: You have oppressed virtue and perpetrated a gross iniquity. You have placed yourself under the control of your passions and deviated from the track of royal duties.

sn: ज्येष्ठो भ्राता पिता वापि यश्च विद्यां प्रयच्छति। त्यस्ते पितरो ज्ञेया धर्मे च पथि वर्तिनः॥
en: The elder brother, father, and the instructor—these three should always be regarded in the light of a father if they tread the paths of virtue and morality,

sn: यवीयानात्मनः पुत्रः शिष्यश्चापि गुणोदितः। पुत्रवत्ते त्रयश्चिन्त्या धर्मश्चैवात्र कारणम्॥
en: A younger brother, a son and an accomplished follower should always be regarded as sons. And virtue is always at the bottom of all such considerations.

sn: सूक्ष्मः परमविज्ञेयः सतां धर्मः प्लवङ्गम। हृदिस्थः सर्वभूतानामात्मा वेद शुभाशुभम्॥
en: O monkey, the religion of the good is indeed very subtle and can comprehend great things the immortal soul can understand what is good or bad.

sn: चपलश्चपलैः सार्धं वानरैरकृतात्मभिः। जात्यन्ध इव जात्यन्धैर्मन्त्रयन् प्रेक्षसे नु किम्॥
en: Fickle as you are, how canst you comprehend what is proper, consulting with your monkey companions who are equally stupid and lighthearted, like to one, born blind, leading with another such?

sn: अहं तु व्यक्ततामस्य वचनस्य ब्रवीमि ते। नहि मां केवलं रोषात् त्वं विगर्हितुमर्हसि ॥
en: I do fairly speak to you that it is not anger only that has led me to bring about your destruction.

sn: तदेतत् कारणं पश्य यदर्थं त्वं मया हतः। भ्रातुर्वर्तसि भार्यायां त्यक्त्वा धर्म सनातनम्॥
en: Do you consider why I have killed you-you had ravished your brother's wife renouncing that ever-existing virtue.

sn: अस्य त्वं धरमाणस्य सुग्रीवस्य महात्मनः। रुमायां वर्तसे कामात् स्नुषायां पापकर्मकृत्॥
en: You, the perpetrator of many evil deeds, have got by Rumā, the wife of your brother-the high-souled Sugrīva.

sn: तद् व्यतीतस्य ते धर्मात् कामवृत्तस्य वानर। भ्रातृभाभिमर्शेऽस्मिन् दण्डोऽयं प्रतिपादितः॥
en: O monkey, you had thus violated the path of virtue. And thus I have punished you who have ravished your elder brother's spouse.

sn: नहि लोकविरुद्धस्य लोकवृत्तादपेयुषः। दण्डादन्यत्र पश्यामि निग्रहं हरियूथप॥
en: o you, the leader of monkey-herds-I find no other alternative than to punish him who act against humanity and violates the sacred sanctions of custom.

sn: न च ते मर्षये पापं क्षत्रियोऽहं कुलोद्गतः। औरसीं भगिनीं वापि भार्या वाप्यनुजस्य यः॥ प्रचरेत नरः कामात्तस्य दण्डो वधः स्मृतः।
en: I am a Ksatrya coming of a high pedigree. I cannot put up with your immoral conduct. Šāstras sanction the destruction of one who under the influence of passion ravishes his own daughter, sister and younger brother's wife.

sn: भरतस्तु महीपालो वयं त्वादेशवर्तिनः॥ त्वं च धर्मादतिक्रान्तः कथं शक्यमुपेक्षितुम्।
en: This is Bharata's commandment-the lord of earth, and we have been satisfying his orders. You have disregarded virtue.

sn: गुरुधर्मव्यतिक्रान्तं प्राज्ञो धर्मेण पालयन्।॥ भरतः कामयुक्तानां निग्रहे पर्यवस्थितः। वयं तु भरतादेशावधिं कृत्वा हरीश्वर। त्वद्विधान् भिन्नमर्यादान् निग्रहीतुं व्यवस्थिताः॥
en: A wise man, living in virtue, cannot let go one who has passed by the sanctions of morality. Bharata has sanctioned the destruction of the amorous; and we, O lord of monkeys, following his orders, thought proper, to encompass the destruction of one like you who has spoliated virtue and morality.

sn: सुग्रीवेण च मे सख्यं लक्ष्मणेन यथा तथा। दारराज्यनिमित्तं च निःश्रेयसकरः स मे॥ प्रतिज्ञा च मया दत्ता तदा वानरसंनिधौ। प्रतिज्ञा च कथं शक्या मद्विधेनानवेक्षितुम् ॥
en: Like to Laksmana, I have contracted friendship with Sugrīva. And with a view to regain his wife and kingdom, he resolved to engage in my well-being. I too also promised the same before the monkeys. And how can a man of my position neglect to make good his promise?

sn: तदेभिः कारणैः सर्वैर्महद्भिर्धर्मसंश्रितैः । शासनं तव यद् युक्तं तद् भवाननुमन्यताम्॥
en: For these causes of very great moment, favoured by virtue, I have adininistered to you this condign punishment. Do you now approve it.

sn: सर्वथा धर्म इत्येव द्रष्टव्यस्तव निग्रहः। वयस्थस्योपकर्तव्यं धर्ममेवानुपश्यता ॥
en: Your discomfiture is quite of a piece with the sanctions of morality-and to assist friends in one of the codes of religion.

sn: शक्यं त्वयापि तत्कार्यं धर्ममेवानुवर्तता। श्रूयते मनुना गीतौ श्लोकौ चारित्रवत्सलौ। गृहीतौ धर्मकुशलैस्तथा तच्चरितं मया॥
en: Hear, Manu has composed a couple of couplets tending to the purification of character and highly prized by the virtuous as well as myself.

sn: राजभिभृतदण्डाश्च कृत्वा पापानि मानवाः। निर्मलाः स्वर्गमायान्ति सन्तः सुकृतिनो यथा॥ शासनाद् वापि मोक्षाद् वा स्तेनः पापात् प्रमुच्यते। राजा त्वशासन् पापस्य तदवाप्नोति किल्विषम्॥
en: Those who, perpetrating iniquity, bear with fortitude the punishment, inflicted by their sovereign get at the abode of the celestials being purified like to the pious. People are freed from their sins, when they confessing their crimes, are either punished or forgiven. But the monarch who does not punish the perpetrator of an evil deed, is visited by a mighty sin.

sn: आर्येण मम मान्धात्रा व्यसनं घोरमीप्सितम्। श्रमणेन कृते पापे यथा पापं कृतं त्वया॥
en: Formerly an iniquity, like one perpetrated by you, was committed by a devotee who was punished severely by my forefather Māndhäta.

sn: अन्यैरपि कृतं पापं प्रमत्तैर्वसुधाधिपैः। प्रायश्चित्तं च कुर्वन्ति तेन तच्छाम्यते रजः॥
en: And other lords of earth punish in the same way the authors of misdeeds. What more, the perpetrators of crime, themselves undergo penances and are thus released from their sins.

sn: तदलं परितापेन धर्मतः परिकल्पितः। वधो वानरशार्दूल न वयं स्ववशे स्थिताः॥
en: Therefore do not repent any more, O best of monkeys. The punishment, I have inflicted on you, is in consonance with the sanctions of morality. We are not our own masters.

sn: श्रृणु चाप्यपरं भूयः कारणं हरिपुंगव। तच्छ्रुत्वा हि महद् वीर न मन्यु कर्तुमर्हसि ॥
en: Hearken, O best of monkeys, there is another argument (for your destruction); and hearing which, O great hero, it behoveth you to renounce your ire.

sn: न मे तत्र मनस्तापो न मन्युहरिपुंगव। बागुराभिश्च पाशैश्च कुटैश्च विविधैर्नराः॥ प्रतिच्छन्नाश्च दृश्याश्च गृह्णन्ति सुवहन मृगान्। प्रधावितान् वा वित्रस्तान् विस्त्रब्दानतिविष्टितान्॥
en: Many persons living on flesh, either lying in ambush, or openly catch and pierce by means of net, noose and trap, many a deer, terrified and trusted, taking to their heels or quarrelling with their companions, careful or careless. They are not to blame in this and I do not cherish, O best of monkeys, any mortification or ire for this.

sn: प्रमत्तानप्रमत्तान् वा नरा मांसाशिनो भृशम्। विध्यन्ति विमुखांश्चापि न च दोषोऽत्र विद्यते॥
en: And even many royal ascetics, versed in religious lore, go a-hunting; and hence you had been killed by me with a shaft, O monkey, in the conflict.

sn: यान्ति राजर्षयश्चात्र मृगयां धर्मकोविदाः। तस्मात् त्वं निहतो युद्धे मया वाणेन वानर । अयुध्यन् प्रतियुध्यन् वा यस्माच्छाखामृगोह्यसि॥ दुर्लभस्य च धर्मस्य जीवितस्य शुभस्य च। राजानो वानरश्रेष्ठ प्रदातारो न संशयः॥ तान् न हिंस्यान चाक्रोशेनाक्षिपेनाप्रियं वदेत्। देवा मानुषरूपेण चरन्त्येते महीतले।॥
en: And I am justified in killing you, whether you did fight or not since you are a monkey. There is no doubt, O best monkeys, that the monarchs confer life and piety auspicious and hard to attain. It does not therefore behove any one to injure them, to blame them and to use improper words by them-since they are the celestials ranging on this earth under the semblance of man.

sn: त्वं तु धर्ममविज्ञाय केवलं रोषमास्थितः। विदूषयसि मां धर्मे पितृपैतामहे स्थितम्॥
en: Not knowing virtue and growing angry why did you blame me who am following the religion of my forefathers?

sn: एवमुक्तस्तु रामेण वाली प्रव्यथितो भृशम्। न दोषं राघवे दध्यौ धर्मेऽधिगतनिश्चयः॥
en: Being thus accosted by Rāma, Vāli, greatly mortified and informed of the principle of religion, observed no delinquency in Rāghava.

sn: प्रत्युवाच ततो रामं प्राञ्जलिर्वानरेश्वरः। यत् त्वमात्थ नरश्रेष्ठ तत् तथैव न संशयः॥
en: Thereupon that lord of monkeys spoke to Răma, with folded hands, saying:-There is not the least doubt, О best of men, in all that you had said.

sn: प्रतिवक्तुं प्रकृष्टे हि नापकृष्टस्तु शक्नुयात्। यदयुक्तं मया पूर्वं प्रमादाद् वाक्यमप्रियम् ॥ तत्रापि खलु मां दोषं कर्तुं नार्हसि राघव। त्वं हि दृष्टार्थतत्वज्ञः प्रजानां च हिते रतः। कार्यकारणसिद्धौ च प्रसन्ना बुद्धिरव्यया॥
en: An inferior person can by no means address his superior improperly. It does not behove you, O Rāghava, therefore to blame me for those unpleasant words which I used towards you, out of foolishness. You have acquired a practical mastery over the principles of religion and are ever engaged in the welfare of your subjects. Your eternal power of ascertaining the crime and meeting its condign punishment is perfectly clear.

sn: मामप्यवगतं धर्माद् व्यतिक्रान्तपुरस्कृतम्। धर्मसंहितया वाचा धर्मज्ञ परिपालय॥
en: Do you know me as the foremost of sinners and one who has deviated from the track of imorality. Do you conduct me, with pious words, to a better land.

sn: वाष्पसंरुद्धकण्ठस्तु वाली सार्तरवः शनैः। उवाच रामं सम्प्रेक्ष्य पङ्कलग्न इव द्विपः॥
en: Vāli, having his throat choked with vapour, addressed again and again, Rāma, with piteous accents, saying.

sn: न चात्मानमहं शोचे न तारां नापि बान्धवान्। यथा पुत्रं गुणज्येष्ठमङ्गदं कनकाङ्गदम्॥
en: I do not mourn so much for me, Tāră, or other friends as for my son Angada, eldest and wearing a golden Angada* *A bracelet worn on the upper arm.

sn: स ममादर्शनाद् दीनो बाल्यात् प्रभृति लालितः। तटाक इव पीताम्बुरुपशोषं गमिष्यति ॥
en: Brought up by me from his very infancy, he shall by my separation, wear away like to a pond having its liquid contents drunk up by an elephant.

sn: बालश्चाकृतबुद्धिश्च एकपुत्रश्च मे प्रियः। तारेयो राम भवता रक्षणीयो महाबलः॥
en: He is my only son, dear and born of Tārā. A mere child and of unripe understanding as he is, that one of mighty strength should always be protected by you, O Rāma.

sn: सुग्रीवे चाङ्गदे चैव विधत्स्व मतिमुत्तमाम्। त्वं हि गोप्ता च शास्ता च कार्याकार्यविधौ स्थितः।।।
en: Do you regard favourable Sugrīva and Angada. You are their protector, and chastiser punishing them for their sins.

sn: या ते नरपते वृत्तिभरते लक्ष्मणे च या। सुग्रीवे चाङ्गदे राजस्तां चिन्तयितुमर्हसि ॥
en: O king, O lord of men, it behoveth you to regard Sugrīva and Angada in the same light in which you regardest Bharata and Laksmana.

sn: मद्दोषकृतदोषां तां यथा तारां तपस्विनीम्। सुग्रीवो नावमन्येत तथावस्थातुमर्हसि॥
en: It behoveth you to so arrange as Sugrīva may not disregard that chaste Tārā who is blameable for my folly only.

sn: त्वया हनुगृहीतेन शक्यं राज्यमुपासितुम्। त्वद्वशे वर्तमानेन तव चित्तानुवर्तिना ५६।। शक्यं दिवं चार्जयितुं वसुधां चापि शासितुम्।
en: He, who is favoured by you, abideth by yourcommandments and acteth after your heart, can acquire kingdom, attain to heaven, and govern the earth.

sn: त्वत्तोऽहं वधमाकासन् वार्यमाणोऽपि तारया॥ सुग्रीवेण सह भ्रात्रा द्वन्द्वयुद्धमुपागतः।
en: Desiring to have my destruction brought about by you, I entered into conflict with my brother Sugrīva, albeit prevented by Târā.

sn: इत्युक्त्वा वानरो रामं विरराम हरीश्वरः॥ न तमाश्वासयद् रामो वालिनं व्यक्तदर्शनम्। साधुसम्मतया वाचा धर्मतत्त्वार्थयुक्तया ॥ न वयं भवता चिन्त्या नाप्यात्मा हरिसत्तम। वयं भवद्विशेषेण धर्मतः कृतनिश्चयाः॥
en: Having addressed Rāma thus the lord of monkeys stopped. Thereupon Rāma consoled Vāli, of clear understanding with the following moral words, acceptable to the Saints. O best of monkeys, do you not consider ourselves as well as yourself blameable. We are more conversant, than you, with the principles of religion.

sn: दण्ड्ये यः पातयेद् दण्डं दण्ड्यो यश्चापि दण्ड्यते। कार्यकारणसिद्धार्थावुभौ तौ नावसीदतः॥ तद् भवान् दण्डसंयोगादस्माद् विगतकल्मषः। गतः स्वां प्रकृतिं धम्यां दण्डदिष्टेन वर्त्मना॥
en: They never lose their virtue being proficient in the mode of ascerting crime and punishing it one administering punishment to the criminal and the criminal receiving it. And therefore receiving punishment (from me) you had been released from your sins and acquired a knowledge of religion.

sn: त्यज शोकं च मोहं च भयं च हृदये स्थितम्। त्वया विधानं हर्यग्र्य न शक्यमतिवर्तितुम्॥
en: Do you therefore renounce your grief, your illusion and the fear that is lurking in your heart. It is impossible for you, O foremost of monkeys, to withstand the course of dispensation.

sn: यथा त्वय्यङ्गदो नित्यं वर्तते वानरेश्वरः। तथा वर्तेत सुग्रीवे मयि चापि न संशयः॥
en: There is not the least doubt, lord of monkeys, that Angada shall be brought up by me and Sugriva in the same way as he was by you.

sn: स तस्य वाक्यं मधुरं महात्मनः। समाहितं धर्मपथानुवर्तितम्। निशम्य रामस्य रणावमर्दिनो वचः सुयुक्तं निजगाद वानरः॥
en: Hearing these sweet, collected and pious words of the high-souled Rāma,-the repressor of the enemies in a battle,-the monkey again addressed him with the following pregnant words.

sn: शराभितप्तेन विचेतसा मया प्रभाषितस्त्वं यदजानता विभो। इदं महेन्द्रपमभीमविक्रम प्रसादितस्त्वं क्षम मे हरीश्वर॥
en: O lord, O you having Mahendra's prowess, I do propitiate you for my having insulted you with improper words, senseless as I was being wounded by shafts. Do you forgive me, O lord of monkeys.

sn: स वानरमहाराजः शयानः शरपीडितः। प्रत्युक्तो हेतुमद्वाक्यैर्नोत्तरं प्रतिपद्यत ॥
en: Being thus accosted with reasonable words, that lord, of monkeys, lying on the ground and wounded with shafts, gave no reply.

sn: अश्मभिः परिभिन्नाङ्गः पादपैराहतो भृशम्। रामबाणेन चाक्रान्तो जीवितान्ते मुमोह सः॥
en: Having his limbs dissevered by stones, being struck with trees and wounded by Rama's shaft, he became senseless at the approach of death.

sn: तं भार्या बाणमोक्षेण रामदत्तेन संयुगे। हतं प्लवगशार्दूलं तारा शुश्राव वालिनम्॥
en: His spouse Tārā heard that Váli, the foremost of monkeys, had been killed in the conflict by Rāma's shaft.

sn: सा सपुत्रापियं श्रुत्वा वधं भर्तुः सुदारुणम्। निष्पपात भृशं तस्मादुद्विग्ना गिरिकन्दरात्॥
en: Hearing the heart-rending news of her husband's demise, she, big with a child, issued out of the mountain cave with a troubled heart.

sn: ये त्वङ्गदपरीवारा वानरा हि महाबलाः। ते सकार्मुकमालोक्य रामं त्रस्ताः प्रदुद्रुवुः॥
en: And beholding Rāma with a bow in his hand, the mighty monkeys, followers of Angada, fled away, terrified.

sn: सा ददर्श ततस्त्रस्तान् हरीनापततो द्रुतम्। यूथादिव परिभ्रष्टान् मृगान् निहतयूथपान्॥
en: Thereupon Tārā observed those monkeys flying away terrified like to deer alienated from their herd, having lost their king.

sn: तानुवाच समासाद्य दुःखितान् दुःखिता सती। रामवित्रासितान् सर्वाननुबद्धानिवेषुभिः॥
en: The chaste lady, racked with sorrow, spoke to those monkeys, afraid of Rāma, wounded with shafts and exercised with grief, saying,

sn: वानरा राजसिंहस्य यस्य यूयं पुरःसराः। तं विहाय सुवित्रस्ताः कस्माद् द्रवत दुर्गताः॥
en: O monkeys, why are you flying away, terrified and distressed, leaving behind that foremost of kings before whom you were used to fight?

sn: राज्यहेतोः स चेद् भ्राता भ्रात्राक्रूरेण पातितः। रामेण प्रसृतैर्दूरान्मार्गणैर्दूरपातिभिः॥
en: Hath Vāli been killed by Rāma, waiting at a distance with fleet and distant-coursing shafts, being requested by Sugrīva for kingdom?

sn: कपिपत्न्या वचः श्रुत्वा कपयः कामरूपिणः। प्राप्तकालमविश्लिष्टमूचुर्वचनमङ्गनाम्॥
en: Hearing the words of that wife of the monkey, they, wearing shapes at will, addressed that damsel with words, worthy of being said on that occasion,

sn: जीवपुत्रे निवर्तस्व पुत्र रक्षस्व चाङ्गदम्। अन्तको रामरूपेण हत्वा नयति वालिनम्॥
en: O you, having your son alive, do you go back and bring up your son Angada. Death himself, under Rāma's semblance, has snatched away Vāli.

sn: क्षिप्रान् वृक्षान् समाविध्य विपुलाश्च तथा शिला:। वाली वज्रसमैर्बाणैर्वज्रेणेव निपातितः॥
en: He was killed by (Rāma's) shafts, resembling thunderbolts as if clapped by thunder itself, having bored trees and big stones (hurled by Vali).

sn: अभिभूतमिदं सर्वं विद्रुतं वानरं बलम्। अस्मिन् प्लवगशार्दूले हते शक्रसमप्रभे॥
en: That king of monkeys, having Sakra's prowess, being made away with this host of monkeys have been taking to their heels being overwhelmed with consternation.

sn: रक्ष्यतां नगरी शूरैरङ्गदश्चाभिषिच्यताम्। पदस्थं वालिनः पुत्रं भजिष्यन्ति प्लवङ्गमाः॥
en: Let the heroes defend the city and install Angada on the throne. And on his being installed the monkeys shall serve Vāli's son.

sn: अथवा रुचितं स्थानमिह ते रुचिरानने। आविशन्ति च दुर्गाणि क्षिप्रमद्यैव वानराः॥ अभार्याः सहभार्याश्च सन्त्यत्र वनचारिणः। लुब्धेभ्यो विप्रलब्धेभ्यस्तेभ्यो नः सुमहद्भयम्॥
en: O you having a fine countenance, the monkeys shall enter this stronghold, although it is a favourite place with you. Herein dwell many forest-rangers, wifeless and having wives. And we are really afraid of them, avaricious, and formerly deprived of their wealth by us.

sn: अल्पान्तरगतानां तु श्रुत्वा वचनमङ्गना। आत्मनः प्रतिरूपं सा बभाषे चारुहासिनी॥
en: Hearing those words of the monkeys, lying at a little distance, that lady, smiling sweet, spoke to them, words worthy of herself.

sn: पुत्रेण मम किं कार्य राज्येनापि किमात्मना। कपिसिंहे महाभागे तस्मिन् भर्तरि नश्यति ॥
en: That great lord of monkeys, my husband, being dead, what shall I do with my son, my kingdom and myself?

sn: पादमूलं गमिष्यामि तस्यैवाहं महात्मनः। योऽसौ रामप्रयुक्तेन शरेण विनिपातितः॥
en: I shall place myself at the feet of that highsouled one, who has been killed by Rama's shaft.

sn: एवमुक्त्वा प्रदुद्राव रुदती शोकमूर्छिता। शिरश्चोरश्च बाहुभ्यां दुःखेन समभिघ्नती॥
en: Having said this, (Tara) proceeded, overwhelmed with grief, weeping and striking her head with her hands.

sn: सा व्रजन्ती ददर्शाथ पतिं निपतितं भुवि। हन्तारं दानवेन्द्राणां समरेष्वनिवर्तिनाम् ॥ क्षेप्तारं पर्वतेन्द्राणां वज्राणामिव वासवम्। महावातसमाविष्टं महामेघौघनि:स्वनम् ॥ शक्रतुल्यपराक्रान्तं वृष्ट्वेवोपरतं धनम्। नर्दन्तं नर्दतां भीमं शूरं शूरेण पातितम्। शार्दूलेनामिषस्यार्थे मृगराजमिवाहतम्॥ अर्चितं सर्वलोकस्य सपताकं सवेदिकम्। नागहेतोः सुपर्णेन चैत्यमुन्मथितं यथा ॥
en: While proceeding, she espied her husband lying on the ground like to the destroyer of the lords of monkeys who have never been discomfited in a battle field, hurling mountains like to Väsava hurling thunderbolts; emitting a roar like to a big cloud assisted by a mighty wind; resembling Sakra in prowess and like to a cloud accompanied by rain; the repressor of repressor; a mighty hero discomfited by an equally powerful one; like to a lion killed by a tiger for flesh; worshipped of all men; like to a caitya*, adorned with pennons and altars, scattered and broken by Garuda with a view to kill serpents. *A pile of stones.

sn: अवष्टभ्यावतिष्ठन्तं ददर्श धनुरूर्जितम्। रामं रामानुजं चैव भर्तुश्चैव तथानुजम्॥
en: She espied Rāma reclining his person on a mighty bow, his younger brother and her husband's younger brother.

sn: तानतीत्य समासाद्य भर्तारं निहतं रणे। समीक्ष्य व्यथिता भूमौ सम्भ्रान्ता निपपात ह॥
en: Passing them by and getting at her husband and beholding him killed in battle, she, losing her sense, fell down to the ground.

sn: सुप्तेव पुनरुत्थाय आर्यपुत्रेति वादिनी। रुरोद सा पतिं दृष्ट्वा संवीतं मृत्युदामभिः॥
en: And thereupon rising again like one asleep, she, beholding her husband engarlanded by death, cried aloud, exclaiming O son of worshipful sire.

sn: तामवेक्ष्य तु सुग्रीवः क्रोशन्ती कुररीमिव । विषादमगमत् कष्टं दृष्ट्वा चाङ्गदमागतम्॥
en: And beholding Tārā like to a she-elephant and Angada, bewailing in this wise, Sugrīva attained to an excess of grief.

sn: रामचापविसृष्टेन शरेणान्तकरेण तम्। दृष्ट्वा विनिहतं भूमौ तारा ताराधिपानना॥ सा समासाद्य भर्तारं पर्यष्वजत भामिनी। इषुणाभिहतं दृष्ट्वा वालिनं कुञ्जरोपमम्॥ वानरं पर्वतेन्द्राभं शोकसंतप्तमानसा। तारा तरुमिवोन्मूलं पर्यदेवयतातुरा॥
en: Beholding her husband lying dead on the ground with the life-destroying shafts of Rama, Tārā, having a moon-like countenance, approaching, embraced him. And seeing him slain with shafts like to an elephant, resembling a lord mountains and an uprooted tree, Tārā, racked with grief began to bewail.

sn: रणे दारुणविक्रान्त प्रवीर प्लवतां वर। किमिदानों पुरोभागामद्य त्वं नाभिभाषसे॥
en: O hero, O foremost of monkeys, O powerful one, O you terrible in warfare, why did you not welcome me to-day who am guilty of some iniquity by you?

sn: उत्तिष्ठ हरिशार्दूल भजस्व शयनोत्तमम्। नैवंविधाः शेरते हि भूमौ नृपतिसत्तमाः॥
en: Rise, O best of monkeys, and lie down on a better bed; monarchs do not stretch themselves on earth.

sn: अतीव खलु ते कान्ता वसुधा वसुधाधिप। गतासुरपि तां गात्रैर्मा विहाय निषेवसे॥
en: O lord of earth, indeed earth is your favourite wife; since renouncing me, you, though dead, are serving her with your body.

sn: व्यक्तमद्य त्वया वीर धर्मतः सम्प्रवर्तता। किष्किन्धेव पुरी रम्या स्वर्गमार्गे विनिर्मिता ॥
en: Evident it is, O hero, that while engaged in a lawful conflict, you hadst created another city of Kiskindha, in the region of the celestials.

sn: यान्यस्माभिस्त्वया सार्धं वनेषु मधुगन्धिषु। विहतानि त्वया काले तेषामुपरमः कृतः॥
en: All your enjoyments with me in nectarsmelling woods, have been brought to a close.

sn: निरानन्दा निराशाहं निमग्ना शोकसागरे। त्वयि पञ्चत्वमापन्ने महायूथपयूथपे॥
en: You, the lord of monkey-herds, being slain, I am deprived of joy and hope and am sunk in the abyss of grief.

sn: हृदयं सुस्थितं मह्यं दृष्ट्वा निपतितं भुवि। यन्न शोकाभिसंतप्तं स्फुटतेऽद्य सहस्रधा ॥
en: Forsooth, my heart is uncommon hard, since beholding you on the ground it has not been sundered into thousand pieces being overwhelmed with grief.

sn: सुग्रीवस्य त्वया भार्या हृता स च विवासितः। यत् तत् तस्य त्वया व्युष्टिः प्राप्तेयं प्लवगाधिप।।११।
en: Sugrīva's wife was carried away and banished by you and this is the result of your action, O foremost of monkeys.

sn: निःश्रेयसपरा मोहात् त्वया चाहं विगर्हिता। यैषाऽब्रुवं हितं वाक्यं वानरेन्द्र हितैषिणी॥
en: O lord of monkeys, out of your ignorance you didst neglect all my well meaning words which I said, being intent on your welfare and benefit.

sn: रूपयौवनदृप्तानां दक्षिणानां च मानद। नूनमप्सरसामार्य चित्तानि प्रमथिष्यसि ॥
en: O worshipful one, you shall captivate today, the hearts of the dextrous Apsarās, proud of their youth and beauty.

sn: कालो नि:संशयो नूनं जीवितान्तकरस्तव। बलाद् येनावपन्नोऽसि सुग्रीवस्यावशो वशम्॥
en: Forsooth, you had been by force brought under the control of Kāla, since you had been discomfited by Sugrīva, albeit you are above the control of others.

sn: अस्थाने वालिनं हत्वा युध्यमानं परेण च। स संतप्यति काकुत्स्थः कृत्वा कर्म सुगर्हितम्।।१५।
en: Destroying Vāli unseasonably, while engaged in conflict with another person, and perpetrating such an iniquitous deed Kākutstha does never relent.

sn: वैधव्यं शोकसंतापं कृपणाकृपणा सती। अदुःखोपचिता पूर्वं वर्तयिष्याम्यनाथवत्॥
en: Unused to miseries before how shall I, being an object commiseration, put up like one helpless, with my widow-hood and grief.

sn: लालितश्चाङ्गदो वीरः सुकुमारः सुखोचितः। वत्स्यते कामवस्था मे पितृव्ये क्रोधमूर्छिते॥
en: How shall the heroic and youthful Angada, brought up in luxury and happiness, be regarded by his uncle, senseless with wrath?

sn: कुरुष्व पितरं पुत्र सुदृष्टं धर्मवत्सलम्। दुर्लभं दर्शनं तस्य तव वत्स भविष्यति॥
en: Do you cast for good, O my son, your looks towards your pious sire, for since now it will be hard for you to see him again.

sn: समाश्वासय पुवं त्वं संदेश संदिशस्व मे। मूर्ध्नि चैनं समाघ्राय प्रवासं प्रस्थितो ह्यसि ॥
en: Do you console your son, favour me with orders, smell his head, as you are going to journey in a foreign land.

sn: रामेण हि महत् कर्म कृतं त्वामभिनिघ्नता। आनृण्यं तु गतं तस्य सुग्रीवस्य प्रतिश्रवे॥
en: By destroying you, Rāma, has performed a great action, since by this he has been released from his vow to Sugriva.

sn: सकामो भव सुग्रीव रुमां त्वं प्रतिपत्स्यसे। भुझ्व राज्यमनुद्विग्नः शस्तो भ्राता रिपुस्तव॥
en: O Sugrīva, do you gain your ends and get back your Rumā, devoid of anxiety do you govern your kingdom-your enemy, the brother has been slain.

sn: किं मामेवं प्रलपती प्रियां त्वं नाभिभाषसे। इमाः पश्य वरा बढ्यो भार्यास्ते वानरेश्वर ॥
en: O lord of monkeys, why did you not welcome me, your beloved spouse, who am bewailing thus? Behold, your other wives are also mourning in the same wise.

sn: तस्या विलपितं श्रुत्वा वानर्याः सर्वतश्च ताः। परिगृह्याङ्गदं दीना दुःखार्ताः प्रतिचुक्रुशुः॥
en: Hearing the bewailings of that she-monkey, others, taking Angada, distressed and overwhelmed with grief, began to cry piteously.

sn: किमङ्गदं साङ्गदवीरबाहो विहाय यातोऽसि चिरं प्रवासम्। न युक्तमेवं गुणसंनिकृष्टं विहाय पुत्रं प्रियचारुवेषम्॥
en: O hero, having Arigada on your arms, why are you proceeding on a journey for good in a foreign land leaving behind (your son) Angada. It does not behove you (to leave aside) your dear son, gifted with diverse accomplishments and wearing a charming and beautiful cloth.

sn: यद्यप्रियं किंचिदसम्प्रधार्य कृतं मया स्यात् तव दीर्घबाहो। क्षमस्व मे तद्धरिवंशनाथ व्रजामि मूर्धा तव वीर पादौ ॥
en: you of long arms, O lord of monkeys, if I have offended you in any way, do you forgive me, after ascertaining my crime.

sn: तथा तु तारा करुणं रुदन्ती भर्तुः समीपे सह वानरीभिः। व्यवस्यत प्रायमनिन्द्यवर्णा उपोपवेष्टं भुवि यत्र वाली॥
en: O hero, I touch your feet with my head. Bewailing thus piteously with other sbemonkeys, Tārā, having a blameless countenance, stationing herself where Vāli was, resolved to put an end to her being by fastings.

sn: ततो निपतिता तारां च्युतां तारामिवाम्बरात्। शनैराश्वासयामास हनुमान् हरियूथपः॥
en: Thereupon beholding Tārā fallen (on the ground) like to a star dropt down from the sky, Hanumān, the lord of monkey-herds, consoled her again and again.

sn: गुणदोषकृतं जन्तुः स्वकर्मफलहेतुकम्। अव्यग्रस्तदवाप्नोति सर्वं प्रेत्य शुभाशुभम्॥
en: Animals unagitated, attain to happiness or misery, as an outcome of their actions performed (in their previous existence) by merits or demerits.

sn: शोच्या शोचसि कं शोच्यं दीनं दीनानुकम्पसे। कश्च कस्यानुशोच्योऽस्ति देहेऽस्मिन् बुदबुदोपमे॥
en: Why did you mourn for others, yourself being an object of mourning? Why did you feel commiseration for the poor, yourself being poorly? In this body like to a bubble who is there who mourneth for another?

sn: अङ्गदस्तु कुमारोऽयं द्रष्टव्यो जीवपुत्रया। आयत्यां च विधेयानि समर्थान्यस्य चिन्तय।४।।
en: It behoveth you now, O you having your son alive, to look after prince Angada and think of those duties which remain to be executed by you (after the demise of Vāli).

sn: जानास्यनियतामेवं भूतानामागतिं गतिम्। तस्माच्छुभं हि कर्तव्यं पण्डितेनेह लौकिकम्॥
en: Do you know that life and death of the animals is very unsettled. It is therefore proper to perform what tends to the welfare of after-life. It does not behove you, O learned damsel, to mourn like others.

sn: यस्मिन् हरिसहस्राणि शतानि नियुतानि च। वर्तयन्ति कृताशानि सोऽयं दिष्टान्तमागतः॥
en: He even, who (while living) was surrounded by thousands of monkeys cherishing hopes, has met his destined end.

sn: यदयं न्यायदृष्टार्थः सामदानक्षमापरः। गतो धर्मजितां भूमिं नैनं शोचितुमर्हसि ॥
en: This hero discharged his royal duties in consonance with the sanctions of morality and was gifted with various kingly accomplishments such as conciliation, clarity and forgiveness. He has attained to the land of kings and it becomes you not to mourn for him.

sn: सर्वे च हरिशार्दूलाः पुत्रश्चायं तवाङ्गदः। हवृक्षपतिराज्यं च त्वत्सनाथमनिन्दिते॥
en: O blameless damsel, all these foremost of monkeys, this your son Angada, this kingdom of the monkey chief, do belong to you.

sn: ताविमौ शोकसंतप्तौ शनैः प्रेरय भामिनि। त्वया परिगृहीतोऽयमङ्गदः शास्तु मेदिनीम्॥
en: Do you soon despatch, O passionate lady, these two (Angada and Sugrīva) exercised with grief as they are (for the performance of Vali's funeral rites). And abiding by your commandments let Angada govern the earth.

sn: संततिश्च यथा दृष्टा कृत्यं यच्चापि साम्प्रतम्। राज्ञस्तत् क्रियतां सर्वमेष कालस्य निश्चयः॥
en: Let Angada perform all those ceremonies, which should be gone through by sons according to the Šāstras and which are for the well-being of the king; this is the time for the performance of those funeral rites.

sn: संस्कार्यो हरिराजस्तु अङ्गदश्चाभिषिच्यताम्। सिंहासनगतं पुत्रं पश्यन्ती शान्तिमेष्यसि॥
en: Performing the funeral ceremonies of the lord of monkeys do you install Angada. And beholding your son thus established on the throne you shall be able to pacify your grief?

sn: सा तस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा भर्तृव्यसनपीडिता। अब्रवीदुत्तरं तारा हनूमन्तमवस्थितम्॥
en: Hearing those words of Hanumān, Tārā, racked with grief consequent upon the loss of her lord, bespake him who was standing there:

sn: अङ्गदप्रतिरूपाणां पुत्राणामेकतः शतम्। हतस्याप्यस्य वीरस्य गात्रसंश्लेषणं वरम्॥
en: I would rather die with this hero who has been slain than have hundred sons like Angada.

sn: न चाहं हरिराज्यस्य प्रभवाम्यङ्गदस्य वा। पितृव्यस्तस्य सुग्रीवः सर्वकार्येष्वनन्तरः॥
en: I cannot myself govern this kingdom nor can I confer it upon Angada. Such duty-devolves upon his (Angada's) uncle Sugrīva now.

sn: नह्येषा बुद्धिरास्थेया हनूमन्नङ्गदं प्रति। पिता हि बन्धुः पुत्रस्य न माता हरिसत्तम ॥
en: O Hanumān, do you not consider that I shall confer this kingdom upon Angada-0 best of monkeys, father is son's friend (in this respect) not mother.

sn: नहि मम हरिराजसंश्रयात् क्षमतरमस्ति परत्र चेह वा। अभिमुखहतवीर सेवितं शयनमिदं मम सेवितुं क्षमम्॥
en: There is no other resource for me tending to my welfare both in this world and the next than taking refuge to this lord of monkeys. It is becoming for me to serve this bed which has been resorted to by the hero, slain (and lying before me.) monkeys, father is son's friend (in this respect) not mother.

sn: नहि मम हरिराजसंश्रयात् क्षमतरमस्ति परत्र चेह वा। अभिमुखहतवीर सेवितं शयनमिदं मम सेवितुं क्षमम्॥
en: There is no other resource for me tending to my welfare both in this world and the next than taking refuge to this lord of monkeys. It is becoming for me to serve this bed which has been resorted to by the hero, slain (and lying before me.)

sn: वीक्षमाणस्तु मन्दासुः सर्वतो मन्दमुच्छ्वसन्। आदावेव तु सुग्रीवं ददर्शानुजमग्रतः॥
en: Vāli, ranging on the verge of death, casting his looks arounds and sighing faintly, espied his younger brother Sugrīva before him.

sn: तं प्राप्तविजयं वाली सुग्रीवं प्लवगेश्वरम्। आभाष्य व्यक्तया वाचा सस्नेहमिदमब्रवीत्॥
en: Welcoming that lord of monkeys with clear accents, Vāli addressed him affectionately saying.

sn: सुग्रीव दोषेण न मां गन्तुमर्हसि किल्वषात्। कृष्यमाणं भविष्येण बुद्धिमोहेन मां बलात्॥
en: O Sugrīva, do you not take to your heart the improper conduct I have shown towards you, being attracted by inevitable foolishness, subject as I was to sin.

sn: युगपद् विहितं तात न मन्ये सुखमावयोः। सौहार्दै भ्रातृयुक्तं हि तदिदं जातमन्यथा॥
en: Methinks, O brother, it is not our fortune to enjoy at the same time the double bliss of fraternal affection and the enjoyment of kingdom, or else why has it happened otherwise?

sn: प्रतिपद्य त्वमद्यैव राज्यमेषां वनौकसाम्। मामप्यद्यैव गच्छन्तं विद्धि वैवस्वतक्षयम्॥
en: Do you acquire to-day this kingdom of the forest-ranges and know me as one who has departed to the abode of Death.

sn: जीवितं च हि राज्यं च श्रियं च विपुलां तथा। प्रजहाम्येष वै तूर्णमहं चागर्हितं यशः॥
en: Soon shall I renounce iny life, kingdom, my exquisite grace and my blameless fame.

sn: अस्यां त्वहमवस्थायां वीर वक्ष्यामि यद् वचः। यद्यप्यसुकरं राजन् कर्तुमेव त्वमर्हसि।७।।
en: It behoveth you, O hero, O king, to perform what I shall speak to you in this plight, however difficult it might be.

sn: सुखाहँ सुखसंवृद्धं बालमेनमबालिशम्। वाष्पपूर्णमुखं पश्य भूमौ पतितमङ्गदम्॥
en: Do you behold Angada fallen on the ground with tears in his eyes-a little boy, incapable, brought up in luxury and deserving happiness.

sn: मम प्राणैः प्रियतरं पुत्रं पुत्रमिवौरसम्। मया हीनमहीनार्थं सर्वतः परिपालय॥
en: Do you maintain this my son, dearer than my life, like to your own son, born of your loins, satisfying all his wants in my absence.

sn: त्वमप्यस्य पिता दाता परित्राता च सर्वशः। भयेष्वभयदश्चैव यथाहं प्लवगेश्वर॥
en: O best of monkeys, like to me, you are his father, protector, conferrer of gifts and remover of fear.

sn: एष तारात्मजः श्रीमांस्त्वया तुल्यपराक्रमः। रक्षसां च वधे तेषामग्रतस्ते भविष्यति॥
en: This graceful son of Tārā equals you in prowess and shall precede you in the destruction of Raksasas.

sn: अनुरूपाणि कर्माणि विक्रम्य बलवान् रणे। करिष्यत्येष तारेयस्तेजस्वी तरुणोऽङ्गदः॥
en: This youthful Angada, Tārā's son, gifted with energy and strength, shall perform befitting exploits displaying his prowess in the battle.

sn: सुषेणदुहिता चेयमर्थसूक्ष्मविनिश्चये। औत्पातिके च विविधे सर्वतः परिनिष्ठिता॥
en: Surasen's daughter is wonderfully expert in ascertaining sabtle things and giving counsels in the time of danger.

sn: यदेषा साध्विति ब्रूयात् कार्यं तन्मुक्तसंशयम्। नहि तारामतं किंचिदन्यथा परिवर्तते॥
en: Do you, without the least doubt perform what shall the chaste lady instruct you to do; for Tārā's advice never goes without effect.

sn: राघवस्य च ते कार्यं कर्तव्यमविशङ्कया। स्यादधर्मो ह्यकरणे त्वां च हिंस्यादमानितः॥
en: It behoveth you to perform Rāghava's service fearlessly or else you shall be visited with sin: on his being insulted you shall be injured.

sn: इमां च मालामाधत्स्व दिव्यां सुग्रीव काञ्चनीम्। उदारा श्रीः स्थिता ह्यस्यां सम्प्रजह्यान्मृते मयि॥
en: O Sugrīva, do you put on this celestial golden garland-herein dwelleth the bounteous Sree who shall renounce me after my death.

sn: इत्येवमुक्तः सुग्रीवो वालिना भ्रातृसौहृदात्। हर्षं त्यक्त्वा पुनर्दीनो ग्रहग्रस्त इवोडुराट्॥
en: Having been accosted thus by Vāli, out of fraternal affection, Sugrīva renouncing joy again became pale like to the Moon possessed by Rahu.

sn: तद्वालिवचनाच्छान्तः कुर्वन् युक्तमतन्द्रितः। जग्राह सोऽभ्यनुज्ञातो मालां तां चैव काञ्चनीम्॥
en: Renouncing his inimical feelings, being thus addressed by Vāli and carrying out his words energetically Sugrīva accepted the golden garland as ordered (by him).

sn: तां मालां काञ्चनीं दत्त्वा दृष्ट्वा चैवात्मजं स्थितम्। संसिद्धः प्रेत्यभावाय स्नेहादङ्गदमब्रवीत्॥
en: And conferring (upon Sugrīva) that golden garland and beholding his son before him, Vāli, resolved upon death, spoke to Angada, saying.

sn: देशकालौ भजस्वाद्य क्षममाणः प्रियाप्रिये। सुखदुःखसहः काले सुग्रीववशगो भव॥
en: Do you place yourself now under the control of Sugrīva, ascertaining time and place, putting up with misery for your welfare and injury.

sn: यथा हि त्वं महाबाहो लालितः सततं मया। न तथा वर्तमानं त्वां सुग्रीवो बहु मन्यते॥
en: O you having long arms, Sugrīva shall not regard you much, if did you remain in the same wise in which you hadst been brought up by me before*. The significance of the passage is as follows:You wert a mere child while I brought you up. But now you are a grown up young man and this is the time for you to serve your elders. Do you therefore serve Sugriva.

sn: नास्यामित्रैर्गतं गच्छेर्मा शत्रुभिररिंदम। भर्तुरर्थपरो दान्तः सुग्रीववशगो भव॥
en: O slayer of foes, do you never mix with Sugrīva's enemies, and place yourself always under Sugrīva's control, having subdued your senses and being intent upon your master's (Sugriva's) welfare.

sn: न चातिप्रणयः कार्यः कर्तव्योऽप्रणयश्च ते। उभयं हि महादोषं तस्मादन्तरदृग्भव॥
en: Do you not cultivate too much of friendship nor be wanting in it-for both of these extremes are sources of disasters. Do you therefore follow the golden mean.

sn: इत्युक्त्वाथ विवृत्ताक्षः शरसम्पीडितो भृशम्। विवृतैर्दशनैर्भीमैर्बभूवोत्क्रान्तजीवितः॥
en: After he had said this, his eyes became expanded, his teeth were opened and his appearance became ghastly. And greatly pained by shafts he breathed his last.

sn: ततो विचुक्रुशुस्तत्र वानरा हतयूथपाः। परिदेवयमानास्ते सर्वे प्लवगसत्तमाः॥
en: And thereupon, the monkeys, the foremost of those who go jumping, having lost their chief, bewailed and cried.

sn: किष्किन्धां ह्यद्य शून्या च स्वर्गते वानरेश्वरे। उद्यानानि च शून्यानि पर्वताः काननानि च॥
en: On that monkey chief's departure to the land of celestials, Kişkindhā was divested of her lord, and gardens, hills and woods were all rendered lonely.

sn: हते प्लवगशार्दूले निष्प्रभा वानराः कृताः। येन दत्तं महद् युद्धं गन्धर्वस्य महात्मनः॥ गोलभस्य महाबाहोर्दश वर्षाणि पञ्च च। नैव रात्रौ न दिवसे तद् युद्धमुपशाम्यति ॥ ततः षोडशमे वर्षे गोलभो विनिपातितः। तं हत्वा दुर्विनीतं तु वाली दंष्ट्राकरालवान्। सर्वाभयंकरोऽस्माकं कथमेष निपातितः॥
en: That best of monkeys, who fought a dreadful battle with the high-souled Gandharvas, being dead, all other monkeys became of pale countenance. Vāli entered into a terrible conflict with the mighty-armed Golava and fought for ten years and five, for nights and days without respite. And on the sixteenth year, Golabha was killed. Bringing about the destruction of that wicked Gandharba, Vāli, having terrible teeth, saved us all from fear. How has he been killed to-day?

sn: हते तु वीरे प्लवगाधिपे तदा वनेचरास्तत्र न शर्म लेभिरे। वनेचराः सिंहयुते महावने यथा हि गावो निहते गवां पतौ॥
en: Like to kine, incapable of enjoying peace in a mighty forest filled with lions, their chief being dead, these forest-rangers could not attain to felicity on the demise of that lord of monkeys.

sn: ततस्तु तारा व्यसनार्णवप्लुता मृतस्य भर्तुर्वदनं समीक्ष्य सा। जगाम भूमिं परिरभ्य वालिनं महादुमं छिन्नमिवाश्रिता लता॥
en: Thereupon, Tārā, sunk in the gulf of disaster, eyeing the countenance of her deceased lord, fell down to the ground embracing Vāli like to a creeper clinging for its support to a mighty but broken tree.

sn: ततः समुपजिघ्रन्ती कपिराजस्य तन्मुखम्। पतिं लोकश्रुता तारा मृतं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Thereupon smelling the face of that lord of monkeys, Tārā again addressed her deceased lord, known all over the world, saying.

sn: शेषे त्वं विषमे दुःखमकृत्वा वचनं मम। उपलोपचिते वीर सुदुःखे वसुधातले॥
en: O hero, disregarding my words, you are lying on the uneven earth, hard and filled with gravels.

sn: मत्तः प्रियतरा नूनं वानरेन्द्र मही तव। शेषे हि तां परिष्वज्य मां च न प्रतिभाषसे॥
en: O lord of monkeys, the earth is dearer to you than I, since you are lying there embracing her and are not welcoming me.

sn: सुग्रीवस्य वशं प्राप्तो विधिरेष भवत्यहो। सुग्रीव एव विक्रान्तो वीर साहसिकप्रिय॥
en: O hero, O dear, O brave lord, wonder it is that God under the semblance of Rāma, has placed himself under the control of Sugrīva; hither to fore he shall be regarded as a hero.

sn: ऋक्षवानरमुख्यास्त्वां बलिनं पर्युपासते। तेषां विलपितं कृच्छ्रमङ्गदस्य च शोचतः॥ मम चेमा गिरः श्रुत्वा किं त्वं न प्रतिबुध्यसे।
en: Why are you not awake, hearing the bewailings of bears and monkeys who used to wait upon you, powerful, as well as that of Angada and myself?

sn: इदं तद् वीरशयनं तत्र शेषे हतो युधि ॥ शायिता निहता यत्र त्वयैव रिपवः पुरा।
en: Alas! you are lying on this bed of the heroes, being slain in the battle, where formerly, your enemies destroyed by you, used to lie down,

sn: विशुद्धसत्त्वाभिजन प्रिययुद्ध मम प्रिय॥ मामनाथां विहायैकां गतस्त्वमसि मानद।
en: O you born of a pure family, O you that are fond of warfare, O my dear, O conferror of honours, whither have you departed making me husbandless?

sn: शूराय न प्रदातव्या कन्या खलु विपश्चिता ॥ शूरभार्यां हतां पश्य सद्यो मां विधवां कृताम्।
en: Let not the wise, henceforth, confer their daughters upon the heroes. Alas! behold me, the wife of a hero, made a widow in no time.

sn: अवभग्नश्च मे मानो भग्ना मे शाश्वती गतिः॥ अगाधे च निमग्नास्मि विपुले शोकसागरे।
en: Shattered is my honour and destroyed is my happiness and I am sunk in the deep abyss of grief.

sn: अश्मसारमयं नूनमिदं मे हृदयं दृढम्॥ भर्तारं निहतं दृष्ट्वा यन्नाद्य शतधा कृतम्।
en: Forsooth, this my firm heart is not sundered into hundred pieces, beholding my husband slain!

sn: सुहृच्चैव च भर्ता च प्रकृत्या च मम प्रियः॥ प्रहारे च पराक्रान्तः शूरः पञ्चत्वमागतः।
en: You are my friend, my dear husband and a great hero-and you had met with destruction, being struck by another man.

sn: पतिहीना तु या नारी कामं भवतु पुत्रिणी॥ धनधान्यसमृद्धापि विधवेत्युच्यते जनैः।
en: A husbandless woman is always styled by the wise as widow, although she might have a son and enough of riches.

sn: स्वगात्रप्रभवे वीर शेषे रुधिरमण्डले॥ कृमिरागपरिस्तोमे स्वकीये शयने यथा।
en: O hero, you are lying down in a pool of blood issuing out of your own person, like to your own bed having a red-dyed bed-sheet.

sn: रेणुशोणितसंवीतं गात्रं तव समन्ततः॥ परिरब्धुं न शक्नोमि भुजाभ्यां प्लवगर्षभ।
en: Your body is on all sides besmeared with blood and dust and I am incapable of embracing you with my arms, O best of monkeys.

sn: कृतकृत्योऽद्य सुग्रीवो वैरेऽस्मिन्नतिदारुणे॥ यस्य रामविमुक्तेन हृतमेकेषुणा भयम्।
en: Surely has Sugrīva satisfied his hostile intention to-day, whose fear has been removed by one shaft, discharged by Rāma.

sn: शरेण हृदि लग्नेन गात्रसंस्पर्शने तव॥ वार्यामि त्वां निरीक्षन्ती त्वयि पञ्चत्वमागते।
en: Thyself departing to the land of the dead. I have been eyeing you simply, being prevented from touching your person by the shaft piercing your heart.* The meaning is:-Lest by my touching that shaft you feelest a greater pain.

sn: उद्घबर्ह शरं नीलस्तस्य गात्रगतं तदा॥ गिरिगह्वरसंलीनं दीप्तमाशीविषं यथा।
en: Thereupon Neela took out that shaft from the person of (Vāli) like to a flaming serpent lurking in a mountain cave.

sn: तस्य निष्कृष्यमाणस्य बाणस्यापि बभौ द्युतिः॥ अस्तमस्तकसंरुद्धरश्मेदिनकरादिव।
en: There beamed the shaft extracted from his body like to the rays of the Sun, stationed on the summit of the setting hill.

sn: पेतुः क्षतजधारास्तु व्रणेभ्यस्तस्य सर्वशः॥ ताम्रगैरिकसम्पृक्ता धारा इव धराधरात्।
en: And there poured forth from all his wounds, streams of blood, like to showers of melted copper and other metals falling from a mountain.

sn: अवकीर्णं विमार्जन्ती भर्तारं रणरेणुना॥ अनैर्नयनजैः शूरं सिषेचास्त्रसमाहतम् ।
en: And (Tārā) washed, with tears, her heroic husband's body covered with dust and wounded with weapons.

sn: रुधिरोक्षितसर्वाङ्गं दृष्ट्वा विनिहतं पतिम्॥ उवाच तारा पिङ्गाक्षं पुत्रमङ्गदमङ्गना।
en: Beholding her husband thus slain and besmeared with blood, she spoke to her son, Angada, having coppery eyes, saying:

sn: अवस्था पश्चिमां पश्य पितुः पुत्र सुदारुणाम्॥ सम्प्रसक्तस्य वैरस्य गतोऽन्तः पापकर्मणा।
en: Behold this terrible declining stage of your Sire. Here is the end of his hostilities collected by his impious action.

sn: बालसूर्योज्ज्वलतनुं प्रयातं यमसादनम्॥ अभिवादय राजानं पितरं पुत्र मानदम्।
en: O my son, do you how to your kingly father, the conferrer of honours, who has departed to the abode of Death, having a flaming person like to the rising Sun.

sn: एवमुक्तः समुत्थाय जग्राह चरणौ पितुः॥ भुजाभ्यां पीनवृत्ताभ्यामङ्गदोऽहमिति ब्रुवन्।
en: Thus accosted, Angada rose up and, saying, I (do touch my Sire's feet), embraced his father's feet with his plump arms.

sn: अभिवादयमानं त्वामङ्गदं त्वं यथा पुरा॥ दीर्घायुर्भव पुत्रेति किमर्थं नाभिभाषसे।
en: (Thereupon Tāră said)—Saying 'Do you live long' why did you not welcome Angada, to-day as before, who has bowed to you?

sn: अहं पुत्रसहाया त्वामुपासे गतचेतनम्। सिंहेन पातितं सद्यो गौः सवत्सेव गोवृषम्॥
en: I am with my son, standing by you who are dead, like to a cow with her calf, having the bull slain by a lion.

sn: इष्ट्वा संग्रामयज्ञेन रामप्रहरणाम्भसा। तस्मिन्नवभृथे स्नातः कथं पत्न्या मया विना ॥ या दत्ता देवराजेन तव तुष्टेन संयुगे। शातकौम्भीं प्रियां मालां तां ते पश्यामि नेह किम्।।२८
en: How have you, without me, your wife, bathed in the water of Rāma's shafts, at the end of your battle-like sacrifice? Why do I not behold here that favourite golden garland of thine, which was conferred on you by the lord of celestials, pleased in a battle?

sn: राज्यश्रीन जहाति त्वां गतासुमपि मानद। सूर्यस्यावर्तमानस्य शैलराजमिव प्रभा॥
en: Royal grace has not renounced you, O conferrer of honours, albeit you are dead, like to the rays not quitting the king of mountains, even after the Sun is set.

sn: न मे वचः पथ्यमिदं त्वया कृतं न चास्मि शक्ता हि निवारणे तव। हता सपुत्रास्मि हतेन संयुगे सह त्वया श्रीजिहाति मामपि॥
en: You didst not act by my wholesome words, nor could I prevent you. And I am now destroyed with my son, along with you in the battle. Truly has Sree (goddess of wealth) renounced me.

sn: तामाशु वेगेन दुरासदेन त्वभिप्लुतां शोकमहार्णवेन। पश्यंस्तदा वाल्यनुजस्तरस्वी भ्रातुर्वधेनाप्रतिमेन तेपे॥
en: Beholding Tārā emerged in a deep and mighty ocean of grief, Vali's younger brother was overwhelmed with penitence, in consequence of the unbecoming destruction of his brother.

sn: स वाष्पपूर्णेन मुखेन पश्यन् क्षणेन निर्विण्णमना मनस्वी। जगाम रामस्य शनैः समीपं भृत्यैर्वृतः सम्परिदूयमानः॥
en: And seeing her countenance full of tears, the high-souled (Sugriva), racked with grief and repentance, approached slowly Ráma along with his followers.

sn: मुदात्तमाशीविषतुल्यबाणम्। मवस्थितं राघवमित्युवाच ॥
en: And nearing him, with a bow in his hand, having arrows like to serpents, famed and having auspicious marks on his person, he spoke to Rāghava, seated there, saying.

sn: यथा प्रतिज्ञामिदं नरेन्द्र कृतं त्वया दृष्टफलं च कर्म। ममाद्य भोगेषु नरेन्द्रसूनो मनो निवृत्तं हतजीवितेन॥
en: O lord of men, you had fulfilled your promise by carrying it out into practice; and as for wretched me, O son of a king, I shall refrain today from all enjoyments.

sn: अस्यां महिष्यां तु भृशं रुदत्यां पुरेऽतिविक्रोशति दुःखतप्ते। हते नृपे संशयितेऽङ्गदे च न राम राज्ये रमते मनो मे।।
en: This queen lamenting piteously, these subjects and retinue bewailing, being overwhelmed with grief, this king being slain, how can kingdom please me.?

sn: क्रोधादमर्षादतिविप्रधर्षाद् भ्रातुर्वधो मेऽनुमतः पुरस्तात्। हते त्विदानी हरियूथपेऽस्मिन् सुतीक्ष्णमिक्ष्वाकुवर प्रतप्स्ये॥
en: O Rāma out of anger, and passion, and on account of my being insulted by him, I did formerly desire to bring about my brother's destruction. But that lord of monkey-herds being shain, O best of lkswakus, I am truly pierced to the quick with anguish.

sn: श्रेयोऽद्य मन्ये मम शैलमुख्ये तस्मिन् हि वासश्चिरमृष्यमूके। यथा तथा वर्तयतः स्ववृत्या नेमं निहत्य त्रिदिवस्य लाभः॥
en: I do prefer living for good in the mount Rșyamūka, earning my livelihood somehow or other, to the accession of heaven by destroying (Vāli).

sn: मयं महात्मा मतिमानुवाच। मिदं वचः कर्म च मेऽनुरूपम्॥
en: This highly intellectual and high-souled one spoke to me Do you range at large, I do not wish to destroy you. Such words were really becoming of him, O Rāma. And these words and this action become me (vile as I am).

sn: भ्राता कथं नाम महागुणस्य भ्रातुर्वधं राम विरोचयेत। राज्यस्य दुःखस्य च वीर सारं विचिन्तयन्कामपुरस्कृतोऽपि॥
en: How can a brother, O Rāma, however avaricious he might be, relish the destruction of his qualified brother, comparing the happiness of a kingdom, with the grief (consequent upon his brother's demise)?

sn: वधो हि मतो नासीत् स्वमाहात्म्यव्यतिक्रमात्। ममासीद् बुद्धिदौरात्म्यात् प्राणहारी व्यतिक्रमः॥
en: He did not desire to slay me, lest his greatness inight be spoiled; but alas! through my wicked sense, I performed an iniquity by taking the life of my brother.

sn: दुमशाखावभग्नोऽहं मुहूर्तं परिनिष्टनन्। सान्त्वयित्वा त्वनेनोक्तो न पुनः कर्तुमर्हसि ॥
en: Being struck by him with branches of trees, while I fled away and wept, he, consoling me, said only Do not do this again.

sn: भ्रातृत्वमार्यभावश्च धर्मश्चानेन रक्षितः। मया क्रोधश्च कामश्च कपित्वं च प्रदर्शितम्॥
en: He all along maintained his fraternal feelings, his honesty and piety; but (woe to me) I have displayed my wrath, passion and monkey-hood.

sn: मनीप्सनीयं स्वनवेक्षणीयम्। प्राप्तोऽस्मि पाप्मानमिदं वयस्य भ्रातुर्वधात् त्वाष्ट्रवधादिवेन्द्रः॥
en: O friend, like to the lord of celestials perpetrating sin by destroying Biswarupa, I have been, by bringing about the destruction of my brother, visited. with this sin, beyond comprehensio”, avoidable, undesirable and invisible.

sn: पाप्मानमिन्द्रस्य मही जलं च वृक्षाश्च कामं जगृहुः स्त्रियश्च। को नाम पाप्मानमिमं सहेत शाखामृगस्य प्रतिपत्तुमिच्छेत्॥
en: Indra's sin was shared by earth, water, trees and women; but who is there who will bear and desire to participate this monkey's sin?-

sn: नार्हामि सम्मानमिमं प्रजानां न यौवराज्यं कुत एव राज्यम्। मेवंविधं राघव कर्म कृत्वा ॥
en: Perpetrating such an improper and irreligious act, tending to the decay of my family, I do not deserve the respect of my subjects and the heirapparentship; what of kingdom, O Rāghava.

sn: पापस्य कर्तास्मि विगर्हितस्य क्षुद्रस्य लोकापकृतस्य लोके। शोको महान् मामभिवर्ततेऽयं वृष्टेर्यथा निम्नमिवाम्बुवेगः॥
en: I am the perpetrator of a vile and disgraceful sin, blamed of all in this world. And like to a current of rain going downwards, this mighty grief has overcome me.

sn: सोदर्यघातापरगाववालः संतापहस्ताक्षिशिरोविषाणः। एनोमयो मामभिहन्ति हस्ती दृप्तो नदीकूलमिव प्रवृद्धः॥
en: This mighty and infuriated elephant of a sin, having the destruction of a brother as its body, repentance, as its trunk, head, eyes and tusks, has been crushing me like to the banks of a river.

sn: अंहो वतेदं नृवराविषह्यं निवर्तते मे हृदि साधुवृत्तम्। अग्नौ विवर्णं परितप्यमानं किट्टं यथा राघव जातरूपम्॥
en: Alas! O best of kings, this unbearable sin has been driving away all pious feelings from my heart like to alloy leaking out of discoloured gold when molten in fire, O Rāghava.

sn: मिदं कुलं राघव मनिमित्तम्। दर्धस्थितप्राणमितीव मन्ये॥
en: Methinks, for me, O Rāghava, these mighty monkeys and Angada are almost half-dead (with grief).

sn: सुतः सुलभ्यः सुजनः सुवश्यः कुतस्तु पुत्रः सदृशोऽङ्गदेन। न चापि विद्येत स वीर देशो यस्मिन् भवेत् सोदरसंनिकर्षः॥
en: A good-natured and obedient son is rare. Where is to be found Angada's equal? O hero, there is no such land where I may meet again my brother.

sn: जीवेत माता परिपालनार्थम्। विना तु पुत्रं परितापदीना सा नैव जीवेदिति निश्चितं मे॥
en: The heroic Angada shall not live to-day and if he lives, his another shall live to bring him up. Forsooth, without her son, she shall not live long.

sn: सोऽहं प्रवेक्ष्याम्यतिदीप्तमग्नि भ्रात्रा च पुत्रेण च सख्यमिच्छन्। इमे विचेष्यन्ति हरिप्रवीराः सीतां निदेशे परिवर्तमानाः॥
en: Therefore shall I enter this flaming fire with a view to place myself on the same level with my brother and his son and all these mighty monkeys shall engage in quest of Sītā, abiding by your commandments.

sn: न्मय्यप्यतीते मनुजेन्द्रपुत्र। कुलस्य हन्तारमजीवना रामानुजानीहि कृतागसं माम्॥
en: O son of a king, they shall all carry out your orders even in my absence, do you, therefore, order me (to enter fire) who am the destroyer of my own race, have performed an inequity and do not deserve living any more.

sn: इत्येवमार्तस्य रघुप्रवीरः श्रुत्वा वचो वालिजघन्यजस्य। संजातवाष्पः परवीरहन्ता रामो मुहूर्तं विमना बभूव ॥
en: Hearing the words of Vali's younger brother, who was bewailing thus, Rāma, the heroic descendant of Rāghu and the slayer of foes, remained stupefied for some time with tears in his eyes.

sn: तस्मिन् क्षणेऽभीक्ष्णमवेक्षमाणः क्षितिक्षमावान् भुवनस्य गोप्ता। रामो रुदन्ती व्यसने निमग्नां समुत्सुकः सोऽथ ददर्श ताराम्॥
en: In the mean-time, Rāma patient like to the protector of the world, worked with curiosity looked again and again towards the bewailing Tārā sunk in the gulf of disaster.

sn: तां चारुनेत्रां कपिसिंहनाथां पतिं समाश्लिष्य तदा शयानाम्। उत्थापयामासुरदीनसत्त्वां मन्त्रिप्रधानाः कपिराजपत्नीम्।।
en: Thereupon the principal counsellors raised up the brave spouse of the lord of monkeys, having graceful eyes and lying on the earth, embracing her husband.

sn: सा विस्फुरन्ती परिरभ्यमाणा भर्तुः समीपादपनीयमाना। ददर्श राम शरचापपाणिं स्वतेजसा सूर्यमिव ज्वलन्तम्॥
en: And snatched away from her husband and trembling, she beheld Rāma, with bow and arrows in his hand burning like to the Sun by virtue of his own effulgence.

sn: सुसंवृतं पार्थिवलक्षणैश्च तं चारुनेत्रं मृगशावनेत्रा। मयं स काकुत्स्थ इति प्रजज्ञे॥
en: Beholding him gifted with all royal marks, having beautiful eyes and never seen before, that one, having the eyes of a fawn, thought within herself. This great one must be Kākutstha.

sn: तस्येन्द्रकल्पस्य दुरासदस्य महानुभावस्य समीपमार्या। आर्ताऽतितूर्णं व्यसनं प्रपन्ना जगाम तारा परिविह्वलन्ती॥
en: The worshipful Tārā, worked with grief, and overwhelmed with disasters, bewailing, neared quickly that high-souled one, resembling the lord of celestials and hard to approach.

sn: तं सा समासाद्य विशुद्धसत्त्वं शोकेन सम्भ्रान्तशरीरभावा। मनस्विनी वाक्यमुवाच तारा रामं रणोत्कर्षणलब्धलक्ष्यम्॥
en: And having reached the pure-souled Rāma, who had his ends fully attained in battle, the high-minded Tārā, having her frame worked with grief, spoke to him, saying.

sn: त्वमप्रमेयश्च दुरासदश्च जितेन्द्रियश्चोत्तमधर्मकश्च। अक्षीणकीर्तिश्च विचक्षणश्च क्षितिक्षमावान् क्षतजोपमाक्षः॥
en: You are immeasurable, hard to approach, highly pious, prudent of controlled senses and increasing fame, forgiving like to earth and of blood-red eyes.

sn: महाबलः संहननोपपन्नः। मनुष्यदेहाभ्युदयं विहाय दिव्येन देहाभ्युदयेन युक्तः॥
en: You have bow and arrows in hand, are highly powerful and of a tough body. And renouncing human grace you had assumed the grace of a celestial person.

sn: येनैव बाणेन हतः प्रियो मे तेनैव बाणेन हि मां जहीहि । हता गमिष्यामि समीपमस्य न मां विना वीर रमेत वाली॥
en: Do you slay me with that self-same shaft with which my dear one was slain. And thus slain, O hero, I shall near him, for Vāli does not relish the company of any other woman but me.

sn: स्वर्गेऽपि पद्मामलपत्रनेत्र समेत्य सम्प्रेक्ष्य च मामपश्यन्। न ह्येष उच्चावचताम्रचूडा विचित्रवेषाप्यसोऽभजिष्यत्॥
en: O you having eyes resembling clean lotuspetals, this (hero) departing to the abode of celestials and not beholding me there, shall not delight in the company of Apsarās, wearing diversified garments and copper-coloured coronets.

sn: स्वर्गेऽपि शोकं च विवर्णतां च मया विना प्राप्स्यति वीर वाली। रम्ये नगेन्द्रस्य तटावकाशे विदेहकन्यारहितो यथा त्वम्॥
en: Even in the land of celestials, O hero, Vāli shall turn pale with grief in my separation, like to you in the picuresque dale of the Lord of mountains, separated from the daughter of the king of Videha.

sn: त्वं वेत्थ तावद् वनिताविहीनः प्राप्नोति दुःखं पुरुषः कुमारः। तत् त्वं प्रजानञ्जहि मां न वाली दुःखं ममादर्शनजं भजेत॥
en: You know well that a hand-some man is greatly afflicted with the separation of his spouse; and knowing this, do you slay me, and Vāli shall not be tormented with grief consequent upon my absence.

sn: यच्चापि मन्येत भवान् महात्मा स्त्रीघातदोषस्तु भवेन मह्यम्। आत्मेयमस्येति हि मां जहि त्वं न स्त्रीवधः स्यान्मनुजेन्द्रपुत्र ॥
en: High-souled as you are, you are thinking that you shall, slaying me, be visited with a sin arising from the destruction of a female. But do you kill me, O son of a king, knowing me as the soul of Vali, and you shall not be responsible for destroying a woman.

sn: दनन्यरूपाः पुरुषस्य दाराः। दारप्रदानाद्धि न दानमन्यत् प्रदृश्यते ज्ञानवतां हि लोके ॥
en: According to the Vedas and various other sacred texts, wives are inseparably blended with their husbands. And the wise say that there is no other gift better than that of a wife in this world.

sn: त्वं चापि मां तस्य मम प्रियस्य प्रदास्यसे धर्ममवेक्ष्य वीर। मधर्मयोगं मम वीर घातात्॥
en: You shall, O hero, confer me religiously upon my dear one and by this gift you shall be saved from the sin consequent upon killing me.

sn: मेवंगतां नार्हसि मामहन्तुम्। अहं हि मातङ्गविलासगामिना प्लवङ्गमानामृषभेण धीमता। विना वराहॊत्तमहेममालिना चिरं न शक्ष्यामि नरेन्द्र जीवितुम्॥
en: It does not behove you not to kill me, who am exercised with grief, without my lord, snatched away from him and reduced to such a (pitiable) plight. O lord of men, I cannot live long without that highly intelligent lord of monkeys, having an elephantine gait and wearing an excellent golden garland.

sn: इत्येवमुक्तस्तु विभुर्महात्मा तारां समाश्वास्य हितं बभाषे। मा वीरभार्ये विमतिं कुरुष्व लोको हि सर्वो विहितो विधात्रा ॥
en: Thus accosted, the high-souled lord consoling Tārā, spoke to her the following well-meaning words.–Do you not lose yourself, O wife of a hero. This whole world of creation is being guided by God's dispensation.

sn: तं चैव सर्वं सुखदुःखयोगं लोकोऽब्रवीत् तेन कृतं विधात्रा। त्रयोऽपि लोका विहितं विधानं नातिक्रमन्ते वशगा हि तस्य॥
en: And by Him is administered misery or happiness as people say. These three worlds cannot neglect His dispensations and are entirely subject to Him.

sn: प्रीतिं परां प्राप्स्यसि तां तथैव पुत्रश्च ते प्राप्स्यति यौवराज्यम्। धात्रा विधानं विहितं तथैव न शूरपत्न्यः परिदेवयन्ति॥
en: Your son shall attain to the heir apparentship of the throne and you shall enjoy excellent joy therefrom.

sn: आश्वासिता तेन महात्मना तु प्रभावयुक्तेन परंतपेन। सा वीरपत्नी ध्वनता मुखेन सुवेषरूपा विरराम तारा॥
en: This has been decreed by the Almighty. Wives of heroes do never relent. Being thus consoled by the high-souled (Rāma) gifted with prowess, and the slayer of foes, Tārā, the wife of a heroic husband and wearing a graceful garment, ceased bewailing.

sn: स सुग्रीवं च तारां च साङ्गदां सहलक्ष्मणः। समानशोकः काकुत्स्थः सान्त्वयनिदमब्रवीत्॥
en: Thereupon, Kākutstha, with Laksmana, equally aggrieved, said, consoling Sugrīva, and Tārā together with Angada.

sn: न शोकपरितापेन श्रेयसा युज्यते मृतः। यदत्रान्तरं कार्यं तत् समाधातुमर्हथ ॥
en: Grief and lamentations do not tend to the welfare of the deceased. It therefore behoveth you to perform the after ceremonies.

sn: लोकवृत्तमनुष्ठेयं कृतं वो बाष्पमोक्षणम्। न कालादुत्तरं किंचित् कर्म शक्यमुपासितुम्॥
en: You have satisfied the worldly practice with a profuse discharge of tears. It is not proper to delay the performance of appointed actions.

sn: नियतिः कारणं लोके नियतिः कर्मसाधनम्। नियतिः सर्वभूतानां नियोगेष्विह कारणम्॥
en: Time is the prime cause in this world, and the source of the accomplishment of actions. And Time it is that leads men to actions.

sn: न कर्ता कस्यचित् कश्चिन्नियोगेनापि चेश्वरः। स्वभावे वर्तते लोकस्तस्य कालः परायणम्॥
en: No one is the lord of another person, and no one leads him to actions. People are subject to their actions of previous existence and Time aids them.

sn: न कालः कालमत्येति न कालः परिहीयते। स्वभावं च समासाद्य न कश्चिदतिवर्तते॥
en: Even the Eternal being cannot withstand the ways of Time. He never decayeth-and no one else can withstand the course of Time.

sn: न कालस्यास्ति बन्धुत्वं न हेतुर्न पराक्रमः। न मित्रज्ञातिसम्बन्धः कारणं नात्मनोऽवशः॥
en: It has no friend, no cause and no one can overcome it. It has no kinsman, no relation; even it is not subject to itself.

sn: किं तु कालपरीणामो द्रष्टव्यः साधु पश्यता। धर्मश्चार्थश्च कामश्च कालक्रमसमाहिताः॥
en: The wise can perceive the work of Time. Piety, wealth and desire are all subject to it.

sn: इतः स्वां प्रकृतिं वाली गतः प्राप्तः क्रियाफलम्। सामदानार्थसंयोगैः पवित्रं प्लवगेश्वरः॥
en: Vāli, the lord of monkeys, has attained to his own true state, reaping the fruits of his actions, acquired by virtue of his royal accomplishments namely forgiveness and charity.

sn: स्वधर्मस्य च संयोगाज्जितस्तेन महात्मना। स्वर्गः परिगृहीतश्च प्राणानपरिरक्षता॥
en: The abode of the celestials, which was conquered by this high-souled one by his former piety, has now been occupied by him after resigning his body.

sn: एषा वै नियतिः श्रेष्ठा यां गतो हरियूथपः। तदलं परितापेन प्राप्तकालमुपास्यताम्॥
en: This is the best course of Time that has been attained to by the lord of monkey-herds. No more with lamentations therefore; do you perform the actions that are worthy of being performed on this occasion.

sn: वचनान्ते तु रामस्य लक्ष्मणः परवीरहा। अवदत् प्रश्रितं वाक्यं सुग्रीवं गतचेतसम्॥
en: After Rāma had spoken thus, Laksmana, the slayer of foes, addressed Sugrīva, senseless with grief, with the following sound words.

sn: कुरु त्वमस्य सुग्रीव प्रेतकार्यमनन्तरम्। ताराङ्गदाभ्यां सहितो वालिनो दहनं प्रति॥
en: Sugrīva, do you perform the funeral ceremonies of Vali along with Tārā and Angada.

sn: समाज्ञापय काष्ठानि शुष्काणि च बहूनि च। चन्दनानि च दिव्यानि वालिसंस्कारकारणात्॥
en: Do you collect for cremation many a dry fuel and celestial sandal.

sn: समाश्वासय दीनं त्वमङ्गदं दीनचेतसम्। मा भूर्बालिशबुद्धिस्त्वं त्वदधीनमिदं पुरम्॥
en: Do you console the unfortunate Angada, who is beside himself with grief. Do not conduct yourself like an ignorant person, for this city is now under you.

sn: अङ्गदस्त्वानयेन्माल्यं वस्त्राणि विविधानि च। घृतं तैलमथो गन्धान् यच्चात्र समनन्तरम्॥
en: Let Angada bring clothes, garlands, scents, clarified butter, oil and other necessary articles.

sn: त्वं तार शिबिकां शीघ्रमादायागच्छ सम्भ्रमात्। त्वरा गुणवती युक्ता ह्यस्मिन् काले विशेषतः॥
en: O Tārā, do you go and bring soon a conveyance; for speediness is a special virtue on an occasion like this.

sn: सज्जीभवन्तु प्लवगाः शिबिकावाहनोचिताः। समर्था बलिनश्चैव निहरिष्यन्ति वालिनम्॥
en: Let the monkeys dress themselves who can convey this hearse. The powerful and the capable only shall carry Vali.

sn: एवमुक्त्वा तु सुग्रीवं सुमित्रानन्दवर्धनः। तस्थौ भ्रातृसमीपस्थो लक्ष्मणः परवीरहा॥
en: Having thus addressed Sugriva, Laksmana, the enhancer of Sumitrā's joy and the destroyer of foes, stood before his elder brother.

sn: लक्ष्मणस्य वचः श्रुत्वा तारः सम्भ्रान्तमानसः। प्रविवेश गुहां शीघ्रं शिबिकासक्तमानसः॥
en: And hearing the words of Laksmana, the counsellor respectfully entered the cave with a view to bring the conveyance.

sn: आदाय शिबिकां तारः स तु पर्यापतत् पुनः। वानरैरुह्यमानां तां शूरैरुद्वनोचितैः॥
en: And taking that conveyance carried by the monkeys and worthy of being carried by the heroes, he issued out again of the cave.

sn: दिव्यां भद्रासनयुतां शिबिकां स्यन्दनोपमाम्। पक्षिकर्मभिराचित्रां दुमकर्मविभूषिताम् ॥
en: It had a celestial throne and was like to a warchariot and had trees and birds painted on it.

sn: आचितां चित्रपत्तीभिः सुनिविष्टां समन्ततः। विमानमिव सिद्धानां जालवातायनायुताम्॥
en: It was painted on all sides with the figures of foot soldiers, had latticed windows and was like to the car of the Siddhas-spacious and artistically and stoutly built by artizans with beautiful carvings like to a wooden hill.

sn: सुनियुक्तां विशालां च सुकृतां शिल्पिभिः कृताम्। दारुपर्वतकोपेतां चारुकर्मपरिष्कृताम्॥ वराभरणहारैश्च चित्रमाल्योपशोभिताम्। गुहागहनसंछन्नां रक्तचन्दनभूषिताम् ॥
en: It was ornamented with excellent ornaments and beautiful garlands, sprinkled with red sandal and skirted with strong ribs.

sn: पुष्पोषैः समभिच्छन्नां पद्ममालाभिरेव च। तरुणादित्यवर्णाभिमा॑जमानाभिरावृताम्॥
en: It was covered with flowers and lotus garlands, crusted with precious clothes and had the colour of the rising Sun.

sn: ईदृशी शिबिकां दृष्ट्वा रामो लक्ष्मणमब्रवीत्। क्षिप्रं विनीयतां वाली प्रेतकार्यं विधीयताम्॥
en: Beholding such a conveyance, Rāma spoke to Lakşmaņa, saying-Do you soon conduct the funeral service of Vāli,

sn: ततो वालिनमुद्यम्य सुग्रीवः शिबिकां तदा। आरोपयत विक्रोशनङ्गदेन सहैव तु॥
en: Thereupon Sugrīva, long with Angada, placing Väli on the conveyance, began to bewail.

sn: आरोग्य शिबिकां चैव वालिनं गतजीवितम्। अलंकारैश्च विविधैर्माल्यैर्वस्त्रैश्च भूषितम्॥
en: And placing the lifeless body of Vāli on it, he covered it with various ornaments, garlands, and clothes.

sn: आज्ञापयत् तदा राजा सुग्रीवः प्लवगेश्वरः। और्ध्वदेहीकमार्यस्य क्रियतामनुकूलतः॥
en: Thereat Sugrīva, the king of monkeys, ordered for the performance of Vāli's funeral rites.

sn: विश्राणयन्तो रत्नानि विविधानि बहूनि च। अग्रतः प्लवगा यान्तु शिबिका तदनन्तरम्॥
en: Let the monkeys go before, scattering many a precious jewel and let the conveyance follow them.

sn: राज्ञामृद्धिविशेषा हि दृश्यन्ते भुवि यादृशाः। तादृशैरिह कुर्वन्तु वानरा भर्तृसत्क्रियाम्॥
en: Let the monkeys perform the obsequies of our master with such grandeur as befits the riches of the kings on this earth, a

sn: तादृशं वालिनः क्षिप्रं प्राकुर्वन्नौदेहिकम्। अङ्गदं परिरभ्याशु तारप्रभृतयस्तथा॥
en: With view to perform the funeral ceremonies of Vāli, the counsellors and other monkeys, having lost their king and embraced Angada, proceeded weeping.

sn: क्रोशन्तः प्रययुः सर्वे वानरा हतबान्धवाः। ततः प्रणिहीताः सर्वा वानर्योऽस्य वशानुगाः॥ चुक्रुशुर्वीरवीरेति भूयः क्रोशन्ति ताः प्रियम्। ताराप्रभृतयः सर्वा वानर्यो हतबान्धवाः॥ अनुजग्मुश्च भर्तारं क्रोशन्त्यः करुणस्वनाः।
en: And other subject monkeys followed them. And all other she-monkeys, headed by Tārā, having lost their lord, bewailed, exclaiming again and again-O hero, O hero. And they, thus bewailing piteously, followed their lord.

sn: तासां रुदितशब्देन वानरीणां वनान्तरे॥ वनानि गिरयश्चैव विक्रोशन्तीव सर्वतः।
en: In response to the bewailings of she-monkeys, hills and forests, as if, bewailed on all sides.

sn: पुलिने गिरिनद्यास्तु विविक्ते जलसंवृते॥ चितां चक्रुः सुबहवो वानरा वनचारिणः। अवरोप्य ततः स्कन्धाच्छिबिकां वानरोत्तमाः॥
