sn: ततः किलकिलां चक्कुर्लक्ष्मणं प्रेक्ष्य वानराः। प्रसादयन्तस्तं क्रुद्धं भयमोहितचेतसः॥
en: Beholding Lakşmaņa highly enraged, the monkeys, possessed by fear, began to make noise as they were welcoming him.

sn: ते महौघनिभं दृष्ट्वा वज्राशनिसमस्वनम्। सिंहनादं समं चक्रुर्लक्ष्मणस्य समीपतः॥
en: They, approaching Lakşmaņa began to set up a terrible roar like to thunder and resembling the uproar of lions and the noise of water-falls.

sn: तेन शब्देन महता प्रत्युबुध्यत वानरः। मदविह्वलताम्राक्षो व्याकुलः स्रग्विभूषणः॥
en: By that terrible sound awoke that monkeychief, having coppery eyes, agitated, adorned with garlands and possessed by liquor.

sn: अथाङ्गदवचः श्रुत्वा तेनैव च समागतौ। मन्त्रिणौ वानरेन्द्रस्य सम्मतोदारदर्शनौ।॥ प्लक्षश्चैव प्रभावश्च मन्त्रिणावर्थधर्मयोः। वक्तुमुच्चावचं प्राप्तं लक्ष्मणं तौ शशंसतुः॥
en: Hearing the words of Angada, the tow counsellors of Sugrīva, intelligent and of magnificent looks, along with him, approached that lord of monkeys. And those two ministers Yaksa and Prabhava, to give him proper counsels, informed (that monkey-chief) of the arrival of Lakşmaņa.

sn: प्रसादयित्वा सुग्रीवं वचनैः सार्थनिश्चितैः। आसीनं पर्युपासीनो यथा शक्रं मरुत्पतिम्॥ सत्यसंधौ महाभागौ भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ। मनुष्यभावं सम्प्राप्तौ राज्याही राज्यदायिनौ ॥ तयोरेको धनुष्पाणिभरि तिष्ठति लक्ष्मणः। यस्य भीताः प्रवेपन्तो नादान् मुञ्चन्ति वानराः॥
en: Satisfying Sugrīva with words pointing out his welfare, they sitting by him, spoke to that lord of wind resembling the king of celestials, saying: Of those two great and truthful brothers Rāma and Lakşmaņa, who are born as men, worthy of attaining to kingdom and who have gained for you your kingdom, Laksmana, with a bow in his hand, is waiting at your gate. And afraid of whom, the monkeys, trembling, are setting up terrible roars.

sn: स एष राघवभ्राता लक्ष्मणो वाक्यसारथिः। व्यवसायरथः प्राप्तस्तस्य रामस्य शासनात्॥
en: That Laksmana, Raghava's brother, having words for his charioteer, and perseverance for his chariot, has approached you at his brother's command.

sn: अयं च तनयो राजस्ताराया दयितोऽङ्गदः। लक्ष्मणेन सकाशं ते प्रेषितस्त्वरयानघ॥
en: O blameless king, by that Laksmana-Tara's darling, Angada has been despatched to you.

sn: सोऽयं रोषपरीताक्षो द्वारि तिष्ठति वीर्यवान्। वानरान् वानरपते चक्षुषा निर्दहनिव॥
en: O king, of monkeys, that highly powerful one, having his eyes full of ire, is waiting at your gate, as if burning down with his eyes all the monkeys.

sn: तस्य मूर्जा प्रणामं त्वं सपुत्रः सहबान्धवः। गच्छ शीघ्रं महाराज रोषो ह्यद्योपशाम्यताम्॥
en: O king, along with your children and friends do you repair to him speedily and bowing to him with your head down do you pacify his wrath.

sn: यथा हि रामो धर्मात्मा तत्कुरुष्व समाहितः। राजस्तिष्ठ स्वसमये भव सत्यप्रतिश्रवः॥
en: And do you, O king, with a composed heart, perform what the virtuous-souled Rāma has ordered you to do and thus fulfil your promise.

sn: अङ्गदस्य वचः श्रुत्वा सुग्रीवः सचिवैः सह। लक्ष्मणं कुपितं श्रुत्वा मुमोचासनमात्मवान्॥
en: Hearing the words of Angada as well as of Laksmana's wrath, the self-controlled Sugriva along with his counsellors, left his seat.

sn: स च तानब्रवीद् वाक्यं निश्चित्य गुरुलाघवम्। मन्त्रज्ञान् मन्त्रकुशलो मन्त्रेषु परिनिष्ठितः॥
en: Ascertaining the weight and lightness of the present occasion, that one, expert in counsels and abiding by their advice spoke to the expert counsellors, saying.

sn: न मे दुर्व्याहृतं किंचित्रापि मे दुरनुष्ठितम्। लक्ष्मणो राघवभ्राता क्रुद्धः किमिति चिन्तये॥
en: I have not done him any wrong, nor have I spoken to him any improper word. I do not know why Rāghava's brother Laksmana has become offended with me.

sn: असुहृद्भिर्ममामित्रैर्नित्यमन्तरदर्शिभिः। मम दोषानसम्भूताऽश्रावितो राघवानुजः॥
en: Lakşmaņa has been falsely apprised of my imaginary weakness by my enemies, always looking to my dark sides.

sn: अत्र तावद् यथाबुद्धिः सर्वैरेव यथाविधि। भावस्य निश्चयस्तावद् विज्ञेयो निपुणं शनैः॥
en: It behoveth you all, to ascertain now speedily according to your knowledge and right understanding (the cause of Laksmana's wrath).

sn: न खल्वस्ति मम त्रासो लक्ष्मणानापि राघवात्। मित्रं स्वस्थानकुपितं जनयत्येव सम्भ्रमम्॥
en: I do not fear Lakşmaņa or Rāghava; but friends enraged without any cause do invariable produce fear.

sn: सर्वथा सुकरं मित्रं दुष्करं प्रतिपालनम्। अनित्यत्वात् तु चित्तानां प्रीतिरल्पेऽपि भिद्यते॥
en: It is easy to contract friendship but very difficult to sustain it; for owing to the fickleness of our minds, a very slight cause bring about separation.

sn: अतोनिमित्तं त्रस्तोऽहं रामेण तु महात्मना। यन्ममोपकृतं शक्यं प्रतिकर्तुं न तन्मया॥
en: I have not done him any good proportionate to what the high-souled Rāma had done for me; and it is for this reason that I am afraid of him.

sn: सुग्रीवेणैवमुक्ते तु हनूमान् हरिपुंगवः । उवाच स्वेन तर्केण मध्ये वानरमन्त्रिणाम्॥
en: Being thus addressed by Sugrīva-Hanumān, the foremost of monkey-counsellors spoke, according to his own understanding, saying.

sn: सर्वथा नैतदाश्चर्ये यत् त्वं हरिगणेश्वर। न विस्मरसि सुस्निग्धमुपकारं कृतं शुभम्॥
en: It is no wonder, O lord of monkeys, that you had not forgot the unexpected benefit, (you hadst received at the hands of Rāma).

sn: राघवेण तु वीरेण भयमुत्सृज्य दूरतः। त्वत्प्रियार्थं हतो वाली शक्रतुल्यपराक्रमः॥ सर्वथा प्रणयात् क्रुद्धो राघवो नात्र संशयः। भ्रातरं सम्प्रहीतवाँल्लक्ष्मणं लक्ष्मिवर्धनम्॥
en: To encompass your well-being, Vali, powerful as the Lord of celestials, was fearlessly destroyed by the heroic Rāghava. There is not the least doubt, that Rāghava, out of love, is enraged with you, and has despatched his younger brother Lakşmaņa, the enhancer of prosperity.

sn: त्वं प्रमत्तो न जानीषे कालं कालविदा वर। फुल्लसप्तच्छदश्यामा प्रवृत्ता तु शरच्छुभा॥
en: O you foremost of those conversant with time, the auspicious autumn, green with Saptchada flowers, has set in and you, given up to enjoyments, does not perceive it.

sn: निर्मलग्रहनक्षत्रा द्यौः प्रणष्टबलाहका। प्रसन्नाश्च दिशः सर्वाः सरितश्च सरांसि च॥.
en: The sky, having the clouds removed, is full of clear stars and planets. The quarters, the ponds and rivers are all clear.

sn: प्राप्तमुद्योगकालं तु नावैषि हरिपुंगव। त्वं प्रमत्त इति व्यक्तं लक्ष्मणोऽयमिहागतः॥
en: O best of monkeys, finding you forgetful, Lakṣmaṇa has come here to inform you that the proper time has arrived.

sn: आर्तस्य हृतदारस्य परुषं पुरुषान्तरात्। वचनं मर्षणीयं ते राघवस्य महात्मनः॥
en: Do you patiently hear all these harsh words of the high-souled Rāma, racked with sorrow and separated from his spouse, which Laksmana, shall relate to you.

sn: कृतापराधस्य हि ते नान्यत् पश्याम्यहं क्षमम्। अन्तरेणाञ्जलिं बद्ध्वा लक्ष्मणस्य प्रसादनात्॥
en: You have acted improperly towards him, and I do not find any thing tending to your welfare but your satisfying Lakşmana with folded hands.

sn: मन्त्रिभिर्वाच्यो ह्यवश्यं पार्थिवो हितम्। इत एव भयं त्यक्त्वा ब्रवीम्यवधृतं वचः॥
en: The kings should be addressed with auspicious words by their counsellors always ministering to them proper counsels. And it is for this reason, I am addressing you with these sound words.

sn: अभिक्रुद्धः समर्थो हि चापमुद्यम्य राघवः। सदेवासुरगन्धर्वं वशे स्थापयितुं जगत्॥
en: Rāghava, taking up his bow, while enraged, can bring under subjection the entire world, inhabited by by the celestials, Asuras and Gandharvas.

sn: न स क्षमः कोपयितुं यः प्रसाद्यः पुनर्भवेत्। पूर्वोपकारं स्मरता कृतज्ञेन विशेषतः॥
en: Remembering his former service, it does not behove you, grateful as you are, to excite his wrath, who should be pleased again.

sn: तस्य मूर्जा प्रणम्य त्वं सपुत्रः ससुहृज्जनः। राजस्तिष्ठ स्वसमये भर्तुर्भार्येव तद्वशे॥
en: Bowing to him, with your children and friends, do you, O king, satisfying your promise, seek his shelter like to a wife placing herself under the control of her husband.

sn: न रामरामानुजशासनं त्वया कपीन्द्र युक्तं मनसाऽप्यपोहितुम्। मनो हि ते ज्ञास्यति मानुषं बलं सराघवस्यास्य सुरेन्द्रवर्चसः॥
en: O lord of monkeys, it does not behove you, to neglect even in thought, the behests of Rāma and his younger brother; for you are fully aware of the prowess of Rāghava like to the lord of celestials, and passing human power.

sn: अथ प्रतिसमादिष्टो लक्ष्मणः परवीरहा। प्रविवेश गुहां रम्यां किष्किन्धां रामशासनात्॥
en: Thereupon, Laksmana, the slayer of foes, commanded, entered, at the behest of Rāma, the pleasant city of Kişkindhā situated in the centre of caves.

sn: द्वारस्था हरयस्तत्र महाकाया महाबलाः। बभूवर्लक्ष्मणं दृष्ट्वः सर्वे प्राञ्जलयः स्थिताः॥
en: Beholding Lakşınaņa, the highly powerful monkeys, having huge persons and waiting at the gate, stood all with folded hands.

sn: निःश्वसन्तं तु तं दृष्ट्वा क्रुद्धं दशरथात्मजम्। बभूवुर्हरयस्त्रास्ता न चैनं पर्यवारयन्॥
en: And seeing Dasaratha's son highly enraged and sighing again and again, the monkeys stood silent and did not interrupt him.

sn: स तां रत्नमयीं दिव्यां श्रीमान् पुष्पितकाननाम्। रम्यां रत्नसमाकीर्णां ददर्श महतीं गुहाम्॥ हर्म्यप्रासादसम्बाधां नानारत्नोपशोभिताम् सर्वकामफलैर्वृक्षैः पुष्पितैरुपशोभिताम्॥ देवगन्धर्वपुत्रैश्च वानरैः कामरूपिभिः। दिव्यमाल्याम्बरधरैः शोभितां प्रियदर्शनैः॥
en: The graceful Lakşmaņa espied that huge picturesque and celestial cave adorned with jewels and flowery gardens. It was filled with palatial buildings, various jewels and flowery trees, producing at all times wished for fruits. It was beautified with good-looking monkeyschildren of the celestials and Gandharabas wearing celestial garlands and clothes and assuming shapes at will.

sn: चन्द्रनागुरुपद्मानां गन्धैः सुरभिगन्धिताम्। : मैरेयाणां मधूनां च सम्मोहितमहापथाम्॥
en: It was fragrant with the sweet smell of sandal wood, Aguru and lotuses and its highway were equally fragrant with the smell of honey.

sn: विन्ध्यमेरुगिरिप्रख्यैः प्रासादै कभूमिभिः। ददर्श गिरिनद्यश्च विमलास्तत्र राघवः॥
en: And Lakşmaņa beheld there many spacious buildings like to the hills Vindhya and Meru and rivers of clear water.

sn: अङ्गदस्य गृहं रम्यं मैन्दस्य द्विविदस्य च। गवयस्य गवाक्षस्य गजस्य शरभस्य च॥ विद्युन्मालेश्च सम्पातेः सूर्याक्षस्य हनूमतः। वीरबाहोः सुबाहोश्च नलस्य च महात्मनः॥ कुमुदस्य सुषेणस्य तारजाम्बवतोस्तथा। दधिवक्त्रस्य नीलस्य सुपाटलसुनेत्रयोः॥ एतेषां कपिमुख्यानां राजमार्गे महात्मनाम्। ददर्श गृहमुख्यानि महासाराणि लक्ष्मणः॥ पाण्डुराभ्रप्रकाशानि गन्धमाल्ययुतानि च। प्रभूतधनधान्यानि स्त्रीरत्नैः शोभितानि च॥
en: And he also surveyed the picturesque dwellings of Angada, Mainda, Divida, Gavaya, Gavaksa, Gaja, Sarava, Vidhutmali, Sampati Suryakşa, Hanumāna, Beerabāhu, Subāhu, Nala, Kumuda, Susena, Tara, Jambavan, Dadhivaktra, Neela, Sunetra and Supātala like to sable clouds adorned with excellent garlands, filled with rice and jewels and beautiful damsels.

sn: पाण्डुरेण तु शैलेन परिक्षिप्तं दुरासदम्। वानरेन्द्रगृहं रम्यं महेन्द्रसदनोपमम्॥ शुक्लैः प्रासादशिखरैः कैलासशिखरोपमैः। सर्वकामफलैर्वृक्षैः पुष्पितैरुपशोभितम्॥ महेन्द्रदत्तैः श्रीमद्भिर्नीलजीमूतसंनिभैः। दिव्यपुष्पफलैर्वृक्षैः शीतच्छायैर्मनोरमैः॥ हरिभिः संवृतद्वारं बलिभिः शस्त्रपाणिभिः। दिव्यमाल्यावृतं शुभ्रं तप्तकाञ्चनतोरणम्॥ सुग्रीवस्य गृहं रम्यं प्रविवेश महाबलः। अवार्यमाणः सौमित्रिर्महाभ्रमिव भास्करः॥
en: Unobstructed the highly powerful Saumitri entered the picturesque abode of Sugrīva like to the Sun entering into a collection of dense clouds. The abode of this lord of monkeys was like to the palace of the Lord of celestials, ornamented with the tops of white buildings resembling the summits of the Kailasa hill and flowery trees producing at all times, wished-for fruits, covered with beautiful trees having cool shades and bearing celestial fruits and flowers resembling the molten-god.

sn: स सप्त कक्ष्या धर्मात्मा यानासनसमावृताः। ददर्श सुमहद्गुप्तं ददर्शान्त:पुरं महत्॥ हैमराजतपर्यकैर्बहुभिश्च वरासनैः। महार्हास्तरणोपेतैस्तत्र तत्र समावृतम्॥
en: And that virtuous-souled one, crossing the seven rooms filled with conveyances and seats beheld the secret apartment (of that monkeychief), having many a gold and silver bed-steads with excellent coverlets and fine seats.

sn: प्रविशन्नेव सततं शुश्राव मधुरस्वनम्। तन्त्रीगीतसमाकीर्णं समतालपदाक्षरम्॥
en: No sooner had he entered the inner apartment than he heard a musical sound, well-measured and accompanied by the music of the stringed instrument.

sn: बह्वीश्च विविधाकारा रूपयौवनगर्विताः। स्त्रियः सुग्रीवभवने ददर्श स महाबलः॥
en: And that highly powerful one beheld in the abode of Sugrīva many a beautiful damsel proud of their youth and beauty sprung from respectable families, adorned with splendid ornaments, engaged in stringing excellent garlands.

sn: दृष्ट्वाभिजनसम्पन्नास्तत्र माल्यकृतस्रजः। वनमाल्यकृतव्यग्रा भूषणोत्तमभूषिताः॥ नातृप्तान् नाति चाव्यग्रान् नानुदात्तपरिच्छदान्। सुग्रीवानुचरांश्चापि लक्षयामास लक्ष्मणः॥
en: And he observed Sugrīva's servants, well fed, contented, not hurry in offering their services and without splendid ornaments.

sn: कूजितं नू पुराणां च काञ्चीनां निःस्वनं तता स निशम्य ततः श्रीमान् सौमित्रिर्लज्रितोऽभवत्॥
en: Hearing the sounds of women's girdles and their Nupurs*, the graceful Lakşınaņa became highly ashamed. *An ornament for their toes or feet.

sn: रोषवेगप्रकुपितः श्रुत्वा चाभरणस्वनम्। चकार जायास्वनं वीरो दिशः शब्देन पूरयन्॥
en: And highly enraged at the sound of the ornaments, the hero filled all the quarters with the twang of his bow.

sn: चारित्रेण महाबाहुरपकृष्टः स लक्ष्मणः। तस्थावेकान्तमाश्रित्य रामकोपसमन्वितः॥
en: Lakşmaņa of mighty arms stood silent in a nook, thinking of his improper conduct of entering into (Sugriva's) seraglio, albeit he was wrought up with ire in consequence of Sugrīva's neglecting Rama's service.

sn: तेन चापस्वनेनाथ सुग्रीवः प्लवगाधिपः। विज्ञायागमनं त्रस्तः स चचाल वरासनात्॥
en: Thereupon Sugrīva, the lord of monkeys, being apprised of Laksmana's approach by the twang of his bow and terrified, trembled on his throne, and thought aside.

sn: अङ्गदेन यथा मह्यं पुरस्तात् प्रतिवेदितम्। सुव्यक्तमेव सम्प्राप्तः सौमित्रिर्धातृवत्सलः॥
en: Forsooth has Saumitri, fond of his brother, come, whose approach was announced by Argada before,

sn: अङ्गदेन समाख्यातो ज्यास्वनेन च वानरः। बुबुधे लक्ष्मणं प्राप्तं मुखं चास्य व्यशुष्यत॥
en: Informed before by Angada of his approach, and made doubly sure by the twang of the bow, that monkey came to know of Lakşmaņa's arrival and turned pale.

sn: ततस्तारां हरिश्रेष्ठः सुग्रीवः प्रियदर्शनाम्। उवाच हितमव्यग्रस्त्राससम्भ्रान्तमानसः॥
en: Thereupon Sugrīva, the foremost of monkeys, wrought up with fear, addressed the fine looking Tārā with the following well-meaning words.

sn: किं नु रुट्कारणं सुभ्र प्रकृत्या मृदुमानसः। सरोष इव सम्प्राप्तो येनायं राघवानुजः॥
en: O beautiful lady, did you know, why has the mild-natured younger brother of Rāma, arrived here enraged?

sn: किं पश्यसि कुमारस्य रोषस्थानमनिन्दिते। न खल्वकारणे कोपमाहरेन्नरपुङ्गवः॥
en: O blameless lady, did you perceive any cause of the Prince's wrath? Forsooth, that best of men, is not enraged for a slight cause.

sn: यद्यस्य कृतमस्माभिर्बुध्यसे किंचिदप्रियम्। तद्बुद्ध्या सम्प्रधाशु क्षिप्रमेवाभिधीयताम्॥
en: Considering aright, did you speedily inform me if I have performed any improper act towards Rāma.

sn: अथवा स्वयमेवैनं द्रष्टुमर्हसि भामिनि। वचनैः सान्त्वयुक्तैश्च प्रसादयितुमर्हसि॥
en: O fine lady, do you approach him in person and pacify him with soothing words.

sn: त्वद्दर्शने विशुद्धात्मा न स्म कोपं करिष्यति। नहि स्त्रीषु महात्मानः क्वचित् कुर्वन्ति दारुणम्॥
en: Beholding you, that pure-souled one shall not be worked with ire; great men do never behave roughly towards the females.

sn: त्वया सान्त्वैरुपक्रान्तं प्रसन्नेन्द्रियमानसम्। ततः मलपत्राक्षं द्रक्ष्याम्यहमरिंदमम्॥
en: Approaching him do you console him and thereafter I shall see that conqueror of foes having eyes resembling lotus-petals.

sn: सा प्रस्खलन्ती मदविह्वलाक्षी प्रलम्बकाञ्चीगुणहेमसूत्रा। सलक्षणा लक्ष्मणसंनिधानं जगाम तारा नमिताङ्गयष्टिः॥
en: Thereupon Tārā, with faltering feet and eyes wild with wine, the golden chains of her zone flowing (about her her hips),-graced with auspicious marks, saught Laksmana's presence with downcast looks.

sn: स तां समीक्ष्यैव हरीशपत्नी तस्थावुदासीनतया महात्मा। अवाङ्मुखोऽभून्मनुजेन्द्रपुत्रः स्त्रीसंनिकर्षाद् विनिवृत्तकोपः॥
en: Beholding Tărā, the queen of the lord of monkeys, Laksmana, the high-souled son of a king, restraining his anger on the approach of a female, stood with his head hung down, conducting himself like an ascetic.

sn: सा पानयोगाच्च निवृत्तलज्जा दृष्टिप्रसादाच्च सरेन्द्रसूनोः। वाक्यं महार्थं परिसान्त्वरूपम्॥
en: Renouncing modesty under the influence of liquor, and finding the king's son well pleased, Tārā spoke to Lakşmaņa, bold and loving words, in order to console him.

sn: किं कोपमूलं मनुजेन्द्रपुत्र कस्ते न संतिष्ठति वानिदेशे। कः शुष्कवृक्षं वनमापतन्तं दावाग्निमासीदति निर्विशङ्कः॥
en: O son of a king, what is the cause of your wrath? Who is there who has not abode by your commands? Who can remain without anxiety, beholding fire in a forest filled with dried trees?

sn: स तस्या वचनं श्रुत्वा सान्त्वपूर्वमशङ्कितः। भूयः प्रणयदृष्टार्थं लक्ष्मणो वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
en: Hearing the soothing words of Tārā, Laks maņa, undaunted, spoke again, greatly manifesting his friendship.

sn: किमयं कामवृत्तस्ते लुप्तधर्मार्थसंग्रहः। भर्ता भर्तहिते युक्ते न चैनमवबुध्यसे॥
en: O you intent on your husband's welfare, did you not perceive that your husband is by and by losing piety and wealth, being addicted to amorcus enjoyments.?

sn: न चिन्तयति राज्यार्थं सोऽस्माशोकपरायणान्। सामान्यपरिषत्तारे काममेवोपसेवते॥
en: O Tāră, your husband does not think of us who are moved with sorrow—but is addicted to sensual enjoyments only, being surrounded by parasites.

sn: स मासांश्चतुरः कृत्वा प्रमाणं प्लवगेश्वरः। व्यतीतांस्तान् मदोदग्रो विहरन् नावबुध्यते॥
en: (Having promised that he would institute enquiries about Sītā after four months), that lord of monkeys has well-nigh spent the entire period, being influenced by liquor and addicted to enjoyments along with you.

sn: नहि धर्मार्थसिद्ध्यर्थं पानमेवं प्रशस्यते। पानादर्थश्च कामश्च धर्मश्च परिहीयते॥
en: For the attainment of piety and wealth, drinking is not a proper course. It is by drinking that people lose piety, wealth and desire.

sn: धर्मलोपो महांस्तावत् कृते ह्यप्रतिकुर्वतः। अर्थलोपश्च मित्रस्य नाशे गुणवतो महान्॥
en: He who does not return the services of his benefactor, loseth piety. He who who loseth friendship with a qualified friend, loseth wealth.

sn: मित्रं ह्यर्थगुणश्रेष्ठं सत्यधर्मपरायणम्। तद्वयं तु परित्यक्तं न तु धर्मे व्यवस्थितम्॥
en: He is the best friend who is gifted with wealth and is truthful; and your husband has relinquished such a friend gifted with these two qualities.

sn: तदेवं प्रस्तुते कार्ये कार्यमस्माभिरुत्तरम्। तत् कार्यं कार्यतत्त्वज्ञे त्वमुदाहर्तुमर्हसि ॥
en: And, therefore, he does not abide by the virtue of preserving friendship. O you expert in business, this being the case, do you advice us as to what we should do.

sn: सा तस्य धर्मार्थसमाधियुक्तं निशम्य वाक्यं मधुरस्वभावम्। तारा गतार्थे मनुजेन्द्रकार्ये विश्वासयुक्तं तमुवाच भूयः। ५०॥
en: Hearing the sweet words of Lakşmaņa consonant with piety and wealth, Tārā again addressed him about Räma's business, yet remaining unaccomplished with words inspiring confidence.

sn: न कोपकालः क्षितिपालपुत्र न चापि कोपः स्वजने विधेयः। त्वदर्थकामस्य जनस्य तस्य प्रमादमप्यर्हसि वीर सोढुम्॥
en: O son of a king, this is not the time for displaying your wrath; it is not proper to be angry with one's own friends. O hero, it behoveth you to put up with the error of him who has your welfare in view.

sn: कोपं कथं नाम गुणप्रकृष्टः कुमार कुर्यादपकृष्टसत्त्वे। कस्त्वद्विधः कोपवशं हि गच्छेत् सत्त्वावरुद्धस्तपसः प्रसूतिः॥
en: O prince, who, accomplished with excellent virtues, gets enraged with one of inferior merits? O prince, who, like you, an offspring of asceticism, is worked up with ire against the virtue of forgiveness?

sn: र्जानामि कार्यस्य च कालसङ्गम्। स्तच्चापि जानामि यदत्र कार्यम् ॥
en: I know the cause of the) wrath of that heroic monkey's friend. I know the time for action. I know what you had done for us. I know what is due from us to you.

sn: तच्चापि जानामि तथाविषा बलं नरश्रेष्ठ शरीरजस्य। जानामि यस्मिंश्च जनेऽवबद्धं कामेन सुग्रीवमसक्तमद्य ॥
en: And, O foremost of men, I also know the irresistible force of Kāma. I know by whom Sugrīva has been taken captive, and that his heart is not now in the work.

sn: न कामतन्त्रे तव बुद्धिरस्ति त्वं वै यथा मन्युवर्श प्रपन्नः। ववेक्षते कामरतिर्मनुष्यः॥
en: As you had come under the governance of anger, your mind has not felt the influence of desire. Even a human being that has conceived love, does not stay for place or time or interest

sn: तं कामवृत्तं मम संनिकृष्टं कामाभियोगाच्च विमुक्तलज्जम्। स्त्वद्भातरं वानरवंशनाथम्॥
en: Do you forgive that lord of the monkey race, your brother influenced by carnality, who is by you, and who through the urgency of lust, has banished shame.

sn: महर्षयो धर्मतपोऽभिरामाः कामानुकामाः प्रतिबद्धमोहाः। अयं प्रकृत्या चपलः कपिस्तु कथं न सज्जेत सुखेषु राजा॥
en: Even Maharșis finding delight in religion and asceticism, setting their hearts upon satisfying lust, (ultimately) become fast bound by ignorance. But this is a monkey, volatile by nature, and has, further more, been enjoying regal state-why should he not act thus?

sn: इत्येवमुक्त्वा वचनं महार्थं सा वानरी लक्ष्मणमप्रमेयम्। पुनः सखेदं मदविह्वलाक्षी भर्तुर्हितं वाक्यमिदं बभाषे॥
en: Having thus said Lakşmaņa of immeasurable intelligence words fraught with high import, that female monkey, her eyes drooping with languor, again sadly spoke in this wise for the behoof of her husband.

sn: उद्योगस्तु चिराज्ञप्तः सुग्रीवेण नरोत्तम। कामस्यापि विधेयेन तवार्थप्रतिसाधने । ५९।।
en: O foremost of men, although Sugrīva has come under the sway of desire, he has, to secure your good, ere this issued orders for preparations to be made.

sn: आगता हि महावीर्या हरयः कामरूपिणः। कोटी: शतसहस्राणि नानाजगनिवासिनः॥
en: And monkeys by hundreds and thousands and koțis, inhabiting various mountains, possessed of exceeding prowess, have already arrived (here). to

sn: तदागच्छ महाबाहो चारित्रं रक्षितं त्वया। अच्छलं मित्रभावेन सतां दारावलोकनम्॥
en: Do you therefore, O mighty-armed one, come. (Having rushed towards the inner apartment), you had not suffered in character. For the good to behold others' wives in a friendly spirit, cannot bring on unrighteousness.

sn: तारया चाभ्यनुज्ञातस्त्वरया वापि चोदितः। प्रविवेश महाबाहुरभ्यन्तरमरिंदमः॥
en: Permitted by Tārā, that long-arined repressor of urged on by (the required) speed, entered the inner apartment.

sn: ततः सुग्रीवमासीनं काञ्चने परमासने। महार्हास्तरणोपेते ददर्शादित्यसंनिभम्॥ दिव्याभरणचित्राङ्गं दिव्यरूपं यशस्विनम्। दिव्यामाल्याम्बरधरं महेन्द्रमिव दुर्जयम्॥
en: There seated on a superb seat spread with a costly carpet, he found Sugrīva resembling the sun himself, his person decked with noble ornaments, of a dignified presence, famous, wearing gay garlands and attire, invincible like to the great Indra.

sn: दिव्याभरणमालाभिः प्रसादाभिः समावृतम्। संरब्धतररक्ताक्षो बभूवान्तकसंनिभः॥
en: And surrounded by dames adorned with elegant ornaments and wreaths, Sugrīva with his eyes still more reddened in wrath, looked like the destroyer himself.

sn: रुमां तु वीरः परिरभ्य गाढं वरासनस्थो वरहेमवर्णः। ददर्श सौमित्रिमदीनसत्त्वं विशालनेत्रः स विशालनेत्रम्॥
en: Then deeply embracing Umā, the large-eyed hero of the hue of fine gold, seated on an excellent seat, saw the powerful Saumitri having expansive eyes.

sn: तमप्रतिहतं क्रुद्धं प्रविष्टं पुरुषर्षभम्। सुग्रीवो लक्ष्मणं दृष्ट्वा बभूव व्यथितेन्द्रियः॥
en: Seeing that foremost of men, Laksmana, exercised with wrath, as he entered in without let, Sugrīva was seized with sadness.

sn: क्रुद्धं निःश्वसमानं तं प्रदीप्तमिव तेजसा। भ्रातुर्व्यसनसंतप्तं दृष्ट्वा दशरथात्मजम्॥ उत्पपात हरिश्रेष्ठो हित्वा सौवर्णमासनम्। महान्महेन्द्रस्य यथा स्वलंकृत इव ध्वजः॥
en: And seeing Dasaratha's son, wroth, and breathing hard, and flaming up in energy, and burning in consequence of the calamity that had overtaken his brother, that chief of monkeys started up, leaving his golden seat, like to the mighty ornamented standard of the great Indra.

sn: उत्पतन्तमनूत्पेतूरुमाप्रभृतयः स्त्रियः। सुग्रीवं गगने पूर्णं चन्द्रं तारागणा इव॥
en: And as Sugrīva rose up, Umā and the other females rose up, like to stars appearing in the sky when the full moon has risen.

sn: संरक्तनयनः श्रीमान् संचचार कृताञ्जलिः। बभूवावस्थितस्तत्र कल्पवृक्षो महानिव ॥
en: And with eyes reddened, and his hands folded, the graceful Sugrīva came (before Laks maņa) and stood there like a mighty Kalpa tree.

sn: रुमाद्वितीयं सुग्रीवं नारीमध्यगतं स्थितम्। अब्रवील्लक्ष्मणः क्रुद्धः सतारं शंशिनं यथा॥
en: And the wrathful Lakşmaņa spoke to Sugrīva stationed among women, having Umā for his second, and resembling the moon with the stars, saying.

sn: सत्त्वाभिजनसम्पन्नः सानुक्रोशो जितेन्द्रियः। कृतज्ञः सत्यवादी च राजा लोके महीयते॥
en: The king that is nobly endowed by heredily, and is kind, that has subdued his senses, and is grateful and truth telling, obtains renown in this world.

sn: यस्तु राजा स्थितोऽधर्मे मित्राणामुपकारिणाम्। मिथ्या प्रतिज्ञां कुरुते को नृशंसतरस्ततः॥
en: And who is more wicked than that king who, rooted in unrighteousness, makes false promises to friends intent upon his welfare?

sn: शतमश्वानृते हन्ति सहस्रं तु गवानृते आत्मानं स्वजनं हन्ति पुरुषः पुरुषानृते॥
en: He that speaks a falsehood with reference to a horse, becomes guilty of the deaths of an hundred horses: he committing himself to a falsehood relative to a cow, reapeth the demerit of slaying a thousand kine; while he that uttereth an untruth touching a person, destroys self as well as his kindred.

sn: पूर्वं कृतार्थो मित्राणां न तत्प्रतिकरोति यः। कृतघ्नः सर्वभूतानां स वध्यः प्लवगेश्वर॥
en: That ungrateful might that having at first attained benefit at the hands of his friends, does not requite it, is, O lord of monkeys, worthy of being slain by all creatures.

sn: गीतोऽयं ब्रह्मणा श्लोकः सर्वलोकनमस्कृतः। दृष्ट्वा कृतघ्नं क्रुद्धेन तन्निबोध प्लवङ्गम॥
en: Seeing an ingrate wretch, the wrathful Brahmā sang the (previous) śloka, bowed down to by all the worlds.

sn: गोध्ने चैव सुरापे च चौरे भग्नव्रते तथा। निष्कृतिर्विहिता सद्भिः कृतघ्ने नास्ति निष्कृतिः॥
en: Do you understand that, O monkey. The pious provide deliverance for the cow-killer, the winebiber, the thief, and the violator of vows; but for the ungrateful person there is no deliverance whatever.

sn: अनार्यस्त्वं कृतघ्नश्च मिथ्यावादी च वानर। पूर्वं कृतार्थो रामस्य न तत्प्रतिकरोषि यत्॥
en: You are ignoble and ungrateful and lying, O monkey, since, having been formerly benefited by Rāma, you did not requite his services.

sn: ननु नाम कृतार्थेन त्वया रामस्य वानर। सीताया मार्गणे यत्नः कर्तव्यः : कृतमिच्छता॥
en: Having been benefited by Rāma, you, anxious to repay his kindness, should exert yourself in search of Sita.

sn: स त्वं ग्राम्येषु भोगेषु सक्तो मिथ्याप्रतिश्रवः। न त्वां रामो विजानीते सधैं मण्डूकराविणम्॥
en: But, of false promises, you had been indulging in gross enjoyments,-nor does Rāma know you for a serpent, croaking like a frog*. *Crying through the voice of the frog in its mouth. Another meaning is, croaking like a frog, to allure frog to it.

sn: महाभागेन रामेण पापः करुणवेदिना। हरीणां प्रापितो राज्यं त्वं दुरात्मा पहात्मना॥
en: A sinful wretch and of wicked soul, you had obtained the kingdom of the monkeys through the agency of the eminently virtuous, kind and high-souled Rāma.

sn: कृतं चेन्नातिजानीषे राघवस्य महात्मनः सद्यस्त्वं निशितैर्भाणैर्हतो द्रक्ष्यसि वालिनम्॥
en: You did not acknowledge the good offices rendered to you by the high-souled Rāghava; and therefore, slain by means of sharpened shafts, you shall soon see Vali.

sn: न स संकुचितः पन्था येन वाली हतो गतः। समये तिष्ठ सुग्रीव मा वालिपथमन्वगाः॥
en: The way that has been wended by the slain Vali, is not yet narrowed. Do you, O Sugriva, desist in time: do not walk in the wake of Vāli.

sn: च्छरांश्च तान् पश्यसि वज्रसंनिभान्। ततः सुखं नाम विषेवसे सुखी न रामकार्ये मनसाप्यवेक्षसे॥
en: Do not behold the shafts resembling thunderbolts shot from the bow of that best of the Ikş wakus. Then, attaining happiness, you shall pass your days in peace. Nor do you mentally neglect Rāma's business.

sn: तथा ब्रुवाणं सौमित्रिं प्रदीप्तमिव तेजसा। अब्रवील्लक्ष्मणं तारा ताराधिपनिभानना॥
en: When Sumitra's son, Laksmana, had spoken thus, flaming in energy, Tārā of face fair as the moon, said to him,

sn: नैवं लक्ष्मण वक्तव्यो नायं परुषमर्हति। हरीणामीश्वरः श्रोतुं तव वक्त्राद् विशेषतः॥
en: O Lakşmaņa, you ought not to speak thus: and this lord of monkeys does not deserve to hear this harsh speech from your lips, in especial.

sn: नैवाकृतज्ञः सुग्रीवो न शठो नापि दारुणः। नैवानृतकथो वीर न जिह्मश्च कपीश्वरः॥
en: Sugrīva is not ungrateful, or cunning, or heartless; nor does he, O hero, deal in falsehood; nor is he deceitful.

sn: उपकारं कृतं वीरो नाप्ययं विस्मृतः कपिः। रामेण वीर सुग्रीवो यदन्यैर्दुष्करं रणे॥
en: Nor has the heroic monkey, O hero, forgotten the good, incapable of being done by others in battle, that the hero; Rāma, has done in his behalf.

sn: रामप्रसादात् कीर्तिं च कपिराज्यं च शाश्वतम्। प्राप्तवानिह सुग्रीवो रुमां मां च परंतप॥
en: O afflictor of foes, through Rāma's grace, Sugriva has here attained fame and the enduring empire of the monkeys, as well as Umā and myself.

sn: सुदुःखशयितः पूर्वं प्राप्येदं सुखमुत्तमम्। प्राप्तकालं न जानीते विश्वामित्रो यथा मुनिः॥
en: Having lain down miserable before, Sugrīva, now that he has attained this supreme happiness, does not heed his urgent duties, like the ascetic Visvamitra.

sn: घृताच्यां किल संसक्तो दश वर्षाणि लक्ष्मण। अहोऽमन्यत धर्मात्मा विश्वामित्रो महामुनिः॥ स हि प्राप्तं न जानीते कालं कालविदां वरः। विश्वामित्रो महातेजाः किं पुनर्यः पृथगजनः॥
en: Attached to Ghrtāci, O Laksmana, the pious and mighty ascetic, Viśvāmitra looked upon ten years as one day; and that best of those conversant with time, Viśvāmitra of mighty energy, did not perceive that the time (for doing a certain act) had arrived. What is to be said of other people?

sn: देहधर्मगतस्यास्य परिश्रान्तस्य लक्ष्मण। अवितृप्तस्य कामेषु रामः क्षन्तुमिहार्हति ॥ न च रोषवशं तात गन्तुमर्हसि लक्ष्मण। निश्चयार्थमविज्ञाय सहसा प्राकृतो यथा॥
en: O Lakşmaņa, it behoveth Rāma to forgive one who has all the bodily exigencies, who is fatigued, and who is not satisfied with the pleasures of Kama. Nor, O Laksmana, does it behove you, without ascertaining the exact import of things, to become suddenly subject to wrath, like any inferior person.

sn: सत्त्वयुक्ता हि पुरुषास्त्वद्विधाः पुरुषर्षभ। अविमृश्य न रोषश्य सहसा यान्ति वश्यताम् ॥
en: O chief of men, persons endowed with the quality of goodness, like to you, do not suffer themselves to come under the sway of passion, without (at first) heedfully revolving matters.

sn: प्रसादये त्वां धर्मज्ञ सुग्रीवार्थं समाहिता। महान् रोषसमुत्पन्नः संरम्भस्त्यज्यतामयम्॥
en: I crave your favour with concentrated mind, O you that know morality. Renounce the mighty grief that springs from your ire.

sn: रुमां मां चाङ्गदं राज्यं धनधान्यपशूनि च । रामप्रियार्थं सुग्रीवस्त्यजेदिति मतिर्मम ॥
en: This is my conviction that for compassing Rāma's welfare, Sugrīva can resign Umã and myself, and Angada, and the kingdom and wealth and corn and animals.

sn: समानेष्यति सुग्रीवः सीतया सह राघवम्। शशाङ्कमिव रोहिण्या हत्वा तं राक्षसाधमम्॥
en: Slaying that worst of Rākṣasas, Sugrīva will bring Rāghava with Sītā, like to the moon accompanied by Rohiņi.

sn: शतकोटिसहस्राणि लङ्कायां किल रक्षसाम्। अयुतानि च षट्त्रिंशत्सहस्राणि शतानि च॥ अहत्वा तांश्च दुर्धर्षान् राक्षसान् कामरूपिणः। न शक्यो रावणो हन्तुं येन सा मैथिली हृता॥
en: Without slaying hundreds of thousands of Kotis, and thirty-six Ayutas, thousands and hundreds of irrepressible Rākṣasas wearing shapes at will, (Rāma) can not slay Rāvana, by whom Maithili has been carried away.

sn: ते न शक्या रणे हन्तुमसहायेन लक्ष्मण। रावणः क्रूरकर्मा च सुग्रीवेण विशेषतः॥
en: They are incapable, O Laksmana, of being slain (by Rāma) in battle, unless he is supported (by others).

sn: एवमाख्यातवान् वाली स ह्यभिज्ञो हरीश्वरः। आगमस्तु न मे व्यक्तः श्रवात् तस्य ब्रवीम्यहम्॥
en: Rāvana is a wily warrior, and hence is the special need of Sugrīva. That knowing lord of monkeys, Väli, had told me all this. I do not know how Rāvana had secured this host: I say what I had heard from Vāli.

sn: त्वत्सहायनिमित्तं हि प्रेषिता हरिपुङ्गवाः। आनेतुं वानरान् युद्धे सुबहून् हरिपुङ्गवान्॥
en: For rendering you assistance, the foremost monkeys have been despatched in order to summon to the conflict numerous principal monkeys.

sn: तांश्च प्रतीक्षमाणोऽयं विक्रान्तान् सुमहाबलान्। राघवस्यार्थसिद्ध्यर्थं न निर्याति हरीश्वरः॥
en: Expecting these powerful and exceedingly strong ones, for attaining Rāghava's end, this lord of monkeys does not (yet) sally out.

sn: कृता सुसंस्था सौमित्रे सुग्रीवेण पुरा यथा। अद्य तैर्वानरैः सर्वैरागन्तव्यं महाबलैः॥
en: Things, O Saumitri, have beforehand been so satisfactorily arranged by Sugrīva, that this very day the mighty one will be joined with all those monkeys.

sn: ऋक्षकोटिसहस्राणि गोलाङ्गुलशतानि च। अद्य त्वमुपयास्यन्ति जहि कोपमरिंदम। कोट्योऽनेकास्तु काकुत्स्थ कपीनां दीप्तेजसाम् ॥
en: This very day billions of bears and thousands of golangulas as well as innumerable Koțis of monkeys flaming in energy shall join you. Therefore, O subduer of enemies, banish your anger.

sn: तव हि मुखमिदं निरीक्ष्य कोपात् क्षतजसमे नयने निरीक्षमाणाः। हरिवरवनिता न यान्ति शान्ति प्रथमभयस्य हि शङ्किताः स्म सर्वाः॥
en: Seeing this your face wrought up with wrath, and your eyes appearing like red sores, the wives of the best of monkeys experience no peace, and they are agitated by the fear that exercised them of late.

sn: इत्युक्तस्तारया वाक्यं प्रश्रितं धर्मसंहतम्। मृदुस्वभावः सौमित्रिः प्रतिजग्राह तद्वचः॥
en: Humbly addressed in these words informed with morality, Sumitra's son, resuming his native mildness, accepted them.

sn: तस्मिन् प्रतिगृहीते तु वाक्ये हरिगणेश्वरः। लक्ष्मणात् सुमहत्वासं वस्त्रं क्लिन्नमिवात्यजत्॥
en: On his accepting the speech, the lord of monkeys like a wet cloth cast off from him the fear he had conceived on account of Lakşmaņa.

sn: ततः कण्ठगतं माल्यं चित्रं बहुगणं महत्। चिच्छेद विमदश्चासीत् सुग्रीवो वानरेश्वरः॥
en: Then Sugriva-lord of monkeys-tore away the gaudy and variegated garland on his neck-potent with many a virtue, and become deprived of energy.

sn: स लक्ष्मणं भीमबलं सर्ववानरसत्तमः। अब्रवीत् प्रश्रितं वाक्यं सुग्रीवः सम्प्रहर्षयन्॥
en: And that master of all the monkeys, Sugrīva, gladdening Lakşmaņa of dreadful prowess, humbly observed to him,

sn: प्रणष्टा श्रीश्च कीर्तिश्च कपिराजं च शाश्वतम्। रामप्रसादात् सौमित्रे पुनश्चाप्तमिदं मया॥
en: You son to Sumitrā, by the favour of Rāma have I received back my lost luck, my fame, and this eternal monarchy of the monkeys.

sn: कः शक्तस्तस्य देवस्य ख्यातस्य स्वेन कर्मणा। तादृशं प्रतिकुर्वीत अंशेनापि नृपात्मज॥
en: O king's son, who is capable of repaying even in part an action like that of the divine (Rāma) renowned by means of his own acts?

sn: सीतां प्राप्स्यति धर्मात्मा वधिष्यति च रावणम्। सहायमात्रेण मया राघवः स्वेन तेजसा।७।।
en: By virtue of native energy, and merely with my help, the righteous Rāghava shall recover Sītā and slay Rāvana to boot.

sn: सहायकृत्यं किं तस्य येन सप्त महाद्रुमाः। गिरिश्च वसुधा चैव बाणेनैकेन दारिताः॥
en: What need of assistance to him who with a single shaft rived seven giant trees, a mountain, and the Earth.

sn: धनुर्विस्फारमाणस्य यस्य शब्देन लक्ष्मण। सशैला कम्पिता भूमिः सहायैः किं नु तस्य वै॥
en: O Lakşmaņa, what is the use of help to him the sounds of whose stretching bow made the Earth tremble with her mountains?

sn: अनुयात्रां नरेन्द्रस्य करिष्येऽहं नरर्षभ। गच्छतो रावणं हन्तुं वैरिणं सपुरस्सरम्॥
en: O best of men, when that foremost of men shall set out for slaying his enemy, Rāvaņa along with those going before him, I will follow him.

sn: यदि किंचिदतिक्रान्तं विश्वासात् प्रणयेन वा। प्रेष्यस्य क्षमितव्यं मे न कश्चिन्नापराध्यति॥
en: I through my confidence, or presuming upon our amity. I have transgressed in any way, (Rāma) ought to excuse his servant,—for there is no servant that does not transgress.

sn: इति तस्य ब्रुवाणस्य सुग्रीवस्य महात्मनः। अभवल्लक्ष्मणः प्रीतः प्रेम्णा चेदमुवाच ह॥
en: When the high-souled Sugrīva had said this, Lakşmaņa became well pleased and he spoke from love,

sn: सर्वथा हि मम भ्राता सनाथो वानरेश्वर। त्वया नाथेन सुग्रीव प्रश्रितेन विशेषतः॥
en: Having in especial, you endued with humility, my brother, O monarch of monkeys, is every way strong, O Sugriva.

sn: यस्ते प्रभावः सुग्रीव यच्च ते शौचमीदृशम्। अर्हस्त्वं कपिराज्यस्य श्रियं भोक्तुमनुत्तमाम्॥
en: Such is your strength, O Sugriva, and such your self-denial, that you are fully worthy to enjoy the good fortune of the king of monkeys.

sn: सहायेन च सुग्रीव त्वया रामः प्रतापवान्। वधिष्यति रणे शत्रूनचिरान्नात्र संशयः॥
en: O Sugrīva, by your help, the puissant Rāma shall speedily slay his foe. Of this there is not the least doubt.

sn: धर्मज्ञस्य कृतज्ञस्य संग्रामेष्वनिवर्तिनः। उपपत्रं च युक्तं च सुग्रीव तव भाषितम्॥
en: O Sugrīva, what you virtuous, grateful and never turning away from fight, have said is fit and proper.

sn: दोषज्ञः प्रतिसामर्थ्य कोऽन्यो भाषितुमर्हति। वर्जयित्वा मम ज्येष्ठं त्वां च वानरसत्तम ॥
en: What knowing person, excepting, O foremost of monkeys, yourself and my elder brother, can speak so.

sn: सदृशश्चासि रामेण विक्रमेण बलेन च। सहायो दैवतैर्दत्तश्चिराय हरिपुंगव॥
en: Resembling Rāma himself in strength and prowess, you, O chief of monkeys, have been ordained his help by the gods.

sn: किं त शीघ्रमितो वीर निष्क्रम त्वं मया सह। सान्त्वयस्व वयस्यं च भार्याहरणदुःखितम्॥
en: But, O hero, do you speedily go out with me and soothe your friend aggrieved for the ravishment of his wife.

sn: यच्च शोकाभिभूतस्य श्रुत्वा रामस्य भाषितम्। मया त्वं परुषाण्युक्तस्तत् क्षमस्व सखे मम॥
en: And do you, my frie forgive what rough speech, on hearing the utterances of Rāma sunk in grief, I have given you.

sn: किं त शीघ्रमितो वीर निष्क्रम त्वं मया सह। सान्त्वयस्व वयस्यं च भार्याहरणदुःखितम्॥
en: But, O hero, do you speedily go out with me and soothe your friend aggrieved for the ravishment of his wife.

sn: यच्च शोकाभिभूतस्य श्रुत्वा रामस्य भाषितम्। मया त्वं परुषाण्युक्तस्तत् क्षमस्व सखे मम॥
en: And do you, my frie forgive what rough speech, on hearing the utterances of Rāma sunk in grief, I have given you.

sn: एवमुक्तस्तु सुग्रीवो लक्ष्मणेन महात्मना। हनूमन्तं स्थितं पार्श्वे वचनं चेदमब्रवीत्॥
en: Thus addressed by the magnanimous Lakşmana Sugrīva said to Hanumān, staying beside him,

sn: महेन्द्रहिमवद्विन्ध्यकैलासशिखरेषु च। मन्दरे पाण्डुशिखरे पञ्चशैलेषु ये स्थिताः॥ तरुणादित्यवर्णेषु भ्राजमानेषु नित्यशः। पर्वतेषु समुद्रान्ते पश्चिमस्यां तु ये दिशि॥ आदित्यभवने चैव गिरौ संध्याभ्रसंनिभे। पद्माचलवनं भीमाः संश्रिता हरिपुंगवाः॥ अञ्जनाम्बुदसंकाशाः कुञ्जरेन्द्रमहौजसः। अञ्जने पर्वते चैव ये वसन्ति प्लवङ्गमाः॥ महाशैलगुहावासा वानराः कनकप्रभाः। मेरुपार्श्वगताश्चैव ये च धूम्रगिरिं श्रिताः॥ तरुणादित्यवर्णाश्च पर्वते ये महारुणे। पिबन्तो मधु मैरेयं भीमवेगा: प्लवङ्गमाः॥ वनेषु च सुरम्येषु सुगन्धिषु महत्सु च। तापसाश्रमरम्येषु वनान्तेषु समन्ततः॥ तांस्तांस्त्वमानय क्षिप्रं पृथिव्यां सर्ववानरान्। सामदानादिभिः कल्पैर्वानरैर्वेगवत्तरैः॥
en: Those that dwell on the summits of Mahendra, Himavat, Vindhya and Kailāsa; on Mandara, the peaks of Pāndu and the five hills; on mountains wearing the hue of the infant sun, and ever bright; and those inhabiting the West, beyond the sea; On mountains in the mansions of the sun, looking like the evening sky, and those dreadful foremost of monkeys that inhabit Padmachala, those monkeys that, resembling collyrium-like clouds, and having the strength of the lord of elephants, dwell in the Añjana hill; monkeys, possessing the splendour of gold, inhabiting the caverns of Mahāsaila; those resorting to the sides of Meru, as well as those dwelling in the Dhūmra mountains; and those, having the hues of the infant sun, dwelling in the Mahāruna mountain, drinking the Maireya wine; and those dwelling in mighty fair and fragrant forests and romantic hermitages all round, lying on the skirts of woods,-do you at once bring all these-all the foremost monkeys of the world, by means of gifts and conciliation, and through the agency of more than usually fleet monkeys.

sn: प्रेषिताः प्रथमं ये च मयाऽऽज्ञाता महाजवाः। त्वरणार्थं तु भूयस्त्वं सम्प्रेषय हरीश्वरान्॥
en: I know those monkeys that I have first despatched, to be gifted with great velocity*, yet, for urging speed upon them, do you send other foremost of monkeys. *The commentator slips the sense here. According to him, the meaning is, Those monkeys whom I have first sent, are known to me.

sn: ये प्रसक्ताश्च कामेषु दीर्घसूत्राश्च वानराः। इहानयस्व ताशीघ्रं सर्वानेव कपीश्वरान् ॥
en: Do you directly bring up here those monkeychiefs that are given up to lust or are dilatory.

sn: अहोभिर्दशभिर्ये च नागच्छन्ति ममाज्ञया। हन्तव्यास्ते दुरात्मानो राजशासनदूषकाः॥
en: Those wicked ones, that finding fault with the royal mandate, do not (come in) at my command within ten days, must be slain.

sn: शतान्यथ सहस्राणि कोट्यश्च मम शासनात्। प्रयान्तु कपिसिंहानां निदेशे मम ये स्थिताः॥
en: Let those hundreds and thousands and kotis of leonine monkeys that abide by my mandate, hie (hence) at my behest.

sn: मेघपर्वतसंकाशाश्छादयन्त इवाम्बरम्। घोररूपाः कपिश्रेष्ठा यान्तु म मच्छासनादितः दितः॥
en: Let (monkey) resembling clouds or mountains, cover up the sky; and let the foremost monkeys of dreadful forms march hence at my command.

sn: ते गतिज्ञा गतिं गत्वा पृथिव्यां सर्ववानराः। आनयन्तु हरीन् सर्वांस्त्वरिताः शासनान्मम॥
en: Let all the monkeys on earth, acquainted with motion lying themselves and summoning speed at my command, bring all the monkeys.

sn: तस्य वानरराजस्य श्रुत्वा वायुसुतो वचः। दिक्षु सर्वासु विक्रान्तान् प्रेषयामास वानरान्॥
en: Hearing the words of the monkey-king, the son of the Wind-god despatched powerful monkeys in all directions.

sn: ते पदं विष्णुविक्रान्तं पतत्रिज्योतिरध्वगाः। प्रयाताः प्रहिता राज्ञा हरयस्तु क्षणेन वै॥
en: Despatched by the king, the monkeys, ranging the sphere of birds and stars, immediately went through the welkin.

sn: ते समुद्रेषु गिरिषु वनेषु च सरस्सु च। वानरा वानरान् सर्वान् रामहेतोरचोदयन्॥
en: And on oceans and mountains, in forests and tanks, the monkeys began to send away all the apes on behalf of Rāma.

sn: मृत्युकालोपमस्याज्ञां राजराजस्य वानराः। सुग्रीवस्याययुः श्रुत्वा सुग्रीवभयशङ्किताः॥
en: Hearing the mandate of that king of kings, Sugriva, resembling the Hour of death, the monkeys, conceiving fear for Sugrīva, set out.

sn: ततस्तेऽञ्जनसंकाशा गिरेस्तस्मान्महाबलाः। तिस्रः कोट्यः प्लवङ्गानां निर्ययुर्यत्र राघवः॥
en: And monkeys resembling collyrium (in hue), numbering three kotis, endued with huge might, set out from the Añjana hill for the place where Rāghava was.

sn: अस्तं गच्छति यत्रार्कस्तस्मिन् गिरिवरे रताः। संतप्तहेमवर्णाभास्तस्मात् कोट्यो दश च्युताः॥
en: And ten koțis having the splendour of molten gold inhabiting the mountain where the sun sets, set out.

sn: कैलासशिखरेभ्यश्च सिंहकेसरवर्चसाम्। ततः कोटिसहस्राणि वानराणां समागमन्॥
en: And a thousand kotis, hued like the lion's mane, came from the peaks of Kailāsa.

sn: फलमूलेन जीवन्तो हिमवन्तमुपाश्रिताः। तेषां कोटिसहस्राणां सहस्रं समवर्तत॥
en: And of those dwelling in Himālaya, subsisting on fruits and roots, numbering a thousand and kotis, a thousand appeared.

sn: अङ्गारकसमानानां भीमानां भीमकर्मणाम्। विन्ध्याद् वानरकोटीनां सहस्राण्यपतन् द्रुतम्॥
en: And thousands of dreadful monkeys of terrible deeds, hued like charcoal, numbering kot is, rushed suddenly from Vindhya.

sn: क्षीरोदवेलानिलयास्तमालवनवासिनः। नारिकेलासनाश्चैव तेषां संख्या न विद्यते॥
en: And there exists no record of the number of those inhabiting the shores of the ocean of milk, and the dwellers in the Tamāla forests, as well as those subsisting on coconuts.

sn: वनेभ्यो गह्वरेभ्यश्च सरिद्भ्यश्च महाबलाः। आगच्छद् वानरी सेना पिबन्तीव दिवाकरम्॥
en: And, as if drinking up the sun, the mighty monkey host came from forests and caves and rivers.

sn: ये तु त्वरयितुं याता वानराः सर्ववानरान्। ते वीरा हिमवच्छैले ददृशुस्तं महादुमम्॥
en: And it came to pass that those heroic monkeys that had gone away to spur others on, found a mighty tree on Himayat.

sn: तस्मिन् गिरिवरे पुण्ये यज्ञो माहेश्वरः पुरा। सर्वदेवमनस्तोषो बभूव सुमनोरमः॥
en: On that sacred mount in days of yore there took place a pleasing Maheswara* sacrifice. *The celestial horse-sacrifice.

sn: अन्ननिस्यन्दजातानि मूलानि च फलानि च। अमृतस्वादुकल्पानि ददृशुस्तत्र वानराः॥
en: There the monkeys found grateful fruits and roots sprung from the streams of sacrificial oblations, and resembling ambrosia.

sn: तदनसम्भवं दिव्यं फलमूलं मनोहरम्। यः कश्चित् सकृदश्नाति मासं भवति तर्पितः॥
en: He that partakes of those excellent fruits and roots sprung from the sacrificial ingredients, does not experience hunger for a month.

sn: तानि मूलानि दिव्यानि फलानि च फलाशनाः। औषधानि च दिव्यानि जगृहुर्हरिपुंगवाः॥
en: Those prime monkeys, feeding on fruits, gathered those sapid fruits and roots and medicinal herbs.

sn: तस्माच्च यज्ञायतनात् पुष्पाणि सुरभीणि च। आनिन्युनिरा गत्वा सुग्रीवप्रियकारणात्॥
en: And for compassing the good of Sugrīva, repairing thither, the monkeys brought ordorous blossoms from the sacrificial ground.

sn: ते तु सर्वे हरिवराः पृथिव्यां सर्ववानरान्। संचोदयित्वा त्वरितं यूथानां जग्मुरग्रतः॥
en: And all those foremost of monkeys, taking all the monkeys of the earth, hastily set off in the van of the herds.

sn: ते तु तेन मुहूर्तेन कपयः शीघ्रचारिणः। किष्किन्धां त्वरया प्राप्ताः सुग्रीवो यत्र वानरः॥
en: And in a short while, those fast-fleeting apes speedily reached Kişkindhā, where the monkey Sugriva was.

sn: ते गृहीत्वौषधीः सर्वा फलमूलं च वानराः। तं प्रतिग्राहयामासुर्वचनं चेदमब्रुवन्॥
en: And taking the healing herbs and the fruits and roots, the monkeys made them over to Sugrīva, and said,

sn: सर्वे परिसृताः शैलाः सरितश्च वनानि च। पृथिव्यां वानराः सर्वे शासनादुपयान्ति ते॥
en: Having traversed mountains, rivers and forests, all the monkeys of the earth bend their steps towards you in obedience to your command.

sn: एवं श्रुत्वा ततो हृष्टः सुग्रीवः प्लवगाधिपः। प्रतिजग्राह च प्रीतस्तेषां सर्वमुपायनम्॥
en: Hearing this, Sugriva-lord of monkeys-was well pleased, and with a glad heart accepted all those present.

sn: प्रतिगृह्य च तत् सर्वमुपायनमुपाहतम्। वानरान् सान्त्वयित्वा च सर्वानिव व्यसर्जयत्॥
en: Having accepted all those presents, (Sugrīva), after soothing the monkeys, dismissed them.

sn: विसर्जयित्वा स हरीन् सहस्रान् कृतकर्मणः। मेने कृतार्थमात्मानं राघवं च महाबलम्॥
en: Having dismissed the thousands of apes, who had performed their task, he deemed himself as well as the mighty Rāghava as having secured success.

sn: स लक्ष्मणो भीमबलं सर्ववानरसत्तमम्। अब्रवीत् प्रथितं वाक्यं सुग्रीवं सम्प्रहर्षयन् ॥
en: Then Lakşmaņa in sweet words spoke to the exceedingly strong chief of monkeysSugriva-gladdening him,

sn: किष्किन्धाया विनिष्क्राम यदि ते सौम्य रोचते। तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा लक्ष्मणस्य सुभाषितम्॥ सुग्रीवः परमप्रीतो वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह।
en: If it please you, O placid one, I will go out of Kiskindhā. Hearing Laksmana's soft speech, Sugriva, highly delighted, said,

sn: एवं भवतु गच्छाम स्थेयं त्वच्छासने मया॥ तमेवमुक्त्वा सुग्रीवो लक्ष्मणं शुभलक्षणम्। विसर्जयामास तदा ताराद्याश्चैव योषितः॥
en: Be it so. Let us go. I abide by your behest. Having said this to Lakşmaņa of auspicious marks, Sugrīva dismissed the women with Tārā at their head.

sn: एहीत्युच्चैर्हरिवरान् सुग्रीवः समुदाहरत्। तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा हरयः शीघ्रमाययुः।७।। बद्धाञ्जलिपुटाः सर्वे ये स्युः स्त्रीदर्शनक्षमाः।
en: Then Sugrīva in a loud voice summoned the foremost monkey, saying, Come (hither). hearing his words, those monkeys that could present themselves before the females, did so with joined hands.

sn: तानुवाच ततः प्राप्तान् वाचार्कसदृशप्रभः॥ उपस्थापयत क्षिप्रं शिबिकां मम वानराः।
en: To them, who had presented themselves, said the king, of splendour resembling that of the Sun, Do, you monkeys, bring hither a car.8

sn: श्रुत्वा तु वचनं तस्य हरयः शीघ्रविक्रमाः॥ समुपस्थापयामासुः शिबिकां प्रियदर्शनाम्।
en: Hearing his words, monkeys uniting vigour with celerity, brought a car lovely to behold.

sn: तामुपस्थापितां दृष्ट्वा शिबिकां वानराधिपः॥ लक्ष्मणारुह्यतां शीघ्रमिति सौमित्रिमब्रवीत्।
en: Seeing the car brought up, the lord of monkeys said to Sumitra's son, O Laksmana, ascend speedily.

sn: इत्युक्त्वा काञ्चनं यानं सुग्रीवः सूर्यसंनिभम्॥ बहुभिर्हरिभिर्युक्तमारुरोह सलक्ष्मणः।
en: Having said this, Sugrīva in company with Lakşınana swiftly ascended the golden car resembling the sun, yoked with numerous steeds.

sn: पाण्डुरेणातपत्रेण ध्रियमाणेन मूर्धनि॥ शुक्लैश्च बालव्यजनैधूयमानैः समन्ततः। शङ्खभेरीनिनादैश्च बन्दिभिश्चाभिनन्दितः॥
en: With a pale umbrella held over his head, and white chowris waving around, with conchs and trumpets blowing, eulogized by bards, Sugrīva marched out, having obtained supreme regal auspiciousness.

sn: निर्ययौ प्राप्य सुग्रीवो राज्यश्रियमनुत्तमाम्। स वानरशतैस्तीक्ष्णैर्बहुभिः शस्त्रपाणिभिः॥
en: And surrounded by hundreds of high-spirited apes and armed people, he proceeded whither Rāma was staying.

sn: परिकीर्णो ययौ तत्र यत्र रामो व्यवस्थितः। स तं देशमनुप्राप्य श्रेष्ठं रामनिषेवितम्॥ अवातरन्महातेजाः शिबिकायाः सलक्ष्मणः। आसाद्य च ततो रामं कृताञ्जलिपुटोऽभवत्॥
en: And having arrived at the excellent spot which was the home of Rāma, that highly energetic one alighted from the car along with Lakşmaņa. And having come to Rāma, Sugrīva (stood) folding his hands.

sn: कृताञ्जलौ स्थिते तस्मिन् वानराश्चाभवंस्तथा। तटाकमिव तं दृष्ट्वा रामः कुड्मलपङ्कजम्॥ वानराणां महत् सैन्यं सुग्रीवे प्रीतिमानभूत्।
en: And when Sugrīva has folded his hands, the monkeys also did so. And beholding the mighty host of the monkeys resembling a tank filled with lotus buds, Rāma was well-pleased with Sugriva.

sn: पादयोः पतितं मूर्धा तमुत्थाप्य हरीश्वरम्॥ प्रेम्णा च बहुमानाच्च राघवः परिषस्वजे।
en: And raising up the monkey-king who had bent his head at Rāma's feet, Rāghava embraced him from love and regard.

sn: परिष्वज्य च धर्मात्मा निषीदेति ततोऽब्रवीत्॥ निषण्णं तं ततो दृष्ट्वा क्षितौ रामोऽब्रवीत् ततः।
en: Having embraced Sugrīva, that righteous one said to him, Be seated. And seeing Sugrīva seated on the ground, Rāma said,

sn: धर्ममर्थं च कामं च काले यस्तु निषेवते॥ विभज्य सततं वीर स राजा हरिसत्तम। हित्वा धर्मं तथाऽर्थं च कामं यस्तु निषेवते॥ स वृक्षाग्रे यथा सुप्तः पतितः प्रतिबुध्यते।
en: He, O best of monkeys, is a king who, O hero, in season follows righteousness, pleasure and profit, always dividing the same (among all). He that, renouncing righteousness and the good, devotes himself to pleasure solely, is like a man that falling asleep on the top of a tree, wakes when he has fallen down.

sn: अमित्राणां वधे युक्तो मित्राणां संग्रहे रतः॥ त्रिवर्गफलभोक्ता च राजा धर्मेण युज्यते।
en: That king is verily virtuous that, engaged in uprooting foes and advancing friends, attends to all the three ends.

sn: उद्योगसमयस्त्वेष प्राप्तः शत्रुनिषूदन ॥ संचिन्यतां हि पिङ्गेश हरिभिः सह मन्त्रिभिः।
en: O destroyer of foes, the time is come for exertion: do you, O lord of monkeys, bethink yourself along with your monkey ministers.

sn: एवमुक्तस्तु सुग्रीवो रामं वचनमब्रवीत्॥ प्रनष्टा श्रीश्च कीर्तिश्च कपिराज्यं च शाश्वतम्। त्वत्प्रसादान्महाबाहो पुनः प्राप्तमिदं मया॥
en: Thus addressed, Sugrīva said to Räma, O mighty-armed one, my lost luck, and repute, and the entire monkey kingdom I have received back through your gift, owing to thine and your brother's grace, you foremost of victors.

sn: तव देव प्रसादाच्च भ्रातुश्च जयतां वर। कृतं न प्रतिकुर्याद् यः पुरुषाणां हि दूषणः॥
en: He that, having received a good office, does not requite it, reapeth obloquy among persons.

sn: एते वानरमुख्याश्च शतशः शत्रुसूदन। प्राप्ताश्चादाय बलिनः पृथिव्यां सर्ववानरान्॥
en: These hundreds of prime monkeys, O destroyer of enemies, have come here, bringing with them all the monkeys of the world.

sn: ऋक्षाश्च वानराः शूरा गोलाङ्कलाश्च राघव। कान्तारवनदुर्गाणामभिज्ञा घोरदर्शनाः॥ देवगन्धर्वपुत्राश्च वानराः कामरूपिणः। स्वैः स्वैः परिवृताः सैन्यैर्वर्तन्ते पथि राघव॥ शतैः शतसहस्रैश्च वर्तन्ते कोटिभिस्तथा। अयुतैश्चावृता वीर शङ्कुभिश्च परंतप ॥ अर्बुदैरर्बुदशतैर्मध्यैश्चान्त्यैश्च वानराः। समुद्राश्च परार्धाश्च हरयो हरियूथपाः॥ आगमिष्यन्ति ते राजन् महेन्द्रसमविक्रमाः। मेघपर्वतसंकाशा मेरुविन्ध्यकृतालयाः॥
en: O Rāghava, bears and monkeys, heroic Golangulas—acquainted with woods and forests and strongholds, and of terrible shapes-and monkeys who are the sons of deities, wearing forms at will-stay on the way, O Raghava, surrounded by their own armies. And, O hero, O repressor of foes, monkeys surrounded by hundreds, and hundred thousands, and kotis, and ayutas, and sankus*, and arvudas and hundreds of arvudas, and Madhyas and antyas wait (here) And samudras, and parārdhas of monkeysleaders of herds — inhabiting Meru and Vindhya resembling clouds or hills, and in might resembling the great Indra, are on their way to you, O king. *A Sanku is thousand Arvudas; a Madhya is an Arvuda ten times; an Antya is a Modhya ten times; a Samudra is a Madhya twenty times; and Parārdha, a Samudra thirty times.

sn: ते त्वामभिगमिष्यन्ति राक्षसं योद्धमाहवे। निहत्य रावणं युद्धे ह्यानयिष्यन्ति मैथिलीम्॥
en: They will join you for battling the fiend in the field; and, slaying Ravana in fight, shall bring Mithilā's daughter.

sn: ततः समिद्योगमवेक्ष्य वीर्यवान् हरिप्रवीरस्य निदेशवर्तिनः। बभूव हर्षाद् वसुधाधिपात्मजः प्रबुद्धनीलोत्पलतुल्यदर्शनः॥
en: Thereat the puissant son of the Earth's lord, witnessing the preparations made by the heroic monkey, remaining under his his command, appeared like a blown blue lotus.

sn: इति ब्रुवाणं सुग्रीवं रामो धर्मभृतां वरः। बाहुभ्यां सम्परिष्वज्य प्रत्युवाच कृताञ्जलिम्॥
en: As Sugrīva was speaking thus with joined hands, that best of the righteous, Rāma, embraced him with his arms, and then replied,

sn: यदिन्द्रो वर्षते वर्षे न तच्चित्रं भविष्यति। आदित्योऽसौ सहस्रांशुः कुर्याद् वितिमिरं नभः॥ चन्द्रमा रजनी कुर्यात् प्रभया सौम्य निर्मलाम्। त्वद्विधो वापि मित्राणां प्रीतिं कुर्यात् परंतप॥
en: That Indra poureth down showers, is no wonder, nor that this thousand-rayed Sun dispels darkness from the sky; nor yet that, O mild one, the Moon by his rays causes the clear night. (And in a similar way), friends like you bring delight, O subduer of foes. O mild one, that 'whatever is graceful, should be harboured in you is not strange.* *The commentator in his usual way of reading between the lines, says that the sense is—That you had gathered forces for serving your friend, is not strange. O placid one, it is well. I give the sense the śloka naturally yields.

sn: एवं त्वयि न तच्चित्रं भवेद् यत् सौम्य शोभनम्। जानाम्यहं त्वां सुग्रीव सततं प्रियवादिनम्॥
en: I know, O Sugrīva, that you always speakst what is for my good.

sn: त्वत्सनाथः सखे संख्ये जेतास्मि सकलानरीन्। त्वमेव मे सुहृन्मित्रं साहाय्यं कर्तुमर्हसि ॥
en: Assisted by you, my friend, I shall in battle vanquish all my foes. You being my friend and my ally, should assist me.

sn: जहारात्मविनाशाय मैथिली राक्षसाधमः। वञ्चयित्वा तु पौलोमीमनुह्लादो यथा शचीम्॥
en: That worst of Rākșasas has carried away Maithilī, to bring down destruction upon himself, even as Anuhlāda ravished Puloma's daughter, Sachi, deceiving her sire.

sn: न चिरात् तं वधिष्यामि रावणं निशितैः शरैः। पौलोम्याः पितरं दृप्तं शतक्रतुरिवारिहा॥
en: That Rāvana I will at no distant date slay with my sharpened shafts, even as that slayer of enemies, he of an hundred sacrifices-slew the haughty father of Paulomi.

sn: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे चैव रजः समभिवर्तत। उष्णतीव्रां सहस्रांशोश्छादयद् गगने प्रभाम्॥
en: Presently appeared volumes of dust, and the hot and fierce rays of the sun were hid in the sky.

sn: दिशः पर्याकुलाश्चासंस्तमसा तेन दूषिताः। चचाल च मही सर्वा सशैलवनकानना॥
en: And darkened by the gloom, all sides became bewildered. And the entire earth with her mountains, forests, and wocds, trembled.

sn: ततो नरेन्द्रसंकाशैस्तीक्ष्णदंष्ट्रैर्महाबलैः। कृत्स्ना संछादिता भूमिरसंख्येयैः प्लवङ्गमैः॥
en: Then the whole ground was covered with innumerable monkeys gifted with great strength, and having sharp teeth, and resembling kings of men.

sn: निमेषान्तरमात्रेण ततस्तैहरियूथपैः। कोटीशतपरीवारैर्वानरैर्हरियूथपैः॥ नादेयैः पार्वतेयैश्च सामुद्रैश्च महाबलैः। हरिभिर्मेघनिदैिरन्यैश्च वनवासिभिः॥ तरुणादित्यवर्णैश्च शशिगौरैश्च वानरैः। पद्मकेसरवर्णैश्च श्वेतैर्हेमकृतालयैः॥ कोटीसहस्रैर्दशभिः श्रीमान् परिवृतस्तदा। वीरः शतबलिर्नाम वानरः प्रत्यदृश्यत ॥
en: Then surrounded by leaders of monkey-herds, and retinues numbering hundreds of koțis, and monkey chiefs from rivers, and mountains, and seas, endowed with prodigious strength, and other apes inhabiting forests, having voices resembling clouds-and monkeys hued like the infant sun, or white like the moon, or coloured like the filaments of the lotus, or pale, having their homes in the Golden mountain-in all, numbering ten thousand koțis,-appeared the graceful and heroic monkey, named Satavali.

sn: ततः काञ्चनशैलाभस्ताराया वीर्यवान् पिता। अनेकैर्बहुसाहौः कोटिभिः प्रत्यदृश्यत॥
en: Then, having the splendour of the Golden hill, the puissant sire of Tārā was seen at the head of many thousand kotis.

sn: तथापरेण कोटीनां सहस्रेण समन्वितः। पिता रुमायाः सम्प्राप्तः सुग्रीवश्वशुरो विभुः॥
en: Then Umā's father, that lord, the father-in-law of Sugrīva, arrived, accompanied with other thousands of kotis (of monkeys),... resembling the filaments of the lotus, of face like to the youthful sun, intelligent, the foremost of monkeys-supreme among them all.

sn: पद्मकेसरसंकाशस्तरुणार्कनिभाननः। बुद्धिमान् वानर श्रेष्ठः सर्ववानरसत्तमः॥ अनेकैर्बहुसाहस्रैर्वानराणां समन्वितः। पिता हनुमतः श्रीमान् केसरी प्रत्यदृश्यत॥
en: And Hanuman's father, the graceful Kasarī, appeared in company with many thousands of monkeys.

sn: गोलाङ्गुलमहाराजो गवाक्षो भीमविक्रमः। वृतः कोटिसहस्रेण वानराणामदृश्यत॥
en: And Gavaksa-sovereign of Golangulas-endowed with dreadful might, appeared, surrounded by thousand koțis of monkeys.

sn: ऋक्षाणां भीमवेगानां धूम्रः शत्रुनिबर्हणः। वृतः कोटिसहस्राभ्यां द्वाभ्यां समभिवर्तत॥
en: And Dhūmra of bears endowed with terrific speed—destroyer of foes—appeared, surrounded by two thousand kotis.

sn: महाचलनिभैोरैः पनसो नाम यूथपः। आजगाम महावीर्यस्तिसृभिः कोटिभिर्वृतः॥
en: And the leader of herds, named Panasa, of exceeding prowess, came, accompanied with three kotis, mighty and dreadful.

sn: नीलाञ्जनचयाकारो नीलो नामैष यूथपः। अदृश्यत महाकायः कोटिभिर्दशभिर्वृतः॥
en: And the leader of herds, named Nīla, of huge body, resembling a mass of blue collyrium. appeared with ten kotis.

sn: ततः काञ्चनशैलाभो गवयो नाम यूथपः। आजगाम महावीर्यः कोटिभिः पञ्चभिर्वृतः॥
en: Then the exceedingly powerful Gavayaleader of herds, having the splendour of the Golden mountain, arrived with five koțis.

sn: दरीमुखश्च बलवान् यूथपोऽभ्याययौ तदा। वृतः कोटिसहस्रेण सुग्रीवं समवस्थितः॥
en: And that powerful leader of herdsDarimukha, came, sutrounded by thousands of kotis, and took up his post by Sugriva.

sn: मैन्दश्च द्विविदश्चोभावश्विपुत्रौ महाबलौ। कोटिकोटिसहस्रेण वानराणामदृश्यताम्॥
en: And Mainda and Dvivida-sons of Asvi both-of mighty strength, appeared with kotis upon thousands of koțis of monkeys.

sn: गजश्च बलवान् वीरस्तिसृभिः कोटिभिर्वृतः। ऋक्षराजो महातेजा जाम्बरान्नाम नामतः।॥ कोटिभिर्दशभिर्व्याप्तः सुग्रीवस्य वशे स्थितः।
en: And the powerful and heroic Gaja (came), surrounded by three kotis. And the king of bears, Jāmbavān by name, (came), surrounded by ten koțis, and enlisted himself under the command of Sugriva.

sn: रुम्णो नाम तेजस्वी विक्रान्तैर्वानरैर्वृतः॥ आगतो बलवांस्तूर्णं कोटीशतसमावृतः।
en: And (the monkey) named Rumna, possessed of energy, and strong, came swiftly, surrounded by an hundred koțis of powerful monkeys.

sn: ततः कोटिसहस्राणां सहस्रेण शतेन च॥ पृष्ठतोऽनुगतः प्राप्तो हरिभिर्गन्धमादनः।
en: Then, followed at his back by hundreds and thousands of koțis, came the monkey, Gandhamādana.

sn: ततः पद्मसहस्रेण वृतः शङ्कुशतेन च ॥ युवराजोऽङ्गदः प्राप्तः पितुस्तुल्यपराक्रमः।
en: Then came the young prince Angada, in prowess resembling his sire, accompanied by a thousand padmas and an hundred sankhas.

sn: ततस्ताराद्युतिस्तारो हरिभिर्भीमविक्रमैः॥ पञ्चभिर्हरिकोटीभिर्दूरतः पर्यदृश्यत।
en: Then appeared at a distance, accompanied by five koțis of monkeys endowed with dreadful prowess,-Tārā, having the splendour of a star.

sn: इन्द्रजानुः कविर्वीरो यूथपः प्रत्यदृश्यत॥ एकादशानां कोटीनामीश्वरस्तैश्च संवृतः।
en: And then appeared Indrajāni, the heroic monkey and leader of herds-lord of eleven kotis-surrounded by them.

sn: ततो रम्भस्त्वनुप्राप्तस्तरुणादित्यसंनिभः॥ अयुतेन वृतश्चैव सहस्रेण शतेन च।
en: Then followed Rambha, resembling the infant sun, accompanied by an ayuta, a thousand, and an hundred.

sn: ततो यूथपतिवीरो दुर्मुखो नाम वानरः॥ प्रत्यदृश्यत कोटीभ्यां द्वाभ्यां परिवृतो बली।
en: Then appeared to the view the stout monkey, named Durmukha, heroic lord of herds, surrounded by two koțis.

sn: कैलासशिखराकारैर्वानरैर्भीमविक्रमैः॥ वृतः कोटिसहस्रेण हनुमान् प्रत्यदृश्यत।
en: And Hanumān showed himself, surrounded by a thousand koțis of monkeys, resembling peaks of Kailāsa, of dreadful vigour.

sn: नलश्चापि महावीर्यः संवृतो दुमवासिभिः॥ कोटीशतेन सम्प्राप्तः सहस्रेण शतेन च।
en: And the exceedingly energetic Nala came, attended with an hundred kotis, a thousand, and an hundred monkeys, living in trees.

sn: ततो दरीमुखः श्रीमान् कोटिभिर्दशभिर्वृतः॥ सम्प्राप्तोऽभिनदंस्तस्य सुग्रीवस्य महात्मनः॥
en: Then surrounded by ten kotis (of monkeys), came the shapely Darimukha before the highsouled Sugriva, from a country bordering on a river.

sn: शरभः कुमुदो वह्निर्वानरो रंभ एव च॥ एते चान्ये च बहवो वानराः कामरूपिणः। आवृत्य पृथिवीं सर्वां पर्वतांश्च वनानि च ॥ यूथपाः समनुप्राप्ता येषां संख्या न विद्यते।
en: And Sarabha, Kumuda, Vahni, the monkey Rambha,-and many other monkeys-lords of herds-passing ennumeration-wearing shapes at will, came covering the entire earth with her mountains and forests.

sn: आगताश्च निविष्टाश्च पृथिव्यां सर्ववानराः॥ आप्लवन्तः प्लवन्तश्च गर्जन्तश्च प्लवङ्गमाः। अभ्यवर्तन्त सुग्रीवं सूर्यमभ्रगणा इव॥
en: And all the monkeys of the world were some of them coming and others putting up. And monkeys-some of them dripping, and some leaping, and some roaring-gathered round Sugriva, like clouds gathering round the sun.

sn: कुर्वाणा बहुशब्दांश्च प्रकृष्टा बाहुशालिनः। शिरोभिर्वानरेन्द्राय सुग्रीवाय न्यवेदयन् ॥
en: And, crying in various tones, prime monkeys furnished with arms, with bent heads spoke humbly to that lord of monkeys—Sugrīva.

sn: अपरे वानरश्रेष्ठाः संगम्य च यथोचितम्। सुग्रीवेण समागम्य स्थिताः प्राञ्जलयस्तदा।॥
en: And other foremost of monkeys, gathering together duly, came before Sugrīva with joined hands.

sn: सुग्रीवस्त्वरितो रामे सर्वांस्तान् वानरर्षभान्। निवेदयित्वा धर्मज्ञः स्थितः प्राञ्जलिरब्रवीत्॥ यथासुखं पर्वतनिझरेषु वनेषु सर्वेषु च वानरेन्द्राः। निवेशयित्वा विधिवद् बलानि बलं बलज्ञः प्रतिपत्तुमीष्टे॥
en: Sugrīva standing with joined hands, expeditiously informed Rāma of the arrival of the monkey-leaders in hot haste; and then spoke (to them, saying, O chiefs of monkeys, stationing the forces duly near mountain-rills and all the woods, let him that is conversant with the army, ascertain who have come and who have not.

sn: अथ राजा समृद्धार्थः सुग्रीवः प्लवगेश्वरः। उवाच नरशार्दूलं रामं परबलार्दनम्॥
en: Then that lord of monkeys, the successful Sugrīva, spoke to Rāma-lion among men and destroyer of hostile hosts-saying,

sn: आगता विनिविष्टाश्च बलिन: कामरूपिणः। वानरेन्द्रा महेन्द्राभा ये मद्विषयवासिनः॥
en: Those foremost monkeys endued strength and capable of wearing any shape at will, and possessed of the splendour of the mishty Indra,-that inhabit my territories, have come and stationed themselves.

sn: त इमे बहुविक्रान्तैर्बलिभिर्भीमविक्रमैः। आगता वानरा घोरा दैत्यदानवसंनिभाः॥ ख्यातकर्मापदानाश्च बलवन्तो जितक्लमाः। पराक्रमेषु विख्याता व्यवसायेषु चोत्तमाः॥
en: And these monkeys-dreadful, and resembling Daityas and Dānvas are accompanied by powerful monkeys of terrific prowess, who have displayed their virtue in many a field, and are of famed renown in battle and, powerful, and who have mastered languor and are celebrated in prowess and sterling in their profession.

sn: पृथिव्यम्बुचरा राम नानानगनिवासिनः। कोट्योधाश्च इमे प्राप्ता वानरास्तव किंकराः॥
en: O Rāma, these koțis of apes that have arrived, inhabiting earth and water and various mountainous tracts, are at your service.

sn: निदेशवर्तिनः सर्वे सर्वे गुरुहिते स्थिताः। अभिप्रेतमनुष्ठातुं तव शक्ष्यन्त्यरिंदम॥
en: All abide by your command all are intent upon the welfare of their master, and, O subduer of foes, they are competent to bring about your end.

sn: त इमे बहुसाहस्रैरनीकैर्भीमविक्रमैः। आगता वानरा घोरा दैत्यदानवसंनिभाः॥
en: And in company with many thousands and innumerable ones that have shewn their ability in many a field, have come monkeys dreadful, and resembling Daityas and Dänavas.

sn: यन्मन्यसे नरव्याघ्र प्राप्तकालं तदुच्यताम्। त्वत्सैन्यं त्वद्वशे युक्तमाज्ञापयितुमर्हसि॥
en: If, O lion among men, you conceive that the time is ripe, tell it (to me). It behoves you to command those forces, remaining under your sway.

sn: काममेवमिदं कार्यं विदितं मम तत्त्वतः। तथापि तु यथायुक्तमाज्ञापयितुमर्हसि॥
en: Although I am full well acquainted with the work in which they are to be employed, yet you ought to order them as to what they are to accomplish.

sn: तथा ब्रुवाणं सुग्रीवं रामो दशरथात्मजः। बाहुभ्यां सम्परिष्वज्य इदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: When Sugriva had spoken thus, Dasaratha's son, Räma, embracing him with his arms, said,

sn: ज्ञायतां सौम्य वैदेही यदि जीवति वा न वा। स च देशो महाप्राज्ञ यस्मिन् वसति रावणः॥
en: O placid one, do you learn whether Videha's daughter is alive or not; as well as ascertain the country, where, O you endowed with eminent wisdom,.liveth Ravana.

sn: अधिगम्य तु वैदेहीं निलयं रावणस्य च। प्राप्तकालं विधास्यामि तस्मिन् काले सह त्वया॥
en: Having come at Vaidehi and Ravana's abode, shall I then appoint the time along with you.

sn: नाहमस्मिन् प्रभुः कार्ये वानरेन्द्र न लक्ष्मणः। त्वमस्य हेतुः कार्यस्य प्रभुश्च प्लवगेश्वर॥
en: O lord of monkeys, I am not the master in this matter, nor Lakşmaņa: you are the cause of this undertaking, as well as, O monarch of monkeys, the lord.

sn: त्वमेवाज्ञापय विभो मम कार्यविनिश्चयम्। त्वं हि जानासि मे कार्यं मम वीर न संशयः॥
en: Do you therefore, O lord, command these as to what is to be done by them in my behalf. O hero, you certainly know my business.

sn: सुहृद्वितीयो विक्रान्तः प्राज्ञः कालविशेषवित्। भवानस्मद्धिते युक्तः सुहृदाप्तोऽर्थवित्तमः॥
en: My second friend (Laksmana being first), you potent, wise, conversant with seasonableness, cognisant of profit, and engaged in our welfare.

sn: एवमुक्तस्तु सुग्रीवो विनतं नाम यूथपम्। अब्रवीद् रामसांनिध्ये लक्ष्मणस्य च धीमतः॥ शैलाभं मेघनिर्घोषमूर्जितं प्लवगेश्वरम्। सोमसूर्यनिभैः सार्धं वानरैर्वानरोत्तम॥ देशकालनयैर्युक्तो विज्ञः कार्यविनिश्चये। वृतः शतसहस्रेण वानराणां तरस्विनाम्॥ अधिगच्छ दिशं पूर्वां सशैलवनकाननाम्। तत्र सीतां च वैदेहीं निलयं रावणस्य च॥ मार्गध्वं गिरिदुर्गेषु वनेषु च नदीषु च।
en: Thus addressed, Sugrīva in presence of Rāma and the intelligent Lakşmaņa, said to a leader of herds of lord of apes, named Vinata, having the splendour of a hill, blazing and emitting sounds as those of clouds, O foremost of monkeys, accompanied with apes resembling the sun and the moon, you cognizant of time, place and morals, and sagacious in deciding course of action,-surrounded by hundreds and thousands are of active apes, march towards the Estern quarter, furnished with woods, forests and hills. There, in mountain fastnesses, and forests and rivers, do you search Videha's daughter, Sītā, as well as the abode of Rāvana.

sn: नदी भागीरथीं रम्यां सरयूं कौशिकी तथा॥ कालिन्दी यमुनां रम्यां यामुनं च महागिरिम्। सरस्वती च सिन्धुं च शोणं मणिनिभोदकम्॥ महीं कालमहीं चापि शैलकाननशोभिताम्। ब्रह्ममालान् विदेहांश्च मालवान् काशिकोसलान्॥ मागांश्च महाग्रामान् पुण्ड्रांस्त्वङ्गांस्तथैव च। भूमिं च कोशकाराणां भूमिं च रजताकराम्॥ सर्वं च तद् विचेतव्यं मृगयद्भिस्ततस्ततः। रामस्य दयितां भार्यां सीतां दशरथस्नुषाम्॥ समुद्रमवगाढांश्च पर्वतान् पत्तनानि च। मन्दरस्य च ये कोटिं संश्रिताः केचिदालयाः॥ कर्णप्रावरणाश्चैव तथा चाप्योष्ठकर्णकाः। घोरलोहमुखाश्चैव जवनाश्चैकपादकाः॥ अक्षया बलवन्तश्च तथैव पुरुषादकाः। किरातास्तीक्ष्णचूडाश्च हेमाभाः प्रियदर्शनाः॥ आममीनाशनाश्चापि किराता द्वीपवासिनः। अन्तर्जलचरा घोरा नरव्याघ्रा इति स्मृताः॥ एतेषामाश्रयाः सर्वे विचेयाः काननौकसः। गिरिभिर्ये च गम्यन्ते प्लवनेन प्लवेन च॥ यत्नवन्तो यवद्वीपं सप्तराज्योपशोभितम्। सुवर्णरूप्यकद्वीपं सुवर्णाकरमण्डितम्॥
en: And while on the search around for Rama's beloved wife, Sita, daughter-in-law to Dasaratha, you should search the beautiful Bhāgirathi, and the Sarayu, and the Kausiki; the Kalindi, and the charming Yamunā, and the mighty hill bordering thereon; and the Saraswati, and the Sindhu, and the Sona with water resembling ruby; and the Mahi and Kālamahi, garnished with woods and hills,-the large tracts-Brahmamālas, Videhas, and Mālavāns, and Kāsikosalas, and Māgadhas, and Pundras, and Angas; and grounds native to silkworms, and containing mines of silver; and mountains and cities embosmed in the sea. Do you also search through the houses in Mandara,-belonging to people having ears resembling cloths, reaching their nether lips, and mouths resembling iron,-one-footed and fleet withal; and whose descendants never, deteriorate;-and to anthropophagi; and hunters dwelling on islands; having sharp hair, goldhued, pleasing, and subsisting on raw fish; and to creatures-tiger-man forms-~-terrible to behold; and, you dwellers of woods, do you carefully search those places that are accessible by crags and bounds, and the island of Yava, adorned by seven several kingdoms, and the island of Suvarna, and Rupayaka,-thronged by gold miners.

sn: यवद्वीपमतिक्रम्य शिशिरो नाम पर्वतः। दिवं स्पृशति शृङ्गेण देवदानवसेवितः॥
en: And, going beyond the island of Yava. (one comes upon) the hill called Sisira, which pierceth the heavens by its peaks, and is inhabited by gods and demons.

sn: एतेषां गिरिदुर्गेषु प्रपातेषु वनेषु च। मार्गध्वं सहिताः सर्वे रामपत्नी यशस्विनीम्॥
en: In all these mountain fastnesses, cascades and woods, do you together search for the renowned wife of Rama.

sn: ततो रक्तजलं प्राप्य शोणाख्यं शीघ्रवाहिनम्। गत्वा पारं समुद्रस्य सिद्धचारणसेवितम्॥
en: Then, arriving at the rapid red waters going under the name of Sona, and repairing to the other shore of the ocean, the abode of Siddhas and Chāraņas, do you search all round for Răvaņa in company with Sītā in the sweet sacred spots and picturesque woods.

sn: तस्य तीर्थेषु रम्येषु विचित्रेषु वनेषु च। रावणः सह वैदेह्या मार्गितव्यस्ततस्ततः॥ पर्वतप्रभवा नद्यः सुभीमबहुनिष्कुटाः। मार्गितव्या दरीमन्तः पर्वताश्च वनानि च॥
en: And you should explore forests, mountainsprung streams, wild tracts subject to storms, and montains cer.aining ceverms.

sn: ततः समुद्रद्वीपांश्च सुभीमान् द्रष्टुमर्हथ। ऊर्मिमन्तं महारौद्रं क्रोशन्तमनिलोद्धतम्॥
en: Then it behoves you to examine horrible ocean islands, heaving with waves, terrific, resounding,-of haughty bearing in consequence of winds.

sn: तत्रासुरा महाकायाश्छायां गृहन्ति नित्यशः। ब्रह्मणा समनुज्ञाता दीर्घकालं बुभुक्षिताः॥
en: There, huge-bodied Asuras, hungering for a long period, permitted by Brahmā, capture creatures, resorting to shades.

sn: तं कालमेघप्रतिमं महोरगनिषेवितम्। अभिगम्य महानादं तीर्थेनैव महोदधिम्॥
en: And adroitly arriving at that great sea, like to clouds at the universal dissolution, inhabited by mighty snakes, sending loud sounds.

sn: ततो रक्तजलं भीमं लोहितं नाम सागरम्। गत्वा प्रेक्ष्यथ तां चैव बृहती कूटशाल्मलीम्॥ गृहं च वैनतेयस्य नानारत्नविभूषितम्। तत्र कैलाससंकाशं विहितं विश्वकर्मणा॥ तत्र शैलनिभा भीमा मन्देहा नाम राक्षसाः। शैलशृङ्गेषु लम्बन्ते नानारूपा भयावहाः॥
en: And there, after passing the terrific sea of red waters called Yellow, you will behold a mighty knarled Śālmali. There, built by Viśvakarmā, peak-like, gigantic, resembling Kailāsa, (towere) the mansion of Vinata's offspring. There, grim Raksasas named Mandehas, resembling hills, of diverse shapes, capable of inspiring fear, hang head foremost on the rocks.

sn: ते पतन्ति जले नित्यं सूर्यस्योदयनं प्रति। अभितप्ताः स्म सूर्येण लम्बन्ते स्म पुनः पुनः।॥
en: Day after day at sunrise, these Rākşasas heated (by solar rays) and struck dead by Brahmā energy,* again and again (hang on the crags). *The commentator explains: energy darted from the three orders.

sn: निहता ब्रह्मतेजोभिरहन्यहनि राक्षसाः। ततः पाण्डुरमेघाभं क्षीरोदं नाम सागरम्॥
en: Then wilt you, O you that are hard to repress, proceeding, view the sea named Kșiroda, having the hue of pale clouds, and looking like a necklace, because of the ripples (on its surface).

sn: गत्वा द्रक्ष्यथ दुर्धर्षा मुक्ताहारमिवोर्मिभिः। तस्य मध्ये महाश्वेतो ऋषभो नाम पर्वतः॥ दिव्यगन्धैः कुसुमितैराचितैश्च नगैर्वृतः। सरश्च राजतैः पद्मज्वलितैर्हेमकेसरैः॥ नाम्ना सुदर्शनं नाम राजहंसैः समाकुलम्।
en: In it there are the mighty white mountain going by the name of Rsabha, covered with trees bearing odorous blossoms; as well as the tank known under the name of Sudarśana, swarming with swans and shining silver lotuses having golden filaments.

sn: विबुधाश्चारणा यक्षाः किंनराश्चाप्सरोगणाः॥ हृष्टाः समधिगच्छन्ति नलिनी तां रिरंसवः।
en: Desirous of sport, resort to this tank delighted troops of Vivudhas and Charanas, Yaksas, Kinnaras and Apsarās.

sn: क्षीरोदं समतिक्रम्य तदा द्रक्ष्यथ वानराः॥ जलोदं सागरं शीघ्रं सर्वभूतभयावहम्। तत्र तत्कोपजं तेजः कृतं हयमुखं महत्॥ अस्याद्भुतं महावेगमोदनं सचराचरम्। तत्र विक्रोशतां नादो भूतानां सागरौकसाम्। श्रूयते चासमर्थानां दृष्ट्वाभूद् वडवामुखम् ॥
en: Leaving behind Ksiroda, O monkeys, you will soon after behold the Jaloda sea, striking terror into all beings. There presideth that mighty ireborn Energy of him*. (embodied in) the mouth of a mule. This wondrous (universe) containing mobile and immobile things and fraught with great impetus, is the aliment of this Energy. There are heard the cries of feeble creatures inhabiting the sea, who began to wail on witnessing the mouth of the mule. *Sage Aurvi.

sn: स्वादूदस्योत्तरे तीरे योजनानि त्रयोदश। जातरूपशिलो नाम सुमहान् कनकप्रभः॥
en: On the north of the Swādu sea, lie thirteen Yojanas (of land), named Jātarūpasila, * exceeding spacious, and of the splendour of gold. Lit. of gold and stone.

sn: तत्र चन्द्रप्रतीकाशं पन्नगं धरणीधरम्। पद्मपत्रविशालाक्षं ततो द्रक्ष्यथ वानराः। ५१।। आसीनं पर्वतस्याने सर्वदेवनमस्कृतम्। सहस्रशिरसं देवमनन्तं नीलवाससम्॥
en: There, you monkeys, you will behold that serpent, the holder of Earth-resembling the moon, and with expansive eyes like lotuspetals-seated at the summit of the mount,-that one worshipped of all deities, having a thousand heads,-the god Ananta, clad in blue apparel.

sn: त्रिशिराः काञ्चनः केतुस्तालस्तस्य महात्मनः। स्थापितः पर्वतस्यागे विराजति सवेदिकः॥
en: And by the dais (there) at the top of the mount is the golden palm, planted by that high souled one,—which is like a banner.

sn: पूर्वस्यां दिशि निर्माणं कृतं तत् त्रिदशेश्वरैः। ततः परं हेममयः श्रीमानुदयपर्वतः॥
en: The chief of the celestials reared it in the Eastern region. After that is the fair Rising mountain.

sn: तस्य कोटिर्दिवं स्पृष्ट्वा शतयोजनमायता। जातरूपमयी दिव्या विराजति सवेदिका॥ सालैस्तालैस्तमालैश्च कर्णिकारैश्च पुष्पितैः। जातरूपमयैर्दिव्यैः शोभते सूर्यसंनिभैः५६।।
en: Its golden peak measuring a hundred Yojanas, reaching to the heavens, rises nobly, with mountains at its base; and looks beautiful with Sālas, palms, Tamālas, and flowering Karnikāras,-golden, splendid and resembling the sun.

sn: तत्र योजनविस्तारमुच्छ्रितं दशयोजनम्। शृङ्ग सौमनसं नाम जातरूपमयं ध्रुवम्।
en: There, spreading a Yojana around, towering up ten, is the peak named Saumanasa-all certainly of gold.

sn: तत्र पूर्वं पदं कृत्वा पुरा विष्णुस्त्रिविक्रमे। द्वितीयं शिखरे मेरोश्चकार पुरुषोत्तमः॥
en: There, formerly on the occasion of invading the earth with three paces, that foremost of persons, Vişņu, planting his first foot planted the other on the summit of Meru.

sn: उत्तरेण परिक्रम्य जम्बूद्वीपं दिवाकरः। दृश्यो भवति भूयिष्ठं शिखरं तन्महोच्छ्रयम्॥
en: The sun, having passed by Jambūdwipa on the north, and, arriving at that mighty and eminent summit, (Saumanasa), again becomes visible to the dwellers of Jambūdwipa.

sn: तत्र वैखानसा नाम वालखिल्या महर्षयः।
en: There are seen those Vālakhilya Maharșis, named Vaikhānasas,-wearing the hue of the sun, leading an ascetic mode of life.

sn: अयं सुदर्शनो द्वीपः पुरो यस्य प्रकाशते। तस्मिंस्तेजश्च चक्षुश्च सर्वप्राणभृतामपि॥
en: This is the island of Sudarsana, before which all creatures inspire energy and have their sight granted to them.

sn: शैलस्य तस्य पृष्ठेषु कन्दरेषु वनेषु च। रावणः सह वैदेह्या मार्गितव्यस्ततस्ततः॥
en: You should search for Rāvana with Vaidehi all round the top of that mountain as well as in its forests and woods.

sn: काञ्चनस्य च शैलस्य सूर्यस्य च महात्मनः। आविष्टा तेजसा संध्या पूर्वा रक्ता प्रकाशते॥
en: (Here) the first twilight enfolded in the glory of the golden hill and that of the high-souled Sun, appeareth roseate.

sn: पूर्वमेतत् कृतं द्वारं पृथिव्या भुवनस्य च। सूर्यस्योदयनं चैव पूर्वा ह्येषा दिगुच्यते॥
en: As this is the first gateway of both Earth and Heaven, and as the sun first rises in this quarter, this is called the East.

sn: तस्य शैलस्य पृष्ठेषु निझरेषु गुहासु च। रावणः सह वैदेह्या मार्गितव्यस्ततस्ततः॥
en: You should search the breast of its mountain, and fountains, and caves for Rāvana in company with Vaidehi.

sn: ततः परमगम्या स्याद् दिक्पूर्वा त्रिदशावृता। रहिता चन्द्रसूर्याभ्यामदृश्या तमसावृता॥
en: Beyond that, is the exceedingly impassable Eastern quarter, thronged by the celestials, covered with darkness and devoid of the sun and the moon.

sn: शैलेषु तेषु सर्वेषु कन्दरेषु नदीषु च। ये च नोक्ता मयोद्देशा विचेया तेषु जानकी॥
en: Do you search for Jānaki in all those rocks, woods and streams as well as in such spots as I have not mentioned.

sn: एतावद् वानरैः शक्यं गन्तुं वानरपुङ्गवाः। अभास्करममर्यादं न जानीमस्ततः परम्॥
en: You foremost of monkeys, the monkeys are competent to proceed thus far. Beyond this, of the tract without sun and without limit, I know nothing.

sn: अभिगम्य तु वैदेहीं निलयं रावणस्य च। मासे पूर्णे निवर्तध्वमुदयं प्राप्य पर्वतम् ॥
en: Meeting with Vaidehi and arriving at) Rāvana's mansion, do you, having reached the Rising hill, turn back, when it shall be a full month.

sn: ऊर्ध्वं मासान्न वस्तव्यं वसन् वध्यो भवेन्मम। सिद्धार्थाः संनिवर्तध्वमधिगम्य च मैथिलीम्॥
en: Do not stay longer than a month. If you do, you shall be slain by me. Having attained your end, do you turn back, having met with Maithili.

sn: महेन्द्रकान्तां वनषण्डमण्डितां दिशं चरित्वा निपुणेन वानराः। अवाप्य सीतां रघुवंशजप्रियां ततो निवृत्ताः सुखिनो भविष्यथ। ७१।।
en: Having adroitly explored (the tract) loved of Mahendra, plated with woods, do you, you monkeys, having come at Sītā—the beloved wife of that descendant of Raghu-desist, attaining happiness.

sn: ततः प्रस्थाप्य सुग्रीवस्तन्महद्वानरं बलम्। दक्षिणां प्रेषयामास वानरानभिलक्षितान्॥
en: Then having sent away that mighty host of monkeys, Sugriva despatched to the South others competent to perform the several tasks entrusted to them.

sn: नीलमग्निसुतं चैव हनूमन्तं च वानरम्। पितामहसुतं चैव जाम्बवन्तं महौजसम्॥ सुहोत्रं च शरारि च शरगुल्मं तथैव च। गजं गवाक्षं गवयं सुषेणं वृषभं तथा॥ मैन्दं च द्विविदं चैव सुषेणं गन्धमादनम्। उल्कामुखमनङ्गं च हुताशनसुताबुभौ॥ अङ्गदप्रमुखान् वीरान् वीरः कपिगणेश्वरः। वेगविक्रमसम्पन्नान् संदिदेश विशेषवित्॥ तेषामग्रेसरं चैव बृहद्बलमथाङ्गदम्। विधाय हरिवीराणामादिशद् दक्षिणां दिशम्॥ ये केचन समुद्देशास्तस्यां दिशि सुदुर्गमाः। कपीशः कपिमुख्यानां स तेषां समुदाहरत्॥
en: And appointing the exceedingly mighty Angada as the leader of those heroic monkeys, that hero, the lord of monkey bands, conversant with the countries intended to be explored, despatched heroes endowed with speed and prowess, headed by Angada, Nīla the son of Fire, and the monkey Hanumān; and the exceedingly energetic Jämbavān, son to the Great-father, and Suhotra, and Sarari, and Saragulma, Gaja, Gavaksya, and Gavaya, Sus ena, Vrsabha, Mainda, Dvivida, and Gandhamādana, and Ulkāmukha and Anangasons of Fire both. And the lord of monkeys began to describe to the monkey-chiefs those tracts in those directions, that were difficult of access.
