sn: सहस्रशिरसं विन्ध्यं नानादुमलतायुतम्। नर्मदां च नदी रम्यां महोरगनिषेविताम्॥ ततो गोदावरी रम्या कृष्णवेणीं महानदीम्। वरदां च महाभागां महोरगनिषेविताम्। मेखलानुत्कलांश्चैव दशार्णनगराण्यपि॥ आब्रवन्तीमवन्ती च सर्वमेवानुपश्यत। विदर्भानृष्टिकांश्चैव रम्यान् माहिषकानपि॥ तथा मत्स्यकलिङ्गांश्च कौशिकांश्च समन्ततः। अन्वीक्ष्य दण्डकारण्यं सपर्वतनदीगुहम्॥ नदी गोदावरी चैव सर्वमेवानुपश्यत। तथैवान्ध्रांश्च पुण्ड्रांश्च चोलान्पाण्ड्यांश्च केरलान्॥
en: You will behold Vindhya having an hundred summits, and furnished with various trees and shrubs, and the romantic river Narmada, frequented by mighty serpents; and the Godāvari', and that mighty river, the captivating Krşnaveņi, and the Mekhalās and Utkalas, and the cities of Dasarna; and Avravanti and Avanti, and the Vidarbhas and Nishtikas and the charming Māhișakas.? And you will see also the Matsyas and Kalingas and Kausikas all round, and the forest of Dandaka, with mountains, rivers and caverns; and the river Godāvarī,' and the Andhras, and Paundras, he Cholas, the Pandyas, and the Keralas. 1. The commentator says, The Godavari flowing through the countries to t'ie east of the Vindya mountains. 2. Some text read-Ristikas instead. 3. The tract, according to Rāmānuja, watered by the Godāvari in the vicinity of Dandaka.

sn: अयोमुखश्च गन्तव्यः पर्वतो धातुमण्डितः। विचित्रशिखरः श्रीमांश्चित्रपुष्पितकाननः॥ सुचन्दनवनोद्देशो मार्गितव्यो महागिरिः।
en: Then shall you repair to the mountain Ayomukha,* plated with ore, having taking summits, graceful, furnished with picturesque flowering woods,-the mighty mountain having groves of excellent sandal. *Another name of this hill is Malaya.

sn: ततस्तामापगां दिव्यां प्रसन्नसलिलाशयाम्॥ तत्र द्रक्ष्यथ कावेरी विहतामप्सरोगणैः।
en: At the foot of the Malaya mountain endued with exceeding energy, you will behold the noble stream Kāveri, of pleasant waters, where sport troops of Apsarās.

sn: तस्यासीनं नगस्याग्रे मलयस्य महौजसम्॥ द्रक्ष्यथादित्यसंकाशमगस्त्यमृषिसत्तमम्।
en: (There) you will see that foremost of saints, Agastya, resembling the sun.

sn: ततस्तेनाभ्यनुज्ञाताः प्रसन्नेन महात्मना॥ ताम्रपर्णी ग्राहजुष्टां तरिष्यथ महानदीम्।
en: Permitted by that gratified high-souled one, you will cross over the great river, Tăniraparni, abounding in alligators.

sn: सा चन्दनवनैश्चित्रैः प्रच्छन्नद्वीपवारिणी॥ कान्तेव युवती कान्तं समुद्रमवगाहते।
en: Like a youthful female in relation to her lover, she (Tāmraparni), with both her waters as well as islets concealed under beautiful sandal woods, bathes in the sea.

sn: ततो हेममयं दिव्यं मुक्तामणिविभूषितम्॥ युक्तं कवाटं पाण्ड्यानां गता द्रक्ष्यथ वानराः।
en: Proceeding (therefrom), the monkeys shall see the grand golden gates belonging to the walls of the capital of the Pāndyas.

sn: ततः समुद्रमासाद्य सम्प्रधार्यार्थनिश्चयम्॥ अगस्त्येनान्तरे तत्र सागरे विनिवेशितः। चित्रसानुनगः श्रीमान् महेन्द्रः पर्वतोत्तमः॥
en: Then arriving at the main, you shall ascertain your ability or otherwise of crossing the same. In the bosom of the deep there, Agastya has placed that foremost of mountains-the charming Mahendra, having picturesque plateaus; golden, and beautiful,-with a portion of it sunk in the great ocean.

sn: जातरूपमयः श्रीमानवगाढो महार्णवम्। नानाविधैर्नगैः फुल्लैलताभिश्चोपशोभितम्॥ देवर्षियक्षप्रवरैरप्सरोभिश्च शोभितम्। सिद्धचारणसङ्घश्च प्रकीर्णं सुमनोरमम्॥ तमुपैति सहस्राक्षः सदा पर्वसु पर्वसु।
en: For aye, He of a thousand eyes at Parvas visiteth this mountain embellished by various blossoming trees and creepers; beauteous with divinities, and saints, and the foremost Yaksas and Apsarās; thronged by numbers of Siddhas and Chāraṇas; and of surpassing loveliness.

sn: द्वीपस्तस्यापरे पारे शतयोजनविस्तृतः॥ अगम्यो मानुषैर्दीप्तस्तं मार्गध्वं समन्ततः। तत्र सर्वात्मना सीता मार्गितव्या विशेषतः॥
en: On its other shore is an island extending over an hundred Yojanas, inaccessible to men*, and of splendid aspect. Do you explore it all round. There, in particular, you must every way search for Sita. *Because, says the commentator,. of the profusion of gold in it.

sn: स हि देशस्तु वध्यस्य रावणस्य दुरात्मनः। राक्षसाधिपतेर्वासः सहस्राक्षसमद्युतेः॥
en: That country belongs to the impious Rāvana, worthy of being slain—the lord of Raksasas, like to the thousand-eyed (deity) in splendour.

sn: दक्षिणस्य समुद्रस्य मध्ये तस्य तु राक्षसी। अङ्गारकेति विख्याता छायामाक्षिप्य भोजनी ॥
en: In the midst of the Southern sea belonging to him (Ravana), there is a Raksasi, named Angāraketi, who procureth her pray by casting her shadow.

sn: एवं निःसंशयान् कृत्वा संशयानष्टसंशयाः। मृगयध्वं नरेन्द्रस्य पत्नीममिततेजसः॥
en: Having (by your search) satisfied yourselves as to those countries where you might suspect Sītā to be, do you, your doubts dispelled, proceeding beyond that, (Lankā), search for the spouse of that monarch endued with unbounded energy.

sn: तमतिक्रम्य लक्ष्मीवान् समुद्रे शतयोजने। गिरिः पुष्पितको नाम सिद्धचारणसेवितः॥ चन्द्रसूर्यांशुसंकाशः सागराम्बुसमाश्रयः। भ्राजते विपुलैः शृङ्गैरम्बरं विलिखन्निव॥ तस्यैकं काञ्चनं शृङ्ग सेवते यं दिवाकरः। न तं कृतघ्नाः पश्यन्ति न नृशंसा न नास्तिकाः॥
en: In the sea extending over an hundred Yojanas, a lovely hill, named Puspitaka, the abode of Siddhas and Chăraņas; resembling the rays of the sun or the moon,-resting on the waters of the ocean, looks splendid, piercing the heavens with its giant peaks. Of this (mountain), there is a particular golden summit, which the sun approaches. It is incapable of being beheld by the ungrateful or the atheistical.

sn: प्रणम्य शिरसा शैलं तं विमार्गथ वानराः। तमतिक्रम्य दुर्धर्षं सूर्यवान्नाम पर्वतः॥ अध्वना दुर्विगाहेन योजनानि चतुर्दश। ततस्तमप्यतिक्रम्य वैद्युतो नाम पर्वतः॥ सर्वकामफलैर्वृक्षैः सर्वकालमनोहरैः। तत्र भुक्त्वा वराहा॑णि मूलानि च फलानि च॥ मधूनि पीत्वा जुष्टानि परं गच्छत वानराः।
en: Bowing your heads down to this hill, let the monkeys search on. Leaving behind that irrepressible one, (you will come upon) a mountain difficult of approach, extending over fourteen Yojanas, named Suryyavān. Passing by that also, (you will see) a mountain, named Vidyut, filled with trees, beautiful at all seasons, and bearing all desirable fruits. There, feeding upon excellent an costly fruits and roots, and drinking delicious honey, let the monkeys pass beyond it.

sn: तत्र नेत्रमन:क्रान्तः कुञ्जरो नाम पर्वतः॥ अगस्त्यभवनं यत्र निर्मितं विश्वकर्मणा। तत्र योजनविस्तारमुच्छ्रितं दशयोजनम्॥ शरणं काञ्चनं दिव्यं नानारत्नविभूषितम्।
en: There is the hill named Kunjara, grateful both to the eye and the mind, where Viśvakarmā had built the abode of Agastya*. There (rises) that stately golden pile, adorned with various gems, extending over one Yojana, and ten in height. *i.e. in that hill.

sn: तत्र भोगवती नाम सर्पाणामालयः पुरी॥ विशालरथ्य दुर्धर्षा सर्वतः परिरक्षिता। रक्षिता पन्नगै।रैस्तीक्ष्णदंष्ट्रैर्महाविषैः॥ सर्पराजो महाघोरो यस्यां वसति वासुकिः। निर्याय मार्गितव्या च सा च भोगवती पुरी॥
en: In it also there is that palace, which is the abode of snakes; having spacious ways, i incapable of being captured, guarded around, and protected by dreadful snakes and sharptoothed serpents of virulent poison; where dwelleth Vāsuki, the exceedingly terrible king of snakes. Proceeding heedfully, you must explore that Bhogavatī palace; also whatever concealed place may lie there.

sn: तत्र चानन्तरोद्देशा ये केचन समावृताः। तं च देशमतिक्रम्य महानृषभसंस्थितिः॥ सर्वरत्नमयः श्रीमानृषभो नाम पर्वतः। गोशीर्षकं पद्मकं च हरिश्यामं च चन्दनम्॥ दिव्यमुत्पद्यते यत्र तच्चैवाग्निसमप्रभम्। न तु तच्चन्दनं दृष्ट्वा स्प्रष्टव्यं तु कदाचन ॥ रोहिता नाम गन्धर्वा घोरं रक्षन्ति तद्वनम्। तत्र गन्धर्वपतयः पञ्च सूर्यसमप्रभाः॥ शैलूषो ग्रामीणी: शिक्षः शुको बभ्रुस्तथैव च। रविसोमाग्निवपुषां निवासः पुण्यकर्मणाम्॥ अन्ते पृथिव्या दुर्धर्षास्ततः स्वर्गजितः स्थिताः।
en: Going beyond that place, (you will see) the mighty mountain named Śrinrsabha, in the form of a bull, full of all gems, and possessed of grace, where are produced excellent Gośirs aka, Padmaka, and Haricyāma sandals, and which in effulgence resembles fire. But, seeing that sandal, you must by no means ask any as questions; certain Gandharvas, named Rohitas, are on guard over that that wood—the lords of Gandharvas, in splendour like to five suns, Cailusha, Grāmani, Siksa, Suka, and Babhru. After that, (Rhisava), at the extremity of the Earth is the abode of persons of pious acts, whose bodies are composed of the Sun, the Moon and Fire.

sn: ततः परं न वः सेव्यः पितृलोकः सुदारुणः॥ राजधानी यमस्यैषा कष्टेन तमसाऽऽवृता।
en: And there reside persons who have won the heavenly regions. After that are the awful regions of the ancestral manes, which you must not approach. This is the metropolis of Yama, covered by deep gloom.

sn: एतावदेव युष्माभिर्वीरा वानरपुंगवाः। शक्यं विचेतुं गन्तुं वा नातो गतिमतां गतिः॥
en: You heroic monkey chiefs, you can seek thus far. Further there is no course for those endued with motion.

sn: सर्वमेतत् समालोक्य यच्चान्यदपि दृश्यते। गतिं विदित्वा वैदेह्याः संनिवर्तितुमर्हथ ॥
en: Having examined all these, as well others that may come within your ken, it behoves you, after having ascertained Vaidehi's course, to return (hither).

sn: यश्च मासानिवृत्तोऽग्रे दृष्ट्वा सीतेति वक्ष्यति। मत्तुल्यविभवो भोगैः सुखं स विहरिष्यति॥
en: He that, returning within a month, shall say,—I have seen Sītā,' shall pass his days in happiness, enjoying affluence like mine own and indulging all pleasures.

sn: ततः प्रियतरो नास्ति मम प्राणाद् विशेषतः। कृतापराधो बहुशो मम बन्धुभविष्यति ॥
en: He shall be dearer to me than life itself, and none dearer (to me) that he; and although he might commit innumerable wrongs, still should he become my friend.

sn: अमितबलपराक्रमा भवन्तो विपुलगुणेषु कुलेषु च प्रसूताः। मनुजपतिसुतां यथा लभध्वं तदधिगुणं पुरुषार्थमारभध्वम्॥
en: Possessed of immeasurable strength and prowess, and sprung from lines crowned with sterling virtues, do you strive manfully in such a glorious way that the king's daughter may be recovered. prowess, and sprung from lines crowned with sterling virtues, do you strive manfully in such a glorious way that the king's daughter may be recovered.

sn: अथ प्रस्थाप्य स हरीन् सुग्रीवो दक्षिणां दिशम्। अब्रवीन्मेघसंकाशं सुषेणं नाम वानरम्॥ तारायाः पितरं राजा श्वशुरं भीमविक्रमम्। अब्रवीत् प्राञ्जलिवाक्यमभिगम्य प्रणम्य च॥ महर्षिपुत्रं मारीचमर्चिष्मन्तं महाकपिम्। वृतं कपिवरैः शूरैर्महेन्द्रसदृशद्युतिम्॥ बुद्धिविक्रमसम्पन्नं वैनतेयसमद्युतिम्। मरीचिपुत्रान् मारीचानचिर्माल्यान् महाबलान्॥ ऋषिपुत्रांश्च तान् सर्वान्प्रतीचीमादिशद् दिशम्। द्वाभ्यां शतसहस्राभ्यां कपीनां कपिसत्तमाः॥ सुषेणप्रमुखा यूयं वैदेही परिमार्गथ।
en: Having despatched those monkeys in a southern direction, Sugrīva spoke to the monkey named Susena, resembling a mass of clouds. Approaching his father-in-law, Tara's father, possessed of dreadful prowess, the king, bowing and with joined hands, spoke to him. And Sugriva commanded the Maharsi's son, Marica, and the mighty ape Archishmat, surrounded by the heroic foremost of monkeys,-possessing the splendour of Mahendra, gifted with sense and vigour; and resembling the offspring himself of Vinată in brightness; and Mārīci's son,-the Mārīcas—the mighty Archirmālyas,-all these sons of the saint*. (to march) towards the West, saying,-You monkey-chiefs, let twice hundred thousand monkeys led by Sușeņa (set out) to search Vaidehi. Märīci.

sn: सौराष्ट्रान् सहबाह्रीकांश्चन्द्रचित्रांस्तथैव च॥ स्फीताञ्जनपदान् रम्यान् विपुलानि पुराणि च। पुंनागगहनं कुक्षिं बकुलोद्दालकाकुलम्॥ तथा केतकखण्डांश्च मार्गध्वं हरिपुङ्गवाः। प्रत्यक्स्रोतोवहाश्चैव नद्यः शीतजला: शिवाः॥ तापसानामरण्यानि कान्तारगिरयश्च ये।
en: You foremost of monkeys, do you explore the Saurastras, the Bahlikas, the Candracitrās, and (other) populous and fair provinces and spacious cities, and Kuksi, dense with Punnāgas,* and filled with Bakulas and Uddālakas; as well as the tracts covered with Ketaka and auspicious streams bearing their cool waters westwards; and the forests of ascetics; and mountains embosoming woods. *Rottleria Tinctoria.

sn: तत्र स्थलीमरुप्राया अत्युच्चशिशिराः शिलाः॥ गिरिजालावृतां दुर्गा मार्गित्वा पश्चिमां दिशम्। ततः पश्चिममागम्य समुद्रं द्रष्टुमहर्थ॥ तिमिनक्राकुलजलं गत्वा द्रक्ष्यथ वानराः। ततः केतकखण्डेषु तमालगहनेषु च॥ कपयो विहरिष्यन्ति नारिकेलवनेषु च। तत्र सीतां च मार्गध्वं निलयं रावणस्य च॥
en: There having explored tracts resembling deserts, and cold cliffs towering high, and the West, covered with mountain ranges, and extremely difficult of access,-and proceeding at a little more to the west, it behoves you a view of the sea. And proceeding on, you monkeys, you shall see (the ocean), whose waters abound in whales and alligators, you monkeys.* Then the apes shall sport in tracts covered by Ketakas, and dense with Tamālas and woods of coconuts. There shall you look for $ītā and the mansion of Rāvana, *The grammar of these slokas is exceedingly vicious; and it has cost the Translator no small amount of labour to assign the necessary logical nexus in a good many praces:

sn: वेलातलनिविष्टेषु पर्वतेषु वनेषु च। मुरचीपत्तनं चैव रम्यं चैव जटापुरम्॥ अवन्तीमङ्गलेषां च तथा चालक्षितं वनम्। राष्ट्राणि च विशालानि पत्तनानि ततस्ततः॥
en: In hills and woods on the shores of the sea; and (explore) Muracipattana, and the delightful Jațāpura, and Avantī, and Angalepā, as well as in the wood (called) Alaksita, and spacious monarchies, and emporiums.

sn: सिन्धुसागरयोश्चैव संगमे तत्र पर्वतः। महान् सोमगिरि म शतशृङ्गो महाद्रुमः॥ तत्र प्रस्थेषु रम्येषु सिंहा पक्षगमाः स्थिताः। तिमिमत्स्यगजांश्चैव नीडान्यारोपयन्ति ते॥
en: There is a mighty mountain where the Sindhu falls into the sea, Somagiri by name; having an hundred summits and tall trees. In its plateaus there are certain birds (called) Sinhas. These lift up to their nests whales and elephants.

sn: तानि नीडानि सिंहानां गिरिशृङ्गगताश्च ये। दृप्तास्तृप्ताश्च मातङ्गास्तोयदस्वननिःस्वनाः॥ विचरन्ति विशालेऽस्मिंस्तोयपूर्णे समन्ततः।
en: The proud elephants carried to the nests and remaining on the summits of the mountain, possessing the roar of clouds, having been gratified (with food), range around this extensive table-land filled with water.

sn: तस्य शृङ्ग दिवस्पर्श काञ्चनं चित्रपादपम्॥ सर्वमाशु विचेतव्यं कपिभिः कामरूपिभिः।
en: The monkeys, capable of wearing shapes at will, should swiftly search its golden summit towering to the sky and filled with graceful trees.

sn: कोटिं तत्र समुद्रस्य काञ्चनीं शतयोजनाम्॥ दुर्दशां पारियात्रस्य गत्वा द्रक्ष्यथ वानराः।
en: Proceeding further, the monkeys shall behold the golden summit of Pāriyātra rising from the sea and extending over an hundred Yojanas.

sn: कोट्यस्तत्र चतुर्विंशद् गन्धर्वाणां तपस्विनाम्॥ वसन्त्यग्निनिकाशानां घोराणां पापकर्मणाम्। पावकार्चिः प्रतीकाशाः समवेताः समन्ततः॥
en: There dwell all around in a body four and twenty kotis of ascetic Gandharvas, resembling fire, dreadful, practicising impiety, and like to flames of fire.

sn: नात्यासादयितव्यास्ते वानरैर्भीमविक्रमैः। नादेयं च फलं तस्माद्देशात् किंचित् प्लवङ्गमैः॥
en: The monkeys of dreadful prowess should not present themselves before those, nor should they take any fruits from that country.

sn: दुरासदा हि ते वीराः सत्त्ववन्तो महाबलाः। फलामूलानि ते तत्र रक्षन्ते भीमविक्रमाः॥
en: Those heroes are hard to approach; and they are truthful and possessed of great might. And there they of dreadful prowess stow away their fruits and roots.

sn: तत्र यत्नश्च कर्तव्यो मार्गितव्या च जानकी। नहि तेभ्यो भयं किंचित् कपित्वमनुवर्तताम्॥
en: There you should heedfully search for Jānakī. you have no fear whatever from them; do you only follow your native nature as monkeys.

sn: तत्र वैदूर्यवर्णाभो वज्रसंस्थानसंस्थितः। नानागुमलताकीर्णो वज्रो नाम महागिरिः॥ श्रीमान् समुदितस्तत्र योजनानां शतं समम्। गुहास्तत्र विचेतव्या प्रयत्नेन प्लवङ्गमाः॥
en: There, in hue like lapises, abounding in various kinds of trees and plants, is a mighty hill of an adamantine basis, called Vajra; beautiful, famous, and measuring an hundred Yojanas in height and area. There let the monkeys carefully explore the caves.

sn: चतुर्भागे समुद्रस्य चक्रवान् नाम पर्वतः। तत्र चक्रं सहस्रारं निर्मितं विश्वकर्मणा ॥
en: On the fourth side of the Ocean is a mountain named Cakravān. There Viśvakarmā forged the discus (called) Sahasrāra.

sn: तत्र पञ्चजनं हत्वा हयग्रीवं च दानवम्। आजहार ततश्चक्रं शङ्ख च पुरुषोत्तमः॥
en: There, slaying Panchajana and the Dānava, Hayagriva*, the best of male beings obtained the discus as well as the conch. *Lit. horse-necked.

sn: तस्य सानुषु रम्येषु विशालासु गुहासु च। रावणः सह वैदह्या मार्गितव्यस्ततस्ततः॥
en: In those beautiful plateous and huge caves, you should everywhere search for Rāvana with Videha's daughter.

sn: योजनानि चतुःषष्टिर्वराहो नाम पर्वतः। सुवर्णशृङ्गः सुमहानगाधे वरुणालये॥
en: Sunk in the depths of the sea, is a very great mountain named Varāha, having golden peaks and measuring four and sixty yojanas.

sn: तत्र प्राग्ज्योतिषं नाम जातरूपमयं पुरम्। यस्मिन् वसति दुष्टात्मा नरको नाम दानवः ॥
en: In it is a city named Prāgjyotişa, all of gold. There dwells the wicked Dänava named Naraka.* *i.e. in the Varadha hill.

sn: तत्र सानुषु रम्येषु विशालासु गुहासु च। रावणः सह वैदेह्या मार्गितव्यस्ततस्ततः॥
en: There do you everywhere search for Rāvana along with Vaidehi in the beautiful plateaus and huge caves.

sn: तमतिक्रम्य शैलेन्द्र काञ्चनान्तरदर्शनम्। पर्वतः सर्वसौवर्णो धाराप्रस्रवणायुतः॥
en: Passing beyond that foremost of mountains, whose sight betrays the secret of its bowels being freighted with gold, (you shall come upon) the mountain Sarvasauvarna, furnished with fountains and cascades.

sn: तं गजाश्च वराहाश्च सिंहा व्याघ्राश्च सर्वतः। अभिगर्जन्ति सततं तेन शब्देन दर्पिताः॥
en: Coming to it, elephants, and boars, and lions, and tigers, on all sides roar ceaselessly, wrought up by the echoes their own cries have produced.

sn: यस्मिन् हरिहयः श्रीमान् महेन्द्रः पाकशासनः। अभिषिक्तः सुरै राजा मेघो नाम स पर्वतः॥
en: This is the mountain named Megha, where the graceful green-horsed vanquisher of Pāka, Mahendra, was installed king by the gods.

sn: तमतिक्रम्य शैलेन्द्र महेन्द्रपरिपालितम्। षष्टिं गिरिसहस्राणि काञ्चनानि गमिष्यथ॥ तरुणादित्यवर्णानि भ्राजमानानि सर्वशः। जातरूपमयैर्वृक्षैः शोभितानि सुपुष्पितैः॥
en: Having passed by that mountain protected by Mahendra, you shall repair to sixty thousand hills of gold; in hue like the infant sun, and blazing on all sides and embellished by blossoming golden trees,

sn: तेषां मध्ये स्थितो राजा मेरुरुत्तमपर्वतः। आदित्येन प्रसन्नेन शैलो दत्तवरः पुरा ॥ तेनैवमुक्तः शैलेन्द्रः सर्व एव त्वदाश्रयाः। मत्प्रसादाद् भविष्यन्ति दिवा रात्रौ च काञ्चनाः॥ त्वयि ये चापि वत्स्यन्ति देवगन्धर्वदानवाः। ते भविष्यन्ति भक्ताश्च प्रभया काञ्चनप्रभाः॥
en: In the midst of them is established as king, Meru, best of mountains, formerly the Sun being well pleased, conferred a boon on this mountain, and he addressed the mountain, saying,—'By my grace all the hills that are under your protection, shall be golden day and night; and also those gods Gandharvas and Dānvas that shall dwell in you, shall be filled with reverence for me and to the boot attain a golden glory.'

sn: विश्वेदेवाश्च वसवो मरुतश्च दिवौकसः। आगत्य पश्चिमां संध्यां मेरुमुत्तमपर्वतम्॥ आदित्यमुपतिष्ठन्ति तैश्च सूर्योऽभिपूजितः। अदृश्यः सर्वभूतानामस्तं गच्छति पर्वतम्।॥
en: Coming to the excellent mountain Meru. Viśvadevas, the Vasus, the Maruts and the celestials, adore the Sun in the western twilight. Adored by them, the Sun, becoming invisible, repaireth to the Setting hill*. The commentator remarks: Although not expressly stated, it is implied that the islands to the west of it are also to be searched.

sn: योजनानां सहस्राणि दश तानि दिवाकरः। मुहूर्तार्धन तं शीघ्रमभियाति शिलोच्चयम्॥
en: In half a muhurta, the Sun swiftly passes over this (mountain), measuring, as it does, ten thousand Yojanas.

sn: शृङ्गे तस्य महद्दिव्यं भवनं सूर्यसंनिभम्। प्रासादगणसम्बाधं विहितं विश्वकर्मणा॥ शोभितं तरुभिश्चित्रै नापक्षिसमाकुलैः। निकेतं पाशहस्तस्य वरुणस्य महात्मनः॥
en: On its peak rises an edifice; resembling the sun (in splendour); consisting of palatial mansions built by Viśvakarmā; and graced by goodly trees rife with various birds,-the residence of the high-souled Varuna, bearing the noose in his hand.

sn: अन्तरा मेरुमस्तं च तालो दशशिरा महान्। जातरूपमयः श्रीमान् भ्राजते चित्रवेदिकः॥
en: Between Meru and the Setting hill, towers a tall palm having ten heads. Golden and graceful, it shineth on a variegated dais.

sn: तेषु सर्वेषु दुर्गेषु सरस्सु च सरित्सु च। रावणः सह वैदेह्या मार्गितव्यस्ततस्ततः॥
en: In all these, difficult of access, as also in rivers and tanks, you should thoroughly search for Rāvana along with Vaidehī.

sn: यत्र तिष्ठति धर्मज्ञस्तपसा स्वेन भावितः। मेरुसावर्णिरित्येष ख्यातो चै ब्रह्मणा समः॥ ।।
en: There dwells there the righteous and famous Merusāvarani, sanctified by virtue of his own ascesticism, and like to Brahmā himself*. *Like to Prajāpati dwelling by Mahameru.

sn: प्रष्टव्यो मेरुसावर्णिमहर्षिः सूर्यसंनिभः। प्रणम्य शिरसा भूमौ प्रवृत्तिं मैथिली प्रति॥
en: Bowing down your heads to the earth, you should ask the Maharși Merusăvarņi, resembling the sun, touching Mithila's daughter.

sn: एतावज्जीवलोकस्य भास्करो रजनीक्षये। कृत्वा वितिमिरं सर्वमस्तं गच्छति पर्वतम्॥
en: On the departure of night, the sun dispels the darkness of the world to this extent, and then enters the Setting hill.

sn: एतावद् वानरैः शक्यं गन्तुं वानरपुङ्गवाः। अभास्करममर्यादं न जानीमस्ततः परम्॥
en: You foremost of monkeys, the monkeys are able to proceed thus far. Beyond this, of what is sunless and boundless I know nothing.

sn: अवगम्य तु वैदेहीं निलयं रावणस्य च अस्तं पर्वतमासाद्य पूर्णे मासे निवर्तत। ५२।।
en: Having come to Vaidehi and Rāvana's mansions, and arrived at the Setting-hill, do you return of the month being complete.

sn: ऊर्ध्वमासान्न वस्तव्यं वसन् वध्यो भवेन्मम। सहैव शूरो युष्माभिः श्वशुरो मे गमिष्यति॥
en: You must not stay above a month; and if you do, you must be slain by me. And along with you goeth that hero, my father-in-law.

sn: श्रोतव्यं सर्वमेतस्य भवद्भिदिष्टकारिभिः। गुरुरेष महाबाहुः श्वशुरो मे महाबलः॥
en: You, abiding by his orders, should listen to all that he sayeth. My mighty-armed father-in-law, gifted with great strength, is my spiritual preceptor.

sn: भवन्तश्चापि विक्रान्ताः प्रमाणं सर्व एव हि। प्रमाणमेनं संस्थाप्य पश्यध्वं पश्चिमां दिशम्॥ कृतकृत्या भविष्यामः कृतस्य प्रतिकर्मणा।।
en: All of you possessed of prowess, yourselves certainly constitute the measure whereby to ascertain the wisdom or otherwise of a course. Making this one also into a measure, survey the western quarter. Having requited the good that has been done to us, we shall attain our end.

sn: अतोऽन्यदपि यत्कार्यं कार्यस्यास्य प्रियं भवेत्। सम्प्रधार्य भवद्भिश्च देशकालार्थसंहितम्॥
en: De you also determine what else is agreeable (to Rāma), and in consonance with place, season and profit, should be performed by you in the matter of this business.

sn: ततः सुषेणप्रमुखाः प्लवङ्गमाः सुग्रीववाक्यं निपुणं निशम्य। आमन्त्र्य सर्वे प्लवगाधिपा ते जग्मुर्दिशं तां वरुणाभिगुप्ताम्॥
en: Then those monkeys-the monkey-chiefs headed by Sușeņa, having heard Sugrīva's deft speech, set out for the quarter protected by Varuna.

sn: ततः संदिश्य सुग्रीवः श्वशुरं पश्चिमां दिशम्। वीरं शतबलं नाम वानरं वानरेश्वरः॥ उवाच राजा सर्वज्ञः सर्ववानरसत्तमः। वाक्यमात्महितं चैव रामस्य च हितं तदा॥
en: Having directed his father-in-law to proceed to the West, that best to monkeys, the allknowing king Sugrīva, lord of apes, then spoke to the heroic monkey, named Satavala, words fraught with good to himself as well as to Rāma,

sn: वृतः शतसहस्रेण त्वद्विधानां वनौकसाम्। वैवस्वतसुतैः सार्धं प्रविष्टः सर्वमन्त्रिभिः॥ दिशं धुंदीची विक्रान्तहिमशैलावतंसिकाम्। सर्वतः परिमार्गध्वं रामपत्नी यशस्विनीम्॥
en: Surrounded by hundreds and thousands of rangers of the forest like yourself, in company with the offspring of Yama as well as the counsellors in a body, do you, O you possessed of prowess, entering the northern quarter furnished with the Himaśaila, search everywhere for the illustrious spouse of Rāma.

sn: अस्मिन् कार्ये विनिर्वृत्ते कृते दाशरथे: प्रिये। ऋणान्मुक्ता भविष्यामः कृतार्थार्थविदां वर ॥
en: Having performed this task satisfactorily, and brought about what is dear to Dasaratha's son, we shall, O best of those that achieve success, be freed from our debts.

sn: कृतं हि प्रियमस्माकं राघवेण महात्मना। तस्य चेत्प्रतिकारोऽस्ति सफलं जीवितं भवेत्॥
en: The high-souled Rāghava had done us good. If we can serve him in turn, our life shall be crowned with success.

sn: अर्थिनः कार्यनिर्वृत्तिमकर्तुरपि यश्चरेत्। तस्य स्यात् सफलं जन्म किं पुनः पूर्वकारिणः।७।।
en: Even the life of him that accomplishes the work of one to whom the former is not obliged, is successful, — what then is to be said in respect of him that has served one formerly.?

sn: एतां बुद्धिं समास्थाय दृश्यते जानकी यथा। तथा भवद्भिः कर्तव्यमस्मत्प्रियहितैषिभिः॥
en: Pondering this, those that are engaged in our welfare, should so act that Jānaki may be discovered.

sn: अयं हि सर्वभूतानां मान्यस्तु नरसत्तमः। अस्मासु च गतः प्रीतिं रामः परपुरंजयः॥
en: And this foremost of men is worthy of being honoured by all creatures; and Rāmacaptor of hostile capitals—has also found delight in us.

sn: इमानि बहुदुर्गाणि नद्यः शैलान्तराणि च। भवन्तः परिमार्गन्तु बुद्धिविक्रमसम्पदा ॥
en: Endowed with sense and prowess, do you explore these many inaccessible places, rivers and mountains.

sn: तत्र म्लेच्छान् पुलिन्दांश्च शूरसेनांस्तथैव च। प्रस्थलान् भरतांश्चैव कुरुंश्च सह मद्रकैः॥ काम्बोजयवनांश्चैव शकानां पत्तनानि च। अन्वीक्ष्य वरदांश्चैव हिमवन्तं विचिन्वथ ॥
en: Having searched there Mlechās, Pulindas, Surasensas, Prasthalas, Bharatas, Kurus, and Madrakas, and Varadas, as well as the cities of Kambojas, Yavanas and Sakas, do you explore Himavān.

sn: लोध्रपद्मकखण्डेषु देवदारुवनेषु च। रावणः सह वैदेह्या मार्गितव्यस्ततस्ततः॥
en: And in tracts of Lodhras and Padmakas, and in Devadāru woods* do you search thoroughly for Ravana along with Videha's daughter. *Belonging, according to the commentator, to Himavān.

sn: ततः सोमाश्रमं गत्वा देवगन्धर्वसेवितम्। कालं नाम महासानुं पर्वतं तं गमिष्यथ॥
en: Then, coming upon the hermitage of Soma, frequented by gods and Gandharvas, do you repair to the mountain called kāla possessing spacious plateaus,

sn: महत्सु तस्य शैलेषु पर्वतेषु गुहासु च। विचिन्वत महाभागां रामपत्नीमनिन्दिताम्॥
en: In those mighty mountains, as also in others and in their caves, do you search for that exalted lady, the blameless wife of Rāma.

sn: तमतिक्रम्य शैलेन्द्रं हेमगर्भ महागिरिम्। ततः सुदर्शनं नाम पर्वतं गन्तुमर्हथ ॥
en: Having passed beyond that mighty mountain containing gold in its womb, it behoves you to go to the mountain called Sudarsana.

sn: ततो देवसखा नाम पर्वतः पतगालयः। नानापक्षिसमाकीर्णो विविधद्रुमभूषितः॥
en: Then (lies) the mountain called Devasakhā, the home of feathered tribes; abounding in various fowls, and embellished with diverse trees.

sn: तस्य काननखण्डेषु निर्झरेषु गुहासु च। रावणः सह वैदेह्या मार्गितव्यस्ततस्ततः॥
en: In its golden tracts, fountains and caves, do you search for Rāvaņa along with Videha's daughter.

sn: तमतिक्रम्य चाकाशं सर्वतः शतयोजनम्। अपर्वतनदीवृक्षं सर्वसत्त्वविवर्जितम्॥
en: Going beyond it, (you come upon) a vacant land, measuring an hundred Yojanas, without mountains, or rivers, or trees; and void of all living beings.

sn: तत्तु शीघ्रमतिक्रम्य कान्तारं रोमहर्षणम्। कैलासं पाण्डुरं प्राप्य हृष्टा यूयं भविष्यथ॥
en: Speedily passing that desert land capable of making one's hair stand on end, you shall feel delighted, on coming to the pale Kailasa.

sn: तत्र पाण्डुरमेघाभं जाम्बूनदपरिष्कृतम्। कुबेरभवनं रम्यं निर्मितं विश्वकर्मणा ॥ विशाला नलिनी यत्र प्रभूतकमलोत्पला। हंसकारण्डवाकीर्णा अप्सरोगणसेविता ॥
en: There (you will behold) the charming mansion of Kuvera, resembling pale clouds, of burnished gold, built by Viśvakarmā; where (lies) the spacious tank overflowing with lotuses and lilies, thronged with swans and Kāraņdavas, and frequented by troops of Apsarās.

sn: तत्र वैश्रवणो राजा सर्वलोकनमस्कृतः। धनदो रमते श्रीमान् गुह्यकैः सह यक्षराट्॥
en: There king Vaiśravana, the lord of Yakşas, bowed down to by all creatures,-the graceful giver of riches—sporteth along with the Guhyakas.

sn: तस्य चन्द्रनिकाशेषु पर्वतेषु गुहासु च। रावणः सह वैदेह्या मार्गितव्यस्ततस्ततः॥
en: In the offshoots belonging to Kailasa resembling the moon, as also in their caverns, do you thoroughly search for Rāvaņa in company with Vaidehī.

sn: क्रौञ्चं तु गिरिमासाद्य बिलं तस्य सुदुर्गमम् । अप्रमत्तैः प्रवेष्टव्यं दुष्प्रवेशं हि तत् स्मृतम्॥
en: And coming to the Kruncha mountain, you should, having your wits about you, enter its inaccessible cavern; for that is well known as difficult of entrance.

sn: वसन्ति हि महात्मानस्तत्र सूर्यसमप्रभाः। देवैरभ्यर्थिताः सम्यग् देवरूपा महर्षयः॥
en: There dwell certain Maharsis, high-souled, of effulgence resembling that of the sun-complete god-like shapes,—who are sought by the deities themselves.

sn: क्रौञ्चस्य तु गुहाश्चान्याः सानूनि शिखराणि च । दर्दराश्च नितम्बाश्च विचेतव्यास्ततस्ततः॥
en: And you should thoroughly explore the other caves of Krauncha, its plateaus and peaks; its passes and sides.

sn: अवृक्षं कामशैलं च मानसं विहगालयम्। न गतिस्तत्र भूतानां देवानां न च रक्षसाम्॥
en: (Then is) the treeless Manasa-abode of birds-the scene of Kāma's austerities. Way there is none for creatures, or for gods, or for Raksasas.

sn: स च सर्वैर्विचेतव्यः ससानुप्रस्थभूधरः। क्रौञ्चं गिरिमतिक्रम्य मैनाको नाम पर्वतः॥
en: are That also must be explored by you, that mountain with plains and plateous. Going beyond Krauncha, (you shall see) the mountain, named Maināka.

sn: मयस्य भवनं तत्र दानवस्य स्वयंकृतम्। मैनाकस्तु विचेतव्यः ससानुप्रस्थकन्दरः॥
en: There is the residence of the Danvava, Maya, reared by himself. Mainaka also with its plains, plateaus and woods must be searched by you.

sn: स्त्रीणामश्वमुखीनां तु निकेतस्तत्र तत्र तु। तं देशं समतिक्रम्य आश्रमं सिद्धसेवितम्॥ सिद्धा वैखानसा यत्र बालखिल्याश्च तापसाः। दतव्यास्ततः सिद्धास्तपसा वीतकल्मषाः॥ प्रष्टव्या चापि सीतायाः प्रवृत्तिर्विनयान्वितैः।
en: There are all over, the homes of females with faces resembling those of horses. Going beyond that part, (you shall come to) the asylum inhabited by Siddhas; where ascetics—Vālakhilyas, Siddhas and Vaikhānasas. Saluting those Siddhas, who have been cleansed of their sins on account of their asceticism, you should in humble guise ask them concerning Sītā.

sn: हेमपुष्करसंछन्नं तत्र वैखानसं सरः॥ तरुणादित्यसंकाशैहँसैर्विचरितं शुभैः।
en: There is the Vaikhānasa tank filled with golden lotuses; and ranged by graceful cranes of the hue of the infant sun.

sn: औपबाह्यः कुबेरस्य सार्वभौम इति स्मृतः॥ गजः पर्येति तं देशं सदा सह करेणुभिः।
en: Kuvera's vehicle, the elephant known (by the name of) Sārvabhauma, ever rangeth that country in company with she-elephants.

sn: तत् सरः समतिक्रम्य नष्टचन्द्रदिवाकरम्। अनक्षत्रगणं व्योम निष्पयोदमनादितम् ॥ गभस्तिभिरिवार्कस्य स तु देशः प्रकाश्यते। विश्राम्यद्भिस्तपः सिद्धैर्देवकल्पैः स्वयंप्रभैः॥
en: Going beyond that expanse of water, (you come upon) a sky void of stars, and where the sun and the moon have been put out; and that land is visible by the rays, as if of the sun, proceeding from (the persons of) self-luminous, god-like ones, who are reposing there, after achieving success in austerities.

sn: तं तु देशमतिक्रम्य शैलोदा नाम निम्नगा। उभयोस्तीरयोस्तस्याः कीचका नाम वेणवः॥
en: Leaving behind that region, (you come to) a stream named Sailoda. On its both banks are bamboos named Kīcaka.

sn: ते नयन्ति परं तीरं सिद्धान् प्रत्यानयन्ति च। उत्तराः कुरवस्तत्र कृतपुण्यप्रतिश्रयाः।
en: These take the Siddhas to the other shore and bring them back again. There (are seen the northern Kurus, the abode of those that have acquired religious merit.

sn: ततः काञ्चनपद्माभिः पद्मिनीभिः कृतोदकाः॥ नीलवैदूर्यपत्राढ्या नद्यस्तत्र सहस्रशः।
en: And there are tanks there with their waters crowned with golden lotuses. There are rivers by thousands with copious blue lapis leaves.

sn: रक्तोत्पलवनैश्चात्र मण्डिताश्च हिरण्मयैः॥ तरुणादित्यसंकाशा भान्ति तत्र जलाशयाः।
en: And the pools here, resembling the tender sun, are embellished with assemblages of golden red lotuses.

sn: महार्हमणिपत्रैश्च काञ्चनप्रभकेसरैः॥ नीलोत्पलवनैश्चित्रैः स देशः सर्वतो वृतः।
en: And that tract is every where filled with costly gems, and jewels, and woods of blue lotuses, having filaments splendid like gold; and with round pearls and costly jewels.

sn: निस्तुलाभिश्च मुक्ताभिर्मणिभिश्च महाधनैः॥ उद्धृतपुलिनास्तत्र जातरूपैश्च निम्नगाः। सर्वरत्नमयैश्चिौरवगाढा नगोत्तमैः॥ जातरूपमयैश्चापि हुताशनसमप्रभैः।
en: And the rivers there have islets covered with gold; and are crowded with lovely hills of gold, bright as fire, furnished with all kinds of precious stones.

sn: नित्यपुष्पफलास्तत्र नगाः पत्ररथाकुलाः॥ दिव्यगन्धरसस्पर्शाः सर्वकामान् स्रवन्ति च।
en: And the trees there, thronged with birds, bear flowers and fruits daily; and, charged with savoury juices, publishing superb perfumes, and of delicious feel, they confer every wish.

sn: नानाकाराणि वासांसि फलन्त्यन्ये नगोत्तमाः॥ मुक्तावैदूर्यचित्राणि भूषणानि तथैव च। स्त्रीणां यान्यनुरूपाणि पुरुषाणां तथैव च॥
en: Other excellent trees bring forth attires of divers kinds, and ornaments decked with pearls and lapises,-coveted alike by males and females*. *The present text, according to Kataka, drops a sloka, whose last line is, Beings possessed of powerful effulgence, sport here always in company with females.

sn: सर्वर्तुसुखसेव्यानि फलन्त्यन्ये नगोत्तमाः। महार्हमणिचित्राणि फलन्त्यन्ये नगोत्तमाः।४६।।
en: And other excellent trees bear fruits fit to be partaken at all seasons. And other excellent trees bring forth precious beds dight with costly jewels and furnished with variegated covers.

sn: शयनानि प्रसूयन्ते चित्रास्तरणवन्ति च। मन:कान्तानि माल्यानि फलन्त्यत्रापरे द्रुमाः॥ पानानि च महार्हाणि भक्ष्याणि विविधानि च। स्त्रियश्च गुणसम्पन्ना रूपयौवनलक्षिताः॥ गन्धर्वाः किन्नराः सिद्धा नागा विद्याधरास्तथा। रमन्ते सततं तत्र नारीभिर्भास्वरप्रभाः॥
en: And other trees bring forth charming wreaths, and costly drinks, and various kinds of viands. And females adorned with every accomplishment, and endowed with youth and beauty, and Gandharvas and Kinnaras, and Siddhas and Nāgas and Vidyādharas, of blazing splendour, ceaselessly sport there in company with females.

sn: सर्वे सुकृतकर्माणः सर्वे रतिपरायणाः। सर्वे कामार्थसहिता वसन्ति सह योषितः॥
en: And all of righteous deeds, and all engaged in amorous disports, and all furnished with desire and profit,-dwell in that place in association with their females.

sn: गीतवादित्रनिर्घोषः सोत्कृष्टहसितस्वरैः। श्रूयते सततं तत्र सर्वभूतमनोरमः॥
en: And there are continually heard there the sounds of instruments and the voice of song mixed with sweet hilarious laughter, capable of taking all crcatures.

sn: तत्र नामुदितः कश्चिन्नात्र कश्चिदसत्प्रियः। अहन्यहनि वर्धन्ते गुणास्तत्र मनोरमाः॥
en: No one is depressed there; nor does any one there want any desirable object; and day after day the delightful qualities find their development there.

sn: समतिक्रम्य तं देशमुत्तरः पयसां निधिः। तत्र सोमगिरि म मध्ये हेममयो महान्।५३।।
en: Passing beyond that is the Northern ocean. In the bosom (of the deep) is the mountain named Somagiri, golden and of great dimensions.

sn: स तु देशो विसूर्योऽपि तस्य भासा प्रकाशते। सूर्यलक्ष्म्याभिविज्ञेयस्तपतेव विवस्वता ॥
en: Albeit without the sun, yet through the brightness of the Soma mountain, the land shines forth with all the loveliness and reality of one warmed by the sun.

sn: भूधरांस्तत्र विश्वात्मा शम्भुरेकादशात्मकः। ब्रह्मा वसति देवेशो ब्रह्मर्षिपरिवारितः॥
en: There that Soul of the Universe, the adorable Sambhu, fraught with the spirits of the eleven Rudras-that lord of the gods-Brahmā.dwelleth, surrounded by the Brahmarsis.

sn: न कथंचन गन्तव्यं कुरूणामुत्तरेण वः। अन्येषामपि भूतानां नानुक्रामति वै गतिः॥
en: You cannot proceed to the north of the Kurus; nor is there way in that region for any other creatures.

sn: स हि सोमगिरि म देवानामपि दुर्गमः। तमालोक्य ततः क्षिप्रमुपावर्तितुमर्हथ॥
en: And that mountain is named Soma, incapable of being entered even by the gods, Sighting this you should speedily turn back.

sn: एतावद् वानरैः शक्यं गन्तुं वानरपुङ्गवाः। अभास्करममर्यादं न जानीमस्ततः परम्॥
en: You foremost of monkey, the monkeys are competent to proceed thus far. Beyond that, of regions sunless and limitless I know nothing.

sn: सर्वमेतद् विचेतव्यं यन्मया परिकीर्तितम्। यदन्यदपि नोक्तं च तत्रापि क्रियतां मतिः॥
en: You should search all these which I have described (to you); and you should also turn your attention to others besides, which I have omitted to mention.

sn: ततः कृतं दाशरथेर्महत्प्रियं महत्प्रियं चापि ततो मम प्रियम्। कृतं भविष्यत्यनिलानलोपमा विदेहजादर्शनजेन कर्मणा॥
en: You that are comparable to the wind or fire, by accomplishing the work of beholding Videha's daughter, you will do what is held as exceedingly dear to Daśaratha's son as well as highly grateful to me.

sn: ततः कृतार्थाः सहिताः सबान्धवा मयार्चिताः सर्वगुणैर्मनोरमैः। चरिष्यथोवीं प्रति शान्तशात्रवाः सहप्रियाभूतधराः प्लवङ्गमाः॥
en: Then, having achieved success, do you, along with your friends, honoured by me, and crowned with every virtue, you monkeys, with your enemies slain, range the earth in company with your wives,-the support of all beings.

sn: विशेषेण तु सुग्रीवो हनूमत्यर्थमुक्तवान्। स हि तस्मिन् हरिश्रेष्ठे निश्चितार्थोऽर्थसाधने॥
en: Sugrīva had declared his conviction that he relied particularly upon Hanumān.

sn: अब्रवीच्च हनूमन्तं विक्रान्तमनिलात्मजम्। सुग्रीवः परमप्रीतः प्रभुः सर्ववनौकसाम्॥
en: And convinced as to the ability of that best of monkeys to accomplish the work, Sugrīva, that lord of all the dwellers of the woods, well pleased, spoke to Hanumān, son to the windgod, saying,

sn: न भूमौ नान्तरिक्षे वा नाम्बरे नामरालये। नाप्सु वा गतिसङ्गं ते पश्यामि हरिपुङ्गव॥
en: O foremost of monkeys, neither on the earth, nor in the sky', nor in the etherial regions, nor yet in water, find I any obstacle to your course. 1. Antariksa-regions above the earth in which the birds fly. 2. Ambara— Upper air.

sn: सासुराः सहगन्धर्वा सनागनरदेवताः। विदिताः सर्वलोकास्ते ससागरधराधराः॥
en: The entire worlds with Asuras, and Gandharvas, and Nāgas, and men, and gods, with oceans, and the earth and the regions beneath—are well known to you.

sn: गतिर्वेगश्च तेजश्च लाघवं च महाकपे। पितुस्ते सदृशं वीर मारुतस्य महौजसः॥ तेजसा वापि ते भूतं न समं भुवि विद्यते। तद् यथा लभ्यते सीता तत्त्वमेवानुचिन्तय॥
en: And your motion, vehemence, energy and fleetness, are, O hero, O mighty ape, even like those of your sire, the powerful wind god; and there exists no creature on earth that is like to you in energy. Therefore do you bethink you how Sītā may be recovered.

sn: त्वय्येव हनुमन्नस्ति बलं बुद्धिः पराक्रमः। देशकालानुवृत्तिश्च नयश्च नयपण्डित।७।।
en: Even in you, O you versed in policy, are strength, and wit, and courage, and policy, and conduct in consonance with season and place.

sn: ततः कार्यसमासङ्गमवगम्य हनूमति। विदित्वा हनुमन्तं च चिन्तयामास राघवः॥
en: Thereat, understanding that success in the task depended upon Hanumān, and also knowing what Hanumān was, Rāghava reflected,

sn: सर्वथा निश्चितार्थोऽयं हनूमति हरीश्वरः। निश्चितार्थतरश्चापि हनूमान् कार्यसाधने॥
en: This lord of monkeys is every way confident concerning Hanumān; and Hanumān himself is even more confident of achieving success in the work.

sn: तदेव प्रस्थितस्यास्य परिज्ञातस्य कर्मभिः। भर्ना परिगृहीतस्य ध्रुवः कार्यफलोदयः॥
en: He that has been tested by his deed, and who has been considered worthiest by his master, having veen commissioned in this business,-success in the work is certain.

sn: तं समीक्ष्य महातेजा व्यवसायोत्तरं हरिम्। कृतार्थ इव संहृष्टः प्रहृष्टेन्द्रियमानसः॥
en: Then beholding that monkey who was the fittest for the task, that exceedingly energetic senses one, (Rāma), with his mind and exhilarated, considering himself as already crowned with success, felt the excess of joy.

sn: ददौ तस्य ततः प्रीतः स्वनामाङ्कोपशोभितम्। अङ्गुलीयमभिज्ञानं राजपुत्र्याः परंतपः॥
en: And well pleased, that subduer of enemies handed to Hanuman a ring inscribed with his name, as a sign to the king's daughter.

sn: अनेन त्वां हरि श्रेष्ठ चिह्वेन जनकात्मजा। मत्सकाशादनुप्राप्तमनुद्विग्नाऽनुपश्यति॥
en: By this sign, O foremost of monkeys, Janaka's daughter will be able to see you fearlessly, as one that has come from me.

sn: व्यवसायश्च ते वीर सत्त्वयुक्तश्च विक्रमः। सुग्रीवस्य च संदेशः सिद्धि कथयतीव मे॥
en: Your firmness, O hero, and sterling prowess, as well as Sugrīva's saying, tell me greatly of success.

sn: स तद् गृह्य हरिश्रेष्ठः कृत्वा मूर्ध्नि कृताञ्जलिः। वन्दित्वा चरणौ चैव प्रस्थितः प्लवगर्षभः॥
en: Thereupon, taking that (ring), and raising his joined palms to his head, that foremost and best of monkeys, saluting (Rāma's) feet, went away.

sn: स तत् प्रकर्षन् हरिणां महद्बलं बभूव वीरः पवनात्मजः कपिः। गताम्बुदे व्योम्नि विशुद्धमण्डलः शशीव नक्षत्रगणोपशोभितः॥
en: Then taking with him that mighty host of monkeys, that hero, the son of the wind, resembled the moon of bright disc in the sky, garnished by the stars, after the clouds have departed.

sn: अतिबल बलमाश्रितस्तवाहं हरिवर विक्रम विक्रमैरनल्पैः। पवनसुत यथाधिगम्यते सा जनकसुता हनुमंस्तथा कुरुष्व॥
en: O you of excessive strength! I take refuge in your mighty. O you endowed with the prowess of the foremost of lions! do you, O son of the Wind, O Hanuman, exert yourself so, summoning the great strength you are master of, that we may obtain Janaka's daughter.* The commentator says that this speech is equally attributable to Rāma and Sugrīva. But I think, it would fit Rāma's lips to a nicely. The commentator says that this speech is equally attributable to Rāma and Sugrīva. But I think, it would fit Rāma's lips to a nicely.

sn: सर्वांश्चाहूय सुग्रीवः प्लवगान् प्लवगर्षभः। समस्तांश्चाब्रवीद् राजा रामकार्यार्थसिद्धये॥
en: Summoning all the monkeys, that foremost of monkeys, king Sugriva, spoke to them all touching the success of Rāma's work.

sn: एवमेतद् विचेतव्यं भवद्भिर्वानरोत्तमैः। तदुग्रशासनं भर्तुर्विज्ञाय हरिपुङ्गवाः॥
en: The monkey-chiefs, knowing the stern command of their lord should search in all these places. Then, covering up the earth like locusts, they marched away.

sn: शलभा इव संछाद्य मेदिनी सम्प्रतिस्थरे। रामः प्रस्रवणे तस्मिन् न्यवसत् सहलक्ष्मणः॥ प्रतीक्षमाणस्तं मासं सीताधिगमने कृतः।
en: Expecting tidings of Sītä, Rāma remained that month in the vicinity of that cascade, in company with Lakşmaņa.

sn: उत्तरां तु दिशं रम्यां गिरिराजसमावृताम्॥ प्रतस्थे सहसा वीरो हरिः शतबलिस्तदा।
en: And that heroic monkey Satavali swiftly set out for the northern regions covered by the monarch of mountains.

sn: पूर्वां दिशं प्रतिययौ विनतो हरियूथपः॥ ताराङ्गदादिसहितः प्लवगः पवनात्मजः। अगस्त्याचरितामाशां दक्षिणां परियूथपः॥ पश्चिमां च दिशं घोरां सुषेणः प्लवगेश्वरः। प्रतस्थे हरिशार्दूलो दिशं वरुणपालिताम्॥
en: And that leader of monkey herds, Vinata, proceeded towards the estern quarter. And that monkey, Hanumān-leader of monkeyherds in company with Tārā, Angada and others, went to the South, inhabited by Agastya. And that lord of monkeys, Suşeņa, lion among monkeys, went to the terrible western quarter, protected by Varuna.

sn: ततः सर्वा दिशो राजा चोदयित्वा यथातथम्। कपिसेनापतिर्वीरो मुमोद सुखितः सुखम्॥
en: Then, having properly despatched (his forces) in all directions, that general of the monkey hosts, being pleased, gave himself up to sport.

sn: एवं संचोदिताः सर्वे राज्ञा वानरयूथपाः। स्वां स्वां दिशमभिप्रेत्य त्वरिताः सम्प्रतस्थिरे॥
en: Thus despatched by the king, the monkeychiefs proceeded apace respectively towards their destined quarters.

sn: नदन्तश्चोन्नदन्तश्च गर्जन्तश्च प्लवङ्गमाः। क्ष्वेडन्तो धावमानाश्च विनदन्तो महाबलाः॥ एवं संचोदिताः सर्वे राज्ञा वानरयूथपाः। आनयिष्यामहे सीतां हनिष्यामश्च रावणम्॥ अहमेको वधिष्यामि प्राप्तं रावणमाहवे। ततश्चोन्मथ्य सहसा हरिष्ये जनकात्मजाम्॥ वेपमानां श्रमेणाद्य भवद्भिः स्थीयतामिति। एक एवाहरिष्यामि क्षोभयिष्यामि सागरान्॥ अहं योजनसंख्यायाः प्लवेयं नात्र संशयः। शतयोजनसंख्यायाः शतं समधिकं ह्यहम्॥ भूतले सागरे वापि शैलेषु च वनेषु च। पातालस्यापि वा मध्ये न ममाच्छिद्यते गतिः॥
en: And the monkeys possessed of great strength cried and howled and roared and shouted and rushed and sent up loud ululations. Thus despatched by the king, the leaders of monkeyherds, said, We shall bring back Sītā, and slay Rāvana. I alone shall slay Răvaņa engaged in conflict. And slaying (him), I shall this very day swiftly carry off Janaka's daughter, trembling because of fatigue, (saying to her), 'Rest you. I single-handed shall recover Jānakī even from the nether regions. I shall uproot trees and rive mountains. I shall cleave the earth and vex the deep. (And some said), I can, without doubt, clear a Yojana at one bound; and another said, I can clear and hundred; and a yet another, I can more than an hundred. And neither on earth, nor in sea, mountains, woods, nor nether regions can my course be obstructed.

sn: इत्येकैकस्तदा तत्र वानरा बलदर्पिताः। ऊचुश्च वचनं तस्य हरिराजस्य संनिधौ॥
en: Thus did the apes proud of their strength, severally speak in presence of the sovereign of the monkeys.

sn: गतेषु वानरेन्द्रेषु रामः सुग्रीवमब्रवीत्। कथं भवान् विजानीते सर्वं वै मण्डलं भुवः॥
en: On the monkey-chiefs having departed, Rāma said to Sugrīva, How is it that you know all the quarters of this earth?'

sn: सुग्रीवश्च ततो राममुवाच प्रणतात्मवान्। श्रूयतां सर्वमाख्यास्ये विस्तरेण वचो मम॥
en: Thereupon, the self-controlled Sugrīva, bowing low, said to Rāma, Do you listen to my words. I shall relate everything.

sn: यदा तु दुन्दुभिं नाम दानवं महिषाकृतिम्। प्रतिकालयते वाली मलयं प्रति पर्वतम्॥ तदा विवेश महिषो मलयस्य गुहां प्रति। विवेश वाली तत्रापि मलयं तज्जिघांसया॥
en: When Vāli pursued the Dānava Dundubhi, wearing the form of a buffalo towards the Malaya mountain, Mahișa entered a cave of that mountain. And Vali also, desirous of slaying the Asura, entered Malaya.

sn: ततोऽहं तत्र निक्षिप्तो गुहद्वारि विनीतवत्। न च निष्क्रामते वाली तदा संवत्सरे गते॥
en: And I was made to stand at the mouth in humble guise; nor did Väli issue out, although a good year rolled away.

sn: ततः क्षतजवेगेन आपुपूरे तदा बिलम्। तदहं विस्मितो दृष्ट्वा भ्रातुः शोकविषादितः॥
en: Then the cave became filled with blood gushing out vehemently. Seeing this, I became amazed, and exercised with the poison of grief of accountri my brother.

sn: अथाहं गतबुद्धिस्तु सुव्यक्तं निहतो गुरुः। शिला पर्वतसंकाशा बिलद्वारि मया कृता॥
en: And I, losing my sense, thought that my superior had for certain been slain. And I placed 7 crag huge as a hill at the mouth of the cave. took to my

sn: असक्नुवन्निष्कमितुं महिषो विनशिष्यति। ततोऽहमागां किष्किन्धां निराशस्तस्य जीविते॥
en: (And thought I), 'Mahisa, unable to issue out, needs must meet his end.' And despairing of his (Vali's) life, I retraced my steps to Kiskindha.

sn: राज्यं च सुमहत् प्राप्य तारां च रुमया सह। मित्रैश्च सहितस्तस्य वसामि विगतज्वरः॥
en: And obtaining the spacious kingdom along with Tãrã and Umā, I began to pass my days in peace in company with his counsellors.

sn: आजगाम ततो वाली हत्वा तं वानरर्षभः। ततोऽहमददां राज्यं गौरवाद् भययन्त्रितः॥ स मां जिघांसुर्दुष्टात्मा वाली प्रव्यथितेन्द्रियः। परिकालयते वाली धावन्तं सचिवैः सह॥
en: Then came that foremost of monkeys, having slain him (Mahisa). Thereupon I, influenced by fear, in consideration of his dignity, made over to him his monarchy. But Vali, his senses exercised with sorrow, anxious to slay me, in company with his counsellors, pursued me, who heels.

sn: ततोऽहं वालिना तेन सोऽनुबद्धः प्रधावितः। नदीश्च विविधाः पश्यन् वनानि नगराणि च ॥ आदर्शतलसंकाशा ततो वै पृथिवी मया। अलातचक्रप्रतिमा दृष्ट्वा गोष्पदवत् कृता॥
en: Hotly pursued and chased by Vāli, I surveyed various streams and woods and cities. And I surveyed the earth like the hoof-print of a cow, or the image reflected from a mirror, or a firebrand whirled (in the air).* *The commentator remarks that like the hoof-print of a cow expresses the case with which Sugrīva travelled the earth; like a fire brand whirled conveys his vehement speed; and like the image reflected on a mirror signifies the lucidity of his perception.

sn: पूर्वां दिशं ततो गत्वा पश्यामि विविधान् दुमान्। पर्वतान् सदरीन् रम्यान् सरांसि विविधानि च॥
en: Then repairing to the East, I see various trees, and mountains, and charming caves, and diverse tanks.

sn: उदयं तत्र पश्यामि पर्वतं धातुमण्डितम्। क्षीरोदं सागरं चैव नित्यमप्सरसालयम्॥
en: And there I behold the Ascending mountain decked with gold,—and that daily abode of Apsarās-the sea of milk.

sn: परिकाल्यमानस्तु तदा वालिनाभिद्रुतो ह्यहम्। पुनरावृत्य सहसा प्रस्थितोऽहं तदा विभो॥
en: And chased by Vāli, and flying on, I suddenly veered round, and then again, O master, off I went.

sn: दिशस्तस्यास्ततो भूयः प्रस्थितो दक्षिणां दिशम्। विन्ध्यपादपसंकीर्णा चन्दनदुमशोभिताम्॥
en: And changing that direction, I again made for the South crowded with trees belonging to Vindhya, and embellished with sandal woods.

sn: दुमशैलान्तरे पश्यन् भूयो दक्षिणतोऽपराम्। अपरां च दिशं प्राप्तो वालिना समभिदुतः॥
en: Then seeing Văli in the mountain among trees, from the south I, pursued by Vāli, betook myself to the western quarter.

sn: स पश्यन् विविधान् देशानस्तं स गिरिसत्तमम्। प्राप्य चास्तं गिरिश्रेष्ठमुत्तरं सम्प्रधावितः॥ हिमवन्तं च मेरुं च समुद्रं च तथोत्तरम्। यदा न विन्दे शरणं वालिना समभिद्रुतः॥ ततो मां बुद्धिसम्पन्नो हनुमान् वाक्यमब्रवीत्।
en: And beholding various countries, and arriving at that foremost and best of mountains Asta* I turned to the north; and (passed) Himavat, and Meru, and the Northern sea. But pursued by Vāli, refuge find I none. Then out spoke Hanumān endued with understanding, *The Setting hill.

sn: इदानीं मे स्मृतं राजन् यथा वाली हरीश्वरः॥ मतङ्गेन तदा शप्तो ह्यस्मिन्नाश्रममण्डले । प्रविशेद् यदि वा वाली मूर्धास्य शतधा भवेत्॥
en: 'O king, now, I remember me how that lord of monkeys, Vāli, was cursed by Matanga in this very hermitage. If Vāli enters (into this asylum), his head becomes cleft in hundred.

sn: तत्र वासः सुखोऽस्माकं निरुद्विग्नो भविष्यति। ततः पर्वतमासाद्य ऋष्यमूकं नृपात्मज ॥ न विवेश तदा वाली मतङ्गस्य भयात् तदा।
en: There shall dwell happily without anxiety.' O king's son, thereupon, we went to the Rișyamuka mountain, nor did then Vāli enter we there from fear of Matanga.

sn: एवं मया तदा राजन् प्रत्यक्षमुपलक्षितम्। पृथिवीमण्डलं सर्वं गुहामस्म्यागतस्ततः॥
en: Thus, O king, did I actually see all the world. And from that place I came to this cave.

sn: दर्शनार्थं तु वैदेह्याः सर्वतः कपिकुञ्जराः। व्यादिष्टाः कपिराजेन यथोक्तं जग्मुरञ्जसा ॥
en: The principal monkeys, having been ordered by the monkey-king, speedily went in all directions to their destinations for the purpose of seeing Vaidehi.

sn: ते सरांसि सरित्कक्षानाकाशं नगराणि च। नदीदुर्गास्तथा देशान् विचिन्वन्ति समन्ततः॥
en: And on all sides they explore watery expanses, and streams, and lawns, and commons, and cities, and tracts rendered impassable by torrents.

sn: सुग्रीवेण समाख्याताः सर्वे वानरयूथपाः। तत्र देशान् विचिन्वन्ति सशैलवनकाननान्॥
en: And the leaders of monkey-herds search all those countries, countries, described described by Sugrīva,-containing mountains, woods and forests.

sn: विचित्य दिवसं सर्वे सीताधिगमने धृताः। समायान्ति स्म मेदिन्यां निशाकालेषु वानराः॥
en: Engaged during the day in search of Sītā, at night the monkeys seek the ground (for sleep).

sn: सर्वर्तुकांश्च देशेषु वानराः सफलदुमान्। आसाद्य रजनी शय्यां चक्रुः सर्वेष्वहःसु ते॥
en: In every place, by day coming to trees aye enjoying every season, and crowned with fruits, the monkeys prepared their beds at night.* *The sense is rather obscure, it being difficult to understand the relation their beds bore to the neighbouring trees.

sn: तदहः प्रथमं कृत्वा मासे प्रस्रवणं गताः। कपिराजेन संगम्य निराशाः कपिकुञ्जराः॥
en: Counting that day* as the first, the principal monkeys, after the month had run out, resigning all hope, came to the Fountain and met with the monkey-king. *i.e. the day of their departure.

sn: विचित्य तु दिशं पूर्वां यथोक्तां सचिवैः सह। अदृष्ट्वा विनतः सीतामाजगाम महाबलः॥
en: And having explored the Eastern regions, as directed, the exceedingly strong Vinata not having been able to see Sītā, came back, in company with his counsellors.

sn: दिशमप्युत्तरां सर्वां विविच्य स महाकपिः। आगतः सह सैन्येन भीतः शतबलिस्तदा॥
en: And then that mighty ape, Satavali, daunted in spirits, arrived with his forces, after having searched all through the North.

sn: सुषेणः पश्चिमामाशां विविच्य सह वानरैः। समेत्य मासे पूर्णे तु सुग्रीवमुपचक्रमे॥
en: And having searched the West in company with his monkeys, Sușeņa, on the month being complete, presented himself before Sugrīva.

sn: तं प्रस्रवणपृष्ठस्थं समासाद्याभिवाद्य च। आसीनं सह रामेण सुग्रीवमिदमब्रुवन्॥
en: And coming to Sugrīva seated along with Rāma behind the Fountain, and saluting the former, Susena said to Sugriva.

sn: विचिताः पर्वताः सर्वे वनानि गहनानि च। निम्नगाः सागरान्ताश्च सर्वे जनपदाश्च ये॥ गुहाश्च विचिता सर्वे याश्च ते परिकीर्तिताः। विचिताश्च महागुल्मा लताविततसंतताः॥ गहनेषु च देशेषु दुर्गेषु विषमेषु च। सत्वान्यतिप्रमाणानि विचितानि हतानि च। ये चैव गहना देशा विचितास्ते पुनः पुनः॥
en: Searched have been all the mountains, and deep woods, and streams, and islands embosomed in the ocean, and the various provinces. And also searched have been all the caves which have been described by you; and searched have been all the groves entertwined with plants; and thickets; and difficult and uneven grounds. And huge animals have been sought out and slain (by us). And all the impracticable places we have explored again and again.

sn: उदारसत्वाभिजनो हनूमान् स मैथिली ज्ञास्यति वानरेन्द्र। दिशं तु यामेव गता तु सीता तामास्थितो वायुसुतो हनूमान् ॥
en: O lord of monkeys, possessed of great strength and nobly born, it is Hanumān who will be able to ascertain the whereabouts of Mithila's daughter. And the Wind's son, Hanumān, has followed even the has by which Sītā has gone.

sn: सह ताराङ्गदाभ्यां तु सहसा हनुमान् कपिः। सुग्रीवेण यथोद्दिष्टं गन्तुं देशं प्रचक्रमे॥
en: The monkey Hanumān in company with Tārā and Angada swiftly set out for the quarter assigned by Sugrīva.

sn: स तु दूरमुपागम्य सर्वैस्तैः कपिसत्तमैः। ततो विचित्य विन्ध्यस्य गुहाश्च गहनानि च॥ पर्वताग्रनदीदुर्गान् सरांसि विपुलदुमान्। वृक्षखण्डाश्च विविधान् पर्वतान् वनपादपान्॥ अन्वेषमाणास्ते सर्वे वानराः सर्वतोदिशम्। न सीतां ददृशुर्वीरा मैथिली जनकात्मजाम्॥
en: And having proceeded far along with all those foremost of monkeys, he explored the caves and woods of Vindhya; spots inaccessible in consequence of streams intervening in front of mountains; and tanks; and tracts filled with trees; and various mountains rife with wild trees. And having searched in all directions, the monkeys could not find Maithilī, Janaka's daughter Sītā.

sn: ते भक्षयन्तो मूलानि फलानि विविधान्यपि। अन्वेषमाणा दुर्धर्षा न्यवसंस्तत्र तत्र ह ॥ स तु देशो दुरन्वेषो गुहागहनवान् महान्। निर्जलं निर्जनं शून्यं गहनं घोरदर्शनम्॥ तादृशान्यप्यरण्यानि विचित्य भृशपीडिताः। स देशश्च दुरन्वेष्यो गुहागहनवान् महान्॥ त्यक्त्वा तु तं ततो देशं सर्वे वै हरियूथपाः। देशमन्यं दुराधर्षं विविशुश्चाकुतोभयाः॥ यत्र वन्ध्यफला वृक्षा विपुष्पाः पर्णवर्जिताः। निस्तोयाः सरितो यत्र मूलं यत्र सुदुर्लभम्॥ न सन्ति महिषा यत्र न मृगा न च हस्तिनः। शार्दूलाः पक्षिणो वापि ये चान्ये वनगोचराः॥
en: And subsisting on various fruits and roots, they were overcome with fatigue, after searching dreadful forests, void of water, still and tenantless, as well as other forests of a similar nature. And having searched that country as well mighty forests containing caves, those leaders of monkeyherds fearlessly explored other places, difficult of access, where the trees are fruitless, and without flowers and foliage; where the streams are waterless, and where roots even are rare; where there are no buffaloes, or deer, or elephants, or tigers, or birds-or any other animals that are found in forests.

sn: न चात्र वृक्षा नौषध्यो न वल्ल्यो नापि वीरुधः। स्निग्धपत्राः स्थले यत्र पद्मिन्यः फुल्लपङ्कजाः॥ प्रेक्षणीयाः सुगन्धाश्च भ्रमरैश्च विवर्जिताः।
en: And there are there neither trees, nor annual plants, nor creepers, nor herbs,-and in that place there are no pleasant pools, with cool leaves, and filled with blown lotuses, and it has been renounced by the black-bees.

sn: कण्डुर्नाम महाभागः सत्यवादी तपोधनः॥ महर्षिः परमामर्षी नियमैर्दुष्प्रधर्षणः।
en: There dwelleth a Maharași, Kandu by name, an eminently pious, and truthful ascetic, irascible, and irrepressible because of his practice of self-discipline.

sn: तस्य तस्मिन् वने पुत्रो बालको दशवार्षिकः॥ प्रणष्टो जीवितान्ताय क्रुद्धस्तेन महामुनिः।
en: In that wood his son, a boy of ten years, his sands having run out, breathed his last; and it is for this that the mighty ascetic has come under the influence of passion.

sn: तेन धर्मात्मना शप्तं कृत्स्नं तत्र महद्वनम्॥ अशरण्यं दुराधर्षं मृगपक्षिविवर्जितम्।
en: And cursed by that high-souled one, the entire mighty forest has become unfit to harbour (any creatures); difficult of entrance; and devoid of birds and beasts.

sn: तस्य ते काननान्तांस्तु गिरीणां कन्दराणि च ॥ प्रभवानि नदीनां च विचिन्वन्ति समाहिताः। तत्र चापि महात्मानो नापश्यञ्जनकात्मजाम्॥ हर्तारं रावणं वापि सुग्रीवप्रियकारिणः।
en: They carefully search the skirts of its woods, mountain-caves, and the sources of its streams. And those high-souled ones, devoted to the good of Sugrīva, did not find Janaka's daughter, or her ravisher, Rāvaņa.

sn: ते प्रविश्य तु तं भीमं लतागुल्मसमावृतम्॥ ददृशुर्भीमकर्माणमसुरं सुरनिर्भयम्।
en: And entering (into a wood), they saw a terrible Asura, concealed by the shrubs and plants-of dreadful deeds, and cherishing no fear even of the gods.

sn: तं दृष्ट्वा वानरा घोरं स्थितं शैलमिवासुरम्॥ गाढं परिहिताः सर्वे दृष्ट्वा तं पर्वतोपमम्।
en: And seeing that dreadful Asura, seated like a hill, and resembling a mountain, they all tightened their cloths,

sn: सोऽपि तान्वानरान्सर्वान्नष्टाः स्थेत्यब्रवीत् बली॥ अभ्यधावत संक्रुद्धो मुष्टिमुद्यम्य संगतम्।
en: And that strong one also, saying to the monkeys, Destroyed are you, and uplifting his clenched fist, rushed after them in rage.

sn: तमापतन्तं सहसा वालीपुत्रोऽङ्गदस्तदा॥ रावणोऽयमिति ज्ञात्वा तलेनाभिजघान ह।
en: And as he darted suddenly, Angada, the son of Vali, knowing, This is Ravana, administered to him a slap.

sn: स वालिपुत्राभिहतो वक्त्राच्छोणितमुद्वमन् ॥ असुरो न्यपतद् भूमौ पर्यस्त इव पर्वतः। ते तु तस्मिन् निरुच्छ्वासे वानरा जितकाशिनः॥ विचिन्वन् प्रायशस्तत्र सर्वे ते गिरिगह्वरम्।
en: Struck by Vāli's son, that Asura, his mouth vomiting blood, fell down to the earth like a hill toppled down. And on his having breathed his last, the monkeys, elated with victory, thoroughly searched that mountain cavern.

sn: विचितं तु ततः सर्वं सर्वे ते काननौकसः॥ अन्यदेवापरं घोरं विविशुर्गिरिगह्वरम्।
en: And when they had satisfied themselves that the cave had been searched all through, the dwellers of the woods entered another fearful mountain cavern.

sn: ते विचित्य पुनः खिन्ना विनिष्पत्य समागताः। एकान्ते वृक्षमूले तु निषेदुर्दीनमानसाः॥
en: And after having searched (that place) also, they came out fatigued; and with desponding hearts sat them down at a distance under the shade of a tree. they came out fatigued; and with desponding hearts sat them down at a distance under the shade of a tree.

sn: अथाङ्गदस्तदा सर्वान् वानरानिदमब्रवीत्। परिश्रान्तो महाप्राज्ञः समाश्वास्य शनैर्वचः॥
en: Then the eminently wise Angada, fatigued, spoke to all the monkeys, cheering them.

sn: वनानि गिरयो नद्यो दुर्गाणि गहनानि च। दरी गिरिगुहाश्चैव विचिताः सर्वमन्ततः॥ तत्र तत्र सहास्माभिर्जानकी न च दृश्यते। तथा रक्षोऽपहर्ता च सीतायाश्चैव दुष्कृती॥
en: Woods, and mountains, and rivers, and impenetrable wilds, and valleys, and mountain caverns have been thoroughly searched. But Jānakī we have failed to find anywhere,—or that wicked wight, the Rākṣasa that has ravished Sītā.

sn: कालश्च नो महान् यातः सुग्रीवश्चोग्रशासनः। तस्माद् भवन्तः सहिता विचिन्वन्तु समन्ततः॥
en: We have spent a great part of the term that had been assigned by Sugrīva of stern commands. Therefore, banishing languor, sadness, and invading drowsiness, do you together search all round.

sn: विहाय तन्द्रीं शोकं च निद्रां चैव समुत्थिताम्। विचिनुध्वं तथा सीतां पश्यामो जनकात्मजाम्॥ अनिर्वेदं च दाक्ष्यं च मनसश्चापराजयम्। कार्यसिद्धिकराण्याहुस्तस्मादेतद् ब्रवीम्यहम्॥
en: Do you so search Sītā, that she may be found out (by us). High spirits, ability and forwardness in action, are said to conduce to success. Therefore it is that I speak thus to you.

sn: अद्यापीदं वनं दुर्गं विचिन्वन्तु वनौकसः। खेदं त्यक्त्वा पुनः सर्वं वनमेव विचन्वताम्॥
en: You dwellers of the wood, do you to day rummage this impenetrable wood; renouncing grief, do you again search through this forest.

sn: अवश्यं कुर्वतां तस्य दृश्यते कर्मणः फलम्। परं निर्वेदमागम्य नहि नोन्मीलनं क्षमम्॥
en: Those who act, for certain behold the fruit of their endeavours; but if people once give way to grief, they cannot again attain vigour.

sn: सुग्रीवः क्रोधनो राजा तीक्ष्णदण्डश्च वानराः। भेतव्यं तस्य सततं रामस्य च महात्मनः॥
en: You monkeys, king Sugrīva is irascible; and inflicteth sharp punishments. He should be always feared, as also the magnanimous Rāma.

sn: हितार्थमेतदुक्तं वः क्रियतां यदि रोचते। उच्यतां हि क्षमं यत् तत् सर्वेषामेव वानराः॥
en: I tell you this for your good. Act accordingly, if you list. And do you also express what else you are capable of.

sn: अङ्गदस्य वचः श्रुत्वा वचनं गन्धमादनः। उवाच व्यक्तया वाचा पिपासाश्रमखिन्नया॥
en: Hearing Angada's words Gandhamādana said in candid words faint from thirst and fatigue,

sn: सदृशं खलु वो वाक्यमङ्गदो यदुवाच ह। हितं चैवानुकूलं च क्रियतामस्य भाषितम्॥
en: What Angada has said to us is worthy of him, and is beneficial and good. Do you follow his speech.

sn: पुनर्मार्गामहे शैलान् कन्दरांश्च शिलास्तथा। काननानि च शून्यानि गिरिप्रस्रवणानि च॥ यथोद्दिष्टानि सर्वाणि सुग्रीवेण महात्मना। विचिन्वन्तु वनं सर्वे गिरिदुर्गाणि संगताः॥
en: Let us afresh search hills, caves and rocks, vacant forests and mountain cascades,-in accordance with what the high-souled Sugrīva has laid down. Let all in a body rummage the wood, and the mountain caverns.

sn: ततः समुत्थाय पुनर्वानरास्ते महाबलाः। विन्ध्यकाननसंकीर्णां विरुदक्षिणां दिशम्॥
en: There rising up, the mighty monkeys again began to range the South close with forests belonging to Vindhya.

sn: ते शारदाभ्रप्रतिमं श्रीमद्रजतपर्वतम्। शृङ्गवन्तं दरीवन्तमधिरुह्य च वानराः॥
en: And the monkeys ascended the Silvern Hill resembling the autumnal welkin, graceful, and furnished with summits and valleys.

sn: तत्र लोध्रवनं रम्यं सप्तपर्णवनानि च। विचिन्वन्तो हरिवराः सीतादर्शनकाङ्क्षिणः॥
en: And eager to behold Sītā, those excellent monkeys began to search the Lodhra wood, and the Saptaparņa forests.

sn: तस्याग्रमधिरूढास्ते श्रान्ता विपुलविक्रमाः। न पश्यन्तु स्म वैदेहीं रामस्य महिषीं प्रियाम् ॥
en: And ascending its top*, those ones endued with immense prowess, experiencing fatigue, could not find Vaidehi, the beloved spouse of Rama. *i.e. the top of the Silvern Hill.

sn: ते तु दृष्टिगतं दृष्ट्वा तं शैलं बहुकन्दरम्। अध्यारोहन्त हरयो वीक्षमाणाः समन्ततः॥
en: And having surveyed that hill having many a grot, so far as the eye could range, the monkeys looking all round, descended (the eminence).

sn: अवरुह्य ततो भूमिं श्रान्ता विगतचेतसः। स्थिता मुहूर्तं तत्राथ वृक्षमूलमुपाश्रिताः॥
en: And having descended to the earth, the monkeys, bewildered, and losing their consciousness, rested for a while at the foot of a tree.

sn: ते मुहूर्तं समाश्वस्ताः किंचिद्भग्नपरिश्रमाः। पुनरेवोद्यताः कृत्स्नां मार्गितुं दक्षिणां दिशम्॥
en: And their fatigue having gone off a little, the monkeys, having been refreshed for a while, again prepared to explore the whole South.

sn: हनुमत्प्रमुखास्तावत् प्रस्थिताः प्लवगर्षभाः। विन्ध्यमेवादितः कृत्वा विचेरुश्च समन्ततः॥
en: And the monkey chiefs, headed by Hanumān, having set out (on the search), began to range all through Vindhya.

sn: सह ताराङ्गदाभ्यां तु संगम्य हनुमान् कपिः। विचिनोति च विन्ध्यस्य गुहाश्च गहनानि च॥ सिंहशार्दूलजुष्टाश्च गुहाश्च परितस्तदा। विषमेषु नगेन्द्रस्य महाप्रस्रवणेषु च॥
en: The monkey, Hanumān, in company with Tārā and Angada searcheth the caves and woods of Vindhya, caverns all around haunted by lions and tigers, and in vast inaccessible cascades in that foremost of mountains.

sn: आसेदुस्तस्य शैलस्य कोटि दक्षिणपश्चिमाम्। तेषां तत्रैव वनतां स कालो व्यत्यवर्तत॥
en: And they came to the south-western summit of the inountain. And when they sojourned there, their (appointed) term had not expired.

sn: स हि देशो दुरन्वेष्यो गुहागहनवान् महान्। तत्र वायुसुतः सर्वं विचिनोति स्म पर्वतम्॥
en: And that spacious country, consisting as it did, of caves and grots and woods, was difficult to search. And there the wind-god's offspring searched all over the mountain.

sn: परस्परेण रहिता अन्योन्यस्याविदूरतः। गजो गवाक्षो गवयः शरभो गन्धमादनः॥ मैन्दश्च द्विविदश्चैव हनूमान् जाम्बवानपि। अङ्गदो युवराजश्च तारश्च वनगोचरः॥ गिरिजालावृतान् देशान् मार्गित्वा दक्षिणां दिशम्। विचिन्वन्तस्ततस्तत्र ददृशुर्विवृतं बिलम्॥ दुर्गमृक्षबिलं नाम दानवेनाभिरक्षितम्। क्षुत्पिपासापरीतास्तु श्रान्तास्तु सलिलार्थिनः॥ अवकीर्णं लतावृक्षैर्ददृशशुस्ते महाबिलम्। तत्र क्रौञ्चश्च हंसाश्च सारसाश्चापि निष्क्रमन्॥ जलार्दाश्चकवाकाश्च रक्ताङ्गाः पद्मरेणुभिः।
en: And each apart remaining at no great distance from the others, Gaja, Gavākha and Gavaya, Sarabha, Gandhamādana, Mainda, Dwivida, and Hanumān, Jambavān, the youthful prince Angada, and Tārā, remaining in sight of the wood, after having searched the South-lands covered with mountain ranges, were searching (about), when they espied an unenclosed cavity, difficult of entry, named Věkşavila, guarded by a Dānava. And tried by hunger and thirst, worn out with fatigue, seeking for water, they found that cavity surrounded by trees and plants. And, with their bodies drenched and reddened with lotus dust, Kraunchas and swans and cranes and Chakravākas, came out of the cavity.

sn: ततस्तद् विलमासाद्य सुगन्धि दुरतिक्रमम्॥ विस्मयव्यग्रमनसो बभूवुर्वानरर्षभाः। संजातपरिशङ्कास्ते तद् बिलं प्लवगोत्तमाः॥
en: And drawing nigh to that fragrant and inaccessible cave, those superior monkeys were struck with amaze, and became eager (to enter into it).

sn: अभ्यपद्यन्त संहृष्टास्तेजोवन्तो महाबलाः। नानासत्त्वसमाकीर्णं दैत्येन्द्रनिलयोपमम्॥ दुर्दर्शमिव घोरं च दुर्विगाह्यं च सर्वशः। ततः पर्वतकूटाभो हनूमान् मारुतात्मजः॥ अब्रवीद् वानरान् घोरान् कान्तारवनकोविदः।
en: And with their minds filled with doubt, those vigorous foremost of monkeys gladly approached that cave; abounding in diverse animals, resembling the residence of the lord of Daityas, dazzling, and dreadful, and impenetrable on all sides. Then Hanuman the son of the wind-god, possessed of the splendour of a mountain-summit, cognizant of woods and forests, said to the grim-visaged apes,

sn: गिरिजालावृतान् देशान् मार्गित्वा दक्षिणां दिशम्॥ वयं सर्वे परिश्रान्ता न च पश्याम मैथिलीम्।
en: Having explored the South, (containing) countries enveloped with mountain chains, we have all got fatigued, but we have failed to find Mithila's daughter.

sn: अस्माच्चापि बिलाद्धंसाः क्रौञ्चाश्च सह सारसैः॥ जलार्द्राश्चक्रवाकाश्च निष्पतन्ति स्म सर्वशः। नूनं सलिलवानत्र कूपो वा यदि वा हृदः॥ तथा चेमे बिलद्वारे स्निग्धास्तिष्ठन्ति पादपाः।
en: And from yonder cave come out swarms of and and kraunchas and chakravākas, drenched with water. For certain here is a well or a watery expanse. And at the mouth of the cave there are these cool trees.'

sn: इत्युक्तास्तद् बिलं सर्वे विविशुस्तमिवावृतम्॥ अचन्द्रसूर्यं हरयो ददृशू रोमहर्षणम्। निशाम्य तस्मात् सिंहांश्च तांस्तांश्च मृगपक्षिणः॥ प्रविष्टा हरिशार्दूला बिलं तिमिरसंवृतम्। न तेषां सज्जते दृष्टिर्न तेजो न पराक्रमः॥ वायोरिव गतिस्तेषां दृष्टिस्तमसि वर्तते।
en: Hanumān having said this, all the monkeys went into the cave covered with darkness; without the sun or the moon, capable of making one's down stand on end. And seeing lions, and birds and beasts (ranging around), those tigerlike monkeys entered that cave covered with swans cranes darkness. And (there) neither their ken, nor their vigour, nor yet their prowess was baffled: and their speed resembled the wind, and their sight remained unimpaired albeit in darkness.

sn: ते प्रविष्टास्तु वेगेन तद् बिलं कपिकुञ्जराः॥ प्रकाशं चाभिरामं च ददृशुर्देशमुत्तमम्। ततस्तस्मिन् बिले भीमे नानापादपसंकुले॥ अन्योन्यं सम्परिष्वज्य जग्मुर्योजनमन्तरम्।
en: And those foremost of monkeys rushed into the cavity; and beheld displayed (before them) an excellent and charming scene. And embracing each other in that fearful cave rife with various trees, they passed over an hundred Yojanas.

sn: ते नष्टसंज्ञास्तृषिताः सम्भ्रान्ताः सलिलार्थिनः॥ परिपेतुर्बिले तस्मिन् कंचित् कालमतन्द्रिताः। ते कृशा दीनवदनाः परिश्रान्ताः प्लवङ्गमाः॥ आलोकं ददृशुर्वीरा निराशा जीविते यदा।
en: And deprived of their sense, and tried with thirst, and bewildered, and thirsting for water, they for a time vigilantly descended in darkness down the cave. And emaciated, with woebegone faces, and spent, those monkeys despairing of their lives, (at last) saw light.

sn: ततस्तं देशमागम्य सौम्या वितिमिरं वनम्॥ ददृशुः काञ्चनान् वृक्षान् दीप्तवैश्वानरप्रभान्।
en: Those mild ones, coming to a spot free from darkness, saw golden trees, possessed of the brightness of flaming fire.

sn: सालास्तालास्तमालांश्च पुंनागान्वञ्जुलान्धवान्॥ चम्पकान् नागवृक्षांश्च कर्णिकारांश्च पुष्पितान्। स्तबकैः काञ्चनैश्चित्र रक्तैः किसलयैस्तथा॥ आपीडैश्च लताभिश्च हेमाभरणभूषितान्। तरुणाादित्यसंकाशान् वैदूर्यमयवेदिकान्॥ विभ्राजमानान् वपुषा पादपांश्च हिरण्मयान्। नीलवैदूर्यवर्णाश्च पद्मिनी: पतगैर्वृताः॥ महद्भिः काञ्चनैर्वृक्षवृतं बालार्कसंनिभैः। जातरूपमयैर्मत्स्यैर्महद्भिश्चाथ पङ्कजैः॥ नलिनीस्तत्र ददृशुः प्रसन्नसलिलायुताः।
en: And Sālas and palms, and Tamālas, Punnāgas, Vañjulas, and Dhavās, Campakas, Nāga trees, Karņikāras in flower, with variegated golden bunches and twigs, and crests of clusters, and plants,-embellished with golden garniture; resembling the infantine sun,-on daises composed of lapises;—golden trees with resplendent bodies, having the hues of purple lapises; and lotus-plants flocked with fowls; and (spots) surrounded by large golden trees, like to the infantine sun; and tanks with large fishes or gold and lotuses, containing pleasant waters-all these saw there.

sn: काञ्चनानि विमानानि राजतानि तथैव च॥ हैमराजतभौमानि वैदूर्यमणिमन्ति च। तपनीयगवाक्षाणि मुक्ताजालावृतानि च॥ ददृशुस्तत्र हरयो गृहमुख्यानि सर्वशः।
en: And the monkeys saw there golden as well as silvern vehicles, and elegant dwellings all round veiled with nets of pearls; having golden balconys; with their grounds paved with gold and silver; and furnished with lapis lazulis.

sn: पुष्पितान् फलिनो वृक्षान् प्रवालमणिसंनिभान्॥ काश्चनभ्रमरांश्चैव मधूनि च समन्ततः। मणिकाञ्चनचित्राणि शयनान्यासनानि च॥ विविधानि विशालानि ददृशुस्ते समन्ततः। हैमराजतकांस्यानां भाजनानां च राशयः॥ अगुरूणां च दिव्यानां चन्दनानां च संचयान्। शुचीन्यभ्यवहाराणि मूलानि च फलानि च॥ महार्हाणि च यानानि मधूनि रसवन्ति च। दिव्यानामम्बराणां च महार्हाणां च संचयान्॥ कम्बलानां च चित्राणामजिनानां च संचयान्।
en: And on all sides they saw trees bearing fruits and flowers resembling coral; and golden black bees, and honey all round, and various spacious seats and beds about dight with gold and jewels. And searching in that cave, the exceedingly effulgent heroic monkeys saw heaps of golden, silver and bell-metal vessels; and heaps of excellent aguru and sandal; and pure fruits and roots; and costly vehicles and various kinds of sapid honey; and loads of costly attire; and lots of variegated woolen cloths and deer-skins; as well as a female, from near.

sn: तत्र तत्र विचिन्वन्तो बिले तत्र महाप्रभाः॥ ददृशुर्वानराः शूराः स्त्रियं कांचिददूरतः। तां च ते ददृशुस्तत्र चीरकृष्णाजिनाम्बराम्॥ तापसी नियताहारां ज्वलन्तीमिव तेजसा।। विस्मिता हरयस्तत्र व्यवतिष्ठन्त सर्वशः। पप्रच्छ हनुमांस्तत्र काऽसि त्वं कस्य वा बिलम्॥
en: And they found her there, wearing a black deer-skin,-a female ascetic, with restrained fare-as if flaming in energy. Amazed, the monkeys sat them down in a body. And then Hanumān asked her,-Who are you? And to whom does this cave belong?

sn: ततो हनूमान् गिरिसंनिकाशः कृताञ्जलिस्तामभिवाद्य वृद्धाम्। पप्रच्छ का त्वं भवनं बिलं च रत्नानि चेमानि वदस्व कस्य॥
en: And-Hanumān like to a hill, bowing down to the old women with joined hands, asked her, saying,-Who are you? And tell me, to whom belong this edifice and the cave as well as all these jewels.

sn: इत्युक्त्वा हनुमांस्तत्र चीरकृष्णाजिनाम्बराम्। अब्रवीत् तां महाभागां तापसी धर्मचारिणीम्॥
en: Having said this to that female clad in a piece of black deer-skin, Hanumān asked that highly religious ascetic practising pious offices,

sn: इदं प्रविष्टा सहसा बिलं तिमिरसंवृताम्। क्षुत्पिपासापरिश्रान्ताः परिखिन्त्राश्च सर्वशः॥ महद् धरण्या विवरं प्रविष्टाः स्म पिपासिताः। इमांस्त्वेवंविधान् भावान् विविधानद्भुतोपमान्॥ दृष्ट्वा वयं प्रव्यथिताः सम्भ्रान्ता नष्टचेतसः। कस्येतै काञ्चना वृक्षास्तरुणादित्यसंनिभाः॥
en: Having rashly entered this cave enveloped in gloom, we have been exercised with hunger and thirst; and are extremely faint. And, having entered this mighty cave underneath the earth, we have become thirsty. And, seeing all these wonderful phenomena, we have become afflicted, and bewildered; and have lost our sense. To whom belong these golden trees resembling the infantine sun;

sn: शुचीन्यभ्यवहाराणि मूलानि च फलानि च। काञ्चनानि विमानानि राजतानि गृहाणि च ॥ तपनीयगवाक्षाणि मणिजालावृतानि च। पुष्पिताः फलवन्तश्च पुण्याः सुरभिगन्धयः॥ इमे जाम्बूनदमयाः पादपाः कस्य तेजसा।
en: And the pure fruits and roots, and the houses and vehicles of gold and silver,-veiled in networks of jewels, and furnished with golden windows? And by whose energy are these golden trees (here), bearing flowers, crowned with fruits, grateful to the sight, and breathing rich odour?

sn: काञ्चनानि च पद्मानि जातानि विमले जले॥ कथं मत्स्याश्च सौवर्णा दृश्यन्ते सह कच्छपैः। आत्मनस्त्वनुभावाद् वा कस्य वैतत्तपोबलम्॥ अजानतां नः सर्वेषां सर्वमाख्यातुमर्हसि।
en: And golden lotuses spring in in lucent water,-how golden fishes are discovered in it along with tortoises! Have these sprung from your power; or do they owe their existence to the ascetic energy of any other? It behoves you to relate all this to us who are ignorant of everything.

sn: एवमुक्ता हनुमता तापसी धर्मचारिणी॥ प्रत्युवाच हनूमन्तं सर्वभूताहिते रता।
en: Thus addressed by Hanumān, the female ascetic practising righteousness, and engaged in the welfare of all beings, replied to Hanumān,

sn: मयो नाम महातेजा मायावी वानरर्षभ॥ तेनेदं निर्मितं सर्वं मायया काञ्चनं वनम्।
en: O foremost of monkeys, there is one, named Maya, spreader of illusions. By him has this entire golden grove been constructed through his wonderful power of construction.

sn: पुरा दानवमुख्यानां विश्वकर्मा बभूव ह॥ येनेदं काञ्चनं दिव्यं निर्मितं भवनोत्तमम्।
en: He that as reared this excellent golden grove, and this charming mansion, was formerly the Viśvakarmā* of the principal Dänavas. *The name of the celestial architect.

sn: स तु वर्षसहस्राणि तपस्तप्त्वा महद्वने॥ पितामहाद् वरं लेभे सर्वमौशनसं धनम्।
en: Having for a thousand years thousand years practised austerities in this vast forest, he obtained a boon from the Great-father,-in virtue of which he had attained consummate mastery in his art, as well as absolute control over the materials required therein.

sn: विधाय सर्वं बलवान् सर्वकामेश्वरस्तदा ॥ उवास सुखितः कालं कंचिदस्मिन् महावने।
en: Having accomplished everything, that powerful one, commanding every enjoyment, for a time happily dwelt in this mighty forest.

sn: तमप्सरसि हेमायां सक्तं दानवपुङ्गवम्॥ विक्रम्यैवाशनिं गृह्य जघानेशः पुरंदरः।
en: Then he, happening to conceive a passion for an Apsara, Hema (by name), Purandara, vigorously wielding his thunder-bolt, struck him dead.

sn: इदं च ब्रह्मणा दत्तं हैमायै वनमुत्तमम्॥ शाश्वतः कामभोगश्च गृहं चेदं हिरण्मयम्।
en: Then Brahmä conferred on Hemā this fine forest and this golden mansion, with the perpetual privilege of enjoying every pleasure herein.

sn: दुहिता मेरुसावर्णेरहं तस्याः स्वयंप्रभा॥ इदं रक्षामि भवनं हेमाया वानरोत्तम।
en: I, Svayamprabhā by name,-the daughter of Merusāvarņi, guard this house of Hemā, O foremost of monkeys.

sn: मम प्रियसखी हेमा नृत्तगीतविशारदा ॥ तया दत्तवरा चास्मि रक्षामि भवनं महत्।
en: Hemā, skilled in dance and song, is my dear friend. having received her blessing, I guard this vast forest.

sn: किं कार्यं कस्य वा हेतोः कान्ताराणि प्रपद्यथ॥ कथं चेदं वनं दुर्गं युष्माभिरुपलक्षितम्।
en: What is your errand? And why is it that you have arrived at these lone woods? And how have you managed to see this inaccessible forest?

sn: शुचीन्यभ्यवहाराणि मूलानि च फलानि च। भुक्त्वा पीत्वा च पानीयं सर्वं मे वक्तुमर्हसि ॥
en: Having partaken of these fruits and roots intended for use, and drunk, do you detail all this to me.

sn: अथ तानब्रवीत् सर्वान् विश्रान्तान् हरियूथपान्। इदं वचनमेकाना तापसी धर्मचारिणी॥
en: Then to all the monkey-chiefs, after they had rested, the female ascetic, engaged in righteous practices, eagerly said these words,

sn: वानरा यदि वः खेदः प्रणष्टः फलभक्षणात्। यदि चैतन्मया श्राव्यं श्रोतुमिच्छामि तां कथाम्॥
en: You monkeys, if your pain has gone off in consequence of the fare of fruits which you have partaken, and also if it be fit to be heard by me, I would listen to your narration.

sn: तस्यास्तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा हनूमान् मारुतात्मजः। आर्जवेन यथातत्त्वमाख्यातुमुपचक्रमे॥
en: Hearing her words, Hanumān, the son of the wind-god, in all candour began to relate everything faithfully.

sn: राजा सर्वस्य लोकस्य महेन्द्रवरुणोपमः। रामो दाशरथिः श्रीमान् प्रविष्टो दण्डकावनम्॥ लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्रात्रा वैदेह्या सह भार्यया। तस्य भार्या जनस्थानाद् रावणेन हृता बलात्॥
en: The Sovereign of all this world, resembling Mahendra or Varuna, Rāma, the graceful son of Dasaratha, entered the woods of Dandaka, in company with his brother, Laksmana, as well as his spouse, Vaidehi. His wife has been forcibly carried of by Rāvana.

sn: वीरस्तस्य सखा राज्ञः सुग्रीवो नाम वानरः। राजा वानरमुख्यानां येन प्रस्थापिता वयम् ॥ अगस्त्यचरितामाशां दक्षिणां यमरक्षिताम्। सहैभिर्वानरैर्मुख्यैरङ्गदप्रमुखैर्वयम्॥
en: His friend is that heroic king, the monkey named Sugrīva. By that monarch of the foremnost monkeys have we been despatched (hither). And we have, joining company with these prime monkeys headed by Angada, come to the South, protected by Yama, and inhabited by Agastya.

sn: रावणं सहिताः सर्वे राक्षसं कामरूपिणम्। सीतया सह वैदेह्या मार्गध्वमिति चोदिताः॥
en: And we have been commissioned, 'Do you all search for the Rākşasa Rāvana, wearing forms at will, along with Videha's daughter, Sītā.'

sn: विचित्य तु वनं सर्वं समुद्र दक्षिणां दिशम्। वयं बुभुक्षिताः सर्वे वृक्षमूलमुपाश्रिताः॥
en: Having searched through the forest as well as the ocean on the South, we becoming hungry, sat down at the foot of a tree.

sn: विवर्णवदनाः सर्वे सर्वे ध्यानपरायणाः। नाधिगच्छामहे पारं मग्नाश्चिन्तामहार्णवे॥
en: And with pallid countenance, we all, absorbed in thought, sank in a wide sea of anxiety, which we could not cross.

sn: चारयन्तस्ततश्चक्षुर्दृष्टवन्तो महद् बिलम्। लतापादपसंछन्नं तिमिरेण समावृतम्॥
en: And casting our eyes around, we spyed a huge cave covered with trees and plants and enveloped in gloom.

sn: अस्माद्धंसा जलक्लिन्नाः पक्षैः सलिलरेणुभिः। कुरराः सारसाश्चैव निष्पतन्ति पतत्त्रिणः॥
en: And (it came to pass that) from this (cave) came out swans, drenched with water, with drops of water on their wings,-and plumed kuravas and cranes.

sn: साध्वत्र प्रविशामेति मया तूक्ताः प्लवङ्गमाः। तेषामपि ह सर्वेषामनुमानमुपागतम्॥ अस्मिन् निपतिताः सर्वेऽप्यथ कार्यत्वरान्विताः। ततो गाढं निपतिता गृह्य हस्तैः परस्परम्॥ इदं प्रविष्टाः सहसा बिलं तिमिरसंवृतम्। . एतन्नः कार्यमेतेन कृत्येन वयमागताः॥
en: Let us enter here', said I to the monkeys. And they also arrived at that conclusion.* And thereupon they, bestirring themselves, entered into the cave. And firmly griping each other's hands, they at once made entry into the cave covered with darkness. This is our errand; and it is on this job that we have come. *Namely, that water was to be found there.

sn: त्वां चैवोपगताः सर्वे परिघुना बुभुक्षिताः। आतिथ्यधर्मदत्तानि मूलानि च फलानि च॥ अस्माभिरुपयुक्तानि बुभुक्षापरिपीडितैः।
en: Having come to you, hungry, and exhausted, we, who had been sore tried by hunger, have been entertained with fruits and roots, agreeably to the code regulating hospitality.

sn: यत् त्वया रक्षिताः सर्वे म्रियमाणा बुभुक्षया॥ ब्रूहि प्रत्युपकारार्थं किं ते कुर्वन्तु वानराः।
