en: And as you had saved the monkeys, who were weary and suffering from hunger, tell (me),-what benefit shall the monkeys do you in return?

sn: एवमुक्ता तु सर्वज्ञा वानरैस्तैः स्वयंप्रभा॥ प्रत्युवाच ततः सर्वानिदं वानरयूथपान्।
en: Thus addressed by the apes, the all-knowing Svayamprabhā replied to the monkey-chiefs, saying,

sn: सर्वेषां परितुष्टाऽस्मि वानराणां तरस्विनाम्॥ चरन्त्या मम धर्मेण न कार्यमिह केनचित्।
en: Well pleased am I with the fast-footing monkeys. But by one engaged in your duties, there is no work that is desiderated.

sn: एवमुक्तः शुभं वाक्यं तापस्या धर्मसंहितम्॥ उवाच हनुमान् वाक्यं तामनिन्दितलोचनाम्।
en: Thus accosted in excellent words fraught with asceticism and righteousness Hanumān spoke to that one of faultless eyes, saying.

sn: शरणं त्वां प्रपन्नाः स्मः सर्वे वै धर्मचारिणीम्॥ यः कृतः समयोऽस्मासु सुग्रीवेण महात्मना। स तु कालो व्यतिक्रान्तो बिले च परिवर्तताम्॥
en: We all take refuge in you, practising piety. the term that had been fixed by the high-souled Sugrīva in respect of us, shall all be spent in this cave. Therefore it behoveth you to deliver us from this place.

sn: सा त्वमस्याद् बिलादस्मानुत्तारयितुमर्हसि। तस्मात् सुग्रीववचनादतिक्रान्तान् गतायुषः॥ त्रातुमर्हसि नः सर्वान् सुग्रीवभयशङ्कितान्।
en: It behove you to save us, exercised with fear for Sugriva,-who, happening to override Sugriva's command, shall lose our lives. And, further, O you that practisest righteousness, great is the task that is to be performed by us.

sn: महच्च कार्यमस्माभिः कर्तव्यं धर्मचारिणि ॥ तच्चापि न कृतं कार्यमस्माभिरिह वासिभिः।
en: But if we stay here, that work of ours shall remain unaccomplished.

sn: एवमुक्ता हनुमता तापसी वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥ जीवता दुष्करं मन्ये प्रविष्टेन निवर्तितुम्। तपसः सुप्रभावेण नियमोपार्जितेन च॥ सर्वानेव बिलादस्माद् तारयिष्यामि वानरान्।
en: Thus addressed by Hanumān, the ascetic said, Once entering, hard it is for any one to return (hence) alive. But by the potency of my asceticism acquired through self-discipline, I shall deliver all the monkeys from this den.

sn: निमीलयत चढूंषि सर्वे वानरपुङ्गवाः॥ नहि निष्क्रमितुं शक्यमनिमीलितलोचनैः।
en: You foremost of monkeys, do you close your eyes. No one is able to issue out of this place without closing one's eyes.

sn: ततो निमीलिताः सर्वे सुकुमाराङ्गुलैः करैः॥ सहसा पिदधुदृष्टिं हृष्टा गमनकाझ्या ।
en: Then they, eagerly desirous of going out, closed their sight* with their hands furnished with tender fingers. *The text has nimilitah—and thus they closed their eyes. This redundant epithet has been left out in the translation, as it would render the version extremely awkward.

sn: वानरास्तु महात्मानो हस्तरुद्धमुखास्तदा॥ निमेषान्तरमात्रेण बिलादुत्तारितास्तया।
en: The magnanimous monkeys, with their faces covered with their palms, were in the twinkling of an eye, liberated from the den by her.

sn: उवाच सर्वांस्तांस्तत्र तापसी धर्मचारिणी॥ निःसृतान् विषमात् तस्मात् समाश्वास्येदमब्रवीत्।
en: And then the pious anchoret spoke to them there. And when they had come out of the fearful den, cheering them up, she said,

sn: एष विन्ध्यो गिरिः श्रीमान् नानादुमलतायुतः॥ एष प्रस्रवणः शैलः सागरोऽयं महोदधिः। स्वस्ति वोऽस्तु गमिष्यामि भवनं वानरर्षभाः। इत्युक्त्वा तद् बिलं श्रीमत् प्रविवेश स्वयंप्रभा॥
en: This is the fair Vindhya mountain filled with various trees and herbs. This is the Praśravaņa hill; and this is the great deep. Fair Fortune! I go to my abode, you foremost of monkeys. Having spokea thus, Svayamprabhā entered that captivating cave.

sn: ततस्ते ददृशुर्घोरं सागरं वरुणालयम्। अपारमभिगर्जन्तं घोरैरुर्मिभिराकुलम्॥
en: Then they saw the ocean—abode of Varuņashoreless, resounding, rife with dreadful billows.

sn: मयस्य मायाविहितं गिरिदुर्गे विचिन्वताम्। तेषां मासो व्यतिक्रान्तो यो राज्ञा समयः कृतः॥
en: Exploring the mountain fateness of Maya*, they spent the month that had been set by the king. *Named Rhiksavila.

sn: विन्ध्यस्य तु गिरेः पाते सम्प्रपुष्पितपादपे। उपविश्य महात्मानश्चिन्तामापेदिरे तदा॥
en: Then sitting down at the foot of the Vindhya mountain, containing blossoming trees, at that time* those high-souled ones indulged-in reflections. *i.e. at the beginning of winter.

sn: ततः पुष्पातिभाराग्रॉल्लताशतसमावृतान्। दुमान् वासन्तिकान् दृष्ट्वा बभूवुर्भयशङ्किताः॥
en: Beholding vernal trees bending beneath the load of flowers, and environed by hundreds of plants, they were inspired with apprehension.

sn: ते वसन्तमनुप्राप्तं प्रतिवेद्य परस्परम्। नष्टसंदेशकालार्था निपेतुर्धरणीतले॥
en: And each knowing that spring had appeared, they, the term appointed for their task having run out, dropped down on the ground.

sn: ततस्तान् कपिवृद्धांश्च शिष्टांश्चैव वनौकसः। वाचा मधुरयाऽऽभाष्य यथावदनुमान्य च॥ स तु सिंहवृषस्कन्धः पीनायतभुजः कपिः। युवराजो महाप्राज्ञ अङ्गदो वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
en: Thereat, with bland words properly honouring the aged apes and the rest dwelling in the woods, that monkey having the shoulders of a lion or a bull, and plump and broad arms-the youthful prince Angada, endowed with high wisdom, spoke,

sn: शासनात् कपिराजस्य वयं सर्वे विनिर्गताः। मासः पूर्णो बिलस्थानां हरयः किं न बुध्यत ॥ वयमाश्वयुजे मासि कालसंख्याव्यवस्थिताः। प्रस्थिताः सोऽपि चातीतः किमतः कार्यमुत्तरम्॥
en: We have come out at the mandate of the monarch of monkeys. While we sojourned in the cave, a full month had passed away, you monkeys. Why do you not understand this? We set out, engaging that our term of search should reach no further than the end of Kärtika;* but that has expired. Now, what next is to be done? *October.

sn: भवन्तः प्रत्ययं प्राप्ता नीतिमार्गविशारदाः। हितेष्वभिरता भर्तुर्निसृष्टाः सर्वकर्मसु॥ कर्मस्वप्रतिमाः सर्वे दिक्षु विश्रुतपौरुषाः। मां पुरस्कृत्य निर्याताः पिङ्गाक्षप्रतिचोदिताः॥ इदानीमकृतार्थानां मर्तव्यं नात्र संशयः। हरिराजस्य संदेशमकृत्वा कः सुखी भवेत्॥ अस्मिन्नतीते काले तु सुग्रीवेण कृते स्वयम्। प्रायोपवेशनं युक्तं सर्वेषां च वनौकसाम्॥
en: Having received the orders (of the king), you, conversant with polity, engaged in the welfare of your master, expert in every work, incomparable in execution, and renowned in every quarter, have come out, commanded by the lord of monkeys. Now, having failed to attain our object, we shall meet with death. There is no doubt whatever about this. Who, having been unsuccessful in doing the mandate of the king of monkeys, enjoyeth ease? Now all the rangers of the forest should fast for death.

sn: तीक्ष्णः प्रकृत्या सुग्रीवः स्वाभिभावे व्यवस्थितः। न क्षमिष्यति नः सर्वानपराधकृतो गतान्॥
en: Naturally stern, Sugrīva, established as our master, shall not forgive us, when we repair there, after having transgressed thus.

sn: अप्रवृत्तो च सीतायाः पापमेव करिष्यति। तस्मात् क्षममिहाद्यैव्र गन्तुं प्रायोपवेशनम्॥ त्यक्त्वा पुत्रांश्च दारांश्च धनानि च गृहाणि च ।
en: Sītā not having been found out, Sugrīva, for certain, shall commit this sin.* Therefore it is fit that, forsaking our sons, and wives, and wealth, and homes, we this very day sit down to starve ourselves to death. *i.e. slay us.

sn: ध्रुवं नो हिंसते राजा सर्वान् प्रतिगतानितः॥ वधेनाप्रतिरूपेण श्रेयान् मृत्युरिहैव नः।
en: Death at this place is preferable to the unequal punishment (we must meet with at the hands of Sugriva).

sn: न चाहं यौवराज्येन सुग्रीवेणाभिषेचितः॥ नरेन्द्रेणाभिषिक्तोऽस्मि रामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा।
en: And, further, I have not been installed heirapparent by Sugrīva: I have been sprinkled by that foremost of kings, Rāma of untiring energy.

sn: स पूर्वं बद्धवैरो मां राजा दृष्ट्वा व्यतिक्रमम्॥ घातयिष्यति दण्डेन तीक्ष्णेन कृतनिश्चयः।
en: Entertaining enmity against me of old, the king, seeing this lapse, must be firmly determined to take my life by means of a severe sentence.

sn: किं मे सुहद्भिर्व्यसनं पश्यद्भिर्जीवितान्तरे। इहैव प्रायमासिष्ये पुण्ये सागररोधसि ॥
en: What is the use of suffering my friends to look on my disaster at the last moment of my existence? Therefore even on this sacred shore of the sea shall I sit down to starve myself.

sn: एतच्छ्रुत्वा कुमारेण युवराजेन भाषितम्। सर्वे ते वानरश्रेष्ठाः करुणं वाक्यमब्रुवन् ॥
en: Hearing the tender prince speak thus, all those principal monkeys pathetically observed,

sn: तीक्ष्णः प्रकृत्या सुग्रीवः प्रियारक्तश्च राघवः। समीक्ष्याकृतकार्यांस्तु तस्मिंश्च समये गते ॥ अदृष्टायां च वैदेह्यां दृष्ट्वा चैव समागतान्। राघवप्रियकामाय घातयिष्यत्यसंशयम्॥
en: Sugrīva is harsh by nature, and Rāghava loveth his wife dearly. The time appointed having passed by, seeing us (come) without attaining success in the task, and seeing us arrive without obtaining a sight of Vaidehi, (Sugrīva) shall certainly slay us from the desire of doing what is agreeable to Rāghava.

sn: न क्षमं चापराद्धानां गमनं स्वामिपार्श्वतः। प्रधानभूताश्च वयं सुग्रीवस्य समागताः॥ इहैव सीतामन्वीक्ष्य प्रवृत्तिमुपलभ्य वा। नो चेद् गच्छाम तं वीरं गमिष्यामो यमक्षयम्॥
en: Those who have transgressed, cannot come to the side of their master. Having come hither as the principal servants of Sugrīva, we shall either see Sītā or obtain information concerning her, or else, O hero, we shall repair to the mansion of Yama.

sn: प्लवङ्गमानां तु भयार्दितानां श्रुत्वा वचस्तार इदं बभाषे। अलं विषादेन बिलं प्रविश्य वसाम सर्वे यदि रोचते वः॥
en: Hearing the speeches of the monkeys afflicted with fear, Tārā said,-No use of indulging in grief. If you relish it, let us all entering the cave, dwell there.

sn: इदं हि मायाविहितं सुदुर्गमं प्रभूतपुष्पोदकभोज्यपेयम्। न राघवाद् वानरराजतोऽपि वा॥
en: This place abounding in flowers and waters, meats and drinks,—which has been brought forth by the power of ilusion, is incapable of being approached. Here we have no fear from Purandara, or Rāghava, or the king of monkeys.

sn: मूचुश्च सर्वे हरयः प्रतीताः। मसक्तमयैव विधीयतां नः॥
en: Hearing the welcome words of Angada, the monkeys,-being convinced, said,-Do you this very day so order that we may not be slain.

sn: तथा ब्रुवति तारे तु ताराधिपतिवर्चसि। अथ मेने हृतं राज्यं हनूमानङ्गदेन तत्॥
en: When Tārā, bright as the moon, had spoken thus, Hanumān felt as if Angada had already deprived (Sugrīva) of his kingdom.* The sense is very obscure. One meaning is: Hanumān thought that Argada acquiescing in what Tārā had said, must remain there,-and ultimately endeavour to wrest the kingdom from Sugriva. Another meaning is: Hanumān conceived that remaining there in peace, Angada would consider his position as enviable as if he had extorted the kingdom from Sugrīva.

sn: बुद्ध्या ह्यष्टाङ्गया युक्तं चतुर्बलसमन्वितम्। चतुर्दशगुणं मेने हनूमान् वालिनः सुतम्॥ आपूर्यमाणं शश्वच्च तेजोबलपराक्रमैः। शशिनं शुक्लपक्षादौ वर्धमानमिव श्रिया॥ बृहस्पतिसमं बुद्ध्या विक्रमे सदृशं पितुः। शुश्रूषमाणं तारस्य शुक्रस्येव पुरंदरम्॥
en: Hanumān deemned Vāli's son as endowed with intelligence consisting of eight elements; with power of four kinds; and the four and ten virtues; as ever fraught with energy, strength and prowess; as growing in grace like the moon during the lighted fortnight; as resembling Brhaspati in intelligence; and in prowess, his own sire; and as ever listening to. Tārā's counsels, as Purandara listens to the counsels of Sukra.

sn: भर्तुरर्थे परिश्रान्तं सर्वशास्त्रविशारदः। अभिसंधातुमारेभे हनूमानङ्गदं ततः॥
en: And Hanumān versed in all branches of learning, finding Angada backward in the affair of his master, began inspire him with fear.* *Touching Tārā.

sn: स चतुर्णामुपायानां द्वितीयमुपवर्णयन्। भेदयामास तान् सर्वान् वानरान् वाक्यसम्पदा॥
en: He, wealthy in words, laying under contribution the second of the four means,* had created division among those monkeys. *Referred to above.

sn: तेषु सर्वेषु भिन्नेषु ततोऽभीषयदङ्गदम्। भीषणैर्विविधैर्वाक्यैः कोपोपायसमन्वतैः॥
en: On their being divided, he (Hanuman) set about raising Angada's apprehension by various fear-fraught speech, referring to punishments.

sn: त्वं समर्थतरः पित्रा युद्धे तारेय वै ध्रुवम्। दृढं धारयितुं शक्तः कपिराज्यं यथा पिता॥
en: O Tārā's son, you are for certain more capable of fight than even your sire; and you are also able to hold the monkey-kingdom as firmly as he.

sn: नित्यमस्थिरचित्ता हि कपयो हरिपुंगव। नाज्ञाप्यं विषहिष्यन्ति पुत्रदारं विना त्वया॥
en: But, O foremost of monkeys, the monkeys are always inconstant in character. Bereft of their wives and sons, they shall not bear your behest.

sn: त्वं नैते ह्यनुरञ्जेयुः प्रत्यक्षं प्रवदामि ते। यथाऽयं जाम्बवान् नीलः सुहोत्रश्च महाकपिः॥ नाहं ते इमे सर्वे सामदानादिभिर्गुणैः। दण्डेन न त्वया शक्याः सुग्रीवादपकर्षितुम् ॥
en: They shall never take to you. This I tell you in presence of all. And I will tell you what. You neither by the virtues of conciliation, charity and the rest, nor by chastisement, shall succeed in drawing to your side this Jāmbavān, or Nīla, or the mighty ape Suhotra, or myself.

sn: विगृह्यासनमप्याहुर्दुर्बलेन बलीयसा। आत्मरक्षाकरस्तस्मान्न विगृह्णीत दुर्बलः॥
en: A strong one wronging another that is weak, can live; therefore a weak person anxious for self-preservation, should never wrong (a strong individual).

sn: यां चेमां मन्यसे धात्रीमेतद् बलमिति श्रुतम्। एतल्लक्ष्मणबाणानामीषत् कार्य विदारणम्॥
en: You considerest that this cave may serve for your protectress,* having heard of it (said by Tārā); but to rive the same is but light work for the shafts of Laksmana. *The word meaning cave is feminine in Sanskrit.

sn: स्वल्पं हि कृतमिन्द्रेण क्षिपता ह्यशनिं पुरा। लक्ष्मणो निशितैर्बाणैर्भिन्द्यात् पत्रकुटं यथा॥
en: Formerly this was cleft a little by Indra, with his thunderbolt hurled (against it);* but now Lakṣmaṇa would pierce it like a leaf-stalk, by means of his keen arrows. *The commentator interprets the passage differently: Formerly Indra did a little damage herein-i.e. merely slew Maya, the architect of the mansion. This is ingenuity. I give the plain sense.

sn: लक्ष्मणस्य च नाराचा बहवः सन्ति तद्विधाः। वज्राशनिसमस्पर्शा गिरीणामपि दारकाः॥
en: Lakşmaņa has many an iron arrow like Indra's thunderbolt or that of the sky,* capable of riving even mountains. 15 *Vajrasani-Vajra is the thunder-bolt in the hand of Indra, and Asani—the thunder-bolt produced by clouds.

sn: अवस्थानं यदैव त्वमासिष्यसि परंतप। तदैव हरयः सर्वे त्यक्ष्यन्ति कृतनिश्चयाः॥
en: O subduer of enemies, soon as you shall set up here, the monkeys, making up their minds, shall forsake you.

sn: स्मरन्तः पुत्रदाराणां नित्योद्विग्ना बुभुक्षिताः। खेदिता दुःखशय्याभिस्त्वां करिष्यन्ति पृष्ठतः॥
en: Remembering their wives and sons, ever anxious (on account of Sugrīva, pining for domestic happiness, ad aggrieved (at their pitiable plight), they shall turn their backs upon you.

sn: स त्वं हीनः सुहृद्भिश्च हितकामैश्च बन्धुभिः। तृणादपि भृशोद्विग्रः स्पन्दमानाद् भविष्यसि ॥ अत्युग्रवेगा निशिता घोरा लक्ष्मणसायकाः। अपावृत्तं जिघांसन्तो महावेगा दुरासदाः॥
en: Then forsaken by the kindred as well as friends seeking your welfare, you shall be struck with affright even at a quaking blade of grass. If you make head (against Sugriva), the sharpened shafts of Laksmana, terrible, of exceeding impetuosity and mighty vehemence, and incapable of being baffled, shall be eager to slay you.

sn: अस्माभिस्तु गतं सार्धं विनीतवदुपस्थितम्। आनुपूर्व्यात्तु सुग्रीवो राज्ये त्वां स्थापयिष्यति॥
en: On the contrary, if you in humble guise present yourself (before him) along with us, he shall-establish you in the kingdom, in consideration of your being the next heir.

sn: धर्मराजः पितृव्यस्ते प्रीतिकामो दृढव्रतः। शुचिः सत्यप्रतिज्ञश्च स त्वां जातु न नाशयेत्॥
en: A righteous sovereign, steady in vow, clean, and truthful in promise, your uncle, who cherishes affection for you shall not by any mears chastise. Ju.

sn: प्रियकामश्च ते मातुस्दर्थं चास्य जीवितम्। तस्यापत्यं च नास्त्यन्यत् तस्मादङ्गद गम्यताम्॥
en: He loves your mother, and his life is for her; and she has no other son. Therefore, O Angada, go along with us.

sn: श्रुत्वा हनुमतो वाक्यं प्रश्रितं धर्मसंहितम्। स्वामिसत्कारसंयुक्तमङ्गदो वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
en: Hearing Hanuman's speech, uttered meekly, fraught with morality, and reflecting honour upon Sugriva, Angada said,

sn: स्थैर्यमात्ममनःशौचमानृशंस्यमथार्जवम्। विक्रमश्चैव धैर्यं च सुग्रीवे नोपपद्यते॥
en: Firmness, and mental sanctity, mercy, candour, prowess, and patience, are not in Sugriva.

sn: भ्रातुज्येष्ठस्य यो भार्यां जीवतो महिषीं प्रियाम्। धर्मेण मातरं यस्तु स्वीकरोति जुगुप्सितः॥ कथं स धर्मं जानीते येन भ्रात्रा दुरात्मना। युद्धायाभिनियुक्तेन बिलस्य पिहितं मुखम्॥
en: He that, while her son is living, appropriateth the beloved queen of his elder brother, mother to him by morality, is hated (of all beings). How can he that could cover up the mouth of the cave, when he had been desired by his brother gone on martial mission, to guard the same,—(how can he) know morality?

sn: सत्यात् पाणिगृहीतश्च कृतकर्मा महायशाः। विस्मृतो राघवो येन स कस्य सुकृतं स्मरेत्॥ लक्ष्मणस्य भयेनेह नाधर्मभयभीरुणा। आदिष्टा मार्गितुं सीता धर्मस्तस्मिन् कथं भवेत्॥
en: Whose good office remembereth he who could forget the renowned Räghava himself of mighty deeds, after having, in the name of truth, taken his hand? How can he reap religious merit that directed us to search Sītā here, from fear of Laksmana, and not from fear of unrighteousness?

sn: तस्मिन् पापे कृतघ्ने तु स्मृतिभिन्ने चलात्मनि। आर्यः को विश्वसेज्जातु तत्कुलीनो विशेषतः॥
en: What noble person, in especial, sprung in his race, shall any longer repose confidence in that impious one of unstable soul who has run amuck of morality?

sn: राज्ये पुत्रः प्रतिष्ठाप्य सगुणो निर्गुणोऽपि वा। कथं शत्रुकुलीनं मां सुग्रीवो जीवयिष्यति।।।।।
en: Meritorious or otherwise, how can Sugriva, having installed in the kingdom me, son (of his enemy) and the enemy sprung in his race, suffer me to live?

sn: भिन्नमन्त्रोऽपराद्धश्च भिन्नशक्तिः कथं ह्यहम्। किष्किन्धां प्राप्य जीवेयमनाथ इव दुर्बलः॥
en: How can I, whose counsels have been revealed, who have transgressed, and who have been deprived of my power, repairing to Kiş kindhā like one forlorn and feeble, live?

sn: उपांशुदण्डेन हि मां बन्धनेनोपपादयेत्। शठः क्रूरो नृशंसश्च सुग्रीवो राज्यकारणात्॥
en: For the sake of his kingdom, Sugrīva, wily, cunning and cruel, shall put me in solitary confinement.

sn: बन्धनाच्चावसादान्मे श्रेयः प्रायोपवेशनम्। अनुजानन्तु मां सर्वे गृहं गच्छन्तु वानराः॥
en: For me fasting to death is better than being confined-and suffering the consequent misery. Do you grant me your permission; and go to your homes, you monkeys.

sn: अहं वः प्रतिजानामि न गमिष्याम्यहं पुरीम् । इहैव प्रायमासिष्ये श्रेयो मरणमेव मे॥
en: I vow before you, to the palace I will never repair. At this very spot will I fast for death; as death is good for me.

sn: अभिवादनपूर्वं तु राजा कुशलमेव च। अभिवादनपूर्वं तु राघवौ बलशालिनौ॥ वाच्यस्तातो यवीयान् मे सुग्रीवो वानरेश्वरः। आरोग्यपूर्वं कुशलं वाच्या माता रुमा च मे॥
en: Bowing to the king as well as to the powerful Rāghava, you should communicate my wellbeing to Sugriva— lord of my health and peace to my mother Umā.

sn: मातरं चैव मे तासमाश्वासयितुमर्हथ। प्रकृत्या प्रियपुत्रा सा सानुक्रोशा तपस्विनी॥ विनष्टमिह मां श्रुत्वा व्यक्तं हास्यति जीवितम्। एतावदुक्त्वा वचनं वृद्धांस्तानभिवाद्य च॥ विवेश चाङ्गदो भूमौ रुदन् दर्भेषु दुर्मखः।
en: It behoves you also to console my mother, Tārā. Naturally fond of her son, and overflowing with tenderness, that lorn one, hearing of my apes-and death at this place, shall certainly renounce her life. Having said this, Angada, saluting the elders, with a woebegone face entered the earth covered with grass.

sn: तस्य संविशतस्तत्र रुदन्तो वानरर्षभाः॥ नयनेभ्यः प्रमुमुचुरुष्णं वै वारि दुःखिताः। सुग्रीवं चैव निन्दन्तः प्रशंसन्तश्च वालिनम्॥ परिवार्याङ्गदं सर्वे व्यवसन् प्रायमासितुम्।
en: When he had entered, those foremost monkeys, stricken with sorrow, weeping shed warm tears from their eyes. And censuring Sugrīva and praising Vāli, they, surrounding Angada, determined to starve themselves to death.

sn: तद् वाक्यं वालिपुत्रस्य विज्ञाय प्लवगर्षभाः॥ उपस्पृश्योदकं सर्वे प्राङ्मुखाः समुपाविशन्। दक्षिणाग्रेषु दर्भेषु उदक्तीरं समाश्रिताः॥ मुमूर्षवो हरिश्रेष्ठा एतत् क्षममिति स्म ह।
en: Taking to heart the speech of Väli's son, those prime monkeys, sipping water, sat down facing the East. And sitting on the edge of the water on grass pointing to the south, the foremost monkeys, wishing for surcease, thought within themselves,-Even this is fit for us.

sn: रामस्य वनवासं च क्षयं दशरथस्य च॥ जनस्थानवधं चैव वधं चैव जयायुषः। हरणं चैव वैदेह्या वालिनश्च वधं तथा। रामकोपं च वदतां हरीणां भयमागतम्॥
en: And as they spoke of the exile of Rāma and the demise of Daſaratha, the carnage in Janasthāna, the slaying of Jațāyu, the ravishment of Vaidehī, the slaughter of Vāli, and the ire of Rāma, the monkeys were seized with fear.

sn: स संविशद्भिर्बहुभिर्महीधरो महाद्रिकूटप्रतिमैः प्लवङ्गमैः। बभूव संनादितनिर्झरान्तरो भृशं नदद्भिर्जलदैरिवाम्बरम्॥
en: When those monkeys resembling mountainsummits had entered in, they set up cries, which, like to the rumbling of clouds, making the sky resound, made that mountain with its rills reverberate.

sn: उपविष्टास्तु ते सर्वे यस्मिन् प्रायं गिरिस्थले। हरयो गृध्रराजश्च तं देशमुपचक्रमे॥ सम्पातिर्नाम नाम्ना तु चिरजीवी विहंगमः। भ्राता जटायुषः श्रीमान् विख्यातबलपौरुषः॥
en: When the monkeys had been seated in that mountain, with the intention of putting a period to their existence through fasting a king of vultures happened to come to that quarter. And that long-lived bird was named Sampāti, the beautiful brother of Jaţāyu, famous for his strength and prowess.

sn: कन्दरादभिनिष्क्रम्य स विन्ध्यस्य महागिरेः। उपविष्टान् हरीन् दृष्ट्वा हृष्टात्मा गिरमब्रवीत्॥
en: Issuing from a cavern of the mighty mountain Vindhya, he, seeing the monkeys seated, well pleased, said.

sn: विधिः किल नरं लोके विधानेनानुवर्तते। यथायं विहितो भक्ष्यश्चिरान्मह्यमुपागतः॥ परम्पराणां भक्षिष्ये वानराणां मृतं मृतम्। उवाचैतद् वचः पक्षी तान् निरीक्ष्य प्लवङ्गमान्॥
en: Verily man reapeth the fruit of his former acts; and therefore it is that this food ordained to that end, comes to me after a long time. I shall feed on these monkeys, one by one, slaying them one after another. Eyeing those apes, the bird expressed himself thus.

sn: तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा भक्ष्यलुब्धस्य पक्षिणः। अङ्गदः परमायस्तो हनूमन्तमथाब्रवीत्॥
en: Hearing this speech of the bird coveting his food, Argada faintly spoke to Hanumān.

sn: पश्य सीतापदेशेन साक्षाद् वैवस्वतो यमः। इंग देशमनुप्राप्ते वानराणां विपत्तये॥
en: Behold! through Sita's simplicity* this onethe very son of the Sun, Yama-has come to this place, to exterminate the monkeys. *Another reading is Gridhra padesana— through the vultur's cunning. This the commentator consider as preferrable.

sn: रामस्य न कृतं कार्यं न कृतं राजशासनम्। हरीणामियमज्ञाता विपत्तिः सहसाऽऽगता॥
en: Rāma's work has not been done; nor the royal mandate. And this disaster has arrived unthought of by the monkeys.

sn: वैदेह्याः प्रियकामेन कृतं कर्म जटायुषा। गृध्रराजेन यत् तत्र श्रुतं वस्तदशेषतः॥
en: You have in detail heard all that, inspired with the desire of doing what is good to Vaidehi, that king of vultures, Jatayu, did here.

sn: तथा सर्वाणि भूतानि तिर्यग्योनिगतान्यपि। प्रियं कुर्वन्ति रामस्य त्यक्त्वा प्राणान्यथा वयम्॥
en: In this way, all creatures, even the brute species, compass the welfare of Rāma, renouncing their lives, as we do.

sn: अन्योन्यमुपकुर्वन्ति स्नेहकारुण्ययन्त्रिताः। ततस्तस्योपकारार्थं त्यजतात्मानमात्मना ॥
en: It is because of the love and tenderness* they bear towards (Rāma), that people do good to each other. *The commentator explains in pure orthodox fashion: Because every-thing is in Rama, people serve each other from the love and tenderness, which partain to him.

sn: प्रियं कृतं हि रामस्य धर्मज्ञेन जटायुषा। राघवार्थे परिश्रान्ता तयं संत्यक्तजीविताः॥ कान्ताराणि प्रपन्नाः स्म न च पश्याम मैथिलीम्।
en: Therefore the righteous Jațãyu, of his own accord laying down his life, has done the pleasure of Rāma. We also, overcome with fatigue and (almost) dying, have come to this forest; but Mithila's daughter we find not.

sn: स सुखी गृध्रराजस्तु रावणेन हतो रणे। मुक्तश्च सुग्रीवभयाद् गतश्च परमां गतिम्॥
en: Happy is that king of vultures, having been slain by Rāvaņa in battle. He has got quit of the fear of Sugrīva, and has also attained supreme state.

sn: जटायुषो विनाशेन राज्ञो दशरथस्य च। हरणेन च वैदेह्याः संशयं हरयो गताः॥
en: In consequence of the death of Jațāyu and that of king Dasaratha, as well as owing to the ravishment of Vaidehi, (the lives of) the monkeys have come into jeopardy.

sn: रामलक्ष्मणयोर्वासमरण्ये सह सीतया। राघवस्य च बाणेन वालिनश्च तथा वधः।। रामकोपादशेषाणां रक्षसां च तथा वधम्। कैकेय्या वरदानेन इदं च विकृतं कृतम्॥
en: Rama's and Laksmana's abode in the forest with Sītā, Rāghava's slaying of Vāli with a shaft, the slaughter of innumerable Räksasas by the enraged Rama, and (finally) this mishap-all these owe their origin to the bestowal of the boon on Kaikeyi.

sn: तदसुखमनुकीर्तितं वचो भुवि पतितांश्च निरीक्ष्य वानरान्। भृशचकितमतिर्महामतिः कृपणमुदाहृतवान् स गृध्रराजः॥
en: Seeing the monkeys stretched on the earth, and hearing their piteous words describing their grief, that magnanimous king of vultures, with his mind agitated said (this).

sn: तत् तु श्रुत्वा तथा वाक्यमङ्गदस्य मुखोद्गतम्। अब्रवीद् वचनं गृध्रस्तीक्ष्णतुण्डो महास्वनः॥
en: Hearing the words that issued from Angada's mouth, the sharp-beaked and high-toned vulture, said,

sn: कोऽयं गिरा घोषयति प्राणैः प्रियतरस्य मे। जटायुषो वधं भ्रातुः कम्पयन्निव मे मनः॥
en: Who is it that, making my mind tremble, speak of the death of my brother, Jațāyu, dearer to me than life.

sn: कथमासीञ्जनस्थाने युद्धं राक्षसगृध्रयोः। नामधेमिदं भ्रातुश्चिरस्याद्य मया श्रुतम्॥
en: How happened in Janasthāna the fight between the Rākṣasa and the vulture? It is after a long time that to-day I hear the name of my brother.

sn: इच्छेयं गिरिदुर्गाच्च भवद्भिरवतारितम्। यवीयसो गुणज्ञस्य श्लाघनीयस्य विक्रमैः॥ अतिदीर्घस्य कालस्य परितुष्योऽस्मि कीर्तनात्। तदिच्छेयमहं श्रोतुं विनाशं वानरर्षभाः॥ भ्रातुर्जटायुषस्तस्य जनस्थाननिवासिनः। तस्यैव च मम भ्रातुः सखा दशरथः कथम्॥ यस्य रामः प्रियः पुत्रो ज्येष्ठो गुरुजनप्रियः।
en: I wish to alight from this mountain-fastness. I have been well pleased by listening after a long time to the celebration of the virtues of my younger brother, cognizant of qualities and worthy of being extolled by reason of his prowess. You foremost of monkeys, I wish to hear of the destruction of Jaţāyu, who dwelt in Janasthāna. And how could Dasaratha, whose beloved eldest son is Rāma, dear to his superiors, be the friend of my brother?

sn: सूर्यांशुदाधपक्षत्वान्न शक्नोमि विसर्पितम्। इच्छेयं पर्वतादस्मादवतर्तुमरिंदमाः॥
en: I can not move in consequence of my wings having been burnt by the solar rays. But I wish that you may take me down from this mountain.

sn: शोकाद् भ्रष्टस्वरमपि श्रुत्वा वानरयूथपाः। श्रद्दधुनैव तद्वाक्यं कर्मणा तस्य शङ्किताः॥
en: Hearing his accents faltering through grief, the leaders of monkey-herds, alarmed by his action*, did not repose confidence in his speech. Karmaņā (instru.) by his action. The commentator explains: alarmed by his speech about eating up the monkeys. The passage is

sn: ते प्रायमुपविष्टास्तु दृष्ट्वा गृधं प्लवङ्गमाः।। चक्रुर्बुद्धिं तदा रौद्रां सर्वान् नो भक्षयिष्यति ॥
en: Seated for the purpose of fasting to death, the monkeys, seeing the vulture, with terror thought within themselves, he shall eat us all up.

sn: सर्वथा प्रायमासीनान् यदि नो भक्षयिष्यति। कृतकृत्या भविष्यामः क्षिप्रं सिद्धिमितो गताः॥
en: If he eat us up, who have sat down to fast to death, we shall secure success, and speedily attain our end.

sn: एतां बुद्धिं ततश्चकुः सर्वे ते हरियूथपाः। अवतार्य गिरेः शृङ्गाद् गृध्रमाहाङ्गदस्तदा॥
en: Then those monkey-chiefs resolved thus. And descending from the summit of the mountain, Angada spoke to the vulture,

sn: बभूवःरजो नाम वानरेन्द्रः प्रतापवान्। ममार्यः पार्थिवः पक्षिन् धार्मिकौ तस्य चात्मजौ॥ सुग्रीवश्चैव वाली च पुत्रौ घनबलाबुभौ। लोके विश्रुतकर्माभूद् राजा वाली पिता मम॥
en: There was a lord of monkeys named Riksaraja, endowed with prowess. That king, O bird, was my grandsire. He had two virtuous sons, exceedingly powerful both-Vāli and Sugriva. My father, Vali, was famed in the world for his deeds.

sn: राजा कृत्स्नस्य जगत इक्ष्वाकूणां महारथः। रामो दाशरथिः श्रीमान् प्रविष्टो दण्डकावनम्॥ लक्ष्मणेन. सह भ्रात्रा वैदेह्या सह भार्यया। पितुर्निदेशनिरतो धर्मं पन्थानमाश्रितः॥
en: It came to pass that mighty monarch of all this earth, descendant of the Ikṣwākus, the great and graceful car warrior, Rāma, son to Dasaratha, intent upon the injunction of his sire, resorting to the path of righteousness, entered the woods of Dandaka in company with his brother, Lakşmaņa and his wife Vaidehī.

sn: तस्य भार्या जनस्थानाद् रावणेन हृता बलात्। रामस्य तु पितुर्मित्रं जटायुर्नाम गृध्रराट्॥ ददर्श सीतां वैदेहीं ह्रियमाणां विहायसा। रावणं विरथं कृत्वा स्थापयित्वा च मैथिलीम्। परिश्रान्तश्च वृद्धश्च रावणेन हतो रणे॥
en: His spouse was forcibly carried away from Janasthāna. And the friend of Rāma's father, the king of vultures, named Jatayu, saw Videha's daughter, Sītā, as she was being carried away in the sky. And after having thrown down Rāvana from his car, and placed Maithili on the ground, (that vulture) old and overcome with fatigue was (at length) slain by Ravana in battle.

sn: एवं गृध्रो हतस्तेन रावणेन बलीयसा। संस्कृतश्चापि रामेण जगाम गतिमुत्तमाम्॥
en: Thus slain by the powerful Rāvana, the vulture, having had his funereal obsequies performed by Rama. (himself), has attained excellent state.

sn: ततो मम पितृव्येण सुग्रीवेण महात्मना। चकार राघवः सख्यं कोऽवधीत् पितरं मम ॥
en: Then Rāghava made friends with my uncle, the high-souled Sugrīva; and he also slew my sire.

sn: मम पित्रा निरुद्धो हि सुग्रीवः सचिवैः सह। निहत्य वालिनं रामस्ततस्तमभिषेचयत्॥
en: My father had debarred Sugrīva from the kingdom along with his counsellors; but Rāma, having slain Vāli, installed him (Sugrīva).

sn: स राज्ये स्थापितस्तेन सुग्रीवो वानरेश्वरः। राजा वानरमुख्यानां तेन प्रस्थापिता वयम्॥
en: And established in the monarchy by him (Rāma), Sugriva is (now) the master of the monkeys and king of all the foremost monkeys. By him have we been sent.

sn: एवं रामप्रयुक्तास्तु मार्गमाणास्ततस्ततः। वैदेहीं नाधिगच्छामो रात्रौ सूर्यप्रभामिव॥
en: Despatched hither by Rāma, we have searched for Sītā all round, but Vaidehī we have not found, as one does not find the solar splendour at night.

sn: ते वयं दण्डकारण्यं विचित्य सुसमाहिताः। अज्ञानात् तु प्रविष्टाः स्म धरण्या विवृतं बिलम्॥
en: It came to pass that, having heedfully explored the Dandaka forest, we through ignorance entered a cave lying open before.

sn: मयस्य मायाविहितं तद् बिलं च विचिन्वताम्। व्यतीतस्तत्र नो मासो यो राज्ञा समयः कृतः॥
en: That cave, you must know, was constructed by the illusive energy of Maya. And there we spent a month the term which had been fixed by the monarch.

sn: ते वयं कपिराजस्य सर्वे वचनकारिणः। कृतां संस्थामतिक्रान्ता भयात् प्रायमुपासिताः॥
en: Doing the behests of the king of monkeys, we, having overstayed the terms which had been appointed, have from fear sat here down for the purpose of fasting to death.

sn: क्रुद्धे तस्मिंस्तु काकुत्स्थे सुग्रीवे च सलक्ष्मणे। गतानामपि सर्वेषां तत्र नो नास्ति जीवितम्॥
en: On that Kākutstha being wrought up with wrath, as well as Sugrīva together with Lakş maņa, we, repairing thither, shall lose our lives.

sn: इत्युक्तः करुणं वाक्यं वानरैस्त्यक्तजीवितैः। सवाष्पो वानरान् गृध्रः प्रत्युवाच महास्वनः॥
en: When the monkeys, whose lives had well nigh departed out of them, had spoken these piteous words, the vulture, in solemn accents, with tears in his eyes, said to the monkeys,

sn: यवीयान् स मम भ्राता जटायुर्नाम वानराः। यमाख्यात हतं युद्ध रावणेन बलीयसा॥
en: You monkeys, you have said that my younger brother, named Jaţāyu, has been slain in battle by the powerful Rāvaņa.

sn: वृद्धभावादपक्षत्वाच्छृण्वंस्तदपि मर्षये। नहि मे शक्तिरस्त्यद्य भ्रातुर्वैरविमोक्षणे॥
en: On account of my age and want of wings, I, although hearing this, bear it. Nor have I strength to-day to clear scores touching my brother's enmity.

sn: पुरा वृत्रवधे वृत्ते स चाहं च जयैषिणौ। आदित्यमुपयातौ स्वो ज्वलन्तं रश्मिमालिनम्॥ आवृत्याकाशमार्गेण जवेन स्वर्गतौ भृशम्। मध्यं प्राप्ते तु सूर्ये तु जटायुरवसीदति ॥
en: Formerly, while engaged in the destruction of Vrtra, he and I, burning for victory, soared in the sky near the flaming sun, garlanded by glory. Thence impetuously wheeling round, we went to the celestial regions along the etherial way. And it came to pass that, coming midway of the sun, Jațāyu was faint.

sn: तमहं भ्रातरं दृष्ट्वा सूर्यरश्मिभिरतिम्। पक्षाभ्यां छादयामास स्नेहात् परमविह्वलम्॥
en: Witnessing my brother severely struck by the solar rays and exceedingly stupefied, I from affection shadowed him with my wings.

sn: निर्दग्धपत्रः पतितो विन्ध्येऽहं वानरर्षभाः। अहमस्मिन् वसन् भ्रातुः प्रवृत्तिं नोपलक्षये॥
en: Thereat, my pinions scathed, I dropped down on Vindhya, you foremost of monkeys; and staying here, I could not know the circumstances that have befallen my brother.

sn: जटायुषस्त्वेवमुक्तो भ्रात्रा सम्पातिना तदा। युवराजो महाप्रज्ञः प्रत्युवाचाङ्गदस्तदा॥
en: Thus addressed by Jatāyu's brother, Sampāti, the eminently wise prince Angada answered,

sn: जटायुषो यदि भ्राता श्रुतं ते गतिदं मया। आख्याहि यदि जानासि निलयं तस्य रक्षसः॥ अदीर्घदर्शिनं तं वै रावणं राक्षसाधमम्। अन्तिके यदि वा दूरे यदि जानासि शंस नः॥
en: 'If you are indeed the brother of Jațāyu, having heard what I have related, tell (us) if you know touching the abode of that Rākşasa. Tell us if you know anent that short-sighted worst of Raksasas, Ravana, whether staying far or near.

sn: ततोऽब्रवीन्महातेजा भ्राता ज्येष्ठो जटायुषः। आत्मानुरूपं वचनं वानरान् सम्प्रहर्षयन्॥
en: Thereat, rejoicing the monkeys, the exceedingly energetic elder brother of Jațāyu spoke words worthy of him.

sn: निर्दग्धपक्षो गृध्रोऽहं गतवीर्यः प्लवङ्गमाः। वाङ्मात्रेणापि रामस्य करिष्ये साह्यमुत्तम्॥
en: You monkeys, my pinions have been burnt; and I am a vulture shorn of strength. Therefore I will help Rāma well by my words.

sn: जानामि वारुणाँल्लोकान् विष्णोस्त्रैविक्रमानपि। देवासुरविमर्दाश्च ह्यमृतस्य विमन्थनम्॥
en: I know the realms of Varuna, and Visnu's Trivikrama* worlds, the wars of the gods and Asuras, and the churning for ambrosia. *i.e. the worlds enveloped by his three steps during his Dwarf incarnation.

sn: रामस्य यदिदं कार्यं कर्तव्यं प्रथमं मया। जरया च हृतं तेजः प्राणाश्च शिथिला मम॥
en: And albeit age has deprived me of energy, and albeit my life hangs loosely on me, yet, if this is Rāma's work, it should be done by me first.

sn: तरुणी रूपसम्पन्ना सर्वाभरणभूषिता। ह्रियमाणा मया दृष्टा रावणेन दुरात्मना॥
en: I have seen a youthful and beautiful female, adorned with all ornaments, carried away by the wicked Rāvana,

sn: क्रोशन्ती रामरामेति लक्ष्मणेति च भामिनी। भूषणान्यपविध्यन्ती गात्राणि च विधुन्वती॥
en: The lady (all the while) crying, 'O Rāma!' 'O Rāma!' '0 Lakşmaņa! And And taking her ornaments from her person, she was throwing them on the ground.

sn: सूर्यप्रभेव शैलाग्रे तस्याः कौशेयमुत्तमम्। असिते राक्षसे भाति यथा वा तडिदम्बुदे॥
en: Her silken cloth seemed like the solar splendour on the summit of a mountain; and herself beside the sable Rākşasa, looked like the lightning in the welkin (beside clouds).

sn: तां तु सीतामहं मन्ये रामस्य परिकीर्तनात्। श्रूयतां मे कथयतो निलयं तस्य रक्षसः॥
en: From your relation of Rāma, I conclude that she must be Sītā. Now listen to me as I tell you about the abode of that Rākşasa.

sn: पुत्रो विश्रवसः साक्षाद् भ्राता वैश्रवणस्य च। अध्यास्ते नगरी लङ्कां रावणो नाम राक्षसः॥
en: Son to Viśravana and brother to Vaiśravaņa, the Rākşasa named Rāvana resides in the city of Lankā.

sn: इतो द्वीपे समुद्रस्य सम्पूर्णे शतयोजने। तस्मिल्लङ्का पुरी रम्या निर्मिता विश्वकर्मणा॥ जाम्बूनदमयैद्वारैश्चित्रैः काञ्चनवेदिकैः। प्रासादैर्हेमवर्णैश्च महद्भिः सुसमाकृता॥ प्राकारेणार्कवर्णेन महता च समन्विता। तस्यां वसति वैदेही दीना कौशेयवासिनी॥ रावणान्तःपुरे रुद्धा राक्षसीभिः सुरक्षिता। जनकस्यात्मजां राज्ञस्तस्यां द्रक्ष्यथ मैथिलीम्॥
en: The lovely city of Lankā, reared by Viśvakarmā, lieth a full hundred Yojanas hence on an island in the sea; furnished with golden gateways, filled with variegated daises, lordly gold-gleaming places; and girt round with great walls hued like sunshine. There stayeth Vaidehi, forlorn and clad in a silken cloth,—-confined in the inner apartment of Rāvana, and carefully guarded by Rākṣasīs. In Lankā protected all round by the sea, you shall behold Janaka's daughter, Maithili.

sn: लङ्कायामथ गुप्तायां सागरेण समन्ततः। सम्प्राप्य सागरस्यान्तं सम्पूर्णं शतयोजनम्॥ आसाद्य दक्षिणं तीरं ततो द्रक्ष्यथ रावणम्। तत्रैव त्वरिताः क्षिप्रं विक्रमध्वं प्लवङ्गमाः॥
en: As the end of the ocean after a full hundred Yojanas, arriving at its southern shore, you shall see Rāvana in Laņkā, protected by ocean from all sides. You monkeys, do you hie thither speedily with vigour.

sn: ज्ञानेन खलु पश्यामि दृष्ट्वा प्रत्यागमिष्यथ। आद्यः पन्थाः कुलिङ्गानां ये चान्ये धान्यजीविनः।।२६।
en: I perceive by my knowledge that having seen (that place) you shall come back. The first course belongs to forktailed shrikes and others living on grain.

sn: द्वितीयो बलिभोजानां ये च वृक्षफलाशनाः। भासास्तृतीयं गच्छन्ति क्रौञ्चाश्च कुररैः सह ॥ श्येनाश्चतुर्थं गच्छन्ति गृध्रा गच्छन्ति पञ्चमम्। बलवीर्योपपन्नानां रूपयौवनशालिनाम्॥ षष्ठस्तु पन्था हंसानां वैनतेयगतिः परा। वैनतेयाच्च नो जन्म सर्वेषां वानरर्षभाः॥
en: The second, to those that live on animals and fruits; the third is ranged by Bhāşas; the fourth by Krunchas, Kuvaras and hawks; the fifth by vultures; the sixth belongs to swans endowed with youth and beauty; and the next to the Vainateyas. We have derived or origin from Vainateya. *Aruna, son to Vinata.

sn: गर्हितं तु कृतं कर्म येन स्म पिशिताशिनः। प्रतिकार्य च मे तस्य वैरं भ्रातृकृतं भवेत्॥
en: (By despatching you thither), I shall avenge the heinous deed perpetrated by the cannibal, as well as the wrong done by Rāvana to my brother.

sn: इहस्थोऽहं प्रपश्यामि रावणं जानकी तथा। अस्माकमपि सौपर्णं दिव्यं चक्षुर्बलं तथा॥
en: Resting here, I see Ravana and Janaki. We have excellent Sauparana' clairvoyance. *Clairvoyance attained by success in knowledge respecting the spiritual Golden eyes. Thus far the commentator. We leave the abstruse point to the apostles of theosophy and spiritism for illucidation.

sn: तस्मादाहारवीर्येण निसर्गेण च वानराः। आयोजनशताद् साग्राद् वयं पश्याम नित्यशः॥
en: For this reason, as well as owing to the energy consequent on our feeding on certain kinds of flesh, we, you monkeys, can see a little further than an hundred Yojanas.

sn: अस्माकं विहिता वृत्तिनिसर्गेण च दूरतः। विहिता वृक्षमूले तु वृत्तिश्चरणयोधिनाम्॥
en: Therefore (the Deity) has ordained such food for us as are fraught with the power of making one see from a great distance. And the abode of cocks and others being underneath trees, their sight is limited to the extent which they require to see.

sn: उपायो दृश्यतां कश्चिल्लङ्घने लवणाम्भसः। अभिगम्य तु वैदेही समृद्धार्था गमिष्यथ ॥ समुद्रं नेतुमिच्छामि भवद्भिर्वरुणालयम्। प्रदास्याम्युदकं भ्रातुः स्वर्गतस्य महात्मनः॥
en: Do you look about for means to cross over the salt waters. Having met with Vaidehi, do you, having achieved success, come back. I wish to be taken by you to the ocean-abode of Varuna. I will offer water to (the manes of) my highsouled brother, who has gone to heaven.

sn: ततो नीत्वा तु तं देशं तीरे नदनदीपतेः। निर्दग्धपक्षं सम्पातिं वानराः सुमहौजसः॥ तं पुनः प्रापयित्वा च तं देशं पतगेश्वरम्। बभूवुर्वानरा हृष्टाः प्रवृत्तिमुपलभ्य ते॥
en: Thereat those heroes, the monkeys possessed of exceeding energy, carried to the destined spot on the shore of the ocean, Sampāti, whose wings had been scathed. Then carrying that lord of vultures back to the self-same place, the monkeys, furnished with information (concerning Sītā), experienced great joy.

sn: ततस्तदमृतास्वादं गृध्रराजेन भाषितम्। निशम्य वदता हृष्टास्ते वचः प्लवगर्षभाः॥
en: Then hearing that ambrosial speech of the vulture-king, the monkey-chiefs, being delighted, kept on parleying (on that topic).

sn: जाम्बवान् वानरश्रेष्ठः सह सर्वैः प्लवङ्गमैः। भूतलात् सहसोत्थाय गृध्रराजानमब्रवीत्॥
en: Then Jāmbavān-foremost of monkeystogether with all the monkeys, arising suddenly from the ground, spoke to the vulture-king, saying,

sn: क्व सीता केन वा दृष्टा को वा हरति मैथिलीम्। तदाख्यातुं भवान् सर्वं गतिर्भव वनौकसाम्॥
en: Where is Sītā? By whom has she been seen? And who has carried away Mithila's daughter? Do you tell us all about this, and (thus) prove the path of these rangers of the woods.

sn: को दाशरथिबाणानां वज्रवेगनिपातिनाम्। स्वयंलक्ष्मणमुक्तानां न चिन्तयति विक्रमम्॥
en: Who is there that does not take heed of the force of Dasarathi's* and Laksmana's arrows, speeding with the vehemence of thunder? *Lit. Dasaratha's son. The term is applied in especial to Rāma.

sn: स हरीन् प्रतिसम्मुक्तान् सीताश्रुतिसमाहितान्। पुनराश्वासयन् प्रीत इदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Thereat, cheering up those monkeys, who had risen from their attitudes of fasting, and who were all attention to hear news concerning Sītā, he (Sampāti), well pleased, said these words,

sn: श्रूयतामिह वैदेह्या यथा मे हरणं श्रुतम्। येन चापि ममाख्यातं यत्र चायतलोचना ॥
en: Listen as to how I came to know of the ravishment of Vaidehī, Sītā, at this place; and who it was that told me where that one of expansive eyes is.

sn: अहमस्मिन् गिरौ दुर्गे बहुयोजनमायते। चिरान्निपतितो वृद्धः क्षीणप्राणपराक्रमः॥ तं मामेवङ्गतं पुत्रः सुपार्यो नाम नामतः। आहारेण यथाकालं विभर्ति पततां वरः॥
en: For a long time I lay here, old, and of feeble life and energy. that best of birds, my son named Supārswa, coming to me, at the proper hour maintained me with food.

sn: तीक्ष्णकामास्तु गन्धर्वास्तीक्ष्णकोपा भुजङ्गमाः। मृगाणां तु भयं तीक्ष्णं ततस्तीक्ष्णक्षुधा वयम्॥
en: Gandharvas exceedingly lascivious; serpents are exceedingly wrathful; fear is excessive in deer; and we have excessive hunger.

sn: स कदाचित् क्षुधार्तस्य ममाहाराभिकाङ्क्षिणः। गतसूर्येऽहनि प्राप्तो मम पुत्रो ह्यनामिषः॥
en: Once on a time my son, going forth about sunrise to procure food for me who was suffering from hunger and (accordingly) eager for it, came back in the evening without any flesh. are

sn: स मयाऽऽहारसंरोधात् पीडितः प्रीतिवर्धनः। अनुमान्य यथातत्वमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Hurt (by my speech uttered) in consequence of my non-receipt of food, that enhancer of my joy, asking my forgiveness, said these words fraught with fact,

sn: अहं तात यथाकालमामिषार्थी खमाप्लुतः। महेन्द्रस्य गिरेरमावृत्य सुसमाश्रितः॥
en: 'Father, taking to my wings at the proper time for procuring flesh, I (went) and stood, obstructing the pass of the Mahendra mountain.

sn: तत्र सत्त्वसहस्राणां सागरान्तरचारिणाम्। पन्थानमेकोऽध्यवसं संनिरोद्धमवाङ्मुखः॥
en: There stood I looking down, obstructing the way of thousands of creatures ranging the sea.

sn: तत्र कश्चिन्मया दृष्टः सूर्योदयसमप्रभाम्। स्त्रियमादाय गच्छन् वै भिन्नाञ्जनचयोपमः॥
en: There I saw somebody resembling a mass of crushed collyrium, going away, taking a female resembling the rising sun in splendour.

sn: सोऽहमभ्यवहारार्थं तौ दृष्ट्वा कृतनिश्चयः। तेन साम्ना विनीतेन पन्थानमनुयाचितः॥
en: Seeing them I had made up my mind that they should serve for your fare, when he humbly in a pacific manner begged for way.

sn: नहि सामोपपन्नानां प्रहर्ता विद्यते भुवि।' नीचेष्वपि जनः कश्चित् किमङ्ग बत मद्विधः॥
en: Even among the mean, there is none on earth that can slay people who assume a mild attitude. What shall I say, alas! of superior ones like myself?

sn: स यातस्तेजसा व्योम संक्षिपन्निव वेगितः। अथाहं खेचरैर्भूतैरभिगम्य सभाजितः॥
en: And summoning celerity, he went on as if pushing off the sky by his energy. Then the rangers of the air and other beings worshipped me.

sn: दिष्ट्या जीवति सीतेति ह्यब्रुवन् मां महर्षयः। कथंचित् सकलत्रोऽसौ गतस्ते स्वस्त्यसंशयम्॥
en: And the Maharsis said to me,-By luck it is that Sītā is still living' — he together with a female, having passed by you, certainly augurs good fortune to you. 1. The commentator supplies the elipsis thus,-Coming within your ken by fuck, Sītā is living. 2. The passage is obscure. The commentator has glossed over this sloka, and the meaning is lone the clear for his explanation.

sn: एवमुक्तस्ततोऽहं तैः सिद्धैः परमशोभनैः। स च मे रावणो राजा रक्षसां प्रतिवेदितः॥
en: Then those eminently handsome Siddhas spoke thus to me.-This is Ravana, the king of the Rākşasas, said they to me.

sn: पश्यन् दाशरथेर्भार्यां रामस्य जनकात्मजाम्। भ्रष्टाभरणकौशेयां शोकवेगपराजिताम्॥ रामलक्ष्मणयोर्नाम क्रोशन्ती मुक्तमूर्धजाम्। एष कालात्ययस्तात इति वाक्यविदां वरः॥ एतदर्थं समग्रं मे सुपार्श्वः प्रत्यवेदयत्। तच्छ्रुत्वापि हि मे बुद्धिर्नासीत् काचित् पराक्रमे॥
en: I (stood), beholding the wife of Rama, son to Dasaratha,—throwing off her ornaments and silken apparel, overwhelmed by might of sorrow, with hair dishevelled crying out the names of Rāma and Lakşmaņa. This O father, is the reason of my passing the time.' That best of those skilled in speech, Suparswa, said all this to me. Even hearing of this, I could not think of putting forth prowess.

sn: अपक्षो हि कथं पक्षी कर्म किंचित् समारभेत्। यत् तु शक्यं मया कर्तुं वाग्बुद्धिगुणवर्तिना॥ श्रूयतां तत्र वक्ष्यामि भवतां पौरुषाश्रयम्।
en: How can a bird bereft of wings, undertake any thing? But listen! I will tell you as to what I am capable of through speech, intellect and merit, and what you can exèrt your manliness in.

sn: वाङ्मतिभ्यां हि सर्वेषां करिष्यामि प्रियं हि वः॥ यद्धि दाशरथेः कार्यं मम तन्नात्र संशयः।
en: I will do what is agreeable to you by my words and my and my intention. That which is Dasarathi's work is also mine. Of this there is no doubt.

sn: तद् भवन्तो मतिश्रेष्ठा बलवन्तो मनस्विनः॥ प्रहिताः कपिराजेन देवैरपि दुरासदाः।
en: You, foremost in intelligence, strong, intellectual, and incapable of being overcome by the gods themselves, have been despatched by the monarch of monkeys.

sn: रामलक्ष्मणबाणाश्च विहिताः कङ्कपत्रिणः॥ त्रयाणामपि लोकानां पर्याप्तास्त्राणनिग्रहे।
en: Rama's and Laksmana's shafts furnished with the feathers of the Kanka, are competent to afflict or save the three worlds.

sn: कामं खलु दशग्रीवस्तेजोबलसमन्वितः। भवतां तु समर्थानां न किंचिदपि दुष्करम्॥
en: And although the Ten-necked one is endowed with strength and energy, yet to you who are competent, nothing is hard to accomplish.

sn: तदलं कालसङ्गेन क्रियतां बुद्धिनिश्चयः। नहि कर्मसु सज्जन्ते बुद्धिमन्तो भवद्विधाः॥
en: There is no need of delay. Make up 'yo minds. Persons like you do not give way to laziness in enterprise.

sn: ततः कृतोदकं स्नातं तं गृधं हरियूथपाः। उपविष्टा गिरौ रम्ये परिवार्य समन्ततः॥
en: When the vulture had offered oblations of water to the manes of his deceased brother and finished his ablutions, the monkey-chiefs sat down in that charming mountain, surrounding him.

sn: तमङ्गदमुपासीनं तैः सर्वैर्हरिभिर्वृतम्। जनितप्रत्ययो हर्षात् सम्पातिः पुनरब्रवीत्॥
en: And inspired with confidence in the words of the Nisakara), Sampati, from delight, said to Angada, who was seated, surrounded by all the monkeys.'

sn: कृत्वा. निःशब्दमेकाग्राः शृण्वन्तु हरयो मम। तथ्यं संकीर्तयिष्यामि यथा जानामि मैथिलीम्॥
en: Remaining silent, do you, you monkeys, heedfully hear what I say. I will tell you truly how I came to know Maithili.

sn: अस्य विन्ध्यस्य शिखरे पतितोऽस्मि पुरानघ। सूर्यतापपरीताङ्गो निर्दग्धः सूर्यरश्मिभिः॥
en: My body being affected by solar heat, and my wings burnt by the rays of the sun, O sinless one, I formerly fell to this summit of Vindhya.

sn: लब्धसंज्ञस्तु षड्रावाद् विवशो विह्वलनिव। वीक्षमाणो दिशः सर्वा नाभिजानामि किंचन॥
en: On regaining my senses after six nights, during which I was insensible, I looked around in bewilderment, but could not recognise anything whatever.

sn: ततस्तु सागराशैलान् नदीः सर्वाः सरांसि च। वनानि च प्रदेशांश्च निरीक्ष्य मतिरागता॥
en: Then closely viewing oceans and mountains, rivers and tanks, and woods and countries, my thoughts came back to me.

sn: हृष्टपक्षिगणाकीर्णः कन्दरोदरकूटवान्। दक्षिणस्योदधेस्तीरे विन्ध्योऽयमिति निश्चितः॥
en: Seeing this place abounding in cheerful birds, containing woods and crested with summits, I for certain concluded it to be Vindhya on the shores of the Southern sea.

sn: आसीच्चात्राश्रमं पुण्यं सुरैरपि सुपूजितम्। ऋषिर्निशाकरो नाम यस्मिन्नुग्रतपाऽभवत्॥
en: And here lay a sacred asylum, honoured even by the celestials, and here dwelt a saint named Niśākara, of fierce austerities.

sn: अष्टौ वर्षसहस्राणि तेनास्मिन्नृषिणा गिरौ। वसतो मम धर्मज्ञे स्वर्गते तु निशाकरे॥
en: After Niśākara cognizant of virtue had gone to heaven, I bereft of that saint, passed eight thousand years in this mountain.

sn: अवतीर्य च विन्ध्याग्रात् कृच्छ्रेण विषमाच्छनैः। तीक्ष्णदर्भा वसुमती दुःखेन पुनरागतः॥
en: Descending with difficulty from the uneven top of Vindhya, I again came* to the earth covered with sharp-pointed grass. *While the saint was staying here.

sn: तमृषिं द्रष्टुकामोऽस्मि दुःखेनाभ्यागतो भृशम्। जटायुषा मया चैव बहुशोऽधिगतो हि सः॥
en: I was eager to see the saint; and (therefore), with much ado I came to him; and Jatāyu and myself saw that saint many a time and oft.

sn: तस्याश्रमपदाभ्याशे ववुर्वाताः सुगन्धिनः। वृक्षो नापुष्पितः कश्चिदफलो वा न दृश्यते॥
en: A fragrant breeze blew about the hermitage; and no tree was found that did not bear flowers and fruits.

sn: उपेत्य चाश्रमं पुण्यं वृक्षमूलमुपाश्रितः। द्रष्टकामः प्रतीक्षे च भगवन्तं निशाकरम्॥
en: Approaching the holy asylum, I, desirous of beholding the worshipful Niśākara, waited at the foot of a tree.

sn: अथ पश्यामि दूरस्थमृषि ज्वलिततेजसम्। कृताभिषेकं दुर्धर्षमुपावृत्तमुदङ्मुखम्॥
en: Then at a distance I saw the saint, flaming in energy and irrepressible,-returning northwards.

sn: तमृक्षाः सृमराव्याघ्राः सिंहा नानासरीसृपाः। परिवार्योपगच्छन्ति दातारं प्राणिनो यथा॥
en: As creatures gather round a giver, bears and Srimaras, tigers lions, and various reptiles, were going along, surrounding him.

sn: ततः प्राप्तमृषि ज्ञात्वा तानि सत्त्वानि वै ययुः। प्रविष्टे राजनि यथा सर्वं सामात्यकं बलम्॥
en: And knowing that the saint had arrived (at his home), the animals went away, as go away forces together with counsellors, when the sovereign has entered (his palace).

sn: ऋषिस्तु दृष्ट्वा मां तुष्टः प्रविष्टश्चाश्रमं पुनः। मुहूर्तमात्रानिर्गम्य ततः कार्यमपृच्छत॥
en: The saint was glad on seeing me. Then reentering his asylum for a short space, he came out and enquired for my mission.

sn: सौम्य वैकल्यतां दृष्ट्वा रोम्णां ते नावगम्यते। अग्निदग्धाविमौ पक्षौ प्राणाश्चापि शरीरके॥
en: O mild one, in consequence of your feathers having undergone alteration, I cannot recognise you. Your two wings have been blasted by fire; and your powers in your frail frame are in the same condition).

sn: गृध्रौ द्वौ दृष्टपूर्वी मे मातरिश्वसमौ जवे। गृध्राणां चैव राजानौ भ्रातरौ कामरूपिणौ॥
en: After time I saw two vultures like to wind in speed,-kings of vultures, brothers, wearing shapes at will.

sn: ज्येष्ठोऽवितस्त्वं सम्पाते जटायुरनुजस्तव। मानुषं रूपमास्थाय गृह्णीतां चरणौ मम॥
en: You are I know, elder, O Sampati; and Jatayu is younger to you. Assuming human forms, you had taken hold of my feet.

sn: किं ते व्याधिसमुत्थानं पक्षयोः पतनं कथम्। दण्डो वायं धृतः केन सर्वमाख्याहि पृच्छतः॥
en: Now, what ailment has attacked you? And why have your plumes fallen off? And who has dealt this punishment to you? Do you tell all this to me, who am asking you.

sn: ततस्तद् दारुणं कर्म दुष्करं सहसा कृतम्। आचचक्षे मुनेः सर्वं सूर्यानुगमनं तथा॥
en: Thereat Sampāti related to the ascetic all about his fearful, arduous, and rash act of following up the sun.

sn: भगवन् व्रणयुक्तत्वाल्लज्जया चाकुलेन्द्रियः। परिश्रान्तो न शक्नोमि वचनं परिभाषितुम्॥
en: O reverend sire, in consequence of my body suffering from sores, I, my senses bewildered from shame, and myself fatigued, cannot utter words.

sn: अहं चैव जटायुश्च संघर्षाद् गर्वमोहितौ। आकाशं पतितौ दूराज्जिज्ञासन्तौ पराक्रमम्॥ कैलासशिखरे बद्ध्वा मुनीनामग्रतः पणम्। रविः स्यादनुयातव्यो यावदस्तं महागिरिम्॥
en: From pride for power of flight, I and Jatayu, being intoxicated by conceit, began to voyage the sky afar off, with the view of testing each other's prowess, binding ourselves by the vow that we would follow the Sun so long as he did not enter that mighty Setting mountain,-and appear before the ascetics on the summit of Kailāsa.

sn: अप्यावां युगपत् प्राप्तावपश्याव महीतले। रथचक्रप्रमाणानि नगराणि पृथक् पृथक् ॥ क्वचिद् वादित्रघोषश्च क्वचिद् भूषणनिःस्वनः। गायन्ती: स्माङ्गना बह्वीः पश्यावो रक्तवाससः॥
en: And simultaneously plunging into the serial deep) we saw on the earth beneath separate cities resembling car-wheels; and here the sound of musical instruments, and there the tinklings of ornaments. And (at places) we beheld many a damsel clad in red attire, engaged in singing.

sn: तूर्णमुत्पत्य चाकाशमादित्यपतमास्थितौ। आवामालोकयावस्तद् वनं शाद्वलसंस्थितम्॥
en: And swiftly darting up into the sky and approaching the path of the Sun, we saw a wood interspersed with swards.

sn: उपलैरिव संछन्ना दृश्यते भूः शिलोच्चयैः। आपगाभिश्च संवीता सूत्रैरिव वसुंधरा॥
en: We saw the earth covered with crags and masses of rocks, and intersected by streams resembling threads.

sn: हिमवांश्चैव विन्ध्यश्च मेरुश्च सुमहागिरिः। भूतले सम्प्रकाशन्ते नागा इव जलाशये॥ तीव्रः स्वेदश्च खेदश्च भयं चासीत् तदावयोः। समाविशत मोहश्च ततो मूर्छा च दारुणा॥
en: Himavān, and Vindhya, and that mighty mountain, Meru, appeared on the earth like elephants in a tank. Then we began to sweat, and to be filled with regret; and fear seized us both. And we became bewildered; and fainted away frightfully.* *Consequent on Jațāyu having dropped down.

sn: न च दिग्ज्ञायते याम्या न चाग्नेयी न वारुणी। युगान्ते नियतो लोको हतो दग्ध इवाग्निना ॥
en: We knew not the south, or the west, or the quarter presided over by Fire;' and the world that was still burning at the end of a Yuga, appeared (to us) as if it had been consumed quite.? 1. South-east. 2. The passage is obscure. This is however, all the explanation that the commentator has to give.

sn: मनश्च मे हतं भूयश्चक्षुः प्राप्य तु संश्रयम्। यत्नेन महता ह्यस्मिन् मनः संधाय चक्षुषी॥ यत्नेन महता भूयो भास्करः प्रतिलोकितः। तुल्यपृथ्वीप्रमाणेन भास्करः प्रतिभाति नौ॥
en: My mind, combined with my eyes waxed feebler. And then fixing with might and main my eyes as well as my mind (on the sun), I could by a violent exercise of my energy behold the sun. And the sun shining, appeared to us like the earth in extent.

sn: जटायुर्मामनापृच्छ्य निपपात महीं ततः। तं दृष्ट्वा तूर्णमाकाशादात्मानं मुक्तवानहम्॥ पक्षाभ्यां च मया गुप्तो जटायुर्न प्रदह्यत। प्रमादात् तत्र निर्दग्धः पतन् वायुपथादहम्॥ आशङ्के तं निपतितं जनस्थाने जटायुषम्। अहं तु पतितो विन्ध्ये दग्धपक्षो जडीकृतः॥
en: Then, without asking me Jațāyu dropped to the earth. Seeing him, I at once descended form the sky and Jațāyu and not burnt in consequence of having been shielded by my wings. And scathed through the agitation* I fell through the serial way. I guessed that Jațāyu fell in Janasthāna. And I myself, my wings blasted, and rendered inert, fell on Vindhya. *Rāmanuya comments: the confusion seized them as the sun was midway. They lost all ense of direction. The faint succeeded.

sn: राज्याच्च हीनो भ्रात्रा च पक्षाभ्यां विक्रमेण च। सर्वथा मर्तुमेवेच्छन् पतिष्ये शिखराद् गिरेः॥
en: Deprived of my kingdom, and my brother, and my wings, and my prowess, I wishing to put a period to my existence, will hurl myself headlong from this summit of the mountain.

sn: एवमुक्त्वा मुनिश्रेष्ठमरुतं भृशदुःखितः। अथ ध्यात्वा मुहूर्तं च भगवानिदमब्रवीत्॥
en: Having said this to that foremost of ascetics, I smitten with grief, began to weep. Thereat, after, reflecting for a while, that reverend one said,

sn: पक्षौ च ते प्रपक्षौ च पुनरन्यौ भविष्यतः। चक्षुषी चैव प्राणाश्च विक्रमश्च बलं च ते॥
en: Your wings together with two smaller ones shall grow again; as also your sight, energy, prowess and strength.

sn: पुराणे सुमहत्कार्यं भविष्यं हि मया श्रुतम्। दृष्टं मे तपसा चैव श्रुत्वा च विदितं मम ॥
en: Having heard of it, and also seen it through ascetic power, I know that a great deed is going to take place.

sn: राजा दशरथो नाम कश्चिदिक्ष्वाकुवर्धनः। तस्य पुत्रो महातेजा रामो नाम भविष्यति ॥
en: There shall be a king named Daſaratha, increaser of the Ikşwāku race. He shall have a son, named Rāma, endowed with exceeding energy.

sn: अरण्यं च सह भ्रात्रा लक्ष्मणेन गमिष्यति। तस्मिन्नर्थे नियुक्तः सन् पित्रा सत्यपराक्रमः॥
en: He (Rāma) shall repair to the forest in company with his brother, Laksmana; that one having truth for prowess, having commissioned to that effect by his sire.

sn: नैर्ऋतो रावणो नाम तस्य भार्या हरिष्यति। राक्षसेन्द्रो जनस्थाने अवध्यः सुरदानवैः॥
en: A friend named Rāvana, the lord of Rākşasas, incapable of being slain by either the gods or the Dāvanas, shall carry off his Rāma's) spouse in Janasthāna.

sn: सा च कामैः प्रलोभ्यन्ती भक्ष्यैर्भोज्यैश्च मैथिली। न भोक्ष्यति महाभागा दुःखमग्ना यशस्विनी॥
en: And albeit tempted by viands and objects of enjoyment and desire, the famous and highly virtuous one, plunged in grief, shall not pertake of those things.

sn: परमान्नं च वैदेह्या ज्ञात्वा दास्यति वासवः। यदन्नममृतप्रख्यं सुराणामपि दुर्लभम्।।८
en: And knowing that Videha's daughter (has been fasting for many a day), Vāsava shall offer Vaidehī pāyasa like to ambrosia, difficult of being procured even by the gods.

sn: तदन्नं मैथिली प्राप्य विज्ञायेन्द्रादिदं त्विति। अग्रमुद्धृत्य रामाय भूतले निर्वपिष्यति॥
en: Receiving that food, Maithili, knowing that it has come from Indra,* took up a little of it from the surface, and dropped it to the earth for Rāma. *From the fact of the food not touching the earth, and other signs. It is humorous to read the explanation of the commentator as to the reason of Indra's supplying Sītā with food. If Sītā remained fasting, Rāvana would forego his attachment for Vaidehi, on seeing her altered appearance; and thus his destruction could not take place. Further, if he saw Sītā retaining her former loveliness, he could conclude that Sītā, as also Rāma, were superhuman character, and that as such they could not be agents for his destruction according to the prophecy Rāvana shall be slain by a human being. This inducing him to persist in his bellicose attitude towards Rāma, would being down ruin upon his head.

sn: यदि जीवति मे भर्ता लक्ष्मणो वापि देवरः। देवत्वं गच्छतोर्वापि तयोरन्नमिदं त्विति ॥
en: Whether my husband as well as his younger brother live, or they have attained godhead, let this food serve for them.

sn: एष्यन्ति प्रेषितास्तत्र रामदूताः प्लवङ्गमाः। आख्येया राममहिषी त्वया तेभ्यो विहङ्गम॥
en: Rāma's envoys, having been despatched thither.* shall come hither. You should relate to them all the facts connected with the queen of Rāma. *For going to Lankā.

sn: सर्वथा तु न गन्तव्यमीदृशः क्व गमिष्यसि। देशकालौ प्रतीक्षस्व पक्षौ त्वं प्रतिपत्स्यसे॥
en: Do not by any means go hence; and in this case, whither, again, wilt you repair? Do you stay here for season and place. You shall regain your wings.

sn: उत्सहेयमहं कर्तुमद्यैव त्वां सपक्षकम्। इहस्थस्त्वं हि लोकानां हितं कार्यं करिष्यसि॥
en: I could this very day furnish you with wings. But, by staying here in this condition, you wilt be able to compass the welfare of the worlds.

sn: त्वयापि खलु तत् कार्यं तयोश्च नृपपुत्रयोः। ब्राह्मणानां गुरूणां च मुनीनां वासवस्य च॥
en: Even you shall do that act in behalf of those sons of the king, of the Brāhmanas, of the spiritual preceptors, of the ascetics, and of Vasava.

sn: इच्छाम्यहमपि द्रष्टुं भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ। नेच्छे चिरं धारयितुं प्राणांस्त्यक्ष्ये कलेवरम्। महर्षिस्त्वब्रवीदेवं दृष्टतत्त्वार्थदर्शनः॥
en: I also am desirous of beholding the brothers, Rāma and Laksmana. I do not wish to hold this life long. I would renounce my life.' That Maharși, conversant with the nature of things, told me this.'

sn: एतैरन्यैश्च बहुभिर्वाक्यैर्वाक्यविशारदः। मां प्रशस्याभ्यनुज्ञाप्य प्रविष्टः स स्वमालयम्॥
en: Having praised me with these and many other words, and bidden me adieu that one skilled in speech, entered his own habitation.

sn: कन्दरात् तु विसर्पित्वा पर्वतस्य शनैः शनैः। अहं विन्ध्यं समारुह्य भवतः प्रतिपालये॥
en: Issuing out gently from the cave of that mountain, I, ascending Vindhya, was expecting you.

sn: अद्य त्वेतस्य कालस्य वर्षे साग्रशतं गतम्। देशकालप्रतीक्षोऽस्मि हृदि कृत्वा मुनेर्वचः॥
en: The space covered by the time intervening between then and to-day is a little over an hundred years;* and laying up in my heart the speech of that ascetic I have been awaiting season and place. *The commentator says the period is one hundred and eight years.

sn: महाप्रस्थानमासाद्य स्वर्गते तु निशाकरे।-मां निर्दहति संतापो वितर्कंबहुभिर्वृतम्॥
en: Setting out on his great journey, on Niśākara having gone to heaven, I distracted with various thoughts, have been consumed by grief. For the loss of my plumage.-

sn: उदितां मरणे बुद्धिं मुनिवाक्यैर्निवर्तये। बुद्धिर्या तेन मे दत्ता प्राणानां रक्षणे मम॥ सा मेऽपनयते दुःखं दीप्तेवाग्निशिखा तमः।
en: My rising intention of doing away with myself I have suppressed in consideration of the words of the ascetic. The reason which he had imparted to me for preserving my life, has removed my pains even as a flaming fire (dispels darkness).

sn: बुध्यता च मया वीर्यं रावणस्य दुरात्मनः॥ पुत्रः संतर्जितो वाग्भिर्न त्राता मैथिली कथम्।
en: And knowing the prowess of the impious Rāvana, I said in rage to my son, versed in speech,-'Hearing her lamentation, and knowing them bereft of Sītā, why didst you not deliver her?'

sn: तस्या विलपितं श्रुत्वा तौ च सीतावियोजितौ॥ न मे दशरथस्नेहात् पुत्रेणोत्पादितं प्रियम्।
en: My son did not do this good office to Daſaratha, influenced by affection for him.

sn: तस्य त्वेवं ब्रुवाणस्य संहतैर्वानरैः सह ॥ उत्पेततुस्तदा पक्षौ समक्षं वनचारिणाम्।
en: As he was speaking thus in the midst of the monkeys, his wings sprang up in presence of the rangers of the forest.

sn: स दृष्ट्वा स्वां तनुं पक्षरुद्तैररुणच्छदैः॥ प्रहर्षमतुलं लेभे वानरांश्चेदमब्रवीत्।
en: Thereupon, seeing his person furnished with grown pinions hued like the infant sun, he experienced incomparable raptures, and addressed the monkeys, saying,

sn: निशाकरस्य राजर्षेः प्रसादादमितौजसः॥ आदित्यरश्मिनिर्दग्धौ पक्षौ पुनरुपस्थितौ।
en: By the grace of that Rājarși of immeasurable energy, my wings, which had been burnt up by the rays of the sun, have grown again.

sn: यौवने वर्तमानस्य ममासीद् यः पराक्रमः॥ तमेवाद्यावगच्छामि बलं पौरुषमेव च।
en: To-day I have got back) the strength and prowess which I possessed while my youth was yet present.

sn: सर्वथा क्रियतां यत्नः सीतामधिगमिष्यथ ॥ पक्षलाभो ममायं वः सिद्धिप्रत्ययकारकः।
en: Do you strive every way. You shall meet with Sītā. And my getting (back) my wings inspires (us) with confidence as to success.

sn: इत्युक्त्वा तान्हरीन् सर्वान्सम्पाति: पतगोत्तमः॥ उत्पपात गिरेः शृङ्गाजिज्ञासुः खगमो गतिम्।
en: Having said this to all the monkeys, that ranger of the sky and best of birds. Sampāti, anxious to ascertain his power of flight, flew up from the mountain summits.

sn: तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा प्रतिसंहृष्टमानसाः। बभूवुर्हरिशार्दूला विक्रमाभ्युदयोन्मुखाः॥
en: Hearing his words, those powerful monkeys, with vigour (enhanced, seeing success before them, felt the height of joy.

sn: अथ पवनसमानविक्रमाः प्लवगवराः प्रतिलब्धपौरुषाः। र्जनकसुतापरिमार्गणोन्मुखाः॥
en: Then those foremost of monkeys, in vigour resembling the Wind, getting occasion for displaying their prowess, intent upon searching the Janaka's daughter, set forward towards the quarter crested by Abhijit.* * Abhijitabhimukhan (acc.) Abhijit—the name of a star. Abhijit may also mean-he who is to be conquered. Then the sense would be the region in which Rāvana was.

sn: आख्याता गृध्रराजेन समुत्प्लुत्य प्लवङ्गमाः। संगताः प्रीतिसंयुक्ता विनेदुः सिंहविक्रमाः॥
en: Having heard all this related to them by the vulture-king, the monkeys possessing the strength of lions, filled with delight, bounded and set up a roar.

sn: सम्पातेर्वचनं श्रुत्वा हरयो रावणक्षयम्। हृष्टाः सागरमाजग्मुः सीतादर्शनकाङ्क्षिणः॥
en: Hearing from Sampāti that Rāvana was to be slain, the monkeys growing glad, came to the ocean, with the desire of seeing Sītā.

sn: अभिगम्य तु तं देशं ददृशुभीमविक्रमाः। कृत्स्नं लोकस्य महतः प्रतिबिम्बमवस्थितम्॥
en: Coming to that country, these ones processing dreadful prowess, beheld (the sea) reflecting the image of this entire mighty world.

sn: दक्षिणस्य समुद्रस्य समासाद्योत्तरां दिशम्। संनिवेशं ततश्चक्रुर्हरिवीरा महाबलाः॥
en: Arriving at the northern side of the Southern sea, those exceedingly powerful heroic monkeys took up their quarters there.

sn: प्रसुप्तमिव चान्यत्र क्रीडन्तमिव चान्यतः। क्वचित् पर्वतमात्रैश्च जलराशिभिरावृतम्॥ संकुलं दानवेन्द्रैश्च पातालतलवासिभिः। रोमहर्षकरं दृष्ट्वा विषेदुः कपिकुञ्जराः॥
en: Seeing the sea, here as if asleep, there, as if playful, and at another place with surges measuring mountains; and thronged with the foremost Dānavas inhabiting the nether regions; and capable of causing one's hair to stand on end, those powerful monkeys were seized with sadness.

sn: आकाशमिव दुष्पारं सागरं प्रेक्ष्य वानराः। विषेदुः सहिताः सर्वे कथं कार्यमिति ब्रुवन्॥
en: Seeing the sea, incapable of being crossed even as the sky, all the monkeys began to lament, saying,-What is to be done?

sn: विषण्णां वाहिनीं दृष्ट्वा सागरस्य निरीक्षणात्। आश्वासयामास हरीन् भयार्तान् हरिसत्तमः॥
en: That best of monkeys-(Angada), seeing the army cast down because of the sight of the sea, began to comfort the monkeys, afflicted with fear.

sn: न विषादे मनः कार्य विषादो दोषवत्तरः। विषादो हन्ति पुरुषं बालं क्रुद्ध इवोरगः॥
en: We should not indulge in grief. Grief is injurious.-Grief destroys a person even as a wrathful serpent does a boy.

sn: यो विषादं प्रसहते विक्रमे समुपस्थिते। तेजसा तस्य हीनस्य पुरुषार्थो न सिद्ध्यति॥
en: He that, when the time is come for displaying his prowess, indulges in sorrow, growing weak in energy, fails to attain his objects.

sn: तस्यां रात्र्यां व्यतीतायामङ्गदो वानरैः सह। हरिवृद्धैः समागम्य पुनर्मन्त्रममन्त्रयत्॥
en: That night having passed away, Angada in company with the monkeys, joined by the old ones, again took counsel with them.

sn: सा वानराणां द्वजिनी परिवार्याङ्गदं बभौ । वासवं परिवार्येव मरुतां वाहिनी स्थितम्॥
en: That monkey-host surrounding Angada, resembled the host of Maruts environing Vasava.

sn: कोऽन्यस्तां वानरी सेनां शक्तः स्तम्भयितुं भवेत्। अन्यत्र वालितन्यादन्यत्र च हनूमतः॥
en: Who save Väli's son (stationed) at one place and at another Hanumān, could be capable of stilling that force?

sn: ततस्तान् हरिवृद्धांश्च तच्च सैन्यमरिंदमः। अनुमान्याङ्गदः श्रीमान् वाक्यमर्थवदब्रवीत्॥
en: Then saluting the elders as well as army, the-graceful Angada-repressor of foes-~-spoke words fraught with sense,

sn: क इदानीं महातेजा लयिष्यति सागरम्। क करिष्यति सुग्रीवं सत्यसंधमरिन्दमम्॥
en: What person, endued with exceeding energy, shall now leap over the main? Who shall serve that subduer of enemies, Sugrīva, ever intent on truth?

sn: को वीरो योजनशतं लङ्घयेत प्लवङ्गमः। इमांश्च यूथपान् सर्वान् मोचयेत् को महाभयात्॥
en: What monkey can leap over an hundred Yojanas? Who shall deliver leaders of herds from a mighty fear?

sn: कस्य प्रसादाद् दारांश्च पुत्रांश्चैव गृहाणि च। इतो निवृत्ताः पश्येम सिद्धार्थाः सुखिनो वयम्॥
en: By whose favour shall we, crowned with success and rendered happy, returning from this place, shall behold our wives and our son, and our homes?

sn: कस्य प्रसादाद् रामं च लक्ष्मणं च महाबलम्। अभिगच्छेम संहृष्टाः सुग्रीवं च वनौकसम्॥ यदि कश्चित् समर्थो वः सागरप्लवने हरिः। स ददात्विह नः शीघ्रं पुण्यामभयदक्षिणाम्॥ अङ्गदस्य वचः श्रुत्वा न कश्चित् किंचिदब्रवीत्। स्तिमितेवाभवत् सर्वा सा तत्र हरिवाहिनी॥
en: By whose favour shall we joyfully meet Rama, and the mighty Laksmana, and that dweller in the woods, Sugrīva? If any monkey among you is competent to bound over the deep, let him at once confer on us Dakșină in the shape of deliverance from fear. Hearing Angada's speech, none said anything, And that host off monkeys wavered.

sn: पुनरेवाङ्गदः प्राह तान् हरीन् हरिसत्तमः। सर्वे बलवतां श्रेष्ठा भवन्तो दृढविक्रमाः। व्यपदेशकुले जाताः पूजिताश्चाप्यभीक्ष्णशः॥
en: Then that foremost of monkeys addressed those monkeys, saying-All of you are the foremost of strong ones, and of steady prowess. And you have sprung in blameless lines, and are ever honoured (by the king).

sn: नहि वो गमने सङ्गः कदाचित् कस्यचिद्भवेत्। ब्रुवध्वं यस्य या शक्तिः प्लवने प्लवगर्षभाः॥
en: And yet no one of you can promise to undertake this journey? You best of monkeys, unfold your respective powers in bounding.

sn: अथाङ्गदवचः श्रुत्वा ते सर्वे वानरर्षभाः। स्वं स्वं गतौ समुत्साहमूचुस्तत्र यथाक्रमम्॥
en: Hearing Angada's speech, those foremost monkeys one after another began to speak, touching their respective competence in coursing.

sn: गजो गवाक्षो गवयः शरभो गन्धमादनः। मैन्दश्च द्विविदश्चैव सुषेणो जाम्बवांस्तथा॥
en: Gaja, and Gavākṣa, and Gavaya, and Sarabha, and Gandhamādana, and Mainda, and Dwivida, and Angada, and Jāmbavān.

sn: आबभाषे गजस्तत्र प्लवेयं दशयोजनम्। गवाक्षो योजनान्याह गमिष्यामीति विंशतिम्॥
en: Gaja said, “I can leap over ten Yojanas," and Gavaksa said, "I shall go twenty Yojanas."

sn: शरभो वानरस्तत्र वानरास्तानुवाच ह। त्रिंशतं तु गमिष्यामि योजनानां प्लवङ्गमाः॥
en: There monkey Sarabha said to those monkeys, “You monkey, I shall go thirty Yojanas."

sn: ऋषभो वानरस्तत्र वानरांस्तानुवाच ह। चत्वारिंशद् गमिष्यामि योजनानां न संशयः॥
en: And the monkey, Rhishava, said to those monkeys,-"I shall, without doubt, go forty Yojanas."

sn: वानरांस्तु महातेजा अब्रवीद् गन्धमादनः। योजनानां गमिष्यामि पञ्चाशत्तु न सशंयः॥
en: And the exceedingly energetic monkey, Gandhamädana, said, I shall for certain go fifty Yojanas.

sn: मैन्दस्तु वानरस्तत्र वानरांस्तानुवाच ह। योजनानां परं षष्टिमहं प्लवितुमुत्सहे॥
en: And the monkey Mainda said to the monkeys there, I shall undertake to leap over sixty Yojanas.

sn: ततस्तत्र महातेजा द्विविदः प्रत्यभाषत। गमिष्यामि न संदेहः सप्ततिं योजनान्यहम्॥
en: And then the highly energetic Dwivida said,-I Shall, for certain, go seventy Yojanas.

sn: सुषेणस्तु महातेजाः सत्त्ववान् कपिसत्तमः। अशीतिं प्रतिजानेऽहं योजनानां पराक्रमे॥
en: And the highly powerful Suşena, possessed of strength-foremost of monkeys said—I declare that in motion I am equal to eighty Yojanas.

sn: तेषां कथयतां तत्र सर्वांस्ताननुमान्य च। ततो वृद्धतमस्तेषां जाम्बवान् प्रत्यभाषत॥
en: As they were speaking thus,' the oldest of them all, Jambavān, saluting them answered.

sn: पूर्वमस्माकमप्यासीत् कश्चिद् गतिपराक्रमः। ते वयं वयसः पारमनुप्राप्ताः स्म साम्प्रतम्॥ किं तु नैवं गते शक्यमिदं कार्यमुपेक्षितुम्। यदर्थं कपिराजश्च रामश्च कृतनिश्चयौ॥ साम्प्रतं कालमस्माकं या गतिस्तां निबोधत। नवतिं योजनानां तु गमिष्यामि न संशयः॥
en: Formerly we had power of motion. But now we have waxed exceeding old. Although this is so, yet we can not overlook this, as both Rama and the monkey-king (by sending us) have become sure of success. At present do you understand the course that is ours. I shall go ninety Yojanas. There is no doubt whatever about this.

sn: तांश्च सर्वान् हरिश्रेष्ठाञ्जाम्बवानिदमब्रवीत्। न खल्वेतावदेवासीद् गमने मे पराक्रमः॥ मया वैरोचने यज्ञे प्रभविष्णुः सनातनः। प्रदक्षिणीकृतः पूर्वं क्रममाणस्त्रिविक्रमः॥
en: Jāmbavān said this to those choice monkeys. But (formerly) my prowess in leaping was forsooth not such.* Of old in the sacrifice of Virocana's son, the external Lord Visnu, when he had covered the entire universe with three steps, was circumambulated by me. *i.e. it was greater.

sn: स इदानीमहं वृद्धः प्लवने मन्दविक्रमः। यौवने च तदासीन्मे बलमप्रतिमं परम्॥
en: But I who was all this, have waxed old, and my vigour sits feebly upon me. In my youth, ever, my strength was exceeding great and incomparable.

sn: सम्प्रत्येतावदेवाद्य शक्यं मे गमने स्वतः। नैतावता च संसिद्धिः कार्यस्यास्य भविष्यति॥
en: Now I can only by my own energy, course thus far. But has a bound shall not bring success on our undertaking.

sn: अथोत्तरमुदारार्थमब्रवीदङ्गदस्तदा। अनुमान्य तदा प्राज्ञो जाम्बवन्तं महाकपिः॥
en: After this, saluting the mighty monkey, Jāmbavān, the wise Angada spoke straight sense, saying,

sn: अहमेतद् गमिष्यामि योजनानां शतं महत्। निवर्तने तु मे शक्तिः स्यान वेति न निश्चितम्॥
en: I can go over this mighty hundred Yojanas; but there is no certainty as to my answer of returning.

sn: तमुवाच हरिश्रेष्ठं जाम्बवान् वाक्यकोविदः। ज्ञापते गमो शक्तिस्तव हवृक्षसत्तम॥ कामं शतसहस्रं वा नह्येष विधिरुच्यते। योजनानां भवाशक्तो गन्तुं प्रतिनिवर्तितुम्॥
en: Thereat, Jāmbavān, cognizant of speech, said to that foremost of monkeys,-0 foremost of leonine as, we know your power of motion, you are capable of ursing a hundred thousand Yojanas, as well as of coming back. But we say that even this is what is fit.

sn: नहि प्रेषयिता तात स्वामी प्रेष्यः कथंचन। भवताऽयं जनः सर्वः प्रेष्यः प्लवगसत्तम ॥
en: My child, ore master must on no account be commanded by his servants. foremost of monkeys, all these should be commanded your you.

sn: भवान् कलत्रमस्माकं स्वाभिभावे व्यवस्थितः। स्वामी कलत्रं सैन्यस्य गतिरेषा परंतप॥
en: You are our spouse, and (at the same time) occuying the position of our husband. The master is the spouse if the army. This is the way of the world.

sn: अपि वै तस्य कार्यस्य भवान् मूलमरिंदम। तस्मात् कलत्रवत् तात प्रतिपाल्यः सदा भवान्॥
en: O repressor of oes! O subduer of enemies, you are the root of this business. Therefore, my child, you should always be maintained by us like a wife.

sn: मूलमर्थस्य संरक्ष्यमेव कार्यविदां नयः। मूले हि सति सिध्यन्ति गुणाः सर्वे फलोदयाः॥
en: The root of any work must be preserved. This is the policy of those versed in business. The root existing, all the virtues, obtaining fruit, certainly meet with success.

sn: तद् भवानस्य कार्यस्य साधनं सत्यविक्रम। बुद्धिविक्रमसम्पन्नो हेतुरत्र परंतप॥ गुरुश्च गुरुपुत्रश्च त्वं हि नः कपिसत्तमः। भवन्तमाश्रित्य वयं समर्था ह्यर्थसाधने॥
en: You, O you having truth for prowess are the instrument of this undertaking, and, O subduer of enemies, furnished with sense and vigour, you are the occasion herein. And, O foremost of monkeys, you are both our superior, and our superior's son; and resorting to you we are enabled to accomplish our object.

sn: उक्तवाक्यं महाप्राज्ञं जाम्बवन्तं महाकपिः। प्रत्युवाचोत्तरं वाक्यं वालिसूनुरथाङ्गदः॥
en: Threat that mighty monkey, Angada, son to Vali, answered the exceedingly wise Jambavan, when he had spoken,

sn: यदि नाहं गमिष्यामि नान्यो वानरपुङ्गवः। पुनः खल्विदमस्माभिः कार्य प्रायोपवेशनम्॥
en: If I go not, nor any other powerful monkey, then we should for certain again sit ourselves down to fast to death.

sn: नह्यकृत्वा हरिपतेः संदेशं तस्य धीमतः। तत्रापि गत्वा प्राणानां न पश्ये परिरक्षणम्॥
en: Without doing the mandate of the intelligent lord of monkeys, we, repairing thither, shall not behold ourselves alive.

sn: स हि प्रसादे चात्यर्थकोपे च हरिरीश्वरः। अतीत्य तस्य संदेशं विनाशो गमने भवेत्॥
en: He is extreme both in showing favour and in anger. Disregarding his order, we shall, going there, meet with destruction. And his ire shall, not take any other course.

sn: तत्तथा ह्यस्य कार्यस्य न भवत्यन्यथा गतिः। तद् भवानेव दृष्टार्थः संचिन्तयितुमर्हति ॥
en: Therefore it behoves you, cap of seeing issues, to reflect.

sn: सोऽङ्गदेन तदा वीरः प्रत्युक्तः प्लवगर्षभः। जाम्बवानुत्तमं वाक्यं प्रोवाचेदं ततोऽङ्गदम्॥
en: Thus addressed by Angada that powerful and heroic monkey Jāmbavān answered Angada in excellent words, saying,

sn: तस्य ते वीर कार्यस्य न किंचित् परिहास्यते। एष संचोदयाम्येनं यः कार्य साधयिष्यति ॥
en: That . business, O hero, say most moult a feather. I shall despatch even him who's bring about success.

sn: ततः प्रतीतं प्लवतां वरिष्ठमेकान्तमाश्रित्य सुखोपविष्टम्। संचोदयामास हरिप्रवीरो हरिप्रवीरं हनुमन्तमेव॥
en: Then that heroic monkey ordered foremost of monkeys, the highly heroic monkey Hanuman who stood apart, convinced (of the wisdom of Jambavān decision).

sn: अनेकशतसाहस्री विषण्णां हरिवाहिनीम्। जाम्बवान् समुदीक्ष्यैवं हनूमन्तमथाब्रवीत्॥
en: Surveying the monkey-host consisting of many hundred and thousand,-crest-fallen, Jämbavān thus spoke to Hanumān,

sn: वीर वानरलोकस्य सर्वशास्त्रविदां वर। तूष्णीमेकान्तमाश्रित्य हनूमन् किं न जल्पसि॥
en: O hero among the monkey-multitude, O be of those versed in all branches of learning, staying apart silent, why did you not speak?

sn: हनूमन्हरिराजस्य सुग्रीवस्य समो ह्यसि। रामलक्ष्मणयोश्चापि तेजसा च बलेन च॥
en: O Hanuman, you are alil in energy and strength, equal to Sugriva, monarch monkeys, and to Rāma and Lakşmaņa.

sn: अरिष्टनेमिनः पुत्रो वैनतेयो महाबलः। गरुत्मानिव विख्यात उत्तमः सर्वपक्षिणाम्॥
en: Aristanemi's son the mighty Vainateya,* famous by the cognomen of Garutmā, is the foremost of birds. *Offspring of Vinatā, Garura's mother.

sn: बहुशो हि मया दृष्टः सागरे स महाबलः। भुजङ्गानुद्धरन् पक्षी महाबाहुर्महाबलः॥
en: Many a time and oft. I have see that exceedingly powerful, mighty-armed one, endowed with strength of will,-raise up serpents in the ocean.

sn: पक्षयोर्यद् बलं तस्य भुजवीर्यबलं तव। विक्रमश्चापि वेगश्च न ते तेनापहीयते॥
en: The strength that is in his wings, is equal to the might and virtues your arm.

sn: बलं बुद्धिश्च तेजश्च सत्त्वं च हरिपुङ्गव। विशिष्टं सर्वभूतेषु किमात्मानं न सज्जसे।७।।
en: Your energy and prowess are not surpassed by him And your strength, and your understanding, your energy, and your vigour, O foremost of monkeys, (is known among all creatures). Why did not you prepare yourself furnished with everything that is noble or great, (for this feat)?

sn: अप्सराऽप्सरसां श्रेष्ठा विख्याता पुञ्जिकस्थला। अञ्जनेति परिख्याता पत्नी केसरिणो हरेः॥ विख्याता त्रिषु लोकेषु रूपेणाप्रतिमा भुवि। अभिशापादभूत् तात कपित्वे कामरूपिणी॥ दुहिता वानरेन्द्रस्य कुञ्जरस्य महात्मनः। मानुषं विग्रहं कृत्वा रूपयौवनशालिनी॥ विचित्रमाल्याभरणा कदाचित् क्षौमधारिणी। अचरत् पर्वतस्याग्रे प्रावृडम्बुदसंनिभे॥
en: That fore most of Apsarās,—the famous Punjikathală, more famed under the name of Añjana, is the spouse of the monkey Kesarin used over the three worlds, and incomparable on earth by to of her beauty, by an imprecation, my son, she was of in the monkey-race, capable of wearing slopes at her Once on a time, that daughter of the high-souled lord monkeys, Kunjara,-endued with youth and beauty,-used in a delightful garland, and clad in silk, —assum human form, was ranging on the summit of a mountain, ambling a mass of clouds in the rainy season.

sn: तस्या वस्त्रं विशालाक्ष्याः पीतं रक्तदशं शुभम्। स्थितायाः पर्वतस्याग्रे मारुतोऽपहरच्छनैः॥
en: It came moss that as that one of expansive eyes was standing on the mit of the mount, the Wind gently stole away her elegant bow cloth with crimson skirts.

sn: स ददर्श ततस्तस्या वृत्तावूरू सुसंहतौ। स्तनौ च पीनौ सहितौ सुजातं चारु चाननम्॥ तां बलादायतश्रोणी तनुमध्यां यशस्विनीम्। दृष्ट्वैव शुभसर्वाङ्गी पवनः काममोहितः॥ स तां भुजाभ्यां दीर्घाभ्यां पर्यष्वजत मारुतः। मन्मथाविष्टसर्वाङ्गो गतात्मा तामनिन्दिताम्॥
en: He had a sight of her and fine face, together with her well-developed breasts. As soon as the Wind saw that illustrious one of spacious and slender waist, and whose every limb was lovely,-was amain overcome by desire. And all his frame sessed by Manmatha, and deprived of self, the Wind emced that blameless one by means of his long arms.

sn: सा तु तत्रैव सम्भ्रान्ता सुव्रता वाक्यमब्रवीत्। एकपत्नीव्रतमिदं को नाशयितुमिच्छति॥
en: There influenced by fear, that one of excellent vows said,-no is it that desireth to lay violent hands upon my chastity?

sn: अनाया वचः तुत्वा मारुतः प्रत्यभाषत। न त्वां हिंसामि सुश्रोणि माभूत् ते मनसो भयम्॥
en: Hearing Anjana's words, the Wind answered, do not wrong you, O you of shapely hips. Let not her enter your heart.

sn: मनसाऽस्मि गतो यत् त्वां परिष्वज्य यशस्विनि। वीर्यवान् बुद्धिसम्पन्नस्तव पुत्रो भविष्यति॥
en: As, O famous damsel, by embracing the, I have mentally entered into your womb, you shall her a son, intelligent and endued with prowess.

sn: महासत्त्वो महातेजा महाबलपराक्रमः। लङ्घने प्लवने चैव भविष्यति मया समः।।१९
en: And, bed with great strength, and possessing exceeding energy, having vast vigour, he shall equal me in bound and leaping.'

sn: एवमुक्ता ततस्तुष्टा जननी ते महाकपे। गुहायां त्वां महाबाहो प्रजज्ञे प्लवगर्षभ॥
en: Thus addressed, O mighty monkeys, your other, O long-armed one, O foremost of monkeys, your has to you in a cave.

sn: अभ्युत्थितं ततः सूर्यं बालो दृष्ट्वा महावने। फलं चेति जिघृक्षुस्त्वमुत्पत्याभ्युत्पतो दिवम्॥
en: In that mighty forest, you, a child, desirous of eating, seeing the sun risen, and taking on to be a fruit, sprang up and leaped into the sky.

sn: शतानि त्रीणि गत्वाथ योजनानां महाकपे। तेजसा तस्य निर्धूतो न विषादं गतस्ततः॥
en: O mighty monkey, going three thousand Yojanas, you, struck by as energy, didst not feel poverty of spirit.
