sn: त्वामप्युपगतं तूर्णमन्तरिक्षं महाकपे। क्षिप्तमिन्द्रेण ते वज्रं कोपाविष्टेन तेजसा ॥
en: And, seeing you shing through the heavens, O mighty monkey, Indra, owing wrath, hurled his thunder-bolt at you.

sn: तदा शैलाग्रशिखरे वामो हनुरभज्यत। ततो हि नामधेयं ते हनुमानिति कीर्तितम्॥
en: Thereat, breaking your left jaw, you (didst fall) on the mountain From this circumstance, your name has been known Hanuman.

sn: ततस्त्वां निहतं दृष्ट्वा वायुर्गन्धवहः स्वयम्। त्रैलोक्यं भृशसंक्रुद्धो न ववौ वै प्रभञ्जनः॥
en: Witnessing you beaten back, that bearer of fumes himself, the Wind, that breaketh everything before in wrath did not blow through the three worlds.

sn: सम्भ्रान्ताश्च सुराः सर्वे त्रैलोक्ये क्षुभिते सति। प्रसादयन्ति संक्रुद्धं मारुतं भुवनेश्वराः॥
en: Thereat, all gods-lords of the universeinfluenced by fear in consequence of the triune world waxing agitated, began to path the wrathful Wind.

sn: प्रसादिते च पवने ब्रह्मा तुभ्यं वरं ददौ। अशस्त्रवध्यतां तात समरे सत्यविक्रम॥
en: And on the Wind being mollified, Bra conferred on him a boon, saying,–O child, O you of prowess, (your son) shall be incapable of being slain in be by means of weapons.'

sn: वज्रस्य च निपातेन विरुजं त्वां समीक्ष्य च। सहस्रनेत्रः प्रीतात्मा ददौ ते वरमुत्तमम्॥ स्वच्छन्दतश्च मरणं तव स्यादिति वै प्रभो।
en: And seeing him sustain (serious) injury consequent on the impact of the thunder. He of a thousand eyes, pleased in his soul, also confer on (you) and excellent boon, O lord, saying, 'Your death: take place according to your will.' *Hanuman.

sn: स त्वं केसरिणः पुत्रः क्षेत्रजो भीमविक्रमः॥ मारुतस्यौरसः पुत्रस्तेजसा चापि तत्समः।
en: You, endowed with drawful vigour, are the son of Kesarī by his wife; and, resemble the Wind in energy, you had sprung from his loins.

sn: त्वं हि वायुसुतो वत्स प्लवने चापि तत्समः॥ वयमद्य गतप्राणा भवानस्मासु साम्प्रतम्। दाक्ष्यविक्रमसम्पन्नः कपिराज इवापरः॥
en: The are the son of the Wind, my child-equal to him in power of leaping. Now we are without our lives. And you, endowed with dexterity and vigour, and like another I of the monkeys,+ are before us. *Sugriva.

sn: त्रिविक्रमे मया तात सशैलवनकानना। त्रिःसप्तकृत्वः पृथिवी परिक्रान्ता प्रदक्षिणम्॥
en: On the occasion of Vişnu enveloping the earth with three steps, I, O child, had circa ambulated the earth with her mountains, woods and fore one and twenty times.

sn: तथा चौषधयोऽस्माभिः संचिता देवशासनात्। निर्मथ्यममृतं याभिस्तदानीं नो महद्बलम्॥
en: Then, commissioned by the gods, had gathered annuals, which (bcing cast on the deep), cat ambrosia to come out after churning. At that time, god was our strength.

sn: स इदानीमहं वृद्धः परिहीनपराक्रमः। साम्प्रतं कालमस्माकं भवान् सर्वगुणान्वितः॥
en: But now I have grown old, and prowess has left me. At present we have you, furnish with every virtue.

sn: तद् विजृम्भस्व विक्रान्त प्लवतामुत्तमो ह्यसि। त्वद्वीर्यं द्रष्टुकामा हि सर्वा वानरवाहिनी॥
en: Therefore, possessed of vigour, do I bestir yourself, and bound over (the main). You are the qualified of all. This entire monkey host is eager to bell your prowess.

sn: उत्तिष्ठ हरिशार्दूल लङ्घयस्व महार्णवम्। परा हि सर्वभूतानां हनुमन् या गतिस्तव॥
en: O redoubtable monkey, do you arise! leap over the mighty ocean. Your motion, Hanumān, asseth that of all beings.

sn: विषण्णा हरयः सर्वे हनुमन् किमुपेक्षसे। विक्रमस्व महावेग विष्णुस्त्रीन् विक्रमानिव ॥
en: All the monkeys are depressed. O Hanuman, did you overlook this? Put forth your you endowed with mighty vehemence, like Vişnu sing over the three worlds in three steps.

sn: ततः कपीनामृषभेण चोदितः प्रतीतवेगः पवनात्मजः कपिः। प्रहर्षयंस्तां हरिवीरवाहिनी चकार रूपं महदात्मनस्तदा॥
en: Exhorted by foremost of monkeys, that one famed for has speech, that key, the offspring of the Wind-god, gladdening the monkey-chiefs, wore (a fit) shape for crossing the ocean.* *Another epithet of Hanumān, Pavanātmaja-son to the Wind?? on the score of Redundency.

sn: तं दृष्ट्वा जृम्भमाणं ते क्रमितुं शतयोजनम्। वेगेनापूर्यमाणं च सहसा वानरोत्तमम्॥ सहसा शोकमुत्सृज्य प्रहर्षेण समन्विताः। विनेदुस्तुष्टुवुश्चापि हनूमन्तं महाबलम्॥
en: Seeing that foremost of monkeys enlarge his person for bossing over an hundred Yojanas, and suddenly filled with energy, (the monkeys) at once renounced sorrow, and, filled with light, set up ululations and fell to eulogizing the mighty Hanuman.

sn: प्रहृष्टा विस्मिताश्चापि ते वीक्षन्ते समन्ततः। त्रिविक्रमं कृतोत्साहं नारायणमिव प्रजाः॥ संस्तूयमानो हनुमान् व्यवर्धत महाबलः। समाविद्ध्य च लालं हर्षाद् बलमुपेयिवान्॥
en: And, struck with amazement, they, (staying) all round, joyfully gazed (at him); even as creatures beheld Nārāyaṇa, then stretching forth his three steps, he prepared him (for the succeeding feat). And, eulogized by them, the odorous mighty Hanuman increased; and, flourishing his tail me joy, attained strength.

sn: तस्य संस्तूयमानस्य वृद्धैर्वानरपुङ्गवैः। तेजसाऽऽपूर्यमाणस्य रूपमासीदनुत्तमम्॥
en: As, extolled by the principal derly monkeys, he became fraught with effulgence, his beauty as great. .

sn: यथा विजृम्भते सिंहो विवृते गिरिगह्वरे। मारुतस्यौरसः : पुत्रस्तथा सम्प्रति जृम्भते॥
en: As a lion fills himself with vigour in an open we, so the son of the Wind-god filled himself with energy.

sn: अशोभत मुखं तस्य जृम्भमाणस्य धीमतः। अम्बरीषोपमं दीप्तं विधूम इव पावकः॥
en: The face of him, as that intelligent one was filling, himself has force was aflame like a frying-pan, or like to themeless fire.

sn: हरीणामुत्थितो मध्यात् सम्प्रहृष्टतनूरुहः। अभिवाद्य हरीन् वृद्धान् हनूमानिदमब्रवीत्॥
en: Rising in the midst of the monkeys, Hanumān has his down standing on end through joy, saluting the monkeys, said,

sn: आरुजन् पर्वताग्राणि हुताशनसखोऽनिलः। बलवानप्रमेयश्च वायुराकाशगोचरः॥ तस्याहं शीघ्रवेगस्य शीघ्रगस्य महात्मनः। मारुतस्यौरसः पुत्रः प्लवनेनास्मि तत्समः॥
en: Wind, the friend of Fire, shattereth summits; and, [ever blowing in the eye of the sky, he is possessed of strength, and is of immeasure (might). Begot from his loins, I am the son of fast-coursing and high-souled Wind, coursing swiftly am his equal in all these accomplishments.* *i.e. pertaining to leaping.

sn: उत्सहे य हि विस्तीर्णमालिखन्तमिवाम्बरम्। मेहं गिरिमसङ्गेन परिगन्तुं सहस्रशः॥ बाहुवेगप्रणुन्नेन सागरेणाहमुत्सहे। समाप्लावयितुं लोकं सपर्वतनदीह्रदम्॥
en: I without once stopping, circumambulate the extensive heaven-cleaving mountain, Meru, for a thousand tin And, dashing the ocean with my arms, I can del the world with its mountains, rivers and lakes.

sn: ममोरुजवावेगेन भविष्यति समुत्थितः। समुत्थितमहाग्राहः समुद्रो वरुणालयः॥
en: Las by the force of my legs and thighs, that abode of Varuņa the sea, out which have sprung the ferocious aqua animals, overleaps its continents.

sn: पन्नागाशनमाकाशे पतन्तं पक्षिसेवितम्। वैनतेयमहं शक्तः परिगन्तुं सहस्रशः॥
en: And for once that lor birds, Vinata's offspring, living on serpents, courseth through the welkin, I can course through it a thousand times.

sn: उदयात् प्रस्थितं वापि ज्वलन्तं रश्मिमालिनम्। अनस्तमितमादित्यमहं गन्तुं समुत्सहे॥ ततो भूमिमसंस्पृष्ट्वा पुनरागन्तुमुत्सहे। प्रवेगेनैव महता भीमेन प्लवगर्षभाः॥
en: And can touch the flaming effulgent Sun ere, beginning his jour from the Rising hill, he ascends the Setting hill. And, foremost of monkeys, I can, fiercely rushing on, come as without touching the earth.

sn: उत्सहेयमतिक्रान्तुं सर्वानाकाशगोचरान्। सागरान् शोषयिष्यामि दारयिष्यामि मेदिनीम्॥ पर्वतांश्चूर्णयिष्यामि प्लवमानः प्लवङ्गमः। हरिष्याम्युरुवेगेन प्लवमानो महार्णवम्॥
en: And I can bound beyound's and planets, suck up the oceans, and rive the earth. And a monkey, I can, leaping, crush mountains; and, leaping can drain the mighty ocean dry.

sn: लतानां विविधं पुष्पं पादपानां च सर्वशः। अनुयास्यति मामद्य प्लवमानं विहायसा॥
en: When I shall learing the sky, flowers from various shrubs and trees shall follow me to-day.

sn: भविष्यति हि मे पन्थाः स्वातेः पन्था इवाम्बरे। चरन्तं घोरमाकाशमुत्पतिष्यन्तमेव च॥ द्रक्ष्यन्ति निपतन्तं च सर्वभूतानि वानराः।
en: And then my course, flecked with flowers), resemble even they sky (studded with stars). And, monkeys, then all creatures shall see me now ranging through the profound firmament, now shooting up, and now descending (on the other shore).

sn: महामेरुप्रतीकाशं मां द्रक्ष्यध्वं प्लवङ्गमाः॥ दिवमावृत्य गच्छन्तं ग्रसमानमिवाम्बरम्। विधमिष्यामि जीमूतान् कम्पयिष्यामि पर्वतान्। सागरं शोषयिष्यामि प्लवमानः समाहितः॥
en: Resembling Mahāmeru, me shall behold, you monkeys, making my way, covering up sky, as if devouring up the heavens. I shall, leaping concentrating my energy, scatter the clouds, shake the I and suck up the ocean.

sn: वैनतेयस्य वा शक्तिर्मम वा मारुतस्य वा। ऋते सुपर्णराजानं मारुतं वा महाबलम्। न तद् भूतं प्रपश्यामि यन्मां प्लुतमनुव्रजेत्॥
en: The strength of Vinata's son the Wind-god's, or mine, (surpasses that of every creature). None save the sovereign of birds, or the exceeding mighty Wind, can follow me in flight.

sn: निमेषान्तरमात्रेण निरालम्बनमम्बरम्। सहसा निपतिष्यामि घनाद् विद्युदिवोत्थिता॥
en: In the twing an eye I shall spread through the unsupported lightning darting from clouds.

sn: भविष्यति हि मे रूपं प्लवमानस्य सागरम्। विष्णोः प्रक्रममाणस्य तदा त्रीन् विक्रमानिव ॥
en: And at the time of leaping over the ocean, my form shall resemble that of the energizing Vişņu, when He had assumed the triune energy.

sn: बुद्ध्या चाहं प्रपश्यामि मनश्रेष्ठा च मे तथा। अहं द्रक्ष्यामि वैदेही प्रमोदध्वं प्लवङ्गमाः॥
en: I perceive through my intelligence, (and my mental motion tallies), that I shall behold Vaidehi. Therefore, you monkeys, rejoice.

sn: मारुतस्य समो वेगे गरुडस्य समो जवे। अयुतं योजनानां तु गमिष्यामीति मे मतिः॥
en: In vehemence like to Garura, I shall, I conceive, go an Ayuta yojanas.

sn: वासवस्य सवज्रस्य ब्रह्मणो वा स्वयम्भुवः। विक्रम्य सहसा हस्तादमृतं तदिहानये॥ लङ्कां वापि समुत्क्षिप्य गच्छेयमिति मे मतिः।
en: I can, suddenly summoning energy, bring hither ambrosia from the very grasp of Vāsava or Brahmā himself. I shall leap sheer over Lankā. Even this is my impression.

sn: तमेवं वानरश्रेष्ठं गर्जन्तममितप्रभम्॥ प्रहृष्टा हरयस्तत्र समुदैक्षन्त विस्मिताः।
en: Filled with delight, the monkeys there amazed see that foremost of monkeys, endued with immeasurable might, storming.

sn: तच्चास्य वचनं श्रुत्वा ज्ञातीनां शोकनाशनम्॥ उवाच परिसंहृष्टो जाम्बवान् प्लवगेश्वरः।
en: And, hearing his speech capable of removing the grief of kindred, that best of monkeys Jambavān, transported with joy, said,

sn: वीर केसरिणः पुत्र वेगवन् मारुतात्मज॥ ज्ञातीनां विपुलः शोकस्त्वया तात प्रणाशितः।
en: O hero! O son of Kesari! O offspring of the Wind! the huge sorrow of your kindred has, my child, been destroyed by you.

sn: तव कल्याणरुचयः कपिमुख्याः समागताः॥ मङ्गलान्यर्थसिद्ध्यर्थं करिष्यन्ति समाहिताः।
en: These foremost of monkeys assembled, who wish for your welfare, shall, with intent mind, perform acts tending to your weal,-so that you mayst succeed in your undertaking.

sn: ऋषीणां च प्रसादेन कपिवृद्धमतेन च॥ गुरूणां च प्रसादेन संप्लव त्वं महार्णवम्।
en: By the grace of the saints, and with the permission of the aged monkeys, and by the blessing of the superiors, do you bound over the mighty main.

sn: स्थास्यामश्चैकपादेन यावदागमनं तव॥ त्वद्गतानि च सर्वेषां जीवनानि वनौकसाम्।
en: Till you return, we shall stay on one leg. The lives of all these rangers of the forest shall go along with you. *i.e. practise austerities on your behalf.

sn: ततश्च हरिशार्दूलस्तानुवाच वनौकसः॥ कोऽपि लोके न मे वेगं प्लवने धारयिष्यति।
en: Then that tiger-like monkey said to those rangers of the woods, None in this world would be able to sustain my impetus in the act of bounding.

sn: एतानीह नगस्यास्य शिलासंकटशालिनः॥ शिखराणि महेन्द्रस्य स्थिराणि च महान्ति च। येषु वेगं गमिष्यामि महेन्द्रशिखरेष्वहम्॥ नानादुमविकीर्णेषु धातुनिष्पन्दशोभिषु।
en: Here are these summits, firm and spacious, of this mountain, Mahendra, thronged with crags. I shall rush forward from these summits of Mahendra, interspersed with trees and adorned with masses of ore.

sn: एतानि मम वेगं हि शिखराणि महान्ति च॥ प्लवतो धारयिष्यन्ति योजनानामितः शतम्।
en: As I leap over a hundred Yojanas, these mighty summits shall sustain my impetus.

sn: ततस्तु मारुतप्रख्यः स हरिर्मारुतात्मजः। आरुरोह नगश्रेष्ठं महेन्द्रमरिमर्दनः॥ वृतं नानाविधैः पुष्पैर्मृगसेवितशाद्वलम्। लताकुसुमसम्बाधं नित्यपुष्पफलद्रुमम्॥ सिंहशार्दूलसहितं मत्तमातङ्गसेवितम्। मत्तद्विजगणोद्धृष्टं सलिलोत्पीडसंकुलम्॥ महद्भिरुच्छ्रितः शृङ्गैर्महेन्द्रस्य महाबलः। विचचार हरिश्रेष्ठो महेन्द्रसमविक्रमः।॥
en: Then he equalling the Wind, that monkey, the son of the Wind-god, pounder of enemies, ascended that best of mountains, Mahendra; covered with with various trees and flowers, furnished with swards; ranged by deer; containing plants and blossoms with trees bearing fruits and flowers daily; having tigers and lions and infuriated elephants; swarming with maddened birds; and abounding with fountains. Ascending (Mahendra), that foremost of monkeys endued with exceeding strength, and resembling Mahendra himself in prowess, began to range from one mighty summit to another.

sn: बाहुभ्यां पीडितस्तेन महाशैलो महात्मना। ररास सिंहाभिहतो महान् मत्त इव द्विपः॥
en: Thereat, hurt by the arms of that high-souled one, the mighty mountain began to cry,* like a mighty mad elephant tormented by a lion. *Through the voices of the animals inhabiting it.

sn: मुमोच सलिलोत्पीडान् विप्रकीर्णशिलोच्चयः। वित्रस्तमृगमातङ्गः प्रकम्पितमहाद्रुमः॥ नानागन्धर्वमिथुनैः पानसंसर्गकर्कशैः। उत्पतद्भिर्विहङ्गैश्च विद्याधरगणैरपि॥ त्यज्यमानमहासानुः संनिलीनमहोरगः। शैलशृङ्गशिलोत्पातस्तदाभूत् स महागिरिः॥
en: And water rushed out of masses of rocks scattered around. And that mighty mountain had its deer and elephants afflicted with affright; and its giant trees shaken; and its spacious uplands deserted by various Gandharva couples engaged in drinking and dalliance, and by birds-flying away, and by bevies of Vidyadharas; and its huge serpents distressed, and its cliffs and peaks toppling down.

sn: निःश्वसद्भिस्तदा तैस्तु भुजगैरर्धनिःसृतैः। सपाताक इवाभाति स तदा धरणीधरः॥ ऋषिभिस्त्रासम्भ्रान्तैस्त्यज्यमानः शिलोच्चयः। सीदन्महति कान्तारे सार्थहीन इवाध्वगः॥
en: With its serpents hissing, with their bodies half issuing (from their holes), the mountain seemed as if it shone with pennons displayed. And the heap of crags forsaken by saints exercised with fear and agitation, looked doleful, like a wayfarer left in a vast forest by his companions.

sn: स वेगवान् वेगसमाहितात्मा हरिप्रवीरः परिवीरहन्ता। मनः समाधाय महानुभावो जगाम लङ्कां मनसा मनस्वी ॥
en: That intelligent, magnanimous and heroic monkey-destroyer of hostile heroes, endowed with speed, concentrating his soul on his energy, mentally went to Lankā.

sn: ततो रावणनीतायाः सीतायाः शत्रुकर्षणः। इयेष पदमन्वेष्टुं चारणाचरिते पथि॥
en: Hanumăn then resolved to travel through the air or the path of Cāraņas (heavens), in quest of Jānaki who had taken away by Rävaņa.

sn: दुष्करं निष्प्रतिद्वन्द्वं चिकीर्षन् कर्म वानरः। समुदग्रशिरोग्रीवो गवां पतिरिवाबभौ॥
en: In order to perform that arduous task he raised his head and stiffened his neck quite erect, for which he looked like a bull.

sn: अथ वैदूर्यवर्णेषु शाद्वलेषु महाबलः। धीरः सलिलकल्पेषु विचचार यथासुखम्॥ द्विजान् वित्रासयन् धीमानुरसा पादपान् हरन्। मृगांश्च सुबहून् निघ्नन् प्रवृद्ध इव केसरी॥
en: Then he, wise and mighty monkey walked over the earth, green with grass, with irresistible steps. At that time, he brushed aside all animals like a lion and crushed down many trees, and thereby scared away the feathered denizens of the forest.

sn: नीललोहितमाञ्जिष्ठपद्मवर्णैः सितासितैः। स्वभावसिद्धैर्विमलैर्धातुभिः समलंकृतम्॥ कामरूपिभिराविष्टमभीक्ष्णं सपरिच्छदैः। यक्षकिन्नरगन्धर्वैर्देवकल्पैः सपन्नगैः॥ स तस्य गिरिवर्यस्य तले नागवरायुते। तिष्ठन् कपिवरस्तत्र हृदे नाग इवाबभौ॥
en: There were various minerals on the Mahendra hill was shining by rosy, ruby-like and white and black hues, which was constantly visited by Yaksas, Kinnaras,, Gandharvas, Nāgas resembling to the celestials capable in their pristine lustre, there Hanumān standing at its foot looked like an elephant immersed in a lake!

sn: स सूर्याय महेन्द्राय पवनाय स्वयंभुवे। भूतेभ्यश्चाञ्जलिं कृत्वा चकार गमने मतिम्॥ अञ्जलिं प्राङ्मुखं कुर्वन् पवनायात्मयोनये। ततो हि ववृधे गन्तुं दक्षिणो दक्षिणां दिशम्॥
en: After this, he bowed down to the Sun, Indra, Svayambhu, Wind-god, and all beings with joined palms and then facing the west he saluted his father and then began to increase in dimension like the sea.

sn: प्लवगप्रवरैर्दृष्टः प्लवने कृतनिश्चयः। ववृधे रामवृद्ध्यर्थं समुद्र इव पर्वसु॥
en: The foremost of the Vānaras at this stared at him, he swelled in size for the purpose of Rāma as the ocean swells on the full-moon days.

sn: निष्प्रमाणशरीरः सँल्लिलवयिषुरर्णवम्। बाहुभ्यां पीडयामास चरणाभ्यां च पर्वतम्॥
en: Hanumān got ready for crossing the ocean having grown his body immensely. He caught hold tightly of the mountain with his hands and feet.

sn: स चचालाचलश्चाशु मुहूर्तं कपिपीडतः। तरूणां पुष्पिताग्राणां सर्वं पुष्पमशातयत्॥ तेन पादपमुक्तेन पुष्पौघेण सुगन्धिना। सर्वतः संवृतः शैलो बभौ पुष्पमयो यथा॥ तेन चोत्तमवीर्येण पीड्यमानः स पर्वतः। सलिलं सम्प्रसुस्राव मदमत्त इव द्विपः॥ पीड्यमानस्तु बलिना महेन्द्रस्तेन पर्वतः। रीतीनिवर्तयामास काञ्चनाञ्जनराजतीः॥
en: The hill at once shook and flowers began to drop down from the trees. Having discharged that fragrant flowers from trees covered all the sides of the mountain which appeared as though it were all flowers. Hanumān began to press the mountain more and more, and it began to spurt forth water like an elephant shedding its temporal sweat, and the golden, silvery and collyrium hues of the different minerals were all destroyed by that torrent of water.

sn: मुमोच च शिलाः शैलो विशालाः समन:शिला :। मध्यमेनार्चिषा जुष्टो धूमराजीरिवानलः॥ हरिणा पीड्यमानेन पीड्यमानानि सर्वतः। गुहाविष्टानि सत्त्वानि विनेदुर्विकृतैः स्वरैः॥ स महान् सत्त्वसंनादः शैलपीडानिमित्तजः। पृथिवीं पूरयामास दिशश्चोपवनानि च॥ शिरोभिः पृथुभिर्नागा व्यक्तस्वस्तिकलत्तणैः। वमन्तः पावकं घोरं ददंशुर्दशनैः शिलाः॥
en: Heavy boulders rolled down with large blocks of red-arsenic; then the hill looked like the smoke of a burning flame. Beasts and birds shrieked in fear and ran in every direction and the snakes reissuing their spacious hoods began to bite at the rocks, as if they vomited fire in anger.

sn: तास्तदा सविषैर्दष्टाः कुपितैस्तैर्महाशिलाः जज्वलुः पावकोद्दीप्ता विभिदुश्च सहस्रधा॥
en: Big rocks bit by those snakes crumbled into pieces and those fragments began to burn with fire-like venom.

sn: यानि त्वौषधजालानि तस्मिञ्जातानि पर्वते। विषघ्नान्यपि नागानां न शेकुः शमितुं विषम्॥
en: Although there were many medical herbs, capable of counteracting poison, which had sprung up on that mountain, could not neutralise that poison of the snakes.

sn: भिद्यतेऽयं गिरिधूतैरिति मत्वा तपस्विनः। त्रस्ता विद्याधरास्तस्मादुत्पेतुः स्त्रीगणैः सह ॥ पानभूमिगतं हित्वा हैममासवभाजनम्। पात्राणि च महार्हाणि करकांश्च हिरण्मयान्॥ लेह्यानुच्चावचान् भक्ष्यान् मांसानि विविधानि च। आर्षभाणि च चर्माणि खङ्गांश्च कनकत्सरून्॥ कृतकण्ठगुणाः क्षीबा रक्तमाल्यानुलेपनाः। रक्ताक्षाः पुष्कराक्षाश्च गगनं प्रतिपेदिरे॥ हारनूपुरकेयूरपारिहार्यधराः स्त्रियः। विस्मिताः सस्मितास्तस्थुराकाशे रमणैः सह ॥
en: At this sudden convulsion, the hermits thought that they were being driven by the Rākşasas. The Vidyādharas with their woman ran away from their drinking haunts, leaving their golden seats, goblets, bowls, delicious articles for chewing, various kinds of meat, oxen, hides and swords with golden hilts. Fair damsels wearing necklaces, bracelets, anklets and carnation garlands, besmeared with red sandal paste and with their eyes red with wine dallying in amorous sports being startled by this strange occurrence, with their lovers, rose in the sky and watched the thing with delightful curiosity from above.

sn: एष पर्वतसंकाशो हनुमान् मारुतात्मजः। तितीर्षति महावेगः समुद्रं वरुणालयम्॥ रामार्थं वानरार्थं च चिकीर्षन् कर्म दुष्करम्। समुद्रस्य परं पारं दुष्प्रापं प्राप्तुमिच्छति॥
en: Looking like a mountain, the hermits thought about Hanumān, son of wind-god, undertaken for the benefit of Rāma and Vānaras in general, and blessed that he would be able to cross the ocean, the abode of Varuņa easily.

sn: इति विद्याधरा वाचः श्रुत्वा तेषां तपस्विनाम्। तमप्रमेयं ददृशुः पर्वते वानरर्षभम्॥
en: Hearing this from the hermits, the Vidyādharas were struck with wonder and they repeatedly looked at Hanumān.

sn: दुधुवे च स रोमाणि चकम्पे चानलोपमः। ननाद च महानादं सुमहानिव तोयदः॥
en: Meanwhile the fire-like mighty hero trembled in his limbs and his hairs stood on their ends, and he roared like the rumbling of a cloud.

sn: आनुपूर्त्यां च वृत्तं तल्लाङ्गलं रोममिश्रितम्। उत्पतिष्यन् विचिक्षेप पक्षिराज इवोरगम्॥ तस्य लाङ्गलमाविद्धमतिवेगस्य पृष्टतः। ददृशे गरुडेनेव ह्रियमाणो महोरगः॥
en: He lashed his roundish tail covered with down and again on his back just to get ready for the spring. It seemed as if Garuda, the king of the birds, was flying off with a huge snake.

sn: बाहू संस्तम्भयामास महापरिघसंनिभौ। आससाद कपिः कट्यां चरणौ संकुकोच॥ संहृत्य च भुजौ श्रीमांस्तथैव च शिरोधराम्। तेजः सत्त्वं तथा वीर्यमाविवेश स वीर्यवान् ॥
en: The monkey firmly planted his arins like bolts, on the mountain; then crouched at the waist and contracted his legs. Contracting his arms, neck and abdomen He, the glorious and powerful Hanumān then, mustered his strengh.

sn: मार्गमालोकयन् दूरादूर्ध्वप्रणिहितेक्षणः। रुरोध हृदये प्राणानाकाशमवलोकयन्॥ पद्भ्यां दृढमवस्थानां कृत्वा स कपिकुञ्जरः। निकुच्य को हनुमानुत्पतिष्यन् महाबलः॥ वानरान् वानरश्रेष्ठ इदं वचनमब्रवीत्।
en: He looked up to survey the distance, he suspended his breath in the heart while looking into sky. Then doing firm his feet and contracting his ears in order to spring, addressing other Vanaras, mighty Hanuman said.

sn: यथा राघवनिर्मुक्तः शरः श्वसनविक्रमः॥ गच्छेत् तद्वद् गमिष्यामि लङ्कां रावणपालिताम्। नहि द्रक्ष्यामि यदि तां लङ्कायां जनकात्मजाम्॥ अनेनैव हि वेगेन गमिष्यामि सुरालयम्।
en: I shall reach Lankā with the velocity of wind, just like an arrow shot by Rāma and if I do not find Jānakī there I shall, at the same speed, go to the region of the gods.

sn: यदि वा त्रिदिवे सीतां न द्रक्ष्यामि कृतश्रमः॥ बद्ध्वा राक्षसराजानमानयिष्यामि रावणम्। सर्वथा कृतकार्योऽहमेष्यामि सह सीतया॥ आनयिष्यामि वा लङ्कां समुत्पाट्य सरावणाम्।
en: If I do not see Sītā in heaven even after exerting myself, I shall bring Ravana, the ruler of Raksasas, in bondage. At anyway with success, I shall come with Sītā or then I shall bring Lankā uprooting it with Rāvana.

sn: एवमुक्त्वा तु हनुमान् वानरो वानरोत्तमः॥ उत्पपाताथ वेगेन वेगवानविचारयन्। सुपर्णमिव चात्मानं मेने स कपिकुञ्जरः॥ समुत्पतति वेगात् तु वेगात् ते नगरोहिणः। संहृत्य विटपान् सर्वान् समुत्पेतुः समन्ततः॥
en: With these words, Hanumān who was full of vigour, sprang into the air accounted himself like a compeer of Garuda. As he flew up with vehemence, trees growing on the mountain, were uprooted from all sides.

sn: स मत्तकोयष्टिभकान् पादपान् पुष्पशालिनः। उद्वहन्नुरुवेगेन जगाम विमलेऽम्बरे॥ ऊरुवेगोत्थिता वृक्षा मुहूर्त कपिमन्वयुः। प्रस्थितं दीर्घमध्वानं स्वबन्धुमिव बान्धवाः॥ तमूरुवेगोन्मथिताः सालाश्चान्ये नगोत्तमाः। अनुजग्मुर्हनूमन्तं सैन्या इव महीपतिम्॥
en: Hanumān coursed through the sky along with these trees, borne up by the violence of his flight. The ſala and palm trees went after him for a short time as people follow their friends bound for a distant land, or as the troops follow their king.

sn: सुपुष्पिताग्रैर्बहुभिः पादपैरन्वितः कपिः। हनूमान् पर्वताकारो बभूवाद्भुतदर्शनः॥ सारवन्तोऽथ ये वृक्षा न्यमज्जल्लवणाम्भसि। भयादिव महेन्द्रस्य पर्वता वरुणालये॥
en: Hanumān thus being covered with buds and blossoms looked like a hill lit up with glowworms. Then the heavy trees being deprived of their flowers by the velocity of the flight began to drop down into the sea like mountains bode, afflicted with the fear of Mahendra.

sn: स नानाकुसुमैः कोर्णः कपिः साङ्करकोरकैः। शुशुभे मेघसंकाशः खद्योतैरिव पर्वतः॥
en: And strewn with various sprouts and buds and blossoms, the monkey resembling a mass of clouds, looked lovely like a bill filled with glowworms.

sn: विमुक्तास्तस्य वेगेन मुक्त्वा पुष्पाणि ते दुमाः। व्यवशीर्यन्त सलिले निवृत्ताः सुहृदो यथा।५० ।।
en: And uprooted by the force of his rush, mose trees, their flowers fallen off, plunged into the sea, like friends returning to their homes (after having accompanied their friend some way).

sn: लघुत्वेनोपपन्नं तद् विचित्रं सागरेऽपतत्। दुमाणां विविधं पुष्पं कपिवायुसमीरितम्॥ पुष्पौघेण सुगन्धेन नानावर्णेन वानरः। बभौ मेघ इवोद्यन् वै विद्युद्गणविभूषितः॥
en: And blown by the wind caused by the a monkey, the various variegated flowers of the trees the consequence of their lightness, showered down on the sea. And covered with heaps of fragrant flowers of diverse hues, the monkey resembled a mass of clouds embellished by lines of lightning

sn: तस्य वेगसमुद्भूतैः पुष्पैस्तोयमदृश्यत। ताराभिरिव रामाभिरुदिताभिरिवाम्बरम्॥ तस्याम्बरगतौ बाहू ददृशाते प्रसारितौ। पर्वताग्राद् विनिष्क्रान्तौ पञ्चास्याविव पन्नगौ॥
en: The waters of the ocean) strewn with blossoms carried off by his motion, operated like the sky garnished with charming stars (cresting the same). His arms stretched in the sky, seemed like five-hooded snakes issuing from mountain.

sn: पिबन्निव बभौ चापि सोर्मिजालं महार्णवम्। पिपासुरिव चाकाशं ददृशे स महाकपिः॥
en: He appeared as if he was drinking up the mightily deep with its multitudes of waves, or as if that redoubtable monkey was desirous of sucking up the sky itself.

sn: तस्य विद्युत्प्रभाकारे वायुमार्गानुसारिणः। नयने विप्रकाशेते पर्वतस्थाविवानलौ।५६।।
en: As he coursed the orbit of air, his eyes flashing like lightning, resembled two craters a glow on a mountain.

sn: पिङ्गे पिङ्गाक्षमुख्यस्य बृहती परिमण्डले। चक्षुषी सम्प्रकाशेते चन्द्रसूर्याविव स्थितौ॥
en: And the eyes of that foremost of tawny-hued ones resembled the sun and the moon stationed in a vast yellow aureola.

sn: मुखं नासिकया तस्य ताम्रया ताम्रमाबभौ। सन्ध्यया समभिस्पृष्टं यथा स्यात् सूर्यमण्डलम्॥ लाङ्गूलं च समाविद्धं प्लवमानस्य शोभते। अम्बरे वायुपुत्रस्य शक्रध्वज इवोच्छ्रितम्॥
en: Beside his coppery nose, his face looked coppery, as looks the solar disc on the approach of eve. And the uplifted tail of the Wind-god's offspring engaged in bounding, appeared beautiful in the sky like the raised standard of Sakra.

sn: लाङ्गलचक्रो हनुमाशुकल्दंष्ट्रोऽनिलात्मजः। व्यरोचत महाप्राज्ञः परिवेषीव भास्करः॥
en: The exceedingly wise son of the Wind, Hanumān, having white teeth, with his tail coiled up, looked handsome like the sun with his disc.

sn: स्फिग्देशेनातितामेण रराज स महाकपिः। महता दारितेनेव गिरिगैरिकधातुना॥
en: On account of his waist being deeply coppery that mighty monkey appeared like a mountain running, mighty torrent mixed with minerals and red chalk.

sn: तस्य वानरसिंहस्य प्लवमानस्य सागरम्। कक्षान्तरगतो वायुर्जीमूत इव गर्जति॥
en: The wind that had got into the armpits of that leonine monkey who was crossing over the main, roar like clouds.

sn: खे यथा निपतत्युल्का उत्तरान्ताद् विनिःसृता। दृश्यते सानुबन्धा च तथा स कपिकुञ्जरः॥
en: As a meteor consisting of many smaller ones, darting from above fall down (to the earth), rushed on that foremost of monkeys.

sn: पतत्पतङ्गसंकाशो व्यायतः शुशुभे कपिः। प्रवृद्ध इव मातङ्गः कक्ष्यया बध्यमानया॥
en: Then that stalwart monkey resembling the careering sun, resembled a mad elephant fettered by the middle, whose bulk has increased immensely.

sn: उपरिष्टाच्छरीरेण च्छायया चावगाढया। सागरे मारुताविष्टा नौरिवासीत् तदा कपिः॥
en: As he coursed above, on account of the reflection cast by his body (on the boson of the deep), the monkey* by his progress, looked link a bark swayed by the breeze. *Under water.

sn: यं यं देशं समुद्रस्य जगाम स महिकपिः। स तु तस्याङ्गवेगेन सोन्माद इव लक्ष्यते॥
en: And wherever that mighty monkey went about the sea, the state of things appeared to undergo a violent convulsion owing to impetus imparted by his body.

sn: सागरस्योर्मिजालानामुरसा शैलवर्मणाम्। अभिघ्नंस्तु महावेगः पुप्लुवे स महाकपिः॥
en: That mighty monkey possessed of exceeding speed rushed on, raising multitudes of surges on the sea by his breast resembling rock.

sn: कपिवातश्च बलवान् मेघवातश्च निर्गतः। सागरं भीमनिर्हादं कम्पयामासतु शम्॥
en: And the wind begot of the monkey as well as that of the clouds, issuing out, made the dreadsounding ocean roll violently.

sn: विकर्षर्मिजालानि बृहन्ति लवणाम्भसि। पुष्लुवे कपिशार्दूलो विकिरनिव रोदसी॥
en: Pushing up multitudes of high-heaving billows from the salt waters, that tiger-like monkey rushed on separating earth and heaven.

sn: मेरुमन्दरसंकाशानुद्रतान् सुमहार्णवे। अत्यक्रामन्महावेगस्तरङ्गान् गणयन्निव॥
en: And that one endued with vehement speed passed over surges in the mighty main resembling Mandara or Meru; as if counting them.

sn: तस्य वेगसमुघुष्टं जलं सजलदं तदा। अम्बरस्थं विबभ्राजे शरदभ्रमिराततम्।७१।।
en: The waters lashed up to the clouds by the force (of his speed), looked like autumnal clouds overspreading the sky.

sn: तिमिनक्रझषा: कूर्मा दृश्यन्ते विवृतास्तदा। वस्त्रापकर्षणेनेव शरीराणि शरीरिणाम्॥
en: Then whales and alligators and fishes and tortoises appeared plainly visible, like the persons of individuals, when the cloth has been taken off then.

sn: क्रममाणं समीक्ष्याथ भुजगाः सागरंगमाः। व्योम्नि तं कपिशार्दूलं सुपर्णमिव मेनिरे॥
en: And sea-serpents, seeing that tiger-like monkey proceeding in the sky, took him for Suparna himself.

sn: दशयोजनविस्तीर्णा त्रिंशद्योजनमायता। छाया वानरसिंहस्य जवे चारुतराभवत्॥
en: The shadow the leonine monkey, measuring ten Yojanas in width and thirty in length, seemed the handsome in consequence of his speed.

sn: श्वेताभ्रघनराजीव वायुपुत्रानुगामिनी। तस्य सा शुशुभे छाया पतिता लवणाम्भसि॥
en: That shadow resembling masses of white clouds, rallying on the salt waters and following the wind-god's son, seemed exceedingly beautiful. on more

sn: शुशुभे स महातेजा महाकायो महाकपिः। वायुमार्गे निरालम्बे पक्षवानिव पर्वतः॥
en: And that exceedingly energetic highly monkey possessed of a gigantic body, appeared splendid in the unsupported aerial way, like a winged mountain.

sn: येनासौ याति बलवान् वेगेन कपिकुञ्जरः। तेन मार्गेण सहसा द्रोणीकृत इवार्णवः॥
en: And the deep beside the course that was being vehemently pursued by that elephantine monkey, was suddenly urned into a water-course.* *The sense is hard to hit. The commentator says, that agitated by Hanuman's peed, the clouds began to pour down showers on the ocean.

sn: आपाते पक्षिसङ्घानां पक्षिराज इव व्रजन्। हनुमान् मेघजालानि प्रकर्षन् मारुतो यथा॥
en: And coursing through the regions of fowls like the monarch of the feathered race, Hanuman, pushing away masses of clouds, resembled the wind himself.

sn: पाण्डुरारुणवर्णानि नीलमञ्जिष्ठकानि च। कपिनाऽऽकृष्यमाणानि महाभ्राणि चकाशिरे॥
en: And colossal clouds scattered by the monkey, pale and crimson and blue and mangistha-hued, looked exceedingly lovely.

sn: प्रविशन्नभ्रजालीनि निष्पतंश्च पुनः पुनः। प्रच्छन्नश्च प्रकाशश्च चन्द्रमा इव दृश्यते॥
en: And now entering into the clouds, and now emerging from them, he looked like the moon, sometimes hid and sometimes visible.

sn: प्लवमानं त तं दृष्ट्वा प्लवगं त्वरितं तदा। ववृषुस्तत्र पुष्पाणि देवगन्धर्वदानवाः॥
en: Beholding that monkey engaged in bounding with celerity, gods, Gandharvas and Dānavas began to strew blossoms (on him).

sn: तताप नहि तं सूर्यः प्लवन्तं वानरेश्वरम्। सिषेवे च तदा वायू रामकार्यार्थसिद्धये॥
en: As he was leaping, the Sun did not burn him; and the Wind ministered to him, for the success of Rāma's work.

sn: ऋषयस्तुष्टुवुश्चैनं प्लवमानं विहायसा। जगुश्च देवगन्धर्वाः प्रशंसन्तो वनौकसम्॥
en: And the saints hymned his praises, as he was leaping on in the sky. And applauding the ranger of forests, they raised the voice of song.

sn: नागाश्च तुष्टुवुर्यक्षा रक्षांसि विविधानि च। प्रेक्ष्य सर्वे कपिवरं सहसा विगतक्लमम् ॥
en: Nagas and Yaksas, and various (races of) Raksasas, eulogized (him), on beholding that tiger-like monkey, Hanumān, in the act of bounding.

sn: तस्मिन् प्लवगशार्दूले प्लवमाने हनूमति। इक्ष्वाकुकुलमानार्थी चिन्तयामास सागरः॥
en: Hanumān, that lord of monkeys, being engaged in the act of bounding, the Ocean, who sought to do honour to the race of Ikşvāku within himself.

sn: साहाय्यं वानरेन्द्रस्य यदि नाहं हनूमतः। करिष्यामि भविष्यामि सर्ववाच्यो विवक्षताम्॥
en: He said himself, ‘Truly shall I be blamed of all persons if I do not assist this lord of monkeys-Hanumān.'

sn: अहमिक्ष्वाकुनाथेन सगरेण विवर्धितः। इक्ष्वाकुसचिवश्चायं तन्नार्हत्यवसादितुम्॥
en: Reared I have been by Sagara, the foremost of the race of the Ikşvākus and this monkey is their counsellor. It therefore dose not behove me to tire him out.

sn: तथा मया विधातव्यं विश्रमेत यथा कपिः। शेषं च मयि विश्रान्तः सुखी सोऽतितरिष्यति॥
en: It become me to do that by which the monkey may take rest in me and, relieved, may happily traverse the remaining way.

sn: इति कृत्वा मतिं साध्वी समुद्रश्छन्नमम्भसि। हिरण्यनाभं मैनाकमुवाच गिरिसत्तमम्॥
en: Having arrived at this wholesome resolution, the Ocean spake upto that best of mountains, Maināka, hued in gold and situate in the waters, saying.

sn: त्वमिहासुरसङ्घानां देवराज्ञा महात्मना। पातालनिलयानां हि परिघः संनिवेशितः॥
en: O lord, you had been placed here by the king of celestials as an outer gate against the Asuras inhabiting the region under the earth.

sn: त्वमेषां ज्ञातवीर्याणां पुरनेवोत्पतिष्यताम्। पातालस्याप्रमेयस्य द्वारमावृत्य तिष्ठसि॥
en: You too, from then, had been waiting at this gate, unapproachable by the Asuras, rising up again and again and whose prowess is wellknown (to the Lord of celestials)

sn: तिर्यगूर्ध्वमधश्चैव शक्तिस्ते शैल वर्धितुम्। तस्मात् संचोदयामि त्वामुत्तिष्ठ गिरिसत्तम॥
en: O mountain, you are capable of expanding yourself upwards, downwards and on they sides. I do command you therefore, O best of mountains, to rise up.

sn: स एष कपिशार्दूलस्त्वामुपर्येति वीर्यवान्। हनूमान् रामकार्यार्थी भीमकर्मा खमाप्लुतः। श्रमं च प्लवगेन्द्रस्य समीक्ष्योत्थातुमर्हसि॥
en: That best of monkeys, the energetic Hanumān, the performer of mighty deeds, engaged in Rāma's service, worn out with fatigue, wait above you. Beholding the exhaustion of that leader of monkeys, it behove you to rise up.

sn: हिरण्यगर्भो मैनाको निशम्य लवणाम्भसः। उत्पपात जलात् तूर्णं महादुमलतावृतः॥
en: Hearing the speech of the Ocean, the golden mountain Maināka, covered with tall trees and creepers, rose up instantly from his watery bed.

sn: स सागरजलं भित्वा बभूवात्युच्छ्रितस्तदा। यथा जलधरं भित्त्वा दीमरश्मिर्दिवाकरः॥
en: Like to the Sun of bright rays rising out of the watery expanse, he uplifted himself from the Ocean.

sn: स महात्मा मुहूर्तेन पर्वतः सलिलावृतः। दर्शयामास शृङ्गाणि सागरेण नियोजितः॥
en: Being thus commanded by the Ocean, the great mountain, covered on all sides with water, immediately brought forth his peaks.

sn: शातकुम्भमयैः शृङ्गैः सकिंनरमहोरगैः। आदित्योदयसंकाशैरुल्लिखद्भिरिवाम्बरम्॥
en: The sky was as if cleft by these golden summits like to the rising of the Sun, inhabited by Kinnaras and large Serpents.

sn: तस्य जाम्बूनदैः शृङ्गः पर्वतस्य समुत्थितैः। आकाशं शस्त्रसंकाशमभवत् काञ्चनप्रभम्॥ जातरूपमयैः शृङ्गैः भ्राजमानैर्महाप्रभैः। आदित्यशतसंकाशः सोऽभवद् गिरिसत्तमः॥
en: To golden summits of that mountain being thus lifted up, the dark-blue sky assumed the golden hue. And by those highly resplendent golden peaks that best of mountains assumed the brilliance of a thousand suns.

sn: समुत्थितमसङ्गेन हनूमानग्रतः स्थितम्। मध्ये लवणतोयस्य विघ्नोऽयमिति निश्चितः॥
en: Beholding before him that up-heaved mountain in the midst of the salt Ocean Hanumān regarded it, as a barrier for aye.

sn: स तमुच्छ्रितमत्यर्थं महावेगो महाकपिः। उरसा पातयामास जीमूतमिव मारुतः॥
en: Like to Wind dispersing clouds, that mighty monkey with great velocity crushed down those up-lifted peaks with his breast.

sn: स तदासादितस्तेन कपिना पर्वतोत्तमः। बुद्ध्वा तस्य हरेर्वेगं जहर्ष च ननाद च॥
en: Being thus crushed down by that monkey, the best of mountains, being apprized of his prowess, began to shout with joy.

sn: तमाकाशगतं वीरमाकाशे समुपस्थितः। प्रीतो हृष्टमना वाक्यमब्रवीत् पर्वतः कपिम्॥ मानुषं धारयन् रूपमात्मनः शिखरे स्थितः।
en: Thereupon, with a glad heart assuming the semblance of a man ånd stationing himself upon his own summit, that mountain-chief addressed Hanumān, saying.

sn: दुष्करं कृतवान् कर्म त्वमिदं वानरोत्तम्॥ निपत्य मम शृङ्गेषु सुखं विश्रम्य गम्यताम्।
en: O best of monkeys, forsooth had you been engaged in this arduous task. Coming down on my peak do you take rest.

sn: राघवस्य कुले जातैरुदधिः परिवर्धितः॥ स त्वां रामहिते युक्तं प्रत्यर्चयति सागरः।
en: This ocean was reared by one born in the family of Raghus. And beholding you engaged on Rāma's behoof he is worshipping you.

sn: कृते च प्रतिकर्तव्यमेष धर्मः सनातनः॥ सोऽयं तत्प्रतिकारार्थी त्वत्तः सम्मानमर्हति।
en: The best and everlasting virtue consists in returning benefits to one who has benefited us. Bent on returning benefits to Raghu's race, he deserve respect from you.

sn: त्वन्निमित्तमनेनाहं बहुमानात् प्रचोदितः॥ योजनानां शतं चापि कपिरेष खमाप्लुतः। तव सानुषु विश्रान्तः शेषं प्रक्रमतामिति ॥
en: And to welcome you properly I have been despatched by him with the message-traversing over a hundred yojans this monkey has been worn out with fatigue; let him voyage to the remaining way after resting for a while on your summit.

sn: तिष्ठ त्वं हरिशार्दूल मयि विश्रम्य गम्यताम्। तदितं गन्धवत् स्वादु कन्दमूलफलं बहु॥ तदास्वाद्य हरिश्रेष्ठ विश्रान्तोऽथ गमिष्यसि।
en: Do you therefore, O best of monkeys, remain here and take rest. And feasting on these many fragrant and sweet fruits and roots, O foremost of monkeys, do you relieve yourself of the toil and proceed.

sn: अस्माकमपि सम्बन्धः कपिमुख्य त्वयास्ति वै। प्रख्यातस्त्रिषु लोकेषु महागुणपरिग्रहः॥
en: O leader of monkeys, my relation with you is replete with many virtues and known all over the three worlds.

sn: वेगवन्तः प्लवन्तो ये प्लवगा मारुतात्मज । तेषां मुख्यतमं मन्ये त्वामहं कपिकुञ्जर ॥
en: O Son of Maruta, O best of monkeys, I know you to be the foremost of all monkeys.

sn: अतिथिः किल पूजार्हः प्राकृतोऽपि विजानता। धर्मे जिज्ञासमानेन किं पुनर्यादृशो भवान् ॥
en: Even an ordinary guest should be adored by him who abide by virtue, what of you great as you are?

sn: त्वं हि देववरिष्ठस्य मारुतस्य महात्मनः। पुत्रस्तस्यैव वेगेन सदृशः कपिकुञ्जर॥
en: O you lion among monkeys, you are the son of Māruta, the foremost of celestials and are his equal in speed.

sn: पूजिते त्वयि धर्मज्ञे पूजां प्राप्नोति मारुतः। तस्मात् त्वं पूजनीयो मे शृणु चाप्यत्र कारणम्॥
en: You that are conversant with virtue, being worshipped, Maruta himself receive offerings. You are therefore worth of my adoration. Hearken, there is another reason for it.

sn: पूर्वं कृतयुगे तात पर्वताः पक्षिणोऽभवन्। तेऽपि जग्मुर्दिशः सर्वा गरुडा इव वेगिनः॥
en: O worshipful one, in olden times, the mountains, gifted with wings, began to range all quarters with velocity like to Garuda.

sn: ततस्तेषु प्रयातेषु देवसङ्घाः सहर्षिभिः। भूतानि च भयं जग्मुस्तेषां पतनशङ्कया॥
en: They moving thus, the celestials, the ascetics, and all creatures became almost faint with fear of their falling down.

sn: ततः क्रुद्धः सहस्राक्षः पर्वतानां शतक्रतुः। पक्षांश्चिच्छेद वज्रेण ततः शतसहस्रशः॥
en: Highly enraged therefore, the thousand-eyed Deity, the performer of hundred sacrifices, hundred with his thunderbolt, the wings of hundreds and thousands of them.

sn: स मामुपगतः क्रुद्धो वज्रमुद्यम्य देवराट्। ततोऽहं सहसा क्षिप्तः श्वसनेन महात्मना॥
en: When with his thunderbolt, the Lord of celestials, wroth, approached me, I was all on a sudden thrown down by the high-souled Wind.

sn: अस्मिल्लवणतोये च प्रक्षिप्तः प्लवगोत्तम। गुप्तपक्षः समग्रश्च तव पित्राभिरक्षितः॥
en: O best of monkeys I was these cast done in this salt ocean and preserved unhurt by your ancestors having my wings hid.

sn: ततोऽहं मानयामि त्वां मान्योऽसि मम मारुते। त्वया ममैष सम्बन्धः कपिमुख्य महागुणः॥
en: I shall therefore adore you and you are object of my worship O Maruta! And this my relation with you, O foremost of monkeys, is pregnant with many virtues.

sn: अस्मिन्नेवंगते कार्ये सागरस्य ममैव च। प्रीतिं प्रीतिमनाः कर्तुं त्वमर्हसि महामते॥
en: The time for returning benefits having arrived, O high-souled one, it behove you to afford me and the ocean, satisfaction with a blessed heart.

sn: श्रमं मोक्षय पूजां च गृहाण हरिसत्तम। प्रीतिं च मम मान्यस्य प्रीतोऽस्मि तव दर्शनात्॥
en: best of monkeys, relieve yourself of the fatigue and accept my affectionate offering, who am worthy of your respect. For his relationship with Wind whose son was Pitupanthānam-the text means "his father's path”-Wind being Hanumān's father the passage means-"aerial way."-Happy am I to see you. *Wrath in consequence of his inability to accept his offerings.

sn: एवमुक्तः कपिश्रेष्ठस्तं नगोत्तममब्रवीत्। प्रीतोऽस्मि कृतमातिथ्यं मन्युरेषोऽपनीयताम्॥
en: Being thus accosted by Maināka, the best of mountains, Hanumān, the foremost of monkeys said, saying: Pleased am I and you had shown me enough of hospitality. Do you give up your wrath.

sn: त्वरते कार्यकाले मे अहश्चाप्यतिवर्तते। प्रतिज्ञा च मया दत्ता न स्थातव्यमिहान्तरा॥
en: Business wants me to go soon and the time is well-nigh spent. Besides I have promised that I shall not halt at any intermediate place.

sn: इत्युक्त्वा पाणिना शैलमालभ्य हरिपुङ्गवः। जगामाकाशमाविश्य वीर्यवान् प्रसहनिव॥
en: Thereupon touching the hill with his hand that highly energetic monkey wended, smiling his aerial way. Ocean

sn: स पर्वतसमुद्राभ्यां बहुमानादवेक्षितः। पूजितश्चोपपन्नाभिराशीर्भिरभिनन्दितः॥
en: Thereat the and the mountain respectfully looked towards him and adored and welcomed him with blessings worthy of the occasion.

sn: अथोर्ध्वं दूरमागत्य हित्वा शैलमहार्णवौ। पितुः पन्थानमासाद्य जगाम विमलेऽम्बरे॥
en: Leaving the mountain and the ocean and rising his up, he proceeded in the clear welkin traversing the aerial way.

sn: भूयश्चोर्ध्वं गतिं प्राप्य गिरं तमवलोकयन्। वायुसूनुर्निरालम्बो जगाम कपिकुञ्जरः॥
en: Rising high up and casting his look down on the hill, that foremost of monkeys proceeded by the unsupported aerial track.

sn: तद् द्वितीयं हनुमतो दृष्ट्वा कर्म सुदुष्करम्। प्रशशंसुः सुराः सर्वे सिद्धाश्च परमर्षयः॥
en: Beholding this singularly arduous work of Hanumān the celestials, the Siddhas and the ascetics all praised him.

sn: देवताश्चाभवन् हृष्टास्तत्रस्थास्तस्य कर्मणा। काञ्चनस्य सुनाभस्य सहस्राक्षश्च वासवः॥
en: All the celestials and others living on its summit, were highly pleased with the mountain arrayed in gold and having beautiful sides.

sn: उवाच वचनं धीमान् परितोषात् सगद्गदम्। सुनाभं पर्वतश्रेष्ठं स्वयमेव शचीपतिः॥
en: And the thousand-eyed Vásava was also pleased. And greatly pleased that highly intelligent Saci's lord, himself, addressed that best of mountains having picturesque sides, saying.

sn: हिरण्यनाभ शैलेन्द्र परितुष्टोऽस्मि ते भृशम्। अभयं ते प्रयच्छामि गच्छ सौम्य यथासुखम्॥
en: Greatly delighted am I, O lord of mountains, O you having golden peaks. 'No fear' I do declare to you. Proceedest you therefore, at your ease, O gently one!

sn: साह्यं कृतं ते सुमहद् विश्रान्तस्य हनूमतः। क्रमतो योजनशतं निर्भरस्य भये सति ॥
en: Greatly had you hoped Hanumān, crossin fearlessly an unceasingly, over hundred yojanas so that he might not fall in danger.

sn: रामस्यैव हितायैष याति दाशरथेः कपिः। सत्क्रियां कुर्वता शक्त्या तोषितोऽस्मि दृढं त्वया।१३४
en: This monkey, is going in the interests of Rāma, Dasaratha's son—and you had welcomed him to the best of your mighty. Therefore I am greatly pleased with you.

sn: स तत् प्रहर्षमलभद् विपुलं पर्वतोत्तमः। देवतानां पतिं दृष्ट्वा परितुष्टं शतक्रतुम्॥
en: Beholding that lord of celestials the performer of an hundred sacrifices, highly gratified, that best of mountains attained to an excess of joy.

sn: स वै दत्तवरः शैलो बभूवावस्थितस्तदा। हनूमांश्च मुहूर्तेन व्यतिचक्राम सागरम्॥
en: Having received boons (from Indra) the Mountain occupied again its pristine place. And Hanumān in a short time crossed over the main.

sn: ततो देवाः सगन्धर्वाः सिद्धाश्च परमर्षयः। अब्रुवन् सूर्यसंकाशां सुरसां नागमातरम्॥
en: Thereupon the celestial along with Gandharvas, Siddhas and the ascetics, spake to Surasā the mother of serpents, resembling the Sun, saying.

sn: अयं वातात्मजः श्रीमान् प्लवते सागरोपरि। हनूमान् नाम तस्य त्वं मुहूर्तं विघ्नमाचर॥
en: The highly effulgent son of Wind named Hanumān is crossing over the main. You are required to throw obstacles in his way for a while.

sn: राक्षसं रूपमास्थाय सुघोरं पर्वतोपमम्। दंष्ट्राकरालं पिङ्गाक्षं वक्त्रं कृत्वा नभःस्पृशम्॥
en: Assuming therefore the semblance of a terrible, grim-visaged Rāksasa, resembling a huge mountain and having terrible teeth and a face with coppery eyes, do you touch the welkin.

sn: बलमिच्छामहे ज्ञातुं भूयश्चास्य पराक्रमम्। त्वां विजेष्यत्युपायेन विषादं वा गमिष्यति॥
en: We are anxious to learn if he defeat you by some means or comes by grief."

sn: एवमुक्ता तु सा देवी दैवतैरभिसत्कृता। समुद्रमध्ये सुरसा बिभ्रती राक्षसं वपुः॥ विकृतं च विरूपं च सर्वस्य च भयावहम्। प्लवमानं हनूमन्तमावृत्येदमुवाच ह॥
en: Thus addressed the worshipful Surasā, having been honoured by the celestials, deformed and horrible and capable of exciting the fear of all beings, and obstructing Hanumān as he was coursing on, said.

sn: मम भक्ष्यः प्रदिष्टस्त्वमीश्वरैर्वानरर्षभ। अहं त्वां भक्षयिष्यामि प्रविशेदं ममाननम्॥
en: O foremost of monkeys, you had been ordained as my fare by the gods themselves. I will eat you up, do you enter my mouth.

sn: वर एष पुरा दत्तो मम धात्रेति सत्वरा। व्यादाय वक्त्रं विपुलं स्थिता सा मारुतेः पुरः॥
en: Even this is the boon that was conferred on me by the Deity. Having delivered herself thus, speedily, she was opening her mouth wide, stood before the son of the wind god.

sn: अथवा मैथिली एवमुक्तः सुरसया प्रहृष्टवदनोऽब्रवीत्। रामो दाशरथिर्नाम प्रविष्टो दण्डकावनम्। लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्रात्रा वैदेह्या चापि भार्यया॥
en: Thus accosted by Surasā, (Hanumān) with a glad countenance, said, Rama, son to Dasaratha, had entered the Dandaka forest in company with his brother, Lakşmaņa, and his wife, Vaidehi.

sn: अस्य कार्यविषक्तस्य बद्धवैरस्य राक्षसैः। तस्य सीता हृता भार्या रावणेन यशस्विनी॥
en: He having created hostility with the Rākṣasas, his illustrious wife, Sītā, while he was engrossed in some work, was carried away by Ravana.

sn: तस्याः सकाशं दूतोऽहं गमिष्ये रामशासनात्। कर्तुमर्हसि रामस्य साह्यं विषयवासिनि॥
en: At Rāma's command, I go to her as his envoy. It behove you, living in (Rāma's) dominions, to lend him your help.

sn: दृष्ट्वा रामं चाक्लिष्टकारिणम्। आगमिष्यामि ते वक्त्रं सत्यं प्रतिशृणोमि ते॥
en: Or having seen Mithila's daughter, as well as Rāma of untiring deeds, I will enter your mouth. This I promise you truly."

sn: एवमुक्ता हनुमता सुरसा कामरूपिणी। अब्रवीन्नातिवर्तेन्मां कश्चिदेष वरो मम॥
en: Thus addressed by Hanumān, Surasā, capable of wearing forms at will, said, “None shall pass me without being devoured by me, even this is the boon that I have received."

sn: तं प्रयान्तं समुद्वीक्ष्य सुरसा वाक्यमब्रवीत्। बलं जिज्ञासमाना सा नागमाता हनूमतः॥
en: Then seeing him go away, the mother of the Nāgās, Surasā, desirous of essaying the strength of Hanuman, spoke.

sn: निविश्य वदनं मेऽद्य गन्तव्यं वानरोत्तम। वर एष पुरा दत्तो मम धात्रेति सत्वरा ॥ व्यादाय विपुलं वक्त्रं स्थिता सा मारुतेः पुरः।
en: O best of monkeys, you shall have to go, today after entering my mouth. Even this is the boon that was conferred on me by the Deity. Having said this swiftly, she extending her capacious mouth wide, stood in front of the wind-god's son.

sn: एवमुक्तः सुरसया क्रुद्धो वानरपुंगवः॥ अब्रवीत् कुरु वै वक्त्रं येन मां विषहिष्यसि। इत्युक्त्वा सुरसां क्रुद्धो दशयोजनमायताम्॥ दशयोजनविस्तारो हनूमानभवत् तदा। चकार सुरसाप्यास्यं विंशद्योजनमायतम्॥
en: Thus addressed by Surasā, that foremost of monkeys, waxing wroth, said, “Extend your mouth so, that you may contain me." Having said this to Surasā, having her mouth measuring ten yojanas, Hanumān enlarged himself as many yojanas. Thereat-Surasā enlarged her mouth twenty yojanas.

sn: (चकार सुरसा वक्त्रं चत्वारिंशत् तथोच्छ्रितम्। बभूव हनुमान् वीरः पञ्चाशद् योजनोच्छ्रितः। चकार सुरसा वक्त्रं षष्टिं योजनमुच्छ्रितम्।। तदैव हनुमान् वीरः सप्ततिं योजनोच्छ्रितः। चकार सुरसा वक्त्रमशीति योजनोच्छ्रितम्।। हनूमाननलप्रख्यो नवतिं योजनोच्छ्रितः। चकार सुरसा वक्त्रं शतयोजनमायतम्।।)
en: Threat, Surasă, extended her mouth forty yojanas, and thereupon the heroic Hanuman attained the altitude of fifty yojanas. Surasā enlarged her mouth sixty yojanas; and the heroic Hanumān anon heightened himself seventy yojanas. Şurasā widened her mouth eighty yoyanas; and Hanumān like to Fire raised himself ninety yojanas. And Surasā enlarged her mouth an hundred yojanas.

sn: तद् दृष्ट्वा व्यादितं त्वास्यं वायुपुत्रः स बुद्धिमान्। दीर्घजिढे सुरसया सुभीमं नरकोपमम्॥ स संक्षिप्यात्मनः कायं जीमूत इव मारुतिः। तस्मिन् मुहूर्ते हनुमान् बभूवाङ्गुष्ठमात्रकः॥ सोऽभिपद्याथ तद्वक्त्रं निष्पत्य च महाबलः। अन्तरिक्षे स्थितः श्रीमानिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Seeing that mouth with its long tongue opened by Surasā which was extremely terrible and was a replica of hell. Thereat diminishing his body like to a cloud, the wind-god's son at that moment measured one thumb only. Then entering her mouth and coming out of it, that exceedingly powerful powerful and graceful one, stationing himself in the sky spoke thus.

sn: प्रविष्टोऽस्मि हि ते वक्त्रं दाक्षायणि नमोऽस्तु ते। गमिष्ये यत्र वैदेही सत्यश्चासीद् वरस्तव॥
en: O descendant of Dakşa, I have entered into your mouth. I bow down to you. I will repair to where Vaidehi is Your boon has proved trve.

sn: तं दृष्ट्वा वदनान्मुक्तं चन्द्रं राहुमुखादिव। अब्रवीत् सुरसा देवी स्वेन रूपेण वानरम्॥
en: Seeing him out of her mouth like the Moon out of the mouth of Rāhu, the venerable Surasā spoke to the monkey in her native form, saying.

sn: अर्थसिद्ध्यै हरिश्रेष्ठ गच्छ सौम्य यथासुखम्। समानय च वैदेहीं राघवेण महात्मना॥
en: For compassing your end, go, O foremost of monkeys, O mild one, at yours ease. And bringing to Vaidehī tidings touching the highsouled Rāghava do you meet her.

sn: तत् तृतीयं हनुमतो दृष्ट्वा कर्म सुदुष्करम्। साधुसाध्विति भूतानि प्रशशंसुस्तदा हरिम्॥
en: Witnessing that third act* The third feat, remarks Rāmānuja, is Hanuman's issuing out of Surasā's mouth. The preceding two are not mentioned. — of Hanumān's hard to perform, all beings extolled the monkey exclaiming, "Excellent! Excellent!" *A kind of also or agallochum.-Wilson.

sn: स सागरमनाधृष्यमभ्येत्य वरुणालयम्। जगामाकाशमाविश्य वेगेन गरुडोपमः॥ सेविते वारिधाराभिः पतगैश्च निषेविते। चरिते कैशिकाचायैरैरावतनिषेविते॥ सिंहकुञ्जरशार्दूलपतगोरगवाहनैः। विमानैः सम्पतद्भिश्च विमलैः समलंकृते॥ वज्राशनिसमस्पर्शेः पावकैरिव शोभिते। कृतपुण्यैर्महाभागैः स्वर्गजिद्भिरधिष्ठिते॥ वहता हव्यमत्यन्तं सेविते चित्रभानुना। ग्रहनक्षत्रचन्द्रार्कतारागणविभूषिते॥ महर्षिगणगन्धर्वनागयक्षसमाकुले। विविक्ते विमले विश्वे विश्वावसुनिषेविते॥ देवराजगजाक्रान्तो चन्द्रसूर्यपथे शिवे। विताने जीवलोकस्य वितते ब्रह्मनिर्मिते॥ बहुशः सेविते वीरैर्विद्याधरगणैर्वृते । जगाम वायुमार्गे च गरुत्मानिव मारुतिः॥
en: Then he, resembling the wind in rush, arrived at the irrepressible ocean-abode of Varuņawent on, enveloping the welkin, on the aerial way, visited by showers, ranged by fowls and Gandharvas, graced by the rşis; embellished by shining vehicles rolling on, drawn by lions, or elephants, or tigers, or bird-serpents; presided over by eminently pious and righteous persons who have won the regions of heaven; and therefore appearing as if adorned by the (five) Fires; of the touch of Asani or Havya; (ever) served by Fire bearing sacrificial oblations; garnished by planets and stars and astral luminaries, and the Sun and the Moon; thronged with Maharsis, and Gandharvas and Nāgas, and Yaksas; and pure, and speckless;-the support of the universe-inhabited by Viswavasu; lorded over by the elephants of the king of the celestials; the orbit of the Sun and Moon, endowed with auspiciousness constituting the canopy of this live world blameless; and made by Brahmā; crowded with countless heroes, and Vidyādharas. And the wind-god's son Hanumnān, scattering clouds like the very Wind himself, coursed on in the aerial way like Garuda.

sn: हनुमान् मेघजालानि प्राकर्षन् मारुतो यथा। कालागुरुसवर्णानि रक्तपीतसितानि च॥
en: And mighty clouds, hued like Kālāguru red, and yellow and sable, on being disperse I by the monkey, burst into brilliance.

sn: कपिना कृष्यमाणानि महाभ्राणि चकाशिरे। प्रविशन्नभ्रजालानि निष्पतंश्च पुनः पुनः॥ प्रावृषीन्दुरिवाभाति निष्पतन् प्रविशंस्तथा!
en: Again and again entering into the clouds and emerging out of them, he resembled the Moon during the rains now entering into clouds) and now issuing out of them.

sn: प्रदृश्यमानः सर्वत्र हनूमान् मारुतात्मजः॥ भेजेऽम्बरं निरालम्बं पक्षयुक्त इवाद्रिराट्।
en: And everywhere Hanumān, son to the wind god coursing through the unsupported sky, looked like the monarch of mountains furnished with wings.

sn: प्लवमानं तु तं दृष्ट्वा सिंहिका नाम राक्षसी॥ मनसा चिन्तयामास प्रवृद्धा कामरूपिणी।
en: And it came to pass that beholding him in the act of bounding, a Rākşasi named Sinhikā, of great age, and capable of wearing forms at will, thought herself.

sn: अद्य दीर्घस्य कालस्य भविष्याम्यहमाशिता॥ इदं मम महासत्त्वं चिरस्य वशमागतम्।
en: Today after a long lapse of time I shall have my fare. This mighty creature has after a long time come within my power.

sn: इति संचिन्त्य मनसा च्छायामस्य समाक्षिपत्॥ छायायां गृह्यमाणायां चिन्तयामास वानरः। समाक्षिप्तोऽस्मि सहसा पङ्गकृतपराक्रमः॥ प्रतिलोमेन वातेन महानौरिव सागरे। तिर्यगूर्ध्वमधश्चैव वीक्षमाणस्तदा कपिः॥ ददर्श स महासत्त्वमुत्थितं लवणाम्भसि।
en: Having thought thus in her mind, she seized (Hanumān's) shadow. On his shadow* Brahmā had conferred on her a boon that she should secure her prey by pulling at it by means of its shadow.— "As a mighty bark is retarded in its course in the sea by adverse wind, have I, my prowess paralysed, been suddenly obstructed in my career.” Then looking above and below and sideways, the monkey saw a mighty creature arisen from the salt waters. *i.e. of securing his shadow.-being secured, the monkey reflected.

sn: तद् दृष्ट्वा चिन्तयामास मारुतिर्विकृताननाम्॥ कपिराज्ञा यथाख्यातं सत्त्वमद्भुतदर्शनम्। छायाग्राहि महावीर्यं तदिदं नात्र संशयः॥
en: Seeing that one of a distorted countenance, the wind-god's son thought, This one is, without doubt, the creature of wonderful form, possessed of exceeding prowess, given to securing its prey by means of its shadow, which had been described by the monkey-king.

sn: स तां बुद्ध्वार्थतत्त्वेन सिंहिकां मतिमान् कपिः। व्यवर्धत महाकायः प्रावृषीव बलाहकः॥
en: And concluding her to be Sinhikā from her act, the intelligent monkey attaining a gigantic body, increased himself, like a mass of clouds during the rains.

sn: तस्य सा कायमुद्वीक्ष्य वर्धमानं महाकपेः। वक्त्रं प्रसारयामास पातालाम्बरसंनिभम्॥ घनराजीव गर्जन्ती वानरं समभिद्रवत्।
en: Seeing the enlarged body of the mighty monkey, she extended her mouth measuring the sky and the nether regions. And roaring like to a mass of clouds, she rushed against the monkey.

sn: स ददर्श ततस्तस्या विकृतं सुमहन्मुखम्॥ कायमात्रं च मेधावी मर्माणि च महाकपिः।
en: Thereat, that intelligent and mighty monkey marked her deformed and huge mouth, her body and its asticulated members.

sn: स तस्या विकृते वक्त्रे वज्रसंहननः कपिः॥ संक्षिप्य मुहुरात्मानं निपपात महाकपिः।
en: And the redoubtable monkey hard as the thunderbolt, contracting himself in a moment, threw himself into her mouth.

sn: आस्ये तस्या निमज्जन्तं ददृशुः सिद्धचारणाः॥ ग्रस्यमानं यथा चन्द्रं पूर्णं पर्वणि राहुणा।
en: And the Siddhas and Chāraņas saw him sink in her mouth, as the full Moon is taken by Rāhu during a Parva.

sn: ततस्तस्या नखैस्तीक्ष्णैर्मर्माण्युत्कृत्य वानरः॥ उत्पपाताथ वेगेन मन:सम्पातविक्रमः।
en: Then tearing her limits by means of his sharp claws, the monkey, endowed with the celerity of thought, vehemently sprang forward.

sn: तां तु दिष्ट्या च धृत्वा च दाक्षिण्येन निपात्य सः।। कपिप्रवीरो वेगेन ववृधे पुनरात्मवान्।
en: Then slaying her by his acuteness of sight, endurance and skill, that heroic, self-controlled monkey again began to swell himself amain.

sn: हृतहृत्सा हनुमता पपात विधुराम्भसि। स्वयम्भुवैव हनुमान् सृष्टास्तस्या निपातने॥
en: Her heart having been crushed out by Hanuman, she, rendered lifeless, fell into the water. The self-create had created him for compassing her destruction.

sn: तां हतां वानरेणाशु पतितां वीक्ष्य सिंहिकाम्। भूतान्याकाशचारीणि तमूचुः प्लवगोत्तमम्॥
en: And seeing Sinhikā speedily slain by the monkey, and fallen, creatures ranging the sky addressed that foremost of monkeys, saying,

sn: भीममद्य कृतं कर्म महत्सत्त्वं त्वया हतम्। साधयार्थमभिप्रेतमरिष्टं प्लवतां वर॥
en: Terrible is the deed that you had performed to day. Mighty was the creature that has been slaughtered by you. Compass you yours wishedfor end without let, О foremost of monkeys.

sn: यस्य त्वेतानि चत्वारि वानरेन्द्र यथा तव। धृतिर्दृष्टिर्मतिर्दाक्ष्य स कर्मसु न सीदति ॥
en: He, O chief of monkeys, that, like you, is endowed with endurance, sharp sightedness, sense, and ability, dose not feel depressed in action.

sn: स तैः सम्पूजितः पूज्यः प्रतिपन्नप्रयोजनैः। जगामाकाशमाविश्य पन्नगाशनवत् कपिः॥
en: Honoured by these and wished well as to his purpose, that monkey, worthy of being honoured, set out, enveloping the sky, like him that subsist on serpents.* *Garuda.

sn: प्राप्तभूयिष्ठपारस्तु सर्वतः परिलोकयन्। योजनानां शतस्यान्ते वनराजी ददर्श सः॥
en: And it came to pass that as he had almost arrived at the other shore (of the ocean), he looking about on all sides at the end of an hundred yojanas saw a range of woods.

sn: ददर्श च पतन्नेव विविधदुमभूषितम्। दीपं शाखामृगश्रेष्ठो मलयोपवनानि च॥
en: As he went on, that best of monkeys saw an island decked with diverse trees, and groves pertaining Malaya.

sn: सागरं सागरानूपान् सागरानूपजान् दुमान्। सागरस्य च पत्नीनां मुखान्यपि विलोकयत्॥
en: He surveyed the sea, and lands bordering thereon, and trees growing on the sea shore, and the countenance of the spouses of the Sea.

sn: स महामेघसंकाशं समीक्ष्यात्मानमात्मवान्। निरुन्धन्तमिवाकाशं चकार मतिमान् मतिम्॥
en: Surveying his own person resembling a mighty mass of clouds, and as if closing up the sky, that self-possessed one ascertained his course of action.

sn: कायवृद्धिं प्रवेगं च मम दृष्ट्वैव राक्षसाः। मयि कौतूहलं कुर्युरिति मेने महामतिः॥
en: Soon as the Rākṣasas shall behold my enlarged body and the vehemence of my motion, they shall be seized with curiosity concerning me.

sn: ततः शरीरं संक्षिप्य तन्महीधरसंनिभम्। पुनः प्रकृतिमापेदे वीतमोह इवात्मवान्॥
en: Thus thought that magnanimous one. Thereat diminishing that person of his resembling a mountain, that self-possessed one, purged on ignorance, resumed his natural shape.

sn: तदूपमतिसंक्षिप्य हनूमान् प्रकृतौ स्थितः। त्रीन् क्रमानिव विक्रम्य बलिवीर्यहरो हरिः॥
en: And diminishing that form into the smallest compass, Hanumān remained in his native form, like that depriver of Vāli's prowess, Hari, after he had placed his three steps.

sn: स चारुनानाविधरूपधारी परं समासाद्य समुद्रतीरम्। परैरशक्यं प्रतिपन्नरूपः समीक्षितात्मा समवेक्षितार्थः॥
en: Thus wearing various graceful forms, that one, acting after reflection, having come to the other shore of the ocean incapable of being reached by others, on looking over his (immensely magnified person), reduced his body (to its former size).

sn: ततः स लम्बस्य गिरेः समृद्ध विचित्रकूटे निपपात कूटे। सकेतकोद्दालकनारिकेले महाभ्रकूटप्रतिमो महात्मा॥
en: That high-souled one resembling a cloudy pavilion, alighted on the (foremost) summit of the splendid mountain, Samva; crested with picturesque peaks; and abounding in ketakas, uddalakas and cocoanuts.

sn: ततस्तु सम्प्राप्य समुद्रतीरं समीक्ष्य लङ्कां गिरिवर्यमूधि। कपिस्तु तस्मिन् निपपात पर्वते विधूय रूपं व्यथयन्मृगद्विजान्॥
en: And reaching the shore of the sea, and beholding Lankā on the top of that foremost of mountains, the monkeys renouncing his native form, fell on that mountain, agitating birds and beasts.

sn: स सागरं दानवपन्नगायुतं बलेन विक्रम्य महोर्मिमालिनम्। निपत्य तारे च महोदयेस्तदा ददर्श लङ्काममरावतीमिव ॥
en: Having by main force bounded over the ocean heaving with surges, and rife with Dānavas and Pannagas, he alighting on the shore of the mighty main, beheld Lankā like to Amarāvati.

sn: स सागरं दानवपन्नगायुतं बलेन विक्रम्य महोर्मिमालिनम्। निपत्य तारे च महोदयेस्तदा ददर्श लङ्काममरावतीमिव ॥
en: Having by main force bounded over the ocean heaving with surges, and rife with Dānavas and Pannagas, he alighting on the shore of the mighty main, beheld Lankā like to Amarāvati.

sn: स सागरमनाधृष्यमतिक्रम्य महाबलः। त्रिकूटस्य तटे लङ्कां स्थितः स्वस्थो ददर्श ह॥
en: Having crossed over the ocean incapable of being repressed, that one endowed with great strength, staying at the plateau of Chitrakūta, and having refreshed himself, cast his eyes on Laukā.

sn: ततः पादपमुक्तेन पुष्पवर्षेण वीर्यवान्। अभिवृष्टस्ततस्तत्र बभौ पुष्पमयो हरिः॥
en: And covered with showers of blossoms poured down by the trees, that monkey possessed of prowess then appeared there like Puspamaya.* *A monkey so named.

sn: योजनानां शतं श्रीमांस्ती।त्युत्तमविक्रमः। अनिःश्वसन् कपिस्तत्र न ग्लानिमधिगच्छति॥
en: Having cleared an hundred Yoyanas, that monkey gifted with first-rate prowess, did not heave sighs or feel any fatigue.

sn: शतान्यहं योजनानां क्रमेयं सुबहून्यपि। किं पुनः सागरस्यान्तं संख्यातं शतयोजनम्॥
en: I am competent to bound over many hundreds of Yojanas. What then is this end of the ocean measuring an hundred Yojanas only?

sn: स तु वीर्यवतां श्रेष्ठः प्लवतामपि चोत्तमः। जगाम वेगवाँल्लङ्कां लवयित्वा महोदधिम्॥
en: That foremost of those endowed with energy and the prime of monkeys, gifted with speed, went to Laikā,* having crossed over the mighty main. *Descending, remarks the commentator, from the mountain-summit.

sn: शाद्वलानि च नीलानि गन्धवन्ति वनानि च । मधुमन्ति च मध्येन जगाम नगवन्ति च॥
en: Seeing blue lawns, and perfumed woods, replete with honey and filled with mountains, he held his way by the central thoroughfare.

sn: शैलांश्च तरुसंछन्नान् वनराजीश्च पुष्पिताः। अभिचक्राम तेजस्वी हनूमान् प्लवगर्षभः॥
en: That foremost of monkeys, the energetic Hanumān, went by hills filled with trees, and ranges of blossoming woods.

sn: स तस्मिन्नचले तिष्ठन् वनान्युपवनानि च। स नगाग्रे स्थितां लङ्कां ददर्श पवनात्मजः॥
en: And stationing himself in that mountain, the offspring of the Wind-god beheld woods and groves and Lankā established at the brow of the mountain.

sn: सरलान् कर्णिकारांश्च खजूरांश्च सुपुष्पितान् । प्रियालान् मुचुलिन्दांश्च कुटजान् केतकानपि॥ प्रियङ्गुन् गन्धपूर्णांश्च नीपान् सप्तच्छदांस्तथा। असनान् कोविदारांश्च करवीरांश्च पुष्पितान्॥ पुष्पभारनिबद्धांश्च तथा मुकुलितानपि। पादपान् विहगाकीर्णान् पवनाधूतमस्तकान्॥ हंसकारण्डवाकीर्णा वापी: पद्मोत्पलावृताः। आक्रीडान् विविधारम्यान्विविधांश्च जलाशयान्॥ संततान् विविधैर्वृक्षैः सर्वर्तुफलपुष्पितैः। उद्यानानि च रम्याणि ददर्श कपिकुञ्जरः॥
en: That elephant of a monkey surveyed Saralas, and Karņikāras, and dates in full flower, priyalas, Muculindas, Kutajas and Ketakas, Priyangus warm with aroma, and Nipas, and Saptachchhadas; Asanas, Kovidaras, and flowering Karavīras, and trees bearing blossoms, filled with swans and Kārandavas, and covered with lotuses and lilies; and charming sporting hills* and various watery expanses; and extensive tracts covered with diverse trees bearing flowers and furies at all seasons, and gardens exceedingly beautiful to behold. *Sporting hills according to Kataka. According to others, akrira means a grove in general.

sn: समासाद्य च लक्ष्मीवॉलङ्कां रावणपालिताम्। परिखाभिः सपद्माभिः सोत्पलाभिरलंकृताम्॥ सीतापहरणात् तेन रावणेन सुरक्षिताम्। समन्ताद् विचरद्भिश्च राक्षसैरुग्रधन्वभिः॥ काञ्चनेनावृतां रम्यां प्राकारेण महापुरीम्। गृहैश्च गिरिसंकाशैः शारदाम्बुदसंनिभैः॥ पाण्डुराभिः प्रतोलीभिरुच्चाभिरभिसंवृताम्। अट्टालकशताकीर्णा पताकाध्वजशोभिताम्॥ तोरणैः काञ्चनैर्दिव्यैर्लतापङ्क्तिविराजितैः। ददर्श हनुमाँल्लङ्कां देवो देवपुरीमिव॥
en: Drawing near to Lankā embellished with lilies and environed by a moat filled with lotuses, that one graced with auspiciousness, that graceful monkey, Hanumān, beheld Lankā vigilantly guarded by Rāvaņa, in consequence of Sītā having been carried away, with Rākṣasas bearing fierce bows ranging all around, that mighty and captivating capital surrounded by a golden wall, filled with edifices resembling cliffs and looking like autumnal clouds, and elevated yellowish highways; abounding in hundreds of banners mounted on the walls, and beautified with pennons an streamers; with noble golden gateways painted with plants; and resembling the metropolis of the very sovereign of the celestials.

sn: पालितां राक्षसेन्द्रेण निर्मितां विश्वकर्मणा। प्लवमानामिवाकाशे ददर्श हनुमान् कपिः॥ वप्रप्राकारजघनां विपुलाम्बुवनाम्बराम्। शतघ्नीशूलकेशान्तामट्टालकावतंसकाम्॥ मनसेव कृतां लङ्कां निर्मितां विश्वकर्मणा।
en: And that graceful monkey saw Lankā situated on the top of the mountain, filled with splendid yellow-white palaces, like to a city stationed in the sky ruled by the lord of Rākşasas and reared by Viśvakarmā himself. And the monkey, Hanumān, beheld Lankā, as if moving in the sky: with her walls furnished with daises for her hips, the immense waters and woods for her cloth, Śataghnīs and darts for her hair ends: and pennons on her walls for earrings, built as if by the agency of the Mind; and constructed by Viśvakarmā himself.

sn: द्वारमुत्तरमासाद्य चिन्तयामास वानरः॥ कैलासनिलयप्रख्यमालिखन्तमिवाम्बरम्। ध्रियमाणमिवाकाशमुच्छ्रितैर्भवनोत्तमैः॥ सम्पूर्णां राक्षसै।रैर्गुहामाशीविषैरिव। तस्याश्च महतीं गुप्तिं सागरं च निरीक्ष्य सः। रावणं च रिपुं घोरं चिन्तयामास वानरः॥ आगत्यापीह हरयो भविष्यन्ति निरर्थकाः। नहि युद्धेन लङ्का शक्या जेतुं सुरैरपि॥
en: And arriving at the Northern gate resembling the mansion of Kailāsa, and cleaving, as it were, the welkin, and as if holding the firmament with lofty and glorious edifices, and observing the sea; his dreadful enemy, Ravana; the city teeming with poisonous snakes, as well as the method of defence (displayed in it)-the monkeys reflected, Even if the monkeys came here, they should fail to achieve success; for Lankā is incapable of being taken in battle by the celestials themselves.

sn: इमां त्वविषमां लङ्कां दुर्गा रावणपालिताम्। प्राप्यापि सुमहाबाहुः किं करिष्यति राघवः॥
en: Even if the mighty-armed Rāghava should reach this terrible-looking and impregnable Lankā reared by Rāvana, what could he do?

sn: अवकाशो न साम्नस्तु राक्षसेप्वभिगम्यते। न दानस्य न भेदस्य नैव युद्धस्य दृश्यते॥
en: Opportunity find I none either for conciliation with the Raksasas, or for (winning them over) by gifts, or for sowing dissensions among them, or for conquering them in fight.

sn: चतुर्णामेव हि गतिर्वानराणां तरस्विनाम्। वालिपुत्रस्य नीलस्य मम राज्ञश्च धीमतः॥
en: Of all the monkeys, four only endowed with (exceptional) celerity, viz., Vāli's son, Nīla, the intelligent king, and myself, heave the power to come over here.

sn: यावज्जानामि वैदेहीं यदि जीवति वा न वा। तत्रैव चिन्तयिष्यामि दृष्ट्वा तां जनकात्मजाम्॥
en: When I have ascertained whether Vaidehī is alive or not, I shall, after interviewing Janaka's daughter, think about this.

sn: ततः स चिन्तयामास मुहूर्तं कपिकुञ्जरः। गिरेः शृङ्गे स्थिस्तस्मिन् रामस्याभ्युदयं ततः॥
en: Then that elephantine monkey, stationed on the summit of that mountain, for a while bethought himself as the success of Rāma.* *About rescuing his wife.

sn: अनेन रूपेण मया न शक्या रक्षसां पुरी। प्रवेष्टुं राक्षसैर्गुप्ता क्रूरैर्बलसमन्वितैः॥
en: I cannot in this form succeed in entering the city of the Rākşasas, guarded by wily and powerful Rākṣasas.

sn: महौजसो महावीर्या बलवन्तश्च राक्षसाः। वञ्चनाया मया सर्वे जानकी परिमार्गता॥
en: I should, while engaged in searching for Jānaki, deceive all the strong and highly energetic Rākşasas gifted with prowess.

sn: लक्ष्यालक्ष्येण रूपेण रात्रौ लङ्कापुरी मया। प्राप्तकालं प्रवेष्टुं मे कृत्यं साधयितुं महत्॥
en: For attaining this mighty object, it behove me to enter Lankā at night in a shape invisible yet well suited to the end in view.

sn: तां पुरी तादृशीं दृष्ट्वा दुराधर्षां सुरासुरैः। हनूमांश्चिन्तयामास विनिःश्वस्य मुहूर्मुहुः॥
en: Beholding the city in that state, difficult of being subdued by the celestials and Asuras (combined), Hanumān, sighing moment arily, thought within himself,

sn: केनोपायेन पश्येयं मैथिली जनकात्मजाम्। अदृष्टो राक्षसेन्द्रेण रावणेन दुरात्मना॥
en: How can I, without being discovered by the impious lord of Rākşasas, Rāvana, succeed in seeing Janaka's daughter, Maithili?

sn: न विनश्येत् कथं कार्यं रामस्य विदितात्मनः। एकामेकस्तु पश्येयं रहिते जनकात्मजाम्॥
en: How can the work of Rāma cognizant of self (be so managed that it) may not be brought to naught? How can I see Janaka's daughter singly in secret?

sn: भूताश्चार्था विनश्यन्ति देशकालविरोधिताः। विक्लवं दूतमासाद्य तमः सूर्योदये यथा॥
en: Action on the very eve of success, on being obstructed by adverse season and place, and through the agency of unreflecting envoys come to nought, even as darkness is dispelled on sunrise.

sn: अर्थानान्तरे बुद्धिनिश्चितापि न शोभते। घातयन्तीह कार्याणि दूताः पण्डितमानिनः॥
en: In respect of what should he undertaken and what not, even the certain decision (of a master assisted by his counsellors), because of a heedless messenger, dose not appear in all its beauty: messengers (foolish) yet proud of their knowledge, bring every business to nought.

sn: न विनश्येत् कथं कार्यं वैक्लव्यं न कथं भवेत्। लङ्घनं च समुद्रस्य कथं नु न भवेद् वृथा॥
en: How can I so manage that my business may not suffer? How can I avoid recklessness? How can my bounding over the deep bear fruit?

sn: मयि दृष्टे तु रक्षोभी रामस्य विदितात्मनः। भवेद् व्यर्थमिदं कार्यं रावणानर्थमिच्छतः॥
en: On my being seen by the Rākşasas, the work of Rāma cognizant of self, desirous of the destruction of Ravana, shall be marred.

sn: नहि शक्यं क्वचित् स्थातुमविज्ञातेन राक्षसैः। अपि राक्षसरूपेण किमुतान्येन केनचित्॥
en: Even if I wear a Rākşasa form, I cannot anywhere remain undiscovered by the Rākṣasas.

sn: वायुरप्यत्र नाज्ञातश्चरेदिति मतिर्मम। नह्यत्राविदितं किंचिद् रक्षसां भीमकर्मणाम्॥
en: What shall I say of any other form? Even the wind, I conceive dose not stray here, unperceived. Nothing whatever is here that is unknown to the Räkşasas of redoubtable deeds.

sn: इहाहं यदि तिष्ठामि स्वेन रूपेण संवृतः। विनाशमुपयास्यामि भर्तुरर्थश्च हास्यति॥
en: Should I stay here embodied in my native form, I shall come by destruction; and the interest also of my master shall suffer.

sn: तदहं स्वेण रूपेण रजन्यां ह्रस्वतां गतः। लङ्कामभिपतिष्यामि राघवस्यार्थसिद्धये॥
en: Therefore, diminishing myself, I shall at night, for compassing the welfare of Rāghava, enter Lankā is my own form.

sn: रावणस्य पुरी रात्रौ प्रविश्य सुदुरासदाम्। प्रविश्य भवनं सर्वं द्रक्ष्यामि जनकात्मजाम्॥
en: Entering at night Råvaņa's capital difficult of access, I shall, obtaining entry into every dwelling seek Janaka's daughter.'

sn: इति निश्चित्य हनुमान् सूर्यस्यास्तमयं कपिः। आचकाङ्के तदा वीरो वैदेह्या दर्शनोत्सुकः॥
en: Having made up his mind thus, the heroic Hanumān, extremely eager to see Vaidehi, wished for the setting of the sun.

sn: सूर्ये चास्तं गते रात्रौ देहं संक्षिप्य मारुतिः। वृषदंशकमात्रोऽथ बभूवाद्भुतदर्शनः॥
en: On the sun having set, at night the Windgod's son, contracting his person, reducing himself to the dimensions of a cat, became wonderful to behold.

sn: प्रदोषकाले हनुमांस्तूर्णमुत्पत्य वीर्यवान्। प्रविवेश पुरी रम्यां प्रविभक्तमहापथाम्॥ प्रासादमालाविततां स्तम्भैः काञ्चनसंनिभैः। शातकुम्भनिभैर्जालैर्गन्धर्वनगरोपमाम्॥
en: At dusk, the powerful Hanumān, springing up, entered the charming city of Lankā with its well divided highways; furnished with rows of edifices having golden pillars, and net-works, resembling the metropolis of the Gandharvas.

sn: सप्तभौमाष्टभौमैश्च स ददर्श महापुरीम्। स्थलैः स्फटिकसंकीर्णैः कार्तस्वरविभूषितैः। तैस्तैः शुशुभिरे तानि भवनान्यत्र रक्षसाम्॥
en: He saw that splendid city containing sevenstoried and eight-storied edifices, studded with crystal and adorned with gold. And the dwellings of the Rākṣasas were embellished with these (ornaments).

sn: काञ्चनानि विचित्राणि तोरणानि च रक्षसाम्। लङ्कामुद्योतयामासुः सर्वतः समलंकृताम्॥
en: And graceful golden gateways belonging to the Rākṣasas everywhere lent splendour to Lankā adorned all over.

sn: अचिन्त्यामद्भुताकारां दृष्ट्वा लङ्कां महाकपिः। आसीद् विषण्णो दृष्टश्च वैदेह्या दर्शनोत्सुकः। ५२।।
en: Beholding Lankā, wonderful and of inconceivable loveliness, the mighty monkey, desirous of beholding Vaidehī, became depressed and delighted at the same time.

sn: स पाण्डुराविद्धविमानमालिनी महार्हजाम्बूनदजालतोरणाम्। यशस्विनी रावणबाहुपालितां क्षपाचरैभीमबलैः सुपालिताम्॥
en: And he (entered Lankā) engarlanded with yellow edifices joined together, with the ornamented arches of her gateways furnished with nets of precious gold; famed (all over the world); ruled by the arm of Ravana, and vigilantly guarded by night-rangers of dreadful strength.

sn: स्तारागणैर्मध्यगतो विराजन्। नुत्तिष्ठतेऽनेकसहस्ररश्मिः ॥
en: As if ministering to him,* the Moon furnished with many thousands of rays arose with the stars in the midst of the sky, spreading lunar light over all creatures. * Hanuman.

sn: मुद्गच्छमानं व्यवभासमानम्। ददर्श चन्द्रं स कपिप्रवीरः पोप्लूयमानं सरसीव हंसम्॥
en: And that heroic monkey behold the Moon possessing the sheen of a conch, and hued like milk or the lotus-stalk, arisen and afloat (in the welkin), like a swan swimming in a tank.

sn: स लम्बशिखरे लंबे लंबतोयदसंनिभे। सत्त्वमास्थाय मेधावी हनुमान् मारुतात्मजः॥ निशि लङ्कां महासत्त्वो विवेश कपिकुञ्जरः। रम्यकाननतोयाढ्यां पुरी रावणपालिताम्॥ शारदाम्बुधरप्रख्यैर्भवनैरुपशोभिताम्। सागरोपमनिर्घोषां सागरानिलसेविताम्॥ सुपुष्टबलसम्पुष्टां यथैव विटपावतीम्। चारुतोरणनिर्वृहां पाण्डुरद्वारतोरणाम्॥ भुजगाचरितां गुप्तां शुभां भोगवतीमिव। तां सविद्युद्घनाकीर्णा ज्योतिर्गणनिषेविताम्॥ चण्डमारुतनिर्हादां यथा चाप्यमरावतीम्।
en: Assuming the quality of goodness and energy on mount Lamba furnished with elevated summits, and resembling long masses of clouds, Hanuman, son to the Wind-god capable of concluding in harmony with season, possessed of exceeding strength an elephant among monkeys-entered Lańkā by night, affluent with charming woods and waters-the city governed by Rāvaņa; beautified with edifices resembling autumnal clouds; sounding like to Vitapāvati* herself with infuriated elephants (stationed) at her graceful gateways; containing white gates with ornainented arches; arches; resembling the handsome Bhogavatī inhabited and protected by serpents. And suddenly coming to that (city) resembling Amarāvatī, scattered with clouds charged with lightning, having hosts of luminaries, and tumultuous with the roars of blustering blasts, *Alakā, the city of Kubera, King of Yaksas.

sn: शातकुम्भेन महता प्राकारेणाभिसंवृताम्॥ किङ्किणीजालघोषाभिः पताकाभिरलंकृताम्। आसाद्य सहसा हृष्टः प्राकारमभिपेदिवान्॥ विस्मयाविष्टहृदयः पुरीमालोक्य सर्वतः। जाम्बूनदमयैारैवैदूर्यकृतवेदिकैः॥ वज्रस्फटिकमुक्ताभिर्मणिकुट्टिमभूषितैः। तप्तहाटकनिषूहै राजतामलपाण्डुरैः॥ वैदूर्यकृतसोपानैः स्फाटिकान्तरपांसुभिः। चारुसंजवनोपैतैः खमिवोत्पतितैः शुभैः॥
en: Girt round by a mighty golden wall, ringing with the tinklings of tiny bells; and embellished with pennons, he growing exceedingly exhilarated, made towards the wall. And beholding the city all round, furnished with golden doors; having quadrangular courts composed of lapises; ornamented with plastered jewelled pavements studded with all gems, crystals, and pearls; with mad elephants of burnished gold and speckless white silver, with stairs of lapises, (doors) devoid of dust with their centres composed of crystal and with stately halls; elegant, and adjoining mansions seeming as if reaching up to the heavens.

sn: क्रौञ्चबर्हिणसंघुष्टै राजहंसनिषेवितैः। तूर्याभरणनिर्घोषैः सर्वतः परिनादिताम्॥
en: Resounding with Krauñca as and peacocks; frequented by swans, and everywhere resonant with the sounds of trumpets and ornaments.

sn: बस्वोकसारप्रतिमां समीक्ष्य नगरी ततः। खमिवोत्पतितां लङ्कां जहर्ष हनुमान् कपिः॥
en: And then beholding the city Lankā, resembling Vasvokasāra,* and appearing to mount to the welkin, the monkey Hanumān was filled with rapture. *Alaka.

sn: तां समीक्ष्य पुरीं लङ्कां राक्षसाधिपतेः शुभाम्। अनुत्तमामृद्धिमतीं चिन्तयामास वीर्यवान्॥
en: And seeing the delightful, . divine and prosperous city of Lankā belonging to the lord of Rākşasas, that one endowed with prowess thought within himself,

sn: नेयमन्येन नगरी शक्या धर्षयितुं बलात्। रक्षिता रावणबलैरुद्यतायुधपाणिभिः॥
en: This city protected by the forces of Rãvaņa with their hands holding upraised arms, is incapable of being forcibly subdued by any other.

sn: कुमुदाङ्गदयोर्वापि सुषेणस्य महाकपेः। प्रसिद्धेयं भवेत् भूमिमॆन्दद्विविदयोरपि॥ विवस्वतस्तनूजस्य हरेश्च कुशपर्वणः। ऋक्षस्य कपिमुख्यस्य मम चैव गतिर्भवेत्॥
en: This place can be easily entered by Kumuda, and Angada, as well as by that mighty monkey, Suşeņa; and also by Mainda and Dvivida. And there is way also for the offspring of the Sun, and that monkey, Kuśaparva, as well as of that foremost of monkeys, Rksya, and myself."

sn: समीक्ष्य च महाबाहो राघवस्य पराक्रमम्। लक्ष्मणस्य च विक्रान्तमभवत् प्रीतिमान् कपिः॥
en: Having witnessed the prowess of Rāghava, as well as the vigour of Lakşmaņa, the monkey was filled with joy.

sn: तां रत्नवसनोपेतां गोष्ठागारवतंसिकाम्। यन्त्रागारस्तनीमृद्धां प्रमदामिव भूषिताम्॥ तां नष्टतिमिरां दीपै स्वरैश्च महाग्रहै:। नगरी राक्षसेन्द्रस्य स ददर्श महाकपिः॥ अथ सा हरिशार्दूलं प्रविशन्तं महाकपिम्। नगरी स्वेन रूपेण ददर्श पवनात्मजम्॥
en: And that redoubtable monkey beheld the metropolis of the monarch of the Räkşasas; having for her cloth the sea; for her pendants, cow-stalls and stables; for her breasts, turrets mounted on the walls for discharging missils, decked out like a damsel; with her darkness dispelled by bright lights and the mighty monkey son to the Wind-god was met by the city in her native shape.

sn: सा तं हरिवरं दृष्ट्वा लङ्का रावणपालिता। स्वयमेवोत्थिता तत्र विकृताननदर्शना ॥ पुरस्तात् तस्य वीरस्य वायुसूनोरतिष्ठत। मुञ्चमाना महानादमब्रवीत् पवनात्मजम्॥
en: Seeing that best of monkeys, Lankā, ruled by Rāvana arising of herself with her countenance rendered deformed, stood before the heroic son of the Wind and, emitting a tremendous roar, addressed the offspring of the Wind-god, saying,

sn: कस्त्वं केन च कार्येण इह प्राप्तो वनालय। कथयस्वेह यत् तत्त्वं यावत् प्राणा धरन्ति ते॥
en: O you that had the woods for the home, who are you? And on what errand had you come hither? Tell me while yet you had your vital powers left in you.

sn: न शक्यं खल्वियं लङ्का प्रवेष्टुं वानर त्वया। रक्षिता रावणबलैरभिगुप्ता समन्ततः॥
en: O monkey, for certain you are unable to obtain entry into this Laňkā, protected by the forces of Rāvaņa, and carefully guarded on all sides.

sn: अथ तामब्रवीत् वीरो हनुमानग्रतः स्थिताम्। कथयिष्यामि तत् तत्त्वं यन्मां त्वं परिपृच्छसे॥ का त्वं विरूपनयना पुरद्वारेऽवतिष्ठसे। किमर्थं चापि मां क्रोधान्निर्भर्त्सयसि दारुणे॥
en: Thereat, the heroic Hanumān spoke to her staying in front of him, “I shall tell you all about that anent which you questionest me. Who are you that having deformed eyes stayest at the gate of this city? And what for, O frightful one, do you rail at me in wrath?"

sn: हनुमद्वचनं श्रुत्वा लङ्का सा कामरूपिणी। उवाच वचनं क्रुद्धा परुषं पवनात्मजम्॥
en: Hearing Hanumān's speech, Lankā, capable of wearing forms at will, waxing wroth addressed the Wind-god's offspring, saying,

sn: अहं राक्षसराजस्य रावणस्य महात्मनः। आज्ञाप्रतीक्षा दुर्धर्षा रक्षामि नगरीमिमाम्॥
en: I, who am incapable of being repressed, abiding by the mandate of the high-souled sovereign of the Rākşasas, protect this city.

sn: न शक्यं मामवज्ञाय प्रवेष्टुं नगरीमिमाम्। अद्य प्राणैः परित्यक्तः स्वप्स्यसे निहतो मया॥
en: You are unable to enter this city, passing me by. You shall to-day, losing your life and slain by me, sleep (the sleep of death).

sn: अहं हि नगरी लङ्का स्वयमेव प्लवङ्गम। सर्वतः परिरक्षामि अतस्ते कथितं मया॥
en: O monkey, I am the City of Lankā myself. I every way guard (all that is here.) that I told you.

sn: लङ्काया वचनं श्रुत्वा हनूमान् मारुतात्मजः। यत्नवान् स हरिश्रेष्ठः स्थितः शैल इवापरः॥
en: Hearing Lankā's words, Hanumān, son to the Wind-god, foremost of monkeys-exerting himself (to secure victory), stood like another hill.

sn: स तां स्त्रीरूपविकृतां दृष्ट्वा वानरपुङ्गवः। आबभाषेऽथ मेधावी सत्त्ववान् प्लवगर्षभः॥
en: Seeing her appear in the form of a deformed female, that foremost and best-of monkeys endued with intelligence, possessed of prowess, said.
