en: I do long for you, O you having expansive eyes; do you esteem me, O my dear one, O you gifted with all accomplishments and pleasant to all persons.

sn: नेह किंचिन्मनुष्या वा राक्षसाः कामरूपिणः। व्यपसर्पतु ते सीते भयं मत्तः समुत्थितम्॥
en: O Sītā, here is no human being or any Rākşasa assuming shapes at will, do you therefore renounce all fear from me.

sn: स्वधर्मो रक्षसां भीरु सर्वदैव न संशयः। गमनं वा परस्त्रीणां हरणं सम्प्रमथ्य वा॥
en: O timid damsel, for certain it is the virtue of the Rākşasas that they always visit others' wives or come by them by force.

sn: एवं चैवमकामां त्वां न च स्प्रक्ष्यामि मैथिलि। कामं कामः शरीरे मे यथाकामं प्रवर्तताम्॥
en: In spite of this, O Maithili, I do not touch you for you are not under the influence of amour—but for me, I am completely under its sway.

sn: देवि नेह भयं कार्यं मयि विश्वसिहि प्रिये। प्रणयस्व च तत्त्वेन मैवं भूः शोकलालसा॥
en: Do not fear me, O worshipful damsel, confide in me O my beloved one, and become attached to me. Do not give way to grief.

sn: एकवेणी अधःशय्या ध्यानं मलिनमम्बरम्। अस्थानेऽप्युपवासश्च नैतान्यौपयिकानि ते॥
en: A single lock of hair, to lie down on earth and useless fast-these do not become you.

sn: विचित्राणि च माल्यानि चन्दनान्यगुरूणि च। विविधानि च वासांसि दिव्यान्याभरणानि च॥ महार्हाणि च पानानि शयनान्यासनानि च। गीतं नृत्यं च वाद्यं च लभ मां प्राप्य मैथिलि॥
en: Attaining me, O Maithili, do you enjoy excellent garlands, sandal, ornaments, costly wines, beds, seats, songs, dancing and music.

sn: स्त्रीरत्नमसि मैवं भूः कुरु गात्रेषु भूषणम्। मां प्राप्य हि कथं वा स्यास्त्वमनीं सुविग्रहे ॥
en: You are a jewel of a female; do you not therefore remain in this guise. Put on your ornaments therefore. How shall you remain unadorned obtaining me, O you of a beautiful figure?

sn: इदं ते चारुसंजातं यौवनं ह्यतिवर्तते। यदतीतं पुनर्रुति स्रोतः स्रोतस्विनामिव ॥
en: This your beautiful youth is passing away, which like the current of a river when once gone, dose not turn back,

sn: त्वां कृत्वोपरतो मन्ये रूपकर्ता स विश्वकृत्। नहि रूपोपमा ह्यन्या तवास्ति शुभदर्शने॥
en: O you of a fair look, having created you, the artist of Gods, the maker of celestial beauties, has ceased from his work, for a match of your beauty I find in none.

sn: त्वां समासाद्य वैदेहि रूपयौवनशालिनीम्। कः पुनर्नातिवर्तेत साक्षादपि पितामहः॥
en: Who is there, O Vaidehi, who can withstand the influence of amour, getting you, gifted with beauty and youth? (What of others) even Brahmā, the grand-father of the celestials, is moved.

sn: यद् यत् पश्यामि ते गात्रं शीतांशुसदृशानने। तस्मिंस्तस्मिन् पृथुश्रोणि चक्षुर्मम निबध्यते॥
en: O you having a moon-like countenance, and well-developed hips, whatever limbs of yours, I behold, I find my gaze fixed therein.

sn: भव मैथिलि भार्या मे मोहमेतं विसर्जय। बह्वीनामुत्तमस्त्रीणां ममाग्रमहिषी भव॥
en: O Maithili, do you become my spouse, and renounce this delusion. Do you become the foremost queen of all my excellent wives.

sn: लोकेभ्यो यानि रत्नानि सम्प्रमथ्याहृतानि मे। तानि ते भीरु सर्वाणि राज्यं चैव ददामि ते॥
en: O timid one, all the jewels that I have collected from the three worlds, and all my kingdom I shall confer on you.

sn: विजित्य पृथिवीं सर्वां नानानगरमालिनीम्। जनकाय प्रदास्यामि तव हेतोर्विलासिनि॥
en: O sportive damsel, for your satisfaction, I shall conquer the whole earth, engarlanded by many cities and bestow it upon Janaka.

sn: नेह पश्यामि लोकेऽन्यं यो मे प्रतिबलो भवेत्। पश्य मे सुमहद्वीर्यमप्रतिद्वन्द्वमाहवे॥
en: Find I none on this earth who can withstand my prowess. Do you behold my matchless prowess in battle.

sn: असकृत्संयुगे भग्ना मया विमृदितध्वजाः। अशक्ताः प्रत्यनीकेषु स्थातुं मम सुरासुराः॥
en: The celestials and Asuras are incapable of withstanding me, defeated as they were by me in battle and their pennons struck down.

sn: इच्छ मां क्रियतामद्य प्रतिकर्म तवोत्तमम्। सुप्रभाण्यवसज्जन्तां तवाङ्गे भूषणानि हि॥
en: Do you therefore desire ine to-day, dress yourself in excellent robes and adorn yourself in beautifully brilliant ornaments.

sn: साधु पश्यामि ते रूपं सुयुक्तं प्रतिकर्मणा। प्रतिकर्माभिसंयुक्ता दाक्षिण्येन वरानने॥
en: I shall behold your dazzling beauty whenadorned with ornaments. For pity to me, do you embellish, yourself with ornaments, O you of a graceful countenance.

sn: भुक्ष्व भोगान् यथाकामं पिब भीरु रमस्व च। यथेष्टं च प्रयच्छ त्वं पृथिवीं वा धनानि च ॥
en: O timid damsel, do you, at your pleasure, enjoy all sorts of comforts and luxuries, and do you, as you desirest, confer wealth and land on others.

sn: ललस्व मयि विस्रब्धा धृष्टमाज्ञापयस्व च। मत्प्रासादाल्ललन्त्याश्च ललतां बान्धवस्तव॥
en: Do you confiding in me, ask for your wishedfor objects and do you command me like to an unmannerly damsel. You shall, by asking favours from me, satisfy the desires of your friends.

sn: ऋद्धिं ममानुपश्य त्वं श्रियं भद्रे यशस्विनि। किं करिष्यसि रामेण सुभगे चीरवासिना॥
en: Ogently lady, O you of great renown, do you observe my prosperity. What shall you do with Răma, wearing bark, O you of pleasant presence.

sn: निक्षिप्तविजयो रामो गतश्रीर्वनगोचरः। व्रती स्थण्डिलशायी च शङ्के जीवति वा न वा॥
en: Rāma has ceased from his endeavours for gaining victory. He has lost all his beauty, lives in the forest, is engaged in observances and always lies down on earth. I fear whether he is living still.

sn: नहि वैदेहि रामस्त्वां द्रष्टुं वाप्युपलभ्यते। पुरोबलाकैरसितैर्मेधैर्योत्स्नामिवावृताम्॥ न चापि मम हस्तात्त्वां प्राप्तुमर्हति राघवः। हिरण्यकशिपुः कीर्तिमिन्द्रहस्तगतामिव ॥
en: O Vaidehī, Rāma shall not be able to see you like to the rays of the moon covered with blue clouds preceded by Balākās.* Rāghava shall never get you back from my hands, like to Hiranyakaśipu unable to regain his wife Kirti from Indra. *A kind of crane.

sn: चारुस्मिते चारुदति चारुनेत्रे विलासिनी। मनो हरसि मे भीरु सुपर्णः पन्नगं यथा॥
en: O you of beautiful teeth, O you having beautiful eyes, O sportive damsel, O timid one, you do steal my mind like to Garuda catching serpents.

sn: क्लिष्टकौशेयवसनां तन्वीमप्यनलंकृताम्। त्वां दृष्ट्वा स्वेषु दारेषु रतिं नोपलभाम्यहम्॥
en: Beholding you, wearing a shattered silken cloth, slender and without any ornaments, I do not find any attachment in my own wives.

sn: अन्तःपुरनिवासिन्यः स्त्रियः सर्वगुणान्विताः। यावत्यो मम सर्वासामैश्वर्यं कुरु जानकि॥
en: O daughter of Janaka, do you exercise, your supremacy, over all my wives, living in my seraglio and gifted with all accomplishments.

sn: मम ह्यसितकेशान्ते त्रैलोक्यप्रवरस्त्रियः। तास्त्वां परिचरिष्यन्ति श्रियमप्सरसो यथा।॥
en: O you having black hair, all my wives are foremost in beauty over the three worlds. And they shall all attained you like to Apsaras waiting upon the Goddess of wealth.

sn: यानि वैश्रवणे सुभ्र रत्नानि च धनानि च। तानि लोकांश्च सुश्रोणि मया भुझ्व यथासुखम्॥
en: O you having beautiful eye brows and welldeveloped hips, do you, along with me, enjoy at your pleasure all the wealth and riches of Kubera. "The God of wealth or Pluto in Greak myth.

sn: न रामस्तपसा देवि न बलेन च विक्रमैः। न धनेन मया तुल्यस्तेजसा यशसाऽपि वा॥
en: O worshipful damsel, in asceticism, strength or prowess, wealth or fame, Rāma is not my equal.

sn: पिब विहर रमस्व भुक्ष्व भोगान् धननिचयं प्रदिशाभि मेदिनीं च। मयि लल ललने यथासुखं त्वं त्वयि च समेत्य ललन्तु बान्धवास्ते॥
en: Do you therefore at your pleasure drink, enjoy and eat. I shall confer on you wealth and the whole earth. Do you satisfy all your desires in me, O fair damsel, and let your friends be satisfied in you.

sn: कुसुमिततरुजालसंततानि भ्रमरयुतानि समुद्रतीरजानि। कनकविमलहारभूषिताङ्गी विहर मया सह भीरु काननानि॥
en: And adorned with beautiful golden necklace, O timid lady, do you at your pleasure, range with me, in the forests, situated on the bank of the ocean, and filled with flowery trees and black bees. a

sn: तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा सीता रौद्रस्य रक्षसः। आर्ता दीनस्वरा दीनं प्रत्युवाच ततः शनैः॥
en: Hearing those words of that terrible Rākşasa, Sītā, stricken with grief and of feeble voice, slowly replied.

sn: दुःखार्ता रुदती सीता वेपमाना तपस्विनी। चिन्तयन्ती वरारोहा पतिमेव पतिव्रता ॥
en: Racked with grief, engaged in asceticism and weeping, Sita began. to tremble. And that excellent damsel, devoted to her husband, began to think of him.

sn: तृणमन्तरतः कृत्वा प्रत्युवाच शुचिस्मिता। निवर्तय मनो मत्तः स्वजने प्रीयतां मनः॥
en: Placing a twig before, that one, of beautiful smile, said-"Do you take back your mind from me and place it in your own wives."

sn: न मां प्रार्थयितुं युक्तस्त्वं सिद्धिमिव पापकृत्। अकार्यं न मया कार्यमेकपत्न्या विगर्हितम्॥
en: Like to a sinner unworthy of praying for final emancipation, it dose not behove you to expect to come by me. Devoted to one husband I shall never perpetrate such an iniquitous act.

sn: कुलं सम्प्राप्तया पुण्यं कुले महति जातया। एवमुक्त्वा तु वैदेही रावणं तं यशस्विनी॥ रावणं पृष्ठतः कृत्वा भूयो वचनमब्रवीत्। नाहमौपयिकी भार्या परभार्या सती तव॥
en: I am born in a high and have been married in a pious family. Having accosted Rāvana thus, the well-known Vaidehi, turning her back, again spake to him, saying. "I should not live with you since I am another's wife and chaste."

sn: साधु धर्ममवेक्षस्व साधु साधुव्रतं चर। यथा तव तथान्येषां रक्ष्या दारा निशाचर॥
en: Have your eyes always on religion and do you follow in the track of piety. Like to yours own wives, others are worthy of being protected by you, O ranger of the night.

sn: आत्मानमुपमां कृत्वा स्वेषु दारेषु रम्यताम्। अतुष्टं स्वेषु दारेषु चपलं चपलेन्द्रियम्। नयन्ति निकृतिप्रज्ञं परदाराः पराभवम्॥
en: Making an example of you, do you enjoy with your own wives. Forsooth those vicious-minded, those of agitated senses, who are not satisfied with their own wives, are brought to misery by others' wives.

sn: इह सन्तो न वा सन्ति सतो वा नानुवर्तसे। यथा हि विपरीता ते बुद्धिराचारवर्जिता॥
en: (Methinks) there are no pious men here and even if there be any you do not follow him since you had such an adverse understanding, against human practice and usage.

sn: वचो मिथ्याप्रणीतात्मा पथ्यमुक्तं विचक्षणैः। राक्षसानामभावाय त्वं वा न प्रतिपद्यसे॥
en: Or the considerate people have spoken the truth, but you, for the destruction of the race of the Raksasas, considering that false, had not followed it.

sn: अकृतात्मानमासाद्य राजानमनये रतम्। समृद्धानि विनश्यन्ति राष्ट्राणि नगराणि च॥
en: Wealth, kingdom and cities-all are brought to naught when they are placed at the hands of a vicious and illiterate king.

sn: तथैव त्वां समासाद्य लङ्का रत्नौघसंकुला। अपराधात् तवैकस्य न चिराद् विनशिष्यति॥
en: Obtaining you, (therefore) as her king and for your folly only, this city of Lankā, abounding in jewels, shall soon be ruined.

sn: स्वकृतैर्हन्यमानस्य रावणादीर्घदर्शिनः। अभिनन्दन्ति भूतानि विनाशे पापकर्मणः॥
en: O Rāvana, every one delight in the destruction of that inconsiderate being, who bring about his own destruction and is engaged in the perpetration of evil deeds.

sn: एवं त्वां पापकर्माणं वक्ष्यन्ति निकृता जनाः। दिष्ट्यैतद् व्यसनं प्राप्तो रौद्र इत्येव हर्षिताः॥
en: In this way, yourself, the perpetrator of vicious acts, meeting with your end, those persons who had been tyrannised by you, shall, delightedly, say, “Oh! blessed are we since this terrible (Raksasa) has met with his end."

sn: शक्या लोभयितुं नाहमैश्वर्येण धनेन वा। अनन्या राघवेणाहं भास्करेण यथा प्रभा॥
en: With wealth or riches you shall not be able to tempt me. As the rays of the sun belong to him, so I am Rāghava's only.

sn: उपधाय भुजं तस्य लोकनाथस्य सत्कृतम्। कथं नामोपधास्यामि भुजमन्यस्य कस्यचित्॥
en: Having laid my head on the beautiful arms of that lord of men, how shall I place it again on another's?

sn: अहमौपयिकी भार्या तस्यैव च धरापतेः। व्रतस्नातस्य विद्येव विप्रस्य विदितात्मनः॥
en: Like the knowledge of one God monopolized by the Brāhmaṇas only, I am the spouse of that lord of earth only, cognisant of higher truths and marrying me according to the pious ceremonials.

sn: साधु रावण रामेण मां समानय दुःखिताम्। वने वासितया सार्धं करेण्वेव गजाधिपम्॥
en: to May good betide you, O Rāvaņa. Do you take me to Rāma, stricken with grief as I am, like to a she-elephant anxiously waiting in the forest brought to the lord of elephants.

sn: मित्रमौपयिकं कर्तुं रामः स्थानं परिप्सता। बन्धं चानिच्छता घोरं त्वयासौ पुरुषर्षभः॥
en: It behove you to make friends with Rāma, that best of men, if do you desire to maintain your empire and do not wish to bring about your own destruction.

sn: विदितः सर्वधर्मज्ञः शरणागतवत्सलः। तेन मैत्री भवतु ते यदि जीवितुमिच्छसि॥
en: It is known to the world, that Rāma know well the sanctions of religion and is kind to them who seek his shelter. Do you seek his friendship, if do you wish to maintain your life.

sn: प्रसादयस्व त्वं चैनं शरणागतवत्सलम्। मां चास्मै प्रयतो भूत्वा निर्यातयितुमर्हसि ॥
en: Do you propitiate him therefore who is kind to his dependents and it become you to take me respectfully to him.

sn: एवं हि ते भवेत् स्वस्ति सम्प्रदाय रघूत्तमे। अन्यथा त्वं हि कुर्वाणः परां प्राप्स्यसि चापदम्॥
en: You shall meet with your well-being if do you in this wise confer me on that best of Raghus. And mighty is the disaster that shall befall you, if do you follow any other procedure.

sn: वर्जयेद् वज्रमुत्सृष्टं वर्जयेदन्तकाश्चिरम्। त्वद्विधं न तु संक्रुद्धो लोकनाथः स राघवः॥
en: Thunderbolt, even, when hurled, may leave you, Death himself may overlook you-but there is no safety for you, if Rāghava, the lord of men is enraged.

sn: रामस्य धनुषः शब्दं श्रोष्यसि त्वं महास्वनम्। शतक्रतुविसृष्टस्य निर्घोषमशनेरिव॥ इह शीघ्रं सुपर्वाणो ज्वलितास्या इवोरगाः। इषवो निपतिष्यन्ति रामलक्ष्मणलक्षिताः॥
en: You shall hear the terrible sound of the twang of Rāma's bow, like to the sound of the thunderbolt hurled by Indra. Soon shall arrows, bearing the names of Rāma and Lakşmaņa and having fiery heads like those of snakes, alight here.

sn: रक्षांसि निहनिष्यन्तः पुर्यामस्यां न संशयः। असम्पातं करिष्यन्ति पतन्तः कङ्कवाससः॥
en: And covered with Kanka leaves they shall undoubtedly cover the whole city and devastate it by destroying all the Rākṣasas.

sn: राक्षसेन्द्र महासन्सि रामगरुडो महान्। उद्धरिष्यति वेगेन वैनतेय इवोरगान्॥
en: Like to Garuda pulling up the snakes, the Garuda like Rāma shall pull up your snake-like Raksasas.

sn: अपनेष्यति मां भर्ता त्वत्तः शीघ्रमरिंदमः। असुरेभ्यः श्रियं दीप्तां विष्णुस्त्रिभिरिव क्रमैः॥
en: Like to Vişņu recovering the effulgent Śrī (the Goddess of wealth) from the Asuras, by crossing over the three worlds with three foot-steps, my husband, the conqueror of foes, shall recover me from you.

sn: जनस्थाने हतस्थाने निहते रक्षसां बले। अशक्तेन त्वया रक्षः कृतमेतदसाधु वै॥
en: Janasthāna has been devastated, the host of Rākṣasas has been killed, and you had been disabled. Truly you had perpetrated an impious deed.

sn: आश्रमं तत्तयोः शून्यं प्रविश्य नरसिंहयोः। गोचरं गतयोर्धात्रोरपनीता त्वयाऽधम॥ नहि गन्धमुपाघ्राय रामलक्ष्मणयोस्त्वया। शक्यं संदर्शने स्थातुं शुना शार्दूलयोरिव ॥
en: O Rākṣasa, those two lions among men going out to enquire about the illusive deer, I was ravished by you, entering the empty hermitage O vile wight. And like to a dog incapable of standing before a tiger, it would have been impossible for you, to wait there in the presence of Rāma and Laksmana.

sn: तस्य ते विग्रहे ताभ्यां युगग्रहणमस्थिरम्। वृत्रस्येवेन्द्रबाहुभ्यां बाहोरेकस्य विग्रहे॥
en: If do you engage in conflict with them, your wealth and friends shall be of no avail to you (and you shall be discomfited) like to onehanded Asura Vſtra by the two handed Indra.* *The allusion is-the mighty Asura Vrtra fought with Indra for a long time even after he had his one hand chopped off.

sn: क्षिप्रं तव सनाथो मे रामः सौमित्रिणा सह । तोयमल्पमिवादित्यः प्राणानादास्यते शरैः॥
en: Soon shall my husband, with the assistance of Lakşmaņa, draw out your life with arrows, like to the sun drying up, by his rays, shallow water.

sn: गिरिं कुबेरस्य गतोऽथवाऽऽलयं सभां गतो वा वरुणस्य राज्ञः। असंशयं दाशरथेविमोक्ष्यसे महाद्रुमः कालहतोऽशनेरिव ॥
en: Whether do you repair to the abode of Kubera, or whether do you, terrified, take refuge to the assembly of Varuna, you shall, for certain, be destroyed by the son of Dasaratha, like to a mighty tree broken down by thunderbolt.

sn: सीताया वचनं श्रुत्वा परुषं राक्षसेश्वरः। प्रत्युवाच ततः सीतां विप्रियं प्रियदर्शनाम्॥
en: Hearing those harsh accents, that lord of Rākṣasas, replied to Sītā, of comely presence, with the following unpleasant words.

sn: यथा यथा सान्त्वयिता वश्यः स्त्रीणां तथा तथा। यथा यथा प्रियं वक्ता परिभूतस्तता तथा॥
en: It is generally found on earth that the more a woman is courted by a man, the more she is brought under his influence, (But for you) the more kindly I have been behaving towards you, the more roughly I have been treated.

sn: संनियच्छति मे क्रोधं त्वयि कामः समुत्थितः। द्रवतो मार्गमासाद्य हयानिव सुसारथिः॥
en: Truly dose my love for you keep in control the wrath like to a good charioteer restraining the swerving steed.

sn: वामः कामो मनुष्याणां यस्मिन् किल निबध्यते। जने तस्मिंस्त्वनुक्रोशः स्नेहश्च किल जायते॥
en: O mighty is amour to men, for on whom this amour fall, albeit she is an object of wrath, becomes an object of kindness and affection.

sn: एतस्मात् कारणान्न त्वां घातयामि वरानने। वधार्हामवमानाहाँ मिथ्या प्रव्रजने रताम्॥
en: O you of fair countenance, it is for this reason, that I do not destroy you, although you, who are engaged in false asceticism, are worthy of being killed and dishonoured. do you

sn: परुषाणि हि वाक्यानि यानि यानि ब्रवीषि माम्। तेषु तेषु वधो युक्तस्तव मैथिलि दारुणः॥
en: O Maithili, for each and every one of all those harsh words which you had used by me, deserve death.

sn: एवमुक्त्वा तु वैदेहीं रावणो राक्षसाधिपः। क्रोधसंरम्भसंयुक्तः सीतामुत्तरमब्रवीत्॥
en: Having spoken thus to Vaidehi, Ravana, the lord of Raksasas, having his wrath subdued, again bespake Sītā.

sn: द्वौ मासौ रक्षितव्यौ मे योऽवधिस्ते मया कृतः। ततः शयनमारोह मम त्वं वरवर्णिनि॥
en: I shall wait for those two months, of which I have made a contract, after which you shall have to share my bed. O you of a comely presence.

sn: द्वाभ्यामूर्ध्वं तु मासाभ्यां भर्तारं मामनिच्छतीम्। मम त्वां प्रातराशार्थे सूदाश्छेत्स्यन्ति खण्डशः॥
en: Even then if you do refuse to regard me as your husband, my cooks shall mince your limbs with steel and serve you for my morning meal.

sn: तां भय॑मानां सम्प्रेक्ष्य राक्षसेन्द्रेण जानकीम्। देवगन्धर्वकन्यास्ता विषेदुर्विकृतेक्षणाः॥
en: Beholding the lord of Rākşasas remonstrate with the daughter of Janaka is this wise, the daughters of the celestials and Gandharvas became exceedingly sorry.

sn: ओष्ठप्रकारैरपरा नेत्रैर्वक्त्रैस्तथापराः। सीतामाश्वासयामासुस्तर्जितां तेन रक्षसा॥
en: Some with lips, some with eyes, and some with gestures of their faces, they all consoled Sita, thus distressed by that Raksasa.

sn: ताभिराश्वासिता सीता रावणं राक्षसाधिपम्। उवाचात्महितं वाक्यं वृत्तशौटीर्यगर्वितम्॥
en: Thus consoled by them, and being proud of her good conduct and her husband's heroism, Sītā thus addressed Rāvana, the lord of Raksasas.

sn: नूनं न ते जनः कश्चिदस्मिन्निःश्रेयसि स्थितः। निवारयति यो न त्वां कर्मणोऽस्माद् विगर्हितात्॥
en: Forsooth there is no person in this city who desire your welfare and therefore prevent you from such an impious deed.

sn: मां हि धर्मात्मनः पत्नीं शचीमिव शचीपतेः। त्वदन्यस्त्रिषु लोकेषु प्रार्थयेन्मनसाऽपि कः॥
en: Who is there in the three worlds, who even desire me in mind, who am the spouse of the virtuous souled (Rāma) like to Indra's Sacī.

sn: राक्षसाधम रामस्य भार्याममिततेजसः। उक्तवानसि यत्पापं व गतस्तस्य मोक्ष्यसे ॥
en: O you the vilest of the Rākşasas, for using those vicious words towards the spouse of Rāma, of immeasured prowess, repairing whither shall you escape vengeance?

sn: यथा दृप्तश्च मातङ्गः शशश्च सहितौ वने। तथा द्विरदवद् रामस्त्वं नीच शशवत्स्मृतः॥
en: Like to an infuriated elephant encountering a hare in the forest, you shall O Vile! a hare as you are, meet with that elephant-like Rāma.

sn: स त्वमिक्ष्वाकुनाथं वै क्षिपनिह न लज्जसे। चक्षुषो विषये तस्य न यावदुपगच्छसि॥
en: You are not ashamed of railing that lord of Ikşvākus, so long as dose you not come within his ken.

sn: इमे ते नयने क्रूरे विकृते कृष्णपिङ्गले। क्षितौ न पतिते कस्मान्मामनार्य निरीक्षतः॥
en: O base! why do not your grim, terrible, coppery eyes, looking so viciously at me, fall down on earth.

sn: तस्य धर्मात्मनः पत्नी स्नुषा दशरथस्य च। कथं व्याहरतो मां ते न जिह्वा पाप शीर्यति ॥
en: O vicious wretch, I am the spouse of that virtuous-souled (Rāma) and daughter-in-law of Dasaratha—using these vile words towards me, why dose not your tongue fall off?

sn: असंदेशात्तु रामस्य तपसश्चानुपालनात्। न त्वां कुर्मि दशग्रीव भस्म भस्मार्हतेजसा॥
en: O Ten-necked one, I can instantly reduce you to ashes but for Rāma's mandate and my ascetic observances.

sn: नापहर्तुमहं शक्या तस्य रामस्य धीमतः। विधिस्तव वधार्थाय विहितो नात्र संशयः॥
en: You could not have ravished me in the presence of the highly intelligent Rāma. And undoubtedly for your destruction this has been brought about by God.

sn: शूरेण धनदभ्रात्रा बलैः समुदितेन च। अपोह्य रामं कस्माच्चिद् दारचौर्यं त्वया कृतम्॥
en: You are heroic and Kubera's brother and great in prowess, why didst you then take me by stealth after despatching Rāma away from the hermitage?”

sn: सीताया वचनं श्रुत्वा रावणो राक्षसाधिपः। विवृत्य नयने क्रूर जानकीमन्ववैक्षत॥
en: Hearing those words of Sītā, Rāvana, the lord of Rāksasas, whirling his grim eyes, looked towards the daughter of Janaka.

sn: नीलजीमूतसंकाशो महाभुजशिरोधरः। सिंहसत्त्वगतिः श्रीमान् दीप्तजिह्वोग्रलोचनः॥
en: He was like to a mass of blue clouds and his arms and necks were long and spacious. He was gifted with elephantine gaits and his tongues and eyes were sharp and flaming.

sn: चलानमुकुटप्रांशुश्चित्रमाल्यानुलेपनः। रक्तमाल्याम्बरधरस्तप्ताङ्गदविभूषणः॥ श्रोणीसूत्रेण महता मेचकेन सुसंवृतः। अमृतोत्पादने नद्धो भुजङ्गनेव मन्दरः॥
en: The top of his crown was shaking and he had charming garland around his neck and his person sprinkled with paste. He had crimson-coloured garlands and clothes on and his charming arms were adorned with ornaments. Encircled with a sword-belt around his waist he appeared like to Mandara, entwined by a snake at the time of the churning of the ocean.

sn: ताभ्यां स परिपूर्णाभ्यां भुजाभ्यां राक्षसेश्वरः। शुशुभेऽचलसंकाशः शृङ्गाभ्यामिव मन्दरः॥
en: With his two plump arms, ihat lord of Rākşasas appeared like to the hill Mandara with its two huge summits.

sn: तरुणादित्यवर्णाभ्यां कुण्डलाभ्यां विभूषितः। रक्तपल्लवपुष्पाभ्यामशोकाभ्यामिवाचलः॥
en: And adorned with a pair of Kundalas (A kind of ornament worn on ears.) resembling the newly risen Sun he looked like a hill covered with two Asoka trees enveloped with crimson flowers and leaves.

sn: स कल्पवृक्षप्रतिमो वसन्त इव मूर्तिमान्। शमशानचैत्यप्रतिमो भूषितोऽपि भयंकरः॥
en: He was like to Kalpa tree (A fabulous tree granting everything desired.) and spring incarnate. And albeit adorned, he looked terrible like to a Caitya (A monument or sculpture raised in honour of a deceased person on the site of a funeral pyre.) on the cremation-ground.

sn: अवेक्षमाणो वैदेही कोपसंरक्तलोचनः। उवाच रावणः सीतां भुजङ्ग इव निःश्वसन्॥
en: And having his eyes red hot with ire, sighing again and again like to a snake and casting his looks upon Sītā, Rāvaņa addressed her again, saying.

sn: अनयेनाभिसम्पन्नमर्थहीनमनुव्रते। नाशायाम्यहमद्य त्वां सूर्यः संध्यामिवौजसा ॥
en: O you following asceticism, this your vow is without any meaning and beyond the pale of morality. Even shall I destroy you today like to the Sun dispelling darkness with his rays.

sn: इत्युक्त्वा मैथिली राजा रावणः शत्रुरावणः। संददर्श ततः सर्वा राक्षसी?रदर्शनाः॥
en: Having thus addressed Maithili, the inimical king Rāvaņa cast his looks towards the grimvisaged Rākşasīs.

sn: एकाक्षीमेककर्णां च कर्णप्रावरणां तथा। गोकर्णी हस्तिकर्णी च लम्बकर्णीमकर्णिकाम्॥ हस्तिपद्यश्वपद्यौ च गोपदीं पादचूलिकाम्। एकाक्षीमेकपादी च पृथुपादीमपादिकाम्॥ अतिमात्रशिरोग्रीवामतिमात्रकुचोदरीम्। अतिमात्रस्यनेत्रां च दीर्घजिह्वानखामपि॥ अनासिकां सिंहमुखीं गोमुखीं सुकरीमुखीम्। यथा मद्वशगा सीता क्षिप्रं भवति जानकी॥ तथा कुरुत राक्षस्यः सर्वाः क्षिप्रं समेत्य वा। प्रतिलोमानुलोमैश्च सामदानादिभेदनैः॥ आवर्जयत वैदेहीं दण्डस्योद्यमनेन च।
en: And among those Rākṣasīs, some had huge ears, some had ears like those of kine, some had ears as long as arms, some had long ears and others were without any. And some had legs like those of an elephant; some had like those of a cow and some had legs covered with hairs. And some had one eye, some had one leg, some had capacious legs and some were without any. And some had huge heads and necks and some had breast and belly beyond proportions and some had faces and eyes above human size. Some had huge tongues and nails. And some were without noses. And some had leonine faces, some had faces like those of kine and some had those of boars. And casting his look towards such Raksasis, he said-You Raksasis, do youall endeavour to bring Sītā, the daughter of Janaka, under my control. By good or bad conduct, by conciliation or gift, by threat or blandishment, do yo so endeavour as Vaidehi's soul night be bent to me.

sn: इति प्रतिसमादिश्य राक्षसेन्द्रः पुनः पुनः॥ काममन्युपरीतात्मा जानकी प्रति गर्जत।
en: And having ordered thus again and again, that lord of Rākşasas, stricken with amour and ire, addressed Sītā, roaring fiercely.

sn: उपगम्य ततः क्षिप्रं राक्षसी धान्यमालिनी॥ परिष्वज्य दशग्रीवमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्।
en: Thereupon approaching speedily and embracing the Ten-necked one, one Rākşasī named Dhānyamālīnī bespoke him.

sn: मया क्रीड महाराज सीतया किं तवानया॥ विवर्णया कृपणया मानुष्या राक्षसेश्वर।
en: Do you sport with me. O great king. What shall you do with her? O lord of Rākşasas-a human being poorly and of a pale countenance.

sn: नूनमस्यां महाराज न देवा भोगसत्चमान्॥ विदधत्यमर श्रेष्ठास्तव बाहुबलार्जितान्।
en: O great king, forsooth, the celestials have not destined for her enjoyment all those objects which you had procured by your prowess.

sn: अकामां कामयानस्य शरीरमुपतप्यते॥ इच्छती कामयानस्य प्रीतिर्भवति शोभना।
en: Again he who desire for an unwilling dame burn his own person—and he who desire for a willing damsel, attain excess of delight.

sn: एवमुक्तस्तु राक्षस्या समुत्क्षिप्तस्ततो बली। प्रहसन् मेघसंकाशो राक्षसः स न्यवर्तत ॥
en: Having said this, the Rākşasī took away Rāvana by force. And that Rākşasa too, resembling a mass of clouds, laughing, turned back.

sn: प्रस्थितः स दशग्रीवः कम्पयन्निव मेदिनीम्। ज्वलद्भास्करसंकाशं प्रविवेश निवेशनम् ॥
en: And that Ten-necked one, strode away as if shaking the whole earth and passed within (his queen's) abode resembling the effulgent Sun.

sn: देवगन्धर्वकन्याश्च नागकन्याश्च तास्ततः। परिवार्य दशग्रीवं प्रविशुस्ता गृहोत्तमम्॥
en: And encircling Rāvana those daughters of celestials Gandharvas and Nāgas, entered into an excellent abode.

sn: स मैथिली धर्मपरामवस्थितां प्रवेपमानं परिभय॑ रावणः। विहाय सीतां मदनेन मोहितः स्वमेव वेश्म प्रविवेश रावणः॥
en: And having remonstrated with and left behind, the firm and pious Sīta with a trembling person, Rāvana, possessed by amour entered into his own palace.

sn: इत्युक्त्वा मैथिली राजा रावणः शत्रुरावणः। संदिश्य च ततः सर्वा राक्षसीर्निर्जगाम ह॥
en: Having spoken thus Maithili and commanded the host of the Räksasīs, Rāvana, a terror to his enemies, went away.

sn: निष्क्रान्ते राक्षसेन्द्रे तु पुनरन्तःपुरं गते। राक्षस्यो भीमरूपास्ताः सीतां समभिदुद्रुवुः॥
en: And after that lord of Rākşasas had gone away and entered his inner apartment, the hideous Rākşasīs drew near Sitä.

sn: ततः सीतामुपागम्य राक्षस्यः क्रोधमूर्छिताः। परं परुषया वाचा वैदेहीमिदमब्रुवन्॥
en: And approaching Sītā that terrible host, almost faint with ire, addressed Vaidehī with the following harsh words.

sn: पौलस्त्यस्य वरिष्ठस्य रावणस्य महात्मनः। दशग्रीवस्य भार्यात्वं सीते न बहु मन्यसे॥
en: You do not regard it highly, Sītā, that you shall become the chosen wife of that highsouled, and great Ravana, the Ten-necked son of Paulastya.

sn: ततस्त्वेकजटा नाम राक्षसी वाक्यमब्रवीत्। आमन्त्र्य क्रोधताम्राक्षी सीतां करतलोदरोम्॥
en: Thereupon another Rākṣasī named Ekjatä, with eyes rendered coppery with ire, addressing Sītā, having a small navel, said.

sn: प्रजापतीनां षण्णां तु चतुर्थोऽयं प्रजापतिः। मानसो ब्रह्मणः पुत्रः पुलस्त्य इति विश्रुतः॥
en: Pulastya is the fourth of the six Prajāpatīs, (Prajāpatis are the lords of the created being first created by Brahmā.) a mind-born son of Brahmā and celebrated in the world.

sn: पुलस्त्यस्य तु तेजस्वी महर्षिर्मानसः सुतः। नाम्ना स विश्रवा नाम प्रजापतिसमप्रभः॥
en: The glorious ascetic, by name Vishravā was the mind-born son to Pulastya, effulgent like to Prajāpatis.

sn: तस्य पुत्रो विशालाक्षि रावणः शत्रुरावणः। तस्य त्वं राक्षसेन्द्रस्य भार्या भवितुमर्हसि॥ मयोक्तं चारुसर्वाङ्गि वाक्यं किं नानुमन्यसे।
en: O large-eyed damsel! Of Visravā came Rāvana terrible to his enemies. And it behove you to become the consort of that lord of Raksasas. Scorn not the words I say to you, O you of comely presence.”

sn: ततो हरिजटा नाम राक्षसी वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥ विवृत्य नयने कोपान्मार्जारसदृशेक्षणा। येन देवास्त्रयस्त्रिंशद् देवराजश्च निर्जितः॥ तस्य त्वं राक्षसेन्द्रस्य भार्या भवितुमर्हसि।
en: Thereupon another Rākşasī named Harijatā, having the eyes of a cat, and whirling them with ire, said It become you to be the wife of that lord of Rākşasas who smote the thirty three celestials and their lord in battle.

sn: वीर्योत्सिक्तस्य शूरस्य संग्रामेष्वनिवर्तिनः। बलिनो वीर्ययुक्तस्य भार्यात्वं किं न लिप्ससे॥
en: Do you not desire to be his wife, who is heroic, of indomitable prowess and who dose not turn back in battle?

sn: प्रियां बहुमतां भार्यां त्यक्त्वा राजा महाबलः। सर्वासां च महाभागां त्वामुपैष्यति रावणः॥ समृद्धं स्त्रीसहस्रेण नानारत्नोपशोभितम्। अन्तःपुरं तदुत्सृज्य त्वामुपैष्यति रावणः॥
en: And turning away in scorn from his beloved wife, highly esteemed, the mighty king Ravana, desire for you. And leaving his inner apartment enriched with thousand of females and adorned with various jewels, Rāvana shall adore you.

sn: अन्या तु विकटा नाम राक्षसी वाक्यमब्रवीत्। असकृद् भीमवीर्येण नागा गन्धर्वदानवाः। निर्जिताः समरे येन स ते पार्श्वमुपागतः॥ तस्य सर्वसमृद्धस्य रावणस्य महात्मनः। किमर्थं राक्षसेन्द्रस्य भार्यात्वं नेच्छसेऽधमे ॥
en: And then followed another Rākşasī by name Vikatā, “The king, who by his terrible prowess subdued the Gandharvas (Heavenly singers and musicians who belong to the heaven of Indra.) and Nāgas, (Serpent-gods who dwell in the regions under the carth.) in battle, has stood by you. O foolish damsel, why do you not wish to be the consort of that high-souled lord of Rākşasas-Rāvana, gifted with wealth and riches."

sn: ततस्तां दुर्मुखी नाम राक्षसी वाक्यमब्रवीत्। यस्य सूर्यो न तपति भीतो यस्य स मारुतः। न वाति स्मायतापाङ्गि किं त्वं तस्य न तिष्ठसे॥
en: Then followed another Rākşaşī named Durmukhi. “Why dose you not approach him, O you having expansive eyes, by whose fear, the sun dose not shine, and the wind dose not blow."

sn: पुष्पवृष्टिं च तरवो मुमुचुर्यस्य वै भयात्। शैलाः सुनुवुः पानीयं जलदाश्च यदेच्छति॥ तस्य नैऋतराजस्य राजराजस्य भामिनि। किं त्वं न कुरुषे बुद्धिं भार्यार्थे रावणस्य हि॥
en: O dame, why do you not wish to be the consort of Rāvana, the lord of Rākṣasas, at whose command the trees shower blossoms and the hills and clouds pour down water. Why do you not make up your mind to be the wife of Rāvana?

sn: साधु ते तत्त्वतो देवी कथितं साधु भामिनि। गृहाण सुस्मिते वाक्यमन्यथा न भविष्यसि ॥
en: O damsel, O worshipful dame, we have spoken thus for your welfare. Do you comply with our request or you shall surely die. CECTION 24

sn: ततः सीतां समस्तास्ता राक्षस्यो विकृताननाः। परुषं परुषानर्हामूचुस्तद्वाक्यमप्रियम्॥
en: Thereupon all those Rākşasīs, having terrible faces again and again pursued Sitä with reproaches rough and rude.

sn: किं त्वमन्तःपुरे सीते सर्वभूतमनोरमे। महार्हशयनोपेते न वासमनुमन्यसे॥
en: Why do you not desire, O Sītā, to live in his inner apartment, liked by all and abounding in costly bed-steads.

sn: मानुषे मानुषस्यैव भार्यात्वं बहु मन्यसे। प्रत्याहर मनो रामानैवं जातु भविष्यति॥
en: O woman, you regardest highly to be the wife of a man. Do you turn back from Rāma-your desire shall never be satisfied.

sn: त्रैलोक्यवसुभोक्तारं रावणं राक्षसेश्वरम्। भर्तारमुपसंगम्य विहरस्व यथासुखम्॥
en: Do you spend happily your days with our lord-Rāvaņa, the Rākşasa chief, who makes his own the treasures of the three worlds.

sn: मानुषी मानुषं तं तु राममिच्छसि शोभने। राज्याद् भ्रष्टमसिद्धार्थं विक्लवन्तमनिन्दिते॥
en: You are a woman, O you of comely presence, and therefore dose your fancy cling to Rāma, O you of a blameless countenance, who is a man, deprived of his kingdom, overwhelmed with disasters and has his desires frustrated.

sn: राक्षसीनां वचः श्रुत्वा सीता पद्मनिभेक्षणा। नेत्राभ्यामश्रुपूर्णाभ्यामिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Hearing the words of those Rākşasīs, the lotus-eyed Sītā, with her eyes full of tears said.

sn: यदिदं लोकविद्विष्टमुदाहरत संगताः। नैतन्मनसि वाक्यं मे किल्विषं प्रतितिष्ठति॥
en: What you have all said and which is against human usage and vicious, dose not find place in my mind.

sn: न मानुषी राक्षसस्य भार्या भवितुमर्हति। कामं खादत मां सर्वा न करिष्यामि वो वचः॥
en: A woman cannot be the wife of a Rākşasa. Eat me up if you will, I will never follow your words.

sn: दीनो वा राज्यहीनो वा यो मे भर्ता स मे गुरुः। तं नित्यमनुरक्ताऽस्मि यथा सूर्यं सुवर्चला॥
en: Poor or deprived of kingdom, he who is my husband, is my preceptor. I am ever devoted to him, like Suvarcalā (The wife of the sun) to the Sun.

sn: यथा शची महाभागा शक्रं समुपतिष्ठति। अरुन्धती वसिष्ठं च रोहिणी शशिनं यथा॥ लोपामुद्रा यथाऽगस्त्यं सुकन्या च्यवनं यथा। सावित्री सत्यवन्तं च कपिलं श्रीमती यथा॥ सौदासं मदयन्तीव केशिनी सगरं यथा। नैषधं दमयन्तीव भैमी पतिमनुव्रता॥ तथाहमिक्ष्वाकुवरं रामं पतिमनुव्रता।
en: Like to the great ſacī standing by Sakra, Arundhati by Vasista, Rohini by the Moon, Lopamudrā by Agastya, Sukanyā by Cyavana, Sāvitrī by Satyavana, Śrīmatī by Kapila, Madayanti by Saudāsa, Kešinī by Sagara and Damayantī the daughter of the king Bhaimnī by her husband Nala, I shall ever remain devoted to my husband Rāma, the foremost of the descendants of lksvaku.

sn: सीताया वचनं श्रुत्वा राक्षस्यः क्रोधमूर्च्छिताः। भर्ल्सयन्ति स्म परुषैर्वाक्यै रावणचोदिताः॥
en: Hearing the words of Sītā, all those Rākşasīs despatched by Rāvana, almost beside themselves with ire, again covered her with reproaches rough and rude.

sn: अवलीनः स निर्वाक्यो हनुमाशिशपादुमे। सीतां संतर्जयन्तीस्ता राक्षसीरशृणोत् कपिः॥
en: Hanumān remained all along speechless and hidden on the ſinsapā tree. And that monkey heard all those demons remonstrate with Sītā in this way.

sn: तामभिक्रम्य संरब्धा वेपमानां समन्ततः। भृशं संलिलिहुर्दीप्तान् प्रलम्बान् दशनच्छदान्॥
en: Those, influenced with ire, approached the trembling Sītā and encircling her, licked again and again their long a burning lips.

sn: ऊचुश्च परमक्रुद्धाः प्रगृह्याशु परश्वधान्। नेयमर्हति भर्तारं रावणं राक्षसाधिपम्॥
en: Taking up instantly spears, they exceedingly wroth, menaced her, saying— "she is not worthy of having Rāvana, the lord of the Rākşasas, as her lord."

sn: सा भय॑माना भीमाभी राक्षसीभिर्वराङ्गना। सा वाष्पमपमार्जन्ती शिंशपां तामुपागमत्॥
en: Being thus remonstrated with by those terrible Raksasis, that excellent damsel, shedding tears, neared the ſinsapa tree.

sn: ततस्तां शिंशपां सीता राक्षसीभिः समावृता। अभिगम्य विशालाक्षी तस्थौ शोकपरिप्लुता॥ तां कृशां दीनवदनां मलिनाम्बरवासिनीम्। भर्त्सयांचक्रिरे भीमा राक्षस्यस्ताः समन्ततः॥
en: The large eyed Sītā, encircled by the Rākşasīs, remained there sunk in grief. And all those hideous demons, showered reproaches, from all sides, on her, greatly reduced, of a poorly countenance, and wearing a soiled cloth.

sn: ततस्तु विनता नाम राक्षसी भीमदर्शना। अब्रवीत् कुपिताकारा कराला निर्णतोदरी॥
en: Thereupon a grim-visaged demon, angry, having hideous teeth and a huge belly extending downwards, by name Vinatā, spoke, saying:

sn: सीते पर्याप्तमेतावद् भर्तुः स्नेहः प्रदर्शितः। सर्वत्रातिकृतं भद्रे व्यसनायोपकल्पते॥
en: O Sītā, you had shown enough of attachment towards your husband. But, O gentle dame, excess of any thing tends to evil.

sn: परितुष्टास्मि भद्रं ते मानुषस्ते कृतो विधिः। ममापि तु वचः पथ्यं ब्रुवन्त्याः कुरु मैथिलि॥
en: We are satisfied. And may good betide you! You had acted worthily like a woman. do you hear, O Maithili, what I say for your welfare.

sn: रावणं भज भर्तारं भर्तारं सर्वरक्षसाम्। विक्रान्तमापतन्तं च सुरेशमिव वासवम्॥ दक्षिणं त्यागशीलं च सर्वस्य प्रियवादिनम्। मानुषं कृपणं रामं त्यक्त्वा रावणमाश्रय॥
en: Do you accept, Rāvana, the lord of the Rākşasa host, as your husband. He withstands powerfully his enemies like to Vāsava, the lord of the celestials, charitable, kind to all, and sweet-speeched. And forsaking Rāma, a poor wight, do you take Rāvana (as your husband)

sn: दिव्याङ्गरागा वैदेहि दिव्याभरणभूषिता। अद्यप्रभृति लोकानां सर्वेषामीश्वरी भव॥ अग्नेः स्वाहा यथा देवी शची वेन्द्रस्य शोभने। किं ते रामेण वैदेहि कृपणेन गतायुषा॥
en: Having your person sprinkled with celestial paste and adorned with excellent ornaments, do you from today O Vaidehī, O you of comely presence, become the queen of all the worlds, like to Sachee of the lord of the celestials and svāhā (An exclamation used in making an oblation to the Gods. A personification of the preceding as the wife of fire and Goddess presiding over burnt offerings.) of the fire. What shall you do with Rama, O Vaidehi, poor and of limited life?

sn: एतदुक्तं च मे वाक्यं यदि त्वं न करिष्यसि। अस्मिन् मुहूर्ते सर्वास्त्वां भक्षयिष्यामहे वयम्॥
en: This is what I say and if do you not follow it we shall all instantly banquet on you.

sn: अन्या तु विकटा नाम लम्बमानपयोधरा। अब्रवीत् कुपिता सीतां मुष्टिमुद्यम्य तर्जती॥
en: Thereupon another Rākşasi named Vikață. having her breast hanging long, exercised with ire, and clinching her fist, addressed, roaring, Sita.

sn: बहून्यप्रतिरूपाणि वचनानि सुदुर्मते। अनुक्रोशान्मृदुत्वाच्च सोढानि तव मैथिलि॥
en: O foolish daughter of the king of Mithilā, we have put up with all your foolish words only out of compassion, and because you are a feeble being.

sn: न च नः कुरुषे वाक्यं हितं कालपुरस्कृतम्। आनीतासि समुद्रस्य पारमन्यैर्दुरासदम्॥ रावणान्तःपुरे घोरे प्रविष्टा चासि मैथिलि। रावणस्य गृहे रुद्धा अस्माभिस्त्वभिरक्षिता॥
en: It will not lead to your well-being if you do not hear our words. You had been brought here, the other side of the ocean, difficult of being approached by others. You had come within the terrible abode of Rāvana O Maithili, and had been shut up in his room guarded by us all.

sn: न त्वां शक्तः परित्रातुमपि साक्षात् पुरंदरः। कुरुष्व हितवादिन्या वचनं मम मैथिलि।॥
en: And even, Purandara's (Another name of Indra-the lord of the celestials.) self cannot save yoll. Do you therefore hear, O Maithili, my well-mcaning words.

sn: अलमश्रुनिपातेन त्यज शोकमनर्थकम्। भज प्रीतिं प्रहर्षं च त्यजन्ती नित्यदैन्यताम्॥
en: Why do you shed tears? Renounce your useless grief. Do you become happy and delighted, renouncing your continued melancholy.

sn: सीते राक्षसराजेन परिक्रीड यथासुखम्। जानीमहे यथा भीरु स्त्रीणां यौवनमध्रुवम्॥
en: Do you sport, O Sītā, at your pleasure, with the lord of the Rākşasas. We know, for certain, O timid damsel, that the youth of the females, is very transient.

sn: यावन्न ते व्यतिक्रामेत् तावद् सुखमवाप्नुहि। उद्यानानि च रम्याणि पर्वतोपवनानि च॥ सह राक्षसराजेन चर त्वं मदिरेक्षणे। स्त्रीसहस्राणि ते देवि वशे स्थास्यन्ति सुन्दरि॥ रावणं भज भर्तारं भर्तारं सर्वरक्षसाम्।
en: And so long as your youth dose not fade, do you pass your days happily, O you having inebriate eyes, with the lord of Rākşasas, in picturesque gardens, and mountain forests. Do you take, O fair damsel, Ravana, the lord of the Rākşasas, for your husband, and thousands of females shall be placed at your service.

sn: उत्पाट्य वा ते हृदयं भक्षयिष्यामि मैथिलि॥ यदि मे व्याहृतं वाक्यं न यथावत् करिष्यसि।
en: If do you not follow, what I say, O Maithili, I shall taking out your heart, banquet on it.

sn: ततश्चण्डोदरी नाम राक्षसी क्रूरदर्शना॥ भ्रामयन्ती महच्छूलमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्। इमां हरिणशावाक्षीं त्रासोत्कम्पपयोधराम्॥ रावणेन हतां दृष्ट्वा दौर्हदो मे महानयम्। यकृत्प्लीहं महत् क्रोडं हृदयं च सबन्धनम्॥ गावाण्यपि तथा शीर्षं खादेयमिति मे मतिः।
en: Thereupon another grim-visaged Rākşasī, named, Candodarī, shaking her terrible spear, said-“Beholding this Sitā having the eyes of a young antelope and her breast trembling with fear, my earnest desire, as I am enciente, has been to banquet on her large eyes, lever, spleen, her plump hands, heart, other limbs and head."

sn: ततस्तु प्रघसा नाम राक्षसी वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥ कण्ठमस्या नृशंसायाः पीडयामः किमास्यते। निवेद्यतां ततो राज्ञे मानुषी सा मृतेति ह।॥ नात्र कश्चन संदेहः खादतेति स वक्ष्यति।
en: Thereupon another Rākşasī named Praghasă and-"I shall grind the throat of this cruel woman. What are you doing, sitting here? You shall then relate to the king that the woman is dead. And undoubtedly he shall say 'Do you eat her up."

sn: ततस्त्वजामुखी नाम राक्षसी वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥ विशस्येमां ततः सर्वान् समान् कुरुत पिण्डकान्। विभजाम ततः सर्वा विवादो मे न रोचते॥ पेयमानीयतां क्षिप्रं माल्यं च विविधं बहु।
en: And thereupon another Räkşasi named Ajāmukhi said, “I do not like quarrels. Let us all divide her into equal portions. Bring soon our favourite drink and various garlands."

sn: ततः शूर्पणखा नाम राक्षसी वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥ अजामुख्या यदुक्तं वै तदेव मम रोचते। सुरा चानीयतां क्षिप्रं सर्वशोकविनाशिनी॥ मानुषं मांसमास्वाद्य नृत्यामोऽथ निकुम्भिलाम्।
en: Then followed another Rākşasí by name Śūrpanakha, I do fully concur with what Ajāmukhi has said. Bring soon wine, the remover of all griefs. Banqueting on human flesh I shall dance before the queen Nikumbhilă.

sn: एवं निर्भय॑माना सा सीता सुरसुतोपमा। राक्षसीभिर्विरूपाभिधैर्यमुत्सृज्य रोदिति ॥
en: Being thus threatened by those grim-visaged Rākṣasīs Sītā, resembling the daughter of a celestial, renouncing patience, began to weep.

sn: अथ तासां वदन्तीनां परुषं दारुणं बहु। राक्षसीनामसौम्यानां रुरोद जनकात्मजा ॥
en: Those hideous Rākşasīs thus threatening her with reproaches rude and rough, the daughter of the king Janaka began to weep.

sn: एवमुक्ता तु वैदेही राक्षसीभिर्मनस्विनी। उवाच परमवस्ता वाष्यगद्गदया गिरा॥
en: And being thus addressed by those Rākşasīs, Vaidehi, of subdued soul, being greatly terrified, said, having her voice choked with vapour.

sn: न मानुषी राक्षसस्य भार्या भवितुमर्हति। कामं खादत मां सर्वा न करिष्यामि वो वचः॥
en: A woman can never be the wife of a Räksasa. Eat ine up if you will, I shall never follow your words.

sn: सा राक्षसीमध्यगता सीता सुरसुतोपमा। न शर्म लेभे शोकार्ता रावणेनेव भर्त्तिता ॥
en: And being surrounded by the Rākṣasīs and threatened by Rāvana, Sītă, resembling the daughter of a celestial, stricken with grief, could not console herself.

sn: वेपते स्माधिकं सीता विशन्तीवाङ्गमात्मनः। वने यूथपरिभ्रष्टा मृगी कोकैरिवादिता ॥
en: And trembling, she shrank from their presence like to a strayed fawn surrounded by wolves.

sn: सा त्वशोकस्य विपुलां शाखामालम्ब्य पुष्पिताम्। चिन्तयामास शोकेन भर्तारं भग्नमानसा ॥
en: And resorting to a flowery branch of an Asoka tree, she sunk in grief, thought upon her lord.

sn: सा स्नापयन्ती विपुलौ स्तनौ नेत्रजलस्रवैः। चिन्तयन्ती न शोकस्य तदान्तमधिगच्छति। ७१३
en: With tears she bathed her beautiful breast and oppressed with woe, she could not reach the other bank of the ocean of grief.

sn: सा वेपमाना पतिता प्रवाते कदली यथा। राक्षसीनां भयवस्ता विवर्णवदनाभवत्॥
en: Like a plantain tree shaken by the breeze, she shook and fell down trembling (on the earth). And being afraid of the Rākşasīs, her cheeks forsook their native hue.

sn: तस्याः सा दीर्घबहुला वेपन्त्याः सीतया तदा। ददृशे कम्पिता वेणी व्यालीव परिसर्पती ॥
en: And herself trembling, her pretty long lock of hair also shook and appeared like a serpent moving this way and that.

sn: सा निःश्वसन्ती शोकार्ता कोपोपहतचेतना। आर्ता व्यसृजदश्रूणि मैथिली विललाप च॥ हा रामेति च दुःखार्ता हा पुनर्लक्ष्यणेति च। हा श्वश्रूर्मम कौसल्ये हा सुमित्रेति भामिनी ॥ लोकप्रवादः सत्योऽयं पण्डितैः समुदाहृतः। अकाले दुर्लभो मृत्युः स्त्रिया वा पुरुषस्य वा॥
en: Overwhelmed with grief and beside herself with ire, the daughter of the king of Mithilā, wept and exclaimed sorrowfully, O Rāma, and again, O Laksmana, O mother Kausalyā! O queen Sumitrā! true is the saying of the wise that death dose never approach untimely the male or the female.

sn: यत्राहमाभिः क्रूराभी राक्षसीभिरिहार्दिता । जीवामि हीना रामेण मुहूर्तमपि दुःखिता॥
en: Or else I would not have lived for a moment, separated from Rama and oppressed by the Raksasis as I am.

sn: एषाल्पपुण्या कृपणा विनशिष्याम्यनाथवत्। समुद्रमध्ये नौः पूर्णा वायुवेगैरिवाहता॥
en: Limited is my virtue, and therefore I am to die the death of a poor deserted thing like to a bark driven by the blast in the midst of the ocean.

sn: भर्तारं तमपश्यन्ती राक्षसीवशमागता। सीदामि खलु शोकेन कूलं तोयहतं यथा॥
en: Debarred from my husband's sight and tortured by the hideous demons, I shall sink, oppressed with woes, like to the banks of a river, washed by the water.

sn: तं पद्मदलपत्राक्षं सिंहविक्रान्तगामिनम्। धन्याः पश्यन्ति मे नाथं कृतज्ञं प्रियवादिनम्॥
en: Oh blest are they who have been resting their eyes upon my grateful and sweet-speeched lord of leonine gaits, having eyes resembling lotus petals!

sn: सर्वथा तेन हीनाया रामेण विदितात्मना। तीक्ष्णं विषमिवास्वाद्य दुर्लभं मम जीवनम् ॥
en: And separated from Rāma of subdued soul, it is as difficult for me to breathe as for him who has drank up virulent poison.

sn: कीदृशं तु महापापं मया देहान्तरे कृतम्। येनेदं प्राप्यते घोरं महादुःखं सुदारुणम्॥
en: What mighty iniquity had I perpetrated in my previous existence that I have met with this terrible disaster!

sn: जीवितं त्यक्तुमिच्छामि शोकेन महता वृता। राक्षसीभिश्च रक्षन्त्या रामो नासाद्यते मया॥
en: I wish to renounce my life under this load of grief-but alas! I am surrounded by the Raks asis and cannot meet Rāma.

sn: धिगस्तु खलु मानुष्यं धिगस्तु परवश्यताम्। न शक्यं यत्परित्यक्तुमात्मच्छन्देन जीवितम्॥
en: Oh! cursed is this subject human life, that they cannot renounce it even at their pleasure!

sn: प्रसक्ताश्रुमुखी त्वेवं ब्रुवती जनकात्मजा। अधोगतमुखी बाला विलप्तुमुपचक्रमे॥ उन्मत्तेव प्रमत्तेव भ्रान्तचित्तेव शोचती। उपावृत्ता किशोरीव विचेष्टन्ती महीतले॥
en: Saying this, the daughter of the king Janaka, bathed her countenance with tears and hanging down her head began to lament. And she began to roll on the earth like to a colt as if she was mad, possessed by a devil and had lost her sense.

sn: राघवस्य प्रमत्तस्य रक्षसा कामरूपिणा। रावणेन प्रमथ्याहमानीता क्रोशती बलात्॥
en: I, the spouse of Rāma, who was drawn away at a distance by the Rākşasa (Mārīca) assuming shapes at will, was seized and borne away by Rāvana.

sn: राक्षसीवशमापना भय॑माना च दारुणम्। चिन्तयन्ती सुदुःखार्ता नाहं जीवितुमुत्सहे ॥
en: A captive of the Rākşasis, subject to their terrible threats and taunts, sunk in grief and anxiety, I desire not to keep my life.

sn: नहि मे जीवितेनार्थो नैवार्थेन च भूषणैः। वसन्त्या राक्षसीमध्ये विना रामं महारथम्॥
en: Of what avail are wealth, ornament and life to me, who am living in the midst of the Răkşasas and separated from Ráma, of the mighty car?

sn: अश्मसारमिदं नूनमथवाप्यजरामरम्। हृदयं मम येनेदं न दुःखेन विशीर्यते॥
en: Forsooth my my life is is made of stone, imperishable and immortal since it is not riven asunder even by this mighty grief.

sn: धिङ्गमनार्यामसती याहं तेन विना कृता। मुहूर्तमपि जीवामि जीवितं पापजीविका॥
en: Woe to me! who am unchaste and vile and my life is vicious, since breathe I still in the absence of my lord.

sn: चरणेनापि सव्येन न स्पृशेयं निशाचरम्। रावणं किं पुनरहं कामयेयं निशाचरम्॥
en: What of fixing my fancy on that night-ranger Rāvaņa, my meaner foot even shall not touch him?

sn: प्रत्याख्यानं न जानाति नात्मानं नात्मनः कुलम्। यो नृशंसस्वभावेन मां प्रार्थयितुमिच्छति॥
en: That (demon) who is courting me in this terrible way, does not know himself, his own race and that I loathe him so much.

sn: छिन्ना भिन्ना प्रभिन्ना वा दीप्ता वाग्नौ प्रदीपिता। रावणं नोपतिष्ठेयं किं प्रलापेन वश्चिरम्॥
en: What more shall I speak to you, I shall never consent to Rāvana's prayer, I might be rent from limb to limb or burnt in fire.

sn: ख्यातः प्राज्ञः कृतज्ञश्च सानुक्रोशश्च राघवः। सवृत्तो निरनुक्रोशः शङ्के मद्भाग्यसंक्षयात्॥
en: Rāghava is grateful, true, wise and kind. I fear it is through my ill-luck that he dose not feel pity for me.

sn: राक्षसानां जनस्थाने सहस्राणि चतुर्दश। एकेनैव निरस्तानि स मां किं नाभिपद्यते॥
en: Will he not take me back who alone slew the thousands of the Rākşasas in Janasthāna?

sn: निरुद्धा रावणेनाहमल्पवीर्येण रक्षसा। समर्थः खलु मे भर्ता रावणं हन्तुमाहवे॥
en: I have been captured by Rāvana, a Rākşasa of feeble prowess. Forsooth my lord is capable of slaying this Rāvana in conflict.

sn: विराधो दण्डकारण्ये येन राक्षसपुङ्गवः। रणे रामेण निहतः स मां किं नाभिपद्यते॥
en: Will not that Rāma regain me, by whom was killed in the forest of Dandaka, Virādha, the foremost of the Rākṣasa crew?

sn: कामं मध्ये समुद्रस्य लङ्केयं दुष्प्रधर्षणा। न तु राघवबाणानां गतिरोधो भविष्यति॥
en: Although situated in the midst of the ocean, Lankā is unapproachable by others, but Raghava's arrows shall also reach here.

sn: किं तु तत् कारणं येन रामो दृढपराक्रमः। रक्षसापहृतां भार्यामिष्टां यो नाभिपद्यते॥
en: (I am at a loss to ascertain) why Rāma of firm prowess, dose not regain me, his beloved spouse who have been borne away by the Räkşasa.

sn: इहस्थां मां न जानीते शङ्के लक्ष्मणपूर्वजः। जानन्नपि स तेजस्वी धर्षणां मर्षयिष्यति ॥
en: Methinks Rāma dose not know that I am here, or else, powerful as he is, he would not have put up with this insult.

sn: हृतेति मां योऽधिगत्य राघवाय निवेदयेत्। गृध्रराजोऽपि स रणे रावणेन निपातितः॥
en: That lord of vultures, who could have informed Rāghava, of my being born away by the Rākṣasa, was killed by Rāvana in the battle.

sn: कृतं कर्म महत् तेन मां तथाभ्यवपद्यता। तिष्ठता रावणवधे वृद्धेनापि जटायुषा॥
en: O great was the work done by him, who, old as he was, for my sake, addressed himself to bring about Rāvana's destruction.

sn: यदि मामिह जानीयाद् वर्तमानां हि राघवः। अद्य बाणैरभिक्रुद्धः कुर्याल्लोकमराक्षसम्॥
en: If Rāghava could know that I was here, he, exceedingly wroth, would have cleared the earth with his arrows, of the Raksasas.

sn: निर्दहेच्च पुरीं लङ्कां निर्दहेच्च महोदधिम्। रावणस्य च नीचस्य कीर्तिं नाम च नाशयेत्॥
en: He would have then burnt down the city of Lankā, dried up the deep and blotted out the name and fame of Rāvana.

sn: ततो निहतनाथानां राक्षसीनां गृहे गृहे। यथाहमेवं रुदती तथा भूयो न संशयः॥
en: And from each ruined home would have risen the Rākşasa widow's groans and cries like to those of mine.

sn: अन्विष्य रक्षसां लङ्का कुर्याद् रामः सलक्ष्मणः। नहि ताभ्यां रिपुर्दृष्टो मुहूर्तमपि जीवति ॥
en: Instituting enquiries, along with Lakṣmaṇa, he shall soon reduce Lankā to this plight. And observed by them the enemy shall not live for a moment.

sn: चिताधूमाकुलपथा गृध्रमण्डलमण्डिता। अचिरेणैव कालेन श्मशानसदृशी भवेत्॥
en: And in no time, shall Lankā, assume the appearance of a cremation ground, having all her high ways enveloped with smoke issuing out of the funeral pyres, and filled with vultures.

sn: अचिरेणैव कालेन प्राप्स्याम्येनं मनोरथम्। दुष्प्रस्थानोऽयमाभाति सर्वेषां वो विपर्ययः॥
en: And soon shall this desire of mine be fulfilled. All these words of mine do sound improbable now but they all indicate your misfortune.

sn: यादृशानि तु दृश्यन्ते लङ्कायामशुभानि तु। अचिरेणैव कालेन भविष्यति हतप्रभा ॥
en: Besides from these bad omens, that are to be seen here, it appear, that Lankä shall soon be shorn of her grace.

sn: नूनं लङ्का हते पापे रावणे राक्षसाधिये। शोषमेष्यति दुर्धर्षा प्रमदा विधवा यथा॥
en: The lord of the Rākşasas, the vicious Rāvana being killed, forsooth shall Lankā, divested of wealth, appear like a widow.

sn: पुण्योत्सवसमृद्धा च नष्टभी सराक्षसा। भविष्यति पुरी लङ्का नष्टभर्ती यथाङ्गना॥
en: This Lankā, which is now full of pious ceremonies, shall, on the death of the Rākṣasas and their master, appear like a husbandless woman.

sn: नूनं राक्षसकन्यानां रुदतीनां गृहे गृहे। श्रोष्यामि नचिरादेव दुःखार्तानामिह ध्वनिम्॥
en: For certain, shall I soon hear the cries and groans in every house, of the daughters of the Rākşasas worn with grief.

sn: सान्धकारा हतद्योता हतराक्षसपुङ्गवा। भविष्यति पुरी लङ्का निर्दग्धा रामसायकैः॥ यदि नाम स शूरो मां रामो रक्तान्तलोचनः। जानीयाद् वर्तमानां यां राक्षसस्य निवेशने॥
en: If that heroic Rāma, having dark-blue eyes, comes to know that I am in the abode of the Rākşasas, the city of Lankā shall be burnt down with his arrows and shall be stricken with darkness and shorn of grace and all the foremost of the Rākşasas shall be destroyed.

sn: अनेन तु नृशंसेन रावणेनाधमेन मे। समयो यस्तु निर्दिष्टस्तस्य कालोऽयमागतः॥
en: The time which was appointed by the vile and cruel Rāvana, has arrived.

sn: स च मे विहितो मृत्युरस्मिन् दुष्टेन वर्तते। अकार्यं ये न जानन्ति नैर्ऋताः पापकारिणः॥
en: And that vicious wretch has resolved to destroy me now. There is no crime which cannot be perpetrated by those vicious demons.

sn: अधर्मात् तु महोत्पातो भविष्यति हि साम्प्रतम्। नैते धर्मं विजानन्ति राक्षसाः पिशिताशनाः॥
en: Mighty is the disaster that shall arise on account of this crime—the Räkşasas who live on flesh do not know what virtue is.

sn: ध्रुवं मां प्रातराशार्थं राक्षस: कल्पयिष्यति। साहं कथं करिष्यामि तं बिना प्रियदर्शनम्॥
en: Forsooth shall the Raksasa serve me for his morning meal. What shall I do without my lord of comely presence?

sn: रामं रक्तान्तनयनमपश्यन्ती सुदु:खिता। क्षिप्रं वैवस्वतं देवं पश्येयं पतिना विना ॥
en: Debarred from my husband's presence, stricken with grief and not beholding Rāma, having dark-blue eyes, I shall soon meet with death.

sn: नाजानाज्जीवती रामः स मां भरतपूर्वजः। जानन्तौ तु न कुर्यात्तां नो। हि परिमार्गणम्॥
en: Rāma, the elder brother of Bharata, dose not know that I am still alive or else he and Lakşmaņa would have ransacked the whole world for me.

sn: नूनं ममैव शोकेन स वीरो लक्ष्मणाग्रजः। देवलोकमितो यातस्त्यक्त्वा देहं महीतले॥
en: Or renouncing his body on this earth for my grief, the heroic elder brother of Lakşmaņa, has repaired to the celestial region.

sn: धन्या देवाः सगन्धर्वाः सिद्धाश्व परमर्षयः। मम पश्यन्ति ये वीरं रामं राजीवलोचनम्॥
en: Blessed the celestials, Gandharvas, Siddhās and mighty ascetics who are beholding my heroic lotus-eyed Rāma.

sn: अथवा नहि तस्यार्थो धर्मकामस्य धीमतः। मया रामस्य राजर्षेर्भार्यया परमात्मनः॥
en: Or that highly intelligent royal ascetic desirous of securing piety and freed from the troubles of life, has no need of a wife like me.

sn: दृश्यमाने भवेत् प्रीतिः सौहृदं नास्त्यदृश्यतः। नाशयन्ति कृतघ्नास्तु न रामो नाशयिष्यति॥
en: Or people have fancy for what they see and are which disappear as soon as the object is out of sight. The ungrateful are capable of renouncing their love, but not Rāma.

sn: किं वा मय्यगुणाः केचित् किं वा भाग्यक्षयो हि मे। या हि सीता वराहेण हीना रामेण भामिनी॥
en: Or there might be some folly in me. Or on the wane of my good luck have been separated from the excellent Rāma.

sn: श्रेयो मे जीवितान्मर्तुं विहीनाया महात्मना। रामादक्लिष्टचारित्राच्छूराच्छत्रुनिबर्हणात्॥
en: Death is more preferable to me than life since. I have been separated from the high-souled heroic Rāma, of unblemished character and the slayer of foes.

sn: अथवा न्यस्तशस्त्रौ तौ वने मूलफलाशनौ। भ्रातरौ हि नरश्रेष्ठौ चरन्तौ वनगोचरौ॥
en: Or those two brothers, the foremost of men, laying aside their weapons, and living on fruits and roots, have been wandering in the forest.

sn: अथवा राक्षसेन्द्रेण रावणेन दुरात्मना। छद्मना घातितौ शूरौ भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ॥
en: Or those two heroic brothers Rāma and Laksmana, have been, by treachery, put to death, by the vicious-souled Rāvana, the lord of Raksasas.

sn: साहमेवंविधे काले मर्तुमिच्छामि सर्वतः। न च मे विहितो मृत्युरस्मिन् दुःखेऽतिवर्तति॥
en: At this time of distress, I do with all my heart long for death, (but alas!) even death is not approaching me is this my misery.

sn: धन्याः खलु महात्मानो मुनयः सत्यसम्मताः। जितात्मानौ महाभागा येषां न स्तः प्रियाप्रिये।४७।।
en: Oh blessed are those high-souled, great ascetics abiding by truth and having their senses in control, who have no objects of love or displeasure.

sn: प्रियान्न सम्भवेद् दुःखमप्रियादधिकं भवेत्। ताभ्यां हि ते वियुज्यन्ते नमस्तेषां महात्मनाम्॥
en: They are not distressed with misery for their objects of love or grief for them whom they do not love. They are freed from them and I do bow to those high-souled ones.

sn: साऽहं त्यक्ता प्रियेणैव रामेण विदितात्मना। प्राणांस्त्यक्ष्यामि पापस्य रावणस्य गता वशम्॥
en: Being forsaken by the beloved Rāma, knowing his ownself, and brought under the control of Ravana, I shall renounce my life.

sn: इत्युक्ताः सीतया घोरं राक्षस्यः क्रोधमूछिताः। कांश्चिज्जग्मुस्तदाख्यातुं रावणस्य दुरात्मनः॥
en: Being thus addressed angrily by Sītā, some of those Raksasis, beside themselves with ire, proceeded to relate this to the vicious-souled Ravana.

sn: ततः सीतामुपागम्य राक्षस्यो भीमदर्शनाः। पुनः परुषमेकार्थमनर्थार्थमथाब्रुवन्॥
en: And approaching Sītā those grim-visaged demons again addressed her with words rude and rough.

sn: अद्येदानीं तवानार्ये सीते पापविनिश्चये। राक्षस्यो भक्षयिष्यन्ति मांसमेतद् यथासुखम्॥
en: O vile Sītă, O you bent on committing sin, we Rākşasīs shall today devour your flesh to the best of our satisfaction.

sn: सीतां ताभिरनार्याभिदृष्ट्वा संतर्जितां तदा। राक्षसी त्रिजटा वृद्धा प्रबुद्धा वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
en: Beholding those vile demons threaten Sītā, a Raksasa matron, wise and old, named, Trijata cried.

sn: आत्मानं खादतानार्या न सीतां भक्षयिष्यथ। जनकस्य सुतामिष्टां स्नुषां दशरथस्य च॥
en: O vile demons, do youeat your own persons (The proper expression, I think, should be-“Eat me.” The commentator Rāmānuja explains Atmanam as your own bodies.) but do not devour Sītā, the daughter of Janaka and the esteemed daughter-in-law of the king Dasaratha.

sn: स्वप्नो ह्यद्य मया दृष्टो दारुणो रोमहर्षणः। राक्षसानामभावाय भर्तुरस्या भवाय च॥
en: I dreamt a terrible dream last night which made my down stand on their end. And in that dream I foresaw the overthrow of the Rāksasa race and the conquest of her husband.

sn: एवमुक्तास्त्रिजटया राक्षस्यः क्रोधमूर्च्छिताः। सर्वा एवाब्रुवन् भीतास्त्रिजटां तामिदं वचः॥
en: And being thus addressed by Trijatā, those demons, exercised with wrath and terrified, accosted her with the following words.

sn: कथयस्व त्वया दृष्टः स्वप्नोऽयं कीदृशो निशि। तासां श्रुत्वा तु वचनं राक्षसीनां मुखोद्गतम्॥ उवाच वचनं काले त्रिजटा स्वप्नसंश्रितम्।
en: "Do you relate (to us) what sort of dream didst you dream last night." And hearing those words proceeding from the mouths of the Rākşasīs, Trijatā began to describe the dream she had at the latter end of the night,

sn: गजदन्तमयीं दिव्यां शिबिकान्तरिक्षगाम्॥ युक्तां वाजिसहस्रेण स्वयमास्थाय राघवः। शुक्लमाल्याम्बरधरो लक्ष्मणेन समागतः॥
en: I saw Rāma, wearing garlands and clothed in white, ride in a celestial chariot, along with Lakşmaņa, made of ivory, traversing the etherial regions and drawn by a hundred steeds.

sn: स्वप्न चाद्य मया दृष्टा सीता शुक्लाम्बरावृता। सागरेण परिक्षिप्तं श्वेतपर्वतमास्थिता॥ रामेण संगता सीता भास्करेण प्रभा यथा।
en: I saw in my dream to-night, that Sītā, clad in the purest white, appearing on a snow-white hill beaten by the waves of the ocean, had at last met Rāma, like to light joined to the Sun.

sn: राघवश्च पुनदृष्टश्चतुर्दन्तं महागजम्॥ आरूढः शैलसंकाशं चकास सहलक्ष्मणः।
en: I again saw Rāma and Lakşmaņa appear in effulgence, seated on a huge elephant, having four tusks and resembling a bull.

sn: ततस्तु सूर्यसंकाशौ दीप्यमानौ स्वतेजसा ॥ शुक्लमाल्याम्बरधरौ जानकी पर्युपस्थितौ।
en: Thereupon those two (brothers), resplendent like to the Sun by their own effulgence, and wearing white garlands and clothes, appeared near Janaka's daughter.

sn: ततस्तस्य नगस्याग्रे ह्याकाशस्थस्य दन्तिनः॥ भ; परिगृहीतस्य जानकी स्कन्धमाश्रिता। भर्तुरङ्कात् समुत्पत्य ततः कमललोचना।। चन्द्रसूर्यौ मया दृष्टा पाणिभ्यां परिमार्जती॥
en: And the lotus-eyed Jānakī, on the top of the hill situate on the welkin, first fell on the lap of her husband and then stationed herself on the neck of the elephant guided by her husband. Then I saw Sītā rubbing the Sun and the Moon with her two hands.

sn: ददस्ताभ्यां कुमाराभ्यामास्थितः स गजोत्तमः। सीतया च विशालाक्ष्या लङ्काया उपरिस्थितः। पाण्डुरर्षभयुक्तेन रथेनाष्टयुजा स्वयम्॥ शुक्लमाल्याम्बरधरो लक्ष्मणेन सहागतः।
en: Then that best of the elephants, with those two princes and the large eyed Sītā on him, stood high above Lanka. I again saw Rāma, clad in white, and adorned with garlands, ride along with Lakşmaņa in a chariot drawn by eight white bullocks.

sn: ततोऽन्यत्र मया दृष्टो रामः सत्यपराक्रमः॥ लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्रात्रा सीतया सह वीर्यवान्। आरुह्य पुष्पकं दिव्यं विमानं सूर्यसंनिभम्॥ उत्तरां दिशमालोच्य प्रस्थितः पुरुषोत्तमः।
en: I again saw that highly energetic, best of men, Rāma, having truth for his prowess, along with his brother Lakşmaņa and Sītā flee to Northern realms, ascending a celestial flowery chariot resembling (in brightness) the Sun.

sn: रावणश्च मया दृष्टो मुण्डस्तैलसमुक्षितः॥ रक्तवासा पिबन्मत्तः करवीरकृतस्रजः। विमानात् पुष्पकादद्य रावणः पतितः क्षितौ॥
en: I saw Ravana too, shaved and shorn, besmeared with oil, wearing a crimson cloth, drinking honey, wearing a garland of Karavīra flowers, fall down on earth from the flowery chariot.

sn: कृष्यमाणः स्त्रिया मुण्डो दृष्टः कृष्णाम्बरः पुनः। रथेन खरयुक्तेन रक्तमाल्यानुलेपनः॥ पिबंस्तैलं हसन्नृत्यन् भ्रान्तचित्ताकुलेन्द्रियः। गर्दभेन ययौ शीघ्रं दक्षिणां दिशमास्थितः॥
en: And dragged by a woman, shaved, wearing a red cloth and garlands and sprinkled with crimson paste, Rāvana was again seen by me riding in a chariot drawn by asses. And quaffing oil, laughing and dancing, that one of agitated senses, forgetting himself sped on the chariot to the South. (In the south is the region of Yama, the God of Death and hence his going to the south is not an auspicious sign.)

sn: पुनरेव मया दृष्टो रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः। पतितो विशिरा भूमौ गर्दभाद्भयमोहितः॥
en: And I again saw Rāvana, the lord of the Raksasas, stricken with fear, fall, headless, down on the earth.

sn: सहसोत्थाय सम्भ्रान्तो भयार्तो मदविह्वलः। उन्मत्तरूपो दिग्वासा दुर्वाक्यं प्रलपन्बहु॥ दुर्गन्धं दुःसहं घोरं तिमिरं नरकोपमम्। मलपङ्कं प्रविश्याशु मग्नस्तत्र स रावणः॥
en: And then rising all on a sudden, and uttering obscene and inconsistent words like to a maniac, Rāvana overwhelmed with fear, and amazement, and intoxicated, fell into a mass of dirt, stinking and resembling the very hell. And again proceeding to the South he entered into a lake devoid of mud and water.

sn: प्रस्थितो दक्षिणामाशां प्रविष्टोऽकर्दमं हृदम्। कण्ठे बद्ध्वा दशग्रीवं प्रमदा रक्तवासिनी॥ कालीकर्दमलिप्ताङ्गी दिशं याम्यां प्रकर्षति। एवं तत्र मया दृष्टः कुम्भकर्णो महाबलः॥ रावणस्य सुताः सर्वे मुण्डास्तैलसमुक्षिताः। वराहेण दशग्रीवं शिशुमारेण चेन्द्रजित्॥ उष्ट्रेण कुम्भकर्णश्च प्रयातो दक्षिणां दिशम्।
en: And a dark woman, clad in a crimson cloth, and bedaubed with mud, dragged the Ten-necked demon, entwining herself around his neck. Then followed the mighty Kumbhakarņa (Rāvana's brother) and all the sons of Rāvana, shaved and shorn and besmeared with oil. And they all proceeded southward—the Ten-necked demon on a boar, Indrajit (Rāvana's son-the name signifies the conqueror of the lord of the celestials) on a porpoise, and Kumbhakarņa on a camel.

sn: एकस्तत्र मया दृष्टः श्वेतच्छत्रो विभीषणः।। चतुर्भिः सचिवैः सार्धं वैहायसमुपस्थितः॥
en: I saw only Vibhīșaņa, with a white umbrella and accompanied by four courtiers, range in the welkin.

sn: समाजश्च महान् वृत्तो गीतवादित्रनि:स्वनः। पिबतां रक्तमाल्यानां रक्षसां रक्तवाससाम्॥ लङ्का चेयं पुरी रम्या सवाजिरथकुञ्जरा। सागरे पतिता दृष्टा भग्नगोपुरतोरणा॥
en: And there was audible in the large assembly sound of music and stringed instruments. And all the Rākşasa wearing crimson clothes and garlands, were quaffing oil, I saw the royal and picturesque city Lankā with her steeds, cars and elephants, drowned in the ocean, having her gateways and ornamented arches broken.

sn: पीत्वा तैलं प्रमत्ताश्च प्रहसन्त्यो महास्वनाः। लङ्कायां भस्मरूक्षायां सर्वा राक्षसयोषितः॥
en: And in Lanka, covered with dust, Raksasa women laughing and making terrible sound, were engaged in quaffing oil.

sn: कुम्भकर्णादयश्चेमे सर्वे राक्षसपुङ्गवाः। रक्तं निवसनं गृह्य प्रविष्टा गोमयहृदम्॥
en: I saw all the leading Raksasas-Kumbhakarņā and others, dark-hued and wearing crimson clothes, emerged in an abyss of cow dung.

sn: अपगच्छत पश्यध्वं सीतामाप्नोति राघवः। घातयेत् परमामर्षी युष्मान् सार्धं हि राक्षसैः॥
en: Do youtherefore fly at some distance, and will find that Rāghava shall regain Sītā. And exercised with ire he shall destroy you all along with the Raksasas.

sn: प्रियां बहुमतां भार्या वनवासमनुव्रताम्। भर्त्तितां तर्जितां वापि नानुमंस्यति राघवः॥
en: Rāghava shall never brook, his esteemed and beloved spouse, living in the forest, being taunted and threatened by you.

sn: तदलं क्रूरवाक्यैश्च सान्त्वमेवाभिधीयताम्। अभियाचाम वैदेहीमेतद्धि मम रोचते॥
en: No more with rough words therefore; do you console the lady and humbly pray her to forgive you. This I think proper.

sn: यस्या ह्येवंविधः स्वप्नो दुःखितायाः प्रदृश्यते। सा दुःखैर्बहुभिर्मुक्ता प्रियं प्राप्नोत्यनुत्तमम्॥
en: Surely shall she, divested of misfortune, he reconciled to her beloved and excellent husband, regarding whom, in her misery, I have dreamt such a dream.

sn: भर्त्तितामपि याचध्वं राक्षस्यः किं विवक्षया। राघवाद्धि भयं घोरं राक्षसानामुपस्थितम्॥
en: YouRaksasis! You have threatened her, do youimplore her forgiveness—no more with harsh words. Forsooth, from Rāghava shall proceed the mighty disaster of the Rākṣasas.

sn: प्रणिपातप्रसन्ना हि मैथिली जनकात्मजा। अलमेषा परित्रातुं राक्षस्यो महतो भयात्॥
en: If Maithili, the daughter of the king Janaka, be pleased with you (for your imploring her forgiveness) you might be saved from the mighty disaster.

sn: अपि चास्या विशालाक्ष्या न किंचिदुपलक्षये। विरूपमपि चाङ्गेषु सुसूक्ष्ममपि लक्षणम्॥
en: I do not perceive any inauspicious mark on the person of this large-eyed dame. It appears from the paleness of her countenance that she has been overcome by misfortune.

sn: छायावैगुण्यमानं तु शङ्के दुःखमुपस्थितम्। अदुःखार्हामिमां देवीं वैहायसमुपस्थिताम् ॥
en: And I saw in my dreams) this worshipful damsel, unworthy of any misfortune, stationed in the welkin.

sn: अर्थसिद्धिं तु वैदेह्याः पश्याम्यहमुपस्थिताम्। राक्षसेन्द्रविनाशं च विजयं राघवस्य च॥
en: Verily I do perceive, before me, the satisfaction of Vaidehi's end, the destruction of the lord of the Rākşasas and the conquest of Raghava.

sn: निमित्तभूतमेतत् तु श्रोतुमस्या महत् प्रियम्। दृश्यते च स्फुरच्चक्षुः पद्मपत्रमिवायतम्॥ ईषच्च हृषितो वास्या दक्षिणाया ह्यदक्षिणः। अकस्मादेव वैदेह्याः बाहुरेकः प्रकम्पते॥
en: Behold! there, her left eye, spacious, as a lotus-petals, is dancing to hear this pleasant dream announcing the satisfaction of her own end. And her left arm is also dancing with joy, all on a sudden.

sn: करेणुहस्तप्रतिमः सव्यश्चोरुरनुत्तमः। वेपन् कथयतीवास्या राघवं पुरतः स्थितम्॥
en: And her excellent beautiful left thigh, resembling the trunk of an elephant, is also dancing as if indicating, that she shall at no distant date, be reconciled to Rāghava.

sn: पक्षी च शाखानिलयं प्रविष्टः पुनः पुनश्चोत्तमसान्त्ववादी। सुखागतां वाचमुदीरयाणः पुनः पुनश्चोदयतीव हृष्टः॥
en: And the birds, again and again, entering their nests, and highly delighted are pouring forth their notes announcing the advent of a happy occasion.

sn: ततः सा ह्रीमती बाला भर्तुर्विजयहर्षिता। अवोचद् यदि तत् तथ्यं भवेयं शरणं हि वः।॥
en: Thereupon that modest dame, dame, greatly delighted in the prospective conquest of her husband, said, “If this be true I shall save you all.”

sn: सा राक्षसेन्द्रस्य वचो निशम्य तद् रावणस्य प्रियमप्रियार्ता। सीता वितत्रास यथा वनान्ते सिंहाभिपन्ना गजराजकन्या॥
en: Hearing those unpleasant words of Rāvana, the lord of Rāksasas, Sītā, racked with sorrow on account of her husband, became terrified, like to a she-elephant, worsted by a lion on the skirt of a forest.

sn: वाग्भि शं रावणतर्जिता च। कान्तारमध्ये विजने विसृष्टा बालेव कन्या विललाप सीता॥
en: Threatened by Rāvana and encircled by the Rākşasīs, that timid damsel bewailed like a girl cast off in a lonely forest.

sn: सत्यं बतेदं प्रवदन्ति लोके नाकालमृत्युर्भवतीति सन्तः। यत्राहमेवं परिभर्व्यमाना जीवामि यस्मात् क्षणमप्यपुण्या॥
en: Truly the sages say that death in this world dose not come untimely. Or else would I have, vicious as I am, lived for a moment, being thus sorely threatened.

sn: मिदं तु नूनं हृदयं स्थिरं मे। विदीर्यते यन्न सहस्रधाद्य वज्राहतं शृङ्गमिवाचलस्य॥
en: Forsooth, my mind, divested of happiness and full of misery, is firin or else why is it not broken in sunder like to the summit of a hill clapped by a thunderbolt.

sn: नैषास्ति नूनं मम दोषमत्र वध्याहमस्याप्रियदर्शनस्य। मलं द्विजो मन्त्रमिवाद्विजाय ॥
en: Nor am I to blame for this. I am worthy of being killed by this demon of uncomely presence. As a Brāhmaṇa cannot impart instructions in Vedas to the people of other castes so I shall not confer my mind on Rāvana.

sn: तस्मिन्ननागच्छति लोकनाथे गर्भस्थजन्तोरिव शल्यकृन्तः। नूनं ममाङ्गान्यचिरादनार्य शस्त्रैः शितैच्छेत्स्यति राक्षसेन्द्रः॥
en: If that lord of the people dose not come within the appointed time, forsooth shall that vile lord, of the Rākşasas, mince my limbs with his arrows like to a surgeon cutting off the limbs of an embryo. (This passage clearly indicates that there were proficient and skilled surgeons at the time when Rāmāyaṇa was written.)

sn: दुःखं बतेदं ननु दुःखिताया मासौ चिरायाभिगमिष्यतो द्वौ। बद्धस्य वध्यस्य यथा निशान्ते राजोपरोधादिव तस्करस्य॥
en: Two months shall pass away in no time and I shall have to suffer the pain of death, overwhelmed with sorrow as I am, like to a thief, confined in stocks, at the command of the sovereign to receive death the next morning.

sn: हा राम हा लक्ष्मण हा सुमित्रे हा राममातः सह मे जनन्यः। मृगरूपधारी एषा विपद्याम्यहमल्पभाग्या महार्णवे नौरिव मूढवाता॥
en: O Rama! O Laksmana! O Sumitra! O Rama's mother! O my mothers! I am worsted in this ocean of grief, like to a bark, driven hither and thither by the blast, in the midst of an ocean.

sn: तरस्विनौ धारयता मृगस्य सत्त्वेन रूपं मनुजेन्द्रपुत्रौ। नूनं विशस्तौ मम कारणात् तौ सिंहर्षभौ द्वाविव वैद्युतेन॥
en: Verily for me, those two powerful, lion-like sons of the king, have been killed by (this demon) effulgent like the lightning and assuming the semblance of a deer.

sn: नूनं स कालो मामल्पभाग्यां लुलुभे तदानीम्। यत्रार्यपुत्रौ विससर्ज मूढा रामानुजं लक्ष्मणपूर्वजं च ॥
en: Unfortunate as I am, forsooth I was tempted then by death wearing the shape of a deer and thus foolishly lost Rāma and Lakşmana, the sons of the worshipful sire.

sn: हा राम सत्यव्रत दीर्घबाहो हा पूर्णचन्द्रप्रतिमानवक्त्र। हा जीवलोकस्य हितः प्रियश्च वध्यां न मां वेत्सि हि राक्षसानाम्॥
en: O Rāma, O you of truthful vows, O you of long arms, O you having the countenance of a full moon! O my life! engaged as you are in the welfare of the people, do you not perceive that I am about to be killed by the Rākşasas.

sn: अनन्यदेवत्वमियं क्षमा च भूमौ च शय्या नियमश्च धर्मे। पतिव्रतात्वं विफलं ममेदं कृतं कृतघ्नेष्विव मानुषाणाम्॥
en: Alas! this my devotedness to my husband, my forgiveness, my lying down on the bare earth, my observance of religious vows, my wife-like virtues, are lost like to service done for an ungrateful wight.

sn: मोघं हि धर्मश्चरितो ममायं तथैकपत्नीत्वमिदं निरर्थकम्। या त्वां न पश्यामि कृशा विवर्णा हीना त्वया सङ्गमने निराशा॥
en: In vain are my pious rites, and in vain is my devotedness to my husband since I do not behold you, am pale and feeble in your absence and have given up all hopes of seeing you.

sn: पितुर्निदेशं नियमेन कृत्वा वनान्निवृत्तश्चरितव्रतश्च। स्त्रीभिस्तु मन्ये विपुलेक्षणाभिः संरंस्यसे वीतभयः कृतार्थः॥
en: And duly satisfying your sire's command, and returning successfully from the forest, you shall fearlessly sport with many a damsel having large eyes.

sn: अहं तु राम त्वयि जातकामा चिरं विनाशाय निबद्धभावा। मोघं चरित्वाथ तपो व्रतं च त्यक्ष्यामि धिग्जीवितमल्पभोग्याम्॥
en: (But for me) O Rama, I was for my own destruction, devoted, soul and heart, to you. Oh! fruitless is my asceticism and wifely virtue! Oh fie on me! I shall renounce this my unfortunate life.

sn: संजीवितं क्षिप्रमहं त्यजेयं विषेण शस्त्रेण शितेन वापि। च्छस्त्रस्य वा वेश्मनि राक्षसस्य॥
en: I desire to do away speedily with my being by means of poison or a sharp weapon. But there is no one in this city of the Rākşasas, who bring me this poison or weapon.

sn: [इतीव देवी बहुधा विलप्य सर्वात्मना राममनुस्मरन्ती। प्रवेपमाना परिशुष्कवक्त्रा नगोत्तमं पुष्पितमाससाद ।। शोकाभितप्ता बहुधा विचिन्त्य सीताऽथ वेणीग्रथनं गृहीत्वा। महं गमिष्यामि यमस्य मूलम्॥
en: Bewailing thus in various accents, and remembering Rāma with all her heart, Sītā, having her countenance dried up, and trembling, got at the biggest tree enveloped with flowers. And thinking thus, Sītā, stricken with grief, took up in her hand, her braid of hair and thought—"I shall soon hang myself with this braid and reach the abode of Death."

sn: उपस्थिता सा मृदुसर्वगात्री शाखां गृहीत्वा च नगस्य तस्य। तस्यास्तु रामं परिचिन्तयन्त्या रामानुजं स्वं च कुलं शुभाङ्गयाः॥ तस्या विशोकानि तदा बहूनि धैर्यार्जितानि प्रवराणि लोके। प्रादुर्निमित्तानि तदा बभूवुः पुरापि सिद्धान्युपलक्षितानि॥
en: And that one of tender person reached the tree, and holding a branch, began to think of Rama, Laksmana, and the glory of her race. And on her person were perceived many auspicious marks, well-known in the world, removing grief, fostering patience and announcing the advent of future welfare.

sn: तथागतां तां व्यथितामनिन्दितां व्यतीतहर्षां परिदीनमानसाम्। शुभां निमित्तानि शुभानि भेजिरे नरं श्रिया जुष्टमिवोपसेविनः॥
en: Like to servants waiting upon a wealthy person various auspicious omens waited upon Sītā of a blameless and comely person, racked with grief and divested of joy.

sn: राज्यावृतं कृष्णविशालशुक्लम्। प्रास्पन्दतैकं नयनं सुकेश्या मीनाहतं पद्ममिवाभिताम्रम्॥
en: And the large left eye of that dame having graceful hairs, having dark pupils, white ends and thick eye-lashes, began to dance like a lotus shaken by a fish.

sn: भुजश्च चार्वञ्चितवृत्तपीनः परायंकालागुरुचन्दनाहः। अनुत्तमेनाध्युषितः प्रियेण चिरेण वामः समवेपताशु॥
en: And her beautiful, round, plump left hand, which, ere this, sprinkled with costly aguru and sandal, used to serve for a pillow to Rāma, began to dance now again and again after a long time.

sn: स्तयोर्द्वयोः संहतयोस्तु जातः। प्रस्पन्दमानः पुनरूरुरस्या रामं पुरस्तात् स्थितमाचचक्षे॥
en: And her well built plump left thigh, resembling the trunk of an elephant, dancing, announced that she would soon behold Rāma.

sn: मीषद्रजोध्वस्तमिवातुलाक्ष्याः। वासः स्थितायाः शिखराग्रदन्त्याःकिंचित् परिस्त्रंसतचारुगात्र्याः॥
en: And the gold-hued cloth, now covered with dust, of that damsel of a comely person, having teeth like pomegranate seeds, slipped a little off its place.

sn: एतैर्निमित्तैरपरैश्च सुभ्रूः संचोदिता प्रागपि साधुसिद्धैः। वातातपक्लान्तमिव प्रणष्टं वर्षेण बीजं प्रतिसंजहर्ष॥
en: And being enlivened by those and various other auspicious omens, she attained joy like to a seed, spoiled by the wind and the sun, growing afresh in the rainy season.

sn: तस्याः पुनर्बिम्बफलोपमोष्ठं स्वक्षिभुकेशान्तमरालपक्ष्म। वक्त्रं बभासे सितशुक्लदंष्ट्र राहोर्मुखाच्चन्द्र इव प्रमुक्तः॥
en: And her countenance, having lips red as Bimba fruits, beautiful eyes, eye-brows extending to ears, curling eye-lashes and white teeth, again appeared graceful like to the Moon released from the full grasp of Rahu. (Like the Moon when full eclipse is just over-In mythology Rāhu is the son of Sinika, a Daitya, with the tail of a dragon whose head was severed from-his body by Vişnu, but being immortal this head and tail retained their separate existence and being transferred to the stellar sphere, became the authors of eclipses.)

sn: सा वीतशोका व्यपनीततन्द्रा शान्तज्वरा हर्षविबुद्धसत्त्वा। अशोभतार्या वदनेन शुक्ले शीतांशुना रात्रिरिवोदितेन ॥
en: Her grief and exhaustion were removed. sorrow was pacified and her heart was filled with joy. And she with her countenance appeared beautiful like a lunar night beautified by the rays of the Moon.

sn: हनुमानपि विक्रान्तः सर्वं शुश्राव तत्त्वतः। सीतायास्त्रिजटायाश्च राक्षसीनां च तर्जितम्॥
en: And the powerful Hanumān, heard from the beginning to the end (the bewailings) of Sitā, the story to Trijatā's dream and the threats of the Rākşasīs.

sn: अवेक्षमाणस्तां देवी देवतामिव नन्दने। ततो बहुविधां चिन्तां चिन्तयामास वानरः॥
en: And beholding the worshipful damsel, living in the forest of Asoka, like to a celestial damsel in the garden of Nandana, the monkey-entered in a maze of anxious thoughts.

sn: यां कपीनां सहस्राणि सुबहून्ययुतानि च। दिक्षु सर्वासु मार्गन्ते सेयमासादिता मया॥
en: At length my watchful eyes have seen her, whom have been seeking in vain, the thousands and millions of the monkeys in all directions and quarters.

sn: चारेण तु सुयुक्तेन शत्रोः शक्तिमवेक्षता। गूढेन चरता तावदवेक्षितमिदं मया॥ राक्षसानां विशेषश्च पुरी चेयं निरीक्षिता। राक्षसाधिपतेरस्य प्रभावो रावणस्य च॥
en: Truly have I seen her today, engaged as I have been as a spy to estimate the strength of the enemy and am ranging secretly everywhere. I have seen minutely the city of the Rākşasas, and the strength of Rāvana the lord of Rākşasas.

sn: तथा तस्याप्रमेयस्य सर्वसत्त्वदयावतः। समाश्वासयितुं भार्यां पतिदर्शनकाङ्क्षिणीम्॥
en: It now remains to console the spouse of Rāma of incomparable power, and kind to all, who pants for her lord.

sn: अहमाश्वासयाम्येनां पूर्णचन्द्रनिभाननाम्। अदृष्टदुःखां दुःखस्य न हन्तमधिगच्छतीम्।७।।
en: I shall console this damsel, having the countenance of the full moon, who had never seen grief before, and who shall not soon reach its end.

sn: यदि ह्यहं सतीमेनां शोकोपहतचेतनाम्। अनाश्वास्य गमिष्यामि दोषवद् गमनं भवेत्॥
en: And if I go away without soothing this chaste lady, who is almost senseless with grief, I shall be blamed of neglect of duty.

sn: गते हि मयि तत्रेयं राजपुत्री यशश्विनी। परित्राणमपश्यन्ती जानकी जीवितं त्यजेत्॥
en: And if I go away, the royal daughter, the famed Janaki, finding no means of safety, shall, for certain, renounce her life.

sn: यथा च स महाबाहुः पूर्णचन्द्रनिभाननः। समाश्वासयितुं न्याय्यः सीतादर्शनलालसः॥
en: She is worthy of being consoled like to the great armed (Rāma) having the countenance of the full-moon and anxious to behold Sita.

sn: निशाचरीणां प्रत्यक्षमक्षमं चाभिभाषितम्। कथं नु खलु कर्तव्यमिदं कृच्छ्रगतो ह्यहम्॥
en: It is not proper to speak before the Rākşasas-What shall I do them? I am in very great difficulty.

sn: अनेन रात्रिशेषेण यदि नाश्वास्यते मया। सर्वथा नास्ति संदेहः परित्यक्ष्यति जीवितम्॥
en: If I do not console her at this later end of the night, surely shall she renounce her life.

sn: रामस्तु यदि पृच्छेन्मां किं मां सीताब्रवीद् वचः। किमहं तं प्रतिब्रूयामसम्भाष्य सुमध्यमाम्॥
en: How shall I answer Rāma, without consoling Sītā of comely stature, when he will ask me “What message from my Sītā?”

sn: सीतासंदेशरहितं मामितस्त्वरया गतम्। निर्दहेदपि काकुत्स्थः क्रोधतीव्रण चक्षुषा ॥
en: And if I speedily repair hence without any information regarding Sītā, surely shall Kākuthutha scorci me lifeless with the fire of his angry eyes.

sn: यदि वोद्योजयिष्यामि भर्तारं रामकारणात्। व्यर्थमागमनं तस्य ससैन्यस्य भविष्यति॥
en: And if I urge my lord the king (Vibhīşaņa) to bring his hosts here for Rāma, in vain shall be his toil. (For before that Sītā shall renounce her life.)

sn: अन्तरं त्वहमासाद्य राक्षसीनामवस्थितः। शनैराश्वासयाम्यद्य संतापबहुलामिमाम्॥
en: And seizing the occasion when she shall be free from her demoniac guards, I shall console her in her dire distress.

sn: अहं ह्यतितनुश्चैव वानरश्च विशेषतः। वाचं चोदाहरिष्यामि मानुषीमिह संस्कृताम्॥
en: And a puny monkey as I am, I shall speak in Sanskrit (The language refined by the strict rules of grammar) which men delight to use.

sn: यदि वाचं प्रदास्यामि द्विजातिरिव संस्कृताम्। रावणं मन्यमाना मां सीता भीता भविष्यति॥
en: And if I speak Sanskrit like a Brāhmaṇa, Sītā shall be terrified considering me Råvaņa.

sn: अवश्यमेव वक्तव्यं मानुषं वाक्यमर्थवत्। मया सान्त्वयितुं शक्या नान्यथेयमनिन्दिता ॥
en: Must I therefore use the language of a common man or else I shall not be able to console the dame of a blameless person.
