(This passage clearly indicates that Sanskrit if not spoken by men, and women of the upper classes of the time when Rāmāyaṇa was written, was at least understood by them, and was commonly spoken by men of priestly class and other educated persons")

sn: सेयमालोक्य मे रूपं जानकी भाषितं तथा। रक्षोभिस्त्रासिता पूर्वं भूयस्त्रासमुपैष्यति॥
en: And beholding my monkey shape and hearing my human language she might be afraid again, terrified as she had been before by the band of the Rākşasas.

sn: ततो जातपरित्रासा शब्दं कुर्यान्मनस्विनी। जानाना मां विशालाक्षी रावणं कामरूपिणम्॥
en: And considering me Rāvaņa wearing shapes at will, that large-eyed and high-minded dame, shall cry piteously for help.

sn: सीतया च कृते शब्दे सहता राक्षसीगणः। नानाप्रहरणो घोर: समयादन्तकोपमः॥
en: And Sītā making a sudden noise, those terrible Rākṣasīs resembling Death himself and arined with various weapons, shall at once arrive there.

sn: ततो मां सम्परिक्षिप्य सर्वतो विकृताननाः। वधे च ग्रहणे चैव कुर्युर्यत्नं महाबलाः॥
en: And thereupon casting their looks all around and finding me out, those highly powerful and grim-viasged demons shall try to kill or catch ine.

sn: तं मां शाखाः प्रशाखाश्च स्कन्धांश्चोत्तमशाखिनाम्। दृष्ट्वा च परिधावन्तं भवेयुः परिशङ्किताः॥
en: Beholding me leap from branch to branch and trunk to trunk of big trees they shall be greatly alarmed.

sn: मम रूपं च सम्प्रेक्ष्य वने विचरतो महत्। राक्षस्यो भयवित्रस्ता भवेयुर्विकृतस्वराः॥
en: And espying my appearance while ranging in the forest, those Rākşasīs greatly terrified, shall fill the wood with their wild shouts.

sn: ततः कुर्युः समाह्वानं राक्षस्यो रक्षसामपि। राक्षसेन्द्रनियुक्तानां राक्षसेन्द्रनिवेशने॥
en: Then they shall call (to their assistance) all those Rākşasīs engaged in guarding the abode of the lord of the Rāksasas.

sn: ते शूलशरनिस्त्रिंशविविधायुधपाणयः। आपतेयुर्विमर्देऽस्मिन् वेगेनोद्वेगकारणात्॥
en: They, greatly agitated, shall with vehemence arrive here, armed with dirts, arrow, scimitars and various other weapons.

sn: संरुद्धस्तैस्तु परितो विधमे राक्षसं बलम्। शक्नुयां न तु सम्प्राप्तं परं पारं महोदधेः॥
en: Being surrounded by them on all sides, If I do kill that host of demons, tired, I shall not be able to bound over the main.

sn: मां वा गृहीयुरावृत्य बहवः शीघ्रकारिणः। स्यादियं चागृहीतार्था मम च ग्रहणं भवेत्॥
en: And if that host of skilled demons, succeed in making me a captive, too shall be in their hands and Sītā shall remain ignorant of my object.

sn: हिंसाभिरुचयो हिंस्युरिमां वा जनकात्मजाम्। विपन्नं स्यात् ततः कार्यं रामसुग्रीवयोरिदम्॥
en: Or the Rākşasas, pernicious as they are, shall kill the daughter of Janaka, and there shall the great work of Rāma and Sugrīva, be spoiled.

sn: उद्देशे नष्टमार्गेऽस्मिन् राक्षसैः परिवारिते। सागरेण परिक्षिप्ते गुप्ते वसति जानकी॥
en: And Jānakī live in this secret place, girt by the ocean, guarded on all sides by the Raksasas, difficult of being got at and having all avenues to it shut up.

sn: विशस्ते वा गृहीते वा रक्षोभिर्मयि संयुगे। नान्यं पश्यामि रामस्य सहायं कार्यसाधने॥
en: If I am killed or captured by Rākşasas in battle, I do not find any who can help Rāma in his enterprise.

sn: विमृशंश्च न पश्यामि यो हते मयि वानरः। शतयोजनविस्तीर्णं लङ्घयेत् महोदधिम्॥
en: Myself killed, I do not find any monkey who can leap a hundred leagues across the sea.

sn: कामं हन्तुं समर्थोऽस्मि सहस्राण्यपि रक्षसाम्। न तु शक्ष्याम्यहं प्राप्तुं परं पारं महोदधेः॥
en: I am capable of destroying thousands of Rākşasas, but I shall not then be able to get at the other shore of the great ocean.

sn: असत्यानि च युद्धानि संशयो मे न रोचते। कश्च निःसंशयं कार्यं कुर्यात् प्राज्ञः ससंशयम्॥
en: Victory or defeat is uncertain in a battle-I do not (therefore) like to engage in such an uncertain (act). What wise man merges certainty in uncertainly?

sn: एष दोषो महान् हि स्यान्मम सीताभिभाषणे। प्राणत्यागश्च वैदह्या भवेदनभिभाषणे॥
en: It is a great sin in me (I own) to talk with Sita-But she will die if I do not talk with her.

sn: भूताश्चार्था विरुद्ध्यन्ति देशकालविरोधिताः। विक्लवं दूतमासाद्य तमः सूर्योदये यथा॥
en: Works, almost accomplished, when entrusted to an inconsiderate emissary, are generally spoiled, out of season and out of place, like to darkness driven by the appearance of the sun.

sn: अर्थानान्तरे बुद्धिनिश्चितापि न शोभते। घातयन्ति हि कार्याणि दूताः पण्डितमानिनः॥
en: All those works, which are generally taken in hand after duly deliberating over their propriety and impropriety, are generally spoiled by those emissaries who are proud of their learing.

sn: न विनश्येत् कथं कार्यं वैक्लव्यं न कथं मम। लङ्घनं च समुद्रस्य कथं नु न वृथा भवेत्॥ कथं नु खलु वाक्यं मे शृणुयानोद्विजेत च। इति संचिन्त्य हनुमांश्चकार मतिमान् मतिम्॥
en: What shall I do, by which my work is not injured, I am not blamed of foolishness and my crossing over the main dose not become fruitless? What shall I do so that Sītā might listen to me without being terrified? Thinking over this, the intelligent Hanumān arrived at a conclusion.

sn: राममक्लिष्टकर्माणं सुबन्धुमनुकीर्तयन्। नैनामुद्वेजयिष्यामि तद्वन्धुगतचेतनाम्॥
en: I shall not disturb her, speaking (all on a sudden) about Rāma of unwearied actions, dear to her and to whom.

sn: इक्ष्वाकूणां वरिष्ठस्य रामस्य विदितात्मनः। शुभानि धर्मयुक्तानि वचनानि समर्पयन्॥ श्रावयिष्यामि सर्वाणि मधुरां प्रब्रुवन् गिरम्। श्रद्धास्यति यथा सीता तथा सर्वं समादधे॥
en: She is firmly attached. Uttering the name of Rāma, the foremost of the Ikşvākus, and of subdued soul and lauding his piety and fame in sweet accents, I shall so manage that Sītā might hear and believe them.

sn: इति स बहुविधं महाप्रभावो जगतिपतेः प्रमदामवेक्षमाणः। मधुरमवितथं जगाद वाक्यं द्रमविटपान्तरमास्थितो हनूमान्॥
en: Beholding the spouse of that high-souled lord of the earth and engaging in this train of thoughts, Hanumān, stationed on a branch of the tree, spoke the following sweet words.

sn: एवं बहुविधां चिन्तां चिन्तयित्वा महामतिः। संश्रवे मधुरं वाक्यं वैदेह्या व्याजहार ह॥
en: Meditating thus the highly intelligent monkey speh in accents, sweet and in such a tone as they mighty be, heard by Vaidehī.

sn: राजा दशरथो नाम रथकुञ्जरवाजिमान्। पुण्यशीलो महाकीर्तिरिक्ष्वाकूणां महायशाः॥
en: There reigned a noble and pious king named Dasaratha, highly glorious among the Ikşvākus, the lord of the warrior-cars, steeds and elephants.

sn: अहिंसारतिरक्षुद्रो घृणी सत्यपराक्रमः। मुख्यस्येक्ष्वाकुवंशस्य लक्ष्मीवॉल्लक्ष्मिवर्धनः॥ पार्थिवव्यजनैर्युक्तः पृथुश्रीः पार्थिवर्षभः। पृथिव्यां चतुरन्तायां विश्रुतः सुखदः सुखी॥
en: Devoid of envy, high-minded, kind, having truth for his prowess, the foremost of the Ikşvāku race, wealthy and the enhancer of wealth; gifted with royal marks; highly beautiful; the foremost of the kings; famous all over the world of many occans; the conferrer of happiness and himself happy.

sn: तस्य पुत्रः प्रियो ज्येष्ठस्ताराधिपनिभाननः। रामो नाम विशेषज्ञः श्रेष्ठः सर्वधनुष्मताम्॥
en: His eldest and most beloved son was the Moon-bright Rāma, wise and the foremost of those who know the science of the bended bow.

sn: रक्षिता स्वस्य वृत्तस्य स्वजनस्यापि रक्षिता। रक्षिता जीवलोकस्य धर्मस्य च परंतपः॥
en: He was the protector of his own character, of his own kinsmen, of the whole world of creation and of virtue and subduer of foes.

sn: तस्य सत्याभिसंधस्य वृद्धस्य वचनात् पितुः। सभार्यः सह च भ्राता वीरः प्रव्रजितो वनम्॥
en: And banished by his old and truthful sire's commands, that hero, along with his wife and brother (Laksmana) repaired to the forest.

sn: तेन तत्र महारण्ये मृगयां परिधावता। राक्षसा निहताः शूराः बहवः कामरूपिणः॥
en: And while roaming a-hunting in the forest he slew many a heroic Raksasa wearing shapes at will.

sn: जनस्थानवधं श्रुत्वा निहतौ खरदूषणौ। ततस्त्वमर्षापहृता जानकी रावणेन तु॥
en: And having heard of the destruction of the Rākşasas of Janasthāna and of Khara and Duşaņa, the illusive Rāvana, assuming shapes at will, beguiling Rāma, it the forest, stole away his consort-the Janaka's daughter.

sn: वञ्चयित्वा वने रामं मृगरूपेण मायया। स मार्गमाणस्तां देवीं रामः सीतामनिन्दिताम्॥
en: And roaming the country around in quest of the blameless and worshipful Sītā, Rāma found a firm friend in Sugrīva.

sn: आससाद वने मित्रं सुग्रीवं नाम वानरम्। ततः स वालिनं हत्वा रामः परपुरंजयः॥ आयच्छत् कपिराज्यं तु सुग्रीवाय महात्मने।
en: And bringing about the destruction of Vāli, Räma, the conqueror of others' cities, conferred the monkey-kingdom upon the high-souled Sugriva.

sn: सुग्रीवेणाभिसंदिष्टा हरयः कामरूपिणः॥ दिक्षु सर्वासु तां देवीं विचिन्वन्तः सहस्रशः।
en: And by Sugrīva's decree, thousands of monkeys, wearing shapes at will, have been searching that worshipful dame in various directions.

sn: अहं सम्पातिवचनाच्छतयोजनमायतम्॥ तस्याहेतोविशालाक्ष्याः समुद्रं वेगवान् प्लुतः।
en: And by Sampāti's counsel and for that largeeyed dame, I have leapt a hundred leagues across the deep.

sn: यथारूपां यथावर्णां यथालक्ष्मवती च ताम्॥ अश्रौषं राघवस्याहं सेयमासादिता मया। विररामैवमुक्त्वा स वाचं वानरपुङ्गवः॥
en: I have at last got her. And such were the form, grace and the marks that Rāghava mentioned to me. Having said this, the foremost of the monkeys ceased.

sn: जानकी चापि तच्छ्रुत्वा विस्मयं परमं गता। ततः सा वक्रकेशान्ता सुकेशी केशसंवृतम्। उन्नम्य वदनं भीरुः शिंशपामन्ववैक्षत ॥
en: And greatly wondered was Sītā hearing those words. Thereupon that timid dame, having good curling hair, raising up her face covered with hairs, looked up to the Singshapă tree.

sn: निशम्य सीता वचनं कपेश्च दिशश्च सर्वाः प्रदिशश्च वीक्ष्य। स्वयं प्रहर्षं परमं जगाम सर्वात्मना राममनुस्मरन्ती॥
en: Hearing the words of the monkey and casting her eyes to all directions and quarters, Sītā attained an excess of delight, being engaged in thoughts, concerning Rāma.

sn: निरीक्षमाणा तमचिन्त्यबुद्धिम्। ददर्श पिङ्गाधिपतेरमात्यं वातात्मजं सूर्यमिवोदयस्थम्॥
en: And looking around her and upwards, she beheld, like to the rising sun, the Wind god's son, gifted with inconceivable intellect, the minister of the king of monkeys.

sn: ततः शाखान्तरे लीनं दृष्ट्वा चलितमानसा। वेष्टितार्जुनवस्त्रं तं विद्युत्संघातपिङ्गलम्॥ सा ददर्श कपि तत्र प्रश्रितं प्रियवादिनम्। फुल्लाशोकोत्कराभासं तप्तचामीकरेक्षणम्॥
en: And beholding that tawny-coloured monkey like to a mass of lightnings and wearing a white cloth, hidden on the tree Sītā's mind was greatly agitated. And she saw there the humble, sweetspeeched monkey, appearing graceful like to a collection of full-blown Asoka flowers and having eyes resembling burning gold.

sn: साऽथ दृष्ट्वा हरिश्रेष्ठं विनीतवदवस्थितम्। मैथिली चिन्तयामास विस्मयं परमं गता॥
en: And observing that foremost of the monkeys, sitting humbly, that daughter of the king of Mithilā, again greatly amazed, thought.

sn: अहो भीममिदं सत्त्वं वानरस्य दुरासदम्। दुर्निरीक्ष्यमिदं मत्वा पुनरेव मुमोह सा ॥
en: “This monkey is the most terrible of his race and therefore hard to be got at and looked at." Thinking this she again sank in fear.

sn: विललाप भृशं सीतां करुणं भयमोहिता। रामरामेति दुःखार्ता लक्ष्मणेति च भामिनी॥
en: And stricken with grief she again bewailed in piteous accents exclaiming, “O Rāma! O Laksmana!"

sn: रुरोद सहसा सीता मन्दमन्दस्वरा सती। साऽथ दृष्ट्वा हरिवरं विनीतवदुपागतम्। थिली चिन्तयामास स्वप्नोऽयमिति भामिनी॥
en: She wept silently and lowly. And then beholding that best of monkeys approach her humbly, the fair daughter of the Mithila's king, thought, "Is this a dream mine eyes have seen?”

sn: सा वीक्षमाणा पृथुभग्नवक्त्रं शाखामृगेन्द्रस्य यथोक्तकारम्। ददर्श पिङ्गप्रवरं महाहँ वातात्मजं बुद्धिमतां वरिष्ठम्॥
en: And she again looked towards that Windgod's son, the foremost of the monkeys, the best of those gifted with intelligence, having a huge disfigured countenance, highly accomplished and wearing a dress mentioned before.

sn: सा तं समीक्ष्यैव भृशं विपन्ना गतासुकल्पेव बभूव सीता। चिरेण संज्ञां प्रतिलभ्य चैवं विचिन्तयामास विशालनेत्रा॥
en: And beholding him Sītā was almost out of breath with fear. And regaining soon her sense the large-eyed damsel again thought.

sn: स्वप्नो मयायं विकृतोऽद्य दृष्टः शाखामृगः शास्त्रगणैर्निषिद्धः। स्वस्त्यस्तु रामाय सलक्ष्मणाय तथा पितुर्मे जनकस्य राज्ञः॥
en: I have seen a very inauspicious dream to-dayto see a monkey in a dream is reckoned inauspicious by the sages. May good betide Rāma, Lakşmaņa and my Sire the king of Janaka.

sn: स्वप्नो हि नायं नहि मेऽस्ति निद्रा शोकेन दुःखेन च पीडितायाः। सुखं हि मे नास्ति यतो विहीना तेनेन्दुपूर्णप्रतिमाननेन॥
en: It is not dream, I have not slept, worn with grief and trouble as I am. Apart form my lord having the countenance of the full-moon, I have no happiness.

sn: रामेति रामेति सदैव बुद्ध्या विचिन्त्य वाचा ब्रुवती तमेव। तस्यानुरूपं च कथां तदर्था मेवं प्रपश्यामि तथा शृणोमि॥
en: Thinking of Rāma always and uttering his name, each sight I see and each sound I hear brings him to my eye or ear.

sn: अहं हि तस्याद्य मनोभवेन सम्पीडिता तद्गतसर्वभावा। विचिन्तयन्ती सततं तमेव तथैव पश्यामि तथा शृणोमि ॥
en: And therefore his form appearing in my mind is distressing me to-day, who am entirely sunk in his thoughts. And thinking of him always I see him before me and hear his words.

sn: मनोरथः स्यादिति चिन्तयामि तथापि बुद्ध्यापि वितर्कयामि। किं कारणं तस्य हि नास्ति रूपं सुव्यक्तरूपश्च वदत्ययं माम्॥
en: Methinks this is but a phantom of the mind. And thinking this I still behold the same. But an imaginary object can never have a form. And I still find a distinct form addressing me.

sn: नमोऽस्तु वाचस्पतये सवज्रिणे स्वयम्भुवे चैव हुताशनाय। अनेन चोक्तं यदिदं ममाग्रतो वनौकसा तच्च तथास्तु नान्यथा॥
en: Be glory to Vācaspati, Indra, the self existent Brahmā, the lord of fire and may they so grant that the creature who has spoken before me, be real and not imaginary.

sn: सोऽवतीर्य दुमात् तस्माद् विद्रुमप्रतिमाननः। विनीतवेषः कृपणः प्रणिपत्योपसृत्य च॥ तामब्रवीन्महातेजा हनूमान् मारुतात्मजः। शिरस्यञ्जलिमाधाय सीतां मधुरया गिरा॥
en: Thereupon coming down from the tree, Hanumān, the highly effulgent son of Wind, having a coral-red countenance and attired in a humble guise, approached Sītā and joining reverentially his palms, addressed her with the following sweet words.

sn: का नु पद्मपलाशाक्षि क्लिष्टकौशेयवासिनि। दुमस्य शाखामालम्ब्य तिष्ठसि त्वमनिन्दिता॥ किमर्थं तव नेत्राभ्यां वारि स्रवति शोकजम्। पुण्डरीकपलाशाभ्यां विप्रकीर्णमिवोदकम्॥
en: Who are you, O you having eyes like lotus petals and wearing a soiled silken cloth, who are waiting there holding a branch of the tree? Why are the tears of sorrow flowing from your eyes like to drops of water falling from lotus petals?

sn: सुराणामसुराणां च नागगन्धर्वरक्षसाम्। यक्षाणां किंनराणां च का त्वं भवसि शोभने ॥ का त्वं भवसि रुद्राणां मरुतां वा वरानने। वसूनां वा वरारोहे देवता प्रतिभासि मे॥
en: Who are you, O most fair of face, among the celestials, Asuras, Nāgas, Gandharvas, Rāks asas, and Yaksas and Kinnaras? Do the Rudra's (The Rudras are manifestations of Śiva) claim your birth O you fair damsel,? Or the swift gods who ride the storm? Or the Vasus? (A kind of demi-gods of whom six are enumerated viz., Dhava, Druva. Soma or the Moon, Visnu, Anila or wind, Anala or fire, Prabhusa and Prabhava) You appear to me as of a celestial race.

sn: किं नु चन्द्रमसा हीना पतिता विबुधालयात्। रोहिणी ज्योतिषां श्रेष्ठा श्रेष्ठा सर्वगुणाधिका॥
en: Are you Rohiņā, the best and most accomplished of the stars, who, left from the Moon, has fallen down from the abode of the celestials?

sn: कोपाद् वा यदि वा मोहाद् भर्तारमसितेक्षणे। वसिष्ठं कोपयित्वा त्वं वासि कल्याण्यरुन्धती॥
en: Who are you O blessed dame, O you having blameless eyes? Are you, O lotus-eyed damsel, the blessed Arundhuti, who has fled in wrath or jealous pride form the side of her lord (Vasistha)?

sn: को नु पुत्रः पिता भ्राता भर्ता वा ते सुमध्यमे। अस्माल्लोकादमुं लोकं गतं त्वमनुशोचसि॥
en: Or O lovely damsel, who is the son, father, brother or husband gone from this world for whom you are weeping?

sn: रोदनादतिनिःश्वासाद् भूमिसंस्पर्शनादपि। न त्वां देवीमहं मन्ये राज्ञः संज्ञावधारणात्॥ व्यञ्जनानि हि ते यानि लक्षणानि च लक्षये। महिषी भूमिपालस्य राजकन्या च मे मता॥
en: Yet by your tears and sighs, by the earth you are treading and by calling on a monarch's name it appears that you are not a celestial. (The celestials never shed tears nor touch the ground when they walk.) But from the marks on your person it appear that you are either the consort or the daughter of a king.

sn: रावणेन जनस्थानाद् बलात् प्रमथिता यदि। सीता त्वमसि भद्रं ते तन्ममाचक्ष्व पृच्छतः॥
en: Are you that Sītā, I do ask you, who had been stolen and borne away by Rāvana from Janasthāna? May good betide you!

sn: यथा हि तव वै दैन्यं रूपं चाप्यतिमानुषम् । तपसा चान्वितो वेषस्त्वं राममहिषी ध्रुवम्॥
en: From your wretched plight, your unrivalled beauty and your ascetic garb, you are, I ween, for certain, the queen of Rāma.

sn: सा तस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा रामकीर्तनहर्षिता। उवाच वाक्यं वैदेही हनूमन्तं दुमाश्रितम्॥
en: Hearing those words of Hanumān and greatly delighted at Rāma's name, Vaidehī spoke to him.

sn: पृथिव्यां राजसिंहानां मुख्यस्य विदितात्मनः। स्नुषा दशरथस्याहं शत्रुसैन्यप्रणाशिनः॥ दुहिता जनकस्याहं वैदेहस्य महात्मनः। सीतेति नाम्ना चोक्ताहं भार्या रामस्य धीमतः॥
en: I am the daughter-in-law of Dasaratha, knowing his own self, the foremost of the kings of the world and the slayer of the enemy's host, and the daughter of Janaka the high-souled king of Vaideha. My name is Sītā and I am the consort of the highly intelligent Rāma.

sn: समा द्वादश तत्राहं राघवस्य निवेशने। भुञ्जाना मानुषान् भोगान् सर्वकामसमृद्धिनी॥
en: I lived twelve years in Rāghava's abode, enjoying every earthly comfort and satisfying every desire.

sn: ततस्त्रयोदशे वर्षे राज्ये चेक्ष्वाकुनन्दनम्। अभिषेचयितुं राजा सोपाध्यायः प्रचक्रमे॥
en: And at the beginning of the thirteenth year the king, advised by his priest, arranged for the installation of the descendant of Ikşvākus (Rāma) on the throne.

sn: तस्मिन् सम्ध्रियमाणे तु राघवस्याभिषेचने। कैकेयी नाम भर्तारमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: And while the articles for the installation were being collected, the queen Kaikeyi addressed her lord saying.

sn: न पिबेयं न खादेयं प्रत्यहं मम भोजनम्। एष मे जीवितस्यान्तो रामो यद्यभिषिच्यते॥
en: I shall not drink or eat for days and this shall be the end of my existence if Räma be installed.

sn: यत्तदुक्तं त्वया वाक्यं प्रीत्या नृपतिसत्तम। तच्चेन्न वितथं कार्यं वनं गच्छतु राघवः॥
en: If you do not wish to falsify the vow (This refers to the vow which Dasaratha made to Kaikeyſ at the time of the war going on between the celestials and the Asuras) you made to me,O best of kings, let Rāma then repair to the forest.

sn: स राजा सत्यवाग् देव्या वरदानमनुस्मरन्। मुमोह वचनं श्रुत्वा कैकेय्याः क्रूरमप्रियम्॥
en: The monarch was truthful and remembering his vow and hearing the unpleasant and vile words of Kaikeyi lost himself (in grief).

sn: ततस्तं स्थविरो राजा सत्यधर्मे व्यवस्थितः। ज्येष्ठं यशस्विनं पुत्रं रुदन् राज्यमयाचत॥
en: Thereupon the old king abiding by truth, weeping, begged of his eldest son, the kingdom.

sn: स पितुर्वचनं श्रीमानभिषेकात् परं प्रियम्। मनसा पूर्वमासाद्य वाचा प्रतिगृहीतवान् ॥
en: The graceful Räma killed his sire's command more than the installation, and resolving within him, promised to obey his words.

sn: दद्यान्न प्रतिगृह्णीयात् सत्यं ब्रूयान्न चानृतम्। अपि जीवितहेतोहि रामः सत्यपराक्रमः॥
en: Rāma, having truth for his prowess, never, for his life, takes back what her gives, never speaks an untruth and always speaks truth.

sn: स विहायोत्तरीयाणि महार्हाणि महायशाः। विसृज्य मनसा राज्यं जनन्यै मां समादिशत्॥
en: Leaving aside his costly attire, the highly glorious (Rāma) renounced with all his heart the kingdom and gave me over to his mother.

sn: साहं तस्याग्रतस्तूर्णं प्रस्थिता वनचारिणी। नहि मे तेन हीनाया वासः स्वर्गेऽपि रोचते॥
en: But myself wearing the garb of an ascetic, repaired speedily before him. Separated from him, I do not like to live even in the celestial region.

sn: प्रागेव तु महाभागः सौमित्रिमित्रनन्दनः। पूर्वजस्यानुयात्रार्थे कुशचीरैरलंकृतः॥
en: The great son of Sumitrā, the enhancer of friends' joys, to follow his elder brother, dressed himself in bark and kusa.

sn: ते वयं भर्तुरादेशं बहुमान्य दृढव्रताः। प्रविष्टाः स्म पुरादृष्टं वनं गम्भीरदर्शनम्॥
en: Thus abiding by our sire's behest, and taking firm vows we entered a dreary forest never seen before.

sn: वसतो दण्डकारण्ये तस्याहममितौजसः। रक्षसापहृता भार्या रावणेन दुरात्मना ॥
en: While that one, of unmitigated effulgence was thus living in the forest of Dandaka, I, his consort, was stolen by the vicious-souled Rākşasa—Rāvaņa.

sn: द्वौ मासौ तेन मे कालो जीवितानुग्रहः कृतः। ऊर्ध्वं द्वाभ्यां तु मासाभ्यां ततस्त्यक्ष्यामि जीवितम्।।
en: He has kindly allowed me two months respite after which I shall be slain.

sn: तस्यास्तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा हनूमान् हरिपुङ्गवः। दुःखाद् दुःखाभिभूतायाः सान्त्वमुत्तरमब्रवीत्॥ अहं रामस्य संदेशाद् देवि दूतस्तवागतः। वैदेहि कुशली रामः स त्वां कौशलमब्रवीत् ॥
en: Hearing those words of Sītā stricken with grief, Hanumān, the foremost of the monkeys, replied in soothing words, O worshipful lady, by Rāma's decree I come as a messenger to these. He is sale and sound, O Vaidehi, and has asked of your welfare.

sn: यो ब्राह्ममस्त्रं वेदांश्च वेद वेदविदां वरः। स त्वां दाशरथी रामो देवि कौशलमब्रवीत्॥
en: O worshipful dame, Rāma, the son of Dasaratha, the master of the Vedas, and the foremost of those conversant with Vedas has enquired of your welfare.

sn: लक्ष्मणश्च महातेजा भर्तुस्तेऽनुचरः प्रियः। कृतवाञ्छोकसंतप्तः शिरसा तेऽभिवादनम्॥
en: And the highly effulgent Lakşmaņa, the beloved follower of your husband, worn with grief, bows his reverential head to you.

sn: सा तयोः कुशलं देवी निशम्य नरसिंहयोः। प्रतिसंहृष्टसर्वाङ्गी हनूमन्तमथाब्रवीत्॥
en: Hearing of the welfare of those two lions among men, the worshipful dame, with all her frame worked up with rapture, again spake to Hanumān, saying.

sn: कल्याणी वत गाथेयं लौकिकी प्रतिभाति मा। एति जीवन्तमानन्दो नरं वर्षशतादपि॥
en: Verily the wise saw of the people appears to me to be true that once in a hundred years true joy appears to a living man.

sn: तयोः समागमे तस्मिन् प्रीतिरुत्पादिताद्भुता। परस्परेण चालापं विश्वस्तौ तौ प्रचक्रतुः॥
en: Sītā, at that time, attained such a wonderful joy, as would have been acquired by her in the company (of Rama and Laksmana). And they confidingly conversed with each other.

sn: तस्यास्तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा हनूमान्मारुतात्मजः। सीतायाः शोकतप्तायाः समीपमुपचक्रमे॥
en: Hearing those words of $ītā, racked with sorrow, Hanumān, the son of the Wind-god drew a little nearer to her.

sn: यथा यथा समीपं स हनूमानुपसर्पति। तथा तथा रावणं सा तं सीता परिशङ्कते॥
en: The more Hanumān approached her the more Sītā suspected him as Rāvaņa.

sn: अहो धिग् धिक्कृतमिदं कथितं हि यदस्य मे। रूपान्तरमुपागम्य स एवायं हि रावणः॥
en: Alas! Alas! why have I spoken to him? It is the Rāvaņa, who has appeared again in a new disguise.

sn: तामशोकस्य शाखां तु विमुक्त्वा शोककर्शिता । तस्यामेवानवद्याङ्गी धरण्यां समुपाविशत्॥
en: And leaving off the Asoka branch, that one having a blameless person, overwhelmed with grief, sat down on the earth.

sn: अवन्दत महाबाहुस्ततस्तां जनकात्मजाम्। सा चैनं भयसंत्रस्ता भूयो नैनमुदैक्षत॥
en: In the meantime the mighty-armed monkey bowed to Janaka's daughter, but she, worked up with fear, did not cast again her looks towards him.

sn: तं दृष्ट्वा वन्दमानं च सीता शशिनिभानना। अब्रवीद् दीर्घमुच्छ्वस्य वानरं मधुरस्वरा ॥
en: Beholding him bow to her, Sítā, having a moon-like countenance, sighing, spoke to that monkey in sweet accents.

sn: मायां प्रविष्टो मायावी यदि त्वं रावणः स्वयम्। उत्पादयसि मे भूयः संतापं तन्न शोभनम्॥
en: If you are that Ravana's self, who, changing your shape by magic art, want to distress me again— this your vile deed dose not behove you.

sn: स्वं परित्यज्य रूपं यः परिव्राजकरूपवान्। जनस्थाने मया दृष्टस्त्वं स एव हि रावणः॥
en: You are surely that Rāvana, whom I saw at Janasthāna, in a mendicant's guise, renouncing his own shape.

sn: उपवासकृशां दीनां कामरूप निशाचर। संतापयसि मां भूयः संतापं तत्र शोभनम्॥
en: O night-ranger, O you wearing shapes at will! it dose not behove you to distress me who am poorly and famished with fasts.

sn: अथवा नैतदेवं हि यन्मया परिशङ्कितम्। मनसो हि मम प्रीतिरुत्पन्ना तव दर्शनात्॥
en: But no, you cannot be (the fiend) whom I suspect, since I have such joy from seeing you.

sn: यदि रामस्य दूतस्त्वमागतो भद्रमस्तु ते। पृच्छामि त्वां हरि श्रेष्ठ प्रिया रामकथा हि मे॥
en: And may good betide you if you are Rāma's messenger. I do ask you, O foremost of monkeys, something about Rāma that is pleasant to me.

sn: गुणान् रामस्य कथय प्रियस्य मम वानर। चित्तं हरसि मे सौम्य नदीकूलं यथा रयः॥
en: O monkey, do you relate the glories of my dear Rama. You are (thus) shaking my mind O gentle one, like to water breaking down the banks of a river.

sn: अहो स्वप्नस्य सुखता याहमेव चिराहता। प्रेषितं नाम पश्यामि राघवेण वनौकसम्॥
en: Alas! this dream has afforded me immense pleasure since, I, who have been separated from my lord for so long a time, have beheld this monkey sent by Rāghava.

sn: स्वप्नेऽपि यद्यहं वीरं राघवं सहलक्ष्मणम्। पश्येयं नावसीदेयं स्वप्नोऽपि मम मत्सरी॥
en: I do not sink even if I can behold in dream the heroic Raghava. along with Laksmana-but dream even is Jealous of my well-being.

sn: नाहं स्वप्नमिमं मन्ये स्वप्ने दृष्ट्वा हि वानरम्। न शक्योऽभ्युदयः प्राप्तुं प्राप्तश्चाभ्युदयो मम॥
en: Nor do I regard this as dream. To behold a monkey in a dream dose not lead to prosperity whereas I have attained it. (Here prosperity means joy-Sītā attained an immense treasure of joy on beholding Rāma's messengerHanumãn.)

sn: किं नु स्याच्चित्तमोहोऽयं भवेद् वातगतिस्त्वियम्। उन्मादजों विकारो वा स्यादयं मृगतृष्णिका॥
en: Or is it mental derangement? Or have I been possessed by a devil? Or have I run mad? Or is it the sultry vapour noating over sands and appearing at a distance like water?

sn: अथवा नायमुन्मादो मोहोऽप्युन्मादलक्षणः। सम्बुध्ये चाहमात्मानमिमं चापि वनौकसम्॥
en: No, it is not madness-for derangement of mind is the sign of madness, I have not lost sense and I do distinctly perceive me and the monkey.

sn: इत्येवं बहुधा सीता सम्प्रधार्य बलाबलम्। रक्षसां कामरूपत्वान्मेने तं राक्षसाधिपम्॥ एतां बुद्धिं तदा कृत्वा सीता सा तनुमध्यमा। न प्रतिव्याजहाराथ वानरं जनकात्मजा॥
en: Thinking thus in many a way and ascertaining the strength of the monkey and the Rākṣasa) Sītā took him for the lord of the Raksasas, wearing shapes at will. And having arrived at this decision, Janaka's daughter-Sītā, ceased from talking with that monkey.

sn: सीताया निश्चितं बुद्ध्वा हनूमान् मारुतात्मजः। श्रोत्रानुकूलैर्वचनैस्तदा तां सम्प्रहर्षयन्॥
en: And apprised of Sītā's thought, Hanumān, the Wind-god's son, (replied) in words sweet to her and enhancing her delight.

sn: आदित्य इव तेजस्वी लोककान्तः शशी यथा। राजा सर्वस्य लोकस्य देवो वैश्रवणो यथा ॥
en: Bright as the sun that lights the sky and dear as the moon to every eye, he pleases all his subjects with bounties like to those of as Vaisravana. (Another name of Kubera, the god of gold.)

sn: विक्रमेणोपपन्नश्च यथा विष्णुर्महायशाः। सत्यवादी मधुरवाग् देवो वाचस्पतिर्यथा॥
en: He is gifted with prowess like to the greatly famed Vişnu, truthful and sweet-speeched like to Vacaspati. (The god of speech)

sn: रूपवान् सुभगः श्रीमान् कन्दर्प इव मूर्तिमान्। स्थानक्रोधे प्रहर्ता च श्रेष्ठो लोके महारथः॥
en: Graceful, grateful to the eye and beautiful like to Kandarva's (Cupid or the god of love in Hindu mythology described the most beautiful of the celestials) Self, he displays his wrath in a proper quarter-the foremost of men and of a mighty car.

sn: बाहुच्छायामवष्टब्धो यस्य लोको महात्मनः। अपक्रम्याश्रमपदान्मृगरूपेण राघवम्॥ शून्ये येनापनीतासि तस्य द्रक्ष्यसि तत्फलम्।
en: The whole world of creation (live safe) in the shadow of the arms of that high-souled one. You shall soon see the consequences he shall reap by whom, assuming the shape of a dear, Rāghava was taken away from the hermitage and you wert stolen away from that lonely place.

sn: अचिराद् रावणं संख्ये यो वधिष्यति वीर्यवान्॥ क्रोधप्रमुक्तैरिषुभिर्व्वलद्भिरिव पावकैः।
en: And soon shall that powerful (hero) destroy Ravana in the battle, with fiery arrows, discharged angrily.

sn: तेनाहं प्रेषितो दूतस्त्वत्सकाशमिहागतः॥ त्वद्वियोगेन दुःखार्तः स त्वां कौशलमब्रवीत्। लक्ष्मणश्च महातेजाः सुमित्रानन्दवर्धनः॥ अभिवाद्य महाबाहुः स त्वां कौशलमब्रवीत्।
en: I have been sent by him as a messenger to you. Worn with grief in your separation he has enquired of your welfare, as well the highly effulgent Lakşmaņa, the enhancer of Sumitrā's joy, bowing reverentially to you.

sn: रामस्य च सखा देवि सुग्रीवो नाम वानरः॥ राजा वानरमुख्यानां स त्वां कौशलमब्रवीत्। नित्यं स्मरति ते रामः ससुग्रीवः सलक्ष्मणः॥
en: The king of monkey host, by name SugrīvaRama's friend, has also enquired of your welfare, O worshipful dame. Rāma, Sugrīva and Laksmana, have you always in their minds.

sn: दिष्ट्या जीवसि वैदेहि राक्षसीवशमागता। नचिराद् द्रक्ष्यसे राम लक्ष्मणं च महारथम्॥ मध्ये वानरकोटीनां सुग्रीवं चामितौजसम्। अहं सुग्रीवसचिवो हनूमान् नाम वानरः॥
en: Blessed are we, O Vaidehi, that you do still live, subject as you are to the Raksasis. You shall soon behold Rāma, and Lakşmaņa of a mighty car, and Sugrīva of unmitigated prowess in the midst of the million of monkey hosts. I am Sugrīva's minister, by name Hanumān.

sn: प्रविष्टो नगरी लङ्कां लवयित्वा महोदधिम्। कृत्वा मूर्ध्नि पदन्यासं रावणस्य दुरात्मनः॥
en: I have entered this city of Lankā after crossing over the great main. And by means of my prowess and placing my feet on the head of the vicious-souled Ravana.

sn: त्वां द्रष्टमुपयातोऽहं समाश्रित्य पराक्रमम्। नाहमस्मि तथा देवि यथा मामवगच्छसि। विशङ्का त्यज्यतामेषा श्रद्धत्स्व वदतो मम॥
en: I have come here to see you I am not he (Ravana) for whom you are taking me, O worshipful dame. Do you renounce your suspicion and rely on my words.

sn: तां तु रामकथां श्रुत्वा वैदेही वानरर्षभात्। उवाच वचनं सान्त्वमिदं मधुरया गिरा॥
en: Hearing the tale of Rāma from that best of monkeys, Vaidehī, spoke in sweet accents, soft and low.

sn: क्व ते रामेण संसर्गः कथं जानासि लक्ष्मणम्। वानराणां नराणां च कथमासीत् समागमः॥
en: Where didst you meet Rāma, how didst you come to know Lakşmaņa? How did the monkeys and men meet on terms of brother-hood?

sn: यानि रामस्य चिह्नानि लक्ष्मणस्य च वानर । तानि भूयः समाचक्ष्व न मां शोकः समाविशेत्॥
en: Do you again relate to me, O monkey, the regal signs that deck the persons of Rāma and Lakşmaņa-and I shall then relinquish all grief.

sn: कीदृशं तस्य संस्थानं रूपं तस्य च कीदृशम्। कथमूरू कथं बाहू लक्ष्मणस्य च शंस मे॥
en: Do you relate to me the form and grace of Rāma, his thighs and arms and as well as those of Laksmana.

sn: एवमुक्तस्तु वैदेह्या हनूमान् मारुतात्मजः। ततो रामं यथातत्त्वमाख्यातुमुपचक्रमे॥
en: Being thus addressed by Vaidehi, Hanuman, the Wind-god's son, began to give an exact description of Rāma.

sn: जानन्ती वत दिष्ट्या मां वैदेहि परिपृच्छसि। भर्तुः कमलपत्राक्षि संस्थानं लक्ष्मणस्य च॥ यानि रामस्य चिह्नानि लक्ष्मणस्य च यानि वै। लक्षितानि विशालाक्षि वदतः शृणु तानि मे।७।।
en: If do you, by my good luck, O Vaidehi, O you having eyes like lotus-petals, knowing me (as his messenger) ask me to describe your lord's person as well as that of Lakşmaņa, I shall relate them to you. Do you hear, O large-eyed dame, what regal signs I have marked on the persons of Rama and Laksmana.

sn: रामः कमलपत्राक्षः पूर्णचन्द्रनिभाननः । रूपदाक्षिण्यसम्पन्नः प्रसूतो जनकात्मजे॥
en: O daughter of Janaka, Rāma has eyes like lotus-petals and a countenance resembling the full-moon and is gifted with great beauty and goodness.

sn: तेजसाऽऽदित्यसंकाशः क्षमया पृथिवीसमः। बृहस्पतिसमो बुद्ध्या यशसा वासवोपमः॥ रक्षिता जीवलोकस्य स्वजनस्य च रक्षिता। रक्षिता स्वस्य वृत्तस्य धर्मस्य च परंतपः॥
en: In effulgence he is like the Sun, in patience like the earth, in intellect like BỊhaspati (The god of wisdom) and in fame like Vāsava. (The lord of celestials) He is the protector of the world of creation and his own kinsmen. He follows right in all his ways and never swerves from his royal duties and is the slayer of foes.

sn: रामो भामिनि लोकस्य चातुर्वर्ण्यस्य रक्षिता। मर्यादानां च लोकस्य कर्ता कारयिता च सः॥
en: O dame, he upholds the dignity of the people of four-castes— he confers honours on the people and preserves them.

sn: अर्चिष्मानर्चितोऽत्यर्थं ब्रह्मचर्यव्रते स्थितः। साधूनामुपकारज्ञः प्रचारज्ञश्च कर्मणाम्॥
en: He is worshipped by all like the Sun, observes ascetic vows, know well the time when the saints should be honoured and is conversant with the nature and procedure of actions.

sn: राजनीत्यां विनीतश्च ब्राह्मणानामुपासकः। ज्ञानवाशीलसम्पन्नो विनीतश्च परंतपः॥
en: He is well acquainted with royal duties and abode by the commandments of the Brāhmaṇas is wise, gifted with a good character, humble and the slayer of foes.

sn: यजुर्वेदविनीतश्च वेदविद्भिः सुपूजितः। धनुर्वेदे च वेदे च वेदाङ्गेषु च निष्ठितः॥
en: He is the master of Yajurvedas and is adored by those who are well-versed in Vedas—is proficient in the science of bended bow, Vedas and Vedāngas. (A sacred science considered as subordinate to and in some sense a part of the Vedas six sciences come under this denimination-Siksha (pronunciation); Kalp. (religious rite) Vyakarana (grammar) Chandas (prosody) Jyotis (astronomy) and and Nirukti explanation of difficult words.)

sn: विपुलांसो महाबाहुः कम्बुग्रीवः शुभाननः। गूढजत्रुः सुताम्राक्षो रामो नाम जनैः श्रुतः॥
en: He is broad-shouldered, large-armed, has a conch-like neck and a beautiful countenance. His throat is plump and his eyes are red-and he is famed all over the world under the name of Rāma.

sn: दुन्दुभिस्वननिर्घोषः स्निग्धवर्णः प्रतापवान्। समश्च सुविभक्ताङ्गो वर्णं श्यामं समाश्रितः॥
en: He has the voice of a bugle, is of a cool hue and highly powerful, has equally proportioned limbs and a green colour.

sn: त्रिस्थिरस्त्रिप्रलम्बश्च त्रिसमस्त्रिषु चोन्नतः। त्रिताम्रस्त्रिषु च स्निग्धो गम्भीरस्त्रिषु नित्यशः॥
en: His three limbs (thigh, fist and wrist) are hard and three others (brow arins and scrotum) are long; and three (tops of the hairs, scrotums and knee-joints) equal and three (navel, abdomen and breast) high. And three (the angles of the or three are cool and three (voice, navel and gait) are grave.

sn: त्रिवलीमांस्त्र्यवनतश्चतुर्व्यङ्गस्त्रिशीर्षवान्। चतुष्कलश्चतुर्लेखश्चतुष्किष्कुश्चतु:समः॥ चतुर्दशसमद्वन्द्वश्चतुर्दष्ट्रश्चतुर्गतिः। महोष्ठहनुनासश्च पञ्चस्निग्धोऽष्टवंशवान् ॥ दशपद्मो दशबृहत्रिभिर्व्याप्तो द्विशुल्कवान्। षडुन्नतो नवतनुस्त्रिभिर्व्याप्नोति राघवः॥
en: His belly and throat have three folds of skin. The sole of the foot, the lines thereon and the nipples are equally bended. His neck, eyes and back are short. He has three locks of hair on his head. He has four lines on his thumb indicating his proficiency in the four Vedas. His body is four hands tall; arms, thighs and checks are plump; eye-brows, the hollows of the nose, eyes, ears, lips, nipples; wrists, knee-joints, scrotums, hips, hands feet are all equally proportioned. Four teeth by the side of each row, are gifted with auspicious marks of the Gästras. His gaits are like those of a lion, tiger, elephant or a bull. His lips and jaws are fleshy and elevated. His nose is long; words, countenance, nails, down and skin are all cool; his two arms, two little fingers, two thighs and two legs are long; his face, eyes, mouth tongue, lips; palate, nipples, nails and feet are like lotuses, his breast, forehead, neck, arms, navel feet, back and ears are spacious. He is gifted with grace, fame and effulgence. His paternal and maternal race are pure. His armpit, belly, breasts, nose, shoulders and forehead are high; his fingers, hairs, down, nails, skin, beard, eye-sight and intellect are thin and sharp. Rāghava, with a due division of his time is engaged in acquiring piety, wealth emancipation and desires,

sn: सत्यधर्मरतः श्रीमान् संग्राहनुग्रहे रतः। देशकालविभागज्ञः सर्वलोकप्रियंवदः॥
en: He is truthful and graceful, amasses wealth and thereby protects his subjects. He is cognisant of the divisions of time and country and dear to all.

sn: भ्राता चास्य च द्वैमात्रः सौमित्रिरमितप्रभः। अनुरागेण रूपेण गुणैश्चापि तथाविधः॥
en: His step brother Saumitri is gifted with incomparable prowess and is his equal in attachment, beauty and accomplishments.

sn: ससुवर्णच्छविः श्रीमान् रामः श्यामो महायशाः। तावुभौ नरशार्दूलौ त्वदर्शनकृतोत्सवौ॥ विचिन्वन्तौ महीं कृत्स्नामस्माभिः सह संगतौ।
en: The person of that graceful one is gold-hued whereas that of the highly famous Rāma is green. And those two lions among men had no other delight but seeing you. And they ransacking the whole worid in quest of you met us in the forest.

sn: त्वामेव मार्गमाणौ तौ विचरन्तौ वसुंधराम्॥ ददर्शतुर्मूगपतिं पूर्वजेनावरोपितम्। ऋष्यमूकस्य मूले तु बहुपादपसंकुले॥ भ्रातुर्भयार्तमासीनं सुग्रीवं प्रियदर्शनम्।
en: And ranging the earth for you they beheld Sugriva, of comely presence, the lord of monkeys, at the foot of the mount Rsyamūka covered with trees, banished by his elder brother and resorting there in his fear.

sn: वयं च हरिराजं तं सुग्रीवं सत्यसङ्गरम्॥ परिचर्यामहे राज्यात् पूर्वजेनावरोपितम्।
en: We wears serving that truthful Sugrīva, the lord of monkeys, driven from the kingdom by his elder brother.

sn: ततस्तौ चीरवसनौ धनुःप्रवरपाणिनौ।। स तौ दृष्ट्वा नरव्याघ्रौ धन्विनौ वानरर्षभः॥ अभिप्लुतो गिरेस्तस्य शिखरं भयमोहितः।
en: Beholding those two best of men, wearing bark and with bows in their hands, that best of monkeys, stricken with fear, leaped above and stationed himself on the crest of the hill.

sn: ततः स शिखरे तस्मिन् वानरेन्द्रो व्यवस्थितः॥ तयोः समीपं मामेव प्रेषयामास सत्वरम्। तावहं पुरुषव्याघ्रौ सुग्रीववचनात् प्रभू॥ रूपलक्षणसम्पन्नौ कृताञ्जलिरुपस्थितः।
en: He then sent me to them. And thereupon by Sugrīva's decree I, approached with joined palms, those two foremost of men gifted with beauty and royal marks.

sn: तौ परिज्ञाततत्त्वार्थो मया प्रीतिसमन्वितौ॥ । पृष्ठमारोप्य तं देशं प्रापितौ पुरुषर्षभौ। निवेदितौ च तत्त्वेन सुग्रीवाय महात्मने॥
en: They were pleased by me, being informed of the real facts. And then placing those two best of men on my back I arrived at the top of the hill and communicated the truth to the high-souled Sugriva.

sn: तयोरन्योन्यसम्भाषाद् भृशं प्रीतिरजायत। तत्र तौ कीर्तिसम्पन्नौ हरीश्वरनरेश्वरौ॥ परस्परकृताश्वासौ कथया पूर्ववृत्तया।
en: And conversing with each other those two lords of men and monkeys attained great delight. And they consoled each other narrating their respective misfortunes.

sn: तं ततः सान्त्वयामास सुग्रीवं लक्ष्मणाग्रजः॥ स्त्रीहेतोलिना भ्रात्रा निरस्तं पुरुतेजसा।
en: And Rāma then consoled Sugrīva, driven away by his greatly powerful elder brother Vāli on his wife's account.

sn: ततस्त्वन्नाशजं शोकं रामस्याक्लिष्टकर्मणः॥ लक्ष्मणो वानरेन्द्राय सुग्रीवाय न्यवेदयत्।
en: Thereupon Lakşmaņa related to Sugrīva, the lord of monkeys, the grief, of Rāma of unwearied actions, in consequence of your being borne away (by Rāvana).

sn: स श्रुत्वा वानरेन्द्रस्तु लक्ष्मणेनेरितं वचः॥ तदासीनिष्प्रभोऽत्यर्थं ग्रहग्रस्त इवांशुमान्।
en: And hearing Laksmana's words, the lord of monkeys became pale, like to the radiant Sun possessed by Rāhu.

sn: ततस्त्वद्गात्रशोभीनि रक्षसा ह्रियमाणया॥ यान्याभरणजालानि पातितानि महीतले। तानि सर्वाणि रामाय आनीय हरियूथपाः॥ संहष्टा दर्शयामासुर्गतिं तु न विदुस्तव।
en: And collecting all those ornaments which were thrown off by you on the earth when you were borne away, the leaders of the monkey hosts, delighted brought them before Räma. But they could not make out your whereabouts.

sn: तानि रामाय दत्तानि मयैवोपहतानि च॥ स्वनवन्त्यवकीर्णानि तस्मिन् विहतचेतसि। तान्यङ्के दर्शनीयानि कृत्वा बहुविधं तदा॥ तेन देवप्रकाशेन देवेन परिदेवितम्।
en: All those ornaments, which were handed over to Rāma, were collected by me when they fell tinkling on the ground, Rāma being beside himself with grief. And placing them on his lap, the god-like Rāma bewailed in various accents.

sn: प्रादीपवद् दाशरथेस्तदा शोकहुताशनम्॥ शायितं च चिरं तेन दुःखार्तेन महात्मना। मयापि विविधैर्वाक्यैः कृच्छादुत्थापितः पुनः॥
en: They inflamed the more Dasarathi's (Son of Dasaratha-Rāma) grief. And being overwhelmed with grief that high-souled one laid himself low on the ground. And consoling him in various words, I raised him up again.

sn: तानि दृष्ट्वा महार्हाणि दर्शयित्वा मुहुर्मुहुः। राघवः सहसौमित्रिः सुग्रीवे संन्यवेशयत्।॥
en: Looking again and again with Saumitri, at those costly ornaments, Rāghava handed them over to Sugriva.

sn: स तवादर्शनादार्ये राघवः परितप्यते। महता ज्वलता नित्यमग्निनेवाग्निपर्वतः॥
en: Rāghava burns in grief, O worshipful dame, in your absence, like to a volcanic mountain burning with a perpetual fire.

sn: त्वत्कृते तमनिद्रा च शोकश्चिन्ता च राघवम्। तापयन्ति महात्मानमग्न्यगारमिवाग्नयः॥
en: For you, sleeplessness, grief and anxiety are distressing Rāghava like to three fires, (The aggregate of the three fires maintained by the Brāhmaṇa house-holder) burning down the fire temple.

sn: तवादर्शनशोकेन राघवः परिचाल्यते। महता भूमिकम्पेन महानिव शिलोच्चयः॥
en: Rāghava is moved by your separation like to a huge mountain shaken by a terrible earth-quake.

sn: काननानि सुरम्याणि नदीप्रस्रवणानि च। चरन रतिमाप्नोति त्वामपश्यन्नृपात्मजे॥
en: O daughter of a king, he is ranging at large in many a beautiful forest, river and fountain-but he finds delight nowhere.

sn: स त्वां मनुजशार्दूलः क्षिप्रं प्राप्स्यति राघवः। समित्रबान्धवं हत्वा रावणं जनकात्मजे॥ ।
en: O daughter of the king Janaka bringing about the destruction of Rāvaņa, with all his kith and kin, Rāghava, the foremost of men, shall soon regain you.

sn: सहितौ रामसुग्रीवावुभावकुरुतां तदा। समयं वालिनं हन्तुं तव चान्वेषणं प्रति ॥
en: Thus Rāma and Sugrīva entered into a friendly covenant, to encompass Vali's destruction and to institute enquiries about you.

sn: ततस्ताभ्यां कुमाराभ्यां वीराभ्यां स हरीश्वरः। किष्किन्धां समुपागम्य वाली युद्धे निपातितः॥
en: Thereupon returning to Kişkindhã with those two heroic princes, the lord of monkeys killed Vāli in battle.

sn: ततो निहत्य तरसा रामो वालिनमाहवे। सर्वक्षहरिसङ्घानां सुग्रीवमकरोत् पतिम्॥
en: And destroying Vāli by his prowess in battle, Rāma made Sugrīva king over all monkeys and bears.

sn: रामसुग्रीवयोरैक्यं देव्येवं समजायत। हनूमन्तं च मां विद्धि तयोर्दूतमुपागतम्॥
en: In this way, O dame, the alliance between Rāma and Sugrīva was made. And know me as Hanumān, their messenger who has come to you.

sn: स्वं राज्यं प्राप्य सुग्रीवः स्वानानीय महाकपीन्। त्वदर्थं प्रेषयामास दिशो दश महाबलान्॥
en: Regaining his kingdom, Sugrīva summoned all the mighty monkeys and despatched them in various quarters in quest of you.

sn: आदिष्टा वानरेन्द्रेण सुग्रीवेण महौजसः। अद्रिराजप्रतीकाशाः सर्वतः प्रस्थिता महीम्॥
en: The highly powerful monkeys, resembling mountains, commanded by that lord of monkeys, proceeded to all the regions of the earth.

sn: ततस्ते मार्गमाणा वै सुग्रीववचनातुराः। चरन्ति वसुधां कृत्स्नां वयमन्ये च वानराः॥
en: And terrified by Sugrīva's decrees, those monkeys, since then, have been ransacking the whole earth for you.

sn: अङ्गदो नाम लक्ष्मीवान् वालिसूनुर्महाबलः। प्रस्थितः कपिशार्दूलस्त्रिभागबलसंवृतः॥
en: Own I am one of them And the beautiful and mighty son of Vali, by name Angada, has proceeded with three armies under him.

sn: तेषां नो विप्रणष्टानां विन्ध्ये पर्वतसत्तमे। भृशं शोकपरीतानामहोरात्रगणा गताः॥
en: Many were the days and nights that we spent, overwhelmed with grief and having lost our way on that best of mountains Vindhya.

sn: ते वयं कार्यनैराश्यात्कालस्यातिक्रमेण च। भयाच्च कपिराजस्य प्राणांस्त्यक्तमुपस्थिताः॥
en: We gave up all our hopes for the accomplishment of our end and our appointed time was well-nigh spent. And in fear of that lord of monkeys we addressed ourselves to put au end to our live.

sn: विचित्य गिरिदुर्गाणि नदीप्रस्रवणानि च। अनासाद्य पदं देव्याः प्राणांस्त्यक्तुं व्यवस्थिताः॥
en: Ranging the mountain strongholds, rivers and fountains and not finding your reverence, we were ready to do away with our existence.

sn: ततस्तस्य गिरिर्मूर्ध्नि वयं प्रायमुपास्महे। दृष्ट्वा प्रायोपविष्टांश्च सर्वान्वानरपुङ्गवान्॥ भृशं शोकार्णवे मग्नः पर्यदेवयदङ्गदः।
en: And on the crest of that hill we took to fasting. And beholding those foremost of monkeys engaged in fasting Angada, sunk in grief, bewailed,

sn: तव नाशं च वैदेहि वालिनश्च तथा वधम्॥ प्रायोपवेशमस्माकं मरणं च जटायुषः। तेषां नः स्वामिसंदेशानिराशानां मुमूर्षताम्॥ कार्यहेतोरिहायातः शकुनिर्वीर्यवान् महान्। गृध्रराजस्य सोदर्यः सम्पातिर्नाम गृध्रराट्॥
en: O Vaidehī, mentioning your rape, the destruction of Vāli in that way, our fastings and Jatayu's death. While we were thus waiting, ready for death and giving up all hopes for the fulfilment of our master's behest, there appeared, as if the cause of our success, the mighty and powerful vulture, the brother of Jațãyu, by name Sampati.

sn: श्रुत्वा भ्रातृवधं कोपादिदं वचनमब्रवीत्। यवीयान् केन मे भ्राता हतः क्व च निपातितः॥ एतदाख्यातुमिच्छामि भवद्भिर्वानरोत्तमाः।
en: Hearing of the destruction of his brother, he in wrath, said-'By whom and where has my younger brother been killed? I wish to hear this from you, the foremost of monkeys.

sn: अङ्गदोऽकथयत् तस्य जनस्थाने महद्वधम्॥ रक्षसा भीमरूपेण त्वामुदिश्य यथार्थतः।
en: Angada related to him verily Jațāyu's destruction at Janasthāna, for you, by that grimvisaged Rākṣasa.

sn: जटायोस्तु वधं श्रुत्वा दुःखितः सोऽरुणात्मजः॥ त्वामाह स वरारोहे वसन्ती रावणालये।
en: Hearing of Jatayu's death, Aruna's son became afflicted with sorrow and informed us, O you exquisitely fine damsel, of your stay in the abode of Rāvaņa.

sn: तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा सम्पातेः प्रीतिवर्धनम्॥ अङ्गदप्रमुखाः सर्वे ततः प्रस्थापिता वयम्। विन्ध्यादुत्थाय सम्प्राप्ताः सागरस्यान्तमुत्तमम्॥ त्वदर्शने कृतोत्साहा हृष्टाः पुष्टाः प्लवङ्गमाः। अङ्गदप्रमुखा सर्वे वेलोपान्तमुपागताः॥
en: Hearing those words of Sampāti, enhancing our delight, we all, headed by Angada, left that place. And leaping from the crest of Vindhya mountain we reached the excellent brink of the Ocean. Being greatly anxious to behold you and delighted, those plump monkeys headed by Angada, arrived at the banks of the main.

sn: चिन्तां जग्मुः पुनर्भीमां त्वदर्शनसमुत्सुकाः। अथाहं हरिसैन्यस्य सागरं दृश्य सीदतः॥ व्यवधूय भयं तीव्र योजनानां शतं प्लुतः। लङ्का चापि मया रात्रौ प्रविष्टा राक्षसाकुला॥ रावणश्च मया दृष्टस्त्वं च शोकनिपीडिता ।
en: And worked up with a strong desire to see you, they again engaged in anxious thought. And beholding the ocean, the monkey hosts lost their heart. And removing their fear, I leaped a hundred leagues across the deep and entered Lankā, at night, infested with demons. I have seen Rāvana, and you stricken with grief.

sn: एतत् ते सर्वमाख्यातं यथावृत्तमनिन्दिते॥ अभिभाषस्व मां देवि दूतो दाशरथेरहम्।
en: O you of a blameless person, I have related all to you in regular order. Do you speak to me, O worshipful dame, I am Dasarathi's messenger.

sn: तन्मां रामकृतोद्योगं त्वन्निमित्तमिहागतम्॥ सुग्रीवसचिवं देवि बुद्ध्यस्व पवनात्मजम्।
en: Do you know me as the Wind-god's son, the counsellor of Sugrīva, who am engaged in Rāma's service and have come here for you.

sn: कुशली तव काकुत्स्थः सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वरः॥ गुरोराराधने युक्तो लक्ष्मणः शुभलक्षणः। तस्य वीर्यवतो देवि भर्तुस्तव हिते रतः।७४।।
en: It is all well with your Kākuthstha, the foremost of those using weapons, as well as with Laksmana, O worshipful dame, gifted with auspicious marks, engaged in the worship of his superiors and in the well being of your lord.

sn: अहमेकस्तु सम्प्राप्तः सुग्रीववचनादिह। मयेयमसहायेन चरता कामरूपिणा॥ दक्षिणा दिगनुक्रान्ता त्वन्मार्गविचयैषिणा।
en: By Sugrīva's decree, I alone have reached here. And I, ranging alone and wearing shapes at will, have come to this southern quarter, to find out your where abouts.

sn: दिष्ट्याहं हरिसैन्यानां त्वन्नाशमनुशोचताम्॥ अपनेष्यामि संतापं तवाधिगमशासनात्।
en: By my good luck I shall be able, with your news, to remove the grief of those monkey hosts who are lamenting for you.

sn: दिष्ट्या हि न मम व्यर्थं सागरस्येह लङ्घनम्॥ प्राप्स्याम्यहमिदं देवि त्वद्दर्शनकृतं यशः।
en: By my good fortune, my crossing over the main, has not become fruitless. I shall be praised there, O worshipful dame, for I have been able to see you.

sn: राघवश्च महावीर्यः क्षिप्रं त्वामभिपत्स्यते। ७८ ।। सपुत्रबान्धवं हत्वा रावणं राक्षसाधिपम्।
en: And the highly powerful Rāghava shall soon regain you, destroying, with all his sons and friends, Ravana the king of Raksasas.

sn: माल्यवान् नाम वैदेहि गिरिणामुत्तमो गिरिः । ७९ ।। ततो गच्छति गोकर्ण पर्वतं केसरी हरिः। स च देवर्षिभिर्दिष्टः पिता मम महाकपिः।। तीर्थे नदीपतेः पुण्ये शम्बसादनमुद्धरन्॥ यस्याहं हरिणः क्षेत्रे जातो वातेन मैथिलि। हनूमानिति विख्यातो लोके स्वेनैव कर्मणा ॥
en: There is a hill, O Vaidehi, named Malyavana, the foremost of all the mountains. There lives my father, the great monkey Kesari. Being commanded by the celestial ascetics, he once repaired thence to the mount Gokarna and at the holy watering place of the lord of the rivers he brought about the destruction of (the Asura) Sammasādana. O Vaidehi, I was bom, on the field, of that monkey. And I am known all over the world as Hanumān by my own actions.

sn: विश्वासार्थं तु वैदेहि भर्तुरुक्ता मया गुणाः। अचिरात् त्वामितो देवि राघवो नयिता ध्रुवम्॥ एवं विश्वासिता सीता हेतुभिः शोककर्शिता। उपपत्नैरभिज्ञानैर्दूतं तमधिगच्छति॥
en: To create your confidence, O Vaidehi, I have related your lord's accomplishments. And forsooth, you shall soon be taken, O worshipful dame, by Rāghava. Having her confidence formed by these reasonings and various marks, Sītā, worn with grief, took him (for Rāma's messenger).

sn: अतुलं च गता हर्षं प्रहर्षेण तु जानकी। नेत्राभ्यां वक्रपक्ष्माभ्यां मुमोचानन्दजं जलम्॥
en: Jānakī attained an excess of delight and shed tears of joy from her eyes having curling eyelashes.

sn: चारु तद् वदनं तस्यास्ताम्रशुक्लायतेक्षणम्। अशोभत विशालाक्ष्या राहुमुक्त इवोडुराट्॥
en: The beautiful countenance of that large-eyed dame, having spacious eyes, appeared like the Moon released from the hold of Rāhu.

sn: हनूमन्तं कपि व्यक्तं मन्यते नान्यथेति सा। अथोवाच हनूमांस्तामुत्तरं प्रियदर्शनाम्॥
en: She then took him for a real monkey and none else. Thereupon Hanumān again spoke to her, having a comely presence,

sn: एतत् ते सर्वमाख्यातं समाश्वसिहि मैथिलि। किं करोमि कथं वा ते रोचते प्रतियाम्यहम्॥
en: I have related to you all this. Do you be consoled, O Maithili! Tell me now, what am I to do and what do you like. I shall soon repair hence.

sn: हतेऽसुरे संयति शम्बसादने कपिप्रवीरेण महर्षिचोदनात्।। ततोऽस्मि वायुप्रभवो हि मैथिलि प्रभावतस्तत्प्रतिमश्च वानरः॥
en: When the Asura Śambasādana was destroyed in conflict by that best of monkeys at the desire of the celestial ascetics, I was born of the Wind, O Maithili. I look like a monkey but am his equa's in prowess.

sn: हतेऽसुरे संयति शम्बसादने कपिप्रवीरेण महर्षिचोदनात्।। ततोऽस्मि वायुप्रभवो हि मैथिलि प्रभावतस्तत्प्रतिमश्च वानरः॥
en: When the Asura Śambasādana was destroyed in conflict by that best of monkeys at the desire of the celestial ascetics, I was born of the Wind, O Maithili. I look like a monkey but am his equa's in prowess.

sn: भूय एव महातेजा हनूमान् पवनात्मजः। अब्रवीत् प्रश्रितं वाक्यं सीताप्रत्ययकारणात्॥
en: The highly effulgent son of the Wind-god, Hanumān, to create Sītā's confidence, again addressed her with the following words.

sn: वानरोऽहं महाभागे दूतो रामस्य धीमतः। रामनामाङ्कितं चेदं पश्य देव्यङ्गुलीयकम्॥ प्रत्ययार्थं तवानीतं तेन दत्तं महात्मना। समाश्वसिहि भद्रं ते क्षीणदुःखफला ह्यसि॥
en: O great dame, I am a monkey, the messenger of the highly intelligent Rāma. Behold this precious ring with Rāma's name engraven on it, given by your high-souled lord and brought as a token to create your confidence. Do you take heart and may good betide you, there will be an end of your grief soon.

sn: गृहीत्वा प्रेक्षमाणा सा भर्तुः करविभूषितम्। भर्तारमिव सम्प्राप्त जानकी मुदिताभवत्॥
en: Taking the ring that used to deck her lord's finger and looking at it, Jānaki seemed to have actually got her lord.

sn: चारु तद् वदनं तस्यास्ताम्रशुक्लायतेक्षणम्। बभूव हर्षोदग्रं च राहुमुक्त इवोडुराट्॥
en: Her graceful countenance, having large eyes, looked, with delight, like to the Moon released from the possession of Rāhu.

sn: ततः सा ह्रीमती बाला भर्तुः संदेशहर्षिता। परितुष्टा प्रियं कृत्वा प्रशशंस महाकपिम्॥
en: And greatly delighted at her husband's news that modest damsel, affectionately welcoming Hanumăn, applauded that great monkey.

sn: विक्रान्तस्त्वं समर्थस्त्वं प्राज्ञस्त्वं वानरोत्तम। येनेदं राक्षसपदं त्वयैकेन प्रधर्षितम्॥
en: O foremost of monkeys, you are brave, powerful and wise, since you had alone smitten this abode of the Rākşasas.

sn: शतयोजनविस्तीर्णः सागरो मकरालयः। विक्रमश्लाघनीयेन क्रमता गोष्पदीकृतः॥
en: You had, with they laudable prowess, leaped, a hundred leagues, across the ocean, the abode of marine mousters, taking it for Gospada. (A measure as much as a cow's foot-step will hold.)

sn: न हि त्वां प्राकृतं मन्ये वानरं वानरर्षभ। यस्य ते नास्ति संत्रासो रावणादपि संभ्रमः॥
en: O foremost of monkeys, I do not consider you as an ordinary monkey, since you do not care or fear Ravana.

sn: अर्हसे च कपिश्रेष्ठ मया समभिभाषितुम्। यद्यसि प्रेषितस्तेन रामेण विदितात्मना॥ प्रेषयिष्यति दुर्धर्षो रामो नह्यपरीक्षितम्। पराक्रममविज्ञाय मत्सकाशं विशेषतः॥
en: O best of monkeys, you are worthy of my welcome, since you had been despatched by Rāma, knowing self, Rāma, hard of being got at, has not sent you, specially to me, without a trial of your prowess.

sn: दिष्ट्या च कुशली रामो धर्मात्मा सत्यसंगरः। लक्ष्मणश्च महातेजाः सुमित्रानन्दवर्धनः॥
en: By my good luck, is it all well with the virtuous-souled and truthful Rāma and the highly powerful Lakşmaņa the enhancer of Sumitra's joy?

sn: कुशली यदि काकुत्स्थः किं न सागरमेखलाम्। मही दहति कोपेन युगान्ताग्निरिवोत्थितः॥
en: And if Kākutstha lives untouched by ill, then why does he not burn the earth, encircled by the ocean with his ire like to the fire of dissolution?

sn: अथवा शक्तिमन्तौ तौ सुराणामपि निग्रहे। ममैव तु न दुःखानामस्ति मन्ये विपर्ययः॥
en: Or they are capable of discomfiting the celestials in a battle but me-thinks by my illluck, the end of my miseries has not arrived as yet.

sn: कच्चिन्न व्यथते रामः कच्चिन्न परितप्यते। उत्तराणि च कार्याणि कुरुते पुरुषोत्तमः॥
en: Is Rāma greatly pained? Does he grieve? Is that foremost of men making preparations of my rescue?

sn: कच्चिन्न दीनः सम्भ्रान्तः कार्येषु च न मुह्यति। कच्चित् पुरुषकार्याणि कुरुते नृपतेः सुतः॥
en: Has he forgotten his work being overwhelmed with fear and poorliness of heart? Is that son of the king performing still his manly duties?

sn: द्विविधं त्रिविधोपायमुपायमपि सेवते। विजिगीषुः सुहृत् कच्चिन्मित्रेषु च परंतपः॥ "
en: Is that slayer of foes, desirous of acquiring victory, pleasing his friends still with forgiveness and gifts and dealing his enemies with punishment, sowing dassensions among them, and with other expedients?

sn: कच्चिन्मित्राणि लभतेऽमित्रैश्चाप्यभिगम्यते। कच्चित् कल्याणमित्रश्च मित्रैश्चापि पुरस्कृतः॥
en: Is he still gaining friends and are friends gathering around him? Is he welcoming his friends and are they honouring him the more?

sn: कचिदाशास्ति देवानां प्रसादं पार्थिवात्मजः। कच्चित् पुरुषकारं च दैवं च प्रतिपद्यते॥
en: Is that son of the king invoking the blessings of the celestials? Has he attained manliness and assistance from the celestials?

sn: कच्चिन्न विगतस्नेहो विवासान्मयि राघवः। कच्चिन्मां व्यसनादस्मान्मोक्षयिष्यति राघवः॥
en: Has Rāghava lost all his affection for me for my living at a distance from him? Will he save me from this disaster?

sn: सुखानामुचितो नित्यमसुखानामनूचितः। दुःखमुत्तरमासाद्य कच्चिद् रामो न सीदति ॥
en: Has not Rāma, ever used to happiness and unused to misery, been enfeebled by this disaster?

sn: कौसल्यायास्तथा कच्चित् सुमित्रायास्तथैव च। अभीक्ष्णं श्रूयते कच्चित् कुशलं भरतस्य च ॥
en: Is he informed always of the welfare of Kauslyā, Sumitrā and Bharata?

sn: मन्निमित्तेन मानाहः कच्चिच्छोकेन राघवः। कच्चिन्नान्धमना रामः कच्चिन्मां तारयिष्यति॥
en: Is not Rāghava, worthy of honours, beside himself with grief in my absence? Will not Rāma rescue me?

sn: कच्चिदक्षौहिणी भीमां भरतो भ्रातृवत्सलः। ध्वजिन मन्त्रिभिर्गुप्तां प्रेषयिष्यति मत्कृते॥
en: Will not Bharata, ever devoted to his brother, send out one Akşauhiņī of terrible soldiers under the command of his ministers for my rescue?

sn: वानराधिपतिः श्रीमान् सुग्रीवः कच्चिदेष्यति। मत्कृते हरिभिवीरैर्वृतो दन्तनखायुधैः॥
en: Will not the graceful Sugrīva, the lord of the monkeys come to help ine with hosts of monkeys having huge teeth and nails?

sn: कच्चिच्च लक्ष्मणः शूरः सुमित्रानन्दवर्धनः। अस्त्रविच्छरजालेन राक्षसान् विधमिष्यति॥
en: Will not the heroic Lakşmaņa, the enhancer of Sumitrā's joy, conversant with the use of weapons, burn down the Rākşasas with this shafts?

sn: रौद्रेण कच्चिदस्त्रेण रामेण निहतं रणे। द्रक्ष्याम्यल्पेन कालेन रावणं ससुहृज्जनम्॥
en: Shall I not behold soon that Rāvana with his kinsmen has been destroyed in battle by Rāma with terrible weapons?

sn: कच्चिन्न तद्धेमसमानवणं तस्याननं पद्मसमानगन्धि। मया विना शुष्यति शोकदीनं जलक्षये पद्ममिवातपेन॥
en: Is not the gold-hued and lotus-smelling countenance (of Rāma) dried up my absence like to lotus dried up by the rays of the sun in shallow water?

sn: धर्मापदेशात् त्यजतः स्वराज्यं मां चाप्यरण्यं नयतः पदातेः। नासीद् यथा यस्य न भीन शोकः कच्चित् स धैर्य हृदये करोति॥
en: Does he still hold patience in his heart, who, renouncing his kingdom for virtue and repairing, on foot with me even to the forest, was not stricken with fear and grief?

sn: न चास्य माता न पिता न चान्यः स्नेहाद् विशिष्टोऽस्ति मया समो वा। तावद्ध्यहं दूत जिजीविषेयं यावत् प्रवृत्तिं शृणुयां प्रियस्य॥
en: His love for his mother, father or any other person is not greater than or equal to his love for me. O messenger, I shall keep my life so long I do not hear anything about my dear one.

sn: इतीव देवीवचनं महार्थं तं वानरेन्द्रं मधुरार्थमुक्त्वा। श्रोतुं पुनस्तस्य वचोऽभिरामं रामार्थयुक्तं विरराम रामा॥
en: Having addressed that lord of monkeys with these highly sound and sweet accents, that graceful and worshipful dame ceased, with a view to hear again from him pleasant tales regarding Rāma.

sn: सीताया वचनं श्रुत्वा मारुतिर्भीमविक्रमः। शिरस्यञ्जलिमाधाय वाक्यमुत्तरमब्रवीत्॥
en: Hearing the words of Sītā the terribly powerful Măruti, placing his joined palms on his head said,

sn: न त्वामिहस्थां जानीते रामः कमललोचनः। तेन त्वां नानयत्याशु शचीमिव पुरंदरः॥
en: The lotus-eyed Rāma dose not know that you are here, and hence he has not been able to rescue you like to Purandara regaining Saci.

sn: श्रुत्वैव च वचो मह्यं क्षिप्रमेष्यति राघवः। चमूं प्रकर्षन् महतीं हर्यक्षगणसंयुताम्॥
en: Hearing about you from me soon shall Rāghava come assisted by a large army of monkeys and bears.

sn: विष्टम्भयित्वा बाणौघैरक्षोभ्यं वरुणालयम्। करिष्यति पुरीं लङ्कां काकुत्स्थः शान्तराक्षसाम्॥
en: Impeding the course of the unagitated deep and building by means of his terrible shafts, a bridge across it, Kākutstha, shall divest the city Lankā of all the Rākşasas.

sn: तत्र यद्यन्तरा मृत्युर्यदि देवा महासुराः। स्थास्यन्ति पथि रामस्य स तानपि वधिष्यति॥
en: And forsooth shall Rāma destroy them, even if the celestials, or Death himself stand in his way.

sn: तवादर्शनजेनार्ये शोकेन परिपूरितः। न शर्म लभते रामः सिंहार्दित इव द्विपः॥
en: O worshipful dame, stricken with grief in your absence, Rāma is restless like to an elephant smitten by a lion.

sn: मन्दरेण च ते देवि शपे मूलफलेन च। मलयेन च विन्ध्येन मेरुणा दर्दुरेण च ॥ यथा सुनयनं वल्गु बिम्बोष्ठं चारुकुण्डलम्। मुखं द्रक्ष्यसि रामस्य पूर्णचन्द्रमिवोदितम्॥
en: I can swear, O worshipful dame, by the mounts Mandara, Malaya, Vindhya, Sumeru, Dardura and all the fruits and roots, that you shall behold like to the rising of the full moon, the countenance of Rāma having beautiful eyes, graceful, Bimba-like lips and beautified with beautiful kundalas.

sn: क्षिप्रं द्रक्ष्यसि वैदेहि रामं प्रस्रवणे गिरौ। शतक्रतुमिवासीनं नागपृष्ठस्य मूर्धनि ॥
en: You shall soon behold, O Vaidehī, Rāma, on the mount Prasravana, like to the performer of hundred sacrifices seated on the back of the elephant (Airăvata).

sn: न मांसं राघवो भुङ्क्ते न चैव मधु सेवते। वन्यं सुविहितं नित्यं भक्तमश्नाति पञ्चमम्॥
en: Rāghava dose not take meat nor drink honeyế he takes every day in the evening boiled rice and such wild fruits as are sanctioned by the Sastras.

sn: नैव दंशान् न मशकान् न कीटान् न सरीसृपान्। राघवोऽपनयेद् गात्रात् त्वद्गतेनान्तरात्मना ॥
en: His heart is so much attached to you, that he does not drive away even flies, insects and snakes from his body.

sn: नित्यं ध्यानपरो रामो नित्यं शोकपरायणः। नान्यच्चिन्तयते किंचित् स तु कामवशं गतः।॥
en: Rāma is always engaged in meditations, overwhelmed with grief, and he has no other thought but seeing you.

sn: अनिद्रः सततं रामः सुप्तोऽपि च नरोत्तमः। सीतेति मधुरां वाणी व्याहरन् प्रतिबुध्यते॥
en: Rāma has no sleep and even when asleep that best of men awakes exclaiming in sweep accents, 'O Sītā!'

sn: दृष्ट्वा फलं वा पुष्पं वा यच्चान्यत् स्त्रीमनोहरम्। बहुशो हा प्रियेत्येवं श्वसंस्त्वामभिभाषते॥
en: He always welcomes you sighing and saying “O my dear love!", whenever he beholds any fruit, flower or any object liked by the ladies.

sn: स देवि नित्यं परितप्यमानस्त्वामेव सीतेत्यभिभाषमाणः। धृतव्रतो राजसुतो महात्मा तवैव लाभाय कृतप्रयत्नः।।४६
en: O worshipful dame, he is always lamenting, exclaiming "O Sītā!, and that high-souled son of the king, to regain you, has resorted to ascetic observances."

sn: सा रामसंकीर्तनवीतशोका रामस्य शोकेन समानशोका। शरन्मुखेनाम्बुदशेषचन्द्रा निशेव वैदेहसुता बभूव ॥
en: On hearing about Rāma, Sītā was greatly delighted and she was equally grieved on hearing of his sorrow. And it appeared like the rising of the moon and the appearance of the clouds at the same time in an autumnal night.

sn: सा सीता वचनं श्रुत्वा पूर्णचन्द्रनिभानना। हनूमन्तमुवाचेदं धर्मार्थसहितं वचः॥
en: Hearing those words, Sītā having a moon-like countenance, again spoke to Hanuman, words, sound and pious:

sn: अमृतं विषसंपृक्तं त्वया वानर भाषितम्। यच्च नान्यमना रामो यच्च शोकपरायणः॥
en: O monkey, what you had said that Rāma is not attached to any other thing and is worn with grief, is like nectar mixed with poison.

sn: ऐश्वर्ये वा सुविस्तीर्णे व्यसने वा सुदारुणे। रज्ज्वेव पुरुषं बद्ध्वा कृतान्तः परिकर्षति॥
en: Whether in the enjoyment of vast riches, or emerged in the abyss of miseries, Death is pulling a man, binding him roughly with a chord.

sn: विधिनमसंहार्यः प्राणिनां प्लवगोत्तम। सौमित्रिं मां च रामं च व्यसनैःपश्य मोहितान्॥
en: O best of monkey, people cannot thwart the course of de tiny. Behold me, Rāma and Saumitri, therefore sunk in miseries.

sn: शोकस्यास्य कथं पारं राघवोऽधिगमिष्यति। प्लवमानः परिक्रान्तो हतनौः सागरे यथा॥
en: I do not know when shall Rāghava get at the other end of the ocean of grief, by displaying his prowess, like to one, swimming across the ocean when the boat is sunk.

sn: राक्षसानां वधं कृत्वा सूदयित्वा च रावणम्। लङ्कामुन्मथितां कृत्वा कदा द्रक्ष्यति मां पतिः॥
en: I do not know when shall my lord see me, destroying the Rākşasas, killing Rāvana and devastating the city of Lankā.

sn: स वाच्यः संत्वरस्वेति यावदेव न पूर्यते। अयं संवत्सरः कालस्तावद्धि मम जीवितम्॥
en: Do you tell him to come before this year expires for till then I shall live.

sn: वर्तते दशमो मासो द्वौ तु शेषौ प्लवङ्गम। रावणेन नृशंसेन समयो यः कृतो मम॥
en: This is the tenth month and two months still remain, O monkey and that is the time appointed by the cruel Rāvaņa.

sn: विभीषणेन च भ्रात्रा मम निर्यातनं प्रति। अनुनीतः प्रयत्नेन न च तत् कुरुते मतिम्॥
en: He was entreated very much by his brother Vibhīşaņa to restore me but he paid no need to his requests.

sn: मम प्रतिप्रदानं हि रावणस्य न रोचते। रावणं मार्गते संख्ये मृत्युः कालवशंगतम्॥
en: Rāvana dose not desire to restore me (to Rāma) for he has been brought under the influence of Death who is seeking him in battle.

sn: ज्येष्ठा कन्या कला नाम विभीषणसुता कपे। तया ममैतदाख्यातं मात्रा प्रहितया स्वयम्॥
en: Vibhisana's eldest daughter, O monkey, by name Kalā, has related this to me, being appointed by her mother.

sn: अविन्ध्यो नाम मेधावी विद्वान् राक्षसपुङ्गवः। धृतिमाञ्छीलवान् वृद्धो रावणस्य सुसम्मतः॥ रामात् क्षयमनुप्राप्तं रक्षसां प्रत्यचोदयत्। न च तस्य स दुष्टात्मा शृणोति वचनं हितम्॥
en: There is a leading, steady, old, intelligent and educated Rākşasa, gifted with a good character, named Avindhya and highly respected of Rāvana who told him that the destruction of the Rākṣasa race would proceed from Rāma, but the vicious-souled one paid no attention to his wellmeaning words. is my

sn: आशंसेयं हरिश्रेष्ठ क्षिप्रं मां प्राप्स्यते पतिः। अन्तरात्मा हि मे शुद्धस्तस्मिंश्च बहवो गुणाः॥
en: I hope, O foremost of monkeys, that my husband shall soon regain me for pure soul and he is gifted with many accomplishments.

sn: उत्साहः पौरुषं सत्त्वमानृशंस्यं कृतज्ञता। विक्रमश्च प्रभावश्च सन्ति वानर राघवे॥
en: Rāghava has in him, O monkeys, energy, manliness, strength, kindness, gratitude and prowess.

sn: चतुर्दश सहस्राणि राक्षसानां जघान यः। जनस्थाने विना भ्रात्रा शत्रुः कस्तस्य नोद्विजेत्॥
en: He brought about without his brother's aid, the destruction of the fourteen thousand Rākṣasas at Janasthāna. What enemy is not troubled at this?

sn: न स शक्यस्तुलयितुं व्यसनैः पुरुषर्षभः। अहं तस्यानुभावज्ञा शक्रस्येव पुलोमजा॥
en: The disaster-creating Rākşasas can never be compared with that best of men. I am cognizant of his prowess as Sacī is of Indra's.

sn: शरजालांशुमाञ्छूरः कपे रामदिवाकरः। शत्रुरक्षोमयं तोयमुपशोषं नयिष्यति॥
en: O monkey, Rāma the Sun, with his arrow-like rays, shall dry up the water-the inimical Rākşasas.

sn: इति संजल्पमानां तां रामार्थे शोककर्शिताम्। अश्रुसम्पूर्णवदनामुवाच हनुमान् कपिः॥
en: Saying this she was overwhelmed with grief on Rāma's account, and Hanumān again spoke to her having her countenance bathed in tears.

sn: श्रुत्वैव च वचो मह्यं क्षिप्रमेष्यति राघवः। चमूं प्रकर्षन् महतीं हर्यक्षगणसंकुलाम्॥
en: No sooner shall Rāghava hear from me than he shall speedily repair hither followed by a huge army of monkeys and bears.

sn: अथवा मोचयिष्यामि त्वामद्यैव सराक्षसात्। अस्माद् दुःखादुपारोह मम पृष्ठमनिन्दिते॥
en: Or I shall release you even to-day from the grasp of that Räkşasa and these miseries. Do you place yourself on my back, O you of a blameless person.

sn: त्वां तु पृष्ठगतां कृत्वा संतरिष्यामि सागरम्। शक्तिरस्ति हि मे वोढुं लङ्कामपि सरावणाम्॥
en: And having you on my back I shall leap over the main. I am capable of carrying the city of Lankā even with Rāvana.

sn: अहं प्रस्रवणस्थाय राघवायाद्य मैथिलि। प्रापयिष्यामि शक्राय हव्यं हुतमिवानलः॥
en: I shall restore you to-day, O Maithili, to Rāghava on the mount Prasravaņa, like to fire carrying to Indra, the sacrificial offerings.

sn: द्रक्ष्यस्यद्यैव वैदेहि राघवं सहलक्ष्मणम्। व्यवसायसमायुक्तं विष्णुं दैत्यवधे यथा॥
en: You shall behold to-day, O Vaidehi, Rama along with Lakşmaņa, making preparations (for the destruction of his enemy) like to Vişņu, engaged in the destruction of demons.

sn: त्वदर्शनकृतोत्साहमाश्रमस्थं महाबलम्। पुरंदरमिवासीनं नगराजस्य मूर्धनि॥
en: (And you shall observe) that highly powerful one, anxious to behold you and seated like to Purandara on the summit of that foremost of mountains.

sn: पृष्ठमारोह मे देवि मा विकाङ्क्षस्व शोभने। योगमन्विच्छ रामेण शशाङ्केनेव रोहिणी॥
en: Do you place yourself on my back, O worshipful dame, do you not neglect it, O beautiful lady, and be thus reconciled to Rāma like to Rohini restored to the Moon.

sn: कथयन्तीव शशिना संगमिष्यसि रोहिणी। मत्पृष्ठमधिरोह त्वं तराकाशं महार्णवम्॥
en: By the time, that we will take in talking thus, you shall reach Rāma like Rohiņi restored to the Moon. Do you therefore place yourself on my back and I shall cross the ocean sailing by the aetherial way.

sn: नहि मे सम्प्रयातस्य त्वामितो नयतोऽङ्गने। अनुगन्तुं गतिं शक्ताः सर्वे लङ्कानिवासिनः॥
en: O fair one, carrying you from this place, none among the inhabitants of Lankä shall be able to follow me.

sn: यथैवाहमिह प्राप्तस्तथैवाहमसंशयम्। यास्यामि पश्य वैदेहि त्वामुद्यम्य विहायसम्॥
en: In the same way I have come here I shall return by the welkin, O Vaidehī placing three on my back.

sn: मैथिली तु हरिश्रेष्ठाच्छ्रुत्वा वचनमद्भुतम्। हर्षविस्मितसर्वाङ्गी हनूमन्तमथामब्रवीत्॥
en: Hearing those surprising words from that best of monkeys, Maithilī, having her entire frame worked up with joy, again bespake Hanumān.

sn: हनूमन् दूरमध्वानं कथं मां नेतुमिच्छसि। तदेव खलु ते मन्ये कपित्वं हरियूथप॥
en: Hanumān, how darest you take me to such a long distance? O lord of monkey hosts, this attests to your monkey-hood.

sn: कथं चाल्पशरीरस्त्वं मामितो नेतुमिच्छसि। सकाशं मानवेन्द्रस्य भर्तुर्मे प्लवगर्षभ॥
en: O foremost of monkeys, little-bodied as you are, how do you desire, to take me hence to my husband the lord of men?

sn: सीतायास्तु वचः श्रुत्वा हनूमान् मारुतात्मजः। चिन्तयामास लक्ष्मीवान् नवं परिभवं कृतम्॥
en: Hearing the words of Sītā, the graceful son of the Wind-god Hanumān reflected aside-This is my first insult.

sn: न मे जानाति सत्त्वं वा प्रभाव वासितेक्षणा। तस्मात् पश्यतु वैदेही यद् रूपं मम कामतः॥
en: The lotus-eyed dame is not cognizant of my prowess or strength. Vaidehi should therefore learn that I can assume shapes at will.

sn: इति संचिन्त्य हनुमांस्तदा प्लवगसत्तमः। दर्शयामास सीतायाः स्वरूपमरिमर्दनः॥
en: Thinking thus, Hanumān, the foremost of the monkeys and the slayer of foes, showed himself to Sītā, in his true shape.

sn: स तस्मात् पादपाद् धीमानाप्लुत्य प्लवगर्षभः। ततो वर्धितुमारेभे सीताप्रत्ययकारणात्॥
en: And leaping down from the tree, that best of monkeys began to increase himself to create Sītā's confidence.

sn: मेरुमन्दरसंकाशो बभौ दीप्तानलप्रभः। अग्रतो व्यवतस्थे च सीताया वानरर्षभः॥ हरिः पर्वतसंकाशस्ताम्रवक्त्रो महाबलः। वज्रदंष्ट्रनखो भीमो वैदेहीमिदमब्रवीत्॥
en: His person appeared like the hill Mandara and the flaming fire. And that best of monkeys having a copper-coloured countenance, thunderlike nails and teeth and mountain-like huge body, appeared before Sītā and said.

sn: सपर्वतवनोद्देशां साट्टप्राकारतोरणाम्। लङ्कामिमां सनाथां वा नयितुं शक्तिरस्ति मे॥
en: I am capable of carrying this Lankā with her lord, the mountains, forests gardens, buildings, walls and gate-ways.

sn: तदवस्थाप्यतां बुद्धिरलं देवि विकाङ्गया। विशोकं कुरु वैदेहि राघवं सहलक्ष्मणम्॥
en: Do you therefore confide in me, O worshipful dame, and be not suspicious. And O Vaidehi, do you remove Rāma's grief as well as Laksmana's.

sn: तं दृष्ट्वाचलसंकाशमुवाच जनकात्मजा। पद्मपत्रविशालाक्षी मारुतस्यौरसं सुतम्॥
en: Beholding the Wind-god's own begotten son, Hanumān, resembling a huge mountain, Sītā, the daughter of Janaka, having eyes resembling lotus-petals, said.

sn: तव सत्त्वं बलं चैव विजानामि महाकपे। वायोरिव गतिश्चापि तेजश्चाग्नेरिवाद्भुतम्।॥
en: O great monkey, I know your strength and bravery, they air-like motion and your wonderful fire-like energy.

sn: प्राकृतोऽन्यः कथं चेमां भूमिमागन्तुमर्हति। उदधेरप्रमेयस्य पारं वानरयूथप॥
en: What ordinary man can come here crossing the incomparable ocean.

sn: जानामि गमने शक्ति नयने चापि ते मम। अवश्यं सम्प्रधाशु कार्यसिद्धरिवात्मनः।॥
en: O lord of monkey hosts, I understand that you are capable of returning and you shall be able to carry me. But I should consider now how the work might be accomplished.

sn: अयुक्तं तु कपिश्रेष्ठ मया गन्तुं त्वया सह। वायुवेगसवेगस्य वेगो मां मोहयेत् तव॥
en: O foremost of monkeys, I should not go with you. Perhaps I might lose my sense with your air-like velocity.

sn: अहमाकाशमासक्ता उपर्युपरि सागरम्। प्रपतेयं हि ते पृष्ठाद् भूयो वेगेन गच्छतः॥
en: When moving terribly you shall proceed high up in the welkin, perhaps I shall then fall down.

sn: पतिता सागरे चाहं तिमिनक्रझषाकुले। भवेयमाशु विवशा यादसामन्नमुत्तमम्॥
en: No sooner I shall fall down into the ocean infested with fish and other animals than I shall be an excellent food to them.

sn: न च शक्ष्ये त्वया सार्धं गन्तुं शत्रुविनाशन। कलत्रवति संदेहस्त्वयि स्यादप्यसंशयम्॥
en: O slayer of foes, I shall not be able to accompany you. For seeing you carry a woman, they shall surely suspect you.

sn: ह्रियमाणां तु मां दृष्ट्वा राक्षसा भीमविक्रमाः। अनुगच्छेयुरादिष्टा रावणेन दुरात्मना ॥
en: And finding me stolen, those terribly powerful Rākşasas commanded by the vicious-souled Rāvana, shall follow you.

sn: तैस्त्वं परिवृतः शूरैः शूलमुद्गरपाणिभिः। भवेस्त्वं संशयं प्राप्तो मया वीर कलत्रवान्॥
en: O hero, carrying me and encircled by those heroic Rākṣasas with maces and darts in their hands, you shall be beset with dangers.

sn: सायुधा बहवो व्योम्नि राक्षसास्त्वं निरायुधः। कथं शक्ष्यसि संयातुं मां चैव परिरक्षितुम्॥
en: And on the sky the Rākşasas shall be armed with weapons and you shall be without any. How shall you be able to fight and protect me at the same time.

sn: युध्यमानस्य रक्षोभिस्ततस्तैः क्रूरकर्मभिः। प्रपतेयं हि ते पृष्ठाद् भयार्ता कपिसत्तम॥
en: When you shall be engaged in conflict with those Rākşasas of terrible deeds, I, O foremost of monkeys, stricken with fear, shall fall down from your back.

sn: अथ रक्षांसि भीमानि महान्ति बलवन्ति च। कथंचित् साम्पराये त्वां जयेयुः कपिसत्तम॥ अथवा युध्यमानस्य पतेयं विमुखस्य ते। पतितां च गृहीत्वा मां नयेयुः पापराक्षसाः॥
en: O foremost of monkeys those terrible and powerful Rākşasas shall be able to defeat you a little. And when you shall be defeated in battle I shall fall down and those vicious Rākṣasas shall carry me away from your hands or destroy me.

sn: मां वा हरेयुस्त्वद्धस्ताद् विशसेयुरथापि वा। अनवस्थौ हि दृश्येते युद्धे जयपराजयौ॥ अहं वापि विपद्येयं रक्षोभिरभितर्जिता। त्वत्प्रयत्नो हरिश्रेष्ठ भवेनिष्फल एव तु॥
en: Victory or defeat is uncertain in a battle. I shall thus be distressed by those Rākşasas setting up terrible roars and they endeavours shall be fruitless, O best of monkeys.

sn: कामं त्वमपि पर्याप्तो निहन्तुं सर्वराक्षसान्। राघवस्य यशो हीयेत् त्वया शस्तैस्तु राक्षसैः॥
en: You are capable of destroying the Rākṣasas very easily (I admit)—but Rama's fame shall then be souled if do you bring about their destruction.

sn: अथवाऽऽदाय रक्षांसि न्यसेयुः संवृते हि माम्। यत्र ते नाभिजानीयुर्हरयो नापि राघवः॥
en: Or the Rākşasas taking me away shall keep me in such a secret place, that neither the monkeys nor Rāghava shall be able to ascertain my where abouts.

sn: आरम्भस्तु मदर्थोऽयं ततस्तव निरर्थकः। त्वया हि सह रामस्य महानागमने गुणः॥
en: All your preparations for me, shall thus be useless. And mighty shall be the result of Rāma's coming with you.

sn: मयि जीवितमायत्तं राघवस्यामितौजसः। भ्रातॄणां च महाबाहो तव राजकुलस्य च॥
en: O large armed one, the life of Rāghava of unmitigated prowess, those of his brothers and of your royal race are all subject to me.

sn: तौ निराशौ मदर्थं च शोकसंतापकर्शितौ। सह सर्वक्षहरिभिस्त्यक्ष्यतः प्राणसंग्रहम्॥
en: When they shall give up their hopes of releasing me, they, worn out with grief and anxiety shall renounce their lives along with the monkeys and bears.

sn: भर्तुर्भक्तिं पुरस्कृत्य रामादन्यस्य वानर। नाहं स्पष्टुं स्वतो गात्रमिच्छेयं वानरोत्तम ॥
en: O monkey, being guided by my love for my husband, I do not like willingly to touch any body's person but Rāma's.

sn: यदहं गात्रसंस्पर्शं रावणस्य गता बलात्। अनीशा किं करिष्यामि विनाथा विवशा सती॥
en: When Rāvaņa, by force touched my person, I had no other help, for I was then without me lord and therefore was subject to another person.

sn: यदि रामो दशग्रीवमिह हत्वा सराक्षसम्। मामितो गृह्य गच्छेत तत्तस्य सदृशं भवेत्॥
en: If Rāma can take me away from here, destroying the Ten-necked one with all the Rākşasas-he shall then perform the worthy action.

sn: श्रुताश्च दृष्ट्वा हि मया पराक्रमा महात्मनस्तस्य रणावमर्दिनः। न देवगन्धर्वभुजङ्गराक्षसा भवन्ति रामेण समा हि संयुगे॥
en: I have heard of and myself seen the prowess of the highly-souled (Rāma) unconquerable in a battle. There is none among the celestials, Gandharvas, Nāgas and the Rākşasas who can match him in a conflict.

sn: समीक्ष्य तं संयति चित्रकार्मुकं महाबलं वासवतुल्यविक्रमम्। सलक्ष्मणं को विषहेत राघवं हुताशनं दीप्तमिवानिलेरितम्॥
en: Beholding that highly powerful Rāghava, in a conflict, like to Vāsava in prowess, holding a wonderful bow and followed by Lakşmaņa, who can withstand his prowess resembling the flaming fire?

sn: सलक्ष्मणं राघवमाजिमर्दनं दिशागजं मत्तमिव व्यवस्थितम्। सहेत को वानरमुख्य संयुगे युगान्तसूर्यप्रतिमं शरार्चिषम्॥
en: O foremost of monkeys, who can withstand Rāghava in a conflict, followed by Lakşmaņa moving like infuriated an elephant and showering shafts like to the rays of the sun at the time of Dissolution?

sn: स मे कपिश्रेष्ठ सलक्ष्मणं प्रियं सयूथपं क्षिप्रमिहोपपादय। चिराय रामं प्रति शोककर्शितां कुरुष्व मां वानरवीर हर्षिताम्॥
en: O best of monkeys do you speedily bring here my dear one along with Lakşmaņa and the lord of monkey hosts. O heroic monkey, do you soon satisfy me, who am stricken with grief in consequence of my long separation from Rāma.

sn: ततः स कपिशार्दूलस्तेन वाक्येन तोषितः। सीतामुवाच तच्छ्रुत्वा वाक्यं वाक्यविशारदः॥
en: Hearing those words, that foremost of monkeys, skilled in speech, was greatly delighted and again addressed Sītā in the following words,

sn: युक्तरूपं त्वया देवि भाषितं शुभदर्शने। सदृशं स्त्रीस्वभावस्य साध्वीनां विनयस्य च॥
en: O worshipful lady, O you of an auspicious presence, what you had said, speaks well for a feminine nature and the modesty of a chaste damsel.

sn: स्त्रीत्वान्न त्वं समर्थासि सागरं व्यतिवर्तितुम्। मामधिष्ठाय विस्तीर्णं शतयोजनमायतम्॥
en: And because you are a female, you are not capable of crossing on my back, the main extending over a thousand leagues.

sn: द्वितीयं कारणं यच्च ब्रवीषि विनयान्विते। रामादन्यस्य नार्हामि संसर्गमिति जानकी॥ एतत् ते देवि सदृशं पत्न्यास्तस्य महात्मनः। का ह्यन्या त्वामृते देवि ब्रूयाद् वचनमीदृशम्॥
en: The second argument—I shall not touch any other person's body than Rāma's, which you have produced, O Janaki! O you gifted with modesty! truely become you, who are the spouse of that high-souled one. Who else than you, O worshipful one, can give expression to such words?

sn: श्रोष्यते चैव काकुत्स्थः सर्वं निरवशेषतः। चेष्टितं यत् त्वया देवि भाषितं च ममाग्रतः॥
en: Truly shall Kākutstha hear from the beginning to the end, O worshipful dame, of your actions before me, and all you had said.

sn: कारणैर्बहुभिर्देवि रामप्रियचिकीर्षया। स्नेहप्रस्कन्नमनसा मयैतत् समुदीरितम्॥
en: For many reason, I gave vent to such words, O lady, I am anxious to compass Rāma's end, and my heart is melted with affection.

sn: लङ्काया दुष्प्रवेशत्वाद् दुस्तरत्वान्महोदधेः। सामर्थ्यादात्मनश्चैव मयैतत् समुदीरितम्॥
en: It is very difficult to enter this city of Lankā, it is equally hard to cross over the main—but I am capable of doing all these, and hence I gave utterance to all those words.

sn: इच्छामि त्वां समानेतुमद्यैव रघुनन्दिना । गुरुस्नेहेन भक्त्या च नान्यथा तदुदाहृतम्॥
en: I wish to take you even to-day to the descendant of Raghu. It is for my devotion to him and regard for you that I said so and for nothing else.

sn: यदि नोत्सहसे यातुं मया सार्धमनिन्दिते। अभिज्ञानं प्रयच्छ त्वं जानीयाद् राघवो हि यत्॥
en: If you do not wish to go with me, O you of a blameless person, do you give me such a token as might create Rāghava's confidence.

sn: एवमुक्ता हनुमता सीता सुरसुतोपमा। उवाच वचनं मन्दं बाष्पप्रग्रथिताक्षरम्॥
en: Being thus accosted by Hanumān, Sītā resembling the daughter of a celestial, spoke, gently, words with their letters strung on the vapour of grief,

sn: इदं श्रेष्ठमभिज्ञानं ब्रूयास्त्वं तु मम प्रियम्। शैलस्य चित्रकूटस्य पादे पूर्वोत्तरे पदे॥ तापसाश्रमवासिन्याः प्राज्यमूलफलोदके। तस्मिन् सिद्धाश्रिते देशे मन्दाकिन्यविदूरतः॥ तस्योपवनखण्डेषु नानापुष्पसुगन्धिषु । विहत्य सलिले क्लिन्नो ममाङ्के समुपाविशः॥
en: Do you mentioned to my dear lord (in my words) what had happened to me while living in the hermitage at the foot of the mount Pratyanga, situate on the north-east of Citrakūta, abounding in roots, fruits and water. At no distance from that place frequented by the ascetics flowed the sacred stream Mandakini. While ranging in that woodland fragrant with the odour of many flowers, you, having your person wet in consequence of your sport in the water, did sit on my lap.

sn: ततो मांससमायुक्तो वायसः पर्यतुण्डयत्। तमहं लोष्टमुद्यम्य वारयामि स्म वायसम्॥ दारयन् स च मां काकस्तत्रैव परिलीयते। न चाप्युपारमन्मांसाद् भक्षार्थी बलिभोजनः॥
en: A crow, at that time, longing to feed on my flesh, tore my breast with its beak. And I threatened it with a pebble. But it continued tearing my breast as if it sat there to feed on my flesh and therefore did not fly off.
