And all the waiters of the garden and the servants of Dadhimukha, were repressed by those terrible monkeys with censure and thrown up in the shy by their Knee-joints. And terrified, they fled to different directions.

sn: अब्रुवन् परमोद्विग्ना गत्वा दधिमुखं वचः। हनूमता दत्तवरैर्हतं मधुवनं बलात्। वयं च जानुभिदृष्टा देवमार्गं च दर्शिताः॥
en: And being worked up with anxiety, they approached Dadhimukha and said "Commanded by Hanumān the monkeys have forcibly devastated the Madhuvana and we were thrown high up by them in the sky.”

sn: तदा दधिमुखः क्रुद्धो वनपस्तत्र वानरः। हतं मधुवनं श्रुत्वा सान्त्वयामास तान् हरीन् ॥
en: Hearing of the destruction of the orchard, Dadhimukha, being greatly enraged, consoled all the monkeys.

sn: एतागच्छत गच्छामो वानरानतिदर्पितान्। बलेनावारयिष्यामि प्रभुञ्जानान् मधूत्तमम्॥
en: Proceed you before, I shall soon follow you and repress by force all those monkeys, greatly excited with pride and the drinking of the excellent honey.

sn: श्रुत्वा दधिमुखस्येदं वचनं वानरर्षभाः। पुनर्वीरा मधुवनं तेनैव सहिता ययुः॥
en: Hearing these works from Dadhimukha those leading and heroic monkeys proceeded with him towards Madhuvana.

sn: मध्ये चैषां दधिमुखः सुप्रगृह्य महातरुम्। समभ्यधावन् वेगेन सर्वे ते च प्लवंगमाः॥ ते शिलाः पादपांश्चैव पाषाणानपि वानराः। गृहीत्वाभ्यागमन् कुद्धा यत्र ते कपिकुञ्जरा ॥
en: And Dadhimukha proceeded with great velocity in their midst taking up a huge tree in his hand. And all his attendants, taking trees, mountain crags, proceeded, wroth, where those leading monkeys were.

sn: बलान्निवारयन्तश्च आसेदुर्हरयो हरीन्। संदष्टौष्ठपुटाः कुद्धा भर्त्सयन्तो मुहुर्मुहुः॥
en: And biting their lips in wrath and remonstrating with them again and again, those monkeys began to suppress them by force.

sn: अथ दृष्ट्वा दधिमुखं क्रुद्धं वानरपुङ्गवाः। अभ्यधावन्त वेगेन हनुमत्प्रमुखांस्तदा॥
en: And beholding Dadhimukha greatly enraged, all the monkeys, headed by Hanumān, approached him with great vehemence.

sn: सवृक्षं तं महाबाहुमापतन्तं महाबलम्। वेगवन्तं विजग्राह बाहुभ्यां कुपितोऽङ्गदः॥
en: And as the mighty Dadhimukha of huge arms, was proceeding towards them vehemently with a huge tree, Angada, wroth, caught him by the hand.

sn: मदान्धो न कृपां चक्रे आर्यकोऽयं ममेति सः। अथैनं निष्पिपेषाशु वेगेन वसुधातले॥-
en: He was beside himself with intoxication and therefore did not show him the least mercy, albeit he (Dadhimukha) was worshipful to him. And accordingly with great vehemence he ground him to the dust.

sn: स भग्नबाहूरुमुखो विह्वलः शोणितोक्षितः। प्रमुमोह महावीरो मुहूर्तं कपिकुञ्जरः॥
en: His arms and thighs were broken and his countenance was disfigured and that great hero, the foremost of the monkeys, bathed in a pool of blood, remained senseless for sometime.

sn: स कथंचिद् विमुक्तस्तैर्वानरैर्वानरर्षभः। उवाचैकान्तमागत्य स्वान् भृत्यान् समुपागतान्॥
en: And thereupon releasing himself from them by some device that leading monkey, proceeded to a nook, and addressed his attendants, saying.

sn: एतागच्छत गच्छामो भर्ता नो यत्र वानरः। सुग्रीवो विपुलग्रीवः सह रामेण तिष्ठति॥
en: Let us all proceed there where our lord, the spacious-necked Sugrīva live with Rāma.

sn: सर्वं चैवाङ्गदे दोषं श्रावयिष्याम पार्थिवे। अमर्षी वचनं श्रुत्वा घातयिष्यति वानरान्॥
en: I shall relate to him all the unfair dealings of Angada and forsooth shall that wrathful king punish all these monkeys

sn: इष्टं मधुवनं ह्येतत् सुग्रीवस्य महात्मनः। पितृपैतामहं दिव्यं देवैरापि दुरासदम्॥
en: The picturesque Madhuvana is the most favourite orchard of the high-souled Sugrīva. It was enjoyed by his forefathers and is not even approached by the celestials.

sn: स वानरानिमान् सर्वान् मधुलुब्धान् गतायुषः। घातयिष्यति दण्डेन सुग्रीवः ससुहृज्जनान्॥
en: And meting out punishment to these monkeys, eager to drink honey and almost half dead, Sugrīva shall slay them as will as their friends and relatives.

sn: बद्ध्वा ह्येते दुरात्मानो नृपाज्ञापरिपन्थिनः। अमर्षप्रभवो रोषः सफलो मे भविष्यति॥
en: Those vicious-souled ones are worthy of being slain since they have transgressed the royal mandate. And then shall my wrath, arising out of impatience, bear fruits.

sn: एवमुक्त्वा दधिमुखो वनपालान् महाबलः। जगाम सहसोत्पत्य वनपालैः समन्वितः॥
en: Having thus spoken to the guards of the forest the highly powerful Dadhimukha leaped high up in the welkin and went away with them.

sn: निमेषान्तरमात्रेण स हि प्राप्तो वनालयः। सहस्रांशुसुतो धीमान् सुग्रीवो यत्र वानरः॥
en: And in no time he reached where the highly intelligent "Niether monkey/Sugriva, the offspring of the sun, was."

sn: रामं च लक्ष्मणं चैव दृष्ट्वा सुग्रीवमेव च। समप्रतिष्ठां जगतीमाकाशान्निपपात ह॥
en: And beholding Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa, and Sugrīva and the level ground he descended from the sky.

sn: स निपत्य महावीरः सर्वैस्तैः परिवारितः। हरिर्दधिमुखः पालैः पालानां परमेश्वरः॥ स दीनवदनो भूत्वा कृत्वा शिरसि चाञ्जलिम्। सुग्रीवस्याशु तौ मूर्धा चरणौ प्रत्यपीडयत्॥
en: And descending from the sky that great and heroic Dabhimukha ,lord over all the monkeys engaged in protecting the forest, placing his folded palms on his forehead and with a poorly countenance, laid low his crown at Sugrīva's feet.

sn: ततो मूर्धा निपतितं वानरं वानरर्षभः। दृष्ट्वैवोद्विग्नहृदयो वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह॥
en: And beholding that monkey place his crown at his feet the monkey-chief, with an anxious mind, accosted him, saying.

sn: उत्तिष्ठोत्तिष्ठ कस्मात् त्वं पादयोः पतितो मम। अभयं ते प्रदास्यामि सत्यमेवाभिधीयताम्॥ किं सम्भ्रमाद्धितं कृत्स्नं ब्रूहि यद् वक्तुमर्हसि। कच्चिन्मधुवने स्वस्ति श्रोतुमिच्छामि वानर ॥
en: Rise up, rise up, why had you lain yourself at my feet? I declare you had you come here? It behove you to suggest the becoming procedure. Is it all well with my orchard Madhuvana? I long to know everything, O monkey.

sn: स समाश्वासितस्तेन सुग्रीवेण महात्मना। उत्थाय स महाप्राज्ञो वाक्यं दधिमुखोऽब्रवीत्॥
en: Being thus addressed hopefully by the highsouled Sugrīva, Dadhimukha, gifted with an intelligence of a very high order, rose up and spoke.

sn: नवद्धृजरता राजन् न त्वया न च वालिना। वनं निसृष्टपूर्वं ते नाशितं तत्तु वानरैः॥
en: Neither yourself, nor Vāli, the lord of the monkeys, O king, allowed that orchard to be freely used by the monkeys but that has been now laid waste by them.

sn: न्यवारयमहं सर्वान् सहैभिर्वनचारिभिः। अचिन्तयित्वा मां हृष्टा भक्षयन्ति पिबन्ति च॥
en: I prevented them along with these attendants, but disregarding me, they drank and feasted there at their pleasure.

sn: एभिः प्रधर्षणायां च वारितं वनपालकैः। मामप्यचिन्तयन् देव भक्षयन्ति वनौकसः॥
en: They were prevented, O lord, in their act of devastation, by these guards, but those monkeys, without caring for me the least, feasted there.

sn: शिष्टमत्रापविध्यन्ति भक्षयन्ति तथापरे। निवार्यमाणास्ते सर्वे भ्रुकुटिं दर्शयन्ति हि।।।।।
en: Some of them went beyond the pale of food conduct, others ate at their pleasure, and all frowned (at us).

sn: इमे हि संरब्धतरास्तदा तैः सम्प्रधर्षिताः। निवार्यन्ते वनात् तस्मात् क्रुद्धैर्वानरपुङ्गवैः॥
en: When these attendants, being insulted by them, were greatly wroth, they were driven out of the garden, by those powerful and enraged monkeys.

sn: ततस्तैबहुभिवीरैर्वानरैर्वानरर्षभाः। संरक्तनयनैः क्रोधाद्धरयः संप्रधर्षिताः॥
en: They were greatly assailed by those many thousand heroic monkeys, worked up with ire and having reddened eyes.

sn: पाणिभिनिहताः केचित् केचिज्जानुभिराहताः। प्रकृष्टाश्च तदा कामं देवमार्गं च दर्शिताः॥
en: Some had their arins broken, some had their knee-joints crushed and some of them were thrown up in the sky.

sn: एवमेते हताः शूरास्त्वयि तिष्ठति भर्तरि। कृत्स्नं मधुवनं चैव प्रकामं तैश्च भक्ष्यते॥
en: Yourself their lord living, these heroes are beaten, and the entire Madhuvana is being freely enjoyed by them.

sn: एवं विज्ञाप्यमानं तं सुग्रीवं वानरर्षभम्। अपृच्छत्तं महाप्राज्ञो लक्ष्मणः परवीरहा॥
en: The highly intelligent Lakşmaņa, the slayer of foes, addressed Sugriva, the foremost O the monkeys, while he was thus being informed, saying.

sn: किमयं वानरो राजन् वनपः प्रत्युपस्थितः। किं चार्थमभिनिर्दिश्य दुःखितो वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
en: O king, why has this monkey, the guard over the forest, come to you, and what sorrow has led him to give vent to these expressions?

sn: एवमुक्तस्तु सुग्रीवो लक्ष्मणेन महात्मना। लक्ष्मणं प्रत्युवाचेदं वाक्यं वाक्यविशारदः॥
en: Being thus addressed by the high-souled Laksmana, Sugriva, skilled in the art of speech, replied.

sn: आर्य लक्ष्मण संप्राह वीरो दधिमुखः कपिः। अङ्गदप्रमुखैवीरैक्षितं मधु वानरैः॥
en: O worshipful Lakşmaņa, the heroic monkey Dadhimukha speaks that the war-like monkeys headed by Angada have drunk honey.

sn: नैषामकृतकार्याणामीदृशः स्याद् व्यतिक्रमः। वनं यदभिपन्नास्ते साधितं कर्म तद्धवम्॥
en: They would not have engaged in such an unfair proceeding had they been unsuccessful in their mission. They have surely achieved success while they have thus been bent upon devastating the orchard.

sn: वारयन्तो भृशं प्राप्ताः पाला जानुभिराहताः। तथा न गणितश्चायं कपिर्दधिमुखो बली॥ पतिर्मम वनस्यायमस्माभिः स्थापितः स्वयम्। दृष्टा देवी न संदेहो न चान्येन हनूमता ॥
en: For this the warders were struck on their kneejoints for obstructing their revelry and for this they went so far as to disregard the powerful monkey Dadhimukha. I myself appointed this monkey the lord of my orchard. Forsooth has Hanumān espied the worshipful Sītā and none else.

sn: नह्यन्यः साधने हेतुः कर्मणोऽस्य हनूमतः। कार्यसिद्धिहर्नुमति मतिश्च हरिपुङ्गवे॥ व्यवसायश्च वीर्यं च श्रुतं चापि प्रतिष्ठितम्।
en: There is none else but Hanumān who is the instrumental of this work, for that best of monkeys has in him a high intellect, know the art of success, is gifted with courage, strength and prowess and is conversant with Śāstras.

sn: जाम्बवान् यत्र नेता स्यादङ्गदश्च महाबलः हनूमांश्चाप्यधिष्ठाता न तत्र गतिरन्यथा।
en: That work is sure to succeed whose leading spirits are the mighty Jāmbavāna and Angada, and worker is Hanumăn.

sn: अङ्गदप्रमुखैवीरैर्हतं मधुवनं किल॥ विचित्य दक्षिणामाशामागतैर्हरिपुङ्गवैः। आगतैश्च प्रहृष्टं तद्यथा मधुवनं हि तैः॥ धर्षितं च वनं कृत्स्नमुपयुक्तं तु वानरैः। पातिता वनपालास्ते तदा जानुभिराहताः॥ एतदर्थमयं प्राप्तो वक्तुं मधुरवागिह। नाम्ना दधिमुखो नाम हरिः प्रख्यातविक्रमः॥
en: Forsooth that orchard has been laid waste by these heroes headed by Angada. And ransacking the southern quarter, those leading monkeys have come back and delightedly entered the Madhuvana. And the whole orchard has been explored and enjoyed by those monkeys and the attendants beaten and wounded on their kneejoints. To communicate to me this intelligence, this monkey of known prowess, and sweet accents, named Dhadimukha, has come here.

sn: दृष्टा सीता महाबाहो सौमित्रे पश्य तत्त्वतः। अभिगम्य यथा सर्वे पिबन्ति मधु वानराः॥
en: O you of mighty arms, O son of Sumitra, forsooth they have beheld Sītā, since the monkeys, just on their return, have engaged in drinking honey.

sn: न चाप्यदृष्ट्वा वैदेही विश्रुताः पुरुषर्षभ। वनं दत्तवरं दिव्यं धर्षयेयुर्वनौकसः॥
en: O best of men, they are all well-known monkeys and without espying Vaidehī they would not have engaged in the destruction of that orchard conferred on us as a gift by the celestials.

sn: ततः प्रहृष्टो धर्मात्मा लक्ष्मणः सहराघवः। श्रुत्वा कर्णसुखां वाणीं सुग्रीववदनाच्च्युताम्॥ प्राहृष्यत भृशं रामो लक्ष्मणश्च महायशाः।
en: Hearing these words from Sugrīva, pleasant to ears, the virtuous-souled Lakşmaņa along with Rāghava, was greatly pleased.

sn: श्रुत्वा दधिमुखस्यैवं सुग्रीवस्तु प्रहष्य च॥ वनपालं पुनर्वाक्यं सुग्रीवः प्रत्यभाषत।
en: And hearing this from Dadhimukha, Sugrīva, greatly gratified; addressed that lord of the for st, gain, Saying.

sn: प्रीतोऽस्मि सोऽहं यद्भुक्तं वनं तैः कृतकर्मभिः॥ धर्षितं मर्षणीयं च चेष्टितं कृतकर्मणाम्। गच्छ शीघ्रं मधुवनं संरक्षस्व त्वमेव हि। शीघ्रं प्रेषय सर्वांस्तान् हनूमत्प्रमुखान् कपीन्॥
en: Greatly pleased I am, since, they, being successful, have explored this forest. And the insulting procedure of the successful is also pardonable. Do you soon go there and protect that orchards, and send here all those monkeys headed by Hanumān.

sn: शाखामृगांस्तान् मृगराजदोन्। प्रष्टुं कृतार्थान्सह राघवाभ्यां श्रोतुं च सीताधिगमे प्रयत्नम्॥
en: Along with these two descendants of Raghu, I long to know soon from these monkeys headed by Hanumān, and proud like lions, what they have settled for the regaining of Sītā.

sn: प्रीतिस्फीताक्षौ संप्रहृष्टौ कुमारौ दृष्ट्वा सिद्धार्थों वानराणां च राजा। अङ्गैः प्रहृष्टैः कार्यसिद्धिं विदित्वा बाह्वोरासन्नामतिमात्रं ननन्द ॥
en: And beholding-these two princes greatly delighted and their eyes expanded with joy, the king of the monkeys, thought that the accomplishment of the great work was near at hand, and was accordingly greatly delighted."

sn: सुग्रीवेणैवमुक्तस्तु हृष्टो दधिमुखः कपिः। राघवं लक्ष्मणं चैव सुग्रीवं चाभ्यवादयत्॥
en: Being thus addressed by Sugrīva, the monkey Dadhimuklia, delighted, bowed to him, Rāghava and Laksmana.

sn: स प्रणम्य च सुग्रीवं राघवौ च महाबलौ। वानरैः सहितः शूरैर्दिवमेवोत्पपात ह॥
en: And adoring Sugrīva and the highly powerful descendants of Raghu, he along with other heroic monkeys, leaped up in the sky.

sn: स यथैवागतः पूर्वं तथैव त्वरितं गतः। निपत्य गगनाद् भूमौ तद् वनं प्रविवेश ह॥
en: He went away with the same speed with which he came and leaping down on the earth from the sky, entered the orchard.

sn: स प्रविष्टो मधुवनं ददर्श हरियूथपान्। विमदानुद्धतान् सर्वान् मेहमानान् मधूदकम्॥
en: And entering that forest he beheld all the leaders of the monkeys spending the hours delightedly, having passed urine, the outcome of honey.

sn: स तानुपागमद् वीरो बद्ध्वा करपुटाञ्जलिम्। उवाच वचनं श्लक्ष्णमिदं हृष्टवदङ्गदम्॥
en: And approaching them, the hero, with folded hands and delighted, addressed Angada, with the following words.

sn: सौम्य रोषो न कर्तव्यो यदेभिः परिवारणम्। अज्ञानाद् रक्षिभिः क्रोधाद् भवन्तः प्रतिषेधिताः॥
en: O gentle one, do you not take offence, for these monkeys, protecting the garden enraged, unwittingly prevented you.

sn: श्रान्तो दूरादनुप्राप्तो भक्षयस्व स्वकं मधु। युवराजस्त्वमीशश्च वनस्यास्य महाबल ॥
en: O you of great strength, you are worn out with your long journey, do you drink your own honey, you are our prince and the master of this garden.

sn: मौात्पूर्वं कृतो रोषस्तद् भवान् क्षन्तुमर्हति । यथैव हि पिता तेऽभूत् पूर्वं हरिगणेश्वरः॥ तथा त्वमपि सुग्रीवो नान्यस्तु हरिसत्तम।
en: It behove you to forgive us for our wrath arising out of ignorance. Like to your sire before, yourself and Sugrīva are the lords of these monkey hosts, O you foremost of them and none else.

sn: आख्यातं हि मया गत्वा पितृव्यस्य तवानघ॥ इहोपयानं सर्वेषामेतेषां वनचारिणाम्। भवदागमनं श्रुत्वा सहैभिर्वनचारिभिः॥ प्रहृष्टो न तु रुष्टोऽसौ वनं श्रुत्वा प्रधर्षितम्।
en: O innocent prince, I have related all about this to your uncle. When I described to him, the arrival of all these forest rangers, as well as of yours accompanied by them, and the destruction of this garden by you all, he was not the least offended, rather delighted.

sn: प्रहृष्टो मां पितृव्यस्ते सुग्रीवो वानरेश्वरः॥ शीघ्रं प्रेषय सर्वांस्तानिति होवाच पार्थिवः।
en: And worked up with joy your uncle Sugrīva, the lord of earth and monkeys, said “Send them all here speedily."

sn: श्रुत्वा दधिमुखस्यैतद् वचनं श्लक्ष्णमङ्गदः॥ अब्रवीत् तान् हरिश्रेष्ठो वाक्यं वाक्यविशारदः।
en: Hearing those words from Dadhimukha, Angada, the foremost of the monkeys and skilled in speech, addressed them all, saying.

sn: शङ्के श्रुतोऽयं वृत्तान्तो रामेण हरियूथपाः॥ अयं च हर्षादाख्याति तेन जानामि हेतुना। तत् क्षमं नेह नः स्थातुं कृते कार्ये परंतपाः॥
en: O you leaders of the monkey hosts, I fear, Rāma has heard all about this. Dadhimukha relates everything joyfully and hence I infer this. And our work finished, O slayer of foes, it dose not behove us to remain here (any longer).

sn: पीत्वा मधु यथाकामं विक्रान्ता वनचारिणः। किं शेषं गमनं तत्र सुग्रीवो यत्र वानरः॥
en: You have all drunk honey at your pleasure and there is nothing left and you should now go where the monkey king Sugrīva is.

sn: सर्वे यथा मां वक्ष्यन्ति समेत्य हरिपुङ्गवाः। तथास्मि कर्ता कर्तव्ये भवद्भिः परवानहम्॥
en: O leading monkeys, I shall follow what you will in a band desire me to do. In action I am subordinate to you all.

sn: नाज्ञापयितुमीशोऽहं युवराजोऽस्मि यद्यपि। अयुक्तं कृतकर्माणो यूयं धर्षयितुं बलात्॥
en: I am not justified to command although I am a prince. You are all of accomplished actions, it is not proper to repress you forcibly.

sn: ब्रुवतश्चाङ्गदस्यैवं श्रुत्वा वचनमुत्तमम्। प्रहृष्टमनसो वाक्यमिदमूचुर्वनौकसः॥
en: Hearing those sweet words of the prince Angada, the monkeys delightedly replied, saying.

sn: एवं वक्ष्यति को राजन् प्रभुः सन् वानरर्षभ। ऐश्वर्यमदमत्तो हि सर्वोऽहमिति मन्यते॥
en: O king, O foremost of monkeys, who else can speak thus being a master? Any one else, we think, is proud of his wealth.

sn: तव चेदं सुसदृशं वाक्यं नान्यस्य कस्यचित्। सन्नतिर्हि तवाख्याति भविष्यच्छुभयोग्यताम् ॥
en: Such like words become you only and none else. Your humility speaks of your future greatness.

sn: सर्वे वयमपि प्राप्तास्तत्र गन्तुं कृतक्षणाः। स यत्र हरिवीराणां सुग्रीवः पतिरव्ययः॥
en: We are all anxious to go there, where Sugriva, the king of the monkeys, is.

sn: त्वया ह्यनुक्तैर्हरिभि व शक्यं पदात् पदम्। क्वचिद् गन्तुं हरिश्रेष्ठ ब्रूमः सत्यमिदं तु ते॥
en: Verily we speak to you, O foremost of monkeys, that without your permission, none among us, is capable of advancing a single step.”

sn: एवं तु वदतां तेषामङ्गदः प्रत्यभाषत। साधु गच्छाम इत्युक्त्वा खमुत्पेतुर्महाबलाः॥ उत्पतन्तमनूत्पेतुः सर्वे ते हरियूथपाः। कृत्वाऽऽकाशं निराकाशं यन्त्रोत्क्षिप्ता इवोपलाः॥
en: They addressing him thus, Angada replied"All right, let us all go.” Saying this he leaped up in the sky and was followed by all those monkeys, clouding the welkin as if with stones thrown up by a tool.

sn: अङ्गदं पुरतः कृत्वा हनूमन्तं च वानरम्। तेऽम्बरं सहसोत्पत्य वेगवन्तः प्लवङ्गमाः॥ विनदन्तो महानादं घना वातेरिता यथा।
en: And placing before them Angada and Hanumān, the monkeys leaping vehemently up in the sky roared like to clouds driven by the wind.

sn: अङ्गदे समनुप्राप्ते सुग्रीवो वानरेश्वरः॥ उवाच शोकसंतप्तं रामं कमललोचनम्।
en: And Angada nearing, Sugrīva, the lord of the monkeys, spoke to the lotus-eyed Rāma, stricken with grief, saying.

sn: समाश्वसिहि भद्रं ते दृष्टा देवी न संशयः॥ नागन्तुमिह शक्यं तैरतीतसमयैरिह।
en: May good betide you. Do you console yourself. The worshipful dame has been found out; there is not the least doubt about it. Or else they would not have come as the time is already past.

sn: अङ्गदस्य प्रहर्षाच्च जानामि शुभदर्शन ॥ न मत्सकाशमागच्छेत् कृत्ये हि विनिपातिते। युवराजो महाबाहुः प्लवतामङ्गदो वरः॥
en: I (further more) infer this from Angada's joy, O you of auspicious presence. Without being successful in his mission, the large-armed prince, Angada, the foremost of the monkeys, would not have come to me.

sn: यद्यप्यकृतकृत्यानामीदृशः स्यादुपक्रमः। भवेत् तु दीनवदनो भ्रान्तविप्लुतमानसः॥
en: If the monkeys had engaged in such an unfair proceeding without being successful in their mission, Angada would have looked poorly and his mind would have been overwhelmed with grief and forgetfulness.

sn: पितृपैतामहं चैतत् पूर्वकैरभिरक्षितम्। न मे मधुवनं हन्याददृष्ट्वा जनकात्मजाम्॥
en: Without beholding the daughter of the king Janaka they would not have dared to destroy Madhuvana obtained and preserved by my forefathers.

sn: कौसल्या सुप्रजा राम समाश्वसिहि सुव्रत। दृष्टा देवी न संदेहो न चान्येन हनूमता॥
en: Do you console yourself, O Räma, by whom Kausalyā has become the mother of a good son. O you, rigidly observing any religious vow or obligation, forsooth has Hanumān behold the worshipful dame and none else.

sn: नह्यस्य कर्मणो हेतुः साधने तद्विधो भवेत्। हनूमतीह सिद्धिश्च मतिश्च मतिसत्तम ॥ व्यवसायश्च शौर्यं च श्रुतं चापि प्रतिष्ठितम्। जाम्बवान् यत्र नेता स्यादङ्गदश्च हरीश्वरः॥ हनूमांश्चाप्यधिष्ठाता न तत्र गतिरन्यथा।
en: No other wight is so qualified an instrument in encompassing this end. O you of excellent intellect, Hanumān know the art of success, is gifted with intellect, perseverance and courage and is versed in Šāstras. That work cannot fail, which is worked out by Jāmbavān and Angada and presided over by Hanumān.

sn: मा भूश्चिन्तासमायुक्तः सम्प्रत्यमितविक्रम॥ यदा हि दर्पितोदग्राः संगताः काननौकसः। नैषामकृतकार्याणामीदृशः स्यादुपक्रमः॥ वनभङ्गेन जानामि मधूनां भक्षणेन च।
en: Be not laden with anxiety, O you of unmitigated prowess. These monkey have come here excited with pride and drink. They would not have come with such a grandeur had they been but unsuccessful. From their breaking down the orchard and drinking honey I inferred SO.

sn: आयताञ्चितलाकॅलः ततः किलकिलाशब्दं शुश्रावासन्नमम्बरे॥ हनूमत्कर्मदृप्तानां नदतां काननौकसाम्। किष्किन्धामुपयातानां सिद्धिं कथयतामिव ॥
en: Thereupon he heard in the sky the joyous sounds of the monkeys proud on account of Hanuman's work, proceeding towards Kişkindhā and as if announcing their success.

sn: ततः श्रुत्वा निनादं तं कपीनां कपिसत्तमः। सोऽभवद्धृष्टमानसः॥
en: Thereupon hearing the noise of these monkeys Sugriva, their chief, being greatly delighted, uplifted his tail.

sn: आजग्मुस्तेऽति हरयो रामदर्शनकाक्षिणः। अङ्गदं पुरतः कृत्वा हनूमन्तं च वानरम्॥
en: And placing Angada and Hanumān before them those monkeys proceeded to behold Rāma.

sn: तेऽङ्गदप्रमुखा वीराः प्रहृष्टाश्च मुदान्विताः। निपेतुर्हरिराजस्य समीपे राघवस्य च॥
en: Those heroes headed by Angada, delighted and intoxicated, descended before Rāghava and the lord of the monkeys.

sn: हनूमांश्च महाबाहुः प्रणम्य शिरसा ततः। नियतामक्षतां देवीं राघवाय न्यवेदयत्॥
en: And the mighty-armed Hanumān, lowering his head, related to Rāghava, Sītā's spiritual and physical well-being.

sn: दृष्टा देवीति हनुमद्वदनादमृतोपमम्। आकर्ण्य वचनं रामो हर्षमाप सलक्ष्मणः॥
en: Hearing from Hanumān the sweet words that he had beheld Sītā, Rāma and Lakşmana were greatly delighted.

sn: निश्चितार्थं ततस्तस्मिन् सुग्रीवं पवनात्मजे। लक्ष्मणः प्रीतिमान् प्रीतं बहुमानादवेक्षत॥
en: And being confirmed thus by the Wind-god's son, Laksmana, greatly pleased, respectfully looked towards Sugriva.

sn: प्रीत्या च परयोपेतो राघवः परवीरहा। बहुमानेन महती हनूमन्तमवैक्षत॥
en: And Rāghava too, the slayer of foes, worked up with joy, cast respectful looks towards Hanuman.

sn: ततः प्रस्रवणं शैलं ते गत्वा चित्रकाननम्। प्रणम्य शिरसा राम लक्ष्मणं च महाबलम्॥ युवराजं पुरस्कृत्य सुग्रीवमभिवाद्य च। प्रवृत्तिमथ सीतायाः प्रवक्तुमुपचक्रमुः॥
en: Thereupon getting at the Mount Prasravana surrounded by a variegated forest, lowering their heads to the mighty Rāma and Lakşmaņa, placing before them their prince (Angada) and bowing to Sugrīva, the monkeys began to relate the story of Sītā.

sn: रावणान्तःपुरे रोधं राक्षसीभिश्च तर्जनम्। रामे समनुरागं च यथा च नियमः कृतः।।३। एतदाख्याय ते सर्वं हरयो रामसंनिधौ। वैदेहीमक्षतां श्रुत्वा रामस्तूत्तरमब्रवीत्॥
en: And they described to Ráma, the confinement of Sītā in Rāvana's seraglio, the remonstrances of the she-demons, her unflinching attachment in her lord and the time appointed (by the Rākṣasa for her destruction). And hearing of Vaidehi's well-being Rāma said.

sn: क्व सीता वर्तते देवी कथं च मयि वर्तते। एतन्मे सर्वमाख्यात वैदेहीं प्रति वानराः॥
en: O monkeys where live the worshipful Sītā? And how is her attachment to me? Do you relate everything to me.

sn: रामस्य गदितं श्रुत्वा हरयो रामसंनिधौ। चोदयन्ति हनूमन्तं सीतावृत्तान्तकोविदम्॥
en: Hearing those painful words of Răma, the monkeys desired Hanumān, conversant with the whereabouts of Sītā, to describe every thing to him.

sn: श्रुत्वा तु वचनं तेषां हनूमान् मारुतात्मजः। प्रणम्य शिरसा देव्यै सीतायै तां दिशं प्रति॥
en: Hearing their words, Hanuman, the Windgod's son, versed in the art of speech, lowering his head in Sītā's name and towards the southern direction (where she lives) began to relate how he succeeded in beholding Sītā.

sn: उवाच वाक्यं वाक्यज्ञः सीताया दर्शनं यथा। तं मणिं काञ्चनं दिव्यं दीप्यमानं स्वेतजसा ॥ दत्त्वा रामाय हनुमांस्ततः प्राञ्जलिरब्रवीत्। समुद्रं लवयित्वाहं शतयोजनमायतम्॥ अगच्छं जानकी सीतां मार्गमाणो दिक्षया। तत्र लङ्केति नगरी रावणस्य दुरात्मनः॥ दक्षिणस्य समुस्य तीरे वसति दक्षिणे।
en: Conferring on (Rāma) the heavenly jewel set on a golden leaf and burning with its own effulgence, Hanumān, with folded hands, began-Anxious to behold Sītā, the daughter of the king Janaka, I ploughing over the main extending over a hundred Yojana, wended my way and by and by reached Lankā, the capital of the vicious-souled Rāvaņa. Lankā is situated on the southern bank of the southern ocean,

sn: तत्र सीता मया दृष्टा रावणान्तः पुरे सती॥ त्वयि संन्यस्य जीवन्ती रामा राम मनोरथम्। दृष्टा मे राक्षसीमध्ये तय॑माना मुहुर्मुहुः॥ राक्षसीभिर्विरूपाभी रक्षिता प्रमदावने।
en: And I saw there Sītā, in the inner appartment of Ravana. Centring all her thoughts in you, breathes that damsel, O Rama. I saw her reviled by the she demons again and again. She is being guarded in that garden by the grim-visaged Raksasis.

sn: दुःखमापद्यते देवी त्वया वीर सुखोचिता ॥ रावणान्तःपुरे रुद्धा राक्षसीभिः सुरक्षिता। एकवेणीधरा दीना त्वयि चिन्तापरायणा ॥
en: And that worshipful came, O hero, ever used to happiness, is now stricken with grief in your absence. Confined in Ravana's inner apartment, well protected by those she-demons, wearing a single braid of hair and poorly, she is engaged only in thoughts touching you.

sn: अधःशय्या विवर्णाङ्गी पद्मिनीव हिमागमे। रावणाद् विनिवृत्तार्था मर्तव्यकृतनिश्चया॥
en: She in lying on earth, shorn of all grace like to a lotus on the appearance of the winter. She has not the least attachment for Rāvana and is resolved upon putting an end to her existence.

sn: देवी कथंचित् काकुत्स्थ त्वन्मना मार्गिता मया। इक्ष्वाकुवंशविख्यातिं शनैः कीर्तयतानघ ॥ सा मया नरशार्दूल शनैर्विश्वासिता तदा। ततः सम्भाषिता देवी सर्वमर्थं च दर्शिता॥
en: O Kākutstha, O innocent prince, after enquiring for sometime, I found that worshipful dame devoted to you, and narrating the glories of the Ikşvāku race, O foremost of men, I created her confidence by and by, and addressing her I related everything.

sn: रामसुग्रीवसख्यं च श्रुत्वा हर्षमुपागता। नियतः समुदाचारो भक्तिश्चास्याः सदा त्वयि॥
en: Hearing of the friendship between you and Sugrīva she was greatly delighted. And she has her respect for you unshaken and all her actions are for you.

sn: एवं मया महाभाग दृष्टा जनकनन्दिनी। उग्रेण तपसा युक्ता त्वद्भक्त्या पुरुषर्षभ॥
en: O great man, O you best of men, I beheld the daughter of Janaka in this plight, engaged in hard austerities and ever devoted to you.

sn: अभिज्ञानं च मे दत्तं यथावृतं तवान्तिके। चित्रकूटे महाप्राज्ञ वायसं प्रति राघव ॥
en: O you of great intelligence, O Raghava, offering me (this jewel) as a token, she wanted me to relate to you, the occurrence at the mount Citrakūța regarding the crow.

sn: विज्ञाप्यः पुनरप्येष रामो वायुसुत त्वया। अखिलेन यथा दृष्टमिति मामाह जानकी॥ अयं चास्मै प्रदातव्यो यत्नात् सुपरिरक्षितः।
en: And Jānakī addressing me said'O Windgod's son, do you describe everything of what you have seen here, to Rāma. And relating everything before Sugrīva, do you present him with this jewel which has been preserved by me with great care.

sn: ब्रुवता वचनान्येवं सुग्रीवस्योपशृण्वतः॥ एष चूडामणिः श्रीमान् मया ते यत्नरक्षितः। मनःशिलायास्तिलकं तत् स्मरस्वेति चाब्रवीत्॥ एष निर्यातितः श्रीमान् मया ते वारिसम्भवः। एनं दृष्ट्वा प्रमोदिष्ये व्यसने त्वामिवानघ ॥
en: I have kept with great care this excellent jewel of great effulgence. Do you remind him of the mark which he made on my forehead with red arsenic. O innocent monkey, greatly delighted am I on beholding the brilliant jewel which he has sent through you.

sn: जीवितं धारयिष्यामि मासं दशरथात्मज। ऊर्ध्वं मासान्न जीवेयं रक्षसां वशमागता॥
en: Breathe shall I only for a month, beyond that I shall never live, subject as I am to the demons.'

sn: इति मामब्रवीत् सीता कृशाङ्गी धर्मचारिणी। रावणान्तःपुरे रुद्धा मृगीवोत्फुल्ललोचना॥
en: Thus was I accosted by Sītā, reduced to a skeleton, observing pious observances, shut up in Rāvana's inner apartment and having eyes like those of a hind.

sn: एतदेव मयाऽऽख्यातं सर्वं राघव यद् यथा। सर्वथा सागरजले संतारः प्रविधीयताम्॥
en: I have described to you everything, O Rāghava, do you make arrangements for bridging over the ocean.

sn: तौ जाताश्वासौ राजपुत्रौ विदित्वा तच्चाभिज्ञानं राघवाय प्रदाय। देव्या चाख्यातं सर्वमेवानुपूर्व्याद् वाचा सम्पूर्णं वायुपुत्रः शशंस॥
en: And considering those two princes greatly consoled, the Wind-god's son handed over that token to Rāghava and described everything from the beginning to the end.

sn: एवमुक्तो हनुमता रामो दशरथात्मजः। तं मणिं हृदये कृत्वा रुरोद सहलक्ष्मणः॥
en: Being thus accosted by Hanumān, Rāma, the son of Dasaratha, placing that jewel on his breast, wept with Laksmana.

sn: तं तु दृष्ट्वा मणिश्रेष्ठं राघवः शोककर्शितः। नेत्राभ्यामश्रुपूर्णाभ्यां सुग्रीवमिदमब्रवीत्॥
en: Beholding that excellent jewel, Rāghava, stricken with grief, with eyes full of tears, spake to Sugriva, saying.

sn: यथैव धेनुः स्रवति स्नेहाद् वत्सस्य वत्सला। तथा ममापि हृदयं मणिश्रेष्ठस्य दर्शनात्॥
en: Forsooth my heart melt on beholding this jewel as milk trickle down from the udders of a cow on beholding its calf.

sn: मणिरत्नमिदं दत्तं वैदेह्याः श्वशुरेण मे। वधूकाले यथा बद्धमधिकं मूर्ध्नि शोभते॥
en: This jewel was conferred on Sītā by my father-in-law at the time of our wedding, and to enhance its beauty, she wore it on her head.

sn: अयं हि जलसम्भूतो मणिः प्रवरपूजितः। यज्ञे परमतुष्टेन दत्तः शक्रेण धीमता॥
en: And this jewel, obtained from the bed of the ocean, was conferred on him (Janaka) by the intelligent Sakra, greatly delighted for being adored in a sacrifice.

sn: इमं दृष्ट्वा मणिश्रेष्ठं तथा तातस्य दर्शनम्। अद्यास्म्यवगतः सौम्य सौम्य वैदेहस्य तथा विभोः॥
en: O gentle one, this bring back to my mind, the memory of my father, and father-in-law the king of Videha.

sn: अयं हि शोभते तस्याः प्रियाया मूर्ध्नि मे मणिः। अद्यास्य दर्शनेनाहं प्राप्तां तामिव चिन्तये।७।।
en: This excellent jewel appeared beautiful on the crown of my dear one, and methinks, on beholding it, I have as if got back my beloved spouse.

sn: किमाह सीता वैदेही ब्रूहि सौम्य पुनः पुनः। परासुमिव तोयेन सिञ्चन्ती वाक्यवारिणा ॥
en: Do you relate to me again and again, O gentle one what Vaidehi has said, as if sprinkling me with the water of her words like to one rendered senseless.

sn: इतस्तु किं दुःखतरं यदिमं वारिसम्भवम् । मणिं पश्यामि सौमित्रे वैदेहीमागतां विना॥
en: What greater grief can there be, O Saumitri, that I behold the jewel obtained from the ocean but not Vaidehi.?

sn: चिरं जीवति वैदही यदि मासं धरिष्यति। क्षणं वीर न जीवेयं विना तामसितेक्षणाम् ॥
en: Truly dose Vaidehī live for a long time if she breathes for a month. But O hero, I cannot live blue eyes.

sn: नय मामपि तं देशं यत्र दृष्टा मम प्रिया। न तिष्ठेयं क्षणमपि प्रवृत्तिमुपलभ्य च॥
en: Do you take me there where you had beheld iny dear spouse. I cannot live for a moment while I have received intelligence about her.

sn: कथं सा मम सुश्रोणी भीरुभीरुः सती तदा। भयावहानां घोराणां मध्ये तिष्ठति रक्षसाम्॥
en: How live that timid damsel, having a beautiful waist, being terrified, amidst the terrible and grim Raksasis?

sn: शारदस्तिमिरोन्मुक्तो नूनं चन्द्र इवाम्बुदैः। आवृतो वदनं तस्या न विराजति साम्प्रतम्॥
en: Truly her countenance is not appearing beautiful like to the autumnal moon, enveloped with clouds, although cleared off the darkness.

sn: किमाह सीता हनुमंस्तत्त्वतः कथयस्व मे। एतेन खलु जीविष्ये भेषजेनातुरो यथा॥
en: Do you relate to me in sooth, O Hanuman, what Şītā has spoken to you. I shall live by these words, as the sick are cured by medicine.

sn: मधुरा मधुरालापा किमाह मम भामिनी। मद्विहीना वरारोहा हनुमन् कथयस्व मे। दुःखाद् दुःखतरं प्राप्य कथं जीवति जानकी॥
en: O Hanumān, what has my dear wife, sweetspeeched, and highly beautiful, spoken to you, being separated form me? How breathes she going through a series of calamities?

sn: एवमुक्तस्तु हनुमान् राघवेण महात्मना। सीताया भाषितं सर्वं न्यवेदयत राघवे॥
en: Being thus addressed by the high-souled Rāghava, Hanumān, related to him all of what Sita had said,

sn: इदमुक्तवती देवी जानकी पुरुषर्षभ। पूर्ववृत्तमभिज्ञानं चित्रकूटे यथातथम्॥
en: O foremost of men, the worshipful Jānaki, related as a token, all the incidents at the Mount Citrakūta from the beginning to the end.

sn: सुखसुप्ता त्वया सार्धं जानकी पूर्वमुत्थिता। वायसः सहसोत्पत्य विददार स्तनान्तरम्॥
en: Sleeping happily with you, Janaki one day awoke before, and in the meantime, a crow wounded her breast with its beaks.

sn: पर्यायेण च सुप्तस्त्वं देव्यङ्के भरताग्रज। पुनश्च किल पक्षी स देव्या जनयति व्यथाम्॥
en: O Rāma, you wert then asleep on Sītā's lap and that crow again afflicted the worshipful dame.

sn: ततः पुनरुपागम्य विददार भृशं किल। ततस्त्वं बोधितस्तस्याः शोणितेन समुक्षितः॥ वायसेन च तेनैवं सततं बाध्यमानया। बोधितः किल देव्या त्वं सुखसुप्तः परंतप॥
en: And it again wounded her. And being bathed in blood and suffering terrible pangs, that worshipful dame aroused you.

sn: तां च दृष्ट्वा महाबाहो दारितां च स्तनान्तरे। आशीविष इव क्रुद्धस्ततो वाक्यं त्वमूचिवान्॥
en: O slayer of foes, O you of mighty-arms, seeing her breast wounded, you, wroth like a serpent, didst speak saying.

sn: नखाग्रैः केन ते भीरु रादितं वै स्तनान्तरम्। कः क्रीडति सरोषेण पञ्चवक्त्रेण भोगिना॥
en: O timid damsel, who, with his nails, has wounded your breast? Who has played with an angry serpent having five faces?

sn: निरीक्षमाणः सहसा वायसं समुदैक्षथाः। नखैः सरुधिरैस्तीक्ष्णैस्तामेवाभिमुखं स्थितम्॥
en: Casting your looks around you didst behold a crow facing the worshipful dame with sharpened nails besmeared with blood.

sn: सुतः किल स शक्रस्य वायसः पततां वरः। धरान्तरगतः शीघ्रं पवनस्य गतौ समः॥
en: That crow, the best of the birds, was Sakra's son. And it entered speedily into the earth with the velocity of the wind,

sn: ततस्तस्मिन् महाबाहो कोपसंवर्तितेक्षणः। वायसे त्वं व्यधाः क्रूरां मतिं मतिमतां वरः॥
en: Thereupon, your eyes rolling with ire, you, O mighty armed hero, O foremost of the intelligent, did resolve to destroy that crow.

sn: स दर्भसंस्तराद् गृह्य ब्रह्मास्त्रेण न्ययोजयः। स दीप्त इव कालाग्निर्जज्वालाभिमुखं खगम्॥
en: Taking a kusa off your seat you did set it on Brahma weapon. And it flamed like to the fire of desolation before that crow.

sn: स त्वं प्रदीप्तं चिक्षेप दर्भ तं वायसं प्रति । ततस्तु वायसं दीप्तः स दर्भोऽनुजगाम ह॥
en: You did let off that burning Kuśa towards that birds. And there upon that burning Kuća followed the crow.

sn: भीतैश्च सम्परित्यक्तः सुरैः सर्वैश्व वायसः। त्रींल्लोकान् सम्परिक्रम्य त्रातारं नाधिगच्छति च॥
en: And being forsaken even by the celestials, who were terrified, and ransacking the three worlds it did not get a refuge.

sn: पुनरप्यागतस्तत्र त्वत्सकाशमरिंदप्त। त्वं तं निपतितं भूमौ शरण्यः शरणागतम्॥ वधार्हमपि काकुत्स्थ कृपया परिपालयः।
en: Thereupon it again came to you, O subduer of foes. And seeking your shelter it laid itself low on the ground. And O Kākutstha, you didst save it albeit it was worthy of being slain.

sn: मोघमस्त्रं न शक्यं तु कर्तुमित्येव राघव ॥ भवांस्तस्याक्षि काकस्य हिनस्ति स्म स दक्षिणम्।
en: And thinking if improper to baffle the aim of the weapon, you didst, O Rāghava, destroy the right eye of the crow.

sn: राम त्वां स नमस्कृत्य राज्ञो दशरथस्य च॥ विसृष्टस्तु तदा काकः प्रतिपेदे स्वमालयम्।
en: Thereupon bowing to you and the king Dasaratha, that crow, bidding adieu, went to its quarter.

sn: एवमस्त्रविदां श्रेष्ठः सत्त्ववाञ्छीलवानपि॥ किमर्थमस्त्रं रक्षःसु न योजयसि राघव।
en: O Rāghava, you are the foremost of those skilled in the use of weapons, powerful and gifted with an excellent character, why do you not discharge weapons towards the Rākşasas?

sn: न दानवा न गन्धर्वा नासुरा न मरुद्गणाः॥ तव राम रणे शक्तास्तथा प्रतिसमासितुम् ।
en: The celestials, the Gandharvas, the Asuras, the Marutas-none of them is qualified, O Rāma, to equal you in conflict.

sn: तव वीर्यवतः कच्चिन्मयि यद्यस्ति सम्भ्रम॥ क्षिप्रं सुनियतैर्बाणैर्हन्यतां युधि रावणः।
en: If you, gifted with great prowess, had any armed shafts, destroy Rāvana in conflict.

sn: भ्रातुरादेशमाज्ञाय लक्ष्मणो वा परंतपः॥ स किमर्थं नरवरो न मां रक्षति राघवः।
en: And obtaining the behests of his brother, why dose not Lakşmaņa, the subduer of foes and best of men, protect me, O Rāghava?

sn: शक्तौ तौ पुरुषव्याघ्रौ वाय्वग्निसमतेजसौ॥ सुराणामपि दुर्धर्षों किमर्थं मामुपेक्षतः।
en: Those two best of men, gifted with the effulgence of Wind and Fire, and incapable of being repressed even by the celestials, are disregarding me.

sn: ममैव दुष्कृतं किंचिन्महदस्ति न संशयः॥ समर्थों सहितौ यन्मां न रक्षेते परंतपौ।
en: Forsooth have I perpetrated a mighty iniquity since those two slayers of foes, being capable, do not protect me.

sn: वैदेह्या वचनं श्रुत्वा करुणं साधुभाषितम्॥ । पुनरप्यहमारू तामिदं वचनमब्रवम्। त्वच्छोकविमुखो रामो देवि सत्येन ते शपे॥ रामे दुःखाभिभूते च लक्ष्मणः परितप्यते।
en: Hearing those sweet and piteous accents of Vaidehi I again spoke to that worshipful dame, saying. 'Forsooth can I swear by you, O worshipful dame, that Rāma is sorely stricken with grief in your absence. And Lakšmaņa too relent heavily beholding him laden with sorrow.

sn: कथंचिद् भवती दृष्टा न कालः परिशोचितुम्॥ इदं मुहूर्तं दु:खानामन्तं द्रक्ष्यसि भामिनि।
en: It dose not behove you to relent any more as I have succeeded in finding you out. You shall at this very moment behold the end of your grief.

sn: तावुभौ नरशार्दूलौ राजपुत्रौ परंतपौ॥ त्वदर्शनकृतोत्साहौ लङ्कां भस्मीकरिष्यतः।
en: And those two princes, the foremost of men and slayers of foes, actuated with energy on hearing that I have seen you, shall reduce Lankā to ashes.

sn: हत्वा च समरे रौद्रं रावणं सहबान्धवम् ॥ राघवस्त्वां वरारोहे स्वपुरी नयिता ध्रुवम्।
en: And slaying in conflict the terrible Rāvaņa, with his kith and kin, Rāghava, in sooth, O excellent damsel, shall take you back to his own city.

sn: यत् तु रामो विजानीयादभिज्ञानमनिन्दिते॥ प्रीतिसंजननं तस्य प्रदातुं तत् त्वमर्हसि।
en: O you of a blameless person, do you confer on me such a token, as might be recognized by Ráma and conduce to his pleasure.

sn: साभिवीक्ष्य दिशः सर्वा वेण्युद्ग्रथनमुत्तमम्॥ मुक्त्वा वस्त्राद् ददौ मह्यं मणिमेतं महाबल।
en: Thereat, casting her looks around, she took out an excellent jewel from her cloth, worthy of being set on her braid and conferred it on me, O you of great strength.

sn: प्रतिगृह्य मणिं दोभ्यां तव हेतो रघुप्रिय॥ शिरसा सम्प्रणम्यैनामहमागमने त्वरे।
en: O you, the most favourite of the Raghu race, taking for you that gem with my hands and bowing to her, I addressed myself speedily for departure.

sn: गमने च कृतोत्साहमवेक्ष्य वरवर्णिनी॥ विवर्धमानं च हि मामुवाच जनकात्मजा। अश्रुपूर्णमुखी दीना बाष्पगद्गदभाषिणी॥ ममोत्पतनसम्भ्रान्ता शोकवेगसमाहता। मामुवाच ततः सीता सभाग्योऽसि महाकपे॥ यद् द्रक्ष्यसि महाबाहुं रामं कमललोचनम्। लक्ष्मणं च महाबाहुं देवरं मे यशस्विनम्॥
en: Thereupon beholding me ready to depart and increase in bulk and about to leap up in the welkin, Sītā, the daughter of the king Janaka, poorly, bathed in tears, overwhelmed with sorrow and having her voice choked with grief, saying 'Blessed are you O great monkey, since you shall behold the large-armed and the lotuseyed Ráma and the highly famed Lakşmaņa, my lord's younger brother.

sn: सीतयाप्येवमुक्तोऽहमब्रुवं मैथिली तथा। पृष्ठमारोह मे देवि क्षिप्रं जनकनन्दिनि॥ यावत्ते दर्शयाम्यद्य ससुग्रीवं सलक्ष्मणम्। राघवं च महाभागे भरिमसितेक्षणे॥
en: And being thus accosted by Maithili, I said-Do you speedily place yourself on my back, O worshipful dame,oyou the daughter of king Janaka, and I shall soon show you, O great dame you having dark blue eyes, your lord along with Sugrīva and Lakşmaņa.'

sn: साब्रवीन्मां ततो देवी नैष धर्मो महाकपे। यत्ते पृष्ठं सिषेवेऽहं स्ववशा हरिपुङ्गव ॥
en: Whereto she replied — 'This is not the pious course, O great monkey, O you the foremost of your race, that I shall, of my own accord, place myself on your back.

sn: पुरा च यदहं वीर स्पृष्टा गात्रेषु रक्षसा। तत्राहं किं करिष्यामि कालेनोपनिपीडिता॥ गच्छ त्वं कपिशार्दूल यत्र तौ नृपतेः सुतौ।
en: And although before this I was touched by the demon, O hero, it was because I could not help otherwise subject as I was to circumstances. Do you yourself repair, O foremost of monkeys, where those two princes are.

sn: इत्येवं सा समाभाष्य भूयः संदेष्टुमास्थिता ॥ हनूमन् सिंहसंकाशौ तावुभौ रामलक्ष्मणौ। सुग्रीवं च सहामात्यं सर्वान् ब्रूया अनामयम्॥
en: Addressing me with these words she again said-O Hanuman, do you relate my well-being to Rāma and Lakshamana of leonine prowess, and Sugrīva accompanied by his followers.

sn: यथा च स महाबाहुर्मी तारयति राघवः। अस्मादुःखाम्बुसंरोधात् तत् त्वमाख्यातुमर्हसि ।॥
en: Do you so describe as the large-armed Rāghava may save me from this ocean of grief.

sn: इदं च तीव्र मम शोकवेगं रक्षोभिरेभिः परिभर्त्सनं च। ब्रूयास्तु रामस्य गतः समीपं शिवश्च तेऽध्वास्तु हरिप्रवीर॥
en: Do you narrate to Rāma this my terrible sorrow and the affliction by the she-demons. May good betide you, on your way, O foremost of the monkeys.'

sn: एतत् तवार्या नृप संयता सा सीता वचः प्राह विषादपूर्वम्। एतच्च बुद्ध्वा गदितं यथा त्वं श्रद्धत्स्व सीतां कुशलां समग्राम्॥
en: Thus the worshipful Sítă gave vent to these piteous accents. Hearing these words do you believe that it is all well with her.

sn: अथाहमुत्तरं देव्या पुनरुक्तः ससम्भ्रमम्। तव स्नेहान्नरव्याघ्र सौहार्दादनुमान्य च॥
en: Thereupon, O foremost of men, out of your love and adoring me for your friendship, that worshipful dame-addressed me again, saying.

sn: एवं बहुविधं वाच्यो रामो दाशरथिस्त्वया। यथा मां प्राप्नुयाच्छीघ्रं हत्वा रावणमाहवे॥
en: Do you thus speak every thing to Rāma, the son of Daśaratha, so that he might soon take me hence, slaying Ravana in battle.

sn: यदि वा मन्यसे वीर वसैकाहमरिंदम। कस्मिश्चित् संवृते देशे विश्रान्तः श्वो गमिष्यसि॥
en: O hero, O slayer of foes, if it please you, you may relieve yourself of the toil by living in a secret nook and then proceed to-morrow.

sn: मम चाप्यल्पभाग्यायाः सांनिध्यात् तव वानर। अस्य शोकविपाकस्य मुहूर्तं स्याद् विमोक्षणम्॥
en: O monkey, in your company, I do momentarily forget the weight of my grief, unfortunate as I am.

sn: गते हि त्वयि विक्रान्ते पुनरागमनाय वै। प्राणानामपि संदेहो मम स्यान्नात्र संशयः॥
en: O you gifted with great prowess, yourself departing, I shall wait for your return, but doubt I very much whether I shall live till then.

sn: तवादर्शनजः शोको भूयो मां परितापयेत्। दुःखाद् दुःखपराभूतां दुर्गतां दुःखभागिनीम्। ६॥
en: Burnt I shall be with the fear of not beholding you again, wretched and stricken with grief as I am. And so I shall be, hereafter, overwhelmed with a mightier grief.

sn: अयं च वीर संदेहस्तिष्ठतीव ममाग्रतः। सुमहांस्त्वत्सहायेषु हर्यक्षेषु हरीश्वर ॥ कथं नु खलु दुष्पारं तरिष्यन्ति महोदधिम्। तानि हपृक्षसैन्यानि तौ वा नरवरात्मजौ॥
en: O hero, besides, I entertain a grave doubt about your assistants, the monkeys and bears. I do not know how shall the host of monkeys and bears and those two princes cross over the mighty main?

sn: त्रयाणामेव भूतानां सागरस्यास्य लङ्घने। शक्तिः स्याद् वैनतेयस्य वायोर्वा तव चानघ॥
en: O innocent monkey of all the creatures three only are qualified to cross over the ocean, yourself, Garuda and the Wind.

sn: तदस्मिन् कार्यनिर्योगे वीरैवं दुरतिक्रमे। किं पश्यसि समाधानं ब्रूहि कार्यविदां वर॥
en: O you foremost of those skilled in speech, what had you settled about the accomplishment of this hard work?

sn: काममस्य त्वमेवैकः कार्यस्य परिसाधने। पर्याप्तः परवीरन यशस्यस्ते बलोदयः॥
en: True it is that you are alone qualified to accomplish this work, you the slayer of inimical heroes-but such manifestation of your prowess shall increase your glory only.

sn: बलैः समग्रैर्यदि मां हत्वा रावणमाहवे। विजयी स्वपुरी रामो नयेत् तत्स्याद् यशस्करम् ॥
en: But if Rāma, obtaining victory, can take me hence to his own city, it shall redound to his glory.

sn: यथाहं तस्य वीरस्य वनादुपधिना हृता। रक्षसा तद्भयादेव तथा नार्हति राघवः॥
en: It dose not behove the heroic Rāghava, to take me away by steal, like to Rāvaņa capturing me from the forest under a disguise.

sn: बलैस्तु संकुलां कृत्वा लङ्कां परबलार्दनः। मां नयेद् यदि काकुत्स्थस्तत् तस्य सदृशं भवेत्॥
en: Truly it shall be his becoming work, if Kākutstha, the repressor of enemy's host, can take me away, enveloping the city Lankā with his army.

sn: तद् यथा तस्य विक्रान्तमनुरूपं महात्मनः। भवत्याहवशूरस्य तथा त्वमुपपादय॥
en: Do you therefore initiate that work as become that high-souled hero and may display his prowess.

sn: तदर्थोपहितं वाक्यं प्रश्रितं हेतुसंहितम्। निशम्याहं ततः शेषं वाक्यमुत्तरमब्रुवम्॥
en: Hearing these sound reasonable and affectionate words I gave her the last reply, saying.

sn: देवि हर्युक्षसैन्यानामीश्वरः प्लवतां वरः। सुग्रीवः सत्त्वसम्पन्नस्त्वदर्थे कृतनिश्चयः॥
en: O worshipful dame, Sugrīva, the foremost of the monkeys, the lord of monkey and bear hosts and gifted with manliness, has resolved upon rescuing you.

sn: तस्य विक्रमसम्पन्नाः सत्त्ववन्तो महाबलाः। मन:संकल्पसदृशा निदेशे हरयः स्थिताः॥
en: He has under his command a number of mighty and courageous monkeys gifted with great prowess and quick-coursing like imagination.

sn: येषां नोपरि नाधस्तान्न तिर्यक् सज्जते गतिः। न च कर्मसु सीदन्ति महत्स्वमिततेजसः॥
en: Their course is never thwarted-whether going upwards or downwardsor moving tortuously. They are never exhausted in their actions—highly courageous and of measureless prowess.

sn: असकृत् तैर्महाभागैर्वानरैर्बलसंयुतैः। प्रदक्षिणीकृता भूमिर्वायुमार्गानुसारिभिः॥
en: And those great and powerful monkeys, coursing in the air, have again and again circumambulated the earth.

sn: मद्विशिष्टाश्च तुल्याश्व सन्ति तत्र वनौकसः। मत्तः प्रत्यवरः कश्चिन्नास्ति सुग्रीवसंनिधौ॥
en: Sugriva has many monkeys-my equal-and greater than I but none of inferior strength.

sn: अहं तावदिह प्राप्तः किं पुनस्ते महाबलाः। नहि प्रकृष्टाः प्रेष्यन्ते प्रेष्यन्ते हीतरे जनाः॥
en: While I have crossed over the main-what of these mighty heroes? The leading heroes are never sent on a mission but only those of inferior merit.

sn: तदलं परितापेन देवि मन्युरपैतु ते। एकोत्पातेन ते लङ्कामेष्यन्ति हरियूथपाः॥
en: No more of bewailing, O worshipful dame. Do you remove your grief. And with one leap these leaders of monkey-hosts shall reach Lankā.

sn: मम पृष्ठगतौ तौ च चन्द्रसूर्याविवोदितौ । त्वत्सकाशं महाभागे नृसिंहावागमिष्यतः॥
en: O great damsel, these two princes, placing themselves on my back shall come to you like to the rising Sun and Moon.

sn: अरिघ्नं सिंहसंकाशं क्षिप्रं द्रक्ष्यसि राघवम्। लक्ष्मणं च धनुष्मन्नं लङ्काद्वारमुपागतम्॥
en: You shall soon behold before Lanka's gate Rāghava the slayer of foes resembling a lion and Lakşmana with a bow in his hand.

sn: नखदंष्ट्रायुधान् वीरान् सिंहशार्दूलविक्रमान्। वानरान् वारणेन्द्राभान् क्षिप्रं द्रक्ष्यसि संगतान् ॥
en: You shall soon observe in a band the heroic monkeys, gifted with the strength of lions and tigers, and having nails and teeth for their weapons.

sn: शैलाम्बुदनिकाशानां लङ्कामलयसानुषु। नर्दतां कपिमुख्यानां नचिराच्छ्रोष्यसे स्वनम्॥
en: You shall soon bear the roaring of the leading monkeys on the summit of mount Malaya, resembling the muttering of the clouds.

sn: निवृत्तवनवासं च त्वया सार्धमरिंदमम्। अभिषिक्तमयोध्यायां क्षिप्रं द्रक्ष्यसि राघवम्॥
en: You shall soon behold Rāghava, the slayer of foes, installed along with you on the throne of Ayodhya after returning from the forest.

sn: ततो मया वाग्भिरदीनभाषिणी शिवाभिरिष्टाभिरभिप्रसादिता। उवाह शान्तिं मम मैथिलात्मजा तवातिशोकेन तथातिपीडिता॥
en: That daughter of the king of Mithilā although heavily laden with sorrow in your absence was greatly comforted and pleased by my auspicious words boding the fulfilment of her desire.

sn: श्रुत्वा हनूमतो वाक्यं यथावदभिभाषितम्। रामः प्रीतिसमायुक्तो वाक्यमुत्तरमब्रवीत्॥
en: Hearing the words of Hanumän rehearsed properly, Rāma, exceedingly delighted, said.

sn: कृतं हनूमता कार्यं सुमहद्भुवि दुर्लभम्। मनसाऽपि यदन्येन न शक्यं धरणीतले॥
en: By Hanumān has been performed a very great deed, rare on earth, and one incapable of being even conceived by any other in the world.

sn: नहि तं परिपश्यामि यस्तरेत महोदधिम्। अन्यत्र गरुडाद्वायोरन्यत्र च हनूमतः॥
en: Save Garuda and the Wind-god, and save also Hanumān, him find I not who cross the wide ocean.

sn: देवदानवयक्षाणां गन्धर्वोरगरक्षसाम्। अप्रधृष्यां पुरीं लङ्कां रावणेन सुरक्षिताम्॥ प्रविष्टः सत्त्वमाश्रित्यं जीवन्को नाम निष्क्रमेत्।
en: Entering by main force the city of Larkā, incapable of being subjugated by the gods and Dänavas and Yaksas, the Gandharvas, serpents or Raksasas, and well protected by Ravana, who, living, come out (of it)?

sn: को विशेत्सुदुराधर्षां राक्षसैश्च सुरक्षिताम् ॥ यो वीर्यबलसंपन्नो न समः स्याद्धनूमतः।
en: Who that is not the compeer of Hanuman in strength and prowess, even enters into (Lankā) hard to subdue, and carefully guarded by the Raksasas?

sn: भृत्यकार्य हनुमता सुग्रीवस्य कृतं महत्। एवं विधाय स्वबलं सदृशं विक्रमस्य च॥
en: Having put forth his strength commensurate with his prowess, Hanuman has also performed a great act befitting a servant on behold of Sugriva.* SO *Having seen Sītā, which was all that he had been commissioned to do by Sugrīva, Hanumān has destroyed Räkşasas and burnt Lankā; and this he did of himself like a good servant.

sn: यो हि भृत्यो नियुक्तः सन्भ; कर्मणि दुष्करे। कुर्यात्तदनुरागेण तमाहुः पुरुषोत्तमम्॥
en: That servant who, being entrusted with a hard task, after having accomplished it, do another work in pursuance of (the prescribed business), is the best of men.

sn: यो नियुक्तः परं कार्यं न कुर्यान्नृपतेः प्रियम्। भृत्यो युक्तः समर्थश्च तमाहुर्मध्यमं नरम्॥
en: That servant is middling, who, deputed to any task,* do not albeit capable, perform any other work which may be dear to the king. *i.e. performing the entrusted work.

sn: नियुक्तो नृपतेः कार्य न कुर्याद्यः समाहितः। भृत्यो युक्तः समर्थश्च तमाहुः पुरुषाधमम्॥
en: That servant who, entrusted with any work of the king do not, although competent, heedfully accomplish the same, has been called the worst.

sn: तन्नियोगे नियुक्तेन कृतं कृत्यं हनूमता। न चात्मा लघुतां नीतः सुग्रीवश्चापि तोषितः॥
en: Anent the order (which he had received), Hanuman has done the work (and more). He has not been humbled,* and, further, he has pleased Sugriva. *By the Raksasas.

sn: अहं च रघुवंशश्च लक्ष्मणश्च महाबलः। वैदेह्या दर्शनेनाद्य धर्मतः परिरक्षिताः॥
en: And by seeing Vaidehī, (Hanumān) has, while reaping righteousness, saved me, the Raghu race, and the highly powerful Lakşmaņa.

sn: इदं तु मम दीनस्य मनो भूयः प्रकर्षति। यदिहास्य प्रियाख्यातुर्न कुर्मि सदृशं प्रियम् ॥
en: This pain my mind sore, that I cannot do a like benefit, returning this dear office of his.

sn: एष सर्वस्वभूतस्तु परिष्वङ्गो हनूमत । मया कालमिमं प्राप्य दत्तस्तस्य महात्मनः॥!'
en: Embrace express the all (of the Deicy),* and, finding this occasion, I extend my embrace to the high-souled Hanumān. *The commentator explains this obscure passage after his own orthodox fashion. The gist is this. Delight is the essence of the Deity, and all His incarnations body forth this. Embrace is typical of this emotion.

sn: इत्युक्त्वा प्रीतिहृष्टाङ्गो रामस्तं परिषस्वजे। हनूमन्तं कृतात्मनं कृतवाक्यमुपागतम्॥
en: Having said this, Rama, with his down standing on end in joy, embraced the selfcontrolled Hanumān, who was present after having finished his speech.

sn: ध्यात्वा पुनरुवाचेदं वचनं रघुसत्तमः। हरीणामीश्वरस्यापि सुग्रीवस्योपशृण्वतः॥
en: Then reflecting for a while, the best of the Raghus again spoke in the presence of Sugrīva, lord of monkeys.

sn: सर्वथा सुकृतं तावत्सीतायाः परिमार्गणम्। सागरं तु समासाद्य पुनर्नष्टं मनो मम॥
en: Complete success has been attained anent the search of Sītā. But when I think of the ocean, my mind is again sunk in dejection.

sn: कथं नाम समुद्रस्य दुष्पारस्य महाम्भसः। हरयो दक्षिणं पारं गमिष्यन्ति समागताः॥
en: How can the assembled monkeys go over to the southern shore of the vastly deep, difficult to cross?

sn: यद्यप्येष तु वृत्तान्तो वैदेह्या गतितो मम। समुद्रपारगमने हरीणां किमिवोत्तरम्॥
en: This tidings you have related to me touching Vaidehī; but what are the monkeys to do next avout crossing the sea?

sn: इत्युक्त्वा शोकसंभ्रान्तो रामः शत्रुनिर्बहणः। हनूमन्तं महाबाहुस्ततो ध्यानमुपागमत्॥
en: Having said this to Hanumān, that slayer of foes, the mighty-armed Rāma, agitated by anxiety, was then plunged in thought.

sn: तं तु शोकपरिघुनं रामं दशरथात्मजम्। उवाच वचनं श्रीमान्सुग्रीवः शोकनाशनम्॥
en: Then the graceful Sugrīva spoke words capable of soothing sorrow, to Dasaratha's son, Rāma, who was wrought up with grief.

sn: किं त्वयातप्यते वीर यथान्यः प्राकृतस्तथा। मैवं भूस्त्यज संतापं कृतघ्न इव सौहृदम्॥
en: Why, O hero, does you grieve, like one that is base? Let not this be so. Chase away you grief, even as an ingrate resign amity.

sn: संतापस्य च ते स्थानं नहि पश्यामि राघव। प्रवृत्तावुपलब्धायां ज्ञाते च निलये रिपोः॥
en: Nor, O Rāghava, when the whereabouts of Sītă has been discovered, and when too the abode itself of the foe has been known, do I perceive the reason of your sorrow.

sn: मतिमाशास्त्रवित्प्राज्ञः पण्डितश्चासि राघव। त्यजेमां प्राकृतां बुद्धिं कृतात्मेवार्थदूषिणीम्॥
en: You, O Raghava, are intelligent, conversant with learning, wise, and judicious. Do you cast away this sorry way of thinking, even as a selfcontrolled (ascetic) caste away any course of thought interfering with the attainment of his purpose.

sn: समुद्रं लवयित्वा तु महानक्रसमाकुलम्। लङ्कामारोहयिष्यामो हनिष्यामश्च ते रिपुम्॥
en: Crossing over the ocean swarming with gigantic alligators, we shall enter Lankā and slay the enemy.

sn: निरुत्साहस्य दीनस्य शोकपर्याकुलात्मनः। सर्वार्था व्यवसीदन्ति व्यसनं चाधिगच्छति॥
en: Of a person that is dispirited and poor in pluck and that has his soul overwhelmed with grief, every interest droops, and he comes by misfortunes (one after another).

sn: इमे शूराः समर्थाश्च सर्वतो हरियूथपाः। त्वत्प्रियार्थं कृतोऽत्साहाः प्रवेष्टुमपि पावकम्। एषां हर्षेण जानामि तर्कश्चापि दृढो मम ॥
en: All these heroes, these leaders of monkeyhordes, who are ardent for they welfare, are competent to enter into fire itself. From their cheerful attitude I know this, and firm is my faith.

sn: विक्रमेण समानेष्ये सीतां हत्वा यथा रिपुम्। रावणं पापकर्माणं तथा त्वं कर्तुमर्हसि॥
en: It behove you so to arrange things that, slaying the foe, Rāvana of impious acts, we may bring higher Sītā by our own prowess.

sn: सेतुरत्र यथा बद्ध्येद्यथा पश्येम तां पुरीम्। तस्य राक्षसराजस्य तथा त्वं कुरु राघव॥
en: Do you, O Rāghava, so order matters that a bridge may be constructed (over the main), and that we may behold the palace of the Rākşasa monarch.

sn: दृष्ट्वा तां हि पुरीं लङ्कां त्रिकूटशिखरे स्थिताम्। हतं च रावणं युद्धे दर्शनादवधारय ॥
en: We having seen the city of Lankā, established on the summit of Triküța, do you for certain conclude Răvaņa as slain in battle immediately after (we see her).

sn: अबद्ध्वा सागरे सेतुं घोरे च वरुणालये। लङ्का न मर्दितुं शक्या सेन्ट्रैरपि सुरासुरैः॥
en: Without throwing a bridge over the ocean-the dread abode of Varuņa-even the Asuras and celestials with Indra (at their head) are unequal to subduing Laňkā.

sn: सेतुबन्धः समुद्रे च यावल्लङ्कासमीपतः। सर्वं तीर्णं च मे सैन्यं जितमित्युपधारय। तथा हि समरे वीरा हरयः कामरूपिणः॥ तदलं विक्लवां बुद्धिं राजन्सर्वार्थनाशनीम्। पुरुषस्य हि लोकेऽस्मिन् शोकः शौर्यापकर्षणः॥
en: When the bridge over the ocean has been constructed up to near Laňkä, and when my forces have crossed (over the sea), consider victory as secured. As these monkeys are heroic in fight, and able to wear forms at will, O king, do not let your intellect get stupefied and thus mar all interests. In this world, sorrow berefts people of their prowess.

sn: यत्तु कार्यं मनुष्येण शौटीर्यमवलम्ब्यताम्। तदलंकरणायैव कर्तुर्भवति सत्वरम्॥
en: Do you do even what should be done by a man-summon your manliness; for what an actor does promptly, conduce to his success.

sn: अस्मिन्काले महाप्राज्ञ सत्त्वमातिष्ठ तेजसा। शूराणां हि मनुष्याणां त्वद्विधानां महात्मनाम्। विनष्टे वा प्रनष्टे वा शोकः सर्वार्थनाशनः॥
en: At this time, O eminently wise one, do you realise goodness through they energy.* Of heroic, high-souled, men like yourself, on their sustaining and entire or a partial loss, grief undo every interest. *i.e. as I understand this rather obscure passage, prove the good through your vigour-secure victory to the cause of goodness through they might.

sn: तत्त्वं बुद्धिमतां श्रेष्ठः सर्वशा स्वार्थकोविदः। मद्विधैः सचिवैः सार्धमरिं जेतुं समर्हसि ॥
en: Therefore, the foremost of intelligent persons, and conversant with every lore, you should along with councillors like me, strive to beat they foe.

sn: नहि पश्याम्यहं कंचित्रिषु लोकेषु राघव। गृहीतधनुषो यस्ते तिष्ठेदभिमुखो रणे॥
en: Find I none in the three worlds, O Rāghava, who can stay in fight before you equipped with your bow,

sn: वानरेषु समासक्तं न ते कार्य विपत्स्यते। अचिराद्रक्ष्यसे सीतां तीर्खा सागरमक्षयम्॥
en: Your business entrusted to these monkeys shall not (anyway) suffer. And soon, crossing over the boundless main, you shall behold Sītā.

sn: तदलं शोकमालम्ब्य क्रोधमालम्ब भूपते। निश्चेष्टाः क्षत्रिया मन्दाः सर्वे चण्डस्य बिभ्यति ॥
en: Therefore, O king, renounce your sorrow, and call up wrath. Those Ksatriyas that conceive no anger in respect of their enemies, have their activity annulled; and all fear furious persons.

sn: लङ्घनार्थं च घोरस्य समुद्रस्य नदीपतेः। सहास्माभिरिहोपेतः सूक्ष्मबुद्धिर्विचारय॥
en: Drawing nigh to us, do you, gifted with acute intelligence, cast about for crossing over the dreadful deep, lord of streams, along with us.

sn: लङ्घिते तत्र तैः सैन्यैर्जितमित्येव निश्चिनु। सर्वं तीर्णं च मे सैन्यं जितमित्यवधार्यताम्॥
en: On these forces getting beyond the ocean, do you take it for certain that we have won; and when my whole host has reached the further shore, do you indubitably conclude that we have obtained victory.

sn: इमे हि हरयः शूराः समरे कामरूपिणः। तानरीन्विधमिष्यन्ति शिलापादपवृष्टिभिः॥
en: These monkeys, heroic and capable of assuming in fight forms at will, shall slaughter those foes by showering rocks and trees.

sn: कथंचित्यपरिपश्यामि लचितं वरुणालयम्। हतमित्येव तं मन्ये युद्धे शत्रुनिबर्हण॥
en: If I see any means of crossing the ocean, Varuna's abode, I shall, O destroyer of foes, deem him as slain in battle.

sn: किमुक्त्वा बहुधा चापि सर्वथा विजयी भवान्। निमित्तानि च पश्यामि मनो मे संप्रहृष्यति॥
en: And what is the use of dilating? Every way you shall prove victorious. And I see omens, and my mind is filled with delight.

sn: सुग्रीवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा हेतुमत्परमार्थवत्। प्रतिजग्राह काकुत्स्थो हनूमन्तमथाब्रवीत्॥
en: Hearing Sugrīva's speech, reasonable and fraught with high sense, Kākutstha accorded his assent to it and spoke to Hanumān, saying.

sn: तपसा सेतुबन्धेन सागरोच्छोषणेन च। सर्वथापि समर्थोऽस्मि सागरस्यास्य लङ्घने॥
en: By asceticism, or constructing a bridge, or drying up the ocean, competent every way am I for crossing over this ocean.

sn: कति दुर्गाणि दुर्गाया लङ्कायास्तद्ब्रवीष्व मे। ज्ञातुमिच्छामि तत्सर्वं दर्शनादिव वानर ॥
en: Of impracticable places, tell me how many there are in (Lankā), which are incapable of being come at.

sn: बलस्य परिमाणं च द्वारदुर्गक्रियामपि। गुप्तिकर्म च लङ्काया रक्षसा सदनानि च॥ यथासुखं यथावच्च लङ्कायामसि दृष्टवान्। सर्वमाचक्ष्व तत्त्वेन सर्वथा कुशलो ह्यसि ॥
en: O monkey, as you have seen personally, I wish to get acquainted with all this. And you have at your leisure duly noticed in Lankā the nur.ber of the army, the inaccessibility (or otherwise) of the gates, the defence of Lankā, and the dwellings of the Rākşasas. Do you faithfully relate this to me, for you are observant.

sn: श्रुत्वा रामस्य वचनं हनूमान्मारुतात्मजः। वाक्यं वाक्यविदां श्रेष्ठो रामं पुनरथाब्रवीत्॥ श्रूयतां सर्वमाख्यास्ये दुर्गकर्म विधानतः। गुप्ता पुरी यथा लङ्का रक्षिता च यथा बलैः॥ राक्षसाश्च यथा स्निग्धा रावणस्य च तेजसा। परां समृद्धिं लङ्कायाः सागरस्य च भीमताम्॥ विभागं च बलौघस्य निर्देशं वाहनस्य च। एवमुक्त्वा कपिश्रेष्ठः कथयामास तत्त्ववित्॥
en: Hearing Rāma's speech, Hanumān, offspring of the Wind-god, foremost of those conversant with speech, again spoke to Rāma, Hearken! I will describe to you by what method is the city of Lankā guarded and protected by the Rākṣasas, how loyal the Rākşasas are, the surpassing prosperity of Lankā, the dreadfulness of the deep, the divisions of the forces, and the number of the elephants, horses, cars, etc.' Having said this, that best of monkeys, knowing the nature of things, went on.

sn: हृष्टप्रमुदिता लङ्का मत्तद्विपसमाकुला। महती रथसंपूर्णा रक्षोगणनिषेविता ॥
en: Lankā, filled with mad elephants, ever rejoice. She is great, thronging with cars and inhabited by Raksasas.

sn: दृढबद्धकपाटानि महापरिघवन्ति च। चत्वारि विपुलान्यस्या द्वाराणि सुमहान्ति च॥
en: Her doors are firmly established and furnished with massy bolts. And she has four wide and giant gates.

sn: तत्रेषूपलयन्त्राणि बलवन्ति महान्ति च। आगतं प्रतिसैन्यं तैस्तत्र प्रतिनिवार्यते॥
en: (At those gates) are powerful and large arms, stones, and engines, whereby a hostile host approaching, is opposed.

sn: द्वारेषु संस्कृता भीमाः कालायसमयाः शिताः। शतशो रचिता वीरैः शतघ्न्यो रक्षसां गणैः॥
en: At the entrances are arrayed and set in order by bands of heroic Rākşasas, hundreds of dreadful sharp iron sataghnis.* *A kind of fire-arms, or ancient Hindu rocket; or a stone set round with sharp iron spikes. According to Rāmānuja, a sort of mace about two yards in length, with spikes.

sn: सौवर्णस्तु महांस्तस्याः प्राकारो दुष्प्रधर्षणः। मणिविद्रुमवैदूर्यमुक्ताविरचितान्तरः॥
en: She has a mighty impassable golden wall, having its side emblazoned in the centre with costly stones, coral, lapises and pearls.

sn: सर्वतश्च महाभीमाः शीततोया महाशुभाः। अगाधा ग्राहवत्यश्च परिखा मीनसेविताः॥
en: Round about is a moat, exceedingly dreadful, with cool water, eminently grand, fathomless, containing ferocious aquatic animals, and inhabited by fishes.

sn: द्वारेषु तासां चत्वारः संक्रमाः परमायताः। यन्त्रैरुपेता बहुभिर्महद्भिर्गृहपङ्क्तिभिः॥
en: At the gates are four broad bridges, furnished with machines and many rows of grand structures.

sn: त्रायन्ते संक्रमास्तत्र परसैन्यागते सति। यन्त्रैस्तैरवकीर्यन्ते परिखासु समन्ततः॥
en: On the approach of hostile forces, their attack is repulsed by these machines, and they are thrown into the ditch.

sn: एकस्त्वकम्प्यो बलवान्संक्रमः सुमहादृढः। काञ्चनैर्बहुभिः स्तम्भैर्वेदिकाभिश्च शोभितः॥
en: One among these bridges is immovable, strong and fast established; adorned with golden pillars and daises.

sn: स्वयं प्रकृतिमापन्नो युयुत्सू राम रावणः। उत्थितश्चाप्रमत्तश्च बलानामनुदर्शने॥
en: O Rāma, albeit Rāvaņa hunger for fight, yet is he calm; and he is vigilant and ever engaged in superintending his army.

sn: लङ्कापुनर्निरालम्बा देवदुर्गा भयावहा। नादेयं पार्वतं चान्यं कृत्रिमं च चतुर्विधम् ॥
en: And dreadful and resembling a celestial citadel, Lankā cannot be ascended by means of any support. She has fortresses composed of streams, those of hills, and artificial ones of four kinds.

sn: स्थिता पारे समुद्रस्य दूरपारस्य राघव। नौपथश्चापि नास्त्यत्र निरुद्देशश्च सर्वशः॥
en: O Rāghava, she is situated on the other shore of the ocean having its limit far away. And way there is none even for barks, and all sides are destitute of division.

sn: शैलाने रचिता दुर्गा सा पूर्देवपुरोपमा। वाजिवारणसंपूर्णा लङ्का परमदुर्जया॥
en: That citadel is built on the mountain's brow; and, resembling the metropolis of the immortals, the exceedingly invincible Larkā is filled with horses and elephants.

sn: परिखाश्च शतघ्यश्च यन्त्राणि विविधानि च। शोभयन्ति पुरीं लङ्कां रावणस्य दुरात्मनः॥
en: And a moat and sataghnís and various engines adorn the city of Lankā, belonging to the wicked Rāvana.

sn: अयुतं रक्षसामत्र पूर्वद्वारं समाश्रितम्। शूलहस्ता दुराधर्षाः सर्वे खङ्गाग्रयोधिनः॥
en: And an ayuta of Raksasas, dart-handed, hard to subdue, and all fighting at the front with their swords-protect the Eastern gate.

sn: नियुतं रक्षसामत्र दक्षिणद्वारमाश्रितम्। चतुरङ्गेण सैन्येन योधास्तत्राप्यनुत्तमाः॥
en: And a lac of Rākşasas with a fourfold force, and with the flower of the soldiery-protect the Southern gate.

sn: प्रयुतं रक्षसामत्र पश्चिमद्वारमाश्रितम्। चर्मखङ्गधराः सर्वे तथा सर्वास्त्रकोविदाः॥
en: And a prayuta of Rākṣasas, bearing swords and shields, and skilled in all arms, protect the Western gate.

sn: न्यर्बुदं रक्षसामत्र उत्तरद्वारमाश्रितम्। रथिनश्चाश्ववाहाश्च कुलपुत्राः सुपूजिताः॥ शतशोऽथ सहस्राणि मध्यमं स्कन्धमाश्रिताः। यातुधाना दुराधर्षाः साग्रकोटिश्च रक्षसाम्॥
en: And an arbuda of Rākṣasas protect the Northern gate. And car-warriors and horsemenpersons honoured and sprung from noble linesby hundreds and thousands,tand irrepressible goblins and koțis of Rākşasas, protect the garrison.

sn: ते मया संक्रमा भग्नाः परिखाश्चावपूरिताः। दग्धा च नगरी लङ्का प्राकाराश्चावसादिताः॥
en: I have broken down the bridges and filled up the entrenchment. I have burnt that city of Lankā and laid the wall low.

sn: येन केन तु मार्गेण तराम वरुणालयम्। हतेति नगरी लङ्का वानरैरुपधार्यताम्॥
en: Let us by any way whatever cross over Varuna's abode. Do you take it for certain that the city of Lankā is subdued by the monkeys.

sn: अङ्गदो द्विविदो मैन्दो जाम्बवान्पनसो नलः। नील: सेनापतिश्चैव बलशेषेण किं तव॥ प्लवमाना हि गत्वा तां रावणस्य महापुरीम्। सपर्वतवना भित्त्वा सखातां च सतोरणाम्।। सप्राकारां सभवनामानयिष्यन्ति राधव॥
en: What is the use of your reckoning the rest? Aigada, Dvivida, Mainda, Jambavan, Panasa, Nala, and the general, Nīla, bounding and reaching Răvana's abode, and riving the same consisting of woods and hills, moat and gateway, walls and dwellings, shall, O Rāghava, bring (hither) Sītā.

sn: एवमाज्ञापय क्षिप्रं बलानां सर्वसंग्रहम्। मुहूर्तेन तु युक्तेन प्रस्थानमभिरोचय॥
en: If this be so,* do you order the entire body of the army to be brought; and do you set out at the proper hour. *Ebam ajnápaya: Ramanuja reads sense into this passage. If you wishes the principal monkeys to go, bring them; if you wish the whole host to march, call it hither, and march at the auspicious moment.

sn: श्रुत्वा हनूमतो वाक्यं यथावदनुपूर्वशः। ततोऽब्रवीन्महातेजा रामः सत्यपराक्रमः॥
en: Hearing Hanumăn's speech duly from the beginning, the exceedingly energetic Rāma having truth for this prowess, said.

sn: यनिवेदयसे लङ्कां पुरीं भीमस्य रक्षसः। क्षिप्रमेनां वधिष्यामि सत्यमेतद्ब्रवीमि ते॥
en: What you say 'I shall speedily destroy the city of this dreadful Raksasa,' is true, I tell you.

sn: अस्मिन्मुहूर्ते सुग्रीवप्रयाणमभिरोचय। युक्तो मुहूर्ते विजये प्राप्तो मध्यं दिवाकरः॥
en: Therefore, at this very moment arrange for Sugrīva's march. The Sun has attained his meridian at this proper moment, capable of conferring victory.* *The moment is named abhijit.

sn: सीतां हृत्वा तु तद्यातु क्वासौ यास्यति जीवितः। सीता श्रुत्वाभियानं मे आशामेष्यति जीविते। जीवितान्तेऽमृतं स्पृष्ट्वा पीत्वाऽमृतमिवातुरः॥
en: Let Rāvana carry away Sītā (to his own country), whither shall Ravana, living, repair? Like a dying person who has taken a deathdispelling drug and drunk ambrosia, Sītā, hearing of my preparations for war, shall inspire hope of life.

sn: उत्तराफाल्गुनी ह्यद्य श्वस्तु हस्तेन योक्ष्यते। अभिप्रयाम सुग्रीव सर्वानीकसमावृताः॥
en: To-day the Northern Phālguni (is in the ascendant); and to-morrow the moon shall be in conjunction with Hasta.* O Sugriva, shall we set our, surrounded by the entire host? *Hastā sprung from Punarvasu is the star of doom, portending death to Rāvana. The Northern Phālguni, is Sita's natal star. The expedition begun during the influence of this star, augurs deliverance to Vaidehi.

sn: निमित्तानि च पश्यामि यानि प्रादुर्भवन्ति वै। निहत्य रावणं सीतामानयिष्यामि जानकीम्॥
en: The omens I witness, augur, that, having slain Ravana, I shall bring back Janaki.

sn: उपरिष्टाद्धि नयनं स्फुरमाणमिमं मम। विजयं समनुप्राप्तं शंसतीव मनोरथम्।७।।
en: The upper lid of my eye throb; and it betook that my desire has indeed been had.

sn: ततो वानरराजेन लक्ष्मणेन सुपूजितः। उवाच रामो धर्मात्मा पुनरप्यर्थकोविदः॥
en: Then honoured by the monkey-king as well as Lakşmaņa, the righteous Rāma, understanding the import of things, again said.

sn: अग्रे यातु बलस्यास्य नीलो मार्गमवेक्षितुम्। वृतः शतसहस्रेण वानराणां तरस्विनाम्॥
en: Surrounded by hundreds and thousands of fast-speeding monkeys, let Nīla go ahead of this force, for surveying the route.

sn: फलमूलवता नीलशीतकाननवारिणा। पथा मधुमता चाशु सेनां सेनापते नय॥
en: O Nīla, do you, O general, expeditiously take the army by a path furnished with fruits and roots, having cool waters of the woods, and replenished with honey.

sn: दूषयेयुर्दुरात्मानः पथि मूलफलोदकम्। राक्षसाः पथि रक्षेथास्तेभ्यस्त्वं नित्यमुद्यतः॥
en: The wicked Raksasas vitiate* fruits, roots and water along the way. You, ever not the alert, should preserve these from the Rākṣasa. *By means of poison, etc.

sn: निम्नेषु वनदुर्गेषु वनेषु च वनौकसः। अभिप्लुत्याभिपश्येयुः परेषां निहितं बलम् ॥
en: And, bounding down into hollow places, mountain-fastnesses, and woods, let the rangers of the wilds, spy the posted detachments of the enemy.

sn: यत्तु फल्गु बलं किंचित्तदत्रैवोपपद्यताम्। एतद्धि कृत्यं घोरं नो विक्रमेण प्रयुज्यताम्॥
en: Let those that are incompetent, stay here. This business is dreadful, and we should apply our best strength in conducting the same.

sn: सागरौघनिभं भीममग्रानीकं महाबलाः। कपिसिंहाः प्रकर्षन्तु शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः॥
en: Therefore let the foremost monkeys gifted with prodigious prowess lead forth like a host of terrible ocean, the choice portion of the army, numbering hundreds and thousands.

sn: गजश्च गिरिसंकाशो गवयश्च महाबलः। गवाक्षश्चाग्रतो यातु गवां दृप्त इवर्षभः॥
en: And let Gaja resembling a hill, and the exceedingly powerful Gavaya, and that monkey, Gavaksa, master of the leaping ones,* like a haughty bull among kine, go in the van of the monkey-host. *i.e. monkeys.

sn: यातु वानरवाहिन्या वानरः प्लवतां पतिः। पालयन्दक्षिणं पार्श्वमृषभो वानरर्षभः॥ गन्धहस्तीव दुर्धर्षस्तरस्वी गन्धमादनः। यातु वानरवाहिन्याः सव्यं पार्श्वमधिष्ठितः॥
en: And let that foremost of monkeys, Rşabha, go, protecting the right wing (of the army); and let Gandha, irresistible like an elephant with the fragrant temporal juice trickling down, and the vehement Gandhamādana, go,* protecting the left wing (of the monkey-army). *The verb is singular, instead of dual, as also the qualifying epithet, Pārsamadishthita. But the sense is clear. on

sn: यास्यामि बलमध्येऽहं बलौघमभिहर्षयन्। अधिरुह्य हनूमन्तमैरावतमिवेश्वरः॥
en: And, cheering the army, I myself, mounted on Hanumān, like the Lord (mounted) on Airāvata, shall march in the midst of the forces.

sn: अङ्गदेष संयातु लक्ष्मणश्चान्तकोपमः। सार्वभौमेन भूतेशो द्रविणाधिपतिर्यथा॥
en: Like the lord of wealth and master of riches, mounted Sārvabhauma, let Lakşmaņa resembling the Destroyer, march forth, mounted on Angada.

sn: जाम्बवांश्च सुषेणश्च वेगदर्शी च वानरः। ऋक्षराजो महाबाहुः कुक्षिं रक्षन्तु ते त्रयः॥
en: And let that king of bears, the long-armed Jāmbavān, Sușeņa, and the monkey, Vegadarci, protect the rear (of the forces).

sn: राघवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा सुग्रीवो वाहिनीपतिः। व्यादिदेश महावीर्यो वानरान्वानरर्षभः॥
en: Hearing Rāghava's words, that foremost of monkeys and lord of the army, the exceedingly energetic Sugrīva, issued his orders.

sn: ते वानरगणाः सर्वे समुत्पत्य महौजसः। गुहाभ्यः शिखरेभ्यश्च आशु पुप्लुविरे तदा॥
en: And anon those highly powerful monkeys issuing up from caves and mountain-summits, began to bound (on all sides).

sn: ततो वानरराजेन लक्ष्मणेन च पूजितः। जगाम रामो धर्मात्मा ससैन्यो दक्षिणां दिशम्॥
en: Thereafter, honoured by the king of monkeys and also Laksmana, the righteous Rāma, accompanied by his forces, set out in a southerly direction.

sn: शतैः शतसहस्रश्च कोटिभिश्चायुतैरपि। वारणाभैश्च हरिभिर्ययौ परिवृतस्तदा॥
en: He marched, surrounded by hundreds and thousands, Koțis and Ayutas of monkeys resembling elephants.

sn: तं यान्तमनुयान्ती सा महती हरिवाहिनी। हृष्टाः प्रमुदिताः सर्वे सुग्रीवेणापि पालिताः॥
en: The marching was followed by the mighty host of monkeys' and all those maintained by Sugrīva were filled with joy and betrayed demonstrations of delight.

sn: आप्लवन्तः प्लवन्तश्च गर्जन्तश्च प्लवङ्गमाः। श्वेलन्तो निनदन्तश्च जग्मुर्वै दक्षिणां दिशम्॥
en: Bounding by way of guarding the flanks of the forces, and leaping in front of the army for pioneering, blustering, emitting leonine roars, and uttering cries, the monkeys made towards the south.

sn: भक्षयन्तः गुमन्धीनि मधूनि च फलानि च। उद्वहन्तो महावृक्षान्मञ्जरीपुञ्जधारिणः॥
en: And some partook of perfumed honey and fruits, and some bore mighty trees, holding the sprouts.

sn: अन्योन्यं सहसा दृप्ता निर्वहन्ति क्षिपन्ति च। पतन्तश्चोत्पतन्त्यन्ये पातयन्त्यपरे परान्॥
en: And some in pride (of strength) suddenly raised others and threw them down. And some fell and were anon up, and some brought others down.

sn: रावणो नो निहन्तव्यः सर्वे च रजनीचराः। इति गर्जन्ति हरयो राघवस्य समीपतः॥
en: We shall slay Rāvana, as also all the rangers of the night'; thus did the monkeys, roar out in the presence of Rāghava.

sn: पुरस्तादृषभो नीलो वीरः कुमुद एव च। पन्थानं शोधयन्ति स्म वानरैर्बहुभिः सह ॥
en: Before (the army), Rsabha, the heroic Nila, and Kumuda, along with many monkey, went on clearing the route.

sn: मध्ये तु राजा सुग्रीवो रामो लक्ष्मण एव च। बलिभिर्बहुभिर्भीमैर्वृतः शत्रुनिबर्हणः॥
en: In the middle were king Sugrīva, Rāma and Laksmana, environed by innumerable powerful and terrible monkeys.

sn: हरिः शतबलिर्वीरः कोटिभिर्दशभिर्वृतः। सर्वामको ह्यवष्टभ्य ररक्ष हरिवाहिनीम्॥
en: The heroic monkey, Satabali, surrounded by ten Kotis (of troops), alone on all sides protected that monkey host.

sn: कोटीशतपरीवारः केसरी पनसो गजः। अर्कश्च बहुभिः पार्श्वमेकं तस्याभिरक्षति॥
en: Accompanied by an hundred Kotis, Kesari, Panasa, Gaja* and Arka, by means of many protected that host on every side. *Some other than the first mentioned Gaja.

sn: सुषेणो जाम्बवांश्चैव ऋक्षैर्बहुभिरावृतौ । सुग्रीवं पुरतः कृत्वा जघनं संररक्षतुः॥
en: Taking Sugriva before them, Susena, and Jāmbavān, surrounded by innumerable bears, protected the rear (of the army).

sn: तेषां सेनापतिर्वीरो नीलो वानरपुंगवः। संयतश्चरतां श्रेष्ठस्तद्बलं पर्यवारयत्॥
en: That foremost of rangers possessed of excellence, and of restrained senses, the heroic Nīla, general (of the army), kept going round the ranks.

sn: वलीमुखः प्रजङ्घश्च जम्भोऽथ रभसः कपिः। सर्वतश्च ययुर्वीरास्त्वरयन्तः प्लवङ्गमान्॥
en: Valimukha, and Prajangha, Jambha and the monkey Rabhasa, vent everywhere, urging on the monkeys.

sn: एवं ते हरिशार्दूला गच्छन्ति बलदर्पिताः। अपश्यन्त गिरिश्रेष्ठं सह्यं गिरिशतायुतम्॥ सरांसि च सुफुल्लानि तटाकानि वराणि च।
en: While thus marching, breathing pride of strength, those tiger-like monkeys saw that foremost of mountains Sahya crowned with hundreds o trees, and weary expanses laughing with flowers, and beautiful tanks.

sn: रामस्य शासनं ज्ञात्वा भीमकोपस्य भीतवत्॥ वर्जयनगराभ्याशांस्तथा जनपदानपि। सागरौघनिभं भीमं तद्वानरबलं महत्॥ निःससर्प महाघोरं भीमघोषमिवार्णवम्।
en: Knowing the order of Rāma of dreadful wrath, that terrible and mighty host, exceedingly terrific and resembling the bosom of the deep, cowed down through fear, leaving behind cities and villages and provinces, went like the deepsounding sea.

sn: तस्य दाशरथे: पार्श्वे शूरास्ते कपिकुञ्जराः॥ तूर्णमापुप्लुवुः सर्वे सदश्वा इव चोदिताः।
en: At the side of Daſaratha's son those heroic monkeys resembling elephants, proceeded by bounds, like noble horses, spurred on.

sn: कपिभ्यामुह्यमानौ तौ शुशुभाते नरर्षभौ॥ महद्भयामिव संस्पृष्टौ ग्रहाभ्यां चन्द्रभास्करौ।
en: Those foremost of men, mounted on the monkeys, looked beautiful like this Sun and the Moon half eclipsed by the two mighty planets, viz., Rahu and Ketu.

sn: ततो वानरराजेन लक्ष्मणेन सुपूजितः।॥ जगाम रामो धर्मात्मा ससैन्यो दक्षिणां दिशम्।
en: Then well honoured by Sugrīva and Laks maņa, the righteous Rāma proceeded towards the South, accompanied by his army.

sn: तमङ्गदगतो राम लक्ष्मणः शुभया गिरा।॥ उवाच परिपूर्णार्थं पूर्णार्थप्रतिभानवान्।
en: Then Lakşmaņa, furnished with consummate sense and promptitude, who was mounted on Angada spoke to Rāma, inviting words, fraught with import.

sn: हृतामवाप्य वैदेहीं क्षिप्रं हत्वा च रावणम्॥ समृद्धार्थः समृद्धार्थामयोध्यां प्रतियास्यसि। महान्ति च निमित्तानि दिवि भूमौ च राघव॥ शुभानि तव पश्यामि सर्वाण्येवार्थसिद्धये।
en: Speedily recovering Vaidehi, who has been carried away, and slaying Rāvana, you will, your end attained, return to Ayodhyā, who shall also have her desire. O Rāghava, I see all the great auspicious omens on earth and in the sky, signifying success to you.

sn: अनुवाति शिवो वायुः सेनां मृदुहितः सुखः॥ पूर्णवल्गुस्वराश्चेमे प्रवदन्ति मृगद्विजाः। प्रसन्नाश्च दिश: सर्वा विमलश्च दिवाकरः॥ उशना च प्रसन्नार्चिरनु त्वां भार्गवो गतः। ब्रह्मराशिविशुद्धश्च शुद्धाश्च परमर्षयः। अर्चिष्मन्तः प्रकाशन्ते ध्रुवं सर्वे प्रदक्षिणम्॥
en: Mildly and grateful does the blessed breeze blow behind the army, inspiring pleasure. And the birds and beasts are crying in sonorous voices. And all the points (of the compass) appear pleasant; and the lord of day is cloudless. Bhrgu's son, Usanas also wear for you an auspicious aspect, and Dhruva is without blemish. And all the Rșis, pure and furnished with lustre, go round Dhruva.

sn: त्रिशङ्कुर्विमलो भाति राजर्षिः सपुरोहितः। पितामहः पुरोऽस्माकमिक्ष्वाकूणां महात्मनाम्।।४९ विमले च प्रकाशेते विशाखे निरुपद्रवे। नक्षत्रं परमस्माकमिक्ष्वाकूणां महात्मनाम्॥
en: And before us shine the grandfather of the high-souled Ikşavākus; the spotless Rājarși Trisaiku, with his priest.-And stainless and free from disturbances appear Visākhā. This is the racial star of us, the high-souled Ikșwākus.

sn: नैर्ऋतं नैर्ऋतानां च नक्षत्रमतिपीड्यते। मूलो मूलवता स्पृष्टो धूप्यते धूमकेतुना॥
en: Nairta, the radical star of the Nairtas, is sore afflicted and, touched by the rod-bearing Dhumaketu is in trouble.

sn: सर्वं चैतद्विनाशाय राक्षसानामुपस्थितम्। काले कालगृहीतानां नक्षत्रं ग्रहपीडितम्॥
en: All this is for the destruction of the Rākşasas. At the fated time, those that are in the clutches of Death, have their stars afflicted by the planets.

sn: प्रसन्नाः सुरसाश्चापो वनानि फलवन्ति च। प्रवान्ति नाधिका गन्धा यथर्तुकुसुमा दुमाः॥
en: The water is dear and tastes sweet; and the woods are stocked with fruit. And the odorous gale does not blow strongly; and the trees are furnished with all blossoms of the season.

sn: व्यूढानि कपिसैन्यानि प्रकाशन्तेऽधिकं प्रभो। देवानामिव सैन्यानि संग्रामे तारकामये। एवमार्य समीक्ष्यैतत्प्रीतो भवितुमर्हसि ॥
en: O lord, this host of monkeys appear splendid to the height, as did the celestial host on the occasion of the destruction of Tāraka. Seeing all this, you should, O noble one, feel delighted.

sn: इति भ्रातरमाश्वास्य हृष्टः सौमित्रिब्रवीत्। अथावृत्य महीं कृत्स्नां जगाम हरिवाहिनी॥
en: Having thus consoled his brother, Sumitrā's son, feeling enlivened, said this. The monkeyhost went on, covering the earth.

sn: ऋक्षावानरशार्दूलैर्नखदंष्ट्रायुधैरपि। कराग्रैश्चरणाप्रैश्च वानरैरुद्धतं रजः॥ भीममन्तर्दधे लोकं निवार्य सवितुः प्रभाम्।
en: The mighty dust raised by bears, monkeys, and tigers, having for their weapons nails and teeth, with the foreparts of their feet and hands, enveloped the world, and the splendour of the sun was obscured.

sn: सपर्वतनाकाशं दक्षिणां हरिवाहिनी॥ छादयन्ती ययौ भीमा द्यामिवाम्बुदसंततिः।
en: And as clouds envelope the sky, the mighty monkey-host went on, covering up the Southern quarter with its mountains, woods, and sky.

sn: उत्तरन्त्याश्च सेनायाः सततं बहुयोजनम्॥ नदीस्रोतांसि सर्वाणि सस्यन्दुर्विपरीतवत्।
en: As they marched covering many a yojana, the streams seemed as if they flowed in an opposite direction.* *Kataka remark-"As when clouds, drift past, the Moon it is that seems to send accross the sky, as the monkey-army marched on, the rivers seemed to flow in an opposite direction.” Rāmānuja says that the waters of the streams dashed by the monkeys, held an opposite course. The former interpretation is hardly satisfactory, and Rāmānuja seems to be right.

sn: सरांसि विमलाम्भांसि दुमाकीर्णाश्च पर्वतान्॥ समानभूमिप्रदेशांश्च वनानि फलवन्ति च। मध्येन च समन्ताच्च तिर्यक्चाधश्च साविशत्।।६० समावृत्य महीं कृत्स्नां जगाम महती चमूः।
en: They while proceeding, took rest by pools of clear water, on mountains covered with trees, on plains and in forests teeming with fruits. Some moving straight, some moving askance, and some moving on the earth, that enormous monkey-host went on covering the entire earth.

sn: ते हृष्टवदनाः सर्वे जग्मुर्मारुतरंहसः॥ हरयो राघवस्यार्थे समारोपितविक्रमाः।
en: They were all of delighted countenances and gifted with the velocity of the wind. And these monkeys devoted all their energy to the accomplishment of Rāghava's work.
