sn: हर्ष वीर्य बलोद्रेकान्दर्शयन्तः परस्परम्॥ यौवनोत्सेकजादपद्विविधांश्चक्रुध्वनि।
en: They were displaying to each other their joy, prowess and energy. And influenced with the vanity of youth they set up diverse cries.

sn: तत्र केचिद्भुतं जग्मुरुत्पेतुश्च तथापरे॥ केचित्किलकिलां चक्रुर्वानरा वनगोचराः। प्रास्फोटयंश्च पुच्छानि संनिजघ्नुः पदान्यपि॥
en: Some proceeded with speed, some leaped, some set up cries expressing joy, some were uplifting their tails, and some were striking the ground with their feet.

sn: भुजान्विक्षिप्य शैलांश्च दुमानन्ये बभञ्जिरे। आरोहन्तश्च शृङ्गाणि गिरीणां गिरिगोचराः॥
en: Some, stretching forth their arms, were breaking the hills, and others the trees. And other were ascending the tops of the hills.

sn: महानादान्प्रमुञ्चन्ति क्ष्वेडामन्ये प्रचक्रिरे। ऊरुवेगैश्च ममृदुर्लताजालान्यनेकशः।॥
en: Some began to make terrible sounds, and other made a tingling noise. And many others blasted the creepers with the velocity of their thighs.

sn: जम्भमाणाश्च विक्रान्ता विचिक्रीडुः शिलानुमैः। ततः शतसहस्रैश्च कोटिभिश्च सहस्रशः॥ वानराणां सुघोराणां श्रीमत्परिवृता मही।
en: Some were engaged in sporting with trees and rocks. And thus was the earth enveloped with millions and koțis of fearful monkeys.

sn: सा स्म याति दिवारानं महती हरिवाहिनी॥ प्रहृष्टमुदिताः सर्वे सुग्रीवेणाभिपालिताः। वानरास्त्वरिता यान्ति सर्वे युद्धाभिनन्दिनः। प्रमोक्षयिषवः सीतां मुहूर्त क्वापि नावसन्॥
en: Thus the enormous monkey host went on day and night. And all those monkeys, delighted, guided by Sugrīva, and taking delight in battle, went on speedily. And they did not take rest even for a moment, desirous of rescuing Sītā.

sn: ततः पादपसंबाधं नानावनसमायुतम्। सह्यपर्वतमासाद्य वानरास्ते समारुहन्।७० ।।
en: Thereupon, getting at the mount Sahya covered with various trees and forests, those monkeys ascended it.

sn: काननानि विचित्राणि नदीप्रस्रवणानि च। पश्यन्नपि ययौ रामः सह्यस्य मलयस्य च॥
en: Rāma went on beholding the variegated forest, rivers and fountains of the mount Sahya and Malaya.

sn: चम्पकांस्तिलकांचूतान्प्रसेकान्सिन्दुवारकान्। तिनिशान्करवीरांश्च भजन्ति स्म प्लवङ्गमाः॥ अशोकांश्च करांश्च प्लक्षन्यग्रोधपादपान्। जम्बुकामलकानागन्भजन्ति स्म प्लवङ्गमाः॥
en: Those monkeys broke down various treesCampakas, Tilakas, mangoes, Prasekas, Sinduvaras, Tinisas and Karaviras, Asokas, Karanjas, Plaksas, Nyagrodhas, Jambukas and Amalakas.

sn: प्रस्तरेषु च रम्येषु विविधाः काननद्रुमाः। वायुवेगप्रचलिताः पुष्पैरवकिरन्ति तान्॥
en: And seated on picturesque rocks, various forest trees, shaken by the wind, showered flowers on them.

sn: मारुतः सुखसंस्पर्शो वाचि चन्दनशीतलः। षट्पदैरनुकूजद्भिर्वनेषु मधुगन्धिषु ॥
en: There blew in those forests filled with the smell of honey, a wind of pleasant touch, cool as the Moon, accompanied by the hummings of the bees.

sn: अधिकं शैलराजस्तु धातुभिस्तु विभूषितः। धातुभ्यः प्रसृतो रेणुर्वायुवेगेन घट्टितः॥ सुमहद्वानरानीकं छादयामास सर्वतः।
en: That mount was richly embellished with diverse metals. And dust issuing from these metals and thickened by the air, enveloped on all sides the huge monkey-host.

sn: गिरिप्रस्थेषु रम्येषु सर्वतः संप्रपुष्पिताः।७७।। केतक्यः सिन्दुवाराश्च वासन्त्यश्च मनोरमाः। माधव्यो गन्धपूर्णाश्च कुन्दगुल्माश्च पुष्पिताः।७८।। चिरिबिल्वा मधूकाश्च वंजुला बकुलास्तथा। रञ्जकास्तिलकाश्चैव नागवृक्षाश्च पुष्पिताः। ७९ ।। चूताः पाटलिकाश्चैव कोविदाराश्च पुष्पिताः। मुचुलिन्दार्जुनाश्चैव शिंशपाः कुटजास्तथा ॥ हिन्तालास्तिनिशाश्चैव चूर्णका नीपकास्तथा। नीलाशोकाश्च सरला अङ्कोलाः पद्मकास्तथा॥
en: There blossomed in that picturesque mountain-vale Ketakis, Sinduvāras, beautiful Vasantis, Madhavis, Gandhapurnas, Kundas, Cirivilvas, Madhūkas, Vañjulas, Bakulas, Ranjakas, Tilakas, Nagas, mangoes, Patalikas, Kovidāras, Muculindas, Arjunas, “insapas, Kutajas, Hintālas, Tinisas, Curnakas, Nipakas, Nila-asokas, Saralas, Ankolas and lotuses.

sn: प्रीयमाणैः प्लवङ्गैस्तु सर्वे प्रयाकुलीकृताः। वाप्यस्तस्मिनिगरौ रम्याः पल्वलानि तथैव च।॥ चक्रवाकानुचारिताः कारण्डवनिषेविताः। प्लवैः क्रौञ्चैश्च संकीर्णा वराहमृगसेविताः॥ ऋक्षस्तरक्षुभिः सिंहै: शार्दूलश्च भयावहैः। व्यालैश्च बहुभिर्भीमैः सेव्यमानाः समन्ततः।॥ पद्मः सौगन्धिकैः फुल्लैः कुमुदैश्चौत्पलैस्तथा। वारिजैविविधैः पुष्पै रम्यास्तन जलाशयाः॥
en: All these trees were greatly disturbed by those monkeys, delighted with their view. There were in that mountain many a picturesque lake and pond filled with Cakravākas and Kārandavas, ducks, Krauñcas and the mount abounded on all sides with boars, deer, and terrible bears, lions and tigers and various other fearful animals, and it was beautified with full blown lotuses, Jilies, Utpalas and various other fragrant trees growing in the water.

sn: तस्य सानुषु कूजन्ति नानाद्विजगणास्तथा। स्नात्वा पीत्वोदकान्यत्र जलेक्रीडन्ति वानराः॥
en: Various birds set up their musical choir on the summit of that mount. And bathing and drinking, these monkeys sported in the water.

sn: अन्योन्यं प्लावयन्ति स्म शैलमारुह्य वानराः। फलान्यमृतगन्धीनि मूलानि कुसुमानि च।८७।। बभञ्जुर्वानरास्तत्र पादपानां मदोत्कटाः। द्रोणमात्रप्रमाणानि लम्बमानानि वानराः॥ ययुः पिबन्तः स्वस्थास्ते मधूनि मधुपिङ्गलाः। पादपानवभञ्जन्तो विकर्षन्तस्तथा लताः॥ विधमन्तो गिरिवरान्प्रययुः प्लवगर्षभाः। वृक्षेभ्योऽन्ये तु कपयो नदन्तो मधुदर्पिताः॥ अन्ये वृक्षान्प्रपद्यन्ते प्रपिबन्त्यपि चापरे। बभूव वसुधा तैस्तु संपूर्णा हरिपुङ्गवैः । यथा कलमकेदारैः पक्वैरिव वसुंधरा ॥
en: Ascending the mount these monkeys continually bounded. And excited with drink, they crumbled into pieces the ambrosia-smelling fruits, roots and flowers of the trees. And those monkeys yellow as honey, delighted, feasted on mangoes, long and measuring a Drona. Breaking down the trees, blasting the creepers, bounding from one tree to another and making the mount Sahya echo, those leading monkeys went on delighted and excited with drink. Some ascending the trees, and others drinking, the whole earth was enveloped with those monkeys, and seemed as if beautified with ripe paddy crops.

sn: महेन्द्रमथ संप्राप्य रामो राजीवलोचनः। आरुरोह महाबाहुः शिखरं दुमभूषितम्॥
en: And reaching the mount Mahendra, the largearmed Rāma, having eyes like lotuses, ascended the summit adorned with diverse trees.

sn: ततः शिखरमारुह्य रामो दशरथात्मजः। कूर्ममीनसमाकीर्णमपश्यत्सलिलाकुलम्॥
en: Getting at the top, Daśaratha's son espied the vast deep filled with tortoises and fishes.

sn: ते सह्यं समतिक्रम्य मलयं च महागिरिम्। आसेदुरानुपूर्येण समुद्रं भीमनिःस्वनम्। ॥
en: There upon, passing by the mounts Sahya and Malaya and arranging their enormous host, they* by and by reached the roaring deep. *The monkey leader.

sn: अवरुह्य जगामाशु वेलावमनुत्तमम्। रामो रमयतां श्रेष्ठः ससुग्रीवः सलक्ष्मणः॥
en: And descending therefore, Rāma, the foremost of those who minister happiness to all, accompanied by Lakṣmaṇa and Sugrīva, entered the forest situate on the banks of the ocean.

sn: अथ धौतोपलतलां तोयौधैः सहसोत्थितैः। वेलामासाद्य विपुलां रामो वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Reaching the expansive banks having rocks there on and continually washed by the rising billow, Rāma spoke these words.

sn: एते वयमनुप्राप्ताः सुग्रीव वरुणालयम्। इहेदानी विचिन्ता सा या नः पूर्वमुपस्थिता॥
en: O Sugrīva we have arrived at the abode of Varuņa. Now has arisen in my mind what I had not thought of before.

sn: अतः परमतीरोऽयं सागरः सरितां पतिः। च चायमनुपायेन शक्यस्तरितुमर्णवः॥
en: This ocean, the lord of the streams, whose other side is not seen, cannot be crossed over without some excellent measure.

sn: तदिहैव निवेशोऽस्तु मन्त्रः प्रस्तूयतामिह । यथेदं वानरबलं परं पारमवाप्नुयात्॥
en: Let the monkey-host be encamped here therefore, and then concert a plan by means of which they might get at the other side.

sn: इतीव स महाबाहुः सीताहरणकर्शितः। रामः सागरमासाद्य वासमाज्ञापयत्तदा॥
en: And reaching the shores of the ocean, the large-armed Rāma, stricken with grief for Sītā, ordered their encampment, saying.

sn: सर्वाः सेना निवेश्यन्तां वेलायां हरिपुङ्गव। संप्राप्तो मन्त्रकालो नः सागरस्येह लङ्घने॥
en: O foremost of monkeys, do you encamp your host on the bring of the ocean. Now has arrived the hour for counsel, when we should devise some plan for crossing over the main.

sn: स्वां स्वां सेनां समुत्सृज्य मा च कश्चित्कुतो व्रजेत्। गच्छन्तु वानराः शूरा ज्ञेयं छन्नं भयं च नः॥
en: I fear the Rākşasas at every step, for they are greatly illusion creating, let the leaders therefore go to their own hosts and let them not proceed anywhere else, renouncing them.

sn: रामस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा सुग्रीवः सहलक्ष्मणः। सेनां निवेशयत्तीरे सागरस्य दुमायुते॥
en: Hearing the words of Rama, Sugrīva along with Lakşmana, encamped the army on the brink of the ocean, covered with trees.

sn: विरराज समीपस्थं सागरस्य त तद्बलम्। मदुपाण्डुजलः श्रीमान्द्वितीय इव सागरः॥
en: Stationed near the main, the monkey-host in consequence of their resemblance in colour with blue contents of the deep, looked like a second ocean.

sn: वेलावनमुपागम्य ततस्ते हरिपुङ्गवाः। निविष्टाश्च परं पारं काङ्माणा महोदधेः॥
en: There upon, reaching the shore, those leading monkeys engaged in concerning a plan to cross over the vastly deep.

sn: तेषां निविशमानानां सैन्यसंनाहनिःस्वनः। अन्तर्धाय महानादमर्णवस्य प्रशुश्रुवे॥
en: The tumult, of that monkey-host encamped there, was heard above the roaring of the deep.

sn: सा वानराणां ध्वजिनी सुग्रीवेणाभिपालिता। त्रिधा निविष्टा महती रामस्यार्थपराभवत्॥
en: That huge army of the monkeys commanded by Sugrīva, and set up in three divisions, were deeply concerned with the accomplishment of Rāma's work.

sn: सा महार्णवमासाद्य हृष्टा वानरवाहिनी। वायुवेगसमाधूतं पश्यमाना महार्णवम्॥
en: And reaching the shore of the vastly deep, that monkey host, delighted, beheld the ocean moved by the Wind.

sn: दूरपारमसंबाधं रक्षोगणनिषेवितम्। पश्यन्तो वरुणावासं निषेदुहरियूथपाः॥ चण्डनक्रग्राहघोरं क्षपादौ दिवसक्षये। हसन्तमिव फेनैधैर्नृत्यन्तमिव चोर्मिभिः॥ चन्द्रोदये समुद्भूतं प्रतिचन्द्रसमाकुलम्। चण्डानिलमहाग्राहै: कीर्णं तिमितिमिङ्गिलैः॥
en: They waited there beholding the deep of unimpeded expanse, having its distant shore inhabited by the demons, and thronged with various aquatic animals. While up heaving its foam on the approach of eve, it appeared laughing and setting up its surges, it appeared to dance. It increased with the rising of the Moon and he reflected himself on its breast.

sn: दीप्तभोगैरिवाकीर्णं भुजङ्गैर्वरुणालयम्। अवगाढं महासत्त्वैर्नानाशैलसमाकुलम्॥ सुदुर्गं दुर्गमार्ग तमगाधमसुरालयम्। मकरैर्नागभोगैश्च विगाढा वातलोलिताः।। उत्पेतुश्च निपेतुश्च प्रहृष्टा जलराशयः॥ अग्निचूर्णमिवाविद्धं भास्वराम्बुमहोरगम्। सुरारिनिलयं घोरं पातालविषयं सदा॥ सागरं चाम्बरप्रख्यमम्बरं सागरोपमम्। सागरं चाम्बरं चेति निर्विशेषमदृश्यत॥
en: That abode of Varuna was infested with gigantic sharks, whales and Timingalas, disturbed with the fury of the Wind, filled with serpents having flaming frames, and various aquatic animals and rocks, and was fathomless deep. It had picturesque fortresses on its marge and its other shore was hard to get at. And the Makarasand serpents living therein were moved by the Wind. The waters, as if delighted, were rising and falling. And having serpents of flaming frames underneath, it appeared as if sprinkled with scintillations of fire. And that terrible abode of the demons extended down to the regions inhabited by the Nāgas or serpents. The deep resembled the welkin and the welkin the deep, and there appeared no difference between them. 1. A large fabulous fish. 2. A marine monster confounded usually with the crocodile and shark.

sn: संपृक्तं नभसाप्यम्भः संपृक्तं च नभोऽम्भसा। तादृग्रूपे स्म दृश्येते तारारत्नसमाकुले॥
en: The sky crested with stars and the deep filled with gems resembled each other.

sn: समुत्पतितमेघस्य वीचिमालाकुलस्य च। विशेषो न द्वयोरासीत्सागरस्याम्बरस्य च॥
en: They sky enveloped with clouds and the ocean overflowing with surges presented no contrast whatsoever.

sn: अन्योन्यैराहताः सक्ताः सस्वनुर्भीमनिःस्वनाः। ऊर्मयः सिन्धुराजस्य महाभेर्य इवाम्बरे॥
en: The waves of the mighty deep beating at each other continually, set up a sound resembling that of a trumpet in the sky.

sn: रत्नौघजलसंनादं विषक्तमिव वायुना। उत्पतन्तमिव क्रुद्धं यादोगणसमाकुलम्॥
en: It was filled with diverse gems and its water was poisoned by means of the air. It was filled with various aquatic animals, and up heaving its billows, it appeared as if excited with ire.

sn: ददृशुस्ते महात्मानो वाताहतजलाशयम्। अनिलोद्भूतमाकाशे प्रलपन्तमिवोर्मिभिः॥
en: There beheld those high-souled monkeys the mighty main agitated by the Wind and muttering as if with the Upheaval of the waves.

sn: ततो विस्मयमापन्ना हरयो ददृशुः स्थिताः। भ्रान्तोर्मिजालसंनादं प्रलोलमिव सागरम्॥
en: There upon, overwhelmed with surprise, those monkeys, stationed there, espied the main brimming with rolling waters and moving as if (off its place).

sn: सा तु नीलेन विधिवत्स्वारक्षा सुसमाहिता। सागरस्योत्तरे तीरे साधु सा विनिवेशिता॥
en: There on the northern shore of the ocean the army was encamped and arranged in order by Nila.

sn: मैन्दश्च द्विविदश्चोभौ तत्र वानरपुङ्गवौ। विचेरतुश्च तां सेनां रक्षार्थं सर्वतो दिशम्॥
en: The two leading monkeys Mainda and Dvivida patrolled about on all sides to protect the monkey host.

sn: निविष्टायां तु सेनायां तीरे नदनदीपतेः। पार्श्वस्थं लक्ष्मणं दृष्ट्वा रामो वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: The army being encamped on the shore of the lord of streams and rivers, Rāma, beholding Laksmana by his side, spoke, saying.

sn: शोकश्च किल कालेन गच्छता ह्यपगच्छति। मम चापश्यतः कान्तामहन्यहनि वर्धते॥
en: I know that grief abates as time passes by, but my sorrow arising from the separation of my spouse, is increasing day by day.

sn: न मे दुःखं प्रिया दूरे न मे दुःखं हृतेति च। एतदेवानुशोचामि वयोऽस्या ह्यतिवर्तते॥
en: I am not sorry that she has been stealthily taken away by the demon-but my sorrow is that her end is drawing high.

sn: वाहि वात यतः कान्ता तां स्पृष्ट्वा मामपि स्पृश। त्वयि मे गात्रसंस्पर्शश्चन्द्रे दृष्टिसमागमः॥
en: O Wind, do you go there where my dear spouse is, and touching her person, do you touch me, for I shall then be happy stationing my looks in the Moon and being touched by you.

sn: तन्मे दहति गात्राणि विषं पीतमिवाशये। हा नाथेति प्रिया सा मां ह्रियमाणा यदब्रवीत्॥
en: Alas! my dear one cried 'O lord, O lord' when she was taken away. Those words, revolving burn me like poison.

sn: तद्वियोगेन्धनवता तच्चिन्ताविमलार्चिषा। रात्रिंदिवं शरीरं मे दह्यते मदनाग्निा॥
en: I am now being burnt down day and night by the fire of desire, having separation from her for its fuel and her thoughts for its flame.

sn: अवगाह्यार्णवं स्वप्स्ये सौमित्रे भवता विना। एवं च प्रज्वलन्कामो न मां सुप्तं जले दहेत्॥
en: Leaving you, O Son of Sumitrā, I shall jump into the deep and then shall not this fire burn me any more.

sn: बह्वेतत्कामयानस्य शक्यमेतेन जीवितुम्। यदहं सा च वामोरूरेका धरणिमाश्रितौ॥
en: This is my only consolation, for which I draw my vital breath-that myself and she breathe on the same earth.

sn: केदारस्येव केदारः सोदकस्य निरूदकः। उपस्नेहेन जीवामि जीवन्तीं यच्छृणोमि ताम्॥
en: Like to a dry land drawing water from a watered ground, I do live, hearing that Janaki still survives.

sn: कदा नु खलु सुश्रोणीं शतपत्रायतेक्षणाम्। विजित्य शत्रून्द्रक्ष्यामि सीतां स्फीतामिव श्रियम्॥
en: When shall I, discomfiting my enemies, behold Sītā, having a beautiful waist and eyes resembling lotus-petals, as a victorious hero behold the royal Grace.

sn: कदा सुचारुदन्तोष्ठं तस्याः पद्ममिवाननम्। ईषदुनाम्य पास्यामि रसायनमिवातुरः॥
en: Like to the sick drinking the elixir of life, when shall I, raising a little her lotus-like countenance having graceful teeth and lips, imprint kisses thereon?

sn: तौ तस्याः सहितौ पीनौ स्तनौ तालफलोपमौ। कदा नु खलु सोत्कम्पौ हसन्त्या मां भजिष्यतः॥
en: When shall she, laughing, embrace me with her rising breast resembling the palm fruit?

sn: सा नूनमसितापाङ्गी रक्षोमध्यगता सती। मन्नाथा नाथहीनेव त्रातारं नाधिगच्छति॥
en: Alas that chaste dame having scarlet corners of the eye, being encircled by the demons, is wishing for a protector like to one having no husband, albeit having a husband in me.

sn: कथं जनकराजस्य दुहिता मम च प्रिया। राक्षसीमध्यगा शेते स्नुषा दशरथस्य च ॥
en: How fare in the midst of the shc-demons, that daughter of the king Janaka, my beloved spouse, and the daughter-in-law of king Dasaratha?

sn: अविक्षोभ्याणि रक्षांसि सा विधूयोत्पतिष्यति। विधूय जलदानीलाञ्छशिलेखा शरत्स्विव॥
en: And having those Rākṣasas, hard to repress, slain by me, truly shall she appear like to the rays of the Moon extricated from sable autumnal clouds.

sn: स्वभावतनुका नूनं शोकेनानशनेन च। भूयस्तनुतरा सीता देशकालविपर्ययात्॥
en: Sītā is constitutionally slender, and forsooth, she has been greatly reduced by sorrow, fasting and calamities touching time and place.

sn: कदा नु राक्षसेन्द्रस्य निधायोरसि सायकान्। शोकं प्रत्याहरिष्यामि शोकमुत्सृज्य मानसम्॥
en: When shall I, piercing with my shafts the breast of the lord of Raksasas, renounce my mind's grief?

sn: कदा नु खलु मे साध्वी सीतामरसुतोपमा। सोत्कण्ठा कण्ठमालम्ब्य मोक्ष्यत्यानन्दजं जलम्॥
en: When shall my devoted Sītā resembling the daughter of a celestial, fling herself anxiously around my neck and shed tears of joy?

sn: कदा शोकमिमं घोरं मैथिलीविप्रयोगजम्। सहसा विप्रमोक्ष्यामि वासः शुक्लेतरं यथा॥
en: When shall I renounce this my sorrow arising out of Maithili's separation, like to one casting off his soiled clothes?

sn: एवं विलपतस्तस्य तत्र रामस्य धीमतः। दिनक्षयान्मन्दवपुर्भास्करोऽस्तमुपागतः॥
en: The highly intelligent Rāma bewailing thus, the day passed away and the Sun, decreasing gradually, disappeared at last.

sn: आश्वासितो लक्ष्मणेन रामः संध्यामुपासत। स्मरन्कमलपत्राक्षी सीतां शोकाकुलीकृतः॥
en: And consoled by Laksmana, Rama, stricken with thought touching Sītā having eyes like lotus-petals, engaged in rites relating to the worship of Eve.

sn: लङ्कायां तु कृतं कर्म घोरं दृष्ट्वा भयावहम्। राक्षसेन्द्रो हनुमता शक्रेणेव महात्मना। अब्रवीद्राक्षसान्सर्वान्हिया किंचिदवाङ्मुखः॥
en: Beholding in Lankā that dreadful and aweinspiring work performed by Hanuman like to the high-souled Sakra, the lord of Raksasas, looking down with shame, addressed them all, saying.

sn: धर्षिता च प्रविष्टा च लङ्का दुष्प्रसहा पुरी। तेन वानरमात्रेण दृष्टा सीता च जानकी॥
en: That monkey alone has invaded and entered the city of Lankā hard to reach and has espied Sītā, the daughter of king Janaka.

sn: प्रासादो धर्षितश्चैत्यः प्रवरा राक्षसा हताः। आविला च पुरी लङ्का सर्वा हनुमता कृता॥
en: He has shattered the palace, and the altar of sacrifice, slain the leading Raksasas, and, in short, agitated the whole city of Lankā.

sn: किं करिष्यामि भद्रं वः किं वो युक्तमनन्तरम्। उच्यतां नः समर्थ यत्कृतं च सुकृतं भवेत्॥
en: What shall I do now? And what should you all do one this occasion? It behove you all go give me such counsel as become me and will conduce to my glory.

sn: मन्त्रमूलं च विजयं प्रवदन्ति मनस्विनः। तस्माद्वै रोचये मन्त्रं रामं प्रति महाबलाः॥
en: 'Victory is the outcome of consultation'-this do the sages* say. Let us, therefore, O mighty ones, engage in counsel, relating to the measures we should adopt towards Rāma. * Manasvin, according to Rāmānuja, means hero.

sn: विविधाः : पुरुषा लोके उत्तमाधममध्यमाः। तेषां तु समवेतानां गुणदोषौ वदाम्यहम्॥
en: There are three orders of men on this earththe superior, the middling and the inferior. This distinction cannot be perceived without a knowledge of the signs, and so I shall relate to you their merits and demerits.

sn: मन्त्रस्त्रिभिर्हि संयुक्तः समर्थैर्मन्त्रनिर्णये। मित्रैर्वापि समानार्थैर्बान्धवैरपि वाधिकैः॥ सहितो मन्त्रयित्वा यः कर्मारम्भान्प्रवर्तयेत्। दैवे च कुरुते यत्नं तमाहुः पुरुषोत्तमम् ॥
en: He is said to belong to the superior order, whose counsel contains the three signs (mentioned below), or who engages in works after consulting duly with friends capable or with persons having the same end in view, and some times with others, and who serve Providence.

sn: एकोऽर्थं विमृशेदेको धर्मे प्रकुरुते मनः। एकः कार्याणि कुरुते तमाहुर्मध्यमं नरम्॥
en: He belongs to the middle order who consults his own self only, depends on the Providence, and engages alone in works.

sn: गुणदोषौ न निश्चित्य त्यक्त्वा दैवव्यपाश्रयम्। करिष्यामीति यः कार्यमुपेक्षेत्स नराधमः॥
en: He belongs to the inferior order who engage in works without ascertaining their merits or demerits, disregarding the will of the Providence and saying, 'I will do this,' and is inactive (at last).

sn: यथेमे पुरुषा नित्यमुत्तमाधममध्यमाः। एवं मन्त्रोऽपि विज्ञेय उत्तमाधममध्यमः॥
en: And counsels are also divided into three divisions like to the three orders of men (mentioned).

sn: ऐकमत्यमुपागम्य शास्त्रदृष्टेन चक्षुषा। मन्त्रिणो यत्र निरतास्तमाहुर्मन्त्रमुत्तमम्॥
en: That counsel belongs to the superior order in which the counsellors with their judgement reinforced by a knowledge of political ethics, are unanimous.

sn: बह्वीरपि मतीर्गत्वा मन्त्रिणामर्थनिर्णयः। पुनर्यत्रैकतां प्राप्तः स मन्त्रो मध्यमः स्मृतः॥
en: That one belongs to the middle order in which the counsellors after varied discussion, arrive at unanimity in the long run.

sn: अन्योन्यमतिमास्थाय यत्र संप्रतिभाष्यते। न चैकमत्ये श्रेयोऽस्ति मन्त्रः सोऽधम उच्यते॥
en: That one is the worst in which the counsellors differ from each other and agree a little in the long run, with no good result.

sn: तस्मात्सुमन्त्रितं साधु भवन्तो मतिसत्तमाः। कार्य संप्रतिपद्यन्तामेतत्कृत्यं मतं मम॥
en: You are all gifted with good intellects: do you all unanimously settle as to what become me and conduce to my well-being.

sn: वानराणां हि धीराणां सहस्त्रैः परिवारितः। रामोऽभ्येति पुरीं लङ्कामस्माकमुपरोधकः॥
en: Environed by a thousand of patient monkeys, Rāma, with a view to capture our city, is approaching towards Lankā.

sn: तरिष्यति च सुव्यक्तं राघवः सागरं सुखम्। तरसा युक्तरूपेण सानुजः सबलानुगः॥
en: Forsooth, shall he cross over the main along with his younger brother and a mighty host.

sn: समुद्रमुच्छोषयति वीर्येणान्यत्करोति वा। तस्मिन्नेवंविधे कार्ये विरुद्ध वानरैः सह।। हितं पुरे च सैन्ये च सर्व संमन्त्र्यतां मम ॥
en: He can by his prowess dry up the ocean and do the other.* Rāma approaching thus with a hostile intention along with the monkeys, it behove you to devise such means as might protect my city and army. *i.e. bridge over the ocean.

sn: इत्युक्ता राक्षसेन्द्रेण राक्षसास्ते महाबलाः। ऊचुः प्राञ्जलयः सर्वे रावणं राक्षसेश्वरम्॥ द्विषत्पक्षमविज्ञाय नीतिबाह्यास्त्वबुद्धयः।
en: Being thus accosted by their lord, the highly powerful Rākşasas, devoid of good sense and ignorant of sound counsel, replied with folded palms, saying.

sn: राजन्परिघशक्त्यष्टिशूलपट्टिशकुन्तलम्॥ सुमहन्नो बलं कस्माद्विषादं भजते भवान्।
en: You have, o king, enough of soldiers and various types of weapons like parighas saktis etc. Why are you smitten with sorrow then?

sn: त्वया भोगवतीं मत्वा निर्जिताः पन्नगा युधि ॥ कैलासशिखरावासी यक्षैर्बहुभिरावृतः। सुमहत्कदनं कृत्वा वश्यस्ते धनदः कृतः॥
en: Repairing to Bhagavatī, you did discomfit the serpents in battle. The God of Death, living on mount Kailasa, encircled by Yaksas, was subjugated by you in a great battle.

sn: स महेश्वरसख्येन श्लाघमानस्त्वया विभो। निर्जितः समरे रोषाल्लोकपालो महाबलः॥
en: That mighty lord of men, proud of his friendship with Śiva, was defeated by you wrathfully in battle.

sn: विनिपात्य च यक्षौघान्विक्षोभ्य विनिगृह्य च। त्वया कैलासशिखराद्विमानमिदमाहृतम्॥
en: Discomfiting and slaying the band of Yaksas, you did bring this flowery car from the mount Kailasa.

sn: मयेन दानवेन्द्रेण त्वद्भयात्सख्यमिच्छता। दुहिता तव भार्यार्थ दत्ता राक्षसपुङ्गव।७।।
en: O lord of Rākşasas, desiring your friendship out of fear, Maya, the king of Danavas, offered you his daughter for your spouse.

sn: दानवेन्द्रो महाबाहो वीर्योत्सिक्तो दुरासदः। विगृह्य वशमानीतः कुम्भीनस्याः सुखावहः॥
en: O you of mighty arms, you did bring under your subjection the powerful and irrepressible Dänava for the pleasure of Kumbhīnasī.

sn: निर्जितास्ते महाबाहो नागा गत्वा रसातलम्। वासुकिस्तक्षकः शङ्खो जटी च वशमाहृताः॥
en: And entering the region under the earth, you did defeat the serpents-and thus bring under your subjection Väsuki, Takşaka, Sankha, and Jațī.

sn: अक्षया बलवन्तश्च शूरा लब्धवराः पुनः। त्वया संवत्सरं युद्ध्वा समरे दानवा विभो॥ स्वबलं समुपाश्रित्य नीता वशमरिन्दम। मायाश्चाधिगतास्तत्र वयो वै राक्षसाधिप॥
en: Those heroic Dänavas, the Kālakeyas, were greatly powerful, irrepressible, and proud of the boons conferred on them. And fighting with them perpetually for a year, you did bring them under your control, O lord, O slayer of foes, and learn from them the science o varied illusions, O king of the Rākşasas.

sn: शूराश्च बलवन्तश्च वरुणश्च सुता रणे। निर्जितास्ते महाभाग चतुर्विधबलानुगाः॥
en: O great hero, by you were defeated in battle, the heroic and powerful sons of Varuņa, followed by a fourfold division of their army.

sn: मृत्युदण्डमहाग्राहं शाल्मलीदुममण्डितम्। कालपाशमहावीचिं यमकिंकरपन्नगम ॥ महाज्वरेण दुर्धर्षं यमलोकमहार्णवम्। अवगाह्य त्वया राजन्यमस्य बलसागरम्॥ जयश्च विपुलः प्राप्तो मृत्युश्च प्रतिषेधितः। सुयुद्धेन च ते सर्वे लोकास्तत्र सुतोषिताः॥
en: The dominion of Death is like the mighty main, having his rod for aquatic animals, agonies for the frees that cover its islands, the noose for the billows, his attendants for the serpents and his terrible fever for the dreadful attitude of the deep. And diving into this terrible deep, you did, O king, discomfit Death himself and win glorious victory. And every one was pleased there with your successful fight.

sn: क्षत्रियैर्बहुभिवीरैः शक्रतुल्यपराक्रमैः। आसीद्वसुमती पूर्णा महद्भिरिव पादपैः॥
en: The Earth was filled with various heroic Kșatriyas, resembling Sakra in prowess as she is adorned now with various trees.

sn: तेषां वीर्यगुणोत्साहैर्न समो राघवो रणे। प्रसह्य ते त्वया राजन्हताः समरदुर्जयाः॥
en: Rāghava is not their equal either is strength or prowess. And all those heroes, hard to repress in battle, were slain by you, O king.

sn: तिष्ठ वा किं महाराज श्रमेण तव वानरान्। अयमेको महाराज इन्द्रजित्क्षपयिष्यति॥
en: Do you wait here, O great king; you need not take any trouble, Indrajit alone shall slay all these monkeys.

sn: अनेन च महाराज माहेश्वरमनुत्तमम्। इष्ट्वा यज्ञं वरो लब्धो लोके परमदुर्लभः॥
en: This one, O mighty monarch, having celebrated the the Māheśvara* sacrifice, has obtained a noble boon, rarely (attained by persons). *Relating to Mahasvara, the great Lord, a designation of Sivā.

sn: शक्तितोमरमीनं च विनिकीर्णान्त्रशैवलम्। गजकच्छपसंबाधमश्वमण्डूकसंकुलम्॥ रुद्रादित्यमहाग्राहं मरुद्वसुमहोरगम्। रथाश्वगजतोयौघं पदातिपुलिनं महत्॥ अनेन हि समासाद्य देवानां बलसागरम्। गृहीतो दैवतपतिर्लङ्कां चापि प्रवेशितः॥
en: Having agitated the ocean of celestial hosts, having darts and lances for its fishes, showering arms for its moss, elephants for its tortoises, steeds for its frogs, Rudra and Aditya for its ferocious animals, the Maruts and Vasus for its mighty serpents, cars, horses, and elephants for its volume of waters, and infantry for its spacious shore, this one (Indrajit), taking captive the lord of the celestials himself, had brought him into Lanka.

sn: पितामहनियोगाच्च मुक्तः शम्बरवृत्रहा। गतस्त्रिविष्टपं राजन्सर्वदेवनमस्कृतः॥
en: Then, O king, liberated agreeably to the injunction of the Great-father, the slayer of Sambara and Vſtra, worshipped of all the celestials, went (back) to heaven.

sn: तमेव त्वं महाराज विसृजेन्द्रजितं सुतम्। यावद्वानरसेनां तां सरामां नयति क्षयम्॥
en: Do you, O great king, entrust Indrajit with this business, until he bring to destruction the monkey-host along with Rāma.

sn: राजन्नापदयुक्तेयमागता प्राकृताज्जनात्। हृदि नैव त्वया कार्या त्वं वधिष्यसि राघवम्॥
en: O king, you must not think that this calamity, coming from an ignoble person is not insignificant. You shall slay Rāghava.

sn: ततो नीलाम्बुदप्रख्यः प्रहस्तो नाम राक्षसः। अब्रवीत्प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यं शूरः सेनापतिस्तदा॥
en: Then that heroic general, the Rākşasa named Prahasta, possessing the splendour of sable clouds, submitted with joined hands.

sn: देवदानवगन्धर्वाः पिशाचपतगोरगाः। सर्वे धर्षयितुं शक्याः किं पुनर्मानवौ रणे॥
en: I am competent to baffle in battle gods and Dänavas and Gandharvas, ghosts, birds and serpents, what then is a couple of human beings?

sn: सर्वे प्रमत्ता विश्वस्ता वञ्चिताः स्म हनूमता। नहि मे जीवतो गच्छेज्जीवन्स वनगोचरः॥
en: Having been negligent and confident (in our power), we have all been deceived by Hanumān. But, I living, that ranger of woods shall not (again) go hence with his life.

sn: सर्वां सागरपर्यन्तां सशैलवनकाननाम्। करोम्यवानरां भूमिमाज्ञापयतु मां भवान्॥
en: All the earth down to the ocean, containing hills, forests and woods, shall be rendered free from monkeys. Do you command me.

sn: रक्षां चैव विधास्यामि वानराद्रजनीचर। नागमिष्यति ते दुःखं किंचिदात्मापराधजम्॥
en: O ranger of the night, I shall deliver (the Rāks asas) from the monkeys; and you shall not have to suffer in the least in consequence of your transgression.* *i.e. the ravishment of Sitā

sn: अब्रवीत्तमसंक्रुद्धो दुर्मुखो नाम राक्षसः। इदं न क्षा गीयं हि सर्वेषां नः प्रधर्षणम्॥ अयं परिभवो भूयः पुरस्यान्तःपुरस्य च। श्रीमतो राक्षसेन्द्रस्य वानरेन्द्रप्रधर्षणम्॥
en: Then the Rāksasa named Durmukha, growing enraged, said, This overpowering of all of us must not be forgiven-this flagrant discomfiture of the metropolis of the auspicious lord of the Rākşasas as well as of his inner apartment by the foremost of monkeys.

sn: अस्मिन्मुहूर्ते गत्वैको निवर्तिष्यामि वानरान्। प्रविष्टान्सागरं भीममम्बरं वा रसातलम्॥
en: This moment marching alone (from hence) will I exterminate the monkeys, even if they shall have entered the dreadful deep, or the sky, or the subterranean regions.

sn: ततोऽब्रवीत्सुसंक्रुद्धो वज्रदंष्ट्रो महाबलः। प्रगृह्य परिघं घोरं मांसशोणितदूषितम्॥
en: Then the exceedingly powerful Vajradańșțra, wielding up a terrific bludgeon, stained with flesh and gore, wrathfully observed.

sn: किं नो हनूमता कार्य कृपणेन तपस्विना। रामे तिष्ठति दुर्धर्षे सुग्रीवेऽपि सलक्ष्मणे॥
en: Rāma the irrepressible existing, and also Sugrīva with Lakşmaņa, what have we to do with the weak and wretched Hanumăn?

sn: अद्य रामं ससुग्रीवं परिघेण सलक्ष्मणम्। आगमिष्यामि हत्वैको विक्षोब्य हरिवाहिनीम्॥
en: This very day, staying single-handed Rāma with Sugrīva and with Lakşmaņa, with this bludgeon shall I return, after having sorely troubled the monkey-host.

sn: इदं ममापरं वाक्यं शृणु राजन्यदीच्छसि। उपायकुशलो ह्येव जयेच्छवूनतन्द्रितः॥
en: O monarch, if you are minded, hear this other word of mine! Verily he that is fertile in resources and ever ready, compass success.

sn: कामरूपधराः शूराः सुभीमा भीमदर्शनाः। राक्षसानां सहस्राणि राक्षसाधिप निश्चिताः॥ काकुत्स्थमुपसंगम्य विवृतं मानुषं वपुः। सर्वे ह्यसंभ्रमा भूत्वा ब्रुवन्तु रघुसत्तमम्॥ प्रेषिता भरतेनैव भ्रात्रा तव यवीयसा। स हि सेनां समुत्थाप्य क्षिप्रमेवोपयास्यति॥
en: Let thousands of Raksasas, heroic, terrible, fearful to behold, and wearing forms at will, appointed by the lord of Rākṣasa, presenting themselves before Käkutstha in palpably human shapes, calmly say to that foremost of the Raghus, 'Despatched have we been by your younger brother.' Hearing this, he (Rāma), summoning his forces without delay, shall come hither.

sn: ततो वयमितस्तूर्णं शूलशक्तिगदाधराः। चापबाणासिहस्ताश्च त्वरितास्तत्र यामहे ॥ आकाशे गणशः स्थित्वा हत्वा तां हरिवाहिनीम्। अश्मशस्त्रमहावृष्ट्या प्रापयाम यमक्षयम्॥
en: Then, equipped with darts, javelins and maces, and bearing bows, arrows and scimitars in our hands, we shall swiftly and summoning speed* set out (from hence); and stationing ourselves in the sky in bands, and slaughtering the monkey-army with mighty showers of rocks and weapons, we shall lead it to Death's door. *Tvarita-summoning speed-redundant.

sn: एवं चेदुपसप्तामनयं रामलक्ष्मणौ। अवश्यमपनीतेन जहतामेव जीवितम्॥
en: Let us in this wise decoy Rāma and Laks mana; and if they fall into our design, they shall, without doubt, lose their lives.

sn: कौम्भकर्णिस्ततो वीरो निकुम्भो नाम वीर्यवान्। अब्रवीत्परमवुद्धो रावणं लोकरावणम्॥
en: Then that hero, Kumbhakarma's son, named Nikumbha, endowed with exceeding prowess, in high wrath remarked to Rāvana, destroyer of worlds.

sn: सर्वे भवन्तस्थिष्ठन्त महाराजेन संगताः। अहमेको हनिष्यामि राघवं सहलक्ष्मणम्॥ सुग्रीवं सहनूमन्तं सर्वांश्चैवात्र वानरान्।
en: Do you, all of you, stay here along with the great king. I alone shall slay Rāghava together with Laksmana, and Sugrīva with Hanumān, and all the monkeys.

sn: ततो वज्रहनुर्नाम राक्षसः पर्वतोपमः॥ क्रुद्धः परिलिहन्सृक्कां जिह्वया वाक्यमब्रवीत्।
en: Then a Raksasa, named Vajrahanu, resembling a hill, in wrath lapping the corners of his mouth with his tongue, said.

sn: स्वैरं कुर्वन्तु कार्याणि भवन्तो विगतज्वराः॥ एकोऽहं भक्षयिष्यामि तां सर्वां हरिवाहिनीम्।
en: Do you, casting off anxiety, engage yourself as you list. I alone shall swallow up that entire monkey-host.

sn: स्वस्थाः क्रीडन्तु निश्चिन्ता पिबन्तु मधु वारुणम्॥ अहमेको वधिष्यामि सुग्रीवं सहलक्ष्मणम्। साङ्गदं च हनूमन्तं सर्वांश्चैवात्र वानरान्॥
en: Do you, remaining at ease and without anxiety, drink Varuņa wine. I single-handed shall slay Sugrīva with Lakşmaņa, as well as Hanumān with Angada, and all the monkeys.

sn: ततो निकुम्भो रभसः सूर्यशत्रुर्महाबलः। सुप्तघ्नो यज्ञकोपश्च महापार्श्वमहोदरौ॥ अग्निकेतुश्च दुर्धर्षो रश्मिकेतुश्च राक्षसाः। इन्द्रशत्रुश्च बलवांस्ततो वै रावणात्मजः॥ प्रहस्तोऽथ विरूपाक्षो वज्रदंष्ट्रो महाबलः। धूम्राक्षोऽथ निकुम्भश्च दुर्मुखश्चैव राक्षसः॥ परिघान्पट्टिशाञ्छूलान्प्रासाशक्तिपरश्वधान्। चापानि च सुबाणानि खङ्गांश्च विपुलाम्बुभान्॥ प्रगृह्य परमक्रुद्धाः समुत्पत्य च राक्षसाः। अब्रुवन्रावणं सर्वे प्रदीप्ता इव तेजसा॥ अद्य रामं वधिष्यामः सुग्रीवं च सलक्ष्मणम्। कृपणं च हनूमन्तं लङ्का येन प्रधर्षिता॥
en: Then, in fierce wrath seizing bludgeons, and pattiśas, lances and bearded darts and javelins, and axes, bows and excellent shafts and swords, resembling crystalline water, sprung up the Rākşasas, Rabhasa, and the mighty Sūryasatru, and Saptaghna, and Yajñakopa, and Mahāpārsva and Mahodra, Agniketu the irrepressible, and the Rākṣasa Rasmiketu, and the lusty Indraśatru, son to Ravana-and Prahasta, Virupaksa, and the exceedingly strong Vajradanstra, and Dhumrākşa, and Nikumbha, and the Rākşasa Durmukha. And, flaming in energy, they all addressed Ravana, To-day shall we slay Rāma, and Sugrīva along with Lakşmaņa, and the helpless Hanumān, who has damaged Lankā.

sn: तान्गृहीतायुधान्सर्वान्वारयित्वा विभीषणः। अब्रवीत्प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यं पुनः प्रत्युपवेश्य तान्।७।।
en: Then, preventing them, who had (thus) equipped themselves with all kinds of weapons, and making them sit down, Vibhisana, with joined hands, again spoke to them, saying.

sn: अप्युपायैस्त्रिभिस्तात योऽर्थः प्राप्तुं न शक्यते। तस्य विक्रमकालांस्तान्युक्तानाहुर्मनीषिणः॥ प्रमत्तेष्वभियुक्तेषु दैवेन प्रहतेषु च। विक्रमास्तात सिद्ध्यन्ति परीक्ष्य विधिना कृताः॥
en: The wise have asserted that an appeal to prowess should be resorted to anent a business then only when the end sought cannot be attained through the three (other) means. Prowess produce fruit only in respect of welladvised action directed while carefully watching (enemies) that are negligent, or captive, or under Divine affliction.

sn: अप्रमत्तं कथं तं तु विजिगीषु बले स्थितम्। जितरोषं दुराधर्षं तं धर्षयितुमिच्छथ॥
en: But why do you intend to discomfit (Rāma), who is vigilant, who desire victory, who is strong in the Divine strength, who has subdued passion, and who is hard to subdue?

sn: समुद्रं लवयित्वा तु घोरं नदनदीपतिम्। गतिं हनूगतो लोके को विद्यात्तर्कयेत वा॥ बलान्यपरिमेयानि वीर्याणि च निशाचराः। परेषां सहावज्ञा न कर्तव्या कथंचन ॥
en: Who had in this world ever thought of or reasoned at ɔut Hanuman's career over the dreadful deep, the lord of streams and rivers? O rangers of the night, the strength and prowess (of the foe) being immeasurable, you should by no means recklessly disregard him.

sn: किं च राक्षसराजस्य रामेणापकृतं पुरा। आजहार जनस्थानाद्यस्य भार्यां यशस्विनः॥
en: And what was the wrong that formerly had been done by Rāma to the king of the Rākşasas, that he has carried off from Janasthāna the spouse of that illustrious one?

sn: खरो यद्यतिवृत्तस्तु स रामेण हतो रणे। अवश्यं प्राणिना प्राणा रक्षितव्या यथाबलम्॥
en: If Khara, who had trespassed into regions not his own, has buen slain in battle by Rāma, surely a creature should to the best of his might preserve his life.

sn: एतनिमित्तं वैदेही भयं नः सुमहद्भवेत्। आहता सा परित्याज्या कलहार्थे कृते नु किम्॥
en: It is for this great fear that exercise us on the score of Vaidehi owing its existence to this,* that she, having been ravished, should (now) be given up. What is the use of acting so that quarrel may be the consequence? *The feeling of revenge for the slaughter of Khara and the rest.

sn: न तु क्षमं वीर्यवता तेन धर्मानुवर्तिना। वैरं निरर्थकं कर्तुं दीयतामस्य मैथिली॥
en: And (Rama), possessed of prowess, yet ever abiding by morality, is incapable of initiating hostilities for no purpose. Therefore, do you give him his Maithili.

sn: यावत्र सगजां साश्वां बहुरत्नसमाकुलाम्। पुरीं दारयते बाणैर्दीयतामस्य मैथिली॥
en: And before, he by means of his shafts rive this city together with her elephants and steeds, overflowing with countless gems, do you give him his Maithili.

sn: यावत्सुघोरा महती दुर्धर्षा हरिवाहिनी। नावस्कन्दति नो लङ्कां तावत्सीता प्रदीयताम्॥
en: And before the dreadful, irrepressible and mighty monkey-host block up this Lankā of ours, do you give (back) Sītā.

sn: विनश्येद्धि पुरी लङ्का शूराः सर्वे च राक्षसाः। रामस्य दयिता पत्नी न स्वयं यदि दीयते॥
en: This city of Lankā shall perish as also all the heroic Rākṣasas, if you did not yourself make over Rāma's spouse to him.

sn: प्रसादये त्वां बन्धुत्वात्कुरुष्व वचनं मम। हितं तथ्यं त्वहं ब्रूमि दीयतामस्य मैथिली॥
en: I exert myself to pleasure you, because of the fraternity (that subsist between us). Do what I say. I say what is truth and what also is for your good. Do you render (back) Rama's Maithili.

sn: पुरा शरत्सूर्यमरीचिसंनिभान् नवाग्रपुङ्खान्सुदृढानृपात्मजः। सृजत्यमोघान्विशिखान्वधाय ते प्रदीयतां दाशरथाय मैथिली।॥
en: Ere yet the king's son, for compassing your destruction, shower sure shafts resembling the rays of the autumnal Sun, having shining heads and feathered parts, and exceedingly hard, do you render Maithili to son of Daſaratha.

sn: त्यजाशु कोपं सुखधर्मनाशनं भजस्व धर्म रतिकीर्तिवर्धनम्। प्रसीद जीवेम सपुत्रबान्धवाः प्रदीयतां दाशरथाय मैथिली॥
en: Forsake your wrath at once, which destroy happiness and virtue; and follow righteousness, which enhance enjoyment and fame. Be you propitious, so that we may live (at ease) along with our sons and relatives. Render (back) Maithili to Dasaratha's son.

sn: विभीषणवचः श्रुत्वा रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः। विसर्जयित्वा तान्सर्वान्प्रविवेश स्वकं गृहम्॥
en: Having heard Vibhisana's speech, Ravanalord of Raksasas-leaving all of them, entered his own chamber.

sn: ततः प्रत्युषसि प्राप्ते प्राप्तधर्मार्थनिश्चयः। राक्षसाधिपतेर्वेश्म भीमकर्मा विभीषणः॥ शैलाग्रचयसंकाशं शैलशृङ्गमिवोन्नतम्। सुविभक्तमहाकक्ष महाजनपरिग्रहम्॥ मतिमद्भिर्महामात्रैरनुरक्तैरधिष्ठितम्। राक्षसैराप्तपर्याप्तैः सर्वतः परिरक्षितम्॥ मत्तमातङ्गनिःश्वासैर्व्याकुलीकृतमारुतम्। शङ्खघोषमहाघोषं तूर्यसंबाधनादितम्॥ प्रमदाजनसंबाधं प्रजल्पितमहापथम्। तप्तकाञ्चननिहं भूषणोत्तमभूषितम्॥ गन्धर्वाणामिवावासमालयं मरुतामिव । रत्नसंचयसंबाधं भवनं भोगिनामिव॥ तं महाभ्रमिवादित्यस्तेजोविस्तृतरश्मिवान्। अग्रजस्यालयं वीरः प्रविवेश महाद्युतिः॥
en: Then early in the morning, like the fiery and refulgent sun entering a mighty mass of clouds, Vibhisana, fast to virtue and interest, heroic and possessed of exceeding splendour, playing a perilous part, * entered the apartment of his elder brother, resembling an assemblage of mountain summits and elevated like the peak of a mountain, orderly, divided into spacious rooms, the resort of the great-inhabited by august and intelligent persons attached (to Răvaņa); guarded around by lusty Rakşasas in limited numbers; having the air agitated by the breath of mad elephants; with loud blares of conchs, and resounding with trumpets; with loud blares of conchs, and resounding with trumpets; embosoming numbers of beautiful damsels, with its high-ways (overflowing with talk); furnished with doors of polished gold; embellished with excellent ornaments; resembling the abode of the Gandharvas, or the mansion of the Maruts; containing heaps of gems; like to the dwelling of serpents. *The project he had conceived, viz., converting Rāvana to his own polloy of pacification, was fraught with peril to himself, considering his brother's fierce temperament.

sn: पुण्यान्पुण्याहघोषांश्च वेदविद्भिदाहृतान्। शुश्राव सुमहातेजा भ्रातुर्विजयसंश्रितान् ॥ पूजितान्दधिपात्रैश्च सर्पिभिः सुमनोक्षतैः। मन्त्रवेदविदो विप्रान्ददर्श स महाबलः॥
en: That one of exceeding energy heard sacred and holy sounds uttered by Veda-versed Brāhmaṇas celebrating the victory of his brother; and that highly powerful (hero) acquainted with Mantras and the Vedas saw Vipras worshipped with vessels of curds, clarified butter, flowers and fried paddy.

sn: स पूज्यमानो रक्षोभिर्दीप्यमानं स्वतेजसा। आसनस्थं महाबाहुर्ववन्दे धनदानुजम्॥
en: The mighty-armed (Vibhisana) saluted the younger brother of the bestower of riches, * seated there. *Kuvera-Ravana was Kuvera's younger brother.

sn: स राजदृष्टिसंपन्नमासनं हेमभूषितम्। जगाम समुदाचारं प्रयुज्याचारकोविदः॥
en: That one acquainted with manners, after proper courtesy, sat him down on a seat decked in gold, which was pointed out (by a royal glance).

sn: स रावणं महात्मानं विजने मन्त्रिसंनिधौ। उवाच हितमत्यर्थं वचनं हेतुनिश्चितम्॥ प्रसाद्य भ्रातरं ज्येष्ठं सान्त्वेनोपस्थितक्रमः। देशकालार्थसंवादि दृष्टलोकपरावरः॥
en: In retirement as also in presence only of his counsellors, Vibhīşaņa spoke to the high souled Rāvana words backed by reason, and greatly fraught with his welfare. And having, with soothing speech, pacified his elder brother and extended towards him the due civilities, that one, who through height of sentiment had noted excellence and the want of it, addressed (Vibhīş aņa) in words befitting the occasion and the place.

sn: यदाप्रभृति वैदेही संप्राप्तेह परंतप। तदाप्रभृति दृश्यन्ते निमित्तान्यशुभानि नः॥
en: Ever since, O subduer of enemies, Vaidehi has come hither, are seen inauspicious omens.

sn: सस्फुलिङ्गः सधूमार्चिः सधूमकलुषोदयः। मन्त्रसङ्घहुतोऽप्यग्निर्न सम्यगभिवर्धते॥
en: Fire, enveloped in smoke at the time of its being ignited, and thereafter throwing out scintillation's, with its brightness obscured by vapour, does not increase adequately even n oblations being poured into it with Mantras,

sn: अग्निष्टेष्वग्निशालासु तथा ब्रह्मस्थलीषु च। सरीसृपाणि दृश्यन्ते हव्येषु च पिपीलिकाः॥
en: Reptiles are discovered in kitchens, sacrificial fire-chambers, and the places of Vaidika recitations; and ants (are found) in clarified butter.

sn: गवां पयांसि स्कन्नानि विमदा वरकुञ्जराः। दीनमश्वाः प्रहेषन्ते नवग्रासाभिनन्दिनः॥
en: The milk of the kine has been dried up; and the nobler elephants are without the temporal juice. And horses, albeit they have feasted on feasted on fresh grass, neigh distressfully.* *The commentator remarks, evidently with justice, "That is, the horses, having eaten their fill, still hunger."

sn: खरोष्ट्रश्वतरा राजन्भिन्नरोमाः सवन्ति च। न स्वभावेऽवतिष्ठन्ते विधानैरपि चिन्तिताः॥
en: Asses, camels and mules, O king, with their hair standing erect, shed tears; and although they are ministered to medically, they do not return to nature.

sn: वायसाः सङ्घशः क्रूरा व्याहरन्ति समन्ततः। समवेताश्च दृश्यन्ते विमानाग्रेषु सङ्घशः॥
en: And crows in numbers emit harsh cries on all sides, and are seen in swarms at the tops of edifices.

sn: गृध्राश्च परिलीयन्ते पुरीमुपरि पीडिताः। उपपन्नाश्च संध्ये द्वे व्याहरन्त्यशिवं शिवाः॥
en: Vultures sit sadly and distressed upon the roofs of houses. During the two twilights, the jackals, coming in sight, utter ominous howls.

sn: क्रव्यादानां मृगाणां च पुरीद्वारेषु सङ्घशः। श्रूयन्ते विपुला घोषाः सविस्फूर्जतनिःस्वनाः॥
en: Wolves and other (ferocious) animals, as well as deer, approaching the gate of the palace in swarms, are heard to set up loud roars resembling the thunder.

sn: तदेवं प्रस्तुते कार्ये प्रायश्चित्तमिदं क्षमम्। रोचये वीर वैदेही राघवाय प्रदीयताम्॥
en: Things having come to this pass, even this expiation, I fancy, is capable of removing the evil omens. Do you render back Vaidehī to Raghava.

sn: इदं च यदि वा मोहाल्लोभाद्वा व्याहृतं मया। तत्रापि च महाराज न दोषं कर्तुमर्हसि ॥
en: If I have said this through ignorance or covetousness, you ought not, O mighty monarch, criminate me.

sn: अयं हि दोषः सर्वस्य जनस्यास्योपलक्ष्यते। रक्षसां राक्षसीनां च पुरस्यान्तःपुरस्य च ॥
en: All Rākşasas and Rākşasis, as well as those belonging to palace and the inner apartmentshall have to experience the even consequence (of this act of your).

sn: प्रापणे चास्य मन्त्रस्य निवृत्ताः सर्वमन्त्रिणः। अवश्यं च मया वाच्यं यदृष्टमथवा श्रुतम्।। संविधाय यथान्यायं तद्भवान्कर्तुमर्हति॥
en: All the counsellors have refrained from tendering this counsel to you; but surely I must tell you what I have seen or heard; and adopting proper measures, it behove you to act so.* *In accordance with my suggestion.

sn: इति स्वमन्त्रिणां मध्ये भ्राता भ्रातरमूचिवान्। रावणं रक्षसां श्रेष्ठं पथ्यमेतद्विभीषणः॥
en: (Ravana's) brother, Vibhisana, thus spoke, to his brother, the chief of Rākşasa, in the midst of counsellors, these words fraught with his good.

sn: हितं महाथ मृदु हेतुसंहितं व्यतीतकालायतिसंप्रतिक्षमम्। निशम्य तद्वाक्यमुपस्थितज्वरः प्रसङ्गवानुत्तरमेतदब्रवीत्॥ भयं न पश्यामि कुतश्चिदप्यहं न राघवः प्राप्स्यति जातु मैथिलीम्। सुरैः सहेन्द्रैरपि संगरे कथं ममाग्रतः स्थास्यति लक्ष्मणाग्रजः॥
en: Hearing this beneficial, mild and pregnant speech, fortified by reasons and capable of compassing (his welfare) for the present, past and the future, (Rāvaņa) who had conceived a passion (for Sītā), getting into a rage, replied, Fear find I none whatever. Rāghava never shall have Mithila's daughter. Even if Laksmana's elder brother should be supported in battle by the celestials with Indra (at their head), how can he stay before me (in the field)?

sn: इत्येवमुक्त्वा सुरसैन्यनाशनो महाबलः संयति चण्डविक्रमः। दशाननो भ्रातरमाप्तवादिनं विसर्जयामास तदा विभीषणम्॥
en: Having said this, that destroyer of celestial hosts, the Ten-necked one, possessed of mighty strength and of terrific prowess in battle, then dismissed his brother Vibhīşaņa, who had spoken truth.

sn: स बभूव कृशो राजा मैथिलीकाममोहितः। असन्मानाच्च सुहृदां पापः पापेन कर्मणा॥
en: The unrighteous king, overmastered by his passion (for Sītā), in consequence of his sinful act as well as the loss of honour he sustained at the hands of his friends, became reduced.

sn: अतीव कामसंपन्नो वैदेहीमनुचिन्तयन्। अतीतसमये काले तस्मिन्वै युधि रावणः। अमात्यैश्च सुहृद्भिश्च प्राप्तकालममन्यत॥
en: The occasion for war was (wanting Rāvana, possessed by lust, and continually thinking of Vaidehī, conceived along with his counsellors that the time for entering into hostilities had arrived.

sn: स हेमजालविततं मणिविद्रुमभूषितम्। उपगम्य विनीताश्वमारुरोह महारथम्॥
en: Sallying forth, he ascended a mighty car furnished with golden network, adorned with pearls and coral and yoked with trained steeds.

sn: तमास्थाय रथश्रेष्ठं महामेघसमस्वनम्। प्रययौ रक्षसां श्रेष्ठो दशग्रीवः सभां प्रति॥
en: Having ascended that excellent vehicle, having sounds resembling those of mighty clouds, that foremost of Raksasa, the Tennecked one, drove towards the court.

sn: असिचर्मधरा योधाः सर्वायुधधरास्ततः। राक्षसा राक्षसेन्द्रस्य पुरस्तात्संप्रतस्थिरे॥
en: As he coursed on, Rākşasas, bearing swords and shields, and carrying all kinds of weapons, went before the lord of the Rākşasas.

sn: नानाविकृतवेषाश्च नानाभूषणभूषिताः। पार्श्वतः पृष्ठतश्चैनं परिवार्य ययुस्तदा॥
en: And (some of) these, wearing various frightful suits, and decked with diverse ornaments, went, surrounding his rear and flanks.

sn: रथैश्चातिरथाः शीघ्रं मत्तैश्च वरवारणैः। अनूत्पेतुर्दशग्रीवमाक्रीडद्भिश्च वाजिभिः॥ गदापरिघहस्ताश्च शक्तितोमरपाणयः।
en: And many atiratha heroes went with cars, and superb mad elephants, and sportive steeds; and bearing in their hands maces and bludgeons; and darts and clubs.

sn: परश्वधधराश्चान्ये तथान्ये शूलपाणयः। ततस्तूर्यसहस्राणां संजज्ञे निःस्वनो महान्॥ तुमुलः शङ्खशब्दश्च सभां गच्छति रावणे।
en: Some of them were bearing spades and others with darts in hands. As Rāvana marched towards the court, there arose the loud blares of a thousand trumpet, and the uproarious sounds of conchs.

sn: स नेमिघोषेण महान्सहसाभिनिनादयन्॥ राजमार्ग श्रिया जुष्टं प्रतिपेदे महारथः।
en: That redoubtable and mighty car-warrior held his course, suddenly making sides resound, and beautifying the high ways.

sn: विमलं चातपत्रं च प्रगृहीतमशोभत ॥ पाण्डुरं राक्षसेन्द्रस्य पूर्णस्ताराधिपो यथा।
en: The spotless white umbrella of the lord of Rākşasa, being raised up, looked beautiful like the Moon at her full.

sn: हेममञ्जरिगर्भे च शुद्धस्फटिकविग्रहे ॥ चामरव्यजने तस्य रेजतुः सव्यदक्षिणे।
en: On his right and left graced two crystal white cámaras furnished with threads of gold.

sn: ते कृताञ्जलयः सर्वे रथस्थं पृथिवीस्थिताः॥ राक्षसा राक्षसश्रेष्ठं शिरोभिस्तं ववन्दिरे।
en: All those Rākşasas standing on the ground with joined hands, bowed down their heads to the foremost of Rākşasas who was seated on his car.

sn: राक्षसैः स्तूयमानः सञ्जयाशीभिररिंदमः॥ आससाद महातेजाः सभां विरचितां तदा।
en: Hymned by the Råkşasas with blessings of victory, that exceedingly energetic chastiser of enemies arrived at the court constructed (by Viśvakarmā).

sn: सुवर्णरजतास्तीणां विशुद्धस्फटिकान्तराम्॥ विराजमानो वपुषा रुक्मपट्टोत्तरच्छदाम्। तां पिशाचशतैः षड्भिरभिगुप्तां सदाप्रभाम्॥ प्रविवेश महातेजाः सुकृतां विश्वकर्मणा।
en: That highly energetic one in person entered that court paved with silver and gold, having its heart decorated with crystal, and gracefully covered with silk, embroidered with gold; excellently constructed by Viśvakarma, and guarded by six hundred ghosts.

sn: तस्याः स वैदूर्यमयं प्रियकाजिनसंवृतम्॥ महत्सोपाश्रयं भेजे रावणः परमासनम्। ततः शशासेश्वरहूताल्लघुपराक्रमान्॥
en: Rävaņa sat down on a superb and august seat consisting of lapises, furnished with a pillow; and covered with a soft dear-skin. And lord-like he commanded the envoys possessed of fleet vigour, saying.

sn: समानयत मे क्षिप्रमिहैताराक्षसानिति । कृत्यमस्ति महज्जाने कर्तव्यमिति शत्रुभिः॥
en: Do you speedily summon hither the Raksasas. I fancy some mighty effort has to be put forth against our foes.

sn: राक्षसास्तद्वचः श्रुत्वा लङ्कायां परिचक्रमुः। अनुगेहमवस्थाय विहारशयनेषु च। उद्यानेषु च रक्षांसि चोदयन्तो ह्यभीतवत्॥
en: Hearing his words, the envoys began to range Lankā; and going to every house, they fearlessly collected the Rākṣasas from places of sport, bedrooms, and gardens.

sn: ते रथान्तरचरा एके दृप्तानेके दृढान्हयान्। नागानेकेऽधिरुरुहुर्जग्मुश्चैके पदातयः॥
en: Then some set out, mounting cars, and some mounting proud coursers, and some on foot.

sn: सा पुरी परमाकीर्णा रथकुञ्जरवाजिभिः। संपतद्भिर्विरुरुचे गरुत्मद्भिरिवाम्बरम्॥
en: And like the welkin filled with fowls, the city thronged with approaching cars, elephants and steeds.

sn: ते वाहनान्यवस्थाय यानानि विविधानि च। सभां पद्भिः प्रविविशुः सिंहा गिरिगुहामिव ॥
en: Leaving their various vehicles and cars behind, they entered the court on foot, like lions entering mountain caverns.

sn: राज्ञः पादौ गृहीत्वा तु राज्ञा ते प्रतिपूजिताः। पीठेष्वन्ये बृसीष्वन्ये भूमौ केचिदुपाविशन्॥
en: Taking the feet of the sovereign, and honoured by him (in turn), they sat them down, some-on raised seats, some on cushions of Kusa, and some on the floor.

sn: ते समेत्य सभायां वै राक्षसा राजशासनात्। यथार्हमुपतस्थुस्ते रावणं राक्षसाधिपम्॥
en: Presenting themselves agreeably to the command of the monarch, they sat them down each according to his position, before the lord of Raksasas, Ravana.

sn: मन्त्रिणश्च यथामुख्या निश्चितार्थेषु पण्डिताः। अमात्याश्च गुणोपेताः सर्वज्ञा बुद्धिदर्शनाः॥ समीयुस्तत्र शतशः शूराश्च बहवस्तथा। सभायां हेमवर्णायां सर्वार्थस्य सुखाय वै॥
en: There came also the learned and competent to arrive at infallible decisions, and they sat them down in order of merit. And there also came courtiers endowed with virtues, versed in every thing, and having intelligence for their eye-sight, and innumerable heroes by hundreds also (arrived) at that court for ascertaining the course the would prove beneficial.

sn: ततो महात्मा विपुलं सुयुग्यं रथं वरं हेमविचित्रताङ्गम्। शुभं समास्थाय ययौ यशस्वी विभीषणः संसदमग्रजस्य॥
en: Then mounting a large, noble and splendid car, having its parts decked with gold, and yoked with horses, the magnanimous and renowned Vibhīşana went to the court of his elder brother.

sn: स पूर्वजायावरजः शशंस नामाथ पश्चाच्चरणौ ववन्दे। शुक्रः प्रहस्तश्च तथैव तेभ्यो ददौ यथार्ह पृथगासनानि॥
en: That younger brother (of Rāvana), announcing his name, bowed down at the feet of his elder brother. And Śuka and Prahasta were employed in giving to each a separate seat befitting his rank.

sn: सुवर्णनानामणिभूषणानां सुवाससां संसदि राक्षसानाम्। तेषां परार्ध्यागुरुचन्दनानां स्रजां च गन्धाः प्रववुः समन्तात्॥
en: From all sides in the court there began to spread the odour of excellent agura and sandal and wreaths belonging to the Räkşasas, decked in gold and various gems, and clad in costly attires.

sn: न चुक्रुशु नृतमाह कश्चित् सभासदो नापि जजल्पुरुच्चैः। संसिद्धार्थाः सर्व एवोग्रवीर्या भर्तुः सर्वे ददृशुश्चाननं ते॥
en: And no one among these present at court uttered any thing, or spoke any falsehood, or conversed in loud accents. And having completely attained their desire, all of fierce prowess, gazed at the face of their lord.

sn: स रावणः शस्त्रभृतां मनस्विनां महाबलानां समितौ मनस्वी। तस्यां सभायां प्रथया चकाशे मध्ये वसूनामिव वज्रहस्तः॥
en: In the assembly of those intelligent, and exceedingly powerful persons, equipped with arms, the intelligent Rāvaņa appeared splendid like the vaira-handed Indra among the Vasus.

sn: स तां परिषदं कृत्स्नां समीक्ष्य समितिंजयः। प्रबोधयामास तदा प्रहस्तं वाहिनीपतिम्॥
en: Then surveying that entire assembly, that conqueror in battle delivered himself to Prahasta, general of the forces, saying.

sn: सेनापते यथा ते स्युः कृतविद्याश्चतुर्विधाः । योधा नगररक्षायां तथा व्यादेष्टुमर्हसि॥
en: O general, it behove you so to order the disciplined fourfold forces that they may successfully protect the city.

sn: स प्रहस्तः प्रणीतात्मा चिकीर्षनराजशासनम्। विनिक्षिप्य बलं सर्वं बहिरन्तश्च मन्दिरे॥
en: Thereat, Prahasta, carefully carrying out the royal behest, stationed all the forces within and without the city.

sn: ततो विनिक्षिप्य बलं सर्वं नगरगुप्तये। प्रहस्तः प्रमुखे राज्ञो निषसाद जगाद च॥
en: Having posted the army for the defence of the city, Prahasta sitting down before the king, said.

sn: विहितं बहिरन्तश्च बलं बलवतस्तव। कुरुष्वाविमनाः क्षिप्रं यदभिप्रेतमस्ति ते।।।
en: I have stationed the forces belonging to you who are possessed of strength, inside as well as outside. (Now), without suffering your mind to be agitated with anxiety, speedily, do what is in your heart.

sn: प्रहस्तस्य वचः श्रुत्वा राजा राज्यहितैषिणः। सुखेप्सुः सुहृदां मध्ये व्याजहार स रावणः॥
en: Hearing the speech of Prahasta seeking the welfare of the kingdom, Rāvaņa craving for enjoyment, spoke in the midst of his aderents.

sn: प्रियाप्रिये सुखे दुःखे लाभालाभे हिताहिते। धर्मकामार्थकृच्छेषु यूयमर्हथ वेदितुम्॥
en: When virtue, or happiness, or interest is in straits, it behove you to (know your course) in relation to pleasant and unpleasant, happiness and misery, profitable and unprofitable, and good and evil.

sn: सर्वकृत्यानि युष्माभिः समारब्धानि सर्वदा। मन्त्रकर्मनियुक्तानि न जातु विफलानि मे॥
en: No business of mine which you have set about after taking counsel, has miscarred.

sn: ससोमग्रहनक्षत्रैमरुद्भिरिव वासवः। भवद्भिरहमत्यर्थं वृतः श्रियमवाप्नुयाम्॥
en: Like Väsava environed by the moon, stars and planets and the Maruts, I surrounded by you, have attained to plenitude of prosperity.

sn: अहं तु खलु सर्वान्वः समर्थयितुमुद्यतः। कुम्भकर्णस्य तु स्वप्नानेममर्थमचोदयम्॥
en: I am, for certain, going to employ you all. In consequence of Kumbhakarņa's sleep, I could not inform him of this matter.

sn: अयं हि सुप्तः षण्मासान्कुम्भकर्णो महाबलः। सर्वशस्त्रभृतां मुख्यः स इदानीं समुत्थित॥
en: After having slept for six months that one of prodigious strength, foremost of those bearing arms, has just risen.

sn: इयं च दण्डकारण्याद्रामस्य महिषी प्रिया। रक्षोभिश्चरितोद्देशादानीता जनकात्मजा ॥
en: Janaka's daughter and Rāma's beloved wife has been brought hither from the forest of Dandaka, the region ranged by Raksasa.

sn: सा मे न शय्यामारोदुमिच्छत्यलसगाभिनी। त्रिषु लोकेषु चान्या मे न सीतासदृशी तथा॥
en: That indolent damsel wish not to ascend my bed; nor is there any in the three spheres, that to me is like to Sītā.

sn: तनुमध्या पृथुश्रोणी शरदिन्दुनिभानना। हेमबिम्बनिभा सौम्या मायेव मयनिर्मिता॥
en: She is slender waisted and high-hipped and her face is as the autumnal Moon resembling a golden image. She is meek and look like the hand work of Maya himself gifted with an infinite variety of fascinations.

sn: सुलोहिततलौ श्लक्ष्णौ चरणौ सुप्रतिष्ठितौ। दृष्ट्वा ताम्रनखौ तस्या दीप्यते मे शरीरजः॥
en: And beholding her dainty and tender fect with roseate soles, and having coppery nails, my mind burn (with desire).

sn: हुताग्निरर्चिः संकाशामेनां सौरीमिव प्रभाम्। उन्नसं विमलं वल्गु वदनं चारुलोचनम्॥ पश्यंस्तदवशस्तस्याः कामस्य वशमेयिवान्।
en: Seeing her resembling the flame of a sacrificial fire and the splendour of the Sun himself; and her fair face furnished with a prominent nose and elegant eyes, I, having lost control over self, have come under the sway of desire.

sn: क्रोधहर्षसमानेन दुर्वर्णकरणेन च॥ शोकसंतापनित्येन कामेन कलुषीकृतः। सा तु संवत्सरं कालं मामयाचत भामिनी॥
en: And my passion, uninfluenced by anger and joy, capable of producing pallor, and constantly causing anguish and sorrow, has rendered me pale.

sn: प्रतीक्षमाणा भर्तारं राममायतलोचना। तन्मया चारुनेत्रायाः प्रतिज्ञातं वचः शुभम्॥
en: Expecting her lord, Rāma, the beautiful one having expansive eyes, has solicited for a year's space; and I have pledged my fair woods to her of graceful eyes.

sn: श्रान्तोऽहं सततं कामाद्यातो हय इवाध्वनि। कथं सागरमक्षोभ्यं तरिष्यन्ति वनौकसः॥ बहुसत्त्वझषाकीर्णं तौ वा दशरथात्मजौ।
en: But tired am I on account of my passion, like a horse spent on the way. How can the rangers of the woods, or the sons of Dasaratha cross over the sea ungovernable and swarming with countless creatures and fishes?

sn: अथवा कपिनैकेन कृतं नः कदनं महत्॥ दुर्जेयाः कार्यगतयो ब्रूत यस्य यथामति। मानुषानो भयं नास्ति तथापि तु विमृश्यताम्॥
en: On the other hand, a single monkey has troubled us grievously. Hard it is therefore to understand the course of events. Do you act, each as he thinks proper, And although no fear come from mortals, yet you should deliberate (as to what you should do).

sn: तदा देवासुरे युद्धे युष्माभिः सहितोऽजयम्। ते मे भवन्तश्च तथा सुग्रीवप्रमुखान्हरीन्॥ परे पारे समुद्रस्य पुरस्कृत्य नृपात्मजौ। सीतायाः पतवीं प्राप्य संप्राप्तौ वरुणालयम्॥
en: Formerly, I had gained victory with the help given by you; do you in the same way stand by me now. The king's son, having learnt that Sita can is on the other shore of the ocean, taking before them monkey headed by Sugriva, reached Varuna's abode.

sn: अदेया च यथा सीता वध्यौ दशरथात्मजौ। भवद्भिर्मन्त्र्यतां मन्त्रः सुनीतं चाभिधीयताम्॥ नहि शक्ति प्रपश्यामि जगत्यन्यस्य कस्यचित्। सागरं वानरैस्तीत्वा निश्चयेन जयो मम ॥
en: Do you so counsel that Sītã may be withholden by me and the sons of Dasaratha may be slain; but you must prefer certain counsel. No other* person in this world has the power to cross the sea along with the monkeys, victory, therefore, is undubitably mine." *I fail to understand anyasya, "no other person" nor does the commentator helps me anyway.

sn: तस्य कामपरीतस्य निशम्य परिदेवितम्। कुम्भकर्णः प्रचुक्रोध वचनं चेदमब्रवीत्॥
en: Hearing the sorrowful speech of (Rāvana) afflicted with lust, Kumbhakarma grew enraged, . and said.

sn: यदा तु रामस्य सलक्ष्मणस्य प्रसह्य सीता खलु सा इहाहृता। सकृत्समीक्ष्यैव सुनिश्चितं तदा भजेत चित्तं यमुनेव यामुनम्॥
en: When just on seeing (Sītā) of Rāma along with Lakşmaņa, you did by main force carry away, it plainly appear that your mind, like the Yamunā filling her bed, has been possessed by her).* *This passage very obscure, and the commentator's gloss does not at all serve.

sn: सर्वमेतन्महाराज कृतमप्रतिमं तव। विधीयेत सहास्माभिरादावेवास्य कर्मणः॥
en: O great king! all this (that you have done) is not worthy of you. If you had at the outset consulted us in this matter, we would have done what was proper. *i.e. we would have prevented you.

sn: न्यायेन राजकार्याणि यः करोति दशानन। न स संतप्यते पश्चानिश्चितार्थमतिर्नृपः॥
en: O ten-faced one, the king, that arriving at certain conclusions, carry on his regal affairs agreeably to justice, has not to repent afterwards.

sn: अनुपायेन कर्माणि विपरीतानि यानि च। क्रियमाणानि दुष्यन्ति हवींष्यप्रयतेष्विव ॥
en: But those actions that are done without deliberation, like to clarified butter poured in an impure sacrifice, conducted only to harma.

sn: यः पश्चात्पूर्वकार्याणि कर्माण्यभिचिकीर्षति। पूर्वं चापरकार्याणि स न वेद नयानयौ ॥
en: He does not know what is proper and what not, that performs prior actions afterwards, and posterior actions first.

sn: चपलस्य तु कृत्येषु प्रसमीक्ष्याधिकं बलम्। छिद्रमन्ये प्रपद्यन्ते क्रौञ्चस्य खमिव द्विजाः॥
en: Others spy holes in the actions of the volatile, the latter may be possessed of great power, like swans passing Krauñca through the hole. * *The hole made by the dart of Kumāra.

sn: त्वयेदं महदारब्धं कार्यमप्रतिचिन्तितम्। दिष्ट्या त्वां नावधीद्रामो विषमिश्रमिवामिषम्॥
en: By luck it is that Rāma has not yet slain you, who has done this tremendous thing, with poison.

sn: तस्मात्त्वया समारब्धं कर्म ह्यप्रतिमं परैः। अहं समीकरिष्यामि हत्वा शस्तवानघ॥
en: But as you have entered upon a course of action which is improper even in respect of foes, I will, O sinless one, perform your work by slaying your enemies.

sn: अहमुत्सादयिष्यामि शत्रुस्तव निशाचर। यदि शक्रविवस्वन्तौ यदि पावकमारुतौ। तावहं योधयिष्यामि कुबेरवरुणावपि॥
en: O ranger of the night, I will exterminate your foe. Even if Sakra and the sun, even if fire and the War-god, even if Kubera and Varuna, should range themselves against me, I will fight them.

sn: गिरिमात्रशरीरस्य महापरिघयोधिनः। नर्दतस्तीक्ष्णदंष्ट्रस्य बिभीयाद्वै पुरन्दरः॥
en: Purandara himself shall be afflicted with fright when I having my body measuring a mountain, and furnished with sharp teeth, shall, setting up roars, fight with my huge bludgeon.

sn: पुना स द्वितीयेन शरेण निहनिष्यति। ततोऽहं तस्य पास्यामि रुधिरं काममाश्वस॥
en: Before Rama shoot a second shaft, to slay me, I shall drink his life-blood.

sn: वधेन वै दाशरथेः सुखावह जयं तवाहर्तुमहं यतिष्ये।। हत्वा च रामं सह लक्ष्मणेन खादामि सर्वानहरियूथमुख्यान्॥
en: Be you comforted by slaying Daſaratha's son, I will exert to secure blessed victory for you. Having killed Rāma along with Lakşmaņa, I shall devour all the principal monkeys.

sn: रमस्य कामं पिब चावयवारुणीं कुरुष्व कार्याणि हितानि विज्वरः। मया तु रामे गमिते यमक्षयं चिराय सीता वशगा भविष्यति।४०॥
en: Do you make merry at your will, drink the Vāruņi, and, with your mind set at rest, conduct affairs fraught with your welfare. On Rāma being despatched to the mansion of Yama, Sītā shall come under your subjection for ever and a day.

sn: रावणं क्रुद्धमाज्ञाय महापार्यो महाबलः। मुहूर्तमनुसंचिन्त्य प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
en: Seeing Ravana wrought up with wrath, the exceedingly strong Mahāpārsva, reflecting for a moment, observed with joined hands.

sn: यः खल्वपि वनं प्राप्य मृगव्यालनिषेवितम्। न पिबेन्मधु संप्राप्य स नरो बालिशो भवेत्॥
en: The man that, entering the forest, abounding with deer and ferocious animals, does not drink honey, make a fool of himself.

sn: ईश्वरस्येश्वरः कोऽस्ति तव शत्रुनिबर्हण। रमस्व सह वैदेह्या शत्रूनाक्रम्य मूर्धसु॥
en: O destroyer of foes, who is the lord of you, that are lord yourself? Enjoy with Vaidehi, taking your enemy by the hand.

sn: बलात्कुक्कुटवृत्तेन प्रवर्तस्व महाबल। आक्रम्याक्रम्य सीतां वै तां भुङ्क्व च रमस्व च।४॥
en: O you endowed with prodigious power, do you exerting your might lead your life, after the manner of hens, and invading Sītā again and again, do you enjoy her and derive pleasure (therefrom).

sn: लब्धकामस्य ते पश्चादागमिष्यति किं भयम्। प्राप्तमप्राप्तकालं वा सर्व प्रतिविधास्यसे॥
en: When you have attained your purpose; what fear can succeed? Alike when on your guard, and off it, you shall provide against all exigencies.

sn: कुम्भकर्णः सहास्माभिरिन्द्रजिच्च महाबलः। प्रतिषेधयितुं शक्तौ सवज्रमपि वज्रिणम्॥
en: Kumbhakarņa along with us, as well the exceedingly powerful Indrajit, are competent to chastise the thunder-bearing (Deity) equipped with his thunder.

sn: उपप्रदानं सान्त्वं वा भेदं वा कुशलैः कृतम्। समतिक्रम्य दण्डेन सिद्धिमर्थेषु रोचये॥
en: Passing by gift, conciliation, and dissension, which have been as signed by the wise as the means of success, I relish the success in business which is attained through chastisement.

sn: इह प्राप्तान्वयं सर्वाञ्छबूंस्तव महाबल। वशं शस्त्रप्रतापेन करिष्यामो न संशयः॥
en: O highly powerful one, we shall, without doubt, by the prowess of our arms, subdue all these enemies of your that have come hither.

sn: एवमुक्तस्तदा राजा महापार्श्वेन रावणः। तस्य संपूजयन्वाक्यमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Thus addressed by Mahāpārsva, king Rāvana, honouring his speech, said.

sn: महापार्श्व प्रवदतो रहस्यं किंचिदात्मनः। चिरवृत्तं तदाख्यास्ये यदवाप्तं पुरा मया॥ पितामहस्य भवनं गच्छन्तीं पुञ्जिकस्थलाम्। चञ्चर्यमाणामद्राक्षमाकाशेऽग्निशिखामिव ॥
en: O Mahāparáva, I will relate to you, who have spoken (thus), a secret matter relating to myself, which befell me long since I saw Puñjikasthală, like a flame in the sky, coursing to the Greatfather's mansion.

sn: सा प्रसह्य मया भुक्ता कृता विवसना ततः। स्वयंभूभवनं प्राप्ता लोलिता नलिनी यथा॥
en: Her pace slackened, as soon as she saw me, (turn) I feasted on her and deprived her of her attire. Then she went to the Great-father's place, like a crumpled lotus.

sn: तच्च तस्य तथा मन्ये ज्ञातमासीन्महात्मनः। अथ संकुपितो वेधा मामिदं वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
en: That high-souled one received information of all that I had done; and thereat, waxing enraged, the Deity spoke to me.

sn: अद्यप्रभृति यामन्यां बलान्नारों गमिष्यसि। तदा ते शतधा मूर्धा फलिष्यति न संशयः॥
en: If from this day, you ravish a female by force, your head certainly shall be riven in an hundred pieces.

sn: इत्यहं तस्य शापस्य भीतः प्रसभमेव ताम्। नारोहये बलात्सीतां वैदेहीं शयने शुभे॥
en: It is for this, that with my mind afflicted with fear, I do not violently force, Videha's daughter Sītā, anent lying with her fair self.

sn: सागरस्येव मे वेगो मारुतस्येव मे गतिः। नैतद्दाशरथिर्वेद ह्यासादयति तेन माम्॥
en: My rush is like that of the sea, and my motion that of the wind. Dasaratha's son does not know this, and therefore does he approach sea.

sn: को हि सिंहमिवासीनं सुप्तं गिरिगुहाशये। क्रुद्धं मृत्युमिवासीनं संबोधयितुमिच्छति॥
en: Who wish to address a lion that is lying asleep in a cave, resembling Death wrought up by wrath?

sn: न मत्तो निर्गतान्बाणान्विजिह्वान्पन्नगानिव। रामः पश्यति संग्रामे तेन मामभिगच्छति॥
en: Răma has not seen shafts shot by me, resembling two-tongued serpents, and therefore, it is that he approach me.

sn: क्षिप्रं वज्रसमैर्बाणैः शतधा कार्मुकच्युतैः। राममादीपयिष्यामि उल्काभिरिव कुञ्जरम्॥
en: Like a meteor burning an elephant, I shall, with shafts shot from bow in hundreds, resembling the thunder-bolt, consume Rāma.

sn: तच्चास्य बलमादास्ये बलेन महता वृतः। उदितः सविता काले नक्षत्राणां प्रभामिव ॥
en: As at the proper hour the risen Sun defeat the splendour of the stars, will I, surrounded by a mighty army, overpower his strength.

sn: न वासवेनापि सहस्रचक्षुषा युधास्मि शक्यो वरुणेन वा पुनः। मया त्वियं बाहुबलेन निर्जिता पुरा पुरी वैश्रवणेन पालिता॥
en: Neither the thousand-eyed Vasava, nor yet Varuņa, is capable of fighting me. By the might of this arm did I formerly conquer this city, governed by Vaiśravana.

sn: निशाचरेन्द्रस्य निशम्य वाक्यं स कुम्भकर्णस्य च गर्जितानि। विभीषणो राक्षसराजमुख्यमुवाच वाक्यं हितमर्थयुक्तम्॥
en: Hearing the words of the lord of Rākşasas, as well as the thundering of Kumbhakarņa, Vibhīşaņa addressed the Rākşasa chief, in a pregnant speech, fraught with his welfare.

sn: वृतो हि बाह्वन्तरभोगराशिश्चिन्ताविषः सुस्मिततीक्ष्णदंष्ट्रः। पञ्चाङ्गुलीपञ्चशिरोऽतिकायः सौतामहाहिस्तव केन राजन्॥
en: You have been bound about your neck by the mighty and huge serpent, Sītā, having her breast for its body anxiety for its venom, smile for its sharp fangs, and her five fingers for its hood.

sn: यावन लङ्कां समभिद्रवन्ति वलीमुखाः पर्वतकूटमात्राः। दंष्ट्रायुधाश्चैव नखायुधाश्च प्रदीयतां दाशरथाय मैथिली॥
en: Therefore before the monkeys, resembling mountain peaks, having teeth for their arms and nails, for their weapons, subjugate Lankā, do you render Maithili to Dasaratha's son.

sn: यावन्न गृह्णन्ति शिरांसि बाणा रामेरिता राक्षसपुङ्गवानम्। वज्रोपमा वायुसमानवेगाः प्रदीयतां दाशरथाय मैथिली।४।।
en: Before the shafts shot by Ráma, resembling the thunder-bolt and having impetuosity of the wind, cut off the heads of the foremost of the Rākșasas, do you render Mithila's daughter to the son of Dasaratha.

sn: न कुम्भकर्णेन्द्रजितौ च राजंस्तथा महापार्श्वमहोदरौ वा। निकुम्भकुम्भौ च तथातिकायः स्थातुं समर्था युधि राघवस्य॥
en: Neither Kumbhakarņa nor Indrajit, neither Mahāparáva nor Mahodara, neither Nikumbha nor Kumbha nor yet Atikāya, O king, can stay in the field against Rāghava.

sn: जीवंस्तु रामस्य न मोक्ष्यसे त्वं गुप्तः सवित्राप्यथवा मरुद्भिः। न वासवस्याङ्कगतो न मृत्योर्नभो न पातालमनुप्रविष्टः॥
en: Living, you, whether you are protected by the Sun or the winds, or throw yourself into the lap itself of Vāsava, or enter the sky or the nether spheres, shall not escape death.

sn: निशम्य वाक्यं तु विभीषणस्य ततः प्रहस्तो वचनं बभाषे। न नो भयं विद्म न दैवतेभ्यो न दानवेभ्योऽप्यथवा कदाचित्।७।। न यक्षगन्धर्वमहोरगेभ्यो भयं न संख्ये पतगोरगेभ्यः। कथं नु रामाद्भविता भयं नो नरेन्द्रपुत्रात्समरे कदाचित्॥
en: Hearing Vibhisana's words, Prahasta said, Fear know we none whatever from the celestials, or Danavas, or Yaksas, or Gandharvas, or huge snakes; fear know we none in battle with birds and serpents. How can fear at all afflict us proceeding from the king's son, Rāma?

sn: प्रहस्तवाक्यं त्वहितं निशम्य विभीषणे राजहितानुकानी। ततो महार्थं वचनं बभाषे धर्मार्थकामेषु निविष्टबुद्धिः॥
en: Hearing Prahasta's speech, Vibhisana, seeking the welfare of the king, and having his intellect grounded in virtue, interest and profit, said words enfolding high sense.

sn: प्रहस्त राजा च महोदरश्च त्वं कुम्भकर्णश्च यथार्थजातम्। ब्रवीत राम प्रति तन्न शक्यं यथा गतिः स्वर्गमधर्मबुद्धेः॥
en: O Prahasta, like a sinful person being unable to ascend heaven what the king, Mahodara, you, and Kumbhakarņa, are saying with reference to Rāma, shall not prove true.

sn: वधस्तु रामस्य मया त्वया च प्रहस्त सर्वैरपि राक्षसैर्वा। कथं भवेदर्थविशारदस्य महार्णवं तर्तुमिवाप्लवस्य॥
en: As one without a raft cannot cross over the mighty main, how can I, or you, or all the Raksasa combined, cause death to Rāma, who, O Prahasta, is versed in the sense of things.

sn: धर्मप्रधानस्य महारथस्य इक्ष्वाकुवंशप्रभवस्य राज्ञः। पुरोऽस्य देवाश्च तथाविधस्य कृत्येषु शक्तस्य भवन्ति मूढाः॥
en: Even the gods become stolid before the sovereign of the Ikşvāku race, having righteousness for his principle quality, and being a mighty car-warrior and of such a character, and who is competent in action.

sn: तीक्ष्णा न तावत्तव कङ्कपत्रा दुरासदा राघवविप्रमुक्ताः। भित्त्वा शरीरं प्रविशन्ति बाणा: प्रहस्त तेनैव विकत्थसे त्वम्॥
en: As yet the Kaňka-feathered, terrible and sharp shafts shot by Raghava, have not pierced into your body; and therefore you did speak so.

sn: भित्त्वा न तावत्प्रविशन्ति कायं प्राणान्तिकास्तेऽशनितुल्यवेगाः। शिताः शरा राघवविप्रमुक्ताः प्रहस्त तेनैव विकत्थसे त्वम्॥ न रावणो नातिबलस्त्रिशीर्षो न कुम्भकर्णस्य सुतो निकुम्भः। न चेन्द्रजिद्दाशरथिं प्रसोढुं त्वं वा रणे शक्रसमं समर्थः॥
en: And, O Prahasta, as yet the sharpened shafts, capable of destroying life and having the impetuosity of the thunder-bolt, have not entered into your body, and therefore you did speak thus, neither Rāvana, nor the exceedingly powerful Trisirşa. Neither Kumbhakarna's son Nikumbha nor Indrajit, is capable of bearing in battle the son of Dasaratha, resembling Sakra himself.

sn: देवान्तको वापि नरान्तको वा तथातिकायोऽतिरथो महात्मा। अकम्पनश्चापि समानसारः स्थातुं न शक्ता युधि राघवस्य॥
en: And neither Devāntaka nor Narāntaka, neither Atikāya, nor the magnanimous Atiratha, nor the equally strong Akampana, is competent to stay Rāghava in fight.

sn: अयं च राजा व्यसनाभिभूतो मित्रैरमित्रप्रतिमैर्भवद्भिः। अन्वास्यते राक्षसनाशनार्थे तीक्ष्णः प्रकृत्या ह्यसमीक्ष्यकारी॥
en: The king, naturally of fierce temper and thoughtless, through the instrumentality of you who appearing to be his friends are in reality his foes, seek to destroy the Rākşasas.

sn: अनन्तभोगेन सहस्रमूर्धा नागेन भीमेन महाबलेन। बलात्परिक्षिप्तमिमं भवन्तो राजानमुत्क्षिप्य विमोचयन्तु॥
en: Do you take out and deliver the monarch, who has through force become subject to a dreadful and mighty, and thousand-headed serpent bursting with immeasurable prowess.

sn: यावद्धि केशग्रहणात्सुहृद्भिः समेत्य सर्वैः परिपूर्णकामैः। निगृह्य राजा परिरक्षितव्यो भूतैर्यथा भीमबलैर्गृहीतः॥
en: As a person possessed by fearfully strong ghosts, is saved by his friends pulling him by his hair, attaining your desire you desire you should, assembling together, rescuer the king.

sn: सुवारिणा राघवसागरेण प्रच्छाद्यमानस्तरसा भवद्भिः। युक्तस्त्वयं तारयितुं समेत्य काकुत्स्थपातालमुखे पतन्सः॥
en: This one is sunk in the Rāghava sea having excellent waters. He (the king) has fallen into the Kākutstha neither regions. Do you speedily coming together deliver him.

sn: इदं पुरस्यास्य सराक्षसस्य राज्ञश्च पथ्यं ससुहज्जनस्य। सम्यग्धि वाक्यं स्वमतं ब्रवीमि नरेन्द्रपुत्राय ददातु मैथिलीम्॥
en: I tell you my full mind, fraught with the welfare of this city together with the Rākṣasas, as well of the king with his adherents. Do you make over Maithili to the son of the king.

sn: परस्य वीर्य स्वबलं च बुद्ध्वा स्थानं क्षयं चैव तथैव वृद्धिम्। तथा स्वपक्षेऽप्यनुमृश्य बुद्ध्या वदेत्क्षम स्वामिहितं स मन्त्री॥
en: He is a true counsellor who advises his master, after duly ascertaining the strength, position, increase or destruction of the enemies as well as of their own party.

sn: निशम्य यत्नेन विभीषणस्य। ततो महात्मा वचनं बभाषे तत्रेन्द्रजिनैर्ऋतयूथमुख्यः॥
en: Hearing carefully the words of Vibhīşaņa, gifted with the intelligence of the lord of speech, the high-souled Indrajit, the leader of demons, spoke, saying.

sn: मनर्थकं वै बहुभीतवच्च। अस्मिन्कुले योऽपि भवेन जातः सोऽपीदृशं नैव वदेन कुर्यात्॥
en: Why are you, O uncle, speaking these useless words like one terrified? He even, who is not born in this race, cannot speak or act in this wise.

sn: सत्त्वेन वीर्येण पराक्रमेण धैर्येण शौर्येण च तेजसा च। एकः कुलेऽस्मिन्पुरुषो विमुक्तो विभीषणस्तात कनिष्ठ एषः॥
en: Only one man in this family, my uncle Vibhisana, is weak in energy, strength, prowess, patience, heroism and vigour.

sn: किं नाम तौ मानुषराजपुत्रावस्माकमेकेन हि राक्षसेन। सुप्राकृतेनापि निहन्तुमेतौ शक्यौ कुतो भीषयसे स्म भीरो॥
en: Why are you O timid one, afraid of them since any one of these Rākṣasas is capable of slaying those two princes, human beings as they are?

sn: त्रिलोकनाथो ननु देवराजः शक्तो मया भूमितले निविष्टः। भयार्पिताश्चापि दिशः प्रपन्नाः सर्वे तदा देवगणाः समग्राः॥
en: The master of the three worlds, the lord of the celestials, has been brought down by me as captive on this earth. And all the celestials smitten with fear fled to different quarters.

sn: ऐरावतो निःस्वनमुनदन्स निपातितो भूमितले मया तु। विकृष्य दन्तौ तु मया प्रसह्य वित्रासिता देवगणाः समग्राः॥
en: I brought down on earth the loud-roaring celestial elephant Airavata and uprooted by force its tusks. And all the celestials were terrified at this.

sn: सोऽहं सुराणामपि दर्पहन्ता दैत्योत्तमानामपि शोककर्ता। कथं नरेन्द्रात्मजरयोर्न शक्तो मनुष्ययोः प्राकृतयोः सुवीर्यः॥
en: Am I not, who have shattered the pride of the celestials, afflicted the leading Daityas, and am gifted with excellent prowess, capable of discomfiting these two princess-very ordinary mortals as they are?

sn: अथेन्द्रकल्पस्य दुरासदस्य महौजसस्तद्वचनं निशम्य। ततो महार्थं वचनं बभाषे विभीषणः शस्त्रभृतां वरिष्ठः।।।।।
en: Hearing the words of (Indrajit) gifted with high energy irrepressible and resembling the lord of celestials, Vibhisana, the foremost of those using weapons, addressed him with words, fraught with high import.

sn: न तात मन्त्रे तव निश्चयोऽस्ति बालस्त्वमद्याप्यविपक्वबुद्धिः। तस्मात्त्वयाप्यात्मविनाशनाय वचोऽर्थहीनं बहु विप्रलप्तम्॥
en: O my son, you are a mere child and of unripe intellect and hence you are not capable of as certaining the propriety and impropriety of counsels. You are therefore speaking thus like a maniac for your own destruction.

sn: पुत्रप्रवादेन तु रावणस्य त्वमिन्द्रजिन्मित्रमुखोऽसि शत्रुः। यस्येदृशं राघवतो विनाशं निशम्य मोहादनुमन्यसे त्वम्॥
en: You are known as a son to Ravana, O Indrajit, but in sooth, you are his foe in disguise, since knowing of his destruction from Rāghava, you did not prevent him.

sn: त्वमेव वध्यश्च सुदुर्मतिश्च स चापि वध्यो य इहानयत्वाम्। बालं दृढं साहसिकं च योऽद्य प्रावेशयन्मन्त्रकृतां समीपम्॥
en: You are brave, childish and have been impelled by your silly understanding. You shall be slain along with him who has brought you in this counsel chamber.

sn: स्तीक्ष्णस्वभावोऽल्पमतिर्दुरात्मा। मूर्खस्त्वमत्यन्तसुदुर्मतिश्च त्वमिन्द्रजिद्वालतया ब्रवीषि॥
en: You are, O Indrajit, foolish, imprudent, devoid of humility, of an irritable temper, of feeble sense, vicious-minded and of a silly understanding. And you did speak so, being impelled by childishness.

sn: नर्चिष्मतः कालनिकाशरूपान्। सहेत बाणान्यमदण्डकल्पान् समक्षमुक्तान्युधि राघवेण॥
en: Who shall withstand in battle, the shafts, shot by Raghava, resembling the rod of Death, the stick of Brahmā, flaming like the Fire of Dissolution.

sn: धनानि रत्नानि सुभूषणानि वासांसि दिव्यानि मणींश्च चित्रान्। सीतां च रामाय निवेद्य देवी वसेम राजनिह वीतशोकाः॥
en: Do you render back Sītā, O king, to Rāma, with riches, jewels, excellent ornaments, clothes and jems and we shall then be able to live here void of grief.

sn: धनानि रत्नानि सुभूषणानि वासांसि दिव्यानि मणींश्च चित्रान्। सीतां च रामाय निवेद्य देवी वसेम राजनिह वीतशोकाः॥
en: Do you render back Sītā, O king, to Rāma, with riches, jewels, excellent ornaments, clothes and jems and we shall then be able to live here void of grief.

sn: सुनिविष्टं हितं वाक्यमुक्तवन्तं विभीषणम्। अब्रवीत्परुषं वाक्यं रावणः कालचोदितः॥
en: Vibhīşaņa addressing him with these excellent and auspicious words, fraught with high sense, Rāvaņa, impelled by Death, again spoke in harsh accents.

sn: वसेत्सह सपत्नेन क्रुद्धनाशीविषेण च। न तु मित्रप्रवादेन संवसेच्छत्रुसेविना॥
en: It is better to live with open enemies or enraged serpents than with those who pass for friends but are in reality foes.

sn: जानामि शीलं ज्ञातीनां सर्वलोकेषु राक्षस। हृष्यन्ति व्यसनेष्वेते ज्ञातीनां ज्ञातयः सदा॥
en: I know well the nature of kinsmen, in all the worlds, O Raksasas, one takes delight in another's misfortune.

sn: प्रधानं साधकं वैद्यं धर्मशीलं च राक्षस। ज्ञातयोऽप्यवमन्यन्ते शूरं परिभवन्ति च॥
en: The kinsmen, O Raksasa, generally disregard him who is their king, * protects the kingdom, educated and pious-and they always try to discomfit him, if he be a heroe. *On account of the priority of his birth,

sn: नित्यमन्योन्यसंहृष्टा व्यसनेष्वाततायिनः। प्रच्छन्नहृदया घोरा ज्ञातयस्तु भयावहाः॥
en: These terrible enemies-the kinsmen, hypocrite as they are, always take delight in one another's calamity.

sn: श्रूयन्ते हस्तिभिर्गीताः श्लोकाः पद्मवने पुरा। पाशहस्तानरान्दृष्ट्वा शृणुष्व गदतो मम॥ नाग्निर्नान्यानि शस्त्राणि न नः पाशा भयावहाः।। घोराः स्वार्थप्रयुक्तास्तु ज्ञातयो नो भयावहाः॥
en: Hear, I shall relate what elephants, in yore, spoke beholding some persons with noose in hand-We do not fear, fire, weapons, or even the terrible noose-we fear only the dreadful kinsmen, blinded with selfishness.

sn: उपायमेते वक्ष्यन्ति ग्रहणे नात्र संशयः। कृत्स्नाद्भयाज्ज्ञातिभयं सुकष्टं विदितं च नः॥
en: They alone unfold the means of our detection, there is not the least doubt about it. Fear from kinsmen is therefore known as the worst of all fears.

sn: विद्यते गोषु संपन्न विद्यते ज्ञातितो भयम्। विद्यते स्त्रीषु चापल्यं विद्यते ब्राह्मणे तपः॥
en: In kine there is milk, in kinsmen, there is fear, in women there is fickleness, and in Brahmanas, there is asceticism.
