sn: ततो नेष्टमिदं सौम्य यदहं लोकसत्कृतः। ऐश्वर्यमभिजातश्च रिपूणां मूर्ध्नि च स्थितः॥
en: It does not please you, I fancy, O gentle one, that I am honoured of the three worlds, the lord of riches, and the subduer of my foes.

sn: यथा पुष्करपत्रेषु पतितास्तोयबिन्दवः। न श्लेषमभिगच्छन्ति तथानार्येषु सौहृदम्॥
en: As the drops of water do not last long on the leaves of lotuses, so is the friendship with unworthy persons.

sn: यथा शरदि मेघानां सिञ्चतामपि गर्जताम्। न भवत्यम्बुसंक्लेदस्तथानार्येषु सौहृदम्॥
en: As the autumnal clouds, albeit muttering, do not pour forth water, so is the friendship with unworthy persons.

sn: यथा मधुकरस्तांद्रसं विन्दन्न तिष्ठति। तथा त्वमपि तत्रैव तथानार्येषु सौहृदम्॥
en: As a bee flies away after sucking up the honey so is the friendship with unworthy persons.

sn: यथा मधुकरस्तर्षात्काशपुष्पं पिबन्नपि। रसमत्रन न विन्देत तथानार्येषु सैहृदम्॥
en: As a bee, after feeding uport the Kāśa flowers, does not get honey so is (fruitless) the friendship with unworthy persons.

sn: यथा पूर्वं गजः स्नात्वा गृह्य हस्तेन वै रजः। दूषयत्यात्मनो देहं तथानार्येषु सौहदम्॥
en: As an elephant, after being bathed, covers its body again with dust, taking it with its trunk, so is the friendship with unworthy persons.* *They afterwards forsake their former friends.

sn: योऽन्यस्त्वेवंविधं ब्रूयाद्वाक्यमेतन्निशाचर। अस्मिन्मुहूर्ते न भवेत्त्वां तु धिक्कुलपांसन॥
en: Fie you, O night ranger, O you that bring disgrace on the family. Had any one else spoken thus he would have ceased to live by this time.

sn: इत्युक्तः परुषं वाक्यं न्यायवादी विभीषणः। उत्पपात गदापाणिश्चतुर्भिः सह राक्षसैः॥
en: Being thus accosted harshly, Vibhisana, speaking truth, rose up along with four Rākṣasas having maces in their hands.

sn: अब्रवीच्च तदा वाक्यं जातक्रोधो विभीषणः। अन्तरिक्षगतः श्रीमान्धाता वै राक्षसाधिपम्॥
en: There upon, rising up in the welkin, the graceful brother Vibhisana, worked up with ire, addressed the lord of Rāshasas.

sn: स त्वं भ्रान्तोऽसि मे राजन्ब्रूहि मां यद्यदिच्छसि। ज्येष्ठो मान्यः पितृसमो न च धर्मपथे स्थितः। इदं हि परुषं वाक्यं न क्षमाम्यग्रजस्य ते॥
en: You are mistaken, O king. Do you speak what you wish, you are my elder brother, adorable like to father-you did not follow the track of virtue. I cannot tolerate the harsh accents of you, my elder brother.

sn: सुनीतं हितकामेन वाक्यमुक्तं दशानन। न गृह्णन्त्यकृतात्मानः कालस्य वशमागताः॥
en: For your welfare I spoke those w ell-meaning words, O Ten-necked one, but you did not pay heed to them being brought under the control of Death.

sn: सुलभाः पुरुषा राजन्सततं प्रियवादिनः। अप्रियस्य च पथ्यस्य वक्ता श्रोता च दुर्लभः॥
en: O king, many are the persons who speak sweet words. hit rare are they who can speak and near anpalatable but well-meaning words.

sn: बद्धं कालस्य पाशेन सर्वभूतापहारिणः। न नश्यन्तमुपेक्षे त्वां प्रदीप्तं शरणं यथा ॥
en: How can I disregard your death like to a burning house bound as you are by the noose of Death, the destroyer of all creatures.

sn: दीप्तपावकसंकाशैः शितैः काञ्चनभूषणैः। न त्वामिच्छाम्यहं द्रष्टुं रामेण निहतं शरैः॥
en: I do not wish to behold you slain by the well sharpened shafts of Rāma, feathered in gold and resembling the flaming fire.

sn: शूराश्च बलवन्तश्च कृतास्त्राश्च नरा रणे। कालाभिपन्नाः सीदन्ति यथा वालुकसेतवः॥
en: Even the heroic and powerful persons, well versed in the use of weapons, wear away like sands in battle, being attracted by Death.

sn: तन्मर्षयतु यच्चोक्तं गुरुत्वाद्धितमिच्छता। आत्मानं सर्वथा रक्ष पुरीं चेमां सराक्षसाम्। स्वस्ति तेऽस्तु गमिष्यामि सुखी भव मया विना॥
en: You are worshipful to me, do you forgive me for what I have said for your welfare. Do you protect yourself and this city, abounding in Raksasas. May good betide you! I am going away and do you be happy without me.

sn: निवार्यमाणस्य मया हितैषिणा न रोचते ते वचनं निशाचर। परान्तकाले हि गतायुषो नरा हितं न गृह्णन्ति सुहृद्भिरीरितम्॥
en: What, I spoke to you, O ranger of the night, to prevent you, for your welfare, did not please you. Persons, whose lease of life is well-nigh expired, do not pay heed to the well-meaning words of their friends.

sn: इत्युक्त्वा परुषं वाक्यं रावणं रावणानुजः। आजगाम मुहूर्तेन यत्र रामः सलक्ष्मणः॥
en: Having addressed Rāvana with these harsh words, his younger brother, reached in no time, where Rāma along with Lakṣmaṇa was.

sn: तं मेरुशिखराकारं दीप्तामिव शतहदाम्। गगनस्थं महीस्थास्ते ददृशुर्वानराधिपाः॥
en: The leading monkeys, stationed on earth, espied him on the welkin, resembling in size the summit of the mount Meru, and burning like lightning in the effulgence of his own person.

sn: ते चाप्यनुचरास्तस्य चत्वारो भीमविक्रमाः। तेऽपि वर्मायुधोपेता भूषणोत्तमभूषिताः॥
en: And his four attendants of terrible prowess were adorned with excellent ornaments and armed with armours and maces.

sn: स च मेघाचलप्रख्यो वज्रायुधसमप्रभः। वरायुधधरो वीरो दिव्याभरणभूषितः॥
en: He was like to a collection of clouds, powerful as the thunder-bolt, holding an excellent mace, heroic and embellished with excellent ornaments.

sn: तमात्मपञ्चमं दृष्ट्वा सुग्रीवो वानराधिपः। वानरैः सह दुर्धर्षश्चिन्तयामास बुद्धिमान्॥
en: Beholding him along with four counsellors, the highly intelligent Sugrīva, the lord of monkeys, engaged in meditation along with them.

sn: चिन्तयित्वा मुहूर्तं तु वानरांस्तानुवाच ह। हनुमत्प्रमुखान्सर्वानिदं वचनमुत्तमम्॥
en: And meditating for a while, he spoke to the monkeys headed by Hanuman the following excellent words.

sn: एष सर्वायुधोपेतश्चतुर्भिः सह राक्षसैः। राक्षसोऽभ्येति पश्यध्वमस्मान्हन्तुं न संशयः।७।।
en: Behold, there comes a Rākşasa, armed with various weapons and followed by four demons to slay us and there is not the least doubt about it.

sn: सुग्रीवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा सर्वे ते वानरोत्तमाः। शालानुद्यम्य शैलांश्च इदं वचनमब्रुवन्।।।।।
en: And hearing the words of Sugrīva, the excellent monkeys, taking up huge trees and crages, bespoke him.

sn: शीघ्रं व्यादिश नो राजन्वधायैषां दुरात्मनाम्। निपतन्ति हता यावद्धरण्यामल्पचेतनाः॥
en: Do you order us, O king, to destroy these vicious-souled demons. These shall crush them to death, limited as is the tenure of their life.

sn: तेषां संभाषमाणानामन्योन्यं स विभीषणः। उत्तरं तीरमासाद्य स्वस्थ एव व्यतिष्ठत॥
en: They addressing each other in this wise, Vibhīşaņa descended from the sky on the northern shore.

sn: स उवाच महाप्राज्ञः स्वरेण महता महान्। सुग्रीवं तांश्च संप्रेक्ष्य स्वस्थ एव विभीषणः॥
en: And beholdings Sugrīva and all others stationed near him, the highly intelligent Vibhīşaņa accosted them, at the highest pitch of his voice, saying.

sn: रावणो नाम दुर्वृत्तो राक्षसो राक्षसेश्वरः। तस्याहमनुजो भ्राता विभीषण इति श्रुतः॥
en: There lives a Raksasa, named Ravana, the lord of demons, and perpetrator of many iniquitous deeds. I am his younger brother known as Vibhişaņa.

sn: तेन सीता जनस्थानाद्धृता हत्वा जटायुषम्। रुद्धा च विवशा दीना राक्षसीभिः सुरक्षिता॥
en: By him, slaying the vulture Jatayu, was carried away Sītā from Janasthana. She is imprisoned, brought under his sway, poorly, and being well guarded by the Rakşasees.

sn: तमहं हेतुभिर्वाक्यैर्विविधैश्च न्यदर्शयम्। साधु निर्यात्यतां सीता रामायेति पुनः पुनः॥
en: With various well meaning words and reasonings I pointed out to him, the necessity of rendering back Sītā to Rāma.

sn: स च न प्रतिजग्राह रावणः कालचोदितः। उच्यमानं हितं वाक्यं विपरीत इवौषधम्॥
en: And Ravana, possessed by Death, paid no heed to my well-meaning words, like to one, lying on the brink of death, neglecting the administration of medicine.

sn: सोऽहं परुषितस्तेन दासवच्चावमानितः। त्यक्त्वा पुत्रांश्च दारांश्च राघवं शरणं गतः॥
en: Being reviled by him and treated harshly like a menial, I have come to seek Rāghava's shelter, renouncing my children and wives.

sn: निवेदयत मां क्षिप्रं राघवाय महात्मने। सर्वलोकशरण्याय विभीषणमुपस्थितम्॥
en: Do you soon mention to the high-souled Rāghava, the refuge of all creatures, that Vibhīşaņa has arrived.

sn: एतत्तु वचनं श्रुत्वा सुग्रीवो लघुविक्रमः। लक्ष्मणस्याग्रतो रामं संरब्धमिदमब्रवीत्॥
en: Hearing those words the quick-paced Sugrīva, excited with ire, spoke to Rāma, before Laksmana, saying.

sn: प्रविष्टः सत्रुसैन्यं हि प्राप्तः शत्रुरतर्कितः। निहन्यादन्तरं लब्ध्वा उलूको वायसानिव॥
en: Forsooth has an enemy entered secretly in our midst and he shall slay us getting an opportunity like to an owl killing the crows.

sn: मन्त्रे व्यूहे नये चारे युक्तो भवितुमर्हसि। वानराणां च भद्रं ते परेषां च परंतप॥
en: O slayer of foes, it now behove you to be particularly careful about the counsels, arrangement of soldiers, polity-civil and military and spies of our own party as well as those of the enemies.

sn: अन्तर्धानगता ह्येते राक्षसाः कामरूपिणः। शूराश्च निकृतिज्ञाश्च तेषां जातु न विश्वसेत्॥
en: These Rākşasas are heroic; they assume shapes at will, always lie in ambush and secretly bring about others' ruin-we should not therefore place confidence in them.

sn: प्रणिधी राक्षसेन्द्रस्य रावणस्य भवेदयम्। अनुप्रविश्य सोऽस्मासु भेदं कुर्यान्न संशयः॥ अथ वा स्वयमेवैष छिद्रमासाद्य बुद्धिमान्। अनुप्रविश्य विश्वस्ते कदाचित्प्रहरेदपि ॥
en: This must be the emissary of Rāvaņa-the lord of Raksasas. Entering in our midst, he shall, in sooth, sow dissensions in our camp, or he shall slay us when we are careless, confiding in them.

sn: मित्राटविबलं चैव मौलभृत्यबलं तथा। सर्वमेतद्वलं ग्राह्यं वर्जयित्वा द्विषद्बलम्॥
en: Avoiding the enemies, we should now collect the forest-rangers our friends and servants.

sn: प्रकृत्या राक्षसो ह्येष भ्रातामित्रस्य वै प्रभो। आगतश्च रिपुः साक्षात्कथमस्मिंश्च विश्वसेत्॥
en: O lord, this man is a Rākşasa by birth and the brother of our foe and so is he our enemy, how can we trust him?

sn: रावणस्यानुजो भ्राता विभीषण इति श्रुतः। चतुर्भिः सह रक्षोभिर्भवन्तं शरणं गतः॥
en: Ravana's younger brother, known Vibilisana, uc come here with four Raksasas, to seck your shelter.

sn: रावणेन प्रणीतं हि तमवेहि विभीषणम्। तस्याहं निग्रहं मन्ये क्षमं क्षमवतां वर॥
en: O you the foremost of forgiving persons, I consider this Vibhīşaņa, who has been despatched by Ravana, worthy of being slain. as

sn: राक्षसो जिह्मया बुद्ध्या संदिष्टोऽयमिहागतः। प्रहर्तुं मायया छनो विश्वस्ते त्वयि चानघ॥ बध्यतामेष तीव्रण दण्डेन सचिवैः सह। रावणस्य नृशंसस्य भ्राता ह्येष विभीषणः॥
en: Being impelled by his wicked intention and commissioned by Rävaņa, this Rākşasa has come here and secretly by virtue of his illusive powers he shall slay you, O innocent one, when you shall place confidence in him.

sn: एवमुक्त्वा तु तं रामं संरब्धो वाहिनीपतिः। वाक्यज्ञो वाक्यकुशलं ततो मौनमुपागमत्॥
en: Having thus accosted Rāma, skilled in the are of speech, that lord of the army, Sugriva, well versed in speech, became silent.

sn: सुग्रीवस्य तु तद्वाक्यं श्रुत्वा रामो महाबलः। समीपस्थानुवाचेदं हनुमत्प्रमुखान्कपीन्॥
en: And hearing the words of Sugrīva, the mighty Rāma spoke to the monkeys, near him, headed by Hanumān, saying.

sn: यदुक्तं कपिराजेन रावणावरजं प्रति। वाक्यं हेतुमदत्यर्थं भवद्भिरपि च श्रुतम्॥
en: You have all heard, the words well grounded in reason, the lord of monkeys has said, regarding Rāvana's younger brother.

sn: सुहृदामर्थकृच्छ्रेषु युक्तं बुद्धिमता सदा। समर्थेनोपसंदेष्टुं शाश्वतीं भूतिमिच्छता॥
en: It behove him, who desires for perpetual wealth, and is intelligent and capable of giving sound counsels, to advise his friends in difficult matters.

sn: इत्येवं परिपृष्टास्ते स्वं स्वं मतमतन्द्रिताः। सोपचारं तदा राममूचुः प्रियचिकीर्षवः॥
en: Being thus addressed by Rāma (to minister to him best counsels) all those monkeys, intent upon encompassing his well-being, gave out their respective opinions.

sn: अज्ञातं नास्ति ते किंचित्रिषु लोकेषु राधव। आत्मानं पूजयन्राम पृच्छस्यस्मान्सुहत्तया ॥
en: O Rāghava, there is nothing beyond your knowledge in the three worlds. It is only to show your respect towards us; O Răma, that you did accost us in this wise.

sn: त्वं हि सत्यव्रतः शूरो धार्मिको दृढविक्रमः। परीक्ष्यकारी स्मृतिमानिसृष्टात्मा सुहृत्सु च।३६।।
en: You are of truthful vows, heroic, pious, of firm prowess, discriminating, recollecting and having implicit confidence in your friends.

sn: तस्मादेकैकशस्तावब्रुवन्तु सचिवास्तव। हेतुतो मतिसंपन्नाः समर्थाश्च पुनस्तथा॥
en: Let the intelligent and capable counsellors deliver their reasonable opinions to you.

sn: इत्युक्ते राघवायाथ मतिमानङ्गदोऽग्रतः। विभीषणपरीक्षार्थमुवाच वचनं हरिः॥
en: They speaking thus to Rāghava, the intelligent monkey Angada, spoke as follows for sounding the intention of Vibhīşaņa.

sn: शत्रोः सकाशात्संप्राप्तः सर्वथा तय॑ एव हि। विश्वासनीयः सहसा न कर्तव्यो विभीषणः॥
en: We should always suspect him since he has come from the side of our enemies, and should not, all on a sudden, place confidence in him.

sn: छादयित्वात्मभावं हि चरन्ति शठबुद्धयः। प्रहरन्ति च रन्ध्रेषु सोऽनर्थः सुमहान्भवेत्॥
en: The wicked-minded always move about hiding their real self, and bring about peoples' calamity, taking advantage of their weak points. And great is the disaster thereof.

sn: अर्थानौँ विनिश्चित्य व्यवसायं भजेत ह। गुणतः संग्रहं कुर्याद्दोषतस्तु विसर्जयेत्॥
en: It is always proper to engage in actions, considering what is right and what is wrong. Virtues should always be gathered and vices abondoned.

sn: यदि दोषो महांस्तस्मिंस्त्यज्यतामविशङ्कितम्। गुणान्वापि बहून्ज्ञात्वा संग्रहः क्रियतां नृप।॥
en: Do you renounce him unhesitatingly, if did you find in him a source of a great calamity and do you embrace him if did you find him crowned with many virtues.

sn: शरभस्त्वथ निश्चित्य सार्थं वचनमब्रवीत्। क्षिप्रमस्मिन्नरव्याघ्र चारः प्रतिविधीयताम्॥
en: There upon followed Sarava with words fraught with high import, best of men, do you speedily despatch emissaries to sound Vibhis ana.

sn: प्रणिधाय हि चारेण यथावत्सूक्ष्मबुद्धिना। परीक्ष्य च ततः कार्यों यथान्यायं परिग्रहः॥
en: If did you, sounding him well through the instrumentality of sharp spies, find him friendly, do you win him over to your side.

sn: जाम्बवांस्त्वथ संप्रेक्ष्य शास्त्रबुद्ध्या विचक्षणः। वाक्यं विज्ञापयामास गुणवद्दोषवर्जितम्॥
en: There upon the wise Jāmbavān, arriving at conclusions by virtue of his knowledge of Šāstras, began with words, void of defects.

sn: बद्धवैराच्च पापाच्च राक्षसेन्द्राद्विभीषणः। अदेशकाले संप्राप्तः सर्वथा शङ्कयतामयम्॥
en: Surely does Vibhīşaņa come from the vicious lord of Räkşasas, dead set against us and has arrived at such a bad piace and in such a bad hour. We should always fear him.

sn: ततो मैन्दस्तु संप्रेक्ष्य नयापनयकोविदः। वाक्यं वचनसंपन्नो बभाषे हेतुमुत्तरम्॥
en: There upon followed Mainda, conversant with what is right and wrong, after due deliberation, with words pregnant with words pregnant with reason.

sn: अनुजो नाम तस्यैष रावणस्य विभीषणः। पृच्छ्यतां मधुरेणायं शनैर्नरपतीश्वर॥
en: He is Rāvana's younger brother, by name Vibhīşana. Let the lord of men ask him every thing at first in sweet words.

sn: भावमस्य तु विज्ञाय तत्त्वतस्त्वं करिष्यसि। यदि दुष्टो न दुष्टो वा बुद्धिपूर्वं नरर्षभ॥
en: Do you first ascertain, O foremost of men, with what intention he has come evil or good and then settle what course to adopt.

sn: अथ संस्कारसंपन्नो हनूमान्सविचोत्तमः। उवाच वचनं श्लक्ष्णमर्थवन्मधुरं लघु॥
en: There upon spoke Hanumān, the foremost of the counsellors and well versed in Šāstras, in accents sweet, glorious and fraught with a high value.

sn: न भवन्तं मतिश्रेष्ठं समर्थं वदतां वरम्। अतिशाययितुं शक्तो बृहस्पतिरपि ब्रुवन्।५१।।
en: Even Brhaspati, (the lord of speech) cannot excel you, capaable,* gifted with the best of intellect and foremost of those skilled in the are of speech, as you are. *Capable to ascertain the truth of all Sastras.

sn: न वादान्नापि संघर्षानाधिक्यान च कामतः। वक्ष्यामि वचनं राजन्यथार्थं राम गौरवात्॥
en: And what I know I speak, o king. I do so, in the interest of Rāma's work and not impelled by my skill in the are of speech, by the pride of being a counsellor, by the vanity of being gifted with a high intellect or by the desire of speaking for its own sake.

sn: अर्थानर्थनिमित्तं हि यदुक्तं सचिवैस्तव। तत्र दोषं प्रपश्यामि क्रिया नह्युपपद्यते॥
en: What your counsellors have said for ascertaining the good or evil intention of Vibhīş aņa appear to me as most defective and productive of no consequence whatever. It is impossible to sound him without any command.* *To command to relate for what he has come.

sn: ऋते नियोगात्सामर्थ्यमवबोद्धं न शक्यते। सहसा विनियोगोऽपि दोषवान्प्रतिभाति मे।५४।।
en: And even to command him now for the same appears to me as improper.

sn: चारप्रणिहितं युक्तं यदुक्तं सचिवैस्तव। अर्थस्यासंभवात्तत्र कारणं नोपपद्यते॥
en: And as regards the despatch of spies, anent what you have been advised by your ministers, I do not observe any utility.

sn: अदेशकाले संप्राप्त इत्ययं यद्भिभीषणः। विवक्षा तत्र मेऽस्तीयं तां निबोध यथामति।५६॥
en: And what little I have thought of, I have something to say (regarding Jambaban's proposal) that Vibhīşaņa has arrived at such a bad place and in such an evil hour.

sn: एष देशश्च कालश्च भवतीह यथा तथा। पुरुषात्पुरुषं प्राप्य तथा दोषगुणावपि ॥ दौरात्म्यं रावणे दृष्ट्वा विक्रमं च तथा त्वयि। युक्तमागमनं ह्यत्र सदृशं तस्य बुद्धितः॥
en: He has really come to a very good place and in a very good hour. And truly has he performed a becoming and sensille action by coming here after duly ascertaining that Rāvana is a vicious wight and you are a pious person-he is full of vices-you are gifted with many virtues-he is tyrannical and you are powerful.

sn: अज्ञातरूपैः पुरुषैः स राजन्पृच्छ्यतामिति। यदुक्तमत्र मे प्रेक्षा काचिदस्ति समीक्षिता॥
en: And what they have said, O king, as regards sounding him through secret spies, appear to me as one requiring great wisdom.

sn: पृच्छयमानो विशङ्केत सहसा बुद्धिमान्वचः। तत्र मित्रं प्रदुष्येत मिथ्या पृष्टं सुखागतम्॥
en: An intelligent man, when questioned by any suddenly, suspects many things. And if the newcomer be a friend and has come here for his own happiness, how greatly shall his mind be changed by such a course?

sn: अशक्यं सहसा राजन्भावो बोद्धं परस्य वै। अन्तरेण स्वरैभिन्नै पुण्यं पश्यतां भृशम्॥
en: Besides by a sudden questioning it is impossible to ascertain the intention of a foreigner. Do you therefore yourself accost him and determine, by his voice, his secret motive.

sn: न त्वस्यब्रुवतो जातु लक्ष्यते दुष्टभावता। प्रसन्न वदनं चापि तस्मान्मे नास्ति संशयः॥
en: I did not however mark anything of his wickedness while he spoke; rather I did observe signs of gladness on his countenance. So I do not suspect him.

sn: अशङ्कितमतिः स्वस्थो न शठः परिसर्पति। न चास्य दुष्टवागस्ति तस्मान्मे नास्ति संशयः॥
en: The wily can never come fearless and undisturbed. Nor were his words cunning. So I do not suspect him.

sn: आकारश्छाद्यमानोऽपि न शक्यो विनिगुहितुम्। बलाद्धि विवृणोत्येव भावमन्तर्गतं नृणाम्॥
en: It is not very easy to hide one's real nature. It manifests itself by force.

sn: देशकालोपपन्नं च कार्य कार्यविदां वर। सफलं कुरुते क्षिप्रं प्रयोगेणाभिसंहितम्॥
en: So this action of Vibhīşana is not out of place or season. When accomplished it shall redound to his own interest.

sn: उद्योगं तव संप्रेक्ष्य मिथ्यावृत्तं च रावणम्। वालिनं च हतं श्रुत्वा सुग्रीवं चाभिषेचितम्॥ राज्यं प्रार्थयमानस्तु बुद्धिपूर्वमिहागतः। एतावतु पुरस्कृत्य विद्यते तस्य संग्रहः॥
en: Considering well your preparations for war and Ravana's vain conduct, hearing of Vah's destruction and Sugrīva's installation on the throne he has, impelled by his good sense, come here, desirous of gaining the kingdom. Taking these into account, it seems prudent to take him to our side.

sn: यथाशक्ति मयोक्तं त राक्षसस्यार्जवं प्रति। प्रमाणं त्वं हि शेषस्य श्रुत्वा बुद्धिमतां वर॥
en: O you the foremost of the intelligent, I have spok thus considering him sincere. It now behove you to perform what you think proper.

sn: अथ रामः प्रसन्नात्मा श्रुत्वा वायुसुतस्य ह। प्रत्यभाषत दुर्धर्षः श्रुतवानात्मनि स्थितम्॥
en: Hearing those words of the Wind-god's son, the irrepressible Rāma, conversant with all the Šāstras, replied, with words expressing his own opinion.

sn: ममापि च विवक्षास्ति काचित्प्रति विभीषणम्। श्रोतुमिच्छामि तत्सर्वं भवद्भिः श्रेयसि स्थितैः॥
en: I have also thought of some thing regarding Vibhisana. I wish you all, interested in my wellbeing, to hear that.

sn: मित्रभावेन संप्राप्तं न त्यजेयं कथंचन। दोषो यद्यपि तस्य स्यात्सतामेतदगर्हितम्॥
en: (Vibhīşaņa) has come here as friend so I cannot forsake him by any means. And even if he has come with any evil intent it is not culpable for the pious to afford him shelter.

sn: सुग्रीवस्त्वथ तद्वाक्यमाभाष्य च विमृश्य च। ततः शुभतरं वाक्यमुवाच हरिपुंगवः॥
en: There upon hearing his words and considering them well, Sugrīva, the lord of the monkeys, replied in more auspicious* word. *More reasonable word.

sn: स दुष्टो वाप्यदुष्टो वा किमेष रजनीचरः। ईदृशं व्यसनं प्राप्तं भ्रातरं यः परित्यजेत् ॥ को नाम स भवेत्तस्य यमेष न परित्यजेत्।
en: Whether this ranger of the night is sincere or wicked, he should never be offered any shelter, since he has forsaken his brother in the midst of these calamities. What reason is there to believe that he shall not renounce us in our difficulty?

sn: वानराधिपतेर्वाक्यं श्रुत्वा सर्वानुदीक्ष्य तु॥ ईषदुत्स्मयमानस्तु लक्ष्मणं पुण्यलक्षणम्। इति होवाच काकुत्स्थो वाक्यं सत्यपराक्रमः।७।।
en: Hearing the words of the lord of monkeys and casting his looks towards them, Kākutstha, having truth for his prowess, smiling a little, spoke, to Lakşmana, crowned with all the marks of piery, saying.

sn: अनधीत्य च शास्त्राणि वृद्धाननुपसेव्य च। न शक्यमीदृशं वक्तुं यदुवाच हरीश्वरः॥
en: Without being conversant with Sastras, and living in the company of old men, none can speak such words as have been uttered by the king of the minkeys.

sn: अस्ति सूक्ष्मतरं किंचिद्यथात्र प्रतिभाति मा। प्रत्यक्षं लौकिकं चापि वर्तते सर्वराजसु॥
en: There appear to me, however two subtler reasons anent the difference between brothers, among the kings-one is evident and another mundane.

sn: अमित्रास्तत्कुलीनाश्च प्रातिदेश्याश्च कीर्तिताः। व्यसनेषु प्रहरिस्तस्मादयमिहागतः॥
en: There are two classes of foes-one consisting of the members of the same line the other of the neighbours. And these generally bring about our misfortune whenever any opportunity presents itself. And it is for this that he has he has come here.

sn: अपापास्तत्कुलीनाश्च मानयन्ति स्वकान्हितान्। एष प्रायो नरेन्द्राणां शङ्कनीयस्तु शोभनः॥
en: Those kinsmen, who do not think of one another's mischief, generally long for their respective well-being. But even such wellmeaning relatives are feared by the kings.

sn: यस्तु दोषस्त्वया प्रोक्तो ह्यादानेऽरिबलस्य च। तत्र ते कीर्तयिष्यामि यथाशास्त्रमिदं शृणु ॥
en: And hear, I shall relate, what the Sastras say regarding the weak points you have mentioned as to the advisability of taking the enemies to our side.

sn: न वयं तत्कुलीनाश्च राज्यकाझी च राक्षसः। पण्डिता हि भविष्यन्ति तस्माद्ग्राह्यो विभीषणः॥
en: We are not his kinsmen and this Rākşasa has come here with a view to gain the kingdom. Even the Rākşasas are wise enough to ascertain the proper course-so we must take Vibhisana.

sn: अव्यग्राश्च प्रहृष्टाश्च ते भविष्यन्ति संगताः। प्रणादश्च महानेषोऽन्योन्यस्य भयमागतम्। इति भेदं गमिष्यन्ति तस्मात्प्राप्तो विभीषणः॥
en: If the brothers are confident and satisfied with each other they generally live together, or else they fear each other and ultimately engage in a tumultuous war. And there has sprung up some difference with Råvana and therefore Vibhīşaņa has come here.

sn: न सर्वे भ्रातरस्तात भवन्ति भरतोपमाः। मद्विधा वा पितुः पुत्राः सुहृदो वा भवद्विधाः॥
en: Nor are, O friend, all brothers like Bharata, all sons like me to their and all friends like you.

sn: एवमुक्तस्तु रामेण सुग्रीवः सहलक्ष्मणः। उत्थायेदं महाप्राज्ञः प्रणतो वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
en: Being thus addressed by Rāma, the highly wise Sugriva, along with Lakşmaņa, rose up and bending low his head, said.

sn: रावणेन प्रणिहितं तमवेहि निशाचरम्। तस्याहं निग्रहं मन्ये क्षमं क्षमवतां वर॥
en: O you the best of all forgiving persons, this night-ranger has been despatched by Rāvana. I therefore think it better to kill him.

sn: राक्षसो जिह्मया बुद्ध्या संदिष्टोऽयमिहागतः। प्रहर्तुं त्वयि विश्वस्ते विश्वस्ते मयि वाऽनघ॥ लक्ष्मणे वा महाबाहो स वध्यः सचिवैः सह। रावणस्य नृशंसस्य भ्राता ह्येष विभीषणः॥
en: Being impelled by his vicious sense that Rākṣasa has come here to slay us, o innocent one, when myself, you and Laksmana shall consider ourselves secure. Therefore the largearmed Vibhīşaņa the younger brother of the ruthless Rāvana, deserves to be slain along with his counsellors.

sn: एवमुक्त्वा रघुश्रेष्ठं सुग्रीवो वाहिनीपतिः। वाक्यज्ञो वाक्यकुशलं ततो मौनमुपागमत् ॥
en: Having thus addressed (Rama) the foremost of Raghu's race, skilled in are of speech, Sugrīva, the lord of monkey host, equally versed in the are of speech, became silent.

sn: स सुग्रीवस्य तद्वाक्यं रामः श्रुत्वा विमृश्य च। ततः शुभतरं वाक्यमुवाच हरिपुङ्गवम्॥
en: Hearing the words of Sugrīva, and weighing them, Rāma again addressed the foremost of monkeys with more reasonable accents.

sn: स दुष्टो वाऽप्यदुष्टो वा किमेष रजनीचरः। सूक्ष्ममप्यहितं कर्तुं मम शक्तः कथंचन ॥
en: Wicked or other wise, whatever this nightranger may be, he shall not be able to do me the least mischief.

sn: पिशाचान्दानवान्यक्षान्पृथिव्यां चैव राक्षसान्। अङ्गुल्यग्रेण तान्हन्यामिच्छन्हरिगणेश्वर ॥
en: Piśācas, Dānavas, Yakşas or all the Rākşasas on earth, I can slay them all, if I like, with the tips of my fingers, O you the lord of monkeys.

sn: श्रूयते हि कपोतेन शत्रुः शरणमागतः। अर्चितश्च यथान्यायं स्वैश्च मासैनिमन्त्रितः॥
en: I have heard of a pigeon adoring and entertaining with its own flesh, an enemy who took its shelter.

sn: स हि तं प्रतिजग्राह भार्याहर्तारमागतम्। कपोतो वानरश्रेष्ठ किंपुनर्मद्विधो जनः॥
en: While a pigeon received so friendly its enemy, the slayer of its mate, how can I then act otherwise, O foremost of the monkeys?

sn: ऋषेः कण्वस्य पुत्रेण कण्डुना परमर्षिणा। शृणु गाथा पुरा गीता धर्मिष्ठा सत्यवादिना॥
en: Do you hear, I shall relate, a sacred story, narrated by the great ascetic, the truthful Kandu, son of the ascetic Kanyā.

sn: बद्धाञ्जलिपुटं दीनं याचन्तं शरणागतम्। न हन्यादानृशंस्यार्थमपि शत्रु परंतप॥
en: o slayer of foes, even a wicked-minded enemy, if he, with folded palms and a poor heart, crave for your shelter, should not be slain.

sn: आतॊ वा यदि वा दृप्तः परेषां शरणं गतः। अरिः प्राणान्परित्यज्य रक्षितव्यः कृतात्मना॥
en: If an enemy, proud or terrified, seek shelter in affright, he should be saved by a great man even at the risk of his own life.

sn: स चेद्रयाद्वा मोहाद्वा कामाद्वापि न रक्षति। स्वया शक्त्या यथान्यायं तत्पापं लोकगर्हितम्॥
en: One, who from fear, ignorance or wilfully does not protect him who seek his shelter, perpetrate a mighty iniquity, blamed of all.

sn: विनष्टः पश्यतस्तस्य रक्षिणः शरणं गतः। आदाय सुकृतं तस्य सर्वं गच्छेदरक्षितः॥
en: When a person is slain before him whose shelter he has taken he take away all the virtues of his protector.

sn: एवं दोषो महानत्र प्रपन्नानामरक्षणे। अस्वयं चायशस्यं च बलवीर्यविनाशनम्॥
en: So great is the sin in not affording shelter to those who seek for it; it stands in the way of going to heaven, brings in calumny and destroys the strength and prowess.

sn: करिष्यामि यथार्थं तु कण्डोर्वचनमुत्तमम्। धर्मिष्ठं च यशस्यं च स्वयं स्यात्तु फलोदये॥
en: I shall therefore follow the excellent words of Kaņdu-leading to piety, fame and the attainment of the abode of the celestials.

sn: सकृदेव प्रपन्नाय तवास्मीति च याचते। अभयं सर्वभूतेभ्यो ददाम्येतद्ब्रतं मम॥
en: I always declare 'no fear' to all creatures, whenever any, approaching me, says, 'I am thine' and seek my shelter. Even this is my pious observance.

sn: आनयैनं हरिश्रेष्ठ दत्तमस्याभयं मया। विभीषणो वा सुग्रीव यदि वा रावणः स्वयम्॥
en: O Sugrīva, O foremost of monkeys, do you soon bring him here, whether he be Rāvaņa or Vibhisana and I shall declare to him 'no fear'.

sn: रामस्य तु वचः श्रुत्वा सुग्रीवः प्लवगेश्वरः। प्रत्यभाषत काकुत्स्थं सौहार्दैनाभिपूरितः॥
en: Hearing the words of Rāma, Sugriva, the lords of those who go bounding, over-flowing with friendliness, bespake Kākutstha.

sn: किमत्र चित्रं धर्मज्ञ लोकनाथशिखामणे। यत्त्वमार्य प्रभाषेथाः सत्त्ववान्सत्पथे स्थितः॥
en: What wonder is there that you wouldst speak these auspicious words, O you the foremost of kings, conversant with morality, gifted with prowess and ever treading the pious track as you are.

sn: मम चाप्यन्तरात्माऽयं शुद्धं वेत्ति विभीषणम्। अनुमानाच्च भावाच्च सर्वतः सुपरीक्षितः॥
en: Truly does my inner self regard Vibhīşana as devoid of any wicked intention. He has been well sounded by signs and gestures.

sn: तस्मात्क्षिप्रं सहास्माभिस्तुल्यो भवतु राघव। विभीषणो महाप्राज्ञः सखित्वं चाभ्युपैतु नः॥
en: And let the greatly wise Vibhīşaņa, O Rāghava, be placed on an equal footing with us and gain our friendship.

sn: ततस्तु सुग्रीववचो निशम्य तद्धरीश्वरेणाभिहितं नरेश्वरः। विभीषणेनाशु जगाम संगमं पतत्त्रिराजेन यथा पुरन्दरः॥
en: Hearing the words of Sugrīva, the lord of monkeys, the king of men (Rāma) made instantly friends with Vibhīşaņa, like to the conqueror of enemies' cities making friends with the king of birds.

sn: राघवेणाभये दत्ते संनतो रावणानुजः। विभीषणो महाप्राज्ञो भूमि समवलोकयत्॥ खात्पपातावनि हृष्टो भक्तैरनुचरैः सह। स तु रामस्य धर्मात्मा निपपात विभीषणः॥
en: Rāghava thus declaring to him 'no fear' Ravana's younger brother, the greatly wise Vibhișana, bending low his head, cast his looks on the earth.

sn: पादयोनिपपाताथ चतुर्भिः सह राक्षसैः। अब्रवीच्च तदा वाक्यं रामं प्रति विभीषणः॥ धर्मयुक्तं च युक्तं च सांप्रतं संप्रहर्षणम्।
en: Descending from the welkin with his devoted attendants the virtuous-souled Vibhisana, delighted, bowed to Rāma. And thereupon touching his feet along with four Rākşasas, Vibhisana addressed Rama, with words, fraught with piety, befitting the occasion and conducing to pleasure.

sn: अनुजो रावणस्याहं तेन चास्म्यवमानितः॥ भवन्तं सर्वभूतानां शरण्यं शरणं गतः। परित्यक्ता मया लङ्का मित्राणि च धनानि च॥ भवद्गतं हि मे राज्यं जीवितं च सुखानि च।
en: I am Rāvana's younger brother and have been greatly insulted by him. I have therefore come to seek your shelter, the refuge of all creatures, abandoning Lanka and renouncing my friends and riches. My kingdom, life and happiness are all at your disposal.

sn: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा रामो वचनमब्रवीत्॥ वचसा सान्त्वयित्वैनं लोचनाभ्यां पिबनिव।
en: Hearing his words Räma replied, comforting him with words and favouring him as if with looks.

sn: आख्याहि मम तत्त्वेन राक्षसानां बलाबलम्॥ एवमुक्तं तदा रक्षो रामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा। रावणस्य बलं सर्वमाख्यातुमुपचक्रमे।४।।
en: Do you relate to me truly the strength and weakness of the enemies. Being thus accosted by Råma unwearied actions, the Raksasa, began to describe the strength of Rāvana.

sn: अवध्यः सर्वभूतानां गन्धर्वोरंगपक्षिणाम्। राजपुत्र दशग्रीवो वरदानात्स्वयंभुवः॥
en: O prince, by virtue of the bocn acquired from the Self-Create, the Ten-necked one is incapable of being slain by all creatures-Gandharvas, serpents, or birds.

sn: रावणानन्तरो भ्राता मम ज्येष्ठश्च वीर्यवान्। कुम्भकर्णो महातेजाः शक्रप्रतिबलो युधि॥
en: My elder brother, the one next to Rāvana, is the heroic and highly effulgent Kumbhakarņa, Śakra's equal in battle.

sn: राम सेनापतिस्तस्य प्रहस्तो यदि ते श्रुतः। कैलासे येन समरे मणिभद्रः पराजितः॥
en: You may have heard, O Rama, his commander is Prahasta, by whom was defeated Manibhadra on the mount Kailāsa.

sn: बद्धगोधाङ्गुलित्रश्च अवध्वकवचो युधि। धनुरादाय यस्तिष्ठन्नदृश्यो भवतीन्द्रजित्॥
en: (His son) Indrajit, equipped with invincible armour, bow and finger-protector made of the skin of iguana, becomes invisible in fight.

sn: संग्रामे सुमहद्व्यूहे तर्पयित्वा हुताशनम्। अन्तर्धानगतः श्रीमानिन्द्रजिद्धन्ति राघव॥
en: And, worshipping Fire and becoming invisible, Indrajit, that graceful hero, O Raghava, slays the enemies in conflict, having the contending parties vast and well arranged.

sn: महोदरमहापाचौं राक्षसश्चाप्यकम्पनः। अनीकपास्तु तस्यैते लोकपालसमा युधि ॥
en: Mahodara, Mahāpārsva and the Rākşasa, Akampana, are his lieutenants, who equal the Lokapālas* in battle. *Divinities who protect regions, or the Sun, Moon, Fire, Wind, Indra, Yama, Varuna and Kabera.

sn: दशकोटिसहस्राणि रक्षसां कामरूपिणाम्। मांसशोणितभक्ष्याणां लङ्कापुरनिवासिनाम्॥ स तैस्तु सहितो राजा लोकपालानयोधयत्। सह देवैस्तु ते भग्ना रावणेन दुरात्मना॥
en: His army consists of ten thousand kotis of Rākşasas, wearing shapes at will, inhabiting the city of Lankā, and living on flesh and gore. And with the Lokpalas and the celestials, they were all defeated by the vicious-souled Ravana.

sn: विभीषणस्य तु वचस्तच्छुत्वा रघुसत्तमः। अन्वीक्ष्य मनसा सर्वमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Hearing the words of Vibhīşana and weighing them in his mind, that foremost of Raghu's race said.

sn: यानि कर्मापदानानि रावणस्य विभीषण। आख्यातानि च तत्त्वेन ह्यवगच्छामि तान्यहम्॥
en: I understand well the strength and prowess of Ravana, which you have depicted truly, O Vibhisana.

sn: अहं हत्वा दशग्रीवं सप्रहस्तं सहात्मजम्। राजानं त्वां करिष्यामि सत्यमेतच्छृणोतु मे॥
en: Do you hear truly that I shall slay the Tennecked one together with Prahasta and his sons, and I shall make you king.

sn: रसातलं वा प्रविशेत्पातालं वापि रावणः। पितामहसकाशं वा न मे जीवन्विमोक्ष्यते॥
en: Whether he entered the Rasåtala or the regions under the earth, or seek shelter of the Grand-father of the celestials, he shall not be able to save his life from me.

sn: अहत्वा रावणं संख्ये सपुत्रजनबान्धवम्। अयोध्यां न प्रवेक्ष्यामि त्रिभिस्तैर्धातृभिः शपे॥
en: I do swear by my three brethren that I shall enter the city of Ayodhyā, after slaying in battle Ravana with his sons, kinsmen and friends.

sn: श्रुत्वा तु वचनं तस्य रामस्याक्लिष्टकर्मणः। शिरसावन्द्य धर्मात्मा वक्तुमेव प्रचक्रमे॥
en: Hearing these words of Rāma of unwearied action, the virtuous-souled (Vibhisana), bowing his head to him, began.

sn: राक्षसानां वधे साह्यं लङ्कायाश्च प्रधर्षणे। करिष्यामि यथाप्राणं प्रवेक्ष्यामि च वाहिनीम्॥
en: I shall lend you my might in slaying the Raksasas and devastating the city of Larkā, and shall be in the midst of Rāvana's army.

sn: इति ब्रुवाणं रामस्तु परिष्वज्य विभीषणम्। अब्रवील्लक्ष्मणं प्रीतः समुद्राज्जलमानय॥ तेन चेमं महाप्राज्ञमभिषिञ्च विभीषणम्। राजानं रक्षसां क्षिप्रं प्रसन्ने मयि मानद॥
en: There upon, embracing Vibhīşaņa, who spoke thus, Rama, delighted, said to Laksmana, Omy brother, do you bring water from the ocean. Sprinkling the greatly wise Vibhișana, I shall make him at once the king of the Rākşasas, o confrere of honour; for I am greatly pleased with him.

sn: एवमुक्तस्तु सौमित्रिरभ्यषिञ्चद्विभीषणम्। मध्ये वानरमुख्यानां राजानं राजशासनात्॥
en: Being thus addressed, Saumitri, at the command of the king, anointed Vibhișana and made him the king of the Räkşasas in the presence of the monkey host.

sn: तं प्रसादं तु रामस्य दृष्ट्वा सद्यः प्लवङ्गमाः। प्रचुक्रुशुर्महात्मानं साधुसाध्विति चाब्रुवन्॥
en: Beholding Rāma's kindness (towards Vibhīş ana), the monkeys eulogized the high-souled one, exclaiming “Excellent! Excellent!”

sn: अब्रवीच्च हनूमांश्च सुग्रीवश्च विभीषणम्। कथं सागरमक्षोभ्यं तराम वरुणालयम्। सैन्यैः परिवृताः सर्वे वानराणां महौजसाम्॥
en: Thereupon, Hanumān and Sugrīva addressed Vibhisana, saying, Do you tell us how we shall cross over the main-the abode of Varuņa, along with the host of the highly powerful monkeys.

sn: उपायैरभिगच्छाम यथा नदनदीपतिम्। तराम तरसा सर्वे ससैन्या वरुणालयम्॥
en: Do you inform us of the means by which we may cross over, along with our army, the lord of rivers and streams-the abode of Varuna."

sn: एवमुक्तस्तु धर्मात्मा प्रत्युवाच विभीषणः। समुद्रं राघवो राजा शरणं गन्तुमर्हसि॥
en: Being thus addressed, the virtuous-souled Vibhisana replied, "It behovth the king, Rāghava, to seek refuge from the Ocean.

sn: खानितः सगरेणायमप्रमेयो महोदधिः। कर्तुमर्हसि रामस्य ज्ञातेः कार्य महोदधिः॥
en: This measureless deep was dug out by (the king) Sagara.* And the great ocean shall surely help Rāma belonging to Sagara's race. *Sagara was a sovereign of Ayodhyā, belonging to the same family with Rāma.

sn: एवं विभीषणेनोक्तं राक्षसेन विपश्चिता। आजगामाथ सुग्रीवो यत्र रामः सलक्ष्मणः॥
en: Being thus accosted by the wise Rākşasa, Vibhīşaņa. Sugrīva reached where Rāma with Laksmana was.

sn: ततश्चाख्यातुमारेभे विभीषणवचः शुभम्। सुग्रीवो विपुलग्रीवः सागरस्योपवेशनम् ॥
en: Thereupon, the broad-necked Sugrīva began to explain the well-meaning words of Vibhīşaņa, requesting Ráma to seek the shelter of the Ocean.

sn: प्रकृत्या धर्मशीलस्य रामस्यास्याप्यरोचत। सलक्ष्मणं महातेजाः सुग्रीवं च हरीश्वरम्॥ सत्क्रियाएं क्रियादक्षं स्मितपूर्वमभाषत।
en: And those words pleased Răma, pious by nature. And the highly effulgent (hero) requested, smiling, the active Lakşmaņa and the monkey-chief Sugrīva to collect necessaries for his adoration.

sn: विभीषणस्य मन्त्रोऽयं मम लक्ष्मण रोचते॥ सुग्रीवः पण्डितो नित्यं भवान्मन्त्रविचक्षणः। उभाभ्यां संप्रधार्थिं रोचते यत्तदुच्यताम्॥
en: O Lakşmaņa, this counsel of Vibhīşaņa appear to me as most sound. Sugrīva is a ways greatly wise, and you are greatly proficient in counsel. Do you, holding a conference, intimate to me what you think becoming."

sn: एवमुक्तौ ततो वीरावुभौ सुग्रीवलक्ष्मणौ। समुदाचारसंयुक्तमिदं वचनमूचतुः॥
en: Thus addressed, those two heroes-Lakşmaņa and Sugriva, spoke respectfully the following words fraught with propriety.

sn: किमर्थं नौ नरव्याघ्र न रोचिष्यति राघव। विभीषणेन यत्तूक्तमस्मिन्काले सुखावहम्॥
en: Why shall not the well-meaning words of Vibhīşaņa expressed now, please us O Rāghava, O you best of men?

sn: अबद्धा सागरे सेतुं घोरेऽस्मिन्वरुणालये। लङ्का नासादितुं शक्या सेन्ट्रैरपि सुरासुरैः॥
en: Without constructing a bridge over the deep, the terrible abode of Varuņa, even the celestials and their lord (India) cannot get at the city of Lanka.

sn: विभीषणस्य शूरस्य यथार्थं क्रियतां वचः। अलं कालात्ययं कृत्वा सागराय नियुज्यताम्। यथा सैन्येन गच्छाम पुरीं रावणपालिताम्॥
en: Do you act on the genuine counsel of the heroic Vibhisana, and without losing time, do you engage the Ocean for this work, so that we may with our army proceed to the city protected by Ravana.

sn: एवमुक्तः कुशास्तीणे तीरे नदनदीपतेः। संविवेश तदा रामो वेद्यामिव हुताशनः॥
en: Being thus addressed Räma reached the shore of the lord of rivers and streams, covered with Kusa, like to fire getting into the sacrificial dais.

sn: ततो निविष्टां ध्वजिनीं सुग्रीवेणाभिपालिताम्। ददर्श राक्षसोऽभ्येत्य शार्दूलो नाम वीर्यवान्॥ चारो राक्षसराजस्य रावणस्य दुरात्मनः। तां दृष्ट्वा सर्वतोऽव्यग्रां प्रतिगम्य स राक्षसः॥ आविश्य लङ्कां वेगेन राजानमिदमब्रवीत्।
en: Thereupon the greatly powerful Rākşasa, by name Śārdüla, beheld the army of Sugrīva arranged on the shore of the ocean. And, beholding the army all busy, the emissary of the vicious-souled Raksasa-Ravana, entered the city of Lanka and, approaching his lord, said.

sn: एष वै वानरक्षौंधो लङ्कां समभिवर्तते॥ अगाधश्चाप्रमेयश्च द्वितीय इव सागरः।
en: The army of monkeys and bears has approached Lanka. It is immeasurably deep as the ocean.

sn: पुत्रौ दशरथस्येमौ भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ॥ उत्तमौ रूपसंपन्नौ सीतायाः पदमागतौ। एतौ सागरमासाद्य संनिविष्टौ महाद्युते॥ बलं चाकाशमावृत्य सर्वतो दशयोजनम्। तत्त्वभूतं महाराज क्षिप्रं वेदितुमर्हसि॥ तव दूता महाराज क्षिप्रमर्हन्ति वेदितुम्। उपप्रदानं सान्त्वं वा भेदो वात्र प्रयुज्यताम्॥
en: And those two sons of the king Dasarathathe brothers Rāma and Lakşmaņa, gifted with great beauty, coming to rescue Sītā, have stationed themselves on the shore of the ocean, O you of great effulgence. The army of Rāma extends over the sky and ten yojanas. I have come, O great king, to acquaint you with the real truth. And, knowing everything, it behove your emissaries, O king, to settle whether to render back Sītā, to adopt measures of conciliation, or to sow dissension's in the enemy's camp.

sn: शार्दूलस्य वचः श्रुत्वा रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः। उवाच सहसा व्यग्रः संप्रधार्यार्थमात्मनः। शुकं साधु तदा रक्षो वाक्यमर्थविदां वरम्।।।।।
en: Hearing the words of Sardāla, Ravana, the lord of Rākşasas, being anxious to ascertain his duty, addressed a Raksasa by name Suka, the most sensible of his counsellors, with the following pregnant words.

sn: सुग्रीवं ब्रूहि गत्वाशु राजानं वचनान्मम। यथासंदेहमक्लीबं श्लक्ष्णया परया गिरा॥
en: Do you go and communicate to king Sugrīva my behest, in becoming and excellent accents.

sn: त्वं वै महाराजकुलप्रसूतो महाबलश्चःरजःसुतश्च। स्तथापि मे भ्रातृसमो हरीश॥
en: You are born of a great family and are the mighty son of the king of bears. I have no dissension with you. In fact I consider you as my brother, O king of monkeys.

sn: अहं यद्यहरं भायाँ राजपुत्रस्य धीमतः। किं तत्र तव सुग्रीव किष्किन्धां प्रति गम्यताम्॥
en: Though I have stolen the spouse of the highsouled prince (Räma), yet what is that to you, Sugriva? Do you return to Kiskindhā.

sn: नहीयं हरिभिर्लङ्का प्राप्तुं शक्या कथंचन। देवैरपि सगन्धर्वैः किं पुनर्नरवानरैः॥
en: The monkeys shall not by any means be able to attack the city of Lankā. Even the celestials and Gandharvas could not-what of these men and monkeys?

sn: स तदा राक्षसेन्द्रेण संदिष्टो रजनीचरः। शुको विहंगमो भूत्वा तूर्णमाप्लुत्य चाम्बरम्॥
en: And being thus commissioned by the lord of Rākşasas, that night-ranger assumed the shape of a bird and, bounding, speedily reached the sky.

sn: स गत्वा दूरमध्वानमुपर्युपरि सागरम्। संस्थितो ज़म्बरे वाक्यं सुग्रीवमिदमब्रवीत्॥ सर्वमुक्तं यथादिष्टं रावणेन दुरात्मना।
en: And, proceeding far over the deep and stationing himself at the welkin, he spoke to Sugrīva all the words with which he was addressed by the vicious-souled Ravana.

sn: तत्प्रापयन्तं वचनं तूणमाप्लुत्य वानराः॥ प्रापद्यन्तः तदा क्षिप्रं लोप्नुं हन्तुं च मुष्टिभिः।
en: Hearing him speak thus, the monkeys leaped up quickly and reached there with a view to chop off his wings or to slay him with their clenched fists.

sn: सर्वैः प्लवंगैः प्रसभं निगृहीतो निशाचरः॥ गगनाद्भूतले चाशु प्रतिगृह्यावतारितः।
en: On being seized vehemently by all these monkeys, that night-ranger was brought down speedily from the sky to the earth.

sn: वानरैः पीड्यमानस्तु शुको वचनमब्रवीत्॥ न दूतान्विन्ति काकुत्स्थ वार्यन्तां साधु वानराः। यस्तु हित्वा मतं भर्तुः स्वमतं संप्रधारयेत्। अनुक्तवादी दूतः सन्स दूतो वधमर्हति॥
en: And being assailed by the monkeys, suka said, O Kākutstha, it does not behove (people) to slay an emissary. Do you therefore prevent the monkeys. He who passing by his master's behest, give out his own intention, is not faithful; and he therefore deserve to be slain.

sn: शुकस्य वचनं रामः श्रुत्वा तु परिदेवितम्। उवाच मावधिष्टेति घ्नतः शाखामृगर्षभान्॥१९
en: Hearing the piteous accents of Suka, Rama spoke to the monkeys, who were about to kill him, saying, Do not kill him.

sn: स च पत्रलघुर्भूत्वा हरिभिर्दर्शितेऽभये। अन्तरिक्षे स्थितो भूत्वा पुनर्वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: And again stationing himself on the welkin, that night-ranger said.

sn: सुग्रीव सत्त्वसंपन्न महाबलपराक्रम। किं मया खलु वक्तव्यो रावणो लोकरावणः॥
en: O Sugrīva, O you gifted with great energy, O you of great prowess, what shall I speak to Rāvana, dreaded by all people?

sn: स एवमुक्तः प्लवगाधिपस्तदा प्लवङ्गमानामृषभो महाबलः। उवाच वाक्यं रजनीचरस्य चारं शुकं शुद्धमदीनसत्त्वः॥
en: Being thus addressed, that mighty king of monkeys the bull among them, of unwearied energy, spoke to that emissary—the nightranger, Suka, saying.

sn: न मेऽसि मित्रं न तथानुकम्प्यो न चोपकर्तासि न मे प्रियोऽसि। स्ततोऽसि वालीव वधार्ह वध्यः॥
en: O Rāvana, you are not my friend or an object of pity. You are not my benefactor, not are liked by me. You are Rāma's enemy, and you did therefore deserve to be slain by him like Vāli along with your friends and relatives.

sn: निहन्म्यहं त्वां ससुतं सबन्धु सज्ञातिवर्गं रजनीचरेश। लङ्कां च सर्वां महता बलेन सर्वैः करिष्यामि समेत्य भस्म॥
en: I shall therefore slay you, O king of nightrangers, together with your sons, friends and relatives. And I shall have the whole city of Lankă reduced to ashes by my mighty force.

sn: न मोक्ष्यसे रावण राघवस्य सर्वैः सहेन्द्रैरपि मूढ गुप्तः। अन्तर्हितः सूर्यपथं गतोऽपि तथैव पातालमनुप्रविष्टः।। गिरीशपादाम्बुजसंगतो वा हतोऽसि रामेण सहानुजस्त्वम्।।
en: You shall not be able to escape Rāghava, O Rāvana, O you who have lost your sense, even if you are protected by the celestials. And you shall with your brother be slain by Rāma, even if you did fly into the sky, enter into the regions under the earth, or seek shelter of Mahādeva.

sn: तस्य ते त्रिषु लोकेषु न पिशाचं न राक्षसम्। त्रातारं नानुपश्यामि न गन्धवं च चासुरम्॥
en: I do not behold any in these three worldsPiśāca, Rākşasa, Gandharva, or Asura, who can protect you.

sn: अवधीस्त्वं जरावृद्धं गृध्रराजं जटायुषम्। किं न ते रामसांनिध्ये सकाशे लक्ष्मणस्य च। हृता सीता विशालाक्षी यां त्वं गृह्य न बुध्यसे ॥ महाबलं महात्मानं दुराधर्ष सुरैरपि। न बुध्यसे रघुश्रेष्ठं यस्ते प्राणान्हरिष्यति॥
en: You have slain the monarch of vultures, who had grown decrepit through age.* You have carried off the large-eyed Sītā from the vicinity of Räma and the neighbourhood of Lakṣmaṇa; but, having captured her, you understand not (your native strength). Nor did you understand that foremost of Raghus, high-souled, possessed of great strength, and incapable of being repressed even by the celestials, who shall take your life. *The commentator has a queer and characteristic note on farduridha-decrepit through age. One that is old, may stave off decrepitude through some drug, while a youthful person may come by the same in consequence of some curse.

sn: ततोऽब्रवीद्वालिसुतोऽप्यङ्गदो हरिसत्तमः। नायं दूतो महाप्राज्ञ चारकः प्रतिभाति मे॥ तुलितं हि बलं सर्वमनेन तव तिरता। गृह्यतां मागमल्लङ्कामेतद्धि मम रोचते॥
en: Then spoke that best of monkeys, Angada, son of Vali, O highly wise one, this is no emissary. This one clearly appear to me as a spy. He has come to form and estimate of your entire army. Take him. Let him not go (back) to lanka. This is indeed what I would,

sn: ततो राज्ञा समादिष्टाः समुत्पत्य वलीमुखाः। जगृहुश्च वबन्धुश्च विलपन्तमनाथवत्॥
en: Thereat, commanded by the king, the monkeys, springing up, seized (Suka) and bound him, as he burst out bewailing like one forlorn.

sn: शुकस्तु वानरैश्चण्डैस्तत्र तैः संप्रपीडितः। व्याचुक्रोश महात्मानं रामं दशरथात्मजम्। लुप्येत मे बलात्पक्षौ भिद्येते मे तथाक्षिणी॥ यां च रात्रिं मरिष्यामि जाये रात्रिं च यामहम्। एतस्मिन्नन्तरे काले यन्मया ह्यशुभं कृतम्।। सर्वं तदुपपद्येथा जह्यां चेद्यदि जीवितम्॥
en: On being sorely handled by the relentless monkeys, Suka cried to the high-souled Rāma, son of Daśaratha, 'They by main force sever my wings, and they pierce my eyes. If I lose my life, may all the evil deeds that I have committed between the night when I was born and the night when I shall die, be your!

sn: नाघातयत्तदा रामः श्रुत्वा तत्परिदेवितम्। वानरानब्रवीद्रामो मुच्यतां दूत आगतः॥
en: Hearing this pitiful cry, Rāma prevented (the monkeys); and he said to them, Let go this envoy, who has come here.

sn: ततः सागरवेलायां दर्भानास्तीर्य राघवः। अञ्जलिं प्राङ्मुखः कृत्वा प्रतिशिश्ये महोदधेः॥
en: Then on the shore of the sea, Rāghava, spreading darbha, with his hands joined towards the great deep, laid him down, with his face to the East.

sn: बाहुं भुजङ्गभोगाभमुपधायारिसूदनः। जारूपमयैश्चैव भूषणैर्भूषितं सदा॥ गणिकाचनकेयूरमुक्तप्रवरभूषणैः। भुजैः परमनारीणामभिमृष्टमनेकधा॥ चन्दनागुरुभिश्चैव पुरस्तादभिसेवितम्। बालसूर्यप्रकाशैश्च चन्दनैरुपशोभितम्॥ शयने चोत्तमाङ्गेन सीतायाः शोभितं पुरा। तक्षकस्येव संभोगं गङ्गाजलनिषेवितम्॥ संयुगे युगसंकाशं शत्रूणां शोकवर्धनम्। सुहृदां नन्दनं दीर्घ सागरान्तव्यपाश्रयम्॥ अस्यता च पुनः सव्यं ज्याघातविहतत्वचम्। दक्षिणो दक्षिणं बाहुं महापरिघसंनिभम्॥ गोसहस्रप्रदातारं ह्युपधाय भुजं महत्। अद्य मे तरणं वाथ मरणं सागरस्य वा॥ इति रामो धृतिं कृत्वा महाबाहुर्महोदधिम्। अधिशिश्य च विधिवत्प्रयतोऽत्रस्थितो मुनिः॥
en: That slayer of foes (lay down), making his pillow his arm resembling the shining form of a serpent; always dight with golden ornaments; full many a time pressed with the palms of beauteous damsels,* decked with jewelled golden Keyūras and superb ornaments studded with pearls; smeared from above with sandal and aguru; (his arm) which formerly had been graced in bed with the head of Sītā; like to the body of Takşaka under the waters of the Gangā; resembling a yoke; in battle increasing the sorrow of foes and enhancing for long the delight of friends; his arm having its skin destroyed by the strokes of the bow-string; which was the refuge of the entire earth; his right arm resembling a mighty bludgeon, the donor of thousands of kine, making this great arm his pillow (he laid him down). To-day either I shall die, or shall the Ocean. Having thus formed his resolution in respect of the great deep, Rama, restraining his speech, with a concentrated mind lay down there agreeably to rule. *The commentator appropriately remarks-As Rāma was wedded to a single wife, these damsels must mean nurses attending on him.

sn: तस्य रामस्य सुप्तस्य कुशास्तीर्णे महीतले। नियमादप्रमत्तस्य निशास्तिस्रोऽभिजग्मतुः॥
en: As Rāma slept on the earth on Kuśa spread over, without ever swerving from the rule, three nights passed away.

sn: स त्रिरात्रोषितस्तत्र नयज्ञो धर्मवत्सलः। उपासत तदा रामः सागरं सरितां पतिम्॥ न च दर्शयते रूपं मन्दो रामस्य सागरः। प्रयतेनापि रामेण यथार्हभिपूजितः॥
en: me. And while spending three nights, Rāma, learned in polity and attached to virtue, prayed to that lord of streams-the Ocean. Yet the wicked Ocean, albeit adored according to his deserts by Rāma with his mind concentrated, did not show himself.

sn: समुद्रस्य ततः क्रुद्धो रामो रक्तान्तलोचनः। समीपस्थमुवाचेदं लक्ष्मणं शुभलक्षणम्॥
en: Thereat Răma grew enraged and had the corners of his eyes crimsoned; and he spank to Laksmana of auspicious marks, saying.

sn: अवलेपः समुद्रस्य न दर्शयति यः स्वयम्। प्रशमश्च क्षमा चैव आर्जवं प्रियवादिता॥ असामर्थ्यफला ह्येते निर्गुणेषु सतां गुणाः।
en: Behold the hauteur of the Ocean in not presenting himself before Calmness, forbearance, candour, and soft speech-these virtues of the good are by the insolent taken for the effects of incompetency.

sn: आत्मप्रशंसिनं दुष्टं धृष्टं विपरिधावकम्॥ सर्वत्रोत्सृष्टदण्डं च लोकः सत्कुरुते नरम्।
en: The person' that is self-laudatory, wicked and badly-bold, publish his own praise and met out chastisement everywhere, is honoured in the world. 1. The word, however, is naram (ac.), man. 2. i.e. indiscriminately.

sn: न साम्ना शक्यते कीर्तिर्न साम्ना शक्यते यशः॥ प्राप्तुं लक्ष्मण लोकेऽस्मिञ्जयो वा रणमूर्धनि।
en: By moderation one cannot attain celebrity, by moderation one cannot attain fame, and, O Lakşmaņa, in this world by moderation one cannot attain victory on the edge of battle.* *Ranamārdhani, 'The perilous edge of battle when it raged.'

sn: अद्य मद्वाणनिर्भग्नैर्मकरैर्मकरालयम्॥ निरुद्धतोयं सौमित्रे प्लवद्भिः पश्य सर्वतः। भोगिनां पश्य भोगानि मया भिन्नानि लक्ष्मण ॥ महाभोगानि मत्स्यानां करिणां च करानिह ।
en: See, O Sumitrā's son, the abode of Makaras, with his waters obstructed all around with Makaras destroyed by my shafts. O Laksmana, see the bodies here of serpents, and the huge on bodies of mighty fishes, and the trunks of elephants, torn by my arrows.

sn: सशङ्खशुक्तिकाजालं समीनमकरं तथा॥ अद्य युद्धेन महता समुद्रं परिशोषये।
en: To day in terrible battle will I dry up the Ocean with conchs and oysters, and fishes and Makaras.

sn: क्षमया हि समायुक्तं मामयं मकरालयः॥ असमर्थ विजानाति धिक्क्षमामीदृशे जने। न दर्शयति साम्ना मे सागरो रूपमात्मनः॥ चापमानय सौमित्रे शरांश्चाशीविषोपमान्। समुद्रं शोषयिष्यामि पद्भयां यान्तु प्लवंगमाः॥
en: This abode of Makaras take me, who is forbearing, to be incompetent. Fie forbearance towards such as he! In consequence of my moderation, Ocean show not his own form. O Saumitri, bring you my bow, my arrows resembling venomous snakes. I will dry up the Ocean, and the monkeys shall go over on foot.

sn: अद्याक्षोभ्यमपि क्रुद्धः क्षोभयिष्यामि सागरम्। वेलासु कृतमर्यादं सहस्रोमिसमाकुलम्॥ निर्मर्यादं करिष्यामि सायकैर्वरुणालयम्। महार्णवं क्षोभयिष्ये महादानवसंकुलम्॥
en: Being angered, today, albeit incapable of being agitated, will I agitate the deep. And by means of my shafts will I make Varuna's abode, surging with a thousand billows and having his dignity maintained by his shores, overleep his continents. And I will agitate the deep harbouring numbers of mighty Dānavas.

sn: एवमुक्त्वा धनुष्पाणिः क्रोधविस्फारितेक्षणः। बभूव रामो दुर्धर्षो युगान्ताग्निरिव ज्वलन्॥
en: Having spoken you, Rāma, equipped with his bow, with his eyes dilated in wrath, became exceedingly irrepressible, like to the flaming fire at the final dissolution.

sn: संपीड्य च धनुर्घोरं कम्पयित्वा शनैर्जगत्। मुमोच विशिखानुग्रान्वजानिव शतक्रतुः॥
en: And straining his dreadful bow, making the earth shake, tremulously, he let fly fierce shafts like him of an hundred sacrifices hurling his thunder-bolt.

sn: ते ज्वलन्तो महावेगास्तेजसा सायकोत्तमाः। प्रविशन्ति समुद्रस्य जलं वित्रस्तपन्नगम्॥
en: Thereat, flaming up, those vehement choice shafts surcharged with energy, enter into the waters of the sea, with its serpents afflicted with fear.

sn: तोयवेगः : समुद्रस्य समीनमकरो महान्। स बभूव महाघोरः समारुतरवस्तथा॥
en: Then great and exceedingly dreadful was the motion of the sea, with fishes and Makaras, and with the roar of the winds (blowing there).

sn: महोर्मिजालचलितः शङ्खजालसमावृतः। सधूमः परिवृत्तोर्मिः सहसासीन्महोदधिः॥
en: On a sudden the mighty deep was heaving with mighty surges, with conchs scattered about, and a smoke (enveloped) the ocean; and the billows became visible on all sides.

sn: व्यथिताः पन्नगाश्चासन्दीप्तास्या दीप्तलोचनाः। दानवाश्च महावीर्याः पातालतलवासिनः॥
en: The serpents were distressed, with their faces flaming and their eyes aglow; as well as the Dānavas of terrific energy, and the dwellers of the nether spheres.

sn: ऊर्मयः सिन्धुराजस्य सनक्रमकरास्तथा। विन्ध्यमन्दरसंकाशाः समुत्पेतुः सहस्रशः॥
en: Billows of the sovran Ocean, resembling Vindhya or Mandara, containing crocodiles and Makaras, sprang up by thousands.

sn: आपूर्णिततरङ्गौधः संभ्रान्तोरगराक्षसः। उद्वर्तितमहाग्राहः संघोषो वरुणालयः॥
en: Varuņa's abode had its surges whirling its serpents and Räkşasas seized with affright, and its ferocious aquatic animals borne all around; and it sent forth sounds.

sn: ततस्तु तं राघवमुग्रवेगं प्रकर्षमाणं धनुरप्रमेयम्। सौमित्रिरुत्पत्त्य विनिःश्वसन्तं मामेति चोक्त्वा धनुराललम्बे॥
en: Then Sumitrā's son, springing up, said to Raghava of fiery vehemence, as he sighed and kept stretching his matchless bow. This must not be. And he took away his (Rāma's) bow.

sn: एतद्विनापि ह्युदधेस्तवाद्य संपत्स्यते वीरतमस्य कार्यम्। भवद्विधाः क्रोधवशं न यान्ति दीर्घं भवान्पश्यतु साधुवृत्तम्॥
en: Without doing this to the Ocean, you supreme of heroes, may have your work accomplished. Personages like you do not come under the influence of passion. Do you deliberately look about for some worthy means (for compassing your end.)

sn: अन्तर्हितैश्चापि तथान्तरिक्षे ब्रह्मर्षिभिश्चैव सुरर्षिभिश्च। र्मामेति चोक्त्वा महता स्वरेण ॥
en: Then remaining invisible in the sky, Brahmarsis and Surarsis,* exclaiming, Well-aday! and Do'nt, in loud accents ajaculated, (Oh! and alas!) *Celestial saints.

sn: अथोवाच रघुश्रेष्ठः सागरं दारुणं वचः। अद्याहं शोषयिष्यामि सपातालं महार्णवम्॥
en: Then the foremost of Raghus addressed Ocean in stern words, saying, To-day will I dry up the Ocean along with the nether regions.

sn: शरनिर्दग्धतोयस्य परिशुष्कस्य सागर। मया निहतसत्त्वस्य पांसुरुत्पद्यते महान्॥
en: O Ocean, your waters being burnt up by my shafts, and you being dried up, with your (aquatic) animals slaughtered, a mighty volume of dust shall arise (from your bed).

sn: मत्कार्मुकनिसृष्टेन शरवर्षेण सागर। परं तीरं गमिष्यन्ति पद्भिरेव प्लवङ्गमाः॥
en: O Ocean, in consequence of the arrowy shower discharged from my bow, the monkeys shall go over to the further shore on foot.

sn: विचिन्वन्नाभिजानासि पौरुषं नापि विक्रमम्। दानवालय संतापं मत्तो नाम गमिष्यसि।४॥
en: Having attained dimensions in consequence of access of waters you know not my manliness or my prowess. But, o abode of Dānavas, grief shall you reap at my hands.

sn: ब्राह्मणास्त्रेण संयोज्य ब्रह्मदण्डनिभं शरम्। संयोज्य धनुषि श्रेष्ठ विचकर्ष महाबलः॥
en: Then fixing an arrow resembling the rod of Brahmā with a Brahmā Mantra, on the best of bows, that exceedingly strong on drew it.

sn: तस्मिन्विकृष्टे सहसा राघवेण शरासने। रोदसी संपफालेव पर्वताश्च चकम्पिरे॥
en: As Rāghava suddenly stretched his bow, heaven and earth seemed to be riven, and the mountains trembled.

sn: तमश्च लोकमावत्रे दिशश्च न चकाशिरे। प्रतिचुक्षुभिरे चाशु सरांसि सरितस्तदा॥
en: And darkness covered the world, and the cardinal points became invisible. And at once the watery expanses and rivers were agitated.

sn: तिर्यक् च सह नक्षत्रैः संगतौ चन्द्रभास्करौ। भास्करांशुभिरादीप्तं तमसा च समावृतम्॥ प्रचकाशे तदाकाशमुल्काशतविदीपितम्। अन्तरिक्षाच्च निर्घाता निर्जग्मुरतुलस्वनाः॥
en: The stars appeared simultaneously with the Sun and Moon.* And the sky was illumined with the rays of the Sun, and yet it was overspread with darkness; and it burned with an hundred meteors. And thunder-bolts sending forth sounds surpassing all others, dropped from the firmament. *The phenomenon, remarks the commentator, was owing to the heavenly bodies obstructing each other's orbit.

sn: वपुःप्रकर्षेण वर्दिव्यमारुतपङ्क्तयः। बभञ्ज च तदा वृक्षाञ्जलदानुद्वहन्मुहुः॥ आरुजंश्चैव शैलानान्शिखराणि बभञ्ज च।
en: The winds began to below violently; breaking down trees and momentarily scattering clouds; damaging mountain-tops and shattering summits.

sn: दिवि च स्म महावेगाः संहताः समहास्वनाः॥ मुमुचुवैद्युतानग्नींस्ते महाशनयस्तदा। यानि भूतानि दृश्यानि चुक्रुशुश्चाशनेः समम्॥ अदृश्यानि च भूतानि मुमुचुभैरवस्वनम्।
en: Then the dread and mighty thunders possessing impetuous speed and emitting tremendous roars, coming together, produced lightning flashes. And those creatures that could be seen, uttered sounds resembling the thunder; and those that were invisible gave forth f rightful cries.

sn: शिश्यिरे चाभिभूतानि संत्रस्तान्युद्विजन्ति च॥ संप्रविव्यथिरे चापि न च पस्पन्दिरे भयात्।
en: And overwhelmed with fright, and quaking (for fear), the creatures began to measure their lengths, and they were sore afflicted, and bereft of motion through terror.

sn: सह भूतैः सतोयोर्मिः सनागः सहराक्षसः॥ सहसाभूत्ततो वेगाद्भीमवेगो महोदधिः। योजनं व्यतिचक्राम वेलामन्यत्र संप्लवात्॥
en: Then the mighty deep with its animals, and with its waters and waves, and with its serpents and Rākşasas, was suddenly wrought up with a violent motion. And albeit it was not the occasion of the universal dissolution, the Ocean passed beyond his shores for a full hundred yojanas.

sn: तं तथा समतिक्रान्तं नातिचक्राम राघवः। तमुद्धतममित्रघ्नो रामो नदनदीपतिम्॥
en: Seeing the elated Ocean-lord of streams and rivers, thus overpass his bounds, that destroyer of enemies, Raghu's son, Rāma, was not moved.* *Naticakrāma may also mean, (Rama) did not discharge any more arrows.

sn: ततो मध्यात्समुद्रस्य सागरः स्वयमुत्थितः। उदयाद्रिमहाशैलान्मेरोरिव दिवाकरः॥
en: Then from forth the mid-sea arose Ocean himself, even as the maker of day rise from the mighty ascending-hill, Meru.

sn: पन्नगैः सह दीप्तास्यैः समुद्रः प्रत्यदृश्यत। स्निग्धवैदूर्यसंकाशो जाम्बूनदविभूषणः॥ रत्नमाल्याम्बरधरः पद्मपत्रनिभेक्षणः। सर्वपुष्पमयीं दिव्यां शिरसा धारयन्स्रजम्॥ जातरूपमयैश्चैव तपनीयविभूषणैः। आत्मजानां च रत्नानां भूषितो भूषणोत्तमैः॥ धातुभिर्मण्डितः शैलो विविधैर्हिमवानिव। एकावलीमध्यगतं तरलं पाण्डरप्रभम्॥ विपुलेनोरसा बिभ्रत्कौस्तुभस्य सहोदरम्। आपूर्णिततरङ्गौघः कालिकानिलसंकुलः।। गङ्गासिन्धुप्रधानाभिरापगाभिः समावृतः।
en: And accompanied by Pannagas* of flaming faces, the Ocean showed himself, appearing like cool lapises, adorned with golden ornaments, wearing a wreath of gems and a jewelled vesture, with his eyes resembling lotus-leaves, bearing on his head a noble garland containing all flowers; decked with ornaments of polished gold; as well with excellent ornaments of gems originating in himself, like the mountains Himavān embellished with metals (sprung in himself).-(the Ocean arose) with wave on wave whirling around, and rife with winds blowing among clouds, surrounded by streams, Gangā, Sindhu (and others). *Semi-divine serpents.

sn: उद्वर्तितमहाग्राहः संभ्रान्तरोगराक्षसः।। देवतानां सुरूपाणां नानारूपाभिरीश्वरः। सागरः समुपक्रम्य पूर्वमामन्त्र्य वीर्यवान्।। अब्रवीत्प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यं राघवं शरपाणिनम् ॥
en: And approaching the arrow-showering Rāma, and greeting him fair, Ocean spoke to him with joined hands.

sn: पृथिवी वायुराकाशमापो ज्योतिश्च राघव। स्वभादे सौम्य तिष्ठन्ति शाश्वतं मार्गमाश्रिताः॥
en: O Rāghava, earth, air, sky, water and light, these, O mild one, retaining their eternal course, maintain their (respective) nature.

sn: तत्स्वभावो ममाप्येष यदगाधोऽहमप्लवः। विकारस्तु भवेद्गाध एतत्ते प्रवदाम्यहम्॥
en: Mine also is that nature whereby I am fathomless and incapable of being crossed. The reverse of this is the having a bottom. And for this reason I speak to you (concerning the means).

sn: न कामान च लोभाद्वा न भयात्पार्थिवात्मज। रागानक्राकुलजलं स्तम्भयेयं कथंचन॥
en: O king's son, not from desire, covetousness, or fear, or anger, can I anywise deprive my waters abounding in alligators of their (perpetual) motion.

sn: विधास्ये येन गन्तासि विषहिष्येऽप्यहं तथा। न ग्राहा विधमिष्यन्ति यावत्सेना तरिष्यति।। हरीणां तरणे राम करिष्यामि यथा स्थलम्॥
en: I will tell you how you will pass (over me); or and I will bear it. And no ferocious aquatic animals shall do wrong so long as your forces have not crossed. And, O Rāma, I will make as it were firm land for the crossing over of the monkeys.

sn: तमब्रवीत्तदा रामः शृणु मे वरुणालय। अमोघोऽयं महाबाणः कस्मिन्देशे निपात्यताम्॥
en: Then Rāma said, O Varuna's abode, listen to me! This arrow (of mine) must accomplish the end (intended). Where shall I let it light?

sn: रामस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा तं च दृष्ट्वा महाशरम्। महोदधिर्महातेजा राघवं वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
en: Hearing Rāma's speech, and looking at the mighty arrow, that exceedingly energetic one, the great Deep, addressed Raghava, saying.

sn: उत्तरेणावकाशोऽस्ति कश्चित्पुण्यतरो मम। दुमकुल्य इति ख्यातो लोके ख्यातो यथा भवान्।।२९ ।
en: There is a certain spot of mine in the North, which is more sacred (than the rest). It is famed as Drumakulya, even as you are famed in the world.

sn: उग्रदर्शनकर्माणो बहवस्तत्र दस्यवः। आभीरप्रमुखाः पापाः पिबन्ति सलिलं मम॥
en: There are there many robbers of ferocious forms and actions, wicked wights, headed bycow-herds, who drink of my water.

sn: तैर्न तत्स्पर्शनं पापं सहेयं पापकर्मभिः। अमोघः क्रियतां राम अयं तत्र शरोत्तमः॥
en: These persons of unrighteous acts touch me, and I cannot bear this sin. O Rāma, do you at that place render this best of arrows successful.

sn: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा सागरस्य महात्मनः। मुमोच तं शरं दीप्तं परं सागरदर्शनात्॥
en: Hearing the words of the high-souled Ocean, (Rama) immediately after,* let fly that flaming shaft. *Săgaradarśanāt-may also mean, agreeably to the instruction.

sn: तेन तन्मरुकान्तारं पृथिव्यां किल विश्रुतम्। निपातितः शरो यत्र वज्राशनिसमप्रभः॥
en: The place where the arrow resembling the thunder-bolt and vajra in splendour, alighted, has been celebrated on earth as Marukāntāra.

sn: ननाद च तदा तत्र वसुधा शल्यपीडिता। तस्माद्ब्रणमुखात्तोयमुत्पपात रसातलात्॥
en: And hurt with the dart, the Earth emitted roars; and in consequence of this, water began to gush out at the mouth of the wound from the subterranean regions.

sn: स बभूव तदा कूपो व्रण इत्येव विश्रुतः। सततं चोत्थितं तोयं समुद्रस्येव दृश्यते॥
en: And this then became well-known as Vrana3; and there are seen the waters of the Ocean spring up.

sn: अवदारणशदश्च दारुणः समपद्यत। तस्मात्तद्बाणपातेन अपः कुक्षिष्वशोषयत्॥
en: There arose a terrific report of riving. And owing to this,* as well as the incident of the arrow, the water that existed in the tanks, was dried up.

sn: विख्यातं त्रिषु लोकेषु मरुकान्तारमेव च। शोषयित्वा तु तं कुक्षिं रामो दशरथात्मजः।। वरं तस्मै ददौ विद्वान्मरवेऽमरविक्रमः॥
en: Having dried up Marukāntāra famous throughout the three regions, as well as the reservoirs of water Rāma the son of Dasaratha, learned and of god-like prowess, conferred a boon on the desert, saying. *i.e. the sound.

sn: पशव्यश्चाल्परोगश्च फलमूलरसायुतः। बहुस्नेहो बहुक्षीरः सुगन्धिर्विविधौषधिः॥
en: This place shall be filled with food nourishing beasts; and ailments shall be rare here. And the fruits and roots shall be replete with relish; and it shall abound in oil and overflow with milk; and it shall contain various adorous drugs.

sn: एवमेतैश्च संयुक्तो बहुभिः संयुतो मरुः। रामस्य वरदानाच्च शिवः पन्था बभूव ह॥
en: Thus did the desert come to possess these attributes; and from Rāma's bestowal of a boon, it attained a pleasant aspect.

sn: तस्मिन्दग्धे तदा कुक्षौ समुद्रः सरितां पतिः। राघवं सर्वशास्त्रज्ञमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: On that place being burnt up, that lord of streams, the Ocean, thus spoke to Rāghava, versed in every branch of learning.

sn: अयं सौम्य नलो नाम तनयो विश्वकर्मणः। पित्रा दत्तवरः श्रीमान्प्रीतिमान्विश्वकर्मणः॥ एष सेतुं महोत्साहः करोतु मयि वानरः। तमहं धारयिष्यामि यथा ह्येष पिता तथा॥
en: O mild one, this one is named Nala, son to Viśvakarmā. He has received a boon from his sire. Visvakarma's son is well pleased with you. Let this monkey, surcharged with exhuberant spirits, build a bridge over me. I will hold that up. This one is as his sire.

sn: एवमुक्त्वोदधिर्नष्टः समुत्थाय नलस्ततः। अब्रवीद्वानरश्रेष्ठो वाक्यं रामं महाबलम्॥
en: Having delivered himself thus, Ocean disappeared. Then that foremost of monkeys, Nala, arising, spoke to the mighty Rāma.

sn: अहं सेतुं करिष्यामि विस्तीर्णे मकरालये। पितुः सामर्थ्यमासाद्य तत्त्वमाह महोदधिः।॥
en: Resorting to my sire's skill, I will build a bridge over the spacious abode of Makaras. The mighty Ocean has spoken justly.

sn: दण्ड एव परो लोके पुरुषस्येति मे मतिः। धिक्क्षमामकृतज्ञेषु सान्त्वं दानमथापि वा॥
en: In respect of the ingrate even chastisement is supreme in this world, this is my conviction. Down with forbearance, or moderation, or gift!

sn: अयं हि सागरो भीमः सेतुकर्मदिदृक्षया। ददौ दण्डभयाद्गाधं राघवाय महोदधिः॥
en: This dreadful Ocean, this mighty deep, expecting to see a bridge (thrown over him), has granted depth to Rāghava.

sn: मम मातुर्वरो दत्तो मन्दरे विश्वकर्मणा। मया तु सदृशः पुत्रस्तव देवि भविष्यति।४७।।
en: (Formerly) in Mandara, Visvakarma had conferred a boon on my mother: 'O exalted one, your son shall be like me.

sn: औरसस्तस्य पुत्रोऽहं सदृशो विश्वकर्मणा। मारितोऽस्म्यहनतेन तत्त्वमाह महोदधिः।। न चाप्यहमनुक्तो वः प्रब्रूयामात्मनो गुणान्॥
en: I am a son of his, sprung from his lions, and I am like to Viśvakarmā. Ocean reminded me all the things. Not having been asked by you, I had not unfolded my qualifications.

sn: समर्थश्चाप्यहं सेतुं कर्तुं वै वरुणालये। तस्मादद्यैव बध्नन्तु सेतुं वानरपुङ्गवाः॥
en: I also am capable of constructing a bridge over Varuna's abode. Therefore this very day let the foremost monkeys construct the bridge.

sn: ततो विसृष्टा रामेण सर्वतो हरिपुङ्गवाः। उत्पेततुर्महारण्यं हृष्टाः शतसहस्रशः॥
en: Then directed by Rāma, the principal monkeys with alacrity entered the mighty forest in hundreds and thousands.

sn: ते नगानगसंकाशाः शाखामृगगणर्षभाः। बभञ्जः पादपांस्तत्र प्रचकर्षुश्च सागरम्॥
en: Themselves resembling mountains, the foremost of the monkeys began to break down trees and draw them towards the Ocean.

sn: ते सालैश्चाश्वकर्णैश्च धवैर्वशैश्च वानराः। कुटजैरर्जुनैस्तालैस्तिलकैस्तिनिशैरपि ॥ बिल्वकैः सप्तपर्णैश्च कर्णिकारैश्च पुष्पितैः। चूतैश्चाशोकवृक्षैश्च सागरं समपूरयन् ॥
en: The monkeys filled the Ocean with Sālas, and Ašvakarņas, dhavas, bamboo's and kutajas, arjunas, palms, tilakas, tinicas, billakas, saptaparnas, and blossoming karnikāras, mangoes, and asoka trees.

sn: समूलांश्च विमूलांश्च पादपान्हरिसत्तमाः। इन्द्रकेतूनिवोद्यम्य प्रजह्वानरास्तरून्॥
en: And those monkeys the foremost of their species-began to gather the trees, some with their roots, and some without them, carrying them like Indra's ensign.

sn: तालान्दाडिमगुल्मांश्च नारिकेलविभीतकान्। हस्तिमात्रान्महाकायाः पाषाणांश्च महाबलाः।।५५ पर्वतांश्च समुत्पाट्य यन्त्रैः परिवहन्ति च। करीरान्बकुलान्नम्बान्समाजहुरितस्ततः॥
en: And those huge-bodied monkeys possessed of prodigious strength, procured palms, and pomegranates, cocoanuts and Vibhitakas, Kariras, Vakulas, and Nimbas, as well as rocks, measuring elephants' dimensions; and uprooting crags, they carried them by means of machines.

sn: प्रक्षिप्यमाणैरचलैः सहसा जलमुद्धृतम्। समुत्ससर्प चाकाशमवासर्पत्ततः पुनः॥
en: And on rocks being plunged into the waters, the latter, suddenly swelling up, mounted to the welkin, and again subsided.

sn: समुद्रं क्षोभयामासुर्निपतन्तः समन्ततः। सूत्राण्यन्ये प्रगृह्णन्ति ह्यायतं शतयोजनम्॥ नलश्चक्रे महासेतुं मध्ये नदनदीपतेः।
en: And (the trees) dropping (into the deep), vexed it all around. And some took lines (for insuring straightness to the bridge). And at the middle of the lord of rivers and streams, Nala made a grand bridge measuring an hundred Yojanas.

sn: स तदा क्रियते सेतुर्वानरै?रकर्मभिः॥ दण्डानन्ये प्रगृह्णन्ति विचिन्वन्ति तथापरे। वानरैः शतशस्तत्र रामस्याज्ञापुरः सरैः॥ मेघाभैः पर्वताभैश्च तृणैः काष्ठैर्वबन्धिरे। पुष्पिताग्रैश्च तरुभिः सेतुं बध्नन्ति वानराः॥
en: Then he set about constructing the bridge with the assistance of monkeys of dreadful deeds. And some took the measuring rod, and others bore (timber tea the sea). And by help of hundreds of monkeys following Rama's mandate, hued like clouds or mountains, (they) constructed a bridge with grass, and wood. And the monkeys made the bridge of trees with blossoming tops.

sn: पाषाणाश्च गिरिप्रख्यान्गिरीणां शिखराणि च। दृश्यन्ते परिधावन्तो गृह्य दानवसंनिभाः॥
en: And (monkeys) resembling Danavas were seen rushing all around with rocks resembling hills, and mountain-summits.

sn: शिलानां क्षिप्यमाणानां शैलानां तत्र पात्यताम्। बभूव तुमुलः शब्दस्तदा तस्मिन्महोदधौ॥
en: And tremendous was the tumult that arose of crags thrown and rocks toppled down into the mighty deep.

sn: कृतानि प्रथमेनाह्रा योजनानि चतुर्दश। प्रहृष्टैर्गजसंकाशैस्त्वरमाणैः प्लवङ्गमैः॥
en: And on the first day the elephant-like monkeys full of spirits and exerting themselves vigorously, finished fourteen Yojanas.

sn: द्वितीयेन तथैवाह्रा योजनानि तु विंशतिः। कृतानि प्लवगैस्तूर्णं भीमकायैर्महाबलैः॥
en: The exceedingly strong and huge-bodied monkeys on the second day speedily disposed of twenty Yojanas.

sn: अह्ना तृतीयेन तथा योजनानि तु सागरे। त्वरमाणैर्महाकायैरेकाविंशतिरेव च ॥
en: And on the third day the huge-bodied active monkeys did one and twenty Yojanas on the sea.

sn: चतुर्थेन तथा चाहा द्वाविंशतिरथापि वा। योजनानि महावेगैः कृतानि त्वरितैस्ततः॥ पञ्चमेन तथा चाहा प्लवगैः क्षिप्रकारिभिः। योजनानि त्रयोविंशत्सुवेलमधिकृत्य वै॥
en: And on fourth day the exceedingly impetuous monkeys, bestirring themselves vigorously, did two and twenty Yojanas. And on the fifth day they monkeys leaping speedily twenty three Yojanas reaching to the fair shore.

sn: स वानरवरः श्रीमान्विश्वकर्मात्मजो बली। वबन्ध सागरे सेतुं यथा चास्य पिता तथा॥
en: And resembling his sire, that best of monkeys, the lusty and graceful offspring of Viśvakarmā, (thus) constructed the bridge over the sea.

sn: स नलेन कृतः सेतुः सागरे मकरालये। शुशुभे सुभगः श्रीमान्स्वातीपथ इवाम्बरे॥
en: That bridge built by force over the abode of makaras, looked graceful and splendid like the Milky way in the firmament.

sn: ततो देवाः सगन्धर्वाः सिद्धाश्च परमर्षयः। आगम्य गगने तस्थुर्द्रष्टुकामास्तदद्भुतम्॥
en: Then the deities and Gandharvas, the Siddhas and the prime saints, appearing in the heavens, stood there, eager to behold this wonder.

sn: दशयोजनविस्तीर्णं शनयोजनमायतम्। ददृशुर्देवगन्धर्वा नलसेतुं सुदुष्करम्॥
en: The gods and Gandharvas saw that bridge of Nala, difficult of being made, having an area of ten Yojanas and measuring an hundred in length.

sn: आप्लवन्तः प्लवन्तश्च गर्जन्तश्च प्लवंगमाः। तमचिन्त्यसमह्यं च ह्यद्भुतं लोमहर्षणम् ॥ ददृशुः सर्वभूतानि सागरे सेतुबन्धनम्।
en: The monkeys, leaping and bounding and roaring, as well as all creatures, beheld that building of the bridge the ocean, on inconceivable, and marvellous, displaying skill past thought and capable of making one's hair stand on end.

sn: तानि कोटिसहस्राणि वानराणां महौजसाम्॥ बध्नन्तः सागरे सेतुं जग्मुः पारं महोदधेः।
en: And those thousands of Koțis of exceeding vigour, having constructed the bridge over the ocean, went over to the other shore of the mighty main.

sn: विशालः सुकृतः श्रीमान्सुभूमिः सुसमाहितः॥ अशोभत महान्सेतुः सीमन्त इव सागरे।
en: And spacious, skilfully constructed, graceful, well-paved and nicely finished, the great bridge appeared like the line where the hair has been parted on the Ocean's head.

sn: ततः पारे समुद्रस्य गदापाणिविभीषणः॥ परेषामभियानार्थमतिष्ठत्सचिवैः सह।
en: Then on the other shore of the ocean, Bibhisbana with the view of opposing foes (that might advance), stationed himself mace in hand, along with some councilors.

sn: सुग्रीवस्तु ततः प्राह रामं सत्यपराक्रमम्।७७।। हनूमन्तं त्वमारोह अङ्गदं त्वथ लक्ष्मणः। अयं हि विपुलो वीर सागरो मकरालयः॥ वैहायसौ युवामेतौ वानरौ धारयिष्यतः।
en: Then Sugrīva spoke to Rāma having truth for his prowess, Do you get upon Hanumān, and let Laksmana get upon Angada. O hero, vast is this Ocean-abode of Makaras. These monkeys, rangers of the sky, shall hold you up both.

sn: अग्रतस्तस्य सैन्यस्य श्रीमानरामः सलक्ष्मणः। ७९ जगाम धन्वी धर्मात्मा सुग्रीवेण समन्वितः।
en: Thereat the graceful and righteous Rāma along with Laksmana, equipped with his bow, set out in the van of the army in company with Sugriva.

sn: अन्ये मध्येन गच्छन्ति पार्श्वतोऽन्ये प्लवंगमाः॥ सलिलं प्रपतन्त्यन्ये मार्गपन्ये प्रपेदिरे। केचिद्वैहायसगताः सुपर्णा इव पुप्लुवुः॥
en: And some monkeys proceeded along the middle, and some plunged into the deep, and some went by the road. And some coursed through the air, bounding up bird-like.

sn: घोषेण महता घोषं सागरस्य समुच्छ्रितम्। भीममन्तर्दधे भीमा तरन्ती हरिवाहिनी।॥
en: That dreadful array of monkeys crossing over, with its mighty uproar drowned the dreadful roar of the deep, which had been arising.

sn: वानराणां हि सा तीर्णा वाहिनी नलसेतुना। तीरे निविविशे राज्ञा बहुमूलफलोदके।॥
en: On the monkey-host having crossed by the bridge of Nala, the king stationed it on the shore abounding in fruits, roots, and water.

sn: तदद्भुतं राघवकर्म दुष्करं समीक्ष्य देवाः सह सिद्धचारणैः। स्तमभ्यषिञ्चन् सुशुभै लैः पृथक् ॥
en: Beholding that work of Rāghava incapable of being performed the deities together with the Siddhas and Caranas, and the Maharsis, suddenly presenting themselves before Rāma, sprinkled him one by one with sacred water, and said.

sn: जयस्व शत्रूनरदेव मेदिनी ससागरां पालय शाश्वतीः समाः। इतीव रागं नरदेवसत्कृतं शुभैर्वचोभिर्विविधैरपूजयत्॥
en: May you be victorious, O human-divine one! Rule you the Earth eternally! Thus in various auspicious words, did they pay homage to that one honoured by the Brāhmanas, Rāma.

sn: निमित्तानि निमित्तज्ञो दृष्ट्वा लक्ष्मणपूर्वजः। सौमित्रिं संपरिष्वज्य इदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Having seen omens, that one, Laksmina's elder brother, conversant with them, embracing the son of Sumitrā, said these words.

sn: परिगृह्योदकं शीतं वनानि फलवन्ति च। बलौघं संविभज्येमं व्यूह्य तिष्ठेम लक्ष्मण॥
en: O Laksmana, occupying (this tract) of cool waters and woods affluent with fruits, will we, dividing and arranging our forces, stay here.

sn: लोकक्षयकर भीमं भयं पश्याम्युपस्थितम्। प्रबर्हणं प्रवीराणामृक्षवानररक्षसाम्॥
en: Mighty is the fear that I see at hand, boding destruction to people and the slaughter of the foremost heroes of bears, monkeys and Rākşasas.

sn: वाताश्च कलुषा वान्ति कम्पते च वसुंधरा। पर्वताग्राणि वेपन्ते पतन्ति च महीरुहाः॥
en: The wind blow darkly, and the Earth shake. The tops of the mountains tremble, and trees topple down.

sn: मेघाः क्रव्यादसंकाशाः परुषाः परुषस्वनाः। क्रूराः क्रूरं प्रवर्षन्ति मिश्रं शोणितबिन्दुभिः॥
en: The clouds are ashen and roistering, and roar roughly. And lowering, they shower portentous drops of blood.

sn: रक्तचन्दनसंकाशा संध्या परमदारुणा। ज्वलतः प्रपतत्येतदादित्यादग्निमण्डलम्॥
en: The twilight is terrible and look like the red sandal. And a fiery circle dropped from the flaming sun.

sn: दीना दीनस्वराः क्रूराः सर्वतो मृगपक्षिणः। प्रत्यादित्यं विनर्दन्ति जनयन्तो महद्भयम्॥
en: And on all sides birds and beasts, distressed, uttering woe-begone notes, and grim-visaged, set up cries against the sun, arousing great fear.

sn: रजन्यामप्रकाशस्तु संतापयति चन्द्रमाः। कृष्णरक्तांशुपर्यन्तो लोकक्षय इवोदितः॥
en: The Moon, although not appearing* in the night, burns, and with dark and red rays rises, as if it intended to exterminate people. *The moon, it seems appear, but does not look out clearly.

sn: ह्रस्वो रूक्षोऽप्रशस्तश्च परिवेषस्तु लोहितः। आदित्ये विमले नीलं लक्ष्म लक्ष्मण दृश्यते।।।।
en: The aspect (of the sun) is slight, rough, and good;* and, O Lakşmaņa, a blue mark is visible on the unclouded Sun. *Prasasta-I do not see the propriety of this epithet in this connection. This may be a mistake.

sn: रजसा महता चापि नक्षत्राणि हतानि च। युगान्तमिव लोकानां पश्य शंसन्ति लक्ष्मण।।१०
en: The stars seem crased by a mighty volume of dust. O Lakşmaņa, behold this sight disastrous to people like to the universal dissolution.

sn: काकाः श्येनास्तथा नीचा गृध्राः परिपतन्ति च। शिवाश्चाप्यशुभानादानदन्ति सुमहाभयान्॥
en: Crows, and hawks, and the inferior vultures, wheel all round. And jackals are sending inauspicious yells, exciting great fear.

sn: शैलैः शूलैश्च खङ्गैश्च विमुक्तैः कपिराक्षसैः। भविष्यत्यावृता भूमिमा॑सशोणितकर्दमा॥
en: The earth shall be covered with darts and javelins, and swords discharged by monkeys and Räkşasas, and be turned into mire with flesh and gore.

sn: क्षिप्रमद्यैव दुर्धर्षां पुरीं रावणपालिताम्। अभियाम जवेनैव सर्वैर्हरिभिरावृताः॥
en: Surrounded by all the monkeys, will we, using speed, this very day rapidly enter into the city ruled by Ravana, incapable of being subdued.

sn: इत्येवमुक्त्वा धन्वी स रामः संग्रामधर्षणः। प्रतस्थे पुरतो रामो लङ्कामभिमुखो विभुः॥
en: Having said this, that subduer in conflict, that lord, that enchanter of men, Rāma,* equipped with his bow, proceeded in the direction of Lankā. *The word Räma occurs twice, one being the cognomen of the solar hero. The other means, the enchanter of men.

sn: सबिभीषणसुग्रीवाः सर्वे ते वानरर्षभाः। प्रतस्थिरे विनर्दन्तो धृतानां द्विषतां वधे॥
en: And all the principal monkeys-Sugrīva with Vibhisana-went on, setting up roars, for the destruction of foes, who were determined to battle with them.

sn: राघवस्य प्रियार्थं तु सुतरां वीर्यशालिनाम्। हरीणां कर्मचेष्टाभिस्तुतोष रघुनन्दनः॥
en: And consequently Raghu's son was well pleased with the fortitude and exertions of the powerful monkeys, for bringing about what dear to Ravhava.

sn: सा वीरसमिति राज्ञा विरराज व्यवस्थिता। शशिना शुभनक्षत्रा पौर्णमासीव शारदी॥
en: With the presence of the king* that assembly of heroes looked beautiful, as does the autumnal night, garnished with beauteous stars, with the Moon. *Rāma.

sn: प्रचचाल च वेगेन त्रस्ता चैव वसुंधरा। पीड्यमाना बलौघेन तेन सागरवर्चसा॥
en: And oppressed with the bursting energy of the host resembling the ocean, the Earth trembled.

sn: ततः शुश्रुवुराक्रुष्टं लङ्कायां काननौकसः। भेरीमृदङ्गसंघुष्टं तुमुलं लोमहर्षणम्॥
en: Then the rangers of the forest heard a hubbub in Lankä, as well as the sounds of trumpets and Mşdangas, mighty and capable of making people's down stand on end.

sn: बभूवुस्तेन घोषेण संहृष्टा हरियूथपाः। अमृष्यमाणास्तद्धोषं विनेदुर्घोषवत्तरम्॥
en: At those sounds, the leaders of monkey-bands were delighted beyond measure, and, resenting the same, set up cries louder than those sounds.

sn: राक्षसास्तत्प्लवंगानां शुश्रुवुस्तेऽपि गर्जितम्। नर्दतामिव दृप्तानां मेघानामम्बरे स्वनम्॥
en: The Rākşasas also heard the roars of the monkeys, resembling the rumbling of haughty clouds in the sky.

sn: दृष्ट्वा दाशरथिर्लङ्कां चित्रध्वजपताकिनीम्। जगाम मनसा सीतां दूयमानेन चेतसा॥
en: Beholding Lankā with variegated standards, and streamers, Dasaratha's son went* to Sītā with an aggrieved heart. *i.e. mentally.

sn: अत्र सा मृगशावाक्षी रावणेनोपरुध्यते। अभिभूता ग्रहेणेव लोहिताङ्गेन रोहिणी॥
en: Here that one having eyes resembling those of a young deer, is confined by Rāvana, like to Rohini overpowered by the red-bodied planet.* *Angāraka.

sn: दीर्घमुष्णं च निःश्वस्य समुद्रीक्ष्य च लक्ष्मणम्। उवाच वचनं वीरस्तकालहितमात्मनः॥
en: Sighing hot and long, and looking at Laks maņa, that hero spoke words fraught with his good at that time.

sn: आलिखन्तीमिवाकाशमुत्थितां पश्य लक्ष्मण। मनसेव कृतां लङ्कां नगाग्रे विश्वकर्मणा॥
en: Behold, O Laksmana, Lanka towering up as if piercing the heavens; and, built by Viśvakarmā on the brow of the mountain, she seems to have been made by the Mind.

sn: विमानैर्बहुभिर्लङ्का संकीर्णा रचिता पुरा । विष्णोः पदमिवाकाशं छादितं पाण्डुभिर्घनैः॥
