And, protecting her at the command of Rāvana, that kind-hearted companion, firm in vows, saw Sītā, deprived of her consciousness. And she' comforted with a friend's affection that one of fair vows, who was rolling in the dust and rising up from it like a mare. 1. Saramă. 2. The commentator intelligently remarks. As a mare does, to remove fatigue.

sn: तां समाश्वासयामास सखी स्नेहेन सुव्रताम्। उक्ता यद्रावणेन त्वं प्रत्युक्तश्च स्वयं त्वया॥ लीनया गहने शून्ये भयमुत्सूज्य रावणात्। तव हेतोविशालाक्षि नहि मे रावणाद्भयम्॥
en: Having come to the solitary wood for protecting you, I, renouncing all fear of Ravana, have, remaining hid, heard everything that he addressed to you, as well as what you had replied to him. For you, O you of expansive eyes, I have no fear of Rāvana.

sn: स संभ्रान्तश्च निष्क्रान्तो यत्कृते राक्षसेश्वरः। तत्र मे विदितं सर्वमभिनिष्क्रम्य मैथिलि।७।।
en: And, O Maithili, I, coming out, have also learnt well as to why the lord of Rākṣasas has gone out hence hurriedly.

sn: न शक्यं सौप्तिकं कर्तुं रामस्य विदितात्मनः। वधश्च पुरुषव्याघ्र यस्मिन्नैवोपपद्यते॥
en: Rāma, acquainted with self, is incapable of being surprised in sleep; nor does the slaying of that tiger-like one commend itself to me as probable.

sn: न त्वेवं वानरा हन्तुं शक्याः पादपयोधिनः। सुरा देवर्षभेणेव रामेण हि सुरक्षिताः॥
en: The monkeys fighting with trees, well protected by Rāghava, like the gods protected by the foremost of the celestials, are incapable of being slain.

sn: दीर्घवृत्तभुजः श्रीमान्महोरस्कः प्रतापवान्। धन्वी संनहनोपेतो धर्मात्मा भुवि विश्रुतः॥ विक्रान्तो रक्षिता नित्यमात्मनश्च परस्य च। लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्रात्रा कुलीनो नयशास्त्रवित्॥ हन्ता परबलौघानामचिन्त्यबलपौरुषः। न हतो राघवः श्रीमान्सीते शत्रुनिबर्हणः॥
en: And, possessed of arms long and rounded; graceful, broad-breasted; powerful; accoutred with the bow; and mailed; righteous; and famous over the earth; endowed with energy; and along with his brother, Lakşmaņa, ever protecting himself and others; of noble descent; and versed in polity; the destroyer of the hostile ranks; and of inconceivable strength and manhood, the graceful Răghava, O Sītā, slayer of foes, is not slain.

sn: अयुक्तबुद्धिकृत्येन सर्वभूतविरोधिना। इव प्रयुक्ता रौद्रेण माया मायाविना त्वयि ॥
en: This illusion has been spread around you by that fierce, illusion-creating one, whose mind over runs upon improper acts and who oppose himself to all creatures.

sn: शोकस्ते विगतः सर्वकल्याणं त्वामुपस्थितम्। ध्रुवं त्वां भजते लक्ष्मीः प्रियं ते भवति शृणु॥
en: All your sorrow has departed, and your good day has dawned. Certainly Laksmi seek you. And, O lady, hearken to what is dear to you!

sn: उत्तीर्य सागरं रामः सह वानरसेनया संनिविष्टः समुद्रस्य तीरमासाद्य दक्षिणम्॥
en: Having crossed over the ocean, along with the monkey-host, Rāma has encamped himself on the southern shore of the sea.

sn: दृष्टो मे परिपूर्णार्थः काकुत्स्थः सहलक्ष्मणः। सहितैः सागरान्तस्थैर्बलैस्तिष्ठति रक्षितः॥
en: By me has been seen the complete Kākutstha along with Lakşmaņa, accompanied by the forces, stationed on the marge of the main, protected (by his native might).

sn: अनेन प्रेषिता ये च राक्षसा लघुविक्रमाः। राघवस्तीर्ण इत्येव प्रवृत्तिस्तैरिहाहता॥
en: Those Rākşasas of fleet vigour who had been despatched by this one, have brought the news that Rāghava has crossed.

sn: स तां श्रुत्वा विशालाक्षि प्रवृत्तिं राक्षसाधिपः। एष मन्त्रयते सर्वैः सचिवैः सह रावणः॥
en: And, O large-eyed lady, having learnt this news, Rāvaņa-lord of Rākşasas, is consulting with all his counsellors.

sn: इति ब्रुवाणा सरमा राक्षसी सीतया सह। सर्वोद्योगेन सैन्यानां शब्दं शुश्राव भैरवम्॥
en: As the Rākşasī, Saramā, was relating this to Sita, she heard the leonine roars of the army, emitted with the greatest energy.

sn: दण्डनिर्घातवादिन्याः श्रुत्वा भेर्या महास्वनम्। उवाच सरमा सीतामिदं मधुरभाषिणी॥
en: Hearing the mighty sounds of kettledrums produced by sticks struck (thereon), the honeytongued Saramā spoke thus to Sītā.

sn: संनाहजननी ह्येषा भैरवा भीरु भेरिका। भेरीनादं च गम्भीरं शृणु तोयदनिःस्वनम्॥
en: These dreadful sounds of the kettledrum, O mother, call to arms. And hark to the solemn notes of the kettledrums, resembling the rumbling of clouds!

sn: कल्प्यन्ते मत्तमातङ्गा युज्यन्ते रथवाजिनः। दृश्यन्ते तुरगारूढाः प्रासहस्ताः सहस्रशः॥
en: The mad elephants are caparisoned and the car-horses are yoked; and thousands of warriors) are seen, mounted on steeds, with bearded darts in their hands.

sn: तत्र तत्र च संनद्धाः संपतन्ति सहस्रशः। आपूर्यन्ते राजमार्गाः सैन्येरद्भुतदर्शनैः॥ वेगवद्भिर्नदद्भिश्च तोयौघैरिव सागरः।
en: As waters fill up the ocean, mailed warriors of wonderful forms, vehement and roaring, by thousands rush out on all aides and fill the highways.

sn: शस्त्राणां च प्रसन्नानां चर्मणां वर्मणां तथा॥ रथवाजिगजानां च राक्षसेन्द्रानुयायिनाम्। संभ्रमो राक्षसामेष हृषितानां तरस्विनाम्। प्रभो विसृजतां पश्य नानावर्णसमुत्थिताम् ॥
en: And mark the splendour spread around by the polished arins and bucklers and mail, and by the cars, horses and elephants of the followers of the Rākşasa-chief, consisting of many hues shooting up, like to the appearance of a fire in summer, burning a forest, and also mark the excitement of the high-spirited and fast-coursing Raksasa! * *This line of verse defies all attempts to make it fall into syntactical order with the rest of the sentence. It is a hideous hiatus in the passage.

sn: संभ्रमो रक्षसामेष तुमुलं लोमहर्षणम्। श्रीस्त्वां भजति शोकघ्नी रक्षसां भयमागतम्॥
en: And fierce is the excitement of these Raksasas— followers of the Raksasa-cheif, with their hands bearing upraised arms, capable of making people's hair stand on end. The sorrow removing Sree espouse you, and the fear of the Rākşasa is come.

sn: रामः कमलपत्राक्षो दैत्यानामिव वासवः। अवजित्य जितक्रोधस्तमचिन्त्यपराक्रमः। रावणं समरे हत्वा भर्ता त्वाधिगमिष्यति॥
en: As Vasava did to the Daityas, the lotus-eyed Rāma, your lord-of controlled anger, and of inconceivable prowess, slaying Rävaņa in battle and thus delivering you, shall approach you.

sn: विक्रमिष्यति रक्षःसु भर्ता ते सहलक्ष्मणः। यथा शत्रुषु शत्रुघ्नो विष्णुना सह वासवः॥
en: And, as Väsava put forth his prowess among his foes, in company with the foe-destroying Visnu, your lord, along with Laksmana, shall display his prowess among the Rākşasa.

sn: आगतस्य हि रामस्य क्षिप्रमङ्कागतां सतीम्। अहं द्रक्ष्यामि सिद्धार्थां त्वां शत्रौ विनिपातिते।।२९
en: On the enemy having fallen, I shall behold you, devoted to your lord, with your desire attained, soon lying on the lap of Rama.

sn: अस्त्राण्यानन्दजानि त्वं वर्तयिष्यसि जानकि। समागम्य परिष्वक्ता तस्योरसि महोरसः॥
en: And, O Janaki, embracing (your lord) you shall shed tears of joy on his mighty breast.

sn: अचिरान्मोक्ष्यते सीते देवि ते जघनं गताम्। धृतामेकां बहून्मासान्वेणी रामो महाबलः॥
en: O Sitä, soon shall the highly powerful Răma loosen this braid of your reaching to your hips, which you have been wearing for many a month.

sn: तस्य दृष्ट्वा मुखं देवि पूर्णचन्द्रमिवोदितम्। मोक्ष्यसे शोकजं वारि निर्मोकमिव पन्नगी॥
en: O exalted one, seeing his face like the full moon risen, you shall shed water begot of ruth, even as a she-serpent casts off her slough.

sn: रावणं समरे हत्वा न चिरादेव मैथिलि। त्वया समग्रः प्रियया सुखार्हो लप्स्यते सुखम्।३३।।
en: O Mithila's daughter, speedily slaying Ravana in battle, that one worthy of happiness shall reap felicity in the company of you, his beloved.

sn: सभाजिता त्वां रामेण मोदिष्यसि महात्मना। सुवर्षेण समायुक्ता यथा सस्येन मेदिनी॥
en: And, loved by the high-souled Rama, you, shall be happy, even as the Earth furnished with crops brought forth by plenteous showers.

sn: गिरिवरमभितो विवर्तमानो हय इव मण्डलमाशु यः करोति। तमिह शरणमभ्युपैहि देवि दिवसकरं प्रभवो ह्ययं प्रजानाम्॥
en: Do you, O exalted one, take refuge with him, who, going round the foremost of mountains, speedily assume a steed-like circular movement; for even the maker of day is the source of people's joy and grief.

sn: अथ तां जातसंतापां तेन वाक्येन मोदिताम्। सरमा हादयामास महीं दग्धामिवाम्भसा ॥
en: Burning with grief on account of those words,* Sarama gladdened and cheered her, even as masses of clouds (cheer up) the burning Earth. *i.e.the words of Ravana.

sn: ततस्तस्या हितं सख्याश्चिकीर्षन्ती सखी वचः। उवाच काले कालज्ञा स्मितपूर्वाभिभाषिणी॥
en: Then, desirous of doing her good, (Sita's) friend, conversant with season, and ever precluding her speech with a smile, spoke to her seasonably.

sn: उत्सहेयमहं गत्वा त्वद्वाक्यमसितेक्षणे। निवेद्य कुशलं रामे प्रतिच्छना निवर्तितुम्॥
en: O you having dark eyes, I can, secretly going to Rama and communicating to him your auspicious words, come back clandestinely.

sn: नहि मे क्रममाणाया निरालम्बे विहायसि। समर्थो गतिमन्वेतुं पवनो गरुडोऽपि वा॥
en: Nor, when I course the supportless sky, can even the Wind or Garuda follow me.

sn: एवं ब्रुवाणां तां सीता सरमामिदमब्रवीत्। मधुरं श्लक्ष्णया वाचा पूर्वशोकाभिपन्नया॥
en: As she said this, Sita with her grief a little lightened, said to Sarama in sweet and smooth words.

sn: समर्था गगनं गन्तुमपि च त्वं रसातलम्। अवगच्छाद्य कर्तव्यं कर्तव्यं ते मदन्तरे॥
en: You are capable of even going to the nethermost regions. But do you on my behalf that which is fit to be done by you.

sn: मत्प्रियं यदि कर्तव्यं यदि बुद्धिः स्थिरा तव। ज्ञातुमिच्छामि तं गत्वा किं करोतीति रावणः॥
en: If you intend doing me a good turn, and if your sense be steady, I would know what Ravana is doing after having left this place.

sn: स हि मायाबलः क्रूरो रावणः शत्रुरावणः। मां मोहयति दुष्टात्मा पीतमात्रेव वारुणी॥
en: That guileful and wicked-minded one, Rāvana, destroyer of enemies, having powers of illusion, overwhelms me even as the Vāruni just drunk.

sn: तर्जापयति मां नित्यं भर्सापयति चासकृत्। राक्षसीभिः सुघोराभिर्यो मां रक्षति नित्यशः॥
en: Confining me here for ever and a day, (Rāvana) sets on dreadful Räksnasas to alike threaten and scold me constantly.

sn: उद्विग्ना शङ्किता चास्मि न स्वस्थं च मनोगम। तद्भयाच्चाहमुद्विग्ना अशोकवनिकां गता॥
en: And I am agitated and alarmed and my mind is (always) uneasy. And I, dwelling in the Asoka wood, is ever agitated.

sn: यदि नाम कथा तस्य निश्चितं वापि यद्भवेत्। निवेदयेथाः सर्वं तद्वरो मे स्यादनुग्रहः॥
en: If there is any talk (of delivering me), or keeping me confined, you should communicate to me the decision arrived at.

sn: साप्येवं ब्रुवतीं सीतां सरमा मृदुभाषिणी। उवाच वचनं तस्याः स्पृशन्ती बाष्पविक्लवम्।।१२
en: This is the highest favour that I seek (at hands). Thereat, the mild-speeched Saramā, wiping (Sītā's) face washed in tears, spoke to her, as she said this.

sn: एष ते यद्यभिप्रायस्तस्माद्गच्छामि जानकि। गृह्य शत्रोरभिप्रायमुपावर्तामि मैथिलि॥
en: If this is your wish, I will go, O Jānaki. O Mithila's daughter, having possessed myself of the intent of the enemy, I shall come back.

sn: एवमुक्त्वा ततो गत्वा समीपं तस्य रक्षसः। शुश्राव कथितं तस्य रावणस्य समन्त्रिणः॥
en: Having said this, (Saramā), repairing to the Raksasa, heard Raksa, heard Ravana's converse with his counsellors.

sn: सा श्रुत्वा निश्चयं तस्य निश्चयज्ञा दुरात्मनः। पुनरेवागमत्क्षिप्रमशोकवनिका शुभाम्॥
en: Having heard of the decision of that wickedminded one, she, understanding decisions, swiftly retraced her steps to the fair Asoka forest.

sn: सा प्रविष्टा ततस्तत्र ददर्श जनकात्मजाम्। प्रतीक्षमाणां स्वामेव भ्रष्टपद्मामिव श्रियम्॥
en: Then, entering there, she saw Janaka's daughter, expecting (her) like a very Sri,, bereft of her lotus.

sn: तां तु साती पुनः प्राप्तां सरमां प्रियभाषिणीम्। परिष्वज्य च सुस्निग्धं ददौ च स्वयमासनम्।।१७
en: And, the fair-spoken Sarama, on getting back (near her), Sītā, embracing her affectionately, herself gave her a seat.

sn: इहासीना सुखं सर्वमाख्याहि मम तत्त्वतः। क्रूरस्य निश्चयं तस्य रावणस्य दुरात्मनः॥
en: Sitting down here at ease, do you relate to me faithfully all about the determination of the wicked-minded and guileful Ravana.

sn: एवमुक्ता तु सरमा सीतया वेपमानया। कथितं सर्वमाचष्ट रावणस्य समन्त्रिणः॥
en: Thus accosted by the trembling Sītä, Saramā related everything that had been said by Råvaņa and his counsellors.

sn: जनन्या राक्षसेन्द्रो वै त्वन्मोक्षार्थं बृहद्वचः। अतिस्निग्धेन वैदेहि मन्त्रिवृद्धेन चोदितः॥
en: O Vaidehi, the Rākşasa lord was advised by his mother and the aged counsellors in pregnant words informed with affection, having your deliverance for their object.

sn: दीयतामभिसत्कृत्य मनुजेन्द्राय मैथिली। निदर्शनं ते पर्याप्त जनस्थाने यदद्भुतम्॥
en: Do you make over Maithili to the king of men, paying him homage due. You have in Janasthāna profusely witnessed wonderful instances (of his prowess).

sn: लङ्घनं च समुद्रस्य दर्शनं च हनूमतः। वधं स रक्षसां युद्धे कः कुर्यान्मानुषो युधि ॥
en: The crossing of the ocean, Hanuman's sight (of Sītā) and the slaughter of the Rākşasa in fight, what person is capable of doing all this in battle?

sn: एवं स मन्त्रिवृद्धैश्च मात्रा च बहु बोधितः। न त्वामुत्सहते मोक्तुमर्थमर्थपरो यथा॥
en: Thus long exhorted by his counsellors as well as his mother, Rāvaņa does not make up his mind to emancipate you, even as a covetous person is loath to pare with wealth (appropriated).

sn: नोत्सहत्यमृतो मोक्तुं युद्धे त्वामिति मैथिलि। सामात्यस्य नृशंसस्य निश्चयो ह्येष वर्तते॥ तदेषां सुस्थिरा बुद्धिर्मृत्युलोभादुपस्थिता। भयान शक्तस्त्वां मोक्तुमनिरस्तः स संयुगे॥ राक्षसानां च सर्वेषामात्मनश्च वधेन हि।
en: O Maithili, without renouncing his life in battle, he does not intend to liberate you. Even this is the determination which that cruel one has arrived at along with his advisers. This intent is in consequence of their coveting surcease. He can not yield you up from sheer fear; not is he backward in battle, or shirk his own destruction or that of all the Rākşasas.

sn: निहत्य रावणं संख्ये सर्वथा निशितैः शरैः। प्रतिनेष्यति रामस्त्वामयोध्यामसितेक्षणे॥
en: O dark-eyed lady slaying Rāvaņa in battle with sharp shafts, Rāma shall take the back to Ayodhyā.

sn: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे शब्दो भेरीशङ्खसमाकुलः। श्रुतो वै सर्वसैन्यानां कम्पयन्धरणीतलम्॥
en: In the meanwhile there was heard a mighty uproar occasioned by the whole host, and drums and conchs, which shook the earth.

sn: श्रुत्वा तु तं वानरसैन्यनादं लङ्कागता राक्षसराजभृत्याः। हतौजसौ दैन्यपरीतचेष्टाः श्रेयो न पश्यन्ति नृपस्य दोषात्॥
en: Hearing that hubbub of the monkey-army, the servants of the Råkşasa monarch, ran who were in Lankā, growing dispirited, and bereft of energy, with weakness overcoming their powers, did not see any good, in consequence of the fault of the ruler.

sn: तेन शङ्खविमिश्रेण भेरीशब्देन नादिना। उपयाति महाबाहू रामः परपुरंजयः॥
en: That captor of hostile capitals, the mightarmed Rāma, was advancing (upon Larikā) with the sounds of drums mixed with the blares of conchs.

sn: तं निनादं निशम्याथ रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः। मुहूर्त ध्यानमास्थाय सचिवानभ्युदैक्षत॥
en: Hearing this noise, Ravana-lord of Raks asas-reflecting for a while, cast his eyes upon his counsellors.

sn: अथ तान्सचिवांस्तत्र सर्वानाभाष्य रावणः। सभां संनादयन्सनित्युवाच महाबलः॥ जगत्संतापनः क्रूरोऽगर्हयनराक्षसेश्वरः। तरणं सागरस्यास्य विक्रमं बलपौरुषम्॥
en: Addressing there all those counsellors, that afflictor of the world—the crooked and highly powerful lord of the Rākşasas, Rāvaņa, making his court resound, running down (Rāma's) crossing the main, as well as his vigour, strength and manhood, said to them.

sn: यदुक्तवन्तो रामस्य भवन्तस्तन्मया श्रुतम्। भवतश्चाप्यहं वेधि युद्धे सत्यपराक्रमान्।। तूष्णीकानीक्षतोन्योन्यं विदित्वा रामविक्रमम् ॥
en: What you have said touching Rama's (prowess), has been heard by me. And I also know you to be of sterling valour in the field. Yet why, knowing Rāma's prowess, do you silently look at each other?

sn: ततस्तु सुमहाप्राज्ञो माल्यवान्नाम राक्षसः। रावणस्य वचः श्रुत्वा इति मातामहोऽब्रवीत्॥
en: Then the maternal grand sire (of Rāvaņa), possessed of exceeding wisdom, named Malyavān, hearing his words, said.

sn: विद्यास्वभिविनीतो यो राजा राजनयानुगः। स शास्ति चिरमैश्वर्यमरीश्च कुरुते वशे॥
en: The king that is accomplished in the various kinds of learning,* and that follow polity, ever command affluence and bring his enemies under his subjection. *The commentator says there are four and ten kinds of learning; but unfortunately he does not enumerate them.

sn: संदधानो हि कालेन विगृह्णश्चारिभिः सह। स्वपक्षे वर्धनं कुर्वन्महदैश्वर्यमश्नुते॥
en: He that seasonably concludes peace and carries on war with his enemies, and who advances his own party, attain great affluence.

sn: हीयमानेन कर्तव्यो राज्ञा संधिः समेन च। न शत्रुमवमन्येत ज्यायान्कुर्वीत विग्रहम्॥
en: A king should enter into peace, if he be an equal or inferior of his adversary, and engage in war, if be more powerful, but an enemy should never be disergarded.

sn: तन्मह्यं रोचते संधिः सह रामेण रावण। यदर्थमभियुक्तोऽसि सीता तस्मै प्रदीयताम्॥
en: Therefore, O Rāvana, peace with Rāma is what commends itself to me; and do you render to him that for which you have been invaded (by him), viz., Sītā.

sn: तस्य देवर्षयः सर्वे गन्धर्वाश्च जयैषिणः। विरोधं मा गमस्तेन संधिस्ते तेन रोचताम्॥
en: All the Devarsis and Gandharvas wish for (Rāma's) victory. Therefore, do not enter into hostilities with him; but do you bend your mind to the conclusion of peace with him.

sn: असृजद्भगवान्पक्षौ द्वावेव हि पितामहः। सुराणामसुराणां च धर्माधर्मों तदाश्रयौ॥
en: That possessor of the six attributes, the Greatfather, has appointed two courses, (respectively) for the Asuras and the celestials, having for their eousness.

sn: धर्मो हि श्रूयते पक्ष अमराणां महात्मनाम्। अधर्मो रक्षसां पक्षो ह्यसुराणां च राक्षस॥
en: Righteousness, we hear, is the course of the high-souled celestials, as, O. Rākşasa, unrighteousness is that of Rākşasa and Asuras.

sn: धर्मो वै ग्रसतेऽधर्मं यदा कृतमभूधुगम्। अधर्मो ग्रसते धर्म तदा तिष्यः प्रवर्तते॥
en: During the Kţta Yuga, righteousness swallow up sin; and during Tisya,* unrighteousness swallow up virtue. *The Kali Yuga.

sn: तत्त्वया चरता ले कान्धर्मोऽपि निहतो महान्। अधर्मः प्रगृहीतश्च तेनास्मदलिनः परे॥
en: You, ranging the three worlds, worlds, had extinguished pregnant piety, and reaped unrighteousness; and it is for this that your foes have waxed potent. *While ranging the three worlds on a career of conquest, you didst, disturbing sacrifices, etc., wrong righteousness.

sn: स प्रमादात्प्रवृद्धस्तेऽधर्मोऽहिर्ग्रसते हि नः। विवर्धयति पक्षं च सुराणां सुरभावनः॥
en: Having grown through through your your neglect, unrighteousness devour us, and that protector of the gods, (righteousness), is strengthening the side of the celestials.

sn: विषयेषु प्रसक्तेन यत्किचित्कारिणा त्वया। ऋषीणामग्निकल्पानामुद्वेगो जनितो महान्॥
en: You, addicted to carnal pleasures and acting in defiance of duty, had aroused the high wrath of the saints resembling fire.

sn: तेषां प्रभावो दुर्धर्षः प्रदीप्त इव पावकः। तपसा भावितात्मानो धर्मस्यानुग्रहे रताः॥
en: The power of these possessed of souls sanctified through asceticism, and ever engaged in invoking the aid of righteousness, is incapable of being resisted and is like flaming fire.

sn: मुख्यैर्यज्ञैर्यजन्त्येते तैस्तैर्यत्ते द्विजातयः। जुह्वत्यग्नींश्च विधिवद्वेदांश्चोच्चैरधीयते। अभिभूय च रक्षांसि ब्रह्मघोषानुदीरयन्॥ दिशो विप्रदूताः सर्वे स्तनयित्नुरिवोष्णगे।
en: The twice-born ones engage in contemplation with intent minds, offer oblations into the fire according to the ordinance, and loudly recite the Vedas. They overpower the Rākşasa, uttering the Vedas; and thereat they fly in all directions like clouds scattered in summer.

sn: ऋषीणामग्निकल्पानामग्निहोत्रसमुत्थितः॥ आवृत्य रक्षसां तेजो धूमो व्याप्य दिशो दश। तेषु तेषु च देशेषु पुण्येष्ट्यवधृतव्रतैः॥
en: The smoke that arise from the Agnihotra sacrifices of saints resembling fire, enveloping the energy of the Räkşasas, spreads over the ten cardinal quarters.

sn: चर्यमाणं तपस्तीव्र संतापयति राक्षसान्। देवदानवयक्षेभ्यो गृहीतश्च वरस्त्वया॥
en: The fierce austerities of vow-observing saints, performed at particular sacred spots, try the Rākş asas sore.

sn: मनुष्या वानरा ऋक्षा गोलाषेला महाबलाः। बलवन्त इहागम्य गर्जन्ति दृढविक्रमाः॥
en: You have obtained a boon, conferring immunity at the hands of deities, Dänavas and Yakşas. But men and monkeys, bears and Golăngülas, possessed of enormous strength and endowed with vigour, and of indomitable prowess, coming here, are setting up roars.

sn: उत्पातान्विविधान्दृष्ट्वा घोरान्बहुविधान्बहून्। विनाशमनुपश्यामि सर्वेषां रक्षसामहम्॥
en: Witnessing various and many dire portents, I perceive the destruction of all the Rākşasas.

sn: खराभिस्तनिता घोरा मेघाः प्रतिभयंकराः। शोणितेनाभिवर्षन्ति लङ्कामुष्णेन सर्वतः॥
en: Dreadful and terrific clouds, uttering harsh sounds, are showering blood all around Lankā.

sn: रुदतां वाहनानां च प्रपतन्त्यश्रुबिन्दवः। रजोध्वस्ता विवर्णाश्च न प्रभान्ति यथापुरम्॥
en: And (live) vehicles are dropping profuse tears. And all sides, covered with dust, do not appear bright as formerly.

sn: व्याला गोमायवो गृध्रा वाश्यन्ति च सुभैरवम्। प्रविश्य लङ्कामारामे समवायाश्च कुर्वते॥
en: And beasts of prey, jackals and vultures, are emitting frightful cries, and, entering into the garden of Lankā, form themselves into bands.

sn: कालिकाः पाण्डुरैर्दन्तैः प्रहसन्त्यग्रतः स्थिताः। स्त्रियः स्वप्नेषु मुष्णन्त्यो गृहाणि प्रतिभाष्य च।।२८
en: In dreams mighty dark-hued women in front of dwellings, seizing at (the furniture) thereof, and speaking inauspiciously, laugh displaying their sable teeth.

sn: गृहाणां बलिकर्माणि श्वानः पर्युपसेवते। खरा गोषु प्रजायन्ते मूषका नकुलेषु च ॥
en: In houses dogs are feasting on the articles of worship. And cows bring forth asses, and mungooses, mice.

sn: मार्जारा द्वीपिभिः सार्धं सूकराः शुनकैः सह। किंनरा राक्षसैश्चापि समेयुर्मानुषैः सह॥
en: And cats are pairing with leopards, and swine with dogs, and Kinnaras with Rākşasas and human being.

sn: पाण्डुरा रक्तपादाश्च विहगाः कालचोदिताः। राक्षसानां विनासाय कपोता विचरन्ति च ॥
en: are And red-footed white sky-coursing pigeons, urged on by Doom, are going about for the destruction of the Raksasas.

sn: चीचीकूचीति वाशन्तः शारिका वेश्मसु स्थिताः। पतन्ति ग्रथिताश्चपि निर्जिताः कलहैषिभिः॥
en: And female-parrots in houses, wounded and worsted by other birds delighting in discord, are dropping down, emitting indistinct notes.

sn: पक्षिणश्च मृगाः सर्वे प्रत्यादित्यं रुदन्ति ते। करालो विकलो मुण्डः पुरुषः कृष्णपिङ्गलः॥ कालो गृहाणि सर्वेषां कलो कालेऽन्ववेक्षते।
en: All the birds and beasts crying (distressfully) with their faces turned towards the sun. And at dusk a frightful, withered, tawnyhued male figure, looking like Death himself, with his head shaven, peer into the houses (of people).

sn: एतान्यन्यानि दुष्टानि निमित्तान्युत्पतन्ति च।। विष्णुं मन्यामहे रामं मानुषं रूपमास्थितम्। न हि मानुषमात्रोऽसौ राघवो दृढविक्रमः।। येन बद्धः समुद्रे च सेतुः स परमाद्भुतः। कुरूष्व नरराजेन सन्धि रामेण रावण।। ज्ञात्वावधार्य कर्माणि क्रियतामायतिक्षमम्॥
en: These and other evil omens occur. Rama I deem as Vişnnu assuming the form of a man. Rāghava of steady prowess, for certain, is no human being, he that has built a bridge over the deep, must be an exceedingly wonderful person. Therefore, O Rāvana, conclude peace with Rāma-king of men. Having ascertained fit course, do you act properly.

sn: इदं वचस्तस्य निगद्य माल्यवान् परीक्ष्य रक्षोधिपतेर्मनः पुनः। अनुत्तमेषूत्तमपौरुषो बली बभूव तूष्णीं समवेक्ष्य रावणम्॥
en: Having said this to that vile one, and known the intention of the lord of Rākşasa, that strong Mālyavān, of exceeding prowess, became silent, eying Ravana.

sn: तत्तु माल्यवतो वाक्यं हितमुक्तं दशाननः। न मर्षयति दुष्टात्मा कालस्य वशमागतः॥
en: The Ten-necked one, come under the control of Time, did not brook the beneficial speech, spoken by Mālyavān.

sn: स बद्ध्वाभ्रुकुटिं वक्त्रे क्रोधस्य वशमागतः। अमर्षात्परिवृत्ताक्षो माल्यवन्तमथाब्रवीत्॥
en: Contracting his face into a frown, he, coming under the masterdom of passion, with his eyes rolling in wrath, addressed Mayavān, saying.

sn: हितबुद्ध्या यदहितं वचः परुषमुच्यते। परपक्षं प्रविश्यैव नैतच्छ्रोक्षगतं मम॥
en: The words which, deeming the strength of the enemy as superior, you have harshly spoken, considering it as beneficial, had never before entered my ears.

sn: मानुषं कृषणं राममेकं शाखामृगाश्रयम्। समर्थ मन्यसे केन त्यक्तं पित्रा वनाश्रयम्।४।।
en: A (mere) man, and feeble, and alone, and having monkeys for his support, why do you deem Rāma, who has (further) been cast off by his sire, and has in consequence taken refuge in the woods, as competent (to cope with me)?

sn: रक्षसामीश्वरं मां च देवानां च भयंकरम्। हीनं मां मन्यसे केन अहीनं सर्वविक्रमैः॥
en: Why do you consider me, who am the lord of the Räksasa, and feared even by the immortals, as weak and reft of all power?

sn: वीरद्वेषेण वा शङ्के पक्षपातेन वा रिपोः। त्वयाहं परुषाण्युक्तो मम प्रोत्साहनेन वा॥
en: You, I suspect, speak (thus) roughly either from jealousy of my heroism, or for inciting me.

sn: प्रभवन्तं पदस्थं हि परुषं कोऽभिभाषते। पण्डितः शास्त्रतत्त्वज्ञो विना प्रोत्साहनेन वा॥
en: Who that is wise and learned, ever address him roughly that is at once puissant and of (high) station, if not to spur him on?

sn: आनीय च वनात्सीतां पद्महीनामिव श्रियम्। किमर्थं प्रतिदास्यामि राघवस्य भयादहम्।।
en: Why, having brought Sītā like a Sri shorn of her lotus, shall I give her up, from fear of Rāghava?

sn: वृत्तं वानरकोटीभिः ससुग्रीवं सलक्ष्मणम्। पश्य कैश्चिदहोभिश्च राघवं निहतं मया॥
en: Behold Rāghava, environed by Koțis of monkeys, with Sugrīva and Lakşmaņa, slain on of these days!

sn: द्वन्द्वे यस्य न तिष्ठन्ति दैवतान्यपि संयुगे। स कस्माद्रावणो युद्धे भयमाहारयिष्यति॥
en: He before whom even the gods cannot stay in the battle field, how can that Råvaņa ever come by fear?

sn: द्विधा भज्येयमप्येवं न नमेयं तु कस्यचित्। एव मे सहजो दोषः स्वभावो दुरतिक्रमः॥
en: Better that I should be riven in twain, but bend I never will. This is my native fault; and nature is incapable of being overcome.

sn: यदि तावत्समुद्रे तु सेतुर्बद्धो यदृच्छया। रामेण विस्मयः कोऽत्र येन ते भयमागतम्॥
en: If Rāma bath at his pleasure constructed a bridge over the ocean, what is the wonder in this that you have conceived such a fear?

sn: स तु तीत्वर्णिवं रामः सह वानरसेनया। प्रतिजानामि ते सत्यं न जीवन्प्रतियास्यति ॥
en: And although Rāma has crossed the ocean along with the monkey-army, yet I swear to you truly, living, he shall not back hence.

sn: एवं ब्रुवाणं संरब्धं रुष्टं विज्ञाय रावणम्। वीडितो माल्यवान्वाक्यं नोत्तरं प्रत्यपद्यत॥
en: When Ravana, wrought up with passion, had spoken thus, Malyavan, knowing him wroth, did not return a reply.

sn: जयाशिषा तु राजानं वर्धयित्वा यथोचितम्। माल्यवानभ्यनुज्ञातो जगाम स्वं निवेशनम्॥
en: And, duly tendering blessings to the king, Mālyavān, taking his permission, went to his own abode.

sn: रावणस्तु सहामात्यो मन्त्रयित्वा विमृश्य च। लङ्कायास्तु तदा गुप्तिं कारयामास राक्षसः॥
en: The Räkşasa, Rāvaņa, along with his courtiers, having consulted together as to what was fit to be done, set about the defence of Lankā.

sn: व्यादिदेश च पूर्वस्यां प्रहस्तं द्वारि राक्षसम्। दक्षिणस्यां महावीयौँ महापार्श्वमहोदरौ॥ पश्चिमायामथ द्वारि पुत्रमिन्द्रजितं तदा। व्यादिदेश महामायं राक्षसैर्बहुभिर्वृतम्॥
en: He commanded the Raksasa Prahasta (to guard) the Eastern gate; and the exceedingly powerful Mahaparsva and Mahodara (to guard) the Southern gate; and he ordered his son Indrajit, possessing mighty powers of illusion, girt by innumerable Räkșasas, to guard the Western gate.

sn: उत्तरस्यां पुरद्वारि व्यादिश्य शुकसारणौ। स्वयं तत्र गमिष्यामि मन्त्रिणस्तानुवाच ह॥
en: He commanded Suka and Sārana to defend the Northern gate. But he said to the counsellors, I will myself go thither.* *i.e. to defend the Northerm gate.

sn: राक्षसं तु विरूपाक्षं महावीर्यपराक्रमम्। मध्यमेऽस्थापयद्गुल्मे बहुभिः सह राक्षसैः॥
en: And he posted in the middle in the garrison the Raksasa, Virupaksa, endowed with exceeding prowess and energy, backed by countless rākşasas.

sn: एवं विधानं लङ्कायां कृत्वा राक्षसपुंगवः। कृतकृत्यमिवात्मानं मन्यते कालचोदितः॥
en: Having taken these measures in Lankā, the raksasa-chief, urged by Fate, deemed himself as having achieved success.

sn: विसर्जयामास ततः म मन्त्रिणो विधानमाज्ञाप्य पुष्कलम्। जयाशिषा मन्त्रिगणेन पूजितो विवेश सोऽन्तःपुरमृद्धिमन्महत्॥
en: Having thus completely provided for the defence of the city, he dismissed the ministers; and, honoured by the counsellors with blessings of victory, (then) entered his magnificent and splendid inner apartment.

sn: नरवानरराजानौ स तु वायुसुतः कपिः। जाम्बवानृक्षराजश्च राक्षसश्च विभीषणः॥ अङ्गदो बालिपुत्रश्च सौमित्रिः शरभः कपिः। सुषेणः सहदायादो मैन्दो द्विविद एव च॥ गजो गवाक्षः कुमुदो नलोऽथ पनसस्तथा। अमित्रविषयं प्राप्ताः समवेताः समर्थयन्॥
en: Those, kings, man and monkey, that monkey the Wind-god's son, Jāmbavān-sovereign of bears—the Rākşasa, Vibhīşaņa, the son of Vālī, Angada, Sumitrā's son, the monkey, Sarabha, Susena along with his friends, Kumuda, Nala, and Panasa, arriving at the dominions of the enemy, assembled together, began to deliberate.

sn: इयं सा लक्ष्यते लङ्का पुरी रावणपालिता। सासुरोरगगन्धर्वैः सर्वैरपि सुदुर्जया॥
en: Yonder is that Lankā ruled by Rāvana, invincible even to the celestials, serpents and Gandharvas.

sn: कार्यसिद्धिं पुरस्कृत्य मन्त्रयध्वं विनिर्णये। नित्यं संनिहितो यत्र रावणो राक्षसाधिपः॥
en: Let us, keeping before us success in the enterprise, consult together for the purpose of arriving at a decision.

sn: अथ तेषु ब्रुवाणेषु रावणावरजोऽब्रवीत्। वाक्यमग्राम्यपदवत्पुष्कलार्थं बिभीषणः॥
en: We are here daily nearing Răvaņa, lord of Raksasas. As they were speaking thus, Ravana's younger brother, Vibhīşaņa, said in a pregnant speech free from provinicialism.

sn: अनलः पनसश्चैव संपातिः प्रमतिस्तथा। गत्वा लङ्कां ममामात्या पुरी पुनरिहागताः॥
en: Anala, Panasa, Sampāti and Pramāti— all courtiers of mine-having gone up to Lanka, have come back here.

sn: भूत्वा शकुनयः सर्वे प्रविष्टाश्च रिपोर्बलम्। विधानं विहितं यच्च तदृष्ट्वा समुपस्थिताः॥
en: Wearing the forms of birds, they entered into the hostile forces; and, having seen the measures that had been adopted (by them, have come (back).

sn: संविधानं यथाहुस्ते रावणस्य दुरात्मनः। राम तब्रुवतः सर्वं याथातथ्येन मे शृणु॥
en: O Rāma, hearken to me as I tell you truly anent the provisions which they have related, made by the wicked-minded Ravana.

sn: पूर्व प्रहस्तः सबलो द्वारमासाद्य तिष्ठति। दक्षिणं च महावीर्यो महापार्श्वमहोदरौ॥ इन्द्रजित्पश्चिमं द्वारं राक्षसैर्बहुभिर्वृतः। पट्टिशासिधनुष्मद्भिः शूलमुद्गरपाणिभिः॥ नानाप्रहरणैः शूरैरावृतो रावणात्मजः।
en: In the Eastern gate stay Prahasta along with his forces; in the Southern, the exceedingly powerful Mahāpārsva and Mahodara, and in the Western. Ravana's son, Indrajit, supported by innumerable Räkşasas, equipped with pattiśas, swords and bows, and bearing darts and maces in their hands, surrounded by heroes carrying various weapons.

sn: राक्षसानां सहस्रेस्तु बहुभिः शस्त्रपाणिभिः॥ युक्तः परमसंविग्नो राक्षसैः सह मन्त्रवित्। उत्तरं नगरद्वारं रावणः स्वयमास्थितः॥
en: And, backed by many thousands of Räkşasas wielding weapons, and accompanied by Rākşasas conversant with counsel, Rāvana himself, his heart agitated to the height, gaurd the Northern gate of the city.

sn: विरूपाक्षस्तु महता शूलमुद्गधनुष्मता। बलेन राक्षसैः सार्धं मध्यमं गुल्ममाश्रितः॥
en: Virüpākṣa with a powerful force accoutred in javelins, clubs and bows, protects the garrison in the centre.

sn: एतानेवंविधान् गुल्मॉल्लङ्कायां समुदीक्ष्य ते। मामका मन्त्रिणः सर्वे शीघ्रं पुनरिहागताः॥
en: Having seen these hosts thus disposed in Lankä, my counsellors have speedily come back here.

sn: गजानां दशसाहस्रं रथानामयुतं तथा। हयानामयुते द्वे च साग्रां कोटिं च रक्षसाम्॥
en: There are ten thousand elephants, an Ayuta cars, two of horses, and abouta koti of Raksasas, powerful and strong, and equipped with arms in conflict.* *These are, remarks the commentator, the leader.

sn: विक्रान्ता बलवन्तश्च संयुगेष्वाततायिनः। इष्टा राक्षसराजस्य नित्यमेते निशाचराः॥ एकैकस्यात्र युद्धार्थे राक्षसस्य विशांपते। परीवारः सहस्राणां सहस्रमुपतिष्ठति॥
en: These night-rangers are ever the favourites of the Raksasa ruler. And, O kine, a koti of forces accompany each of these Rākşasas in battle.

sn: एतां प्रवृत्तिं लङ्कायां मन्त्रिप्रोक्तां बिभीषणः। एवमुक्त्वा महाबाहू राक्षसांस्तानदर्शयत्॥ लङ्कायां सचिवैः सर्वं रामाय प्रत्यवेदयत्।
en: Having conveyed this information concerning Lankā, which had been communicated by his counsellors, the mighty-armed Vibhīşaņa showed (to Rama) those Raksasas themselves.

sn: रामं कमलपत्राक्षमिदमुत्तरमब्रवीत्॥ रावणावरजः श्रीमानरामप्रियचिकीर्षया।
en: In company with his counsellors, Ravana's graceful younger brother, ever striving for the welfare of Rama, by way of answer communicated everything that was going forward in Lankā to Räma, having eyes resembling lotus leaves.

sn: कुबेरं तु यदा राम रावणः प्रतियुद्ध्यति॥ षष्टिः शतसहस्राणि तदा निर्यान्ति राक्षसाः। पराक्रमेण वीर्येण तेजसा सत्त्वगौरवात्।। सदृशा ह्यत्र दर्पण रावणस्य दुरात्मनः॥
en: O Răma, when Rāvana battled with Kuvera, sixty lacs of Raksasas marched forth (to meet him). In prowess, energy, vigour, exceeding fortitude, and hauteur, they resembled the wicked-minded Ravana himself.

sn: अत्र मन्युर्न कर्तव्यः कोपये त्वां न भीषये। समर्थो ह्यसि वीर्येण सुराणामपि निग्रहे॥
en: In this matter, you ought not to grow wroth, I only arouse your wrath, and do not endeavour to frighten you. You can subdue even the celestials by your prowess. *i.e. You ought not to be angry with me; for I do not frighten you, but rouse your wrath against Ravana.

sn: तद्भवांश्चतुरङ्गेण बलेन महता वृतम्। व्यूह्येदं वानरानीकं निर्मथिष्यसि रावणम्॥
en: Therefore you, environed by a mighty army, having arrayed the monkey-forces in order of battle, shall thrash Ravana (in battle)

sn: रावणावरजे वाक्यमेवं ब्रुवति राघवः। शत्रूणां प्रतिघातार्थमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: When Rāvana's younger brother had spoken thus, Rāghava, said these words with reference to his beating the foe.

sn: पूर्वद्वारं तु लङ्काया नीलो वानरपुंगवः। प्रहस्तं प्रतियोद्धा स्याद्वानरैर्बहुभिर्वृतः॥
en: Let that foremost of monkey, Nila, surrounded to by an immense number of monkeys, cope with Prahasta at the Eastern gate of Lankā.

sn: अङ्गदो वालिपुत्रस्तु बलेन महता वृतः। दक्षिणे बाधतां द्वारे महापार्श्वमहोदरौ॥
en: And, engirt by a mighty force, let Angada, son of Válī, resist Mahăpărśva and Mahodara at the Southern gate (thereof).

sn: हनूमान्पश्चिमद्वारं निष्पीड्य पवनात्मजः। प्रविशत्वप्रमेयात्मा बहुभिः कपिभिर्वृतः॥
en: And let that son of the Wind-god, Hanuman, backed by innumerable monkeys, (beating the host stationed) at the Western gate, find entrance (into the city).

sn: दैत्यदानवसङ्घानामृषीणां च महात्मनाम्। विप्रकारप्रियः क्षुद्रो वरदानबलान्वितः॥ परिक्रमति यः सर्वांल्लोकान्संतापयन्प्रजाः। तस्याहं राक्षसेन्द्रस्य स्वयमेव वधे धृतः॥ उत्तरं नगरद्वारमहं सौमित्रिणा सह । निपीड्याभिप्रवेक्ष्यामि सबलो यत्र रावणः॥
en: I myself, determined compass the destruction of the lord of Räkşasas, who, waxing powerful in consequence of the boon he has received, has brought about the destruction of high-souled saints resembling gods and Dänavas, and who goes round all regions, oppressing people, will, along with Sumitra's son, smiting (the foe), occupy the Northern entiuile., where Rāvana with his army is stationed.

sn: वानरेन्द्रश्च बलवानृक्षराजश्च वीर्यवान्। राक्षसेन्द्रानुनश्चैव गुल्मे भवतु मध्यमे॥
en: And let the powerful king of monkeys, and the puissant sovereign of bears, and the younger brother of the Raksasa-chief, manage the soldiery posted in the centre.

sn: न चैव मानुषं रूपं कार्य हरिभिराहवे। एषा भवतु नः संज्ञा युद्धेऽस्मिन्वानरे बले॥ वानरा एव नश्चिहूं स्वजनेऽस्मिन्भविष्यति। वयं तु मानुषेणेव सप्त योत्स्यामहे परान्॥
en: In this battle, the monkeys need not assume the forms of human being. And let this serve for a sign that the monkeys, in order to the recognition of our own forces, appear with their proper monkey-marks. We seven only shall battle with the foe in human shapes, viz.

sn: अहमेव सह भ्रात्रा लक्ष्मणेन महौजसा। आत्मना पञ्चमश्चायं सखा मम बिभीषणः॥
en: I along with my brother, the exceedingly energetic Lakşmaņa, and my friend Vibhīşaņa counting for the fifth in company with his own following.

sn: स रामः कृत्यसिद्ध्यर्थमेवमुक्त्वा बिभीषणम्। सुवेलारोहणे बुद्धिं चकार मतिमान्प्रभुः।। रमणीयतरं दृष्ट्वा सुवेलस्य गिरेस्तटम्॥
en: Having said this to Vibhísaņa for attaining success in the enterprise, that lord, the intelligent Rāma, seeing the sides of Suvela more beautiful (than other places), intended to ascend it.

sn: ततस्तु रामो महता बलेन प्रच्छाद्य सर्वां पृथिवीं महात्मा। प्रहृष्टरूपोऽभिजगाम लङ्कां कृत्वा मतिं सोऽरिवधे महात्मा॥
en: Then, environed by a mighty host, the highsouled and magnanimous Rāma, his features mirroring forth high exultation, overshadowing the entire Earth (with his forces), set out for Lankā, determined upon destroying the enemy.

sn: स तु कृत्वा सुवेलस्य मतिमारोहणं प्रति। लक्ष्मणानुगतो रामः सुग्रीवमिदमब्रवीत्॥ विभीषणं च धर्मज्ञमनुरक्तं निशाचरम्। मन्त्रज्ञं च विधिज्ञं च श्लक्ष्णया परया गिरा॥
en: Having been bent upon mounting Suvela, Rāma, followed by Lakşmaņa, addressed in sweet and excellent words, Sugriva, and that righteous night-ranger, Vibhisana, versed in। counsel and conversant with precepts, who was devoted to him, saying.

sn: सुवेलं साधुशैलेन्द्रमिमं धातुशतैश्चितम्। अध्यारोहामहे सर्वे वत्स्यामोऽत्र निशामिमाम्॥
en: We shall all ascend this mount Suvela, be dight with metals; and pass this night even here.

sn: लङ्कां चालोकयिष्यामो निलयं तस्य रक्षसः। येन मे मरणान्ताय हृता भार्या दुरात्मना॥ येन धर्मो न विज्ञातो न वृत्तं न कुलं तथा। राक्षस्या नीचया बुद्ध्या येन तद्गर्हितं कृतम्।। तस्मिन्मे वर्तते रोषः कीर्तिते राक्षसाधमे। यस्यापराधानीचस्य वधं द्रक्ष्यामि रक्षसाम्।। एको हि कुरुते पापं कालपाशवशं गतः। नीचेनात्मापचारेण कुलं तेन विनश्यति।।
en: And (from here) will we view the abode of that Raksasa who, foul of soul, has carried off my spouse, to bring destruction down on himself, who knows normorality not good conduct nor behaviour (conducive to the dignity of his descent), and who, in consequence of his base propensity, has committed himself to so heinous a course of action.

sn: एवं संमन्त्रयन्नेव सक्रोधो रावणं प्रति। रामः सुवेलमासाद्य चित्रसानुमुपारुहत्॥
en: Having decided thus, Rāma, filled with wrath at Ravana, coming to Suvela, ascended its variegated plateau.

sn: पृष्ठतो लक्ष्मणश्चैनमन्वगच्छत् समाहितः। सशरं चापमुद्यम्य सुमहविक्रमे रतः॥ तमन्वारोहत्सुग्रीवः सामात्यः सविभीषणः। ते वायुवेगप्रवणास्तं गिरि गिरिचारिणः।।।।
en: And Laksmana, collected, went in his wake. And, upraising bow and arrow, Sugriva, (ever) engaged in valorous acts, accompanied with Vibhişaņa as well as his counsellors, following him, also ascended (the mountain).

sn: अध्यारोहन्त शतशः सुवेलं यत्र राघवः। ते त्वदीर्पण कालेन गिरिमारुह्य सर्वतः।।।।
en: And all those rangers of mountains, gifted with the vehemence of the Wind in hundreds ascended mount Suvela, where Rāghava was stationed.

sn: ददृशुः शिखरे तस्य विषक्तामिव खे पुरीम्। तां शुभां प्रवरद्वारा प्राकारवरशोभिताम्॥ लङ्कां राक्षससंपूर्णां ददृशुहरियूथपाः।
en: Ascending the mountain in a short time, they all beheld from its summit the city, appearing to be built on the air. And the monkey-leaders beheld Lankā, exceedingly splendid with noble gateways; gracefully enclosed with a wall; thronging with Rakşasas; and defended by sable Raksasas.

sn: प्राकारवरसंस्थैश्च तथा नीलैश्च राक्षसैः। ददृशुस्ते हरिश्रेष्ठाः प्राकारमपरं कृतम्॥
en: The foremost of monkeys saw these appearing like another wall (overtopping the one beneath).

sn: तं दृष्ट्वा वानराः सर्वे राक्षसान्युद्धकाङ्गिणः। मुमुचुर्विविधान्नादांस्तस्य रामस्य पश्यतः॥
en: On seeing the Rākşasas, the monkeys burning for battle set up various roars in the presence of Rama.

sn: ततोऽस्तमगमत्सूर्यः संध्यया प्रतिरञ्जितः। पूर्णचन्द्रप्रदीप्ता च क्षपा समतिवर्तत ॥
en: Then the Sun, crimsoned with Eve, ascended the Setting-hill; and Night came, illumined by the Moon at his full.

sn: विभीषणेन प्रतिनन्ध सत्कृतः। सलक्ष्मणो यूथपयूथसंयुतः सुवेलपृष्ठे न्यवसद्यथासुखम्॥
en: Then the master of the monkey-army, Rāma, saluted and honoured by Vibhisana, accompanied by Lakşmaņa as well as the leaders of the monkeys, sojourned happily on the beast of Suvela.

sn: तां रात्रिमुषितास्तत्र सुवेले हरियूथपाः। लङ्कायां ददृशुर्वीरा वनान्युपवनानि च॥
en: Having passed the night in Suvela, the heroic monkey-leaders surveyed woods and forests in Lankā.

sn: समसौम्यानि रम्याणि विशालान्यायतानि च। दृष्टिरम्याणि ते दृष्ट्वा बभूवुर्जातविस्मयः॥
en: Seeing those extensive (woods and forests), mild, and charming, and beautiful to behold, they were seized with wonderment.

sn: चम्पकाशोकबकुलशालतालसमाकुला। तमालापनसच्छन्ना नागमालासमावृता॥ हिन्तालैरर्जुनैींपैः सप्तवर्णैः सुपुष्पितैः। तिलकैः कर्णिकारैश्च पाटलैश्च समन्ततः॥ शुशुभे पुष्पिताणैव लतापरिगतदुमैः। लङ्कां बहुविधैर्दृश्यैर्यथेन्द्रस्यामरावती॥
en: Abounding in champakas, asokas, vakulas, śālas, and palms; covered with tamālas and panišas, and environed all around with trees, and surrounded with Hintālas, Arjunas, blossoming Saptaparmas, Tilakas, Karmikāras, and Patalas, trees with flowering tops, entertwined with creepers, Larkā looked exceedingly lovely, with various sights, resembling the Amarāvatī herself of Indra.

sn: विचित्रकुसुमोपेतै रक्तकोमलपल्लवैः। शाद्वलैश्च तथा नीलश्चित्राभिर्वनराजिभिः॥ गन्धाढ्यान्यतिरम्याणि पुष्पाणि च फलानि च। धारयन्त्यगमास्तत्र भूषणानीव मानवाः।७।।
en: And trees there, furnished with variegated flowers having tender rosy leaves, and blue lawns, and rows of woods; and bearing odorous and charming blossoms and fruits, looked like men adorned with ornaments.

sn: तच्चैत्ररथसंकाशं मनोज्ञं नन्दनोपमम्। वनं सर्वर्तुकं रम्यं शुशुभे षट्पदायुतम्॥
en: There a delightful and pleasant wood resembling Caitraratha, and like to Nandana itself, having all the seasons present, appeared beauteous to the view, with black bees all around.

sn: दात्यूहकोयष्टिवकैर्नृत्यमानैश्च बहिणैः। रुतं परभृतानां च शुश्रुवे वननिझरे॥
en: And it had Dātyühas, and Koyașthivas, and peacocks dancing; and the strains of the coels were heard at the woodland rills.

sn: नित्यमत्तविहंगानि भ्रमराचरितानि च। कोकिलाकुलखण्डानि विहंगाभिरुतानि च॥ भृङ्गराजाधिगीतानि कुररस्वनितानि च। विविशुस्ते ततस्तानि वनान्युपवनानि च॥
en: The heroic and exhilarated monkeys, capable of wearing forms at pleasure, entered those woods and groves frequented by maddened birds and ranged by Bhramaras, tracts overflowing with the lays of coels, and ringing with the voices of songsters, resonant with the notes of Bhramaras, sovereigns of their species and eloquent with the cries of ospreys.

sn: हृष्टाः प्रमुदिता वीरा हरयः कामरूपिणः। तेषां प्रविशतां तत्र वानराणां महौजसाम्॥ पुष्पसंसर्गसुरभिर्ववौ प्राणसमोऽनिलः। अन्ये तु हरिवीराणां यूथानिष्क्रम्य यूथपाः।। सुग्रीवेणाभ्यनुज्ञाता लङ्का जग्मुः पताकिनीम्॥
en: As the exceedingly energetic monkeys entered, there blew upon them the breeze-like to life-redolent of perfume obtained from contact with the blossoms. And others of the leaders among the heroic monkeys, coming out from the bands, ordered by Sugriva, made in the direction of Lankā crowned with ensigns.

sn: वित्रासयन्तो विहगान ग्लापयन्तो मृगद्विपान्। कम्पयन्तश्च तां लङ्कां नादैः स्वैर्नदतां वराः॥
en: And, terrifying the fowls and dispiriting beasts and birds and shaking Lankā with their roars, those foremost monkeys set up shouts.

sn: कुर्वन्तस्ते महावेगा महीं चरणपीडिताम्। रजश्च सहसैवोर्ध्वं जगाम चरणोत्थितम्॥
en: They, endowed with great impetuosity, went on, oppressing the earth with their battle-array; and clouds of dust suddenly arose from the march of the soldiery.

sn: ऋक्षाः सिंहाश्च महिषा वारणाश्च मृगाः खगाः। तेन शब्देन विवस्ता जग्मुर्भीता दिशो दश॥
en: And bears, and lions, and buffaloes, and elephants, and deer, and birds, overwhelmed with affright, made for the t en cardinal points.

sn: शिखरं तु त्रिकूटस्य प्रांशु चैकं दिविस्पृशम्। समन्दात्पुष्पसंछनं महारजतसंनिभम् ॥ शतयोजनविस्तीर्णं विमलं चारुदर्शनम्। श्लक्ष्णं श्रीमन्महच्चैव दुष्प्रापं शकुनैरपि॥ मनसापि दुरारोहं किं पुनः कर्मणा जनैः। निविष्टा तस्य शिखरे लङ्का रावणपालिता॥ दशयोजनविस्तीर्णा विंशद्योजनमायता। सा पुरी गोपुरैरुच्चैः पाण्डुराम्बुदसंनिभैः।। काञ्चनेन च शालेन राजतेन च शोभते॥ प्रासादैश्च विमानैश्च लङ्का परमभूषिता। घनैरिवातपापाये मध्यमं वैष्णवं पदम्॥
en: The graceful and lovely summit of Trikūța was entire, elevated, skypiercing, of golden splendour, measuring an hundred Yojanas, clearshining, level, inaccessible even to fowls, and not to say of actual ascension by people. Lanka, ruled by Ravana, was situated on its' top, ten Yojanas in width and twenty in length. And that city was graced with lofty ornamented gateways resembling pale clouds, and golden and silver wall; and Lankā was adorned with palaces and piles; like the sky graced with clouds on the approach of the rainy season. 1. Trikūța's. 2. Madhyamam Vaisnavam padam, the middle foot of Vişnu. When Vişņu in his Dwarf-from took the conceit out of Vāli, the renowned Asura king, he covered the earth with one pace, the sky with another and heaven with last.

sn: यस्यां स्तम्भसहस्रेण प्रासादः समलंकृतः। कैलासशिखराकारो दृश्यते खमिवोल्लिखन्।।२२ चैत्यः स राक्षसेन्द्रस्य बभूव पुरभूषणम्। शतेन रक्षसां नित्यं यः समग्रेण रक्ष्यते॥
en: That palace, which was adorned with thousands of pillars, and which, as if piercing the heavens, looked like a peak of Kailasa—was the residence of the Sovereign of the Rākşasas—the ornament of the city, (ever guarded by full hundreds of Raksasas.

sn: मनोज्ञां काञ्चनवतीं पर्वतैरुपशोभिताम्। नानाधातुविचित्रैश्च उद्यानैरुपशोभिताम्॥ नानाविहगसंघुष्टां नानामृगनिषेविताम्। नानाकुसुमसंपन्नां नानाराक्षससेविताम्॥ तां समृद्धां समृद्धार्थां लक्ष्मीवॉल्लक्ष्मणाग्रजः। नगरीं त्रिदिवप्रख्या विस्मयं प्राप वीर्यवान्॥
en: Lakṣmaṇa's auspicious and puissant elder brother, beholding that flourishing and wealthy city resembling the celestial regions, charming to the mind, made of gold, graced with mountains, and decked out with mountains containing various metals, resonant with the notes of various birds; abounding in various beasts, furnished with various kinds of flowers, and inhabited by various orders of Rākşasas, was struck with astonishment.

sn: तां रत्नपूर्णां बहुसंविधानां प्रासादमालाभिरलङ्कृतां च। पुरीं महायन्त्रकवाटमुख्यां ददर्श रामो महता बलेन।।२७
en: Rāma, surrounded by his mighty forces, saw that palace, filled with diverse kinds of gems, adorned with rows of edifices, and having huge engines and gateways.

sn: ततो रामः सुवेलाग्रं योजनद्वयमण्डलम्। उपारोहत्ससुग्रीवो हरियूथैः समन्वितः॥
en: Then Rāma, accompanied by the monkeyleaders, along with Sugrīva, ascended the top of Suvela, measuring a circumference of two Yojanas.

sn: स्थित्वा मुहूर्तं तत्रैव दिशो दश विलोकयन्। त्रिकूटशिखरे रम्ये निर्मितां विश्वकर्मणा॥ ददर्श लङ्कां सुन्यस्तां रम्यकाननशोभिताम्। तस्य गोपुरशृङ्गस्थं राक्षसेन्द्रं दुरासदम्॥ श्वेतचामरपर्यन्तं विजयच्छत्रशोभितम्। रक्तचन्दनसंलिप्तं रक्ताभरणभूषितम्॥ नीलजीमूतसंकाशं हेमसंछादिताम्बरम्। ऐरावतविषाणा।रुत्कृष्टकिणवक्षसम्॥ शशलोहितरागेण संवीतं रक्तवाससा। संध्यातपेन संछन्नं मेघराशिमिवाम्बरे।६॥
en: And staying there for a while and looking at the ten cardinal points, he saw Lankā finely placed on the charming summit of Trikūța, graced with elegant groves; and (he also saw) the unconquerable lord of Räksasas, stationed at the top of the gateway, fanned with white chāmaras; graced with the umbrella betokening victory; smeared with red sandal; adorned in red ornaments; resembling masses of sable clouds; and apparelled in golden attire, his breast bearing scars from the tusk-ends of Airavata; covered with a sheet hued like the blood of hares; and appearing like clouds lighted up by the evening sun.

sn: पश्यतां वानरेन्द्राणां राघवस्यापि पश्यतः। दर्शनाद्राक्षसेन्द्रस्य सुग्रीवः सहसोत्थितः॥
en: On seeing the Raksasa-chief, Sugriva suddenly rose up in the sight of the lords of monkeys as well as Rāghava.

sn: क्रोधवेगेन संयुक्तः सत्त्वेन च बलेन च। अचलाग्रादथोत्थाय पुप्लुवे गोपुरस्थले॥
en: And influenced by wrath, he, mustering strength and vigour, rising from the brow of the mountain, bounded to the gateway.

sn: स्थित्वा मुहूर्त संप्रेक्ष्य निर्भयेनान्तरात्मना। तृणीकृत्य च तद्रक्षः सोऽब्रवीत् परुषं वचः॥
en: And pausing for a while and eyeing the Rāks asa intrepidly, he, slighting the Raksasa, addressed him in harsh speech, saying.

sn: लोकनाथस्य रामस्य सखा दासोऽस्मि राक्षस। न मया मोक्ष्यसेऽद्य त्वं पार्थिवेन्द्रस्य तेजसा ॥
en: O Rākşasa, I am the friend as well as the slave of Rāma-lord of men. Me, backed by the energy of that king of the Earth, shall you not escape today.

sn: इत्युक्त्वा सहसोत्पत्य पुप्लुवे तस्य चोपरि। आकृष्य मुकुटं चित्र पातयामास तद्भुवि॥
en: Saying this, he, suddenly springing up, descended on him; and snatching away his variegated crown, let it fa}l on the earth.

sn: समीक्ष्य तूर्णमायान्तं बभाषे तं निशाचरः। सुग्रीवस्त्वं परोक्षं मे हीनग्रीवो भविष्यसि ॥
en: Seeing his come abruptly, the night-ranger spoke to him thus, Thus that were Sugrīva beyond my ken, shall be neckless near me.

sn: इत्युक्त्वोत्थाय तं क्षिप्रं बाहुभ्यामाक्षिपत्तले। कन्दुवत्स समुत्थाय बाहुभ्यामाक्षिपद्धरिः॥
en: Having said this, be rose up swiftly and dragged him down to the earth. Thereat springing like pith, the monkey pushed down his antagonist with his arms.

sn: परस्परं स्वेदविदिग्धगात्रौ परस्परं शोणितरक्तदेहौ। परस्परं श्लिष्टनिरुद्धचेष्टौ परस्परं शाल्मलिकिंशुकाविव।। मुष्टिप्रहारैश्च तलप्रहारैररनिघातैश्च कराग्रघातैः। तौ चक्रतुयुद्धमसह्यरूपं महाबलौ राक्षसवानरेन्द्रौ॥
en: Each having his body bathed in sweat and his person covered with blood each choking and annulling the efforts of the other, and resembling a Sālmali or a Kinsuka, and dealing blows and slaps, and hitting with his arms and hands, those exceedingly strong ones, the lord of the Rākşasas and that of the monkeys, fought wonderfully.

sn: कृत्वा नियुद्धं भृशमुग्रवेगौ कालं चिरं गोपुरवेदिमध्ये। उत्क्षिप्य चोत्क्षिप्य विनम्य देहौ पादक्रमानोपुरवेदिलग्नौ॥
en: And having for a long time encountered each other in combat on the dais belonging to the gate, they, now lifting up their persons and now lowering them, went down, each felling the other with his legs.

sn: अन्योन्यमापीड्य विलग्नदेहौ तौ पेततुः सालनिखातमध्ये। उत्पेततुर्भूमितलं स्पृशन्तौ स्थित्वा मुहूर्तं त्वभिनिःश्वसन्तौ ॥
en: Smiting each other, they, their bodies fastened together, went down between the wall and the moat, and again stood upon the ground.

sn: आलिङ्ग्य चालिङ्गय च बाहुयोक्त्रैः संयोजयामासतुराहवे तौ। संरम्भशिक्षाबलसंप्रयुक्तौ सुचेरतुः संप्रति युद्धमार्गे॥ शार्दूलसिंहाविव जातदंष्ट्री गजेन्द्रपोताविव संप्रयुक्तौ। संहत्य संवेद्य च तौ कराभ्यां तौ पेततुर्वै युगपद्धरायाम्॥ उद्यम्य चान्योन्यमधिक्षिपन्तौ संचक्रमाते बहु युद्धमार्गे। व्यायामशिक्षाबलसंप्रयुक्तौ क्लमं न तौ जग्मतुराशु वीरौ ॥
en: Having breath, they, resting for a space, grappled with each other; and they fast bound each other with their arms serving for ropes. And each fired with wrath, and each having both strength and skill, they now bore themselves in the lists like a tiger and a lion, furnished with teeth; or like the young of the foremost elephants engaged in encounter, and restraining and pushing each other with their arms, they simultaneously both came down to the ground, Then starting again to their feet, they, vituperating each other, ranged the lists, displaying feats expressive of skill and strength. Nor did those heroes speedily come by fatigue.

sn: बाहूत्तमैवरिणवारणाभैर्निवारयन्तौ परवारणाभौ। चिरेण कालेन भृशं प्रयुद्धौ संरतुर्मण्डलमार्गमाशु ॥
en: And resembling mighty elephants, they, resisting each other by means of their powerful arms like to the trunks of elephants, fought for a long while, swiftly wheeling about the arena.

sn: तौ परस्परमासाद्य यत्तावन्योन्यसूदने। मार्जाराविव भक्षार्थेऽवतस्थाते मुहुर्महुः॥
en: Approaching each other, they strove to slay each other, like to two cats seated, momentarily encountering each other over some food.

sn: मण्डलानि विचित्राणि स्थानानि विविधानि च। गोमूत्रकाणि चित्राणि गतप्रत्यागतानि च॥ तिरश्चीनगतान्येव तथा वक्रगतानि च। परिमोक्षं प्रहाराणां वर्जनं परिधावनम्॥ अभिद्रवणमाप्लावमवस्थानं सविग्रहम्। परावृत्तमपावृत्तमपद्रुतमवप्लुतम्॥ उपन्यस्तमपन्यस्तं युद्धमार्गविशारदौ। तौ विचेरतुरन्योन्यं वानरेन्द्रश्च रावणः॥
en: The lord of monkeys and Ravana, accomplished in fight, coursed the arena, displaying wonderful Mandalas, various sthānas, (a) curious gomutrakas, (b) gatapratyagatas, tirascinagatas, Vakragatas, parimoksas, varjanas, paridhāvanas, abhidravaņas, (c) aplavanas (d) savigrahāvasthānas, (e) paravrttas, (1) apavrttas, (g) apadrutas, (h) avaplutas, (i) apanyastas, (j) and upanyastas (k).

sn: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे रक्षो मायाबलमथात्मनः। आरब्धुमुपसंपेदे ज्ञात्वा तं वानराधिपः॥ उत्पपात तदाकाशं जिकाशी जितक्लमः। रावणं स्थित एवात्र हरिराजेन वञ्चितः॥
en: In the meanwhile the Rākşasa attempted to put forth his power of illusion. Knowing this, the king of monkeys shot into the sky. And Rāvana, overpowered by fatigue and out of breath, thus baffled by the monkey-king, stood where he was.

sn: अथ हरिवरनाथः प्राप्तसंग्रामकीर्थिर्निशिचरपतिमाजौ योजयित्वा श्रमेण। गगनमतिविशालं लङ्घयित्वार्र्कसॊनुर्हरिगणबलमध्ये रामपार्वं जगाम ॥
en: Thus the master of the foremost monkeys, securing fame in fight, beat the night-ranger, causing him to experience fatigue. And bounding beyond the spacious sky, the offspring of the Sun came to the side of Rāma in the midst of the monkey-forces.

sn: स इति सवितृसूनुस्तत्र तत्कर्म कृत्वा पवनगतिरनीकं प्राविशत्संप्रहृष्टः। रघुवरनृपसूनोर्वर्धयन्युद्धहर्ष तरुमृगगणमुख्यैः पूज्यमानो हरीन्द्रः॥
en: Having done that deed, the son of the Sun, lord of monkeys-with his heart surcharged with rejoicing, entered that host having the speed of the wind; enhancing the martial ardour of the son of the foremost of the Raghus, and honoured by the monkeys.

sn: अथ तस्मिन्निमित्तानि दृष्ट्वा लक्ष्मणपूर्वजः। सुग्रीवं संपरिष्वज्य रामो वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Seeing those ominous signs, Lakşmaņa's elder brother, Ramā, embracing Sugrīva, said.

sn: असंमन्त्र्य मया सार्धं तदिदं साहसं कृतम्। एवं साहसयुक्तानि न कुर्वन्ति जनेश्वराः॥
en: Without consulting with me, you have acted thus rashly. But kings should not act in such a rash way.

sn: संशये स्थाप्य मां चेदं बलं चेमं बिभीषणम्। कष्टं कृतमिदं वीर साहसं साहसप्रिय॥
en: Placing in suspense, me, this army and Vibhīş aņa, you, O hero, enamoured of daring deeds, have put yourself to all this trouble.

sn: इदानीं मा कृथा वीर एवंविधमरिंदम। त्वयि किंचित्समापन्ने किं कार्य सीतया मम॥ भरतेन महाबाहो लक्ष्मणेन यवीयसा। शत्रुघ्नेन च शत्रुघ्न स्वशरीरेण वा पुनः॥
en: But, O hero, henceforth, do not act so. O subduer of enemies, if you come by any mischance, what shall Sita avail me; or Bharata; my younger brother-Lakşmaņa; or Satrughna, O slayer of enemies; or, again, my own person?

sn: त्वयि चानागते पूर्वमिति मे निश्चिता मतिः। जानतश्चापि ते वीर्य महेन्द्रवरुणोपम॥ हत्वाहं रावणं युद्धे सपुत्रबलवाहनम्। अभिषिच्य च लङ्कायां विभीषणमथाप च।७।। भरते राज्यमारोप्य त्यक्ष्ये देहं महाबल।
en: Ere you had come, I had arrived at this determination; albeit, O you that are equal to the mighty Indra or Varuna, I knew your prowess full well. Slaying Rāvana in battle along with his sons, forces and vehicles, and installing Vibhīşaņa in Lankā, and placing the kingdom in the hands of Bharata, I shall renounce my body, O exceedingly powerful one!

sn: तमेवं वादिनं रामं सुग्रीवः प्रत्यभाषत।।।। तव भार्यापहर्तारं दृष्ट्वा राघव रावणम्। मर्षयामि कथं वीर जानन्विक्रममात्मनः।९।।
en: When Rāma had said this, Sugrīva answered, Knowing my own strength, how, O Rāghava, viewing Rāvana, who had ravished away your wife, could I forbear, O hero?

sn: इत्येवं वादिनं वीरमभिनन्द्य च राघवः। लक्ष्मणं लक्ष्मिसंपन्नमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: As that hero was speaking thus Raghava addressed Lakṣmaṇa having auspiciousness, thus.

sn: परिगृह्योदकं शीतं वनानि फलवन्ति च। बलौघं संविभज्येमं व्यूह्य तिष्ठाम लक्ष्मण॥
en: O Lakşmaņa, occupying some tract furnished with cool water and woods bearing fruits, we shall sojourn, dividing and marshalling our forces.

sn: लोकक्षयकरं भीमं भयं पश्याम्युपस्थितम्। निबर्हणं प्रवीराणामृक्षवानररक्षसाम्॥
en: I see a mighty fear present, destructive of people, and boding destruction to the foremost heroes among the bears, monkeys and Rākşasas.

sn: वाता हि परुषं वान्ति कम्पते च वसुंधरा। पर्वताग्राणि वेपन्ते नदन्ति धरणीधराः॥
en: The winds ruffle; and the earth is tremulous. And the tops of mountains tremble, and the mountains themselves send up loud sounds.

sn: मेघाः क्रव्यादसंकाशाः परुषाः परुषस्वराः। क्रूराः क्रूरं प्रवर्षन्ते मिश्रं शोणितबिन्दुभिः॥
en: The clouds are goblinish; and fierce; and harsh-sounding. And wearing terrific looks, they fiercely pour down showers mixed with drops of blood.

sn: रक्तचन्दनसंकाशा संध्या परमदारुणा। ज्वलच्च निपतत्येतदादित्यादग्निमण्डलम्॥
en: The Evening resembles the red sandal, and is fearful. And a flaming circle dropped from the Sun.

sn: आदित्यमभिवाश्यन्ति जनयन्तो महद्भयम्। दीना दीनस्वराः क्रूरा अप्रशस्ता मृगद्विजाः॥
en: And exciting great fear, inauspicious birds and beasts, wearing cruel looks, and in distressful guise, cry in piteous accents, facing the Sun.

sn: रजन्यामप्रशस्तश्च संतापयति चन्द्रमाः। कृष्णरक्तांशुपर्यन्तो यथा लोकस्य संक्षये॥
en: At night, the ominous Moon with a black-red brim as at the time of universal wreck, burn.

sn: हस्वो रूक्षो प्रशस्तश्च परिवेषः सुलोहितः। आदित्यमण्डले नीलं लक्ष्म लक्ष्मण दृश्यते॥
en: O Laksmana, there is a crimson, rough, slight, and graceful rim round the Sun; and a blue mark is visible on his disc.

sn: दृश्यते न यथावच्च नक्षत्राण्यभिवर्तते। युगान्तमिव लोकस्य पश्य लक्ष्मण शंसति॥
en: The stars do not course as formerly. Behold, O Laksmana, all these, prefiguring the Doom.

sn: काकाः श्येनास्तथा गृध्रा नीचैः परिपतन्ति च। शिवाश्चाप्यशुभा वाचः प्रवदन्ति महास्वनाः॥
en: And crows and hawks and vultures drop down. And jackals yell loud inauspicious notes.

sn: शैलैः शूलैश्च खङ्गैश्च विमुक्तैः कपिराक्षसैः। भविष्यत्यावृता भूमिमा॑सशोणितकर्दमा।२१।।
en: The Earth, converted into mud with flesh and gore, shall be covered with darts and javelins and swords, discharged by Rākşasas and monkeys.

sn: क्षिप्रमद्य दुराधर्षों पुरीं रावणपालिताम्। अभियाम जवेनैव सर्वतो हरिभिर्वृताः॥
en: This very day with all expedition shall we surrounded on all sides by the monkeys, march towards the city governed by Rāvaņa.

sn: इत्येवं तु वदन्वीरो लक्ष्मणं लक्ष्मणाग्रजः। तस्मादवातरच्छीघ्रं पर्वताग्रान्महाबलः॥
en: Having said this to Laksmana, Laksmana's elder brother possessed of exceeding strength, hastily descended from the top of the mountain.

sn: अवतीर्य तु धर्मात्मा तस्माच्छैलात्स राघवः। परैः परमदुर्धर्षं ददर्श बलमात्मनः॥
en: And descending from the mountain, the righteous Rāghava surveyed his troops, incapable of being beaten by enemies.

sn: संनह्य तु ससुग्रीवः कपिराजबलं महत्। कालज्ञो राघवः काले संयुगायाभ्यचोदयत्॥
en: After making the mighty host of the monkeysking equip itself, Raghava versed in season, along with Sugrīva, at the proper hour, issued orders for battle.

sn: ततः काले महाबाहुर्बलेन महता वृतः। प्रविष्टः पुरतो धन्वी लङ्कामभिमुखः पुरीम्॥
en: Then in due time that one, accoutred with his bow, surrounded by a mighty army, set out, with the intention of entering the city of Lanka.

sn: तौ बिभीषणसुग्रीवौ हनूमाञ्जाम्बवानलः। ऋक्षराजस्तथा नीलो लक्ष्मणश्चान्वयुस्तदा॥
en: Those two-Vibhisana and Sugriva-~-and Hanumān, and jāmbavăn, and Nala, and the bear-king Nila, and Laksmana, followed (Rama).

sn: ततः पश्चात्सुमहती पृतनक्षवनौकसाम्। प्रच्छाद्य महती भूमिमनुयाति स्म राघवम्।।२८
en: Behind them, the mighty array of bears and monkeys followed Rāghava, severing a wide surface of land.

sn: शैलशृङ्गाणि शतशः प्रवृद्धांश्च महीरुहान्। जगृहुः कुअरप्रख्या वानराः परवारणाः।२९।।
en: The monkeys, resembling elephants, capable of resisting foes, took mountain-peaks and tall trees by hundreds.

sn: तौ त्वदीर्पण कालेन भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ। रावणस्य पुरीं लङ्कामासेदतुररिंदमौ॥ पताकामालिनी रम्यामुद्यानवनशोभिताम्। चित्रवप्रां सुदुष्प्रापामुच्चैः प्राकारतोरणाम्॥
en: In a short time those repressors of foes— two brothers Rāma and Lakşmaņa-arrived at the city of Răvaņa; with pennons streaming over her; charming; garnished with groves and woods, having variegated gateways; inaccessible; and having walls and gates.

sn: तां सुरैरपि दुर्धर्षां रामवाक्यप्रचोदिताः। यथा निदेशं संपीड्य न्यविशन्त वनौकसः॥
en: And urged on by Rāma's command, the wood-raingers,* as commanded, blocking up (Lankā) incapable of being subdued even by the gods, stationed themselves. *Monkeys.

sn: लङ्कायास्तूत्तरद्वारं शैलशृङ्गमिवोत्रतम्। रामः सहानुजो धन्वी जुगोप च रुरोध च॥ लङ्कामुपनिविष्टस्तु रामो दशरथात्मजः। लक्ष्णानुचरो वीरः पुरीं रावणपालिताम्॥ उत्तरद्वारमासाद्य यत्र तिष्ठति रावणः। नान्यो रामाद्धि तद्वारं समर्थः परिरक्षितुम्॥ रावणाधिष्ठितं भीमं वरुणेनेव सागरम्। सायुधै राक्षसैीमैरभिगुप्तं समन्ततः॥ लघूनां त्रासजननं पातालमिव दानवैः। विन्यस्तानि च योधाना बहूनि विविधानि च॥ ददर्शायुधजालानि तथैव कवचानि च।
en: Coming to Lanka ruled by Ravana, that hero, Rama, son to Dasaratha, along with Laksmana, remained stationed at the Northern gate, where Råvaņa used to reside. None save Rāma was competent to protect that dreadful gate, where Råvaņa used to reside and guarded by Rāvana himself, like the Ocean guarded by Varuna, and protected on all sides by terrible Rākşasas equipped with weapons; capable of striking terror into the weak; like to the nether regions guarded by Danavas. And (Rama) saw there : many and various arms and mail of the warriors, ranged together.

sn: पूर्वं तु द्वारमासाद्य नीलो हरिचमूपतिः॥ अतिष्ठत्सह मैन्देन द्विविदेन च वीर्यवान् ।
en: And coming to the Eastern gate, that leader of the monkeys-army, the powerful Nila, along with Mainda and Dvivida, took up his post there.

sn: अङ्गदो दक्षिणद्वारं जग्राह सुमहाबलः॥ ऋषभेण गवाक्षेण गजेन गवयेन च। हनूमान्पश्चिमद्वारं ररक्ष बलवान्कपिः४०।।
en: The exceedingly strong Angada, accompanied by Risabha, Gavaksa, Gaya, and Gavaya, occupied the Southern gate. And the mighty monkey Hanumān protected the Western entrance.

sn: प्रजङ्घतरसाभ्यां च वीरैरन्यैश्च संगतः। मध्यमे च स्वयं गुल्मे सुग्रीवः समतिष्ठत॥
en: And Sugrīva himself, with Prajangha, Tarasa and other heroes, was quartered near the garrison in the centre.

sn: सह सर्वैर्हरिश्रेष्ठैः सुवर्णपवनोपमैः। वानराणां तु षट्त्रिंशत्कोट्यः प्रख्यातयूथपाः॥ निपीड्योपनिविष्टाश्च सुग्रीवो यत्र वानरः।
en: And accompanied by all the foremost monkeys resembling Suparņa or the Wind, twenty kotis of renowned monkey-leaders, blocking up all sides, stationed themselves near the monkeys, Sugriva.

sn: शासनेन तु रामस्य लक्ष्मणः सविभीषणः॥ द्वारे द्वारे हरीणां तु कोटि कोटीयवेशयत्।
en: At Rama's command, Laksmana along with Vibhisana, went from door to door, issuing instructions to kotis of monkeys.

sn: पश्चिमेन तु रामस्य सुषेणः सहजाम्बवान्॥ अदूरान्मध्यमे गुल्मे तस्थौ बहुबलानुगः।
en: On the west of Rāma, Jāmbavän along with Susena, followed by innumerable troops, remained hard by at the garrison in the minddle.

sn: ते तु वानरशार्दूलाः शार्दूला इव दंष्ट्रिणः।। गृहीत्वा द्रुमशैलाग्रान्हष्टा युद्धाय तस्थिरे॥
en: And those tiger-like monkeys, furnished with teeth like to tigers, wielding trees and mountaintops, stood ready for fight.

sn: सर्वे विकृतलाङ्गलाः सर्वे दंष्ट्रानखायुधाः। सर्वे विकृतचित्राङ्गाः सर्वे च विकृताननाः॥
en: All had their tails curled up, and all were armed with teeth and nails, and all had chequered bodies, and all had frightful faces.

sn: दशनागबलाः केचित् केचिद्दशगुणोत्तराः। केचिन्नागसहस्रस्य बभूवुस्तुल्यविक्रमाः॥
en: Some had the strength of ten elephants; and some had strength ten times as much; and some of the monkeys-leaders there had the strength of a thousand elephants.

sn: सन्ति चौघबलाः केचित्केचिच्छतगुणोत्तराः। अप्रमेयबलाश्चान्ये तत्रासन्हरियूथपाः॥
en: Some had the strength of numbers (of elephants); and some had strength hundred times as much. And others had immeasurable might.

sn: अद्भुतश्च विचित्रश्च तेषामासीत्समागमः। तत्र वानरसैन्यानां शलभानामिवोद्गमः।॥
en: And wonderful and astonishing was their meeting. And the concourse at that place of the monkey-forces was like the concourse of locusts.

sn: प्रतिपूर्णमिवाकाशं संपूर्णेव च मेदिनी। लङ्कामुपनिविष्टैश्च संपतद्भिश्च वानरैः॥
en: The air was filled up, and the earth was covered quite with the monkeys coursing towards Lankā and dropping down into it.

sn: शतं शतसहस्राणां पृतनार्शवनौकसाम्। लङ्काद्वाराण्युपाजग्मुरन्ये योद्धं समन्ततः॥
en: And hundreds and thousands making up the army of monkeys, arrived at the gate of Lanka; while others were pouring in from all sides for encounter.

sn: आवृतः स गिरिः सर्वैस्तैः समन्तात्प्लवङ्गमैः। अयुतानां सहस्रं च पुरी तामभ्यवर्तत॥
en: That mount was covered with monkeys by all sides and a thousand ayutas were going round the city.

sn: वानरैर्बलवद्भिश्च बभूव दुमपाणिभिः। सर्वतः संवृता लङ्का दुष्प्रवेशापि वायुना॥
en: And Larkā, blocked up everywhere with powerful monkeys bearing trees in their hands, was incapable of being entered even by the Wind.

sn: राक्षसा विस्मयं जग्मुः सहसाभिनिपीडिताः। वानरैर्मेघसंकाशैः शक्रतुल्यपराक्रमैः॥
en: The Rākşasas, sore pressed by thousands of monkeys resembling masses of clouds, and like to Śakra himself in battle, were seized with amazement.

sn: महाञ्छब्दोऽभवत्तत्र बलौघस्याभिवर्ततः। सागरस्येव भित्रस्य यथा स्यात्सलिलस्वनः॥
en: Like to the roar of water on the ocean being riven, there arose a mighty tumult in consequence of the forces surging hither and thither.

sn: तेन शब्देन महता सप्राकारा सतोरणा। लङ्का प्रचलिता सर्वा सशैलवनकानना ॥
en: With that sound the entire Lankā, with her wall and gateways, her mountains, woods, and forests, began to shake.

sn: रामलक्ष्मणगुप्ता सा सुग्रीवेण च वाहिनी। बभूव दुर्धर्षतरा सर्वैरपि सुरासुरैः॥
en: That army, protected by Rāma and Lakşmaņa as well as Sugrīva, became and the more invincible even by the Asuras and celestials.

sn: राघवः संनिवश्यैव स्वसैन्यं रक्षसां वधे। संमन्त्र्य मन्त्रिभिः सार्धं निश्चित्य च पुनः पुनः॥ आनन्तर्यमभिप्रेप्सुः क्रमयोगार्थतत्त्ववित्।। बिभीषणस्यानुमते राजधर्ममनुस्मरन्॥ अङ्गदं वालितनयं समाहूयेदमब्रवीत्।
en: Having arraigned his forces with the view of destroying the Räkşasa, Rāghava, versed in the resources of war, taking counsel of the counsellors, and deciding again and again his course of action, intending to adopt further measures, resolved to abide by the advice of Vibhīşaņa, remembering the morality regulating monarchs. And then, calling Vāli's son, Angada, (Rāma) said.

sn: गत्वा सौम्य दशग्रीवं ब्रूहि मद्वचनात्कपे॥ लङ्घयित्वा पुरीं लङ्कां भयं त्यक्त्वा गतव्यथः। भ्रष्टश्रीकं गतैश्वर्यं मुमूर्षानष्टचेतनम्॥
en: O mild one, going to the Ten-necked one, tell him in my words, Bounding over the deep and casting off fear and dejection, I have laid siege to the city of Lankā; and have reft you of your prosperity and your wealth; and rendered you moribund and senseless.

sn: ऋषीणां देवतानां च गन्धर्वाप्सरसां तथा। नागानामथ यक्षाणां राज्ञां च रजनीचर॥ यच्च पापं कृत मोहादवलिप्तेन राक्षस। नूनं ते विगतो दर्पः स्वयंभूवरदानजः॥ यस्य दण्डधरस्तेऽहं दाराहरणकर्शितः। दण्डं धारयमाणस्तु लङ्काद्वारे व्यवस्थितः॥
en: You have, O night-ranger, through delusion and pride injured saints and celestials, and Gandharvas and Apsaras, and Serpents, and Yaksas, and crowned heads. But, O Raksasa, your pride begot of the boon received from the Self-create has gone from you, whose destroyer I, afflicted in consequence of my wife having been carried off, wielding the rod, have sat down at the door of Lankā.

sn: पदवी देवतानां च महर्षीणां च राक्षस। राजर्षीणां च सर्वेषां गमिष्यसि युधि स्थिरः॥
en: O Rākşasa, you shall, remaining steady in fight, attain the state of celestials and Maharsis and Rājarşis.

sn: बलेन येन वै सीतां मायया राक्षसाधम। मामतिक्रमयित्वा त्वं हृतवांस्तनिदर्शय॥
en: O worst of Rākşasas, do you display that prowess of your by which, aided by your power of illusion, you have forcible carried off Sītā, disregarding me.

sn: अराक्षसमिमं लोकं कर्तास्मि निशितैः शरैः। न चेच्छरणमभ्येषि तामादाय तु मैथिलीम्॥
en: I shall with my sharpened shafts render this world free from Rākşasas, unless rendering back Mitbila's daughter, you throw yourself on my mercy.

sn: धर्मात्मा राक्षसश्रेष्ठः संप्राप्तोऽयं बिभीषणः। लकैश्वर्यमिदं श्रीमान्ध्रुवं प्राप्नोत्यकण्टकम्॥
en: And, for certain, that foremost of Rākşasas, the righteous and graceful Vibhīşaņa, who has joined us, shall obtain, without having a thorn in his side, all this wealth of Lankā.

sn: नहि राज्यमधर्मेण भोक्तुं क्षणमपि त्वया। शक्यं मूर्खसहायेन पापेनाविदितात्मना ॥
en: For you, foolish, wicked, ignorant of selfknowledge, and having dolts for councillors, are not competent to unrighteously exercise kingship for a moment.

sn: युध्यस्व मा धृतिं कृत्वा शौर्यमालम्ब्य राक्षस। मच्छरैस्त्वं रणे शान्तस्ततः शान्तो भविष्यसि।।७०
en: Fight you, O Rāksasa, summoning fortitude and heroism. On being slain with my shafts, you shall attain peace.

sn: यद्याविशसि लोकांस्त्रीन्पक्षीभूतो निशाचर। मम चक्षुःपथं प्राप्य न जीवन्प्रतियास्यसि।७१।।
en: O night-ranger, if you should range the three worlds in the shape of a bird, you, coming in my ken, shall not be able to preserve your life.

sn: ब्रवीमि त्वां हितं वाक्यं क्रियतामौर्ध्वदेहिकम्। सुदृष्टा क्रियतां लङ्का जीवितं ते मयि स्थितम्॥
en: It is all this for your good; do you perform acts for the good of your body surviving death; and do you see Lankā well; for your life is in my keeping.

sn: इत्युक्तः स तु तारेयो रामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा। जगामाकाशमाविश्य मूर्तिमानिव हव्यवाट्॥
en: Thus addressed by Rāma of untiring deeds, Tara's son went through the welkin like the embodied bearer of sacrificial offerings.

sn: सोऽतिपत्य मुहूर्तेन श्रीमान्रावणमन्दिरम्। ददर्शासीनमव्यग्रं रावणं सचिवैः सह॥
en: Arriving near that subduer of enemies, Rāvana, in a moment, that graceful one saw Rāvana, sitting calmly in the midst of his ministers.

sn: ततस्तस्याविदूरेण निपत्य हरिपुंगवः। दीप्ताग्निसदृशस्तस्थावङ्गदः कनकाङ्गदः।७५ ।।
en: And dropping down in his vicinity like a flaming fire, that best of monkeys, Augada, resembling a golden bracelet, stood there.

sn: तद्रामवचनं सर्वमन्यूनाधिकमुत्तमम्। सामात्यं श्रावयामास निवेद्यात्मानमात्मना ॥
en: Then introducing himself, Angada delivered to Rāvana along with his ministers all that Rama had excellently spoken to him, neither extenuating nor setting down aught of himself.

sn: दूतोऽहं कोशलेन्द्रस्य रामस्याक्लिष्टकर्मणः। बालिपुत्रोऽङ्गदो नाम यदि ते श्रोत्रमागतः।७७।।
en: I am the envoy of the king of Kosala, Rāma of untiring deeds; and I am the son of Vāli I do not know whether you have heard of me.

sn: आह त्वां राघवो रामः कौसल्यानन्दवर्धनः। निष्पत्य प्रतियुध्यस्व नृशंस पुरुषो भव॥
en: Raghu's son, Rāma-enhancer of Kausaiya's joy-has said to you, 'Do you, O fell one, coming out, give me battle and prove your prowess.

sn: हन्तास्मि त्वां सहामात्यं सपुत्रज्ञातिबान्धवम्। निरुद्विग्नास्त्रयो लोका भविष्यन्ति हते त्वयि। ७९ ।।
en: I shall slay you together with your ministers, and with your sons and relations and friends. And you being slain, the three worlds shall attain peace.

sn: देवदानवयक्षापां गन्धर्वोरंगरक्षसाम्। शत्रुमद्योद्धरिष्यामि त्वामृषीणां च कण्टकम्॥
en: Today shall I destroy the enemy of the gods and Dänavas, and Yakşas, of the Gandharvas serpents and Rākṣasas, and the thorn (in the side of the Saints).

sn: विभीषणस्य चैश्वर्यं भविष्यति हते त्वयि। न चेत्सत्कृत्य वैदेही प्रणिपत्य प्रदास्यसि॥
en: On you being slain, all the wealth shall be Vibhisana's; unless, bowing down (to me) and paying me homage, you render back Maithilī.

sn: इत्येवं परुषं वाक्यं ब्रुवाणे हरिपुंगवे। अमर्षवशमापन्नो निशाचरगणेश्वरः।॥
en: When that monkey-chief had spoken thus, the lord of the night-rangers was wrought up with wrath.

sn: ततः स रोषमापन्नः शशास सचिवांस्तदा। गृह्यतामिति दुर्मेधा वध्यतामिति चासकृत्॥
en: And coming under the sway of passion, he commanded his counsellors, saying, "Take this one of perverse understanding, and slay him at once.”

sn: रावणस्य वचः श्रुत्वा दीप्ताग्निमिव तेजसा। जगृहुस्तं ततो घोराश्चत्वारो रजनीचराः।॥
en: Hearing Råvaņa's speech, four grim-visaged night rangers seized (Angada) flaming in energy like fire itself,

sn: ग्राहयामास तारेयः स्वयमात्मानमात्मवान्। बलं दर्शयितुं वीरो यातुधानगणे तदा॥
en: Tara's son suffered himself to be taken, in order that the hero might then display his prowess before the Yātudhānas.

sn: स तान्बाहुद्वयासक्तानादाय पतगानिव। प्रासादं शैलसंकाशमुत्पपाताङ्गदस्तदा॥
en: Then Angada, taking them up, who were pressed against his arms, like insects, leapt up on a palace resembling a hill.

sn: तस्योत्पतनवेगेन निधूतास्तत्र राक्षसाः। भूमौ निपतिताः सर्वे राक्षसेन्द्रस्य पश्यतः॥
en: Thereat, in consequence of the impetuosity of his bound, the Raksasas, slipping off, fell on to the ground in the very sight of the Rākṣasa king.

sn: ततः प्रासादशिखरं शैलशृङ्गमिवोन्नतम्। चक्राम राक्षसेन्द्रस्य वालिपुत्रः प्रतापवान्॥
en: Then the powerful son of Vāli with his legs attacked the top of that palace, elevated like a hill, of the lord of Rākşasas.

sn: पफाल च तदाक्रान्तं दशग्रीवस्य पश्यतः। पुरा हिमवतः शृङ्गं वज्रेणेव विदारितम्॥
en: Thereat, as formerly the summit of the Himavān had been cleft by the thunder bold, the palace, thus assailed, was split in the very presence of the Ten-necked one.

sn: भङ्क्त्वा प्रासादशिखरं नाम विश्राव्य चात्मनः। विनद्य सुमहनादमुत्पपात विहायसा॥
en: Having reft the top of the edifice, and proclaimed his name, Angada, setting up a mighty roar, sprang into the sky.

sn: व्यथयन्राक्षसान्सर्वान्हर्षयंश्चापि वानरान्। स वानराणां मध्ये तु रामपार्श्वमुपागतः॥
en: Aggrieving the Rākşasas and rejoicing all the monkeys, he came back to the side of Rāma in the midst of the monkeys.

sn: रावणस्तु परं चक्रे क्रोधं प्रासादधर्षणात्। विनाशं चात्मनः पश्यन्निःश्वासपरमोऽभवत्॥
en: Rāvana was transported with wrath in consequence of the breaking down of the palace. And, finding his destruction (at hand), he began to heave sighs.

sn: रामस्तु बहुभिहृष्टैर्विनदद्भिः प्लवंगमैः। वृतो रिपुवधाकाङ्क्षी युद्धायैवाभिवर्तत॥
en: Rāma, surrounded by innumerable delighted monkeys setting up shouts, anxious for slaying his foe, prepared for battle.

sn: सुषेणस्तु महावीर्यो गिरिकूटोपमो हरिः। बहुभिः संवृतस्तत्र वानरैः कामरूपिभिः॥ स तु द्वाराणि संयम्य सुग्रीववचनात्कपिः। पर्यक्रामत दुर्धर्षो नक्षत्राणीव चन्द्रमाः॥
en: At the command of Sugrīva, the exceedingly powerful monkey-Susena, resembling a mountain-summit, surrounded by a large number of monkeys capable of assuming shapes at pleasure, began to range from door to door; like the Moon ranging the stars.

sn: तेषामक्षौहिणिशतं समवेक्ष्य वनौकसाम्। लङ्कामुपनिविष्टानां सागरं चाभिवर्तताम्॥ राक्षसा विस्मयं जग्मुस्खासं जग्मुस्तथापरे। अपरे समरे हर्षाद्धर्षमेवोपपेदिरे।९७।।
en: Seeing the hundred Akşauhinis of the woodrangers, stationed in Lankā, extending down to the sea, some of the Rākşasas were struck with astonishment, while some came under the influence of fear; and some experienced delight from the (anticipated) delight of battle.

sn: कृत्स्नं हि कपिभिर्व्याप्तं प्राकारपरिखान्तरम्। ददृशू राक्षसा दीनाः प्राकारं वानरीकृतम्।। हाहाकारमकुर्वन्त राक्षसा भयमागताः॥
en: The space between the well and the moat all was flooded with monkeys. And the distressed Rākşasas saw the wall thronging with monkeys; and thereat exclaiming “Alas” “Alas,” the Rāks asa were extremely terrified. *A translator cannot help feeling of disappointment at the difference, to the disadvantage of English-between Sanskrit and English. The original for 'thronging with monkeys' is a verbal attributivevanarikrita-lit. monkeyed.

sn: तस्मिन् महाभीषणके प्रवृत्ते कोलाहले राक्षसराजयोधाः। प्रगृह्य रक्षांसि महायुधानि युगान्तवाता इव संविचेरुः॥
en: On that frightful uproar arising, the warriors of the Rākşasa monarch, Raksasa-seizing mighty arms, began to patrol about, like to winds blowing at the time to the universal dissolution. a

sn: ततस्ते राक्षसास्तत्र गत्वा रावणमन्दिरम्। न्यवेदयन्पुरीं रुद्धां रामेण सह वानरैः॥
en: Then those Rākşasas, going to that subduer of enemies, Rāvana, informed him that Rāma along with the monkeys had laid siege to the city.

sn: रुद्धां तु नगरी श्रुत्वा जातक्रोधो निशाचरः। विधानं द्विगुणं श्रुत्वा प्रासादं चाप्यरोहत॥
en: Hearing the city besieged, the night-ranger was enraged. And, hearing that double arrangements had been made (by Rāma) in guarding the gateways (Råvaņa) ascended the palace.

sn: स ददर्श वृतां लङ्कां सशैलवनकाननाम्। असंख्येयैर्हरिंगणैः सर्वतो युद्धकाटिभिः॥
en: He saw Lanka with her hills, woods, and forests, covered everywhere with innumerable monkeys eager for encounter.

sn: स दृष्ट्वा वानरैः सर्वैर्वसुधां कपिलीकृताम्। कथं क्षपयितव्याः स्युरिति चिन्तापरोऽभवत्॥
en: He saw the entire Earth tawneyed with the monkeys; and he reflected within himself how he could destroy these.

sn: स चिन्तयित्वा सुचिरं धैर्यमालम्ब्य रावणः। राघवं हरियूथांश्च ददर्शायतलोचनः॥
en: And reflecting for long, Rāvana having expansive eyes, Assuming patience, gazed at Rāghava and the leader of monkeys.

sn: राघवः सह सैन्येन मुदितो नाम पुप्लुवे। लङ्कां ददर्श गुप्तां वै सर्वतो राक्षसैर्वृताम्॥
en: Rāghava with his host was fast approaching (the wall); and Ravana saw Lanka defended on all sides by Rākşasas.

sn: दृष्ट्वा दाशरथिर्लङ्कां चित्रध्वजपताकिनीम्। जगाम मनसा सीतां दूयमानेन चेतसा॥
en: Dasaratha's son, seeing Lankā crowned with variegated ensigns and standards, mentally went to Sītā, with a sad heart.

sn: अत्र सा मृगशावाक्षी मत्कृते जनकात्मजा। पीड्यते शोकसंतप्ता कृशा स्थण्डिलशायिनी॥
en: For my sake, here that one. Janaka's daughter, having eyes resembling those of a young deer, is undergoing affliction; and Leith down on the ground.

sn: निपीड्यमानां धर्मात्मा वैदेहीमनुचिन्तयन्। क्षिप्रमाज्ञापयद्रामो वानरान्द्विषतां वधे॥
en: And aggrieved at the thought of Vaidehī; the righteous Rāma speedily commanded the monkeys to compass the destruction of the enemies.

sn: एवमुक्ते तु वचसि रामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा। संघर्षमाणाः प्लवगाः सिंहनादैरपूरयन्॥
en: As Rāma of untiring deeds said this, the monkeys, filling (The air) with leonine roars, began to press forward furiously.

sn: शिखरैर्विकिरामैतां लङ्कां मुष्टिभिरेव वा। इति स्म दधिरे सर्वे मनांसि हरियूथपाः॥
en: "We shall cleave Lankā with mountainpeaks, or with our blows" thus thought the leaders within themselves.

sn: उद्यम्य गिरिशृङ्गाणि महान्ति शिखराणि च। तरूंश्चोत्पाट्य विविधांस्तिष्ठन्ति हरियूथपाः॥
en: The monkey-leaders stood, raising up gigantic mountain peaks and tops of mountains, and rooting up various trees.

sn: प्रेक्षतो राक्षसेन्द्रस्य तान्यनीकानि भागशः। राघवप्रियकामार्थ लङ्कामारुरुहुस्तदा॥
en: And for doing what was dear to Rāma, that army, divided into separate parties, in the presence of the Raksasa chief commenced scaling Lanka.

sn: ते ताम्रवक्त्रा हेमाभा रामार्थे त्यक्तजीविताः। लङ्कामेवाभ्यवर्तन्त सालभूधरयोधिनः॥
en: Those copper-faced once of golden sheen, who had consecrated their lives to the service of Rāma, equipped with trees and rocks, began to throng upon Lankā.

sn: ते दुमैः पर्वतायैश्च मुष्टिभिश्च प्लवंगमाः। प्राकाराग्राण्यसंख्यानि ममन्थुस्तोरणानि च ॥ परिखान्पूरयन्तश्च प्रसनसलिलाशयान्। पांसुभिः पर्वतायैश्च तृणैः काष्ठैश्च वानराः॥
en: The monkeys with trees and hill-tops and blows crushed countless gates and tops of walls; and they filled the moat containing crystal water with dust, tops of crags, straw, and wood.

sn: ततः सहस्रयूथाश्च कोटियूथाश्च यूथपाः। कोटियूथशताश्चान्ये लङ्कामारुरुहुस्तदा॥
en: Then leader of thousands and koțis and hundreds of koțis began to scale Lanka.

sn: काञ्चनानि प्रमर्दन्तस्तोरणानि प्लवंगमाः। कैलासशिखराग्राणि गोपुराणि प्रमथ्य च॥ आप्लवन्तः प्लवन्तश्च गर्जन्तश्च प्लवंगमाः। लङ्कां तामभिधावन्ति महावारणसंनिभाः॥
en: The monkeys crushed golden gateways; and, breaking down gates resembling the tops of the summits of Kailasa, bounded roaring, some towards the wall and some all around. And resembling gigantic elephants, they rushed towards Lankā.

sn: जयत्युरुबलो रामो लक्ष्मणश्च महाबलः। राजा जयति सुग्रीवो राघवेणाभिपालितः॥ इत्येवं घोषयन्तश्च गर्जन्तश्च प्लवंगमाः। अभ्यधावन्त लङ्कायाः प्राकारं कामरूपिणः॥
en: Victory to the mighty Rāma, and victory to the exceedingly powerful Lakşmaņa, and Victory to king Sugriva, who is protected by Rāghava.' Thus shouting, those monkeys, wearing forms at will, sending up roars, rushed amain towards the wall of Lankā.

sn: वीरबाहुः सुबाहुश्च नलश्च पनसस्तथा। निपीड्योपनिविष्टास्ते प्राकारं हरियूथपाः।। एतस्मिन्नन्तरे चक्रुः स्कन्धावारनिवेशनम्॥
en: And Virabăhu, Subāhu, Nala and Panasaleader of monkeys-breaking (a portion of) the wall, took up their post there. In the meantime, (they) arranged the forces in order of battle.

sn: पूर्वद्वारं तु कुमुदः कोटिभिर्दशभिर्वृतः। आवृत्य बलवांस्तस्थौ हरिभिर्जितकाशिभिः॥
