en: The strong Kumuda, surrounded by ten kotis of victorious monkeys, stood obstruction the Estern gate.

sn: सहायार्थे तु तस्यैव निविष्टः प्रसभो हरिः। पनसश्च महाबाहुर्वानरैरभिसंवृतः॥
en: For backing him, there remained the monkey, Prasabha, as also the long-armed Panasa, surrounded by monkeys.

sn: दक्षिणद्वारमासाद्य वीरः शतबलिः कपिः। आवृत्य बलवांस्तस्थौ विंशत्या कोटिभिर्वृतः॥
en: And obstruction the Southern entrance stood the strong and gallant monkey, Śatabali surrounded by twenty koțis.

sn: सुषेण: पश्चिमद्वारं गत्वा तारापिता बली। आवृत्य बलवांस्तस्थौ कटिकोटिभिरावृतः॥
en: The strong sire of Tārā the powerful Sus ena, obstructed the Western gate, backed by kot is upon kotis (of monkeys).

sn: उत्तरद्वारमागम्य रामः सौमित्रिणा सह। आवृत्य बलवांस्तस्थौ सुग्रीवश्च हरीश्वरः॥
en: Obstructing the Northern gate, remained the puissant Răma himself along with Sumitrā's son, as well as the king of monkeys-Sugriva.

sn: गोलाङ्गुलो महाकायो गवाक्षो भीमदर्शनः। वृतः कोट्या महावीर्यस्तस्थौ रामस्य पार्श्वतः॥
en: That huge-bodied and dreadful Golangula-the mighty and powerful Gavākşa-surrounded by a koti, remained by the side of Rama.

sn: ऋक्षाणां भीमकोपानां धूम्रः शत्रुनिबर्हणः। वृतः कोट्या महावीर्यस्तस्थौ रामस्य पार्श्वतः॥ संनद्धस्तु महावीर्यो गदापाणिविभीषणः। वृतो यत्तैस्तु सचिवैस्तस्थौ यत्र महाबलः॥
en: That destroyer of foes-the exceedingly mighty Dhūmra of the bears of terrific wrath, remained by the side of Rāma-where, surrounded by vigilant counsellors, and bearing a mace in his hand stood the exceedingly strong Vibhīşana, endowed with wonderful powers, in complete panoply.

sn: गजो गवाक्षो गवयः शरभो गन्धमादनः। समन्तात्परिधावन्तो ररक्षुहरिवाहिनीम्॥
en: And Gaya, and Gavāksa, and Gavaya, and Śarabha, and Gandhamādana, protected the monkey-army, coursing all around.

sn: ततः कोपपरीतात्मा रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः। निर्याणं सर्वसैन्यानां द्रुतमाज्ञापयत्तदा॥
en: Then, his soul wrought up with wrath, Rāvaņa-lord of Rākşasas-speedily ordered the whole host to sally out.

sn: एतच्छ्रुत्वा तदा वाक्यं रावणस्य मुखेरितम्। सहसा भीमनिर्घोषमुद्धष्टं रजनीचरैः॥
en: Hearing those words, which came out from Ravana's mouth, all of a sudden the nightrangers sent up a dreadful yell.

sn: ततः प्रबोधिता भेर्यञ्चन्द्रपाण्डुरपुष्कराः। हेमकोणैरभिहता राक्षसानां समन्ततः॥
en: Then awoke the kettle-drums, having moonlike pale faces-sounded by means of golden sticks.

sn: विनेदुश्च महाघोषाः शङ्खाः शतसहस्रशः। राक्षसानां सुघोराणां मुखमारुतपूरिताः॥
en: And conchs by hundreds and by thousands, capable of producing loud blares, filled with air proceeding from the mouths of dreadful Rāks asas-were winded.

sn: ते बभुः शुकनीलाङ्गाः सशला रजनीचरः। विद्युन्मण्डलसंनद्धाः सबलाक इवाम्बुदाः॥
en: With conchs placed in their mouths, those night-rangers, having bodies blue like those of Śukas, resembled masses of clouds, with lightning and cranes.

sn: निष्पतन्ति ततः सैन्या हृष्टा रावणचोदिताः। समये पूर्यमाणस्य वेगा इव महोदधेः॥
en: And commanded by Råvana, the troops cheerfully issued forth like the onrushing of the mighty main filling all at the time of the universal dissolution.

sn: ततो वानरसैन्येन मुक्तो नादः समन्ततः। मलयः पूरितो येन ससानुप्रस्थकंदरः॥
en: Then the monkeys-army gave roar, spreading all around, and it seemed as if the sound filled all Malaya with its sides and caves.

sn: शङ्खदुन्दुभिनिर्घोषः सिंहनादस्तरस्विनाम्। पृथिवीं चान्तरिक्षं स सागरं चाभ्यनादयत्॥ गजानां बृंहितैः सार्धं हयानां हेषितैरपि। रथानां नेमिनिर्घोषै रक्षसां पदनिःस्वनैः॥
en: And sounds of conchs, and drums as well as the leonine shouts of the impetuous (warriors), made the earth, air, and ocean, resound: and these mixed with the roars of elephants, the neighing of steeds, the rattle of the car-wheels, ant the tread of the Rākşasa' feet.

sn: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे घोरः संग्रामः समपद्यत। रक्षसां वानराणां च यथा देवासुरे पुरा॥
en: In the meantime there commenced a mighty a encounter between the Raksasas and the monkey, like that which took place of yore between the gods and the Asuras.

sn: ते गदाभिः प्रदीप्ताभिः शक्तिशूलपरश्वधैः। निजघ्नुर्वानरान्सर्वान्कथयन्तः स्वविक्रमान्॥
en: And displaying their prowess, They* began to slaughter monkeys with maces, and darts, and adzes. *Raksasas.

sn: तथा वृक्षैर्महाकायाः पर्वताग्रेश्च वानराः। निजघ्नुस्तानि रक्षांसि नखैर्दन्तैश्च वेगिनः॥
en: The vehement monkeys (on their side) slaughtered Rākşasa with trees and tops of crags as well as with their nails and teeth.

sn: राजा जयति सुग्रीव इति शब्दो महानभूत्। राजञ्जयजयेत्युक्त्वा स्वस्वनामकथां ततः॥
en: A mighty sound arose of 'Victory to king Sugrīva!' and 'Victory to you, O king,' each army taking the name of its king.

sn: राक्षसास्त्वपरे भीमाः प्राकारस्था महीं गतान्। वानरान्भिन्दिपालैश्च शूलैश्चैव व्यदारयन् ॥
en: Then other dreadful Rākṣasa that were stationed upon the wall, dropping down, pierced the monkeys with darts and bhindipālas.

sn: वानराश्चापि संक्रुद्धाः प्राकारस्थान्महीं गताः। राक्षसान्पातयामासुः खमाप्लुत्य स्वबाहुभिः॥
en: And (thereat) the monkeys, flying into fury, descending to the earth and bounding, brought down the Rākşasas with their arms.

sn: स संप्रहारस्तुमुलो मांसशोणितकर्दमः। रक्षसां वानराणां च संबभूवाद्भुतोपमः।॥
en: That encounter of the Rākşasas and the monkeys was mighty and wonderful, and the ground became wet with flesh and gore.

sn: युध्यतां तु ततस्तेषां वानराणां महात्मनाम्। रक्षसां संबभूवाथ बलरोषः सुदारुणः॥
en: As the high-soulcd monkeys and Raksasas taught on, their wrath vastly increase at sight of each other's forces.

sn: ते हयैः काञ्चनापीडैर्गजैश्चाग्निशिखोपमैः। रथैश्चादित्यसंकाशैः कवचैश्च मनोरमैः॥ निर्ययू राक्षसा वीरा नादयन्तो दिशो दश। राक्षसा भीमकर्माणो रावणस्य जयैषिणः॥
en: And furnished with steeds in golden trappings, and elephants resembling flames of fire; and cars appearing like (so many) suns; and shining armour, the valiant Räkşasas issued, making the ten cardinal points resound. The Rākşasas of terrific exploits were burning for victory on behalf of Rāvana.

sn: वानराणामपि चमूवृंहति जयमिच्छताम्। अभ्यधावत तां सेनां रक्षसां घोरकर्मणाम्॥
en: The mighty monkey-army also, eager for victory, darted against the host of the Rākşasa of dreadful deeds.

sn: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे तेषामन्योन्यमभिधावताम्। रक्षसां वानराणां च द्वन्द्वयुद्धमवर्तत॥
en: In the meanwhile, as either party assailed the other, there took place single combats between the Raksasas and the monkeys.

sn: अङ्गदेनेन्द्रजित्सार्धं वालिपुत्रेण राक्षसः। अयुध्यत,महातेजास्त्र्यम्बकेण यथान्धकः॥
en: And as Andhaka had combated with the Three-eyed (deity), That Raksasas, the exceedingly energetic Indrajit, faught with Angada, Son to Vāli.

sn: प्रजङ्ग्रेन च संपातिनित्यं दुर्धर्षणो रणे। जम्बुमालिनामारब्धो हनूमानपि वानरः॥
en: Sampāti, hard to to bear, engaged with Prajangha; and the monkey, Hanumān, entered into conflict with Jambumālī.

sn: संगतस्तु महाक्रोधो राक्षसो रावणानुजः। समरे तीक्ष्णवेगेन शत्रुघ्नेन विभीषणः।८।।
en: And Ravana's younger brother, Vibhisana, fired with wrath, encountered Śatrughna, endowed with exceeding impetuosity.

sn: तपनेन गजः सार्धं राक्षसेन महाबलः। निकुम्भेन महातेजा नीलोऽपि समयुध्यत॥ वानरेन्द्रस्तु सुग्रीवः प्रघसेन सुसंगतः। संगतः समरे श्रीमान्विरूपाक्षेण लक्ष्मणः॥
en: The highly powerful Nīla engaged with undertook Praghasa, and the graceful Lakşmaņa was engaged with Virüpākşa.

sn: अग्निकेतुः सुदुर्धर्षो रश्मिकेतुश्च राक्षसः। मित्रघ्नो यज्ञकोपश्च रामेण सह संगताः॥
en: The exceedingly irrepressible Agniketu and the Raksasa Rasmiketu-and Mitraghna and Yajñakopa, were engaged with Rāma.

sn: वज्रमुष्टिश्च मैन्देन द्विविदेनाशनिप्रभः। राक्षसाभ्यां सुघोराभ्यां कपिमुख्यौ समागतौ ।।१२ वीरः प्रतपनो घोरो राक्षसो रणदुर्धरः। समरे तीक्ष्णवेगेन नलेन समयुध्यत॥ धर्मस्य पुत्रो बलवान्सुषेण इति विश्रुतः। स विद्युन्मालिना सार्धमयुध्यत महाकपिः॥
en: Vajramuștti encountered Mainda, and Asaniprabha Dvivida. And those foremost of monkeys faught with those dreadful Rākşasas, the heroic and terrible Pratapana, incapable of being overcome in battle, was combating with Nala of terrific force; and that lusty son of Righteousness, well-known as Susena, a mighty monkey-battled with Vidyunmāli.

sn: वानराश्चापरे घोरा राक्षसैरपरैः सह। द्वन्द्वं समीयुः सहसा युद्ध्वा च बहुभिः सह ॥
en: And other fearful monkeys encountered other Rākşasas; and many were the encounters the took place.

sn: तत्रासीत्सुमहद्युद्धं तुमुलं रोमहर्षणम्। रक्षसां वानराणां च वीराणां जयमिच्छताम्॥
en: And great and fierce was the engagement that took place between the heroic Rakşasas and monkeys burning for victory, capable of making people's hair stand on end.

sn: हरिराक्षसदेहेभ्यः : प्रसृताः केशशाद्वला:। शरीरसंघाटवहाः प्रसुनुः शोणितापगाः॥
en: And from the persons of the Räkşasas and the monkeys there flowed a river of gore, having hair for grass (growing on its banks) and the bodies of the warriors for pieces of planks floating (a down the current).

sn: आजघानेन्द्रजित्क्रुद्धो वज्रेणेव शतक्रतुः। अङ्गदं गदया वीरं शत्रुसैन्यविदारणम्॥
en: Indrajit, growing enraged, with his mace dealt a blow at that tearer of hostile ranks, angada, like him of an hundred sacrifices striking with his · thunderbolt.

sn: तस्य काश्चनचित्राङ्गं रथं साश्वं ससारथिम्। जघान गदया श्रीमानङ्गदो वेगवान्हरिः॥
en: Thereat, that graceful monkey, Angada, gifted with vehemence, with his mace crushed his car decked in gold, together with the steeds and the charioteer.

sn: संपातिस्तु प्रजङ्ग्रेन त्रिभिर्बाणैः समाहतः। निजघानाश्वकर्णेन प्रजङ्घ रणमूर्धनि ॥
en: Sampāti was pierced with three arrows by Prajangha; and the former (in his turn) slew Prajangha on the edge of battle with an Ašvakarņa.

sn: जम्बुमाली रथस्थस्तु रथशक्त्या महाबलः। बिभेद समरे क्रद्धो हनूमन्तं स्तनान्तरे॥
en: And Jambumali, mounted on a car, possessed of prodigious strength, fired with wrath, with all the access of force derived from his car wounded Hanumān between his paps.

sn: तस्य तं रथमास्थाय हनूमान्मारुतात्मजः। प्रममाथ तलेनाशु सह तेनैव रक्षसा॥
en: Thereat, getting at his car, Hanumān-son to the Wind-god with a slap speedily crushed his adversary's vehicle along with the Raksasa.

sn: नदन्प्रतपनो घोरो नलं सोऽभ्यनुधावत। नलः प्रपनस्याशु पातयामास चक्षुषी॥ भिन्नगात्रः शरैस्तीक्ष्णैः क्षिप्रहस्तेन रक्षसा।
en: Then the terrific Pratapana, roaring, rushed at Nala; and thereat Nala, with his body pierced with sharp shafts by that swift handed Rākşasa, plucked out Pratapana's eyes, and cast them to the earth.

sn: ग्रसन्तमिव सैन्यानि प्रघसं वानराधिपः॥ सुग्रीवः सप्तपर्णेन निजघान जवेन च।
en: That lord of monkeys, Sugrīva, with a Saptaparma-swiftly slew Praghasa, who appeared to be devouring up the troops.

sn: प्रपीड्य शरवर्षेण राक्षसं भीमदर्शनम्॥ निजघान विरूपाक्षं शरेणैकेन लक्ष्मणः।
en: Tormenting the Räkşasa Virupākṣa of dreadful form, Laksmana killed him with a single arrow.

sn: अग्निकेतुश्च दुर्धर्षो रश्मिकेतुश्च राक्षसः।। मित्रघ्नो यज्ञकोपश्च राममादीपयच्छरैः।२६।।
en: The irrepressible Agniketu, the Rākṣasas Raśmiketu, Mitraghna and Yajñakopa, with their arrows rendered Rāma aflame.

sn: तेषां चतुर्णा रामस्तु शिरांसि समरे शरैः। क्रुद्धश्चतुर्भिश्चिच्छेद घोरैरग्निशिखोपमैः॥
en: Thereat, Rāma, growing wroth, in battle severed the heads of those four by means of four shafts, dreadful, and resembling the tongues of a fame.

sn: वज्रमुष्टिस्तु मैन्देन मुष्टिना निहतो रणे। पपात सरथः साश्वः सुराट्ट इव भूतले॥
en: Vajramuști was slain in conflict by Mainda with a clenched fist; and down came he to the ground along with his car and horses, like a turret toppling (headlong.)

sn: निकुम्भस्तु रणे नीलं नीलाञ्जनचयप्रभम्। निर्बिभेद शरैस्तीक्ष्णैः करैर्मेधमिवांशुमान्॥
en: Nikumbha in fight wounded Nila resembling a mass of blue collyrium, with sharpened shafts, as the Sun pierce clouds with his rays.

sn: पुनः शरशतेनाथ क्षिप्रहस्तो निशाचरः। बिभेद समरे नीलं निकुम्भः प्रजहास च॥
en: Again with an hundred arrows, that lighthanded night-ranger pierced Nīla in the field; and Nikumbha laughed thereat.

sn: तस्यैव रथचक्रेण नीलो विष्णुरिवाहवे। शिरश्चिच्छेद समरे निकुम्भस्य च सारथेः॥
en: At this, even as Visnu did in battle, Nila with a wheel of his car, cut off in conflict Nikumbha's head together with that of his charioteer.

sn: वज्राशनिसमस्पर्शी द्विविदश्च समप्रभम्। जधान गिरिशृङ्गेण मिषतां सर्वरक्षसाम्॥
en: Dvivida, possessed of the touch of the Vajra and thunder bolt, in the presence of the entire Rākşasas host hurled a mountain-peak at him that was endowed with the splendour of the thunder bolt.

sn: द्विविदं वानरेन्द्रं तं दुमयोधिनमाहवे। शरैरशनिसंकाशैः स विव्याधाशनिप्रभः॥
en: Asaniprabha in encounter pierced that foremost of monkeys bearer of trees in conflict, Dvivida, with shafts resembling thunder-bolts.

sn: स शरैरभिविद्धाङ्गो द्विविदः क्रोधमूर्च्छितः। सालेन सरथं साश्वं निजघानाशनिप्रभम्॥
en: Thereat, beside himself with wrath, with his entire body wounded with arrows, Dvivida with a sala destroyed Asaniprabha along with his car and horses.

sn: विद्युन्माली रथस्थस्तु शरैः काञ्चनभूषणैः। सुषेणं ताडयामास ननाद च मुहुर्मुहुः॥
en: And Vidyanmālī, mounted on a car, assailed Suşeņa with shafts decked with gold, and behan to shout momentarily.

sn: तं रथस्थमथो दृष्ट्वा सुषेणो वानरोत्तमः गिरिशृङ्गेण महता रथमाशु न्यपातयत्॥
en: Seeing him mounted on his car, Suşena-best of monkeys-taking up a huge crag, swiftly brought his car down to the ground.

sn: लाघवेन तु संयुक्तो विद्युन्माली निशाचरः। अपक्रम्य रथातूर्णं गदापाणिः क्षितौ स्थितः॥
en: Thereat, endowed with lightness, that nightranger, Vidyunmāli, at once extricating himself from his car, stood on the ground with a mace in his hand.

sn: ततः क्रोधसमाविष्टः सुषेणो हरिपुंगवः। शिलां सुमहतीं गृह्य निशाचरमभिद्रवत्॥
en: Thereupon that foremost of monkeys, Sușeņa, growing furious, taking up a gigantic crag, rushed at the night-ranger.

sn: तमापतन्तं गदया विद्युन्माली निशाचरः। वक्षस्यभिजधानाशु सुषेणं हरिपुङ्गवम्॥
en: As he was descending, the night-ranger, Vidyunmālī, with his mace swiftly hit at the breast of Susena-greatest of monkeys.

sn: गदाप्रहारं तं घोरमचिन्त्य प्लवगोत्तमः। तां तूष्णीं पातयामास तस्योरसि महामृधे।।४०१
en: Thereat, without thinking at all of the terrific hit of the mace, that best of monkeys in mighty conflict brought down that upon his head.

sn: शिलाप्रहाराभिहतो विद्युन्माली निशाचरः। निष्पिष्टहृदयो भूमौ गतासुर्निपपात ह॥
en: Assailed with the crag, the night-ranger Vidyanmali, having his chest crushed, fell down to the earth, deprived of life.

sn: एवं तैर्वानरैः शूरैः शूरास्ते रजनीचराः। द्वन्द्वे विमथितास्तत्र दैत्या इव दिवौकसैः।॥
en: Like the celestials warring against the Daityas, the heroic monkeys warred on and confounded the valiant rangers of the night.

sn: भल्लैश्चान्यैर्गदाभिश्च शक्तितोमरसायकैः। अपविद्धैश्चापि रथैस्तथा साङ्ग्रामिकैहयैः।॥ निहतैः कुञ्जरैर्मतैस्तथा वानरराक्षसैः। चक्राक्षयुगदण्डैश्च भग्नैर्धरणिसंश्रितैः।॥ बभूवायोधनं घोरं गोमायुगणसेवितम्। कबन्धानि समुत्येतुर्दिक्षु वानररक्षसाम्।। विमर्दे तुमुले तस्मिन्देवासुररणोपमे॥
en: And frightful was the field of battle, with darts, and other arms; and clubs, and javelins, and lances, and other weapons, and with broken cars, and war-horses, and mad horses slain, and monkeys and Rākşasas, and wheels and Akşas, and yokes and standards, broken and scattered over the ground; and swarms of jackals began to range on all sides of the monkeys and the Raksasas; and Kabandhas began to rise in that terrific encounter, resembling the encounter of the gods and the Asuras.

sn: निहन्यमाना हरिपुंगवैस्तदा निशाचराः शोणितगन्धमूर्च्छिताः। पुनः सुयुद्धं तरसा समाश्रिता दिवाकरस्यास्तमयाभिकामिणः॥
en: Thus destroyed by the foremost of monkeys, the rangers of night, beyond themselves with the smell of blood, eagerly wishing for the setting of the Sun, again made active preparation for a renewal of the fight.

sn: युध्यतामेव तेषां तु तदा वानररक्षसाम्। रविरस्तं गतो रात्रिः प्रवृत्ता प्राणहारिणी॥
en: As the monkeys and the Rākşasas thus faught on, the sun set, ant the fatal Night came.

sn: अन्योन्यं बद्धवैराणां घोराणां जयमिच्छताम्। संप्रवृत्तं निशायुद्धं तदा वानररक्षसाम्॥
en: Then commenced a night-engagement between the dreadful Rākşasas and the monkeys of fixed hostility, each party burning for victory.

sn: राक्षसोऽसीति हरयो वानरोऽसीति राक्षसाः। अन्योन्यं समरे जघ्नुस्तस्मिंस्तमसि दारुणे॥
en: In that profound darkness, the monkeys and the Rākşasas began to slay each other, exclaiming, You are a Raksasa,' and 'you are a monkey.'

sn: हत दारय चैहीति कथं विद्रवसीति च। एवं सुतुमुलः शब्दस्तस्मिन्सैन्ये तु शुश्रुवे॥
en: And in that army there was heard a mighty uproar of 'slain,' 'rive!" 'come!' 'why fliest?'

sn: कालाः काञ्चनसंनाहास्तरिमम्मरसि राक्षसाः। संप्रदृश्यन्त शैलेन्द्रा दीप्तौषधिवना इव ॥
en: And, dark-hued, the Raksasas, equipped in golden mail, in that deep darkness appeared like elevated hills clad with woods of flaming incdicinal herbs.

sn: तस्मिंस्तमसि दुष्पारे राक्षसाः क्रोधमूच्छिताः। परिपेतुर्महावेगा भक्षयन्ता प्लवंगमान्॥
en: And in that limitless gloom, the Rākṣasas, transported with wrath, advanced with impetuous speed, devouring monkeys.

sn: ते हयान्काञ्चनापीडान्ध्वजश्चिशीविषोपमान्। आप्लुत्य दशनैस्तीक्ष्णैर्भीमकोपा व्यदारयन्॥
en: And, fired with terrible wrath, they, bounding up, with their sharp tecih tore up steeds caparisoned in gold, and standards resembling venomous serpents. *i.e. the monkeys, as appears from the context.

sn: वानरा बलिनो युद्धेऽक्षोभयनराक्षसी चमूम्। कुञ्जरान्कुञ्जरारोहान्पताकाध्वजिनो रथात्॥ चकर्षुश्च ददंशुश्च दशनैः क्रोधमूर्च्छिताः।
en: The lusty monkeys in battle agitated the Rāks asa host, and, waxing furious, with their teeth pulled and bit elephants and the riders there of, and cars furnished with flags and standards.

sn: लक्ष्मणश्चापि रामश्च शरैराशीविषोपमैः।।।। दृश्यादृश्यानि रक्षांसि प्रवराणि निजघ्नतुः।
en: Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa with shafts resembling venomous serpents, slaughtered the foremost among the Rakşasas-both those that were seen and those that were not.

sn: तुरंगखुरविध्वस्तं रथनेमिसमुत्थितम्॥ रुरोध कर्णनेत्राणि युध्यतां धरणीरजः।
en: The dust of the earth arising from warring combatants, and from the hoofs of horses and the wheels of cars, choked up eye and ear.

sn: वर्तमाने तथा घोरे सङ्ग्रामे लोमहर्षणे।। रुधिरौघा महाघोरा नद्यस्तत्र विसुनुवुः॥
en: And as the mighty envounter, capable of making people's hair stand on end, went on, there flowed a fearful river of gore.

sn: ततो भेरीमृदङ्गानां पणवानां च निःस्वनः। शङ्खनेमिस्वनोन्मिश्रः संबभूवाद्भुतोपमः॥
en: The sounds of kettle-drums and Mşdangas and Panavas, mingled with those of conchs and carwheels, were wonderful (to hear).

sn: हयानां स्तनमानानां राक्षसानां च नि:स्वनः। शस्तानां वानराणां च संबभूवात्र दारुणः॥
en: The sounds of steeds neighing, and Rāks asas (roaring) and monkeys, rejoicing, were something tremendous.

sn: हतैर्वानरमुख्यैश्च शक्तिशूलपरश्वधैः। निहतैः पर्वताकारै राक्षसैः कारूपिभिः॥ शस्त्रपुष्पोपहारा च तवासीधुद्धमेदिनी। दुर्जेया दुर्निवेशा च शोणितास्रावकर्दमा॥
en: And, with able monkeys slain; and darts and javelins and axes; and slaughtered Raksasa wearing forms at pleasure, lying mountain likethe field of battle, seeming to have offerings of arms representing flowers, became difficult to recognise, and inaccessible; and the earth was drenched with streams of blood.

sn: सा बभूव निशा घोरा हरिराक्षसहारिणी। कालरात्रीव भूतानां सर्वेषां दुरतिक्रमा॥
en: That Night, destructive to monkeys and Rākş asas, was dreadful, and difficult of being outsped by all, like to the Fatal Night of beings.

sn: ततस्ते राक्षसास्तत्र तस्मिंस्तमसि दारुणे। राममेवाभ्यवर्तन्त संहृष्टाः शरवृष्टिभिः॥
en: And in that attacked Rama with a shower of shafts.

sn: तेषामापततां शब्दः कुद्धानामपि गर्जताम्। उद्वर्त इव सत्त्वानां समुद्राणामभूत्स्वनः॥
en: The roars of those beings as they advanced, sending up shouts in anger, resembled the dashing of the Ocean at the time of the universal dissolution.

sn: तेषां रामः शरैः षड्भिः षड् जघान निशाचरान्। निमेषान्तरमात्रेण शरैरग्निशिखोपमैः॥ यज्ञशत्रुश्च दुर्धर्षो महापार्श्वमहोदरौ। वज्रदंष्ट्रो महाकायस्तौ चोभौ शुकसारणौ॥
en: In the twinkling of an eye, Räma by means of six shafts resembling tongues of flames, struck six of the night-rangers, viz., Yajñaśatru, irrepressible (in fight), and Mahaparsva, and Mahodara, and the huge bodied Vajradanstra, and those two-Suka and Sarana.

sn: ते तु रामेण बाणौधैः सर्वमर्मसु ताडिताः। युद्धादपसृतास्तत्र सावशेषायुषोऽभवन् ॥
en: And, pierced in their vitals with Rama's shafts, they, having only their lives left to them, disappeared from the field.

sn: निमेषान्तरमात्रेण घोरैरग्निशिखोपमैः। दिशश्चकार विमलाः प्रदिशश्च महारथः॥ ये त्वन्ये राक्षसा वीरा रामस्याभिमुखे स्थिताः। तेऽपि नष्टाः समासाद्य पतङ्गा इव पावकम्॥
en: Then in the twinkling of an eye, that Mahāratha rendered all sides clear (of all gloom) by means of arrows resembling tongues of fire; and those other heroic Raksasas that were in front of Rāma, were destroyed on approaching the place, like insects approaching a fire.

sn: सुवर्णपुङ्खैर्विशिखैः संपतद्भिः समन्ततः। बभूव रजनी चित्रा खद्योतैरिव शारदी॥
en: And with shafts plated with gold lying in all directions the night resembled one in autumn decked with fire-flies.

sn: राक्षसानां च निनदैर्भेरीणां चैव निःस्वनैः। सा बभूव निशा घोरा भूयो घोरतराभवत्॥
en: And in consequence of the uproar occasioned by the Rakşasas, and the sounds of drums, that night, already dreadful (in itself), became all the more so,

sn: तेन शब्देन महता प्रवृद्धेन समन्ततः। त्रिकूटः कन्दरः कीर्णः प्रव्याहरदिवाचलः॥
en: On that sound attaining dimensions on all sides, it seemed as if the mount Trikuta, containing numerous caverns, had been speaking.

sn: गोलाङ्गूला महाकायास्तमसा तुल्यवर्चसः। संपरिष्वज्य बाहुभ्यां भक्षयन्रजनीचरान्॥
en: And huge-bodied Golangulas of equal lustre with darkness itself binding fast the nightrangers with their arms, began to swallow them up.

sn: अङ्गदस्तु रणे शत्रूत्रिहन्तुं समुपस्थितः। रावणिं निजघानाशु सारथिं च हयानपि। वर्तमाने तदा घोरे संग्रामे भृशदारुणे।। इन्द्रजित्तु रथं त्यक्त्वा हताश्वो हतसारथिः। अङ्गदेन महायस्तस्तत्रैवान्तरधीयत॥
en: And Angada was present in the encounter, for slaying foes. And Indrajit, fairing sadly at the hands of Angada, abandoning his vehicle, and having his horses as well as his charioteer slain, vanished then and there.

sn: तत्कर्म वालिपुत्रस्य सर्वे देवाः सहर्षिभिः। तुष्टवुः पूजनार्हस्य तौ चोभौ रामलक्ष्मणौ॥
en: That feat of Väli's son, worthy of being honoured, all the celestials with the saints and both Rāma and Lakşmaņa lauded to the height.

sn: प्रभावं सर्वभूतानि विदुरिन्द्रजितो युधि। ततस्तेन महात्मानं दृष्ट्वा तुष्टाः प्रधर्षितम्॥
en: All beings were acquainted with the might of Indrajit in battle; and, therefore, witnessing his discomfiture, and seeing that high-souled one, they refoiced exceedingly.

sn: ततः प्रहृष्टाः कपयः ससुग्रीवविभीषणाः। साधुसाध्विति नेदुश्च दृष्ट्वा शत्रु पराजितम्॥
en: Seeing the enemy vanquished, all the .monkeys with Sugrīva and Vibhisana, experiencing high delight, exclaimed, "Excellent !" "Excellent!"

sn: इन्द्रजित्तु तदानेन निर्जितो भीमकर्मणा। संयुगे वालिपुत्रेण क्रोधं चक्रे सुदारुणम्॥
en: In the battle field beaten by Valr's son , of dreadful deeds, Indrajit was fired with a mighty wrath.

sn: सोऽन्तर्धानगतः पापो रावणी रणकर्शितः। ब्रह्मदत्तवरो वीरो रावणिः क्रोधमूर्च्छितः॥ अदृश्यो निशितान्बाणान्मुमोचाशनिवर्चसः।
en: And, being handled hard in battle, and having vanished from the field, the heroic and wicked son to Răvana, who had received a boon from Brahmä, transported with passion, remaining invisible, began to discharge sharpened shafts of the splendour of the thunder-bolt.

sn: रामं च लक्ष्मणं चैव घोरैनागमयैः शरैः॥ बिभेद समरे क्रुद्धः सर्वगात्रेषु राघवौ।
en: And worked up into rage, he in the conflict pierced Raghu's sons, Rāma and Lakşmaņa all over their bodies, with terrific arrows consisting of serpents.

sn: मायया संवृतस्तत्र मोहयराघवौ युधि॥ अदृश्यः सर्वभूतानां कूटयोधी निशाचरः। बबन्ध शरबन्धेन भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ॥
en: And himself engirt with illusion, that nightranger, given to fighting in crooked ways, remaining invisible to all creatures, stupefied the descendants of Raghu in battle; and by means of his shafts bound the brothers, Rāma and Laksmana.

sn: तौ तेन पुरुषव्याघ्रौ क्रुद्धनाशीविषैः शरैः। सहसाभिहतौ वीरौ तदा प्रेक्षन्त वानराः ॥
en: Then in the sight of the monkeys, those heroes and foremost of men were suddenly overpowered with shafts by the enraged (Indrajit).

sn: प्रकाशरूपस्तु यदा न शक्तस्तौ बाधितुं राक्षराजपुत्रः। मायां प्रयोक्तुं समुपाजगाम बबन्ध तौ राजसुतौ दुरात्मा॥
en: And when the son of the Rākşasa monarch felt himself incompetent to cope with them openly, then that impious one, resorting to illusion, bound those princes (by that means).

sn: स तस्य गतिमन्विच्छन्राजपुत्रः प्रतापवान्। दिदेशातिबलो रामो दश वानरयूथपान्॥
en: Then, anxious to ascertain his* course, the king's son possessed of prowess, and endowed with exceeding strength, Rāma, ordered ten of the monkey-leaders. * Indrajit's.

sn: द्वौ सुषेणस्य दायादौ नीलं च प्लवगाधिपम्। अङ्गदं वालिपुत्रं च शरभं च तरस्विनम् ॥ द्विविदं च हनूमन्तं सानुप्रस्थं महाबलम्। ऋषभं चर्षभस्कन्धमादिदेश परन्तपः॥
en: The repressor of foes ordered Väli's sonAngada, the vigorous Śarabha, Dvivida, Hanumān, the mighty Sānuprastha, Rşabha and Rşabhaskandha.

sn: ते संप्रहृष्टा हरयो भीमानुद्यम्य पादपान्। आकाशं विविशुः सर्वे मार्गमाणा दिशो दश॥
en: Thereat with alacrity those monkeys, wielding mighty trees, shot up into the sky, and began to scour the ten cardinal points.

sn: तेषां वेगवतां वेगमिषुभिर्वेगवत्तरैः। अस्त्रवित्परमात्रेण वारयामास रावणिः॥
en: And Ravana's son, skilled in arms, resisted the impetuous march of those vehement ones by means of a powerful weapon as well as arms more forceful (than the force of their rush).

sn: तं भीमवेगा हरयो नाराचैः क्षतविक्षताः। अन्धकारे न ददृशुर्मेधैः सूर्यमिवावृतम्॥
en: The exceedingly vehement monkeys, cut and mangled with Nărăcas, saw him in the dark like the sun enveloped in clouds.

sn: रामलक्ष्मणयोरेव सर्वदेहभिदः शरान्। भृशमावेशयामास रावणिः समितिंजयः॥
en: That conqueror in battle, Ravana's son, with shafts sorely pierced the persons of Rāma and Laksmana.

sn: निरन्तरशरीरौ तु तावुभौ रामलक्ष्मणौ। क्रुद्धनेन्द्रजिता वीरौ पन्नगैः शरतां गतः॥
en: And both Rāma and Lakşmaņa had their bodies entirely covered by the angry Indrajit with shafts turned into serpents.

sn: तयोः क्षतजमार्गेण सुस्राव रुधिरं बहु। तावुभौ च प्रकाशेते पुष्यिताविव किंशुकौ॥
en: And from their wounds blood began to gush out in streams; and they looked like flowercrowned Kinsukas.

sn: ततः पर्यन्तरक्ताक्षो भिन्नाञ्जनचयोपमः। रावणिर्धातरौ वाक्यमन्तर्धानगतोऽब्रवीत्॥
en: Then that one having red corners to his eyes and resembling a mass of crushed collyrium, Rāvana's son, said to the brothers, as he vanished.

sn: युध्यमानमनालक्ष्यं शक्रोऽपि विदशेश्वरः। द्रष्टुमासादितुं वापि न शक्तः किं पुनर्युवाम्॥
en: When I fight remaining invisible, even Sakrathe lord of the celestials-cannot see or approach me, and who are you?

sn: प्रापिताविषुजालेन राघवौ कङ्कपत्रिणा। एष रोषपरीतात्मा नयामि यमसादनम्॥
en: And I, with my soul surcharged with wrath, shall, assailing them with showers of weapons furnished with Karka feathers, send Raghu's sons to the abode of Yama."

sn: एवमुक्त्वा तु धर्मज्ञौ भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ। निर्बिभेद शितैर्बाणैः प्रजहर्ष ननाद च॥
en: Having spoken thus to the brothers-Rāma and Laksmana, cognizant of righteousness-(Indrajit)pierced them with sharpened shafts, and shouted in joy.

sn: भिन्नाञ्जनचयश्यामो विस्फार्य विपुलं धनुः। भूय एव शरान्धोरान्विससर्ज महामृधे॥
en: And stretching his large bow, that one sable like to a mass of crushed collyrium again discharged terrific shafts in battle.

sn: ततो मर्मसु मर्मज्ञो मज्जयनिशिताशरान्। रामलक्ष्मणयोर्वीरो ननाद च मुहुर्मुहुः॥
en: That one versed in the inner sense of things, with whetted arrows pierced the vitals of Rāma and Lakşmaņa and shouted momentarily.

sn: बद्धौ तु शरबन्धेन तावुभौ रणमूर्धनि। निमेषान्तरमात्रेण न शेकतुरवेक्षितुम्॥
en: And fast bound by the shackles of shafts on the edge of battle, they* could not attain respite for a moment, *i.e. Rama and Laksmana.

sn: ततो विभिन्नसर्वाङ्गौ शरशल्याचितौ कृतौ। ध्वजाविव महेन्द्रस्य रज्जुमुक्तौ प्रकम्पितौ ॥ तौ संप्रबलितौ वीरौ मर्मभेदेन कर्शितौ। निपेततुर्महेष्वासौ जगत्यां जगतीपती॥
en: Then with their persons pierced with shafts and darts, and resembling the flags of the Great Indra let loose from the cords and trembling (in the air), and with their bodies bristling with arrows, those heroes and mighty bowmen-lords of the earth-tormented in consequence of their vitals having been pierced, dropped down to the earth.

sn: तौ वीरशयने वीरौ शयानौ रुधिरोक्षितौ। शरवेष्टितसर्वाङ्गावातौं परमपीडितौ॥
en: Those heroes, bathed in blood and their persons covered with arrows-pained and suffering terribly, lay down as became heroes.

sn: नह्यविद्धं तयोर्गाने बभूवाङ्गुलमन्तरम्। नानिविण्णं न चाध्वस्तमाकराग्रादजिह्मगैः॥
en: There was not so much room unpierced in their persons as could be measured by a finger; and they were wounded with arrows up to the fore-parts of their hands.

sn: तौ तु क्रूरेण निहतौ रक्षसा कामरूपिणा। असृक्सुनुवतुस्तीवं जलं प्रस्रवणाविव ॥
en: They being wounded by that fell one capable of assuming shapes at will, blood violently gushed out of their bodies like water from a spring.

sn: पपात प्रथमं रामो विद्धो मर्मसु मार्गणैः। क्रोधादिन्द्रजिता येन पुरा शक्रो विनिर्जितः॥ रुक्मपुङ्खैः प्रसन्नात्रै रजोगतिभिराशुगैः। नाराचैरर्धनाराचैर्भल्लैरञ्जलिकैरपि।। विव्याध वत्सदन्तैश्च सिंहदंष्ट्रैः क्षुरैस्तथा॥ स वीरशयने शिश्येऽविज्यमाविध्य कार्मुकम्। भिन्नमुष्टिपरीणाहं त्रिनतं रुक्मभूषितम्॥
en: Rāma fell first, pierced in the vitals with the shafts. And the same Indrajit who had formerly wrathfully routed Śakra, (now) pierced (Rāma) with Närācas knotted with fold, and having polished heads; swift-speeding; and resembling dust carried about by the wind; and halfNārācas; and darts resembling anjalis;' and Vatsadantas; and simhadamstras; and razors; and, resigning his stringless bow decked in gold and curved in three places, with its part for grasping shattered-he lay down like a hero. 1. The hands joined at the lower sides, with the palms hollowed. 2. Weapons resembling the teeth of a calf. 3. Weapons resembling the lion's teeth. 4. Rāma.

sn: बाणपातान्तरे रामं पातितं पुरुषर्षभम्। स तत्र लक्ष्मणो दृष्ट्वा निराशो जीवितेऽभवत्॥
en: Seeing Rāma, the foremost of men-down within arrow-range, Laksmana despaired of his life.

sn: रामं कमलपत्राक्षं शरण्यं रणतोषिणम्। शुशोच भ्रातरं दृष्ट्वा पतितं धरणीतले॥
en: Seeing his brother, Rāma having eyes resembling lotus petals and ever delighting in battle, himself the refuge of others, lying down in the field; (Laksmana) began to weep.

sn: हरयश्चापि तं दृष्ट्वा संतापं परमं गताः। शोकाश्चिकुशुधैरमश्रुपूरितलोचनाः॥
en: The monkeys also seeing him, were plunged in sorrow; and they, their eyes flooded with tears, began to cry in grief of heart.

sn: बद्धौ त तौ वीरशये शयानौ ते वानराः संपरिवार्य तस्थुः। समागता वायुसुतप्रमुख्या विषादमार्ताः परमं च जग्मुः॥
en: When they had been bound and had laid themselves down as become heroes, the monkeys stood around them-and, conversing with one another, they, headed by the son of the Wing, were seized with extreme sorrow.

sn: ततो द्यां पृथिवीं चैव वीक्षमाणा वनौकसः। ददृशुः संततौ बाणैर्धातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ॥
en: The rangers of woods, gazing at the earth and the sky, at length cast their eyes on the brothersRāma and Lakşmaņa covered all over with arrows. And after that Rākşasa had gone away having performed his work, like the God* going away, after having showered, there came to that place Vibhīşaņa with sugrīva. *Indra.

sn: वृष्ट्वेवोपरते देवे कृतकर्मणि राक्षसे। आजगामाथ तं देशं ससुग्रीवो विभीषणः॥ नीलश्च द्विविदो मैन्दः सुषेणः कुमुदोऽङ्गदः। तूर्णं हनुमता सार्धमन्वशोचन्त राघवौ॥
en: And mourning Raghu's sons, there also came in all haste Nila and Dvivida and Mainda and Sușeņa and Kumuda and Angada in company with Hanuman.

sn: अचेष्टौ मन्दनिःश्वासौ शोणितेन परिप्लुतौ। शरजालाचितौ स्तब्धौ शयानौ शरतल्पगौ॥
en: And moveless; breathing covered with bloodpierced all over with net-works of shafts; dumb; they* were lying on the field. *Rama and Laksmana.

sn: निःश्वसन्तौ यथा सौ निश्चेष्टौ दीनविक्रमौ। रुधिरस्रावदिग्धाङ्गौ तपनीयाविव ध्वजौ॥
en: They were sighing like serpents; and were inert; and deprived of prowess; and washed in blood; and looking like to golden standards.

sn: तौ वीरशयने वीरौ शयानौ मन्दचेष्टितौ। यूथपैः स्वैः परिवृतौ वाष्पव्याकुललोचनैः॥
en: And as they lay moveless, as become heroes, the leaders of monkeys environed them with tear-charged eyes.

sn: राघवौ पतितौ दृष्ट्वा शरजालसमन्वितौ। बभूवुर्व्यथिताः सर्वे वानराः सविभीषणाः।७॥
en: Seeing the sons of Raghu lying, covered with showers of shafts, the monkeys, with Vibhisana, were pained (exceedingly).

sn: अन्तरिक्षं निरीक्षन्तो दिशः सर्वाश्च वानराः। न चैनं मायया छनं ददृशू रावणिं रणे॥
en: The monkeys, Surveying the sky as well as all directions, could not see Rāvana's son in battle enveloped with illusion.

sn: तं तु मायाप्रतिच्छन्नं माययैव बिभीषणः। वीक्षमाणो ददर्शाग्रे भ्रातुः पुत्रमवस्थितम्।। तमप्रतिमकर्माणमप्रतिद्वन्द्वमाहवे॥ ददर्शान्तर्हितं वीरं वरदानाद्विभीषणः। तेजसा यशसा चैव विक्रमेण च संयुतः॥
en: Then Vibhīşaņa by means of illusion saw his brother's son staying before, hidden by illusion. And Vibhīşaņa saw that hero of incomparable deeds, who had no compeer in the field and who had energy, fame and prowess-as he remained invisible in consequence of the boon received from Brahma.

sn: इन्द्रजित्त्वात्मनः कर्म तौ शयानौ समीक्ष्य च। उवाच परमप्रीतो हर्षयन्सर्वराक्षसान्॥
en: And Indrajit, seeing his own feat and them lying at length, spoke in excess of joy, gladdening all the Rākşasas.

sn: दूषणस्य च हन्तारौ खरस्य च महाबलौ। सादितौ मामकैर्बाणैतिरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ॥
en: The brothers-Rāma and Lakşmaņa, possessed of great strength, who had slain Khara and Dūşaņa, are themselves slain with my shafts.

sn: नेमौ मोक्षयितुं शक्यावेतस्मादिषुबन्धनात्। सर्वैरपि समागम्य सर्षिसङ्घः सुरासुरैः॥
en: All the celestials and Asuras assembled together with the saints, are incompetent to emancipate these from the fetters of my shafts.

sn: यत्कृते चिन्तयानस्य शोकार्तस्य पितुर्मम। अस्पृष्ट्वा शयनं गात्रैस्त्रियामा याति शर्वरी॥ कृत्स्नेयं यत्कृते लङ्का नदी वर्षास्विवाकुला। सोऽयं मूलहरोऽ नर्थः सर्वेषां शमितो मया॥
en: He for whom my father was exercise with anxiety and tormented by grief, for whom my sire used to spend nights without pressing his bed, for whom this entire Lankā had resembled a river turbulent in the rainy reason, that same evil sticking by the root of all, has been dispensed his quietus by me.

sn: रामस्य लक्ष्मणस्यैव सर्वेषां च वनौकसाम्। विक्रमा निष्फलाः सर्वे यथा शरदि तोयदाः॥
en: And like clouds of autumn, the prowess of Råma and Laksmana as well as that of all the rangers of the woods, has been rendered useless.

sn: एवमुक्त्वा तु तान्सरािक्षसान्परिपश्यतः। यूथपानपि तान्सांस्ताडयत्स च रावणिः॥ नीलं नवभिराहत्य मैन्दं सद्विविदं तथा। त्रिभिस्त्रिभिरमित्रघ्नस्तताप परमेषुभिः॥
en: Saying this in the presence of all the Raksasas, Ravana's son-destroyer of foesfencing the monkey-leaders, hit Nila with nine arrows, and hurt Mainda and Dvivida each with three powerful shafts.

sn: जाम्बवन्तं महेष्वासो विद्ध्वा बाणेन वक्षसि । हनूमतो वेगवतो विससर्ज शरान्दश॥
en: And piercing Jāmbavān with an arrow in the chest, that mighty bowman discharged ten at Hanumān.

sn: गवाक्षं शरभं चैव तावप्यमितविक्रमौ। द्वाभ्यां द्वाभ्यां महावेगो विव्याध युधि रावणिः।।२०
en: And ravana's son possessed of exceeding impetuosity, pierced in the conflict with two shafts each Gavākşa and Śarabha of immeasurable vigour.

sn: गोलाङ्गुलेश्वरं चैव वालिपुत्रमथाङ्गदम्। विव्याध बहुभिर्बाणैस्त्वरमाणोऽथ रावणिः॥
en: And Rāvana's son, summoning celerity, pierced the king of Golangulas and Vāli's son, Angada, with innumerable arrows.

sn: तान्वानरवरान्भित्त्वा शरैरग्निशिखोपमैः। ननाद बलवांस्तत्र महासत्त्वः स रावणिः॥
en: The powerful son of Rāvana, endowed with might, piercing the foremost monkeys with shafts resembling tongues of flames, set up shouts in the field of battle.

sn: तानर्दयित्वा बाणौषैत्रासयित्वा च वानरान्। प्रजहास महाबाहुर्वचनं चेदमब्रवीत्॥
en: And tormenting the monkeys with volleys of shafts and striking terror into them, that mightyarmed one. bursting out into a laugh, said.

sn: शरबन्धेन घोरेण मया बद्धौ चमूमुखे। सहितौ भ्रातरावेतौ निशामयत राक्षसाः॥
en: “Let the Raksasas behold these brothers lying fast bound with dreadful arrows in front of the forces."

sn: एवमुक्तास्तु ते सर्वे राक्षसाः कूटयोधिनः। परं विस्मयमापन्नाः कर्मणा तेन हर्षिताः॥ विनेदुश्च महानादान्सर्वे ते जलदोपमाः। हतो राम इति ज्ञात्वा रावणिं समपूजयन्॥
en: Thus addressed, those Rākşasas-wily warriors all-resembling masses of clouds, witnessing that deed (of Indrajit), struck with wonder and rejoicing (greatly), set up tremendous roars. And thinking that Rāma was slain, they honoured Ravana's son.

sn: निष्पन्दौ तु तदा दृष्ट्वा भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ। वसुधायां निरुच्छ्वासौ हतावित्यन्वमन्यत ॥
en: Seeing the brothers-Rāma and Laksmanamotionless, and lying inert on the ground, they took them for slain.

sn: हर्षेण तु समाविष्ट इन्द्रजित्समितिंजयः। प्रविवेश पुरीं लङ्कां हर्षयन्सर्वनैर्ऋतान् ॥
en: And, experiencing excess of joy, Indrajitconquerer in conflict-entered the city of Lankā, rejoicing all the Nairtas.

sn: रामलक्ष्मणयोर्दृष्ट्वा शरीरे सायकैश्चिते। सर्वाणि चाङ्गोपाङ्गानि सुग्रीवं भयमाविशत्॥
en: Seeing the bodies as well as the limbs of Rāma and Lakşmana, covered entirely with arrows, fear took possession of Sugriva.

sn: तमुवाच परित्रस्तं वानरेन्द्र विभीषणः। सवाष्पवदनं दीनं क्रोधव्याकुललोचनम्। अलं त्रासेन सुग्रीव वाष्पवेगो निगृह्यताम्॥
en: Thereat Vibhīşaņa said to that lord of monkeys, staying in woe-begone guise, with a tearful countenance, and his eyes wild with wrath, "Do not give way to fear, O Sugriva. Restrain your rising tears!

sn: एवं प्रायाणि युद्धानि विजयो नास्ति नैष्ठिकः। सभाग्यशेषतास्माकं यदि वीर भविष्यति॥ मोहमेतौ प्रहास्येते महात्मानौ महाबलौ। पर्यवस्थापयात्मानमनाथं मां च वानर।। सत्यधर्माभिरक्तानां नास्ति मृत्युकृतं भयम्॥
en: This is the way of warfare: victory is not (always) sure But, O hero, If Fortune ultimately smile upon us, this stupor shall go off from these high-souled and exceedingly powerful ones. therefore, O monkey, do you cheer me, who am forlorn.

sn: एवमुक्त्वा ततस्तस्य जलक्लिन्नेन पाणिना। सुग्रीवस्य शुभे नेत्रे प्रममार्ज विभीषणः॥
en: Saying this, with hand Vibhīşaņa washed Sugriva's graceful eyes with water.

sn: ततः सलिलमादाय विद्यया परिजप्य च। सुग्रीवनेत्रे धर्मात्मा प्रममार्ज विभीषणः॥
en: And taking water, the righteous Vibhīşaņa by means of his knowledge, washed Sugrīva's eyed there with.

sn: विमृज्य वदनं तस्य कपिराजस्य धीमतः। अब्रवीत्कालसंप्राप्तमसंभ्रान्तमिदं वचः॥
en: And washing the face of the intelligent monkey-monarch, Vibhisana spoke these words, seasonable and sedate.

sn: न काल: कपिराजेन्द्र वैकलव्यमवलम्बितुम्। अतिस्नेहोऽपि कालेऽसिमान्मरणायोपकल्पते॥
en: O foremost of monkey-kings, this is no time for being overcome with stupor. At this hour, even immoderate affection may lead destruction.

sn: तस्मादुत्सृज्य वैक्लव्यं सर्वकार्यविनाशनम्। हितं रामपुरोगाणां सैन्यानामनुचिन्तय॥
en: Therefore, casting off stupor, which tends to mar all work, do you bethink you how you may serve this army headed by Rāma.

sn: अथ वा रक्ष्यतां रामो यावत्संज्ञाविपर्ययः। लब्धसंज्ञौ हि काकुत्स्थौ भयं नौ व्यपनेष्यतः॥
en: Or do you protect Rāma so long as he does not regain consciousness; and when the Kākutsthas shall have regained consciousness, all our apprehension shall vanish.

sn: नैतत्किंचन रामस्य न च रामो मुमूर्षति। नोन हास्यते लक्ष्मीर्दुर्लभा या गतायुषाम्॥
en: This is nothing to Rāma is not dying. And Lakşmi* who is incapable of being attained by those that are doomed, shall not forsake this one. *The goddess of prosperity. to

sn: तस्मादाश्वासयात्मानं बलं चाश्वासय स्वकम्। यावत्सैन्यानि सर्वाणि पुनः संस्थापयाम्यहम्॥
en: Therefore do you comfort yourself, do you also cheer up your own forces, while I am engaged in composing all the troops.

sn: एते हि फुल्लनयनास्त्रासादागतसाध्वसाः। कर्णे कर्णे प्रकथिता हरयो हरिसत्तम॥
en: O best of monkeys, these with distended eyes, come under the governance of terror, are, stricken with panic, whispering into each other's ears.

sn: मां तु दृष्ट्वा प्रधावन्तमनीकं संप्रहर्षितम्। त्यजन्तु हरयस्त्रासं भुक्तपूर्वामिव स्रजम्॥
en: But seeing me, let the forces rushing about, cheered up, as well as the monkeys, cast off all fear, like a wreath that has been used before.

sn: समाश्वास्य तु सुग्रीवं राक्षसेन्द्रो विभीषणः। विद्रुतं वानरानीकं तत्समाश्वासयत्पुनः॥
en: Thus comforting Sugriva, Vibhisana-lord of Rākṣasas-again instilled spirits into the flying forces of monkeys.

sn: इन्द्रजित्तु महामायः सर्वसैन्यसमावृतः। विवेश नगरी लङ्कां पितरं चाभ्युपागमत्॥
en: And Indrajit, worker of mighty illusionsaccompanied by his troops, entered the city of Larkā and presented himself before his father.

sn: तत्र रावणमासाद्य अभिवाद्य कृताञ्जलिः। आचचक्षे प्रियं पित्रे निहतौ रामलक्ष्मणौ॥
en: And approaching Rāvana and saluting him with joined hands, he informed his sire of the welcome tidings that Răma and Lakṣmaṇa had been slain.

sn: उत्पपात ततो हृष्टः पुत्रं च परिषस्वजे। रावणो रक्षसां मध्ये श्रुत्वा शत्रूनिपातितौ ॥
en: And hearing that his foe had fallen, Rāvana springing up in the midst of the Rākşasas, With great joy embraced his son.

sn: उपाघ्राय च तं मूर्ध्नि पप्रच्छ प्रीतमानसः। पृच्छते च यथावृत्तं पित्रे तस्मै न्यवेदयत्। यथा तौ शरबन्धेन निश्चेष्टौ निष्प्रभौ कृतौ॥
en: And scenting the crown of his head, (Rāvana) with a delighted heart, asked (Indrajit as to all that had taken place). And on being asked, he (Indrajit) truly related to his sire how (Rāma and Lakşmaņa) had been rendered senseless and lack-Lustre by being fastened with shafts.

sn: स हर्षवेगानुगतान्तरात्मा श्रुत्वा गिरं तस्य महारथस्य जहौ ज्वरं दाशरथेः समुत्थं प्रहृष्टवाचाभिननन्द पुत्रम्।।
en: Thereat, with rapture surcharging his inmost soul, Rāvana, hearing the speech of the mighty car warrior, banished his fear of Dasaratha's son, and rising up, honoured his son with glad words. that had taken place). And on being asked, he (Indrajit) truly related to his sire how (Rāma and Lakşmaņa) had been rendered senseless and lack-Lustre by being fastened with shafts.

sn: स हर्षवेगानुगतान्तरात्मा श्रुत्वा गिरं तस्य महारथस्य जहौ ज्वरं दाशरथेः समुत्थं प्रहृष्टवाचाभिननन्द पुत्रम्।।
en: Thereat, with rapture surcharging his inmost soul, Rāvana, hearing the speech of the mighty car warrior, banished his fear of Dasaratha's son, and rising up, honoured his son with glad words.

sn: तस्मिन्प्रविष्टे लगायां कृतार्थे रावणात्मजे। राघवं परिवार्याथ ररक्षुर्वानरर्षभाः॥
en: When Rāvana's son entered Lankā, after having accomplished his purpose, the foremost monkeys protected Raghava, surrounding him on all sides.

sn: हनुमानङ्गदो नीलः सुषेणः कुमुदो नलः। गजो गवाक्षः पनसः सानुप्रस्थो महाहरिः॥ जाम्बवानृषभः सुन्दो रम्भः शतबलिः पृथुः। व्यूढानीकाश्च यत्ताश्च दुमानादाय सर्वतः॥ वीक्षमाणा दिशः सर्वास्तिर्यगूर्ध्वं च वानराः। तृणेष्वपि च चेष्टत्सु राक्षसा इति मेनिरे॥
en: And Hanumān, and Angada, and Nīla, and Susena, and Kumuda, and Nala, and Gaya, and Gavākṣa, and Panas, and Sānuprastha-a mighty monkey-and Jämbavān, and Rishava, and Sunda, and Rambha, and Satabali, and Prthu, all forming them selves into array, and equipped with trees on all sides, and remaining vigilantthe monkeys kept gazing at all sides, awry and upwards; and even when a straw stirred, they thought it to be a Rākşasa.

sn: रावणश्चापि संहृष्टो विसृज्येन्द्रजितं सुतम्। आजुहाव ततः सीतारक्षणी राक्षसोस्तदा॥
en: Rāvana, on his part experiencing the height of exaltation, summoned the Rākṣasais engaged in guarding Sita.

sn: राक्षस्यस्त्रिजटा चापि शासनात्तमुपस्थिताः। ता उवाच ततो हृष्टो राक्षसी राक्षसाधिपः॥
en: Thereat the Raksasi-Trijata and otherspresented themselves at his command. And then the lord of Rākşasas, delighted addressed then the Raksasis, saying.

sn: हताविन्द्रजिताख्यात वैदेह्या रामलक्ष्मणौ। पुष्पकं तत्समारोप्य दर्शयध्वं रणे हतौ।७।।
en: Tell Vaidehí that Rāma and Lakşmaņa have been slain in battle by Indrajit. And taking her on Pushaka, show her (Rāma and Lakşmaņa) lying slain on the field of battle.

sn: यदाश्रयादवष्टव्धा नेयं मामुपतिष्ठते। सोऽस्या भर्ता सह भ्रात्रा निहतो रणमूर्धनि ॥
en: That one depending on whom she had proudly set her face against me, that husband of hers, along with his brother, has been slain in conflict.

sn: निर्विशङ्का निरुद्विग्ना निरपेक्षा च मैथिली। मामुपस्थास्यते सीता सर्वाभरणभूषिता ॥
en: Then methyl's daughter, her fear gone off with her anxiety, and herself losing all support, Sītādaughter to methyl-decked out in all ornaments, shall seek me.

sn: अद्य कालवशं प्राप्तं रणे रामं सलक्ष्मणम्। अवेक्ष्य विनिवृत्ता सा चान्यां गतिमपश्यती।। अनपेक्षा विशालाक्षी मामुपस्थास्यते स्वयम्॥
en: And today beholding Rāma with Lakşmaņa, come under the away of Time, she, finding no other way, shall desist from her present course. And seeing no other resource, that one of expansive eyes shall of herself seek me.

sn: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा रावणस्य दुरात्मनः। राक्षस्यस्तास्तथेत्युक्त्वा जग्मुर्वै यत्र पुष्पकम्॥
en: Hearing those words of the wicked-minded Rāvana, the Rākşasais, saying, “So be it,” went to where Puspaka was.

sn: ततः पुष्पकमादाय राक्षस्यो रावणाज्ञया। अशोकवनिकास्थां तां मैथिली समुपानयन्॥
en: Then taking Pușpaka, the Rākşasis at Rāvana's command went to Maithilī staying in theasoka wood.

sn: तामादाय तु राक्षस्यो भर्तृशोकपराजिताम्। सीतामारोपयामासुर्विमानं पुष्पकं तदा॥
en: Then, taking Sītā, who was overcome with grief for her lord, the Raksasais, placed her on the car, Puspaka.

sn: ततः पुष्पकमारोप्य सीतां त्रिजटया सह। रावणश्चारयामास पताकाध्वजमालिनीम्॥ प्रावोषयत हृष्टश्च लङ्कायां राक्षसेश्वरः। राघवो लक्ष्मणश्चैव हताविन्द्रजिता रणे॥ विमानेनापि गत्वा तु सीता त्रिजटया सह। ददर्श वानराणां तु सर्वं सैन्यं निपातितम्॥
en: Placing Sītā on Puşpaka along with Trijatā, Răvana took her all round (Lankā) crowded with ensigns and standards. And the lord of Rākşasas jubilantly proclaimed in Lankā, Rāghava as well as Lakşmaņa have been slain by Indrajit in battle. And going about with Trijatā Sītā saw all the monkey-troops slain.

sn: प्रहृष्टमनसश्चापि ददर्श पिशिताशनान्। वानरांश्चातिदुःखार्तान्रामलक्ष्मणपार्श्वतः॥
en: She found the flesh-eaters elated in spirits, and the monkeys afflicted with extreme grief at the side of Rāma and Lakşmaņa.

sn: ततः सीता ददर्शोभौ शयानौ शरतल्पगौ। लक्ष्मणं चैव रामं च विसंज्ञौ शरपीडितौ॥
en: Then Sītā beheld both Lakşmaņa and Rāma lying in the field, senseless and bound with arrows.

sn: विध्वस्तकवचौ वीरौ विप्रविद्धशरासनौ। सायकैश्छिन्नसर्वाङ्गौ शरस्तम्बमयौ क्षितौ ॥
en: Those heroes were lying on the earth, their mail torn, their bows cast off their bodies mangled all over and thickly pierce with shafts.

sn: तौ दृष्ट्वा भ्रातरौ तत्र प्रवीरौ पुरुषर्षभौ। शयानौ पुण्डरीकाक्षौ कुमारविव पावकी॥ शरतल्पगतौ वीरौ तथाभूतौ नरर्षभौ। दुःखार्ता करुणं सीता सुभृशं विललाप ह॥
en: Seeing those brothers, foremost of heroes and best of men-having eyes resembling white lotuses, and them selves like to Kumāras, lying in the field,* the fire sprung one, Sītā stricken with grief, beg a to weep piteously. *Virān narashabhān-heroes and best of menoccurs again, left out on the score of redendancy.

sn: भर्तारमनवद्याङ्गी लक्ष्मणं चासितेक्षणा। प्रेक्ष्य पांसुषु चेष्टन्तौ रुरोद जनकात्मजा॥
en: That black-eyed one of an excellent person, Janaka's daughter-seeing them roll in the dust, broke out into lamentation.

sn: सबाष्पशोकाभिहता समीक्ष्य तौ भ्रातरौ देवसुतप्रभावौ। वितर्कयन्ती निधनं तयोः सा दुःखान्विता वाक्यमिदं जगाद॥
en: With her eyes shedding plentiful tears, she seeing those brothers, endowed with god-like prowess, concluded them to be dead; and overwhelmed with grief, spoke as follows. as as

sn: भर्तारं निहतं दृष्ट्वा लक्ष्मणं च महाबलम्। विललाप भृशं सीता करुणं शोककर्शिता॥
en: Seeing her husband, well the exceedingly powerful Laksmana, slain, Srta, afflicted with grief, burst into bitter lamentation.

sn: ऊचुर्लाक्षणिका ये मां पुत्रिण्यविधवेति च। तेऽद्य सर्वे हते रामे ज्ञानिनोऽनृतवादिनः॥
en: The soothsayers had said that I should have sons, and should never be a widow. But on Råma being slain, it sees now that those ones, possessed of knowledge, had spoken untruthfully.

sn: यज्वनो महिषीं मामूचुः पत्नी च सत्रिणः। तेऽद्य सर्वे हते रामे ज्ञानिनोऽनृतवादिनः॥
en: Those also, who having celebrated sacrifices and rites, had said that I should become the queen (of Rama), on Rāma being slain, seems today to have spoken a falsehood, although they are possessed of knowledge.

sn: वीरपार्थिवपत्नीनां ये विदुर्भर्तृपूजिताम्। तेऽद्य सर्वे हते रामे ज्ञानिनोऽनृतवादिनः॥
en: They also asserted that I should be honoured of the wives of heroic kings as well as of my lord, but on Rāma being slain, they seem to have spoken a falsehood, although possessed of knowledge.

sn: ऊचुः संश्रवणे ये मां द्विजाः कान्तिकाः शुभाम्। । तेऽद्य सर्वे हते रामे ज्ञानिनोऽनृतवादिनः॥
en: Those twice-born ones that in any hearing had said auspicious words, on Rāma being slain, seem today to have spoken a falsehood although they were possessed of knowledge.

sn: इमानि खलु पद्मानि पादयोर्वै कुलस्त्रियः। आधिराज्येऽभिषिच्यन्ते नरेन्द्रैः पतिभिः सह॥
en: These lotus-marks on the feet, betokening to gentlewomen possessing them, that they are to be installed in the kingdom in company with their husbands-who are kings-are on me.

sn: वैधव्यं यान्ति यैर्नार्योऽलक्षणैर्भाग्यदुर्लभाः। नात्मनस्तानि पश्यामि पश्यन्ती हतलक्षणा।७।।
en: Those marks find I none on me by which women of rare fortune come by widowhood, but I find that in me these good tokens are nullified.

sn: सत्यनामानि पद्मानि स्त्रीणामुक्तानि लक्षणैः। तान्यद्य निहते रामे वितथानि भवन्ति मे॥
en: Those marks that are pronounced infallible by those versed in such knowledge, on Rama being slain, are nullified in me.

sn: केशाः सूक्ष्माः समा नीला ध्रुवौ चासंहते मम। वृत्ते चारोमके जो दन्ताश्चाविरला मम।।।।
en: My hairs are fine, equal, and blue; my eyebrows touch each other; my hips are devoid of down and round; and my teeth are close.

sn: शो नेत्रे करौ पादौ गुल्फावूरू समौ चितौ। अनुवृत्तनखाः स्निग्धाः समाश्चाङ्गुलयो मम॥
en: My temples, and eyes hands, feet, ankles, and thighs are equal. And my fingers are furnished with round nails, and are plump and even in the middle.

sn: स्तनौ चाविरलौ पीनौ मामको मग्नचूचुकौ। मग्ना चोत्सेधनी नाभिः पार्थोरस्कं च मे चितम्॥
en: And my breasts are close and firm and developed, and have their nipples sunk. And my navel is depressed, with high sides. And my chest is swelling.

sn: मम वर्णो मणिनिभौ मृदून्यङ्गरुहाणि च। प्रतिष्ठितां द्वादशभिरमामूचुः शुभलक्षणाम्॥
en: My complexion is like the hue of gems, and my down soft. And they said that I was furnished with twelve auspicious signs.

sn: समग्रयवमच्छिद्रं पाणिपादं च वर्णवत्। मन्दस्मितेत्येव च मां कन्यालाक्षणिका विदुः॥
en: And my hands in the middle parts of my fingers contain wheat-marks, and in the spaces between the fingers, have no uneven corners. And my feet also partake of the general complexion. And my laugh is a gentle smile. And those versed in marks of women knew that I was possessed of such marks.

sn: आधिराज्येऽभिषेको मे ब्राह्मणैः पतिना सह। कृतान्तकुशलैरुक्तं तत्सर्वं वितथीकृतम्॥१४॥
en: Those Brähmaņas skilled in telling fortune said that I should be installed in the kingdom along with my husband; but all that has been falsified.

sn: शोधयित्वा जनस्थानं प्रवृत्तिमुपलभ्य च। तीर्वा सागरमक्षोभ्यं भ्रातरौ गोष्पदे हतौ॥
en: Having purified Janasthana (of Raksasas), obtained tidings of me, and crossed the Ocean* incapable of being agitated, those brothers have been slain in the footprint of a cow! *The commentator assigns a metaphorical sense to ocean-but this is hardly necessary.

sn: ननु वारुणाग्नेयमैन्द्रं वायव्यमेव च। अस्त्रं ब्रह्मशिरश्चैव राघवौ प्रत्यपद्यत॥
en: The descendants of Raghu had obtained Väruņa and Āgneya and Aindra and Vāyavya and Brahmasira weapons.* * And did they not remember this now? completes the sense.

sn: अदृश्यमानेन रणे भायया वासवोपमौ। मम नाथावनाथाया निहतौ रामलक्ष्मणौ॥
en: Through illusion have those lords of me, who am forlorn. Rāma and Lakşmaņa, resembling Vasava himself in battle, been slain.

sn: नहि दृष्टिपथं प्राप्य राघवस्य रणे रिपुः। जीवन्प्रतिनिवर्तेत यद्यपि स्यान्मनोजवः॥
en: Coming in battle within ken of Raghava, a foe, even if he be endowed with the fleetness of thought, does not go back living.

sn: न कालस्यातिभारोऽस्ति कृतान्तश्च सुदुर्जयः। यत्र रामः सह भ्रात्रा शेते युधि निपातितः॥
en: There is nothing which is too hard for Time; and the Destroyer is incapable of being overcome; inasmuch as Rāma along with his brother Lakşmaņa has fallen in fight.

sn: न शोचामि तथा राम लक्ष्मणं च महारथम्। नात्मानं जननीं चापि यथा श्वश्रू तपस्विनीम्॥ सा तु चिन्तयते नित्यं समाप्तव्रतमागतम्। कदा द्रक्ष्यामि सीतां च लक्ष्मणं च सराघवम्॥
en: I do not so much mourn Rāma or the mighty car-warrior-Laksmana-or, for that matter, self, as I do the wretched mother-in-law of mine. She ever think of the period of the promise. "When shall I behold Sītā and Lakşmaņa with Rāghava?

sn: परिदेवयमानां तां राक्षसी त्रिजटाब्रवीत्। मा विषादं कृथा देवि भर्तायं तव जीवति॥
en: As she was thus lamenting, the Rākṣasai, said, O exalted lady, do not weep thus, your lord live.

sn: कारणानि च वक्ष्यामि महान्ति सदृशानि च। यथेमौ जीवतो देवि भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ॥
en: O dignified one, I shall unfold to you potent and probable reasons why the brothers Rāma and Laksmana live.

sn: नहि कोपपरीतानि हर्षपर्युत्सुकानि च। भवन्ति युधि योधानां मुखानि निहते पतौ॥
en: When their leader fall, the countenances of the warriors in battle are not overspread with passion, or display cheerfulness and vivacity.

sn: इदं विमानं वैदेहि पुष्पकं नाम नामतः। दिव्यं त्वां धारयेनेदं यद्येतौ गतजीवितौ ॥
en: O Vaidehi, if those had lost their lives, this celestial chariot, named Puspaka, would not have held you.

sn: हतवीरप्रधाना हि गतोत्साहा निरुद्यमा। सेना भ्रमति संख्येषु हतकणेव नौ ले॥ इयं पुनरसंभ्रान्ता निरुद्विग्ना तपस्विनि। सेना रक्षति काकुत्स्थौ मया प्रीत्या निवेदितौ ॥
en: An army that has its heroes and chiefs slainbecoming dispirited and drooping, range the field, like a vessel on water that has losi its helmsman. But, O lorm one, these troops, be trying neither agitation nor anxiety, are guarding the Kākutsthas, This I tell you of them out of affection.

sn: सा त्वं भव सुविस्रब्धा अनुमानैः सुखोदयैः। अहतौ पश्य काकुत्स्थौ स्नेहादेतद्ब्रवीमि ते॥
en: Do you, at this conclusion bringing in joy, take comfort; and behold the Kākutsthas unslain. This I tell you from affection.

sn: अनृतं नोक्तपूर्व मे न च वक्ष्यामि मैथिलि। चारित्रसुखशीलत्वात्प्रविष्टासि मनो मम ॥
en: I never told you untruths heretofore; nor, O Mithila's daughter, will I tell them to you now. You by virtue of your character conducive to delight, have found an access into my heart.

sn: नेमौ शक्यौ रणे जेतुं सेन्ट्रैरपि सुरासुरैः। तादृशं दर्शनं दृष्ट्वा मया चोदीरितं तव॥
en: These even the celestials and Asuras with Indra (at their head) are incompetent to quell. Seeing such sight, I speak to you as to their being alive.

sn: इदं तु सुमहच्चित्रं शरैः पश्यस्व मैथिलि। विसंज्ञौ पतितावेतौ नैव लक्ष्मीर्विमुञ्चति ॥
en: And behold O Maithili, this mighty wonder! These are lying insensible with arrows; but of these Grace has not taken leave.

sn: प्रायेण गतसत्वानां पुरुषाणां गतायुषाम्। दृश्यमानेषु वक्रेषु परं भवति वैकृतम्॥ त्यज शोकं च दुःखं च मोहं च जनकात्मजे। रामलक्ष्मणयोरर्थे नाद्य शक्यमजीवितुम्॥
en: It generally happens that the faces of persons dead and gone, are unsightly to a degree. Therefore, O Janka's daughter, leave off grief and sorrow and stupor. For the sake of Rāma and Lakşmaņa you can not today put a period to your existence.

sn: श्रुत्वा तु वचनं तस्याः सीता सुरसुतोपमा। कृताञ्जलिरुवाचेमामेवमस्त्विति मैथिली॥
en: Hearing her words, Mithila's daughter-Sītāresembling the daughter of a celestial, with hands joined, said, "May this be so!

sn: विमानं पुष्पकं तत्तु संनिवर्त्य मनोजवम्। दीना त्रिजटया सीता लङ्कामेव प्रवेशिता॥
en: Then turning away the car Puşpaka fleet as the mind, the distressed Sītā entered Lankā along with Trijata.

sn: ततस्त्रिजटया सार्धं पुष्पकादवरुह्य सा। अशोकवनिकामेव राक्षसीभिः प्रवेशिता॥
en: Then in company with Trijatā alighting from Puşpaka, she along with the Rākşasis entered the asoka wood.

sn: प्रविश्य सीता बहुवृक्षखण्डां तां राक्षसेन्द्रस्य विहारभूमिम्। संप्रेक्ष्य संचिन्त्य च राजपुत्रौ परं विषादं समुपाजगाम्॥
en: Entering that sporting-ground of the Raksasa lord abounding in woody tracts, Sītā, having beheld those princes and reflected on them, became subject to a mighty grief.

sn: घोरेण शरबन्धेन बद्धौ दशरथात्मजौ। निःश्वसन्तौ यथा नागौ शयानौ रुधिरोक्षितौ॥
en: Bound up terribly with shafts, Dasaratha's sons, lying down bathed in blood, sighed hard like to serpents.

sn: सर्वे ते वानरश्रेष्ठाः ससुग्रीवमहाबलाः। परिवार्य महात्मानौ तस्थुः शोकपरिप्लुताः॥
en: All those foremost monkeys, along with Sugrīva, possessed of exceeding strength, overwhelmed with sorrow, remained surrounding those high-souled ones.

sn: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे रामः प्रत्यबुध्यत वीर्यवान्। स्थिरत्वात्सत्वयोगाच्च शरैः संदानितोऽपि सन्॥
en: In the meanwhile, the powerful Rāma, albeit fast bound by the shafts, awoke by virtue of the exceeding toughness of his person, as well as his might.

sn: ततो दृष्ट्वा सरुधिरं निषण्णं गाढमर्पितम्। भ्रातरं दीनवदनं पर्यदेवयदातुरः॥
en: Then, seeing his brother having a distressful countenance, covered with blood, feeble, and fast bound by the shafts, Rāma, greatly aggrieved, began to mourn.

sn: किं न मे सीतया कार्यं लब्धया जीवितेन वा। शयानं योऽद्य पश्यामि भ्रातरं युधि निर्जितम्॥
en: Of what use to me is the recovery of Sītă, or life either, when today I see my brother vanquished in fight and lying down in the field?

sn: शक्या सीतासमा नारी मर्त्यलोके विचिन्वता। न लक्ष्मणसमो भ्राता सचिवः सांपरायिकः॥
en: Seeking in the world (of men), I may light upon a woman like Sītā; but never on a brother, or a helper, or a warrior like to Laksmana.

sn: परित्यक्ष्याम्यहं प्राणान्वानराणां तु पश्यताम्। यदि पञ्चत्वमापन्नः सुमित्रानन्दवर्धनः॥
en: If that enhancer of Sumitra's joy have met with his end, my life I must renounce in the sight of the monkeys.

sn: किं नु वक्ष्यामि कौसल्यां मातरं किं नु कैकयीम्। कथमम्बां सुमित्रां च पुत्रदर्शनलालसाम्॥ विवत्सां वेपमानां च वेपन्ती कुररीमिव। कथमाश्वासयिष्यामि यदि यास्यामि तं विना ॥
en: What shall I say to Kausalyā; and what shall I say to Kaikeyi ? And what shall I say to mother Sumitrā eager for a sight of her son? And if I go (back) without him, how shall I soothe her, like to a cow reft of her calf; and trembling; and resembling a mourning Kurari?

sn: कथं वक्ष्यामि शत्रुघ्नं भरतं च यशस्विनम्। मया सह वनं यातो विना तेनाहमागतः॥
en: How shall I say to Satrughna and the illustrious Bharata, 'He went with me to the forest; but I come (back) here without him "?

sn: उपालम्भं न शक्ष्यामि सोढुमम्बासुमित्रया। इहैव देहं त्यक्ष्यामि नहि जीवितुमुत्सहे॥
en: I shall not be able to bear the rebuke of mother Sumitră. Therefore even here shall I renounce my person; for certainly I dare not live.

sn: धिङ् मां दुष्कृतकर्माणमनायं मत्कृते ह्यसौ। लक्ष्मणः पातितः शेते शरतल्पे गतासुवत्॥
en: Fie on me, who am wicked and base; for me this Lakşmaņa, brought down, leith in the field of battle, like one that is without life.

sn: त्वं नित्यं सुविषण्णं मामाश्वासयसि लक्ष्मण। गतासुर्नाद्य शक्तोऽसि मामार्तमभिभाषितुम्॥
en: O Lakşmaņa, you ever comforts me when I am dispirited. But today, having lost your life, you can not speak to me, who am afflicted.

sn: येनाद्य बहवो युद्धे निहता राक्षसाः क्षितौ। तस्यामेवाद्य शूरस्त्वं शेषे विनिहतः शरैः॥
en: You, O hero, who had in battle slain innumerable Rākṣasa lying around, have (at length) yourself been slain in the field with shafts.

sn: शयानः शरतल्पेऽस्मिन्सशोणितपरिसुतः। शरभूतस्ततो भासि भास्करोऽस्तमिव व्रजन्॥
en: And lying down in the battle-field, bleeding and covered with arrows, you appear like the Sun when he has gone up the Setting-hill.

sn: बाणाभिहतमर्मत्वान्न शक्नोषीह भाषितुम्। रुजा चाब्रुवतो यस्य दृष्टिरागेण सूच्यते॥
en: In consequence of shafts piercing your vitals, you cannot speak; but your visible expression, albeit you are dumb, betokens pain.

sn: यथैव मां वनं यान्तमनुयातो महाद्युतिः। अहमप्यनुयास्यामि तथैवैनं यमक्षयम्॥
en: O you endowed with exceeding splendour, even as you did follow me into the forest, will I follow you to the mansion of Yama.

sn: इष्टबन्धुजनो नित्यं मां च नित्यमनुव्रतः। इमामद्य गतोऽवस्थां ममानार्यस्य दुर्नयैः॥
en: You having dear friends, and ever following me, has come by this plight in consequence of my reprehensible conduct.

sn: सुरुष्टेनापि वीरेण लक्ष्मणेन न संस्मरे। परुषं विप्रियं चापि श्रावितं तु कदाचन॥
en: I do not remember having heard any harsh speech from the heroic Lakşmaņa, even when he had happened to be exceedingly wroth.

sn: विसस कवेगेन पञ्च बाणशतानि यः। इष्वस्त्रेष्वधिकस्तस्मात्कार्तवीर्याच्च लक्ष्मणः॥
en: He that could discharge at one shot five hundred shafts, that Lakşmaņa is superior to karttaviryya himself in that weapon-the bow.

sn: अस्त्रैरसत्राणि यो हन्याच्छक्रस्यापि महात्मनः। सोऽयमुव्या हतः शेते महार्हशयनोचितः॥
en: He that with his arms could resist the arms of Sakra himself, that one worthy of a costly couchLeith down on the ground, slain.

sn: तत्तु मिथ्या प्रलप्तं मां प्रधक्ष्यति न संशयः। यन्मया न कृतो राजा राक्षसानां विभीषणः॥
en: That false babble shall now, without doubt, consume me; for by me has not Bibhishna been made monarch of the Rákşasas.

sn: अस्मिन्मुहूर्ते सुग्रीव प्रतियातुमिवाहसि। सत्त्वहीनं मया राजरावणोऽभिभविष्यति॥
en: Do you, O Sugrīva, this very moment retrace your steps. Bereft of your strength through me you will be worsted by Rāvaņa.

sn: अङ्गदं तु पुरस्कृत्य ससैन्यं सपरिच्छदम्। सागरं तर सुग्रीव नीलेन च नलेन च॥
en: O Sugriva, placing Angada to the fore, do you, taking your host as well as the equipage, in company with Nila and Nala, cross over the Ocean.

sn: कृतं हि सुमहत्कर्म यदन्यैर्दुष्करं रणे। ऋक्षराजेन तुष्यामि गोलाङ्गुलाधिपेन च॥ अङ्गदेन कृतं कर्म मैन्देन द्विविदेन च। युद्ध केसरिणा संख्ये घोरं संपातिना कृतम्॥
en: By you has been achieved a mighty feat incapable of being done by another in battle. And pleased am I with the king of bears, and the lord of Golãngulas; and Angada has quit himself nobly, as also Mainda and Dvivida. And Kesarin and Sampāti have both faught terribly.

sn: गवयेन गवाक्षेण शरभेण गजेन च। अन्यैश्च हरिभियुद्धं दुर्धरं त्यक्तजीवितैः॥
en: Gavaya, and Gavākşa, and Sarabha, and Gaja, and other monkeys have faught as others are incapable of fighting, determined to lay down their lives (for me).

sn: न चातिक्रमितुं शक्यं दैवं सुग्रीव मानुषैः। यत्तु शक्यं वयस्येन सुहृदा वा परं मम।२८॥ कृतं सुग्रीव तत्सर्वं भवता धर्मभीरुणा। मित्रकार्यं कृतमिदं भवद्भिर्वानरर्षभाः॥ अनुज्ञाता मया सर्वे यथेष्टं गन्तुमर्हथ।
en: But, O Sugriva, man cannot overrule Destiny. You, my friend, fearing righteousness, has done what lay in your power. And, You foremost of monkeys, you also have acted as become friends. Now, with my permission, go you whitersoever you are minded.

sn: शुश्रुवुस्तस्य ये सर्वे वानराः परिदेवितम्।। वर्तयांचक्रिरेऽश्रूणि नेत्रैः कृष्णेतरेक्षणाः॥
en: Hearing Rāma's lament, the monkeys-those dark-eyed and others-began to shed tears from their eyes.

sn: ततः सर्वाण्यनीकानि स्थापयित्वा विभीषणः। आजगाम गदापाणिस्त्वरितं यत्र राघवः॥
en: Then Vibhisana, quieting the army, taking a mace in his hand, swiftly went to where Rāghava was.

sn: तं दृष्ट्वा त्वरितं यान्तं नीलाञ्जनचयोपमम्। वानरा दुद्रुवुः सर्वे मन्यमानास्तु रावणिम्॥
en: Seeing him fast making his way, resembling a mass of dark collyrium, the monkeys taking him to be Ravana's son, began to run away.

sn: अथोवाच महातेजा हरिराजो महाबलः। किमियं व्यथिता सेना मूढवातेव नौर्जले॥
en: Then out spoke the highly energetic and exceedingly mighty king of monkeys, “Why is this host agitated like a bark driven hither and thither by the wind?"

sn: सुग्रीवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा वालिपुत्रोऽङ्गदोऽब्रवीत्। न त्वं पश्यसि रामं च लक्ष्मणं च महारथम्॥
en: Hearing Sugriva's speech, Vali's son said, Did you not see both those heroes-sons of Dasaratha, Rama and that mighty car-warriorLakşmaņa-covered with arrows?

sn: शरजालाचितौ वीरावुभौ दशरथात्मजौ। शरतल्ये महात्मानौ शयानौ रुधिरोक्षितौ॥
en: And (did you not see) those high-should ones lying in the field of battle, covered with blood ?

sn: अथाब्रवीद्वानरेन्द्रः सुग्रीवः पुत्रमङ्गदम्। नानिमित्तमिदं मन्ये भवितव्यं भयेन तु।४।।
en: Thereat, the lord of monkeys, Sugrīva, spoke to his son, Angada "I do not deem it without cause. This may have come to pass through sheer fear.

sn: विषण्णवदना ह्येते त्यक्तप्रहरणा दिशः। पलायन्तेऽत्र हरयस्त्रासादुत्फुल्ललोचनाः ॥
en: These monkeys with sad faces, leaving their arms behind them are flying in all directions, their eyes distended in affright.

sn: अन्योन्यस्य न लज्जन्ते न निरीक्षन्ति पृष्ठतः। विप्रकर्षन्ति चान्योन्यं पतितं लयन्ति च॥
en: They are not ashamed of each other, and they do not cast their looks back. And they hug each other, and go leaping over the fallen.

sn: एतस्मिनन्तरे वीरो गदापाणिविभीषणः। सुग्रीवं वर्धयामास राघवं च जयाशिषा ॥
en: In the meanwhile that hero, Vibhisana, bearing a mace in his hand, (approaching) greeted Sugrīva as well as Rāghava with blessings of victory.

sn: विभीषणं च सुग्रीवो दृष्ट्वा वानरभीषणम्। ऋश्रराजं महात्मानं समीपस्थमुवाच ह॥
en: And Sugriva, seeing Vibhisana, capable of inspiring fear in the monkeys, spoke to the highsouled sovereign of bears, who stood by.

sn: विभीषणोऽयं संप्राप्तो यं दृष्ट्वा वानरर्षभाः। द्रवन्त्यायतसंत्रासा रावणात्मजशङ्कया॥
en: This is Vibhișana that has come hither, seeing whom the foremost among the monkeys, from fear of Rāvana's son who, they apprehend, he is, are fleeing away, seized with a panic.

sn: शीघ्रमेतान्सुसंत्रस्तान्बहुधा विप्रधावितान्। पर्यवस्थापयाख्या हि विभीषणमुपस्थितम्।।१०
en: Do you at once stay these agitated with fear and scampering all around; and proclaim, 'This is Vibhisana, who has come here.'

sn: सुग्रीवेणैवमुक्तस्तु जाम्बवानृक्षपार्थिवः। वानरान्सान्त्वयामास संनिवर्त्य प्रधावतः॥
en: Thus directed, Jõmbavān-king of bearsrestraining those that were flying, composed the monkeys.

sn: ते निवृत्ताः पुनः सर्वे वानरास्त्यक्तसाध्वसाः। ऋक्षराजवचः श्रुत्वा तं च दृष्ट्वा विभीषणम्।।१२
en: Hearing the bear-king's words, and seeing Vibhisana, the monkeys, renouncing fear, desisted (from their flight).

sn: विभीषणस्तु रामस्य दृष्ट्वा गात्रं शरैश्चितम्। लक्ष्मणस्य तु धर्मात्मा बभूव व्यथितस्तदा॥
en: Then the righteous Vibhīșaņa, viewing Rama's as well as Laksmana's body pierced with arrows, was exceedingly aggrieved.

sn: जलक्लिन्नेन हस्तेन तयोर्ने। विमृज्य च। शोकसंपीडितमना रुरोद विललाप च॥
en: Washing their eyes with water, he, with his mind overpowered with grief, began to weep and broke out into lamentation.

sn: इमौ तौ सत्त्वसंपन्नौ विक्रान्तौ प्रियसंयुगौ। इमामवस्थां गमितौ राक्षसैः कूटयोधिभिः॥
en: The Rāksasas, fighting in wily ways, have brought to this pass these ones endowed with prowess and possessed of every perfection and gifted with might (of arm).

sn: भ्रातृपुत्रेण चैतेन दुष्पुत्रेण दुरात्मना । राक्षस्या जिह्मया बुद्ध्या वञ्चितावृजुविक्रमौ ॥
en: And with his guileful mind, that brother's son of mine, wicked-souled and an evil son (to me), has deceived these ones of straight prowess.

sn: शरैरिमावलं विद्धौ रुधिरेण समुक्षितौ । वसुधायामिमौ सुप्तौ दृश्येते शल्यकाविव ॥
en: Pierced with innumerable shafts, and covered with blood, these are lying on the ground like Salyakas.

sn: ययोर्वीर्यमुपाश्रित्य प्रतिष्ठा काङ्किता मया। ताविमौ देहनाशाय प्रसुप्तौ पुरुषर्षभौ॥
en: Those depending on whose prowess, I had sought eminence, those foremost of men, sleep here soundly for renouncing their bodies.

sn: जीवनद्य विपन्नोऽस्मि नष्टराज्यममनोरथः। प्राप्तप्रतिज्ञश्च रिपुः सकामो रावणः कृतः॥
en: Living, today I am in distress: and my desire of dominion is annihilated; and my foe, Rāvana, has his promise fulfilled and his aim crowned with success.

sn: एवं विलपमानं तं परिष्वज्य विभीषणम्। सुग्रीवः सत्त्वसंपन्नो हरिराजोऽब्रवीदिदम्॥
en: As Vibhīşana was thus lamenting, the lord of monkeys-Sugriva-endowed with strength, embracing him spoke to him.

sn: राज्यं प्राप्स्यसि धर्मज्ञ लङ्कायां नेह संशयः। रावणः सह पुत्रेण स्वकामं नेह लप्स्यते॥
en: O you cognisant of righteousness, you will here in Lankā obtain empire: no doubt of this; and Răvaņa along with his sons will be disappointed in their expectations.

sn: गरुडाधिष्ठितावेतावुभौ राघवलक्ष्मणौ। त्यक्त्वा मोहं वधिष्येते सगणं रावणं रणे॥
en: Both these-Rāma and Lakşmaņa-are under the aegis of Garuda; and, casting off their stupor: they will in battle slay Rävaņa along with his adherents.

sn: तमेव सान्त्वयित्वा तु समाश्वास्य तु राक्षसम्। सुषेणं श्वशुरं पार्श्वे सुग्रीवस्तमुवाच ह॥
en: Having thus soothed and comforted the Raksasa, Sugriva addressed his father-in-law, who was at his side, saying.

sn: सह शूरैर्हरिगणैर्लब्धसंज्ञावरिंदमौ गच्छ त्वं भ्रातरौ गृह्य किष्किन्धां रामलक्ष्मणौ ॥
en: Do you along with numbers of heroic monkeys, taking those repressors of foes, the brothers-Rama and Laksmana-when they shall have regained their consciousness, repair to Kiskindha.

sn: अहं तु रावणं हत्वा सपुत्रं सहबान्धवम्। मैथिलीमानयिष्यामि शक्रो नष्टामिव श्रियम्॥
en: And I, slaying Råvaņa along with his sons and friends, shall bring back Mithila's daughter, even as Sakra recovered the lost Sri.

sn: श्रुत्वैतद्वानरेन्द्रस्य सुषेणो वाक्यमब्रवीत्। देवासुरं महायुद्धमनुभूतं पुरातनम् ॥
en: Hearing the words of the monkey-king, Suşeņa said, I had witnessed the war of yore between the gods and the Asuras.

sn: तदा स्म दानवा देवाशरसंस्पर्शकोविदान्। निजघ्नुः शस्त्रविदुषश्छादयन्तो मुहुर्मुहुः॥
en: Then the Dänavas, enveloping themselves, momentarily destroyed the deities, albeit versed in arms and accomplished in weapons.

sn: तानानिष्टसंज्ञांश्च गतासुंश्च बृहस्पतिः। विद्याभिर्मन्त्रयुक्ताभिरोषधीभिश्चिकित्सति ॥
en: They, their senses lost, and their lives departed, Bịhaspati treated by means of his knowledge of mantras, as well with medicines.

sn: तान्यौषधान्यानयितुं क्षीरोदं यान्तु सागरम्। जवेन वानराः शीघ्रं संपातिपनसादयः॥
en: Let Sampati, Panasa, and other monkeys speedily hie to the Milky Ocean for the purpose of bringing those medicines.

sn: हरयस्तु विजानन्ति पार्वती ते महौषधी। संजीवकरणी दिव्यां विशल्यां देवनिर्मिताम्॥
en: The monkeys well know that mighty mountainous medicine-divine and capable of reviving the dead, and made by the deities themselves-visalya.

sn: चन्द्रश्च नाम द्रोणश्च क्षीरोदे सागरोत्तमे। अमृतं यत्र मथितं तत्र ते परमौषधी॥ तौ तत्र विहितौ देवैः पर्वतौ तौ महोदधौ। अयं वायुसुतो राजन्हनूमांस्तत्र गच्छतु।॥
en: There are (the mountains) named Candra and Drona: where the ambrosia was churned, there is that supreme drug. And those mountains have been placed by the deities in the mighty deep. And, o king, let the son of the Wing-god go thither.

sn: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे वायुर्मेघाश्चापि सविद्युतः। पर्यस्य सागरे तोयं कम्पयन्निव पर्वतान्॥
en: In the meanwhile, the wing arose, and masses of clouds appeared along with lightning, and the wind blew, agitating the waters of the deep, and shaking the mountains.

sn: महता पक्षवातेन सर्वद्वीपमहाद्रुमाः। निपेतुर्भग्नविटपाः सलिले लवणाम्भसि ॥
en: And mighty trees of the ocean-islands, broken down by-the terrible wing-raised wind, began to topple headlong into the salt waters.

sn: अभवन्पन्नगास्त्रस्ता भोगिनस्तत्रवासिनः। शीघ्रं सर्वाणि यादांसि जग्मुश्च लवणार्णवम्॥
en: The serpents dwelling there were seized with affright; and speedily all the aquatic animals dived into the Salt sea,

sn: ततो मुहूर्ताद् गरुडं वैनतेयं महाबलम्। वानरा ददृशुः सर्वे ज्वलन्तमिव पावकम्॥
en: Then in a moment the monkeys saw Vinatā's son possessed of terrific strength, like to a flaming fire.

sn: तमागतमभिप्रेक्ष्य नागास्ते विप्रदुद्रुवुः। यैस्तु तौ पुरुषौ बद्धौ शरभूतैर्महाबलैः॥
en: Seeing him come, the serpents began to dart away, those exceedingly powerful ones that, turning into shafts, had bound those persons.* *Rama and Laksmana.

sn: ततः सुपर्णः काकुत्स्थौ स्पृष्ट्वा प्रत्यभिनन्द्य च। विममर्श च पाणिभ्यां मुखे चन्द्रसमप्रभे॥
en: Then, touching the Kākutsthas and saluting them, Suparna rubbed with his hands their countenances furnished with the splendour of the Moon.

sn: वैनतेयेन संस्पृष्टास्तयोः संरुरुहुव्रणाः। सुवर्णे च तनू स्निग्धे तयोराशु बभूवतुः॥
en: Their wounds, on being touched by Vinata's son, were (immediately) healed: and the bodies of both speedily became cool and shone with an excellent complexion.

sn: तेजो वीर्यं बलं चौज उत्साहश्च महागुणाः। प्रदर्शनं च बुद्धिश्च स्मृतिश्च द्विगुणा तयोः॥
en: They attained immense energy and prowess; and a double share of strength, and of rational and perceptive powers, and of memory.

sn: तावुत्थाप्य महातेजा गरुडो वासवोपमौ। उभौ च सस्वजे हृष्टो रामश्चैनमुवाच ह॥
en: Then raising them up, the exceedingly energetic Garuda, resembling Vāşava himself, embraced both joyfully. And then Rāma addressed (Garuda), saying.

sn: भवत्प्रसादाद्व्यसनं रावणिप्रभवं महत्। उपायेन व्यतिक्रान्तौ शीघ्रं च बलिनौ कृतौ।॥
en: By your grace we have through means survived the mighty calamity that had sprung from Răvana's son; and we have also speedily been rendered strong.

sn: यथा तातं दशरथं यथाजं च पितामहम्। तथा भवन्तमासाद्य हृदयं मे प्रसीदति।॥
en: My heart is delighted on having these, like to my father, Dasaratha, or my grand sire, Aja.

sn: को भवानरूपसंपन्नो दिव्यस्त्रगनुलेपनः। वसानो विरजे वस्त्रे दिव्याभरणभूषितः॥
en: Who are your, furnished with beauty, and bearing wreaths and unguents (on your person); clad in stainless attire: and adorned in noble ornaments ?

sn: ते तमुवाच महातेजा वैनतेयो महाबलः। पतत्रिराजः प्रीतात्मा हर्षपर्याकुलेक्षणम्॥
en: To him spoke the exceedingly energetic son of Vinată endowed with great strength, the lord of birds, with a pleased heart, and his eyes wild with glee.

sn: अहं सखा काकुत्स्थः प्रियः प्राणो बहिश्चरः। गरुत्मानिह संप्राप्तो युवयोः साह्यकारणात्॥
en: O Kakutstha, I am your friend-your life ranging externally-Garutmän. I am come hither for aiding you.

sn: असुरा वा महावीर्या वानरा वा महाबलाः। सुराश्चापि सगन्धर्वाः पुरस्कृत्य शतक्रतुम्॥ नेमं मोक्षयितुं शक्काः शरबन्धं सुदारुणम्। मायाबलादिन्द्रजिता निर्मितं क्रूरकर्मणा ॥ एते नागाः काद्रवेयास्तीक्ष्णदंष्ट्रा विषोल्बणाः। रक्षोमायाप्रभावेण शरभूतास्त्वदाश्रयाः॥
en: Neither the highly powerful Asuras, nor the exceedingly strong monkeys, nor the celestials along with the Gandharvas, having him of an hundred sacrifices at their head are, capable of delivering (any one) from these dreadful arrowy bonds, which had been forged by Indrajit of tortous deeds by help of illusion. These serpentsoffspring of Kadru-are sharp-fanged and venomous; and had bound you as arrows through the potency of illusion.

sn: सभाग्यश्चासि धर्मज्ञ राम सत्यपराक्रम। लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्रात्रा समरे रिपुषातिना॥
en: O Ráma having truth for prowess, you are fortunate-along with that destroyer of foe in fight, Laksmana.

sn: इमं श्रुत्वा तु विक्रान्तस्त्वरमाणोऽहमागतः। सहसैवावयोः स्नेहात्सखित्वमनुपालयन्॥ मोक्षितौ च महाघोरादस्मात्सायकबन्धनात्।
en: Hearing this, I, summoning energy: have come hither swiftly, and I, doing by you as a friend, have from affection at once set you free from these dreadful arrowy bonds.

sn: अप्रमादश्च कर्तव्यो युवाभ्यां नित्यमेव हि ॥ प्रकृत्या राक्षसाः सर्वे संग्रामे कूटयोधिनः। शूराणां शुद्धभावानां भवतामार्जवं बलम्॥
en: you should always be on your guard. By nature the Rākşasas have cunning shifts in fight and you, who are heroic and of a pure spirit, can but rely on your simplicity alone for strength.

sn: तन्न विश्वसनीयं वो राक्षसानां रणाजिरे। एतेनैवोपमानेन नित्यं जिह्मा हि राक्षसाः॥
en: Therefore you must not trust the Raksasas in the field of battle. By this one instance you must know that Rakşasas are ever deceitful in fight.

sn: एवमुक्त्वा तदा रामं सुपर्णः स महाबलः। परिष्वज्य च सुस्निग्धमाप्रष्टमुपचक्रमे॥
en: Having said this the wondrous mighty Suparna, embracing Rama tenderly again) said.

sn: सखे राघव धर्मज्ञ रिपूणामपि वत्सल। अभ्युनुज्ञातुमिच्छामि गमिष्यामि यथासुखम् ॥ न च कौतूहलं कार्य सखित्वं प्रति कांक्षिणाः। कृतकारणे वीर सखित्वं प्रतिवेत्स्यसि॥
en: My friend Raghava, O you who even cherish affection for your foes, permit me, I shall go at pleasure. And O Raghva, entertain no curiosity as to our friendship. when, O hero, you shall have achieved success in battle, you shall know all about this friendship of ours.

sn: बालवृद्धावशेषां तु लङ्कां कृत्वा शरोमिभिः। रावणं तु रिपुं हत्वा सीतां त्वपमुलप्स्यसे॥
en: And with the surges of your shafts, making Larkā contain only children and aged, and slaying your foe, Ravana, you shall recover Sita.

sn: इत्येवमुक्त्वा वचनं सुपर्णः शीघ्रविक्रमः। रामं च नीरुनं कृत्वा मध्ये तेषां वनौकसाम्॥ प्रदक्षिणं ततः कृत्वा परिष्वज्य च वीर्यवान्। जगामाकाशमाविश्य सुपर्णः पवनो यथा।६।।
en: Having spoken thus, Suparna, endowed with vigour, having rendered Rāma hale in the midst of the monkeys, having gone round them and embrace them also, that one possessed of prowess, set out, covering up the sky, like to the wind.

sn: नीरुजौ राघवौ दृष्ट्वा ततो वानरयूथपाः। सिंहनादं तदा नेदुर्लाङ्गलं दुधुवुश्च ते॥
en: Seeing Raghu's sons rendered hale, the monkey-leaders set up leonine roars, and began to flourish their tails.

sn: ततो भेरी: समाजघ्नुर्मृदङ्गाश्चाप्यवादयन्। दध्मुः शङ्खान्संप्रहृष्टा श्वेलन्त्यपि यथापुरम्॥
en: Then beat the kettle-drums and the drums struck up. And conchs were cheerfully blown; and shouts were sent.

sn: अपरे स्फोट्य विक्रान्ता वानरा नगयोधिनः। दुमानुत्पाट्य विविधांस्तस्थुः शतसहस्रशः॥ विसृजन्तो महानादांस्त्रासयन्तो निशाचरान्। लङ्काद्वाराण्युपाजग्मुर्युद्धकामाः प्लवंगमाः॥
en: And others struck at their arms with their hands. The monkeys, accustomed to battle with trees, uprooting them, stood by hundreds and thousands. And emitting tremendous roars and thereby frightening the night-rangers, the monkeys eager for encounter, approached the gate of Lanka.

sn: तेषां सुभीमस्तुमुलो निनादो बभूव शाखामृगयूथपानाम्। क्षये निदाघस्य यथा घनानां नादः सुभीमो नदतां निशीथे॥
en: That mighty and dreadful din raised by the monkeys, resembled the terrible rumbling of the clouds at midnight about the end of Summer.

sn: तेषां तु तुमुलं शब्दं वानराणां महौजसाम्। नर्दतां राक्षसैः सार्धं तदा शुश्राव रावणः॥
en: Then Rāvana heard the tumult raised by the highly energetic monkeys roaring in company with the Rākşasas.

sn: स्निग्धगम्भीरनिर्घोषं श्रुत्वा तं निनदं भृशम्। सचिवानां ततस्तेषां मध्ये वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Hearing that low and solemn noise-that prodigious uproar-Rävaņa said in the midst of his counsellors.

sn: यथासौ संप्रहृष्टानां वानराणामुपस्थितः। बहूनां सुगहानादो मेघानामिव गर्जताम्॥ सुव्यक्तं महती प्रीतिरेतेषां नात्र संशयः। तथा हि विपुलैनदैिश्चुर्भे लवणार्णवः॥
en: From mighty roars that are heard of in innumerous delighted monkeys, resembling the roar of couds, it is evident, beyond a doubt, that there is great rejoicing there. And the salt Ocean is vexed with these thundering noises.

sn: तौ तु बद्धौ शरैस्तीक्ष्णैभ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ। अयं च सुमहानादः शङ्कां जनयतीव मे॥
en: The brother-Rama and Laksmana-have been fast bound with sharp shafts, and here this uproar is exciting my alarm.

sn: एवं च वचनं चोक्त्वा मन्त्रिणो राक्षसेश्वरः। उवाच नैर्ऋतांस्तत्र समीपपरिवर्तिनः॥
en: Having spoken thus to his ministers, the lord of the Rākşasas addressed the Naiſtas present there, saying.

sn: ज्ञायतां तूर्णमेतेषां सर्वेषां च वनौकसाम्। शोककाले समुत्पन्ने हर्षकारणमुत्थितम्॥
en: Do you speedily acquaint yourselves with the cause of rejoicing that has arisen of these monkeys on this mournful occasion.

sn: तथोक्तास्ते सुसंभ्रान्ताः प्राकारमधिरुह्य च। ददृशुः पालितां सेनां सुग्रीवेण महात्मना॥ तौ च मुक्तौ सुधोरेण शरबन्धेन राघवौ। समुत्थितौ महाभागौ विषेदुः सर्वराक्षसाः॥
en: Thus accosted, they hurriedly mounting up on the wall, surveyed the forces maintained by the high-souled Sugrīva as well as those exalted ones-Raghu's sons-emancipated from their terrific arrowy fetters and arisen (now).

sn: संत्रस्तहृदयाः सर्वे प्राकारादवरुह्यते। विवर्णा राक्षसा घोरा राक्षसेन्द्रमुपस्थिताः॥
en: Thereat, with their hearts wrought up, grimvisaged Rākşasas descending from the wall appeared before the Rākşasa-lord with pale faces.

sn: तदप्रियं दीनमुखा रावणस्य च राक्षसाः। कृत्स्नं निवेदयामासुर्यथावद्वाक्यकोविदाः॥
en: Then with woe-begone faces, those Raksasas, skilled in speech, faithfully informed Rāvana in full of that unfortunate circumstance.

sn: यौ ताविन्द्रजिता युद्धे भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ। निबद्धौ शरबन्धेन निष्प्रकम्पभुजौ कृतौ॥ विमुक्तौ शरबन्धेन दृश्येते तौ रणाजिरे। पाशानिव गजौ छित्त्वा गजेन्द्रसमविक्रमौ॥
