en: Those brothers-Rāma and Lakşmaņa-who had in battle been bound up in arrowy fetters by Indrajit, and whose arms lay moveless, having been emancipated from the arrowy bonds, are seen in the field of battle; and those ones like to the foremost of elephants in strength, seem like elephants that have snapped their fetters.

sn: तच्छुत्वा वचनं तेषां राक्षसेन्द्रो महाबलः। चिन्तारोषसमाक्रान्तो विवर्णवदनोऽभवत्॥
en: Hearing those words of theirs, the exceedingly powerful lord of the Raksasas was wrought up with anxiety and anger, and his countenance lost its complexion.

sn: घोरैर्दत्तवरैर्बद्धौ शरैराशीविषोपमैः। अमोघैः सूर्यसंकाशैः प्रमध्येन्द्रजिता युधि ॥ तदनबन्धमासाद्य यदि मुक्तौ रिपू मम। संशयस्थमिदं सर्वमनुपश्याम्यहं बलम्॥
en: Indrajit, having routed them in conflict, had bound them by means of irresistible and terrible arrows, resembling venomous serpents, and like to the Sun himself, which had been conferred on (Indrajit) as boons. But if my enemy having actually been bound by the weapons, can have been liberated, all this strength of mine I see placed in peril.

sn: निष्फलाः खलु संवृत्ताः शराः पावकतेजसः। आदत्तं यैस्तु सङ्ग्रामे रिपूणां जीवितं मम॥
en: And those shafts resembling Fire in fierceness, which had in battle deprived my foes of their lives, have forsooth been rendered fruitless.

sn: एवमुक्त्वा तु संक्रुद्धो निःश्वसन्नुरगो यथा। अब्रवीद्रक्षसां मध्ये धूम्राक्षं नाम राक्षसम्॥
en: Having said this in high rage Rāvana, sighing like a serpent, addressed a Raksasa, named Dhūmrākṣa, seated in the midst of the Rākşasa.

sn: बलेन महता युक्तो राक्षसैर्भीमविक्रमः। त्वं वधायाशु निर्याहि रामस्य सह वानरैः॥
en: O you of dreadful prowess, surrounded by a mighty force, do you march forth to compass the destruction of Rāma along with the monkeys.

sn: एवमुक्तस्तु धूम्राक्षो राक्षसेन्द्रेण धीमता परिक्रम्य ततः शीघ्रं निर्जगाम नृपालयात्॥
en: Thus accosted by the intelligent lord of the Raksasas, Dhumraksa, turning about, issued out of the abode of the king.

sn: अभिनिष्क्रम्य तद्द्वारं बलाध्यक्षमुवाच ह। त्वरयस्व बलं शीघ्रं किं चिरेण युयुत्सतः॥
en: And speedily sallying forth from the gate of (Ravana's residence, he said to the general of the forces, “Do you speedily move off your forces. why should a warrior linger?”

sn: धूम्राक्षवचनं श्रुत्वा बलाध्यक्षो बलानुगः। बलमुद्योजयामास रावणस्याज्ञया भृशम्॥
en: Hearing Dhumraksa's words, the general of the forces, following them, at the command of Rāvaņa forthwith made the army ready.

sn: ते बद्धघण्टा बलिनो घोररूपा निशाचराः। विनद्यमानाः संहृष्टा धूम्राक्षं पर्यवारयन्॥
en: And those powerful and dreadful nightrangers, bursting with high spirits, with bells tied to their arms, set up shouts, and surrounded Dhumraksa.

sn: विविधायुधहस्ताश्च शूलमुद्गरपाणयः। गदाभिः पट्टिशैर्दण्डैरायसैर्मुसलैरपि॥ परिधैर्भिन्दिपालैश्च भल्लैः पाशैः परश्वधैः। निर्ययू राक्षसा घोरा नर्दन्तो जलदा यथा॥
en: And bearing various weapons in their hands, and wielding darts and clubs, and equipped with maces and bearded darts and rods and iron bludgeons and parighas and bhindipālas and lances and nooses and axes, those terrific Rāks asas sallied out roaring like to clouds.

sn: रथैः कवचिनस्त्वन्ये ध्वजैश्च समलंकृतैः। सुवर्णजालविहितैः खरैश्च विविधाननैः॥ हयैः परमशीघेश्च गजैश्चैव मदोत्कटैः। निर्ययुनैर्ऋतव्याघ्रा व्याघ्रा इव दुरासदाः॥
en: And others, accoutred in armour, with cars; adorned with banners; furnished with golden networks, and mules having various faces, and extremely swift steeds, and lusty elephants in rut, tiger-like Naiſtas incapable of being subdued even as tigers-sallied out (thereafter).

sn: मृगसिंहमुखैर्युक्तं खरैः कनकभूषितैः। आरुरोह रथं दिव्यं धूम्राक्षः खरनिःस्वनः॥
en: Then Dhūmrākṣa himself ascended a superb car, bearing faces of deer and lions decked with gold, and sending forth a loud clatter.

sn: स निर्यातो महावीर्यो धूम्राक्षो राक्षसैर्वृतः। हसन्वै पश्चिमद्वाराद्धनूमान्यत्र तिष्ठति॥
en: The highly powerful Dhūmrākşa, surrounded by Rākşasas, cheerfully issued out of the Western Entrance, where Hanumān was posted.

sn: रथप्रवरमास्थाय खरयुक्तं खरस्वनम्। प्रयान्तं तु महाघोरं राक्षसं भीमदर्शनम्॥ अन्तरिक्षगताः क्रूराः शकुनाः प्रत्यषेधयन्।
en: Thereat, fell fowls of the air forbade that exceedingly dreadful Räksasa of a fearful form, as he went out ascending an excellent car joked with mules, and sending sharp sounds.

sn: रथशीर्षे महाभीमो गृध्रश्च निपपात ह॥ ध्वजाग्रे ग्रथिताश्चैव निपेतुः कुणपाशनाः। रुधिराो महाश्वेतः कबन्धः पतितो भुवि॥
en: And an exceedingly terrific vulture alighted at the crest of the car and forming themselves into lines, vultures began to drop down about the top of the banner. And emitting a frightful cry, (a headless trunk) dropped down before Dhumraksa.

sn: विस्वरं चोत्सृजन्नादान्धूम्राक्षस्य निपातितः। ववर्ष रुधिरं देवः संचचाल च मेदिनी॥ प्रतिलोमं ववौ वायुनिर्घातसमनिःस्वनः। तिमिरौघवृतास्तत्र दिशश्च न चकाशिरे॥
en: That god* showered down blood; and the earth shook. And the wind blew awry with a sound resembling thunder. And every side, covered with darkness, appeared dim. *Indra-cloud compeller.

sn: स तूत्पातांस्ततो दृष्ट्वा राक्षसानां भयावहान्। प्रादुर्भूतान्सुघोरांश्च धूम्राक्षो व्यथितोऽभवत्।। मुमुहू राक्षसाः सर्वे धूम्राक्षस्य पुरःसराः॥
en: And witnessing those dreadful inauspicious omens at the outset, fraught with fear to the Räkşasas, Dhūmrākṣa was greatly aggrieved; and the Räksaşas marching before him, were stupefied.

sn: वृतोभिनिष्क्रम्य रणोत्सुको बली। ददर्श तां राघवबाहुपालितां महौघकल्पां बहु वानरी चमूम्॥
en: Then as that strong and fearful one, eager for encounter, surrounded by in numerable nigh rangers, issued out (of the city), he beheld that monkey-host, protected by the arm of Rāghava, resembling the deep at the time of universal dissolution.

sn: धूम्राक्षं प्रेक्ष्य निर्यान्तं राक्षसं भीमविक्रमम्। विनेदुर्वानराः सर्वे प्रहृष्टा युद्धकाङ्गिणः॥
en: Seeing the Rākṣasa-Dhūmrākṣa of dreadful prowess-issue out, the monkeys, rejoicing greatly, eager for encounter, set up roars.

sn: तेषां सुतुमुलं युद्धं संजज्ञे कपिरक्षसाम्। अन्योन्यं पादपैोरैनिघ्नतां शूलमुद्गरैः॥
en: Then there took place a terrific conflict between the monkeys and the Rākşasas, charging each other with fearful trees, and darts, and maces.

sn: राक्षसैर्वानरा घोरा विनिकृत्ताः समन्ततः। वानरै राक्षसाश्चापि दुमैर्भूमिसमीकृताः॥
en: The Rākşasas began to scatter the dreadful monkeys on all sides; and the monkeys (on their parts) felled the Raksasas with trees.

sn: राक्षसास्त्वभिसंक्रुद्धा वानरानिशितैः शरैः। विव्यधु_रसंकाशैः कङ्कपत्रैरजिह्मगैः॥
en: The Raksasas, growing enraged, began to pierce that monkeys with straight speeding sharp shafts winged with Kanka plumes.

sn: ते गदाभिश्च भीमाभिः पट्टिशैः कूटमुद्गरैः। घौरैश्च परिधैश्चिस्त्रिशूलैश्चापि संश्रितैः॥ विदार्यमाणा रक्षोभिर्वानरास्ते महाबलाः। अमर्षजनितोद्धर्षाश्चक्रुः कर्माण्यभीतवत्॥
en: And riven by the Rākşasa with drcadful clubs and bearded darts, daggers and maces and terrible and curious bludgeons and grasped javelins, the exceedingly powerful (monkeys), their anger aroused, began with alacrity to perform deeds of intrepid valour.

sn: शरनिर्भिन्नगात्रास्ते शूलनिर्भिन्नदेहिनः। जगृहुस्ते द्रुमांस्तत्र शिलाश्च हरियूथपाः॥
en: Those monkey-leaders, their bodies pierced with shafts and their persons riven with darts, took up trees and crags.

sn: ते भीमवेगा हरयो नर्दमानास्ततस्ततः। ममन्थुराक्षसान्वीरान्नामानि च बभाषिरे॥
en: Those monkeys, endowed with terrific vehemence, sending up shouts, and proclaiming their respective names, set about tossing the brave Rākşasa rank,

sn: तद्बभूवाद्भुतं घोरं युद्धं वानररक्षसाम्। शिलाभिर्विविधाभिश्च बहुशाखैश्च पादपैः॥
en: The monkeys, waged with diverse rocks and innumerable trees, waxed exceedingly furious.

sn: राक्षसा मथिताः केचिद्वानरैर्जितकाशिभिः। प्रवेमू रुधिरं केचिन्मुखै रुधिरभोजनाः॥
en: Sparkling in the glory of victory, the monkeys crushed the Rākşasas and some among them feeding on gore began to vomit blood.

sn: पार्श्वेषु दारिताः केचित्केचिद्राशीकृता दुमैः। शिलाभिश्चूर्णिताः केचित्केचिद्दन्तैर्विदारिताः॥
en: And some were severed along their flanks; and, some, slain with trees, were heaped up; and some were crushed with crags; and some were torn with teeth.

sn: ध्वजैविमथितैर्भग्नैः खङ्गैश्च विनिपातितैः। रथैविध्वंसिताः केचिद्व्यथिता रजनीचराः॥
en: Some being broken down by means of broken standards, and some by means of fallen swords, and some crushed down by cars, the rangers of the night suffered sorely.

sn: गजेन्द्रैः पर्वताकारैः पर्वताग्रैर्वनौकसाम्। मथितैर्वाजिभिः कीर्णं सारोहैर्वसुधातलम्॥
en: And (anon) the earth was covered with huge elephants measuring mountains, and mountaintops, and steeds crushed and the riders thereof, all borne down by the monkeys.

sn: वानरैर्भीमविक्रान्तैराप्लुत्योत्प्लुत्य वेगितैः। राक्षसाः करजैस्तीक्ष्णैर्मुखेषु विनिदारिताः॥
en: Bounding again and again, the vehement monkeys endowed with terrific prowess, with their finger-nails tore up the Rākṣasas by the mouths.

sn: विषण्णवदना भूयो विप्रकीर्णशिरोरुहाः। मूढाः शोणितगन्धेन निपेतुर्धरणीतले॥
en: With woebegone faces, and with hair dishevelled, (the Raksasas), stupified with the smell of blood, saught the earth.

sn: अन्ये तु परमक्रुद्धा राक्षसा भीमविक्रमाः। तलैरेवाभिधावन्ति वज्रस्पर्शसमैर्हरीन्॥
en: Other Rākşasas endowed with dreadful vigour, waxing wondrous wroth, dealt the monkeys slaps with hands having the touch of the thunder-bolt.

sn: वानरैः पातयन्तस्ते वेगिता वेगवत्तरैः। मुष्टिभिश्चरणैर्दन्तैः पादपैश्चावपोथिताः॥
en: Gift with greater impetuosity, the monkeys felled the impetuous (Raksasas) with blows, and feet and teeth; and some were slain with trees.

sn: सैन्यं तु विद्रुतं दृष्ट्वा धूम्राक्षो राक्षसर्षभः। रोषेण कदनं चक्रे वानराणां युयुत्सताम्॥
en: Seeing the forces fleeing away, that foremost of Raksasas-Dhumraksa-flying into fury, began a terrific conflict with the monkeys desirous of encounter.

sn: प्रासैः प्रमाथिताः केचिद्वानराः शोणितस्त्रवाः। मुद्गरैराहताः केचित्पतिता धरणीतले॥
en: Some of the monkeys, sore assailed with prāśas, began to bleed; and some, wounded with maces, dropped down to the ground.

sn: परिधैर्मथिताः केचिद्भिन्दिपालैश्च दारिताः। पट्टिशैर्मथिताः केचिद्विह्वलन्तो गतासवः॥
en: Some were beaten hard with bludgeons; and some were cleft with bhindipālas. And some, on being assailed with bearded darts, became insensible and lost their lives.

sn: केचिद्विनिहता भूमौ रुधिरार्दा वनौकसः। केचिद्विद्राविता नष्टाः संक्रुद्धै राक्षसैर्युधि ॥
en: Some among the monkeys lay slain on the ground, drenched in blood. and some, fleeing away from the field, were slaughtered by the infuriated Rākşasas.

sn: विभिन्नहृदयाः केचिदेकपार्श्वेन शायिताः। विदारितास्त्रिशूलैश्च केचिदान्त्रैर्विनिःसृताः॥
en: Some, having their breasts pierced, lay on their sides. and some were riven with tridents; and the entrails of some had come out.

sn: तत्सुभीमं महाद्धं हरिराक्षससंकुलम्। प्रबभौ शस्त्रबहुलं शिलापादपसंकुलम्॥
en: That mighty and dreadful encounter of the Räksasas and the monkeys, was waged with countless weapons and rocks and trees.

sn: धनुातन्त्रिमधुरं हिमतालसमन्वितम्। मन्दस्तनितगी तं तद्युद्धगान्धर्वमाबभौ॥
en: That battle he come a musical entertainment' mellifluous with bow-string for Vina, having the neighing of chargers for its measure, and with the cries of Maindas' for its strains. 1. The reader has already perceived that the carrying out of a simile to a number of details is a characteristic as much of Vālmīki as of his rival in the epic sphere-Vyāsa, but the comparisons are never on all fours, as in the case before us. 2. A classical Hindu musical instrument, having metallic strings, with a pair of gourds at one end for the sounding-board. Vide Yantra-Kosa by Sir Saurindra Mohan Tagore, Mus-Doc. 3. A species of elephants.

sn: धूम्राक्षस्तु धनुष्पाणिनिरारणमूर्धनि। हसन्विद्रावयामास दिशस्ताञ्छरवृष्टिभिः॥
en: Then in the field, Dhūmrākṣa bow in hand, laughing, pursued the monkeys in all directions with showers of shafts.

sn: धूम्राक्षेणार्दितं सैन्यं व्यथितं प्रेक्ष्य मारुतिः। अभ्यवर्तत संक्रुद्धः प्रगृह्य विपुलां शिलाम्॥
en: Seeing the forces hard beset by Dhūmrākşa and distressed thereat, the Windgod's offspring, waxing enraged, seizing a huge crag, approached (the Rākşasa).

sn: क्रोधाद्द्विगुणताम्राक्षः पितुरतुल्यपराक्रमः। शिलां तां पातयामास धूम्राक्षस्य रथं प्रति॥
en: And with his eyes double reddened in wrath, the one, like to his sire himself in prowess, brought down the crag upon Dhūmrākṣa's car.

sn: आपतन्तीं शिलां दृष्ट्वा गदामुद्यम्य संभ्रमात्। रथादाप्लुत्य वेगेन वसुधायां व्यतिष्ठत॥ सा प्रमथ्य रथं तस्य निपपात शिला भुवि।
en: Seeing the crag, (Dhumraksa) upraising his mace hurriedly, leapt down in vehemence, and stood on the ground. And having shattered his car, that crag fell down to the earth.

sn: सचक्रकूबरमुखं सध्वजं सशरासनम्॥ स त्यक्त्वा तु रथं तस्य हनूमान्मारुतात्मजः। रक्षसां कदनं चक्रे सस्कन्धविटपैर्दुमैः॥
en: Thereat letting go the car furnished with wheels, Kuvaras and a face, as well as a banner; in which Dhūmrākṣa had left his bow, Hanuman-son to the Wind-god-laid about him right lustily for destroying the Rākşasas, with trees having branches long and short.

sn: विभिन्नशिरसो भूत्वा राक्षसा रुधिरोक्षिताः। दुमैः प्रमथिताश्चान्ये निपेतुर्धरणीतले॥
en: Thereat some Rākşasas with their heads shattered, lay drenched in blood; and others, struck with trees, dropped down to the earth.

sn: विद्राव्य राक्षसं सैन्यं हनूमान्मारुतात्मजः। गिरेः शिखरमादाय धूम्राक्षमभिदुद्रुवे॥
en: Then Hanumān-son to the Wind-god-charged in full career against the Räkşasa army; and, taking a mountain-peak, he rushed against Dhumraksa.

sn: तमापतन्तं धूम्राक्षो गदामुद्यम्य वीर्यवान्। विनर्दमानः सहसा हनूमन्तमभिद्रवत्॥
en: As Hanumān was descending, the powerful Dhūmrākşa, upraising a mace and giving out a shout, made towards him speedily.

sn: तस्य क्रुद्धस्य रोषेण गदां तां बहुकण्टकाम्। पातयामास धूम्राक्षो मस्तकेऽथ हनूमतः॥
en: Then Dhūmrākṣa enraged, brought down that mace studded with innumerable pricks, on the head of Hanumān fired with wrath.

sn: ताडितः स तया तत्र गदया भीमवेगया। स कपिर्मारुतबलस्तं प्रहारमचिन्तयन्॥ धूम्राक्षस्य शिरोमध्ये गिरिशृङ्गमपातयत्।
en: Thus assailed with the mace of fearful impetuosity, the monkey endowed with he mace of fearful impetuosity, the monkey endowed with the strength of the wind without at all heeding that blow, let fall a mountain-top right against Dhumraksa's head.

sn: स विस्फारितसर्वाङ्गो गिरिशृङ्गेण ताडितः॥ पपात सहसा भूमौ विकीर्ण इव पर्वतः।
en: On being assailed with the mountain-peak, Dhūmrākşa, having his entire body mangled, suddenly fell to the earth, like to a toppling hill.

sn: धूम्राक्षं निहतं दृष्ट्वा हतशेषा निशाचराः।। त्रस्ताः प्रविविशुर्लङ्कां वध्यमानाः प्लवंगमैः॥
en: Seeing Dhūmrākṣa slain, those night-rangers that survived the carnage, in extreme agitation began to pour into Lankā, attacked by the monkeys.

sn: स तु पवनसुतो निहत्य शत्रून् क्षतजवहाः सरितश्च संविकीर्य। रिपुवधजनितश्रमो महात्मा मुदमगमत्कपिभिः सुपूज्यमानः॥
en: That high-souled offspring of the Wind-god, having slain his foes, and come under the influence of fatigue incident to his slaughtering his enemies, having caused rivers of gore to flow (in the field), experienced the excess of joy on being honoured of the monkeys.

sn: धूम्राक्षं निहतं दृष्ट्वा हतशेषा निशाचराः।। त्रस्ताः प्रविविशुर्लङ्कां वध्यमानाः प्लवंगमैः॥
en: Seeing Dhūmrākṣa slain, those night-rangers that survived the carnage, in extreme agitation began to pour into Lankā, attacked by the monkeys.

sn: स तु पवनसुतो निहत्य शत्रून् क्षतजवहाः सरितश्च संविकीर्य। रिपुवधजनितश्रमो महात्मा मुदमगमत्कपिभिः सुपूज्यमानः॥
en: That high-souled offspring of the Wind-god, having slain his foes, and come under the influence of fatigue incident to his slaughtering his enemies, having caused rivers of gore to flow (in the field), experienced the excess of joy on being honoured of the monkeys.

sn: धूम्राक्षं निहतं श्रुत्वा रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः। क्रोधेन महताविष्टो निःश्वसनुरगो यथा॥
en: Hearing Dhūmrākṣa slain, Rāvana-lord of the Raksasas-overwhelmed with a mighty rage, began to sigh like a serpent.

sn: दीर्घमुष्णं विनिःश्वस्य क्रोधेन कलुषीकृतः। अब्रवीद्राक्षसं क्रूरं वज्रदंष्ट्र महाबलम्॥
en: And collide with passion, and sighing hot for a long time, he addressed a cruel Rākşasa-the exceedingly strong Vajradanșrta. *Lit-the thunder-toothed.

sn: गच्छ त्वं वीर निर्याहि राक्षसैः परिवारितः। जहि दाशरथिं रामं सुग्रीवं वानरैः सह॥
en: Go you, O hero. Go out, environed by the Rākşasa. Slay Daśaratha's son-Rāma and Sugrīva along with the monkeys.

sn: तथेत्युक्त्वा द्रुततरं मायावी राक्षसेश्वरः। निर्जगाम बलैः सार्द्ध बहुभिः परिवारितः॥ नागैरश्वैः खरष्ट्रैः संयुक्तः सुसमाहितः। पताकाध्वजचित्रैश्च बहुभिः समलंकृतः॥
en: Thereupon hastily answering “So be it,” that foremost of the Rákşasas skilled in illusion, marched forth surrounded by many a leader* of armies, furnished with elephants and steeds, mules and camels, with his mind concentrated; and adorned with innumerable variegated flags and banners. *Valai-forces-is interpreted leaders by the commentator.

sn: ततो विचित्रकेयूरमुकुटेन विभूषितः। तनुत्रं च समावृत्य सधनुर्निर्ययौ द्रुतम्॥
en: Then decked out with curious keyūras and a tiara, and wearing armour, he rushed out with his bow in his hand.

sn: पताकालंकृतं दीप्तं तप्तकाञ्चनभूषितम्। रथं प्रदक्षिणं कृत्वा समारोहच्चमूपतिः॥
en: Then going round his flaming vehicle, adorn with pennons and garnished with gold, the king* ascended the same. *Vajradanstra.

sn: ऋष्टिभिस्तोमरैश्चित्रैः श्लक्ष्णैश्च मुसलैरपि। भिन्दिपालैश्च चापैश्च शक्तिभिः पट्टिशैरपि॥ खङ्गैश्चक्रैर्गदाभिश्च निशितैश्च परश्वधैः। पदातयश्च नियन्ति विविधाः शस्त्रपाणयः॥
en: And equipped with slender swords and curious Tomaras and smooth maces and bhindipālas and bows and darts and pattiśa and scimitars and discuses and clubs and sharpened axes, the multiform infantry march bearing arms in their hands.

sn: विचित्रवाससः सर्वे दीप्ता राक्षसपुंगवाः। गजा मदोत्कटाः शूराश्चलन्त इव पर्वताः॥ ते युद्धकुशला रूढास्तोमराङ्कुशपाणिभिः। अन्ये लक्षणसंयुक्ताः शूरारूढा महाबलाः॥
en: All those powerful and flaming Rākşasas wore variegated raiments. And heroic elephants in rut resembling mountains in motion, marched, being led by those well-skilled in battle carrying Tomaras and hooks in their hands. And mighty steeds bearing auspicious marks, marched ridden by heroes.

sn: तद्राक्षसबलं सर्वं विप्रस्थितमशोभत। प्रावृट्काले यथा मेघा नर्दमानाः सविद्युतः॥
en: That entire Rākşasa army. as it marched forth, resemble clouds in summer roaring with lightning.

sn: निःसृता दक्षिणद्वारादङ्गदो यत्र यूथपः। तेषां निष्क्रममाणानामशुभं समजायत ॥
en: And (the Raksasa) sallied forth through the Southern Entrance, where that leader of herdsAngads-was stationed. And as they went out, evil omens appeared.

sn: आकाशाद्विधनात्तीव्रादुल्मुकान्यपतंस्तदा। वमन्तः पावकज्वालाः शिवा घोरा ववाशिरे॥
en: From the cloudless yet fierce sky meteors began to shoot. and throwing up flames from their mouths, dreadful jackals began to emit cries.

sn: व्याहरन्त मृगा घोरा रक्षसां निधनं तदा। समापतन्तो योधास्तु प्रास्खलंस्तत्र दारुणम्॥
en: And frightful beasts betokened the destruction of the Räkşasa in battle. And warriors began to tumble down in an ominous way.

sn: एतानौत्पातिकान्दृष्ट्वा वज्रदंष्ट्रो महाबलः। धैर्यमालम्ब्य तेजस्वी निर्जगाम रणोत्सुकः॥
en: Witnessing these evil omens, the exceedingly powerful and energetic Vajradanșțra, assuming patience, set out, eager for encounter.

sn: तांस्तु विद्रवतो दृष्ट्वा वानरा जितकाशिनः। प्रणेदुः सुमहानादान्दिशः शब्देन पूरयन्॥
en: Seeing them flee away, the monkeys burning for victory, set up tremendous shouts, filling all the ten cardinal points.

sn: ततः प्रवृत्तं तुमुलं हरीणां राक्षसैः सह। घोराणां भीमरूपाणामन्योन्यवधकाक्षिणाम्॥
en: Then there came on a terrific encounter of the monkeys and the Räksasas, dreadful, of terrific deeds, and wishing for each other' death.

sn: निष्पतन्तो महोत्साहा भिन्नदेहशिरोधराः। रुधिरोक्षितसर्वाङ्गा न्यपतन्धरणीतले॥
en: And warriors fraught with high spirits, springing up, dropped down to the earth their bodies and hands riven and all their person bathed in blood.

sn: केचिदन्योन्यमासाद्य शूराः परिघबाहवः। चिक्षिपुर्विविधाशस्त्रान्समरेष्वनिवर्तिनः॥
en: And some approaching each other, with bludgeons in their hands, with turning away from the field, discharged various weapons at each other.

sn: दुमाणां च शिलानां च शस्त्राणां चापि निस्वनः। श्रूयते सुमहांस्तत्र घोरो हृदयभेदनः॥
en: There were heard sounds of trees and rocks and weapons, mighty and dreadful and capable of striking terror into the heart.

sn: रथनेमिस्वनस्तत्र धनुषश्चापि घोरवत्। शङ्खभेरीमृदङ्गानां बभूव तुमुलः स्वनः॥
en: And dreadful and mighty were the sounds of car-weapons, mighty and dreadful and capable of string terror into the heart. And dreadful and mighty were the sounds of car-wheels, and conchs and trumpets and drums.

sn: केचिदस्त्राणि संत्यज्य बाहुयुद्धमकुर्वत । तलैश्च चरणैश्चापि मुष्टिभिश्च दुमैरपि॥ जानुभिश्च हताः केचिद्भग्नदेहाश्च राक्षसाः। शिलाभिश्चूर्णिताः केचिद्वानरैयुद्धदुर्मदैः॥
en: Some, casting off weapons, engaged in a hand to hand combat by means of slaps, and kicks, and bones, and trees. And some Raksasa, having their bodies broken, were killed by means of thighs. And some were crushed with crags by Dänavas invincible in battle.

sn: वज्रदंष्ट्रोऽथ तं दृष्ट्वा रणे वित्रासयन्हरीन्। चचार लोकसंहारे पाशहस्त इवान्तकः॥
en: Vajradanșțra, resembling the noose, handed Destroyer, frightening the monkeys, ranged in that field fatal to people.

sn: बलवन्तोऽस्त्रविदुषो नानाप्रहरणा रणे। जघ्नुर्वानरसैन्यानि राक्षसाः क्रोधमूर्छिताः॥
en: Raksasas, possessed of strength; equipped with various weapons, transported with passion, slew the monkey-forces.

sn: जघ्ने ताराक्षसान्सर्वान्धृष्टो वायुसुतो रणे। क्रोधेन द्विगुणाविष्टः संवर्तक इवानलः॥
en: Then in the conflict the proud Wind-god's son, influenced by twofold wrath, spread havoc among the Rākşasa ranks, like the Fire at the universal dissolution.

sn: ताराक्षसगणान्सर्वान्वृक्षमुद्यम्य वीर्यवान्। अङ्गदः क्रोधताम्राक्षः सिंहः क्षुद्रमृगानिव॥ चकार कदनं घोरं शक्रतुल्यपराक्रमः।
en: The energetic Angada possessed of the prowess of a lion, with his eyes coppery with wrath, upraising a tree, began to spread terrible destruction among the Rākşasa, even as a lion destroys tiny deer.

sn: अङ्गदाभिहतास्तत्र राक्षसा भीमविक्रमाः॥ विभिन्नशिरस: पेतुर्निकृता इव पादपाः।
en: And attacked by Angada there, the Raksasas of dreadful vigour, with their heads riven, fell down like to trees that have been uprooted.

sn: रथैश्चित्रैर्ध्वजैरश्वैः शरीरैर्हरिरक्षसाम्॥ रुधिरौघेण संछन्ना भूमिर्भयकरी तदा। हारकेयूरवस्त्रैश्च छत्रैश्च समलंकृता॥ भूमि ति रणे तत्र शारदीव यथा निशा।
en: The earth became frightful (to behold), being covered with variegated cars and standards and steeds and the bodies of monkeys and of Rāks asas and streams of blood. And adorned with chains, and Keyūras, and attires, and umbrellas, the field of battle looked like an autumnal night.

sn: अङ्गदस्य च वेगेन तद्राक्षसबलं महत्।। प्राकम्पत तदा तत्र पवनेनाम्बुदो यथा॥
en: And agitated by Angada's impetuosity, that mighty army of Rākṣasas began to shake, even as water tremble, moved by the wind.

sn: स्वबलस्य च घातेन अङ्गदस्य बलेन च। राक्षसः क्रोधमाविष्टो वज्रदंष्ट्रो महाबलः॥
en: Finding his own army destroyed by the might of Angada, the exceedingly powerful RäkșasaVajradaistra-was overcome with rage.

sn: विस्फार्य च धनुर्घोरं शक्राशनिसमप्रभम्। वानराणामनीकानि प्राकिरच्छरवृष्टिभिः॥
en: And stretching his dreadful bow of the splendour of Sakra's thunder-bolt, he began to shower shafts among the monkeys-ranks.

sn: राक्षसाश्चापि मुख्यारते रथैश्च समवस्थिताः। नानाप्रहरणाः शूराः प्रायुध्यन्त तदा रणे॥
en: The foremost among the heroic Rākşasas also, stationed on cars, furnished with various arms, warred on in the encounter.

sn: वानराणां च शूरास्तु ते सर्वे प्लवगर्षभाः। अयुध्यन्त शिलाहस्ताः समवेताः समन्ततः॥
en: The heroic monkeys also-foremost of their kind-with rocks in their hands, faught around in united strength.

sn: तत्रायुधसहस्राणि तस्मिन्नायोधने भृशम्। राक्षसाः कपिमुख्येषु पातयांचक्रिरे तदा॥
en: In that conflict, the Rākşasas began to incessantly shower ayutas of arms among the flower of the monkeys-army.

sn: वानराश्चैव रक्षःसु गिरिवृक्षान्महाशिलाः। प्रवीराः पातयामासुर्मत्तवारणसंनिभाः॥
en: The monkeys, pre-eminently valiant, and resembling mad elephants kept showering over the Raksasa mountain-trees and mighty rocks.

sn: शूराणां युध्यमानानां समरेष्वनिवर्तिनाम्। तद्राक्षसगणानां च सुयुद्धं समवर्तत ॥
en: Then took place a hot contest among heroic warring monkeys and Raksasa, eager for encounter.

sn: अभग्नशिरसः केचिच्छिन्नैः पादैश्च बाहुभिः। शस्त्रैरर्दितदेहास्तु रुधिरेण समुक्षिताः॥
en: And some, with their heads unbroken, had their arms and legs torn; and their bodies pierced with weapons, and laved in blood.

sn: हरयो राक्षसाश्चैव शेरते गां समाश्रिताः। कङ्कगृध्रबलाढ्याश्च गोमायुकुलसंकुलाः॥
en: Monkeys and Rākşasas lay down in the field, thronged with numbers of Kankas, and vultures, and swarming with flock of jackals.

sn: कबन्धानि समुत्पेतुर्भीरूणां भीषणानि वै। भुजपाणिशिरश्छिन्नाश्छिन्नकायाश्च भूतले॥
en: Striking affright to the timid, on the earth started up (spectral) headless trunks, with their arms and heads torn, ant their bodies riven all over.

sn: वानरा राक्षसाश्चापि निपेतुस्तत्र भूतले। ततो वानरसैन्येन हन्यमानं निशाचरम्॥ प्राभज्यत बलं सर्वं वज्रदंष्ट्रस्य पश्यतः।
en: Monkeys and Rākşasas began to drop down to the earth. And the army of night-rangers, being sadly handled by the monkey-hosts, broke up at every point in the very sight of Vajradanştra.

sn: राक्षसान्भयवित्रस्तान्हन्यमानान्प्लवंगमैः॥ दृष्ट्वा स रोषताम्राक्षो वज्रदंष्ट्रः प्रतापवान्। प्रविवेश धनुष्पाणिस्त्रासयन्हरिवाहिनीम्॥ शरैर्विदारयामास कङ्कपत्रैरजिह्मगैः। बिभेद वानरांस्तत्र सप्ताष्टौ नव पञ्च च॥ विव्याध परमक्रुद्धो वज्रदंष्ट्रः प्रतापवान्। त्रस्ताः सर्वे हरिगणाः शरैः संकृत्तदेहिनः।
en: Seeing the Rākşasas, distressed with fright and harassed by the monkeys, the powerful Vajradarstra, with his eyes crimsoned with choler, entered the arena, bow in hand, frightening the monkey-forces, and he began to pierce the monkeys with straight-speeding shafts winged with Kanka feathers; and he pierced simultaneously seven, eight, nine, five, monkeys (in the field). and the exceedingly powerful Vajradanștra, transported into a towering passion, began to cleave the hostile ranks.

sn: अङ्गदं संप्रधावन्ति प्रजापतिमिव प्रजाः॥ ततो हरिगणान्भग्नान्दृष्ट्वा वालिसुतस्तदा। क्रोधेन वज्रदंष्ट्र तमुदीक्षन्तमुदैक्षत॥
en: Thereat terrified, the monkeys, with their bodies cut with arrows, rushed towards Angada, like creatures resorting to the Creator. And finding the monkeys ranks disordered, Vāli's son in a range cast his eyes on Vajradaństra, who also was eyeing him.

sn: वज्रदंष्ट्रोऽङ्गदश्चोभौ योयुध्येते परस्परम्। चेरतुः परमक्रुद्धौ हरिमत्तगजाविव॥
en: Vajradarşțra and Angada faught fiercely with each other over and over again; ranging the field like a tiger and a mad elephant.

sn: ततः शतसहस्रेण हरिपुत्रं महाबलम्। जघान मर्मदेशेषु शरैरग्निशिखोपमैः॥
en: Then (Vajradanstra) with hundreds and thousands of shafts) resembling tongues of flames, pierced the powerful son of the monkey in the vitals.

sn: रुधिरोक्षितसर्वाङ्गो वालिसूनुर्महाबलः। चिक्षेप वज्रदंष्ट्राय वृक्ष भीमपराक्रमः॥
en: Thereupon Vāli's son of mighty strength and tremendous prowess, with his body covered all over with blood, hurled a free at Vajradanstra.

sn: दृष्ट्वा पतन्तं तं वृक्षमसंभ्रान्तश्च राक्षसः। चिच्छेद बहुधा सोऽपि मथितः प्रापतद्भुवि ॥
en: Seeing the tree in full career, the Räksasa without betraying any agitation, severed it in pieces; and the tree, thus assailed, fell to the earth.

sn: तं दृष्ट्वा वज्रदंष्ट्रस्य विक्रमं प्लवगर्षभः। प्रगृह्य विपुलं शैलं चिक्षेप च ननाद च॥
en: Seeing that feat of Vajradanșra, that foremost of monkeys taking up a huge crag, hurled it (at his foe) and sent up shouts.

sn: तमापतन्तं दृष्ट्वा स रथादाप्लुत्य वीर्यवान्। गदापाणिरसंभ्रान्तः पृथिव्यां समतिष्ठत॥
en: Seeing this descend upon him, that powerful one, calmly leaping down from his vehicle, stood on his feet on the ground.

sn: अङ्गदेन शिला क्षिप्ता गत्वा तु रणमूर्धनि । सचक्रकूबरं साश्वं प्रममाथ रथं तदा॥
en: The crag discharged by Angada, coursing on in the field, dashed to pieces the car along with the wheels and the Kuvara as well as the horses.

sn: ततोऽन्यच्छिखरं गृह्य विपुलं दुमभूषितम्। वज्रदंष्ट्रस्य शिरसि पातयामास वानरः॥
en: Then the the monkey, taking up another prodigious peak crowned with trees, let it alight on Varradanstra's head.

sn: अभवच्छोणितोद्गारी वज्रदंष्ट्रः सुमूर्छितः। मुहूर्तमभवन्मूढो गदामालिङ्ग्य निःश्वसन्॥
en: Thereat vomiting blood, Vajradanstra, deprived of his senses, fro a moment overcome with stupor, stood embracing his mace, sighing.

sn: स लब्धसंज्ञो गदया वालिपुत्रमवस्थितम्। जघान परमक्रुद्धो वक्षोदेशे निशाचरः॥
en: Then the night-ranger, recovering his senses, with his mace in high rage hit at the breast Vāli's son staying in the field.

sn: गदां त्यक्त्वा ततस्तत्र मुष्टियुद्धमकुर्वत । अन्योन्यं जघ्नतुस्तत्र तावुभौ हरिराक्षसौ॥ रुधिरोद्गारिणौ तौ तु प्रहारैर्जनितश्रमौ। बभूवतुः सुविक्रान्तावङ्गारकबुधाविव॥
en: Thereupon, giving up his mace, he entered into a boxing encounter (with Angada). And hitting each other there, they both-the monkey and the Rākṣasa, richly with prowess, appeared like Angāraka and Budha.

sn: ततः परमतेजस्वी अङ्गदः प्लवगर्षभः। उत्पाट्य वृक्षं स्थितवानासीत्पुष्पफलैर्युतः॥
en: Then the exceedingly energetic Angada-best of-monkeys-uprooting a tree, stood there, covered with flowers and leaves.

sn: जग्राह चार्षभं चर्म खङ्गं च विपुलं शुभम्। किङ्किणीजालसंछन्नं चर्मणा च परिष्कृतम्॥
en: And (Vajradanștra) took a shield composed of ass's hid, and a sword broad and sightly, covered with bells, and graced with a leathern sheath. *What could this weapon be like?

sn: चित्रांश्च रुचिरान्मार्गाश्चेरतुः कपिराक्षसौ। जघ्नतुश्च तदान्योन्यं नर्दन्तौ जयकाङ्गिणौ॥
en: The monkey and the Rākşasa displayed curious and graceful movements. And attacking each other, they gave shouts eager for victory.

sn: व्रणैः समुत्थैः शोभेतां पुष्पिताविव किंशुकौ। युध्यमानौ परिश्रान्तौ जानुभ्यामवनीं गतौ॥
en: And with blooding flowing from their wounds, they looked beautiful like blossoming Kinsukas. And warring, both, overcome with fatigue, went to the ground on their knees.

sn: निमेषान्तरमात्रेण अङ्गदः कपिकुञ्जरः। उदतिष्ठत दीप्ताक्षो दण्डाहत इवोरगः॥
en: Anon in the twinkling of an eye, that powerful monkey-Angada-started up, with his eyes glowing, like to a serpent that has been smitten with a rod.

sn: निर्मलेन सुधौतेन खङ्गेनास्य महच्छिरः। जघान वज्रदंष्ट्रस्य वालिसूनुर्महाबलः॥
en: And (at length) with his stainless and sharpened sword, Vali's son, endued with exceeding strength severed Vajradaństra's huge head.

sn: रुधिरोक्षितगात्रस्य बभूव पतितं द्विधा। तच्च तस्य परीताक्षं शुभं खङ्गहतं शिरः॥
en: The graceful head of the one having his body covered with blood, cut off by the sword, falling to the ground with its eyes rolling, was severed in twain.

sn: वज्रदंष्ट्रं हतं दृष्ट्वा राक्षसा भयमोहिताः। त्रस्ता ह्यभ्यद्रवल्लंङ्कां वध्यमानाः प्लवंगमैः।। विषण्णवदना दीना ह्रिया किंचिदवाङ्मुखाः॥
en: Seeing Vajradanştra slain, the Rākşasas, overwhelmed with fear and exceedingly agitated, in pitiful plight, with woe-begone faces and heads hung in shame, fled towards Lankā, attacked (all the while) by the monkeys.

sn: निहत्य तं वज्रधरः प्रतापवान् स वालिसूनुः कपिसैन्यमध्ये। जगाम हर्ष महितो महाबलः सहस्रनेत्रस्त्रिदशैरिवावृतः॥
en: Having compassed Vajradanstra's destruction, the powerful son of Vali, endowed with exceeding strength, in the midst of the monkeyarmy experienced great joy on being honoured by the monkeys, like the wielder of the thunderbolt the thousand-eyed (Deity) surrounded by the celestials.

sn: वज्रदंष्ट्र हतं श्रुत्वा वालिपुत्रेण रावणः। बलाध्यक्षमुवाचेदं कृताञ्जलिमुपस्थितम्॥
en: Hearing Vajradanștra slain by the son of Vāli, Rāvaņa said to the general of his forces, standing before him with joined hands,

sn: शीघ्रं निर्यान्तु दुर्धर्षा राक्षसा भीमविक्रमाः। अकम्पनं पुरस्कृत्य सर्वशस्त्रास्त्रकोविदम्॥
en: Let invincible Rākşasas of dreadful prowess, march forth, placing before them Akampana, skilled in all weapons and arms.

sn: एष शास्ता च गोप्ता च नेता च युधि सत्तमः। भूतिकामश्च मे नित्यं नित्यं च समरप्रियः॥
en: He is capable of chastising foes as well as of protecting his own and leading them; and he is excellent in warfare. And he is always desirous of my prosperity, and always love warfare.

sn: एष जेष्यति काकुत्स्थौ सुग्रीवं च महाबलम्। वानरांश्चापरान्धोरान्हनिष्यति न संशयः॥
en: He will conquer the Kākutsthas, as well as sugrīva endowed with exceeding strength, and, without doubt, slay all the other dreadful monkeys.

sn: परिगृह्य स तमाज्ञां रावणस्य महाबलः। बलं संप्रेषयामास तदा लघुपराक्रमः॥
en: Taking Rāvana's command, that highly powerful one endowed with fleet vigour, marshalled those forces.

sn: ततो नानाप्रहरणा भीमाक्षा भीमदर्शनाः। निष्पेतू राक्षसा मुख्या बलाध्यक्षप्रचोदिताः॥
en: Then equipped with various arms, the foremost of Rākşasas, having dreadful eyes (in their heads, and of dreadful forms, marched forth, urged on by their general.

sn: रथमास्थाय विपुलं तप्तकाञ्चनभूषणम्। मेघाभो मेघवर्णश्च मेघस्वनमहास्वनः॥ राक्षसैः संवृतो घोरैस्तदा निर्यात्यकम्पनः।
en: Ascending a large car, adorned with burnished gold, Akampana, possessed of the splendour of clouds,* and cloud-hued, and furnished with a voice resembling the roar of clouds, went out, environed by Rākașasas of terrific forms. *There is a pun here on the word Akampana-lit.one incapable of being shaken.

sn: नहि कम्पयितुं शक्यः सुरैरपि महामृधे।।।।। अकम्पनस्ततस्तेषामादित्य इव तेजसा।
en: Akampana, resembling the sun in power, was incapable of being shaken in fight by the very gods, and of being beheld by them. 1. Possessed of a person measuring, according to the commentator, a mass of clouds. I give the apparent sense, which answers. 2. Monkeys.

sn: तस्य निर्धावमानस्य संरब्धस्य युयुत्सया॥ अकस्मादैन्यमागच्छद्धयानां रथवाहिनाम्।
en: And as, burning for battle, he rushed out in wrath, the steeds drawing his car suddenly lost their energy.

sn: विस्फुरन्नयनं चास्य सव्यं युद्धाभिनन्दिनः॥ विवर्णो मुखवर्णश्च गद्गदश्चाभवत्स्वनः।
en: The left eye of that one delighting in encounter, began to throb. And his continence grew pale, and his voice faltered.

sn: अभवत्सुदिने काले दुर्दिनं रूक्षमारुतम्॥ ऊचुः खगमृगाः सर्वे वाचः क्रूरा भयावहाः।
en: In a fair day, it looked foul with the wind breathing roughly. And fierce and frightful beasts and birds began to emit cries.

sn: सिंहोपचितस्कन्धः शार्दूलसमविक्रमः॥ तानुत्पातानचिन्त्यैव निर्जगाम रणाजिरम्।
en: That lion-shouldered one like a tiger in prowess, without heeding these ominous occurrences, marched forth into the field.

sn: तथा निर्गच्छतस्तस्य रक्षसः सह राक्षसैः॥ बभूव सुमहानादः क्षोभयन्निव सागरम्।
en: As that Rākşasa was setting out along with the Rākṣasas, he set up mighty roars as if agitating the deep.

sn: तेन शब्देन वित्रस्ता वानराणां महाचमूः॥ दुमशैलप्रहाराणां योद्धं समुपतिष्ठताम्। तेषां युद्धं महारौद्रं संजज्ञे कपिरक्षसाम्॥ रामरावणयोरर्थे समभित्यक्तदेहिनः । सर्वे ह्यतिबलाः शूराः सर्वे पर्वतसंनिभाः॥
en: The mighty army of monkeys was seized with trepidation at that sound. And then there took place a mighty encounter of the Rākṣasas and the monkeys equipped staying in fight with trees and rocks, who had given up all concern for their selves in behalf of Rāma and Rävaņa.

sn: हरयो राक्षसाश्चैव परस्परजिघांसया। तेषां विनर्दतां शब्दः संयुगेऽतितरस्विनाम्॥ शुश्राव सुमहान्कोपादन्योन्यमभिगर्जताम्।
en: And each side desirous of slaying the other, the monkeys and the Raksasas were exceedingly strong and heroic and like to mountains. And each party storming at the other, in that conflict were heard loud cries emitted by those swiftspeeding ones in anger.

sn: रजश्चारुणवर्णाभं सुभीममभवद्भृशम्॥ उद्धृतं हरिरक्षोभिः संरुरोध दिशो दश।
en: And fearful was the dust red-hued that was raised incessantly by the monkeys and the Rākṣasa; and it enveloped the ten cardinal points.

sn: अन्योन्यं रजसा तेन कौशेयोद्धतपाण्डुना ॥ संवृतानि च भूतानि ददृशुर्न रणाजिरे।
en: In the field of battle, each enveloped with that dust raised, pale as silk, could not be discovered by the other.

sn: न ध्वजो न पताका वा चर्म वा तुरगोऽपि वा॥ आयुधं स्यन्दनो वापि ददृशे तेन रेणुना।
en: In consequence of that dust arising, neither standard, nor ensign, nor shield, nor steed, nor weapon, nor car could be seen.

sn: शब्दश्च सुमहांस्तेषां नर्दतामभिधावताम्॥ श्रूयते तुमुलो युद्धे न रूपाणि चकाशिरे।
en: The fierce cries alone of those roaring and rushing were heard in that dreadful battle; but their forms were not visible to the sight.

sn: हरीनेव सुसंरुष्टा हरयो जघ्नुराहवे॥ राक्षसा राक्षसांश्चापि निजघ्नुस्तिमिरे तदा।
en: In that conflict in the dark then monkeys extremely enraged slew monkeys, and Räkşasas also killed the Rākşasas.

sn: ते परांश्च विनिघ्नन्तः स्वांश्च वानरराक्षसाः॥ रुधिराज् तदा चक्कुर्महीं पङ्कानुलेपनाम्।
en: And monkeys and Rākşasas slaying (indiscriminately) friends and foes, made the earth wet with blood, and miry.

sn: ततस्तु रुधिरौघेण सिक्तं ह्यपगतं रजः॥ शरीरशवसंकीर्णा बभूव च वसुंधरा।
en: Then with showers of blood the dust was layed; and the earth was covered with corpses.

sn: दुमशक्तिगदाप्रासैः शिलापरिघतोमरैः॥ राक्षसा हरयस्तूर्णं जघ्नुरन्योन्यमोजसा। बाहुभिः परिघाकारैर्युध्यन्तः पर्वतोपमान्॥ हरयो भीमकर्माणो राक्षसाञ्जघ्नुराहवे।
en: Rākşasas and monkeys fast slew each other vigorously with trees and darts, maces and prasas, rocks, bludgeons and Tomaras, and by means of their arms resembling bludgeons, coped with their adversaries appearing like hills.

sn: राक्षसास्त्वभिसंक्रुद्धाः प्रासतोमरपाणयः॥ कपीनिजनिरे तत्र शस्त्रैः परमदारुणैः।
en: And in the encounter monkeys slew Rākşasas of dreadful deeds. And in their turn Rākşasas, wrought up with passion, bearing in their hands prāśas and tomaras destroyed monkeys wielding dire arms.

sn: अकम्पनः सुसंक्रुद्धो राक्षसानां चमूपतिः॥ संहर्षयति तान्सर्वान्राक्षसान्भीमविक्रमान्।
en: That leader of the force-Akampana-growing wroth, inspired with cheerfulness all the Rāks asas endowed with dreadful vigour.

sn: हरयस्त्वपि रक्षांसि महादुममहाश्मभिः॥ विदारयन्त्यभिक्रम्य शस्त्राण्याच्छिद्य वीर्यतः।
en: And the monkeys forcibly snatching away the weapons (of the Rākşasas), began to rive the Rákşasas with mighty trees and giant crags.

sn: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे वीरा हरयः कुमुदो नलः॥ मैन्दश्च परमक्रुद्धश्चक्रुर्वेगमनुत्तमम्।
en: In the meanwhile those heroes among the monkeys-Kumuda, Nīla and the exceedingly exasperated Mainda, summoned the utmost impetuosity they were masters of.

sn: ते तु वृक्षैर्महावीरा राक्षसानां चमूमुखे।॥ कदनं सुमहच्चनुर्लीलया हरिपुंगवाः। ममन्थू राक्षसान्सर्वे नानाप्रहरणैर्भृशम्॥
en: And those foremost of monkeys and redoubtable able warriors without much ado began to spread quite a carnage in the van of the Rākşasa army, and by means of various arms terribly beat the Rākşasas.

sn: तदृष्ट्वा सुमहत्कर्म कृतं वानरसत्तमैः। क्रोधमाहारयामास युधि तीव्रमकम्पनः॥
en: And witnessing that mighty exploit of the foremost of the monkeys, Akampana waxed furious with wrath.

sn: क्रोधमूर्च्छितरूपस्तु धुन्वन्यरमकार्मुकम्। दृष्ट्वा तु कर्म शत्रूणां सारथिं वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
en: And transported with passion, he, twanging his mighty bow seeing that feat of his foe, addressed his charioteer saying.

sn: तत्रैव तावत्त्वरितो रथं प्रापय सारथे। एते च बलिनो घ्नन्ति सुबहूनराक्षसारणे॥
en: O charioteer, swiftly conduct you the car to that same place. These powerful ones are slaying innumerable Rākşasas in fight.

sn: एते च बलवन्तो वा भीमकोपाश्च वानराः। द्रुमशैलप्रहरणास्तिष्ठन्ति प्रमुखे मम॥
en: And all those vigorous monkeys of dreadful deeds stay before me, armed with trees and rocks.

sn: एतानिहन्तुमिच्छामि समरश्लाघिनो ह्यहम्। एतैः प्रमथितं सर्वं रक्षसां दृश्यते बलम्॥
en: Those, pluming themselves overmuch on their martial worth, I intended to slay in battle. And all this Rākşasa force appeared to be harassed by these.

sn: ततः प्रचलिताश्वेन रथेन रथिनां वरः। हरीनभ्यपतराच्छरजालैरकम्पनः॥
en: Then on a car drawn by moving steeds, Akampana from a distance attacked the monkeys with showers of arrows.

sn: न स्थातुं वानराः शेकुः किं पुनर्योद्धमाहवे। अकम्पनशरैर्भग्ना सर्व एवाभिदुद्रुवुः॥
en: Thereat the monkeys could not so much as maintain their ground in the field, and how could they fight?

sn: तान्मृत्युवशमापनानकम्पनशरानुगान्। समीक्ष्य हनुमाञ्ज्ञातीनुपतस्थे महाबलः॥ तं महाप्लवगं दृष्ट्वा सर्वे ते प्लवगर्षभाः। समेत्य समरे वीराः सहिताः पर्यवारयन्॥
en: Broken by the arrows of Akampana, they began to fly. and the exceedingly strong Hanumān, seeing his kindred come under the masterdom of Death and follow the course pursued by the shafts of Akampana, advanced (to the conflict). And seeing that mighty monkey, all those heroic prime monkeys together surrounded (Hanumān) in the field.

sn: व्यवस्थितं हनूमन्तं ते दृष्ट्वा प्लवगर्षभाः। बभूवुर्बलवन्तो हि बलवन्तमुपाश्रिताः॥
en: Those best of monkeys, seeing Hanumán stay, grew strong by relying on that strong one.

sn: अकम्पनस्तु शैलाभं हनूमन्तमवस्थितम्। महेन्द्र इव धाराभिः शरैरभिववर्ष ह॥
en: And even as the great Indra shower down rain, Akampana showered shafts on Hanuman resembling a mountain-summit in grandeur.

sn: अचिन्तयित्वा बाणौघाशरीरे पातितान्कपिः। अकम्पनवधार्थाय मनो दध्ने महाबलः॥
en: And without casting a thought on the showers of arrows poured on his person, that monkey gifted with exceeding strength, set his heart on compassing the death of Akampana.

sn: स प्रहस्य महातेजा हनूमान्मारुतात्मजः। अभिदुद्राव तद्रक्षः कम्पयन्निव मेदिनीम्॥
en: And laughing, that exceedingly energetic offspring of the Wind-god rushed after that Rākşasa, as if making the Earth herself tremble.

sn: तस्याथ नर्दमानस्य दीप्यमानस्य तेजसा। बभूव रूपं दुर्धर्षं दीप्तस्येव विभावसोः॥
en: The form of that one roaring and flaming up in energy, was irresistible, like to the appearance of a flaming fire.

sn: आत्मानं त्वप्रहरणं ज्ञात्वा क्रोधसमन्वितः। शैलमुत्पाटयामास वेगेन हरिपुंगवः॥
en: And thinking that he was unfurnished with any arms, that foremost of monkeys, waxing wroth, vehemently rooted up a hill.

sn: गृहीत्वा सुमहाशैलं पाणिनैकेन मारुतिः। स विनद्य महानादं भ्रामयामास वीर्यवान्॥
en: And taking that huge hill, the Wind-god's son endowed with prowess, sending up a tremendous roar, began to whirl it with a single arm.

sn: ततस्तमभिदुद्राव राक्षसेन्द्रमकम्पनम्। पुरा हि मनुचिं संख्ये वज्रेणेव पुरंदरः॥
en: As of yore Purandara had in encounter pursued Namuchi with the thunder-bolt, (Hanuman) pursued that best of RāksasasAkampana.

sn: अकम्पनस्तु तदृष्ट्वा गिरिशृङ्ग समुद्यतम्। दूरादेव महाबाणैरर्धचन्द्रैरदारयत्॥
en: Akampana, seeing that uplifted crag, from a distance cut it off with mighty crescent-shaped shafts.

sn: तं पर्वताग्रमाकाशे रक्षोबाणविदारितम्। विकीर्णं पतितं दृष्ट्वा हनूमान्क्रोधमूर्च्छितः॥
en: And finding that mountain top severed by the shafts of the Räksasa and scattered in pieces, Hanumān was seized with a mighty wrath.

sn: सोऽश्वकर्ण समासाद्य रोषदान्वितो हरिः। तूर्णमुत्पाटयामास महागिरिमिवोच्छ्रितम्॥
en: That monkey, wrought up with rage and pride, grasping an Aśvakarņa elevated like to a hill, at once uprooted it.

sn: तं गृहीत्वा महास्कन्धं सोऽश्वकर्णं महाद्युतिः। प्रगृह्य परया प्रीत्या भ्रामयामास भूतले॥
en: And taking that broad-shouldered Asvakarma, that one furnished with high splendour, with great glee whirled it above the ground.

sn: प्रधावनुरुवेगेन बभञ्ज तरसा दुमान् । हनूमान्परमनुद्धश्चरणैर्दारयन्महीम्॥
en: Thereat rushing a main vehemently (Akampana) speedily broke the trees. And (seeing this) Hanumān, transported with passion, rived the earth with his kicks.

sn: गजांश्च सगजारोहान्सरथारथिनस्तथा जघान हनुमान्भीमानराक्षसांश्च पदातिगान्॥
en: And Hanumān slaughtered elephants, and the riders thereof, and cars with their riders, and dreadful Rākṣasas and footmen.

sn: तमन्तकमिव क्रुद्धं सदुमं प्राणहारिणम्। हनूमन्तमभिप्रेक्ष्य राक्षसा विप्रदुद्रुवुः॥
en: Seeing the enraged Hanumān resembling the Finisher armed with trees and destructive, the Rākşasas began to fly fast.

sn: तमापतन्तं संक्रुद्धं राक्षसानां भयावहम्। ददर्शाकम्पनो वीरश्चक्षोभ च ननाद च ॥
en: Seeing that one enraged, terrific to the Rāks asas, the heroic Akampana was agitated greatly and sent up shouts.

sn: स चतुर्दशभिर्बाणैर्निशितैर्देहदारणैः। निर्बिभेद महावीर्यं हनूमन्तमकम्पनः॥
en: Akampana pierced Hanumān endowed with exceeding prowess with four and ten shafts, sharpened and capable of cleaving the bodies of people.

sn: स तथा विप्रकीर्णस्तु नाराचैः शितशक्तिभिः। हनूमान्ददृशे वीरः प्ररूढ इव सानुमान्॥
en: And thus covered with iron arrows and whetted darts, that hero Hanumân-looked like a hill covered with trees.

sn: विरराज महावीर्यो महाकायो महाबलः। पुष्पिताशोकसंकाशो विधूम इव पावकः॥
en: That huge-bodied one endowed with wondrous prowess and great strength, appeared like a flowering Asoka or a fie without smoke.

sn: ततोऽन्यं वृक्षमुत्पाट्य कृत्वा वेगमनुत्तमम्। शिरस्याभिजघानाशु राक्षसेन्द्रमकम्पनम्॥
en: Then uprooting another tree, (Hanuman) summoning up hi best impetuosity, swiftly hit Akampana foremost of Rākşasas-on the head.

sn: स वृक्षेण हतस्तेन सक्रोधेन महात्मना। राक्षसो वानरेन्द्रेण पपात च ममार च॥
en: And slain with that tree by that high souled monkeys chief wrought up with passion that Raksasas fell down and died.

sn: तं दृष्ट्वा निहतं भूमौ राक्षसेन्द्रमकम्पनम्। व्यथिता राक्षसाः सर्वे क्षितिकम्प इव दुमाः॥
en: Seeing that foremost of Rākşasas-Akampanaslain (and lying) on the ground, the Raksasa were extremely aggrieved, and (appeared)like trees in an earthquake.

sn: त्यक्तप्रहरणाः सर्वे राक्षसास्ते पराजिताः। लङ्कामभिययुस्त्रासाद्वानरैस्तैरभिद्रुताः॥
en: And those Rākşasas defeated, leaving their arms behind, made for Lankā in fear, pursued by the monkeys.

sn: ते मुक्तकेशाः संभ्रान्ता भग्नमानाः पराजिताः। भयाच्छ्रमजलैरङ्गैः प्रस्रवद्भिर्विदुद्रुवुः॥
en: And with their hair flowing loosely, (the Rāks asas), afflicted with affright, and dispirited and beaten, fled fast, with the water of fatigue running down their persons.

sn: अयोन्यं ते प्रमनन्तो विविशुनगरं भयात्। पृष्ठतस्ते तु संमूढाः प्रेक्षमाणा मुहुर्मुहुः॥
en: And crushing down each other, they entered the city in a panic, momentarily casting their looks behind them.

sn: तेषु लङ्कां प्रविष्टेषु राक्षसेषु महाबलाः। समेत्य हरयः सर्वे हनूमन्तमपूजयन्॥
en: When the Rákşasas had entered Lankā, the exceedingly mighty monkeys, assembled together, paid homage to Hanuman.

sn: सोऽपि प्रवृद्धस्तान्सर्वान्हरीन्संप्रेत्यपूजयत्। हनूमान्सत्त्वसंपन्नो यथार्हमनुकूलतः॥
en: And Hanumăn, gifted with strength, honoured the seniors each as he deserved in consideration of his lineage.

sn: विनेदुश्च यथाप्राणं हरयो जितकाशिनः। चकृषुश्च पुनस्तत्र सप्राणानेव राक्षसान्॥
en: The monkeys eager for victory shouted with might and main, and began to drag the Rākşasas with the view of taking their lives.

sn: स वीरशोभामभजन्महाकपिः समेत्य रक्षांसि निहत्य मारुतिः। महासुरं भीमममित्रनाशनं विष्णुर्यथैवोरुबलं चमूमुखे॥ अपूजयन्देवगणास्तदा कपि स्वयं च रामोतिबलश्च लक्ष्मणः। तथैव सुग्रीवमुखाः प्लवंगमा विभीषणश्चैव महाबलस्तदा॥
en: That mighty monkey-son to the Wind godhaving destroyed the Rākşasas and arrived (in the midst of the host), attained heroic glory, even as did Vişnu, having slain that destroyer of enemies-the mighty and dreadful Asura possessed of exceeding strength, stationed in the ban of the forces. And then the deities and Rāma himself and the highly powerful Lakşmaņa, also the monkeys headed by Sugrīva, and Vibhīşaņa endowed with great strength, honoured that monkey.

sn: अकम्पनवधं श्रुत्वा क्रुद्धो वै राक्षसेश्वरः। किंचिद्दीनमुखश्चापि सचिवांस्तानुदैक्षत॥
en: Hearing that Akampana had been killed, the lord of Raksasas, overwhelmed with anger, with his face somewhat fallen, cast his eyes on his counsellors.

sn: स तु ध्यात्वा मुहूर्तं तु मन्त्रिभिः संविचार्य च। ततस्तु रावणः पूर्वदिवसे राक्षसाधिपः।। पुरीं परिययौ लङ्कां सर्वान्गुल्मानवेक्षितुम्॥
en: Then pondering and reflecting for a while, in the forenoon he went round the city of Lankā for inspecting the barracks.

sn: तां राक्षसगणैर्गुप्तां गुल्मैर्बहुभिरावृताम्। ददर्श नगरी राजा पताकाध्वजमालिनीम्॥
en: The king surveyed the city guarded by the Rakşsasas, covered with innumerable barracks, and crowned with ensigns and standards,

sn: रुद्धां तु नगरी दृष्ट्वा रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः। उवाचात्महितं काले प्रहस्तं युद्धकोविदम्॥
en: Seeing the city besieged, Ravana-lord of the Rākşaşas-seasonably spoke words of welfare to Prahasta skilled in fight.

sn: पुरस्योपनिविष्टस्य सहसा पीडितस्य ह। नान्ययुद्धात्प्रपश्यामि मोक्षं युद्धविशारदाः॥
en: "Save battle, deliverance find I none for the city suddenly beleaguered and put to straits.

sn: अहं वा कुम्भकर्णो वा त्वं वा सेनापतिर्यम। इन्द्रजिद्धा निकुम्भो वा वहेयुर्भारमीदृशम्॥
en: And this strain must be borne by these versed in warfare-me or Kumbhakarna or you-my general or Indrajit or Nikumbha.

sn: सत्त्वं बलमतः शीघ्रमादाय परिगृह्य च। विजयायाभिनियहि यत्र सर्वे वनौकसः॥
en: Therefore do you from this place, speedily taking this force, march to where the monkeys are, for securing victory (in the encounter).

sn: निर्याणादेव तूर्णं च चलिता हरिवाहिनी। नर्दतां राक्षसेन्द्राणां श्रुत्वा नादं द्रविष्यति॥
en: And as soon as you set out, the monkeyforces, hearing the roars of the foremost Rākșasas-speedily setting themselves in motionshall flee away.

sn: चपला ह्यविनाताश्च चलचित्ताश्च वानराः। न सहिष्यन्ति ते नादं सिंहनादमिव द्विषा:॥
en: And volatile and haughty and of fickle minds, the monkeys will not be able to bear your shouts; even as elephants are incapable of bearing the roaring of a lion.

sn: विद्वते च बले तस्मिन्रामः सौमित्रिणा सह। अवशस्तु निरालम्बः प्रहस्तवशमेष्यति॥
en: And on that monkey-army running away, Rāma in company with Sumitrās son, deprived of his power and shorn of support, shall, O Prahasta, come under your subjection.

sn: आपत्संशयिता श्रेयो नात्र निःसंशयीकृता। प्रतिलोमानुलोमं वा यत्तु नो मन्यसे हितम्॥
en: In this matter, your being slain is uncertain, but victory is certain. Now do you, as you weigh out welfare, declare yourself for or against this course.

sn: रावणेनैवमुक्तस्तु प्रहस्तो वाहिनीपतिः। राक्षसेन्द्रमुवाचेदमसुरेन्द्रमिवोशना॥
en: Thus addressed by Ravana, Prahasta-general of the forces-said to the Rākşaas-chief; like Uśanas addressing the lord of Asuras.

sn: राजन्मन्त्रितपूर्वं नः कुशलैः सह मन्त्रिभिः। विवादश्चापि नो वृत्तः समवेक्ष्य परस्परम्॥
en: O king before this we had deliberated together with wise counsellors, and then we disputed with each other in our respective views.

sn: प्रदानेन तु सीतायाः श्रेयो व्यवसितं मया। अप्रदाने पुनयुद्धं दृष्टमेव तथैव नः॥
en: And I had declared myself for giving up Sītā as fraught with our welfare; and we saw war involved in withholding her.

sn: सोऽहं दानैश्च मानैश्च सततं पूजितस्त्वया। सान्त्वैश्च विविधैः काले किं न कुर्यां हितं तव॥
en: I have ever been honoured by you variously with gifts and regard and soft speech. And what is your good for which I shall not be at the pains?

sn: नहि मे जीवितं रक्ष्यं पुत्रदारधनानि च। त्वं पश्य मां जुहूषन्तं त्वदर्थे जीवितं युधि॥
en: My life I do not care to keep, nor yet my sons or my wife. Behold! for you will I offer up my life into the sacrificial fire of conflict.

sn: एवमुक्त्वा तु भर्तारं रावणं वाहिनीपतिः। उवाचेदं बलाध्यक्षान्प्रहस्तः पुरतः स्थितान्॥
en: Having said this to his master-Rävaņa-the general, Prahasta, addressed his generals staying before him, saying.

sn: समानयत मे शीघ्रं राक्षसानां महाबलम्। मद्बाणानां तु वेगेन हतानां तु रणाजिरे॥ अद्य तृप्यन्तु मांसादाः पक्षिणः काननौकसः।
en: At once bring up the mighty host of Raksasas Today in the field of fight will I entertain the flesh-feeding fowls of the forest with the bodies of the foes slain with my resistless shafts.

sn: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा बलाध्यक्षा महाबलाः॥ बलमुद्योजयामासुस्तस्मिनाक्षसमन्दिरे।
en: Hearing his speech, the highly powerful leaders arrayed the army in that abode of the Raksasa.

sn: सा बभूव मुहूर्तेन भीमैर्नानाविधायुधैः॥ लङ्का राक्षसवीरैस्तैर्गजैरिव समाकुला। हुताशनं तर्पयतां ब्राह्मणांश्च नमस्यताम्॥ आज्यगन्धप्रतिवहः सुरभिर्मारुतो ववौ।
en: In a moment Lankā swarmed with heroic and terrific Rākşasas equipped with various arms, as if with elephants, as well as with people worshipping Fire and bowing down to Brāhmaṇas. And the perfumed breeze blew, laden with the incense of sacrificial offerings.

sn: सजश्च विविधाकारा जगृहुस्त्वभिमन्त्रिताः॥ संग्रामसज्जाः संहृष्टा धारयनराक्षसास्तदा।
en: The Raksasas, inspired with martial ardour, put on diverse garlands, consecrated with scriptural formulae; and donned on their armour.

sn: सधनुष्काः कवचिनो वेगादुत्सृज्य राक्षसाः॥ रावणं प्रेक्ष्य राजानं प्रहस्तं पर्यवारयन्।
en: And furnished with their boys and wearing their armour, the Rākşasas, on seeing king Ravana, leaving (their vehicles), stood, surrounding Prahasta.

sn: अथामन्त्र्य तु राजानं भेरीमाहत्य भैरवाम्।।२४ आरुरोह रथं युक्तः प्रहस्तः सज्जकल्पितम्। हयैर्महाजवैर्युक्तं सम्यक्सूतं सुसंयतम्॥ महाजलदनिर्घोषं साक्षाच्चन्द्रार्कभास्वरम्। उरगध्वजदुर्धर्षं सुवरूथं स्वपस्करम्॥ सुवर्णजालसंयुक्तं प्रहसन्तमिव श्रिया।
en: The greeting the monarch, Prahasta, furnished (with all appliances of battle), winding his dreadful trumpet, ascended his car; having all sorts of weapons; yoked with wondrous fleet steeds; driven by a competent charioteer, excellently furnished; sending up sounds resembling the rumbling of mighty masses of cloud, appearing like the very sun or Moon; invincible with a serpent-standard; having a defence as well as a portion exceedingly handsome; netted with gold all round; and seeming to be laughing in grace.

sn: ततस्तं रथमास्थाय रावणार्पितशासनः॥ लङ्काया निर्ययौ तूर्णं बलेन महता वृतः। ततो दुन्दुभिनिर्घोषः पर्जन्यनिनदोपमः।। वादित्राणां न निनदः पूरयन्निव मेदिनीम्॥ शुश्रुवे शङ्खशब्दश्च प्रयाते वाहिनीपतौ।
en: Then ascending this car, Prahasta, whom Rāvana had entrusted with authority, surrounded by a vast host, swiftly went out of Larkā. And then there were heard the sounds of kettledrums, resembling the roars of Parjanya, and the sounds of musical instruments, as if filling the Earth.

sn: निनदन्तः स्वरान्घोराराक्षसा जग्मुरग्रतः॥ भीमरूपा महाकायः प्रहस्तस्य पुनःसराः।
en: And on that general of the forces marching, sounds of conchs were heard (all around); and the Rākşasas of dreadful forms and huge bodies, going before Prahasta, advanced, emitting tremendous roars.

sn: नरान्तकः कुम्भहनुर्महानादः समुन्नतः।। प्रहस्तसचिवा ह्येते निर्ययुः परिवार्य तम्॥
en: Narāntaka, Kumbhahunu, Mahānāda, and Samunnata Prahasta's counsellors all of themwent on, surrounding him.

sn: व्यूढेनैव सुघोरेण पूर्वद्वारात्स निर्ययौ। गजयूथनिकाशेन बलेन महता वृतः॥
en: And he went out by the Eastern entrance, environed by this exceedingly dreadful array, resembling troops of elephants.

sn: सागरप्रतिमौधेन वृतस्तेन बलेन सः। प्रहस्तो निर्ययौ क्रुद्धः कालान्तकयमोपमः॥
en: And resembling the Destroyer-Yama himselfPrahasta in rage went out surrounded by that mighty host resembling the sea.

sn: तस्य निर्याणघोषेण राक्षसानां च नर्दताम्। लङ्कायां सर्वभूतानि विनेदुर्विकृतैः स्वरैः॥
en: And at the tumult raised by their exodus, as well as the roars of the Rākşasas, all creatures in Lankā began to cry in preternatural tones.

sn: व्यभ्रमाकाशमाविश्य मांसशोणितभोजनाः। मण्डलान्यपसव्यानि खगाश्चक्रू रथं प्रति॥
en: And swarming under the cloudless welkin, birds feasting on flesh and gore began to gyrate at the right hand of the car.

sn: वमन्ति पावकज्वालाः शिवा घोरा ववाविशे। अन्तरिक्षात्पपातोल्का वायुश्च परुषं ववौ॥
en: And dreadful jackals, emitting live flames from their mouths, set up cries. And stars began to shoot from the firmament; and the winds to ruffle.

sn: अन्योन्यमभिसंरब्धा ग्रहाश्च न चकाशिरे। मेघाश्च खरनिर्घोषा रथस्योपरि रक्षसः॥ ववधू रुधिरं चास्य सिषिचुश्च पुरःसरान्। केतुमूर्धनि गृध्रस्तु विलीनो दक्षिणामुखः॥ नदन्नुभयतः पार्श्व समयां श्रियमाहरन्।
en: And enraged at each other, the planetary bodies were shorn of their brightness. And clouds emitting sharp sounds, showered down blood upon the car, and those marching in front were washed therewith. And alighting at the top of the standard, a vulture set up cries, facing the south and began to prick both its sides, thereby depriving (Prahasta) of his grace.

sn: सारथेर्बहुशश्चात्र संग्राममानिवर्तिनः॥ प्रतोदो न्यपतद्धस्तात्सूतस्य हयसादिनः।
en: And from the hands of his charioteer and his driver conducting the steeds, never given to turning away from the field the goad began to drop again and again.

sn: निर्याणश्रीश्च या चस्याद्भास्वरा च सुदुर्लभा॥ सा ननाश मुहूर्तेन समे च स्खलिता हयाः।
en: The auspiciousness that was bright and rare when the army set out, was clean gone in a moment, and the steeds began to stumble on even ground.

sn: प्रहस्तं तं हि निर्यान्तं प्रख्यातगुणपौरुषम्।। युधि नानाप्रहरणा कपिसेनाभ्यवर्तत॥
en: And as Prahasta of renowned worth and valour marched, the monkey-army equipped with various arms, presented themselves before him.

sn: अथ घोषः सुतुमुलो हरीणां समजायत। वृक्षानारुजतां चैव गुर्वी गृह्णतां शिलाः॥ नदतां राक्षसानां च वानराणां च गर्जताम्। उभे प्रमुदिते सैन्ये रक्षोगणवनौकसाम्।॥ वेगितानां समर्थानामन्योन्यवधकाक्षिणाम्। परस्परं चाह्वयतां निनादः श्रूयते महान्॥
en: And loud was the tumult that was raised by the monkeys. And mighty was the din that was heard of those, uprooting trees and taking up ponderous crags, of the Räkşasas roaring and the monkeys storming in both the exhilarated armies of Raksasa and wood-rangers, of vehement and able (warriors) eager for slaying each other, and challenging each other to fight.

sn: ततः प्रहस्तः कपिराजवाहिनीमभिप्रतस्थे विजयाय दुर्मतिः। विवृद्धवेगश्च विवेशितां चमूं यथा मुमूर्षुः शलभो विभावसुम्॥
en: And like an insect falling into a flame, the wicked-minded Prahasta for obtaining victory, increasing his impetuosity entered into that host of the monkey-king.

sn: ततः प्रहस्तं निर्यान्तं दृष्ट्वा रणकृतोद्यमम्। उवाच सस्मितं रामो विभीषणमरिंदमः॥
en: Seeing Prahasta sally, ready for encounter that chastiser of foes-Rāma-with a smile said to Vibhisana.

sn: क एष सुमहाकायो बलेन महता वृतः। आगच्छति महावेगः किंरूपबलपौरुषः॥ आचक्ष्व मे महाबाहो वीर्यवन्तं निशाचरम्।
en: Who is this huge-bodied one that armed with impetuosity, advance to the encounter And what is his power and prowess like O Mighty-armed one, tell me this concerning this powerful nightranger.

sn: राघवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा प्रत्युवाच विभीषणः॥ एष सेनापतिस्तस्य प्रहस्तो नाम राक्षसः। लङ्कायां राक्षसेन्द्रस्य त्रिभागबलसंवृतः।। वीर्यवानस्त्रविच्छूरः सुप्रख्यातपराक्रमः॥
en: Hearing Raghava's words, Vibhîşana answered, In Laňkā this is the general of the lord of Rākşasas-the Rākşasa named Prahasta, surrounded by a third of the forces. He is possessed of prowess and is of distinguished gallantry.

sn: ततः प्रहस्तं निर्यान्तं भीमं भीमपराक्रमम्। गर्जन्तं सुमहाकायं राक्षसैरभिसंवृतम्॥ ददर्श महती सेना वानराणां बलीयसाम्। अभिसंजातघोषाणां प्रहस्तमभिगर्जताम्॥
en: That mighty army of strong monkeys, wrought up with wrath, and roaring at Prahasta, saw him dreadful and of terrific prowess and huge-bodied, surrounded on all sides by the Raksasas, and setting up roars, marching.

sn: खङ्गशक्त्वृष्टिशूलाश्च बाणानि मुसलानि च। गदाश्च परिघाः प्रासा विविधाश्च परश्वधाः॥ धनूंषि च विचित्राणि राक्षसानां जयैषिणाम्। प्रगृहीतान्यराजन्त वानरानभिधावताम्॥
en: The Raksasas, eagerly desirous of victory, pursued the monkeys, wielding swords and darts and Rştis, and javelins and shafts and maces and clubs and bludgeons and práşas and various axes and curious bows.

sn: जगृहुः पादपांश्चापि पुष्पितांस्तु गिरीस्तथा। शिलाश्च विपुला दीर्घा योद्धकामाः प्लवंगमाः।९।।
en: The monkeys on their part, eager for encounter, took up flowing trees and hills and huge and broad crags.

sn: तेषामन्योन्यमासाद्य संग्रामः सुमहानभूत्। बहूनामश्मवृष्टिं च शरवर्ष च वर्षताम्॥
en: And each party approaching the other, great was the encounter that took place. And innumerable (monkeys and Rākṣasas) kept showering rocks and arrows.

sn: बहवो राक्षसा युद्धे बहून्वानरपुंगवान्। वानरा राक्षसांश्चापि निजघ्नुर्बहवो बहून्॥
en: And many Rākşasas in conflict slew many a powerful monkey, and the monkeys on their part slaughtered many a Rākşasa.

sn: शूलैः प्रमथिताः केचित्केचित्तु परमायुधैः । परिघेराहताः केचित्केचिच्छिन्नाः परश्वधैः॥
en: Some were pierced with darts and with (other) powerful weapons; and some were wounded with bludgeons; and some were hewn with axes.

sn: निरुच्छ्वासाः पुनः केचित्पतिता जगतीतले। विभिन्नहृदयाः केचिदिषुसंधानसाधिताः॥
en: Some rendered senseless, dropped down to the earth, and some hit with weapons, had their breasts riven.

sn: केचिद्विधा कृताः खङ्गैः स्फुरन्तः पतिता भुवि। वानरा राक्षसैः शूरैः पार्श्वतश्च विदारिताः॥
en: Some, severed in twain with swords, dropped to the earth lifeless, and monkeys were hewn in their sides by heroic Rākşasas.

sn: वानरैश्चापि संक्रुद्धे राक्षसौघाः समन्ततः। पादपैर्गिरिशृङ्गैश्च संपिष्टा वसुधातले॥
en: Numbers of Rākşasas all around were beaten to the ground by infuriated monkeys with trees and mountain-peaks.

sn: वज्रस्पर्शतलैर्हस्तैर्मुष्टिभिश्च हता भृशम्। वमशोणितमास्येभ्यो विशीर्णवदनेक्षणाः॥
en: Some smitten sore with slaps having the touch of the thunder-bolt, began to vomit blood from their mouths, with faces and eyes turned pale.

sn: आस्विनं च स्वनतां सिंहनादं च नर्दताम्। बभूव तुमुल: शब्दो हरीणां रक्षसामपि॥
en: And great was the uproar that arose in consequence of Rākṣasas and monkeys emitting distressful cries and sending forth leonine roars.

sn: वानरा राक्षसाः क्रुद्धा वीरमार्गमनुव्रताः। विवृत्तवदनाः क्रूराश्चक्रुः कर्माण्यभीतवत्॥
en: Monkeys and Rākṣasas wrought up with wrath, engaged in treading the path of heroes, looking terrific with their faces moving about, performed deeds of intrepid courage.

sn: नरान्तकः कुम्भहनुर्महानादः समुन्नतः। एते प्रहस्तसचिवाः सर्वे जघ्नुर्वनौकसः॥
en: Narāntaka and Kambhahanu and Mahānand and Samunnata-all counsellors of Prahasta-set about slaughtering the rangers of the woods.

sn: तेषां निपततां शीघ्रं निघ्नतां चापि वानरान्। द्विविदो गिरिशृङ्गेण जघानैकं नरान्तकम्॥
en: Of these doing swift execution among the monkeys, Dvivida, taking up a mountain-peak, slew one-namely Narāntaka.

sn: दुर्मुखः पुनरुत्थाय कपिः सविपुलदुमम्। राक्षसं क्षिप्रहस्तं तु समुन्नतमपोथयत्॥
en: Then the monkey, Durmaukha, rising up afresh, armed with a mighty tree, killed the lighthanded Räksasa-Samunnata.

sn: जाम्बवांस्तु सुसंक्रुद्धः प्रगृह्य महतीं शिलाम्। पातयामास तेजस्वी महानादस्य वक्षसि॥
en: Jāmbavān endowed with energy, waxing enraged, uplifting a giant crag brought the same down on Mahananda's breast.

sn: अथ कुम्भहनुस्तत्र तारेणासाद्य वीर्यवान्। वृक्षेण महता सद्यः प्राणान्संत्याजयद्रणे॥
en: There speedily assailed by Tārā, with a mighty tree, the powerful Kumbhahanu gave up the ghost in the conflict.

sn: अमृष्यमाणस्तत्कर्म प्रहस्तो रथमाश्रितः। चकार कदनं घोरं धनुष्पाणिर्वनौकसाम्॥
en: And not brooking that feat, Prahasta, mounted on a car, taking a bow in his hand, fell to spreading a dreadful havoc among the rangers of the woods.

sn: आवर्त इव संजज्ञे सेनयोरुभयोस्तदा। क्षुभितस्याप्रमेमस्य सागरस्येव नि:स्वनः॥
en: Then there the two hosts mingled into almost a vortex; and the sounds that arose from those infuriated once of immeasurable might, resembled the roar of the ocean.

sn: महता हि शरौघेण राक्षसो रणदुर्मदः। अर्दयामास संक्रुद्धो वानरान्परमाहवे॥
en: In terrific encounter the enraged Rākşasa irresistible in battle drove the monkeys to sore straits with showers of arrows.

sn: वानराणां शरीरैस्तु राक्षसानां च मेदिनी। बभूवातिचिता घोरैः पर्वतैरिव संवृता॥
en: The earth was covered quite with the terrible bodies of monkeys and Rākşasas; and it looked as if covered with mountains.

sn: सा मही रुधिरौधेण प्रच्छन्ना संप्रकाशते। संछन्ना माधवे मासि पलाशैरिव पुष्पितैः॥
en: The earth drenched with streams of gore looked as if swarming with blossoming palāśas in the month of spring.

sn: हतवीरौघवप्रां तु भग्नायुधमहादुमाम्। शोणितौघमहातोयां यमसागरगामिनीम्॥ यकृत्प्लीहमहापदां विनिकीर्णान्त्रशैवलाम्। भिन्नकायशिरोमीनामङ्गावयवशाद्वलाम्॥ गृध्रहंसवराकीर्णा कङ्कसारससेविताम्। मेदःफेनसमाकीर्णामावर्तस्वननिःस्वनाम्॥ तां कापुरुषदुस्तारां युद्धभूमिमयीं नदीम्। नदीमिव घनापाये हंससारससेविताम्॥ राक्षसाः कपिमुख्यास्ते तेरुस्तां दुस्तरां नदीम्। यथा पद्मग्जोध्वस्तां नलिनी गजयूथपाः॥
en: As leaders of elephant-herds cross a lotus-tank covered with lotus-dust, those Rākşasas and choice monkeys crossed that river flowing in the field of conflict incapable of being crossed; having for her banks hosts of heroic warriors slain; for her mighty trees broken arms; for her volume of waters showers of blood; coursing to Yama resembling the Ocean; with livers and spleens for her vast slime; with scattered entrails for her moss; with riven bodies and heads for her fish; limbs for her lawns; swarming with vultures for her swans; with Kankas for her cranes, filled with fat representing her foam; with the roars (of warriors) for her sounds, incapable of being crossed by cravens, and resembling a real river swarming at the end of the rains with cranes and swans.

sn: ततः सृजन्तं बाणौघान्प्रहस्तं स्यन्दने स्थितम्। ददर्श तरसा नीलो विधमन्तं प्लवंगमान्॥
en: Then all of a sudden Nila saw Prahasta stationed on his car, discharging vollies of shafts and harassing the monkeys therewith.

sn: उद्धृत इव वायुः खे महदभ्रबलं बलात्। समीक्ष्याभिद्रुतं युद्धे प्रहस्तो वाहिनीपतिः॥ रथेनादित्यवर्णेन नीलमेवामेवाभिदुद्रुवे।
en: Mounted on a sun-bright vehicle, that leader of the army-Prahasta-seeing Nīla advance towards him a main in the encounter, like the wind in the sky scattering a mighty mass of clouds, rushed towards Nila.

sn: स धनुर्धन्विनां श्रेष्ठो विकृष्य परमाहवे॥ नीलाय व्यसृजद्वाणान्प्रहस्तो वाहिनीपतिः।
en: That leader of forces-Prahasta-foremost of bowmen, stretching his bow, began to shower arrows on Nila.

sn: ते प्रेत्य विशिखा नीलं विनिर्भिद्य समाहिताः॥ महीं जग्मुर्महावेगा रोषिता इव पत्रगाः।
en: Having pierced Nīla sore and wounded him, those shafts sought the earth like enraged serpents.

sn: नीलः शरैरभिहतो निशितैर्व्वलनोपमैः॥ स तं परमदुर्धर्षमापतन्तं महाकपिः। प्रहस्तं ताडयामास वृक्षमुत्पाट्य वीर्यवान्॥
en: That mighty monkey-Nila-endowed with energy, struck with those sharpened shafts resembling flames, uprooting a tree, assailed therewith the irrepressible Prahasta-who was rushing against him.

sn: स तेनाभिहतः क्रुद्धो नर्दनराक्षसपुंगवः। ववर्ष शरवर्षाणि प्लवंगानां चमूपतौ॥
en: Thereat, that foremost of Raksasas, on being attacked, flaming up into fury and uttering roars, poured showers of arrows on the monkeyleader.

sn: तस्य बाणगणानेव राक्षसस्य दुरात्मनः। अपारयन्वारयितुं प्रत्यगृह्णानिमीलितः। यथैव गोवृषो वर्ष शारदं शीघ्रमागतम्।॥ एवमेव प्रहस्तस्य शरवर्षान्दुरासदान्। निमीलिताक्षः सहसा नीलः सेहे दुरासदान्।॥
en: And not being able to resist the arrowy vollies of that wicked-minded Raksasas, (Nila) bore them, even as a bull bear with closed eyes a fastdescending autumnal shower. And in the very same way did Nila with his eyes closed suddenly stand the mighty arrowy buffet of Prahasta incapable of being withstood.

sn: रोषितः शरवर्षेण सालेन महता महान्। प्रजघान हयानीलः प्रहस्तस्य महाबलः।४३।।
en: And wrought up with rage, the exceedingly strong and mighty Nila with a giant Sala slew the steeds of Prahasta.

sn: ततो रोषपरीतात्मा धनुस्तस्य दुरात्मनः। बभञ्ज तरसा नीलो ननाद च पुनः पुनः॥
en: Then his-soul surcharged with wrath, Nīla swiftly shattered the bow of that wicked-minded one, and then shouted again and again.

sn: विधनुः स कृतस्तेन प्रहस्तो वाहिनीपतिः। प्रगृह्य मुसलं घोरं स्यन्दनादवपुप्लुवे॥
en: On being bereft of his bow, Prahasta, general of forces, taking a terrible mace, leapt down from his car.

sn: तावुभौ वाहिनीमुख्यौ जातवैरौ तरस्विनौ। स्थितौ क्षतजसिक्ताङ्गौ प्रभिन्नाविव कुञ्जरौ॥
en: The redoubtable leaders endowed with activity, bearing hostility to each other, their persons bathed in blood, stood (on the ground) like two elephants (with their temples) riven,

sn: उल्लिखन्तौ सुतीक्ष्णाभिदंष्ट्राभिरितरेतरम्। सिंहशार्दूलसदृशौ सिंहशार्दूलचेष्टितौ॥
en: They kept tearing each other with their teeth like a lion and a tiger, and alsò striving like a lion and a tiger.

sn: विक्रान्तविजयौ वीरौ समरेष्वनिवर्तिनौ। काङ्कमाणौ यशः प्राप्तुं वृत्रवासवयोरिव ॥
en: Endowed with victorious vigour, those heroes, never knowing to desist from fight, were eager for fame, even like Vrtra and Vasava (fighting).

sn: आजघान तदा नीलं ललाटे मुसलेन सः। प्रहस्तः परमायत्तस्ततः सुस्राव शोणितम्॥
en: Then Prahasta putting forth his dearest effort, hit Nila on the temples with a mace; and the blood began to flow.

sn: ततः शोणितदिग्धाङ्गः प्रगृह्य च महातरुम्। प्रहस्तस्योरसि क्रुद्धो विससर्ज महाकपिः॥
en: Then the mighty monkey, with his person drenched in blood, wrought up with passion, discharged a tall tree at Prahasta's breast.

sn: तमचिन्त्य प्रहारं स प्रगृह्य मुसलं महत्। अभिदुद्राव बलिनं बलानीलं प्लवंगमम्।।
en: Without caring for that hit, he, taking up a mighty mace, furiously rushed against the monkey-Nila.

sn: तमुग्रवेगं संरब्धमापतन्तं महाकपिः॥ ततः संप्रेक्ष्य जग्राह महावेगो महाशिलाम्।
en: Witnessing that enraged (hero) rushing against him with exceeding impetuosity, that redoubted monkey endowed with vehemence, took up a tremendous crag.

sn: तस्य युद्धाभिकामस्य मृधे मुसलयोधिनः॥ प्रहस्तस्य शिलां नीलो मूर्ध्नि तूर्णमपातयत्। नीलेन कपिमुख्येन विमुक्ता महती शिला।। बिभेद बहुधा घोरा प्रहस्तस्य शिरस्तदा ॥
en: In the encounter Nila at once let that crag alight right on the head of Prahasta, eager for encounter and fighting with the mace. And hurled by that foremost of monkeys, that huge and terrific crag then shattered Prahasta's head in pieces.

sn: स गतासुर्गतश्रीको गतसत्त्वो गतेन्द्रियः। पपात सहसा भूमौ छिन्नमूल इव दुमः। ५४॥
en: Then bereft of life and shorn of nerve and devoid of sense he suddenly dropped down to the earth like a tree whose roots have been severed.

sn: विभिन्नशिरसस्तस्य बहु सुस्राव शोणितम्। शरीरादपि सुस्राव गिरेः प्रस्रवणो यथा॥
en: Even as fountains flow from the sides of a hill, blood flowed profusely from the person of that one, whose head had been riven.

sn: हते प्रहस्ते नीलेन तदकम्प्यं महाबलम्। राक्षसानामहृष्टाना लङ्कामभिजगाम हा५६।।
en: On Prahasta being slain by Nila, that mighty army of Raksasas never trembling (from fear). retreated towards Larikā.

sn: न शेकुः समवस्थातुं निहते वाहिनीपतौ। सेतुबन्धं समासाद्य विशीणं सलिलं यथा॥ हते तस्मिंश्चमूमुख्ये राक्षसास्ते निरुद्यमाः। रक्षःपतिगृहं गत्वा ध्यानमूकत्वमागताः।। प्राप्ताः शोकार्णवं तीव्र विसंज्ञा इव तेऽभवन्।५८।।
en: And like waters rushing (through a breach in) a dyke, the Rākşasas could not stand their ground, on their leader being slain. And on that head of the hosts being killed, the Rākşasas, growing dispirited, repairing to the residence of the lord of Rākşasa, remained plunged in thought, without speaking anything. And plunged in that sea of sorrow, they seemed as if they had been bereft of their senses.

sn: ततस्तु नीलो विजयी महाबलः प्रशस्यमानः सुकृतेन कर्मणा। समेत्य रामेण सलक्ष्मणेन प्रहृष्टरूपस्तु बभूव यूथपः।५९।।
en: Then the highly powerful and victorious Nila, leader of forces, on being extolled with gracious offices, and on being joined by Rāma and Laks maņa looked exceedingly exhilarated.

sn: तस्मिन्हते राक्षससैन्यपाले प्लवंगमानामृषभेण युद्धे। भीमायुधं सागरवेगतुल्यं विदुद्रवे राक्षसराजसैन्यम्॥
en: On the leader of the Rākşasa host being slain in battle by the foremost of monkeys, that army of the Rākşasas monarch, resembling the ocean in violence, furnished with dreadful weapons, began to scamper away.

sn: गत्वा तु रक्षोधिपतेः शशंसुः सेनापतिं पावकसूनुशस्तम्। तच्चापि तेषां वचनं निशम्य रक्षोधिपः क्रोधवशं जगाम॥
en: Going to the lord of the Rākşasas, they ar prised hin, of the dealth of his general at the hands of the Fire-god's offspring. And hearing those words of theirs, the Rākşasas lord was overcome with rage.

sn: संख्ये प्रहस्तं निहतं निशम्य क्रोधार्दितः शोकपरीतचेताः। निन्द्रो यथा निर्जरयूथमुख्यान्॥
en: And hearing that Prahasta had been killed in battle (he), exercised with passion, with his heart influenced with grief, addressed those foremost of the Raksasas host, even as Indra addressed the chiefs among the celestials, saying

sn: नावज्ञा रिपवे कार्या यैरिन्द्रबलसादनः। सूदितः सैन्यपालो मे सानुयात्रः सकुञ्जरः॥
en: That foe should no longer be disregarded that has slain along with his followers and elephants that leader of my host that had destroyed the forces of Indra himself.

sn: सोऽहं रिपुविनाशाय विजयायाविचारयन्। स्वयमेव गमिष्यामि रणशीर्षं तदद्भुतम्॥
en: Therefore, without taking thought, will I, for compassing the destruction of the foe myself march to that marvellous field of fight.

sn: अद्य तद्वानरानीकं रामं च सलक्ष्मणम्। निर्दहिष्यामि बाणौधैर्वनं दीप्तैरिवाग्निभिः॥
en: Today, even as a flaming fire burn down a forest, will I with showers of shafts burn up that monkey-army, and Rama and Laksmana.

sn: स एवमुक्त्वा ज्वलनप्रकाशं रथं तुरंगोत्तमराजियुक्तम्। प्रकाशमानं वपुषा ज्वलन्तं समारुरोहामरराजशत्रुः॥
en: Saying this, that enemy of the sovereign of the immortals ascended a flaming vehicle of dazzling sheen yoked to rows of excellent steeds, displaying itself gloriously and having a glowing body.

sn: रास्फोटितक्ष्वेडितसिंहनादैः। स्तदा ययौ राक्षसराजमुख्यः॥
en: And eulogized with sacred hymns, the sovereign of the Rākşasa rulers then set out to the sounds of conchs and trumpets and Panavas; and in the midst of those produced by persons striking at their arms, with their hands, and of the sounds defiance, and leonine roars.

sn: मांसाशनैः पावकदीप्तनेत्रैः। बभौ वृतो राक्षसराजमुख्यो भूतैर्वृतो रुद्र इवामरेशः। ॥
en: Like that lord of the immortals-Rudrasurrounded by ghosts, the foremost of the Rākṣsa monarchs was surrounded by bands of flesh-feeding (Raksasa) resembling cliffs and clouds-with eyes glowing like fire.

sn: ततो नगर्याः सहसा महौजा निष्क्रम्य तद्वानरसैन्यमुग्रम्। महार्णवाभ्रस्तनितं ददर्श समुद्यतं पादपशैलहस्तम्॥
en: At once issuing from the city, that one endowed with high energy saw that fierce array of monkeys, extended as the ocean or a mighty mass of clouds, with arms upraised with rocks and stones.

sn: मालोक्य रामो भुजगेन्द्रबाहुः। मुवाच सेनानुगतः पृथुश्रीः॥
en: Seeing that terrific host of Räkşasas, that eminently auspicious one, followed by the forces, having arms resembling the lord of serpents-Rama-spoke to Vibhişana foremost of those bearing arms.

sn: नानापताकाध्वजछऋजुष्टं प्रासासिशूलायुधशस्त्रजुष्टम्। कस्येदमक्षोभ्यमभीरुजुष्टं सैन्यं महेन्द्रोपमनागजुष्टम्॥
en: Whose is this force furnished with various ensigns and standards-and equipped with pracas and swords and darts and other arms, consisting of intrepid (Rakşasas), and having, elephants resembling Mahendra* itself. *The mountain so named.

sn: ततस्तु रामस्य निशम्य वाक्यं विभीषणः शक्रसमानवीर्यः। शशंस रामस्य बलप्रवेकं महात्मनां राक्षसपुङ्गवानाम्॥
en: Then hearing Rama's speech, Vibhisana, possessed of the prowess of Sakra himself, informed Råma anent that foremost of hosts consisting of that flower of high souled Räkş asas, saying.

sn: योऽसौ गजस्कन्धगतो महात्मा नवोदितार्कोपमताम्रवक्त्रः। संकम्पयनागशिरोऽभ्युपैति हाकम्पनं त्वेनमवेहि राजन् ॥
en: O king, him do you know to be Akampana, who, possessed of a high soul, is on the back of that elephant, whose face looks like the sun new risen, and who approach making the head of his elephant tremble (with the splendour of his person).* *This meaning is the commentator's.

sn: धुंन्वन्धनुः शक्रधनुःप्रकाशम्। करीव भात्युग्रविवृत्तदंष्ट्रः स इन्द्रजिन्नाम वरप्रधानः॥
en: That one is named Indrajit-foremost by virtue of the boon (that he has obtained), who ascending a car and having a lion for his ensign, twange his bow like the very bow of Sakra displayed, and who with his terrific round teeth appear like an elephant.

sn: यश्चैष विन्ध्यास्तमहेन्द्रकल्पो धन्वी रथस्थोऽतिरथोऽतिवीरः। विस्फारयंश्चापमतुल्यमानं नाम्नातिकायोऽतिविवृद्धकायः॥
en: That one of a gigantic person is named Atikāya, that, like to the Setting-hill of Vindhya, furnished with the bow and stationed on a car, highly heroic, stretch his bow of unparalleled proportions.

sn: रारुह्य घण्टानिनदप्रणादम्। गजं खरं गर्जति वै महात्मा महोदरो नाम स एष वीरः॥
en: That high souled hero is named Mahodara that, furnished with right coppery eyes resembling the sun new risen, and ascending a car resonant with the sound of bells, shout shrill.

sn: मारुद्य संध्याभ्रगिरिप्रकाशः प्रासं समुद्यम्य मरीचिनद्धं पिशाच एषोऽशनितुल्यवेगः॥
en: That one having the vehemence of the thunder-bolt is Pisacha, that, mounted on a steed in variegated golden trappings, and having the aspect of a mass of evening clouds, or a mountain, (appear) with a prāsa furnished with effulgence.

sn: यश्चैष शूलं निशितं प्रगृह्य विद्युत्प्रभं किंकरवज्रवेगम्। मायाति योऽसौ त्रिशिरा यशस्वी॥
en: That one is the famed Trisiras, that grasping a whetted dart endowed with the splendour of lightning and having the speed of the thunder for its minister, approach, riding a bull-the best of his species-and having the appearance of the Moon himself.

sn: असौ च जीमूतनिकाशरूपः कुम्भः पृथुव्यूढसुजातवक्षाः। विस्फारयन्याति धनुर्विधुन्वन्॥
en: That one looking like a mass of clouds, that, having a broad and beautiful breast and a banner surmounted with the king of serpents, goes in collected carriage, stretching his bow is Kumbha.

sn: यश्चैष जाम्बूनदवज्रजुष्टं दीप्तं सधूमं पिरघं प्रगृह्य। आयाति रक्षोबलकेतुभूतो योऽसौ निकुम्भोऽद्भुतवीरकर्मा॥
en: That one is Nikumbha of wondrous valorous deeds (in battle) that, grasping a flaming and smoky bludgeon embellished with gold and diamonds, come-a very banner of the entire Rāksasa host.

sn: यश्चैष चापासिशरौघजुष्टं पताकिनं पावकदीप्तरूपम्। रथं समास्थाय विभात्युदयो नरान्तकोऽसौ नगशृङ्गयोधी॥
en: That one is Narāntaka, fighting with mountain-peaks, that appear before us, mounted on a car flaming like fire, furnished with pennons and equipped with bows and swords and shafts.

sn: यश्चैव नानाविधघोररॊपैर्व्याघ्रोष्ट्रनागेन्द्रमृगाश्ववक्रैः। भूतैवृतो भाति विवृत्तनेत्रैर्योऽसौ सुराणामपि दर्पहन्ता ॥ यत्रैतदिन्दुप्रतिमं विभातिच्छत्रं सितं सूक्ष्मशलाकमग्र्यम्। अत्रैव रक्षोधिपतिर्महात्मा भूतैर्वृतो रुद्र इवावभाति ॥ असौ किरीटी चलकुण्डलास्यो नगेन्द्रविन्ध्योपमभीमकायः। महेन्द्रवैवस्वतदर्पहन्ता रक्षोधिपः सूर्य इवावभाति ॥
en: That crusher of the hauteur of even the celestials, that surrounded by various spectres of dreadful forms having faces of tigers, or camels, or powerful elephants, or deer, or horses, and with their eyes rolling, where the white umbrella resembling the Moon, shine, graced with slender ribs-the high-souled sovereign of Rākṣasa appear like Rudra himself environed by spectres, the sovereign of the Rākṣasa looked with a diadem, with his countenance graced with pendulous earrings, with a person resembling that monarch of mountains-even Vindhya himself-that humbler of the pride of Indra the Great and Yama, shine like the Sun.

sn: प्रत्युवाच ततो रामो विभीषणमरिंदमः। अहो दीप्तमहातेजा रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः॥ आदित्य इव दुष्प्रेक्ष्यो रश्मिभिर्भाति रावणः। न व्यक्तं लक्षये ह्यस्य रूपं तेजःसमावृतम्॥
en: Then Rāma-repressor of foes-answered Vibhisana, saying, “Alas! Ravana-lord of the Rākşasas-is of exceeding glowing splendour; and Rāvana shine in glory, and is incapable of being gazed at like the Sun himself. And his grace, being enshrouded in his own splendour, I cannot view plainly.

sn: देवदानववीराणां वपुर्नैवंविधं भवेत्। यादृशं राक्षसेन्द्रस्य वपुरेतद्विराजते॥
en: The persons of celestials appear splendid as does the person of the Raksasa-chief.

sn: सर्वे पर्वतसंकाशाः सर्वे पर्वतयोधिनः। सर्वे दीप्तायुधधरा योधास्तस्य महात्मनः॥
en: All the warriors of the high-souled one are like mountain and fight with crags; and all are equipped with flaming weapons.

sn: विभाति रक्षोराजोऽसौ प्रदीप्तीमदर्शनैः। भूतैः परिवृतैस्तीक्ष्णैर्देहवद्भिरिवान्तकः॥
en: And environed by glowing ghosts of dreadful forms and fierce-looking and furnished with material tenements the king of Räkşasas appear imposing like the Destroyer himself.

sn: दिष्ट्यायमद्य पापात्मा मम दृष्टिपथं गतः। अद्य क्रोधं विमोक्ष्यामि सीताहरणसंभवम्॥
en: And by luck it is that today the wickedminded one has come within the range of my vision; and today will I vent my wrath incident to the ravishment of Sītā.

sn: एवमुक्त्वा ततो रामो धनुरादाय वीर्यवान्। लक्ष्मणानुचरस्तस्थौ समुद्धृत्य शरोत्तमम्॥
en: Having said this, Rāma endowed with prowess, eve followed by Laksmana, stood, taking up his bow and pulling out a powerful shaft.
