sn: ततः स रक्षोधिपतिर्महात्मा रक्षांसि तान्याह महाबलानि। द्वारेषु चर्यागृहगोपुरेषु सुनिर्वृतास्तिष्ठत निर्विशङ्काः॥
en: Then that high-souled lord of Rākşasas addressed that mighty host, saying, "Do you casting off fear stay at ease, at the gateways, high ways, and the edifices (in Lankā).

sn: इहागतं मां सहितं भवद्भिर्वनौकसश्छिद्रमिदं विदित्वा। शून्यां पुरीं दुष्प्रसहां प्रमथ्य प्रधर्षयेयुः सहसा समेताः॥
en: Taking note of this lapse, viz., that you have all come hither with me, the wood-rangers in a body, subduing the empty city incapable of being withstood, shall suddenly put (all) to straits.

sn: विसर्जयित्वा सचिवांस्ततस्तान् गतेषु रक्षःसु यथानियोगम्। व्यदारयद्वानरसागरौधं महाझषः पूर्णमिवार्णवौघम्॥
en: Then leaving those counsellors, (Ravana) on the Raksasa having departed agreeably to his injunction, dived into that ocean of monkeys, like a mighty fish diving into the waves of over brimming deep.

sn: तमापतन्तं सहसा समीक्ष्य दीप्तेषुचापं युधि राक्षसेन्द्रम्। महत्समुत्पाट्य महीधराग्रं दुद्राव रक्षोधिपति हरीशः॥
en: Seeing the lord of Rākşasas, furnished with flaming deep. And seeing the lord of Rākşasas, furnished with flaming a bow and arrows, suddenly rushing, the king of monkeys uprooting a mighty mountain-top, darted against the sovereign of the Rākşasa.

sn: तच्छैलशृङ्गं बहुवृक्षसार्नु प्रगृह्य चिक्षेप निशाचराय। तमापतन्तं सहसा समीक्ष्य चिच्छेद बाणैस्तपनीयपुखैः।।
en: Taking up that mountain-peak having its sides covered with innumerable trees, he hurled it at the night ranger. And seeing it descend swiftly, (Rāvana) in battle severed the same by means of gold-knobbed shafts.

sn: तस्मिन्प्रवृद्धोत्तमसानुवृक्षे शृङ्गे विदीर्णे पतिते पृथिव्याम्। महाहिकल्पं शरमन्तकाभं समादधे राक्षसलोकनाथः॥
en: On that gigantic peak furnished with fair sides filled with trees, falling to the earth, severed in pieces, the lord of Råkşasas took up an arrow, resembling a mighty serpent and having the splendour of the Destroyer himself.

sn: स तं गृहीत्वानिलतुल्यवेगं सविस्फुलिङ्गज्वलनप्रकाशम्। बाणं महेन्द्राशनितुल्यवेगं चिक्षेप सुग्रीववधाय रुष्टः॥
en: Taking that shaft endowed with the vehemence of the wind, flaming like a fire aglow, and having the impetuosity of the great Indra's thunder-bolt, (Ravana) hurled it in rage to compass the destruction of Sugrīva.

sn: स सायको रावणबाहुमुक्तः शक्राशनिस्पर्शवपुः प्रकाशम् सुग्रीवमासाध्य बिभेद वेदाग्दहेरिता क्रौञ्चमिवोग्रशक्तिः॥
en: Even as the fierce dart discharged by Guha' had pierced Krauñca, that shaft shot by Rāvana, rushing in violence at Sugrīva possessed of a person having the touch of Sakra's thunder-bolt, pierced it.

sn: स सायकार्तो विपरीतचेताः कूजन्पृथिव्यां निपपात वीरः। तं वीक्ष्य भूमौ पतितं विसंज्ञं नेदुः प्रहृष्टा युधि यातुधानाः॥
en: Thereat, agonised by the shaft, that hero, with his senses bewildered, dropped down to the ground with shrieks. And seeing him down on the earth bereft of his senses, the Yātudhānas were filled with rejoicing.

sn: ततो गवाक्षो गवयः सुषेणस्त्वथर्षभो ज्योतिमुखो नलश्च। शैलान्समुत्पाट्य विवृद्धकायाः प्रदुद्रुवुस्तं प्रति राक्षसेन्द्रम्॥
en: Then Gavaksa and Gavaya, Susena, Rsabha, Jyotimukha and Nala, uprooting crags and magnifying their bodies, rushed against the lord of Raksasas.

sn: तेषां प्रहारान्स चकार मोघान् राक्षोधिपो बाणशतैः शिताग्रैः। तान्वानरेन्द्रानापि बानजालैर्बिभेद जाम्बॊनदचित्रपुङ्खैः॥ ते वानरेन्द्रारित्रदशारिबाणैर्भिन्ना निपेतुर्भुवि भीमकायाः।। ततस्तु तद्वानरसैन्यमुग्रं प्रच्छादयामास स बाणजालैः। ४४॥
en: The lord of Rākşasas with hundreds of shafts having sharpened heads, rendered their strokes fruitless. And then he rived those foremost of monkeys with showers of arrows having variegated golden knobs, and covered those fierce monkey-ranks with networks of arrows.

sn: ते वध्यमानाः पतिताश्च वीरा नानद्यमाना भयशल्यविद्धाः। शाखामृगा रावणसायकार्ता जग्मुः शरण्यं शरणं स्म रामम्॥ ततो महात्मा स धनुर्धनुष्मानादाय रामः सहसा जगाम। तं लक्ष्मणः प्राञ्जलिरभ्युपेत्य उवाच रामं परमार्थयुक्तम्॥
en: On being sore assailed and falling in consequence, those heroes, the monkeys, pierced with terrific arrows, and distressed with the shafts of Rāvana, emitting cries, sought the shelter of Rāma worthy of being sought. Then the high-souled and excellent bowman-Rāma, taking his bow, at once sallied forth. And thereat, Laksmana, approaching Rama, with joined hands addressed him words couching prime import.

sn: काममार्य सुपर्याप्तो वधायास्य दुरात्मनः। विधमिष्याम्यहं चैतमनुजानीहि मां विभो॥
en: O noble one, I alone am fit to compass the destruction of this wicked-minded one. I will slay him. Do you, O master, permit me.

sn: तमब्रवीन्महातेजा रामः सत्यपराक्रमः। गच्छ यत्नपरश्चाप भव लक्ष्मण संयुगे॥
en: To him replied Rāma of exceeding energy, having truth for his prowess, “Go then O Lakşmaņa, and put forth your utmost exertions in the encounter.

sn: रावणो हि महावीर्यो रणेऽ दुतपराक्रमः। त्रैलोक्येनापि संक्रुद्धो दुष्प्रसह्यो न संशयः॥
en: Rāvana is forsooth endowed with mighty energy, and his prowess in battle is wonderful. Without doubt, when enraged, he is incapable of being borne by this triple world.

sn: तस्याच्छिद्राणि मार्गस्व स्वच्छिद्राणि च लक्षय। चक्षुषा धनुषात्मानं गोपायस्व समाहितः॥
en: Do you keep an eye on his shortcomings as you should watch your own failings. Being always on the alert, you must with your eyes as much as your bow protect yourself.

sn: राघवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा संपरिष्वज्य पूज्य च। अभिवाद्य च रामाय ययौ सौमित्रिराहवे॥
en: Hearing Rāghava's speech, Sumitrā's son, embracing Rāma, and saluting him and paying him his respect, went forth to battle.

sn: स रावणं वारणहस्तबाहुं ददर्श भीमोद्यतदीप्तचापम्। प्रच्छादयन्तं शरवृष्टिजालैस्तान्वानरान्भिनविकीर्णदेहान्। ५१।।
en: And (going to the field), he found Ravana, endowed with arms resembling the trunks of elephants, wielding his dreadful and flaming bow, and covering with showers of arrows those monkeys, whose bodies had been swarming with shafts.

sn: तमालोक्य महातेजा हनूमान्मारुतात्मजः। निवार्य शरजालानि विदुद्राव स रावणम्॥
en: Seeing Răvaņa, the exceedingly powerful Hanuman-son to the Wind-god, resisting that downpour of arrows, charged him vehemently.

sn: रथं तस्य समासाद्य बाहुमुद्यम्य दक्षिणम्। त्रासयनरावणं धीमान्हनूमान्वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
en: Coming at his car, the intelligent Hanumān, uplifting his right arm and terrifying Rāvana, said.

sn: देवदानवगन्धर्वैर्यक्षैश्च सह राक्षसैः। अवध्यत्वं त्वया प्राप्तं वानरेभ्यस्तु ते भयम्। ५४।।
en: Incapable of being slain by gods, Dānavas or Gandharvas, Yaksas or Raksasas, Fear has (at last), found you, coming even from monkeys.

sn: एष मे दक्षिणो बाहुः पञ्चशाखः समुद्यतः। विधमिष्यति ते देहे भूतात्मानं चिरोषितम्।५५ ।।
en: This my upraised right arm furnished with five fingers shall rod you of your soul long resident (in your body).

sn: श्रुत्वा हनूमतो वाक्यं रावणो भीमविक्रमः। संरक्तनयनः क्रोधादिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Hearing Hanuman's words, Ravana possessed of dreadful prowess, with his eyes reddened in wrath, said these words.

sn: क्षिप्रं प्रहर निःशङ्कं स्थिरां कीर्तिमवाप्नुहि। ततस्त्वां ज्ञातविक्रान्तं नाशयिष्यामि वानर॥
en: Strike you swift maugre fear; and acquire lasting renown. And, O monkey, having (at first) taken the measure of your might, will I finish you.

sn: रावणस्य वचः श्रुत्वा वायुसूनुर्वचोऽब्रवीत्। प्रहतं हि मया पूर्वमक्षं तव सुतं स्मर॥
en: Hearing Rāvana's words, the offspring of the Wind-god said, "(First) remember you your sonAkşa-slaughtered by me !"

sn: एवमुक्तो महातेजा रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः। आजघानानिलसुतं तलेनोरसि वीर्यवान्।। स तलाभिहतस्तेन चचाल च मुहुर्मुहुः। ५९।।
en: Thus addressed, the exceedingly energetic lord of the Rākṣasas possessed of prowess dealt a slap to the offspring of the Wind-god. Struck with his slap, he shook momentarily.

sn: स्थितो मुहुर्त तेजस्वी स्थैर्य कृत्वा महामतिः। आजघान च संक्रुद्धस्तलेनैवामरद्विषम्॥
en: And staying for a moment and calling up fortitude, that magnanimous one administered a slap to the foe of the immortals.

sn: ततः स तेनाभिहतो वानरेण महात्मना। दशग्रीवः समाधूतो यथा भूमितलेऽचलः॥
en: Hit by the high souled monkey, the Tennecked one trembled, as tremble a mountain during an earthquake.

sn: संग्रामे तं तथा दृष्ट्वा रावणं तलताडितम्। ऋषयो वानराः सिद्धा नेदुर्देवाः सुरासुरैः॥
en: Witnessing Răvaņa struck with a slap (by Hanumān saints and Siddhas and celestials and the Asuras shouted in glee.

sn: अथाश्वस्य महातेजा रावणो वाक्यमब्रवीत्। साधु वानर वीर्येण श्लाघनीयोऽसि मे रिपुः॥
en: Then attaining a little respite, Ravana said, “Well done, O monkey. In prowess you are a foe I pride in."

sn: रावणेनैवमुक्तस्तु मारुतिर्वाक्यमब्रवीत्। धिगस्तु मम वीर्यस्य यत्त्वं जीवसि रावण ॥
en: Thus addressed by Ravana, the Wind-god's son said, "Fie on my prowess seeing that you breath yet, O Rāvana.

sn: सकृत्तु प्रहरेदानी दुर्बुद्धे किं विकत्थसे। ततस्त्वां मामको मुष्टिर्नयिष्यति यमक्षयम्॥
en: Strike at the same time, O perverse one. Why did you bluster? And then my blow shall despatch you to the mansions of Yama.

sn: ततो मारुतिवाक्येन कोपस्तस्य प्रजज्वले। संरक्तनयनो यत्नान्मुष्टिमावृत्य दक्षिणम्।। पातयामासवेगेन वानरोरसि वीर्यवान्।६६।।
en: At the speech of the Wind-god's son, his ire flamed up. And then that one endowed with prowess clenching his right fist carefully, let it alight a main on the monkey's chest.

sn: हनूमान्वक्षसि व्यूढे संचचाल पुनः पुनः। विह्वलं तं तदा दृष्ट्वा हनूमन्तं महाबलम्॥ रथेनातिरथः शीघ्रं नीलं प्रतिसमभ्यगात्।
en: Hit at his spacious chest, Hanumān shook over and over again. And seeing the mighty Hanumān overwhelmed, that powerful carwarrior ascended on his car, approached Nīla.

sn: राक्षसानामधिपतिर्दशग्रीवः प्रतापवान्॥ पन्नगप्रतिमैर्भीमैः परमर्माभिभेदनैः। शरैरादीपयामास नीलं हरिचभूपतिम्॥
en: The powerful lord of Raksasas-the Tennecked one-made that general of forces-Nilaaflame with dreadful shafts entering into the vitals, resembling snakes.

sn: स शरौघसमायस्तो नीलो हरिचमूपतिः। करेणैकेन शैलाग्रं रक्षोधिपतयेऽसृजन्॥
en: Assailed with shafts, Nila-leader of monkeyswith one arm took up a mountain-top and hurled it at the lord of Rākşasa.

sn: हनूमानपि तेजस्वी समाश्वस्तो महामनाः। विप्रेक्षमाणो युद्धेप्सुः सरोषमिदमब्रवीत्।७१।। नीलेन सह संयुक्तं रावणं राक्षसेश्वरम्। अन्येन युध्यमानस्य न युक्तमभिधावनम्॥
en: The energetic and high-minded Hanumăn, attaining respite, eager for encounter, seeing (the fight between the Raksasa and the monkey), wrought up with rage said, “It is not meet for me to attack Rāvaņa-lord of Rākşasas-engaged with Nila."

sn: रावणोऽथ महातेजास्तं शृङ्गं सप्तभिः शरैः। आजधान सुतीक्ष्णाग्रैस्तद्धिशीणं पपात ह।७३।।
en: The highly powerful Rāvana, by means of seven shafts with sharpened points, hit at the mountain-top; and shivered in pieces, it fell (to the earth).

sn: तद्विशीर्णं गिरेः शृङ्गं दृष्ट्वा हरिचमूपतिः। कालाग्निरिव जज्वाल कोपेन वरवीरहा। ७४ ।।
en: Seeing that mountain peak shattered, that general of the monkey-forces-slayer of hostile heroes-flamed up in wrath like the fire at the universal wreck.

sn: सोऽश्वकर्णदुमाशालांश्चूतांश्चापि सुपुष्पितान्। अन्यांश्च विविधान्वृक्षानीलश्चिक्षेप संयुगे।७५ ।।
en: In that encounter Nīla discharged Aśvakarņa trees, and sālas, and mangoes in full flower, and also various other trees.

sn: स तान्वृक्षान्समासाद्य प्रतिचिच्छेद रावणः। अभ्यवर्षच्च घोरेण शरवर्षेण पावकिम्॥
en: Ravana, getting at the trees, severed them (by means of his arrows), and poured on the Firegod's son terrific showers of shafts.

sn: अभिवृष्टः शरौघेण मेघेनेव महाबलः। ह्रस्वं कृत्वा ततो रूपं ध्वजाग्रे निपपात ह।७७॥
en: Assailed with fearful showers of arrows as with a mass of clouds, that one endowed with eminent strength, decreasing his dimensions, dropped on the top of Ravana's banner.

sn: पावकात्मजमालोक्य ध्वजाग्रे समवस्थितम्। जज्वाल रावणः क्रोधात्ततो नीलो ननाद च। ७८ ।।
en: Seeing the son of the Fire-god descend on the top of his banner. Råvana was fired with ire, and Nila shouted (thereat).

sn: ध्वजाग्रे धनुषश्चाग्रे किरीटाग्रे च तं हरिम्। लक्ष्मणोऽथ हनूमांश्च रामश्चापि सुविस्मिताः।७९ ।।
en: Seeing the monkey (now) at the top of the banner, and (now) at the end of his bow, and (now) at the crest of his tiara, Laksmana and Hanuman and Rāma were stuck with astonishment.

sn: रावणोऽपि महातेजाः कपिलाघवविस्मितः। अस्त्रमाहारयामास दीप्ताग्नेयमद्भुतम्॥
en: Rāvana also endowed with exceeding energy, astonished at the lightness of the monkey, took up a wonderful flaming fiery weapon.

sn: ततस्ते चुक्रुशुहृष्टा लब्धलक्षाः प्लवंगमाः। नीललाघवसंभ्रान्तं दृष्ट्वा रावणमाहवे॥
en: The monkeys seeing Rāvana bewildered, and delighted thereat, set up shouts.

sn: वानराणां च नादेन संरब्धो रावणस्तदा। संभ्रमाविष्टहृदयो न किंचित्प्रत्यपद्यत।॥
en: Rāvana enraged at the shouts of the monkeys, with his heart overwhelmed with agitation, could not address himself to any affort.

sn: आग्नेयेनापि संयुक्तं गृहीत्वा रावणः शरम्। ध्वजशीर्णस्थितं नीलमुर्दक्षत निशाचरः॥
en: Then taking a fiery shaft and setting the same on his bow, that night-ranger Rāvaņa gazed at Nila who was on the tip of his banner.

sn: ततोऽब्रवीन्महातेजा रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः। कपे लाघवयुक्तोऽसि मायया परया सह॥
en: Then exceedingly energetic lord of the Rākşasas said, O monkey, by virtue of your skill in illusion, you are furnished with lightness.

sn: जीवितं खलु रक्षस्य यदि शक्तोऽसि वानर। तानि तान्यात्मरूपाणि सृजसि त्वमनेकशः॥ तथापि त्वां मया मुक्त: नायकोऽस्त्रप्रयोजितः। जीवितं परिरक्षन्तं जीविताभ्रंशयिष्यति॥
en: But O monkey, if you can, preserve your life. You transform yourself into many shapes. Yet this shaft of mine discharged from my weapon, shall deprive of your life you that are preserving it.

sn: एवमुक्त्वा महाबाहु रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः। संधाय बाणमस्त्रेण चमूपतिमताडयत्॥
en: Having said this, the mighty-armed Ravanalord of the Rākşasas-fixing his shaft on his bow, shot it at the general.

sn: सोऽस्त्रमुक्तेन बाणेन नीलो वक्षसि ताडितः। निर्दह्यमानः सहसा स पपात महीतले॥
en: Nila, struck at the chest with that arrow, which had been shot (by Ravana), burning, suddenly fell down to the earth.

sn: पितृमाहात्म्यसंयोगादात्मनश्चापि तेजसा। जानुभ्यामपतद्भूभौ न तु प्राणैर्वियुज्यत॥
en: And by virtue of the greatness of his sire and also of his own energy, he went to the earth on his knees, but was not utterly deprived of life.

sn: विसंजं वानरं दृष्ट्वा दशग्रीवो रणोत्सुकः। रथेनाम्बुदनादेन सौमित्रिमभिदुद्रुवे॥
en: Seeing the monkey deprived of his senses, the Ten-necked one, eager for encounter, riding a car emitting a rattle resembling the rumbling of clouds, darted against Sumitra's son.

sn: आसाद्य रणमध्ये तं वारयित्वा स्थितो ज्वलन्। धनुर्विस्फारयामास राक्षसेन्द्रः प्रतापवान्॥
en: Entering into the arena of fight and posted there flaming, the powerful lord of the Rakşasas, baffling (the foe), kept stretching his bow.

sn: तमाह सौमित्रिरदीनसत्त्वो विस्फारयन्तं धनुरप्रमेयम्। अवेहि मामद्य निशाचरेन्द्र न वानरांस्त्वं प्रतियोद्धमर्हसि ॥
en: As that one of immeasurable prowess kept stretching his bow. And as that one of immeasurable prowess kept stretching his bow, Sumitrā's son of unflagging mettle, addressed him saying, “O lord of night-rangers, do you today try me in encounter. You ought not to strive with the monkeys."

sn: स तस्य वाक्यं प्रतिपूर्णघोषं ज्याशब्दमुग्रं च निशम्य राजा। आसाद्य सौमित्रिमुपस्थितं तं रोषान्वितं वाचमुवाच रक्षः॥
en: Hearing Saumitri's speech uttered in a full voice, as well as the terrific twangs of his bowstring, that Raksasa-the king-approaching Sumitrā son staying in the field, spoke to him wrathfully.

sn: दिष्ट्यासि मे राघव दृष्टिमार्ग प्राप्तऽन्तगामी विपरीतबुद्धिः। अस्मिन्क्षणे यास्यसि मृत्युलोकं संसाद्यमानो मम बाणजालैः।१४॥
en: O Raghu's son, by my luck have you of perverse sense, finding your fate come within the range of my ken. This very instant, tormented with the springs of my shafts, you will repair to the regions of Death.

sn: तमाह सौमित्रिरविस्मयानो गर्जन्तमुवृत्तशिताग्रदंष्ट्रम्। राजन्न गर्जन्ति महाप्रभावा विकत्थसे पापकृतां वरिष्ठ।१५॥
en: Thereat Sumitra's son, without being overwhelmed with wonder (on witnessing Rāvana's prowess), addressed that one furnished with large and sharp teeth, setting up roars, “O king, those who are (really) endowed with prowess, do no storm. O prince of sinners, in vain you vauntest.

sn: जानामि वीर्यं तव राक्षसेन्द्र बलं प्रतापं च पराक्रमं च रागच्छ किं मोघविकत्थनेन।१६॥
en: O lord of Raksasas, I know your prowess and strength and energy and vigour. Here am I stationed, bow and shafts in hand. Come you. What is the use of vain-glorious self-laudation?

sn: स एवमुक्तः कुपितः ससर्ज रक्षोधिपः सप्त शरान्सुपुङ्खान्।। ताल्लक्ष्मणः काञ्चनचित्रपुङ्खैश्चिच्छेद् बाणैर्निशिताग्रधारैः॥
en: Thus accosted, the Raksasa monarch, growing wroth, discharged seven shafts furnished with knobs. Thereupon Lakşmaņa split them up with sharp-pointed arrows having variegated golden knobs.

sn: तान्प्रेक्षमाणः सहसा निकृत्तान्निकृत्तभोगानिव पन्नगेन्द्रान्। लङ्केश्वरः क्रोधवशं जगाम ससर्ज चान्यानिशितान्पृषत्कान्॥
en: They suddenly severed like powerful serpents cut.off, Lanka's lord came under the away of passion, and discharged other whetted arrows.

sn: स बाणवर्षं तु ववर्ष तीवं रामानुजः कार्मुकसंप्रयुक्तम्। क्षुरार्धचन्द्रोत्तमकर्णभल्लैः शरांश्च चिच्छेद न चुक्षुभे च ॥
en: Rāma's younger brother poured showers of arrows from his bow; and, planting himself at his post, cut off those arrows (of his adversary) by means of .razors, and crescents, and excellent karnas and darts.

sn: स बाणजालान्यपि तानि तानि मोघानि पश्यंत्रिदशारिराजः। विसिस्मिये लक्ष्मणलाघवेन पुनश्च बाणानिशितान्मुमोच॥
en: Seeing his arrowy net-v orks rendered ineffectual, that enemy of the celestials-the kingwas seized with wonderment, and again shot sharpened arrows.

sn: स लक्ष्मणश्चापि शिताशिताग्रान् महेन्द्रतुल्योऽशनिभीमवेगान्। संधाय चापे ज्वलनप्रकाशान् ससर्ज रक्षोधिपतेर्वधाय॥
en: Laksmana also, resembling Indra the Great, setting on his bow sharpened, sharp-pointed, flaming, and luminous shafts, endowed with the dreadful vehement impetus of the thunder-bolt, discharged (them) to compass the destruction of the lord of Räkşasa.

sn: स तान्प्रचिच्छेद हि राक्षसेन्द्रः शिताशरांल्लक्ष्मणमाजघान। शरेण कालाग्निसमप्रभेण स्वयंभुदत्तेन ललाटदेशे॥
en: Thereat the Rākşasa sovereign cut off those whetted arrows; and smote Lakşmaņa in the foreheads with an arrow resembling the Fire of Dooms-day in energy, which had been conferred on him by the Self-create.

sn: स लक्ष्मणो रावनसायकार्तश्चचाल चापं शिथिलं प्रगृह्य । पुनश्च संज्ञां प्रतिलभ्य कृच्छ्राच्चिच्छेद चापं त्रिदशेन्द्रशत्रोः॥
en: Laksmana, tortured with Ravan's arrow, shook, loosely holding his bow; and then recovering his consciousness after undergoing extreme agony he severed the bow of the foe of the foremost of celestials.

sn: निकृत्तचापं त्रिभिराजघान बाणैस्तदा दाशरथिः शिताग्रैः। स सायकार्तो विचचाल राजा कृच्छ्राच्च संज्ञां पुनराससाद ॥
en: Having cut off Ravana's bow, Dasaratha's son hit (him) with three sharp-pointed arrows. And the king smarting under the shafts, with much ado regained his consciousness.

sn: स कृत्तचापः शरताडितश्च मेदागात्रो रुधिरावसिक्तः। जग्राह शक्तिं स्वयमुग्रशक्तिः स्वयंभुदत्तां युधि देवशत्रुः॥
en: The enemy of the immortals of terrific power with his bow severed, and himself hit with shafts, and his body covered with fat, and himself washed in blood, took up a dart conferred on him by the Self-create.

sn: स तां सधूमानलसंनिकाशा वित्रासनां संयति वानराणाम्। चिक्षेप शक्तिं तरसा ज्वलन्ती सौमित्रये राक्षसराष्ट्रनाथः॥
en: The sovereign of the Rākşasas and their lord in that encounter hurled at Sumitrā's son the dart resembling smoking fire, sending up living flames, and striking terror into the monkeys.

sn: तामापतन्तीं भरतानुजोस्त्रैर्जधान बाणैश्च हुताग्निकल्पैः। तथापि सा तस्य विवेश शक्तिर्भुजान्तरं दाशरथेविशालम्॥
en: As it coursed on, Bharata's younger brother resisted it with arrows resembling a sacrificial flame. Yet the dart pierced into the broad arm of Dasaratha's son.

sn: स शक्तिमाशक्तिसमाहतः सन् जज्वाल भूमौ स रघुप्रवीरः। तं विह्वलन्तं सहसाभ्युपेत्य जग्राह राजा तरसा भुजाभ्याम्॥
en: Smite with the dart, that hero of the Raghu race, although possessed of strength, was aglow. And the king at once with his arms seized that one, who had been deprived of his senses.

sn: हिमवान्मन्दरो मेरुस्त्रैलोक्यं वा सहामरैः। शक्यं भुजाभ्यामुद्धर्तुं न शक्यो भरतानुजः॥
en: But he that could with his arms wield Himavan or Mandara or Meru or the triple world itself along with the immortals, could not (for all his strength) lift up Bharata's younger brother.

sn: शक्त्या ब्राया तु सौमित्रिस्ताडितोऽपि स्तनान्तरे। विष्णोरमीमांस्यभागमात्मानं प्रत्यनुस्मरत्॥
en: And hit at his chest by the dart of Brahmā, Sumitrā's son remembered that he was verily a portion of Vişņu himself.

sn: ततो दानवदर्पघ्नं सौमित्रिं देवकण्टकः। तं पीडयित्वा बाहुभ्यां न प्रभुर्लङ्घनेऽभवत्॥
en: Then pressing hard Sumitrā's son-that humbler of the hauteur of the Daityas, that thorn in the sides of the celestials-could not move him (from his place).

sn: ततः क्रुद्धो वायुसुतो रावणं समभिद्रवत्। आजघानोरसि क्रुद्धो वज्रकल्पेन मुष्टिना॥
en: Then the Wind-god's offspring waxing wroth rushed at Rāvana, and overwhelmed with rage smote at his chest with his clenched fist resembling the thunderbolt.

sn: तेन मुष्टिप्रहारेण रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः। जानुभ्यामगमद्भूमौ चचाल च पपात च॥
en: And boxed (by Hanumāna), Ravana-lord of the Rākşasas-went down to the ground on his knees, and shook and dropped to the earth.

sn: आस्यैश्च नेत्रैः श्रवणैः पपात रुधिरं बहु। विघूर्णमानो निश्चेष्टो रथोपस्य उपाविशत्॥
en: And blood gushed out in streams from his mouths and eyes and arms, and staggered and senseless, he sat down on the platform of his car.

sn: विसंज्ञो मूर्च्छितश्चासीन च स्थानं समालभत्। विसंज्ञं रावणं दृष्ट्वा समरे भीमविक्रमम्॥ ऋषयो वानराश्चैव नेदुर्देवाश्च सासुराः।
en: He was rendered insensible with his senses lost; and he knew no where he was. And seeing Rāvana endued with terrific prowess, rendered insensible in the encounter, saints and monkeys and gods with the Asuras set up shouts.

sn: हनूमानथ तेजस्वी लक्ष्मणं रावणार्दितम्॥ आनयद्राघवाभ्याशं बाहुभ्यां परिगृह्य तम्। वायुसूनोः सुहृत्त्वेन भक्त्या परमया च सः। शत्रूणामप्यकम्प्योऽपि लघुत्वमगमत्कपेः॥
en: Then energetic Hanumān taking Lakşmaņa racked by Rävaņa, with his arms brought him before Rāghava. And albeit incapable of being moved by the foes, (Laksmana), on account of the friendship of the Wind-god's offspring as well as the high reverence in which he was held by Hanumān, became extremely light to the monkey.

sn: तं समुत्सृज्य सा शक्तिः सौमित्रिं युधि निर्जितम्। रावणस्य रथे तस्मिन्स्थानं पुनरुपागमत्॥
en: Then that dart, renouncing Sumitra's son vanquished in fight, again sought its place in Ravana's car.

sn: रावणोऽपि महातेजाः प्राप्य संज्ञां महाहवे। आददे निशितान्बाणाञ्जग्राह च महद्धनुः॥
en: The exceedingly powerful Răvaņa recovering his consciousness in the dread encounter, took up whetted shafts and seized a mighty bow.

sn: आश्वस्तश्च विशल्यश्च लक्ष्मणः शत्रुसूदनः। विष्णोर्भागममीमांस्यमात्मानं प्रत्यनुस्मरन्॥
en: That finisher of foes-Lakşmaņa-recovered the exercise of his senses, and had his entire person perfectly healed, on his recalling that he verily was a part and parcel of Vişņu himself.

sn: निपातितमहावीरां वानराणां महाचमूम्। राघवस्तु रणे दृष्ट्वा रावणं समभिद्रवत्॥
en: Witnessing the mighty army of the monkeys and the redoubted heroes brought down in the conflict, Rāghava rushed at Ravana.

sn: अथैनमनुसंक्रम्य हनूमान्वाक्यमब्रवीत्। मम पृष्ठं समारुह्य राक्षसं शास्तुमर्हसि ॥ विष्णुर्यथा गरुत्मन्तमारुह्यामरवैरिणम्।
en: Thereat drawing near to him, Hanuman said to him, "It behove you to chastise the foe ascending my back, even as Vişņu chastise the enemies of the immortals, riding Garutmān."

sn: तच्छ्रुत्वा राघवो वाक्यं वायुपुत्रेण भाषितम्॥ अथारुरोह सहसा हनूमन्तं महाकपिम्।
en: Hearing the words spoken by Hanumān, Rāghava at once got up on that gigantic monkey; and that master of men beheld Rāvana in battle.

sn: रथस्थं रावणं संख्ये ददर्श मनुजाधिपः॥ तमालोक्य महातेजाः प्रदुद्राव स रावणम्। वैरोचनमिव क्रुद्धो विष्णुरभ्युद्यतायुधः॥
en: Seeing him, that highly powerful one darted against Rāvaņa, even as the enraged Vişnu had rushed against Virocana's son, upraising his weapons.

sn: ज्याशब्दमकरोत्तीव्र वज्रनिष्पेषनिष्ठुरम्। गिरा गम्भीरया रामो राक्षसेन्द्रमुवाच ह॥
en: He sharply twanged his bow-string sounding like the terrific crash of thunder, and then in solemn tones, Rāma addressed the lord of Răks asas, Saying.

sn: तिष्ठ तिष्ठ मम त्वं हि कृत्वा विप्रियमीदृशम्। क्व नु राक्षसशार्दूल गत्वा मोक्षमवाप्स्यसि॥
en: Stay, stay, having done me such wrong. Repairing whither, shall you, O powerful Raksasa, attain respite?

sn: यदीन्द्रवैवस्वतभास्करान्वा स्वयंभुवैश्वानरशंकरान्वा। गमिष्यसि त्वं दशधा दिशो वा तथापि ने नाद्य गतो विमोक्ष्यसे ॥
en: Even if you should seek Yama or Indra or the Sun-son to Vivaśvăn-or the Self-sprung or the Fire-god or Sankara himself, or go to the ten cardinal points in ten portions, yet shall you not, so resorting attain deliverance.

sn: यश्चैष शक्त्या निहतस्त्वयाद्य गच्छन्विषादं सहसाभ्युपेत्य। स एष रक्षोगणराजमृत्युः सपुत्रपौत्रस्य तवाद्य युद्धे ॥
en: And (Laksmana), going forth to the fight, has been wounded with the dart and has suddenly been stupefied. But, o king of the Rākşasa today in conflict Death shall claim for his own you and your sons and grandsons.

sn: एतेन चात्यद्भुतदर्षनानि शरैर्जनस्थानकृतालयानि। चतुर्दशान्यात्तवरायुधानि रक्षः सहस्राणि निषूदितानि ॥
en: By me with my shafts have been slaughtered four and ten thousand Rākṣasa residing in Janasthāna, wielding excellent weapons.

sn: राघवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा राक्षसेन्द्रो महाबलः। वायुपुत्रं महावेगं वहन्तं राघवं रणे॥ रोषेण महताविष्टः पूर्ववैरमनुस्मरन्। आजघान शरैर्दीप्तैः कालानलशिखोपमैः॥
en: Hearing Rāghava's words, the exceedingly strong lord of the Rākşasas, overwhelmed with a mighty wrath, recalling enmity a gone, with burning shafts resembling the fire of Doom hit in encounter the exceedingly impetuous offspring of the Wind-god, who was bearing Rāghava.

sn: राक्षसेनाहते तस्य ताडितस्यापि सायकैः। स्वभावतेजोयुक्तस्य भूयस्तेजोऽभ्यवर्धत॥
en: Although struck and resisted by the Rākşasa with arrows, the energy of that one, endowed by nature with prowess-increased greatly.

sn: ततो रामो महातेजा रावणेन कृतव्रणम्। दृष्ट्वा प्लवगशार्दूलं क्रोधस्य वशमेयिवान्॥
en: The exceedingly energetic Rāma, on seeing that foremost of the monkeys wounded by Ravana, was mastered by wrath.

sn: तस्याभिसंक्रम्य रथं सचक्रं साश्वध्वजच्छत्रमडापताकम्। ससारथिं साशनिशूलखङ्गं रामः प्रचिच्छेद शितैः शराग्रैः॥
en: Rāma, closing with his enemy, by means of whetted arrow-points severed in pieces his car together with the wheels and the steeds, the banner, the umbrella, and the majestic streamer, as well as with the charioteers and the thunderbolts and darts and swords.

sn: अथेन्द्रशत्रु तरसा जघान बाणेन वज्राशनिसंनिभेन। भुजान्तरे व्यूढसुजातरूपे वज्रेण मेरुं भगवानिवेन्द्रः॥
en: Then as the reverend Indra cleave Meru with his thunder-bolt, (Raghava) swiftly smote on Rāvaņa's spacious and shapely chest with a shaft resembling Vajra and the thunderbolt.

sn: यो वज्रपाताशनिसंनिपातान् न चुक्षुभे नापि चचाल राजा। स रामबानाभिहतो भृशार्तश्चचाल चापं च मुमोच वीरः॥
en: That the king hero-who had not smarted nor shaken under the impetus of Vajra and the thunder-bolt, assailed with the arrows of Răma and agonised in consequence, shock and lost hold of his bow.

sn: तं विह्वलन्तं प्रसमीक्ष्य रामः समाददे दीप्तमथार्धचन्द्रम्। तेनार्कवर्णं सहसा किरीटं चिच्छेद रक्षोधिपतेर्महात्मा॥
en: Seeing him overwhelmed, Ráma took up a flaming half-moon and with the same at once severed the sun-bright tiara of the high-souled sovereign of the Rākşasas.

sn: तं निर्विषाशीविषसंनिकाशं शान्तार्चिषं सूर्यमिवाप्रकाशम्। गतश्रियं कृत्तकिरीटकूटमुवाच रामो युधि राक्षसेन्द्रम् ॥
en: Rāma in the encounter addressed the lord of Rākşasas, resembling a serpent bereft of venom, shorn of his splendour, like to the sun shrouded (in mist), without his wonted grace, and having his entire tiara riven-saying.

sn: कृतं त्वया कर्म महत्सुभीमं हतप्रवीरश्च कृतस्त्वथाहम्। तस्मात्परिश्रान्त इति व्यवस्य न त्वां शरैर्मृत्युवशं नयामि॥
en: You have in battle) performed high and dreadful deeds, and have also (in-the conflict) slain my foremost heroes. And therefore I know you are fatigued. And for this reason it is that I will not with my shafts bring you to the door of Death.

sn: प्रयाहि जानामि रणार्दितस्त्वं प्रविश्य रात्रिंचरराज लङ्काम्। आश्वस्य निर्याहि रथी सधन्वी तदा बलं प्रेक्ष्यसि मे रथस्थः॥
en: Go you. I know that you are worn out with fight. Therefore, O king of night-rangers, enter Lankā. Havirg a little respite, do you depart on your car along with your bowmen. Afterwards, mounted on your car, shall you behold my power.

sn: स एवमुक्तो हतदर्पहर्षो निकृत्तचापः स हताश्वसूतः। शरादितो भग्नमहाकिरीटो विवेश लङ्कां सहसा स्म राजा॥
en: Thus addressed, the king, with his pride and joy defeated, with his bow severed, and his steeds and charioteer killed himself smarting under. shafts, and having his crown splintered, speedily entered Lankā.

sn: तस्मिन्प्रविष्टे रजनीचरेन्द्रे महाबले दानवदेवशत्रौ। हरीन्विशल्यान्सह लक्ष्मणेन चकार रामः परमाहवाग्रे॥
en: On that foe of the deities and the Dănavas-the puissant lord of the night-rangers-entering (into Lankā), Rāma rendered the monkeys along with Lakşmaņa hale in that fierce conflict.

sn: तस्मिन्प्रभग्ने त्रिदशेन्द्रशत्रौ सुरासुरा भूतगणा दिशश्च। ससागराः सर्वमहोरगाश्च तथैव भूम्यम्बुचराः प्रहृष्टाः॥
en: At the break-down of that foe of the immortals, the celestials and the Asuras, the ghosts and the Cardinal points, and all the mighty serpents together with the oceans and the creatures inhabiting earth and water, felt exceedingly delighted.

sn: स प्रविश्य पुरीं लङ्कां रामबाणभयादितः। भग्नदर्पस्तदा राजा बभूव व्यथितेन्द्रिथः॥
en: Entering the city of Larkā, the king afflicted with the fear of Rāma's arrows, with his pride humbled, was undergoing great torments:

sn: मातंग इव सिंहेन गरुडेनेव पन्नगः। अभिमूतोऽभवद्राजा राघवेण महात्मना॥
en: Overpowered by the high souled Rāghava, the king resembled an elephant defeated by a lion or a serpent defeated by Garuda.

sn: ब्रह्मदण्डप्रतीकानां विद्युच्चलितवर्चसाम्। स्मरराघवबाणानां विव्यथे राक्षसेश्वरः॥
en: Remembering Råghava's arrows resembling a comet risen at the universal wreck, and of the splendour of live lightning, the Raksasa chief was aggrieved.

sn: स काञ्चनमयं दिव्यमाश्रित्य परमासनम्। विप्रेक्षमाणो रक्षांसि रावणो वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
en: Rāma, seated on a superb golden seat and eyeing the Raksasas, spoke this word.

sn: सर्वं तत्खलु मे मोघं यत्तप्तं परमं तपः। यत्समानो महेन्द्रेण मानुषेण विनिर्जितः॥
en: Forsooth all the austere asceticism I have performed go go for nothing, for although resembling the redoubtable Indra, I have been overcome by a mortal.

sn: इदं तद्ब्रह्मणो घोरं वाक्यं मामभ्युपस्थितम्। मानुषेभ्यो विजानीहि भयं त्वमिति तत्तथा॥
en: This dire speech of Brahmā also reverts to my remembrance, Know you that the fear come from a human being.

sn: देवदानवगन्धर्यक्षराक्षसपनगैः। अवध्यत्वं मया प्रोक्तं मानुषेभ्यो न याचितम्॥
en: You are incapable of being slain by deities and Danavas, Gandharvas, Yaksas, Raksasas and serpents. But you have not asked for immunity from men.

sn: तमिमं मानुषं मन्ये रामं दशरथात्मजम्। इक्ष्वाकुकुलजातेन अनरण्येन यत्पुरा॥ उत्पत्स्यति हि मद्वंशपुरुषो राक्षसाधम। यस्त्वां सपुत्रं सामात्यं सबलं साश्वसारथिम्।९।। निहनिष्यति संग्रामे त्वां कुलाधम दुर्मते।
en: I deem even this son of Dasaratha as the occasion of my fear. I was formerly cursed by that lord of the Ikşawaku line-Anaranya-saying, 'O worst of Rākşasas, a person shall spring in my race, who, O wicked-minded one, shall you in battle along with your sons and courtiers and forces and horses and charioteers.

sn: शप्तोऽहं वेदवत्या च यथा सा धर्षिता पुरा ॥ सेयं सीता महाभागा जाता जनकनन्दिनी।
en: I was also cursed by Vedavatī, who was formerly outraged by me. And she is (perchance) born as the exalted daughter of Janaka.

sn: उमा नन्दीश्वरश्चापि रम्भा वरुणकन्यका॥ यथोक्तास्तन्मया प्राप्तं न मिथ्या ऋषिभाषितम्।
en: What had also been uttered by Umā and Nandisvara and Rambhā and Varuna's daughter, has come to pass.

sn: एतदेव समागम्य यत्नं कर्तुमिहार्हथ ॥ राक्षसाश्चापि तिष्ठन्तु चर्यागोपुरमूर्धसु।
en: Taking note of this, you should strive (to the uttermost.) And let the Räkşasas be posted at the gateways, highways, and the walls.

sn: स चाप्रतिमगाम्भीर्यो देवदानवदर्पहा॥ ब्रह्मशापाभिभूतस्तु कुम्भकर्णो विबोध्यताम्।
en: Do you wake up that destroyer of the pride of the deities and then Danavas-Kumbhakarma, endowed with unparalleled gravity, overwhelmed with the curse of Brahmā.

sn: समरे जितमात्मानं प्रहस्तं च निषूदितम्॥ ज्ञात्वा रक्षो भीमबलमादिदेश महाबलः। द्वारेषु यत्नः क्रियतां प्राकारश्चाधिरुह्यताम्॥ निद्रावशसमाविष्टः कुम्भकर्णो विबोध्यताम्।
en: Seeing himself worsted and Prahasta also slain, that Rākşasa endowed with dreadful power issued his orders to the fearful force. “Do you vigilantly guard the gates and mount the wall. And do you wake up Kumbhakarņa come under the sway of slumber.

sn: सुखं स्वपिति निश्चिन्तः कामोपहतचेतनः॥ नव सप्त दशाष्टौ च मासान्स्वपिति राक्षसः। मन्त्रं कृत्वा प्रसुप्तोऽयमितस्तु नवमेऽहनि॥
en: And deprived of his senses through lust, he sleep secure. And the Rākşasa sometimes sleep nine, seven, ten, or eight months away. Of measureless might he has slept for nine months.

sn: तं तु बोधयत क्षिप्रं कुम्भकर्ण महाबलम्। स हि संख्ये महाबाहुः ककुदं सर्वरक्षसाम्। वानरान्राजपुत्रौ च क्षिप्रमेव हनिष्यति॥
en: Therefore, speedily rouse very powerful Kumbhakarņa. Foremost of all the Rākşasas in fight, that long armed one shall speedily slay the monkeys as well as the princes.

sn: एष केतुः परं संख्ये मुख्यो वै सर्वरक्षसाम्। कुम्भकर्णः सदा शेते मूढो ग्राम्यसुखे रतः॥
en: He is a very banner in battle, and the crown of all the Raksasa. But intent on common pleasure, Kumbhakarna, with his senses stupefied, sleep ever.

sn: रामेणाभिनिरस्तस्य संग्रामेऽस्मिन्सुदारुणे। भविष्यति न मे शोकः कुम्भकर्णे विबोधिते॥
en: I have been worsted in fierce fight by Rāma; but on Kumbhakarņa being awakened, my grief shall go.

sn: किं करिष्याम्यहं तेन शक्रतुल्यबलेन हि। ईदृशे व्यसने घोरे यो न साह्याय कल्पते॥
en: If he does not help me in such high peril, what shall I do with his strength resembling the strength of Sakra himself?

sn: ते तु तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा राक्षसेन्द्रस्य राक्षसाः। जग्मुः परमसंभ्रान्ताः कुम्भकर्णनिवेशनम्॥
en: Hearing the words of the lord of the Rākşasas, the Rākşasas, bestirring themselves, went to the abode of Kumbhakarņa.

sn: ते रावणसमादिष्टा मांसशोणितभोजनाः। गन्धं माल्यं महद्भक्ष्यामादाय सहसा ययुः॥
en: And desired by Rāvana, those feeding on flesh and blood went off hurriedly taking perfumes and wreaths and a mass of food.

sn: तां प्रविश्य महाद्वारा सर्वतो योजनायताम्। कुम्भकर्णगुहां रम्यां पुष्पगन्धप्रवाहिनीम्॥ कुम्भकर्णस्य निःश्वासादवधूता महाबलाः। प्रतिष्ठमानाः कृच्छ्रेण यत्नात्प्रविविशुर्गुहाम्॥
en: And entering Kumbhakarņa's charming cave having a wide gateway, measuring a yojana breathing around perfumes of flowers, those highly powerful ones, pushed off by Kumbhakarna's breath, with the utmost energy they could summon up stood their ground and entered the cave.

sn: तां प्रविश्य गुहां रम्यां रत्नकाञ्चनकुट्टिमाम्। ददृशुर्नैर्ऋतव्याघ्राः शयानं भीमविक्रमम्॥
en: Then entering that charming cave having floors paved with gold and gems. those Naiſtas endowed with great strength, saw that one of dreadful prowess, lying down.

sn: ते तु तं विकृतं सुप्तं विकीर्णमिव पर्वतम्। कुम्भकर्ण महानिद्रं समेताः प्रत्यबोधयन्॥ ऊर्ध्वलोमाञ्चिततनुं श्वसन्तमिव पन्नगम्। भ्रामयन्तं विनिःश्वासैः शयानं भीमविक्रमम्॥ भीमनासापुटं तं तु पातालविपुलाननम्। शयने न्यस्तसर्वाङ्ग मेदोरुधिरगन्धिनम्॥ काञ्चनाङ्गदनद्धाङ्गं किरीटेनार्कवर्चसम्। ददृशुर्नैर्ऋतव्याघ्र कुम्भकर्णमरिंदमम्॥
en: Then they together set about waking up the slumbering Kumbhakarņa looking like a hill extended, and sunk in profound slumber; with his body having its down standing on end; lying down; like a sighing serpent; rolling people* with his powerful breath, reposing; possessed of dreadful prowess; having a huge nose; of a person vast as the nether sphere; lying stretched at length; smelling of fat and blood; decked with golden Angadas; and warning a diadem endowed with the splendour of the sun. And (they) saw that subduer of enemies and foremost of Nairtas-Kumbhakarna.

sn: ततश्चक्रुर्महात्मानः कुम्भकर्णस्य चाग्रतः। भूतानां मेरुसंकाशं राशिं परमतर्पणम्॥ मृगाणां महिषाणां च वराहाणां च संचयान्। चकुर्नैर्ऋतशार्दूला राशिमन्त्रस्य चाद्भुतम्॥
en: Then they huge bodied Rākșasas piled up before Kumbhakarma, Meru-like animals for conferring rare gratification and heaps of deer and buffaloes and boars. And the Rākşasas made an astounding heap of rice.

sn: ततः शोणितकुम्भांश्च मांांसानि विविधानि च। पुरस्तात्कुम्भकर्णस्य चक्रुस्त्रिदशशत्रवः॥ लिलिपुश्च परार्थेन चन्दनेन परंतपम्। दिव्यैराश्वासयामासुर्माल्यैर्गन्धैश्च गन्धिभिः॥ धूपगन्धांश्च ससृजुस्तुष्टुवुश्च परंतपम्। जलदा इव चानेदुर्यातुधानास्ततस्ततः॥
en: Then the enemies of the immortals put up before Kumbhakarņa jars of blood and various kinds of food, and smeared that repressor of foes with excellent sandal, and made him inhale perfumes and the aroma of wreaths. And they made (the place) rife with the incense of dhupa, and extolled that smiter of enemies. And then the Yātudhānas roared around here and there like clouds.

sn: शङ्खांश्च पूरयामासुः शशाङ्कसदृशप्रभान्। तुमुलं युगपच्चापि विनेदुश्चाप्यमर्षिताः॥
en: They winded conchs beaming moon-like. And they incapable of being beaten shouted in full chorus.

sn: नेदुरास्फोटयामासुश्चिक्षिपुस्ते निशाचराः। कुम्भकर्णविबोधार्थं चक्रुस्ते विपुलं स्वरम्॥
en: The night-rangers shouted and struck at their arms with their hands and began to pull him. And for rousing Kumbhakarņa, mighty was the din that they raised.

sn: स शङ्खभेरीपणवप्रणादं सास्फोटितक्ष्वेलितसिंहनादम्। दिशो द्रवन्तस्त्रिदिवं किरन्तः श्रुत्वा विहंगाः सहसा निपेतुः॥
en: Hearing those loud sounds of conchs and drums and Papavas; and those proceeding from persons striking at their arms with their hands; and leonine roars, rushing on all sides and riving the very heavens, birds suddenly dropped down.

sn: यदा भृशानिनदैर्महात्मा न कुम्भकर्णो बुबुधे प्रसुप्तः। ततो भुशुण्डीर्मुसलानि सर्वे रक्षोगणास्तं जगृहुर्गदाश्च ॥
en: When the high-souled Kumbhakarņa sleeping soundly did not awake at that terrific tumult, the Raksasas took up Bhusundis and maces.

sn: र्वक्षस्थले मुद्गरमुष्टिभिश्च। सुखप्रसुप्तं भुवि कुम्भकर्ण रक्षांस्युदग्राणि तदा निजघ्नुः॥
en: Then the Raksasas, drawing near, smote Kumbhakarņa sleeping sweetly in the chest with mountain-peaks, maces and clubs.

sn: तस्य निःश्वासवातेन कुम्भकर्णस्य रक्षसः। राक्षसाः कुम्भकर्णस्य स्थातुं शेकुर्न चाग्रतः॥
en: But the Rākşasas could not stay before Kumbhakarņa owing to the hurricane heaving at his breath.

sn: ततः परिहिता गाढं राक्षसा भीमविक्रमाः। मृदङ्गपणवान् शङ्खकुम्भगणांस्तथा॥ दश राक्षससाहस्रं युगपत्पर्यवारयत्। नीलाञ्जनचयाकारं ते तु तं प्रत्यबोधयन्॥
en: Then tightening their cloth (about their waist), those Rākşasas of dreadful prowess sounded Mşdangas and Paņavas, conchs and kumbhas. And ten thousand Rākṣasas together surrounded that one resembling a heap of darkblue collyrium and fell to rousing him.

sn: अभिघ्नन्तो नदन्तश्च न च संबुबुधे तदा। यदा चैनं न शेकुस्ते प्रतिबोधयितुं तदा॥ ततो गुरुतरं यत्नं दारुणं समुपाक्रमन्।
en: But albeit assailed with shouts and smite with weapons, he did not wake up. And when they succeeded not in rousing him, they more than ever exerted themselves.

sn: अश्वानुष्ट्रान्खरान्नागाञ्जघ्नुर्दण्डकशाङ्कुशैः॥ भेरीशङ्खमृदङ्गांश्च सर्वप्राणैरवादयन्। निजघ्नुश्चास्य गात्राणि महाकाष्ठकटंकरैः।॥ भेरी: मुद्गरैर्मुसलैश्चापि सर्वप्राणसमुद्यतैः। तेन नादेन महता लङ्का सर्वा प्रपूरिता।। सपर्वतवना सर्वा सोऽपि नैव प्रबुध्यते॥
en: Then they smote him with horses and camels, and mules and snakes, rods and lashes and hooks, and with might and main sounded kettledrums and conchs and Mțdangas. And they struck his body with innumerable huge blocks of wood. And summoning up their dearest energy, they dealt him blows with maces and clubs. And at that mighty uproar, entire Lankā was filled with her woods and hills; yet he did not wake up.

sn: ततो भेरीसहस्रं तु युगपत्समहन्यत। मृष्टकाञ्चनकोणानामसक्तानां समन्ततः॥
en: Then they simultaneously sounded a thousand kettle-drums beaten with sticks of polished gold.

sn: एवमप्यतिनिद्रस्तु यदा नैव प्रबुध्यत। शापस्य वशमापनस्ततः कुद्धा निशाचराः॥
en: And coming under the sway of the curse, when that one sunk in slumber did not wake up, the night-rangers were wrought up with wrath.

sn: ततः कोपसमाविष्टाः सर्वे भीमपराक्रमाः। तद्रक्षो बोधयिष्यन्तश्चक्रुरन्ये पराक्रमम्॥
en: And overcome with choler, they endowed with dreadful prowess addressed themselves vigorously to awakening him; and others put forth their energy.

sn: अन्ये भेरीः समाजघ्नुरन्ये चक्रुर्महास्वनम्। केशानन्ये प्रलुलुपुः कर्णानन्ये दशन्ति च। ५१।।
en: Others smote the kettle-drums, and others set up loud cries. And others cut off his hair, and others bit his ears.

sn: उदकुम्भशतानन्ये समसिञ्चन्त कर्णयोः। न कुम्भकर्णः पस्पन्दे महानिद्रावशं गतः॥
en: Others poured into his ears a thousand vessels of water. But Kumbhakarņa come under the spell of a mighty slumber did not wink.

sn: अन्ये च बलिनस्तस्य कूटमुद्गरपाणयः। मूर्ध्नि वक्षसि गात्रेषु पातयन्कूटमुद्गरान् ॥
en: Others-strong ones-armed with poniards (kūt as) and maces, made their poniards and maces alight on his person.

sn: रज्जुबन्धनबद्धाभिः शतघ्नीभिश्च सर्वशः। वध्यमानो महाकायो न प्राबुध्यत राक्षसः।५४।।
en: And struck with sataghnis bound with cords, that huge-bodied one did not wake up.

sn: वारणानां सहस्रं च शरीरेऽस्य प्रधावितम्। कुम्भकर्णस्तदा बुद्ध्वा स्पर्श परमबुध्यत ॥
en: Then when a thousand elephants rushed against his body, recovering his consciousness, he awoke.

sn: रचिन्तयंस्तान्विपुलान्प्रहारान्। निद्राक्षयात्क्षुद्भयपीडितश्च विजृम्भमाणः सहसोत्पपात।५६।।
en: Assailed with mountain-peaks and trees descending on his body, he without minding those tremendous blows, on sleep having been dispelled. Suddenly got up yawning, suffering the pangs of hunger.

sn: स नागभोगाचलशृङ्गकल्पौ विक्षिप्य बाहू जितवज्रसारौ। विवृत्य वक्रं वडवामुखाभं निशाचरोऽसौ विकृतं जजृम्भे॥
en: Then that night-ranger resembling an elephant or a serpent or a mountain-peak, casting about his arms superior in force to the thunder-bolt itself, and opening his deformed mouth like to that of a mule, yawned (again and again).

sn: तस्य जाजृम्भमाणस्य वक्रं पातालसंनिभम्। ददृशे मेरुशृङ्गाग्रे दिवाकर इवोदितः॥
en: As he yawned, his mouth resembling the subterraneous regions, looked like the Sun stationed at the summit of Meru.

sn: स जृम्भमाणोऽतिबलः प्रबुद्धस्तु निशाचरः। निःपासश्चास्य संजज्ञे पर्वतादिव मारुतः॥
en: That night ranger possessed of unwieldly strength woke up, yawning. And the breath that he breathed resembled a storm raging in a mountain.

sn: रूपमुत्तिष्ठतस्तस्य कुम्भकर्णस्य तद्बभौ। युगान्ते सर्वभूतानि कालस्येव दिधक्षतः॥
en: Then as he sat up, Kumbhakarņa's form appeared like that of the Destroyer himself at the universal wreck, intent upon consuming all creatures.

sn: तस्याग्निदीप्तसदृशे विद्युत्सदृशवर्चसी। ददृशाते महानेत्रे दीप्ताविव महाग्रहौ॥
en: The large eyes of that one, resembling a life flame and endowed with the splendour of lighting, appeared like a pair of glowing planets.

sn: ततस्त्वदर्शयन्सर्वान्भक्ष्यांश्च विविधान्बहून्। वराहान्महिषांश्चैव बभक्ष स महाबलः॥
en: Then they pointed to him all those heaps of edibles, various and profuse, bears and buffaloes, and that powerful (Raksasa) fell to.

sn: आद(भुक्षितो मांसं शोणितं तृषितोऽपिबत्। मेदःकुम्भांश्च मद्यांश्च पपौ शक्ररिपुस्तदा॥
en: And hungering, he fed on flesh and athirst, drank blood. And then that enemy of Sakra drank vesselfuls of fat and blood.

sn: ततस्तृप्त इति ज्ञात्वा समुत्पेतुर्निशाचराः। शिरोभिश्च प्रणम्यैनं सर्वतः पर्यवारयन्॥
en: And concluding that he was replete, the nightrangers came up; and bowing down their heads stood circling him on all sides.

sn: निद्राविशदनेत्रस्तु कलुषीकृतलोचनः। चारयन्सर्वतो दृष्टिं तानुवाच निशाचरान्॥
en: Then with his eyes discoloured and drooping from drowsiness, he casting his eyes around addressed those night-rangers.

sn: स सर्वान्सान्त्वयामास नैर्ऋतानैर्ऋतर्षभः। बोधनाद्विस्मितश्चापि राक्षसानिदमब्रवीत्॥
en: That foremost of Naiſtas cheered all those Naiſtas: and surprised at his having been roused, spoke to the Rākşasas.

sn: किमर्थमहमादृत्य भवद्भिः प्रतिबोधितः। कच्चित्सुकुशलं राज्ञो भयं वा नेह किंचन॥
en: Why, being honoured, have I been awakened by you? Is it well with the king? Or has any fear : sprung up here?

sn: अथ वा ध्रुवमन्येभ्यो भयं परमुपस्थितम्। यदर्थमेव त्वरितैर्भवद्भिः प्रतिबोधितः॥
en: Or has a mighty fear presented itself forsooth from among others; for which I have bee speedily awakened by you?

sn: अद्य राक्षसराजस्य भयमुत्पाटयाम्यहम्। दारयिष्ये महेन्द्रं वा शीतयिष्ये तथानलम्॥
en: This very day will I uproot quite the fear of the sovereign of the Rākşasas. I will split up the great Indra himself, or make Fire himself give up his heat.

sn: नह्यल्पकारणे सुप्तं बोधयिष्यति मादृशम्। तदाख्यातार्थतत्त्वेन मत्प्रबोधनकारणम्।७० ॥
en: One does not awaken my like for a light cause. therefore do you give the real truth of the cause of your awakening me.

sn: एवं ब्रुवाणं संरब्धं कुम्भकर्णमरिंदमम्। यूपाक्षः सचिवो राज्ञः कृताञ्जलिरभाषत॥
en: Thereat a minister of the king, named Yupakş a, with joined hands said to that humbler of foesKumbhakarna-wrought up with wrath, who was thus speaking.

sn: न नो देवकृतं किंचिद्भयमस्ति कदाचन। मानुषानो भयं राजंस्तुमुलं संप्रबाधते॥
en: No fear anywise springs to us fro the Deities. But, О king, a great fear does cross us, coming from a mortal.

sn: न दैत्यदानवेभ्यो वा भयमस्ति न नः क्वचित्। यादृशं मानुषं राजन्भयमस्मानुपस्थितम्॥
en: And never fear so come to us anywise from Daityas or Dānavas, as it has arrived from a man, O king.

sn: वानरैः पर्वताकारैर्लङ्केयं परिवारिता। सीताहरणसंतप्ताद्रामानस्तुमुलं भयम्॥
en: This Lanka has been hemmed in by monkeys resembling mountains. And terrific is the terror that come even from Rāma scorched with fire springing from the ravishment of Sītă.

sn: एकेन वानरेणेयं पूर्वं दग्धा महापुरी। कुमारो निहतश्चाक्षः सानुयात्रः सकुञ्जरः॥
en: Ere this by a single monkey was this splendid city burnt down. And the prince Akşa has been slain along with his following and elephants.

sn: स्वयं रक्षोधिपश्चापि पौलस्त्यो देवकण्टकः। व्रजेति संयुगे मुक्तो रामेणादित्यवर्चसा ॥
en: That thorn in the sides of deities, that lord of the Raksasas-Pulastya's son himself-has been set free in conflict by Rāghava endowed with the splendour of the Sun, Saying, “Go you.

sn: यन्न देवैः कृतो राजा नापि दैत्यैर्न दानवः। कृतः स इह रामेण विमुक्तः प्राणसंशयात्॥
en: What had been done to the king by neither the gods nor Daityas nor yet the Dănavas, has been done by Rāma; and he has been set free, having come to a pass imperilling his life.

sn: स यूपाक्षवचः श्रुत्वा भ्रातुर्युधि पराभवम्। कुम्भकर्णो विवृत्ताक्षो यूपाक्षमिदमब्रवीत्॥
en: Hearing Yüpākşa's speech and hearing of the defeat of his brother, Kumbhakarņa, with his eyes whirling, spoke to him, saying..

sn: सर्वमद्यैव यूपाक्ष हरिसैन्यं सलक्ष्मणम्। राघवं च रणे जित्वा ततो द्रक्ष्यामि रावणम्॥
en: Today, O Yüpākṣa, after vanquishing in battle the monkey-army together with Laksmana and Raghava, shall I see Ravana.

sn: राशसांस्तर्पयिष्यामि हरीणां मांसशोणितैः। रामलक्ष्मणयोश्चापि स्वयं पास्यामि शोणितम्।।८०
en: I shall regale the Rākṣasas with the flesh and blood of the monkeys, and myself drink the blood of Rāma and Lakşmaņa.

sn: तत्तस्य वाक्यं ब्रुवतो निशम्य सगर्वितं रोषविवृद्धदोषम्। महोदरो नैऋतयोधमुख्यः कृताञ्जलिर्वाक्यमिदं बभाषे।८१॥
en: Hearing his words as he haughtily spoke thus with his spirit of insolence magnified by much, that foremost of the Nairta soldiers, Mahodara, with joined hands observed.

sn: रावणस्य वचः श्रुत्वा गुणदोषौ विमृश्य च। पश्चादपि महाबाहो शत्रून्युधि विजेष्यसि ॥
en: O long-armed one, having at first heard Rāvana's words and considered their justice or otherwise, you will afterwards defeat the foe in fight.

sn: महोदरवचः श्रुत्वा राक्षसैः परिवारितः। कुम्भकर्णो महातेजाः संप्रतस्थे महाबलः॥
en: Hearing Mahodara's words, the exceedingly energetic and mighty (Kumbhakarma) surrounded by the Rākşasas, prepared to depart.

sn: सुप्तमुत्थाप्य भीमाक्षं भीमरूपपराक्रमम्। राक्षसास्त्वरिता जग्मुर्दशग्रीवनिवेशनम्॥
en: Having roused from his slumbers that one of terrific prowess having dreadful eyes the Rāks asas speedily arrived at the residence of the Tennecked one.

sn: तेऽभिगम्य दशग्रीवमासीनं परमासने। ऊचुर्बद्धाञ्जलिपुटाः सर्व एव निशाचराः॥
en: And presenting themselves before the Tennecked on seated on a superb seat, all the nightrangers spoke with joined hands.

sn: कुम्भकर्णः प्रबुद्धोऽसौ भ्राता ते राक्षसेश्वर। कथं तत्रैव निर्यातु द्रक्ष्यसे तमिहागतम्॥
en: O lord of the Rākṣasas, your brother, Kumbhakarņa, has been roused. Shall he march from there; or will you see him come here?

sn: रावणस्त्वब्रवीद्धृष्टो राक्षसांस्तानुपस्थितान्। द्रष्टुमेनमिहेच्छामि यथान्यायं च पूज्यताम्॥
en: Thereat, Ravana, pleased, spoke to those Raks asas who had presented themselves, “I wish to see him here, and do you honour him fittingly."

sn: तथेत्युक्त्वा तु ते सर्वे पुनरागम्य राक्षसाः। कुम्भकर्णमिदं वाक्यमूचू रावणचोदिताः॥
en: Thereat, saying 'So be it', the Rākşasas, directed by Ravana, going back, spoke to Kumbhakarna.

sn: द्रष्टुं त्वां काश्ते राजा सर्वराक्षसपुङ्गवः। गमने क्रियतां बुद्धिर्धातरं संप्रहर्षय॥
en: That foremost of all the Rākşasas-the kingwish to see you. So mind you going, and gladden your brother.

sn: कुम्भकर्णस्तु दुर्धर्षो भ्रातुराज्ञाय शासनम्। तथेत्युक्त्वा महावीर्यः शयनादुत्पपात ह॥
en: The irrepressible Kumbhakarna possessed of prodigious prowess, learning the mandate of his brother, sa', ing, 'So be it', rose up from his bed.

sn: प्रक्षात्य वदनं हृष्टः स्नातः परमहर्षितः। पिपासुस्त्वरयामास पानं बलसमीरणम्॥
en: Washing his face, and having bathed, that one, feeling refreshed and enjoying exceeding exhilaration of spirit, wishing to drink, urged (the Rākşasas) to bring the nerve-conferring draught.

sn: ततस्ते त्वरितास्तत्र राक्षसा रावणाज्ञया। मद्यं भक्ष्यांश्च विविधान्क्षिप्रमेवोपहारयन्॥
en: Then the Rākşasas at the command of Rāvana speedily procured wine and various kinds of viands.

sn: पीत्वा घटसहस्रे द्वे गमनायोपचक्रमे। ईषत्समुत्कटो मत्तस्तेजोबलसमन्वितः॥ कुम्भकर्णो बभौ रुष्टः कालान्तकयमोपमः। भ्रातुः स भवनं गच्छन्रक्षोबलसमन्वितः।। कुम्भकर्णः पदन्यासैरकम्पयत मेदिनीम् ॥
en: Having drunk two thousand vessels (of wine) he prepared to go. And slightly swollen and flushed, Kumbhakarma, attaining access of strength and fire, waxed wroth and resembled the Doom and Destroyer-Yama himself. And striding to the residence of his brother backed by the Raksasa force, Kumbhakarņa shook the earth with his tread.

sn: स राजमार्गं वपुषा प्रकाशयन् सहस्ररश्मिर्धरणीमिवांशुभिः। जगाम तत्राञ्जलिमालया वृतः शतक्रतुर्गेहमिव स्वयंभुवः॥
en: Illuming the highway with the splendour of his person, like the thousand-rayed (Sun) discovering the earth with his rays, (Kumbhakarna) went on, engirt around by joined hands resembling wreaths, like Śatakratu* going to the abode of the Self-sprung. *Lit. him of an hundred sacrifices-an appellation of Indra.

sn: तं राजमार्गस्थममित्रघातिनं वनौकसस्ते सहसा बहिः स्थिताः। दृष्ट्वाप्रमेयं गिरिशृङ्गकल्पं वितत्रसुस्ते सह यूथपालैः॥
en: Suddenly seeing that slayer of foes of immeasurable prowess, resembling a mountainsummit, walking along the highways, the woodrangers stationed outside (the monkey-camp), along with the leaders of bands, were seized with affright.

sn: केचिच्छरण्यं शरणं स्म रामं व्रजन्ति केचिद्व्यथिताः पतन्ति। केचिदिशश्च व्यथिताः पतन्ति केचिद्भयार्ता भुवि शेरते स्म ॥
en: Then some sought the shelter of Răma, worthy of being so sought; and some, stricken (with panic), dropped to the earth; and some, suffering (from fear), fled to the carindal points; and some through stress (of apprehension) lay down on the ground.

sn: तमद्रिशृङ्गप्रतिमं किरीटिनं स्पृशन्तमादित्यमिवात्मतेजसा। वनौकसः प्रेक्ष्य विवृद्धमद्भुतं भयादिता दुदुविरे यतस्ततः॥
en: Seeing that one resembling a very mountainpeak, decked with a diadem, seeming to touch the Sun himself with his energy, of colossal altitude, and wonderful to behold, the woodrangers, tormented with fright, began to scamper on all sides.

sn: ततो रामो महातेजा धनुरादाय वीर्यवान्। किरीटिनं महाकायं कुम्भकर्णं ददर्श ह॥
en: Then the exceedingly energetic Rāma possessed of prowess, taking his bow, saw Kumbhakarņa, having a huge body and decked with a diadem.

sn: तं दृष्ट्वा राक्षसश्रेष्ठ पर्वताकारदर्शनम्। क्रममाणमिवाकाशं पुरा नारायणं यथा॥ सतोयाम्बुदसंकाशं काञ्चनाङ्गदभूषणम्। दृष्ट्वा पुनः प्रदुद्राव वानराणां महाचमूः॥
en: Seeing that foremost of Rākşasas looking like a mountain; filling all the heavens as formerly Nārāyaṇa had done; resembling clouds charged with rain; and adorned with golden Angadas, the mighty army of monkeys began to run away at the top of its speed.

sn: विदूतां वाहिनीं दृष्ट्वा वर्धमानं च राक्षसम्। सविस्मितमिदं रामो विभीषणमुवाच ह॥
en: Seeing the army scamper and the Rākşasa swelling, Rāma struck with surprise, said to Vibhisana. mass

sn: कोऽसौ पर्वतसंकाशः किरीटी हरिलोचनः। लङ्कायां दृश्यते वीरः सविद्युदिव तोयदः॥
en: Who is that tawny-eyed one, decked with a diadem, and looking like a hill? And in Lankā the hero appear like a of clouds embosoming lightning.

sn: पृथिव्यां केतुभूतोऽसौ महानेकोऽत्र दृश्यते। यं दृष्ट्वा वानराः सर्वे विद्रवन्ति यतस्ततः॥
en: And alone he seem like an ensign of the Earth; and seeing him the monkeys dart away hither and thither.

sn: आचक्ष्व सुमहान्कोऽसौ रक्षो वा यदि वासुरः। न मयैवंविधं भूतं दृष्टपूर्वं कदाचन।७।।
en: Tell me who he is, whether a Rākṣasa or an Asura. The like of him mine eyes had never before lighted on.

sn: संपृष्टो राजपुत्रेण रामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा। विभीषणो महाप्रज्ञः काकुत्स्थमिदमब्रवीत्॥
en: Accosted by the king's son-Rāma of untiring deeds-the exceedingly wise Vibhīşaņa said to Kakutstha.

sn: येन वैवस्वतो युद्धे वासवश्च पराजितः। सैष विश्रवसः पुत्रः कुम्भकर्णः प्रतापवान्।। अस्य प्रमाणसदृशो राक्षसोऽन्यो न विद्यते॥
en: By whom in battle Vivasvata's offspring* and Vasava himself had been vanquished this is hethe wondrous powerful Kumbhakarņa, son to Visravā. No Rākṣasa is there that equals this one in size. *Yama-son of Vivasvata or the Sun.

sn: एतेन देवा युधि दानवाश्च यक्षा भुजंगाः पिशिताशनाश्च। गन्धर्वविद्याधरपन्नगाश्च सहस्रशो राघव संप्रभग्नाः॥
en: O Rāghava, this one in battle has brought down Dānavas and Yakşas and Serpents' and flesh-feeders and Gandharvas and Vidyādharas and Pannagas by thousands. 1. Bhujanga:-semi-divine serpents. 2. Semi-divine serpents.

sn: शूलपाणिं विरूपाक्षं कुम्भकर्म महाबलम्। हन्तुं न शेकुस्त्रिदशा: कालोऽयमिति मोहिताः॥
en: The immortals themselves thinking the darthanded and fierce-eyed Kumbhakarņa possessed of great strength, as the Destroyer himself, were overwhelmed with stupor and were foiled in their exertions to slay him.

sn: प्रकृत्या ह्येष तेजस्वी कुम्भकर्णो महाबलः। अन्येषां राक्षसेन्द्राणां वरदानकृतं बलम्॥
en: The exceedingly powerful Kumbhakarņa is mighty by nature: the strength of other redoubtable Rākşasas is owing to boons obtained by them.

sn: बालेन जातमात्रेण क्षुधार्तेन महात्मना। भक्षितानि सहस्राणि प्रजानां सुबहून्यपि॥
en: As soon as this high-souled one was born and was a babe, he began to devour up countless creatures by the thousand.

sn: तेषु संभक्ष्यमाणेषु प्रजा भयनिपीडिताः। यान्ति स्म शरणं शक्रं तमप्यर्थं न्यवेदयन्॥
en: On these having been devoured, creatures, afflicted with affright consequent on those having been eaten up, sought the shelter of Sakra and told him what had happened.

sn: स कुम्भकर्ण कुपितो महेन्द्रो जघान वज्रेण शितेन वज्री। स शक्रवज्राभिहतो महात्मा चचाल कोपाच्च भृशं ननाद॥
en: Thereat the great Indra, waxing wroth, smote Kumbhakarna with the whetted levin. And hit at with Sakra's thunder bolt, that high-souled (hero) shook, and in wrath set up roars.

sn: तस्य नानद्यमानस्य कुम्भकर्णस्य रक्षसः। श्रुत्वा निनादं वित्रस्ताः प्रजा भूयो वितत्रसुः॥
en: Hearing the roars of the Raksasa-Kumbhakarna, as he kept crying, creatures, seized with fear, were greatly agitated.

sn: ततः क्रुद्धो महेन्द्रस्य कुम्भकर्णो महाबलः। निष्कृष्यरावताहन्तं जघानोरसि वासवम्॥
en: Thereat, enraged with the great Indra, the mighty Kumbhakarņa plucking a tusk of Airāvata, hurled it at Vāsava's chest.

sn: कुम्भकर्णप्रहारा” विजज्वाल स वासवः। ततो विषेदुः सहसा देवा ब्रह्मर्षिदानवाः।। प्रजाभिः सह शक्रश्च ययौ स्थानं स्वयंभुवः॥
en: With blood overflowing his person, Vāsava looked as if aflame. Thereat, all of a sudden the gods and the Brahmarşis and the Dānavas were dispirited. Then ſakra Then Śakra alongwith alongwith others proceeded to the abode of Brahma.

sn: कुम्भकर्णस्य दौरात्म्यं शशंसुस्ते प्रजापतेः। प्रजानां भक्षणं चापि शशंसुस्ते दिवौकसाम्।। आश्रमध्वंसनं चापि परस्त्रीहरणं तथा॥ एवं प्रजा यदि त्वेष भक्षयिष्यति नित्यशः। अचिरेणैव कालेन शून्यो लोको भविष्यति॥
en: Then they informed the lord of creatures touching the ravages of Kumbhakarna, and informed the gods about Kumbhakarna's devouring up, destroying asylums and outraging others, wives. If this one devour creatures constantly, in a short space the world would be empty of any.

sn: वासवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा सर्वलोकपितामहः। रक्षास्यावाहयामास कुम्भकर्म ददर्श ह॥
en: Hearing Vasava's speech, the Great-father of all creatures called up* the Rākṣasas and saw Kumbhakarņa (before him). *By reciting a certain scriptural formula.

sn: कुम्भकर्म समीक्ष्यैव वितत्रास प्रजापतिः। कुम्भकर्णमथाश्वस्तः स्वयंभूरिदमब्रवीत्॥
en: Seeing Kumbhkarņa, Prajāpati* was seized with exceeding great fear. And then pacifying Kumbhakarma, the Self-sprung addressed him, saying. *Lit. lord of creatures.

sn: ध्रुवं लोकविनाशाय पौलस्त्येनासि निर्मितः। तस्मात्त्वमद्यप्रभृति मृतकल्पः शयिश्यसे॥
en: Forsooth for compassing the destruction of creatures, have you been begot by Paulasta* Therefore from this day forth, you shall lie down as one dead. *ViSravana.

sn: ब्रह्मशापाभिभूतोऽथ निपपाताग्रतः प्रभोः। ततः परमसंभ्रान्तो रावणो वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
en: Stricken with the of Brahma, Kumbhakarma fell down before the Lord. Then, "extremely agitated, Ravana said. curse

sn: प्रवृद्धः काञ्चनो वृक्षः फलकाले निकृन्त्यते। न नप्तारं स्वकं न्याय्यं शप्तुमेवं प्रजापते॥
en: You hew down a golden tree when about to bear fruit. O lord of creatures, you ought not to curse thus your own grandson.

sn: न मिथ्यावचनश्च त्वं स्वप्स्यत्येव न संशयः। कालस्तु क्रियतामस्य शयने जागरे तथा॥
en: Your words will never go for naught; sleep he will, without doubt. But do you appoint a time for his sleeping and one for his awaking,

sn: रावणस्य वचः श्रुत्वा स्वयंभूरिदमब्रवीत्। शयिता ह्येष षण्मासमेकाहं जागरिष्यति॥
en: Hearing Rāvana's speech, the Self-sprung said, "having slept for six months, he shall wake for one day.

sn: एकनाह्वा त्वसौ वीरश्चरन्भूमिं बुभुक्षितः। व्यात्तास्यो भक्षयेल्लोकान्संवृद्ध इव पावकः॥
en: And for a single day, that hero, coming under the influence of hunger, shall range the earth, opening his mouth wide open, and devouring people like a fire that has spread far and wide.

sn: सोऽसौ व्यसनमापन्नः कुम्भकर्णमबोधयत्। त्वत्पराक्रमभीतश्च राजा संप्रति रावणः॥
en: Now king Rāvaņa struck with terror at your prowess, encompassed with peril, has waked up Kumbhakarņa.

sn: स एष निर्गतो वीरः शिविराद्भीमविक्रमः। वानरान्भृशसंक्रुद्धो भक्षयन्परिधावति॥
en: That hero possessed of dreadful prowess, wrought up with high wrath, sallying forth from his camp, rush about, eating up monkeys.

sn: कुम्भकर्ण प्रतीक्ष्यैव हरयोऽद्य प्रदुद्रुवुः। कथमेनं रणे क्रुद्धं वारयिष्यन्ति वानराः॥
en: Soon as the monkeys see Kumbhakarna, they fly away. And How can they resist in battle the enraged Kumbhakarna?

sn: उच्यन्तां वानराः सर्वे यन्त्रमेतत्समुच्छ्रितम्। इति विज्ञाय हरयो भविष्यन्तीह निर्भया:॥
en: Do you tell the monkeys this is an uplifted engine. Thus assured, the monkeys shall take heart.

sn: विभीषणवचः श्रुत्वा हेतुमत्सुमुखोद्गतम्। उवाच राघवो वाक्यं नीलं सेनापतिं तदा॥
en: Hearing Vibhīşaņa's words informed with reason and tending to the good (of the monkeys), Rāghava then addressed general Nila, saying.

sn: गच्छ सैन्यानि सर्वाणि व्यूह्य तिष्ठस्व पावके। द्वाराण्यादाय लङ्कायाश्चर्याश्चास्याथ संक्रमान्॥ शैलशृङ्गाणि वृक्षांश्च शिलाश्चाप्युपसंहरन्। भवन्तः सायुधाः सर्वे वानराः शैलपाणयः॥
en: Let you, monkeys, equipped with weapons and holding hill tops in your hands, and furnished with mountain-summits and trees and rocks, stay, occupying the highways and the bridges.

sn: राघवेण समादिष्टो नीलो हरिचमूपतिः। शशास वानरानीकं यथावत्कपिकुञ्जरः॥
en: Thus instructed by Rāghava, that powerful monkey, Nila-general of the forces-accordingly issue I his orders to the monkey-hosts.

sn: ततो गवाक्षः शरभो हनूमानङ्गदस्तथा। शैलशृङ्गाणि शैलाभा गृहीत्वा द्वारमभ्ययुः॥
en: Then Gavākṣa and Sarabha and Hanumān and Angada, themselves endowed with the splendour of mountain-summits, taking up mountain-tops, drew towards the gateway.

sn: रामवाक्यमुपश्रुत्य हरयो जितकाशिनः। पादपैरर्दयन्वीरा वानराः परवाहिनीम्॥
en: Hearing Rāma's words,* the heroic monkeys inspired with intrepidity, fiercely fell on the foe with trees. *Namely, "that is an uplifted engine.”

sn: ततो हरीणां तदनीकमुग्रं रराज शैलोद्यतवृक्षहस्तम्। गिरेः समीपानुगतं यथैव महन्महाम्भोधरजालमुग्रम्॥
en: Then that dreadful army of monkeys, upraising crags and holding trees in their hands, appeared like mighty masses of scowling clouds bordering a mountain.* *This is apt, seeing that Larika was situated on a hill.

sn: स तु राक्षसशार्दूलो निद्रामदसमाकुलः। राजमार्ग श्रिया जुष्टं ययौ विपुलविक्रमः॥
en: That tiger-like Rakşasa possessed of prowess, (still) under the influence of slumber, strode along the picturesque highway.

sn: राक्षसानां सहस्रैश्च वृतः परमदुर्जयः। गृहेभ्यः पुष्पवर्षेण कीर्यमाणस्तदा ययौ॥
en: That exceedingly unconquerable one, surrounded by thousands of Raksasas, went on, showered with blossoms from the houses (standing by).

sn: स हेमजालविततं भानुभास्वरदर्शनम्। ददर्श विपुलं रम्यं राक्षसेन्द्रनिवेशनम्॥
en: Then he saw the grand and graceful residence of the lord of the Räkşasas, having golden networks and sun-bright to behold.

sn: स तत्तदा सूर्य इवाभ्रजालं प्रविश्य रक्षोधिपतेर्निवेशनम्। ददर्श दूरेऽग्रजमासनस्थं स्वयंभुवं शक्र इवासनस्थम्।४।।
en: Entering the mansion of the Raksasa sovereign, like the sun entering into a mass of clouds, he saw his elder brother seated at a distance; even as Sakra sees the Self-sprung seated.

sn: भ्रातुः स भवनं गत्वा रक्षोगणसमन्वितः। कुम्भकर्ण: पदन्यासैरकम्पयत मेदिनीम्॥
en: Kumbhakarņa surrounded by numbers of Rākşasas, entered his brother's abode, making the very earth tremble with his tread.

sn: सोऽभिगम्य गृहं भ्रातुः कक्ष्यामभिविगाह्य च। दद द्विग्नमासीनं विमाने पुष्पके गुरुम् ॥
en: Arriving at the abode and passing the entrance, he saw his superior anxiously seated on the car, Pusphaka.

sn: अथ दृष्ट्वा दशग्रीवः कुम्भकर्णमुपस्थितम्। तूर्णमुत्थाय संहृष्टाः संनिकर्षमुपानयत्॥
en: Seeing Kumbhakarņa come, the Ten necked one, exceedingly rejoiced, raised him up and drew him near himself.

sn: अथासीनस्य पर्यङ्के कुम्भकर्णो महाबलः। भ्रातुर्ववन्दे चरणौ किं कृत्यमिति चाब्रवीत्॥
en: Then the exceedingly mighty Kumbhakarņa saluted the feet of his brother and said, "What did you say ?"

sn: पुनः स मुदितोत्पत्य रावणः परिषस्वजे। स भ्रात्रा संपरिष्वक्को यथावच्चाभिनन्दितः॥
en: Thereat, delighted, Ravana, springing up, again embraced (his brother). And embraced (by his brother), and duly greeted by him, that brother (of Ravana).

sn: कुम्भकर्णः शुभं दिव्यं प्रतिपेदे वरासमम्। स तदासनमाश्रित्य कुम्भकर्णो महाबलः॥ संरक्तनयनः क्रोधाद्रावणं वाक्यमब्रवीत्।
en: Kumbhakarņa seated himself on a shining and superb seat. And seating himself on that seat, the wondrous powerful Kumbhakarna, with his eyes reddened in wrath, addressed Ravana, saying.

sn: किमर्थमहमादृत्य त्वया राजप्रबोधितः॥ शंस कस्माद्भयं तेऽत्र को वा प्रेतो भविष्यति। भ्रातरं रावणः क्रुद्धं कुम्भकर्णमवस्थितम्।। रोषेण परिवृत्ताभ्यां नेत्राभ्यां वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
en: O king, why honouring me, has you awaked me? Tell me whence springs your fear? And who shall be a ghost?* Thereat Ravana, waxing wroth, and with his eyes rolling in rage, said to Kumbhakarma, seated. *Having been slain by me.

sn: अयं ते सुमहान्कालः शयानस्य महाबल। सुषुप्तस्त्वं न जानीये मम रामकृतं भयम्॥
en: O highly powerful one, you have slept away a long space of time. And having been asleep, you did not know the great fear of mine springing from Rama.

sn: एष दाशरथिः श्रीमान्सुग्रीवसहितो बली। समुद्रं लवयित्वा तु कुलं नः परिकृन्तति॥
en: This graceful son to Daśaratha possessed of strength, along with Sugriva, having crossed the ocean, is destroying our race.

sn: हन्त पश्यस्व लङ्कायां वनान्युपवनानि च। सेतुना सुखमागत्य वानरैकार्णवं कृतम्॥
en: Alack! see in own Lanka, woods and forests have been flooded with an ocean of monkeys never even coming without any ado by the bridge (which they have constructed).

sn: ये राक्षसा मुख्यतमा हतास्ते वानरैर्युधि वानराणां क्षयं युद्धे न पश्यामि कथंचन।। न चापि वानरा युद्धे जितपूर्वाः कदाचन॥
en: Those Rākşasas that were prime have been slain in battle by the monkeys; but I find no destruction of the monkeys in fight. Nay, the monkeys have been before vanquished (by the Raksasas) in battle.

sn: तदेतद्भयमुत्पन्नं त्रायस्वेह महाबल। नाशय त्वमिमानद्य तदर्थं बोधितो भवान्॥
en: Therefore has this fear sprung up in my heart). Save me from this, O exceedingly powerful one. Do you now destroy these. It is for this that I have roused you.

sn: सर्वक्षपितकोशं च स त्वमभ्युपपद्य माम्। त्रायस्वेमां पुरीं लङ्कां बालवृद्धावशेषिताम्॥
en: Do you, favouring me, whose exchequer is empty, save this city of Lanka, having only young folks and the aged left.

sn: भ्रातुरर्थे महाबाहो कुरु कर्म सुदुष्करम्। मयैवं नोक्तपूर्वो हि भ्राता कश्चित्परंतप ॥
en: O long-armed one, do you perform your dearest acts in behalf of your brother. O subduer of enemies, I had never before said so to my brother.

sn: त्वय्यस्ति मम च स्नेहः परा संभावना च मे। देवासुरेषु युद्धेषु बहुशो राक्षसर्षभ।। त्वया देवाः प्रतिव्यूह्य निर्जिताश्चामरा युधि ॥
en: In you is my affection and great is the probability of your succeeding. In the wars of the celestials and Asuras, O foremost of Rāks asas, countless were the celestials that you as an antagonist had beaten.

sn: तदेतत्सर्वमातिष्ठ वीर्य भीमपराक्रम। नहि ते सर्वभूतेषु दृश्यते सदृशो बली॥
en: Therefore, o you of dreadful strength! summon your entire energy. Him find I not among all beings, who is your peer in prowess.

sn: कुरुष्व मे प्रियहितमेतदुत्तम यथाप्रियं प्रियरण बान्धवप्रिय। स्वतेजसा व्यथय सपत्नवाहिनीं शरद्धनं पवन इवोद्यतो महान्॥
en: O lover of battle! O dear to friends, as you like, do this beloved good office, this prime benefit, to me. By your own energy, smite the hostile hosts, even as a mighty and strong wind (scattered away) autumnal clouds.

sn: तस्य राक्षसराजस्य निशम्य परिदेवितम्। कुम्भकर्णो बभाषेदं वचनं प्रजहास च॥
en: Hearing the lament of the king of Rākşasas, Kumbhakarma, laughing said.

sn: दृष्टो दोषो हि योऽस्माभिः पुरा मन्त्रविनिर्णये। हितेष्वनभियुक्तेन सोऽयमासादितस्त्वया॥
en: That evil which on the occasion of the conclave we had seen, has befallen you, who have passed by what was fraught with your good.

sn: शीघ्रं खल्वभ्युपेतं त्वां फलं पापस्य कर्मणः। निरयेष्वेव पतनं यथा दुष्कृतकर्मणः॥
en: Even as a sinner reaps perdition, verily has the fruit of your unrighteous act found you.

sn: प्रथमं वै महाराज कृत्यमेतदचिन्तितम्। केवलं वीर्यदर्पण नानुबन्धो विचारितः॥
en: At first, O mighty king, you did not ponder over this course of conduct; nor, from pride of prowess, did you at all take note of the evil thereof.

sn: यः पश्चात्पूर्वकार्याणि कुर्यादैश्वर्यमास्थितः। पूर्वं चोत्तरकार्याणि न स वेद नयानयौ॥
en: He that dose last what should be done first, and what should be done last, is ignorant of what is prudence and what not.

sn: देशकालविहीनानि कर्माणि विपरीतवत्। क्रियमाणानि दुष्यन्ति हवींष्यप्रयतेष्विव॥
en: Acts not performed in harmony with season and place, like to acts performed counter to season and place, are the occasions of misery, and resemble clarified butter poured into fire that has not been sanctified.

sn: त्रयाणां पञ्चधा योगं कर्मणां यः प्रपद्यते। सचिवैः समयं कृत्वा स सम्यग्वर्तते पथि॥
en: He stay well in the path that, in consultation with his counsellors, ascertain the five way touching the three kinds of action* *The five ways are (1) the mans of commencing an act (2) person, thing and wealth, (3) division of season and place, (4) providing agains mischance (5) success. The three kinds of action are treaty, war, etc. All this is nebulous; And the commentator is sadly reticent over this extremely important passage.

sn: यथागमं च यो राजा समयं च चिकीर्षति। बुध्यते सचिवैर्बुद्ध्या सुहृदश्चानुपश्यति।८।। धर्ममर्थ हि कामं वा सर्वान्वा रक्षसां पते। भजते पुरुषः काले त्रीणि द्वन्द्वानि वा पुनः॥
en: The king that aided by his own intelligence as well as his counsellors act after reflection in consonance with the science of polity, that distinguish his friends from his foes), and, O lord of the Raksasas, that seasonably' pursue righteousness, or profit, or desire, or any two, or all these combined-truly has understanding.? 1. Religion is to be sought in the morning, profit in the afternoon, and desire at nigh, so the commentator. 2. One is at sea in the midst of these formless generalities. The tantalized intellect makes a desperate attempt to grasp the body of the shadow seeming substance, but the empty air mocks his pains. A translator, however, is fast bound to the oar and must pull on, will be, nil he.

sn: त्रिषु चैतेषु यच्छेष्ठं श्रुत्वा तनावबुध्यते। राजा वा राजमात्रो वा व्यर्थं तस्य बहुश्रुतम्॥
en: But the king or the heir apparent, that, having heard what is prime among the three, does not understand, has his time in vain on his erudition.

sn: उपप्रदानं सान्त्वं च भेदं काले च विक्रमम्। योगं च रक्षसां श्रेष्ठ तावुभौ च नयानयौ॥ काले धर्मार्थकामान्यः संमन्य सचिवैः सह। निषेवेतात्मवाल्लोके न स व्यसनमाप्नुयात्॥
en: He that controlling his own self, consult with his counsellors seasonably touching gift, forbearance, difference and prowess, as well as virtue, profit and desire-does not in this world come by calamity.

sn: हितानुबन्धमालोक्य कुर्यात्कार्यमिहात्मनः। राजा सहार्थतत्त्वज्ञैः सचिवैर्बुद्धिजीविभिः॥
en: Perceiving the fair fruit (of a line of action) accruing to him here, a king should act in consultation with counsellors endowed with intelligence and versed in the import of things.

sn: अनभिज्ञाय शास्त्रार्थान्पुरुषाः पशुबुद्धयः। प्रागल्भ्याद्वक्तुमिच्छन्ति मन्त्रिष्वभ्यन्तरीकृताः॥
en: Not understanding the sense of the scriptures, persons possessed of beastly intelligence, entering into the heart of their counsellors, are inspired with a desire of speaking out of sheer volubility.

sn: अशास्त्रविदुषां तेषां कार्यं नाभिहितं वचः। अर्थशास्त्रानभिज्ञानां विपुलां श्रियमिच्छताम्॥
en: Albeit uttered heedfully, the speech of those that are ignorant of learning and the knowledge of the sense of things, and who are intent upon attaining abounding affluence, should not be acted upon.

sn: अहितं च हिताकारं धाष्टाजल्पन्ति ये नराः। अवश्यं मन्त्रबाह्यास्ते कर्तव्याः कृत्यदूषकाः॥
en: Those-spoilers of business-who from recklessness talk of pernicious as if profitableshould certainly be rejected as counsellors.

sn: विनाशयन्तो भर्तारं सहिताः शत्रुभिर्बुधैः। विपरीतानि कृत्यानि कारयन्तीह मन्त्रिणः॥
en: Some counsellors-destroyers of their mastersjoining intelligent enemies (of their lords), act in a way opposed to their interests in this world.

sn: तान्भर्ता मित्रसंकाशानमित्रान्मन्त्रनिर्मये। व्यवहारेण जानीयात्सचिवानुपसंहितान्॥
en: Their lords, at the hour of consultation, by their behaviour should know these counsellorsenemies in the guise of friends-who have been won over (by the opposite party).

sn: चपलस्येह कृत्यानि सहसानुप्रधावतः। क्षिप्रमन्ये प्रपद्यन्ते क्रौञ्चस्य खमिव द्विजाः॥
en: Even as the fowls of the air enter the hole in the Krauñca, enemies find and easy entrance into the short comings of him that is fickle and that rush into act without heed.

sn: यो हि शत्रुमवज्ञाय आत्मानं नाभिरक्षति। अवाप्नोति हि सोऽनन्स्थानाच्च व्यवरोप्यते॥
en: He that disregarding his foe, omits to guard himself, come by disasters and lose his place.

sn: यदुक्तमिह ते पूर्वं प्रियया मेऽनुजेन च। तदेव नो हितं वाक्यं यथेच्छसि तथा कुरु॥
en: Even what had been advanced by the beloved and my younger brother is fraught with our welfare. Do you now what you-wish.

sn: तत्तु श्रुत्वा दशग्रीवः कुम्भकर्णस्य भाषितम्। भ्रुकुटिं चैव संचक्रे क्रुद्धश्चैनमभाषत ॥
en: Hearing Kumbhakarma's words, the Tennecked one knit up his brows, and, wrought up with wrath, said to him.

sn: मान्यो गुरुरवाचार्यः किं मां त्वमनुशाससे। किमेवं वाक्श्रमं कृत्वा यद्युक्तं तद्विधीयताम्॥
en: I am worthy of being honoured by you, like your superior. What needs this verbal travail? Do you what is fit.

sn: विभ्रमाच्चित्तमोहाद्वा बलवीर्याश्रयेण वा। नाभिपन्नमिदानीं यद्वयर्था तस्य पुनः कथा॥
en: Vain is the mention now of what I did either through stupor or delusion or pride of prowess. Now bethink you of what is proper.

sn: अस्मिन्काले तु यद्युक्तं तदिदानी विचिन्त्यताम्। ममापनयजं दुःखं विक्रमेण समीकुरु।२५।। यदि खल्वस्ति मे स्नेहो विक्रमं वाधिगच्छसि। यदि कार्य ममैतत्ते हृदि कार्यतमं मतम्॥
en: Do you through your prowess assuage the sorrow of mine springing from my impolitic conduct, if you cherish any feeling for me, if your strength stay and if you deem this business of mine as by far more momentous to you.

sn: स सुहृद्यो विपन्नाथ दीनमभ्युपपद्यते। स बन्धुर्योऽपनीतेषु साहाय्यायोपकल्पते॥
en: He is a friend that succour one fallen in distress and is undergoing affliction; and he acts friendly that helped a person lapsing from the path of morality.

sn: तमथैवं ब्रुवाणं स वचनं धीरदारुणम्। रुष्टोऽयमिति विज्ञाय शनैः श्लक्ष्णमुवाच ह॥ अतीव हि समालक्ष्य भ्रातरं क्षुभितेन्द्रियम्। कुम्भकर्णः शनैर्वाक्यं बभाषे परिसान्त्वयन्॥
en: As he was speaking thus in words sedate yet severe, Kumbhakarma, concluding that Ravana was undelighted, makes his remarks mildly. And seeing his brother extremely sorry, Kumbhakarņa, pacifying him, gently said.

sn: शृणु राजन्नवहितो मम वाक्यमरिंदम। अलं राक्षसराजेन्द्र संतापमुपपद्य ते।। रोषं च संपरित्यज्य स्वस्थो भवितुमर्हसि॥
en: O king, intently hear my words. O repressor of foes! O lord of Raksasas, banish this sorrow, and casting away your wrath, return you to nature.

sn: नैतन्मनसि कर्तव्यं मयि जीवति पार्थिव। तमहं नाशयिष्यामि यत्कृते परितप्यते॥
en: O king, so long as I live, you must not suffer your heart to fare thus. Him will I slay for whom you grieve.

sn: अवश्यं च हितं वाच्यं सर्वावस्थां गतं मया। बन्धुभावादभिहितं भ्रातृस्नेहाच्च पार्थिव॥
en: But whatever condition you may be in, I must tell what is for your welfare; and therefore from sentiment of friendship as well as from fraternal affection I have spoken thus to you o King.

sn: सदृशं यच्च कालेऽस्मिन्कर्तुं स्नेहेन बन्धुना। शत्रूणां कदनं पश्य क्रियमाणं मया रणे॥
en: What a friend from affection should do at a time like this, I shall do the same. See the havoc I spread among the foes in fight.

sn: अद्य पश्य महाबाहो मया समरमूर्धनि। हते रामे सह भ्रात्रा द्रवन्तीं हरिवाहिनीम्॥
en: O long-armed one, behold, on Rāma having been slain by me on the edge of battle along with his brother, the monkey-army in headlong flight.

sn: अद्य रामस्य तद्दृष्ट्वा मया नीतं रणाच्छिरः। सुखी भव महाबाहो सीता भवतु दुःखिता॥
en: And today seeing Rāma's head brought by me from the field, be you, O long-armed one, happy; and let Sitā be overwhelmed with woe.

sn: अद्य रामस्य पश्यन्तु निधनं सुमहत्प्रियम्। लङ्कायां राक्षसाः सर्वे ये ते निहतबान्धवाः॥
en: And let those Raksasas in Lankā who have had their kindred slain (in battle), see that dear sight-Rāma slain (in fight).

sn: अद्य शोकपरीतानां स्वबन्धुवधशोचिनाम्। शत्रोर्युधि विनाशेन करोम्यश्रुप्रमार्जनम्॥
en: Today shall I slaying the enemies in battle, wipe the tears of those who mourn their friend slain and are overwhelmed with grief.

sn: अद्य पर्वतसंकाशं ससूर्यमिव तोयदम्। विकीर्णं पश्य समरे सुग्रीवं प्लवगेश्वरम्॥
en: To-day behold the lord of monkeys-Sugrivaresembling a mountain or a mass of clouds lighted up by (the living) sun, lying stretched on the field.

sn: कथं च राक्षसैरेभिर्मया च परिसान्त्वितः। जिघांसुभिर्दाशरथिं व्यथसे त्वं सदानघ॥
en: But why, O sinless one, albeit comforted by these Rākşasas eager for saying Dasaratha's son, as well as by me, did your persist in your sorrow?

sn: मां निहत्य किल त्वां हि निहनिष्यति राघवः। नाहमात्मनि संतापं गच्छेयं राक्षसाधिप।४।।
en: Rāghava forsooth shall slay you after slaying me But, O lord of Raksasas, I cannot come by grief (at Rāghava's hands).

sn: कामं त्विदानीमपि मां व्यादिश त्वं परंतप। न परः प्रेक्षणीयस्ते युद्धायातुलविक्रम॥
en: O repressor of foes, do you now command me O you of unparalleled prowess, you need not yourself face the foe in fight.

sn: अहमुत्सादयिष्यामि शबूंस्तव महाबलान्। यदि शक्रो यदि यमो यदि पावकमारुतौ।॥ तानहं योधयिष्यामि कुबेरवरुणावपि।
en: I shall abolish your foes endowed with redoubted might. If even Śakra himself, and Yama, and the god of Fire, and the god of Wind, and Kubera, and Varuņa-shall range themselves against me, them shall I encounter in fight.

sn: गिरिमात्रशरीरस्य शितशूलधरस्य मे।॥ नर्दतस्तीक्ष्णदंष्ट्रस्य बिभीयाद्वैपुरंदरः।
en: Purandara himself is seized with fright at sight of me, having a body measuring a mountain, equipped with sharpened spears, furnished with sharp teeth, and setting up shouts.

sn: अथ वा त्यक्तशस्त्रस्य मृगतस्तरसा रिपून्॥ न मे प्रतिमुखः कश्चित्स्थातुं शक्तो जिजीविषुः।
en: And who wishing to save himself shall be able to stay before me as I casting away my weapons keep pounding my enemies with celerity?

sn: नैव शक्त्या न गदया नासिना निशितैः शरैः॥ हस्ताभ्यामव संरभ्य हनिष्यामि सवज्रिणम्।
en: No need of the dart, or the mace, or the sword, or whetted arrows. I shall with my bare arms alone slay (Rāma) along with the thunderer himself.

sn: यदि मे मुष्टिवेगं स राघवोऽद्य सहिष्यति॥ ततः पास्यन्ति बाणौधा रुधिरं राघवस्य मे।
en: If Raghava bear the impetus of my blows, the shall the vollies of my shafts drink his life blood.

sn: चिन्तया तप्यसे राजन्किमर्थं मयि तिष्ठति ॥ सोऽहं शत्रुविनाशाय तव निर्यातुमुद्यतः।
en: Why, O king, while I remain, did you burn in anxiety. And I am ready to sally out for compassing the destruction of your enemies.

sn: मुश्च रामाद्भयं घोरं निहनिष्यामि संयुगे॥ राघवं लक्ष्मणं चैव सुग्रीवं च महाबलम्। हनूमन्तं च रक्षोघ्नं येन लङ्का प्रदीपिता॥ हरीश्च भक्षयिष्यामि संयुगे समुपस्थिते। असाधारणमिच्छामि तव दातुं महद्यशः॥
en: Cast off all terror of Rāma. I shall slay in battle Rāghava and Lakşmaņa and the exceedingly powerful Sugrīva and the Räksasadestroying Hanumān, who made Lankā blaze. I shall cat up the monkeys present in the encounter. And signal is the celebrity that I shall confer on you.

sn: यदि चेन्द्राद्भयं राजन्यदि चापि स्वयंभुवः। अपि देवाः शयिष्यन्ते मयि कुद्धे महीतले। ५१।। यमं च शमयिष्यामि भक्षयिष्यामि पावकम्।
en: O king, if your fear springs from Indra or the Self-create, even the immortals shall measure their lengths on the earth when I am wrought with rage. And I shall subdue Yama himself and devour the God of Fire.

sn: आदित्यं पातयिष्यामि सनक्षत्रं महीतले॥ शतक्रतुं वधिष्यामि पास्यामि वरुणालयम्।
en: I shall bring down the very welkin garnished with stars. And I shall slay Satakratu and drink up the abode itself of Varuna.

sn: पर्वतांचूर्णयिष्यामि दारयिष्यामि मेदिनीम्॥ दीर्घकालं प्रसुप्तस्य कुम्भकर्णस्य विक्रमम्। अद्य पश्यन्तु भूतानि भक्ष्यमाणानि सर्वशः।। न त्विदं त्रिदिवं सर्वमाहारो मम पूर्यते॥
en: I shall crush the mountains and rive the earth. And today let all creatures as they are being eaten up, witness the prowess of Kumbhakarņa, after he has slept for a long time. Even the celestial regions do not suffice for me as my fare.

sn: वधेन ते दाशरथेः सुखावहं सुखं समाहर्तुमहं व्रजामि। निहत्य रामं सह लक्ष्मणेन खादामि सर्वान्हरियूथमुख्यान्॥
en: I go for securing felicity us huring in pleasures plenteous flowing from the destruction of Dasaratha's son. And slaying Rāma along with Lakşmaņa, I shall eat up all the foremost of monkey-bands.

sn: रमस्व राजन्पिब चाद्य वारुणीं कुरुष्व कृत्यानि विनीय दुःखम्। मयाद्य रामे गमिते यमक्षयं चिराय सीता वशगा भविष्यति ॥
en: Make merry, my king; today drink Varuni. Enjoy pleasures, banishing sorrow. And today on my having despatched Rāma to the mansion of Yama, Sītā shall come under your control for good.
