sn: तदुक्तमतिकायस्य बलिनो बाहुशालिनः। कुम्भकर्णस्य वचनं श्रुत्वोवाच महोदरः॥
en: Hearing the speech of the huge-bodied, longarmed and mighty Kumbhkarma, Mahodara said.

sn: कुम्भकर्ण कुले जातो धृष्टः प्राकृतदर्शनः। अविलसो न शक्नोषि कृत्यं सर्वत्र वेदितुम्॥
en: O Kumbhakarņa, although sprung in a noble line, you are wondrous haughty and of a vulgar form; and you are not everywhere competent to discern your course.

sn: नहि राजा न जानीते कुम्भकर्ण नयानयौ। त्वं तु कैशोरकाद्धृष्टः केवलं वक्तुमिच्छसि॥
en: It certainly cannot well be that the king cannot distinguish between proper and improper; but you has from your youth upwards been insolent; and your joy is in talking perenially.

sn: स्थानं वृद्धिं च हानिं च देशकालविधानवित्। आत्मनश्च परेषां च बुध्यते राक्षसर्षभः॥
en: But the foremost of the Raksasa is versed in place and increase and injury, and know the duties touching season and place, and how to advance his own party and lower that of the foe.

sn: यत् त्वशक्यं बलवता कर्तुं प्राकृतबुद्धिना। अनुपासितवृद्धेन कः कुर्यात्तादृशं नरः॥
en: But what person ever act according to what is proposed feebly by one having strength, yet of inferior intelligence, and who has never respected the aged.

sn: यांस्तु धर्मार्थकामांस्त्वं ब्रवीषि पृथगाश्रयान्। अवबोद्धं स्वभावेन नहि लक्षणमस्ति तान्॥
en: You are not naturally competent to understand what you yourself says touching the opposed virtue, profit and desire.

sn: कर्म चैव हि सर्वेषां कारणानां प्रयोजनम्। श्रेयः पापीयसां चात्र फलं भवति कर्मणाम्।७।। निःश्रेयसफलावेव धर्मार्थवितरावपि। अधर्मानर्थयोः प्राप्तं फलं च प्रात्यवायिकम्॥ ऐहलौकिकपारक्यं कर्म पुंभिनिषेव्यते। कर्माण्यपि तु कल्पानि लभते काममास्थितः।९।। तत्र क्लृप्तमिदं राज्ञा हृदि कार्य मतं च नः। शत्रौ हि साहसं यत्तत्किमिवानापनीयते॥
en: Verily action is the spring of all agencies of happiness or misery; and it is only those that act either well or ill that reap the results of their acts. Virtue, and interest bring about emancipation as well as heaven and prosperity. But evil come from unrighteousness and harms spring therefrom. People reap the fruit of their acts in this world or the next; but the fruit of desire is reaped readily. Therefore should a king set about attaining his desire. And this also had we advised you with our soul. And that is the harm that one should display his prowess before a foe?

sn: एकस्यैवाभियाने तु हेतुर्यः प्राहतस्त्वया। तत्राप्यनुपपन्नं ते वक्ष्यामि यदसाधु च॥
en: Did you show the reasons for your taking the field alone? But I shall point you out what is improper and unreasonable in this (proposed) course.

sn: येन पूर्वं जनस्थाने बहवोऽतिबलास्तदा। राक्षसा राघवं ध्वस्ताः कथमेको जयिष्यसि॥
en: How shall you alone vanquish that Rāghava who formerly routed in Jansthāna innumerable Rākşasas possessed of exceeding strength?

sn: ये पूर्व निर्जितास्तेन जनस्थाने महौजसः। राक्षसांस्तान्पुरे सर्वान्भीतानद्य न पश्यसि ॥
en: Did you not today in the palace behold those powerful Rākşasas that had been beaten in Janasthana-cowed down in fear?

sn: तं सिंहमिव संक्रुद्धं रामं दशरथात्मजम्। सर्प सुप्तमहो बुद्ध्वा प्रबोधयितुमिच्छसि॥
en: Alas! you wished to awake Rima, son to Daśaratha-knowing full well that le resembles an enraged lion or a sleeping serpeni.

sn: ज्वलन्तं तेजसा नित्यं क्रोधेन च दुरासदम्। कस्तं मृत्युमिवासह्यमासादयितुमर्हति॥
en: But whom does it behove to confront him ever flaming in energy, difficult of being approached when enraged, and unbearable even like Death himself?

sn: संशयस्थमिदं सर्व शत्रोः प्रतिसमासने। एकस्य गमनं तात नहि मे रोचते भृशम्॥
en: On approaching the foe, this whole host itself shall be imperilled: and therefore, my child, your marching alone does nowise recommend itself to me.

sn: हीनार्थस्तु समृद्धार्थ को रिपुं प्राकृतं यथा। निश्चितं जीवितत्यागे वशमानेतुमिच्छति॥
en: Who is there that, albeit weak bent on renouncing his life, wish to bring under subjection a foe that is powerful, as if he would act with reference to one that is inferior?

sn: यस्य नास्ति मनुष्येषु सदृशो राक्षसोत्तम। कथमाशंससे योद्धं तुल्येनेन्द्रविवस्वतोः॥
en: O foremost of Rākasas, why did you wish to fight with him whose peer there is none among men, and who is equal to Indra and Vavasvata himself?

sn: एवमुक्त्वा तु संरब्धं कुम्भकर्ण महोदरः। उवाच रक्षसां मध्ये रावणं लोकरावणम्॥
en: Having said this to Kumbhakarņa wrought up with wrath, Mahodara addressed that destroyer of creature-Ravana-in the midst of the Raksasas.

sn: लब्ध्वा पुरस्ताद्वैदहीं किमर्थं त्वं विलम्बसे। यदीच्छसि तदा सीता वशगा ते भविष्यति॥
en: Having already obtained Vaidehi, why did you delay ? If you wish it, Sītā shall come under your control.

sn: दृष्टः कश्चिदुपायो मे सीतोपस्थानकारकः। रुचितश्चेतस्वया बुद्ध्या राक्षसेन्द्र ततः शृणु॥
en: I have perceived a way as to how Sītā may smile upon you. Do you listen: and should it please you; act you accordingly.

sn: अहं द्विजिह्वः संहादी कुम्भकर्णो वितर्दनाः। पञ्च रामवधायैते निर्यान्तीत्यवघोषय॥
en: Do you proclaim it about that I and Dvijihva and Samhrādī, and Kumbhakarņa and Vitardanathese five-are marching for compassing the destruction of Rāma.

sn: ततो गत्वा वयं युद्धं दास्यामस्तस्य यत्नतः। जेष्यामो यदि ते शत्रूनोपायैः कार्यमस्ति नः॥
en: We, marching out, shall battle with Rāma, putting forth our uttermost. And if we succeed in securing victory, no expedient need we resort to (or bringing Sītā round).

sn: अथ जीवति नः शत्रुर्वयं च कृतसंयुगाः। ततः समभिपत्स्यामो मनसा यत्समीक्षितम्॥
en: But if our foe live after fight and we also having faught the fight, then shall we do what I conceive in my mind.

sn: वयं युद्धादिहैष्यामो रुधिरेण समुक्षिताः। विदार्य स्वतनुं बाणै रामनामाङ्कितैः शरैः॥ भक्षितो राघवोऽस्माभिर्लक्ष्मणश्चेति वादिनः। ततः पादौ ग्रहीष्यामस्त्वं नः कामं प्रपूरय॥
en: We shall come hither from the field, bathed in blood, and having our bodies cleft with arrows marked with the name of Rama. And we shall give out that both Ráma and Lakşmaņa have been eaten up by us And then we Shall hold your feet, saying, 'Do you gratify us'.

sn: ततोऽवघोषय पुरे गजस्कन्धेन पार्थिव। हतो रामः सह भ्रात्रा ससैन्य इति सर्वतः॥
en: Then, O king, do you through Gajaskandha publish it all round that Ráma has been slain along with his brother and the army.

sn: प्रीतो नाम ततो भूत्वा भृत्यानां त्वमरिंदम! भोगांश्च परिवारांश्च कामान्वसु च दापय॥ ततो माल्यानि वासासि वीराणामनुलेपनम्। देयं च बहु योधेभ्यः स्वयं च मुदितः पिब॥
en: O repressor of foes, (pretending to be) well pleased, do you dispense-viands, and servants, and objects of enjoyments, and wealth to your retainers; and to the many heroes and warriors distribute wreaths and attires and unguents. And do you (Simulating) delight drink.

sn: ततोऽस्मिन्बहुलीभूते कौलीने सर्वतो गते। भक्षितः ससुहृद्रामो राक्षसैरिति विश्रुते॥ प्रविश्याश्वास्य चापि त्वं सीतां रहसि सान्त्वयन्। धनधान्यैश्च कामैश्च रत्नैश्चैनां प्रलोभय ॥
en: On this report-name that Rāma has been eaten up by the Rākşasas along with his friends, having spread round and round entering (the Asoka wood), and soothing and pacifying Sītā in solitude, Allure her with corn and riches and gems.

sn: अनयोपधया राजन्भूयः शोकानुबन्धया। अकामा त्वद्वशं सीता नष्टनाथा गमिष्यति॥
en: By this deceit, О king, working powerfully through Sītā's sorrow, she albeit unwilling, shall, having lost her lord, come under your control.

sn: रमणीयं हि भर्तारं विनष्टमधिगम्य सा। नैराश्यात्स्त्रीलघुत्वाच्च त्वद्वशं प्रतिपत्स्यते ॥
en: Losing her charming husband, she from despair and female railty, shall come under your away.

sn: सा पुरा सुखसंवृद्धा सुखार्हा दुःखकर्षिता। त्वय्यधीनं सुखं ज्ञात्वा सर्वथैव गमिष्यति॥
en: Having formerly been brought up in happiness, she, although worthy of felicity, (ultimately) had come by misfortune. And now finding happiness to be in your custody, she shall unreservedly come over to you.

sn: एतत्सुनीतं मम दर्शनेन रामं हि दृष्टैव भवेदनर्थः। इहैव ते सेत्स्यति मोत्सुको भूर्महानयुद्धेन सुखस्य लाभः॥
en: In my opinion this is the proper course to follow. As soon as you see Rāma, evil shall befall you. Remain here. Do not wish (to go to the field). By refraining from fight, you shall acquire great good.

sn: अनष्टसैन्यो हनवाप्तसंशयो रिपुं त्वयुद्धेन जयञ्जनाधिप। यशश्च पुण्यं च महान्महीपतिः श्रियं च कीर्ति च चिरं समश्नुते॥
en: O lord of people, by conquering the foe without battle, you without losing your forces and putting yourself to peril, you, O lord of earth, shall attain fame and high religious merit, and prosperity and renown for ever and for ever.

sn: स तथोक्तस्तु निर्भय॑ कुम्भकर्णो महोदरम्। अब्रवीद्राक्षसश्रेष्ठं भ्रातरं रावणं ततः॥
en: Thus addressed, Kumbhakarņa rebuking Mahodara, said to that foremost of Rākşasa-his brother-Ravana.

sn: सोऽहं तव भयं घोरं वधात्तस्य दुरात्मनः। रामस्याद्य प्रमार्जामि निर्वैरो हि सुखी भव॥
en: Even I shall remove your great fear by slaying the wicked minded Råma. On your foe having been slain, attain you ease.

sn: गर्जन्ति न वृथा शूरा निर्जला इव तोयदाः। पश्य संपद्यमानं तु गर्जितं युधि कर्मणा॥
en: It is not for naught that the heroes roar, like to clouds containing no rain. Behold you their, like roaring resulting in action in the field!

sn: न मर्षयन्ति चात्मानं संभावयितुमात्मना। अदर्शयित्वा शूरास्तु कर्म कुर्वन्ति दुष्करम्॥
en: Heroes do not vaunt: but without boasting of their prowess in speech, they perform feats difficult of being achieved.

sn: विक्लवानां ह्यबुद्धीनां राज्ञां पण्डितमानिनाम्। रोचते त्वद्वचो नित्यं कथ्यमानं महोदर॥
en: O Mahodara, what you say is ever acceptable only to kings that are incompetent, and foolish, pluming themselves on their knowledge.

sn: युद्धे कापुरुषैनित्यं भवद्भिः प्रियवादिभिः। राजानमनुगच्छद्भिः सर्वं कृत्यं विनाशितम्॥ राजशेषा कृता लङ्का क्षीणः कोशो बलं हतम्। राजानमिममासाद्य सुहृच्चिह्नममित्रकम्॥
en: All the affairs of the monarch have been wrecked by you-cravens in fight, sleek-tongued, following the king (fawning) you have made Lankā contain only the king, the treasury is lean; and the forces have been slain. By the king you have done like foes in the guise of friends.

sn: महोदरोऽयं रामात्तु एष निर्याम्यहं युद्धमुद्यतः शत्रुनिर्जये। दुर्नयं भवतामद्य समीकर्तुं महाहवे।।।।।
en: For repairing in mighty conflict the wrong that you have perpetrated, I am about to set out for battle for routing the enemy.

sn: एवमुक्तवतो वाक्यं कुम्भकर्णस्य धीमतः। प्रत्युवाच ततो वाक्यं प्रहसनराक्षसाधिपः॥
en: Thus addressed by the intelligent Kumbhakarna, the lord of Raksasas, laughing answered.

sn: परित्रस्तो न संशयः। नहि रोचयते तात युद्धं युद्धविशारद ॥
en: Sure this Mahodara is affrighted at Rāma. Therefore, my child, O you versed in warfare, he does not relish battle.

sn: कश्चिन्मे त्वत्समो नास्ति सौहृदेन बलेन च। गच्छ शत्रुवधाय त्वं कुम्भकर्णजयाय च॥
en: Like you have I none either in friendship or strength. Therefore, O Kumbhakama, go for destroying the foe and securing celebrity.

sn: शयानः शत्रुनाशार्थं भवान्संबोधितो मया। अयं हि कालः सुमहान्राक्षसानामरिंदम॥
en: I have waked you up that wast lying down, in order that you mightst destroy the enemy. O subduer of foes, perilous is the time for the Rāks asas.

sn: संगच्छ शूलमादाय पाशहस्त इवान्तकः। वानरानराजपुत्रौ च भक्षयादित्यतेजसौ॥
en: Go forth, grasping your spear, like the noosehanded Destroyer himself. Do you devour up the monkeys as well as the princes possessed of the energy of the Sun himself.

sn: समालोक्य तु ते रूपं विद्रविष्यन्ति वानराः। रामलक्ष्मणयोश्चापि हृदये प्रस्फुटिष्यतः॥
en: On seeing your form the monkeys shall flee away; and the breasts of Rāma and Lakşmaņa shall be riven.

sn: एवमुक्त्वा महातेजाः कुम्भकर्ण महाबलम्। पुनर्जातमिवात्मानं मेने राक्षसपुङ्गवः॥
en: Having spoken thus to Kumbhakarna endowed with prodigious might, that foremost of Rakşasas-the exceedingly energetic Rāvaņa-felt as if he had received life over again.

sn: कुम्भकर्णबलाभिज्ञो जानंस्तस्य पराक्रमम्। बभूव मुदितो राजा शशाङ्क इव निर्मलः॥
en: And well acquainted with Kumbhakarņa's might, and knowing his prowess, the king felt delighted, like the cloudless Moon.

sn: इत्येवमुक्तः संहृष्टो निर्जगाम महाबलः। राज्ञस्तु वचनं श्रुत्वा योद्धमुद्युक्तवांस्तदा॥
en: Having been thus accosted, that highly powerful one, went out cheerfully. And hearing the king's speech, he made ready for fight.

sn: आददे निशितं शूलं वेगाच्छत्रुनिबर्हणः। सर्वं कालायसं दीप्तं तप्तकाञ्चनभूषणम्॥ इन्द्राशनिसमप्रख्यं वज्रप्रतिमगौरवम्। देवदानवगन्धर्वयक्षपन्नगसूदनम्॥ रक्तमाल्यमहादामं स्वतश्चोद्तपावकम्। आदाय विपुलं शूलं शत्रुशोणितरञ्जितम्॥ कुम्भकर्णो महातेजा रावणं वाक्यमब्रवीत्। गमिष्याम्यहमेकाकी तिष्ठत्विह बलं महत्॥
en: He took a whetted dart, destructive to foes on account of its impetuous vehemence; entirely made of black iron; flaming: decorated with garniture, of shining gold; looking like Indra's asani; ponderous as the thunder-bolt; capable of destroying gods and Dānavas, Gandharvas, Yakşas and Pannagas, adorned with festoons of crimson flowers; and belching forth flames. And taking that huge dart decked with the blood of foes. The wondrous energetic Kumbhakarna spoke to Ravana, saying, I shall go alone; let this mighty host remain here.

sn: अद्य तान्क्षुधितः क्रुद्धो भक्षयिष्यति वानरान्। कुम्भकर्णवचः श्रुत्वा रावणो वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
en: Today hungry and enraged, I shall devour up the monkeys. Hearing Kumbhakarma's words. Rāvana said.

sn: सैन्यैः परिवृतो गच्छ शूलमुद्गरपाणिभिः। वानरा हि महात्मानः शूराः सुव्यवसायिनः॥ एकाकिनं प्रमत्तं वा नयेयुदर्शनैः क्षयम्। तस्मात्परमदुर्धर्षः सैन्यैः परिवृतो व्रज॥ रक्षसामहितं सर्वं शत्रुपक्षं निषूदय॥
en: Go you surrounded by the forces bearing darts and maces in their hands. The monkeys are highsouled, heroic and well-skilled in battle; and if they find you alone or unwary, they may slay you with their teeth, Therefore do you exceedingly irresistible, go, environed by the forces; and destroy the entire party of the foes, who are bent upon doing harm to the Rākşasa.

sn: अथासनात्समुत्पत्य स्रजं गणिकृतान्तराम्। आबबन्ध महातेजाः कुम्भकर्णस्य रावणः॥
en: Then starting up form his seat, the exceedingly energetic Rāvana hung on Kumbhakarņa's neck a wreath stringed with gems in the centre.

sn: अङ्गदान्यङ्गुलीवेष्टन्वराण्याभरणानि च। हारं च शशिसंकाशमाबबन्ध महात्मनः॥
en: Rāvaņa also decked that high-souled one with Angadas, and finger fences and noble ornaments, and a chain resembling the Moon.

sn: दिव्यानि च सुगन्धीनि माल्यदामानि रावणः। गात्रेषु सज्जयामास श्रोत्रयोश्चास्य कुण्डले॥ काञ्चनाङ्गदकेयूरनिष्काभरणभूषितः। कुम्भकर्णो बृहत्कर्णः सुहृतोऽग्निरिवाबभौ ॥
en: Rāvaņa adorned his person with garlands gorgeous and fragrant, and set ear-rings to his ears. And adorned with golden Angadas and Keyūras and other ornaments of gold, the largeeared Kumbhakarņa appeared like a fire fed full of sacrificial libations.

sn: श्रोणिसूत्रेण महता मेचकेन व्यराजत। अमृतोत्पादने नद्धो भुजंगेनेव मन्दरः॥
en: With his great dark girdle he seemed like the Mandara fastened by the serpent on the occasion of the churning of the sea.

sn: स काञ्चनं भारसहं निवातं विद्युत्प्रभं दीप्तमिवात्मभासा। आबध्यमानः कवचं रराज संध्याभ्रसंवीत इवाद्रिराजः॥
en: Donning on his impenetrable golden mail, splendid like lightning, and shining in its own brilliance, Kumbhakarņa appeared like the monarch of mountains enveloped with evening clouds.

sn: सर्वाभरणसर्वाङ्गः शूलपाणिः स राक्षसः। त्रिविक्रमकृतोत्साहो नारायण इवाबभौ॥
en: Having all his limbs adorned with ornaments and bearing a dart in his hand, the Rakşasas resembled Nārāyaṇa in elation of spirits, when he covered heaven and earth and the nether regions with three paces.

sn: भ्रातरं संपरिष्वज्य कृत्वा चापि प्रदक्षिणम्। प्रणम्य शिरसा तस्मै प्रतस्थे स महाबलः॥
en: Then embracing his brother and going round him and bowing down the head to him, that exceedingly powerful one went out.

sn: तमाशीभिः प्रशस्ताभिः प्रेषयामास रावणः। शङ्खदुन्दुभिनिर्घोषैः सैन्यैश्चापि वरायुधैः॥
en: Rāvana sent him with choice benedictions, while he caused kettle-drums and conchs to be sounded and force equipped with excellent weapons, to accompany Kumbhakarņa.

sn: तं गजैश्च तुरंगैश्च स्यन्दनैश्चाम्बुदस्वनैः। अनुजग्मुर्महात्मानो रथिनो रथिनां वरम्॥
en: And high-souled mighty warriors followed that foremost of heroes with elephant and steeds and chariots sending out rattle resembling the rumbling of thunder.

sn: स(रुष्टैः खरैश्चैव सिंहद्विपमृगद्विजैः। अनुजग्मुश्च तं घोरं कुम्भकर्ण महाबलम्॥
en: And mounting serpents and camels and asses and lions and leopards and deer and birds, (Rāks asas) followed the grim Kumbhakarņa endowed with tremendous strength.

sn: स पुष्पवर्षैरवकीर्यमाणो धृतातपत्रः शितशूलपाणिः। महोत्कटः शोणितगन्धमत्तो विनिर्ययौ दानवदेवशत्रुः॥
en: And strewn with blossoms, and, with an umbrella held over him, that exceedingly terrible enemy of the Deities and the Dănvas, wielding a dz.: in his hand-went out maddened with the smell of blood.

sn: पदातयश्च बहवो महासारा महाबलाः। अन्वयू राक्षसा भीमा भीमाक्षाः शस्त्रपाणयः॥
en: Countless footmen wondrous powerful and mighty and dreadful and fierce-sighted Räksasas, carrying weapons in their hands, went in his wake.

sn: रक्ताक्षाः सुबहुव्यामा नीलाञ्जनचयोपमाः। शूलानुद्यम्य खङ्गांश्च निशितांश्च परश्वधान्॥ भिन्दिपालांश्च परिघान्गदाश्च मुसलानि च। तालस्कन्धांश्च विपुलान्क्षेपणीयान्दुरासदान्॥
en: The Räkşasa measuring each many a vyama and red, eyed, and resembling masses of darkblue collyrium, went out upraising darts and swords and sharpened axes and bhindipälas and parighas and maces and huge talaskandhas and irrisistible Kșepaņis.

sn: अथान्यद्वपुरादाय दारुणं घोरदर्शनम्। निष्पपात महातेजाः कुम्भकर्णो महाबलः॥
en: The exceedingly energetic Kumbhakarna endowed with prodigious strength sallied forth, assuming another form terrific and dreadful to behold.

sn: धनुःशतपरिणाहः स षट्शतसमुच्छ्रितः। रौद्रः शकटचक्राक्षो महापर्वतसंनिभः॥ संनिपत्य च रक्षांसि दग्धशैलोपमो महान्। कुम्भकर्णो महावक्रः प्रहसन्निदमब्रवीत्।॥ अद्य वानरमुख्यानां तानि यूथानि भागशः। निर्दहिष्यामि संक्रुद्धः पतङ्गानिव पावकः॥
en: And the gigantic huge-faced and fierce Kumbhakarņa, measuring an hundred bows in breadth and six hundred in altitude, having eyes resembling car-wheels, and resembling a towering hill, or a mountain burnt, marshalling the Raksasa, said with a complacent countenance, “Like fire consuming insects, shall I today, wrought up with wroth, burn up one by one the bands of the flower of the monkeyforces.

sn: नापराध्यन्ति मे कामं वानरा वनचारिणः। जातिरस्मद्विधानां सा पुरोद्यानविभूषणम्॥
en: But the wood-ranging monkeys have not transgressed anywise to the like of us. That species is the ornament of the gardens attached to our residences.

sn: पुररोधस्य मूलं तु राघवः सहलक्ष्मणः। हते तस्मिन्हतं सर्व तं वधिष्यामि संयुगे॥
en: The cause of the siege of the city is Rāghava along with Laksmana. He being slain, all are slain. Therefore shall I slay him in battle.

sn: एवं तस्य ब्रुवाणस्य कुम्भकर्णस्य रक्षसः। नादं चक्कुर्महाघोरं कम्पयन्त इवार्णवम्॥
en: As the Rākşa—Kumbhakarņa—was speaking thus, the Rākşasas sent up terrific shouts, as if making the very sea shake.

sn: तस्य निष्पततस्तूर्णं कुम्भकर्णस्य धीमतः। बभूवुर्घोररूपाणि निमित्तानि समन्ततः॥
en: As the intelligent Kumbhakarņa sallied out speedily, dreadful were the omens that presented themselves on all sides.

sn: उल्काशनियुता मेघा बभूवुर्गर्दभारुणाः। ससागरवना चैव वसुधा समकम्पत ॥
en: Clouds containing meteors and lightning looked dark like asses. And the earth shook with her oceans and woods.

sn: घोररूपाः शिवा नेदुः सज्वालकवलैर्मुखैः। मण्डलान्यपसव्यानि बबन्धुश्च विहंगमाः॥
en: And fierce jackals began to cry, opening their fiaming mouths. And birds began to wheel at the left.

sn: निष्पपात च गृध्रोऽस्य शूले वै पथि गच्छतः। प्रास्फुरनयनं चास्य सव्यो बाहुरकम्पत॥
en: As he marched a vulture alighted on his dart. And his left eye throbbed and his left arm shook.

sn: निष्पपात तदा चोल्का ज्वलन्ती भीमनि:स्वना। आदित्यो निष्प्रभश्चासीन वाति च सुखोऽनिलः॥
en: A meteor dropped down with a tremendous crash. And the sun was bedimmed, and the air did not blow, enhancing pleasure.

sn: अचिन्तयन्महोत्पातानुदितान्रोहमर्षणान्। निर्ययौ कुम्भकर्णस्तु कृतान्तबलचोदितः॥
en: But without heeding these mighty omens that took place, capable of making people's down stand on end, Kumbhakarna went out, urged on by the force of the Finisher.

sn: स लवयित्वा प्राकारं पद्भ्यां पर्वतसंनिभः। स ददर्श धनप्रख्यं वानरानीकमद्भुतम्॥
en: And leaping over the wall with his legs, that one resembling a mountain saw the wonderful array of the monkeys, resembling clouds.

sn: ते दृष्ट्वा राक्षसश्रेष्ठं वानराः पर्वतोपमम्। वायुनुन्न इव घना ययुः सर्वा दिशस्तदा॥
en: Seeing that foremost of Rākşasas resembling a hill, the monkeys began to disperse in all the ten cardinal directions like clouds driven by the wind.

sn: तद्वानरानीकमतिप्रचण्डं दिशो द्रवद्भिनमिवाभ्रजालम्। स कुम्भकर्णः समवेक्ष्य हर्षान्ननाद भूयो घनवद्धनाभः॥
en: Seeing that terrific host of monkeys scattering in all directions, like clouds broken through (by winds), Kumbhakarņa possessed the splendour of clouds, from joy, emitted roars like clouds.

sn: ते तस्य घोरं निनदं निशम्य यथा निनादं दिवि वारिदस्य। पेतुर्धरण्यां बहवः प्लवंगा निकृत्तमूला इव शालवृक्षाः॥
en: Hearing those terrible shouts like to the roaring of clouds in the welkin, innumerable monkeys dropped to the earth even as sāla trees that have their roots severed.

sn: विपुलपरिघवान्स कुम्भकर्णो रिपुनिधनाय विनिःसृतो महात्मा। कपिगणभयमाददत्सुभीमं प्रभुरिव किंकरदण्डवान्युगान्ते॥
en: And issuing forth for destroying the foe, the high-souled Kumbhakarņa, equipped with a tremendous bludgeon, struck extreme terror into the monkey-ranks, like to the Lord armed with the Fatal rod at the Universal wreck.

sn: स लवयित्वा प्राकारं गिरुकूटोपमो महान्। निर्ययौ नगरातूर्णं कुम्भकर्णो महाबलः॥
en: Having leapt over the wall, the exceedingly powerful and gigantic Kumbhakarņa resembling a mountain-summit, speedily went out of the city.

sn: ननाद च महानादं समुद्रमभिनादयन्। विजयन्निव निर्घातान्विधमन्निव पर्वतान् ॥
en: Then he sent up a mighty shout making the sea resound, and as if drowning the roar of the thunder and riving mountains.

sn: तमवध्यं मघवता यमेन वरुणेन वा। प्रेक्ष्य भीमाक्षमायन्तं वानरा विप्रदुद्रुवुः॥
en: Seeing that fierce-eyed one, incapable of being vanquished by Maghavān or Varuņa or Yama, the monkeys began to fly away.

sn: तांस्तु विप्रदुतान्दृष्ट्वा राजपुत्रोऽङ्गदोऽब्रवीत्। नलं नीलं गवाक्षं च कुमुदं च महाबलम्॥
en: Seeing them scamper, the king's son-Angada said to Nala and Nīla and Gavākșa and the mighty Kumuda.

sn: आत्मनस्तानि विस्मृत्य वीर्याण्यभिजनानि च। क्व गच्छत भयत्रस्ताः प्राकृता हरयो यथा॥
en: Forgetting your lineage and prowess, whither do you, exercised with fear, fly-like inferior monkeys?

sn: साधु सौम्या निवर्तध्वं किं प्राणान्परिरक्षथ। नालं युद्धाय वै रक्षो महतीयं विभीषिका॥
en: You amiable ones, desist. Why should you save yourselves? This Rākşasa does not come to fight, this is only a great phenomenon to affright.

sn: महतीमुत्थितामेनां राक्षसानां विभीषिकाम्। विक्रमाद्विधमिष्यामो निवर्तध्वं प्लवंगमाः।७।।
en: We shall by our vigour destroy this featful phenomenon of the Rākşasas that has presented itself. Therefore, let the monkeys desist.

sn: कृच्छ्रेण तु समाश्वस्य संगम्य च ततस्ततः। वृक्षानगृहीत्वा हरयः संप्रतस्थू रणाजिरे॥
en: Cheered with much ado, the monkeys rallying, took up trees and advanced to the field of fight.

sn: ते निवर्त्य तु संरब्धाः कुम्भकर्णं वनौकसः। निर्जघ्नुः पर क्रुद्धाः समदा इव कुञ्जराः॥ प्रांशुभिर्गिरिशृङ्गैश्च शिलाभिश्च महाबलाः। पादपैः पुष्पिताग्रैश्च हन्यमानो न कम्पते॥
en: Ceasing from flight, the wood-rangers waxing, enraged, began to assail Kumbhakarņa, like to elephants in rut. And the exceedingly strong Kumbhakarna, attacked with towering mountain peaks and crags and trees with flowering top, did not shake.

sn: तस्य गात्रेषु पतिता भिद्यन्ते बहवः शिलाः। पादपाः पुष्पिताग्राश्च भग्नाः पेतुर्महीतले॥
en: And countless crags descending on his person, were shattered; and trees with flowering tops, being broken, fell down to the earth.

sn: सोऽपि सैन्यानि संक्रुद्धो वानराणां महौजसाम्। ममन्थ परमायत्तो वनान्यग्निरिवोत्थितः॥
en: Incapable of containing himself (through rage), Kumbhakarņa on his part fell to agitating the ranks of the powerful monkeys, even as a fire breaking out burn dowit a forest.

sn: लोहितार्दास्तु बहवः शेरते वानरर्षभाः। निरस्ताः पतिता भूमौ ताम्रपुष्पा इव दुमाः॥
en: Many a prime monkey, crimsoned and drenched (with blood) lay down (on the ground); and many, resisted dropped to the earth, like trees bearing coppery flowers.

sn: लक्यन्तः प्रधावन्तो वानरा नावलोकयन्। केचित्समुद्रे पतिताः केचिद्गगनमास्थिताः॥
en: Without looking before or after, the monkeys bounded and rushed. And on being attacked by the Rāksasa with ease some of those heroes dropped into the deep and some entered the wilderness.

sn: वध्यमानास्तु ते वीरा राक्षसेन च लीलया। सागरं येन ते तीर्णाः यथा तेनैव दुद्रुवुः॥ ते स्थलानि तदा निम्नं विवर्णवदना भयात्। ऋक्षा वृक्षान्समारूढाः केचित्पर्वतमाश्रिताः॥
en: Some ran by the same way by which they had crossed the ocean; and some with pale faces darted into downs. And some of the bears ascended up trees, and some took shelter in mountains.

sn: निपेतुः केचिदपरे केचिन्नैवावतस्थिरे। केचिद्भूमौ निपतिताः केचित्सुप्ता मृता इव॥
en: Others dropped down; and some ran on. And some fell down to the earth, and some lay insensible as if dead.

sn: तान्समीक्ष्याङ्गदो भग्नान्वानरानिदमब्रवीत्। अवतिष्ठत युध्यामो निवर्तध्वं प्लवंगमाः॥
en: Seeing the monkeys break down, Angada addressed them, saying, “Stay we shall fight.

sn: भग्नानां वो न पश्यामि परिक्रम्य महीमिमाम्। स्थानं सर्वे निवर्तध्वं किं प्राणान्परिरक्षथ ॥
en: Desist, you monkeys. Going round this Earth place find I none where you may rest. Stop you all. What is the need of preserving your lives.

sn: निरायुधानां क्रमतामसङ्गगतिपौरुषाः। दारा ह्युपहसिष्यन्ति स वै घातः सुजीवताम्॥
en: You poltroons, if you fly away leaving your arms behind, your wives shall deride you; and that is more painful to honourable persons than death itself.

sn: कुलेषु जाताः सर्वेऽस्मिन्विस्तीर्णेषु महत्सु च। कव गच्छत भयत्रस्ताः प्राकृता हरयो यथा। अनार्याः खलु यद्भीतास्त्यक्त्वा वीर्यं प्रधावत॥
en: Born in long and noble lines, whither go you, suffering from fear, like abject monkeys? When renouncing your prowess, you fly away in fear, forsooth you are base.

sn: विकत्थनानि वो यानि भवद्भिर्जनसंसदि। तानि वः क्व नु यातानि सोदग्राणि हतानि च॥
en: Where now is gone that talk of your anent your nobility and the welfare (of your king) which you had held in society.

sn: भीरोः प्रवादाः श्रूयन्ते यस्तु जीवति धिक्कृतः। मार्गः सत्पुरुषैर्जुष्टः सेव्यतां त्यज्यतां भयम्॥
en: He that live, despised (of all), hear the reproach of being a craven. Therefore do you follow the way frequented by the worthy, and cast off fear.

sn: शयामहे वा निहताः पृथिव्यामल्पजीविताः। प्राप्नुयामो ब्रह्मलोकं दुष्प्रापं च कुयोधिभिः॥ अवाप्नुयामः कीर्ति वा निहत्वा शत्रुमाहवे। निहता वीरलोकस्य भोक्ष्यामो वसु वानराः॥
en: We will either lie down on the earth, being slain in consequence of our shortness of days, and thus attain the region of Brahmä incapable of being attained by dastards; or achieve renown by slaying the foe in fight and slain in battle, we shall enjoy the wealth of the region of heroes.

sn: न कुम्भकर्णः काकुत्स्थं दृष्ट्वा जीवन्गमिष्यति। दीव्यमानमिवासाद्य पतङ्गो ज्वलनं यथा॥
en: Like an insect coming to a glowing and flaming fire, Kumbhakarna, seeing Kākutstha, shall not away.hence living.

sn: पलायनेन चोद्दिष्टाः प्राणानक्षामहे वयम्। एकेन बहवो भग्ना यशोनाशं गमिष्यति॥
en: If we save our lives by flight, and if the many are brought down by one, we shall lose our fame utterly.

sn: एवं ब्रुवाणं तं शूरमङ्गदं कनकाङ्गदम्। द्रवमाणास्ततो वाक्यमूचुः शूरविगर्हितम् ॥
en: As Angada decked in golden angadas was saying this, the monkeys, flying away spoke to that hero words not worthy of being spoken to an hero.

sn: कृतं नः कदनं घोरं कुम्भकर्णेन रक्षसा। न स्थानकालो गच्छामो दयितं जीवितं हि नः॥
en: Great is the havoc that the Rākşasa-Kumbhakarma-has spread among us. “This not the time to stay: life is dear to us."

sn: एतावदुक्त्वा वचनं सर्वे ते भेजिरे दिशः। भीमं भीमाक्षमायान्तं दृष्ट्वा वानरयूथपाः॥
en: Having said this the monkey bands darted to the ten cardinal points, as they saw that dreadful and grim-eyed one approach.

sn: द्रवमाणास्तु ते वीरा अङ्गदेन वलीमुखाः। सान्त्वनैश्चानुमानैश्च ततः सर्वे निवर्तिताः॥
en: As those flower of the forces were on the flight, those heroes were made to desist by Angada with words of comfort and hope pointing to the future.

sn: प्रहर्षमुपनीताश्च वालिपुत्रेण धीमता। आज्ञाप्रतीक्षास्तस्थुश्च सर्वे वानरयूथपाः॥
en: On being cheered by the intelligent son of Vāli, all the monkey-bands stood expecting his commands.

sn: ऋषभशरभमैन्दधूम्रनीलाः कुमुदसुषेणगवाक्षरम्भताराः। द्विविदपनसवायुपुत्रमुख्यास्त्वरिततराभिमुखं रणं प्रयाताः॥
en: Rşabha, Sarabha, Mainda, Dhūmra, Nila, Kumuda, Susena, Gavaksa, Rambha, Dvivida, Panasa, and son of wind Hanuman and other powerf:! leaders speedily proceeded to the battle field.

sn: ते निवृत्ता महाकायाः श्रुत्वाङ्गदवचस्तदा। नैष्ठिकी बुद्धिमास्थाय सर्वे संग्रामकाङ्गिणः॥
en: Having desisted on hearing the words of Angada those huge-bodied ones, regaining calmness, became (again) intent on fight.

sn: समुदीरितवीर्यास्ते समारोपितविक्रमाः। पर्यवस्थापिता वाक्यैरङ्गदेन बलीयसा ॥
en: Attaining energy at the exhortation (of Angada), and summoning up their prowess, they stayed in the field agreeable to the words of the powerful Angada.

sn: प्रयाताश्च गता हर्ष मरणे कृतनिश्चयाः। चक्रुः सुतुमुलं युद्धं वानरास्त्यक्तजीविताः॥
en: Inspired with spirits, the monkeys, determined to face their fate, rushed into the conflict, and, casting away all care for their lives, entered into a furious fight (with the foe)

sn: अथ वृक्षान्महाकायाः सानूनि सुमहान्ति च। वानरास्तूर्णमुद्यम्य कुम्भकर्णमभिद्रवन्॥
en: And speedily upraising trees and gigantic crags, the huge-bodied monkeys charged Kumbhakarņa.

sn: कुम्भकर्णः सुसंक्रुद्धो गदामुद्यम्य वीर्यवान्। धर्षयन्स महाकायः समन्ताद्व्यक्षिपद्रिपून्॥
en: Thereat the mighty Kumbhakarņa possessed of a prodigious person waxing wroth taking up his mace let the same alight on the enemies.

sn: शतानि सप्त चाष्टौ च सहस्राणि च वानराः। प्रकीर्णाः शेरते भूमौ कुम्भकर्णेन ताडिताः॥
en: Attacked by Kumbhakarma, seven, eight hundreds and thousands of monkeys measure their lengths on the earth.

sn: षोडशाष्टौ च दश च विंशत्रिंशत्तथैव च। परिक्षिप्य च बाहुभ्यां खादन्स परिधावति।। भक्षयन्भृशसंक्रुद्धो गरुडः पनगानिव॥
en: Casting about his arms, he rush on, devouring sixteen, eight, ten, twenty or thirty. And he devoured (the monkeys) like Garuda swallowing up serpents.

sn: कृच्छ्रेण च समाश्वस्ताः संगम्य च ततस्ततः। वृक्षाद्रिहस्ता हरयस्तस्थुः संग्राममूर्धनि।।।।
en: Then cheered up with much ado, the monkeys meeting together, and taking trees and rocks in their hands, stood their ground in the van of battle.

sn: ततः पर्वतमुत्पाट्य द्विविदः प्लवगर्षभः। दुद्राव गिरिशृङ्गाभं विलम्ब इव तोयदः॥
en: Then uprooting a crag, Dvivide-foremost of monkeys-resembling an extended mass of clouds rushed against (Kumbhakarņa) having the aspect of a mountain-summit.

sn: तं समुत्पाट्य चिक्षेप कुम्भकर्णाय वानरः। तमप्राप्य महाकायं तस्य सैन्येऽपतत्ततः॥ ममर्दाश्वान्गजांश्चापि रथांश्चापि गजोत्तमान्। तानि चान्यानि रक्षांसि एवं चान्यद्रेिः शिरः॥
en: And uprooting it, the monkey hurled it at Kumbhakarņa. And without descending on him, the crag fell down amidst the army, and smashed steeds and elephants and cans and choice chargers.

sn: तच्छैलवेगाभिहतं हताश्वं हतसारथिम्। रक्षसां रुधिरक्लिन्नं बभूवायोधनं महत्॥
en: Then taking another mountain top, Dvivida hurled it at other Rākşas. And smite with the impetus of the peak, Kumbhakarna had his chargers and his charioteers slain; and the terrific field overflowed with the blood of Rākşas.

sn: रथिनो वानरेन्द्राणां शरैः कालान्तकोपमैः। शिरांसि नर्दतां जह्वः सहसा भीमनिःस्वनाः॥
en: And Räksasa car-warriors by means of arrows resembling the Destroyer himself, cut off the heads of the foremost monkeys who had been setting up roars.

sn: वानराश्च महात्मानः समुत्पाट्य महादुमान्। रथानश्वान्गजानुष्ट्राराक्षसानभ्यसूदयन्॥
en: The high-souled monkeys also, uprooting gaints trees, destroyed cars and horses and elephants and camels and Raksasas

sn: हनूमान्शैलशृङ्गाणि शिलाश्च विविधान्दुमान्। ववर्ष कुम्भकर्णस्य शिरस्यम्बरमास्थितः॥
en: And remaining in the sky, Hanumān discharged at Kumbhakarņa's head mountainpeaks and rocks and various trees.

sn: तानि पर्वतशृङ्गाणि शूलेन स बिभेद ह। बभञ्ज वृक्षवर्षं च कुम्भकर्णो महाबलः॥
en: And all those mountain-tops he cut off with his dart; and the mighty Kumbhakarņa also baffled the shower of trees.

sn: ततो हरीणां तदनीकमुग्रं दुद्राव शूलं निशितं प्रगृह्य। तस्थि स तस्यापततः पुरस्तान्महीधराग्रं हनुमान्प्रगृह्य ॥
en: Then grasping his sharpened spear, Kumbhakarņa darted against that terrific array of monkeys. And as he charged them, Hanuman armed with a mountain-peak, stood before him.

sn: स कुम्भकर्ण कुपितो जघान वेगेन शैलोत्तमभीमकायम्। संचुक्षुभे तेन तदाभिभूतो मेदागात्रो रुधिरावसिक्तः॥
en: Waxing enraged (Hanuman) vehemently smote Kumbhakarņa with a gigantic crag. And overpowered by that, Kumbhakarna experienced great torments, and his body was covered with fat and blood.

sn: स शूलमाविध्य तडित्प्रकाशं गिरिर्यथा प्रज्वलिताग्निशृङ्गम्। बाह्वन्तरे मारुतिमाजघान गुहोऽचलं क्रौञ्चमिवोग्रशक्त्या॥
en: Then as Guha had pierced Krauñca with his fierce dart, Kumbhakarna the mountain-like smote the Wind-god's son in the chest with his dart resembling lightning or like a glowing mountain-summit.

sn: स शूलनिर्भिन्नमहाभुजान्तरः प्रविह्वलः शोणितमुद्वमन्रुषा। ननाद भीमं हनुमान्महाहवे युगान्तमेघस्तनितस्वनोपमम्॥
en: And having his mighty chest pierced in the mighty encounter, Hanumān, overwhelmed, and vomiting blood-transported with wrath, set up roars resembling the roaring of the clouds at the universal disruption.

sn: ततो विनेदुः सहसा प्रहृष्टा रक्षोगणास्तं व्यथितं समीक्ष्य। प्लवंगमास्तु व्यथिता भयार्ताः प्रदुद्रुवुः संयति कुम्भकर्णात् ॥
en: Then, beholding him in torments, Raksasas suddenly rejoiced, emitted shouts; and the monkeys aggrieved and overcome with fright, began to fly Kumbhakarna in battle.

sn: ततस्तु नीलो बलवान्पर्यस्थापयन्बलम्। प्रविचिक्षेप शैलाग्रं कुम्भकर्णाय धीमते॥
en: Then the powerful Nīla, arranging his forces, discharged a mountain-peak at the intelligent Kumbhakarma.

sn: तदापतन्तं संप्रेक्ष्य मुष्टिनाभिजघान ह। मुष्टिप्रहाराभिहतं तच्छैलाग्रं व्यशीर्यत।। सविस्फुलिङ्गं सज्वालं निपपात महीतले॥
en: Seeing it descend, he dealt it a blow; and struck by the blow, the mountain-top was shattered in pieces; and dropped to the earth glowing and shooting living flames.

sn: ऋषभः शरभो नीलो गवाक्षो गन्धमादनः। पञ्च वानरशार्दूलाः कुम्भकर्णमुपाद्रवन्॥
en: Then Rşabha and Sarabha and Nīla and Gavākṣa and Gandhamādana, these five terrific monkeys, rushed against Kumbhakarņa.

sn: शैलैर्वृक्षस्तलैः पादैर्मुष्टिभिश्च महाबलाः। कुम्भकर्म महाकायं निजघ्नुः सर्वतो युधि॥
en: And in the encounter those mighty monkeys began to sorely assail the huge-bodied Kumbhakarma with crags and trees and slaps and kicks and blows.

sn: स्पर्शानिव प्रहारांस्तान्वेदयानो न विव्यथे। ऋषभं तु महावेगं बाहुभ्यां परिषस्वजे॥
en: But those blows seemed to him like touches* and did not at all pain him. Then he fastened the vehement Rşabha with his arms. *Like the feel, remarks Rāmánuja, of wreaths, unguents, etc. blows

sn: कुम्भकर्णभुजाभ्यां तु पीडितो वानरर्षभः। निपपातर्षभो भीमः प्रमुखागतशोणितः॥
en: Agonised on being fastened with Kumbhakarma's arms, that foremost of monkeys, the dreadful Rşabha, fell down to the earth, vomiting blood by his mouth.

sn: मुष्टिना शरभं हत्वा जानुना नीलमाहवे। आजघान गवाक्षं तु तलेनेन्द्ररिपुस्तदा ॥
en: Then the enemy of Indra smite, Sarabha with blow, and Nila, in the conflict with his thigh, struck a slap at Gavākṣa.

sn: पादेनाभ्यहनत्क्रुद्धस्तरसा गन्धमादनम्। दत्तप्रहारव्यथिता मुमुहुः शोणितोक्षिताः। निपेतुस्ते तु मेदिन्यां निकृत्ता इव किंशुकाः॥
en: Then he speedily hit by his feet with wrath Gandhamadana. Suffering great . pain in consequence of the (dealt by Kumbhakarņa those monkeys), deprived of their senses and bathed in blood, dropped down to the earth like Kinśukas that have been cut down.

sn: तेषु वानरमुख्येषु पातितेषु महात्मसु। वानराणां सहस्राणि कुम्भकर्ण प्रदुद्रुवुः॥
en: On those high-souled and mighty monkeys falling down, thousands of monkeys rushed at Kumbhakarna.

sn: तं शैलमिव शैलाभाः सर्वे तु प्लवगर्षभाः। समारुह्य समुत्पत्य ददंशुः प्लवगर्षभाः।३१॥
en: Ascending a mountain-summit, those foremost of monkeys, possessed of the splendour of a mountain-peak, sprang upon him and tore him with their teeth.

sn: तं नखैर्दशनैश्चापि मुष्टिभिबाहुभिस्तथा। कुम्भकर्ण महाबाहुं निजघ्नुः प्लवगर्षभाः॥
en: And those foremost of monkeys attacked the long-armed Kumbhakarma with their claws and teeth and blows and arms.

sn: स वानरसहस्रेस्तु विचितः पर्वतोपमः। रराज राक्षसव्याघ्रो गिरिरात्मरुहैरिव॥
en: Then with thousands of monkeys on him that extraordinary onethat fearful Raksasa-resembling a hill, looked like a mountain with trees on it.

sn: बाहुभ्यां वानरान्सर्वान्प्रगृह्य स महाबलः। भक्षयामास संकृद्धो गरुडः पन्नगानिव॥
en: Like Garuda eating up serpents, that wondours strong one, wrought up with rage, devoured those monkeys, seizing them with his arms.

sn: प्रक्षिप्ताः कुम्भकर्णेन वक्रे पातालसंनिभे। नासापुटाभ्यां संजग्मुः कर्णाभ्यां चैव वानराः॥
en: And cast by Kumbhakarņa into his mouth resembling the nether regions the monkeys emerged from his nose and ears.

sn: भक्षयन्भृशसंक्रुद्धो हरीन्पर्वतसंनिभः। बभञ्ज वानरान्सर्वान्संकृद्धो राक्षसोत्तमः॥
en: And eating up the monkeys, that foremost of Raksasas resembling a hill, growing worth, and fired with rage, began to break the monkeys down.

sn: मांसशोणितसंक्लेदां कुर्वन्भूमि स राक्षसः। चचार हरिसैन्येषु कालाग्निरिव मूर्च्छितः॥
en: And transported with passion, that Raksasa, making the earth miry with flesh and blood, spread among the monkey-ranks like to the fire at the time of the Universal dissolution.

sn: वज्रहस्तो यथा शक्रः पाशहस्त इवान्तकः। शूलहस्तो बभौ युद्धे कुम्भकर्णो महाबलः॥
en: In that encounter, Kumbhakarņa armed with his dart in his hand, resembled the thunderhanded ſakra, or the noose-handed Destroyer himself.

sn: यथा शुष्काण्यरण्यानि ग्रीष्मे दहति पावकः। तथा वानरसैन्यानि कुम्भकर्णो ददाह सः।३९।।
en: As a conflagration burn up a withered forest in the summer, Kumbhakarna burnt that host of the monkeys.

sn: ततस्ते वध्यमानास्तु हतयूथाः प्लवंगमाः। वानरा भयसंविग्ना विनेदुर्विकृतैः स्वरैः॥
en: Thus beaten (by Kumbhakarna), those monkeys, with their ranks destroyed, the monkeys, racked with anxiety, began to cry in unnatural tones.

sn: अनेकशो वध्यमानाः कुम्भकर्णेन वानराः। राघवं शरणं जग्मुर्व्यथिता भित्रचेतसः॥
en: Having innumerable monkeys slain by Kumbhakarņa, the monkeys, aggrieved and their hearts riven with sorrow, sought the shelter of Raghava.

sn: प्रभग्नान्वानरान्दृष्ट्वा वज्रहस्तात्मजात्मजः। अभ्यधावत वेगेन कुम्भकर्ण महाहवे॥
en: Seeing the monkeys broken in the terrific encounter, the son of the thunder-handed, darted impetuously against Kumbhakarņa.

sn: शैलशृङ्ग महदृह्य विनदन्स मुहुर्मुहुः। त्रासयनराक्षसान्सर्वान्कुम्भकर्णपदानुगान्॥
en: Taking up a mighty crag, he momentarily setting up roars, and thereby terroizing all the Raksasas-followers of Kumbhakarma, he discharged the mountain-peak right against Kumbhakarma's crown.

sn: चिक्षेप शैलशिखरं कुम्भकर्णस्य मूर्धनि । स तेनाभिहतो मूर्ध्नि शैलेनेन्द्ररिपुस्तदा॥ कुम्भकर्णः प्रजज्वाल क्रोधेन महता तदा। सोऽभ्यधावत वेगेन वालिपुत्रममर्षणम्॥ कुम्भकर्णो महानादत्रासयन्सर्ववानरान्। शूलं ससर्ज वै रोषादङ्गदे तु महाबलः॥
en: And struck with that mountain-peak, Indra's enemy-Kumbhakarņa-flamed in fierce wrath. And the loud-throated Kumbhakarņa, terrifying all the monkeys vehemently darted against the enraged son of Vāli; and then that wondrous strong one hurled his dart at Angada.

sn: तदापतन्तं बलवान्युद्धमार्गविशारदः। लाघवान्मोक्षयामास बलवान्वानरर्षभः॥
en: As the dart descended, that foremost of monkeys endowed with strength. and skilled in battle, evaded the weapon from his fleetness.

sn: उत्पत्य चैनं तरसा तलेनोरस्यताडयत्। स तेनाभिहतः कोपात्प्रमुमोहाचलोपमः॥
en: up Then swiftly springing up, the slapped (his antagonist) in the chest. And thereat that one resembling a hill, lost his senses.

sn: स लब्धसंज्ञोऽतिबलो मुष्टिं संगृह्य राक्षसः। अपहासेन चिक्षेप विसंज्ञः स पपात ह॥
en: Recovering his senses, that exceedingly strong Räksasa, dealt a blow at Angada; and the latter dropped down senseless.

sn: तस्मिन्प्लवगशार्दूले विसंज्ञे पतिते भुवि। तच्छूलं समुपादाय सुग्रीवमभिदुद्रुवे॥
en: On that powerful monkey falling down insensible, Kumbhakarma, taking his dart, rushed against Sugriva.

sn: तमापतन्तं संप्रेक्ष्य कुम्भकर्ण महाबलम्। उत्पपात तदा वीरः सुग्रीवो वानराधिपः। ५१।। स पर्वताग्रमुत्क्षिप्य समाविध्य महाबलः। अभिदुद्राव वेगेन कुम्भकर्ण महाबलम्॥
en: Seeing the exceeding stout Kumbhakarņa approach, the heroic king of monkeys-Sugriva-sprang up; and taking a mountain-top that one possessed of great strength darted against the mighty Kumbhakarņa.

sn: तमापतन्तं संप्रेक्ष्य कुम्भकर्णः प्लवंगमम्। तस्थौ विवृत्तसर्वाङ्गो वानरेन्द्रस्य संमुखः। ५३।।
en: Seeing that monkey, Kumbhakarņa, stretching his limbs, stood before the lord of monkeys.

sn: कपिशोणितदिग्धाङ्ग भक्षयन्तं महाकपीन्। कुम्भकर्णं स्थितं दृष्ट्वा सुग्रीवो वाक्यमब्रवीत्।५४।।
en: Seeing Kumbhakarņa, with his body laved in the blood of monkeys; and eating up mighty monkeys, Sugriva addressed him, saying.

sn: पातिताश्च त्वया वीराः कृतं कर्म सुदुष्करम्। भक्षितानि च सैन्यानि प्राप्तं ते परमं यशः॥ त्यज तद्वानरानीकं प्राकृतैः किं करिष्यसि। सहस्वैकं निपातं मे पर्वतस्यास्य राक्षस।५६।।
en: You have felled heroes done deeds difficult of being performed, and have devoured the warriors; and you have thus attained renown. But let go now the monkey-army. What shall you do with the ignoble? Do you, O Raksasa bear the descent of this mountain.

sn: तद्वाक्यं हरिराजस्य सत्त्वधैर्यसमन्वितम्। श्रुत्वा राक्षसशार्दूलः कुम्भकर्णोऽब्रवीद्वचः॥
en: Hearing those words of the monkey-king instinct with strength and fortitude, that terrible Raksasa-Kumbhakarna-said.

sn: प्रजापतेस्तु पौत्रस्त्वं तथैवर्करजःसुतः। धृतिपौरुषसंपन्नस्तस्माद्र्जसि वानर॥
en: O monkey, you storm, because you are the grandson of Prajāpati and the son of the king of bears; and because as such you are endowed with fortitude and prowess.

sn: स कुम्भकर्णस्य वचो निशम्य व्याविध्य शैलं सहसा मुमोच। तेनाजघानोरसि कुम्भकर्ण शैलेन वज्राशनिसंनिभेन।५९॥
en: Hearing Kumbhakarna's speech, Sugrīva whirling that mountain-peak, suddeniy let it go; and with that rock resembling Vajra or the thunder-bolt, smote Kumbhakarņa in the chest.

sn: तच्छलशृङ्ग सहसा विभिन्न भुजान्तरे तस्य तदा विशाले। ततो विषेदुः सहसा प्लवंगा रक्षोगणाश्चापि मुदा विनेदुः॥
en: On coming in contact with his wide breast, that mountain-peak was at once shattered in shivers, And thereat the monkeys grew dispirited and the Raksas's ranks shouted in joy.

sn: स शैल शृङ्गाभिहतश्चुकोप ननाद रोषाच्च विवृत्य वक्रम्। व्याविध्य शूलं च तडित्प्रकाशं चिक्षेप हयृक्षपतेर्वधाय॥
en: And struck with the mountain-summit, Kumbhakarna was fired with wrath; and roared, expending his face. And then, whirling his dart resembling lightning displayed, he hurled it for compassing the destruction of the master of monkeys.

sn: तत्कुम्भकर्णस्य भुजप्रणुन्नं शूलं शितं काञ्चनदामयष्टिम्। क्षिप्रं समुत्पत्य निगृह्य दोभ्या बभञ्ज वेगेन सुतोऽनिलस्य॥
en: Then swiftly bounding up, the Wind-god's son, resisting that whetted dart fastened with golden chains, with his hands violently snapped it in twain.

sn: कृतं भारसहस्रस्य शूलं कालायसं महत्। बभञ्ज जानुमारोप्य तदा हृष्टः प्लवंगमः॥
en: And placing the same on his thighs, (Hanuman) snapped that ponderous and terrible dart composed of black iron, and thereat the monkeys waxed delighted.

sn: शूलं भग्नं हनुमता दृष्ट्वा वानरवाहिनी। हृष्टा ननाद बहुशः सर्वतश्चापि दुद्रुवे॥
en: Seeing the dart severed by Hanumān, the monkey-army, growing delighted, set up countless shouts and rushed in all directions.

sn: बभूवाथ परित्रस्तो राक्षसो विमुखोऽभवत्। सिंहनादं च ते चक्रुः प्रहृष्टा वनगोचराः।। मारुतिं पूजयांचक्रुर्दृष्ट्वा शूलं तथागतम्॥
en: The Rākşasa was seized with fear and turned away (from the field.) And the monkeys excessively delighted, set up loud shouts, and finding the dart broken, poured forth thanks to the Wind-god's son.

sn: स तत्तथा भग्नमवेक्ष्य शूलं चुकोप रक्षोधपतिर्महात्मा। उत्पाट्य लङ्कामलयात्सशृङ्ग जधान सुग्रीवमुपेत्य तेन।६६।।
en: Then the mighty-minded lord of Rákşasas seeing the dart thus severed, uprooted a peak from the Malaya and with it smote Sugrīva.

sn: स शैलशृङ्गाभिहतो विसंज्ञः पपात भूमौ युधि वानरेन्द्रः। तं वीक्ष्य भूमौ पतितं विसंज्ञं नेदुः प्रहृष्टा युधि यातुधानाः॥
en: The king of monkeys struck with the mountain-peak fell senseless upon the field, and the demons finding him in this plight shouted out in great joy.

sn: समभ्युपेत्याद्भुतघोरवीर्य स कुम्भकर्णो युधि वानरेन्द्रम्। जहार सुग्रीवमभिप्रगृह्य यथानिलो मेघमिव प्रचण्डः॥
en: Then Kumbhakarna coming to the wonderfully mighty master of monkeys, took him up and stole away from the field, as a violent gust of wind steal away a patch of cloud.

sn: स तं महामेधनिकाशरूपमुत्पाट्य गच्छन्युधि कुम्भकर्णः। रराज मेरुप्रतिमानरूपो मेरुर्यथा व्युच्छ्रितघोरशृङ्गः॥
en: Kumbhakarņa, who resembled a mountain in loftiness of stature, while taking him away like a mass of cloud appeared like Sumeru overtopped with lofty peaks.

sn: ततस्तमादाय जगाम वीरः संस्तूयमानो युधि राक्षसेन्द्रः। शृण्वन्निनादं त्रिदवालयानां प्लवंगराजग्रहविस्मितानाम्॥
en: Thus the lord of Rākşasas went on hearing thanks (from the Rākşasas) and shouts from the lords of the heavens, wondered at the capture of the foremost of monkeys.

sn: ततस्तमादाय तदा स मेने हरीन्द्रमिन्द्रोपममिन्द्रवीर्यः। अस्मिहन्ते सर्वमिदं हतं स्यात् सराघवं सैन्यमितीन्द्रशत्रुः॥
en: Thus taking him captive, that mighty one resembling Indra in puissance, thought his death would destroy the entire host of the opponents together with Rāghava.

sn: विद्वतां वाहिनीं दृष्ट्वा वानराणामितस्ततः। कुम्भकर्णेन सुग्रीवं गृहीतं चापि वानरम्॥ हनूमांश्चिन्तयामास मतिमान्मारुतात्मजः। एवं गृहीते सुग्रीवे किं कर्तव्यं मया भवेत्॥
en: Then Hanumān, the shrewd son of Maruta, finding the whole host of monkeys scattered in all directions, as well as Sugrīva captured by Kumbhakarņa bethought himself—“What ought to be done by me now that our king has been captured?

sn: यद्धि न्याय्यं मया कर्तुं तत्करिष्याम्यसंशयम्। भूत्वा पर्वतसंकाशो नाशयिष्यामि राक्षसम्।७४।।
en: I will doubtless do as befits me now let me assume the shape of a mountain and kill the Raksasas.

sn: मया हते संयति कुम्भकर्णे महाबले मुष्टिविशीर्णदेहे। विमोचिते वानरपार्थिवे च भवन्तु हृष्टाः प्लवगाः समग्राः॥
en: Let me kill the mighty Kumbhakarņa, splitting his body with my strong fist and thus relive the master of monkeys—thus let the whole host of monkeys become delighted.

sn: अथवा स्वयमप्येष मोक्षं प्राप्स्यति वानरः। गृहीतोऽयं यदि भवेत्रिदशैः सासुरोरगैः॥
en: Or, even when captured by the whole host of gods or Asuras or serpents he is mighty enough to extricate himself.

sn: मन्ये न तावदात्मानं बुध्यते वानराधिपः। शैलप्रहाराभिहतः कुम्भकर्णेन संयुगे॥
en: Meseems, the lord of monkeys struck with dart in battle by Kumbhakarna has not yet recovered his senses.

sn: अयं मुहूर्तात्सुग्रीवो लब्धसंज्ञो महाहवे। आत्मनो वानराणां च यत्पथ्यं तत्करिष्यति॥
en: Else in a moment he would do the needful for himself as well as the monkeys.

sn: मया तु मोक्षितस्यास्य सुग्रीवस्य महात्मनः। अप्रीतिश्च भवेत्कष्टा कीर्तिनाशश्च शाश्वतः॥ तस्मान्मुहूर्त काशिष्ये विक्रम मोक्षितस्य तु। भिन्नं च वानरानीकं तावदाश्वासयाम्यहम्॥
en: Should the relief of the mighty-minded Sugrīva come from me, I should be incurring his displeasure and it would certainly lead to the loss of his reputation for ever; then I must wait a moment and see his own mighty displayed by himself when relieved. Meanwhile let me cheer up the monkey-host.

sn: इत्येवं चिन्तयित्वाथ हनूमान्मारुतात्मजः। भूयः संस्तम्भयामास वानराणां महाचमूम्॥
en: Thinking thus within himself, Hanumăn, that son of Maruta, began to stay the mighty host of Monkeys.

sn: स कुम्भकर्णोऽथ विवेश लङ्कां स्फुरन्तमादाय महाहरिं तम्। विमानचर्यागृहगोपुरस्थैः पुष्पाग्र्यवरभिपूज्यमानः॥
en: In the meantime Kumbhakarņa entered Lankā with Sugrīva trembling, being honoured with the showering of beautiful flowers from the sky, the buildings on the main roads and the town-gate.

sn: लाजगन्धोदवर्षैस्तु सेव्यमानः शनैः शनैः। राजवीथ्यास्तु शीतत्वात्संज्ञां प्राप महाबलः।॥
en: Then the mighty one (Sugriva) slowly recovered his senses with the shower of fried paddy and sweet scent and the sprinkling of water as well as with the coolness of the streets.

sn: ततः स संज्ञामुपलभ्य कृच्छ्रद्वलीयसस्तस्य भुजान्तरस्थः। अवेक्षमाणः पुरराजमार्ग विचिन्तयामास मुहुर्महात्मा।८४।।
en: Then that mighty-minded (Sugriva), caught in the arms of the powerful Räksasa, having with difficulty come to his senses and surveying around him the streets of the town bethought himself.

sn: एवं गृहीतेन कथं नु नाम शक्यं मया संप्रति कर्तुमद्य। तथा करिष्यामि यथा हरीणां भविष्यतीष्टं च हितं च कार्यम्॥
en: When thus within the grasp of the enemy how can I take revenge? Or let me do what will be acceptable and advantageous to our army.

sn: ततः कराग्रैः सहसा समेत्य राजा हरीणाममरेन्द्रशत्रोः। खरैश्च कर्णौ दशनैश्च नासां ददंश पादैविददार पाचौँ ॥
en: Then advancing all on a sudden, he with his nails and sharp teeth cut off the ears and nose of that lord of the enemies of the gods and split both his sides with the blow of his feet.

sn: स कुम्भकर्णो हृतकर्णनासो विदारितस्तेन रदैनखैश्च। रोषाभिभूतः क्षतजार्द्रगावः सुग्रीवमाविध्य पिपेष भूमौ ॥
en: Kumbhakarņa losing his ears and nose and having his sides split with nails and teeth grew angry, and becoming all covered over with blood, threw Sugrīva to the ground and pressed him.

sn: स भूतले भीमबलाभिपिष्टः सुरारिभिस्तैरभिहन्यमानः। जगाम खं कन्दुकवज्जवेन पुनश्च रामेण समाजगाम।०८।।
en: Thus pressed upon the ground with main force and severely struck by the enemies of gods, he flew to the skies like a ball-rolling, and once morejoined Rāma.

sn: कर्णनासाविहीनस्तु कुम्भकर्णो महबालः। रराज शोणितोत्सितो गिरिः प्रस्रवणैरिव।॥
en: The mighty Kumbhakarna having lost his nose and ears and drenched in blood, appeared like a mountain covered all over with streamlets.

sn: शोणितानॊ महाकायो राक्षसो भीमदर्शनः। अमर्षाच्छोणितोद्गारी शुशुभे रावणानुजः॥ नीलाञ्जनचयप्रख्यः ससंध्य इव तोयदः। युद्धायाभिमुखो भीमो मनश्चके निशाचरः॥
en: That huge-bodied Rākşasa, younger brother of Ravana, terrible in appearance, resembling a mass of deep black collyrium, and covered all over with blood, appeared like an evening cloud; and (once more) made up his mind to appear in battle.

sn: गते च तमिन्सुरराजशत्रुः क्रोधात्प्रदुद्राव रणाय भूयः। अनायुधोऽस्मीति विचिन्त्य रौद्रो घोरं तदा मुद्गरमाससाद॥
en: Sugrīva having thus escaped, that dreadful enemy of the king of the celestials in wrath again rushed to battle; and finding himself destitute of arms took up a fearful mace.

sn: ततः सपुर्याः सहसा महात्मा निष्क्रम्य तद्वानरसैन्यमुग्रम्। बभक्ष रक्षो युधि कुम्भकर्णः प्रजा युगान्ताग्निरिव प्रवृद्धः।९३॥
en: Then that mighty-minded one, the Raksasa Kumbhakarņa, issuing out of the city began to devour the terrific host of monkeys, as do the mighty fire eat up people at the end of a Yuga.

sn: बुभुक्षितः शोणितमांसगृध्नुः प्रविश्य तद्वानरसैन्यमुग्रम्। चखाद रक्षांसि हरॆन्पिशाचान्नृक्षांश्च मोहाधुधि कुम्भकर्णः।। यथैव मृत्युहरते युगान्ते स भक्षयामास हरीश्च मुख्यान्॥
en: On entering the mighty host of monkeys, the hungry Kumbhakarna, hankering after flesh and blood, ate up the monkeys and with them, devoured many a Rākşasa and Piśāca by, mistake. Thus, as Death devour creatures at the end of a Yuga, he destroyed the mighty monkeys.

sn: एकं द्वौ बीन्बहून्क्रुद्धो वानरान्सह राक्षसैः। समादायैकहस्तेन प्रचिक्षेप त्वरन्मुखे॥
en: He in wrath, taking up with one hand the monkeys along with the Rākṣasa, hurriedly threw them into his mouth, one, two three, or many at a time.

sn: संप्रस्रवत्तदा मेदः शोणिते च महाबलः। वध्यमानो नगेन्द्रागैर्भक्षयामास वानरान् ॥
en: And blood and fat flowed copiously down his body; and though struck by the monkeys with peaks of mountains, the mighty one devoured all those monkeys.

sn: ते भक्ष्यमाणा हरयो रामं जग्मुस्तदा गतिम्। कुम्भकर्णो भृशं क्रुद्धः कपीन्खादन्प्रधावति॥ शतानि सप्त चाष्टौ च विंशत्रिंशतथैव च। संपरिष्वज्य बाहुभ्यां खादन्विपरिधावति ॥
en: The monkeys as they were being devoured, saught the shelter of Rāma. And Kumbhakarna wrought up with wrath, chased a main hundreds of monkeys, eating up seven, eight, twenty, or thirty. And fastening (the monkeys) with his arms, he, devouring them, rushed on.

sn: मेदोवसाशोणितदिग्धगात्रः कर्णावसक्तग्रथितान्त्रमालः। ववर्ष शूलानि सुतीक्ष्णदंष्ट्रः कलो युगान्तस्थ इव प्रवृद्ध ।१९।।
en: Resembling the Destroyer of prodigious dimensions at the end of a Yuga, that one furnished with extremely sharp teeth, having his body covered with far, marrow ind blood, and coiling entrails about his ears, began to discharge darts.

sn: तस्मिन्काले सुमित्रायाः पुत्रः परबलार्दनः। चकार लक्ष्मणः क्रुद्धो युद्धं परपुरंजयः॥
en: At this moment, that subduer of hostile hosts and captor of the capitals of foes-Sumitra's son-Laksmana, growing enraged, entered on an encounter with the enemy.

sn: स कुम्भकर्णस्य शरान्शरीरे सप्त वीर्यवान्। निचखानाददे चान्यान्विससर्ज च लक्ष्मणः॥
en: Lakşamna endued with prowess shot seven shafts at Kumbhakarma's body; and next, taking up other arrows also discharged them (at his antagonist).

sn: पीड्यमानस्तदत्रं विशेषं तत्स राक्षसः। ततश्चुकोप बलवान् सुमित्रानन्दवर्धनः॥
en: Thereat that Rākṣasa, smarting under the wounds inflicted by that weapon cut it off (by means of a weapon). Thereupon grew enraged the powerful Lakşmaņa-enhancer of Sumitrā's joy.

sn: अथास्य कवचं शुभ्रं जाम्बूनदमयं शुभम्। प्रच्छादयामास शरैः संध्याभ्रमिव मारुतः॥
en: Then as the wind overspread evening clouds, he with his shafts covered his shining and graceful mail entirely made of gold.

sn: नीलाञ्जनचयप्रख्यः शरैः काञ्चनभूषणैः। अपीड्यमानः शुशुभे मेघैः सूर्य इवांशुमान्॥
en: And smite with arrows dight with gold, that one resembling a mass of dark-blue collyrium appeared beautiful like the ray-furnished Sun surrounded by clouds.

sn: ततः स राक्षसो भीमः सुमित्रानन्दवर्धनम्। सावज्ञमेव प्रोवाच वाक्यं मेघौघनिःस्वनः॥
en: Then that dreadful Rākṣasa voiced like masses of clouds, scornfully addressed the enhancer of Sumitra's felicity, saying.

sn: अन्तकस्याप्यकष्टेन युधि जेतारमाहवे। युध्यता मामभीतेन ख्यापिता वीरता त्वया॥
en: By dauntlessly fighting with me, who have without ado brought down the Destroyer himself in battle, you have established you heroism.

sn: प्रगृहीतायुधस्येह मृत्योरिव महामृधे। तिष्ठन्नप्यग्रतः पूज्यः किमु युद्धप्रदायकः॥
en: Even by staying before me, who am equipped with arms in this encounter, and who in mighty conflict resemble Death himself, you deserve to be honoured. What shall I say of you fighting?

sn: ऐरावतं समारूढो वृतः सर्वामरैः प्रभुः। नैव शक्रोऽपि समरे स्थितपूर्वः कदाचन॥
en: Not even that lord-Sakra himself-mounted on his Airāvata, and engirt by all the immortals, had ever before stayed before me in the field.

sn: अद्य त्वयाहं सौमित्रे बालेनापि पराक्रमैः। तोषितो गन्तुमिच्छामि त्वामनुज्ञाप्य राघवम्॥
en: But today, O Sumitra's son, albeit a boy, you have gratified me with you prowess. Now taking your leave, I wish to go to Rāghava.

sn: यत्तु वीर्यबलोत्साहैस्तोषितोऽहं रणे त्वया। राममेवैकमिच्छामि हन्तुं यस्मिन्हते हतम्॥
en: As I have been well pleased in battle with your vigour and strength and enthusiasm, I now wish to slay Rāma alone, who being slain, all are slain.

sn: रामे मयात्र निहते येऽन्ये स्थास्यन्ति संयुगे। तानहं योधयिष्यामि स्वबलेन प्रमाथिना॥
en: On Rāma being here slain by me, the rest remaining in the encounter-them shall I undertake with my all-crushing vigour.

sn: इत्युक्तवाक्यं तद्रक्षः प्रोवाच स्तुतिसंहितम्। मृधे घोरतरं वाक्यं सौमित्रिः प्रहसन्निव॥
en: When that Rākşasa had spoken thus, (Lakş mana). Sumitrā's son, present in that contest, answered him laughing in terrible words, saying.

sn: यस्त्वं शक्रादिभिर्देवैरसह्यः प्राप्य पौरुषम्। तत्सत्यं नान्यथा वीर दृष्टस्तेऽद्य पराक्रमः॥ एष दाशरथी रामस्तिष्ठत्यद्रिरिवाचलः।
en: That your prowess is incapable of being borne by Sakra and other celestials-is true. It is not otherwise, O hero. To-day I myself have witnessed your prowess. Yonder is Dasaratha's son Rāma, staying like a moveless mountain.

sn: इति श्रुत्वा ह्यनादृत्य लक्ष्मणं स निशाचरः॥ अतिक्रम्य च सौमित्रिं कुम्भकर्णो महाबलः। राममेवाभिदुद्राव कम्पयन्निव मेदिनीम्॥
en: Hearing this, that night-ranger Kumbhakarna, possessed of immense might, disregarding Laks maņa and passing beyond Sumitrā's son, rushed against Rāma, making the earth tremble.

sn: अथ दाशरथी रामो रौद्रमस्त्रं प्रयोजयन्। कुम्भकर्णस्य हृदये ससर्ज निशिताशरान् ॥
en: Thereat Dasaratha's son, Rāma, employing a terrific weapon, discharged sharpened shafts at Kumbhakarņa's breast.

sn: तस्य रामेण विद्वस्य सहसाभिप्रधावतः। अङ्गारमिश्राः क्रुद्धस्य मुखात्रिश्चेरुरर्चिषः॥
en: Thereat flames mixed with live embers shot out from the mouth of that enraged one suddenly rushing (against Răma), as Rama pierced him (with his arrows).

sn: रामास्त्रविद्धो घोरं वै नर्दन्राक्षसपुङ्गवः। अभ्यधावत तं क्रुद्धो हरीन्विद्रावयन्रणे॥
en: On being frightfully pierced by Rāma's weapons, that foremost of Rākşasas roaring wrathfully darted against Rāma, and pursued the monkeys in the conflict.

sn: तस्योरसि निमग्नास्ते शरा बहिणवाससः। हस्ताच्चास्य परिभ्रष्टा गदा चोव्या पपात ह ॥ आयुधानि च सर्वाणि विप्रकीर्यन्त भूतले। स निरायुधमात्मानं यदा मेने महाबलः॥ मुष्टिभ्यां च कराभ्यां च चकार कदनं महत्।
en: Those shafts adorned with peacock's plumes, alighting on (Kumbhakarna's) chest, his mace, escaping his hand, dropped to the earth; and all his (other) arms also were scattered on the ground. And when that exceedingly powerful one saw himself deprived of all his arms, he began to spread a huge havoc by means of his clenched fists and hands.

sn: स बाणैरतिविद्धाङ्गः क्षतजेन समुक्षितः।। रुधिरं परिसुस्राव गिरिः प्रस्रवणं यथा॥
en: With his body entirely covered with arrows and bathed in blood, he began to bleed like a hill overflowing with fountains.

sn: स तीव्रेण च कोपेन रुधिरेण च मूर्च्छितः। वानरान्राक्षसानृक्षान्खादन्स परिधावति॥
en: And fired with wrath and maddened with blood, he rushed on, devouring monkeys and Rākşasas and bears.

sn: अथ शृङ्ग समाविध्य भीमं भीमपराक्रमः। चिक्षेप राममुद्दिश्य बलवानन्तकोपमः॥
en: That redoubtable one possessed of dreadful prowess, resembling the Reaper himself, whirling a mighty mountain-peak, hurled it aiming at Rāma.

sn: अप्राप्तमन्तरा रामः सप्तभिस्तमजिह्मगैः। चिच्छेद गिरिशृङ्गं तं पुनः संधाय कार्मुकम्॥ ततस्तु रामो धर्मात्मा तस्य शृङ्ग महत्तदा। शरैः काञ्चनचित्राङ्गैश्चिच्छेद भरताग्रजः॥ तन्मेरुशिखराकारै?तमानमिव श्रिया। द्वे शते वानराणां च पतमानमपातयत्॥
en: Thereat Bharata's elder brother, the righteous Rāma, ere that prodigious peak had alighted, severed the same by means of seven straightspeeding shafts wrought with gold. Then that crag, like a peak of mountain Meru and shining with its radiance, falling on the earth knocked down two hundred monkeys too.

sn: तस्मिन्काले स धर्मात्मा लक्ष्मणो राममब्रवीत्। कुम्भकर्णवधे युक्तो योगान्परिमृशन्बहून्॥
en: Intent on finishing Kumbhakarņa, the virtuous Laksmana, revolving many a means, (at last) spoke to Rāma.

sn: नैवायं वानरान्राजन्न विजानाति राक्षसान्। मत्तः शोणितगन्धेन स्वान्परांश्चैव खादते॥
en: O king, this one know not monkeys and Rākşasas, maddened with the smell of blood, he eat up his own as well as his enemies.

sn: साध्वेनमधिरोहन्तु सर्वतो वानरर्षभाः। यूथपाश्च यथा मुख्यास्तिष्ठन्त्वस्मिन्समन्ततः॥
en: Now let the foremost monkeys, putting forth their best mount on him; and let the leaders of bands according to their rank, stand surrounding him.

sn: अद्यायं दुर्मतिः काले गुरुभारप्रपीडितः। प्रचरराक्षसो भूमौ नान्यान्हन्यात्प्लवंगमान् ॥
en: Then today this wicked-minded Rākşasa, oppressed with a mighty weight, will no longer be able to eat up any more monkeys.

sn: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा वजपुत्रस्य धीमतः। ते समारुरुहुहृष्टाः कुम्भकर्ण महाबलाः॥
en: Hearing the words of the intelligent prince, those exceedingly powerful monkeys with alacrity ascended Kumbhakarņa.

sn: कुम्भकर्णस्तु संक्रुद्धः समारूढाः प्लवंगमैः। व्यधूनयत्तान्वेगेन दुष्टहस्तीव हस्तिपान्॥
en: Kumbhakarna mounted by those monkeys, waxing exceedingly enraged, shook them vehemently, even as mad elephants shake the drivers thereof,

sn: तान्दृष्ट्वा निधुतान्रामो रुष्टोऽयमिति राक्षसम्। समुत्पपात वेगेन धनुरुत्तममाददे॥
en: Rāghava seeing them shaken, and concluding the Rāksasa to be wroth, furiously sprang forward, taking his bow.

sn: क्रोधरक्तेक्षणो धीरो निर्दहन्निव चक्षुषा। राघवो राक्षसं वेगादभिदुद्राव वेगितः।। यूथपान्हर्षयन्सर्वान्कुम्भकर्णबलार्दितान्॥
en: With his eyes crimsoned with choler, the gentle Rāghava, as if burning up the Räkşasa with his eyes, rushed forth vehemently, summoning up all his impetuosity, thereby cheering up the leaders of bands that had been sore tried by the might of Kumbhakarma.

sn: स चापमादाय भुजंगकल्पं दृढज्यमुग्रं तपनीयचित्रम्। हरीन्समाश्वास्य समुत्पपात रामो निबद्धोत्तमतूणबाणः॥
en: And equipped with an excellent quiver and arrows, Rāma checring up the monkeys sprang forward, taking a bow, resembling a serpent; terrific; having a stout string; and embellished in gold.

sn: स वानरगणैस्तैस्तु वृतः परमदुर्जयैः। लक्ष्मणानुचरो वीरः संप्रतस्थे महाबलः॥
en: Then surrounded by exceedingly invincible monkey-bands, that highly powerful hero, followed by Laksmana, marched forth.

sn: स ददर्श महात्मानं किरीटिनमरिंदमम्। शोणितावृतरक्ताक्षं कुम्भकर्ण महाबलः॥ सर्वान्समभिधावन्तं यथारुष्टं दिशागजम्। मार्गमाणं हरीन्क्रुद्धं राक्षसैः परिवारितम्॥ विन्ध्यमन्दरसंकाशं काञ्चनाङ्गदभूषणम्। स्रवन्तं रुधिरं वक्त्राद्वर्ष मेघमिवोत्थितम्॥ जिह्वया परिलिह्यन्तं सृक्किणी शोणितोक्षिते। मृद्गन्तं वानरानीकं कालान्तकयमोपमम्॥
en: He saw the redoubtable and high-souled Kumbhakarņa, with his body drenched in blood, and with blood-shot eyes; rushing against all, like to an infuriated elephant of the cardinal points; pursuing the monkeys; wrought up with wrath; environed by Rakşasas; appearing like the Vindhya or the Mandara; decked with golden angadas; bleeding from his mouth; like clouds pouring showers; licking at the corners of his mouth laved with blood; smashing the monkeyranks; and resembling Yama the Destroyer.

sn: तं दृष्ट्वा राक्षसश्रेष्ठं प्रदीप्तांनलवर्चसम्। विस्फारयामास तदा कार्मुकं पुरुषर्षभः॥
en: That best of persons, seeing that foremost of Rākṣasas having the splendour of a living fire, stretched his bow to its full bent.

sn: स तस्य चापनि?षात्कुपितो राक्षसर्षभः। अमृष्यमाणस्तं घोषमभिदुद्राव राघवम् ॥
en: And fired with wrath at the twang of his bow, that foremost of Raksasas, inflamed with wrath, not brooking that report, rushed against Rāghava.

sn: ततस्तु धारोद्धतमेघकल्पं भुजंगराजोत्तमभोगबाहुः। तमापतन्तं धरणीधाराभमुवाच रामो युधि कुम्भकर्णम्॥
en: Thereat, the gentle Rāma, endowed with arms resembling the body of the sovereign of serpents, in that encounter addressed Kumbhakarņa, like to an elevated cloud and possessed of the splendour of a mountain, as he darted forward, saying.

sn: मवस्थितोऽहं प्रगृहीतचापः। अवेहि मां राक्षसवंशनाशनं यस्त्वं मुहूर्ताद्भविता विचेताः॥
en: Come, O king of Rākşasa! Let no grief be your! Here I stay, taking my bow in my hand. Know me for the destroyer of the race of the Rākṣasas—you who in a moment shall be deprived of your senses.

sn: रामोऽयमिति विज्ञाय जहास विकृतस्वनम्। अभ्यधावत संक्रुद्धो हरीन्विद्रावयरणे॥
en: Kowing that this was Rāma, (Kumbhakarņa) laughed in frightful accents; and then, wrought up with wrath, rushed against the monkeys in the encounter.

sn: दारयन्निव सर्वेषां हृदयानि वनौकसाम्। प्रहस्य विकृतं भीमं स मेघस्तनितोपमम्॥ कुम्भकर्णो महातेजा राघवं वाक्यमब्रवीत्। नाहं विराधो विज्ञेयो न कबन्धः खरो न च। न वाली न च मारीचः कुम्भकर्णः समागतः॥
en: As if riving the breasts of all the monkeys (present) the exceedingly energetic Kumbhakarņa, laughing frightfully and in a terrific manner, resembling the rumbling of clouds, addressed Rāghava, saying, “Take me not for Virādha, or for Kabandha, or yet for Khara. I am not Vāli or Mārīca. I am Kumbhakarma, that am come.

sn: पश्य मे मुद्गरं भीमं सर्वं कालायसं महत्। अनेन निर्जिता देवा दानवाश्च पुरा मया॥
en: Behold my dreadful and mighty mace entirely made of iron. By help of this I had formerly brought down deities and Dänavas.

sn: विकर्णनास इति मां नावज्ञातुं त्वमर्हसि। स्वल्पापि हि न मे पीडा कर्णनासाविनाशनात् ॥
en: It does not behove you to scorn me in that my nose has been severed. I do not feel any the smallest torment in consequence of my ears and nose having been cut off.

sn: दर्शयेक्ष्वाकुशार्दूल वीर्य गात्रेषु मेऽनघ। ततस्त्वां भक्षयिष्यामि दृष्टपौरुषविक्रमम्॥
en: O tiger of the Ikşvāku line, O sinless one, do you witness the prowess that is in my frame. And thereafter, when you shall have displayed your prowess and power, shall I devour you up.

sn: स कुम्भकर्णस्य वचो निशम्य रामः सपङ्खान्विससर्ज बाणान्। तैराहतो वज्रसमप्रवेगैर्न चुक्षुभे न व्यथते सुरारिः॥
en: Hearing Kumbhakarna's words, Rama discharged (at him) shafts furnished with knobs. And smite with these having the impetus of the thunder-bolt, the foe of the celestials did not feel any pain or sinart.

sn: यैः सायकैः सालवरा निकृत्ता बाली हतो वानरपुङ्गवश्च। ते कुम्भकर्णस्य तदा शरीरं वज्रोपमानं व्यथयांप्रचक्रुः॥
en: Those shafts which had severed the seven stately salas, and, to boot, had slain Vāli—best of monkeys, they resembling the thunder itselfcould not impart any pain to Kumbhakarņa's body.

sn: स वारिधारा इव सायकांस्तान् पिबशरीरेण महेन्द्रशत्रुः। जघान रामस्य शरप्रवेगं व्यविध्य तं मुद्गरमुग्रवेगम्॥
en: Drinking up in his body those arrows resembling a shower, the enemy of the great Indra whirling his mace possessed of fierce ventinence, put out the arrowy discharge of Rāma.

sn: ततस्तु रक्षः क्षतजावलिप्तं वित्रासनं देवमहाचमूनाम्। व्याविध्य तं मुद्गरमुग्रवेगं विद्रावयामास चमूं हरीणाम्॥
en: Then that Rākşasa whirling his mace washed in blood, capable of striking terror into the mighty hosts of gods and Dānavas, and possessed of fierce impetus, made the monkeyarmy take to its heels.

sn: वायव्यमादाय ततोऽपरास्त्रं रामः प्रचिक्षेप निशाचराय। समुद्गरं तेन जहार बाहुं •सकृत्तबाहुस्तुमुलं ननाद॥
en: Then Rāma, taking a trighty Vāyavya weapon, used the same against the night-ranger; and cut off his arm with the mace. And having his arm cut off, he set up tremendousrears.

sn: स तस्य बाहुर्गिरिशृङ्गकल्पः समुद्रो राघवबाणकृत्तः। पपात तस्मिन्हरिराजसैन्ये जघान तां वानरवाहिनीं च॥
en: And his arm with the mace, resembling a mountain-peak, cut off by Rāghava's arrows, fell in the midst of the army of the monkey-king, and destroyed that army,* * This, or course, is not to be taken literally.

sn: ते वानरा भग्नहतावशेषाः पर्यन्तमाश्रित्य तदा विषण्णाः। प्रपीडिताङ्गा ददृशुः सुघोरं नरेन्द्ररक्षोधिपसंनिपातम्॥
en: Thereat the monkeys remaining after those broken and slain, dispirited, and having their limbs wounded, moving aside, looked on the dreadfiil encounter between the Rākşasa and the lord of men.

sn: स कुम्भकर्णोस्त्रनिकृत्तबाहुर्महासिकृचान इवाचलेन्द्रः। उत्पादयामास करेण वृक्षं ततोऽभिदुद्राव रणे नरेन्द्रम्॥
en: Then Kumbhakarma, having his arm severed, resembling the foremost of mountains with its crest hewn away by a mighty sabre, tore up a tree with his (remaining) arm and in the conflict rushed against the monarch of men.

sn: तं तस्य बाहुं सहतालवृक्षं समुद्यतं पन्नगभोगकल्पम्। ऐन्द्रास्त्रयुक्तेन जघान रामो बाणेन जाम्बूनदचित्रितेन ॥
en: Thereupon with a shaft plated in gold, set upon a weapon of Indra, Rāma cut off his uplifted arm with a palm tree, looking like the body of a pannaga.

sn: स कुम्भकर्णस्य भुजो निकृत्तः पपात भूमौ गिरिसंनिकाशः। विचेष्टमानो निजदान व्रुक्षान्शैलाशिलावानरराक्षसांश्च ॥
en: That arm of Kumbhakarma, being severed, dropped inert on the earth, like a hill, and crushed trees and rocks and crags and monkeys and Raksasas.

sn: तं छिन्नबाहुं समवेक्ष्य रामः समापतन्तं सहसा नदन्तम्। द्वावर्धचन्द्रौ निशितौ प्रगृह्य चिच्छेद पादौ युधि राक्षसस्य॥
en: Rāma, seeing that one shorn of his arms suddenly spring up, roaring, took up two whetted crescents, and in the contest cut off the legs of the Rākşasa.

sn: तौ तस्य पादौ प्रदिशो दिशश्च गिरेगुहाश्चैव महार्णवं च। लङ्कां च सेनां कपिराक्षसानां विनादयन्तौ विनिपेततुश्च ॥
en: Thereupon those legs (of his), making all sides and quarters and rocks and caves and the mighty main and Lankā herself and the army of the monkeys and the Rākşasas, resound, dropped down (on the ground).

sn: निकृत्तबाहुर्विनिकृत्तपादो विदार्य वक्रं वडवामुखाभम्। दुद्राव रामं सहसाभिगर्जन् राहुर्यथा चन्द्रमिवान्तरिक्षे॥
en: Having his arms cut off and his legs also severed, (Kumbhakarma), opening wide his mouth resembling in sheen the mouth of a mare, roaring swiftly darted against Rāghava, even as Rāhu pursue the Moon in the firmament.

sn: अपूरयत्तस्य मुखं शिताङ्ग रामः शरैर्हेमपिनद्धपुखैः। संपूर्णवक्त्रो न शशाक वक्तुं चुकूज कृच्छ्रेण मुमूर्छ चापि॥
en: Then Rama stuffed his mouth full of sharpened shafts having their feathered parts furnished with gold. And having his mouth filled, he could not articulate; but with extreme effort uttered indistinct accents and swooned away.

sn: अथाददे सूर्यमरीचिकल्पं सब्रह्मदण्डान्तककालकल्पम्। अरिष्टमैन्द्र निशितं सुपुङ्खं रामः शरं मारुततुल्यवेगम्॥ तं वज्रजाम्बूनदचारुपुङ्ख प्रदीप्तसूर्यज्वलनप्रकाशम्। महेन्द्रवज्राशनितुल्यवेगं रामः प्रचिक्षेप निशाचराय।।
en: Then Rāma took an arrow of Indra, whetted and knobbed, impetuous as the wind, resembling the effulgence of the Sun, and like to the very banner of Brahmā, or the destroyer himself; and fatal to foes. And then Rāma hurled it at the ranger of the night.

sn: स सायको राघवबाहुचोदितो दिशः स्वभासा दश संप्रकाशयन्। विधूमवैश्वानरभीमदर्शनो जगाम शक्राशनिभीमविक्रमम्॥
en: Thereat that weapon hurled by Rāma's arm, resembling a smokeless flame, lighting up the ten cardinal points with its own glory, saught him that was possessed of the dreadful energy of Sakra's thunder-bolt.

sn: स तन्महापर्वतकूटसंनिभं सुवृत्तदंष्ट्र चलचारुकुण्डलम्। चकर्त रक्षोधिपतेः शिरस्तदा यथैव वृत्रस्य पुरा पुरंदरः॥
en: Therewith he (Rāma) cut off the head of the lord of Räkşasa resembling a mountain-summit, furnished with prominent teeth, from which the ear-rings had fallen off, even as formerly Purandara had cut off the head of Vſtra.

sn: कुम्भकर्णशिरो भाति कुण्डलालंकृतं महत्। आदित्येऽभ्युदिते रात्रौ मध्यस्थ इव चन्द्रमाः॥
en: Then Kumbhakarņa's huge head deprived of the ear-rings appeared like the Moon seated in the midst of the heavens) on the rising of the Sun in the morning.* *This Sloka is wanting in many texts.

sn: तद्रामबाणाभिहतं पपात रक्ष:शिरः पर्वतसन्निकाशम्। बभञ्ज चर्यागृहगोपुराणि प्राकारमुच्वं तमपातयच्च ॥
en: And struck with Rāma's arrow, the head of the Rākşasa resembling a hill fell down to the earth; and (in its fall) crushed edifices on the highways and gateways; and elevated walls also it bore down to the ground.

sn: तच्चातिकायं हि महत्प्रकाशं रक्षस्तदा तोयनिधौ पपात। ग्राहान्परान्मीनवरान्भुजंगमान् ममर्द भूमिं च तथा विवेश ॥
en: Then that Rākşasa of gigantic proportions and vast to the view plunged into the deep; and crushing huge and mighty fishes and serpents, saught the depths.

sn: तस्मिन्हते ब्राह्मणदेवशत्रौ महाबले संयति कुम्भकर्णे। चचाल भूर्भूमिधराश्च सर्वे हर्षाच्च देवास्स्तुमुलं प्रणेदुः॥
en: On that enemy of the Brāhmanas and gods, endowed with immense strength, having been slain in battle, the earth shook and the mountains also; and from excess of joy the celestials shouted aloud.

sn: ततस्तु देवर्षिमहर्षिपन्नगाः सुराश्च भूतानि सुपर्णगुह्यकाः। सयक्षगन्धर्वगणा नभोगताः प्रहर्षिता रामपराक्रमेण ॥
en: Those deities and saints and Maharsis and Pannagas, and celestials and (other), beings and birds and Guhyakas, together with Yakşas and Gandharvas, all these who had stationed themselves in the welkin, were rejoiced at the prowess of Rama.

sn: ततस्तु ते तस्य वधेन भूरिणा मनस्विनो नैर्ऋतराजबान्धवाः। विनेदुरुच्चैर्व्यथिता रघूत्तमं हरिं समीक्ष्यैव यथा मतंगजाः॥
en: At his (Kumbhakarna's) great destruction, the intelligent adherents of the king of Nairtas, aggrieved exceedingly, began to cry at the sight of that best of the Raghus, even as mad elephants cry at sight of a lion.

sn: स देवलोकस्य तमो निहत्य सूर्यो यथा राहुमुखाद्विमुक्तः। तथा व्याभासीद्धरिसैन्यमध्ये निहत्य रामो युधि कुम्भकर्णम्॥
en: Like to the Sun emerged from the mouth of Rāhu, and destroying the darkness of the celestial fields, shone Rāma in the midst of the monkey-army having slain Kumbhakarņa in battle.

sn: प्रहर्षमीयुर्बहवश्च वानराः प्रबुद्धपद्मप्रतिमैरिवाननैः। अपूजयराघवमिष्टभागिनं हते रिपौ भीमबले नृपात्मजम्॥
en: And countless monkeys experienced the very height of delight; and on (their) foe of terrific strength having been slain, they with countenances resembling awaked lotuses paid homage to the king's son-Rāghava—the sharer of good fortune.

sn: स कुम्भकर्णं सुरसैन्यमर्दनं महत्सु युद्धेषु कदाचनाजितम्। ननन्द हत्वा भरताग्रजो रणे महासुरं वृत्रमिवामराधिपः॥
en: As the monarch of the immortals had rejoiced on slaying the mighty Asura Vrtra-Bharata's elder brother rejoiced on having in battle slain that smiter of celestial hosts, Kumbhakarna in mighty conflict, never (before) vanquished in renowned encounters.

sn: कुम्भकर्णं हतं दृष्ट्वा राघवेण महात्मना। राक्षसा राक्षसेन्द्राय रावणाय न्यवेदयन्॥
en: Seeing Kumbhakarņa slain by the high-souled Rāghava, the Räkşasas conveyed the tidings to the lord of the Raksasas-Ravana; (and addressed him, saying)

sn: राजन्स कालसंकाशः संयुक्तः कालकर्मणा। विद्राव्य वानरों सेनां भक्षयित्वा च वानरान्॥ प्रतपित्वा मुहूर्तं तु प्रशान्तो रामतेजसा। कायेनार्धप्रविष्टेन समुद्रं भीमदर्शनम्॥ निकृत्तनासाकर्णेन विक्षरदुधिरेण च। रुद्ध्वा द्वारं शरीरेण लङ्कायाः पर्वतोपमः॥ कुम्भकर्णस्तव भ्राता काकुत्स्थशरपीडितः। अगण्डभूतो विवृतो दावदग्ध इव दुमः॥
en: O king, that one resembling the destroyer himself, urged on by death, having scoured the monkey-army and eaten up monkeys, and for a while displayed his prowess, has met with his quietus at the hands of Rāma exerting his energy. And with half his body immersed in the dreadful deep, your brother, Kumbhakarņa, with his nose and ears cut off, and blood besmearing his body, with his head and limbs hewn away, and his body uncovered, mountain-like block up the gate of Laňkă with his person-and resemble a tree that has been consumed by a forest-fire.

sn: श्रुत्वा विनिहतं संख्ये कुम्भकर्ण महाबलम्। रावणः शोकसंतप्तो मुमोह च पपात च॥
en: Hearing the mighty Kumbhakarņa slain in battle, Ravana burning in grief, swooned away and dropped to the earth.

sn: पितृव्यं निहतं श्रुत्वा देवान्तकनरान्तकौ। त्रिशिराश्चातिकायश्च रुरुदुः शोकपीडिताः॥
en: Hearing their uncle slain, Trisiras* and Atikāya-destroyers of gods and men, began to weep, oppressed with sorrow. *Three-headed.

sn: भ्रातरं निहतं श्रुत्वा रामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा। महोदरमहापाचौं शोकाक्रान्तौ बभूवतुः॥
en: Mahodara' and Mahāpārśvahearing of their uncle slain by Rāma of untiring deeds, were overcome with grief. 1. Huge-bellied. 2. Mighty flanked.

sn: ततः कृच्छत्समासाद्य संज्ञां राक्षसपुङ्गवः। कुम्भकर्णवधाद्दीनो विललापाकुलेन्द्रियः॥
en: Then regaining his senses with extreme exertion, that foremost of Rākṣasas, distressed in consequence of the destruction of Kumbhakarna, mourned with his senses overwhelmed, saying.

sn: हा वीर रिपुदर्पघ्न कुम्भकर्ण महाबल। त्वं मां विहाय वै दैवाद्यातोऽसि यमसादनम्॥
en: O hero! O humbler of the pride of the foe! O mighty Kumbhakarna! Leaving me, you through stiny, have gone to the abode of Yama.

sn: मम शल्यमनुद्धृत्य बान्धवानां महाबल। शत्रुसैन्यं प्रताप्यैकः क्व मां संत्यज्य गच्छसि॥
en: O exceedingly powerful one, leaving me (alone) whither did you wend, without extracting my dart as well as that of your friends?

sn: इदानीं खल्वहं नास्मि यस्य मे पतितो भुजः। दक्षिणोऽयं समाश्रित्य न बिभेमि सुरासुरात्॥
en: Now really I am not, inasmuch as my right arm has dropped. Backed by this one, I would not fear celestials and Asuras.

sn: कथमेवंविधो वीरो देवदानवदर्पहा। कालाग्निप्रतिमो ह्यद्य राघवेण रणे हतः॥
en: How today forsooth has such a hero-crusher of the hauteur of gods and Dänavas—resembling the fire arisen at the hour of universal wreck, been slain in fight by Raghava?

sn: यस्य ते वज्रनिष्पेषो न कुर्याद्व्यसनं सदा। स कथं रामबाणातः प्रसुप्तोऽसि महीतले॥
en: He who could not be harmed by the concussion of the thunder-bolt itself-how can he, smitten with Rāma's arrows, sleep soundly on the earth?

sn: एते देवगणाः सार्धमृषिभिर्गगने स्थिताः। निहतं त्वां रणे दृष्ट्वा निनदन्ति प्रहर्षिताः॥
en: These gods stationed in the sky along with the saints, beholding you slain the battle, are shouting in glee.

sn: ध्रुवमद्यैव संहृष्टा लब्धलक्षाः प्लवंगमाः। आरोक्ष्यन्तीह दुर्गाणि लङ्काद्वाराणि सर्वशः॥
en: Surely today the monkeys overjoyed, finding occasion, well scale all the gateways and fortifications of Lankā.

sn: राज्येन नास्ति मे कार्य किं करिष्यामि सीतया। कुम्भकर्णविहीनस्य जीविते नास्ति मे मतिः॥
en: I have nothing to do with empire. And what shall I do with Sītā? And deprived of Kumbhakarma, I do not even wish to live.

sn: यद्यहं भ्रातृहन्तारं न हन्मि युधि राघवम्। ननु मे मरणं श्रेयो न चेदं व्यर्थजीवितुम्॥
en: If I do not slay in encounter that slayer of my brother-Rāghava, certainly death is even that which is good for me, otherwise, this life is useless.

sn: अद्यैव तं गमिष्यामि देशं यत्रानुजो मम। नहि भ्रातृन्समुत्सृज्य क्षणं जीवितुमुत्सहे॥
en: This very day will I repair to that place where my younger brother is. Forsaking my brother, I forsooth dare not live for a moment.

sn: देवा हि मां हसिष्यन्ति दृष्ट्वा पूर्वापकारिणम्। कथमिन्द्रं जयिष्यामि कुम्भकर्ण हते त्वयि ॥
en: For the gods shall laugh on seeing me, who had formerly wronged them. But, how, O Kumbhakarņa, you having been slain, shall I conquer Indra?

sn: तदिदं मामनुप्राप्तं विभीषणवचः शुभम्। यदज्ञानान्मया तस्य न गृहीतं महात्मनः॥ विभीषणवचस्तावत्कुम्भकर्णप्रहस्तयोः। विनाशोऽयं समुत्पनो मां वीडयति दारुणः॥
en: Now the beneficial words of Vibhīşaņa have been verified. And as through blindness I did not accept the advice of that high-souled one, Kumbhakarņa and of Prahasta, this disaster arisen, shame me sore.

sn: तस्यायं कर्मणः प्राप्तो विपाको मम शोकदः। यन्मया धार्मिकः श्रीमान्स निरस्तो विभीषणः॥
en: As I had disgraced the virtuous and graceful Vibhīşaņa, this peril producing grief, has been the consequence of my conduct.

sn: इति बहुविधमाकुलान्तरात्मा कृपणमतीव विलप्य कुम्भकर्णम्। स्तमनुजमिन्द्ररिपुं हतं विदित्वा॥
en: Having thus piteously and long lamented Kumbhakarna, the Ten-necked one, with his inmost soul overwhelmed with sorrow, and sore distressed in consequence of grief, fell down, knowing his brother—the enemy of Indra-slain in battle.

sn: एवं विलपमानस्य रावणस्य दुरात्मनः। श्रुत्वा शोकाभिभूतस्य त्रिशिरा वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
en: Hearing the lamentations of the wickedminded Ravana, overwhelmed with grief, Trisiras addressed him, saying.

sn: एवमेव महावीर्यो हतो नस्तातमध्यमः। न तु सत्पुरुषा राजन्विलपन्ति यथा भवान्॥
en: O Sire, this second uncle to us possessed of mighty prowess has* forsooth been slain in fight. But, О king, heroes never indulge in grief as youdoes. as *Evameva-forsooth, I render it. The commentator, however, says it means such as you have described him.

sn: नूनं त्रिभुवनस्यापि पर्याप्तस्त्वमसि प्रभो। स कस्मात्प्राकृत इव शोचस्यात्मानमीदृशम्॥
en: O lord, you certainly alone are competent to conquer the triple world. Wherefore then did you went such sorrow like an ignoble one?

sn: ब्रह्मदत्तास्ति ते शक्तिः कवचं सायको धनुः। सहस्रस्वरसंयुक्तो रथो मेघसमस्वनः॥
en: You have your dart conferred on you by Brahmā; and your mail and your weapon—the bow-and your car yoked with a thousand asses, sending forth clatter resembling the rumbling of clouds.

sn: त्वयासकृद्धि शस्त्रेण विशस्ता देवदानवाः। स सर्वायुधसंपन्नो राघवं शास्तुमर्हसि॥
en: The deities and the Dănavas have by means of your arms been terrified over and over again. And furnished with all arms, you ought to chastise Rāghava.

sn: कामं तिष्ठ महाराज निर्गमिष्याम्यहं रणे। उद्धरिष्यामि ते शत्रूनगरुडः पन्नगानिव॥
en: But stay at your pleasure, O mighty sovereign, I will go out to battle; and even as Garuda capture serpents, will I capture your enemies.

sn: शम्बरो देवराजेन नरको विष्णुना यथा । तथाद्य शयिता रामो मया युधि निपातितः॥
