en: As Sambara was vanquished by the lord of the immortals, or Naraka by Visnu, will I bringing down Rāma in battle make him sleep (in the field).

sn: श्रुत्वा त्रिशिरसो वाक्यं रावणो राक्षसाधिप.। पुनतिमिवात्मानं मन्यते कालचोदितः॥
en: Hearing Triſiras words Rāvana-lord of Rākşasas-urged on by fate, considered himself as having regained his life.

sn: श्रुत्वा त्रिशिरसो वाक्यं देवान्तकनरान्तकौ। अतिकायश्च तेजस्वी बभूवुयुद्धहर्षिताः॥
en: Hearing the speech of Triģiras, Devāntaka, and Narāntaka, and the energetic Atikāya also, were wrought up with martial enthusiam.

sn: ततोऽहमहमित्येवं गर्जन्तो नैर्ऋतर्षभाः। रावणस्य सुता वीराः शक्रतुल्यपराक्रमाः॥
en: Then those foremost of Naiſtas-the heroic sons of Rāvaņa-endowed with the prowess of Sakra himself-roared out, I will go,' 'I will go.' or

sn: अन्तरिक्षगताः सर्वे सर्वे मायाविशारदा। सर्वे त्रिदशदर्पघ्नाः सर्वे समरदुर्मदाः॥
en: All could range the sky, and all were skilled in illusion, and all were crushers of the pride of the immortals; and all were irresistible in encounter.

sn: सर्वे सुबलसंपन्नाः सर्वे विस्तीर्णकीर्तयः। सर्वे समरमासाद्य न श्रूयन्ते स्म निर्जिताः॥ देवैरपि सगन्धर्वैः सकिंनरमहोरगैः। सर्वेऽस्त्रविदुषो वीराः सर्वे युद्धविशारदाः।। सर्वे प्रवरविज्ञानाः सर्वे लब्धवरास्तथा॥
en: All of them were endowed with superior strength, and all had achieved wide celebrity. They had never been heard of as having been beaten in fight even by the gods along with the Gandharvas, the mighty serpents accompanied by the Kinnaras. And all were skilled in weapons and heroic; and all were versed in werfare. And all were possessed of the higher knowledge; and all had obtained boons.

sn: स तैस्तथा भास्करतुल्यदर्शनैः सुतैर्वृतः शत्रुबलश्रियार्दनैः। वृतो महादानवदर्पनाशनैः॥
en: Then the king surrounded by those sons of his, appearing like celestials, capable of injuring the force and fortune of the foes, looked splendid like Maghavan environed by the immortals, humblers of the hauteur of mighty Danavas.

sn: स पुत्रान्संपरिष्वज्य भूषयित्वा च भूषणैः। आशीभिश्च प्रशस्ताभिः प्रेषयामास वै रणे॥
en: Embracing his sons and adorning them in ornaments, he sent them to the field with his best benedictions.

sn: युद्धोन्मत्तं च मत्तं च भ्रातरौ चापि रावणः। रक्षणार्थ कुमाराणां प्रेषयामास संयुगे॥
en: Rävaņa sent the brothers, Yudhyonmatta and Matta, for protecting the princes in the field.

sn: तेऽभिवाद्य महात्मानं रावणं लोकरावणम्। कृत्वा प्रदक्षिणं चैव महाकायाः प्रतस्थिरे॥
en: Then, saluting the high-souled Ravanadestroyer of creatures, and going round him, those huge-bodied ones marched forth.

sn: सर्वोषधीभिर्गन्धैश्च समालभ्य महाबलाः। निर्जग्मुर्नैर्ऋतश्रेष्ठाः षडेते युद्धकाङ्गिणः॥ त्रिशिराश्चातिकायश्च देवान्तकनरान्तकौ। महोदरमहापाचौं निर्जग्मुः कालचोदिताः॥
en: And furnished with every description of medicinal herbs and perfumes, these six Nairtas-foremost of their kind endowed with great strength, burning for battle, marched forth, Triširas and Atikāya, and Devântaka and Narāntaka, and Mahodara and Mahāpāśva went out, urged on by Fate.

sn: ततः सुदर्शनं नागं नीलजीमूतसंनिभम्। ऐरावतकुले जातमारुरोह महोदरः॥
en: Then Mahodara mounted the elephant Sudarsana-sprung in the race of Airāvata, and resembling dark-blue clouds.

sn: सर्वायुधसमायुक्तस्तूणीभिश्चाप्यलंकृतः। रराज गजमास्थाय सवितेवास्तमूर्धनि॥
en: Accoutred in every weapon, and decked with quivers, he looked splendid on his elephant like the Sun ascending the crest of the Setting-hill.

sn: हयोत्तमसमायुक्तं सर्वायुधसमाकुलम्। आरुरोह रथश्रेष्ठं त्रिशिरा रावणात्मजः॥
en: Ravana's son-Trisiras, ascended a car yoked with excellent steeds, and furnished with every variety of arms.

sn: त्रिशिरा रथमास्थाय विरराज धनुर्धरः। सविधुदुल्कः सज्वाल: सेन्द्रचाप इवाम्बुदः॥
en: Having ascended the car, Trisiras bow in hand appeared beautiful like a mass of burning clouds having lightning and meteors, and crowned with Indra's bow.. *The rain-bow is called sometimes Indra's bow and at others Rama's bow.

sn: त्रिभिः किरीटैलिशिराः शुशुभे स रथोत्तमे। हिमवानिव शैलेन्द्रखिभिः काञ्चनपर्वतैः॥
en: Dight with three diadems, Trisiras looked splendid in that superb car, like the monarch of mountains Himavān—with the three golden hills.

sn: अतिकायोऽतितेजस्वी राक्षसेन्द्रसुतस्तदा। आरुरोह रथश्रेष्ठं श्रेष्ठः सर्वधनुष्मताम्॥ सुचक्राक्षं सुसंयुक्तं सानुकर्ष सकूबरम्। तूणीबाणासनैर्दीप्तं प्रासासिपरिघाकुलम्॥
en: Then that foremost of all bowmen-the powerful Atikāya-son to the lord of Raksasas-ascended the best of cars, having excellent wheels and akşas, and yoked with excellent steeds, and furnished with bottoms and holes; flaming with quivers and bows; and bristling with prāścas and swords and blugdeons.

sn: स काञ्चनविचित्रेण किरीटेन विराजता। भूषणैश्च बभौ मेरुः प्रभाभिरिव भासयन्॥
en: Adorned with a crown plated with wrought gold' and (other) ornaments he looked like the Meru swimming in its own splendour.

sn: स रराज रथे तस्मिन्राजसूनुर्महाबलः। वृतो नैऋतशार्दूलर्वज्रपाणिरिवामरैः॥
en: That powerful son of the kind surrounded by the Naiſtas looked lovely on that car like the thunder-handed (Deity) engirt by the immortals.

sn: हयमुच्चैःश्रवःप्रख्यं श्वेतं कनकभूषणम्। मनोजवं महाकायमारुरोह नरान्तकः॥
en: Narāntaka mounted a white steed resembling Uccaiḥśravă, caparisoned in gold, having a large frame and endowed with the velocity of the wind.

sn: गृहीत्वा प्रासमुल्काभं विरराज नरान्तकः। शक्तिमादाय तेजस्वी गुहः शिखिगतो यथा॥
en: Taking a prāśa, Narāntaka appeared like the energetic Guha mounted on the peacock, grasping his dart.

sn: देवान्तकः समादाय परिघं हेमभूषणम्। परिगृह्य गिरि दोभ्यां वपुर्विष्णोविडम्बयन्॥
en: Taking a bludgeon decked in golden Ornaments, Devántaka resembled Vişņu at the time of the churning of the ocean, holding the Dorbhya* and staying burthening (the earth). *The mountain Mandara which served as the churning-stick..

sn: महापार्थो महातेजा गदामादाय वीर्यवान्। विरराज गदापाणिः कुवेर इव संयुगे॥
en: The powerful Mahāpārsva endowed with terrific energy, taking his mace, appeared like Kuvera holding in his hand a mace in the encounter.

sn: ते प्रतस्थुमहात्मानोऽमरावत्याः सुरा इव। तान्गजैश्च तुरङ्गैश्च रथैश्चाम्बुदनिःस्वनैः॥ अनूत्पेतुर्महात्मानो राक्षसाः प्रवरायुधाः।
en: Like immortals issuing out of Amarāvatſ, they marched out with elephants and steeds and cars sending out clatter resembling the rumbling of clouds. And them followed high-souled Räkşasas equipped with mighty-arms.

sn: ते विरेजुर्महात्मानः कुमाराः सूर्यवर्चसः॥ किरीटिनः श्रिया जुष्टा ग्रहा दीप्ता इवाम्बरे।
en: Those sun-bright high-souled princes decked with diadems appeared splendid like burning planets in the firmament.

sn: प्रगृहीता बभौ तेषां वस्त्राणामावलिः शिवा ॥ शरदभ्रप्रतीकाशा हंसावलिरिवाम्बरे।
en: The various gorgeous attires which they had worn resembled rows of cranes in the sky, looking like autumnal clouds.

sn: मरणं वापि निश्चित्य शत्रूणां वा पराजयम्॥ इति कृत्वा मतिं वीराः संजग्मुः संयुगार्थिनः।
en: Resolved on dying or conquering the foe in fight, those heroes sallied out seeking encounter.

sn: जगर्जुश्च प्रणेदुश्च चिक्षिपुश्चापि सायकान्॥ जगृहुश्च महात्मानो निर्याता युद्धदुर्मदाः।
en: Those high-souled ones, incapable of being repressed in fight, roared and shouted and discharged shafts and held them,

sn: वेडितास्फोटितानां वै संचचालेव मेदिनी॥ रक्षसां सिंहनादैश्च संस्फोटितमिवाम्बरम्।
en: The earth shook as they sent up leonine roars and struck at their arms with their hands; and the sky seemed riven with the leonine roars of the Rākşasa.

sn: तेऽभिनिष्क्रम्य मुदिता राक्षसेन्द्रा महाबलाः॥ ददृशुर्वानरानीकं समुद्यतशिलानगम्।
en: Issuing out cheerfully, those foremost of Rāks asas endowed with great strength beheld that monkey-army staying with upraised rocks and stones.

sn: हरयोऽपि महात्मानो ददृशू राक्षसं बलम्॥ हस्त्यश्वरथसंबाधं किङ्किणीशतनादितम्। नीलजीमूतसंकाशं समुद्यतमहायुधम्॥ दीप्तानलरविप्रख्यैनैर्ऋतैः सर्वतो वृतम्।
en: The high souled monkeys also saw that mighty host of Räkşasas thronging with elephants, horses and cars, and ringing with hundreds of bell-lets; resembling dark-blue clouds; upraising mighty arms; and environed on all sides by Naiſtas resembling flaming fire.

sn: तदृष्ट्वा बलमायातं लब्धलक्षाः प्लवंगमाः।॥ समुद्यतमहाशैलाः संप्रणेदुर्मुहुर्मुहुः। अमृष्यमाणा रक्षांसि प्रतिनर्दन्त वानराः॥ ततः समुत्कृष्टरवं निशम्य रक्षोगणा वानरयूथपानाम्। महाबला भीमतरं प्रणेदुः।॥
en: Seeing that force advance, the monkeys, finding opportunity, upraising gaint crags momentarily set up shouts. And thereat, the Rakş asas, incapable of bearing those shouts, shouted in reply to the monkeys. And again the monkeys shouted to the Raksasa, who were unable to put up with that cry. And hearing that loud shout of the monkey-leaders, the mighty Raksasa, incapable of bearing that noise expressive of exhilaration, shouted still more dreadfully.

sn: ते राक्षसबलं घोरं प्रविश्य हरियूथपाः। विचेरुरुद्यतैः शैलैनंगाः शिखरिणो यथा॥
en: Then diving into that dreadful Räkşasa army, the monkey-leaders began to range it with uplifted rocks, like to mountains.

sn: कोचिदाकाशमाविश्य केचिदुर्व्या प्लवंगमाः। रक्ष:सैन्येषु संक्रुद्धाः केचिद्रुमशिलायुधाः॥
en: Equipped with trees and stones, the monkeys enraged, ranged the Raksasa army, now rising into the sky, and now coming down to the earth. And some among the powerful monkeys went about taking broad-shouldered trees.

sn: द्रुमांश्च विपुलस्कन्धान्गृह्य वानरपुङ्गवाः। तद्युद्धमभवद्घोरं रक्षोवानरसंकुलम्॥ ते पादपशिलाशैलैश्चक्रुर्वृष्टिमनूपमाम्। बाणौधैर्यमाणाश्च हरयो भीमविक्रमाः।॥
en: The encounter that took place between the thronging Räkşasa and monkeys was some-thing terrific. And (the monkeys) began to pour a wonderful shower of trees and rocks and cliffs. The monkeys of dread prowess were resisted with vollies of shafts.

sn: सिंहनादान्विनेदुश्च रणे राक्षसवानराः। शिलाभिश्चूर्णयामासुर्यातुधानाप्लवंगमाः।॥ निजघ्नुः संयुगे क्रुद्धाः कवचाभरणावृतान्। केचिद्रथगतान्वीरान्गजवाजिगतानपि॥ निर्जघ्नुः सहसा वीरान्यातुधानान्प्लवंगमाः।
en: In the contest the monkeys and Rākşasas emitted leonine roars. And monkeys crushed Yatudhānas with rocks, and, wrought with rage, (they) in the encounter slew (Raksasas) covered with armour and ornaments; and steeds. The monkeys on a sudden slew heroic Yätudhānas.

sn: शैलशृङ्गान्विताङ्गास्ते मुष्टिभिर्वान्तलोचनाः॥ चेलुः पेतुश्च नेदुश्च तत्र राक्षसपुङ्गवाः।
en: Smite with mountain-peaks on their persons, and with their eyes falling off, the foremost of Rakşasas moved, dropped down, or roared in the scene of conflict.

sn: राक्षसाश्च शरैस्तीक्ष्णैर्बिभिदुः कपिकुञ्जरान्॥ शूलमुद्रखङ्गैश्च जघ्नुः प्रासैश्च शक्तिभिः।
en: The Rakşasas (on their part) pierced the foremost of monkeys with sharpened and keen darts and clubs and scimitars; and slew them with darts and pracas.

sn: अन्योन्यं पातयामासुः परस्परजयैषिणः॥ रिपुशोणितदिग्धाङ्गास्तत्र वानरराक्षसाः।
en: And, eager for bringing down each other, the monkeys and the Räkşasas with their persons washed with the blood of their antagonists felled each other.

sn: ततः शैलैश्च खङ्गैश्च विसृष्टैर्हरिराक्षसैः॥ मुहूर्तेनावृता भूमिरभवच्छोणितौक्षिता।
en: In a moment the earth was covered with crags and swords discharged by monkeys and Raksasas, and was drenched in gore.

sn: विकीर्णैः पर्वताकारे रक्षोभिरभिमार्दितैः।। आसीद्वसुमती पूर्णा तदा युद्धमदान्वितैः॥
en: The field was blocked up with scattered mountain-like Rākşasas influenced by martial ardour, mangled by their enemies.

sn: आक्षिप्ताः क्षिप्यमाणाश्च भग्नशैलैश्च वानरैः। पुनरङ्गैस्तदा चक्रुर्वानरा युद्धमद्भुतम्॥
en: The monkeys thrown down and felled by means of broken crags and monkeys* and arms and legs, waged a wonderful war. *i.e. the carcasses thereof.

sn: वानरान्वानरैरेव जघ्नुस्ते नैतर्षभाः। राक्षसान्राक्षसैरेव जघ्नुस्ते वानरा अपि॥ आक्षिप्य च शिलाः शैलाञ्जघ्नुस्ते राक्षसास्तदा। तेषां चाच्छिद्य शस्त्राणि जघ्नू रक्षांसि वानराः॥ निर्जघ्नुः शैलशृङ्गैश्च बिभिदुश्च परस्परम्। सिंहनादान्विनेदुश्च रणे राक्षसवानराः॥
en: Those foremost of Naiſtas slew monkeys with (the dead bodies of monkeys); and the monkeys smote Rākṣasas with (the dead bodies of) Rāks asas; and the Raksasas slew (the monkeys), hurling rocks and crags. And snatching away their own arms by main force, the monkeys finished Rākṣasa; and they, slaughtered them with mountain-peaks, and also wounded each other. The monkeys and Räkşasas emitted leonine roars in the encounter.

sn: छिन्नवर्मतनुत्राणा राक्षसा वानरैर्हताः। रुधिरं प्रसृतास्तत्र रससारमिव दुमाः॥
en: The Rākşasas, slain by the monkeys, having their mail and defence for the body rent, bled like to trees exuding sap.

sn: रथेन च रथं चापि वारणेनापि वारणम्। हयेन च हयं केचिनिर्जघ्नुर्वानरा रणे॥
en: And in that encounter, some among the monkeys destroyed cars with cars, elephants with elephants, and steeds with steeds.

sn: क्षुरप्रैरर्धचन्द्रैश्च भल्लैश्च निशितैः शरैः। राक्षसा वानरेन्द्राणां बिभिदुः पादपाशिलाः॥
en: The Raksasas rived the trees and rocks of the foremost monkeys by means of Kșurapras and crescents and sharpened Bhallas and arrows.

sn: विकीर्णा पर्वतास्तैश्च दुमच्छिन्नैश्च संयुगे। हतैश्च कपिरक्षोभिर्दुर्गमा वसुधाभवत्॥
en: In that encounter the earth became impassable, having been scattered with crags baffled and severed trees and (warriors) slain by monkeys and Rākṣasa.

sn: ते वानरा गर्वितहृष्टचेष्टाः संग्राममासाद्य भयं विमुच्य। युद्धं स्म सर्वे सह राक्षसैस्ते नानायुधाश्चक्रुरदीनसत्त्वाः॥
en: Those monkeys, equipped with various weapons and with their vigour unworn, entering upon the conflict casting off fear, cheerfully putting forth efforts springing from pride of spirit, warred on with the Räkşasas.

sn: तस्मिन्प्रवृत्ते तुमुले विमर्दे प्रहष्यमाणेषु वलीमुखेषु। निपात्यमानेषु च राक्षसेषु महर्षयो देवगणाश्च नेदुः॥
en: In that fearful conflict, which was being waged, on the monkeys having been exhilarated and the Rākşasas having been brought down, the Maharsis and the deities sent up shouts.

sn: मारुह्य शक्तिं निशितां प्रगृह्य। नरान्तको वानरसैन्यमुग्रं महार्णवं मीन इवाविवेश॥
en: Then mounted on a charger endued with the celerity of the wind, and grasping a whetted dart, Narāntaka entered into that fierce army of monkeys, like a fish diving into the deep.

sn: स वानरान्सप्त शतानि वीरः प्रासेन दीप्तेन विनिर्बिभेद। एक: क्षणेनेन्द्ररिपूर्महात्मा जघान सैन्यं हरिपुङ्गवानाम्॥
en: That hero by means of an effulgent bearded dart pierced seven hundred monkeys, and at one time the high-souled enemy of Indra slew the army of the foremost of monkeys.

sn: ददृशुश्च महात्मानं हयपृष्ठप्रतिष्ठितम्। चरन्तं हरिसैन्यैषु विद्याधरमहर्षयः॥
en: The Vidyadharas and Maharsis saw that highsouled one mounted on horseback, ranging the monkey-ranks.

sn: स तस्य ददृशे मार्गो मांसशोणितकर्दमः। पतितैः पर्वताकारैर्वानरैरभिसंवृतः॥
en: His course was discovered, miry with flesh and blood and blocked up with mountain-like monkeys fallen.

sn: यावद्विक्रमितुं बुद्धिं चक्रुः प्लवगपुङ्गवाः। तावदेतानतिक्रम्य निर्बिभेद नरान्तकाः। ७०॥
en: When the monkeys set their hearts on displaying their prowess, Narāntaka, baffling them, pierced them with shafts.

sn: ददाह हरिसैन्यानि वनानीव विभावसुः। यावदुत्पाटयामासुर्वृक्षाशैलान्वनौकसः॥ तावत्प्रासहताः पेतुर्वज्रकृत्ता इवाचलाः।
en: He consumed the monkey-army, like fire burning a forest. And when the wood-rangers uprooted trees and crags, they slain by bearded darts dropped down like mountains riven by the thunder.

sn: ज्वलन्तं प्रासमुद्यम्य संग्रामान्ते नरान्तकः॥ दिक्षु सर्वासु बलवान्विचचार नरान्तकः। प्रमृद्गन्सर्वतो युद्धे प्रावृट्काले यथानिलः।७३।।
en: Raising a glowing prasa, the powerful Narāntaka began to range about in the rear of the forces; dashing everywhere (against the foe) in fight, like the wind in the rainy season. *Sangramānte, I presume, means rear of the forces; although literally it means, at the conclusion of the conflict, because this interpretation would not be proper, the battle being now at its hottest.

sn: न शेकुर्भाषितुं वीरा न स्थातुं स्पन्दितुं कुतः। उत्पतन्तं स्थितं यान्तं सर्वान्विव्याध वीर्यवान्॥
en: The heroes could not appear prominently, or keep their posts. And how could they then move freely? And that one endued with prowess pierced everyone, whether springing, or staying, or moving.

sn: एकेनान्तककल्पेन प्रासेनादित्यतेजसा। भग्नानि हरिसैन्यानि निपेतुर्धरणीतले।७५।।
en: Broken through by a single praśa, resembling the Reaper, and furnished with solar effulgence, the monkey-ranks began to roll on the earth.

sn: वज्रनिष्पेषसदृशं प्रासस्याभिनिपातनम्। न शेकुर्वानराः सोढुं ते विनेदुर्महास्वनम्॥
en: The monkeys were ill fitted to bear the impetus of that präśa having the touch of thunder itself; and they raised a loud cry.

sn: पततां हरिवीराणां रूपाणि प्रचकाशिरे। वभिन्नाग्रकूटानां शैलानां पततामिव। ७७।।
en: The appearances of those monkey-heroes falling were like mountains toppling, having their summits riven with the thunder-bolt.

sn: ये तु पूर्व महात्मानः कुम्भकर्णेन पातिताः। ते स्वस्था वानरश्रेष्ठाः सुग्रीवमुपतस्थिरे॥
en: Those high-souled and powerful monkeys that formerly had been brought down by Kumbhakarma, having recovered, were present with Sugrīva in this encounter.

sn: प्रेक्षमाणः स सुग्रीवो ददृशे हरिवाहिनीम्। नरान्तक यत्रस्तां विद्रवन्ती यतस्ततः। ७९।।
en: Sugrīva, looking around, saw that monkeyarmy flying in all directions, agitated with the fear of Narantaka.

sn: विद्वतां वाहिनीं दृष्ट्वा स ददर्श नरान्तकम्। गृहीतप्रासमायान्तं हयपृष्ठप्रतिष्ठितम् ॥
en: After seeing the army in flight, he saw Narāntaka himself, advancing, wielding a prasa, and mounted on a steed.

sn: दृष्ट्वोवाच महातेजाः सुग्रीवो वानराधिपः। कुमारमङ्गदं वीरं शक्रतुल्यपराक्रमम्॥
en: As soon as he saw (that hero), the exceedingly energetic lord of monkeys, Sugriva addressed the heroic prince Angada endowed with strength equal to that of Indra, saying.

sn: गच्छैनं राक्षसं वीरं योऽसौ तुरगमास्थितैः। भक्षयन्तं परबलं क्षिप्रं प्राणैर्वियोजय।८२॥
en: Go against this heroic Raksasas that is mounted on a steed; and speedily deprive of life that one who is devouring up the ranks of his foes.

sn: स भर्तुर्वचनं श्रुत्वा निष्पपाताङ्गदस्तदा। अनीकान्मेघसंकाशादंशुमानिव वीर्यवान्॥
en: Hearing his master's speech, Angada descended from that host resembling clouds, like the powerful Sun himself.

sn: शैलसंघातसंकाशो हरीणामुत्तमोऽङ्गदः। रराजाङ्गदसंनद्धः स धातुरिव पर्वतः॥
en: And resembling a mass of crags, Angada-foremost of monkeys, Adorned with Angadas, appeared beautiful like a mountain with metals on it.

sn: निरायुधो महातेजाः केवलं नखदंष्ट्रवान्। नरान्तकमभिक्रम्य वालिपुत्रोऽब्रवीद्वचः॥
en: And weaponless himself, and furnished only with nails and teeth, Vali's son attacking Narāntaka, said.

sn: तिष्ठ किं प्राकृतैरेभिर्हरिभिस्त्वं करिष्यसि। अस्मिन्वज्रसमस्पर्श प्रासं क्षिप ममोरसि॥
en: Stay! What shall you do with these inferior monkeys? This prasa, having the feel of the thunder-bolt, do you hurl at my heart itself.

sn: अङ्गदस्य वचः श्रुत्वा प्रचुक्रोध नरान्तकः। संदश्य दशनैरोष्ठं निःश्वस्य च भुजंगवत्।। अभिगम्याङ्गदं क्रुद्धो वालिपुत्रं नरान्तकः॥
en: Hearing Angada's words, Narāntaka was fired with wrath. And knawing his upper lip with his teeth and sighing like a serpent, Narāntaka, wrought with wrath, approached Vali's son.

sn: स प्रासमाविध्य तदाङ्गदाय समुज्ज्वलन्तं सहसोत्ससर्ज। स वालिपुत्रोरसि वज्रकल्पे बभूव भग्नो न्यपतच्च भूमौ ॥
en: Then whirling his praśa, he suddenly discharged that flaming (weapon) against Argada. And then it was snapped on the breast of Vali's son, resembling the thunder-bolt, and dropped to the earth.

sn: तं प्रासमालोक्य तदा विभग्नं सुपर्णकृत्तोरगवीर्यकल्पम्। स्तुरंगमस्याभिजघान मूर्धि॥
en: Seeing the praśa broken in pieces, like a powerful snake severed by Suparna, Vāli's son, raising his hand, dealt a slap at the head of his (Narāntaka's) steed.

sn: निमग्नपादः स्फुटिताक्षितारो निष्क्रान्तजिह्वोऽचलसंनिकाशः। स तस्य वाजी निपपात भूमौ तलप्रहारेण विकीर्णमूर्धा १०॥
en: Thereat, with his legs sinking down and his eye-balls coming off and his tongue hanging down, and wearing the look of a mountain, on being smite with that slap, Narāntaka's steed fell down to the ground, with its head lying at random.

sn: नरान्तकः क्रोधवशं जगाम हतं तुरंगं पतितं समीक्ष्य। स मुष्टिमुद्यम्य महाप्रभावो जघान शीर्षे युधि वालिपुत्रम्॥
en: Narāntaka seeing his charger slain and fallen, was seized with a furious wrath, and raising his clenched fist, that one endowed with exceeding great energy in that conflict hit Vāll's son on the head.

sn: अथाङ्गदो मुष्टिविशीर्णमूर्धा सुस्राव तीव्र रुधिरं भृशोष्णम्। मुहुर्विजज्वाल मुमोह चापि संज्ञां समासाद्य विसिष्मिये च॥
en: Thereat Angada having his head wounded by that blow, warm blood gushed out plentifully. And momentarily burning and momentarily swooning he, regaining his senses, was amazed.

sn: अथाङ्गदो मृत्युसमानवेगं संवर्त्य मुष्टिं गिरिशृङ्गकल्पम्। निपातयामास तदा महात्मा नसन्तकस्योरसि वालिपुत्रः॥
en: Then Vāli's son, the high-souled Angada clenching his fist into a blow resembling Death itself in energy, and like to a mountain-peak, let it descend on the chest of Narāntaka.

sn: स मुष्टिनिर्भिननिमग्नवक्षा ज्वाला वमशोणितदिग्धगात्रः। नरान्तको भूमितले पपात यथाचलो वज्रनिपातभग्नः॥
en: Thereat, with his breast riven and broken down, vomiting flames and having his body bathed in blood, Narāntaka dropped down to the earth, like a hill shattered by the impetus of the thunder-bolt.

sn: तदान्तरिक्षे त्रिदशोत्तमानां वनौकसां चैव महाप्रणादः।। बभूव तस्मिनिहतेऽग्र्यवीर्ये नरान्तके वालिसुतेन संख्ये॥
en: On Narāntaka of exceeding prowess having been slain by Vali's son in battle, there arose a tremendous uproar in the firmament from the wood-rangers and the foremost of celestials.

sn: अथाङ्गदो राममनः प्रहर्षणं सुदुष्करं तं कृतवान्हि विक्रमम्। विसिष्मिये सोऽप्यथ भीमकर्मा पुनश्च युद्धे स बभूव हर्षितः॥
en: Angada having performed that difficult deed of prowess, capable of delighting the mind of Rāma, was seized with amazement;* and that one of terrific feats in fight was again inspired with delight in the encounter. * Probably, at his own prowess.

sn: नरान्तकं हतं दृष्ट्वा चुक्रुशुनैऋतषर्भाः। देवान्तकरित्रमूर्धा च पौलस्त्यश्च महोदरः॥
en: Seeing Narāntaka slain, the foremost of Naiſtas-including the three-headed Devāntaka and Pulastya's descendant, Mahodara, began to cry (in chorus).

sn: आरूढो मेघसंकाशं वारणेन्द्र महोदरः। वालिपुत्रं महावीर्यमभिदुद्राव वेगवान्॥
en: Then the vehement Mahodara, mounted (on horseback), rushed against Vali's son endued with energy.

sn: भ्रातृव्यसनसंतप्तस्तदा देवान्तको बली। आदाय परिघं घोरमङ्गदं समभिद्रवत्॥
en: Aggrieved in consequence of the calamity that had befallen his brother, the strong Devāntaka grasping a dreadful bludgeon, darted against Angada.

sn: रथमादित्यसंकाशं युक्तं परमवाजिभिः। आस्थाय त्रिशिरा वीरो वालिपुत्रमथाभ्यगात्॥
en: Ascending a car resembling the Sun yoked with superb steeds, the heroic Triģiras rushed against Vali's son.

sn: स त्रिभिर्देवदर्पघ्नै राक्षसेन्ट्रैरभिद्रुतः। वृक्षमुत्पाटयामास महाविटपमङ्गदः॥ देवान्तकाय तं वीरश्चिक्षेप सहसाङ्गदः। महावृक्षं महाशाखं शक्रो दीप्तामिवाशनिम्॥
en: Then charged by those three powerful Räkş asas-crushers of the hauteur of immortals, Angada uprooted a tree furnished with gigantic branches. And as Sakra hurl the mighty flaming thunder-bolt, that hero-Angada, at once hurled against Devāntaka that mighty tree having giant branches.

sn: त्रिशिरास्तं प्रचिच्छेद शरैराशीविषोपमैः। स वृक्षं कृत्तमालोक्य उत्पपात तदाङ्गदः।७।। स ववर्ष ततो वृक्षाशिलाश्च कपिकुञ्जरः। तान्प्रचिच्छेद संक्रुद्धस्त्रिशिरा निशितैः शरैः॥ परिघाग्रेण तान्वृक्षान्बभञ्ज स महोदरः। त्रिशिराश्चाङ्गदं वीरमभिदुद्राव सायकैः।९।। गजेन समभिद्रुत्य वालिपुत्रं महोदरः। जघानोरसि संक्रुद्धस्तोमरैर्वज्रसंनिभैः॥
en: Trisiras cut off that tree in pieces by means of shafts resembling serpents. And seeing the tree severed, Angada darted up; and then that foremost of monkeys showered crags and trees. And all those Triſiras wrought with wrath cut off by means of whetted arrows; and Mahodara snapped those trees with the end of his bludgeon. And then Trisiras rushed against that hero-Valr's son-with shafts; and Mahodara chased him, mounted own an elephant; and struck Angada in the chest with Tomaras resembling the thunder-bolt. 1. The text has Angada avoided for euphony. 2. The text has Vali's son.

sn: देवान्तकश्च संक्रुद्धः परिघेण तदाङ्गदम्। उपगम्याभिहत्याशु व्यपचक्राम वेगवान्॥
en: Devantaka, enraged advancing, hit Angada with his bludgeon, and then, endowed with velocity, he swiftly turned away.

sn: स त्रिभिनैर्ऋतश्रेष्ठैर्युगपत्समभिद्रुतः। न विव्यथे महातेजा वालिपुत्रः प्रतापवान्॥
en: Attacked simultaneously by those three powerful Naiſtas, the exceedingly energetic son of Vali's possessed of prowess, did not feel any pain.

sn: स वेगवान्महावेगं कृत्वा परमदुर्जयः। तलेन समभिदुत्य जघानास्य महागजम्॥
en: That impetuous one incapable of being conquered, summoning his utmost vehemence, rushing on, pealt a slap at his* mighty elephant. *Mahodara's.

sn: तस्य तेन प्रहारेण नागराजस्य संयुगे॥ पेततुर्नयने तस्य विननाश स कुञ्जरः।
en: Thereat in the conflict the king elephant fell down in his very sight and expired.

sn: विषाणं चास्य निष्कृष्य वालिपुत्रो महाबलः॥ देवान्तकमभिदुत्य ताडयामास संयुगे।
en: Then pulling out his tusks, the highly powerful son of Vāli, darting against Devāntaka, dealt him a blow therewith in that encounter.

sn: स विह्वलस्तु तेजस्वी वातोद्भूत इव दुमः॥ लाक्षारससवर्णं च सुस्राव रुधिरं महत्।
en: Thereupon that strong one overwhelmed like a tree buffeted by the wind, began to discharge blood profusely, looking like the hue of lac.

sn: अथाश्वस्य महातेजाः कृच्छ्राद्देवान्तको बली॥ आविध्य परिघं वेगादाजधान तदाङ्गदम्।
en: Then cheering him, the exceedingly energetic and powerful Narāntaka, violently whirling his bludgeon with might and main, hit Angada with it.

sn: परिघाभिहतश्चापि वानरेन्द्रात्मजस्तदा॥ जानुभ्यां पतितो भूमौ पुनरेवोत्पपात ह।
en: And albeit struck with the bludgeon, the son of the lord of monkeys, going down on his knees, again darted up.

sn: तमुत्पतन्तं त्रिशिरास्त्रिभिर्बाणैरजिह्मगैः॥ घोरैर्हरिपतेः पुत्रं ललाटेऽभिजघान ह।
en: As he sprang up, Triśiras hit at the temples of the son of the king of monkeys with three straight-speeding terrific shafts.

sn: ततोऽङ्गदं परिक्षिप्तं विभिनैर्ऋतपुङ्गवैः॥ हनूमानथ विज्ञाय नीलश्चापि प्रतस्थतुः।
en: Seeing Angada assailed by the three redoubtable Rakşasas, Hanumān and Nila proceeded (to his rescue).

sn: ततश्चिक्षेप शैलाग्रं नीलत्रिशिरसे तदा॥ तद्रावणसुतो धीमान्बिभेद निशितैः शरैः।
en: Then Nila hurled a mountain-top at Trisiras; and thereat that son of Rāvaņa severed it with sharpened arrows.

sn: तदेबाणशतनिर्भिन्नं विदारितशिलातलम्॥ सविस्फुलिङ्गं सज्वालं निपपात गिरेः शिरः।
en: That mountain-top on being riven, dropped down, aflame and shooting out sparks of fire.

sn: स विजृम्भितमालोक्य हर्षाद्देवान्तको बली॥ परिघेणाभिदुद्राव मारुतात्मजमाहवे।
en: Seeing him* yawning in joy, the stalwart Devāntaka in that encounter pursued the windgod's son with his bludgeon. *Triśiras.

sn: तमापतन्तमुत्पत्य हनूमान्कपिकुञ्जरः॥ आजघान तदा मूर्ध्नि वज्रकल्पेन मुष्टिना।
en: As he rushed on, that foremost of monkeysHanuman-~-dealt on the crown of his head, a blow resembling the thunder-bolt itself.

sn: शिरसि प्राहरद्वीरस्तदा वायुसुतो बली।। नादेनाकम्पयच्वैव राक्षसान्स महाकपिः॥
en: The mighty and heroic son of the wind-god hit (at his antagonist); and that redoubted monkey also with his roars made the Raksasas tremble (in fear).

sn: स मुष्टिनिष्पिष्टविभिन्नमूर्धा निर्वान्तदन्ताक्षिविलम्बिजिह्वः। र्गतासुरुव्यां सहसा पपात॥
en: Thereat with his head crushed and cleft, and his ieeth and eyes falling out, and his tongue hanging down, that son to the sovereign of the Rākşasas suddenly dropped to the earth, deprived of life.

sn: तस्मिन्हते राक्षसयोधमुख्ये महाबले संयति देवशत्रौ। क्रुद्धस्त्रिशीर्षो निशितास्त्रमुग्रं ववर्ष नीलोरसि बाणवर्षम्॥
en: On that fierce and mighty Rākşasas warriorthat foe of the immortals— having fallen in fight, the three-headed one, waxing wondrous enraged began to shower terrific sharpened shafts on Nila's chest.

sn: महोदरस्तु संक्रुद्धः कुञ्जरं पर्वतोपमम्। भूयः समधिरुह्याशु मन्दरं रश्मिवानिव॥
en: Mahodara, getting enraged, again swiftly mounted an elephant like the ray-furnished (Sun) mounting Mandara.

sn: ततो बाणमयं वर्ष नीलस्योपर्यपातयत्। गिरौ वर्ष तडिच्चक्रं स गर्जनिव तोयदः।।२८। ततः शरौधैरभिवृष्यमाणो विभिन्नगात्रः कपिसैन्यपालः। नीलो बभूवाथ विसृष्टगात्रो विष्टम्भितस्तेन महाबलेन॥
en: Then even as a mass of roaring clouds poured down showers enwheeled with levin on a mountain, he showered arrows right on Nīla's breast. Threat showered with those shafts, that leader of monkeys Nīla with his person pierced, had his body riven and was stupefied by that exceedingly powerful one.

sn: ततस्तु नीलः प्रतिलब्धसंज्ञः शैलं समुत्पाट्य सवृक्षखण्डम्। ततः समुत्पत्य महोग्रवेगो महोदरं तेन जघान मूर्ध्निः॥
en: Then that (monkey) possessed of tremendous vehemence, having regained his senses, uprooting a crag with a whole tract of trees, struck it at Mahodara's head.

sn: ततः स शैलाभिनिपातभग्नो महोदरस्तेन महाद्विपेन। व्यामोहितो भूमितले गतासुः पपात वज्राभिहतो यथाद्रिः॥
en: Struck by that mighty enemy, Mahodara, broken down by the impetus of that rock, deprived of his senses, dropped down dead on the ground, like a cliff smite with the thunderbolt.

sn: पितृव्यं निहतं दृष्ट्वा त्रिशिराश्चापमाददे। हनूमन्तं च संक्रुद्धो विव्याध निशितैः शरैः॥
en: Seeing his uncle slain, Triſiras took up his bow; and inflamed with fury pierced Hanumān with whetted arrows.

sn: स वायुसूनुः कुपितश्चिक्षेप शिखरं गिरेः। त्रिशिरास्तच्छरैस्तीक्ष्णैर्बिभेद बहुधा बली॥
en: Thereat the wind-god's son, enraged, hurled a mountain-peak (at his adversary). And Trisiras by means of keen arrows severed the same in shivers.

sn: तद्व्यर्थं शिखं दृष्ट्वा द्रुमवर्षं तदा कपिः। विससर्ज रणे तस्मिन्रावणस्य सुतं प्रति ॥
en: Seeing the mountain-peak baffled, the monkey in the encounter began to shower trees on Ravana's son.

sn: तमापतन्तमाकाशं दुमवर्ष प्रतापवान्। त्रिशिरानिशितैर्बाणैश्चिच्छेद च ननाद च ॥
en: Trisiras endowed with prowess by means of sharpened shafts cut off that descending arrowy shower in the sky and shouted (in delight).

sn: हनूमांस्तु समुत्पत्य हयं त्रिशिरसस्तदा। विददार नखैः क्रुद्धो नागेन्द्रं मृगराडिव॥
en: Then Hanumān flying into a fury, bounding to the welkin, with his nails ript the steed of Triớiras, even as a lion cleave a powerful elephant.

sn: अथ शक्तिं समासाद्य कालरात्रिमिवान्तकः। चिक्षेपानिलपुत्राय त्रिशिरा रावणात्मजः॥
en: Then taking a dart even as the destroyer employ the fatal night, Ravana's son, TriSiras discharged it at the offspring of the wind-god.

sn: दिवः क्षिप्तामिवोल्कां तां शक्तिं क्षिप्तामसंगताम्। गृहीत्वा हरिशार्दूलो बभञ्ज च ननाद च॥
en: Thereat catching the dart of resistless course as it descended from the sky, the powerful monkey snapped it and then shouted.

sn: तां दृष्ट्वा घोरसंकाशां शक्तिं भग्नां हनूमता। प्रहृष्टा वानरगणा विनेदुर्जलदा यथा॥
en: Seeing that dreadful dart broken by Hanumān, the monkeys, transported with delignt, sent up shouts, even as clouds rumble.

sn: ततः खङ्गं समुद्यम्य त्रिशिरा राक्षसोत्त निचखान तदा खङ्गं वानरेन्द्रस्य वक्षसि ॥
en: Then upraising his sword, that foremost of Raksasas-Trisiras-brought it down on the breast of the monkey-chief.

sn: खङ्गप्रहाराभिहतो हनूमान्मारुतात्मजः। आजघान त्रिमूर्धानं तलेनोरसि वीर्यवान्।४१॥
en: Overpowered with the sword-blow, Hanumān son to the wind-god, endowed with energy, dealt the three-headed one a slap on the head.

sn: स तलाभिहतस्तेन स्रस्तहस्ताम्बरो भुवि। निपपात महातेजास्त्रिशिरास्त्यक्तचेतनः।॥
en: And smitten with that slap, the highly powerful Triśiras, with his hands and attire dropping off, fell down to the earth, deprived of consciousness.

sn: स तस्य पततः खङ्गं तमाच्छिद्य महाकपिः। ननाद गिरिसंकाशस्त्रासयन्सर्वराक्षसान्॥
en: Then that mighty monkey-resembling a hill broke his sword as he fell, and roared, terrifying all the Raksasas.

sn: अमृष्यमाणस्तं घोषमुत्पपात निशाचरः। उत्पत्य च हनूमन्तं ताडयामास मुष्टिना ॥
en: But not brooking that uproar, that night-ranger sprang up; and springing up, he dealt a blow at Hanuman.

sn: तेन मुष्टिप्रहारेण संचुकोप महाकपिः। कुपितश्च निजग्राह किरीटे राक्षसर्षभम्॥
en: At that blow, the redoubtable monkey was wrought up with wrath; and inflamed with rage, he smote that foremost of Räkşasas about his diadem.

sn: स तस्य शीर्षाण्यसिना शितेन किरीटजुष्टानि सकुण्डलानि। क्रुद्धः प्रचिच्छेद सुतोऽनिलस्य त्वष्टः सुतस्येव शिरांसि शक्रः॥
en: Then with a sharp sword the wind-god's son cut off his heads decked with diadems and furnished with ear-rings; even as Sakra had severed the heads of Tastri' son.* *Visvarupa.

sn: तान्यायताक्षाण्यगसंनिभानि प्रदीप्तवैश्वानरलोचनानि। पेतुः शिरांसीन्द्ररिपोः पृथिव्यां ज्योतींषि मुक्तानि यथेन्द्रमार्गात्॥
en: Thereat even as burning stars, loosened, drop down from the course of Indra, the large organs of sense, and eyes flaming like glowing fire, and heads of that foe of Indra, dropped down to the ground.

sn: तस्मिन्हते देवरिपौ त्रिशीर्षे हनूमता शक्रपराक्रमेण। नेदुः प्लवंगाः प्रचचाल भूमी रक्षास्यथो दुद्रुविरे समन्तात्॥
en: On Trisiras, enemy of the immortals-having been slain by Hanuman endowed with the prowess itself of Sakra, the monkeys shouted, the earth shook, and the Rākṣas began to fly on all sides.

sn: हतं त्रिशिरसं दृष्ट्वा युद्धोन्मत्तं तथैव च। हतौ प्रेक्ष्य दुराधर्षों देवान्तकनरान्तकौ॥ चुकोप परमामर्षी मत्तो राक्षसपुङ्गवः। जग्राहार्चिष्मतीं चापि गदां सर्वायसीं तदा॥ हेमपट्टपरिक्षिप्तां मांसशोणितफेनिलाम्। विराजमानां विपुलां शत्रुशोणिततर्पिताम्॥ तेजसा संप्रदीप्ताग्रां रक्तमाल्यविभूषिताम्। ऐरावतमहापद्मसार्वभौमभयावहाम्॥ गदामादाय संक्रुद्धो मत्तो राक्षसपुङ्गवः। हरीन्समभिदुद्राव युगान्ताग्निरिव ज्वलन्॥
en: Seeing Triſira and Yuddhonmatta slain and seeing also the irrepressible Devāntaka and Narāntaka slain (in the encounter), that highly irascible and powerful Räkşasas-Matta, was transported with passion, and then took up a flaming mace entirely wrought with iron inlaid with gold; frothy with flesh and gore; mighty to behold; gratified with the blood of foes; with its end flaming in splendour; decked with red wreaths; and capable of striking terror into Airāvata and Mahāpadma and Sárvabhauma.* And flaming up like the fire arisen at the end of a Yuga, that foremost of Raksasas-Matta, wrought with fury, rushed against the monkeys. *Elephants of the cardinal points.

sn: अथर्षभः : समुत्पत्य वानरो रावणानुजम्। मत्तानीकमुपागम्य तस्थौ तस्याग्रतो बली॥
en: Then the mighty and powerful monkey Risabha-springing up before Ravana's son, stood before the hosts of Matta.

sn: तं पुरस्तारिथतं दृष्ट्वा वानरं पर्वतोपमम्। आजघानोरसि क्रुद्धो गदया वज्रकल्पया॥
en: Seeing that mountain-like monkey staying before (him), Matta, enraged, dealt him a blow on the breast.

sn: स तयाभिहतस्तेन गदया वानरर्षभः। भिन्नवक्षाः समाधूतः सुस्राव रुधिरं बहु।५६॥
en: And smite with the mace, that foremost of monkeys, with his breast riven and trembling, began to bleed copiously.

sn: स संप्राप्य चिरात्संज्ञामृषभो वानरेश्वरः। क्रुद्धो विस्फुरमाणौष्ठौ महापार्श्वमुदैवत॥
en: And regaining his senses after a long while, Risabha-lord of monkeys-inflamed with wrath pouting out his upper lip, gazed at Mahāpārsva.* *Otherwise, called Matta.

sn: स वेगवान्वेगवदभ्युपेत्य तं राक्षसं वानरवीरमुख्यः। संवर्त्य मुष्टिं सहसा जघान बाह्वन्तरे शैलनिकाशरूपः॥
en: Then impetuously approaching the Räks asas, that foremost of heroic monkeys resembling a hill, endowed with vehemence, clenching his fist, suddenly smote him with a blow on his breast.

sn: स कृत्तमूलः सहसेव वृक्षः क्षितौ पपात क्षतजोक्षिताङ्गः। तां चास्य घोरां यमदण्डकल्पां गदां प्रगृह्याशु तदा ननाद। ५९।।
en: Thereat like a tree whose roots have been severed, he suddenly dropped on the ground, covered with blood. And thereupon, (Risabha) swiftly snatched his dreadful mace resembling the rod of Yama himself; and shouted.

sn: मुहूर्तमासीत्स गतासुकल्पः प्रत्यागतात्मा सहसा सुरारिः। स्तं वारिराजात्मजमाजघान॥
en: Only for a moment did he remain like one dead. Recovering his senses, the enemy of the immortals, looking like evening clouds in hue, suddenly springing up, attacked the son of the king of waters.

sn: स मूर्छितो भूमितले पपात मुहूर्तमुत्पत्य पुनः ससंज्ञः। तामेव तस्याद्रिवराद्रिकल्पां गदां समाविध्य जघान संख्य।६१।।
en: Thereat, the dropped down to the earth, senseless. In a moment regaining his consciousness, he again bounded up, and whirling the mace resembling a peak of the foremost of mountains, in that encounter dealt (Matta) a blow therewith.

sn: सा तस्य रौद्रा समुपेत्य देहं रौद्रस्य देवाध्वरविप्रशत्रोः। बिभेद वक्षः क्षतजं च भूरि सुस्राव धात्वम्भ इवाद्रिराजः॥
en: And descending on the body of that dreadful one-the enemy of deities, sacrifices and Vipras-that terrific mace rived his breast; and the began to bleed profusely, even as the lord of mountains discharges minerals and water.

sn: अभिदुद्राव वेगेन गदां तस्य महात्मनः। तां गृहीत्वा गदां भीमामाविध्य च पुनः पुनः॥
en: And taking the terrific mace of the highsouled (Matta) and swinging it again and again, (Risabha) rushed (against the Raksasas). And that high-souled one began to slaughter Matta's forces in the field.

sn: मत्तानीकं महात्मा स जघान रणमूर्धनि। स स्वया गदया भग्नो विशीर्णदशनेक्षणः॥ निपपात तदा मत्तो वजाहत इवाचलः। विशीर्णनयनो भूमौ गतसत्त्वो गतायुषः। पतिते राक्षसे तस्मिन्विद्रुतं राक्षसं बलम्॥
en: Broken down by his own mace, Matta dropped down like a hill, with his teeth and eyes shrivelled up; and he dropped to the earth deprived of strength and life, with his eyes paling. And on that Räkşasas falling, the Raksas forces began to fly.

sn: तस्मिन्हते भ्रातरि रावणस्य तनैर्ऋतानां बलमर्णवाभम्। त्यक्तायुधं केवलजीवितार्थ दुद्राव भिन्नार्णवसंनिकाशम्॥
en: On that brother of Rāvaņa having been slain, that host of Nairtas appearing like the ocean in grandeur, leaving its arms behind, solely for life rushed away, like to the deep riven (by the winds).

sn: स्वबलं व्यथितं दृष्ट्वा तुमुलं लोमहर्षणम्। भ्रातृ॑श्च निहतान्दृष्ट्वा शक्रतुल्यपराक्रमान्॥ पितृव्यौ चापि संदृश्य समरे संनिपातितौ। युद्धोन्मत्तं च मत्तं च भ्रातरौ राक्षसोत्तमौ।२।। चुकोप च महातेजा ब्रह्मदत्तवरो युधि। अतिकायोऽद्रिसंकाशो देवदानवदर्पहा॥
en: Seeing in sore straits his own mighty forces capable of making people's down stand on end, and seeing his brothers resembling Sakra in prowess, routed; and seeing also his uncles brought down in battle, as well as his brothersYuddhonmatta and Matta— foremost of Råkş asas, that crusher of the pride of deities and Dānavas-the exceedingly energetic Atikāya-resembling a hill, who had obtained from Brahmă a boon in battle, was fired with wrath.

sn: स भास्करसहस्रस्य संघातमिव भास्वरम्। रथमारुह्य शक्रारिरभिदुद्राव वानरान्॥
en: Ascending a car effulgent like a thousand suns mingling their rays into a burst of brilliance, that enemy of Sakra, charged the monkeys.

sn: स विस्फार्य तदा चापं किरीटी मृष्टकुण्डलः। नाम संश्रावयामास ननाद च महास्वनम्॥
en: Stretching his bow, (Atikāya) decked with a diadem wearing polished ear-rings, proclaimed his name (among the monkey-ranks) and shouted in lofty tones.

sn: तेन सिंहप्रणादेन नामविश्रावणेन च। ज्याशब्देन च भीमेन त्रासयामास वानरान्।६॥
en: And with his leonine roars and the proclamation of his name, and the tremendous twang of his bow-string, he struck terror into the monkeys.

sn: ते दृष्ट्वा देहमाहात्म्यं कुम्भकर्मोऽयमुत्थितः। भयार्ता वानराः सर्वे संश्रयन्ते परस्परम्॥
en: Seeing the magnitude of his person, the monkeys thinking that it was Kumbhakarna who had come, and affrighted thereat, sought the shelter of each other.

sn: ते तस्य रूपमालोक्य यथा विष्णोस्त्रिविक्रमे। भयाद्वानरयोधास्ते विद्रवन्ति ततस्ततः।।।।।
en: Seeing his form like to that of Vişnu when he displayed his threefold energy, the monkeywarriors seized with fear, began to scour on all sides.

sn: तेऽतिकार्य समासाद्य वानरा मूढचेतसः। शरण्यं शरणं जग्मुर्लक्ष्मणाग्रजमाहवे॥
en: On Atikāya appearing before them, the monkeys stupefied in that conflict, saught the shelter of Laksmana's elder brother.

sn: ततोऽतिकायं काकुत्स्थो रथस्थं पर्वतोपमम्। ददर्श धन्विनं दूरागर्जन्तं कालमेघवत्॥
en: And from a distance Kakutstha saw the mountain-like Atikāya mounted on the car and equipped with his bow, like to roaring clouds (seen) on the occasion of the universal disruption.

sn: स तं दृष्ट्वा महाकायं राघवस्तु सुविस्मितः। वानरान्सान्त्वयित्वा च विभीषणमुवाच ह।॥
en: Seeing that huge-bodied one, Rāghava struck with surprise, comforting the monkeys, addressed Vibhisana, saying.

sn: कोऽसौ पर्वतसंकाशो धनुष्मान्हरिलोचनः। युक्ते हयसहस्रेण विशाले स्यन्दने स्थितः॥ य एष निशितैः शूलैः सुतीक्ष्णैः प्रासतोमरैः। अर्चिष्मद्भिर्वृतो भाति भूतैरिव महेश्वरः॥ कालजिह्वाप्रकाशाभिर्य एषोऽभिविराजते। आवृतो रथशक्तीभिर्विद्युद्भिरिव तोयदः॥
en: Who is this one resembling a mountain, furnished with a bow and having leonine eyes, that is stationed on a large car hoked with a thousand steeds, he that with effulgent sharpened darts and keen práśas and tomaras, shine like Maheśvara environed by spectres-he that displaying his fatal tongue appear splendid surrounded with darts in his car; like a mass of clouds graced with lightning.

sn: धनूंषि चास्य सज्जानि हेमपृष्ठानि सर्वशः। शोभयन्ति रथश्रेष्ठं शक्रचापमिवाम्बरम्॥
en: And his bows adorned and backed with gold all over, beautify his car even as Indra's bow beautify the firmament.

sn: य एष रक्षःशार्दूलो रणभूमिं विराजयत्। अभ्येति रथिनां श्रेष्ठो रथेनादित्यवर्चसा॥ ध्वजशृङ्गप्रतिष्ठेन राहुणाभिविराजते। सूर्यरश्मिप्रभैर्बाणर्दिशो दश विराजयन्॥ त्रिनतं मेघनिदिं हेमपृष्ठमलंकृतम्। शतक्रतुधनुःप्रख्यं धनुश्चास्य विराजते॥
en: Who is this foremost of Räkşasas and best of bowmen that embellishing the field of battle, approach on a car glorious as the sun; who, . displaying the ten cardinal points with his shafts resembling the rays of the sun, appear handsome with his peak of a banner bearing the figure of Rāhu, whose bow bent in three places, emitting roars resembling the rumbling of clouds, and plated with gold, look like the bow itself of Satakratu?

sn: सध्वजः सपताकश्च सानुकर्षों महारथः। चतुःसादिसमायुक्तो मेघस्तनितनिःस्वनः॥
en: His mighty car furnished with a banner and ensign and bottom, and having clatter resembling the roaring of clouds, has four horsemen (attached to it).

sn: विंशतिर्दश चाष्टौ च तूणास्य रथमास्थिताः। कार्मुकाणि च भीमानि ज्याश्च काञ्चनपिङ्गलाः॥
en: There are on the car eight and thirty quivers and dreadful bows and yellow-golden bowstrings.

sn: द्वौ च खङ्गौ च पार्श्वस्थौ प्रदीपौ पार्श्वशोभितौ। चतुर्हस्तत्सरुचितौ व्यक्तहस्तदशायतौ॥
en: There are (in that car) two effulgent swords at iis side, illumining it, their hafts measuring four lands and their blades ten each.

sn: रक्तकण्ठगुणो धीरो महापर्वतसंनिभः। कालः कालमहावक्रो मेघस्थ इव भास्करः॥
en: That calm (warrior) wears red garlands about is neck, and resembles-a mighty mountain. And very destroyer, he has a mighty mouth, appearing like that of the destroyer himself; and he look like the sun stationed on clouds.

sn: काञ्चनाङ्गदनद्वाभ्यां भुजाभ्यामेष शोभने। शृङ्गाभ्यामिव तुङ्गाभ्यां हिमवान्पर्वतोत्तमः॥
en: With his arms adorned with golden angadas, he appear splendid like that best of mountains the Himavān with its towering summits.

sn: कुण्डलाभ्यामुभाभ्यां च भाति वक्रं सुभीषणम्। पुनर्वस्वन्तरगतः परिपूर्णो निशाकरः॥
en: With his pair of ear-rings, his charming yet terrific countenance shine like the full Moon entering into Punarvasu.* *The seventh lunar asterism.

sn: आचक्ष्व मे महाबाहो त्वमेनं राक्षसोत्तमम्। यं दृष्ट्वा वानराः सर्वे भयार्ता विद्रुता दिशः॥
en: O mighty-armed one, tell me all about this foremost of Rākşasas, seeing whom the monkeys, overwhelmed with fear, fly away in all directions.

sn: स पृष्टो राजपुत्रेण रामेणामिततेजसा। आचचक्षे महातेजा राघवाय विभीषणः॥
en: Asked by the king's son Rāma of immeasurable prowess, the exceedingly energetic Vibhīşaņa spoke to Rāma, informing him.

sn: दशग्रीवो महातेजा राजा वैश्रवणानुजः। भीमकर्मा महात्मा हि रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः॥ तस्यासीद्वीर्यवान्पुत्रो रावणप्रतिमो बले। वृद्धसेवी श्रुतिधरः सर्वस्त्रविदुषां वरः॥
en: The highly powerful .king, Vaisravana's younger brother of dreadful deeds, the highsouled Rävaņa, is the sovereign of the Rāks asas. This one is his mighty son, like to Rāvaņa himself in strength. He serve the aged, is of wide celebrity and is the prime of those versed in all branches of knowledge.

sn: अश्वपृष्ठे नागपृष्ठे खड्ने धनुषि कर्षणे। भेदे सान्त्वे च दाने च नये मन्त्रे च संमतः॥ यस्य बाहुं समाश्रित्य लङ्का भवति निर्भया। तनयं धान्यमालिन्या अतिकायमिमं विदुः॥
en: He is competent to ride horses and elephants, to wield the sword or draw the bcw, or in sowing dissensions, or giving away, or in counsel, he reposing in whose arm Lanka has cast off fear. Know him to be Atikāya, son to Dhānyamāli.

sn: एतेनाराधितो ब्रह्मा तपसा भावितात्मना। अस्त्राणि चाप्यवाप्तानि रिपवश्च पराजिताः॥
en: Having adored the pure-souled Brahma with austerities, he has obtained weapons, and has defeated his foes (in fight).

sn: सुरासुरैरवध्यत्वं दत्तमस्मै स्वयंभुवा। एतच्च कवचं दिव्यं रथश्च रविभास्वरः॥
en: You shall be incapable of being slain by celestials and Asura's was the boon conferred on him by the self-sprung; and he also gave him this celestial mail and this car resembling the effulgent Sun himself.

sn: एतेन शतशो देवा दानवाश्च पराजिताः। रक्षितानि च रक्षांसि यक्षाश्चापि निषूदिताः॥
en: He has vanquished (in battle) hundreds of deities and Dänavas; and he has always) protected the Rakşasas, and destroyed Yakşas.

sn: वजं विष्टम्भितं येन बाणैरिन्द्रस्य धीमता। पाशः सलिलराजस्य युद्धे प्रतिहतस्तथा ॥
en: This intelligent one resisted the thunder-bolt itself of Indra; and in encounter baffled the very noonse of the king of waters.

sn: एषोऽतिकायो बलवान्राक्षसानामथर्षभः। स रावणसुतो धीमान्देवदानवदर्पहा॥
en: This one is Atikāya-foremost of Raksasas; and that son of Rāvana is the humbler of the hauteur of deities and Dänavas.

sn: तदस्मिन्क्रियतां यत्नः क्षिप्रं पुरुषपुङ्गव। पुरा वानरसैन्यानि क्षयं नयति सायकैः॥
en: Therefore, O best of persons, do you endeavour your best. This one with his shafts slaughter the monkey-hosts before (us).

sn: ततोऽतिकायो बलवान्प्रविश्य हरिवाहिनीम्। विस्फारयामास धनुर्ननाद च पुनः पुनः॥
en: Then the powerful Atikāya entering that monkey-force, stretched his bow and shouted again and again.

sn: तं भीमवपुषं दृष्ट्वा रथस्थं रथिनां वरम्। अभिपेतुर्महात्मानः प्रधाना ये वनौकसः॥ कुमुदो द्विविदो मैन्दो नीलः शरभ एव च। पादपैर्गिरिशृङ्गैश्च युगपत्समभिद्रवन्॥
en: The high-souled principal monkeys, seeing that (hero) possessed of a dreadful person, that best of car-warriors-stationed on his car, rushed forward. And Kumuda and Dvivida and Mainda and Nila and Sarabha dashed on at one time with trees and mountain-peaks.

sn: तेषां वृक्षांश्च शैलांश्च शरैः कनकभूषणैः। अतिकायो महातेजाश्चिच्छेदास्त्रविदां वरः।४।।
en: Thereupon that foremost of those skilled in weapons, the exceedingly energetic Atikāya, severed those trees and rocks by means of shafts dight with gold.

sn: तांश्चैव सर्वान्स हरीशरैः सर्वायसैबली। विव्याधाभिमुखान्संख्ये भीमकायो विशारदः॥
en: In that encounter that powerful one possessed of a gigantic person, skilled in arms, pierced all those monkeys staying before him with arrows entirely made of iron.

sn: तेऽर्दिता बाणवर्षेण भिन्नगात्राः पराजिताः। न शेकुरतिकायस्य प्रतिकतुं महाहवे।॥
en: And agonised, having their persons pierced in that mighty conflict by that arrowy shower, they were incapable of resisting the same.

sn: तत्सैन्यं हरिवीराणां त्रासयामास राक्षसः। मृगयूथमिव क्रुद्धो हरियौवनदर्पितः।॥
en: The Rakşasas terrified that host of monkeyheroes, even as an enraged lion priding in his youth terrify a society of deer.

sn: स राक्षसेन्द्रो हरियूथमध्ये नायुध्यमानं निजघान कंचित्। उत्पत्य रामं च धनु:कलापी सगर्वितं वाक्यमिदं बभाषे॥
en: In the midst of those bands of monkeys, that lord of Raksasas did not slay anyone without battle. And then springing up before Rāma, that one furnished with his bow and quiver, addressed him in haughty words, saying.

sn: नप्राकृतं कंचन योधयामि। यस्यास्ति शक्तिर्व्यवसाययुक्तो ददातु मे शीघ्रमिहाद्य युद्धम्॥
en: Stationed in this car holding the bow and arrows in my hands, I will not fight any that is ignoble. Him that has strength, and that also understand this business, let him today speedily give me battle.

sn: तत्तस्य वाक्यं ब्रुवतो निशम्य चुकोप सौमित्रिरमित्रहन्ता। अमृष्यमाणश्च समुत्पपात जग्राह चापं च ततः स्मयित्वा ॥
en: Hearing his speech, that slayer of foesSumitrā's son, was fired with wrath. And not bearing him, he sprang forward disregarding his antagonist's words, and took up his bow.

sn: क्रुद्धः सौमित्रिरुत्पत्य तूणादाक्षिप्य सायकम्। पुरस्तादतिकायस्य विचकर्ष महद्धनुः॥
en: And flying to fury, Sumitra's son, darting up, took out arrows from his quiver, and stretched his mighty bow in front of Atikāya.

sn: पूरयन्स महीं सर्वामाकाशं सागरं दिशः। ज्याशब्दो लक्ष्मणस्योग्रस्त्रासयन्रजनीचरान्॥
en: Filling the entire earth and the sky and the ocean and all the cardinal quarters, the terrific twang of Lakşmaņa's bow struck terror into the (hearts of the) night-rangers.

sn: सौमित्रेश्चापनिर्घोषं श्रुत्वा प्रतिभयं तदा। विसिष्मिये महातेजा राक्षसेन्द्रात्मजो बली॥
en: Hearing the dreadful twang of the bow of Sumitrā's son , the exceedingly energetic and powerful son of the lord of Rākşasas was struck with surprise.

sn: तदातिकायः कुपितो दृष्ट्वा लक्ष्मणमुत्थितम्। आदाय निशितं बाणमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Then Atikāya, enraged, seeing Lakşmaņa advance, taking sharpened shafts, spoke to him.

sn: बालस्त्वमसि सौमित्रे विक्रमेष्वविचक्षणः। गच्छ किं कालसंकाशं मां योधयितुमिच्छसि॥
en: You are a bc/, O Sumitra's sons and as such know not how to display prowess. Go you. Why wish you to fight with me resembling death itself.

sn: नहि मद्बाहुसृष्टानां बाणानां हिमवानपि। सोढुमुत्सहते वेगमन्तरिक्षमथो मही॥
en: Not Himālaya itself or the firmament or the earth is capable of bearing the impetuosity of shafts shot by my arms.

sn: सुखप्रसुप्तं कालाग्नि विबोधयितुमिच्छसि। न्यस्य चापं निवर्तस्व प्राणान्न जहिमद्गतः॥
en: You wish to rouse a fire slumbering sweetly. Leaving alone your bow, do you return. Do not lose your life by coming in contact with me.

sn: अथवा त्वं प्रतिस्तब्धो न निवर्तितुमिच्छसि। तिष्ठ प्राणान्परित्यज्य गमिष्यसि यमक्षयम्॥
en: Or it may be that you are proud; and therefore, have no mind to return. Stay then. Renouncing your life, you shall go to Yama's mansion.

sn: पश्य मे निशितान्बाणानिरपुदर्पनिषूदनान्। ईश्वरायुधसंकाशांस्तप्तकाञ्चनभूषणान्। ५५ ।।
en: Behold my whetted arrows-crushers of the insolence of foes resembling the weapon itself of the Lord,* adorned with burnished gold. *Isvara, Siva, His weapon is the trident.

sn: एष ते सर्पसंकाशो बाणः पास्यति शोणितम्। मृगराज इव क्रुद्धो नागराजस्य शोणितम्। इत्येवमुक्त्वा संक्रुद्धः शरं धनुषि संदधे॥
en: Even as a lion enraged shedded the blood of a mighty elephant, this arrow of mine resembling a serpent shall shed your blood. Having delivered himself thus, he fired with wrath set his shaft on his bow.

sn: श्रुत्वातिकायस्य वचः सरोषं सगर्वितं संयति राजपुत्रः। स संचुकोपातिबलो मनस्वी उवाच वाक्यं च ततो बृहच्छ्रीः॥
en: Hearing in that encounter Atikāya's wrathful speech fraught with hauteur, the highly powerful and intelligent son of the king possessed of exceeding grace, was transported with passion; and he said.

sn: न वाक्यमात्रेण भवान्प्रधानो न कत्थनात्सत्पुरुषा भवन्ति। मयि स्थिते धन्विनि बाणपाणौ निदर्शयस्वात्मबलं दुरात्मन्॥
en: You can not attain pre-eminence solely by virtue of your speech. One cannot be a worthy person simply by say. O wicked-minded one, do you display your strength on me equipped with the bow and holding arrows in my hands.

sn: कर्मणा सूचयात्मानं न विकस्थितुमर्हसि । पौरुषेण तु यो युक्तः स तु शूर इति स्मृतः। ५९।।
en: Manifest yourself by your valour, you ought not to blow your own trumpet. He, who is actually powerful identified as a real gallant.

sn: सर्वायुधसमायुक्तो धन्वी त्वं रथमास्थितः। शरैर्वा यदि वाप्यस्त्रैर्दर्शयस्व पराक्रमम्॥
en: Seated on a chariot and skilled in archery you are equipped with all weapons, therefore, you display your own prowess either with your arrows or with arms.

sn: ततः शिरस्ते निशितैः पातयिष्याम्यहं शरैः। मारुतः कालसंयुक्तं वृन्तात्तालफलं यथा॥
en: Then, I shall cut off your head with my sharpened arrows like wind falls down a palm fruit from its stalk, ripened in the process of time.

sn: अद्य ते मामका बाणास्तप्तकाञ्चनभूषणाः। पास्यन्ति रुधिरं गात्राबाणशल्यान्तरोत्थितम्॥
en: To-day shall my shafts decked in gold, drink your blood flowing from your person and issuing of wounds inflicted by my resembling darts.

sn: बालोऽयमिति विज्ञाय न चावज्ञातुमर्हसि। बालो वा यदि वा वृद्धो मृत्यु जानीहि संयुगे॥
en: 'This one is a boy', thinking this, you ought not to slight me. Whether I am a boy or an old* man' death shall you know in the conflict. *The commentator says the passage means-"You know (me) for death itself.” I prefer the sense given.

sn: बालेन विष्णुना लोकास्त्रयः क्रान्तास्त्रिविक्रमैः। लक्ष्मणस्य वचः श्रुत्वा हेतुमत्परमार्थवत्।। अतिकायः प्रचुक्रोध बाणं चोत्तममाददे॥ ततो विद्याधरा भूता देवदैत्या महर्षयः। गुह्यकाश्च महात्मानस्तद्युद्धं ददृशुस्तदा॥
en: It was as a boy that Vişņu had overpowered the triune world with his prowess.” Hearing Laksmana's words, fraught with reason and high sense, Vidyadharas and ghosts, deities, Daityas out arrows and Maharşis, and the high-souled Guhyakas then beheld that marvel.* *The encounter that ensued between Lakşmaņa and Atikāya.

sn: ततोऽतिकायः कुपितश्चापमारोप्य सायकम्। लक्ष्मणाय प्रचिक्षेप संक्षिपन्निव चाम्बरम्॥
en: Then Atikāya, enraged, setting his arrow on his bow, shot it at Lakşmaņa, as if devouring up the welkin.

sn: तमापतन्तं निशितं शरमाशीविषोपमम्। अर्धचन्द्रेण चिच्छेद लक्ष्मणः परवीरहा॥
en: Thereat, Lakşmaņa-slayer of hostile heroes-with a crescent severed that sharpened shaft resembling a venomous serpent, as it was descending.

sn: तं निकृत्तं शरं दृष्ट्वा कृत्तभोगमिवोरगम्। अतिकायो भृशं क्रुद्धः पञ्च बाणान्समादधे॥ ताशरान्संप्रचिक्षेप लक्ष्मणाय निशाचरः। तानप्राप्ताशितैर्बाणैश्चिच्छेद भरतानुजः॥
en: Seeing the shaft severed, like a serpent having its person cut off, Atikāya waxing exceedingly enraged, took up five arrow; and the nightranger discharged them at Lakşmaņa. Thereat Bharata's younger brother cut off the approaching arrows with whetted shafts.

sn: स ताञ्छित्त्वा शितैर्बाणैर्लक्ष्मणः परवीरहा। आददे निशितं बाणं ज्वलन्तमिव तेजसा ॥
en: Having severed them with sharpened shafts, Lakşmaņa— slayer of hostile heroes-took up a sharpened arrow, as if flaming in energy.

sn: तमादाय धनुःश्रेष्ठे योजयामास लक्ष्मणः। विचकर्ष च वेगेन विससर्ज च सायकम्॥
en: And taking it, Lakşmaņa set it on his excellent bow; and drawing the latter, vigorously discharged the shaft.

sn: पूर्णायतविसृष्टेन शरेण नतपर्वणा। ललाटे राक्षसश्रेष्ठमाजघान स वीर्यवान्।७२।।
en: That hero endowed with prowess hit that foremost of Rākşasas in the forehead with that i shaft having bent knots, discharged from his bow drawn to its full bent.

sn: स ललाटे शरो मग्नतस्य भीमस्य रक्षसः। ददृशे शोणितेनाक्तः पन्नगेन्द्र इवाचले।७३।।
en: That arrow piercing the forehead of that dreadful Raksasas, and smeared with blood, appeared like the lord of serpents in a mountain.

sn: राक्षसः प्रचकम्पेऽथ लक्ष्मणेषुप्रपीडितः। रुद्रबाणहतं घोरं यथा त्रिपुरगोपुरम्।। चिन्तयामास चाश्वस्य विमृश्य च महाबलः।७४।। साधु बाणनिपातेन श्लाघनीयोऽसि मे रिपुः।
en: The Raksasas, smarting under Laksmana's shaft, showered, like the dreadful gateway of Tripura battered by Rudra. Then recovering himself and reflecting, he said.* *Cintayāmasa-thought, I apprehend, means said in this connection.

sn: विधायैवं विदार्यास्यं विनम्य च महाभुजौ। स रथोपस्थमास्थाय रथेन प्रचचार ह!७५ ।।
en: Excellent well! By this discharge of your shaft, you approve yourself as a foe in whom I can well glory. Having spoken thus candidly, he, folding his hands at ease, and seated on the platform of his car, began to range in it.

sn: एकं त्रीपञ्च सप्तति सायकान्राक्षसर्षभः। आददे संदधे चापि विचकर्षोत्ससर्ज च।७६ ।।
en: Then that foremost of Raksasas began to take up, set and shoot one, three, five, or seven shafts.

sn: ते बाणाः कालसंकाशा राक्षसेन्द्रधनुश्च्युताः। हेमपुङ्खा रविप्रख्याश्चर्दीप्तमिवाम्बरम्॥
en: Those shafts resembling Fate itself, plated with gold at the feathered parts, and looking like the Sun himself (in splendour), discharged from the bow of the lord of Rakşasas, lighted up the heavens.

sn: ततस्ताराक्षसोत्सृष्टाशरौघानराघवानुजः। असंभ्रान्तः प्रचिच्छेद निशितैर्बहुभिः शरैः॥
en: Thereat Raghava's younger brother by means of many a sharpened shaft calmly cut off all those vollies of arrows shot by the Rakşasas.

sn: ताशरान्युधि संप्रेक्ष्य निकृत्तान्रावणात्मजः। चुकोप त्रिदशेन्द्रारिर्जग्राह निशितं शरम्॥
en: And finding all those arrows riven in the encounter, that enemy of the lord of the immortals, Ravana's son, was fired with wrath, and took up a whetted shaft.

sn: स संधाय महातेजास्तं बाणं सहसोत्सृजत्। तेन सौमित्रिमायान्तमाजघान स्तनान्तरे॥
en: Then aiming that arrow, that highly powerful one suddenly shot it; and with that, rushing on, hit Sumitra's son in the chest.

sn: अतिकायेन सौमित्रिस्ताडितो युधि वक्षसि। सुस्राव रुधिरं तीव्र मदं मत्त इव द्विपः॥
en: Struck in the encounter by Atikaya, the son of Sumitra began to bleed copiously, like a mad elephant discharging the temporal jouice.

sn: स चकार तदात्मानं विशल्यं सहसा विभुः। जग्राह च शरं तीक्ष्णमस्त्रेणापि समाददे।८।।
en: Then that lord at once extricated the arrow; and then took up a keen shaft and fixed the same on his weapon.* *i.e. the bow.

sn: आग्नेयेन तदात्रेण योजयामास सायकम्। स जज्वाल तदा बाणो धनुश्चास्य तदात्मनः॥
en: Then he set a shaft (on his bow-string) reciting a formula for the Agneya* (Belonging to the god of Fire.) weapon; and thereat his arrow as well as bow flamed up.

sn: अतिकायोऽतितेजस्वी रौद्रमलं समाददे। तेन बाणं भुजंगाभं हेमपुखमयोजयत्॥
en: Then the highly powerful Atikaya took up a Ruadra* weapon; and thereon fixed a shaft plated with gold at the feathered part, and resembling a serpent in sheen. *Relative to Rudra.

sn: तदलं ज्वलितं घोरं लक्ष्मणः शरमाहितम्। अतिकायाय चिक्षेप कालदण्डमिवान्तकः॥
en: And even as the reaper hurled his rod, did Lakşmaņa hurl that weapon inspired with divine energy, dreadful and aflame, at Atikaya.

sn: आग्नेयास्त्राभिसंयुक्तं दृष्ट्वा बाणं निशाचरः। उत्ससर्ज तदा बाणं रौद्रं सूर्यास्त्रयोजितम्॥
en: Seeing that shaft set upon an Āgneya weapon, that night-ranger discharged a Raudra arrow set upon a Solar weapon.

sn: तावुभावम्बरे बाणावन्योन्यमभिजन्नतुः। तेजसा संप्रदीप्ताग्रो कुद्धाविव भुंजगमौ।। तावन्योन्य विनिर्दह्य पेततुः पृथिवीतले॥ निरर्चिषौ भस्मकृतौ न भ्राजेते शरोत्तमौ। तावुभौ दीप्यमानौ स्म न भ्राजेते महीतले॥
en: There like a pair of infuriated serpents, those arrows with their heads flaming in energy, baffled each other in the sky. And burning each other, the shafts fell on the earth; and those best of arrows, shorn of brilliance and reduced to ashes, were deprived of their splendour. And having blazed in the welkin, those two fell down to the earth reft of their lustre.

sn: ततोऽतिकायः संक्रुद्धस्त्वाष्ट्रमैषीकमुत्सृजत्। ततश्चिच्छेद सौमित्रिरस्त्रमैन्द्रेण वीर्यवान्।॥
en: Then Atikāya wrought up with wrath discharged an arrow called Aişīka dedicated to Tvaştā. Thereat the powerful son of Sumitrā severed that shaft by an Aindra* weapon. *Belonging to Indra.

sn: ऐषीकं निहतं दृष्ट्वा कुमारो रावणात्मजः। याम्येनास्त्रेण संकुद्धो योजयामास सायकम्॥ ततस्तदत्रं चिक्षेप लक्ष्मणाय निशाचरः। वायव्येन तदत्रेण निजघान स लक्ष्मणः॥
en: Seeing Aisika baffled, that Prince-son to Rāvana-fired with rage, fixed an arrow on a Yămya' weapon; and then the night-ranger shot that weapon at Lakşmaņa. And Lakşmaņa resisted it by a Vāyavya' weapon. 1. What could this be like? The commentator is silent over this important point. 2. Belonging to the wind-god.

sn: अथैनं शरधाराभिर्धाराभिरिव तोयदः। अभ्यवर्षत संक्रुद्धो लक्ष्मणो रावणात्मजम्।१२।।
en: Then as a mass of clouds poured down showers, Laksmana, enraged, poured volleys of shafts on Rāvana's son.

sn: तेऽतिकायं समासाद्य कवचे वज्रभूषिते। भग्नाग्रशल्याः सहसा पेतुर्बाणा महीतले।१३।।
en: Thereupon, hitting Atikāya, those arrows coming in contact with his mail, had their barbs broken, and fell down to the earth.

sn: तान्मोघानभिसंप्रेक्ष्य लक्ष्मणः परवीरहा। अभ्यवर्षत बाणानां सहस्रेण महायशाः।१४।।
en: Seeing them baffled, that slayer of hostile heroes-the renowned Laksmana-began to shower shafts by thousands.

sn: स वृष्यमाणो बाणौधैरतिकायो महाबलः। अवध्यकवचः संख्ये राक्षसो नैव विव्यथे॥ न शशाक रुजं कर्तुं युधि तस्य नरोत्तमः।
en: And albeit showered with those arrows, that Raksasas, the mighty Atikāya-in that encounter was not pierced by them on account of his impenetrable mail; and that best of men failed to hurt him in the contest.

sn: अथैनमभ्युपागम्य वायुर्वाक्यमुवाच ह॥ ब्रह्मदत्तवरो ह्येष अवध्यकवचावृतः। ब्राह्मणास्त्रेण भिन्ध्येनमेष वध्यो हि नान्यथा।। अवध्य एष ह्यन्येषामस्त्राणां कवची बली॥
en: Then approaching him, the wind-god spoke to him, saying, "This one has received a boon from Brahmā, and is covered with an impenetrable mail. Pierce him with a Brahma* weapon. He cannot otherwise be slain. This one clad in mail and endowed with prowess is forsooth incapable of being slain by others." *Belonging to Brahma.

sn: ततस्तु वायोर्वचनं निशम्य सौमित्रिरिन्द्रप्रतिमानवीर्यः। समादधे बाणमथोग्रवेगं तद्ब्राह्ममस्त्रं सहसा नियुज्य।१८॥
en: Hearing the words of the wind-god, Sumitrā's son like to Indra in prowess took an arrow endowed with fierce impetuosity, and at once set it on a Brahma weapon.

sn: तस्मिन्वरास्त्रे तु नियुज्यमाने सौमित्रिणा बाणवरे शिताओ। दिशश्च चन्द्रार्कमहाग्रहाश्च नभश्च तत्रास ररास चोर्वी॥
en: On that sharp-headed best of arrows being fixed on that foremost of weapons, the cardinal quarters and the Moon and the sun and the mighty planets and the sky were saized with affright; and the earth shook.

sn: तं ब्रह्मणोऽस्त्रेण नियुज्य चापे शरं सपुवं यमदूतकल्पम्। सौमित्रिरिन्द्रारिसुतस्य तस्य ससर्ज बाणं युधि वज्रकल्पम्॥
en: And inspiring that arrow furnished with a feathered part and resembling an emissary of Yama himself, and fixing the same on his bow, Sumitrā's son in that encounter discharged that shaft like to the thunder-bolt at the son of the enemy of Indra.

sn: तं लक्ष्मणोत्सृष्टविवृद्धवेगं समापतन्तं श्वसनोग्रवेगम्। सुपर्णवज्रोत्तमचित्रपुङ्ख तदातिकायः समरे ददर्श॥
en: And in that conflict Atikāya beheld that shaft fair-feathered and having its feathered part dight with splendid diamonds, acquiring enhanced vehemence arising from its having been discharged by Lakşmaņa, and hissing and rushing on with tremendous impetuosity.

sn: तं प्रेक्षमाणः सहसातिकायो जघान बाणैनिशितैरनेकैः। स्तथातिवेगेन जगाम पार्श्वम्॥
en: Seeing it, Atikäya swiftly resisted it with countless sharpened shafts. But endowed with the energy of Suparna himself, that shaft vehemently went to him.

sn: तमागतं प्रेक्ष्य तदातिकायो बाणं प्रदीप्तान्तककालकल्पम्। जघान शक्त्यष्टिगदाकुठारैः शूलैः शरश्चाप्यविपनचेष्टः॥
en: Seeing that shaft flaming and resembling the Fatal destroyer himself, coming, he, exerting himself to the utmost resisted it with darts and Rştis and maces and adzes and javelins and arrows.

sn: तान्यायुधान्यद्भुतविग्राहणि मोघानि कृत्वा स शरोऽग्निदीपः। प्रगृह्य तस्यैव किरीटजुष्टं तदातिकायस्य शिरो जहार॥
en: But beating down all those weapons of wonderful forms, that arrow alive with flames, coming to the diadem-decked head of Atikāya, severed the same (in twain).

sn: तच्छिरः सशिरस्त्राणां लक्ष्मणेषुप्रमर्दितम्। पपात सहसा भूमौ शृङ्ग हिमवतो यथा॥
en: That head furnished with a corsalet, cut off by Laksmana's arrow, suddenly dropped to the earth, like a summit of Himavān toppling (to the ground).

sn: तं भूमौ पतितं दृष्ट्वा विक्षिप्ताम्बरभूषणम्। बभूवुर्व्यथिताः सर्वे हतशेषा निशाचराः॥
en: Seeing him rolling on the earth, with his attire and ornaments scattered about, those nightrangers that survived were overwhelmed with grief.

sn: ते विषण्णमुखा दीनाः प्रहारजनितश्रमाः। विनेदुरुच्चैर्बहवः सहसा विस्वरैः स्वरैः॥
en: And with pale forces and distressed, they, fatigued in consequence of the thrashing they had undergone, suddenly began to cry in frightful accents.

sn: ततस्तत्परितो याता निरपेक्षा निशाचराः। पुरीमभिमुखा भीता द्रवन्तो नायके हते॥
en: On their leader having been slain, those nightrangers that were about (Atikāya), without waiting any longer, overwhelmed with panic, rushed towards the city.

sn: प्रहर्षयुक्ता बहवस्तु वानराः प्रफुल्लपद्मप्रतिमाननास्तदा। अपूजयल्लक्ष्मणमिष्टभागिनं हते रिपौ भीमबले दुरासदे॥
en: On their foe endowed with terrific prowess and incapable of being conformed, having been slain, innumerable monkeys filled with excess of joy, and displaying countenances resembling blown lotuses, paid homage to Lakşmaņa working out their welfare.

sn: अतिकायं हतं श्रुत्वा लक्ष्मणेन महात्मना। उद्वेगमगमद्राजा वचनं चेदमब्रवीत्॥
en: Hearing Atikāya slain by the high-souled Lakşmaņa, the king was filled with exceeding great anxiety and spoke thus.

sn: धूम्राक्षः परमामर्षी सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वरः। अकम्पनः प्रहस्तश्च कुम्भकर्णस्तथैव च।२।। एते महाबला वीरा राक्षसा युद्धकाङ्गिणः। जेतारः परसैन्यानां परैर्नित्यापराजिताः॥ ससैन्यस्ते हता वीरा रामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा। राक्षसाः सुमहाकाया नानाशस्त्रविशारदाः।४॥
en: Dhūmråkșa exceedingly wrathful-best of those equipped with all arms—and Akampana and Prahasta and Kumbhakarņa-all these exceedingly mighty heroes— Räkșasas ever seeking warfare, conquerors of the forces of foes, and never defeated by antagonists, have together with their hosts been slain by Rāma of untiring feats.

sn: अन्ये च बहवः शूरा महात्मानो निपातिताः। प्रख्यातबलवीर्येण पुत्रेणेन्द्रजिता मम॥ तौ भ्रातरौ तदा बद्धौ घोरैर्दत्तवरैः शरैः। यन्न शक्यं सुरैः सर्वैरसुरैर्वा महाबलैः॥ मोक्तुं तद्वन्धनं घोरं यक्षगन्धर्वपत्रगैः। तन्न जाने प्रभावैर्वा मायया मोहनेन वा॥ शरबन्धाद्विमुक्तौ तौ भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ।
en: Other Rākşasas having gigantic bodies and skilled in various arms, countless high-souled heroes—have also been brought down. These brothers were formerly bound by my son Indrajit of renowned strength and prowess with terrific shafts, obtained as boons. And I do not know by what power or superhuman virtue stupefying energy did those brothers, Rāma and Lakşmaņa-liberate themselves from those dreadful bonds, which could be loosed neither by celestials nor the highly powerful Asuras combined Yaksas, Gandharvas and Pannagas.

sn: ये योधा निर्गताः शूरा राक्षसा मम शासनात्॥ ते सर्वे निहता युद्धे वानरैः सुमहाबलैः।
en: All those heroic Rākşasa warriors that marched forth at my bidding, have been destroyed by monkeys of marvellous might.

sn: तं न पश्याम्यहं युद्धे योऽद्य रामं सलक्ष्मणम्।। नाशयेत्सबलं वीरं ससुग्रीवं विभीषणम्।९।।
en: Him see I not that can now slay Rāma with Lakşmaņa, that hero together with his forces and Sugrīva and Vibhīşana.

sn: अहो सुबलवान्रामो महदस्त्रबलं च वै। यस्य विक्रममासाद्य राक्षसा निधनं गताः॥
en: Alack! mighty must be Rāma and wondrous is or nor his strength of weapon-he coming in contact with whose prowess, these Rākşasas have met with their deaths.

sn: अप्रमत्तैश्च सर्वत्र गुल्मै रक्ष्या पुरी त्वियम्। अशोकवनिका चैव यत्र सीताभिरक्ष्यते॥
en: Now let this palace be everywhere guarded by a vigilant garrison, as also the Asoka wood where Sītā is being guarded.

sn: निष्क्रमो वा प्रवेशो वा ज्ञातव्यः सर्वदैव नः। यत्र यत्र भवेद्गुल्मस्तत्र तत्र पुनः पुनः॥ सर्वतश्चापि तिष्ठध्वं सैन्यैः परिवृता बलैः। द्रष्टव्यं च पदं तेषां वानराणां निशाचराः॥ प्रदोषे वार्धरावे वा प्रत्यूषे वापि सर्वशः।
en: We should always be acquainted with the ingress and egress (of every person). And do you, surrounded by forces, remain where there are garrisons. And the night-rangers should in the evening at midnight and in the morning always watch the movements of the monkeys.

sn: नावज्ञा तत्र कर्तव्या वानरेषु कदाचन ॥ द्विषतां बलमुद्युक्तमापतत्कि स्थितं यथा।
en: The monkeys should by no means be slighted. And you should know whether the enemy put forth (fresh) efforts, and whether they advance or remain stationed where they at present are.

sn: ततस्ते राक्षसाः सर्वे श्रुत्वा लङ्काधिपस्य तत्।। वचनं सर्वमातिष्ठन्यथावत्तु महाबलाः॥
en: Thereupon hearing from the lord of Lankā those exceeding mighty Rākşasas did as they hat been desired.

sn: तान्सर्वान्हि समादिश्य रावणो राक्षसाधिपः। मन्युशल्यं वहन्दीनः प्रविवेश स्वमालयम्॥
en: Having directed them, Ravana, lord O Rākşasas, bearing the dart of ire (in his heart), i forlorn guise entered his own mansion.

sn: निशाचराणामधिपो महाबलः। तदेव पुत्रव्यसनं विचिन्तयन् मुहुर्मुहुश्चैव तदा विनिःश्वसन्॥
en: With the fire of his rage blazing up, th exceedingly powerful sovereign of the nigh rangers, absorbed with the danger that ha befallen his son, began to sigh momentarily.

sn: ततो हताराक्षसपुङ्गवांस्तान् देवान्तकादित्रिशिरोऽतिकायान्। स्ते रावणाय त्वरिताः शशंसुः॥
en: Those Raksas that remained after the others had been slain, swiftly informed Răvaņa that all those foremost of Rākşasas Devantaka and the rest, Trisiras, Atikāya and others-had been slain.

sn: ततो हतांस्तान्सहसा निशम्य राजा महाबाष्पपरिप्लुताक्षः। पुत्रक्षयं भ्रातृवधं च घोरं विचिन्त्य राजा विपुलं प्रदध्यौ॥
en: Suddenly hearing them slain, the king with his eyes charged with brine, thinking of the disastrous destruction of his sons and brothers, was extremely agonized.

sn: ततस्तु राजानमुदीक्ष्य दीनं शोकार्णवे संपरिपुप्लुवानम्। स्तमिन्द्रजिद्वाक्यमिदं बभाषे॥
en: Thereupon, seeing the king afflicted, and sunk in a sea of sorrow, that foremost of carwarriors-son to the Räkşasa king—Indrajit, addressed (his sire), saying.

sn: न तात मोहं परिगन्तुमर्हसे योन्द्रजिज्जीवति नैऋतेश। नेन्द्रारिबाणाभिहतो हि कश्चित् प्राणान्समर्थः समरेऽभिषातुम्॥
en: O father, it does not behove you to be overcome with this excessive grief, inasmuch as, O lord of Nairtas, Indrajit yet breaths. Smite by the enemy of Indra, (Rāghava) can by no means save his life in encounter.

sn: पश्याद्य रामं सह लक्ष्मणेन मद्वाणनिर्भिनविकीर्णदेहम्। गतायुषं भूमितले शयानं शितैः शरैराचितसर्वगात्रम्॥
en: To-day behold Rāma along with Lakşmaņa with their bodies torn with my shafts, lying down lifeless on the ground, having their persons covered with my sharpened arrows!

sn: इमां प्रतिज्ञां शृणु शक्रशत्रोः सुनिश्चितां पौरुषदैवयुक्ताम्। अद्यैव रामं सह लक्ष्मणेन संतर्पयिष्यामि शरैरमोथैः॥
en: Hear this vow of the foe of Indra, never swerving and instinct with prowess and divinity, this very day will I with unfailing shafts slay Rāma along with Lakşmaņa.

sn: साध्याश्च वैश्वानरचन्द्रसूर्याः। द्रक्ष्यन्तु मे विक्रममप्रमेयं विष्णोरिवोग्रं बलियज्ञवाटे।७।।
en: To-day let Indra and Vaivasvata and Vişnu and Rudra and Sādhyas and Vaiśvānaras (Agni) and the Sun and the Moon, behold my immeasurable prowess, terrific like that of Vişņu at the sacrificial ground of Vali.

sn: रापृच्छ्य राजानमदीनसत्त्वः। समारुरोहानिलतुल्यवेगं रथं स्वरश्रेष्ठसमाधियुक्तम्॥
en: Having spoken thus, that foe of the lord of celestials endowed with exceeding energy, taking the king's permission, ascended a car having the velocity of the wind itself, yoked with asses, and furnished with every variety of weapons.

sn: समास्थाय महातेजा रथं हरिरथोपमम्। जगाम सहसा तत्र यत्र युद्धमरिंदमः।।।।
en: Ascending the car, resembling the car of Hari himself, that exceedingly powerful repressor of enemies at once set out for the field of battle.

sn: तं प्रस्थितं महात्मानमनुजग्मुर्महाबलाः। संहर्षमाणा बहवो धनुःप्रवरपाणयः॥
en: As that high-souled (hero) marched, he was followed by countless mighty (Rākşasas) breathing spirits; bearing bows in their strong hands.

sn: गजस्कन्धगताः केचित्केचित्परमवाजिभिः। व्याघ्रवृश्चिकमार्जारखरोष्ट्रैश्च भुजंगमैः॥ वराहैः श्वापदैः सिंहैर्जम्बुकैः पर्वतोपमैः। काकहंसमयूरैश्च राक्षसा भीमविक्रमाः।। प्रासमुद्रनिस्त्रिंशपरश्वधगदाधराः। भुशुंडिमुद्गरायष्टिशतघ्नीपरिघायुधाः॥
en: Some of those, resembling mountains, were mounted on elephants, and some on superb steeds, and some on bears, and some on beasts of prey, and some on lions and jackals, and some of the Rākşasas endowed with dreadful vigour were mounted on crows, and some on swans, and some on peacock, they were equipped with präsas and maces and nistrinsas and axes and clubs.

sn: स शङ्खनिनदैः पूर्णैर्भेरीणां चापि नि:स्वनैः। जगाम त्रिदशेन्द्रारिराजिं वेगेन वीर्यवान् ॥
en: All sides were filled with the blares of conchs and the sounds of kettle-drums. And then that enemy of the lord of celestials marched forth with impetuosity.

sn: स शङ्खशशिवर्णेन छत्रेण रिपुसूदनः। रराज प्रतिपूर्णेन नभश्चन्द्रमसा यथा॥
en: And with an umbrella hued like the Moon, that destroyer of enemies appeared like the full Moon stationed in the sky.

sn: वीज्यमानस्ततो वीरो हैमैर्हेमविभूषणः। चारुचामरमुख्यैश्च मुख्यः सर्वधनुष्मताम्॥
en: That hero garnished in golden ornaments that foremost of all bowmen, was fanned by an excellent and graceful golden chowri.

sn: ततस्त्विन्द्रजिता लङ्का सूर्यप्रतिमतेजसा। रराजाप्रतिवीर्येण द्यौरिवार्केण भास्वता॥
en: With Indrajit furnished with the splendour of the Sun himself, and possessed of peerless prowess, Lankā looked beauteous even as the firmament graced with the glorious Sun.

sn: स संप्राप्य महातेजा युद्धभूमिमरिंदमः। स्थापयामास रक्षांसि रथं प्रति समन्ततः॥
en: Arriving at the scene of conflict, that highly powerful repressor of foes arrayed his forces around the car.

sn: ततस्तु हुतभोक्तारं हुतभुक्सदृशप्रभः। जुहुवे राक्षसश्रेष्ठो विधिवन्मन्त्रसत्तमैः॥ स हविलाजसत्कारैर्माल्यगन्धपुरस्कृतैः। जुहुवे पावकं तब राक्षसेन्द्रः प्रतापवान्॥
en: Then that foremost of Rākşasas with choice mantras duly offered libations to fire.* And that powerful lord of Rākşasas there worshipping fire with fragrant wreaths and fired paddy, sacrificed to it. *Hutabhoktāram-eater of sacrificial offerings-a designation of fire.

sn: शस्त्राणि शरपत्राणि समिधोऽथ बिभीतकाः। लोहितानि च वासांसि स्रुवं कार्णायसं तथा॥
en: Arms served for Kasa and Bibhitakas for fuel; and there were red cloths and a ladle made black iron.

sn: स तत्राग्नि समास्तीर्य शरपत्रैः सतोमरैः। छागस्य कृष्णवर्णस्य गलं जग्राह जीवतः॥
en: Spreading fire there, with tomaras representing Kāśa, he seized the neck of a living goat of black colour.

sn: सकृदेव समिद्धस्य विधूमस्य महार्चिषः। बभूवुस्तानि लिङ्गानि विजयं यान्यदर्शयन् ॥
en: Then the kindled smokeless fire blazing up brilliantly, displayed signs betokening victory.

sn: प्रदक्षिणावर्तशिखस्तप्तकांचनसंनिभः। हविस्तत्प्रतिजग्राह पावकः स्वयमुत्थितः॥
en: Thereat, with his right tongue whirling, the Deity of fire himself looking like one made of gold, arising, accepted the offering.

sn: सोऽस्त्रमाहारयामास ब्राह्मशस्त्रविशारदः। धनुश्चात्मरथं चैव सर्वं तत्राभ्यमन्त्रयत्॥
en: Then that (Rākşasa) skilled in weapons acquired a Brāhma weapon (from that deity), and inspired his bow and car with mantras.

sn: तस्मिन्नाहूयमानेऽस्त्रे हूयमाने च पावके। सार्कग्रहेन्दुनक्षत्रं वितत्रास नभःस्थलम्॥
en: On that weapon having been invoked, * and on (the god of fire) also having been worshipped, the firmament furnished with the suns and stars and planets was afflicted with affright. *i.e. on the deity presiding over that weapon, being invoked.

sn: स पावकं पावकदीप्ततेजा हुत्वा महेन्द्रप्रतिमप्रभावः। सचापबाणासिरथाश्वशूलः खेऽन्तर्दधेऽत्मानमचिन्त्यवीर्यः॥
en: Having worshipped (the god of fire), that one endowed with the splendour of fire itself, that one possessed of the prowess of the great Indra and gifted with inconceivable vigour, accoutred in bows and arrows and swords and having steeds and cars and darts, disappeared in the sky.

sn: ततो हयरथाकीर्णं पताकाध्वजशोभितम्। निर्ययौ राक्षसबलं नर्दमानं युयुत्सया॥
en: Then burning for battle, setting up roars went out the Rākşasas ranks, thronging with steeds and cars, and graced with pennons and standards.

sn: ते शरैर्बहुभिश्चित्रैस्तीक्ष्णवेगैरलंकृौः। तोमरैरङ्कुशैश्चापि वानराञ्जघ्नुराहवे॥
en: They fell to slaughtering monkeys in the engagement with countless shafts, sharp, variegated and decorated; as also with Tomaras and hooks.

sn: रावणिस्तु सुसंस्क्रुद्धस्तानिरीक्ष्य निशाचरान्। हृष्टा भवन्तो युध्यन्तु वानराणां जिघांसया॥
en: Rāvana's son, fired with wrath, seeing those night-rangers, addressed them, saying, “Do you, burning with a desire to destroy the monkeys, fight cheerfully."

sn: ततस्ते राक्षसाः सर्वे गर्जन्तो जयकाक्षिणः। अभ्यवर्षस्ततो घोरं वानराशरवृष्टिभिः॥
en: Thereat all those Raksasas, eager for victory, smiting roars, covered the dreadful monkeys with showers of shafts.

sn: स तु नालीकनाराचैर्गदाभिर्मुसलैरपि। रक्षोभिः संवृतः संख्ये वानरान्विचकर्ष ह॥
en: And environed by Rākşasas in that encounter, he* poured on the monkeys nälikas and nårācas and maces and clubs.. *Indrajit.

sn: ते वध्यमानाः समरे वानराः पादपायुधाः। अभ्यवर्षन्त सहसा रावणिं शैलपापैः॥
en: Trembling in the encounter, those monkeys armed with trees at once began to shower rocks and trees on Ravana's son.

sn: इन्द्रजित्तु तदा क्रुद्धो महातेजा महाबलः। वानराणां शरीराणि व्यधमद्रावणात्मजः॥
en: Then the exceedingly powerful Indrajit, son to Ravana, endowed with wondrous energy, pierced the bodies of the monkeys (with arrows).

sn: शरेणैकेन च हरीन्नव पञ्च च सप्त च। बिभेद समरे क्रुद्धो राक्षसान्संप्रहर्षयन्॥
en: Fired with wrath, that (hero) rejoicing the Rākṣasas with a single shaft pierced nine and seven monkeys in that encounter.

sn: स शरैः सूर्यसंकाशैः शातकुम्भविभूषणैः। वानरान्समरे वीरः प्रममाथ सुदुर्जयः॥
en: That invincible hero in that conflict mangled the monkeys with shafts resembling the Sun, decked with gold.

sn: ते भिन्नगात्राः समरे वानराः शरपीडिताः। पेतुर्मथितसंकल्पाः सुरैरिव महासुराः॥
en: Their persons pierced in that contest, and the myself pained with those arrows, they began to fall down, giving up all intention of fight, like mighty Asuras smite by the celestials.

sn: ते तपन्तमिवादित्यं घोरैर्बाणगभस्तिभिः। अभ्यधावन्त संक्रुद्धाः संयुगे वानरर्षभाः॥
en: Then waxing highly enraged, those considerable monkeys in that conflict hotly pursued (Indrajit) resembling the sun himself and having terrific arrows for his rays.

sn: ततस्तु वानराः सर्वे भिन्नदेहा विचेतसः। व्यथिता विद्रवन्ति स्म रुधिरेण समुक्षिताः॥
en: All the monkeys, with their bodies riven and deprived of their senses, and bathed in blood and writhing in torments, pursued (Indrajit).

sn: रामस्यार्थे पराक्रम्य वानरास्त्यक्तजीविताः। नर्दन्तस्तेऽनिवृत्तास्तु समरे सशिलायुधाः॥
en: Putting forth their prowess in behalf of Rama, those monkeys, equipped with rocks in the encounter, who had set apart their very lives (for him), paused, shouting up loudly.

sn: ते दुमैः पर्वताग्रैश्च शिलाभिश्च प्लवंगमाः। अभ्यवर्षन्त समरे रावणिं समवस्थिताः॥
en: They in that conflict showered trees and crags and mountain-tops on Ravana's son.

sn: तं दुमाणां शिलानां च वर्ष प्राणहरं महत्। व्यापोहत महातेजा रावणिः समितिजय॥
en: That destroyer of foes—the exceedingly energetic son to Rāvaņa resisted that mighty shower of trees and stones capable of compassing destruction.

sn: ततः पावकसंकाशैः शरैराशीविषोपमैः। वानराणामनीकानि बिभेद समरे प्रभुः॥
en: Then that lord pierced the monkey-hosts in the encounter with shafts resembling fire or venomous serpents.

sn: अष्टादशशरैस्तीक्ष्णैः स विद्ध्वा गन्धमादनम्। विव्याध नवभिश्चैव नलं दूरादवस्थितम्।॥
en: And piercing Gandhamādana with eight and ten sharp arrows, he wounded Nila stationed at a distance with nine shafts.

sn: सप्तभिस्तु महावीर्यो मैन्दं मर्मविदारणैः। पञ्चभिर्विशिशैश्चैव गजं विव्याध संयुगे॥
en: That one endowed with redoubtable prowess pierced Mainda with seven shafts capable of piercing into the pith; and he pierced Gaja with five shafts in the encounter.

sn: जाम्बवन्तं तु दशभिर्नीलं त्रिंशद्भिरेव च। सुग्रीवमृषभं चैव सोऽङ्गदं द्विविदं तथा॥
en: He pierced Jāmbavān with ten and Nīla with thirty. And then with dreadful sharp shafts obtained as boons, he rendered Sugrīva and Riş abha and Angada and Dvivida (almost) lifeless.

sn: घोरैर्दत्तवरैस्तीक्ष्णैर्निष्प्राणानकरोत्तदा। वन्यानपि तदा मुख्यान्वानरान्बहुभिः शरैः॥
en: And transported with passion, and resembling the Five arisen at doomsday, Indrajit, harassed other principal monkeys with countless arrows.

sn: अर्दयामास संक्रुद्धः कालाग्निरिव मूर्च्छितः। स शरैः सूर्यसंकाशैः सुमुक्तै शीघ्रगामिभिः॥
en: In that terrific conflict, he agitated the monkey-hosts with swift-speeding shafts, resembling the Sun himself, deftly discharged (from his bow).

sn: वानराणामनीकानि निर्ममन्थ महारणे। आकुलां वानरी सेनां शरजालेन पीडिताम्॥ हृष्टः स परया प्रीत्या ददर्श क्षतजोक्षिताम्। पुनरेव महातेजा राक्षसेन्द्रात्मजो बली॥ संसृज्य बाणवर्षं च शस्त्रवर्षं च दारुणम्। ममर्द वानरानीकं परितस्त्विन्द्रजिद्बली॥
en: In the great battle, he crushed the forces of monkeys and put them into trouble by shooting out arrows.
