Seeing the monkeys wounded he was delighted immensely and again the effulgent and foremost of Raksasas, powerful Indrajit by shooting out dreadful arrows and missiles, crushed the army of monkeys from all sides.

sn: स्वसैन्यमुत्सृज्य समेत्य तूर्णं महाहवे वानरवाहिनीषु। अदृश्यमानः शरजालमुग्रं ववर्ष नीलाम्बुधरो यथाम्बु।५१॥
en: Then in that encounter, leaving his army, Indrajit became suddenly invisible to the monkey-hosts—and began to shower fierce arrows, like dark clouds pouring rain.

sn: ते शक्रजिद्वाणविशीर्णदेहा मायाहता विस्वरमुत्रदन्तः। रणे निपेतुर्हरयोऽद्रिकल्पा यथेन्द्रवज्राभिहता नगेन्द्राः॥
en: With their persons torn by the arrows of the conqueror of Sakra, slain by his power of illusion, with their teeth uprooted, those mountain-like monkeys fell down in the field, emitting frightful cries, like a mountain smite with Indra's thunderbolt.

sn: ते केवलं संददृशुः शिताग्रान् बाणारणे वानरवाहिनीषु। मायाविगूढं च सुरेन्द्रशत्रु न चात्र तं राक्षससम्पपश्यन्।५३ ।।
en: In the conflict they could only see sharp pointed shafts among the monkey-ranks, but that foe of the celestial chief-the Raksasas, hidden by virtue of illusion, they could not discover there.

sn: ततः स रक्षोधिपतिर्महात्मा सर्वा दिशो बाणगतैः शिताग्रैः। विदारयामास च वानरेन्द्रान्॥
en: Then the high-souled lord of Rākṣasa covered all sides with sharp-pointed shafts resembling the rays of the sun; and he rived the foremost monkeys.

sn: स शूलनिस्त्रिंशपरश्वधानि व्याविद्धदीप्तानलसप्रभाणि। सविस्फुलिङ्गोज्ज्वलपावकानि ववर्ष तीव्र प्लवगेन्द्रसैन्ये॥
en: And whirling darts and nistraišas and axes, flaming and having the effulgence of fire, and furnished with flames shooting forth sparks, he discharged them furiously at the forces of the sovereign of monkeys.

sn: ततो ज्वलनसंकाशैर्बाणैर्वानरयूथपाः। ताडिताः शक्रजिद्बाणैः प्रफुल्ला इव किंशुकाः॥
en: The monkey-leaders struck with Śakrajit's shafts. resembling flames, appeared like laughing Kinsukas.

sn: तेऽन्योऽन्यमभि सर्पन्तो निनदन्तश्च विस्वरम्। राक्षसेन्द्रास्त्रनिर्भिन्ना निपेतुर्वानरर्षभाः।
en: They foremost of Vānaras, pierced by the missiles of the lord of Raksasas gliding towards one another and crying bitterly fell down on earth.

sn: उदीक्षमाणा गगनं केच्चिनेत्रेषु ताडिताः। शनैर्विविशुरन्योन्यं पेतुश्च जगतीतले॥
en: Some looking at the sky were struck at their eyes. They gradually began to hide themselves in each other and drop to the earth.

sn: हनूमन्तं च सुग्रीवमङ्गदं गन्धमादनम्। जाम्बवन्तं सुषेणं च वेगदर्शिनमेव च॥ मैन्दं च द्विविदं नीलं गवाक्षं गवयं तथा। केसरि हरिलोमानं विद्युदंष्ट्रं च वानरम्॥ सूर्याननं ज्योतिमुखं तथा दधिमुखं हरिम्। पावकाक्षं नलं चैव कुमुदं चैव वानरम्॥ प्रासैः शूलैः शितैर्बाणैरिन्द्रजिन्मन्त्रसंहितैः। विव्याध हरिशार्दूलान्सांस्ताराक्षसोत्तमः॥
en: That foremost of Raksasas-Indrajit-with präsas and darts and whetted arrows, inspired with mantras, pierced all those powerful monkeys, Hanuman and Sugrīva and Angada and Gandhạmādana and Jämbhavān and Sușeņa and Vegadarsin, and Mainda and Dvivida and Nīla and Gavākṣa and Gavaya and Kesari and Hariloman and the monkey Vidyutdanshtra and Suryyānana and Jyotimukha and the monkey Dadhimukha and Pāvakākṣa and Nala and the monkey Kumuda.

sn: निर्भिद्य बाणैस्तपनीयवर्णैः। ववर्ष राम शरवृष्टिजालैः सलक्ष्मणं भास्कररश्मिकल्पैः॥
en: Having pierced those foremost monkeys with golden-hued maces, he showered on Rāma and Lakşmaņa arrows resembling the rays of the sun.

sn: स बाणव(रभिवृष्यमाणो धारानिपातानिव तानचिन्त्य। समीक्षमाणः परमाद्भुतश्री रामस्ततो लक्ष्मणमित्युवाच ॥
en: And showered with those vollies of arrows, Rāma, without heeding that discharge resembling a very downpour, reflecting, spoke to Laksmana.

sn: असौ पुनर्लक्ष्मण राक्षसेन्द्रो महास्त्रमाश्रित्य सुरेन्द्रशत्रुः। शितैः शरैरर्दयति प्रसक्तम्॥
en: O Lakşmaņa, this lord of Rākşasas, this foe of the lord of celestials, having obtained the Brāhma weapon, after having brought down the monkey-hosts, are assailing us with sharpened shafts.

sn: स्वयंभुवा दत्तवरो महात्मा समाहितोऽन्तर्हितभीमकायः। कथं नु शक्यो युधि नष्टदेहो निहन्तुमद्येन्द्रजिदुद्यतास्त्रः॥
en: That high-souled heedful one, having been given a boon by the self-sprung, has rendered his dreadful body invisible. How can we slay him, who is fighting with upraised weapons, but who has hid his body.

sn: स्तस्यैतदत्रं प्रभवश्च योऽस्य। बाणावपातं त्वमिहाद्य धीमन् मया सहाव्यग्रमनाः सहस्वा६६॥
en: The reverend self-sprung, I deem, is incomprehensible. And this is his weapon, embodying his energy. Therefore, O intelligent one, do you today along with me calmly bear this.

sn: प्रच्छादयत्वेष हि राक्षसेन्द्रः सर्वाधिकः सायकवृष्टिजालैः। एतच्च सर्व पतिताग्र्यशूरं न भ्राजते वानरराजसैन्यम्॥
en: Let this foremost of them all, this lord of Rāks asas-cover all sides with the showers of his shafts. And in consequence of this, the army of the monkey-king with its greatest heroes fallen, does not appear to advantage.

sn: आवां तु दृष्ट्वा पतितौ विसंज्ञौ निवृत्तयुद्धौ हतहर्षरोषौ। मसौ समासाद्य रणाग्र्यलक्ष्मीम्॥
en: Seeing us also fallen, senseless, and desisting from fight with our joy and anger gone off from us, for certain will the enemy of the immortals, taking the Fortune of fight seek his home.

sn: र्बभूवतुस्तत्र तदा विशस्तौ। स चापि तौ तत्र विषादयित्वा ननाद हर्षाधुधि राक्षसेन्द्रः॥
en: Assailed by Indrajit with networks of arrows, they were then sore distressed in the field. And having struck them with sadness, Indrajit from joy shouted in the encounter.

sn: ततस्तदा वानरसैन्यमेवं रामं च संख्ये सह लक्ष्मणेन। विषूदयित्वा सहसा विवेश पुरी दशग्रीवभुजाभिगुप्ताम्।। संस्तूयमानः स तु यातुधानैः पित्रे च सर्वं हृषितोऽभ्युवाच॥
en: Having thus worsted in battle that monkey army and Rāma along with Lakşmaņa, he-speedily entered the city ruled by the hand of the Ten-necked one. And extolled by the Yatudhānas, he, filled with delight, related everything to his sire.

sn: तयोस्तदासादितयो रणाग्रे मुमोह सैन्यं हरियूथपानाम्। सुग्रीवनीलाङ्गदजाम्बवन्तो न चापि किंचित्प्रतिपेदिरे ते॥
en: They were rendered inert in the field; and the army of the monkey-leaders was stupefied, with Sugrīva and Nīla and Angada and Jāmbavān, and they did not show any signs of activity.

sn: ततो विषण्णं समवेक्ष्यं सर्व विभीषणो बुद्धिमतां वरिष्ठः। नाश्वासयन्त्रप्रतिमैर्वचोभिः॥
en: Thereupon, seeing them dispirited, that foremost of intelligent persons, Vibhisana, cheering them up with his peerless speech, said.

sn: मा भैष्ट नास्त्यत्र विषादकालो यदार्यपुत्रौ ह्यवशौ विषण्णौ। स्वयंभुवो वाक्यमथोद्वहन्तौ यत्सादिताविन्द्रजितास्त्रजालैः॥
en: You heroes of the king of monkeys, do not give way to fear. This is not the time to indulge in grief at this place; for the sons of that noble one,' inactive and depressed, and seeming to be wounded with the showers of Indrajit's shafts, are in reality in this plight, for showing reverence to the words of the self-sprung one. 1. Dasaratha. 2.Mantra.

sn: स्वयंभुवा ब्राह्मममोघवीर्यम्। तन्मानयन्तौ युधि राजपुत्रौ निपातितौ कोऽत्र विषादकालः।४।।
en: On him the self-sprung has conferred the mighty Brahmă weapon of unfailing power; and the king's sons are doing honour to it by lying down on the field of battle. Why then do you grieve now?

sn: ब्रह्ममत्रं ततो धीमान्मानयित्वा तु मारुतिः। विभीषणवचः श्रुत्वा हनूमानिदमब्रवीत्॥
en: Hearing the words of Vibhisana and honouring the Brahma weapon, Hanumăn spoke as follows.

sn: अस्मित्रत्रहते सैन्ये वानराणां तरस्विनाम्। यो यो धारयते प्राणांस्तं तमाश्वासयावहे॥
en: The host of the quick-paced monkeys has been slain by this weapon. Let us go and console them who are still living.

sn: तावुभौ युगपद्वीरौ हनूमद्राक्षसोत्तमौ। उल्काहस्तौ तदा रात्रौ रणशीर्षे विचेरतुः॥
en: Those two great heroes— Hanumān and that foremost of the Rakşasas, with fire-brands in their hands, began to range to and fro in the battle field.

sn: भिन्नलालहस्तोरुपादाङ्गुलिशिरोधरैः। स्रवद्भिः क्षतजं गात्रैः प्रस्रवद्भिः समन्ततः॥ पतितैः पर्वताकारैर्वानरैरभिसंवृताम्। शस्त्रैश्च पतितैर्दीप्तैर्ददृशाते वसुंधराम्॥
en: They beheld there the earth strewn on all sides with monkeys lying down like so many hills and various shining weapons. And some of these monkeys were deprived of their tails, some of their hands, some of their thighs, some of their legs, some of their fingers, and some of their heads. And blood was gushing out from the persons of some, and others were urinating out of fear.

sn: सुग्रीवमङ्गदं नीलं शरभं गन्धमादनम्। जाम्बवन्तं सुषेणं च वेगदर्शिनमेव च॥ मैन्दं नलं ज्योतिमुखं द्विविदं चापि वानरम्। विभीषणो हनूमांश्च ददृशाते हतारणे॥
en: Vibhīşaņa and Hanuman beheld there Sugriva, Angada Nila, Gandhamādana, Jambhavan, Susena, Vegadarshin, Mainda, Nala, Jyotimukha, and the monkey, Dvivida, almost slain.

sn: सप्तषष्टिर्हता: कोट्यो वानराणां तरस्विनाम्। अह्नः पञ्चमशेषेण वल्लभेन स्वयम्भुवः॥
en: Vibhișana and Hanuman saw in the field seven and sixty kotis of fleet-footing monkeys slain (in battle) at the fifth part of the day by the darling of the self-sprung.

sn: सागरौघनिभं भीमं दृष्ट्वा बाणादितं बलम्। मार्गते जाम्बवन्तं च हनूमान्सविभीषणः॥
en: And surveying that host worsted, dreadful like the surges of the sea, Hanumăn and Vibhīşaņa began to search for Jāmbavān.

sn: स्वभावजरया युक्तं वृद्धं शरशतैश्चितम्। प्रजापतिसुतं वीरं शाम्यन्तमिव पावकम्॥ दृष्ट्वा समभिसंक्रम्य पौलस्त्यो वाक्यमब्रवीत्। कश्चिदार्यशरैस्तीक्ष्णैर्न प्राणा ध्वंसितास्तव ॥
en: Finding that heroic son of Prajāpati, afflicted with natural decrepitude, aged, and resembling smouldering fire, wounded with hundreds of shafts, Pulastya's son said, “O noble one, has not your life been destroyed with those sharp shafts?"

sn: विभीषणवचः श्रुत्वा जाम्बवानृक्षपुङ्गवः। कृच्छादब्युद्गिरन्वाक्यमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Hearing Vibhisana's words, Jambevan, best of bears, evoking utterance with extreme effort, said.

sn: नैऋतेन्द्र महावीर्य स्वरेण त्वाभिलक्षये। विद्धगात्रः शितैर्बाणैर्न त्वां पश्यामि चक्षुषा॥
en: O foremost of Naiſtas, endowed with exceeding prowess, I know you by your voice. Having my person pierced with sharp shafts, I cannot see you with my eyes.

sn: अञ्जना सुप्रजा येन मातरिश्वा च सुव्रत। हनूमान्वानरश्रेष्ठः प्राणान्धारयते क्वचित्॥
en: Does he through whom Añjanä as well as Mātariśvan* are blessed with fair offspring, does that prince of monkeys-Hanumān, live? *The wind-god.

sn: श्रुत्वा जाम्बवतो वाक्यमुवाचेदं विभीषणः। आर्यपुत्रावतिक्रम्य कस्मात्पृच्छसि मारुतिम्॥
en: Hearing Jambavan's speech, Vibhisana said, “Why, passing by the son of the high and mighty,* did you enquire after the wind-god's offsprmg? *Vide Hamlet.

sn: नैव राजनि सुग्रीवे नाङ्गदे नापि राघवे। आर्य संदर्शितः स्नेहो यथा वायुसुते परः॥
en: O noble one, you did not show that overflowing affection either for king Sugrīva or Angada and Raghava that you show for the son of the wind-god.

sn: विभीषणवचः श्रुत्वा जाम्बवान्वाक्यमब्रवीत्। शृणु नैर्ऋतशार्दूल यस्मात्पृच्छामि मारुतिम्॥
en: Hearing Vibhisana's words, Jambavan said, "Hear, O foremost of Raksasas, why I enquire after the wind-god's son.

sn: अस्मिञ्जीवति वीरे तु हतमप्यहतं बलम्। हनूमत्युज्झितप्राणे जीवन्तोऽपि मृता वयम्॥
en: While this hero is alive, this force, albeit destroyed, live; but if Hanumān is reft of life, although living, we are destroyed.

sn: धरते मारुतिस्तात मारुतप्रतिमो यदि। वैश्वानरसमो वीर्ये जीविताशा ततो भवेत्॥
en: O child, if the wind-god's offspring, resembling his sire himself or (the deity of) fire in prowess, is alive, there is hope for our lives.

sn: ततो वृद्धमुपागम्य विनयेनाभ्यवादयत्। गृह्य जाम्बवतः पादौ हनूमान्मारुतात्मजः॥
en: Then approaching that aged one, Hanumanson to the wind-god-saluted him humbly, holding Jāmbavān's feet.

sn: श्रुत्वा हनूमतो वाक्यं तदा विव्यथितेन्द्रियः। पुनर्जातमिवात्मानं मन्यते प्लवगोत्तमः॥
en: Hearing Hanuman's voice, that foremost of monkeys with his senses sorely smarting, deemed himself as having regained his life.

sn: ततोऽब्रवीन्महातेजा हनूमन्तं स जाम्बवान्। आगच्छ हरिशार्दूल वानरांस्त्रातुमर्हसि ॥
en: Then that exceedingly energetic Jåmbavān addressed Hanumān, saying, “Come, O powerful monkey, It behove you to rescue the monkeys."

sn: नान्यो विक्रमपर्याप्तस्त्वमेषां परमः सखा। त्वत्पराक्रमकालोऽयं नान्यं पश्यामि कंचन ॥
en: There is none else. Endowed with profuse prowess, you are the greatest friend of these. This is the hour when you should display you might. Any other see I not.

sn: ऋक्षवानरवीराणामनीकानि प्रहर्षय। विशल्यौ कुरु चाप्येतौ सादितौ रामलक्ष्मणौ॥
en: Do you cheer up this host consisting of bears and monkeys; and do you also heal the wounds of these two tormented by them.

sn: गत्वा परममध्वानमुपर्युपरि सागरम्। हिमवन्तं नगश्रेष्ठं हनूमन्गन्तुमर्हसि॥
en: Bounding sheer over the main, you, O Hanumān, should repair to the Himavānforemost of mountains.

sn: ततः काञ्चनमत्युग्रमृषभं पर्वतोत्तमम्। कैलासशिखरं चात्र द्रक्ष्यस्यरिनिषूदन ॥
en: There you will see that best of mountiansthe golden Rşabha of terrific aspect, and, O smiter of foes, the peak also of Kailāśa.

sn: तयोः शिखरयोर्मध्ये प्रदीप्तमतुलप्रभम्। सौषधियुतं वीर द्रक्षस्योषधिपर्वतम्॥
en: Lying in the lap of these two, you, O hero, O powerful monkey, will see the mountain of medicines, fraught with healing herbs of all kinds.

sn: तस्य वानरशार्दूल चतस्रो मूर्ध्नि संभवाः। द्रक्षस्योषधयो दीप्ता दीपयन्तीदिशो दश॥ मृतसंजीवनीं चैव विशल्यकरणीमपि। सुवर्णकरणीं चैव संधानी च महौषधीम्॥
en: On its summit you will find four medicinal herbs flaming and illumining the ten cardinal quarters-viz., Mſtasanjivani,' Višalyakarani, Suvarnakarani, and the mighty medicine, Sandhănī. 1. Lit. reviving the dead. 2. Lit. healing wounds inflicted by darts. 3. Lit. transmuting any thing to gold.

sn: ताः सर्वा हनुमन्गृह्य क्षिप्रमागन्तुमर्हसि। आश्वासय हरीन्प्राणैर्योज्य गन्धवहात्मज ॥
en: O Hanumān, providing yourself with these, you should come here without delay. Do you, O offspring of the wind-god* bringing back lives to these monkeys, cheer them up. *Gandhavahātanaya-lit., son to the bearer of smell-a designation of the wind in Sanskrit.

sn: श्रुत्वा जाम्बवतो वाक्यं हनूमान्मारुतात्मजः। आपूर्यत बलोद्धर्वायुवेगैरिवार्णवः॥
en: Thereat hearing the words of Jāmbavān Hanumān, son of wind-god filled himself with energy, even as the Ocean heave with the force of the winds (blowing on its breast).

sn: स पर्वततटाग्रस्थः पीडयन्पर्वतोत्तमम्। हनूमान्दृश्यते वीरो द्वितीय इव पर्वतः॥
en: Ascending the summit of that mountain,* and hurting it with his tread, that hero-Hanumanappeared like a second mountain. *Trikuta.

sn: हरिपादविनिर्भग्नो निषसाद स पर्वतः। न शशाक तदात्मानं वोढुं भृशनिपीडितः॥
en: Crushed under the tread of that monkey, the mountain was dispirited; and sore distressed, it could hardly contain itself.

sn: तस्य पेतुर्नगा भूमौ हरिवेगाच्च जज्वलुः। शृङ्गाणि च व्यकीर्यन्त पीडितस्य हनूमता ॥ तस्मिन्संपीड्यमाने तु भग्नद्रुमशिलातले। न शेकुर्वानराः स्थातुं घूर्णमाने नगोत्तमे॥
en: The trees on it began to topple to the earth; and on account of the vehemence of the monkey, they flamed up. And smitten by Hanumān, its peaks were scattered around. And monkeys could no longer dwell on that fore. Most of mountains, which being hard pressed (by Hanumān), was trembling all over, with its slopes covered with broken trees and rocks.

sn: सा घूर्णितमहाद्वारा प्रभग्नगृहगोपुरा। लङ्का त्रासाकुला रात्रौ प्रनृत्येवाभवत्तदा॥
en: With her giant gateways shaking, and the doors of her edifices broken, that night Lankā, over-whelmed with fright, seemed to be dancing.

sn: पृथिवीधरसंकाशो निपीड्य पृथिवीधरम्। पृथिवीं क्षोभयामास सार्णवां मारुतात्मजः॥
en: The offspring of the wind-god, resembling a mountain itself, bringing that mountain to sore straits, agitated the entire earth with her oceans.

sn: पद्भ्यां तु शैलमाविध्य वडवामुखवन्मुखम्। विवृत्योग्रं ननादोच्वैस्वासयन्रजनीचरान्।॥
en: And hurting the mountain with his tread, he, opening wide his mouth resembling that of a mare, sent up loud shouts, terrifying the nightrangers.

sn: तस्य नानद्यमानस्य श्रुत्वा निनदमुत्तमम्। लङ्कास्था राक्षसव्याघ्रा न शेकुः स्पन्दितुं क्वचित्॥
en: Hearing those tremendous roars as he kept emitting cries, the powerful Rākṣasas were quite stupified.

sn: नमस्कृत्वा समुद्राय मारुतिर्भीमविक्रमः। राघवार्थे परं कर्म समीहत परंतपः॥
en: Bowing down to the Ocean, that subduer of enemies, the Wind-god's son, endowed with dreadful prowess, began to ponder over the mighty mission with which he had been entrusted in the interests of Rāghava.

sn: स पुच्छमुद्यम्य भुजंगकल्पं विनम्य पृष्ठं श्रवणे निकुच्य। मापुप्लुवे व्योम्नि च चण्डवेगः॥
en: Then upraising his tail resembling a serpent, bending his back, contracting his ears, and opening his mouth looking like that of a mare, that one possessed of terrific impetuosity, bounded into the sky.

sn: स वृक्षखण्डांस्तरसा जहार शैलाशिलाः प्राकृतवानरांश्च । स्ते क्षीणवेगाः सलिले निपेतुः॥
en: With the vehemence of his rush, he carried away in his wake whole tracts of trees, and rocks, and crags, and inferior monkeys;* and after having been carried away some distance by the vehemence of his arms and thighs, they, at length losing their velocity, fell into the waters (of the Ocean.) *Residing in the Trikuta mountain.

sn: स तौ प्रसार्योरगभोगकल्पौ भुजौ भुजंगारिनिकाशवीर्यः। जगाम शैलं नगराजमग्र्यं दिशः प्रकर्षनिव वायुसूनुः॥
en: Stretching his arms resembling serpents, the son of the Wind-god endowed with the prowess of Garuda* coursed on towards the monarch of mountains, as if making all the quarters tremble. *The text has, the foe of serpents—an appellation of Garuda

sn: स सागरं घूर्णितवीचिमालं तदम्भसा भ्रामितसर्वसत्त्वम्। समीक्षमाणः सहसा जगाम चक्रं यथा विष्णुकरारमुक्तम्॥
en: Seeing the sea with its hosts of billows rolling furiously and with the confederacies of aquatic animals bewildered by the angry waters, he coursed on rapidly, like the discus discharged by the hand of Vişnu.

sn: स पर्वतान्पक्षिगणान्सरांसि नदीस्तटाकानि पुरोत्तमानि। स्फीताञ्जनांस्तानपि संप्रवीक्ष्य जगाम वेगापितृतुल्यवेगः॥
en: Surveying hills and birds and pools and rivers and tanks and splendid cities and flourishing provinces, that one equal to his sire himself in celerity, held his way.

sn: आदित्यपथमाश्रित्य जगाम स गतश्रमः। हनूमांस्त्वरितो वीरः पितुस्तुल्यपराक्रमः॥
en: That hero Hanuman—like to his father in prowess, and incapable of being fatigued, vigorously proceeded along the orbit of the sun.

sn: जवेन महता युक्तो मारुतितिरंहसा। जगाम हरिशार्दूलो दिशः शब्देन नादयन्।५१।।
en: That powerful monkey possessed of the speed of the Wind itself, and having mighty impetuosity, careered, making all sides resound with his roars.

sn: स्मरञ्जाम्बवतो वाक्यं मारुतिर्भीमविक्रमः। ददर्श सहसा चापि हिमवन्तं महाकपिः।१२।। नानाप्रस्रवणोपेतं बहुकंदरनिर्झरम्। श्वेताभ्रश्यसंकाशैः शिखरैश्चारुदर्शनैः।। शोभितं विविधैर्वृक्षरगमत्पर्वतोचमम्॥
en: Remembering Jāmbavān's words, that redoubtable monkey, son to the Wind-god, possessed of terrific prowess, and resembling a mountain, suddenly saw (before him) the Himavān; furnished with countless cascades and numerous caves and rivulets; with splendid summits appearing like massess of pale clouds, and graced with various trees.

sn: मतिप्रवृद्धोत्तमहेमशृङ्गम्। ददर्श पुण्यानि महाश्रमाणि सुरर्षिसङ्घोत्तमसेवितानि॥
en: Arriving at that lord of mighty mountains, furnished with excellent towering golden summits, he saw the great sacred asylums (of the ascetics), inhabited by the flower of celestial saints.

sn: स ब्रह्मकोशं रजतालयं च शक्रालयं रुद्रशरप्रमोक्षम्। हयाननं ब्रह्मशिरश्च दीप्तं ददर्श वैवस्वतकिंकरांश्च ॥
en: He beheld Brahmakosa (a) Rajatalaya (b) Śakrālaya (c) Rudraśarapramokṣa (d) Hayānana (e) and the flaming Brahmasiras (f) and the servants of Vaivasvata (g). (a) The place of Hiranyagarbha (b) The place of Rajatanăbha— silver-neededanother from of Hiranyagarbha (c) The abode of Sakra. (d) The place where from Rudra discharged his arrow on the occasion of the destruction of Tripurā (e) Theplace of the horse-necked. (f) The place of the deity presiding ever the Brahma-weapon. (g) An appellation of Yama.

sn: वयालयं वैश्रवणालयं च सूर्यप्रभं सूर्यनिबन्धनं च। ब्रह्मालयं शंकरकार्मुकं च ददर्श नाभिं च वसुंधरायाः।५६।। कैलासमुग्रं हिमवच्छिलां च तं वै वृषं काञ्चनशैलमग्र्यम्। प्रदीप्तसौषधिसंप्रदीप्तं ददर्श सौषधिपर्वतेन्द्रम्॥
en: He saw the abode of the Fire-god, and the abode of Vaiśravana and the effulgent suryyanivandhana, (h) and the abode of Brahmă, (i) and the bow of Sankara, and the navel of the Earth. (j) And he saw Kailasa of terrific aspect, and the stone, (k) of Himavăn, and that bull, (1) and the golden mountain, and that foremost of mountains furnished with all medicinal herbs, flaming, and illuminated with every kind of medicinal plants. (h) The spot where the suns meet. (i) The place of the four-faced Brahmă. (i) The spot of Prajāpati. (k) On which Rudra sat when engaged in asceticism. (1) Which had been mentioned by Jambavan.

sn: स तं समीक्ष्यानलराशिदीप्तं विसिष्मिये वासवदूतसूनुः। आप्लुत्य तं चौषधिपर्वतेन्द्र तत्रौषधीनां विचयं चकार॥
en: Beholding that flaming mass of fire, the offspring of Vasava's* emissary wondered. And bounding up to the lord of medicinal mountains, he fell to searching for the drugs. * The emissary of Vāsavain his cloud-from is the wind driving the cloud; and the passage refers to Hanuman,

sn: स योजनसहस्राणि समतीत्य महाकपिः। दिव्यौषधिधरं शैलं व्यचरन्मारुतात्मजः॥
en: That mighty monkey-the Wind-god's son-leaving behind a thousand Yojanas, began to range the mountain containing the divine remedies in its entrails.

sn: महौषध्यस्ततः सर्वास्तस्मिन्पर्वतसत्तमे। विज्ञायार्थिनमायान्तं ततो जग्मुरदर्शनम्॥
en: Those potent medicines, in that foremost of mountains, knowing (before-hand) that one was coming seeking for them, rendered themselves invisible.

sn: श्चुकोप रोषाच्च भृशं ननाद। महीधरेन्द्र तमुवाच वाक्यम्॥
en: And not seeing them, the high-souled Hanumān was angered; and from wrath he set up roars. And not brooking that, (Hanumān) with eyes resembling glowing fire, addressed that foremost of mountains, saying.

sn: किमेतदेवं सुविनिश्चितं ते यद्राघवेनासि कृतानुकम्पः। पश्याद्य मद्बाहुबलाभिभूतो विकीर्णमात्मानमथो नगेन्द्र॥
en: What is ihis that you have decided on, that you show no compassion for Rāghava? But, O lord of mountains, today witness yourself, overpowered by my arms and torn in pieces!

sn: स तस्य शृङ्ग सनगं सनागं सकाञ्चनं धातुसहस्त्रजुष्टम्। विकीर्णकूटं ज्वलिताग्रसार्नु प्रगृह्य वेगात्सहसोन्ममाथ॥
en: And (anon) on a sudden, he violently rooted up its summit with trees and elephants and gold, and furnished with thousand varieties of ore, having its tops torn and its slopes aflame.

sn: स तं समुत्पाट्य खमुत्पपात चित्रास्य लोकान्ससुरान्सुरेन्द्रान्। जंगाम वेगाद्गरुडोग्रवेगः॥ स्तं भास्काराभं शिखरं प्रगृह्य । बभौ तदा भास्करसंनिकाशो रवेः समीपे प्रतिभास्कराभः॥
en: And uprooting it, he sprang into the bosom of the air), terrifying the worlds containing celestials and the lords thereof. And hymned by countless rangers of the air, that one endowed with the terrific impetuosity of Garuda himself, taking that summit furnished with the splendour of the Sun, went along the orbit of the Sun. And near the Sun, that Sun-like one seemed to be another sun.

sn: स तेन शैलेन भृशं रराज शैलोपमो गन्धवाहत्मजस्तु। सहस्रधारेण सपावकेन चक्रेण खे विष्णुरिवार्पितेन॥
en: With that mountain, the offspring of the bearer of perfumes appeared surpassingly grand, like very Vişņu equipped with the flaming discus having a thousand edges.

sn: तं वानराः प्रेक्ष्य तदा विनेदुः स तानपि प्रेक्ष्य मुदा ननाद। तेषां समुत्कृष्टरवं निशम्य लङ्कालया भीमतरं विनेदुः॥ स्युः।
en: Seeing him, the monkeys shouted, and he also, seeing them, shouted in delight. And hearing their tremendous cheers, those residing in Lankā shouted still more dreadfully.

sn: ततो महात्मा निपपात तस्मिन् शैलोत्तये वानरसैन्यमध्ये। हर्युत्तमेभ्यः शिरसाभिवाद्य विभीषणं तत्र च सस्वजे सः॥
en: Then the high-souled one dropped on that best of mountains in the midst of the monkey-forces; and, bowing down to the principal monkeys there, he embraced Vibhisana.

sn: तावप्युभौ मानुषराजपुत्रौ तं गन्धमाघ्राय महौषधीनाम्। वुत्तस्थुरन्ये च हरिप्रवीराः॥ सर्वे विशल्या विरुजाः क्षणेन हरिप्रवीराश्च हताश्च ये गन्धेन तासां प्रवरोषधीनां सुप्ता निशान्तेष्विव संप्रबुद्धाः। ७०।।
en: Then those sons of that king of men, smelling the perfume of that mighty medicine, were then and there healed of their wounds; and the heroic monkeys also sat up. And all the heroic monkeys were instantly healed and cured; and those also that were slain (in battle), through the smell of that best of drugs, sat up, like persons risen after sleep at break of day.

sn: यदा प्रभृति लङ्कायां युध्यन्ते हरिराक्षसाः। यदा प्रभृति मानार्थमाज्ञया रावणस्य च।७१।। ये हन्यन्ते रणे तत्र राक्षसाः कपिकुञ्जरैः। हता हतास्तु क्षिप्यन्ते सर्व एव तु सागरे॥
en: Even since the monkeys and Rākşasas had began to fight; for maintaining honour, all those Rākşasas that were slain there by the mighty monkeys, were thrown into the sea.

sn: ततो हरिर्गन्धवहात्मजस्तु तमोषधीशैलमुदग्रवेगः। निनाय वेगाद्धिमवन्तमेव पुनश्च रामेण समाजगाम।७३ ।।
en: Then that monkey, the offspring of the bearer of fragrance, endowed with terrific speed, took that medicinal mountain (back) to Himavān and again presented himself before Rāma.

sn: ततोऽब्रवीन्महातेजाः सुग्रीवो वानरेश्वरः। अयं विज्ञापयंश्चापि हनूमन्तमिदं वचः॥
en: Then the exceedingly energetic lord of monkeys, Sugrīva, said to Hanumān these words fraught with import,

sn: यतो हतः कुम्भकर्णः कुमाराश्च निषूदिताः। नेदानीमुपनिरिं रावणो दातुमर्हति ॥
en: Inasmuch as Kumbhakarma has been slain as also the princes,' Rāvana can no longer defend the city.

sn: ये ये महाबलाः सन्ति लघवश्च प्लवंगमाः। लङ्कामभिपतन्त्वाशु गृह्योल्काः प्लवगर्षभाः॥
en: Now let those principal monkeys that are endowed with great strength and that are furnished with fleetness, taking fire-brands (in their hands) rapidly rush towards Lankā.

sn: ततोऽस्तं गत आदित्ये रौद्रे तस्मिन्निशामुखे। लङ्कामभिमुखाः सोल्का जग्मुस्ते प्लवगर्षभाः॥
en: Then when the Sun had set and at the terrific front of Night, those foremost of monkeys marched towards Larikā, equipped with firebrands.

sn: उल्काहस्तैहरिगणैः सर्वतः समभिदुताः। आरक्षस्था विरूपाक्षाः सहसा विप्रदुद्रुवुः।५।।
en: Charged at all points by nur bers of monkeys armed with fire-brands, those firece-eyed (Rākş asas) that guarded the gates.* suddenly fled away. *Araksasthā-according to some means gates. According to others, a gulma or division of an army.

sn: गोपुराट्टप्रतोलीषु चर्यासु विविधासु च। प्रासादेषु च संहृष्टाः ससृजुस्ते हुताशनम्॥
en: Thereat (the monkeys) delighted set fire to gates and upper apartments and spacious highways and various by-ways and edifices.

sn: तेषां गृहसहस्राणि ददाह हुतभुक्तदा।। प्रासादाः पर्वताकाराः पतन्ति धरणीतले।७।।
en: The fire' burnt their mansions by thousands; and mountain-like superstructures toppled headiong to the earth. 1. Hutabhuk-lit. eater of sacrificial offspring's, a designation of fire. 2. According to the commentator this refers to the fire lighted by the monkeys. I differ.

sn: अगुरुर्दह्यते तत्र परं चैव सुचन्दनम्। मौक्तिका मणयः स्निग्धा वजं चापि प्रवालकम्।८।।
en: There burnt aguru, and sweet sandal, and pearls, and sheeny gems, and diamonds and corals.

sn: क्षौमं च दह्यते तत्र कौशेयं चापि शोभनम् । आविकं विविधं चौर्ण काश्चनं भाण्डमायुधम्।९।। नानाविकृतसंस्थानं वाजिभाण्डपरिच्छदम्। गजौवेयकक्ष्याश्च रथभाण्डांश्च संस्कृतान्॥ तनुत्राणि च योधानां हस्त्यश्वानां च चर्म च।
en: There burnt linen and fine silk and avikas and various kinds of woollen cloths; and vessels of gold, and weapons; divers kinds of furniture, trappings and omaments of steeds; cords for tying elephants; burnished ornaments for cars; armour of warriors; and hides of horses and elephants.

sn: खड्गा धनूंषि ज्याबाणास्तोमराङ्कुशशक्तयः॥ रोमजं वालजं चर्म व्याघ्रजं चाण्डजं बहु। मुक्तामणिविचित्रांश्च प्रासादांश्च समन्ततः॥ विविधानत्रसंघातानग्निर्दहति तत्र वै।
en: Swords and bows and bow-strings and arrows and tomaras' and ankusas and darts. And blankets and chowris and tiger-skins and musk and other things. And pearls and excellent gems; and edifices all around. And there the fire burn heap of various kinds of arms. 1. An Iron club. 2. The hook used to drive an elephant.

sn: नानाविधान्गृहांश्चित्रान्ददाह हुतभुक्तदा॥ आवासाराक्षसानां च सर्वेषां गृहगृनुनाम्। हेमचित्रतनुत्राणां स्रग्भाण्डाम्बरधारिणाम्॥ सीधुपानचलाक्षाणां मदविह्वलगामिनाम्। कान्तालम्बितवस्त्राणां शत्रुसंजातमन्युनाम्॥ गदाशूलासिहस्तानां खादतां पिबतामपि। शयनेषु महार्हेषु प्रसुप्तानां प्रियैः सह ॥ त्रस्तानां गच्छतां तूर्णं पुत्रानादाय सर्वतः।
en: Then the fire burnt various kinds of curious structures, and the dwellings of Räkşasas and all house-holders. And there the fire flaming up again and again burnt down by hundreds and thousands the houses of the denizons of Lanka, clad in curious golden mail; and wearing wreaths and ornaments and attires; having their eyes wildly moving in intoxication; reeling in drink; those whose paramours were dressed in flowing apparels; or those wroth with their foes; or bearing maces and darts and swords in their hands; or engaged in eating or drinking; or asleep with their beloved on costly couches; or who, agitated with fright, were hastily going taking their sons with them.

sn: तेषां शतसहस्राणि तदा लङ्कानिवासिनाम्॥ अदहत्पावकस्तत्र जज्वाल च पुनः पुनः। सारवन्ति महार्हाणि गम्भीरगुणवन्ति च॥ हेमचन्द्रार्धचन्द्राणि चन्द्रशालोत्तमानि च। तत्र चित्रगवाक्षाणि साधिष्ठानानि सर्वशः॥ मणिविदुमचित्राणि स्पृशन्तीव दिवाकरम्। क्रौञ्चबर्हिणवर्णानां भूषणानां च निःस्वनैः।।२० नादितान्यचलाभानि वेश्मान्यग्निर्ददाह सः। ज्वलनेन परीतानि तोरणानि चकाशिरे॥ विद्युद्भिरिव नद्धानि मेघजालानि धर्मगे। ज्वलनेन परीतानि गृहाणि प्रचकाशिरे॥ दावाग्निदीप्तानि यथा शिखराणि महागिरेः।
en: That fire burnt down firm-based rich dwellings furnished with innumerable apartments, and garnished with golden Moons and crescents, and mansions having graceful crests; and variegated windows and daises raised there, embellished with rubies and lapises, and seeming to touch the Sun; and piles resembling mountains in grandeur, and resonant with the cries of Krauñas and peacocks and the tinklings of omaments. The flaming gateways all round appeared like clouds in the rainy season lighted up by lightning, or like the peaks of a mighty mountain ablaze with forest-conflagration.

sn: विमानेषु प्रसुप्ताश्च दह्यमाना वराङ्गनाः॥ त्यक्ताभरणसंयोगा हाहेत्युच्चैर्विचुक्रुशुः।
en: And superb damsels asleep in lofty edifices, being burnt, cast away their ornaments and shrieked bitterly saying "Alas! Woe is me". * Vimäna, according to Rämānuja, is a sevenstoried edifice.

sn: तत्र चाग्निपरीतानि निपेतुर्भवनान्यपि॥ वज्रिवज्रहतानीव शिखराणि महागिरेः।
en: Consumed by the fire, buildings began to drop down like the summits of a mighty mountain smite with the thunder-bolt of the thunderer.

sn: तानि निर्दह्यमानानि दूरतः प्रचकाशिरे॥ हिमवच्छिखराणीव दह्यमानानि सर्वशः।
en: And those burning, appeared from a distance like the peaks of Himalaya aglow.

sn: हार्दह्यमानैश्च ज्वालाप्रज्वलितैरपि॥ रात्रौ सा दृश्यते लङ्का पुष्पितैरिव किंशुकैः।
en: In consequence of those tops of the edifices burning and of the living flames, that night Lankā looked as if swarming with flowering Kinsukas.

sn: हस्त्यध्यक्षैर्गजैर्मुक्तैर्मुक्तैश्च तुरगैरपि।। बभूव लङ्का लोकान्ते भ्रान्तग्राह इवार्णवः॥
en: With elephant-riders, and elephants, and steeds let loose, Lankä appeared like the Ocean at the hour of Universal tumbling, with its ferocious aquatic animals whirling in wild chaos.

sn: अश्वं मुक्तं गजो दृष्ट्वा क्वचिद्रीतोऽपसर्पति। भीतो भीतं गजं दृष्ट्वा क्वचिदश्वो निवर्तते॥
en: Sometimes, an elephant seeing a steed let loose, was flying away in fear, and sometimes a horse seeing a frightened elephant, was stopping, himself seized with fear.

sn: लङ्कायां दह्यमानायां शुशुभे च महोदधिः। छायासंसक्तसलिलो लोहितोद इवार्णवे॥
en: On Larkā burning, the mighty main with the reflection (of the conflagration) looked like an ocean of red waters.

sn: सा बभूव मुहूर्तेन हरिभिर्दीपिता पुरी। लोकस्यास्य क्षये घोरे प्रदीप्तेव वसुंधरा ॥
en: In a short time that city set on fire by the monkeys, looked like the earth glowing at the time of the Universal dissolution.

sn: नारीजनस्य धूमेन व्याप्तस्योच्चैर्विनेदुषः। स्वनो ज्वलनतप्तस्य शुश्रुवे शतयोजनम्॥
en: The cries of the females amidst the drift of smoke, heated by the flames, could be heard from an hundred Yojanas.

sn: प्रदग्धकायानपरान्राक्षसान्निर्गतान्बहिः। सहसा ह्युत्पतन्ति स्म हरयोऽथ युयुत्सवः॥
en: As Rākşasas having their bodies burnt came out of houses, monkeys eager for encounter on a sudden sprung upon them.

sn: उद्धृष्टं वानराणां च राक्षसानां च निःस्वनम्। दिशो दश समुद्रं च पृथिवीं च व्यनादयत्॥
en: The shouts of the monkeys and the cries of the Rākşasas made the ten cardinal quarters and the ocean and the Earth resound.

sn: विशल्यौ च महात्मानौ तावुभौ रामलक्ष्मणौ। असंभ्रान्तौ जगृहतुस्ते उभे धनुषी वरे॥
en: On those high-souled ones both Rāma and Lakşmaņa-having been cured of their wounds, possessing themselves in calmness, took up their excellent bows.

sn: ततो विस्फारयामास रामश्च धनुरुत्तमम्। बभूव तुमुलः शब्दो राक्षसानां भयावहः॥
en: Rāma drew that best of bows. And thereat there was heard a tremendous twang striking terror into the Rákşasas,

sn: अशोभत तदा रामो धनुर्विस्फारयन्महत्। भगवानिव संक्रुद्धो भवो वेदमयं धनुः॥
en: And drawing his redoubtable bow, Rāma appeared like the reverend enraged Bhava, drawing his bow having sounds, and instinct with Brahma energy.

sn: उद्देष्टं वानराणां च राक्षसानां च निःस्वनम्। ज्याशब्दस्तावुभौ शब्दावतिरामस्य शुश्रुवे॥
en: The twang of Rama's bow, drowning the roars of both the monkeys and die Rákşasas: was alone heard.

sn: वानरोद्धृष्टघोषश्च राक्षसानां च निःस्वनः। ज्याशब्दश्चापि रामस्य त्रयं व्याप दिशो दश।३८॥
en: The ululations of the monkeys and the cries of the Raksasas and the rattle of Rama's bowthese three filled the ten cardinal quarters.

sn: तस्य कार्मुकनिर्मुक्तैः शरैस्तत्पुरगोपुरम्। कैलासशृङ्गप्रतिमं विकीर्णमभवद्भुवि॥
en: With the shafts discharged from his bow, the gieway of the city resembling the summit of 1. islās. was crushed in pieces, scattered around cr the ground.

sn: नतो रामशरान्दृष्ट्वा विमानेषु गृहेषु च। संनाहो सक्षसेन्द्राणां तुमुलः समपद्यत॥
en: See cs Rāma's shafts in cars and dwellings, the preparations for conflict were pushed on with great viour.

sn: तेषां संनह्यमानानां सिंहनादं च कुर्वताम्। शर्वरी राक्षसेन्द्राणां रौद्रीव समपद्यत॥
en: An' in consequence of the foremost Rakşasas preparing for fight, and emitting roars, that night appeared like the Fatal Night itself.

sn: आदिष्टा वानरेन्द्रास्ते सुग्रीवेण महात्मना। आसन्नं द्वारमासाद्य युध्यध्वं च प्लवंगमाः।॥
en: The foremost monkeys were directed by the high-souled Sugriva, saying, “You monkeys, do you fight, approaching the gate lying at hand.

sn: यश्च वो वितथं कुर्यात्तत्र तत्राप्युपस्थितः। स हन्तव्योऽभिसंप्लुत्य राजशासनदूषकः॥
en: But he that fly from his ranks, should be slain by main force.

sn: तेषु वानरमुख्येषु दीप्तोल्कोज्ज्वलपाणिषु। स्थितेषु द्वारमाश्रित्य रावणं क्रोध आविशत्॥
en: As the principal monkeys stationed themselves at the gate, equipped with fire-brands, wrath took possession of Rävana.

sn: तस्य जृम्भितविक्षेपाव्यामिश्रा वै दिशो दश। रूपवानिव रुद्रस्य मन्युर्गात्रेष्वदृश्यत॥
en: And as he yawned, the wind (blowing) from his mouth), filled the ten cardinal regions; and his wrath resembled that appearing in the person of Rudra.

sn: स कुम्भं च निकुम्भं च कुम्भकर्णात्मजावुभौ । प्रेषयामास संक्रुद्धो राक्षसैर्बहुभिः सह ॥
en: And wrought up with a mighty rage, he sent forth Kumbha and Nikumbha-both sons of Kumbhakarna-in company with innumerable Raksasas.

sn: यूपाक्षः शोणिताक्षश्च प्रज़जः कम्पनस्तथा। निर्ययुः कौम्भकर्णाभ्यां सह रावणशासनात्॥
en: In accordance with Ravana's command, Yupaksa and Sonitaksa, and Prajarigha, and Kampana went with Kumbhakarna's sons.

sn: शशास चैव तान्सर्वान्राक्षसान्स महाबलान्। राक्षसा गच्छताद्यैव सिंहनादं च नादयन्।॥
en: Setting up leonine roars, he commanded all those highly powerful Raksasas, saying, "Do you go this very day for battle."

sn: ततस्तु चोदितास्तेन राक्षसा ज्वलितायुधाः। लङ्काया निर्ययुर्वीराः प्रणदन्तः पुनः पुनः॥
en: Thus directed, those heroic heroic Rakşasas, equipped with flaming weapons, went out, roaring again and again.

sn: रक्षसां भूषणस्थाभि भिः स्वाभिश्च सर्वशः। चकृस्ते सप्रभं व्योम हरयश्चाग्निभिः सह ॥
en: The firmament was illuminated with the splendour of the ornaments of the Rakşasas and the splendour of their persons and the fire kindled by the monkeys.

sn: तत्र ताराधिपस्याभा ताराणां भा तथैव च। तयोराभरणाभा च ज्वलिता द्यामभासयत्॥
en: There the light of the moon and that of the stars and the brilliance of their omaments, combined, lighted up the welkin.

sn: चन्द्राभा भूषणाभा च ग्रहाणां ज्वलिता च भा। हरिराक्षससैन्यानि भाजयामास सर्वतः॥
en: The beams of the Moon and the brilliance of the ornaments and the flaming splendour of the planets emblazoned all round the forces of the monkeys and Raksasas.

sn: तत्र चार्धप्रदीप्तानां गृहाणां सागरः पुनः। भाभिः संसक्तसलिलश्चलोमिः शुशुभे ध्रुवम्॥
en: The light of half-burnt houses, again, falling on the restless ripples of the sea, made it wear an extremely beautiful aspect.

sn: पताकाध्वजसंयुक्तमुत्तमासिपरश्वधम्। भीमाश्वरथमातंग नानापत्तिसमाकुलम्॥ दीप्तशूलगदाखड्गप्रासतोमरकार्मुकम्। तद्राक्षसबलं भीमं घोरविक्रमपौरुषम्॥ ददृशे ज्वलितप्रासं किङ्किणीशतनादितम्। हेमजालाचितभुजं व्यावेष्टितपरश्वधम्॥ व्याघूर्णितमहाशस्त्रं बाणसंसक्तकार्मुकम्। गन्धमाल्यमधूत्सेकसंमोदितमहानिलम्॥
en: Those dreadful Rākşasa hosts, possessed of dreadful prowess and energy, were seen-with ensigns and banners; excellent swords and parasvadhas,* (A platoon consisting of one chariot, one elephant, three horse and five foot.) terrific steeds and cars and elephants rife with paths,* (A kind of sword.) and flaming darts and clubs and scimitars and präsas and tomaras and bows; bearing blazing prāsas; ringing with the tinklings of hundreds of balls; with their arms encased in golden networks; flourishing axes; whirling their mighty weapons, fixing shafts on their bows; making the air swoon away with the perfumes of their wreaths; extremely terrific; swarming with heroes; sending out sounds like those of the sea.

sn: घोरं शूरजनाकीणं महाम्बुधरनिःस्वनम्। तदृष्ट्वा बलमायातं राक्षसानां दुरासदम्॥
en: Seeing the army of the Räkşasas incapable of being coped with advance, the monkey-forces began to move and send up loud cheers.

sn: संचचाल प्लवंगानां बलमुच्चैर्ननाद च। जवेनाप्लुत्य च पुनस्तद्बलं रक्षसां महत्॥
en: Thereat that array of Räkşasas vehemently sprang forward before the force of the foe, like to insects plunging into a flame.

sn: अभ्ययात्प्रत्यरिबलं पतंगा इव पावकम्। तेषां भुजपरामर्शव्यामृष्टपरिघाशनि॥
en: And whirling with their arms bludgeons and asanis, that army of Rakşasas appeared exceedingly grand.

sn: राक्षसानां बलं श्रेष्ठं भूयः परमशोभत। तत्रोन्मत्ता इवोत्पेतुर्हरयोऽथ युयुत्सवः॥
en: The monkeys, eager for encounter, darted forward like maniacs, and began to despatch the night-rangers with rocks and trees and clenched fist.

sn: तरुशैलैरभिघ्नन्तो मुष्टिभिश्च निशाचरान्। तथैवापततां तेषां हरीणां निशितैः शरैः॥
en: Rākşasas possessed of dreadful prowess with whetted arrows swiftly cut off the heads of falling monkeys.

sn: शिरांसि सहसा जडू राक्षसा भीमविक्रमाः। दशनैर्हतकर्णाश्च मुष्टिभिभिन्नमस्तकाः।। शिलाप्रहारभग्नाङ्गा विचेरुस्तत्र राक्षसाः॥
en: The Rākşasas ranged there, with their ears torn with teeth, or their heads broken by blows, or their limbs crushed with the discharge of crags.

sn: तथैवाप्यपरे तेषां कपीनामसिभिः शितैः। प्रवरानभितो जघ्नुर्घोररूपा निशाचराः॥
en: In the same way other grim-visaged nightrangers slew with sharpened swords the foremost of monkeys on all sides.

sn: घ्नन्तमन्यं जघानान्यः पातयन्तमपातयत्। गर्हमाणं जगन्यिो दशन्तमपरोऽदशत्॥
en: And one about to slay another was himself slain by the latter; and one, about to bring another down, was himself brought down (by his adversary, and one that was railing at another, was in turn rebuked by his enemy; and one who was going to bite his foe, was himself bitten by him.

sn: देहीत्यन्यो ददात्यन्यो ददामीत्यपरः पुनः। किं क्लेशयसि तिष्ठेति तत्रान्योन्यं बभाषिरे॥
en: One was crying 'Give.'* and his adversary anon give; and another, again said, I will give. Why put yourself to trouble? Stay. *Battle.

sn: विप्रलम्भितशस्त्रं च विमुक्तकवचायुधम्। समुद्यतमहाप्रासं मुष्टिशूलासिकुन्तलम्॥ प्रावर्तत महारौद्रं युद्धं वानररक्षसाम्। वानरान्दश सप्तेति राक्षसा जघ्नुराहवे॥
en: Thus there did they accost each other. And there was waged a terrific encounter between the monkeys and the Rākşasas, in which arms lay scattered about; and armour and weapons strewn around; and mighty prāsas' were upraised; and which was fought with blows and darts and swords and Kuntalas? And in that conflict the Rākşasas slaughtered monkeys by tens and sevens. 1. A bearded dart. 2. What could this be like? The commentator is mute. Wilson has Kuntalik-butter-knife or scoop. Kuntala may, however, mean a plough.

sn: विप्रलम्बितवस्त्रं च विमुक्तकवचध्वजम्। बलं राक्षसमालम्ब्य वानराः पर्यवारयन्॥
en: Then the monkeys hemmed in the Rākşasaforces, with their apparels falling off and with their mail and standards strewn around. swords and Kuntalas? And in that conflict the Rākşasas slaughtered monkeys by tens and sevens. 1. A bearded dart. 2. What could this be like? The commentator is mute. Wilson has Kuntalik-butter-knife or scoop. Kuntala may, however, mean a plough.

sn: विप्रलम्बितवस्त्रं च विमुक्तकवचध्वजम्। बलं राक्षसमालम्ब्य वानराः पर्यवारयन्॥
en: Then the monkeys hemmed in the Rākşasaforces, with their apparels falling off and with their mail and standards strewn around.

sn: प्रवृत्ते संकुले तस्मिन्वीरे घोरजनक्षये। अङ्गदः कम्पनं वीरमाससाद रणोत्सुकः॥
en: On that furious and destructive carnage proceeding, Angada eager for encounter, approached the heroic Kampana.

sn: आहूय सोऽङ्गदं कोपात्ताडयामास वेगितः। गदया कम्पनः पूर्व स चचाल भृशाहतः॥
en: Thereat, challenging Angada in wrath, he assailed him with impetuosity. And Kampana dealt a blow to Angada with his mace; and thereat, wounded with it, he reeled.

sn: स संज्ञां प्राप्य तेजस्वी चिक्षेप शिखरं गिरेः। अर्दितश्च प्रहारेण कम्पनः पतितो भुवि॥
en: Then regaining his senses, that energetic one hurled a mountain-top. Borne down by the blow, Kampana dropped down to the earth.

sn: ततस्तु कम्पनं दृष्ट्वा शोणिताक्षो हतं रणे। रथेनाभ्यपतित्क्षिप्रं तत्राङ्गदमभीतवत्॥
en: Seeing Kampana slain in the conflict, ſoņitākṣa mounted on a car, intrepidity rushed against Angada.

sn: सोऽङ्गदं निशितैर्बाणैस्तदा विव्याध वेगितः। शरीरदारणैस्तीक्ष्णैः कालाग्निसमविग्रहैः॥ क्षुरक्षुरखनाराचैर्वत्सदन्तैः शिलीमुखैः। कर्णिशल्यविपाठैश्च बहुभिर्निशितैः शरैः॥ अङ्गदः प्रतिविद्धाङ्गो वालिपुत्रः प्रतापवान्। धनुरुग्रं रथं बाणान्ममर्द तरसा बली॥
en: He then impetuously pierced Angada with sharpened shafts, keen and capable of cleaving the body and resembling the fatal fire itself in appearance, with Kșuras' and Kșurapras? and Näräcas and Vatsadantas* and Silīmukhas and Karmis and Salyas and Vipathas, and countless (other) whetted arrows. And the powerful son of Vāli, Angada endowed with prowess having his person pierced with arrows suddenly smashed (his adversary's) car and arrows and dreadful bow. 1. Arrows having razor-like edges. 2. Crescent-shaped shafts. 3. Arrows made entirely of iron. 4. Arrows resembling the teeth of calves. 5. Arrows resembling the feathers of the Kanka. 6. Arrow furnished with two sides resembling cars. 7. Arrow with short leads. 8. Arrows resembling the tops of KaravīrasTirtha.

sn: शोणिताक्षस्ततः क्षिप्रमसिचर्म समाददे। उत्पपात तदा कुद्धो वेगवानविचारयन्॥
en: Thereat, Šoņitākṣa swiftly took up his sword and shield; and without reflecting for a moment, that vigorous one sprang forward.

sn: तं क्षिप्रतरमाप्लुत्य परामृश्याङ्गदो बली। करेण तस्य तं खङ्गं समाच्छिद्य ननाद च॥
en: The powerful Angada speedily bounding up, seized his enemy's sword and holding the same with his hands shouted.

sn: तस्यां स फलके खङ्गं निजघान ततोऽङ्गदः। यज्ञोपवीतवच्चैनं चिच्छेद कपिकुञ्जरः॥
en: Then hitting at (Akampana's) shoulder-blade, that powerful monkey-Angada hewed him in twain, his blow going obliquely down like the sacred thread.

sn: तं प्रगृह्य महाखड्गं विनद्य च पुनः पुनः। वालिपुत्रोऽभिदुद्राव रणशीर्ष परानरीन्॥
en: Taking that terrific sword, and shouting again and again, in the field, Valr's son rushed against other enemies.

sn: प्रजङ्घसहितो वीरो यूपाक्षस्तु ततो बली। रथेनाभिययौ क्रुद्धो वालिपुत्रं महाबलम्॥
en: Then strong and heroic Yüpākṣa accompanied by Prajangha, mounted on a car, wrathfully approached the mighty son of Vali.

sn: आयसीं तु गदां गृह्य स वीरः कनकाङ्गदः। शोणिताक्षः समाश्वस्य तमेवानुपपात ह॥
en: Taking an iron mace, that hero, Sonitaksa, adorned with a golden Angada attaining a little respite, advanced against Angada.

sn: प्रजङ्घस्तु महावीरो यूपाक्षसहितो बली। गदयाभिययौ क्रुद्धो वालिपुत्रं महाबलम्॥
en: That redoubtable hero, the powerful Prajangha, also accompanied by Yüpākşa, fired with wrath, equipped with a mace, advanced towards the son of Vāli endowed with exceeding prowess.

sn: तयोर्मध्ये कपिश्रेष्ठः क्षोणिताश्रप्रजङ्घयोः। विशाखयोर्मध्यगतः पूर्णचन्द्र इवाबभौ॥
en: And placed between those two Soņitākşa and Prajangha-that foremost of monkeys appeared like the full moon placed between the Visākhās.* *The asterisks so named

sn: अङ्गदं परिरक्षन्तौ मैन्दो द्विविद एव च। तस्य तस्थतुरभ्याशे परस्परदिदृक्षया॥
en: Mainda and Dvivida defending Angada remained beside him, desirous of witnessing the encounter between those two (combatants).

sn: अभिपेतुर्महाकायाः प्रतियत्ता महाबलाः। राक्षसा वानरानरोषादसिबामगदाधराः॥
en: And fired with fury, those huge-bodied Räkş asas endowed with dreadful prowess, equipped with swords and shafts and maces, being on their guard, fell upon the monkeys.

sn: त्रयाणां वानरेन्द्राणां त्रिभी राक्षसपुङ्गवैः। संसक्तानां महद्युद्धमभवद्रोमहर्षणम्॥
en: The encounter that took place between those three lords of monkeys combined (on one side), and the three redoubtable Rākşasas (on the other), was dreadful and capable of making people's down stand on end.

sn: ते तु वृक्षान्समादाय संप्रचिक्षिपुराहवे। खङ्गेन प्रतिचिक्षेप तान्प्रजङ्घो महाबलः॥
en: They, taking up trees, hurled them in the conflict (against their antagonists); and the powerful Prājantha resisted all those with his swords.

sn: रथान्सर्वान्दुमाञ्छैलान्प्रतिचिक्षिपुराहवे। शरौधैः प्रतिचिच्छेद तान्यूपाक्षो महाबलाः॥
en: And (the monkeys) in the contest showered rocks and trees on the cars (of their) enemies; and the exceedingly strong Yūpākşa cut them off with vollies of arrows.

sn: सृष्टान्विविदमैन्दाभ्यां दुमानुत्पाट्य वीर्यवान्। बभञ्ज गदया मध्ये शोणिताक्षः प्रतापवान्॥
en: The powerful Sonitaksa, endowed with prowess, with his mace severed in the middle the trees which Dvivida and Mainda had uprooted and discharged.

sn: उद्यम्य विपुलं खङ्गं परमर्मविदारणम्। प्रजबो वालिपुत्राय अभिदुद्राव वेगितः॥
en: And summoning speed, Prajangha darted against Väli's son, upraising a huge scimitar capable of piercing into the vitals of trees.

sn: तमभ्याशगतं दृष्ट्वा वानरेन्द्रो महाबलः। आजघानाश्वकर्णेन दुमेणातिबलस्तदा॥ बाहुं चास्य सनिस्त्रिंशमाजघान स मुष्टिना। बालिपुत्रस्य घातेन स पपात क्षितावसिः॥
en: Seeing him approach, that lord of monkeys possessed of exceeding strength and great prowess struck him with an Aśvakarņa tree; and with a blow smote his antagonist on his arm holding a nistringa.

sn: तं दृष्ट्वा पतितं भूमौ खङ्गं मुसलसंनिभम्! मुष्टिं संवर्तयामास वज्रकल्पं महाबलः॥ स ललाटे महावीर्यमङ्गदं वानरर्षभम्। आजघान महातेजाः स मुहूर्त चचाल ह॥
en: Seeing the sword resembling a mace dropped to the earth, that exceedingly mighty one clenched his fist into a blow like to the levin; and that one, endowed with wondrous energy, smote in the forehead that foremost of monkeys possessed of redoubtable prowess. And thereat he for a moment was staggered.

sn: स संज्ञां प्राप्य तेजस्वी वालिपुत्रः प्रतापवान्। प्रजङ्घस्य शिरः कायात्पातयामास मुष्टिना॥
en: Then recovering his senses, the energetic and powerful son of Vālī by means of his clenched fist severed Prajangha's head from his body.

sn: स यूपाक्षोऽश्रुपूर्णाक्षः पितृव्ये निहते रणे।। अवरुह्य रथात्क्षिप्रं क्षीणेषु खङ्गमाददे॥
en: Thereat Yüpākşa, seeing his uncle slain in battle, with his eyes filled with tears, finding his shafts exhausted, swiftly descended from his car and took a sword.

sn: तमापतन्तं संप्रेक्ष्य यूपाक्षं द्विविदस्त्वरन्। आजघानोरसि क्रुद्धो जग्राह च बलाबली॥
en: Finding Yūpākṣa charge, Dvivida, waxing wroth, speedily smote him on the breast; and that powerful one also seized him.

sn: गृहीतं भ्रातरं दृष्ट्वा शोणिताक्षो महाबलम्। आजधान महातेजा वक्षसि द्विविदं ततः॥
en: And finding his brother taken, the highly energetic Soạitākṣa then dealt the mighty Dvivida a blow in the chest.

sn: स ततोऽभिहतस्तेन चचाल च महाबलः। उद्यतां च पुनस्तस्य जहार द्विविदो गदाम्॥
en: And overcome by that blow, that one endowed with great sirength, shook; and Dvivida seized his antagonist's upraised mace.

sn: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे मैन्दो द्विविदाभ्याशमागमत्। तौ शोणिताक्षयूपाक्षौ प्लवंगाभ्यां तरस्विनौ। चक्रतुः समरे तीव्रमाकर्षोत्पाटनं भृशम्॥
en: In the meanwhile Mainda came to the side of Dvivida. And śoṇitākṣa and Yüpākşa, bestirring themselves, began to vehemently and forcibly drag and pull those (two) monkeys.

sn: द्विविदः शोणिताक्षं तु विददार नखैर्मुखे। निष्पिपेष स वीर्येण क्षितावाविध्य वीर्यवान्॥
en: And Dvivida with his nail tore ſoņitākşa's face; and that powerful one violently bringing him down to the earth, pressed him with might and main.

sn: यूपाक्षमभिसंक्रुद्धो मैन्दो वानरपुङ्गवः। पीडयामास बाहुभ्यां पणत स हतः क्षितौ॥
en: And fired with wrath, Mainda-foremost of monkeys-grasped Yupaksa with his arms; and that one dropt down dead on the earth.

sn: हतप्रवीरा व्यथिता राक्षसेन्द्रचमूस्तथा। जगामाभिमुखी सा तु कुम्भकर्णात्मजो यतः॥
en: Thereupon the force of the lord of the Rāks asas, having its foremost heroes slain, and aggrieved thereat, went to where Kumbhakarma's son was.

sn: आपतन्तीं च वेगेन कुम्भस्तां सान्त्वयच्चमूम्। अथोत्कृष्टं महावीयौलब्धलक्षैः प्लवंगमैः॥ निपातितमहावीरां दृष्ट्वा रक्षश्चमूं तदा। कुम्भः प्रचक्रे तेजस्वी रणे कर्म सुदुष्करम्॥
en: Then cheering up the flying forces, that best (of Raksas)-the energetic Kumbha-seeing that Rakşasa host with its mighty herocs slain by highly powerful monkey crowned with success, began to perform difficult feats in the encounter.

sn: स धनुर्धन्विनां श्रेष्ठः प्रगृह्य सुसमाहितः। मुमोचाशीविषप्रख्याञ्छरान्देहविदारणान्॥
en: And heedfully taking his bow, that first of bowmen discharged shafts resembling venomous serpents capable of piercing the body.

sn: तस्य तच्छुशुभे भूयः सशरं धनुरुत्तमम्। विद्युदैरावतार्चिष्माद्दितीयेन्द्रधनुर्यथा॥
en: And his excellent bow with shafts shone resplendent like the very bow of Indra himself affluent with the splendour of Airāvata and lightning.

sn: आकर्णकृष्टमुक्तेन जघान द्विविदं तदा। तेन हाटकपुनेन पत्रिणा पत्रवाससा॥
en: Then drawing his bow to its utmost bent, he hit Dvivida with a feathered shaft knobbed with gold.

sn: सहसाभिहतस्तेन विप्रमुक्तपदः स्फुरन्। निपपात त्रिकूटाभो विह्वलन्प्लवगोत्तमः॥
en: Suddenly wounded with it, that best of monkeys having the splendour of Trikūța, fell down senseless to the earth, stretching his legs wide.

sn: मैन्दस्तु भ्रातरं तत्र भग्नं दृष्ट्वा महाहवे। अभिदुद्राव वेगेन प्रगृह्य विपुलां शिलाम्॥ तां शिलां तु प्रचिक्षेप राक्षसाय महाबलः। बिभेदं तां शिलां कुम्भः प्रसन्नैः पञ्चभिः शरैः।॥
en: Mainda, seeing his brother, broken in mighty encounter, furiously rushed forward, taking a gigantic crag; and that one possessed of great strength, hurled it at the Raksasa. And thereat Kumbha "severed that crag with five shafts discharged (from his bow).

sn: संधाय चान्यं सुमुखं शरमाशीविषोपमम्। आजघान महातेजा वक्षसि द्विविदाग्रजम्॥
en: Then aiming other fair-headed arrows resembling venomous snakes, that exceedingly energetic one smote Dvivida's elder brother in the chest.

sn: स तु तेन प्रहारेण मैन्दो वानरयूथपः। मर्मण्यभिहतस्तेन पपात भुवि मुर्छितः॥
en: And struck (with those arrows), that leader of monkey-bands, Mainda, with his marrow pierced therewith, fell down to the earth, deprived of his senses.

sn: अङ्गदो मातुलौ दृष्ट्वा मथितौ तु महाबलौ। अभिदुद्राव वेगेन कुम्भमुद्यतकार्मुकम्॥
en: Angada seeing his uncles* endowed with exceeding prowess, overpowered, darted vehemently at Kumbha staying with bow upraised. *Maternal uncles.

sn: तमापतन्तं विव्याध कुम्भः पञ्चभिरायसैः। त्रिभिश्चान्यैस्त्रिभिर्बाणैर्मातंगमिव तोमरैः।। सोऽङ्गदं बहुभिर्बाणैः कुम्भो विव्याध वीर्यवान् ॥ अकुण्ठधारैर्निशितैस्तीक्ष्णैः कनकभूषणैः।
en: As he descended, Kumbha pierced him with five shafts; and as one pierce an elephant with tomaras, he also pierced (Angada) with three other arrows. And the powerful Kumbha pierced Angada with a great many arrows, sharppointed, whetted, keen and ornamented with gold.

sn: अङ्गदः प्रतिविष्टाङ्गो वालिपुत्रो न कम्पते।॥ शिलापादपवर्षाणि तस्य मूर्ध्नि ववर्ष ह। स प्रचिच्छेद तान्सर्वान् बिभेद च पुनः शिलाः॥ कुम्भकर्णात्मजः श्रीमान्वालिपुत्रसमीरितान्।
en: Vāli's son Angada albeit pierced all over in his person, did not shake; and he kept showering on his* head stones and trees. And the graceful son of Kumbhakarņa cut off and cleft all those (stone and trees) discharged by Valr's son. *Kumbha's.

sn: आपतन्तं च संप्रेक्ष्य कुम्भो वानरयूथपम्॥ ध्रुवौ विव्याध बाणाभ्यामुल्काभ्यामिव कुञ्जरम्।
en: Seeing him spring up, Kumbha pierced that monkey-leader on the ground with shafts, even as one assail an elephant with fire-brands.

sn: तस्य सुस्राव रुधिरं पिहिते चास्य लोचने॥ अङ्गदः पाणिना नेत्रे पिधाय रुधिरोक्षिते। सालमासन्नमेकेन परिजग्राह पाणिना। ५२।। संपीड्योरसि सस्कन्धं करेणाभिनिवेश्य च। किंचिदभ्यवनम्यैनमुन्ममाथ महारणे॥ तमिन्द्रकेतुप्रतिमं वृक्षं मन्दरसंनिभम्। समुत्सृजत वेगेन मिषतां सर्वरक्षसाम्॥
en: And blood gushed out of his closed eyes. And then covering his eyes with his hand, Angada with another took a Sala that was hard by. And placing on his breast the Sala furnished with shoulders, and pulling its branches and bending its top, he cleared it of its foliage, in that mighty encounter. Then in the sight of all the Rākşasas he violently discharged that tree resembling the very banner of Indra and appearing like Mandara itself.

sn: स चिच्छेद शितैर्बाणैः सप्तभिः कायभेदनैः। अङ्गदो विव्यथेऽभीक्ष्णं स पपात मुमोह च॥
en: Thereat he* severed it with seven sharp shafts capable of piercing the body. And Angada experienced a sharp pang and fell down deprived of his senses. *Kumbha.

sn: अङ्गदं पतितं दृष्ट्वा सीदन्तमिव सागरम्। दुरासदं हरिश्रेष्ठा राघवाय न्यवेदयन् ॥
en: Seeing the invincible Angada down like ebbing sea, the foremost monkeys informed Raghava of it.

sn: रामस्तु व्यथितं श्रुत्वा वालिपुत्रं महाहवे। व्यादिदेश हरिश्रेष्ठाञ्जाम्बवत्प्रमुखांस्ततः॥
en: Rama, hearing that Vali's son had come to grief in terrific fight, directed the principal monkeys, headed by Jambavan.

sn: ते तु वानरशार्दूलाः श्रुत्वा रामस्य शासनम्। अभिपेतुः सुसंक्रुद्धाः कुम्भमुद्यतकार्मुकम्॥
en: And hearing Rama's command, the monkeys, fired with wrath, charged Kumbha, staying with his bow upraised.

sn: ततो दुमशिलाहस्ताः कोपसंरक्तलोचनाः। रिरक्षिषन्तोऽभ्यपतनङ्गदं वानरर्षभाः॥
en: Those powerful monkeys, with their eyes crimsoned with choler and bearing rocks and trees in their hands, were engaged in defending Angada.

sn: जाम्बवांश्च सुषेणश्च वेगदर्शी च वानरः। कुम्भकर्णात्मजं वीरं क्रुद्धाः समभिदुद्रुवुः॥
en: Jāmbavān and Suşeņa and the monkey, Vegadarsi, wrought with wrath, darted against that hero-son to Kumbhakarma.

sn: समीक्ष्यापततस्तांस्तु वानरेन्द्रान्महाबलान्। आववार शरौघेण नगेनेव जलाशयम्॥
en: Seeing them spring forward; he covered up those exceedingly mighty lords of monkey, with showers of shafts, even as a crag obstruct the course of a current.

sn: तस्य बाणपथं प्राप्य न शेकुरपि वीक्षितुम्। वानरेन्द्रा महात्मानो वेलामिव महोदधिः॥
en: Even the great deep cannot see his own shores, those high-souled lord of monkeys, coming within the range of his arrows, could not even see.

sn: तांस्तु दृष्ट्वा हरिगणाशरवृष्टिभिरर्दितान्। अङ्गदं पृष्ठतः कृत्वा भ्रातृजं प्लवगेश्वरः॥ अभिदुद्राव सुग्रीवः कुम्भकर्णात्मजं रणे। शैलसानुचरं नागं वेगवानिव केसरी॥
en: Seeing those monkeys sore distressed by the shafts, the king of the monkeys, Sugrīva, in that conflict taking his brother's son on his back, rushed against the son of Kumbhakarna, even as a powerful lion rush at an elephant ranging on the slopes of a mountain.

sn: उत्पाट्य च महावृक्षानश्वकर्णादिकान्बहून्। अन्यांश्च विविधान्वृक्षांश्चिक्षेप स महाकपिः॥
en: That mighty monkey, uprooting many an asvakarna and other mighty trees of various kinds, discharged them (at the foe).

sn: तां छादयन्तीमाकाशं वृक्षवृष्टिं दुरासदाम्। कुम्भकर्णात्मजः श्रीमांश्चिच्छेद स्वशरैः शितैः॥ अर्दितास्ते दुमा रेजुर्यथा घोराः शतघ्नयः।
en: By means of his sharp arrows the graceful son of Kumbhakarņa cut off that down-pour of trees covering the welkin; and incapable of being resisted. And being beffled those trees looked like sataghnis.

sn: दुमवर्षं तु तद्भिन्नं दृष्ट्वा कुम्भेन वीर्यवान्॥ वानराधिपतिः श्रीमान्महासत्त्वो न विव्यथे।
en: Seeing that shower of trees riven by Kumbha, the graceful lord of the monkeys endowed with exceeding strength and prowess, did not feel any mortification.

sn: स विध्यमानः सहसा सहमानस्तु ताञ्छरान्॥ कुम्भस्य धनुराक्षिप्य बभञ्जेन्द्रधनुष्प्रभम्। अवप्लुत्य धनुः शीघ्रं कृत्वा कर्म सुदुष्करम्॥ अब्रवीत्कुपितः कुम्भं भग्नशृङ्गमिव द्विपम्।
en: Suddenly attacked, he bearing those arrows, seized Kumbha's bow resembling in resplendence the very bow of Indra. And swiftly bounding up and performing that feat difficult of being achieved, he, exceedingly enraged, addressed Kumbha resembling an elephant shorn of his tusks, saying.

sn: निकुम्भाग्रज वीर्यं ते बाणवेगं तदद्भुतम्॥ संनतिश्च प्रभावश्च तव वा रावणस्य वा। प्रह्लादबलिवृत्रघ्नकुबेरवरुणोपम॥ एकस्त्वमनुजातोऽसि पितरं बलवत्तरम्। त्वामेवैकं महाबाहुं शूलहस्तमरिंदमम्॥ त्रिदशा नातिवर्तन्ते जितेन्द्रियमिवाधयः। विक्रमस्व महाबुद्धे कर्माणि मम पश्य च॥
en: O elder brother of Nikumbha, marvellous are your might and the force of yourself as well as the modesty and prowess that are your and Ravana's. And, o you equal to Prahrada or Vall or the slayer of Vặtra or Varuņa or Kuvera! You alone walk in the wake of you yet mightier father. As mental anguish does not dog one that has controlled his senses, the celestials cannot cope in conflict with you alone, O repressor of foes, O of mighty arms, bearing your dart in your hand. O you of high intelligence, put forth your prowess! and do you also witness my work.

sn: वरदानात्पितृव्यस्ते सहते देवदानवान्। कुम्भकर्णस्तु वीर्येण सहते च सुरासुरान्॥ धनुषीन्द्रजितस्तुल्यः प्रतापे रावणस्य च। त्वमद्य रक्षसां लोके श्रेष्ठोऽसि बलवीर्यतः॥
en: It is only by virtue of the boon he has received, that your uncle can bear the deities and the Dānavas. But Kumbhakarņa cop with the immortals and Asuras by means of his native might. And in the bow equal to Indrajit himself and in power equal to Rāvana, you now in might and energy are the foremost of Räkşasas.

sn: महाविम समरे मया सह तवाद्भुतम्। अद्य भूतानि पश्यन्तु शक्रशम्बरयोरिव॥
en: Today let all creatures witness the mighty and wonderful encounter in conflict between you and me, like to the meeting of Śakra and Sambara.

sn: कृतमप्रतिमं कर्म दर्शितं चास्त्रकौशलम्। पतिता हरिवीराश्च त्वयैते भीमविक्रमाः।७७।।
en: Unparalleled is the feat you have performed; and you have displayed your skill in weapons. And heroic monkeys endowed with dreadful vigour, have been brought down by you.

sn: उपालम्भभयाच्चैव नासि वीर मया हतः। कृतकर्मपरिश्रान्तो विश्रान्तः पश्य मे बलम्॥
en: O hero it is only because of the apprehension* of censure of the people that I do not slay you who are fatigued in consequence of the acts that you have performed. And reposing from fight, do you see my strength! *i.e. Lest people should censure me, saying, Sugrīva slew Kumbha when he was fatigued in fight.

sn: तेन सुत्रीववाक्येन सावमानेन मानितः। अग्नेराज्यहुतस्येव तेजस्तस्याभ्यवर्धत॥
en: Being thus honoured (by Sugrīva) with fair speech, (Kumbha) flamed up like a flame into which oblations have been poured.

sn: ततः कुम्भस्तु सुग्रीवं बाहुभ्यां जगृहे तदा। गजाविवावीतमदौ निःश्वसन्तौ मुहुर्मुहुः॥ अन्योन्यगात्रग्रथितौ घर्षन्तावितरेतरम्। सधूमां मुखतो ज्वालां विसृजन्तौ परिश्रमात्॥
en: Then Kumbha seized Sugriva by the arms. And like two elephants in rut, they sighing momentarily, fastened on each other's person, and possessed each other, and from fatigue emitting from their mouth flames mixed with vapour.

sn: तयोः पादाभिघाताच्च निमग्ना चाभवन्मही। व्याघूशिततरङ्गश्च चुक्षुभे वरुणालयः॥
en: And with the stamping of their feet, the earth was rent into rivers, and the main was waxed, with its billows surging furiously.

sn: ततः कुम्भं समुत्क्षिप्य सुग्रीवो लवणाम्भसि। पातयामास वेगेन दर्शयन्नुदधेः स्थलम्॥ ततः कुम्भनिपातेन जलराशिः समुत्थितः। विन्ध्यमन्दरसंकाशो विससर्प समन्ततः॥
en: Then Sugrīva lifting up Kumbha clean, violently plunged him into the salt wash, making his eyes acquainted with the locality of the deep. And in consequence of Kumbha's plunge, the waters heaving up, rolled on all sides like the Vindhya or Mandara.

sn: ततः कुम्भः समुत्पत्य सुग्रीवमभिपात्य च। आजघानोरसि क्रुद्धो वज्रकल्पेन मुष्टिना॥
en: Then springing up, and bringing Sugriva down, Kumbha, transported with wrath dealt a blow on his chest, like to the levin.

sn: तस्य वर्म च पुस्फोट संजज्ञे चापि शोणितम्। तस्य मुष्टिर्महावेगः प्रतिजघ्नेऽस्थिमण्डले॥
en: Thereat his skin was rent, and blood began to gush out, and the impetus of that blow broke Sugriva's bones.

sn: तस्य वेगेन तत्रासीत्तेजः प्रज्वलितं महत्॥ वज्रनिष्पेषसंजाता ज्वाला मेरोर्यथा गिरेः॥
en: The vehemence (of the blow) caused a great fire to blaze up at that spot, even as the thunderbolt smiting the mountain Meru, make place blazed.

sn: स तत्राभिहतस्तेन सुग्रीवो वानरर्षभः। मुष्टिं संवर्तयामास वज्रकल्पं महाबलः॥ अर्चिःसहस्रविकचरविमण्डलवर्चसम्।
en: The mighty Sugrīva foremost of monkeys-sorely handled by him, fastened his fingers into a box resembling the thunder-bolt, and furnished with all the effulgence of the solar disc having a thousand rays.

sn: स मुष्टिं पातयामास कुम्भस्योरसि वीर्यवान् ॥ स तु तेन प्रहारेण विह्वलो भृशपीडितः। निपपात तदा कुम्भो गतार्चिरिव पावकः।१०।।
en: Then that powerful one made that blow descend right on on Kumbha's breast. And agonised with that stroke, Kumbha reft of his senses, dropped like to a fire that has lost its brightness.

sn: मुष्टिनाभिहतस्तेन निपपाताशु राक्षसः। लोहिताङ्ग इवाकाशाद्दीप्तरश्मिर्यदृच्छया॥
en: And overpowered by that blow, the Rākṣasa anon dropped down, like to the bright Lohitānga dropping from the firmament urged on by Destiny.

sn: कुम्भस्य पततो रूपं भग्नस्योरसि मुष्टिना। बभौ रुद्राभिपन्नस्य यथा रूपं गवां पतेः॥
en: The aspect of the falling Kumbha with his breast broken by the blow, appeared like that of the Sun routed by Rudra.

sn: तस्मिन्हते भीमपराक्रमेण प्लवंगमानामृषभेण युद्धे। मही सशैला सवना चचाल भयं च रक्षांस्यधिकं विवेश।१३।।
en: On his being slain, in encounter, by the foremost of monkeys endowed with terrific strength, the earth with her hills and woods, shook; and a mighty fear took possession of the Raksasas.

sn: निकुम्भो भ्रातरं दृष्ट्वा सुग्रीवेण निपातितम्। प्रदहन्निव कोपेन वानरेन्द्रमुर्दक्षत॥
en: Seeing his brother slain by Sugrīva, Nikumbha, gazed at the lord of the monkeys, as if consuming him with his passion.

sn: ततः स्रग्दामसंनद्धं दत्तपञ्चाङ्गुलं शुभम्। आददे परिघं धीरो महेन्द्रशिखरोपमम्॥ हेमपट्टपरिक्षिप्तं वज्रविदूमभूषितम्। यमदण्डोपमं भीमं रक्षसां भयनाशनम्॥
en: Then that one endowed with calmness, grasped a bludgeon entwined with wreaths, and furnished with an iron ring measuring five fingers, and resembling the top of the Mahendra;* plated with gold and embellished with diamonds and lapises, and looking like the rod of Yama himself; dreadful and capable of removing the fear of the Raksas. *The mountain, so named.

sn: तमाविध्य महातेजाः शक्रध्वजसमौजसम्। निननाद विवृत्तास्यो निकुम्भो भीमविक्रमः॥
en: And whirling this, that highly powerful one, resembling the banner itself of Sakra in energy, Nikumbha possessed of terrific strength, with his mouth wide open, set up shouts.

sn: उरोगतेन निष्केण भुजस्थैरङ्गदैरपि। कुण्डलाभ्यां च चित्राभ्यां मालया च स चित्रया।।५ निकुम्भो भूषणैाति तेन स्म परिघेण च। यथेन्द्रधनुषा मेघः सविद्युत्स्तनयित्नुमान्॥
en: With gold adorning his breast, and Angadas placed on his arms and a pair of curious and variegated ear-rings, Nikumbha, with his ornaments and that same bludgeon, appeared beautiful like a mass of roaring clouds laughing with lightning and furnished with the iris.

sn: परिघाग्रेण पुस्फोट वातग्रन्धिर्महात्मनः। प्रजज्वाल सघोषश्च विधूम इव पावकः॥
en: The head of that huge-bodied hero's parigha undid the conjunction of the seven' Winds and appeared? like a noiseless and smokeless flame. 1. This indicates the length of the Parigha. 2. This might refer to Kumbha as well.

sn: नगर्या विटपावत्या गन्धर्वभवनोत्तमैः। सतारागणनक्षत्रं सचन्द्रसमहाग्रहम्।। निकुम्भपरिघाघूर्ण भ्रमतीव नभस्थलम्॥
en: Along with the gyration of Nikumbha's parigha the whole welkin, together with the excellent city* of the gandharvas, and the planets, stars and the moon, began to whirl. *Some say Vitapabati and some say Alaka.

sn: दुरासदश्च संजज्ञे परिघाभरणप्रभः। क्रोधेन्धनो निकुम्भाग्नियुगान्ताग्निरिवोत्थितः॥
en: Nikumbha was hard to approach like to the fire of dissolution, being resplendent with the brilliance of parigha and other ornaments and having his anger for its fuels.

sn: राक्षसा वानराश्चापि न शेकुः स्पन्दितुं भयात्। हनुमांस्तु विवृत्योरस्तस्थौ प्रमुखतो बली॥
en: The Rākşasas and monkeys did not dare stir even out of fear. And the heroic Hanumān, spreading his breast, stood before him.

sn: परिघोपमबाहुस्तु परिघं भास्करप्रभम्। बली बलवतस्तस्य पातयामास वक्षसि॥
en: Thereat the powerful (Nikumbha) having long-arm* threw his parigha resembling the Sun at the breast of that powerful one. *Lit. arms resembling parighas.

sn: स्थिरे तस्योरसि व्यूढे परिघः शतधा कृतः। विकीर्यमाणः सहसा उल्काशतमिवाम्बरे॥
en: Falling on the firm and spacious breast of Hanumān it was broken into hundred pieces. The broken portions, being scattered, appeared like hundreds of fire-brands in the sky.

sn: स तु तेन प्रहारेण न चचाल महाकपिः। परिघेण समाधूतो यथा भूमिचलेऽचलः॥
en: Like to a mountain standing still even at the time of an earthquake that mighty monkey was not moved albeit struck with the parigha.

sn: स तथाभिहतस्तेन हनूमान् प्लवगोत्तमः। मुष्टिं संवर्तयामास बलेनातिमहाबलः॥
en: Being thus hurt that highly powerful Hanumān, the foremost of the monkeys, with great velocity clenched his fist.

sn: तमुद्यम्य महातेजा निकुम्भोरसि वीर्यवान्। अभिचिक्षेप वेगेन वेगवान्वायुविक्रमः॥
en: With this, the powerful (monkey) gifted with great impetuosity, and resembling the wind in prowess, struck Nikumbha on his breast.

sn: तत्र पुस्फोट वर्मास्य प्रसुस्राव च शोणितम्। मुष्टिना तेन संजज्ञे मेघे विद्युदिवोत्थिता॥
en: With that fist, his (Nikumbha's) armour* was riven and blood gushed out. And a light rising out of his breast suddenly disappeared like to lightning disappearing in a mass of clouds. *Some texts read carma (skin) in the place of Varma-(armour) i.e., his skin was rent-This equally indicates Hanuman's strength.

sn: स तु तेन प्रहारेण निकुम्भो विचचाल च। स्वस्थश्चापि निजग्राह हनूमन्तं महाबलम्॥
en: Being struck with his (Hanuman's) fist Nikumbha was greatly moved and restoring himself attacked the mighty Hanumān and pulled him up.

sn: चुक्रुशुश्च तदा संख्ये भीमं लङ्कानिवासिनः। निकुम्भेनोद्यतं दृष्ट्वा हनूमन्तं महाबलम्॥
en: Beholding in conflict the terrible and powerful Hanumăn pulled up by Nikumbha, the residents of Lankā began to shout with joy.

sn: स तथा ह्रियमाणोऽपि हनूमांस्तेन रक्षसा। आजघाननिलसुतो वज्रकल्पेन मुष्टिना॥
en: Being thus put to shame by that Rākşasa, Hanumăn the son of the Wind, struck him with his iron fist.

sn: आत्मानं मोक्षयित्वाथ क्षितावभ्यवपद्यत। हनूमानुन्ममाथाशु निकुम्भं मारुतात्मजः॥
en: And releasing himself from the grasp of Nikumbha, Hanumān the Wind-god's son instantly planted his foot on the earth.

sn: निक्षिप्य परमायत्तो निकुम्भं निष्पिपेष च। उत्पत्य चास्य वेगेन पपातोरसि वेगवान् ॥ परिगृह्य च बाहुभ्यां परिवृत्य शिरोधराम्। उत्पाटयामास शिरो भैरवं नदतो महत्॥
en: Inflamed with ire, he, throwing down Nikumbha, began to crush him; and gifted with vehemence, he, with great impetuosity, leaped up and sat on the breast (of the Raksa). And halding his head with two hands, he, emitting loud roars, displaced his head.

sn: अथ निनदति सादिते निकुम्भे पवनसुतेन रणे बभूव युद्धम्। {शतरमागतरोषयोः सुभीमम्॥
en: Nikumbha being thus slain in conflict by the Wind-god's son, there ensued a terrible conflict between the highly enraged armies of the son of Dasaratha and the lord of Rākşasas.

sn: व्यपेते तु जीवे निकुम्भस्य हृष्टा विनेदुः प्लवंगा दिश: सस्वनुश्च । बलं राक्षसानां भयं चाविवेश॥
en: Nikumbha being deprived of his life, the monkeys began to shout-as if resounding all the quarters. And with it the whole earth moved and the abode of the celestials dropped down. And the Rākşasas-hosts were greatly terrified.

sn: निकुम्भं निहतं दृष्ट्वा कुम्भं च विनिपातितम्। रावणः परमामर्षी प्रजज्वालानलो यथा॥
en: Beholding Kumbha and Nikumbha slain, Rāvana was excited with ire like to flaming fire.

sn: नैर्ऋतः क्रोधशोकाभ्यां द्वाभ्यां तु परिमूर्च्छितः। खरपुत्रं विशालाक्षं मकराक्षमचोदयत्॥ गच्छ पुत्र मयाज्ञप्तो बलेनाभिसमन्वितः। राघवं लक्ष्मणं चैव जहि तौ सवनौकसौ॥
en: Being beside himself, simultaneously with wrath and grief Rāvana* spoke to Makarāksa, Kahara's son, having spacious eyes, saying, O child, do you proceed at my command with the army and destroy Rāghava and Laksmana with all the monkeys. *Nairta is another name of Ravana.

sn: रावणस्य वचः श्रुत्वा शूरमानी खरात्मजः। बाढमित्यब्रवीद्धृष्टो मकराक्षो निशाचरम्॥ सोऽभिवाद्य दशग्रीवं कृत्वा चापि प्रदक्षिणम्। निर्जगाम गृहाच्छुभ्राद्रावणस्याज्ञया बली ॥
en: Hearing the words of Rāvana, Khara's son, Makarākşa, proud of his own own prowess, delightedly spoke to the night-ranger, saying, “Be it so." And saluting and circumambulating the ten-necked one, that hero, at Ravana's behest, issued out of the house.

sn: समीपस्थं बलाध्यक्षं खरपुत्रोऽब्रवीद्वचः। रथमानीयतां तूर्णं सैन्यं त्वानीयतां त्वरात्॥
en: Khara's son spoke to the commander who was near him, saying, “Do you speedily bring the chariot here and all the soldiers."

sn: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा बलाध्यक्षो निशाचरः। स्यन्दनं च बलं चैव समीपं प्रत्यपादयत्॥
en: Hearing his words, that commanding nightranger, soon let before him the army and the chariot.

sn: प्र.क्षेणं रथं कृत्वा समाहूय निशाचरः। संचोदयायास शीघ्रं वै रथमावह॥
en: And going round the chariot and addressing the charioteer that night-ranger (Makarāksa) said, O charioteer, do you soon drive the chariot.

sn: अथ ताराक्षसान्सर्वान्मकराक्षोऽब्रवीदिदम्। यूयं सर्वे प्रयुध्यध्वं पुरस्तान्मम राक्षसाः॥
en: Thereat Makarākṣa addressed those Räkşasas, saying, O Raksasas! do you all fight before me.

sn: अहं राक्षसराजेन रावणेन महात्मना। आज्ञप्तः समरे हन्तुं तावुभौ रामलक्ष्मणौ ॥
en: I have been commanded by the high-souled Rāvana, the lord of Räksasas, to slay both Rāma and Lakşmaņa in conflict.

sn: अद्य रामं वधिष्यामि लक्ष्मणं च निशाचराः। शाखामृगं च सुग्रीवं वानरांश्च शरोत्तमैः॥
en: I shall slay to-day, O night-ranger, with my excellent arrows, Rama, Laksmana, Sugriva and all other monkeys.

sn: अद्य शूलनिपातैश्च वानराणां महाचमूम्। प्रदहिष्यामि संप्राप्तां शुष्कन्धनमिवानलः॥
en: Like to fire consuming dry fuel, shall I today slay the host of monkeys with my darts.

sn: मकराक्षस्य तच्छुत्वा वचनं ते निशाचराः। सर्वे नानायुधोपेता बलवन्तः समाहिताः॥
en: Hearing those words of Makarākşa, the mighty night-rangers, (addressed themselves for fight).

sn: ते कामरूपिणः क्रूरा दंष्ट्रिणः पिङ्गलेक्षणः। मातंगा इव नर्दन्तो ध्वस्तकेशा भयावहाः॥ परिवार्य महाकाया महाकायं खरात्मजम्। अभिजघ्नुस्ततो हृष्टाश्चालयन्तो नभस्तलम्॥
en: They were armed with various weapons, cautious; assuming shapes at will, crooked, having fearful teeth, coppery eyes; roaring like elephants, having dishevelled hair and terrible. And encircling the huge-bodied son of Khara, those gigantic (Raksasas) began to proceed, delighted and moving the earth (with the weight of their persons).

sn: शङ्खभेरीसहस्राणामाहतानां समन्ततः। क्ष्वेलितास्फोटितानां च तत्र शब्दो महानभूत्॥
en: There arose a terrible noise on all sides from the sound of conches, and thousands of bugles, and from the moving of the arms of the heroes.

sn: प्रभ्रष्टोऽथ करात्तस्य प्रतोदः सारथेस्तदा। पपात सहसा दैवाद्ध्वजस्तस्य तु रक्षसः॥
en: And all on a sudden the reins slipped off (the hands of) the charioteer and the flag of the Råkşasas dropped down.

sn: तस्य ते रथसंयुक्ता हया विक्रमवर्जिताः। चरणैराकुलैर्गत्वा दीनाः सास्रमुखा ययुः॥
en: The course of the steeds was thus slackened and they began to move slowly and poorly with their heads drooping down.

sn: प्रवाति पवनस्तस्मिन्सपांसुः खरदारुणः। निर्याणे तस्य रौद्रस्य मकराक्षस्य दुर्मते॥
en: There blew a terribly rough wind mixed with dust when the fearfully wicked-minded Makaraksa's issued out for battle.

sn: तानि दृष्ट्वा निमित्तानि राक्षसा वीर्यवत्तमाः। अचिन्त्य निर्गताः सर्वे यत्र तौ रामलक्ष्मणौ॥
en: Those powerful Rākşasas neglecting those bad omens proceeded towards where Rāma and Laksmana were.

sn: घनगजमहिषाङ्गतुल्यवर्णा समरमुखेष्वसकृद्गदासिभिन्नाः। अहमहमिति युद्धकौशलास्ते स्जनिचराः परिबभ्रमुर्मुहुस्ते॥
en: They were all black like to clouds, elephants and buffaloes, and had marks of swords and maces on their persons. And all those nightrangers were skilled in the art of warfare and began to range to and fro (in the battle field) saying, “I shall to first.”

sn: निर्गतं मकराक्षं ते दृष्ट्वा वानरपुङ्गवाः। आप्लुत्य सहसा सर्वे योद्धकामा व्यवस्थिताः॥
en: Beholding Makarākṣa out for battle, those foremost monkeys leaping on a sudden, addressed themselves for fight.

sn: ततः प्रवृत्तं सुमहत्तद्युद्धं लोमहर्षणम्। निशाचरैः प्लवंगानां देवानां दानवैरिव ॥
en: Thereupon ensued a terrible conflict, capable of making one's down stand on end, between the right-rangers and the monkeys like to one between the celestials and Dänavas.

sn: वृक्षशूलनिपातैश्च गदापरिघपातनैः। अन्योन्यं मर्दयन्ति स्म तदा कपिनिशाचराः।३।।
en: Those monkeys and night-rangers crushed each other down with trees, darts, maces and parighas.

sn: शक्तिखङ्गादाकुन्तैस्तोमरैश्च निशाचराः। पट्टिशैभिन्दिपालैश्च बाणपातैः समन्ततः॥ पाशमुद्गरदण्डैश्च नितिश्चापरैस्तथा। कदनं कपिसिंहानां चक्रुस्ते रजनीचराः॥
en: Those night-rangers began to assail those foremost of monkeys with sakti.' swords, maces, kuntas, tomaras, pattisas, Bhindipālas, arrows, nooses and clubs. 1. A short arrow thrown from the hand or shot through a tube. 2. An Iron spear or dart.

sn: बाणौरर्दिताश्चापि खरपुत्रेण वानराः। संभ्रान्तमनसः सर्वे दुद्रुवुर्भयपीडिताः॥
en: Being thus assailed with fearful arrows by Khara's son, those monkeys, stricken with fear, fled away.

sn: तान्दृष्ट्वा राक्षसाः सर्वे द्रवमाणान्वनौकसः। नेदुस्ते सिंहवहुप्ता राक्षसा जितकाशिनः॥
en: Beholding those monkeys fly away, all the victorious Rakşasas began to roar like excited lions.

sn: विद्रवत्सु तदा तेषु वानरेषु समन्ततः। रामस्तान्वारयामास शरवर्षेण राक्षसान् ॥
en: The monkeys thus flying away to all quarters, Rāma with a downpour of shafts assailed the Räkşasas.

sn: वारिताराक्षसान्दृष्ट्वा मकराक्षो निशाचरः। कोपानलसमाविष्टो वचनं चेदमब्रवीत्॥
en: Beholding the Rākşasas thus overpowered, the night-ranger Makarākşa, excited with the flame of ire, said.

sn: तिष्ठ राम मया साधं द्वन्द्वयुद्धं भविष्यति। त्याजयिष्यामि ते प्राणान्धनुर्मुक्तैः शितैः शरैः॥
en: Stay, O Rama, let us both fight with each other; I shall take your life with sharp arrows discharged off my bow.

sn: यत्तदा दण्डकारण्ये पितरं हतवान्मम। तदग्रतः स्वकर्मस्थं स्मृत्वा रोषोऽभिवर्धते॥
en: You did slay my father in the forest of Dandaka. Remembering your action and finding you before, my ire is excited.

sn: दह्यन्ते भृशमङ्गानि दुरात्मन्मम राघव। यन्मयासि न दृष्टस्त्वं तस्मिन्काले महावने॥
en: O Raghava! O Vicious souled one! My limbs are being burnt (with wrath) for I did not see you then in that mighty forest.

sn: दिष्ट्यासि दर्शनं राम मम त्वं प्राप्तवानिह। काशितोऽसि क्षुधार्तस्य सिंहस्येवेतरो मृगः॥
en: O Rāma, by my good luck, I have got you today, like to a hungry lion desiring to have other animals.

sn: अद्य मद्वाणवेगेन प्रेतराविषयं गतः। ये त्वया निहताः शूराः सह तैश्च वसिष्यसि ॥
en: Being despatched by my arrows to the world of devils, you shall live with those heroes, who had been killed by you before.

sn: बहुनात्र किमुक्तेन शृणु राम वचो मम। पश्यन्तु सकला लोकात्स्वां मां चैव रणाजिरे॥
en: What is the use of speaking more, O Rāma, do you hear my words. Let all the people behold your as well as my prowess in the battle-field.

sn: अस्त्रैर्वा गदया वापि बाहुभ्यां वा रणाजिरे। अभ्यस्तं येन वा राम वर्ततां तेन वा मृधम्॥
en: Either with weapon or with clubs, in whatever you are expert, do you fight .with me in the battle-field, O Rāma.

sn: मकराक्षवचः श्रुत्वा रामो दशरथात्मजः। अब्रवीत्प्रहसन्वाक्यमुत्तरोत्तरवादिनम्॥
en: Hearing the words of Makarākşa, Rāma, Dasaratha's son, smiling, replied to the words of the babbler.

sn: कत्थसे किं वृथा रक्षो बहून्यसदृशानि ते। न रणे शक्यते जेतुं विना युद्धेन वाग्बलात्॥
en: O Rākşasa, what is the use of idle prating? None can achieve success in a battle with idle words—but with fighting.

sn: त्ततुर्दश सहस्राणि रक्षसां त्वत्पिता च यः। विपि. दूषणाश्चापि दण्डके निहतो मया॥ स्वाशिताश्चापि मांसेन गृध्रगोमायुवायसाः। भविष्यन्त्यद्य वै पाप तीक्ष्णतुण्डनखाङ्कुशाः॥
en: I slew in the forest of Dandaka your father with fourteen thousand Räksasas, Trisira and Duşana. O vile one, you being slain to day, with your flesh, vultures and crows, having sharp beaks and nails, and jackals shall be satisfied.* [*Here is another śloka, which is to be found in all N.W.P. texts and in one or two texts published in Bengal-but it has been omitted by many for it conveys the same meaning as the previous ſloka; the meaning is-And the birds drinking your blood shall fly away to various quarters.]

sn: राघवेणैवमुक्तस्तु मकराक्षो महाबलः। बाणौधानमुचत्तस्मै राघवाय रणाजिरे॥
en: Being thus addressed by Rāghava, the mighty Makarākşa, began to dart sharp arrows towards him in the battle-field.

sn: ताञ्छराञ्छरवर्षेण रामाश्चिच्छेद नैकधा। निपेतुर्भुवि विच्छिन्ना रुक्मपुङ्खाः सुवाससः॥
en: And Rāma, with his shafts, sundered into several pieces, those arrows. And being thus rendered useless those arrows, feathered in gold, fell down on the earth.

sn: तद्युद्धमभवत्तत्र समेत्यान्योन्यमोजसा। खरराक्षसपुत्रस्य सूनोर्दशरथस्य च॥
en: Then there arose a terrible conflict between the Raksasa Khara's son and Dasaratha's son.

sn: जीमूतयोरिवाकाशे शब्दो ज्यातलयोरिव। धनुर्मुक्तः स्वनोऽन्योन्यं श्रूयते च रणाजिरे॥
en: There were audible in that battle-field, the outcry of the heroes and the twang of the bows stretched by their hands, like to the muttering of the clouds in the sky.

sn: देवदानवगन्धर्वाः किंनराश्च महोरगाः। अन्तरिक्षगताः सर्वे द्रष्टकामास्तदद्भुतम्॥
en: To see that wondrous conflict, the celestials, Dānavas, Gandharvas, Kinnaras and the mighty serpents stationed themselves in the sky.

sn: विद्धमन्योन्यगात्रेषु द्विगुणं वर्धते बलम्। कृतप्रतिकृतान्योन्यं कुरुतां तौ रणाजिरे॥ राममुक्तांस्तु बाणौघाराक्षसस्त्वच्छिनद्रणे। रक्षोमुक्तांस्तु रामो वै नैकधा प्राच्छिनच्छरैः॥
en: They were wounded with the discharged by each other and their strength was doubled. And they began to fight in that battlefield one attacking and the other withstanding the attack. And in that conflict the Rākşasa artOWS sundered the shafts discharged by Räma. And likewise Rāma severed into several pieces the arrows shot by the Räksasa.

sn: बाणौघवितताः सर्वा दिशश्च प्रदिशस्तथा। संछना वसुधा चैव समन्तान प्रकाशते॥
en: All the quarters were covered with arrows and nothing on earth or in the sky was visible.

sn: ततः क्रुद्धो महाबाहुर्धनुश्चिच्छेद संयुगे। अष्टाभिरथ नाराचैः सूतं विव्याध राघवः॥
en: Thereupon being excited with ire, Rāghava of long arms sundered his (Raksasa's) bow in conflict and with eight Näräcas pierced the charioteer.

sn: भित्त्वा रथं शरै रामो हत्वा अश्वानपातयत्। विरथो वसुधास्थः स मकाराक्षो निशाचरः॥
en: And with arrows Rāma sundered the chariot and killing the horses brought them down. And the night-ranger Makarākṣa was brought down on the earth from the chariot.

sn: तत्तिष्ठद्वसुधां रक्षः शूलं जग्राह पाणिना। त्रासनं सर्वभूतानां युगान्ताग्निसमप्रभम्॥ दुरवापं महच्छूलं रुद्रदत्तं भयंकरम्। जाज्वल्यमानमाकाशे संहारास्त्रमिवापरम्॥
