en: He then again rose up with a dart in his hand creating terror to all creatures and resembling the Fire of Dissolution in resplendence. It was a terribly huge dart conferred on him by Śiva, shining in the sky in its native brilliance and like to another weapon of destruction.* *This refers to the weapon used by Śiva for destruction-for Siva, according to the Hindu Mythology is the God of destruction.

sn: यं दृष्ट्वा देवताः सर्वा भयार्ता विद्वता दिशः। विभ्राम्य च महच्छूलं प्रज्वलन्तं निशाचरः॥ स क्रोधात्प्राहिणोत्तस्मै राघवाय महात्मने।
en: Beholding which dart even the celestials fly away in fear to different quarters. And taking up that huge flaming dart, the night-ranger, being excited with ire, hurled it at the high-souled Rāghava.

sn: तमापतन्तं ज्वलितं खरपुत्रकराच्च्युतम्॥ बाणैश्चतुर्भिराकाशे शूलं चिच्छेद राघवः।
en: Rāghava, with four shafts, sundered that dart, in the sky, flaming and hurled at him by the son of Khara.

sn: स भिन्नो नैकधा शूलो दिव्यहाटकमण्डितः।। व्यशीर्यत महोल्केव रामबाणादितो भुवि॥
en: That flaming dart, feathered in gold, being splintered into several pieces by Rāma's arrows fell down on earth like a huge fire-brand.

sn: तच्छूलं निहतं दृष्ट्वा रामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा। साधु साध्विति भूतानि व्याहरन्ति नभोगताः॥
en: Beholding that dart beffled thus by Rāma of unwearied actions all those, stationed in the welkin began to shout, “Well done! Well done!"

sn: तं दृष्ट्वा निहतं शूलं मकराक्षो निशाचरः। मुष्टिमुद्यम्य काकुत्स्थं तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति चाब्रवीत्॥
en: Beholding his dart thus sundered, the nightranger Makarākșa clenching his fist spoke to Kakutstha, saying, "Stay! Stay!"

sn: स तं दृष्ट्वा पतन्तं तु प्रहस्य रघुनन्दनः। पावकास्त्रं ततो रामः संदधे तु शरासने॥
en: Seeing him advance thus, the descendant of Raghu, smiling, fixed a fiery arrow on his bow.

sn: तेनास्त्रेण हतं रक्षः काकुत्स्थेन तदा रणे। सच्छिन्नहृदयं तत्र पपात च ममार च॥
en: With that arrow the Räksa was slain by Kākutstha in battle. And having his heart pierced he fell down and died.

sn: दृष्ट्वा ते राक्षसाः सर्वे मकराक्षस्य पातनम्। लङ्कामेव प्रधावन्त रामबाणभयार्दिताः॥
en: Beholding Makarākṣa thus slain all the Rāks asas, being afraid of Rama's arrows, proceeded towards Lankā.

sn: दशरथनृपसूनुबाणवेगै रजनिचरं निहतं खरात्मजं तम्। प्रददृशुरथ देवताः : प्रहृष्टा गिरिमिव वज्रहतं यथा विकीर्णम् ॥
en: Seeing that night-ranger, the son of Khara, slain by Rāma's arrows, like to a mountain clept by a thunder-bolt, the celestials were greatly delighted.

sn: मकराक्षं हतं श्रुत्वा रावणः समितिंजयः। रोषेण महताविष्टो दन्तान्कटकटाय्य च॥
en: Hearing of the destruction of Makarākşa, the heroic Răvaņa, being excited with ire, began to grind his teeth.

sn: कुपितश्च तदा तत्र किं कार्यमिति चिन्तयन्। आदिदेशाथ संकुद्धो रणायेन्द्रजितं सुतम्॥
en: Being thus angered, and thinking within himself what steps to take, he ordered his son Indrajit to proceed to the battle-field.

sn: जहि वीर महावीयौं भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ। अदृश्योदृश्यमानो वा सर्वथा त्वं बलाधिकः॥
en: O hero, gifted with great prowess as you are, do you, hidden (in clouds) or appearing before them, slay the two heroic brothers Rāma and Laksmana.

sn: त्वमप्रतिमकर्माणमिन्द्रं जयसि संयुगे। किं पुनर्मानुषौ दृष्ट्वा न वधिष्यसि संयुगे॥
en: You did defeat in conflict Indra of unequalled prowess. Shall you then neglect to slay men as they are?

sn: तथोक्तो राक्षसेन्द्रेण प्रतिगृह्य पितुर्वचः। यज्ञभूमौ स विधिवत्पावकं जुहवेन्द्रजित् ॥
en: Being thus addressed by the lord of the Raks asas and obeying his father's command, Indrajit proceeded towards the sacrificial ground to satisfy Fire (with oblations).

sn: जुह्वतश्चापि तत्राग्नि रक्तोष्णीषधराः स्त्रियः। आजग्मुस्तत्र संभ्रान्ता राक्षस्यो यत्र रावणिः॥
en: There came some she-demons with crimson turbans and waited respectfully where Rävaņa's son was offering oblations to Fire.

sn: शस्त्राणि शरपत्राणि समिधोऽथ बिभीतकाः। लोहितानि च वासांसि स्रुवं कार्णायसं तथा॥
en: In that sacrifice the weapons were the leaves of sara,' bibhitakas? were fuels, and there were brought crimson clothes and sruvas made of black iron. 1. Saccharum-a reed or grass. 2. Beleric myrobalan. 3. A ladle with a double extremity or two oval collateral excavations made of wood to pour ghee

sn: सर्वतोऽग्नि समास्तीर्य शरपत्रैः सतोमरैः। छागस्य सर्वकृष्णस्य गलं जग्राह जीवतः॥
en: Spreading fire on all sides with śare leaves and Tomaras, (Indrajit) caught a living goat, all black, by the neck.

sn: शरहोमसमिद्धस्य विधूमस्य महार्चिषः। बभूवुस्तानि लिङ्गानि विजयं दर्शयन्ति च।९।।
en: The fire, with oblations of sara, became greatly blazed and devoid of smoke. There were visible many good omens indicating victory.

sn: प्रदक्षिणावर्तशिखस्तप्तहाटकसंनिभः। हविस्तत्प्रतिजग्राह पावकः स्वयमुत्थितः॥
en: The flame of the fire was like to gold, and moving Southwards began to receive offerings of clarified butter.

sn: हुत्वाग्नि तर्पयित्वाथ देवदानवराक्षसान्। आरुरोह रथश्रेष्ठमन्तर्धानगतं शुभम्॥
en: Thus offering oblations to fire and to celestials, Dänavas and Raksasas, he ascended in excellent car and soon disappeared.

sn: स वाजिभिश्चतुर्भिस्तु बाणैस्तु निशितैर्युतः। आरोपितमहाचापः शुशुभे स्यन्दनोत्तमे॥
en: It was drawn by four horses and a huge bow, set with sharp arrows, appeared beautiful on that excellent car.

sn: जाज्वल्यमानो वपुषा तपनीयपरिच्छदः। मृगैश्चन्द्रार्धचन्द्रश्च स रथः समलंकृतः॥
en: The chariot was brilliant with its own native resplendence, adorned with gold and painted with the figures of deer and a cresent.

sn: जाम्बूनदमहाकम्बुर्दीप्तपावकसंनिभः। बभूवेन्द्रजितः केतुर्वैदूर्यसमलंकृतः॥
en: It was encircled on all sides with golden bracelets, adorned with flags made of viadurja and was like to the flaming fire.

sn: तेन चादित्यकल्पने ब्रह्मास्त्रेण च पालितः। स बभूव दुराधर्षो रावणिः सुमहाबलः॥
en: Being thus well protected with Brahma weapons resembling the Sun in brilliance, the mighty son of Rāvana became invincible.

sn: सोऽभिनिर्याय नगरादिन्द्रजित्समितिंजयः। हुत्वाग्नि राक्षसैर्मन्त्रैरन्तर्धानगतोऽब्रवीत्॥
en: Offering oblations to Fire in accordance with demoniac incantations and thus obtaining the power of hiding himself, that hero, ever victorious in battle, issued out of the city and said.

sn: अद्य हत्वा रणे यौ तौ मिथ्या प्रव्रजितौ वने। जयं पित्रे प्रदास्यामि रावणाय रणेऽधिकम्॥
en: Slaying these two brothers in battle, who have uselessly wandered away into the forest, shall I crown my father Răvana with victory.

sn: अद्य निर्वानरामुर्वी हत्वा रामं च लक्ष्मणम्। करिष्ये परमां प्रीतिमित्युक्त्वान्तरधीयत॥
en: Destroying Rāma and Lakşmaņa, and clearing the monkeys off the earth, shall I satisfy my sire greatly. Saying this, he disappeared from their view.

sn: आपपाताथ संक्रुद्धो दशग्रीवेण चोदितः। तीक्ष्णकार्मुकनाराचैस्तीक्ष्णस्त्विन्द्ररिपू रणे॥
en: Thereupon that fearful foe of the lord of celestials appeared in the battle-field, excited with wrath, armed with bow and sharp Nārācas and commissioned thus by the Ten-necked one.

sn: स ददर्श महावीयौँ नागौ त्रिशिरसाविव। सृजन्ताविषुजालानि वीरौ वानरमध्यगौ॥
en: He beheld there those two heroes discharging flaming arrows and surrounded by the monkeys like to the fearful three-hooded serpent in the midst of other serpents.

sn: इमौ ताविति संचिन्त्य सज्यं कृत्वा च कार्मुकम्। संततानिषुधाराभिः पर्जन्य इव वृष्टिमान्॥
en: Thinking "these must be both brothers, Rāma and Lakşmaņa," and stretching his bow he began showering arrows like to clouds.

sn: स तु वैहायसरथो युधि तौ रामलक्ष्मणौ। अचक्षुर्विषये तिष्ठन्विव्याध निशितैः शरैः॥
en: He was seated in a car in the welkin and hidden from the human gaze and began to assail! Ráma and Lakşmaņa with sharp shafts.

sn: तौ तस्य शरवेगेन परीतौ रामलक्ष्मणौ। धनुषी सशरे कृत्वा दिव्यमस्त्रं प्रचक्रतुः॥
en: Being hurt with the arrows, Rāma and Lakş mana, fixing arrows on their bows, began to discharge celestial shafts.

sn: प्रच्छादयन्तौ गगनं शरजालैर्महाबलौ। तमस्त्रैः सूर्यसंकाशैनँव पस्पर्शतुः शरैः॥
en: Those two highly powerful heroes could not even touch his person with their arrows resembling the Sun albeit they covered the whole welkin therewith.

sn: स हि धूमान्धकारं च चक्रे प्रच्छादयन्नभः। दिशश्चान्तर्दधे श्रीमान्त्रीहारतमसा वृतः॥
en: And clouding the whole sky with smoke that effulgent one, enveloped in frost, his himself from their gaze.

sn: नैव ज्यातलनिर्घोषी न च नेमिखुरस्वनः। शुश्रुवे चरतस्तस्य न च रूपं प्रकाशते॥
en: There was not audible the twang of kis bow, the sound of the wheels, or the noise of the steeds. Nor was he seen by any.

sn: घनान्धकारे तिमिरे शिलावर्षमिवाद्भुतम्। स ववर्ष महाबाहुर्नाराचशरवृष्टिभिः॥
en: In that terrible darkness of clouds that one of mighty arms began to make a downpour of Nāracas and arrows like hail storms.

sn: स रामं सूर्यसंकाशैः शरैर्दत्तवरै शम्। विव्याध समरे क्रुद्धः सर्वगात्रेषु रावणिः॥
en: In that encounter, Rāvana's son, inflamed with ire, wounded Rāma, with shafts, resembling the Sun and obtained by him as a boon.

sn: तौ हन्यमानौ नाराचैर्धाराभिरिव पर्वतौ। हेमपुवानरव्याघ्रौ तिग्मान्मुमुचतुः शरान्॥
en: Being hurt with Nārāchas, like to mountains wet with rain, those two foremost of men, began to discharge shafts feathered in gold.

sn: अन्तरिक्षे समासाद्य रावणिं कङ्कपत्रिणः। निकृत्य पतगा भूमौ पेतुस्ते शोणिताप्लुताः॥
en: Reaching the son of Rāvana in the sky and soaked in blood those golden arrows, fell down on earth.

sn: अतिमात्रं शरौघेण दीप्यमानौ नरोत्तमौ। तानिषून्पततो भल्लैरनेकैविचकर्ततुः॥
en: Those two best of men, hurt with his arrows, became more effulgent and beffled the shafts discharged by the Räkşasa.

sn: यतो हि ददृशाते तो शरानिपतिताञ्छितान्। ततस्तु तौ दाशरथी ससृजातेऽस्त्रमुत्तमम्॥
en: Thereupon Rama and Lakşmaņa began to aim their sharp shafts to the direction whence the arrows came down.

sn: रावणिस्तु दिशः सर्वा रथेनातिरथोऽपतत्। विव्याध तौ दाशरथी लघ्वस्त्रौ निशितैः शरैः॥
en: And stationed in his chariot that mighty carwarrior disturbed all quarters with his arrows and pierced Dasaratha's sons with sharp shafts won by him.

sn: तेनातिविद्धौ तौ वीरौ रुक्मपुत्रैः सुसंहतैः। बभूवतुर्दाशरथी पुष्पिताविव किंशुकौ॥
en: Being greatly hurt with those sharp-pointed and terrible arrows Rāma and Lakşmaņa appeared like blossoming kingsukas.

sn: नास्य वेगगतिं कश्चिन्न च रूपं धनुः शरान्। न नास्य विदितं किंचित्सूर्यस्येवाभ्रसंप्लवे॥
en: Like to the sun hidden in clouds they could see neither his countenance and motion, nor his bow and arrows.

sn: तेन विद्धाश्च हरयो निहताश्च गतासवः। बभूवुः शतशस्तत्र पतिता धरणीतले।३६॥
en: Being wounded with those arrows hundreds of monkeys died and fell down on the earth.

sn: लक्ष्मणस्तु ततः क्रुद्धो भ्रातरं वाक्यमब्रवीत्। ब्राह्ममस्त्रं प्रयोक्ष्यामि वधार्थ सर्वरक्षसाम्॥
en: Thereupon Lakşmaņa, being excited with wrath, spoke to his brother, saying-"To slay all the Rākṣasas shall I discharge today Brahma weapon.'

sn: तमुवाच ततो रामो लक्ष्मणं शुभलक्षणम्। नैकस्य हेतो रक्षांसि पृथिव्यां हन्तुमर्हसि ॥
en: Thereupon Rāma spoke to Lakşmaņa, gifted with auspicious . marks, saying.-"It does not behove you to clear all the Rākşasas off the earth for the folly of one individual.

sn: अयुध्यमानं प्रच्छन्नं प्राञ्जलिं शरणागतम्। पलायमानं मत्तं वा न हन्तुं त्वमिहार्हसि॥ तस्यैव तु वधे यत्नं करिष्यामि महाभुज। आदेक्ष्यावो महावेगानस्त्रानाशीविषोपमान्॥
en: You should not slay him, who has retired from battle, has hidden himself, has sought your shelter, has stood before you with joined palms, has fled away or who is bewildered. O you of mighty-arms, let us try to slay him (Indrajit). And to accomplish it I shall use the weapons gifted with great impetuosity and resembling the serpents.

sn: तमेनं मायिनं क्षुद्रमन्तर्हितरथं बलात्। राक्षसं निहनिष्यन्ति दृष्ट्वा वानरयूथपाः॥
en: He is hidden from the public gaze so we must slay him, had he been fighting openly the leaders of the monkey hosts could have slain that Räks asas.

sn: यद्येष भूमिं विशते दिवं वा रसातलं वापि नभस्तलं वा। एवं विगूढोऽपि ममास्त्रदग्धः पतिष्यते भूमितले गतासुः।॥
en: Truly he shall be burnt to death with my shafts and fall down on the earth albeit he entered the regions under the earth of the abode of the celestials.

sn: इत्येवमुक्त्वा वचनं महाथ रघुप्रवीरः प्लवगर्षभैर्वृतः। स्तदा महात्मा त्वरितं निरीक्षते।४३॥
en: Having said these words pregnant with a high significance, the high-souled and heroic descendant of Raghu, being surrounded by monkeys, began to concert various plans for the destruction of that terrible Raksasa of wicked deeds.

sn: विज्ञाय तु मनस्तस्य राघवस्य महात्मनः। स निवृत्याहवात्तस्मात्प्रविवेश पुरं ततः॥
en: Having read the intention of that high-souled Raghava, he retired from the battle-field and entered into the city of Lankā.

sn: सोऽनुस्मृत्य वधं तेषां राक्षसानां तरस्विनाम्। क्रोधताप्रेक्षणः शूरो निर्जगामाथ रावणिः॥
en: And remembering the destruction of many a। quick-paced Raksasa, his eyes were rendered coppery with ire; and that hero, the son of Ravana, issued out of the city again.

sn: स पश्चिमेन द्वारेण निर्ययौ राक्षसैर्वृतः। इन्द्रजित्सुमहावीर्य: पौलस्त्यो देवकण्टकः॥
en: That highly powerful, Indrajit, a descendant of Pulasta and an enemy of the celestials, issued out, encircled by the Rākşasas, by the western gate.

sn: इन्द्रजित्तु ततो दृष्ट्वा भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ। रणायात्युद्धतौ वीरौ मायां प्रादुष्करोत्तदा॥
en: Then beholding the heroic brothers Rāma and Lakşmaņa prepared for fight, Indrajit spread illusions.

sn: इन्द्रजित्तु रथे स्थाप्य सीतां मायामयीं तदा। बलेन महतावृत्य तस्या वधमरोचयत्॥
en: Placing an illusory figure of Sītā on the car, encircled by a huge army he began to make arrangements for her destruction.

sn: मोहनार्थं तु सर्वेषां बुद्धिं कृत्वा सुदुर्मतिः। हन्तुं सीतां व्यवसितो वानराभिमुखो ययौ॥
en: Desiring to charm all with his illusions, that one of wicked intent, preparing himself to slay Sītā, proceeded towards the monkeys.

sn: तं दृष्ट्वा त्वभिनिर्यान्तं सर्वे ते काननौकसः। उत्पेतुरभिसंक्रुद्धाः शिलाहस्ता युयुत्सवः॥
en: Beholding him thus proceed, the monkeys, inflamed with ire, desirous of fighting and with crags in their hands, moved on.

sn: हनूमान्पुरतस्तेषां जगाम कपिकुञ्जरः। प्रगृह्य सुमहच्छ्रङ्ग पर्वतस्य दुरासदम्।।।।
en: And preceded them all, Hanuman, the foremost of the monkeys, with a huge mountaintop in his hand.

sn: स ददर्श हतानन्दां सीतामिन्द्रजितो रथे। एकवेणिधरां दीनामुपवासकृशाननाम्॥
en: He beheld there, on Indrajit's car, Sita, deprived of all joy, poorly, greatly reduced with fasts and wearing a single braid.

sn: परिक्लिष्टैकवसनाममृजां राघवप्रियाम्। रजोमलाभ्यामालिप्तैः सर्वगात्रैर्वरस्त्रियम्॥
en: Rāghava's beloved spouse wore a piece of soiled cloth, and though highly beautiful, the grace of her person was greatly spoiled with dirt.

sn: तां निरीक्ष्य मुहूर्तं तु मैथिलीमध्यवस्य च। बभूवाचिरदृष्टा हि तेन सा जनकात्मजा॥
en: That daughter of Janaka, was not seen by him for a long time. And beholding her and deciding instantly that she is the daughter of Mithilā, (he became greatly sorry).

sn: अब्रवीचां तु शोकाता निरानन्द तपस्विनीम्। दृष्ट्वा रथस्थितां दीनां राक्षसेन्द्रसुतश्रिताम् ॥ किं समर्थितमस्येति चिन्तयन्स महाकपिः। सह तैर्वानरश्रेष्ठैरभ्यधावत रावणिम्॥
en: Seeing her on the car, innocent, poor, deprived of joy and brought under the influence of the son of the lord Rākşasas that great monkey thought within himself— 'What must be the intention of Indrajit?' and accompanied by heroic monkeys advanced towards the son of Ravana.

sn: तद्वानरबलं दृष्ट्वा रावणिः क्रोधमूर्च्छितः। कृत्वा विकोशं निस्त्रिंशं मूर्ध्नि सीतामकर्षयत्॥
en: Beholding that monkey host, Ravana's son became beside himself with ire and unsheathing his weapon Nistrinsha, caught her by the hair.

sn: तां स्त्रियं पश्यतां तेषां ताडयामास राक्षसः। क्रोशन्ती रामरामेति मायया योजितां रथे॥
en: The Räkşasa addressed himself to strike her in the presence of all those monkeys and that illusory figure of Sītā began to bewail saying, “O Rāma! O Rāma!”

sn: गृहीतमूर्धजां दृष्ट्वा हनूमान्दैन्यमागतः। दुःखजं वारि नेत्राभ्यामुत्सृजन्मारुतात्मजः॥
en: Seeing her thus caught by the head, Hanumān, the son of Maruta, greatly sorry, began to shed tears.

sn: तां दृष्ट्वा चारुसर्वाङ्गी रामस्य महिषीं प्रियाम्। अब्रवीत्परुषं वाक्यं क्रोधाद्रक्षोधिपात्मजम्॥
en: Beholding that beloved spouse of Räma, having a tender and beautiful person, he addressed angrily the son of the lord of Rākşasas with harsh words.

sn: दुरात्मनात्मनाशाय केशपक्षे परामृशः। ब्रह्मर्षीणां कुले जातो राक्षसी योनिमाश्रितः॥
en: It is for your destruction, O Vicious-souled one! that you have touched her hair. Being descended from that great Brahmă ascetic you are born as a Rākşasa.

sn: धिक्त्वां पापसमाचारं यस्य ते मतिरीदृशी। नृशंसानार्य दुर्वृत्त क्षुद्र पापपराक्रम। अनार्यस्येदृशं कर्म घृणा ते नास्ति निघृण ॥
en: O! cursed are you, since you have cherished such a desire and engaged in such a vicious deed. O vile! O wicked! O! cruel and dishonourable wight! O you having vice for your prowess!

sn: च्युता गृहाच्च राज्याच्च रामहस्ताच्च मैथिली। किं तवैषापराद्धा हि यदेनां हंसि निर्दय॥
en: O shameless! Are you not ashamed of perpetrating such an inhuman deed. What has Maithili done by you, O cruel one! that you are ready to slay her—She has been banished from her home, territory and has been separated from her lord.

sn: सीतां हत्वा तु न चिरं जीविष्यसि कथंचन। वधाहकर्मणा तेन मम हस्तगतो ह्यसि॥
en: O you worthy of being slain, destroying Sītā, you shall not live long as you have been brought under me.

sn: ये च स्त्रीघातिनां लोका लोकवध्यैश्च कुत्सिताः। इह जीवितमुत्सृज्य प्रेत्य तान्प्रति लप्स्यसे॥
en: You shall after the death reach the place which is occupied by those who murder women, a place which is avoided even by those who commit every sort of crime punishable by law.

sn: इति ब्रुवाणो हनुमान्सायुधैर्हरिभिर्वृतः। अभ्यधावत्सुसंक्रुद्धो राक्षसेन्द्रसुतं प्रति॥
en: Saying this Hanuman, accompanied by monkeys armed with weapons, and excited with ire, proceeded towards the son of the lord or Raksasas.

sn: आपतन्तं महावीर्य तदनीकं वनौकसाम्। रक्षसां भीमकोपानामनीकेन न्यवारयत्॥
en: Beholding the highly powerful monkeys advance thus the Rākṣasas, inflamed with wrath, obstructed them.

sn: स तां बाणसहस्रेण विक्षोभ्य हरिवाहिनीम्। हनूमन्तं हरिश्रेष्ठमिन्द्रिजित्प्रत्युवाच ह॥
en: Assailing the monkey-hosts with thousands of arrows, Indrajit spoke to that foremost of monkeys, Hanumān, saying.

sn: सुग्रीवस्त्वं च रामश्च यनिमित्तमिहागताः। तां वधिष्यामि वैदेहीमद्यैव तव पश्यतः॥ इमां हत्वा ततो राम लक्ष्मणं त्वां च वानर। सुग्रीवं च वधिष्यामि तं चानार्य विभीषणम्।२७॥
en: Today I shall slay before you all Vaidehī, for whom you, Sugriva and Rama have come. Slaying her, O monkey, I shall afterwards kill you, Rama, Laksmana and Sugriva and the dishonourable Vibhişaņa.

sn: न हन्तव्याः स्त्रियश्चेति यद्ब्रवीषि प्लवङ्गम। पीडाकरममित्राणां यच्च कर्तव्यमेव तत्॥
en: O monkey, about not destroying women, of which you were speaking (I might say) that we must always do what pains our enemies."* *There is one śloka intervening according to some texts, but it has been omitted by many. The reasons for this omission are best known to them. The purport is:-"Why did Rama slay Taraka before? And I shall therefore slay his spouse the daughter of king Janaka.” Hear in Indrajit attempts to justify himself and wants to prove that Räma is equally blameable for this.)

sn: तमेवमुक्त्वा रुदती सीतां मायामयीं च ताम्। शितधारेण खङ्गेन निजघानेन्द्रजित्स्वयम्॥
en: Saying this, Indrajit with a sharp sword, himself killed the illusory Sitā thus bewailing.

sn: यज्ञोपवीतमार्गेण छिन्ना तेन तपस्विनी। सा पृथिव्यां पृथुश्रोणी पपात प्रियदर्शना॥
en: Being sundered by him obliquely in a way in which a sacred thread lies on one's own person, the innocent (Sitā) having beautiful countenance fell down on the earth.

sn: तामिन्द्रजित्त्रियं हत्वा हनूमन्तमुवाच ह। मया रामस्य पश्येमां प्रियां शस्त्रनिषूदिताम्।। एषा विशस्ता वैदेही निष्फलो वः परिश्रमः॥
en: Slaying her Indrajit spoke to Hanumān,“Behold I have slain (before you) with my sword Rāma's beloved. And Vaidehi being thus slain, all your labours have been rendered useless."

sn: ततः खङ्गेन महता हत्वा तामिन्द्रजित्स्वयम्। हृष्टः स रथमास्थाय ननाद च महास्वनम्॥
en: a Destroying her with his own hand by means of a huge sword, Indrajit, greatly pleased ascended his car and began to emit dreadful roars.

sn: वानराः शुश्रुवुः शब्दमदूरे प्रत्यवस्थिताः। व्यादितास्यस्य नदतस्तदुर्ग संश्रितस्य तु॥
en: The monkeys stationed near heard that terrible roar and saw him enter the castel.* *The castle built by Indrajit by means of his illusory power in the air.

sn: तथा तु सीतां विनिहत्य दुर्मतिः प्रहष्टचेताः स बभूव रावणिः। तं हृष्टरूपं समुदीक्ष्य वानरा विषण्णरूपाः समभिप्रदुद्रुवुः॥
en: And slaying Sītā that wicked-minded son of Rāvana became greatly pleased. And beholding him thus delighted the monkeys being greatly sorry fled away.

sn: श्रुत्वा तं भीमनिदिं शक्राशनिसमस्वनम्। वीक्षमाणाः दिशः सर्वा दुद्रुवुर्वानरा भृशम्॥
en: Hearing that dreadful uproar resembling the sound of Indra's thunder-bolt, the monkeys, casting their looks on all sides fled away.

sn: तानुवाच ततः सर्वान्हनूमान्मारुतात्मजः। विषण्णवदनान्दीनांस्त्रस्तान्विद्रवतः पृथक् ॥
en: Thereupon Hanumān, the son of Maruta, spoke to them, poorly, terrified and of a sorrowful countenance, saying.

sn: कस्माद्विषण्णवदना विद्रवध्वं प्लवंगमाः। त्यक्तयुद्धसमुत्साहाः शूरत्वं क्व नु वो गतम्॥
en: O monkeys, why do you look so melancholy and why are you flying away? Why have you renounced your earnest desire for fight? And where is your heroism gone?

sn: पृष्ठतो न व्रजध्वं मामग्रतो यान्तमाहवे। शूरैरभिजनोपैतेरयुक्तं हि निवर्तितुम्॥
en: Do you remain behind me, I shall go first in the battle. It is improper for heroes of noble descent to escape from battle field.

sn: एवमुक्ताः सुसंक्रुद्धा वायुपुत्रेण धीमता। शैलशृङ्गान्दुमांचैव जगृहुईष्टमानसाः।।।।
en: Being thus addressed by that highly intelligent son of the Wind-god, they were greatly excited with wrath and being pleased took up trees and। crags in their hands.

sn: अभिपेतुश्च गर्जन्तो राक्षसान्वानरर्षभाः। परिवार्य हनूमन्तमन्वयुश्च महाहवे॥
en: Roaring thus the leading monkeys advanced towards the Rākşasas and stood encircling Hanumān in the battle-field.

sn: स तैर्वानरमुख्यैस्तु हनूमान्सर्वतो वृतः। हुताशन इवार्चिष्मानदहच्छत्रुवाहिनीम्॥
en: Being surrounded on all sides by leading monkeys, Hanuman began to burn down enemy's host like to fire spreading its flames.

sn: स राक्षसानां कदनं चकार सुमहाकपिः। वृतो वानरसैन्येन कालान्तकयमोपमः॥
en: Being encircled by monkey-hosts that mighty monkey resembling death himself began to grind the Rākşasas.

sn: स तु शोकेन चाविष्टः कोपेन महता कपिः। हनूमानरावणिरथे महतीं पातयच्छिलाम्॥
en: Being overwhelmed with grief and wrought up with ire, that monkey Hanumān, threw a huge crag on the car of that son of Rāvana.

sn: तामापतन्ती दृष्ट्वैव रथं सारथिना तदा। विधेयाश्वसमायुक्तो विदूरमपवाहितः॥
en: Beholding that crag about to fall down on the car, the charioteer moved his horses and it was speedily brought at some distance.

sn: तमिन्द्रजितमप्राप्यरथस्थं सहसारथिम्। विवेश धरणी भित्वा सा शिला व्यर्थमुद्यता॥
en: And not reaching Indrajit stationed on the car and the charioteer, that crag, uselessly hurled, fell down on the earth.

sn: पतितायां शिलायां तु व्यथिता रक्षसां चमूः। निपतन्त्या च शिलया राक्षसा मथिता भृशम्॥
en: As the crag falling down the army of the Rakşasas were violently crushed.

sn: तमभ्यधावशतशो नदन्तः काननौकसः। ते दुमांश्च महाकाया गिरिशृङ्गाणि चोद्यतः॥
en: Thereupon hundreds of huge-bodied monkeys, emitting cries and taking up crags and trees proceeded towards him (Indrajit) and hurled them at him.

sn: क्षिपन्तीन्द्रजितं संख्ये वानरा भीमविक्रमाः। वृक्षशैलमहावर्षं विसृजन्तः प्लवङ्गमाः॥ शत्रूणां कदनं चक्रुर्नेदुश्च विविधैः स्वनैः।
en: The monkeys gifted with dreadful prowess began to make a down-pour of crags and trees. They thus assailed the enemies and frequently emitted cries.

sn: वानरैस्तैर्महाभीमैर्घोररूपा निशाचराः॥ वीर्यादभिहता वृक्षय॑चेष्टन्त रणक्षितौ।
en: The grim-visaged night-rangers were assailed with trees in that field by the terrible monkeys.

sn: स सैन्यमभिवीक्ष्याथ वानरादितमिन्द्रजित्॥ प्रगृहीतायुधः क्रुद्धः परानभिमुखो ययौ। स शरौघानवसृजन्स्वसैन्येनाभिसंवृतः॥ जघान कपिशार्दूलान्सुबहून्दृढविक्रमः। शूलैरशनिभिः खङ्गैः पट्टिशैः शूलमुद्गरैः।। ते चाप्यनुचरांस्तस्य वानरा जघ्नुराहवे॥
en: Beholding his army thus distressed by the monkeys, Indrajit, excited with wrath, and taking up his dart, proceeded towards the enemies, and encircled by his soldiers showered terrible shafts upon them. And that one of dreadful prowess slew many a leading monkey by means of darts, Asanis, swords, pattisas and clubs.

sn: सुस्कन्धविटपैः शैलैः शिलाभिश्च महाबलः। हनूमान्कदनं चक्रे रक्षसां भीमकर्मणाम्॥
en: The highly powerful monkeys destroyed his retinue, with crags, stones and trees having strong trunks. And Hanumān thus crushed many a Rākşasa of terrible deeds.

sn: संनिवार्य परानीकमब्रवीत्तान्वनौकसः। हनूमान्संनिवर्तध्वं न नः साध्यमिदं बलम्॥
en: Obstructing the Rākṣasas (for some time) Hanumān spoke to monkeys, saying, “Stay, we should not fight now.

sn: त्यक्त्वा प्राणान्विचेष्टन्तो रामप्रियचिकीर्षवः। यन्निमित्तं हि युध्यामो हता सा जनकात्मजा॥
en: That daughter of Janaka has been slain, for whom we have engaged in fight, renouncing all hope of life and desiring to accomplish Rāma's satisfaction.

sn: इममर्थ हि विज्ञाप्य रामं सुग्रीवमेव च। तौ यत्प्रतिविधास्येते तत्करिष्यामहे वयम्॥
en: Let us now go and inform Rāma and Sugrīva of it. And we shall do as we shall be commanded by them.

sn: इत्युक्त्वा वानरश्रेष्ठो वारयन्सर्ववानरान्। शनैः शनैरसंत्रस्तः सबलः संन्यवर्तत ॥
en: Saying this and desisting all the monkeys from encounter that foremost of monkeys proceeded undaunted and heroically.

sn: ततः प्रेक्ष्य हनूमन्तं व्रजन्तं यत्र राघवः। स होतुकामो दृष्टात्मा गतश्चैत्यं निकुम्भिलाम्॥ निकुम्भिलामधिष्ठाय पावकं जुहवेन्द्रजित्।
en: Beholding Hanumăn proceed thus where Rāghava was that wicked-minded one (Indrajit) with a view to offer oblations to fire entered the sacrificial altar Nikumbhila.

sn: यज्ञभूम्यां ततो गत्वा पावकस्तेन रक्षसा ॥ हूयमानः प्रजज्वाल होमशोणितमुक्तदा। साचिः पिनद्धो ददृशे होमशोणिततर्पितः।। संध्यागत इवादित्यः सुतीव्रोऽग्निः समुत्थितः॥
en: Reaching there Indrajit lighted up fire and began to pour oblations therein. And the fire blazed up receiving oblations of blood, and being satisfied assumed the appearance of the setting sun.

sn: अथेन्द्रजिद्राक्षसभूतये तु जुहाव हव्यं विधिना विधानवित्। दृष्ट्वा व्यतिष्ठन्त च राक्षसास्ते महासमूहेषु नयानयज्ञाः॥
en: Indrajit conversant with all ceremonials, offered oblations in due form for the welfare of the Rākşasas. And they all stood there watching the result and desirous of ascertaining the success of the battle.* *This Sloka has been left off in some editions.

sn: राघवश्चापि विपुलं तं राक्षसवनौकसाम्। श्रुत्वा संग्रामनिर्घोषं जाम्बवन्तमुवाच ह॥
en: Hearing the terrible war-cry of the Rākşasas and monkeys Rāghava spoke to Jämbavän, saying.

sn: सौम्य नूनं हनुमता कृतं कर्म सुदुष्करम्। श्रूयते च यथा भीमः सुमहानायुधस्वनः॥
en: O gentle one, forsooth has Hanumān performed some mighty act for I hear the dreadful sound of the weapons.

sn: तद्गच्छ कुरु साहाय्यं स्वबलेनाभिसंवृतः। क्षिप्रमृक्षपते तस्य कपिश्रेष्ठस्य युध्यतः॥
en: Do you therefore proceed speedily, O lord of bears, with all your soldiers to assist that foremost of monkeys.

sn: ऋक्षराजस्तथेत्युक्त्वा स्वेनानीकेन संवृतः। आगच्छत्पश्चिमं द्वारं हनूमान्यत्र वानरः॥
en: Thereupon, saying, 'So be it,' that king of bears, surrounded by his forces, approached the Western gate, where the monkey, Hanumān, was stationed.

sn: अथायान्तं हनूमन्तं ददर्शक्षपतिस्तदा। वानरैः कृतसंग्रामैः श्वसद्भिरभिसंवृतम्॥
en: Then the lord of bears saw Hanumān approach, surrounded by monkeys sighing hard, who had faught the fight.

sn: दृष्ट्वा पथि हनूमांश्च तदृक्षबलमुद्यतम्। नीलमेघनिभं भीमं संनिवार्य न्यवर्तत॥
en: Seeing on the way that host of bears dreadful and resembling dark clouds, on the march, Hanumān made them desist.

sn: स तेन सह सैन्येन संनिकर्ष महायशाः। शीघ्रमागम्य रामाय दुःखितो वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
en: That illustrious one along with that force, speedily presented himself (before Rāma), and with a heavy heart addressed him, saying.

sn: समरे युध्यमानानामस्माकं प्रेक्षतां च सः। जघान रुदती सीतामिन्द्रजिद्रावणात्मजः॥
en: As we were fighting the field, Ravana's son, Indrajit in our very sight slew Sītā, crying (in distress).

sn: उद्भान्तचित्तस्तां दृष्ट्वा विषण्णोऽहमरिंदम। तदहं भवतो वृत्तं विज्ञापयितुमागतः॥
en: O subduer of enemies, seeing her (in this plight) I, with my senses bewildered, have been overwhelmed with grief. Therefore I have come to you to inform you of what has befallen.

sn: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा राघवः शोकमूर्च्छितः। निपपात तदा भूमौ छिन्नमूल इव द्रुमः॥
en: Hearing these words of his, Raghava, overwhelmed with grief, dropped down to the earth, like a tree whose roots have been severed.

sn: तं भूमौ देवसंकाशं पतितं दृश्य राघवम्। अभिपेतुः समुत्पत्य सर्वतः कपिसत्तमाः॥
en: Seeing the god-like Råghava down on the earth, the foremost monkeys from all sides rushed forward and came to where (he was).

sn: आसिञ्चन्सलिलैश्चैनं पद्मोत्पलसुगन्धिभिः। प्रदहन्तमसंहार्यं सहसाग्निमिवोत्थितम्॥
en: With water scented with lotuses, they fell to sprinkling that one resembling a furious fire that has suddenly arisen. 1. Padmotpalasugadhibhiḥ-water scented with padmas-lotuses proper, and utpalas-blue lotuses (Nymphea cerulea). 2. 'Rama,' remarks the commentator, 'was a fire lighted by his grief for Sītā.'

sn: तं लक्ष्मणोऽथ बाहुभ्यां परिष्वज्य सुदुःखितः। उवाच राममस्वस्थं वाक्यं हेत्वर्थसंयुतम्॥ शुभे वर्त्मनि तिष्ठन्तं त्वामार्य विजितेन्द्रियम्। अनर्थेभ्यो न शक्नोति त्रातुं धर्मो निरर्थकः॥
en: Thereat Laksmana, over-come with sorrow, embracing Rāma, spoke to his words fraught with reason and import, “Profitless* virtue is incapable, O noble one, of delivering from calamities you, who have subdued your senses, and who ever abidst in the good path. * 'Profitless, although apparently an epither of virtue, is really the predicate of the sentence. 'Virtue, incapable of delivering you is profitless.

sn: भूतानां स्थावराणां च जङ्गमानां च दर्शनम्। यथास्ति न तथा धर्मस्तेन नास्तीति मे मतिः॥
en: Beings and the mobile as well as the immobile cannot have that direct perception of virtue which they have of happiness. Therefore, I ween, virtue is a non-entity.

sn: यथैव स्थावरं व्यक्तं जङ्गमं च तथाविधम्। नायमर्थस्तथा युक्तस्त्वद्विधो न विपद्यते॥
en: Inasmuch as the immobile (albeit devoid of any regard for virtue) are nevertheless happy and as the mobile also are so, this virtue cannot lead to happiness. (If it were so), one like you would have not been placed in peril.

sn: यद्यधर्मो भवेद्भूतो रावणो नरकं व्रजेत्। भवांश्च धर्मसंयुक्तो नैव व्यसनमाप्नुयात्॥
en: If unrighteousness would bring unhappiness on creatures, Ravana should hence to hell, and you possessed of virtue, should not come by misfortune.

sn: तस्य च व्यसनाभावाद्व्यसनं चागते त्वयि। धर्मो भवत्यधर्मश्च परस्परविरोधिनौ॥
en: Seeing that he is free from danger, and you are in itrighteousness and its opposite are found to have tendencles the very reverse of those assigned to them respectively (by the Vedas).

sn: धर्मेणोपलभेद्धर्ममधर्म चाप्यधर्मतः। यद्यधर्मेण युज्येयुर्येष्वधर्मः प्रतिष्ठितः॥ न धर्मेण वियुज्येरनाधर्मरुचयो जनाः। धर्मेणाचरतां तेषां तथा धर्मफलं भवेत्॥
en: If by means of virtue, one attain the felicity attached to it, and by means of unrighteouness, one reap its proper fruit, then let those that are unrighteous reap the fruit of their impiety nor let those that set their face against sin, be deprived of the fruit of their righteousness, and let those that walk in the way of virtue reap the fruit of their piety.

sn: यस्मादर्था विवर्धन्ते येष्वधर्मः प्रतिष्ठितः। क्लिश्यन्ते धर्मशीलाश्च तस्मादेतौ निरर्थकौ॥
en: But as prosperity attend those that are established in unrighteousness, and as those regardful of righteousness fare lamentably, these*have not the senses assigned to them (by the scriptures). *Virtue and vice.

sn: वध्यन्ते पापकर्माणो यद्यधर्मेण राघव। वधकर्महतोऽधर्मः स हतः कं वधिष्यति॥
en: If, O Rāghava, Rāghava, (it is contended that) unrighteousness cut off the wicked, then whom shall Unrighteousness, himself slain by the act of slaughter of the destroyer, slay in his turn?

sn: अथवा विहितेनायं हन्यते हन्ति चापरम्। विधिः स लिप्यते तेन न स पापेन कर्मणा॥
en: Or if it is said that one is slain or slay another by ordinance, then it is destiny, which is touched by the sinful act and not he.

sn: अदृष्टप्रतिकारेण अव्यक्तेनासता सता। कथं शक्यं परं प्राप्तुं धर्मेणारिविकर्षण॥
en: O chastiser of foes, incapable of meting out retribution,* unmanifest itself, and non-existent, how can virtue, even if we grant its existence, find out the person that should be slain? *"In consequence,' remarks Ramanuja, 'of their being devoid of consciousness.

sn: यदि सत्स्यात्सतां मुख्य नासत्स्यात्तव किंचन। त्वया यदीदृशं प्राप्तं तस्मात्तन्नोपपद्यते॥
en: If, O foremost of the good, it had existed, you wouldst not have come by any misfortune. But inasmuch as you have fallen into this plight, there is no such thing as virtue.

sn: अथवा दुर्बलः क्लीबो बलं धर्मोऽनुवर्तते। दुर्बलो हृतमर्यादो न सेव्य इति मे मतिः॥
en: Or itself feeble and impotent, it take refuge in manliness. And being powerless and bereft of dignity, it should, I deem, by no means be followed.

sn: बलस्य यदि चेद्धर्मो गुणभूतः पराक्रमैः। धर्ममुत्सृज्य वर्तस्व यथा धर्मे तथा बले॥
en: If virtue is a property of manliness, then carefully forsaking virtue, do you follow strength as you have hitherto followed virtue.

sn: अथ चेत्सत्यवचनं धर्मः किल परंतप। अनृतं त्वथ्यकरणे किं न बद्धस्त्वया विना॥
en: But, O subduer of enemies, if truthfulness be virtue, are you not bound by that departing from which the king lost his life?* *Explains the commentator, 'King Dasaratha lost his life, because he did not observe his word of installing you in the kingdom. Are you not bound by his word as well?'

sn: यदि धर्मो भवेद्भूत अधर्मो वा परंतप। न स्म हत्वा मुनि वज्री कुर्यादिज्यां शतक्रतुः॥
en: O chastiser of foes, if virtue must be practised above all, or if prowess must have precedence, then the thunder-handed Satakratu would not have celebrated his sacrifice, slaying the ascetic.* *The Logic is all in a jumble; but such is the text. The ascetic was Visvarūpa. The meaning, according to the commentator, is that, prowess is first and virtue next. Indra first used force, and then acquired merit.)

sn: अधर्मसंश्रितो धर्मो विनाशयति राघव। सर्वमेतद्यथाकर्म काकुत्स्थ कुरुते नरः॥
en: O Rāghava, virtue aided by prowess, destroy enemies. Therefore, O Kakutstha, people, for compassing their ends, resort to both virtue and prowess.

sn: मम चेदं मतं तात धर्मोऽयमिति राघव। धर्ममूलं त्वया छिन्नं राज्यमुत्सृजता तदा॥
en: This, sire, is my opinion, this, O Raghava, is virtue. But you, having then renounced the kingdom, have laid the axe at the root* of righteousness. **Root, remarks, Rāmānuja, 'which is interest!'

sn: अर्थेभ्योऽथ प्रवृद्धेभ्यः संवृत्तेभ्यस्ततस्ततः। क्रियाः सर्वाः प्रवर्तन्ते पर्वतेभ्य इवापगाः॥
en: Like streams issuing out mountains, all acts spring from wealth flowing from various regions and attaining magnitude.

sn: अर्थेन हि विमुक्तस्य पुरुषस्याल्पचेतसः। विच्छिद्यन्ते क्रियाः सर्वा ग्रीष्मे कुसरितो यथा॥
en: Like a shrunken stream in summer, all the acts of that foolish person who has been devorced by wealth, are annihilated.

sn: सोऽयमर्थं परित्यज्य सुखकामः सुखैधितः। पापमाचरते कतु तदा दोष प्रवर्तते॥
en: He that renouncing riches, within his reach,* hankers after enjoyment, being carried away by his overmastering desire, take to getting at wealth by sinful acts; and then he incur guilt. *The commentator would have gotten riches.'

sn: यस्यार्थास्तस्य मित्राणि यस्यास्तस्य बान्धवाः। यस्यार्थाः स पुमाल्लोके यस्यार्थाः स च पण्डितः।।३५
en: To him that has wealth are friends, to him that has wealth are acquaintances, he that has wealth is an individuality in this world, and he that has wealth is a learned person.

sn: यस्यार्थाः स च विक्रान्तो यस्यार्थाः स च बुद्धिमान्। यस्यार्थाः स महाबाहुर्यस्यार्थाः स गुणाधिकः॥
en: He that has wealth is powerful; he that has wealth is intelligent; he that has wealth is mighty-armed; and he that has wealth is full of all graces.

sn: अर्थस्यैते परित्यागे दोषाः प्रव्याहृता मया। राज्यमुत्सृजता धीर येन बुद्धिस्त्वया कृता॥
en: All these that I have en-numerated are the evils of forsaking fortune. (I cannot divine) what made you, renouncing the monarchy, to adopt such a course.

sn: यस्यार्था धर्मकामार्थास्तस्य सर्व प्रदक्षिणम्। अधनेनार्थकामेन नार्थः शक्यं विचिन्वता॥
en: He that has riches, has virtue and desire attending on him, and has everything auspicious. That one without wealth, that seek it, cannot secure the wealth of prowess, without riches and desire.

sn: हर्षः कामश्च दर्पश्च धर्मः क्रोधः शमो दमः। अर्थादेतानि सर्वाणि प्रवर्तन्ते नराधिप॥
en: O lord of men, cheerfulness, and desire, and pride, and piety, and anger, and self-restraint, and self-control, all these come from wealth.

sn: येषां नश्यत्ययं लोकश्चरतां धर्मचारिणाम्। तेऽस्त्वयि न दृश्यन्ते दुर्दिनेषु यथा ग्रहाः॥
en: As the planets are not discovered on a stormy day, that wealth, the want of which renders this world naught even to the ascetics practising righteousness, is not visible in you.

sn: त्वयि प्रवजिते वीर गुरोश्च वचने स्थिते। रक्षसापहता भार्या प्राणैः प्रियतरा तव॥
en: O hero, you having abode by the words of your superior and having come (to the forest), your wife dearer then life itself has been ravished by Rākṣasas.

sn: तदद्य विपुलं वीर दुःखमिन्द्रजिता कृतम्। कर्मणा व्यपनेष्यामि तस्मादुचिष्ठ राघव।॥
en: But, O hero, today, O Raghava, by my acts will I remove this huge sorrow that has been heaped upon us by Indrajit. Therefore, rise you up.

sn: उत्तिष्ठ नरशार्दूल दीर्घबाहो धृतव्रत। किमात्मानं महात्मानमात्मानं नावबुध्यसे॥
en: Rise up, O foremost of men, O long-armed one, O you who observe vows. Why did you not understand yourself as the supreme soul?* *Räma is conceived as an incarnation of Vişnu.

sn: अयमनघ तवोदितः प्रियार्थ जनकसुतानिधनं निरीक्ष्य रुष्टः। सरथगजहयां सराक्षसेन्द्रां भृशमिषुभिर्विनिपातयामि लङ्काम्॥
en: Osinless one, urged on behalf of your welfare, I, waxing wroth on hearing of the slaughter of Janaka's daughter, shall with my shafts entirely raze to the ground Larkā with cars and elephants and steeds and the foremost Rākşasas.

sn: राममाश्वासमाने तु लक्ष्मणे भ्रातृवत्सले। निक्षिप्य गुल्मान्स्वस्थाने तत्रागच्छद्विभीषणः॥ नानाप्रहरणैवीरैश्चतुर्भिरभिसंवृतः। नीलाञ्जनचयाकारैर्मातंगैरिव यूथपैः॥
en: As Lakşmaņa devoted to his brother was comforting Rāma, Vibhīşaņa, posting his forces at their proper quarters, came there, surrounded by four heroes accoutred in various arms, resembling masses of collyrium or leaders of elephant-herds.

sn: सोऽभिगम्य महात्मानं राघवं शोकलालसम्। वानरांश्चापि ददृशे वाष्पपर्याकुलेक्षणान्॥
en: And approaching the high-souled Rāghava, overwhelmed with grief, he saw the monkeys with tears in their eyes.

sn: राघवं च महात्मानमिक्ष्वाकुकुलनन्दनम्। ददर्श मोहमापन्नं लक्ष्मणस्याङ्कमाश्रितम्॥
en: He saw that joy of the Ikşvāku race the high-souled Raghava-stupefied with grief, lying on the lap of Lakşmaņa.

sn: व्रीडितं शोकसंतप्तं दृष्ट्वा रामं विभीषणः। अन्तर्दुःखेन दीनात्मा किमेतदिति सोऽब्रवीत्॥
en: son Seeing Rāma cast down and inflamed with grief, Vibhisana, inlay pained, said, "What is this?

sn: विभीषणमुखं दृष्ट्वा सुग्रीवं तांश्च वानरान्। लक्ष्मणोवाच मन्दार्थमिदं वाष्पपरिप्लुतः॥
en: Thereat, gazing at Vibhisana's countenance as well as all those monkeys, Laksmana, with his eyes flooded with tears, said these words pregnant with dire import.

sn: हता इन्द्रजिता सीता इति श्रुत्वैव राघवः। हनूमद्वचनात्सौम्य ततो मोहमुपाश्रितः॥
en: O placid one, hearing from Hanumān's lips that Sītā has been slain by Indrajit. Rāghava has been overcome with stupor.

sn: कथयन्तं तु सौमित्रिं संनिवार्य विभीषणः। पुष्कलार्थमिदं वाक्यं विसंज्ञं राममब्रवीत्।।।।।
en: As Sumitra's was speaking thus, Vibhisana,. preventing him, addressed the stupefied Rāma in these pregnant words.

sn: मनुजेन्द्रार्तरूपेण यदुक्तस्त्वं हनूमता। तदयुक्तमहं मन्ये सागरस्येव शोषणम्॥
en: O king, all that Hanumān in distressful guise had communicated to you I deem as improbable, like to the drying of the deep.

sn: अभिप्रायं तु जानामि रावणस्य दुरात्मनः। सीतां प्रति महाबाहो न च घातं करिष्यति॥
en: I know the intent of the impious Rāvana with reference to Sita, O mighty-armed one. Her he will not slay.

sn: याच्यमानः सुबहुशो मया हितचिकीर्षुणा। वैदेहीमुत्सृजस्वेति न च तत्कृतवान्वचः॥
en: I, seeking his welfare, had besought him much, saying, 'Let go Vaidehi', but he did not act up to my speech.

sn: नैव साम्ना न दानेन न भेदेन कुतो युधा। सा द्रष्टुमपि शक्येत नैव चान्येन केनचित्॥
en: Neither by conciliation, nor by gift, nor by dissension, and where is war? nor by any other means is one capable of obtaining the very sight of Sītā.

sn: वानरान्मोहयित्वा तु प्रतियातः स राक्षसः। मायामयीं महाबाहो तां विद्धि जनकात्मजाम्॥
en: Having bewildered the monkeys, the Raksasa has gone back; and, O mighty-armed one, know her to be the illusory daughter of Janaka.

sn: चैत्यं निकुम्भिलामद्य प्राप्य होमं करिष्यति। हुतवानुपयातो हि देवैरपि सवासवैः॥
en: Today, going to the sacrificial ground (called) Nikumbhilā, he will offer oblations into fire; and there the deity of fire will present himself along with Vasava and the (other) divinities.

sn: दुराधर्षो भवत्येष संग्रामे रावणात्मजः। तेन मोहयता नूनमेषा माया प्रयोजिता ।।
en: Then Rāvana's son shall be invincible in batile. Indubitably that illusion has been wrought by him, to deceive (the monkeys), so that they might not through their prowess disturb him there.

sn: विघ्नमन्विच्छता तत्र वानराणां पराक्रमे॥ ससैन्यास्तत्र गच्छामो यावत्तन्न समाप्यते।
en: Thither will we go before he has furnished his (sacrifice). O foremost of men, shake off this vain sorrow that has overcome you!

sn: त्यजैनं नरशार्दूल मिथ्या संतापमागतम्॥ सीदते हि बलं सर्वं दृष्ट्वा त्वां शोककर्शितम्। इह त्वं स्वस्थहृदयस्तिष्ठ सत्वसमुच्छ्रितः।। लक्ष्मणं प्रेषयास्माभिः सह सैन्यानुकर्षिभिः॥
en: Seeing you smitten with grief, this entire host is dispirited. Here, with your heart composed, do your stay, summoning your strength. Send Lakşmañana along with us and the flower of the forces.

sn: एष तं नरशार्दूलो रावणिं निशितैः शरैः। त्याजयिष्यति तत्कर्म ततो वध्यो भविष्यति॥
en: This foremost of men by means of sharpened shafts will make Rāvana's son give up his rites; and then shall he be capable of being slain by us.

sn: तस्यैते निशितास्तीक्ष्णाः पत्रिपत्राङ्गवाजिनः। पतत्रिण इवासौम्याः शराः पास्यन्ति शोणितम्॥
en: These keen and sharpened shafts of his, attaining access of velocity through the feathers of birds, and themselves resembling fierce fowls, will drink his* blood. *Indrajit's.

sn: तत्संदिश महाबाहो लक्ष्मणं शुभलक्षणम्। राक्षसस्य विनाशाय वज्र वज्रधरो यथा ॥
en: Therefore, O mighty-armed one, do you in order to the destruction of the Rākşasa, commission Lakşmana, even as the wielder of the thunder-bolt command the same.

sn: मनुजवर न कालविप्रकर्षों रिपुनिधनं प्रति यत्क्षमोऽद्य कर्तुम्। त्वमतिसृज रिपोर्वधाय वज्रं दिविजरिपुमथने यथा महेन्द्रः॥
en: As today no time should be lost, therefore do you send Lakşmaņa for campassing the destruction of the foe, even as Mahendra send the thunder-bolt for bringing about the destruction of the enemies of the immortals.

sn: समाप्तकर्मा हि स राक्षसर्षभो भवत्यदृश्यः समरे सुरासुरैः। युयुत्सता तेन समाप्तकर्मणा भवेत्सुराणामपि संशयो महान्॥
en: If that foremost of Räkşasas can finish his rites, he shall be invisible to both celestials and Asuras; and, he fighting after finishing his sacrifice, the celestials themselves shall be placed in great jeopardy.

sn: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा राघवः शोककर्शितः। नोपधारयते व्यक्तं यदुक्तं तेन रक्षसा॥
en: Hearing his speech, Rāghava, overwhelmed with grief, could not perfectly comprehend what was said by the Rākşasa.

sn: ततो धैर्यमवष्टभ्य रामः परपुरंजयः। विभीषणमुपासीनमुवाच कपिसंनिधौ॥
en: Then, summoning up patience, Rāma-captor of hostile capitals, spoke to Vibhisana, seated near the monkeys.

sn: नैऋताधिपते वाक्यं यदुक्तं ते विभीषण। भूयस्तच्छ्रोतुमिच्छामि ब्रूहि यत्ते विवक्षितम्॥
en: O lord of Naiſtas, I once more wish to hear what, O Vibhisana, you have said.

sn: राघवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा वाक्यं वाक्यविशारदः। यत्तत्पुनरिदं वाक्यं बभाषेऽथ विभीषणः॥
en: Hearing Raghava's words, Vibhisana, skilled in speech, again spoke these words, saying.

sn: यथाज्ञप्तं महाबाहो त्वया गुल्मनिवेशनम्। तत्तथानुष्ठितं वीर त्वद्वाक्यसमनन्तरम्॥
en: O mighty-armed one, I have stationed the forces, O hero, agreeably to your directions.

sn: तान्यनीकानि सर्वाणि विभक्तानि समन्ततः। विन्यस्ता यूथपाश्चैव यथान्यायं विभागशः॥
en: The entire force has been divided around; and the leaders have also been placed properly.

sn: भूयस्तु मम विज्ञाप्यं तच्छृणुष्व महाप्रभो। त्वय्यकारणसंतप्ते संतप्तहृदया वयम्॥
en: Further, O mighty master, listen to what I have to say. On your having been causelessly aggrieve, we all of us were seized with grief.

sn: त्यज राजन्निमं शोकं मिथ्या संतापमागतम्। यदियं त्यज्यतां चिन्ता शत्रुहर्षविवर्धिनी॥
en: It this anxiety of your conduce to the joy of the enemy, do you cast it off. and, O hero, bestir yourself, and summon up spirits.

sn: उद्यमः क्रियतां वीर हर्षः समुपसेव्यताम्। प्राप्तव्या यदि ते सीता हन्तव्याश्च निशाचराः॥
en: If you are to have Sītā, and if the nightrangers are to be slain by you, do you, Raghu's son, listen to my profitable speech.

sn: रघुनन्दन वक्ष्यामि श्रूयतां मे हितं वचः। साध्वयं यातु सौमित्रिर्बलेन महता वृतः॥ निकुम्भिलायां संप्राप्तं हन्तुं रावणिमाहवे। धनुर्मण्डलनिर्मुक्तैराशीविषविषोपमैः॥
en: Let Sumitra's son go forth, environed by a mighty force, for slaying in battle the son of Ravana, who has gone to Nikumbhila; with shafts resembling Venomous serpents, discharged from the round* of his bow. *The bow drawn to its full stretch, becomes circular.

sn: शरैर्हन्तुं महेष्वासो रावणिं समितिंजयः। तेन वीरेण तपसा वरदानात्स्वयंभुवः। अस्त्रं ब्रह्मशिरः प्राप्तं कामगाश्च तुरंगमाः॥
en: By virtue of his austerities, that hero, from a boon conferred by the self-sprung, has obtained the Brahmasira weapon, together with steeds coursing at their will.

sn: स एष किल सैन्येन प्राप्तः किल निकुम्भिलाम्। यद्युत्तिष्ठेत्कृतं कर्म हतान्सर्वांश्च विद्धि नः॥
en: Now he with his army has gone to Nikumbhilā; and when, having finished his rites, he gets up, know that all of us are slain.

sn: निकुम्भिलामसंप्राप्तमकृताग्निं च यो रिपुः। त्वामाततायिनं हन्यादिन्द्रशत्रो स ते वधः॥ वरो दत्तो महाबाहो सरवलोकेश्वरेण वै। इत्येवं विहितो राजन्वधस्तस्यैष धीमतः॥
en: When not reaching Nikumbhilā, and not having finished your offerings to fire, you, equipped with arms, are slain by a foe, O enemy of Indra, that is your death. Thus, O mightyarmed one, did the lord of all creatures confer a boon (on Indrajit), and, o king, thus was the death of this intelligent one ordained.

sn: वधायेन्द्रिजितो राम संदिशस्व महाबलम्। हते तस्मिन्हतं विद्धि रावणं ससुहृद्गणम्॥
en: O Rāma, for compassing the destruction of Indrajit, do you commission a mighty force. On his being slain, know that Rāvana along with his retainers are slain.

sn: विभीषणवचः श्रुत्वा रामो वाक्यमथाब्रवीत्। जानामि तस्य रौद्रस्य मायां सत्यपराक्रम॥
en: Hearing Vibhīşana's words, Rāma said, “O you having truth for prowess, I know the illusion of that fierce one.

sn: स हि ब्रह्मास्त्रवित्प्राज्ञो महामायो महाबलः। करोत्यसंज्ञान् संग्रामे देवान्सवरुणानपि॥
en: Without doubt, the is skilled in the Brahma weapon, is potent in illusion and, is possessed of exceeding strength. In conflict, he deprive of consciousness even the celestials with Varuņa (at their head).

sn: तस्यान्तरिक्षे चरतः सरथस्य महायशः। न गतिञ्जयते वीर सूर्यस्येवाभ्रसंप्लवे॥ राघवस्तु रिपोर्ज्ञात्वा मायावीयं दुरात्मनः। लक्ष्मणं कीर्तिसंपन्नमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: As that illustrious (one) go about in the welkin on his chariot, none, can perceive his course, like the course of the sun when the sky is covered with clouds.” And Raghava, being well acquainted with the illusive energy of his wicked-minded foe, addressed the renowned Laksmana, saying.

sn: यद्वानरेन्द्रस्य बलं तेन सर्वेण संवृतः। हनूमत्प्रमुखैश्चैव यूथपैः सह लक्ष्मण॥ जाम्बवेनःपतिना सह सैन्येन संवृतः। जहि तं राक्षससुतं मायाबलसमन्वितम्॥
en: Environed by the entire host of the lord of monkeys, accompanied by the leaders, O Laksmana, headed by Hanuman, with Jambavan, king of bears-and girt round by the forces, do you slay this son of the Raksasa, possessed of the strength of illusion.

sn: अयं त्वां सचिवैः सार्धं महात्मा रजनीचरः। अभिज्ञातस्य मायानां पृष्ठतोऽनुगमिष्यति॥
en: And accompanied by his counsellors, this high-souled night-ranger shall follow at you back, in this engagement with that one skilled in illusion.

sn: राघवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा लक्ष्मणः सविभीषणः। जग्राह कार्मुकश्रेष्ठमन्यद्भीमपराक्रमः॥
en: Then hearing Rāghava's words, Lakşmaņa endowed with dreadful prowess, with Vibhīşaņa, took up another excellent bow.

sn: संनद्धः कवची खङ्गी सशरी वामचापभृत्। रामपादावुपस्पृश्य हृष्टः सौमित्रिरब्रवीत्॥
en: And donning on his mail, and putting on his armour and his sword, and furnished with arrows, and a bow in his left hand, Sumitrā's son, touching Rāma's feet, feeling elated, addressed Rāma, saying.

sn: अद्य मत्कार्मुकोन्मुक्ताः शरा निर्भिद्य रावणिम्। लङ्कामभिपतिष्यन्ति हंसाः पुष्करिणीमिव ॥
en: Today the shafts discharged from my bow, piercing Ravana's son, shall fall into Lanka, even as swans drop into a tank.

sn: अद्यैव तस्य रौद्रस्य शरीरं मामकाः शराः। विधमिष्यन्ति भित्त्वा तं महाचापगुणच्युताः॥
en: This very day shall my arrows, shot from my redoubtable bow-string, rive the body of that terrific one.

sn: एवमुक्त्वा तु वचनं द्युतिमान्धातुरग्रतः। स रावणिवधाकाली लक्ष्मणस्त्वरितं ययौ॥
en: Having spoken thus, the effulgent Lakşmana, eager to slay Rāvana's son, went before his brother.

sn: सोऽभिवाद्य गुरोः पादौ कृत्वा चापि प्रदक्षिणम्। निकुम्भिलामभिययौ चैत्यं रावणिपालितम्॥
en: Having saluted at the feet of his superior and went round him, Lakşmaņa set out for the sacrificial ground (named) Nikumbhila, protected by the son of Rāvana.

sn: विभीषणेन सहितो राजपुत्रः प्रतापवान्। कृतस्वस्त्ययनो भ्रात्रा लक्ष्मणस्त्वरितो ययौ॥
en: Accompanied by Vibhīşaņa, that powerful son of the king-Lakşmaņa-after his brother had offered up prayers in his behalf, set off with all speed.

sn: वानराणां सहस्रेस्तु हनूमान्बहुभिर्वृतः। विभीषणश्च सामात्यो लक्ष्मणं त्वरितं ययौ॥
en: Surrounded by thousands of monkeys, Hanumān as well as Vibhīşaņa together with his counsellors speedily went in the wake of Lakş mana.

sn: महता हरिसैन्येन सवेगमभिसंवृतः। ऋक्षराजबलं चैव ददर्श पथि विष्ठितम्॥
en: And strongly encompassed by that mighty monkey-host, (Laksmana) saw the forces of the bear-king stationed on the way.

sn: स गत्वा दूरमध्वानं सौमित्रिमित्रनन्दनः। राक्षसेन्द्रबलं दूरादपश्यद्व्यूहमाश्रितम्॥
en: Having proceeded far, Sumitra's Sumitra's son-enhancer of the delight of friends, from a distance discovered the forces of the Rākşasmonarch, drawn up in battle-array.

sn: स संप्राप्य धनुष्याणिर्मायायोगमरिंदमः। तस्थौ ब्रह्मविधानेन विजेतुं रघुनन्दनः॥
en: That subduer of enemies-Raghu's sonbearing his bow in his hand, coming upon him whose martial might lay in illusion, stopped (there) for conquering his foe agreeably to the ordinance * of Brahma. *The ordinance was that Indrajit should be slain while remaining outside Nikumbhilā, his rites not yet finished.

sn: विभीषणेन सहितो राजपुत्रः प्रतापवान्। अङ्गदेन च वीरेण तथानिलसुतेन च॥ विविधममलशस्त्रभास्वरं तद्ध्वजगहनं गहनं महारथैश्च। प्रतिभयतममप्रमेयवेगं तिमिरमिव द्विषतां बलं विवेश॥
en: Accompanied by Vibhīşaņa, the heroic Angada, and the Wind-god's offspring, the powerful son of the king dived into the forces of the foe, various, blazing with burnished arms, dense with standards, and thronging with mighty cars,* capable of striking terror (into the hearts of the spectators), instinct with immeasurable energy, and resembling darkness. *Maharathai (ab.) may also mean with mighty carwarriors.

sn: अथ तस्यामवस्थायां लक्ष्मणं रावणानुजः। परेषामहितं वाक्यमर्थसाधकमब्रवीत्॥
en: When things were in this condition, Rāvana's younger brother addressed Lakşmaņa in words fraught with evil to foes and conducing to the welfare (of his own party), saying.

sn: यदेतद्राक्षसानीकं मेघश्याम विलोक्यते। एतदायोध्यतां शीघ्रं कपिभिश्च शिलायुधैः॥ तस्यानीकस्य महतो भेदने यत लक्ष्मण। राक्षसेन्द्रसुतोऽप्यत्र भिन्ने दृश्यो भविष्यति॥
en: Do you without delay bring on an engagement between this cloud-black Räksasa army, which you behold, and the monkeys having rocks for their arms. O Lakşmaņa, do you exert yourself to break through his* mighty-army; and when the ranks are broken, the son of the Rákşasa-lord shall be visible. * Indrajit's, that is.

sn: स त्वमिन्द्राशनिप्रख्यैः शरैरवकिरन्परान्। अभिद्रवाशु यावद्वै नैतत्कर्म समाप्यते॥
en: Scattering among the foes shafts resembling Indra's thunder-bolt, charge him while he has not yet finished this ceremony.

sn: जहि वीर दुरात्मानं मायापरमधार्मिकम्। रावणिं क्रूरकर्माणं सर्वलोकभयावहम्॥
en: Slay, O hero, this wicked one, this son of Ravana, given to illusion, and of terrific feats, the fear of all the worlds.

sn: विभीषणवचः श्रुत्वा लक्ष्मणः शुभलक्षणः। ववर्ष शरवर्षेण राक्षसेन्द्रसुतं प्रति॥
en: Hearing Vibhisana's.words, Laksmana graced with auspicious marks began to shower arrows on the son of the Raksasa-chief.

sn: ऋक्षाः शाखामृगाश्चैव दुमप्रवरयोधिनः। अभ्यधावन्त सहितास्तदनीकमवस्थितम्॥
en: And bears and monkeys, given to fighting excellently with trees, in a body rushed towards that army (of Rākşasa) drawn up there.

sn: राक्षसाश्च शितैर्बाणैरसिभिः शक्तितोमरैः। अभ्यवर्तन्त समरे कपिसैन्यजिघांसवः॥
en: The Rākşasas (on their part) burning to slaughter the monkey-forces, rushed in the encounter with sharpened shafts and darts and tomaras.

sn: स संप्रहारस्तुमुल: संजज्ञे कपिरक्षसाम्। शब्देन महता लङ्कां नादयन्वै समन्ततः॥ शस्त्रैश्च विविधाकारैः शितैर्बाणैश्च पादपैः। उद्यतैर्गिरिशृङ्गैश्च घोरैराकाशमावृतम्॥
en: There took place a tremendous onslaught of the monkeys and the Raksasas. And Lankā resounded all around with that mighty tumult; and the sky was covered with weapons of various shapes, and whetted arrows and trees and dreadful upraised mountain-tops.

sn: राक्षसा वानरेन्द्रेषु विकृताननबाहवः। निवेशयन्तः शस्त्राणि चक्रुस्ते सुमहद्भयम्॥
en: Rākşasas having frightful faces and arms, playing their arms among the foremost monkeys, began to spread terror (there).

sn: तथैव सकलैर्वृक्षैर्गिरिशृङ्गैश्च वानराः। अभिजघ्नुनिजघ्नुश्च समरे सर्वराक्षसान्॥
en: In the same way the monkeys in the conflict fell to slaying and wounding the Rākşasas with trees and hill-tops.

sn: ऋक्षवानरमुख्यैश्च महाकायैर्महाबलैः। रक्षसां युध्यमानानां महद्भयमजायत॥
en: And great was the terror that was spread among the warring Räkşasas by the flower of the bears and monkeys, possessed of gigantic persons and endowed with prodigious strength.

sn: स्वमनीकं विषण्णं तु श्रुत्वा शत्रुभिरर्दितम्। उदतिष्ठत दुर्धर्षः स कर्मण्यननुष्ठिते॥
en: Hearing his own army hard beset by the enemies, and dropping, the unconquerable one, ere yet he had finished his rites, rose up.

sn: वृक्षान्धकारान्निर्गम्य जातक्रोधः स रावणिः। आरुरोह रथं सज्ज पूर्वयुक्तं सुसंयतम्॥
en: Issuing from the gloom of the trees, Ravana's son, fired with wrath, ascended his car, which had already been well yoked (with steeds).

sn: स भीमकार्मुकशरः कृष्णाञ्जनचयोपमः। रक्तास्यनयनो भीमो बभौ मृत्युरिवान्तकः॥
en: Accoutred in a dreadful bow and arrows, that one, resembling a mass of collyrium, having a red face and eyes, looked dreadful like the reaper-death.

sn: दृष्ट्वैव तु राथस्थं तं पर्यवर्तत तद्बलम्। रक्षसां भीमवेगानां लक्ष्मणेन युयुत्सताम्॥
en: As soon as they saw him mounted on his car, that host of Rākşas possessed of dreadful impetuosity, eager to engage with Lakşmaņa, stood on their ground.

sn: तस्मिंस्तु काले हनुमानरुजत्स दुरासदम्। धरणीधरसंकाशो महावृक्षमरिंदमः॥
en: At this time that subduer of enemies, Hanumăn-resembling a mountain, uprooted a giant tree incapable of being handled.

sn: स राक्षसानां तत्सैन्यं कालाग्निरिव निर्दहन्। चकार बहुभिर्वृक्षैनि:संज्ञं युधि वानरः॥
en: In that encounter, the monkey, consuming (the forces) like the fire risen at Doomsday, made that army of Rākşasas insensible with innumerable trees.

sn: विध्वंसयन्तं तरसा दृष्ट्वैव पवनात्मजम्। राक्षसानां सहस्राणि हनूमन्तमवाकिरन्॥
en: Finding the Wind-god's son, Hanumān, suddenly spreading devastation among the Rāks asas by thousands, (they) showered (shafts) on him.

sn: शितशूलधराः शूलैरसिभिश्चासिपाणयः। शक्तिहस्ताश्च शक्तीभिः पट्टिशैः पट्टिशायुधाः॥ परिधश्च गदाभिश्च कुन्तैश्च शुभदर्शनैः। शतशश्च शतघ्नीभिरायसैरपि मुद्गरैः॥ घोरैः परशुभिश्चैव भिन्दिपालैश्च राक्षसाः। मुष्टिभिर्वज्रकल्पैश्च तलैरशनिसंनिभैः॥ अभिजघ्नुः समासाद्य समन्तात्पर्वतोपमम्। तेषामपि च संक्रुद्धश्चकार कदनं महत्॥
en: Approaching on all sides that one resembling a hill, those bearing whetted darts attacked him with darts; those bearing swords in their hands, with swords; those bearing javelins in their hands, with javelins; with pattisas, those equipped with pattiśas; and with bludgeons, and maces and graceful kuntas; and with hundred of sataghnis, and iron clubs; and with terrific axes; and with Bhindipälas, and with boxes like to thunder-bolts; and slaps resembling the asani. And fired with fury, he (on his part) spread a huge havoc among them.

sn: स ददर्श कपिश्रेष्ठमचलोपममिन्द्रजित्। सूदमानमसंत्रस्तममित्रान्पवनात्मजम्॥
en: Indrajit saw that foremost of monkeys resembling a hill, the offspring of the Windgod possessing himself if calmness, while destroying his foes.

sn: स सारथिमुवाचेदं याहि यत्रैष वानरः। क्षयमेव हि नः कुर्याद्राक्षसानामुपेक्षितः॥
en: Thereat, be* addressed his charioteer, saying, "Go where the monkeys is. Being disregarded by the Raksasas, he makes havoc among us." *Indrajit.

sn: इत्युक्तः सारथिस्तेन ययौ यत्र स मारुतिः। वहन्परमदुर्धर्षं स्थितमिन्द्रजितं रथे॥
en: Thus accosted by him, the charioteer went where the Wind-god's offspring was, carrying the exceedingly invincible Indrajit seated on the car.

sn: सोऽभ्युपेत्य शरान्खङ्गान्पट्टिशासिपरश्वधान्। अभ्यवर्षत दुर्धर्षः कपिमूर्धनि राक्षसः॥
en: And rushing forward, that irrepressible one the Rākşasas-began to shower on the monkey's head arrows and swords and pațțišas and scimitars and axes.

sn: तानि शस्त्राणि घोराणि प्रतिगृह्य स मारुतिः। रोषेण महताविष्टो वाक्यं चेदमुवाच ह॥
en: And bearing all those dreadful arms, the Wind-god's offspring, overcome with a mighty rage said.

sn: युध्यस्व यदि शूरोऽसि रावणात्मज दुर्मते। वायुपुत्रं समासाद्य न जीवन्प्रतियास्यसि।॥
en: O wicked-minded son of Rävaņa, if you are a hero, fight on. Combat with me with your arms.

sn: बाहुभ्यां संप्रयुध्यस्व यदि मे द्वन्द्वमाहवे। वेगं सहस्व दुर्बुद्धे ततस्त्वं रक्षसां वरः॥
en: If in the encounter, you bear my impetus, then, O you of perverse sense, you indeed are the foremost of Rākşasas.

sn: हनूमन्तं जिघांसन्तं समुद्यतशरासनम्। रावणात्मजमाचष्टे लक्ष्मणाय विभीषणः॥
en: Then Vibhīşana pointed out to Lakşmaņa the son of Ravana, who with his bow upraised, was eager to slay Hanumān.

sn: यः स वासवनिर्जेता रावणस्यात्मसंभवः। स एष रथमास्थाय हनूमन्तं जिघांसति ॥ तमप्रतिमसंस्थानैः शरैः शत्रुनिवारणैः। जीवितान्तकरैोरैः सौमित्रे रावणिं जहि ॥
en: This one that, mounted on his car, is eager to slay Hanumăn, is the son of Rāvaņa that has vanquished Vasava himself (in battle). Do you, O son of Sumitrā, with peerless shafts capable of resisting enemies, dreadful, and competent to finish the lives (of foes), slay the son of Ravana.

sn: इत्येवमुक्तस्तु तदा महात्मा विभीषणेनारिविभीषणेन। ददर्श तं पर्वतसंनिकाशं रथस्थितं भीमबलं दुरासदम्॥
en: Thus accosted by Vibhīşaņa terrific to foes, that high-souled one saw (Indrajit) of dreadful prowess, difficult to gut at, and resembling a hill, stationed on his car.

sn: एवमुक्त्वा तु सौमित्रिं जातहर्षो विभीषणः। धनुष्पाणिं तमादाय त्वरमाणो जगाम सः॥
en: Having spoken thus to Sumitra's son, Vibhișaņa experienced delight, and taking (Laksmana) bearing a bow in his hand, hurriedly went off.

sn: अविदूरं ततो मत्वा प्रविश्य तु महद्वनम्। अदर्शयत तत्कर्म लक्ष्मणाय विभीषणः॥
en: Proceeding some way and entering the mighty wood, Vibhīşaņa pointed out to Lakşmaņa the place (of sacrifice).

sn: नीलजीमूतसंकाशं न्यग्रोधं भीमदर्शनम्। तेजस्वी रावणभ्राता लक्ष्मणाय न्यवेदयत्॥
en: The energetic brother of Rāvana showed to Lakşmaņa the Nyagrodha, dreadful to behold and resembling a mass of sable clouds.

sn: इहोपहारं भूतानां बलवान्रावणात्मजः। उपहृत्य ततः पश्चात्संग्राममभिवर्तते।४॥
en: Here offering presents to the ghosts, the powerful son of Răvaņa afterwards engages in conflict.

sn: अदृश्यः सर्वभूतानां ततो भवति राक्षसः। निहन्ति समरे शत्रून्बध्नाति च शरोत्तमैः॥
en: Then the Rākşasas becomes invisible to all beings; and he slay his enemies in battle and fastens them with excellent shafts.

sn: तमप्रविष्टं न्यग्रोधं बलिनं रावणात्मजम्। विध्वंसय शरैर्दीप्तैः सरथं साश्वसारथिम्॥
en: Do you, ere he has passed beyond the Nyagrodha, with flaming arrows destroy the powerful son of Rävaņa along with his car and steeds and charioteer.

sn: तथेत्युक्त्वा महातेजाः सौमित्रिमित्रनन्दनः। बभूवावस्थितस्तत्र चित्रं विस्फारयन्धनुः॥
en: Thereupon saying, 'So be it,' the exceedingly energetic son of Sumitrā-that delight of his friends, took up his post there stretching his variegated bow.

sn: स रथेनाग्निवर्णेन बलवानरावणात्मजः। इन्द्रजित्कवची खङ्गी सध्वजः प्रत्यदृश्यत ।।।।
en: Ravana's son Indrajit, endowed with strength, mailed, and armed with a sword, and furnished with a banner, was seen mounted on a fire-hued chariot.

sn: तमुवाच महातेजाः पौलस्त्यमपराजितम्। समाह्वये त्वां समरे सम्यग्युद्धं प्रयच्छ मे।९।।
en: The highly powerful Lakşmaņa addressed Pulastya's son never knowing defeat, saying, I challenge you to the encounter. Do you give me battle, exerting your utmost.

sn: एवमुक्तो महातेजा मनस्वी रावणात्मजः। अब्रवीत्परुषं वाक्यं तत्र दृष्ट्वा विभीषणम्॥
en: Thus addressed, the exceedingly energetic and intelligent son of Rāvana, seeing Vibhīşaņa there, spoke to him harshly, thus.

sn: इह त्वं जातसंवृद्धः साक्षाद्भाता पितुर्मम। कथं दुह्यसि पुत्रस्य पितृव्यो मम राक्षस॥
en: Born and bred in this Rākşasa race, you are the very brother of my father Why, O Rākşasa being my uncle, did you range yourself against your son?

sn: न ज्ञातित्वं न सौहार्द न जातिस्तव दुर्मते। प्रमाणं न च सौदर्यं न धर्मो धर्मदूषण॥
en: But neither kinship, nor emity, nor race, O wicked-minded one, nor co-birth, can, destroyer of righteousness, avail to make you discern your duty.

sn: शोच्यस्त्वमसि दुर्बुद्धे निन्दनीयश्च साधुभिः। यस्त्वं स्वजनमुत्सृज्य परभृत्यत्वमागतः॥
en: O you of perverse understanding you are indeed to be pitied; as you are worthy of being reproached by the virtuous; since, renouncing your own, you have espoused servitude under another.

sn: नैतच्छिथिलया बुद्ध्या त्वं वेत्सि महदन्तरम्। क्व च स्वजनसंवासः क्व च नीचपराश्रयः॥
en: Neither by your character nor yet your understanding did you perceive the mighty difference that Leith between living with one's own kindred, and taking refuge with the base.

sn: गुणवान्वा परजनः स्वजनो निर्गुणोऽपि वा। निर्गुणः स्वजनः श्रेयान्यः परः पर एव सः॥
en: If one that is not our own, be furnished with every grace, and if one's own be void of all merit, one's kindred, albeit unworthy, is preferable; and he that is not ours, is even always such.

sn: यः स्वपक्षं परित्यज्य परपक्षं निषेवते। स स्वपक्षे क्षयं याते पश्चात्तैरेव हन्यते॥
en: He that, forsaking his own party, serve that of another, is destroyed even by the latter, when his own party is destroyed.

sn: निरनुक्रोशता चेयं यादृशी ते निशाचर। स्वजनेन त्वया शक्यं पौरुषं रावणानुज॥
en: O night-ranger, such is this your relentlessness, that, O Ravana's younger brother, you being a kindred, are capable of displaying your manliness (as no other person can do so).

sn: इत्युक्तो भ्रातृपुत्रेण प्रत्युवाच विभीषणः। अजानन्निव मच्छीलं किं राक्षस विकत्थसे॥
en: Thus addressed by his brother's son, Vibhis ana answered, “O Raksasa, why did you speak as if in ignorance of my character? O impious son of the Rākşasa chief, do you for ego the roughness which you assume on behalf of my dignity.* *Or, on account of your heroism.

sn: राक्षसेन्द्रसुतासाधो पारुष्यं त्यज गौरवात्। कुले यद्यप्यहं जातो रक्षसां क्रूरकर्मणाम्।। गुणो यः प्रथमो नृणां तन्मे शीलमराक्षसम्॥ न रमे दारुणेनाहं न चाधर्मेण वै रमे। भ्रात्रा विषमशीलोऽपि कथं भ्राता निरस्यते॥
en: Albeit born in the race of Rākşas of cruel deeds, yet having regard to the first of principles pertaining to men, my character is not that of a Rākşasa. I do not take pleasure in the terrible; not do I revel in unrighteousness.” But how can a brother, although differing from his brother in character, be renounced by the latter?* *Some read Vişamasilena. Then the sense would be: 'How else could a brother bearing a difference in character, renounce his brother' meaning Ravana.

sn: धर्मात्प्रच्युतशीलं हि पुरुषं पापनिश्चयम्। त्यक्त्वा सुखमवाप्नोति हस्तादाशीविषं यथा॥
en: One renouncing a person, lapsing from virtue and bent on sinful acts, attain happiness, even as one does by shaking off a venomous snake from his hand.

sn: परस्वहरणे युक्तं परदाराभिमर्शकम्। त्याज्यमाहुर्दुरात्मानं वेश्म प्रज्वलितं यथा ॥
en: The wise have called that impious cne given to stealing others goods and violating others wives, as worthy of being forsaken, even like a house that is aflame.

sn: परस्वानां च हरणं परदाराभिमर्शनम्। सुहृदामतिशङ्का च त्रयो दोषाः क्षयावहाः॥
en: Robbing others property, outraging the wives of others, and inspiring fear among friends, these three vices lead to destruction.

sn: महर्षीणां वधो घोरः सर्वदेवैश्च विग्रहः। अभिमानश्च रोषश्च वैरत्वं प्रतिकूलता॥ एते दोषा मम भ्रातुर्जीवितैश्वर्यनाशनाः। गुणान्प्रच्छादयामासुः पर्वतानिव तोयदाः॥
en: The dreadful slaughter of sages, rebellion against all the gods, overweening conceit, anger long-continued enmity, and running amuck of counsel, these sins are sapping the life and fortune of my brother; and they have hidden his virtues even as clouds cover a mountain.

sn: दोषैरेतैः परित्यक्तो मया भ्राता पिता तव। नेयमस्ति पुरी लङ्का न च त्वं न च ते पिता॥
en: It is on account of these vices that my brother, your sire, has been deserted by me. And this city of Lankā will not be, nor you, nor your father.

sn: अतिमानश्च बालश्च दुर्विनीतश्च राक्षस। बद्धस्त्वं कालपाशेन ब्रूहि मां यद्यदिच्छसि ॥
en: You are proud, and haughty, and a boy, O Raksasa. You are fettered by the noose of Fate. Do you say to me whatever you like.

sn: अद्येह व्यसनं प्राप्तं यन्मां परुषमुक्तवान्। प्रवेष्टुं न त्वया शक्यं न्यग्रोधं राक्षसाधम ॥
en: To-day you have addressed harshly me, who have fallen on evil days; but, O worst of Raks asas, you cannot pass this Nyagrodha.

sn: धर्षयित्वा च काकुत्स्थं न शक्यं जीवितुं त्वया। युध्यस्व नरदेवेन लक्ष्मणेन रणे सह।। हतस्त्वं देवताकार्य करिष्यसि यमक्षयम्॥
en: Having smitten the Kākutstha, you cannot live. Fight with that man-god, Laksmana, in encounter. Being slain, you shall serve the deities in the abode of Yama.

sn: निदर्शयित्वात्मबलं समुद्यतं कुरुष्व सर्वायुधसायकव्ययम्। न लक्ष्मणस्यैत्य हि बाणगोचरं त्वमद्य जीवन्सबलो गमिष्यसि॥
en: Displaying you own prowess, do you spend all your weapons and all your shafts. But coming within the ken of Laksmana's arrows, your will not today go hence, living with your forces.

sn: विभीषणवचः श्रुत्वा रावणिः क्रोधमूर्छितः। अब्रवीत्परुषं वाक्यं क्रोधेनाभ्युत्पपात च॥
en: Hearing Vibhisana's words, the son of Ravana, deprived of his senses by passion, spoke harshly, and rushed forward in wrath.

sn: उद्यतायुधनिस्त्रिंशो रथे सुसमलंकृते। कालाश्वयुक्ते महति स्थितः कालान्तकोपमः॥
en: With upraised weapons and scimitars, he, resembling the Destroyer himself, was mounted on a mighty car yoked with black steeds, and ornamented (on all sides).

sn: महाप्रमाणमुद्यम्य विपुलं वेगवदृढम्। धनुर्भीमबलो भीमं शरांश्चामित्रनाशनान् ॥
en: That one endowed with terrific strength upraised a huge, gigantic, strong and powerful bow, and shafts capable of destroying foes.

sn: तं ददर्श महेष्वासो रथस्थः समलंकृतः। अलंकृतममित्रघ्नो रावणस्यात्मजो बली॥ हनूमत्पृष्ठमारूढमुदयस्थरविप्रभम्। उवाचैनं सुसंरब्धः सौमित्रिं सविभीषणम्॥ तांश्च वानरशार्दूलान्पश्यध्वं मे पराक्रमम्। अद्य मत्कार्मुकोत्सृष्टं शरवर्ष दुरासदम्॥ मुक्तवर्षमिवाकाशे धारयिष्यथ संयुगे।
en: That mighty bowman and slayer of foes-the powerful son of Ravana, adorned (with ornaments, and mounted on his chariot, saw him dight (with his own splendour). And fired wrath (Indrajit) addressed Sumitra's son, who, mounted on Hanumān's back, like to the risen sun in splendour-accompanied Vibhīşaña; and he also addressed all those principal monkeys saying, "Do you behold my prowess! today do you in the conflict bear my arrowy shower shot from my bow, incapable of being approached, and resembling the down pour in the sky.

sn: अद्य वो मामका बाणा महाकार्मुकनिःसृताः। विधमिष्यन्ति गात्राणि तूलराशिमिवानलः॥
en: fo-day my shafts discharged from my mighty bow shall mangle your limbs, even as fire burn up a heap of cotton.

sn: तीक्ष्णसायकनिर्भिन्नाशूलशक्त्वृष्टिसायकैः। अद्य वो गमयिष्यामि सर्वानेव यमक्षयम्॥
en: To-day with your persons pierced with sharp shafts, with darts, and javelins, and Rstis and arrows, Shall I despatch you all to the abode of Yama.

sn: सृजतः शरवर्षाणि क्षिप्रहस्तस्य संयुगे। जीमूतस्येव नदतः कः स्थास्यति ममाग्रतः।।।।
en: Who shall stay before me, fleet-handed, creating an arrows shower in the field, and roaring like to clouds?

sn: रात्रियुद्धे तदा पूर्व वज्राशनिसमैः शरैः। शायितौ तौ मया भूयो विसंज्ञौ सपुरःसरौ॥ स्मृतिर्न तेऽस्ति वा मन्ये व्यक्तं या तो यमक्षयम्। आशीविषसमं क्रुद्धं यन्मां योद्धमुपस्थितः॥
en: Formerly in a night-engagement, with my shafts resembling the thunder-bolt and Vajra, you two along with your foremost adherents, were rendered insensible and laid down on the earth by me. But, perhaps, you have forgotten it. As you have presented yourself for battle before me, fired with wrath and resembling a venomous serpent, it is evident you will go to the region of Yama.

sn: तच्छुत्वा राक्षसेन्द्रस्य गर्जितं राघवस्तदा। अभीतवदनः क्रुद्धो रावणिं वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
en: Hearing the vaunt of the Rākşasa-chief, Rahgu's son, inflamed with rage, with an undaunted countenance, spoke to Ravana's son.

sn: उक्तश्च दुर्गमः पार:कार्याणां राक्षस त्वया। कार्याणां कर्मणा पारं यो गच्छति स बुद्धिमान्॥ स त्वमर्थस्य हीनार्थो दुरवापस्य केनचित्। वाचा व्याहृत्य जानीषे कृतार्थोऽस्मीति दुर्मते॥
en: O Rākşasa, hard is the achievement of the task that you have mentioned. He that compass business by act is alone intelligent. He that compass business by act is alone intelligent. But you, O wicked-minded one, incompetent as you are to bring about your end, attaining your arduous aim by words only, deem yourself as crowned with success.

sn: अन्तर्धानगतेनाजौ यत्त्वया चरितस्तदा। तस्कराचरितो मार्गो नैष वीरनिषेवितः॥
en: That your had rendered yourself invisible in the field of conflict, was the work of a thief, and not the way of a hero.

sn: यथा बाणपथं प्राप्य स्थितोऽस्मि तव राक्षस। दर्शयस्वाद्य तत्तेजो वाचा त्वं किं विकत्थसे॥
en: Coming within the range of your shafts, I stay here, do you display your prowess. What did you say in words.?

sn: एवमुक्तो धनुर्भीम परामृश्य महाबलः। ससर्ज निशितान्बाणानिन्द्रजित्समितिजयः॥
en: Thus addressed, the mighty IndrajitConqueror of enemies-stretching his dreadful bow, showered sharpened shafts.

sn: तेन सृष्टा महावेगाः शराः सर्पविषोपमाः। संप्राप्य लक्ष्मणं पेतुः श्वसन्त इव पनगाः॥
en: And discharged by him, those exceedingly impetuous arrows, resembling the venom of serpents, hitting Laksmana, fell down like to hissing snakes.

sn: शरैरतिमहावेगैर्वेगवान्रावणात्मजः। सौमित्रिमिन्द्रजिद्युद्धे विव्याध शुभलक्षणम्॥
en: In that encounter, Rāvana's son-Indrajit, possessed of eminent impetuosity, pierced Laksmana, graced with auspicious marks, with vehement shafts.

sn: स शरैरतिविद्धाङ्गो रुधिरेण समुक्षितः। शुशुभे लक्ष्मणः श्रीमान्विधूम इव पावकः॥
en: And pierced with those arrows and bathed in blood, the graceful Lakşmaņa appeared like a smokeless fire.

sn: इन्द्रजित्त्वात्मनः कर्म प्रसमीक्ष्याभिगम्य च। विनद्य सुमहानादमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Seeing his own feat, Indrajit, coming forward, and setting up a tremendous cry, said.

sn: पत्रिणः शितधारास्ते शरा मत्कार्मुकच्युताः। आदास्यन्तेऽद्य सौमित्रे जीवितं जीवितान्तकाः॥
en: O son of Sumitrā, my feathered and sharpedged shafts shot from my bow, capable of destroying life, will today finish you up.

sn: अद्य गोमायुसङ्घाश्च श्येनसङ्घाश्च लक्ष्मण। गृध्राश्च निपतन्तु त्वां गतासुं निहतं मया॥
en: To-day, O Laksmana, swarms of jackals and hosts of hawks and vultures shall alight on you lying lifeless, having been slain by me.

sn: क्षत्रबन्धुं सदानार्य रामः परमदुर्मतिः। भक्तं भ्रातरमचैव त्वां द्रक्ष्यति हतं मया॥ वित्रस्तकवचं भूमौ व्यपविद्धशरासनम्। हृतोत्तमाङ्गं सौमित्रे त्वामद्य निहतं मया।॥
en: This very day shall the exceedingly wicked Råma behold you, who are the friend of Kș atriyas and devoted to your brother, and who ėver bear yourself ignobly, slain by me; today see you, O Sumitra's son, slain by me, with your armour fallen off your person, your bow broken, and your head severed.

sn: इति ब्रवाणं संक्रुद्धः परुषं रावणात्मजम्। हेतुमद्वाक्यमर्थज्ञो लक्ष्मणः प्रत्युवाच ह॥
en: As Ravana's son was speaking thus harshly, Lakşmaņa conversant with the import of words, replied in a reasonable speech, saying.

sn: वाग्बलं त्यज दुर्बुद्धे क्रूरकर्मन्हि राक्षस। अथ कस्माद्वदस्येतत्संपादय सुकर्मणा ॥
en: Leave off your strength of tongue, O you of perverse sense, O Räkşasa, O you of crooked ways! Wherefore did you speak thus? Bring all this to pass in worthy deed.

sn: अकृत्वा कत्थसे कर्म किमर्थमिह राक्षस। कुरु तत्कर्म येनाहं श्रद्धेयं तव कत्थनम्॥
en: Why, O Raksasa, without doing (what you say), did you simply say it? Do the deed, so that I may have regard for your utterances.

sn: अनुक्त्वा परुषं वाक्यं किंचिदप्यनवक्षिपन्। अविकत्थन्वधिष्यामि त्वां पश्य पुरुषादन॥
en: Mark! without speaking anything harsh, without censuring you in the least, without venting any brag, shall, I, O cannibal, slay you.

sn: इत्युक्त्वा पञ्च नाराचानाकर्णापूरिताशरान्। विजषान महावेगाल्लक्ष्मणो राक्षसोरसि॥
en: Saying this, Lakşmaņa drawing his bow to its full bent, hit at the Raksasas chest five nārācas, wondrous impetuous arrows.

sn: सपत्रवाजिता बाणा ज्वलिता इव पन्नगाः। नैर्ऋतोरस्यभासन्त सवितू रश्मयो यथा॥
en: Those arrows resembling flaming serpents, with their velocity accelerated by the feathers (with which they were furnished), blazed on the Nairta's breast like the rays of the sun.

sn: स शरैराहतस्तेन सरोषो रावणात्मजः। सुप्रयुक्तैस्त्रिभिर्बाणैः प्रतिविव्याध लक्ष्मणम्॥
en: And wounded with those shafts, Ravana's son, fired with wrath, pierced Lakşmaņa with arrows discharged (from his bow).

sn: स बभूव महाभीमो नरराक्षससिंहयोः। विमर्दस्तुमुलो युद्धे परस्परजयैषिणोः॥
en: And exceedingly dreadful was the encounter that took place between those leonine man and Rākşasa, each eager to conquer the other.

sn: विक्रान्तौ बलसंपन्नावुभौ विक्रमशालिनौ। उभौ परमदुर्जेयावतुल्यबलतेजसौ॥ युयुधाते तदा वीरौ ग्रहाविव नभोगतौ। बलवृत्राविव हि तौ युधि वै दुष्प्रधर्षणौ॥ युयुधाते महात्मानौ तदा केसरिणाविव। बहूनवसृजन्तौ हि मार्गणौघानवस्थितौ।। नरराक्षसमुख्यौ तौ प्रहृष्टावभ्ययुध्यताम्॥
en: Both powerful, and both endowed with strength and possessed of prowess, and both exceedingly invincible; and both having unparalleled might and energy, those heroes faught like two planets in the welkin; or like Bala and Vộtra, irresistible in conflict; and those high-souled ones faught like two lions. And showering countless shafts and displaying many manoeuvres, that foremost of men and that Rāks asas, faught on cheerfully,

sn: ततः शरान्दाशरथिः संधायामित्रकर्षणः। ससर्ज राक्षसेन्द्राय क्रुद्धः सर्प इव श्वसन्॥
en: Then sighing like an enraged serpent, that chastiser of foes, Dasaratha's son, setting shafts (on his bow-string) showered them on the Raksasa-chief.

sn: तस्य ज्यातलनिर्घोषं स श्रुत्वा राक्षसाधिपः। विवर्णवदनो भूत्वा लक्ष्मणं समुदैक्षत॥
en: And hearing the twang of his bow-string the lord of Rākṣasas, with his countenance fallen, gazed at Laksmana.

sn: विषण्णवदनं दृष्ट्वा राक्षसं रावणात्मजम्। सौमित्रिं युद्धसंयुक्तं प्रत्युवाच विभीषणः॥
en: Then Vibhīşaņa spoke to Sumitrā's son as he was fighting, “I find (inauspicious) signs in Rāvana's son.

sn: निमित्तान्युपपश्यामि यान्यस्मिन्रावणात्मजे। त्वर तेन महाबाहो भग्न एष न संशयः॥
en: Do therefore hasten on, broken he is, without doubt.

sn: ततः संधाय सौमित्रिः शरानाशीविषोपमान्। मुमोच विशिखांस्तस्मिन्सानिव विषोल्बणान्॥
en: Then fixing arrows (on his bow) resembling venomous snakes, he let go those keen shafts, like to serpents furnished with poison.

sn: शक्राशनिसमस्पर्शेर्लक्ष्मणेनाहतः शरैः। मुहूर्तमभवन्मूढः सर्वसंक्षुभितेन्द्रियः।॥
en: And smite by Lakşmaņa with arrows having the touch of the levin, (Indrajit) for a while was stupefied and had his senses overwhelmed.

sn: ददर्शावस्थितं वीरमाजौ दशरथात्मजम्। सोऽभिचक्राम सौमित्रिं रोषात्संरक्तलोचनः॥
en: And eyeing that heroson to Dasaratha-present in the encounter, (Indrajit) with his eyes crimsoned on choler, drew near Sumitrā's son. And coming up to him (Laksmana), he again addressed (that hero) in a harsh speech, saying.

sn: अब्रवीच्चैनमासाद्य पुनः स परुषं वचः। किं न स्मरसि तद्युद्धे प्रथमे मत्पराक्रमम्।। निबद्धस्त्वं सह भ्रात्रा यदा युधि विचेष्टसे॥ युवां खलु महायुद्धे वज्राशनिसमैः शरैः। शायितौ प्रथमं भूमौ विसंज्ञौ सपुर:सरौ॥
en: Did you not remember my prowess at that first encounter, when you along with your brother was bound up, that now you are discharging arms (at me)? Forsooth you two in mighty encounter, with shafts resembling the thunder-bolt and vajra, by me were first laid down on the ground, deprived of your lives, along with your principal adherents.

sn: स्मृतिर्वा नास्ति ते मन्ये व्यक्तं वा यमसादनम्। गन्तुमिच्छसि यन्मां त्वमाधर्षयितुमिच्छसि॥
en: Either this has escaped your memory or I fancy, you plainly act to go to the abode of Yama, inasmuch as you have set your heart on beating me.

sn: यदि ते प्रथमे युद्धे न दृष्टो मत्पराक्रमः। अद्य त्वां दर्शयिष्यामि तिष्ठेदानी व्यवस्थितः॥
en: If at the first encounter you have not witnessed my prowess, today shall I show it to you. Do you now stay, summoning your attention.

sn: इत्युक्त्वा सप्तभिर्बाणैरभिविव्याध लक्ष्मणम्। दशभिस्तु हनूमन्तं तीक्ष्णधारैः शरात्तमैः॥
en: Seeing this, he pierced Lakşmaņa with seven shafts, and Hanumān with ten keen-edged excellent shafts.

sn: ततः शरशतेनैव सुप्रयुक्तेन वीर्यवान्। क्रोधाद् द्विगुणसंरब्धो निर्बिभेद विभीषणम्॥
en: Then, fired with double fury, that powerful one pierced Vibhīşana with an hundred arrows, powerfully discharged (from his weapons.)

sn: तदृष्ट्वेन्द्रजिता कर्म कृतं रामानुजस्तदा। अचिन्तयित्वा प्रहसनैतत्किचिदिति ब्रुवन्। ५० ।।
en: Seeing this act of Indrajit, that foremost of men, Rama's younger brother, Laksmana, with an undaunted countenance, fired with wrath without minding the same, and saying with a laugh, this is nothing.'

sn: मुमोच च शरान्घोरान्संगृह्य नरपुङ्गवः। अभीतवदनः क्रुद्धो रावणिं लक्ष्मणो युधि॥ नैवं रणगताः शूराः प्रहरन्ति निशाचर। लघवश्चाल्पवीर्याश्च शरा हीमे सुखास्तव॥
en: Taking dreadful arrows, in the conflict, discharged them at the son of Ravana. "O nightrangers, heroes, coming to the field never discharge (such shafts as these). These arrows of your are light and of slight strength, and they conduce to my comfort. Heroic warriors eager for encounter, do not fight thus.

sn: नैवं शूरास्तु युध्यन्ते समरे युद्धकाङ्गिणः। इत्येवं तं ब्रुवन्धन्वी शरैरभिववर्ष ह॥
en: Speaking thus, (Laksmana) accoutred with his bow showered vollies of shafts (on his adversary).

sn: तस्य बाणैः सुविध्वस्तं कवचं काञ्चनं महत्। व्यशीर्यत रथोपस्थे ताराजालमिवाम्बरात्॥
en: And at his arrows (hitting), (Indrajit's) mighty golden mail fell off his person, and dropped to the platform of his car like a cluster of stars dropping from the welkin.

sn: विधूतवर्मा नाराचैर्बभूव स कृतव्रणः। इन्द्रजित्समरे वीरः प्रत्यूषे भानुमानिव ॥
en: With his armour dropping off, that hero— Indrajit was wounded with nárachas, like the Sun at dawn.

sn: ततः शरसहस्रेण संक्रुद्धो रावणात्मजः। बिभेद समरे वीरो लक्ष्मणं भीमविक्रमः॥
en: That hero, Ravana's son endowed with dreadful prowess, in that conflict, pierced Lakşmaņa with a thousand shafts.

sn: व्यशीर्यत महद्दिव्यं कवचं लक्ष्मणस्य तु। कृतप्रतिकृतान्योन्यं बभूवतुरभिद्रुतौ ॥
en: Thereat Lakşmaņa's gorgeous and mighty mail was rent in pieces. And each rushing forward was engaged in dealing blows and harrying them.
