sn: अभीक्ष्णं निःश्वसन्तौ वै युध्येतां तुमुलौ युधि। शरसंकृत्तसर्वाङ्गौ सर्वतो रुधिरोक्षितौ।। सुदीर्घकालं तौ वीरावन्योन्यं निशितैः शरैः॥
en: And sighing again and again, they faught furiously. And with their persons cut all over, and laved in blood, for a long while the heroes kept cleaving each other with sharpened shafts.

sn: ततक्षतुर्महात्मानौ रणकर्मविशारदौ। बभूवतुश्चात्मजये यत्तौ भीमपराक्रमौ॥
en: And those high-souled ones versed in warfare, and endowed with terrific prowess exerted their utmost in securing victory.

sn: तौ शरौषैस्तथाकीर्णो निकृत्तकवचध्वजौ। सृजन्तौ रुधिरं चोष्णं जलं प्रस्रवणाविव॥
en: And covered with vollies of shafts, with their armour and banners rent, they drew each other's warm blood flowing like water from a fountain.

sn: शरवर्षं ततो घोरं मुञ्चतोर्भीमनिःस्वनम्। सासारयोरिवाकाशे नीलयोः कालमेघयोः॥
en: They discharged dreadful showers attended with tremendous sounds, like the sounds of black clouds at Dooms-day* pouring torrents in the sky. * Kalameghayo (gen). The commentator says the word means (black clouds; but I prefer the sense given.

sn: तयोरथ महान्कालो व्यतीयाधुध्यमानयोः। न च तौ युद्धवैमुख्यं क्लमं चाप्युपजग्मतुः॥
en: A long time went by as they faught. Not did they turn away from the encounter, or know fatigue.

sn: अस्त्राण्यस्त्रविदां श्रेष्ठौ दर्शयन्तौ पुनः पुनः। शरानुच्चावचाकारानन्तरिक्षे बबन्धतुः॥
en: Those foremost of those acquainted with weapons repeatedly displayed their weapons; and their long and short shafts enveloped the welkin.

sn: व्यपेतदोषमस्यन्तौ लघु चित्रं च सुष्ठु च। उभौ तु तुमुलं घोरं चक्रतुर्नरराक्षसौ॥
en: The skill that they displayed was perfect, and showed lightness, variety and grace; and both man and the Rākşasa carried on fearful and terrible conflict.

sn: तयोः पृथक्पृथग्भीमः शुश्रुवे तुमुलः स्वनः। स कम्पं जनयामास निर्घात इव दारुणः॥
en: The dreadful and tremendous roars of each were audible (at that place); and terrific like the levin, they made the hearts of hearers tremble (in terror).

sn: तयोः स भ्राजते शब्दस्तथा समरयत्तयोः। सुघोरयोनि:स्वनतोगगने मेघयोरिव॥
en: As they faught with might and main, the sounds that they sent resembled the deep rumbling of clouds in the sky.

sn: सुवर्णपुजैर्नाराचैर्बलवन्तौ कृतव्रणौ। प्रसुनुवाते रुधिरं कीर्तिमन्तौ जये धृतौ॥
en: And pierced with närâchas knobbed with gold, those-powerful and illustrious (warriors) with their hearts set on celebrity, bled profusely.

sn: ते गात्रयोनिपतिता रुक्मपुङ्खाः शरा युधि। असृग्दिग्धा विनिष्पेतुर्विविशुर्धरणीतलम्॥
en: in that engagement gold-knobbed shafts hitting each other's person, pierced the same and covered with gore, entered the earth.

sn: अन्ये सुनिशितैः शस्त्रैराकाशे संजघट्टिरे। बभञ्जश्चिच्छिदुश्चैव तयोर्बाणाः सहस्रशः॥
en: And other shafts were resisted in the sky by sharpened weapons, and some were snapped, and thousands of their arrows were cleft (in the sky).

sn: स बभूव रणे घोरस्तयोर्बाणमयश्चयः। अग्निभ्यामिव दीप्ताभ्यां सत्रे कुशमयश्च यः॥
en: In that field, the vollies of their shafts were dreadful to behold like to a heap of Kusa aflame in a sacrifice.

sn: तयोः कृतव्रणौ देहौ शुशुभाते महात्मनोः। सुपुष्पाविव निष्पत्रौ वने किंशुकशाल्मली।७१।।
en: The wounded frames of those high-souled ones appeared beautiful like a leafless flowering Kinsuka and Sālmali in wood.

sn: चक्रतुस्तुमुलं घोरं संनिपातं मुहुर्मुहुः। इन्द्रजिल्लक्ष्मणश्चैव परस्परजयैषिणौ॥
en: Each eager to vanquish the other, Indrajit and Lakşmaņa momentarily discharged tremendous and terrific showers (of arms).

sn: लक्ष्मणो रावणिं युद्ध रावणिश्चापि लक्ष्मणम्। अन्योन्यं तावविभिघ्नन्तौ न श्रमं प्रतिपद्यताम्॥
en: Laksmana smiting Ravana's son, and Ravana's son smiting Lakşmaņa, they did not experience any fatigue.

sn: बाणजालैः शरीरस्थैरवगाडैस्तरस्विनौ। शुशुभाते महावीर्यो प्ररूढाविव पर्वतौ॥
en: With net-works of arrows deeply entering their persons, those vehement and exceedingly powerful ones resembled mountains topped (with trees).

sn: ततो रुधिरसिक्तानि संवृतानि शरैर्भृशम्। बभ्राजुः सर्वगात्राणि ज्वलन्त इव पावकाः॥
en: All their limbs, drenched in blood and covered with arrows, looked like a blazing fire.

sn: तयोरथ महान्कालो व्यतीयाधुध्यमानयोः। न च तौ युद्धवैमुख्यं श्रमं चाप्यभिजग्मतुः॥
en: A great while did they fight; yet they neither turned away (from the fight), nor did they experience any exhaustion.

sn: अथ समरपरिश्रमं निहन्तुं समरमुखेष्वजितस्य लक्ष्मणस्य। प्रियहितमुपपादयन्महात्मा समरमुपेत्य विभीषणोऽवतस्थे॥
en: Then to remove (Laksmana's) fatigue from fight, the high-souled Vibhisana, working the weal of Laksmaņa staying in front of the field, came forward in the encounter and took up his post.

sn: युध्यमानौ ततो दृष्ट्वा प्रसक्तौ नरराक्षसौ। प्रभिन्नाविव मातंगौ परस्परजयैषिणौ॥ तयायुद्धं द्रष्टुकामो वरचापधरो बली। शूरः स रावणभ्राता तस्थौ संग्राममूर्धनि ॥
en: Seeing the man and the Rākṣasa engaged in battle, with their whole soul, each eager to beat the other, like to elephants with the temporal juice trickling from their temples, desirous of beholding their encounter, Răvaņa's mighty and heroic brother, bearing an excellent bow, stood in front of the arena.

sn: ततो विस्फारयामास महद्धनुरवस्थितः। उत्ससर्ज च तीक्ष्णग्रान्राक्षसेषु महाशरान्॥
en: Taking up his post, he stretched his great bow and shot terrific sharp-pointed shafts at the Rāks asas.

sn: ते शराः शिखिसंस्पर्शा निपतन्तः समाहिताः। राक्षसान्दारयामासुर्वज्रा इव महागिरीन्॥
en: Even like thunder-bolt cleaving mighty mountains, those shafts furnished with peacock's plumes falling powerfully (upon the foe), rent the Raksasas.

sn: विभीषणस्यानुचरास्तेऽपि शूलासिपट्टिशैः। चिच्छिदुः समरे वीराराक्षसान्राक्षसोत्तमाः॥
en: Those foremost of Raksasas, Vibhisana's followers, also in the encounter discharged darts and scimitars and pațțiśas at heroic Rākşasas.

sn: राक्षसैस्तैः परिवृतः स तदा तु विभीषणः। बभौ मध्ये प्रधृष्टानां कलभानामिव द्विपः॥
en: Surrounded by those Raksasas, Vibhisana, then in the midst of his followers, appeared like an elephant in the midst of young ones.

sn: ततः संचोदमानो वै हरीरक्षोवधप्रियान्। उवाच वचनं काले कालज्ञो रक्षसां वरः॥
en: Then inciting the monkeys, whose dear object was to slay Ravana, that one versed in time, the foremost of Rākşasas,spoke seasonably thus.

sn: एकोऽयं राक्षसेन्द्रस्य परायणमवस्थितः। एतच्छेषं बलं तस्य किं तिष्ठत हरीश्वराः॥ तस्मिंश्च निहते पापे राक्षसे रणमूर्धनि। रावणं वर्जयित्वा तु शेषमस्य बलं हतम्॥
en: This one that stay (in the field) is the sole and mighty support of the Raksasa-chief; and this is his remaining force. Why then do the monkeychiefs remain inactive? On this wicked Rāksasa being slain on the edge of battle, the remnant of his army, with the single exception of Rāvawa, is destroyed.

sn: प्रहस्तो निहतो वीरो निकुम्भश्च महाबलः। कुम्भकर्णश्च कुम्भश्च धूम्राक्षश्च निशाचरः॥ जम्बुमाली महामाली तीक्ष्णवेगोऽशनिप्रभः। सुप्तघ्नो यज्ञकोपश्च वज्रदंष्ट्रश्च राक्षसः॥ संहादी विकटोऽरिघ्नस्तपनो मन्द एव च। प्रघासः प्रघसश्चैव प्रजङ्घो जङ्घ एव च॥ अग्निकेतुश्च दुर्धर्षो रश्मिकेतुश्च वीर्यवान्। विद्युज्जिह्वो द्विजिह्वश्च सूर्यशत्रुश्च राक्षसः॥ अकम्पनः सुपार्श्वश्च चक्रमाली च राक्षसः। कम्पनः सत्त्ववन्तश्च देवान्तकनरान्तकौ॥
en: That hero-prahasta-has been slain, and Nikumbha possessed of wondrous strength, and Kumbhakarņa, and Kumbha and the night-ranger Dhūmrākṣa, and Jämbumāli and Mahāmāli and Tikşņavega and Hemaprabha, and Suptaghna, and Yajñakopa, and the Rākşasa Vajradanștra, Samhradi, and Vikata, and Arighna, and Tapana, and Manda, and Fraghāsa and Praghasa, and Prajangha, and Jangha, and Agniketu, and Durdharsa, and the powerful Rasmiketu and Vidyujjihva, and Dvijihva, and the RaksasaSüryaśatru, and Akampana, and Supārsva, and the Raksasas-Cakramali, and Kampana, and Satvavanta, and Devāntaka and Narāntaka.

sn: एतानिहत्यातिबलान्बहूराक्षससत्तमान्। बाहुभ्यां सागरं तीर्खा लङ्घयतां गोष्पदं लघु।।१५
en: Having slain these many powerful Rākşasas endowed with excess of might, having crossed the sea with your arms, do you cross this foot print of a cow.

sn: एतावदेव शेषं वो जेतव्यमिति वानराः। हताः सर्वे समागम्य राक्षसा बलदर्पिताः॥
en: This is the remaining force which you monkeys must conquer; all those Rākşasas, that had come forward, elated with the pride of strength, have all been slain.

sn: अयुक्तं निधनं कर्तुं पुत्रस्य जनितुर्मम । घृणामपास्य रामार्थे निहन्यां भ्रातुरात्मजम्॥
en: It is not meet for me to slay the son of my brother, yet, casting off compassion will I for Rama slay him.* *The text has 'brother's son.'

sn: हन्तुकामस्य मे बाष्पं चक्षुश्चैव निरुध्यति। तमेवैष महाबाहुर्लक्ष्मणः शमयिष्यति॥
en: Tears surcharge the eyes of me who seek to slay him. Let therefore Lakşmaņa administer him his quietus.

sn: वानरा घ्नत संभूय भृत्यानस्य समीपगान्। इति तेनातियशसा राक्षसेनाभिचोदिताः॥
en: You monkeys, do you in a body (first) slaughter those that are beside him (Indrajit.)" Thus exhorted by that illustrious Rākşasa, the monkey-chiefs, were exhilarated and began to flourish their tails.

sn: वानरेन्द्रा जहषिरे लांगूलानि च विव्यधुः। ततस्तु कपिशार्दूलाः श्वेडन्तश्च पुनः पुनः।। मुमुचुर्विविधानादान्मेघान्दृष्ट्वेव बर्हिणः॥
en: Then those mighty monkeys roared again and again, and sent up various shouts, even as peacocks cry on seeing clouds.

sn: जाम्बवानपि तैः सर्वैः सयूथ्यैरभिसंवृतः। तेऽश्मभिस्ताडयामासुर्नखैर्दन्तैश्च राक्षसान्॥
en: Then Jämbavān surrounded by his own forces, assailed the Raksasas with rocks-and with their nails and teeth.

sn: निघ्नन्तमृक्षाधिपतिं राक्षसास्ते महाबलाः। परिभर्त्य भयं त्यक्त्वा तमनेकविधायुधाः॥ शरैः परशुभिस्तीक्ष्णैः पट्टिशैर्यष्टितोमरैः। जाम्बवन्तं मृधे जघ्नुनिघ्नन्तं राक्षसी चमूम्॥
en: Thereat Räkşasas, endowed with exceeding strength, equipped with various weapons reproaching the lord of bears, as he was engaged in smiting (the foe), and renouncing fear, with shafts and sharp axes and pațțiśas and yaşțis, and tomaras, in the encounter assailed Jambavān, who was engaged in beating the Räkşasa forces.

sn: स संप्रहारस्तुमुलः संजज्ञे कपिरक्षसाम्। देवासुराणां क्रुद्धानां यथा भीमो महास्वनः॥
en: That conflict between the monkeys and the Rākşasas, waxed furious, like to the tumultuous encounter of the immortals and the Asuras fired with wrath.

sn: हनूमानपि संक्रुद्धः सानुमुत्पाट्य पर्वतात्। स लक्ष्मणं स्वयं पृष्ठादवरोप्य महामनाः॥ रक्षसां कदनं चक्रे दुरासादः सहस्रशः।
en: The magnanimous Hanumān incapable of being approached growing wroth, uprooting a mountain, and putting down Lakşmaņa from his back, began a great carnage among the Rākşasas by thousands.

sn: स दत्त्वा तुमुलं युद्धं पितृव्यस्येन्द्रजिद्बली॥ लक्ष्मणं परवीरघ्नः पुनरेवाभ्यधावत।
en: And fighting a furious fight with his uncle, the powerful Indrajit, slayer of hostile heroesagain rushed against Lakşmaņa.

sn: तौ प्रयुद्धौ तदा वीरौ मृधे लक्ष्मणराक्षसौ॥ शरौघानभिवर्षन्तौ जघ्नतुस्तौ परस्परम्। अभीक्ष्णमन्तर्दधतुः शरजालैर्महाबलौ॥ चन्द्रादित्याविवोष्णान्ते यथा मेघैस्तरस्विनौ।
en: Then there took place an encounter between those heroes in the field, Laksmana and the Räksasa-discharging vollies of shafts and smiting each other; and those mighty and impetuous ones repeatedly covered each other with networks of arrows; like to the sun and the moon covered by clouds at the expiration of Summer.

sn: नह्यादानं न संधानं धनुषो वा परिग्रहः॥ न विप्रमोक्षो बाणानां न विकर्षों न विग्रहः। न मुष्टिप्रतिसंधानं न लक्ष्यप्रतिपादनम्॥
en: And on account of their light-handedness, neither discharge of arrows, nor the drawing of the bow; nor the setting of the shaft on the bowstring; not the taking of the bow; nor the selection of shafts; nor the clenching fast of their fists; nor the hitting of aims, could be perceived as they faught on.

sn: अदृश्यत तयोस्तत्र युध्यतोः पाणिलाघवात्। चापवेगप्रयुक्तैश्च बाणजालैः समन्ततः॥ अन्तरिक्षेऽभिसंपन्ने न रूपाणि चकाशिरे।
en: In consequence of the sky being covered with networks of arrows all around, discharged powerfully from their bows, the forms (of objects) could not be discovered.

sn: लक्ष्मणो रावणिं प्राप्य रावणिश्चापि लक्ष्मणम्॥ अव्यवस्था भवत्युग्रा ताभ्यामन्योन्यविग्रहे।
en: Laksmana having at Ravana's son, and Rāvana's son having at Lakşmana, critical was the huggermugger that ensued* in the encounter between each other. *i.e. in consequence of all sides being covered with arrows, neither the Rākşas nor the monkeys could distinguish their several parties in the encounter, and the blows that each dealt were misdirected in consequence.

sn: ताभ्यामुभाभ्यां तरसा प्रसृष्टैर्विशिखैः शितैः॥ निरन्तरमिवाकाशं बभूव तमसा वृतम्।
en: They both kept ceaselessly showering feathered and sharpened shafts, the firmament was engulphed with a deep darkness.

sn: तैः पतद्भिश्च बहुभिस्तयोः शरशतैः शितैः॥ दिशश्च प्रदिशश्चैव बभूवुः शरसंकुलाः।
en: In consequence of countless keen arrow alighting in hundreds, all sides and all the cardinal quarters were swarming with shafts.

sn: तमसा पिहितं सर्वमासीत्प्रतिभयं महत्॥ अस्तं गते सहस्रांशी संवते तमसा च वै। रुधिरौघा महानद्यः प्रावर्तन्त सहस्रशः।२६।। क्रव्यादा दारुणा वाग्भिश्चिक्षिपुर्भीमनिःस्वनान्। न तदानीं ववौ वायुर्न च जज्वाल पावकः॥ स्वस्त्यस्तु लोकेभ्य
en: And all being overspread with gloom, a mighty fright took possession (of creatures) when the Sun having ascended the setting-hill, and darkness environing all objects. And that day* mighty torrents of blood flowed in thousands of streams; and fierce beasts of prey set up terrific yells (all around). And at that hour the wind did not blow, and fire did not blaze. * Aiya today in the text.

sn: इति जजल्पुस्ते महर्षयः। संपेतुश्चात्र संतप्ता गन्धर्वाः सह चारणैः॥
en: The Maharsis said, 'Fair befell creatures.' And the Gandharvas along with the Cāranas grew exceedingly agitated.

sn: अथ राक्षससिंहस्य कृष्णान्कनकभूषणान्। शरैश्चतुर्भिः सौमित्रिर्विव्याध चतुरो हयान्॥
en: Then Sumitrā's son pierced the four black steeds of the leonine Räksasa, caparisoned in gold.

sn: ततोऽपरेण भल्लेन पीतेन निशितेन च। संपूर्णायतमुक्तेन सुपत्रेण सुवर्चसा ॥ महेन्द्राशनिकल्पेन सूतस्य विचरिष्यतः। स तेन बाणाशनिना तलशब्दानुनादिना ॥ लघवाद्राघवः श्रीमाशिरः कायादपाहरत्।
en: Then he hit at (Indrajit's) charioteer with another yellow and sharpened javelin splendid, furnished with feathers; and resembling the thunder-bolt of the great Indra. And through his fleet handedness the graceful son of Raghu with the thunder-bolt of his shaft, resonant with the sound of his palm, separated the (charioteer's head) from his trunk.

sn: स यन्तरि महातेजा हते मन्दोदरीसुतः।॥ स्वयं सारथ्यमकरोत्पुनश्च धनुरस्पृशत्। तदद्भुतमभूत्तत्र सारथ्यं पश्यतां युधि ॥
en: And on his charioteer having been slain the exceedingly energetic son of Mandodari, himself began to perform the function of a charioteer, and took up his bow. And this in the encounter was wonderful to behold.

sn: हयेषु व्यग्रहस्तं तं विव्याध निशितैः शरैः। धनुष्यथ पुनर्व्यग्रं हयेषु मुमुचे शरान्॥
en: Then as (Indrajit) was eagerly engaged in managing the steeds, (Laksmana) pierced him with sharpened shafts; and when (Indrajit) was eagerly wielding his bow, (Laksmana) discharged shafts at his steeds.

sn: छिन्नेषु तेषु बाणौधैर्विचरन्तमभीतवत्। अर्दयामास समरे सौमित्रिः शीघ्रकृत्तमः॥
en: And on his steeds having been torn with shafts, Sumitrā's-foremost of fleet-handed in the encounter assailed (Indrajit) doubtlessly ranging the field.

sn: निहतं सारथिं दृष्ट्वा समरे रावणात्मजः। प्रजही समरोद्धर्ष विषण्णः स बभूव ह।॥
en: Seeing his charioteer slain in the contest, Rāvana's son forewent his martial ardour, and was cast down.

sn: विषण्णवदनं दृष्ट्वा राक्षसं हरियूथपाः। ततः परमसंहृष्टा लक्ष्मणं चाभ्यपूजयन्॥
en: Seeing the Rākşasa with his face fallen, the leaders of monkey-hands, were exceedingly delighted and rendered homage to Lakşmaņa.

sn: ततः प्रमाथी रभसः शरभो गन्धमादनः। अमृष्यमाणाश्चत्वारश्चनुर्वेगं हरीश्वराः॥
en: Then those monkey-chiefs— Pramāthi, Rabhasa, Sarabha and Gandamādana, not brooking (their foe) summoned their impetuosity.

sn: ते चास्य हयमुख्येषु तूर्णमुत्पत्य वानराः। चतुर्षु सुमहावीर्या निपेतुर्भीमविक्रमाः॥
en: And suddenly springing up, those highly powerful monkeys endowed with terrific prowess descended upon those four best of steeds.

sn: तेषामधिष्ठितानां तैर्वानरैः पर्वतोपमैः। मुखेभ्यो रुधिरं व्यक्तं हयानां समवर्तत॥
en: On those chargers being assailed by those monkeys resembling mountains, blood gushed out of their mouths.

sn: ते हया मथिता भग्ना व्यसवो धरणीं गताः। ते निहत्य हयांस्तस्य प्रमथ्य च महारथम्॥ पुनरुत्पत्य वेगेन तस्थुर्लक्ष्मणपार्श्वतः॥
en: Then the steeds were smashed and sent to the ground. And having slain the steeds, and smitten the mighty car-warrior,* again by a vehement bound, came to the side of Laksmana. *Maharatham (ac.) may also mean mighty car. By the way the samasa or junction called Tatpurusha is a frequent source of obscurity in Sanskrit specially where the gender of the word without samása is the same with that of the thing signified by the samāsa, as in this case.

sn: स हताश्वादवप्लुत्य रथान्मथितसारथिः। शरवर्षेण सौमित्रिमभ्यधावत रावणिः॥
en: Springing down from his car whose steeds had been slain, Ravana's son, his charioteer having been pounded, charged the son of Sumitra with arrows.

sn: ततो महेन्द्रप्रतिमः सलक्ष्मणः पदातिनं तं निहतैहयोत्तमैः। मृजन्तमाजौ निशिताञ्छरोत्तमान्भृशं तदा बाणगतैर्व्यदारयत्॥
en: Then Lakşmaņa resembling the great Indra, on (Indrajit's) best of chargers having been despatched, in the encounter began to terribly rive with arrows discharged (his foe) footing on the earth and showering excellent sharpened shafts.

sn: स हताश्वो महातेजा भूमौ तिष्ठनिशाचरः। इन्द्रजित्परमक्रुद्धः संप्रजज्वाल तेजसा॥
en: Having his steeds slain, the night-rangerIndrajit, standing on the ground, waxing fiercely angered, flamed up in energy.

sn: तौ धन्विनौ जिघांसन्तावन्योन्यमिषुभिर्भृशम्। विजयेनाभिनिष्क्रान्तौ वने गजवृषाविव॥
en: And armed with bows, they, desirous of slaying each other with shafts resembled an elephant and a bull in a forest, came out for securing victory in encounter.

sn: निबर्हयन्तश्चान्योन्यं ते राक्षसवनौकसः। भर्तारं न जहुयुद्धे संपतन्तस्ततस्ततः॥
en: And slaughtering one another the Rākşasas and the wood-rangers, rushing this way and that, did not (for a moment) leave their lords.

sn: ततस्तान्राक्षसान्सर्वान्हर्षयन्रावणात्मजः। स्तुन्वानो हर्षमाणश्च इदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Then Rāvana's son, gladdening all the Rākşasas, and himself feeling cheered, addressed them in words of praise, saying.

sn: तमसा बहुलेनेमाः संसक्ताः सर्वतो दिश:। नेह विज्ञायते स्वो वा परो वा राक्षसोतमाः।।।।
en: All sides are entirely enveloped in this gioom, so that, O foremost of Raksasas, here we dysiot know who belong to us and who not.

sn: धृष्टं भवन्तो युध्यन्तु हरीणां पोहताय वै। अहं तु रथमास्थाय आगमिष्या संयुगे ।।। तथा भवन्तः कुर्वन्तु यथेगे हि बनौकसः। न युध्येयुर्महात्मानः प्रविले नगरं पयि ! १ !!
en: Do you fight fearlessly for stupefying the monkeys; and I too, mounted on a car, shall come hither into the conflict. Do you so act that the high-souled rangers of the woods may not attack me as I enter the city

sn: इत्युक्त्वा रावणसुतो वञ्चयित्वा वनौकराः प्रविवेश पुरीं लङ्का रथहेतोरमित्रहा ! १८ ।। स रथं भूषयित्वाथ रुचिरं हेगभूषितम्। प्रासासिशरसंयुक्तं युक्तं परमवाजिभिः॥ अधिष्ठितं हयज्ञेन सूतेनाप्तोपदेशिला। आरुरोह महातेजा रावणिः समितिजसः ॥
en: Saying this, that slayer of foes-Rávana's son. deceiving the wood-rangers, entered the ciiy of Lankā for providing himself with a (freah) car And embeilishing a chariot, graceful and adorned with gold, furnished with prāsas and swords and arrows, yoked with superb steeds, and driven by a charioteer, knowing horses and possessed of instructions (anent his art), that victor in battle-the exceedingly energetic son of Ravana-ascended it,

sn: स राक्षसगणैर्मुख्यैर्वृतो मन्दोदरीसुतः। निर्ययौ नगराद्वीरः कृतान्तबलचोदितः १११।। सोऽभिनिष्क्रम्य नगरादिन्द्रजित्परौजसा। अभ्ययाज्जवनैरश्वैर्लक्ष्यणं सविभीषण!१२३
en: That hero, Mandodari's son urged on by the force of the Finisher, went out of the city, surrounded by the foreinost Räksasas; and drawn by fast-speeding steeds, he presented himself before Lakşmaņa along with Vibhisana.

sn: ततो रथस्थमालोक्य सौमित्री रावणात्मजम्। वानराश्च महावीर्या राक्षसश्च विभीषणः॥ विस्मयं परमं जग्मुर्लाघवात्तस्य धीमतः।
en: Seeing Răvaşa's son seated on the car, the son of Sumitrā and the exceedingly powerful monkeys and the Raksasa-Vibhisana-were highly amazed at the lighthandedness of that intelligent one.

sn: रावणिश्चापि संक्रुद्धो रणे वानरयूथपान्॥ पातयामास बाणौषैः शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः।
en: And Ravana's son, waxing furious, in that contest began to bring down monkeys by hundreds and by thousands.

sn: स मण्डलीकृतधनू रावणिः समितिंजयः॥ हरीनभ्यहनत्क्रुद्धः परं लाघवमास्थितः।
en: That victor in battle— Rāvana's son fired with wrath, summoning all his celerity, slaughtered monkeys, drawing his bow into a circle.

sn: ते वध्यमाना हरयो नाराचैर्भीमविक्रमैः॥ सौमित्रिं शरणं प्राप्ताः प्रजापतिमिव प्रजाः।
en: And slaughtered by närâchas of terrific impetuosity, the monkeys saught the shelter of Sumitrā's son, like creatures seeking the refuge of their lord.

sn: ततः समरकोपेन ज्वलितो रघुनन्दनः।। चिच्छेद कार्मुकं तस्य दर्शयन्पाणिलाघवम्॥
en: Then the son of Raghu, flaming up in martial wrath, severed his* bow, displaying his fleethandedness. *Indrajit's.

sn: सोऽन्यत्कार्मुकमादाय सज्ज चक्रे त्वरत्रिव। तदप्यस्य त्रिभिर्बाणैर्लक्ष्मणो निरकृन्तत ॥
en: Thereat, taking another bow, (Indrajit) hurriedly fastened the string to it. And this bow also did Lakşmaņa cut off by means of a brace of arrows.

sn: अथैनं छिन्नधन्वानमाशीविषविषोपमैः। विव्याधोरसि सौमित्री रावणिं पञ्चभिः शरैः॥
en: When (Indrajit) had his bow severed, Suinitra's son pierced the son of Rāvana with five shafts resembling the venom of a poisonous serpent. piercing his?

sn: ते तस्य कायं निर्भिद्य महाकार्मुकनिःसृताः। निपेतुर्धरणी बाणा रका इव महोरगाः॥
en: The shafts discharged from his' mighty bow, person, dropped to the earth like to powerful red serpents. 1. Laksmana's. 2. Indrajit's.

sn: स छिनधन्वा रुधिरं वमन्वक्रेण रावणिः। जग्राह कार्मुकश्रेष्ठं दृढज्यं बलवत्तरम्॥
en: Having his bow cut off, Ravana's son, vomiting blood by his mouth, took up a superior bow powerful to a degree and having a stout string.

sn: स लक्ष्मणं समुद्दिश्य परं लाघवमास्थितः। ववर्ष शरवर्षाणि वर्षाणीव पुरंदरः॥
en: Then aiming at Lakşmaņa, he, summoning his utmost celerity, showered arrows, as shower Purandara in the season of rains.

sn: मुक्तमिन्द्रजिता तत्तु शरवर्षमरिंदमः। आवारयदसंभ्रान्तो लक्ष्मणः सुदुरासदम्॥
en: Thereat Laksmana, subduer of enemies, retaining his calmness, resisted that powerful arrows shower shot by Indrajit.

sn: संदर्शयामास तदा रावणिं रघुनन्दनः। असंभ्रान्तो महातेजास्तदद्भुतमिवाभवत्॥
en: Then that exceedingly energetic one, Rahgu's son, possessing himself in calmness, displayed (his prowess) to the son of Ravana; and this was wonderful (to behold).

sn: ततस्ताराक्षसान्सस्त्रिभिरेकैकमाहवे। अविध्यत्परमनुद्धः शीघ्रास्त्रं संप्रदर्शयन्।। राक्षसेन्द्रस्तु तं चापि बाणौघैः समताडयत्॥
en: Then displaying his lightness in the use of weapons, Laksmana, growing furious, pierced the Rakşasas with three arrows each in that mighty encounter; and the lord of Räkşasas struck him with showers of shafts.

sn: सोऽतिविद्धो बलवता शत्रुणा शत्रुघातिना। असक्तं प्रेषयामास लक्ष्मणाय बहूशरान्॥
en: And pierced sore by that powerful enemyslayer of foes— be incessantly sent innumerable arrows after Lakşmaņa.

sn: तानप्राप्ताशितैर्भाणैश्चिच्छेद परवीरहा। सारथेरस्य च रणे रथिनो रथसत्तमः॥ शिरो जहार धर्मात्मा भल्लेनानतपर्वणा।
en: And ere they reached their destination, that slayer of hostile heroes severed them with whetted arrows; and in the encounter that righteous one and foremost of car-warriors with a dart having bent joints, cut off the head of his charioteer mounted on the car.

sn: असूतास्ते हयास्तत्र रथमूहुरविक्लवाः॥ मण्डलान्यभिधावन्ति तदद्भुतमिवाभवत्।
en: And deprived of their driver, there the steeds, retaining their calmness, began to go in rounds and this was wonderful.

sn: अमर्षवशमापन्नः सौमित्रिर्दृढविक्रमः॥ प्रत्यविध्यद्धयांस्तस्य शरैर्वित्रासयन्रणे।
en: Then Sumitrā's son of steady prowess, fired with anger, in that contest, frightening all, pierced his horses with arrows.

sn: अमर्षमाणस्तत्कर्म रावणस्य सुतो रणे॥ विव्याध दशभिर्बाणैः सौमित्रिं रोमहर्षणम्।
en: And not brooking that act (of his adversary), Rāvana's son in the encounter pierced with ten shafts Sumitrā's son capable of making people's down stand on end.

sn: ते तस्य वज्रप्रतिमाः शराः सर्वविषोपमाः।। विलयं जग्मुरागत्य कवचं काञ्चनप्रभम्॥
en: And his shafts resembling thunder-bolts, and like to all varieties of venom, touching (Lakş mana's) mail having a golden splendour, were reduced to naught.

sn: अभेद्यकवचं मत्वा लक्ष्मणं रावणात्मजः। ललाटे लक्ष्मणं बाणैः सुपझेस्त्रिभिरिन्द्रजित्॥ अविध्यत्परमक्रुद्धः शीघ्रमस्त्रं प्रदर्शयन्। तैः पृषत्कैर्ललाटस्थैः शुशुभे रघुनन्दनः॥ रणाग्रे समरश्लाघी त्रिशृङ्ग इव पर्वतः।
en: Thereat considering Lakşmaņa as clad in an impenetrable armour, Ravana's son-Indrajitgrowing furiously enraged, displaying his lighthanedness in arms, pierced Lakşmaņa in the temples with three well-knobbed shafts. And with those arrows lodged in his temples, Raghu's son, delighting in battle, appeared beautiful in the field like a mountain furnished with three summits.

sn: स तथाप्यर्दितो बाणै राक्षसेन तदा मृधे॥ तमाशु प्रतिविव्याध लक्ष्मणः पञ्चभिः शरैः। विकृष्येन्द्रजितो युद्धे वदने शुभकुण्डले॥
en: Albeit thus smitten in the contest by the Rākşa with shafts, Lakşmaņa swiftly smote him in turn with five arrows; and in the encounter Lakşmaņa drawing his bow, pierced with shafts Indrajit's face graced with elegant ear-rings.

sn: लक्ष्मणेन्द्रजितौ वीरौ महाबलशरासनौ। अन्योन्यं जघ्नतुर्वीरौ विशिखैीमविक्रमौ॥
en: And those heroes-Lakşmaņa and Indrajitequipped with exceedingly powerful bows, and endowed with heroism and dreadful prowess, wounded each other with sharp arrows.

sn: ततः शोणितदिग्धाङ्गो लक्ष्मणेन्द्रजितावुभौ। रणे तौ रेजतुर्वीरौ पुष्पिताविव किंशुकौ॥
en: Both Lakşmaņa and Indrajit, with their persons bathed in blood in that encounter, appeared like to flowering Kinsukas.

sn: तौ परस्परमभ्येत्य सर्वगात्रेषु धन्विनौ। घोरैर्विव्यधतुर्बाणैः कृतभावावुभौ जये॥
en: And approaching each other, those bowmen, each setting his heart on victory, wounded each other all over the body with terrific shafts.

sn: ततः समरकोपेन संयुतो रावणात्मजः। विभीषणं त्रिभिर्बाणैर्विव्याध वदने शुभे॥
en: Then Ravana's son, carried away by martial rage, pierced Vibhīşaņa in his handsome face with three arrows.

sn: अयोमुखैत्रिभिर्विद्ध्वा राक्षसेन्द्र विभीषणम्। एकैकानभिविव्याध तान्सन्हिरियूथपान्॥
en: And piercing the lord of Rākṣasas, Vibhișaņa, he with three iron-headed arrows, pierced the monkey-leaders each with a shaft.

sn: तस्मै दृढतरं क्रुद्धो जघान गदया हयान्। विभीषणो महातेजा रावणेः स दुरात्मनः॥
en: Thereat, enraged at him more furiously then ever, the exceedingly energetic Vibhīşana with his mace despatched the steeds of the wickedminded son of Răvaņa.

sn: स हताश्वादवप्लुत्य रथान्मथितसारथिः। अथ शक्तिं महातेजाः पितृव्याय मुमोच ह।॥
en: Then jumping down from his chariot with its horses slain, (Indrajit), endowed with great cnergy, who had his charioteer pounded, discharged a dart at his uncle.

sn: तामापतन्ती संप्रेक्ष्य सुमित्रानन्दवर्धनः। चिच्छेद निशितैर्बाणैर्दशधापातयद्भुवि ॥
en: Seeing it descend, the enhancer of Sumitrā's joy severed the same with whetted arrows and brought it down in ten fragments to the ground.

sn: तस्मै दृढधनुः क्रुद्धो हताश्वाय विभीषणः। वज्रस्पर्शसमान्पञ्च सस।रसि मार्गणान्॥
en: And Vibhîşana of a tough bow, growing enraged, discharged at (Indrajit), who had his steeds slain, five speeding shafts having the touch of the thunder-bolt.

sn: ते तस्य कायं भिष्ट्वा तु रुक्मपुङ्खा निमित्तगाः। बभूवुर्लोहिता दिग्धा रक्ता इव महोरगाः॥
en: And those arrows furnished with gold at the feathered parts, riving his person, were bathed in blood, and resembled mighty red serpents.

sn: स पितृव्यस्य संक्रुद्ध इन्द्रजिच्छरमाददे। उत्तमं रक्षसां मध्ये यमदत्तं महाबलम्॥
en: Thereat wroth with his uncle, Indrajit took up an excellent shaft-bestowed on him by Yama himself-endowed with terrific force, the flower of shafts among all the Rākşasas.

sn: तं समीक्ष्य महातेजा महेषु तेन संधितम्। लक्ष्मणोऽप्याददे बाणमन्यद्भीमपराक्रमः॥ कुबेरेण स्वयं स्वप्ने यद्दत्तममितात्मना। दुर्जयं दुर्विषां च सेन्ट्रैरपि सुरासुरैः॥
en: Seeing that mighty shaft set by him (on the bow-string), the highly powerful Laksmana, possessed of dreadful prowess, (in his turn) took up another arrow, bestowed by Kuvera himself of imme jurable soul in a dream, unconquerable, and incapable of being borne even by the celestials and Asuras with Indra at their head.

sn: तयोस्तु धनुषी श्रेष्ठे बाहुभिः परिघोपमैः। विकृष्यमाणे बलवत्क्रौञ्चाविव चुकूजतुः॥
en: On their best of bows being powerfully drawn with their arms resembling bludgeons, they set up cries like to Krauñcas.

sn: ताभ्यां तु धनुषि श्रेष्ठे संहितौ सायकोत्तमौ। विकृष्यमाणौ वीराभ्यां भृशं जज्वलतुः श्रिया।५०॥
en: On those foremost of shafts set on those excellent bows of those heroes, being drawn, flamed up in exceeding splendour.

sn: तौ भासयन्तावाकाशं धनुभ्यां विशिखौ च्युतौ। मुखेन मुखमाहत्य संनिपेततुरोजसा॥
en: Those flaming arrows, discharged from the bows, illumining the welkin, with vehemence struck at each others head.

sn: संनिपातस्तयोश्चासीच्छरयो?ररूपयोः। सधूमविस्फुलिङ्गश्च तज्जोऽग्निर्दारुणोऽभवत्।५२।।
en: A concussion took place of those arrows of terrific aspects; and a furious fire sprang up thereat, with embers shooting around.

sn: तौ महाग्रहसंकाशावन्योन्यं संनिपत्य च। संग्रामे शतधा यातौ मेदिन्यां चैव पेततुः॥
en: And dashing against each other like to mighty planets, they, reduced to an hundred shivers in the encounter, saught the earth.

sn: शरौ प्रतिहतौ दृष्ट्वा तावुभौ रणमूर्धनि। वीडितौ जातरोषौ च लक्ष्मणेन्द्रजितौ तदा॥
en: Seeing their shafts baffled, Indrajit and Laks mana, staying on the edge of the battie, were seized with shame and wrath.

sn: स संरब्धस्तु सौमित्रिरत्रं वारुणमाददे। रौद्रं महेन्द्रजियुद्धेऽप्यसृजधुद्धविष्ठितः॥ तेन तद्विहतं शस्त्रं वारुणं परमाद्भुतम्।
en: Thereat Sumitra's son, flying into a fury, took up a Vāruņa weapon. And the conqueror of the great Indra intent on battle, in the encounter discharged a terrific Raudra weapon; and the exceedingly wonderful Văruņa weapon was baffled by him.

sn: ततः क्रुद्धो महातेजा इन्द्रजित्समितिंजयः।। आग्नेयं संदधे दीप्तं सलोकं संक्षिपन्निव। ५६॥
en: Then, waxing wroth, that victor in battle-the wondrous energetic Indrajit—as if annihilating the world, discharged a flaming Angeya weapon.

sn: सौर्येणास्त्रेण तं वीरो लक्ष्मणः पर्यवारयत्। अस्त्रं निवारितं दृष्ट्वा रावणिः क्रोधमूर्च्छितः।।५७ आददे निशितं बाणमासुरं शत्रुदारणम्। तस्माच्चापाद्विनिष्पेतु स्वराः कूटमुद्गराः॥ शूलानि च भुशुण्ड्यश्च गदाः खङ्गाः परश्वधाः।
en: The heroic Lakşmaņa resisted it with a Solar weapon. Seeing his weapon resisted, Ravana's son, transported with passion, took up an Asura arrow, capable of rending foes. And from that weapon issued daggers and clubs and darts and bhusundis and maces and swords and axes.* *This arrow resembled somewhat the bomb-shells in modern European warfare.

sn: तदृष्ट्वा लक्ष्मणः संख्ये घोरमस्त्रं सुदारुणम्।।५९ अवार्यं सर्वभूतानां सर्वशस्त्रविदारणम्। माहेश्वरेण द्युतिमांस्तदत्रं प्रत्यवारयत्॥
en: And in the conflict, seeing that dire and dreadful weapon, irresistible to all creatures and capable of riving all arms, the effulgent Lakşmaņa baffled it with a Māheśvara* weapon. *i.e. belonging to Maheśvara or Śiva.

sn: तयोः समभवद्युद्धमद्भुतं रोमहर्षणम्। गगनस्थानि भूतानि लक्ष्मणं पर्यवारयन्॥
en: The encounter that took place between them was wonderful and capable of making people's down stand on end. And beings stationed in the sky surrounded Lakşmaņa on all sides.

sn: भैरवाभिरुते भीमे युद्धे वानररक्षसाम्। भूतैर्बहुभिराकाशं विस्मितैरावृतं बभौ॥
en: In that terrific encounter of the monkeys and the Rākşasas resounding with dreadful roars, the welkin was covered with innumerable beings seized with wonderment.

sn: ऋषयः पितरो देवा गन्धर्वगरुडोरगाः। शतक्रतुं पुरस्कृत्य ररक्षुर्लक्ष्मणं रणे॥
en: Saints and Pitrs and deities and Gandharvas and birds and serpents, placing Satakratu in their front, protected Laksmana in the conflict.

sn: अथान्यं मार्गणश्रेष्ठं संदधे राघवानुजः। हुताशनसमस्पर्श रावणात्मजदारणम्॥ सुपत्रमनुवृत्तानं सुपर्वाणं सुसंस्थितम्। सुवर्णविकृतं वीरः शरीरान्तकरं शरम्॥ दुरावारं दुर्विषमं राक्षसानां भयावहम्। आशीविषविषप्रख्यं देवसङ्घः समर्चितम्। ६६ ।। येन शक्रो महातेजा दानवानजयत्प्रभुः। पुरा देवासुरे युद्धे वीर्यवान्हरिवाहनः ॥ अथैन्द्रमस्त्रं सौमित्रिः संयुगेष्वपराजितम्। शरश्रेष्ठं धनुःश्रेष्ठे विकर्षन्निदमब्रवीत् ॥ लक्ष्मीवांल्लक्ष्मणो वाक्यमर्थसाधकमात्मनः। धर्मात्मा सत्यसंधश्च रामो दाशरथिदि।। पौरुषे चाप्रतिद्वन्द्वस्तदैनं जहि रावणिम् ॥ इत्युक्त्वा बाणमाकर्णं विकृष्य तमजिह्मगम्। लक्ष्मणः समरे वीरः ससर्जेन्द्रजितं प्रति।।
en: Then that hero, Rāghava's younger brother, fixed (on his bow) another superior shaft, having the feel of fire itself, and capable of riving the son of Rävaņa; furnished with fair feathers; tapering; having elegant joints; symmetrical; and plated with gold, and arrow capable of finishng the body; irresistible; dreadful; terrific to Raks asas; resembling the venoin of poisonous serpents; and worshipped by the celestial hosts; by which the exceedingly energetic and wonderful Lord riding the horse' Sakra-of old in the war between the celestials and the Asuras had defeated the Dānavas. And Sumitra's son, Lakşmana graced with auspiciousness, drawing on his best of bows that foremost of sharts to Airdra weapon-invincible in conflict, spoke these words, tending to bring about his success, "If Daſaratha's son-Rāma is righteous and truthful, and if in prowess he has no rival, then slay this son of Ravana.” Saying this, the heroic Lakşmaņa in that conflict, drawing the straightspeeding arrow up to his car,' discharged it at Indrajit. 1. The celestial steed, Uchchaiśrvā, sprung from the ocean on the occasion of the churning of the deep. 2. Words addressed to the deity presiding over the weapon. 3. i.e. drawing the bow to its utmost stretch.

sn: ऐन्द्रास्त्रेण समायुज्य लक्ष्मणः परवीरहा।७० !! तच्छिरः सशिरस्त्राणं श्रीमज्ज्वलितकुण्डलम्। प्रमथ्येन्द्रजितः कायात्पातयामास भूतले।७१।।
en: And shooting the Aindra Hearon, that destroyer of hostile heroes-Laksmana-severing from its trunk the head of Indrajit with its corslet, graced with burning ear-rings, brought it down to the ground.

sn: तद्राक्षसतनूजस्य भिन्नस्कन्धं शिरो महत्। तपनीयनिभं भूमौ ददृशे रुधिरोक्षितम्॥
en: The mighty severed head of the Rākşasas son, resembling one made of gold, was seen covered with blood.

sn: हतः सः निपपाताथ धरण्यां रावणात्मजः। कवची सशिरस्त्राणो विप्रविद्धशरासनः॥
en: And slain, Ravana's son dropped to the earth, with his armour and corslet on, and his bow fallen (from his grasp).

sn: चुक्रुशुस्ते ततः सर्वे वानराः सविभीषणाः। हृष्यन्ते निहते तस्मिन्देवा वृत्रवधे यथा॥
en: Then all the monkeys with Vibhīşaņa set up cheers, even as the immortals cheered at the destruction of Vrtra.

sn: अथान्तरिक्षे भूतानामृषीणां च महात्मनाम्। जज्ञेऽथ जयसंनादो गन्धर्वाप्सरसामपि। ७५॥
en: And in the sky there arose the victorious shouts of all beings and high souled saints, and also of Gandharvas and Apsarās.

sn: पतितं समभिज्ञाय राक्षसी सा महाचमूः। वध्यमाना दिशो भेजे हरिभिर्जितकाशिभिः॥
en: And knowing (Indrajit) fallen (in fight), the mighty army of Rākşasas, attacked by monkeys burning for victory, fled in the ten cardinal directions.

sn: वानरैर्वध्यमानास्ते शस्त्राण्युत्सृज्य राक्षसाः। लङ्कामभिमुखाः सस्रुभ्रष्टसंज्ञाः प्रधाविताः॥
en: And assailed by the monkeys, the Raksasas, pursued (by their foes), with their senses lost, rushed towards Lankā, leaving their arms behind.

sn: दुद्रुवुर्बहुधा भीता राक्षसाः शतशो दिशः। त्यक्त्वा प्रहरणान्सर्वे पट्टिशासिपरश्वधान्॥
en: And overwhelmed with fright, Rākṣasas fled in an hundred directions, all renouncing their arms-bearded darts, and swords, and axes.

sn: केचिल्लङ्कां परित्रस्ताः प्रविष्टा वानरार्दिताः। समुद्रे पतिताः केचित्केचित्पर्वतमाश्रिताः॥
en: And harassed by the monkeys, some hurriedly entered, Lankā, and some plunged into the sea, and some saught shelter in the mountains.

sn: हतमिन्द्रजितं दृष्ट्वा शयनां च रणक्षितौ। राक्षसानां सहस्रेषु न कश्चित्प्रत्यदृश्यत॥
en: Seeing Indrajit slain and lying down on the field of battle, thousands of Raksasas fled away.

sn: यथास्तं गत आदित्ये नावतिष्ठन्ति रश्मयः। तथा तस्मिन्निपतिते राक्षसास्ते गता दिशः ८१॥ शान्तरश्मिरिवादित्यो निर्वाण इव पावकः। बभूव स महाबाहुर्व्यपास्तगतजीवितः॥
en: As when the Sun sets, his rays remain no longer, on that Raksasas having fallen, the Raks asas dispersed in the ten cardinal quarters, like to the sun when his rays have been rendered mild, or fire which has been extinguished.

sn: प्रशान्तपीडाबहुलो विनष्टारिः प्रहर्षवान्। बभूव लोकः पतिते राक्षसेन्द्रसुते तदा॥
en: The mighty-armed (Indrajit) was utterly shorn of life. And on the son of the Raksasa-chief falling, the world, having its foe slain, with its huge affliction gone off, experienced the height of joy.

sn: हर्ष च शक्रो भगवान्सह सर्वैर्महर्षिभिः। जगाम निहते तस्मिन्राक्षसे पापकर्मणि॥
en: On that unrighteous Raksasa having been slain, the reverend Sakra together with the Maharsis was filled with delight.

sn: आकाशे चापि देवानां सुश्रुवे दुन्दुभिस्वनः। नृत्यद्भिरप्सरोभिश्च गन्धर्वैश्च महात्मभिः॥ ववर्षः पुष्पवर्षाणि तदद्भुतमिवाभवत्। प्रशशाम हते तस्मिन्राक्षसे क्रूरकर्मणि॥ शुद्धा आपो नभश्चैव जहषुर्देवदानवाः। आजग्मुः पतिते तस्मिन्सर्वलोकभयावहे॥ ऊचुश्च सहितास्तुष्टा देवगन्धर्वदानवाः। विज्वराः शान्तकलुषा ब्राह्मणा विचरन्त्विति।।८८
en: And sounds of kettle-drums were heard in the sky proceeding from the celestials. And blossoms were showered by dancing Apsarās and high-souled Gandharvas. And this was wonderful (to behold.) And on that Raksasa of fell deeds having been slain, the dust was laid, the water became transparent, the sky looked bright, and the deities and Dänavas were filled with rejoicings. And on that dread of all creatures having been slain, the gods, Gandharvas and Dänavas, assembled together in joy, said, "Now let the Brahmanas who have their sins removed, with their anxiety gone off, range about.”

sn: ततोऽभ्यनन्दन्संहृष्टाः समरे हरियूथपाः। तमप्रतिबलं दृष्ट्वा हतं नैर्ऋतपुङ्गवम्॥
en: Then the monkey-leaders, seeing that foremost of Naiſtas of unparalleled prowess slain in battle, began to gladly pay homage (to Lakş mana).

sn: विभीषणो हनूमांश्च जाम्बवांश्चर्क्षयूथपः। विजयेनाभिनन्दन्तस्तुष्टुवुश्चापि लक्ष्मणम्।९०॥
en: And Vibhīşaņa and Hanumān and Jāmabavān, leader of bears-saluted and hymned Lakşmaņa on the score of his victory.

sn: क्ष्वेडन्तश्च प्लवन्तश्च गर्जन्तश्च प्लवंगमाः। लब्धलक्षा रघुसुतं परिवार्योपतस्थिरे॥
en: And shouting and bounding and roaring, the monkeys at this hour of high joy stood surrounding Raghu's son.* *Descendant, that is.

sn: लांगूलानि प्रविध्यन्तः स्फोटयन्तश्च वानराः। लक्ष्मणो जयतीत्येव वाक्यं विश्रावयंस्तदा।१२।
en: And flourishing their tails and striking the earth (with them), the monkeys shouted, 'Victory to Laksmana!'

sn: अन्योन्यं च समाश्लिष्य हरयो हृष्टमानसाः। चनुरुच्चावचगुणा राघवाश्रयसत्कथाः॥
en: And embracing each other, the monkeys with delighted spirits began to converse in various ways touching Raghava's welfare.

sn: तदसुकरमथाभिवीक्ष्य हृष्टाः प्रियसुहृदो युधि लक्ष्मणस्य कर्म। परममुपलभन्मनः प्रहर्ष विनिहतमिन्द्ररिपुं निशम्य देवाः।१४।।
en: Beholding that deed, difficult of being done, performed by their beloved friend, Laks mana, and hearing their foe, Indrajit, slain (in battle), the celestials attained the summit of joy.

sn: रुधिरक्लिनगावस्तु लक्ष्मणः शुभलक्षणः। बभूव हृष्टस्तं हत्वा शत्रुजेतारमाहवे॥
en: Having in the conflict slain that conqueror of enemies, Lakşmaņa graced with auspicious marks, with his body bathed in blood, experienced delight.

sn: ततः स जाम्बवन्तं च हनूमन्तं च वीर्यवान्। संनिपत्य महातेजास्तांश्च सर्वान्वनौकसः॥ आजगाम ततः शीघ्रं यत्र सुग्रीवराघवौ। विभीषणमवष्टभ्य हनूमन्तं च लक्ष्मणः॥
en: Then supporting himself on Vibhīşana and Hanuman, the exceedingly powerful Lakşmaņa endowed with prowess, taking Jambavan, Hanuman and all the monkeys with him, speedily went to the place where Sugrīva and Raghava were.

sn: ततो राममभिक्रम्य सौमित्रिरभिवाद्य च। तस्थौ भ्रातृसमीपस्थः शक्रस्येन्द्रानुजो यथा।४॥
en: Then going round Rāma and saluted him, Sumitra's son stood before his brother, like Indra's brother staying before Sakra.

sn: निष्टनत्रिव चागत्य राघवाय महात्मने। आचचक्षे तदा वीरो घोरमिन्द्रजितो वधम्॥
en: And approaching with a look which of itself was significant,* the heroic Vibhīşaņa described to the high-souled Räghava the dreadful destruction of Indrajit. *i.e. of the destruction of Indrajit.

sn: रावणेस्तु शिरश्छिनं लक्ष्मणेन महात्मना। न्यवेदयत रामाय तदा हृष्टो विभीषणः॥
en: Then the delighted Vibhişaņa related to Rāma how the high-souled Lakşmaņa had cut off the head of Ravana's son.

sn: श्रुत्वैव तु महावीर्यो लक्ष्मणेनेन्द्रजिद्वधम्। प्रहर्षमतुल लेभे वाक्यं चेदमुवाच ह॥
en: As soon as that exceedingly powerful one heard of the destruction of Indrajit by Lakşmana, he experienced a huge accession of joy, and thus delivered himself.

sn: साधु लक्ष्मण तुष्टोऽस्मि कर्म चासुकरं कृतम्। रावणेहि विनाशेन जितमित्युपधारय।।।।
en: Excellent, O Laksmana! Pleased am I (with you). You have performed a difficult feat. The son of Rävana having been slain, know for certain that we have been victorious.

sn: स तं शिरस्युपाघ्राय लक्ष्मणं कीर्तिवर्धनम्। लज्जमानं बलात्स्नेहादङ्कमारोप्य वीर्यवान्॥ उपवेश्य तमुत्सङ्गे परिष्वज्यावपीडितम्। धातर लक्ष्मण स्निग्धं पुनः पुनरुदैक्षत॥
en: Then smelling the head of the bashful Laks miana, enhancer of fame, (Rāma) endowed with prowess, from affection forcibly hugged him into his lap. And making him seat on his lap, and overpowering him with embraces,* (Rama) again and again tenderly eyed his brother, Lakş imana. * Aapiritam-fac) pained. Rāmānaya says this epithet refers to Laksmana's having been wounded in the encounter. I differ from him.

sn: शल्यसंपीडितं शस्तं नि:सन्तं तु लक्ष्मणम्। समस्तु दुःखसंतप्तं तं तु निःश्वासपीडितम्॥ मूर्धि चैनमुपाघ्राय भूयः संस्पृश्य च त्वरन्। उवाच लक्षमणं वाक्यमाश्वास्य पुरुषर्षभः॥
en: And moved with grief, that best of persons, Rama, smelling head of Laksmana, wounded with darts and having his person pierced (with salms, sighing and breathing hard-and nursing ms body with his hand, addressed Laksmana, soothing him.

sn: कृतं परमकल्याणं कर्म दुष्करकर्मणा। अद्य मन्ये हते पुत्रे रावणं निहतं युधि ॥ अद्याहं विजयी शत्रौ हते तस्मिन्दुरात्मनि। रावणस्य नृशंसस्य दिष्ट्या वीर त्वया रणे॥ छिनो हि दक्षिणो बाहुः स हि तस्य व्यपाश्रयः।
en: To-day his son having been slain, I deem Råvaņa himself as slain in fight. On that wickedminded enemy of mine having been destroyed, I am viciorious (in encounter). By luck, o hero, have you in conflict suvered the right arm of the fell Rävana. Verily he (Indrajit) was his stay.

sn: विभीषणहनूमद्भयां कृतं कर्म महद्रणे॥ अहोरात्रस्त्रिभिर्वीरः कथंचिद्विनिपातितः। निमित्रः कृतोऽस्यद्य निर्यास्यति हि रावणः।।१६
en: Both Vibhīşaņa and Hanumān have done mighty deeds in battle. In three days and nights, (my enemy) has been brought down. To-day have I been made foeless. Now Rāvana will for certain march forth, backed by a mighty phalanx.

sn: बलव्यूहेन महता निर्यास्यति हि रावणः। बलव्यूहेन महता श्रुत्वा पुत्रं निपातितम्॥ तं पुत्रवधसंतप्तं निर्यान्तं राक्षसाधिपम्। बलेनावृत्य महता निहनिष्यामि दुर्जयम्॥
en: Rāvana will for certain sally out, hearing his son brought down. That unconquerable lord of Rakşasas, aggrieved for the destruction of his son, marching out, shall I slay, environed with a mighty force.

sn: त्वया लक्ष्मण नाथेन सीता च पृथिवी च मे। न दुष्प्रापा हते तस्मिशक्रजेतरि चाहवे॥
en: O Lakşmaņa, the conqueror of Sakra having in battle been slain by you-who are my lord-Sītā and the entire) earth are not incapable of being obtained by me.

sn: स तं भ्रातरमाश्वास्य परिष्वज्य च राघवः। रामः सुषेणं मुदितः समाभाष्येदमब्रवीत्॥
en: Having thus soothed and embraced his brother, Raghu's son Rama highly rejoiced calling Suşeņa said.

sn: विशल्योऽयं महाप्राज्ञः सौमित्रिमित्रवत्सलः। यथा भवति सुस्वस्थस्तथा त्वं समुदाचर॥
en: Do you so act that this highly wise son of Sumitrā, devoted to his friends, may be healed and be eased.

sn: विशल्यः क्रियतां क्षिप्रं सौमित्रिमित्रवत्सलः। ऋक्षवानरसैन्यानां शूराणां दुमयोधिनाम्॥ ये चाप्यन्येऽत्र युध्यन्ति सशल्या व्रणिनस्तता। तेऽपि सर्वे प्रयत्नेन क्रियतां सुखिनस्तथा॥
en: Do you without delay heal Sumitra's son, attached to his friends, of his wounds. And do you also carefully relieve all those heroes in the army of bears and monkeys fighting with trees, as well as others, who have been wounded and have got sores (in consequence).

sn: एवमुक्तः स रामेण महात्मा हरियूथपः। लक्ष्मणाय ददौ नस्तः सुषेणः परमौषधम्॥
en: Thus addressed by Rāma, the high-souled monkey-leader administered a potent medicine to the nose of Laksmana.

sn: स तस्य गन्धमाघ्राय विशल्यः समपद्यत। तदा निर्वेदनश्चैव संरुद्धप्राण एव च॥
en: And smelling the same, he got healed; he was relieved of his pain and his outgoing vitality was shut up.

sn: विभीषणमुखानां च सुहृदां राघवाज्ञया। सर्ववानरमुख्यानां चिकित्सासमकरोत्तदा ॥
en: At the mandate of Rāghava he likewise treated his friends headed by Vibhișaņa and all the principal monkeys.

sn: ततः प्रकृतिमापनो हृतशल्यो गतक्लमः। सौमित्रिMमुदे तत्र क्षणेन विगतज्वरः॥
en: And restored to his natural condition, Sumitrā's son, healed, and with his exhaustion removed, and his suffering gone off in a moment, experienced exhilaration of spirits.

sn: तदैव रामः प्लवगाधिपस्तथा विभीषणश्चर्क्षपतिश्च वीर्यवान्। अवेक्ष्य सौमित्रिमरोगमुत्थितं मुदा ससैन्याः सुचिरं जहषिरे॥
en: Rāma and the monkey-king and Vibhīşaņa! and the powerful lord of bears along with their hosts, seeing Sumitrā's son risen hale, rejoiced greatly in delight.

sn: अपूजयत्कर्म स लक्ष्मणस्य सुदुष्करं दाशरथिर्महात्मा। बभूव हृष्टो युधि वानरेन्द्रो निशम्य तं शक्रजितं निपातितम्॥
en: The high-souled son of Dasaratha honoured exceedingly that exceedingly hard feat of Laks amana; and the monkey-king, hearing that the conqueror of Sakra had fallen in fight, was filled with joy.

sn: ततः पौलस्त्यसचिवाः श्रुत्वा चेन्द्रजितो वधम्। आचचक्षुरवज्ञाय दशग्रीवाय सत्वराः॥
en: Then the counsellors of Pulastya's son, hearing of Indrajit having been slain, speedily conveyed the tidings to the Ten-necked one, who was ignorant* of the same.

sn: युद्धे हतो महाराज लक्ष्मणेन तवात्मजः। विभीषणसहायेन मिषतां नो महाद्युतिः॥
en: O mighty monarch, in our very sight your exceedingly effulgent son has been slain by Lakş maņa with the help of Vibhīşaņa.

sn: शूरः शूरेण संगम्य संयुगेष्वपराजितः। लक्ष्मणेन हतः शूरः पुत्रस्ते विबुधेन्द्रजित्॥ गतः स परमाल्लोकाशरैः संतर्घ्य लक्ष्मणम्।
en: That hero confronted by the (other) heros, has been vanquished in fight. And the hero, you son, the conqueror of the celestial chief, has also been slain by Lakşmaņa. And having gratified Lakş maņa with his shafts, he has repaired to the supreme regions.

sn: स तं प्रतिभयं श्रुत्वा वधं पुत्रस्य दारुणम्॥ घोरमिन्द्रजितः संख्ये कश्मलं प्राविशन्महत्।
en: Hearing of that mighty terror, viz., the rueful and dreadful destruction of his son, "Indrajit, in battle, he straightway swooned away.

sn: उपलभ्य चिरात्संज्ञां राजा राक्षसपुङ्गवः॥ पुत्रशोकाकुलो दीनो विललापाकुलेन्द्रियः।
en: Then regaining his consciousness after a long while, that foremost of Räkşasas-the kingover-whelmed with grief for his son, and distressed, burst into lamentations, with his senses wildered, thus.

sn: हा राक्षसचमूमुख्य मम वत्स महाबल॥ जित्वेन्द्रं कथमद्य त्वं लक्ष्मणस्य वशं गतः।
en: O foremost in the Räkşasa army! O my child endowed with high might! Having conquered Indra himself, wherefore today have you come under the sway of Lakşmaņa?

sn: ननु त्वमिषुभिः कृद्धो भिन्द्याः कालान्तकावपि॥ मन्दरस्यापि शृङ्गाणि किं पुनर्लक्ष्मणं युधि।
en: Doubtless, you enraged could pierce with you arrows the Destroyer of Time himself, and the summit of Mandāra, what shall I say of Laks mana in encounted?

sn: अद्य वैवस्वतो राजा भूयो बहुमतो मम॥ येनाद्य त्वं महाबाहो संयुक्तः कालधर्मणा।
en: Today king Vivasvata has raised himself immensely in my estimation, for today he, O mighty-armed one, has brought you under the law of Time.

sn: एष पन्थाः सुयोधानां सर्वामरगणेष्वपि।। यः कृते हन्यते भर्तुः स पुमान्स्वर्गमृच्छति॥
en: But this is the way of capable warriors as well as celestials. He that lay down his life for his lord, repair to heaven.

sn: अद्य देवगणाः सर्वे लोकपाला महर्षयः। हतमिन्द्रजितं दृष्ट्वा सुखं स्वप्स्यन्ति निर्भयाः॥
en: To-day seeing Indrajit slain, the deities and the guardians of the worlds, and the mighty saints, their fear gone off, shall sleep peacefully.

sn: अद्य लोकास्त्रयः कृत्स्ना पृथिवी च सकानना। एकेनेन्द्रजिता हीना शून्येव प्रतिभाति मे॥
en: This triple world and this entire earth with her woods, reft of one—Indrajit—appear to me as vacant.

sn: अद्य नैर्ऋतकन्यानां श्रोष्याम्यन्तःपुरे रवम्। करेणुसङ्घस्य यथा निनादं गिरिगह्वरे॥
en: To-day shall I hear the cries of the daughters of the Naiſtas in my inner apartment, like to the roars of she-elephants in a mountain-cavern.

sn: यौवराज्यं च लङ्कां च रक्षांसि च परंतप। मातरं मां च भार्याश्च क्व गतोऽसि विहाय नः॥
en: Renouncing your state of an heir-apparent, and Lanka and Raksasas, O subduer of enemies, and your mother, and me, and your wifewhither have you gone, (leaving) us all?

sn: मम नाम त्वया वीर गतस्य यमसादनम्। प्रेतकार्याणि कार्याणि विपरीते हि वर्तसे॥
en: O hero, I having gone to the region of Yama, you ought to have performed my last rites, but you stand in a relation the very reverse of this.* *i.e. I have to perform your last rites, you having fallen in fight while I am alive.

sn: स त्वं जीवति सुग्रीवे लक्ष्मणे न च राघवे। मम शल्यमनुढत्य क्व गतोऽसि विहाय नः॥
en: And Sugriva living and Lakşmana and Raghava, without extracting my dart, whither have you gone, leaving us all?

sn: एवमादिविलापात रावणं राक्षसाधिपम्। आविवेश महान्कोपः पुत्रव्यसनसंभवः॥ प्रकृत्या कोपनं ह्येनं पुत्रस्य पुनराधयः। दीप्तं संदीपयामासुर्धर्मेऽर्कमिव रश्मयः॥
en: Then arising from the disaster that had befallen his son, a mighty wrath overcame the lord of Räkşasas-Rāvaņa, as he was thus indulging in lamentations. And even as in summer, the (Solar) rays flame up the Sun, the destruction of his son flamed up all the fiercer, him, who was naturally irascible.

sn: कोपाद्विजृम्भमाणस्य वक्राव्यक्तमिव ज्वलन्। उत्पपात सधूमाग्निवृत्रस्य वदनादिव॥
en: As he kept yawning in passion, a flaming fire with smoke darted from his mouth, even as it did from the mouth of Vſtra.

sn: स पुत्रवधसंतप्तः शूरः क्रोधवशं गतः। समीक्ष्य रावणो बुद्ध्या वैदेहा रोचयद्वधम्॥
en: And burning in grief for the destruction of his son, and coming under masterdom of passion, that hero-Ravana-reflecting (awhile) in his mind, resolved upon slaying Vaidehi.

sn: तस्य प्रकृत्या रक्ते च रक्ते क्रोधाग्निनापि च। रावणस्य महाघोरे दीप्ते नेत्रे बभूवतुः।२०।।
en: And naturally red, and reddened (still more by the fire of wrath, Ravana's glowing eyes were dreadful (to behold).

sn: घोरं प्रकृत्या रूपं तत्तस्य क्रोधाग्निमूर्च्छितम्। बभूव रूपं क्रुद्धस्य रुद्रस्येव व्यवस्थितम्॥
en: And his form, terrific by nature, in consequence of the fire of his wrath having possessed it entirely, resembled the form of the enraged Rudra.

sn: तस्य कृद्धस्य नेत्राभ्यां प्रापतनशुबिन्दवः। दीपाभ्यामिव दीप्ताभ्यां साचिषः स्नेहबिन्दवः॥
en: And from the eyes of that infuriated one fell drops of tears as drop from a flaming lamp drops of burning oil.

sn: दन्तान्विदशतस्तस्य श्रूयते दशनस्वनः। यन्त्रस्याकृष्यमाणस्य मध्नतो दानवैरिव ॥
en: As the grinded his teeth, the gnashing resembled the sounds sent by the machine* drawn by the Dänavas and churing the deep. *Meaning the mountain Mandara.

sn: कालाग्निरिव संक्रुद्धो यां यां दिशमवैक्षत। तस्यां तस्यां भयत्रस्ता राक्षसाः संविलिल्यिरे।। तमन्तकमिव क्रुद्धं चराचरचिखादिषुम्। वीक्षमाणं दिशः सर्वा राक्षसा नोपचक्रमुः॥
en: The Rakşasas durst not approach that one eyeing round and resembling the Destroyer himself, intent on devouring both mobile and immobile.

sn: ततः परमसंक्रुद्धो रावणो राक्षसाधिपः। अब्रवीद्रक्षसां मध्ये संस्तम्भयिषुराहवे॥
en: Then exceedingly enraged, Ravana-lord of Rākşasas-spoke in the midst of the Räkşasas, inciting them to battle.

sn: मया वर्षसहस्राणि चरित्वा परमं तपः। तेषु तेष्ववकाशेषु स्वयंभूः परितोषितः॥
en: I practised severe austerities for thousands of years; and gratified the Self-sprung at times.

sn: तस्यैव तपसा व्युष्ट्या प्रसादाच्च स्वयंभुवः। नासुरेभ्यो न देवेभ्यो भयं मम कदाचन॥।
en: Neither from Asuras nor from celestials can any fear spring to me.

sn: कवचं ब्रह्मदत्तं मे यदादित्यसमप्रभम्। देवासुरविमर्देषु न छिन्नं वज्रमुष्टिभिः॥
en: My mail conferred on me by Brahma, which in effulgence resembles the Sun himself, was not broken by blows like to thunder-bolt at the war between the deities and demons.

sn: तेन मामद्य संयुक्तं रथस्थमिह संयुगे। प्रतीयात्कोऽद्य मामाजौ साक्षादपि पुरन्दरः॥
en: Today who will come forward against me in battle accoutred in that and mounted on a car in the conflict? Not even Purandara himself.

sn: यत्तदाभिप्रसन्नेन सशरं कार्मुकं महत्। देवासुरविमर्देषु मम दत्तं स्वयंभुवा॥ अद्य तूर्यशतैर्भीमं धनुरुत्थाप्यतां मम। रामलक्ष्मणयोरेव वधाय परमाहवे॥
en: Do you, beating hundreds of drums, today raise that mighty and dreadful bow of mine which, with arrows, had been bestowed on one by the gratified Self-sprung at the war of the gods and Asuras, so that I may therewith compass the destruction of Rama and Lakşmaņa in mighty battle.

sn: स पुत्रवधसंतप्तः क्रूरः क्रोधवशं गतः। समीक्ष्य रावणो बुद्ध्या सीतां हन्तुं व्यवस्यत॥
en: Burning (in grief) for the destruction of his son, the fell Råvana. coming under the influence of anger, reflection (in his mind), resolved to slay Sīta.

sn: प्रत्यवेक्ष्य तु ताम्राक्षः सुघोरो घोरदर्शनः। दीनो दीनस्वरान्सांस्तानुवाच निशाचरान्॥
en: And eyeing round, that copper-eyed and dreadful one of a terrific aspect, distressed, in a piteous voice addressed all the night-rangers, saying.

sn: मायया मम वत्सेन वञ्चनार्थ वनौकसाम्। किंचिदेव हतं तत्र सीतेयमिति दर्शितम्॥
en: By his power of illusion, my beloved child, for deceiving the wood-rangers, slaying something (else), had shown it to them as Sītā.

sn: तदिदं तथ्यमेवाहं करिष्ये प्रियमात्मनः। वैदेहीं नाशयिष्यामि क्षत्रबन्धुमनुव्रताम्।। इत्येवमुक्त्वा सचिवान्खङ्गमाशु परामृशत्॥
en: Now will I do that good office myself, Vaidehi will I slay-even her that is devoted to that friend of Ksatriyas.

sn: उत्प्लुत्य गुणसंपन्नं विमलाम्बरवर्चसम्। निष्पपात स वेगेन सभार्यः सचिवैर्वृतः॥ रावणः पुत्रशोकेन भृशमाकुलचेतनः। संक्रुद्धः खङ्गमादाय सहसा यत्र मैथिली॥
en: Having spoken thus to his counsellors he swiftly took up a sword; and raising it, of excellent temper and of cerulean hue, he rushed out vehemently, surrounded by his wives and counsellors. From grief for his son. Råvana with his consciousness wilderd, taking up a sword; in rage, rushed towards the place where Mithila's daughter was.

sn: व्रजन्तं राक्षसं प्रेक्ष्य सिंहनादं विचुक्रुशुः। ऊचुश्चान्योन्यमालिङ्गय संक्रुद्धं प्रेक्ष्य राक्षसम्॥
en: Seeing the Räksasa rising on, some, emitted leonine roars, and seeing the Räkşasa enraged, embracing each other, said-"To-day those two brothers, seeing this one, will be exceedingly pained.

sn: अद्यैनं तावुभौ दृष्ट्वा भ्रातरौ प्रव्यथिष्यतः। लोकपाला हि चत्वारः क्रुद्धेनानेन निर्जिताः।। बहवः शत्रवश्चान्ये संयुगेष्वभिपातिताः॥
en: By this one influenced with passion were the four guardians of the worlds conquered; and many other foes were brought down in battle.

sn: त्रिषु लोकेषु रत्नानि भुङ्क्ते आहृत्य रावणः। विक्रमे च बले चैव नास्त्यस्य सदृशो भुवि॥
en: Procuring gems from the three worlds, Răvana enjoy them. Neither in strength nor in prowess is there and one on earth who is his compeer.

sn: तेषां संजल्पमानानामशोकवनिकां गताम्। अभिदुद्राव वैदेहीं रावणः क्रोधमूर्च्छितः॥
en: As they were speaking thus, Ravana, reft of his senses by wrath, rushed against Vaidehi, who had taken up her abode in the Asoka wood.

sn: वार्यमाणः सुसंस्क्रुद्धः सुहृद्भिर्हितबुद्धिभिः। अभ्यधावत संक्रुद्धः खे ग्रहो रोहिणीमिव।॥
en: And dissuaded by his friends endowed with good intelligence, he wrought up with high wrath, darted (against Sītā), even as an enraged planet' rush against Rohinr in the firmament. 1. Kuja etc. 2. Hesperus.

sn: मैथिली रक्ष्यमाणा तु राक्षसीभिरनिन्दिता। ददर्श राक्षसं क्रुद्धं निस्त्रिंशवरधारिणम् ॥ तं निशम्य सनिस्त्रिंश व्यथिता जनकात्मजा। निवार्यमाणं बहुशः सुहृद्भिरनिवर्तिनम्॥ सीता दुःखसमाविष्टा विलपन्तीदमब्रवीत्। यथायं मामभिक्रुद्धः समभिद्रवति स्वयम्।। वधिष्यति सनाथां मामनाथामिव दुर्मतिः॥
en: The blameless daughter of Mithilă protected by the Rākşasis, saw the infuriated Rāvana bearing that best of blades in his hand. Seeing (Ravana) approach, sword in hand, despite the earnest entreaties of his friends, Janaka's daughter, SIta, pained and overcome by grief, said, weeping-From the way in which, wrought up with wrath, this wicked-minded one is rushing on at me personally it appears that he will slay me, who have a lord, as one who has not.

sn: बहुशश्चोदयामास भर्तारं मामनुव्रताम्। भार्या मम भवस्वेति प्रत्याख्यातो ध्रुवं मया॥
en: He did urge me much ever devoted to my lord saying Be you my wife; but forsooth I disregarded him.

sn: सोऽयं मामनुपस्थाने व्यक्तं नैराश्यमागतः। क्रोधमोहसमाविष्टो व्यक्तं मां हन्तुमुद्यतः॥
en: And plainly in consequence of my refusal, he has given way to despair. And overcome by anger and passion, he is ready to slay me.

sn: अथवा तौ नरव्याघ्रौ भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ। मन्निमित्तमनार्येण समरेऽद्य निपातितौ॥
en: Or it may be that today for me those foremost of men, the brothers-Rama and Laksmana-have been slain in encounter by this inglorious one.

sn: भैरवो हि महानादो राक्षसानां श्रुतो भया। बहूनामिह हृष्टानां तथा विक्रोशतमां प्रियम्॥
en: I heard a furious and fearful uproar raised by countless Rākşasas rejoicing and expressing their delight.

sn: अहो धिङ्मन्निमित्तोऽयं विनाशो राजपुत्रयोः। अथवा पुत्रशोकेन अहत्वा रामलक्ष्मणौ॥ विधमिष्यति मां रौद्रो राक्षसः पापनिश्चयः।
en: Alas! O fie! For me those princes have met with destruction. Or it may be that not without slaying Rāma and Laksmana, this terrific Rākşasa having his heart set on sin, from grief for his son will slay me.

sn: हनूमतस्तु तद्वाक्यं न कृतं क्षुद्रया मया॥ यद्यहं तस्य पृष्ठेन तदायासमनिर्जिता। नाद्यैवमुशोचेयं भर्तुरङ्कगता सती॥
en: Fool that I am I did not then act agreeably to Hanumān's words. If I had gone away seated on his back, without waiting for the victory (of my lord). I devoted to him placed on his lap, should not have come by this repentance.

sn: मन्ये तु हृदयं तस्याः कौसल्यायाः फलिष्यति। एकपुत्रा यदा पुत्रं विनष्टं श्रोष्यते युधि ॥
en: When Kausalya, having an only son, will hear of her son slain in battle, I fancy, her heart shall burst.

sn: सा हि जन्म च बाल्यं च यौवनं च महात्मनः। धर्मकार्याणि रूपं च रुदती संस्मरिष्यति॥
en: And weeping she will remember that highsouled one's birth and weeping, she will remember that high-souled one's birth and boyhood, and youth and pious acts and loveliness.

sn: निराशा निहते पुत्रे दत्त्वा श्राद्धमचेतना। अग्निमावेक्ष्यते नूनमपो वापि प्रवेक्ष्यति॥
en: That one bereft of her consciousness, filled with despair, after having performed his srāddha,* will doubtless enter into fire or water. *Funereal rites performed in accordance with the injunctions of the Hindu Scriptures.

sn: धिगस्तु कुब्जामसती मन्थरां पापनिश्चयाम्। यनिमित्तमिमं शोकं कौसल्या प्रतिपत्स्यते॥
en: Shame on the unchaste and hump-backed Manthara, having her heart fixed in sin, for whose sake this grief shat Rāvana's exercise Kausalya!

sn: इत्येवं मैथिली दृष्ट्वा विलपन्तीं तपस्विनीम्। रोहिणीमिव चन्द्रेण विना ग्रहवशं गताम्॥ एतस्मिन्नन्तरे तस्य अमात्यः शीलवञ्छुचिः। सुपार्थो नाम मेधावी रावणं रक्षसां वरम्।। निवार्यमाणः सचिवैरिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Seeing the distressed daughter of Mithila lament thus, like to Rohiņi come under the sway of a planet in the absence of the Moon, in the meanwhile his (Rāvana's) pure and good courtier, named Suparsva, endowed with intelligence, albeit prevented by other courtiers, spoke to Rāvana, foremost of Räkșasa.

sn: कथं नाम दशग्रीव साक्षाद्वैश्रवणानुज। हन्तुमिच्छसि वैदेही क्रोधाद्धर्ममपास्य च॥
en: Wherefore, O Ten-necked one, O you who are the very younger brother of Vaiśravaņa himself, Did you desire to slay Vaidehī, forsaking righteousness?

sn: वेदविद्याव्रतस्नातः स्वकर्मनिरतस्तथा। स्त्रियः कस्माद्वधं वीर मन्यसे राक्षसेश्वर॥
en: Why O hero! O lord of Rākşasas! having led the Brahmacarya mode of life, studied the Vedas, and returned from the house of your spiritual guide, and ever engaged in religious acts, today did you intend to slay a woman?

sn: मैथिली रूपसंपन्नां प्रत्यवेक्षस्व पार्थिव । तस्मिन्नेव सहास्माभिराहवे क्रोधमुत्सृज॥
en: Do you, O king, now stay expecting Mithila's daughter' endowed with loveliness; and do you along with us vent your wrath on him." 1. Explains the commentator: till you slay Rāma in battle. 2. Rama.

sn: अभ्युत्थानं त्वमद्यैव कृष्णपक्षचतुर्दशी। कृत्वा निर्याह्यमावास्यां विजयाय बलैर्वृतः॥
en: To-day being the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, do you this very day prepare for conflict; at amăvāsyā,* environed with your forces do you march for victory. *i.e. tomorrow.

sn: शूरो धीमारथी खङ्गी रथप्रवरमास्थितः। हत्वा दाशरथिं भीमं भवान्प्राप्स्यति मैथिलीम्॥
en: Heroic, and intelligent, a mighty car-warrior and swordsman, you, mounted on a car, slay the redoubtable son of Dasaratha, will obtain Mithilā's daughter.

sn: स तदुरात्मा सुहृदा निवेदितं वचः सुधयं प्रतिगृह्य रावणः। गृहं जगामाथ ततश्च वीर्यवान् पुनः सभां च प्रययौ सुहृद्वृतः॥
en: Thus exhorted by his friend, the untighteous Rāvana accepted his virtuous speech; and then that powerful one went (back) to his house, and, surrounded by his friends, entered the court.

sn: स प्रविश्य सभां राजा दीनः परमदुःखितः। निषसादासने मुख्ये सिंहः क्रुद्ध इव श्वसन्॥
en: Entering his court, the king, distressed, and exceeding aggrieved sat him down on the foremost seat sighing like an enraged lion.

sn: अब्रवीच्च स तान्सर्वान्बलमुख्यान्महाबलः। रावणः प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यं पुत्रव्यसनकर्शितः॥
en: And stricken with grief in consequence of his son's death, that highly powerful Ravana, with folded hands, addressed all the heroic Rākşasas saying.

sn: सर्वे भवन्तः सर्वेण हस्त्यश्वेन समावृताः। निर्यात रथसङ्घश्च हस्त्यश्वैश्चोपशोभिताः॥ एकं रामं परिक्षिप्य समरे हन्तुमर्हथ। प्रहृष्टाः शरवर्षाणि प्रावृट्काल इवाम्बुदाः॥
en: Do you all proceed to battle with elephants, horses and cars. And encircling Rāma only and discharging shafts at him, delightedly, like to clouds, in the rainy season, poring water, do you slay him.

sn: अथवाहं शरैस्तीक्ष्णैभिन्नगात्रं महाहवे। भवद्भिः श्वो निरन्तास्मि रामं लोकस्य पश्यतः॥
en: Or I shall slay him to morrow in the presence of all, wounded by you in the mighty encounter with sharpened arrows.

sn: इत्येतद्वाक्यमादाय राक्षसेन्द्रस्य राक्षसाः। निर्ययुस्ते रथैः शीघे नानीकैश्च संयुताः॥
en: Hearing the speech of their lord the Rākṣasas, with a huge army and a host of cars, speedily issued out for battle.

sn: परिघान्पट्टिशांश्चैव शरखङ्गपरश्वधान्। शरीरान्तकरान्सर्वे चिक्षिपुर्वानरान्प्रति।। वानराश्च द्रुमाञ्छैलानराक्षसान्प्रति चिक्षिपुः॥
en: They all threw at the monkeys life-destroying Parighas, pattisas, arrows, daggers and Parasvadhas. And the monkeys too threw crags and trees at the Rākşasas.

sn: स संग्रामो महाभीमः सूर्यस्योदयनं प्रति। रक्षसां वानराणां च तुमुलः समपद्यत।।।।
en: Thus on the eve of sun set there arose a terrible conflict between the Rakşasas and the monkeys.

sn: ते गदाभिश्च चित्राभिः प्रासैः खङ्गैः परश्वधैः। अन्योन्यं समरे जघ्नुस्तदा वानरराक्षसाः।९।।
en: They struck each other in the conflict with clubs chitras, Prasas daggers and Parasvadha.

sn: एवं प्रवृत्चे संग्रामे ह्यद्भुतं सुमहद्रजः। रक्षसां वानराणां च शान्तं शोणितविस्रवैः॥
en: The conflict being thus carried on, there arose a mighty dust which was again destroyed by the current of blood gushing out of the persons of the Rakşasas and the monkeys:

sn: मातंगरथकूलाश्च शरमत्स्या ध्वजदुमाः। शरीरसंघाटवहाः प्रसस्नुः शोणितापगाः॥
en: Elephants and cars were like the banks of that river of blood, the arrows were like the fishes, and the flags were the trees on their banks and the corpses were like planks afloat there.

sn: ततस्ते वानराः सर्वे शोणितौघपरिप्लुताः। ध्वजवर्मरथानश्वान्नानाप्रहरणानि च।। आप्लुत्याप्लुत्य समरे वानरेन्द्रा बभञ्जिरे॥
en: Being thus wounded and assailed by the Rākşasas, those heroic monkeys leaped and broke down the flags, armours, cars, horses and other weapons.

sn: केशान्कर्णललाटं च नासिकाश्च प्लवंगमाः। रक्षसां दशनैस्तीक्ष्णैर्नखैश्चापि व्यकर्तयन्॥
en: With their sharp teeth and nails they scratched the hair, ears, foreheads and the noses of the Raksasas.

sn: एकैकं राक्षसं संख्ये शतं वानरपुङ्गवाः। अभ्यधावन्त पतितं वृक्षं शकुनयो यथा॥
en: Like to vultures falling upon a felled tree, hundreds of monkeys fell upon one Räkşasas in that encounter.

sn: तदा गदाभिर्गुर्वीभिः प्रासैः खङ्गैः परश्वधैः। निर्जघ्नुर्वानरान्घोराराक्षसाः पर्वतोपमाः॥
en: The Rákşasas resembling mountains, with huge clubs, prasas, daggers and Parasvādhas, struck the monkeys (in their turn).

sn: राक्षसैर्वध्यमानानां वानराणां महाचमूः। शरण्यं शरणं याता रामं दशरथात्मजम्॥
en: Being thus assailed by the Räkşasas, the mighty host of monkeys took refuge of Răma, the son of Dasaratha, the worthy refuge of all creatures.

sn: ततो रामो महातेजा धनुरादाय वीर्यवान्। प्रविश्य राक्षसं सैन्यं शरवर्ष ववर्ष च॥
en: Thereupon the highly effulgent and powerful Rāma, taking up his bow, entered the Rākşasa host and began to make a downpour of arrows.

sn: प्रविष्टं तु तदा रामं मेघाः सूर्यमिवाम्बरे। नाधिजग्मुर्महाघोरा निर्दहन्तं शराग्निना॥
en: Rama entering the field, those terrible Rakş asas, being burnt with the fire of his arrows, could not stand before him like to clouds disappearing before the Sun in the welkin.

sn: कृतान्येव सुघोराणि रामेण रजनीचराः। रणे रामस्य ददृशुः कर्माण्यसुकाराणि ते॥
en: The night-rangers only espied the dreadful feats performed by Råma and which were above the power of others.

sn: चालयन्तं महासैन्यं विधमन्तं महारथान्। ददृशुस्तेन वै रामं वातं वनगतं यथा॥
en: Except when guiding the huge army or driving the cars they could not see Rama like to the wind invisible in a forest.

sn: छिन्नं भिन्नं शरैर्दग्धं प्रभग्नं शस्त्रपीडितम्। बलं रामेण ददृशुर्न रामं शीघ्रकारिणम्॥
en: The all beheld the Råkşasas force scattered, wounded, burnt down with arrows, broken and assailed with weapons by Rāma But none could see the quick moving Rāma.

sn: प्रहरन्तं शरीरेषु न ते पश्यन्ति राघवम्। इन्द्रियार्थेषु तिष्ठन्तं भूतात्मानामिव प्रजाः॥
en: As people cannot see the soul which governs all objects of sense so they could not see Rāma, who was thus inflicting wounds on them.

sn: एष हन्ति गजानीकमेष हन्ति महारथान्। एष हन्ति शरैस्तीक्ष्णैः पदातीन्वाजिभिः सह॥ इति ते राक्षसाः सर्वे रामस्य सदृशारणे। अन्योन्यं कुपिता जघ्नुः सादृश्याद्राघवस्य तु॥
en: It is he who is destroying the soldiers riding the elephants, it he who is breaking down the mighty cars, and it is he who with sharp arrows is slaying the cavalry-rider and horse. "Thus saying those Räkşasas, in that conflict and in the very presence of Rāma, highly enraged began to slay each other.

sn: न ते ददृशिरे रामं दहन्तमपि वाहिनीम्। मोहिताः परमात्रेण गान्धर्वेण महात्मना॥
en: They were all bewildered by the huge Gandharva weapon discharged by the high souled Rama and so they could not see Rama, whose was thus burning down their force.

sn: ते तु रामसहस्राणि रणे पश्यन्ति राक्षसाः। पुनः पश्यन्ति काकुत्स्थमेकमेव महाहवे॥
en: The Rákşasas sometimes beheld thousands of Rāma in the battle field and again saw one Rāma only.

sn: भ्रमन्ता काञ्चनी कोटिं कार्मुकस्य महात्मनः। अलातचक्रप्रतिमां ददृशुस्ते न राघवम्॥
en: They at times saw the quick-moving golden end of the bow of that high-souled one, resembling a circular fire brand but they did not behold Rāghava.

sn: शरीरनाभिसत्वार्चिः शरीरं नेमिकार्मुकम्। ज्याघोषतलनिर्घोषं तेजोबुद्धिगुणप्रभम्॥ दिव्यास्त्रगुणपर्यन्तं निघ्नन्तं युधि राक्षसान्। ददृशू रामचक्रं तत्कालचक्रमिव प्रजाः॥
en: He looked like kālacakra, having his middle body as its navel, his own strength as its lustre, the arrow for its radius or spoke, the bow for the circumference, the twang of the bow for its sound, his power and intelligence for its brightness, and the aim of the celestial Weapons for its limit.

sn: अनीकं दशसाहस्रं रथानां वातरंहसाम्। अष्टादश सहस्राणि कुञ्जराणां तरस्विनाम्।।३० चतुर्दश सहस्राणि सारोहाणां च वाजिनाम्। पूर्णे शतसहस्रे द्वे राक्षसानां पदातिनाम्॥ दिवसस्याष्टभागेन शरैरग्निशिखोपमैः। हतान्येकेन रामेण रक्षसां कामरूपिणाम्॥
en: In the eighth division of the time by Rāma alone with arrows resembling the flame of fire were destroyed ten thousands swift-coursing cars, eighteen thousand elephants fourteen thousand horses and riders and tow million Rākṣasas infantry assuming shapes at will.

sn: ते हताश्वा हतरथाः शान्ता विमथितध्वजाः। अभिपेतुः पुरीं लङ्कां हतशेषा निशाचराः॥
en: And those night rangers, who were still left, having their horses killed, cars and flags broken fled in fear of life to the city of Lanka.

sn: हतैर्गजपदात्यश्वैस्तद्वभूव रणाजिरम्। आक्रीडभूमिः क्रुद्धस्य रुद्रस्येव महात्मनः॥
en: The battle field, filled with slain horses, elephants and infantry, looked like the high-souled and enraged Rudra's arena of sports.

sn: ततो देवाः सगन्धर्वाः सिद्धाश्च परमर्षयः। साधुसाध्विति रामस्य तत्कर्म समपूजयन्॥
en: Thereupon the celestials with Gandarbas, Siddhas and the great ascetics glorified the wonderful feat of Rāma.

sn: अब्रवीच्च तदा राम सुग्रीवं प्रत्यनन्तरम्। विभीषणं च धर्मात्मा हनूमन्तं च वानरम्॥ जाम्बवन्तं हरिश्रेष्ठं मैन्दं द्विविदमेव च। एतदत्रबलं भीमं मम वा त्र्यम्बकस्य वा॥
en: The virtuous-souled Rāma addressed Sugrīva, Vibhīşaņa the monkey Hanumān, the leading monkeys Jämbavān, Mainda and Divada who were near him, saying, This is the power of my weapons and as well as that of Rudra.

sn: निहत्य तां राक्षसराजवाहिनी रामस्तदा शक्रसमो महात्मा।। अस्त्रेषु शस्त्रेषु जितक्लमश्च संस्तूयते देवगणैः प्रहृष्टैः॥
en: The high-souled Rāma, equalling Śakra in prowess, thus slaying the huge host of the lord of Rākşasas and assailing them with shafts and weapons-the celestials, delighted, saying his praises.

sn: तानि नागसहस्राणि सारोहाणि च वाजिनाम्। रथानां त्वग्निवर्णानां सध्वजानां सहस्रशः॥ राक्षसानां सहस्राणि गदापरिघयोधिनाम्। काञ्चनध्वजचित्राणां शूराणां कामरूपिणाम्॥ निहतानि शरैर्दीपैस्तप्तकाञ्चनभूषणैः। रावणेन प्रयुक्तानि रामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा॥ दृष्ट्वा श्रुत्वा च संभ्रान्ता हतशेषा निशाचराः। राक्षस्यश्च समागम्य दीनाश्चिन्तापरिप्लुताः॥
en: By Rāma of unwearied actions, with flaming arrows feathered in burning gold, were destroyed thousands of elephants-many horses with their riders, many a car crested with flaming banners; thousands of heroic Rákşasas assuming shapes at will engaged by Råvana, and armed with clubs and parighas; and golden pennons. Beholding and hearing of this the remaining night-rangers assembled and were greatly bewildered, poorly and stricken with anxiety.

sn: विधवा हतपुत्राश्च क्रोशन्त्यो हतबान्धवाः। राक्षस्यः सह संगम्य दुःखार्ताः पर्यदेवयन्॥
en: The widows and those who had lost their children or kinsmen approached those Rākşasas and overwhelmed with grief bewailed piteously.

sn: कथं शूर्पणखा वृद्धा कराला निर्णतोदरी। आससाद वने रामं कंदर्पसमरूपिणम्॥
en: Alas! why did the aged and grim-visaged Śūrpanakhă, having her belly extending down ward, behold in the forest Rāma graceful like Kandarpa.

sn: सुकुमारं महासत्त्वं सर्वभूतहिते रतम्। तं दृष्ट्वा लोकवध्या स हीनरूपा प्रकामिता॥
en: Beholding him of great beauty and prowess, ever engaged in the welfare of all creatures, that ugly one, worthy of being slain by people, was excited with lust.

sn: कथं सर्वगुणैींना गुणवन्तं महोजसम्। सुमुखं दुर्मुखी रामं कामयामास राक्षसी॥
en: Why did that ugly-faced she-demon, devoid of all qualities, address Räma, having a beautiful countenance, gifted with many virtues and great effulgence?

sn: जनस्यास्याल्पभाग्यत्वाद्वलिनी श्वेतमूर्धजा। अकार्यमपहास्यं च सर्वलोकविगर्हितम्॥ राक्षसानां विनाशाय दूषणस्य खरस्य च। चकाराप्रतिरूपा सा राघवस्य प्रधर्षणम्॥
en: Alas for the misfortune of the Rākşasas, the aged Rākşasaee brought before him such a vile proposal, hated of all and worthy of creating laughter. for the destruction of Khara, Düşaņa and other Räksasas that ugly one approached Rāghava with such a vile intention.

sn: तन्निमित्तमिदं वैरं रावणेन कृतं महत्। वधाय सीता सा नीता दशग्रीवेण रक्षसा॥
en: It was for her that Rāvana created enmity (with Răma) and Sītä was carried away by the Ten-necked Rākşasa.

sn: न च सीतां दशग्रीवः प्राप्नोति जनकात्मजाम्। बद्धं बलवता वैरमक्षयं राघवेण च ॥
en: But he could not spread his influence upon Sitā the daughter of king Jannak and deep rooted and eternal became the enmity with the highly powerful Rāghava.

sn: वैदेही प्रार्थयानं तं विराधं प्रेक्ष्य राक्षसम्। हतमेकेन रामेण पर्याप्तं तन्निदर्शनम्॥
en: Beholding the Rākşasa Virādha slain by Rāma alone (Rāvana) wishing Vaidehỉ should have regarded that as a sufficient proof of his prowess.

sn: चतुर्दश सहस्राणि रक्षसां भीमकर्मणाम्। निहतानि जनस्थाने शरैरग्निशिखोपमैः॥ खरश्च निहतः संख्ये दूषणः स्त्रिशिरास्तथा। शरैरादित्यसंकाशैः पर्याप्तं तन्निदर्शनम् ॥
en: And fourteen thousand Rākşasas of terrible deeds were slain by him in janasthāna with shafts resembling the flame of fire. Khara Düş aņa as well as Tricira were slain by him in conflict with arrows resembling the Sun-this was a sufficient proof (of his power).

sn: हतो योजनबाहुश्च कबन्धो रुधिराशनः। क्रोधान्नादं नदन्सोऽथ पर्याप्तं तन्निदर्शनम्॥
en: Yojanabāhu and Kabandha, drinking blood, were slain by him, roaring with wrath-this too was a sufficient proof of his power.

sn: जघान बलिनं रामः सहस्रनयनात्मजम्। वालिनं मेघसंकाशं पर्याप्तं तन्निदर्शनम्॥
en: Rāma slew the powerful Vāli, the son of the thousand eyed one, resembling the cloud-that too was the sufficient proof of his prowess.

sn: ऋष्यमूके वसंश्चैव दीनो भग्नमनोरथः। सुग्रीवः प्रापितो राज्यं पर्याप्तं तन्निदर्शनम् ॥
en: By him Sugriva, poorly and living in the mount Rșyamūka, having all his desires frustrated, was placed on the throne-that too even was the sufficient proof of his power.

sn: धर्मार्थसहितं वाक्यं सर्वेषां रक्षसां हितम्। युक्तं विभीषणेनोक्तं मोहात्तस्य न रोचते॥ विभीषणवचः कुर्याद्यदि स्म धनदानुजः। श्मशानभूता दुःखार्ता नेयं लङ्का भविष्यति॥
en: He (Rāvana) from foolishness did not like the becoming speech of Vibhīşaņa conducive to the acquirement of piety and wealth and securing the welfare of the Rakşasas. Had the younger brother of the lord of wealth (Rāvana) observed the words of Vibhīşaņa, Lanka would not have been overwhelmed with grief and reduced to the state of a cremation ground.

sn: कुम्भकर्णं हतं श्रुत्वा राघवेण महाबलम्। अतिकायं च दुर्मर्ष लक्ष्मणेन हतं तदा।। प्रियं चेन्द्रजितं पुत्रं रावणो नावबुद्ध्यते॥
en: Hearing of the destruction of the highly powerful Kumbhakarņa by Rāma of the irrepressible Atikay by Lakşmaņa as well as of his beloved son Indrajit, Rāvana did not come to his senses.* *One śloka has been omitted here by some of the editors which when translated stands thus; When one monkey only Hanumān killed the prince Akşaya and reduced the whole city to ashes with the fire of his tail Rāvana should have come to his senses.

sn: मम पुत्रो मम भ्राता मम भर्ता रणे हतः। इत्येष श्रूयते शब्दो राक्षसीनां कुले कुले॥
en: There is audible in every house of the Rāks sas, the cry-My son, my brother, my husband is slain in battle.

sn: रथाश्वनागाश्च हतास्तत्र तत्र सहस्रशः। रणे रामेण शूरेण हताश्चापि पदातयः॥
en: In conflict have been destroyed by the heroic Rāma, thousand cars, horses, serpents and infantry.

sn: रुद्रो वा यदि वा विष्णुर्महेन्द्रो वा शतक्रतुः। हन्ति नो रामरूपेण यदि वा स्वयमन्तकः॥
en: Perhaps Rudra, Visnu, Mehendra or the performer of hundred sacrifices, or even Death, in the shape of Rāma, is slaying us.

sn: हतप्रवीरा रामेण निराशा जीविते वयम्। अपश्यन्त्यो भयस्यान्तमनाथा विलपामहे ॥
en: By Rāma all the heroes have been slaindespair has taken possession of our minds-we do not behold the end of our terror and are bewailing being deprived of our lords.

sn: रामहस्ताद्दशग्रीवः शूरो दत्तमहावरः। इदं भयं महाघोरं समुत्पन्नं न बुद्ध्यते।२६।।
en: Does not the Ten-necked hero, who has obtained boons (from Brahmă) perceive that a mighty disaster shall befall him from Råma?

sn: तं न देवा न गन्धर्वा न पिशाचा न राक्षसाः। उपसृष्टं परित्रातुं शक्ता रामेण संयुगे॥
en: Neither the celestials Gandharvas, Piśācas nor Rāksasas shall be able to save him from Rāma in conflict.

sn: उत्पाताश्चापि दृश्यन्ते रावणस्य रणे रणे। कथयन्ति हि रामेण रावणस्य निबर्हणम्॥
en: In very battle many an accident befalls Rāvaņa, this bespeaks of his destruction at the hands of Rāma.

sn: पितामहेन प्रीतेन देवदानवराक्षसैः। रावणस्याभयं दत्तं मनुष्येभ्यो न याचितम्॥
en: The great Patriarch, being pleased conferred upon Rāvaņa the boon that no fear would proceed to him from the celestials, the Dānavas or the Rākşasas-but he did not beg of him, security from men.

sn: तदिदं मानुषं मन्ये प्राप्तं निःसंशयं भयम्। जीवितान्तकरं घोरं रक्षसां रावणस्य च॥
en: Forsooth, he is that fearful man who shall slay Rāvana and the Rākşasas.

sn: पीड्यमानास्तु बलिना वरदानेन रक्षसा। दीप्तैस्तपोभिर्विबुधाः पितामहपूजयन् ॥
en: The celestials being thus oppressed by Ravana, who had obtained the boon, worshipped the great Patriachs with sever austerities.

sn: देवतानां हितार्थाय महात्मा वै पितामहः। उवाच देवतास्तुष्ट इदं सर्वा महद्वचः॥
en: Being propitiated with them, the high-souled Patriarch, for their welfare, addressed the celestials, with the following pregnant speech.

sn: अद्यप्रभृति लोकांस्त्रीन्सर्वे दानवराक्षसाः। भयेन प्रभृता नित्यं विचरिष्यन्ति शाश्वतम्॥
en: From today shall the Rākṣasas and Dänavas roam for ever afraid of the celestials in three worlds,

sn: दैवतैस्तु समागम्य सर्वेश्चन्द्रपुरोगमैः। वृषध्वजस्त्रिपुरहा महादेवः प्रतोषितः॥
en: Thereupon the celestials headed by Indra engaged in propitiating Mahādeva, the slayer of Tripura, and who rides upon a bull.

sn: प्रसन्नस्तु महादेवो देवानेतद्वचोऽब्रवीत्। उत्पत्स्यति हितार्थं वो नारी रक्षःक्षयावहा॥
en: And being pleased, Mahädeva addressed them saying, For your welfare there will be born a woman who shall be the cause of the destruction of the Rākşasas.

sn: एषा देवैः प्रयुक्ता तु क्षुद्यथा दानवान्पुरा। भक्षयिष्यति नः सर्वान्राक्षसघ्नी सरावणान्॥
en: As hunger, being engaged by the celestials, did destroy in olden time, all the Dānvas, so shall she (Sītā) the root of the extinction of Rāksasa race destroy us all with Rāvana.

sn: रावणस्यापनीतेन दुविनीतस्य दुर्मतेः। अयं निष्टानको घोरः शोकेन समभिप्लुतः॥
en: Alas! for the foolishness of the vicious minded and insolent Răvaņa destruction has faced us and we are overwhelmed with grief.

sn: तं न पश्यामहे लोके यो नः शरणदो भवेत्। राघवेणोपसृष्टानां कालेनेव युगक्षये॥ नास्ति नः शरणः किंचिद्भये महति तिष्ठताम्। दावाग्निवेष्टितानां हि करेणूनां यथा वने॥
en: We do not see any such being in the world who can afford us shelter. Rāghava has attacked us like to the fire of dissolution. There is no refuge for who have been stricken with fear as no help re.. hes the elephants in a forest best with fire.

sn: प्राप्तकालं कृतं तेन पौलस्त्येन महात्मना। यत एव भयं दृष्टं तमेव शरणं गतः॥
en: The high-souled Vibhīşaņa did the just thing in proper time-he took shelter of him from whom he expected danger.

sn: इतीव सर्वा रजनीचरस्त्रियः परस्परं संपरिरभ्य बाहुभिः। विषेदुरार्तातिभयाभिपीडिता विनेदुरुच्चैश्च तदा सुदारुणम्॥
en: Thus bewailed piteously and loudly-the she demons holding each other by neck and being stricken with fear and grief.

sn: आर्तानां राक्षसीनां तु लङ्कायां वै कुले कुले। रावणः करुणं शब्दं शुश्राव परिदेवितम्॥
en: Thereupon Rāvana heard in every house of Lankā the piteous cries of the she-demons possessed by sorrow.

sn: स तु दीर्घ विनिःश्वस्य मुहूर्तं ध्यानमास्थितः। बभूव परमक्रुद्धो रावणो भीमदर्शनः॥
en: And sighing hard he engaged in mediations for some time. And terrible-looking as he was greatly worked up with ire.

sn: संदश्य दशनैरोष्ठं क्रोधसंरक्तलोचनः। राक्षसैरपि दुर्दर्शः कालाग्निरिव मूर्तिमान् ॥
en: Having his eyes reddened with anger and gnashing his teeth and biting the lips, that one, irrepressible by other Raksasas, looked like the fire of dissolution incarnate.

sn: उवाच च समीपस्थानराक्षसान्राक्षसेश्वरः। क्रोधाव्यक्तकथस्तत्र निर्दहत्रिव चक्षुषा ॥
en: There upon the lord of Rākşasas, in anger as if burning down everything with his look addressed the Rākşasas who were near him.
