en: Like to the thousand-eyed Indra in his car, drawn by horses the blameless Rāma; seated in his car, proceeded towards the excellent city.

sn: जग्राह भरतो रश्मीशत्रुघ्नश्छत्रमाददे। लक्ष्मणो व्यजनं तस्य मूर्ध्नि संवीजयंस्तदा॥
en: Bharata took up the reins, ſatrughna held the umbrella and Lakşmaņa began to fan him on the head with Chowries.

sn: श्वेतं च बालव्यजनं जगृहे परितः स्थितः। अपरं चन्द्रसंकाशं राक्षसेन्द्रो विभीषणः॥
en: Vibhīşaņa, the lord of Rākşasas standing on one side, took up the white Chowrie shining like the second moon.

sn: ऋषिसङ्घस्तदाकाशे देवैश्च समरुद्गणैः। स्तूयमानस्य रामस्य शुश्रुवे मधुरध्वनिः॥
en: There was audible the sweet encomium of Rāma chanted by the crowd of ascetics in the sky, the celestials and the Marutas.

sn: ततः शत्रुजयं नाम कुञ्जरं पर्वतोपमम्। आरुरोह महातेजा सुग्रीवः प्लवगर्षभः॥
en: Thereupon the highly effulgent Sugrīva, the foremost of monkeys, got up upon an elephant named Śatruñjaya resembling a mountain.

sn: नव नागसहस्राणि ययुरास्थाय वानराः। मानुषं विग्रहं कृत्वा सर्वाभरणभूषिताः॥
en: And riding nine thousand elephants proceeded the monkeys assuming human shapes and adorned with various ornaments.

sn: शङ्खशब्दप्रणादैश्च दुन्दुभीनां च निःस्वनैः। प्रययौ पुरुषव्याघ्रस्तां पुरीं हर्नामालिनीम्॥
en: And with the music of conches and bugles that foremost of men entered the city abounding in houses.

sn: ददृशुस्ते समायान्तं राघवं सपुरःसरम्। विराजमानं वपुषा रथेनातिरथं तदा॥
en: They (citizens) beheld Raghava enter the city with a graceful person and seated in the car.

sn: ते वर्धयित्वा काकुत्स्थं रामेण प्रतिनन्दिताः। अनुजग्मुर्महात्मानं भ्रातृभिः परिवारितम्॥
en: They having bowed to that descendant of Kākutstha were welcomed by him. And they followed that high souled one encircled by his brothers.

sn: अमात्यैर्ब्राह्मणैश्चैव तथा प्रकृतिभिर्वृतः। श्रिया विरुरुचे रामो नक्षत्रैरिव चन्द्रमाः॥
en: And surrounded by his courtiers, Brāhmaṇas and subjects Rāma appeared beautiful like to the Moon encircled by stars.

sn: स पुरोगामिभिस्तूर्यैस्तालस्वस्तिकपाणिभिः। प्रव्याहरद्भिर्मुदितैर्मङ्गलानि वृतो ययौ॥
en: He went preceded by men who play on stringed instruments, by people with Karatal and Sustika in their hands and by men chanting delightedly auspicious songs.

sn: अक्षतं जातरूपं च गावः कन्याः सहद्विजाः। नरा मोदकहस्ताश्च रामस्य पुरतो ययुः॥
en: Persons with Aksata and gold in their hands, kine, girls, Brāhmaṇas and persons with Modaka in their hands went before Rāma.

sn: सख्यं च रामः सुग्रीवे प्रभावं चानिलात्मजे। वानराणां च तत्कर्म ह्याचचक्षेऽथ मन्त्रिणाम्॥
en: Thereupon before the ministers Rāma began to describe the friendship of Sugrīva, the prowess of the Wind-gods son and the works accomplished by the monkeys.

sn: श्रुत्वा च विस्मयं जग्मुरयोध्यापुरवासिनः। वानराणां च तत्कर्म राक्षसानां च तद्बलम्॥
en: Hearing of the amazing works of the monkeys and the prowess of the Rākşasas, the inhabitants of the city of Ayodhyā attained to astonishment.

sn: द्युतिमानेतदाख्याय रामो वानरसंयुतः। हृष्टपुष्टजनाकीर्णामयोध्यां प्रविवेश सः॥
en: Having related thus (the works of the monkeys) the graceful Rāma encircled by the monkeys entered (the city of) Ayodhya abounding in delighted and plump persons.

sn: ततो ह्यभ्युच्छ्रयन्पौराः पताकाश्च गृहे गृहे। ऐक्ष्वाकाध्युषितं रम्यमाससाद पितुर्मुहम्।॥
en: Thereupon the citizens hoisted up flags upon every house and he reached the picturesque abode of his ancestors inhabited by the descendants of Ikşvāku.

sn: अथाब्रवीद्राजपुत्रो भरतं धर्मिणां वरम्। अर्थोपहितया वाचा मधुरं रघुनन्दनः।॥ पितुर्भवनमासाद्य प्रवेश्य च महात्मनः। कौसल्यां च सुमित्रां च कैकेयीमभिवादय॥
en: Having reached and entered his ancestral palace and bowed to Kausalyä, Sumitra and Kaikeyī, the high-souled prince, the enhancer of the joy of the descendants of Raghu, addressed Bharata the foremost of the pious, with sweet words instinct with meaning, saying.

sn: तच्च मद्भवनं श्रेष्ठं साशोकवनिकं महत्। मुक्तावैदूर्यसंकीर्णं सुग्रीवाय निवेदय ॥
en: Kākutstha, living in the forest of Dandaka with bark and matted hairs, for whom you are lamenting, has, “Do you set apart for Sugrīva my huge and excellent palace abounding in pearls and Vaiduryas."

sn: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा भरतः सत्यविक्रमः। हस्ते गृहीत्वा सुग्रीवं प्रविवेश तमालयम्॥
en: Hearing those words, Bharata, having truth for his prowess, taking Sugrīva by the hand, conducted him to the palace.

sn: ततस्तैलप्रदीपांश्च पर्यङ्कास्तरणानि च। गृहीत्वा विविशुः क्षिप्रं शत्रुघ्नेन प्रचोदिताः॥
en: And commanded by Śatrughna, (servants) speedily entered (that palace) with oil, lamps, bedsteads and beddings.

sn: उवाच च महातेजाः सुग्रीवं राघवानुजः। अभिषेकाय रामस्य दूतानाज्ञापय प्रभो॥
en: Thereupon the highly effulgent younger brother of Raghava spoke to Sugriva, saying, "Do you, O lord, order some (to bring water) for Rama's installation."

sn: सौवर्णान्वानरेन्द्राणां चतुर्णां चतुरो घटान्। ददौ क्षिप्रं स सुग्रीवः सर्वरत्नविभूषितान्॥
en: Sugrīva conferred upon four leading monkeys four golden jars crested with diverse jewels and said to them.

sn: तथा प्रत्यूषसमये चतुणां सागराम्भसाम्। पूर्णैर्घटैः प्रतीक्षध्वं तथा कुरुत वानराः॥
en: "Do you so conduct, O monkeys, that you may return by the dawn with the jars filled with the water of the four oceans."

sn: एवमुक्ता महात्मानो वानरा वारणोपमाः। उत्पेतुर्गगनं शीघ्रं गरुडा इव शीघ्रगाः। ५१ ।।
en: Being thus addressed by the high-souled (Sugrīva) the monkeys resembling the elephants speedily rose up in the welkin like to quick coursing vultures.

sn: जाम्बवांश्च हनूमांश्च वेगदर्शी च वानरः। ऋषभश्चैव कलशाञ्जलपूर्णानथानयन्॥ नदीशतानां पञ्चानां जलं कुम्भैरुपाहरन्।
en: Jambavan, Hanumān, the monkey Vegadarsi and Rşabha brought the jars filled with water and another monkeys brought the water in jars from five hundred rivers.

sn: पूर्वात्समुद्रात्कलशं जलपूर्णमथानयत्॥ सुषेणः सत्त्वसंपन्नः सर्वरत्नविभूषितम्।
en: Suşeņa, gifted with prowess, brought that jar crested with gems, filled with water from the Eastern Ocean.

sn: ऋषभो दक्षिणातूर्णं समुद्राज्जलमानयत्॥ रक्तचन्दनकपूरैः संवृतं काञ्चनं घटम्। गवयः पश्चिमातोयमाजहार महार्णवात्॥
en: Rşabha speedily brought water from the southern Ocean. Gavaya brought from the great Western Ocean in that golden jar, water perfumed with the fragrance of red sandal and camphor.

sn: रत्नकुम्भेन महता शीतं मारुतविक्रमः। उत्तराच्च जलं शीघ्रं गरुडानिलविक्रमः॥ आजहार स धर्मात्मानिलः सर्वगुणान्वितः।
en: The virtuous-souled Wind-gods son, gifted with all accomplishments and the prowess of Garuda and Wind-god, brought, speedily from the Northern Ocean, water in that large jewelled jar.

sn: ततस्तैर्वानरश्रेष्ठैरानीतं प्रेक्ष्य तज्जलम्। ५७।। अभिषेकाय रामस्य शत्रुघ्नः सचिवैः सह। पुरोहिताय श्रेष्ठाय सुहद्भयश्च न्यवेदयत्।५८॥
en: Beholding water thus brought by the leading monkeys for the installation of Rāma, Satrughna, with his ministers, communicated that to the leading priests and friends.

sn: ततः स प्रयतो वृद्धो वसिष्ठो ब्राह्मणैः सह। राम रलमये पीठे ससीतं संन्यवेशयत्॥
en: Thereupon the self-controlled Vasistha, stricken in years, along with other Brāhmaṇas placed Rāma with Sītā on a jewelled seat.

sn: वसिष्ठो विजयश्चैव जाबालिरथ काश्यपः। कात्यायनो गौतमश्च वामदेवस्तथैव च॥ अभ्यषिञ्चनरव्याघ्र प्रसन्नेन सुगन्धिना। सलिलेन सहस्राक्षं वसवो वासवं यथा॥
en: Vasistha, Vijaya, Jabali, Katyayana, Gautama and Vāmadeva, sprinkled that foremost of men, with clear and fragrant water as Vasus did the thousand eyed Vasava.

sn: ऋत्विग्भिाह्मणैः पूर्व कन्याभिर्मन्त्रिभिस्तथा। योधैश्चैवाभ्यषिञ्चस्ते सम्प्रहृष्टैः सनैगमैः॥ सौषधिरसैश्चापि दैवतैर्नभसि स्थितैः। चतुभिर्लोकपालैश्च सर्वैर्देवैश्च संगतैः॥
en: Ministers, soldiers and the merchants all delighted. (Thereupon with the juice of Oshadhis (he was sprinkled by) the celestials stationed in the sky, the deities presiding over four quarters and all other celestials collected.

sn: ब्रह्मणा निर्मितं पूर्व किरीटं रत्नशोभिताम्। अभिषिक्तः पुरा येन मनुस्तं दीप्ततेजसम्॥ तस्यान्ववाये राजानः क्रमायेनाभिषेचिताः। सभायां हेमक्लुप्तायां शोभितायां महाधनैः॥ रत्नैर्नानाविधैश्चैव चित्रितायां सुशोभनैः। नानारत्नमये पीठे कल्पयित्वा यथाविधि।६६॥ किरीटेन ततः पश्चाद्वसिष्ठेन महात्मना। ऋत्विग्भिभूषणैश्चैव समयोक्ष्यत राघवः॥
en: Having placed him on a seat crested with various jewels in the arena decorated with gold, various jewels and rich parapharnalia, (he placed on his head) the jewelled crown made by Brahmā, brilliant and with which in the days of yore Manu and other kings, born in his race, were installed. And being decked by the highsouled Vasistha with that crown, Rāghava was afterwards dressed with the celestial garments by the Rtvigas.* *A domestic chaplain a family priest.

sn: छत्रं तस्य च जग्राह शत्रुघ्नः पाण्डुरं शुभम्। श्वेतं च बालव्यजनं सुग्रीवो वानरेश्वरः॥ अपरं चन्द्रसंकाशं राक्षसेन्द्रो विभीषणः।
en: Śatrughna held the white and excellent umbrella and Sugrīva the lord of monkeys took the white Chowrie. And Vibhīşaņa the lord of Rákşasas took up another Chowrie resembling the moon.

sn: मालां ज्वलन्तीं वपुषा काञ्चनीं शतपुष्कराम्॥ राघवाय ददौ वायुर्वासवेन प्रचोदितः। सर्वरत्नसमायुक्तं मणिभिश्च विभूषितम्।७०।। मुक्ताहारं नरेन्द्राय ददौ शक्रप्रचोदितः।
en: The wind commanded by Väsava conferred upon Rāghava, a garland or hundred golden lotuses, shining in their native lustre. And the wind commanded by Sakra conferred upon that lord of men a jewelled garland crested with diverse gems.

sn: प्रजगुर्देवगन्धर्वा ननृतुश्चाप्सरोगणाः।७१।। अभिषेके तदहस्य तदा रामस्य धीमतः।
en: The intelligent and worthy Rāma being installed the celestials and the Gandharvas sang and the Apsaras danced.

sn: भूमिः सस्यवती चैव फलवन्तश्च पादपः।७२।। गन्धवन्ति च पुष्पाणि बभूवू राघवोत्सवे।
en: The earth was filled with crops, the trees with fruits and the flowers were fragrant on the occassion of Rāghava's installation.

sn: सहस्रशतमश्वानां धेनूनां च गवां तथा॥ ददौ शतवृषान्पूर्व द्विजेभ्यो मनुजर्षभः। त्रिंशत्कोटीर्हिरण्यस्य ब्राह्मणेभ्यो ददौ पुनः॥ नानाभरणवस्त्राणि महार्हाणि च राघवः।
en: That foremost of men conferred upon the twice-born ones one million of horses, hundred thousand cows and hundred thousand bulls. And Rāghava again conferred upon the Brāhmaṇas thirty crores of golden coins and diverse costly ornaments and clothes.

sn: अर्करश्मिप्रतीकाशां काञ्चनीं मणिविग्रहाम्।७५।। सुग्रीवाय जं दिव्यां प्रायच्छन्मनुजाधिपः।
en: Thereupon that lord of men conferred upon Sugriva a celestial garland brilliant like the rays of the Sun and crested with gold and jewels.

sn: वैदूर्यमयचित्रे च चन्द्ररश्मिविभूषिते॥ वालिपुत्राय धृतिमानङ्गदायाङ्गदे ददौ।
en: And he, gifted with intelligence, conferred upon Angada, Vali's son, two Angadas (A kind of ornament worn on upper arms.) brilliant as the rays of the moon and made of Vaidurya.

sn: मणिप्रवरजुष्टं तं मुक्ताहारमनुत्तमम्॥ सीतायै प्रददौ रामश्चन्द्ररश्मिसमप्रभम्। अरजे वाससी दिव्ये शुभान्याभरणानि च॥
en: Rāma conferred upon Sitā an excellent pearl necklace crested with precious jems, celestial clothes and various excellent ornaments.

sn: अवेक्षमाणा वैदेही प्रददौ वायुसूनवे। अवमुच्यात्मनः कण्ठाद्वारं जनकनन्दिनी॥ अवैक्षत हरीन्सर्वान्भर्तारं च मुहुर्मुहुः।
en: And taking off the necklace from her person Vaidehi, the daughter of king Janaka, conferred it upon the Wind-god's son remembering the services (rendered by him) and cast her looks again and again upon her lord and the monkeys.

sn: तामिङ्गितज्ञः संप्रेक्ष्य बभाषे जनकात्मजाम्॥ प्रदेहि सुभगे हारं यस्य तुष्टासि भामिनि ।
en: Beholding that (Rāma) capable of reading the gestures, spoke to the daughter of king Janaka, saying, "O fortunate and beautiful lady, do you confer this necklace upon him with whom you are pleased."

sn: अथ सा वायुपुत्राय तं हारमसितेक्षणा।८१।। तेजो धृतिर्यशो दाक्ष्यं सामर्थ्य विनयो नयः। पौरुषं विक्रमो बुद्धिर्यस्मिनेतानि नित्यदा।॥ हनूमांस्तेन हारेण शुशुभे वानरर्षभः। चन्द्रांशुचयगौरेण श्वेताभ्रेण यथाचलः।८३॥
en: Thereupon the lotus-eyed (Sitā) conferred that upon the Wind god's son. And Hanuman, the foremost of monkeys, in whom perpetually exist, energy, forgiveness, fame, skilfulness, prowess, humility, tactics, manliness, valiance and intellect, appeared with that necklace like a mountain beautified with the rays of the moon and white clouds.

sn: सर्वे वानरवृद्धाश्च ये चान्ये वानरोत्तमाः। वासोभिर्भूषणैश्चैव यथार्ह प्रतिपूजिताः॥
en: All other elderly and leading monkeys were respectively honoured with clothes and ornaments.

sn: विभीषणोऽथ सुग्रीवो हनूमाञ्जाम्बवांस्तथा। सर्वे वानरमुख्याश्च रामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा॥ यथाहं पूजिताः सर्वे कामै रत्नैश्च पुष्कलैः। प्रहृष्टमनसः सर्वे जग्मुरेव यथागतम्॥
en: Being honoured by Rāma of unwearied actions with enough of jewels and other wishedfor objects, Vibhisana, Sugriva, Hanuman, Jambavan and other leading monkeys, delighted, returned to their respective habitations.

sn: ततो द्विविदमैन्दाभ्यां नीलाय च परंतपः। सर्वान्कामगुणान्वीक्ष्य प्रददौ वसुधाधिपः॥
en: Thereupon, the lord of earth and the slayer of foes conferred, all wished for things, upon Dvivida, Mainda and Nila.

sn: दृष्ट्वा सर्वे महात्मानस्ततस्ते वानरर्षभाः। विसृष्टाः पार्थिवेन्द्रेण किष्किन्धां समुपागमन्॥
en: Beholding (the installation of Rāma) the highsouled monkeys, taking leave of the lord of earth, went to Kiskindha.

sn: सुग्रीवो वानरश्रेष्ठो दृष्ट्वा रामाभिषेचनम्। पूजितश्चैव रामेण किष्किन्धां प्राविशत्पुरीम्॥
en: And beholding the inauguration of Răma, Sugrīva, the foremost of monkeys, honoured by Rāma, repaired to the city of Kiskindhā.

sn: विभीषणोऽपि धर्मात्मा सह तैर्नैऋतर्षभैः। लब्ध्वा कुलधनं राजा लङ्कां प्रायान्महायशाः॥
en: Having obtained his own kingdom, the greatly famous and virtuous souled Vibhīşaņa, with all the Rākşasas, repaired to the city of Lankā.

sn: स राज्यमखिलं शासनिहतारिमहायशाः। राघवः परमोदारः : शशास परया मुदा।। उवाच लक्ष्मणं रामो धर्मज्ञं धर्मवत्सलः॥
en: Having slain his foes, the highly generous and glorious Rama, ruled in great delight, the kingdom extending all over the earth. And Rama, fond of the pious, spoke to Laksmana, conversant with piety, saying-

sn: आतिष्ठ धर्मज्ञ मया सहेमां गां पूर्वराजाध्युषितां बलेन। तैयौँवराज्ये दुरमुद्वहस्व॥
en: O you conversant with piety, do you with me and four fold forces, govern this kingdom, ruled by our predecessors. Like to our ancestors do you now carry the burden of an associate in the throne.

sn: सर्वात्मना पर्यनुनीयमानो यदा न सौमित्रिरुपैति योगम्। नियुज्यमानो ततोऽभ्यषिञ्चद्भरतं महात्मा॥
en: When the son of Sumitrā did not accept the heir apparentship albeit solicited earnestly again and again, the high-souled (Rāma) conferred upon Bharata that dignity.

sn: पौण्डरीकाश्वमेधाभ्यां वाजिमेधेन चासकृत्। अन्यैश्च विविधैर्यज्ञैरयजत्पार्थिवात्मजः॥ भुवि यौवराज्ये
en: That son of king performed various sacrifices such as Paundarika, Asvamedha', Vajimedha and other of various kinds. 1. A kind of sacrifice. 2. A kind of Sacrifice in which a horse is slain.

sn: राज्यं दशसहस्राणि प्राप्य वर्षाणि राघवः। दशाश्वमेधानाजह्वे सदश्वान्भूरिदक्षिणान्॥
en: And governing the kingdom for ten thousand years Rāghava performed ten horse-sacrifices with excellent horses and profuse presents.

sn: आजानुलम्बिबाहुः स महावक्षाः प्रतापवान्। लक्ष्मणानुचरो रामः शशास पृथिवीमिमाम्॥
en: That highly powerful Rāma, having his arms extended up to the knee-joint, having a spacious breast and Lakşmaņa as his attendant, ruled the earth (in this.wise).

sn: राघवश्चापि धर्मात्मा प्राप्य राज्यमनुत्तमम्। ईजे बहुविधैर्यज्ञैः ससुतभ्रातृबान्धवः॥
en: Obtaining that excellent kingdom, the virtuous souled Raghava performed many sacrifices with his sons, brothers and friends.

sn: न पर्यदेवन्विधवा न च व्यालकृतं भयम्। न व्याधिजं भयं चासीद्रामे राज्यं प्रशासति ॥
en: Rāma governing the kingdom, the widows were not distressed and there was no fear from voracious animals or from diseases.

sn: निर्दस्युरभवल्लोको नानर्थं कश्चिदस्पृशत्। न च स्म वृद्धा बालानां प्रेतकार्याणि कुर्वते॥
en: The people were saved from the thieves and there was no other trouble. And the old were not constrained to perform the funeral ceremonies of the children.

sn: सर्व मुदितमेवासीत्सर्वो धर्मपरोऽभवत्। राममेवानुपश्यन्तो नाभ्यहिंसन्परस्परम्॥
en: All were delighted and devoted to pious observances. And beholding Rāma they did not envy one another.

sn: आसन्वर्षसहस्राणि तथा पुत्रसहस्रिणः। निरामया विशोकाश्च रामे राज्यं प्रशासति ॥
en: Rāma governing the kingdom, (people) lived for thousand years and had thousand children, they were freed from diseases and sorrow.

sn: नित्यमूला नित्यफलास्तरवस्तत्र पुष्पिताः। कामवर्षी च पर्जन्यः सुखस्पर्शश्च मारुतः॥
en: The trees bore fruits and flowers perpetuallythere were showers at will and the wind blew pleasant.

sn: स्वकर्मसु प्रवर्तन्ते तुष्टाः स्वैरेव कर्मभिः। आसन्प्रजा धर्मपरा रामे शासति नानृताः॥ सर्वे लक्षणसंपन्नाः सर्वे धर्मपरायणाः। दशवर्षसहस्राणि रामो राज्यमकारयत्॥
en: The people delighted engaged in their respective works and the subjects grew pious and truthful, under Rāma's regime, and were devoted to the observances of all pious works and gifted with all auspicious marks. And Rāma ruled the kingdom for ten thousand years.

sn: धयं यशस्यमायुष्यं राज्ञां च विजयावहम्। आदिकाव्यमिदं चार्ष पुरा वाल्मीकिना कृतम्॥
en: This sacred Epic, the first of its kind, affording piety, fame, and long life, and describing the conquest of tire kings, was composed by Vālmīki in the days of yore.

sn: यः शृणोति सदा लोके नरः पापात्प्रमुच्यते। पुत्रकामश्च पुत्रान्वै धनकामो धनानि च॥ लभते मनुजो लोके श्रुत्वा रामाभिषेचनम्। महीं विजयते राजा रिपूंश्चाप्यधितिष्ठति॥
en: He, who on this earth, shall hear (this story) shall be divested of sins. People, wishing for children, shall obtain the same and those, wishing for riches, shall get by them. Thus people on this earth shall attain to their wished for objects hearing of this Răma's installationthe king may conquer the earth and subdue his foes.

sn: राघवेण यथा माता सुमित्रा लक्ष्मणेन च। भरतेन च कैकेयी जीवपुत्रास्तथा स्त्रियः॥
en: Females may obtain sons (in the same way) as Kausalyā gave birth to Rāma, Sumitrā to Lakşmaņa and Kaikeyi to Bharata.

sn: श्रुत्वा रामायणमिदं दीर्घमायुश्च विन्दति। रामस्य विजयं चेमं सर्वमक्लिष्टकर्मणः॥
en: Hearing the story of this work describing the victory of Rāma of unwearied actions one may attain to a long life.

sn: शृणोति य इदं काव्यं पुरा वाल्मीकिना कृतम्। श्रद्दधानो जितक्रोधो दुर्गाण्यतितरत्यसौ॥
en: He, who with devotion and having his anger subdued, shall hear the story of this epic written by Vālmīki in the days of yore shall get over all troubles.

sn: समागम्य प्रवासान्ते रमन्ते सह बान्धवैः। शृण्वन्ति य इदं काव्यं पुरा वाल्मीकिना कृतम्।।१११। ते प्रार्थितान्वरान्सर्वान्प्राप्नुवन्तीह राघवात्। श्रवणेन सुराः सर्वे प्रीयन्ते संप्रशृण्वताम्॥ विनायकाश्च शाम्यन्ति गृहे तिष्ठति यस्य वै।
en: Hearing the story of the Epic composed by Vālmīki in the days of yore, one living in foreign countries, shall return home and enjoy in the company of his friends. Hearing this people shall secure all their wished for objects from Rāghava and the celestials shall be greatly delighted. When this book is kept in a house it becomes free from the disturbance of evil spirits.

sn: विजयेत महीं राजा प्रवासी स्वस्तिमान्भवेत्॥ स्त्रियो रजस्वलाः श्रुत्वा पुत्रान्सूयुरनुत्तमान्।
en: Hearing this a king may conquer the earth, and one living in a foreign country fare well. If a female, during her monthly course, hears the story, she shall give birth to an excellent son.

sn: पूजयंश्च पठंश्चैनमितिहासं पुरातनम्॥ सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्येत दीर्घमायुरवाप्नुयात्।
en: By reading and worshipping this ancient history people are freed from all sins and attain to a long life.

sn: प्रणम्य शिरसा नित्यं श्रोतव्यं क्षत्रियैर्द्विजात्॥ ऐश्वर्यं पुत्रलाभश्च भविष्यति न संशयः। रामायणमिदं कृत्स्नं शृण्वतः पठतः सदा॥
en: The Kșatriyas, bending low their heads, should hear this daily from the Brāhmaṇas. Hearing or reading the whole of Rāmāyaṇa, forsooth shall people get sons and riches.

sn: प्रीयते सततं रामः स हि विष्णुः सनातनः। आदिदेवो महाबाहुर्हरिनारायणः प्रभुः॥
en: Rāma is ever pleased with him. He is the ever existing Visnu-the first God, the huge-armed Hari, Narayana and Lord.

sn: एवमेतत्पुरावृत्तमाख्यानं भद्रमस्तु वः। प्रव्याहरत विस्रब्धं बलं विष्णोः प्रवर्धताम्॥
en: This ancient work produce such fruits. May good betide you. Do you openly declare that Visnu's prowess may increase.

sn: देवाश्च सर्वे तुष्यन्ति ग्रहणाच्छ्वणात्तथा। रामायणस्य श्रवणे तृप्यन्ति पितरः सदा॥
en: The celestials shall be greatly delighted for reading or hearing this story of Rāma and the progenitors shall be always pleased.

sn: भक्त्या रामस्य ये चेमा संहितामृषिणा कृताम्। ये लिखन्तीह च नरास्तेषां वासस्त्रिविष्टपे॥
en: Those, who shall write this story of Rāma first recorded by the Rși (Vālmīki) shall reach the region of Brahma.

sn: कुटुम्बवृद्धिं धनधान्यवृद्धि स्त्रियश्च मुख्याः सुखमुत्तमं च। श्रुत्वा शुभं काव्यमिदं महार्थ प्राप्नोति सर्वां भुवि चार्थसिद्धिम्॥
en: Hearing this poem of great merits, people attain to, on this earth, multiplied relations, increased wealth and crops, beautiful wives, excellent happiness, and the accomplishment of all desires.

sn: आयुष्यमारोग्यकरं यशस्यं सौभ्रातृकं बुद्धिकरं शुभं च। राख्यानमोजस्करमृद्धिकामैः॥
en: They attain to long life, health, fame, intellect, prowess, and good brothers. Therefore it behove those good men, who wish for prosperity, to hear this story perpetually.

sn: प्राप्तराज्यस्य रामस्य राक्षसानां वधे कृते। आजग्मुर्मुनयः सर्वे राघवं प्रतिनन्दितुम् ॥
en: On the Rākṣasas having been slain, all the ascetics, for the purpose of congratulating Rāghava, came to Rāma as he gained (back) his kingdom.

sn: कौशिकोऽथ यवक्रीतो गार्यो गालव एव च। कण्वो मेधातिथेः पुत्रः पूर्वस्यां दिशि ये श्रिताः॥ स्वस्त्यात्रेयश्च भगवान्नमुचिः प्रमुचिस्तथा। अगस्त्योऽत्रिश्च भगवान्सुमुखो विमुखस्तथा॥ आजग्मुस्ते सहागस्त्या ये श्रिता दक्षिणां दिशम्।
en: Kausika, and Yavakrīta, and Gārgya, and Gālava and Kaņva, son of Medhātithi,who dwelt in the east, (came thither); and the reverend Svastyāstreya, and Namuci, and Pramuci, and Agastya, and the worshipful Atri, and Sumukha, and Vimukha, who dwelt in the south, came in company with Agastya.* *The name of Agastya had before been just specified among the incomes; but so it is in the text.

sn: नृषङ्गुः कवषी धौम्यः कौषेयश्च महानृषिः॥ तेऽप्याजग्मुः सशिष्या वै ये श्रिताः पश्चिमां दिशम्।
en: Nrisadgu, and Kavasi, and Dhaumya, and that mighty sage-Kauseya-who abode in th quarter, came there accompanied by their disciples.

sn: वसिष्ठः कश्यपोऽथात्रिविश्वामित्रः सगौतमः॥ जमदग्निर्भरद्वाजस्तेऽपि सप्तर्षयस्तथा। उदीच्यां दिशि सप्तैते नित्यमेव निवासिनः॥
en: Vasiştha and Kasyapa and Atri and Viśvāmitra with Gautama and Jamadagni and Bharadvāja and also the seven sages*, who for aye resided in the northern quarter, (came there). *Ursa Major, or the great bear, the seven stars of which are the souls of as many saints, Marici, Atri, Angiras, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu and Vasistha.

sn: संप्राप्यते महात्मानो राघवस्य निवेशनम्। विष्टिताः प्रतिहारा) हुताशनसमप्रभाः॥
en: On arriving at the residence of Rāghava, those high-souled ones, resembling the fire in radiance, stopped at the gate, with the intention of communicating their arrival (to Rama) through the warder.

sn: वेदवेदाङ्गविदुषो नानाशास्त्रविशारदाः। द्वाःस्थं प्रोवाच धर्मात्मा अगस्त्यो मुनिसत्तमः।।८
en: That foremost of ascetics-the righteous Agastya-versed in various branches of learning and cognisant of the Vedas along with their branches, addressed the warder, saying, “Do you say to Dasaratha's son that we-the sages-have come (here)."

sn: निवेद्यतां दाशरथेऋषयो वयमागताः। प्रतीहारस्ततस्तूर्णमगस्त्यवचनाद्भुतम्॥ समीपं राघवस्याशु प्रविवेश महात्मनः। नयेङ्गितिज्ञः सद्वृत्तो दक्षो धैर्यसमन्वितः॥ स रामं दृश्य सहसा पूर्णचन्द्रसमद्युतिम्। अगस्त्यं कथयामास संप्राप्तमृषिसत्तमम्॥
en: Then at the words of Agastya, the gate-keeper quick* and swift presented himself with celerity before the high-souled Rāghava. And that one versed in polity and emotional expressions, of worthy ways, possessed of ability, and endowed with patience swiftly seeing Rāma resembling the full moon in brightness, communicated to him the arrival of that supreme of saintsAgastya. *Turnam-according to the commentator, is mental celerity, and drutam-physical. This distinction, however, is seldom, if ever, observed by Sanskrit authors.

sn: श्रुत्वा प्राप्तान्मुनींस्तांस्तु बालसूर्यसमप्रभान्। प्रत्युवाच ततो द्वा:स्थं प्रवेशय यथासुखम्॥
en: Hearing of the arrival of the anchorets, possessed of the effulgence of the sun new-risen, he answered the warder, saying, "Do you usher them in, having regard to their comfort."

sn: दृष्ट्वा प्राप्तान्मुनींस्तांस्तु प्रत्युत्थाय कृताञ्जलिः। पाद्याादिभिरान गां निवेद्य च सादरम्॥ रामोऽभिवाद्य प्रयत आसनान्यादिदेश ह।
en: Seeing the ascetics him, Rāma with joined hands worshipped their feet with arghyas, and with regard consecrated a cow to each, and saluting them with the collecting mind, he ordered seats (for the saints).

sn: तेषु काञ्चनचित्रेषु महत्सु च वरेषु च॥ कुशान्तर्धानदत्तेषु मृगचर्मयुतेषु च। यथार्हमुपविष्टास्ते आसनेष्वृषिपुङ्गवाः॥ रामेण कुशलं पृष्टाः सशिष्याः सपुरोगमाः। महर्षयो वेदविदो रामं वचनमब्रुवन्।
en: And having, according to their rank, seated themselves on gorgeous and superb seats of kuća or deerskins embroidered with gold, those foremost of sages-those mighty saints, versed in the Vedas, along with their disciples and leaders, having (previously) been asked as to their welfare, addressed Rāma, saying.

sn: कुशलं नो महाबाहो सर्वत्र रघुनन्दन॥ त्वां तु दिष्ट्या कुशलिनं पश्यामो हतशात्रवम्। दिष्ट्या त्वया हतो राजन्रावणो लोकरावणः॥
en: O son of Raghu. O mighty-armed one, complete welfare is ours. By good luck it is that we see you fortunate, with all your foes finished. Bygood luck it is that, Oking, Ravana-destroyer of creatures, has been slain byyou.

sn: नहि भारः स ते राम रावणः पुत्रपौत्रवान्। सधनुस्तवं हि लोकांस्त्रीन्विजयेथा न संशयः॥
en: Sure, O Rama, it was no great matter for you (to slay) Rāvaņa along with his sons and grandsons. Furnished with your bow, you can, without doubt, destroy the three worlds themselves.

sn: दिष्ट्या त्वया हतो राम रावणः पुत्रपौत्रवान्। दिष्ट्या विजयिनं त्वाद्य पश्यामः सह सीतया॥ लक्ष्मणेन च धर्मात्मन्ध्रात्रा त्वद्धितकारिणा। मातृभिर्धातृसहितं पश्यामोऽद्य वयं नृप॥
en: By good fortune it is, O Rama, that Ravana along with his sons and grandsons has been slain by you. By good fortune it is that today we see you victorious along with $ītā, and, O righteoussouled one, with your brother, Lakşmaņa, (ever) compassing your profit. (By good fortune it is) that, Oking, today we behold (you) in company with your mothers and your brothers.

sn: दिष्ट्या प्रहस्तो विकटो विरूपाक्षो महोदरः। अकम्पनश्च दुर्धर्षो निहतास्ते निशाचराः॥
en: By good fortune it is that those night-rangers, Prahasta, and Vikata; and Virupāksa, and Mahodara, and the unconquerable Akampana, have all been slain (by you).

sn: यस्य प्रमाणाद्विपुलं प्रमाणं नेह विद्यते। दिष्ट्या ते समरे राम कुम्भकर्णो निपातितः॥
en: By good fortune it is, O Rama, that he than whose proportions there are no other's greater on earth, even Kumbhakarņa, was brought downy (by you).

sn: त्रिशिराश्चातिकायश्च देवान्तकनरान्तकौ। दिष्ट्या ते निहता राम महावीर्या निशाचराः॥
en: By good luck it is, O Rama, that these highly powerful night-rangers. Trisiras and Atikāya and Devāntaka and Narāntaka, have been slain by you.

sn: दिष्ट्या त्वं राक्षसेन्द्रेण द्वन्द्वयुद्धमुपागतः। देवतानामवध्येन विजय प्राप्तवानसि॥
en: By good luck it is that you had been encountered in a hand-to-hand combat with that foremost of Rākşasas, incapable of being slain by the celestials themselves; and achieved victory (ultimately).

sn: संख्ये तस्य न किंचित्तु रावणस्य पराभवः। द्वन्द्वयुद्धमनुप्राप्तो दिष्ट्या ते रावणिर्हतः॥
en: To defeat Ravana in battle was (for you) in small matter; but it is a piece of good fortune that Ravana's son, who had confronted you for combat, has been slain (by you) in battle.

sn: दिष्ट्या तस्य महाबाहो कालस्येवाभिधावतः। मुक्तः सुररिपोर्वीर प्राप्तश्च विजयस्त्वया॥
en: By good fortune it is that you, O mightyarmed one, had been liberated from the bonds of) that foe of the celestials whose course resembled that of Time;*-and that you also had secured victory. *i.e. surpassing perception.

sn: अभिनन्दाम ते सर्वे संश्रुत्येन्द्रजितो वधम्। अवध्यः सर्वभूतानां महामायाधरो युधि॥
en: Hearing of the destruction of Indrajit, we congratulate you (on your success). He was in capable of being slain by all creatures, and in battle possessed mighty powers of illusion.

sn: विस्मयस्त्वेष चास्माकं तं श्रुत्वेन्द्रजितं हतम्। दत्त्वा पुण्यामिमां वीर सौम्यामभयदक्षिणाम्।। दिष्ट्या वर्धसि काकुत्स्थ जयेनामित्रकर्शन॥
en: Hearing that Indrajit slain, amazement have seized us all. Having conferred on us this holy freedom from fear, O Kākutstha, O repressor of enemies. you through good fortune, will grow in victory.

sn: श्रुत्वा तु वचनं तेषां मुनीनां भावितात्मनाम्। विस्मयं परमं गत्वा रामः प्राञ्जलिरब्रवीत्॥
en: Hearing the speech of the ascetics of sacred souls, Rāma, coming under the influence of a mighty wonder, said with joined hands.

sn: भगवन्तः कुंभकर्णं रावणं च निशाचरम्। अतिक्रम्य महावीयौँ किं प्रशंसथ रावणिम्॥
en: You worshipful ones, wherefore, passing by those exceedingly powerful ones-Kumbhakarna and the night-ranger, Ravana, do you praise Ravana's son?

sn: महोदरं प्रहस्तं च विरूपाक्षं च राक्षसम्। मत्तोन्मत्तौ च दुर्धर्षों देवान्तकनरान्तकौ।। अतिक्रम्य महावीरान् किं प्रशंसथ रावणिम्॥
en: Wherefore, passing by Mahodara, and Prahasta, and the Rākşasa-Virüpākşa-and Matta, and Unmatta, and the irrepressible Devāntaka and Narāntaka-redoubtable heroes all-do you extol Ravana's son?

sn: अतिकायं त्रिशिरसं धूम्राक्षं च निशाचरम्। अतिक्रम्य महावीर्यान्कि प्रशंसथ रावणिम्॥
en: And wherefore, passing by Atikāya and Trisiras and Dhumraksa, that night-ranger-all endowed with exceeding powers, do you extol Ravana's son?

sn: कीदृशो वै प्रभावोऽस्य किं बलं कः पराक्रमः। के वा कारणेनैष रावणादतिरिच्यते॥
en: What was his prowess? And what his strength? And what his might? And by virtue of what cause did he surpass Rāvana?

sn: शक्यं यदि मया श्रोतुं न खल्वाज्ञापयामि वः। यदि गुह्यं न चेद्वक्तुं श्रोतुमिच्छामि कथ्यताम्॥
en: If I can well hear the same (do you tell it me). I by no means command you. If the thing can bear disclosure, I would hear it. Pray, speak out.

sn: शक्रोऽपि विजितस्तेन कथं लब्धवरश्च सः। कथं च बलवानन्पुत्रो न पिता तस्य रावणः॥
en: How was Śakra vanquished by him, and how also did he obtain the boon? And how was the son powerful and not his sire Rāvaņa.

sn: कथं पितुश्चाप्यधिको महाहवे शक्रस्य जेता हि कथं स राक्षसः। वराश्च लब्धाः कथयस्व मेऽद्य पाप्रच्छतश्चास्य मुनीन्द्र सर्वम्॥
en: How could that Raksasa, surpassing his sire, conquer Sakra in mighty encounter, and how did he obtain the boon? O foremost of anchorets, do you today unfold all this to me, who ask (for the same).

sn: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा राघवस्य महात्मनः। कुम्भयोनिर्महातेजा वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह॥
en: Hearing those words of Rāghva, the exceedingly energetic Kumbhayoni spoke as follows.

sn: शृणु राम तथा वृत्तं तस्य तेजोबलं महत्। जघान शत्रून्येनासौ न च वध्यः स शत्रुभिः॥
en: Having regard to his (Indrajit's) energy and might, I shall relate to you the history of his race, in the light of which you will perceive why Rāvana's son had been capable of slaying his enemies, but could not himself be slain by them.

sn: तावत्ते रावणस्येदं कुलं जन्म च राघव। वरप्रदानं च तथा तस्मै दत्तं ब्रवीमि ते॥
en: I shall, O Rāghava, describe to you Răvaņa's race and birth, as well as the boon that had been conferred on him.

sn: पुरा कृतयुगे राम प्रजापतिसुतः प्रभुः। पुलस्त्यो नाम ब्रह्मर्षिः साक्षादिव पितामहः॥
en: Formerly in the Krita age, O Rama, there was a Brahmarsi-lord (of creatures), son to Prajapati, and like to the very self of the great-father.

sn: नानुकीर्त्या गुणास्तस्य धर्मतः शीलतस्तथा। प्रजापतेः पुत्र इति वक्तुं शक्यं हि नामतः॥
en: His virtues, springing from righteousness and excellency of character, are past all delineation; I can only say that, forsooth, he went by the name of Prajāpati's son.

sn: प्रजापतिसुतत्वेन देवानां वल्लभो हि सः। इष्टः सर्वस्य लोकस्य गुणैः शुभैर्महामतिः॥
en: Verily on account of his being the son of Prajāpati, he was the darling of the deities; as by virtue of his spotless perfections, that magnanimous one was loved of all creatures.

sn: स तु धर्मप्रसङ्गेन मेरोः पार्श्वे महागिरेः। तृणबिन्द्वाश्रमं गत्वाप्यवसन्मुनिपुङ्गवः॥
en: And on a religious mission that foremost of ascetics, repairing to the asylum of Triņabindu at the side of the mighty mountain, Meru, took up his abode there.

sn: तपस्तेपे स धर्मात्मा स्वाध्यायनियतेन्द्रियः। गत्वाश्रमपदं तस्य विघ्नं कुर्वन्ति कन्यकाः॥ ऋपिपन्नगकन्याश्च राजर्षितनयाश्च याः। क्रीडन्त्योऽप्सरसश्चैव तं देशमुपपेदिरे॥
en: And with his senses centred on the study of the Vedas, that righteous-souled one, going to the hermitage, carried on austerities; but his religious rites were disturbed by certain girls. And daughters of sages and Pannagas and those of Rājarşis, as well as those of Apsarās, sporting, arrived at that quarter.

sn: सर्वर्तुषूपभोग्यत्वाद्रम्यत्वात्काननस्य च। नित्यशस्तास्तु तं देशं गत्वा क्रीडन्ति कन्यकाः॥
en: And an account of every season being genial at that spot and also of the loveliness of the wood, the damsels, repairing to this place. ever disport there.

sn: देशम्य रमणीयत्वात्पुलस्त्यो यत्र स द्विजः। गायन्त्यो वादयन्त्यश्च लासयन्त्यस्तथैव च॥ मुनेस्तपस्विनस्तस्य विघ्नं चक्रुरनिन्दिताः। अथ रुष्टो महातेजा व्याजहार महामुनिः॥
en: And on account of the beauty of that region, those wenches, coming to where that twice-born one, Pulastya was, used to sing, to play on instruments, and to dance; and thus those blameless beauties disturbed the rites of that anchoret practising austerities. Thereat, the mighty ascetic, waxing wroth, said,

sn: या मे दर्शनमागच्छेत्सा गर्भ धारयिष्यति। तास्तु सर्वाः प्रतिश्रुत्य तस्य वाक्यं महात्मनः॥ ब्रह्मशापभयागीतास्तं देशं नोपचक्रमुः। तृणबिन्दोस्तु राजर्षेस्तनया न शृणोति तत्॥ गत्वाश्रमपदं तत्र विचचार सुनिर्भया।
en: ‘She that comes within my kin, shall conceive.' Hearing the words of the high-souled one, (the damsels), afraid of a Brāhamana's curse, ceased to to haunt that place. But Triņabindu's daughter had not heard anything of all this, and going to the asylum, she ranged it fearlessly.

sn: न चापश्यच्च सा तत्र कांचिदभ्यागतां सखीम्॥ तस्मिन्काले महातेजाः प्राजापत्यो महानृषिः। स्वाध्यायमकरोत्तत्र तपसा भावितः स्वयम्॥
en: She did not see there any of her associates come to that spot. And at that time that exceedingly energetic and mighty sage, Prajāpati's son, with his soul sanctified through eticism, was engaged in the study of the Veda.

sn: सा तु वेदश्रुतिं दृष्ट्वा वै तपसो निधिम्। अभवत्पाण्डुदेहा सा सुव्यञ्जितशरीरजा॥
en: Hearing the sounds of Vedic recitation, and seeing that storehouse of asceticism, she had her body turned pale, and signs of pregnancy displayed themselves.

sn: बभूव च समुद्विग्ना दृष्ट्वा तद्दोषमात्मनः। इदं मे किंत्विति ज्ञात्वा पितुर्गत्वाश्रमे स्थिता॥
en: Seeing that evil befall her, she was wrought up with anxiety; and, understanding matters, she said, "What is this?' And, going to her father's hermitage, stayed there.

sn: तां तु दृष्ट्वा तथाभूतां तृणबिन्दुरथाब्रवीत्। किं त्वमेतत्त्वसदृशं धारयस्यात्मनो वपुः॥
en: Seeing her in this condition, Triņabindu said, "Wherefore is the person that you bear unlike what it used to be?'

sn: सा तु कृत्वाञ्जलिं दीना कन्योदाच तपोधनम्। न जाने कारणं तात येन मे रूपमीदृशम्॥
en: Thereat, in .woe-begone guise, with joined hands, his daughter replied to that one having asceticism for the riches, 'O father, cause know I none whereby I have come by this appearance.

sn: किं तु पूर्व गतास्म्येका महर्षे वितात्मनः। पुलस्त्यस्याश्रमं दिव्यमन्वेष्टुं स्वसखीजनम्॥
en: But searching for my associates, I had ere this alone repaired to the noble asylum of the Maharși Pulastya of a purified spirit.

sn: न च पश्याम्यहं तत्र कांचिदभ्यागतां सखीम्। रूपस्य तु विपर्यासं दृष्ट्वा त्रासादिहागता॥
en: But associate found there I none, that had come thither. And seeing this change for the worse of my form, I from fear have come hither.

sn: तृणबिन्दुस्तु राजर्षिस्तपसा द्योतितप्रभः। ध्यानं विवेश तच्चापि अपश्यदृषिकर्मजम्॥
en: Thereat the Rajarsi, Trinabindu, having a live effulgence through asceticism, entered into contemplation, and saw the consequence of the sage's act.

sn: स तु विज्ञाय तं शापं महर्षे वितात्मनः। गृहीत्वा तनयां गत्वा पुलस्त्यमिदमब्रवीत्॥
en: And coming to know that curse of the Maharși of a purified spirit, he, taking his daughter, went to Pulastya and said.

sn: भगवंस्तनयां मे त्वं गुणैः स्वैरेव भूषिताम्। भिक्षां प्रतिगृहाणेमां महर्षे स्वयमुद्यताम्॥
en: O worshipful one, O mighty sage, do you accept this daughter of mine, adorned with her native perfections, who of herself has come to you as alms.

sn: तपश्चरणयुक्तस्य श्राम्यमाणेन्द्रिस्य ते। शुश्रूषणपरा नित्यं भविष्यति न संशयः॥
en: She will, without doubt, constantly tend you, practising asceticism, and having your senses fatigued.

sn: तं ब्रुवाणं तु तद्वाक्यं राजर्षि धार्मिकं तदा। जिघृक्षुरब्रवीत्कन्यां बाढमित्येव स द्विजः॥
en: When that virtuous (sage) had said this, the twice-born Räjarși, desirous of accepting the girl (after due nuptial rights), said to the former, 'Well !'

sn: दत्त्वा तु तनयां राजा स्वमाश्रमपदं गतः। सापि तत्रावसत्कन्या तोषयन्ती पतिं गुणैः॥
en: Having given away his daughter, the king went (back) to his asylum; and the girl stayed there, gratifying her husband with her virtues.

sn: तस्यास्तु शीलवृत्ताभ्यां तुतोष मुनिपुङ्गवः। प्रीतः स तु महातेजा वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह॥
en: And that best of ascetics was gratified with her character and behaviour. And well pleased (with her), that highly energetic one said.

sn: परितुष्टोऽस्मि सुश्रोणि गुणानां संपदा भृशम्। तस्माद्देवि ददाम्यद्य पुत्रमात्मसमं तव। उभयोवंशकर्तारं पौलस्त्य इति विश्रुतम्॥
en: 'O you of shapely hips, well-pleased am I with you with your wealth of worth, and therefore, O exalted one, I will today confer on you a son like to yourself, who will perpetuate both the lines*-being celebrated as Paulastya. *(i.e. maternal and paternal lines.)

sn: यस्मात्तु विश्रुतो वेदस्त्वयेहाध्ययतो मम। तस्मात्स विश्रवा नाम भविष्यति न संशयः॥
en: And as you had heard the Veda recited by me, so, without doubt, he shall be named Visravā.* *(From the root, Śru-to hear.)

sn: एवमुक्ता तु सा देवी प्रहृष्टेनान्तरात्मना। अचिरेणैव कालेनासूत विश्रवसं सुतम्। त्रिषु लोकेषु विख्यातं यशोधर्मसमन्वितम्॥ श्रुतिमान्समदर्शी च व्रताचाररतस्तथा। पितेव तपसा युक्तो अभवद्विश्रवा मुनिः॥
en: Thus addressed, that noble damsel with her soul wrought with delight, in a short time brought forth her son Visravā, famed over the three worlds and furnished with virtue and fame: versed in the Vedas, of an impartial spirit, and ever engaged in observing vows. And the ascetic, Viśravă, was furnished with asceticism even like his sire. ever

sn: अथ पुत्रः पुलस्त्यस्य विश्रवा मुनिपुङ्गवः। अचिरेणैव कालेन पितेव तपसि स्थितः॥
en: Pulastya's son-that prime of ascetics-Visravāin a short time was engaged in asceticism like his father.

sn: सत्यवाञ्शीलवान्दान्तः स्वाध्यायनिरतः शुचि। सर्वभोगेष्वसंसक्तो नित्यं धर्मपरायणः॥
en: And he was truthful, and of excellent character and controlled senses; was engaged in the study of the Vedas; and was of the sanctified spirit; and he was not addicted to any of the pleasures of life, and was always studious of religion.

sn: ज्ञात्वा तस्य तु तद्वृत्तं भरद्वाजो महामुनिः। ददौ विश्रवसे भार्यां स्वसुतां देववर्णिनीम्॥ प्रतिगृह्य तु धर्मेण भरद्वाजसुतां तदा। प्रजान्वीक्षिकया बुद्ध्या श्रेयो ह्यस्य विचिन्तयन्॥ मुदा परमया युक्तो विश्रवा मुनिपुङ्गवः। स तस्यां वीर्यसंपन्नमपत्यं परमाद्भुतम्॥ जनयामास धर्मज्ञः सर्वैर्ब्रह्मगुणैर्वृतम्। तस्मिञ्जाते तु संहृष्टः स बभूव पितामहः॥ दृष्ट्वा श्रेयस्करी बुद्धिं धनाध्यक्षो भविष्यति। नाम चास्याकरोत्प्रीतः सार्धं देवर्षिभिस्तदा॥ यस्माद्विश्रवसोऽपत्यं सादृश्याद्विश्रवा इव। तस्माद्वैश्रवणो नाम भविष्यत्येष विश्रुतः॥
en: Learning of his ways, that mighty ascetic, Bharadvāja, gave to Visravā for his wife, his daughter, Devavarņinſ. And having religiously wed Bhāradvāja's daughter, that foremost of ascetics, Visravā, conceiving the highest delight, began to reflect on the welfare of his offspring with an intelligence concentrated on them. And on her that one cognisant of righteousness begot child, exceedingly wonderful, endowed with energy, and adorned with all Brahma* qualities. On his having been born, his grand-father was rejoiced, and, marking the profitable intelligence (of the boy, he thought that) he would be the lord of riches. And well-pleased, (Pulastya) in company with the Devarsis (thought), Inasmuch as this is Viśravá's offspring, and as he resembles Viśravā himself, so he should be known by the name of Vaisravana. own a *Such as self-control, asceticism, purity, etc.

sn: स तु वैश्रवणस्तत्र तपोवनगतस्तदा। अवर्धताहुतिहुतो महातेजा यथानलः॥
en: Then the exceedingly energetic Vaiśravana, repairing to the wood of asceticism, increased in power) like to a fire fed by sacrificial oblations.

sn: तस्याश्रमपदस्थस्य बुद्धिर्जज्ञे महात्मनः। चरिष्ये परमं धर्म धर्मो हि परमा गतिः॥
en: And as he was staying in the hermitage, that high-souled one thought, 'I shall practice prime righteousness: verily virtue is the supreme way.'

sn: स तु वर्षसहस्राणि तपस्तप्त्वा महावने। यन्त्रितो नियमैरुप्रैश्चकार सुमहत्तपः॥
en: For a thousand years, he, having his senses controlled, practised rigid austerities in that mighty forest, observing (all the while) the most rigorous restrictions.

sn: पूर्णे वर्षसहस्रान्ते तं तं विधिमकल्पयत्। जलाशी मारुताहारो निराहारस्तथैव च। एवं वर्षसहस्राणि जग्मुस्तान्येकवर्षवत्॥
en: And on a thousand years having been numbered, he by turns observed the rules relative to each term; (at first) living on water, (then) on air, and (last) going absolutely without any food. Thus passed away a thousand years like one.

sn: अथ प्रीतो महातेजाः सेन्द्रैः सुरगणैः सह। गत्वा तस्याश्रमपदं ब्रह्मेदं वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥ परितुष्टोऽस्मि ते वत्स कर्मणानेन सुव्रत। वरं वृणीष्व भद्रं ते वराहस्त्वं महामते॥
en: Then the highly energetic Brahmā along with the Indra and the celestials, coming to that asylum, addressed (Vaisravana), saying, '0 child, I am well-pleased with you for this act of your, O you of excellent vows. Do you, good betide you, ask for the 'boon (that you would have), for, O magnanimous one, you are worthy of a boon.'

sn: अथाब्रवीद्वैश्रवणः पितामहमुपस्थितम्। भगवॅल्लोकपालत्वमिच्छेयं लोकरक्षणम्॥
en: Then Vaisravaņa said to the Pitāmaha, who was present, 'O reverend one, I crave for the power of maintaining and protecting people.'

sn: अथाब्रवीद्वैश्रवणं परितुष्टेन चेतसा। ब्रह्मा सुरगणैः सार्धं बाढमित्येव हृष्टवत्॥
en: Thereat, Brahmä along with the deities gladly said to Vaiśravana in a gratified spirit, Very well!

sn: अहं वै लोकपालानां चतुर्थं स्रष्टुमुद्यतः। यमेन्द्रवरुणानां च पदं यत्तव चेप्सितम्॥
en: I am about to create the fourth of the Protectors of the creatures-Yama, Indra and Varuna, the position which is sought for by you.

sn: तद्गच्छ बत धर्मज्ञ निधीशत्वमवाप्नुहि । शक्राम्बुपयमानां च चतुर्थस्त्वं भविष्यसि ॥
en: Do you, O you cognisant of righteousness, attain the same; do you receive the position of the lord of riches. You shall be the fourth among the Sakra, the lord of waters, etc.

sn: एतच्च पुष्पकं नाम विमानं सूर्यसंनिभम्। प्रतिगृह्णीष्व यानार्थं त्रिदशैः समतां व्रज॥
en: Do you take for your vehicle this car, named Puşpaka, resembling the Sun himself, and thus raise yourself to an equality with the celestials.

sn: स्वस्ति तेऽस्तु गमिष्यामः सर्व एव यथागतम्। कृतकृत्या वयं तात दत्त्वा तव वरद्वयम्॥
en: Good betide you! We shall (now) go whither we had come, having, my child, done my duty and bestowed on you the couple of boons.

sn: इत्युक्त्वा स गतो ब्रह्मा स्वस्थानं त्रिदशैः सह। गतेषु ब्रह्मपूर्वेषु देवेष्वथ नभस्तलम्॥ धनेशः पितरं प्राह प्राञ्जलिः प्रयतात्मवान्। भगवल्लब्धवानस्मि वरमिष्टं पितामहात्॥ निवासनं न मे देवो विदधे स प्रजापतिः। तं पश्य भगवन्कंचिनिवासं साधु मे प्रभो। न च पीडा भवेद्यत्र प्राणिनो यस्य कस्यचित्।।२३ एवमुक्तस्तु पुत्रेण विश्रवा मुनिपुङ्गवः। वचनं प्राह धर्मज्ञ श्रूयतामिति सत्तम॥
en: Having said this, Brahmă along with the celestials went to his own quarters. On the deities with Brahmã at their head, having departed foe the heavenly regions, the selfpossessed lord of wealth of subdued senses with joined hands spoke to his sire, saying, 'o reverend one, I have received the wished-for boon from the great-father, but the exalted lord of creatures has not fixed any abode for me. Therefore, O lord, do you seek out some dwelling for me, where no creature whatever can come by misfortune. Thus accosted by his son, that best of ascetics, Viśravä, spoke, O righteous one,' Listen! O excellent one.

sn: दक्षिणस्योदधेस्तीरे त्रिकूटो नाम पर्वतः। तस्याने तु विशाला सा महेन्द्रस्य पुरी यथा॥ लङ्का नाम पुरी रम्या निर्मिता विश्वकर्मणा। राक्षसानां निवासार्थं यथेन्द्रस्यामरावती॥ तब त्वं वस भद्रं ते लङ्कायां नात्र संशयः। हेमप्राकारपरिखा यन्त्रशस्त्रसमावृता॥ रमणीया पुरी सा हि रुक्मवैदूर्यतोरणा।
en: On the shore of the Southern sea there is a mount named Trikūta. On its brow is a beautiful and broad city built by Viśvakarmā, named Lankā, resembling the city itself of Indra the great, designed for the abode of Rākşasas, like to the Amaravati of Indra. There in Lanka, do you, forsooth, reside. That romantic city is surrounded with a golden wall and a moat, and is furnished with engines and weapons, and has gateways of gold and lapises.

sn: राक्षसैः सा परित्यक्ता पुरा विष्णुभयार्दितैः॥ शून्या रक्षोगणैः सर्वै रसातलतलं गतः। शून्या संप्रति लङ्का सा प्रभुस्तस्या न विद्यते॥ स त्वं तत्र निवासाय गच्छ पुत्र यथासुखम्। निर्दोषस्तत्र ते वासो न बाधस्तत्र कस्यचित् ॥
en: Formerly she was renounced by the Raksasas afflicted with the fear of Vişnu; and was empty of swarms of Rākşasa, who had gone to the nethermost regions. Now Lanka is vacant, and there is no one that lords it over her. Do you, my child, for abode, at your ease repair thither. Your stay there shall meet with no rub, and no manner of disturbance shall occur there.

sn: एतच्छुत्वा स धर्मात्मा धर्मिष्ठं वचनं पितुः। निवासयामास तदा लङ्कां पर्वतमूर्धनि ॥
en: Hearing the righteous speech of his sire, that virtuous-souled one along with thousands of delighted and joyous Rākşasas, began to reside in Lanka stationed on the ion of the mount.

sn: नैर्ऋतानां सहस्रैस्तु हृष्टैः प्रमुदितैः सदा। अचिरेणैव कालेन संपूर्णा तस्य शासनात्॥ स तु तत्रावसत्प्रीतो धर्मात्मा नैर्ऋतर्षभः। समुद्रपरिखायां स लङ्कायां विश्रवात्मजः॥
en: In a short time (Lankā), through his sway, abounded (in wealth). And that foremost of Nairtas, the righteous-son of Visrava, wellpleased, abode in Lankā having the Ocean for her entrenchment.

sn: काले काले तु धर्मात्मा पुष्पकेण धनेश्वरः। अभ्यागच्छद्विनीतात्मा पितरं मातरं च हि ॥
en: At times the righteous-souled lord of riches, mounted on Pușpaka, in humble guise visited his father and mother.

sn: स्तथाप्सरोनृत्यबिभूषितालयः। गभस्तिभिः सूर्य इवावभासयन् पितुः समीपं प्रययौ स वित्तपः॥
en: And hymned by hosts of deities and Gandharvas, having his mansion graced with the dancing of Apsarās, and floating on rays like the sun himself, that ruler of riches went to his sire.

sn: श्रुत्वागस्त्येरितं वाक्यं रामो विस्मयमागतः। कथमासीत्तु लङ्कायां संभवो रक्षसां पुरा॥
en: Hearing the words uttered by Agastya, Răma wondered as to how formerly Rākşasas were generated in Lanka.

sn: ततः शिरः कम्पयित्वा त्रेताग्निसमविग्रहम्। तमगस्त्यं मुहुर्दृष्ट्वा स्मयमानोऽभ्यभाषत ॥
en: Then shaking his head, he, struck with wonder, momentarily eyeing Agastya, addressed Agastya resembling fire, saying.

sn: भगवन्पूर्वमप्येषा लङ्कासीत्पिशिताशिनाम्। श्रुत्वेदं भगवद्वाक्यं जातो मे विस्मयः परः॥
en: O worshipful one, hearing your words that formerly Lankā had been in the possession of the flesh-eaters, I have been seized with great amazement.

sn: पुलस्त्यवंशादुद्भूता राक्षसा इति नः श्रुतम्। इदानीमन्यतश्चापि संभवः कीर्तितस्त्वया॥
en: We had heard that the Rākṣasas had sprung in the race of Pulastya. But now you have said that they owe their origin to a different source.

sn: रावणात्कुम्भकर्णाच्च प्रहस्ताद्विकटादपि। रावणस्य च पुत्रेभ्यः किं नु ते बलवत्तराः॥
en: But were they more powerful than Rāvana, Kumbhakarma and Prahasta and Vikața and the sons of Rāvana?

sn: क एषां पूर्वको ब्रह्मन्किनामा च बलोत्कटः। अपराधं च कं प्राप्य विष्णुना द्राविताः कथम्॥
en: Who was their progenitor? And what was the name of that terrific strength? And through what transgression were they driven out by Vişnu?

sn: एतद्विस्तारतः सर्वं कथयस्व ममानघ । कुतूहलमिदं मह्यं नुद भानुर्यथा तमः।७।।
en: All this, O sinless one, do you tell me in detail, and do you dispel my curiosity even as the sun dispels darkness.

sn: राघवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा संस्कारालंकृतं शुभम्। अथ विस्मयमानस्तमगस्त्यः प्राह राघवम्॥
en: Hearing Rāghava's words, fair and fraught with polished phrase and period, Agastya, struck with surprise, said to Rāghava.

sn: प्रजापतिः पुरा सृष्ट्वा अपः सलिलसंभवः। तासां गोपायने सत्त्वानसृजत्पद्मसंभवः॥
en: The lord of creatures sprang from water, first created water. And the lotus-born one generated creatures for protecting that element.

sn: ते सत्त्वाः सत्त्वकर्तारं विनीतवदुपस्थिताः। किं कुर्म इति भाषन्तः क्षुत्पिपासाभयार्दिताः॥
en: Thereupon those creatures humbly presented themselves before the creator, saying, What shall we do? We are sore tried by hunger and thirst.

sn: प्रजापतिस्तु तान्सर्वान्प्रत्याह प्रहसन्निव। आभाष्य वाचा यत्नेन रक्षध्वमिति मानवाः॥
en: The lord of creatures, laughing, addressed them, saying, “You men, do you carefully guard this (water).”

sn: रक्षाम इति तत्रान्यैर्यक्षाम इति चापरैः। @क्षिता क्षितैरुक्तस्ततस्तानाह भूतकृतः॥
en: Thereat some said 'Raksama,' (i.e. we shall protect.) and others 'Yaksāma.' (We shall worship.) Thus accosted by those afflicted with hunger and thirst, the creator said.

sn: रक्षाम इति यैरुक्तं राक्षसास्ते भवन्तु वः। रक्षाम इति यैरुक्तं यक्षा एव भवन्तु वः॥
en: Those among you who have said 'Raksama,' shall be Raksasas; and those among you, who have said 'Yaksama' shall be Yaksas.

sn: तत्र हेतिः प्रहेतिश्च भ्रातरौ राक्षसाधिपौ। मधुकैटभसंकाशौ बभूवतुररिंदमौ ॥
en: And there sprang the brothers-repressors of foes-Heti and Praheti lords of Raksasas, resembling Madhu Kaitabha himself.

sn: प्रहेतिरर्धार्मिकस्तत्र तपोवनगतस्तदा। हेतिरक्रियार्थे तु परं यत्नमथाकरोत्॥
en: Praheti, who was righteous, went to the wood of asceticism. And Heti exerted himself to the utmost to get himself wived.

sn: स कालभगिनीं कन्यां भयां नाम महाभयाम्। उदावहदमेयात्मा स्वयमेव महामतिः॥
en: And that magnanimous one of immeasurable soul married the exceedingly terrific sister of Kala, named Bhayā (Fear.)

sn: स तस्यां जनयामास हेती राक्षसपुङ्गवः। पुत्र पुत्रवतां श्रेष्ठो विद्युत्केशमिति श्रुतम्॥
en: And on her Heti-foremost of Rākşasas and best of those having sons-beget a son, known as Vidyutkeśa.

sn: विद्युत्केशो हेतिपुत्रः स दीप्तार्कसमप्रभः। व्यवर्धत महातेजास्तोयमध्य इवाम्बुजम् ॥
en: Heti's son, the exceedingly energetic Vidyutkeśa, possessed of the splendour of the sun, grew up even like a lotus in water.

sn: स यदा यौवनं भद्रमनुप्राप्तो निशाचरः। ततो दारक्रियां तस्य कर्तुं व्यवसितः पिता॥
en: And when that night-ranger arrived at proper youth, his sire turned his attention towards his marriage.

sn: संध्यादुहितरं सोऽथ संध्यातुल्यां प्रभावतः। वरयामास पुत्रार्थ हेती राक्षसपुङ्गवः॥
en: And that best of Rākṣasas-heti-in the interests of his son asked for the hand of Sandhya's daughter; like to Sandhyā* herself in the potency. * The evening Twilight-spouse of the Sun.

sn: अवश्यमेव दातव्या परस्मै सेति संध्यया। चिन्तयित्वा सुता दत्ता विद्युत्केशाय राघव ।।२१ संध्यायास्तनयां लब्ध्वा विद्युत्केशो निशाचरः। रमते स तया साधं पौलोम्या मघवानिव॥
en: Sandhya, reflecting that she needs must have to be given away by her, bestowed her on Vidyutkesa, O Raghava. Having obtained Sandhya's daughter, the night-ranger Vidyutkeśa, sports with her even as Maghavan does with the daughter of Puloma.

sn: केनचित्त्वथ कालेन राम सालकटङ्कटा। विद्युत्केशाद्गर्भमाप घनराजिरिवार्णवात्॥
en: It came to pass that after a length of time, O Răma, Sälakatankata was filled with child by Vidyutkeśa, as the clouds are furnished with water by the Ocean,

sn: ततः सा राक्षसी गर्भ घनगर्भसमप्रभम्। प्रसूता मन्दरं गत्वा गङ्गा गर्भमिवाग्निजम्। समुत्सृज्य तु सा गर्भ विद्युत्केशरतार्थिनी॥
en: Then repairing to Mandara, the Rākşasi brought forth her child, having the splendour of rain-charged clouds; even as Gangā had delivered herself of the child begotten by fire.* And having delivered herself of her offspring, she again became bent on disporting with Vidyutkeśa. *Mahesvara.

sn: रेमे तु सार्धं पतिना विसृज्य सुतमात्मजम् । उत्सृष्टस्तु तदा गर्भो घनशब्दसमस्वनः॥
en: Then forsaking her son, she began to sport with her husband; and the child having sounds resembling the rumbling of clouds, was renounced (by his mother).

sn: तयोत्सृष्टः स तु शिशुः शरदर्कसमद्युतिः। निधायास्ये स्वयं मुष्टिं रुरोद शनकैस्तदा॥
en: And forsaken by them both, the infant furnished with the brightness of the autumnal sun, entering his clenched fist into his mouth, began to cry slowly.

sn: ततो वृषभमास्थाय पार्वत्या सहितः शिवः। वायुमार्गेण गच्छन्वै शुश्राव रुदितस्वनम्॥
en: It so fell that, journeying with Parvati, Siva, riding his bull through the serial regions, heard the sounds of weeping, on

sn: अपश्यदुमया सार्धं रुदन्तं राक्षसात्मजम्। कारुण्यभावात्पार्वत्या भवस्त्रिपुरसूदनः॥ तं राक्षसात्मजं चक्रे मातुरेव वयःसमम्। अमरं चैव तं कृत्वा महादेवोऽक्षरोऽव्ययः॥ पुरमाकाशगं प्रादात्पार्वत्याः प्रियकाम्यया।
en: Along with Uma, he saw the Raksasas's son, as he was crying. And sent by Pārvatī, whose heart was moved by by compassion, Bhava destroyer of Tripura-made that Raksasa's offspring attain the age of his mother, and conferred him immortality. And for compassing Parvati's pleasure, Mahadeva, indestructible and undeteriorating granted (the Raksasa) the power of ranging the air.

sn: उभयापि वरो दत्तो राक्षसीनां नृपात्मज॥ सद्योपलब्धिर्गर्भस्य प्रसूतिः सद्य एव च। सद्य एव वय:प्राप्ति मातुरेव वयःसमम्॥
en: O son of the king, Umă also bestowed a boon: “Henceforth the Rāksasis shall conceive in a day, bring forth (child) in a day, and the child shall in a day be furnished with the age of its mother.'

sn: ततः सुकेशो वरदानगर्वितः श्रियं प्रभोः प्राप्य हरस्य पार्श्वतः। चचार सर्वत्र महान्महामतिः खगं पुरं प्राप्य पुरंदरो यथा।॥
en: Then the great and magnanimous Sukeśa, puffed up with the receipt of boons, having obtained auspiciousness at the hands of the lord, Hara, began to range everywhere, even as Purandara did on having obtained heaven.

sn: सुकेशं धार्मिकं दृष्ट्वा वरलब्धं च राक्षसम्। ग्रामणी म गन्धर्वो विश्वावसुसमप्रभः॥ तस्य देववती नाम द्वितीया श्रीरिवात्मजा। त्रिषु लोकेषु विख्याता रूपयौवनशालिनी॥ तां सुकेशाय धर्मात्मा ददौ रक्षः श्रियं यथा।
en: Cveing Sukeśa righteous and furnished with the boon, a virtuous Gandharva, named Grāmani, of the effulgence of fire, who had a daughter, called Devavati, like to a second Sri herself, famed over the three worlds, and endowed with beauty and youth, bestowed her on Sukeśa as if he had bestowed the goddess of fortune of the Rākşasa.

sn: वरदानकृतैश्वर्यं सा तं प्राप्य पति प्रियम्॥ आसीद्देववती तुष्टा धनं प्राप्येव निर्धनः। स तया सह संयुक्तो रराज रजनीचरः॥ अञ्जनादभिनिष्क्रान्तः करेण्वेव महागजः।
en: And like an indigent person on obtaining wealth, Devavati, on obtaining her beloved husband, affluent in consequence of having received the boon, was (greatly) delighted. And in her company, that night-ranger appeared graceful, even as a mighty elephant sprung from Añjanā* does in the company of a she-elephant. *The designation of an elephant.

sn: ततः काले सुकेशस्तु जनयामास राघव। चीन् पुत्रान् जनयामास त्रेताग्निसमविग्रहान्॥
en: In good time Sukesa, O Raghava, begot (on her) three sons, resembling the bodies of the three Fires.

sn: माल्यवन्तं सुमालिं च मालिं च बलिनां वरम्। त्रीत्रिनेत्रसमान्पुत्राराक्षसानराक्षसाधिपः॥ त्रयो लोका इवाव्यग्राः स्थितास्त्रयः इवाग्नयः। यो मन्त्रा इवात्युग्रास्त्रयो घोरा इवामयाः।७।।
en: That lord of Rākşasas begot (on her) three sons, resembling his three eyes the Raksasas, Mālyavän, Sumāli and that foremost of the strong-Māli; all resembling the three worlds possessing themselves in calmness; like to the three Fires established; fierce like to the three mantras, dreadful like three diseases springing respectively from morbid Air, Bile and Phlegm.* *The entire edifice of Hindu Pathology is based on the three-fold division of the morbid humours into Air, Bile and Phlegm. This division, albeit it may appear crude and unscientific to Europeans, taken all, in all, wonderfully answers its purpose. The tact displayed by Hindu physicians in diagnosing diseases on this method is wonderful. From feeling the Pulse alone, a Hindu physician, getting at the predominance of one or more morbid humours of the system, can accurately ascertain a patient's health. The infallibility with which predictions of death are generally made, attests the scientific soundness of the division in question, and renders superfluous any elaborate argument in its defence.

sn: त्रयः सुकेशस्य सुतास्त्रेताग्निसमतेजसः। विवृद्धिमगमंस्तत्र व्याधयोपेक्षिता इव ॥
en: The three sons of Sukeśa, having the energy of the three fires, grew up like a disease which has been disregarded.

sn: वरप्राप्ति पितुस्ते तु ज्ञात्वैश्वर्यं तपोबलात्। तपस्तप्तुं गता मेरुं भ्रातरः कृतनिश्चयाः॥
en: And learning that their father had received a boon by virtue of his power proceeding from asceticism, the brothers, firmly resolved, went to Meru for practising penances.

sn: प्रगृह्य नियमान्धोराराक्षसा नृपसत्तम। विचेरुस्ते तपो घोरं सर्वभूतभयावहम्॥
en: And adopting rigid restrictions, the Rākṣasas, O best of kings, entered upon austerities, terrible, and capable of arousing the fear of all beings.

sn: सत्यार्जवशमोपेतैस्तपोभिर्भुवि दुर्लभैः। संतापयन्तस्त्रील्लोकान्सदेवासुरमानुषान्॥
en: Practising penances rare on the earth with truth and candour and self-control, they afflicted the three worlds with gods, Asuras and human beings.

sn: ततो विभुश्चतुर्वक्रो विमानवरमाश्रितः। सुकेशपुत्रानामन्त्र्य वरदोऽस्मीत्यभाषत॥
en: Then that lord-the four-faced one-stationed on a superb car, addressed Sukeśa's sons, saying, “I am for conferring boons (on you).'

sn: ब्रह्माणं वरदं ज्ञात्वा सेन्ट्रैर्देवगणैर्वृतम्। ऊचुः प्राञ्जलयः सर्वे वेपमाना इव दुमाः॥
en: Knowing that Brahmā surrounded by Indra and the other celestials was ready to bestow boons, they, with joined hands, said, trembling like trees.

sn: तपसाराधितो देव यदि नो दिशसे वरम्। अजेयाः शत्रुहन्तारस्तथैव चिरजीविनः। प्रभविष्ण्वो भवामेति परस्परमनुव्रताः॥
en: O god! that have been adored through asceticism, if you do intend to confer on us a boon, let us be invincible, capable of slaying foes, immortal, lordly, and ever devoted to each other.'

sn: एवं भविष्यथेत्युक्त्वा सुकेशतनयान्विभुः। स ययौ ब्रह्मलोकाय ब्रह्मा ब्राह्मणवत्सलः॥ वरं लब्ध्वा तु ते सर्वे राम रात्रिंचरास्तदा। सुरासुरान्प्रबाधन्ते वरदानसुनिर्भयाः॥
en: Thereat saying 'So be it,' to the sons of Sukeśa, the lord Brahmā, (ever) cherishing Brāhmaṇas with affection, went to the Brahmā regions. O Rāma, having obtained the boons, those night-rangers, rendered intrepid in consequences of having the boon conferred on them, began to disturb celestials and Asuras.

sn: तैर्बाध्यमानास्त्रिदशाः सर्षिसङ्घाः सचारणाः। त्रातारं नाधिगच्छन्ति निरयस्था यथा नराः॥ अथ ते विश्वकर्माणं शिल्पिनां वरमव्ययम्। ऊचुः समेत्य संहृष्टा राक्षसा रघुसत्तम॥
en: And like to men abiding in hell, the celestials, chāraṇas and hosts of sages, being harassed (by Raksasas), did not find any deliverer. And then, O foremost of the Raghus, the Raksasas, assembled together, joyfully said to the undeteriorating Viśvakarmá—prince of artist.

sn: ओजस्तेजोबलवतां महतामात्मतेजसा। गृहकर्ता भवानेव देवानां हृदयेप्सितम्॥ अस्माकमपि तावत्त्वं गृहं कुरु महामते। हिमवन्तमुपाश्रित्य मेरुमन्दरमेव वा॥ महेश्वरगृहप्रख्यं गृहं नः क्रियतां महत्। विश्वकर्मा ततस्तेषां राक्षसानां महाभुजः॥ निवासं कथयामास शक्रस्येवामरावतीम्।
en: 'You by your own energy are the architect of the great gods, endowed with energy and prowess and strength. Do you, O magnanimous one, construct a fabric for us after our heart hard by Himavān, or Meru, or Mandara. And do you erect a magnificent mansion for us resembling the mansion itself of Maheśvara.' Thereat Viśvakarmā the mighty-arm of the Rākṣasas spoke of a building like the Amarāvati of Sakra.

sn: दक्षिणस्योदधेस्तीरे त्रिकूटो नाम पर्वतः॥ सुवेल इति चाप्यन्यो द्वितीयो राक्षसेश्वराः।
en: 'On the shore of the Southern sea is a mountain named Trikūța. A second also is there called Suvela, you lords of Raksasas.

sn: शिखरे तस्य शैलस्य मध्यमेऽम्बुदसंनिभे॥ शकुनैरपि दुष्प्रापे टङ्कच्छिन्नचतुर्दिशि। त्रिंशद्योजनविस्तीर्णा शतयोजनमायता॥ स्वर्णप्राकारसंवीता हेमतोरणसंवृता। मया लङ्केति नगरी शक्याज्ञप्तेन निर्मिता ॥
en: On the midmost peak of that mountain resembling clouds, inaccessible even to the fowls of the air, all the four quarters have been hewn with bones.* If I am desired by you, I can construct the city of Lanka (there), having an area of thirty Yojanas, and measuring an hundred in length; surrounded with a golden wall and furnished with golden gateways. *Tanka-may also mean a hatchet or a sword.

sn: तस्यां वसत दुर्धर्षा यूयं राक्षसपुङ्गवाः। अमरावतीं समासाद्य सेन्द्रा इव दिवौकसः॥
en: In her do-you dwell, you irrepressible ones, you foremost of Rākşasas; even as do the elestials with Indra, approaching Amaravati.

sn: लङ्कादुर्गं समासाद्य राक्षसैर्बहुभिर्वृताः। भविष्यथ दुराधर्षाः शत्रूणां शत्रुसूदनाः॥
en: And occupying the citadel of Lankā, backed by innumerable Rākṣasas, you will be invincible to foes and capable of destroying them.'

sn: विश्वकर्मवचः श्रुत्वा ततस्ते राक्षसोत्तमाः। सहस्रानुचरा भूत्वा गत्वा तामवसन्पुरीम्॥ दृढप्राकारपरिखां हैमैहशतैर्वृताम्। लङ्कामवाप्य ते हृष्टा न्यवसन्रजनींचराः॥
en: Hearing Viśvakarmā's speech, those foremost of Rākṣasas, accompanied by thousands of followers, went to the palace and set-up in the same, having a strong wall and a moat, abounding in hundreds of golden edifices. And obtaining Lanka, the night-rangers, exceedingly delighted, began to dwell therein.

sn: एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु यथाकामं च राघव। नर्मदा नाम गन्धर्वी बभूव रघुनन्दन ॥ तस्याः कन्यात्रयं ह्यासीद्धीश्रीकिर्तिसमद्युति। ज्येष्ठक्रमेण सा तेषां राक्षसानामराक्षसी॥ कन्यास्ताः प्रददौ हृष्टा पूर्णचन्द्रनिभाननाः।
en: At this time, O Rāghava, there lived at her pleasure a Gandharvi, named Narmadā. O son of Raghu, She hai three daughters, resembling Sri, Hri, and kirti in splendour. And albeit no Rāks asi herself, she, beginning with the eldest, gladly married to the Räkşasas her daughter having faces resembling the full moon.

sn: त्रयाणां राक्षसेन्द्राणां तिस्रो गन्धर्वकन्यकाः॥ दत्ता मात्रा महाभागा नक्षत्रे भगदैवते।
en: And under the influence of the star, Bhagadaivata, those three exalted daughters of a Gandharvi were respectively conferred by their mother on the three several Raksasas of eminence.

sn: कृतदारास्तु ते राम सुकेशतनयास्तदा॥ चिक्रीडुः सह भाभिरप्सरोभिरिवामराः।
en: And having wedded, O Rama, Sukesa's sons began to sport with their wives, like celestials sporting with Apsarās.

sn: ततो माल्यवतो भार्या सुन्दरी नाम सुन्दरी।।३४ स तस्यां जनयामास यदपत्यं निबोध तत्।
en: Malyavän's beautiful spouse was named Sundari. On her he begot, do you understand, whom.

sn: वज्रमुष्टिविरूपाक्षोदुर्मुखश्चैव राक्षसः॥ सुप्तघ्नो यज्ञकोपश्च मत्तोन्मत्तौ तथैव च। अनला चाभवत्कन्या सुन्दयाँ राम सुन्दरी॥ सुमालिनोऽपि भार्यासीत्पूर्णचद्रनिभानना। नाम्ना केतुमती राम प्राणेभ्योऽपि गरीयसी।।३७
en: Vajramuşti, and Virūpākşa, and the Räksasa Durmukha, and Suptaghna, and Yajñakopa, and Matta and Unmatta; and, O Rāma, there was also born a lovely daughter of Sundari, Anala. And Sumāli's wife of face like the full Moon, named Ketumati, was dearer to him than his life itself.

sn: सुमाली जनयामास यदपत्यं निशाचरः। केतुमत्यां महाराज तन्निबोधानुपूर्वशः॥ प्रहस्तोऽकम्पनश्चैव विकटः कालिकामुखः। धूम्राक्षश्चैव दण्डश्च सुपार्श्वश्च महाबलः॥ संहादिः प्रघसश्चैव भासकर्णश्च राक्षसः। राका पुष्पोत्कटा चैव कैकसी च शुचिस्मिताः। कुम्भीनसी च इत्येते सुमालेः प्रसवाः स्मृताः॥ मालेस्तु वसुदा नाम गन्धर्वी रूपशालिनी। भार्यासीत्पद्मपत्राक्षी स्वक्षी यक्षीवरोपमा॥
en: O mighty king, do you, gradually, know the offspring that were begot by Sumāli on Ketumatī-Prahasta and Akampana, and Vikata, and Kālikāmukha, and DhumrāKșa, and Danda, and the redoubtable Supārsva, and Sañhrãi, and Praghasa, and the Rākşasa, Bhāsakarņa, and Rākā, and Pushpotkată, and Kaikasi of luminous smiles, and Kumbhinasi these are known as the offspring of Sumali. Māli had for wife a graceful Gandharvi, named Vasudă having having eyes resembling lotus-petals, of a lovely look and like to the most magnificent Yakși of them all.

sn: सुमालेरनुजस्तस्यां जनयामास यत्प्रभो। अपत्यं कथ्यमानं तु मया त्वं शृणु राघव।॥ अनलथानिलचैव हरः संपातिरेव च। एते बिभीषणामात्या मालेयास्ते निशाचराः॥
en: Do you, O master, listen to me as I mention to you, O Raghava the offspring that Sumali's younger brother beget on her, Anala, and Nila, and Sampāti. These night-rangers sons to Mali were the courtiers of Vibhișana.

sn: ततस्तु ते राक्षसपुङ्गवास्त्रयो निशाचरैः पुत्रशतैश्च संवृता। सुरान्सहेन्द्रानृषिनागयक्षान् बबाधिरे तान्बहुवीर्यदर्पिताः॥
en: And those three foremost of Rākṣasa, accompanied by hundreds of sons night rangers all-elated on account of their measureless prowess, began to worry the sages and serpents and Yakşas, and celestials with Indra (at their head).

sn: जगभ्रमन्तोऽनिलवद्दुरासदा रणेषु मृत्युप्रतिमानतेजसः। वरप्रदानादपि गर्विता भृशं क्रतुक्रियाणां प्रशमंकराः सदा॥
en: Incapable of being confronted (in battle), these resembling Death himself in energy, wondrous elated in consequences of the boon having been conferred on them, ranging the world like to the Wind, were ever engaged in disturbing the sacrifices (of the sages).

sn: तैर्वध्यमाना देवाश्च ऋषयश्च तपोधनाः। भयार्ताः शरणं जग्मुर्देवदेवं महेश्वरम्॥ जगत्सृष्ट्यन्तकर्तारमजमव्यक्तरूपिणम्। आधारं सर्वलोकानामाराध्यं परमं गुरुम्॥ ते समेत्य तु कामारिं त्रिपुरारं त्रिलोचनम्। ऊचुः प्राञ्जलयो देवा भयगद्गदभाषिणः॥
en: Thus afflicted, the deities, sages, and ascetics, wrought up with fear, sought the protection of that god of gods Maheswara creator and destroyer of the cosmos, unborn, of an unmanifest form, the stay of all creatures, worthy of being adored, and the . supreme preceptors (of all). And coming to that enemy of Kama* and foc of Tripura the three-eyed (Deity), the gods with their voices faltering through fear, represented with joined hands. *The Hindu Cupid. Mahadeva had burnt to ashes Kama, when he had the fool-hardiness to disturb the contemplation of the former. By the way, Kalidasa has cared his faery fabric, entitled Kumāra Sambhava, on the basis of this legend.

sn: सुकेशपुत्रैर्भगवन्पितामहवरोद्धतैः। प्रजाध्यक्ष प्रजाः सर्वा बाध्यन्ते रिपुबाधनैः॥ शरणान्यशरण्यानि आश्रमाणि कृतानि नः। स्वर्गाच्च देवान्प्रच्याव्य स्वर्गे क्रीडन्ति देववत्॥
en: O reverend one, the creatures of the lord of creatures are being (sorely) troubled by the sons of Sukesa, given to harassing their foes,-swolen with insolence on account of the benn conferred on them by the great-father, asylums, constituting our refuges,-have been divested of their power of granting shelter, and driving off the deities from the etherial regions, they are sporting there like the immortals.

sn: अहं विष्णुरहं रुद्रो ब्रह्माहं देवराडहम्। अहं यमश्च वरुणश्चन्द्रोऽहं रविरप्यहम्॥ इति माली सुमाली च माल्यवांश्चैव राक्षसाः। बाधन्ते समरोद्धर्षा ये च तेषां पुरःसराः॥
en: 'I am Vişnu,' 'I am Rudra,' 'I am the king of the celestials,' 'I am Yama,' 'I an Varuna,' 'I am the moon,' 'I am the Sun,' flattering themselves in this fashion, Māli and Sumāli and the Rākşasa Malyavān as well as those going before them, are annoying (the gods), breathing exhilaration of martial spirits.

sn: तन्नो देव भयार्तानामभयं दातुमर्हसि। अशिवं वपुरास्थाय जहि वै देवकण्टकान्॥
en: Therefore, O god, it behove you to liberate us from fear, who have been greatly tormented by it. Do you, assuming your terrific form, slay the thorns of the celestials.

sn: इत्युक्तस्तु सुरैः सर्वैः कपर्दी नीललोहितः। सुकेशं प्रति सापेक्षः प्राह देवगणान्प्रभुः॥
en: Thus addressed by the immortals in a body, that lord, Kaparddi of red-blue hue, reflecting that it would be wrong for him to destroy Sukesa (with his own hands), spoke to the gods.

sn: अहं तान्न हनिष्यामि ममावध्या हि ते सुराः। किं तु मन्त्रं प्रदास्यामि यो वै तानिहनिष्यति ॥
en: I shall not slay them, you gods; they are incapable of being slain by me. But I shall unfold to you the way in which they will be destroyed.

sn: एतमेव समुद्योगं पुरस्कृत्य महर्षयः गच्छध्वं शरणं विष्णुं हनिष्यति स तान्प्रभुः॥
en: Do you, you Maharsis, in the heat of this affairs, seck the shelter of Visnu. That lord will slay them.

sn: ततस्तु जयशब्देन प्रतिनन्द्य महेश्वरम्। विष्णोः समीपमाजग्मुर्निशाचरभयार्दिताः॥
en: Thereat, saluting Maheśvara with the sounds of Jaya, (the celestial) afflicted with the fear of the night-rangers, presented themselves before Visnu.

sn: शङ्खचक्रधरं देवं प्रणम्य बहुमान्य च। ऊचुः संभ्रान्तवद्वाक्यं सुकेशतनयान्प्रति ॥
en: And bowing down to the god holding the conch, discus and mace, and paying him high homage, they, greatly flurried, addressed him about the sons of Sukeśa, saying.

sn: सुकेशतनयैर्देव त्रिभिस्त्रेताग्निसंनिभैः। आक्रम्य वरदानेन स्थानान्यपहतानि नः॥
en: O god, by virtue of the boon (that has been bestowed on them), resembling the three fires, Sukesa's three sons, assailing us, have deprived us of our abode.

sn: लङ्का नाम पुरी दुर्गा त्रिकूटशिखरे स्थिता। तत्र स्थिताः प्रबाधन्ते सर्वान्नः क्षणदाचराः॥
en: There is a city named Lankā, stationed on the top of Trikuta, (extremely) difficult of entrance. Taking up their station at that place, the nightrangers in a body pursue us.

sn: स त्वमस्मद्धितार्थाय जहि तान्मधुसूदन । शरणं त्वां वयं प्राप्ता गतिर्भव सुरेश्वर ॥
en: Do you, O slayer of Madhu, destroy them for our welfare. We have sought your shelter. Become our refuge, O foremost of celestials.

sn: चक्रकृत्तास्यकमलात्रिवेदय यमाय वै। भयेष्वभयदोऽस्माकं नान्योऽस्ति भवता विना॥
en: Do you dedicate to Yama the lotuses of their faces, severed (in pieces) with your discus. Save you, we have none who can, while tormented with fright, inspire us with courage.

sn: राक्षसान्समरे हृष्टान्सानुबन्धान्मदोद्धतान्। नुद त्वं नो भयं देव नीहारमिव भास्करः॥
en: Slay in encounter the elated Rākşasas along with their adherents; and even as the sun dried up dew, do you dispel this fear of ours.

sn: इत्येवं दैवतैरुक्तो देवदेवो जनार्दनः। अभयं भयदोऽरीणां दत्त्वा देवानुवाच ह॥
en: Thus accosted by the deities, that god of gods Janārdana who brings fear to foes cheering up the celestial up the celestials, said to them.

sn: सुकेशं राक्षसं जाने ईशानवरदर्पितम्। तांश्चास्य तनयाञ्जाने येषां ज्येष्ठः स माल्यवान्॥ तानहं समतिक्रान्तमर्यादानराक्षसाधमान्। निहनिष्यामि संक्रुद्धः सुरा भवत विज्वराः॥
en: 'I know the Raksasa, Sukesa, as flushed with the boon bestowed by Iśāna. And I also know his sons, of whom Mālyavān is the eldest. Those worst if Rākṣasas that have over-riden your dignity will I, wrought up with wrath, slay (in battle); therefore, you gods, be of good cheer.

sn: इत्युक्तास्ते सुराः सर्वे विष्णुना प्रभविष्णुना। यथावासं ययुर्हष्टाः प्रशंसन्तो जनार्दनम्॥
en: Thus addressed by the mighty Vişņu, the gods, highly rejoiced, went to their respective quarters, extolling Janārdana.

sn: विबुधानां समुद्योगं माल्यवांस्तु निशाचरः। श्रुत्वा तौ भ्रातरौ वीराविदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: And hearing of the activity of the celestials; the night-rangers Mālyavân addressed his heroic brothers, saying.

sn: अमरा ऋषयश्चैव संगम्य किल शंकरम्। अस्मद्वधं परीप्सन्त इदं वचनमब्रुवन्॥ सुकेशतनया देव वरदनाबलोद्धताः। बाधन्तेऽस्मान्समुद्रुप्ता घोररूपाः पदे पदे॥
en: The immortals and sages, going to Sankara, spoke these words, desirous of our destruction, The terrific sons of Sukeśa, puffed up, and swollen on account of their strength flowing from the boon, are crossing us at every step.

sn: राक्षसैरभिभूताः स्मो न शक्ताः स्म प्रजापते। स्वेषु सद्मसु संस्थातुं भयात्तेषां दुरात्मनाम्॥
en: We have been overpowered by the Rākṣasas. And, o lord of creatures, from fear of those wicked-minded ones, we cannot remain in our own homes.

sn: तदस्माकं हितार्थाय जहि तांश्च त्रिलोचन। राक्षसान्हंकृतेनैव दह प्रदहतां वर॥
en: Therefore, to do us good, do you, O threeeyed one, destroy them; and, O best of consuming ones, do you with your roars, burn them up.

sn: इत्येवं त्रिदशैरुक्तो निशम्यान्धकसूदनः। शिरः करं च धुन्वान इदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Thus addressed by the deities, the slayer of Andhaka, hearing their speech, said, shaking his head and hands.

sn: अवध्या मम ते देवाः सुकेशतनया रणे। मन्त्रं तु वः प्रदास्यामि यस्तान्वै निहनिष्यति॥
en: You gods, Sukesa's sons are incapable of being slain by me in battle. But I shall tell you the means whereby they may be slain.

sn: योऽसौ चक्रगदापाणिः पीतवासा जनार्दनः। हरिनारायणः श्रीमाशरणं तं प्रपद्यथ॥
en: Do you seek the shelter of him who hold the discus and mace in his hands, and who is clad in a yellow attire, of Janardana, Hari, even of the auspicious Nārāyaṇa.

sn: हरादवाप्य ते मन्त्र कामारिमभिवाद्य च। नारायणालयं प्राप्य तस्मै सर्वं न्यवेदयन्॥
en: Having received this counsel of Hara, they, rendering reverence to that enemy of Kāma, came the abode of Nārāyana and communicated everything to him.

sn: ततो नारायणेनोक्ता देवा इन्द्रपुरोगमाः। सुरारीस्तान्हनिष्यामि सुरा भवत निर्भयाः॥
en: Then Nārāyana spoke to the celestials with Indra at their head, I will slay those foes of the celestials. You gods, cast off all fear!

sn: देवानां भयभीतानां हरिणा राक्षसर्षभौ। प्रतिज्ञातो वधोऽस्माकं चिन्त्यतां यदिह क्षमम्।।३३
en: to O foremost of Rākşasas, Hari promised to the frightened celestials that he would slay us. Therefore do you think as to what is fit.

sn: हिरण्यकशिपोर्मृत्युरन्येषां च सुरद्विषाम्। नमुचिः कालनेमिश्च संहादो वीरसत्तमः॥ राधेयो बहुमायी च लोकपालोऽथ धार्मिकः। यमलार्जुनौ च हार्दिक्यः शुम्भश्चैव निशुम्भकः।।३५ असुरा दानवाश्चैव सत्त्ववन्तो महाबलाः। सर्वे समरमासाद्य न श्रूयन्तेऽपराजिताः॥ सर्वैः क्रतुशतैरिष्टं सर्वे मायाविदस्तथा। सर्वे सर्वास्त्रकुशलाः सर्वे शत्रुभयंकराः॥ नारायणेन निहताः शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः। एतज्ज्ञात्वा तु सर्वेषां क्षमं कर्तुमिहार्हथ। दुःखं नारायणं जेतुं यो नो हन्तुमिहेच्छति॥
en: Hiranyakaśipu has met with death (at the hands of Hari), as also other enemies of the immortals. And Namuci and Kālanemi, and that foremost of heroes, Sanhrada and Rādheya, and Bahumāyī, and the virtuous Lokapāla, and Yamala, and Arjuna, and Hardikya, and Sumbha and Niśumbhaka, Asuras and Dānavas endowed with strength and possessed of terrific prowess all these, who having come to the field, had never been heard of as worsted, who had performed hundreds of sacrifices, who had been well skilled in illusion, who had been versed in every branch of knowledge, and who were the terrors of their foes have by hundreds and by thousands been destroyed by Narayana. Learning this, it behove you to do what would conduce to the behoof of all. It is a sore task to defeat Narayana, who wish to slay us.

sn: ततः सुमाली माली च श्रुत्वा माल्यवतो वचः। ऊचतुर्भ्रातरं ज्येष्ठमश्विनाविव वासवम्॥
en: Thereat Sumāli and Māli, hearing the words of Malyavān, said to their eldest brother, like the Asvins addressing Vāsava.

sn: स्वधीतं दत्तमिष्टं च ऐश्वर्यं परिपालितम्। आयुर्निरामयं प्राप्तं सुधर्मः स्थापितः पथि॥
en: We have studied, performed sacrifices, practised charity, and obtained riches; and attaining long health and long life, we have established sterling righteousness in our path.

sn: देवसागरमक्षोभ्यं शस्त्रैः समवगाह्य च। जिता द्विषो ह्यप्रतिमास्तन्नो मृत्युकृतं भयम्॥
en: With arms plunging into the sea of celestials, we have conquered our unrivalled enemies. Therefore, we have no fear touching death.

sn: नारायणश्च रुद्रध शक्रश्चापि यमस्तथा। अस्माकं प्रमुख स्थातुं सर्वे बिभ्यति सर्वदा।॥
en: Even Narayana and Rudra, Sakra and Yama, ever fear to stay before us (in the field).

sn: विष्णोद्वेषस्य नास्त्येव कारणं राक्षसेश्वर। देवानामेव दोषेण विष्णोः प्रचलितं मनः॥
en: O lord of Raksasas. There is no occasion for Visnu's displeasure of us. The mind of Visnu has wavered in consequence of the evil caused by the celestials.

sn: तस्मादद्यैव सहिताः सर्वेऽन्योन्यसमावृताः। देवानेव जिघांसामो येभ्यो दोषः समुत्थितः॥
en: Therefore, will we even avenge ourselves on the gods, from whom has sprung this wrong.

sn: एवं संमन्त्र्य बलिनः सर्वसैन्यमुपासिताः। उद्योगं घोषयित्वा तु सर्वे नैर्ऋतपुङ्गवाः॥ युद्धाय निर्ययुः क्रुद्धाः जम्भवृत्रादयो यथा।
en: Having taken counsel together, those powerful ones conciliated their forces. And proclaiming (their order) that preparations were to be made, all the foremost Nairtas sallied forth for battle, like to those led by Jambha and Vſtra.

sn: इति ते राम संमन्त्र्य सर्वोद्योगेन राक्षसाः॥ युद्धाय निर्ययुः सर्वे महाकाया महाबलाः। स्पन्दनैारणैश्चैव हयैश्च करिसंनिभैः॥ खरैर्गोभिरथोष्ट्रैश्च शिशुमारैर्भुजंगमैः। मकरैः कच्छपैर्मी विहंगैर्गरुडोपमैः॥ सिंहैव्या॑।र्वराहैश्च समरैश्चमरैरपि। त्यक्त्वा लङ्कां गताः सर्वे राक्षसा बलगर्विताः॥४९ प्रयाता देवलोकाय योद्धं दैवतशत्रवः।
en: O Rāma, having thus taken counsel together, with all the preparations complete, those hugebodied and redoubtable Rākşasa marched forth for conflict, mounted on cars, and elephants, and horses resembling elephants, and mules, and kine, and camels, and purpoises, and serpents, makaras, and tortoises, and fishes, and fowls resembling Garua himself, lions and tigers and boars and Srmaras and Camaras.' up with pride of prowess, the Raksasa Marica, leaving Lanka, and the enemies of the celestials went to the heavenly regions for battle, 1. How purpoises could be pressed into the service passes my conception, unless Sicumdra have any other meaning. 2. Wilson gives the meaning: (1) a kind of animal,' and (2) 'a young deer, 3. Bos Gruniens.

sn: लङ्काविपर्ययं दृष्ट्वा यानि लङ्कालयान्यथ ॥ भूतानि भयदर्शीनि विमनस्कानि सर्वशः।
en: Perceiving the destruction of Lanka hand, those deities that had taken up their quarters there, everywhere were struck with fear and felt their spirits depressed.

sn: रथोत्तमैरुह्यमानाः शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः॥ प्रयाता राक्षसास्तूर्णं देवलोकं प्रयत्नतः। रक्षसामेव मार्गेण दैवतान्यपचक्रमुः॥
en: Mounting the best of the cars, the Rakşasas by hundreds and thousands with intent mind swiftly sallied forth for the celestial regions. And the deities (aforementioned) followed the tract of the Raksasas.

sn: भूतानि भयदर्शीनि विषमस्थानि सर्वशः। भौमाश्चैवान्तरिक्षाश्च कालज्ञप्ता भयावहाः। उत्पाता राक्षसेन्द्राणामभावाय समुत्थिताः॥
en: At the command of Kala, terrible evil omens foreshadowing the destruction of the Raksasachief began to arise on the earth well as in the sky.

sn: अस्थीनि मेघा ववृषुरुष्णं शोणितमेव च। वेला समुद्राश्चोत्क्रान्ताश्चेलुश्चाप्यथ भूधराः॥
en: The clouds showered down bones and hot blood. The oceans overleapt their continents and the mountains shook.

sn: अट्टहासान्विमुञ्चन्तो घननादसमस्वनाः। वाश्यन्त्यश्च शिवास्तत्र दारुणं घोरदर्शनाः॥
en: And jackals of terrific forms, having voices resembling the roaring of clouds, bursting out into a horse-laugh, began to emit cries frightfully.

sn: संपतन्त्यथ भूतानि दृश्यन्ते च यथाक्रमम्। गृध्रचक्रं महच्चात्र प्रज्वालोदारिभिर्मुखैः॥ रक्षोगणस्योपरिष्टात्परिभ्रमति कालवत्।
en: Creatures were one after another seen to drop down; and mighty swarms of vultures, with mouths belching forth flames, began to wheel over the Raksasa, like to Kala himself.

sn: कपोता रक्तपादाच सारिका विदुता ययुः॥ काका वाश्यन्ति तत्रैव बिडालाय द्विपादिकाः।
en: And blood-footed pigeons and Sarikas* darted off (around). And crows and two-legged cats began to cry in loud accents. *A species of harlot.

sn: उत्पातांस्ताननादृत्य राक्षसा बलदर्पिताः॥ यान्त्येव न निवर्तन्ते मृत्युपाशवपाशिताः। माल्यवांश्च सुमाली च माली च सुमहाबलः॥ पुरःसरा राक्षसानां ज्वलिता इव पावकाः।
en: But fast bound with the noose of Death, the Raksasas, proud of their strength, disregarding these omens, march on, and do not stay their course, Mälyavān and Sumāli possessed of prodigious strength, going before the Raksasas, like flaming fires.

sn: माल्यवन्तं तु ते सर्वे माल्यवन्तमिवाचलम् ॥ निशाचरा आश्रयन्ति धातारमिव देवताः।
en: Even as the gods take refuge under Dhātā, the night-rangers take refuge under Mālyavân resembling the mountain, Mälyavān.

sn: तलं राक्षसेन्द्राणां महाभ्रघननादितम् ॥ जयेप्सया देवलोकं ययौ मालिवशे स्थितम्।
