en: Under the command of Māli that host of Raksasas, roaring like mighty clouds, inspired with the desire of victory, went to the celestial regions.

sn: राक्षसानां समुद्योगं तं तु नारायणः प्रभुः॥ देवदूतादुपश्रुत्य चक्रे युद्धे तदा मनः। ससज्जायुधतूणीरो वैनतेयोपरि स्थितः॥
en: The lord Nārāyana, hearing of the preparations of the Rākşasas from a celestial messenger, set his heart on fight. And equipped with weapons and quivers, he mounted on Vinata's offspring.* *Garuda, Narayana's vehicle.

sn: आसाद्य कवचं दिव्यं सहस्रार्कसमद्युति। आबध्य शरसंपूर्णे इषुधी विमले तदा॥ श्रोणिसूत्रं च खङ्गं च विमलं कमलेक्षणः। शङ्खचक्रगदाशार्ङ्गखङ्गांश्चैव वरायुधान्॥ संपूर्ण गिरिसंकाशं वैनतेयमथास्थितः। राक्षसानामभावाय ययौ तूर्णतरं प्रभुः॥
en: And donning on his mail furnished with the effulgence of a thousand suns, fastening his spotless quivers filled with shafts, being engirt with his waist-band and bright falchion, and equipped with his conch, discus, mace, Sariga,* sword, and other superior weapons, that lotuseyed lord, seated on Vinata's offspring like a very mountain, set out speedily for compassing the destruction of the Raksasas.

sn: सुपर्णपृष्टे स बभौ श्यामः पीताम्बरो हरिः। काञ्चनस्य गिरेः शृङ्गे सतडित्तोयदो यथा॥
en: Seated on Suparma's* back, the blue-brown Hari clad in yellow attire resembled a mass of clouds on the crest of the golden mountain, with lightning playing through it. *Lit. fair-feathered-a name of Garua.

sn: स सिद्धदेवर्षिमहोरगैश्च गन्धर्वयक्षरुपगीयमानः। समाससादासुरसैन्यशत्रुश्चक्रासिशाङ्गमयुधशङ्खपाणिः।।६८
en: And hymned by Siddhas and celestials and sages and mighty (semi-divine) serpents and Gandharvas and Yakşas, the enemy of the Asura hosts presented himself, bearing in his hands the discus, sword, that weapon Śärnga and the conch.

sn: सुपर्णपक्षानिलनुनपक्षं भ्रमत्पताकं प्रविकीर्णशस्त्रम्। चचाल तद्राक्षसराजसैन्यं चलोपलं नीलमिवाचलानम्॥
en: The Raksasa-hosts, struck by the wind produced by the wings of Suparņa, with their pennons swinging to and fro and their weapons scattered about, quaked like the blue summit of a mountain with its crags tossed about.

sn: युगान्तवैश्वानरतुल्यविग्रहैः। निशाचराः संपिवार्य माधवं वरायुधैर्निर्बिभिदुः सहस्रशः॥
en: Then the night-rangers, hemming in Madhava,* began to pierce him with thousands of excellent sharpened weapons dyed in flesh and blood, and resembling the fire of Doomsday. *One of the many designations of Visnu.

sn: नारायणगिरिं ते तु गर्जन्तो राक्षसाम्बुदाः। अर्दयन्तोऽस्त्रवर्षेण वर्षेणेवाद्रिमम्बुदाः॥
en: As clouds assail a mountain with showers, then the Raksasas, representing clouds, setting up shouts, began to assail Nārāyaṇa representing a mountain.

sn: श्यामावदातस्तैर्विष्णुर्नीलैर्नक्तंचरोत्तमैः। वृतोऽञ्जनगिरीवायं वर्षमाणैः पयोधरैः॥
en: Visnu of a bright brown-blue hue, being surrounded by the flower of the night-rangers with dark visages, resembled the Añjana mountain, on which the clouds pour down.

sn: शलभा इव केदारं मशका इव पावकम्। यथामृतघटं दंशा मकरा इव चार्णवम्॥ तथा रक्षोधनुर्मुक्ता वज्रानिलमनोजवाः। हरिं विशन्ति स्म शरा लोका इव विपर्यये।४।।
en: As locusts (flood) a field, knots (throng) about a flame, gad-flies (cluster) around a pot of honey, or makaras (range) in the sea, so the shafts shot by the bows of the Rākṣasa, having (the energy of) the thunder-bolt and endowed with (the velocity of) the wind or thought, pierce Hari as if at the universal dissolution.

sn: स्यन्दनैः स्यन्दनगता गजैश्च गजमूर्धगाः। अश्वारोहास्तथाश्वैश्च पादाताश्चाम्बरे स्थिताः॥ राक्षसेन्द्राः गिरिनिभाः शरैः शक्त्य॒ष्टितोमरैः। निरुछ्वासं हरिं चक्रुः प्राणायामा इव द्विजम्॥
en: Those mounted on cars (assailed him) with their cars, and those mounted on the backs of elephants (assailed him) with their elephants, and those riding horses (assailed him) with their horses, and the foot-soldiers attacked him, stationed in the sky; and the foremost of Rākşasas resembling mountains, by means of darts, rstis and tomaras, suspended the respiration of Hari even as the prāņāyāma* does that of a twice-born one. *The practice of regulation respiration and finally suspending the same. This is practised by the Yogis of India, who attribute wonderful virtues to it.

sn: निशाचरैस्ताड्यमानो मीनैरिव महोदधिः। शाङ्गमायम्य दुर्धर्षो राक्षसेभ्योऽसृजच्छरान्॥
en: On being sore tried by the night-rangers, like the great Ocean by the fishes (residing in it), that invincible one, taking his ſārņga, showered shafts among the Rākşasas.

sn: शरैः पूर्णायतोत्सृष्टैर्वज्रकल्पैर्मनोजवैः। चिच्छेद विष्णुनिशितैः शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः॥
en: With sharpened arrows resembling the thunder, and endowed with the velocity of the wind, shot from his bow drawn to its fullest stretch, Visnu cut off (Raksasas) by hundreds and by thousands.

sn: विद्राव्य शरवर्षेण वर्ष वायुरिवोत्थितम्। पाञ्चजन्यं महाशङ्ख प्रदध्मौ पुरुषोत्तमः॥
en: And dashing away (the Rākṣasa ranks) with his arrowy shower, even as the wind aroused dashes away a downpour, that best of male beings blew his mighty conch Pāñcajanya.

sn: सोऽम्बुजो हरिणाध्मातः सर्वप्राणेन शङ्खराट्। ररास भीमनिर्हादस्त्रैलोक्यं व्यथयन्निव॥
en: Winded by Hari with his utmost might, that water-sprung king of conchs, endowed with terrific blares, roared, as if afflicting the three worlds.

sn: शङ्खराजरवः सोऽथ त्रासयामास राक्षसान् । मृगराज इवारण्ये समदानिव कुञ्जरान्॥
en: The sounds of that king of conchs struck terror into the Rākşasas, even as in a mighty forest a lion (strikes terror into the hearts of) elephants in rut.

sn: न शेकुरश्वाः संस्थातुं विमदाः कुञ्जराभवन्। स्यन्दनेभ्यश्च्युता वीराः शङ्खरावितदुर्बलाः॥
en: Thereat the horses could not keep their ground, and the elephants were reſt of their temporal flow, and shorn of their virtue at the roars of the conch, heroes began to topple down from their cars.

sn: शाङ्गचापविनिर्मुक्ता वज्रतुल्याननाः शराः। विदार्य तानि रक्षांसि सुपुङ्खा विविशुः क्षितिम्॥
en: And dight with dainty feathered parts having heads, the shafts discharged from the śārnga, resembling thunder-bolts, riving those Rākşása, entered the earth.

sn: भिद्यमानाः शरैः संख्ये नारायणकरच्युतैः। निपेतू राक्षसा भूमौ शैला वज्रहता इव ॥
en: In that conflict, pierced by the arrows discharged from Nārāyana's arm, the Rākşasa began to drop to the ground like mountains struck with the thunder-bolt.

sn: व्रणानि परगात्रेभ्यो विष्णुचक्रकृतानि हि। असृक्क्षरन्ति धाराभिः स्वर्णधारा इवाचलाः॥
en: The wounds on the persons of the foes inflicted by the discus of Vişnu discharge blood in streams, like mountains discharging streams of red chalk.

sn: शङ्खराजरवश्चापि शार्ङ्गचापरवस्तथा। राक्षसानां रवांश्चापि ग्रसते वैष्णवो रवः॥
en: The sound of that king of conchs, as well as those of the Sārnga, combined with the roars emitted by Vişņu himself, swallowed up the roars of the Rākşasas.

sn: तेषां शिरोधरान्धूताञ्छरध्वजधनूंषि च। रथान्पताकास्तूणीरांश्चिच्छेद स हरिः शरैः॥
en: Hari by means of his shafts cut off their necks, and arrows, and standards, and bows, and cars, and ensigns and quivers.

sn: सूर्यादिव करा घोरा वार्योघा इव सागरात्। पर्वतादिव नागेन्द्रा धारौघा इव चाम्बुदात्॥ तथा शाङ्गविनिर्मुक्ताः शरा नारायणेरितात्। निर्धावन्तीषवस्तूर्णं शतशोथ सहस्रशः॥
en: Like fierce rays streaming about from sun, like torrents dashing from the ocean, like elephants coming adown a mountain, or like showers descending from clouds, the shafts shot by Nārāyaṇa pursue (the foes) by hundreds and by thousands.

sn: शरभेण यथा सिंहाः सिंहेन द्विरदा यथा। द्विरेदेन यथा व्याघ्रा व्याघ्रण द्वीपिनो यथा॥ द्वीपिनेव यथा श्वानः शुना मार्जारको यथा। माजरिण यथा सर्पाः सर्पेण च यथाखवः॥ तथा ते राक्षसाः सर्वे विष्णुना प्रभविष्णुना। द्रवन्ति द्राविताश्चान्ये शायिताश्च महीतले॥
en: Even as an elephant pursuits a tiger, a tiger a wolf, a wolf a dog, a dog a cat, a cat a snake, or a snake a rat, so the mighty Vişnu pursuit the Rākșasa host; and others, (struck down by him), measure their lengths on the ground.

sn: राक्षसानां सहस्राणि निहत्य मधुसूदनः। वारिजं पूरयामास तोयदं सुरराडिव॥
en: Then, having despatched thousands of Rākşasas, the destroyer of Madhu blew his water-sprung (conch), even as the sovereign of the celestials filleth clouds (with rain).

sn: नारायणशरत्रस्तं शङ्खनादसुविह्वलम्। ययौ लङ्कामभिमुखं प्रभग्नं राक्षसं बलम् ॥
en: Agitated by the arrows of Nārāyaṇa, with their senses bewildered by the blares of the conch, the broken Raksasa forces made for Lankā.

sn: प्रभग्ने राक्षसबले नारायणशराहते। सुमाली शरवर्षेण निववार रणे हरिम्॥
en: On the Rākşasa army having been broken in consequence of the beating it got at the hands of Nārāyaṇa, Sumāli with showers of shafts resisted Hari in the encounter.

sn: स तु तं छादयामास नीहार इव भास्करम्। राक्षसाः सत्त्वसंपन्नाः पुनधैर्य समादधुः॥
en: As a mist envelops the Sun, he enveloped him (with his arrows). Thereat, the Rākşasas again summoned up their fortitude.

sn: अथ सोऽभ्यपतद्रोषाद्राक्षसो बलदर्पितः। महानादं प्रकुर्वाणो राक्षसाञ्जीवयन्निव॥
en: And fired with range, that Rākşasa, inflated with insolence on account of his strength, setting up a tremendous roar, darted at his antagonist in the conflict, thereby seeming to receive the Råkş asas.

sn: उत्क्षिप्य लम्बाभरणं धुन्वन्करमिव द्विपः। ररास राक्षसो हर्षात्सतडित्तोयदो यथा॥
en: As an elephant flourishes its trunk, that Rāks asa, lifting up his arm adorned with ornaments, began to roar from rapture, like a mass of clouds, lighted up with lightening.

sn: सुमाले र्दतस्तस्य शिरो ज्वलितकुण्डलम्। चिच्छेद यन्तुरश्वाश्च भ्रान्तास्तस्य तु रक्षसः॥
en: And (Visņu) cut off the head flaming with ear rings of the charioteer of the shouting Sumáli; and thereat the horses of that Raksasa aimlessly strayed hither and thither.

sn: तैरश्वैर्धाम्यते भ्रान्तैः सुमाली राक्षसेश्वरः। इन्द्रियाश्वैः परिभ्रान्तैधृतिहीनो यथा नरः॥
en: And with his bewildered steeds Sumali wanders like a person deprived of patience, whose senses are under hallucination.

sn: ततो विष्णुं महाबाहुं प्रपतन्तं रणाजिरे। हते सुमालेर वैश्च रथे विष्णुरथं प्रति। माली चाभ्यद्रवधुक्तः प्रगुम स शरासनम्॥
en: And on Sumali's car being drawn at random by his steeds, Mali, taking his bow and equipped therewith, darted at Vişnu's car and assailed that mighty-armed one as he was descending on the field of fight.

sn: मालेधनुश्च्युता बाणाः कार्तस्वरविभूषिताः। विविशुहरिमासाद्य क्रौञ्चं पत्ररथा इव ॥
en: Like birds entering the Krauñca mountain, the arrows discharged from Mali's bow, graced with gold, hit Hari and entered (into his body).

sn: अर्धमानः शरैः सोऽथ मालिमुक्तैः सहस्रशः। चुक्षुभे न रणे विष्णुर्जितेन्द्रिय इवाधिभिः॥
en: Thereat, as a person holding his senses under subjection is not thrown out of his mental balance, Vişnu, assailed in that encounter with thousands of arrows shot by Māli, was not disturbed ever so little.

sn: अथ मौर्वीस्वनं कृत्वा भगवान्भूतभावनः। मालिनं प्रति बाणौघान्ससर्जासिगदाधरः॥
en: Then that creator of all beings, the reverend Gadādhara,* twanging his bow-string, showered volleys of shafts on Máli. *Lit. the holder of the mace, a name of Visnu.

sn: ते मालिदेहमासाद्य वज्रविद्युत्प्रभाः शराः। पिबन्ति रुधिरं तस्य नागा इव सुधारसम्॥
en: And getting at Mali's body, the arrows furnished with the luminousness of lightening drink his blood, like to serpents drinking nectar.

sn: मालिनं विमुखं कृत्वा शङ्खचक्रगदाधरः। मालिमौलिं ध्वजं चापं वाजिनश्चाप्यपातयत्॥
en: And baffling Māli, the holder of the conch, discus, and mace, brought down Māli's crown, standard, bow and steeds.

sn: विरथस्तु गदां गृह्य माली नक्तंचरोत्तमः। आपुप्लुवे गदापाणिगिर्यग्रादिव केसरी॥
en: Then that foremost of night-rangers, on being deprived of his car, sprang forward, mace in hand, even as lion bounds up from the brow of a hillock.

sn: गदया गरुडेशानमीशानमिव चान्तकः। ललाटदेशेऽभ्यहनद्वजेणेन्द्रो यथाचलम् ॥
en: He with his mace smote at the forehead of that lord of birds, even as the Destroyer had smitten Isana,* or as Indra smites a mountain with his thunder-bolt. *There took place an encounter betwcen Radra and Yama in the Sveta forest, for the protection of Märkandeya and a certain king. In this battle, Yama had smitten Rudra. This is narrated in the Puranas.

sn: गदयाभिहतस्तेन मालिना गरुडो भृशम्। रणात्पराङ्मुखं देवं कृतवान्वेदनातुरः॥
en: On being severely struck by Mali with his mace, Garuda, writhing in torments, moved the god away from the field of battle.

sn: पराङ्मुखे कृते देवे मालिना गरुडेन वै। उदतिष्ठन्महाशब्दो रक्षसामभिनर्दताम्॥
en: On the god having been removed from the field by Mäli as well as Garuda, there arose a mighty din of Raksasa roaring (in chorus).

sn: रक्षसां रुवतां रावं श्रुत्वा हरिहयानुजः। तिर्यगास्थाय संक्रुद्धः पक्षीशे भगवान्हरिः॥ पराङ्मुखोऽप्युत्ससर्ज मालेश्चक्रं जिघांसया।
en: Hearing the cheers of the Raksasa, Indra's younger brother, the reverend Hari, sitting on that lord of birds, albeit moved off from the scene of conflict, waxing enraged, from a desire of slaying (Mali) hurled his disc at him.

sn: तत्सूर्यमण्डलाभासं स्वभासा भासयन्नभः॥ कालचक्रनिभं चक्रं मालेः शीर्षमपातयत्।
en: Thereat the disc, possessed of the splendour of the solar disc, and resembling the wheel itself of Kāla, flooding all the heavens with radiance, brought down Māli's head to the ground.

sn: तच्छिरो राक्षसेन्द्रस्य चक्रोत्कृत्तं बिभीषणम्। पपात रुधिरोद्गारि पुरा राहुशिरो यथा।॥
en: That head of lord of Rākşasas, terrific to behold, on being cut off (by Visnu), vomiting blood, fell down before (the Rākşasas), as formerly Rahu's head had fallen.

sn: ततः सुरैः संप्रहृष्टैः सर्वप्राणसमीरितः। सिंहनादरवो मुक्तः साधु देवेतिवादिभिः॥ मालिनं निहतं दृष्ट्वा सुमाली माल्यवानपि। सबलौ शोकसंतप्तौ लङ्कामेव प्रधावितौ ॥
en: Then the deities experiencing excess of joy set up leonine cheers with might and main, crying,' Excellent, O god.' Seeing Mali slain, Sumali and Mālyavån, burning in grief, fled precipitately towards Lankä along with their forces.

sn: गरुडस्तु समाश्वस्तः संनिवृत्य यथा पुरा। राक्षसान्द्रावयामास पक्षवातेन कोपितः॥
en: Garuda, being cheered, turned round, and growing enraged, as before drove the Rākşasas with the wind of his wings.

sn: चक्रकृत्तास्यकमला गदासंचूर्णितोरसः। लाङ्गलग्लपितग्रीवा मुसलैभिन्नमस्तकाः॥ केचिच्चैवासिना छिन्नास्तथान्ये शरताडिताः। निपेतुरम्बरातूर्णं राक्षसाः सागराम्भसि ॥
en: And (some) with their lotus-faces cut by the discus, (some) with their chests crushed with the mace, (some) with their necks torn off by the plough, (some) with their heads riven by the club, and some hewn by the sword, and others pierced by arrows, the Rākṣasas began to drop fast from the sky into the waters of the ocean.

sn: नारायणोऽपीषुवराशनीभिर्विदारयामास धनुर्विमुक्तैः। नक्तंचरान्धूतविमुक्तकेशान्यथाशनीभिः सतडिन्महाभ्रः।।
en: And as the thunder-bolt with lightening (riveth) a mighty mass of clouds, Narayana by means of the thunder-bolts of his arrows discharged from his bow, rived the night-rangers with their hair dishevelled and streaming (in the wind).

sn: भिन्नातपत्रं पतमानशस्त्रं शरैरपध्वस्तविनीतवेषम्। विनिःसृतान्त्रं भयलोलनेत्रं बलं तदुन्मत्ततरं बभूव॥
en: The forces having their umbrellas rent, their arms falling off, their goodly garments scattered, their entrails coming out and their eyes rolling, became incapable of distinguishing their own party from that of the foe.

sn: सिंहार्दितानामिव कुञ्जराणां निशाचराणां सह कुञ्जराणाम्। रवाश्च वेगाश्च समं बभूवुः पुराणसिंहेन विमर्दितानाम्॥
en: Even like (the roars and the vehemence) displayed by elephants on being attacked by lions, the roars, and the vehemence of the nightrangers and their elephants, sore assailed by the Primaeval Lion,* were equal. *Vişnu as a man-lion had formerly taken the conceit out of Hiranyakasipu the Asura king-and slain him, to rid his devotee Prahlada of his mortal foc in the from of a father.

sn: ते वार्यमाणा हरिबाणजालैः स्वबाणजालानि समुत्सृजन्तः। धावन्ति नक्तंचरकालमेघा वायुप्रणुन्ना इव कालमेघाः॥
en: And driven by Hari's networks of arrows, and discharging (all the while) their own showers of shafts, those night-rangers resembling the clouds of doom, are driven like the veritable clouds of the universal dissolution drifted by the wind.

sn: चक्रप्रहारैर्विनिकृत्तशीर्षाः संचूर्णिताङ्गाश्च गदाप्रहारैः। असिप्रहारैर्द्विविधा विभिन्नाः पतन्ति शैला इव राक्षसेन्द्राः॥
en: Their heads cut by discus, their parts of bodies crushed with the mace, and hewn in twain with swords, thus they foremost of Rākşasas fell like to hills (toppling headlong).

sn: निशाचरैर्नीलबलाहकोपमैः। निपात्यमानैर्ददृशे निरन्तरं निपात्यमानैरिव नीलपर्वतैः॥
en: The Earth was seen to be (covered) with night-rangers resembling dark clouds, adorned with jewelled necklaces and ear rings, falling down, as if covered with dark mountains dropping down.

sn: हन्यमाने बले तस्मिन्पद्मनाभेन पृष्ठतः। माल्यवान्संनिवृत्तोऽथ वेलामेत्य इवार्णवः॥
en: On that host being sore pressed at its back by Padmanabha,* Mālyavăn turned back even as the ocean does on meeting with its shore. *Lit. the lotus-naveled-a name of Visnu.

sn: संरक्तनयनः क्रोधाच्चलन्मौलिनिशाचरः। पद्मनाभमिदं प्राह वचनं पुरुषोत्तमम्॥
en: And with his eyes reddened, that night-ranger waxing wroth, shaking his head, addressed that prime of male persons Padmanabha, saying.

sn: नारायण न जानीषे क्षात्रधर्म पुरातनम्। अयुद्धमनसो भीतानस्मान्हंसि यथेतरः॥
en: O Nārāyaṇa, you are ignorant of the timehonoured morality of Kşatriyas; and therefore like a base wight you slay us, desisting from fight and exercised with fear.

sn: पराङ्मुखवधं पापं यः करोति सुरेश्वर। स हन्ता न गतः स्वर्ग लभते पुण्यकर्मणाम्॥
en: O lord of the celestials, he that commits the crime of slaying one that desists from fight cannot go to the celestial regions as the fruit of meritorious acts.

sn: युद्धश्रद्धाथवा तेऽस्ति शङ्खचक्रगदाधर। अहं स्थितोऽस्मि पश्यामि बलं दर्शय यत्तव॥
en: If you are bent upon battle, a holder of the conch, the discus and the mace, taking up my post (here), I shall see (your strength). Do you show (me) the same.

sn: माल्यवन्तं स्थितं दृष्टवा माल्यवन्तमिवाचलम्। उवाच राक्षसेन्द्रं तं देवराजानुजो बली॥
en: Seeing Mālyavān resembling the mountain, Mālyavān, stay, the powerful younger brother of the sovereign of the celestials spoke to him.

sn: युष्मत्तो भयभीतानां देवानां वै मयाभयम्। राक्षसोत्सादनं दत्तं तदेतदनुपाल्यते॥
en: I have removed the fear of the deities, affrighted at you, by promising that I will make root and branch work with the Räkşasas; and that same promise I am now fulfilling.

sn: प्राणैरपि प्रियं कार्यं देवानां हि सदा मया। सोऽहं वो निहनिष्यामि रसातलगतानपि॥
en: I should always lay down my life for serving the celestials and you I will slay even if you should go to the nethermost regions.

sn: देवदेवं ब्रुवाणं तं रक्ताम्बुरुहलोचनम्। शक्त्या बिभेद संक्रुद्धो राक्षसेन्द्रो भुजान्तरे॥
en: As that god of gods having eyes resembling the red lotuses was speaking thus, the lord of Rākşasas in high wrath pierced his breast with a dart.

sn: माल्यवद्भुजनिर्मुक्ता शक्तिघण्टाकृतस्वना। हरेरुरसि बभ्राज मेघस्थेव शतदा॥
en: And hurled by the hand of Mālyavān, the dart resonant with bells, appeared graceful on Hari's breast like lightening embosomed in clouds.

sn: ततस्तामेव चोत्कृष्य शक्तिं शक्तिधरप्रियः। माल्यवन्तं समुद्दिश्य चिक्षेपाम्बुरुहेक्षणः॥
en: Thereat drawing out the same dart, that one dear to the Wielder of the Dart,* having eyes resembling red lotuses, aiming at Mālyāvan, hurled it at him. *A name of Kārtikeya, the celestial generallissimo.

sn: स्कन्दोत्सृष्टेव सा शक्तिर्गोविन्दकरनिःसृता। काङ्क्षन्ती राक्षसं प्रायान्महोल्केवाञ्जनाचलम्॥ सा तस्योरसि विस्तीर्णे हारभारावभासिते। आपतद्राक्षसेन्द्रस्य गिरिकूट इवाशनिः॥
en: Thereat the dart discharged by the hand of Govinda like to the Dart discharged by the hand of Skanda, rushing towards the Rākṣasa like a meteor coursing towards the Anjana mountain, descended on the spacious chest of the lord of the Rākşasas decked with the weight of a chain, even as the thunder clap bursts at the summit of the mountain.

sn: तया भिन्नतनुत्राणः प्राविशद्विपुलं तमः। माल्यवान्पुनराश्वस्तस्तस्थौ गिरिरिवाचलः॥
en: On having his mail rent, Mālyāvan was utterly deprived of his senses; but (anon) reposing for a while, he again stood like a moveless hill.

sn: ततः कालायसं शूलं कण्टकैर्बहुभिश्चितम्। प्रगृह्याभ्यहनद्देवं स्तनयोरन्तरे दृढम्॥
en: Then taking up a javelin made of black iror girt with many a thorn, he furiously smote that deity on the chest.

sn: तथैव रणरक्तस्तु मुष्टिना वासवानुजम्। ताडयित्वा धनुर्मात्रमपक्रान्तो निशाचरः॥
en: And that night-ranger delighting in battle, dealing a box at Vāsavā's younger brother, moved away a distance measuring a bow's length.

sn: ततोऽम्बरे महाञ्छब्दः साधुसाध्विति चोत्थितः। आहत्य राक्षसो विष्णुं गरुडं चाप्यताडयत्॥
en: And now there arose a mighty tumult in the sky of 'Excellent!' 'Excellent!' and having struck Visnu, the Raksasa also hit Garuda.

sn: वैनतेयस्ततः क्रुद्धः पक्षवातेन राक्षसम्। व्यपोहबलवान्वायुः शुष्कपर्णचयं यथा।॥
en: Thereat Vinata's son, growing engaged, drove the Rākşasas away with the wind of his wings, even as the lusty wind bloweth about sere leaves.

sn: द्विजेन्द्रपक्षवातेन द्रावितं दृश्य पूर्वजम्। सुमाली स्वबलैः सार्धं लङ्कामभिमुखो ययौ॥
en: Seeing his elder brother driven by the wind produced by the wings of that bird, Sumali along with his forces, made for Lankā.

sn: पक्षवातबलोद्भूतो माल्यवानपि राक्षसः। स्वबलेन समागम्य ययौ लङ्कां ह्रिया वृतः॥
en: And pushed off by the violence of the wind of (Garuda's) wings, the Rākṣasa Mālyavān also, joined by his own forces, departed for Lankā, covered with shame.

sn: एवं ते राक्षसा राम हरिणा कमलेक्षण। बहुशः संयुगे भग्ना हतप्रवरनायकाः॥
en: Thus, O Rama, O lotus-eyed one, (the Rākşasas) had innumerable warriors beaten down and their foremost leaders slain.

sn: अशक्नुवन्तस्ते विष्णुं प्रतियोद्धं बलार्दिताः। त्यक्त्वा लङ्कां गता वस्तुं पातालं सहपत्नयः॥
en: And albeit inflated with pride, they, incapable of coping with Vişnu, leaving Lankā, went to the nether regions with their wives dwelling there.

sn: सुमालिनं समासाद्य राक्षसं रघुसत्तम। स्थिताः प्रख्यातवीर्यास्ते वंशे सालकटङ्कटे॥
en: O best of the Raghus, these Rākşasa of celebrated prowess, related to the race of Sälakatankața, remained under the leadership of the Rākṣasa Sumāli.

sn: ये त्वया निहतास्ते तु पौलस्त्या नाम राक्षसाः। समाली माल्यवान्माली ये च तेषां पुरःसराः। सर्व एते महाभागा रावणाद्बलवत्तराः॥
en: All those exalted Rākşasas going under the name of Pulastya that had been headed by Sumāli, Mālyavān and Māli, were stronger than Ravana.

sn: न चान्यो राक्षसान्हन्ता सुरारीन्देवकण्टकान्। ऋते नारायणं देवं शङ्खचक्रगदाधरम्॥
en: No other than the god Nārāyaṇa, holding the conch, the discus and the mace, could slay those Råkşasa-foes to the celestials and thorns in the side of the deties.

sn: भवान्नारायणो देवश्चतुर्बाहुः सनातनः। राक्षसान्हन्तुमुत्पन्नो ह्यजय्यः प्रभुरव्ययः॥
en: And you are that eternal god the four armed Narayana, the lord, undeteriorating and unconquerable, sprung to exterminate Rāksasas.

sn: नष्टधर्मव्यवस्थानां काले काले प्रजाकरः। उत्पद्यते दस्युवधे शरणागतवत्सलः॥
en: The creator of beings that one ever cherishing those seeking his refuge appeares at times to compass the destruction of marauders, bringing the religion of the people to rack and ruin.* *This tallies wonderfully with the corresponding view given in the Bible. Great men appear in the fullness of time to bring about reforms in religion, when, as was the case before the birth of Christ, men have wandered farthest from the true path.

sn: मुत्पत्तिरद्य कथिता सकला यथावत्। भूयो निबोध रघुसत्तम रावणस्य जन्मप्रभावमतुलं ससुतस्य सर्वम्॥
en: Thus, O lord of men, to-day I have truely related to you at length the origin of the Raksasas. Again, O foremost of the Raghus, do you understand the matchless birth and potency of Rāvana and his sons related in detail.

sn: चिरात्सुमाली व्यचरद्रसातलं स राक्षसो विष्णुभयादितस्तदा। पुत्रैश्च पौत्रैश्च समन्वितो बली ततस्तु लङ्कामवसद्धनेश्वरः॥
en: And that powerful Rākṣasa, Sumāli, afflicted with the fear of Vişnu, along with his sons and grand-sons for a long time ranged the nether regions, and the lord of riches resided in Lankā.

sn: कस्यचित्त्वथ कालस्य सुमाली नाम राक्षसः। रसातलान्मर्त्यलोकं सर्व वै विचचार ह॥ नीलजीमूतसंकाशस्तप्तकाश्चनकुण्डलः। कन्यां दुहितरं गृह्य विना पद्ममिव श्रियम्॥ राक्षसेन्द्रः स तु तदा विचरन्वै महीतले। तदापश्यत्स गच्छन्तं पुष्पकेण धनेश्वरम्॥ गच्छन्तं पितरं द्रष्टुं पुलस्त्यतनयं विभुम्। तं दृष्टामरसंकाशं गच्छन्तं पावकोमम्॥ रसातलं प्रविष्टः सन्मर्त्यलोकात्सविस्मयः।
en: After a while the Rākşasa named Sumāli, coming up from the nether regions, began to range all over the earth. And resembling dark clouds, that lord of Rakşasas decked in ear-rings of burnished gold, taking his daughter like to Sri herself without her lotus, and wandering over the earth, saw the lord of riches journeying in his Puspaka, going to see his sire-that lord, the son of Pulastya. And seeing that one resembling an immortal and like to fire, journeying on, (Sumāli) struck with amazement, entered the nether regions from the earth.

sn: इत्येवं चिन्तयामास राक्षसानां महामतिः॥ किं कृत्वा श्रेय इत्येवं वर्धेमहि कथं वयम्।
en: And that mighty-minded one reflected thus, ‘By adopting what measure may the welfare of the Rākṣasa he brought about, and how can we increase (in power)?'

sn: नीलजीमूतसंकाशस्तप्तकाश्चनकुण्डलः॥ राक्षसेन्द्रः स तु तदा चिन्तयत्सुमहामतिः। अथाब्रवीत्सुतां रक्षः कैकसी नाम नामतः॥
en: And that great-minded lord of Rākşasas, resembling dark clouds, decked in burnished earrings of gold, then began to reflect. And then the Raksasa addressed his daughter, named Kaikasi.

sn: पुत्रि प्रदानकालोऽयं यौवन व्यतिवर्तते। प्रत्याख्यानाच्च भीतैस्त्वं न वरैः परिगृह्यसे॥
en: O daughter, the time has come when I should give you away. Your youth is about to be passed. (Kept back) by the fear of refusal, no suiter has sought you (up to his time).

sn: तत्कृते च वयं सर्वे यन्त्रिता धर्मबुद्धयः। त्वं हि सर्वगुणोपेता श्रीः साक्षादिव पुत्रिके॥
en: But desirous of acquiring religious merit, we are striving our best in your interests. My daughter, you are finished with every perfection like to Śrī herself.

sn: कन्यापितृत्वं दुःखं हि सर्वेषां मानकाङ्क्षिणाम्। न ज्ञायते च कः कन्यां वरयेदिति कन्यके॥
en: The being father to a daughter is misery to every one that seekes honour. O daughter, one does not know who shall ask for one's daughter.

sn: मातुः कुलं पितृकुलं यत्र चैव च दीयते। कुलत्रयं सदा कन्यां संशये स्थाप्य तिष्ठति ॥
en: Whenever may a daughter be conferred, a daughter stayes, placing in uncertainly the three races* to which she is related. *The races respectively of her father, mother and husband.

sn: सा त्वं गुनिवरं श्रेष्ठं प्रजापतिकुलोद्भवम्। भज विश्रवसं पुत्रि पौलस्त्यं वरय स्वयम्॥
en: Do you, my daughter, seek for your husband that best and foremost of ascetics sprung in the line of Prajăpati Pulastya's son, Viśravā, and of yourself accept him (for your lord).

sn: ईदृशास्ते भविष्यन्ति पुत्राः पुत्रि न संशयः। तेजसा भास्करसमो यादृशोऽयं धनेश्वरः॥
en: Then, O daughter, even as this lord of riches, so you will, without doubt, have sons resembling the Sun himself in energy.

sn: सा तु तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा कन्यका पितृगौरवात्। तत्र गत्वा च सा तस्थौ विश्रवा यत्र तप्यते॥
en: Hearing that speech of his, the daughter for the sake of dignity of her sire, going to where Viśravā was practising penances, stood there.

sn: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे राम पुलस्त्यतनयो द्विजः। अग्निहोत्रमुपातिष्ठच्चतुर्थ इव पावकः॥
en: In the meanwhile, O Rama, that twice-born one-Pulastya's was performing the Agnihotra, like the fourth Fire itself.

sn: अविचन्त्य तु तां वेला दारुणां पितृगौरवात्। उपसृत्याग्रतस्तस्य चरणाधोमुखी स्थिता ॥ विलिखन्ती मुहुभूमिमङ्गुष्ठाग्रेण भामिनी।
en: And without minding that terrific time, (Kaikasi), having regard to the dignity of her sire, coming up before him, stood (there) son hanging her head down towards his feet and throwing up the earth with her great foe.

sn: 'स तु तां वीक्ष्य सुश्रोणी पूर्णचन्द्रनिभाननाम्॥ अब्रवीत्परमोदारो दीप्यमानां स्वतेजसा। भद्रे कस्यासि दुहिता कुतो वा त्वमिहागता। किं कार्य कस्य वा हेतोस्तत्त्वतो ब्रूहि शोभने ।।१८
en: Seeing that one of the shapely hips, having a face fair as the full Moon, (that exceedingly high-minded ascetic) flaming in energy accosted her thus. O gentle one, whose daughter are you? And when do you come hither? And what is your errand? And for whom (do you come)? O beauteous (damsel), truly tell me this.

sn: एवमुक्ता तु सा कन्या कृताञ्जलिरथाब्रवीत्। आत्मप्रभावेण मुने ज्ञातुमर्हसि मे मतम्॥ किं तु मां विद्धिब्रह्मर्षे शासनात्पितुरागताम्। कैकसी नाम नाम्नाहं शेषं त्वं ज्ञातुमर्हसि॥
en: Thus addressed, the girl, with joined hands, said, 'O ascetic, you are competent to get at my intent by virtue of your own power. Yet, O Brahmarși, know me as having come here at the mandate of my sire. My name is Kaikasī. The rest do you read yourself.

sn: स तु गत्वा मुनिर्व्यानं वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह। विज्ञातं ते मया भद्रे कारणं यन्मनोगतम्॥ सुताभिलाषो मत्तस्ते मत्तमातंगगामिनि। दारुणायां तु वेलायां यस्मात्त्वं मामुपस्थिता॥ शृणु तस्मात्सुतान्भद्रे यादृशाञ्जनयिष्यसि। दारुणान्दारुणाकारान्दारुणाभिजनप्रियान्॥ प्रसविष्यसि सुश्रोणि राक्षसान्क्रूरकर्मणः।
en: Thereupon, the ascetic, entering into contemplation, said these words, 'O gentle lady, I have learnt the purpose that is in your heart. O you having the gait of a mad elephant, there reigns a powerful desire in you for having offspring. Inasmuch as you have come to me at this fierce hour, hearken, you amiable one, as to the kind of offspring that you shall bring forth. You shall, O you of graceful hips, bring forth terrible and grim-visaged Rākşasas delighting in frightful friends, and of cruel deeds.

sn: सा तु तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा प्रणिपत्याब्रवीद्वचः॥ भगवन्नीदृशान्पुत्रांस्त्वत्ताऽहं ब्रह्मवादिनः। नेच्छामि सुदुराचारान्प्रसादं कर्तुमर्हसि॥
en: Hearing his speech, she, bowing down, said, 'O reverend (ascetic), such sons of terrific ways seek I not from you that follow the Veda. Therefore it behoves you to favour me.'

sn: कन्यया त्वेवमुक्तस्तु विश्रवा मुनिपुङ्गवः। उवाच कैकसीं भूयः पूर्णेन्दुरिव रोहिणीम्॥
en: On being thus besought by the girl, Visravabest of ascetics, again addressed Kaikasi, like the full moon addressing Rohini.* *Hesperus.

sn: पश्चिमो यस्तव सुतो भविष्यति शुभानने। मम वंशानुरूपः स धर्मात्मा च न संशयः॥
en: O fair-faced one, the son that you bring forth last, shall be like to my line, he shall, without doubt-be righteous-souled.

sn: एवमुक्ता तु सा कन्या राम कालेन केनचित्। जनयामास बीभत्सं रक्षोरूपं सुदारुणम्॥ दशग्रीवं महादंष्ट्र नीलाञ्जनचयोपमम्। ताम्रोष्ठं विंशतिभुजं महास्यं दीप्तमूर्धनम्॥
en: Having been thus accosted, the girl, O Rama, after a length of time brought forth a very terrible and hideous offspring having the form of a Raksasa, having ten necks, furnished with large teeth, and resembling a heap of collyrium, with coppery lips, twenty arms, huge faces, and flaming hair.

sn: तस्मिञ्जाते ततस्तस्मिन्सज्वालकबलाः शिवाः। क्रव्यादाश्चापसव्यानि मण्डलानि प्रचक्रमुः॥
en: On his having been born, jacka.s with flaming mouths and other ferocious beasts began to gyrate on the left.

sn: ववर्ष रुधिरं देवो मेघाश्च खरनिःस्वनाः। प्रभभौ न च सूर्यो वै महोल्काश्चापतन्भुवि॥ चकम्पे जगती चैव ववुर्वाताः सुदारुणाः। अक्षोभ्यः क्षुभितश्चैव समुद्रः सरितां पतिः॥
en: That god showered down blood; and the clouds uttered forth harsh sounds. And the sun was deprived of his splendour; and meteors began to dart to the earth. And the earth shook; and the wind swept away violently. And that lord of streams-the ocean, which was calm before, became agitated.

sn: अथ नामाकरोतस्य पितामहसमः पिता। दशग्रीवः प्रसूतोऽयं दशग्रीवो भविष्यति॥
en: And his sire resembling his grand-father named him, (saying), 'As this one has been born with ten necks, he shall be called Ten-necked.'

sn: तस्य त्वनन्तरं जातः कुम्भकर्णो महाबलः। प्रमाणाद्यस्य विपुलं प्रमाणं नेह विद्यते॥
en: After him was born Kumbhakarņa endowed with prodigious strength, than whose proportions there are none other's on earth.

sn: ततः शूर्पणखा नाम संजज्ञे विकृतानना। विभीषणश्च धर्मात्मा कैकस्याः पश्चिमः सुतः॥
en: Then was born she that, having a frightful visage, goes under the name of Surpanakha; the righteous Vibhīşaņa is the youngest son of Kaikasi.

sn: तस्मिाते महासत्त्वे पुष्पवर्ष पपात ह। नभःस्थाने दुन्दुभयो देवानां प्राणदंस्तथा। वाक्यं चैवान्तरिक्षे च साधु साध्विति तत्तदा ॥
en: On that one endowed with great strength having been born, blossoms were showered down from heaven; and celestial kettle-drums were sounded in the heavenly regions. And then there arose the sounds of 'Excellent!'

sn: तौ तु तत्र महारण्ये ववृधाते महौजसौ। कुम्भकर्णदशग्रीवौ लोकोद्वेगकरौ तदा ॥
en: 'Excellent!' And in that extensive forest those exceedingly energetic ones, Kumbhakarņa and the Ten-necked one grew up, and became the sources of anxiety to the people.

sn: कुम्भकर्णः प्रमत्तस्तु महर्षीन्धर्मवत्सलान्। त्रैलोक्ये नित्यासंतुष्टो भक्षयन्विचचार ह॥
en: Kumbhakarma, maddened to the height, devouring mighty-saints devoted to religion, constantly ranged the triune world in a dissatisfied spirit.

sn: विभीषणस्तु धर्मात्मा नित्यं धर्मर्यवस्थितः। स्वाध्यायनियताहार उवास विजितेन्द्रियः॥
en: But the righteous Vibhișana, ever intent on piety, dwelt there studying the Veda, restraining his fare, and controlling his senses.

sn: अथ वैश्रवणो देवस्तत्र कालेन केन चित्। आगतः पितरं द्रष्टुं पुष्पकेण धनेश्वरः॥
en: It came to pass that after a length of time the god, Vaisravana-lord of riches-came to see his sire, mounted on Puspaka.

sn: तं दृष्ट्वा कैकसी तत्र ज्वलन्तमिव तेजसा। आगम्य राक्षसी तत्र दशग्रीवमुवाच ह॥
en: Seeing him, the Raksasi-Kaikasi-flaming up in energy, coming to the Ten-necked one, represented to him.

sn: पुत्र वैश्रवणं पश्य भ्रातरं तेजसा वृतम्। भ्रातृभावे समे चापि पश्यात्मानं त्वमीदृशम्॥
en: O son, behold your brother, Vaisravana, enfolded in effulgence; and, albeit of equal fraternity, behold you in this plight!

sn: दशग्रीव तथा यत्नं कुरुष्वामितविक्रम। यथा त्वमपि मे पुत्र भवेर्वैश्रवणोपमः।॥
en: Therefore, O Ten-necked one, O you of measureless prowess, do you so strive that you also, my son, may be like Vaisravana himself.

sn: मातुस्तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा दशग्रीवः प्रतापवान्। अमर्षमतुलं लेभे प्रतिज्ञां चाकरोत्तदा।॥
en: Hearing that speech of his mother, the powerful Ten-necked one was wrought up with exceeding great ill-will, and he vowed then.

sn: सत्यं ते प्रतिजानामि भ्रातृतुल्योऽधिकोऽपि वा। भविष्याम्योजसा चैव संतापं त्यज हृद्गतम्॥
en: I truly promise to you that I will be equal to my brother (in energy), or excel him in it. Therefore do you cast off this sorrow in your heart.

sn: ततः क्रोधेन तेनैव दशग्रीवः सहानुजः। चिकीर्षुर्दुष्करं कर्म तपसे धृतमानसः॥ प्राप्स्यामि तपसा काममिति कृत्वाध्यवस्य च। आगच्छदात्मसिद्ध्यर्थं गोकर्णस्याश्रमं शुभम्।।४७
en: And influenced by that passion, the tennecked one with his younger brother began to perform rigid acts, with his mind fixed on asceticism. 'I must through austerities have my wish,' thus fixed and resolved, he compassing his end, came to the sacred asylum of Gokarna.

sn: स राक्षसस्तत्र सहानुजस्तदा तपश्चचारातुलमुग्रविक्रमः। अतोषयच्चापि पितामहं विभुं ददौ स तुष्टश्च वराञ्जयावहान॥
en: There the Rākşasa of unrivalled prowess along with his younger brother carried on austerities and thus gratified that lord-the greatfather. And being gratified (with him), he conferred on him boons bringing on victory.

sn: अथाब्रवीन्मुनि रामः कथं ते भ्रातरो भने। कीदृशं तु तदा ब्रह्मस्तपस्तेपुर्महाबलाः॥
en: Then Rāma spoke to the ascetic, O Brahmana, how did those exceedingly mighty brothers carry on austerities in that forest; and what kind of penances was theirs?

sn: अगस्त्यस्त्वब्रवीत्तत्र रामं सुप्रीतमानसम्। तांस्तान्धर्मविधींस्तत्र भ्रातरस्ते समाविशन्॥
en: Thereat there Agastya said to Rāma of a complacent mind, “The brothers severally observed the morality proper to each.”

sn: कुम्भकर्णस्ततो यत्तो नित्यं धर्मपथे स्थितः। तताप ग्रीष्मकाले तु पञ्चागनीन्परितः स्थितः॥ मेधाम्बुसिक्तो वर्षासु वीरासनमसेवत। नित्यं च शिशिरे काले जलमध्यप्रतिश्रयः॥
en: And Kumbhakarņa, putting forth his best energies, constantly abode in the path of righteousness, and remaining in the midst of five fires in summer, he practised austerities, and in the rainy season, soaked in water (poured down) by clouds, he sat in the heroic attitude.* And in winter he always remained in the water. *Hindu Yogis practise various attitudes, which are favourable to the regulation of respiration.

sn: एवं वर्षसहस्राणि दश तस्यापचक्रमुः। धर्मे प्रयतमानस्य सत्पथे निष्ठितस्य च॥
en: Thus passed away ten thousand of that one putting forth exertions in behalf of religion, and established in the path of honesty.

sn: विभीषणस्तु धर्मात्मा नित्यं धर्मपरः शुचिः। पञ्चवर्षसहस्राणि पादेनैकेन तस्थिवान्॥
en: The virtuous Vibhīşaņa, ever intent on virtue and pure of spirit, remained standing on one leg for five thousand years.

sn: समाप्ते नियमे तस्य ननृतुश्चाप्सरोगणाः। पपात पुष्पवर्षं च तुष्टवुश्चापि देवताः।७।।
en: When he had completed (his term of restriction), swarms of apsaras danced, and blossoms showered, and the deities hymned (him).

sn: पञ्चवर्षसहस्राणि सूर्यं चैवान्ववर्तत। तस्थौ चोर्ध्वशिरोबाहुः स्वाध्याये धृतमानसः॥
en: And for five thousand years, he adored the Sun, and with his mind concentrated in the study of the Veda, remained with his head and hands raised up.

sn: एवं विभीषणस्यापि स्वर्गस्थस्येव नन्दने। दशवर्षसहस्राणि गतानि नियतात्मनः॥
en: In this wise Vibhīşaņa like a deity in Nandana passed away ten thousand years, observing restrictions.

sn: दशर्वषसहस्रं तु निराहारो दशाननः। पूर्णे वर्षसहस्रे तु शिरश्चाग्नौ जुहाव सः॥
en: The ten-necked passed ten thousand years without fare. On a thousand years being complete, he offered his own head as a sacrifice to Fire.

sn: एवं वर्षसहस्राणि नव तस्यातिचक्रमुः। शिरांसि नव चाप्यस्य प्रविष्टानि हुताशनम्॥
en: In this way, he passed away nine thousand years, and nine of his heads entered into Fire.

sn: अथ वर्षसहस्त्रे तु दशमे दशमं शिरः। छेत्तुकामे दशग्रीवे प्राप्तस्तत्र पितामहः॥
en: And as in the tenth year he intended to strike off his tenth head, the Great-father (Brahmā) presented himself at that place.

sn: पितामहस्तु सुप्रीतः सार्धं देवैरुपस्थितः। तव तावद्दशग्रीव प्रीतोऽस्मीत्यभ्यभाषत॥
en: Well-pleased, the Pitamaha Brahmā came there along with the celestials. 'O Ten-necked one,' said (the Great-father), 'I am well-pleased with you.

sn: शीघ्रं वरय धर्मज्ञ वरो यस्तेऽभिकाङ्कितः। कं ते कामं करोम्यद्य न वृथा ते परिश्रमः॥
en: Do you, O cognisant of righteousness, at once ask for the boon that you wish to have. What wish of your shall I realise? Your toil must not go for nothing.

sn: अथाब्रवीद्दशग्रीवः प्रहृष्टेनान्तरात्मना। प्रणम्य शिरसा देवं हर्षगद्गदया गिरा॥
en: Thereat, the Ten-necked one, bowing down his head to the deity, said with a delighted heart, his words faltering with ecstasy.

sn: भगवन्प्राणिनां नित्यं नान्यत्र मरणाद्भयम्। नास्ति मृत्युसमः शत्रुरमरत्वमहं वृणे॥
en: O reverend one, creatures have no other fear than (that of) death; and enemy there is none that is like to death. Therefore immortality is even what I crave for.

sn: एवमुक्तस्तदा ब्रह्मा दशग्रीवमुवाच ह। नास्ति सर्वामरत्वं ते वरमन्यं वृणीष्व मे॥
en: Thus accosted, Brahma spoke to the Tennecked one, 'You can not be immortal. Do you therefore ask of me some other boon.'

sn: एवमुक्ते तदा राम ब्रह्मणा लोककर्तृणा। दशग्रीव उवाचेदं कृताञ्जलिरथाग्रतः॥
en: Thus addressed by the creator, Brahma, the Ten-necked one, O Rāma, standing before him with joined hands, said.

sn: सुपर्णनागयक्षाणां दैत्यदानवरक्षसाम्। अवध्योऽहं प्रजाध्यक्ष देवतानां च शाश्वत ॥ नहि चिन्ता ममान्येषु प्राणिष्वमरपूजित। तृणभूता हि ते मन्ये प्राणिनो मानुषादयः॥
en: O lord of creatures, I would, O external one, he incapable of being slain by birds and serpents, Yaksas, Daityas, Danavas and Raksasas, and the deities; for, O you that are worshipped by the immortals, anxiety I have none from any other beings. Indeed, I deem as straw creatures such as men etc.

sn: एवमुक्तस्तु धर्मात्मा दशग्रीवेण रक्षसा। उवाच वचनं देवः सह देवैः पितामहः॥
en: Thus accosted by the Rākşasa the Ten-necked one-that righteous-souled one, the great-father, along with the celestials, said.

sn: भविष्यत्येवमेतत्ते वचो राक्षसपुङ्गव । एवमुक्त्वा तु तं गम दशग्रीवं पितामहः॥
en: O foremost of Rākşasas, what you say shall come to pass. Having O Rāma, said this to the Ten-necked one, the Great-father (again spoke), Hear!

sn: शृणु चापि वरो भूयः प्रीतस्येह शुभो मम। हुतानि यानि शीर्षाणि पूर्वमग्नौ त्वयानघ॥ पुनस्तानि भविष्यन्ति तथैव तव राक्षस। वितरामीह ते सौम्य वरं चान्यं दुरासदम्॥ छन्दतस्तव रूपं च मनसा यद्यथेप्सितम्।
en: I, having been gratified, will confer on you a fresh boon. O Raksasa, O sinless one, those heads of your which have been offered as sacrifices and which have sunk, into the fire, shall again be your. And, a placid one, I shall also confer on you another boon difficult of being obtained, The form that you shall wish to wear, shall instantly be yours.

sn: एवं पितामहोक्तं च दशग्रीवस्य रक्षसः॥ अग्नौ हुतानि शीर्षाणि पुनस्तान्युत्थितानि वै।
en: As soon as the Ten-necked Rākṣasa had spoken, thus, the heads that had been offered as sacrifices into the fire, rose up again.

sn: एवमुक्त्वा तु तं राम दशग्रीवं पितामहः॥ विभीषणमथोवाच वाक्यं लोकपितामहः।
en: Having said this to the Ten-necked one, the. great sire of all creatures addressed Vibhīşana, saying.

sn: विभीषण त्वया वत्स धर्मसंहितबुद्धिना॥ पतितुष्टोऽस्मि धर्मात्मन्वरं वरय सुव्रत।
en: O Vibhisana, gratified have I been by you, whose intelligence is established in righteousness. Therefore, my child, O righteoussouled one, O you of excellent vows, ask for the boon that you would have.

sn: विभीषणस्तु धर्मात्मा वचनं प्राह साञ्जलिः॥ वृतः सर्वगुणैर्नित्यं चन्द्रमा रश्मिभिर्यथा। भगवन्कृतकृत्योऽहं यन्मे लोकगुरुः स्वयम्॥ प्रीतेन यदि दातव्यो वरो मे शृणु सुव्रत ।
en: Thereat the virtuous Vibhīşaņa spoke with joined hands, 'O reverend one, since the spiritual preceptor of all creatures himself (is pleased) with me, I (deem myself) as furnished with every perfection, even as the Moon is envisioned with rays. If you will bestow on me a boon with pleasure, then, O you of excellent vows, hear of the boon that I would have.

sn: परमापद्गतस्यापि धर्मे मम मतिर्भवेत्॥ अशिक्षितं च ब्रह्मास्त्रं भगवन्प्रतिभातु मे।
en: May my mind remained fast fixed on righteousness, even when I shall happen to fall into high peril; and may I attain Brahma knowledge without any instructions!

sn: या या मे जायते बुद्धिर्येषु येष्वाश्रमेषु च॥ सा सा भवतु धर्मिष्ठा तं तं धर्म च पालये। एष मे परमोदार वरः परमको मतः॥ नहि धर्माभिरक्तानां लोके किंचन दुर्लभम्। पुनः प्रजापतिः प्रीतो विभीषणमुवाच ह॥
en: And inay every sense of mine sprung during the observance of particular modes of life, be in unison with righteousness, so that I may practice the form of religion (in harmony with any particular mode of life !) O exceedingly noble one, this best of boons, is even what is sought for by me, for nothing in this world is incapable of being attained by those attached to righteousness.' Then the lord of creatures, being again delighted, spoke to Vibhīşaņa.

sn: धर्मिष्ठ त्वं यथा वत्स तथा चैतद्भविष्यति। यस्माद्राक्षसयोनौ ते जातस्यामित्रनाशन॥ नाधर्मे जायते बुद्धिरमरत्वं ददामि ते। इत्युक्त्वा कुम्भकर्णाय वरं दातुमवस्थितम्॥
en: As you are virtuous, so all this shall come to pass on your behalf. And inasmuch as in spite of your having been born in the Rākṣasa race, your thoughts, ( destroyer of enemies, do not originate in sin, I confer on the immortality. Having said this, he intended to grant boons to Kumbhakarna.

sn: प्रजापतिं सुराः सर्वे वाक्यं प्राञ्जलयोऽब्रुवन्। न तावत्कुम्भकर्णाय प्रदातव्यो वरस्त्वया॥ जानीषे हि यथा लोकांस्त्रासयत्येष दुर्मतिः।
en: Thereat the celestials in a body represented to the lord of creatures with joined hands. 'On Kumbhakarņa you should confer no boons, since you know in what manner does this wickedminded one frighten people.

sn: नन्दनेऽप्सरसः सप्त महेन्द्रानुचरा दश॥ अनेन भक्षिता ब्रह्मऋषयो मानुषास्तथा।
en: And, O Brāhmaṇa, even Apsarās in Nandana, ten attendants of Mahendra, as well as sages and human beings, have been devoured by this one.

sn: अलब्धवरपूर्णेन यत्कृतं राक्षसेन तु॥ यद्येष वरलब्धः स्याद्भक्षयेद्भुवनत्रयम्।
en: Considering what this Rākşasa did when he had not obtained any boon whatever, if he obtain one now, he shall eat up the three worlds.

sn: वरव्याजेन मोहोऽस्मै दीयताममितप्रभ॥ लोकानां स्वस्ति चैवं स्याद्भवेदस्य च संमतिः।
en: Do you then, o lord having immeasurable prowess, pretending to give him a boon, give stupefaction (instead). Thereby the welfare of the people would be secured, and the honour of this one too shall be maintained.

sn: एवमुक्तः सुरैर्ब्रह्माचिन्तयत्पद्मसंभवः॥ चिन्तिता चोपतस्थेऽस्य पार्श्व देवी सरस्वती।
en: Thus addressed by the celestials, Brahmā, the Lotus-sprung one, pondered. The goddess, Sarasvatī, who was by his side was also agitated by anxiety.

sn: प्राञ्जलिः सा तु पार्श्वस्था प्राह वाक्यं सरस्वती॥ इयमस्म्यागता देव किं कार्य करवाण्यहम्।
en: And remaining by him, Sarasvatī with joined hands observed, 'O god, I have come here. What work shall I accomplish?'

sn: प्रजापतिस्तुं तां प्राप्तां प्राह वाक्यं सरस्वतीम्॥ वाणि त्वं राक्षसेन्द्रस्य भव वाग्देवतेप्सिता।
en: And the lord of creatures, on having her, spoke to Sarasvatī,' O Vāņi!' be you the goddess of speech of this foremost of Rākşasas, favourable to the deities. 1. Lit. word, a designation of Saraswati. 2. i.e. preside over Kumbhakarna's speech while asking for the boon, and let him, through your power, ask for such a gift as may turn our profitable to the gods.

sn: तथेत्युक्त्वा प्रविष्टा सा प्रजापतिरथाब्रवीत्॥ कुम्भकर्ण महाबाहो वरं वरय यो मतः।
en: Having said, 'So be it,' she entered (within Kumbhakarna's throat); and Prajapati said,' O Kumbhakarma, O mighty-armed one, do you ask for the boon that you would have.

sn: कुम्भकर्णस्तु तद्वाक्यं श्रुत्वा वचनमब्रवीत्॥ स्वप्तुं वर्षाण्यनेकानि देवदेव ममेप्सितम्। एवमस्त्विति तं चोक्त्वा प्रायाद्ब्रह्मा सुरैः समम् ।।४५ । देवी सरस्वती चैव राक्षसं तं जहौ पुनः। ब्रह्मणा सह देवेषु गतेषु च नभःस्थलम्॥ विमुक्तोऽसौ सरस्वत्या स्वां संज्ञां च ततो गतः। कुम्भकर्णस्तु दुष्टात्मा चिन्तयामास दुःखितः॥
en: Hearing those words, Kumbhakarņa said,' O god of gods, my wish is that I may sleep for a good many years.' Thereupon, saying,' So be it, “Brahmä along with the celestials went away; and the goddess, Sarasvati, also again left the Rākşasa. And on Brahmă accompanied by the deities going to the celestial regions, he was renounced by Sarasvatī, and then he regained his consciousness. And then the wicked-minded Kumbhakarņa sorrowfully thought.

sn: ईदृशं किमिदं वाक्यं ममाद्य वदनाच्च्युतम्। अहं व्यामोहितो देवैरिति मन्ये तदागतैः॥
en: What is this speech that has to-day come out from my lips? Meseems I had then been stupefied by the deities that had come.

sn: एवं लब्धवराः सर्वे भ्रातरो दीप्ततेजसः। श्लेष्मातकवनं गत्वा तत्र ते न्यवसन्सुखम्॥
en: Having thus obtained the boons, the brothers endowed with flaming energy, going to the Śleşmātaka wood, began to dwell there peacefully.

sn: सुमाली वरलब्धांस्तु ज्ञात्वा चैतानिशाचरान्। उदतिष्ठद्भयं त्यक्त्वा सानुगः स रसातलात्॥
en: Learning that these night-rangers had obtained boons, Sumāli with his followers, casting off fear, rose up from the nether regions.

sn: मारीचश्च प्रहस्तश्च विरूपाक्षो महोदरः। उदतिष्ठन्सुसंरब्धाः सचिवास्तस्य रक्षसः॥
en: And wrought up with exceeding great wrath, the counsellors of that Rākşasas-Mārīca and Prahasta and Virūpākṣa and Mahodara-also rose up.

sn: सुमाली सचिवैः सार्धं वृतो राक्षसपुङ्गवैः। अभिगम्य दशग्रीवं परिष्वज्येदमब्रवीत्॥
en: Accompanied by his counsellors-foremost of Rākşasas-Sumāli presenting himself before the Ten-necked one and embracing him, addressed him, saying.

sn: दिष्ट्या ते वत्स संप्राप्तश्चिन्तितोऽयं मनोरथः। यस्त्वं त्रिभुवनश्रेष्ठाल्लब्धवान्वरमुत्तमम्॥
en: By good fortune it is, O child, that through you we have had the wish that was in our heart, inasmuch as you have received the best of boons from him that is the foremost of all these three worlds.

sn: यत्कृते च वयं लङ्कां त्यक्त्वा याता रसातलम्। तद्गतं नो महाबाहो महद्विष्णुकृतं भयम्॥
en: O mighty-armed one, that great fear arising from Vişnu, from which leaving Larkā, we had gone to the nethermost abysses, has been removed.

sn: असकृत्तद्भयाद्भग्नाः परित्यज्य स्वमालयम्। विदूताः सहिताः सर्वे प्रविष्टाः स्म रसातलम् ॥
en: Full many a time, brought down by that fear, we, on being pursued (by our enemies), forsaking our homes, had gone to the nether regions along with all those (related to us).

sn: अस्मदीया च लङ्केयं नगरी राक्षसोषिता। निवेशिता तव भ्रात्रा धनाध्यक्षेण धीमता॥
en: This Lankā was our city, inhabited by Rākşasas. (Now) it is inhabited by the brotherthe intelligent lord of riches.

sn: यदि नामात्र शक्यं स्यात्साम्ना दानेन वानघ। तरसा वा महाबाहो प्रत्यानेतुं कृतं भवेत्॥ त्वं च लङ्केश्वरस्तात भविष्यसि न संशयः। त्वया राक्षसवंशोऽयं निमग्नोऽपि समुद्धृतः॥
en: O mighty-armed one, if you can through selfcontrol or charity or by a sudden display of prowess, repossesses yourself of the same, a (great) thing shall have been achieved; and then, O child, you should, without doubt, be the lord of Lankā; and this Raksasa race, which has sunk, shall have been raised up by you.

sn: सर्वेषां नः प्रभुश्चैव भविष्यसि महाबल। अथाब्रवीद्दशग्रीवो मातामहमुपस्थितम्॥
en: O you endowed with prodigious strength, you shall be the lord of all. Then the Ten-necked one addressed his maternal grand-father, who was present.

sn: वित्तेशो गुरुरस्माकं नार्हसे वक्तुमीदृशम्। साम्ना हि राक्षसेन्द्रेण प्रत्याख्यातो गरीयसा॥ किंचिन्नाह तदा रक्षो ज्ञात्वा तस्य चिकीर्षितम्।
en: The lord of riches is our superior; therefore you ought not to speak thus. On that dignified were Rākşasa-chief having through moderation thus passed it by, that Rākşasa, understanding his intent, did not then say anything more.

sn: कस्यचित्त्वथ कालस्य वसन्तं रावणं ततः॥ प्रहस्तः प्रश्रितं वाक्यमिदमाह स रावणम्।
en: It came to pass that when Rāvana had resided there for a time, Prahasta addressed him in humble speech.

sn: दशग्रीव महाबाहो नार्हसे वक्तुमीदृशम्॥ सौभ्रात्रं नास्ति शूराणां शृणु चेदं वचो मम।
en: O Ten-necked one, O long-armed (hero), it does not behove you to speak thus. Faternal feeling there is none among heroes. Listen to these words of mine!

sn: अदितिश्च दितिश्चैव भगिन्यौ सहिते हि ते॥ भार्ये परमरूपिण्यौ कश्यपस्य प्रजापतेः।
en: There two sisters-Aditi and Diti, mutually attached to each other, those (damsels) endowed with surpassing beauty, became the wives of that lord of creatures-Kaśyapa.

sn: अदितिर्जनयामास देवांस्त्रिभुवनेश्वरान्॥ दितिस्त्वजनयदैत्यान्कश्यपस्यात्मसंभवान्।
en: Aditi brought forth the gods, who are the lords of three worlds. And Diti gave birth to the Daityas, offspring of Kasyapa.

sn: दैत्यानां किल धर्मज्ञ पुरेयं वसनार्णवा॥ सपर्वता मही वीर तेऽभवन्प्रभविष्णवः। निहत्य तांस्तु समरे विष्णुना प्रभविष्णुना ॥ देवानां वशमानीतं त्रैलोक्यमिदमव्ययम्।
en: O you cognisant of righteousness, formerly this earth, O hero, having the ocean for her garment, and furnished with mountains, belonged to the Daityas; and (gradually) they grew very powerful. And then this undeteriorating triune world was brought under the dominion of the celestials.

sn: नैतदेको भवानेव करिष्यति विपर्ययम्॥ सुरासुरैराचरितं तत्कुरुष्व वचो मम।
en: So that you are not the only one that would act inimically (to your brother); but this course had formerly been pursued by both the celestials and the Asuras. Therefore do you act in conformity with my word.

sn: एवमुक्तो दशग्रीवः प्रहृष्टेनान्तरात्मना॥ चिन्तयित्वा मुहूर्त वै बाढमित्येव सोऽब्रवीत्। स तु तेनैव हर्षेण तस्मिनहनि वीर्यवान्॥ वनं गतो दशग्रीवः सह तैः क्षणदाचरैः।
en: Thus exhorted, the Ten-necked one, with a delighted heart, reflecting for a moment, said, 'Very well.' And wrought up with delight, the Ten-necked one endowed with prowess the very same day went to the forest, accompanied by the night-rangers.

sn: त्रिकूटस्थः स तु तदा दशग्रीवो निशाचरः॥ प्रेषयामास दौत्येन प्रहस्तं वाक्यकोविदः।
en: Arriving at Trikuta, that one skilled in speechthe night-ranger, Ravana-sent Prahasta in the ca vacity of an ambassador:

sn: प्रहस्त शीघ्रं गच्छ त्वं ब्रूहि नैर्ऋतपुङ्गवम्॥ वचसा मम वित्तेशं सामपूर्वमिदं वचः।
en: O Prahasta, hie you; and tell the foremost of Naiſtas-the lord of riches-in my words informed with mildness.

sn: इयं लङ्का पुरी राजनराक्षसानां महात्मनाम्॥ त्वया निवेशिता सौम्य नैतद्युक्तं तवानघ।
en: This city of Lankā, O king, belongs to the high-souled Rākṣasas; but you have established yourself in her. This, O sinless one, is not proper for you.

sn: तद्भवान्यदि नो ह्यद्य दद्यादतुलविक्रम॥ कृता भवेन्मम प्रीतिर्धर्मश्चैवानुपालितः।
en: Therefore, O you of unrivalled prowess, if you should render the same (back), I shall be highly gratified; and righteousness also you will maintain.

sn: स तु गत्वा पुरीं लङ्कां धनदेन सुरक्षिताम्॥ अब्रवीत्परमोदारं वित्तपालमिदं वचः।
en: Thereupon, repairing to Lankā, well-protected by the giver of riches, Prahasta communicated these words to the highly generous ruler of riches.

sn: प्रेषितोऽहं तव भ्रात्रा दशग्रीवेण सुव्रत॥ त्वत्समीपं महाबाहो सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वर। वचनं मम वित्तेश यद्ब्रवीति दशाननः॥
en: O you of excellent vows, I have been sent to you by your brother, the Ten-necked one. O long-armed one, O foremost of those versed in all branches of learning, do you listen to my words, O lord of wealth, and what the Ten-faced one says.

sn: इयं किल पुरी रम्या सुमालिप्रमुखैः पुरा। भुक्तपूर्वा विशालाक्ष राक्षसैर्भीपविक्रमैः॥ तेन विज्ञाप्यते सोऽयं सांप्रतं विश्रवात्मज। तदेषा दीयतां तात याचतस्तस्य सामतः॥
en: This beautiful city, O you furnished with expansive eyes, was formerly inhabited by Räkşasas of dreadful prowess headed by Sumāli; and for that reason, O son of Viśravā, he asks you this. Do you, my child, grant this to him, who is humbly begging for it.

sn: प्रहस्तादपि संश्रुत्य देवो वैश्रवणो वचः। प्रत्युवाच प्रहस्तं तं वाक्यं वाक्यविदां वरः॥
en: Hearing these words from Prahasta, the god Vaiśravaņa, best of those skilled in speech, answered the former.

sn: दत्ता ममेयं पित्रा तु लङ्का शून्या निशाचरैः। निवेशिता च मे रक्षो दानमानादिभिर्गुणैः॥
en: My father had given this to me, when it had been emptied of night-rangers; and, O Raksasa, I have inhabited this place, furnished with charity, honour and other virtues.

sn: ब्रूहि गच्छ दशग्रीवं पुरी राज्यं च यन्मम। तवाप्येतन्महाबाहो भुक्ष्व राज्यमकण्टकम्॥
en: Go and tell the Ten-necked one, as this city and this kingdom are mine, so they are your, O mighty-armed one. Do you enjoy this kingdom without a foe.

sn: अतिभक्तं त्वया सार्धं राज्यं यच्चापि मे वसु। एवमुक्त्वा धनाध्यक्षो जगाम पितुरन्तिकम्॥ अभिवाद्य गुरुं प्राह रावणस्य यदीप्सितम्। एष तात दशग्रीवो दूतं प्रेषितवान्मम॥ दीयतां नगरी लङ्का पूर्वं रक्षोगणोषिता। मयात्र यदनुष्ठेयं तन्ममाचक्ष्व सुव्रत॥
en: May my kingdom and wealth never undergo division when you are present! 'Having said this, the lord of riches sought the side of his sire, and, paying him reverence, he communicated Ravana's wish to him:' My father, this Tennecked one had sent a messenger to me, saying, Give (back) the city Lankā, which had before been inhabited by hosts of Rakşasa. Now, O you of excellent vows, do you tell me what I should do.

sn: ब्रह्मर्षिस्त्वेवमुक्तोऽसौ विश्रवा मुनिपुंगवः। प्राञ्जलिं धनदं प्राह शृणु पुत्र वचो मम॥
en: Thus accosted, that foremost of ascetics, the Brahmarși Viśravă spoke to the lord of riches (standing) with joined hands, 'O son, listen to my words.

sn: दशग्रीवो महाबाहुरुक्तवान्मम संनिधौ। मया निर्भर्त्सतश्चासीद्बहुशोक्तः सुदुर्मतिः॥ स क्रोधेन मया चोक्तो ध्वंससे च पुनः पुनः।
en: The mighty-armed Ten-necked one had (once); spoken in my presence (to that effect). Thereat I greatly rebuked that wicked-minded one; and I said again and again in anger, You disregard (your religion and honour).

sn: श्रेयोऽभियुक्तं धयं च शृणु पुत्र वचो मम॥ वरप्रदानसंमूढो मान्यामान्यं सुदुर्मतिः। न वेत्ति मम शापाच्च प्रकृति दारुणां गतः॥
en: Do you listen to my words fraught with religion and profit. Of a wicked heart, you, with your understanding spoilt in consequence of the granting of the boon, can not distinguish between those deserving honour and those not; and, further, through my curse, you have come by fierce nature.

sn: तस्माद्गच्छ महाबाहो कैलासं धरणीधरम्। निवेशय निवासार्थं त्यक्त्वा लङ्कां सहानुगः॥
en: Therefore, O mighty-armed one, go to the mountain, Kailasa. Do you, along with your retainers, for the purpose of dwelling there, take up your quarters (there).

sn: तत्र मन्दाकिनी रम्या नदीनामुत्तमा नदी. काञ्चनैः सूर्यसंकाशैः पङ्कजैः संवृतोदका॥ कुमुदैरुत्पलैश्चैव अन्यैश्चैव सुगन्धिभिः।
en: There flowes the Mandākini best of streams, with her water covered with golden lotuses resembling suns, as also with lilies and blue lotuses and various other fragment flowers.

sn: तत्र देवाः सगन्धर्वाः साप्सरोरगकिंनराः।॥ विहारशीलाः सततं रमन्ते सर्वदाश्रिताः। नहि क्षमं तवानेन वैरं धनद रक्षसा। जानीषे हि यथानेन लब्धः परमको वरः।॥
en: And coming there frequently, celestials with Gandharvas and Apsarās and serpents and Kinnaras, ever sport there. O lord of riches, you ought not to enter into hostilities with that Raksasa. You know how he has obtained a great boon.

sn: एवमुक्तो गृहीत्वा तु तद्वचः पितृगौरवात्। सदारपुत्रः सामात्यः सवाहनधनो गतः॥
en: Thus addressed, Vaisravana, for the sake of his father's dignity, with his wives and sons, with his counsellors and his vehicles and wealth went (to Kailasa).

sn: प्रहस्तोऽथ दशग्रीवं गत्वा वचनमब्रवीत्। प्रहृष्टात्मा महात्मानं महामात्यं सहाजुनम् ॥
en: And Prahasta, going (back), joyfully spoke to the high-souled Ten-necked one, (seated) with his counsellors and his younger brothers.

sn: शून्या सा नगरी लङ्का त्यक्त्त्वैनां धनदो गतः। प्रविश्य तां महास्माभिः स्वधर्म तत्र पालयः॥
en: The city of Lanka is (now) empty. Renouncing her, the bestower of riches has gone out of her. (Now) entering into her, along with us, do you there maintain your own religion.

sn: एवमुक्तो दशग्रीवः प्रहस्तेन महाबलः। विवेश नगरी लङ्का भ्रातृभिः सबलानुगैः॥ धनदेन परित्यक्तां सुविभक्तमहापथाम्। आरुरोह स देवारिः स्वर्ग देवाधिपो यथा॥
en: Thus addressed by Prahasta, the redoubtable Ten-necked one, entered the city of Lanka with his brothers and forces and followers. And then even as the lord of the celestials ascends heaven, that foe of the immortals ascended Lanka welldivided by highways, which had been forsaken by the lord of wealth.

sn: स चाभिषिक्तः क्षणदाचरैस्तदा निवेशयामास पुरी दशाननः। निकामपूर्णा च बभूव सा पुरी निशाचरैर्नीलबलाहकोपमैः।॥
en: Having been installed, that night-ranger the Ten-faced one dwelt in that city; and that city teemed with night-rangers resembling dark clouds.

sn: वेशयच्छशिविमले गिरौ पुरीम्। स्वलंकृतैर्भवनवरैर्विभूषितां पुरंदरः स्वरिव यथामरावतीम्॥
en: The lord of riches, for the sake of his father's dignity, dwelt in a palace situated on the hill bright as moon-light, graced with ornamented superb piles; even as Purandara dwells in Amaravati.

sn: राक्षसेन्द्रोऽभिषिक्तस्तु भ्रातृभिः सहितस्तदा। ततः प्रदानं राक्षस्या भगिन्याः समचिन्तयत्॥
en: The lord of Räkşasas was installed along with his brothers. And then he thought of the giving away in marriage of his Rakşasi sister.

sn: ददौ तां कालकेन्द्राय दानवेन्द्राय राक्षसीम्। स्वसां शूर्पणखां नाम विद्युज्जिह्वाय राक्षसः॥
en: Then that Raksasa bestowed his sister, the Rākşasī Śūrpanakhā, on that lord of the Dänavas and king of the Kālakeśa Vidyujjihvä.

sn: अथ दत्त्वा स्वयं रक्षो मृगयामटते स्म तत्। तत्रापश्यत्ततो राम मयं नाम दितेः सुतम्॥ कन्यासहायं तं दृष्ट्वा दशग्रीवो निशाचरः। अपृच्छत्को भवानेको निर्मनुष्यमृगे वने॥ अनया मृगशावाक्ष्या किमर्थं सह तिष्ठसि। मयस्तदाब्रवीद्राम पृच्छन्तं तं निशाचरम्॥
en: Having given her away, the Rākşasa was wandering about for the purpose of hunting, when, o Rāma, he happened to see Diti's son, named Maya. And seeing him accompanied by his daughter, that night-ranger the Ten-necked one asked him, saying, 'Who are you that (wanderest) alone in this first devoid of men as well as deer? And are you accompanied by this one having the eyes of a young deer?' Thereat Maya, O Rama, answered that nightranger, when he had asked this.

sn: श्रूयतां सर्वमाख्यास्ये यथावृत्तमिदं तव। हेमा नामाप्सरास्तत्र श्रुतपूर्वा यदि त्वया ॥ दैवतैर्मम सा दत्ता पौलोमीव शतक्रतोः। तस्यां भक्तमना ह्यासं दशवर्षशतान्यहम्॥ सा च दैवतकार्येण त्रयोदश समा गताः। वर्ष चतुर्दशं चैव ततो हेममयं पुरम्॥ वज्रवैदूर्यचित्रं च मायया निर्मितं मया। तत्राहमवसं दीनस्तया हीनः सुदुःखितः।।।।
en: 'Listen. I shall tell you all about this. You may ere this have heard of an Apsarā named Hemā. She like to the Paulomi of Satakratu was bestowed on me, by the gods. And I passed a thousand years, being devoted her. Thirteen years have passed away since she had gone on a business of the celestials, as also the fourteenth year. Then I through my extraordinary skill constructed a golden palace, adorned with diamond and lapises. There I dwelt, aggrieved and sorrowful on account of her separation.

sn: तस्मात्पुरा दुहितरं गृहीत्वा वनमागतः। इयं ममात्मजा राजंस्तस्याः कुक्षौ विवर्धिता॥
en: From then, taking my daughter, I have come to this wood. This, O king, is my daughter, grown in her womb.

sn: भर्तारमनया सार्धमस्याः प्राप्तोऽस्मि मार्गितुम्। कन्यापितृत्वं दुःखं हि सर्वेषां मानकाङ्क्षिणाम्॥ कन्या हि द्वे कुले नित्यं संशये स्थाप्य तिष्ठति।
en: I have come hither with her, seeing of her husband. Verily being father to a daughter is misery to everyone that seekes one's honour. A daughter, forsooth, stayes, ever placing the two lines* in uncertainity. *The lines, namely, of her father and mother. The line of a mother as distinct from that of a father would be impossible under the present economy of Hindu society inasmuch as, as soon as a girl is married, she by that ceremony leaves her father's line and becomes incorporated with that of her husband. But this seems to have been otherwise in ancient times, This opens up an interesting social problem for the research of orientalists.

sn: पुत्रद्वयं ममाप्यस्यां भार्यायां संबभूव ह॥ मायावी प्रथमस्तात दुन्दुभिस्तदनन्तरः।
en: On this wife of mine I have also beget two sons. The first is Māyāvī and the next Dundubhi.

sn: एवं ते सर्वमाख्यातं यथातथ्येन पृच्छतः॥ त्वामिदानी कथं तात जानीयां को भवानिति।
en: Thus have I truly related to everything to you that had asked for it. But, my child, how can I know you now? Who are you?

sn: एवमुक्तं तु तद्रक्षो विनीतमिदमब्रवीत्॥ अहं पौलस्त्यतनयो दशग्रीवश्च नामतः। मुनेर्विश्रवसो यस्तु तृतीयो ब्रह्मणोऽभवत्॥
en: Thus addressed, the Rākşasas humbly said, 'Ten-necked by name, I am the son of ascetic, Paulastya, who was born as the third son of Brahmā.

sn: एवमुक्तस्तदा राम राक्षसेन्द्रेण दानवः। महर्षेस्तनयं ज्ञात्वा मयो दानवपुङ्गवः॥ दातुं दुहितरं तस्मै रोचयामास तत्र वै।
en: Thus accosted, O Rama, by that lord of Raks asas, that Dänava and foremost of Dānavas, Maya; learning that he was the son of Maharsi, Paulastya, there desired in his heart to give away his daughter to him.

sn: करेण तु करं तस्या ग्राहयित्वा मयस्तदा॥ प्रहसन्प्राह दैत्येन्द्रो राक्षसेन्द्रमिदं वचः।
en: Taking her hand with his own, Maya, the lord of Daityas, laughing said to that lord of Raksasas.

sn: इयं ममात्मजा राजन्हेमयाप्सरसा धृता ॥ कन्या मन्दोदरी नाम पल्यर्थं प्रतिगृह्यताम्।
en: This daughter of mine, O king, O king, borne by the Apsarā, Hemā, this my daughter named Mandodari do you accept as my wife.

sn: बाढमित्येव तं राम दशग्रीवोऽभ्यभाषत ॥ प्रज्वाल्य तत्र चैवाग्निमकरोत्पाणिसंग्रहम्।
en: 'Well' thereupon the Ten-necked answered him, O Rāma. And lighting a fire, he took her hand.

sn: स हि तस्य मयो राम शापाभिज्ञस्तपोधनात्॥ विदित्वा तेन सा दत्ता तस्य पैतामहं कुलम्। अमोघां तस्य शक्तिं च प्रददौ परमाद्भुताम् ॥ परेण तपसा लब्धां जनिवाँल्लक्ष्मणं यया।
en: O Rāma, Maya knew the curse of the sage touching him.* Knowing this, he gave away his daughter, having regard to the race of Ravana's paternal grand-father; and he also conferred on him an exceedingly wonderful dart acquired through the most rigid austerities, by which he wounded Laksmana. *Respecting his birth.

sn: एवं स कृत्वा दारान्वै लङ्काया ईश्वरः प्रभुः॥ गत्वा तु नगरी भार्ये भ्रातृभ्यां समुपाहरत्।
en: Having thus wedded, that master-Lankā's lord-going (back) to that city, married his brothers.

sn: वैरोचनस्य दौहित्रीं वज्रज्वालेति नामतः॥ तां भार्यां कुम्भकर्णस्य रावणः समकल्पयत्। गन्धर्वराजस्य सुतां शैलूषस्य महात्मनः॥ सरमां नाम धर्मज्ञां लेभे भार्यां विभीषणः।
en: Rāvana married the grand-daughter of Virocana (on the maternal side) named Vajrajvālā, to Kumbhakarņa. And Vibhīşaņa obtained for his wife the righteous (damsel) named Saramā-daughter to the high-souled Sailusa-sovereign of the Gandharvas.

sn: तीरे तु सरसो वै तु संजज्ञे मानसस्य हि॥ सरस्तदा मानसं तु ववृधे जलदागमे। मात्रा तु तस्याः कन्यायाः स्नेहेनाक्रन्दितं वचः॥ सरो मा वर्धतेत्युक्तं ततः सा सरमाभवत्।
en: Saramā was born on the shores of the lake, Mānasa, was swollen with water on the arrival of the rains, her mother, hearing her cries, affectionately said, Saro mā varddhata 'O lake, do not swell,' and from this circumstance, her name became Saramā.

sn: एवं ते कृतदारा वै रेमिरे तत्र राक्षसाः॥ स्वां स्वां भार्यामुपादाय गन्धर्वा इव नन्दने। ततो मन्दोदरी पुत्रं मेघनादमजीजनत्॥ स एष इन्द्रजिन्नाम युष्माभिरभिधीयते।
en: Having thus wedded, those Rākşasas, taking each his wife, set about sporting there, like to Gandharvas sporting in Nandana. And then was born Mandodari's son-Meghanāda. Him you call Indarjit.

sn: जातमात्रेण हि पुरा तेन रावणसूनुना॥ रुदता सुमहान्मुक्तो नादो जलधरोपमः।
en: As soon as he was born, Ravana's son, formerly crying, emitted a tremendous roar resembling the rumbling of clouds.

sn: जडीकृता च सा लङ्का तस्य नादेन राघव॥ पिता तस्याकरोन्नाम मेघनाद इति स्वयम्।
en: O Rāghava, Lankā was petrified at his voice: and (accordingly) his sire himself kept his name, Meghanāda.

sn: सोवर्धत तदा राम रावणान्तःपुरे शुभे ॥ रक्ष्यमाणो वरस्त्रीभिश्छन्नः काष्ठैरिवानलः। मातापित्रोर्हहाहर्ष जनयन्रावणात्मजः॥
en: O Rāma, remaining hidden like a fire by fuel, Ravana's son, rejoicing (the bosoms of) his father and mother, grew up in Rāvana's elegant inner apartments.

sn: अथ लोकेश्वरोत्सृष्टा तब कालेन केन चित्। निद्रा समभवत्तीव्रा कुम्भकर्णस्य रूपिणी॥
en: Once upon a time in came to pass that, despatched by the lord of creatures, Steep in her (native) form powerfully overpowered Kumbhakarna.

sn: ततो भ्रातरमासीनं कुम्भकर्णोऽब्रवीद्वचः। निद्रा मां बाधते राजन्कारयस्व ममालयम्॥
en: Then Kumbhakarņa spoke to his brother, who was seated, 'O king, Sleep obstructs me. Do you, therefore, have my mansion made.

sn: विनियुक्तास्ततो राज्ञा शिल्पनो विश्वकर्मवत्। विस्तीर्ण योजनं स्निग्धं ततो द्विगुणमायतम्॥ दर्शनीयं निराबाधं कुम्भकर्णस्य चक्रिरे। स्फाटिकैः काञ्चश्चित्रैः स्तम्भैः सर्वत्र शोभितम्॥ वैदूर्यकृतसोपानं किङ्किणीजालकं तथा। दान्ततोरणविन्यस्तं वज्रस्फटिकवेदिकम्।५।। मनोहरं सर्वसुखं कारयामास राक्षसः। सर्वत्र सुखदं नित्यं मेरोः पुण्यां गुहामिव ॥
en: Thereupon, employed by the king, architects resembling Viśvakarmă constructed an edifice beautiful to behold, measuring the smooth space of a Yojana diagonally and two in area; graceful to the view and having no obstruction (to hide its beauty). And the Rākşasa caused a splendid and delightful pile to be built, adorned all round with pillars decked with gold and crystal, having stairs composed of lapises, furnished with networks of small bells, set with ivory gateways, and containing daises-dight with diamonds and crystal elegant throughout, and enduring, like to a goodly cave of Maru.

sn: तत्र निद्रां समाविष्टः कुम्भकर्णो महाबलः। बहून्यब्दसहस्राणि शयानो न च बुद्ध्यते॥
en: There, overcome with slumber, the wondrous strong Kumbhakarņa, lying down for many thousand years, did not wake up.

sn: निद्राभिभूते तु तदा कुम्भकर्णे दशाननः। देवर्षियक्षगन्धर्वान्संजघ्ने हि निरङ्कुशः॥ उद्यानानि विचित्राणि नन्दनादीनि यानि च। तानि गत्वा सुसंक्रुद्धो भिनत्ति स्म दशाननः॥
en: While Kumbhakarna was overpowered by sleep, Daśānana* without let began to destroy Devarşis, Yakşas and Gandharvas, and going to graceful gardens, Nandana, etc., he devastated them (ruthlessly). *Henceforth we shall use this significant surname of Rāvana, meaning Ten-faced.

sn: नदी गज इव क्रीडन्वृक्षान्वायुरिव क्षिपन्। नगान्वज्र इवोत्सृष्टो विध्वंसयति राक्षसः॥
en: That Rākşasa spread destruction, even as an elephant sporting agitates a river, as the wind bring down trees, or as the thunder-bolt rive mountain-peaks.

sn: यथावृत्तं तु विज्ञाय दशग्रीवं धनेश्वरः। कुलानुरूपं धर्मज्ञो वृत्तं संस्मृत्य चात्मनः॥ सौभ्रात्रदर्शनार्थं तु दूतं वैश्रवणस्तदा। लङ्कां संप्रेषयामास दशग्रीवस्य वै हितम्॥
en: Hearing of the doings of Dasagrīva,* and remembering his conduct chiming in with his race, the righteous lord of riches Vaisravanashowing his fraternal affection, despatched a messenger to Lankā, seeking the welfare of Dasagriva. *Ten-necked.

sn: स गत्वा नगरी लङ्काससाद विभीषणम्। मानितस्तेन धर्मेण पृष्टश्चागमनं प्रति॥
en: Going to the city of Lankā, he presented himself before Vibhīşaņa. And having received him with honour, he asked him as to the cause of his visit.

sn: पृष्ट्वा च कुशलं राज्ञो ज्ञातीनां च बिभीषणः। सभायां दर्शयामास तमासीनं दशाननम्॥
en: Having enquired after the welfare of the king as well as his kindred, Vibhīşaņa, showed him to Daśānana seated in his court.

sn: स दृष्ट्वा तत्र राजानं दीप्यमानं स्वतेजसा। जयेति वाचा संपूज्य तूष्णीं समभिवर्तते॥
en: Seeing the king there flaming in his own energy, he (the messenger), saluting him (Rāvana) with the word Jaya* stood silent. *Jaya may mean (1) victory and (2) all the deities of the Hindu pantheon.

sn: स तत्रोत्तमपर्यङ्के वरास्तरणशोभिते। उपविष्टं दशग्रीवं दूतो वाक्यमथाब्रवीत्॥
en: The envoy addressed Dasagrīva, seated on a superb couch, graced with a costly coverlet.

sn: राजन्वदामि ते सर्व भ्राता तव यदब्रवीत्। उभयोः सदृशं वीर वृत्तस्य च कुलस्य च ॥ साधु पर्याप्तमेतावत्कृत्यश्चारिक्षसंग्रहः। साधु धर्मे व्यवस्थानं क्रियतां यदि शक्यते॥ दृष्टं मे नन्दनं भग्नमृषयो निहताः श्रुताः। देवतानां समुद्योगस्त्वत्तो राजन्मया श्रुतः॥
en: O king, I shall tell you all that your brother has said, worthy of both the character and race of your father and mother, Enough of wrong doing. Now you should mend your ways. If you can, stay in righteousness. I have seen Nandana ravaged; and I have heard of the sages slain, and Oking, of the preparations the deities are making against you.

sn: निराकृतश्च बहुशस्त्वयाह राक्षसाधिप। सापराधोऽपि बालो हि रक्षितव्यः स्वबान्धवैः।।२०
en: I have been utterly disregarded by you; but even if a boy should transgress, he should, for all that be protected by his family members.

sn: अहं तु हिमवत्पृष्ठं गतो धर्ममुपासितुम्। रौद्रं व्रतं समास्थाय नियतो नियतेन्द्रियः॥
en: Self-restrained and controlling my senses, I, adopting a terrific vow, had gone to the breast to the Himavān for practising righteousness.

sn: तत्र देवो मया दृष्ट उमया सहितः प्रभुः। सव्यं चक्षुर्मया दैवात्तत्र देव्यां निपातितम् ॥ कान्वेषेति महाराज न खल्वन्येन हेतुना। रूपं चानुपमं कृत्वा रुद्राणी तत्र तिष्ठति ॥
en: There I saw that lord of the gods in company with Umā. There I happened to cast my left eye on the goddess, for ‘knowing, O mighty king, who she was, and not for any other reason. Rudrāņi was staying then, wearing a surpassing form.

sn: देव्या दिव्यप्रभावेण दग्धं सव्यं ममेक्षणम्। रेणुध्वस्तमिव ज्योतिः पिङ्गलत्वमुपागतम्॥
en: Thereupon through the divine energy of the goddess my left eye was burnt and seemed to be covered with dust, and its lustre became tawny.

sn: ततोऽमन्यद्विस्तीर्णं गत्वा तस्य गिरेस्तटम्। तूष्णीं वर्षशतान्यष्टौ ममवारं महाव्रतम्॥
en: Then I, going to another spacious peak of the inountain, became engaged in silently observing a mighty vow.

sn: समाप्ते नियमे तस्मिंस्तत्र देवो महेश्वरः। ततः प्रीतेन मनसा प्राह वाक्यमिदं प्रभुः॥
en: On my term of restraint having been complete, that lord of the gods Maheśvara with a gratified heart addressed me, saying.

sn: प्रीतोऽस्मि तव धर्मज्ञ तपसानेन सुव्रत। मया चैतव्रतं चीर्णं त्वया चैव धनाधिप॥
en: O righteous one, you of fair vows, I am wellpleased with this asceticism of your. I also had observed this vow; and you also, O lord of riches, have done the same.

sn: तृतीयः पुरुषो नास्ति यश्चेरद्बतमीदृशम्। व्रतं सुदुष्करं ह्येतन्मयैवोत्पादितं पुरा ॥
en: A third person there is none that practise such a vow. This vow is hard to perform, and formerly it was I that introduced it.

sn: तत्सखित्वं मया सौम्य रोचयस्व धनेश्वर। तपसा निर्जीतश्चैव सखा भव ममानघ ॥
en: Therefore, O mild one, O lord of riches, do you contract friendship with me. And you have conquered me by your penances. Therefore, O be you my friend.

sn: देव्या दग्धं प्रभावेण यच्च सव्यं तवेक्षणम्। पैङ्गल्यं यदवाप्तं हि देव्या रूपनिरीक्षणात्॥ एकाक्षिपिङ्गलीत्येव नाम स्थास्यति शाश्वतम्। एवं तेन सखित्वं च प्राप्यानुज्ञां च शंकरात्॥ आगतेन मया चैवं श्रुतस्ते पापनिश्चयः।
en: This your left eye has been burnt through the energy of the goddess, and has turned tawny in consequence of having seen the grace of the goddess; your shall be Ekāksipingala. Then at Saikara's command I sinless one, SO name ever have obtained the privilege of companionship (with him). Having come here I have heard of your evil designs.

sn: तदधर्मिष्ठसंयोगानिवर्त कुलदूषणात्॥ चिन्त्यते हि वधोपायः सर्षिसङ्घः सुरैस्तव।
en: Do you then desist from this impious course, tending to sully your line. The celestials along with the sages are pondering over the means of compassing your death.

sn: एवमुक्तो दश्ग्रीवः कोपसंरक्तलोचनः॥ हस्तान्दन्तांश्च संपिष्य वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह।
en: Thus addressed, the Ten necked one, with his eyes reddened in wrath, rubbing his hands and knashing his teeth, said.

sn: विज्ञातं ते मया दूत वाक्यं यत्त्वं प्रभाषसे॥ नैव त्वमसि नैवासौ भ्रात्रा येनासि चोदितः। हितं नैष ममैतद्धि ब्रवीति धनरक्षकः॥ महेश्वरसखित्वं तु मूढः श्रावयते किल।
en: O messenger, I have learnt what you have uttered. Neither you nor this brother of mine by whom you have been despatched, (shall live); nor does the keeper of riches say what is for my good. And the fool makes me hear the circumstance of his having made friends with Mahesvara.

sn: नैवेदं क्षमणीयं मे यदेतद्भाषितं त्वया॥ यदेतावन्मया कालं दूत तस्य तु मर्षितम्। न हन्तव्यो गुरुज्येष्ठो मयायमिति मन्यते॥
en: I shall never forgive what you have said. Up to this I had borne him, considering that he, being my elder brother and as such my superior should not be slain by me.

sn: तस्य त्विदानीं श्रुत्वा मे वाक्यमेषा कृता मतिः। त्रौंल्लोकानपि जेष्यामि बाहुवीर्यमुपाश्रितः॥
en: But now hearing his (utterances), even this is my resolve. Depending upon the might of my arms, I shall conquer the three worlds.

sn: एतन्मुहूर्तमेवाहं तस्यैतस्य तु वै कृते। चतुरो लोकपालांस्तानयिष्यामि यमक्षयम्॥
en: On his account solely I shall on the instant despatch the four Lokapālas to the abode of Death.

sn: एवमुक्त्वा तु लङ्केशो दूतं खङ्गेन जघ्निवान्। ददौ भक्षयितुं ह्येनं राक्षसानां दुरात्मनाम्॥
en: Having said this, Lanka's lord killed the emissary with his sword and made him over to the wicked Räksasas for being eaten.

sn: ततः कृतस्वस्त्ययनो रथमारुह्य रावणः। त्रैलोक्यविजयाकांक्षी ययौ यत्र धनेश्वरः॥
en: Then, having performed Svastyayana, Rāvana, ascending his car, went to where the lord of riches was, bent on conquering the three worlds.

sn: ततः स सचिवैः सार्धं षड्भिर्नीत्यबलोद्धतः। महोदरप्रहस्ताभ्यां मारीचशुकसारणैः॥ धूम्राक्षेण च वीरेण नित्यं समरगर्धिना। वृतः संप्रययौ श्रीमान्क्रोधाल्लोकान्दहन्निव॥
en: Accompanied by his six counsellor Mohodara and Prahasta, Marica, Suka and Sarana, and the heroic Dhümrākṣa eager for encounter the graceful Rāvana, elated with his strength sallied out, as if consuming all creatures with his wrath.

sn: पुराणि स नदी शैलान्वनान्युपवनानि च। अतिक्रम्य मुहूर्तेन कैलासं गिरिमागमत्॥
en: Leaving behind cities and steams and hills and woods and groves, he in a moment came to the mountain Kailāśa.

sn: संनिविष्टं गिरौ तस्मिन्राक्षसेन्द्रं निशम्य तु। युद्धेप्सुं तं कृतोत्साहं दुरात्मानं समन्त्रिणम्॥ यक्षा न शेकुः संस्थातुं प्रमुखे तस्य रक्षसः। राज्ञो भ्रातेति विज्ञाय गता यत्र धनेश्वरः॥
en: And hearing that wicked-minded lord of Räks asas, breathing high spirits, had arrived at the mount in company with his counsellors, the Yakşas could not stay before that Rākşasa, and knowing this one is the king's brother,' went to where the lord of riches was.

sn: ते गत्वा सर्वमाचख्युर्धातुस्तस्य चिकीर्षितम्। अनुज्ञाता ययुहृष्टा युद्धाय धनदेन ते॥
en: Going to him they in full related all about the doings of his brother. And on being permitted by the bestower of treasures, they went out for battle.

sn: ततो बलानां संक्षोभो व्यवर्धत इवोदधेः। तस्य नैऋतराजस्य शैलं संचलयनिव॥
en: And then, like to the agitation of the ocean, there took place a mighty ferment of the forces of the Naiſta king, as if making the mountain tremble.

sn: ततो युद्धं समभवद्यक्षराक्षससंकुलम्। व्यथिताश्चाभवंस्तत्र सचिवा राक्षसस्य ते।।।
en: And then there took place an encounter between the Yakşas and the Räksasa were smitten fiercely.

sn: स दृष्ट्वा तादृशं सैन्यं दशग्रीवो निशाचरः। हर्षनादान्बहून्कृत्वा स क्रोधादभ्यभाषत॥
en: And finding his forces in that plight, Daśagrīva set up full many a cheerful shout and in wrath began to speak.

sn: ये तु ते राक्षसेन्द्रस्य सचिवा घोरविक्रमाः। तेषां सहस्रमेकैको यक्षाणां समयोधयत्॥
en: Each of the terrific and mightiest councillors of the Rākşasa-chief, coped with a thousand Yaksas.

sn: ततो गदाभिर्मुसलैरसिभिः शक्तितोमरैः। हन्यमानो दशग्रीवास्तत्सैन्यं समगाहत॥ स निरुच्छ्वासवत्तत्र वध्यमानो दशाननः। वर्षद्भिरिव जीमूतैर्धाराभिरवरुध्यत॥ न चकार व्यथां चैव यक्षशस्त्रैः समाहतः। महीधर इवाम्भोदैर्धाराशतसमुक्षितः॥
en: And then struck with maces and clubs and swords and darts and tomaras, the Ten-necked one dived into (that deep) of a host. And rendered inert and sore assailed, Daśānana was deprived of his movements with volleys of weapons resembling torrents of rain. And albeit drenched with blood streaming dowli in hundreds of torrents, he like a mountain flooded with a downpour, being wounded with the weapons of the Yakşa, does not betray any smart.

sn: स महात्मा समुद्यस्य कालदण्डोपमां गदाम्। प्रविवेश ततः सैन्यं नयन्यक्षान्यमक्षयम्॥
en: And that high-souled one, raising up his mace resembling the rod itself of Time, entered into that army, despatching Yakşas to the abode of Yama.

sn: स कक्षमिव विस्तीर्णं शुष्कन्धनमिवाकुलम्। वातेनाग्निरिवादीप्तो यक्षसैन्यं ददाह तत्.।१५।।
en: And as a flaming fire burn up an extensive sward of grass stocked with dry fire-wood, he began to consume that Yakşa army.

sn: तैस्तु तत्र महामात्यैर्महोदरशुकादिभिः। अलापवशेषास्ते यक्षाः कृता वातैरिवाम्बुदाः।।१६
en: And as the wind scatter clouds, the small remnant of Yaksa army was scattered by the redoubtable councillors (of Ravana) Mahodara, Suka, etc.

sn: केचित्समाहता भिन्नाः पतिताः समरे क्षितौ। ओष्ठांश्च दशनैस्तीक्ष्णैरदशन्कुपिता रणे॥ श्रान्ताश्चान्योन्यमालिङ्गय भ्रष्टशस्त्रा रणाजिरे। सीदन्ति च तदा यक्षाः कूला इव जलेन ह॥
en: And some were wounded, and (some) broken down, and (some) measured their lengths on the ground in the encounter, and other Yakşas deprived of their arms in the field, being fatigued, sank down, embracing each other, even as banks drop down, on being worn away by water.

sn: हतानां गच्छतां स्वर्ग युध्यतामथ धावताम्। प्रेक्षतामृषिसङ्घानां बभूव न तदान्तरम्॥
en: And no room was left (in the sky) in consequence of its being thronged by hosts of sages; and warriors, wounded and rushing for conflict, and (finally) ascending heaven.* *The idea of the author is: "The welkin was thronged with sages as well as warriors, who swelled the ranks of the sages stationed in the sky, by ascending heaven after having fallen in fight.”

sn: भग्नांस्तु तान्समालक्ष्य यक्षेन्द्रांस्तु महाबलान्। धनाध्यक्षो महाबाहुः प्रेषयामास यक्षकान्॥
en: And finding the foremost Yakşas endowed with great strength give way, the mighty-armed lord of riches despatched (other) Yaksas.

sn: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे राम विस्तीर्णबलवाहनः। प्रेषितो न्यपतद्यक्षो नाम्ना संयोधकण्टकः॥
en: In the meantime, o Rāma, a Yakşa named Sañyodhakanțaka, accompanied by an extensive force and a large number of vehicles, on being despatched, rushed (on the foe).

sn: तेन चक्रेण मारीचो विष्णुनेव रणे हतः। पतितो भूतले शैलात्क्षीणपुण्य इव ग्रहः॥
en: And wounded in the conflict (by Sañyodhakanţaka) with his discus, as if by Vişnu himself, Márica toppled down to the ground from the mountain, like to a planet whose merit has waned.

sn: ससंज्ञस्तु मुहूर्तेन स विश्रम्य निशाचरः। तं यक्षं योधयामास स च भग्नः प्रदुद्रुवे॥
