en: And in a moment regaining his consciousness and resting (for a while), that night-ranger fought with the Yaksa; and thereat, on being defeated, he* fled. *The Yaksa, that is.)

sn: ततः काञ्चनचित्राङ्गं वैदूर्यजतोक्षितम्। मर्यादां प्रतिहाराणां तोरणान्तरमाविशत्॥ तं तु राजन्दशग्रीवं प्रविशन्तं निशाचरम्। सूर्यभानुरिति ख्यातो द्वारपालो न्यवारयत्॥
en: Then (Rāvana) entered within the gate-way (of the place), garnished with gold, and decked with lapises and silver, And thereat, o king, the warder named Sūryabhānu prevented the nightranger Daśagrīva as he was entering.

sn: स वार्यमाणो यक्षेण प्रविवेश निशाचरः। यदा तु वारितो राम न व्यतिष्ठत्स राक्षसः॥ ततस्तोरणमुत्पाट्य तेन यक्षेण ताडितः। रुधिरं प्रस्रवन्भाति शैलो धातुस्रवैरिव॥
en: And albeit prevented, the nigh-ranger entered in. And when O Rama, that Raksasa was prevented, he did not stay. And then struck by that Yaksa with the gate-way uprooted, he, discharging blood in streams, looked like a hill with minerals running on it.

sn: स शैलशिखराभेण तोरणेन समाहतः। जगाम न क्षतिं वीरो वरदानात्स्वयंभुवः॥
en: And hit with that gate-way resembling a mountain-summit in splendour, that hero did not sustain any injury, on account of the boon he had received from the Self-sprung.

sn: तेनैव तोरणेनाथ यक्षस्तेनाभिताडितः। नादृश्यत तदा यक्षो भस्मीकृततनुस्तदा ॥
en: And on being struck by the same gate-way, the Yakșa ceased to be seen, his body having then been consumed to ashes.

sn: ततः प्रदुद्रुवुः सर्वे दृष्ट्वा रक्षःपराक्रमम्। ततो नदीर्गुहाश्चैव विविशुर्भयपीडिताः। त्यक्तप्रहरणाः श्रान्ता विवर्णवदनास्तदा॥
en: And witnessing the prowess of the Rākșasa, all began to flee; and then they afflicted with affright, fatigued, and with pale faces entered into rivers and caves, leaving their arms behind.

sn: ततस्ताल्लक्ष्य वित्रस्तान्यक्षेन्द्रांश्च सहस्रशः। धनाध्यक्षो महायक्षं माणिचारमथाब्रवीत्॥
en: Seeing the foremost of the Yakşas by thousands undergoing trepidation, the lord of riches spoke to a mighty Yakşa Māņichara.

sn: रावणं जहि यक्षेन्द्र दुर्वृत्तं पापचेतसम्। शरणं भव वीराणां यक्षाणां युद्धशालिनाम्॥
en: O foremost of Yakşas, slay the wicked Ravana, set on sin; and do you (thus) become the refuge of those heroic Yakşas, who are carrying on the conflict.

sn: एवमुक्तो महाबाहुर्माणिभद्रः सुदुर्जयः। वृतो यक्षसहस्रेस्तु चतुर्भिः समयोधयत्॥
en: Thus addressed, the mighty-armed and invincible Mānibhadra, surrounded by four thousand Yakşas began the fight.

sn: ते गदामुसलप्रासैः शक्तितोमरमुद्गरैः। अभिघ्नन्तस्तदा यक्षा राक्षसान्समुपाद्रवन्।४।।
en: And attacking the Rākşasas with maces and clubs and bearded darts, and with darts tomoras and bludgeons, the Yaksas rushed at (their adversaries).

sn: कुर्वन्तस्तुमुलं युद्धं चरन्तः श्येनवल्लघु। बाढं प्रयच्छ नेच्छामि दीयतामिति भाषिणः।५।।
en: And fast safely whirling about like hawks, they fought fiercely. And (some) said, 'Well, give me battle,' and (others), 'I don't want,' and (other) again), 'Let me have (fight)'.

sn: ततो देवाः सगन्धर्वा ऋषयो ब्रह्मवादिनः। दृष्ट्वा तत्तुमुलं युद्धं परं विस्मयमागमन्॥
en: And then the celestials and the Gandharvas and the sages studying the Vedas, beholding the great encounter, were filled with mighty amazement.

sn: यक्षाणां तु प्रहस्तेन सहस्रं निहतं रणे। महोदरेण चानिन्द्यं सहस्रमपरं हतम्।७॥
en: And a thousand of the Yakşas were slain by Praśasta in the conflict; and another thousand of capable warriors were slain by Mahodara.

sn: कुद्धेन च तदा राजन्मारीचेन युयुत्सुना। निमेथान्तरमात्रेण द्वे सहस्र निपातिते॥
en: O king, in the twinkling of an eye Märīca, waxing wroth and eager for encounter brought down two thousand (of enemy's soldiers).

sn: क्व च यक्षार्जवं युद्धं क्व च मायाबलाश्रयम्। रक्षसां पुरुषव्याघ्र तेन तेऽभ्यधिका युधि॥
en: Where is the candid-coursing fight of the Yakşas and where the fight of the Rākşas by help of the power of illusion; and therefore in that battle the advantage was on the side of the Raksasas.

sn: धूम्राक्षेण समागम्य माणिभद्रो महारणे। मुसलेनोरसि क्रोधात्ताडितो न च कम्पितः॥
en: And Dhūmrākşa, confronting Māņibhadra in the mighty conflict hit him as the chest with a bludgeon; but he did not move thereat.

sn: ततो गदां समाविध्य माणिभद्रेण राक्षसः। धूम्राक्षस्ताडितो मूर्ध्नि विह्वलः स पपात ह॥
en: Then Mänibhadra dealt the Raksasa a blow with his mace; and thereat Dhūmrākṣa smite at the head fell down senseless (on the ground).

sn: धूम्राक्षं ताडितं दृष्ट्वा पतितं शोणितोक्षितम्। अभ्यधावत संग्रामे माणिभद्रं दशाननः॥
en: And seeing Dhūmrākṣa wounded and down, bathed in blood, the Ten-necked Răvaņa rushed at Māņibhadra in the encounter.

sn: संक्रुद्धमभिधावन्तं माणिभद्रो दशाननम्। शक्तिभिस्ताडयामास तिसृभिर्यक्षपुङ्गवः॥
en: Then that foremost of Yakşas hit Daśānana with three darts as he was rushing in wrath.

sn: ताडितो माणिभद्रस्य मुकुटे प्राहरद्रणे। तस्य तेन प्रहारेण मुकुटं पार्श्वमागतम्॥
en: And on being thus hit, (Rāvana) struck at Manibhadra's head: and at that stroke his crown was depressed at one side.

sn: ततः प्रभृति यक्षोऽसौ पार्श्वमौलिरभूत्किल। तस्मिंस्तु विमुखीभूते माणिभद्रे महात्मनि। संनादः सुमहानराजेस्तस्मिन्शैले व्यवर्धत॥
en: From that day forth that Yaksa remained with his head hollow on one side. And on the highsouled Māņibhadra having been baffled, a great uproar, O king rose in that mountain.

sn: ततो दूरात्प्रददृशे धनाध्यक्षो गदाधरः। शुक्रप्रौष्द्वपदाभ्यां च पद्मशङ्खसमावृतः॥
en: Then at a distance, the lord of riches, mace in hand, accompanied by Sukra and Praushthapada and Padma and Sanka saw (Ravana) in the field.

sn: स दृष्ट्वा भ्रातरं संख्ये शापाद्विभ्रष्टगौरवम्। उवाच वचनं धीमान्युक्तं पैतामहे कुले॥
en: Seeing his brother in the encounter with his glory obscured through the curse (he had ere this come by), the intelligent (Lord of Yaksas) spoke in words worthy of the line of his grand-father.

sn: यन्मया वार्यमाणस्त्वं नावगच्छसि दुर्मते। पश्चादस्य फलं प्राप्य ज्ञास्यसे निरयं गतः॥
en: As, O wicked-minded one, you desistest not, albeit forbidden by me, you shall, afterwards attaining the fruit of this, and repairing to hell, know (the fate that follow there).

sn: यो हि मोहाद्विषं पीत्वा नावगच्छति दुर्मतिः। स तस्य परिणामान्ते जानीते कर्मणः फलम् ॥
en: That perverse one, that through ignorance having drunk poison, neglects to adopt proper measures, know the consequence of his act ultimately.

sn: दैवतानि न नन्दन्ति धर्मयुक्तन केन चित्। येन त्वमीदृशं भावं नीतस्तच्च न बुद्ध्यसे॥
en: The gods have set their face against you on account of a certain misdeed of your; and having for this, been reduced to this condition, you do not understand things.

sn: मातरं पितरं विप्रमाचार्य चावमन्य वै। स पश्यति फलं तस्य प्रेतराजवशं गतः॥
en: He that dishonour his father and mother* and spiritual preceptor, reap the fruit of his act on coming under the sway of the sovereign of the dead. *Unless he serve his parents, his heart does not incline to piety.

sn: अध्रुवे हि शरीरे यो न करोति तपोजनम्। स पश्चात्तप्यते मूढो मृतो गत्वात्मनो गतिम्॥
en: Having regard that this body is uncertain, that foolish person, that does not acquire asceticism, dying go the way that he deserve.

sn: कस्य चिन हि दुर्बुद्धेश्छन्दतो जायते मतिः। यादृशं कुरुते कर्म तादृशं फलमश्नुते॥
en: The mind of a perverse man does not willingly incline towards good; and as he acts, he gets the fruits (he reaps as he sows).

sn: ऋद्धिंरूपं बलं पुत्रान्वित्तं शूरत्वमेव च। प्राप्नुवन्ति नरा लोके निर्जितं पुण्यकर्मभिः॥
en: In this world people, making their own good fortune and beauty, strength, sons, wealth and valour, gain these by virtue of their pious acts.

sn: एवं निरयगामी त्वं यस्य ते मतिरीदृशी। न त्वां समभिभाषिष्येसद्वत्तेष्वेष निर्णयः॥
en: Being given to such iniquitous acts, you will go to hell; and your designs being such, I will not hold parley with you.

sn: एवमुक्तास्ततस्तेन तस्यामात्याः समाहताः। मारीचप्रमुखाः सर्वे विमुखा विप्रदुद्रुवुः॥
en: Honest people should act carefully in connection with the wicked.' Thus reprimanded by him, his (Rāvana's) councillors, headed by Marica, on being struck, took to their heels.

sn: ततस्तेन दशग्रीवो यक्षेन्द्रेण महात्मना। गदयाभिहतो मूर्ध्नि न च स्थानात्प्रकम्पितः॥
en: Then Daśagrīva on being Struck in the head with the mace by the lord of Yakşas, did not move from his place.

sn: ततस्तौ राम निघ्तौ तदान्योन्यं महामृधे। न विह्वलौ न च श्रान्तौ तावुभौ यक्षराक्षसौ॥
en: And then, O Rama, the Yaksa and Raksasa, smiting each other in mighty encounter, did not get bewildered of experience fatigue.

sn: आग्नेयमत्रं तस्मै स मुमोच धनदस्तदा। राक्षसेन्द्रो वारुणेन तदत्रं प्रत्यवारयत्॥
en: And then the bestower of riches discharged a fiery weapon at him; and thereat the lord of Rāks asa resisted it with a Varuņa weapon.

sn: ततो मायां प्रविष्टोऽसौ राक्षसी राक्षसेश्वरः। रूपाणां शतसाहस्रं विनाशाय चकार च॥
en: And then the Rākşasa king entered upon shapes for compassing the destruction of his adversary).

sn: व्याघ्रो वराहो जीमूतः पर्वतः सागरो दुमः। यक्षो दैत्यस्वरूपी च सोऽदृश्यत दशाननः॥
en: The Ten-necked Ravana (successively) assumed the shapes of a tiger, a boar, a cloud, a hill, the ocean, a tree, a Yaksa and a Daitya.

sn: बहूनि च करोति स्म दृश्यन्ते न त्वसौ ततः। प्रतिगृह्य ततो राम महदस्त्रं दशाननः। जघान मूर्ध्नि धनदं व्याविद्ध्य महतीं गदाम्॥
en: Thus he wore full many forms and he was not visible in his native shape. And then, O Rāma, seizing a mighty weapon the Ten-necked one, whirling the same, brought that redoubtable mace down on the head of the bestower of riches.

sn: एवं स तेनाभिहतो विह्वलः शोणितोक्षितः। कृत्तमूल इवाशोको निपपात धनाधिपः॥
en: Thus smitten by him, the lord of wealth, baffled, toppled down to the earth covered with blood like an aśoka whose roots have been hewn away.

sn: ततः पद्मादिभिस्तत्र निधिभिः स तदा वृतः। धनदोच्छ्वासितस्तैस्तु वनमानीय नन्दनम्॥
en: Thereat Padma and other Nidhi deities, surrounding the granter the granter of wealth, raised him up and brought him to the Nandana wood.

sn: निर्जित्य राक्षसेन्द्रस्तं धनदं हृष्टमानसः। पुष्पकं तस्य जग्राह विमानं जयलक्षणम्॥ काञ्चनस्तम्भसंवीतं वैदूर्यमणितोरणम्। मुक्काजालप्रतिच्छन्नं सर्वकालफलद्रुमम्॥ मनोजवं कामगमं कामरूपं विहङ्गमम्। मणिकाञ्चनसोपानं तप्तकाञ्चनवेदिकम्॥ देवोपवाह्यपक्षय्यं सदादृष्टिमनःसुखम्। बह्वाश्चर्य भक्तिचित्रं ब्रह्मणा परिनिर्मितम्॥ निर्मितं सर्वकामैस्तु मनोहरमनुत्तमम्। न तु शीतं न चोष्णं च सर्वर्तुसुखदं शुभम्॥ स तं राजा समारुह्य कामगं वीर्यनिर्जितम्। जितं त्रिभुवनं मेने दर्पोत्सेकात्सुदुर्मतिः। जित्वा वैश्रवणं देवं कैलासात्समवातरत्॥
en: Conquering the bestower of wealth, the lord of Raksasas, with a delighted heart, possessed himself of his Puspaka, the car, as a sign of victory; furnished with golden pillars, gateways set with lapises, covered with networks of pearls, having three yielding the fruits of all seasons, endowed with the celerity of thought, ranging everywhere at will, wearing forms at pleasure, capable of coursing in the sky, with golden and jewelled stairs, and daises of polished gold, the vehicle of the gods undeteriorating, bringing delight to the mind and sight; wonderous exceedingly: painted with images designed to fill the mind with reverence, constructed by Brahmä, containing all objects of desire, charming and nonpariel not cold and not yet hot, granting gratification in every season, and graceful to the view. And ascending that (car) coursing at will, won by his prowess, that utterly wicked one, out of swelling insolence, deemed himself master of the three worlds. And having vanquished the deity Vaiśravaņa, he descended from Kailasa.

sn: स तेजसा विपुलमवाप्य तं जयं प्रतापवान्विमलकिरीटहारवान्। रराज वै परमविमानमास्थितो निशाचरः सदसि गतो यथानलः॥
en: Having by his energy obtained the victory, the powerful night-ranger wearing a bright diadem and necklace, and seated on that superb car, appeared radiant in his court like Fire himself.

sn: स जित्वा धनदं राम भ्रातरं राक्षसाधिपः। महासेनप्रसूतिं तद्ययौ शरवणं महत्॥
en: O Rāma, having, vanquished his brother, the lord of riches, the king of Räkşasas went to the great wood of reeds, where Mahasena was born.

sn: अथापश्यद्दशग्रीवो रौक्मं शरवणं महत्। गभस्तिजालसंवीतं द्वितीयमिव भास्करम्॥ स पर्वतं समारुह्य कंचिद्रम्यवनान्तरम्। प्रेक्षते पुष्पकं तत्र रामविष्टम्भितं तदा॥
en: The Ten-necked Rāvana saw the great golden wood of reeds. Furnished with networks of solar rays, and appearing like a second Sun, and ascending the mountain, he was surveying the heart of the forest, when, O Rama, Puspaka was (suddenly) deprived of its motion.

sn: विष्टब्धं किमिदं कस्मानागमत्कामगं कृतम्। अचिन्तयद्राक्षसेन्द्रः सचिवैस्तैः समावृतः॥ किनिमित्तमिच्छया मे नेदं गच्छति पुष्पकम्। पर्वतस्योपरिष्ठस्य कर्मेदं कस्यचिद्भवेत्॥ ततोऽब्रवीत्तदा राम मारीचो बुद्धिकोविदः। नेदं निष्कारणं राजन्पुष्पकं यन्न गच्छति॥ अथ वा पुष्पकमिदं धनदानान्यवाहनम्। अतो निस्पन्दमभवद्धनाध्यक्षविनाकृतम्॥
en: The lord of Räkşasas, could not comprehend how the car which had been so made as to course in accordance with the wish of the rider, could have its course impeded; and thereat he in company with his. councillors thought, 'Wherefore does not his Puşpaka course at my desire over this mountain? Whose act is this?' Thereat Mārīca foremost of intelligent ones said, 'That Puspaka does not course cannot, sire, be without cause; or it may be that in consequence of Puşpaka not having borne any other than the bestower of riches, it has ceased its course not having the lord of wealth for its rider.'

sn: इति वाक्यान्तरे तस्य करालः कृष्णपिङ्गलः। वामनो विकटो मुण्डी नन्दी हस्वभुजो बली॥ ततः पार्श्वमुपागभ्य भवस्यानुचरोऽब्रवीत्। नन्दीश्वरो वचश्चेदं राक्षसेन्द्रमशङ्कितः॥
en: As they were speaking thus, that attendant of Bhava, Nandi, terrific, of yellow black hue, dwarfish, frightful, with his head shaven, having short arms, and stout, coming up to them, said (this). And the lordly Nandi, undaunted, addressed the sovereign of the Raksasas, saying.

sn: निवर्तस्व दशग्रीव शैले क्रीडति शंकरः। सुपर्णनागयक्षाणां देवगन्धर्वरक्षसाम्॥ सर्वेषामेव भूतानामगम्यः पर्वतः कृतः।
en: Desist you O Ten-necked one; Śankara sport in the mountain; and (now) He is incapable of being approached by every one, birds, serpents and Yaksas; gods, Gandharvas and Raksasas?

sn: इति नन्दिवचः श्रुत्वा क्रोधात्कम्पितकुण्डलः॥ रोषात्तु ताम्रनयनः पुष्पकादवरुह्य सः। कोऽयं शंकर इत्युक्त्वा शैलमूलमुपागतः॥ सोऽपश्यन्नन्दिनं तत्र देवस्यादूरतः स्थितम्। दीप्तं शूलमवष्टभ्य द्वितीयमिव शंकरम्॥
en: Hearing Nandi's speech, (Ravana), wrought up with wrath, his eyes coppery, and his earrings shaking, leapt down from Puspaka. And saying, 'who is this Sankara? and he came down to the base of the mount. He beheld there Nandi stationed at the side of the deity, supporting himself on his flaming dart, resembling a second Sankara.

sn: तं दृष्ट्वा वानरमुखमवज्ञाय स राक्षसः। प्रहासं मुमुचे तत्र सतोय इव तोयदः॥
en: And seeing that one having the face of a monkey, the Raksasas, deriding him, burst out into laughter, and seemed as if a mass of clouds were sending roars.

sn: तं कुद्धो भगवानन्दी शंकरस्यापरा तनुः। अब्रवीत्तत्र तद्रक्षो दशाननमुपस्थितम्॥
en: Thereat, growing enraged, the reverend Nandi Sankara's other body spoke into that Rākṣasa The Ten-necked one present there.

sn: यस्माद्वानररूपं मामवज्ञाय दशानन। अशनीपातसंकाशमपहासं प्रमुक्तवान्॥ तस्मान्मवीर्यसंयुक्ता मद्रूपसमतेजसः। उत्पत्स्यन्ति वधार्थ हि कुलस्य तव वानराः॥
en: “As O Daśānana, deriding me for my monkery-form, you have indulged in a laughter resembling the bursting of thunder, do monkeys endowed with prowess, and possessed of my form and energy shall be born for compassing the destruction of your race.

sn: नखदंष्ट्रायुधाः क्रूर मन:संपातरंहसः। युद्धोन्मत्ता बलोद्रिक्ताः शैला इव विसर्पिणः॥ ते तव प्रबलं दर्पमुत्सेधं च पृथग्विधम्। व्यपनेष्यन्ति संभूय सहामात्यमुतस्य च॥
en: And armed with teeth and claws, and fierce and furnished with the fleetness of thought, and mad for encounter, and bursting with vigour, and resembling moving mountains and being born, they shall crush your high pride and power along with your courtiers and sons.

sn: किं त्विदानी मया शक्यं हन्तुं त्वां हे निशाचर। न हन्तव्यो हतस्त्वं हि पूर्वमेव स्वकर्मभिः॥
en: But, O night-ranger, I can even now end you quite; yet I must not slay you for you have ere this been slain by your acts.

sn: इत्युदीरितवाक्ये तु देवे तस्मिन्महात्मनि। देवदुन्दुभ्यो नेदुः पुष्पवृष्टिश्च खाच्च्युता॥
en: When that high-souled god had spoken thus celestial kettle-drums sounded and a blossomy shower rained from the sky.

sn: अचिन्तयित्वा स तदा नन्दिवाक्यं महाबलः। पर्वतं तु समासाद्य वाक्यमाह दशाननः॥
en: But without heeding Nandi's speech, that highly powerful one Daśānana coming to the mountain, said.

sn: पुष्पकस्य गतिश्छिन्ना यत्कृते मम गच्छतः। तमिमं शैलमुन्मूलं करोमि तव गोपते॥
en: 'O Gopati, I will even uproot this mountain, for whom Pușpaka was deprived of its motion as I was journeying.

sn: केन प्रभावेण भवा नित्यं क्रीडति राजवत्। विज्ञातव्यं न जानीते भयस्थानमुपस्थितम्॥
en: It must be known by what influence Bhavasvara sport here king-like. He does not know that an occasion of fear has presented itself?'

sn: एवमुक्त्वा तं राम भुजान्विक्षिप्य पर्वते। तोलयामास तं शीघ्रं स शैलं समकम्पत॥
en: Having said this, O Rama, Ravana seizing the mountain with his arms, lifted it up at once; and then the mountain trembled greatly.

sn: चा नात्पर्ततस्यैव राणा देवस्य कम्पिताः। चचाल पार्वती चापि तदाश्लिष्टा महेश्वरम्॥
en: And in consequence of the mountain shaking the attendants of the deity (dwelling in it) also shook. And Pārvatí also trembled and embraced Mahesvara. as

sn: ततो राम महादवो देवानां प्रवरो हरः। पादाङ्गुष्ठेन तं शैलं पीडयामास लीलया॥
en: Then, O Rāma, Mahadeva foremost of the deities even Hara, as in sport pressed the mount with his great toe.

sn: पीडितास्तु ततस्तस्य शैलस्तम्भोपमा भुजाः। विस्मिताश्चाभवंस्तत्र सचिवास्तस्य रक्षसः॥
en: Thereat his arms, resembling blocks of stone felt the shock and then there the councillors of that Rākşasa were struck with amaze.

sn: रक्षसा तेन रोषाच्च भुजानां पीडनात्तथा। मुक्तो विरावः सहसा त्रैलोक्यं येन कम्पितम्।।२९
en: The Rākṣasa, from wrath and the pain felt in his arms, set up a shout that shook the entire triune world.

sn: मेनिरे वज्रनिष्पेषं तस्यामात्या युगक्षये। तदा वर्त्मसु चलिता देवा इन्द्रपुरोगमाः॥ समुद्राश्चापि संक्षुब्धाश्चलिताश्चापि पर्वताः। यक्षा विद्याधराः सिद्धाः किमेतदिति चाब्रुवन्।।३१
en: His councillors considered it the concussion of the thunder at the universal disruption. And then the celestials with Indra at their head shook on their way; and the sea was wild and the mountains shook. And Yakşas and Vidyadharas and Siddhas asked, "What is this.'

sn: तोषयस्व महादेवं नीलकण्ठमुमापतिम्। तमृते शरणं नान्यं पश्यामोऽत्र दशानन॥
en: 'Do you propitiate Uma's lord the bluethroated Mahādeva; for, O Daśānana, save him your refuge see we none in this matter.

sn: स्तुतिभिः प्रणतो भूत्वा तमेव शरणं व्रज। कृपालुः शंकरस्तुष्टः प्रसादं ते विधास्यति ॥
en: Bowing yourself down, do you seek him as your shelter. Then the kind Sankara, on being gratified, will confer on you his favour.

sn: एवमुक्तस्तदामात्यैस्तुष्टाव वृषभध्वजम् । समाभिर्विविधैः स्तोत्रैः प्रणभ्य स दशाननः। संवत्सरसहस्रं तु रुदतो रक्षसो गतम्॥
en: Thus accosted by his councillors, the Tenfaced one, bowing down to him having the bull for his standard, began to hymn him with various soma hymns; and the Rākşasa passed away a good thousand years in lamentations.

sn: ततः प्रीतो महादेवः शैलाने विष्ठितं प्रभुः। मुक्त्वा चास्य भुजाराम प्राह वाक्यं दशाननम्॥
en: Thereat that Lord Mahādeva, pleased, set free the hands of Daśānana stationed at the top of the mount, and O Rāma, addressed him, saying.

sn: प्रीतोऽस्मि तव वीरस्य शौटीर्याच्च दशानन। शैलाक्रान्तेन यो मुक्तस्त्वयारावः सुदारुणः॥ यस्माल्लोकत्रयं चैतद्रावितं भयमागतम्। तस्मात्त्वं रावणो नाम नाम्ना राजन्भविष्यसि ॥
en: O Daśānana, pleased am I with you on account of your hymns. And as in consequence of your arms having been hurt by the mountain, you have uttered a terrific yell, which struck horror into the worlds and put them shaking, therefore, o King, your name shall be Ravana.

sn: देवता मानुषा यक्षा ये चान्ये जगतीतले। एवं त्वामभिधास्यन्ति रावणं लोकरावणम्॥
en: And deities and men, Yakşas and others living on earth shall call you Rāvana terror to creatures,

sn: गच्छ पौलस्त्य विस्रब्धं पथा येन त्वमिच्छसि। मया चैवाभ्यनुज्ञातो राक्षसाधिप गम्यताम्॥
en: Go, O Paulastya, which way you wish with confidence, and permitted by me, O Lord of Raksasas, go you.

sn: एवमुक्तस्तु लङ्केशः : शंभुना स्वयमब्रवीत्। प्रीतो यदि महादेव वरं मे देहि याचतः॥
en: Thus accosted by Sambhu, Larkā's lord said of himself. 'If you are pleased with me, grant me a boon, who ask you for it.

sn: अवध्यत्वं मया प्राप्तं देवगन्धर्वदानवैः। राक्षसैर्गुह्यकै गैर्ये चान्ये बलवत्तराः॥
en: I have already obtained a boon, bestowing on me immunity from death at the hands of gods, Gandharvas and Dānavas; and Rākşasas and Guyhakas and Nāgas; and others also that are of more than ordinary strength.

sn: मानुषान गणे देव स्वल्पास्ते मम संमताः। दीर्घमायुश्च में प्राप्तं ब्रह्मणस्त्रिपुरान्तक। वाञ्छितं चायुषः शेषं शस्त्रं त्वं च प्रयच्छ मे॥
en: Man count I not ogod: They, I deem, are insignificant. I have also, O destroyer of Tripura, received a long lease of life from Brahmä. Now I wish to pass the remainder of my days in peace: and do you grant me a weapon.

sn: एवमुक्तस्ततस्तेन रावणेन स शंकरः। ददौ खङ्गं महादीप्तं चन्द्रहासमिति श्रुतम्। आयुषश्चावशषं च ददौ भूतपतिस्तदा॥
en: Thus addressed by him, (Ravana,) Sankara gave him an exceedingly effulgent sword, famed as Candrahāsa; and the master of spectres then also granted him peace for the rest of his life.

sn: दत्त्वोवाच ततः शंभु वज्ञेयमिदं त्वया। अवज्ञातं यदि हि ते मामेवैष्यत्यसंशयः॥
en: And making (the sword) over to him, Sambhu said, “You must not disregard this. If disregarded, it will for certain come (back) to me?'

sn: एवं महेश्वेणैव कृतनामा स रावणः। अभिवाद्य महादेवमारुरोहाथ पुष्पकम्॥
en: Having thus received his his name from Mahesvara, Rāvana, saluting Mahadeva, ascended Puspaka.

sn: ततो महीतलं राम पर्यक्रामत रावणः। क्षत्रियान्सुमहावीर्यान्बाधमानस्ततस्ततः॥ केचित्तेजस्विनः शूराः क्षत्रिया युद्धदुर्मदाः। तच्छासनमकुर्वन्तो विनेशुः सपरिच्छदाः॥
en: Then, O Rāma, Rāvaņa, began to go round the earth. And opposed at places, by the heroic Kșatriyas endowed with energy and irrepressible in fight, fight, who refused submission, he exterminated them along with their retainers.

sn: अपरे दुर्जयं रक्षो जानन्तः प्राज्ञसंमताः। जिताः स्म इत्यभाषन्त राक्षसं बलदर्पितम्॥
en: While other men of wisdom, knowing the Räkşasa to be invincible, said to the Rākṣasas elated with strength, "We have been conquered?”

sn: अथ राजन्महाबाहुर्विचरन्पृथिवीतले। हिमवद्वनमासाद्य परिचक्राम रावणः॥
en: Then, O King, the mighty-armed Ravana ranging the earth, came to Himavān and began to go round it.

sn: तत्रापश्यत्स वै कन्यां कृष्णाजिनजटाधराम्। आर्षेण विधिना युक्तां दीप्यन्ती देवतामिव ॥
en: It came to pass that there he saw a damsel wearing a dark deer-skin and matted locks, leading the life of a saint, and flaming like a celestial.

sn: स दृष्ट्वा रूपसंपन्नां कन्यां तां सुमहाव्रताम्। काममोहपरीतात्मा पप्रच्छ प्रहसन्निव॥
en: Seeing the girl observing high vows, endowed with beauty, he, with his soul overwhelmed with lust asked her, laughing.

sn: किमिदं वर्तसे भद्रे विरुद्धं यौवनस्य ते। नहि युक्ता तवैतस्य रूपस्यैव प्रतिक्रिया।४॥
en: How is it, o amiable one, that you act thus contrary to your youth? This course of life surely does not befit your beauty.

sn: रूपं तेऽनुपमं भीरु कामोन्मादकरं नृणाम्। न युक्तं तपसि स्थातुं निर्गतो ह्येष निर्णयः॥
en: Your loveliness, O timid one, is peerless, capable of maddening folk with desire. It does not behove you to lead an ascetic mode of life,-this would suit an old person.

sn: कस्यासि किमिदं भद्रे कश्च भर्ता वरानने। येन संभुज्यसे भीरु स नरः पुण्यभाग्भुवि॥ पृच्छतः शंस मे सर्वं कस्य हेतोः परिश्रमः।
en: Whose daughter are you, O gentle lady? And what is this (vow) that you practise? And O fair faced wrench, who is your husband? He who has you for his wife, is, O timorous one, has religious merit on earth. Tell all about this to me who ask for it. For whom do you put yourself to trouble?

sn: एवमुक्ता तु सा कन्या रावणेन यशस्विनी।७।। अब्रवीद्विधिवत्कृत्वा तस्यातिथ्यं तपोधना।
en: Thus accosted by Rāvana, that illustrious girl, having asceticism for wealth, having received him hospitably in due form, said.

sn: कुशध्वजो नाम पिता ब्रह्मर्षिरमितप्रभः। बृहस्पतिसुतः श्रीमान्बुद्ध्या तुल्यो बृहस्पतेः।।।।।
en: My sire is named Kušadhvaja a Brahmarși of immeasurable energy, son to Bệhaspati, endowed with grace, and like to Bphaspati himself in intelligence.

sn: तस्याहं कुर्वतो नित्यं वेदाभ्यासं महात्मनः। संभूता वाङ्गायी कन्या नाम्ना वेदवती स्मृता॥
en: And while that high sound one was engaged in the daily study of the Vedas, I was born as his word-impregnated daughter, named Vedavati.

sn: ततो देवाः सगन्धर्वा यक्षराक्षसपन्नगाः। ते चापि गत्वा पितरं वरणं रोचयन्ति मे॥ न च मां स पिता तेभ्यो दत्तवान् राक्षसेश्वर। कारणं तद्वदिष्यामि निशामय महाभुज ॥
en: When the gods and the Gandharvas and the Yaksas, Raksasas, and Pannagas, coming to my sire asked for me, O foremost of Rākşasas, my father did not bestow me on any one of them. And I shall you the reason thereof; listen, O long-armed one.

sn: पितुस्तु मम जामाता विष्णुः किल सुरेश्वर। अभिप्रेतस्त्रिलोकेशस्तस्मानान्यस्य मे पिता॥ दातुमिच्छति तस्मै तु तच्छुत्वा बलदर्पितः। शंभुर्नाम ततो राजा दैत्यानां कुपितोऽभवत्। तेन रात्रौ शयानो मे पिता पापेन हिंसितः॥ ततो मे जननी दीना तच्छरीरं पितुर्मम। परिष्वज्य महाभागा प्रविष्टा हव्यवाहनम्॥
en: My father's intended son-in-law was even Vişņu sovereign of the celestials, and the lord of the triune world; and my father would not bestow me on any other. And hearing this, a certain king of the Daityas, named Sambhu proud, of his prowess was wrought up with wrath, and one night as my sire was on bed, that wicked one slew him. Thereat my forlorn mother, of exalted righteousness embracing my father's body entered into fire.

sn: ततो मनोरथं सत्यं पितुर्नारायणं प्रति। करोमीति तमेवाहं हृदयेन समुद्वहे ॥
en: Then wishing to realise my father's wish touching Närāyana, I have fixed my heart even upon him.

sn: इति प्रतिज्ञामारुह्य चरामि विपुलं तपः। एतत्ते सर्वमाख्यातं मया राक्षसपुङ्गव।॥
en: Having made this promise, I have been carrying on rigid austerities. Thus, o foremost of Raksasas. I have related to you everything.

sn: नारायणो मम पतिर्न त्वन्यः पुरुषोत्तमात्। आश्रये नियमं घोरं नारायणपरीप्सया॥
en: Nārāyaṇa is my husband, and not any one else than that best of male beings; and desirous of having Nārāyaṇa I have adopted severe restraints.

sn: विज्ञातस्त्वं हि मे राजन्गच्छ पौलस्त्यनन्दन। जानामि तपसा सर्वं त्रैलोक्ये यद्धिवर्तते॥
en: I know you, O king. Go you, O son of Paulastya. By virtue of my asceticism I know all that takes place in these three regions.

sn: सोऽब्रवीद्रावणो भूयस्तां कन्यां सुमहाव्रताम्। अवरुह्य विमानाग्रात्कंदर्पशरपीडितः॥
en: Thereat descending from the front of his car, Ravana, affected with the shafts of Kandarpa, again addressed that girl, observant of a mighty VOW. a

sn: अवलिप्तासि सुश्रोणि यस्यास्ते मतिरीदृशी। वृद्वानां मृगशावाक्षि भ्राजते पुण्यसंचयः॥
en: O you of sharply hips, in as much as such is your intent, you must be very proud. O you having the eyes of young antelope, accumulation of religious merit suits old people.

sn: त्वं सर्वगुणसंपन्ना नार्हसे वक्तुमीदृशम्। त्रैलोक्यसुन्दरी भीरु यौवनं तेऽतिवर्तते॥
en: You, furnished with every perfection, should not talk thus. You are the paragon in these three worlds,. Your youth wax away.

sn: अहं लङ्कापतिर्भद्रे दशग्रीव इति श्रुतः। तस्य मे भव भार्या त्वं भुव भोगान्यथासुखम्।।२२।
en: I am the lord of Lărkā., O gentle lady. known as Dasagriva. Be you my wife, and enjoy pleasures according to your desire.

sn: कश्च तावदसौ यं त्वं विष्णुरित्यभिभाषसे। वीर्येण तपसा चैव भोगेन च बलेन च। स मया नो मसो भद्रे यं त्वं कामयसेऽङ्गने॥
en: Who is he whom you call Vişņu O mild one, neither in prowess, nor in asceticism, nor in enjoyment, nor in strength, is he my equal, whom, O damsel, you seek.

sn: इत्युक्तवति तस्मिंस्तु वेदवत्यथ साब्रवीत्। मा मैवमिति सा कन्या तमुवाच निशाचरम्॥ त्रैलोक्याधिपतिं विष्णुं सर्वलोकनमस्कृतम्। त्वदृते राक्षसेन्द्रान्यः कोऽवमन्येत बुद्धिमान्॥
en: Thus accosted, Vedavati said to the nightranger 'Do not say so' in respect of Visnu, lord of this triune sphere, bowed down to by all creatures. Save and except you alone, O King of Raksasa, who, that is intelligent, cried down (Narayana).

sn: एवमुक्तस्तया तत्र वेदवत्या निशाचरः। मूर्धजेषु तदा कन्यां कराग्रेण परामृशत्॥
en: Thus addressed there by Vedavatī, the nightranger seized the girl by the hair.

sn: ततो वेदवती क्रुद्धा केशान्हस्तेन साच्छिनत्। असिर्भूत्वा करस्तस्याः केशांश्छिन्नांस्तदाकरोत्॥
en: Thereat Vedavati, wroth, cut off her hair with her hand transformed into a sword.

sn: सा ज्वलन्तीव रोषेण दहन्तीव निशाचरम्। उवाचाग्नि समाधाय मरणाय कृतत्वरा॥
en: Then, flaming up in ire and as if consuming the night-ranger, she, preparing a funeral pyre, hastened to make away with herself.

sn: धर्षितायास्त्वयानार्य न मे जीवितमिष्यते। रक्षस्तस्मात्प्रवेक्ष्यामि पश्यतस्ते हुताशनम्॥
en: You object, having been outraged by you I wish not to live. Therefore, O Raksasa, I will enter into fire in your very presence.

sn: यस्मात्तु धर्षिता चाहं त्वया पापात्मना वने। तस्मात्तव वधार्थ हि समुत्पत्स्यत्यहं पुनः॥
en: As I have in this world been dishonoured by you you are nefarious. I shall again be born to compass your destruction.

sn: नहि शक्यः स्त्रिया हन्तुं पुरुषः पापनिश्चयः। शापे त्वयि मयोत्सृष्टे तपसश्च व्ययो भवेत्॥
en: It lie not in a female to slay a male intent on sin; and if I utter a curse, it shall cost my asceticism.

sn: यदि त्वस्ति मया किंचित्कृतं दत्तं हुतं तथा। तस्मात्त्वयोनिजा साध्वी भवेयं धर्मिणः सुता ॥
en: But if I have done anything, given away any thing, offered oblations to the fire, then I shall be the chaste daughter of some virtuous person, albeit unborn of any female vessel.

sn: एवमुक्त्वा प्रविष्टा सा ज्वलितं जातवेदसम्। पपान च दिवो दिव्या पुष्पवृष्टिः समन्ततः॥
en: Having delivered herself thus, she entered into the flaming fire; and thereat a celestial shower of blossoms rained all around from heaven.

sn: सैषा जनकराजस्य प्रसूता तनया प्रभो। तव भार्या महाबाहो विष्णुस्त्वं हि सनातनः॥
en: O Lord, this is she that has been born as the daughter of king Janaka, your wife, O mightyarmed one. You are the eternal Visnu.

sn: पूर्वं क्रोधहतः शत्रुर्ययासौ निहतस्तया। उपाश्रयित्वा शैलाभस्तव वीर्यममानुषम्॥
en: The enemy, endowed with the splendour of a hill, formerly that been slain by her, by help of your superhuman prowess.

sn: एवमेषा महाभागा मत्र्येषूत्पत्स्यते पुनः। क्षेत्रे हलमुखोत्कृष्टे वेद्यामग्निशिखोपमा॥
en: This one of eminent righteousness would again spring up on earth like a flame from a field furrowed by the plough.

sn: एषा वेदवती नाम पूर्वमासीत्कृते युगे। त्रेतायुगमनुप्राप्य वधार्थं तस्य राक्षसः। उत्पन्ना मैथिलकुले जनकस्य महात्मनः। सीतोत्पन्ना तु सीतेति मानुषेः पुनरुच्यते॥
en: This one named Vedavatſ was born in the Kệta age; and in the Tretā age, for compassing the destruction of that Rākşasa, she was born in the Maithila line of the high-souled Janaka.

sn: प्रविष्टायां हुताशं तु वेदवत्यां स रावणः। पुष्पकं तु समारुह्य परिचक्राम मेदिनीम्॥
en: When Vedavati had entered into the fire, Rāvana, ascending Puşpaka, began to range the earth.

sn: ततो मरुत्तं नृपतिं यजन्तं सह दैवतैः। उशीरबीजमासाद्य ददर्श स तु रावणः॥
en: And coming to Uśirabīja, Rāvaņa saw a king (named) Marutta, sacrificing along with the deities.

sn: संवर्तो नाम ब्रह्मर्षिः साक्षाद्धाता बृहस्पतेः। याजयामास धर्मज्ञः सर्वैर्देवगणैर्वृतः॥
en: And a righteous Brahmarşi named Samvarta, the very brother of Bphaspati, officiated at the sacrifice accompanied by the deities.

sn: दृष्ट्वा देवास्तु तद्रक्षो वरदानेन दुर्जयम्। तिर्यग्योनि समाविष्टास्तस्य धर्षणभीरवः॥
en: Seeing that Rākşasa invincible by reason of the boon he had received, the deities, apprehensive of being worsted by him, assumed the forms of beasts.

sn: इन्द्रो मयूरः संवृत्तो धर्मराजस्तु वायसः। कृकलासो धनाध्यक्षो हंसश्च वरुणोऽभवत्।।५ अन्येष्वपि गतेष्वेवं देवेष्वरिनिषूदन। रावणः प्राविशद्य सारमेय इवाशुचिः॥
en: Indra became a peacock and the king of righteousness, a crow and the bestower of riches a lizard, and Varuna a swan; and, O slayer of foes, others also became other beasts. And then Rāvana entered into that sacrifice like an unclean dog.

sn: तं च राजानमासाद्य रावणो राक्षसाधिपः। प्राह युद्धं प्रयच्छेति निर्जितोऽस्मीति वा वद।७।।
en: Then coming up to the king, Răvaņa lord of Raksāsas said: 'Give me battle, or say, I am defeated.

sn: ततो मरुत्तो नृपतिः को भवानित्युवाच तम्। अवहासं ततो मुक्त्वा रावणो वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥ अकुतूहलभावेन प्रीतोऽस्मि तव पार्थिव. धनदस्यानुजं यो मां नावगच्छसि रावणम्॥
en: Whereat king Marutta asked, him 'Who are you'? And Ravana laughing in contempt said. "O king, I am delighted, that lacking curiosity, you do not dishonour Rävaņa, younger brother to the bestower of riches.

sn: त्रिषु लोकेषु कोऽन्योऽस्ति यो न जानाति मे बलम्। भ्रातरं येन निर्जित्य विमानमिदमाहृतम्॥
en: What other man is there in these three regions that know not the might of me, who, conquering my brother, has got possession of this car.

sn: ततो मरुत्तः स नृपस्तं रावणमथाब्रवीत्। धन्यः खलु भवान्येन ज्येष्ठो भ्राता रणे जितः।। न त्वया सदृशः श्लाघ्यस्त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्वते। नाधर्मसहितं श्लाघ्यं तल्लोकं प्रतिसंहितम्। कर्म दौरात्म्यकं कृत्वा श्लाघ्यसे भ्रातृनिर्जयात्॥ कं त्वं प्राक्केवलं धर्म चरित्वा लब्धवान्वरम्। श्रुतपूर्व हि न मया भाषसे यादृशं स्वयम्॥
en: Thereat Marutta spoke to Ravana, saying, "Blessed for sooth are you, by whom your elder brother has been vanquished in fight. And a person so praise-worthy there is not in the three worlds. An act, that is divorced from righteousness and that is reprehended by people, can never be praiseworthy. Having committed a foul act, plumest you upon your having vanquished your brother? And practising what piety had you a-fortune received the boon? I had never before heard the like of what you say.

sn: तिष्ठेदानीं न मे जीवन्प्रतियास्यति दुर्मते। अद्य त्वां निशितैर्बाणैः प्रेषयामि यमक्षयम्॥
en: But O perverse one, stay now. Living you shall not back. To-day with my sharpened shafts shall I despatch you to the abode of Yama.

sn: ततः शरासनं गृह्य सायकांश्च नराधिपः। रणाय निर्ययौ क्रुद्धः संवर्तो मार्गमावृणोत्॥
en: Then taking up his bow and arrows, that king of men went out for encounter; but Samavartta stood in the way.

sn: सोऽब्रवीत्स्नेहसंयुक्तं मरुत्तं तं महानृषिः। श्रोतव्यं यदि मद्वाक्यं संप्रहारो न ते क्षमः॥
en: And that great sage said to Marutta words informed with affection 'If you hear my speech, you should not fight.

sn: माहेश्वरमिदं सत्रमसमाप्तं कुलं दहेत्। दीक्षितस्य कुतो युद्धं क्रोधित्वं दीक्षिते कुतः॥ संशयश्च जये नित्यं राक्षसश्च सुदुर्जयः। स निवृत्तो गुरोर्वाक्यान्मरुत्तः पृथिवीपतिः। विसृज्य सशरं चापं स्वस्थो मखमुखोऽभवत्॥ ततस्तं निर्जितं मत्वा घोषयामास वै शुकः। रावणो जयतीत्युच्चैहर्षानादं विमुक्तवान्॥
en: If this Maheśvara-sacrifice should remain incomplete, it will burn up your dynasty. Where is the fight of one initiated in a sacrifice? And where is the passion of one initiated in a sacrifice? And victory is ever uncertain; and the Rākşasa is difficult to vanquish. And thereupon, the lord of Earth Marutta desisted in consonance with the instructions of his spiritual preceptor; and composed addressed himself to completing the sacrifice, giving up his bow with the arrow set. And thereat considering him as defeated, Suka proclaimed this all round, and from delight cried aloud, 'Victory to Rāvana!

sn: तान्भक्षयित्वा तत्रस्थान्महर्षीन्यज्ञमागतान्। वितृप्तो रुधिरैस्तेषां पुनः संप्रययौ महीम्॥
en: Then devouring the Maharsis that were present at the place of sacrifice, Rāvana, satiated with their blood, again went to the earth.

sn: रावणे तु गते देवाः सेन्द्राश्चैव दिवौकसः। ततः स्वां योनिमासाद्य तानि सत्त्वानि चाब्रुवन्॥
en: On Ravana having departed, the deities, inhabiting the etherial regions Indra etc. assuming their proper forms, addressed those creatures.

sn: हर्षात्तदाब्रवीदिन्द्रो मयूरं नीलबर्हिणम्। प्रीतोऽस्मि तव धर्मज्ञ भुजंगाद्धिन ते भयम्॥ इदं नेत्रसहस्रं तु यत्तद्वर्हे भविष्यति। वर्षमाणे मयि मुदं प्राप्स्यसे प्रीतिलक्षणम्। एवमिन्द्रो वरं प्रादान्मयूरस्य सुरेश्वरः॥
en: And from joy Indra spoke to the purpleplumed peacock, 'Pleased am I with you righteous one. No fear shall spring to you from serpents; and your plumage shall be furnished with an hundred eyes. And when I shall shower, you shall be filled with glee as a token of my satisfaction with you.' Thus did Indra chief of celestials, confer a boon on the peacock.

sn: नीलाः किल पुरा बर्हा मयूराणां नराधिप। सुराधिपाद्वरं प्राप्य गताः सर्वेऽपि बहिणः॥
en: Formerly, O King, the peacock's wings had one unvaried blue. Having received the boon, the peacock departed.

sn: धर्मराजोऽब्रवीद्राम प्राग्वंशे वायसं प्रति। पक्षिस्तवास्मि सुप्रीतः प्रीतस्य वचनं शृणु॥
en: O Rāma, then the king of righteousness said to the crow, seated in front of the sacrificial apartment 'O bird, I am well pleased with you. Listen to my words as I utter them.

sn: यथान्ये विविधै रोगैः पीड्यन्ते प्राणिनो मया। ते न ते प्रभविष्यन्ति मयि प्रीते न संशयः॥
en: As I have been pleased with you, you shall without doubt, enjoy immunity from the various ailments to which the birds are subject.

sn: मृत्युतस्ते भयं नास्ति वरान्मम विहंगम। यावत्त्वां न वधिष्यन्ति नरास्तावद्भविष्यसि॥
en: O bird, from my curse fear of death shall not approach you; and you shall exist so long as people do not slay you.

sn: ये च मद्विषयस्था वै मानवाः क्षुधयार्दिताः। त्वयि भुक्ते सुतृप्तास्ते भविष्यन्ति सबान्धवाः॥
en: Those men residing in my dominion, being smitten with hunger, shall be refreshed along with your relations, when you have eaten and been refreshed.

sn: वरुणस्त्वब्रवीद्धंसं गङ्गातोयविचारिणम्। श्रूयतां प्रीतिसंयुक्तं ततः पत्ररथेश्वरम्॥ वर्णो मनोरमः सौम्यश्चन्द्रमण्डलसंनिमः। भविष्यति तवोदग्रः शुद्धफेनसमप्रभः॥
en: Then Varuņa addressed that lord of birds the swan ranging the waters of the Gangā, 'Listen to my words fraught with joy, your hue shall be charming, mild, and like to the lunar disc; and it shall be beautiful, resembling the sheen of spotless foam.

sn: मच्छरीरं समासाद्य कान्तो नित्यं भविष्यसि। प्राप्स्यसे चातुलां प्रीतिमेतन्मे प्रीतिलक्षणम्॥
en: And approaching my person you shall ever be beautiful to behold; and you shall, as a sign of my gratification, attain unparalleled complacence.

sn: हंसानां हि पुरा राम न वर्णः सर्वपाण्डुरः। पक्षा नीलाग्रसंवीताः क्रोडाः शष्पाग्रनिर्मलाः॥ अथाब्रवीद्वैश्रवणः कृकलासं गिरौ स्थितम्।
en: Formerly, O Rama, swans had not a hue of one unvaried whiteness. Their wings ended in, blue, and their breasts wore the spotless hue of tender grass. Then Vaiśravana addressed the chameleon as it was stationed at the mountain.

sn: हैरण्यं संप्रयच्छामि वर्णं प्रीतस्तवाप्यहम्॥ सद्रव्यं च शिरो नित्यं भविष्यति तवाक्षयम्। एष काञ्चनको वर्णो मत्प्रीत्या ते भविष्यति॥
en: Your hue shall be gold-gleaming. Pleased am I with you. Your undeteriorating head shall be ever gold-hued. And this golden hue of your shall proceed from my gratification?

sn: एवं दत्त्वा वरांस्तेभ्यस्तस्मिन्यज्ञोत्सवे सुराः। निवृत्ते सह राज्ञा ते पुनः स्वभवनं गताः॥
en: Having thus conferred boons on them at that festal place, the celestials, along with the king, (on the sacrifice) having ended, went to their abode.

sn: अथ जित्वा मरुत्तं स प्रययौ राक्षसाधिपः। नगराणि नरेन्द्राणां युद्धकाङ्क्षी दशाननः॥
en: Having vanquished Marutta, that lord of Rākşasas the Ten-faced Răvaņa, eager for encounter, began to range the capitals of the foremost monarchs (of the earth).

sn: समासाद्य तु राजेन्द्रान्महेन्द्रवरुणोपमान्। अब्रवीद्राक्षसेन्द्रस्तु युद्ध मे दीयतामिति॥ निर्जिताः स्मेति वा ब्रूत एष मे हि सुनिश्चयः। अन्यथा कुर्वतामेवं मोक्षो नैवोपपद्यते॥
en: And coming to the most powerful crowned heads (in the world) resembling Mahendra and Varuna, the Raksasa king said: 'Give me battle; or declare we have been defeated. This I am resolved upon. Otherwise there is no escape for you?'

sn: ततस्त्वभीरवः प्राज्ञाः पार्थिवा धर्मनिश्चयाः। मन्त्रयित्वा ततोऽन्योन्यं राजानः सुमहाबलाः॥ निर्जिताः स्मेत्यभाषन्त ज्ञात्वा वरबलं रिपोः।
en: Thereat those wise kings, possessed of great strength, and ever abiding by righteousness, being frightened (at Ravana's intimidation), took counsel of each other. And knowing the superior strength of the foe, they said, “We have been defeated.

sn: दुष्यन्तः सुरथो गाधिर्गयो राजा पुरूरवः॥ एते सर्वेऽब्रुवंस्तात निर्जिताः स्मेति पार्थिवाः। अथायोध्यां समासाद्य रावणो राक्षसाधिपः॥ सुगुप्तामनरण्येन शक्रेणेवामरावतीम्। स तं पुरुषशार्दूलं पुरंदरसमं बले॥ प्राह राजानमासाद्य युद्धं देहीति रावणः। निर्जितोऽस्मीति वा ब्रूहि त्वमेवं मम शासनम्॥
en: O child, Dusyanta, Suratha, Gadhi, and Gaya and king Pururavă all these kings said: 'We have been defeated.' And then Rāvaņa sovereign of the Rākşasas presented himself before Ayodhyā, governed by Anaranya, like Amarāvati ruled by. Sakra. And coming to that foremost of men king like to Purandara himself in prowess, Rāvana said, 'Give me battle; or say I have been defeated. This is my mandate.'

sn: अयोध्याधिपतिस्तस्य श्रुत्वा पापात्मनो वचः। अनरण्यस्तु संक्रुद्धो राक्षसेन्द्रमथाब्रवीत्॥ दीयते द्वन्द्वयुद्धं ते राक्षसाधिपते मया। संतिष्ठ क्षिप्रमायत्तो भव चैवं भवाम्यहम्॥
en: The lord of Ayodhyā, on hearing the words of that wicked-minded one, Anaranya, enraged, addressed the Raksasa-chief, saying, 'O king of Raksasas, I will give you combat, stay you. At once prepare for fight, and I also shall go and prepare myself.'

sn: अथ पूर्व श्रुतार्थेन निर्जितं सुमहद्बलम्। निष्क्रामत्तन्नरेन्द्रस्य बलं रक्षोवधोद्यतम्॥ नागानां दशसाहस्रं वाजिनां नियुतं तथा। रथानां बहुसाहस्रं पत्तीनां च नरोत्तम॥ महीं संछाद्य निष्क्रान्तं सपदातिरथं रणे।
en: When he had heard everything (regarding Răvaņa), the forces of that foremost of kings that had been intended for conquering (Ravana), sallied forth ready for bringing about the destruction of the of the Raksasa, ten-thousand elephants, a niyuta horse, and many thousands of cars and infantry, O best of men; and, that host consisting of infantry and cars, marched for encounter, covering up the earth.

sn: ततः प्रवृत्तं सुमहद्युद्धं युद्धविशारद॥ अनरण्यस्य नृपते राक्षसेन्द्रस्य चाद्भुतम्।
en: Then, O you proficient in fight, there took place a mighty and wonderful encounter between king Anaranya and that lord of Raksasas.

sn: तद्रावणबलं प्राप्य बलं तस्य महीपतेः॥ प्राणश्यत तदा सर्व हव्यं हुतमिवानले। युद्ध्वा च सुचिरं कालं कृत्वा विक्रममुत्तमम्॥ प्रज्वलन्तं तमासाद्य क्षिप्रमेवावशेषितम्। प्राविशत्संकुलं तत्र शलभा इव पावकम्॥
en: That host, of the king encountering the forces of Rāvana, were extinguished like to clarified butter thrown into the (sacrificial) fire. And having fought valorously for a long time, the remnant of the royal forces, suddenly coming in contact with the flaming Räkşasas ranks, were destroyed like to swarms of locusts entering into fire.

sn: सोऽपश्यत्तन्नरेन्द्रस्तु नश्यमानं महाबलम्। महार्णवं समासाद्य वनापगशतं यथा॥
en: He saw the mighty army of that powerful monarch destroyed by the (adversary), like to a hundred streams absorbed by an approaching ocean.

sn: ततः शक्रधनुःप्रख्यं धनुर्विस्फारयन्स्वयम्। आससाद नरेन्द्रस्तं रावणं क्रोधमूर्छितः॥
en: And then himself drawing his bow resembling the bow itself of Sakra, that foremost of sovereigns, beside himself with wrath, approached Rāvana.

sn: अनरण्येन तेऽमात्या मारीचशुकसारणाः। प्रहस्तसहिता भग्ना व्यद्रवन्त मृगा इव॥
en: Brought down by Anaranya, his (Ravana's) councillors Mārica, Suka, and Sarana with Prahasta, took to their heels like to dear.

sn: ततो बाणशतान्यष्टौ पातयामास मूर्धनि । तस्य राक्षसराजस्य इक्ष्वाकुकुलनन्दनः॥
en: Then that son of the Ikşvāku race discharged eight hundred arrows at Rāvana's head.

sn: तस्य बाणाः पतन्तस्ते चक्रिरे न क्षतं क्वचित्। वारिधारा इवाभ्रेम्यः पतन्त्यो गिरिमूर्धनि ॥
en: And like to showers pouring down on the top of a mountain, his shafts did not inflict any wound (on Ravana).

sn: ततो राक्षसराजेन क्रुद्धेन नृपतिस्तदा। तलेनाभिहतो मूर्ध्नि स रथानिपपात ह॥
en: Then the king, smitten on the head with a slap by the enraged king of Rākşasas, dropped down from his car.

sn: स राजा पतितो भूमौ विह्वलः प्रविवेपितः। वज्रदग्ध इवारण्ये सालो निपतितो यथा॥
en: The king, deprived of his senses, fell down on the earth, with his body trembling all over; as falls in a forest a sāla scathed with heaven's fire.

sn: तं प्रहस्याब्रवीद्रक्ष इक्ष्वाकुं पृथिवीपतिम्। किमिदानी फलं प्राप्तं त्वया मां प्रति युद्ध्यता॥
en: Thereat the Raksasa, laughing, spoke to that Iksvāku, lord of the earth, 'What is this that you have gathered as the fruit of your encounter with me.

sn: त्रैलोक्ये नास्ति यो द्वन्द्वं मम दद्यानराधिप। शङ्के प्रसक्तो भोगेषु न शृणोषि बलं मम॥
en: O king, there is none in this triune sphere that can combat with me. Having hitherto been sunk in lunacy, you have not heard of my strength.

sn: तस्यैवं ब्रुवतो राजा मन्दासुर्वाक्यमब्रवीत्। किं शक्यमिह कर्तुं वै कालो हि दुरतिक्रमः॥
en: As he was speaking thus, the king, whose sounds were fast running out said: 'What can I do in this matter. Verily time is incapable of being controlled.

sn: नह्यहं निर्जितो रक्षस्त्वया चात्मप्रशंसिना। कालेनैव विपन्नोऽहं हेतुभूतस्तु मे भवान्।॥ किं त्विदानी मया शक्यं कर्तुं प्राणपरिक्षये। नह्यहं विमुखी रक्षो युध्यमानस्त्वया हतः॥
en: I have been overcome by Time; you are merely an instrument. What can I do now, when I am going to-lose my life? I never turned away from fight; I have been slain fighting.

sn: इक्ष्वाकुपरिभावित्वाद्वचो वक्ष्यामि राक्षस। यदि दत्तं यदि हुतं यदि मे सुकृतं तपः। यदि गुप्ताः प्रजाः सम्यक् तदा सत्यं वचोऽस्तु मे।।२९
en: But, O Raksasas, I shall tell you something in consequence of the disgrace that the Ikşvāku race has met with (today). If I have practised charity, if I have offered oblations into fire, if I have carried on pious penances, if i have governed my people well, then be my words verified!

sn: उत्पत्स्यते कुले ह्यस्मिनिक्ष्वाकूणां महात्मनाम्। रामो दाशरथि म यस्ते प्राणान्हरिष्यति।३०॥
en: There shall spring in the line of the highsouled Ikşvāku, one named Rāma son to Dasaratha who shall deprive your life.

sn: ततो जलधरोदग्रस्ताडितो देवदुन्दुभिः। तस्मिन्नुदाहृते शापे पुष्पवृष्टिश्च खाच्च्युता॥
en: As he uttered this imprecation, the celestial kettle-drums sounded like the roaring of clouds; and blossoms showered down from the sky.

sn: ततः स राजा राजेन्द्र गतः स्थानं त्रिविष्टपम्। स्वर्गते च नृपे तस्मिन्राक्षसः सोऽपसर्पत॥
en: Then, that best of kings, went to heaven; and when that king had gone to the celestial regions, the Raksasa (also) went away.

sn: ततो वित्रासयन्मान्पृथिव्यां राक्षसाधिपः। आससाद घने तस्मिन्नारदं मुनिपुङ्गवम्॥
en: As the lord of Rākşasas was ranging the earth frightening everyone, Nārada foremost of ascetics, came to that wood mounted on a cloud,

sn: तस्याभिवादनं कृत्वा दशग्रीवो निशाचरः। अब्रवीत्कुशलं पृष्ट्वा हेतुमागमनस्य च॥
en: Thereupon saluting him, the night-ranger Tennecked one enquired after his welfare as well as the occasion of his visit.

sn: नारदस्तु महातेजा देवर्षिरमितप्रभः। अब्रवीन्मेघपृष्ठस्थो रावणं पुष्पके स्थितम्॥ राक्षसाधिपते सौम्य तिष्ठ विश्रवसः सुत। प्रीतोऽस्म्यभिजनोपेत विक्रमैरूर्जितैस्तव॥
en: That Devarsi the exceedingly energetic Nārada of immeasurable splendour, seated on the back of the cloud, addressed Ravana, who was stationed in Puspaka, saying, O lord of Raks asas, o placid one, O son of Viśravā, stay. I am well pleased with your prowess and fame.

sn: विष्णुना दैत्यघातैश्च गन्धर्वोरंगधर्षणैः। त्वया समं विमर्दैश्च भृशं हि परितोषितः॥
en: And even as Vişnu had pleased me by destroying the Daityas, you pleased me by harassing the Gandharvas and serpents.

sn: किंचिद्वक्ष्यामि तावत्तु श्रोतव्यं श्रोष्यसे यदि। तन्मे निगदतस्तात समाधिं श्रवणे कुरु॥
en: I will tell you something. If you would hear what I have to say then, O child, listen heedfully as I unfold it.

sn: किमयं बध्यते तात त्वयावध्येन दैवतैः। हत एव ह्ययं लोको यदा मृत्युवशं गतः।७।।
en: Why, my child, do you slay these*; you are incapable of being slain by even the celestials. All these (men) are subject to death, they are verily slain. *i.e. human being.

sn: देवदानवदैत्यानां यक्षगन्धर्वरक्षसाम्। अवध्येन त्वया लोकः क्लेष्टुं योग्यो न मानुषः॥
en: The world of man is unworthy of being afflicted by you who are incapable of being destroyed by Deities, Dānavas, Daityas, Yakşas, Gandharvas and Rākşasas.

sn: नित्यं श्रेयसि सम्मूढं महद्भिर्व्यसनैर्वृतम्। हन्यात्कस्तादृशं लोकं जराव्याधिशतैर्युतम्॥
en: Who should slay creatures, who are ever stupid in respect of their welfare, environed by mighty dangers, and encompassed by hundreds of decrepitude and decease?

sn: तैस्तैरनिष्टोपगमैरजस्रं यत्र कुत्र कः। मतिमान्मानुषे लोके युद्धेन प्रणयी भवेत्॥
en: What sensible person can set his heart on slaying human beings, who are everywhere beset with a perennial stream of evils.

sn: क्षीयमाणं दैवहतं क्षुत्पिपासाजरादिभिः। विषादशोकसंमूढं लोकं त्वं क्षपयस्व मा॥
en: Do not you enfeeble those beings who are already enfeebled and smitten by Divinity with hunger, thirst, old age etc. and who are overwhelmed with sorrow, and grief.

sn: पश्य तावन्महाबाहो राक्षसेश्वर मानुषम्। मूढमेवं विचित्रार्थं यस्य न ज्ञायते गतिः॥ क्वचिद्वादित्रनृत्यादि सेव्यते मुदितैर्जनैः। रुद्यते चापरैरातैर्धाराश्रुनयनाननैः॥
en: O mighty-armed one, o lord of Rākşasas, behold man, albeit having their sense stupified, engaged in the pursuit of various interests, and themselves not understanding their own ways;* some pass their time merrily with dancing and playing on musical instruments while others weep distressfully with tears streaming from their eyes down their cheeks. *Gati, according to the commentator, means the time of employment and suffering. I think the ordinary meaning answers, and give it accordingly.

sn: मातापितृसुतस्नेहभाबन्धुमनोरमैः। मोहितोऽयं जनो ध्वस्तः क्लेशं स्वं नावबुध्यते।।१४
en: Down fallen on account of their attachment for their mothers and fathers and sons, and of their desires touching their wives and friends they set small store by labours having the hereafter as their object.

sn: तत्किमेवं परिक्लिश्य लोकं मोहनिराकृतम्। जित एव त्वया सौम्य मर्त्यलोको न संशयः॥
en: What then is the use of affecting a race that is brought down ever by its own infatuation. O placid one, this world is verily conquered by you, there is no doubt.

sn: अवश्यमेभिः सर्वैश्च गन्तव्यं यमसादनम्। तन्निगृणीष्व पौलस्त्य यमं परपुरंजय॥ तस्मिञ्जिते जितं सर्वं भवत्येव न संशयः।
en: These for certain will have to repair to the abode of Yama. Therefore, O Paulastya, O captor of hostile capitals, do you put down Yama. On him being conquered, all will doubtless be conquered by you.

sn: एवमुक्तस्तु लङ्केशो दीप्यमानं स्वतेजसा ॥ अब्रवीनारदं तत्र संप्रहस्याभिवाद्य च। महर्षे देवगन्धर्वविहार समरप्रिय॥ अहं समुद्यतो गन्तुं विजयार्थं रसातलम्।
en: Thus addressed Lankā's lord, flaming in native energy, addressed Narada, laughing and saluting him. 'O you that delightest in the sport of gods and Gandharvas, and that take pleasure in warfare, I am ready to go to the nethermost regions for the purpose of conquest.

sn: ततो लोकत्रयं जित्वा स्थाप्य नागान्सुरान्वशे। समुद्रममृतार्थं च मथिष्यामि रसालयम्॥
en: And conquering the three worlds, and bringing under subjection serpents and celestials I shall for ambrosia churn the nether regions.

sn: अथाब्रवीद्दशग्रीवं नारदो भगवानृषिः। क्व खल्विदानी मार्गेण त्वयेहान्येन गम्यते॥ अयं खलु सुदुर्गम्यः प्रेतराजपुरं प्रति। मार्गो गच्छति दुर्धर्ष यमस्यामित्रकर्शन ॥
en: Then the reverend sage Närada spoke to the Ten-necked Ravana, Who save you can on forsooth go that journey? Verily, o irrepressible one, O destroyer of foes, the way leading to the city of the lord of the dead is difficult of access.

sn: स तु शारदमेघाभं हासं मुक्त्वा दशाननः। उवाच कृतमित्येव वचनं चेदमब्रवीत्॥
en: Thereat laughing, the Ten-faced one said to the saint resembling a mass of white clouds, "This is done.

sn: तस्मादेवं महाब्रह्म वैवस्वतवधोद्यतः। गच्छामि दक्षिणामाशां यत्र सूर्यात्मजो नृप॥
en: Therefore,* O great Brahmana, intent upon slaying the Vaivasvata's son, I will go by this way which lead to the king-the offspring of the sun. *As you has commanded me.

sn: मया हि भगवन्क्रोधात्प्रतिज्ञातं रणार्थिना। अवजेष्यामि चतुरो लोकपालानिति प्रभो॥
en: O master, from wrath I have vowed that I will, eager for encounter, O reverend one, conquer the four Lokapālas.

sn: तदिह प्रस्थितोऽहं वै पितृराजपुरं प्रति। प्राणिसंक्लेशकर्तारं योजयिष्यामि मृत्युना ॥
en: Then here go I to the city of the lord of the Pitſs; and I am determined to compass the death of him that visit creatures with smart.

sn: एवमुक्त्वा दशग्रीवो मुनिं तमभिवाद्य च। प्रययौ दक्षिणामाशां प्रविष्टः सह मन्त्रिभिः॥
en: Having delivered himself thus and saluted the sage, he, entering the southern way with his councillors, proceeded along.

sn: नारदस्तु महातेजा मुहूर्तं ध्यानमास्थितः। चिन्तयामास विप्रेन्द्रो विधूम इव पावकः॥
en: The exceedingly energetic Nārada best of Brāhmaṇas resembling a smokeless fire, remaining rapt for a while, began to reflect.

sn: येन लोकस्वयः सेन्द्राः क्लिश्यन्ते सचराचराः। क्षीणे चायुषि धर्मेण स कालो जेष्यते कथम्॥
en: How can (Ravana) conquer Time who, when its life wane, righteously visit with affection the time, sphere with Indra, fraught with mobile and immobile.

sn: स्वदत्तकृतसाक्षी यो द्वितीय इव पावकः। लब्धसंज्ञा विचेष्टन्ते लोका यस्य महात्मनः॥ यस्य नित्यं त्रयो लोका विद्रवन्ति भयार्दिताः। तं कथं राक्षसेन्द्रोऽसौ स्वयमेव गमिष्यति॥
en: How can this lord of Raksasas, of himself, go to him who, resembling another fire, bear to the gifts and acts (of persons), that high-souled one of whom attaining consciousness, people put forth their activity; and; afflicted with the fear of whom these three worlds fall away?

sn: यो विधाता च धाता च सुकृतं दुष्कृतं तथा। त्रैलोक्यं विजितं येन तं कथं विजयिष्यते। अपरं किं तु कृत्वैवं विधानं संविधास्यति॥
en: How can (Rāvana) subdue him who ordain things both great and small, who met rewards and punishments for good and bad acts, and who himself has conquered the three worlds? Resorting* to what other means shall Rāvana secure (victory)? *Explains the commentator: "Time has every thing under its control. Like the all-enclosing space, time pervades all that is. This being so, resorting what transcending Time, shall Rāvana obtain victory over it."

sn: कौतूहलं समुत्पन्नो यास्यामि यमसादनम्। विमर्दै द्रष्टुमनयोर्यमराक्षसयोः स्वयम्॥
en: I am curious about it. To Yama's abode shall I go for witnessing the encounter between Yama and the Raksasa.

sn: एवं संचिन्त्य विप्रेन्द्रो जगाम लघुविक्रमः। आख्यातुं तद्यथावृत्तं यमस्य सदनं प्रति॥
en: Having reflected thus, that foremost of Vipras endowed with fleet vigour, bent his steps towards the abode of Yama, for the purpose of relating to him all that had taken place.

sn: अपश्यत्स यमं तत्र देवमग्निपुरस्कृतम्। विधानमनुतिष्ठन्तं प्राणिनो यस्य यादृशम्॥
en: There he saw that god Yama sitting in front of fire and offering into it the good and evil fruits of their actions. * *Ordaining happiness and misery to the lives of people according to their acts.'

sn: स तु दृष्ट्वा यमः प्राप्तं महर्षि तत्र नारदम्। अब्रवीत्सुखमासीनमय॑मावेद्य धर्मतः॥
en: Seeing the Maharși Nārada arrive there, Yama offering him arghya according to the ordinance, addressed him saying, when he was seated at his case:

sn: कच्चित्क्षेमं नु देवर्षे कच्चिद्धर्मो न नश्यति। किमागनकृत्यं ते देवगन्धर्वसेवित ॥
en: 'O Devarsi, is it well with you? And does virtue deteriorate.'* And, why, O you honoured of deities, and Gandharvas, do you come?' *The Original has: "Do not virtue wane." This in English would imply the very reverse what Nārada intends to say. He says: 'Do religion deteriorate?' i.e. 'I hope, religion does not deteriorate.' This is an idiom and natural usage accounts for it, although that usage must in the nature of things be based on a subtle ground of season.

sn: अब्रवीत्तु तदा वाक्यं नारदो भगवानृषिः। श्रूयतामभिधास्यामि विधानं च विधीयताम्॥ एष नाम्नो दशग्रीवा पितृराज निशाचरः। उपयाति वशं नेतुं विक्रभैस्त्वां सुदुर्जयम्॥
en: Thereat the reverend sage, Narada, said; Hearken. I shall tell (you); and (after hearing me out) do you what is fit. o king of the Pitrs, here come the night-ranger named ten-necked, for bringing you under his sway you who are incapable of being conquered.

sn: एतेन काणेनाहं त्वरितो ह्यागतः प्रभो। दण्डप्रहरणस्याद्य तव किं नु भविष्यति॥
en: O master, for this reason it is that I have come hither hastily, doubtful what shall befall you who have the rod for your weapon.

sn: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे दूरादंशुमन्तमिवोदितम्। ददृशुर्दीप्तमायान्तं विमानं तस्य रक्षसः॥
en: In the meanwhile they saw the Rākṣasa's car approach from afar, flaming and like to the rayfurnished (one) risen.

sn: तं देशं प्रभया तस्य पुष्पकस्य महाबलः। कृत्वा वितिमिरं सर्वं समीपमभ्यवर्तत॥
en: And dispelling the gloom of that region with the effulgence of Pușpaka; that exceedingly powerful (Raksasa) came forward.

sn: सोऽपश्यत्स महाबाहुर्दशग्रीवस्ततस्ततः। प्राणिनः सुकृतं चैव भुञ्जानांश्चैव दुष्कृतम्॥
en: The mighty-armed ten-necked one all around saw creatures reaping the consequences of their fair and foul acts.

sn: अपश्यत्सैनिकांश्चास्य यमस्यानुचरैः सह। यमस्य पुरुषैरुप्रै।ररूपैर्भयानकैः॥ ददर्श वध्यमानांश्च किलश्यमानांश्च देहिनः। क्रोशतश्च महानादं तीव्रनिष्टनतत्परान्॥ कृमिभिर्भक्ष्यमाणांश्च सारमेयैश्च दारुणैः। श्रोत्रायासकरा वाचो वदतश्च भयावहाः॥ संतार्यमाणान्वैतरणी बहुशः शोणितोदकाम्। वालुकासु च तप्तासु तप्यमानान्मुहुर्मुहुः॥ असिपत्रवने चैव भिद्यमानानधार्मिकान्। रौरवे क्षारनद्यां च क्षुरधारासु चैव हि ॥ पानीयं याचमानांश्च तृषितान्क्षुधितानपि। शवभूतान्कृशान्दीनान्विवर्णान्मुक्तमूर्धनान् ॥ मलपङ्कधरान्दीनान्रुक्षांश्च परिधावतः। ददर्श रावणो मार्गे शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः॥
en: There he saw Yama's soldiery along with Yama's followers, fierce-forms, grim-visaged and terrific. And he saw corporeal beings undergoing torments and pain, and emitting loud cries and sharp shrieks; preyed on by worms and fell dogs: and uttering words capable of striking pain and terror into the heart (of the hearer): and people swimming in the Vaitarani profusely running blood; and momentarily burning with hot sands; unrighteous wights pierced in a wood of asipatra, (plunged) in Raurava, in the river of borate of soda; and (cut) with razor-edges; asking for drinks; and afflicted with hunger and thirst; converted into corpses, lean, woe-begone, and pallid with hair flowing loosely; having dust and filth (on their bodies), and running about distressfully with dry forms; on the way saw Rāvana by hundreds and by thousands.

sn: कांश्चिच्च गृहमुख्येषु गीतवादित्रनिःस्वनैः। प्रमोदमानानद्राक्षीद्रावणः सुकृतैः स्वकैः॥ गोरसं गोप्रदातारो अन्नं चैवानदायिनः। गृहांश्च गृहदातारः स्वकर्मफलमश्नतः॥ सुवर्णमणिमुक्ताभिः प्रमदाभिरलंकृताम्। धार्मिकानपरांस्तत्र दीप्यमानान्स्वतेजसा॥ ददर्श स महाबाहू रावणो राक्षसाधिपः। ततस्तान्भिद्यमानांश्च कर्मभिर्दुष्कृतैः स्वकैः॥ रावणो मोचयामास विक्रमेण बलाबली।
en: Rāvana also saw some in front of houses engaged in merry-making with songs and strains of instruments, as the fruit of their pious acts; and (saw) the giver of kine regaling themselves with milk; the dispenser of rice, feeding on the same, the bestower of abodes, enjoying mansions, as the fruit of their several acts; and persons living with damsels decked with gold and gems and jewels; and other pious folks, flaming in their native energy, all these saw Rāvana lord of Rākşasas. And by his might that mighty one delivered those that were being tormented by their wicked acts.

sn: प्राणिनो मोक्षितास्तेन दशग्रीवेण रक्षसा॥ सुखमापुर्मुहूर्त ते ह्यतर्कितमचिन्तितम्। प्रेतेषु मुच्यमानेषु राक्षसेन महीयसा॥ प्रेतगोपाः सुसंक्रुद्धा राक्षसेन्द्रमभिद्रवन्।
en: On being liberated by that Rākṣasa the tennecked one, those creatures in a moment began to enjoy their release, that had come to them without thought or suspense. And on the dead being delivered by the magnanimous Rākşasa, the guards of the dead, getting enraged, rushed at the Rākşasa sovereign.

sn: ततो हलहलाशब्दः सर्वदिग्भ्यः समुत्थितः। धर्मराजस्य योधानां शूराणां संप्रधावताम्॥
en: There arose a mighty clamour from all sides; from the heroic warriors of the king of righteousness rushing (all around.)

sn: ते प्रासैः परिधैः शूलैर्मुसलैः शक्तितोमरैः। पुष्पकं समधर्षन्त शूराः शतसहस्रशः॥ तस्यासनानि प्रासादन्वेदिकास्तोरणानि च। पुष्पकस्य बभञ्जुस्ते शीघ्रं मधुकरा इव ॥
en: And those heroes by hundreds and by thousands assailed (Puspaka) with prāsas, and bludgeons, and darts and maces, and spears and tomaras. And swiftly swarming like bees, they began to break the seats, blocks, daises and gateways (of the car.)

sn: देवनिष्ठानभूतं तद्विमानं पुष्पकं मृधे। भज्यमानं तथैवासीदक्षयं ब्रह्मतेजसा ॥
en: In that conflict Pușpaka presided over by divine energy, incapable of being destroyed by virtue of Brahma power, being broken, resumed its former shape.

sn: असंख्या सुमहत्यासीत्तस्य सेना महात्मनः। शूराणामग्रयातॄणां सहस्राणि शतानि च ॥
en: Countless were the soldiers of that highsouled one consisting hundreds and thousands of heroic warriors, (ever) forward for fight.

sn: ततो वृक्षैश्च शैलैश्च प्रासादानां शतैस्तथा। ततस्ते सचिवास्तस्य यथाकामं यथाबलम्॥ अयुध्यन्त महावीराः स च राजा दशाननः। ते तु शोणितदिग्धाङ्गाः सर्वशस्त्रसमाहताः॥
en: According to the measure of their might his (Rāvana's) councillors great heroes all, as well as the ten-faced one himself with might and main, fought with trees and crags and hundreds of blocks of buildings.

sn: अमात्या राक्षसेन्द्रस्य चक्रुरायोधनं महत्। अन्योन्यं ते महाभागा जघ्नुः प्रहरणै शम्॥
en: And those councillors of the lord of Räkşasas, assailed with every kind of weapons, with their persons bathed in blood, fought fiercely.

sn: यमस्य च महाबाहो रावणस्य च मन्त्रिणः। अमात्यांस्तांस्तु संत्यज्य यमयोधो महाबलाः॥
en: And O large-armed the exalted councillors of Yama and Răvaņa sore assailed each other with And leaving the councillors alone the highly powerful warriors of Yama rushed against and Daśānana* with a shower of spears. *Ravana.

sn: तमेव चाभ्यधावन्त शूलवर्दशाननम्। ततः शोणितदिग्धाङ्गः प्रहारैर्जर्जरीकृतः। फुल्लाशोक इवाभाति पुष्पके राक्षसाधिपः॥
en: And then pierced through and through by those weapons, with his person covered with blood, the Rākṣasa king appeared like a flowering Kinśuka in Pușpaka. * *This simile is peculiarly appropriate and beautiful. Puspaka, the name of Ravana's car, means composed of flowers; and this signification shining one arms. a askance, as it were, over the direct sense of the sentence, heightens the delight the reader feels on imagining the principal figure. "Rāvana seated in Puspaka, covered with blood, looked likeblossoming Kinsuka.'

sn: स तु शूलगदाप्रासाञ्छक्तितोमरसायकान्। मुमोच च शिलावृक्षान्मुमोचास्त्रबलाद्बली॥
en: Thereat that powerful one, by virtue of his mastery over weapons, began to hurl darts and maces, prāsas and spears and tomaras and crags and trees.

sn: तरूणां च शिलानां च शस्त्राणां चातिदारुणम्। यमसैन्येषु तद्वर्ष पपात धरणीतले॥
en: That terrific shower of trees, rocks and arms, alighted on the army of Yama (fighting) on the earth.

sn: तांस्तु सर्वान्विनिर्मिद्य तदत्रमपहत्य च। जघ्नुस्ते राक्षसं घोरमेकं शतसहस्रशः॥
en: And snapping those weapons and resisting (those volleys of) arms, they smote at the Räkșasa fighting alone by hundreds and thousands.

sn: परिवार्य च तं सर्वे शैलं मेघोत्करा इव। भिन्दिपालैश्च शूलैश्च निरुच्छ्वासमपोथयन्॥ विमुक्तकवचः क्रुद्धः सिद्धः शोणितविस्रवैः। ततः स पुष्पकं त्यक्त्वा पृथिव्यामवतिष्ठत॥
en: And encompassing him even as clouds encompass mountain, they rendered (Ravana) inert by means of Bhindipālas and darts. And with his mail torn open, his anger raging fiercely, and covered with blood streaming over his person, he, forsaking, his car, stood upon the ground.

sn: ततः स कार्मुकी वाणी समरे चाभिवर्धत। लब्धसंज्ञो मुहूर्तेन क्रुद्धस्तस्थौ यथान्तकः॥
en: Then furnished with his bow and holding his shafts, (Ravana) regaining his senses in a short time, increased in energy and stood in the field like the finisher.

sn: ततः पाशुपतं दिव्यमस्त्रं संधाय कार्मुके। तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति तानुक्त्वा यच्चापं व्यपकर्षत॥
en: Now fixing the divine Pāśupata on his bow, and saying to them, 'stay! stay!' he drew that bow.

sn: आकर्णात्स विकृष्याथ चापमिन्द्रारिराहवे। मुमोच तं शरं क्रुद्धस्त्रिपुरे शंकरो यथा॥
en: And enraged, (Ravana) resembling Rudra himself, in fight drawing his bow to his car, discharged that shaft even as Sankara had discharged at Tripura.

sn: तस्य रूपं शरस्यासीत्सधूमज्वालमण्डलम्। वनं दहिष्यतो धर्मे दावाग्नेरिव मूर्च्छतः॥
en: And the appearance of the shaft was like an extinguishing fire in summer with smoke with flames, burning up a forest.

sn: ज्वालामाली स तु शरः क्रव्यादानुगतो रणे। मुक्तो गुल्मान्दुमांश्चापि भस्म कृत्वा प्रधावति ॥
en: And garlanded with glory that shaft followed byghosts,* in that encounter; rushed on, burning to ashes the loose bushes and trees lying in its way. *The instrument being Siva's, it naturally was followed by ghosts as his attendants.

sn: ते तस्य तेजसा दग्धाः सैन्या वैवस्वतस्य तु। बले तस्मिन्निपतिता माहेन्द्रा इव केतवः॥
en: And burnt up by its energy, the most of Vaivasvata fell down in the field like to banners of Mahendra.

sn: ततस्तु सचिवैः सार्धं राक्षसो भीमविक्रमः। ननाद सुमहानादं कम्पयनिव मेदिनीम्॥
en: Thereat the Räksasa of terrific prowess along with his councillors began to set up tremendous shouts; as if making the earth tremble.

sn: स तस्य तु महानादं श्रुत्वा वैवस्वतः प्रभुः। शत्रु विजयिनं मेने स्वबलस्य च संक्षयम्॥
en: Hearing his mighty-shouts, that lord Vaivasvata knew that his adversary had gained the day and that his own host had been destroyed.

sn: स हि योधान्हतान्मत्वा क्रोधसंरक्तलोचनः। अब्रवीत्त्वरितः सूतं रथो मे उपनीयताम्॥
en: Knowing that his forces had been slain, he, with his eyes crimsoned with passion hastily spoke to his charioteer, ‘Bring you my car.'

sn: तस्य सूतस्तदा दिव्यमुपस्थाप्य महारथम्। स्थितः स च महातेजा अध्यारोहत तं रथम्॥
en: Thereat the charioteer brought the noble and mighty car and stood (there) and then that exceeding energetic one mounted the car.

sn: प्रासमुद्गरहस्तश्च मृत्युस्तस्याग्रतः स्थितः। येन संक्षिप्यते सर्वं त्रैलोक्यमिदमव्ययम्॥
en: In front (of his car) stood death, equipped with prāsas and maces in his hands, who makes nothing of this entire triune world; incapable of deterioration.

sn: कालदण्डस्तु पार्श्वस्थो मूर्तिमानस्य चाभवत्। यमप्रहरणं दिव्यं तेजसा ज्वलदग्निवत्॥
en: And beside (him) was the rod of Kāla in its native from the divine instrument of Yama like to a flaming fire on account of its own energy.

sn: ततो लोकत्रयं क्षुब्धमकम्पन्त दिवौकसः। कालं दृष्ट्वा तथा क्रुद्धं सर्वलोकभयावहम्॥ ततस्त्वचोदयत्सूतस्तानश्वान्रुचिरप्रभान्। प्रययौ भीमसंनादो यत्र रक्षःपतिः स्थितः॥
en: Then on beholding Kāla, infuriated, tending to strike terror into all creatures, was agitated the triune universe, and trembling over took the denizens of heaven. The charioteer urged on the steeds possessed of graceful splendour; and arrived where the lord of Rākşasas was posted.

sn: मुहूर्तेन यमं ते तु हया हरिहयोपमाः। प्रापयन्मनसस्तुल्या यत्र तत्प्रस्तुतं रणम्॥ दृष्ट्वा तथैव विकृतं रथं मृत्युसमन्वितम्। सचिवा राक्षसेन्द्रस्य सहसा विप्रदुर्दुवुः॥
en: In a moment those horses like to thought (in celerity,) and resembling the steeds themselves of Hari, took Yama where the warfare had already begun. Seeing the frightful car in that aspect with Death present in it, the ministers of the Rākşasa monarch at once took to their heels.

sn: लघुसत्त्वतया ते हि नष्टसंज्ञा भयार्दिताः। नेह युद्धं समर्थाः स्म इत्युक्त्वा प्रययुर्दिशः॥
en: In vonsequence of their being comparatively inferior in point of strength they were deprived of their senses, and afficted with fear; and saying, 'Here we are not equal to fighting' they went their way.

sn: स तु तं तादृशं दृष्ट्वा रथं लोकभयावहम्। नाक्षुभ्यत दशग्रीवो न चापि भयमाविशत्॥ स तु रावणमासाद्य व्यसृजच्छक्तितोमरान्। यमो मर्माणि संक्रुद्धो रावणस्य न्यकृन्तत॥
en: But seeing that car capable of striking terror into folks, the Ten-necked did not experience any agitation, nor did fear enter his heart. And approaching Ravana, Yama, enraged, discharged spears and tomaras, and began to pierce Rāvana's marrow.

sn: रावणस्तु ततः स्वस्थः शरवर्षं मुमोच ह। तस्मिन्वैवस्वतरथे तोयवर्षमिवाम्बुदः॥
en: But Rāvana, without at all feeling any smart, began to shower arrows on Vaivasvata's vehicle, resembling a downpour caused by clouds.

sn: ततो महाशक्तिशतैः पात्यमानैर्महोरसि । नाशक्नोत्प्रतिकर्तुं स राक्षसः स्वल्पपीडितः॥
en: Again at his spacious breast, that Raksasa who had undergone slender injury, could not resist, (Yama's arms) with hundreds of mighty darts hurled.

sn: एवं नानाप्रहरणैर्यमेनामित्रकर्षिणा। सप्तरात्रं कृतः संख्ये विसंज्ञो विमुखो रिपुः॥
en: And in this way that destroyer of foes Yama fought for seven nights with various arms; until at length his enemy was driven back and deprived of his senses.

sn: तदासीत्तुमुलं युद्धं यमराक्षसयोर्द्वयोः। जयमाकाङ्क्षतोर्वीर समरेष्वनिवर्तिनोः॥
en: Then, O hero, there took place nighty onset between Yama and the Rākşasas both eager for victory and both never tiring of fight.

sn: ततो देवाः सगन्धर्वाः सिद्धाश्च परमर्षयः। प्रजापतिं पुरस्कृत्य समेतास्तद्रणाजिरे॥
en: And celestials and Gandharvas and Siddhas, and the supreme saints, placing Prajāpati at their head, presented themselves at the fight.

sn: संवर्त इव लोकानां युध्यतोरभवत्तदा। राक्षसानां च मुख्यस्य प्रेतानामीश्वरस्य च॥
en: The encounter that then took place between that foremost of Rākşasas and the lord of the Dead was like the universal upheaval.

sn: राक्षसेन्द्रोऽपि विस्फार्य चापमिन्द्राशनिप्रभम्। निरन्तरमिवाकाशं कुर्वन्बाणांस्ततोऽसृजत्॥
en: And stretching his bow resembling in splendour the thunderbolt of Indra, he discharged arrows covering up the sky.

sn: मृत्युं चतुर्भिर्विशिखैः सूतं सप्तभिरार्दयत्। यमं शतसहस्रेण शीघ्रं मर्मस्वताडयत्॥
en: And he smote Death with four, the (Yama's), charioteer with seven, and swiftly struck Yama in the marrow with hundreds and thousands of shafts. :

sn: ततः क्रुद्धस्य वदनाद्यमस्य समजायत। ज्वालामाली सनिःश्वासः सधूमः कोपपावकः॥
en: Then from forth Yama's mouth there issued darted flames with his teeth mixed with smoke, the fire of his fury.

sn: तदाश्चर्यमथो दृष्ट्वा देवदानवसंनिधौ। प्रहर्षितौ सुसंरब्धौ मृत्युकालौ बभूवतुः॥
en: Witnessing this wonder in the presence of the deities and Dānavas, both Death and Time were fixed with wrath and were filled with delight.

sn: ततो मृत्युः क्रुद्धतरो वैवस्वतमभाषत। मुञ्च मां समरे यावद्धन्मीमं पापराक्षसम्॥
en: Then Death, growing still more wroth, addressed Vaivasvata saying; “Let me go. I shall slay this sinful Rākşasa.”

sn: नैषा रक्षो भवेदद्य मर्यादा हि निसर्गतः। हिरण्यकशिपुः श्रीमान्नमुचिः शम्बरस्तथा॥ निसन्दिधूमकेतुश्च बलिर्वैरोचनोऽपि च। शंभुर्दैत्यो महाराजो वृत्रो बाणस्तथैव च ॥ राजर्षयः शास्त्रविदो गन्धर्वाः समहोरगाः। ऋषयः पन्नगा दैत्या यक्षाश्च ह्यप्सरोगणाः॥ युगान्तपरिवर्ते च पृथिवी समहार्णवा। क्षयं नीता महाराज सपर्वतसरिद्रुमा॥ एते चान्ये च बहवो बलवन्तो दुरासदाः। विनिपन्ना मया दृष्टाः किमुतायं निशाचरः॥
en: Even this is my native might this Räksasa will be no more. Hiranyakasipu, the graceful Namuci, and Sambara, Nişandi and Dhūmaketu and Virocana's offspring Bali, and the Daitya Śambhu that mighty monarchs, Vſtra and Bāņa; and Rājarșis versed in all branches of learnings and Gandharvas, and mighty serpents, and sages, and Pannagas and Yaksas, and swarms of Apsarās and the Earth herself containing vastly oceans and mountains and rivers and trees, at the unrolling of a Yuga all these, O mighty monarch have I brought to dissolution. All these and many more endowed with strength and incapable of being overcome, were at the very sight of me compassed with peril, and what is this ranger of the night?

sn: मुश्च मां साधु धर्मज्ञ यावदेनं निहन्म्यहम्। नहि कश्चिन्मया दृष्टो बलवानपि जीवति ॥
en: Let me go. O you cognisant of righteousness, I shall slay this one. There is none that, albeit strong, can survive after having been seen by me.

sn: बलं मम न खल्वेतन्मर्यादैषा निसर्गतः। स दृष्टो न मया काल मुहूर्तमपि जीवति॥
en: Verily this is not mine strength, this might pertain to me by nature. O Time, if seen by me, he won't live for a moment.

sn: तस्यैवं वचनं श्रुत्वा धर्मराजः प्रतापवान्। अब्रवीत्तत्र तं मृत्युं त्वं तिष्ठेनं निहन्म्यहम्॥ ततः संरक्तनयनः क्रुद्धो वैवस्वतः प्रभुः। कालदण्डममोघं तु तोलयामास पाणिना॥ यस्य पार्श्वेषु निहिताः कालपाशाः प्रतिष्ठिताः। पावकाशनिसंकाशो मुद्गरो मूर्तिमान्स्थितः॥
en: Hearing these words of his, the puissant king of righteousness spoke there to death, 'Do you stay. I myself shall slay him.' Then with his eyes reddened that lord, Vaivasvata, wielded with his hand the infallible dart of time; while by him lay the redoubtable noose of time and the mace in its native shape resembling fire and the thunderbolt.

sn: दर्शनादेव यः प्राणान्प्राणिनामपि कर्षति। किं पुनः स्पृशमानस्य पात्यमानस्य वा पुनः॥
en: He, who by his very sight draw away the lives of creatures, what should be said of its touching and being hurled at people?

sn: स ज्वालापरिवारस्तु निर्दहन्निव राक्षसम्। तेन स्पृष्टो बलवता महाप्रहरणोऽस्फुरत्॥
en: And touched by that powerful one, that mighty weapon, engist with flames, attained access of energy, and seemed to consume the Raksasa.

sn: ततो विदुद्रुवुः सर्वे तस्मात्रस्ता रणाजिरे। सुराश्च क्षुभिताः सर्वे दृष्ट्वा दण्डोद्यतं यमम्॥
en: In the field of battle, everyone afficted with fear, ran away from it. And beholding Yama with his rod uplifted, the celestials were agitated.

sn: तस्मिन्प्रहर्तुकामे तु यमे दण्डेन रावणम्। यमं पितामहः साक्षादर्शयित्वेदमब्रवीत्॥
en: On Yama being desirous of slaying Rāvana, by his rod, the great-father manifesting himself spoke to Yama.

sn: वैवस्वत महाबाहो न खल्वमितविक्रम। न हन्तव्यस्त्वयैतेन दण्डेनैष निशाचरः॥
en: O Vaivasvata, O mighty-armed one, O you of immeasurable prowess, this certainly must not be. You should not with your rod slay the nightranger.

sn: वरः खलु मयैतस्मै दत्तस्त्रिदशपुङ्गव। स त्वया नानृतः कार्यो यन्मया व्याहृतं वचः॥
en: For, O foremost of celestials, I have conferred a boon on him; and you should not render false the words that I have uttered.

sn: यो हि मामनृतं कुर्याद्देवो वा मानुषोऽपि वा। त्रैलोक्यमनृतं तेन कृतं स्यान्नात्र संशयः॥ क्रुद्धेन विप्रमुक्तोऽयं निर्विशेष प्रियाप्रिये। प्रजाः संहरते रौद्रो लोकत्रयभयावहः॥
en: Verily he, that, whether a god or a human being, shall falsify my words, shall render the triune universe false. There is no doubt about this. If this terrific weapon, capable of affrighting the three spheres, be discharged alike at friends and foes, it will destroy creatures.

sn: अमोघो ोष सर्वेषां प्राणिनाममितप्रभः। कालदण्डो मया सृष्टः सर्वं मृत्युपुरस्कृतः।॥
en: This rod of Kāla, of immeasurable might and incapable of being resisted by creatures, was created by me as having the power of compassing th : death of all beings.

sn: तन्न खल्वेष ते सौम्य पात्यो रावणमूर्धनि। नह्यस्मिन्पतिते कश्चिन्मुहूर्तमपि जीवति॥
en: Therefore, O mild one, you forsooth should not bring it down on Rāvana's head. If this alights on any one, he does not live for a moment.

sn: यदि ह्यस्मिन्निपतिते न म्रियेतैष राक्षसः। प्रियते वा दशग्रीवस्तदाप्युभयतोऽनृतम्॥
en: Whether on this weapon alighting, the tennecked does not die, or if he does do either way falsehood is the consequence.

sn: तन्निवर्तय लङ्केशाद्दण्डमेतं समुद्यतम्। सत्यं च मां कुरुष्वाद्य लोकांस्त्वं यद्यवेक्षसे॥
en: Therefore do you keep your uplifted weapon off Larkā's lord. If you have any care for these worlds do you establish my truth.

sn: एवमुक्तस्तु धर्मात्मा प्रत्युवाच यमस्तदा। एष व्यावर्तितो दण्डः प्रभविष्णुहि नो भवान्॥
en: Thus addressed, Yama then answered, I restrain this rod. You are our lord.

sn: किं त्विदानी मया शक्यं कर्तुं रणगतेन हि। न मया यद्ययं शक्यो हन्तुं वरपुरस्कृतः॥
en: But as I can not slay this one, who has obtained a boon, what then shall I do now in the field?

sn: एष तस्मात्प्रणश्यामि दर्शनादस्य रक्षसः। इत्युक्त्वा सरथः साश्वस्तत्रैवान्तरधीयत॥
en: Therefore shall I disappear from the sight of this Rākşasa.' Having said this, even there did he vanish with his car and horses.

sn: दशग्रीवस्तु तं जित्वा नाम विश्राव्य चात्मनः। आरुह्य पुष्पकं भूयो निष्क्रान्तो यमसादनात्॥
en: Having vanquished him and distinguished his name, Rāvaņa again ascended his Puşpaka and went out of the abode of Yama.

sn: स तु वैवस्वतो देवैः सह ब्रह्मपुरोगमैः। जगाम त्रिदिवं हृष्टो नारदश्च महामुनिः॥
en: With a delighted heart Vaivasvata along with the deities headed by Brahmā as well as that mighty ascetic-Narada, went to the celestial regions.

sn: ततो जित्वा दशग्रीवो यमं त्रिदशपुंगवम्। रावणस्तु रणश्लाघी स्वसहायान्ददर्श ह॥
en: Having vanquished Yama, the foremost of celestials, Rāvana delighting in warfare, saw his adherents.

sn: ततो रुधिरसिक्ताङ्गं प्रहारैर्जर्जरीकृतम्। रावणं राक्षसा दृष्ट्वा विस्मयं समुपागमन्॥
en: Then seeing Rāvaņa, with his person bathed in blood, bettered by the weapon discharged at him, they were seized with surprise.

sn: जयेन वर्धयित्वा च मारीचप्रमुखास्ततः। पुष्पकं भेजिरे सर्वे सान्त्विता रावणेन तु॥
en: And hailing him with victory, the councillors headed by Mārīca, having been encouraged by Ravana, ascended Puspaka.

sn: ततो रसातलं रक्षः प्रविष्टः पयसां निधिम्। दैत्योरगगणाध्युष्टं वरुणेन सुरक्षितम्॥
en: Then the Rākṣasa entered the region of waters the abode of Daityas and serpents, well protected by Varuna.

sn: स तु भोगवतीं गत्वा पुरीं वासुकिपालिताम्। कृत्वा नागान्वशे हृष्टो ययौ मणिमयीं पुरीम्॥
en: Arriving at Bhogavati the city governed by Vāsuki, he brought the serpents under subjection and then, delighted, bent his course to the palace Manimayi.

sn: निवातकवचास्तत्र दैतेया लब्धवरा वसन्। राक्षसस्तान्समागम्य युद्धाय समुपाह्वयत्॥ ते तु सर्वे सुविक्रान्ता दैतेया बलशालिनः। नानाप्रहरणास्तत्र प्रहृष्टा युद्धदुर्मदाः॥ शूलैस्त्रिशूलैः कुलिशैः पट्टिशासिपरश्वधैः। अन्योन्यं बिभिदुः कृद्धा राक्षसा दानवास्तथा॥ तेषां तु युध्यमानानां साग्रः संवत्सरो गतः। न चान्यतरतस्तत्र विजयो वा क्षयोऽपि वा।।।।
en: There dwelt the Nivātakavacas, who had obtained boons. Those Daityas were possessed of prowess and endowed with strength, carrying various weapons, breathing high spirits and invincible in battle. And the Dānavas and Rāks asas growing enraged fell to raving each other with darts and tridents, Kuliśas and axes and pațțiśas. And as they fought one entire year passed away and neither side obtained victory or was worsted.

sn: ततः पितामहस्तत्र त्रैलोक्यगतिरव्ययः। आजगाम द्रुतं देवो विमानवरमास्थितः॥
en: Then that way of the triune sphere, that God, the undeteriorating Great-father, swiftly presented himself on the scene mounted on his excellent car.

sn: निवातकवचानां तु निवार्य रणकर्म तत्। वृद्धः पितामहो वाक्यमुवाच विदितार्थवत्॥
en: Making the Nivātakavacas desist from battle the ancient great-father spoke in clear words.

sn: नह्ययं रावणो युद्धे शक्यो जेतुं सुरासुरैः। न भवन्तः क्षयं नेतुमपि सामरदानवैः॥
en: Even the celestials and the Asuras are not able to vanquish this Rāvaņa in battle; nor can the Dänavas backed by the gods can destroy you.

sn: राक्षसस्य सखित्वं च भवद्भिः सह रोचते। अविभक्ताश्च सर्वार्थाः सुहृदां नात्र संशयः॥
en: Do you therefore turn your minds to making friendship with the Rākşasas. All interests are forsooth the common possession of friends.

sn: ततोऽग्निसाक्षिकं सख्यं कृतवांस्तत्र रावणः। निवातकवचैः सार्धं प्रीतिमानभवत्तदा ॥
en: Thereat Rāvaņa made friendship with the Nivātakavacas in the presence of Fire; and then rejoiced greatly.

sn: अर्चितस्तैर्यथान्यायं संवत्सरमथोषितः। स्वपुरानिर्विशेषं च प्रियं प्राप्तो दशाननः॥
en: And duly honoured (by then) Daśānana passed there a year, without any feeling of that place being different from his own home: and spent his time agreeably.

sn: तत्रोपधार्य मायानां शतमेकं समाप्तवान्। सलिलेन्द्रपुरान्वेषी भ्रमति स्म रसातलम्॥
en: Having learnt there a hundred sorts of illusion, he directed his course to Rasātala, searching for the city of the lord of waters.

sn: ततोऽश्मनगरं नाम कालकेयैरधिष्ठितम्। गत्वा तु कालकेयांश्च हत्वा तत्र बलोत्कटान्॥ शूर्पणख्याश्च भर्तारमसिना प्राच्छिनत्तदा। श्यालं च बलवन्तं च विद्युज्जिह्व बलोत्कटम्॥ जिह्वया संलिहन्तं च राक्षसं समरे तदा।
en: And then going to the city named Asma ruled by the Kālakāyas, (Rāvana) slew the Kālakāyas endowed with terrific strength; and then with his sword cut off his brother-in-law,' the husband of Śūrpanakhā, he mighty Vidyutjibha possessed of terrific strength; as the Rākşasa in the encounter was licking (the limbs of Ravana's followers).
