sn: मुहुर्मुहुश्च वैदेही परिदाय महायशाः। स्वमाश्रमं शिष्यवृतः पुनरायान्महातपाः॥
en: Having consigned the charge of Sītā to the hands of the female ascetics, the great and illustrious ascetic Vālmīki, followed by his disciples, speedily proceeded towards his holy hermitage.

sn: दृष्ट्वा तु मैथिली सीतामाश्रमे संप्रवेशिताम्। संतापमगमद्धोरं लक्ष्मणो दीनचेतनः॥
en: Beholding the great ascetic Vālmīki thus conducting Sītā into his own hermitage Lakş mana's heart was bewildered with grief.

sn: अब्रवीच्च महातेजाः सुमन्वं मन्त्रसारथिम्। सीतासंतापजं दुःखं पश्य रामस्य सारथे॥
en: Thereupon he said to the expert charioteer Sumantra. Do you perceive Rāma's grief consequent upon the separation from Sītā.

sn: ततो दुःखतरं किं नु राघवस्य भविष्यति। पत्नी शुद्धसमाचारां विसृज्य जनकात्मजाम्॥
en: His spouse-the daughter of Janaka, is perfectly pure; what can be more painful than that Rāma is living alone having renounced her?

sn: व्यक्तं दैवादहं मन्ये राघवस्य विनाभवम्। वैदेह्या सारथे नित्यं दैवं हि दुरतिक्रमम्॥
en: It is clear to me, O Sumantra, that this separation of Rāma, has been brought about by the influence of destiny-for it is hard to get over accident.

sn: यो हि देवान्सगन्धर्वानसुरान्सह राक्षसैः। निहन्याद्राघवः क्रुद्धः स दैवं पर्युपासते॥
en: Even that Rāma, who, when enraged, is capable of slaying the celestials, Gandharvas, Asuras and Rākşasas, has been engaged in the worship of destiny.

sn: पुरा रामः पितुर्वाक्याद्दण्डके विजने वने। उषित्वा नव वर्षाणि पञ्च चैव महावने॥
en: Formerly did Rāma go through miserics, residing in the forest of Dandaka, at the command of his sire for fourteen years.

sn: ततो दुःखतरं भूयः सीताया विप्रवासनम्। पौराणां वचनं श्रुत्वा नृशंसं प्रतिभाति मे॥ को नु धर्माश्रयः सूत कर्मण्यस्मिन्यशोहरे। मैथिली समनुप्राप्तः पौरे नार्थवादिभिः॥
en: But this banishment of Sītā appears to me as exceedingly painful and most ruthless. O charioteer, the opinion of the citizens is by no means just; consequently what shall we gain by performing such a bad action for fame as the exile of Sita?

sn: एता वाचो बहुविधाः श्रुत्वा लक्ष्मणभाषिताः। सुमन्त्रः श्रद्धया प्राज्ञो वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह॥
en: Hearing those words of Lakşmaņa of various types, the wise Sumantra reverentially replied.

sn: न संतापस्त्वया कार्यः सौमित्रे मैथिली प्रति। दृष्टमेतत्पुरा विप्रैः पितुस्ते लक्ष्मणाग्रतः॥
en: Be not aggrieved for Sītā, O Saumitri Formerly in the presence of your sire the Brāhmaṇas related this account of Sītā's exile.

sn: भविष्यति दृढं रामो दुःखप्रायो विसौख्यभाक् । प्राप्स्यते च महाबाहुर्विप्रयोगं प्रियैर्वृतम् ॥ त्वां चैव मैथिली चैव शत्रुघ्नभरतौ तथा। स त्यजिष्यति धर्मात्मा कालेन महता महान्॥
en: Rāma shall be deprived of all happiness and be separated from his dear wife; what more, the virtuous-souled Rāma, having long arms, shall, under the influence of time, renounce you, Sītā, Śatrughna and Bharata.

sn: इदं त्वयि न वक्तव्यं सौमित्रे भरतेऽपि वा। राज्ञा वो व्याहृतं वाक्यं दुर्वासा यदुवाच ह॥ महाजनसमीपे च मम चैव नरर्षभ। ऋषिणा व्याहृतं वाक्यं वसिष्ठस्य च संनिधौ ॥
en: O Lakṣmaṇa, when Durvāsa was addressed by the king Dasaratha as to your future he replied in the above way. I have told you the same. Do you not communicate this to Śatrughna Bharata or any body. O foremost of men, Durbasa said this to Daſaratha before me, Vaşistha and other great men.

sn: ऋषेस्तु वचनं श्रुत्वा मामाह पुरुषर्षभः। सूत न क्वचिदेवं ते वक्तव्यं जनसंनिधौ॥
en: Hearing the words of Rsi, Dasaratha, the foremost of men, said to me, "O charioteer, do not reveal this secret to any body.

sn: तस्याहं लोकपालस्य वाक्यं तत्सुसमाहितः। नैव जात्वनृतं कुर्यामिति मे सौम्य दर्शनम्॥ सर्वथैव न वक्तव्यं मया सौम्य तवाग्रतः। यदि ते श्रवणे श्रद्धा श्रूयतां रघुनन्दन ॥
en: O gentle one, it is not proper by any means to falsify the words of the king Dasaratha. I shall always, very carefully, carry out his orders. It is not proper to reveal this mystery before you. Still I do so for your curiosity has been greatly excited.

sn: यद्यप्यहं नरेन्द्रेण रहस्यं श्रावितं पुरा। तथाप्युदाहरिष्यामि दैवं हि दुरतिक्रमम्॥ येनेदमीदृशं प्राप्तं दुःखं शोकसमन्वितम्। न त्वया भरतस्याग्रे शत्रुघ्नस्यापि संनिधौ॥
en: Tough this mystery was communicated formerly by the king Dasaratha and though it is not proper to reveal it to any body, still I express it before you that you may not, on hearing it, be worked up with sorrow; for destiny is hard to be got over. And it is by the influence of that destiny that you have met with such a sorrow and grief. However, do you not reveal this secret to Satrughna and Bharata.

sn: तच्छ्रुत्वा भाषितं तस्य गम्भीरार्थपदं महत्। तयं ब्रूहीति सौमित्रिः सूतं तं वाक्यमब्रवीत्।।२०
en: Hearing these grave and important words of Sumantra, Laksmana ordered him to relate.

sn: तथा संचोदितः सूतो लक्ष्मणेन महात्मना। तद्वाक्यमृषिणा प्रोक्तं व्याहर्तुमुपनक्रमे॥
en: Being thus requested by the high-souled Laks maņa, Sumantra began to reveal the mystery of Durbasa's account.

sn: पुरा नाम्ना हि दुर्वासा अत्रेः पुत्रो महामुनिः। वसिष्ठस्याश्रमे पुण्ये वार्षिक्यं समुवास ह॥
en: In the days of yore the great ascetic Durbāsā, the son of Atri, resided for a year in the holy hermitage of Vasiştha.

sn: तमाश्रमं महातेजाः पिता ते सुमहायशाः। पुरोहितं महात्मानं दिदृक्षुरगमत्स्वयम्॥
en: At that time your sire, the highly effulgent and illustrious Dasaratha, with a view to see his high-souled priest Vasistha, repaired there.

sn: स दृष्ट्वा सूर्यसंकाशं ज्वलन्तमिव तेजसा। उपविष्टं वसिष्ठस्य सव्यपार्श्वे महामुनिम्॥
en: He saw the great ascetic Durbásā, burning like the sun in his effulgence, seated on the right hand side of Vasiștha. Thereupon he humbly saluted those two leading ascetics.

sn: तौ मुनी तापसश्रेष्ठौ विनीतावभ्यवादयत्। स ताभ्यां पूजितो राजा स्वागतेनासनेन च। पाद्येन फलमूलैश्च उवास मुनिभिः सह॥
en: And they too, welcoming him, received him duly with seat, water to wash feet, Arghya, fruits and roots, Then he lived there in the company of the ascetics.

sn: तेषां तत्रोपविष्टानां तास्ताः सुमधुराः कथाः। बभूवुः परमर्षीणां मध्यादित्यगतेऽहनि॥
en: Thereupon during the noon, all those ascetics, seated there, began to dwell upon various pleasant topics.

sn: ततः कथायां कस्यांचित्प्राञ्जलिः प्रग्रहो नृपः। उवाच तं महात्मानमत्रेः पुत्रं तपोधनम्॥
en: During an interval Dasaratha, with folded hands and uplifted arms, said to the high-souled son of Atri-Durbāsā, having asceticism for his wealth.

sn: भगवन्किप्रमाणेन मम वंशो भविष्यति। किमायुश्च हि मे रामः पुत्राश्चान्ये किमायुषः॥
en: O illustrious Sir, how long shall my family remain in existence? What is the extent of the lease of life granted to Rāma and my other sons?

sn: रामस्य च सुता ये स्युस्तेषामायुः कियद्भवेत्। काम्यया भगवन्ब्रूहि वंशस्यास्य गतिं मम॥
en: How long shall the descendants of Rāma live? And what shall be the end of my race? Do you relate all this to me.

sn: तच्छ्रुत्वा व्याहृतं वाक्यं राज्ञो दशरथस्य तु। दुर्वासाः सुमहातेजा व्याहर्तुमुपचक्रमे॥
en: Hearing the words of the king Dasaratha the highly effulgent Durbāsā replied.

sn: शृणु राजन्पुरावृतं तदा देवासुरे युधि। दैत्याः सुरैर्भय॑माना भृगुपत्नी समाश्रिताः। तया दत्ताभयास्तत्र न्यवसन्नभयास्तदा॥
en: Hear, the early history, O king. During the encounter between the celestials and Asuras, the demons, ,, being remonstrated with by the celestials sought shelter of the wife of Bhrguyour priest. Bhrgu's wife having promised them help they lived there fearlessly.

sn: तया परिगृहीतांस्तान्दृष्ट्वा क्रुद्धः सुरेश्वरः। चक्रेण शितधारेण भृगुपन्याः शिरोऽहरत्॥
en: Having beheld the demons thus helped by Bhrgu's wife, Hari, the king of celestials, enraged, chopped off her head with his sharp discuss.

sn: ततस्तां निहतां दृष्ट्वा पत्नीं भृगुकुलोद्वहः। शशाप सहसा क्रुद्धो विष्णुं रिपुकुलार्दनम्॥
en: And angry on beholding his wife slain, Bhrgu, imprecated a curse on Vişņu, the slayer of enemies' race, saying.

sn: यस्मादवध्यां मे पत्नीमवधीः क्रोधमूर्च्छितः। तस्मात्त्वं मानुषे लोके जनिष्यसि जनार्दन॥ तत्र पत्नीवियोगं त्वं प्राप्स्यसे बहुवार्षिकम्।
en: Being beside yourself with anger you have slain my wife, not worthy of being killed; therefore, O Janārddana, you shall be born in the region of mortals. And there you shall remain separated from your spouse for many long years.

sn: शापाभिहतचेतास्तु स्वात्मना भावितोऽभवत्॥ अर्चयामास तं देवं भृगुः शापेन पीडितः। तपसाराधितो देवो ह्यब्रवीद्भक्तवत्सलः॥ लोकानां संप्रियार्थ तं शापं मृह्यमुक्तवान्।
en: Having imprecated this curse, Bhțgu was greatly pained and being propitiated by his adoration, Visnu, fond of disciples, said. “Having slain Rāvaņa and others, I shall be, for the behoof of . mankind, subject to this imprecation."

sn: इति शप्तो महातेजा भृगुणा पूर्वजन्मनि॥ इहागतो हि पुत्रत्वं तव पार्थिवसत्तम। राम इत्यभिविख्यातस्त्रिषु लोकेषु मानद ॥
en: O bestower of kings, the highly effulgent Vişnu, thus imprecated by Bhrgu in the days of yore, has been born as your son in this birth and has been celebrated under the appellation of Rama.

sn: तत्फलं प्राप्स्यते चापि भृगुशापकृतं महत्। अयोध्यायाः पती रामो दीर्घकालं भविष्यति ॥
en: O conferer of honours, for sooth shall Rāma partake of the fruits of Bhrgu's curse. He shall reign in Ayodhyā for a long time.

sn: सुखिनश्च समृद्धाश्च भविष्यन्त्यस्य येऽनुगाः। दशवर्षसहस्राणि दशवर्षशतानि च॥ रामो राज्यमुपासित्वा ब्रह्मलोकं गमिष्यति।
en: All his followers shall be happy and prosperous. Having reigned for eleven thousand years Rāma shall repair to the region of Brahmă.

sn: समृद्धैश्चाश्वमेधैश्च इष्ट्वा परमदुर्जयः॥ राजवंशांश्च बहुशो बहून्संस्थापयिष्यति।
en: None shall be able to vanquish him. He shall celebrate many a horse-sacrifice with profuse gifts and shall establish many royal families.

sn: द्वौ पुत्रौ तु भविष्येते सीतायां राघवस्य तु॥ स सर्वमखिलं राज्ञो वंशस्याह गतागतम्। आख्याय सुमहातेजास्तूष्णीमासीन्महामुनिः।।२३
en: He shall beget on Sită two sorts. Having thus related to Dasaratha the past and future of his family the highly effulgent great ascetic Durbāsā became silent.

sn: तूष्णीभूते तदा तस्मिनराजा दशरथो मुनौ। अभिवाद्य महात्मानौ पुनरायात्पुरोत्तमम्॥
en: He being silent-the great king Dasaratha, having bowed to the two high-souled ascetics, again returned to his city Ayodhyā.

sn: एतद्वचो मया तत्र मुनिना व्याहृतं पुरा। श्रुतं हृदि च निक्षिप्तं नान्यथा तद्भविष्यति॥
en: I had heard there all there words of the great ascetic Durbāså. Up to this time they are lying in my heart. Rsis' words shall never prove fruitless.

sn: सीतायाश्च ततः पुत्रावभिषेक्ष्यति राघवः। अन्यत्र न त्वयोध्यायां मुनेस्तु वचनं यथा॥
en: According to the words of Rși Rāma shall install two sons of Sītā in Ayodhyā, not anywhere else.

sn: एवं गते न संतापं कर्तुमर्हसि राघव। सीतार्थे राघवार्थे वा दृढो भव नरोत्तम॥
en: Under these circumstances, O Laksmana, you should not grieve for Sītā or Rāma; in their interest do you become patient.

sn: श्रुत्वा तु व्याहृतं वाक्यं सूतस्य परमाद्भुतम्। प्रहर्षमतुलं लेभे साधु साध्विति चाब्रवीत्॥
en: Hearing those wondrous words of the charioteer Sumantra, Lakşmaņa became greatly happy and eulogised him again and again?

sn: ततः संवदतोरेवं सूतलक्ष्मणयोः पथि। अस्तम गते वासं केशिन्यां तावथोषतुः॥
en: They thus conversing with one another on their way back, the sun set. They accordingly spent that night on the banks of Kesini.

sn: तत्र तां रजनीमुष्य केशिन्यां रघुनन्दनः। प्रभाते पुनरुत्थाय लक्ष्मणः प्रययौ तदा॥ ततोऽर्धदिवसे प्राप्ते प्रविवेश महारथः। अयोध्यां रत्नसंपूर्णां हृष्टपुष्टजनावृताम्॥
en: Having spent the night on the banks of Kesini, the mighty car-warrior Lakşmaņa, got up early in the morning and again proceeded on his journey (home) and reached in the noon the city of Ayodhyā filled with various jewels and delighted and plump citizens.

sn: सौमित्रिस्तु परं दैन्यं जगाम सुमहामतिः। रामपादौ समासाद्य वक्ष्यामि किमहं गतः॥
en: But the high-souled Lakşmaņa became greatly sorry stricken with the thought as to what he should relate on approaching the feet of Rāma.

sn: तस्यैवं चिन्तयानस्य भवनं शशिसंनिभम्। रामस्य परमोदारं पुरस्तात्समदृश्यत॥
en: While proceeding with this thought he saw the highly picturesque palace of Rāma resembling the rays of the moon.

sn: राज्ञस्तु भवनद्वारि सोऽवतीर्य नरोत्तमः। अवाङ्मुखो दीनमनाः प्रविवेशानिवारितः॥
en: Having descended from his car at the palacegate, Laksmana, the foremost of men, with his face down wards and a distressed heart, unobstructed, entered the palace.

sn: स दृष्ट्वा राघवं दीनमासीनं परमासने। नेत्राभ्यामश्रुपूर्णाभ्यां ददर्शाग्रजमग्रतः॥ जग्राह चरणौ तस्य लक्ष्मणो दीनचेतनः। उवाच दीनया वाचा प्राञ्जलिः सुसमाहितः।७।।
en: Having entered there he saw his elder brother Rāma seated poorly on an excellent seat with his eyes full of tears. Being greatly pained at the sight, Saumitri touched his feet and with folded palms said.

sn: आर्यस्याज्ञां पुरस्कृत्य विसृज्य जनकात्मजाम्। गङ्गातीरे यथोद्दिष्टे वाल्मीकेराश्रमे शुभे।८॥ तत्र तां च शुभाचारामाश्रमान्ते यशस्विनीन्। पुनरप्यागतो वीरपादमूलमुपासितुम्॥
en: O worshipful sir, having obeyed your behest's I have left the daughter of Janaka at the holy hermitage of Vālmiki near the banks of the Gangā. Having left that illustrious pure lady at the skirt of the hermitage. I have again come to serve your feet

sn: मा शुचः पुरुषव्याघ्र कालस्य गतिरीदृशी। त्वद्विधा नहि शोचन्ति बुद्धिमन्तो मनस्विनः॥
en: Do you not grieve, O foremost of men, for such is the cause of time. The intelligent people like you do not grieve.

sn: सर्वे क्षयान्ता निचयाः पतनान्ताः समुच्छ्याः। संयोगा विप्रयोगान्ता मरणान्तं च जीवितम्॥
en: When there is grow there is decay, where there is prosperity there is ruin, and where there is birth there is death.

sn: तस्मात्पुत्रेषु दारेषु मित्रेषु च धनेषु च। नातिप्रसङ्गः कर्तव्यो विप्रयोगो हि तैध्रुवम्॥
en: Therefore attachment to wife, sons, friends and riches is not proper, for surely shall be brought about separation with them.

sn: शक्तस्त्वमात्मनात्मानं विनेतुं मनसा मनः। लोकान्सर्वांश्च काकुत्स्थ किं पुनः शोकमात्मनः॥ नेदृशेषु विमुह्यन्ति त्वद्विधाः पुरुषर्षभाः।
en: O Kakutstha, While you can control yourself and your mind, should you not be able to bear this trifling pain of separation? Leading men like yourself are never overwhelmed by all these things.

sn: अपवादः स किल ते पुनरेष्यति राघव॥ यदर्थं मैथिली त्यक्ता अपवादभयानृप। सोऽपवादः पुरे राजन्भविष्यति न संशयः॥
en: O Rāghava, you shall again be blamed by the people. In fear of this calumny, O king, that you have renounced Maithili. And if do you grieve for that spouse your calumny shall undoubtedly be deep-routed in the kingdom.

sn: स त्वं पुरुषशार्दूल धैर्येण सुसमाहितः। त्यजेमां दुर्बलां बुद्धिं संतापं मा कुरुष्व ह॥
en: Therefore do you restore yourself patiently, O foremost of men. Do you give up this weakness and or not sorry.

sn: एवमुक्तः स काकुत्स्थो लक्ष्मणेन महात्मना। उवाच परया प्रीत्या सौमित्रिं मित्रवत्सलः॥
en: The intelligent Lakşmaņa, the son of Sumitrā, having said this, Rāma, the descendant of Käkutstha and fond of friends, with great delight said.

sn: एवमेतन्नरश्रेष्ठ यथा वदसि लक्ष्मण। परितोपश्च मे वीर मम कार्यानुशासने॥
en: You have spoken the truth, O Laksmana, O foremost of men. I have been greatly delighted, O hero for your carrying out my orders.

sn: निवृत्तिश्चागता सौम्य संतापश्च निराकृतः। भवद्वाक्यैः सुरुचिरैरनुनीतोऽस्मि लक्ष्मण॥
en: O gentle Saumitrī, my grief and sorrow have been removed for those pleasant words of yours.

sn: लक्ष्मणस्य तु तद्वाक्यं निशम्य परमाद्भुतम्। सुप्रीतश्चाभवद्रामो वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह॥
en: Hearing those wondrous words of Lakşmaņa Rāma was greatly delighted and said.

sn: दुर्लभस्त्वीदृशो बन्धुरस्मिन्काले विशेषतः। यादृशस्त्वं महाबुद्धिर्मम सौम्य मनोऽनुगः॥
en: O you having an auspicious look, you are gifted with great intellect and after my heart; a friend like you is rare at such a time.

sn: यच्च मे हृदये किंचिद्वर्तते शुभलक्षण। तन्निशामय च श्रुत्वा कुरुष्व वचनं मम॥
en: But O beautiful Saumitrī, do you, apprised of my intention, carry out my words.

sn: चत्वारो दिवसाः सौम्य कार्य पौरजनस्य च । अकुर्वाणस्य सौमित्रे तन्मे मर्माणि कृन्तति॥
en: O gentle son of Sumitrā, for not looking to state business for these days I have been pierced to the very vitals.

sn: आहूयन्तां प्रकृतयः पुरोधा मन्त्रिणस्तथा। कार्यार्थिनश्च पुरुषाः स्त्रियो वा पुरुषर्षभ॥
en: Do you therefore call here men, or women, priests or councillors who have come for business.

sn: पौरकार्याणि यो राजा न करोति दिने दिने। संवृते नरके घोरे पतितो नात्र संशयः॥
en: For sooth do a king falls into the dreadful bell where the wind does not blow, who does not daily look into his state affairs.

sn: श्रूयते हि पुरा राजा नृगो नाम महायशाः। बभूव पृथिवीपालो ब्रह्मण्यः सत्यवाक्शुचिः॥
en: I have heard, O foremost of men, that there lived in the days of yore a highly illustrious, truthful and pure-minded king, ever devoted to the Brahmanas, by the name Nrga.

sn: स कदाचिद्भवां कोटी: सवत्साः स्वर्णभूषिताः। नृदेवो भूमिदेवेभ्यः पुष्करेषु ददौ नृपः॥
en: Once on a time at the sacred pilgrimage of Puşpaka that king conferred upon the Brāhmaṇas one Koți of kine with calves adorned with golden ornaments.

sn: ततः सङ्गाद्गता धेनुः सवत्सा स्पर्शितानघ। ब्राह्मणस्याहिताग्नेस्तु दरिद्रस्योञ्छवर्तिनः॥
en: Accidentally on that occasion, a cow with calf belonging to a poor Brāhmaṇa, living upon law means, was given away along with other kine.

sn: नष्टां गां क्षुधातॊ वै अन्विषंस्तत्र तत्र ह। नापश्यत्सर्वराष्ट्रेषु संवत्सरगणान्बूहन्॥
en: Undergoing hunger and thirst, the master of that cow travelled for a long time in many places in search of it.

sn: ततः कनखलं गत्वा जीर्णवत्सां निरामयाम्। ददृशे तां स्विकां धेनुं ब्राह्मणस्य निवेशने॥
en: Thereupon having reached the province of Kanakhala he espied his own cow in the house of a Brāhmaṇa. The cow was well kept and the young one was grown up.

sn: अथ तां नामधेयेन स्वकेनोवाच ब्राह्मणः। आगच्छ शबलेत्येवं सा तु शुश्राव गौः स्वरम्॥
en: Thereupon the Brāhmaṇa called the cow by the name given by him saying “Sabalā, come."

sn: तस्य तं स्वरमाज्ञाय क्षुधार्तस्य द्विजस्य वै। अन्वगात्पृष्ठतः सा गौर्गच्छन्तं पावकोपमम्॥
en: The cow heard that and recognising the voice of the Brāhmaṇa followed him. And he preceded her burning like fire.

sn: योऽपि पालयते विप्रः सोऽपि गामन्वगाबृतम्। गत्वा च तमृषि चष्टे मम गौरिति सत्वरम्॥ स्पर्शिता राजसिंहेन मम दत्ता नृगेण ह।
en: And the Brāhmaṇa, in whose house the cow so long remained, speedily pursued her and approaching the ascetic said. “This cow is mine. The king Nrga conferred this upon me.”

sn: तयोर्ब्राह्मणयोर्वादो महानासीद्विपश्चितोः॥ विवदन्तौ ततोऽन्योन्यं दातारमभिजग्मतुः।
en: So there arose a great quarrel between the two learned Brāhmaṇas. And thus quarrelling they both approached him who had given away the cow.

sn: तौ राजभवनद्वारि न प्राप्तौ नृगशासनम्॥ अहोरात्राण्यनेकानि वसन्तौ क्रोधमीयतुः। ऊचतुश्च महात्मानौ तावुभौ द्विजसत्तमौ। क्रुद्धौ परमसंप्राप्तौ वाक्यं घोराभिसंहतम्॥ अर्थिनां कार्यसिद्ध्यर्थं यस्मात्त्वं नैषि दर्शनम्। अदृश्यः सर्वभूतानां कृकलासो भविष्यसि ॥ बहुवर्षसहस्राणि बहुवर्षशतानि च। श्वभ्रे त्वं कृकलीभूो दीर्घकालं निवत्स्यसि॥
en: And though they waited for a long time at the gate they did not obtain permission to enter the palace. Thereat both of them were greatly enraged and imprecated dreadful curses, saying Since you have not granted us an interview though we have been waiting here for a long time, you shall, by our curse, remain invisible, being a lizard. You shall in this state live in a den for many hundred and thousand years.

sn: उत्पत्स्यते हि लोकेऽस्मिन्यदूनां कीर्तिवर्धनः। वासुदेव इति ख्यातो विष्णुः पुरुषविग्रहः॥ स ते मोक्षयिता शापाद्राजस्तस्माद्भविष्यसि। कृता च तेन कालेन निष्कृतिस्ते भविष्यति ॥ भारावतरणार्थं हि नरनारायणावुभौ। उत्पत्स्येते महावीरों कलौ युग उपस्थिते॥
en: When Vişņu assuming a human person shall be born in the Vasudeva family of Yādavas and enhance their glory he shall liberate you from the curse. Immediately before the advent of the Kali Yuga the Rși Nara Nārāyaṇa gifted with great prowess shall descend upon earth to relieve her of the burden.

sn: एवं तौ शापमुत्सृज्य ब्राह्मणौ विगतज्वरौ। तां गां हि दुर्बलां वृद्धां ददतुर्ब्राह्मणाय वै॥
en: Having thus imprecated the curse upon the king the Rșis became silent. The cow was old and weak so they both, with mutual consent, conferred that upon another Brāhmaṇa.

sn: एवं स राजा तं शापमुपभुङ्क्ते सुदारुणम्। कार्यार्थिनां विमर्दो हि राज्ञां दोषाय कल्पते॥ तच्छीघ्रं दर्शनं मह्यमभिवर्तन्तु कार्यिणः। सुकृतस्य हि कार्यस्य फलं नावैति पार्थिवः। तस्माद्गच्छ प्रतीक्षस्व सौमित्रे कार्यवाञ्जनः॥
en: O Lakşmaņa, the king Nțga is still suffering from that dreadful curse. It is the king's folly that is manifest from the mutual disagreement of the workers. Do you bring them all speedily to me who have come for business. For, sooth shall the kings profit by the just administration. Do you therefore go in person, O Lakşmaņa and see who has come for business.

sn: रामस्य भाषितं श्रुत्वा लक्ष्मणः परमार्थवित्। उवाच प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यं राघवं दीप्ततेजसम्॥
en: Hearing the words of the highly effulgent Rama, Laksmana, conversant with discriminative knowledge, replied with folded hands, saying.

sn: अल्पापराधे काकुत्स्थ द्विजाभ्यां शाप ईदृशः। महानृगस्य राजर्षेर्यमदण्ड इवापरः॥
en: "O Kakutstha, it is for a very simple folly that the two Brāhmaṇas imprecated that curse upon the king Nrga, dreadful as the rod of Yama.

sn: श्रुत्वा तु पापसंयुक्तमात्मानं पुरुषर्षभ। किमुवाच नृगो राजा द्विजौ क्रोधसमन्वितौ॥
en: May I ask you, O foremost of men, what did that king say to the Brāhmaṇas when he saw thus imprecated?

sn: लक्ष्मणेनैवमुक्तस्तु राघवः पुनरब्रवीत्। शृणु सौम्य यता पूर्व स राजा शापविक्षतः॥
en: Where to Rāma replied saying:-O gentle one, hear, what the king Nrga said when imprecated.

sn: अथाध्वनि गतौ विप्रौ विज्ञाय स नृपस्तदा। आहूय मन्त्रिणः सर्वान्नैगमान्सपुरोधसः॥ तानुवाच नृगो राजा सर्वाश्च प्रकृतीस्तथा। दुःखेन सुसमाविष्टः श्रूयतां मे समाहिताः॥
en: Hearing of the departure of the Brāhmaṇas he sent for his priest, minister, the citizens and subjects and filled with sorrow said: "Do you all hear attentively my words.

sn: नारदः पर्वतश्चैव मम दत्त्वा महद्भयम्। गतौ त्रिभुवनं भद्रौ वायुभूतावनिन्दितौ ॥
en: Having imprecated a dreadful curse upon me the jolly saint Nārada and the ascetic Parvata have speedily, like the wind, repaired to the region of Brahmă.

sn: कुमारोऽयं वसुर्नाम स चेहाद्याभिषिच्यताम्। श्वभ्रं च यत्सुखस्पर्श क्रियतां शिल्पिभिर्मम।।।।।
en: Do you therefore even today, place the prince Vasu on the throne, and let the architects prepare ap leasant den for me.

sn: यत्राहं संक्षयिष्यामि शापं ब्राह्मणनिःसृतम्। वर्षघ्नमेकं श्वभ्रं तु हिमघ्नमपरं तथा॥ ग्रीष्मघ्नं तु सुखस्पर्शमेकं कुर्वन्तु शिल्पिनः।
en: Living therein I shall waste the curse of the Brāhmaṇas. Let the architects dog one den to protect me against the rains, one against the affliction of the winter and one against the distresses of summer.

sn: फलवन्तश्च ये वृक्षाः पुष्पवत्यश्च या लताः॥ विरोप्यन्तां बहुविधाश्छायावन्तश्च गुल्मिनः। क्रियतां रमणीयं च श्वभ्राणां सर्वतोदिशम्॥ सुखमत्र वसिष्यामि यावत्कालस्य पर्ययः। पुष्पाणि च सुगन्धीनि क्रियन्तां तेषु नित्यशः॥ ग्रीष्मघ्नं तु सुखस्पर्शमेकं कुर्वन्तु शिल्पिनः।
en: Let them enhance the picturesqueness of those dens by planting many trees having profuse branches and fruits and flowers. As long as time shall not change so long I shall spend my days happily in the den. For a half league on all sides around me let flower trees be planted.

sn: एवं कृत्वा विधानं स संनिवेश्य वसुं तदा॥ धर्मनित्यः प्रजाः पुत्र क्षत्रधर्मेण पालय।
en: Having made those arrangements and placed Vasu on the throne the king Nļga said:-“Do not leave the path of morality, O my son, and do you duly govern the subjects according to the custom of the Ksatriyas.

sn: प्रत्यक्षं ते यथा शापो द्विजाभ्यां मयि पातितः।।१४ नरश्रेष्ठ सरोषाभ्यामपराधेऽपि तादृशे।
en: You have seen, with your own eyes, the curse that the Brāhmaṇas have given me being enraged for a very trifling folly of mine.

sn: मा कृथास्त्वनुसंतापं मत्कृते हि नरर्षभ॥ कृतान्तः कुशलः पुत्र येनास्मि व्यसनीकृतः।
en: Do you not repent for me. My son, time is the lord of happiness and sorrow; it is by the influence of time that I have fallen into such a disaster.

sn: प्राप्तव्यान्येव प्राप्नोति गन्तव्यान्येव गच्छति॥ लब्धव्यान्येव लभते दुःखानि च सुखानि च। पूर्वे जात्यन्तरे वत्स मा विषादं कुरुष्व ह॥
en: Creatures must meet with what is kept in store by destiny; they must go where they are bound for and they must acquire what is set apart for them. Pristine actions are the root of all these; so, be not sorry, O my son.

sn: एवमुक्त्वा नृपस्तत्र सुतं राजा महायशाः। श्वभ्रं जगाम सुकृतं वासाय पुरुषर्षभः॥
en: O foremost of men, having given this advice to his son, the highly illustrious king Nțga proceeded to live in the sweet fragrant den.

sn: एवं प्रविश्यैव नृपस्तदानीं श्वभ्रं महद्रत्नविभूषितं तत्। संपादयामास तदा महात्मा शाप द्विजाभ्यां हि रुषा विमुक्तम्॥
en: Having entered the den filled with many jewels the high-souled king began to spend his days in the satisfaction of the curse imprecated by the two Brāhmaṇas.

sn: एष ते नृगशापस्य विस्तरोऽभिहितो मया। यद्यस्ति श्रवणे श्रद्धा शृणुष्वेहापरां कथाम्॥
en: I Have thus given to you an account of the curse imprecated on Nțga. Listen, if do you wish to hear of any other theme.

sn: एवमुक्तस्तु रामेण सौमित्रिः पुनरब्रवीत्। तृप्तिराश्चर्यभूतानां कथानां नास्ति मे नृप॥
en: Råma having said this Lakşmaņa replied: “I am not satiated with the account of those wonderful stories, oking."

sn: लक्ष्मणेनैवमुक्तस्तु राम इक्ष्वाकुनन्दनः। कथां परमधर्मिष्ठां व्याहर्तुमुपचक्रमे॥
en: Hearing the reply of Laksmana, Rama, the descendant of Ikşvāku, began again with themes instinct with morality.

sn: आसीद्राजा निमिर्नाम इक्ष्वाकूणां महात्मनाम्। पुत्रो द्वादशमो वीर्ये धर्मे च परिनिष्ठितः॥
en: There lived a highly pious and powerful king by the name of Nimi. He was twelfth of Ikş vāku's sons.

sn: स राजा वीर्यसंपन्नः पुरं देवपुरोपमम्। निवेशयामास तदा अभ्याशे गौतमस्य तु॥
en: That powerful king made a picturesque city like that of the celestials near the hermitage of Gautama.

sn: पुरस्य सुकृतं नाम वैजयन्तमिति श्रुतम्। निवेशं यत्र राजर्षिनिमिश्चक्रे महायशाः॥
en: The name of that beautiful city was Vaijayanta and the highly illustrious royal saint used to live there.

sn: तस्य बुद्धिः समुत्पन्ना निवेश्य सुमहापुरम्। यजेयं दीर्घसत्रेण पितुः प्रह्लादयन्मनः॥
en: Having thus reared a highly picturesque city he thought of worshipping the deity by celebrating a sacrifice for the satisfaction of his sire.

sn: ततः पितरमामन्त्र्य इक्ष्वाकुं हि मनोः सुतम्। वसिष्ठ वरयामास पूर्वं ब्रह्मर्षिसत्तमम्॥ अनन्तरं स राजर्षिनिमिरिक्ष्वाकुनन्दनः। अत्रिमङ्गिरसं चैव भृगुं चैव तपोनिधिम्॥
en: Having thus resolved and invited his sire Ikşvāku the son of Manu, he first welcomed the celestial saint. Nimi, the descendant of Ikşvāku, then welcomed the saints Atri, Angiras and Bhrgu having asceticism for their wealth.

sn: तमुवाच वसिष्ठस्तु निर्मि राजर्षिसत्तमम्। वृतोऽहं पूर्वमिन्द्रेण अन्तरं प्रतिपालय॥
en: Thereupon Vasiştha said to Nimi, the foremost of royal_saints-"I have already been engaged by Indra. Do you therefore wait as long as his sacrifice is not finished there."

sn: अनन्तरं महाविप्रो गौतमः प्रत्यपूरयत्। वसिष्ठोऽपि महातेजा इन्द्रयज्ञमथाकरोत्॥
en: After the departure of Vasiştha the great Gautama engaged in the satisfaction of Vasist ha's duties. And the high-souled Vasistha too engaged in Indra's sacrifice.

sn: निमिस्तु राजा विप्रांस्तान्समानीय नराधिपः। अयजद्धिमवत्पार्श्वे स्वपुरस्य समीपतः॥
en: On the other hand having united all the Brāhmaṇas the great king began to celebrate the sacrifice extending over five thousand years near his city by the side of the Himālaya.

sn: पञ्चवर्षसहस्राणि राजा दीक्षामथाकरोत्। इन्द्रयज्ञावसाने तु वसिष्ठो भगवानृषिः॥
en: There upon having finished the sacrifice of Indra there come to the King, the blameless and the illustrious Rși Vasiştha.

sn: सकाशमागतो राज्ञो हौत्रं कर्तुमनिन्दितः। तदन्तरमथापश्यद्गौतमेनाभिपूरितम्॥ कोपेन महताविष्टो वसिष्ठो ब्रह्मणः सुतः। स राज्ञो दर्शनाकाङ्क्षी मुहूर्त समुपाविशत्। तस्मिनहनि राजर्षिन्द्रियापहृतो भृशम्॥
en: Finding Gautama engaged in his room he was exceedingly enraged. Thereupon he waited there for some time to see the King. On that day the royal saint Nimi was deeply asleep.

sn: ततो मन्युर्वसिष्ठस्य प्रादुरासीन्महात्मनः। अदर्शनेन राजाहर्तुमुपचक्रमे।॥
en: And not beholding the King the high-souled Vasiştha was greatly angry and said.

sn: यस्मात्त्वमन्यं वृतवान्मामवज्ञाय पार्थिव। चेतनेन विनाभूतो देहस्ते पार्थिवैष्यति॥
en: Since you have, O king, engaged another neglecting me, your body shall remain senseless.

sn: ततः प्रबुद्धो राजा तु श्रुत्वा सापमुदाहृतम्। ब्रह्मयोनिमथोवाच स राजा क्रोधमूर्च्छितः॥
en: Thereupon hearing the curse of Vasiştha, the king got up. There beside himself with ire he said.

sn: अजानतः शयानस्य क्रोधेन कलुषीकृतः। उक्तवान्मम शापाग्निं यमदण्डमिवापरम्॥
en: I was unconscious in sleep-— still soiled with anger you have hurled the fiery curse against me like the second rod of Yama.

sn: तस्मात्तवापि ब्रह्मर्षे चेतनेन विनाकृतः। देहः स सुचिरप्रख्यो भविष्यति न संशयः॥
en: Therefore, O ascetic, your person shall remain senseless for a long time.

sn: इति रोषवशावुभौ तदानीमन्योन्यं शपितौ नृपद्विजेन्द्रौ। सहसैव बभूवतुर्विदेही तत्तुल्याधिगतप्रभाववन्तौ ॥
en: That king and the ascetic having thus imprecated one another under the influence of anger, they immediately were deprived of their bodies.

sn: रामस्य भाषितं श्रुत्वा लक्ष्मणः परवीरहा। उवाच प्राञ्जलिर्भूत्वा राघवं दीप्ततेजसम्॥
en: Hearing the words of the effulgent Rāma, Lakşmaņa, the slayer of enemies, said with folded hands.

sn: निक्षिप्य देहौ काकुत्स्थ कथं तौ द्विजपार्थिवौ। पुनर्देहेन संयोग जग्मतुर्देवसंमतौ॥
en: Having thus cast off their bodies how did that Brāhmaṇa worshipped of the celestial and the king regain them?

sn: लक्ष्मणेनैवमुक्तस्तु राम इक्ष्वाकुन्दनः। प्रत्युवाच महातेजा लक्ष्मणं पुरुषर्षभः॥
en: Having been thus accosted by Lakşmaņa, Rāma, the descendant of Ikşvākus and the foremost of men, replied.

sn: तौ परस्परशापेन देहमुत्सृज्य धार्मिकौ। अभूतां नृपविप्रर्षी वायुभूतौ तपोधनौ॥
en: Having renounced their persons both Nimi and the pious Vasiştha, having asceticism for their wealth, were metamorphosed into air.

sn: अशरीरः शरीरस्य कृतेऽन्यस्य महामुनिः। वसिष्द्वस्तु महातेजा जगाम पितुरन्तिकम्॥
en: Thereupon being thus deprived of his body like the highly effulgent and great ascetic Vasiştha went to the Patriarch Brahmā with the object of acquiring from his another.

sn: सोऽभिवाद्य ततः पादौ देवदेवस्य धर्मवित्। पितामहमथोवाच वायुभूत इदं वचः॥
en: Being merged in the air, he, conversant with religion, bowed to his father and said.

sn: भगवन्निमिशापेन विदेहत्वमुपागमम्। देवदेव महादेव वायुभूतोऽहमण्डज॥
en: O illustrious god of gods! O you lotus-sprung! by the imprecation of Nimi I have been now deprived of my body and been converted into air.

sn: सर्वेषां देहहीनानां महद्दुःखं भविष्यति। लुप्यन्ते सर्वकार्याणि हीनदेहस्य वै प्रभो॥
en: O lord, the state of being bodiless is highly painful to all. The bodiless cannot perform any work; do you, therefore, by the favour, grant me another body.

sn: देहस्यान्यस्य सद्भावे प्रसादं कर्तुमर्हसि । तमुवाच ततो ब्रह्मा स्वयंभूरमितप्रभः॥ मित्रावरुणज तेज आविश त्वं महायशः। अयोनिजस्त्वं भविता तत्रापि द्विजसत्तम्। धर्मेण महता युक्तः पुनरेष्यसि मे वशम्॥
en: Whereto the self-sprung Brahma, of unmitigated prowess, replied. O great one, do you enter into the vital energy of Mitra and Varuņa; and even then, O foremost of twiceborn ones, you shall not be born of a woman and being greatly pious shall attain to the rank of a patriarch.

sn: एवमुक्तस्तु देवेन अभिवाद्य प्रदक्षिणम्। कृत्वा पितामहं तूर्णं प्रययौ वरुणालयम्॥
en: The Patriarch Brahma having said this, Vasishtha, saluting and circumbulating him, repaired to the region of Varuņa.

sn: तमेव कालं मित्रोऽपि वरुणत्वमकारयत्। क्षीरोदेन सहोपेतः पूज्यमानः सुरेश्वरैः॥
en: At that time Mitra in conjunction with Varuņa was reigning in Varuna's kingdom being worshipped by all celestials.

sn: एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु उर्वशी परमाप्सराः। यदृच्छया तमुद्देशमागता सखिभित्ता॥
en: Meanwhile encircled by her mates the leading Apsarā Urvasi by name arrived there at her pleasure.

sn: तां दृष्ट्वा रूपसंपन्नां क्रीडन्तीं वरुणालये। तदाविशत्परो हर्षो वरुणं चोर्वशीकृते॥
en: Beholding the frolicsome and beautiful Urvasi, Varuna attained to an excess of delight.

sn: स तां पद्मपलाशाक्षी पूर्णचन्द्रनिभाननाम्। वरुणो वरयामास मैथुनायाप्सरोवराम्॥
en: Thereupon he expressed his intention of living with that queen of Apsarās, having a moon-like countenance and lotus-eyes.

sn: प्रत्युवाच ततः सा तु वरुणं प्राञ्जलिः स्थिता। मित्रेणाहं वृता साक्षात्पूर्वमेव सुरेश्वर॥
en: Thereat Urvasi, with folded hands, said-0 lord of celestials, Mitra himself has already invited me for the same.

sn: वरुणस्त्वब्रवीद्वाक्यं कंदर्पशरपीडितः। इदं तेजः समुत्स्रक्ष्ये कुम्भेऽस्मिन्देवनिर्मिते॥ एवमुत्सृज्य सुश्रोणि त्वय्यहं वरवर्णिनि। कृतकामो भविष्यामि यदि नेच्छसि संगमम्।।१८
en: Being stricken by the bow of Kupid, Varuņa said to Urvasī I shall discharge my vital energy into this pot if you do not wish to live with me.

sn: तस्य तल्लोकनाथस्य वरुणस्य सुभाषितम्। उर्वशी परमप्रीता श्रुत्वा वाक्यमुवाच ह॥
en: Hearing those sweet words of the Patriarch Varuna, Urvasi was highly pleased and said.

sn: काममेतद्भवत्वेवं हृदयं मे त्वयि स्थितम्। भावश्चाप्यधिकं तुभ्यं देहो मित्रस्य तु प्रभो॥
en: Do what you have said. Now my body is under the possession of Mitra but my mind is attached to your and you are equally attached to me.

sn: उर्वश्या एवमुक्तस्तु रेतस्तन्महदद्भुतम्। ज्वलदग्निसमप्रख्यं तस्मिन्कुम्भे न्यवासृजत्।।२१
en: Urvaśī having said this, Varuņa discharged his vital energy into the pot.

sn: उर्वशी त्वगमत्तत्र मित्रो वै यत्र देवता। तां तु मित्रः सुसंक्रुद्धउर्वशीमिदमब्रवीत्॥
en: Thereupon Urvasi approached Mitra. And thereat highly enraged he said to her.

sn: मयाभिमन्त्रिता पूर्वं कस्मात्त्वमवसर्जिता। पतिमन्यं वृतवती किमर्थ दुष्टचारिणि ॥ अनेन दुष्कृतेन त्वं मत्क्रोधकलुषीकृता। मनुष्यलोकमास्थाय कंचित्कालं निवत्स्यसि।।२४
en: I invited you first; O you of vicious actions, why have, you, renouncing me, secured another. for this vile action, you shall, by my curse live in the land of mortals for some time.

sn: बुधस्य पुत्रो राजर्षिः काशिराजः पुरूरवाः। तमभ्यागच्छ दुर्बुद्धे स ते भर्ता भविष्यति ॥
en: The royal saint Pururava, the king of kasi, is the son of Budha. Do you go to him, O you of a vicious intellect; he shall be your husband.

sn: ततः सा शापदोषेण पुरूरवसमभ्यगात्। प्रतिष्ठाने पुरूरवं बुधस्यात्मजमौरसम्॥
en: Thereupon being thus placed under the influence of curse Urvasi went to Pururavă.

sn: तस्य जज्ञे ततः श्रीमानायुः पुत्रो महाबलः। नहुषो यस्य पुत्रस्तु बभूवेन्द्रसमद्युतिः॥
en: The king Paruravă was the begotten son of Budha. He reigned in the foremost of cities Pratişțaro. He begot on Urvaší a highly powerful and beautiful son by the name of Āyu. Nahuşa, powerful as Indra, was the son of

sn: वज्रमुत्सृज्य वृत्राय श्रान्तेऽथ त्रिदिवेश्वरे। शतं वर्षसहस्राणि येनेन्द्रत्वं प्रशासितम्॥
en: When Indra, the king of the celestials, was assailed with thunderbolt by the Asura Větra, Nahuşa governed his kingdom for a hundred thousand years.

sn: सा तेन शापेन जगाम भूमि तदोर्वशी चारुदती सुनेत्रा। बहूनि वर्षाण्यवसच्च सुभ्रूः शापक्षयादिन्द्रसदो ययौ च ॥
en: In this wise Urvasi, having beautiful teeth, eyes and brow, remained on earth for many years and then returned to the region of Indra after the period of curse had been over.

sn: तां श्रुत्वा दिव्यसंकाशां कथामद्भुतदर्शनाम्। लक्ष्मणः परमप्रीतो राघवं वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
en: Hearing this wonderful and heavenly theme Lakşmaņa was highly gratified and said to Rāma.

sn: निक्षिप्तदेहौ काकुत्स्थ कथं तौ द्विजपार्थिवौ। पुनर्देहेन संयोग जग्मतुर्देवसंमतौ॥
en: O Kakuthstha, how did that twice-born one worshipped by the celestials and the king regain their bodies, after being bodiless.

sn: तस्य तद्भाषितं श्रुत्वा रामः सत्यपराक्रमः। तां कथां कथयामास वसिष्ठस्य महात्मनः॥
en: Hearing the words of Laksmana, Rama, having truth for his prowess, began to relate the story of Vasiştha.

sn: यः स कुम्भो रघुश्रेष्ठ तेजःपूर्णो महात्मनोः। तस्मिंस्तेजोमयौ विप्रौ संभूतावृषिसत्तमौ॥
en: O foremost of Raghus, there sprang up two foremost Brahmin saints from the vital energy discharged by the high-souled Mitra and Varuņa into the pot.

sn: पूर्व समभवत्तत्र अगस्त्यो भगवानृषिः। नाहं सुतस्तवेत्युक्त्वा मित्रं तस्मादपाक्रमत्॥
en: At first therefrom rose up the illustrious Rși Agastya and saying 'I am not your son' Varuņa was thrown into the pot Mitra.

sn: तद्धि तेजस्तु मित्रस्य उर्वश्याः पूर्वमाहितम्। तस्मिन्समभवत्कुम्भे तत्तेजो यत्र वारुणम्॥
en: Before the vital energy of Varuna was thrown into the pot Mitra discharged his own on Urvasi's account which was the source of Agastya's birth. (Into the pot in which Mitra's energy was discharged Varuņa also put his own and both the energies were mixed up).

sn: कस्यचित्त्वथ कालस्य मित्रावरुणसंभवः। वसिष्ठस्तेजसा युक्तो जज्ञे इक्ष्वाकुदैवतम्॥
en: There upon after some time from the energies of both Mitra and Varuņa sprang up the effulgent Vasistha-the priest of Iksvākus.

sn: तमिक्ष्वाकुर्महातेजा जातमात्रमनिन्दितम्। ववे पुरोधसं सौम्य वंशस्यास्य हिताय नः।।।।।
en: O gentle one, the highly effulgent Iksavāku appointed that blameless Rși as the priest of our family as soon as he was born.

sn: एवं त्वपूर्वदेहस्य वसिष्ठस्य महात्मनः। कथितो निर्गमः सौम्य निमेः शृणु यथाभवत्॥
en: I have thus described to you the story of Vasistha's birth possessing a wonderful body. Hear now what befell the king Nimi.

sn: दृष्ट्वा विदेहं राजानमृषयः सर्व एव ते। तं च ते याजयामसुर्यज्ञदीक्षां मनीषिणः॥
en: And beholding the king Nimi bodiless the intelligent Rșis initiated him into the rites of sacrifice.

sn: तं च देहं नरेन्द्रस्य रक्षन्ति स्म द्विजोत्तमाः। गन्धैर्माल्यैश्च वस्त्रैश्च पौरभृत्यसमन्विताः॥
en: And those leading twice-born ones, with assembled citizens and servants, began to protect that body with unguents, garlands and clothes.

sn: ततो यज्ञे समाप्ते तु भृगुस्तत्रेदमब्रवीत्। आनयिष्यामि ते चेतस्तुष्टोऽस्मि तव पार्थिव ॥
en: There upon at the end of the sacrifice Bhrgu said O king, I am propitiated with you; I shall restore you to senses.

sn: सुप्रीताश्च सुराः सर्वे निमेश्चेतस्तदाब्रुवन्। वरं वरय राजर्षे क्व ते चेतो निरूप्यताम्॥
en: There upon the celestials, highly pleased, addressed the consciousness of Nimi saying O royal saint, do you accept boons; where shall we place your consciousness?

sn: एवमुक्तः सुरैः सर्वैर्निमेश्चेतस्तदाब्रवीत्। नेत्रेषु सर्वभूतानां वसेयं सुरसत्तमाः॥
en: There upon being addressed by the celestials the consciousness said I may live in the eyes of the celestials.

sn: बाढमित्येव विबुधा निमेश्चेतस्तदाब्रुवन्। नेत्रेषु सर्वभूतानां वायुभूतश्चरिष्यसि॥
en: They agreed to it and said ( lord of earth, for you, their eyes shall be influenced within a moment.

sn: त्वत्कृते च निमिष्यन्ति चढूंषि पृथिवीपते। वायुभूतेन चरता विश्रामार्थं मुहुर्मुहुः॥
en: The exhaustion, that their their eyes shall experience on account of your moving about as the air, shall be removed within this moment.

sn: एवमुक्त्वा तु विबुधाः सर्वे जग्मुर्यथागतम्। ऋषयोऽपि महात्मानो निमेहं समाहरन्॥ अरणिं तत्र निक्षिप्य मथनं चक्रुरोजसा। मन्त्रहोमैर्महात्मानः पुत्रहेतोनिमेस्तदा ॥
en: Having said this the celestials repaired to their respective quarters and the high-souled Rșis having conveyed Nimi's body to the sacrificial ground and dedicated it as an edy began to churn it with great energy accompanied by incantations.

sn: अरण्यां मध्यमानायं प्रादुर्भूतो महातपाः। मथनान्मिथिरित्याहुर्जननाज्जनकोऽभवत्॥ यस्माद्विदेहात्संभूतो वैदेहस्तु ततः स्मृतः। एवं विदेहराजश्च जनकः पूर्वकोऽभवत्। मिथिर्नाम महातेजास्तेनायं मैथिलोऽभवत्॥
en: They being thus engaged in churning the edy for the purpose of having a son of Nimi there sprang up a son of devout austerities. He was called Mithi for he originated from Manthana; he was called Janaka for his having sprung up from Janana and Vaideha from having been born from Videha. In this wise Janaka, the first king of Videhas, was born. His other name was Mithi and his family were celebrated as Maithilas.

sn: इति सर्वमशेषतो मया कथितं संभवकारणं तु सौम्य नृपपुङ्गव शाफ्जं द्विजस्य द्विजशापाच्च यदद्भुतं नृपस्य।
en: O gentle one, I have thus related to you the wondrous births, in consequence of the curse, of the great ascetic Vasistha and the royal saint Nimi.

sn: एवं ब्रुवति रामे तु लक्ष्मणः परवीरहा। प्रत्युवाच महात्मानं ज्वलन्तमिव तेजसा ॥
en: Rama having said this, Laksmana, the slayer of enemies, burning in his native effulgence, said.

sn: महदद्भुतमाश्चर्य विदेहस्य पुरातनम्। निर्वृत्तं राजशार्दूल वसिष्ठस्य मुनेश्च ह॥
en: O foremost of kings, this ancient account of the ascetic Vasiştha and the king Nimi is highly surprising and wonderful.

sn: निमिस्तु क्षत्रियः शूरो विशेषेण च दीक्षितः। न क्षमं कृतवानराजा वसिष्ठस्य महात्मनः॥
en: But Nimi is a Ksatriya king and a hero besides although initiated he did not forgive the highsouled Vasiştha.

sn: एवमुक्तस्तु तेनायं रामः क्षत्रियपुङ्गवः। उवाच लक्ष्मणं वाक्यं सर्वशास्त्रविशारदम्॥
en: Being thus accosted Rāma, the Kșatriya-chief, said to the effulgent Lakşmaņa conversant with all Sastras.

sn: रामो रमयतां श्रेष्ठो भ्रातरं दीप्ततेजसम्। न सर्वत्र क्षमा वीर पुरुषेषु प्रदृश्यते॥ सौमित्रे दुःसरो रोषो यथा क्षान्तो ययातिना। सत्त्वानुगं पुरस्कृत्य तन्निबोध समाहितः॥
en: O hero, forgiveness is not to be seen in all men. O Saumitri, do you hear attentively, the unbearable anger which was you hear attentively, the unbearable anger which was forgiven by the king Yayāti resorting to the quality of goodness.

sn: नहुषस्य सुतो राजा ययातिः पौरवर्धनः। तस्य भार्याद्वयं सौम्य रूपेणाप्रतिमं भुवि॥ एका तु तस्य राजर्षेरनाहुषस्य पुरस्कृता। शर्मिष्ठा नाम दैतेयी दुहिता वृषपर्वणः॥
en: Yayāti, the enhancer of the prosperity of cities, was the son of Nahusa. He had two beautiful wives, one of whom was Sarmistha, grand daughter of Aditi, the daughter of Vrsaparvan.

sn: अन्या तूशनसः पत्नी ययातेः पुरुषर्षभ। न तु सा दयिता राज्ञो देवयानी सुमध्यमा।९।। तयोः पुत्रौ तु संभूतौ रूपवन्तौ समाहितौ। शर्मिष्ठाजनयत्पूरुं देवयानी यदुं तदा॥
en: She was the more beloved of the two; his other spouse was Devayāni, grand daughter of Ušanas. She was not liked by her husband. Both of them gave birth to a son each and both the sons were beautiful and attentive. Puru was born of Śarmisthā and Yadu of Devayāni.

sn: पूरुस्तु दयितो राज्ञो गुणैर्मातृकृतेन च। ततो दुःखसमाविष्टो यदुर्मातरमब्रवीत्॥
en: Puru was the favourite son of the king, both on account of his mother and of his personal graces, Thereat Yadu, greatly sorry, said to his mother.

sn: भार्गवस्य कुले जाता देवस्याक्लिष्टकर्मणः। सहसे हृद्गतं दुःखमवमानं च दुःसहम्॥ आवां च सहितौ देवि प्रविशाव हुताशनम्। राजा तु रमतां सार्धं दैत्यपुत्र्या बहुक्षपाः॥
en: Born in the race of the illustrious Bhārgava of unwearied actions, you are going tough mental afflictions and unbearable insults; therefore, O mother, let us both enter into fire. Let the king spend many nights with Śarmişthā, the daughter of a demon.

sn: यदि वा सहनीयं ते मामनुज्ञातुमर्हसि। क्षम त्वं न क्षमिष्येऽहं मरिष्यामि न संशयः॥
en: You may withstand the insults but I shall never broke them. Permit me, I shall, in sooth, renounce my life.

sn: पुत्रस्य भाषितं श्रुत्वा परमार्तस्य रोदतः। देवयानी तु संक्रुद्धा सस्मार पितरं तदा॥
en: The son having, weepingly and distressingly, said this, Devayāni was greatly engaged and thought of her father.

sn: इङ्गितं तदभिज्ञाय दुहितुर्भार्गवस्तदा। आगतस्त्वरितं तत्र देवयानी स्म यत्र सा॥ दृष्ट्वा चाप्रकृतिस्थां तामप्रहृष्टामचेतनाम्। पिता दुहितरं वाक्यं किमेतदिति चाब्रवीत्॥
en: As soon as he was thought of by his daughter Bhargava speedily came there and beholding her senseless and deprived from joy said "Daughter, what is the matter?

sn: पृच्छन्तमसकृत्तं वै भार्गवं दीप्तचेतसम्। देवयानी तु संक्रुद्धा पितरं वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥ अहमग्नि विषं तीक्ष्णमपो वा मुनिसत्तम। 'भक्षयिष्ये प्रवेक्ष्ये वा न तु शक्ष्यामि जीवितुम्॥
en: The effulgent father having addressed his daughter repeatedly in this wise, Devayāni, enraged, replied, O foremost of ascetics, I shall either enter into fire water or drink poison, by no means I shall preserve this life of mine.

sn: न मां त्वमवजानीषे दुःखितामवमानिताम्। वृक्षस्यावज्ञया ब्रह्मश्छिद्यन्ते वृक्षजीविनः॥ अवज्ञया च राजर्षिः परिभूय च भार्गव। मय्यवज्ञां प्रयुङ्क्ते हि न च मां बहु मन्यते ॥
en: You do not know of the miseries and insults I have been subject to. O Brāhmaṇa, when a tree is neglected, those who live thereon are also distressed. The king having disregarded me, forsooth you have also been neglected.

sn: तस्यास्तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा कोपेनाभिपरिवृतः। व्याहर्तुमुपचक्राम भार्गवो नहुषात्मजम्॥
en: Hearing the words of his daughter, Bhārgava, being enraged said to the king Yayāti.

sn: यस्मान्मामवजानीषे नाहुष त्वं दुरात्मवान्। वयसा जरया जीर्णः शैथिल्यमुपयास्यसि॥
en: You are vicious-minded, O son of Nahusa; you have dishonoured me and therefore in your youth shall be subject to decrepitude and infirmities of age.

sn: एवमुक्त्वा दुहितरं समाश्वास्य स भार्गवः। पुनर्जगाम ब्रह्मर्षिर्भवनं स्वं महायशाः॥
en: Having thus imprecated the curse and consoled his sorrowful daughter the highly illustrious Rși Bhārgava repaired to his own habitation.

sn: स एवमुक्त्वा द्विजपुङ्गवावयः सुतां समाश्वास्य च देवयानीम्। पुनर्ययौ सूर्यसमानतेजा दत्त्वा च शापं नहुषात्मजाय॥
en: Having thus conferred solace to his daughter that leading Brahmana, effulgent as the son, returned therefrom.

sn: श्रुत्वा तूशनसं क्रुद्धं तदार्तो नहुषात्मजः। जरां परमिकां प्राप्य यदुं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Yayāti the son of Nahușa, was greatly distressed on hearing of the ire of the preceptor Sukra. Thereupon meeting with the infirmities of age by the imprecation of the saint he said to his son Yadu.

sn: यदो त्वमसि धर्मज्ञो मदर्थं प्रतिगृह्यताम्। जरां परमिकां पुत्र भोगै रंस्ये महायशः॥ न तावत्कृतकृत्योऽस्मि विषयेषु नरर्षभ। अनुभूय तदा कामं ततः प्राप्स्याम्यहं जराम्॥
en: O Yadu you are cognisant of religion; do you therefore take this decrepitude for me; I shall satisfy myself with various enjoyments. O foremost of men, I have not yet been satisfied with worldly enjoyments, I shall therefore again take upon myself this decrepitude after having enjoyed all objects of sense.

sn: यदुस्तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा प्रत्युवाच नरर्षभम्। पुत्रस्ते दयितः पूरुः प्रतिगृह्णातु वै जराम्॥
en: Hearing those words of Yayāti, the foremost of men, Yadu replied: "Let your most favourite son Puru take upon himself this decrepitude.

sn: बहिष्कृतोऽहमर्थेषु संनिकर्षाच्च पार्थिव । प्रतिगृह्णातु वै राजन्यैः सहाश्नासि भोजनम्॥
en: O king, you have deprived me from all things, what more, you do not allow me to come near you. Let that Puru take this, with whom you do eat and live.

sn: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा राजा पूरुमथाब्रवीत्। इयं जरा महाबाहो मदर्थं प्रतिगृह्यताम्॥
en: Hearing the words of Yadu, Yayāti said to Puru: “O you having large arms, do you take the decrepitude for me."

sn: नाहुषेणैवमुक्तस्तु पूरुः प्राञ्जलिरब्रवीत्। धन्योऽस्म्यनुगृहीतोऽस्मि शासनेऽस्मि त्व स्थितः॥
en: Hearing the words of Yayāti, Puru, with folded hands, said: “I am always ready to satisfy your commands; and I have been favoured and honoured by this command of your."

sn: पूरोवर्चनमाज्ञाय नाहुषः परया मुदा। प्रहर्षमतुलं लेभे जरां संक्रामयच्च ताम्॥
en: Hearing those words of Puru Yayāti was highly pleased and attained to an excess of delight and then transferred his won decrepitude to him.

sn: ततः स राजा तरुणः प्राप्य यज्ञान्सहस्रशः। बहुवर्षसहस्राणि पालयामास मेदिनीम्॥
en: Thereupon regaining his youth the king reigned in earth for many thousand years celebrating thousands of sacrifices.

sn: अथ दीर्घस्य कालस्य राजा पूरुमथाब्रवीत्। आनयस्व जरां पुत्र न्यासं निर्यातयस्व मे॥
en: Thereupon after a long time Yayāti said to Puru O my son, do you bring the decrepitude I have kept as deposit with you, let it now assail me.

sn: न्यासभूता मया पुत्र त्वयि संक्रामिता जरा। तस्मात्प्रतिग्रहीष्यामि तां जरां मा व्यथां कृथाः।।११
en: I transferred it to you as a deposit. For this I shall take it back; be not sorry for this.

sn: प्रीतश्चास्मि महाबाहो शासनस्य प्रतिग्रहात्। त्वां चाहमभिषेक्ष्यामि प्रीतियुक्तो नराधिपम्॥
en: I have been greatly pleased that you have satisfied my behests. I shall, now pleased, install you on the royal throne.

sn: एवमुक्त्वा सुतं पूरुं ययातिर्नहुषात्मजः। देवयानीसुतं क्रुद्धो राजा वाक्यमुवाच ह ॥
en: Having thus addressed his son Puru, the king Yayāti angrily said to Yadu, the son of Devayāni.

sn: राक्षसस्त्वं मया जातः क्षत्ररूपो दुरासदः। प्रतिहसि ममाज्ञां त्वं प्रजार्थे विफलो भव॥
en: You, vicious Rākhasa, are born of me in the shape of a Kşatriya, or else why should you disobey my orders? For this you shall never be a king.

sn: पितरं गुरुभूतं मां यस्मात्त्वमवमन्यसे। राक्षसान्यातुधानांस्त्वं जनयिष्यसि दारुणान्॥
en: I am your father and preceptor and still you have disregarded me. You shall be the father of dreadful Räksasas.

sn: न तु सोमकुलोत्पन्ने वंशे स्थास्यति दुर्मतेः। वंशोऽपि भवतस्तुल्यो दुविनीतो भविष्यति॥
en: O vicious minded; your descendants shall be degraded from the lunar race and your children shall be equally vicious-minded like you.

sn: तमेवमुक्त्वा राजर्षिः पूरुं राज्यविवर्धनम्। अभिषेकेण संपूज्य आश्रमं प्रविवेश ह॥
en: Having thus imprecated Yadu, the royal saint Yayāti honoured Puru, Puru, the enhancer of prosperity of the kingdom, with installation and then retired to woods.

sn: ततः कालेन महता दिष्टान्तमुपजग्मिवान्। त्रिदिवं स गतो राजा ययातिनहुषात्मजः॥
en: Thereupon after a long time he breathed his last and went to the abode of the celestials.

sn: पूरुश्चकार तद्राज्यं धर्मेण महता वृतः। प्रतिष्ठाने पुरवरे काशिराज्ये महायशाः॥
en: The highly illustrious Puru reigned piously in the foremost of cities Pratisthan.

sn: यदुस्तु जनयामास यातुधानान्सहस्रशः। पुरे क्रौञ्चवने दुर्गे राजवंशबहिष्कृते॥
en: Yadu begot thousands and thousands of Räkşasas and being degraded from the royal family reigned in a city named Krauñcavana, hard to be got at.

sn: एष तूशनसा मुक्तः शापोत्सर्गो ययातिना। धारितः क्षत्रधर्मेण यं निमिश्चक्षमे न च ॥
en: In this wise, according to the custom of the Kșatriya the king Yayāti took upon himself the imprecation of the preceptor śukra, but he did not forgive him.

sn: एतत्ते सर्वमाख्यातं दर्शनं सर्वकारिणाम्। अनुवर्तामहे सौम्य दोषो न स्याद्यथा नृगे॥
en: I have thus related to you everything. O gentle one, we shall follow the examples of these illustrious men. And in that case we shall not be degraded like the king Nļga.

sn: इति कथयति रामे चन्द्रतुल्याननेन प्रविरलतरतारं व्योम जज्ञे तदानीम्। अरुणकिरणरक्ता दिग्बभौ चैव पूर्वा कुसुमरसविमुक्तं वस्त्रमागुण्ठितेव॥
en: While Rāma, having moon-like countenance, was speaking thus, the stars became fewer in the welkin, and east, stricken with the early rays of the sun, appeared like a damsel, clothed in a raiment coloured with the dye of flowers.

sn: ततः प्रभाते विमले कृत्वा पौर्वाह्निकी क्रियाम्। धर्मासनगतो राजा रामो राजीवलोचनः॥ राजधर्मानवेक्षन्वै ब्राह्मणैर्नंगमैः सह। पुरोधसा वसिष्ठेन ऋषिणा कश्यपेन च॥ मन्त्रिभिर्व्यवहारज्ञैस्तथान्यैर्धर्मपाठकैः। नीतिज्ञैरथ सभ्यैश्च राजभिः सा सभा वृता॥ सभा यथा महेन्द्रस्य यमस्य वरुणस्य च। शुशुभे राजसिंहस्य रामस्याक्लिष्टकर्मणः॥
en: Thereupon having performed the morning rites the lotus-eyed Rama, in the early morning, sat on his royal throne and in the company of Brāhmaṇas and citizens engaged in looking into state affairs. The assembly consisted of the priest Vasiştha, the saint Kashyapa, ministers well versed in politics, other religious preceptors, moralists, members and kings. The assembly of Rāma, of unwearied, actions appeared like that of Mahendra, Yama and Varuna.

sn: अथ रामोऽब्रवीत्तत्र लक्ष्मणं शुभलक्षणम्। निर्गच्छ त्वं महाबाहो सुमित्रानन्दवर्धन॥
en: Rāma said to Lakşmaņa, gifted with auspicious marks “O Saumitri having long arms, do you proceed to the city-gate to receive those who have come here for business."

sn: कार्यार्थिनश्च सौमित्रे व्याहतुं त्वमुपाक्रम। रामस्य भाषितं श्रुत्वा लक्ष्मणः शुभलक्षणः॥ द्वारदेशमुपागम्य कार्यिणश्चाह्वयस्त्वयम्। न कश्चिदब्रवीत्तत्र मम कार्यमिहाद्य वै॥
en: According to Rāma's command Laksmana, gifted with auspicious mark, arrived at the gate and called those who had come there for business. But none said that he had been brought there by any business.

sn: नाधयो व्याधयश्चैव रामे राज्यं प्रशासति। पक्क सस्या वसुमती सर्वोषधिसमन्विता॥
en: For there was neither decease nor poverty in the kingdorm. During Rama's regime, the earth was filled with corns and Asadhis.

sn: न बालो म्रियते तत्र न युवा न च मध्यमः। धर्मेण शासितं सर्वं न च बाधा विधीयते॥
en: Children, youngmen and middle-aged people did not meet with death. The earth was governed piously so there was no obstacle.

sn: दृश्यते न च कार्यार्थी रामे राज्यं प्रशासति। लक्ष्मणः प्राञ्जलिर्भूत्वा रामायैवं न्यवेदयत्॥
en: Thus during the administration of Rāma none was seen who wanted justice. Laksmana, with folded hands, said to Rāma, “None has come for business."

sn: अथ रामः प्रसन्नात्मा सौमित्रिमिदमब्रवीत्। भूय एव तु गच्छ त्वं कार्यिणः प्रविचारय॥
en: Thereat, Rāma, with a delighted heart, replied"Do you go, O Saumitri, and see if nay one has come for business.

sn: सम्यकप्रणीतया नीत्या नाधर्मो विद्यते व चित्। तस्माद्राजभयात्सर्वे रक्षन्तीह परस्परम्॥ बाणा इव मया मुक्ता इह रक्षन्ति मे प्रजाः। तथापि त्वं महाबाहो प्रजा रक्षस्व तत्परः॥
en: Royal policy if properly adopted, impiety can stand nowhere. It is for the fear of the king that people protect one another. And although laws, instituted by the are protecting the subjects like so many arrows, still, O you having long arms, do you be engaged in governing the subjects.”

sn: एवमुक्तस्तु सौमित्रिनिर्जगाम नृपालयात्। अपश्यदूरदेशे वै श्वानं तावदवस्थितम्॥ तमेवं वीक्षमाणो वै विक्रोशन्तं मुहुर्मुहुः। दृष्ट्वाथ लक्ष्मणस्तं वै स पप्रच्छाथ वीर्यवान्॥
en: Being thus addressed Lakşmaņa issued out of the house and saw that a dog was waiting at the gate. Casting its looks around it was again and again barking. Beholding it in that plight the valiant Lakşmaņa said.

sn: किं ते कार्यं महाभाग बूहि विस्रब्धमानसः। लक्ष्मणस्य वचः श्रुत्वा सारमेयोऽभ्यभाषत॥
en: "O generous sir, what business has brought you hither-do you relate it confidentially.” Hearing the words of Lakşmaņa the dog replied.

sn: सर्वभूतशरण्याय रामायाकिष्टकर्मणे। भयेष्वभयदात्रे च तस्मै वक्तुं समुत्सहे॥
en: "I wish to relate it to Räma of unwearied actions, who is the refuge of all creatures and who declares fearlessness to all.

sn: एतच्छुत्वा च वचनं सारमेयस्य लक्ष्मणः। राघवाय तदाख्यातुं प्रविवेशालयं शुभम्॥
en: Hearing the words of the dog Laksmana entered the beautiful palace to relate it to Rāma.

sn: निवेद्य रामस्य पुनर्निर्जगाम नृपालयात्। वक्तव्यं यदि ते किंचित्तत्त्वं ब्रूहि नृपाय वै॥
en: And having communicated it to Rāma he issued out and said to the dog:-"If you have anything true to speak you may come and communicate it to the king."

sn: लक्ष्मणस्य वचः श्रुत्वा सारमेयोऽभ्यभाषत। देवागारे नृपागारे द्विजवेश्मसु वै तथा॥ वह्निः शतक्रतुश्चैव सूर्यो वायुश्च तिष्ठति। नात्र योग्यास्तु सौमित्रे योनीनामधमा वयम्॥
en: Hearing the words Lakşmaņa the dog said, "We cannot enter into the house of divinities, kings and Brāhmaṇas nor can we go there where is fire, Indra, the sun or the wind, for we are the vilest born; so I cannot enter there.

sn: प्रवेष्टुं नात्र शक्ष्यामि धर्मो विग्रहवानृपः। सत्यवादी रणपटुः सर्वसत्त्वहिते रतः॥
en: For king is the personification of virtue and specially the king Råma is truthful, well versed in the science of fighting and ever engaged in the welfare of all beings.

sn: पाङ्गुण्यस्य पदं वेत्ति नीतिकर्ता स राघवः। सर्वज्ञः सर्वदर्शी च रामो रमयतां वरः॥
en: He is perfectly cognisant of where the six qualities are to be applied master of morality, know all, see all and the best of beautiful.

sn: स सोमः स च मृत्युश्च स यमो धनदस्तथा। वह्निः शतक्रतुश्चैव सूर्यो वै वरुणस्तथा॥
en: He is the moon, death, Yama, Kubera, the giver of riches, fire, Indra, the sun and Varuna.

sn: तस्य त्वं ब्रूहि सौमित्रे प्रजापालः स राघवः। अनाज्ञप्तस्तु सौमित्रे प्रवेष्टुं नेच्छयाम्यहम्॥
en: O Saumitri, do you go and communicate to the king protecting his subjects that without his permission I do not wish to go there."

sn: आनृशंस्यान्महाभाग प्रविवेश महाद्युतिः। नृपालयं प्रविश्याथ लक्ष्मणो वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
en: Thereupon the highly effulgent and noble-minded Lakşmaņa entered the palace and said to Rama:

sn: श्रूयतां मम विज्ञाप्यं कौसल्यानन्दवर्धन। यन्मयोक्तं महाबाहो तव शासनजं विभो॥
en: "O you having long arms, O you the enhancer of Kausalya's joy-I have communicated your orders—I shall relate shortly everything regarding that; do you hear.

sn: श्वा वै ते तिष्ठते द्वारि कार्यार्थी समुपागतः। लक्ष्मणस्यः वचः श्रुत्वा रामो वचनमब्रवीत्।। संप्रवेशय वै क्षिप्रं कार्यार्थी योऽत्र तिष्ठति॥
en: That dog, as a beggar, is waiting at the gate for your commands.” Whereto Rāma replied: “Bring him speedily here who is waiting at the gate for business."

sn: श्रुत्वा रामस्य वचनं लक्ष्मणस्त्वरितस्तदा। श्वानमाहूय मतिमानराधवाय न्यवेदयत्॥ दृष्ट्वा समागतं श्वानं रामो वचनमब्रवीत्। विवक्षितार्थं मे ब्रूहि सारमेय न ते भयम्॥
en: Hearing the words of Rāma the intelligent Laks maņa immediately sent for the dog and informed Rāma, who, on beholding it, said "Do you communicate your desire to me; be not afraid.”

sn: अथापश्यत तत्रस्थं रामं श्वा भिन्नमस्तकः। ततो दृष्ट्वा स राजानं सारमेयोऽब्रवीद्वचः॥ राजैव कर्ता भूतानां राजा चैव विनायकः। राजा सुप्तेषु जागर्ति राजा पालयति प्रजाः॥
en: Thereupon beholding the king Räma, the dog, having his head cut off, said. “The king is the preceptor of animals and their lord. The king is awake when the subjects are asleep and he protects them.

sn: नीत्या सुनीतया राजा धर्म रक्षति रक्षिता। यदा न पालयेद्राजा क्षिप्रं नश्यन्ति वै प्रजाः॥
en: By administering the laws properly the king protects piety. Without his shelter the subjects meet with destruction.

sn: राजा कर्ता च गोप्ता च सर्वस्य जगतः पिता। राजा कालो युगं चैव राजा सर्वमिदं जगत्॥
en: The king is the lord and father of the whole universe. He is time, he is Yuga and he is the creation, mobile and immobile.

sn: धारणाद्धर्ममित्याहुर्धर्मेण विधृताः प्रजाः। यस्माद्धारयते सर्वं त्रैलोक्यं सचराचरम्॥
en: He is called Dharma because he hold all. It is Dharma (virtue) that uphold all mankind. It is by Dharma that the three worlds are being preserved.

sn: धारणाद्विद्विषां चैत्र धर्मेणारझ्-यन्प्रजाः। यस्माद्धारणमित्युक्तं स धर्म इति निश्चयः॥ एष राजन्परो धर्मः फलवाओत्य राघव। नहि धर्माद्भवेत्किंचिहुष्प्रापमिति मे मतिः॥
en: It is Dharma or virtue that thwarts the enemies. It is virtue that governs the subjects duly. It is for this that virtue is called Dhārana or the holder. The virtue of preservation is the greatest and confers fruits in alter life. There is nothing like virtue hard to acquire in this world,

sn: दानं दया सतां पूजा व्यवहारेषु चार्जवम्। एष राम परो धर्मो रक्षणात्प्रेत्य चेह च॥
en: Charity, kindness, honouring the pious and innocent conduct constitute the chief virtues; for by those the well-being of this life and the next is brought about.

sn: त्वं प्रमाणं प्रमाणानामसि राघव सुव्रत। विदितश्चैव ते धर्मः सद्भिराचरितस्तु वै॥ धर्माणां त्वं परं धाम गुणाना सागरोपमः। अज्ञानाच मया राजनुक्तस्त्वं राजसत्तम॥
en: O Rāghava, O you of firms vows—you are an example of examples. You are cognisant of the conduct of the pious. You are like an ocean, the refuge of all virtues. O foremost of kings, out of ignorance, I have spoken to you so many things.

sn: प्रसादयामि शिरसा न त्वं क्रोद्भुमिहार्हसि। शुनः स वचनं श्रुत्वा राघवो वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥ किं ते कार्य करोम्यद्य ब्रूहि विस्रब्ध मा चिरम्। रामस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा सारमेयोऽब्रवीदिदम्॥ धर्मेण राष्ट्रं विन्देत धर्मेणैवानुपालयेत्। धर्माच्छरण्यतां याति राजा सर्वभयापहः॥ इदं विज्ञाय यत्कृत्यं श्रूयतां मम राघव।
en: With my head downwards, I beg for your satisfaction. Be not offended with me.' Hearing those wise words of the dog, Rāma said. “What shall I do for you? Do you mention it confidentially.” Whereto the dog replied, saying: It is by piety that a king governs his kingdom-it is by virtue that a king protects his subjects, becomes a refuge to all and removes the fear of his men. Keeping an eye on this, O Rāma do you hear, what I say.

sn: भिक्षुः सर्वार्थसिद्धश्च ब्राह्मणावसथे वसन्॥ तेन दत्तः प्रहारो मे निष्कारणमनागसः।
en: In the house of a certain Brāhmaṇa there lives a': beggar by the name of Sarvārthasiddha (i.e., who has got all his desires satisfied). And although I am innocent, he has for nothing hurt me.

sn: एतच्छुत्वा तु रामेण द्वा:स्थः संप्रेषितस्तदा।॥ आनीतश्च द्विजस्तेन सर्वसिद्धार्थकोविदः।
en: Hearing those words Rāma sent his messenger who brought Sarvărthasiddha, master of all subjects.

sn: अथ द्विजवरस्तत्र रामं दृष्ट्वा महाद्युतिः॥ किं ते कार्यं मया राम तब्रूहि त्वं ममानघ। एवमुक्तस्तु विप्रेण रामो वचनमब्रवीत्॥ त्वया दत्तः प्रहारोऽयं सारमेयस्य वै द्विजा किं तवापकृतं विप्र दण्डेनाभिहतो यतः॥
en: Thereupon beholding Rāma in the assembly that effulgent and leading twice-born one said: "O blameless Rāma, tell me what I shall do for you. Whereto Rāmă said "Otwice-born one, you have hurt this dog. What offence did it commit by you that you did strike it severely with a rod.

sn: क्रोधः प्राणहरः शत्रुः क्रोधोऽमित्रमुखो रिपुः। क्रोधो ह्यसिर्महातीक्ष्णः सर्वं क्रोधोऽपकर्षति॥ तपते यजते चैव यच दानं प्रयच्छति। क्रोधेन सर्वं हरति तस्मात्क्रोधं विसर्जयेत्॥ इन्द्रियाणां प्रदुष्टानां हयानामिव धावताम्। कुर्वीत धृत्या सारथ्यं संहत्येन्द्रियगोचरम्॥
en: Anger in an enemy which take away life. Anger is a sweet-speeched enemy in the grab of a friend. It is the foremost of passions and like to a sharp dagger. And it is anger that steal away everything. It pilfers all that is acquired by asceticism, sacrifices and gifts. it is proper therefore by every means to kill anger. Passions are running amok on all sides like so many exceedingly wicked steeds. Being satiated with of all objects of enjoyments it is better to govern them by patience.

sn: मनसा कर्मणा वाचा चक्षुषा च समाचरेत्। श्रेयो लोकस्य चरतो न द्वेष्टि न च लिप्यते॥ न तत्कृर्यादसिस्तीक्ष्णः सर्पो वा व्याहृतः पदा। अरिर्वा नित्यसंक्रुद्धो यथात्मा दुरनुष्ठितः॥ विनीतविनयस्यापि प्रकृतिर्न विधीयते। प्रकृति गृहमानस्य निश्चयेन कृतिधुंवा॥ एवमुक्तः स विप्रो वै रामेणाविष्टकर्मणा। द्विजः सर्वार्थसिद्धस्तु अब्रवीद्रामसंनिधौ॥
en: By mind, actions, words and eyes a man should engage in the well being of people. He should not injure any body and he not addicted to any thing. The harm, that a mind not under control, can accomplish, is beyond the range of a sharp dagger, trodden serpent and of an enemy always enraged. Even the nature of one, who has learnt humility, cannot be trusted. He, who hides his nature, himself reveals his true self.” Răma, of unwearied actions, having said this, Sarvarthāa, siddha, the foremost of twice-born ones, said:

sn: मया दत्तप्रहारोऽयं क्रोधेनाविष्टचेतसा। भिक्षार्थमटमानेन काले विगतभैक्षके॥ रथ्यास्थितस्त्वयं श्वा वै गच्छ गच्छेति भाषितः। अथ स्वरेण गच्छंस्तु रथ्यान्ते विषमः स्थितः॥ क्रोधेन क्षुधयाविष्टस्ततो दत्तोऽस्य राघव। प्रहारो राजराजेन्द्र शाधि मामपराधिनम्॥ त्वया शस्तस्य राजेन्द्र नास्ति मे नरकाद्भयम्।
en: "Knocking about whole day for alms I was highly enraged and struck this dog. It was sitting in the mid-way and I asked it again and again to more away. Thereupon, moving away and standing with reluctance. It stood fearfully on the roadside. O descendant of Raghu, I was at that time stricken with hunger, and struck it for its vicious conduct. O king of kings, I am guilty in this, and you must punish me, O lord of kings, do you administer punishment to me,-I shall then be released from the fear of hell."

sn: अथ रामेण संपृष्टाः सर्व एव सभासदः॥ किं कार्यमस्य वै बूत दण्डो वै कोऽस्य पात्यताम्। सम्यक्प्रणिहिते दण्डे प्रजा भवति रक्षिता॥
en: Thereupon, Rāma asked all the ministers, saying:-"What is to be done now? What punishment is to be inflicted on him? We can protect subjects, if we can administer punishment proportionate to crime."

sn: भृग्वाङ्गिरसकृत्साद्या वसिष्ठश्च सकाश्यपः। धर्मपाठकमुख्याश्च सचिवा नैगमास्तधा॥ एते चान्ये च बहवः पण्डितास्तत्र संगताः। अबध्यो ब्राह्मणो दण्डैरिति शास्त्रविदो विदुः॥
en: Thereat, Bhrgu, Angiras, Kutsa, Vasistha, Káshya and other ascetic, the leading preachers, the ministers, the citizens, and other sages conversant with Sastras present there, said:-“A Brahmana should not be punished with death.”

sn: बुवते राघवं सर्वे राजधर्मेषु निष्ठिताः। अथ मुनयः सर्वे राममेवाब्रुवंस्तदा॥ राजा शास्ता हि सर्वस्य त्वं विशेषेण राघव। त्रैलोक्यस्य भवाशास्ता देवो विष्णुः सनातनः॥
en: The sages conversant with laws having said this, the ascetics addressed Rama, saying:-"O Rāghava, a king is the governor of all-specially yourself. You are the chastiser of the three worlds, the eternal Visnu.”

sn: एवमुक्ते तु तैः सर्वैः श्वा वै वचनमब्रवीत्। यदि तुष्टोऽसि मे राम यदि देयो वरो मम॥ प्रतिज्ञातं त्वया वीर किं करोमीति विश्रुतम्। प्रयच्छ ब्राह्मणस्यास्य कौलपत्यं नराधिप॥ कालञ्जरे महाराज कौलपत्यं प्रदीयताम्। एतच्छ्रुत्वा तु रामेण कौलपत्येऽभिषेचितः॥ प्रययौ ब्राह्मणो हृष्टो गजस्कन्धेन सोऽर्चितः।
en: They all having said this, the dog began:“You did solemnly say 'What shall I do for you?' Therefore, if you are gratified with me, and if you do wish to confer boons on me, do you appoint this Brahmana as the head of family.” Thereupon, having been thus honoured and pleased and ascending an elephant, he proceeded to occupy his new dignified station.

sn: अथ ते रामसचिवाः स्मयमाना वचोऽब्रुवन्॥ वरोऽयं दत्त एतस्य नायं शापो महायुते।
en: At this, the councillors of Råma, surprised, said:-"O you of great effulgence, he has not been punished. Rather you have conferred on him a boon."

sn: एवमुक्तस्तु सचिवै रामो वचनमब्रवीत्॥ न यूयं गतितत्त्वज्ञाः श्वा वै जानाति कारणम्।
en: Hearing the words of ministers., Rāma said: "You do not know the real truth of the whole thing-the dog knows it well."

sn: अथ पृष्टस्तु रामेण सारमेयोऽब्रवीदिदम्॥ अहं कुलपतिस्तत्र आसं शिष्टान्नभोजनः। देवद्विजातिपूजायां दासीदासेषु राघव॥ संविभागी शुभरतिर्देवद्रव्यस्य रक्षिता। विनीतः शीलसंपन्न: सर्वसत्त्वहिते रतः॥
en: Being accosted by Rāma, the dog said: "O Rāghava, I was the head of the family of Kālanyava. After the worship of the deities and Brāhmaṇa and the feasting of the servants, male, and female, I used to take my food. I used to parcel out things duly, and my mind was not in the least attached to sin. I used to preserve with great care the articles belonging to the tutelary deities, was humble, good-natured and engaged in the wellbeing of all animals.

sn: सोहं प्राप्त इमां घोरामवस्थामधमा गतिम्। एवं क्रोधान्वितो विप्रस्त्यक्तधर्मा हिते रतः॥ क्रुद्धो नृशंसः परुष अविद्वांश्चाप्यधार्मिकः। कुलानि पातयत्येव सप्त सप्त च राघव॥
en: Still I have fallen into this dreadful and wretched condition. O Rāghava, this Brāhmaṇa is angry by nature, and impious, injures others, and is impatient, cruel, harsh in words and ignorant, and therefore shall degrade his seven generations up and down.

sn: तस्मात्सर्वास्ववस्थासु कौलपत्यं न कारयेत्। यमिच्छेन्नरकं नेतुं सपुत्रपशुबान्धवम्॥ देवेष्वधिष्ठितं कुर्याद्गोषु तं ब्राह्मणेषु च।
en: He will by no means be able to discharge the duties of a head of a family. He, whom you wishes to take to hell with her son, beasts and friends, should be engaged in the serving the Brāhmaṇs and kine.

sn: ब्रह्मस्वं देवताद्रव्यं स्त्रीणां बालधनं च यत्॥ दत्तं हरति यो भूय इष्टैः सह विनश्यति। ब्राह्मणद्रव्यमादत्ते देवानां चैव राघव॥ सद्यः पतति घोरे वै नरके वीचिसंज्ञके। मनसापि हि देवस्वं ब्रह्मस्वं च हरेत्तु यः॥ निरयान्निरयं चैव पतत्येव नराधमः।
en: For all his good actions, he is slain who steals the wealth of a Brāhmaṇa, a deity, a woman, and a boy, and the riches given away by him. O Rāghava, one who pilfers the riches of a Brāhmaṇa or a deity falls into a hell called Vici. Even he who thinks in his mind of stealing it goes once and again into hell."

sn: तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं रामो विस्मयोत्फुल्ललोचनः॥ श्वाप्यगच्छन्महातेजा यत एवागतस्ततः।
en: Hearing the words of the dog, the eyes of the effulgent Rāma were expanded with surprise. The dog went back from where it had come.

sn: मनस्वी पूर्वजात्या स जातिमात्रोऽपदूषितः॥ वाराणस्यां महाभागः प्राय चोपविवेश ह॥
en: In its pristine birth the dog was high-minded it is now cursed for being born in a degraded state of existence. Thereupon, repairing at last to Vārāṇasi the dog took the vow of fasting.

sn: अथ तस्मिन्वनोद्देश रम्ये पादपशोभिते। नदीकोणे गिरिवरे कोकिलानेककूजिते॥ सिंहव्याघ्रसमाकीर्णे नानाद्विजगणावृते। गृध्रोलको प्रवसतो बहुवर्षगणानपि॥ अथोलूकस्य भवनं गृध्रः पापविनिश्चयः। ममेदमिति कृत्वासौ कलहं तेन चाकरोत्॥ राजा सर्वस्य लोकस्य रामो राजीवलोचनः। तं प्रपद्यावहे शीघ्रं यस्यैतद्भवनं भवेत्॥
en: There lived for a long time a vulture and an own on a mountain extending over the banks of a river, resonant with the notes of cuckoos and filled with lions, tigers and various birds, situated in a pleasant forest abounding in trees near the city of Ayodhyā. Once on a time the vicious vulture alleging that the nest of the owl was his own, began to quarrel with "The lotus-eyed Rama is the king of all people; let us go to him and he will decide to whom the nest belongs."

sn: इति कृत्वा मतिं तां तु निश्चयार्थं सुनिश्चिताम्। गृध्रोलूको प्रपद्येतां कोपाविष्टौ हमर्षितौ॥ रामं प्रपद्य तौ शीघ्रं कलिव्याकुलचेतसौ। तौ परस्परविद्वेषात्स्पृशतश्चरणौ तदा॥ अथ दृष्ट्वा नरेन्द्रं तं गधो वचनमब्रवीत्। सुराणामसुराणां च प्रधानस्त्वं मतो मम॥ बृहस्पतेश्च शुक्राच विशिष्टोऽसि महाधुते। परावरज्ञो भूतानां कात्या चन्द्र इवापरः॥
en: Having thus settled the vulture and the owl, being impatient with rage, quarrellirg with one another, appeaid before Rāma and touched his feet. Beholding that lord of men, the vulture said: "O preserver of humanity, you are the foremost of celestials and Asuras. O you of great effulgence, you are gifted with intelligence and learning more than BỊhaspati and Sukrácārya. You are cognisant of the good and bad conditions of creatures. In beauty you are like the Moon and are irrepressible like the Sun.

sn: दुर्निरीक्ष्यो यथा सूर्यो हिमांश्चैव गौरवे। सागरचैव गाम्भीर्ये लोकपालो यमो ह्यसि॥ क्षान्त्या धरण्या तुल्योऽसि शीघ्रस्वे ह्यनिलोपमः। गुरुस्त्व सर्वसंपन्नः कीर्तियुक्तश्च राघव॥ अमर्षी दुर्जयो जेता सर्वास्त्रविधिपारगः। शृणुष्व मम वै राम विज्ञाप्यं नरपुंगव॥ ममालयं पूर्वकृतं बाहुवीर्येण राघव। उलूको हरते राजंस्तत्र त्वं त्रातुमर्हसि॥
en: In glory you are like Himālaya, in gravity like the Ocean, in prowess like the Patriarch, in patience like the Earth, and in velocity like the Wind. O Råghava, you are the preceptor of the mobile and immobile creation, gifted with all sorts of wealth, illustrious, devoid of a revengeful spirit, unconquerable, victorious, and master of all Sāstras and laws. O foremost of men, hear. I have an application to you. O Raghava, I had built a nest for myself; this owl is now occupying it as his own; therefore, O king, do you save me.”

sn: एवमुक्ते तु गृध्रेण उलूको वाक्यमब्रवीत्। सोमाच्छतक्रतोः सूर्याद्धनदाद्वा यमात्तथा॥ जायते वै नृपो राम किंचिद्भवति मानुषः। त्वं त सर्वमयो देवो नारायण इवापरः॥ याचते सौम्यता राजन्सम्यकप्रणिहिता विभो। समं चरसि चान्विष्य तेन सोमांशको भवान्॥ क्रोधे दण्डे प्रजानाथ दाने पापभयापहः। दाता हर्तासि गोप्तासि तेनेन्द्र इव नो भवान्॥ अधृष्यः सर्वभूतेषु तेजसा चानलोपमः। अभीक्ष्णं तपसे लोकांस्तेन भास्करसंनिमः॥
en: The vulture having said this, the owl began:"True, it is, o king, that is him are the portions of the Moon, Indra, the Sun, Kubera and Yama, but there is in him also a portion of man. But you are yourself the omnipresent deity, Narayana. You, impelled by your own self, do judge all creatures impartially; therefore, a portion of gentleness is well manifest in you and therefore do people call you, a portion of the Moon. O patriarch, in anger, punishment, gift with and fear, you are our giver, destroyer and protector,-it is for this that you are called Indra. in energy you are like fire irrepressible to all creatures, and because you do spread your lustre upon all creatures that you are called the Sun.

sn: साक्षाद्वित्तेशतुल्योऽसि अथवा धनदाधिकः। वित्तेशस्येव पद्मा श्रीनित्यं ते राजसत्तम॥ धनदस्य तु कार्येण धनदस्तेन नो भवान्। समः सर्वेषु भूतेषु स्थावरेषु चरेषु च॥ शत्रौ मित्रे च ते दृष्टिः समतां याति राघव। धर्मेण शासनं नित्यं व्यवहारो विधिक्रमात्॥
en: You are the very lord of riches or are even superior to Kubera; like Padmā to the lord of riches. Sri is always by you. Because you do discharge the functions of Kubera, you are the giver of wealth to us. O Rāghava, you look upon all creatures, mobile and immobile, with an impartial eye-you do regard your friends and foes with impartiality, and you are duly protecting, your subjects.

sn: यस्य रुष्यसि वै राम तस्य मृत्युर्विधावति। गीयसे तेन वै राम यम इत्यभिविक्रमः॥ यश्चैष मानुषो भावो भवतो नृपसत्तम। आनृशंस्यपरो राजा सत्त्वेषु क्षमयान्वितः॥ दुर्बलस्य त्वनाथस्य राजा भवति वै बलम्। अचक्षुषोत्तमं चक्षुरगतेः स गतिर्भवान्॥ अस्माकमपि नाथस्त्वं श्रूयतां मम धार्मिक। ममालयं प्रविष्टस्तु गृध्रो मां बाधते नृप।॥ त्वं हि देव मनुष्येषु शास्ता वै नरपुंगव।
en: O Rāghava, death pursues him with whom you are offended and it is for this reason that you are styled by people 'the highly powerful Yama. O foremost o kings, because you are forgiving to all creatures and a kind king that people sing your glories as of a man on earth. The king is the strength of the weak and helpless and he is the eye of the blind and the refuge of those who have no shelter. You are also our king: therefore do you listen to our petition. O king, entering into my nest, this vulture is oppressing me. You only, O foremost of men, are the divine chastiser of mankind.

sn: एतच्छ्रुत्वा तु वै रामः सचिवानाह्वयत्स्वयम्॥ धृष्टिर्जयन्तो विजयः सिद्धार्थो राष्ट्रवर्धनः। अशोको धर्मपालश्च सुमन्त्रश्च महाबलः॥ एते रामस्य सचिवा राज्ञो दशरथस्य च। नीतियुक्ता महात्मानः सर्वशास्त्रविशारदाः॥ ह्रीमन्तश्च कुलीनश्च नये मन्त्रे च कोविदाः। तानाहूय च धर्मात्मा पुष्पकादवतीर्य च॥ गृधोलूकविवादं तं पृच्छति स्म रघूत्तमः। कति वर्षाणि वै गृध्र तवेदं निलयं कृतम्॥ एतन्मे कारणं ब्रूहि यदि जानासि तत्त्वतः। एतच्छ्रुत्वा तु वै गृध्रो भाषते राघवं स तम्॥ इयं वसुमती राम मनुष्यैः परितो यदा। उत्थितैरावृता सर्वा तदा प्रभृति मे गृहम्॥
en: Hearing those words, Rāma sent for his councillors. The ministers of Dasaratha and Rāma, Brhaspati, Yayanta, Vijaya, Siddhartha, Rast ravarddhana, Asoka, Daramapāla the highly powerful Sumantra and others were all versed in laws, high-minded, conversant with all the Sastras, intelligent, born in respectable families, and adepts in counsel. Having invited them all and ascending his Puspaka car, he went to the place in question, and, descending there, asked the vulture, “How long has this nest been made? Tell me, if you remember it." Whereto the vulture replied:"From the time when mankind were first born and spread over the four quarters of the globe have I been living in this nest."

sn: उलूकश्चाब्रवीद्रामं पादपैरुपशोभिता। यदेयं पृथिवी राजंस्तदाप्रभृति मे गृहम्॥ एतच्छुत्वा तु वै रामः सभासदमुवाच ह॥ न सा सभा यत्र न सन्ति वृद्धा वृद्धा न ते ये न वदन्ति धर्मम्। नासौ धर्मो यत्र न सत्यमस्ति न तत्सत्यं यच्छलेनानुविद्धम्॥ ये तु सभ्याः सदा ज्ञात्वा तूष्णीं ध्यायन्त आसते। यथाप्राप्तं न बुवते ते सर्वेऽनृतवादिनः॥ जानन वाब्रवीत्प्रश्नान्कामात्क्रोधाद्भयात्तथा। सहस्रं वारुणान्याशानात्मनि प्रतिमुञ्चति॥ तेषां संवत्सरे पूर्णे पाश एकः प्रमुच्यते। तस्मात्सत्येन वक्तव्यं जानता सत्यमञ्जसा॥ एतच्छ्रुत्वा तु सचिवा राममेवाद्वंस्तदा। उलूकः शोभते राजन्न तु गृयो महामते॥ त्वं प्रमाणं महाराज राजा हि परमा गतिः। राजमूलाः प्रजाः सर्वा राजा धर्मः सनातनः॥ शास्ता नृणां नृपो येषां ते न गच्छन्ति दुर्गतिम्। वैवस्वतेन मुक्तास्तु भवन्ति पुरुषोत्तमाः॥
en: The owl also said: "At the time when the earth was (first) adorned with trees that this nest of mine was constructed." Hearing these words, Rama said to the councillors:-"That assembly is not an assembly where there are no friends—nor are they old men who do not dwell upon religious topics. That religion is not a religion where there is no truth and that truth is not the truth where there is hypocrisy. Those councillors are liars who do not give proper replies in time on the subjects they are well-informed on. He who does give reply to a question under the influence of passion, anger or fear, binds himself with. thousand nooses of Varuņa, and at the expiration of full one year he is released from a single sin.” Hearing these words, the ministers said to Rāma: "0 you having a large mind, what the owl has said is true the vulture has not spoken the truth. You are the evidence this, O great king-for the king is the last refuge of all-the root of the subject and the eternal religion. He who is punished by the king, is not doomed in a degraded state. He is, in truth, saved from the fear of hell and reaches a better state."

sn: सचिवानां वचः श्रुत्वा रामो वचनमब्रवीत्। श्रूयतामभिधास्यामि पुराणे यदुदाहृतम्॥ द्यौः सचन्द्रार्कनक्षत्रा सपर्वतमहावना। सलिलार्णवसंपूर्णं त्रैलोक्यं सचराचरम्॥ एक एव तदा ह्यासीद्युक्तो मेरुरिवापरः। पुरा भूः सह लक्ष्या च विष्णोर्जठरमाविशत्॥ तां निगृह्य महातेजाः प्रविश्य सलिलार्णवम्। सुष्वाप देवो भूतात्मा बहून्वर्षगणानपि॥ विष्णोसुप्ते नदा ब्रह्मा विवेश जठरं ततः। रुद्धस्रोतं तु तं ज्ञात्वा महायोगी समाविशत्॥ नाभ्यां विष्णोः समुत्पन्ने पद्मे हेमविभूषिते। स तु निर्गम्य वै ब्रह्मा योगी भूत्वा महाप्रभुः॥ सिसृक्षुः पृथिवीं वायु पर्वतान्समहीरुहान्। तदन्तरे प्रजाः शर्वाः समनुष्यसरीस्पाः॥ सयुजाण्डजाः शर्वाः स ससर्ज महातपाः। तत्र श्रोत्रमलोत्पन्न: कैटभो मधुना सह॥ दानवौ तौ महावीर्यो घोररूपौ दुरासदौ। दृष्ट्वा प्रजापतिं तत्र क्रोधाविष्टौ बभूवतुः॥ वेगेन महता तत्र स्वयंभुवमधावताम्। दृष्ट्वा स्वयंभुवा मुक्तो रावो वै विकृतस्तदा॥ तेन शब्देन संप्राप्तौ दानवौ हरिणा सह। अथ चक्रप्रहारेण सूदितौ मधुकैटभौ॥ मेदसा प्लाविता सर्वा पृथिवी च समन्ततः। भूयो विशोधिता तेन हरिणा लोकधारिणा॥ शुद्धां वै मेदिनी तां तु वृक्षः सर्वामपूरयत्। ओषध्यः सर्वसस्यानि निष्पद्यन्त पृथग्विधाः॥ मेदोगन्धा तु धरणी मेदिनीत्यभिसंज्ञिता। तस्मान गृध्रस्य गृहमूलूकस्येति मे मतिः॥ तस्माद् गृध्रस्तु दण्ड्यो वै पापो हर्ता परालयम्। पीडां करोति पापात्मा दुर्विनीतो महानयम्॥
en: Hearing the words of the ministers, Rāma said: "Hear what is mentioned in the Purānas. Formerly the Sun, the Moon, the welkin with the stars, the earth with the mountains and forests—the three worlds, the mobile and the immobile, were under water. At that time only Nārāyaṇa existed as the second Sumeru. In Nārāyaṇa's belly was stationed the earth with Lakşmi. Having destroyed the creation and entered water, the highly effulgent Vişnu, identical with the souls of creatures, lay asleep there for many long years. Beholding Vişņu asleep after the destruction of the universe and knowing Vişņu of obstructed breath, the great ascetic Brahmā entered his abdomen. Thereupon, when a golden lotus sprang from Vişnu's navel. That great lord, ascetic Brahmā, originated therefrom and was engaged in austere penances for the purpose of creating earth, air, mountains, trees, men, reptiles and all animals born from womb or egg. At that time from the ears of Nārāyaṇa originated two valiant and dreadful demons under the name of Madhu and Kaitabha. Beholding the Patriarch, there they were greatly enraged and pursued him. Thereat the self-born cried aloud hideously. Awakened by that sound Nārāyaņa engaged in fighting with Madhu and Kaitabha, and slew them with his discus. And with their gore the whole earth was delighted. Thereupon, purifying the earth again, Hari, preserver of the world, covered it with trees. And various drugs were also created. And the earth was called Medini because it was filled with Medas, marrow of Madhu and Kaitabha. It is for this that I hold, O ministers, that this house not belong to the vulture, but to the owl. Therefore, this vicious vulture should be punished for this wicked, vicious-minded one, robbing another's nest, is oppressing him.” years.'

sn: अथाशरीरिणी वाणी अन्तरिक्षात्प्रबोधिनी। मावधी राम गृधं त्वं पूर्वदग्धं तपोबलात्॥ कालगौतमदग्धोऽयं प्रजानाथो नरेश्वर। ब्रह्मदत्तेति नाम्नैष शूरः सत्यव्रतः शुचिः॥ गृहं त्वस्यागतो विप्रो भोजनं प्रत्यमार्गत। साग्रं वर्षशतं चैव भोक्तव्यं नृपसत्तम॥
en: In the interval a voice was heard in the sky stating the true facts: "O Rāma, do not slay the vulture,—for it has already been reduced to ashes by the force of Gautama's asceticism. O lord of men, this vulture, in its pristine birth, was a heroic truthful and pure king by the name of Brahmadatta. Once on a time a Brhāmaņa, by the name of Gautama, the very personification of Kāla, came to the house of Brahmadatta for food and said:-'0 king, I shall feed in your house for more than a hundred
