sn: ब्रह्मदत्तः स वै तस्य पाद्यमर्थ्य स्वयं नृपः। हार्द चैवाकरोत्तस्य भोजनार्थं महाद्युतेः॥ मांसमस्याभवत्तत्र आहारे तु महात्मनः। अथ क्रुद्धेन मुनिना शापो दत्तोऽस्य दारुणः॥ गृध्रस्त्वं भव वै राजन्मा मैनं ह्यथ सोऽब्रवीत्। प्रसादं कुरु धर्मज्ञ अज्ञानान्मे महाव्रत॥ शापस्यान्तं महाभाग क्रियतां वै ममानघ। तदज्ञानकृतं मत्वा राजानं मुनिरब्रवीत्॥ उत्पत्स्यति कुले राज्ञां रामो नाम महायशाः। इक्ष्वाकूणां महाभागो राजा राजीवलोचनः॥
en: Thereupon, offering that effulgent Brāhmaṇa, with his own hands, water to wash his feet the king Brahmadatta, made arrangements for his meal. Accidentally flesh was mixed with the food of the high-souled Gautama. Being enraged thereat, the ascetic imprecated him with a dreadful curse and said: "O king, you become a vulture.' The king said: 'Be propitiated, O you of great vows, do not imprecate me thus. I have out of ignorance committed this offence. O great one, O blameless one, do you act so that this curse may find termination.' Thereat understanding that this offence was committed by the king unwittingly, the ascetic said-'o king, in the race of Iksawkus a king shall be born under the name of Rāma.

sn: तेन स्पृष्टो विपापस्त्वं भविता नरपुंगव। स्पृष्टो रामेण तच्छुत्वा नरेन्द्रः पृथिवीपतिः॥ गृध्रत्वं त्यक्तवानराजा दिव्यगन्धानुलेपनः। पुरुषो दिव्यरूपोऽभूदुवाचेदं च राघवम्॥ साधु राघव धर्मज्ञ त्वत्प्रसादादहं विभो। विमुक्तो नरकाद्धोराच्छापस्यान्तः कृतस्त्वया।॥
en: O foremost of men, you shall be released from the curse when he shall touch you.' Hearing the voice in the sky, Rāma touched Brahmadatta. Thereupon renouncing his venture from and assuming a beautiful body smeared with celestial perfumes, he praised Rāma and said: "O you conversant with piety, by your favour have I been saved from the dreadful hell—here has ended my curse."

sn: तयोः संवदतोरेवं रामलक्ष्मणयोस्तदा। वासन्तिकी निशा प्राप्ता न शीता न च धर्मदा॥
en: As Rama and Laksmana were (daily) engaged. in conversing thus, the vernal night; neither hot nor cold, came on.

sn: ततः प्रभाते विमले कृतपूर्वाहिणकक्रियः। अभिचक्राम काकुत्स्थो दर्शनं पौरकार्यवित्॥
en: And it came to pass that one bright morning, after having performed his first diurnal rites, Käkutstha, understanding the ways of the citizens, became anxious to present himself at a spot when he could observe the citizens.

sn: ततः सुमन्त्रस्त्वागम्य राघवं वाक्यमब्रवीत्। एते प्रतिहता राजन्द्वारि तिष्ठन्ति तापसाः॥ भार्गवं च्यवनं चैव पुरस्कृत्य महर्षयः। दर्शनं ते महाराज चोदयन्ति कृतत्वराः॥ प्रीयमाणा नरव्याघ्र यमुनातीरवासिनः। तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा रामः प्रोवाच धर्मवित्॥ प्रवेश्यन्तां महाभागा भार्गवप्रमुखा द्विजाः।
en: At this time Sumantra, entering, addressed him, saying, “O king, stopped at the gate, some ascetic stay there, Maharsis, led by Bhargava and Cyavana. And, O mighty monarch, eager for a sight of you, those dwellers on the banks of the Yamunā, well pleased, have despatched me (hither), O tiger among men.” Hearing his words, the righteous Rāma answered: “Let the exalted Brāhmaṇas leaded by Bhārgava, enter."

sn: राज्ञस्त्वाज्ञां पुरस्कृत्य द्वाः स्थो मूर्धा कृताञ्जलिः॥ प्रवेशयामास तदा तापसान्सुदुरासदान्।
en: Thereat, honouring the royal mandate, the warder with joined hands brought those ascetics difficult of being approached.

sn: शतं समधिकं तत्र दीप्यमानं स्वतेजसा॥ प्रविष्टं राजभवनं तापसानां महात्मनाम्। ते द्विजाः पूर्णकलशैः सर्वतीर्थाम्बुसत्कृतः॥ गृहीत्वा फलमूलं च रामस्याभ्याहरन्बहु। प्रतिगृह्य तु तत्सर्वं रामः प्रीतिपुरस्कृतः॥ तीर्थोदकानि सर्वाणि फलानि विविधानि च। उवाच च महाबाहुः सर्वानेव महामुनीन्॥
en: And numbering over an hundred, flaming up in their native effulgence, those high-souled anchorites entered the royal residence. And they presented Rāma with various fruits in profusion and vessels filled with sanctified waters of all holy spots. Thereupon, accepting the waters of the holy places as well as the various kinds of fruit, that mighty-armed one spoke to the mighty ascetics.

sn: इमान्यासनमुख्यानि यथार्हमुपविश्यताम्। रामस्य भाषितं श्रुत्वा सर्व एव महर्षयः॥
en: "Do you agreeably to desert take these seats." Hearing Rāma's speech, all the Maharşis sat down on those graceful and elegant golden seats.

sn: बृसीषु रुचिराख्यासु निषेदुः काञ्चनीषु ते। उपविष्टानृषीस्तत्र दृष्ट्वा परपुरंजयः। प्रयतः प्राञ्जलिर्भूत्वा राघवो वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
en: And seeing the saints seated there, that captor of hostile capitals Rāghava, restraining himself, with joined hands, observed.

sn: किमागमनकार्य वः किं करोमि समाहितः। आज्ञाप्योऽहं महर्षीणां सर्वकामकरः सुखम्॥
en: What is the reason of your visit? What shall I heedfully perform for you? I am worthy of being commanded by the Maharşis; and I must without demur compass every pleasure of theirs.

sn: इदं राज्यं च सकलं जीवितं च हृदि स्थितम्। सर्वमेतद् द्विजार्थं मे सत्यमेतद्ब्रवीमि वः॥
en: And this entire monarchy, and the life that is resident in my heart, all these are for the regenerate ones. This I tell you in the name of truth.

sn: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा साधुकारो महानभूत्। ऋषीणामुग्रतपसां यमुनातीरवासिनाम्॥
en: Hearing his words, the sages of fierce austerities inhabiting the banks of the Yamunā, broke out into a peal of plandits.

sn: ऊचुश्चैव महात्मानो हर्षेण महता वृताः। उपपत्रं नरश्रेष्ठ तवैव भुवि नान्यतः॥
en: And those high-souled ones, exceedingly rejoiced, said: On earth, O crown of men, this can only be expected from you and nobody else.

sn: बहवः पार्थिवा राजन्नातिक्रान्ता महाबलाः। कार्यस्य गौरवं मत्वा प्रतिज्ञां नाभ्यरोचयन्॥
en: Many kings wielding great power have passed away who, having regard to the (possible) gravity of the undertaking, could not bring themselves to promise anything before hand.

sn: त्वया पुनर्ब्राह्मणगौरवादियं कृता प्रतिज्ञा ह्यनवेक्ष्य कारणम्। ततश्च कर्ता ह्यसि नात्र संशयो महाभयात्त्रातुमृषींस्त्वमर्हसि ॥
en: But, without knowing the task, you have bound yourself by a promise for the glory of the Brahmanas. And you, without doubt, will succeed in effecting the work; and it behove you to deliver the sages from a mighty fright.

sn: ब्रुवद्भिरेवमृषिभिः काकुत्स्थो वाक्यमब्रवीत्। किं कार्य ब्रूत मुनयो भयं तावदपैतु वः॥
en: When the sages had spoken thus, Käkutstha said: "O ascetics, tell me what is the work which I shall have to accomplish in your behalf. Your fear shall be removed."

sn: तथा ब्रुवति काकुत्स्थे भार्गवो वाक्यमब्रवीत्। भयानां शृणु यन्मूलं देशस्य च नरेश्वर॥
en: As Käkutstha was speaking thus, Bhārgava remarked! O lord of men, do you hear of the origin of the fear that threatens our country.

sn: पूर्व कृतयुगे राजन्दैतेयः सुमहामतिः। लोलापुत्रोऽभवज्ज्येष्ठो मधुर्नाम महासुरः॥
en: O king, formerly in the Kita age, there was a magnanimous offspring of Diti, the mighty Asura, Madhu, eldest son of Lotā.

sn: ब्रह्मण्यश्च शरण्यश्च बुद्ध्या च परिनिष्ठितः। सुरैश्च परमोदारैः प्रीतिस्तस्यातुलाभवत्॥
en: He was well disposed towards Brāhmaṇas, kind to those seeking his refuge, and gifted with high intelligence. The exceedingly generous deities delighted in him greatly.

sn: स मधुर्वीर्यसंपन्नो धर्म च सुसमाहितः। बहुमानाच्च रुद्रेण दत्तस्तस्याद्भुतो वरः॥
en: And by way of honouring him, Rudra conferred a wonderful boon upon Madhu endowed with prowess and ever intent on religion.

sn: शूलं शूलाद्विनिष्कृष्य महावीर्य महाप्रभम्। ददौ महात्मा सुप्रीतो वाक्यं चैतदुवाच ह।६।।
en: And extracting a dart from his own, possessed of terrific energy, endowed with great force; and furnished with exceeding splendour that highsouled one, well pleased, made it over (to Madhu) and spoke to him.

sn: त्वयायमतुलो धर्मो मत्प्रसादकरः शुभः। प्रीत्या परमया युक्तो ददाम्यायुधमुत्तमम्॥
en: You have practised excellent and unrivalled righteousness, which has won my good graces, and (therefore), I highly gratified, bestow on you this choice weapon.

sn: यावत्सुरैश्च विप्रैश्च न विरुध्येर्महासुर। तावच्छूलं तवेदं स्यादन्यथा नाशमेष्यति॥
en: So long as you, O mighty Asura, do not assail celestials and Vipras, so long shall this be your, otherwise it shall come to naught.

sn: यश्च मामभियुञ्जीत युद्धाय विगतज्वरः। तं शूलो भस्मसात्कृत्वा पुनरेष्यति ते करम्।।।।।
en: Reducing to cinders the person that shall rashly enter upon conflict with you, this dart shall return to your hand.

sn: एवं रुद्राद्वरं लब्ध्वा भूय एव महासुरः। प्रणिपत्य महादेवं वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह॥
en: Having thus obtained the boon from Rudra, the mighty Asura, again bowing to Mahādeva, addressed him, saying.

sn: भगवन्मम वंशस्य शूलमेतदनुत्तमम्। भवेत्तु सततं देव सुराणामीश्वरो ह्यसि॥
en: O reverend one, may this excellent dart be the possession of my family O god, you are the lord of the immortals.

sn: तं ब्रुवाणं मधुं देवः सर्वभूतपतिः शिवः। प्रत्युवाच महादेवो नैतदेवं भविष्यति॥
en: Thereat the lord of all beings, the mighty deity Śiva, answered Madhu, when he had spoken thus: This will not be.

sn: मा भूत्ते विफला वाणी मत्प्रसादकृता शुभा। भवतः पुत्रमेकं तु शूलमेतद्भविष्यति॥
en: But in order that your prayer may not go for nothing. I graciously say in your behalf that one of your sons shall sway this dart.

sn: यावत्करस्थः शूलोऽयं भविष्यति सुतस्य ते। अवध्यः सर्वभूतानां शूलहस्तो भविष्यति ॥
en: So long that dart-handed one shall be incapable of being destroyed be any creature.

sn: एवं मधुर्वरं लब्ध्वा देवात्सुमहदद्भुतम्। भवनं सोऽसुरश्रेष्ठः कारयामास सुप्रभम्॥
en: Having obtained this wonderful boon from the god, Madhu, foremost of Asuras, caused a splendid city to be constructed.

sn: तस्य पत्नी महाभागा प्रिया कुम्भीनसीति या। विश्वावसोरपत्यं साप्यनलायां महाप्रभा॥
en: His beloved wife the exalted and majestic Kumbhīnasſ is the offspring of Viśvāvasu by Anala.

sn: तस्याः पुत्रो महावीर्यो लवणो नाम दारुणः। बाल्यात्प्रभृति दुष्टात्मा पापान्येव समाचरत्॥
en: Her son, the highly powerful wicked, and fierce Lavana, ever since his boyhood, gave himself up to a sinful course of life.

sn: तं पुत्रं दुर्विनीतं तु दृष्ट्वा क्रोधसमन्वितः। मधुः स शोकमापेदे न चैनं किंचिदब्रवीत्॥
en: Seeing his son, committed to an impious course Madhu was overcome with grief, but he did not say anything to him.

sn: स विहाय इमं लोकं प्रविष्टो वरुणालयम्। शूलं निवेश्य लवणे वरं तस्मै न्यवेदयत्॥
en: And forsaking this world, he entered the region of Varuņa; and making over the dart to Lavana, communicated to him all about the boon he had obtained.

sn: स प्रभावेण शूलस्य दौरात्म्येनात्मनस्तथा। संतापयति लोकांस्त्रीन्विशेषेण च तापसान्॥ एवंप्रभावो लवणः शूलं चैव तथाविधम्। श्रुत्वा प्रमाणं काकुत्स्थ त्वं हि नः परमा गतिः॥
en: And by virtue of the power of the dart, he oppress the three worlds in especial the ascetics; such is the power of Lavaņa, and such is his dart. Hearing all this O Kākutstha, you are capable (of righting our wrong.) You are our chief resource.

sn: बहवः पार्थिवा राम भयातॆषिभिः पुरा। अभयं याचिता वीर त्रातारं न च विद्महे ॥
en: O Rāma, many a monarch has been already sued by the sages, O hero, to deliver them from this fear, but we have not yet found a deliverer.

sn: ते वयं रावणं श्रुत्वा हतं सबलवाहनम्। त्रातारं विद्महे तात नान्यं भुवि नराधिपम्। तत्परित्रातुमिच्छामो लवणाद्भयपीडितान्॥
en: Hearing, O child, that Ravana together with all his forces and vehicles has been destroyed (by you), we know that there breathes not another king on earth capable of delivering us. Therefore our prayer is that you may deliver us afflicted with the fear of Lavana.

sn: इति राम निवेदितं तु ते भयजं कारणमुत्थितं च यत्। विनिवारयितुं भवान्क्षमः कुरु तं काममहीनविक्रम॥
en: Thus, O Rāma, have we acquainted you with the occasion of fear that has arisen. You are capable of coping with the same. Do you of undeteriorated prowess, do the needful.

sn: तथोक्ते तानृषीरामः प्रत्युवाच कृताञ्जलिः। किमाहारः किमाचारो लवणः क्व च वर्तते॥
en: Thus accosted (by the sages), Rāma answered them with joined hands: "What does he live on? What are his ways? And where does Lavana live?"

sn: राघवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा ऋषयः सर्व एव ते। ततो निवेदयामासुर्लवणो ववृधे यथा॥
en: Hearing Räghava's words, the sages informed him of the way in which Lavana increased in power.

sn: आहारः सर्वसत्त्वानि विशेषेण च तापसाः। आचारो रौद्रता नित्यं वासो मधुवने तथा॥
en: His food is every creature specially ascetics; his manner of life is regulated by ferocity and his constant home is Madhuvana.

sn: हत्वा बहुसहस्राणि सिंहव्याघ्रमृगाण्डनान्। मानुषांश्चैव कुरुते नित्यमाहारमाह्निकम्॥
en: Slaying constantly thousands on thousands of lions and tigers and deer, and birds and human beings, he provides his daily food (with their flesh.)

sn: ततोऽन्तराणि सत्त्वानि खादते स महाबलः। संहारे समनुप्राप्ते व्यादितास्य इवान्तकः॥
en: And like the Destroyer on the occasion of the universal dissolution, that one possessed of gigantic strength feeds on other creatures as well.

sn: तच्छ्रुत्वा राघवो वाक्यमुवाच स महामुनीन्। घातयिष्यामि तद्रक्षो व्यपगच्छतु वो भयम्॥
en: Hearing this, Rāghava spoke to the mighty ascetics: "I will slay that Raksasa. Let your depart."

sn: प्रतिज्ञाय तदा तेषां मुनीनामुग्रतेजसाम्। स भ्रातृन्सहितान्सर्वानुवाच रघुनन्दनः।७।।
en: Having thus bound himself with that promise to the ascetics of fierce energy, Raghu's son along with his brothers spoke.

sn: को हन्ता लवणं वीरः कस्यांशः स विधीयताम्। भरतस्य महाबाहोः शत्रुघ्नस्य च धीमतः॥
en: What hero shall slay Lavana? Do you decide this. On whom shall devolve this duty? Whether the mighty armed Bharata or the intelligent Śatrughna shall (do this work?).

sn: राघवेणैवमुक्तस्तु भरतो वाक्यमब्रवीत्। अहमेनं वधिष्यामि ममांशः स विधीयताम्।।
en: Thus addressed by Raghava Bharata remarked: "I will slay this. Let this task be entrusted to me."

sn: भरतस्य वचः श्रुत्वा धैर्यशौर्यसमन्वितम्। लक्ष्मणावरजस्तस्थौ हित्वा सौवर्णमासनम्॥ शत्रुघ्नस्त्वब्रवीद्वाक्यं प्रणिपत्य नराधिपम्। कृतकर्मा महाबाहुर्मध्यमो रघुनन्दन॥ आर्येण हि पुरा शून्या त्वयोध्या परिपालिता। संतापं हृदये कृत्वा आर्यस्यागमनं प्रति॥
en: Hearing Bharata's speech instinct with fortitude and valour, the younger brother of Lakş maņa stood up, leaving his golden seat. And Śatrughna, saluting the king represented: “The mighty-armed second son of Raghu has already achieved a grand work: he formerly governed Ayodhyā empty of the noble one,* bearing in his heart the grief connected with his return. *Rama.

sn: दुःखानि च बहूनीह अनुभूतानि पार्थिव। शयानो दुःखशय्यासु नन्दिग्रामे महायशाः॥ फलमूलाशनो भूत्वा जटी चीरधरस्तथा।
en: Undergoing many a hardship, o king, that illustrious one passed his days, lying down on a bed of sorrow, and living on fruits and roots, and wearing rags.

sn: अनुभूयेदृशं दुःखमेष राघवनन्दनः॥ प्रेष्ये मयि स्थिते राजन्न भूयः क्लेशमाप्नुयात्।
en: Having suffered such misery, Raghu's son should not be suffered to undergo trouble, while, O king I his servant is by.

sn: तथा ब्रुवति शत्रुघ्ने राघवः पुनरब्रवीत्॥ एवं भवतु काकुत्स्थ क्रियतां मम शासनम्। राज्ये त्वामभिषेक्ष्यामि मधोस्तु नगरे शुभे॥ निवेशय महाबाहो भरतं यद्यवेक्षसे। शूरस्त्वं कृतविद्यश्च समर्थश्च निवेशने॥ नगरं यमुनाजुष्टं तथा जनपदाशुभान्। यो हि वंशं समुत्पाद्य पार्थिवस्य निवेशने॥ न विधत्ते नृपं तत्र नरकं स हि गच्छति।
en: On Satrughna saying this, Raghava again said: Let this be so. Do you do my bidding. I shall install you on the graceful city of Madhu; or if you wish without and entrust Bharata with this task, O long-armed Heroic, and accomplished, you are combatant to found a city on the Yamună as well as flourishing provinces. He that, having people's dominion, does not flourish it with a king. Go to hell. one.

sn: स त्वं हत्वा मधुसुतं लवणं पापनिश्चयम्॥ राज्यं प्रशाधि धर्मेण वाक्यं मे यद्यवेक्षसे। उत्तरं च न वक्तव्यं शूर वाक्यान्तरे मम॥ बालेन पूर्वजस्याज्ञा कर्तव्या नात्र संशयः। अभिषेकं च काकुत्स्थ प्रतीच्छस्व ममोद्यतम्। वसिष्ठप्रमुखैविप्रैर्विधिमन्त्रपुरस्कृतम्॥
en: So if you accept my words, then slaying Madhu's son, the sinful Lavana, rule the kingdom righteously. O hero, you must say anything after what I have spoken. Without doubt, a youthful younger brother must obey the injunctions of his elder brother. Do you, o Kākutstha, accept the installation which I confer on the, precluded by the prescribed religious formulae uttered by Vipras headed by Vasiştha."

sn: एवमुक्तस्तु रामेण परां व्रीडामुपागमत्। शत्रुघ्नो वीर्यसंपन्नो मन्दं मन्दमुवाच ह॥
en: Thus accosted by Rāma, the exceedingly energetic Satrughna was powerfully wrought up with bashfulness, and replied slowly.

sn: अधर्म विद्म काकुत्स्थ अस्मिन्नर्थे नरेश्वर। कथं तिष्ठत्सु ज्येष्ठेषु कनीयानभिषिच्यते॥
en: O lord of men, this does not appear to be in consonance with morality. Wherefore, an elder brother existing, would you install a younger one?

sn: अवश्यं करणीयं च शासनं पुरुषर्षभ। तव चैव महाभाग शासनं दुरतिक्रमम्॥
en: I must, O best of men, do your behest: for, O exalted one, your mandate can never be passed by me.

sn: त्वत्तो मया श्रुतं वीर श्रुतिभ्यश्च मया श्रुतम्। नोत्तरं हि मया वाच्यं मध्यमे प्रतिजानति।४।। व्याहृतं दुर्वचो घोरं हन्तास्मि लवणं मृधे। तस्यैवं मे दुरुक्तस्य दुर्गतिः पुरुषर्षभ॥
en: O hero, I have heard from you as well as from the Śruti (touching the morality concerned).* i.e. of being installed as a king during the life of my elder brother. When my second brother had already vowed (that he would slay Lavana), I ought not to have returned the answer I actually have. I saying, 'I will in battle slay the dreadful Lavaņa.' I have been guilty of an unrighteous speech. And it is for this transgression that, O powerful one, I shall have to undergo this improper process. *(i.e. of being installed as a king during the life of my elder brother.)

sn: उत्तरं नहि वक्तव्यं ज्येष्ठेनाभिहिते पुनः। अधर्मसहितं चैव परलोकविवर्जितम्॥
en: But, albeit this course is unrighteous and entails perdition, yet desired by an eldest brother, I certainly ought not to make any answer.

sn: सोऽहं द्वितीयं काकुत्स्थ न वक्ष्यामीति चोत्तरम्। मा द्वितीयेन दण्डो वै निपतेन्मयि मानद॥
en: And, O Kākutstha, a second answer I would not return; so that, О bestower of honour, I may not, by a second reply, render myself liable to a fresh punishment.

sn: कामकारो ह्यहं राजंस्तवास्य पुरुषर्षभ। अधर्म जहि काकुत्स्थ मत्कृते रघुनन्दन ॥
en: In this matter, O chief of men, I will even do your desire. Do you, O descendant of Ragu, so order that sin may not be mine (in having obeyed your mandate.)

sn: एवमुक्ते तु शूरेण शत्रुघ्नेन महात्मना। उवाच रामः संहृष्टो भरतं लक्ष्मणं तथा॥
en: Thus addressed by the heroic and high-souled Śatrughna, Rāma, delighted, spoke to Bharata and Laksmana.

sn: संभारानभिषेकस्य आनयध्वं समाहिताः। अद्यैव पुरुषव्याघ्रमभिषेक्ष्यामि राघवम्॥
en: Do you carefully provide the things necessary for the coronation: this very day shall I install that foremost of men, the descendant of Raghu.

sn: पुरोधसं च काकुत्स्थ नैगमानृत्विजस्तथा। मन्त्रिणश्चैव तान्सर्वानानयध्वं ममाज्ञया॥
en: And by my order do you summon the Purodhasas, O Kākutstha, and the citizens and the Rtvijas, and the councillors.

sn: राज्ञः शासनमाज्ञाय तथाकुर्वन्महारथाः। अभिषेकसमारम्भं पुरस्कृत्य पुरोधसम्॥ प्रविष्टा राजभवनं राजानो ब्राह्मणास्तथा।
en: Having received the royal behest, the mighty car-warriors did accordingly. And the Kșatriyas and the Brāhmaṇas entered the royal mansion with the priest as well as the requisite things for the installation.

sn: ततोऽभिषेको ववृधे शत्रुघ्नस्य महात्मनः॥ संप्रहर्षकरः श्रीमानराघवस्य पुरस्य च।
en: And then commenced the auspicious sprinkling of the high-souled Satrughna, gladdening (the hearts of all in) the palace of Rāghava.

sn: अभिषिक्तस्तु काकुत्स्थो बभौ चादित्यसंनिभः॥ अभिषिक्तः पुरा स्कन्दः सेन्ट्रैरिव दिवौकसैः।
en: And on being installed Käkutstha resembled the sun; and he like Skanda formerly installed by the celestials led by Indra.

sn: अभिषिक्ते तु शत्रुघ्ने रामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा॥ पौराः प्रमुदिताश्चासन्ब्राह्मणाश्च बहुश्रुताः।
en: And when Šatrughna had been installed by Rāma of untiring deeds, the citizens as well as the Brāhmaṇas of vast Vedic, attainments experienced excess of joy.

sn: कौसल्या च सुमित्रा च मङ्गलं केकयी तथा॥ चकुस्ता राजभवने याश्चान्या राजयोषितः। ऋषयश्च महात्मानो यमुनातीरवासिनः॥
en: And Kausaly, and Sumitrā and Kaikeyi and the other wives of the king set up festal salutation in the palace. And on Satrughna having been installed the high-souled sages dwelling on the banks of the Jamunā, thought that Lavaņa had been slain.

sn: हतं लवणमाशंसुः शत्रुघ्नस्याभिषेचनात्। ततोऽभिषिक्तं शत्रुघ्नमङ्कमारोप्य राघवः। उवाच मधुरां वाणी तेजस्तस्याभिपूरयन्॥
en: Then placing the installed Satrughna on his lap Rāghava, extolling his prowess, addressed him sweet words.

sn: अयं शरस्त्वमोघस्ते दिव्यः परपुरंजयः। अनेन लवणं सौम्य हन्तासि रघुनन्दन ॥
en: O captor of hostile capitals, this divine arrow never missing is your. With this, O son of Raghu, you, O spliced one, with slay Lavana.

sn: सृष्टः शरोऽयं काकुत्स्थ यदा शेते महार्णवे। स्वयंभूरजितो दिव्यो यं नापश्यन्सुरासुराः॥ अदृश्यः सर्वभूतानां तेनायं हि शरोत्तमः। सृष्टः क्रोधाभिभूतेन विनाशार्थ दुरात्मनोः॥ मधुकैटभयोर्वीर विघाते सर्वरक्षसाम्। स्रष्टुकामेन लोकांस्त्रीस्तौ चानेन हतौ युधि ॥ हत्वा जनभोगार्थे कैटभं तु मधुं तथा। अनेन शरमुख्येन ततो लोकांश्चकार सः॥
en: O Kākutstha, this shaft was forged when invisible by celestials and Asuras the divine selfsprung and invincible (deity) reposed on the mighty main, and when creation was oppressed by Madhu and Kaitabha as well as other Räks asas. He, overwhelmed with rage desirous of creating the three worlds, created the best of arrows invincible to all beings, for the extraction of the wicked ones; and destroyed them in battle by means of this very arrow. And having with this foremost of shafts finished Madhu and Kait abha, they set about creating the worlds.

sn: नायं मया शरः पूर्व रावणस्य वधार्थिना। मुक्तः शत्रुघ्न भूतानां महान्हासो भवेदिति॥
en: When, O Satrughna, formerly I sought to slay Råvaņa, I did not discharge this arrow, thinking that if discharged, it would inflict great havoc on creatures.

sn: यच्च तस्य महच्छूलं त्र्यम्बकेण महात्मना। दत्तं शत्रुविनाशाय मधोरायुधमुत्तमम्॥ तत्संनिक्षिप्य भवने पूज्यमानं पुनः पुनः। दिशः सर्वाः समासाद्य प्राप्नोत्याहारमुत्तमम्॥ यदा तु युद्धमाकाङ्क्षन्यदि कश्चित्समाह्वयेत्। तदा शूलं गृहीत्वा तु भस्म रक्षः करोति हि॥
en: Keeping in his abode that great and redoubled which had been bestowed on Madhu by the high-souled Tryambaka, for the destruction of foes, and worshipping the same ever, Lavaņa go about and secure excellent fare( for himself) when one challenge him, desirous of reducing him (his antagonist) to ashes.

sn: स त्वं पुरुषशार्दूल तमायुधविनाकृतम्। अप्रविष्टं पुरं पूर्वं द्वारि तिष्ठ धृतायुधः॥ अप्रविष्टं च भवनं युद्धाय पुरुषर्षभ। आह्वयेथा महाबाहो ततो हन्तासि राक्षसम्॥
en: Therefore, O foremost of men, you should, before entering the city, stand at the gate obstructing his course. O you having long arms, you should invite him for battle when he shall be weaponless and in that way would be able to destroy him.

sn: अन्यथा क्रियमाणे तु अवध्यः स भविष्यति। यदि त्वेवं कृतं वीर विनाशमुपयास्यति॥
en: And by no other means he is to be slain. If you can encompass this, he shall forsooth be slain.

sn: एतत्ते सर्वमाख्यातं शूलस्य च विपर्ययः। श्रीमतः शितिकण्ठस्य कृत्यं हि दुरतिक्रमम्॥
en: O my son, I have thus told you the way in which the dare should be thwarted. It is impossible to surpass the prowess of the graceful Nilkantha.

sn: एवमुक्त्वा च काकुत्स्थं प्रशस्य च पुनः पुनः। पुनरेवापरं वाक्यमुवाच रघुनन्दनः॥
en: Having thus addressed Satrughna, Rāma again and again praised him and said.

sn: इमान्यश्वसहस्राणि चत्वारि पुरुषर्षभ। रथानां द्वे सहस्रे च गजानां शतमुत्तमम्॥ अन्तरापणवीथ्यश्च नानापण्योपशोभिताः। अनुगच्छन्तु काकुत्स्थं तथैव नटनर्तकाः॥
en: O foremost of men, let four thousand horses, two thousand chariots, one hundred excellent elephants, shops with various articles and songsters follow you.

sn: हिरण्यस्य सुवर्णस्य नियतं पुरुषर्षभ। आदाय गच्छ शत्रुघ्न पर्याप्तधनवाहनः॥
en: O foremost of men, O Śatrughna, do you proceed with Niyuta gold and silver coins and necessary riches and conveyances.

sn: बलं च सुभृतं वीर हृष्टतुष्टमनुद्धतम्। संभाषासंप्रदानेन रञ्जयस्व नरोत्तम॥ न ह्यास्तत्र तिष्ठन्ति न दारा न च बान्धवाः। सुप्रीतो भृत्यवर्गस्तु यत्र तिष्ठति राघव॥
en: Do you so act, O hero, that soldiers might be well-fed and delighted and be not annoyed with you. Do you please them with sweet words, for the servants, when they face enemies, have not with them friends or wives—and so they are pleased, O Rāghava when they receive sufficient food and presents.

sn: अतो हृष्टजनाकीर्णां प्रस्थाप्य महतीं चमूम्। एक एव धनुष्पाणिर्गच्छ त्वं मधुनो वनम्।७।। यथा त्वां न प्रजानाति गच्छन्तं युद्धकाङ्क्षिणम्। लवणस्तु मधोः पुत्रस्तथा गच्छेरशङ्कितम्॥
en: O Śatrughna, having sent before a huge and well contended army do you proceed afterwards to Madhuvana. You should proceed so fearlessly that Madhu's son Lavaņa might not know that you were going for encounter.

sn: न तस्य मृत्युरन्योऽस्ति कश्चिद्धिपुरुषर्षभ। दर्शनं योऽभिगच्छेत स वध्यो लवणेन हि॥
en: O foremost of men, he shall not be slain by any other expedient than that I have acquainted yourself with. If he can perceive before, whoever that enemy might be, Lavana shall forsooth destroy him.

sn: स ग्रीष्म अपयाते तु वर्षारात्र उपागते। हन्यास्त्वं लवणं सौम्य स हि कालोऽस्य दुर्मतेः॥
en: When rains shall set in after the expiration of the present summer you should slay him for that is the proper time for destroying that viciousminded one.

sn: महर्षीस्तु पुरत्कृत्य प्रयान्तु तव सैनिकाः। यथा ग्रीष्मवशेषेण तरेयुर्जाह्नवीजलम्॥ तत्र स्थाप्य बलं सर्वं नदीतीरे समाहितः। अग्रतो धनुषा सार्धं गच्छ त्वं लघुविक्रम ॥
en: Let the soldiers only now proceed with ascetics before them; the summer has not as yet fully expired and this is the time, when they shall, without any trouble, be able to cross the Gangā. Afterwards having encamped your army on the other side of the Gangā you should alone proceed speedily with your bow.

sn: एवमुक्तस्तु रामेण शत्रुघ्नस्तान्महाबलान्। सेनामुख्यान्समानीय ततो वाक्यमुवाच ह॥ एते वो गणिता वासा यत्र तत्र निवत्स्यथ। स्थातव्यं चाविरोधेन यथा बाधा न कस्यचित्॥
en: Hearing those words of Rāma and summoning all his highly powerful and leading warriors Satrughna said "Do you all proceed and halt at those places which are well known to you. Do not oppress any body."

sn: तथा तांस्तु समाज्ञाप्य प्रस्थाप्य च महद्बलम्। कौसल्यां च सुमित्रां च कैकेयीं चाभ्यवादयत्।।१५
en: Having thus ordered the powerful warriors the highly powerful Śatrughna bowed to Kausalyā, Sumitrā and Kaikeyi.

sn: रामं प्रदक्षिणीकृत्य शिरसाभिप्रणम्य च। लक्ष्मणं भरतं चैव प्रणिपत्य कृताञ्जलिः॥ पुरोहितं वसिष्ठं च शत्रुघ्नः पयतात्मवान्। रामेण चाभ्यनुज्ञातः शत्रुघ्नः शत्रुतापनः। प्रदक्षिणमथो कृत्वा निर्जगाम महाबलः॥
en: Thereupon having circumambulated with folded hands Rāma, Lakşmaņa and Bharata he reverentially saluted the feet of the priests. And then with Rāma's permission and having gone round him the highly powerful Śatrughna issued out.

sn: निर्याप्य सेनामथ सोऽग्रतस्तदा गजेन्द्रवाजिप्रवरौघसंकुलाम्। उपास्यमानः स नरेन्द्रपार्श्वतः प्रतिप्रयातो रघुवंशवर्धनः॥
en: Having thus despatched before a huge army consisting of selected elephants and horses, Śatrughna, the enhancer of the glory of Raghu's race, took farewell from Rāma. And all showed him proper respect.

sn: प्रस्थाप्य च बलं सर्वं मासमात्रोषितः पथि। एक एवाशु शत्रुघ्नो जगाम त्वरितं तदा॥
en: Having thus despatched his army and waited at Ayodhya for a month Śatrughna, the slayer of enemies, proceeded alone.

sn: द्विरात्रमन्तरे शूर उष्य राघवनन्दनः। वाल्मीकेराश्रमं पुण्यमगच्छद्वासमुत्तमम्॥
en: Having spent two nights on his way he arrived at the holy and picturesque hermitage of the great ascetic Vālmīki.

sn: सोऽभिवाद्य महात्मानं वाल्मीकिं मुनिसत्तमम्। कृताञ्जलिरथो भूत्वा वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह॥
en: And having bowed to that high-souled Muni Vālmīki, he with folded palms, said thus.

sn: भगवन्वस्तुमिच्छामि गुरोः कृत्यादिहागतः। श्वः प्रभाते गमिष्यामि प्रतीची दारुणां दिशम्॥
en: "O illustrious Sir, I wish to wait here this day; I have come here for some business of our master Rāma. To-morrow morning I shall proceed to the dreadful West.”

sn: शत्रुघ्नस्य वचः श्रुत्वा प्रहस्य मुनिपुङ्गवः। प्रत्युवाच महात्मानं स्वागतं ते महायशः॥ स्वमाश्रममिदं सौम्य राघवाणां कुलस्य वै। आसनं पाद्यमयं च निर्विशङ्कः प्रतीच्छ मे॥
en: Hearing the words of the high-souled Śatrughna, Vālmīki, the foremost of ascetics, replied saying: “O you of great renown, do you wait here without any hesitation. O gentle one, this hermitage belongs to the descendants of the Raghu face. Do you fearlessly take your seat and water to wash your feet.”

sn: प्रतिगृह्य तदा पूजां फलमूलं च भोजनम्। भक्षयामास काकुत्स्थस्तृप्तिं च परमां गतः॥
en: Thereupon taking water to wash his feet and feeding upon fruits and roots Satrughna attained to great delight.

sn: स भुक्त्वा फलमूलं च महर्षि तमुवाच ह। पूर्वा यज्ञविभूतीयं कस्याश्रमसमीपतः।।।।।
en: After eating the fruits and roots he asked the great ascetic Vālmīki saying: “O great ascetic, to whom belong the articles of sacrifice in the east near this hermitage?”

sn: तत्तस्य भाषितं श्रुत्वा वाल्मीकिर्वाक्यमब्रवीत्। शत्रुघ्न शृणु यस्येदं बभूवायतनं पुरा ॥
en: Whereto Vālmīki replied “Satrughna, hear I shall tell you, whose sacrificial ground was this in the days of yore.

sn: युष्माकं पूर्वको राजा सौदासस्तस्य भूपतेः। पुत्रो वीर्यसहो नाम वीर्यवानतिधार्मिकः॥
en: There was a king by the name of Saudāsa, one of your ancestors. His son Vīryasaha was a highly powerful and pious king.

sn: स बाल एव सौदासो मृगयामुपचक्रमे। चञ्चूर्यमाणं ददृशे स शूरो राक्षसद्वयम्॥ शार्दूलरूपिणौ घोरौ मृगान्बहुसहस्रशः। भक्षमाणावसंतुष्टौ पर्याप्ति नैव जग्मतुः॥
en: The heroic Saudāsa was fond of hunting from his boyhood. Once on a time while a hunting, he espied two Rākṣasas in the forest. He had heard about them many times before: they were in the shape of tigers and of a dreadful figure and were not satisfied with devouring many thousand deer.

sn: स तु तौ राक्षसौ दृष्ट्वा निर्मूगं च वनं कृतम्। क्रोधेन महताविष्टो जधानैकं महेषुणा॥
en: King Saudāsa saw those two Rākşasas and found the forest divested of all creatures. And enraged in consequence thereof he slew one of them.

sn: विनिपात्य तमेकं तु सौदासः : पुरुषर्षभः। विज्वरो विगतामर्षो हतं रक्षो छुदैक्षत ॥ निरीक्षमाणं तं दृष्ट्वा सहायं तस्य रक्षसः। संतापमकरोद्धोरं सौदासं चेदमब्रवीत्॥ यस्मादनपराधं तं सहायं मम जनिवान्। तस्मात्तवापि पापिष्ठ प्रदास्यामि प्रतिक्रियाम्॥
en: Having slain him and here at ease, Saudasa, the foremost of men, began to eye that Rākşasas. His mate, greatly aggrieved, said to him. “O vicious one, you have, without any fault, siain my companion, I shall therefore mete out becoming punishment to you."

sn: एवमुक्त्वा तु तद्रक्षस्तत्रैवान्तरधीयत। कालपर्याययोगेन राजा मित्रसहोऽभवत्॥
en: Having said this the Rākşasa vanished therefrom. Thereupon in time the prince Mitrasaha became king.

sn: राजापि यजते यज्ञमस्याश्रमसमीपतः। अश्वमेधं महायज्ञं तं वसिष्ठोऽप्यपालयत्॥
en: Saudása engaged in celebrating a mighty horse-sacrifice in the vicinity of this hermitage. Vasiștha officiated as a priest at that sacrifice.

sn: तत्र यज्ञो महानासीद्बहुवर्षगणायुतः। समृद्धः परया लक्ष्म्या देवयज्ञसमोऽभवत्॥
en: It continued for many Ayuta years. For immense riches the sacrifice appeared like one performed by the celestials.

sn: अथावसाने यज्ञस्य पूर्ववैरमनुस्मरन्। वसिष्ठरूपी राजानमिति होवाच राक्षसः॥
en: Thereupon when the sacrifice was about to be finished the aforesaid Rākşasa, remembering his former enmity, assumed the shape of Vasiştha and said to the king Saudāsa.

sn: अद्य यज्ञावसानान्ते सामिष भोजनं मम। दीयतामिति शीघ्रं वै नात्र कार्या विचारणा॥
en: O king, today the sacrifice shall end; do therefore, without any delay, feed me with meat.

sn: तच्छ्रुत्वा व्याहृतं वाक्यं रक्षसा ब्रह्मरूपिणा। सूदान्संस्कारकुशलानुवाच पृथिवीपतिः॥
en: Hearing the words of the Rākşasa in the guise of a Brāhmaṇa, the king ordered his expert cooks, saying.

sn: हविष्यं सामिषं स्वादु यथा भवति भोजनम्। तथा कुरुत शीघ्रं वै परितुष्येद्यथा गुरुः॥
en: "Do you soon prepare such dishes of meat as may satisfy my preceptor Vasiştha."

sn: शासनात्पार्थिवेन्द्रस्य सूदः संभ्रान्तमानसः। तच्च रक्षः पुनस्तत्र सूदवेषमथाकरोत्॥ स मानुषमयो मांसं पार्थिवाय न्यवेदयत्। इदं स्वादु हविष्यं च सामिषं चानमाहृतम्॥ स भोजनं वसिष्ठाय पत्न्या सार्धमुपाहरत्। मदयन्त्या नरश्रेष्ठ सामिषं रक्षसा हृतम्॥ ज्ञात्वा तदामिषं विप्रो मानुषं भोजनागतम्। क्रोधेन महताविष्टो व्याहर्तुमुपचक्रमे॥
en: Having been ordered by the king the cooks reverentially went away and the Rākşasas assuming their shape brought before the king dishes. The king and queen Madayantſ offered those dishes to the ascetic Vasistha, who, after being treated to them, perceived that there was human flesh, terribly enraged and said.

sn: यस्मात्त्वं भोजनं राजन्ममैतद्दातुमिच्छसि। तस्माद्भोजनमेतत्ते भविष्यति न संशयः॥
en: "O king, let this be your food which you have offered me; this shall not prove otherwise."

sn: ततः क्रुद्धस्तु सौदासस्तोयं जग्राह पाणिना। वसिष्ठं शप्तुमारेभे भार्या चैनमवारयत्॥ राजन्प्रभुर्यतोऽस्माकं वसिष्ठो भगवानृपिः। प्रतिशप्तुं न शक्तस्त्वं देवतुल्यं पुरोधसम्॥
en: Being enraged on hearing it the king Saudāsa took water in his palms and was about to imprecate Vasiștha, when his queen, preventing him said. “O king, the illustrious great ascetic Vasiştha is our preceptor and priest and so you should not imprecate him."

sn: ततः क्रोधमयं तोयं तेजोबलसमन्वितम्। व्यसर्जयत धर्मात्मा ततः पादौ सिषेच च॥ तेनास्य राज्ञस्तौ पादौ तदा कल्माषतां गतौ। तदाप्रभृति राजासौ सौदासः सुमहायशाः॥ कल्माषपादः संवृत्तः ख्यातश्चैव तथा नृपः।
en: Hearing those words of his queen, the king Saudāsa, threw off that powerful water on his own feet which at once became dark. From that time the illustrious king Saudása became also known by the name of Kalmāşapāda.

sn: स राजा सह पत्न्या वै प्रणिपत्य मुहुर्मुहुः। पुनर्वसिष्ठं प्रोवाच यदुक्तं ब्रह्मरूपिणा॥
en: Thereupon the king with his spouse again and again bowed to Vasistha's feet and informed him of what the Rākşasa had done under the guise of a Brāhmana.

sn: तच्छ्रुत्वा पार्थिवेन्द्रस्य रक्षसा विकृतं च तत्। पुनः प्रोवाच राजानं वसिष्ठः पुरुषर्षभम्॥ मया रोषपरीतेन यदिदं व्याहृतं वचः। नैतच्छक्यं वृथा कर्तुं प्रदास्यामि च ते वरम्॥ कालो द्वादश वर्षाणि शापस्यान्तो भविष्यति। मत्प्रासादाच्च राजेन्द्र अतीतं न स्मरिष्यसि॥
en: Hearing the words of the king and being apprised that this wife vile act had been done by the Rākşasa, Vasiștha said, “O king, even what I have said angrily shall not prove futile. However I confer upon you this boon that after twelve years you shall be freed from this curse, and by my favour you shall cherish no recollection of your condition extending ever those twelve years."

sn: एवं स राजा तं शापमुपभुज्यारिसूदनः। प्रतिलेभे पुना राज्यं प्रजाश्चैवान्वपालयत्॥
en: Having thus suffered the consequences of the curse, Saudasa, the slayer of enemies, again obtained his kingdom an governed his subjects.

sn: तस्य कल्माषपादस्य यज्ञस्यायतनं शुभम्। आश्रमस्य समीपेऽस्मिन्यन्मां पृच्छसि राघव॥
en: O descendant of Raghu, the sacrificial ground of which you have asked me, belongs to the king Saudasa.

sn: तस्य तां पार्थिवेन्द्रस्य कथां श्रुत्वा सुदारुणाम्। विवेश पर्णशालायां महर्षिमभिवाद्य च॥
en: Having thus heard the dreadful; story of the king Saudāsa and saluted the ascetic Vālmīki, Śatrughna entered a thatched cottage.

sn: यामेव रात्रि शत्रुघ्नः पर्णशालां समाविशत्। तामेव रात्रि सीतापि प्रसूता दारकद्वयम्॥
en: On the same night ſatrughna housed himself in a thatched cottage Sitā gave birth to twin sons.

sn: ततोऽर्धरात्रसमये बालका मुनिदारकाः। वाल्मीके प्रियमाचख्युः सीतायाः प्रसवं शुभम्॥ भगवरामपत्नी सा प्रसूता दारकद्वयम्। ततो रक्षां महातेजः कुरु भूतविनाशिनीम्॥
en: In the midnight the Muni boys came to Vālmīki and communicated to him this auspicious intelligence, saying. “O illustrious Sir, the beloved spouse of Rāma has given birth to two sons; do you so protect them that evil spirits not injure them."

sn: तेषां तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा महर्षिः समुपागमत्। बालचन्द्रप्रतीकाशौ देवपुत्रौ महौजसौ॥ जगाम तत्र हृष्टात्मा ददर्श च कुमारको। भूतघ्नीं चाकरोत्ताभ्यां रक्षा रक्षोविनाशिनीम्॥
en: Hearing those words the highly effulgent Vālmīki went there and attained to great on beholding those two highly effulgent sons, resembling the newly risen sun and the celestials. Thereupon he made arrangements against the oppression of ghosts and goblins.

sn: कुशमुष्टिमुपादाय लवं चैव तु स द्विजः। वाल्मीकिः प्रददौ ताभ्यां रक्षां भूतविनाशिनीम्॥
en: Thereupon taking Kuśa (the upper part of the grass) and Lava (the lower part) the great ascetic Vālmīki made those arrangements.

sn: यस्तयोः पूर्वजो जातः स कुशैर्मन्त्रसत्कृतैः। निर्मार्जनीयस्तु तदा कुश इत्यस्य नाम तत्॥ यश्चावरो भवेत्ताभ्यां लवेन सुसमाहितः। निर्मार्जनीयो वृद्धाभिलवेति च स नामतः॥ एवं कुशलवौ नाम्ना तावुभौ यमजातको। मत्कृताभ्यां च नामभ्यां ख्यातियुक्तौ भविष्यतः॥
en: And giving Kuśa sanctified by Mantras to the hands of elderly women he said, “do you rub the person of the elder boy with these”; and giving them Lava he said “do you rub the person of the younger brother with this. And according to this I shall name the first Son Kuśa and the second Lava; and by those names they shall be celebrated on earth.”

sn: तां रक्षां जगृहुस्तां च मुनिहस्तात्समाहिताः। अकुर्वश्च ततो रक्षा तयोविगतकल्मषाः॥ तथा तां क्रियमाणां च वृद्धाभिर्गोत्रनाम च।
en: Thereupon reverentially taking from the hands of Vālmīki and Kuśa Lava, the means of protection, the elderly ladies engaged in guarding them.

sn: संकीर्तनं च रामस्य सीतायाः प्रसवौ शुभौ॥ अर्धरात्रे तु शत्रुघ्नः शुश्राव सुमहत्प्रियम्। पर्णशालां ततो गत्वा मातर्दिष्ट्येति चाब्रवीत्॥
en: Hearing the Sītā without any trouble had given birth to two sons and elderly female ascetics had been engaged in protecting them and bearing the chanting of Råma's glories in the midnight, Satrughna thought within himself.

sn: तदा तस्य प्रहृष्टस्य शत्रुघ्नस्य महात्मनः। व्यतीता वार्षिकी रात्रिः श्रावणी लघुविक्रमा॥
en: "Blessed it is that Sītā has given birth to two sons.” And with this joy the live long night of Śrāvaņa passed away in no time.

sn: प्रभाते सुमहावीर्यः कृत्वा पौर्वाहिणकी क्रियाम्। मुनि प्राञ्जलिरामन्त्र्य ययौ पश्चान्मुखः पुनः॥
en: Having performed the morning rites after the expiration of the night and taken farewell from the ascetic Vālmīki, Lakşmaņa proceeded towards the west.

sn: स गत्वा यमुनातीरं सप्तरात्रोषितः पथि। ऋषीणां पुण्यकीर्तीनामाश्रमे वासमभ्ययात्॥
en: And having spent seven nights he at last arrived at the hermitage of the pious Rși living on the banks of the Yamuna.

sn: स तत्र मुनिभिः सार्धं भार्गवप्रमुखैर्नृपः। कथाभिरभिरूपाभिर्वासं चक्रे महायशाः॥ स काञ्चनाद्यैर्मुनिभिः समेतै रघुप्रवीरो रजनी तदानीम् कथाप्रकारैर्बहुभिर्महात्मा विरामयामास नरेन्द्रसूनुः।।१७।
en: Taking shelter there be engaged in pleasant conversation with Cyavana (son of Bhrgu), and other ascetics. Having remained there for the night and talked with those ascetics the highsouled, heroic Raghu prince Śatrughna was greatly delighted.

sn: अथ रात्र्यां प्रवृत्तायां शत्रुघ्नो भृगुनन्दनम्। पप्रच्छ च्यवनं विप्रं लवणस्य यथाबलम्॥ शूलस्य च बलं ब्रह्मन्के च पूर्वं विनाशिताः। अनेन शूलमुख्येन द्वन्द्वयुद्धमुपागताः॥
en: Thereupon when the night set in Śatrughna accosted Bhrgu's son Cyavana saying, “O Brāhmaṇa how powerful is Lavaņa? And what is the strength of his dart? What persons before had been destroyed by this dart in conflict?”

sn: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा शत्रुघ्नस्य महात्मनः। प्रत्युवाच महातेजाश्च्यवनो रघुनन्दनम्॥
en: Hearing the words of the high-souled descendant of Raghu, Satrughna, the highly effulgent Cyavana replied saying.

sn: असंख्येयानि कर्माणि यान्यस्य रघुनन्दन। इक्ष्वाकुवंशप्रभवे यद्वृत्तं तच्छृणुष्व मे॥
en: O descendant of Raghu, Lavaņa has accomplished many works by this dart; among them, hear, what Māndhāta, born in the race of Iksawaku, did.

sn: अयोध्यायां पुरा राजा युवनाश्वसुतो बली। मांधाता इति विख्यातस्त्रिषु लोकेषु वीर्यवान्॥
en: The early king of Ayodhyā was known over the three worlds under the name of Māndhātā. He was the son of Yuvanāśva, highly powerful and strong.

sn: स कृत्वा पृथिवीं कृत्स्ना शासने पृथिवीपतिः। सुरलोकमितो जेतुमुद्योगमकरोनृपः॥
en: Having brought the whole world under his subjection the king Māndhātā engaged in the conquest of the celestial region.

sn: इन्द्रस्य च भयं तीव्र सुराणां च महात्मनाम्। मांधातरि कृतोद्योगे देवलोकजिगीषया॥
en: He having been engaged in making preparations to conquer the world of gods—the celestial chief Indra with other immortals was greatly terrified.

sn: अर्धासनेन शक्रस्य राज्यार्धेन च पार्थिवः। वन्द्यमानः सुरगणैः प्रतिज्ञामध्यरोहत।।।। तस्य पापमभिप्रायं विदित्वा पाकशासनः। सान्त्वपूर्वमिदं वाक्यमुवाच युवनाश्वजम्॥
en: With this promise, the king Mândhāta went into the celestial region that he would occupy the half of Indra's throne and kingdom and the celestials would adore him. Being apprised of this vicious intention of his, Indra, the slayer of Pāka, consoled him in sweet words, saying.

sn: राजा त्वं मानुषे लोके न तावत्पुरुषर्षभ। अकृत्वा पृथिवीं वश्यां देवराज्यमिहेच्छसि॥
en: O foremost of men, even in the land of men, you have not been able to become the real king. Without perfectly subjugating the earth how do you wish to lord over the celestial kingdom?

sn: यदि वीर समग्रा ते मेदिनी निखिला वशे। देवराज्यं कुरुष्वेह सभृत्यबलवाहनः॥
en: If the whole world is under your subjection, O hero, be you, with the whole host of your servants and soldiers, installed on the celestial throne.

sn: इन्द्रमेवं ब्रुवाणं तं मांधाता वाक्यमब्रवीत्। क्व मे शक्र प्रतिहतं शासनं पृथिवीतले॥
en: Indra having said this, the high-souled Māndhātā replies: O Sakra, who on this earth, has disobeyed my commands.?

sn: तमुवाच सहस्राक्षो लवणो नाम राक्षसः। मधुपुत्रो मधुवने न तेऽऽज्ञां कुरुतेऽनघ॥
en: Whereto Indra replied o sinless one, the night-ranger, Lavana, Madhu's son, living in Madhuvana, is not under your control.

sn: तच्छुत्वा विप्रियं घोरं सहस्राक्षेण भाषितम्। वीडितोऽवाङ्मुखो राजा व्याहतुं न शशाक ह॥
en: Hearing those dreadful and unpleasant words from Indra, the king lowered his head in shame and became silent.

sn: आमन्त्र्य तु सहस्राक्षं प्रायात्किचिदवाङ्मुखः। पुनरेवागमच्छीमानिमं लोकं नरेश्वरः॥ स कृत्वा हृदयेऽमर्ष सभृत्यबलवाहनः। आजगाम मधोः पुत्रं वशे कर्तुमरिंदमः॥
en: Thereupon, having welcomed Indra in that way, he left there and returned earth. O slayer of enemies, with an angry heart, army and conveyance he went to subjugate Madhu's son Lavaņa and sent an emissary inviting him to battle.

sn: स काङ्खमाणो लवणं युद्धाय पुरुषर्षभः। दूतं संप्रेषयामास सकाशं लवणस्य सः॥ स गत्वा विप्रियाण्याह बहूनि मधुनः सुतम्। वदन्तमेवं तं दूतं भक्षयामास राक्षसः॥
en: The ambassador, having gone there, addressed many unpleasant words to Lavaņa and the nightranger devoured him.

sn: चिरायमाणे दूते तु राजा क्रोधसमन्वितः। अर्दयामास तद्रक्षः शरवृष्ट्या समन्ततः॥
en: On the other hand finding the delay of his return the king Māndhāta, enraged, began to assail the Raksasa Lavaņa with arrows from all sides.

sn: ततः प्रहस्य तद्रक्षः शूलं जग्राह पाणिना। वधाय सानुबन्धस्य मुमोचायुधमुत्तमम्॥
en: Laughing wild Lavaņa took up the dart in his hand and discharged it to destroy the king with his followers.

sn: तच्छूलं दीप्यमानं तु सभृत्यबलवाहनम्। भस्मीकृत्वा नृपं भूमौ लवणस्यागमत्करम्॥
en: Thereupon growing powerful the dart reduced the king with his servants and army into ashes and returned to Lavaņa.

sn: एवं स राजा सुमहान्हतः सबलवाहनः। शूलस्य तु बलं सौम्य अप्रमेयमनुत्तमम्॥
en: In this wise the high-souled king Māndhāta, with his huge army, was slain. O gentle hero, incomparable and great is the strength of the dart..

sn: श्वः प्रभाते तु लवणं वधिष्यसि न संशयः। अगृहीतायुधं क्षिप्रं ध्रुवो हि विजयस्तव॥
en: Forsooth you shall slay Lavaņa next morning. Certain is your victory if Lavana cannot take up his dart.

sn: लोकानां स्वस्ति चैवं स्यात्कृते कर्मणि च त्वया। एतत्ते सर्वमाख्यातं लवणस्य दुरात्मनः॥ शूलस्य च बलं घोरमप्रमेयं नरर्षभ। विनाशश्चैव मांधातुर्यत्नेनाभूच्च पार्थिव ॥
en: People shall be at ease if you can bring about the destruction of Lavaņa. O foremost of men, I shall then describe to you the incomparable and dreadful prowess of the vicious-souled Lavaņa and his dart. O king, with great exertions did Lavaņa slay Māndhāta and not easily.

sn: त्वं श्वः प्रभाते लवणं महात्मन् वधिष्यसे नात्र तु संशयो मे। शूलं विना निर्गतमामिषार्थे ध्रुवो जयस्ते भविता नरेन्द्र॥
en: O high-minded one, next morning you shall surely destroy Lavaņa. He shall issue our for flesh without taking his dart. And at that time, O lord of man, you shall, forsooth, be crowned with victory.

sn: कथां कथयतस्तेषां जयं चाकाङ्क्षतां शुभम्। व्यतीता रजनी शीघ्रं शत्रुघ्नस्य महात्मनः॥
en: They being thus engaged in conversation regarding his achieving victory without any danger Satrughna in no time passed the night.

sn: ततः प्रभाते विमले तस्मिन्काले स राक्षसः। निर्गतस्तु पुराद्वीरो भक्ष्याहारप्रचोदितः॥
en: The clear morning having arrived, that time the heroic Lavana issued out of his city to collect food.

sn: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे वीर उत्तीर्य यमुना नदीम्। ती। मधुपुरद्वारि धनुष्पाणिरतिष्ठत॥
en: In the meantime having crossed the river Yamunā, the heroic Satrughna, with bow in his hands, stood at the gate of Madhu's city.

sn: ततोऽर्धदिवसे प्राप्ते क्रूरकर्मा स राक्षसः। आगच्छद्बहुसाहस्रं प्राणिनां भारमुद्वहन्।॥ ततो ददर्श शत्रुघ्नं स्थितं द्वारि धृतायुधम्। तमुवाच किमनेन करिष्यसि॥ ततो रक्षः ईदृशानां सहस्राणि सायुधानां नराधम। भक्षितानि मया रोषात्कालेनानुगतो ह्यसि॥
en: There upon returning in the noon with many thousand animals, the night-ranger Lavana, of dreadful actions, espied Satrughna standing at the gate with a weapon in his hand. Thereupon he said: What shall you do with this weapon? O vile wight, enraged I have devoured many thousand persons holding weapons like you. I now perceive you have also been possessed by Kala.

sn: आहारश्चाप्यसंपूर्णो ममायं पुरुषाधम। स्वयं प्रविष्टोऽद्य मुखं कथमासाद्य दुर्मते॥
en: O vile man, I am fully fed. How shall you, of your own accord, enter into my mouth?

sn: तस्यैवं भाषमाणस्य हसतश्च मुहुर्मुहुः। शत्रुघ्नो वीर्यसंपन्नो रोषादश्रूण्यासृजत्॥
en: Lavaņa having said this again and again laughing the great hero Satrughna shed tears in anger.

sn: तस्य रोषाभिभूतस्य शत्रुघ्नस्य महात्मनः। तेजोमया मरीच्यस्तु सर्वगात्रैर्विनिष्पतन्॥
en: The high-minded Śatrughna being beside himself with rage, from all his person issued burning lustre.

sn: उवाच च सुसंक्रुद्धः शत्रुघ्नः स निशाचरम्। योद्धमिच्छामि दुर्बुद्धेः द्वन्द्वयुद्धं त्वया सह ॥
en: Greatly enraged he said to the night-ranger O you of a vicious intellect, I wish to enter into a dual encounter with you.

sn: पुत्रो दशरथस्याहं भ्राता रामस्य धीमतः। शत्रुघ्नो नाम शत्रुघ्नो वधाकाङ्क्षी तवागतः॥
en: I am the son of the great king Dasaratha, brother of the intelligent Rāma and my name is Satrughna. I slay all my enemies and have come here to destroy you.

sn: तस्य मे युद्धकामस्य द्वन्द्वयुद्धं प्रदीयताम्। शस्त्वं सर्वभूतानां न मे जीवन्गमिष्यसि॥
en: I wish now to fight with you-do you enter into a dual conflict. You are the enemy of all animals. You shall not be able to survive at my hands.

sn: तस्मिंस्तथा ब्रुवाणे तु राक्षसः प्रहसन्निव। प्रत्युवाच नरश्रेष्ठं दिष्ट्या प्राप्तोऽसि दुर्मते॥
en: He having said this, the Rākṣasa, laughing aloud, replied to that foremost of men:-Your understanding is bewildered. By the influence of destiny you have come under my control.

sn: मम मोतृष्वसुर्धाता रावणो नाम राक्षसः। हतो रामेण दुर्बुद्धे स्त्रीहेतोः पुरुषाधम॥
en: The Räksasa Rāvana was the brother of my aunts. O you of vicious understanding, O vile wight, it is for his wife that Rāma did slay him.

sn: तच्च सर्वं मया क्षान्तं रावणस्य कुलक्षयम्। अवज्ञा पुरतः कृत्वा मया यूयं विशेषतः॥
en: It is out of hatred that I have tolerated the destruction of Rāvana's family and have pardoned you all.

sn: निहताश्च हि ते सर्वे परिभूतास्तृणं यथा। भूताश्चैव भविष्याश्च यूयं च पुरुषाधमाः॥
en: You are all vile men; I have slain and defeated all of your family that have passed away and shall destroy all that are living and shall come into existence.

sn: तस्य ते युद्धकामस्य युद्धं दास्यामि दुर्मते। तिष्ठ त्वं च मुहूर्त तु यावदायुधमानये॥
en: O you of vicious intellect, if you wish I shall fight with you. Do you wait here so long I do not bring my weapon.

sn: ईप्सितं यादृशं तुभ्यं सज्जये यावदायुधन्। तमुवाचाशु शत्रुघ्नः क्व मे जीवन्गमिष्यसि॥
en: Do you remain here as long as I with that shall not kill you. Where to Satrughna immediately replied Where shall you go while I am alive?

sn: स्वयमेवागतः शत्रुर्न मोक्तव्यः कृतात्मना। यो हि विक्लवया बुद्ध्या प्रसरं शत्रवे दिशेत्। स हतो मन्दबुद्धिः स्याद्यथा कापुरुषस्तथा॥
en: The practical men should never let off the enemies who come out of their own accord. He, who invite an enemy into battle under the influence of perverted understanding, is slain like a coward.

sn: तस्मात्सुदृष्टं कुरु जीवलोकं शरैः शितैस्त्वां विविधैर्नयामि। यमस्य गेहाभिमुखं हि पापं रिपुं त्रिलोकस्य च राघवस्य॥
en: Do you behold this world of creatures to your hearts' content for I shall by various sharp weapons despatch you to Yama's abode who is the enemy of the three worlds and Rāghava.

sn: तच्छुत्वा भाषितं तस्य शत्रुघ्नस्य महात्मनः। क्रोधमाहारयत्चीव्र तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति चाब्रवीत्॥
en: Hearing the words of the high-souled Śatrughna Lavaņa was greatly enraged and again and again asked him to wait.

sn: पाणौ पाणिं स निष्पिष्य दन्तान्कटकटाय्य च। लवणो रघुशार्दूलमाह्वयामास चासकृत्॥
en: Clashing his hands and grinding his teeth he invited that foremost of Raghus to fight.

sn: तं ब्रुवाण तथा वाक्यं लवणं घोरदर्शनम्। शत्रुघ्नो देवशत्रुघ्न इदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: And Satrughna, the slayer of celestial's enemies, said to the dreadful Lavaņa, giving vent to those words.

sn: शत्रुघ्नो न तदा जातो यदान्ये निर्जितास्त्वया। तदद्य बाणाभिहतो व्रज त्वं यमसादनम्॥
en: Śatrughna was not born when you did defeat other kings; do you therefore proceed to Death's abode being assailed by shafts.

sn: ऋषयोऽप्यद्य पापात्मन्मया त्वां निहतं रणे। पश्यन्तु विप्रा विद्वांसस्त्रिदशा इव रावणम्॥
en: O you of a vicious soul, as did the celestials behold Rāvana slain so shall the Rșis and learned Brāhmaṇas behold you, destroyed by me.

sn: त्वयि मद्वाणनिर्दग्धे पतितेऽद्य निशाचरे। पुरे जनपदे चापि क्षेममेव भविष्यति॥
en: O Rākşasa, forsooth shall good crown cities and villages when you shall fall down brunt by my arrow.

sn: अद्य मदाहुनिष्क्रान्तः शरो वज्रनिभाननः। प्रवेक्ष्यते ते हृदयं पद्ममंशुरिवार्कजः॥
en: As the rays of the sun enter into lotus so shall arrows, hard as lightning, discharged by my hands, shall enter into your heart.

sn: एवमुक्तो महावृक्षं लवणः क्रोधमूर्च्छितः। शत्रुघ्नोरसि चिक्षेप स च तं शतधाच्छिनत्॥
en: Being beside himself with ire on hearing those words of Śatrughna, Lavaņa threw a huge tree against his breast. And ſatrughna too sundered it into a hundred pieces.

sn: तदृष्ट्वा विफलं कर्म राक्षसः पुनरेव तु। पादपान्सुबहूगृह्य शत्रुघ्नायासृजद्बली॥ शत्रुघ्नश्चापि तेजस्वी वृक्षानापततो बहून्। त्रिभिश्चतुर्भिरेकैकं चिच्छेद नतपर्वभिः॥
en: Beholding his own action baffled the Rākşasa again took up many trees and hurled them at Śatrughna, who, with three or four hundred bent arrow, cut them all, one by one, into pieces.

sn: ततो बाणमयं वर्षं व्यसृजद्राक्षसोपरि। शत्रुघ्नो वीर्यसंपन्नो विव्यथे न स राक्षसः॥
en: Thereupon when the powerful Satrughna assailed him with arrows the Rākşasa was not the least pained.

sn: ततः प्रहस्य लवणो वृक्षमुद्यम्य वीर्यवान्। शिरस्यभ्यहनच्छूरं स्रस्ताङ्गः स मुमोह वै॥
en: Rather laughing aloud the valiant Räksasa uprooted a tree and struck him with that on the head. With that stroke he was wounded and slain.

sn: तस्मिन्निपतिते वीरे हाहाकारो महानभूत्। ऋषीणां देवसङ्घानां गन्धर्वाप्सरसां तथा॥
en: And that hero falling there arose a terrible uproar among the Rșis, celestials, Gandharvas and Apsarās.

sn: तमवज्ञाय तु हतं शत्रुघ्नं भुवि पातितम्। रक्षो लब्धान्तरमपि न विवेश स्वमालयम्॥ नापि शूलं प्रजग्राह तं दृष्ट्वा भुवि पातितम्। ततो हत इति ज्ञात्वा तान्भक्षान्समुदावहत्॥
en: There upon considering Śatrughna slain the night-ranger did not enter his house albeit he got the opportunity; and moreover beholding him fallen and destroyed he did not take up his dart. He then began to carry his collected food.

sn: मुहूर्ताल्लब्धसंज्ञस्तु पुनस्तस्थौ धृतायुधः। शत्रुघ्नो वै पुरद्वारि ऋषिभिः संप्रपूजितः॥
en: Regaining his sense within a moment, Śatrughna, with a weapon in his hand, stood at the city gate and the Rșis began to praise him.

sn: ततो दिव्यममोघं तं जग्राह शरमुत्तमम्। ज्वलन्तं तेजसा घोरं पूरयन्तं दिशो दश॥
en: There upon, he having taken up an excellent arrow of unfailing aim the ten quarters were filled with its native brilliance.

sn: वज्राननं वज्रवेगं मेरुमन्दरसंनिभम्। नतं पर्वसु सर्वेषु संयुगेष्वपराजितम्॥
en: Its face was like lightning and its velocity the same and it looked like Meru and Mandāra; its joints were all bent. None could defeat it in battle.

sn: असृक्चन्दनदिग्धाङ्गं चारुपत्रं पतत्रिणम्। दानवेन्द्राचलेन्द्राणामसुराणां च दारुणम्॥ तं दीप्तमिव कालाग्निं युगान्ते समुपस्थितम्। दृष्ट्वा सर्वाणि भूतानि परित्रासमुपागमन्॥
en: It was pasted with red sandal resembling blood and its feathers were beautiful. Beholding that dart like to the fire of dissolution, and dreadful to lords of Dānavas, mountains and Asuras, the creatures were greatly terrified.

sn: सदेवासुरगन्धर्वं मुनिभिः साप्सरोगणम्। जगद्धिसर्वमस्वस्थं पितामहमुपस्थितम्॥ ऊचुश्च देवदेवेशं वरदं प्रपितामहम्। देवानां भयसंमोहो लोकानां संक्षयं प्रति ॥
en: What more, being disturbed, the celestials, Asuras, Gandharvas, saints and Apsarās and all other creatures of the world approached the Great Patriarch, the conferrer of boons and said. The fear of the celestials and the destruction of the creatures has arrived.

sn: तेषां तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा ब्रह्मा लोकपितामहः। भयकारणमाचष्ट देवानामभयंकरः॥ उवाच मधुरां वाणीं शृणुध्वं सर्वदेवताः। वधाय लवणस्याजौ शरः शत्रुघ्नदारितः॥
en: Hearing those words the Patriarch Brahmă replied Although it is a source of great fear still it is not dreadful to the celestials. There upon with sweet accents he said:-Hear, O you celestials, ſatrughna has taken up this arrow for the destruction of Pavana.

sn: तेजसा तस्य संमूढाः सर्वे स्मः सुरसत्तमाः। एषो पूर्वस्य देवस्य लोककर्तुः सनातनः॥ शरस्तेजोमयो वत्सा येन वै भयमागतम्। एष वै कैटभस्यार्थे मधुनश्च महाशरः॥ सृष्टो महात्मना तेन वधार्थे दैत्ययोस्तयोः।
en: By the energy thereof we have all been overwhelmed. This effulgent, ever existing arrow was made by the Primeval, Deity, Vis nu-the lord of creatures. My children, the burning arrow, of which you are afraid, was made by the high-minded Vişņu for slaying the demons Madhu and Kaitabha.

sn: एक एव प्रजानाति विष्णुस्तेजोमयं शरम् ॥ एषा एव तनुः पूर्वा विष्णोस्तस्य महात्मनः। इतो गच्छत पश्यध्वं वध्यमानं महात्मना॥ रामानुजेन वीरेण लवणं राक्षसोत्तमम्।
en: Vişņu alone is cognisant of its energy. This Śatrughna is the first portion of Vişnu's person; do you all go hence and behold the destruction of the foremost Raksasa, Lavana, by the highsouled, heroic Satrughna, the younger brother of Rama.

sn: तस्य ते देवदेवस्य निशम्य वचनं सुराः।२९।। आजग्मुर्यत्र युध्येते शत्रुघ्नलवणावुभौ। तं शरं दिव्यसंकाशं शत्रुघ्नकरधारितम्॥ ददृशुः सर्वभूतानि युगान्ताग्निमिवोत्थितम्।
en: Hearing the words of the Patriarch Brahmă, the celestials arrived at the battle-field of Šatrughna and Lavana and saw that the arrow, held by Satrughna's hands, was burning like the fire of dissolution.

sn: आकाशमावृतं दृष्ट्वा देवैर्हि रघुनन्दनः॥ सिंहनादं भृशं कृत्वा ददर्श लवणं पुनः। आहूतश्च पुनस्तेन शत्रुघ्नेन महात्मना ॥ लवणः क्रोधसंयुक्तो युद्धाय समुपस्थितः।
en: Beholding the welkin covered by the celestials, Satrughna, the descendant of Raghu, emitting leonine roars, again and again looked towards Lavaņa. And being again excited by the high-souled Śatrughna and enraged Lavaņa arrived for encounter.

sn: आकर्णात्स विकृष्याथ तद्धनुर्धन्विनां वरः॥ स मुमोच महाबाणं लवणस्य महोरसि। उरस्तस्य विदार्यासु प्रविवेश रसातलम्॥ गत्वा रसातलं दिव्यः शरो विबुधपूजितः। पुनरेवागमत्तर्णमिक्ष्वाकुकुलनन्दनम्॥
en: There upon expanding his bow up to ears, Satrughna, the the most accomplished archer, discharged his arrow against the spacious breast of Lavaņa. And piercing his heart that arrow entered speedily into Rasātala and having entered Rasātala that arrow, honoured by the celestials, again came to the descendant of Raghu.

sn: शत्रुघ्नशरनिर्भिन्नो लवणः स निशाचरः। पपात सहसा भूमौ वज्राहत इवाचलः॥
en: And being pierced by that shaft the nightranger Lavaņa fell down on earth like a mountain clapped by a thunder-bolt.

sn: तच्च शूलं महद्दिव्यं हते लवणराक्षसे। पश्यतां सर्वदेवानां रुद्रस्य वशमन्वगात्॥
en: The Rākşasa being slain that celestial, huge arrow came into the possession of Rudra before the gods.

sn: एकेषुपातेन भयं निपात्य लोकत्रयस्यास्य रघुप्रवीरः। स्तमः प्रणुद्येव सहस्ररश्मिः॥
en: Having removed the fear of the three worlds with one shaft, that heroic Raghu, Satrughnayounger brother of Lakşmaņa, holding excellent bow and arrow, appeared like the Sun of thousand rays removing darkness.

sn: ततो हि देवा ऋषिपन्नगाश्च प्रपूजिरे ह्यप्सरसश्च सर्वाः स्त्यक्त्वा भयं सर्प इव प्रशान्तः॥
en: There upon chanting the glories of Satrughna, the celestials, Rşis, Pannagas, Apsarās, said “O son of Dasaratha, it is really fortunate, that you, renouncing fear, have acquired victory, and that the Rākṣasa Lavaņa has been vanquished like a serpent."

sn: हते तु लवणे देवाः सेन्द्राः साग्निपुरोगमाः। ऊचुः सुमधुरां वाणीं शत्रुघ्नं शत्रुतापनम्॥
en: Lavana being slain the celestials headed by Agni and Indra said in sweet accents to Śatrughna the represser of enemies.

sn: दिष्ट्या ते विजयो वत्स दिष्ट्या लवणराक्षसः। हतः पुरुषशार्दूल वरं वरय सुव्रत।२।।
en: O child, fortunate it is that you have been crowned with success after slaying the Rākṣasa Lavaņa. Do you, therefore, O foremost of men, O you of firm vows, accept boons.

sn: वरदास्तु महाबाहो सर्व एव समागताः। विजयाकाङ्क्षिणस्तुभ्यममोघं दर्शनं हि नः॥
en: O you having long arms, all those who can confer boons have arrived here; they all wish for your victory; seeing us does not go without fruits.

sn: देवानां भाषितं श्रुत्वा शूरो मूर्ध्नि कृताञ्जलिः। प्रत्युवाच महाबाहुः शत्रुघ्नः प्रयतात्मवान्॥
en: Hearing the words of the celestials the largearmed and self-controlled Satrughna placed his hands on his head and said.

sn: इयं मधुपुरी रम्या मधुरा देवनिर्मिता। निवेशं प्राप्नुयाच्छीघ्रमेष मेऽस्तु वरः परः॥
en: Let this picturesque and charming city of Madhu, built by the celestials, by my capital; this is the only excellent boon I can beg.

sn: तं देवाः प्रीतमनसो बाढमित्येव राघवम्। भविष्यति पुरी रम्या शूरसेना न संशयः॥
en: The celestials, with a delighted heart, said to the descendant of Raghu.-Your desire shall be fulfilled and forsooth shall your city be turned into a picturesque capital under the name of Surasena.

sn: ते तथोक्त्वा महात्मानो दिवमारुरुहुस्तदा। शत्रुघ्नोऽपि महातेजास्तां सेनां समुपानयत्॥
en: The high-souled celestials having ascended the welkin saying this, the highly effulgent Śatrughna brought the soldiers there, that were encamped on the banks of the Gangā.

sn: सा सेना शीघ्रमागच्छच्छुत्वा शत्रुघ्नशासनम्। निवेशनं च शत्रुघ्नः श्रावणेन समारभत्॥
en: When the soldiers arrived there on hearing the commands of Satrughna he engaged in making encampments in the month of Śrāvan.

sn: स पुरा दिव्यसंकाशो वर्षे द्वादशमे शुभे। निविष्टः शूरसेनानां विषयश्चाकुतोभयः॥ क्षेत्राणि सस्ययुक्तानि काले वर्षति वासवः। अरोगवीरपुरुषा शत्रुघ्नभुजपालिता ॥
en: In this wise the fearlessness of the celestial host, taking the shape of a country, that beautiful and picturesque city was reared in the course of twelve years. All the fields there were filled with crops and Indra began to pour showers in due seasons. And being protected by the strength of Śatrughna's arms all men there became valiant and were freed from deseases.

sn: अर्धचन्द्रप्रतीकाशा यमुनातीरशोभिता। शोभिता गृहमुख्यैश्च चत्वरापणवीथिकैः। चातुर्वर्ण्यसमायुक्ता नानावाणिज्यशोभिता॥
en: That city on the banks of Yamună appeared beautiful like the half moon and was filled with yards, shops, streets beautiful houses, men of four orders and various articles of trade.

sn: यच्च तेन पुरा शुभ्रं लवणेन कृतं महत्। तच्छोभयति शत्रुघ्नो नानावर्णोपशोभिताम्॥
en: Śatrughna now engaged in beautifying the spacious, white houses that were made by Lavana before, with various ornamental works.

sn: आरामैश्च विहारैश्च शोभमानं समन्ततः। शोभितां शोभनीयैश्च तथान्यैर्दैवमानुषैः॥ तां पुरीं दिव्यसंकाशां नानापण्योपशोभिताम्। नानादेशगतैश्चापि वणिग्भिरुपशोभिताम्॥ तां समृद्धां समृद्धार्थः शत्रुघ्नो भरतानुजः। निरीक्ष्य परमप्रीतः परं हर्षमुपागमत्॥
en: Beholding the city interspersed with various excellent gardens, pleasure grounds and prosperously filled with celestials and men and diverse articles of trade and merchants hailing from various countries, Satrughna, the younger brother of Bharata, attained to the satisfaction of desire and excess of delight.

sn: तस्य बुद्धिः समुत्पन्ना निवेश्य मधुरां पुरीम्। रामपादौ निरीक्षेऽहं वर्षे द्वादश आगते॥
en: Having thus reared the beautiful city he resolved within himself The twelfth year has come. I shall now behold the feet of Rāma.

sn: ततः स ताममरपुरोपमां पुरी निवेश्य वै विविधजनाभिसंवृताम्। नराधिपो रघुपतिपाददर्शने दधे मतिं रघुकुलवंशवर्धनः॥
en: There upon having set up the city resembling the region of the celestials and filled with various men, the king Satrughna, the enhancer of Raghu's race, determined on beholding Rāma's feet.

sn: ततो द्वादशमे वर्षे शत्रुघ्नो रामपालिताम्। अयोध्यां चकमे गन्तुमल्पभृत्यबलानुगः॥
en: There upon on the completion of the twelfth year, Satrughna, with few servants, soldiers and followers, desired to proceed to Ayodhyā protected by Rama.

sn: ततो मन्त्रिपुरोगांश्च बलमुख्यानिवर्त्य च। जगाम हयमुख्येन रथानां च शतेन सः॥
en: Having prevented his minister and leading generals he proceeded with one hundred chariots and cavalry.

sn: स गत्वा गणितान्वासान्सप्ताष्टौ रघुनन्दनः। वाल्मीकाश्रममागत्य वासं चक्रे महायशाः॥
en: And having counted seven halting stations on his way, the highly illustrious descendant of Raghu, Satrughna, arrived at the hermitage of Valmiki.

sn: सोऽभिवाद्य ततः पादौ वाल्मीकेः पुरुषर्षभः। पाद्यमयं तथातिथ्यं जग्राह मुनिहस्ततः॥
en: And having bowed to the feet of the leading Muni, that foremost of men took from his hands water to wash feet and Arghya and accepted his hospitality.

sn: बहुरूपाः सुमधुराः कथास्तत्र सहस्रशः। कथयामास स मुनिः शत्रुघ्नाय महात्मने॥
en: The great ascetic Valmiki addressed to the high-souled Śatrughna many sweet word.

sn: उवाच च मुनिर्वाक्यं लवणस्य वधाश्रितम्। सुदुष्करं कृतं कर्म लवणं निघ्नता त्वया॥
en: Having referred first Lavana's destruction, he said: Having slain Lavana you have performed a very hard work.

sn: बहवः पार्थिवाः सौम्य हताः सबलवाहनाः। लवणेन महाबाहो युध्यमाना महाबलाः।७।।
en: O gentle one, O foremost of men, Lavana had slain in conflict many hundred highly powerful kings with their army and conveyances. at to

sn: स त्वया निहतः पापो लीलया पुरुषर्षभ। जगतश्च भयं तत्र प्रशान्तं तव तेजसा॥
en: And you have easily slain that vicious-souled Rākşasa, Lavaņa. By your prowess the whole world has been divested of fear.

sn: रावणस्य वधो घोरो यत्नेन महता कृतः। इदं च सुमहत्कर्म त्वया कृतमयत्नतः॥
en: With great difficulty Rāma had slain Rāvana but without any trouble whatsoever you have accomplished this mighty work,

sn: प्रीतिश्चास्मिन्परा जाता देवानां लवणे हते। भूतानां चैव सर्वेषां जगतश्च प्रियं कृतम्॥
en: Lavaņa being slain, the celestials have been greatly delighted-what more the well-being of the whole universe and all creatures has been brought about.

sn: तच्च युद्धं मया दृष्टं यथावत्पुरुषर्षभ। सभायां वासवस्याथ उपविष्टेन राघव॥
en: O Rāghava, O foremost of men, being present in the assemblage of Vāsava I duly witnessed your combat.

sn: ममापि परमा प्रीतिर्हदि शत्रुघ्न वर्तते। उपाघ्रास्यामि ते मूर्ध्नि स्नेहस्यैषा परा गतिः॥
en: O Śatrughna, I too have been greatly delighted I therefore smell your crown for this is the best expression of love.

sn: इत्युक्त्वा मूर्ध्नि शत्रुघ्नमुपाघ्राय महामतिः। आतिथ्यमकरोत्तस्य ये च तस्य पदानुगाः॥
en: Saying this the high-minded Vālmīki smelled his crown and made arrangements for his reception as well as that of his followers.

sn: स भुक्तवान्नर श्रेष्ठो गीतामाधुर्यमुत्तमम्। शुश्राव रामचरितं तस्मिन्काले यथा कृतम्॥ तन्त्रीलयसमायुक्तं त्रिस्थानकरणान्वितम्। संस्कृतं लक्षणोपेतं समतालसमन्वितम्।।१५।
en: After meals, Satrughna, the foremost of men, listened to themes relating to Rāma and set musical notes. Those themes were composed describing the early actions of Rāma. They were composed in Sanskrit, set to the tune of a musical instrument, adorned with all the marks of vocal music and arranged in accompaniment with notes.

sn: शुश्राव रामचरितं तस्मिन्काले पुरा कृतम्। तान्यक्षराणि सत्यानि यथावृत्तानि पूर्वशः॥
en: Śatrughna, the foremost of men, heard them from the beginning to the end, pregnant with truth and composed of those words. And on hearing it he was beside himself with joy and his eyes were full of tears.

sn: श्रुत्वा पुरुषशार्दूलो विसंज्ञो बाष्पलोचनः। स मुहूर्तमिवासंज्ञो विनिःश्वस्य मुहुर्मुहुः॥
en: And remaining stunned for some time and regaining his sense afterwards he began to breathe hard out of excess of surprise. He heard in that song, of pasi events as things passing on.

sn: तस्मिन्गीते यथावृत्तं वर्तमानमिवाशृणोत्। पदानुगाश्च ये राज्ञस्तां श्रुत्वा गीतिसंपदम्॥ अवाङ्मुखाश्च दीनाश्च ह्याश्चर्यमिति चाब्रुवन्। परस्परं च ये तत्र सैनिकाः संबभाषिरे॥ किमिदं क्व च वर्तामः किमेतत्स्वप्नदर्शनम्। अर्थो यो नः पुरा दृष्टस्तमाश्रमपदे पुनः॥
en: And hearing it, his followers, with their heads down and sorrowfully said: Wonder; and saying this they began to converse with one another: Alas! Where are we? Is this a dream? WE have been hearing at this hermitage what we had not seen before.

sn: शृणुमः किमिदं स्वप्ने गीतबन्धनमुत्तमम्। विस्मयं ते परं गत्वा शत्रुघ्नमिदमब्रुवन्॥
en: What wonder, that in a dream we hear such an excellent song. Being in this wise greatly surprised they said to Satrughna.

sn: साधु पृच्छ नरश्रेष्ठ वाल्मीकिं मुनिपुङ्गवम्। शत्रुघ्नस्त्वब्रवीत्सर्वान्कौतूहलसमन्वितान्॥ सैनिकानक्षमोऽस्माकं परिप्रष्टुमिहेदृशः। आश्चर्याणि बहूनीह भवन्त्यस्याश्रमे मुनेः॥
en: O foremost of men, do you ask particularly, about this, Vālmīki, the foremost of ascetics. They being all thus struck with curiosity, Satrughna said: It is not proper for us, O You soldiers, to question him in this way. There are many such wonders in the hermitage of this ascetic.

sn: न तु कौतूहलाद्युक्तमन्वेष्टं तं महामुनिम्। एवं तद्वाक्यमुक्त्वा तु सैनिकान् रघुनन्दनः। अभिवाद्य महर्षि तं स्वं निवेशं ययौ तदा॥
en: It is not therefore becoming to ask him about this our of curiosity. Having thus addressed the soldiers and bowed to the ascetic, Satrughna, the descendant of Raghu, entered his own quarter.

sn: तं शयानं नरव्याघ्रं निद्रा नाभ्यागमत्तदा। चिन्तयानमनेकार्थं रामगीतमनुत्तमम्॥
en: There upon going to bed, ſatrughna began to meditate upon that excellent theme relating to Rāma and treating of diverse subjects and did not enter into sleep.

sn: तस्य शब्दं सुमधुरं तन्त्रीलयसमन्वितम्। श्रुत्वा रात्रिजगामाशु शत्रुघ्नस्य महात्मनः॥
en: In sooth the high-minded Śatrughna spent the night in no time listening to that charming song set unmusical notes.

sn: तस्यां रजन्यां व्युष्टायां कृत्वा पौर्वाणिकक्रमम्। उवाच प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यं शत्रुघ्नो मुनिपुङ्गवम्॥
en: The night being over, he first went through the morning sites and then with folded hands addressed the foremost of ascetics, Valmiki, saying.

sn: भगवन्द्रष्टुमिच्छामि राघवं रघुनन्दनम्। त्वयानुज्ञातमिच्छामि सहैभिः संशितव्रतैः॥
en: O illustrious Sir, I am anxious to see Rāma, the enhancer of the delight of the Raghu race, And my desire is that you may with other illustrious Rsis, grant me permission on this.

sn: इत्येवं वादिनं तं तु शत्रुघ्नं शत्रुसूदनम्। वाल्मीकिः संपरिष्वज्य विससर्ज स राघवम्॥
en: Satrughna, the slayer of enemies, having said this, the great ascetic Vālmīki embraced and bacle him farewell.

sn: सोऽभिवाद्य मुनिश्रेष्ठं रथमारुह्य सुप्रभम्। अयोध्यामगमत्तूर्णं राघवोत्सुकदर्शनः॥
en: He was greatly anxious to behold Rāma and saluting the foremost of Munis he speedily preceded to Ayodhyā.

sn: स प्रविष्टः पुरी रम्यां श्रीमानिक्ष्वाकुनन्दनः। प्रविवेश महाबाहुर्यत्र रामो महाद्युतिः।७।।
en: There upon having entered the highly picturesque city Ayodhyā, city Ayodhyā, the graceful descendant of Ikşvākus, ſatrughna, reached where the long-armed and the highly effulgent Råma was waiting.

sn: स राम मन्त्रिमध्यस्थं पूर्णचन्द्रनिभाननम्। पश्यन्नमरमध्यस्थं सहस्रनयनं यथा।।।। सोऽभिवाद्य महात्मानं ज्वलन्तमिव तेजसा। उवाच प्राञ्जलिर्भूत्वा रामं सत्यपराक्रमम्॥
en: He espied there Rāma in the midst of the councillors like Indra among the immortals burning in his own effulgence. And having bowed with folded hands to Răma, having truth for his prowess, Śatrughna, said.

sn: यदाज्ञप्तं महाराज सर्व तत्कृतवानहम्। हतः स लवणः पापः पुरी चास्य निवेशिता॥ द्वादशैतानि वर्षाणि त्वां विना रघुनन्दन। नोत्सहेयमहं वस्तुं त्वया विरहितो नृप॥
en: O great king, I have carried out all your behests; I have slain the vicious Lavaņa and filled his city with subjects. O descendant of Raghu, twelve years have passed away without you, I do not wish to live any longer separated from you.

sn: स मे प्रसादं काकुत्स्थ कुरुष्वामितविक्रम। मातृहीनो यथा वत्सो न चिरं प्रवसाम्यहम्॥
en: Do you therefore, O Kākutstha of unmitigated prowess, have compassion on me. Without you, I cannot live for ever in a foreign province like a motherless child.

sn: एवं ब्रुवाणं काकुत्स्थः परिष्वज्येदमब्रवीत्। मा विषादं कृथाः शूर नैतत्क्षत्रियचेष्टितम्॥
en: He having said this, Rāma embraced him and said: Be not sorry O hero. This is not a becoming action for Kşatriyas.

sn: नावसीदन्ति राजानो विप्रवासेषु राघव। प्रजा हि परिपाल्या हि क्षत्रधर्मेण राघव॥
en: The kings, O Raghava, are never tired of living in a foreign land. According to the morality of the Kșatriyas, their greatest duty consists in governing the subjects.

sn: काले काले तु मां वीर अयोध्यामवलोकितुम्। आगच्छ त्वं नरश्रेष्ठ गन्तासि च पुरं तव॥
en: O heroic and foremost of men, do you, at intervals, come to Ayodhyå to see me and return to your own city.

sn: ममापि त्वं सुदयितः प्राणैरपि न संशयः। अवश्यं करणीयं च राज्यस्य परिपालनम्॥ तस्मात्त्वं वस काकुत्स्थ सप्तरात्रं मया सह। ऊवं गन्तासि मधुरां सभृत्यबलवाहनः॥
en: Forsooth you are dearer than my life. But it is an incumbent duty to govern the kingdom. Do you therefore, O Kakutstha, live with me for seven nights, and afterwards return to your city with your servants, army and conveyances.

sn: रामस्यैतद्वचः श्रुत्वा धर्मयुक्तं मनोनुगम्। शत्रुघ्नो दीनया वाचा बाढमित्येव चाब्रवीत्।।१८
en: Hearing those moral and charming words of Rama, Satrughna poorly replied, saying: Your command shall be carried out.

sn: सप्तरात्रं च काकुत्स्थो राघवस्य यथाज्ञया। उष्य तत्र महेष्वासो गमनायोपचक्रमे॥
en: Thereupon Satrughna, well-skilled in the use of bows, remained with Rāma for seven nights and then addressed himself for departure.

sn: आमन्त्र्य तु महात्मानं रामं सत्यपराक्रमम्। भरतं लक्ष्मणं चैव महारथमुपारुहत्॥
en: Thereupon having invited Bharata and Laksmana, the high-souled Rama, having truth for his prowess, speedily went for his city in a huge chariot.

sn: दूरं पद्भ्यामनुगतो लक्ष्मणेन महात्मना। भरतेन च शत्रुघ्नो जगामाशु पुरीं तदा॥
en: The high-souled Lakşmaņa and slayer of enemies Bharata followed him on foot for some distance.

sn: प्रस्थाप्य तु स शत्रुघ्नं भ्रातृभ्यां सह राघवः। प्रमुमोद सुखी राज्यं धर्मेण परिपालयन्॥
en: Having bade adieu to Satrughna, Rama, the descendant of Raghu, was greatly delighted by governing his subjects piously in the company of Bharata and Laksmana.

sn: ततः कतिपयाहःसु वृद्धो जानपदो द्विजः। मृतं बालमुपादाय राजद्वारमुपागमत्॥
en: Some days having passed in this wise-a villager, an old Brālimaņa, arrived at the palace gate with a dead boy.

sn: किं नु मे दुष्कृतं कर्म पुरा देहान्तरे कृतम्। रुदन्बहुविधा वाचः स्नेहदुःखसमन्वितः। असकृत्पुत्र पुत्रेति वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह॥ किं नु मे दुष्कृतं कर्म पुरा देहान्तरे कृतम्। यदहं पुत्रमेकं तु पश्यामि निधनं गतम्॥
en: That Brāhmaṇa, stricken with affection, again and again bewailed in various piteous accents exclaiming What heinous crime had I committed in my pristine birth that I have been constrained to witness the death of my son.

sn: अप्राप्तयौवनं बालं पञ्चवर्षसहस्रकम्। अकाले कालमापन्नं मम दुःखाय पुत्रक॥ अल्पैरहोभिनिधनं गमिष्यामि न संशयः। अहं च जननी चैव तव शोकेन पुत्रक॥
en: My son, you have not as yet completed fourteen years. To my misery you have met with untimely death. Forsooth, for your grief, O my son, myself and your mother shall soon be snatched away by death.

sn: न स्मराम्यनृतं ह्युक्तं न च हिंसां स्मराम्यहम्। सर्वेषां प्राणिनां पापं न स्मरामि कदाचन।७।। केनाद्य दुष्कृतेनायं बाल एव ममात्मजः। अकृत्वा पितृकार्याणि गतो वैवस्वतक्षयम्॥
en: I do not remember to have ever uttered a falsehood, or injured an animal or perpetrated any other crime. Therefore for some other sinful action, this boy, without performing the son's duties towards his parents, has gone to the abode of death.

sn: नेदृशं दृष्टपूर्वं मे श्रुतं वा घोरदर्शनम्। मृत्युरप्राप्तकालानां रामस्य विषये ह्ययम्॥
en: Save under the regime of Rama, I have never seen or heard of the dreadful death of such a boy who has not attained the age.

sn: रामस्य दुष्कृतं किंचिन्महदस्ति न संशयः। यथा हि विषयस्थानां बालानां मृत्युरागतः॥
en: Forsooth, Rāma has perpetrated a mighty iniquity for which boys, during his administration, have been meeting with untimely death.

sn: नह्यन्यविषयस्थानां बालानां मृत्युतो भयम्। स राजञ्जीवयस्वैनं बालं मृत्युवशं गतम्॥ राजद्वारि मरिष्यामि पत्न्या सार्धमनाथवत्। ब्रह्महत्यां ततो राम समुपेत्य सुखी भव॥ भ्रातृभिः सहितो राजन्दीर्घमायुरवाप्स्यसि।
en: In other governments boys have no fear of such an untimely death. Therefore, O king confer life upon this dead child. Or else with my spouse I shall renounce my life at this gate like one having no lord. O Rāma, soiled by the sin consequent upon the destruction of a Brāhmaṇa, do you live long happily with brother.

sn: उषिताः स्म सुखं राज्ये तवास्मिन्सुमहाबल॥ इदं तु पतितं तस्मात्तव राम वशे स्थितान्। कालस्य वशमापन्नाः स्वल्पं हि नहि नः सुखम्॥
en: O you of great prowess, up to this time we have lived happily in your kingdom. And now, O Räma, under your subjection we are being troubled with the sorrow or our son's death. We have been brought under the influence of Kāla; so in your kingdom there is not the least happiness for us.

sn: संप्रत्यनाथो विषय इक्ष्वाकूणां महात्मनाम्। राम नाथमिहासाद्य बालान्तकरणं ध्रुवम्॥ राजदोषैविपद्यन्ते प्रजा ह्यविधिपालिताः। असद्धृत्ते हि नृपतावकाले म्रियते जनः॥ यद्वा पुरेष्वयुक्तानि जना जनपदेषु च। कुर्वते न च रक्षास्ति तदा कालकृतं भयम्॥
en: Having attained Rāma as its lord, the kingdom, of the high-souled Ikşvākus, has attained to the condition of one having no master, where during Rāma's regime the death of a boy has been brought about. For being impiously governed by a king, for his sin, the subjects meet with calamities. And a king following evil tracks and not governing the subjects righteously people meet with untimely death. Therefore, when a king does mot suppress the crimes committed by people either in cities, or provinces the fear, of untimely death, comes in.

sn: सुव्यक्तं राजदोषो हि भविष्यति न संशयः। पुरे जनपदे चापि तथा बालवधो ह्ययम्॥
en: Evident it is therefore that undoubtedly the sin of the king has appeared in cities and provinces. And for that reason this boy has met with death.

sn: एवं बहुविधैर्वाक्यैरुपरुध्य मुहुर्मुहुः। राजानं दुःखसंतप्तः सुतं तमुपगृहति॥
en: Being overwhelmed with sorrow that old Brāhmaṇa again and again remonstrated with the king in these 'piteous words and afterwards covered the dead body (of his son.)

sn: तथा तु करुणं तस्य द्विजस्य परिदेवनम्। शुश्राव राघवः सर्वं दुःखशोकसमन्वितम्॥ स दुःखेन च संतप्तो मन्त्रिणस्तानुपाह्वयत्। वसिष्ठं वामदेवं च भ्रातृ॑श्च सह नैगमान्॥
en: Hearing those sorrowful words of the Brāhmaṇa, Rāma was greatly sorry and sent for Vasistha, Vamadeva, his brothers, citizens and councillors.

sn: ततो द्विजा वसिष्ठेन सार्धमष्टौ प्रवेशिताः। राजानं देवसंकाशं वर्धस्वेति ततोऽब्रुवन्॥
en: There upon having entered the apartment in the company of Vasiştha, eight Brāhmaṇas blessed the king Rāma, resembling a celestial, saying 'may victory crown you.'

sn: मार्कण्डेयोऽथ मौद्गल्यो वामदेवश्च काश्यपः। कात्यायनोऽथ जाबालिगौतमो नारदस्तथा॥ एते द्विजर्षभाः सर्वे आसनेषूपवेशिताः। महर्षीन्समनुप्राप्तानभिवाद्य कृताञ्जलिः॥ मन्त्रिणो नैगमाश्चैव यथार्हमनुकूलिताः। तेषां समुपविष्टानां सर्वेषां दीप्ततेजसाम्॥ राघवः सर्वमाचष्टे द्विजोऽयमुपरोधति।
en: Markandeya, Maudgalya, Vamadeva, Kashyapa, Katyayana, Javali, Gautama, and Nārada, these eight leading Brāhmaṇas having takes their seats, Rāma with folded hands, saluted them. And he showed due civilities towards his minister, citizens, Rșis and all others. There upon all the highly effulgent Rșis being accommodated with seats Råma narrated duly before them the account of the Brāhmaṇa and said. This Brāhmaṇa is waiting at the Palace-gate.

sn: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा राज्ञो दीनस्य नारदः॥ प्रत्युवाच शुभं वाक्यमृषीणां संनिधौ स्वयम्।
en: Hearing those words of the poorly king, Narada, in the presence of all other Rsis, replied.

sn: शृणु राजन्यथाकाले प्राप्तो बालस्य संक्षयः॥ श्रुत्वा कर्तव्यतां राजन्कुरुष्वरघुनन्दन।
en: Hear, o king, why this boy has met with untimely death. And hearing this, O descendant or Raghu, do you settle what you think proper.

sn: पुरा कृतयुगे राजन्ब्राह्मणा वै तपस्विनः।।।। अब्राह्मणस्तदा राजन्न तपस्वी कथंचन।
en: O king, in the golden age, only the Brahmanas used to engage in asceticism. At that age save the Brāhmaṇas no other caste used to lead the life of an anchoret.

sn: तस्मिन्युगे प्रज्वलिते ब्रह्मभूते त्वनावृते॥ अमृत्यवस्तदा सर्वे जज्ञिरे दीर्घदर्शिनः।
en: And for this, the Brāhmaṇas were the highest caste, effulgent in asceticism, asceticism, shorn shorn of ignorance, above death and conversant with three ages.

sn: ततस्त्रेतायुगं नाम मानवानां वपुष्मताम्॥ क्षत्रिया यत्र जायन्ते पूर्वेण तपसान्विताः। वीर्येण तपसा चैव तेऽधिकाः पूर्वजन्मनि॥ मानवा ये महात्मानस्तत्र त्रेतायुगे युगे।
en: There upon at the end of the golden age, Brāhmaṇa's understanding became loose and the Tretā Yuga set in. At this age Kşatriyas, gifted with the power acquired by pristine asceticism, were born. And those men, intent upon austere penances, that were born in the Tretā age, were more powerful and greater devotees than those in the former age.

sn: ब्रह्म क्षत्रं च तत्सर्वं यत्पूर्वमवरं च यत्॥ युगयोरुभयोरासीत्समवीर्यसमन्वितम्।
en: In the golden age the Brāhmaṇas were more powerful than the Kșatriyas. But in the Tretā age the Brāhmaṇas and the Ksatriyas were equally powerful.

sn: अपश्यन्तस्तु ते सर्वे विशेषमधिकं ततः॥ स्थापनं चक्रिरे तत्र चातुर्वर्ण्यस्य संमतम्।
en: Thus in the Tretā age, not beholding prominence of the Brāhmaṇas greater than that of the Kşatriyas, Manu and other religious leaders of the time composed the Sastra describing and setting in the four divisions of castes.

sn: तस्मिन्युगे प्रज्वलिते धर्मभूते ह्यनावृते॥ अधर्मः पादमेकं तु पातयत्पृथिवीतले। अधर्मेण हि संयुक्तस्तेजो मन्दं भविष्यति।।१६
en: In this wise the Tretā age was prolific with virtues of the four Varņas, and many pious sacrifices and was shorn of iniquities. But being attacked a little with iniquity, one portion of sin appeared on earth. And growing impious people of sin appeared on earth. And growing impious people lost their strength.

sn: आमिषं यच्च पूर्वेषां राजसं च मलं भृशम्। अनृतं नाम तद्भूतं क्षिप्तेन पृथिवीतले॥ अनृतं पातयित्वा तु पादमेकमधर्मतः। ततः प्रादुष्कृतं पूर्वमायुषः परिनिष्ठितम्॥
en: And for houses and farms that were the property of the former age, people of the Tretā Yuga were possessed by envy, the outcome of the quality of darkness. And with the treading of impiety on earth during Tretā, the soiled sin of untruth appeared. And this iniquity stretching one footstep, the lease of people's lives, for sins, became limited.

sn: पातिते त्वनृते तस्मिनधर्मेण महीतले। शुभान्येवाचरैल्लोकः सत्यधर्मपरायणः॥
en: And the sin of untruth descending on earth, people, to a void the extinction of life in consequence thereof, became truthful and engaged in many pious observances.

sn: त्रेतायुगे च वर्तन्ते ब्राह्मणाः क्षत्रियाश्च ये। तपोऽतप्यन्त ते सर्वे शुश्रूषामपरे जनाः॥
en: During the Tretă age the Brāhmaṇas and Kș atriyas engaged in austere penances and the Vaiśyas and Sūdras engaged in serving them.

sn: स्वधर्मः परमस्तेषां वैश्यशूद्रं तदागमत्। पूजां च सर्ववर्णानां शूद्राश्चनुर्विशेषतः॥
en: And the greatest piety of the Vaiśyas and Śūdras at that time consisted of serving the Brāhmaṇas and Ksatriyas and specially for the Śūdras the highest religion was to serve people of all Varnas.
