en: In this Drona Parva is narrated the deaths of Alambusha, Shrutayus, valorous Jalasandha, Somdatti, Virata, great car-warrior Drupada, Ghatotkacha and others. Being exceedingly angry on account of the death of Drona in battle, Ashvathama also.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: अस्त्रं प्रादुश्चकारोग्रं नारायणममर्षितः। आग्नेयं कीर्त्यते यत्र रुद्रमाहात्म्यमुत्तमम्॥ व्यासस्य चाप्यागमनं माहात्म्यं कृष्णपार्थयोः॥
en: Discharged his fearful weapon Narayana. Then is told the story of Rudra, in connection with the burning of the cities. The arrival of Vyasa and the glories of Partha and Krishna are told by him.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: सप्तमं भारते पर्व महदेतदुदाहृतम्। यत्र ते पृथिवीपालाः प्रायशो निधनं गताः॥
en: These are the matters elaborately narrated in the seventh Parva of the Bharata, in which all the chief and potentates mentioned were killed.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: द्रोणपर्वणि ये शूरा निर्दिष्टाः पुरुषर्षभाः। अत्राध्यायशतं प्रोक्तं तथाध्यायाश्च सप्ततिः॥ अष्टौ श्लोकसहस्राणि तथा नव शतानि च। श्लोका नव तथैवात्र संख्यातास्तत्त्वदर्शिना॥ पाराशर्येण मुनिना संचिन्त्य द्रोणपर्वणि।
en: The number of chapters in this Parva is one hundred and seventy. The number of slokas composed in the Drona Parva by the great Rishi, the son of Parashara and the master of great knowledge, is eight thousand nine hundred and nine.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: अतः परं कर्णपर्वं प्रोच्यते परमाद्भुतम्। सारथ्ये विनियोगश्च मद्रराजस्य धीमतः॥
en: Then comes the most wonderful Parva named Karna. In it is described the appointment of king of the Madra as the charioteer (of Karna).

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: आख्यातं यत्र पौराणं त्रिपुरस्य निपातनम्। प्रयाणे परुषश्चात्र संवादः कर्णशल्ययोः॥
en: Then is told the old story of the death of Tripura; the interchange of strong words between Karna and Shalya on their setting out to battle.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: हंसकाकीयमाख्यानं तत्रैवाक्षेपसंहितम्। वधः पाण्ड्यस्य च तथा अश्वत्थाम्ना महात्मना।।२७१।
en: Then is narrated the story of the swan and the crow as an insulting allusion to Karna. Then is the death of Pandya at the hands of the high-souled Ashvathama.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: दण्डसेनस्य च ततो दण्डस्य च वधस्तथा। द्वैरथे यत्र कर्णेन धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः॥ संशयं गमितो युद्धे मिषतां सर्वधन्विनाम्। अन्योन्यं प्रति च क्रोधो युधिष्ठिरकिरीटिनोः॥
en: Then the death of Dandasena and then that of Danda, then the imminent risk of Yudhishthira in single combat with Karna which took place before all the warriors; the anger of Yudhishthira and Arjuna towards each other;

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: यत्रैवानुनयः प्रोक्त माधवेनार्जुनस्य हि। प्रतिज्ञापूर्वकं चापि वक्षो दुःशासनस्य च॥ भित्वा वृकोदरो रक्तं पीतवान्यत्र संयुगे। द्वैरथे यत्र पार्थेन हतः कर्णो महारथः॥
en: Krishna's pacification of Arjuna; Bhima's fulfilment of his vow by drinking the heart's blood of Dushasana after ripping open his breast; the slaying of Karna by Arjuna in single combat.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: अष्टमं पर्व निर्दिष्टमेतद्भारतचिन्तकैः। एकोनसप्ततिः प्रोक्ता अध्यायाः कर्णपर्वणि॥ चत्वार्येव सहस्राणि नव श्लोकशतानि च। चतुःषष्टिस्तथा श्लोकाः पर्वण्यस्मिन् प्रकीर्तिताः॥
en: The leader of the Bharata calls this Parva the eighth Parva. The number of its chapters is sixty nine and that of the slokas is four thousand nine hundred and sixty four.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: अतः परं विचित्रार्थं शल्यपर्व प्रकीर्तितम्। हतप्रवीरे सैन्ये तु नेता मद्रेश्वरोऽभवत्॥
en: Then is told the wonderful, Parva called Shalya. After the death of all great warriors, the king of Madra became the commander.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: यत्र कौमारमाख्यानमभिषेकस्य कर्म च। वृत्तानि स्थयुद्धानि कीर्त्यन्ते यत्र भागशः। विनाशः कुरुमुख्यानां शल्यपर्वणि कीर्त्यते॥
en: Then is described one after the other the encounters of various charioteer; then the deaths of the chief warrior of the Kuru army.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: शल्यस्य निधनं चात्र धर्मराजान्महात्मनः। शकुनेश्च वधोऽत्रैव सहदेवेन संयुगे॥
en: Then the death of Shalya at the hands of Yudhishthira, the death of Shakuni at the hands of Sahadeva.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: सैन्ये च हतभूयिष्ठे किंचिच्छिष्टे सुयोधनः। ह्रदं प्रविश्य यत्रासौ संस्तभ्यापो व्यवस्थितः॥
en: When only a small remnant of his troops remained alive, Suyodhana retired in to a lake and there creating room for himself, lay hidden.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: प्रवृत्तिस्तत्र चाख्याता यत्र भीमस्य लुब्धकैः। क्षेपयुक्तैर्वचोभिश्च धर्मराजस्य धीमतः॥ ह्रदात्समुत्थितो यत्र धार्तराष्ट्रोऽत्यमर्षणः। भीमेन गदया युद्धं यत्रासौ कृतवान्सह॥
en: The receipt of this news by Bhima from some hunters. Then is related how Duryodhana, ever unable to bear affronts, came out of the water, being angered by the insulting words of Yudhishthira. Then is described the fight of Bhima and Duryodhana with clubs.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: समवाये च युद्धस्य रामस्यागमनं स्मृतम्। सरस्वत्याश्च तीर्थानां पुण्यता परिकीर्तिता॥
en: The arrival of Balarama at the time of the fight is next described. Then is told the sacredness of the Sarasvati.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: गदायुद्धं च तुमुलमत्रैव परिकीर्तितम्। दुर्योधनस्य राज्ञोऽथ यत्र भीमेन संयुगे॥ ऊरू भग्नौ प्रसह्याजौ गदया भीमवेगया। नवमं पर्व निर्दिष्टमेतदद्भुतमर्थवत्॥
en: The continuation of the club fight; the breaking of Duryodhana's thighs by Bhima by a fearful hurl of his club. All this has been described in the wonderful ninth Parva.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: एकोनषष्टिरध्यायाः पर्वण्यत्र प्रकीर्तिताः। संख्याता बहुवृत्तान्ताः श्लोकसंख्याऽत्र कथ्यते॥ त्रीणि श्लोकसहस्राणि द्वे शते विंशतिस्तथा। मुनिना संप्रणीतानि कौरवाणां यशोभृता॥
en: The number of chapters in this Parva is fifty-nine and the number of slokas composed by the great Vyasa, the spreader of the fame of the Kuru Dynasty, is three thousand two hundred and twenty.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि सौप्तिकं पर्व दारुणम्। भग्नोरं यत्र राजानं दुर्योधनममर्षणम्॥ अपयातेषु पार्थेषु त्रयस्तेऽभ्याययूरथाः। कृतवर्मा कृपो द्रौणि: सायाह्ने रुधिरक्षितम्॥
en: I shall now describe the contents of the terrible tenth Parva, named Sauptika. On the departure of the Pandavas the great car-warrior, Kritavarma. Kripa and the son of Drona (Ashvathama) came in the evening to he place where Duryodhana was lying with the brocken thigh.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: समेत्य ददृशुर्भूमौ पतितं रणमूर्धनि। प्रतिजज्ञे दृढक्रोधो द्रौणिर्यत्र महारथः॥
en: They saw King Duryodhana lying on the ground, his thighs broken and his body covered with blood. The great car-warrior, fearfully angry son of Drona vowed.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: अहत्वा सर्वपञ्चालान् धृष्टद्युम्नपुरोगमान्। पाण्डवांश्च सहामात्यान्न विमोक्ष्यामि दंशनम्॥
en: "I will not take off my armour without killing all the Panchalas with Dhristadyumna and the Pandavas with their allies."

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: यत्रैवमुक्त्वा राजानमपक्रम्य त्रयो स्थाः। सूर्यास्तमनवेलायामासेदुस्ते महद्वनम्॥
en: Having said these words, the three warriors left Duryodhana and entered into the great forest just when the sun was setting.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: न्यग्रोधस्याथ महतो यत्राधस्ताद्व्यवस्थिताः। ततः काकान्बहून् रात्रौ दृष्टवोलूकेन हिंसिताम्॥
en: While they were resting under a large banian tree, they saw owl killing innumerable crows at night.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: द्रौणिः क्रोधसमाविष्टः पितुर्वधमनुस्मरन्। पञ्चालानां प्रसुप्तानां वधं प्रति मनो दधे॥
en: Seeing this, Ashvathama, his heart being full of rage, remembering the death of his father, determined kill the sleeping Panchalas.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: गत्वा च शिविरद्वार दुर्दृशं तत्र राक्षसम्। घोररूपमपश्यत्स दिवमावृत्य धिष्ठितम्॥
en: Going to the gate of the camp, he saw a fearful Rakshasa, his head reaching to the very skies, guarding the door. an to

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: तेन व्याघातमस्त्राणां क्रियमाणमवेक्ष्य च। द्रौणिर्यत्र विरूपाक्षं रुद्रमाराध्य सत्वरः॥
en: Seeing also that the Rakshasa obstructed him in his discharge of weapons, he began to worship the three-eyed divinity and it pacified him.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: प्रसुप्तान्निशि विश्वस्तान् धृष्टद्युम्नपुरोगमान्। पञ्चालान्सपरीवारान्द्रौपदेयांश्च सर्वशः॥ कृतवर्मणा च सहितः कृपेण च निजनिवान्। यत्रामुच्यन्त ते पार्थाः पञ्च कृष्णबलाश्रयात्॥ सात्यकिश्च महेष्वासः शेषाश्च निधनं गताः। पञ्चालानां प्रसुप्तानां यत्र द्रोणसुताद्वधः॥
en: Then accompanied by Kripa and Kritavarma, he entered the camp and killed all the sons of Draupadi and all the family of Panchalas, including Dhristadyumna, when they were all unsuspectingly sleeping on their beds. Only Satyaki and the five Pandavas escaped through the counsel of Krishna.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: धृष्टद्युम्नश्च सूतेन पाण्डवेषु निवेदितः। द्रौपदी पुत्रशोकार्ता पितृभ्रातृवधार्दिता॥
en: The charioteer of Dhristhadyumna brought to the Pandavas the news of the massacre of the slumbering Panchalas by the son of Drona. Draupadi, grieved by the death of her father, brother and sons.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: कृतानशनसंकल्पा पत्र भर्तृनुपाविशत्। द्रौपदीवचनाद्यत्र भीमो भीमपराक्रमः॥
en: Sat before her husbands and resolved to die of fasting. Then Bhima of fearful deed, being moved by the words of Draupadi.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: प्रियं तस्याचिकीर्षन्वै गदामादाय वीर्यवान्। अन्वधावत्सुसंक्रुद्धो भारद्वाजं गुरोः सुतम्॥
en: Determined to please her, he speedily took up his club and ran in pursuit of the son of his preceptor.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: भीमसेनभयाद्यत्र दैवेनाभिप्रचोदितः। अपाण्डवायेति रुषा द्रौणिरस्त्रमवासृजत्॥
en: The son of Drona, out of fear of Bhima and as fate would have it discharged the celestial weapon, crying “Let it make the world free of all the Pandavas."

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: मैवमित्यब्रवीत्कृष्णः शमयंस्तस्य तद्वचः। यत्रास्त्रमस्त्रेण च तच्छमयामास फाल्गुनः॥
en: Krishna neutralised the words by saying, “This shall not be," and Arjuna neutralised the weapon by one of his own.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: द्रौणेश्च द्रोहबुद्धित्वं वीक्ष्य पापात्मनस्तदा। द्रौणिद्वैपायनादीनां शापाश्चान्योन्यकारिताः॥
en: Seeing the wicked intention of Ashvathama, Dvaipayana cursed him and he too cursed Dvaipayana.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: मणिं तथा समादाय द्रोणपुत्रान्महारथात्। पाण्डवाः प्रददुहृष्टा द्रौपद्यै जितकाशिनः॥
en: The Pandavas took the Jewel on the head of Ashvathama and they with much pleasure presented it to the aggrieved and sorrowing Draupadi.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: एतद्वैदशमं पर्व सौप्तिकं समुदाहृतम्। अष्टादशास्मिन्नध्यायाः पर्वण्युक्ता महात्मना॥ श्लोकानां कथितान्यत्र शतान्यष्टौ प्रसंख्यया। श्लोकाश्च सप्ततिः प्रोक्ता मुनिना ब्रह्मवादिना॥
en: These matters are dwelt with in this tenth Sauptika Parva. The great Vyasa composed it in eighteen chapters. The numbers of slokas composed in it by the great reciter of the sacred truths, is eight hundred and seventy.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: सौप्तिकैषीके संबद्ध पर्वण्युत्तमतेजसी। अत ऊर्ध्वमिदं प्राहुः स्त्रीपर्व करुणोदयम्॥
en: The great Rishi has put together two Parvas, namely Sauptika and Aishika in this Parva. Then the most pathetic Parva called Stree is next told.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: पुत्रशोकाभिसंतप्तः प्रज्ञाचक्षुर्नराधिपः। कृष्णोपनीतां यत्रासावायसी प्रतिमां दृढाम्॥ भीमसेनद्रोहबुद्धिधृतराष्ट्रो बभञ्ज ह। तथा शोकाभितप्तस्य धृतराष्ट्रस्य धीमतः॥ संसारगहनं बुद्ध्या हेतुभिर्मोक्षदर्शनैः। विदुरेण च यत्रास्य राज्ञ आश्वासनं कृतम्॥
en: Then greatly wise Dhritarashtra, being much afflicted by the death of his sons, moved with vengeance, crushed into pieces an iron statute, the substitute for Bhima, placed before him by Krishna. Then Vidura consoled the great king by removing his worldly affections with reasons pointing to final emancipation.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: धृतराष्ट्रस्य चात्रैव कौरवायोधनं तथा। सान्तःपुरस्य गमनं शोकार्तस्य प्रकीर्तितम्॥
en: Then is described the journey of Dhritarashtra with the ladies of his house to the field of battle.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: विलापो वीर पत्नीनां यत्रातिकरुणः स्मृतः। क्रोधावेशः प्रमोहश्च गान्धारीधृतराष्ट्रयोः॥
en: Then were the pathetic and heartrending lamentations of the wives of the heroes. The wrath of Gandhari and Dhritarashtra and their falling into a swoon.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: यत्र तान् क्षत्रियाः शूरान्संग्रामेष्वनिवर्तिनः। पुत्रान् भ्रातॄन् पितंश्चैव ददृशुनिहतान् रणे॥
en: Then did the ladies see those heroes, their slain sons, brothers and father, lying on the field of battle.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: पुत्रपौत्रवधार्तायस्तथात्रैव प्रकीर्तिता। गान्धार्याश्चापि कृष्णेन क्रोधोपशमनक्रिया॥
en: The pacification by Krishna of the wrath of Gandhari, who was greatly afflicted by the death of her sons and grandsons.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: यत्र राजा महाप्राज्ञः सर्वधर्मभृतां वरः। राज्ञां तानि शरीराणि दाहयामास शास्त्रतः॥
en: The cremation of the chiefs and potentates by king Yudhishthira, the greatly wise and the foremost of all virtuous men, according to due rites.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: तोयकर्माणि चारब्धे राज्ञामुदकदानिके। गूढोत्पन्नस्य चाख्यानं कर्णस्य पृथयात्मनः॥
en: When the presentation of water to the deceased princes was commenced, Kunti acknowledged Karna as her son born in secret.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: सुतस्यैतदिह प्रोक्तं व्यासेन परमर्षिणा। एतदेकादशं पर्व शोकवैक्लव्यकारणम्॥
en: All this has been described by the great Rishi Vyasa in the most pathetic eleventh Parva.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: प्रणीतं सज्जनमनो वैक्लव्याश्रुप्रवर्तकम्। सप्तविंशतिरध्यायाः पर्वण्यस्मिप्रकीर्तिताः॥ श्लोकसप्तशती चापि पञ्चसप्ततिसंयुता। संख्यया भारताख्यानमुक्तं व्यासेन धीमता॥
en: Its perusal moves every heart and draws tears from every eye. It contains twenty-seven chapters and its number of slokas is seven hundred and seventy-five.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: अतः परं शान्तिपर्व द्वादशं बुद्धिवर्धनम्। यत्र निर्वेदमापन्नो धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Then comes the Shanti Parva, the twelfth in number, which increases the understanding. It relates the despondency of Yudhishthira.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: घातयित्वा पितॄन् भ्रातॄन् पुत्रान् संबन्धिमातुलान्। शान्तिपर्वणि धर्माश्च व्याख्याताः शारतल्पिकाः॥ राजभिर्वेदितव्यास्ते सम्यग्ज्ञानबुभुत्सुभिः। आपद्धर्माश्च तत्रैव कालहेतुप्रदर्शिनः॥
en: On his having slain his fathers, brothers, sons, maternal uncles and relations by marriage. There is related how Bhishma taught laws and duties, worth the study of kings who desire to possess knowledge.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: यान्बुध्वा पुरुषः सम्यक्सर्वज्ञत्वमवाप्नुयात्। मोक्षधर्माश्च कथिता विचित्रा बहुविस्तराः॥
en: If a person understands them, he attains to, consummate knowledge. The mysteries of final emancipation is also elaborately discussed.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: द्वादशं पर्व निर्दिष्टमेतत्प्राज्ञजनप्रियम्। अत्र पर्वणि विज्ञेयमध्यायानां शतत्रयम्॥
en: This twelfth Parva, the favourite of the wise, contains three hundred and thirty nine chapters.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: त्रिंशच्चैव तथाध्याया नव चैव तपोधनाः। चतुर्दश सहस्राणि तथा सप्त शतानिच॥ सप्त श्लोकास्तथैवात्र पञ्चविंशतिसंख्यया। अत ऊर्ध्वं च विज्ञेयमनुशासनमुत्तमम्॥
en: O Rishis, the wise son of Parashara has described this Parva in fourteen thousand seven hundred and thirty two slokas. Next comes the excellent Anushasana Parva.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: यत्र प्रकृतिमापन्नः श्रुत्वा धर्मविनिश्चयम्। भीष्माद्भागीरथीपुत्रात्कुरुराजो युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: The king of the Kurus, Yudhishthira was consoled by hearing the expositions of duties by the son of the Bhagirathi, Bhishma.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: व्यवहारोऽत्र कात्स्येन धर्मार्थीयः प्रकीर्तितः। विविधानां च दानानां फलयोगाः प्रकीर्तिताः॥
en: It then treats of the rules Dharma and Artha in detail, then the various rules of charity and its different merits.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: तथा पात्रविशेषाश्च दानानां च परो विधिः। आचारविधियोगश्च सत्यस्य च परागतिः॥
en: The different merits of charity according to the subjects of charity; the rules of living, the ceremonials of individual duty and the matchless merits of truth.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: महाभाग्यं गवां चैव ब्राह्मणानां तथैव च। रहस्यं चैव धर्माणां देशकालोपसंहितम्॥
en: It describes the great merit of Brahmanas and kine and it reveals the duties in relation to time and place.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: एतत्सुबहुवृत्तांतमुत्तमं चानुशासनम्। भीष्यस्यात्रैव संप्राप्तिः स्वर्गस्य परिकीर्तिता॥
en: All these excellent matters have been treated in this Anushasana Parva containing variety of incidents. It also describes ascension of Bhishma to heaven.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: एतत्त्रयोदशं पर्व धर्मनिश्चयकारकम्। अध्यायानां शतं त्वत्र षट्चत्वारिंशदेव तु॥
en: This is the thirteenth Parva which describe the certainty of righteousness. It contains one hundred and forty six chapters.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: श्लोकानां तु सहस्राणि प्रोक्तान्यष्टौ प्रसंख्यया। ततोऽश्वमेधिकं नाम पर्व प्रोक्तं चतुर्दशम्॥
en: The number of slokas in it is eight thousand. Then comes the fourteenth Parva, called Ashvamedhika.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: तत्संवर्तमरुत्तीयं यत्राख्यानमनुत्तमम्। सुवर्णकोशसंप्राप्तिर्जन्म चोक्तं परीक्षितः॥
en: It relates the beautiful story of Samvarta and Marutta; the discovery of treasures (by the Pandavas). Then is described the birth of Parikshit.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: दग्धस्यास्त्राग्निना पूर्वं कृष्णात् संजीवनं पुनः। चर्यायां हयमुत्सृष्टं पाण्डवस्यानुगच्छतः॥
en: Who was burnt by the weapon of Ashvathama and therefore almost dead, but he was revived by Krishna; Arjuna's journey with the sacrificial horse let loose.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: तत्र तत्र च युद्धानि राजपुत्रैरमर्षणैः। चित्राङ्गदाया: पुत्रेण पुत्रिकाया धनंजयः॥
en: And his fight with various chiefs and potentates who seized it in wrath, the encounter of Arjuna with the son of Chitrangada.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: संग्रामे बभ्रुवाहेन संशयं चात्र दर्शितः। अश्वमेधे महायज्ञे नकुलाख्यानमेव च॥
en: And his great risk in the fight with Babhruvahana. Then follows the story of the mongoose in the horse-sacrifice.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: इत्याश्वमेधिकं पर्व प्रोक्तमेतन्महाद्भुतम्। अध्यायानां शतं चैव त्रयोऽध्यायाश्च क्रीर्तिताः॥
en: Thus is described the wonderful Parva, called Ashvamedhika. Its number of chapters is one hundred and three.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: त्रीणि श्लोकसहस्राणि तावन्त्येव शतानि च। विंशतिश्च तथा श्लोकाः संख्यातास्तत्त्वदर्शिना।।
en: The number of slokas, composed by the greatly wise Rishi, is three thousand three hundred and twenty.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: ततस्त्वाश्रमवासाख्यं पर्व पञ्चदशं स्मृतम्। यत्र राज्यं समुत्सृज्य गान्धार्या सहितो नृपः॥ धृतराष्ट्रोश्रमपदं विदुश्च जगाम ह। यं दृष्ट्वा प्रस्थितं साध्वी पृथाप्यनुययौ तदा॥ पुत्रराज्यं परित्यज्य गुरुश्रुश्रूषणे रता। यत्र राजा हतान्पुत्रान्यौत्रानन्यांश्च पार्थिवान्॥
en: Then comes the fifteenth Parva, named Ashramvasika, in which, abdicating the kingdom and accompanied by Gandhari and Vidura, the King Dhritarashtra went to the forest. Seeing this, virtuous Pritha (Kunti) ever engaged in serving her superiors, left the kingdom of her sons and followed the old couple.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: लोकान्तरगतान्वीरानपश्यत्पुनरागतान्। ऋषेः प्रसादात्कृष्णस्य दृष्ट्वाश्चर्यमनुत्तमम्॥
en: His wonderful seeing of the spirits of the slain heroes through the favour of Vyasa.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: त्यक्त्वा शोकं सदारश्च सिद्धि परमिकां गतः। यत्र धर्मं समाश्रित्य विदुरः सुगतिं गतः॥
en: On this the old monarch abandoned his sorrow and acquired with his wife the highest fruits of his virtuous deeds Vidura also attained to the highest state, having learned on virtue all his life.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: संजयश्च सहामात्यो विद्वान्गावल्गणिर्वशी। ददर्श नारदं यत्र धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: The learned son of Gavalgana the wise and learned Sanjaya also, attained to the highest state. Then it relates the meeting of the just king Yudhishthira with Narada.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: नारदाच्चैव शुश्राव वृष्णीनां कदनं महत्। एतदाश्रमवासाख्यं पर्वोक्तं महदद्भुतम्॥
en: Yudhishthira heard from Narada destruction of the Vrishni race. Thus is described this wonderful Parva, called Ashramvasika.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: द्विचत्वारिंशदध्यायाः पर्वैतदभिसंख्यया। सहस्रमेकं श्लोकानां पञ्च श्लोकशतानि च॥ घडेव च तथा श्लोकाः संख्यातास्तत्त्वदर्शिना। अतः परं निबोधेदं मौसलं पर्व दारुणम्॥
en: The number of chapters in it is forty two and the number of slokas, composed by the great Rishi, learned in truth, is one thousand five hundred and six. Then is told the terrible Mausala Parva.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: यत्र ते पुरुषव्याघ्राः शस्त्रस्पर्शहता युधि। ब्रह्मदण्डविनिष्पिष्टाः समीपे लवणाम्भसः॥ आपाने पानकलिता दैवेनाभिप्रचोदिताः। एरकारूपिभिर्वर्जेनिजरितरेतरम्॥
en: It relates how on account of the Brahmana a curse, when they were all deprived of their senses with drink, those tigers of men (belonging to the Vrishni race), with many scars of battle on their bodies, slew one another on the shores of the salt-sea with Eraka grass which became deadly thunders in their hands,

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: यत्र सर्वक्षयं कृत्वा तावुभौ रामकेशवौ। नातिचक्रामतुः कालं प्राप्तं सर्वहरं महत्॥
en: It then relates that Rama and Krishna, after destroying their race, did not rise superior to the way of all-destroying time.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: यत्रार्जुनो द्वारवतीमेत्य वृष्णिविनाकृताम्। दृष्ट्वा विषादमगमत्परां चार्तिं नरर्षभः॥
en: Then is described the arrival of Arjuna, the foremost of men, at Dwarka and his sorrow and affliction seeing the city destitute of the Vrishnis.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: स संस्कृत्य नरश्रेष्ठं मातुलं शौरिमात्मनः। ददर्श यदुवीराणामापाने वैशसं महत्॥
en: Performing the funeral ceremony of his maternal uncle Vasudeva, the foremost man of the Yadu dynasty, he saw the Yadu heroes lying dead where they had been drinking.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: शरीरं वासुदेवस्य रामस्य च महात्मनः। संस्कारं लम्भयामास वृष्णीनां च प्रधानतः॥
en: He then performed the cremation ceremonies of the illustrious Krishna and Balarama and of the other chief men of the Yadu race.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: स वृद्धबालमादाय द्वारवत्यास्ततो जनम्। ददर्शापदि कष्टायां गाण्डीवस्य पराभवम्॥
en: Then is described the journey of Arjuna from Dwarka with the women and children, the old and the decrepit and the great calamity he met with on the way. He also saw the overthrow of his Gandiva.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: सर्वेषां चैव दिव्यानामस्तत्राणामप्रसन्नताम्। नाशं वृष्णिकलत्राणां प्रभावानामनित्यताम्॥
en: He also saw unpropitiousness of his celestial weapons. Seeing that it was impossible to protect the Yadu women.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: दृष्ट्वा निर्वेदमापन्नो व्यासवाक्यप्रचोदितः। धर्मराजं समासाद्य संन्यासं समरोचयत्॥
en: And seeing all this, he went to Yudhishthira by the advice of Vyasa and asked permission to adopt the life of an ascetic.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: इत्येतन्मौसलं पर्व षोडशं परिकीर्तितम्। अध्यायाष्टौ समाख्याताः श्लोकानां च शतत्रयम्।। श्लोकानां विंशतिश्चैव संख्याता तत्त्वदर्शिना। महाप्रस्थानिकं तस्मादूर्ध्वं सप्तदशं स्मृतम्॥
en: Thus is described the sixteenth Parva, called Mausala Parva. Its number of chapters is eight and the number of slokas, composed by Vyasa, learned in truth, is three hundred and twenty. The next is Mahaprasthanika, the seventeenth Parva.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: यत्र राज्यं परित्यज्य पाण्डवाः पुरुषर्षभाः। द्रौपद्या सहिता देव्या महाप्रस्थानमास्थिताः॥
en: It relates that the best of men, the Pandavas, abdicating their kingdom went with Draupadi in their great journey (Mahaprasthana.)

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: यत्र तेऽग्नि ददृशिरे लौहित्यं प्राप्य सागरम्। यत्राग्निना चोदितश्च पार्थस्तस्मै महात्मने॥
en: They met with Agni when they arrived at the sea of red waters. Asked by Agni, the highsouled Partha.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: ददौ संपूज्य तद्दिव्यं गाण्डीवं धनुरुत्तमम्। यत्र भ्रातृन्निपतितान् द्रौपदी च युधिष्ठिरः॥ दृष्ट्वा हित्वा जगामैव सर्वाननवलोकयन्। एतत्सप्तदशं पर्व महाप्रस्थानिकं स्मृतम्॥
en: After worshipping him duly, returned to him the great celestial bow Gandiva. Yudhishthira went on his journey and did not look back when one afier the other of his brothers, including Draupadi dropped down dead. Thus is told the seventeenth Parva, called, Mahaprasthanika.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: यत्राध्यायास्त्रयः प्रोक्ताः श्लोकानां च शतत्रयम्। विंशतिश्च तथा श्लोकाः संख्यातास्तत्त्वदर्शिना॥३६७।
en: There are three chapters in it and the number of slokas, composed by all truthknowing Vyasa, is three hundred and twenty.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: स्वर्गपर्व ततो ज्ञेयं दिव्यं यत्तदमानुषम्। प्राप्तं दैवस्थं स्वर्गान्नेष्टवान्यत्र धर्मराट्॥
en: Know, the Parva that comes next is called Svarga, full of heavenly matters; in which is related how the celestial car came to take Yudhishthira.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: आरोढुं सुमहाप्राज्ञ आनृशंस्याच्छुना विना। तामस्या विचला ज्ञात्वा स्थिति धर्मे महात्मनः॥ श्वरूपं यत्र तत्त्यक्त्वा धर्मेणासौ समन्वितः। स्वर्ग प्राप्तः स च तथा यातना विपुला भृशम्॥
en: He however, declined to ascend it without the dog that accompanied him. Seeing the steady adherence of the illustrious Yudhishthira to virtue Dharma giving up the from of the dog, showed himself to the king. Then Yudhishthira, attaining to the celestial regions, felt much pain.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: देवदूतेन नरकं यत्र व्याजेन दर्शितम्। शुश्राव यत्र धर्मात्मा भ्रातृणां करुणा गिरः॥
en: The celestial messenger showed him hell by deception, where the virtuous minded king heard the heart-rending lamentations of his brothers,

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: निदेशे वर्तमानानां देशे तत्रैव वर्तताम्। अनुदर्शितश्च धर्मेण देवराज्ञा च पाण्डवः॥
en: Suffering in that region by the laws of Yama. This was shown to Yudhishthira by Indra and Dharma.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: आप्लुत्याकाशगङ्गायां देहं त्यक्त्वा स मानुषम्। स्वधर्मनिर्जितं स्थानं स्वर्गे प्राप्य स धर्मराट्॥
en: Then Yudhishthira, after bathing in the celestial Ganga, gave up his human body and gained that state which his acts merited.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: मुमुदे पूजितः सर्वैः सेन्द्रैः सुरगणैः सह। एतदष्टादशं पर्व प्रोक्तं व्यासेन धीमता॥
en: He lived in happiness, honoured by Indra and the celestial. This is the eighteenth Parva narrated by the illustrious Vyasa.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: अध्यायाः पञ्च संख्याताः पर्वण्यस्मिन्महात्मना। श्लोकानां द्वे शते चैव प्रसंख्याते तपोधनाः॥ नव श्लोकास्तथैवान्ये संख्याताः परमर्षिणा। अष्टादशैवमेतानि पर्वाण्येतान्यशेषतः॥
en: The number of chapters in it is five and its numbers of slokas, O Rishis, composed by the great Vyasa, is two hundred and nine. These are the contents of the eighteen Parvas.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: खिलेषु हरिवंशश्च भविष्यं च प्रकीर्तितम्। दश श्लोकसहस्राणि विंशच्छ्लोकशतानि च॥ खिलेषु हरिवंशे च संख्यातानि महर्षिणा। एतत्सर्वं समाख्यातं भारते पर्वसंग्रहः॥
en: There are Harivansha and Bhavishya in its appendix. The number of slokas, composed by the great Rishi in the Harivansha, is twelve thousand. These are the contents of the chapters called Parva Sangraha in the Bharata.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: अष्टादश समाजग्मुरक्षौहिण्यो युयुत्सया। तन्महादारुणं युद्धमहान्यष्टादशाभवत्॥
en: Eighteen Akshauhinis of soldiers assembled to fight and the battle raised for eighteen days.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: यो विद्याच्चतुरो वेदान् साङ्गोपनिषदो द्विजः। न चाख्यानमिदं विद्यान्नैव स स्याद्विचक्षणः॥
en: He who is learned in the four Vedas with all the Angas and Upanishads, but does not know this history, cannot be considered to be wise.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: अर्थशास्त्रमिदं प्रोक्तं धर्मशास्त्रमिदं महत्। कामशास्त्रमिदं प्रोक्तं व्यासेनामितबुद्धिना॥
en: The greatly intelligent Vyasa has spoken it as a treatise on Dharma, Artha and Kama.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: श्रुत्वा त्विदमुपाख्यानं श्राव्यमन्यन्न रोचते। पुंस्कोकिलगिरं श्रुत्वा रूक्षा ध्वांक्षस्य वागिव॥३८२
en: Those who have heard it can never listen to other histories, as those who have heard the sweet voice of the male Kokila (bird) can never listen to the harsh cawing of the crows.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: इतिहासोत्तमादस्माज्जायन्ते कविबुद्धयः। पञ्चभ्य इव भूतेभ्यो लोकसंविधयस्त्रयः॥
en: As the three worlds have been created from the five elements, so inspiration of all poets proceeds from this excellent work.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: अस्याख्यानस्य विषये पुराणं वर्तते द्विजाः। अन्तरिक्षस्य विषये प्रजा इव चतुर्विधाः॥
en: O Brahmanas, as four kinds of creatures depend on space for their existence so all the Puranas depend on this history,

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: क्रियागुणानां सर्वेषामिदमाख्यानमाश्रयः। इन्द्रियाणां समस्तानां चित्रा इव मनःक्रियाः॥
en: As all the senses are dependent on the wonderful workings of the mind, so all the acts and moral qualities depend on this treatise.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: अनाश्रित्यैतदाख्यानं कथा भुवि न विद्यते। आहारमनपाश्रित्य शरीरस्येव धारणम्॥
en: As the body depends on the food is takes, so all the stories current in the world depend on this work.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: इदं कविवरैः सर्वैराख्यानमुपजीव्यते। उदयप्रेप्सुभिर्भूत्यैरभिजात इवेश्वरः॥
en: As servants, wishing to have elevation, always depend on their noble masters, so do all poets depend on this Bharata.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: अस्य काव्यस्य कवयो न समर्था विशेषणे। साधोरिव गृहस्थस्य शेषास्त्रय इवाश्रमाः॥
en: As the blessed domestic Ashrama cannot be surprised by the other Ashramas, so can no poet surpass this poem.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: धर्मे मतिर्भवतु वः सततोत्थितानां स ह्येक एव परलोकगतस्य बन्धुः। अर्थाः स्त्रियश्च निपुणैरपि सेव्यमाना नैवाप्तभावमुपयान्ति न च स्थिरत्वम्॥
en: O Rishis, be up and doing. Let your hearts be fixed in virtue, for virtue is the only friend in the other world. Even the most intelligent men can never make their wealth and wives their own hy carefully cherishing them. They are not things lasting.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: द्वैपायनौष्ठपुटनिःसृतमप्रमेयं पुण्यं पवित्रमथ पापहरं शिवं च। यो भारतं समधिगच्छति वाच्यमानं किं तस्य पुष्करजलैरभिषेचनेन॥
en: The Bharata, uttered from the lips of Dvaipayana is matchless, it is sacred, it is virtue itself. It destroys sins and produces good. What is the necessity for him, who hears it when it is being recited, to bathe in the sacred Pushkara!

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: यदह्नात् कुरुते पापं ब्राह्मणस्त्विन्द्रियैश्चरन्। महाभारतमाख्याय सन्ध्यां मुच्यति पश्चिमाम्॥३९१
en: What ever sin committed in the day by a Brahmana through his senses are all purged off, if he reads the Bharata in the evening.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: यद्रात्रौ कुरुते पापं कर्मणा मनसा गिरा। महाभारतमाख्याय पूर्व सन्ध्यां प्रमुच्यते॥
en: Whatever sins also he might have cominit in the night by deeds words or mind are all purged off if he reads the Bharata in the first twilight of the morning.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: यो गोशतं कनकशृङ्गमयं ददाति विप्राय वेदविदुषे च बहुश्रुताय। पुण्यां च भारतकथां शृणुयाच्च नित्यं तुल्यं फलं भवति तस्य च तस्य चैव।। ३९३।
en: He who gives to a Brahmana, learned in the Vedas and other sciences, one hundred cows with their horns plated with gold and he who listens, daily to the sacred histories of the Bharata, gain equal merit.

description: Brief introduction to the story of Mahabharata
sn: आख्यानं तदिदमनुत्तमं महार्थं विज्ञेयं महदिह पर्वसंग्रहेण। श्रुत्वादौ भवति नृणां सुखावगाहं विस्तीर्णं लवणजलं यथा प्लवेन॥
en: As the wide ocean can be easily crossed by men having boats, so this extensive history of great excellence and deep meaning can be understood by the help of this chapter, which is called Parva-Sangraha.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: सौतिरुवाच जनमेजयः पारिक्षितः सह भ्रातृभिः भ्रातृभिः कुरुक्षेत्रे दीर्घसत्रमुपास्ते। तस्य भ्रातरस्त्रयः श्रुतसेन। उग्रसेनो भीमसेन इति। तेषु तत्सत्रमुपासीनेष्वागच्छत्सारमेयः॥
en: Sauti said: The son of Parikshit, Janamejaya, with his brothers, was attending his long sacrifice in the field of Kurukshetra. His brothers were three, namely-Shrutasena, Ugrasena and Bhimasena. When they were sitting at the sacrifice, there came the son of Sarama.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: जनमेजयस्य भ्रातृभिरभिहतो भ्रातृभिरभिहतो रोरूयमाणो मातुः समीपमुपागच्छत्॥
en: He, being beaten by the brothers of Janamejaya, went to his mother weeping.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: पुत्रदुःखार्ता तं माता रोरूयमाणमुवाच 'किं रोदिषि, केनास्यभिहत' इति॥
en: His mother, seeing him weep, asked him, “Why are you weeping, who has beaten you?"

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: प्रत्युवाच-'जनमेजयस्य भ्रातृभिरभिहतोऽस्मि' इति॥
en: Being thus questioned, he replied to his mother, “I have been beaten by the brothers of Janamejaya."

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: तं माता प्रत्युवाच-'व्यक्तं त्वया तत्रापराद्धम्, येनास्यभिहतः' इति॥
en: And then his mother said, "You must have committed some fault, for which you have been beaten.'

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: स तां पुनरुवाच 'नापराध्यामि, किंचिन्नावेक्षे, हवींषि नावलिह' इति॥
en: He replied, “I committed no fault. I did not lick the sacrificial ghee, I did not cast even a look at it."

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: तच्छ्रुत्वा माता सरमा तत्सत्रमुपागच्छत्, यत्र स जनमेजयः सह भ्रातृभिर्दीर्घसत्रमुपास्ते॥
en: Hearing this her mother, being very sorry for the affliction of his son, went to the place where Janamejaya with his brothers were attending his long sacrifice.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: तया क्रुद्धया तत्रोक्त 'अयं मे पुत्रो न किंचिदपराध्यति, नावेक्षते, हवींषि, नावलेढि, किमर्थमभिहतः' इति॥
en: She angrily addressed Janamejaya thus, “My son did not commit any fault. He did not lick your sacrificial ghee, he did not even look at it. Why did you then beat him?”

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: न किंचिदुक्तवन्तस्ते सा तानुवाच 'यस्मादयमभिहतो ऽनपकारी, तस्माददृष्टं त्वां भयमागमिष्यति' इति।॥
en: They did not (condescend) to reply to her. On this she said, “ As you beat my son who did not commit any fault, so will evil come to you when you least expect it."

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: जनमेजय एवमुक्तो देवशुन्या सरमया भृशं संभ्रान्तो विषण्णश्चासीत्॥ स
en: Janamejaya, having been thus cursed by the celestial bitch, Sarama, was very much alarmed and dejected.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: तस्मिन्सत्रे समाप्ते हास्तिनपुरं प्रत्येत्य पुरोहितमनुरूपमन्विष्यमाणः परं यत्नमकरोद्यो मे पापकृत्यां शमयेदिति॥
en: After finishing the sacrifice, he returned to Hastinapur and took great pains to find out a priest who could neutralise the effect of the curse by procuring absolution from his sin.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: स कदाचिन्मृगयां गतः पारिक्षितो जनमेजयः कस्मिंश्चित्स्वविषय आश्रममपश्यत्॥
en: Janamejaya, the son of Parikshit, when out in hunting, saw in one part of his dominion a holy hermitage.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: तत्र कश्चिद्ऋषिरासाञ्चक्रे श्रुतश्रवा नाम। तपस्यभिरतः पुत्र आस्ते सोमश्रवा नाम॥
en: Where lived a Rishi, named Srutashrava; he had a son who was named Somashrava, who was deeply engaged in austere penances.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: तस्य तं पुत्रमभिगम्य जनमेजयः पारिक्षितः पौरोहित्याय ववे॥
en: Being desirous to make the son of the Rishi his priest, Janamejaya,

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: स नमस्कृत्य तमृषिमुवाच-'भगवन्यं तव पुत्रो मम पुरोहितोऽस्तु' इति॥
en: Saluted him and said, "O Bhagvan, allow your son to be my priest."

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: स एवमुक्तः प्रत्युवाच जनमेजयम् 'भो जनमेजय, पुत्रोऽयं मम सर्म्या जातो महातपस्वी स्वाध्यायसंपन्नो मत्तपोवीर्यसंभृतो मच्छुक्रं पीतवत्यास्तस्याः कुक्षौ जातः॥
en: Being thus addressed by Janamejaya, the Rishi replied, “O Janamejaya, my son is accomplished in the study of the Vedas, endued with my full asceticism and deep in devotion, but he is born in the womb of a serpent who swallowed my vital fluid.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: समर्थोऽयं भवतः सर्वाः पापकृत्याः शमयितुमन्तरेण महादेवकृत्याम्॥
en: "He is able to absolve you from all sins except those committed against Mahadeva.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: अस्य त्वेकमुपांशुव्रतं यदेनं कश्चिद् ब्राह्मण: कंचिदर्थमभियाचेत्तं तस्मै दद्यादयम् यद्येतदुत्सहसे ततो नयस्वैनम्' इति॥
en: But he observes a particular rule, namely he grants to a Brahmana whatever he asks from him. If you can allow him to do it, you can then take him."

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: तेनैवमुक्तो जनमेजयस्तं प्रत्युवाच-'भगवंस्तत् तथा भविष्यति ॥
en: Janamejaya thus addressed by the Rishi, said "It shall be as you say.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: स तं पुरोहितमुपादायोपावृत्तो भ्रातूनुवाच-'मयाऽयं वृत उपाध्याय यदयं ब्रूयात्तत् कार्यमविचारयद्भिर्भवद्भिः' इति। तेनैवमुक्ता भ्रातरस्तस्य तथा चक्रुः स तथा भ्रातृन् संदिश्य तक्षशिलां प्रत्यभिप्रतस्थे तं च देशं वशे स्थापयामास॥
en: He then took him as his priest and returned to his capital. He then addressed his brothers thus, I have chosen this person as my priest. Whatever he will command to do must be obeyed by you without questioning.” The brothers did as they were requested. Giving these instructions to his brothers he marched against Takshashila and conquered that country.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे कश्चिद् ऋषिौम्यो नामायोदः। तस्य शिष्यास्त्रयो बभूवुः॥ उपमन्युरारुणिर्वेदश्चेति स एकं शिष्यमारुणिं पाञ्चाल्यं प्रेषयामास 'गच्छ, केदारखण्डं बधान' इति॥
en: About this time there was also a Rishi, named Ayoda-Dhaumya. He had three disciples namely Upamanyu, Aruni and Veda. One day the Rishi asked one of these three disciples, Aruni of Panchala, to go and stop a breach in the water-course in his field.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: स उपाध्यायेन संदिष्ट आरुणिः पाञ्चाल्यस्तत्र गत्वा तम्, केदारखण्डं बर्द्ध नाशकत्। क्लिश्यमानोऽपश्यदुपायम् भवत्वेवं करिष्यामि॥ स तत्र संविवेश केदारखण्डे। शयाने च तथा तस्मिंस्तदुदकं तस्थौ॥
en: Thus ordered by the preceptor, Aruni of Panchala went to the spot, but could not stop the breach. He was very sorry that he could not carry out his preceptor's bidding, but at last he saw a means and he said, “I shall do it in this way." He entered into the breach and there laid himself down and thus the water was stopped.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: ततः कदाचिदुपाध्याय आपोदो धौम्यः शिष्यानपृच्छत् 'क्व आरुणिः पाञ्चाल्यो गतः' इति॥
en: Sometime after, the preceptor AyudaDhaumya enquired of his other disciples where Aruni of Panchala went.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: ते तं प्रत्यूचुः ‘भगवंस्त्वयैव प्रेषितः' गच्छ केदारखण्डं बधान इति। स एवमुक्तस्तान् शिष्यान् प्रत्युवाच'तस्मात्तत्र सर्वे गच्छामो यत्र स गतः' इति।॥
en: Having been thus addressed, they replied, “Sir, he has been sent by you to stop the breach of the water-course in the field.” Dhaumya, thus reminded, said to his pupils, “Let us all go to the place where he is."

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: स तत्र गत्वा तस्याहानाय शब्दं चकार-'भो आरुणे, पाञ्चाल्य, क्वासि वत्स, एहि, इति॥
en: Having gone there, he cried, “O Aruni of Panchala, where are you? Come here, my child."

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: स तच्छ्रुत्वा आरुणिरुपाध्यायवाक्यं तस्मात् केदारखण्डात् सहसोत्याय तमुपाध्यायमुपतस्थे॥
en: Having heard the voice of his preceptor, Aruni rose speedily from the breach and stood before him.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: प्रोवाच चैनम् 'अयमस्मि, अत्र केदारखण्डे निःसरमाणमुदकमवारणीयं संरोद्धं संविष्टः, भगवच्छब्दं श्रुत्वैव, सहसा विदार्य केदारखण्डम्, भवन्तमुपस्थितः। तदभिवादये भगवन्तम्, आज्ञापयतु भवान् कमर्थं करवाणि इति॥२९-३०॥
en: Addressing his preceptor Aruni said. “I was in the breach of the water-course. Having been unable to stop it by and other means, I entered myself into the breach to prevent the water from running out. It is only when I heard your honour's voice that I have left it and allowed the waters to escape. I salute you, great teacher, tell me what I am to do now.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: स एवमुक्त उपाध्यायः प्रत्युवाच 'यस्माद्भवान् केदारखण्डं विदार्योत्थितः, तस्मादुद्दालक एव नाम्ना भवान् भविष्यति इत्युपाध्यायेनानुगृहीतः॥
en: The preceptor, thus addressed, said, "As you have opened the water-course in getting from the ditch, you shall be henceforth known as Uddalaka as a mark of your action" and blessed him.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: 'यस्माच्च त्वया मद्वचनमनुष्ठितम्, तस्माच्छ्रेयो ऽवाप्स्यसि। सर्वे च ते वेदाः प्रतिभास्यन्ति, सर्वाणि च धर्मशास्त्राणि' इति॥
en: And as you have obeyed my command, you shall obtain good fortune. All the Vedas will shine in you and so will all the Dharma Shastras."

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: स एवमुक्त उपाध्यायेनेष्टं देशं जगाम। अथापर: शिष्योऽस्यैवापोदस्य धौम्यस्योपमन्युर्नाम॥
en: Being thus blessed by his preceptor, Aruni went away to the country where his heart longed to go. The name of another AyudaDhaumya's disciples was Upamanyu.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: तं चोपाध्यायः प्रेषयामास-'वत्सोपमन्यो! गा रक्षस्व' इति॥
en: Him the preceptor thus addressed, “Go my child, look after my kine.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: स उपाध्यायवचनादरक्षद्गाः। स चाहनि गा रक्षित्वा दिवसक्षये गुरुगृहमागम्योपाध्यायस्याग्रतः स्थित्वा नमश्चक्रे॥
en: As ordered by his preceptor, he went to look after the cows. Having tended them all day, he came back to the preceptor's house in the evening. He then stood before him and respectfully saluted him.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: तमुपाध्यायः पीवानमपश्यदुवाच चैनं 'वत्सोपमन्यो केन! वृत्तिं कल्पयसि, पीवानसि दृढम् इति॥
en: His preceptor, seeing him in the best of health, asked, “Upamanyu, my child, by what means you support yourself? You exceedingly plump?"

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: स उपाध्यायं प्रत्युवाच-'भो भैक्ष्येण वृत्तिं कल्पयामि' इति॥
en: He answered to his preceptor, “I support myself by begging."

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: तमुपाध्यायः 'मय्यनिवेद्य भैक्ष्य नोपयोक्तव्यम्' इति। स तथेत्युक्तो भैक्ष्यं चरित्वोपाध्यायाय न्यवेदयत्॥
en: are The preceptor said, “You should not appropriate what you receive by begging without offering it to me." Being thus told he went away and offered all that he got by begging to his preceptor;

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: स तस्मादुपाध्यायःसर्वमेव भैक्ष्यमगृह्णात्। स तथेत्युक्तः पुनररक्षद्गाः। अहनि रक्षित्वा निशामुखे गुरुकुलमागम्य गुरोरग्रत:स्थित्वा नमश्चक्रे॥
en: And the preceptor took from him all that he got. He, being thus treated, went away to look after the cattle. And after having tended them all day he came back in the evening. He stood before his preceptor and respectfully saluted him.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: तमुपाध्यायस्तथापि पीवानमेव दृष्ट्वोवाच'वत्सोपमन्यो! सर्वमशेषतस्ते भैक्ष्यं गृह्णामि। केनेदानीं वृत्तिं कल्पयसि' इति॥
en: The preceptor, seeing him still as plump as before, said, “Upamanyu, my child. I take from you all that you get by begging. How do you contrive to support yourself now?”

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: 'भगवते निवेद्य पूर्वमपरं चरामि। तेन वृत्तिं कल्पयामि' इति॥
en: Being thus questioned, he answered to his preceptor, “Sir, after giving you all I get by begging, I go again to beg to support myself.”

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: तमुपाध्यायः प्रत्युवाच 'नैषा न्याय्या 'नैषा न्याय्या गुरुवृत्तिः अन्येषामपि भैक्ष्योपजीविनां वृत्त्युपरोधं करोषि, इत्येवं वर्तमानो लुब्धोऽसि' इति॥
en: The preceptor, said “This is not the way you should obey your preceptor. You diminish the support of others who live by begging. Having thus supported yourself you have showed that you are coveteous.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: स तथेत्त्युक्त्वा गा अरक्षत्। रक्षित्वा पुनरुपाध्यायगृहमागम्योपाध्यायस्याग्रतः स्थित्वा नमश्चक्रे॥
en: Having assented to all his preceptor's words, he went away (again) to tend the kine Having done it, he stood before the preceptor and respectfully saluted him.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: तमुपाध्यायस्तथापि पीवानमेव दृष्ट्वा पुनरुवाच-'वत्सोपमन्यो! अहं ते सर्वं भक्ष्यं गृह्णामि न चान्यच्चरसि। पीवानसि भृशम् केन वृत्तिं कल्पयसि' इति॥
en: The preceptor saw that he was still plump and said, "Upamanyu, my child, I take from you all that you get by begging. You do not also go out begging for the second time. How do you now manage to support yourself?”

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: स एवमुक्तस्तमुपाध्यायं प्रत्युवाच-'भो एतासां गवां पयसा वृत्ति कल्पयामि' इति। तमुवाचोपाध्यायः 'नैतन्याय्यं पय उपयोक्तुम्। भवतो मया नाभ्यनुज्ञात' इति॥
en: Upamanyu, thus questioned, replied, “Sir, I now support myself with the milk of these cows.” Hearing which the preceptor said, “It is not proper for you to drink the milk, since you were not addressed by me."

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: स तथेति प्रतिज्ञाय गा रक्षित्वा पुनरुपाध्यायगृहमेत्य गुरोरग्रत: स्थित्वा नमश्चक्रे॥
en: He assented to his preceptor's words and went to tend the cattle. Having done it he stood before his preceptor and respectfully saluted him.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: तमुपाध्याय: पीवानमेव दृष्टोवाच 'वत्सोपमन्यो भैक्ष्य नाश्नासि, न चान्यच्चरसि, पयो न पीबसि, पीवानसि भृशम् केनेदानी वृत्ति कल्पयसि' इति॥
en: The preceptor saw that he was still fat and he asked, “Upamanyu my child, you do not support yourself by alms, nor do you go begging for the second time, nor do you drink the milk of my cows, but you are still fat, how do you support yourself now?"

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: स एवमुक्त उपाध्यायं प्रत्युवाच-'भोः फेनं पिबामि यमिमे वत्सा मातृणां स्तनात्पिबन्त उद्गिरन्ति॥
en: Thus questioned he said, “I now drink the froth that the calves throw out when they suck their mother's teats."

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: तमुपाध्यायः प्रत्युवाच ‘एते त्वदनुकम्पया गुणवन्तो वत्साः प्रभूततरं फेनमुद्गिरन्ति। तदेषामपि तदेषामपि वत्सानां वृत्त्युपरोधं करोष्येवं वर्तमानः। फेनमपि भवान्न पातुमर्हति' इति। स तथेति प्रतिश्रुत्य पुनररक्षद्गाः॥
en: The preceptor replied, “The good calves, out of kindness towards you, throw out a large quantity of froth. You should not stand in the way of their full meal. Know, it is not proper for you to drink the froth.” Upamanyu assented to this and went to tend the cattle.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: तथा प्रतिषिद्धो भैक्ष्यं नाश्नाति न चान्यच्चरति पयो न पिबति। फेनं नोपयुङ्क्ते स कदा चिदरण्ये क्षुधार्तोऽर्कपत्राण्यभक्षयत्॥ तैरर्कपत्रैक्षितैः क्षारतिक्तकटुरूक्षैस्तीक्ष्णविपाकैश्चक्षुष्युपहतोऽन्धो बभूव। ततः सोऽन्धोऽपि चङ्कम्यमाण: कूपे पपात॥
en: Thus prevented by his preceptor (from supporting himself,) he did not feed on alms, he did not drink the milk, or taste the froth, he had thus nothing to eat. One day being very much oppressed by hunger he ate the leaves of Arka tree in a forest. His eyes were affected by the pungent, acrimonious, crude and saline qualities of the leaves and he became blind. When he was thus walking about feeling his way he fell into a deep well.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: अथ तस्मिन्ननागच्छति, सूर्ये चास्ताचलावलम्बिनि उपाध्यायः शिष्यानवोचत्-'नायात्युपमन्युः।' ते ऊचु 'वनं गतो गा रक्षितुम्' इति॥
en: As he did not return that day to the Rishi's house when the sun was sinking down behind the summit of the western mountain, the preceptor said to his pupils that Upamanyu had not yet returned. And they replied that he had gone to the forest to tend the cattle.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: तानाह उपाध्याय:-'मयोपमन्युः सर्वतः प्रतिषिद्धः स नियतं कुपितस्ततो नागच्छति चिरं ततोऽन्वेष्यः' इत्येवमुक्त्वा शिष्यैः सार्धमरण्यं गत्वा तस्याह्वानाय शब्दं चकार-'भो उपमन्यो! क्वासि वत्स! एहि' इति॥
en: On this the preceptor said, Upamanyu is displeased, because he has been prevented from the use of everything. He is therefore, making late to come home. Let us go and find him out." Having said this, he went with his pupils into the forest and called aloud. “Ho, Upamanyu, where are you? My child, come here."

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: स उपाध्यायवचनं श्रुत्वा प्रत्युवाचोच्चैः-'अयमस्मिन् कूपे पतितोऽहम्' इति। तमुपाध्यायः प्रत्युवाच-'कथं त्वमस्मिन् कूपे पतितः' इति॥
en: Having heard the voice of his preceptor he replied, “I have fallen into this well.” The preceptor asked, “How have you fallen into this well?"

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: स उपाध्यायं प्रत्युवाच-'अर्कपत्राणि भक्षयित्वाऽन्धीभूतोऽस्मि। अतः कूपे पत्तितः' इति॥
en: He answered to the preceptor, “I have become blind by eating the leaves of Arka tree and thus fallen into this well."

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: तमुपाध्यायः प्रत्युवाच-'अश्विनौ स्तुहि। तौ देवभिषजौ त्वां चक्षुष्मन्तं कर्तारौ' इति। स एवमुक्त उपाध्यायेनोपमन्युरश्विनौ स्तोतुमुपचक्रमे देवावश्विनौ वाग्भिधंग्भिः॥
en: On this the preceptor replied, “Worship the twin Ashvinis, the physicians of the celestials and they will restore you your sight.” Thus addressed, Upamanyu began to worship the twin Ashvinis by reciting the following words from the Rigveda.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: प्रपूर्वगौ पूर्वजौ चित्रभानू गिरा वाऽऽशंसामि तपसा ह्यनन्तौ। वधिक्षिपन्तौ भुवनानि विश्वा॥
en: You have existed before the creation, O you first-born beings; you are manifest in this wonderful universe of five elements. You are . infinite, you are the course of nature and intelligent Soul that pervades all. I desire to obtain you by the knowledge, derived from hearing and meditation, You are birds of beautiful feathers, that roost on the body which is likened to a tree. You are free from the three common attributes of all souls. You are beyond all comparison. You pervade the universe through its spirit in every created thing.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: हिरण्मयौ शकुनी साम्परायौ नासत्यदस्त्रौ सुनसौ वै जयन्तौ। वधिव्ययन्तावसितं विवस्वतः॥
en: You are golden eagles. You are the essence in which all things disappear. You are free from error and you do not deteriorate. You are of beautiful beaks. which will not unjustly wound and which are ever victorious in all fights. Having created the sun, you weave the wonderful cloth of night and day by the black and white threads. You have established with as the cloth thus woven two courses of action; one regarding the Devas and the other regarding the Pitris.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: ममुञ्चतामश्विनौ सौभगाय। तावत् सुवृत्तावनमन्त मायया वसत्तमा गा अरुणा उदावहन्॥
en: You set free the bird of life, seized by Time representing the infinite soul, so that it may be delivered to great happiness. Those that are greatly ignorant on account of the delusion of their senses, think that you, who have no attributes of matter, have forms.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: षष्टिश्च गावस्त्रिशताश्च धेनव एकं वत्सं सुवते तं दुहन्ति। स्तावश्विनौ दुहतो धर्ममुक्थ्यम्॥
en: Three hundred and sixty cows represented by three hundred and sixty days give birth to one calf which is year. This calf is the creator and destroyer of all. Those that search after truth, through following different routes, draw the milk of true knowledge with its help.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: एकां नाभिं सप्तशता अराः श्रिताः प्रधिष्वन्या विंशतिरर्पिता अराः। अनेमि चक्रं परिवर्ततेऽजरं मायाऽश्विनौ समनक्ति चर्षणी॥
en: The year is a navel of the wheel with seven hundred and twenty spokes, representing nights and days. The circumference of this wheel is without an end and is represented by twelve months. This wheel is full of delusion and does not know deterioration. It affects all creatures belonging to this or the other world. O Ashvinis, set this wheel in motion.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: एकं चक्रं वर्तते द्वादशारं घण्णाभिमेकाक्षमृतस्य धारणम्। स्तावश्विनौ मुञ्चतं मा विषीदतम्॥
en: The wheel of time represented by the year has also a nave, the six seasons. It has twelve spokes represented by the twelve signs of the Zodiac. This wheel of Time displays the fruits of all beings' actions. The Presiding Deities of Time obey this wheel. Bound as I am to its bound, O Ashvinis, makes me free from this wheel of Time.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: अश्विनाविन्दुममृतं वृत्तभूयौ तिरोधत्तामश्विनौ दासपत्नी। हित्वा गिरिमश्विनौ गा मुदा चरन्तौ तवृष्टिमह्ना प्रस्थितौ बलस्य॥
en: O Ashvinis, you are this universe of five elements. You are the objects that are enjoyed in this and the next world. Raise me beyond the influence of the five elements. You are the supreme Brahma, but you move on earth in forms and enjoy those pleasures that the senses give.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: युवां दिशो जनयथो दशाये समानं मूर्ध्नि रथयानं वियन्ति। तासां यातमृषयोऽनुप्रयान्ति देवा मनुष्याः क्षितिमाचरन्ति॥
en: You created ten points of the universe in the beginning of the creation. You have placed the sun and the moon above. The Rishis perform their Yajnas according to the course of the sun. The celestials and men also perform their Yajnas as settled for them and they enjoy the fruits of those acts.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: युवां वर्णान् विकुस्थो विश्वरूपां स्तेऽधिक्षियन्ते भुवनानि विश्वा। ते भानवोऽप्यनुसृताश्चरन्ति देवा मनुष्याः क्षितिमाचरन्ति॥
en: Mixing the ten colours, you have produced all the objects of form. The universe has sprung from these objects in which both the celestials and men and all creatures endued with life are engaged in their respective works.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: तौ नासत्यावश्विनौ वां महेऽहं स्रजं च यां विभृथः पुष्करस्य। तौ नासत्यावमृतावृतावृधावृते देवास्तत् प्रपदे न सूते॥
en: O Ashvinis, I worship you. I also worship the sky that is your handiwork. You are the ordainers of the fruits of all acts from which even the celestials are not free; you are, however, free from the fruits of your actions.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: मुखेन गर्भं लभेतां युवानी गतासुरेतत् प्रपदेन सूते। स्तावश्विनौ मुञ्चथो जीवसे गाः॥
en: You are the parents of all. You as males and females swallow the food which subsequently develops into the vital-fluid and blood. The new-born baby sucks her mother's breast, it is you who take the shape of the babe. O Ashvinis, restore my sight and protect my life."

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: स्तोतुं न शक्नोमि गुणैर्भवन्तौ चक्षुर्विहीनः पथि संप्रमोहः। दुर्गेऽहमस्मिन् पतितोऽस्मि कूपे युवां शरण्यौ शरणं प्रपद्ये॥
en: O Ashvinis, I am unable to praise both of you by describing your virtues. Now I am blind and can't even detect the right path. So, I have fallen down in this deep well. You only are capable to provide us shelter and therefore, 1 have come to seek your shelter.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: इत्येवं तेनाभिष्टुतावश्विनावाजग्मतुराहतुश्चैनम्-'प्रीतौ स्वः, एष तेऽपूपः, अशानैनम्' इति॥
en: When Upamanyu thus adored the twin Ashvinis, they appeared and said. "We are pleased with your devotion. Here is a cake for you. Take it and eat it."

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: स एवमुक्तः प्रत्युवाच-'नानृतमूचतुर्भगवन्तौ न त्वहमेतमपूपमुपयोक्तुमुत्सहे गुरवेऽनिवेद्य' इति॥
en: Thus addressed he replied, “O Ashvinis, your words never prove untrue. But I cannot take this cake without offering it to my preceptor.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: ततस्तमश्विनावूचतुः 'आवाभ्यां पुरस्ताद्भवत उपाध्यायेनैवमेवाभिष्टुताभ्यामपूपो दत्तः, उपयुक्तः स तेनानिवेद्य गुरवे। त्वमपि तथैव कुरुष्व यथा कृतमुपाध्यायेन' इति॥
en: The Ashvinis said-"Your preceptor also once invoked us, we gave him a cake and he took it without offering it to his teacher. Do what your preceptor did."

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: एवमुक्तः प्रत्युवाच-'एतत् प्रत्यनुनये भवन्तावश्विनौ, नोत्सहेऽहमनिवेद्य गुरवेऽपूपमुपयोक्तुम्' इति॥
en: Thus addressed he said, "O Ashvinis, I ask your pardon. I cannot take this cake without offering it to my preceptor.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: तमश्विनावाहतु:-'प्रीतौ स्वस्तवानया गुरुभक्त्या उपाध्यायस्य ते कार्णायसा दन्ता भवतोऽपि हिरण्मया भविष्यन्ति, चक्षुष्मांश्च भविष्यसीति, श्रेयश्चावाप्स्यसि इति॥
en: The Ashvinis said, “We are pleased with your this devotion to your preceptor. Your teacher's teeth are of black iron, yours will be those of Gold. Your sight will be restored and you will possess good fortune."

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: एवमुक्तोऽश्विभ्यां लब्धचक्षुरुपाध्यायसकाशमागम्याभ्यवादयत्॥ आचचक्षे च स चास्य प्रीतिमान् बभूव।। आह चैनम् 'यथाऽश्विनावाहतुस्तथा त्वं श्रेयोऽवाप्स्यसि॥ सर्वे च ते वेदाः प्रतिभास्यन्ति, सर्वाणि च धर्मशास्त्राणि, इति। एषा तस्यापि परीक्षोपमन्योः॥
en: Having been thus addressed by the Ashvinis he regained his sight. He then went to his preceptor, saluted him and told him all that had happened. And his preceptor was very much pleased with him and told him that he would obtain immense prosperity as the Ashvinis had said. All the Vedas will shine on him and so also all Dharma Shastras. This was his trial.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: अथापरः शिष्यस्तस्यैवायोदस्य धौम्यस्य वेदो नाम। तमुपाध्यायः समादिदेश-'वत्स, वेद इहास्यतां तावन्मम गृहे कञ्चित् कालम्। शुश्रूषुणा च भवितव्यम्। श्रेयस्ते भविष्यति' इति॥
en: The other pupil of Ayuda Dhaumya was called Veda. One day his preceptor addressed him thus, “Veda, my child, remain in my house and serve your teacher. It will be to your profit."

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: स तथेत्युक्त्वा गुरुकुले दीर्घकालं गुरुशुश्रूषणपरोऽवसत्-गौरिव नित्यं गुरुणा धूर्षु नियोज्यमानः शीतोष्णक्षुत्तृष्णादुःखसहः सर्वत्राप्रतिकूलः। तस्य महताकालेन गुरुः परितोषं जगाम॥
en: Veda, having assented to it, remained long in the family of his preceptor, being always mindful to serve him. Like an ox under the burden of his owner, he bore heat and cold, hunger and thirst, without any complaint at all times; and many years thus passed before his preceptor was satisfied.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: तत्परितोषाच्च श्रेयः सर्वज्ञतां चावाप। एषा तस्यापि परीक्षा वेदस्य॥
en: Veda obtained good fortune and universal knowledge as the result of his preceptor's satisfaction. This was his trial.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: स उपाध्यायेनानुज्ञातः समावृत्तस्तस्माद्गुरुकुलवासाद् गृहाश्रमं प्रत्यपद्यत। तस्यापि स्वगृहे वसतस्त्रयः शिष्याः बभूवुः। स शिष्यान्नकिंचिदुवाच कर्म वा क्रियता गुरुशुश्रूषा चेति। दुःखाभिज्ञो हि गुरुकुलवासस्य शिष्यान् परिक्लेशेन योजयितुं नेयेष॥
en: Having received his preceptor's permission he left his house after the completion of living at his house and entered the domestic inode of life. When he was living in his house he got, three pupils. But he never asked them to perform any work or to serve him in any way. Having himself suffered much woe when living in the family of his preceptor, he did nor like to treat his pupils with severity

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: अथ कस्मिंश्चित् काले वेदं ब्राह्मणं जनमेजयः पौष्यश्च क्षत्रियावुपेत्य वरयित्वोपाध्यायं चक्रतुः॥
en: Once on a time both the kings Janamejaya and Paushya came to his house and appointed him as their preceptor.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: स कदाचिद्याज्यकार्येणाभिप्रस्थित उत्तङ्कनामानं शिष्यं नियोजयामास॥ 'भो यत् किंचिदस्मद्गृहे परिहीयते, तदिच्छाम्यहमपरिहीयमानं भवता क्रियमाणम्' इति। स एवं प्रतिसंदिश्योत्तवं वेदः प्रवासं जगाम॥
en: One day when he was going to depart on a sacrificial business, he employed one of his pupils, named Uttanka, to look after nis house and family. He said, “Uttanka, whatever should be required to be done in my house, let it be done by you without neglect." Having given him these instructions, Veda went away on his journey.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: अथोत्तङ्कः शुश्रूषुर्गुरुनियोगमनुतिष्ठमानो गुरुकुले वसति स्मा स तत्र वसमान उपाध्यायस्त्रीभिः सहिताभिराहूयोक्तः॥
en: Uttanka, being always mindful of the service, as asked by his preceptor, lived in the family of his teacher While he was staying there, the females of his preceptor's house assembled near him and addressed him thus.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: 'उपाध्यायिनी ते ऋतुमती। उपाध्यायश्च प्रोषितः अस्या यथाऽयमृतुर्वन्ध्यो न भवति, तथा क्रियताम् एषा विषीदति' इति॥
en: "O Uttanka, the wife of your preceptor is in the state in which she might bear a child. Your preceptor is absent, therefore you are requested to stand in his place and do what is needful."

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: एवमुक्तस्ताः स्त्रियःप्रत्युवाच-'न मया स्त्रीणां वचनादिदमकार्यं करणीयम्। ह्यहमुपाध्यायेन संदिष्टः-अकार्यमपि त्वया कार्यम्' इति॥
en: Uttanka, having been thus addressed, said to the women, “It is not proper for me to do it at the request of women. I have not been asked by my preceptor to do any thing which is not proper."

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: तस्य पुनरुपाध्याय: कालान्तरेण गृहमाजगाम तस्मात् प्रवासात्। स तु तद्वृत्तं तस्याशेषमुपलभ्य प्रीतिमानभूत्॥
en: Some time after his preceptor returned from his journey. He heard all that had happened and was much pleased.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: उवाच चैनम्-'वत्सोत्तङ्क, किं ते प्रियं करवाणि' इति। धर्मतो हि शुश्रूषितोऽस्मि भवता। तेन प्रीतिः परस्परेण नौ संवृद्धा। तदनुजाने भवन्तम्, सर्वानेव कामानवाप्स्यसि, गम्यताम् इति॥
en: He said, “Uttanka, my child, what favour may I bestow on you? I have been properly and faithfully served by you. Our friendship for each other has, therefore, increased. I grant you permission to go. Depart and let your wishes be fulfilled."

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: स एवमुक्तः प्रत्युवाच-'किं ते प्रियं करवाणि' इति, एवमाहुः॥
en: Uttanka, thus addressed, replied. “Let me do something which you wish to be done.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: यश्चाधर्मेण वै ब्रूयाद्यश्चाधर्मेण पृच्छति। तयोरन्यतरः प्रैति विद्वेषं चाधिगच्छति॥
en: It is said, he who bestows instructions, but does not receive Dakshina and he who receives it without giving Dakshina, in both the cases, either of them dies and bitter enmity is created between them.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: सोहमनुज्ञातो भवता इच्छामीष्टं गुर्वर्थमुपहर्तुमिति। तनेवैमुक्त उपाध्यायः प्रत्युवाच-'वत्सोत्तङ्क! उष्यतां तावत्' इति॥
en: I, who have got your permission to go, wish to bring some Dakshina for you.” On hearing this, his preceptor said, "Uttanka, my child, then wait some time."

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: स कदाचिदुपाध्यायमाहोत्तङ्कः-'आज्ञापयतु भवान् किं ते प्रियमुपहरामि गुर्वर्थम्' इति॥
en: Some time after Uttanka again said to his preceptor, “Command me to bring what you wish to have as Dakshina.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: तमुपाध्यायः प्रत्युवाच वत्सोत्तङ्क बहुशो मां चोदयसि गुर्वर्थमुपाहरामीति तद्गच्छैनां प्रविश्योपाध्यायिनीं पृच्छ किमुपाहरामीति॥ एषा यद्वीति तदुपाहरस्वेति। एवमुक्त उपाध्यायेनोपाध्यायिनीमपृच्छद्भगवत्युपाध्यायेनासम्यनुज्ञातो गृहं गंतुमिच्छामीष्टं ते गुर्वर्थमुपहृत्यानृणो गन्तुमिति॥
en: His preceptor then said, "My beloved Uttanka, you have repeatedly expressed your desire to bring something as an acknowledgement of the instructions you have received from me. Go to your mistress and ask her what you will bring for Dakshina.” Thus directed by his preceptor, Uttanka went to his teacher's wife and said, "Madam, I have received permission of my preceptor to depart and I am desirous to bring something that would be agreeable to you as my Dakshina for the instruction I have received, so that I may be free from my debt of gratitude."

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: स स स तदाज्ञापयतु भवती किमुपहरामि गुर्वर्थमिति सैवमुक्तोपाध्यायिनी तमुत्तकं प्रत्युवाच। गच्छ पौष्यं प्रति राजानं कुण्डले भिक्षितुं तस्य क्षत्रियया पिनद्धे॥
en: "Therefore, command me what am I to bring as Dakshina." His preceptress, thus addressed, said, "Go to king Paushya and beg from him the ear-rings that are worn by his queen.'

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: आनयस्व चतुर्थेऽहनि पुण्यकं भविता ताभ्यामाबद्धाभ्यां शोभमाना ब्राह्मणान्यपरिवेष्टुमिच्छामि तत्संपादयस्व एवं हि कुर्वतःश्रेयो भविताऽन्यथा कुतःश्रेय इति॥
en: "And bring them here four days hence is a sacred day; on that day I wish to appear before the Brahmanas and distribute their food wearing those ear-rings. Do this, O Uttanka. If you be successful, good fortune will by yours. If not, what good can you expect?”

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: एवमुक्तस्तया प्रातिष्ठतोत्तङ्कः। पथि गच्छन्नपश्यदृषभमतिप्रमाणं तमधिरूढं पुरुषमतिप्रमाणमेव। स पुरुष उत्तङ्कमभ्यभाषत॥
en: Thus ordered, Uttanka took his departure.' When he was passing along the road he met with an extraordinary large bull and a man of extraordinary large stature riding on it. The man addressed Uttanka thus.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: भो उत्तकैतत्पुरीषमस्य ऋषभस्य भक्षयस्वेति स एवमुक्तो नैच्छत्॥
en: "O Uttanka, eat the dung of this bull." But Uttanka was not willing to eat it.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: तमाह पुरुषो भूयो भक्षयस्वेत्तङ्क मा विचारयोपाध्यायेनापि ते भक्षितं पूर्वमिति॥
en: The man again said, "O Uttanka, eat it without hesitation. Your teacher ate it before."

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: स एवमुक्तो बाढमित्युक्त्वा तदा तवृषभस्य मूत्रं पुरीषं च भक्षयित्वोत्तङ्कःसंभ्रमादुत्थित एवाप उपस्पृश्य प्रतस्थे॥
en: When he was thus addressed, he expressed his willingness to eat,) and ate the dung and drank the urine of the bull and then respectfully rose and washed his hands as he went on.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: यत्र स क्षत्रियः पौष्यस्तमुपेत्यासीनमपश्यदुत्तङ्कः। स उत्तङ्कस्तमुपेत्याशीभिरभिनंद्योवाच॥ प्रत्युवाच पौष्यः
en: He arrived at the palace of king Paushya who was seated on his throne. Uttanka went to him and saluted him; and pronouncing blessings said,

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: अर्थी भवन्तमुपागतोऽस्मीति स एनमभिवाद्योवाच। भगवन्पौष्य:खल्वहं किं करवाणीति॥
en: “I have come to you and stand before you a petitioner.” King Paushya, returning his salutations said, "Sir, what shall I do for you?"

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: तमुवाचगुर्वर्थं कुण्डलयोरर्थेनाभ्यागतोऽस्मीति। ये वै ते क्षत्रियया पिनद्धे कुण्डले ते भवान्दातु-मर्हतीति॥
en: Uttanka replied, “I have come to beg from you your queen's ear-rings as a Dakshina to be given to my preceptor. You should give me those ear-rings."

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: तं पौष्यः प्रविश्यान्तःपुरं क्षत्रिया याच्यतामिति। स तेनैवमुक्तः प्रविश्यान्तःपुरं क्षत्रियां नापश्यत्॥
en: King Paushya said “Go into the innerapartment and ask it from the queen.” He went there, but could not see her.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: स पौष्यं पुनरुवाच न युक्तं भवताऽहमनृतेनोपचरितुं न हि तेऽन्तःपुरे क्षत्रिया सन्निहिता नैनां पश्यामि॥
en: He again said to the king, "You should not deceitfully treat me Your queen is not in the inner-apartment and I could not find her."

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: स एवमुक्तः पौष्यःक्षणमात्रं विमृश्योत्तकं प्रत्युवाच। नियतं भवानुच्छिष्टः। स्मर तावन्न हि सा क्षत्रिया उच्छिष्टेनाशुचिना शक्या द्रष्टुं। पतिव्रतात्वात्सैषा नाशुचेर्दर्शनमुपैतीति॥
en: Paushya thought for a while and then replied “Carefully recollect, Sir, whether you are defiled with the impurities of a repast. The queen is a chaste woman and therefore she cannot be seen by one who is defiled by the impurities of a repast. She does not appear before one who is so defiled."

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: अथैवमुक्त उत्तङ्कः स्मृत्वोवाचास्ति खलु मयोत्थितेनोपस्पृष्टं गच्छता चेति। तं पौष्यः प्रत्युवाच एष ते व्यतिक्रमो नोत्थितेनोपस्पृष्टं भवतीति शीघ्रं गच्छता चेति॥
en: Uttanka, thus addressed, thought for a while and then replied, “ Yes, it is so. As I was in a hurry, I performed my ablutions when I was walking." Paushya said, "This is a transgression. Ablutions cannot properly be performed standing or walking in a hurry.”

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: अथोत्तङ्कस्तं तथेत्युक्त्वा प्राडुमुख उपविश्य सुप्रक्षालितपाणिपादवदनो निःशब्दाभिरफेनाभिरनुष्णाभिहृद्गताभिराद्भिस्त्रिः पीत्वा द्विः परिमृज्य खान्यद्भिपस्पृश्य चान्तःपुरं प्रविवेश॥
en: Uttanka assented to what fell from the king and sat with his face turned towards the east. He washed his hands and feet thoroughly. He then without sound thrice sipped water which was free from scum and froth and which was not warm. He took only so much of it as to reach his stomach. He then wiped his face twice. He then touched his eyes, ears etc., with water. Having done all this he again went to the inner-apartment.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: ततस्तां क्षत्रियामपश्यत् सा च दृष्ट्वैवोत्तत प्रत्युत्थायाभिवाद्योवाच स्वागतं ते भगवन्नाज्ञापय किं करवाणीति॥
en: He saw the queen this time. Seeing him, she saluted him reverentially and said, “Welcome, Sir; command me what I shall do for you.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: स तामुवाचैते कुण्डले गुर्वर्थं मे भिक्षिते दातुमर्हसीति। सा प्रीता तेन तस्य सद्भावेन पात्रमयमनतिक्रमणीयश्चेति मत्वा ते कण्डलेऽवमुच्यास्मै प्रायच्छदाह तक्षको नागराजः सुभृशं प्रार्थयत्यप्रमत्तो नेतुमर्हसीति॥
en: Uttanka said to her, “You should give me your ear-rings. I beg them from you as I wish to present them to my preceptor.” The queen, having been highly pleased with the conduct of Uttanka, thought that he was a very good man and he could not be refused. Therefore. she took off her ear-rings and handed them over to him. On giving them to Uttanka she said, “These ear-rings are very much sought after by Takshaka, the King of the Nagas. Therefore take them with the greatest care."

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: स एवमुक्तस्तां क्षत्रियां प्रत्युवाच भगवति सुनिवृता भव। न मां शक्तस्तक्षको नागराजो घर्षयितुमिति॥
en: Uttanka, being thus told, replied to the queen, "Madam, you need not be under any apprehension. Takshaka, the king of the Nagas, cannot overcome me."

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: स एवमुक्त्वा तां क्षत्रियामामन्त्र्य पौष्यसकाशमागच्छत्। आह चैनं भोः पौष्य प्रीतोऽस्मीति तमुत्तकं पौष्यः प्रत्युवाच॥
en: Having said this, he took leave of the queen and went back to the king, whom he addressed thus, "Paushya, I am much pleased." Paushya replied,

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: भगवंश्चिरेण पात्रमासाद्यते भवांश्च गुणवानतिथिस्तदिच्छे श्राद्धं कर्तुं, क्रियतां क्षण इति॥
en: “A proper man on whom charity can be bestowed is got at long intervals. You are a guest with many qualifications, therefore I wish to perform a Shraddha. Kindly wait a little."

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: तमुत्तङ्कः प्रत्युवाच कृतक्षण एवास्मि शीघ्रमिच्छामि। यथोपपन्नममुपस्कृतं भवतेति तथेत्युक्त्वा यथोपपन्नेनान्नेनैनं भोजयामास॥
en: Uttanka said, "Yes, I shall wait. Bring soon the provisions that are ready.” The king, having signified his assent, duly entertained Uttanka.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: अथोत्तङ्कः सकेशं शीतमन्नं दृष्ट्वा अशुच्येतदिति मत्वा तं पौष्यमुवाच। यस्मान्मे अशुच्यन्नं ददासि तस्मादन्धो भविष्यसीति॥
en: Uttanka, seeing that the food that was brought before him was cold and had hair in it, considered it unclean and said to Paushya, "You give me food that is not clean, therefore you will lose your sight.”

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: तं पौष्यः प्रत्युवाच यस्मात्त्वमप्यदुष्टमन्नं दूषयसि तस्मात्त्वमनपत्यो भविष्यसीति तमुत्तङ्कः प्रत्युवाच॥
en: Paushya replied, "As you impute uncleanliness to the food which is clean, you will be without a child," Uttanka said,

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
