sn: न युक्तं भवताऽन्नमशुचि दत्वा प्रतिशापं दातुं तस्मादन्नमेव प्रत्यक्षीकुरु। ततः पौष्यस्तदन्नमशुचि दृष्ट्वा तस्याशुचिभावमपरोक्षयामास॥
en: “It is not proper for you to curse me after having given me unclean food. You can satisfy yourself by occular proof.” Thereupon Paushya by seeing it personally satisfied himself that the food was unclean.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: अथ तदन्नं मुक्तकेश्यां स्त्रिया यत्कृतमनुष्णं सकेशं चाशुच्येतदिति मत्वा तमृषिमुत्तकं प्रसादयामास॥
en: Having seen that the food was really unclean, cold and mixed with hair, because it was prepared by a woman whose hair was not braided, Paushya began to pacify the Rishi Uttanka, saying.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: भगवन्नेतदज्ञानादन्नं सकेशमुपाहृतं शीतं तत्क्षामये भवन्तं न भवेयमन्ध इति तमुत्तङ्कः प्रत्युवाच॥
en: “Sir, the food placed before you is cold and has really hair in it, having been prepared without sufficient care. Therefore, I pray you, kindly pardon me. Let me not become blind." Uttanka replied.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: न मृषा ब्रवीमि भूत्वा त्वमन्धो न चिरादनन्धो भविष्यसीति। ममापि शापो भवता दत्तो न भवेदिति॥
en: “What I say must happen. Having become blind, you may however regain your sight soon, Grant also that your curse on me may not take effect."

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: तं पौष्यः प्रत्युवाच न चाहं शक्तः शापं प्रत्यादातुं न हि मे मन्युरधाप्युपशमं गच्छति किं चैतद्भवता न ज्ञायते तथा॥
en: Paushya said, "I am not capable of revoking my curse. My anger is not appeased even now. But you do not know it.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: नवनीतं हृदयं ब्राह्मणस्य, वाचि क्षुरो निशितस्तीक्ष्णधारः। तदुभयमेतद्विपरीतं क्षत्रियस्य वाड्नवनीतं हृदयं तीक्ष्णधारमिति॥
en: Brahmana's heart is as soft as butter even though his words are like sharp razors. But contrary is the case with the Kshatriya. His words are as soft as butter, but his heart is like a sharp instrument.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: तदेवं गते न शक्तोऽहं तीक्ष्णहृदयत्वात्तं शापमन्यथा कर्तुं गम्यतामिति। तमुत्तङ्कः प्रत्युवाच। प्रत्युवाच। भवताऽहमन्नस्याशुचिभावमालक्ष्य प्रत्यनुनीतः प्राक् तेऽभिहितम्॥ च
en: Such being the case, I cannot revoke my curse, as my heart is very hard. You may go.' Uttanka replied, "I showed you the uncleanliness of the food placed before me. I am also pacified by you.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: यस्माददुष्टमन्नं दूषयसि तस्मादनपत्यो भविष्यसीति दुष्टे चान्ने नैष मम शापो भविष्यतीति॥
en: Besides you said that I should be without issue, because I falsely imputed uncleanliness to the food. The food, being really unclean, your curse cannot take effect. I am sure of it."

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: साधयामस्तावदित्युक्त्वा प्रातिष्ठतोत्तंङ्कस्ते कुण्डले गृहीत्वा। सोऽपश्यदथ पथि नग्नं क्षपणकमागच्छन्तं मुहुर्मुहुर्दृश्यमानं च॥
en: Uttanka, having said this, went away with the ear-rings. On his way he saw a naked beggar, coming towards him. He was sometimes coming in view view and sometimes disappearing.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: अथोत्तङ्कस्ते कुण्डले संन्यस्य भूमावुदकार्थं प्रचक्रमे। एतस्मिन्नन्तरे स क्षपणकस्त्वरमाण उपसृत्य ते कुण्डले गृहीत्वा प्राद्रवत्॥
en: Uttanka, having occasion to have some water, placed the ear-rings on the ground and went for it. In the mean time the beggar came quickly to the place and taking up the ear-rings and ran away.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: तमुत्तकोऽभिसृत्य कृतोदककार्यः शुचिः प्रयतो नमो देवेभ्यो गुरुभ्यश्च कृत्वा महता जवेन तमन्वयात्॥
en: Having completed his ablutions and purified himself and having bowed down to the divinities and spiritual masters, he ran after the thief as fast as possible.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: तस्य तक्षको दृढमासन्नः स तं जग्राह गृहीतमात्रः स तद्रूपं विहाय तक्षकस्वरूपं कृत्वा सहसा धरण्यां विवृतं महाबिलं प्रविवेश॥
en: Having overtaken him, he seized him with all his might, but the disguised Takshaka, suddenly quitting the form of the beggar, assumed his own real form and quickly disappeared into a large hole in the ground.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: प्रविश्य च नागलोकं स्वभवनमगच्छत्। अथोत्तङ्कस्तस्याः क्षत्रियाया वचः स्मृत्वा तं तक्षकमन्वगच्छत्॥
en: Entering the region of the Nagas, he proceeded to his Own home. Uttanka, remembering the words of the queen, pursued Takshaka.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: स तद्विलं दण्डकाष्ठेन चखान न चाशकत्। तं क्लिश्यमानमिन्द्रोऽपश्यत्स वज्रं प्रेषयामास॥
en: He began to dig open the hole with a stick, but did not make much progress. Seeing his distress Indra sent his thunderbolt to his assistance.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: गच्छास्य ब्राह्मणस्य साहाय्यं कुरुष्वेति। अथ वज्रं दण्डकाष्ठमनुप्रविश्य तद्विलमदारयत्॥
en: Saying, “Go and help that Brahmana.” The thunderbolt entering into the stick enlarged the hole.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: तमुत्तोऽनुविवेश तेनैव बिलेन प्रविश्य च तं नागलोकमपर्यन्तमनेकाविधप्रासादहऱ्यावलभीनि!हशतसंकुलमुच्चावचक्रीडश्चर्यस्थानावकीर्णमपश्यत्॥
en: Uttanka entered into the hole; and thus entering it he saw the land of the Nagas, with hundreds of palaces, elegant mansions, with turrets and domes and gateways, with wonderful arenas for various games and entertainments.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: स तत्र नागांस्तानस्तुवदेभिः श्लोकैः य ऐरावतराजानः सर्पाः समितिशोभनाः। क्षरन्त इव जीमूताः सविद्युत्पवनेरिताः॥
en: To please the Nagas, he uttered the following slokas, “O serpents, subjects of the king Airavata, you are brilliant in battles, you shower weapons like clouds, charged with lightning and driven by wind.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: सुरूपा बहुरूपाश्च तथा कल्माषकुण्डलाः। आदित्यवन्नाकपृष्ठे रेजुरैरावतोद्भवाः॥
en: Beautiful, variously formed, decked with many coloured ear-rings, children of Airavata, you shine like the sun in the sky.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: बहूनि नागवेश्मानि गङ्गायास्तीर उत्तरे। तत्रस्थानपि संस्तौमि महतः पन्नगानहम्॥
en: These are many settlements of Nagas on the northern banks of the Ganges and there do I often worship the great Nagas.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: इच्छेत्कोऽर्षांशुसेनायां चर्तुमैरावतं विना। शतान्यशीतिरष्टौ च सहस्राणि च विंशतिः॥ सर्पाणां प्रग्रहा यन्ति धृतराष्ट्रो यदैजति।
en: Who but Airavata can desire to move in the burning sun? When Dhritarashtra goes out, twenty eight thousand and eight Nagas follow him.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: ये चैनमुपसर्पन्ति ये च दूरपथं गताः। अहमैरावतज्येष्ठभ्रातृभ्योऽकरवं नम:॥
en: I salute you all that have Airavata for their elder brother, whether you live near him or stay at a distance from him.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: यस्य वासः कुरुक्षेत्रे खाण्डवे कुरुक्षेत्रे खाण्डवे चाभवत्पुरा। तं नागराजमस्तौषं कुण्डलार्थाय तक्षकम्॥
en: In order to get beck my ear-rings I worship you, Takshaka, the Naga-king, who formerly lived in Kurukshetra and the forest of Khandhava.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: तक्षकश्चाश्वसेनश्च नित्यं सहचरावुभौ। कुरुक्षेत्रं च वसतां नदीमिक्षुमतीमनु॥
en: 1 Takshaka and Ashvasena were constant companions when they lived in Kurukshetra on the banks of the river Ikshumati.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: जघन्यजस्तक्षकश्च श्रुतसेनेति यः सुतः। अवसद्यो महद्युम्नि प्रार्थयन्नाममुख्यताम्॥ करवाणि सदा चाहं नमस्तस्मै महात्मने।
en: I also worship Takshaka's younger brother Shrutasena, who dwelt at the holy place called Mahadyumna with the intention of becoming one of the chiefs of the Nagas.”

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: एवं स्तुत्वा स विप्रर्षिरुत्तङ्को भुजगोत्तमान्। नैव ते कुण्डले लेभे ततश्चिन्तामुपागमत्॥
en: After having thus praised the chief Nagas, the Brahmana Rishi, Uttanka did not get his ear-rings; and he became very thoughtful.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: एवं स्तुवन्नपि नागान्यदा ते कुण्डले नालभत्तदाऽपश्यत्स्त्रियौ तन्त्रे अधिरोप्य सुवेमे पटं वयन्त्यौ। तस्मिंस्तन्त्रे कृष्णाः सिताश्च तन्तवश्चक्रं चापश्यत् द्वादशारं षड्भिः कुमारैः परिवर्त्यमानं पुरुषं चापश्यदश्वं च दर्शनीयम्॥ स तान्सर्वांस्तुष्टाव एभिर्मन्त्रवदेव श्लोकैः।
en: When he saw that he did not get the earrings, although he had worshipped the Nagas, he looked around him and beheld two women working in a loom with fine shuttle and weaving a piece of cloth. There were black and white threads in the loom. He also saw a wheel, with twelve spokes, which was turned round by six boys. He also saw a man with a horse. In order to please them all he uttered the following Mantras.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: त्रीण्यर्पितान्यत्र शतानि मध्ये घष्टिश्च नित्यं चरति ध्रुवेऽस्मिन्। चक्रे चतुर्विशतिपर्वयोगे षड्वै कुमाराः परिवर्तयन्ति॥
en: “This wheel, the circumference of which is marked by twenty-four divisions. representing twenty-four, Lunar changes, contains three hundred and sixty spokes. It is continually set in motion by six boys.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: तन्त्रं चेदं विश्वरूपे युवत्यौ वयतस्तंतून्सततं वर्तयन्त्यौ। कृष्णान्सितांश्चैव विवर्तयन्त्यौ भूतान्यजस्रं भुवनानि चैव॥
en: These maidens, representing the universe, are continually, weaving a cloth with white and black threads, creating innumerable words and millions of beings to inhabit them.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: वज्रस्य भर्ता भुवनस्य गोप्ता वृत्रस्य हन्ता नमुचेनिहन्ता। कृष्णे वसानो वसने महात्मा सत्यानृते यो विविनक्ति लोके॥
en: O, the master of thunder, the protector of the universe, the slayer of Vritra and Namuchi, O illustrious one, wearing the black cloth, O Deity, who displays truth and untruth in the universe.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: यो वाजिनं गर्भमपां पुराणं वैश्वानरं वाहनमभ्युपैति। नमोऽस्तु तस्मै जगदीश्वराय लोकत्रयेशाय पुरंदराय॥
en: Who owns the horse that was obtained from the depths of the ocean and which is but another form of Agni, I bow to you, O supreme being, O Lord of the three worlds, O Purandara,"

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: ततः स एनं पुरुषः प्राह-'प्रीतोऽस्मि तेऽहमनेन स्तोत्रेण, किं ते प्रियं करवाणि' इति स तमुवाच॥
en: Then said the man with the horse, "I have been much pleased with your adoration. What good can I do to you?"

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: नागा मे वशमीयुरिति। स चैनं पुरुषः पुनरुवाच एतमश्चमपाने धमस्वेति॥
en: Uttanka replied, “Let the Nagas be brought under my power." The man then said, “Blow into this horse."

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: ततोऽश्वस्यापानमधमत्ततोऽश्वाद्धम्यमानात्सर्वस्त्रोतोभ्यः पावकार्चिषः सधूमा निष्पेतुः॥
en: Thereupon Uttanka blew into the horse and thousands of flames and fires with smoke issued forth from every aperture of the horse thus blown into.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: ताभिर्नागलोक उपधूपितेऽथ संभ्रान्तस्तक्षको ऽग्नेस्तेजोभयाद्विषण्ण: कुण्डले गृहीत्वा सहसा भवनान्निष्क्रम्योत्तङ्कमुवाच॥
en: The land of the Nagas was at the point of being burnt down, when Takshaka, taking the ear-rings, hastened to Uttanka, from his palace and said,

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: इमे कुण्डले गृह्णातु भवानिति स ते प्रतिजग्राहोत्तङ्कः प्रतिगृह्य च कुणलेऽचिन्तयत्॥
en: “Pray,-Sir, take back your ear-rings," Receiving back his ear-rings Uttanka thought.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: अद्य तत्पुण्यकमुपाध्यायिन्या दूरं चाहमभ्यागत: स कथं संभावयेयमिति तत एनं चिन्तयानमेव स पुरुष उवाच॥
en: "Today is the sacred day mentioned by my preceptress. I am at a distance, how can I, therefore, show my regard for her I by presenting her with the ear-rings)!" When he was thus meditating the man said,

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: उत्तङ्क एनमेवाश्वमधिरोह त्वां क्षणेनैवोपाध्यायकुलं प्रापयिष्यतीति॥
en: "Uttanka, get on this horse. He will take you in a moment to the family of your preceptor."

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: स तथेत्युक्त्वा तमश्वमधिरुह्य प्रत्याजगामोपाध्यायकुलमुपाध्यायिनी च स्माता केशानावापयन्त्युपविष्टोत्तको नागच्छतीति शापायास्य मनो दधे॥
en: Uttanka signified his assent, mounted the horse and reached his preceptor's house in a moment's time. The preceptress, after bathing, was dressing her hair, sitting and thinking that if Uttanka did not come, she would curse him.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: अथ तस्मिन्नन्तरे स उत्तङ्कः प्रविश्य उपाध्यायकुलमुपाध्यायिनीमभ्यवादयत् ते चास्यै कुण्डले प्रायच्छत्सा चैनं प्रत्युवाच॥
en: At this very time Uttanka entered the house of his preceptor and made proper salutation to his preceptress. When he presented her with the ear-rings, she said.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: उत्तङ्क देशे कालेऽभ्यागतः स्वागतं ते वत्स त्वमनागसि मया न शप्तः श्रेयस्तवोपस्थितं सिद्धिमाप्नुहीति॥
en: “Uttanka, you have come at the proper time. Welcome, my child. As you are innocent, I do not curse you. Good fortune will come to you. Let your wishes be crowned with success."

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: अथोत्तङ्क उपाध्यायमभ्यवादयत्। तमुपाध्यायः प्रत्युवाच वत्सोत्तङ्क स्वागतं ते किं चिरंकृतमिति॥
en: Then did Uttanka salute his preceptor and his preceptor said, “Uttanka, my child, welcome to you. What made you to be so long away?"

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: तमुत्तङ्क उपाध्यायं प्रत्युवाच भोस्तक्षकेण मे नागराजेन विघ्नः कृतोऽस्मिन्कर्मणि तेनाऽस्मि नागलोकं गतः॥
en: Uttanka replied to the preceptor, “The king of the Nagas, Takshaka, offered obstruction to the business I went and therefore I had to go to the land of the Nagas.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: तत्र च मया दृष्टे स्त्रियौ तन्त्रेऽधिरोप्य पटं वयन्त्यौ तस्मिश्च कृष्णाः सिताश्च तन्तवः किं तत्॥
en: There I saw two maidens working in a loom and weaving a cloth with black and white threads. What may it be?

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: तत्र च मया चक्रं दृष्टं द्वादशारं षड्वैनं कुमारा: परिवर्तयन्ति तदपि किम्। पुरुषश्चापि मया दृष्टः स चाऽपि कः। अश्वश्चातिप्रमाणो दृष्टः स चाऽपि कः॥
en: I then saw a wheel, with twelve spokes, which was being continually turned by six boys. What does it mean? I also saw a man, who is he? I saw also a horse of extraordinary size, what is that horse?

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: पथि गच्छता च मया ऋषभो दृष्टस्तं च पुरुषोऽधिरूढस्तेनाऽस्मि सोपचारमुक्त उत्तङ्कस्य ऋषभस्य पुरीषं भक्षय उपाध्यायेनापि ते भक्षितमिति॥
en: On my way I saw on the road a man mounted on a bull. He lovingly addressed me thus, “Uttanka, eat the dung of this bull, which was eaten by your preceptor."

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: ततस्तस्य वचनान्मया तदृषभस्य पुरीषमुपयुक्तं स चापि कः। तदेतद्भवतोपदिष्टमिच्छेयं श्रोतुं किं तदिति। स तेनैवमुक्त उपाध्यायः प्रत्युवाच॥
en: Thus toled by him, I ate the dung of that bull. Who is this man? Being instructed by you I wish to hear all about them."

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: ये ते स्त्रियौ धाता विधाता च ये च ते कृष्णाः सितास्तन्तवस्ते रात्र्यहनी। यदपि तच्चक्रं द्वादशारं षड्वै कुमाराः परिवर्तयन्ति तेऽपि षऋतवः संवत्सरश्चक्रम्॥
en: His preceptor thus addressed said to him, “The two maidens you saw are Dhata and Vidhata. The black and white threads represent night and day. The wheel, with twelve spokes turned by six boys, is the year, having six seasons.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: यः पुरुषः स पर्जन्यो योऽश्वः सोऽग्निर्य ऋषभस्त्वया पथि गच्छता दृष्टः स ऐरावतो नागराट्॥
en: The man is Parjanya (the deity of rain); the horse is Agni, (deity of fire). The bull which you saw on the road is the Airavata, the king of elephants.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: यश्चैनमधिरूढः पुरुषः स चेन्द्रो यदपि ते भक्षितं तस्य ऋषभस्य पुरीषं तदमृतं तेन खल्वसि तस्मिन्नागभवने न व्यापन्नस्त्वम्॥
en: The man who rode it is Indra. The dung of the Bull, which you ate is Ambrosia. Certainly on account of this (eating) you were not slain in the land of the Nagas.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: स हि भगवानिन्द्रो मम सखा त्वदनुक्रोशादिममनुग्रहं कृतवान्। तस्मात्कृण्डले गृहीत्वा पुनरागतोऽसि॥
en: Lord Indra is my friend; he, being moved by kindness towards you, showed you this favour; therefore, you have been able to return safely with the ear-rings.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: तत्सौम्य गम्यतामनुजाने भवन्तं श्रेयोऽवाप्स्यसीति। स उपाध्यायेनानुज्ञातो भगवानुत्तङ्कः क्रुद्धस्तक्षकं प्रतिचिकीर्षमाणो हास्तिनपुरं प्रतस्थे॥
en: Now, mild-natured Uttanka, I give you permission to go. You will obtain good fortune." Uttanka, thus obtaining his preceptor's leave and being deadly angry against Takshaka, went towards Hastinapur, resolved to take revenge on the Naga king.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: स हास्तिनपुरं प्राप्य न चिराद्विप्रसत्तमः। समागच्छत राजानमुत्तको जनमेजयम्।. १७०॥
en: The good Brahmana, Uttanka reached Hastinapur and then he met king Janamejaya,

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: पुरा तक्षशिलासंस्थं निवृत्तमपराजितम्। सम्यग्विजयिनं दृष्ट्वा समन्तान्मन्त्रिभिर्वृतम्॥
en: Who had only recently returned victorious from Takshashila. He saw him seated surrounded by his ministers.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: तस्मै जयाशिषः पूर्वं यथान्यायं प्रयुज्य सः। उवाचैनं वचः काले शब्दसंपन्नया गिरा॥
en: He uttered blessings in proper time and addressed him in speech of correct accent and melodious sound.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: उत्तङ्क उवाच अन्यस्मिन्करणीये तु कार्ये पार्थिवसत्तम। बाल्यादिवान्यदेव तवं कुरुषे नृपसत्तम॥
en: Uttanka said: O best of kings, you are spending your time like a child when a most important matter urgently demands your attention.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: सौतिरुवाच एवमुक्तस्तु विप्रेण स राजा जनमेजयः। अर्चयित्वा यथान्यायं प्रत्युवाच द्विजोत्तमम्॥
en: Sauti said: Having been thus addressed by the Brahmana, king Janamejaya duly saluted him and said to the best of Brahmanas.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: जनमेजय उवाच आसां प्रजानां परिपालनेन स्वं क्षत्रधर्मं परिपालयामि। प्रब्रूहि मे किं करणीयमद्य येनासि कार्येण समागतस्त्वम्॥
en: Janamejaya said : I perform the duties of my Kshatriya race, by looking after my these subjects. Tell me what is the business that I am to perform by which you are led to come here.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: सौतिरुवाच स एवमुक्तस्तु नृपोत्तमेन द्विजोत्तमः पुण्यकृतां वरिष्ठः। उवाच राजानमदीनसत्वं स्वमेव कार्यं नृपते कुरुष्व॥
en: Sauti said : Having been thus addressed by the best of kings, Janamejaya, the best of Brahmanas, distinguished for good deeds, thus replied, "O king, the business is your own that demands your attention. Therefore do it."

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: उत्तङ्क उवाच तक्षकेण महीन्द्रेन्द्र येन ते हिंसित: पिता। तस्मै प्रतिकुरुष्व त्वं पन्नगाय दुरात्मने॥
en: Uttanka said : O king of kings, your father was killed by Takshaka, therefore take revenge on that vile serpent for the death of your noble father.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: कार्यकालं हि मन्येऽहं विधिदृष्टस्य कर्मणः। तद्गच्छापचिति राजन्पितुस्तस्य महात्मनः॥
en: The time has come, I say, for your taking vengeance, ordained by Fate. Go, O king and revenge the death of your noble father,

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: ते ह्यनपराधी स दुष्टान्तरात्मना। पञ्चत्वमगमद्राजा वजाहत इव दुमः॥
en: Who was unoffending, but who died like a tree stricken by thunder, having been bitten by this vile serpent.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: बलदर्पसमुत्सितस्तक्षकः पन्नगाधमः। अकार्यं कृतवान्पापो योऽदशत्पितरं तव॥
en: The worst of the serpent race, Takshaka, being intoxicated with power, committed a wicked act when he bit your father.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: राजर्षिवंशगोप्तारममरप्रतिमं नृपम्। यियासुं कश्यपं चैव न्यवर्तयत पापकृत्॥
en: Wicked in his deeds, he even made Kashyapa run away when he was coming for the relief of your god-like father, the protector of the race of royal sages.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: हेतुमर्हसि तं पापं ज्वलिते हव्यवाहने। सर्पसत्रे महाराज त्वरितं तद्विधीयताम्॥
en: It is proper for you to burn the wicked wretch in the blazing fire of a Snake-Sacrifice. Therefore, O king, soon do the needful for it.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: एवं पितुश्चापचितिं कृतवांस्त्वं भविष्यसि। मम प्रियं च सुमहत्कृतं राजन् भविष्यति॥
en: You can thus revenge your father's death. O king, You can thus do me a great favour.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: कर्मणः पृथिवीपाल मम येन दुरात्मना। विघ्नः कृतो महाराज गुर्वर्थं चरतोऽनघ॥
en: O king of the world, my business was obstructed on one occasion by that wretch when I was going (to get a present for my preceptor.)

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: सौतिरुवाच एतच्छ्रुत्वा तु नृपतिस्तक्षकाय चुकोप है। उत्तङ्कवाक्यहविषा दीप्तोऽग्निर्हविषा यथा॥
en: Sauti said : The king, having heard these words, got angry on Takshaka. Uttanka's speech inflamed him as ghee does the sacrificial fire.

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: अपृच्छत्स तदा राजा मन्त्रिणस्तान्सुदुःखितः। उत्तङ्कस्यैव सान्निध्ये पितुः स्वर्गगति प्रति॥
en: Even in the presence of Uttanka, he sorrowfully asked his ministers the particulars of his father's going to heaven (death).

description: Curse of Janamejaya by Sarama, Story of the Aruni, Upamanyu, Veda and Uttanka
sn: तदैव हि स राजेन्द्रो दुःखशोकाल्पुतोऽभवत्। यदैव वृत्तं पितरमुत्तङ्कादशृणोत्तदा॥
en: When he heard all the circumstances of his father's death from Uttanka, the king of kings was overcome with sorrow and pain.

sn: लोमहर्षणपुत्र उग्रश्रवाः पौराणिको नैमिषारण्ये शौनकस्य कुलपतेादशवार्षिक सत्रे ऋषीनभ्यागतानुपतस्थे॥
en: Lomaharshana's son Ugrashrava Sauti, well-read in the Puranas, being present at the twelve years' sacrifice of Kulapati Shaunaka in the forest of Naimisha, stood before the Rishis in attendance.

sn: पौराणिकः पुराणे कृतश्रमः स कृताञ्जलिस्तानुवाच। किं भवन्तः श्रोतुमिच्छन्ति किमहं ब्रवाणीति॥
en: Having read the Puranas with great pains he was very learned in them. Now with joined hands he addressed them thus, "What, Reverend Sirs, do you wish to hear? What am I to relate?"

sn: तमृषयः ऊचुः परमं लोमहर्षणे वक्ष्यामस्त्वां नः प्रतिवक्ष्यसि वचः शुश्रूषतां कथायोगं न: कथायोगे॥
en: The Rishis replied, "O son of Lomaharshana, we shall ask you and you will relate to us, who are anxious to hear, some excellent stories.

sn: तत्र भगवान् कुलपतिस्तु मध्यास्ते॥
en: But noble Kulapati Shaunaka is now engaged in the room of the holy fire,

sn: योऽसौ दिव्या:कथा वेद देवतासुरसंश्रिताः। मनुष्योरगगन्धर्वकथा वेद च सर्वशः॥
en: He knows the divine stories relating to the Devas and Asuras. He also knows the stories relating to men, Nagas and Gandharvas.

sn: स चाप्यस्मिन्मखे सौते विद्वान् कुलपतिर्द्विजः। दक्षोधृतव्रतो धीमान् शास्त्रे चारण्यके गुरुः॥
en: O Sauti, that Kulapati Brahmana is the chief in this sacrifice; he is able, faithful to his vows, wise and a master of the Shastras and Aranyakas.

sn: सत्यवादी शमपरस्तपस्वी नियतव्रतः। सर्वेषामेव नो मान्यः स तावत्प्रतिपाल्यताम्॥
en: He is truthful, a lover of peace, a Rishi of hard austerities and an observer of the ordained penances. He is respected by all of us and we should, therefore, wait for him.

sn: तस्मिन्नध्यासति गुरावासनं परमार्चितम्। ततो वक्ष्यसि यत्त्वां स प्रक्ष्यति द्विजसत्तमः॥
en: When he will sit on the highly honoured seat for the preceptor, you will reply to what best of the twice born will ask you.

sn: सौतिरुवाच एवमस्तु गुरौ तस्मिन्नुपविष्टे महात्मनि। तेन पृष्टः कथा: पुण्या वक्ष्यामि विविधाश्रयाः॥
en: Sauti said: So be it. When the noble Rishi will be seated, I shall relate sacred stories relating to variety of subjects as I shall be asked by him.

sn: सोऽथ विप्रर्षभः सर्वं कृत्वा कार्यं यथाविधि। देवान्वाग्भिः पितॄनद्भिस्तर्पयित्वाजगाम ह। यत्र ब्रह्मर्षयः सिद्धाः सुखासीना धृतव्रताः। यज्ञायतनमाश्रित्य सूतपुत्रपुरःसराः॥
en: The best of Brahmanas (Shaunaka) after having performed all his Prayers to Devas and the Pitris by offering water, came back to the place of sacrifice where Sauti was seated before the assembly of Rishis of rigid vows.

sn: ऋत्विक्ष्वथ सदस्येषु स वै गृहपतिस्तदा। उपविष्टेषूपविष्टः शौनकोऽथाब्रवीदिदम्॥
en: When Shaunaka was seated in the midst of Ritviks and Sadasyas (members) who also had come to their places, Sauti spoke as follows.

sn: शौनक उवाच पुराणमखिलं तात पिता तेऽधीतवान्पुरा। कच्चित्त्वमपि तत्सर्वमधीषे लौमहर्षणे॥
en: Shaunaka said: Your father read the whole of the Puranas in the days of yore. O Son of Lomaharshana, have you also made them your study?

sn: पुराणे हि कथा दिव्या आदिवंशाश्च धीमताम्। कथ्यन्ते ये पुराऽस्माभिः श्रुतपूर्वाः पितुस्तव।॥
en: There are in the Puranas interesting stories and the history of the first generations of the wise men. We have heard them all recited by your father.

sn: चैव ततो मया। तत्र वंशमहं पूर्वं श्रोतुमिच्छामि भार्गवम्। कथयस्व कथामेतां कल्याः स्म श्रवणे तव॥
en: I am desirous of hearing the history of the Bhrigu race. Tell us that history. We are all attention to listen to you.

sn: सौतिरुवाच यदधीतं पुरा सम्यक् द्विजश्रेष्ठैर्महात्मभिः। वैशंपायनविप्रायैस्तैश्चापि कथितं यथा॥
en: Sauti said : That which was formerly studied by the noble Brahmanas, which was studied and narrated by Vaishampayana and others.

sn: यदधीतं च पित्रा मे सम्यक् तावच्छृणुष्व यो देवैः सेन्द्रैःसर्षिमरुद्गणैः॥ पूजितः प्रवरो वंशो भार्गवो भृगुनन्दन। इमं वंशमहं पूर्वं भार्गवं ते महामुने॥
en: Which was also studied by my father, has been acquired by me. Hear with all attention, O descendant of the Bhrigu race, the history of your race, respected by Indra and all the celestials, all the Rishis and the Marutas. In this great race the great and blessed Rishi Bhrigu was born.

sn: निगदामि यथायुक्तं पुराणाश्रयसंयुतम्। भृगुर्महर्षिर्भगवान् ब्रह्मणा वै स्वयंभुवा॥ वरुणस्य क्रतौ जातः पावकादिति नः श्रुतम्। भृगोः सुदयितः पुत्रश्च्यवनो नाम भार्गवः॥
en: I shall properly relate, O great Rishi, the history of this race, as it is in the Puranas. We are told that great Bhrigu was begotten by selfexisting Brahma from the fire at Varuna's sacrifice. Bhrigu had a beloved son, named Chyavana.

sn: च्यवनस्य च दायादः प्रमतिर्नाम धार्मिकः। प्रमतेरप्यभूत्पुत्रो घृताच्यां रुरुरित्युत॥
en: Chyavana had a virtuous son, named Pramati. He had a son, named Ruru by Ghritachi.

sn: रुरोरपि सुतो जज्ञे शुनको वेदपारगः। प्रमद्वरायां धर्मात्मा तव पूर्वपितामहः॥
en: Ruru had a son by his wife Pramadvara. O Shaunaka, he was your grandfather; he was very virtuous and greatly learned in the Vedas.

sn: तपस्वी च यशस्वी च श्रुतवान् ब्रह्मवित्तमः। धार्मिकः सत्यवादी च नियतो नियताशनः॥
en: He was devoted to asceticism, had great repute, was learned in the Shruti, truthful, virtuous, well-regulated in his meals and was the most eminent amongst the learned in the Vedas.

sn: शौनक उवाच सूतपुत्र यथा तस्य भार्गवस्य महात्मनः। च्यवनत्वं परिख्यातं तन्ममाचक्ष्व पृच्छतः॥
en: Shaunaka said : O Son of Suta, why was the illustrious son of Bhrigu named Chyavana? I ask you, tell me all about it.

sn: सौतिरुवाच भृगोः सुदयिता भार्या पुलोमेत्यभिविश्रुता। तस्यां समभवद्गर्भो भृगुवीर्यसमुद्भवः॥
en: Sauti replied : Bhrigu had a very beloved wife, (named Puloma) who became quick with child by him.

sn: तस्मिन् गर्भेऽथ संभूते पुलोमायां भृगूद्वह। समये समशीलिन्यां धर्मपत्न्यां यशस्विनः॥ अभिषेकाय निष्क्रान्ते भृगौ धर्मभृतां वरे। आश्रमं तस्य रक्षोऽथ पुलोमाभ्याजगाम ह॥
en: When the virtuous and chaste Pauloma was in that condition, one day the greatly famous and virtuous Bhrigu, leaving her at home, went to perform his ablutions. And it was then that a Rakshasa, named Puloma, came to the Rishi's hermitage.

sn: तं प्रविश्याश्रमं दृष्ट्वा भृगोर्भार्यामनिन्दिताम्। हृच्छयेन समाविष्टो विचेताः समपद्यत॥
en: He, having entered into the hermitage, saw the irreproachable wife of Bhrigu. Seeing her he was filled with lust and lost his reason.

sn: अभ्यागतं तु तद्रक्षः पुलोमा चारुदर्शना। न्यमन्त्रयत वन्येन फलमूलादिना तदा॥
en: Seeing that a guest had come, beautiful Puloma, entertained him with roots and fruits of the wood.

sn: तां तु रक्षस्तदा ब्रह्मन् हृच्छयेनाभिपीडितम्। दृष्ट्वा हृष्टमभूद्राजन् जिहीर्षुस्तामनिन्दिताम्॥
en: O Rishi, the Rakshasa, having seen her, burnt in lust. He was very much delighted and he determined to carry away the irreproachable lady.

sn: जातमित्यब्रवीत्कार्यं जिहीर्षुर्मुदितः शुभाम्। सा हि पूर्वं वृता तेन पुलोम्ना तु शुचिस्मिता॥
en: He said, “My desire is fulfilled.” So saying he seized that beautiful lady and carried her away. And in fact that lady of captivating smiles, was formerly betrothed to the Rakshasa by her father.

sn: तां तु प्रादात्पिता पश्चाद् भृगवे शास्त्रवत्तदा। तस्य तत्किल्बिषं नित्यं हृदि वर्तति भार्गव॥
en: But he afterwards gave her away to the Rishi Bhrigu in due rites. Since then, O descendant of the Bhrigu race, this wound rankled deep in the heart of the Rakshasa.

sn: इदमन्तरमित्येवं हर्तुं चक्रे मनस्तदा। अथाग्निशरणेऽपश्यज्ज्वलन्तं जातवेदसम्॥
en: He thought this very good opportunity to carry the lady away. Then he entered into the room of the holy fire where it was brightly burning.

sn: तमपृच्छत्ततो रक्षः पावकं ज्वलितं तदा। शंस मे कस्य भार्येयमग्ने पृच्छे ऋतेन वै॥
en: The Rakshasa asked the burning fire, “O Agni! tell me whose rightful wife this lady is.

sn: मुखं त्वमसि देवानां वद पावक पृच्छते। मया हीयं वृता पूर्वं भार्यार्थे वरवर्णिनी॥
en: You, O Agni, is the mouth of celestials, tell me, I ask you. This beautiful lady was formerly betrothed to me;

sn: पश्चादिमां पिता प्रादाद्धगवेऽनृतकारकः। सेयं यदि वरारोहा भृगोर्भार्या रहोगता॥
en: was a But her vile father subsequently gave her to Bhrigu. (Tell me truly) if she can be truly called the wife of Bhrigu.

sn: तथा सत्यं समाख्याहि जिहीर्षाम्याश्रमादिमाम्। समन्युस्तत्र हृदयं प्रदहन्निव तिष्ठति। मत्पूर्वाभार्यां यदिमां भृगुराप सुमध्यमाम्॥
en: As I have found her alone in the hermitage, I am determined to carry her away by force. My heart burns with rage when I think that Bhrigu has obtained this beautiful woman who was betrothed to me.

sn: सौतिरुवाच एवं रक्षस्तमामन्त्र्य ज्वलितं जातवेदसम्। शङ्कमानं भृगोर्भार्यां पुन:पुनरपृच्छत॥
en: Thus did the Rakshasa ask the flaming fire again and again, whether the lady was Bhrigu's wife.

sn: त्वमग्ने! सर्वभूतानामन्तश्चरसि नित्यदा। साक्षिवत्पुण्यपापेषु सत्यं ब्रूहि कवे वचः॥
en: “O Agni, you always dwell in every creature as the witness of their piety and impiety. Answer my question truthfully.

sn: मत्पूर्वाऽपहता भार्या भृगुणाऽनृतकारिणा। सेयं यदि तथा मे त्वं सत्यमाख्यातुमर्हसि॥
en: Bhrigu has appropriated her who was chosen by me as my wife. Tell me truly therefore, whether she is not truly my wife by first choice.

sn: श्रुत्वा त्वत्तो भृगोर्भार्यां हरिष्याम्याश्रमादिमाम्। जातवेदः पश्यतस्ते वद सत्यां गिरं मम॥
en: Hearing from you whether she is Bhrigu's wife or not, I shall carry her away from the hermitage even in your presence. Therefore, answer me truthfully."

sn: सौतिरुवाच तस्यैतद्वचनं श्रुत्वा सप्ताचिर्दुःखितोऽभवत्। भीतोऽनृताच्च शापाच्च भृगोरित्यब्रवीच्छनैः॥
en: Sauti said: Having heard his words, the seven flamed Deity felt himself very much in difficulty. He was afraid to tell an untruth and was equally afraid of Bhrigu's curse. He at last slowly said.

sn: अग्निरुवाच त्वया वृता पुलोमेयं पूर्वं दानवनन्दन। किं त्वियं विधिना पूर्वं मन्त्रवन वृता त्वया॥
en: Agni said : "O Rakshasa, it is true that this Puloma was first betrothed to you, but she was not taken by you with (the necessary) holy rites and invocations.

sn: पित्रा तु भृगवे दत्ता पुलोमेयं यशस्विनी। ददाति न पिता तुभ्यं वरलोभान्महायशाः॥
en: And her father gave this famous Puloma to Bhrigu in gift. He did not give her to you.

sn: अथेमां वेददृष्टेन कर्मणा विधिपूर्वकम्। भार्यामृषि गुः प्राप मां पुरस्कृत्य दानव॥
en: O Rakshasa, she was duly taken by Bhrigu as his wife in my presence with all the Vedic rites.

sn: सेयमित्यवगच्छामि नानृतं वक्तुमुत्सहे। नानृतं हि सदा लोके पूज्यते दानवोत्तम॥
en: This is she, I cannot tell a falsehood. O best of Rakshasa, falsehood is never respected in this world.

description: Birth of Chyavana, Bhrigu's curse on Agni
sn: सौतिरुवाच अग्नेस्थ वचः श्रुत्वा तद्रक्षः प्रजहार ताम्। ब्रह्मन्वराहरूपेण मनोमारुतरंहसा॥
en: Sauti said: O Brahman, having heard these words of Agni, the Rakshasa assumed the form of a boar and carried her away as fast as the wind or the mind.

description: Birth of Chyavana, Bhrigu's curse on Agni
sn: ततः स गर्भो निवसत्कुक्षौ भृगुकुलोद्वह। रोषान्मातुश्च्युतः कुक्षेश्च्यवनस्तेन सोऽभवत्॥
en: The child, of Bhrigu, who was in her womb, was very much enraged at this violence and he dropped down from his mother's womb, For this reason he got the name as Chyavana.

description: Birth of Chyavana, Bhrigu's curse on Agni
sn: तं दृष्ट्वा मातुरुदराच्च्युतमादित्यवर्चसम्। तद्रक्षो भस्मसाद्भूतं पपात परिमुच्य ताम्॥
en: On seeing that the child had dropped from her mother's womb as shinning as the sun, he quitted the grasp of the lady. But he fell down and was burnt to ashes.

description: Birth of Chyavana, Bhrigu's curse on Agni
sn: सा तमादाय सुश्रोणि ससार भृगुनन्दनम्। च्यवनं भार्गवं पुत्रं पुलोमा दुःखमूर्छिता॥
en: O descendant of Bhrigu, the beautiful Puloma, heing afflicted with grief, took up her child Chyavana and walked away.

description: Birth of Chyavana, Bhrigu's curse on Agni
sn: तां ददर्श स्वयं ब्रह्मा सर्वलोकपितामहः। रुदतीं बाष्पपूर्णाक्षी भृगोर्भार्यामनिन्दिताम्॥
en: The Grandfather of all beings, Brahma himself saw the faultless wife of Bhrigu weeping with eyes full of tears.

description: Birth of Chyavana, Bhrigu's curse on Agni
sn: सान्त्वयामास भगवान्वधूं ब्रह्मा पितामहः। अश्रुबिन्दूद्भवा तस्याः प्रावर्तत महानदी॥
en: The Grandfather of all beings, noble Brahma consoled his own daughter-in-law (Puloma) and a great river was formed from the tears thai fell from her eyes.

description: Birth of Chyavana, Bhrigu's curse on Agni
sn: आवर्तन्ती सृति तस्या भृगोः पत्न्यास्तपस्विनः। तस्या मार्ग सृतवतीं दृष्ट्वा तु सरितं तदा॥ नाम तस्यास्तदा नद्याश्चक्रे लोकपितामहः। वधूसरेति भगवांश्च्यवनस्याश्रमं प्रति॥
en: The river followed the foot-steps of the wife of the great Rishi Bhrigu; and the Grandfather of the worlds seeing, it follow the path of his son's wife, named it himself. He called it Vadhusara and it passed by the hermitage of Chyavana.

description: Birth of Chyavana, Bhrigu's curse on Agni
sn: स एवं च्यवनो जज्ञे भृगोः पुत्रः प्रतापवान्। तं ददर्श पिता तत्र च्यवनं तां च भाविनीम्। स पुलोमां ततो भार्यां पप्रच्छ कुपितो भृगुः॥
en: In this way was born Chyavana, the son of Bhrigu of great power. And Bhrigu saw his son (yavana aid his beautiful mother. He asked his wife Puloma in a rage.

description: Birth of Chyavana, Bhrigu's curse on Agni
sn: भृगुरुवाच केनाऽसि रक्षसे तस्मै कलिता त्वं जिहीर्षते। न हि त्वां वेद तद्रक्षो मद्भार्यां चारुहासिनीम्॥
en: Bhrigu said : Who made you known to the Rakshasa resolved to carry you away? O lady of captivating smiles, he could not (himself) know you to be my wife.

description: Birth of Chyavana, Bhrigu's curse on Agni
sn: तत्त्वमाख्याहि तं ह्यद्य शप्तुमिच्छाम्यहं रुषा। बिभेति को न शापान्मे कस्यचायं व्यतिक्रमः॥
en: Tell me who it was that told the Rakshasa of you, so that I may curse him from anger. Who is that one who is not afraid of my curse? By whom was this offence done?

description: Birth of Chyavana, Bhrigu's curse on Agni
sn: पुलोमोवाच अग्निना भगवंस्तस्मै रक्षसेऽहं निवेदिता। ततो मामनयद्रक्षः क्रोशन्ती कुररीमिव॥
en: Puloma said: O Lord, I was made known to the Rakshasa by Agni. He carried me away who was weeping like the Kurari.

description: Birth of Chyavana, Bhrigu's curse on Agni
sn: साऽहं तव सुतस्यास्य तेजसा परिमोक्षिता। भस्मीभूतं च तद्रक्षो मामुत्सृज्य पपात वै॥
en: I was rescued only by the extraordinary brightness of your son. The Rakshasa quitted his grasp and falling to the ground, was turned into ashes.

description: Birth of Chyavana, Bhrigu's curse on Agni
sn: सौतिरुवाच इति श्रुत्वा पुलोमाया भृगुः परममन्युमान्। शशापाग्निमतिक्रुद्धः सर्वभक्षो भविष्यसि॥
en: Sauti said: Having heard this from Puloma Bhrigu became exceedingly angry and out of anger he cursed Agni, saying, “Be an all devouring (element).

sn: सौतिरुवाच शप्तस्तु भृगुणा वह्निः क्रुद्धो वाक्यमथाब्रवीत्। किमिदं साहसं ब्रह्मन्कृतवानसि मां प्रति॥
en: Sauti said: Thus being cursed by Bhrigu. Agni said in anger, “What do you mean, Brahmana, by this rashness that you have shown towards me.”

sn: धर्मे प्रयतमानस्य सत्यं च वदतः समम्। पृष्टो यदब्रवं सत्यं व्यभिचारोऽत्र को मम॥
en: What transgression is committed by me, who tried to do justice and to speak the truth impartially? Being asked, I told the truth.

sn: पृष्टो हि साक्षी यः साक्ष्यं जानानोऽप्यन्यथा वदेत्। स पूर्वानात्मनः सप्त कुले हन्यात्तथा परान्॥
en: A witness, who being asked about a thing which he knows, says something else than what it (really) is, ruins his ancestors and descendants, both to the seventh generations.

sn: यश्च कार्यार्थतत्त्वज्ञो जानानोऽपि न भाषते। सोऽपि तेनैव पापेन लिप्येन नात्र संशयः॥
en: He, who, knowing a thing full well, does not disclose what he knows when asked is undoubtedly tainted with sin.

sn: शक्तोऽहमपि शप्तुं त्वां मान्यास्तु ब्राह्मणा मम। जानतोऽपि च ते ब्रह्मन्कथयिष्ये निबोध तत्॥
en: I can also curse you, but Brahmanas are held in respect by me. Although, O Brahinana, these are known to you, I shall yet speak them to you. Please understand.

sn: योगेन बहुधात्मानं कृत्वा तिष्ठामि मूर्तिषु। अग्निहोत्रेषु सत्रेषु क्रियासु च मखेषु च॥
en: Having multiplied myself by Yoga power, I am present in many forms. (I am present) in the Agnihotra, Satras, rituals and in other sacrifices.

sn: वेदोक्तेन विधानेन मयि यद्भूयते हविः। देवता पितरश्चैव तेन तृप्ता भवन्ति वै॥
en: The Devas and Pitris are satisfied from the ghee that is offered in my flame, according to the ordinances of the Vedas.

sn: आपो देवगणाः सर्वे आपः पितृगणास्तथा। दर्शश्च पौर्णमासश्च देवानां पितृभिः सह॥
en: The waters are all the Devas. Waters are the Pitris. The Devas have equal rights with the Pitris to perform the sacrifices, called Darsha and Paurnamasa. Darsha and Paurnamasa yajnas are performed for both Devas and Pitris.

sn: देवताः पितरस्तस्मात्पितरश्चापि देवताः। एकीभूताश्च पूज्यन्ते पृथक्त्वेन च पर्वसु॥
en: Therefore the Devas are the Pitris and the Pitris are the Devas. They are worshipped as identical beings and they are also separately worshipped at Parvas (changes of the moon).

sn: देवता: पितरश्चैव भुञ्जते मयि यद्भुतम्। देवतानां पितॄणां च मुखमेतदहं स्मृतम्॥
en: The Devas and the Pitris eat what is offered unto me. I am. therefore, called the mouth of the Devas and the Pitris.

sn: अमावास्यां हि पितरः पौर्णमास्यां हि देवताः। मन्मुखेनैव हूयन्ते भुञ्जते च हुतं हविः॥ सर्वभक्षः कथं त्वेषां भविष्यामि मुखं त्वहम्।
en: At the new-moon the Pitris and at the fullmoon the Devas are fed through my mouth with the oblations are offered unto me. Being their mouths, how can I be the eater of all things?"

sn: सौतिरुवाच चिन्तयित्वा ततो वह्निश्चक्रे संहारमात्मनः। द्विजानामग्निहोत्रेषु यज्ञसत्रक्रियासु च॥
en: Sauti said: After reflecting for some time, Agni withdrew himself from all places in the world. (he withdrew himself) from the Agnihotra of the twice-born, yajnas, satras and from other ceremonies.

sn: निरोंकारवषट्काराः स्वधास्वाहाविवर्जिताः। विनाऽग्निना प्रजाः सर्वास्तत आसन्सुदुःखिताः॥
en: Without the fire being deprived of Oms and Vashats, of Svadhas and Svahas, all creatures became very much distressed.

sn: अथर्षयः समुद्विग्ना देवान्गत्वाब्रुवन्वचः। अग्निनाशाक्रियाभ्रंशाभ्रान्ता लोकास्त्रयोऽनघाः।। विधद्ध्वमत्र तत्कार्यं न स्यात्कालात्ययो यथा। अथर्षयश्च देवाश्च ब्रह्माणमुपगम्य तु॥
en: Thereupon the Rishis went to the celestials in great anxiety and addressed them thus, "O immaculate beings, the three worlds have been confounded at the cessation of their sacrifices and ceremonies for the loss of fire. Therefore, be pleased to do the needful. There should not be any loss of time.” Their celestials and the Rishis together having approached the great Brahma,

sn: अग्नेरावेदयन्शापं क्रियासहरमेव च। भृगुणा वै महाभागः शप्तोऽग्निः कारणान्तरे॥
en: They told him all about the curse on Agni and consequent interruption of all ceremonies. They said, “O Mahabhaga, Agni has been cursed by Bhrigu for some reason.

sn: कथं देवमुखो भूत्वा यज्ञभागाग्रभुक्तथा। हुतभुक्सर्वलोकेषु सर्वभक्षत्वमेष्यति॥
en: How is it possible for Agni, who is the mouth of the celestials, who eats the first part of what is offered in sacrifice, who eats also the sacrificial ghee to become the eater of everything promiscuously?”

sn: श्रुत्वा तु तद्वचस्तेषामग्निमाहूय विश्वकृत्। उवाच वचनं श्लक्ष्णं भूतभावनमव्ययम्॥
en: The creator of the world having heard all this, called Agni to his presence. He said, to Agni, who is eternal like him and who is creator of all, in gentle words.

sn: लोकानामिह सर्वेषां त्वं कर्ता चान्त एव च। त्वं धारयसि लोकांस्त्रीन् क्रियाणां च प्रवर्तकः॥
en: "You are the creater of all creatures, you are their destroyer, you preserve the three words, you are also the promoter of all sacrifices and ceremonies,

sn: स तथा कुरु लोकेश नोच्छिोरन्यथा क्रियाः। कस्मादेवं विमूढस्त्वमीश्वरःसन्हुताशन॥
en: Therefore act in a way, so that world's ceremonies are not interrupted. O the eater of sacrificial ghee, being the Lord of all, how have you become so foolish?

sn: त्वं पवित्र सदा लोके सर्वभूतगतिश्च ह। न त्वं सर्वशरीरेण सर्वभक्षत्वमेष्यसि॥
en: You are always pure in the Universe, you are the stay of all creatures. You shall not be the eater of all things with all your body,

sn: अपाने ह्यर्चिी यास्ते सर्वं भक्ष्यन्ति ताः शिखिन्। क्रव्यादा च तनुर्या ते सा सर्वं भक्षयिष्यति॥
en: O deity of flames, Only the flames, that are in the vilest part of your body, will eat all things, alike and the part of your body which eats will also eat all things.

sn: यथा सूर्यांशुभिः स्पृष्टं सर्वं शुचि विभाव्यते। तथा त्वदर्चिनिर्दग्धं सर्वं शुचि भविष्यति॥ त्वमग्ने परमं तेजः स्वप्रभावाद्विनिर्गतम्। स्वतेजसैव तं शापं कुरु सत्यमृषेविभो। देवानां चात्मनो भागं गृहाण त्वं मुखे हुतम्॥
en: As all thing become pure, touched by the sunbeams, so will everything be pure that will be burnt in your flames. O Agni, you are the supreme energy, born of your own power. By that power, make the Rishi's curse true. Continue to receive your portion and that of the celestials offered into your mouth."

sn: सौतिरुवाच एवमस्त्विति तं वह्निः प्रत्युवाच पितामहम्। जगाम शासनं कर्तुं देवस्य परमेष्ठिनः॥
en: Sauti said: Agni then replied to the Grandfather, "Be it so" and he went away to obey the command of the Parameshthi (Supreme Lord).

sn: देवर्षयश्च मुदितास्ततो जग्मुर्यथागतम्। ऋषयश्च यथापूर्वं क्रियाः सर्वाः प्रचक्रिरे॥
en: The Rishis and the celestial also in great delight returned to the place whence they came. And the Rishis continued to perform their ceremonies and sacrifices as before.

sn: दिवि देवा मुमुदिरे भूतसंघाश्च लौकिकाः। अग्निश्च परमां प्रीतिमवाप हतकल्मषः॥
en: The celestials in heaven and all creatures on earth were exceedingly rejoiced; and Agni too rejoiced, because he became free from the curse.

sn: एवं स भगवाञ्छापं लेभेऽग्निर्भृगुतः पुरा। एवमेष पुरावृत्त इतिहासोऽग्निशापजः। पुलोम्नश्च विनाशोऽयं च्यवनस्य च संभवः॥
en: Thus in the days of yore, O possessor of the six attributes, was Agni cursed by Bhrigu, Such is the ancient history founded thereon, which contains the account of the destruction of Puloma, the Rakshasa and the birth of Chyavana.

sn: सौतिरुवाच स चापि च्यवनो ब्रह्मम्भार्गवोऽजनयत्सुतम्। सुकन्यायां महात्मानं प्रमतिं दीप्ततेजसम्॥
en: Sauti said: O Brahmana, Chyavana, the son of Bhrigu begot a son on his wife, named Sukanya. And son of Sukanya was the illustrious and the resplendently energetic Pramati.

sn: प्रमतिस्तु रुरुं नाम घृताच्यां समजीजनत्। रुरुः प्रमद्वरायां तु शुनकं समजीजनत्॥
en: Pramati begot a son called Ruru on Ghritachi. Ruru begot a son called Sunaka on his wife, Pramadvara.

sn: तस्य ब्रह्मन् रुरोः सर्वं चरितं भूरितेजसः। विस्तरेण प्रवक्ष्यामि तच्छृणु त्वमशेषतः॥
en: I shall tell you at length, O Brahmana, the history of the resplendently energetic Ruru. Listen to it in detail.

sn: ऋषिरासीन्महान्पूर्वं तयोविद्यासमन्वितः। स्थूलकेश इति ख्यातः सर्वभूतहिते रतः॥
en: In the days of yore, there was a Rishi, named Sthulakesha, who was possessed of ascetic powers and learning and engaged in doing good to all creatures.

sn: एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु मेनकायां प्रजज्ञिवान्। गन्धर्वराजो विप्रर्षे विश्वावसुरिति स्मृतः॥
en: At this time, O Brahmana Rishi, Menaka became quick with child by the king of the Gandharvas, named Vishvavasu.

sn: अप्सरा मेनका तस्य तं गर्भं भृगुनन्दन। उत्ससर्ज यथाकालं स्थूलकेशाश्रमं प्रति॥
en: O Descendant of Bhrigu, the Apsara Menaka, when the time came, delivered her child near the herinitage of Sthulakesha.

sn: उत्सृज्य चैव तं गर्भ नद्यास्तीरे जगाम सा। अप्सरा मेनका ब्रह्मन्निर्दया निरपत्रपा॥
en: And, O Brahmana, the cruel and shameless Apsara Menaka, after leaving the child on the banks of the river, went away.

sn: कन्यामरगर्भाभा ज्वलन्तीमिव च श्रिया। तां ददर्श समुत्सृष्टां नदीतीरे महानृषिः॥ स्थूलकेशः स तेजस्वी विजने बन्धुवर्जिताम्। स तां दृष्ट्वा तदा कन्यां स्थूलकेशो महाद्विजः॥
en: The great Rishi saw the girl lying forsaken in a lonely place on the banks of the river, blazing in beauty; she was as beautiful as a child of an immortal. And the great Brahmana, Sthulakesha, the chief of Munis, finding that female child.

sn: जग्राह च मुनिश्रेष्ठः कृपाविष्टः पुपोष च। ववृधे सा वरारोहा तस्याश्रमपदे शुभे॥
en: Out of compassion, took it home and brought it up. The lovely child grew up in the hermitage of the great Rishi.

sn: जातकाद्याः क्रियाश्चास्या विधिपूर्वं यथाक्रमम्। स्थूलकेशो महाभागश्चकार सुमहानृषिः॥
en: The great Rishi, the blessed Sthulakesha, performed for her in succession all the ceremonies with that of her birth, as ordained in the Shastras.

sn: प्रमदाभ्यो वरा सा तु सत्त्वरूपगुणान्विता। ततः प्रमद्वरेत्यस्या नाम चक्रे महानृषिः॥
en: As the surpassed all other ladies in beauty in goodness and in every good quality, the gave her the name as Pramadvara.

sn: तामाश्रमपदे तस्य रुरुर्दृष्ट्वा प्रमद्वराम्। बभूव किल धर्मात्मा मदनोहतस्तदा॥
en: Ruru saw her in the hermitage and the pious man fell in love with her.

sn: पितरं सखिभिः सोऽथ श्रावयामास भार्गवम्। प्रमतिश्चाभ्ययाचत्तां स्थूलकेशं यशस्विनम्॥
en: He made his father Pramati, the son of Bhrigu, acquainted with his love through his companions. Thereupon Pramati asked the illustrious Sthulakesha to give Pramadvara to his son.

sn: ततः प्रादात्पिता कन्यां रुरवे तां प्रमद्वराम्। विवाहं स्थापयित्वाऽग्रे नक्षत्रे भगदैवते॥
en: The Rishi betrothed Pramadvara to Ruru, fixing the day of marriage when the star Bhaga Daivata would be in ascendant. great Rishi

sn: ततः कतिपयाहस्य विवाहे समुपस्थिते। सखीभिः क्रीडती सार्धं सा कन्या वरवर्णिनी॥
en: A few days before the date fixed for the nuptials, while the lovely girl was playing with her companions.

sn: नापश्यत्संप्रसुप्तं वै भुजंगं तिर्यगायतम्। पदा चैनं समाक्रामन्मुमूर्षुःकालचोदिता॥
en: Her time having come and impelled by Fate, she trod upon a snake. She did not perceive it, as it lay coiled.

sn: स तस्याः संप्रमत्तायाश्चोदितः कालधर्मणा। विषोपलिप्तान्दशनाम्भृशमङ्गे न्यपातयत्॥
en: The snake, to fulfil the will of Fate, bit the heedless girl with its venomous fangs.

sn: सा दष्टा तेन सर्पण पपात सहसा भुवि। विवर्णा विगतश्रीका भ्रष्टाभरणचेतना॥
en: Bitten by the snake, she suddenly fell senseless on the ground with her colour faded all her beauties gone and all her ornaments scattered.

sn: निरानन्दकरी तेषां बधूनां मुक्तमूर्धजा। व्यसुरप्रेक्षणीया सा प्रेक्षणीयतमाऽभवत्॥
en: Her hair dishevelled, a spectacle of woe to her friends and companions. She, who was so handsome when alive, became in death what was too painful to look at.

sn: प्रसुप्तेवाभवच्चापि भुवि सर्पविषार्दिता। भूयो मनोहरतरा बभूव तनुमध्यमा॥
en: The slender-waisted girl, as she lay on the ground as one asleep, looked more beautiful than she was when alive.

sn: ददर्श तां पिता चैव ये चैवान्ये तपस्विनः। विचेष्टमानां पतितां भूतले पद्मवर्चसम्॥
en: Her father and other ascetics, who were present, saw her lying motionless on the ground with the beauty of a lotus.

sn: ततः सर्वे द्विजवराः समाजग्मुः कृपान्विताः। स्वस्त्यात्रेयो महाजानुः कुशिकः शंखमेखलः॥
en: Then there came all the noted Brahmanas, filled with compassion. Svastyatreya, Mahajanu, Kushika, Shankhamekhala.

sn: उद्दालकः कठश्चैव श्वेतश्चैव महायशाः। । भरद्वाजः कौणकुत्स्य आर्टिषेणोऽथ गौतमः॥
en: Uddalaka, Katha and the renowned Shveta, Bharadvaja, Kaunakutsya, Arshtishena, Goutama,

sn: प्रमति: सहपुत्रेण तथाऽन्ये वनवासिनः। तां ते कन्यां व्यसुं दृष्ट्वा भुजंगस्य विषार्दिताम्।। रुरुदुः कृपयाविष्टा रुरुस्त्वार्तो बहिर्ययौ। ते च सर्वे द्विजश्रेष्ठास्तत्रैवोपाविशंस्तदा।॥
en: Pramati and Pramati's son Ruru and other inhabitants of the forest were filled with compassion and they all wept when they saw the maiden lying on the ground overcome by the poison of the snake. And Ruru, being exceedingly pained, left the scene. A

sn: सौतिरुवाच तेषु तत्रोपविष्टेषु ब्राह्मणेषु महात्मसु। रुक्षुक्रोश गहनं वनं गत्वाऽतिदुःखितः॥
en: Sauti replied : While the noble Brahmanas were sitting round the dead body, Ruru, much aggrieved, retired into a deep forest and wept aloud.

sn: शोकेनाभिहतः सोऽथ विलपन्करुणं बहु। अब्रवीद्वचनं शोचन्धियां स्मृत्वा प्रमद्वराम्॥
en: Overwhelmed with grief, he indulged in much piteous lamentations. Remembering his beloved Pramadvara, he thus lamented in grief,

sn: शेते सा भुवि तन्वङ्गी मम शोकविवर्धिनी। बान्धवानां च सर्वेषां किं नु दुःखमत:परम्॥
en: “Alas! The slender-bodied beauty who increases my grief, is now lying on the bare ground. What can be more painful than this to all her friends!

sn: यदि दत्तं तपस्तप्तं गुरवो वा मया यदि। सम्यगाराधितास्तेन संजीवतु मम प्रिया॥
en: If ever I have bestowed charity, if ever I have observed penances, if ever I have showed respect to my superiors, let the merits of these acts restore to life my beloved one.

sn: यथा च जन्मप्रभृति यतात्माऽहं धृतव्रतः। प्रमद्वरा तथा ह्येषा समुत्तिष्ठतु भामिनी॥
en: If ever I have controlled my passions from my birth, if ever I have stuck to my vows, let the beautiful Pramadvara rise from the ground.”

sn: एवं लालप्यतस्तस्य भार्यार्थे दुःखितस्य च। देवदूतस्तदाऽभ्येत्य वाक्यमाह रुरुं वने।॥
en: While he was thus lamenting in sorrow for the loss of his bride a heaven's messenger came to him in the forest and addressed hiin thus:

sn: देवदूत उवाच अभिधत्से ह यद्वाचा रुरो दुखेन तन्मृषा। यतो मर्त्यस्य धर्मात्मन्नायुरस्ति गतायुषः॥
en: The Devaduta said: O Ruru, the words that you are uttering in grief can have no effect; for, O noble-minded (Rishi), one belonging to this world, whose days are run out, cannot come back to life again.

sn: गतायुरेषा कृपणा गन्धर्वाप्सरसोः तस्माच्छोके मनस्तात मा कृथास्त्वं कथंचन॥
en: This poor child of the Gandharva and the Apsara has her days run out; therefore, O child, do not give yourself up to grief.

sn: उपायश्चात्र विहितः पूर्वं देवैर्महात्मभिः। तं यदीच्छसि कर्तुं त्वं प्राप्स्यसीह प्रमद्वराम्॥
en: The great deities, however, have provided beforehand a means. If you comply with it, you may get back your Pramadvara.

sn: रुरुरुवाच क उपायः कृतो देवै—हि तत्त्वेन खेचर। करिष्येऽहं तथा श्रुत्वा त्रातुमर्हति मां भवान्॥
en: Ruru said: O messenger of heaven, (tell me) what means have been provided beforehand by the deities. Tell me in full, so that I may comply with it. You should save me.

sn: देवदूत उवाच आयुषोऽर्धं प्रयच्छत्वं कन्यायै भृगुनन्दन। सुता। एवमुत्थास्यति रुरो तव भार्या प्रमद्वरा॥
en: The Devaduta said : O Descendant of Bhrigu, give up half of your own life to your bride and O Ruru, your Pramadvara will then rise from the ground.

sn: रुरुरुवाच आयुषोऽर्धं प्रयच्छामि कन्यायै खेचरोत्तम। श्रृंगाररूपाभरणा समुत्तिष्ठतु मे प्रिया॥
en: Ruru said: O best of heaven's messengers, 1 give up half of my life to my bride. Let my beloved one rise in the beautiful form decked with ornaments.

sn: सौतिरुवाच ततो गन्धर्वराजश्च देवदूतश्च सत्तमौ। धर्मराजमुपेत्येदं वचनं प्रत्यभाषताम्॥
en: Sauti said: The king of the Gandharvas and the greatly qualified messenger of heaven, both went to the Deity Dharma and addressed him thus :

sn: धर्मराजायुषोर्धेन रुरोर्भार्या प्रमद्वरा। समुत्तिष्ठतु कल्याणी मृतैवं यदि मन्यसे॥
en: "O king Dharma, if it please you, let the beautiful bride of Ruru, Pramadvara, who is dead, rise up endued with a half of Ruru's life.”

sn: धर्मराज उवाच प्रमद्वरां रुरोर्भार्यां देवदूत यदीच्छसि। उत्तिष्ठत्वायुषोऽर्धेन रुरोरेव समन्विता॥
en: The Dharmaraja said : "O messenger of heaven, if it be your wish, let the bride of Ruru Pramadvara, rise up endued with a half of Ruru's life.

sn: सौतिरुवाच एवमुक्ते ततः कन्या सोदतिष्ठत्प्रमद्वरा। रुरोस्तस्यायुषोऽर्धेन सुप्तेव वरवर्णिनी॥
en: Sauti said : When Dharma thus spoke, the beautiful Pramadvara, the betrothed bride of Ruru, rose up as from a slumber, with a half of Ruru's life.

sn: एतदृष्टं भविष्ये हि रुरोरुत्तमतेजसः। आयुषोऽतिप्रवृद्धस्य भार्यार्थेऽर्धमलुप्यत॥
en: It was seen afterwards that the bestowal of a half of his own life to resuscitate his bride by Ruru of long life, led to a curtailment of his own life.

sn: तत इष्टेऽहनि तयोः पितरौ चक्रतुर्मुदा। विवाहं तौ च रेमाते परस्परहितैषिणौ॥
en: Thereupon their fathers gladly married them off with due rites and the couple passed their days devoted to each other.

sn: स लब्ध्वा दुर्लभां भार्या पद्मकिञ्जल्कसुप्रभाम्। व्रतं चक्रे विनाशाय जिह्मगानां धृतव्रतः॥
en: Thus having obtained a wife, difficult to be obtained, who was beautiful and bright as the filaments of the lotus, the Rishi of hard austerities (Ruru) made a vow to destroy the serpent race.

sn: स दृष्ट्वा जिह्मगान्सर्वांस्तीव्रकोपसमन्वितः। अभिहन्ति यथा सत्त्वं गृह्य प्रहरणं सदा॥
en: Whenever he saw a snake, he was filled with great anger and he always killed it with a weapon.

sn: स कदाचिद्वनं विप्रो रुरुरभ्यागमन्महत्। शयानं तत्र चापश्यत् डुण्डुभं वयसान्वितम्॥
en: One day, the Brahmana, Ruru entered into a very large forest. He saw an old Dundubha snake lying on the ground.

sn: तत उद्यम्य दण्डं स कालदण्डोपमं तदा। जिघांसुः कुपितो विप्रस्तमुवाचाऽथ डुण्डुभः॥
en: Thereupon with the intention of killing it, Ruru raised his staff in anger, A staff like the staff of Death. The Dundubha then said to the angry Brahmana.

sn: नापराध्यामि ते किंचिदहमद्य तपोधन। संरंभाच्च किमर्थं मामभिहंसि रुषाऽन्वितः॥
en: "O Rishi, I have done you no harm. Why should you kill me in anger?"

sn: रुरुरुवाच मम प्राणसमाभार्या दष्टासीद्भुजगेन ह। तत्र मे समयो घोर आत्मनोरग वै कृतः॥
en: Ruru said : My wife, who was as dear to me as my life, was bitten by a snake; on which I took, O snake, a fearful vow;

sn: भुजंगं वै सदा हन्यां यं यं पश्येयमित्युत। ततोऽहं त्वां जिघांसामि जीवितेनाद्य मोक्ष्यसे॥
en: Namely that I would kill every snake that I might meet with. Therefore I shall strike you and you shall be deprived of your life.

sn: डुण्डुभ उवाच अन्ये ते भुजगा ब्रह्मन् ये दशन्तीह मानवान्। डुण्डुभानहिगन्धेन न त्वं हिंसितुमर्हसि॥
en: The Dundubha said: O Brahmana, there are other snakes which bite man. The Dundubhas are only snakes in name. Therefore, you should not kill the Dundubhas.

sn: एकानर्थान्पृथगर्थानेकदुःखान्पृथक्सुखान्। डुण्डुभान्धर्मविद्भूत्वा न त्वं हिंसितुमर्हसि॥
en: Subject to the same calamity but not sharing the same good fortune, being same in woe, but different in joy, you should not kill the Dundubhas, being a knower of right and wrong.

sn: सौतिरुवाच इति श्रुत्वा वचस्तस्य भुजगस्य रुरुस्तदा। नावधीद्भयसंविग्नमृर्षि मत्वाऽथ डुण्डुभम्॥
en: Sauti said: Hearing those words of the snake and seeing that the snake was really of the Dundubha kind and that it was terribly frightened. Ruru did not kill it, thinking that it is a Rishi.

sn: उवाच चैनं भगवान् रुरुः संशमयन्निव। कामं मां भुजग ब्रूहि कोऽसीमां विक्रियां गतः॥
en: Then Ruru, the possessor of six attributes, cheering up the snake, said to it, “Who are you, tell me, O snake, that have been thus metamorphosed?”

sn: डुण्डुभ उवाच अहं पुरा रुरो नाम्ना ऋषिरासं सहस्रपात्। सोऽहं शापेन विप्रस्य भुजगत्वमुपागतः। :॥
en: The Dundubha said: O Ruru, I was formerly a Rishi, named Shahasrapat. It is by the curse of a Brahmana that I have become a snake.

sn: रुरुरुवाच किमर्थं शप्तवान्क्रुद्धो द्विजस्त्वां भुजगोत्तम। कियन्तं चैव कालं ते वपुरेतद्भविष्यति॥
en: Ruru said : O best of snakes, why were you cursed by an angry Brahmana? And how long will your this body continue?

sn: डुण्डुभ उवाच सखा बभूव मे पूर्वं खगमो नाम वै द्विजः। भृशं संशितवाक्तात तपोबलसमन्वितः॥
en: The Dundubha said : In time gone by, I had a friend, a Brahmana, by name Khagama. He was truthful and possessed spiritual powers by penances.

sn: स मया क्रीडता बाल्ये कृत्वा तार्ण भुजंगमम्। अग्निहोत्रे प्रसक्तस्तु भीषितः प्रमुमोह वै॥
en: When he was engaged in Agnihotra, out of boyish frivolity, I made a snake of the blades of grass and tried to frighten him. He fainted away (when he saw this mock snake).

sn: लब्वा स च पुनः संज्ञां मामुवाच तपोधनः। निर्दहन्निव कोपेन सत्यवाक्संशितव्रतः॥
en: Recovering his senses, that truthful and penance-performing Rishi exclaimed to me in anger.

sn: यथावीर्यस्त्वया सर्पः कृतोऽयं मद्विभीषया। तथावीर्यो भुजंगस्त्वं मम शापाद्भविष्यसि॥
en: "As you made a powerful mock snake to frighten me, you will yourself turn into a venomless serpent by my curse."

sn: तस्याहं तपसो वीर्यं जानन्नासं तपोधन। भृशमुद्विग्नहृदयस्तमवोचमहं तदा॥
en: O Rishi, I was well aware of the power of penances that he possessed. Therefore, with an agitated heart, I addressed him thus,

sn: प्रणत: संभ्रमादेव प्राञ्जलिः पुरतः स्थितः। सखेति सहसेदं ते नर्मार्थं वै कृतं मया॥
en: Bending low and joining both hands, "As I am your friend, I have done this only as a joke to make you laugh.

sn: क्षन्तुमर्हसि मे ब्रह्मन् शापोऽयं विनिवर्त्यताम्। सोऽथ मामब्रवीदृष्ट्वा भृशमुद्विग्मनचेतसम्॥ मुहुरुष्णं विनिःश्वस्य सुसंभ्रान्तस्तपोधनः। नानृतं वै मया प्रोक्तं भवितेदं कथंचन॥
en: You should, O Brahmana, pardon me and revoke your curse." Seeing me very much distressed, the ascetic moved and breathing hot and hard, he said, What I have said must happen.

sn: यत्तु वक्ष्यामि ते वाक्यं शृणु तन्मे तपोधन। श्रुत्या च हृदि ते वाक्यमिदमस्तु सदानघ॥
en: O ascetic, listen to what I say and hearing it, O pious man, always keep it to your heart.

sn: उत्पत्स्यति रुरुर्नाम प्रमतेरात्मजः शुचिः। तं दृष्ट्वा शापमोक्षस्ते भविता न चिरादिव॥
en: When Ruru the holy, the son of Pramati will appear, you will be immediately relieved of the curse on seeing him.”

sn: स त्वं रुरुरितिख्यातः प्रमतेरात्मजोऽपि च। स्वरूपं प्रतिपद्याहमद्य वक्ष्यामि ते हितम्॥
en: You are the very Ruru, the son of Pramati. Now regaining my natural form I shall speak something for your benefit.

sn: स डौण्डुभं परित्यज्य रूपं विप्रर्षभस्तदा। स्वरूपभास्वरं भूयः प्रतिपेदे महायशाः॥
en: was Souti said : That illustrious man and the best of Brahmanas then left his snake-body and attained his own form with original brightness.

sn: इदं चोवाच वचनं रुरुमप्रतिमौजसम्। अहिंसा परमो धर्मः सर्वप्राणभृतां वर॥
en: He then addressed Ruru of incomparable power, saying, “O best of beings, the highest morality is not to hurt others.

sn: तस्मात्प्राणभृतः सर्वान्न हिंस्याब्राह्मणः क्वचित्। ब्राह्मणः सौम्य एवेह भवतीति परा श्रुतिः॥
en: Therefore, a Brahmana should never hurt any creature. The injunction of the Shruti is that a Brahmana should always be mild.

sn: वेदवेदाङ्गविन्नाम सर्वभूताभयप्रदः। अहिंसा सत्यवचनं क्षमा चेति विनिश्चितम्॥
en: Learned in the Vedas and the Vedangas and an inspirer of confidence in all creatures, kind to all, truthful and forgiving.

sn: ब्राह्मणस्य परो धर्मो वेदानां धारणापि च। क्षत्रियस्य हि यो धर्मः स हि नेष्येत वै तव॥
en: And a great retainer of the Vedas in memory, these are the natural duties of a Brahmana. The natural duties of Kshatriya are not those of yours.

sn: दण्डधारणमुग्रत्वं प्रजानां परिपालनम्। तदिदं क्षत्रियस्यासीत्कर्म वै शृणु मे रुरो॥
en: To be stern, to hold a rod (for punishable), to rule the subjects, are the natural duties of the Kshatriya. Listen to ine, O Ruru.

sn: जनमेजयस्य यज्ञेऽस्मिन् सर्पाणां हिंसनं पुरा। परित्राणां च भीतानां सर्पाणां ब्राह्मणादपि॥
en: In days of yore, the snakes were destroyed in the sacrifice of Janamejaya, but the terrified snakes were saved by a Brahmana.

sn: तपोवीर्यबलोपेताद्वेवदेदाङ्गपारगात्। आस्तीकाद्विजमुख्याद्वै सर्पसत्रे द्विजोत्तम॥
en: It was by Astika learned in the Vedas and the Vedangas and mighty in spiritual power.

sn: रुरुरुवाच कथं हिंसितवान्सन्स राजा जनमेजयः। सर्पा वा हिंसितास्तत्र किमर्थं द्विजसत्तम॥
en: Ruru said: O best of the twice-born, why did king Janamejaya become the destroyer of the snakes and how did he destroy them?

sn: किमर्थं मोक्षिताश्चैव पन्नगास्तेन धीमता। आस्तीकेन द्विजश्रेष्ठ श्रोतुमिच्छाम्यशेषतः॥
en: Why were they saved by wise Astika, the best of Brahmanas? I am desirous of hearing all this.

sn: ऋषिरुवाच श्रोष्यसि त्वं रुरो सर्वमास्तीकचरितं महत्। ब्राह्मणानां कथयतामित्युक्त्वान्तरधीयत॥
en: Rishi said: O Ruru, you will hear the important history of Astika from the Brahmanas. Saying this he disappeared.

sn: सौतिरुवाच रुस्श्चापि वनं सर्वं पर्यधावत्समन्ततः। तमृषि नष्टमन्विच्छन्संश्रान्तो न्यपत वि॥
en: Sauti said: Ruru rushed in search of the Rishi, but he did not find him in all the forest. Finding him not, he sat down on the ground, much fatigued.

sn: स मोहं परमं गत्वा नष्टसंज्ञ इवाभवत्। तदृषेर्वचनं तथ्यं चिन्तयानं पुनः पुनः॥
en: He felt himself confounded and seemed to lose his senses. He repeatedly pondered over the Rishi's words.

sn: लब्धसंज्ञो रुस्चायात्तदाचख्यौ पितुस्तदा। पिता चास्य तदाख्यानं पृष्टः सर्वं न्यवेदयत्॥
en: Regaining his senses, he came home and asked his father (to relate the history) and his father related to him the story. End of Pau loma Parva

sn: शौनक उवाच किमर्थं राजशार्दूल: स राजा जनमेजयः। सर्पसत्रेण सणां गतोऽन्तं तद्वदस्व मे॥
en: Shaunaka said: son was Why did that best of kings, king Janamejaya, resolve to destroy the snakes in a Snake-sacrifice?

sn: निखिलेन यथातत्त्वं सौते सर्वमशेषतः। आस्तीकश्च द्विजश्रेष्ठः किमर्थं जयतां वरः॥
en: O Sauti, tell us in full the true story. Why did the best of the twice-born Astika, the foremost of ascetics, rescue the snakes from the blazing fire?

sn: मोक्षयामास भुजगान् प्रदीप्ताद्वसुरेतसः। कस्य पुत्रः स राजासीत्सर्पसत्रं य आहरत्॥ स च द्विजातिप्रवरः कस्य पुत्रोऽभिधत्स्व मे।
en: Whose the monarch who performed the Snake-sacrifice? Whose son was that best of the twice-born, (who saved the snakes)? Tell us this.

sn: सौतिरुवाच महदाख्यानमास्तीकं यथैतत्प्रोच्यते द्विजः। सर्वमेतदशेषेण शृणु मे वदतां वर॥
en: Sauti said: O best of speakers, the story of Astika is very long, I shall relate it in full. O Listen.

sn: शौनक उवाच श्रोतुमिच्छाम्यशेषेण कथामेतां मनोरमाम्। आस्तीकस्य पुराणाह्मणस्य यशस्विनः॥
en: Shaunaka said : I am desirous of hearing in detail the interesting story of Astika, the illustrious Brahmana.

sn: सौतिरुवाच इतिहासमिमं विप्राः पुराणं परिचक्षते। कृष्णद्वैपायनप्रोक्तं नैमिषारण्यवासिषु॥
en: Sauti said: m The Brahmanas call this history, recited by Krishna Dvaipayana, a Purana, to the dwellers of Naimisharanya.

sn: पूर्वं प्रचोदितः सूतः पिता मे लोमहर्षणः। शिष्यो व्यासस्य मेधावी ब्राह्मणेष्विदमुक्तवान्॥
en: It was formerly narrated by my learned father Lomaharshana, the disciple of Vyasa, as requested by the Brahmanas.

sn: तस्मादहमुपश्रुत्य प्रवक्ष्यामि यथातथम्। इदमास्तीकमाख्यानं तुभ्यं शौनक पृच्छते॥
en: I was present at the time, O Shaunaka, As you ask me, I shall recite it exactly as I heard it.

sn: कथयिष्याम्यशेषेण सर्वपापप्रणाशनम्। आस्तीकस्य पिता ह्यासीत्प्रजापतिसमः प्रभुः॥
en: (Listen) to this all sin-destroying history. Astika's father was as powerful as the Prajapati.

sn: ब्रह्मचारी यताहारस्तपस्युग्रे रतः सदा। जरत्कारुरिति ख्यात अर्ध्वरेता महातपाः॥
en: He was a Brahmachari, always engaged in austere penances, regular in meals, a great Rishi of controlled sexual desire. He was known by the name of Jaratkaru.

sn: यायावराणां प्रवरो धर्मज्ञः संशितव्रतः। स कदाचिन्महाभागस्तपोबलसमन्वितः॥
en: He was the foremost of Yayavaras, a man of rigid vows, highly religious and endowed with great ascetic powers. Once upon a time this great ascetic,

sn: चचार पृथिवीं सर्वां यत्र सायंगृहो मुनिः। तीर्थेषु च समाप्लावं कुर्वनटति सर्वशः॥
en: Being Yatra Sayan Griha (living in the place where night overtook him), roamed all over the world, bathed in many sacred waters and visited many holy shrines.

sn: चरन्दीक्षां महातेजा दुश्चरामकृतात्मभिः। वायुभक्षो निराहारः शुष्यन्ननिमिषो मुनिः॥
en: He practised difficult austere penances; and feeding on air, remaining in fast and renouncing sleep forever, he roamed (over the world.)

sn: इतस्ततः परिचरन् दीप्तपावकसप्रभः। अटमानः कदाचित्स्वान् स ददर्श पितामहान्॥
en: As bright as a blazing fire, he roamed about and thus roving about, he one day saw his ancestors,

sn: लम्बमानान्महागर्ते पादैरूधैरवाङ्मुखान्। तानब्रवीत्स दुष्टवैव जरत्कारुः पितामहान्॥
en: Hanging their heads down in a great hole, their feet pointing upwards. On seeing them, Jaratkaru addressed his ancestors thus,

sn: के भवन्तोऽवलम्बन्ते गर्ने ह्यस्मिन्नधोमुखाः। वीरणस्तम्बके लग्नाः सर्वतः परिभक्षिते॥ मूषकेन निगूढेन गर्तेऽस्मिन्नित्यवासिना।
en: “Who are you thus hanging in the hole, your heads downward, by a rope of the Virana fibre which has been eaten by the rats that live secretly near this hole?"

sn: पितर ऊचुः यायावरा नाम वयमृषयः संशितव्रताः। संतानप्रक्षयाब्रह्मन्नधो गच्छाम मेदिनीम्॥
en: The Ancestors said : We are Rishis of austere penances, called Yayavaras. We are sinking down into the earth for want of an offspring.

sn: अस्माकं संततिस्त्वेको जरत्कारुरिति स्मृतः। मन्दभाग्योऽल्पभाग्यानां तप एव समास्थितः॥
en: We have a son, named Jaratkaru. Unfortunate we are, that wretch has adopted asceticism.

sn: न स पुत्राञ्जनयितुं दारान्मूढश्चिकीर्षति। तेन लम्बामहे गर्ने संतानस्य क्षयादिह॥
en: And therefore that fool does not think of marriage to raise up offspring. It is for this reason, namely for the want of offspring that we are thus suspended in the hole.

sn: अनाथास्तेन नाथेन यया दुष्कृतिनस्तथा। कस्त्वं बन्धुरिवास्माकमनुशोचसि सत्तम॥
en: Having means, we are like sinners who have no means. O excellent man, who are you that are sorrowing for us like a friend?

sn: ज्ञातुमिच्छामहे ब्रह्मन् कोभवानिह न: स्थितः। किमर्थं चैव नः शोच्याननुशोचसि सत्तम॥
en: O Brahmana, we wish to know who you are that stand near us and why? O excellent iman, are you sorrowing for us?

sn: जरत्कारुरुवाच मम पूर्वे भवन्तो वै पितरः सपितामहाः। ब्रूत किं करवाण्यद्य जरत्कारुरहं स्वयम्॥
en: Jaratkaru said: You are my sires and grand-sires. I am that very Jaratkaru. Tell me what I should do.

sn: पितर ऊचुः यतस्व यत्नवांस्तात संतानाय कुलस्य नः। आत्मनोऽर्थेस्मदर्थे च धर्म इत्येव वा विभो॥
en: The Ancestors said : Try your best to do that by which you can raise up an offspring to extend our line. You will then do an act meritorious both for you and for us.

sn: न हि धर्मफलैस्तात न तपोभिः सुसंचितैः। तां गतिं प्राप्नुवन्तीह पुत्रिणो यां व्रजन्ति वै॥
en: O Son, not by the fruits of virtue, nor by the hoarded-up ascetic penances, does one acquire such merit as is acquired by one who is a father.

sn: तद्दारग्रहणे यत्नं संतत्यां च मनः कुरु। पुत्रकास्मन्नियोगात्त्वमेतन्नः परमं हितम्॥
en: Therefore, O son, set your mind upon marriage and offspring at our command. It will do us the highest good.

sn: जरत्कारुरुवाच न दारान्वै करिष्येऽहं न धनं जीवितार्थतः। भवतां तु हितार्थाय करिष्ये दारसंग्रहम्॥
en: Jaratkaru said : I shall not marry, nor shall I earn money for my own self. But I shall marry to do you good.

sn: समयेन च कर्ताहमनेन विधिपूर्वकम्। यथा यधुपलप्स्यामि करिष्ये नान्यथा ह्यहम्॥ सनाम्नी या भवित्री मे दित्सिता चैव बन्धुभिः। भैक्ष्यवत्तामहं कन्यामुपयंस्ये विधानतः॥
en: If a bride can be had whose name will be the same as mine, whose friends will give her to me willingly and as a gift, O fathers, under these conditions, if I get a girl, your command will be obeyed. I shall duly marry her according to the ordinances of the Shastras.

sn: दरिद्राय हि मे भार्यां को दास्यति विशेषतः। प्रतिग्रहीष्ये भिक्षां तु यदि कश्चित्प्रदास्यति॥
en: But who will give his daughter to a poor man like me to be my wife? I shall, however, accept the girl who will be given to me as gift.

sn: एवं दारक्रियाहेतोः प्रयतिष्ये पितामहाः। अनेन विधिना शश्वन्न करिष्येऽहमन्यथा।॥
en: O sires, I shall try to marry such a girl. Having said so, I shall not act otherwise.

sn: तत्र चोत्पत्स्यते जन्तुर्भवतां तारणाय वै। शाश्वतं स्थानमासाद्य मोदन्तां पितरो मम॥
en: O fathers, I shall beget offspring on her for your release, so that you may attain to the heaven, called Shashvata and rejoice there at will.

sn: सौतिरुवाच ततो निवेशाय तदा स विप्रः संशितव्रतः। महीं चचार दारार्थी न च दारानविन्दतः॥
en: Sauti said : The Brahmana of hard austerities (Jaratkaru) roamed over the world for a wife, but he did not get a wife.

sn: स कदाचिद्वनं गत्वा विप्रः पितृवचः स्मरन्। चुक्रोश कन्याभिक्षार्थी तिस्रो वाचः शनैरिव॥
en: One day he went into the forest and remembering the words of his ancestors, he thrice begged for a bride in a faint voice.

sn: तं वासुकिः प्रत्यगृह्णादुद्यम्य भगिनीं तदा। न स तां प्रतिजग्राह न सनाम्नीति चिन्तयन्॥
en: Thereupon, Vasuki appeared and offered his sister for the Rishi's acceptance. But the Rishi hesitated to accept her, thinking her to be not of the same name with himself.

sn: सनाम्नी चोद्यतां भार्यां गृह्णीयामिति तस्य हि। मनो निविष्टमभवज्जरत्कारोर्महात्मनः॥
en: The high-souled Jaratkaru thought within himself, “I will take none for my wife who does not bear my name."

sn: तमुवाच महाप्राज्ञो जरत्करुमहातपाः। किं नाम्नी भगिनीयं ते ब्रूहि सत्यं भुजंगम॥
en: Then Jaratkaru, the great ascetic of rigid austerities, said, “O snake tell me truly what is the name of your sister?”

sn: वासुकिरुवाच जरत्कारो जरत्कारुः स्वसेयमनुजा मम। प्रतिगृह्णीष्व भार्यार्थे मया दत्तां सुमध्यमाम्। त्वदर्थं रक्षिता पूर्वं प्रतीच्छेमां द्विजोत्तम॥
en: Vasuki said: O Jaratkaru, my sister's name is also Jaratkaru. Given as a gift by me, accept this girl of slender waist for your wife. O best of the twice born, I had kept her in reserve for you. Therefore, take her.

sn: एवमुक्त्वा ततः प्रादाद्भार्यार्थे वरवर्णिनीम्। स च तां प्रतिजग्राह विधिदृष्टेन कर्मणा॥
en: Saying this he offered his beautiful sister to Jaratkaru, who then married her according to the ordained rites.

description: Curse of snakes by mother Kadru
sn: सौतिरुवाच मात्रा हि भुजगा: शप्ताः पूर्वं ब्रह्मविदांवर। जनमेजयस्य वो यज्ञे धक्ष्यत्यनिलसारथिः॥
en: Sauti said : O foremost of Brahma knowing men, the mother of the snakes, in the days of yore, cursed the Naga race, saying, "He whose charioteer is wind (Agni) will consume you at Janamejaya's sacrifice.

description: Curse of snakes by mother Kadru
sn: तस्य शापस्य शान्त्यर्थं प्रददौ पन्नगोत्तमः। स्वसारमृषये तस्मै सुव्रताय महात्मने।॥
en: To neutralise ve effect of that curse, the best of snakes (Vasuki) married off his sister to the high-souled Rishi of rigid vow.

description: Curse of snakes by mother Kadru
sn: स च तां प्रतिजग्राह विधिदृष्टेन कर्मणा। आस्तीको नामपुत्रश्च तस्यां जज्ञे महामनाः॥
en: Accepting her according to the ordained rites, he begot on her a high-souled son, called Astika,

description: Curse of snakes by mother Kadru
sn: तपस्वी च महात्मा च वेदवेदाङ्गपारगः। समः सर्वस्य लोकस्य पितृमातृभयापहः॥
en: Who was a great ascetic, who was vastly learned in the Vedas and the Vedangas, who removed the fears of his parents and who saw everything with an equal eye.

description: Curse of snakes by mother Kadru
sn: अथ दीर्घस्य कालस्य पाण्डवेयो नराधिपः। आजहार महायज्ञं सर्पसत्रमिति श्रुतिः॥
en: Then after a long time, a descendant of the Pandavas, celebrated a great sacrifice, known as the Snake-sacrifice.

description: Curse of snakes by mother Kadru
sn: तस्मिन्प्रवृत्ते सत्रे तु सर्याणामन्तकाय वै। मोचयामास तान्नागानास्तीकः सुमहातपाः॥
en: When the sacrifice for the destruction of the snakes had begun, the great ascetic Astika rescued the Nagas,

description: Curse of snakes by mother Kadru
sn: भ्रातृ॑श्च मातुलांश्चैव तथैवान्यान्स पन्नगान्। पितुंश्च तारयामास संतत्या तपसा तथा॥
en: His brothers, his maternal uncles and other snakes. He also delivered his fathers by begetting a child.

description: Curse of snakes by mother Kadru
sn: व्रतैश्च विविधैर्ब्रह्मन्स्वाध्यायैश्चानृणोऽभवत्। देवांश्च तर्पयामास यज्ञैर्विविधदक्षिणैः। :॥
en: O Brahmana, he freed himself from their debts by rigid austerities, by various vows and the study of the Vedas. He propitiated the celestials by sacrifices in which various presents were made.

description: Curse of snakes by mother Kadru
sn: ऋषींश्च ब्रह्मचर्येण संतत्या च पितामहान्। अपहृत्य गुरुं भारं पितॄणां संशितव्रतः॥
en: He pleased the Rishis by his Brahmacharya and his ancestors by begetting offspring. Thus discharging the heavy debt that he owed to his ancestors.

description: Curse of snakes by mother Kadru
sn: जरत्कारुर्गतः स्वर्गं सहित: स्वैः पितामहैः। आस्तीकं च सुतं प्राप्य धर्मं चानुत्तमं मुनिः॥
en: Jaratkaru, of great austerity, attained heaven with his forefathers. Begetting the son, Astika and acquiring great religious merit, the best of the Munis,

description: Curse of snakes by mother Kadru
sn: जरत्कारुः सुमहता कालेन स्वर्गमेयिवान्। एतदाख्यानमास्तीकं यथावत्कथितं मया। प्रब्रूहि भृगुशार्दूल किमन्यत्कथयामि ते॥
en: The greatly noble Jaratkaru, after a long course of years, went to heaven. This is the story of Astika. I have narrated it (to you) as it is. Now, tell me, O best of the Bhrigu race, what else shall I narrate.

description: Story of the origin of snakes
sn: शौनक उवाच सौते त्वं कथयस्वेमां विस्तरेण कथां पुनः। आस्तीकस्य कवेः साधोः शुश्रूषा परमा हि नः॥
en: Shaunaka said: O Sauti, once more relate to us in detail the history of the learned and virtuous Astika. Great is our curiosity to hear it.

description: Story of the origin of snakes
sn: मधुरं कथ्यते सौम्य श्लक्ष्णाक्षरपदं त्वया। प्रीयामहे भृशं तात पितेवेदं प्रभाषसे॥
en: O gentle one, you speak very sweetly with proper accent and emphasis. We are very much, pleased with your speech. You speak like your (late) father.

description: Story of the origin of snakes
sn: अस्मच्छुश्रूषणे नित्यं पिता हि निरतस्तव। आचष्टैतद्यथाख्यानं पिता ते त्वं तथा वद॥
en: Your father was always ready to please us. Tell us, therefore, the story that your father had related.

description: Story of the origin of snakes
sn: सौतिरुवाच आयुष्मन्निदमाख्यानमास्तीकं कथयामि ते। यथाश्रुतं कथयतः सकाशाद्वै पितुर्मया॥
en: Sauti said: O long-lived ones, I shall narrate this story of Astika as I heard it from my father.

description: Story of the origin of snakes
sn: पुरा देवयुगे ब्रह्म प्रजापतिसुते शुभे। आस्तां भगिन्यौ रूपेण समुपेतेद्धतेऽनघ॥
en: O Brahmana, in the golden age Prajapati had two fair daughters. O sinless one, the two sisters were endued with great beauty.

description: Story of the origin of snakes
sn: ते भार्ये कश्यपस्यास्तां कद्रूश्च विनता च ह। प्रादात्ताभ्यां वरं प्रीतः प्रजापतिसमः पतिः॥
en: They were named Kadru and Vinata and they were the wives of Kashyapa. Their husband, who like Prajapati, having been pleased with them, gave each a boon

description: Story of the origin of snakes
sn: कश्यपो धर्मपत्नीभ्यां मुदा परमया युतः। वरातिसगं श्रुत्वैवं कश्यपादुत्तमं च ते॥
en: Kashyapa derived much happiness from his wives. Hearing that their husband Kashyapa was willing to bestow on them boons.

description: Story of the origin of snakes
sn: हषार्दप्रतिमां प्रीतिं प्रापतुःस्म वरस्त्रियौ। वने कदूः सुतान्नागान्सहस्रं तुल्यवर्चसः॥
en: The most beautiful damsels felt a transport of joy. Kadru wished to have one thousand snakes as her sons, all of equal splendour.

description: Story of the origin of snakes
sn: द्वौ पुत्रौ विनता वने कदूपुत्राधिको बले। तेजसा वपुषा चैव विक्रमेणाधिकौ च तौ॥
en: Vinata asked for two sons, more in strength, energy, size and prowess than the sons of Kadru.

description: Story of the origin of snakes
sn: तस्यै भर्ता वरं प्रादादत्यर्थं पुत्रमीप्सितम्। एवमस्त्विति तं चाह कश्यपं विनता तदा॥
en: On her did her husband bestow the boon of the desired sons; and Vinata said to him, “Be it so."

description: Story of the origin of snakes
sn: यथावत्प्रार्थित लख्वा वरं तुष्टाऽभवत्तदा। कृतकृत्या तु विनता लब्ध्वा वीर्याधिको सुतौ॥
en: Vinata, having got the boon as she requested, was much pleased and having obtained two greatly powerful sons, she regarded herself gratified.

description: Story of the origin of snakes
sn: कदूश्च लब्ध्वा पुत्राणां सहस्रं तुल्यवर्चसाम्। धार्यो प्रयत्नतो गर्भावित्युक्त्वा स महातपाः॥ ते भार्ये वरसंतुष्टे कश्यपो वनशाविशत्।
en: Kadru also obtained one thousand sons, all of equal spiendour. “Bear the embryos carefully.” So saying the great ascetic Kashyapa went into the forest, leaving his two wives much gratified with his boons.

description: Story of the origin of snakes
sn: सौतिरुवाच कालेन महता कद्दूरण्डानां दशतीर्दश। जनयामास विप्रेन्द्र द्वे चाण्डे विनता तदा॥
en: Sauti said: O best of Brahmanas, after a long time Kadru gave birth to one thousand eggs and Vinata two eggs.

description: Story of the origin of snakes
sn: तयोरण्डानि निदधुः प्रहृष्टाः परिचारिकाः। सोपस्वेदेषु भाण्डेषु पञ्चवर्षशतानि च॥
en: Their maid servants kept them separately in warm vessels and thus five hundred years passed away.

description: Story of the origin of snakes
