sn: ततः पञ्चशते काले कद्रूपुत्रा विनिःसृताः। अण्डाभ्यां विनतायास्तु मिथुनं न व्यदृश्यत॥
en: After five hundred years, the sons of Kadru came out of the eggs, but Vinata's eggs did not produce anything.

description: Story of the origin of snakes
sn: ततः पुत्रार्थिनी देवी वीडिता च तपस्विनी। अण्डं बिभेद विनता तत्र पुत्रमपश्यत॥
en: Thereupon the ascetic lady desiring the sons, Vinata, feeling shame, broke open one of the eggs and saw her offspring,

description: Story of the origin of snakes
sn: अध्यर्धकायसंपन्नमितरेणाप्रकाशता। स पुत्रः क्रोधसंरब्धः शशापैनामिति श्रुतिः॥
en: As an embryo with the upper part developed, but the lower part undeveloped. Thereupon the child grew angry and cursed its mother, saying,

description: Story of the origin of snakes
sn: योऽहमेवं कृतो मातस्त्वया लोभपरीतया। शरीरेणासमग्रेण तस्माद्दासी भविष्यसि॥
en: "O mother, as you have prematurely broken this egg and did not allow my body to be fully developed, being jealous (of Kadru), you will have to serve as the slave (of that very Kadru).

description: Story of the origin of snakes
sn: पञ्चवर्षशतान्यस्या यया विस्पर्धसे सह। एष च त्वां सुतो मातर्दासीत्वान्मोचयिष्यति॥ यद्येनमपि मातस्त्वं मामिवाण्डबिभेदनात्। न करिष्यस्यनङ्गं वा व्यङ्गं वापि तपस्विनम्॥
en: O mother, if you wait with patience five hundred years and do not destroy the other egg, the illustrious child within it will deliver you from your slavery.

description: Story of the origin of snakes
sn: प्रतिपालयितव्यस्ते जन्मकालोऽस्य धीरया। विशिष्टं बलमीप्सन्त्या पञ्चवर्षशतात्परः॥
en: O mother, if you are desirous of having your son strong, take tender care of the egg for five hundred years.

description: Story of the origin of snakes
sn: एवं शप्त्वा ततः पुत्रो विनतामन्तरिक्षगः। अरुणो दृश्यते ब्रह्मन्प्रभातसमये यदा॥ आदित्यरथमध्यास्ते सारथ्यं समकल्पयत्। गरुडोऽपि यथाकालं जज्ञे पन्नगभोजनः॥
en: Thus cursing his mother Vinata, the child rose to the sky. O Brahmana, Aruna (this child) became the charioteer of the Sun and he is to be seen in the hour of the morning. At the stipulated time was also born the snake-eater Garuda.

description: Story of the origin of snakes
sn: स जातमात्रो विनतां परित्यज्य खमाविशत्। आदास्यन्नात्मनो भोज्यमन्नं विहितमस्य यत्। विधात्रा भृगुशार्दूल क्षुधितः पतगेश्वरः॥
en: As soon as he was born, he left his mother and the king of the birds, being hungry, mounted on his wings to seek for the food assigned to him by the great Ordainer.

sn: सूत उवाच एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु भगिन्यौ ते तपोधन। अपश्यतां समायाते उच्चैःश्रवसमन्तिकात्॥
en: Sauti said : O ascetic Rishi, about this time the two sisters one day saw Uchaishrava approaching towards them.

sn: यं तं देवगणाः सर्वे हृष्टरूपमपूजयन्। मथ्यमानेऽमृते जातमश्वरत्नमनुत्तमम्॥
en: (It was the horse) who was worshipped by the celestials, who was the gem among all horses, who rose at the churning of the ocean for the Ambrosia,

sn: अमोघबलमश्वानामुत्तमं जगतां वरम्। श्रीमन्तमजरं दिव्यं सर्वलक्षणपूजितम्॥
en: Who was divine, graceful, ever-young, irresistible, vigorous, who was creator's masterpiece and who was blessed with all the auspicious marks.

sn: शौनक उवाच कथं तदमृतं देवैर्मथितं क्व च शंस मे। यत्र जज्ञे महावीर्यः सोऽश्वराजो महाद्युतिः॥
en: Why and where did the celestial churn the ocean for the Ambrosia, in which did rise, as you say, this best of steeds, so powerful and resplendent? Tell me this.

sn: सौतिरुवाच ज्वलन्तमचलं मेलं तेजोराशिमनुत्तमम्। आक्षिपन्तं प्रभां भानो:स्वशृंगैःकाञ्चनोज्वलैः॥
en: Sauti said: There is a very great mountain, called Meru of blazing and effulgent appearance. The rays of the sun are scattered away when they fall on its golden summit.

sn: कनकाभरणं चित्रं देवगन्धर्वसेवितम्। अप्रमेयमनाधृष्यमधर्मबहुलैर्जनैः॥
en: Decked with gold and exceedingly beautiful, this mountain is frequented by the Devas and Gandharvas; it is immeasurable and unapproachable by men of many sins.

sn: व्यालैरावारितं घोरैर्दिव्यौषधिविदीपितम्। नाकमावृत्य तिष्ठन्तमुच्छ्रयेण महागिरिम्॥
en: It is illuminated with many medicinal plants and fearful beasts of prey roam on its heights.

sn: अगम्यं मनसाऽप्यन्यैर्नदीवृक्षसमन्वितम्। नानापतगसबैश्च नादितं सुमनोहरैः॥
en: It is unapproachable even by mind; it is graced with many trees and stream-lets and resounds with the sweet melody of innumerable birds.

sn: तस्य शृङ्गमुपारुह्य बहुरत्नाचितं शुभम्। अनन्तकल्पमुद्विद्धं सुरा: सर्वे महौजसः।॥
en: It stands high for infinite ages. Once did the celestials sit on its golden summit and held a conclave.

sn: ते मन्त्रयितुमारब्धास्तत्रासीना दिवौकसः। अमृताय समागम्य तपोनियमसंयुताः॥ तत्र नारायणो देवो ब्रह्माणमिदमब्रवीत्। चिन्तयत्सु सुरेष्वेवं मन्त्रयत्सु च सर्वशः॥
en: They, who had practised penances and observed vows, came in quest of the Ambrosia. They consulted together about the possession of the Ambrosia and seeing them in this mood Narayana addressed Brahma saying;

sn: देवैरसुरसंड्बैश्च मथ्यतां कलशोदधिः। भविष्यत्यमृतं तत्र मथ्यमाने महोदधौ॥ सर्वोषधी: समावाप्य सर्वरत्नानि चैव ह। मन्यध्वमुदधिं देवा वेत्स्यध्वममृतं ततः॥
en: "Churn the ocean with both the Devas and the Asuras. By doing so, the Ambrosia and all drugs and gems will be obtained. O celestials, churn the ocean and you will get the Ambrosia.

description: Story of the churning the ocean
sn: सौतिरुवाच ततोऽभ्रशिखराकारैर्गिरिशृंङ्गैरलंकृतम्। मन्दरं पर्वतवरं लताजालसमाकुलम्॥
en: Sauti said: There is a mountain called Mandara with peaks like the clouds. It is the best of mountains and adorned with innumerable creepers.

description: Story of the churning the ocean
sn: नानाविहगसंघुष्टं नानादंष्ट्रिसमाकुलम्। किन्नरैरप्सरोभिश्च देवैरपि च सेवितम्॥
en: On it do many birds pour forth their melody and may beasts of prey roam about; it is frequented by the Kinnaras, Apsaras and। celestials.

description: Story of the churning the ocean
sn: एकादशसहस्राणि योजनानां समुच्छ्रितम्। अधोभूमेः सहस्रेषु तावत्स्वेव प्रतिष्ठितम्॥
en: It rises eleven thousand Yojanas upwards and descends eleven thousand Yojanas downwards.

description: Story of the churning the ocean
sn: तमुद्धर्तुमशक्ता वै सर्वे देवगणास्तदा। विष्णुमासीनमभ्येत्य ब्रह्माणं चेदमब्रुवन्॥
en: The celestials, having failed to uproot it, came to Vishnu and Brahma who were sitting together and said to them.

description: Story of the churning the ocean
sn: भवन्तावत्र कुर्वीतां बुद्धिंः नैःश्रेयसी पराम्। मन्दरोद्धरणे यत्नः क्रियतां च हिताय नः॥
en: "Devise some means you yourselves. Do try to uproot Mandara for our good.”

description: Story of the churning the ocean
sn: सौतिरुवाच तथेति चाब्रवीद्विष्णुर्ब्रह्मणा सह भार्गव अचोदयदमेयात्मा फणीन्द्रं पद्मलोचनः॥
en: O son of Bhrigu, “Let it be so" said both Narayana and Brahma. The lotus-eyed (Vishnu) laid the hard task on the king of the snakes, (Ananta).

description: Story of the churning the ocean
sn: ततोऽनन्तः समुत्थाय ब्रह्मणा परिचोदितः। नारायणेन चाप्युक्तस्तस्मिन्कर्मणि वीर्यवान्॥ अथ पर्वतराजानं तमनन्तो महाबलः। उज्जहार बलाद्ब्रह्मन् सवनं सवनौकसम्॥
en: Being directed by both Brahma and Narayana to do it, the mighty Ananta uprooted the mountain with all the woods and the denizens of woods that were on it.

description: Story of the churning the ocean
sn: ततस्तेन सुराः सार्धं समुद्रमुपतस्थिरे। तमूचुरमृतस्यार्थे निर्मथिष्यामहे जलम्॥
en: Then came all the celestial with Ananta to the shores of the ocean, Addressing it they said, “O Ocean, we have come to churn you for the Ambrosia.

description: Story of the churning the ocean
sn: अपां पतिरथोवाच ममाप्यंशो भवेत्ततः। सोढाऽस्मि विपुलं मर्द मन्दरभ्रमणादिति॥
en: The ocean replied, “Be it so, as I shall get a share of it. I am quite able to bear the great agitation arising out of the churning of my water by Mandara.

description: Story of the churning the ocean
sn: ऊचुश्च कूर्मराजानमकूपारे सुरासुराः। अधिष्ठानं गिरेरस्य भवान्भवितुमर्हति॥
en: The Devas and the Danavas then went to the Tortoise king and said, “You will have to support the mountain on your back.”

description: Story of the churning the ocean
sn: कूर्मेण तु तथेत्युक्त्वा पृष्ठमस्य समर्पितम्। तं शैलं तस्य पृष्ठस्थं वज्रणेन्द्रो न्यपीडयत्॥
en: The Tortoise king having agreed, Indra pressed that mountain on its back by means of his thunderbolt.

description: Story of the churning the ocean
sn: मन्थानं मन्दरं कृत्वा तथा नेत्रं च वासुकिम्। देवा मथितुमारब्धाः समुद्र निधिमम्भसाम्॥ अमृतार्थे पुरा ब्रह्मंस्तथैवासुरदानवाः। एकमन्तमुपाश्लिष्टा नागराज्ञो महासुराः॥ विबुधाः सहिताः सर्वे यत: पुच्छं ततः स्थिताः।
en: The Devas and the Danavas having made Mandara the churning staff and Vasuki the rope. O Brahmana, in days of yore, began to churn the ocean for the Ambrosia. The Asuras held him by the head and the Devas by the tail.

description: Story of the churning the ocean
sn: अनन्तो भगवान्देवो यतो नारायणस्ततः। शिर उत्क्षिप्य नागस्य पुनः पुनरवाक्षिपत्॥
en: And Ananta, who was a manifested form of Narayana, again and again raised and lowered the hood of the Naga.

description: Story of the churning the ocean
sn: वासुकेरथ नागस्य सहसाक्षिप्यतः सुरैः। सधूमाः सार्चिधो वाता निष्पेतुरसकृन्मुखात्॥
en: On account of the great agitation, received at the hands of the celestials, black vapours with flames issued from the mouth of the Naga Vasuki.

description: Story of the churning the ocean
sn: ते धूमसंघा: संभूता मेघसंघा: सविद्युतः। अभ्यवर्षन्सुरगणान् श्रमसंतापकर्शितान्॥
en: From these vapours were created clouds with lightning; and they poured showers on the tired celestials who were thus refreshed.

description: Story of the churning the ocean
sn: तस्माच्च गिरिकूटाग्रात्प्रच्युताः पुष्पवृष्टयः। सुरासुरगणान्सर्वान्समन्तात्समवाकिरन्॥
en: The flowers that fell from the trees on the mountain-sides on the Devas and the Danavas also refreshed them.

description: Story of the churning the ocean
sn: बभूवात्र महानादो महामेघरवोपमः। उदधेर्मथ्यमानस्य मन्दरेण सुरासुरैः॥
en: There rose from Mandara being dragged by the Devas and the Danavas, a terrible roar like the roar of the clouds (at the Universal dissolution).

description: Story of the churning the ocean
sn: तत्र नानाजलचरा विनिष्पिष्टा महाद्रिणा। विलयं समुपाजग्मुः शतशो लवणाम्भसि॥
en: Various aquatic animals were crushed by the great mountain and gave up their lives in the salt sea.

description: Story of the churning the ocean
sn: वारुणानि च भूतानि विविधानि महीधरः। पातालतलवासीनि विलयं समुपानयत्॥
en: Many denizens of the lower region and those of the land of Varuna were killed by the mountain.

description: Story of the churning the ocean
sn: तस्मिश्च भ्राम्यमाणेऽद्रौ संघृष्यन्तः परस्परम्। न्यपतन्पतगोपेताः पर्वताग्रान्महाद्रुमाः॥
en: From the whirling Mandara large trees, being struck at one another, were torn from their roots and fell into the ocean with all the birds (that roosted on their branches).

description: Story of the churning the ocean
sn: तेषां संघर्षजश्चाग्निरर्चिभि: प्रज्वलन्मुहुः। विद्युद्भिरिव नीलाभ्रमावृणोन्मन्दरं गिरिम्॥
en: And great fires were produced from the mutual friction of the trees that frequently blazed up and the Mandara mountain looked like black clouds charged with lightning,

description: Story of the churning the ocean
sn: ददाह कुंजरांस्तत्र सिंहांश्चैव विनिर्गतान्। विगतासूनि सर्वाणि सत्त्वानि विविधानि च॥
en: It burnt the lions, elephants and other various creatures that were on the mountain and killed them (on the spot).

description: Story of the churning the ocean
sn: तमग्निममरश्रेष्ठः प्रदहन्तमितस्ततः। वारिणा मेघजेनेन्द्रः शमयामास सर्वशः।॥
en: Then the best of the celestials, Indra began to extinguish the blazing fire by pouring heavy showers.

description: Story of the churning the ocean
sn: ततो नानाविधास्तत्र सुस्रुवुः सागराम्भसि। महाद्रुमाणां निर्यासा बहवश्चौषधीरसाः॥
en: Then the gums of various great trees and juices from herbs mingled with the waters of the ocean.

description: Story of the churning the ocean
sn: तेषाममृतवीर्याणां रसानां पयसैव च। अमरत्वं सुरा जग्मुः काञ्चनस्य च नि:स्रवात्॥
en: The celestials became immortal by drinking the water mixed with the liquid extract of gold and those gums which had the quality of the Ambrosia.

description: Story of the churning the ocean
sn: ततस्तस्य समुद्रस्य तज्जातमुदकं पयः। रसोत्तमैर्विमिदं च तत: क्षीरादभूद्धृतम्॥
en: The milky water of the churned ocean by degrees produced clarified butter by virtue of those gums and juices.

description: Story of the churning the ocean
sn: ततो ब्रह्माणमासीनं देवा वरदमब्रुवन्। श्रान्ता:स्म सुभृशं ब्रह्मन्नोद्भवत्यमृतं च तत्॥
en: Thereupon the Devas came to the boongranting God who was comfortably seated on his seat and said, “O Brahman, we are spent out but the Ambrosia has not yet arisen."

description: Story of the churning the ocean
sn: विना नारायणं देवं सर्वेऽन्ये देवदानवाः। चिरारब्धमिदं चापि सागरस्यापि मन्थनम्॥
en: Except Narayana, both the Devas and the Danavas have no strength to churn the ocean (any longer).

description: Story of the churning the ocean
sn: ततो नारायणं देवं ब्रह्मा वचनमब्रवीत्। विधत्स्वैषां बलं विष्णो भवानत्र परायणम्॥
en: Then did Brahma say to Narayana, “Kindly give the celestials strength to churn the Ocean again with Mandara mountain, O Vishnu you are our refuge."

description: Story of the churning the ocean
sn: विष्णुरुवाच बलं ददामि सर्वेषां कमैतद्ये समास्थिताः। क्षोभ्यतां कलशः सर्वैर्मन्दरः परिवर्त्यताम्॥
en: Narayana said : I grant all necessary strength for all those who are engaged in this action. Go, insert the mountain and churn the Ocean.

description: Story of the churning the ocean
sn: सूत उवाच नारायणवचः श्रुत्वा बलिनस्ते महोदधेः। तत्पयः सहिता भूयश्चक्रिरे भृशमाकुलम्॥
en: Thus hearing the words of Narayana and being re-equipped with fresh strength the celestial recommenced churning of the waters.

description: Story of the churning the ocean
sn: ततः शतसहस्रांशुर्मथ्यमानात्तु सागरात्। प्रसन्नात्या समुत्पन्नः सोमः शीतांशुरुज्ज्वलः॥
en: Then from churning the ocean rose the amiable and brilliant Moon of thousand rays.

description: Story of the churning the ocean
sn: श्रीरनन्तरमुत्पन्ना घृतात्पाण्डुरवासिनी। सुरादेवी समुत्पन्ना तुरगः पाण्डुरस्तथा॥
en: Then rose from that ghee, the whiteclothed Lakshmi; then Sura Devi (Wine) then the great white steed.

description: Story of the churning the ocean
sn: कौस्तुभस्तु मणिर्दिव्य उत्पन्नो घृतसंभवः। मरीचिविकचः श्रीमान्नारायण उरोगतः॥ पारिजातश्च तत्रैव सुरभिश्च महामुने। जज्ञाते तौ तदा सर्वकामफलप्रदायिनौ॥
en: Then from the ghee rose the celestial gem Kaustubha, the splendid by rays, which adorns the breast of Narayana. Then rose, O Brahmana, Parijata tree and Surabhi, all giver of everything.

description: Story of the churning the ocean
sn: श्री: सुरा चैव सोमश्च तुरगश्च मनोजवः। यतो देवास्ततो जग्मुरादित्यपथमाश्रिताः॥
en: Lakshmi, Wine, Moon, Horse (Uchchaishrava) which is fleet as the mind, all directed by Aditya went to the place where the celestials were.

description: Story of the churning the ocean
sn: धन्वन्तरिस्ततो देवो वपुष्मानुदतिष्ठत। श्वेतं कमण्डलुं बिभ्रदमृतं यत्र तिष्ठति॥
en: Then rose the divine Dhanvantari with a white vessel in his hand and there in that vessel) was the Ambrosia.

description: Story of the churning the ocean
sn: एतदत्यद्भुतं दृष्ट्वा दानवानां समुत्थितः। अमृतार्थे महान्नादो ममेदमिति जल्पताम्॥
en: Seeing this wonderful phenomenon, the Danavas raised a a great uproar for the Ambrosia, saying “It is mine."

description: Story of the churning the ocean
sn: श्वेतैर्दन्तैश्चतुर्भिस्तु महाकायस्ततः परम्। ऐरावतो महानागोऽभवद्वज्रभृता धृतः॥
en: Then rose the great elephant Airavata, with four white tusks and a huge body and he was seized by the wielder of thunder (Indra).

description: Story of the churning the ocean
sn: अतिनिर्मथनादेव कालकूटस्ततः परः। जगदावृत्य सहसा सधूमोऽग्निरिव ज्वलन्॥
en: Because of the great churning, then appeared deadly poison, which soon covered the whole earth and blazed up like a fire with fumes.

description: Story of the churning the ocean
sn: त्रैलोक्यं मोहितं यस्य गन्धमाघ्राय तद्विषम्। प्राग्रसल्लोकरक्षार्थं ब्रह्मणो वचनाच्छिवः॥
en: The three worlds were stupified by its terrible smell; and then Shiva, asked by Brahma, swallowed it to save the creation.

description: Story of the churning the ocean
sn: दधार भगवान्कण्ठे मन्त्रमूर्तिर्महेश्वरः। तदा प्रभृति देवस्तु नीलकण्ठ इति श्रुतिः॥
en: The great Deity Maheshvara of Mantraform held it in his throat and it is said that from the very day he was called Nilkantha (bluethroated).

description: Story of the churning the ocean
sn: एतत्तदद्भुतं दृष्ट्वा निराशा दानवाः स्थिताः। अमृतार्थे च लक्ष्यर्थे महान्तं वैरमाश्रिताः॥
en: Seeing all those wonderful phenomena, the Danavas were filled with despair. They raised up great hostilities with the celestials for the possession of Lakshmi and Ambrosia.

description: Story of the churning the ocean
sn: ततो नारायणो मायां मोहिनी समुपाश्रितः। स्त्रीरूपमद्भुतं कृत्वा दानवानभिसंश्रितः॥
en: Thereupon Narayana assumed a form of a ravishing beauty by the aid of Maya and he began a flirtation with the Danavas in the form of a female.

description: Story of the churning the ocean
sn: ततस्तदमृतं तस्यै ददुस्ते मूढचेतसः। स्त्रियै दानवदैतेयाः सर्वे तद्गतमानसाः॥
en: The foolish Danavas and Daityas becoming fully, enamoured of her, placed the Ambrosia in her hands.

sn: सौतिरुवाच अथावरणमुग्यानि नानाप्रहरणानि च। प्रगृह्याभ्यद्रवन्देवान्सहिता दैत्यदानवाः॥
en: Sauti said : Then the Daityas and Danavas, in best armours and with various weapons, pursued the celestials.

sn: ततस्तदमृतं देवो विष्णुरादाय वीर्यवान्। जहार दानवेन्द्रेभ्यो नरेण सहितः प्रभुः॥
en: In the meantime the greatly powerful Lord Vishnu, accompanied with Nara, took away the Ambrosia from the mighty Danavas.

sn: ततो देवगणाः सर्वे पपुस्तदमृतं तदा। विष्णोः सकाशात्संप्राप्य संभ्रमे तुमुले सति॥
en: Thereupon all the celestials, in that great struggle, drank the Ambrosia receiving it from Vishnu.

sn: ततः पिबत्सु तत्कालं देवेष्वमृतमीप्सितम्। राहुविबुधरूपेण दानवः प्रापिबत्तदा॥
en: When the celestials were drinking the much longed-for Ambrosia, a Danava, named Rahu, drank it in the guise of a celestial.

sn: तस्य कण्ठमनुप्राप्ते दानवस्यामृते तदा। आख्यातं चन्द्रसूर्याभ्यां सुराणां हितकाम्यया॥
en: When the Ambrosia has only reached his throat, Chandra and Surya (recognised him and) informed the celestials of what had happened.

sn: ततो भगवता तस्य शिरश्छिन्नमलंकृतम्। चक्रायुधेन चक्रेण पिबतोऽमृतमोजसा॥
en: Narayana immediately with his discus cut off the well-adorned head of the Danava who was drinking the Ambrosia.

sn: तच्छैलशृङ्गप्रतिमं दानवस्य शिरो महत्। चक्रच्छिन्नं खमुत्पत्य ननादातिभयंकरम्॥
en: The huge head of the Danava cut off by the discus, appeared like a mountain peak and it rose to the sky and uttered terrible cries.

sn: तत्कबन्धं पपातास्य विस्फुरद्धरणीतले। सपर्वतवनद्वीपां दैत्यस्याकम्पयन्महीम्॥
en: The headless body of the Daitya fell on the earth, shaking it with all her mountains, forests and islands.

sn: ततो वैरविनिर्बन्धः कृतो राहुमुखेन वै। शाश्वतश्चन्द्रसूर्याभ्यां ग्रसत्यद्यापि चैव तौ॥
en: From that day a great enmity was created between the head of Rahu and Chandra and Surya. To this day it swallows Chandra and Surya (causing eclipses.)

sn: विहाय भगवांश्चापि स्त्रीरूपमतुलं हरिः। नानाप्रहरणैर्भीमैर्दानवान्समकम्पयत्॥
en: Then Hari, quitting his matchless female form, made the Danavas tremble by hurling at them various weapons.

sn: ततः प्रवृत्तः संग्राम: समीपे लवणाम्भसः। सुराणामसुराणां च सर्वघोरतरो महान्॥
en: Thus began the terrible battle between the Devas and Danavas on the shores of the salt sea.

sn: प्रासाश्च विपुलास्तीक्ष्णा न्यपतन्त सहस्रशः। तोमराश्चसुतीक्ष्णाग्राः शस्त्राणि विविधानि च॥
en: Thousands of sharp javelins and lances and various other weapons were hurled on all sides.

sn: ततोऽसुराश्चक्रभिन्ना वमन्तो रुधिरं बहु। असिशक्तिगदारुग्णा निपेतुर्धरणीतले॥
en: Cut by the discus and wounded by swords, darts and maces, the Asuras vomited blood and lay prostrate on earth.

sn: छिन्नानि पट्टिशैश्चैव शिरांसि युधि दारुणैः। तप्तकाञ्चनमालीनि निपेतुरनिशं तदा॥
en: The heads, adorned with bright goldchains, cut off by the discus, fell continually in the fearful battle.

sn: रुधिरेणानुलिप्ताङ्गा निहताश्च महासुराः। अद्रीणामिव कूटानि धातुरक्तानि शेरते॥
en: The great Asuras, covered with blood, lay dead everywhere and they looked like red dyed mountain peaks.

sn: हाहाकारः समभवत्तत्र तत्र सहस्रशः। अन्योऽन्यं छिन्दतां शस्त्रैरादित्ये लोहितायति॥
en: When the sun grew red, the piteous cries of distress issued from everywhere and from the dying Asuras.

sn: परिघेरायसैस्तीक्ष्णैः संनिकर्षे च मुष्टिभिः। निघ्नतां समरेऽन्योऽन्यं शब्दो दिवमिवास्पृशत्॥
en: The roars, of the warriors that cut one another down by missiles when at a distance and by blows of their fists when at close quarters, rose to the sky.

sn: छिन्द्धि भिन्द्धि प्रधाव त्वं पातयाभिसरेति च। व्यश्रूयन्त महाघोराः शब्दास्तत्र समन्ततः॥
en: "Cut down,” “pierce them”, “pursue”, “fell them down", "advance” these fearful war-cries were heard everywhere.

sn: एवं सुतुमुले युद्धे वर्तमाने महाभये। नरनारायणौ देवौ समाजग्मतुराहवम्॥
en: When this fearful battle was raging, the Devas Nara and Narayana entered the field.

sn: तत्र दिव्यं धनुर्दृष्ट्वा नरस्य भगवानपि। चिन्तयामास तच्चक्रं विष्णुर्दानवसूदनम्।॥
en: Seeing the celestial bow in the hand of Nara, Narayana thought of his Danava destroying discus.

sn: ततोऽम्बराच्चिन्तितमात्रमागतं महाप्रभं चक्रममित्रतापनम्। विभावसोस्तुल्यमकुण्ठमण्डलं सुदर्शनं संयति भीमदर्शनम्॥
en: As soon as it was thought of the discus Sudarshana, the destroyer of enemies, effulgent as Agni and dreadful in battle, came down from the sky.

sn: तदागतं ज्वलितहुताशनप्रभं भयंकरं करिकरबाहुरच्युतः। मुमोच वै प्रबलवदुगवेगवान्। महाप्रभं परनगरावदारणम्॥
en: When it came, Achyuta, of fearful energy (Narayana) as bright as the blazing fire, with arms like the trunk of an elephant, hurled with great force that weapon, as bright as the blazing fire, dreadful, of extraordinary lustre, capable of destroying hostile towns.

sn: तदन्तकज्वलनसमानवर्चसं पुनः पुनर्व्यपतत वेगवत्तदा। विदारयद्दितिदनुजान्सहस्रशः करेरितं पुरुषवरेण संयुगे॥
en: That discus, blazing like the fire at the great dissolution of the universe being hurled by the hand of Narayana, continually falling everywhere, destroyed the Daityas and the Danavas by thousands.

sn: दहत्क्वचिज्ज्वलन इवावलेलिहत् प्रसह्य तानसुरगणान्यकृन्तत। प्रवेरितं वियति मुहुः क्षितौ तथा पपौ रणे रुधिरमथो पिशाचवत्॥
en: Sometimes it blazed like fire and consumed them all; sometimes it struck them down like a goblin; sometimes it drank the blood of the slain Danavas as it travelled through earth and sky.

sn: तथाऽसुरा गिरिभिरदीनचेतसो मुहुर्मुहुः सरगणमादयस्तदा। महाबला विगलितमेघवर्चसः सहस्रशो गगनमभिप्रपद्य ह॥
en: The greatly powerful and bold Danavas, looking like the rainless clouds, rose to the sky and continually hurled down thousands of mountains, on the celestials, thus harassing them (with terrible vengeance).

sn: अथाम्बराद्भयजननाः प्रपेदिरे सपादपा बहुविधमेघरूपिणः। महाद्रयः परिगलिताग्रसानवः परस्परं द्रुतमभिहत्य सस्वनाः॥
en: And those fearful mountains, with their forests and flat tops, like masses of clouds, fell from the sky, collided with one another and produced a tremendous roar.

sn: ततो मही प्रविचलिता सकानना महाद्रिपाताभिहता समन्ततः। परस्परं भृशमभिवर्जतां मुहू रणाजिरे भृशमभिसंप्रवर्तिते॥
en: And when thousands of warriors continually shouted on the field of battle and mountains, with forests thereon, fell all around, the earth with her forests began to tremble.

sn: नरस्ततो वरकनकाग्रभूषणैमहेषुभिर्गगनपथं समावृणोत्। विदारयन्गिरिशिखराणि पत्रिभिः महाभयेऽसुरगणविग्रहे तदा॥
en: Then the divine Nara, appearing in the fearful battle of the Asuras and Ganas and reducing to dust those mountains by means of his gold-headed arrows, covered the heavens with dust.

sn: ततः महीं लवणजलं च सागरं महासुराः प्रविविशुरर्दिताः सुरैः। वियद्गतं ज्वलितहुताशनप्रभं सुदर्शनं परिकुपितं निशम्य ते॥
en: Then the mighty Danavas, having been overpowered by the celestials and having seen the fearful discus roving over the fields of heaven like a blazing fire, entered into the bowels of the earth; and some of them plunged into the salt-sea.

sn: ततः सुरैविजयमवाप्य मन्दरः स्वमेव देशं गमितः सुपूजितः। विनाद्य खं दिवमपि चैव सर्वशः ततो गताः सलिलधरा यथागतम्॥
en: The celestials, having gained the victory, placed with due respect Mandara on its own base; and the clouds, making the heaven resound with their shouts, went to their own abodes.

sn: ततोऽमृतं सुनिहितमेव चक्रिरे सुराः परां मुदमभिगम्य पुष्कलाम्। ददौ च तं निधिममृतस्य रक्षितुं किरीटिने बलभिदथामरैः सह॥
en: The celestial returning to heaven, were greatly rejoiced and kept the Ambrosia in great care. Indra and other celestial made over the vessel containing Ambrosia to Nara to keep it with all care.

sn: सौतिरुवाच एतत्ते कथितं सर्वममृतं मथितं तथा। यत्र सोऽश्वः समुत्पन्नः श्रीमानतुलविक्रमः॥
en: Sauti said : Thus have I narrated to you how the Ambrosia was churned out of the Ocean, in which the beautiful and powerful horse (Uchchaishrava) was produced.

sn: यं निशम्य तदा कदूर्विनतामिदमब्रवीत्। उच्चैःश्रवा हि किं वर्णो भद्रे प्रब्रूहि मा चिरम्॥
en: Beholding this horse Kadru asked Vinata, saying, “Tell me, sister, without delay, what is the colour of Uchchaishrava?”

sn: विनतोवाच श्वेत एवाश्वराजोऽयं किं वा त्वं मन्यसे शुभे। ब्रूहि वर्णं त्वमप्यस्य ततोऽत्र विपणावहे॥
en: Vinata said: This king of the horses is of white colour. What colour do you think, sister? Say what is its colour; let us lay a wager on it.

sn: कदूरुवाच कृष्णवालमहं मन्ये हयमेनं शुचिस्मिते। एहि सार्धं मया दीव्य दासीभावाय भामिनि॥
en: Kadru said : O sweet lady of smiles, I think the horse is black in its tail. Let us lay this wager that she, whose words will be untrue, will become the slave of the other.

sn: सौतिरुवाच एवं ते समयं कृत्वा दासीभावाय वै मिथः। जग्मतुः स्वगृहानेव श्वो द्रक्ष्याव इति स्म ह॥
en: Sauti said: Thus wagering that one will be the slave of the other, they went home, saying "We shall see the horse tomorrow."

sn: ततः पुत्रसहस्रं तु कर्जिा चिकीर्षती। आज्ञापयामास तदा वाला भूत्वाचनप्रभाः॥
en: Wishing to play a deception, Kadru ordered her thousand sons to be black hair;

sn: आविशध्वं हयं क्षिप्रं दासी न स्यामहं यथा। नावपद्यन्त ये वाक्यं ताशशाप भुजंगमान्॥
en: And speedily cover the horse's tail so that she might not become a slave. But on their refusal to do her bidding. She cursed the snakes, saying,

sn: सर्पसत्रे वर्तमाने पावको वः प्रधक्ष्यति। जनमेजयस्य राजर्षेः पाण्डवेयस्य धीमतः॥
en: "In the Snake-sacrifice of the royal sage, wise Janamejaya of the Pandava race Agni will consume you all.

sn: शापमेनं तु शुश्राव स्वयमेव पितामहः। अतिक्रूरं समुत्सृष्टं कवा दैवादतीव हि॥
en: The Grandsire (Brahma) himself heard this exceedingly cruel curse, denounced by Kadru, impelled by Fate.

sn: सार्धं देवगणैः सर्वैर्वाचं तामन्वमोदत। बहुत्वं प्रेक्ष्य सर्पाणां प्रजानां हितकाम्यया॥
en: And he (Brahma), out of kindness for creatures and seeing that the snakes had enormously multiplied, approved of this curse with all the deities.

sn: तिग्मवीर्यविषा होते दन्दशूका महाबलाः। तेषां तीक्ष्णविषत्वाद्धि प्रजानां च हिताय च॥ युक्तं मात्रा कृतं तेषां परपीडोपसर्पिणाम्। अन्येषामपि सत्त्वानां नित्यं दोषपरास्तु ये॥
en: "Considering their virulent poison, excessive strength, great prowess, biting propensity, their mother's curse had been very proper for the good of all creatures.

sn: तेषां प्राणान्तिकी दण्डो दैवेन विनिपात्यते। एवं संभाष्य देवस्तु पूज्य कदूं च तां तदा॥
en: “Fate always inflicts death on those who seek the death of others.” Talking thus, the celestials much praised Kadru.

sn: आहूय कश्यपं देव इदं वचनमब्रवीत्। यदेते दन्दशूकाश्च सर्पा जातस्त्वयानघ॥ विषोल्बणा महाभोगा मात्रा शप्ताः परंतप। तत्र मन्युस्त्वया तात न कर्तव्यः कथंचन॥
en: Then calling Kashyapa, the Deity said. “O sinless one, O powerful one, the snakes of virulent poison, of huge bodies and of biting propensity whom you have begotten have been cursed by their mother. O child, you should not be angry with her.

sn: दृष्टं पुरातनं ह्येतद्यज्ञे सर्पविनाशनम्। इत्युक्त्वा सृष्टिकृदेवस्तं प्रसाद्य प्रजापतिम्। प्रादाद्विषहरी विद्यां कश्यपाय महात्मने॥
en: The destruction of the snakes in the sacrifice (of Janamejaya) has been told in the Purana.” Saying this, the Divine creator of the Universe propitiated Kashyapa and bestowed on the knowledge of neutralising poison. that great man

sn: सौतिरुवाच ततो रजन्या व्युष्टायां प्रभातेऽभ्युदिते रवौ। कदूश्च विनताचैव भगिन्यौ तै तपोधन॥
en: Sauti said: O Rishi, when the night was gone and the sun rose in the morning, the sisters, Kadru and Vinata.

sn: अमषिते सुसंरब्धे दास्ये कृतपणे तदा। जग्मतुस्तुरगं द्रष्टुमुच्चैःश्रवसमन्तिकात्॥
en: Having laid an wager of slavery and burning with jealously, went to see the horse Uchchaishrava.

sn: ददृशातेऽथ ते तत्र समुद्र निधिमम्भसाम्। महान्तमुदकागाधं क्षोभ्यमाणं महास्वनम्॥
en: On their way they saw the great ocean, vast and deep, agitated by wind, making a tremendous roar.

sn: तिमिङ्गिलझषाकीर्णं मकरैरावृतं तथा। सत्त्वैश्च बहुसाहर्नानारूपैः समावृतम्॥
en: It was full of whales, fishes large enough to swallow whales, Makaras, tortoises and creatures of various forms by thousands.

sn: भीषणैर्विकृतैरन्यैोरैजलचरैस्तथा। उग्रैर्नित्यमनाधृष्यं कूर्मग्राहसमाकुलम्॥
en: It was inaccessible by any creatures on account of the presence of terrible, monstershaped, dark and fierce aquatic animals. It was full of crocodiles and tortoises.

sn: आकरं सर्वरत्नानामालयं वरुणस्य च। नागानामालयं रम्यमुत्तमं सरितां पतिम्॥
en: It abounded with all kinds of gems; it was the home of Varuna, the beautiful and excellent abode of the Nagas; it was the lord of all rivers.

sn: पातालज्वलनावासमसुराणां च बान्धवम्। भयंकरं च सत्त्वानां पयसां निधिमर्णवम्॥
en: It was the abode of subterranean fire, the friend of the Asuras, the terror of all creatures, the great reservoir of waters, having no deterioration.

sn: शुभं दिव्यममानाममृतस्याकरं परम्। अप्रमेयमचिन्त्यं च सुपुण्यजलमद्भुतम्॥
en: It was holy, it was beneficial to the celestials, it was the great mine of Ambrosia, it was infinite, inconceivable, sacred and highly wonderful.

sn: घोरं जलचरारावरौद्रं भैरवनि:स्वनम्। गंभीरावर्तकलिलं सर्वभूतभयंकरम्॥
en: It was fearful with the terrible roars of acquatic creatures, tremendously-roaring and full of deep whirlpools. It was an object of terror to all creatures.

sn: वेलादोलानिलचलं क्षोभोद्वेगसमुच्छ्रितम्। वीचीहस्तैः प्रचलितैर्नृत्यन्तमिव सर्वतः॥
en: Moved by winds, heaving high with agitation and disturbance, it seemed to dance everywhere with uplifted hands represented by its waves.

sn: चन्द्रवृद्धिक्षयवशादुद्वृत्तोर्मिसमाकुलम्। पाञ्चजन्यस्य जननं रत्नाकरमनुत्तमम्॥
en: It was full of heaving billows, caused by the changes of the moon, it was the parent of (the great conch of Krishna) Panchajanya, it was the great mine of gems.

sn: गां विन्दता भगवता गोविन्देनामितौजसा। वराहरूपिणा चान्तर्विक्षोभितजलाविलम्॥
en: It was in days of yore disturbed by the greatly powerful Lord Govinda (Vishnu) when he assumed the form, of a boar for raising the earth.

sn: ब्रह्मर्षिणा व्रतवता वर्षाणां शतमत्रिणा। अनासादितगाधं च पातालतलमव्ययम्॥
en: The Rishi Atri of great austerity could not fathom its bottom, lower than the nether regions, though he tried to do it for one hundred years.

sn: अध्यात्मयोगनिद्रां च पद्मनाभस्य सेवतः। युगादिकालशयनं विष्णोरमिततेजसः॥
en: It became the bed of lotus-navelled Vishnu when at the end of every Yuga the immeasurably powerful Deity fell asleep in spiritual meditation.

sn: वज्रपातनसंत्रस्तमैनाकस्याभयप्रदम्। डिम्बाहवादितानां च असुराणां परायणम्॥
en: It was the asylum in which (the hill) Mainaka took under the fear of the falling thunderbolt. It was the retreat of the Asuras, overcome (by the celestials) in the fearful battle.

sn: वडवामुखदीप्ताग्नेस्तोयहव्यप्रदं शिवम्। अगाधपारं विस्तीर्णमप्रमेयं सरित्यतिम्॥
en: It was the ghee, in the shape of its waters, in the (sacrificial) fire that issued forth from the mouth of Vadava. It was without limits, fathomless, vast, immeasurable and the lord of rivers.

sn: महानदीभिर्बह्वीभिःस्पर्धयेव सहस्रशः अभिसार्यमाणमनिशं ददृशाते महार्णवम्। आपूर्यमाणमत्यर्थं नृत्यमानमिवोर्मिभिः॥
en: They saw that thousands of great rivers were rushing into it in great pride like rivals of its love. They saw that it was full, always dancing in its waves.

sn: गंभीरं तिमिमकरोग्रसंकुलं तं। गर्जन्त जलचररावरौद्रनादैः। विस्तीर्णं ददृशतुरम्बरप्रकाशं तेऽगाधं निधिमुरुमम्भसामनन्तम्॥
en: They saw that it was deep and resounded with the terrible uproar of Makaras Timis and other aquatic creatures; they saw it was vast, unlimited as space, unfathomable, infinite and the great reservoir of waters.

sn: सौतिरुवाच नागाश्च संविदं कृत्वा कर्तव्यमिति तद्वचः। निःस्नेहा वै दहेन्माता असंप्राप्तमनोरथा॥
en: Sauti said: The Nagas, after a consultation came to the conclusion that they should obey their mother's command, for if her wish was not gratified, she, abandoning her love towards them, would burn them all.

sn: प्रसन्ना मोक्षयेदस्मांस्तस्माच्छापाच्च भामिनी। कृष्णं पुच्छं करिष्यामस्तुरगस्य न संशयः॥
en: If she was gratified, she might free them from the curse. They said:-“We shall undoubtedly make the horse's hair black.”

sn: तथा हि गत्वा ते तस्य पुच्छे वाला इति स्मृताः। एतस्मिन्नन्तरे ते तु सपत्न्यौ पणिते तदा॥
en: It is said that they then went and became hairs on the tail of the horse (Uchchaishrava). In the mean time the two co-wives laid the wager.

sn: ततस्ते पणितं कृत्वा भगिन्यौ द्विजसत्तम। जग्मतुः परया प्रीत्या परं पारं महोदधेः॥
en: And having laid the wager, o best of Brahmanas, the two sisters proceeded in great delight to the other side of the great ocean.

sn: कदूश्च विनताचैव दाक्षायण्यौ विहायसा। आलोकयन्त्यावक्षोभ्यं समुद्र निधिमम्भसाम्॥
en: Kadru and Vinata, the daughters of Daksha, saw on their way the ocean, incapable of being easily disturbed.

sn: वायुनाऽतीव सहसा क्षोभ्यमाणं महास्वनम्। तिमिगिलसमाकीर्णं मकरैरावृतं तथा॥
en: (But) greatly agitated all on a sudden by the wind. (It was) terribly roaring, full of Timingilas and Makaras.

sn: संयुतं बहुसाहस्रैः सत्त्वैर्नानाविधैरपि। घोरै?रमनाधृष्यं गंभीरमतिभैरवम्॥
en: And many thousands of other creatures of various forms; it was frightful with the presence of horrible monsters; it was inaccessible, fearful and terrible,

sn: आकरं सर्वरत्नानामालयं वरुणस्य च। नागानामालयं चापि सुरम्यं सरितां पतिम्॥
en: The mine of all gems, the home of Varuna, the beautiful habitation of the Nagas, the Lord of rivers,

sn: पातालज्वलनावासमसुराणां तथालयम्। भयंकराणां सत्त्वानां पयसो निधिमव्ययम्॥
en: The abode of subterranean fire, the home of the Asuras and many fearful creatures, the reservoir of waters.

sn: शुभं दिव्यममानाममृतस्याकरं परम्। अप्रमेयमचिन्त्यं च सुपुण्यजलसंमितम्॥
en: It was holy, the great receptacle of the Arabrosia of the celestials, immeasurable and inconceivable, full of holy waters.

sn: महानदीभिर्बह्वीभिस्तत्र तत्र सहस्रशः। आपूर्यमाणमत्यर्थं नृत्यन्तमिव चोर्मिभिः॥
en: Filled with many thousands of and thus disturbed, dancing with its waves.

sn: इत्येवं तरलतरोर्मिसंकुलं ते गंभीरं विकसितमम्बरप्रकाशं। पातालज्वलनशिखाविदीपिताङ्गं गर्जन्तं द्रुतमभिजग्मतुस्ततस्ते॥
en: Such was the ocean full of liquid waves, (it was) vast as the sky, deep, lighted with the flames of subterranean fire, roaring; they (the sisters) passed quickly over it. great rivers

sn: सौतिरुवाच तं समुद्रमतिक्रम्य कर्विनतया सह। न्यपतत्तुरगाभ्याशे न चिरादिव शीघ्रगा॥
en: Sauti said: Kadru, of swift speed, accompanied by Vinata, having crossed the ocean, very soon came to the horse.

sn: ततस्ते तं हयश्रेष्ठं ददृशाते महाजवम्। शशाङ्ककिरणप्रख्यं कालवालमुभे तदा।॥
en: They then saw that swift and the best of horses, as white as the rays of the moon but with black hairs (in the tail).

sn: निशम्य च बहून्वालान् कृष्णान्पुच्छसमाश्रितान्। विषण्णरूपां विनतां कदूर्दास्ये न्ययोजयत्॥
en: Seeing many black hairs in the tail, Kadru put much dejected Vinata into slavery.

sn: ततः सा विनता तस्मिन्पणितेन पराजिता। अभवदुःखसंतप्ता दासीभावं समास्थिता॥
en: Thus having lost wager, Vinata became a slave and became exceedingly sad.

sn: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे चापि गरुडः काल आगते। विना मात्रा महातेजा विदार्याण्डमजायत॥
en: Meanwhile, when the time came, Garuda of great splendour came out bursting the egg without the help of his mother.

sn: महासत्त्वबलोपेतः सर्वा विद्योतयन्दिशः। कामरूपः कामगमः कामवीर्यो विहंगमः॥
en: He enkindled all the points of the universe, he was the bird endowed with strength, capable of assuming any form at will, of going every where at will and calling any amount of energy to action at will.

sn: अग्निराशिरिवोद्भासन्समिद्धोऽतिभयंकरः। विद्युदविस्पष्टपिङ्गाक्षो युगान्ताग्निसमप्रभः॥
en: He looked terrible like a heap of blazing fire, of lustre equal to that of the fire at the end of Yuga. His eyes were bright like the flash of lightning.

sn: प्रवृद्धः सहसा पक्षी महाकायो नभोगतः। घोरो घोरस्वनो रौद्रो वह्निरौर्व इवापरः॥
en: As soon as he was born, the huge bird, increasing his body, rose to the sky, fearfully roaring like a second ocean-fire.

sn: तं दृष्ट्वा शरणं जग्मुर्देवाः सर्वे विभावसुम्। प्रणिपत्याब्रुवंश्चैनमासीनं विश्वरूपिणम्॥
en: All the celestials seeing him, sought the protection of Vibhavasu (Agni). They bowed down to that Deity of Universal form who was seated on his seat and addressed him thus:

sn: अग्ने मा त्वं प्रवर्धिष्ठाः कच्चिन्नो न दिधक्षसि। असौ हि राशिः सुमहान्समिद्धस्तव सर्पति॥
en: “O Agni, do not extend your body. Have you resolved to consume us? Lo, the huge heap of your flames is spreading wide!"

sn: अग्निरुवाच नैतदेवं यथा यूयं मन्यध्वमसुरार्दनाः। गरुडो बलवानेष मम तुल्यश्च तेजसा॥
en: Agni said : O persecutors of the Asuras, it is not as you think. It is mighty Garuda, equal to me in splendour.

sn: जातः परमतेजस्वी विनतानन्दवर्धनः। तेजोराशिमिमं दृष्ट्वा युष्मान्मोहः समाविशत्॥
en: He is born endued with great energy to promote the joy of Vinata. Seeing this heap of effulgence, this delusion has come (in you).

sn: नागक्षयकरश्चैव काश्यपेयो महाबलः। देवानां च हिते युक्तस्त्वहितौ दैत्यरक्षसाम्॥
en: He is the mighty son of Kashyapa, he is the destroyer of the Nagas, the enemy of the Daityas and Rakshasas, he is ever engaged to do good to the celestials.

sn: न भीः कार्या कथं चात्र पश्यध्वं सहिता मम॥
en: Do not be afraid in the least. Come with me and see him.

sn: एवमुक्तास्तदा गत्वा गरुडं वाग्भिरस्तुवन्। ते दूरादभ्युपेत्यैनं देवाः सर्षिगणास्तदा॥
en: Sauti said: Thus asked, the celestial went with the Rishis towards Garuda and from a distance addressed him thus.

sn: देवा ऊचुः त्वमृषिस्त्वं महाभागस्त्वं देवः पतगेश्वरः। त्वं प्रभुस्तपनः सूर्यः परमेष्ठी प्रजापतिः॥
en: The Celestials said: O Lord of birds, you are a Rishi, you are the partaker of the largest portion of the sacrifice, you are Deity. You are Lord of the birds, you are the sun of hot rays, you are Parameshti, you are Prajapati.

sn: त्वमिन्द्रस्त्वं हयमुखस्त्वं शर्वस्त्वं जगत्पतिः। त्वं मुखं पद्मजो विप्रस्त्वमग्निः पवनस्तथा।॥
en: You are Indra, you are steed-necked Vishnu, you are Shiva, You are the Lord of the universe, you are the principal, you are Brahma and Brahmanas, you are Agni, you are the wind.

sn: त्वं हि धाता विधाता च त्वं विष्णुः सुरसत्तमः। त्वं महानभिभूः शश्वदमृतं त्वं महद्यशः॥ त्वं प्रभास्त्वमभिप्रेतं त्वं नस्त्राणमनुत्तमम्।
en: You are Dhata and Vidhata, you are Vishnu the best of celestials, you are the great Truth, you are fearless, you are ever unchanged, you are great glory. You are the energy of the sun, you are the intellectual function, you are our great protector.

sn: बलोमिमान्साधुरदीनसत्त्वः समृद्धिमान्दुर्विषहस्त्वमेव॥
en: You are the ocean of strength, you are purity, you are beyond the attributes and darkness, you are the possessor of all wealth, you are unconquerable.

sn: त्वत्त: सृतं सर्वमहीनकीर्ते ह्यनागतं चोपगतं च सर्वम्। त्वमुत्तमः सर्वमिदं चराचरं गभस्तिभिर्भानुरिवावभाससे॥
en: From you have emanated all things, you are the doer of excellent acts. You are all that has not been and all that has been. You are pure knowledge, you display as sun by his rays, this animate and inanimate universe.

sn: समाक्षिपन्भानुमतः प्रभां मुहुः त्वमन्तकः सर्वमिदं ध्रुवाध्रुवम्। दिवाकरः परिकुपितो यथा दहेत् प्रजास्तथा दहसि हुताशनप्रभः॥
en: Darkening the splendour of the sun, you become the destroyer of all; you are all that is perishable and all that is imperishable. O Deity, with the splendour of fire you consume all as sun in his anger burns all creatures.

sn: भयंकरः प्रलय इवाग्निरुत्थितः विनाशयन्युगपरिवर्तनान्तकृत्॥ खगेश्वरं शरणमुपागता वयं महौजसं ज्वलनसमानवर्चसम्।
en: You rise like the fire which, at the changes of the Yuga and at the dissolution of the creation, destroys everything. O king of birds, having come to you, we seek your protection, you move in the sky, your energy is great, you are as mighty as the fire.

sn: तडित्प्रभं वितिमिरमभ्रगोचरं महाबलं गरुडमुपेत्य खेचरम्। परावरं वरदमजय्यविक्रम तवौजसा सर्वमिदं प्रतापितम्॥
en: Your brightness is like the lightning. You are the dispeller of darkness, you reach the very clouds, you are mighty bird Garuda. You are both the cause and the effect, you are the dispenser of boons and invincible in prowess.

sn: जगत्प्रभो तप्तसुवर्णवर्चसा त्वं पाहि सर्वांश्च सुरान्महात्मनः। भयान्विता नभसि विमानगामिनो विमानिता विपथगतिं प्रयान्ति ते॥
en: O Lord of the whole universe, by your brilliance like the heated gold, protect the noble celestials, who having been frightened, are flying along the heaven in all directions.

sn: ऋषेः सुतस्त्वमसि दयावतः प्रभो महात्मनः खगवर कश्यपस्य ह। स मा क्रुधः कुरु जगतो दयां परां त्वमीश्वरः प्रशममुपैहि पाहि नः॥
en: O best of birds, you are the son, of the merciful and high-souled Rishi Kashyapa, you are the lord of all, therefore do not be angry with the universe, have mercy for it. You are the Supreme Lord, assuage your anger and save us.

sn: महाशनिस्फुरितसमस्वनेन ते दिशोऽम्बरं त्रिदिवमियं च मेदिनी। चलन्ति नः खगहृद्यानि चानिशं निगृह्यतां वपुरिदमग्निसंनिभम्॥
en: The ten points, the skies, the heavens, the earth and our hearts, O bird, are continuously trembling at your voice, loud as the roar of thunder. Diminish your body which is like the fire.

sn: तव द्युतिं कुपितकृतान्तसंनिभां निशम्य नश्चलति मनोऽव्यवस्थितम्॥
en: Our hearts, losing all equanimity, are trembling at your splendour, resembling that of the angry Yama.

sn: प्रसीद नः पतगपते प्रयाचतां शिवश्च नो भव भगवन्सुखावहः। एवं स्तुतः सुपर्णस्तु देवैः सर्षिगणैस्तदा तेजसः प्रतिसंहारमात्मनः स चकार ह॥
en: O king of birds, we pray to you, be kind towards us. Bestow on us, O Bhagavan, benefit, fortune and happiness. Having been thus adored by all the celestials and Rishis, the bird, of beautiful feathers, diminished his own energy and splendour.

sn: सौतिरुवाच स श्रुत्वाऽथात्मनो देहं सुपर्णः प्रेक्ष्य च स्वयम्। शरीरप्रतिसंहारमात्मनः संप्रचक्रमे॥
en: Sauti said : Having heard (of the hugeness of his body) and seeing it himself, he began to diminish his body.

sn: सुपर्ण उवाच न मे सर्वाणि भूतानि बिभियुर्देहदर्शनात्। भीमरूपात्समुद्विग्नास्तस्मात्तेजस्तु संहरे॥
en: Garuda said: No one need be afraid of seeing my body. As you are also very much frightened at its sight, I shall diminish it.

sn: सौतिरुवाच ततः कामगम: पक्षी कामवीर्यो विहंगमः। अरुणं चात्मनः पृष्ठमारोप्य स पितुर्ग्रहात्॥ मातुरन्तिकमागच्छत्परं तीरं महोदधेः। तत्रारुणश्च निक्षिप्तो दिशं पूर्वां महाद्युतिः॥ सूर्यस्तेजोभिरत्युप्रैर्लोकान्दग्धुमना यदा।
en: Sauti said: Then the bird, capable of going every where at will and of calling all energy at will, placing his brother Aruna on his back, went from his father's house to that of his mother, (which was situated) on the other side of the ocean. He placed in the East Aruna of great splendour when the sun determined to burn the world with its fearful rays.

sn: रुरुरुवाच किमर्थं भगवान्सूर्यो लोकान्दग्धुमनास्तदा। किमस्यापहृतं देवैयेनमं मन्युराविशत्॥
en: Ruru said: What for did the highly noble sun resolve to burn the world? What wrongs were done to him by the celestials, that he grew angry?

sn: प्रमतिरुवाच चन्द्रादित्यैर्यदा राहुराख्यातो ह्यमृतं पिबन्। वैरानुबन्धं कृतवांश्चन्द्रादित्ये तदाऽनघ॥
en: Sauti said: sinless one, from the day on which Rahu was discovered by Surya and Chandra in the act of drinking the Ambrosia, he bore a deadly enmity towards them.

sn: वध्यमाने ग्रहेणाथ आदित्ये मन्युराविशत्। सुरार्थाय समुत्पन्नो रोषो राहोस्तु मां प्रति॥
en: When Rahu began to devour Surya, he became angry and thought. “This enmity of Rahu has risen from my benefiting the celestials,

sn: बबनर्थकरं पापमेकोऽहं समवाप्नुयाम्। सहाय एव कार्येषु च कृच्छ्रेषु दृश्यते॥
en: And I am alone to suffer from this great evil; I do not get any help at my this difficulty.

sn: पश्यन्ति ग्रस्यमानं मां सहन्ते वै दिवौकसः। तस्माल्लोकविनाशार्थं ह्यवतिष्ठे न संशयः॥
en: The inhabitants of the celestial regions (unconcernedly) see me devoured and they quietly brook it. Therefore, I must make an attempt to destroy the worlds. There is no doubt about it.

sn: एवं कृतमति: सूर्यो ह्यस्तमभ्यगमद्गिरिम्। तस्माल्लोकविनाशाय संतापयत भास्करः॥
en: With this resolution Surya went to the western mountains and from that place began to scatter his scorching rays to destroy the worlds.

sn: ततो देवानुपागम्य प्रोचुरेवं महर्षयः। अद्यार्धरात्रसमये सर्वलोकभयावहः॥ उत्पत्स्यते महान्दाहस्त्रैलोक्यस्य विनाशनः।
en: Thereupon the great Rishis, came to the celestials and said; “Today in the middle of the night, a fire, fearful to all creatures, will rise to destroy the universe."

sn: ततो देवाः सर्षिगणा उपगम्य पितामहम्॥ अब्रुवन्किमिवेहाद्य महद्दाहकृतं भयम्।
en: Then the celestials with the Rishis went to the Grandsire (Brahma) and said, "What is this great and fearful heat today?"

sn: न तावद् दृश्यते सूर्यः क्षयोऽयं प्रतिभाति च। उदिते भगवद्भानौ कथमेतद्भविष्यति॥
en: The sun has not as yet risen, still destruction of the world is obvious. What will happen when he rises?

sn: पितामह उवाच एष लोकविनाशाय रविरुद्यन्तुमुद्यतः। दृश्यन्नेव हि लोकान्स भस्मराशीकरिष्यति॥
en: Brahma said: The sun is ready to rise in order to destroy the worlds. As soon as he will rise he will burn everything into ashes.

sn: तस्य प्रतिविधानं च विहितं पूर्वमेव हि॥
en: I have, however, provided the remedy beforehand.

sn: कश्यपस्य सुतो धीमानरुणेत्यभिविश्रुतः। महाकायो महातेजाः स स्थास्यति पुरो रवेः॥ करिष्यति च सारथ्यं तेजश्चास्य हरिष्यति। लोकानां स्वस्ति चैवं स्यादृषीणां च दिवौकसाम्।।
en: The wise son of Kashyapa, known by the name of Aruna, has a huge body. He will sit before the sun as his charioteer and will take energy. This will secure the good of the world, of the Rishis and of the celestials.

sn: प्रमतिरुवाच ततः पितामहाज्ञातः सर्वं चक्रे तदाऽरुणः। उदितश्चैव सविता ह्यरुणेन समावृतः॥
en: Sauti said : away all his Thereupon Aruna, ordered by the Grandsire, did all that he was commanded to do. The sun rose covered by Aruna.

sn: एतत्ते सर्वमाख्यातं यत्सूर्यं मन्युराविशत्। अरुणश्च यथैवास्य सारथ्यमकरोत्प्रभुः। भूय एवापरं प्रश्नं शृणु पूर्वमुदाहृतम्॥
en: I have told you why Surya was in anger and how Aruna was appointed his charioteer. Hear next, the reply to the other question, asked by you a little while ago.

sn: सौतिरुवाच ततः कामगम: पक्षी महावीर्यो महाबलः। मातुरन्तिकमागच्छत्परं पारं महोदधेः॥
en: Sauti said: Then the bird, of great strength and energy, capable of going every where at will, went to his mother on the other side of the great ocean.

sn: यत्र सा विनता तस्मिन्पणितेन पराजिता। अतीव दुःखसंतप्ता दासीभावमुपागता॥
en: There lived Vinata in great affliction after losing the wager and becoming a slave.

sn: ततः कदाचिद्विनतां प्रणतां पुत्रसंनिधौ। काले चाहूय वचनं कदूरिदमभाषत।। नागानामालयं भद्रे सुरम्यं चारुदर्शनम्। समुद्रकुक्षावेकान्ते तत्र मां विनते नय॥
en: Sometime after on a certain day, Kadru called Vinata, who prostrated herself before her and said before her son (Garuda). "O gentle Vinata, take me to the beautiful and delightful abode of the Nagas which is situated in the deep recess of the sea.”

sn: ततः सुपर्णमाता तामवहत्सर्पमातरम्। पन्नगागरुडश्चापि मातुर्वचनचोदितः॥
en: Thereupon the mother of the bird took upon her shoulder the mother of the snakes. Garuda also, requested by his mother, took the snakes on his back.

sn: स सूर्यमभितो याति वैनतेयो विहंगमः। सूर्यरश्मिप्रतप्ताश्च मूर्च्छिताः पन्नगाऽभवन्।॥
en: The son, of Vinata, the bird, began to ascend towards the sun; and the snakes, scorched by the rays of the sun, all fainted away.

sn: तदवस्थान्सुतान्दृष्ट्वा कदूः शक्रमथास्तुवत्। नमस्ते सर्वदेवेश नमस्ते बलसूदन॥
en: Seeing her sons in this plight, Kadru began to praise Indra thus : "I bow to you, O Lord of the celestials, I bow to you, O slayer of Bala.

sn: नमुचिघ्न नमस्तेऽस्तु सहस्राक्ष शचीपते। सर्पाणां सूर्यतप्तानां वारिणा त्वं प्लवो भव॥
en: O slayer of Namuchi, I bow to thee, O god of thousand eyes, O Lord of Sachi, save my sons, oppressed by the rays of the sun by your showers.

sn: त्वमेव परमं त्राणमस्माकममरोत्तम। ईशो ह्यसि पयः स्रष्टुं त्वमनल्पं पुरन्दर॥
en: You are our great protector. O best of gods, O Purandara, you can grant rains in torrents.

sn: त्वमेव मेघस्त्वं वायुस्त्वमग्निर्विद्युतोऽम्बरे। त्वमभ्रगणविक्षेप्ता त्वामेवाहुर्महाधनम्॥
en: You are Vayu, you are the clouds, you are Agni, you are the lightning in the sky, you are the propellers of the clouds and therefore you are called the great clouds.

sn: त्वं वज्रमतुलं घोरं घोषवांस्त्वं बलाहकः। स्रष्टा त्वमेव लोकानां संहर्ता चापराजितः॥
en: You are the incomparable thunder, you are the roaring clouds, you are the creator and the destroyer of the worlds, you are unconquerable.

sn: त्वं ज्योतिः सर्वभूतानां त्वमादित्यो विभावसुः। त्वं महद्भूतमाश्चर्यं त्वं राजा त्वं सुरोत्तमः॥
en: You are the light of all creatures you are Aditya and Vibhavasu, you are the highest knowledge, you are wonderful, you are king, you are the best of the celestials.

sn: त्वं विष्णुस्त्वं सहस्राक्षस्त्वं देवस्त्वं परायणम्। त्वं सर्वमनृतं देवः त्वं सोमः परमार्चितः॥
en: You are Vishnu, you have one thousand eyes, you are a deity, you are the final refuge, you are all Ambrosia, you are the much adored Soma.

sn: त्वं मुहूर्तस्तिथिस्त्वं च त्वं लवस्त्वं पुनः क्षणः। शुक्लस्त्वं बहुलस्त्वं च कला काष्ठा त्रुटिस्तथा। संवत्सरर्तवो मासा रजन्यश्च दिनानि च॥
en: You are moments, you are the Tithis, you are the Lava you are the Kshana, you are the white fortnight, you are Kala, Kashtha, Truti, you are the year, seasons, months, the nights and the days.

sn: त्वमुत्तमा सगिरिवना वसुन्धरा सभास्करं वितिमिरमम्बरं तथा। महोदधिः सतिमितिमिगिलस्तथा महोर्मिमान्बहुमकरो झषाकुलः॥
en: You are the beautiful earth with its mountains and forests, you are the clear sky with the sun that drives away all darkness. You are the great ocean with heaving billows and abounding in Timingilas, Timis, Makaras and various other fishes.

sn: महायशास्त्वमिति सदाऽभिपूज्यसे मनीषिभिर्मुदितमना महर्षिभिः। अभिष्टुतः पिबसि च सोममध्वरे वषट् कृतान्यपि च हवींषि भूतये॥
en: You are of renown, you are always adored by the wise and the great contemplative Rishis, you drink the Soma juice and the clarified butter offered with sacred invocation in the sacrifices.

sn: त्वं विप्रैः सततमिहेज्यसे फलार्थ वेदाङ्गेष्वतुलबलौघ गीयसे च। त्वद्धतोर्यजनपरायणा द्विजेन्द्रा वेदाङ्गान्यभिगमयन्ति सर्वयत्नैः॥
en: You are always worshipped in the sacrifices by the Brahmanas, desirous of receiving fruits. O God of incomparable strength, you are sung in the Vedas. It is for this reason that the learned Brahmanas, engaged in sacrifices, study the Vedangas with all care."

sn: सौतिरुवाच एवं स्तुतस्तदा कव्वा भगवान्हरिवाहनः। नीलजीमूतसंघातैः सर्वमम्बरमावृणोत्॥
en: Sauti said: Having been thus adored by Kadru, the God, having the best horses to ride, covered all the sky with blue clouds.

sn: मेघानाज्ञापयामास वर्षध्वममृतं शुभम्। ते मेघामुमुचुस्तोयं प्रभूतं विधुदुज्ज्वलाः॥
en: He commanded the clouds saying. “Pour down your life-giving and beneficial showers." Those clouds, luminous with lightning, then poured abundant water.

sn: परस्परमिवात्यर्थं गर्जन्तः सततं दिवि। संवर्तितमिवाकाशं जलदैः सुमहाद्भुतैः॥ सृजद्भिरतुलं तोयमजस्रं सुमहारवैः। संप्रनृत्तमिवाकाशं धारोमिभिरनेकशः॥
en: On account of the wonderful and terribly roaring clouds, that incessantly begot water, the sky looked as if the end of the Yuga had come. And in consequence of myriads of waves, caused in the falling torrents, of the deep roars of the clouds, the flashing of lightnings, the violence of the wind and the general agitation, the sky looked, as if it was dancing in madness.

sn: मेघस्तनितनिर्घोषैर्विद्युत्पवनकम्पितैः। तैर्मेधैः सततासारं वर्षद्भिरनिशं तदा॥ नष्टचन्द्रार्ककिरणमम्बरं समपद्यत। नागानामुत्तमो हर्षस्तथा वर्षति वासवे॥
en: The sky thus became dark, the rays of the sun and the moon disappeared on account of the incessant downpour. And upon Indra's causing this downpour, the Nagas became exceedingly delighted.

sn: आपूर्यत मही चापि सलिलेन समन्ततः। रसातलमनुप्राप्तं शीतलं विमलं जलम्॥
en: The world became full of water; the cool and clear water reached even the nether regions.

sn: तदा भूरभवच्छन्ना जलोर्मिभिरनेकशः। रामणीयकमागच्छन्मात्रा सह भुजंगमाः॥
en: When there became countless watery waves, the snakes with their mother reached the island called Ramaniyaka.

sn: सौतिरुवाच संप्रहृष्टात्स्ततो नागा जलधाराप्लुतास्तदा। सुपर्णेनोह्यमानास्ते जग्मुस्तं द्वीपमाशु वै॥
en: Sauti said: The Nagas became exceedingly glad on being wetted by the great shower; and carried by the bird (Garuda) they soon arrived at the island.

sn: तं द्वीपं मकरावासं विहितं विश्वकर्मणा। तत्र ते लवणं घोरं ददृशुः पूर्वमागताः॥
en: That island was assigned by the creator as the abode of Makaras. Coming there they first saw the fearful Lavana.

sn: सुपर्णसहिताः सर्पाः काननं च मनोरमम्। सागराम्बुपरिक्षिप्तं पक्षिसंघनिनादितम्॥
en: They with Garuda saw the charming woods, washed by the waters of the sea and resounding with the music of the birds.

sn: विचित्रफलपुष्पाभिर्वनराजिभिरावृतम्। भवनैरावृतं रम्यैस्तथा पद्माकरैरपि॥
en: There were beautiful trees full of various fruits and flowers, there were also charming mansions and many tanks with lotuses.

sn: प्रसन्नसलिलैश्चापि ह्रदैर्दिव्यैर्विभूषितम्। दिव्यगन्धवहैः पुण्यैर्मारुतैरुपवीजितम्॥
en: It was adorned with many beautiful lakes of pure water; it was refreshed with sweet incense-carrying breezes.

sn: उत्पतद्भिरिवाकाशं वृक्षैर्मलयजैरपि। शोभितं पुष्पवर्षाणि मुञ्चद्भिर्मारुतोद्धतैः॥
en: It was adorned with many trees that only grow on the Malaya hill, as high as the high heavens. It, being shaken by the breeze, dropped showers of flowers.

sn: वायुविक्षिप्तकुसुमैस्तथाऽन्यैरपि पादपैः। किरद्भिरिव तत्रस्थानागान्पुष्पाम्बुवृष्टिभिः॥
en: There were also various other trees whose flowers were scattered about by the breeze. It seemed as if these trees bathed the Nagas with a shower of rain in the shape of their flowers.

sn: मन:संहर्षजं दिव्यं गन्धर्वाप्सरसां प्रियम्। मत्तभ्रमरसंघुष्टं मनोज्ञाकृतिदर्शनम्॥
en: It was charming, beautiful and dear to the Gandharvas and always gave them pleasure. It was full of bees intoxicated with the honey they sucked. The sight of its appearance was exceedingly beautiful.

sn: रमणीयं शिवं पुण्यं सर्वैर्जनमनोहरैः। नानापक्षिरुतं रम्यं कदूपुत्रप्रहर्षणम्॥
en: It was beautiful, beneficial, holy and charming to all. Echoing with the sweet notes of various birds, it much delighted the sons of Kadru.

sn: तत्ते वनं समासाद्य विजह्वः पन्नगास्तदा। अब्रुवंश्च महावीर्यं सुपर्णं पतगेश्वरम्॥
en: Having arrived at that forest, the snakes very much enjoyed themselves and then they commanded the king of the birds, Garuda of great strength.

sn: वहास्मानपरं द्वीपं सुरम्यं विमलोदकम्। त्वं हि देशान्बहूनम्यान्व्रजन्पश्यसि खेचर॥
en: “Take us to some other beautiful islands with pure water. O bird, you must have seen many beautiful countries when coursing through the sky."

sn: स विचिन्त्याब्रवीत्पक्षी मातरं विनतां तदा। किं कारणं मया मातः कर्तव्यं सर्पभाषितम्॥
en: Having reflected for some time he (Garuda) asked his mother. “Why, O mother, am I to do the bidding of these snakes?"

sn: विनतोवाच दासीभूतास्मि दुर्योगात्सपल्याः पतगोत्तम। पणं वितथमास्थाय सस्पधिना कृतम्॥
en: Vinata said: O best of birds, from misfortune, I have become a slave of my husband's second wife. The snakes caused me to lose the wager by deception; and thus have I become a slave.

sn: तस्मिंस्तु कथिते मात्रा कारणे गगनेचरः। उवाच वचनं सस्तेिन दुःखेन दुःखितः॥
en: When his mother told him the reason, the bird in great sorrow said to the snakes.

sn: किमाहत्य विदित्वा वा किं वा कृत्वेह पौरुषम्। दास्याद्वो विप्रमुच्येयं तथ्यं वदत लेलिहाः॥
en: “Tell me, O snakes, by bringing what, or gaining what knowledge or doing what great work, we may be freed from this state of slavery.

sn: सौतिरुवाच श्रुत्वा तमब्रुवन्सर्पा आहरामृतमोजसा। ततो दास्याद्विप्रमोक्षो भविता तव खेचर॥
en: Sauti said: Having heard him the snakes said, “Bring the Ambrosia by force. Then, O bird, you will be freed from slavery."

sn: सौतिरुवाच इत्युक्तो गरुडः सर्पस्ततो मातरमब्रवीत्। गच्छाम्यमृतमाहर्तुं भक्ष्यमिच्छामि वेदितुम्॥
en: Sauti said : Thus told by the snakes, Garuda said to his mother, “I shall go to bring the Ambrosia, but I wish to eat something. Tell me where to get it.”

sn: विनतोवाच समुद्रकुक्षावेकान्ते निषादालयमुत्तमम्। निषादानां सहस्राणि तान्भुक्त्वाऽमृतमानय॥
en: Vinata said: The Nishadas have their homes in a remote place in the midst of the ocean. Eat thousands of Nishadas and bring the Ambrosia.

sn: न च ते ब्राह्मणं हन्तुं कार्या बुद्धिः कथंचन। अवध्यः सर्वभूतानां ब्राह्मणो ह्यनलोपमः॥
en: But let not your heart be ever set on killing a Brahmana. A Brahmana is not to be killed amongst all creatures; he is like the fire.

sn: अग्निरों विषं शस्त्रं विप्रो भवति कोपितः। गुरुर्हि सर्वभूतानां ब्राह्मणः परिकीर्तितः॥ एवमादिभिरूपैस्तु सतां वै ब्राह्मणो मतः।
en: A Brahmana, when angry; becomes like the fire or the sun or the poison or a sharp weapon. A Brahmana is declared to be the preceptor of all creature. For these and other reasons the Brahmana is adored by all.

sn: स ते तात न हन्तव्यः संक्रुद्धेनापि सर्वथा॥ ब्राह्मणानामभिद्रोहो न कर्तव्यः कथंचन।
en: O child, he is never to be killed by you even if you be angry. Enmity with Brahmanas is never proper under any circumstances.

sn: न ह्येवमग्निर्नादित्यो भस्म कुर्यात्तथाऽनघ॥ यथा कुर्यादभिक्रुद्धो ब्राह्मणः संशितव्रतः।
en: O sinless one, neither fire nor the sun does consume so much as does a Brahman of rigid austerity when angry.

sn: तदेतैर्विविधैर्लिङ्गैस्त्वं विद्यास्तं द्विजोत्तमम्। भूतानामग्रभूविप्रो वर्णश्रेष्ठः पिता गुरुः॥
en: You must know a good Brahmana by these indications. A Brahmana is the first-born of all creatures, the best of four castes, the father, master and teacher of all.

sn: गरुड उवाच किं रूपो ब्राह्मणो मतः किं शीलः किं पराक्रमः। किंस्विदग्निनिभो भाति किंस्वित्सौम्यप्रदर्शनः॥
en: Garuda said: O mother, what form a Brahmana has? What is his character and what is his power? Does he shine like fire or is he of gentle nature?

sn: यथाहमभिजानीयां ब्राह्मणं लक्षणैः शुभैः। तन्मे कारणतो मातः पृच्छतो वक्तुमर्हसि॥
en: O mother, you should tell me, who ask you, the auspicious indications by which I shall be able to recognise a Brahmana.

sn: विनतोवाच यस्ते कण्ठमनुप्राप्तो निगीर्णं बडिशं यथा। दहेदङ्गारवत्पुत्र तं विद्याद्राह्मणर्षभम्॥
en: Vinata said: O son, know him to be a Brahmana who will torture you like a fishhook, or burn you like a hot charcoal, when he will enter into your throat.

sn: विप्रस्त्वया न हन्तव्यः संक्रुद्धेनापि सर्वदा। प्रोवाच चैनं विनता पुत्रहार्दादिदं वचः॥
en: You must not kill a Brahmana even in anger." Out of affection for her son Vinata again said,

sn: जठरे न च जीर्येद्यस्तं जानीहि द्विजोत्तमम्। पुनः प्रोवाच विनता पुत्रहार्दादिदं वचः॥
en: “Know him to be a good Brahmana, who will not be digested in your stomach.” Vinata again repeated those words from the great love she bore for her son.

sn: जानन्त्यप्यतुलं वीर्यमाशीर्वादपरायणा। प्रीता परमदुःखार्ता नागैविप्रकृता सती॥
en: Sauti said: Though she knew the matchless strength of her son, yet being exceedingly sorrowful and gentle and deceived by the Nagas, Vinata heartily blessed him, (saying)

sn: विनतोवाच पक्षौ ते मारुतः पातु चन्द्रसूर्यौ च पृष्ठतः। शिरश्च पातु वह्निस्ते वसवः सर्वतस्तनुम्॥
en: Vinata said : Let Maruta protect your wings, let Chandra and Surya protect your back; let Agni protect your head and the Vasus your whole body.

sn: अहं च ते सदा पुत्र शान्तिस्वस्तिपरायणा। इहासीना भविष्यामि स्वस्तिकारे रता सदा॥ अरिष्टं व्रज पन्थानं पुत्र कार्यार्थसिद्धये।
en: I also, my son, shall somewhere, wishing for your good and being engaged in ceremonies that will produce you good. Go then, my son, in safety to accomplish your purpose.

sn: सौतिरुवाच ततः स मातुर्वचनं निशम्य वितत्य पक्षौ नभ उत्पपात। ततो निषादान्बलवानुपागतो बुभुक्षित: काल इवान्तकोऽपरः॥
en: Sauti said: Having heard what his mother said, Garuda stretched his wings and rose to the skies and then being endued with great strength like another Yama, he soon came upon the Nishadas.

sn: स तान्निषादानुपसंहरंस्तदा रजः समुद्भूय नभःस्पृशं महत्। समुद्रकुक्षौ च विशोषयन्पयः समीपजाम्भूधरजान्विचालयन्॥
en: Bent upon destroying the Nishadas he raised up a great storm of dust that covered the whole sky. He sucked up water from the ocean and shook the trees growing on adjacent mountains.

sn: ततः स चक्रे महदाननं तदा निषादमार्ग प्रतिरुध्य पक्षिराट्। ततो निषादास्त्वरिताः प्रवव्रजुः यतो मुखं तस्य भुजंगभोजिनः॥
en: Then the king of birds, opening his great mouth, stopped the road of the Nishadas and the Nishadas too went into his open mouth flying in fright.

sn: तदाननं विवृतमतिप्रमाणवत् समभ्ययुर्गगनमिवार्दिताः खगाः। सहस्रशः पवनरजो विमोहिता यथाऽनिलप्रचलितपादपे वने॥
en: As birds in great affliction rose by thousands into the skies when the trees of the forest were shaken in a great storm, so the Nishadas, blinded by the dust raised by the storm, entered into the wide-opened mouth of the great snake-eater.

sn: ततः खगो वदनममित्रतापनः समाहरत्परिचपलो महाबलः। निषूदयन्बहुविधमत्स्यजीविनो बुभुक्षितो गगनचरेश्वरस्तदा॥
en: Then the hungry bird, the chastiser of his enemies, who is endued with great strength and who moves with the greatest speed to achieve his end, closed his mouth, thereby killing thousands of Nishadas who followed the occupation of fishermen.

sn: सौतिरुवाच तस्य कण्ठमनुप्राप्तो ब्राह्मणः सह भार्यया। दहन्दीप्त इवाङ्गारस्तमुवाचन्तरिक्षगः॥
en: Sauti said : A Brahmana with his wife had entered into his throat and he began to burn the bird's throat like a flaming piece of charcoal. The great bird addressed him thus,

sn: द्विजोत्तम विनिर्गच्छ तूर्णमास्यादपावृतात्। न हि मे ब्राह्मणो वध्यः पापेष्वपि रतः सदा॥
en: "O best of the twice born! soon come out of my mouth. I open it for you. A Brahmana will never be killed by me, even if he is always engaged in sinful acts."

sn: ब्रुवाणमेवं गरुडं ब्राह्मणः प्रत्यभाषत। निषादी मम भार्येयं निर्गच्छतु मया सह॥
en: When Garuda addressed the Brahmana thus, he said, "Let my wife who is a Nishada come out with me."

sn: गरुड उवाच एतामपि निषादी त्वं परिगृह्याशु निष्पत। तूर्णं संभावयात्मानमजीर्णं मम तेजसा॥
en: Garuda said: Take the Nishada woman with you and come out at once. Save yourself without delay for you are not yet digested by the heat of my stomach.

sn: सौतिरुवाच ततः स विप्रो निष्क्रान्तो निषादीसहितस्तदा। वर्धयित्वा च गरुडमिष्टं देशं जगाम ह॥
en: Sauti said: Thereupon the Brahmana came out with the Nishada woman and eulogising Garuda went to the country where he desired to go.

sn: सह भार्ये विनिष्क्रान्ते तस्मिन्विप्रे च पक्षिराट्। वितत्य पक्षावाकाशमुत्पपात मनोजवः॥
en: When the Brahmana with his wife came out, the king of the birds, fleet as mind, stretching his wings, rose to the sky.

sn: ततोऽपश्यत्स पितरं पृष्ठश्चाख्यातवान्पितुः। यथान्यायममेयात्मा तं चोवाच महानृषिः॥
en: He then saw his father and hailed by him, made him proper answer. And the great Rishi then asked him.

sn: कश्यप उवाच कच्चिद्वः कुशलं नित्यं भोजने बहुलं सुत। कच्चिच्च मानुषे लोके तवान्नं विद्यते बहु॥
en: Kashyapa said : My son, are you doing well? Do you get sufficient food every day. Is there plenty of food for you in the world of men?

sn: गरुड उवाच माता मे कुशला शश्वत्तथा भ्राता तथा ह्यहम्। न हि मे कुशलं तात भोजने बहुले सदा॥
en: Garuda said: My mother is well; and so is my brother and so am I. But, father, I do not get sufficient food and therefore my happiness is not complete.

sn: अहं हि सर्पः प्रहित: पोममाहर्तुमुत्तमम्। मातुर्दास्यविमोक्षार्थमाहरिष्ये तमद्य वै॥
en: I have been sent by the snakes to get the Ambrosia, which is not easy to get. (However) I shall bring it to-day in order to emancipate my mother from her slavery.

sn: मात्रा चात्र समादिष्टो निषादान्भक्षयेति ह। न च मे तृप्तिरभवद्भक्षयित्वा सहस्रशः॥
en: My mother commanded me to eat the Nishadas. I have eaten thein by thousands, but my hunger is not appeased.

sn: तस्माद्भक्ष्यं त्वमपरं भगवन्प्रदिशस्व मे। यद्भुक्त्वाऽमृतमाहर्तुं समर्थः स्यामहं प्रभो॥ क्षुत्पिपासाविघातार्थं भक्ष्यमाख्यातु मे भवान्।
en: O great one, point out to me some other food, by eating which, O Lord, I would become capable to bring the Ambrosia by force. You should point out some food which can appease my hunger and thirst.

sn: कश्यप उवाच इदं सरो महापुण्यं देवलोकेऽपि विश्रुतम्। यत्र कूर्माग्रजं हस्ती सदाकर्षत्यवाङ्मुखः॥
en: Kashyapa said : This lake you see before you is very sacred. It is even known in the celestial regions. There is an elephant with its face downwards continually dragging a tortoise which is his elder brother.

sn: तयोर्जन्मान्तरे वैरं संप्रवक्ष्याम्यशेषतः। तन्मे तत्त्वं निबोधत्स्व यत्प्रमाणौ च तावुभौ॥
en: I shall speak to you in detail their hostility in the former life. Hear from me the true story, the proof of which is their presence here.

sn: आसीद्विभावसुर्नाम महर्षिः कोपनो भृशम्। भ्राता तस्यानुजश्चासीत्सुप्रतीको महातपाः॥
en: There was in the olden days a great Rishi, named Vibhavasu, who was of exceedingly angry disposition. He had a younger brother, named Supratika, a great ascetic.

sn: स नेच्छति धनं भ्राता सहैकस्थं महामुनिः। विभाग कीर्तयत्येवसुप्रतीको हि नित्यशः॥
en: That great Rishi was not willing to keep his wealth joint with his brother, Supratika always spoke of a partition.

sn: अथाब्रवीच्च तं भ्राता सुप्रतीकं विभावसुः। विभागं बहवो मोहात्कर्तुमिच्छन्ति नित्यशः॥
en: Some time after Vibhavasu told his brother S ratika, “It is from foolishness, blinded by wealth, that many wish to divide (paternal) wealth.

sn: ततो विभक्तास्त्वन्योऽन्य विक्रुध्यन्तेऽर्थमोहिताः। ततः स्वार्थपरान्मूढान्पृथग्भूतान्स्वकैर्धनैः॥ विदित्वा भेदयन्त्येतानमित्रामित्ररूपिणः। विदित्वा चापरे भिन्नानन्तरेषु पतन्त्यथ॥
en: But as soon as it is partitioned, they begin to quarrel from the blindness arising from wealth. And enemies in the guise of friends, cause estrangement between ignorant and selfish brothers. They confirm their quarrels by pointing out faults and thus they fall one by one.

sn: भिन्नानामतुलो नाशः क्षिप्रमेव प्रवर्तते। तस्माद्विभागं भ्रातृणां न प्रशंसन्ति साधवः॥
en: Absolute ruin very soon overtakes those (brothers) that are separated. Therefore, good men never approve of the partition amongst brothers,

sn: गुरुशास्त्रेऽनिबद्धानामन्योऽन्येनाभिशंकिनाम्। नियन्तुं न हि शक्यस्त्वं भेदतो धनमिच्छसि॥
en: Who, when divided, do not have any regard for Shastras or Gurus. As you, without regarding my advice, impelled by the desire of separation, wish to partition for wealth,

sn: यस्मात्तस्मात्सुप्रतीक हस्तित्वं समवाप्स्यसि। शप्तस्त्वेवं सुप्रतीको विभावसुमथाब्रवीत्॥
en: For this, O Supratika, you will become an elephant.” Thus being cursed Supratika told Vibhavasu,

sn: त्वमप्यन्तर्जलचरः कच्छपः संभविष्यसि। एवमन्योन्यशापात्तौ सुप्रतीकविभावसू॥
en: “You will become an aquatic tortoise." Thus being cursed by each other Supratika and Vibhavasu,

sn: गजकच्छपतां प्राप्तावार्थं मूढचेतसौ। रोषदोषानुषङ्गेन तिर्यग्योनिगतावुभौ॥
en: Both fools now live as a tortoise and an elephant. Owing to their wrathful nature they have both become inferior animals.

sn: परस्पर द्वेषरतौ प्रमाणबलदर्पितौ। सरस्यस्मिन्महाकायौ पूर्ववैरानुसारिणौ॥
en: They are both engaged in hostilities with each other. Proud of their great strength and the weight of their body, in this lake, these two huge creatures are now engaged in their old hostilities.

sn: तयोरन्यतरः श्रीमान्समुपैति महागजः। यस्य बृंहितशब्देन कूर्मोऽप्यन्तर्जलेशयः॥ उत्थितोऽसौ महाकायः कृत्स्नं विक्षोभयन्सरः। यं दृष्ट्वा वेष्टितकरः पतत्येष गजो जलम्॥
en: Look, the handsome elephant is coming to the lake. Hearing his roar the huge tortoise rises up, violently agitating the water of the lake; and seeing him the elephant, coiling his trunk, rushes into the water.

sn: दन्तहस्ताग्रलांगूलपदावेगेन वीर्यवान्। विक्षोभयंस्ततोनागः सरो बहुझषाकुलम्॥
en: The greatly powerful elephant, with the motion of his tusks and fore-part of his trunk and with tail and feet, violently agitates the water of the lakes full of fishes.

sn: कूर्मोऽष्यभ्युद्यतशिरा युद्धायाभ्येति वीर्यवान्। षडुच्छ्रितो योजनानि गजस्तद्द्विगुणायतः॥
en: The greatly powerful tortoise also, with its head up, comes to the fight. The elephant is six Yojanas in height and twice that measure in circumference.

sn: कूर्मस्त्रियोजनोत्सेधो दशयोजनमण्डलः। तावुभौ युद्धसंमत्तौ परस्परवधैषिणौ।॥
en: The tortoise is also three Yojanas in height and his circumference is ten Yojanas. Eat up both of these animals, madly engaged in battle and bent upon killing each other.

sn: उपयुज्याशु कर्मेदं साधयेत्सितमात्मनः। महाभ्रघनसंकाशं तं भुक्त्वामृतमानय। महागिरिसमप्रख्यं घोररूपं च हस्तिनम्॥
en: (After eating them), accomplish the task you desire to perform. Eating the fearful elephant which looks like a huge mountain and a huge mass of clouds, go and bring the Aimbrosia.

sn: सौतिरुवाच इत्युक्त्वा गरुडं सोऽथ माङ्गल्यमकरोत्तदा॥
en: Sauti said : Having said this to Garuda, he blessed him, saying,

sn: युध्यतः सह देवैस्ते युद्धे भवतु मङ्गलम्। पूर्णकुम्भो द्विजा गावो यच्चान्यत्किंचिदुत्तमम्॥ शुभं स्वस्त्ययनं चापि भविष्यति तवाण्डज। युध्यमानस्य संग्रामे देवैः सार्धं महाबल॥
en: “O oviparous one, let good come to you when you engage in battle with the celestials. Let water-pots filled to the brim, let Brahmanas, kine and other auspicious objects bless you. In the battle with the powerful celestials,

sn: ऋचो यजूंषि सामानि पवित्राणि हवींषि च। रहस्यानी च सर्वाणि सर्वे वेदाश्च ते बलम्॥
en: Let Riks, Yajus, Saman, the sacred sacrificial ghee, all the mysteries and all the Vedas become your strength."

sn: इत्युक्तो गरुडः पित्रा गतस्तं ह्रदमन्तिकात्। अपश्यन्निर्मलजलं नानापक्षिसमाकुलम्॥
en: Having been thus addressed by his father, Garuda went to the side of the lake. He saw it full of clear water and full of birds of various kinds flying all around.

sn: स तत्स्मृत्वा पितुर्वाक्यं भीमवेगोऽन्तरिक्षगः। नखेन गजमेकेन कूर्ममेकेन चाक्षिपत्॥
en: Remembering his father's words, the swiftflying great bird seized the elephant and the tortoise, one in each claw.

sn: समुत्पपात चाकाशं तत उच्चैविहंगमः। सोऽलम्बं तीर्थमासाद्य देववृक्षानुपागमत्॥
en: The great bird then soared high into the sky. Coming to a holy shrine, called Alamba, where there were many celestial trees.

sn: ते भीताः समकम्पन्त तस्य पक्षानिलाहताः। नो भञ्ज्यादिति तदा दिव्याः कनकशाखिनः॥
en: Struck by the wind raised by his wings, the trees began to tremble in fear. Those trees, with golden boughs, feared that they would be broken down.

sn: प्रचलाङ्गान्स तान्दृष्ट्वा मनोरथफलद्रुमान्। अन्यानतुलरूपाङ्गानुपचक्राम खेचरः॥
en: Thereupon the bird, seeing the trees that are capable of giving everything, were trembling in fear, went to other trees of matchless appearance.

sn: काञ्चनै राजतैश्चैव फलैर्वैदूर्यशाखिनः। सागराम्बुपरिक्षिप्तान्भ्राजमानान्महादुमान्॥
en: And those big trees were adorned with fruits of gold and silver; and with branches of precious gems; and they were washed by the waters of the sea. There was a big banian amongst them.

sn: तमुचाच खगश्रेष्ठं तत्र रौहिणपादपः। अतिप्रवृद्धः सुमहानापतन्तं मनोजवम्॥
en: The great tree spoke to the best of the birds, who was flying away with the speed of the mind, saying,

sn: रौहिण उवाच यैषा मम महाशाखा शतयोजनमायता। एतामास्थाय शाखां त्वं खादेमौ गजकच्छपौ॥
en: “Sit down on this big branch of mine which extends a hundred Yojanas; and eat the elephant and the tortoise."

sn: ततो दुमं पतगसहस्रसेवितम् महीधरप्रतिमवपुः प्रकम्पयन्। खगोत्तमो द्रुतमभिपत्य वेगवान् बभञ्जतामविरलपत्रसंचयाम्॥
en: When the best of birds, huge as a huge mountain and of great swiftness, alighted on the tree, the abode of thousands of birds, it trembled; and the bough, full of leaves, was broken.

sn: सौतिरुवाच स्पृष्टमात्रा तु पद्भ्यां सा गरुडेन बलीयसा। अभज्यत तरोः शाखां भग्नां चैकामधारयत्॥
en: Sauti said: The moment the branch of the tree was touched by the greatly powerful Garuda with his feet, it broke down. As it was about to fall, it was caught by him.

sn: तां भक्त्वा स महाशाखां स्मयमानो विलोकयन्। अथात्र लम्बतोऽपश्यद्वालखिल्यानधोमुखान्॥ ॥
en: As he cast his eyes in wonder on the broken branch of the tree, he saw that the Valakhilya Rishis were hanging form it, with their heads downwards.

sn: ऋषयो ह्यत्र लम्बन्ते न हन्यामिति तानृषीन्। तपोरतान्लम्बमानान्ब्रह्मर्षीनभिवीक्ष्य सः॥
en: Having seen the holy Rishis thus suspended, he said to himself, “These Rishis of great penances must not be killed.

sn: हन्यादेतान्संपतन्ती शाखेत्यथ विचिन्त्य सः। नखैदूंढतरं वीरः संगृह्य गजकच्छपौ॥
en: If the bough fell down, the Rishis will be killed.” Reflecting thus, the mighty bird held more firmly the elephant and the tortoise.

sn: स तद्विनाशसंत्रासादभिपत्य खगाधिपः। शाखामास्येन जग्राह तेषामेवान्ववेक्षया॥
en: The king of birds, from the fear of killing the Rishis and from the desire of saving them held the bough in his beaks and rose on his wings.

sn: अतिदैवं तु तत्तस्य कर्म दृष्ट्वा महर्षयः। विस्मयोत्कम्पहृदया नाम चक्रुर्महाखगे॥
en: The great Rishis, seeing this act which was beyond the powers of the celestials, was filled with wonder and they gave the great bird a name.

sn: गुरुं भारं समासाद्यड्डीन एष विहंगमः। गरुडस्तु खगश्रेष्ठस्तस्मात्पन्नगभोजनः॥
en: They said "As this great bird rises on its wings with a heavy burden, let the best of the birds, the eater of snakes, be called Garuda.”

sn: ततः शनैः पर्यपतत्पक्षैः शैलाप्रकम्पयन्। एवं सोऽभ्यपतद्देशान्बहून्सगजकच्छपः॥
en: Then shaking the mountains, the bird with the elephant and tortoise, slowly moved onward in the sky and when he was thus going he saw many countries underneath.

sn: दयार्थं बालखिल्यानां न च स्थानमविन्दत। स गत्वा पर्वतश्रेष्ठं गन्धमादनमञ्जसा॥
en: Wishing to save the Valakhilyas he could not find a (proper) place to sit on. At last he went to that best of mountains, called Gandhamadana.

sn: ददर्श कश्यपं तत्र पितरं तपसि स्थितम्। ददर्श तं पिता चापि दिव्यरूपं विहंगमम्॥
en: There he saw his father, Kashyapa, engaged in ascetic devotions. His father also saw that great bird of divine form.

sn: तेजोवीर्यबलोपेतं मनोमारुतरंहसम्। शैल,ङ्गप्रतीकाशं ब्रह्मदण्डमिवोद्यतम्॥
en: And of great splendour, strength and energy, as swift as the wind or the mind, huge as a mountain peak, a ready smiter as a curse of a Brahmana,

sn: अचिन्त्यमनभिध्येयं सर्वभूतभयंकरम्। महावीर्यधरं रौद्रं साक्षादग्निमिवोद्यतम्॥
en: Inconceivable, indescribable, fearful to all creatures possessed of great powers, terrible, as full of splendour as Agni himself.

sn: अप्रधृष्यमजेयं च देवदानवराक्षसैः। भेत्तारं गिरिशृङ्गाणां समुद्रजलशोषणम्॥
en: Incapable of being overcome by the Devas and Danavas, capable of splitting mountains and of sucking the ocean,

sn: लोकसंलोडनं घोरं कृतान्तसमदर्शनम्। तमागतमभिप्रेक्ष्य भगवान्कश्यपस्तदा। विदित्वा चास्य संकल्पमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Capable of destroying the three worlds and as fierce-looking as Yama himself. The greatly illustrious Kashyapa, seeing him approach and knowing his intention, thus addressed him,

sn: कश्यप उवाच पुत्र मा साहसं कार्षीर्मा सद्यो लप्स्यसे व्यथाम्। मा त्वां दहेयुः संक्रुद्धा वालखिल्या मरीचिपाः॥
en: Kashyapa said : My son, do not commit a rash act, for you will then have to suffer pain. The Valakhilyas, that support on the rays of the sun, if angry, can blast you.

sn: सौतिरुवाच ततः प्रसादयामास कश्यपः पुत्रकारणात्। वालखिल्यान्महाभागांतपसा हतकल्मषान्॥
en: Sauti said: Therefore, Kashyapa for the snake of his son, propitiated the very glorious, exceedingly ascetic and sinless Valakhilyas.

sn: कश्यप उवाच प्रजाहितार्थमारम्भो गरुडस्य तपोधनाः। चिकीर्षति महत्कर्म तदनुज्ञातुमर्हथ॥
en: Kashyapa said : O great Rishis, the action of Garuda is for the good of all creatures. He is trying to accomplish a great act and therefore, you should give him permission.

sn: सौतिरुवाच एवमुक्ता भगवता मुनयस्ते समभ्ययुः। मुक्त्वा शाखां गिरिं पुण्यं हिमवन्तंतपोऽर्थिनः॥
en: Sauti said: The great ascetics, having been thus addressed by the illustrious Kashyapa, quitting the bough, went to the sacred Himalayas to observe ascetic penances.

sn: ततस्तेष्वपयातेषु पितरं विनतासुतः। शाखाव्याक्षिप्तवदनः पर्यपृच्छत कश्यपम्॥
en: When the Rishis went away, the son of Vinata, his voice choked by the bough in his beaks, asked his father Kashyapa,

sn: भगवन्क्व विमुञ्चामि तरोः शाखामिमामहम्। वर्जितं मानुषैर्देशमाख्यातु भगवान्मम॥
en: "O illustrious one, where stall I throw this great bough of the tree? O illustrious one, point me a place free from men."

sn: ततो निःपुरुषं शैलं हिमसंरुद्धकन्दरम्। अगम्यं मनसाप्यन्यैस्तस्याचख्यौ स कश्यपः॥
en: Kashyapa told him of a mountain without human beings, with caves and dales, always covered with snow and inaccessible by ordinary men even in thought.

sn: तं पर्वतं महाकुक्षिमुद्दिश्य स महाखगः! जवेनाभ्यपतत्तार्क्ष्य: सशाखागजकच्छपः॥
en: The great bird, carrying the bough, the elephant and the tortoise, proceeded in great speed towards that mountain of broad waist.

sn: न तां वध्री परिणहेच्छतचर्मा महातनुम्। शाखिनो महतीं शाखां यां प्रगृह्य ययौ खगः॥
en: The great bough with which the huge bird flew away could be girt round with a cord made of a hundred hides.

sn: स ततः शतसाहस्रं योजनान्तरमागतः। कालेन नातिमहता गरुडः पतगेश्वरः॥
en: The king of the birds, Garuda, flew away one hundred thousand Yojanas in the shortest time.

sn: स तं गत्वा क्षणेनैव पर्वतं वचनापितुः। अमुञ्चन्महतीं शाखां सस्वनं तत्र खेचरः॥
en: Going almost within a moment to the mountains as directed by his father, the bird let fall the great bough. And it fell with a great noise.

sn: पक्षानिलहतश्चास्य प्राकम्पत स शैलराट्। मुमोच पुष्पवर्षं च समागलितपादपः॥
en: That king of the mountains trembled, having been struck with the storm, raised by Garuda's wings. The trees thereon dropped showers of flowers.

sn: शृङ्गाणि च व्यशीर्यन्त गिरेस्तस्य समन्ततः। मणिकाञ्चनचित्राणि शोभयन्ति महागिरिम्॥
en: And the peaks of that great mountain, decked with gems and gold, were loosened and fell down on all sides.

sn: शाखिनो बहवश्चापि शाखायाऽभिहतास्तया। काञ्चनैः कुसुमैर्भान्त विद्युत्त्वन्त इवाम्बुदाः॥
en: The falling bough struck down many trees, which, with golden flowers amid their dark leaves, looked like clouds charged with lightning.

sn: ते हेमविकचा भूमौ युताः पर्वतधातुभिः। व्यराजञ्छाखिनस्तत्र सूर्यांशुप्रतिरञ्जिताः॥
en: And these trees, bright as gold, falling down upon the ground and dyed with the mountain metals, looked as if they were bathed in the rays of the sun.

sn: ततस्तस्य गिरेः शृङ्गमास्थाय स खगोत्तमः। भक्षयामास गरुडस्तावुभौ गजकच्छपौ॥
en: Then the best of birds sat on the summit of that mountain and ate both the elephant and the tortoise.

sn: तावुभौ भक्षयित्वा तु स तायः कूर्मकुञ्जरौ। ततः पर्वतकूटाग्रादुत्पपात महाजवः॥
en: The son of Tarkshya (Garuda), having thus eaten the elephant and the tortoise, rose on his wings from the top of that mountain summit.

sn: प्रावर्तन्ताथ देवानामुत्पाताभयशंसिनः। इन्द्रस्य वज्रं दयितं प्रजज्वाल भयात्ततः॥
en: Various evil omens appeared before the celestial foreboding fear. Indra's thunder-bolt blazed up in a fright.

sn: सधूमा न्यपतत्सार्चिर्दिवोल्का नभसश्च्युता। तथा वसूनां रुद्राणामादित्यानां च सर्वशः॥ साध्यानां मरुतां चैव ये चान्ये देवतागणाः। स्वं स्वं प्रहरणं तेषां परस्परमुपाद्रवत्॥
en: Meteors with flames and smoke, loosened from the welkin, shot down during the day; and the weapons of the Vasus, the Rudras, la Adityas, the Sadhyas, the Maruts and of all other classes of celestials began to fight among one another.

sn: अभूतपूर्वं संग्रामे तदा देवासुरेऽपि च। वदुर्वाताः सनिर्घाता: पेतुरुल्काः सहस्रशः॥
en: Such things had never happened, not even during the war between the Devas and the Danavas. The winds blew with thunder; meteors fell in thousands;

sn: निरभ्रमेव चाकाशं प्रजगर्न महास्वनम्। देवानामपि यो देवः सोऽप्यवर्षत शोणितम्॥
en: The cloudless sky made a tremendous roar. Even he who was the god of the gods, dropped blood,

sn: मम्लुर्माल्यानि देवानां नेशुस्तेजांसि चैव हि। उत्पातमेघा रौद्राश्च ववृषुः शोणितं बहु॥
