en: The garlands in the necks of the celestials grew pale and dim and their splendour was lost. And terrible masses of clouds vomited thick showers of blood.

sn: रजांसि मुकुटान्येषामुत्थिानि व्यघर्षयन्। ततस्त्राससमुद्विग्नः सह देवैः शतऋतुः। उत्पातान्दारुणान्पश्यन्नित्युवाच बृहस्पतिम्॥
en: The dust, raised by the winds, darkened the splendour of the coronets worn by the celestial. Thereupon, Indra with the other celestials, perplexed with fear on account of these evil omens, addressed Brihaspati thus.

sn: इन्द्र उवाच किमर्थं भगवन्योरा उत्पाताः सहसोस्थिताः। न च शत्रु प्रपश्यामि युधि यो नः प्रधर्षयेत्॥
en: Indra said : O illustrious one, why have these great disasters suddenly arisen? I do not see any enemy who will oppress us in a war.

sn: बृहस्पतिरुवाच तवापराधाद्देवेन्द्र प्रमादाच्च शतक्रतो। तपसा बालखिल्यानां महर्षीणां महात्मनाम्॥
en: Brihaspati said : O king of the celestials, O Shatakratu, it is from your carelessness and from your fault and owing to the penances of the illustrious Rishi Valakhilyas,

sn: कश्यपस्य मुनेः पुत्रो विनतायाश्च खेचरः। हर्तुं सोममभिप्राप्तो बलवान्कामरूपधृक्॥
en: That the son of the Rishi Kashyapa and Vinata, the great bird, capable of assuming any form at will, is coming to take away the Soma.

sn: समर्थो बलिना श्रेष्ठो हर्तुं सोमं विहंगमः। सर्वं संभवायाम्यस्मिन्नसाध्यमपि साधयेत्॥
en: And the strongest of all the strong, that bird is capable of taking away the Soma. Everything is possible in him. He can achieve even the unachievable.

sn: सौतिरुवाच श्रुत्वैतद्वचनं शक्रः प्रोवाचामृतरक्षिणः। महावीर्यबल: पक्षी हर्तुं सोममिहोद्यतः॥
en: Sauti said : Having heard this, Indra spoke to those that guarded the Ambrosia, "A greatly powerful bird has determined to take away the Soma;

sn: युष्मान्संबोधयाम्येष यया न स हरेबलात्। अतुलं हि बलं तस्य बृहस्पतिरुवाच ह॥
en: I warn you beforehand, so that he may not succeed in taking it by force. Brihaspati has told me that his strength is matchless."

sn: तच्छ्रुत्वा विबुधा वाक्यं विस्मिता यत्नमास्थिताः। परिवार्यामृतं तस्थुर्वज्री चेन्द्रः प्रतापवान्॥
en: The celestials, when they heard it, were astonished and they took precautions. They stood surrounding the Ambrosia and the greatly powerful Indra stood with them, thunder-bolt in hand.

sn: धारयन्तो विचित्राणि काञ्चनानि मनस्विनः। कवचानि महार्हाणि वैदूर्यविकृतानि च॥
en: The celestials wore wonderful and greatly valuable breast-plates of gold, set with gems;

sn: चर्माण्यपि च गात्रेषु भानुमन्ति दृढानि च। विविधानि च शस्त्राणि घोररूपाण्यनेकशः॥
en: They wore bright leather arīnours of great toughness and wielded various sharp weapons of terrible forms,

sn: शिततीक्ष्णाग्रधाराणि समुद्यम्य सुरोत्तमाः। सविस्फुलिङ्गज्वालानि सधूमानि च सर्वशः॥
en: All emitting fire with smoke and all raised up by the best of the celestials.

sn: चक्राणि परिघांश्चैव त्रिशूलानि परश्वधान्। शक्तीश्च विविधास्तीक्ष्णा: करवालांश्च निर्मलान्। स्वदेहरूपाण्यादाय गदाश्चोग्रप्रदर्शनाः॥
en: They were armed with many discusses, iron maces, spikes, lances, tridents, battle-axes and various other sharp-pointed missiles, polished swords and maces of terrible forms, all suited to their respective bodies.

sn: तैः शस्त्रैर्भानुमद्भिस्ते दिव्याभरणभूषिताः। भानुमन्तः सुरगणास्तस्थुर्विगतकल्मषाः॥
en: Armed with these bright weapons and adorned with all celestial ornaments, the celestials, having their fear allayed, waited there (ready to meet Garuda).

sn: अनुपमबलवीर्यतजेसो धृतमनसः परिरक्षणेऽमृतस्य। असुरपुरविदारणाः सुरा ज्वलनसमिद्धवपु:प्रकाशिनः॥
en: The celestials of matchless strength, energy and splendour, capable of splitting the cities of the Asuras, displayed themselves in forms resplendent as the blazing fire; they all resolved to protect the Ambrosia (at all hazard).

sn: इति समरवरं सुराः स्थितास्ते परिघसहस्रशतैः समाकुलम्। विगलितमिव चाम्बरान्तरं तपनमरीचिविकाशितं बभासे॥
en: And in consequence of the celestials standing there and owing to hundreds of thousands of maces furnished with iron spokes, that battle-field looked like another firmament illuminated by the rays of the sun.

sn: शौनक उवाच कोऽपराधो महेन्द्रस्य कः प्रमादश्च सूतज। तपसा वालखिल्यानां संभूतो गरुडः कथम्॥
en: Shaunaka said: O son of Suta, what was the fault of Indra and what was his carelessness? How was Garuda born owing to the penances of the Valakhilyas?

sn: कश्यपस्य द्विजातेश्च कथं वै पक्षिराट् सुतः। अधृष्यः सर्वभूतानामवध्यश्चाभवत्कथम्॥
en: Why had Kashyapa, a Brahmana, the king of the birds for his son? Why was he invincible of all creatures and indestructible of all?

sn: कथं च कामचारी स कामवीर्यश्च खेचरः। एतदिच्छाम्यहं श्रोतुं पुराणे यदि पठ्यते॥
en: Why was that bird capable of going every where and mastering any misuse of strength at will? I am willing to hear all this, if they are narrated in the Puranas.

sn: सौतिरुवाच विषयोऽयं पुराणस्य यन्मां त्वं परिपृच्छसि। शृणु मे वदतः सर्वमेतत्संक्षेपतो द्विजः॥
en: Sauti said: What you ask me is narrated in the Puranas. O Brahmana, listen to them. I shall briefly narrated them all.

sn: यजतः पुत्रकामस्य कश्यपस्य प्रजापतेः। साहाय्यमृषयो देवा गन्धर्वाश्च ददुः किल॥
en: When Prajapati Kashyapa from the desire of begetting offspring was engaged in a sacrifice, the Rishis, the Devas and the Gandharvas all gave him help.

sn: तत्रेध्मानयने शक्रो नियुक्तः कश्यपेन ह। मुनयो बालखिल्याश्च ये चान्ये देवतागणाः॥
en: Indra with Valakhilya Rishis and other celestial were appointed by Kashyapa to bring fuel for the sacrifice.

sn: शक्रस्तु वीर्यसदृशमिध्मभारं गिरिप्रभम्। समुद्यम्यानयामास नातिकृच्छादिव प्रभुः॥
en: And Lord Indra, taking up according to his great strength a weight which was mountainlike, brought it without any fatigue.

sn: अथापश्यदृषीन्ह्रस्वानङ्गुष्ठोदरवर्मणः। पलाशवर्तिकामेकां वहतः संहतान्पथि॥
en: He saw on the way some Rishis, as small in size as the thumb, carrying together one single stalk of Palasa leaf.

sn: प्रलीनान्स्वेष्विवाङ्गेषु निराहारांस्तपोधनान्। क्लिश्यमानान्मन्दबलान्गोष्पदे संप्लुतोदके॥
en: They were exceedingly lean for want of food and they were much distressed when they fell into an indentation in the road caused by the hoop of a cow.

sn: तान्सर्वान्विस्मयाविष्टो वीर्योन्मत्तः पुरन्दरः। अवहस्याभ्यगाच्छीघ्रं लम्बयित्वावमन्य च॥
en: Purandara (Indra), madly proud of his strength, saw them with surprise and laughing at them in derision, passed them, crossing over their heads and thus grossly insulting them.

sn: तेऽथ रोषसमाविष्टाः सुभृशं जातमन्यवः। आरेभिरे महत्कर्म तदा शक्रभयंकरम्॥
en: On this the Rishis became exceedingly angry and were filled with sorrow. They began a great act which was a terror to Indra.

sn: जुहुवुस्ते सुतपसो विधिवज्जातवेदसम्। मन्त्रैरुच्चावचैर्विप्रा येन कामेन तच्छृणु॥
en: Hear, Sir, desiring what these excellent Rishi's poured ghee in the sacrificial fire loudly reciting Mantras, saying,

sn: कामवीर्यः कामगमो देवराजभयप्रदः। इन्द्रोऽन्यः सर्वदेवानां भवेदिति यतव्रताः॥
en: “There will be another Indra of all the celestials, capable of going everywhere at will mustering any measure of strength at will and imparting fear to the present Indra.

sn: इन्द्राच्छतगुणः शौर्ये वीर्ये चैव मनोजवः। तपसो नः फलेनाद्य दारुणः संभवत्विति॥
en: By the fruit of our penances, let there be born a hero, who is hundred times stronger and valorous than Indra, fleet as the mind and frightful to present Indra."

sn: तबुध्वा भृशसंतप्तो देवराज: शतक्रतुः। जगाम शरणं तत्र कश्यपं संशितव्रतम्॥
en: The Lord of the celestials Shatakratu, becoming very much alarmed, went to ask the protection of the great ascetic, the selfcontrolled Rishi Kashyapa.

sn: तच्छ्रुत्वा देवराजस्य कश्यपोऽथ प्रजापतिः। वालखिल्यानुपागम्य कर्मसिद्धिमपृच्छत॥
en: Prajapati Kashyapa, having heard every thing from Indra, went to the Valakhilyas and asked whether their act had been successful.

sn: एवमस्त्विति तं चापि प्रत्यूचुः सत्यवादिनः। तान्कश्यप उवाचेदं सान्त्वपूर्वं प्रजापतिः॥
en: Thus addressed, those truthful Rishis said, “Yes, it is done.” Then Prajapati Kashyapa pacified them and said,

sn: अयमिन्द्रस्त्रिभुवने नियोगाद्ब्रह्मणः कृतः। इन्द्रार्थे च भवन्तोऽपि यत्नवन्तस्तपोधनाः॥
en: “The present Indra has been appointed the lord of the three worlds by Brahma. O Rishis you are also trying to create another Indra.

sn: न मिथ्या ब्रह्मणो वाक्यं कर्तुमर्हथ सत्तमाः। भवतां हि न मिथ्याऽयं संकल्पो वै चिकीर्षितः॥
en: O excellent men, you should not make the words of Brahma untrue and I too do not wish to make your desire futile.

sn: भवत्वेष पतत्त्रीणामिंद्रोऽतिबलसत्त्ववान्। प्रसादः क्रियतामस्य देवराजस्य याचतः॥
en: Let there be an Indra of the winged creatures, endued with great strength. Be gracious to Indra who is suppliant to you."

sn: एवमुक्ताः कश्यपेन वालखिल्यास्तपोधनाः। प्रत्यूचुरभिसंपूज्य मुनिश्रेष्ठं प्रजापतिम्॥
en: Having been thus addressed by Kashyapa, the Valakhilya Rishis saluted the great Prajapati and spoke thus,

sn: वालखिल्या ऊचुः इन्द्रार्थोऽयं समारम्भः सर्वेषां नः प्रजापते। अपत्यार्थं समारम्भो भवतश्चायमीप्सितः॥
en: The Valakhilyas said : O Prajapati, our this action (penance) is for creating an Indra. It is also meant for a son being born to you.

sn: तदिदं सफलं कर्म त्वयैव प्रतिगृह्यताम्। तथा चैवं विधत्स्वात्र यथा श्रेयोऽनुपश्यसि॥
en: Let this successful act be accepted by you; and in this matter, do whatsoever you think good and proper.

sn: सौतिरुवाच एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु देवी दाक्षायणी शुभा। विनता नाम कल्याणी पुत्रकामा यशस्विनी॥ तपस्तप्त्वा व्रतपरा स्नाता पुंसवने शुचिः। उपचक्राम भर्तारं तामुवाचाथ कश्यपः॥
en: Sauti said: At this time, the good and illustrious daughter of Daksha, named Vinata, being desirous of having an offspring an having purified herself by bathing after her season of impurity, came to her husband and Kashyapa spoke to her thus.

sn: आरम्भः सफलो देवि भविता यस्त्वयेप्सितः। जनयिष्यसि पुत्रौ द्वौ वीरौ त्रिभुवनेश्वरौ॥
en: “O Lady, the sacrifice, commenced by me, has borne fruit. What you have desired to get, you will get. Two heroic sons will be born in you who will be the lords of the three worlds.

sn: तपसा वालखिल्यानां मम संकल्पजौ तथा। भविष्यतो महाभागौ पुत्रौ त्रैलोक्यपूजितौ॥
en: Owing to the penances of the Valakhilyas and by virtue of the desire with which I had began my sacrifice, those sons will be of exceeding good fortune and they will be worshipped by the three worlds.

sn: उवाच चैनां भगवान्कश्यपः पुनरेव ह। धार्यतामप्रमादेन गर्भोऽयं सुमहोदयः॥
en: The illustrious Kashyapa again spoke to her, "Carefully bear these auspicious seeds.

sn: एतौ सर्वपतत्त्रीणमिन्द्रत्वं कारयिष्यतः। लोकसंभावितौ वीरौ कामरूपौ विहंगमौ॥
en: These two will be the lords of all the winged creatures. They will be birds, capable of assuming any form at will and they will be great heroes, respected by all the worlds."

sn: शतक्रतुमथोवाच प्रीयमाणः प्रजापतिः। त्वत्सहायौ महावीर्यो भ्रातरौ ते भविष्यतः॥
en: The Prajapati then addressed Indra thus, "You will have two brothers of great power and strength, who will be your helps.

sn: नैताभ्यां भविता दोषः सकाशात्ते पुरंदर। व्येतु ते शक्र संतापस्त्वमेवेन्द्रो भविष्यसि॥
en: O Purandara, by them will no injury be done to you. Let your sorrow cease. O Indra, you will remain as the only one Indra in the world.

sn: न चाप्येवं त्वया भूयः क्षेप्तव्या ब्रह्मवादिनः। न चावमान्या दोत्ते वाग्वज्रा भृशकोपनाः॥
en: But let not the utterers of Brahma, Brahmanas be ever slighted by you. Let not those, whose words are like the thunderbolt, be again insulted by you."

sn: एवमुक्तो जगामेन्द्रो निर्विशङ्कस्त्रिविष्टपम्। विनता चापि सिद्धार्था बभूव मुदिता तथा॥
en: Having been thus addressed Indra, his fear being dispelled, went to heaven; and Vinata was much pleased, because her desire was accomplished.

sn: जनयामास पुत्रौ द्वावरुणं गरुडं तथा। विकलाङ्गोरुणस्तत्र भास्करस्य पुरस्सरः॥
en: She gave birth to two sons, Aruna and Garuda and the undeveloped-bodied Aruna became the fore-runner (charioteer) of the sun.

sn: पतत्त्रीणां च गरुडमिन्द्रत्वेनाभ्यषिञ्चत। तस्यैतत्कर्म सुमहच्छ्रयतां भृगुनन्दन॥
en: Garuda became the king of the birds. O descendent of Bhrigu, listen to his great deeds.

sn: सौतिरुवाच ततस्तस्मिन्द्विजश्रेष्ठ समुदीर्णे तथाविधे। गरुडः पक्षिराट् तूर्णं संप्राप्तो विबुधान्प्रति॥
en: Sauti said : O best of the twice born, the celestials, having stood prepared for battle (in he way already narrated), the king of the birds Garuda soon came upon them.

sn: तं दृष्ट्वातिबलं चैव प्राकम्पन्त सुरास्ततः। परस्परं च प्रत्यघ्नन् सर्वप्रहरणान्युत॥
en: The celestials, having seen him of excessive strength, began to tremble in fear; and (having been confused) struck one another with all their weapons.

sn: तत्र चासीदमेयात्मा विद्युदग्निसमप्रभः। भौमनः सुमहावीर्यः सोमस्य परिरक्षिता॥
en: Amongst those that were guarding the Soma Bhaumana (Vishvakarma) of matchless strength and of great energy. He was as effulgent as the lightning and fire.

sn: स तेन पतगेन्द्रेण पक्षतुण्डनखक्षतैः। मुहूर्तमतुलं युद्धं कृत्वा विनिहतो युधि॥
en: But after a moment's fight he lay dead, mangled by the king of the birds with his beaks, talons and wings.

sn: रजश्चोद्धय सुमहत्पक्षवातेन खेचरः। कृत्वा लोकान्निरालोकांस्तेन देवानवाकिरत्॥
en: The great bird, darkening the worlds with the dust raised by the great storm created by his wings, overwhelmed the celestials. was

sn: तेनावकीर्णा रजसा देवा मोहमुपागमन्। न चैवं ददृशुश्छन्ना रजसाऽमृतरक्षिणः॥
en: Having been overwhelmed with that dust, the celestials fainted away. Those that were guarding the Ambrosia could not see Garuda on account of the dust.

sn: एवं संलोडयामास गरुडस्त्रिदिवालयम्। पक्षतुण्डप्रहारैस्तु देवान्स विददार ह॥
en: Thus Garuda agitated the celestial regions and mangled the celestial with his wings and beaks.

sn: ततो देवः सहस्राक्षस्तूर्णं वायुमचोदयत्। विक्षिपेमां रजोवृष्टिं तवेदं कर्म मारुत॥
en: Thereupon the celestials, the god of thousand eyes (Indra), commanded Vayu, saying, “O Maruta, it is your work to drive the dust away.

sn: अथ वायुरपोवाह तद्रजस्तरसा बली। ततो वितिमिरे जाते देवाः शकुनिमार्दयन्॥
en: Then the mighty Vayu drove away the dust; and when darkness thus disappeared, the celestials attacked the bird.

sn: ननादोच्चैः स बलवान्महामेघ इवाम्बरे। वध्यमानः सुरगणैः सर्वभूतानि भीषयन्॥
en: When he was attacked by the celestials, he roared in the sky, like the great cloud, frightful to every creature.

sn: उत्पपात महावीर्यः पक्षिराट् परवीरहा। समुत्पत्यान्तरिक्षस्थं देवानामुपरिस्थितम्॥ वर्मिणो विबुधाः सर्वे नानाशस्त्रैरवाकिरन्। पट्टिशैः परिषैः शूलैर्गदाभिश्च सवासवाः॥ क्षुरप्रैचलितैश्चापि चक्रैरादित्यरूपिभिः। नानाशास्त्रविसर्गस्तैर्वध्यमानः समन्ततः॥
en: The greatly powerful king of birds, the slayer of enemies, rose on his wings and stayed in the sky over the heads of the celestials, with their lord Indra, who showered on him double edged swords, iron maces, sharp lances, bright arrows and discus of the form of the sun. Being thus attacked from every side,

sn: कुर्वन्सुतुमुलं युद्धं पक्षिरान व्यकम्पत। निर्दहन्निव चाकाशे वैनतेयः प्रतापवान्। पक्षाभ्यामुरसा चैव समन्ताद्व्याक्षिपत्सुरान्॥
en: The king of birds fought the great battle without being weary for a moment and the greatly powerful son of Vinata, blazing in the sky, attacked the celestials on all sides by his wings and breast and scattered them in all directions.

sn: ते विक्षिप्तास्ततो देवा दुद्रुवुर्गरुडार्दिताः। नखतुण्डक्षताश्चैव सुस्रुवुः शोणितं बहु॥
en: Mangled by the talons and the beaks of Garuda, copious blood began to flow from the bodies of the celestials. Afflicted thus, the Devas ran away hither and tither.

sn: साध्याः प्राची सगन्धर्वा वसवो दक्षिणां दिशम्। प्रजग्मुः सहिता रुद्राः पतगेन्द्रप्रधर्षिताः॥
en: Thus overcome by the king of birds, the Sadhyas fled with the Gandharvas towards the east, the Vasus with the Rudras towards the south,

sn: दिशं प्रतीजीमादित्या नासत्यावुत्तरां दिशम्। मुहुर्मुहुः प्रेक्षमाणा युध्यमाना महौजसः॥
en: The Adityas towards the west and the Ashvinis towards the north. Gifted with great powers, they retreated from fighting and looking back every moment at their enemy, they fled.

sn: अश्वक्रन्देन वीरेण रेणुकेन च पक्षिराट्। क्रथनेन च शूरेण तपनेन च खेचरः॥ उलूकश्वसनाभ्यां च निमेषेण च पक्षिराट्। प्ररुजेन च संग्रामं चकार पुलिनेन च॥
en: Garuda fought with the greatly courageous Ashvakranda and Renuka, the bold Krathana and Tapana, Uluka and Shvasana, Nimesha, Praruja and Pulina.

sn: तान्पक्षनखतुण्डात्रैरभिनद्विनतासुतः। युगान्तकाले संक्रुद्धः पिनाकीव परंतपः॥
en: The son of Vinata mangled them with his wings, talons and beaks, like the chastiser of foes, the angry Pinaki (Shiva) at the end of the Yuga..

sn: महाबला महोत्साहास्तेन ते बहुधा क्षताः। रेजुरभ्रधनप्रख्या रुधिरौघप्रवर्षिणः॥
en: Those greatly powerful and energetic celestials, mangled all over by that great bird, looked like masses of black clouds, dropping showers of blood.

sn: तान्कृत्वा पतगश्रेष्ठः सर्वानुत्क्रान्तजीवितान्। अतिक्रान्तोऽमृतस्यार्थे सर्वतोऽग्निमपश्यत॥
en: Thus making the celestials almost dead, the best of the birds went where the Ambrosia was. He saw it surrounded on all sides by fire.

sn: आवृण्वानं महाज्वालमर्चिभिः सर्वतोऽम्बरम्। दहन्तमिव तीक्ष्णांशुं चण्डवायुसमीरितम्॥
en: The terrible flames of that fire covered whole of the sky and moved by violent winds, they bent on burning the very sun.

sn: ततो नवत्या नवतीर्मुखानां कृत्वा महात्मा गरुडस्तपस्वी। नदीः समापीय मुखैस्ततस्तैः सुशीघ्रमागम्य पुनर्जवेन॥ ज्वलन्तमग्नि तममित्रतापनः समास्तरत्पत्ररथो नदीभिः। ततः प्रचक्रे वपुरन्यदल्पं प्रवेष्टकामोऽग्निमभिप्रशाम्य॥
en: The illustrious Garuda assumed ninety times ninety mouths and drinking in many rivers by those mouths and coming back in great speed, having wings for his vehicle, extinguished the fire with those rivers' water. And extinguishing that fire, he assumed a very small form, wishing to enter into the place where the Ambrosia was,

sn: सौतिरुवाच जाम्बूनदमयो भूत्वा मरीचिनिकरोज्ज्वलः। प्रविवेश बलात्पक्षी वारिवेग इवार्णवम्॥
en: Sauti said : The great bird, assuming a golden body, bright as the rays of the sun, entered (where the Soma was) with great force as a torrent enters the sea.

sn: स चक्रं क्षुरपर्यन्तमपश्यदमृतान्तिके। परिभ्रमन्तमनिशं तीक्ष्णधारमयस्मयम्॥
en: He saw near the Ambrosia a wheel, keenedged and sharp as the razor, revolving incessantly (round it).

sn: ज्वलनार्कप्रभं घोरं छेदनं सोमहारिणाम्। घोररूपं तदत्यर्थं यन्त्रं देवैः सुनिर्मितम्॥
en: And that fearful instrument of fearful form, as blazing as the blazing sun, was skillfully created by the celestials to cut down the robbers of the Ambrosia.

sn: तस्यान्तरं स दृष्दैव पर्यवर्तत खेचरः। अरान्तरेणाभ्यपतत्संक्षिप्याङ्गं क्षणेन ह॥
en: The great bird saw a passage through it and stopped for a while. Diminishing his body within an instant, he passed through the spokes of that wheel.

sn: अधश्चक्रस्य चैवात्र दीप्तानलसमद्युती। विद्युज्जिह्वौ महावीर्यो दीप्तास्यौ दीप्तलोचनौ॥ चक्षुर्विषौ महाघोरी नित्यं क्रुद्धौ तरस्विनी। रथार्थमेवामृतस्य ददर्श भुजगोत्तमौ॥
en: He beheld, within the line of the wheel, stationed there to guard the Soma, two great snakes, as blazing as the blazing fire, having tongues like lightning; power incomparable, face and eyes emitting fire, poisonous terrible, always in anger and always in activity.

sn: सदा संरब्धनयनौ सदा चानिमिषेक्षणौ। तयोरेकोऽपि यं पश्येत् स तूर्णं भस्मसाद्भवेत्॥
en: Their eyes were winkless and always inflamed with anger. He who was even seen by any of the two was instantly reduced to ashes.

sn: तयोश्चक्षूसि रजसा सुपर्णः सहसाऽऽवृणोत्। ताभ्यामदृष्टरूपोऽसौ सर्वतः समताडयत्॥
en: The great bird (Suparna) suddenly covered their eyes with dust and thus making them blind, he attacked them from all sides.

sn: तयोरंङ्गे समाक्रम्य वैनतेयोऽन्तरिक्षगः। आच्छिनत्तरसा मध्ये सोममभ्यद्रवत्ततः॥
en: The son of Vinata, that ranger of the sky, attacking their bodies, mangled them into pieces, and he then without the least delay came to the place where the Soma was.

sn: समुत्पाट्यामृतं तत्र वैनतेयस्ततो बली। उत्पपात जवेनैव यन्त्रमन्मथ्य वीर्यवान्॥
en: The mighty son of Vinata, taking up the Ambrosia from the place where it was, rose on his wings, breaking the instrument into pieces.

sn: अपीत्वैवाऽमृतं पक्षी परिगृह्याशुनिःसृतः। आगच्छदपरिश्रान्त आवार्यार्कप्रभां ततः॥
en: He soon came out, but he did not drink the Ambrosia. He then proceeded on his way without the least fatigue, darkening the splendour of the sun.

sn: विष्णुना च तदाकाशे वैनतेयः समेयिवान्। तस्य नारायणस्तुष्टस्तेनालौल्येन कर्मणा॥
en: The son of Vinata then saw Vishnu on his way in the sky and Narayana was pleased with him for his self-denial.

sn: तमुवाचाऽव्ययो देवो वरदोऽस्मीति खेचरम्। स वने तव तिष्ठेयमुपरीत्यन्तरिक्षगः॥
en: The undeteriorating Deity said to the great bird, “I am willing to grant you a boon." Thereupon the bird said, "I want to stay above you.”

sn: उवाच चैनं भूयोऽपि नारायणमिदं वचः। अजस्चामस्थ स्याममृतेन विनाऽप्यहम्॥
en: He again said to Narayana, “I want to be immortal and free from disease without drinking the Ambrosia."

sn: एवमस्त्विति तं विष्णुरुवाच विनतासुतम्। प्रतिगृह्य वरौ तौ च गरुडो विष्णुमब्रवीत्॥
en: Vishnu said to the son of Vinata, “Be it so." Receiving these two boons, Garuda said to Vishnu,

sn: भवतेऽपि वरं दद्यां वृणोतु भगवानपि। तं वव्रे वाहनं विष्णुर्गरुत्मन्तं महाबलम्॥
en: "I shall also grant you a boon.” Thereupon Vishnu asked the mighty carrier of great veight to become his vehicle.

sn: ध्वजं च चक्रे भगवानुपरि स्थास्यसीति तम्। एवमस्त्विति तं देवमुक्त्वा नारायणं खगः॥
en: He placed the bird on the flag-staff of his car saying, “Thus shall you stay above me." And the bird said to Narayana, “Be it so,"

sn: वव्राज तरसा वेगाद्वायुं स्पर्धन्महाजवः। तं व्रजन्तं खगश्रेष्ठं वज्रेणेन्द्रोऽभ्यताडयत्॥
en: Mocking the wind with fleetness, he then swiftly proceeded on his way and when the great bird was thus going away, Indra hurled at him thunder-bolt.

sn: हरन्तममृतं रोषाद्गरुडं पक्षिणां वरम्। तमुवाचेन्द्रमाक्रन्दे गरुडः पततां वरः॥
en: The best of birds, Garuda, when carrying away the Ambrosia, was thus struck with the thunder-bolt; and being greatly angry, he laughingly spoke to Indra.

sn: प्रहसन् श्लक्ष्णया वाचा तथा वज्रसमाहतः। ऋषेर्मानं करिष्यामि वज्रं यस्यास्थिसंभवम्॥
en: In sweet words, “I shall respect the Rishi, with whose bones the thunder-bolt is made.

sn: वज्रस्य च करिष्यामि तवैव च शतक्रतो। एतत्पनं त्यजाम्येकं यस्यान्तं नोपलप्स्यसे॥
en: I shall respect the thunder-bolt and you also, O Indra, I cast a feather of mine, end of which even you will never find.

sn: न च वज्रनिपातेन रुजा मेऽस्तीह काचन। एवमुक्त्वा ततः पत्रमुत्ससर्ज स पक्षिराट्॥
en: I have not felt the slightest pain being struck by your thunder-bolt.” Having said this, the king of birds threw out one of his feathers.

sn: तदुत्सृष्टमभिप्रेक्ष्य तस्य पर्णमनुत्तमम्। हृष्टानि सर्वभूतानि नाम चक्रुर्गरुत्मतः॥ सुरूपं पत्रमालक्ष्य सुपर्णोऽयं भवत्विति। तदृष्ट्वा महदाश्चर्य सहस्राक्षः पुरंदरः। खगो महदिदं भूतमिति मत्वाऽभ्यभाषत॥
en: Seeing that beautiful feather, cast by Garuda, all creatures became exceedingly pleased and they said, “Let this bird be called Suparna (bird with beautiful feathers)." Seeing this, the deity of thousands eyes, Purandara, was much surprised and he thought the bird must be a great being. He then addressed him thus,

sn: शक्र उवाच बलं विज्ञातुमिच्छामि यत्ते परमनुत्तमम्। सख्यं चानन्तमिच्छामि त्वया सह खगोत्तम॥
en: Indra said: "O best of birds, I desire to know the limit of your strength, I also desire to form an eternal friendship with you.

sn: गरुड उवाच सख्यं मेऽस्तु त्वया देव यथेच्छसि पुरंदर। बलं तु मम जानीहि महच्चासह्यमेव च॥
en: Garuda said: “O Purandara, Let there be friendship between us as you desire. Know, my strength is great and is hard to bear.

sn: काम नैतत्प्रशंसन्ति सन्तः स्वबलसंस्तवम्। गुणसंकीर्तनं चापि स्वयमेव शतक्रतो॥
en: O Shatakratu, the learned do not approve of speaking highly of their own strength or of their own merits.

sn: सखेति कृत्वा तु सखे पृष्टो वक्ष्याम्यहं त्वया। न ह्यात्मस्तवसंयुक्तं वक्तव्यमनिमित्ततः॥
en: O friend, as we are now made friends and as you ask me, I will tell you, although selfpraise without reason is always improper.

sn: सपर्वतवनामुर्वी ससागरजलामिमाम्। वहे पक्षेण वै शक्र त्वामप्यत्रावलम्बिनम्॥
en: O Indra, I can bear, on a single feather of mine, this earth with her mountains forests, oceans and even you with it.

sn: सर्वान्सपिण्डितान्वापि लोकान्सस्थाणुजङ्गमान्। वहेयमपरिश्रान्तो विद्धीदं मे महद् बलम्॥
en: Know, my strength is such that I can bear, without fatigue, even all the worlds put together, with their mobile and immobile objects.

sn: सौतिरुवाच इत्युक्तवचनं वीरं किरीटी श्रीमतां वरः। आह शौनक देवेन्द्रः सर्वलोकहितः प्रभुः॥
en: Sauti said: O Shaunaka, when the great hero (Garuda) said all this, the great Lord, the king of the celestials, the wearer of the heaven's crown, the possessor of wealth, the benefactor of all the worlds said:

sn: एवमेव यथास्थ त्वं सर्वं संभाव्यते त्वयि। संगृह्यतामिदानीं मे सख्यमत्यन्तमुत्तमम्॥
en: It is true what you say, Everything is possible in you. Accept now my sincere and eternal friendship

sn: न कार्यं यदि सोमेन मम सोमः प्रदीयताम्। अस्मांस्ते हि प्रबाधेयुर्येभ्यो दद्याद्भवानिमम्॥
en: If you do not require the Soma, kindly return it to me. Those to whom you will give it will always quarrel with us.

sn: गरुड उवाच किंचित्कारणमुद्दिश्य सोमोऽयं नीयते मया। न दास्यामि समादातुं सोमं कस्मैचिदप्यहम्॥
en: Garuda said: There is a reason why I am taking away the Soma. I shall not give the Soma to any body to drink.

sn: यत्रेम तु सहस्राक्ष निक्षिपेयमहं स्वयं। त्वमादाय ततस्तूर्णं हरेथास्त्रिदिवेश्वर॥
en: O deity of thousand eyes, after I shall place it down, O King of heavens, you can instantly take it up and bring it away.

sn: शक्र उवाच वाक्येनानेन तुष्टोऽहं यत्त्वयोक्तमिहाण्डजा यमिच्छसि वरं मत्तस्तं गृहाण
en: Indra said: O oviparous One, I am highly pleased with what you have just now said. O best of birds, accept from me any boon you like to have.

sn: सौतिरुवाच इत्युक्तः प्रत्युवाचेदं कदूपुत्राननुस्मरन्। स्मृत्वा चैवोपधिकृतं मातुर्दास्यनिमित्ततः॥
en: Sauti said : Being thus addressed, Garuda recollecting the sons of Kadru and the slavery of his mother by deception said,

sn: खगोत्तम॥ ईशोऽहमपि सर्वस्य करिष्यामि तु तेऽर्थिताम्। भवेयुर्भुजगाः शक्र मम भक्ष्या महाबलाः॥
en: “Though I have power to do everything over all creatures, yet, O Indra, I shall do your bidding. Let the mighty snakes be my food.”

sn: तथेत्युक्त्वाऽन्वगच्छत्तं ततो दानवसूदनः। देवदेवं महात्मानं योगिनामीश्वरं हरिम्॥
en: "Be it so." said the destroyer of the Danavas and he went to Hari, the god of gods, the great Soul, the lord of Yogis.

sn: स चान्वमोदत्तं चार्थं यथोक्तं गरुडेन वै। इदं भूयो वचः प्राह भगवांस्त्रिदशेश्वरः॥
en: He (Vishnu) sanctioned all that was said by Garuda. The illustrious lord of all the worlds thus spoke to him,

sn: हरिष्यामि विनिक्षिप्तं सोममित्यनुभाष्य तम्। आजगाम ततस्तूर्णं सुपर्णो मातुरन्तिकम्॥
en: "I shall take away the Soma when you will place it down." Having said this he bade farewell to Garuda, And Suparna (Garuda) went to the presence of his mother with great speed.

sn: अथ सर्पानुवाचेदं सर्वान्परमहष्टवत्। इदमानीतममृतं निक्षेप्स्यामि कुशेषु वः॥
en: He then said to all the snakes in joy, "Here have I brought the Ambrosia. I shall place it on the (sacred) Kusha grass.

sn: स्नाता मङ्गलसंयुक्तास्ततः प्राश्नीत पन्नगाः। भवद्भिरिदमासीनैर्यदुक्तं तद्वचस्तदा॥
en: O snakes, drink it after performing your ablutions and religious rites. I have done what you asked me to do.

sn: अदासी चैव मातेयमद्यप्रभृति चास्तु मे। यथोक्तं भवतामेतद्वचो मे प्रतिपादितम्॥ ततः स्नातुं गताः सर्पाः प्रत्युक्त्वा तं तथेत्युत। शक्रोप्यमृतमाक्षिप्य जगाम त्रिदिवं पुनः॥
en: Therefore, as you promised, let my mother become free from this day," "Be it so," said the snakes and went to perform their ablutions. In the meantime, Indra taking up the Ambrosia, went away to heaven.

sn: अथागतास्तमुद्देशं सर्पाः सोमार्थिनस्तदा। स्नाताश्च कृतजप्याश्च प्रहृष्टाः कृतमङ्गलाः॥
en: The snakes, after performing their ablutions, their daily devotions and other sacred rites, came in joy to drink the Ambrosia.

sn: यत्रैतदमृतं चापि स्थापितं कुशसंस्तरे। तद्विज्ञाय हृतं सर्पाः प्रतिमाया कृतं च तत्॥
en: They saw that the Kusha grass on which the Ambrosia had been placed was empty. It had been taken away by a counter act of deception.

sn: सोमस्थानमिदं चेति दर्खास्ते लिलिहुस्तदा। ततो द्विधाकृता जिह्वाः सर्पाणां तेन कर्मणा॥
en: They began to lick with their tongues the Kusha grass in which the Ambrosia had been placed; and by that act, their tongues became divided into two.

sn: अभवंश्चामृतस्पर्शाद्दर्भास्तेऽथ पवित्रिणः। एवं तदमृतं तेन हृतमाहतमेव च। द्विजिह्वाश्च कृताः सर्पा गरुडेन महात्मना॥
en: The Kusha grass, from the contact of the Ambrosia, became sacred from that day. Thus did the illustrious Garuda bring the Ambrosia and bring it for the snakes, and thus were their tongues divided by what he did.

sn: ततः सुपर्णः परमप्रहर्षवान् विहृत्य मात्रा सह तत्र कानने। रहीनकीर्तिविनतामनन्दयत्॥
en: Then Suparna (Garuda) lived in that forest with his mother in great joy. The son of Vinata delighted his mother by becoming the eater of snakes, by being respected by all birds and by doing other great acts.

sn: इमां कथां यः शृणुयान्नरः सदा पठेत वा द्विजगणमुख्यसंसदि असंशयं त्रिदिवमियात्स पुण्यभाक् महात्मनः पतगपतेः प्रकीर्तनात्॥
en: He, who would listen to this story or read it to an assembly of Brahmanas, will must surely go to heaven, acquiring great merit from its recitation.

sn: शौनक उवाच भुजंगमानां शापस्य मात्रा चैव सुतेन च। विनतायास्त्वया प्रोक्तं कारणं सूतनन्दन॥
en: Shaunaka said : O son of Suta, you have told us why the snakes were cursed by their mother; and why Vinata also cursed her son.

sn: वरप्रदानं भा च कदूविनतयोस्तथा। नामनी चैव ते प्रोक्ते पक्षिणोर्वैनतेययोः॥
en: You have told us the bestowal of boons on Kadru and Vinata by their husband; you have also told us the names of the two sons of Vinata.

sn: पन्नगानां तु नामानि न कीर्तयसि सूतज। प्राधान्येनापि नामानि श्रोतुमिच्छामहे वयम्॥
en: O son of Suta, you have not told us the names of the snakes (the sons of Kadru). We are anxious to know at least the names of the chief ones.

sn: सौतिरुवाच बहुत्वान्नामधेयानि पन्नगानां तपोधन। न कीर्तयिष्ये सर्वेषां प्राधान्येन तु मे शृणु॥
en: Sauti said: O Rishi, for fear of being lengthy, I shall not mention the names of all the snakes. But hear, I shall only mention the names of the chief ones.

sn: शेषः प्रथमतो जातो वासुकिस्तदनन्तरम्। ऐरावतस्तक्षकश्च कर्कोटकधनंजयौ॥ कालियो मणिनागश्च नागश्चापूरणस्तथा। नागस्तथापिञ्जरकः एलापत्रोऽथ वामनः॥ नीलानीलौ तथा नागौ कल्माषशबलौ तथा। आर्यकश्चोग्रकश्चैव नाग: कलशपोतकः॥ सुमनाख्यो दधिमुखस्तथा विमलपिण्डकः। आप्तः कर्कोटकश्चैव शंखो वालिशिखस्तथा॥ निष्टानको हेमगुहो नहुष: पिङ्गलस्तथा। बाह्यकर्णो हस्तिपदस्तथा मुद्गरपिण्डकः॥ कम्बलाश्वतरौ चापि नागः कालीयकस्तथा। वृत्तसंवर्तकौ नागौ द्वौ च पद्माविति श्रुतौ॥ नागः शंखमुखश्चैव तथा कूष्माण्डकोऽपरः। क्षेमकश्च तथा नागो नागः पिण्डारकस्तथा॥ करवीरः पुष्पदंष्ट्रो बिल्वको बिल्वपाण्डुरः। मूषकादः शंखशिराः पूर्णभद्रो हरिद्रकः॥ अपराजितौ ज्योतिकश्च पन्नगः श्रीवहस्तथा। कौरव्यो धृतराष्ट्रश्च शंखपिण्डश्च वीर्यवान्॥ विरजाश्चः सुबाहुश्च शालिपिण्डश्च वीर्यवान्। हस्तिपिण्डः पिठरकः सुमुखः कौणपाशनः।.१४॥ कुठरः कुञ्जरश्चैव तथा नागः प्रभाकरः। कुमुदः कुमुदाक्षश्च तित्तिरिर्हलिकस्तथा॥ कर्दमश्च महानागो नागश्च बहुमूलकः। कर्कराकर्करौ नागौ कुण्डोदरमहोदरौ॥
en: Shesha was born first and then Vasuki. (There were born) Airavata, Takshaka, Karkotaka, Dhananjaya, Kalakeya, Mani, Purana, Pinjaraka, Elapatara, Vamana, Nila, Anila, Kalamsha, Shabala, Aryaka, Ugraka, Kalashpotaka, Sumanakhya, Dadhimukha, Vimalapindaka, Apta, Karkotaka, Shankha, Valisikha, Nisthanaka, Hemaguha, Nahusha, Pingala, Bahyakarna, Hastipada, Mudgarapindaka, Kambala, Ashvatara, Kaliyaka, Vritta, Samvartaka, Padma, Mahapadma, Shankhamukha, Kushmandaka, Kshemaka, Pindaraka, Karavira, Pushpadanshtraka, Bilvaka, Bilvapandura, Mushakada, Shankhashiras, Purnabhadra, Haridraka, Aparajita, Jyotika, Srivaha, Kauravya, Dhritarashtra, Shankhapinda, Virajas, Subahu, Shalipinda, Prabhakara, Hastipinda, Pitharaka, Sumukha, Kaunapashana, Kuthara, Kunjara, Kumuda, Kumudakshya, Tittiri, Halika, Kardama, Bahumulaka, Karakara, Akarkara, Kundodara and Mahodara.

sn: एते प्राधान्यतो नागाः कीर्तिता द्विजसत्तम। बहुत्वान्नामधेयानामितरे नानुकीर्तिताः॥
en: O best of the twice-born, I have told you the names of the chief snakes. For fear of being tedious, I have not told you the names of the rest.

sn: एतेषां प्रसवो यश्च प्रसवस्य च संततिः। असंख्येयेति मत्वा तान्न ब्रवीमि तपोधन॥
en: O Rishi, the sons and the grandsons of the snakes were innumerable, therefore, I shall not mention their names to you.

sn: बहूनीह सहस्राणि प्रयुतान्यर्बुदानि च। अशक्यान्येव संख्यातुं पन्नगानां तपोधन॥
en: O Rishi, the number of snakes defies calculation in this world. There are many thousands and millions of the snakes.

sn: शौनक उवाच आख्याता भुजगास्तात वीर्यवन्तो दुरासदाः। शापं तं तेऽभिविज्ञाय कृतवन्तः किमुत्तरम्॥
en: Shaunaka said: O child, you have told us of many greatly powerful and unconquerable serpents. What did they do after hearing of the curse?

sn: सौतिरुवाच तेषां तु भगवाञ्च्छेषः कदूं त्यक्त्वा महायशाः। उग्रं तपः समातस्थे वायुभक्षो यतव्रतः॥
en: Sauti said: Illustrious and famous Shesha, having left (his mother) Kadru, practised austere penances, living on air and rigidly observing vows.

sn: गन्धमादनमासाद्य बदर्यां च तपोरतः। गोकर्णे पुष्करारण्ये तथा हिमवतस्तटे॥
en: He practised his penances, going to Gandhamadana, Badari, Gokarna, the forest of Pushkara and the foot of the Himalayas.

sn: तेषु तेषु च पुण्येषु तीर्थेष्वायतनेषु च। एकान्तशीलो नियतः सततं विजितेन्द्रियः॥
en: He passed his days in these sacred places, rigidly observing his vows, completely controlling his passions and concentrating his mind.

sn: तप्यमानं तपो घोरं तं ददर्श पितामहः। संशुष्कमांसत्वक्स्नायुं जटाचीरधरं मुनिम्॥
en: The Grandsire saw him with knotted hair, clad in rags, his flesh, skin and sinews dried up owing to the austere penances he was practising.

sn: तमब्रवीत्सत्यधृतिं तप्यमानं पितामहः। किमिदं कुरुषे शेष प्रजानां स्वस्ति वै कुरु॥
en: The Grandsire, addressing that penancepractising ascetic, said, “O Shesha, what are you doing? let the welfare of the worlds also engage your thoughts.

sn: त्वं हि तीव्रण तपसा प्रजास्तापयसेऽनघ। ब्रूहि कामं च मे शेष यस्ते हृदि व्यवस्थितः॥
en: O sinless one, you are giving pain to all creatures by your austere penances. O Shesha, tell me the desire of your mind."

sn: शेष उवाच सोदर्या मम सर्वे हि भ्रातरो मन्दचेतसः। सह तै!त्सहे वस्तुं तद्भवाननुमन्यताम्॥
en: Shesha said: My brothers are all of wicked hearts. I do not wish to live with them. Kindly sanction this.

sn: अभ्यसूयन्ति सततं परस्परममित्रवत्। ततोऽहं तप आतिष्ठं नैतान्पश्येयमित्युत॥
en: They are jealous of one another like great enemies. I am, therefore, engaged in penances. I shall not even see them.

sn: न मर्षयन्ति ससुतां सततं विनतां च ते। अस्माकं चापरो भ्राता वैनतेयोऽन्तरिक्षगः॥
en: They never show any kindness for Vinata and her son, who is our other brother, the bird of the air.

sn: तं च द्विषन्ति सततं स चापि बलवत्तरः। वरप्रदानात्स पितुः कश्यपस्य महात्मनः॥
en: They always envy him. He too is much stronger than (all of us), owing to the boon granted by our father, the illustrious and noble Kashyapa.

sn: सोऽहं तपः समास्थाय मोक्ष्यामीदं कलेवरम्। कथं मे प्रेत्यभावेऽपि न तैः स्यात्सहसंगमः॥
en: Therefore, I am practising penances and I shall cast off this body of mine, so that I may not any association with them even after death.

sn: सौतिरुवाच तमेवं वादिनं शेषं पितामह उवाच ह। जानामि शेष सर्वेषां भ्रातृणां ते विचेष्टितम्॥
en: Sauti said : When Shesha thus spoke, the Grandsire told him, "O Shesha, I know the character of your brothers.

sn: मातुश्चाप्यपराधाद्वै भ्रातृणां ते महद्भयम्। कृतोऽत्र परिहारश्च पूर्वमेव भुजंगम॥
en: (And I know also) their great danger owing to their offence against their mother. O snake, a remedy has been already provided by me.

sn: भ्रातृणां तव सर्वेषां न शोकं कर्तुमर्हसि। वृणीष्व च वरं मत्तः शेष यत्तेऽभिकांक्षितम्॥
en: You should not grieve for your brothers. O Shesha, whatever you desire to possess, ask it from me.

sn: दास्यामि हि वरं तेऽद्य प्रीतिर्मेपरमा त्वयि। दिष्ट्या बुद्धिश्च ते धर्मे निविष्टा पन्नगोत्तम। भूयो भूयश्च ते बुद्धिर्धर्मे भवतु सुस्थिरा॥
en: I am highly pleased with you and I shall grant you a boon today. O best of snakes, it is very good that your heart has been set on virtue. Let your heart be more and more firmly set on virtue."

sn: शेष उवाच एषः एव वरो देव कांक्षितो मे पितामह। धर्मे मे रमतां बुद्धिः शमे तपसि चेश्वर॥
en: Shesha said: Odivine Grandsire, O lord of all, I ask this boon. Let my heart always delight in virtue and in blessed penances.

sn: ब्रह्मोवाच प्रीतोऽस्यनेन ते शेष दमेन च शमेन च। त्वया त्विदं वचः कार्यं मन्नियोगात्प्रजाहितम्॥ त्वं शेष सम्यक्
en: Brahma said :: O Shesha, I am highly pleased with your self-denial and love of peace. By my command let the following act be done by you for the good of all creatures.

sn: इमां महीं शैलवनोपपन्नां ससागरग्रामविहारपत्तनाम्। चलितां यथावत् संगृह्य तिष्ठस्व यथाऽचला स्यात्॥
en: Bearing properly and well, this earth which is so very unsteady, towns retreats and seas, with all her mountains and forests with her O Shesha, remain in the way as she may be steady.

sn: शेष उवाच महीपतिर्भूतपतिर्जगत्पतिः। तथा महीं धारयिताऽस्मि निश्चला प्रयच्छतां मे शिरसि प्रजापते॥
en: Shesha said: O divine lord of all creatures, O granter of boons, O lord of the earth,O the lord of every created thing, O the lord of the universe, I shall hold the earth steady, as you command. O Prajapati, place it upon my head.

sn: ब्रह्मोवाच अधो महीं गच्छ भुजंगमोत्तम स्वयं तवैषा विवरं प्रदास्यति। इमां धरां धारयता त्वया हि मे महत्प्रियं शेषकृतं भविष्यति॥
en: Brahma said: O best of snakes, go underneath the earth. She herself will make a passage for you. O Shesha, you will certainly do what is highly valued by me by holding the earth (on your head.)

sn: सौतिरुवाच तथैव कृत्वा विवरं प्रविश्य स प्रभुर्भुवो भुजगवराग्रजः स्थितः। बिभर्ति देवीं शिरसा महीमिमां समुद्रनेमिं परिगृह्य सर्वतः॥
en: Sauti said: The elder brother of the king of the snakes, entering into a hole, went to the other side of the earth. He held that goddess (earth) with her belt of seas all around her.

sn: ब्रह्मोवाच शेषोऽसि नागोत्तम धर्मदेवो महीमिमां धारयसे यदेकः। अनन्तभोगैः परिगृह्य सर्वां यथाऽहमेवं बलभिद्यथा वा॥
en: Brahma said: O Shesha, O best of snakes, you are the Dharma, because you hold the earth alone with your infinite hoods, with every thing on her, what I myself and Indra can do.

sn: सौतिरुवाच अधोभूमौ वसत्येवं नागोऽनन्तः प्रतापवान्। धारयन्वसुधामेकः शासनाद्ब्रह्मणो विभुः॥
en: Sauti said: Thus does the snake, Shesha, the greatly powerful lord Ananta, lives underneath the earth, alone supporting the world at the command of Brahma.

sn: सुपर्णं च सहायं वै भगवानमरोत्तमः। प्रादादनन्ताय तदा वैनतेयं पितामहः॥
en: Then the Grandsire, the illustrious lord of the immortals, gave Suparna (Garuda), the son of Vinata as Ananta's help.

description: Coversation of Vasuki and other snakes
sn: सौतिरुवाच मातुः सकाशात्तं शापं श्रुत्वा वै पन्नगोत्तमः। वासुकिश्चिन्तयामास शापोऽयं न भवेत्कथम्॥
en: Sauti said: The best of snakes, Vasuki, hearing the curse of his mother, pondered over how to make it abortive.

description: Coversation of Vasuki and other snakes
sn: ततः स मन्त्रयामास भ्रातृभिः सह सर्वशः। ऐरावतप्रभृतिभिः सर्वधर्मपरायणैः॥
en: He held a consultation with all his brothers, Airavata and others, who were virtuous.

description: Coversation of Vasuki and other snakes
sn: वासुकिरुवाच अयं शापो यथोद्दिष्टो विदितं वस्तथाऽनघाः। तस्य शापस्य मोक्षार्थ मन्त्रयित्वा यतामहे॥
en: Vasuki said: O sinless ones, the curse on us is well known to you. We should try to neutralise it.

description: Coversation of Vasuki and other snakes
sn: सर्वेषामेव शापानां प्रतिधातो हि विद्यते। न तु मात्राभिशप्तानां मोक्षः क्व च न विद्यते॥
en: Remedies exist for all curses, but no remedy can avail those who are cursed by their mother.

description: Coversation of Vasuki and other snakes
sn: अव्ययस्याप्रमेयस्य सत्यस्य च तथाऽग्रतः। शप्ता इत्येव मे श्रुत्वा जायते हृदि वेपथुः॥
en: Hearing that this curse was uttered before the immutable, the infinite and the true one, my heart trembles.

description: Coversation of Vasuki and other snakes
sn: नूनं सर्वविनाशोऽयमस्माकं समुपागतः। न ह्येतां सोऽव्ययो देवः शपन्तीं प्रत्यषेधयत्॥
en: Our annihilation has certainly come; otherwise the immutable Lord should have prevented our mother from uttering the curse.

description: Coversation of Vasuki and other snakes
sn: तस्मात्संमन्त्रयामोऽद्य भुजंगानामनामयम्। यथा भवेद्धि सर्वेषां मा नः कालोऽत्यगादयम्॥
en: Therefore, let us consult today how we may secure the safety of the snakes. Let us not waste time.

description: Coversation of Vasuki and other snakes
sn: सर्व एव हि न स्तावबुद्धिमन्तो विचक्षणाः। अपि मन्त्रयमाणा हि हेतुं पश्याम मोक्षणे॥
en: You are all wise and discerning. We shall all consult together and find out a means of deliverance,

description: Coversation of Vasuki and other snakes
sn: यथा नष्टं पुरा देवा गूढमग्निं गुहागतम्। यथा स यज्ञो न भवेद्यथा वापि पराभवः। जनमेजयस्य सर्पाणां विनाशकरणाय वै॥
en: As did the celestials, in the days of yore, to regain the lost Agni who had concealed himself within a cave, cave, so that the sacrifice of Janamejaya for the destruction of the snakes may not take place and so that we may not meet with our destruction.

description: Coversation of Vasuki and other snakes
sn: सौतिरुवाच तथेत्युक्त्वा ततः सर्वे काद्रवेयाः समागताः। समयं चक्रिरे तत्र मन्त्रबुद्धिविशारदाः॥
en: Sauti said: Thus addressed, all the offspring of Kadru assembled together; they were all wise in counsel and they gave their opinions (one after the other.)

description: Coversation of Vasuki and other snakes
sn: एके तत्राब्रुवन्नागा वयं भूत्वा द्विजर्षभाः। जनमेजयं तु भिक्षामो यज्ञस्ते न भवेदिति॥
en: One party said, “We shall assume the guise of Brahmana Rishis and asked Janamejaya not to hold the sacrifice.”

description: Coversation of Vasuki and other snakes
sn: अपरे त्वब्रुवन्नागास्तत्र पण्डितमानिनः। मन्त्रिणोऽस्य वयं सर्वे भविष्यामः सुसंमताः॥
en: Others, thinking themselves wise, said, "We shall all become his favourite counsellors.

description: Coversation of Vasuki and other snakes
sn: स नः प्रक्ष्यति सर्वेषु कार्येष्वर्थविनिश्चयम्। तत्र बुद्धिं प्रदास्यामो यथा यज्ञो निवर्त्यति॥
en: He will then certainly ask our advice in all things and we shall then give him such advice as may obstruct the sacrifice.

description: Coversation of Vasuki and other snakes
sn: स नो बहुमतानराजा बुध्या बुद्धिमतां वरः। यज्ञार्थं प्रक्ष्यति व्यक्तं नेति वक्ष्यामहे वयम्॥
en: The king, thinking us wise, will certainly ask our advice about his sacrifice and we shall say, "Don't hold it."

description: Coversation of Vasuki and other snakes
sn: दर्शयन्तो बहून्दोषान्प्रेत्य चेह च दारुणान्। हेतुभिः कारणैश्चैव यथा यज्ञो भवेन्न सः॥
en: We shall point him out many serious evils in this world and the next, with reasons and causes, so that the sacrifice may not take place.

description: Coversation of Vasuki and other snakes
sn: अथवाऽयमुपाध्यायः क्रतोस्तस्य भविष्यति। सर्पसत्रविधानज्ञो राजकार्यहिते रतः॥ तं गत्वा दशतां कश्चिद् भुजङ्गः स मरिष्यति। तस्मिन्मृते यज्ञकारे क्रतुः स न भविष्यति॥
en: (We can do this also); let one of the snakes by biting kill the persons, who will try to do good to the king and who will be wellacquainted with the rites of the Snake-sacrifice and who will be appointed as the sacrificial priest. And by his death, the sacrifice will not be completed.

description: Coversation of Vasuki and other snakes
sn: ये चान्ये सर्पसत्रज्ञा भविष्यन्त्यस्य चविजः। तांश्च सर्वान्दशिष्यामः कृतमेवं भविष्यति॥
en: We shall also bite those who are acquainted with the Snakes-sacrifice and who may be appointed as the Ritviks of the sacrifice. Thus we shall obtain our object."

description: Coversation of Vasuki and other snakes
sn: अपरे त्वब्रुवन्नागा धर्मात्मानो दयालवः। अबुद्धिरेषा भवतां ब्रह्महत्या न शोभनम्॥
en: Some other snakes, who were kind hearted and virtuous, said, “Your this advice is not good. It is not proper to kill Brahmanas.”

description: Coversation of Vasuki and other snakes
sn: सम्यक्सद्धर्ममूला वै व्यसने शान्तिरुत्तमा। अधर्मोत्तरता नाम कृत्स्नं व्यापादयेज्जगत्॥
en: That remedy is proper in a danger which rests on righteousness. Unrighteousness finally destroys the world.”

description: Coversation of Vasuki and other snakes
sn: अपरे त्वब्रुवन्नागाः समिद्धं जातवेदसम्। वनिर्वापयिष्यामो मेघा भूत्वा सविद्युतः॥
en: Other snakes said : “We shall extinguish the sacrificial fire by becoming clouds luminous with lightning and pouring down showers.

description: Coversation of Vasuki and other snakes
sn: स्रुग्भाण्डं निशि गत्वा च अपरे भुजगोत्तमाः। प्रमत्तानां हरन्त्वाशु विघ्न एवं भविष्यति॥
en: Other good snakes said, “Let us go in the night and steal away the vessel of the Soma. This will obstruct the sacrifice.

description: Coversation of Vasuki and other snakes
sn: यज्ञे वा भुजगास्तस्मिञ्छतशोऽथ सहस्रशः। जनान्दशन्तु वै सर्वे नैवं त्रासो भविष्यसि॥
en: Or let the snakes go in hundred and thousands to the sacrifice, bite every one and thus create a terror.

description: Coversation of Vasuki and other snakes
sn: अथवा संस्कृतं भोज्यं दूषयन्तु भुजंगमाः। स्वेन मूत्रपुरीषेण सर्वभोज्यविनाशिना॥
en: Or let the serpents defile the pure food with their urine and dung."

description: Coversation of Vasuki and other snakes
sn: अपरे त्वब्रुवंस्तत्र ऋत्विजोऽस्य भवामहे। यज्ञविघ्नं करिष्यामो दीयतां दक्षिणा इति॥
en: Others said, “Let us become the Ritviks of the king and obstruct the sacrifice by saying at the very outset, 'Give us our Dakshina."

description: Coversation of Vasuki and other snakes
sn: वश्यतां च गतोऽसौ नः करिष्यति योप्सितम्। अपरे त्वब्रुवंस्तत्र जले प्रकीडितं नृपम्॥
en: The king, being placed in our power, will do whatever we will ask him to do." Other said, “When the king will play in the waters,

description: Coversation of Vasuki and other snakes
sn: गृहमानीय बनीमः क्रतुरेवं भवेन्न सः। अपरे त्वब्रुवंस्तत्र नागाः पण्डितमानिनः॥
en: Let us carry him to our home and keep him bound, so that the sacrifice may not take place.” Others, thinking themselves wise, said,

description: Coversation of Vasuki and other snakes
sn: दशामस्तं प्रगृह्याशु कृतमेवं भविष्यति। छिन्नं मूलमनर्थानां मृते तस्मिन्भविष्यति॥
en: “Let us go to the king and bite him, so that our object may be accomplished. By his death the root of all evil will be destroyed.

description: Coversation of Vasuki and other snakes
sn: एषा नो नैष्ठिकी बुद्धिः सर्वेषामीक्षणश्रवः। अथ यन्मन्यसे राजन्दुतं तत्संविधीयताम्॥
en: O snake, that hears by the eyes, this is the final result of our deliberations. O king, do speedily what you think proper.

description: Coversation of Vasuki and other snakes
sn: इत्युक्त्वा समुदैक्षन्त वासुकिं पन्नगोत्तमम्। वासुकिश्चापि संचिन्त्य तानुवाच भुजङ्गमान्॥
en: Having said this, they all eagerly looked at the best of the snakes, Vasuki. And Vasuki, after reflecting a while, told the snakes,

description: Coversation of Vasuki and other snakes
sn: नैषा वो नैष्ठिकी बुद्धिमता कर्तु भुजंगमाः। सर्वेषामेव मे बुद्धिः पन्नगानां न रोचते॥
en: "O snakes, your this final determination does not seem worthy of adoption. The advice, that all give, are not to my liking.

description: Coversation of Vasuki and other snakes
sn: किं तत्र संविधातव्यं भवतां स्याद्धितं तु यत्। श्रेयः प्रसादनं मन्ये कश्यपस्य महात्मनः॥
en: What I suggest would be for your good! I think the favour of (our father) the illustrious Kashyapa can alone do us good.

description: Coversation of Vasuki and other snakes
sn: ज्ञातिवर्गस्य सौहार्दादात्मनश्च भुजंगमाः। न च जानाति मे बुद्धिः किंचित्कर्तुं वचो हि वः॥३३।
en: O snakes, my mind does not know which of your suggestions to adopt for the welfare of my race and mine.

description: Coversation of Vasuki and other snakes
sn: मयाहीदं विधातव्यं भवतां यद्धितं भवेत्। अनेनाहं भृशं तप्ये गुणदोषो मदाश्रयौ।॥
en: I should do that would be good to you all. It is this that makes me so anxious, for the credit and the discredit of the act will rest on me alone.

sn: सौतिरुवाच सर्पाणां तु वचः श्रुत्वा सर्वेषामिति चेति च। वासुकेश्च वचः श्रुत्वा एलापत्रोऽब्रवीदिदम्॥
en: Sauti said: Having heard the words that fell from the snakes and also what fell from Vasuki, Elapatra addressed them thus.

sn: न स यज्ञो न भविता न स राजा तथाविधः। जनमेजयः पाण्डवेयो यतोऽस्माकं महद्भयम्॥
en: "That sacrifice is not such as would be prevented and Janamejaya of the Pandava race, who is our great terror, is not such as he can be obstructed.

sn: देवेनोपहतो राजन्यो भवेदिह पूरुषः। स दैवमेवाश्रयते नान्यत्तत्र परायणम्॥
en: O King, he who is afflicted by Fate, has his recourse to Fate alone. Nothing else can be his refuge.

sn: तदिदं चैवमस्माकं भयं पन्नगसत्तमाः। दैवमेवाश्रयामोऽत्र शृणुध्वं च वचो मम॥
en: O best of the snakes, the root of our terror is Fate and therefore, Fate alone must be our refuge. Listen to what I say.

sn: अहं शापे समुत्सृष्टे समश्रौषं वचस्तदा। मातुरुत्संगमारूढो भयात्पन्नगसत्तमाः॥ देवानां पन्नगश्रेष्ठास्तीक्ष्णास्तीक्ष्णा इति प्रभो। पितामहमुपागम्य दुःखार्तानां महायुते॥
en: O best of the snakes, when that curse was uttered, I lay in fear, crouching on my mother's lap. O best of the snakes, O Lord, O snake of great splendour, I heard from that place the sorrowing gods speaking to the Grandsire saying,

sn: देवा ऊचुः का हि लब्ध्वा प्रियान्पुत्राञ्च्छपेदेवं पितामह। ऋते कद्दू तीक्ष्णरूपां देव देव तवाग्रतः॥
en: The celestials said: O Grandsire, O god of gods, who but Kadru, after getting such dear children, can curse them even in your presence!

sn: तथेति च वचस्तस्यास्त्वयाप्युक्तं पितामह। एतदिच्छामि विज्ञातुं कारणं यन्न वारिता॥
en: O Grandsire, you have also said, “Be it so." We wish to know the reason why you did not prevent her,

sn: ब्रह्मोवाच बहवः पन्नगास्तीक्ष्णा घोररूपा विषोल्बणाः। प्रजानां हितकामोऽहं न च वारितवांस्तदा।॥
en: Brahma said: The snakes have multiplied, they are cruel, terrible in form and deadly poisonous. I did not prevent Kadru (from uttering the curse) from the desire of doing good to all creatures.

sn: ये दन्दशूकाः क्षुद्राश्च पापाचारा विषोल्बणाः। तेषां विनाशो भविता न तु ये धर्मचारिणः॥
en: The poisonous serpents that have always the biting propensity, those that bite for little faults and those who are sinful, will be destroyed, but not those that are virtuous.

sn: यन्निमित्तं च भविता मोक्षस्तेषां महाभयात्। पन्नगानां निबोधध्वं तस्मिन्काले समागते॥
en: Hear, how the snakes may escape from this dreadful calamity when the time will come,

sn: यायावरकुले धीमान्भविष्यति महानृषिः। जरत्कारुरिति ख्यातस्तपस्वी नियतेन्द्रियः॥
en: There will be born in the race of Yayavaras, a great Rishi, known by the name of Jaratkaru, who will be intelligent, greatly ascetic and self-controlled.

sn: तस्य पुत्रो जरत्कारोर्भविष्यति तपोधनः। आस्तीको नाम यज्ञं स प्रतिषेत्स्यति तं तदा। तत्र मोक्ष्यन्ति भुजगा ये भविष्यन्ति धार्मिकाः॥
en: That Jaratkaru will have a son, named Astika, who will also be a great Rishi. He will put a stop to the Snake-sacrifice. Those snakes that will be virtuous will escape (from the Snake-sacrificial fire.)

sn: देवा ऊचुः स मुनिप्रवरो ब्रह्मञ्जरत्कारुर्महातपाः। कस्यां पुत्रं महात्मानं जनयिष्यति वीर्यवान्।॥
en: The celestials said : O Brahma, in whom will Jaratkaru, the foremost of the Rishis, gifted with great powers and asceticism, beget that illustrious son?

sn: ब्रह्मोवाच सनामायां सनामा स कन्यायां द्विजसत्तमः। अपत्यं वीर्यसंपन्नं वीर्यवाञ्जनयिष्यति॥
en: Brahma said: The best of Brahmanas, the greatly powerful (Jaratkaru) will beget a greatly powerful son on his wife who will bear the same name as his.

sn: वासुकेः सर्पराजस्य जरत्कारुः स्वसा किल। स तस्यां भविता पुत्रः शापान्नागांश्च मोक्ष्यति॥
en: Vasuki, the king of the snakes, has a sister, named Jaratkaru: the son I speak of will be born in her womb and he will save the snakes.

sn: एलापत्र उवाच एवमस्विति तं देवाः पितामहमथाब्रुवन्। उक्त्वैवं वचनं देवान्विरिञ्चिस्त्रिदिवं ययौ॥
en: Elapatra said : The celestials said to the Grandsire, "Be it so," and the lord Brahma, having said all this to the celestial went to heaven.

sn: सोऽहमेवं प्रपश्यामि वासुके भगिनीं तव। जरत्कारुरितिख्यातां तां तस्मै प्रतिपादय॥ भैक्षवद्धिक्षमाणाय नागानां भयशान्तये। ऋषये सुव्रतायैनामेष मोक्षः श्रुतो मया।॥
en: O Vasuki, I see before me your that sister, known by the name of Jaratkaru. To save us from this great calamity, give her as a gift to the Rishi Jaratkaru of rigid vows, who will roam about begging for a bride. This means of our safety has been heard by me.

sn: सौतिरुवाच एलापत्रवचः श्रुत्वा ते नागा द्विजसत्तम। सर्वे प्रहृष्टमनसः साधु साध्वित्यथाब्रुवन्॥
en: Sauti said : O best of the twice born, hearing what Elapatra said, all the snakes exclaimed in joy, "Well said! Excellent man!"

sn: ततः प्रभृति तां कन्यां वासुकिः पर्यरक्षत। जरत्कारुं स्वसारं वै परं हर्षमवाप च॥
en: From that day Vasuki carefully kept that maiden, his sister Jaratkaru and he took great pleasure in rearing her up.

sn: ततो नातिमहान्काल: समतीत इवाभवत्। अथ देवासुराः सर्वे ममथुर्वरुणालयम्॥
en: Not long after this, the Devas and the Asuras churned the abode of Varuna (Ocean).

sn: तत्र नेत्रमभून्नागो वासुकिर्बलिनां वरः। समाप्यैव च तत्कर्म पितामहमुपागमन्॥
en: And the greatly powerful Vasuki became its churning cord. As soon as this work was done, he approached the grandsire.

sn: देवा वासुकिना सार्धं पितामहमथाब्रुवन्। भगवञ्च्छापभीतोऽयं वासुकिस्तप्यते भृशम्॥
en: The celestial with Vasuki addressed the Grandsire thus, “O lord, Vasuki is suffering from the fear of the curse.

sn: अस्यैतन्मानसं शल्यं समुद्धर्तुं त्वमर्हसि। जनन्याः शाप देव ज्ञातीनां हितमिच्छतः॥
en: You should draw out the dart, begotten by his mother's curse, which pierces the heart of Vasuki who is desirous of the weal of his race.

sn: हितो ह्ययं सदाऽस्माकं प्रियाकारी च नागराट्। प्रसादं कुरु देवेश शमयास्य मनोज्वरम्॥
en: The king of the snakes is always our friend and benefactor; O lord of the gods, be gracious to him and remove the fever of his mind.

sn: ब्रह्मोवाच मयैव तद्वितीर्णं वै वचनं मनसाऽमराः। एलापत्रेण नागेन यदस्याभिहितं पुरा॥ तत्करोत्वेष नागेन्द्रः प्राप्तकालं वचः स्वयम्। विनशिष्यन्ति ये पापा न तु यै धर्मचारिणः॥
en: Brahma said: O immortals, I have thought in my mind what you have said. Let the king of the snakes do what Elapatra had told him before. When the time comes, the wicked only will be destroyed and not the virtuous.

sn: उत्पन्नः स जरत्कारुस्तपस्युग्रे रतो द्विजः। तस्यैष भगिनी काले जरत्कारुं प्रयच्छतु॥
en: Jaratkaru is (already) born; that Brahmana is now engaged in penances. Let him (Vasuki), at the proper time, give his sister to Jaratkaru.

sn: एलापत्रेण यत्प्रोक्तं वचनं भुजगेन ह। पन्नगानां हि तं देवास्तत्तथा न तदन्यथा॥
en: O celestials! what had been said by Elapatra for the weal of the snakes is true. It is not otherwise.

sn: सौतिरुवाच एतच्छ्रुत्वा नागेन्द्रः पितामहवचस्तदा। संदिश्य पन्नगान्सर्वान्वासुकिः शापमोहितः॥
en: Sauti said : The king of the snakes, afflicted with the curse, having heard what the Grandsire said, commanded all the snakes,

sn: स्वसारमुद्यम्य तदा जरत्कारुमृषि प्रति। सर्पान्बहूञ्जरत्कारौ नित्ययुक्तान्समादधत्॥
en: A large number of them who are always attentive to their duties, to watch the Rishi Jaratkaru. He said,

sn: जरत्कारुर्यदा भार्यामिच्छेद्वरयितुं प्रभुः। शीघ्रमेत्य तदाख्येयं तन्नः श्रेयो भविष्यति॥
en: "When the Lord Jaratkaru will ask for a wife, come immediately and inform me of it. The weal of our race depends upon it.”

description: Asceticism of Jaratkaru, King keeps dead snake on shoulder of Rishi
sn: शौनक उवाच जरत्कारुरिति ख्यातो यस्त्वया सूतनन्दन। इच्छामि तदहं श्रोतुं ऋषेस्तस्य महात्मनः॥ किं कारणं जरत्कारो मैतत्प्रथितं भुवि। जरत्कारुनिरुक्तिं त्वं यथावद्वक्तुमर्हसि॥
en: Shaunaka said : O son of Suta, I desire to know why the illustrious Rishi whom you call Jaratkaru came to be so called. You should tell us the Etymology of the name of Jaratkaru.

description: Asceticism of Jaratkaru, King keeps dead snake on shoulder of Rishi
sn: सौतिरुवाच जरेति क्षयमाहुर्वै दारुणं कारुसंज्ञितम्। शरीरं कारु तस्यासीत्तत्स धीमाञ्च्छनैः शनैः॥ क्षपयामास तीव्रण तपसेत्यत उच्यते। जरत्कारुरिति ब्रह्मन्वासुकेर्भगिनी तथा॥
en: Sauti said: Jara, means “waste" Karu means “huge." The body of this Rishi was huge, but he reduced it by severe penances. O Brahmana, because he thus reduced his body, he was called Jaratkaru. The sister of Vasuki was called Jaratkaru for the same reason.

description: Asceticism of Jaratkaru, King keeps dead snake on shoulder of Rishi
sn: एवमुक्तस्तु धर्मात्मा शौनकः प्राहसत्तदा। उग्रश्रवसमामन्त्र्य उपपन्नमिति ब्रुवन्॥
en: When the pious Shaunaka heard this, he smiled and addressing Ugrashrava (Sauti) said, “It is true."

description: Asceticism of Jaratkaru, King keeps dead snake on shoulder of Rishi
sn: शौनक उवाच उक्तं नाम यथापूर्वं सर्वं तच्छ्रुतवानहम्। यथा तु जातो ह्यास्तीक एतदिच्छामि वेदितुम्। तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं तस्य सूतः प्रोवाच शास्त्रतः॥
en: Shaunaka said : I have heard all that you have narrated. Now I wish to hear how Astika was born.

description: Asceticism of Jaratkaru, King keeps dead snake on shoulder of Rishi
sn: सौतिरुवाच संदिश्य पन्नगान्सर्वान्वासुकिः सुसमाहितः। स्वसारमुद्यम्य तदा जरत्कारुमृषि प्रति॥
en: Sauti said : Vasuki, wishing to bestow his sister on Rishi Jaratkaru, gave the snakes (all necessary) orders.

description: Asceticism of Jaratkaru, King keeps dead snake on shoulder of Rishi
sn: अथ कालस्य महत: स मुनिः संशितव्रतः। तपस्यभिरतो धीमान्स दारानाभ्यकांक्षत॥
en: Many years rolled away, but the Rishi of rigid vows, deeply engaged in ascetic devotions, did not seek for a wife.

description: Asceticism of Jaratkaru, King keeps dead snake on shoulder of Rishi
sn: स तूर्ध्वरेतास्तपसि प्रसक्तः स्वाध्यायवान्वीतभयः कृतात्मा। चचार सर्वां पृथिवीं महात्मा न चापि दारान्मनसाध्यकांक्षत॥
en: That high-souled Rishi, his sexual passion completely under control, engaged in deep study and devoted to rigid asceticism, fearlessly roamed over the world, having no desire for a wife.

description: Asceticism of Jaratkaru, King keeps dead snake on shoulder of Rishi
sn: ततो परस्मिन्संप्राप्ते काले कस्मिंश्चिदेव तु। परिक्षिन्नाम राजासीद्ब्रह्मन्कौरववंशजः॥
en: O Brahmana, once upon a time there was a king, named Parikshit, born in the race of the Kurus.

description: Asceticism of Jaratkaru, King keeps dead snake on shoulder of Rishi
sn: यथा पाण्डुर्महाबाहुर्धनुर्धरवरो युधि। वभूब मृगयाशील: पुराऽस्य प्रपितामहः॥
en: He was like his great grandfather, Pandu, mighty in arms, the best of all bow-men in battle and was very fond of hunting.

description: Asceticism of Jaratkaru, King keeps dead snake on shoulder of Rishi
sn: मृगान्विध्यन्वराहांश्च तरशून्महिषांस्तथा। अन्यांश्च विविधान्वन्यांश्चचार पृथिवीपतिः॥
en: That king of the world roamed about, hunting deer, wild boars, hyena and buffaloes and various other wild animals.

description: Asceticism of Jaratkaru, King keeps dead snake on shoulder of Rishi
sn: स कदाचिन्मृगं विध्वा बाणेनानतपर्वणा। पृष्ठतो धनुरादाय ससार गहने वने॥
en: One day, having pierced a deer with an arrow, he slang his bow on his back and following it, he entered into a deep forest.

description: Asceticism of Jaratkaru, King keeps dead snake on shoulder of Rishi
sn: यथैव भगवान्रुद्रो विध्वा यज्ञमृगं दिवि। अन्वगच्छद्धनुष्पाणि: पर्यन्वेष्टुमितस्ततः॥
en: He searched for it in the forest here and there, as Rudra did in heaven for the sacrificial deer which was pierced with his arrow.

description: Asceticism of Jaratkaru, King keeps dead snake on shoulder of Rishi
sn: न हि तेन मृगो विद्धो जीवन्गच्छति वै वने। पूर्वरूपं तु तत्तूर्णं सोऽगात्स्वर्गगति प्रति॥
en: Never had a deer, pierced by Parikshit, escaped in the forest with life. This deer, however, wounded as the others, fled away with speed. It shows the proximity of the king's going to heaven (death).

description: Asceticism of Jaratkaru, King keeps dead snake on shoulder of Rishi
sn: परिक्षितो नरेन्द्रस्य विद्धो यन्नष्टवान्मृगः। दूरं चापहृतस्तेन मृगेण स महीपतिः॥
en: The deer, that the king of men, Parikshit wounded, was soon lost out of his sight and the king went in pursuit it far into the forest.

description: Asceticism of Jaratkaru, King keeps dead snake on shoulder of Rishi
sn: परिश्रान्तः पिपासात आससाद मुनि वने। गवां प्रचारेष्वासीनं वत्सानां मुखनिःसृतम्॥ भूयिष्ठमुपयुञ्जानं फेनमापिबतां पयः। तमभिद्रुत्य वेगेन स राजा संशितव्रतम्॥ अपृच्छद्धनुरुद्यम्य तं मुनि क्षुच्छ्रमान्वितः। भो भो ब्रह्मन्नहं राजा परीक्षिदभिमन्युजः॥
en: Fatigued and thirsty he came upon a Rishi, in the forest, seated in a cow-shed, drinking the froth oozing out of the mouths of the calves sucking the milk of their mothers. Coming to him with all haste, the king asked that Rishi of great austerity, O Brahmana, I am king Parikshit, the son of Abhimanyu.

description: Asceticism of Jaratkaru, King keeps dead snake on shoulder of Rishi
sn: मया विद्धो मृगो नष्टः कच्चित्तं दृष्टवानसि। स मुनिस्तं तु नोवाच किंचिन्मौनव्रते स्थितः॥
en: Have you seen where the deer pierced by me has gone? But the Rishi, observing the vow of silence, did not reply to him.

description: Asceticism of Jaratkaru, King keeps dead snake on shoulder of Rishi
sn: तस्य स्कन्धे मृतं सर्प क्रुद्धो राजा समासजत्। समुत्क्षिप्य धनुष्कोट्या स चैनं समुपेक्षत॥
en: The king being angry took up a dead snake with the end of his bow and placed it round the neck of the Rishi, but the Rishi did not prevent him from doing it.

description: Asceticism of Jaratkaru, King keeps dead snake on shoulder of Rishi
sn: न स किंचिदुवाचैनं शुभं वा यदि वाऽशुभम्। स राजा क्रोधमुत्सृज्य व्यथितस्तं तथागतम्। दृष्ट्वा जगाम नगरमृषिस्त्वासीत्तथैव सः॥ नहि तं राजशार्दूलं क्षमाशीलो महामुनिः। स्वधर्मनिरतं भूपं समाक्षिप्तोऽप्यधर्षयत्॥
en: He did not even say a word, either good or bad. Seeing him in that state, the king cast off his anger and became very sorry. He went away to his capital and the Rishi remained as he was. The forgiving great Rishi knowing him, that best of kings,

description: Asceticism of Jaratkaru, King keeps dead snake on shoulder of Rishi
sn: न हि तं राजशार्दूलस्तथा धर्मपरायणम्। जानाति भरतश्रेष्ठस्तत एनमधर्षयत्॥ तरुणस्तस्य पुत्रोऽभूत्तिग्मतेजा महातपाः।
en: To be true to the duties of his order, did not curse him. That best of kings, the best of the Bharata race, also did not know that the Rishi was a virtuous man. It is for this that he thus insulted him. This Rishi had a young, greatly powerful and exceedingly ascetic son,

description: Asceticism of Jaratkaru, King keeps dead snake on shoulder of Rishi
sn: शृंगी नाम महाक्रोधो दुष्प्रसादो महाव्रतः। स देवं परमासीनं सर्वभूतहिते रतम्॥ ब्रह्माणमुपतस्थे वै काले काले सुसंयतः। स तेन समनुज्ञातो ब्रह्मणा गृहमेयिवान्॥
en: Who was named Shringi. He was full of wrath, severe in his vows and difficult to be appeased. He sometimes worshipped with great attention his (preceptor) Brahma, seated on his seat and ever engaged in doing good to all creatures. Commanded by him, he was coming home one day.

description: Asceticism of Jaratkaru, King keeps dead snake on shoulder of Rishi
sn: सख्योक्तः क्रीडमानेन स तत्र हसता किल। संरंभात्कोपनोऽतीव विषकल्पो मुनेः सुतः॥ उद्दिश्य पितरं तस्य यच्छ्रुत्वा रोषमाहरत्। ऋषिपुत्रेण धर्मार्थे कृशेन द्विजसत्तम॥
en: When his friend (Krisha) in a playful mood, laughingly spoke to him about his father, the Rishi's son, ever wrathful and like poison itself, hearing what had happened to his father, blazed up in a rage.

description: Asceticism of Jaratkaru, King keeps dead snake on shoulder of Rishi
sn: कृश उवाच तेजस्विनस्तव पिता तथैव च तपस्विनः। शवं स्कन्धेन वहति मा शृङ्गिगवितो भव॥
en: Krisha said: O Shringi, do not be proud. Ascetic as you are and possessed of great powers, (go and see) your father who is carrying a dead body (on his shoulder),

description: Asceticism of Jaratkaru, King keeps dead snake on shoulder of Rishi
sn: व्याहरत्स्वृषिपुत्रेषु मा स्म किंचिद्वचो वद। अस्मद्विधेषु सिद्धेषु ब्रह्मवित्सु तपस्विषु॥
en: Don't speak with the sons of the Rishis like ourselves, who are deep in asceticism, who have knowledge of truth and who have attained Success.

description: Asceticism of Jaratkaru, King keeps dead snake on shoulder of Rishi
sn: क्व ते पुरुषमानित्वं क्व ते वाचस्तथाविधाः। दर्पजाः पितरं द्रष्ट्वा यस्त्वं शवधरं तथा॥
en: Where is your that manliness and where are your those proud words, when you see your father carrying a dead snake?

description: Asceticism of Jaratkaru, King keeps dead snake on shoulder of Rishi
sn: पित्रा च तव तत्कर्म नानुरूपमिवात्मनः। कृतं मुनिजनश्रेष्ठ येनाहं भृशदुःखितः॥
en: O best of Rishis, your father did nothing to meet with this treatment. I am pained as if it has been done to me.

sn: सौतिरुवाच एवमुक्तः स तेजस्वी श्रृंगी कोप समन्वितः मृतधारं गुरुं श्रुत्रा पर्यतप्यत मन्युना॥
en: Sauti said: Being thus addressed and having heard that his father was bearing a dead snake, the powerful Shringi grew exceedingly angry.

sn: स तं कृशमभिप्रेक्ष्य सूनृतां वाचमुत्सृजन्। अपृच्छत्तं कथं तातः स मेऽद्य मृतधारकः॥
en: Looking at Krisha, he softly asked him, “Why does my father bear a dead snake?”

sn: कृश उवाच राज्ञा परिक्षिता तात मृगयां परिधावता। अवसक्तः पितुस्तेऽद्य मृतः स्कन्धे भुजंगमः॥
en: Krisha said: O dear friend, when Parikshit was roving for the purpose of hunting, he placed the dead snake of the shoulder of your father.

sn: शृंग्युवाच किं मे पित्रा कृतं तस्य राज्ञोऽनिष्टं दुरात्मनः। ब्रूहि तत्कृश तत्त्वेन पश्य मे तपसो बलम्॥
en: Shringi said : What harm was done by my father to that miscreant king? Tell me this, O Krisha and (you will then) see my ascetic powers.

sn: कृश उवाच स राजा मृगयां यातः परिक्षितभिमन्युजः। ससार मृगमेकाकी विद्ध्वा बाणेन शीघ्रगम्॥
en: Krisha said: King Parikshit, the son of Abhimanyu, having wounded a fleet stag with an arrow while hunting, chased it alone.

sn: न चापश्यन्मृगं राजा चरंस्तस्मिन्महावने। पितरं ते स दृष्ट्वैव पप्रच्छानभिभाषिणम्॥
en: He lost sight of the stag in the wilderness of the forest and seeing your father he accosted him.

sn: तं स्थाणुभूतं तिष्ठन्तं क्षुत्पिपासाश्रमातुरः। पुनः पुनर्पगं नष्टं पप्रच्छ पितरं तव॥
en: But he (your father) was then observing the vow of silence. Oppressed by hunger, thirst and fatigue, the king repeatedly asked your father about the missing deer.

sn: स च मौनव्रतोयेतो नैवं तं प्रत्यभाषत। तस्य राजा धनुष्कोट्या सर्प स्कन्धे समासजत्॥
en: But the Rishi, being then under the vow of silence, did not make any reply. Thereupon the king, becoming angry, placed the snake on his shoulder, taking it up with the end of his bow.

sn: शृंगिस्तव पिता सोऽपि तथैवास्ते यतव्रतः। सोऽपि राजा स्वनगरं प्रस्थितो गजसाह्वयम्॥
en: O Shringi, your father, engaged in devotion, is still in that posture. The king has, however, gone away to his capital (Hastinapur), named after the elephant.

sn: सौतिरुवाच श्रुत्वैवमृषिपुत्रस्तु शवं स्कन्धे प्रतिष्ठितम्। कोपसंरक्तनयनः प्रज्वलन्निव मन्युना॥
en: Sauti said : Having heard that a dead snake had been placec. on his father's shoulder, the Rishi's son looked like a blazing fire, his eyes reddened with anger.

sn: आविष्टः स हि कोपेन शशाप नृपतिं तदा। वायुपस्पृश्य तेजस्वी क्रोधवेगबलात्कृतः॥
en: Inflamed with anger, the powerful Rishi, touching water, cursed the king thus,

sn: शृङ्गयुवाच योऽसौ वृद्धस्य तातस्य तथा कृच्छ्रगतस्य ह। स्कन्धे मृतं समानाक्षीत्पन्नगः राजकिल्बिषी॥ तं पापमतिसंक्रुद्धस्तक्षकः पन्नगेश्वरः। आशीविषस्तिग्मतेजा मद्वाक्यबलचोदितः॥ सप्तरात्रादितो नेता यमस्य सदनं प्रति। द्विजानामवमन्तारं कुरूणामयशस्करम्॥
en: Shringi said : He who has placed the dead snake on the shoulder of my old and lean father, that miscreant of a king, that insulter of the Brahmanas, the destroyer of the fame of the Kuru race, will be taken within seven days from to-day to the land of Yama: by the snake Takshaka, the powerful king of the serpents, stimulated by my words.

sn: सौतिरुवाच इति शप्त्वाऽतिसंक्रुद्धः शृंगी पितरमभ्यगात्। आसीनं गोव्रजे तस्मिन्वहन्तं शवपन्नगम्॥
en: Sauti said: Having thus cursed the king from anger, Shringi went to his father and saw that he was sitting in the cow-shed, the dead snake (was still) on his shoulder.

sn: स तमालक्ष्य पितरं शृङ्गी स्कन्धगतेन वै। शवेन भुजगेनासीद्भूयः क्रोधसमाकुलः॥
en: Seeing that the dead snake was on the shoulder of his father, he was again inflamed with anger.

sn: दुःखाच्चाश्रूणि मुमुचे पितरं चेदमब्रवीत्। श्रुत्वेमां धर्षणां तात तव तेन दुरात्मना॥
en: He shed tears in grief; and addressed his father thus, “O father, hearing the insult offered to you by the miscreant,

sn: राज्ञा परिक्षिता कोपादशपन्तमहं नृपम्। यथार्हति स एवोगं शापं कुरुकुलाधमः। सप्तमेऽहनि तं पापं तक्षकः पन्नगोत्तमः॥ वैवस्वतस्य सदन नेता परमदारुणम्। तमब्रवीत्पिता ब्रह्मस्तथा कोपसमन्वितम्॥
en: King Parikshit, I have cursed him from। anger, that wretch of the Kurus richly deserves। my potent curse. Within seven days from this date the king of snakes, Takshaka will take the sinner to the fearful house of Death." And the father said to the enraged son,

sn: शमीक उवाच न मे प्रियं कृतं तात नैष धर्मस्तपस्विनाम्। वयं तस्य नरेन्द्रस्य विषये निवसामहे॥
en: Shamika said: O child, I am not pleased with your act. It is not proper for ascetics to act thus. We live in the domains of that king.

sn: न्यायतो रक्षितास्तेन तस्य पापं न रोचये। सर्वथा वर्तमानस्य राज्ञो ह्यस्मद्विधैः सदा॥
en: We are righteously protected by him and therefore, we should not mind his faults, The reigning kings should always be pardoned by men like us.

sn: क्षन्तव्यं पुत्रधर्मो हि हतो हन्ति न संशयः। यदि राजा न संरक्षेत्पीडा नः परमा भवेत्॥
en: O son, if you destroy Dharma, (piety), Dharma will certainly destroy you. If the king. does not protect us, we meet with many afflictions. was

sn: न शक्नुयाम चरितुं धर्म पुत्र यथासुखम्। रक्ष्यमाणा वयं तात राजभिर्धर्मदृष्टिभिः॥२३.।
en: O son, we cannot then perform our religious rites as we desire. Protected by virtuous kings,

sn: चरामो विपुलं धर्मं तेषां भागोऽस्ति धर्मतः। सर्वथा वर्तमानस्य राज्ञः क्षन्तव्यमेव हि॥
en: We achieve great merits; and a share of it always goes to such kings. Therefore, reigning kings are always to be forgiven;

sn: परिक्षित्तु विशेषेण यथाऽस्य प्रपितामहः। रक्षत्यस्मांस्तथा राज्ञा रक्षितव्याः प्रजा विभो॥
en: Specially Parikshit, who, like his great grandfather, protects us as a king should protect his subjects.

sn: तेनेह क्षुधितेनाद्य श्रान्तेन च तपस्विना। अजानता कृतं मन्ये व्रतमेतदिदं मम॥
en: That penance-practising king oppressed by hunger and thirst and he did not know that I was observing the vow of silence.

sn: अराजके जनपदे दोषा जायन्ति वै सदा। उद्वृत्तं सततं लोकं राजा दण्डेन शास्ति वै॥
en: Disasters always befall on a country where there is no king. The king punishes those who grow wicked.

sn: दण्डात्प्रतिभयं भूयः शान्तिरुत्पद्यते तदा। नोद्विग्नश्चरते धर्मं नोद्विग्नश्चरते क्रियाम्॥
en: The fear of punishment brings in peace and men thus perform their duties and their rites undisturbed.

sn: राज्ञा प्रतिष्ठितो धर्मो धर्मात्स्वर्गः प्रतिष्ठितः। राज्ञो यज्ञक्रियाः सर्वा यज्ञाद्देवाः प्रतिष्ठिता॥
en: The king establishes dharma, and by dharma, one gains the kingdom of heaven. The king protects all sacrifices and the sacrifices please the celestials;

sn: देवावृष्टिः प्रवर्तेत वृष्टेरोषधयः स्मृताः। ओषधिभ्यो मनुष्याणां धारयन्सततं हितम्॥
en: The celestials cause rain and rain produces medicinal herbs; the medicinal herbs do immense good to mankind.

sn: मनुष्याणां च यो धाता राजा राज्यकरः पुनः। दशश्रोत्रियसमो राजा इत्येवं मनुरब्रवीत्॥
en: Manu said, “The ruler of the destiny of is equal to ten Veda-knowing Brahmanas.'

sn: तेनेह क्षुधितेनाद्य श्रान्तेन च तपस्विना। अजानता कृतं मन्ये व्रतमेतदिदं मम॥
en: That penance-observing king, oppressed by hunger and thirst, has done this through ignorance of my vow.

sn: कस्मादिदं त्वया बाल्यात्सहसा दुष्कृतं कृतम्। न हर्हति नृपः शापमस्मत्तः पुत्र सर्वथा॥
en: Why have you, through childishness, done rashly this unrighteous action? O son, that king in no way deserves a curse from us.

sn: शृङ्गयुवाच यद्येतत्साहसं तात यदि वा दुष्कृतं कृतम्। प्रियं वाऽप्यप्रियं वा ते वागुक्ता न मृषा भवेत्॥
en: Shringi said : O father, whether my act was rash oi improper, whether you like it or dislike it, the words spoken by me shall never be vain.

sn: नैवान्यथेदं भविता पितरेष ब्रवीमि ते। नाहं मृषा ब्रवीम्येवं स्वैरेष्वपि कुतः शपन्॥
en: O father, I tell you, this can never be otherwise. I have never spoken a lie even in jest.

sn: शमीक उवाच जानाम्युग्रप्रभावं त्वां तात सत्यगिरं तथा। नानृतं चोक्तपूर्वं ते नैतन्मिथ्या भविष्यति॥
en: Shamika said: My child, I know, you are greatly powerful and you are very truthful. You have never spoken a falsehood in your life and therefore your curse will never be false.

sn: पित्रा पुत्रो वयःस्थोऽपि सततं वाच्य एव तु। यथा स्याद्गुणसंयुक्तः प्राप्नुयाच्च महद्यशः॥
en: But the son, even he is grown up, should always be advised by his father, so that adorned with good qualities, he may earn great renown.

sn: किं पुनर्बाल एव त्वं तपसा भावितः सदा। वर्धते च प्रभवतां कोपोऽतीव महात्मनाम्॥
en: You are mere child and therefore, how much more do you stand in need of counsel! You are always engaged in asceticism. Even the anger of illustrious and high-souled men increases with the increase of their powers.

sn: सोऽहं पश्यामि वक्तव्यं त्वयि धर्मभूतां वर। पुत्रत्वं बालता चैव तवावेक्ष्य च साहसम्॥
en: O best of pious men, considering that you are my son and a mere boy and seeing your rashness, I see I must give you advice.

sn: स त्वं शमपरो भूत्वा वन्यमाहारमाचरन्। चर क्रोधमिमं हत्वा नैवं धर्मं प्रहास्यसि॥
en: Live, O son, having your mind inclined to peace; live on fruits and roots of the forest. Destroy your anger; but do not destroy the fruits of your asceticism (by giving vent to anger).

sn: क्रोधो हि धर्मं हरति यतीनां दुःखसंचितम्। ततो धर्मविहीनानां गतिरिष्टां न विद्यते॥
en: Anger diminishes the merits that ascetics acquire with great pains. There is no hope for those who are deprived of virtue.

sn: शम एव यतीनां हि क्षमिणां सिद्धिकारकः। क्षमावतामयं लोकः परश्चैव क्षमावताम्॥
en: Peacefulness produces success to the forgiving ascetics. Good come to the forgiving men, both in this world and in the next.

sn: तस्माच्चरेथाः सततं क्षमाशीलो जितेन्द्रियः। क्षमया प्राप्स्यसे लोकान्ब्रह्मणः समनन्तरान्॥
en: Therefore, you should always live, being forgiving in your temper and self-controlling of your passions. By forgiveness you will attain to worlds that are beyond the reach of even Brahma.

sn: मया तु शममास्थाय यच्छक्यं कर्तुमद्य वै। तत्करिष्याम्यहं तात प्रेषयिष्ये नृपाय वै॥
en: O my son, having adopted peacefulness, I shall do as much as lies in my power. I shall do this. I shall send word to the king, telling him,

sn: मम पुत्रेण शप्तोऽसि बालेन कृशबुद्धिना। ममेमां धर्षणां त्वत्तः प्रेक्ष्य राजन्नमर्षिणा॥
en: "O king, you have been cursed by my son, who is a mere child and whose intellect is not yet developed. Seeing your disrespect towards me, (he has done this) in anger."

sn: सौतिरुवाच एवमादिश्य शिष्यं स प्रेषयामास सुव्रतः। परिक्षिते नृपतये दयापन्नो महातपाः॥
en: Sauti said : That great ascetic, observant of vows, moved by kindness, sent a disciple to Parikshit with proper instructions,

sn: संदिश्य कुशलप्रश्नं कार्यवृत्तान्तमेव च। शिष्यं गौरमुखं नाम शीलवन्तं समाहितम्॥
en: He sent his disciple, named Gauramukha, a young man of good manners and of ascetic penances, instructing him to enquire first about the welfare of the king and then to communicate the real business.

sn: सोऽभिगम्य ततः शीघ्रं नरेन्द्रं कुरुवर्धनम्। विवेश भवनं राज्ञः पूर्वं द्वास्थैर्निवेदितः॥
en: Going (to Hastinapur) he soon came to the king, the head of the Kuru race. He entered the king's palace, having first sent the notice of his arrival through gate-keeper.

sn: पूजितस्तु नरेन्द्रेण द्विजो गौरमुखस्तदा। आचख्यौ च परिश्रान्तो राज्ञः सर्वमशेषतः॥ शमीकवचनं घोरं यथोक्तं मन्त्रिसन्निधौ।
en: The Brahmana, Gaurmukha, was received in all honours. And then after resting for a while, he told the king in the presence of his ministers, the terrible words of Shamika, exactly as he was instructed.

sn: गौरमुख उवाच शमीको नाम राजेन्द्र वर्तते विषये तव॥ ऋषिः परमधर्मात्मा दान्तः शान्तो महातपाः। तस्य त्वया नरव्याघ्र सर्पः प्राणैर्वियोजितः॥ तक्षकः सप्तरात्रेण अवसक्तो धनुष्कोट्या स्कन्धे मौनान्वितस्य च। क्षान्तवांस्तव तत्कर्म पुत्रस्तस्य न चक्षमे॥
en: Gaurmukha said : O king of kings, there lives within your dominions, a Rishi, named Shamika. He is greatly virtuous, very peaceful, his passions under control and a great ascetic. O best of men, a dead snake was placed by you with the end of your bow on the shoulder of this Rishi who was then observing the vow of silence. He himself forgave the act, but his son did not.

sn: तेन शप्तोऽसि राजेन्द्र पितुरज्ञातमद्य वै। मृत्युस्तव भविष्यति॥
en: O king of kings, you have been to-day cursed by him without the knowledge of his father. Takshaka will be your death after seven nights from this day.

sn: तत्र रक्षां कुरुष्वेति पुनः पुनस्थाऽब्रवीत्। तदन्यथा न शक्यं च कर्तुं केनचिदप्युत॥
en: Shamika repeatedly asked his son to save you, but there is none to falsify his curse.

sn: न हि शक्नोति तं यन्तुं पुत्रं कोपसमन्वितम्। ततोऽहं प्रेषितस्तेन तव राजन्हितार्थिना॥
en: As he has been unable to pacify his angry son, therefore, O king, I have been sent by him to you for your good.

sn: सौतिरुवाच इति श्रुत्वा वचो घोरं स राजा कुरुनन्दनः। पर्यतप्यत तत्पापं कृत्वा राजा महातपाः॥
en: Sauti said : Having heard these terrible words and recollecting his own sinful act, the king, the descendant of the Kuru race, a great ascetic himself, grew exceedingly sorry.

sn: तं च मौनव्रतं श्रुत्वा वने मुनिवरं तदा। भूय एवाभवद्राजा शोकसंतप्तमानसः॥
en: Having heard that the best of the Rishi (Shamika) had been observing the vow of silence, he was doubly afflicted with sorrow.

sn: अनुक्रोशात्मतां तस्य शमीकस्यावधार्य च। पर्यतप्यत भूयोऽपि कृत्वा तत्किल्बिषं मुनेः॥
en: Seeing also the great kindness shown to him by the Rishi and recollecting his own great act, the king became very penitent.

sn: न हि मृत्युं तथा राजा श्रुत्वा वै सोऽन्वतप्यत। अशोचदमरप्रख्यो यथा कृत्वेह कर्म तत्॥
en: The king, who looked like a celestial, did not grieve so much for hearing that he would die, as for having done that (insulting) act to the Rishi.

sn: ततस्तं प्रेषयामास राजा गौरमुखं तदा। भूयः प्रसादं भगवान्करोत्विह ममेति वै॥
en: The king then sent away Gaurmukha, saying "Let the adored Rishi be gracious to me!”

sn: तस्मिंश्च गतमात्रेऽथ राजा गौरमुखे तदा। मन्त्रिभिर्मन्त्रयामास सह संविग्नमानसः॥
en: When Gaurmukha had gone away the king in great anxiety consulted with all his ministers without delay.

sn: संमन्त्र्य मन्त्रिभिश्चैव स तथा मन्त्रतत्त्ववित्। प्रासादं कारयामास एकं स्तम्भं सुरक्षितम्॥
en: Having consulted with his ministers, the king himself, wise in counsels, caused a palace to be erected on a pillar, guarded day and night by men.

sn: रक्षां च विदधे तत्र भिषजश्चौषधानि च। ब्राह्मणान्मन्त्रसिद्धांश्च सर्वतो वै न्ययोजयत्॥
en: For his protection, he placed all around the palace, physicians, medicines and Brahmanas skilled in Mantras.

sn: राजकार्याणिः तत्रस्थः सर्वाण्येवाकरोच्च सः। मन्त्रिभिः सह धर्मज्ञः समन्तात्परिरक्षितः॥
en: Thus being protected on all sides, the king discharged his royal duties, surrounded by his virtuous ministers.

sn: न चैनं कश्चिदारूढं लभते राजसत्तमम्। वातोऽपि निश्चरंस्तत्र प्रवेशे विनिवार्यते॥
en: None could approach that best of kings there (in that palace.) Even air could not go there, being prevented from entering.

sn: प्राप्ते च दिवसे तस्मिन्सप्तमे द्विजसत्तमः। काश्यपोऽभ्यागमद्विद्वांस्तं राजानं चिकित्सितुम्॥
en: When the seventh day came, the best of Brahmanas, Kashyapa, was coming with the intention of treating the king, (if bitten by the snake).

sn: श्रुतं हि तेन तदभूद्यथा तं राजसत्तमम्। तक्षकः पन्नगश्रेष्ठो नेष्यते यमसादनम्॥
en: He had heard all that had happened; he had heard that the best of snakes, Takshaka would take the king to Yama's, abode.

sn: तं दष्टं पन्नगेन्द्रेण करिष्येऽहमपज्वरम्। तत्र मेऽर्थश्च धर्मश्च भवितेति विचिन्तयन्॥
en: He thought, “I will cure the king bitten by the best of the snakes. By this I may gain both wealth and virtue."

sn: तं ददर्श स नागेन्द्रस्तक्षकः काश्यपं पथि। गच्छन्तमेकमनसं द्विजो भूत्वा वयोतिगः॥
en: The king of the snakes, Takshaka, saw on the way, Kashyapa, going with the intention of curing the king. He appeared before him in the form of an old Brahmana.

sn: तमब्रवीत्पन्नगेन्द्रः काश्यपं मुनिपुंगवम्। क्व भवांस्त्वरितो याति किं च कार्यं चिकीर्षति॥
en: Thereupon the king of the snakes spoke to the best of the Rishis, Kashyapa, saying, “Where are you going with such speed? What is the business upon which you are going

sn: काश्यप उवाच नृपं कुरुकुलोत्पन्न परिक्षितमरिन्दमम्। तक्षकः पन्नगश्रेष्ठस्तेजसाऽद्य प्रधक्ष्यति॥
