sn: शकुनि म यस्त्वासीद्राजा लोके महारथः। द्वापरं विद्धि तं राजन्संभूतमरिमर्दनम्॥
en: O king, that king and great car-warrior, that chastiser of foes, who was known as Shakuni in the world, know him to be the Dvapara himself.

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: सात्यकिः सत्यसन्धश्च योऽसौ वृष्णिकुलोद्वहः। पक्षात्स जज्ञे मरुतां देवानामरिमर्दनः॥
en: He who was known as Satyaki, the upholder of the pride of Vrishnis and the chastiser of foes, was born of the portion of celestial Marutas.

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: दुपदश्चैव राजर्षिस्तत एवाभवद्गणात्। मानुषे नृपलोकेऽस्मिन्सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वरः॥
en: That royal sage, king Drupada, the best of all the wielder of arms, was also born the portions of the same celestials (Marutas).

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: ततश्च कृतवर्माणं विद्धि राजञ्जनाधिपम्। तमप्रतिमकर्माणं क्षत्रियर्षभसत्तमम्॥
en: O king, know that Kritavarma that king of men, that man of matchless deeds, that best of best Kshatriyas,

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: मरुतां तु गणाद्विद्धि संजातमरिमर्दनम्। विराटं नाम राजानं परराष्ट्रप्रतापनम्॥
en: That chastiser of foes, was also born of the same celestials. The king Virata, the conqueror of other kingdoms, was also born of the same celestials.

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: अरिष्टायास्तु यः पुत्रो हंस इत्यभिविश्रुतः। स गन्धर्वपतिर्जज्ञे कुरुवंशविवर्धनः॥
en: That son of Arishta, known as Hansa, the king of the Gandharvas, was born to increase the Kuru race.

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: धृतराष्ट्र इति ख्यातः कृष्णद्वैपायनात्मजः। दीर्घबाहुर्महातेजाः प्रज्ञाचक्षुर्नराधिपः॥
en: He was known on earth as Dhritarashtra, the son of Krishna Dvaipayana; he had long arms, he was greatly powerful and he was a king with prophetic eyes.

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: मातुर्दोषादृषेः कोपादन्ध एव व्यजायत। तस्यैवावरजो भ्राता महासत्त्वो महाबलः॥ स पाण्डुरिति विख्यातः सत्यधर्मरतः शुचि।
en: He became blind for the fault of his mother and anger of the Rishi. His younger brother was greatly powerful and strong. He was known as Pandu and was devoted to truth, virtue and purity.

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: अत्रेस्तु सुमहाभागं पुत्रं पुत्रवतः वरम्। विदुरं विद्धि तं लोके जातं बुद्धिमतां वरम्॥
en: Know, that he who was known as Vidura, he wino was the best of all virtuous men, he who was the god of justice himself who was the excellent and greatly fortunate son of Atri (Surya). one

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: कलेरंशस्तु संजज्ञे भुवि दुर्योधनो नृपः। दुर्बुद्धिर्दुर्मतिश्चैव कुरूणामयशस्करः॥
en: The evil and wicked-minded king Duryodhana, the destroyer of the fame of the Kuru dynasty, was born of the portion of the Kali.

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: जगतो यस्तु सर्वस्य विद्विष्ट कलिपूरुषः। यः सर्वां घातयामास पृथिवीं पृथिवीपते॥
en: O king, It was he who was the cause of the slaughter of all creatures and of the world, he ruined the earth.

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: उद्दीपितं येन वैरं भूतान्तकरणं महत्। पौलस्त्या भ्रातरश्चास्य जज्ञिरे मनुजेष्विह॥
en: It was he who fanned the fire of hostility, the great fire of destruction. The sons of Pulastya became on earth the brothers of Duryodhana.

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: शतं दुःशासनादीनां सर्वेषां क्रूरकर्मणाम्। दुर्मुखो दुःसहश्चैव ये चान्येनानुकीर्तिताः॥
en: They were hundred, Dushasana Durmukha, Dusaha and others, all wicked to the extreme. I do not mention their names.

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: दुर्योधनसहायास्ते पौलस्त्या भरतर्षभ। वैश्यापुत्रो युयुत्सुश्च धार्तराष्ट्रः शताधिकः॥
en: All of them supported Duryodhana in his wicked acts. O best of the Bharata race, they were all sons of Pulastya (Rakshas). Over and above these one hundred sons, Dhritarashtra had another son Yuyutsu, begot on a Vaisya woman.

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: जनमेजय उवाच ज्येष्ठानुज्येष्ठा तामेषां नामधेयानि वा विभो। धृतराष्ट्रस्य पुत्राणामानुपूर्वेण कीर्तय॥
en: Janamejaya said : O Lord, tell me the names of all the sons of Dhritarashtra beginning from the eldest, according to the order of their births.

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: वैशंपायन उवाच दुर्योधनो युयुत्सुश्च राजन्दुश्शासनस्तथा। दुःसहो दुःशलश्चैव दुर्मुखश्च तथापरः॥ विविंशतिर्विकर्णश्च जलसन्धः सुलोचनः। विन्दानुविन्दौ दुर्घर्ष: सुबाहुर्दुष्प्रधर्षणः॥ दुर्मर्षणो दुर्मुखश्च दुष्कर्णः कर्ण एव च। चित्रोपचित्रौ चित्राक्षश्चारुचित्राङ्गदश्च ह॥ दुर्मदो दुष्प्रहर्षश्च विवित्सुर्विकटः समः। ऊर्णनाभः पद्मनाभस्तथा नन्दोपनन्दकौ॥ सेनापतिः सुषेणश्च कुण्डोदरमहोदरौ। चित्रबाहुश्चित्रवर्मा सुवर्मा दुर्विरोचनः॥ अयोबाहुर्महाबाहुश्चित्रचापसुकुण्डलौ। भीमवेगो भीमबलो बलाकी भीमविक्रमः॥ उग्रायुधो भीमशरः कनकायुदृढायुधः। दृढवर्मा दृढक्षत्रः सोमकीर्तिरनूदरः :॥ जरासन्धो दृढसन्धः सत्यसन्धः सहस्रवाक्। उग्रश्रवा उग्रसेनः क्षेममूर्तिस्तथैव च॥ अपराजितः पण्डितको विशालाक्षो दुराधनः॥ दृढहस्तः सुहस्तश्च वातवेगसुवर्चसौ। आदित्यकेतुर्बह्वाशी नागदत्तानुयायिनौ॥ कवची निषङ्गी दण्डो दण्डधारो धनुर्ग्रहः। उग्रो भीमरथो वीरो वीरबाहुरलोलुपः॥ अभयो रौद्रकर्मा च तथा दृढरथश्च यः। अनाधृष्यः कुण्डभेदी विरावी दीर्घलोचनः॥ दीर्घबाहुर्महाबाहुयूंढोरुः कनकाङ्गदः। कुण्डजश्चित्रकश्चैव दुःशला च शताधिका॥ वैश्यापुत्रो युयुत्सुश्च धार्तराष्ट्रः शताधिकः।
en: Vaishampayana said : (They are) Duryodhana, Yuyutsa, Dushasana, Dussaha, Dushala, Durmukha, Vivingshati, Vikarna, Jalasandha, Sulochana, Vinda, Anuvinda, Durdharsha, Subahu, Dushpradharshana, Durmarshana, Durmukha, Dushkarna, Karna, Chitra, Upachitra, Chitraksha, Charu, Chitrangada, Durmada, Dushpradharsha, Vivitsu, Vikata, Sama, Urnanabha, Padmanabha, Nanda, Upananda, Senapati, Shushena, Kundodara, Mahodara, Chitrabahu, Chitravarma, Suvarmana, Durvirochana, Ayobahu, Mahabahu, Chitrachapa, Sukundala, Bhimavega, Bhimabala, Balaki, Bhima, Vikrama, Ugrayudha, Bhimashara, Kanakayu, Drindayudha, Drindavarmana, Drindakshetra, Somakirti, Anudara, Jarasandha, Drindasandha, Satyasandha, Sahasrayaka, Ugrashrava, Ugrasena, Kshemamurti, Aparajita, Panditaka, Vishalaksha, Duradhana, Drindahasta, Suhasta, Vatavega, Suvarcha, Adityaketu, Bahvashi, Nagadatta, Anuyayi, Nishangi, Kavachi, Dandi, Dandadhara, Dhanugraha, Ugra, Bhimaratha, Vira, Virabahu, Alolupa, Abhaya, Raudrakarma, Drindaratha, Anadhrishya, Kundabhedi, Viravi, Dirghalochana, Dirghbahu, Mahabahu, Vyudhoru, Kanakangada, Kundaja and Chitraka. He (Dhritarashtra) had also a daughter, named Dushala, above and over these one hundred sons. Dhritarashtra had another son, named Yuyutsa, born of a Vyasa woman, who was also above and over these one hundred sons.

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: एतदेकशतं राजन्कन्या चैका प्रकीर्तिता।। नामधेयानुपूर्व्या च ज्येष्ठानुज्येष्ठतां विदुः॥
en: O king, thus have I told you the names of the one hundred sons (of Dhritarashtra) and also of the name of his daughter. You have now known their names according to the orders of their births.

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: सर्वे त्वतिरथाः शूराः सर्वे युद्धविशारदाः। सर्वे वेदविदश्चैव राजञ्च्छास्त्रे च पारगा॥
en: They were all heroes, great car-warriors and learned in the use of arms. They were also well-versed in the Vedas and experts in statesmanship

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: सर्वे संग्रामविद्यासु विद्याभिजनशोभिनः। सर्वेषामनुरूपाश्च कृता दारा महीपते॥
en: O king, all of them were mighty in attack and defence and all of them were learned. They married wives suitable to them in beauty and accomplishments.

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: दुःशलां समये राजन्सिन्धुराजाय कौरवः। जयद्रथाय प्रददौ सौबलानुमते तदा॥
en: At the marriageable age, the king of the Kurus at the advice of Shakuni bestowed his daughter Dushala on Jayadratha, the king of the Sindhus.

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: धर्मस्यांशं तु राजानं विद्धि राजन्युधिष्ठिरम्। भीमसेनं तु वातस्य देवराजस्य चार्जुनम्॥
en: Know, O king, king Yudhishthira was a portion of Dharma; Bhima was that of Maruta; Arjuna was that of the king of the celestials (Indra).

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: अश्विनोस्तु तथैवांशौ रूपेणाप्रतिमौ भुवि। नकुलः सहदेवश्च सर्वभूतमनोहरौ॥
en: The most handsome men amongst all men and the matchless beauties on earth, Nakula and Sahadeva were the portions of the Ashvinas.

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: यस्तु वर्चा इति ख्यातः सोमपुत्रः प्रतापवान्। सोऽभिमन्युर्वृहत्कीर्तिरर्जुनस्य सुतोऽभवत्॥
en: He, who was known as Varcha the son of Soma, became Abhimanyu of wonderful deeds, the son of Arjuna.

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: यस्यावतरणे राजन्सुरान्सोमोऽब्रवीदिदम्। नाहं दद्यां प्रियं पुत्रं मम प्राणैर्गरीयसम्॥
en: O king, before his (Varcha) incarnation on earth, Soma thus spoke to the celestials, "I cannot part with my son; he is dearer to me than life.

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: समयः क्रियतामेष न शक्यमतिवर्तितम्। सुरकार्यं हि नः कार्यमसुराणां क्षितौ वधः॥
en: Let this agreement be made and let not that agreement be violated. The destruction of the Asuras is the work of the celestials, therefore it is our work also.

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: तत्र यास्यत्ययं वर्चा न च स्थास्यति वै चिरम्। ऐन्द्रिनरस्तु भविता यस्य नारायणः सखा॥
en: Let this Varcha go, but let him not stay long on earth. Nara will be born as Indra's son and he will have Narayana as his friend.

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: सोऽर्जुनोत्यभिविख्यातः पाण्डोः पुत्रः प्रतापवान्। तस्यायं भविता पुत्रो बालो भुवि महारथः॥
en: He will be known on earth as powerful Arjuna, the son of Pandu. My boy will be his son and even in his boyhood will be a great car-warrior.

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: ततः षोडशवर्षाणि स्थास्यत्यमरसत्तमाः। अस्य षोडशवर्षस्य स संग्रामो भविष्यति॥
en: O best of immortals, let him remain on earth only for sixteen years. On his sixteenth year, will take place that great fight.

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: यत्रांशा वः करिष्यन्ति कर्मवीरनिषूदनम्। नरनारायणाभ्यां तु स संग्रामो विना कृतः॥
en: In which your incarnations will kill innumerable heroes. And in the fight in which Nara and Narayana (Arjuna and Krishna) will not be present,

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: चक्रव्यूह समास्थाय योधयिष्यन्ति वः सुराः। विमुखञ्च्छात्रवान्सर्वान्कारयिष्यति मे सुतः॥
en: And in which, O celestials, the (Kuru) heroes will fight with constructing a Chakravyuha, (in that fight) my son will defeat all foes and compel them to retreat.

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: बालः प्रविश्य च व्यूहमभेद्यं विचरिष्यति। महारथानां वीराणां कदनं च करिष्यति॥
en: The boy will enter into that impenetrable Vyuha and will walk about the place. He will defeat and kill many heroes and great carwarriors.

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: सर्वेषामेव शत्रूणां चतुर्थांशं नयिष्यति। दिनार्धेन महाबाहुः प्रेतराजपुरं प्रति॥
en: The mighty-armed hero, within the course of half a day, will send the one-fourth part of the foes, to the land of the dead.

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: ततो महारथैर्वीरैः समेत्य बहुशो रणे। दिनक्षये महाबाहुर्मया भूयः समेष्यति॥
en: Then towards the close of the day, many heroes and great car-warriors will return to the charge and attack my son. Thereupon, my mighty-armed son will come back to me.

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: एकं वंशकरं पुत्रं वीरं वै जनयिष्यति। प्रनष्टं भारतं वंशं स भूयो धारयिष्यति॥
en: He will beget one heroic son who will keep alive the almost extinct Bharata dynasty."

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: एतत्सोमवचः श्रुत्वा तथास्विति दिवौकसः। प्रत्यूचुः सहिताः सर्वे ताराधिपमपूजयन्॥
en: Having heard these words of Soma, the celestials said, “Be it so.” They then all worshipped and praised the lord of the stars (Soma).

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: एवं ते कथितं राजंस्तव जन्म पितुः पितुः। अग्नेर्भागं तु विद्धि त्वं धृष्टद्युम्नं महारथम्॥
en: O king, thus have I told you the accounts of the births of your father and his father (and so on;. Know, O king, the great car-warrior Dhrishtadyumna was born of a portion of Agni.

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: शिखण्डिनमथोराजस्त्रीपूर्वं विद्धि राक्षसम्। द्रौपदेयाश्च ये पञ्च बभूवुर्भरतर्षभ।१२७॥
en: Know that Shikhandi, who was previously a woman, was born of a portion of a Rakshasa. O best of the Bharata race, those that became the five sons of Draupadi,

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: विश्वान्देवगणान्विद्धि संजातान्भरतर्षभ। प्रतिविध्यः सुतमोसः श्रुतकीर्तिस्तथापरः॥
en: Know, O best of the Bharata race, were the celestials called Vishvedevas. (They were) Prativindhya, Sutasoma, Shrutakirti.

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: नाकुलिस्तु शतानीकः श्रुतसेनश्च वीर्यवान्। शूरो नाम यदुश्रेष्ठो वसुदेवपिताभवत्॥
en: Shatanika, the son of Nakula and the powerful Shrutasena. The best of the Yadus, Shura, became the father of Vasudeva.

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: तस्य कन्या पृथा नाम रूपेणासदृशी भुवि। पितुः स्वस्त्रीयपुत्राय सोऽनपत्याय वीर्यवान्॥ अग्रमग्रे प्रतिज्ञाय स्वस्यापत्यस्य वै तदा। अग्रजातेति तां कन्यां शूरोऽनुग्रहकांक्षया॥ अददत्कुन्तिभोजाय स तां दुहितरं तदा। सा नियुक्ता पितुर्गेहे ब्राह्मणातिथिपूजने॥
en: His daughter was named Pritha, who was matchless on earth in beauty. Her father (Shura) promised before Fire that he would give his first-born child to the son of his paternal aunt, king Kuntibhoja, who was childless. He gave his daughter (Pritha) to that king, expecting to get his favour. And king Kuntibhoja, adopted her as his daughter. She was engaged in her (foster) father's house in attending upon Brahmanas and guests.

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: उग्रं पर्यचरद्घोरं ब्राह्मणं संशितव्रतम्। निगूढनिश्चयं धर्मे यं तं दूर्वाससं विदुः॥ तमुग्रं शंसितात्मानं सर्वयत्तैरतोषयत्। तुष्टोऽभिचारसंयुक्तमाचचक्षे यथाविधि॥
en: One day she attended upon the terrible and wrathful ascetic, vow-observing Durvasa, who was learned in the mysteries of religion and well-acquainted with truth. She, with all possible care, gratified that self-controlled ascetic.

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: उवाच चैनां भगवान्प्रीतोऽस्मि सुभगे तव। यं यं देवं त्वमेतेन मन्त्रेणावाहयिष्यसि॥
en: The illustrious man said, “O fortunate girl, I am much pleased with you. To those of the celestials whom you will call by this Mantra (that I teach you).

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: तस्य तस्य प्रसादात्त्वं देवि पुत्राञ्जनिष्यसि। एवमुक्ता च सा बाला तदा कौतूहलान्विता॥
en: (They will instantly come) and by their grace you will give birth to offspring." Thus addressed that girl, being much curious (to see the effect of the Mantra).

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: कन्या सती देवमर्कमाजुहाव यशस्विनी। प्रकाशकर्ता भगवांस्तस्यां गर्भं दधौ तदा॥
en: Called Surya when she was a maid. The illustrious god of light (Surya) made her conceive.

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: अजीजनत्सुतं चास्यां सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वरम्। सकुण्डलं सकवचं देवगर्भश्रियान्वितम्॥
en: And she begot a son, who became the best of all wielders of arms. He was born with a coat of arms and a pair of ear-rings and he looked as handsome as a celestial child.

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: दिवाकरसमं दीप्त्या चारुसर्वाङ्गभूषितम्। निगूहमाना जातं वै बन्धुपक्षभयात्तदा॥
en: And as effulgent as the sun and every part of his body was well embellished. From the fear of her friends and relatives, privately,

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: उत्ससर्ज जले कुन्ती तं कुमारं यशस्विनम्। तमुत्सृष्टं जले गर्भं राधाभर्ता महायशाः॥
en: She throw that illustrious son into water (river). But the child, thus thrown into the water, was taken up by the illustrious husband of Radha.

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: राधायाः कल्पयामास पुत्रं सोऽधिरथस्तदा। चक्रतुर्नामधेयं च तस्य बालस्य तावुभौ॥ दम्पतीव सुषेणेति दिक्षु सर्वासु विश्रुतम्। संवर्धमानो बलवान्सर्वास्त्रेषूत्तमोऽभवत्॥
en: Adhiratha (the husband of Radha) made the child his son. And the couple then gave him the name of Vasushena, by which name he soon became known all over the country. As he grew up, he became very strong and excelled in the use of all weapons.

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: वेदाङ्गानि च सर्वाणि जजाप जयतां वरः। यस्मिन्काले जपन्नास्ते धीमान्सत्यपराक्रमः॥ नादेयं ब्राह्मणेष्वासीत्तस्मिन्काले महात्मनः। तमिन्द्रो ब्राह्मणो भूत्वा पुत्रार्थे भूतभावनः॥
en: He became the best victor and learned in all the Vedangas. When that wise and truthloving man was doing his japa, then there was nothing to that high-souled man which he could not give to the Brahmanas. To do good to his son (Arjuna), illustrious Indra, one day assuming the form of a Brahimana,

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: ययाचे कुण्डले वीरं कवचं च सहाङ्गजम्। उत्कृत्य कर्णो ह्यददत्कवचं कुण्डले तथा॥
en: Begged from him his ear-rings and his natural coat of arms. Removing the ear-rings and coat of arms from his ear and breast, he gave them to him (Indra).

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: शक्तिं शक्रो ददौ तस्मै विस्मितश्चेदमब्रवीत्। देवासुरमनुष्याणां गन्धर्वोरगरक्षसाम्॥
en: Indra, who being much surprised (for his liberality), presented him with a dart and spoke to him thus, "The Devas, Asuras, Gandharvas, Rakshasas, Uragas or men,

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: यस्मिन्क्षेप्स्यसि दुर्धर्षं स एको न भविष्यति। पुरा नाम च तस्यासीद्वसुषेण इति क्षितौ॥
en: At whoinever, O hero, you will hurt this weapon, he will certainly be killed. He (the son of Pritha) was previously known by the name of Vasushena,

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: ततो वैकर्तनः कर्णः कर्मणा तेन सोऽभवत्। आमुक्तकवचो वीरो यस्तु जज्ञे महायशाः॥
en: But for his mighty deeds, he was subsequently called Karna. Because the greatly illustrious hero removed his natural coat of Arms (from his breast).

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: स कर्ण इति विख्यातः पृथायाः प्रथमः सुतः। स तु सूतकुले वीरो ववृधे राजसत्तम॥
en: He, the eldest son of Pritha, was called Karna. O best of kings, he thus began to grow up in the Suta caste.

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: दुर्योधनस्य सचिवं मित्रं शत्रुविनाशनम्। दिवाकरस्य तं विद्धि राजन्नशमनुत्तमम्॥ यस्तु नारायणो नाम देवदेवः सनातनः। तस्यांशो मानुष्वेसीद् वासुदेवः प्रतापवान्॥
en: Karna, the best of kings, expert in the use of all arms, the destroyer of his foes, became the friend and counsellor of Duryodhana, Know, O king, he was born of a portion of the sun. Of that god of gods, that everlasting Being, whose name is Narayana, the powerful Vasudeva (Krishna), was a portion in the world of men.

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: शेषस्यांशश्च नागस्य बलदेवो महाबलः। सनत्कुमारं प्रद्युम्नं विद्धि राजन् महौजसम्॥ एवमन्ये मनुष्येन्द्रा बहवोंऽशा दिवौकसाम्। जज्ञिरे वसुदेवस्य कुले कुलविवर्धनाः॥
en: Baladeva was a portion of the Naga, Shesha. O king, know that the greatly energetic Pradyumna was a portion of Sanatkumara. In this was many dwellers of heaven became great men on earth, In the race of Vasudeva, thus increasing its glory.

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: गणस्त्वप्सरसां यो वै मया राजन् प्रकीर्तितः। तस्य भागः क्षितौ जज्ञे नियोगाद् वासवस्य ह॥
en: O king, the Apsaras, of whom I have already spoken, were also born on earth in portions as ordered by Indra.

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: तानि षोडश देवीनां सहस्राणि नराधिप। बभूवुर्मानुषे लोके वासुदेवपरिग्रहः॥ श्रियस्तु भाग: संजज्ञे रत्यर्थं पृथिवीतले।
en: O king, sixteen thousand portions of these celestial ladies, became in the world of men the wives of Vasudeva. A portion of Sree (Lakshmi), herself became incarnate on earth out of love (for Narayana).

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: भीष्मकस्य कुले साध्वी रुक्मिणी नाम नामतः॥१५६। द्रौपदी त्वथ संजज्ञे शचीभागादनिन्दिता। द्रुपदस्य कुले कन्या वेदिमध्यादनिन्दिता॥
en: She was born in the race of Bhishmaka and that illustrious lady was named Rukmini. Draupadi was born from a portion of Sachi, (the wife of Indra) in the race of Drupada and from the altar of the sacrifice.

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: नातिइस्वा न महती नीलोत्पलसुगन्धिनी। पद्मायताक्षी सुश्रोणी स्वसिताञ्चितमूर्धजा॥
en: She was neither tall nor short, she had the fragrance of blue lotus. Her eyes were like the lotus leaves, her thighs were fair and round and her dense masses of hair were black and curly.

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: सर्वलक्षणसम्पूर्णा वैदूर्यमणिसन्निभा। पञ्चानां पुरुषेन्द्राणां चित्तप्रमथनी रहः॥
en: She was endued with all auspicious marks and her complexion was like the emerald. She was the charmer of the hearts of the five kings of men (the Pandavas).

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: सिद्धिधृतिश्च ये देव्यौ पञ्चानां मातरौ तु ते। कुन्ती माद्री च जज्ञाते मतिस्तु सुबलात्मजा॥
en: The goddesses Siddhi and Dhriti became the mothers of the five (Pandavas). They were named Kunti and Madri. And the goddess, who was Mati, became the daughter of Subala (Gandhari, the wife of Dhritarashtra).

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: इति देवासुराणां ते गन्धर्वाप्सरसां तथा। अंशावतरणं राजन् राक्षसानां च कीर्तितम्॥ ये पृथिव्यां समुद्धृता राजानो युद्धदुर्मदाः। महात्मानो यदूनां च ये जाता विपुले कुले॥ ब्राह्मणाः क्षत्रिया वैश्या मया ते परिकीर्तिताः। धन्यं यशस्यं पुत्रीयमायुष्यं विजयावहम्। इदमंशावतरणं श्रोतव्यमनसूयता॥
en: Thus, O king, have I described to you the births and incarnations of the portions of the Devas, Asuras, Gandharvas, Apsaras and Rakshasas, those that appeared on earth as invincible kings. Those illustrious ones that were born in the extensive race of the Yadus, those that were born as Brahmanas, Kshatriyas and Vaishyas, have all been described. This Anshavatarana (accounts of incarnations), which is capable of bestowing wealth, fame, long-life, offspring and victory, should be heard with proper frame of mind.

description: Descent of the Celestials, Gandharvas, Danavas etc.
sn: अंशावतरणं श्रुत्वा देवगन्धर्वरक्षसाम्। प्रभवाप्ययवित् प्राज्ञो न कृच्छ्रेष्ववसीदति॥
en: Hearing the incarnations of the Devas, the Asuras and the Gandharvas, the learned person, thus knowing the mystery of creation, preservation and destruction, does not feel depressed, even in the greatest sorrow.

sn: जनमेजय उवाच त्वत्तः श्रुतमिदं ब्रह्मन् देवदानवरक्षसाम्। अंशावतरणं सम्यग् गन्धर्वाप्सरसां तथा॥
en: Janamejaya said : O Brahmana, I have heard in detail the account of the births of the Devas, the Danavas, the Rakshasas, the Gandharvas and the Apsaras.

sn: इमं तु भूय इच्छामि कुरूणां वंशमादितः। कथ्यमानं त्वया विप्र विप्रर्षिगणसंनिधौ॥
en: Now I desire to hear the accounts of the births of the kings of the Kuru race from the beginning. Therefore, O Brahmana, narrate them before all these Brahmana Rishis.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच पौरवाणां वंशकरो दुष्यन्तो नाम वीर्यवान्। पृथिव्याश्चतुरन्ताया गोप्ता भरतसत्तम।॥
en: Vaishampayana said : O best of the Bharata race, the founder of the Paurava dynasty was a greatly powerful king, named Dushyanta. He was the protector of the earth bounded by the four seas.

sn: चतुर्भागं भुवः कृत्स्नं यो भुङ्क्ते मनुजेश्वरः। समुद्रावरणांश्चापि देशान् स समितिंजयः॥ आम्लेच्छावधिकान् सर्वान् सभुङ्क्ते रिपुमर्दनः। रत्नाकरसमुद्रान्तांश्चातुर्वर्ण्यजनावृतान्॥
en: That king of men enjoyed the fourth part of all the products of the land. He was (also) the lord of various countries in the midst of the sea. That chastiser of foes had sway even over all the countries begining from that of upto the sea, the mine of gems, Mlecchas, which were full of men of the four orders.

sn: न वर्णसंकरकरो न कृप्याकरकृजनः। न पापकृत् कश्चिदासीत् तस्मिन् राजनि शासति॥
en: During his reign, there were no mixed castes, no tillers of the land, no toilers of the mines and no sinful men.

sn: धर्मे रतिं सेवमाना धर्मार्थावभिपेदिरे। तदा नरा नरव्याघ्र तस्मिञ्जनपदेश्वरे॥ नासीचौरभयं तात न क्षुधाभयमण्वपि। नासीद् व्याधिभयं चापि तस्मिञ्जनपदेश्वरे॥
en: O best of men, during his reign, all men, were virtuous and they did every thing with an eye on virtue. O child, during his reign, there was no fear from the thieves and no fear from famines; and there was no fear of diseases.

sn: स्वधर्मे रेमिरे वर्णा दैवे कर्मणि नि:स्पृहाः। तमाश्रित्य महीपालमासंश्चैवाकुतो भयाः॥
en: Men of all the four castes took pleasure in doing their respective duties and they performed all acts without the desire of gaining fruits. O protector of the world, depending upon him, his subjects felt no fear.

sn: कालवर्षी च पर्जन्यः सस्यानि रसवन्ति च। सर्वरत्नसमृद्धा च मही पशुमती तथा॥
en: Parjanya (Indra) poured showers of rains at the proper time and the crops were all juicy. The earth was full of all kinds of wealth and animals.

sn: स्वकर्मनिरता विप्रा नानृतं तेषु विद्यते। स चाद्भुतमहावीर्यो वज्रसंहननो युवा॥
en: The Brahmanas were always engaged in their duties and they were very truthful. He (Dushyanta) was a young prince of wonderful prowess and of a body like the thunder-bolt.

sn: उद्यम्य मन्दरं दोभ्यॊ वहेत् सवनकाननम्। चतुष्पथगदायुद्धे सर्वप्रहरणेषु च॥ नागपृष्ठेऽश्वपृष्ठे च बभूव परिनिष्ठितः। बले विष्णुसमश्चासीत् तेजसा भास्करोपमः॥
en: He could support the Mandara (mountain) with its woods and forests, raising it up on his arins. He was an expert in the four kinds of club-fight and also in using every kind of weapons. He was greatly expert in riding elephants and horses. In strength, he was like Vishnu and in splendour he was like the sun.

sn: अक्षोभ्यत्वेऽर्णवसमः सहिष्णुत्वे धरासमः! सम्मतः स महीपाल: प्रसन्नपुरराष्ट्रवान्॥ भूयो धर्मपरैर्भावैर्मुदितं जनमादिशत्॥
en: In gravity he was like the ocean and in patience he was like the earth. The king (Dushyanta) was loved by all his subjects and he too ruled very virtuously those contented men.

sn: जनमेजय उवाच सम्भवं भरतस्याहं चरितं च महामतेः। शकुन्तलायाश्चोत्पत्तिं श्रोतुमिच्छामि तत्त्वतः॥
en: Janamejaya said : I desire to hear in detail the account of the birth and career of the high-souled Bharata and the birth of Shakuntala.

sn: दुष्यन्तेन च वीरेण यथा प्राप्ता शकुन्तला। तं वै पुरुषसिंहस्य भगवन् विस्तरं त्वहम्॥ श्रोतुमिच्छामि तत्त्वज्ञ सर्वं मतिमतां वर।
en: O holy man, tell me in full how that hero, that lion among men, obtained Shakuntala. I desire to hear it, therefore, O knower of truth, O best among wise-men! you should narrate it to me.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच स कदाचिन्महाबाहुः प्रभूतबलवाहनः॥ वनं जगाम गहनं हयनागशतैर्वृतः। बलेन चतुरङ्गेण वृतः परमवल्गुना॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Once upon a time that king (Dushyanta) of mighty arms, accompanied with a very large force with hundreds of horses and elephants, went into a dense forest. The force were of four kinds (infantry cavalry, elephant-men, horsemen and car-warriors).

sn: खड्गशक्तिधरैवीरैर्गदामुसलपाणिभिः। प्रासतोमरहस्तैश्च ययौ योधशतैर्वृतः॥
en: Surrounded by hundreds of warriors who were armed with swords, darts, maces and big clubs, lances and spears in their hands, the king marched out.

sn: सिंहनादैश्च योधानां शङ्खदुन्दुभिनिःस्वनैः। स्थनेमिस्वनैश्चैव सनागवरबंहितैः॥ नानायुधधरैश्चापि नानावेषधरैस्तथा। हेषितस्वनमित्रैश्च क्ष्वेडितास्फोटितस्वनैः॥ आसीत् किलकिलाशब्दस्तस्मिन् गच्छति पार्थिवे। प्रासादवरशृङ्गस्थाः परया नृपशोभया॥ ददृशुस्तं स्त्रियस्तत्र शूरमात्मयशस्करम्।
en: The lion-like roars of the warriors, the sounds of conches and drums. The rattle of the wheels of the cars, the shrieks of the huge elephants and the clash of weapons of various soldiers dressed in various dresses, and the neighing of horses. All these indistinct, sounds, mixing together, raised a deafening (Kil Kil) sound when the king was on the march. Beautiful ladies from the terraces of the magnificent mansions beheld the heroic, illustrious and kingly monarch (to pass).

sn: शक्रोपमममित्रघ्नं परवारणवारणम्॥ पश्यन्तः स्त्रीगणास्तत्र वज्रपाणिं स्म मेनिरे। अयं स पुरुषव्याघ्रो रणे वसुपराक्रमः॥ यस्य बाहुबलं प्राप्य न भवन्त्यसुहृद्गणाः।
en: They knew that king to be the destroyer of foes like Indra; they thought him to be the wielder of thunder-bolt himself. They said, “This is that best of heroic men who is as powerful in the battle as the Vasu. All enemies are destroyed by his great prowess.

sn: इति वाचो ब्रुवन्त्यस्ताः स्त्रियः प्रेम्णा नराधिपम्॥ तुष्टुवुः पुष्पवृष्टीश्च ससृजुस्तस्य मूर्धनि। तत्र तत्र च विप्रेन्द्रैः स्तूयमानः समन्ततः॥
en: Saying this, the ladies, out of love towards him, showered flowers on the head of the king to his great gratification. Having been blessed by the best of Brahmanas everywhere on the way.

sn: निर्ययौ परमप्रीत्या वनं मृगजिघांसया। तं देवराजप्रतिमं मत्तवारणधूर्गतम्॥ द्विजक्षत्रियविट्शूद्रा निर्यान्तमनुजग्मिरे। ददृशुर्वर्धमानास्ते आशीर्भिश्च जयेन च॥
en: The king started for the forest with the eager desire of killing deer. The king, seated on the back of a mad elephant, looked like the king of the celestials and he was followed by Brahmanas, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas and Shudras. They uttered blessings and cried victory from all sides.

sn: सुदूरमनुजग्मुस्तं पौरजानपदास्तथा। न्यवर्तन्त ततः पश्चादनुज्ञाता नृपेण ह॥
en: The citizens and other people also followed the king for some distance. Then they returned when they were commanded by the king.

sn: सुपर्णप्रतिमेनाथ रथेन वसुधाधिपः। महीमापूरयामास घोषेण त्रिदिवं तथा॥ स गच्छन् ददृशे धीमान् नन्दनप्रतिमं वनम्। बिल्वार्कखदिराकीर्णं कपित्यधवसंकुलम्॥
en: Thereupon, the king of the world got upon his car which was equal to Garuda in speed and filled the whole world, even the heavens, with the rattle of his car-wheels. Thus proceeding he saw a forest like the Nandanavana of heaven. It abounded in Bilva, Arka, Khadira, Kapittha and Dhava trees.

sn: विषमं पर्वतस्रस्तैरश्मभिश्च समावृतम्। निर्जलं निर्मनुष्यं च बहुयोजनमायतम्॥
en: Its soil was uneven and covered with blocks of stone, loosened from the hills. There were no water and human habitations; it extended to many yojanas.

sn: मृगसिंहैर्वृतं घोरैरन्यैश्चापि वनेचरैः। तद् वनं मनुजव्याघ्रः सभृत्यबलवाहनः॥ लोडयामास दुष्यन्तः सूदयन् विविधान् मृगान्। बाणगोचरसम्प्राप्तांस्तत्र व्याघ्रगणान् बहून्॥ पातयामास दुष्यन्तो निर्बिभेद च सायकैः। दूरस्थान् सायकैः कांश्चिदभिनत् स नराधिपः॥ अभ्याशमागतांश्चान्यान् खङ्गेन निकृन्तत। कांश्चिदेगान् समाजघ्ने शक्त्या शक्तिमतां वरः॥
en: It was full of deer, lions and other fearful ! animals of the forest. That best of kings, Dushyanta, with the help of his soldiers and servants, beat the forest, thus killing many animals. Dushyanta pierced with his arrows many tigers that were within shooting range and killed them (by hundreds). The king wounded many by arrows (that were out of the shooting range and not to be killed by swords); he killed by his sword those that were near at hand. That best of the wielders of darts, killed many by hurling his darts at them.

sn: गदामण्डलतत्त्वज्ञश्चचारामितविक्रमः। तोमरैरसिभिश्चापि गदामुसलकम्पनैः॥ चचार स विनिघ्नन् वै स्वैरचारान् वनद्विपान्। राज्ञा चाद्भुतवीर्येण योधैश्च समरप्रियैः॥ लोड्यमानं महारण्यं तत्यजुः स्म मृगाधिपाः। तत्र विद्रुतयूथानि हतयूथपतीनि च॥ मृगयूथान्यथौत्सुक्याच्छब्दं चक्रुस्ततस्ततः। शुष्काश्चापि नदीर्गत्वा जलनैराश्यकर्शिताः॥ व्यायामकान्तहृदया: पतन्ति स्म विचेतसः। क्षुत्पिपासापरीताश्च श्रान्ताश्च पतिता भुवि॥
en: The greatly expert player of clubs, the king of matchless prowess (Dushyanta), thus fearlessly roamed over the forest. The king, as he roamed about, killed many beasts of the forest with his swords and some by his swift flying darts and some by his heavy clubs. When the forest was thus agitated by the wonderfully powerful king and his soldiers, ever delighting in it like in sports, the lions left in thousands that forest. Having thus lost their kings, the other beasts uttered loud cries in fear and anxiety and fled in all directions. They fell down on all sides, being hungry, thirsty and tired of running and without being able to quench their thirst in the river-beds which were dry.

sn: केचित् तत्र नरव्याग़रभक्ष्यन्त बुभुक्षितैः। केचिदग्निमथोत्पाद्य संसाध्य च वनेचराः॥ भक्षयन्ति स्म मांसानि प्रकुट्य विधिवत् तदा। तत्र केचिद् गजा मत्ता बलिनः शस्त्रविक्षताः॥ संकोच्याग्रकरान् भीताः प्रद्रवन्ति स्म वेगिताः। शकृन्मूत्रं सृजन्तश्च क्षरन्तः शोणितं बहु॥
en: Some of them were eaten up by those best of warriors. Some were quarter d and roasted in fires lit up by them and then they were eaten by the warriors in the proper way. Many strong elephants, maddened with the pains of their wounds, fled in fear with their upraised trunks. Those wild elephants, ejecting urine and dung in fear and copiously vomiting blood, fled.

sn: वन्या गजवरास्तत्र ममृदुर्मनुजान् बहून्। तद् वनं बलमेघेन शरधारेण संवृतम्। व्यरोचत मृगाकीर्णं राज्ञा हतमृगाधिपम्॥
en: Many big and strong elephants during the time of running trampled to death many soldiers (of the king). The forest, which had been full of animals, was soon made by the king and his innumerable followers, bereft of lions and tigers and other beasts.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततो मृगसहस्राणि हत्वा सबलवाहनः। राजा मृगप्रसङ्गेन वनमन्यद् विवेश ह॥
en: Vaishampayana said : The king with his soldiers, having killed thousands of animals, entered another forest following an animal.

sn: एक एवोत्तमबलः क्षुत्पिपासाश्रमान्वितः। स वनस्यान्तमासाद्य महच्छून्यं समासदत्॥
en: Alone, fatigued with hunger and thirst he came to a large desert at the end of the forest.

sn: तचाप्यतीत्य नृपतिरुत्तमाश्रमसंयुतम्। मनःप्रह्लादजननं दृष्टिकान्तमतीव च॥
en: Having passed over this her bless desert, the king came to a forest full of holy hermitages. It was beautiful to the eyes and delightful to the heart.

sn: शीतमारुतसंयुक्तं जगामान्यन्महद् वनम्। पुष्पितैः पादपैः कीर्णमतीव सुखशाद्वलम्॥ विपुलं मधुरारावैर्नादितं विहगैस्तथा। पुंस्कोकिलनिनादैश्च झिल्लीकगणनादितम्॥
en: It was cool and it breathed delightful breeze. It was full of trees covered with flowers. It extended far and wide in green soft grass. It echoed with the sweet songs of the birds. It resounded with the sweet notes of the male Kokila and the shrill cries of cicadas.

sn: प्रवृद्धविटपैर्वृक्षः सुखच्छायैः समावृतम्। षट्पदाघूर्णिततलं लक्ष्म्या परमया युतम्॥
en: It contained magnificent trees withstretched out branches, which had formed pleasant shady canopies. The bees hovered over the flowery creepers and beautiful groves were every where.

sn: नापुष्पः पादपः कश्चिन्नाफलो नापि कण्टकी। षट्पदैर्नाप्यपाकीर्णस्तस्मिन् वै काननेऽभवत्।॥
en: There was no tree without flowers and fruits; there was no shrub with prickles on them; there was no plant that had no bees swarming around it.

sn: विहगैर्नादितं पुष्पैरलंकृतमतीव च। सर्वर्तुकुसुमैर्वृक्षैः सुखच्छायैः समावृतम्॥
en: The whole forest resounded with the sweet songs of the birds; and it was decked with all the beautiful flowers of all the seasons. It was full of pleasant shades of blossoming trees.

sn: मनोरमं महेष्वासो विवेश वनमुत्तमम्। मारुताकलितास्तत्र द्रुमाः कुसुमशाखिनः॥ पुष्पवृष्टिं विचित्रां तु व्यसृजंस्ते पुनः पुनः। दिवःस्पृशोऽथ संघुष्टाः पक्षिभिर्मधुरस्वनैः॥
en: Such was the charming and excellent forest that the great bow-man (Dushyanta) entered. The trees, decked with flowers and waved with the soft breeze. Showered sweet flowers, again and again, on the head of the king.

sn: विरेजुः पादपास्तत्र विचित्रकुसुमाम्बराः। तेषां तत्र प्रवालेषु पुष्पभारावनामिषु॥ रुवन्ति रावान् मधुरान् षट्पदा मधुलिप्सवः। तत्र प्रदेशांश्च बहून् कुसुमोत्करमण्डितान्॥ लतागृहपरिक्षिप्तान् मनसः प्रीतिवर्धनान्। सम्पश्यन् सुमहातेजा बभूव मुदितस्तदा॥
en: Clad with the flowery attire of many colours, the sweet singing birds sitting on their branches hanging with the weight of flowers, the busy bees tempted by honey buzzing in sweet chorus around their blossoms, stood many trees (in that forest). There were innumerable bowers of creepers covered with thick clusters of flowers. The greatly energetic king was much pleased and charmed with the scenery.

sn: परस्पराश्लिष्टशाखैः पादपैः कुसुमान्वितैः। अशोभत वनं तत् तु महेन्द्रध्वजसंनिभैः॥
en: The trees, with its flowery branches, entwining with one another, looked exceedingly beautiful and appeared like so many Indra's poles.

sn: सिद्धचारणसंधैश्च गन्धर्वाप्सरसां गणैः। सेवितं वनमत्यर्थं मत्तवानरकिन्नरम्॥
en: It was the abode of the Siddhas, the Charanas, the various sorts of Gandharvas, the Apsaras, the monkeys and the Kinnaras, all drunk with joy.

sn: सुखः शीतः सुगन्धी च पुष्परेणुवहोऽनिलः। परिक्रामन् वने वृक्षानुपैतीव रिरंसया॥
en: Pleasant, cool and fragrant breezes, mixed with the effluvia of sweet flowers, blew every where and appeared as if they had come there to play with the trees.

sn: एवंगुणसमायुक्तं ददर्श स वनं नृपः। नदीकच्छोद्भवं कान्तमुच्छ्रितध्वजसंनिभम्॥
en: The king saw that forest endued with such beauties. It was situated in the delta of a river and looked like a pole erected in Indra's honour.

sn: प्रेक्षमाणो वनं तत् तु सुप्रहृष्टविहङ्गमम्। आश्रमप्रवरं रम्यं ददर्श च मनोरमम्॥
en: The king saw in that forest, the abode of ever cheerful birds, a charming and delightful hermitage of ascetics.

sn: नानावृक्षसमाकीर्णं सम्प्रज्वलितपावकम्। तं तदाप्रतिमं श्रीमानाश्रमं प्रत्यपूजयत्॥
en: It was surrounded by many trees and the holy fire was burning within it. He (the king) worshipped that matchless hermitage.

sn: यतिभिर्वालखिल्यैश्च वृतं मुनिगान्वितम्। अग्न्यगारैश्च बहुभिः पुष्पसंस्तरसंस्तृतम्॥
en: He saw innumerable Yatis, Valakhilyas and other Munis sitting there in that hermitage). It was adorned with rooms containing the sacrificial fire. The flowers, dropping from the trees, had made a beautiful carpet on the ground.

sn: महाकच्छैङ्घहद्भिश्च विभ्राजितमतीव च। मालिनीमभितोराजन् नदी पुण्यां सुखोदकाम्॥ नैकपक्षिगणाकीर्णां तपोवनमनोरमाम्। तत्र व्यालमृगान् सौम्यान् पश्यन् प्रीतिमवाप सः॥
en: The place looked very beautiful with the tall trees with their large trunks. O king, the transparent and sacred river Malini flowed by it. The river was charming to the ascetics and abounded with every species of water-fowls. He (the king) was much delighted to see the innocent deer-cubs playing (playfully) on her banks.

sn: तं चाप्रतिस्थः श्रीमानाश्रमं प्रत्यपद्यत। देवलोकप्रतीकाशं सर्वतः सुमनोहरम्॥
en: Thereupon, the king, whose chariot no foe could obstruct, entered that charming hermitage, exceedingly beautiful all over and which was like the region of heaven.

sn: नदीं चाश्रमसंश्लिष्टां पुण्यतोयां ददर्श सः। सर्वप्राणभृतां तत्र जननीमिव धिष्ठिताम्॥
en: He saw that the hermitage was situated on the banks of the river, a most sacred one and she flowed as the mother of all the creatures living there.

sn: सचक्रवाकपुलिनां पुष्पफेनप्रवाहिनीम्। सकिन्नरगणावासां वानरःनिषेविताम्॥
en: Milk-white waves played on her breast. Chakravakas sported on her banks. It was the abode of the Kinnaras and it was frequented by the monkeys and the bears.

sn: पुण्यस्वाध्यायसंघुष्टां पुलिनैरुपशोभिताम्। मत्तवारणशार्दूलभुजगेन्द्रनिषेविताम्॥
en: The holy ascetics, engaged in study and meditation, lived there on the beautiful banks of that river. It was frequented by the intoxicated elephants, tigers and great snakes.

sn: तस्यास्तीरे भगवतः काश्यपस्य महात्मनः। आश्रमप्रवरं रम्यं महर्षिगणसेवितम्॥
en: On the banks of that river, stood the excellent and charming hermitage of the illustrious Rishi, (the descendant of) Kashyapa, frequented by many great ascetic Rishis.

sn: नदीमाश्रमसम्बद्धां दृष्ट्वाऽऽश्रमपदं तथा। चकाराभिप्रवेशाय मतिं स नृपतिस्तदा॥
en: Having seen the river and the hermitage he desired to enter into that sacred place.

sn: अलंकृतं द्वीपवत्या मालिन्या रम्यतीरया। नरनारायणस्थानं गङ्गयेवोपशोभितम्॥
en: The river was studded with many islands with beautiful and charming shores. It looked like the abode of Nara and Narayana, beautified with the river Ganges.

sn: मत्तबहिणसंघुष्टं प्रविवेश महद् वनम्। तत् स चैत्ररथप्रख्यं समुपेत्य नरर्षभः॥
en: The best of men then entered that hermitage, which was resounding with the notes of the intoxicated pea-cocks and which appeared like the gardens of Chitraratha of Kubera.

sn: अतीवगुणसम्पन्नमनिर्देश्यं च वर्चसा। महर्षि काश्यपं द्रष्टुमथ कण्वं तपोधनम्॥
en: He desired to see the great ascetic Rishi, the illustrious Kanva, of the lineage of Kashyapa, the possessor of all virtues and who was too effulgent to be looked at.

sn: ध्वजिनीमश्वसम्बाधां पदातिगजसंकुलाम्। अवस्थाप्य वनद्वारि सेनामिदमुवाच सः॥
en: Halting his army of flag-holders, cavalry, infantry and elephants at the out-skirt of the

sn: मुनि विरजसं द्रष्टुं गमिष्यामि तपोधनम्। काश्यपं स्थीयतामत्र यावदागमनं मम॥
en: “I shall go to see the mighty ascetic, the son of Kashyapa, who is free from Rajoguna. Stay here till I return."

sn: तद् वनं नन्दनप्रख्यमासाद्य मनुजेश्वरः। क्षुत्पिपासे जहौ राजा मुदं चावाप पुष्कलाम्॥
en: The king forgot his hunger and thirst and derived infinite pleasure as soon as he entered that forest, like Nandana, (the garden of Indra.)

sn: सामात्यो राजलिङ्गानि सोऽपनीय नराधिपः। पुरोहितसहायश्च जगामाश्रममुत्तमम्॥
en: The king, having laid aside all signs of royalty, entered that excellent hermitage with his Minister and Priest only.

sn: दिदृक्षुस्तत्र तमृषि तपोराशिमथाव्ययम्। ब्रह्मलोकप्रतीकाशमाश्रमं सोऽभिवीक्ष्य ह। षट्पदोद्गीतसंघुष्टं नानाद्विजगणायुतम्॥
en: He desired to see that Rishi who was an indestructible mass of ascetic merit. He saw that the hermitage was like the region of Brahma. Bees were sweetly buzzing and birds were pouring forth their melodies.

sn: ऋचो बह्वचमुख्यैश्च प्रेर्यमाणाः पदक्रमैः। शुश्राव मनुजव्याघ्रो विततेष्विह कर्मसु॥
en: That best of men heard in one place the chanting of the Rigveda with the proper intention by the best of Brahmanas.

sn: यज्ञविद्याङ्गविद्भिश्च यजुर्विद्भिश्च शोभितम्। मधुरैः सामगीतैश्च ऋषिभिर्नियतव्रतैः॥ भारुण्डसामगीताभिरथर्वशिरसोद्गतः। यतात्मभिः सुनियतैः शुशुभे स तदाश्रमः॥
en: That hermitage was beautified with Brahmanas, learned in the Angas of Yajnavidya, reciting the hymns of Yajur-veda, The Rishis of rigid vows were reciting Saman hymns in harmonious strains. That time the hermitage aorned with Brahmanas who controlled their senses were reciting the Saman songs of Atharvashiras known as Bharunda.

sn: अथर्ववेदप्रवराः पूगयज्ञियसामगाः। संहितामीरयन्ति स्म पदक्रमयुतां तु ते॥ शब्दसंस्कारसंयुक्तैर्बुवद्भिश्चापरैर्द्विजैः। नादितः स बभौ श्रीमान् ब्रह्मलोक इवापरः॥
en: Brahmanas, learned in the Atharva Veda, reciting the Sanhitas according to the proper rules of voice. At other places, Brahmanas learned in the science of ortheopy, were reciting Mantras of other kinds. That holy hermitage, resounding with these holy sounds, did really look like the region of Brahma.

sn: यज्ञसंस्कारविद्भिश्च क्रमशिक्षाविशारदैः। न्यायतत्त्वात्मविज्ञानसम्पन्नैर्वेदपारगैः॥ नानावाक्यसमाहारसमवायविशारदैः। विशेषकार्यविद्धिश्च मोक्षधर्मपरायणैः॥ स्थापनाक्षेपसिद्धान्तपरमार्थज्ञतां गतः। शब्दच्छन्दोनिरुक्तज्ञैः कालज्ञानविशारदैः॥ द्रव्यकर्मगुणज्ञैश्च कार्यकारणवेदिभिः। पक्षिवानररुतज्ञैश्च व्यासग्रन्थसमाश्रितैः॥ नानाशास्त्रेषु मुख्यैश्च शुश्राव स्वनमीरितम्। लोकायतिकमुख्यैश्च समन्तादनुनादितम्॥
en: There were many Brahmanas who were experts in the art of making sacrificial platforms and in the rules of Krama in sacrifice. There were many other learned in Nyaya, (Logic) and mental sciences; and many having complete knowledge of the Veda. There were those that were learned in the meanings of every kind of expressions, those that were experts in performing special rites, those that knew the Moksha-dharma. Those that were well-versed in establishing propositions, rejecting superfluous causes and were learned in the science of words, of prosody and of Nirukta, those that were learned in the science of Time (Astrology). In the properties of matter, in the fruits of sacrificial rites, those that possessed a knowledge of causes and effects, those that understood the languages of monkeys and birds and those that were wellread in all large treatises. And various Shastras. The king, as he proceeded, heard their incantations and chanting, which were capable of charming all human arts.

sn: तत्र तत्र च विप्रेन्द्रान् नियतान् संशितव्रतान्। जपहोमपरान् विप्रान् ददर्श परवीरहा॥
en: The destroyer of the enemy's army, (Dushyanta), saw around him innumerable learned Brahmanas of rigid vows who were all engaged in japa and homa.

sn: आसनानि विचित्राणि रुचिराणि महीपतिः। प्रयत्नोपहितानि स्म दृष्ट्वा विस्मयमागमत्॥
en: The king was much astonished to see the beautiful carpets which these Brahmanas offered him (for his seat).

sn: देवतायतनानां च प्रेक्ष्य पूजां कृतां द्विजैः। ब्रह्मलोकस्थमात्मानं मेने स नृपसत्तमः॥
en: That best of kings, seeing the rites with which the Brahmanas worshipped the deities, thought himself in the land of Brahma.

sn: स काश्यपतपोगुप्तमाश्रमप्रवरं शुभम्। नातृप्यत् प्रेक्षमाणो वै तपोवनगुणैर्युतम्॥ वृतं समन्तादृषिभिस्तपोधनैः। विवेश सामात्यपुरोहितोऽरिहा विविक्तमत्यर्थमनोहरं शुभम्॥
en: The more the king saw that auspicious and sacred hermitage of the son of Kashyapa (Kanva), protected by that Rishi's ascetic virtues and endued with all the requisites of a holy retreat, more he desired to see it. He was not satisfied with this cursory view of the beautiful hermitage). The destroyer of foes, accompanied by his Minister and his Priest, then entered that charming and sacred hermitage of the son of Kashyapa, inhabited by the great ascetic Rishis of rigid vows.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततोऽगच्छन्महाबाहुरेकोऽमात्यान् विसृज्य तान्। नापश्यचाश्रमे तस्मिंस्तमृषि संशितव्रतम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having proceeded further, leaving behind him all his attendants that mighty, armed king entered the hermitage alone but he did not find there the Rishi of rigid vows, (Kanva).

sn: सोऽपश्यमानस्तमृषि शून्यं दृष्ट्वा तथाऽऽश्रमम्। उवाच क इहेत्युचैर्वनं संनादयन्निव॥
en: Having seen that the Rishi's hermitage was empty, he hailed aloud, "Ho, who is here?" And his voice was echoed in the forest.

sn: श्रुत्वाथ तस्य तं शब्दं कन्या श्रीरिव रूपिणी। निश्चक्रामाश्रमात् तस्मात् तापसीवेषधारिणी॥
en: Hearing his voice, a maiden, in the garb of ascetics, as beautiful as Shree (Lakshmi), came out of the hermitage.

sn: सा तं दृष्दैव राजानं दुष्यन्तमसितेक्षणा। स्वागतं त इति क्षिप्रमुवाच प्रतिपूज्य च॥
en: No sooner that black-eyed damsel saw the king Dushyanta, that she instantly bade him welcome and worshipped him in due form,

sn: आसनेनार्चयित्वा च पाद्यनायेण चैव हि। पप्रच्छानामयं राजन् कुशलं च नराधिपम्॥
en: She respected him with offering a seat, she gave him water to wash his feet and she then offered him the argha. Having done all this, O king, she then enquired after his health and peace.

sn: यथावदर्चयित्वाथ पृष्ट्वा चानामयं तदा। उवाच स्मयमानेव किं कार्य क्रियतामिति॥
en: Having thus honoured him in due form and enquired about his health and peace, the maiden most respectfully asked the king, "What should be done?”

sn: तामब्रवीत् ततो राजा कन्यां मधुरभाषिणीम्। दृष्ट्वा चैवानवद्यागी यथावत् प्रतिपूजितः॥
en: Having been thus honoured in due form, the king replied to that sweet-speeched and

sn: आगतोऽहं महाभागमृर्षि कण्वमुपासितुम्। क्व गतो भगवान् भद्रे तन्ममाचक्ष्व शोभने।॥
en: "I have come to worship the greatly blessed Rishi Kanva. O amiable and beautiful lady, tell me where has the illustrious man gone?"

sn: शकुन्तलोवाच गत: पिता मे भगवान् फलान्याहर्तुमाश्रमात्। मुहूर्तं सम्प्रतीक्षस्व द्रष्टास्येनमुपागतम्॥
en: Shakuntala said : My noble father has gone away from the hermitage to collect fruits. Kindly wait for a moment and you will see him when he will come.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच अपश्यमानस्तमृषि तथा चोक्तस्तया च सः। तां दृष्ट्वा च वरारोहां श्रीमती चारुहासिनीम्॥ विभ्राजमानां वपुषा तपसा च दमेन च। रूपयौवनसम्पन्नामित्युवाच महीपतिः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : The king, having not seen the Rishi and having been thus addressed by the maiden, saw that she was exceedingly beautiful, she was an exquisite beauty of sweet smiles and a lady of perfect symmetry of shape. She was in the bloom of her youth and beauty; she was adorned with the beauty of faultless features, hard asceticism and sweet humility. The king

sn: का त्वं कस्यासि सुश्रोणि किमर्थं चागता वनम्। एवंरूपगुणोपेता कुतस्त्वमसि शोभने॥
en: "Who are you? O beautiful lady, whose daughter are you? Why have you come into this forest? ( beautiful lady, accomplished and beautiful as you are, whence have you come here?"

sn: दर्शनादेव हि शुभे त्वया मेऽपहतं मनः। इच्छामि त्वामहं ज्ञातुं तन्ममाचक्ष्व शोभने॥
en: O charming lady, you have stolen my heart at the very first glance. I desire to know all about you. O beautiful lady, tell me all.”

sn: एवमुक्ता तु सा कन्या तेन राज्ञा तमाश्रमे। उवाच हसती वाक्यमिदं सुमधुराक्षरम्॥
en: Having been thus addressed by the king in that lermitage, the maiden smilingly replied to him in sweet words.

sn: कण्वस्याहं भगवतो दुष्यन्त दुहिता मता। तपस्विनो धृतिमतो धर्मज्ञस्य महात्मनः॥
en: "O (king) Dushyanta, I am the daughter of the illustrious, virtuous, wise and high-souled ascetic Kanva.

sn: दुष्यन्त उवाच ऊर्ध्वरेता महाभागे भगवाँल्लोकपूजितः। चलेद्धि वृत्ताद् धर्मोऽपि न चलेत् संशितव्रतः॥
en: Dushyanta said : The illustrious and highly blessed Rishi is worshipped by all the world. He has completely controlled his sexual passions. Even Dharma may fall from the right path, but an ascetic of rigid vows can never fall from it.

sn: कथं त्वं तस्य दुहिता सम्भूता वरवर्णिनी। संशयो मे महानत्र तन्मे छेत्तुमिहार्हसि॥
en: O beautiful and charming lady, how can you be his daughter? You should dispel from my mind this great doubt of mine.

sn: शकुन्तलोवाच यथायमागमो मह्यं यथा चेदमभूत् पुरा। शृणु राजन् यथातत्त्वं यथास्मि दुहिता मुनेः॥
en: Shakuntala said : O king! hear, what I have learnt (from the Rishi), regarding all that happened to me and how I became the daughter of the Rishi (Kanva).

sn: ऋषिः कश्चिदिहागम्य मम जन्माभ्यचोदयत्। तस्मै प्रोवाच भगवान् यथा तच्छणु पार्थिव॥
en: Once on a time, a Rishi came here and asked about my birth. () king, hear what the illustrious Rishi (Kanva) told him about me.

sn: कण्व उवाच तप्यमानः किल पुरा विश्वामित्रो महत् तपः। सुभृशं तापयामास शक्रं सुरगणेश्वरम्॥
en: Kanva said: In days of yore, Vishvamitra were engaged in austere asceticism and he thus alarmed Indra, the king of the celestials.

sn: तपसा दीप्तवीर्योऽयं स्थानान्मां च्यावयेदिति। भीत: पुरंदरस्तस्मान्मेनकामिदमब्रवीत्॥
en: He (Indra) thought that the Rishi by his great ascetic penances would hurl him from his high seat in heaven. Being thus alarmed, he called Menaka and told her,

sn: गुणैरप्सरसां दिव्यैर्मेनके त्वं विशिष्यसे। श्रेयो मे कुरु कल्याणि यत् त्वां वक्ष्यामि तच्छृणु॥२२ असावादित्यसंकाशो विश्वामित्रो महातपाः। तप्यमानस्तपो घोरं मम कम्पयते मनः॥
en: "O Menaka, you are the best of all celestial Apsaras. O amiable girl, do me this service. Listen to what I say. The great ascetic Vishvamitra, as effulgent as the Sun, is now engaged in great asceticism and therefore my heart is trembling.

sn: मेनके तव भारोऽयं विश्वामित्र: सुमध्यमे। शंसितात्मा सुदुर्धर्ष उग्रे तपसि वर्तते॥
en: O Menaka, O slender-waisted girl, it is your business. You must see Vishvamitra, whose soul is rapt in contemplation and who is deeply engaged in the austere penances.

sn: समां न च्यावयेत् स्थानात् तं वै गत्वा प्रलोभय। चर तस्य तपोविघ्नं कुरु मेऽविघ्नमुत्तमम्॥
en: He may displace me from my (high) seat (in heaven). Go and tempt him. Frustrating his asceticism, do my good.

sn: रूपयौवनमाधुर्यचेष्टितस्मितभाषणैः। लोभयित्वा वरारोहे तपसस्तं निवर्तय॥
en: O beautiful girl, win him from his asceticism, by tempting him with your beauty, youth, agreeableness, arts, smiles and speech.

sn: मेनकोवाच महातेजाः स भगवांस्तथैव च महातपाः। कोपनश्च तथा ह्येनं जानाति भगवानपि॥
en: Menaka said: That illustrious Rishi, is a great ascetic and is greatly effulgent; your illustrious self known also that he is very wrathful.

sn: तेजसस्तपसश्चैव कोपस्य च महात्मनः। त्वमप्युद्विजसे यस्य नोद्विजेयमहं कथम्॥
en: The energy, the asceticism and the wrath of that illustrious man have made even you anxious. Why should I not be afraid of him?

sn: महाभागं वसिष्ठं यः पुत्ररिष्टैर्व्ययोजयत्। क्षत्रजातश्च यः पूर्वमभवद् ब्राह्मणो बलात्॥ शौचार्थं यो नदी चक्रे दुर्गमां बहुभिर्जलैः। यां तां पुण्यतमां लोके कौशिकीति विदुर्जनाः॥
en: He made even the illustrious Vasishtha to suffer the grief of the premature death of his sons. He was originally a Kshatriya, but has become a Brahmana by his own strength (of asceticism). He created a deep river of strong currents for the purposes of ablutions. That holy river is still known in the world by the name of Kaushika.

sn: बभार यत्रास्य पुरा काले दुर्गे महात्मनः। दारान्मतङ्गो धर्मात्मा राजर्षिाधतां गतः॥
en: Here (on the banks of this river) the wife (of this illustrious man) was maintained during a famine by the royal sage Matanga, who was living there as a hunter (under a curse)

sn: अतीतकाले दुर्भिक्षे अभ्येत्य पुनराश्रमम्। मुनिः पारेति नद्या वै नाम चक्रे तदा प्रभुः॥
en: O Lord, this illustrious man, after the famine was over, came back to his hermitage and gave the river the name of Para,

sn: मतङ्गं याजयाञ्चक्रे यत्र प्रीतमनाः स्वयम्। त्वं च सोमं भयाद् यस्य गतः पातुं सुरेश्वर॥
en: Being very much pleased with Matanga, this illustrious man became his priest for the purpose of sacrifice. O king of the celestials, out of fear you yourself went to that sacrifice to drink this Soma.

sn: चकारान्यं च लोकं वै क्रुद्धो नक्षत्रसम्पदा। प्रतिश्रवणपूर्वाणि नक्षत्राणि चकार यः। गुरुशापहतस्यापि त्रिशङ्कोः शरणं ददौ॥
en: This illustrious man created in anger another world with stars; he created numerous other stars, beginning from Shravana. This illustrious man gave protection to Trishanku, cursed by his preceptor.

sn: एतानि यस्य कर्माणि तस्याहं भृशमुद्विजे। यथासौ न दहेत् क्रुद्धस्तथाऽऽज्ञापय मां विभो॥
en: I am afraid to go to a man whose deeds are such. O Lord, ordain that which may prevent him from burning me in anger.

sn: तेजसा निर्दहेल्लोकान् कम्पयेद् धरणी पदा। संक्षिपेच महामेरुं तूर्णमावर्तयेद् दिशः॥
en: He burn the worlds with his effulgence; he can make the earth quake by a kick; he can uproot the great Meru (mountain) and hurl it to a great distance and go round the ten points of the earth in a moment. can

sn: तादृशं तपसा युक्तं प्रदीप्तमिव पावकम्। कथमस्मद्विधा नारी जितेन्द्रियमभिस्पृशेत्॥
en: How can a woman (like my humble self) touch such a man who is full of ascetic virtues, who is as blazing as the blazing fire and who has completely controlled his passions.

sn: हुताशनमुखं दीप्तं सूर्यचन्द्राक्षितारकम्। कालजिह्व सुरश्रेष्ठ कथमस्मद्विधा स्पृशेत्॥
en: His mouth is as blazing as the fire, the pupils of his eyes are like the sun and the moon and his tongue is like Yama himself. O best of the celestials, how can women like ourselves touch him?

sn: यमश्च सोमश्च महर्षयश्च साध्या विश्वे वालखिल्याश्च सर्वे। एतेऽपि यस्योद्विजन्ते प्रभावात् तस्मात् कस्मान्मादृशी नोद्विजेत॥
en: Yama, Soma, great Rishis, the Sadhyas, the Vishvedevas, the Valakhilyas, all are alarmed at the thought of his prowess. Why should not a woman (like myself) be afraid of him?

sn: मृषेर्न गच्छेयमहं सुरेन्द्र। रक्षां तु मे चिन्तय देवराज यथा त्वदर्थं रक्षिताहं चरेयम्॥
en: O king of the celestials, commanded by you somehow or other I must go to that Rishi. But, O king of the celestials, devise some means by which, under your protection, I can safely inove about him.

sn: काम त मे मारुतस्तत्र वास: प्रक्रीडिताया विवृणोतु देवा भवेच मे मन्मथस्तत्र कार्ये सहायभूतस्तु तव प्रसादात्॥
en: Ocelestial ! when I shall be near the Rishi, Maruta (wind) should be there and rob me of my cloth. Manmatha (the god of love) should at your command help me in my this work.

sn: वनाच्च वायुः सुरभिः प्रवायात् तस्मिन् काले तमृषि लोभयन्त्याः। स्ततोययौसाऽऽश्रमं कौशिकस्य॥
en: Let the wind carry sweet fragrance from the wood to tempt the Rishi. Having said this and having seen that all that she wanted had been duly provided, she went to the hermitage of the great Kaushika, (Vishvamitra).

sn: कण्व उवाच एवमुक्तस्तया शक्रः संदिदेश सदागतिम्। प्रातिष्ठत तदा काले मेनका वायुना सह॥
en: Kanva said: Having been thus addressed, Indra commanded the wind to be present with Menaka when she would be present before the Rishi.

sn: अथापश्यद् वरारोहा तपसा दग्धकिल्बिषम्। विश्वामित्रं तप्यमानं मेनका भीरुराश्रमे॥
en: The timid and the beautiful girl then entered the hermitage and saw Vishvamitra, who had destroyed all his sins by penances and who was still engaged in austere penances.

sn: अभिवाद्य ततः सा तं प्राक्रीडदृषिसंनिधौ। अपोवाह च वासोऽस्या मारुतः शशिसंनिभम्॥
en: Having saluted the Rishi, she then began to sport near him. At this very time Maruta robbed of her cloth, which was as white as the moon (light.)

sn: सागच्छत् त्वरिता भूमि वासस्तदभिलिप्सती। स्मयमानेव सव्रीडं मारुतं वरवर्णिनी॥
en: And that beautiful girl in great bashfulness began to run after the cloth to catch it and she appeared to express her great annoyance at the conduct of Maruta (wind).

sn: पश्यतस्तस्य तत्ररप्यग्निसमतेजसः। विश्वामित्रस्ततस्तां तु विषमस्थामनिन्दिताम्॥ गृद्धां वाससि सम्भ्रान्तां मेनकां मुनिसत्तमः। अनिर्देश्यवयोरूपामपश्यद् विवृतां तदा॥
en: She did all this before that great Rishi Vishvamitra, as effulgent as the fire and he saw her in that state. He marked that she was of faultless features. In her nude state, the best of the Rishis saw that Menaka was exceedingly beautiful, with no marks of age on her person.

sn: तस्या रूपगुणान् दृष्ट्वा स तु विप्रर्षभस्तदा। चकार भावं संसर्गात् तया कामवशं गतः॥
en: Seeing her great beauty and accomplishments, that best of Rishis was filled with desire and wished for her company.

sn: न्यमन्त्रयत चाप्येनां सा चाप्यैच्छदनिन्दिता। तौ तत्र सुचिरं कालमुभौ व्यहरतां तदा॥ रममाणौ यथाकामं यथैकदिवसं तथा। जनयामास स मुनिर्मेनकायां शकुन्तलाम्॥ प्रस्थे हिमवतो रम्ये मालिनीमभितो नदीम्। जातमुत्सृज्य तं गर्भ मेनका मालिनीमनु॥ कृतकार्या ततस्तूर्णमगच्छच्छक्रसंसदम्। तं वने विजने गर्भ सिंहव्याघ्रसमाकुले॥ दृष्ट्वा शयानं शकुनाः समन्तात् पर्यवारयन्। नेमां हिंस्युर्वने बालां क्रव्यादा मांसगृद्धिनः॥
en: He invited her to come to him and that faultless featured beauty too accepted his invitation. They then passed many days in each others' company. Sporting with each other, they passed many years and thought that it was but only a day. That Rishi begot Shakuntala on her. Menaka went to the banks of the river Malini which passed playfully through the beautiful valley of the Himalaya mountains and there she gave birth to a daughter. She then left the child there (on the banks of the river) and went away. Thus having been successful in her mission, she soon returned to Indra. Some vultures, seeing that the child lay in the deep forest abounding in lions and tigers, sat round it to protect it from harm, so that no carnivorous animals might take her life.

sn: पर्यरक्षन्त तां तत्र शकुन्ता मेनकात्मजाम्। उपस्प्रष्टुं गतश्चाहमपश्यं शयितामिमाम्॥ निर्जने विपिने रम्ये शकुन्तैः परिवारिताम्। आनयित्वा ततश्चैनां दुहितृत्वे न्यवेशयम्॥ शरीरकृत् प्राणदाता यस्य चान्नानि भुञ्जते। क्रमेणैते त्रयोऽप्युक्ताः पितरो धर्मशासने॥ ॥
en: The vultures protected the life of Menaka's child. I had gone there to perform my ablutions. I saw the child lying. In the deep solitude of the forest, surrounded by the vultures. Bringing her here, I have made her my daughter. According to the scriptures, the maker of the body, the protector of life and the giver of food, these three, are in their order considered to be fathers.

sn: निर्जने तु वने यस्माच्छकुन्तैः परिवारिता। शकुन्तलेति नामास्याः कृतं चापि ततो मया॥
en: Because she was found in the solitude of the forest, protected by the Shakuntas (birds), she has been named Shakuntala (protected by birds.)

sn: एवं दुहितरं विद्धि मम विप्र शकुन्तलाम्। शकुन्तला च पितरं मन्यते मामनिन्दिता॥
en: O Brahmana, know that it is thus that Shakuntala has become my daughter. And faultless Shakuntala also regards me as her father.

sn: शकुन्तलोवाच एतदाचष्ट पृष्टः सन् मम जन्म महर्षये। सुतां कण्वस्य मामेवं विद्धि त्वं मनुजाधिप।॥ कण्वं हि पितरं मन्ये पितरं स्वमजानती। इति ते कथितं राजन् यथावृत्तं श्रुतं मया॥
en: Shakuntala said: Thus the great Rishi (Kanva), when asked, told (the Brahmana) the account of my birth. O king of men, you must know that I have thus become the daughter of Kanva. Not knowing who is my real father, I regard Kanva as my father. Thus have I told you, O king, all that I heard about my birth.

sn: दुष्यन्त उवाच सुव्यक्तं राजपुत्री त्वं यथा कल्याणि भाषसे। भार्या मे भव सुश्रोणि ब्रूहि किं करवाणि ते॥
en: Dushyanta said : O princess, O blessed lady, all that you have said is well-spoken. O beautiful lady, be my wife. Tell me what I shall do (for you).

sn: सुवर्णमालां वासांसि कुण्डले परिहाटके। नानापत्तनजे शुभ्रे मणिरत्ने च शोभने॥ आहरामि तवाद्याहं निष्कादीन्यजिनानि च। सर्वं राज्यं तवाद्यास्तु भार्या मे भव शोभने॥
en: I shall present you, this very day, gold and golden-garlands, robes, ear-rings, white and beautiful pearls and gems, golden coins and finest carpets, coilected from various countries. Let the whole of my kingdom be yours. O beautiful lady, be my wife.

sn: गान्धर्वेण च मां भीरु विवाहेनैहि सुन्दरि। विवाहानां हि रम्भोरु गान्धर्वः श्रेष्ठ उच्यते॥
en: O handsome lady, O timid maiden, O beauty of tapering thighs, marry me according to the Gandharva form, for the form of marriage is said to be the best.

sn: शकुन्तलोवाच फलाहारो गतो राजन् पिता मे इत आश्रमात्। मुहूर्तं सम्प्रतीक्षश्च स मां तुभ्यं प्रदास्यति॥
en: Shakuntala said: O king, my father has gone from the hermitage to collect fruits. Kindly wait for a moment. He will bestow me upon you.

sn: दुष्यन्त उवाच इच्छामि त्वां वरारोहे भजमानामनिन्दिते। त्वदर्थं मां स्थितं विद्धि त्वद्गतं हि मनो मम॥
en: Dushyanta said : O beautiful lady, O faultless beauty, I desire that you yourself should accept me. Know that I exist for you. Know also, my heart is completely in you.

sn: आत्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव गतिरात्मैव चात्मनः। आत्मनो मित्रमात्मैव तथाऽऽत्मा चात्मनः पिता। आत्मनैवात्मनो दानं कर्तुमर्हसि धर्मतः॥
en: One is certainly one's own friend; one can certainly depend upon one's own self. Therefore, according to the ordinance, you yourself should bestow your own self on others.

sn: अष्टावेव समासेन विवाहा धर्मतः स्मृताः। ब्राह्मो दैवस्तथैवार्षः प्राजापत्यस्तथासुरः॥ गान्धर्वो राक्षसश्चैव पैशाचश्चाष्टमः स्मृतः। तेषां धान् यथापूर्वं मनुः स्वायम्भुवोऽब्रवीत्॥
en: According to the ordinance, there are eight kinds of marriages, namely, Brahma, Daiva, Arsha, Prajapatya, Asura. Gandharva, Rakshasas and Paishacha. The son of the selfcreated (Brahma), Manu, has spoken which of these forms (of marriages) is appropriate to each of the four castes.

sn: प्रशस्ताश्चतुरः पूर्वान् ब्राह्मणस्योपधारय। षडानुपूर्व्या क्षत्रस्य विद्धि धाननिन्दिते॥
en: O faultless beauty, know that the first four forms are appropriate to the Brahmanas and the first six for Kshatriyas.

sn: राज्ञां तु राक्षसोऽप्युक्तो विट्शूद्रेष्वासुरः स्मृतः। पञ्चानां तु त्रयो धा अधौ द्वौ स्मृताविह॥
en: To the kings, even the Rakshasas form is permissible. The Asura form is permissible to the Vaishyas and Shudras. Of the first five (forms), three are proper and two improper.

sn: पैशाच आसुरश्चैव न कर्तव्यौ कदाचन। अनेन विधिना कार्यो धर्मस्यैषा गतिः स्मृता॥
en: The Paishacha and Asura forms should never be adopted (by any man). These are the ordinances of the scriptures and man should act according to them.

sn: गान्धर्वराक्षसौ क्षत्रे धौ तौ मा विशङ्किथाः। पृथग् वा यदि वा मिश्री कर्तव्यौ नात्र संशयः॥
en: The Gandharva and the Rakshasas forms are proper to the Kshatriyas, therefore, you need no entertain the least fear. There is not the least doubt that either according to one single form or according to the mixed form of these two, marriage is proper to us, (and we may be married).

sn: सा त्वं मम सकामस्य सकामा वरवर्णिनि। गान्धर्वेण विवाहेन भार्या भवितुमर्हसि॥
en: O beautiful lady, I am full of desire, so are you. You should, therefore, become my wife according to the Gandharva form.

sn: शकुन्तलोवाच यदि धर्मपथस्त्वेष यदि चात्मा प्रभुर्मम। प्रदाने पौरवश्रेष्ठ शृणु मे समयं प्रभो॥
en: Shakuntala said: ( best of the Puru race, if this are the dictates of the scriptures and if I am really my own disposer, know then my terms.

sn: सत्यं मे प्रतिजानीहि यथा वक्ष्याम्यहं रहः। मयि जायेत यः पुत्रः स भवेत् त्वदनन्तरः॥ युवराजो महाराज सत्यमेतद् ब्रवीमि ते। यद्येतदेवं दुष्यन्त अस्तु मे सङ्गमस्त्वया॥
en: Promise to give me what I ask, in this lonely place, alone, between ourselves. The son that will be here after born of me, will become the hire-apparent (to your throne). O Dushyanta, I tell you the truth. If this be the case, we may be united.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमस्त्विति तां राजा प्रत्युवाचाविचारयन्। अपि च त्वां हि नेष्यामि नगरं स्वं शुचिस्मिते॥
en: Vaishampayana said: The king, without taking time to consider the demand, told her at once, “O beauty of sweet smiles, let it be so. I shall even take you to my capital.

sn: यथा त्वमर्हा सुश्रोणि सत्यमेतद् ब्रवीमि ते। एवमुक्त्वा स राजर्षिस्तामनिन्दितगामिनीम्॥ जग्राह विधिवत् पाणावुवास च तया सह। विश्वास्य चैनां स प्रायादब्रवीच पुनः पुनः॥ प्रेषयिष्ये तवार्थाय वाहिनीं चतुरङ्गिणीम्। तया त्वां नाययिष्यामि निवासं स्वं शुचिस्मिते॥
en: O handsome maiden, I tell you the truth. You deserve all this. I promise to do what you ask. So saying, the royal sage, (Dushyanta) married the beautiful Shakuntala of graceful walking, according to the due rites; and she accepted him as her husband. He returned to his capital after assuring her of his promise. He repeatedly told her, “I shall send for you my troops of the four sorts. O beauty of sweet smiles, it is thus (with all honour). I shall take you to my capital."

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच इति तस्याः प्रतिश्रुत्य स नृपो जनमेजय। मनसा चिन्तयन् प्रायात् काश्यपं प्रति पार्थिवः॥ भगवांस्तपसा युक्तः श्रुत्वा किं किं न करिष्यति। एवं स चिन्तयन्नेव प्रविवेश स्वकं पुरम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : O Janamejaya, having thus promised to her, the king went away. The king, as he went (towards his capital), began to think of Kanva. (He thought), “What would the illustrious ascetic do when he would hear all. Thus thinking on his way, he entered his capital.

sn: मुहूर्तयाते तस्मिंस्तु कण्वोऽप्याश्रममागमत्। शकुन्तला च पितरं ह्रिया नोपजगाम तम्॥
en: The moment the king had gone away, Kanva came to the hermitage. But Shakuntala did not go out to receive her father for shame.

sn: विज्ञायाथ च तां कण्वो दिव्यज्ञानो महातपाः। उवाच भगवान् प्रीतः पश्यन् दिव्येन चक्षुषा॥
en: The great ascetic Kanva, possessed of spiritual knowledge (sight), knew all. Having thus seen everything with his spiritual sight, the illustrious man was pleased and saidत्वयाद्य भद्रे रहसि मामनादृत्य यः कृतः।

sn: पुंसा सह समायोगो न स धर्मोपघातकः॥
en: “O amiable child, the act that you have committed today in secret without having waited (to receive my permission), has not been destructive of your virtue.

sn: क्षत्रियस्य हि गान्धर्वो विवाहः श्रेष्ठ उच्यते। सकामायाः सकामेन निर्मन्त्रो रहसि स्मृतः॥
en: The marriage according to the Gandharva form, without Mantras and between a willing woman and a willing man, is said to be the best to a Kshatriya.

sn: धर्मात्मा च महात्मा च दुष्यन्तः पुरुषोत्तमः। अभ्यगच्छः पतिं यत् त्वं भजमानं शकुन्तले॥ महात्मा जनिता लोके पुत्रस्तव महाबलः। य इमां सागरापाङ्गीं कृत्स्नां भोक्ष्यति मेदिनीम्॥
en: The best of men Dushyanta, is virtuousminded and high-souled. O Shakuntala, you have accepted (this Dushyanta) for your husband. The son, whom you will give birth to, will be mighty and illustrious in this world. He will extend his sway over the whole of this earth bounded by the sea.

sn: परं चाभिप्रयातस्य चक्रं तस्य महात्मनः। भविष्यत्यप्रतिहतं सततं चक्रवर्तिनः :॥
en: When that illustrious king of kings (your son) will march out against his foes, his army will be irresistible to all opposition.

sn: ततः प्रक्षाल्य पादौ सा विश्रान्तं मुनिमब्रवीत्। विनिधाय ततो भारं संनिधाय फलानि च॥
en: Shakuntala, then came to her fatigued father and washed his feet. She took down the heavy load that was on his shoulder and placed the fruits in proper order. Then she said-

sn: शकुन्तलोवाच मया पतिवृतो राजा दुष्यन्तः पुरुषोत्तमः। तस्मै ससचिवाय त्वं प्रसादं कर्तुमर्हसि॥
en: Shakuntala said: (O father), you should give your grace to my husband, king Dushyanta, the best of men.

sn: कण्व उवाच प्रसन्न एव तस्याहं त्वत्कृते वरवर्णिनी। गृहाण च वरं मत्तस्त्वं शुभे यदभीप्सितम्॥
en: Kanva said: O beautiful child, I am prepared to bless him for your sake. But O blessed girl, receive from me the boon you desire to have.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततो धर्मिष्ठतां वने राज्याचास्खलनं तथा। शकुन्तला पौरवाणां दुष्यन्तहितकाम्यया॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Thereupon, Shakuntala, moved with the desire to do good to Dushyanta, asked the boon that Paurava kings should be ever virtuous and never to be deprived of their thrones.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच प्रतिज्ञाय तु दुष्यन्ते प्रतियाते शकुन्तलाम्। गर्भं सुषाव वामोरू: कुमारममितौजसम्॥ त्रिषु वर्षेषु पूर्णेषु दीप्तानलसमद्युतिम्। रूपौदार्यगुणोपेतं दौष्यन्ति जनमेजय॥
en: Vaishampayana said : When Dushyanta went away from the hermitage, making the (above) promises to Shakuntala, she gave birth to a boy of immeasurable energy. When the child grew only three years old, he became in splendour as blazing as the blazing fire. O Janamejaya, he was endued with great beauty, magnanimity and all accomplishments.

sn: जातकर्मादिसंस्कारं कण्वः पुण्यकृतां वरः। विधिवत् कारयामास वर्धमानस्य धीमतः॥
en: The best of pious men, Kanvas, performed all the rites ordained by the scriptures on that intelligent boy who began to grow up day by day.

sn: दन्तैः शुकैः शिखरिभिः सिंहसंहननो महान्। चक्राङ्कितकरः श्रीमान् महामूर्धा महाबलः॥
en: The boy was gifted with sharp, strong and pearly teeth; he was strong enough to kill lions, he had all auspicious signs on his palms, he had a broad forehead, he was beautiful and strong.

sn: कुमारो देवगर्भाभः स तत्राशु व्यवर्धत। षड्वर्ष एव बालः स कण्वाश्रमपदं प्रति॥ सिंहव्याघ्रान् वराहांश्च महिषांश्च गजांस्तथा। बबन्ध वृक्षे बलवानाश्रमस्य समीपतः॥
en: Like a celestial child, he began daily to grow up. When he grew six years old, he was so strong that he seized and bound tigers, boars, buffaloes and elephants to the trees that stood near the hermitage.

sn: आरोहन् दमयंश्चैव क्रीडंश्च परिधावति। ततोऽस्य नाम चक्रुस्ते कण्वाश्रमनिवासिनः॥ अस्त्वयं सर्वदमनः सर्वं हि दमयत्यसौ। स सर्वदमनो नाम कुमारः समपद्यत॥ विक्रमेणौजसा चैव बलेन च समन्वितः।
en: He rode on some of these wild beasts; he seized some of them and sometimes he pursued some of them in playful mood. The dwellers of the hermitage of Kanva, (finding all this), gave him a name. (They said,) “As he subjugated all beasts, let him be called Sarvadamana". Thus the prince came to be called Sarvadamana, endued as he was with great strength, energy and powers.

sn: तं कुमारमृषिर्दृष्ट्वा कर्म चास्यातिमानुषम्॥ समयो यौवराज्यायेत्यब्रवीच शकुन्तलाम्।
en: Seeing the extraordinary acts of the boy, the Rishi (Kanva) told Shakuntala that the time had come when he should be installed as the heir-apparent.

sn: तस्य तद् बलमाज्ञाय कण्वः शिष्यानुवाच ह॥ शकुन्तलामिमां शीघ्रं सहपुत्रामितो गृहात्। भर्तुः प्रापयतागारं सर्वलक्षणपूजिताम्॥
en: Seeing the great strength of the boy, Kanva spoke to his disciples thus, "Take Shakuntala with her son from the hermitage to the house of her husband, blessed with all auspicious signs."

sn: नारीणां चिरवासो हि बान्धवेषु न रोचते। कीर्तिचारित्रधर्मजस्तस्मान्नयत मा चिरम्॥
en: "It is not fit for women to live for ever in the house of their paternal or maternal relations. Such residence destroys their good name, good conduct and virtue. Therefore, take her to her husband's house without delay."

sn: तथेत्युक्त्वा तु ते सर्वे प्रातिष्ठन्त महौजसः। शकुन्तलां पुरस्कृत्य दुष्यन्तस्य पुरं प्रति॥
en: The greatly effulgent disciples (of Kanva), having promised to do it, started with Shakuntala and her son towards the city of Hastinapur.

sn: गृहीत्वामरगर्भाभं पुत्रं कमललोचनम्। आजगाम ततः सुभूर्दुष्यन्तं विदिताद् वनात्॥
en: That beauty of fair eye-brows, taking her lotus-eyed son of celestial beauty with her, left the forest where she had first met Dushyanta.

sn: अभिसृत्य च राजानं विदिता च प्रवेशिता। सह तेनैव पुत्रेण बालार्कसमतेजसा॥
en: Having sent words, she entered the royal court with her son, as effulgent as the morning sun. And she was then introduced to him.

sn: निवेदयित्वा ते सर्वे आश्रमं पुनरागताः। पूजयित्वा यथान्यायमब्रवीच शकुन्तला॥
en: The disciples of the Rishi, having told the king everything, returned to the hermitage. And Shakuntala, after duly worshipping the

sn: शकुन्तलोवाच अयं पुत्रस्त्वया राजन् यौवराज्येऽभिषिच्यताम्। त्वया ह्ययं सुतो राजन् मय्युत्पन्नः सुरोपमः। यथासमयमेतस्मिन् वर्तस्व पुरुषोत्तम॥
en: Shakuntala said : O King, this is your son. Let him be installed as your heir-apparent. O King, this god-like boy was begotten by you on me. O best of men, fulfil now the promise you made of me.

sn: यथा मत्सङ्गमे पूर्वं यः कृतः समयस्त्वया। तं स्मरस्व महाभाग कण्वाश्रमपदं प्रति॥
en: O illustrious man, call to your mind the agreement you made with me on the occasion of our marriage at the hermitage of Kanva.

sn: सोऽथ श्रुत्वैव तद् वाक्यं तस्या राजा स्मरन्नपि। अब्रवीन्न स्मरामीति कस्य त्वं दुष्टतापसि॥
en: Having heard her words, the King remembered everything, but he said, “I remember nothing. O wicked ascetic woman, to whom do you belong?"

sn: धर्मकामार्थसम्बन्धं न स्मरामि त्वया सह। गच्छ वा तिष्ठ वा कामं यद् वापीच्छसि तत् कुरु॥
en: "I do not remember to have any connection with you with regard to (either) Dharma, Artha and Kama. Go or stay or do whatever you please."

sn: सैवमुक्ता वरारोहा वीडितेव तपस्विनी। नि:संज्ञेव च दुःखेन तस्थौ स्थूणेव निश्चला॥
en: Thus being addressed, the beautiful ascetic lady was filled with shame. She lost her consciousness from grief and she stood like a wooden post.

sn: संरम्भामर्षताम्राक्षी स्फुरमाणौष्ठसम्पुटा। कटाक्षैर्निर्दहन्तीव तिर्यग् राजानमैक्षत॥
en: Soon became her eyes red like copper; her lips began to quiver; she cast upon the king her (angry) glances which seemed to burn him.

sn: आकारं गूहमानां च मन्युना च समीरिता। तपसा सम्भृतं तेजो धारयामास वै तदा।॥
en: Her rising anger and blazing fire of her asceticism she kept down with a great effort.

sn: सा मुहूर्तमिव ध्यात्वा दुःखामर्षसमन्विता। भर्तारमभिसम्प्रेक्ष्य क्रुद्धा वचनमब्रवीत्॥ जानन्नपि महाराज कस्मादेवं प्रभाषसे। न जानामीति निःशङ्कं यथान्यः प्राकृतो जनः॥
en: Collecting her thought in a moment, she thus addressed her husband looking straight at him in grief and in anger. “O great king, knowing everything, how can you, like a mean and inferior man, say that you know nothing'?

sn: अत्र ते हृदयं वेद सत्यस्यैवानृतस्य च। कल्याणं वद साक्ष्येण माऽऽत्मानमवमन्यथाः॥
en: Your heart is the witness to the truth or to the falsehood of my words. Therefore, speak the truth and do not degrade yourself.

sn: योऽन्यथा सन्तमात्मानमन्यथा प्रतिपद्यते। किं तेन न कृतं पापं चौरेणात्मापहारिणा॥
en: He, who has one thing in his mind, but represents another thing to others, is a thief and a robber of his own self. What sin is he not capable of committing?

sn: एकोऽहमस्मीति च मन्यसे त्वं न हृच्छयं वेत्सि मुनि पुराणम्। यो वेदिता कर्मणः पापकस्य तस्यान्तिके त्वं वृजिनं करोपि॥
en: You think that you alone know what you did. But do you not know that the great Omniscient One dwells in your heart. He knows all your sins and you sin in his presence.

sn: मन्यते पापकं कृत्वा न कश्चिद् वेत्ति मामिति। विदन्ति चैनं देवाश्च यश्चैवान्तरपूरुषः॥
en: Man, when sinning, thinks that no one sees him. But he is seen by the celestials and by the Deity who dwells in every heart.

sn: आदित्यचन्द्रावनिलानलौ च द्यौर्भूमिरापो हृदयं यमश्च। अहश्च रात्रिश्च उभे च संध्ये धर्मश्च जानाति नरस्य वृत्तम्॥
en: The sun, the moon, the air, the fire, the earth, the sky, the water, the heart, Yama, the day, the night, the twilight and Dharma see every act of man.

sn: यमो वैवस्वतस्तस्य निर्यातयति दुष्कृतम्। हृदि स्थितः कर्मसाक्षी क्षेत्रज्ञो यस्य तुष्यति॥
en: Yama, the son of Vivasvata, takes no account of the sins of that man with whom the Deity, the witness of all acts, remains pleased.

sn: न तु तुष्यति यस्यैष पुरुषस्य दुरात्मनः। तंयमः पापकर्माणं वियातयति दुष्कृतम्॥
en: But that sinner, with whom the great Deity is not pleased, is punished by Yama for his wicked deeds.

sn: योऽवमन्यात्मनाऽऽत्मानमन्यथा प्रतिपद्यते। न तस्य देवाः श्रेयांसो यस्यात्मापि न कारणम्॥ स्वयं प्राप्तेति मामेवं मावमंस्थाः पतिव्रताम्। अर्चाहीं नार्चयसि मां स्वयं भार्यामुपस्थिताम्॥
en: He, who falsely represents his self and thus degrades himself, is never blessed by the celestials. Even his own soul does not bless him. I have come of my own accord, but I am a devoted wife to my husband. Do not disrespect me. I am your wife and deserve to be treated respectfully.

sn: किमर्थं मां प्राकृतवदुपप्रेक्षसि संसदि। न खल्वहमिदं शून्ये रौमि किं न शृणोषि मे॥
en: Why do you treat me before all these men like an ordinary woman? I am certainly not crying in the wilderness. Do you not hear me?

sn: यदि मे याचमानाया वचनं न करिष्यसि। दुष्यन्त शतधा मूर्धा ततस्तेऽद्य स्फुटिष्यति॥
en: O Dushyanta, If you refuse what I ask you to do, your head will to day be divided into a thousand pieces.

sn: भार्यां पतिः सम्प्रविश्य स यस्माजायते पुनः। जायायास्तद्धि जायात्वं पौराणाः कवयो विदुः॥
en: The learned men of old say that the husband himself, entering into the womb of his wife, comes out as the son. Therefore, the wife is called Jaya.

sn: यदागमवतः पुंसस्तदपत्यं प्रजायते। तत् तारयति संतत्या पूर्वप्रेतान् पितामहान्॥
en: The son, that is born to a wise man, rescues the spirits of his deceased ancestors.

sn: पुत्राम्नो नरकाद् यस्मात् पितरं त्रायते सुतः। तस्मात् पुत्र इति प्रोक्तः स्वयमेव स्वयम्भुवा॥
en: Because the son rescues his ancestors from the hell, called Put, therefore he has been called by the self-created (Brahma) himself as Putra.

sn: (पुत्रेण लोकाञ्जयति पौत्रेणानन्त्यमश्नुते। अथ पौत्रस्य पुत्रेण मोदन्ते प्रपितामहः।।)
en: A man conquers the world by the birth of a son; he enjoys eternity by that of a grandson; the great grandfathers enjoy eternal happiness by the birth of a grandson's son.

sn: सा भार्या या गृहे दक्षा सा भार्या या प्रजावती। सा भार्या या पतिप्राणा सा भार्या या पतिव्रता॥
en: She is a true wife who is a good housewife; she is a true wife whose heart is devoted to her husband; she is a true wife who is faithful to her husband,

sn: अर्धं भार्या मनुष्यस्य भार्या श्रेष्ठतमः सखा। भार्या मूलं त्रिवर्गस्य भार्या मूलं तरिष्यतः॥
en: A man's half is his wife, the wife is her husband's best of friends; the wife is the source of Dharma, Artha and Kama; the wife is the source of salvation.

sn: भार्यावन्त: क्रियावन्तः सभार्या गृहमेधिनः। भार्यावन्तः प्रमोदन्ते भार्यावन्तः श्रियान्विताः॥
en: Those that have wives can perform religious acts; those that have wives lead domestic lives. Those that have wives can be happy and those that have wives can achieve good fortune.

sn: सखायः प्रविविक्तेषु भवन्त्येताः प्रियंवदाः। पितरो धर्मकार्येषु भवन्त्यार्तस्य मातरः॥
en: The sweet-speeched wives their husband's friends on the occasion of joy; they are as fathers on occasions of religious acts; they are as mothers in the hours of illness and are woe.

sn: कान्तारेष्वपि विश्रामो जनस्याध्वनिकस्य वै। यः सदारः स विश्वास्यस्तस्माद् दाराः परागतिः॥४४।
en: Even in the deep forest, the wife is the refreshment and solace to her roaming husband. He who has a wife, is trusted by all. The wife, therefore, is man's great means of salvation.
