sn: संसरन्तमपि प्रेतं विषमेष्वेकपातिनम्। भावान्वेति भर्तारं सततं या पतिव्रता॥
en: When the husband goes to the land of Yama, leaving this world, it is the devoted wife only that accompanies him there.

sn: प्रथमं संस्थिता भार्या पतिं प्रेत्य प्रतीक्षते। पूर्वं मृतं च भर्तारं पश्चात् साध्व्यनुगच्छति॥
en: The wife, gone before (dying before her husband), waits for the spirit of her husband and if the husband goes before, the chaste wife soon follows him.

sn: एतस्मात् कारणाद् राजन् पाणिग्रहणमिष्यते। यदाप्नोति पतिर्भार्यामिहलोके परत्र च॥
en: O king, for all these reasons, marriage exists (in this world). The husband enjoys the company of his wife, both here in this world and hereafter.

sn: आत्माऽऽत्मनैव जनितः पुत्र इत्युच्यते बुधैः। तस्माद् भार्यां नरः पश्येन्मातृवत् पुत्रमातरम्॥
en: The learned men have said that a man himself is born as his son; therefore, a man whose wife has given birth to a son, should look upon her as his mother.

sn: भार्यायां जनितं पुत्रमादर्शेष्विव चाननम्। ह्लादते जनिता प्रेक्ष्य स्वर्गं प्राप्येव पुण्यकृत्॥
en: Looking at the face of the son, begotten on his wife, a man sees his own face as he does in a mirror; and feels himself as happy as a virtuous man attaining to heaven.

sn: दह्यमाना मनोदुःखैर्व्याधिभिश्चातुरा नराः। ह्लादन्ते स्वेषु दारेषु धर्मार्ताः सलिलेष्विव॥
en: Men, burnt out by mental grief or afflicted by disease, feel as much relieved in the company of their wives as a perspiring man does in a cool bath.

sn: सुसंरब्धोऽपि रामाणां न कुर्यादप्रियं नरः। रतिं प्रीतिं च धर्मं च तास्वायत्तमवेक्ष्य हि॥
en: No man, even in anger, should even do any thing that is disagreeable to his wife; for happiness, joy, virtue and everything depend on the wife.

sn: आत्मनो जन्मनः क्षेत्रं पुण्यं रामाः सनातनम्। ऋषीणामपि का शक्तिः स्रष्टुं रामामृते प्रजाम्॥
en: Wife is the sacred soil in which the husband is born again. Even Rishis cannot create men without women.

sn: प्रतिपद्य यदा सूनुर्धरणीरेणुगुण्ठितः। पितुराश्लिष्यतेऽङ्गानि किमस्त्यभ्यधिकं ततः॥
en: What is a greater happiness to a father than what the father feels when his son, running to him, clasps him with his (tiny little) arms, though his body is full of dust and dirt?

sn: स त्वं स्वयमभिप्राप्तं साभिलाषमिमं सुतम्। प्रेक्षमाणं कटाक्षेण किमर्थमवमन्यसे॥ अण्डानि बिभ्रति स्वानि न भिन्दन्ति पिपीलिकाः। न भरेथाः कथं न त्वं धर्मज्ञः सन् स्वमात्मजम्॥
en: Why are you treating with indifference this your son who has himself come to you and who is wistfully casting his glances towards you? Even ants support their off-spring and do not destroy their eggs. Why then should you not, being learned in the rules of piety, support your own child?

sn: न वाससां न रामाणां नापां स्पर्शस्तथाविधः। शिशोरालिङ्ग्यमानस्य स्पर्शः सूनोर्यथा सुखः॥
en: The touch of the sandal-paste, that of women and water, is not so pleasing as that of one's own infant son, locked in his embrace.

sn: ब्राह्मणो द्विपदां श्रेष्ठो गौर्वरिष्ठा चतुष्पदाम्। गुरुर्गरीयसां श्रेष्ठः पुत्रः स्पर्शवतां वरः॥
en: As the Brahmana is the best among bipeds (men), as cow is the best among quadrupeds, as preceptor is the best among all superiors, so is the son among all objects pleasing to the touch.

sn: स्पृशतु त्वां समाश्लिष्य पुत्रोऽयं प्रियदर्शनः। पुत्रस्पर्शात् सुखतरः स्पर्शो लोके न विद्यते॥
en: Let this handsome son touch you in your embrace. There is nothing in the world more pleasing to the touch than that of a son.

sn: त्रिषु वर्षेषु पूर्णेषु प्रजाताहमरिंदम। इमं कुमारं राजेन्द्र तव शोकविनाशनम्॥ आहर्ता वाजिमेधस्य शतसंख्यस्य पौरव। इति वागन्तरिक्षे मां सूतकेऽभ्यवदत् पुरा॥
en: O chastiser of foes, O great king, I gave birth to this boy, the dispeller of your grief, after the completion of three years. O descendant of the Puru race, when I was in the lying-in room, the following words were uttered in the sky, He shall perform one hundred horse-sacrifices.

sn: ननु नामाङ्कमारोप्य स्नेहाद् ग्रामान्तरं गताः। मूर्ध्नि पुत्रानुपाघ्राय प्रतिनन्दन्ति मानवाः॥
en: Men, going to places remote from their homes, take up other men's sons on their laps and smelling their heads, feel great happiness.

sn: वेदेष्वपि वदन्तीमं मन्त्रग्रामं द्विजातयः। जातकर्माणि पुत्राणां तवापि विदितं तथा॥
en: You know that the Brahmanas utter the following Vedic Mantras at the birthday, ceremony of the child.

sn: अङ्गादङ्गात् सम्भवसि हृदयादधिजायसे। आत्मा वै पुत्रनामासि स जीव शरदः शतम्॥
en: “You are born of my body; you have sprung from my heart. You are myself in the form of my son. Live for one hundred years."

sn: जीवितं त्वदधीनं मे संतानमपि चाक्षयम्। तस्मात् त्वं जीव मे पुत्र सुसुखी शरदां शतम्॥
en: "My life depends on you. The continuation of my race also depends on you. Therefore, live in happiness for one hundred years."

sn: त्वदङ्गेभ्यः प्रसूतोऽयं पुरुषात् पुरुषोऽपरः। वै सरसीवामलेऽऽत्मानं द्वितीयं पश्य सुतम्॥
en: He (this boy) has sprung from your body, he is a second being begotten from you. Behold your own self in your own son, as you see your image in the clear waters of the lake.

sn: यथा ह्याहवनीयोऽग्निर्गार्हपत्यात् प्रणीयते। तथा त्वत्तः प्रसूतोऽयं त्वमेकः सन् द्विधा कृतः॥ मृगावकृष्टेन पुरा मृगयां परिधावता। अहमासादिता राजन् कुमारी पितुराश्रमे॥
en: As the sacrificial fire is kindled from the domestic fire, so has this one (your son), sprung from you. Though you are one, you have divided yourself in two. O king, in your hunting expedition, I was approached by you when I was a virgin in my father's hermitage.

sn: उर्वशी पूर्वचित्तिश्च सहजन्या च मेनका। विश्वाची च घृताची च षडेवाप्सरसां वराः॥
en: Urvashi, Purvachitti, Sahajanya, Menaka, Vishvachi and Ghritachi, these are the six foremost Apsaras.

sn: तासां सा मेनका नाम ब्रह्मयोनिर्वराप्सराः। दिवः सम्प्राप्य जगतीं विश्वामित्रादजीजनत्॥
en: Amongst them again, Menaka, born of a Brahmana, is the first. Descending from heaven on earth, she gave me birth from her association with Vishvamitra.

sn: सा मां हिमवतः प्रस्थे सुषुवे मनेकाप्सराः। अवकीर्य च मां याता परात्मजमिवासती॥
en: The Apsara Menaka gave me birth in a valley of the Himalayas. Devoid of affections, she went away, leaving me there, as if I was a child of some others.

sn: किं नु कर्माशुभं पूर्वं कृतवत्यन्यजन्मनि। यदहं बान्धवैस्त्यक्ता बाल्ये सम्प्रति च त्वया।॥
en: What great sin did I commit of old in some other life that I was cast away by my parents in my infancy and now I am cast away by you?

sn: कामं त्वया परित्यक्ता गमिष्यामि स्वमाश्रमम्। इमं तु बालं संत्यक्तुं नार्हस्यात्मजमात्मनः॥
en: Cast off from you, I am ready to go back to the hermitage. But you should not cast off this child who is your own son.

sn: दुष्यन्त उवाच न पुत्रमभिजानामि त्वयि जातं शकुन्तले। असत्यवचना नार्यः कस्ते श्रद्धास्यते वचः॥ मेनका निरनुक्रोशा बन्धकी जननी तव। यया हिमवतः पृष्ठे निर्माल्यमिव चोज्झिता॥
en: Dushyanta said : O Shakuntala, I do not know that I begot this child on you. Women generally speak falsehood. Who will believe your words? Your mother is lewd Menaka, destitute of affection; she cast off you in the valley of the Himalayas as one casts off the flowers after offering them to the gods.

sn: स चापि निरनुक्रोशः क्षत्रयोनिः पिता तव। विश्वामित्रो ब्राह्मणत्वे लुब्धः कामवशं गतः॥
en: Your father also is lustful Vishvamitra of the Kshatriya race, destitute of all affection, the ! man who was tempted to become a Brahmana.

sn: मेनकाप्सरसां श्रेष्ठा महर्षीणां पिता च ते। तयोरपत्यं कस्मात् त्वं पुंश्चलीव प्रभाषसे॥
en: But (if you say), Menaka is the foremost of Apsaras and Vishvamitra is the foremost of Rishis, why then do you, being their daughter, speak like a lewd woman?

sn: अश्रद्धेयमिदं वाक्यं कथयन्ती न लजसे। विशेषतो मत्सकाशे दुष्टतापसि गम्यताम्॥
en: Your these words deserve no credence. Are you not ashamed to utter them, specially before me? Go away, O wicked ascetic woman.

sn: व महर्षिः स चैवाग्र्यः साप्सराः क्व च मेनका। क्व च त्वमेवं कृपणा तापसीवेषधारिणी॥
en: Where is now that best of great Rishis (Vishvamitra) and that best of Apsaras Menaka? And where are you, (though) in the humble garb of ascetics.

sn: अतिकायश्च ते पुत्रो बालोऽतिबलवानयम्। कथमल्पेन कालेन शालस्तम्भ इवोद्गतः॥
en: Your this son is very big and appears to be very strong. How has he, within so short time, grown up like a Sala sprout?

sn: सुनिकृष्टा च ते योनिः पुंश्चलीव प्रभाषसे। यदृच्छया कामरागाजाता मेनकया ह्यसि॥
en: You are born very low, you speak also like a lewd woman. You were lustfully conceived by Menaka.

sn: सर्वमेतत् परोक्षं मे यत् त्वं वदसि तापसि। नाहं त्वामभिजानामि यथेष्टं गम्यतां त्वया॥
en: O ascetic woman, all that you say is quite unknown to me. I do not know you. Go away wherever you please.

sn: शकुन्तलोवाच राजन् सर्पपमात्राणि परच्छिद्राणि पश्यसि। आत्मनो बिल्वमात्राणि पश्यन्नपि न पश्यसि॥
en: Shakuntala said: O king, you (can) see the faults of others, though they may be as small as the mustard seed. But you can not see your own faults, though they are as big as the Bilva fruit.

sn: मेनका त्रिदशेष्वेव त्रिदशाश्चानु मेनकाम्। ममैवोद्रिच्यते जन्म दुष्यन्त तव जन्मनः॥
en: Menaka is a celestial, (nay) Menaka is considered to be the best of celestial. O Dushyanta, my birth is noble than your own.

sn: क्षितावटसि राजेन्द्र अन्तरिक्षे चराम्यहम्। आवयोरन्तरं पश्य मेरुसर्षपयोरिव॥
en: O great king, you walk on earth, but I roam in the sky. Know that the difference between you and me is like that of a mustard seed and the Meru (mountain).

sn: महेन्द्रस्य कुबेरस्य यमस्य वरुणस्य च। भवनान्यनुसंयामि प्रभावं पश्य मे नृप॥
en: O king, behold, I can go to the abodes of Indra, Kubera, Yama and Varuna.

sn: सत्यश्चापि प्रवादोऽयं यं प्रवक्ष्यामि तेऽनघ। निदर्शनार्थं न द्वेषाच्छ्रुत्वा तं क्षन्तुमर्हसि॥
en: O sinless man, there is a proverb which I am going to mention to you; (but I am not doing it) from any evil motive, but only as an example. Therefore, kindly pardon me for referring to it.

sn: विरूपो यावदादर्श नात्मनः पश्यते मुखम्। मन्यते तावदात्मानमन्येभ्यो रूपवत्तरम्॥
en: The ugly man, until he sees his face in a mirror, considers himself more handsome than others.

sn: यदा स्वमुखमादर्श विकृतं सोऽभिवीक्षते। तदान्तरं विजानीते आत्मानं चेतरं जनम्।। ८८
en: But when he sees his own face in the mirror, it is then that he perceives the difference between himself and others.

sn: अतीवरूपसम्पन्नो न कंचिदवमन्यते। अतीव जल्पन् दुर्वाचो भवतीह विहेठकः॥
en: He, who is really very handsome, never taunts others. He, who too much vilifies others, is only considered to be a reviler.

sn: मूतॊ हि जल्पतां पुंसां श्रुत्वा वाचः शुभाशुभाः। अशुभं वाक्यमादत्ते पुरीषमिव सूकरः॥
en: As the swine seeks for the dirt and filth even when it is in a flower-garden, so does a wicked man chose only evil out of the evil and the good that others speak.

sn: प्राज्ञस्तु जल्पतां पुंसां श्रुत्वा वाचः शुभाशुभाः। गुणवद् वाक्यमादत्ते हंसः क्षीरमिवाम्भसः॥
en: But as the geese always extract milk, though inixed with water, so does a wise man accept only what is good from the speech that is intermixed with both good and evil.

sn: अन्यान् परिवदन् साधुर्यथा हि परितप्यते। तथा परिवदन्नन्यांस्तुष्टो भवति दुर्जनः॥
en: Honest men always feel pain to speak ill of others, but wicked men always derive pleasure in doing it.

sn: अभिवाद्य यथा वृद्धान् सन्तो गच्छन्ति निर्वृतिम्। एवं सज्जनमाक्रुश्य मूर्यो भवति निर्वृतः॥ सुखं जीवन्त्यदोषज्ञा मूर्खा दोषानुदर्शिनः। यत्र वाच्याः परैः सन्तः परानाहुस्तथाविधान्॥
en: Honest men always feel pleasure in showing respect towards the old (good men), but the fools always feel pleasure in abusing them. Honest men are happy in not seeking others' fault, but the fools are happy in doing it. The wicked always speak ill of honest men, but honest men never injure the wicked, even if injured by them.

sn: अतो हास्यतरं लोके किंचिदन्यन्न विद्यते। यत्र दुर्जनमित्याह दुर्जनः सज्जनं स्वयम्॥
en: What could be more ridiculous in the world than this, that those that are wicked should represent really honest men as wicked.

sn: सत्यधर्मच्युतात् पुंसः क्रुद्धादाशीविषादिव। अनास्तिकोऽप्युद्विजते जनः किं पुनरास्तिकः॥
en: Even atheists are afraid of those who have fallen from truth and virtue, as all men are afraid of the snakes of virulent poison. (When such is the case with an atheist), what shall I speak of me who is atheist?

sn: स्वयमुत्पाद्य वै पुत्रं सदृशं यो न मन्यते। तस्य देवाः श्रियं प्रन्ति न च लोकानुपाश्नते॥
en: The man, who having begotten a son who is his own image, does not look after him, never gains the higher worlds. The celestial destroy his good fortune an wealth.

sn: कुलवंशप्रतिष्ठां हि पितरः पुत्रमब्रुवन्। उत्तमं सर्वधर्माणां तस्मात् पुत्रं न सन्त्यजेत्॥
en: The Pitris (ancestors) have said that the son continues the race and supports the relations; therefore, to give birth to a son is the best of all pious acts. Therefore, your this son should not be abandoned.

sn: स्वपत्नीप्रभवान् पञ्च लब्धान् क्रीतान् विवर्धितान्। कृतानन्यासु चोत्पन्नान् पुत्रान् वै मनुरब्रवीत्॥
en: Manu has said that there are five kinds of sons, namely those begotten by one on his wife, those obtained from others, those purchased for a price, those reared out of affection and those begotten on other women.

sn: धर्मकीर्त्यावहा नृणां मनस: प्रीतिवर्धनाः। त्रायन्ते नरकाजाता: पुत्रा धर्मप्लवाः पितॄन्। १०० ।।
en: Sons support the religion and achievements of men; they increase their happiness; they rescue the dead ancestor from hell.

sn: स त्वं नृपतिशार्दूल पुत्रं न त्यक्तुमर्हसि। आत्मानं सत्यधर्मी च पालयन् पृथिवीपते। नरेन्द्रसिंह कटं न वोढुं त्वमिहार्हसि॥
en: Therefore, O best of kings, it is not proper for you to abandon your son. O king of the earth, cherish your own self, truth and virtue, more more (by cherishing your this son). () best of the kings, it is not proper for you to play hypocrite's in this matter.

sn: वरं कूपशताद् वापी वरं वापीशतात् क्रतुः। वरं क्रतुशतात् पुत्रः सत्यं पुत्रशताद् वरम्॥
en: The dedication of a tank is meritorious than that of one hundred wells. A sacrifice is meritorious than the dedication of a tank. But (to beget a son) is inore meritorious than the celebration of sacrifices. Truth (however) is more meritorious than the birth of one hundred sons.

sn: अश्वमेधसहस्रं च सत्यं च तुलया धृतम्। अश्वमेधसहस्राद्धि सत्यमेव विशिष्यते॥
en: If one thousand horse-sacrifices and truth were weighed, truth would be found heavier than one thousand horse-sacrifices.

sn: सर्ववेदाधिगमनं सर्वतीर्थावगाहनम्। सत्यं च वचनं राजन् समं वा स्यान्न वा समम्।। १०४।
en: O king, I tell you, truth is equal to the study of the entire Vedas and ablutions in all the sacred pilgrimages.

sn: नास्ति सत्यसमो धर्मो न सत्याद् विद्यते परम्। न हि तीव्रतरं किंचिदनृतादिह विद्यते॥
en: There is no virtue equal to truth, there is nothing (in this world) superior to truth. And there is nothing (again) more sinful than falsehood.

sn: राजन् सत्यं परं ब्रह्म सत्यं च समयः परः। मा त्याक्षीः समयं राजन् सत्यं संगतमस्तु ते॥
en: O king, truth is the great Brahma, truth is the great vow; therefore, O king, do not violate your pledge. Let truth and yourself be ever united.

sn: अनृते चेत् प्रसङ्गस्ते श्रद्दधासि न चेत् स्वयम्। आत्मना हन्त गच्छामि त्वादृशे नास्ति संगतम्॥
en: If, however, you are united with falsehood, li you do not place any credence on my word, I shall go away from this place of my own accord. Your companionship should not be sought after.

sn: त्वामृतेऽपि हि दुष्यन्त शैलराजावतंसकाम्। चतुरन्ताभिमामुर्वी पुत्रो मे पालयिष्यति॥
en: But, ( Dushyanta, (know this for a certainty), that when you are dead, my this son shall rule the whole earth, surrounded by the four seas and adorned by the king of mountains.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एतावदुक्त्वा राजानं प्रातिष्ठत शकुन्तला। अथान्तरिक्षाद् दुष्यन्तं वागुवाचाशरीरिणी॥ ऋत्विक्पुरोहिताचार्यैर्मन्त्रिभिश्च वृतं तदा।
en: Vaishampayana said : Having said all this to the king, Shakuntala turned her back. Thereupon a voice from the sky, coming from one who had no visible shape, addressed Dushyanta who was sitting, surrounded by his ministers, priests and Ritvikas.

sn: भस्त्रा माता पितुः पुत्रो येन जातः स एव सः॥ भरस्व पुत्रं दुष्यन्त मावमंस्थाः शकुन्तलाम्। रेतोधाः पुत्र उन्नयति नरदेव यमक्षयात्॥ त्वं चास्य धाता गर्भस्य सत्यमाह शकुन्तला। जाया जनयते पुत्रमात्मनोऽङ्गं द्विधा कृतम्॥
en: (It said), “O Dushyanta, the mother is but a sheath of flesh (within which the son dwells). The son, sprung from the father, is the father himself. Therefore, cherish your son and do not insult Shakuntala. O best of men, the son begotten by one's own self, rescues him from the abode of Yama. You are the father of this son. Shakuntala has spoken the truth. The husband divides his body in two parts and is born in the womb of his wife as the son.

sn: तस्माद् भरस्व दुष्यन्त पुत्रं शाकुन्तलं नृप। अभूतिरेषा यत् त्यक्त्वा जीवेजीवन्तमात्मजम्॥
en: O king, O Dushyanta, therefore, cherish your this son, born of Shakuntala. To forsake one's own son and to live thereafter is a great misfortune.

sn: शाकुन्तलं महात्मानं दौष्यन्ति भर पौरव। भर्तव्योऽयं त्वया यस्मादस्माकं वचनादपि॥ तस्माद् भवत्वयं नाम्ना भरतो नाम ते सुतः।
en: Therefore, O descendant of the Puru race, cherish your this high-souled son, born of Shakuntala. As you will cherish this child at our word, therefore, your this son will be known by the name of Bharata.

sn: तच्छ्रुत्वा पौरवो राजा व्याहृतं त्रिदिवौकसाम्॥ पुरोहितममात्यांश्च सम्प्रहृष्टोऽब्रवीदिदम्। शृण्वन्त्वेतद् भवन्तोऽस्य देवदूतस्य भाषितम्॥
en: Having heard these words of the dwellers of heaven, the king of the Puru race was much pleased and addressing his priests and ministers, he said : “Hear all of you the words of the messenger of heaven."

sn: अहं चाप्येवमेवैनं जानामि स्वयमात्मजम्। यद्यहं वचनादस्या गृह्णीयामि ममात्मजम्॥ भवेद्धि शङ्कयो लोकस्य नैव शुद्धो भवेदयम्।
en: "I myself know that this boy is my son. If I had accepted him as my son at Shakuntala's words, my people would have been suspicious and my son also would not have been considered to be pure (of pure birth).”

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तं विशोध्य तदा राजा देवदूतेन भारत। हृष्टः प्रमुदितश्चापि प्रतिजग्राह तं सुतम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : O descendant of the Virata race, the king was exceedingly pleased, because the purity of the birth of his son was established by the messenger of heaven.

sn: ततस्तस्य तदा राजा पितृकर्माणि सर्वशः। कारयामास मुदितः प्रीतिमानात्मजस्य ह॥
en: He then performed with joy all those rites which a father should perform for his son.

sn: मूर्ध्नि चैनमुपाघ्राय सस्नेहं परिषस्वजे। सभाज्यमानो विप्रैश्च स्तूयमानश्च वन्दिभिः। स मुदं परमां लेभे पुत्रसंस्पर्शजां नृपः॥
en: He smelt his son's head; he embraced him with affection. The Brahmanas uttered blessings on him and the bards began to applaud him. The king then enjoyed the great pleasure that one feels at the touch of one's own son.

sn: धर्मतः। तां चैव भार्या दुष्यन्तः पूजयामास अब्रवीचैव तां राजा सान्त्वपूर्वमिदं वचः॥
en: Dushyanta also received his wife (Shakuntala) with all honour and affection. Affectionately pacifying her, he spoke to her thus,

sn: कृतो लोकपरोक्षोऽयं सम्बन्धो वै त्वया सह। तस्मादेतन्मया देवि त्वच्छुद्ध्यर्थं विचारितम्॥ मन्यते चैव लोकस्ते स्त्रीभावान्मयि संगतम्। पुत्रश्चायं वृतो राज्ये मया तस्माद् विचारितम्॥
en: “O lady, my union with you took place in private. None knew of it and therefore, it is natural that people should have thought that our union was only out of lust and that we were not husband and wife. This son, installed as my heir-apparent, would have been considered as a man of impure birth. Therefore, I was thinking how best to establish your purity.

sn: यच्च कोपितयात्यर्थं त्वयोक्तोऽस्म्यप्रियं प्रिये। प्रणयिन्या विशालाक्षि तत् क्षान्तं ते मया शुभे॥
en: "O dearest, O lady of beautiful eyes, I have forgiven you for all the hard words you have uttered in anger. You are my darling.”

sn: तामेवमुक्त्वा राजर्षिर्दुष्यन्तो महिषीं प्रियाम्। वासोभिरन्नपानैश्च पूजयामास भारत॥
en: O descendant of the Bharata race, having spoken thus to his dear queen (Shakuntala), the royal sage Dushyanta, received her with the presents of perfume, food and drink.

sn: दुष्यन्तस्तु तदा राजा पुत्रं शाकुन्तलं तदा। भरतं नामतः कृत्वा यौवराज्येऽभ्यषेचयत्॥
en: The king Dushyanta, thereupon, installed the son of Shakuntala as his heir-apparent bestowing upon him the name of Bharata.

sn: तस्य तत् प्रथितं चक्रं प्रावर्तत महात्मनः। भास्वरं दिव्यमजितं लोकसंनादनं महत्॥
en: From that day the invincible car of Bharata, like the car of the celestials, with its famous and bright wheels, traversed the whole earth, filling it with its rattle.

sn: स विजित्य महीपालांश्चकार वशवर्तिनः। चचार च सतां धर्मं प्राप चानुत्तमं यशः॥
en: The son of Dushyanta (Bharata) brought under his sway all the kings of the world. He ruled his subjects virtuously and gained great fame.

sn: स राजा चक्रवर्त्यासीत् सार्वभौमः प्रतापवान्। ईजे च बहुभिर्यज्ञैर्यथा शक्रो मरुत्पतिः॥
en: That king (Bharata) was known by the name of Chakravarti and Sarvabhauma. He performed many sacrifices like Indra, the lord of the Marutas.

sn: याजयामास तं कण्वो विधिवद् भूरिदक्षिणम्। श्रीमान् गोविततं नाम वाजिमेधमवाप सः। यस्मिन् सहस्रं पद्मानां कण्वाय भरतो ददौ॥
en: Kanva was the chief priest in those sacrifices and great offerings were made to the Brahmanas. The fortunate king performed both the cow and the horse-sacrifices. Bharata gave one thousand gold coins to Kanva as his sacrificial fee.

sn: भरताद् भारती कीर्तिर्यनदं भारतं कुलम्। अपरे ये च पूर्वे वै भारता इति विश्रुता॥
en: From this Bharata has followed this, "achievement of Bharata," from him has sprung this great race (of Bharata.) All kings that were born after him are called after his name.

sn: भरतस्यान्ववाये हि देवकल्पा महौजसः। बभूवुर्ब्रह्मकल्पाश्च बहवो राजसत्तमाः॥ येषामपरिमेयानि नामधेयानि सर्वशः। तेषां तु ते यथामुख्यं कीर्तयिष्यामि भारत। महाभागान् देवकल्पान् सत्यार्जवपरायणान्॥
en: And in this Bharata race were many godlike and greatly powerful best of monarchs. They were like Brahma himself. Their names are countless. O descendant of the Bharata race, I shall name only the chief ones, who were all blessed with great fortune and devoted to truth and honesty. They were all like the celestial.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच प्रजापतेस्तु दक्षस्य मनोवैवस्वतस्य च। भरतस्य कुरो पूरोराजमीढस्य चानघ॥ यादवानामिमं वंशं कौरवाणां च सर्वशः। तथैव भरतानां च पुण्यं स्वस्त्ययनं महत्॥ धन्यं यशस्यमायुष्यं कीर्तयिष्यामि तेऽनघ। तेजोभिरुदिताः सर्वे महर्षिसमतेजसः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : O sinless one, Prajapati Daksha, Vaivasvata Manu, Manu, Bharata, Kuru, Puru, Ajamidha, Yadava and all the other kings of the Bharata race, O sinless king, I shall now recite the holy, illustrious and long lifebestowing histories of these great men. They were as effulgent as the sun and the great Rishis.

sn: दश प्राचेतसः पुत्राः सन्तः पुण्यजनाः स्मृताः। मुखजेनाग्निना यैस्ते पूर्वं दग्धा महीरूहाः॥
en: Pracheta had ten sons, who were all devoted to asceticism and they all possessed every virtue. They burnt with the fire of their mouth many medicinal plants.

sn: तेभ्यः प्राचेतसो जज्ञे दक्षो दक्षादिमाः प्रजाः। सम्भूताः पुरुषव्याघ्र स हि लोकपितामहः॥
en: O lion among the men, from them was born Prachetas Daksha and from Daksha sprang all creatures. Therefore, he was called the Grandsire.

sn: वीरिण्या सह संगम्य दक्षः प्राचेतसो मुनिः। आत्मतुल्यानजनयत् सहस्रं संशितव्रतान्॥
en: The Rishi Daksha, born of Prachetas, begot one thousand sons, uniting with Virini; they were all of rigid vows like himself.

sn: सहस्रसंख्यान् सम्भूतान् दक्षपुत्रांश्च नारदः। मोक्षमध्यापयामास सांख्यज्ञानमनुत्तमम्॥
en: Narada taught these one thousand sons of Daksha the excellent knowledge of Sankhya, the means of salvation.

sn: ततः पञ्चाशतं कन्या: पुत्रिका अभिसंदधे। प्रजापतिः प्रजा दक्षः सिसृक्षुर्जनमेजय॥
en: Janamejaya, the lord of creation Prajapati Daksha, from the desire of creating more creatures, begot fifty daughters. He made them all his Putrikas.

sn: ददौ दश स धर्माय कश्यपाय त्रयोदश। कालस्य नयने युक्ताः सप्तविंशतिमिन्दवे॥
en: He bestowed ten of his daughters on Daksha, thirteen on Kashyapa and twentyseven on Chandra who were all engaged in indicating time.

sn: त्रयोदशानां पत्नीनां या तु दाक्षायणी वरा। मारीचः कश्यपस्त्वस्यामादित्यान् समजीजनत्॥ इन्द्रादीन् वीर्यसम्पन्नान् विवस्वन्तमथापि च। विवस्वतः सुतो जज्ञे यमो वैवस्वतः प्रभुः॥
en: Kashyapa, the son of Marichi, begot on his wife, the daughter of Daksha, who was the eldest among his thirteen wives, Aditya, the greatly effulgent celestials, Indra, being at their head and Vaivasvata also, Vaivasvata's son was born Yama, the great lord.

sn: मार्तण्डस्य मनु/मानजायत सुतः प्रभुः। यमश्चापि सुतो जज्ञे ख्यातस्तस्यानुजः प्रभुः॥
en: Martanda (Vaivasvata) begot another son who was gifted with great intelligence and was called Manu. Yama was his younger brother.

sn: धर्मात्मा स मनु/मान् यत्र वंशः प्रतिष्ठितः। मनोर्वंशो मानवानां ततोऽयं प्रथितोऽभवत्॥
en: Manu was greatly wise and virtuous; he became the progenitor of a race. The offspring of Manu were called Manavas, (human beings.)

sn: ब्रह्मक्षत्रादयस्तस्मान्मनोर्जातास्तु मानवाः। ततोऽभवन्महाराज ब्रह्मक्षत्रेण संगतम्॥
en: It was from Manu that all men, including Brahmanas, Kshatriyas and others have been born. O great king, the Brahmanas and Kshatriyas were subsequently united.

sn: ब्राह्मणा मानवास्तेषां साङ्गं वेदमधारयन्। वेनं धृष्णुं नरिष्यन्तं नाभागेक्ष्वाकुमेव च॥ कारूषमथ शर्याति तथा चैवाष्टमीमिलाम्। पृषधं नवमं प्राहुः क्षत्रधर्मपरायणम्॥ नाभागारिष्टदशमान् मनो: पञ्चाशत्तु मनोः पुत्रास्तथैवान्येऽभवन् क्षितौ॥
en: Those sons of Manu, who were Brahmanas, became devoted to the study of the Vedas. Vena, Dhrishnu, Narishyanta, Nabhaga, Ikshvaku, Karusha and Sharyati, the eighth a daughter, named Ila, the ninth Prishadhra, who was gifted with all the virtues of Kshatriyas. Nabhagarishta was the tenth son of Daksha. Besides these, Manu had fifty other sons on earth.

sn: अन्योन्यभेदात् ते सर्वे विनेशुरिति नः श्रुतम्। पुरूरवास्ततो विद्वानिलायां समपद्यत॥
en: We have heard, they all perished quarrelling with one another. The learned Pururava was born of Ila.

sn: सा वै तस्याभवन्माता पिता चैवेति नः श्रुतम्। त्रयोदश समुद्रस्य द्वीपानश्नन् पुरूरवाः॥
en: We have heard that Ila was both the father and the mother of Pururava. He had sway over thirteen islands of the sea.

sn: अमानुषैर्वृतः सत्त्वैर्मानुषः सन् महायशाः। विप्रैः स विग्रहं चक्रे वीर्योन्मत्तः पुरूरवाः॥ जहार च स विप्राणां रत्नान्युत्क्रोशतामपि।
en: Though he was a human being, yet he remained always surrounded by superhuman companions. Pururava, intoxicated with the pride of power which he possessed, quarrelled with the Brahmanas, caring little for their anger. He robbed them of their wealth.

sn: सनत्कुमारस्तं राजन् ब्रह्मलोकादुपेत्य ह॥ अनुदर्श ततश्चक्रे प्रत्यगृह्णान्न चाप्यसौ। ततो महर्षिभिः क्रुद्धैः सद्यः शप्तो व्यनश्यत॥
en: Seeing this, Sanatkumar came from the region of Brahma and gave him good counsel, which he did not accept. Thereupon, the wrath of the great Rishis was excited and the king, who was intoxicated with the pride of power and who lost his reason, was immediately killed by their curse.

sn: लोभान्वितो बलमदानष्टसंज्ञो नराधिपः। स हि गन्धर्वलोकस्थानुर्वश्या सहितो विराट्॥ आनिनाय क्रियार्थेऽग्नीन् यथावद् विहितांस्त्रिधा। षट् सुता जज्ञिरे चैलादायु/मानमावसुः॥ दृढायुश्च वनायुश्च शतायुश्चोर्वशीसुताः। नहुषं वृद्धशर्माणं रजिं गयमनेनसम्॥ स्वर्भानवीसुतानेतानायोः पुत्रान् प्रचक्षते। आयुषो नहुषः पुत्रो धीमान् सत्यपराक्रमः॥
en: This king (Pururava) brought from the region of the Gandharvas, three kinds of fire for sacrificial purposes with the Apsara Urvashi. He begot six sons on Urvashi, namely Ayush, Dhiman, Amavasu, Dhridhayu, Vanayu and Shatayus. It is said that Ayush begot on the daughter of Svarbhanu five sons, namely Nahusha, Vriddhasharma, Raji, Gaya and Anenasa. Of all the sons of Ayush, Nahusha was exceedingly intelligent and powerful.

sn: राज्यं शशास सुमहद् धर्मेण पृथिवीपते। पितॄन् देवानृषीन् विप्रान् गन्धर्वोरगराक्षसान्॥ नहुषः पालयामास ब्रह्मक्षत्रमथो विशः। स हत्वा दस्युसंघातानृषीन् करमदापयत्॥
en: O king, He ruled his kingdom with great virtue. King Nahusha equally supported the Pitris, the Devas, the Rishis, the Gandharvas, the Nagas, the Rakshasas, the Brahmanas, the Kshatriyas and the Vaishyas. He suppressed all the robbers with a mighty hand; he made Rishis to pay tribute to himself.

sn: पशुवच्चैव तान्पृष्ठे वाहयामास वीर्यवान्। कारयामास चेन्द्रत्वमभिभूय दिवौकसः॥ तेजसा तपसा चैव विक्रमेणौजसा तथा। यतिं ययाति संयातिमायातिमयति ध्रुवम्॥ नहुषो जनयामास षट्सुतान्प्रियवादिनः। यतिस्तु योगमास्थाय ब्रह्मभूतोऽभवन्मुनिः॥
en: And like animal, the powerful one Nahusha carried them on the back of Rishis. Beating the very dwellers of heaven with his beauty, his asceticism, his prowess and energy, he ruled the earth, as if he was Indra himself. Nahusha begot six sweet-speeched sons, namely, Yati, Yayati, Sanyati, Aayati, Ayati and Dhruva. Yati adopted asceticism and became a great Rishi like Brahma himself.

sn: ययाति हुष: सम्राडासीत् सत्यपराक्रमः। स पालयामास महीमीजे च बहुभिर्मखैः॥ अतिभक्त्या पितॄनर्चन् देवांश्च प्रयतः सदा। अन्वगृह्णात् प्रजाः सर्वा ययातिरपराजितः॥ तस्य पुत्रा महेष्वासाः सर्वैः समुदिता गुणैः। देवयान्यां महाराज शर्मिष्ठायां च जज्ञिरे॥ देवयान्यामजायेतां यदुस्तुर्वसुरेव च। द्रुह्युश्चानुश्च पूरुश्च शर्मिष्ठायां च जज्ञिरे॥
en: were Yayati became greatly virtuous. He ruled over the whole earth; he performed many sacrifices; he worshipped the Pitris with great reverence and showed a great respect towards the celestial. He showed great kindness and favour to all his subjects and he was never defeated by any foe. His sons were all great bow-men and gifted with all accomplishments. Ogreat king, they were bom of Devayani and Sharmishtha, his two wives. From Devayani were born Yadus and Turvasu. From Sharinishtha were born Druhyu, Anu and Puru.

sn: स शाश्वती: समा राजन् प्रजा धर्मेण पालयन्। जरामार्छन्महाघोरां नाहुषो रूपनाशिनीम्॥
en: O king, after ruling his subjects with virtue for a long time. The son of Nahusha (Yayati) was attacked by the terrible old age which destroyed his personal beauty.

sn: जराभिभूतः पुत्रान् स राजा वचनमब्रवीत्। यदुं पूरुं तुर्वसुं च द्रुह्यं चानुं च भारत॥
en: Having been thus attacked by old age, the king thus addressed his sons, namely Yadu, Puru, Turvasu, Druhyu and Anu.

sn: यौवनेन चरन् कामान् युवा युवतिभिः सह। विहर्तुमहमिच्छामि साह्यं कुरुत पुत्रकाः॥
en: “O Dear sons, I wish to be young and desire to pass my time with young women. Help me in this."

sn: तं पुत्रो दैवयानेयः पूर्वजो वाक्यमब्रवीत्। किं कार्यं भवतः कार्यमस्माकं यौवनेन ते॥
en: His eldest son, born of Devayani said, “Why do you require? Do you want to have our youth?"

sn: ययातिरब्रवीत् तं वै जरा मे प्रतिगृह्यताम्। यौवनेन त्वदीयेन चरेयं विषयानहम्॥
en: Yayati replied, “Accept my old age.” I would then enjoy myself with your youth.

sn: यजतो दीर्घसत्रैर्मे शापाचोशनसो मुनेः। कामार्थः परिहीणोऽयं तप्येयं तेन पुत्रकाः॥
en: During a long sacrifice, I was cursed by the Rishi Ushanas and therefore, thus have I lost all my powers of enjoying sensual pleasures. O sons, I shall enjoy myself with your youth.

sn: मामकेन शरीरेण राज्यमेकः प्रशास्तु वः। अहं तन्वाभिनवया युवा काममवाप्नुयाम्॥
en: (Therefore), take any of you my decrepitude and rule the kingdom with my body. I would then enjoy myself with a renovated youthful body.

sn: ते न तस्य प्रत्यगृह्णन् यदुप्रभृतयो जराम्। तमब्रवीत् ततः पूरुः कनीयान् सत्यविक्रमः॥ राजश्चराभिनवया तन्वा यौवनगोचरः। अहं जरां समादाय राज्ये स्थास्यामि तेऽऽज्ञया॥
en: Yadu and other sons did not agree to take upon them his old age. Thereupon, his youngest son, the virtuous and powerful Puru said-"O king, enjoy again with a renovated body and returned youth. I shall take upon me your old age and I shall rule the kingdom at your command."

sn: एवमुक्तः स राजर्षिस्तपोवीर्यसमाश्रयात्। संचारयामास जरां तदा पुत्रे महात्मनि॥
en: Thus being addressed, the royal sage (Yayati) transferred his old age on his highsouled son (Puru) with his power of asceticism.

sn: पौरवेणाथ वयसा राजा यौवनमास्थितः। यायातेनापि वयसा राज्यं पूरुरकारयत्॥
en: The king again became a young man with the youth of Puru; and Puru with the old age of his father upon him ruled the kingdom.

sn: ततो वर्षसहस्राणि ययातिरपराजितः। स्थितः स नृपशार्दूल: शार्दूलसमविक्रमः॥
en: Even when one thousand years had thus passed away, Yayati, the best of kings, the invincible hero, remained as strong and powerful as a tiger.

sn: ययातिरपि पत्नीभ्यां दीर्घकालं विहृत्य च। विश्वाच्या सहितो रेमे पुनश्चैत्ररथे वने॥
en: He enjoyed for a long time the sweet company of his two wives. He enjoyed with (Apsara) Vishvachi in the gardens of Chitraratha (Gandharva king.)

sn: नाध्यगच्छत् तदा तृप्ति कामानां स महायशाः। अवेत्य मनसा राजन्निमां गाथां तदा जगौ॥
en: That illustrious man had not his desires satiated even after this. Thereupon, the king remembered the following words of the Purana.

sn: न जातु कामः कामानामुपभोगेन शाम्यति। हविषा कृष्णवर्मेव भूय एवाभिवर्धते॥
en: "One's desires are never satiated with enjoyments. On On the the other hand, with indulgence they flame up like the sacrificial fire with ghee poured into it.

sn: पृथिवी रत्नसम्पूर्णा हिरण्यं पशवः स्त्रियः। नालमेकस्य तत् सर्वमिति मत्वा शमं व्रजेत्॥
en: Even if one enjoys the whole earth, with its wealth, its diamonds, gold, aniimals and women, still his desires will not be satiated.

sn: यदा न कुरुते पापं सर्वभूतेषु कर्हिचित्। कर्मणा मनसा वाचा ब्रह्म सम्पद्यते तदा॥
en: It is only when a man does not commit a sin in thought, deed or word in respect of any living creatures, it is then that he attains to the purity of Brahma.

sn: यदा चायं न बिभेति यदा चास्मान्न बिभ्यति। यदा नेच्छति न द्वेष्टि ब्रह्म सम्पद्यते तदा॥
en: When a man fears nothing and when he is feared by none, when he desires for nothing and when he injures none, it is then that he attains to the purity of Brahma."

sn: इत्यवेक्ष्य महाप्राज्ञः कामानां फल्गुतां नृप। समाधाय मनो बुद्ध्या प्रत्यगृह्णाजरां सुतात्॥
en: The greatly wise king, seeing this and having been satisfied that one's desires are never satiated, received back his old age from his son.

sn: दत्त्वा च यौवनं राजा पूरूं राज्येऽभिषिच्य च। अतृप्त एव कामानां पूरुं पुत्रमुवाच ह॥
en: Though his desires were not satiated, he gave back his youth to his son Puru and

sn: त्वया दायादवानस्मि त्वं मे वंशकरः सुतः। पौरवो वंश इति ते ख्याति लोके गमिष्यति॥
en: "From you my race would continue. You are my true son and heir. My race will be known in the world after your name."

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततः स नृपशार्दूल पूरुं राज्येऽभिषिच्य च। ततः सुचरितं कृत्वा भृगुतुङ्गे महातपाः॥ कालेन महता पश्चात् कालधर्ममुपेयिवान्। कारयित्वा त्वनशनं सदारः स्वर्गमाप्तवान्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : That best of kings, (Yayati), having installed Puru on the throne went to the mount Bhrigu to become a great ascetic. After many years he succumbed to the inevitable influence of Time. Observing the vow of fasting, he ascended heaven with his wives.

sn: जनमेजय उवाच ययातिः पूर्वजोऽस्माकं दशमो यः प्रजापतेः। कथं स शुक्रतनयां लेभे परमदुर्लभाम्॥ एतदिच्छाम्यहं श्रोतुं विस्तरेण तपोधन। आनुपूर्व्या च मे शंस राज्ञो वंशकरान् पृथक्॥
en: Janamejaya said : How did our ancestor (Yayati) who was the tenth from Prajapati, obtain the unobtainable daughter of Shukra? O great ascetic, I desire to hear this in detail. Tell me also separately the account of those kings who were the founders of dynasties.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ययातिरासीनृपतिर्देवराजसमद्युतिः। तं शुक्रवृषपर्वाणौ वब्राते वै यथा पुरा॥ तत् तेऽहं सम्प्रवक्ष्यामि पृच्छते जनमेजय। देवयान्याश्च संयोगं ययाते हुषस्य च॥
en: Vaishampayana said : O Janamejaya, the king Yayati was as effulgent as Indra himself. I shall tell you in reply to your question how Shukra and Vrishaparva bestowed (on the king) their daughters in due rites and I shall specially narrate how the union of the Nahusha, took place with Devayani.

sn: सुराणामसुराणां च समजायत वै मिथः। ऐश्वर्य प्रति संघर्षस्त्रैलोक्ये सचराचरे॥
en: In the days of yore, great battles were often faught between the Devas and the Asuras for the sovereignty over the three worlds.

sn: जिगीषया ततो देवा वव्रिरेऽऽङ्गिरसं मुनिम्। पौरोहित्येन याज्यार्थे काव्यं तूशनसं परे॥ ब्राह्मणौ तावुभौ नित्यममन्योन्यस्पर्धिनौ भृशम्। तत्र देवा निजघ्नुर्यान् दानवान् युधि संगतान्॥ तान् पुनर्जीवयामास काव्यो विद्याबलाश्रयात्। ततस्ते पुनरुत्थाय योधयांचक्रिरे सुरान्॥
en: From the desire of securing victory, the celestials appointed the Rishi who was the son of Angirasa (Brihaspati) as their priest to conduct their sacrifices; and their opponents appointed Ushanas (Shukra) as their priest for the same purpose. There was much boastful rivalry between these two Brahmanas. All those Danavas that were killed in battle by the Devas were revived by that sage (Shukra) with the power of his knowledge; and they, thus being made alive, fought again with the celestial.

sn: असुरास्तु निजघ्नुर्यान् सुरान् समरमूर्धनि। न तान् संजीवयामास बृहस्पतिरुदारधीः॥
en: The Asuras also killed many Devas, but the greatly learned Brihaspati could not revive them.

sn: न हि वेद स तां विद्यां यां काव्यो वेत्ति वीर्यवान्। संजीविनी ततो देवा विषादमगमन् परम्॥
en: He did not know the science of Sanjivini (giving life to the dead) which the greatly powerful Rishi (Shukra) knew very well. The celestial were, therefore, very sorry.

sn: ते त देवा भयोद्विग्ना: काव्यादुशनसस्तदा। ऊचुः कथमुपागम्य ज्येष्ठं पुत्रं बृहस्पतेः॥
en: Thereupon, the celestials, in great anxiety and in fear of the learned Ushanas, went to Kacha, the eldest son of Brihaspati; and they spoke to him thus.

sn: भजमानान् भजस्वास्मान् कुरु नः साह्यमुत्तमम्। था सा विद्या निवसति ब्राह्मणेऽमिततेजसि॥
en: "We ask for your protection, we worship you. Help us in a work which we consider as very important. The knowledge of that science which is known to that Brahmana of immeasurable prowess. Shukra, must be obtained by you as soon as possible. You will then be a sharer with us in all sacrificial offerings. You shall find that Brahmana (Shukra) in the court of (king) Vrishaparva.

sn: रक्षते दानवांस्तत्र न स रक्षत्यदानवान्। तमाराधयितुं शक्तो भवान् पूर्ववयाः कविम्॥
en: He always protects the Danavas, but never the celestials, their opponents. You are younger than he and you are, therefore, able to revere him.

sn: देवयानी च दयितां सुतां तस्य महात्मनः। त्वमाराधयितुं शक्तो नान्यः कश्चन विद्यते॥
en: You can also adore Devayani, the favourite daughter of that illustrious man. You are capable of conciliating them both. There is none else who can do it.

sn: शीलदाक्षिण्यमाधुर्यैराचारेण दमेन च। देवयान्यां हि तुष्टायां विद्यां तां प्राप्स्यसि ध्रुवम्॥
en: "You are sure to obtain that knowledge (of Sanjivini from the Rishi) by gratifying Devayani with your conduct, liberality, sweetness and general behaviour.”

sn: तथेत्युक्त्वा ततः प्रायाद् बृहस्पतिसुत: कचः। तदाभिपूजिता देवैः समीपे वृषपर्वणः॥
en: Having been thus addressed and worshipped by the celestials, he said, “Be it so." He then went to the court of king Vrishaparva.

sn: स गत्वा त्वरितो राजन् देवैः सम्प्रेषित: कचः। असुरेन्द्रपुरे शुक्रं दृष्ट्वा वाक्यमुवाच ह॥
en: O king, having been thus sent by the celestials, Kacha soon came to the city of the king of the Asuras; and seeing Shukra there, he thus addressed him.

sn: ऋषेरङ्गिरस: पौत्रं पुत्रं साक्षाद् बृहस्पतेः। नाम्ना कचमिति ख्यातं शिष्यं गृह्णातु मां भवान्॥
en: “Reverend Sir, accept me as your disciple. I am the grandson of Rishi Angirasa and the son of Brihaspati. I am known as Kacha by naine.

sn: ब्रह्मचर्य चरिष्यामि त्वय्यहं परमं गुरौ। अनुमन्यस्व मां ब्रह्मन् सहस्रं परिवत्सरान्॥
en: Accepting you as my great preceptor, I shall practise Brahmacharya for one thousand years. Therefore, command me.

sn: शुक्र उवाच कच सुस्वागतं तेऽस्तु प्रतिगृह्णामि ते वचः। अर्चयिष्येऽहमय॑ त्वामर्चितोऽस्तु बृहस्पतिः॥
en: Shukra said:: O Kacha, you are welcome, I accept your words. I shall treat you with regard, for by my doing it, Brihaspati will be regarded.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच कचस्तु तं तथेत्युक्त्वा प्रतिजग्राह तद् व्रतम्। आदिष्टं कविपुत्रेण शुक्रेणोशनसा स्वयम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Commanded by the son of Kavi, Ushanas, also called Shukra, Kacha said, “Be it so." And he rook the vow he spoke of.

sn: व्रतस्य प्राप्तकालं स यथोक्तं प्रत्यगृह्णत। आराधयन्नुपाध्यायं देवयानी च भारत॥ नित्यमाराधयिष्यंस्तौ युवा यौवनगोचरे। गायन् नृत्यन् वादयंश्च देवयानीमतोषयत्॥
en: O descendant of the Bharata race, (Kacha) took the vow he had spoken of at the proper time and began to worship his preceptor (Shukra) and Devayani. That youth (Kacha) daily gratified Devayani who was also in her youth with singing, dancing and playing on various kinds of instruinents.

sn: स शीलयन् देवयानी कन्यां सम्प्राप्तयौवनाम्। पुष्पैः फलैः प्रेषणैश्च तोषयामास भारत॥
en: O descendant of the Bharata race, he gratified that maiden, Devayani, who was in her youth, with the presentations of flowers and fruits and serving her as an obedient servant.

sn: देवयान्यपि तं विप्रं नियमव्रतधारणम्। गायन्ती च ललन्ती च रहः पर्यचरत् तथा॥
en: And Devayani also, when they were alone, gratified that vow-observing youth (Kacha) with her songs and sweetness of manners.

sn: पञ्चवर्षशतान्येवं कचस्य चरतो व्रतम्। तत्रातीयुरथो बुद्ध्वा दानवास्तं ततः कचम्॥ गा रक्षन्तं वने दृष्ट्वा रहस्येकममर्षिताः। जघ्नुर्वृहस्पतेद्वेषाद् विद्यारक्षार्थमेव च॥
en: When five hundreds years had thus passed away of his vow, the Danavas came to know his intention. One day the Danavas saw Kacha when he was tending (his preceptor's) kine. They then killed him out of the hatred they bore against Brihaspati and from the desire of saving the knowledge of Sanjivini.

sn: हत्वा शालावृकेभ्यश्च प्रायच्छल्लवशः कृतम्। ततो गावो निवृत्तास्ता अगोपा: स्वं निवेशनम्॥
en: They hacked him to pieces and gave his body to be devoured by jackals and wolves. The kine returned to the fold without the cowherd (Kacha).

sn: सा दृष्ट्वा रहिता गाश्च कचेनाभ्यागता वनात्। उवाच वचनं काले देवयान्यथ भारत॥
en: O descendant of the Bharata race, when Devayani saw that the kine had returned

sn: देवयान्युवाच आहुतं चाग्निहोत्रं ते सूर्यश्चास्तं गतः प्रभो। अगोपाचागता गावः कचस्तात न दृश्यते॥
en: Devayani said: O sire, the Agnihotra (evening fire) is kindled, the sun has also set. The kine have come back without their cowherd. But Kacha is not to be seen.

sn: व्यक्तं हतो मृतो वापि कचस्तात भविष्यति। तं विना न च जीवेयमिति सत्यं ब्रवीमि ते॥
en: O father, it is evident, Kacha is either dead or killed. I tell you truly that I shall not live without him.

sn: शुक्र उवाच अयमेहीति संशब्द्य मृतं संजीवयाम्यहम्। ततः संजीविनी विद्यां प्रयुज्य कचमाह्वयत्॥
en: Shukra said: I will revive him by saying, "Come here." Then with the help of the knowledge of Sanjivini, he summoned Kacha (to come to him.)

sn: भित्त्वा भित्त्वा शरीराणि वृकाणां स विनिर्गत:। आहूतः प्रादुरभवत् कचो हृष्टोऽथ विद्यया॥
en: Having been thus summoned, Kacha appeared in joy, tearing the bodies of the wolves (that had devoured him.)

sn: कस्माचिरायितोऽसीति पृष्टस्तामाह भार्गवीम्। समिधश्च कुशादीनि काष्ठभारं च भामिनि॥ गृहीत्वा श्रमभारातॊ वटवृक्षं समाश्रितः। गावश्च सहिताः सर्वा वृक्षच्छायामुपाश्रिताः॥
en: Having been asked by the daughter of Bhargava, (Shukra) the reason of his delay, he said, “O sweet lady, burdened with sacrificial wood and Kusha grass, I was coming towards the hermitage and feeling tired, I sat under a banian tree. All the kine also were staying under the shade of that tree.

sn: असुरास्तत्र मां दृष्ट्वा कस्त्वमित्यभ्यचोदयन्। बृहस्पतिसुतश्चाहं कच इत्यभिविश्रुतः॥
en: The Asuras, having seen me there, asked me, “Who are you?” They heard my this reply, "I am Kacha, the son of Brihaspati."

sn: इत्युक्तमात्रे मां हत्वा पेषीकृत्वा तु दानवाः। दत्त्वा शालावृकेभ्यस्तु सुखं जग्मुः स्वमालयम्॥
en: As soon as I said this, those Danavas killed me and having hacked my body to pieces, they gave it to jackals and wolves. They then went to their homes in joy.

sn: आहूतो विद्यया भद्रे भार्गवेण महात्मना। त्वत्समीपमिहायातः कथंचित् समजीवितः॥
en: "O amiable lady, summoned by the illustrious Bhargava (your father), I have somehow or other come before you having been made alive."

sn: हतोऽहमिति चाचख्यौ पृष्टो ब्राह्मणकन्यया। स पुनर्देवयान्योक्तः पुष्पाहारो यदृच्छया॥ वनं ययौ कचो विप्रो ददृशुर्दानवाश्च तम्। पुनस्तं पेषयित्वा तु समुद्राम्भस्यमिश्रयन्॥
en: On another occasion, the Brahmana Kacha at the request of Devayani, went into the forest to collect flowers and when he was freely roaming there, he was again seen by the Danavas. They again killed him, (pounded him to powders) and mixed him with the waters of the ocean.

sn: चिरं गतं पुन: कन्या पित्रे तं संन्यवेदयत्। विप्रेण पुनराहूतो विद्यया गुरुदेहजः। पुनरावृत्य तद् वृत्तं न्यवेदयत तद् यथा॥
en: Finding him again late in coming home, that maiden again told her father what had happened. Having been again summoned by that Brahmana (Shukra) to come home, Kacha appeared before the daughter of his preceptor. He again repeated to her all that had happened to him.

sn: ततस्तृतीयं हत्वा तं दग्ध्वा कृत्वा च चूर्णशः। प्रायच्छन् ब्राह्मणायैव सुरायामसुरास्तदा।॥
en: They killed him for the third time. And having reduced him to ashes by burning, they mixed those ashes with the wine which they offered to the Brahmana (Shukra).

sn: देवयान्यथ भूयोऽपि पितरं वाक्यमब्रवीत्। पुष्पाहारः प्रेषणकृत् कचस्तात न दृश्यते॥
en: Devayani again spoke to her father thus, "O father, Kacha was sent to gather flowers, but he is not to be seen.

sn: व्यक्तं हतो मृतो वापि कचस्तात भविष्यति। तं विना न च जीवेयं कचं सत्यं ब्रवीमि ते॥
en: It is evident, Kacha is either dead or killed. I tell you truly, I shall not live without him.”

sn: शुक्र उवाच बृहस्पतेः सुतः पुत्रि कचः प्रेतगतिं गतः। विद्यया जीवितोऽप्येवं हन्यते करवाणि किम्॥ मैवं शुचो मा रुद देवयानि न त्वादृशी मर्त्यमनुप्रशोचते। यस्यास्तव ब्रह्म च ब्राह्मणाश्च सेन्द्रा देवा वसवोऽथाश्विनौ च॥ मुपस्थाने संनमन्ति प्रभावात्। अशक्योऽसौ जीवयितुं द्विजातिः संजीवितो बध्यते चैव भूयः॥
en: Shukra said : O daughter, the son of Brihaspati, Kacha has gone to the land of the Dead. Though again and again revived by my knowledge, he is often killed. What shall I do? O Devayani, do not grieve, do not weep. One like you should not grieve for one who is mortal. You are worshipped by Brahma, by Brahmanas, the celestials with (their king) Indra, the Vasus, the Ashvinis, the Asuras and by the whole universe. It is impossible to keep him alive. For every time I revive him he is killed (by the Danavas).

sn: देवयान्युवाच यस्याङ्गिरा वृद्धतमः पितामहो बृहस्पतिश्चापि पिता तपोनिधिः। ऋषेः पुत्रं तमथो वापि पौत्रं कथं न शोचेयमहं न रुद्याम्॥
en: Devayani said : Why should I not grieve and weep for Kacha, whose grandfather is old Angirasa himself and whose father is the great ascetic Brihaspati, who is the grandson of a Rishi and the son of a Rishi.

sn: स ब्रह्मचारी च तपोधनश्च सदोत्थितः कर्मसु चैव दक्षः। कचस्य मार्ग प्रतिपत्स्ये न भोक्ष्ये प्रियो हि मे तात कचोऽभिरूपः॥
en: He himself is a Brahmachari and an ascetic; he is always wakeful in every work. O father, I shall starve and follow the way on which Kacha has gone. The handsome Kacha is dear to me.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच स पीडितो देवयान्या महर्षिः समाह्वयत् संरम्भाचैव काव्यः। असंशयं मामसुरा द्विषन्ति ये मे शिष्यानागतान् सूदयन्ति॥
en: Vaishampayana said : The great Rishi (Shukra), the son of Kavi, being much afflicted by Devayani's words, cried in anger, "The Asuras certainly want to injure me, for they killed my disciple living with ime.

sn: स्ते मां यथा व्यभिचरन्ति नित्यम्। अप्यस्य पापस्य भवेदिहान्तः कं ब्रह्महत्या न दहेदपीन्द्रम्॥
en: These followers of Rudra (Asuras) want to make me a non-Brahmana by making me participate in their crimes of killing Brahmanas. The crime of killing a Brahmana even bums Indra. This crime has a terrible end."

sn: गुरोहि भीतो विद्यया चोपहूतः शनैर्वाक्यं जठरे व्याजहार।
en: Having said this, he summoned Kacha, but being afraid of his preceptor's safety, he feebly replied from within the stomach of Shukra.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच स्त्वं चोदरे तिष्ठसि ब्रूहि विप्र॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Shukra then asked him, “O Brahmana, how have you entered my stomach. Tell me truth."

sn: कच उवाच तव प्रसादान्न जहाति मां स्मृतिः स्मरामि सर्वं यच्च यथा च वृत्तम्। न त्वेवं स्यात् तपसः संक्षयो मे ततः केशं घोरमिमं सहामि॥
en: Kacha said: By your grace my memory has not left me. I recollect every thing that had happened not been destroyed. Therefore, I am capable of bearing this insufferable pain.

sn: असुरैः सुरायां भवतोऽस्मि दत्तो हत्वा दग्ध्वा चूर्णयित्वा च काव्य। ब्राह्मीं मायां चासुरीं विप्र मायां त्वयि स्थिते कथमेवातिवर्तेत्॥
en: O son of Kavi, I was killed by the Asuras; my body was burnt and reduced to ashes and I was then given to you with your wine. O Brahman, when you are present, how is possible for the Asura Maya (the power of the Asuras) to overcome the Brahma Maya (the power of the Brahmanas)?

sn: शुक्र उवाच किं ते प्रियं करवाण्यद्य वत्से वधेन मे जीवितं स्यात् कचस्य। नान्यत्र कुर्मम भेदनेन दृश्येत् कचो मद्गतो देवयानि॥
en: Shukra said: O Devayani, what good can I do to you? Kacha's life can be revived only with my death. Kacha is within me. There is no other way of his coming out, except by ripping open my stomach.

sn: देवयान्युवाच द्वौ मां शोकावग्निकल्पौ दहेतां कचस्य नाशस्तव चैवोपघातः। कचस्य नाशे मम नास्ति शर्म तवोपघाते जीवितुं नास्मि शक्ता॥
en: Devayani said : Both the shocks will burn me like fire. The death of Kacha and that of yours are both same to me. The death of Kacha will kill me. If you die, I shall not be able to bear life.

sn: शुक्र उवाच संसिद्धरूपोऽसि बृहस्पतेः सुत यत् त्वां भक्तं भजते देवयानी। विद्यामिमां प्राप्नुहि जीविनीं त्वं न चेदिन्द्रः कचरूपी त्वमद्य॥
en: Shukra said: O son of Brihaspati, you are crowned with success, when Devayani adores you so much. If you are not Indra in the guise of Kacha, today, accept, I give you the science of reviving life.

sn: न निवर्तेत् पुनर्जीवन् कश्चिदन्यो ममोदरात्। ब्राह्मणं वर्जयित्वैकं तस्माद् विद्यामवाप्नुहि॥
en: come None can out alive from my stomach. A Brahmana, however, must not be killed. Therefore, accept the knowledge I teach you.

sn: मस्मद्देहादुपनिष्क्रम्य तात। समीक्षेथा धर्मवतीमवेक्षा गुरोः सकाशात् प्राण्य विद्यां सविद्यः॥
en: Come to life again as my son. Possessed of the knowledge I teach you and being again revived by me, O child, take care that you act with gratitude when you come out of my stomach.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच गुरोः सकाशात् समवाप्य विद्यां भित्त्वा कुक्षि निर्विचक्राम विप्रः। कचोऽभिरूपस्तत्क्षणाद् ब्राह्मणस्य शुकात्यये पौर्णमास्यामिवेन्दुः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Receiving the knowledge (of reviving life) from his preceptor, the handsome Kacha ripped open the stomach (of Shukra) and came out like the moon on the evening of the full-moon night.

sn: मुत्थापयामास मृतं कचोऽपि। विद्यां सिद्धां तामवाप्याभिवाद्य ततः कचस्तं गुरुमित्युवाच॥
en: Seeing the remains of his preceptor lying like a heap of ascetic virtues and learning, Kacha revived him with the knowledge he had received. He then spoke to the preceptor thus-

sn: यः श्रोत्रयोरमृतं संनिषिञ्चेद् विद्यामविद्यस्य यथा ममायम्। तं मन्येऽहं पितरं मातरं च तस्मै न दुह्येत् कृतमस्य जानन्॥
en: “I regard him, who pours the Ambrosia of knowledge into one's ears, as you have done to me who was devoid of knowledge, both as my father and as my mother. He who has gratitude can never injure his preceptor.

sn: ऋतस्य दातारमनुत्तमस्य निधिं निधीनामपिलब्धविद्याः। ये नाद्रियन्ते गुरुमर्चनीयं पापाँल्लोकांस्ते व्रजन्त्यप्रतिष्ठाः॥
en: Those that, having acquired knowledge, injure their preceptor who is an object of adoration, who is the giver of knowledge and who is the most precious of all precious objects on earth, become hated on earth and finally go to the regions of the sinful.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच सुरापानाद् वञ्चनां प्राप्य विद्वान् संज्ञानाशं चैव महातिघोरम्। दृष्ट्वा कचं चापि तथाभिरूपं पीतं तदा सुरया मोहितेन॥ स्तदोशना विप्रहितं चिकीर्षुः। सुरापानं प्रति संजातमन्युः काव्यः स्वयं वाक्यमिदं जगाद।॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having been deceived while under the influence of wine and remembering the terrible consequences of drink and the total loss of consciousness, the result of it and seeing before him the handsome Kacha whom he had drink with the wine while intoxicated, (the learned Shukra), with the wish of effecting a reform in the manner of the Brahmanas, rose from the ground in anger and spoke thus-

sn: न्मोहात् सुरां पास्यति मन्दबुद्धिः। दस्मिल्लोके गर्हितः स्यात् परे च॥
en: "That wretched Brahmana, who being unable to resist the temptation, will drink liquor from this day, shall be considered as to have committed the sin of slaying a Brahmana and he shall be hated both in this and in the other world."

sn: मया चैतां विप्रधर्मोक्तिसीमां मर्यादां वै स्थापितां सर्वलोके। सन्तो विप्राः शुश्रुवांसो गुरूणां देवा लोकाश्चोपशृण्वन्तु सर्वे॥६८।
en: I set this limit to the conduct of the Brahmanas everywhere. Let this (my solemn words) be heard by the honest men, by the Brahmanas, by the celestials and by those who regard their superiors."

sn: स्तपोनिधीनां निधिरप्रमेयः। निदं समाहूय वचोऽभ्युवाच॥
en: Having said this, the illustrious Rishi, the ascetic of ascetics, summoned the Danavas who had been deprived of their good sense by Fate. He then told them.

sn: आचक्षे वो दानवा बालिशाः स्थ सिद्धः कचो वत्स्यति मत्सकाशे। संजीविनीं प्राप्य विद्यां महात्मा तुल्यप्रभावो ब्राह्मणो ब्रह्मभूतः॥
en: "O foolish Danavas, know that Kacha had obtained his wish. He will henceforth dwelt with me. Having obtained the knowledge of Sanjivini, that illustrious Brahmana has become as powerful as Brahma himself."

sn: एतावदुक्त्वा वचनं विरराम स भार्गवः। दानवा विस्मयाविष्टाः प्रययुः स्वं निवेशनम्॥
en: Having said this much, Bhargava (Shukra) stopped. The Danavas, being astonished, went away to their homes.

sn: गुरोरुष्य सकाशे तु दशवर्षशतानि सः। अनुज्ञात: कचो गन्तुमियेष त्रिदशालयम्॥
en: Kacha, after having lived with his preceptor for full one thousand years, prepared to go to the land of the celestials with the permission of his preceptor.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच समावृतव्रतं तं तु विसृष्टं गुरुणा तदा। प्रस्थितं त्रिदशावासं देवयान्यब्रवीदिदम्॥ ऋषेरङ्गिरसः पुत्र वृत्तेनाभिजनेन च। भ्राजसे विद्यया चैव तपसा च दमेन च।॥
en: Vaishampayana said : When the period of his vow expired and when he was prepared to go to the land of the celestials, after having received the permission of his preceptor, Devayani addressed him thus-"O the grandson of Rishi Angirasa, you shine most brightly in conduct, in birth, in learning, in asceticism and in humility.

sn: ऋषिर्यथाङ्गिरा मान्यः पितुर्मम महायशाः। तथा मान्यश्च पूज्यश्च मम भूयो बृहस्पतिः॥
en: As the Rishi Angirasa is honoured by me illustrious father, so is (your father) Brihaspati honoured and respected by me.

sn: एवं ज्ञात्वा विजानीहि यद् ब्रवीमि तपोधन। व्रतस्थे नियमोपेत यथा वर्ताम्यहं त्वयि॥
en: O great ascetic, knowing this, hear what I say. You are aware of my behaviour towards you during the period of your vow.

sn: स समावृतविद्यो मां भक्तां भजितुमर्हसि। गृहाण पाणिं विधिवन्मम मन्त्रपुरस्कृतम्॥
en: "Your vow is now over; you should now fix your affection on me who love you. Accept my hand with ordained rites and Mantras."

sn: कच उवाच पूज्यो मान्यश्च भगवान् यथा तव पिता मम। तथा त्वमनवद्याङ्गि पूजनीयतरा मम॥
en: Kacha said: You are an object of my respect and worship, as is your illustrious father. O lady of faultless features, you are an object of greater reverence to me (than your father).

sn: प्राणेभ्योऽपि प्रियतरा भार्गवस्य महात्मनः। त्वं भद्रे धर्मतः पूज्या गुरुपुत्री सदा मम॥७)]
en: You are dearer than life to the high-souled Bhargava. O amiable lady, you are ever worthy of my worship, as you are the daughter of my preceptor.

sn: यथा मम गुरुर्नित्यं मान्य: शुक्रः पिता तव। देवयानि तथैव त्वं नैवं मां वक्तुमर्हसि॥
en: As your father Shukra, my preceptor, is ever honoured by me, so are you. O Devayani, therefore, you should not speak to me thus.

sn: देवयान्युवाच गुरुपुत्रस्य पुत्रो वै न त्वं पुत्रश्च मे पितुः। तस्मात् पूज्यश्च मान्यश्च ममापि त्वं द्विजोत्तम॥ असुरैर्हन्यमाने च कच त्वयि पुनः पुनः। तदा प्रभृति या प्रीतिस्तां त्वमद्य स्मरस्व मे॥
en: Devayani said : O best of the twice born, you are the son of my preceptor's son, you are not the son of my father. Therefore, you are an object of my respect and worship. O Kacha, when the Asuras killed you again and again, you should recollect today the love I showed towards you.

sn: सौहार्दे चानुरागे च वेत्थ मे भक्तिमुत्तमाम्। न मामर्हसि धर्मज्ञ त्यक्तुं भक्तामनागसम्॥
en: O virtuous man, remembering my love and affection for you and also my devoted regard for you, you should not abandon me without any faults.

sn: कच उवाच अनियोज्ये नियोगे मां नियुनसि शुभव्रते। प्रसीद सुभु त्वं मह्यं गुरोर्गुरुतरा शुभे॥ यत्रोषितं विशालाक्षि त्वया चन्द्र निभानने। तत्राहमुषितो भद्रे कुक्षौ काव्यस्य भामिनि॥ भगिनी धर्मतो मे त्वं मैवं वोचः सुमध्यमे। सुखमसम्युषितो भद्रे न मन्युर्विद्यते मम॥
en: Kacha said: O lady of virtuous vows, do not urge me into such a sinful course. O lady of fair eyebrows, be graceful to me. O amiable lady, you are an object of greater regard than my preceptor. O large-eyed lady, O lady of handsome face, O amiable maiden, the place the body of the son of Kavi, (Shukra) where you live, is also my abode. You are truly my sister. O slender-waisted lady, O_amiable maiden, do not say so. We have most happily passed the days we have lived together. There is perfect good feeling now existing between us.

sn: आपृच्छे त्वां गमिष्यामि शिवमाशंस मे पथि। अविरोधेन धर्मस्य स्मर्तव्योऽस्मि कथान्तरे। अप्रमत्तोत्थिता नित्यमाराधय गुरुं मम॥
en: I ask your leave to go away. Bless me so that good may come to my journey. Remember me in your conversations as one who has not transgressed virtue. Serve my preceptor with readiness and singleness of heart.

sn: देवयान्युवाच यदि मां धर्मकामार्थे प्रत्याख्यास्यसि याचितः। ततः कच न ते विद्या सिद्धिमेषा गमिष्यति॥
en: Devayani said: If you refuse to make me your wife, solicited by me as I do, O Kacha, (indeed I say) your knowledge will bear no fruits.

sn: कच उवाच गुरुपुत्रीति कृत्वाहं प्रत्याचक्षे न दोषतः। गुरुणा चाननुज्ञातः काममेवं शपस्व माम्॥
en: Kacha said: I refused to comply with your request, because you are my preceptor's daughter. (I did not refuse you) for any fault of yours. my preceptor also had not issued any command regarding this matter. Curse me if it pleases you.

sn: आर्ष धर्मं ब्रुवाणोऽहं देवयानि यथा त्वया। शप्तो ना.ऽस्मि शापस्य कामतोऽद्य न धर्मतः॥ तस्माद् भवत्या यः कामो न तथा स भविष्यति। ऋषिपुत्रो न ते कश्चिजातु पाणिं ग्रहीष्यति॥
en: O Devayani, I have told you what should be the conduct of Rishis. I, therefore, do not deserve your curse. But notwithstanding all this you have cursed me out of desire and not from a sense of duty. Therefore, your desire shall not be fulfilled no Rishi's son will ever accept your hand.

sn: फलिष्यति न ते विद्या यत् त्वं मामात्थ तत् तथा। अध्यापयिष्यामि त यं तस्य विद्या फलिष्यति॥
en: You have said that my knowledge would not bear fruits. Let it be so. But it shall bear fruits in him whom I shall teach it.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्त्वा द्विजश्रेष्ठो देवयानी कचस्तदा। त्रिदशेशालयं शीघ्रं जगाम द्विजसत्तमः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having said this to Devayani, that best of Brahmanas, that foremost of the twice-born, Kacha hurriedly went away to the land of the celestials.

sn: तमागतमभिप्रेक्ष्य देवा इन्द्रपुरोगमाः। बृहस्पति सभाज्येदं कचं वचनमब्रुवन्॥
en: Seeing him arrived, the celestials with Indra at their head looked with delight towards Brihaspati and spoke to him thus.

sn: देवा ऊचुः यत् त्वयास्मद्धितं कर्म कृतं वै परमाद्भुतम्। न ते यशः प्रणशिता भागभाक् च भविष्यसि॥
en: The Devas said : You have performed an act of great good for us; your achievements are wonderful, your fame will never die, you will be the sharer with us in the sacrificial offerings.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच कृतविद्ये कचे प्राप्ते हृष्टरूपा दिवौकसः। कचादधीत्य तां विद्यां कृतार्था भरतर्षभ।॥
en: Vaishampayana said: O best of the Bharata race, the dwellers of heaven were exceedingly glad to get back Kacha who had learnt the knowledge (of Sanjivini). The celestial then learnt the Sanjivini from Kacha and considered their object achieved.

sn: सर्व एव समागम्य शतक्रुतमथाब्रुवन्। कालस्ते विक्रमस्याद्य जहि शत्रून् पुरन्दर॥
en: They all assembled together and thus spoke to Indra. “O Indra, the time has come to show your prowess. Kill your enemies."

sn: एवमुक्तस्तु सहितैस्त्रिदशैर्मघवांस्तदा। तथेत्युक्त्वा प्रचक्राम सोऽपश्यत वने स्त्रियः॥
en: Having been thus addressed, Indra said “Be it so." He then, accompanied by the celestials set out. He saw many damsels in the forest.

sn: क्रीडन्तीनां त कन्यानां वने चैत्ररथोपमे। वायुभूत: स वस्त्राणि सर्वाण्येव व्यमिश्रयत्॥
en: The maidens were sporting in a lake in the wood which was like that of Chitraratha. Changing himself into wind, he (Indra) mixed up their clothes.

sn: ततो जलात् समुत्तीर्य कन्यास्ताः सहितास्तदा। वस्त्राणि जगृहुस्तानि यथासन्नान्यनेकशः॥ तत्र वासो देवयान्याः शर्मिष्ठा जगृहे तदा। व्यतिमिश्रमजानन्ती दुहिता वृषपर्वणः॥
en: The maidens, after rising from the water all together, put on the clothes which each got near her from the mixed up heap. The cloth of Devayani was thus taken up and worn by Sharmishtha, the daughter of king Vrishaparva, not knowing that it belonged to others.

sn: ततस्तयोमिथस्तत्र विरोधः समजायत। देवयान्याश्च राजेन्द्र शर्मिष्ठायाश्च तत्कृते॥
en: O great king, a dispute, thereupon, arose between Devayani and Sharmishtha.

sn: देवयान्युवाच कस्माद् गृह्णासि मे वस्त्रं शिष्या भूत्वा ममासुरि। समुदाचारहीनाया न ते साधु भविष्यति॥
en: Devayani said : O daughter of the Asura, how do you dare take my cloth, being my pupil. Destitute of good conduct, nothing good can come to you.

sn: शर्मिष्ठोवाच आसीनं च शयानं च पिता ते पितरं मम। स्तौति वन्दीव चाभीक्ष्णं नीचैः स्थित्वा विनीतवत्॥
en: Sharmishtha said : Whether my father is sitting or lying your father, occupying a lower seat and casting his eyes downwards, adores him like a Vandi (a chanter of praises.)

sn: याचतस्त्वं हि दुहिता स्तुवतः प्रतिगृह्णतः। सुताहं स्तूयमानस्य ददतोऽप्रतिगृह्णतः॥ आदुन्वस्व विदुन्वस्व दुह्य कुष्यस्व याचकि। अनायुधा सायुधाया रिक्ता क्षुभ्यसि भिक्षुकि। लप्स्यसे प्रतियोद्धारं न हि त्वां गणयाम्यहम्॥
en: You are the daughter of a man who begs and I am the daughter of one who bestows alms. your father chants praises of others and my father's praises are chanted. Your father lives on alms, my father bestows them. O beggar's girl, you are free to strike your breast, to use harsh words, to vow enmity to me and to give way to your wrath. O beggarly woman, you weep in vain. You cannot harm me, though I can harm you. You desire to quarrel with me, but I do not at all consider you as my equal.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच समुच्छ्रयं देवयानीं गतां सक्तां च वाससि॥ शर्मिष्ठा प्राक्षिपत् कूपे ततः स्वपुरमागमत्। हतेयमिति विज्ञाय शर्मिष्ठा पापनिश्चया॥ अनवेक्ष्य ययौ वेश्म क्रोधवेगपरायणा। अथ तं देशमभ्यागाद् ययातिर्नहुषात्मजः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having heard this, Devayani became very angry and she began to tear her cloth. But Sharmishtha, throwing her into a well, went away to her home. The wicked Sharmishtha thought her to be dead and went home in a wrathful mood. When she went away, the son of Nahusha, Yayati came to that place; he was after deer.

sn: श्रान्तयुग्यः श्रान्तहयो मृगलिप्सुः पिपासितः। स नाहुषः प्रेक्षमाण उदपानं गतोदकम्॥
en: The pair of horses in his car were fatigued and he himself was thirsty. That son of Nahusha (Yayati) saw a well in which there was no water.

sn: ददर्श राजा तां तत्र कन्यामग्निशिखामिव। तामपृच्छत् स दृष्ट्वैव कन्याममरवर्णिनीम्॥
en: There (in that well) the king saw a maiden as effulgent as fire. Seeing her within the well, the illustrious king addressed that girl who was as beautiful as a celestial maiden.

sn: सान्त्वयित्वा नृपश्रेष्ठः साम्ना परमवल्गुना। का त्वं ताम्रनखी श्यामा सुमृष्टमणिकुण्डला॥
en: Thai best of kings, pacifying her with sweet words said, O fair lady, O lady with bright nails, as burnished copper and with earrings of celestial gems, who are you?

sn: दीर्घ ध्यायसि चात्यर्थं कस्माच्छोचसि चातुरा। कथं च पतितास्यस्मिन् कूपे वीरुत्तृणावृते॥ दुहिता चैव कस्य त्वं वद सत्यं सुमध्यमे।
en: Why are you in such anxiety? Why are you weeping in distress? How have you fallen into this well covered with long grass and creepers? O beauty of slender-waist, tell me truly, whose daughter are you?

sn: देवयान्युवाच योऽसौ देवैर्हतान् दैत्यानुत्थापयति विद्यया॥ तस्य शुक्रस्य कन्याहं स मां नूनं न बुध्यते।
en: Devayani said : I am the daughter of Shukra who revives the Asuras, killed by the celestial. He knows not what has befallen me.

sn: एष मे दक्षिणो राजन् पाणिस्ताननखाङ्गुलिः॥ समुद्धर गृहीत्वा मां कुलीनस्त्वं हि मे मतः। जानामि त्वां हि संशान्तं वीर्यवन्तं यशस्विनम्॥ तस्मान्मां पतितामस्मात् कूपादुद्धर्तुमर्हसि।
en: O king, this is my right hand with nails as bright as the burnished copper. You are nobly born, I ask you, take my hand and raise me up. I know, you are very gentle, very powerful and greatly famous. You should raise me up from this well.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तामथो ब्राह्मणी राजा विज्ञाय नहुषात्मजः॥ गृहीत्वा दक्षिणे पाणावुजहार ततोऽवटात्। उद्धृत्य चैनां तरसा तस्मात् कूपान्नराधिपः॥ आमन्त्रयित्वा सुश्रोणी ययाति स्वपुरं ययौ। गते तु नाहुषे तस्मिन् देवयान्यप्यनिन्दिता॥ उवाच शोकसंतप्ता घूर्णिकामागतां पुरः।
en: Vaishampayana said : The son of Nahusha, king (Yayati) having learnt that she was the daughter of a Brahmana, took hold of her right hand and raised her up from that well. The king, after speedily raising her from the well and speaking sweet and courteous words to that beauty of tapering thighs, went away to his own capital. After the departure of the son of Nahusha (Yayati), the faultless featured Devayani spoke in sorrow to Ghurnika who came there.

sn: देवयान्युवाच त्वरितं घूर्णिके गच्छ शीघ्रमाचक्ष्व मे पितुः॥ नेदानीं सम्प्रवेक्ष्यामि नगरं वृषपर्वणः।
en: Devayani said : O Ghurnika, go speedily to my father and tell him as soon as possible all that had happened. I shall not enter the city of Vrishaparva.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच सा तत्र त्वरितं गत्वा घूर्णिकासुरमन्दिरम्॥ दृष्ट्वा काव्यमुवाचेदं सम्भ्रमाविष्टचेतना। आचचक्षे महाप्राज्ञं देवयानी वने हताम्॥ शर्मिष्ठया महाभाग दुहित्रा वृषपर्वणः। श्रुत्वा दुहितरं काव्यस्तत्र शर्मिष्ठया हताम्॥ त्वरया निर्ययौ दुःखान्मार्गमाणः सुतां वने। दृष्ट्वा दुहितरं काव्यो देवयानीं ततो वने॥ बाहुभ्यां सम्परिष्वज्य दुःखितो वाक्यमब्रवीत्। आत्मदोषैर्नियच्छन्ति सर्वे दुःखसुखे जनाः॥ मन्ये दुश्चरितं तेऽस्ति यस्येयं निष्कृतिः कृता।
en: Vaishampayana said: Ghurnika speedily went to the palace of the Asura (chief). Finding the son of Kavi (Shukra), she spoke to his thus, her perception having been dimmed by anger. “O great Brahmana, O illustrious man, I tell you, Devayani had been ill-used by Sharmishtha, the daughter of Vrishaparva. Having heard that his daughter had been ill-used by Sharmishtha, he soon went to search for her with a heavy heart. And when he found her in the forest, the son of Kavi embraced her with affection and spoke to her with his voice choked with grief. “The weal and woe that befall on people is always due to their own faults. You had some fault, I am sure, which has been thus expiated."

sn: देवयान्युवाच निष्कृतिर्मेऽस्तु वा मास्तु शृणुष्वावहितो मम॥ शर्मिष्ठया यदुक्तास्मि दुहिता वृषपर्वणः। सत्यं किलैतत् सा प्राह दैत्यानामसि गायनः॥ एवं हि मे कथयति शर्मिष्ठा वार्षपर्वणी। वचनं तीक्ष्णपरुषं क्रोधरक्तेक्षणा भृशम्॥ स्तुवतो दुहिता नित्यं याचत: प्रतिगृह्णतः। अहं तु स्तूयमानस्य ददतोऽप्रतिगृह्णतः॥
en: Devayani said: Be it punishment of my fault or not (O father), hear all that the daughter of Vrishaparva, Sharmishtha, had said to me. She has said, (I say) truly, that you are a Bandi (hired chanter) of the Asura king. Even thus did Sharmishtha, the daughter of Vrishaparva, speak. These cruel and piercing words, with her eyes red (with anger). (She said), “You are the daughter of one who always chants the praise of others for hire and who always asks for charity.

sn: इदं मामाह शर्मिष्ठा दुहिता वृषपर्वणः। क्रोधसंरक्तनयना दर्पपूर्णा पुनः पुनः॥
en: And who accepts alms, whereas I am the daughter of one who is the adored of all, who gives alms and never receives and gift from any body.” Thus again and again spoke to me Sharmishtha, the daughter of Vrishaparva, full of pride, her eyes red in anger.

sn: यद्यहं स्तुवतस्तात दुहिता प्रतिगृह्णतः। प्रसादयिष्ये शर्मिष्ठामित्युक्ता तु सखी मया॥
en: O father, if I am really the daughter of a hired chanter of others' praises and of one who accepts alms, I must adore her in the hope of getting her favour. I have already told this to her.

sn: शुक्र उवाच स्तुवतो दुहिता न त्वं याचतः प्रतिगृह्णतः। अस्तोतुः स्तूयमानस्य दुहिता देवयान्यसि॥
en: Shukra said: O Devayani, you are not the daughter of a hired chanter of praises, nor that of one who asks for alms and receives them. You are the daughter of one who is adored by all and who adores none.

sn: वृषपर्वैव तद् वेद शक्रो राजा च नाहुषः। अचिन्त्यं ब्रह्म निर्द्वन्द्वमैश्वरं हि बलं मम॥
en: Vrishaparva and Indra and king Yayati, (all) know my strength to be inconceivable like Brahma and unapproachable God.

sn: यच किंचित् सर्वगतं भूमौ वा यदि वा दिवि। तस्याहमीश्वरो नित्यं तुष्टेनोक्तः स्वयम्भुवा॥
en: The Self created (Brahma) himself, being pleased with me said that I was the lord of that which was in all things on earth or in heaven.

sn: अहं जलं विमुञ्चामि प्रजानां हितकाम्यया। पुष्णाम्योषधयः सर्वा इति सत्यं ब्रवीमि ते॥
en: I tell you truly, that it is I who pour rain for the good of all and nourish the annual plants that sustain all living creatures.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवं विषादमापन्नां मन्युना सम्प्रपीडिताम्। वचनैर्मधुरैः श्लक्ष्णैः सान्त्वयामास तां पिता॥
en: Vaishampayana said : It was thus with such sweet and sensible words, the father tried to pacify his angry and sorrowful daughter.

sn: शुक्र उवाच यः परेषां नरो नित्यमतिवादांस्तितिक्षते। देवयानि विजानीहि तेन सर्वमिदं जितम्॥ उच्यते॥ यः समुत्पतितं क्रोधं निगृह्णाति हयं यथा। स यन्तेत्युच्यते सद्भिर्न यो रश्मिषु लम्बते॥२१.
en: Shukra said: O Devayani, know that the man who does not regard the evil words of others, conquers every thing. The wise men call him a true charioteer who holds tightly the reins of his horses. He is a true man who subdues his rising anger.

sn: यः समुत्पतितं क्रोधमक्रोधेन निरस्यति। देवयानि विजानीहि तेन सर्वमिदं जितम्॥
en: O Devayani, know that he who subdues the rising anger by his feeling of non-anger, conquers everything on earth.

sn: यः समुत्पतितं क्रोधं क्षमयेह निरस्यति। यथोरगस्त्वचं जीर्णा स वै पुरुष
en: He who subdues his rising anger by forgiveness like the casting off the slough of a snake is called a true man.

sn: यः संधारयते मन्यु योऽतिवादांस्तितिक्षते। यश्च तप्तो न तपति दृढं सोऽर्थस्य भाजनम्॥
en: He who subdues his anger, he who does not regard the bad words of others, he who is not angry even when there is a cause, certainly acquires the four objects for which we live (namely Dharma, Artha, Kama and Moksha.)

sn: यो यजेदपरिश्रान्तो मासि मासि शतं समाः। न क्रुद्धेयद् यश्च सर्वस्य तयोरक्रोधनोऽधिकः॥
en: Between the two men, one performing sacrifices continually every month for one hundred years and one who does not feel any anger, the man who does not feel any anger is the greater man.

sn: यत् कुमाराः कुमार्यश्च वैरं कुर्युरचेतसः। न तत् प्राज्ञोऽनुकुर्वीत न विदुस्ते बलाबलम्॥
en: Boys and girls, who are incapable of distinguishing between right and wrong, quarrel among one another. The wise never imitate them.

sn: देवयान्युवाच वेदाहं तात बालापि धर्माणां यदिहान्तरम्। अक्रोधे चातिवादे च वेद चापि बलाबलम्॥
en: the power Devayani said: O father, I know, though I am a girl, what are duties and virtues. I also know the difference between anger and forgiveness and of each.

sn: शिष्यस्याशिष्यवृत्तेस्तु न क्षन्तव्यं बुभूषता। तस्मात् संकीर्णवृत्तेषु वासो मम न रोचते॥
en: But when a pupil behaves disrespectfully towards his tutor, he should never be forgiven by the preceptor, if he wants to benefit him. Therefore, I do not desire to live in a country where the people are so bad.

sn: पुमांसो ये हि निन्दन्ति वृत्तेनाभिजनेन च। न तेषु निवसेत् प्राज्ञः श्रेयोऽर्थी पापबुद्धिषु॥
en: The wise man who desire the good of all, should not live among men who are sinfully inclined and she always speak ill of men of high birth and good behaviour.

sn: ये त्वेनपभिजानन्ति वृत्तेनाभिजनेन वा। तेषु साधुषु वस्तव्यं स वासः श्रेष्ठ उच्यते॥
en: It is said to be the best place to live where high birth and good conduct are known and respected and where men know our birth and behaviour.

sn: वाग् दुरुक्तं महाघोरं दुहितुर्वृषपर्वणः। मम मनाति हृदयमग्निकाम इवारणिम्॥
en: The cruel words of the daughter of Vrishaparva burn my heart, as men, desirous of kindling a fire, burn the dry woods.

sn: यः सपत्नश्रियं दीप्तां हीनश्रीः पर्युपासते। मरणं शोभनं तस्य इति विद्वज्जना विदुः॥
en: I think nothing is more painful in the three worlds than to adore one's enemies, who are blessed with good fortune, whereas he possesses none. The learned men have said that death would be preferable to such a man.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततः काव्यो भृगुश्रेष्ठ समन्युरुपगम्य हा वृषपर्वाणमासीनमित्युवाचाविचारयन्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : The best of the Bhrigu race, the son of Kavi (Shukra) himself became angry. Coming to the place where Vrishaparva was seated he fearlessly addressed him thus-

sn: नाधर्मश्चरितो राजन् सद्यः फलति गौरिव। शनैरावय॑मानो हि कर्तुर्मूलानि कृन्तति॥
en: "O king, the sinful acts like the earth immediately do not bear fruit. But they do gradually and secretly cut away the roots of their doer.

sn: पुत्रेषु वा नतृषु वा न चेदात्मनि पश्यति। फलत्येव ध्रुवं पापं गुरुभुक्तमिवोदरे॥
en: Such fruits, are seen, either in one's ownself, or in one's son, or in one's grandson. Sin must bear fruits, like rich food they cannot be digested.

sn: यदधात यथा विप्रं कचमाङ्गिरसं तदा। अपापशीलं धर्मज्ञं शुश्रूषं मद्गृहे रतम्॥
en: As you killed the grandson of Rishi Angirasa, the Brahmana Kacha, who was virtuous, learned in religious precepts and attentive to duties, when he lived with me.

sn: वधादनहतस्तस्य वधाच दुहितुर्मम। वृषपर्वन् निबोधेदं त्यक्ष्यामि त्वां सबान्धवम्। स्थातुं त्वद्विषये राजन् न शक्ष्यामि त्वया सह॥
en: As you have mal-treated my daughter who did not deserve it, O Vrishaparva, know, I shall leave you and all your race. O king, for this reason I can no longer stay with you.

sn: अहो मामभिजानासि दैत्य मिथ्याप्रलपिनम्। यथेममात्मनो दोषं न नियच्छस्युपेक्षसे॥
en: Do not think, O Danava, that I am raving or I am a liar. You think very little of your faults and do not try to correct them.

sn: वृषपर्वोवाच नाधर्मं न मृषावादं त्वयि जानामि भार्गव। त्वयि धर्मश्च सत्यं च तत् प्रसीदतु नो भवान्॥ यद्यस्मानपहाय त्वमितो गच्छसि भार्गव। समुद्रं सम्प्रवेक्ष्यामो नान्यदस्ति परायणम्॥
en: Vrishaparva said : O son of Bhrigu, never I attributed to you falsehood or impiety. Virtue and truth ever dwell in you. Be gracious to me. O son of Bhrigu, if you really leave me and go away (from this place), we shall have then to go into the deep bottom of the ocean. There is no other alternative for us.

sn: शुक्र उवाच समुद्रं प्रविशध्वं वा दिशो वा द्रवतासुराः। दुहितु प्रियं सोढुं शक्तोऽहं दयिता हि मे॥
en: Shukra said: O Asura, I care very little whether you go into the bottom of the sea, of fly away to all directions, I am incapable of bearing my daughter's grief.

sn: प्रसाद्यतां देवयानी जीवितं यत्र मे स्थितम्। योगक्षेमकरस्तेऽहमिन्द्रस्येव बृहस्पतिः॥
en: My life depends on her. Seek, O Asuras, to please her. As Brihaspati always seeks the good of Indra, so I seek your good with my ascetic powers.

sn: वृषपर्वोवाच यत् किंचिदसुरेन्द्राणां विद्यते वसु भार्गव। भुवि हस्तिगवाश्वं च तस्य त्वं मम चेश्वरः॥
en: Vrishaparva said : O son of Bhrigu, you are the absolute master of everything that belongs to the Asura chief in this world these elephants, kine and horses, nay even myself.

sn: शुक्र उवाच यत् किंचिदस्ति द्रविणं दैत्येन्द्राणां महासुर। तस्येश्वरोऽस्मि यद्येषा देवयानी प्रसाद्यताम्॥
en: Shukra said: Ogreat Asura, if it is (really) true that I am the lord over all the wealth of the Asuras, then go and try to please Devayani.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्तस्तथेत्याह वृषपर्वा महाकविः। देवयान्यन्तिकं गत्वा तमर्थ प्राह भार्गवः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : When the great son of Kavi (Shukra) was thus addressed by Vrishaparva, he went to Devayani and the son of Bhrigu told her all.

sn: देवयान्युवाच यदि त्वमीश्वरस्तात राज्ञो वित्तस्य भार्गव नाभिजानामि तत् तेऽहं राजा तु वदतु स्वयम्॥
en: Devayani said : O son of Bhrigu, O father, if you are really the lord over the Asura king and all his wealth, then let the king come personally to me and speak it in my presence.

sn: वृषपर्वोवाच यं काममभिकामासि देवयानि शुचिस्मिते। तत् तेऽहं सम्प्रदास्यामि यदि वापि हि दुर्लभम्॥
en: Vrishaparva said : O Devayani, O lady of sweet smiles, whatever you desire to possess, however difficult it may be to get, I am willing to give you.

sn: देवयान्युवाच दासी कन्यासहस्रेण शर्मिष्ठामभिकामये। अनु मां तत्र गच्छेत् सा यत्र दद्याच मे पिता॥
en: Devayani said : I desire to have Sharmishtha as my maidservant one thousand other damsels. She must also follow me to the house of him on whom my father will bestow me.

sn: वृषपर्वोवाच उत्तिष्ठ त्वं गच्छ धात्रि शर्मिष्ठां शीघ्रमानय। यं च कामयते कामं देवयानी करोतु तम्॥
en: Vrishaparva said : O nurse, go and bring quickly Sharmishtha here. Let her also act according to the desire of Devayani.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततो धात्री तत्र गत्वा शर्मिष्ठां वाक्यमब्रवीत्। उत्तिष्ठ भद्रे शर्मिष्ठे ज्ञातीनां सुखमावह॥
en: Vaishampayana said : The nurse then went to Sharmishtha and told her, “O amiable Sharmishtha, rise and follow me.

sn: त्यजति ब्राह्मण: शिष्यान् देवयान्या प्रचोदितः। सायं कामयते कामं स कार्योऽद्य त्वयानघे॥
en: Accomplish the good of your race. Urged by Devayani, the Brahmana (Shukra) is about to leave his disciples (the Asuras). O sinless lady, you must do as Devayani desires."

sn: शर्मिष्ठोवाच यं सा कामयते कामं करवाण्यहमद्य तम्। यद्येवमाह्वयेच्छुक्रो देवयानीकृते हि माम्। मद्दोषान्मा गमच्छुक्रो देवयानी च मत्कृते॥
en: Sharmishtha said : I shall cheerfully do as Devayani desires. Both Shukra and Devayani, must not leave the Asuras through any fault of mine.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततः कन्यासहस्रेण वृता शिबिकया तदा। पितुर्नियोगात् त्वरिता निश्चक्राम पुरोत्तमात्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having been commanded by her father, Sharmishtha with one thousand maidens came out of her father's excellent palace.

sn: शर्मिष्ठोवाच अहं दासीसहस्रेण दासी ते परिचारिका। अनु त्वां तत्र यास्यामि यत्र दास्यति ते पिता॥
en: Sharmishtha said : I am your maid-servant, with my one thousand maids. I shall follow you where your father will bestow you.

sn: देवयान्युवाच स्तुवतो दुहिताहं ते याचतः प्रतिगृह्णतः । स्तूयमानस्य दुहिता कथं दासी भविष्यसि॥
en: Devayani said: I am the daughter of one who is a hired chanter of praise, who asks for alms and accepts them, whereas you are the daughter of one who is adored. Why should you become my maid-servant?

sn: शर्मिष्ठोवाच येन केनचिदार्तानां ज्ञातीनां सुखमावहेत्। अतस्त्वामनुयास्यामि यत्र दास्यति ते पिता॥
en: Sharmishtha said : One must try to do good to one's affected relatives. Therefore, I shall follow you where your father will bestow you.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच प्रतिश्रुते दासभावे दुहित्रा वृषपर्वणः। देवयानी नृपश्रेष्ठ पितरं वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : O best of kings, when Sharmishtha thus promised to be the maid-servant of Devayani, she then thus spoke to her father.

sn: देवयान्युवाच प्रविशामि पुरं तात तुष्टास्मि द्विजसत्तम। अमोघं तव विज्ञानमस्ति विद्याबलं च ते॥
en: Devayani said : () best of Brahmanas, O father, I am satisfied. I shall now enter the Asura capital. I know your science and power of knowledge is not futile.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्तो दुहित्रा स द्विजश्रेष्ठो महायशाः। प्रविवेश पुरं हृष्टः पूजितः सर्वदानवैः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having been thus addressed by his daughter, that best of Brahmanas, that illustrious man entered the capital with all happiness, sand he was worshipped by all the Danavas.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच अथ दीर्घस्य कालस्य देवयानी नृपोत्तम। वनं तदेव निर्याता क्रीडाथ वरवर्णिनी।॥
en: Vaishampayana said : O best of kings, after a long time the beautiful Devayani went to the same wood to sport.

sn: तेन दासीसहस्रेण सार्धं शर्मिष्ठया तदा। तमेव देशं सम्प्राप्ता यथाकामं चचार सा॥ ताभिः सखीभिः सहिता सर्वाभिर्मुदिता भृशम्। क्रीडन्त्योऽभिरताः सर्वाः पिबन्त्यो मधुमाधवीम्॥ खादन्त्यो विविधान् भक्ष्यान् विदशन्त्यः फलानि च। पुनश्च नाहुषो राजा मृगलिप्सुर्यदृच्छया॥ तमेव देशं सम्प्राप्तो जलार्थी श्रमकर्शितः। ददृशे देवयानी स शर्मिष्ठां ताश्च योषितः॥
en: She reached the spot with Sharmishtha and her one thousand maids. She wandered about at pleasure. She felt herself very happy, being waited upon by these companions.
