They all sported there, they drank the honey of the flowers. They ate various fruits, (they threw away many) after biting. The king (Yayati), the son of Nahusha, in the course of his wanderings for hunting again came there, tired and thirsty. He saw Devayani and Sharmishtha and all those maidens.

sn: पिबन्तीर्ललमानाश्च दिव्याभरणभूषिताः। उपविष्टां च ददृशे देवयानी शुचिस्मिताम्॥
en: They were all decked with beautiful omaments and they were full of voluptuous languor on account of the honey they drank. Devayani of sweet smiles, was reclining at her same case.

sn: रूपेणाप्रतिमां तासां स्त्रीणां मध्ये वराङ्गनाम्। शर्मिष्ठया सेव्यमानां पादसंवाहनादिभिः॥
en: She was matchless in beauty and the most handsome of all the damsels. She was waited upon by Sharmishtha who was gently pressing her feet.

sn: ययातिरुवाच द्वाभ्यां कन्यासहस्राभ्यां द्वे कन्ये परिवारिते। गोत्रे च नामनी चैव द्वयोः पृच्छाम्यहं शुभे॥
en: Yayati said : O amiable ladies, it seems that these one thousands maids wait on you two. I would ask you (to tell me) both your names and parentage.

sn: देवयान्युवाच आख्यास्याम्यहमादत्स्व वचनं मे नराधिप। शुक्रो नामासुरगुरुः सुतां जानीहि तस्य माम्॥
en: Devayani said : O king, hear my words, Know that I am the daughter of Shukra, the preceptor of the Asuras.

sn: इयं च मे सखी दासी यत्राहं तत्र गामिनी। दुहिता दानवेन्द्रस्य शर्मिष्ठा वृषपर्वणः॥
en: This my companion is my maid, she will go wherever I shall go. She is Sharmishtha, the daughter of the Asura king, Vrishaparva.

sn: ययातिरुवाच कथं तु ते सखी दासी कन्येयं वरवर्णिनी। असुरेन्द्रसुता सुभ्रूः परं कौतूहलं हि मे॥
en: Yayati said : I am curious to know why this lady of fair eye-brows, this most beautiful damsel, this daughter of the Asura king, companion, is your maid-servant?

sn: देवयान्युवाच सर्व एव नरश्रेष्ठ विधानमनुवर्तते। विधानविहितं मत्वा मा विचित्राः कथा: कृथाः॥
en: Devayani said : O best of kings, everything comes to pass according to Fate. Do not be astonished at this. V:10w it to be also the result of Fate.

sn: राजवद् रूपवेषौ ते ब्राह्मीं वाचं बिभर्षि च। को नाम त्वं कुतश्चासि कस्य पुत्रश्च शंस प्रे॥
en: Your features and attire are both like a king. Your speech is also like the words of the Vedas. Tell me your name. Whence have you come? Whose son are you?

sn: ययातिरुवाच ब्रह्मचर्येण वेदो मे कृत्स्नः श्रुतिपथं गतः। राजाहं राजपुत्रश्च ययातिरिति विश्रुतः॥
en: this your Yayati said : In my Brahmacharya, the whole of the Vedas entered my ears. I am a king and a son of a king; I am known as Yayati.

sn: देवयान्युवाच केनास्यर्थेन नृपते इमं देशमुपागतः। जिघृक्षुर्वारिज किंचिदथवा मृगलिप्सया॥
en: Devayani said : O king, why have you come here? Is it to gather lotuses, or to angle, or to hunt.

sn: ययातिरुवाच मृगलिप्सुरहं भद्रे पानीयार्थमुपागतः। बहुधाप्यनुयुक्तोऽस्मि तदनुज्ञातुमर्हसि।॥
en: Yayati said : O amiable lady, I was thirsty in the pursuit of deer. I have come here in search of water. I wait but your commands to leave this place.

sn: देवयान्युवाच द्वाभ्यां कन्यासहस्राभ्यां दास्या शर्मिष्ठया सह। त्वदधीनास्मि भद्रं ते सखा भर्ता च मे भव॥
en: Devayani said: Prosperity to you? Be my friend and husband. I wait for your commands with my two thousand damsels and Sharmishtha, my maid-servant.

sn: ययातिरुवाच विद्ध्यौशनसि भद्रं ते न त्वामोऽस्मि भाविनि। अविवाह्या हि राजानो देवयानि पितुस्तव॥
en: Yayati said : O beautiful lady, I do not deserve you. You are the daughter of Shukra, (therefore) you are far superior to me. O Devayani, your father cannot bestow you on even great king.

sn: देवयान्युवाच संसृष्टं ब्रह्मणा क्षत्रं क्षत्रेण ब्रह्म संहितम्। ऋषिश्चाप्यधिपुत्रश्च नाहुषाङ्ग वहस्व माम्॥
en: Devayani said : Brahmanas have already been mixed with Kshatriyas and Kshatriyas with Brahmanas. You are a son of a Rishi and a yourself a Rishi. Therefore, O son of Nahusha, marry me.

sn: ययातिरुवाच एकदेहोद्भवा वर्णाश्चत्वारोऽपि वराङ्गने। पृथग्धर्माः पृथक्छौचास्तेषां तु ब्राह्मणो वरः॥
en: Yayati said : O beautiful lady, the four orders have no doubt sprung from one body. But they have different duties and virtues, which are not the same (for every order.) The Brahmanas are superior to all.

sn: देवयान्युवाच पाणिधर्मो नाहुषायं न पुम्भिः सेवितः पुरा। तं मे त्वमग्रहीर वृणोमि त्वामहं ततः॥
en: Devayani said : This hand of mine was never touched by any man except you. Therefore, I accept you as my husband.

sn: कथं नु मे मनस्विन्याः पाणिमन्यः पुमान् स्पृशेत्। गृहीतमृषिपुत्रेण स्वयं वाप्य॒षिणा त्वया॥
en: How will any other man touch my hand of wise one which is touched by you who are a Rishi?

sn: ययातिरुवाच क्रुद्धादाशीविषात् सर्पाज्ज्वलनात् सर्वतोमुखात्। दुराधर्षतरो विप्रो ज्ञेयः पुंसा विजानता॥
en: Yayati said : The wise men know that a Brahmana is to be avoided than an angry and virulently poisonous snake, or a blazing and flaming fire.

sn: देवयान्युवाच कथमाशीविषात् सर्पाज्ज्वलनात् सर्वतोमुखात्। दुराधर्षतरो विप्र इत्यात्य पुरुषर्षभ॥
en: Devayani said : O best of men, why do you say that a Brahmana is to be avoided like an angry and virulently poisonous snake, or a blazing and flaming fire?

sn: ययातिरुवाच एकमाशीविषो हन्ति शस्त्रेणैकश्च वध्यते। हन्ति विप्रः सराष्ट्राणि पुराण्यपि हि कोपितः॥ दुराधर्षतरो विप्रस्तस्माद् भीरु मतो मम। अतोऽदत्तां च पित्रा त्वां भद्रे न विवहाम्यहम्॥
en: Yayati said : The snake kills only one. The sharpest weapon kills but a single person. But the Brahmana, if angry, destroys many cities and kingdoms. Therefore, O beautiful lady, I think that Brahmanas should be avoided more than the two, (the snake and the fire) O amiable lady, I cannot marry you, unless your father bestows you on me.

sn: देवयान्युवाच दत्तां वहस्व तन्मा त्वं पित्रा राजन् वृतो मया। अयाचतो भयं नास्ति दत्तां च प्रतिगृह्णतः॥
en: Devayani said : You are chosen by me. O king it is then settled that you will accept me if my father bestows you on me. You need not fear in accept my humble self, if bestowed on you. You have not asked for me.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच त्वरितं देवयान्याथ संदिष्टं पितुरात्मनः। सर्वं निवेदयामास धात्री तस्मै यथातथम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Devayani quickly sent a maid-servant to her father. The maid told Shukra all that had happened.

sn: श्रुत्वैव च सा राजानं दर्शयामास भार्गवः। दृष्ट्वैव चागतं शुक्रं ययातिः पृथिवीपतिः। ववन्दे ब्राह्मणं काव्यं प्राञ्जलिः प्रणतः स्थितः॥
en: Having heard this, the son of Bhrigu went to see the king. The king of the world Yayati, seeing that Shukra was coming, bowed to him. He worshipped and adored that Brahmana and stood before him with joined hands to receive his commands.

sn: देवयान्युवाच राजायं नाहुषस्तात दुर्गमे पाणिमग्रहीत्। नमस्ते देहि मामस्मै लोके नान्यं पतिं वृणे॥
en: Devayani said : O father, this is the son of Nahusha. He took hold of my hand when I was in difficulty (thrown into the well), Bestow me on him. I shall not marry any other man in the world.

sn: शुक्र उवाच वृतोऽनया पतिर्वीर सुतया त्वं ममेष्टया। गृहाणेमां मया दत्तां महिषीं नहुषात्मज॥
en: Shukra said: O splendidly courageous king, you have been accepted by my dear daughter as her husband. I bestow her on you. Therefore, O son of Nahusha, accept her as your wife.

sn: ययातिरुवाच अधर्मो न स्पृशेदेष महान् मामिह भार्गव। वर्णसंकरजो ब्रह्मन्निति त्वां प्रवृणोम्यहम्॥
en: Yayati said : O Brahmana, I solicit the boon by which the sin of my begetting a mixed caste may not touch me.

sn: शुक्र उवाच अधर्मात् त्वां विमुञ्चामि वृणु त्वं वरमीप्सितम्। अस्मिन् विवाहे मा म्लासीरहं पापं नुदामि ते॥
en: Shukra said: I shall absolve you from the sin (of begetting a mixed caste). Fear not to marry her. grant you absolution.

sn: वहस्व भार्यां धर्मेण देवयानीं सुमध्यमाम्। अनया सह सम्प्रीतिमतुलां समवाप्नुहि॥
en: Maintain virtuously your wife, Devayani of beautiful slender waist. Let great happiness be yours in her company.

sn: इयं चापि कुमारी ते शर्मिष्ठा वार्षपर्वणी। सम्पूज्या सततं राजन् मा चैनां शयने ह्वयेः॥
en: O king, this maiden, Sharmishtha, the daughter of Vrishaparva, should always be respected by you. But you must no call her to your bed.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्तो ययातिस्तु शुक्रं कृत्वा प्रदक्षिणम्। शास्त्रोक्तविधिना राजा विवाहमकरोच्छुभम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having been thus addressed by Shukra, the king walked round the Brahmana. The king then performed the auspicious ceremony of inarriage according to the rites of the ordinance.

sn: सम्पूजितश्च शुक्रेण दैत्यैश्च नृपसत्तमः। जगाम स्वपुरं हृष्टोऽनुज्ञातोऽथ महात्मना॥
en: Having received from Shukra a rich treasure in Devayani with Sharmishtha and two thousand maidens. That best of kings, being duly honoured by Shukra and the Asuras, returned to his capital, after receiving the commands of the illustrious of Bhrigu.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ययाति: स्वपुरं प्राप्य महेन्द्रपुरसंनिभम्। प्रविश्यान्तःपुरं तत्र देवयानी न्यवेशयत्॥ देवयान्याश्चानुमते सुतां तां वृषपर्वणः। अशोकवनिकाभ्याशे गृहं कृत्वा न्यवेशयत्॥ वृतां दासीसहस्रेण शर्मिष्ठां वार्षपर्वणीम्। वासोभिरन्नपानैश्च संविभज्य सुसत्कृताम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Yayati, then coming to his capital which was like that of Indra, entered the innerapartment and installed Devayani there. At the request of Devayani, he established the daughter of Vrishaparva in a house which he caused to be erected in the Ashoka groves of his gardens. The king honoured the daughter of Vrishaparva, Sharmishtha, surrounded by her one thousand maids, by making every arrangement for her food and garments.

sn: देवयान्या तु सहितः स नृपो नहुषात्मजः। विजहार बहूनब्दान् देववन्मुदितः सुखी॥
en: The king, the son of Nahusha, happily passed many years in the company of Devayani.

sn: ऋतुकाले तु सम्प्राप्ते देवयानी वराङ्गना। लेभे गर्भं प्रथमतः कुमारं च व्यजायत॥
en: The beautiful lady, Devayani conceived when her season came. She gave birth to her eldest child which was a boy.

sn: गते वर्षसहस्र तु शर्मिष्ठा वार्षपर्वणी। ददर्श यौवनं प्राप्ता ऋतुं सा चान्वचिन्तयत्॥
en: When one thousand years had passed away, Sharmishtha, the daughter of Vrishaparva, attained her puberty and her season came. She (therefore) began to ponder.

sn: ऋतुकालश्च सम्प्राप्तो न च मेऽस्ति पतिर्वृतः। किं प्राप्तं किं नु कर्तव्यं किं वा कृत्वा कृतं भवेत्॥
en: (She said to herself), "My season has come. But I have not yet chosen a husband. What would happen? What should I do? How am I to accomplish my wishes?

sn: देवयानी प्रजातासौ वृथाहं प्राप्तयौवना। यथा तया वृतो भर्ता तथैवाहं वृणोमि तम्॥
en: Devayani has given birth to a son. My youth is in vain. I shall choose him as my husband whom Devayani has chosen.

sn: राज्ञा पुत्रफलं देयमिति मे निश्चिता मतिः। अपीदानी स धर्मात्मा इयान्मे दर्शनं रहः॥
en: The king should give me a son. This is a firm resolve. Will not that virtuous-minded king grant me a private interview?

sn: अथ निष्क्रम्य राजासौ तस्मिन् काले यदृच्छया। अशोकवनिकाभ्याशे शर्मिष्ठां प्रेक्ष्य विष्ठितः॥
en: (One day) the king listlessly came to the Ashoka grove and seeing Sharmishtha he stood before her.

sn: तमेकं रहिते दृष्ट्वा शर्मिष्ठा चारुहासिनी। प्रत्युद्गम्याञ्जलिं कृत्वा राजानं वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
en: Sharmishtha, of sweet smiles, finding the king alone before her, thus addressed the king with joined hands.

sn: शर्मिष्ठोवाच सोमस्येन्द्रस्य विष्णोर्वा यमस्य वरुणस्य च। तव वा नाहुष गृहे कः स्त्रियं द्रष्टुमर्हति॥ रूपाभिजनशीलैहि त्वं राजन् वेत्थ मां सदा। सा त्वां याचे प्रसाद्याहमृतुं देहि नराधिप॥
en: Sharmishtha said: O son of Nahusha, none can see the ladies that dwell in the inner-apartments of Soma, Indra, Vishnu, Yama, Varuna and your own. O king, you know that I am handsome and wellborn. O great king, I solicit you. My season has come. See that it goes not in vain.

sn: ययातिरुवाच वेद्मि त्वां शीलसम्पन्नां दैत्यकन्यामनिन्दिताम्। रूपं च ते न पश्यामि सूच्यग्रमपि निन्दितम्॥
en: Yayati said : I know very well the great birth of yours, born as you are in the race of the Danavas. You are also exceedingly beautiful. I do not find the least defeat in your beauty.

sn: अब्रवीदुशना काव्यो देवयानीं यदावहम्। नेयमाह्वयितव्या ते शयने वार्षपर्वणी॥
en: Ushanas, the son of Kavi, however, commanded me when I was married to Devayani that Vrishaparva's daughter shall not be my bed.

sn: शर्मिष्ठोवाच न नर्मयुक्तं वचनं हिनस्ति न स्त्रीषु राजन् न विवाहकाले। प्राणात्यये सर्वधनापहारे पञ्चानृतान्याहुरपातकानि॥
en: Sharmishtha said: It is not sinful to speak falsehood in the following five cases, namely in joke, in respect of women to be associated with, in marriage, in prospect of immediate death and at the time of the loss of one's whole fortune.

sn: पृष्टं तु साक्ष्ये प्रवदन्तमन्यथा वदन्ति मिथ्या पतितं नरेन्द्र। एकार्थतायां तु समाहितायां मिथ्या वदन्तं त्वनृतं हिनस्ति॥
en: O king, it is not true that he is fallen who does not speak out the truth when asked (for there are occasions when to speak falsehood is an act of piety.) The falsehood is sinful when one (harmful) object is to be accomplished.

sn: ययातिरुवाच राजा प्रमाणं भूतानां स नश्येत मृषा वदन्। अर्थकृच्छ्रमपि प्राप्य न मिथ्या कर्तुमुत्सहे॥
en: Yayati said : A king should be a model prince in the eyes of his people. That king who speaks falsehood is sure to meet with his destruction. I do not dare to speak a lie, though the greatest losses threaten me.

sn: शर्मिष्ठोवाच समावेतौ मतौ राजन् पति: सख्याश्च यः पतिः। समं विवाहमित्याहुः सख्या मेऽसि वृतः पतिः॥
en: Sharmishtha said: O king, you have been chosen by my friends as her husband. One's friend's marriage is the same as one's own. You are, therefore, as much my husband (as Devayani's).

sn: ययातिरुवाच दातव्यं याचमानेभ्य इति मे व्रतमाहितम्। त्वं च याचसि मां कामं ब्रूहि किं करवाणि ते॥
en: Yayati said : It is one of my strict vows no doubt that I should grant what is asked of me. You ask me (to grant you a favour). Therefore, tell me what should I do?

sn: शर्मिष्ठोवाच अधर्मात् पाहि मां राजन् धर्मं च प्रतिपादय। त्वत्तोऽपत्यवती लोके चरेयं धर्ममुत्तमम्॥
en: Sharmishtha said : O king, save me from sin. Protect my virtue. Becoming a mother by you, let me perform the greatest pious act in the world.

sn: त्रय एवाधना राजन् भार्या दासस्तथा सुतः। यत् ते समधिगच्छन्ति यस्यैते तस्य तद् धनम्॥
en: O king, it is ordained that three persons can never earn wealth for themselves. They are the wife, the slave and the son. That which they earn belong to him who owns them.

sn: देवयान्या भुजिष्यास्मि वश्या च तव भार्गवी। सा चाहं च त्वया राजन् भजनीये भजस्व माम्॥
en: O king, I am the slave of Devayani, the lady of the Bhrigu race. You are Devayani's master and lord. Therefore, you are my master and lord as well. I solicit you. Fulfill my wishes.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्तस्तु राजा स तथ्यमित्यभिजज्ञिवान्। पूजयामास शर्मिष्ठां धर्मं च प्रत्यपादयत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Thus having been addressed by Sharmishtha, the king was persuaded to believe that what she said was true. He fulfilled Sharmishtha's wishes and thus protected her virtue.

sn: स समागम्य शर्मिष्ठां यथाकाममवाप्य च। अन्योन्यं चाभिसम्पूज्य जग्मतुस्तौ यथागतम्॥
en: They passed some time together. They took affectionate farewell of each other and separated. Each went whence they came.

sn: तस्मिन् समागमे सुभूः शर्मिष्ठाः चारुहासिनी। लेभे गर्भं प्रथमतस्तस्मानृपतिसत्तमात्॥
en: Sharmishtha of sweet smiles and fair eyebrows conceived in consequence of that connection with that best of kings.

sn: प्रजज्ञे च ततः काले राजन् राजीवलोचना। कुमारं देवगर्भाभं राजीवनिभलोचनम्॥
en: O king, in due time the lotus-eyed lady (Sharmishtha) gave birth to a son, as effulgent as a celestial child and with eyes like lotus leaves.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच श्रुत्वा कुमारं जातं तु देवयानी शुचिस्मिता। चिन्तयामास दुःखार्ता शर्मिष्ठां प्रति भारत॥ अभिगम्य च शर्मिष्ठा देवयान्यब्रवीदिदम्।
en: Vaishampayana said : O descendant of the Bharata race, when Devayani heard of the birth of this boy, she ! became very sorry and Sharmishtha became an object of her sad reflections. Going to Sharmishtha, Devayani thus spoke to her.

sn: देवयान्युवाच किमिदं वृजिनं सुभ्र कृतं वै कामलुब्धया।॥
en: Devayani said: O girl of fair-eye-brows, what sin is this you have committed out of lust!

sn: शर्मिष्ठोवाच ऋषिरभ्यागतः कश्चिद् धर्मात्मा वेदपारगः। स मया वरदः कामं याचितो धर्मसंहितम्॥
en: Sharmishtha said: A Rishi of virtuous mind, learned in the Vedas, came to me. He was capable of granting boons and he was solicited by me to grant my wishes based on virtue.

sn: नाहमन्यायत: काममाचरामि शुचिस्मिते। तस्मादृषेर्ममापत्यमिति सत्यं ब्रवीमि ते॥
en: O lady of sweet smiles, I would never seek the fulfillment of my desires by sinful means. I tell you truly, this child was begotten by a Rishi.

sn: देवयान्युवाच शोभनं भीरु यद्येवमथ स ज्ञायते द्विजः। गोत्रनामाभिजनतो वेत्तुमिच्छामि तं द्विजम्॥
en: Devayani said: O timid maiden, it is all right if that is the case. If you know the lineage, the name and the family of that Brahmana, tell me I wish to hear them. my

sn: शर्मिष्ठोवाच तपसा तेजसा चैव दीप्यमानं यथा रविम्। तं दृष्ट्वा मम सम्प्रष्टुं शक्तिर्नासीच्छुचिस्पिते॥
en: Sharmishtha said : O lady of sweet smiles, that Rishi was as effulgent in asceticism and energy as the sun. Seeing him, I had no power of making these enquiries.

sn: देवयान्युवाच यद्येतदेवं शर्मिष्ठे न मन्युर्विद्यते मम। अपत्यं यदि ते लब्धं ज्येष्ठाच्छ्रेष्ठाच वै द्विजात्॥
en: Devayani said : O Sharmishtha, If this be true, if you have received this your son from such a great Brahmana, I have then no cause for anger.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच अन्योन्यमेवमुक्त्वा तु सम्प्रहस्य च ते मिथः। जगाम भार्गवी वेश्म तथ्यमित्यवजग्मुषी॥
en: Vaishampayana said: They talked and laughed with each other and then they separated, (Devayani) the daughter of the Bhrigu race going to her mansion and believing what Sharmishtha told her.

sn: ययातिर्देवयान्यां तु पुत्रावजनयनृपः। यदुं च तुर्वसुं चैव शक्रविष्णू इवापरौ॥
en: O king, Yayati begot on Devayani two more sons (namely) Yadu and Turvasu, who were like Indra and Vishnu.

sn: तस्मादेव तु राजर्षेः शर्मिष्ठा वार्षपर्वणी। दुह्यं चानुं च पूरुं च त्रीन् कुमारानजीजनत्॥
en: The daughter of Vrishaparva, Sharmishtha, by that royal sage gave birth to three sons in all, namely Druhyu, Anu and Puru.

sn: ततः काले तु कस्मिंश्चिद् देवयानी शुचिस्मिता। ययातिसहिता राजञ्जगाम रहितं वनम्॥
en: O king, one day Devayani of sweet smiles went with Yayati into a solitary part of the royal park.

sn: ददर्श च तदा तत्र कुमारान् देवरूपिणः। कुमारान् पर्यपृच्छता क्रीडमानान् सुविश्रब्धान् विस्मिता चेदमब्रवीत्॥
en: There she saw three children of celestial beauty, playing with perfect ease. She was surprised and thus spoke to the king.

sn: देवयान्युवाच कस्यैते दारका राजन् देवपुत्रोपमाः शुभाः। वर्चसा रूपतश्चैव सदृशा मे मतास्तव॥
en: Devayani said : O king, whose children are these, so handsome, so like the children of the celestial? They are exactly like you in splendour and beauty.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवं पृष्ट्वा तु राजानं
en: Vaishampayana said : Having asked the king, she asked the children.

sn: देवयान्युवाच किं नामधेयं वंशो व: पुत्रकाः कश्च वः पिता। प्रब्रूत मे यथातथ्यं श्रोतुमिच्छामि तं ह्यहम्॥
en: Devayani said : O children, what if your lineage! Who is your father? Answer me truly. I desire to know all.

sn: तेऽदर्शयन् प्रदेशिन्या तमेव नृपसत्तमम्। शर्मिष्ठा मातरं चैव तथाऽऽचख्युश्च दारकाः॥
en: The children then pointed to the king with their fingers and said that Sharmishtha was their mother.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच इत्युक्त्वा सहितास्ते तु राजानमुपचक्रमुः। नाभ्यनन्दत तान् राजा देवयान्यास्तदान्तिके॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having said this, they came to the king to clasp his knees. But the king dared not caress them before Devayani.

sn: रुदन्तस्तेऽथ शर्मिष्ठामभ्ययुर्बालकास्ततः। श्रुत्वा तु तेषां बालानां सव्रीड इव पार्थिवः॥
en: The boys wept in grief and they left the place, going towards their mother. The king became very much abashed of this conduct of the boys.

sn: दृष्ट्वा तु तेषां बालानां प्रणयं पार्थिवं प्रति। बुद्ध्वा च तत्त्वं सा देवी शर्मिष्ठामिदमब्रवीत्॥
en: Seeing the affection of the boys towards the king, (Devayani) understood all. All the addressed Sharmishtha thus :

sn: देवयान्युवाच मदधीना सती कस्मादकार्षीविप्रियं मम। तमेवासुरधर्मं त्वमास्थिता न बिभेषि मे॥
en: Devayani said : How have you dared to do me an injury, dependant as you are on me? Do you not fear to have recourse once more to your Asura conduct?

sn: शर्मिष्ठोवाच यदुक्तमृषिरित्येव तत् सत्यं चारुहासिनि। न्यायतो धर्मतश्चैव चरन्ती न बिभेमि ते॥
en: Sharmishtha said: O lady of sweet smiles! all that I told you about the Rishi is quite true. My acts were according to the precepts of virtue and right.

sn: यदा त्वया वृतो भर्ता वृत एव तदा मया। सखीभर्ता हि धर्मेण भर्ता भवति शोभने॥ पूज्यासि मम मान्या च ज्येष्ठा च ब्राह्मणी ह्यसि। त्वत्तोऽपि मे पूज्यतमो राजर्षिः किं न वेत्थ तत्॥
en: Therefore, I am not afraid of you. When you chose the king as your husband, I too did the same. O beautiful lady, a friend's husband is one's own husband according to the precept of religion. You are a daughter of a Brahmana and therefore you deserve my greatest worship and regard. Do you no know that this royal sage (Yayati) is the object of greater esteem to me?

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच श्रुत्वा तस्यास्ततो वाक्यं देवयान्यब्रवीदिदम्। राजन् नाघेह वत्स्यामि विप्रियं मे कृतं त्वया।॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having heard these words, Devayani said, "O king, you have wronged me, I will not live here any longer."

sn: सहसोत्पतितां श्यामां दृष्ट्वा तां साश्रुलोचनाम्। तूर्णं सकाशं काव्यस्य प्रस्थितां व्यथितस्तदा॥
en: Having said this, she with tearful eyes quickly rose to go away to her father. And the king was grieved to see her thus angry.

sn: अनुवव्राज सम्भ्रान्तः पृष्ठतः सान्त्वयन् नृपः। न्यवर्तत न चैव स्म क्रोधसंरक्तलोचना॥
en: He became very much alarmed; and he followed her, trying to appease her wrath. But she did not return. Her eyes were red in anger.

sn: आविब्रुवन्ती किंचित् सा राजानं साश्रुलोचना। अचिरादेव सम्प्राप्ता काव्यस्योशनसोऽन्तिकम्॥
en: She did not speak a word to the king, but she, with her eyes full of tears, soon reached her father, Ushanas, the son of Kavi.

sn: सा तु दृष्ट्वैव पितरमभिवाद्याग्रतः स्थिता। अनन्तरं ययातिस्तु पूजयामास भार्गवम्॥
en: Seeing her father, she made to him due salutation and stood before him. Yayati also came immediately after her and he saluted and worshipped the son of Bhrigu.

sn: देवयान्युवाच अधर्मेण जितो धर्मः प्रवृत्तमधरोत्तरम्। शर्मिष्ठयातिवृत्तास्मि दुहित्रा वृषपर्वणः॥
en: Devayani said: O father, virtue has been defeated by vice. The low have risen and the high have fallen. I have been insulted by the daughter of Vrishaparva.

sn: त्रयोस्यां जनिताः पुत्रा राज्ञानेन ययातिना। दुर्भगाया मम द्वौ तु पुत्रौ तात ब्रवीमि ते॥
en: Three sons have been begotten on her by this king Yayati. O father, unfortunate am I! I have got only two sons.

sn: धर्मज्ञ इति विख्यात एष राजा भृगूद्वह। अतिक्रान्तश्च मर्यादां काव्यैतत् कथयामि ते॥
en: O son of Bhrigu, this king is renowned for his knowledge in religion and virtue. But, O son of Kavi, I tell you, he has fallen from the path of virtue.

sn: शुक्र उवाच धर्मज्ञः सन् महाराज योऽधर्ममकृथाः प्रियम्। तस्माजरा त्वामचिराद् धर्षयिष्यति दुर्जया।। ३१!
en: Shukra said: ( king, as you have made vice your favourite pursuit, though well-acquainted with the precepts of virtue, terrible decrepitude will overtake you.

sn: ययातिरुवाच ऋतुं वै याचमानाया भगवन् नान्यचेतसा। दुहितुर्दानवेन्द्रस्य धर्म्यमेतत् कृतं मया॥ ऋतुं वै याचमानाया न ददाति पुमानृतुम्। भ्रूणहेत्युच्यते ब्रह्मन् स इह ब्रह्मवादिभिः॥ अभिकामां स्त्रियं यश्च गम्यां रहसि याचितः। नोपैति स च धर्मेषु भ्रूणहेत्युच्यते बुधैः॥
en: Yayati said: Adorable Rishi, I was solicited by the daughter of the Danava king to make her season fruitful. I did grant her prayer from a sense of virtue. O Rishi, men learned in the Vedas say that he, who does not grant the prayer of a woman in season, commits the sin of killing an embryo. He, who, being solicited in secret by a woman full of desire and in season, does not grant her wishes, loses virtue. The learned say that he becomes a killer of embryo.

sn: इत्येतानि समीक्ष्याहं कारणानि भृगूद्वह। अधर्मभयसंविग्नः शर्मिष्ठामुपजग्मिवान्॥
en: O son of Bhrigu, for these reason and being afraid of committing a sin, I went to Sharmishtha.

sn: शुक्र उवाच नन्वहं प्रत्यवेक्ष्यस्ते मदधीनोऽसि पार्थिवा मिथ्याचारस्य धर्मेषु चौर्यं भवति नाहुष॥
en: Shukra said: O king, you are dependent on me. You should have waited to receive my command. O son of Nahusha, having acted falsely in the matter of your duty, you have committed the sin of theft.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच क्रुद्धेनोशनसा शप्तो ययाति हुषस्तदा। पूर्व वयः परित्यज्य जरां सद्योऽन्वपद्यत॥
en: Vaishampayana said :; Thus being cursed by the angry Ushanas, Yayati, the son of Nahusha, was then deprived of his youth and terrible decrepitude soon overcame him.

sn: ययातिरुवाच अतृप्तो यौवनस्याहं देवयान्यां भृगूद्वह। प्रसादं कुरु मे ब्रह्मञ्जरेयं न विशेच माम्॥
en: Yayati said : O son of Bhrigu, I have not been as yet satiated with youth of Devayani. Therefore, O Brahmana, be graceful to Let not decrepitude overcome me. me.

sn: शुक्र उवाच नाहं मृषा द्रवीभ्येतज्जरां प्राप्तोऽसि भूमिप। जरां त्वेतां त्वमन्यस्मिन् संक्रामय यदीच्छसि॥
en: Shukra said : I never speak an untruth, O king, (see), you have been immediately attacked by old age. But if you like, you can transfer this decrepitude to some other man.

sn: ययातिरुवाच राज्यभाक् स भवेद् ब्रह्मन् पुण्यभाक् कीर्तिभाक् तथा। यो मे दद्याद् वयः पुत्रस्तद् भवाननुमन्यताम्॥
en: Yayati said : O Brahmana, let this be ordered by you that, the son of mine who will accept my this old age will enjoy my kingdom and gain both virtue and fame.

sn: शुक्र उवाच संक्रामयिष्यसि जरां यथेष्टं नहुषात्मज। मामनुध्याय भावेन न च पापमवाप्स्यसि॥ वयो दास्यति ते पुत्रो यः स राजा भविष्यति। आयुष्मान् कीर्तिमांश्चैव बह्वपत्यस्तथैव च॥
en: Shukra said: O son of Nahusha, remembering me you will be able to transfer your this decrepitude to whomever you like. Your that son who will give you his youth will become your successor on the throne. He will have long life, widespread fame and a large progeny.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच जरां प्राप्य ययातिस्तु स्वपुरं प्राप्य चैव हि। पुत्रं ज्येष्ठं वरिष्ठं च यदुमित्यब्रवीद् वचः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having been thus attacked by old age, Yayati returned to his capital. He summoned his eldest and accomplished son Yadu and thus spoke to him.

sn: ययातिरुवाच जरा वली च मां तात पलितानि च पर्यगुः। काव्यस्योशनसः शापान च तृप्तोऽस्मि यौवने॥
en: Yayati said : O child; Old age, wrinkles and white hair have come over to me by the curse the son of Kavi who is called Ushanas. But I am not yet satiated with youth.

sn: त्वं यदो प्रतिपद्यस्व पाप्मानं जरया सह। यौवनेन त्वदीयेन चरेयं विषयानहम्॥ पूर्णे वर्षसहस्रे तु पुनस्ते यौवनं त्वहम्। दत्त्वा स्वं प्रतिपत्स्यामि पाप्मानं जरया सह।॥
en: O Yadu, take you upon yourself my this decrepitude and consequent old age. I shall then enjoy with your youth. When one thousand years will be completed, I shall return to you your youth and take back my decrepitude and its consequent weakness,

sn: यदुरुवाच जरायां बहवो दोषाः पानभोजनकारिताः। तस्माजरां न ते राजन् ग्रहीष्य इति मे मतिः॥
en: Over are Yadu said: There are many inconveniences in old age about eating and drinking. Therefore, O king, I shall not take your decrepitude upon me. This is my determination.

sn: सितश्मश्रुनिरानन्दो जरया शिथिलीकृतः। बलीसंगतगात्रस्तु दुर्दर्शो दुर्बलः कृशः॥ अशक्तः कार्यकरणे परिभूत: स यौवतैः। सहोपजीविभिश्चैव तां जरां नाभिकामये॥
en: White hair, cheerlessness, relaxation of nerves, wrinkles, all the body, deformities, weakness, leanness, inability of work, these the consequences of decrepitude. Even friends and dependants forsake an old decrepit man.

sn: सन्ति ते बहवः पुत्रा मत्तः प्रियतरा नृप। जरां ग्रहीतुं धर्मज्ञ तस्मादन्यं वृणीष्व वै॥
en: O king, you have many sons, some of them are dearer to you (than I). O virtuous man, ask some other son of yours to take upon him your decrepitude.

sn: ययातिरुवाच यत् त्वं मे हृदयाजातो वयः स्वं न प्रयच्छसि। तस्मादराज्यभाक् तात प्रजा तव भविष्यति॥
en: Yayati said : O son, you have sprung from my heart, but you do not give me your youth. Therefore, your children will never be ruling kings.

sn: तुर्वसो प्रतिपद्यस्व पाप्मानं जरया सह। यौवनेन चरेयं वै विषयांस्तव पुत्रक॥
en: O Turvasu, take upon yourself my decrepitude and consequent weakness. I wish to enjoy the pleasures of life with your youth.

sn: पूर्णे वर्षसहस्रे तु पुनर्दास्यामि यौवनम्। स्वं चैव प्रतिपत्स्यामि पाप्मानं जरया सह॥
en: After the expiration of one thousand years, I shall return, to you, your youth and take back my decrepitude and its consequent weakness.

sn: तुर्वसुरुवाच न कामये जरां तात कामभोगप्रणाशिनीम्। बलरूपान्तकरणां बुद्धिप्राणप्रणाशिनीम्॥
en: Turvasu said : O father, I do not like old age. It destroys all pleasures and enjoyments, strength and beauty, the intellect and the memory, nay even life.

sn: ययातिरुवाच यत् त्वं मे हृदयाजातो वयः स्वं न प्रयच्छसि। तस्मात् प्रजा समुच्छेदं तुर्वसो तव यास्यसि॥
en: Yayati said : You are born from my heart, but you do not give me your youth. Therefore, O Turvasu, your line will be extinct.

sn: संकीर्णचारधर्मेषु प्रतिलोमचरेषु च। पिशिताशिषु चान्त्येषु मूढ राजा भविष्यसि॥ गुरुदारप्रसक्तेषु तिर्यग्योनिगतेषु च। पशुधर्मेषु पापेषु म्लेच्छेषु त्वं भविष्यसि॥
en: You shall be the foolish king of those whose practise and precepts will be impure, whose women of superior birth will give birth to children by men of inferior birth, who will live on meat, who will be mean, who will not hesitate to appropriate the wives of their superiors, who will be like birds and beasts in their practise and who will be sinful and Mlecchas.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवं स तुर्वसुं शप्त्वा ययातिः सुतमात्मनः। शर्मिष्ठायाः सुतं दुह्युमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said: Having thus cursed his son Turvasu, Yayati spoke to Sharmishtha's son Druhyu thus:

sn: ययातिरुवाच दुह्यो त्वं प्रतिपद्यस्व वर्णरूपविनाशिनीम्। जरां वर्षसहस्रं मे यौवनं स्वं ददस्व च॥
en: Yayati said : O Druhyu, take upon yourself for one thousand years my decrepitude, destructive of beauty and complexion. Give me your youth.

sn: पूर्णे वर्षसहस्रे तु पुनर्दास्यामि यौवनम्। स्वं चादास्यामि भूयोऽहं पाप्मानं जरया सह॥
en: After the expiration of one thousand years, I shall return to you your youth and take back my own decrepitude.

sn: दुखुरुवाच न गजं न रथं नाश्वं जीर्णो भुङ्क्तेन च स्त्रियम्। वाक्सङ्गश्चास्य भवति तां जरां नाभिकामये॥
en: Druhyu said: O king, one, if he is decrepit, cannot enjoy elephants, cars, horses or women. His voice also becomes indistinct. Therefore, I do no desire (to take upon myself) your old age.

sn: ययातिरुवाच यत् त्वं मे हृदयाजातो वयः स्वं न प्रयच्छसि। तस्माद् द्रुह्यो प्रियः कामो न ते सम्पत्स्यते क्वचित्।२०
en: Yayati said : O son, you are sprung from my heart, but you refuse to give me your youth. Therefore, your cherished wishes will never be fulfilled.

sn: यत्राश्वरथमुख्यानामश्वानां स्याद् गतं न च। हस्तिनां पीठकानां च गर्दभानां तथैव च॥ बस्तानां च गवां चैव शिबिकायास्तथैव च। उडुपप्लवसंतारो यत्र नित्यं भविष्यति। अराजा भोजशब्दं त्वं तत्र प्राप्स्यसि सान्वयः॥
en: You shall be a king only in name. You shall rule over a region where there will be no roads, no passages for horses, cars, elephants, asses, goats, bullocks, palanquins and other good vehicles, where the only means of locomotion will be rafts and floats. In such a place you will live with all your friends.

sn: ययातिरुवाच अनो त्वं प्रतिपद्यस्व पाप्मानं जरया सह। एकं वर्षसहस्रं तु चरेयं यौवनेन ते॥
en: Yayati said: O Anu, take my decrepitude and its consequent weakness. I shall enjoy the pleasures of life for one thousand years with your youth.

sn: अनुरुवाच जीर्ण: शिशुवदादत्तेऽकालेऽत्रमशुचिर्यथा। न जुहोति च कालेऽग्निं तां जरां नाभिकामये।॥
en: Anu said: Those that are decrepit eat like children and they are always impure. They cannot pour libations on sacrificial fire at the proper time. Therefore, I do not like to take upon myself your old age.

sn: ययातिरुवाच यत् त्वं मे हृदयाजातो वयः स्वं न प्रयच्छसि। जरादोषस्त्वया प्रोक्तस्तस्मात् त्वं प्रतिपत्स्यसे॥ प्रजाश्च यौवनप्राप्ता विनाशिष्यन्त्यनो तव। अग्निप्रस्कन्दनपरस्त्वं चाप्येर्वं भविष्यसि॥
en: Yayati said : O son, you have sprung from my heart, but you do not give me your youth. As you find so many faults with decrepitude, decrepitude will overcome you. Your sons will die as soon as they will attain to their youth. You shall not be able to perform any sacrifice before fire.

sn: ययातिरुवाच पूरो त्वं मे प्रियः पुत्रस्त्वं वरीयान् भरिष्यसि। जरा वली च मां तात पलितानि च पर्यगुः॥
en: Yayati said : O Puru, you are my youngest and dearest son, you will become the foremost of them. Old age, wrinkles and white hair, O child, have come over me.

sn: काव्यस्योशनसः शापान्न च तृप्तोऽस्मि यौवने। पूरो त्वं प्रतिपद्यस्व पाप्मानं जरया सह। कंचित् कालं चरेयं वै विषयान् वयसा तव॥ पूर्णे वर्षसहस्रे तु पुनर्दास्यामि यौवनम्। स्वं चैव प्रतिपत्स्यामि पाप्मानं जरया सह॥
en: On account of the curse of the son of Kavi, who is called Ushanas. But I am not yet satiated with youth. O Puru, take my decrepitude upon you and consequent weakness. I shall enjoy the pleasures of life for one thousand years with your youth. After the expiration of one thousand years, I shall return to you your youth and take my own decrepitude.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्तः प्रत्युवाच पूरुः पितरपञ्जसा। यथाऽऽत्य मां महाराज तत् करिष्यामि ते वचः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having been thus addressed the king, Puru replied to him with all humility. (He said:) “O great king, I shall do as you command me to do.

sn: प्रतिपत्स्यामि ते राजन् पाप्मानं जरया सह। गृहाण यौवनं मत्तश्चर कामान् यथेप्सितान्॥
en: O king, I shall take upon myself your old age and its consequent weakness. Take my youth and enjoy as you like the pleasures of life.

sn: जरयाहं प्रतिच्छन्नो वयोरूपधरस्तव। यौवनं भवते दत्त्वा चरिष्यामि यथाऽऽत्थ माम्॥
en: "Attacked by your old age, deprived of youth and beauty, I shall at your command live and give you my youth.”

sn: ययातिरुवाच पूरो प्रीतोऽस्मि ते वत्स प्रतिश्चेदं ददामि ते। सर्वकामसमृद्धा ते प्रजा राज्ये भविष्यति॥
en: Yayati said : O Puru, my child, I am much pleased with you. I grant you the following boon with great pleasure. "The people of your kingdom will have all their desires fulfilled."

sn: एवमुक्त्वा ययातिस्तु स्मृत्वा काव्यं महातपाः। संक्रामयामास जरां तदा पूरौ महात्मनि॥
en: Having said this, Yayati remembered the great ascetic, the son of Kavi (Shukra) and transferred his decrepitude to the body of the high-souled Puru.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच पौरवेणाथ वयसा ययातिनहुषात्मजः। प्रीतियुक्तो नृपश्रेष्ठश्चचार विषयान् प्रियान्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having thus received the youth of Puru, Yayati the son of Nahusha, that best of kings, was exceedingly delighted. He again indulged in the pleasures of life.

sn: यथाकामं यथोत्साहं यथाकालं यथासुखम्। धर्माविरुद्धं राजेन्द्र यथार्हति स एव हि॥
en: He enjoyed himself to the full extent of his desires and to the full limit of his powers, as much as he desired and as the seasons called forth. But, O king, he did nothing against the precepts of religion.

sn: देवानतर्पयद् यज्ञैः श्राद्धस्तद्वत् पितृनपि। दीनाननुग्रहैरिष्टैः कामैश्च द्विजसत्तमान्॥
en: He pleased the celestials, by performing sacrifices, the Pitris by Shraddhas, the poor by charities and the good Brahmana by fulfilling their desires.

sn: अतिथीनन्नपानैश्च विशश्च परिपालनैः। आनृशंस्येन शूद्रांश्च दस्यून संनिग्रहेण च॥ धर्मेण च प्रजाः सर्वा यथावदनुरञ्जयन्। ययातिः पालयामास साक्षादिन्द्र इवापरः॥
en: The guests by food and drink, the Vaishyas by protection, the Shudras by kindness and the robbers by proper punishments, Yayati pleased all classes of his subjects by ruling over them virtuously like Indra.

sn: स राजा सिंहविक्रान्तो युवा विषयगोचरः। अविरोधेन धर्मस्य चचार सुखमुत्तमम्॥
en: That king was as powerful as the lion. He was young and enjoyed all the pleasures of life. He enjoyed unlimited happiness without violating the precepts of religion.

sn: स सम्प्राप्य शुभान् कामांस्तृप्तः खित्रश्च पार्थिवः। कालं वर्षसहस्रान्तं सस्मार मनुजाधिपः॥ परिसंख्याय कालज्ञः कला: काष्ठाश्च वीर्यवान्। यौवनं प्राप्य राजर्षिः सहस्रपरिवत्सरान्॥ विश्वाच्या सहितो रेमे व्यभ्राजन्नन्दने वने। अलकायां स कालं तु मेरुशृङ्गे तथोत्तरे॥ यदा स पश्यते कालं धर्मात्मा तं महीपतिः। पूर्णं मत्वा ततः कालं पूरूं पुत्रमुवाच ह॥
en: The king (Yayati) became exceedingly happy in thus being able to enjoy all the best objects of enjoyments. That king of men was only sorry (in remembering) that one thousand years would soon come to an end. That royal sage, learned in the mystery of time and possessed of great prowess, having obtained youth for one thousand years and watching proper Kalas and Kashthas. Sported with Vishvachi (Apsara), some time in the garden (of Indra) Nandana, sometimes in Aloka and sometimes on the summit of the Meru Mountain. That virtuous king then found that the fixed time (one thousand) years had come to an end. He then called Puru and addressed him thus.

sn: यथाकामं यथोत्साहं यथाकालमरिंदम। सेविता विषयाः पुत्र यौवनेन मया तव॥
en: O son, O chastiser of foes, I have enjoyed with your youth to the full extent of my desires and to the full limit of my powers and all according to their seasons.

sn: न जातु कामः कामानामुपभोगेन शाम्यति। हविषा कृष्णवर्देव भूय एवाभिवर्धते॥
en: But desires never die. They are never satiated by indulgence. By indulgence they flame up like the sacrificial fire with ghee poured into it.

sn: यत् पृथिव्यां व्रीहियवं हिरण्यं पशवः स्त्रियः। एकस्यापि न पर्याप्तं तस्मात् तृष्णां परित्यजेत्॥
en: If one becomes the sole lord of all the earth with its paddy, oats, gems, beasts and women, still it will not be considered by him enough. Therefore, the thirst for enjoyment, should be abandoned.

sn: या दुस्त्यजा दुर्मतिभिर्या न जीर्यति जीर्यतः। योऽसौ प्राणान्तिको रोगस्तां तृष्णां त्यजतः सुखम्।१४
en: The thirst (of enjoyments), which is difficult to be cast off by the wicked, which does not fail even with falling life, is truly a fatal disease in man. To get rid of this thirst is real happiness.

sn: पूर्ण वर्षसहस्रं मे विषयासक्तचेतसः। तथाप्यनुदिनं तृष्णा ममैतेष्वभिजायते॥
en: My mind was attached to the pleasures of life for full one thousand years. My thirst for them, however, without being abated, is daily being increased.

sn: तस्मादेनामहं त्यक्त्वा ब्रह्मण्याधाय मानसम्। निर्द्वन्द्वो निर्ममो भूत्वा चरिष्यामि मृगैः सह॥
en: Therefore, I shall get rid of it. I shall fix my mind on Brahma and becoming peaceful and having no attachment, I shall pass the rest of my days in the forest with the innocent deer.

sn: पूरो प्रीतिऽस्मि भद्रं ते गृहाणेदं स्वयौवनम्। राज्यं चेदं गृहाण त्वं त्वं हि मे प्रियकृत् सुतः॥
en: O Puru, I am exceedingly pleased with you. Take (back) your own youth. Prosperity be to you. Receive my kingdom. You are my son who has done my favourite work.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच प्रतिपेदे जरां राजा ययाति हुषस्तदा। यौवनं प्रतिपेदे च पूरुः स्वं पुनरात्मनः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Yayati, the son of Nahusha, then received back his own old age and his son Puru also received back his youth.

sn: अभिषेक्तुकामं नृपति पूरुं पुत्रं कनीयसम्। ब्राह्मणप्रमुखा वर्णा इदं वचनमब्रुवन्॥
en: Yayati became desirous of installing his youngest son Puru on the throne. But the four orders of his subject with Brahmanas at their

sn: कथं शुक्रस्य नप्तारं देवयान्याः सुतं प्रभो। ज्येष्ठं यदुर तिक्रम्य राज्यं पूरोः प्रयच्छसि॥
en: “O lord, how can you install Puru on the throne, passing over your eldest son Yadu, born of Devayani and grandson of Shukra?

sn: यदुर्येष्ठस्तव सुतो जातस्तमनु तुर्वसुः। शर्मिष्ठायाः सुतो दुह्युस्ततोऽनुः पूरुरेव च।॥
en: Yadu is your eldest son, after him was Turvasu. Then Sharmishtha's son Druhyu, Anu and last Puru.

sn: कथं ज्येष्ठानतिक्रम्य कनीयान् राज्यमर्हति। एतत् सम्बोधयामस्त्वां धर्मं त्वं प्रतिपालय॥
en: How it would be proper to pass over all the elders and install 1 the youngest? We represent this to you, act according to the precepts of religion.

sn: ययातिरुवाच ब्राह्मणप्रमुखा वर्णाः सर्वे शृण्वन्तु मे वचः। ज्येष्ठं प्रति यथा राज्यं न देयं मे कथंचन॥
en: Yayati said : Hear all of you of the four orders of the caste with the Brahmanas at their head, why my kingdom should not be given to my eldest son.

sn: मम ज्येष्ठेन यदुना नियोगो नानुपालितः। प्रतिकूलः पितुर्यश्च न स पुत्रः सतां मतः॥
en: My commands were disobeyed by my eldest son. The opinion of the wise men is that the son disobeys his father is no son at all.

sn: मातापित्रोर्वचनकृद्धितः पथ्यश्च यः सुतः। स पुत्रः पुत्रवद् यश्च वर्तते पितृमातृषु॥
en: The son who obeys the commands of his father and mother, who is humble and a wellwisher of his parents and who loves them, is the best of sons.

sn: यदुनाहमवज्ञातस्तथा तुर्वसुनापि च। द्रुाना चानुना चैव मय्यवज्ञा कृता भृशम्॥
en: I have been slighted by Yadu and Turvasu; much have I been slighted by Druhyu and Anu.

sn: पूरुणा तु कृतं वाक्यं मानितं च विशेषतः। कनीयान् मम दायादो धृता येन जरा मम॥
en: Only Puru obeyed my commands and much have I been honoured and respected by him. He accepted my old age and therefore, though he is the youngest, yet he should be made king.

sn: मम कामः स च कृतः पूरुणा मित्ररूपिणा। शुक्रेण च वरो दत्तः काव्येनोशनसा स्वयम्॥ पुत्रो यस्त्वानुवर्तेत स राजा पृथिवीपतिः। भवतोऽनुनयाम्येवं पूरू राज्येऽभिषिच्यताम्॥
en: Puru is a great friend of mine and he did what was agreeable to me. And the son of Kavi, Ushanas, Shukra himself, granted me this boon. The son who would obey me would become the king and the lord of the earth. Therefore, I entreat you, let Puru be installed on the throne.

sn: प्रकृतय ऊचुः यः पुत्रो गुमसम्पन्नो मातापित्रोर्हितः सदा। सर्वमर्हति कल्याणं कनीयानपि सत्तमः॥
en: The people said : O king, it is true that, the son who is accomplished and who seeks the good of his parents, deserves all prosperity, though he is the youngest.

sn: अर्हः पूरुरिदं राज्यं यः सुतः प्रियकृत् तव। वरदानेन शुक्रस्य न शक्यं वक्तुमुत्तरम्॥
en: Therefore, Puru, who has done good to you, deserve, to have the kingdom. As Shukra has granted this boon, we have no power to say anything.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच पौरजानपदैस्तुष्टैरित्युक्तो नाहुषस्तदा। अभ्यषिञ्चत् तत: पूरुं राज्ये स्वे सुतमात्मनः॥
en: Vaishampayana said: Having been thus addressed the contented people the son of Nahusha (Yayati) installed his son Puru on the throne.

sn: दत्त्वा च पूरवे राज्यं वनवासाय दीक्षितः। पुरात् स निर्ययौ राजा ब्राह्मणैस्तापसैः सह॥
en: Bestowing the kingdom on Puru he resolved to live in the forest and he left his capital with Brahmanas and ascetics.

sn: यदोस्तु यादवा जातास्तुर्वसोर्यवनाः स्मृताः। दुह्योः सुतास्तु वै भोजा अनोस्तु म्लेच्छजातयः॥
en: The son of Yadu are known as the Yadavas, those of Turvasu as the Yavanas, those of Druhyu as the Bhojas and those of Anu as the Mlecchas,

sn: पूरोस्तु पौरवो वंशो यत्र जातोऽसि पार्थिव। इदं वर्षसहस्राणि राज्यं कारयितुं वशी॥
en: Those of Puru as the Pauravas, in which dynasty, O king, you are born to rule the country for one thousand years.

sn: पूरोस्तु पौरवो वंशो यत्र जातोऽसि पार्थिव। इदं वर्षसहस्राणि राज्यं कारयितुं वशी॥
en: Those of Puru as the Pauravas, in which dynasty, O king, you are born to rule the country for one thousand years.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवं स नाहुषो राजा ययातिः पुत्रमीप्सितम्। राज्येऽभिषिच्य मुदितो वानप्रस्थोऽभवन्मुनिः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having thus installed his dear son Puru on the throne, the son of Nahusha king Yayati, became very happy and accepted the Vanaprastha mode of life.

sn: उषित्वा च वने वासं ब्राह्मणैः संशितव्रतः। फलमूलाशनो दान्तस्तत: स्वर्गमितो गतः॥
en: He lived in the forest with the Brahmanas, becoming self-controlled and living on fruits and roots. Thus patiently bearing privations of all sorts, he at last ascended to heaven.

sn: स गतः स्वर्निवासं तं निवसन् मुदितः सुखी। कालेन चातिमहता पुनः शक्रेण पातितः॥ निपतन् प्रच्युतः स्वर्गादप्राप्तो मेदिनीतलम्। स्थित आसीदन्तरिक्षे स तदेति श्रुतं मया॥
en: Having thus ascended heaven, the king lived there in bliss. But some time after, he was hurled down (from heaven) by Indra. I have heard that having thus fallen from heaven, he stayed in the sky and did not fall on the earth.

sn: तत एव पुनश्चापि गतः स्वर्गमिति श्रुतम्। राज्ञा वसुमता सार्धमष्टकेन च वीर्यवान्॥ प्रतर्दनेन शिबिना समेत्य किल संसदि।
en: I have heard that some tiine after, he again ascended heaven in company with greatly powerful Vasumana, Ashtaka, Pratardana and Shibi.

sn: जनमेजय उवाच कर्मणा केन स दिवं पुनः प्राप्तो महीपतिः॥६।
en: Janamejaya said : I desire to hear in detail why that king, after entering heaven, was hurled down from it and why he again gained admittance.

sn: सर्वमेतदशेषेण श्रोतुमिच्छामि तत्त्वतः। कथ्यमानं त्वया विप्र विप्रर्षिगणसंनिधौ॥ देवराजसमो ह्यासीद् ययातिः पृथिवीपतिः। वर्धनः कुरुवंशस्य विभावसुसमद्युतिः॥ तस्य विस्तीर्णयशसः सत्यकीर्तेर्महात्मनः। चरितं श्रोतुमिच्छामि दिवि चेह च सर्वशः॥
en: O Brahmana, let this be narrated by you before all these Brahmana Rishis. The lord of the earth Yayati was like the king of the celestials (Indra). He was the progenitor of the exhaustive Kuru race; he was as effulgent as the sun. He was illustrious, world-wide famous and a man of wonderful achievements. I desire to hear in full the story of his life both here in this world and in heaven.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच हन्त ते कथयिष्यामि ययातेरुत्तमां कथाम्। दिवि चेह च पुण्यार्थी सर्वपापप्रणाशिनीम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said: I shall narrate to you the excellent history of Yayati's exploits both here on earth and in heaven. The story is sacred and it destroys all the sins of those that hear it.

sn: ययाति हुषो राजा पूरूं पुत्रं कनीयसम्। राज्येऽभिषिच्य मुदितः प्रवव्राज वनं तदा॥ अन्त्येषु स विनिक्षिप्य पुत्रान् यदुपुरोगमान्। फलमूलाशनो राजा वने संन्यवसचिरम्॥
en: The son of Nahusha, king Yayati, having installed his youngest son Puru on the throne, went to the forest to lead the life of a recluse. He passed over the claims of his other sons with Yadu at their head and he lived in the forest on fruits and roots.

sn: शंसितात्मा जितक्रोधस्तर्पयन् पितृदेवताः अग्नींश्च विधिवत्रुह्वन् वानप्रस्थविधानतः॥
en: He brought his mind and his passions under complete control. He pleased the Pitris and celestial by performing sacrifices. He poured libations according to the prescribed rites of men leading the Vanaprastha.

sn: अतिथीन् पूजयामास वन्येन हविषा विभुः। शिलोच्छवृत्तिमास्थाय शेषान्नकृतभोजनः॥
en: The illustrious king entertained the guests and strangers with fruits of the forest and ghee. He supported himself by eating only the scattered corn seeds.

sn: पूर्ण वर्षसहस्रं च एवंवृत्तिरभूनृपः। अब्भक्षः शरदस्त्रिंशदासीनियतवाङ्गनाः॥ ततश्च वायुभक्षोऽभूत् संवत्सरमतन्द्रितः। तथा पञ्चाग्निमध्ये च तपस्तेपे स वत्सरम्॥ एकपादः स्थितश्चासीत् षण्मासाननिलाशनः। पुण्यकीर्तिस्ततः स्वर्गे जगामावृत्य रोदसी॥
en: The king thus passed full one thousand years. He passed thirty years, living on water only and observed the vow of silence with mind under complete control. He passed full one year in fasting, living on air alone and having no sleep. He passed another one year in the midst of four fires and the burning sun overhead. He stood for six months continually on one leg. (Having thus passed his life in austere penances), the king, (Yayati) the doer of sacred deeds, ascended heaven.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच स्वर्गतः स तु राजेन्द्रो निवसन् देववेश्मनि। पूजितस्त्रिदशैः साध्यैर्मरुद्भिर्वसुभिस्तथा॥
en: Vaishampayana said : When that great king was living in heaven, he was adored by the celestials, the Sadhyas, the Marutas and the Vasus.

sn: देवलोकं ब्रह्मलोकं संचरन् पुण्यकृद् वशी। अवसत् पृथिवीपालो दीर्घकालमिति श्रुतिः॥
en: That doer of pious acts (Yayati) often went from the region of the celestials to the region of Brahma. It is heard that he lived in heaven for a long time.

sn: स कदाचिनृपश्रेष्ठो ययातिः शक्रमागमत्। कथान्ते तत्र शक्रेण स पृष्टः पृथिवीपतिः।३॥
en: One day the best of kings, Yayati, went to Indra and in the course of conversation the lord of earth was asked by Indra.

sn: शक्र उवाच यदा स पूरुस्तव रूपेण राजन् जरां गृहीत्वा प्रचचार भूमौ। तदा च राज्यं सम्प्रदायैव तस्मै त्वया किमुक्तः कथयेह सत्यम्॥
en: Indra said: O king, what did you say when Puru took your old age on earth and when you gave him his kingdom?

sn: ययातिरुवाच गङ्गायमुनयोर्मध्ये कृत्स्नोऽयं विषयस्तव। मध्य पृथिव्यास्त्वं राजा भ्रातरोऽन्त्याधिपास्तव॥
en: Yayati said : I told him the whole country between the rivers Ganges and the Yamuna which is in fact the central region of the earth, is yours. Your brothers will have the outlying regions.

sn: स्तथा तितिक्षुरतितिक्षोर्विशिष्टः। अमानुषेभ्यो मानुषाश्च प्रधाना विद्वांस्तथैवाविदुषः प्रधानः॥
en: I told him, the men having no anger are superior to men with anger; men having forgiveness are superior to men having no forgiveness. Man is superior to animals and the learned to the ignorant.

sn: आक्रुश्यमानो नाक्रोशेन्मन्युरेव तितिक्षतः। आक्रोष्टारं निर्दहति सुकृतं चास्य विन्दति॥
en: If wronged, you should not wrong in return. One's anger, if not subdued, burns one's own self. If subdued, it procures the virtues of the doers of good acts.

sn: नारुन्तुदः स्यान्न नृशंसवादी न हीनतः परमभ्याददीत्। ययास्य वाचा पर उद्विजेत न तां वदेदुषती पापलोक्याम्॥
en: You should never give pain to others by cruel words. Never defeat your enemies by despicable means. Never utter such sinful and burning words as may give pain to others.

sn: अरुन्तुदं परुषं तीक्ष्णवाचं वाक्कण्टकैर्वितुदन्तं मनुष्यान्। विद्यादलक्ष्मीकतमं जनानां मुखे निबद्धां निर्ऋतिं वहन्तम्॥
en: He who pricks another by the thorns of cruel words holds in his mouth a persecuting Rakshasa. Lakshmi (prosperity) leaves the man who casts his eyes on even such a man.

sn: सद्भिः पुरस्तादभिपूजित: स्यात् सद्भिस्तथा पृष्ठतो रक्षितः स्यात्। सदासतामतिवादांस्तितिक्षेत् सतां वृत्तं चाददीतार्यवृत्तः॥
en: You should always keep the virtuous man before you as your model. You should always compare your acts with those of the virtuous. You should always disregard the cruel words of the wicked.

sn: वाक्सायका वदनान्निष्पतन्ति यैराहतः शोचति रात्र्यहानि। परस्य नामर्मसु ते पतन्ति तान् पण्डितो नावसृजेत् परेषु॥
en: He who keeps the arrows of cruel words in his lips weeps day and night. The cruel words strike at the inmost part of the body. The wise men never fling such arrows (of cruel words) at others.

sn: न हीदृशं संवननं त्रिषु लोकेषु विद्यते। दया मैत्री च भूतेषु दानं च मधुरा च वाक्॥
en: There is nothing in the three worlds with which you can worship the deities as kindness, friendship, charity and sweet words.

sn: तस्मात् सान्त्वं सदा वाच्यं न वाच्यं परुषं क्वचित्। पूज्यान् सम्पूजयेद् दद्यान्न च याचेत् कदाचन॥
en: Therefore, you should always utter sweet words that give pleasure and not pain. You should always give and never beg. You should show respects to those that deserve your respect.

sn: इन्द्र उवाच सर्वाणि कर्माणि समाप्य राजन् गृहं परित्यज्य वनं गतोऽसि। तत् त्वां पृच्छामि नहुषस्य पुत्र केनासि तुल्यस्तपसा ययाते॥
en: Indra said: O king, O son of Nahusha, O Yayati, after accomplishing all your duties, you went to the forest, leaving your home. I ask you, tell me like whom you are in ascetic merits.

sn: ययातिरुवाच नाहं देवमनुष्येषु गन्धर्वेषु महर्षिषु। आत्मनस्तपसा तुल्यं कंचित् पश्यामि वासव॥
en: Yayati said: O Vasava (Indra), I do not find among men, the celestials, the Gandharvas and great Rishis, any one equal to me in ascetic merits.

sn: इन्द्र उवाच यदावमंस्थाः सदृशः श्रेयसश्च अल्पीयसश्चाविदितप्रभावः। तस्माल्लोकास्त्वन्तवन्तस्तवेमे क्षीणे पुण्ये पतितास्यद्य राजन्॥
en: Indra said: O king, as you disregard those that are your superiors, those that are your equals and those that are your inferiors, your virtues, therefore, suffer a diminution and thus you must fall from heaven.

sn: ययातिरुवाच सुरर्षिगन्धर्वनरावमानात् क्षयं गता मे यदि शक्र लोकाः। इच्छाम्यहं सुरलोकाद् विहीनः सतां मध्ये पतितुं देवराज॥
en: Yayati said : O king of the celestials, if my virtues have really been diminished (by my pride), let me fall at least among men who are virtuous and honest.

sn: इन्द्र उवाच श्च्युतः प्रतिष्ठां यत्र लब्धासि भूयः। एतद् विदित्वा च पुनर्ययाते त्वं मावमंस्थाः सदृशः श्रेयसश्च॥
en: Indra said: O king, you shall fall among those that are virtuous and honest. You shall also gain great renown. O Yayati, after your this experience, never again disregard any one, your superiors, your equals or even your inferiors.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततः प्रहायामरराजजुष्टान् पुण्याँल्लोकान् पतमानं ययातिम्। मुवाच सद्धर्मविधानगोप्ता॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Thereupon Yayati fell from the region of the holy. And he was seen when thus falling by that royal sage, Ashtaka, the protector of religion. Seeing him he asked.

sn: अष्टक उवाच कस्त्वं युवा वासवतुल्यरूप: स्वतेजसा दीप्यमानो यथाग्निः। पतस्युदीर्णाम्बुधराम्धकारात् खात् खेचराणां प्रवरो यथार्कः॥
en: Ashtaka said: Who are you, young as you are, as handsome as Indra, as prominent by your own splendour as that of fire? Who are you falling like the foremost ranger of the sky, the sun, driving away the dark masses of clouds?

sn: दृष्ट्वा च त्वां सूर्यपथात् पतन्तं वैश्वानरार्कातिभप्रमेयम्। किं नु स्विदेतत् पततीति सर्वे वितर्कयन्तः परिमोहिताः स्मः॥
en: Seeing you fall from the region of the sun, as effulgent as the fire or the sun, all men are asking themselves, "What is this that falls?" They are deprived of their consciousness.

sn: दृष्ट्वा च त्वां धिष्ठितं देवमार्गे शक्रार्कविष्णुप्रतिमप्रभावम्। अभ्युद्गतास्त्वां वयमद्य सर्वे तत्त्वं प्रपाते तव जिज्ञासमानाः॥
en: Seeing you in the path of the celestials, as effulgent as Surya, Indra or Vishnu, we have all come to you to ascertain the truth.

sn: न चापि त्वां धृष्णुमः प्रष्टुमग्रे न च त्वमस्मान् पृच्छसि ये वयं स्मः। तत् त्वां पृच्छामि स्पृहणीयरूप कस्य त्वं वा किंनिमित्तं त्वमागाः॥
en: O enviably handsome one, we would not have been guilty of incivility by first asking you who you are, if you would have asked us first who we are. We ask you, (tell us) who you are and why you come here?

sn: भयं तु ते व्येतु विषादमोही त्यजाशु चैवेन्द्रसमप्रभाव। त्वां वर्तमानं हि सतां सकाशे नालं प्रसोढुं बलहापि शक्रः॥
en: O Indra-like great one, let your fears be dispelled, let your woes and afflictions cease. । You are now in the presence of the virtuous and the wise. Even Indra, the slayer of Bala, cannot do you any harm.

sn: सन्तः प्रतिष्ठा हि सुखच्युतानां सतां सदैवामरराजकल्प। ते संगताः स्थावरजङ्गमेशा: प्रतिष्ठिस्त्वं सदृशेषु सत्सु॥
en: O Indra-like great one, the honest and the virtuous are the support of their brethren. Here are assembled the protectors of the movable and the immovables of the world, the honest and the virtuous. You are now with such ones.

sn: प्रभुरग्निः प्रतपने भूमिरावपने प्रभुः। । प्रभुः सूर्यः प्रकाशित्वे सतां चाभ्यागतः प्रभुः॥
en: As Agni is the lord that gives heat, as earth is the lord that holds the seed (and produces corn), as sun is the lord that dispels darkness, so is a guest the lord of the honest and the virtuous.

sn: ययातिरुवाच अहं ययातिनहुषस्य पुत्रः पूरोः पिता सर्वभूतावमानात्। प्रभ्रंशितः सुरसिद्धर्षिलोकात् परिच्युतः प्रपताम्यल्पपुण्यः॥
en: Yayati said : I am Yayati, the son of Nahusha and the father of Puru. I am falling down from the region of the celestials, the Siddhas and the Rishis, for the diminution of my virtues. (I am falling), because I disregarded every creature on earth.

sn: स्तेनाभिवादं भवतां न प्रयुञ्जे। यो विद्यया तसा जन्मना वा वृद्धः स पूज्यो भवति द्विजानाम्॥
en: As I am older than in age, I did not salute you first. He who is older in age or superior in learning or asceticism is revered by Brahmanas.

sn: अष्टक उवाच अवादीस्त्वं वयसा यः प्रवृद्धः स वैराजन् नाभ्यधिकः कथ्यते च। यो विद्यया तपसा सम्प्रवृद्धः स एव पूज्यो भवति द्विजानाम्॥
en: Ashtaka said : O king, you say that he, who is older in years, deserves the respect and reverence of others. But it is said that he is truly worthy of respect is superior in learning and asceticism.

sn: ययातिरुवाच स्तद् वर्ततेऽप्रवणे पापलोक्यम्। सन्तोऽसतां नानुवर्तन्ति चैतद् यथा चैषामनुकूलास्तथाऽऽसन्॥
en: Yayati said : It is said that sin destroys the merit of all virtuous acts. Vanity contains the element of that which leads to hell. The virtuous never follow the path of the sinful.

sn: अभूद् धनं मे विपुलं गतं तद् विचेष्टमानो नाधिगन्ता तदस्मि। एवं प्रधार्यात्महिते निविष्टो यो वर्तते स विजानाति धीरः॥
en: They act in a way as to increase their virtue. I myself had great religious merits, but all is now gone. I shall never be able to regain them with my best efforts. He, who will take lesson from my this fate, will be wise and virtueus.

sn: र्यः सर्वविद्यासु विनीतबुद्धिः। वेदानधीत्य तपसाऽऽयोज्य देह दिवं समायात् पुरुषो वीतमोहः॥
en: He who, having acquired great wealth performs sacrifices, who, having acquired all kinds of learning, remains humble, who, having studied the entire Vedas, devotes himself to asceticism, goes to heaven.

sn: न जातु हृष्येन्महता धनेन वेदानधीयीतानहंकृतः स्यात्। नानाभावा बहवो जीवलोके दैवाधीना नष्टचेष्टाधिकाराः। तत् तत् प्राप्य न विहन्येत धीरो दिष्टं बलीय इति मत्वाऽऽत्मबुद्ध्या॥
en: No one should be proud of his great wealth; no one should feel exalted, because he has studied the entire Vedas. Men are of different dispositions in the world, but Destiny is supreme. Power and exertion are both futile and useless. Knowing Destiny to be supreme (over all), the wise should neither feel pride nor grief.

sn: सुखं हि जन्तुर्यदि वापि दुःखं दैवाधीनं विन्दते नात्मशक्त्या। तस्माद् दिष्टं बलवन्मन्यमानो न संज्वरेनापि हृष्येत् कथंचित्॥
en: Remembering that Destiny is supreme (over all), creatures should know that happiness and misery depend on Destiny and not on their own exertion and power.

sn: दुःखैन तप्येन्न सुखैः प्रहृष्येत् समेन वर्तेत सदैव धीरः। दिष्टं बलीय इति मन्यमानो न संज्वरेनापि हृष्येत् कथंचित्॥
en: The wise should always live contented, without grieving for misery or exalting for happiness. When Destiny is supreme, both grief and exaltation are useless.

sn: भये न मुह्याम्यष्टकाहं कदाचित् संतापो मे मानसो नास्ति कश्चित्। धाता यथा मां विदधीत लोके ध्रुवं तथाहं भवितेति मत्वा॥
en: O Ashtaka, I never feel terrified with fear, nor do I ever feel grief, for I know that I shall be on earth exactly what the great Ordainer has made me.

sn: संस्वेदजा अण्डजाचोद्भिदश्च सरीसृपाः कृमयोऽथाप्सु मत्स्याः। तथाश्मानस्तृणकाष्ठं च सर्वे दिष्टक्षये स्वां प्रकृतिं भजन्ति॥
en: The Insects, the worms, all the oviparous creatures, vegetables, crawling animals, vermins, fishes, stones, wood, in fact all created things, are united with the Prakriti when they are freed from their acts.

sn: अनित्यतां सुखदुःखस्य बुद्ध्वा कस्मात् संतापमष्टकाहं भजेयम्। किं कुर्यां वै किं च कृत्वा न तष्ये तस्मात् संतापं वर्जयाम्यप्रमत्तः॥
en: Happiness and misery are transitory, O Ashtaka, knowing this, why should I grieve? We never know how we are to act to avoid misery. Therefore, grief must be cast off.

sn: वैशम्पयान उवाच मथाष्टकः पुनरेवान्वपृच्छत्। मातामहं सर्वगुणोपपन्नं तत्र स्थितं स्वर्गलोके यथावत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said: King Yayati, possessed of every accomplishment, who was the maternal grand father of Ashtaka, was again asked by him to tell him the account of his living in heaven.

sn: अष्टक उवाच स्त्वया भुक्ता यं च कालं यथावत्। तान् मे राजन् ब्रूहि सर्वान यथावत् क्षेत्रज्ञवद् भावसे त्वं हि धर्मान्॥
en: Ashtaka said: O king of the world, tell me in detail the account of all those regions which you have visited and in which you passed your time in bliss. (Tell me also) the period for which you thus lived.

sn: ययातिरुवाच स्ततो लोकान् महतश्चाजयं वै। तत्रावसं वर्षसहस्रमानं ततो लोकं परमस्म्यभ्युपेतः॥
en: Yayati said: I was a great king on earth, ruling over the whole world as my kingdom. I acquired many high regions by my religious merits. I lived full one thousand years on earth and then I ascended to a very high region.

sn: ततः पुरीं पुरुहूतस्य रम्यां सहस्रद्वारां शतयोजनायताम्। अध्यावसं वर्षसहस्रमात्र ततो लोकं परमस्म्यभ्युपेतः॥
en: It is the abode of Indra. It is very beautiful; it has one thousand gates and it extends one hundred Yojanas all around. Here lived I for another one thousand years. And then I ascended to a higher region.

sn: ततो दिव्यमजरं प्राप्य लोकं प्रजापतेर्लोकपते१रापम्। तत्रावसं वर्षसहस्रमानं ततो लोकं परमस्म्यभ्युपेतः॥
en: This is the region of supreme beatitude, the abode of the Prajapati, the lord of the earth, a region very difficult to attain. Here lived I for another on thousand years. And I then ascended to a higher region.

sn: स देवदेवस्य निवेशने च विहत्य लोकानवसं यथेष्टम्। स्तुल्यप्रभावद्युतिरीश्वराणाम्॥
en: It is the abode of the god of gods, (Vishnu), where I lived for many years in supreme bliss. I have lived in various regions and I was adored by the celestials and I possessed splendour and prowess like the celestial.

sn: तथावसं नन्दने कामरूपी संवत्सराणामयुतं शतानाम्। सहाप्सरोभिर्विहरन् पुण्यगन्धान् पश्यन् नगान् पुष्पितांश्चारुरूपान्॥
en: I was capable of assuming any form at will; I sported for many millions of years with the Apsaras in the gardens of Nandana, under innumerable beautiful trees clad in flowery garb and spreading delicious perfume.

sn: तत्र स्थितं मां देवसुखेषु सक्तं कालेऽतीते महति ततोऽतिमात्रम्। दूतो देवानामब्रवीदुग्ररूपो ध्वंसेत्युचैस्त्रिः प्लुतेन स्वरेण॥
en: I lived there in celestial happiness for many years, when a celestial messenger of grim visage thrice shouted to me in a loud and deep voice, “Ruined, Ruined, Ruined."

sn: एतावन्मे विदितं राजसिंह ततो भ्रष्टोऽहं नन्दनात् क्षीणपुण्यः। वाचोऽश्रौषं चान्तरिक्षे सुराणां सानुक्रोशाः शोचतां मां नरेन्द्र॥
en: O best of kings, this much I remember that I fell from Nandana and all my religious merits were gone. O king of men, I heard the voices of the celestials in the sky exclaiming in grief.

sn: अहो कष्टं क्षीणपुण्यो ययाति: पतत्यसौ पुण्यकृत् पुण्यकीर्तिः। तानब्रुवं पतमानस्ततोऽहं सतां मध्ये निपतेयं कथं नु॥
en: "What misfortune! The virtuous and meritorious Yayati is falling! His all religious merits are destroyed!” And when I was falling, I asked them, “Where are those wise ones amongst whom am I to fall?"

sn: तैराख्याता भवतां यज्ञभूमिः समीक्ष्य चेमां त्वरितमुपागतोऽस्मि। धूमापाङ्गं प्रतिगृह्य प्रतीतः॥
en: They pointed out to me this sacred sacrificial region belonging to you. I am hastily coming to this your sacrificial ground, seeing the curls of smoke that rise from the sacrificial fire and blacken the sky. I smelt the perfume of the sacrificial ghee.

sn: अष्टक उवाच यदावसो नन्दने कामरूपी संवत्सराणामयुतं शतानाम्। किं कारणं कार्तयुगप्रधान हित्वा च त्वं वसुधामन्वपद्यः॥
en: Ashtaka said: O foremost man of the Krita Yuga, you having been able to assume any form at will, passed millions of years in the garden of Nandana. For what reason have you been compelled to leave that happy region and come here today?

sn: ययातिरुवाच ज्ञातिः सुहृत् स्वजनो वा यथेह क्षीणे वित्ते त्यज्यते मानवैहि। तथा तत्र क्षीणपुण्यं मनुष्यं त्यजन्ति सद्यः सेश्वरा देवसङ्घाः॥
en: Yayati said : As relatives and kinsmen forsake in this world a man who has lost his wealth, so in the other world Indra and the celestials forsake one who loses his righteousness.

sn: अष्टक उवाच तस्मिन् कथं क्षीणपुण्या भवन्ति सम्मुह्यते मेऽत्र मनोऽतिमात्रम्। किं वा विशिष्टाः कस्य धामोपयान्ति तदे वै ब्रूहि क्षेत्रवित् त्वं मतो मे॥
en: Ashtaka said: O king, I am very curious to learn how men can lose their righteousness in the other world. Tell me also what regions are attained by what means. I know you are acquainted with all the doings and the sayings.

sn: ययातिरुवाच इमं भौमं नरकं ते पतन्ति लालप्यमाना नरदेव सर्वे। ते कङ्कगोमायुबलाशनार्थे क्षीणा विवृद्धिं बहुधा व्रजन्ति॥
en: Yayati said : O God-like man, they that speak of their own merits are doomed to the painful hell called Bhauma, (earth). Though really lean, they appear to grow (fat on earth) to become the food for vultures, dogs and jackals.

sn: तस्मादेतद् वर्जनीयं नरेन्द्र दुष्टं लोके गर्हणीयं च कर्म। आख्यातं ते पार्थिव सर्वमेव भूयश्चेदानीं वद किं ते वदामि॥
en: Therefore, O king, this censurable and wicked vice should be cast off in this world. O king, I have now told you all. Tell me what more I shall speak.

sn: अष्टक उवाच यदा तु तान् वितुदन्ते वयांसि तथा गृध्राः शितिकण्ठाः पतङ्गाः। कथं भवन्ति कथमाभवन्ति न भौममन्यं नरकं शृणोमि॥
en: Ashtaka said: When life is destroyed by age, vultures, Shitikantha, insects and worms eat up the human body, where does man then live? How does he come to life again? I have never heard of any hell called Bhauma.

sn: ययातिरुवाच ऊर्ध्वं देहात् कर्मणा जृम्भमाणाद् व्यक्तं पृथिव्यामनुसंचरन्ति। इमं भौमं नरकं ते पतन्ति नावेक्षन्ते वर्षपूगाननेकान्॥
en: Yayati said : When the body is destroyed (by death), man, according to the effects of his acts, is born again in the womb of his mother. He stays there in an indistinct form and he then gradually assumes distinct and visible form. He then reappears and walks on the earth. Thus he falls into the hell Bhauma (earth) and does not see the end of his existence.

sn: षष्टिं सहस्राणि पतन्ति व्योम्नि तथा अशीतिं परिवत्सराणि तान् वै तुदन्ति पततः प्रपातं भीमा भौमा राक्षसास्तीक्ष्णदंष्ट्राः॥
en: Some thus falling live for sixty thousand years in the firmament; some again for eighty thousand years. They then fall (on this earth) and they are attacked by fearful Bhauma Rakshasas of sharp teeth.

sn: अष्टक उवाच यदेनसस्ते पततस्तुदन्ति भीमा भौमा राक्षसास्तीक्ष्णदंष्ट्राः। कथं भवन्ति कथमाभवन्ति कथंभूता गर्भभूता भवन्ति॥
en: Ashtaka said : Why are men, when thus falling from heaven, attacked by these fearful and sharpteethed Rakshasas? Why are they not annihilated? How do they again enter the womb?

sn: ययातिरुवाच मन्वेति तद् वै पुरुषेण सृष्टम्। स वै तस्या रज आपद्यते वै स गर्भभूतः समुपैति तत्र॥ वनस्पतीनोषधीश्चाविशन्ति अपो वायुं पृथिवीं चान्तरिक्षम्। मेवम्भूता गर्भभूता भवन्ति॥
en: Yayati said : All beings, thus fallen from heaven, become subtle substance, living in water. This water subsequently becomes the semen from which life is created. It then enters the womb of a woman in her season and develops into the embryo. It then becomes visible life like the fruit from the flower. Entering into trees, plants, vegetables, water, air, earth and space, the watery seed of life becomes quadrupeds of bipeds. This is the case with all creatures.

sn: अष्टक उवाच मुताहोस्वित् स्वेन कायेन याति। माचक्ष्व मे संशयात् प्रब्रवीमि॥ शरीरभेदाभिसमुच्छ्रयं च चक्षुःश्रोत्रे लभते केन संज्ञाम्। एतत् तत्त्वं सर्वमाचक्ष्व पृष्टः क्षेत्रज्ञं त्वां तात मन्याम सर्वे॥
en: Ashtaka said: Does a being who has got a human form enter the womb in its own shape or in some other? How does it acquire its distinct and visible shape, its eyes, ears and consciousness? Tell me all this, I ask you, because I have my doubts.

sn: ययातिरुवाच वायुः समुत्कर्षति गर्भयोनिमृतौ रेत: पुष्परसानुपृक्तम्। स तत्र तन्मात्रकृताधिकारः। क्रमेण संवर्धयतीह गर्भम्॥
en: Yayati said: The being that remains in a subtle form in the seed, when dropped into the womb, is attracted by atmospheric force for purposes of rebirth, according to the merits of one's acts.

sn: स जायमानो विगृहीतमात्रः संज्ञामधिष्ठाय ततो मनुष्यः। स श्रोत्राभ्यां वेदयतीह शब्दं स वै रूपं पश्यति चक्षुषा च॥ घ्राणेन गन्धं जिह्वयाथो रसं च त्वचा स्पर्श मनसा वेद भावम्। इत्यष्टकेहोपहितं हि विद्धि महात्मनां प्राणभृतां शरीरे॥
en: He then develops in course of time into the embryo. He is then furnished with the visible organisation. Coming out of the womb in course of time, he becomes conscious of his existence. He then becomes sensible of sound by his ears, of colour and form by his eyes, of scent by his nose, of taste by his tongue, of touch by his whole body and of ideas by his mind. O Ashtaka, it is thus that the gross and visible body develops from the subtle essence.

sn: अष्टक उवाच यः संस्थितः पुरुषो दह्यते वा निखन्यते वापि निकृष्यते वा। अभावभूतः स विनाशमेत्य केनात्मना चेतयते परस्तात्॥
en: Ashtaka said: The body is burnt, buried of otherwise destroyed after death. Reduced to nothing on one's death, by what principle is one again revived.

sn: भवन्ति पापा ययातिरुवाच हित्वा सोऽसून् सुप्तवन्निष्टनित्वा पुरोधाय सुकृतं दुष्कृतं वा। अन्यां योनि पवनाग्रानुसारी हित्वा देहं भजते राजसिंह॥
en: Yayati said : O lion of kings, the man who dies, assumes a subtle form, but he retains the consciousness of all his acts as if in a dream. He then assumes some other form with a quicker speed than that of air.

sn: पुण्यां योनि पुण्यकृतो व्रजन्ति पापां योनि पापकृतो व्रजन्ति। कीटाः पतङ्गाश्च न मे विवक्षास्ति महानुभाव॥ चतुष्पदा द्विपदाः षट्पदाश्च तथाभूता गर्भभूता भवन्ति। आख्यातमेतन्निखिलेन सर्वं भूयस्तु किं पृच्छसि राजसिंह॥
en: The virtuous attain to a superior and the vicious to an inferior form of existence. The vicious becomes worms and insects. O illustrious one, I have nothing more to say. I have told you, how beings are born by the development of their embryonic formas quadrupeds, bipeds and six-footed creatures. What more will you ask me?

sn: अष्टक उवाच किंस्वित् कृत्वा लभते तात लोकान् मर्त्यः श्रेष्ठांस्तपसा विद्यया वा। च्छुभाँल्लोकान् येन गच्छेत् क्रमेण॥
en: Ashtaka said: O sire, how does a man attain to those higher regions whence there is no return to earthly life again? Is it by asceticism or knowledge? How does a man attain to the region of the highest bliss? As I ask you, tell me all.

sn: ययातिरुवाच तपश्च दानं च शमो दमश्च हीरार्जवं सर्वभूतानुकम्पा। स्वर्गस्य लोकस्य वदन्ति सन्तो द्वाराणि सप्तैव महान्ति पुंसाम्। नश्यन्ति मानेन तमोऽभिभूताः पुंसः सदैवेति वदन्ति सन्तः॥
en: Yayati said ; The wise say that there are seven gates through which admission might be gained to heaven. These are asceticism, gift, tranquility of mind, self-command, modesty, simplicity and kindness. A person loses all this in consequence of vanity.

sn: अधीयानः पण्डितं मन्यमानो यो विद्यया हन्ति यशः परेषाम्। तस्यान्तवन्तश्च भवन्ति लोका न चास्य तद् ब्रह्म फलं ददाति॥
en: The man who, having acquired knowledge, regards himself as learned and destroys, the reputation of others by his learning, never goes to the region of the highest bliss. It does not also give him the power of attaining to Brahma.

sn: चत्वारि कर्माण्यभयंकराणि भयं प्रयच्छन्त्ययथाकृतानि। मानाग्निहोत्रमुत मानमौनं मानेनाधीतमुत पानयज्ञः॥
en: Study, taciturnity, worship before fire and sacrifices, these are the four means through which fear is removed. But when these four are mixed with vanity, they cause fear instead of removing it.

sn: न मानमान्यो मुदमाददीत न संतापं प्राप्नुयाचावमानात्। सन्तः सतः पूजयन्तीह लोके नासाधवः साधुबुद्धिं लभन्ते॥ इति दद्यामित यज इत्यधीय इति व्रतम्। इत्येतानि भयान्याहुस्तानि वानि सर्वशः॥
en: The wise should never feel pride in receiving honours, nor should they be sorry if insulted. For it is the wise alone that honour the wise; the wicked and vicious can never act like the virtuous. I have given so much, I have performed so many sacrifices, I have studied so much, I have observed so many vows, such vanity and pride are the roots of all fear. Therefore, it must be abandoned by all means.

sn: ये चाश्रयं वेदयन्ते पुराणं मनीषिणो मानसमार्गरुद्धम्। तद्वः श्रेयस्तेन संयोगमेत्य परां शान्तिं प्राप्नुयुः प्रेत्य चेह॥
en: Those learned men who accept as their only support the unchangeable and inconceivable Brahma, Brahma that showers blessings on persons virtuous as you are, enjoy perfect peace here in this world and hereafter in heaven.

sn: अष्टक उवाच चरन् गृहस्थः कथमेति धर्मान् कथं भिक्षुः कथमाचार्यकर्मा। वानप्रस्थः सत्पथे संनिविष्टो बहून्यस्मिन् सम्प्रति वेदयन्ति॥
en: Ashtaka said: Those that are learned in the Vedas differ in opinions as regards the respective methods which should be practised by the Grihastas, Brahmacharis, Bhikshus and Vanaprasthas, so that they may acquire religious merits.

sn: ययातिरुवाच आहूताध्यायी गुरुकर्मस्वचोद्यः पूर्वोत्थायी चरमं चोपशायी। मृदुर्दान्तो धृतिमानप्रमत्तः ध्यायशील: सिध्यति ब्रह्मचारी॥
en: Yayati said: A Brahmachari must do the following. When he will live in the house of his preceptor, he must receive lessons only when his preceptor will call him to do it. He must serve his preceptor without waiting for his command. He must rise before his preceptor from his bed and go to bed after him. He must be humble, self-controlled, patient, vigilant and devoted to study.

sn: धर्मागतं प्राप्य धनं यजेत दद्यात् सदैवातिथीन् भोयजेच्च। अनाददानश्च परैरदत्तं सैषा गृहस्थोपनिषत् पुराणी॥
en: It is said in the oldest Upanishad that he must perform sacrifices after acquiring wealth by honest means. He should spend it in charity; he should be hospitable to all that would come to his house; he should never use anything without giving a portion to others.

sn: स्ववीर्यजीवी वृजिनान्निवृत्तो दाता परेभ्यो न परोपतापी। तादृङ्मुनिः सिद्धिमुपैति मुख्यां वसन्नरण्ये नियताहारचेष्टः॥
en: A Muni (Brahmachari) should live in the forest, depending on his own vigour and without searching for food. He should abstain from all vicious acts; he should give away in charity; he should never inflict pain upon any creatures. It is then only that he can gain success.

sn: अशिल्पजीवी गुणवांश्चैव नित्यं जितेन्द्रियः सर्वतो विप्रयुक्तः। श्चरन् देशानेकचरः स भिक्षुः॥
en: He is a true Bhikshu, who does not support himself by any manual labour, who possesses many accomplishments, who has his passions under complete control, who is thoroughly unconnected with all worldly concerns, who does not sleep under the shelter of a householder's roof, who is without wife and who travels over many countries, going some distance every day.

sn: रात्र्या यया वाभिजिताच लोका भवन्ति कामाभिजिताः सुखाचा नरण्यसंस्थो भवितुं यतात्मा॥ दशैव पूर्वान् दश चापरांश्च ज्ञातीनथात्मानमथैकविंशम्। अरण्यवासी सुकृते दधाति विमुच्यारण्ये स्वशरीरधातून्॥
en: A learned should adopt the Vanaprastha mode of life, after the performance of the necessary rites. He should adopt it when he has been able to control his thirst for enjoyments and desire of acquiring wealth. When a man dies in the forest, leading the Vanaprastha mode of life, he mixes his ancestors and grand-children, numbering ten generations including himself, with the divine man essence.

sn: अष्टक उवाच कतिस्विदेव मुनयः कति मौनानि चाप्युत। भवन्तीति तदाचक्ष्व श्रोतुच्छिामहे वयम्॥
en: Ashtaka said : How many kinds of Munis are there and how many kinds of Munis (observers of vows)? We desire to hear all this.

sn: ययातिरुवाच अरण्ये वसतो यस्य ग्रामो भवति पृष्ठतः। ग्रामे वा वसतोऽरण्यं स मुनिः स्याजनाधिप॥
en: Yayati said: O king, he is a true Muni, who possesses all things pertaining to a village though living in the forest and also possesses all things pertaining to the forest though living in a village.

sn: अष्टक उवाच कथंस्विद् वसतोऽरण्ये ग्रामो भवति पृष्ठतः। ग्रामे वा वसतोऽरण्यं कथं भवति पृष्ठतः॥
en: Ashtaka said : How is it possible to possess all things pertaining to a village when living in the forest and all things pertaining to a forest when living in a village?

sn: ययातिरुवाच न ग्राम्यमुपयुञ्जीत य आरण्यो मुनिर्भवेत्। तथास्य वसतोऽरण्ये ग्रामो भवति पृष्ठतः॥
en: Yayati said : A Muni lives in the forest after withdrawing himself from all worldly objects. But though he never seeks to possess things pertaining to a village, he may yet get them by his ascetic powers.

sn: अनग्निरनिकेतश्चाप्यगोत्रचरणो मुनिः। कौपीनाच्छादनं यावत् तावदिच्छेच चीवरम्॥ यावत् प्राणाभिसंधानं तावदिच्छेच भोजनम्। तथास्य वसतो ग्रामेऽरण्यं भवति पृष्ठतः॥ यस्तु कामान् परित्यज्य त्यक्तकर्मा जितेन्द्रियः। आतिष्ठेच मुनिर्मीनं स लोके सिद्धिमाप्नुयात्॥
en: A true Muni, withdrawn from all earthly objects, might live in a village, leading the life of a hermit. Chad in Kaupina (scantiest of robes,) he considers himself attired in the richest robe. He is content with food just sufficient to support life. He who abandons all desires, who has all his passions under complete control and who has given up all actions, is the man who attains success.

sn: धौतदन्तं कृत्तनखं सदा स्नातमलंकृतम्। असितं सितकर्माणं कस्तमर्हति नार्चितुम्॥
en: Why should you not revere the man who lives on pure food, who refrains from injuring others, whose heart is ever holy, who is effulgent in his ascetic merits, who is free from the leaden weight of desire and who abstains from injury even when it is sanctioned by the scriptures?

sn: तपसा कर्शितः क्षामः क्षीणमांसास्थिशोणितः। स च लोकमिमं जित्वा लोकं विजयते परम्॥
en: Emaciated by hard asceticism and reduced in marrow, blood and flesh, such a Muni not only conquers this world, but the highest world.

sn: यदा भवति निर्द्वन्द्वो मुनिर्मौनं समास्थितः। अथ लोकमिमं जित्वा लोकं विजयते परम्॥
en: The Muni who sits in Yoga mediation and who becomes indifferent to happiness and misery, honour and insult, conquers this world and conquering it, he conquers the highest world.

sn: आस्येन तु यदाहारं गोवन्मृगयते मुनिः। अथास्य लोकः सर्वोऽयं सोऽमृतत्वाय कल्पते॥
en: The Muni who eats like the kine and other animals, without providing for it beforehand and without any relish, becomes identified with the whole universe.

sn: अष्टक उवाच कतरस्त्वनयोः पूर्वं देवानामेति सात्मताम्। उभयोर्धावतो राजन् सूर्याचन्द्रमसोरिव॥
en: Ashtaka said: O king, who does amongst the two, namely the ascetic and the man of knowledge, first attain to the communion with Brahma, although both exerting like the sun and the moon!

sn: ययातिरुवाच अनिकेतो गृहस्थेषु कामवृत्तेषु संयतः। ग्राम एव वसन् भिक्षुस्तयोः पूर्वतरं गतः॥
en: Yayati said : He who is a man of knowledge and who is self controlled, though living among the householders with various sorts of desires, attains to salvation first.

sn: अवाप्य दीर्घमायुस्तु यः प्राप्तो विकृतिं चरेत्। तप्यते यदि तत् कृत्वा चरेत् सोऽन्यत् तपस्ततः॥
en: Those that devote themselves to Yoga meditation take time to acquire that knowledge, for by practice alone they divest themselves from the idea of duality.

sn: पापानां कर्मणां नित्यं बिभियाद् यस्तु मानवः। सुखमप्याचरन् नित्यं सोऽत्यन्तं सुखमेधते॥ र्यः सेवतेऽधर्ममनर्थबुद्धिः। स्तदार्जवं स समाधिस्तदार्यम्॥
en: Then again, if a man devoted to Yoga do not find sufficient time to attain to success in one's one life, he is benefited in his next life by the progress already made. But the man of knowledge ever sees the indestructible Unity, therefore he, though emerged in worldly enjoyments, is never affected in the heart.

sn: अष्टक उवाच केनासि हूतः प्रहितोऽसि राजन् युवा स्रग्वी दर्शनीयः सुवर्चाः। मुताहोस्वित् पार्थिवं स्थानमस्ति॥
en: Ashtaka said: O king, you are young, you are handsome, you are decorated with celestial garlands, your splendour is great. From what place have you come and where do you go? Whose messenger are you? Are you going to earth?

sn: ययातिरुवाच इमं भौमं नरकं क्षीणपुण्यः प्रवेष्टुमुर्वी गगनाद् विप्रहीणः। उक्त्वाहं वः प्रपतिष्याम्यनन्तरं त्वरन्ति मां लोकपा ब्रह्मणो ये॥
en: Yayati said : As I have lost my religious virtues, I am falling into the Bhauma,(earth) hell. I shall go there after finishing my talk with you. The Lokapalas are commanding me even now to hasten thither.

sn: स्ते गंगता गुणवन्तस्तु सर्वे। शक्राच लब्धो हि वरो मयैष पतिष्यता भूमितलं नरेन्द्र॥
en: O king, I have obtained the following boon from Indra. Though I shall fall on earth, yet I shall fall among wise and virtuous men.

sn: अष्टक उवाच पृच्छामि त्वां मा प्रपत प्रपातं यदि लोकाः पार्थिव सन्ति मेऽत्र। यद्यन्तरिक्षे यदि वा दिवि स्थिताः क्षेत्रज्ञं त्वां तस्य धर्मस्य मन्ये॥
en: Ashtaka said : O king, I believe, you know every thing. I ask you, is there any region for myself either in heaven or in the firmament? If there be any, you shall not fall.

sn: ययातिरुवाच यावत् पृथिव्यां विहितं गवावं सहारण्यैः पशुभिः पार्वतैश्च। तावल्लोका दिवि ते संस्थिता वै तथा विजानीहि नरेन्द्रसिंह॥
en: Yayati said : O best of kings, there are many regions for you to enjoy in heaven, as many as the kine and horses of earth, as the animals in the wilderness and the hills.

sn: अष्टक उवाच तांस्ते ददामि मा प्रपत प्रपातं ये मे लोका दिवि राजेन्द्र सन्ति स्तानाक्रम क्षिप्रमपेतमोहः॥
en: Ashtaka said: O king, I give to you all those regions in heaven or in the firmament that are for me to enjoy. Therefore, though falling, you must not fall. Take them soon, wherever they may be, in heaven or in the firmament. Let your sorrow cease.

sn: ययातिरुवाच नास्मद्विधो ब्राह्मणो ब्रह्मविच प्रतिग्रहे वर्तते राजमुख्य। स्तथाददं पूर्वमहं नरेन्द्र॥
en: Yayati said : O best of kings, a Brahma-knowing Brahmana alone can accept gifts and not men like ourselves. O king, I myself have given away (many gifts) to Brahmanas, as I should do.

sn: नाब्राह्मणः कृपणो जातु जीवेद् याच्यापि स्याद् ब्राह्मणी वीरपत्नी। सोऽहं नैवाकृतपूर्वं चरेयं विधिसमानः किमु तत्र साधु॥
en: Let no man, who is not a Brahmana and no woman who is the wife of a hero, earn infamy by accepting gifts. I have always desired to perform virtuous acts on earth. What I have never done before, how shall I do it now and accept a gift?
