en: Thereupon, the officers of the king, in searching that hermitage, found the thieves with the stolen properties concealed there.

sn: ततः शङ्का समभवद् रक्षिणां तं मुनि प्रति। संयम्यैनं ततो राज्ञे दस्यूंश्चैव न्यवेदयन्॥
en: The suspicion of the guards fell upon the Rishi; they seized him with the thieves and brought him before the king.

sn: तं राजा सह तैश्चौरैरन्वशाद् वध्यतामिति। स रक्षिभिस्तैरज्ञात: शूले प्रोतो महातपाः॥
en: The king sentenced him along with the thieves. The guards, acting in ignorance, put the great Rishi also on the Shula (an instrument of death).

sn: ततस्ते शूलमारोप्य तं मुनि रक्षिणस्तदा। प्रतिजग्मुर्महीपालं धनान्यादाय तान्यथ॥
en: Having put them (the thieves) and the Rishi on an iron-spit, they returned to the king with the stolen property they had recovered.

sn: शूलस्थः स तु धर्मात्मा कालेन महता ततः। निराहारोऽपि विप्रर्षिर्मरणं नाभ्यपद्यत॥
en: Though the virtuous-minded Brahmana Rishi remained for many years on the Shula (iron-spit) without food, yet he did not die.

sn: धारयामास च प्राणानृषींश्च समुपानयत्। शूलाग्रे तप्यमानेन तपस्तेन महात्मना॥ संतापं परमं जग्मुर्मुनयस्तपसान्विताः। ते रात्रौ शकुना भूत्वा संनिपत्य तु भारत। दर्शयन्तो यथाशक्ति तमपृच्छन् द्विजोत्तमम्॥
en: The illustrious man, who was in deep Tapa, at the point of the Shula, kept up his life and brought other Rishis there by his ascetic power. O descendant of the Bharata race, they came in the night in the forms of birds; and seeing him engaged in Tapa (ascetic meditation), though fixed on the Shula, they were extremely aggrieved. Having shown themselves in their own forms, they asked that excellent Brahmana

sn: श्रोतुमिच्छामहे ब्रह्मन् किं पापं कृतवानसि। येनेह समनुप्राप्तं शूले दुःखभयं महत्॥
en: "O Brahmana, we desire to hear what is your sin for which you suffer this torture of being placed at the point of the Shula."

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततः स मुनिशार्दूलस्तानुवाच तपोधनान्। दोषतः कं गमिष्यामि न हि मेऽन्योऽपराध्यति॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Thereupon, that best of Rishis thus replied to the ascetics, "Whom shall I blame? None is to blame."

sn: तं दृष्ट्वा रक्षिणस्तत्र तथा बहुतिथेऽहनि। न्यवेदयंस्तथा राज्ञे यथावृत्तं नराधिप॥
en: O king, the guards, having seen him after many days in that state, told the king all that had happened.

sn: श्रुत्वा च वचनं तेषां निश्चित्य सह मन्त्रिभिः। प्रसादयामास तथा शूलस्थमृषिसत्तमम्॥
en: Having heard their words, the king after consulting with his ministers, gratified that excellent Rishi fixed on the Shula.

sn: राजोवाच यन्मयापकृतं मोहादज्ञानादृषिसत्तम। प्रसादये त्वां तत्राहं न मे त्वं क्रोद्भुमर्हसि।॥
en: The king said : O best of Rishis, I have offended you out of ignorance. I beseech you, pardon me. You should not be angry with me.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्तस्ततो राज्ञा प्रसादमकरोन्मुनिः। कृतप्रसादं राजा तं ततः समवतारयत्॥ अवतार्य च शूलाग्रात् तच्छूलं निश्चकर्ष ह। अशक्नुवंश्च निष्क्रष्टुं शूलं मूले च चिच्छिदे॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having been thus addressed by the king, the Rishi was gratified. Having thus gratified him, the king took down the Shula and tried to draw it out from him but he was unable to do it.

sn: स तथान्तर्गतेनैव शूलेन व्यतरन्मुनिः। तेनातितपसा लोकान् विजिग्ये दुर्लभान् परैः॥
en: The Rishi in that state with Shula practised the austerest penances and he thus conquered by his asceticism many regions difficult to be obtained.

sn: अणीमाण्डव इति च ततो लोकेषु गीयते। स गत्वा सदनं विप्रो धर्मस्य परमात्मवित्॥ आसनस्थं ततो धर्मं दृष्ट्वोपालभत प्रभुः। किं नु तद् दुष्कृतं कर्म मया कृतमजानता॥ यस्येयं फलनिर्वृत्तिरीदृश्यासादिता मया। शीघ्रमाचक्ष्व मे तत्त्वं पश्य मे तपसो बलम्॥
en: Therefore, he called earth Animandavya. That great truth-knowing Brahmana (one day) went to Dharma (the god of justice). Seeing the god seated on his seat, the lord (Rishi) asked him reproachingly, "What is the sinful act which has been committed unconsciously by me. For which I am suffering from this punishment? Tell me without delay and then see my ascetic power." was on

sn: धर्म उवाच पतङ्गिकानां पुच्छेषु त्वयेषीका प्रवेशिता। कर्मणस्तस्य ते प्राप्तं फलमेतत् तपोधन॥
en: Dharma said : O ascetic, a little insect was once pierced by you with a blade of grass; you now receive the fruit of your action.

sn: अणीमाण्डव्य उवाच अल्पेऽपराधेऽपि महान् मम दण्डस्त्वया कृतः। शूद्रयोनावतो धर्म मानुषः सम्भविष्यसि। मर्यादां स्थापयाम्यद्य लोके धर्मफलोदयाम्॥ आ चतुर्दशकाद् वर्षान्न भविष्यति पातकम्। परतः कुर्वतामेवं दोष एव भविष्यति॥
en: Animandavya said : You have inflicted upon me a great punishment for a little fault. Therefore o Dharma, you will be born as a man in the womb of a Shudra woman. I establish this rule today on earth in respect of the consequences of one's act that no sin will be committed in any act done by a man below the age of fourteen years. When committed only above that age, it will be sin.”

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एतेन त्वपराधेन शापात् तस्य महात्मनः। धर्मो विदुररूपेण शूद्रयोनावजायत॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Being cursed by that illustrious man for this fault, Dharma was born as Vidura in the womb of a Shudra woman.

sn: धर्मे चार्थे च कुशलो लोभक्रोधविवर्जितः। दीर्घदर्शी शमपरः कुरूणां च हिते रतः॥
en: He (Vidura) was learned in Dharma and Artha; he was free from avarice and anger; he was fore-seeing, tranquil in mind and ever engaged in doing good to the Kurus.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तेषु त्रिषु कुमारेषु जातेषु कुरुजाङ्गलम्। कुरवोऽथ कुरुक्षेत्रं त्रयमेतदवर्धत॥
en: Vaishampayana said : On the birth of these three sons (Dhritarashtra, Pandu and Vidura), Kurujangala, Kurukshetra and the Kurus grew in prosperity.

sn: ऊर्ध्वसस्याभवद् भूमिः सस्यानि रसवन्ति च। यथर्तुवर्षी पर्जन्यो बहुपुष्पफला दुमाः॥
en: The land gave abundant harvests and the crops were juicy. The clouds showered rains at proper time and the trees became full of fruits and flowers.

sn: वाहनानि प्रहृष्टानि मुदिता मृगपक्षिणः। गन्धवन्ति च माल्यानि रसवन्ति फलानि च।॥
en: The beasts of burdens were happy and the deer and the birds were exceedingly glad. The flowers became fragrant and the fruits became sweet.

sn: वणिम्भिश्चान्वकीर्यन्त नगराण्यथ शिल्पिभिः। शूराश्च कृतविद्याश्च सन्तश्च सुखिनोऽभवन्॥
en: The cities were filled with merchants and artisans; the people became brave, learned, honest and happy.

sn: नाभवन् दस्यवः केचिन्नाधर्मरुचयो जनाः। प्रदेशेष्वपि राष्ट्राणां कृतं युगमवर्तत॥
en: There were no thieves, there was none who was sinful. It seemed that Satyayuga had come over all parts of the kingdom.

sn: धर्मक्रिया यज्ञशीलाः सत्यव्रतपरायणाः। अन्योन्यप्रीतिसंयुक्ता व्यवर्धन्त प्रजास्तदा॥
en: The people were devoted to virtuous acts, sacrifices and the vow of the truth. Bearing love and affection for one another, they grew in prosperity.

sn: मानक्रोधविहीनाश्च नरा लोभविवर्जिताः। अन्योन्यमभ्यनन्दन्त धर्मोत्तरमवर्तत॥
en: They were free from pride, anger and covetousness; they took delight in sports which were perfectly innocent.

sn: तन्महोदधिवत् पूर्णं नगरं वै व्यरोचत। द्वारतोरणनिर्दूहैर्युक्तमध्चयोपमैः॥ प्रासादशतसम्बाधं महेन्द्रपुरसंनिभम्। नदीषु वनखण्डेषु वापीपल्वलसानुषु। काननेषु च रम्येषु विजहर्मुदिता जनाः॥
en: The holy city (Hastinapur) like the wide ocean, full of hundreds of palaces and mansions, possessing gates and arches and looking like dark clouds, appeared like the celestial capital of Indra. The people sported in great delight in the rivers, lakes, tanks, beautiful groves and woods.

sn: उत्तरैः कुरुभिः सार्धं दक्षिणा: कुरवस्तथा। विस्पर्धमाना व्यचरंस्तथा देवर्षिचारणैः॥
en: The Southern Kurus, in virtuous rivalry with the Northern Kurus, walked with the Devarshis and Charanas.

sn: नाभवत् कृपणः कश्चिन्नाभवन् विधवाः स्त्रियः। तस्मिञ्जनपदे रम्ये कुरुभिर्बहुलीकृते॥
en: None was there miserly and there was no woman who was a widow in that delightful country whose prosperity was thus increased by the Kurus.

sn: कूपारामसभावाप्यो ब्राह्मणावसथास्तथा। बभूवुः सर्वर्द्धियुतास्तस्मिन् राष्ट्रे सदोत्सवाः॥
en: The wells were full of water, the groves abounded with trees, the houses of Brahmanas were full of wealth and the whole kingdom was full of prosperity.

sn: भीष्मेण धर्मतो राजन् सर्वतः परिरक्षिते। बभूव रमणीयश्च चैत्ययूपशताङ्कितः॥
en: O king, thus virtuously ruled by Bhishma, the kingdom was adorned with hundreds of sacrificial stakes.

sn: स देशः परराष्ट्राणि विमृज्याभिप्रवर्धितः। भीष्मेण विहितं राष्ट्र धर्मचक्रमवर्तत॥
en: The wheel of virtue being thus set in motion by Bhishma, the country was full of increased population, people coming from other countries.

sn: क्रियमाणेषु कृत्येषु कुमाराणां महात्मनाम्। पौरजानपदाः सर्वे बभूवुः सततोत्सवाः॥
en: The citizens and the people were all filled with hope on seeing the achievements and behaviour of the youthful princes.

sn: गृहेषु कुरुमुख्यानां पौराणां च नराधिप। दीयतां भुज्यतां चेति वाचोऽश्रूयन्त सर्वशः॥
en: O king, in the house of the chief Kurus and in those of the people, "Give” “Eat” were the words that were constantly heard.

sn: धृतराष्ट्रश्च पाण्डुश्च विदुरश्च महामतिः। जन्मप्रभृति भीष्मेण पुत्रवत् परिपालिताः॥
en: Dhritarashtra, Pandu and Vidura were brought up from their birth by Bhishma, as if they were his own sons.

sn: संस्कारैः संस्कृतास्ते तु व्रताध्ययनसंयुताः। श्रमव्यायामकुशलाः समपद्यन्त यौवनम्॥
en: They passed through the usual rites of their order; they engaged themselves in study and vows; they grew up into youths, expert in athletic sports and labour.

sn: धनुर्वेदऽश्वपृष्ठे च गदायुद्धेऽसिचर्मणि। तथैव गजशिक्षायां नीतिशास्त्रेषु पारगाः॥
en: They became expert in archery, learned in the Veda, skillful in club-fight and in using sword and shield. They were experts in horsemanship and in the management of elephants; they were learned in the science off morality.

sn: इतिहासपुराणेषु नानाशिक्षासु बोधिताः। वेदवेदाङ्गतत्त्वज्ञाः सर्वत्र कृतनिश्चयाः॥
en: They were acquainted with history, Puranas and with many other branches of learning. They were well-acquainted with the mystery of the Vedas and the Vedangas. The knowledge they acquired was versatile and deep.

sn: पाण्डुर्धनुषि विक्रान्तो नरेष्वभ्यधिकोऽभवत्। अन्येभ्यो बलवानासीद् धृतराष्ट्रो महीपतिः॥
en: The greatly powerful Pandu excelled all men in the science of archery. The king Dhritarashtra excelled all men in personal strength.

sn: त्रिषु लोकेषु न त्वासीत् कश्चिद् विदुरसम्मितः। धर्मनित्यस्तथा राजन् धर्मे च परमं गतः॥
en: O king, there was none in the three worlds, who excelled Vidura in his devotion towards religion and virtue and in his knowledge of the science of morality.

sn: प्रणष्टं शन्तनोर्वंशं समीक्ष्य पुनरुद्धृतम्। ततो निर्वचनं लोके सर्वराष्ट्रेष्ववर्तत॥
en: On seeing the restoration of the extinct dynasty of Shantanu, the following saying became current over all countries.

sn: वीरसूनां काशिसुते देशानां कुरुजाङ्गलम्। सर्वधर्मविदां भीष्मः पुराणां गजसाह्वयम्॥ धृतराष्ट्रस्त्वचक्षुष्ट्वाद् राज्यं च प्रत्यपद्यत। पारसवत्वाद् विदुरो राजा पाण्डुर्बभूव ह॥
en: "Amongst the mothers of heroes, the daughter of the king of Kashi; among all countries, Kurujangalas; among all virtuous men, Bhishma; and among all cities, Hastinapur, are the foremost. Dhritarashtra did not get the kingdom, because he was blind; and Vidura also did not get it, because he was born of a Shudra woman, therefore Pandu became king.

sn: कदाचिदथ गाङ्गेय सर्वनीतिमतां वरः। विदुरं धर्मतत्त्वज्ञं वाक्यमाह यथोचितम्॥
en: One day the foremost of all statesmen, the learned in all the moral precepts, the son of Ganga (Bhishma), spoke to Vidura thus.

sn: भीष्म उवाच गुणैः समुदितं सम्यगिदं नः प्रथितं कुलम्। अत्यन्यान् पृथिवीपालान् पृविव्यामधिराज्यभाक्॥
en: Bhishma said : This our famous dynasty, endued with every virtue and accomplishment, has all along ruled over all other kings on earth.

sn: रक्षितं राजभिः पूर्वं धर्मविद्भिर्महात्मभिः। नोत्सादमगमचेदं कदाचिदिह नःकुलम्॥ मया च सत्यवत्या च कृष्णेन च महात्मना। समवस्थापितं भूयो युष्मासु कुलतन्तुषु॥
en: It was perpetuated by many virtuousminded and virtuously inclined kings. Satyavati, the illustrious Krishna (Dvaipayana) and myself, have raised you up in order that this our great dynasty may not be extinct.

sn: तचैतद् वर्धते भूयः कुलं सागरवद् यथा। तथा मया विधातव्यं त्वया चैव न संशयः॥
en: It is certainly your duty and mine to take such steps as our this dynasty may expand as the sea. we

sn: श्रूयते यादवी कन्या स्वानुरूपा कुलस्य नः। सुबलस्यात्मजा चैव तथा मद्रेश्वरस्य च॥
en: I have heard that the princess of the Yadavas, the daughter of Subala and the princess of Madra, are worthy of being allied to our dynasty.

sn: कुलीना रूपवत्यश्च ताः कन्याः पुत्र सर्वशः। उचिताश्चैव सम्बन्धे तेऽस्माकं क्षत्रियर्षभाः॥
en: O sons, all these maidens are the best of Kshatriyas; they are beautiful and of are birth; they are eminently fit for alliance with our family.

sn: मन्ये वरयितव्यास्ता इत्यहं धीमतां वर। संतानार्थं कुलस्यास्य यद् वा विदुर मन्यसे॥
en: O foremost of intelligent men, Vidura, I think should chose them for the perpetuation of our race. Tell me what you think.

sn: विदुर उवाच भवान् पिता भवान् माता भवान् नः परमो गुरुः। कुलस्यास्य विचार्य कुरु यद्धितम्॥
en: Vidura said: You are our father, you are our mother, you are our great preceptor. You yourself do what you think proper for the welfare of this dynasty.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच अथ शुश्राव विप्रेभ्यो गान्धारी सुबलात्मजाम्। आराध्य वरदं देवं भगनेत्रहरं हरम्॥ गान्धारी किल पुत्राणां शतं लेभे वरं शुभा। इति शुश्राव तत्त्वेन भीष्मः कुरुपितामहः॥ ततो गान्धारराजस्य प्रेषयामास भारत। अचक्षुरिति तत्रासीत् सुबलस्य विचारणा॥ तस्मात् स्वयं
en: Vaishampayana said: He (Bhishma) heard from the Brahmanas that the daughter of Subala, Gandhari, had received a boon by worshipping the destroyer of eyes of Bhaga, the boon-giving deity Hara (Shibi). The amiable, Gandhari would get one hundred sons. Having heard this, the grandsire of the Kurus, Bhishma, sent messengers to the king of Gandhara. O descendant of the Bharata race, (king) Subala hesitated on account of the blindness (of the bridegroom).

sn: कुलं ख्यातिं च वृत्तं च बुद्ध्या तु प्रसमीक्ष्य सः। ददौ तां धृतराष्ट्राय गान्धारी धर्मचारिणीम्॥
en: But taking into consideration the noble blood, the fame and the conduct of the Kurus, he bestowed the virtuous Gandhari on Dhritarashtra.

sn: गान्धारी त्वथ सुश्राव धृतराष्ट्रमचक्षुषम्। आत्मानं दित्सितं चास्मै पित्रा मात्रा च भारत॥ ततः सा पट्टमादाय कृत्वा बहुगुणं तदा। बबन्ध नेत्रे स्वे राजन् पतिव्रतपरायणा॥ नाभ्यसूयां पतिमहमित्येवं कृतनिश्चया। ततो गान्धारराजस्य पुत्रः शकुनिरभ्ययात्॥ स्वसारं वयसा लक्ष्या युक्तामादाय कौरवान्। तां तदा धृतराष्ट्राय ददौ परमसत्कृताम्। भीष्मस्यानुमते चैव विवाहं समकारयत्॥
en: O descendant of the Bharata race, having heard of the blindness of Dhritarashtra and that her parents had consented to bestow her (Gandhari) upon him. O king, ever-devoted to her husband, (Gandhari) bandaged her own eyes with cloth, gathered into many folds, out of her desire that she would not be wanting in respect and love for her husband. Thereupon, the son of the king of Gandhara, Shakuni bringing his beautiful and young and wellbehaved sister to the Kurus, formally gave her to Dhritarashtra.

sn: दत्त्वा स भगिनीं वीरो यथार्ह च परिच्छदम्। पुनरायात् स्वनगरं भीष्मेण प्रतिपूजितः॥
en: The nuptials were solemnised with the permission of Bhishma. The hero (Shakuni), giving away his sister with (many valuable) robes, returned to his own capital, after being duly worshipped by Bhishma.

sn: गान्धार्यपि वरारोहा शीलाचारविचेष्टितैः। तुष्टिं कुरूणां सर्वेषां जनयामास भारत॥
en: O descendant of the Bharata race, the beautiful Gandhari pleased all the Kurus by her behaviour and respectful attentions.

sn: वृत्तेनाराध्य तान् सर्वान् गुरून् पतिपरायणा। वाचापि पुरुषानन्यान् सुव्रता नान्वकीर्तयत्॥
en: She, ever-devoted to her husband, pleased her superiors by her good conduct and vowobserving as she was, she never referred to other men even in words.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच शूरो नाम यदुश्रेष्ठो वसुदेवपिताभवत्। तस्य कन्या पृथा नाम रूपेणाप्रतिमा भुवि॥
en: Vaishampayana said: There was a chief among the Yadus, named Shura, who was the father of Vasudeva. His daughter was named Pritha, she was matchless in beauty on earth.

sn: पितृष्वस्रीयाय स तामनपत्याय भारत। अग्यमग्रे प्रतिज्ञाय स्वस्यापत्य स सत्यवाक्॥ अग्रजामथ तां कन्यां शूरोऽनुग्रहकांक्षिणे। प्रददौ कुन्तिभोजाय सखा सख्ये महात्मने।॥
en: O descendant of the Bharata race, that truthful man (Shura) give his first born child to the son of his paternal aunt, his childless cousin and favour seeking friend, the high-souled Kuntibhoja, according to a promise given before.

sn: सा नियुक्ता पितुर्गेह देवतातिथिपूजने। उग्रं पर्यचरत् तत्र ब्राह्मणं संशितव्रतम्॥ निगूढनिश्चयं धर्मे यं तं दुर्वाससं विदुः। तमुग्रं संशितात्मानं सर्वयत्नैरतोषयत्॥
en: She (Pritha) was appointed as her (adoptive) father's house to look after the hospitality to the Brahmanas and guests. One day by careful attentions she gratified the terrible Brahmana of rigid vows, known by the name of Durvasa, learned in the mystery of religion.

sn: तस्यै स प्रददौ मन्त्रमापद्धर्मान्ववेक्षया। अभिचाराभिसंयुक्तमब्रवीच्चैव तां मुनिः॥
en: Anticipating the future difficulty of her getting sons, he (Durvasa) taught her a Mantra for invoking any of the celestials (she liked for growing her children). The Rishi then said to her.

sn: यं यं देवं त्वमेतेन मन्त्रेणावाहयिष्यसि। तस्य तस्य प्रसादेन तव पुत्रो भविष्यति॥
en: “Through the effulgence of those celestial whom you will invoke by this Mantra, offspring will be certainly begotten on you”.

sn: तथोक्ता सा तु विप्रेण कुन्ती कौतुहलान्विता। कन्या सती देवमर्कमाजुहाव यशस्विनी॥
en: Having been thus told by the Brahmana, (Durvasa) the illustrious Kunti (Pritha), being curious, invoked in her maidenhood the god Arka (Sun).

sn: सा ददर्श तमायान्तं भास्करं लोकभावनम्। विस्मिता चानवद्याङ्गी दृष्ट्वा तन्महदद्भुतम्॥
en: She immediately saw (before her) that effulgent deity (Sun), that beholder of everything in the world. Seeing the wonderful sight, that maiden of fruitless feature was very much surprised.

sn: तां समासाद्य देवस्तु विवस्वानिदमब्रवीत्। अयमस्म्यसितापाङ्गि ब्रूहि किं करवाणि ते॥
en: The deity Vivasvan (Sun), coming to her said, “O black-eyed lady, here I am. Tell me what I can do for you."

sn: कुन्त्युवाच कश्चिन्मे ब्राह्मणः प्रादाद्वरं विद्यां च शत्रुहन्। तद्विजिज्ञासयाऽऽह्वानं कृतवत्यस्मि ते विभो॥
en: Kunti said: O slayer of foes, a certain Brahmana gave। me this science (Mantra). O Lord, I have invoked you, only to see the efficacy of the Mantra.

sn: एतस्मिन्नपराधे त्वां शिरसाहं प्रसादये। योषितो हि सदा रक्ष्याः स्वापराद्धापि नित्यशः॥
en: For my this fault, I bow down my head to you to ask for your grace. A woman, however guilty, deserves protection.”

sn: सूर्य उवाच वेदाहं सर्वमेवैतद्यदुर्वासा वरं ददौ। संत्यज्य भयमेवेह क्रियतां संगमो मम॥
en: The Sun said: I know Durvasa has given you this boon. Cast off your fears and allow me your embrace.

sn: अमोघं दर्शनं मह्यमाहूतश्चास्मि ते शुभे। वृथाह्यानेऽपि ते भीरु दोषः स्यान्नात्र संशयः॥
en: O amiable girl, my approach is infallible; it must be fruitful. O timid maiden, if my coming be for nothing, it will be certainly a transgression of yours.”

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्ता बहुविधं सान्त्वपूर्वं विवस्वता। सा तु नैच्छद्वरारोहा कन्याहमिति भारत॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Vivasvat thus spoke to her many things to allay her fears. O descendant of the Bharata race, the illustrious and beautiful girl, as she was a maid.

sn: बन्धुपक्षभयादीता लज्जया च यशस्विनी। तामर्कः पुनरेवेदमब्रवीद्भरतर्षभ॥
en: Did not grant his request from modesty and from the fear of her relatives. O best of the Bharata race, Arka again addressed her thus.

sn: मत्प्रसादान ते राज्ञि भविता दोष इत्युत। एवमुक्त्वा स भगवान्कुन्तिराजसुतां तदा॥
en: "O princess, there will be no sin in gratifying me." Having said this to the daughter of Kuntibhoja, that illustrious deity.

sn: प्रकाशकर्ता तपनः संबभूव तया सह। आमुक्तकवचः श्रीमान्देवगर्भः श्रियान्वितः॥ सहजं कवचं बिभ्रत्कुण्डलो द्योतिताननः। अजायत सुतः कर्णः सर्वलोकेषु विश्रुतः॥
en: That illuminator of the universe, Tapana (Sun) received her embraces. Thereupon was born a hero, known all over the world by the name of Karna, the foremost of all wielders of arms, encased in a natural armour, blessed with good fortune and endued with celestial beauty and all auspicious marks and with a face brightened by ear-rings.

sn: प्रादाच्च तस्यै कन्यात्वं पुनः स परमद्युतिः। दत्वा च तपतां श्रेष्ठो दिवमाचक्रमे ततः॥
en: The greatly effulgent Tapana, then giving Pritha her maiden-hood, again went to heaven.

sn: दृष्ट्वा कुमारं जातं सा वार्ष्णेयी दीनमानसा। एकाग्रं चिन्तयामास किं कृत्वा सुकृतं भवेत्॥
en: The princess of the Vrishni race (Pritha) became affected with sorrow to see the birth of the child. She intently reflected on the course she should adopt.

sn: गृहमानापचारं सा बन्धुपक्षभयात्तदा। उत्ससर्ज कुमारं तं जले कुन्ती महाबलम्॥
en: She resolved to conceal her frailty from the fear of her friends and relatives. Kunti threw her that powerful son into water.

sn: तमुत्सृष्टं जले गर्भं राधाभर्ता महायशाः। पुत्रत्वे कल्पयामास सभार्यः सूतनन्दनः॥
en: The illustrious husband of Radha took up that child thrown into the water. That son of Suta, (the husband of Radha), with his wife brought him up as their son.

sn: नामधेयं च चक्राते तस्य बालस्य तावुभौ। वसुना सह जातोऽयं वसुषेणो भवत्विति॥
en: They gave that son the name of Vasusena, because he was born with wealth, (a natural armour and ear-rings).

sn: स वर्धमानो बलवान्सर्वास्त्रेषुद्यतोऽभवत्। आ पृष्ठतापादादित्यमुपातिष्ठत वीर्यवान्॥
en: He grew up very strong and became expert in all weapons. Possessed of great energy, he worshipped the Sun until his back was scorched by its rays.

sn: तस्मिन्काले तु जपतस्तस्य वीरस्य धीमतः। नादेयं ब्राह्मणेष्वासीत्किंचिदृसु महीतले॥
en: When he was thus engaged in his worship, there was nothing on earth that the heroic and intelligent Vasusena would not give to Brahmanas.

sn: तमिन्द्रो ब्राह्मणो भूत्वा भिक्षार्थी समुपागमत्। कुण्डले प्रार्थयामास कवचं च महाद्युतिः॥
en: Indra, assuming the form of a Brahmana, came to him for alms. Ever engaged to do good to Arjuna, he asked for the armour.

sn: स्वशरीरात् समुत्कृत्य कवचं स्वं निसर्गजम्। कर्णस्तु कुण्डले छित्त्वा प्रायच्छत् स कृताञ्जलिः।।
en: Taking off the natural armour from his body, Karna with joined hands gave it to Indra in the form of a Brahmana.

sn: प्रतिगृह्य तु देवेशस्तुष्टस्तेनास्य कर्मणा। ददौ शक्तिं सुरपतिर्वाक्यं चेदमुवाच ह॥
en: The king of the celestials received the gift and he was exceedingly pleased with his liberality. The lord of the celestials gave him a weapon, saying.

sn: देवासुरमनुष्याणां गन्धर्वोरंगरक्षसाम्। यमेकं जेतुमिच्छेथाः सोऽन्या न भविष्यति॥
en: "Among the celestials, the Asuras, the Gandharvas, the Nagas and the Rakshasas, whoever you will desire to conquer he will certainly be killed by this weapon.

sn: प्राङ्नाम तस्य कथितं वसुषेण इति क्षितौ। को वैकर्तनश्चैव कर्मणा तेन सोऽभवत्॥
en: The son of Surya was known by the name of Vasushena, but after his cutting off his natural armour, he was called Karna (cutter).

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच सत्त्वरूपगुणोपेता धर्मारामा महाव्रता। दुहिता कुन्तिभोजस्य पृथा पृथुलोचना॥
en: Vaishampayana said : The daughter of Kuntibhoja, Pritha, had large eyes; she was endued with beauty and every accomplishment; she was of rigid vows, devoted to virtue; and she possessed every good quality.

sn: तां तु तेजस्विनी कन्यां रूपयौवनशालिनीम्। व्यवृण्वन्पार्थिवाः केचिदतीव स्त्रीगुणैर्युताम्॥
en: But through the maiden was effulgent and possessed beauty and all womanly qualifications and youth, yet no king sought for her hand.

sn: ततः सा कुन्तिभोजेन राज्ञाऽऽहूय नराधिपान्। पित्रा स्वयंवरे दत्ता दुहिता राजसत्तम॥
en: O best of kings, thereupon, the king Kuntibhoja invited all the monarchs and offered her in a Svyamvara.

sn: ततः सा रङ्गमध्यस्थं तेषां राज्ञां मनस्विनी। ददर्श राजशार्दूलं पाण्डुं भरतसत्तमम्॥
en: The intelligent Kunti saw that best of kings, the foremost of the Bharata race, Pandu, in the assembly of the kings.

sn: सिंहदर्यं महोरस्कं वृषभाक्षं महाबलम्। आदित्यमिव सर्वेषां राज्ञां प्रच्छाद्य वै प्रभाः॥
en: Proud as the lion, broad-chested, bulleyed, greatly strong, like sun outshining all the kings in splendour.

sn: तिष्ठन्तं राजसमितौ पुरंदरमिवापरम्। तं दृष्ट्वा सानवद्यागी कुन्तिभोजसुता शुभा॥ पाण्डुं नरवरं रङ्गे हृदयेनाकुलाभवत्। ततः कामपरीताङ्गी सकृत्प्रचलमानसा॥
en: He (Pandu) looked among the kings as the second Indra. In the assembly that best of men, Pandu, having seen the maiden of faultless feature, the amiable daughter of Kuntibhoja, became very much agitated in mind.

sn: व्रीडमाना स्रजं कुन्ती राज्ञः स्कन्धे समासृजत्। तं निशम्य वृतं पाण्डु कुन्त्या सर्वे नराधिपाः॥ यथागतं समाजग्मुर्गजैरश्वैः रथैस्तथा। ततस्तस्याः पिता राजन्विवाहमकरोत्प्रभुः॥
en: Kunti advanced in modesty, quivering with emotion and placed the nuptial garland round the neck of the king (Pandu). Finding that Kunti had chosen Pandu, the other kings returned to their kingdoms on elephants, on horses and cars on which they had come. O king, her father then performed the nuptial rites in due form.

sn: स तया कुन्तिभोजस्य दुहित्रा कुरुनन्दनः। युयुजेऽमितसौभाग्य: पौलोम्या मघवानिव॥
en: The descendant of Kuru (Pandu) and the daughter of Kuntibhoja (Kunti) blessed with great and good fortune, formed a couple like Indra and Sachi.

sn: कुन्त्याः पाण्डोश्च राजेन्द्र कुन्तिभोजो महीपतिः। कृत्वोद्वाहं तदा तं तु नानावसुभिरर्चितम्। स्वपुरं प्रेषयामास स राजा कुरुसत्तम॥ ततो बलेन महता नानाध्वजपताकिना। स्तूयमानः स चाशीर्भिर्ब्राह्मणैश्च महर्षिभिः॥ संप्राप्य नगरं राजा पाण्डुः कौरवनन्दनः। न्यवेशयत तां भार्यां कुन्तीं स्वभवने प्रभुः॥
en: O king, Kuntibhoja, after the marriage of Kunti presented the bridegroom with much wealth. O best of the Kuru race, the king (Kuntibhoja) then sent him (Pandu) to his own capital. Accompanied by a large force, bearing various kinds of banners and pennons and eulogised and blessed by many Brahmanas and great Rishis. The descendant of Kuru, king Pandu, reached his own capital and that lord (Pandu) established his wife Kunti there.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततः शान्तनवो भीष्मो राज्ञः पाण्डोर्यशस्विनः। विवाहस्यापरस्यार्थे चकार मतिमान् मतिम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Some time after, the son of Shantanu, the intelligent Bhishma, thought of marrying Pandu to a second wife.

sn: सोऽमात्यैः स्थविरैः सार्धं ब्राह्मणैश्च महर्षिभिः। बलेन चतुरङ्गेण ययौ मद्रपतेः पुरम्॥
en: Accompanied by the aged ministers Brahmanas and great Rishis and with a force of the four kinds he went to the capital of the king of Madra.

sn: तमागतमभिश्रुत्य भीष्मं वाह्रीकपुङ्गवः। प्रत्युद्गम्यार्चयित्वा च पुरं प्रावेशयन्नृपः॥
en: That best of Valhikas (the king of Madra), having heard of his coming, went out to receive him with all honour; and that king (Bhishma) also entered his capital.

sn: दत्त्वा तस्यासनं शुभं पाद्यमर्थ्य तथैव च। मधुपर्कं च मद्रेशः पप्रच्छागमनेऽर्थिताम्॥
en: The king of Madra, having given him a white seat, water for washing his feet and Arghya, asked the reason of his coming.

sn: तं भीष्मः प्रत्युवाचेदं मद्रराजं कुरूद्वहः। आगतं मां विजानीहि कन्यार्थिनमरिन्दम॥
en: The supporter of the Kurus' honour, Bhishma replied to the king of Madra," chastiser of foes, know that I have come for a maiden.

sn: श्रूयते भवतः साध्वी स्वसा माद्री यशस्विनी। तामहं वरयिष्यामि पाण्डोरर्थे यशस्विनीम्॥
en: We have heard that you have an illustrious and chaste sister, named Madri. I chose that illustrious maiden for Pandu.

sn: युक्तरूपो हि सम्बन्धे त्वं नो राजन् वयं तव। एतत् संचिन्त्य मद्रेश गृहाणास्मान् यथाविधि॥
en: O king, you are in every way worthy of alliance with us. We also are worthy of you. O king of Madra, considering all this, accept us in from."

sn: तमेवंवादिनं भीष्मं प्रत्यभाषत मद्रपः। न हि मेऽन्यो वरस्त्वत्तः श्रेयानिति मतिर्मम॥
en: Having been thus addressed by Bhishma, the king of Madra replied, "To my mind there is no other better bridegroom than one of your family.

sn: पूर्वैः प्रवर्तितं किंचित् कुलेऽस्मिन् नृपसत्तमैः। साधु वा यदि वासाधु तन्नातिक्रान्तमुत्सहे॥
en: But there is a custom in our family ever observed by all the best of our kings. Be it good or bad, I can not transgress it.

sn: व्यक्तं तद् भवतश्चापि विदितं नात्र संशयः। न च युक्तं तथा वक्तुं भवान् देहीति सत्तम॥
en: It (this custom) is well known and there is no doubt that it is also known to you. O the proper excellent man, therefore, it is not proper for you to say "Bestow your sister.”

sn: कुलधर्मः स नो वीर प्रमाणं परमं च तत्। तेन त्वां न ब्रवीम्येतदसंदिग्धं वचोऽरिहन्॥
en: O hero, it is our family custom to receive tribute. Therefore, I cannot give you any . assurance in the matter of your request.'

sn: तं भीष्मः प्रत्युवाचेदं मद्रराजं जनाधिपः। धर्म एष परो राजन् स्वयमुक्तः स्वयम्भुवा॥
en: The king Bhishma thus replied to the king of Madra, "O king, this is a great virtue; the self created (Brahma) has himself said it.

sn: नात्र कश्चन दोषोऽस्ति पूर्वैर्विधिरयं कृतः। विदितेयं च ते शल्य मर्यादा साधुसम्मता॥
en: Your ancestors have observed this custom. There is no fault to be found with it. O Salya, it is well known that this custom has the approbation of the wise."

sn: इत्युक्त्वा स महातेजाः शातकुम्भं कृताकृतम्। रत्नानि च विचित्राणि शल्यायादात् सहस्रशः॥ गजानश्वान् रथांश्चैव वासांस्याभरणानि च। मणिमुक्ताप्रवालं च गाङ्गेयो व्यसृजच्छुभम्॥
en: Having said this, that greatly effulgent son of Ganga (Bhishma) gave Salya much gold, both coined and uncoined, precious stones of various colors, elephants, horses and cars, much cloth and many ornaments, many gems, pearls and corals.

sn: तत् प्रगृह्य धनं सर्वं शल्यः सम्प्रीतमानसः। ददौ तां समलंकृत्य स्वसारं कौरवर्षभे॥
en: Salya receive all these wealth in delightful health and gave away his sister decked with ornaments, to that lion of the Kuru race.

sn: स तां माद्रीमुपादाय भीष्मः सागरगासुतः। आजगाम पुरीं धीमान् प्रविष्टो गजसाह्वयम्॥
en: The son of ocean going Ganga, intelligent Bhishma, taking Madri with him, returned to the capital, named after the elephant (Hastinapur).

sn: तत इष्टेऽहनि प्राप्ते मुहूर्ते साधुसम्मते। जग्राह विधिवत् पाणिं मात्र्याः पाण्डुराधिपः॥
en: The king Pandu, on an auspicious day and at the time indicated by the wise accepted the hands of Madri in due form.

sn: ततो विवाहे निवृत्ते स राजा कुरुनन्दनः। स्थापयामास तां भार्यां शुभे वेश्मनि भाविनीम्॥
en: After the completion of the marriage, that king, the descendant of the Kuru race, established his beautiful wife in handsome mansions.

sn: स ताभ्यां व्यचरत् सार्धं भार्याभ्यां राजसत्तमः। कुन्त्या माझ्या च राजेन्द्रो यथाकामं यथासुखम्॥
en: O king of kings, that best of kings (Pandu) then give himself up to enjoyments with his two wives, Kunti and Madri, at will and at pleasure.

sn: ततः स कौरवो राजा विहृत्य त्रिदशा निशाः। जिगीषया महीं पाण्डुनिरक्रामत् पुरात् प्रभो॥
en: O king, when thirty days had passed away that Kuru king, the lord Pandu, started from his capital to conquer the world.

sn: स भीष्मप्रमुखान् वृद्धानभिवाद्य प्रणम्य च। धृतराष्ट्रं च कौरव्यं तथान्यान् कुरुसत्तमान्। आमन्त्र्य प्रययौ राजा तैश्चैवाप्यनुमोदितः॥ मङ्गलाचारयुक्ताभिराशीभिरभिनन्दितः। गजवाजिरथौघेन बलेन महतागमत्॥ स राजा देवगर्भाभो विजिगीषुर्वसुंधराम्। हृष्टपुष्टबलैः प्रायात् पाण्डुः शत्रूननेकशः॥
en: After saluting and bowing to Bhishma and other elders and bidding adieu to Dhritarashtra and other best of the Kurus, receiving their permission and performing all auspicious rites, the king (Pandu) set out on his great campaign blessed by all around and accompanied by a great army of elephants, horses and cars. That celestial like king was desirous of conquering the whole earth.

sn: पूर्वमागस्कृतो गत्वा दशार्णाः समरे जिताः। पाण्डुना नरसिंहेन कौरवाणां यशोभृता।२५॥
en: Pandu marched against the enemies with such strong forces (as narrated above). Going to the east, that best of men, that spreader of Kuru fame, Pandu, defeated the Dasharnas.

sn: ततः सेनामुपादाय पाण्डुर्नानाविधध्वजाम्। प्रभूतहस्त्यश्वयुतां पदातिरथसंकुलाम्॥ आगस्कारी महीपानां बहूनां बलदर्पितः। गोप्ता मगधराष्ट्रस्य दीर्घो राजगृहे हतः॥
en: Pandu then with his army of innumerable elephants, cavalry, infantry and charioteers and various colored banners. Marched against Dirgha, the king of Magadha, who being proud of his strength, had offended many kings. Attacking him in his capital, Rajgriha, he killed him.

sn: ततः कोशं समादाय वाहनानि च भूरिशः। पाण्डुना मिथिलां गत्वा विदेहाः समरे जिताः॥
en: Taking possession of his treasury and many beasts of burden Pandu, went to Mithila and conquered the Videha in battle.

sn: तथा काशिषु सुह्येषु पुण्ड्रेषु च नरर्षभ। स्वबाहुबलवीर्येण कुरूणामकरोद् यशः॥
en: O best of men, he then conquered Kashi, Sumha and Pundra; and by the strength of his prowess he spread the fame of the Kurus.

sn: तं शरोधमहाज्वालं शस्त्रार्चिषमरिन्दमम्। पाण्डुपावकमासाद्य व्यदह्यन्त नराधिपाः॥
en: The kings were burnt by the far reaching flames, represented by his arrows and the splendour of his weapons, of the great fire represented by that chastiser of foes, Pandu.

sn: ते ससेनाः ससेनेन निध्वंसितबला नृपाः। पाण्डुना वशगाः कृत्वा कुरुकर्मसु योजिताः॥
en: Pandu defeated with his army the kings with their forces; he kept them engaged in the works of the Kurus.

sn: तेन ते निर्जिताः सर्वे पृथिव्यां सर्वपार्थिवाः। तमेकं मेनिरे शूरं देवेष्विव पुरंदरम्॥
en: Having been thus defeated by him, all the kings of the world recognised him as the only hero on earth as Indra is among the celestial.

sn: कृताञ्जलयः सर्वे प्रणता वसुधाधिपाः। उपाजग्मुर्धनं गृह्य रत्नानि विविधानि च॥
en: All the kings of the world bowed to him with joined hands and they waited upon him with presents of various kinds of gems and wealth.

sn: तं तदादाय ययौ मणिमुक्ताप्रवालं च सुवर्णं रजतं बहु। गोरत्नान्यश्वरत्नानि रथरत्नानि कुञ्जरान्॥ खरोष्ट्रमहिषीश्चैव यच्च किंचिदजाविकम्। कम्बलाजिनरत्नानि रारूवास्तरणानि च। तत् सर्वं प्रतिजग्राह राजा नागपुराधिपः॥
en: Precious stones, pearls, corals, much gold and silver, the jewels of cows and horses, elephants and cars. Asses, camels, buffaloes, goats and sheep, blankets and beautiful birds and carpets made of the skin of Ranku. Having taken them all, the king of Hastinapur.

sn: पाण्डुः पुनर्मुदितवाहनः। हर्षयिष्यन् स्वराष्ट्राणि पुरं च गजसाह्वयम्॥
en: Pandu, returned to his own capital Hastinapur to the great delight of all his subjects and citizens.

sn: शन्तनो राजसिंहस्य भरतस्य च धीमतः। प्रणष्टः कीर्तिजः शब्दः पाण्डुना पुनराहृतः॥
en: O the lion of kings, the fame of Shantanu and that of Bharata, was about to be extinct, but it was now revived by Pandu.

sn: ये पुरा कुरुराष्ट्राणि जहः कुरुधनानि च। ते नागपुरसिंहेन पाण्डुना करदीकृताः॥
en: They, who robbed the Kurus before of both territory and wealth, were now forced by Pandu, the lion of Hastinapur, to pay tributes."

sn: इत्यभाषन्त राजानो राजामात्याश्च संगताः। प्रतीतमनसो हृष्टाः पौरजानपदैः सह॥
en: Thus said in joyful heart the kings with their ministers and with the citizens and people.

sn: प्रत्युद्ययुश्च तं प्राप्तं सर्वे भीष्मपुरोगमाः। ते नदूरमिवाध्वानं गत्वा नागपुरालयात्॥ आवृतं ददृशशुहष्टा लोकं बहुविधैर्धनैः। नानायानसमानीतै रत्नैरुच्चावचैस्तदा॥ हस्त्यश्वरथरत्नैश्च गोभिरुष्ट्रैस्तथादिभिः। नान्तं ददृशुरासाद्य भीष्मेण सह कौरवाः॥
en: All the Kurus with Bhishma at their head went out to receive him when he was near Hastinapur. They saw in delight the attendants of the king (Pandu), laden with much wealth; the train of various conveyances, of elephants, horses, cars, kine, camels and other animals laden with all kinds of wealth was so long that they could not find its end.

sn: सोऽभिवाद्य पितुः पादौ कौसल्यानन्दवर्धनः। यथार्ह मानयामास पौरजानपदानपि॥
en: Then the dweller of Kausalya's joy, (Pandu), worshipped the feet of his father (uncle) Bhishma and then saluted the citizens and others as each deserved.

sn: प्रमृद्य परराष्ट्राणि कृतार्थं पुनरागतम्। पुत्रमाश्लिष्य भीष्मस्तु हर्षादश्रुण्यवर्तयत्॥
en: Bhishma also shed tears of joy and embraced his son who had returned victorious after subjugating many kingdoms of others.

sn: स तूर्यशतशङ्खानां भेरीणां च महास्वनैः। हर्षयन् सर्वशः पौरान विवेश गजसाह्वयम्॥
en: And he (Pandu), instilling joy into the hearts of his people, entered Hastinapur in a flourish of hundreds of trumpets and bugles,

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच धृतराष्ट्राभ्यनुज्ञातः स्वबाहुविजितं धनम्। भीष्माय सत्यवत्यै च मात्रे चोपजहार सः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : He (Pandu), at the command of Dhritarashtra, offered the wealth acquired by the prowess of his arms of Bhishma, to Satyavati and to their mother (Kausalya).

sn: विदुराय च वै पाण्डुः प्रेषयामास तद् धनम्। सुहृदश्चापि धर्मात्मा धनेन समतर्पयत्॥
en: Pandu sent a portion of the wealth to Vidura. The virtuous minded man (Pandu) gratified his friends and relatives with (the presents of) wealth.

sn: ततः सत्यवती भीष्मं कौसल्यां च यशस्विनीम्। शुभैः पाण्डुजितैरथै स्तोषयामास भारत॥
en: The descendant of Bharata, (Pandu) gratified Satyavati, Bhishma and the illustrious and amiable princess of Kausalya with the wealth, acquired by his prowess of arms.

sn: ननन्द माता कौसल्या तमप्रतिमतेजसम्। जयन्तमिव पौलोमी परिष्वज्य नरर्षभम्॥
en: Kausalya, in embracing her son of matchless prowess became as glad as Sachi on embracing Jayanta (her son).

sn: तस्य वीरस्य विक्रान्तैः सहस्रशतदक्षिणैः। अश्वमैधशतैरीजे धृतराष्ट्रो महामखैः॥
en: Dhritarashtra performed with the wealth acquired by that hero five great sacrifices, in which offerings were made to the Brahmanas by hundreds and thousands and in which so much wealth was spent as would have been sufficient for one hundred Horse sacrifices.

sn: सम्प्रयुक्तस्तु कुन्त्या च माद्र्या च भरतर्षभ। जिततन्द्रीस्तदा पाण्डुर्बभूव वनगोचरः॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, some time after, Pandu, who had mastered over his senses, retired into a forest with (his wives) Kunti and Madri.

sn: हित्वा प्रासादनिलयं शुभानि शयनानि च। अरण्यनित्यः सततं बभूव मृगयापरः॥
en: He left his excellent palace and its luxurious bed. He lived always in the forest, being ever engaged in hunting.

sn: स चरन् दक्षिणं पार्श्व रम्यं हिमवतो गिरेः। उवास गिरिपृष्ठेषु महाशालवनेषु च॥
en: He lived in a delightful and hilly region over grown with huge Shala trees on the southern slope of the Himalayas where he roamed freely.

sn: रराज कुन्त्या मात्र्या च पाण्डुः सह वने चरन्। करेण्वोरिव मध्यस्थः श्रीमान् पौरंदरो गजः॥
en: The handsome Pandu roamed in the forest with Kunti and Madri like Airavata with two female elephants.

sn: भारतं सह भार्याभ्यां खड्गबाणधनुर्धरम्। विचित्रकवचं वीरं परमास्त्रविदं नृपम्। देवोऽयमित्यमन्यन्त चरन्तं वनवासिनः॥ तस्य कामांश्च भोगांश्च नरा नित्यमतन्द्रिताः। उपाजहुर्वनान्तेषु धृतराष्ट्रेण चोदिताः॥
en: The dwellers of (that) forest regarded the heroic Bharata prince with his two wives, (Pandu), armed with swords, arrows and bows and encased in beautiful armour, as a god wandering amongst them. The people were busy in supplying every object of pleasure and enjoyment to him in his retirement at the command of Dhritarashtra.

sn: अथ पारशवीं कन्यां देवकस्य महीपतेः। रूपयौवनसम्पन्नां स शुश्रावायगासुतः॥
en: The son of the river (Bhishma) heard that king Devaka had a daughter, young and beautiful, born in a Shudra wife.

sn: ततस्तु वरयित्वा तामानीय भरतर्षभः। विवाहं कारयामास विदुरस्य महामतेः॥
en: The best of the Bharata race (Bhishma) brought her from her father's abode and he married her to the high minded Vidura.

sn: तस्यां चोत्पादयामास विदुरः कुरुनन्दनः। पुत्रान् विनयसम्पन्नानात्मनः सदृशान् गुणैः॥
en: The descendant of Kuru, Vidura, begot on her children as gentle and accomplished as he himself was.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततः पुत्रशतं जज्ञे गान्धार्यां जनमेजय। धृतराष्ट्रस्य वैश्यायामेकश्चापि शतात् परः॥
en: Vaishampayana said: O Janamejaya, one hundred sons of Dhritarashtra were born in the womb of Gandhari. Besides these one hundred sons, one more was born by a Vaishya wife.

sn: पाण्डोः कुन्त्यां च मात्र्यां च पुत्राः पञ्च महारथाः। देवेभ्यः समपद्यन्त संतानाय कुलस्य
en: Pandu had by his wives) Kunti and Madri five sons, all great car warriors, who were all begotten by celestial for the perpetuation of the (Kuru) dynasty.

sn: जनमेजय उवाच कथं पुत्रशतं जज्ञे गान्धार्यां द्विजसत्तम। कियता चैव कालेन तेषामायुश्च किं परम्॥ वै॥
en: Janamejaya said : O best of the twice born, why did Gandhari give birth to one hundred sons? In how many years (they were born)? What was their period of life?

sn: कथं चैकः स वैश्यायां धृतराष्ट्रसुतोऽभवत्। कथं च सदृशी भार्यां गान्धारी धर्मचारिणीम्॥ आनुकूल्ये वर्तमानां धृतराष्ट्रोऽभ्यवर्तत।
en: How did Dhritarashtra beget a son on a Vaishya wife? How did Dhritarashtra behave towards his loving, obedient and virtuous wife, Gandhari?

sn: कथं च शप्तस्य सतः पाण्डोस्तेन महात्मना।॥ समुत्पन्ना दैवतेभ्यः पुत्राः पञ्च महारथाः। एतद् विद्वन् यथान्यायं विस्तरेण तपोधन॥
en: How were born the five sons of Pandu, those great car warriors, through cursed by the high-souled man (the Rishi in the form of deer)?

sn: कथयस्व न मे तृप्तिः कथ्यमानेषु बन्धुषु।
en: O ascetic, tell me all this in detail. I am not satiated with hearing the accounts of my friends and relatives.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच क्षुच्छ्रमाभिपरिग्लानं द्वैपायनमुपस्थितम्॥ तोषयामास गान्धारी व्यासस्तस्यै वरं ददौ।
en: Vaishampayana said : One day Gandhari gratified Dvaipayana who came hungry and fatigued. Vyasa granted her a boon.

sn: सा वब्रे सदृशं भर्तुः पुत्राणां शतमात्मनः॥ ततः कालेन सा गर्भ धृतराष्ट्रादवाग्रहीत्।
en: (Namely) that she should have one hundred sons like her husband. Sometime after she conceived by Dhritarashtra.

sn: संवत्सरद्वयं तं तु गान्धारी गर्भमाहितम्॥ अप्रजा धारयामास ततस्तां दुःखमाविशत्।
en: She bore the burden in her womb for two years without being delivered; she was, therefore, much afflicted with grief.

sn: श्रुत्वा कुन्तीसुतं जातं बालार्कसमतेजसम्॥ उदरस्यात्मनः स्थैर्यमुपलभ्यान्वचिन्तयम्। अज्ञातं धृतराष्ट्रस्य यत्नेन महता ततः॥ सोदरं घातयामास गान्धारी दुःखमूर्च्छिता। ततो जज्ञे मांसपेशी लोहाष्ठीलेव संहता॥
en: She heard that a son was born to Kunti, as effulgent as the morning sun. Being sorry that in her case the time of bearing the child in the womb was too long and being deprived of reason by grief, she stuck her womb with violence without the knowledge of Dhritarashtra. Thereupon was brought forth a hard mass of flesh like an iron ball.

sn: द्विवर्षसम्भृता कुक्षौ तामुत्स्रष्टुं प्रचक्रमे। अथ द्वैपायनो ज्ञात्वा त्वरितः समुपागमत्॥
en: She bone in her womb for two years. To seeing hard mass of flesh, she decided to throw it. Dvaipayana, knowing it, soon came to her.

sn: तां स मांसमयीं पेशीं ददर्श जपतां वरः। ततोऽब्रवीत् सौबलेयीं किमिदं ते चिकीर्षितम्॥ सा चात्मनो मतं सत्यं शशंस परमर्षये।
en: The best of ascetics (Vyasa) saw that mass of flesh and asked the daughter of Subala, “What have you done?” And she (Gandhari) told her real feeling to the great Rishi.

sn: गान्धार्युवाच ज्येष्ठं कुन्तीसुतं जातं श्रुत्वा रविसमप्रभम्॥ दुःखेन परमेणेदमुदरं घातितं मया। शतं च किल पुत्राणां वितीर्णं मे त्वया पुरा॥ इयं मे मांसपेशी जाता पुत्रशताय वै।
en: Gandhari said : Having heard that Kunti had first given birth to a son, as effulgent as the sun. I struck at my womb in grief. You granted me the boon that I should get one hundred sons. But a ball of flesh has come out in the place of one hundred sons.

sn: व्यास उवाच एवमेतत् सौबलेयि नैतज्जात्वन्यथा भवेत्॥
en: Vyasa said : O daughter of Subala, it is even so. My words can never be futile.

sn: वितथं नोक्तपूर्वं मे स्वैरेष्वपि कुतोऽन्यथा। घृतपूर्णं कुण्डशतं क्षिप्रमेव विधीयताम्॥ सुगुप्तेषु च देशेषु रक्षा चैव विधीयताम्। शीताभिरद्भिरष्ठीलामिमां च परिषेचय॥
en: I have not spoken an untruth even in jest, why then will my words be futile! Let one hundred jars, filled with ghee, be brought in the proper way; let them be placed at a concealed place and let cool water be sprinkled on this ball of flesh.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच सा सिच्यमाना त्वष्ठीला बभूव शतधा तदा। अङ्गुष्ठपर्वमात्राणां गर्भाणां पृथगेव तु॥
en: Vaishampayana said : The ball of fresh, being thus sprinkled with water, became divided into hundred parts. They separately became hundred parts, each about the size of the thumb.

sn: एकाधिकशतं पूर्णं यथायोगं विशाम्पते। मांसपेश्यास्तदा राजन् क्रमश: कालपर्ययात्॥
en: O king, that ball of fresh in time became gradually one hundred and one separate parts.

sn: ततस्तांस्तेषु कुण्डेषु गर्भानवदधे तदा। स्वानुगुप्तेषु देशेषु रक्षां वै व्यदधात् ततः॥
en: These were then placed into the jars, filled with ghee and they were placed at a concealed spot and were carefully watched.

sn: शशंस चैव भगवान् कालेनैतावता पुनः। उद्घाटनीयान्येतानि कुण्डानीति च सौबलीम्॥
en: The illustrious (Vyasa) then said to the daughter of Subala that she should open the covers of the jars after full two years.

sn: इत्युक्त्वा भगवान् व्यासस्तथा प्रतिनिधाय च। जगाम तपसे धीमान् हिमवन्तं शिलोच्चयम्॥
en: Having said this and having made these arrangements, the illustrious and wise Vyasa went to the Himalayas mountains to perform his penances.

sn: जज्ञे क्रमेण चैतेन तेषां दुर्योधनो नृपः। जन्मतस्तु प्रमाणेन ज्येष्ठो राजा युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: King Duryodhana was then in time born from them (the parts of the fleshy ball). According to the order of birth, Yudhisthira was the eldest.

sn: तदाख्यातं तु भीष्माय विदुराय च धीमते। यस्मिन्नहनि दुर्धर्षो जज्ञे दुर्योधनस्तदा॥ तस्मिन्नेव महाबाहुर्जज्ञे भीमोऽपि वीर्यवान्। स जातमात्र एवाथ धृतराष्ट्रसुतो नृप॥ रासभारावसदृशं रुराव च ननाद च। तं खरा: प्रत्यभाषन्त गृध्रगोमायुवायसाः॥
en: The news of Duryodhana's birth was carried to Bhishma and the wise Vidura. On the day when haughty Duryodhana was born, on that very day was born mighty armed and greatly powerful Bhima. O king, as soon as that son of Dhritarashtra (Duryodhana) was born, he roared and brayed like an ass, Hearing that sound, the arsons vultures, jackals and crows spontaneously cried.

sn: वाताश्च प्रववुश्चापि दिग्दाहश्चाभवत् तदा। ततस्तु भीतवद् राजा धृतराष्ट्रोऽब्रवीदिदम्॥ समानीय बहून् विप्रान् भीष्मं विदुरमेव च। अन्यांश्च सुहृदो राजन् कुरून् सर्वांस्तथैव च॥
en: Strong wind began to blow and fires regard in every direction. Thereupon, the frightened king Dhritarashtra summoning many Brahmanas, Bhishma, Vidura and other friends, relatives and Kurus, said-

sn: युधिष्ठिरो राजपुत्रो ज्येष्ठो नः कुलवर्धनः। प्राप्तः स्वगुणतो राज्यं न तस्मिन् वाच्यमस्ति नः।३१।।
en: “The eldest of the princes, Yudhisthira is the perpetuator of your race. He has acquired the kingdom by virtue of his birth. We have nothing to say to this.

sn: अयं त्वनन्तरस्तस्मादपि राजा भविष्यति। एतद् विब्रूत मे तथ्यं यदत्र भविता ध्रुवम्॥
en: "But will my son be able to become king after hi“? Tell me what is right and lawful.

sn: वाक्यस्यैतस्य निधने दिक्षु सर्वासु भारत। क्रव्यादाः प्राणदान् घोराः शिवाश्चाशिवशसिनः॥
en: O descendant of the Bharata race, jackals and other carnivorous animals began to how! ominously from all sides.

sn: लक्षयित्वा निमित्तानि तानि घोराणि सर्वशः। तेऽब्रुवन् ब्राह्मणा राजन् विदुश्च महामतिः॥ यथेमानि निमित्तानि घोराणि मनुजाधिप। उत्थितानि सुते जाते ज्येष्ठे ते पुरुषर्षभ॥ व्यक्तं कुलान्तकरणो भवितैष सुतस्तव। तस्य शान्तिः परित्यागे गुप्तावपनयो महान्॥
en: O king, seeing these frightful ominous signs, the assembled Brahmanas and the high minded Vidura said, “O king, O best of men, when these fearful ominous signs are seen at the birth of your eldest son. It is evident he will be exterminator of your race. The prosperity of the race depends upon his abandonment. There must be great calamity in keeping him.

sn: शतमेकोनमप्यस्तु पुत्राणां ते महीपते। त्यजैनमेकं शान्तिं चेत् कुलस्येच्छसि भारत॥
en: O king, if you abandon him, there still remain ninety nine sons of yours. O descendant of the Bharata race, if you desire the good of your dynasty, abandon him.

sn: एकेन कुरु वै क्षेमं कुलस्य जगतस्तथा। त्यजेदेकं कुलस्यार्थे ग्रामस्यार्थे कुलं त्यजेत्॥ ग्रामं जनपदस्यार्थे आत्मार्थे पृथिवीं त्यजेत्। स तथा विदुरेणोक्तस्तैश्च सर्वैद्विजोत्तमैः॥ न चकार तथा राजा पुत्रस्नेहसमन्वितः। ततः पुत्रशतं पूर्ण धृतराष्ट्रस्य पार्थिव॥
en: Do good to the world and to your own race by abandoning him. It is said that an individuals should be abandoned for the sake of the family; a family should be abandoned for the sake of a village; a village should be abandoned for the sake of a country and the world should be abandoned for the sake of the soul.” Having been thus addressed by Vidura and the Brahmanas, the king, out of affection (for the son) did not act accordingly.

sn: मासमात्रेण संजज्ञे कन्या चैका शताधिका। गान्धार्यां क्लिश्यमानायामुदरेण विवर्धता॥ धृतराष्ट्र महाराज वैश्या पर्यचरत् किल। तस्मिन् संवत्सरे राजन् धृतराष्ट्रन्महायशाः॥ जज्ञे धीमांस्ततस्तस्यां युयुत्सुः करणो नृप। एवं पुत्रशतं जज्ञे धृतराष्ट्रस्य धीमतः॥ महारथानां वीराणां कन्या चैका शताधिका। युयुत्सुश्च महातेजा वैश्यापुत्रः प्रतापवान्॥
en: O king, there were born within a month one hundred sons of Dhritarashtra and also a daughter above and over that one hundred. When Gandhari was effected with her advanced pregnancy, a Vaishya maid servant was engaged to attended upon Dhritarashtra. O king, during that year, was begotten on her by Dhritarashtra illustrious and greatly intelligent son, who was afterwards named Yuyutsu, also called Karana. Thus were begotten by the wise Dhritarashtra one hundred sons, who were all heroes and (thus also was born) greatly powerful Yuyutsu born at a Vaishya woman. an

sn: जनमेजय उवाच धृतराष्ट्रस्य पुत्राणामादितः कथितं त्वया। ऋषेः प्रसादात् तु शतं न च कन्या प्रकीर्तिता॥
en: Janamejaya said : You have told me from the beginning all about the birth of Dhritarashtra's one hundred sons, the result of the boon granted by the Rishi, but you have not told me (the particular of the birth) of the daughter.

sn: वैश्यापुत्रो युयुत्सुश्च कन्या चैका शताधिका। गान्धारराजदुहिता शतपुत्रेति चानघ॥ उक्ता महर्षिणा तेन व्यासेनामिततेजसा। कथं त्विदानी भगवन् कन्यां त्वं तु ब्रवीषि मे॥
en: O sinless one, you have said that over and above one hundred sons, there was another son, named Yuyutsu, born of a Vaishya woman and also a daughter by Gandhari. The daughter of the king of Gandhara would get one hundred sons. O illustrious man, so said the great Rishi Vyasa of immeasurable effulgence. How do you then tell me that a daughter was born (over and above the hundred)?

sn: यदि भागशतं पेशी कृता तेन महर्षिणा। न प्रजास्यति चेद् भूयः सौबलेयी कथंचन॥ कथं तु सम्भवस्तस्या दुःशलाया वदस्व मे। यथावदिह विप्रः परं मेऽत्र कुतूलहम्॥
en: The ball of flesh was divided by the great Rishi into only one hundred parts and the daughter of Subala (Gandhari) did not conceive at any other time. How then was born Duhshala? O Brahmana Rishi, tell me this; my curiosity is very great.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच साध्वयं प्रश्न उद्दिष्टः पाण्डवेय ब्रवीमि ते। तां मांसपेशी भगवान् स्वयमेव महातपाः॥ शीताभिरद्धिरासिच्य भागं भागमकल्पयत्। यो यथा कल्पितो भागस्तं तं धात्र्या तथा नृप॥ घृतपूर्णेषु कुण्डेषु एकैकं प्राक्षिपत् तदा। एतस्मिन्नन्तरे साध्वी गान्धारी सृदृढव्रता॥ दुहितुः स्नेहसंयोगमनुध्याय वराङ्गना। मनसाचिन्तयद् देवी एतत् पुत्रशतं मम॥ भविष्यति न संदेहो न ब्रवीत्यन्यथा मुनिः। ममेयं परमा तुष्टिर्दुहिता मे भवेद् यदि॥
en: Vaishampayana said : O descendant of Pandu, your question is just. I shall tell you how it happened. The great ascetic, the illustrious Rishi himself, sprinkled that ball of fresh with cool water and begin to divide it into hundred parts, O king, as it was being divided into parts, the nurse began to take them up and put them one by one into the jars filled with ghee. In the meanwhile the beautiful and chaste Gandhari of rigid vows, feeling the affection for a daughter. Reflected in her mind, there is no doubt that I shall have one hundred sons. The Rishi had said this and it cannot be otherwise. If a daughter is born to me over and above my one hundred sons, I shall be exceedingly happy.

sn: एका शताधिका बाला भविष्यति कनीयसी। ततो दौहित्रजाल्लोकादबाह्योऽसौ पतिर्मम॥
en: My husband may then go to those worlds that the possession of a daughter's sons confers on a man.

sn: अधिका किल नारीणां प्रीतिर्जामातृजा भवेत्। यदि नाम ममापि स्याद् दुहितैका शताधिका॥ कृतकृत्या भवेयं वै पुत्रदौहित्रसंवृता। यदि सत्यं तपस्तप्तं दत्तं वाप्यथवा हुतम्॥ गुरवस्तोषिता वापि तथास्तु दुहिता मम। एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु कृष्णद्वैपायनः स्वयम्॥ व्यभजत् स तदा पेशी भगवानृषिसत्तमः। गणयित्वा शतं पूर्णमंशानामाह सौबलीम्॥
en: Every woman feels a very great affection for her son-in-law. If, therefore, I get a daughter over and above my one hundred sons, then surrounded by sons and daughter's sons, I shall feel myself supremely happy. If I have truly performed penances, if I have ever given in charity, if I have ever performed Homa, if ever I have respected my superiors, lets a daughter be born to me." All this time that best of Rishis, the illustrious Krishna Dvaipayana himself was dividing that ball of flesh. Counting full one hundred parts, he said to the daughter of Subala (Gandhari).

sn: व्यास उवाच पूर्णं पुत्रशतं त्वेतन्न मिथ्या वागुदाहृता। दौहित्रयोगाय भाग एकः शिष्टः शतात् परः। एषा ते सुभगा कन्या भविष्यति यथेप्सिता॥
en: "Here are your one hundred sons, I did not speak to you anything that was not true. Here is a part over and above one hundred which will give you a daughter's son. From this will be born an amiable and fortunate daughter, as you have desired."

sn: ततोऽन्यं घृतकुम्भं च समानाय्य महातपाः। तं चापि प्राक्षिपत् तत्र कन्यामागं तपोधनः॥ एतत् ते कथितं राजन् दुःशलाजन्म भारत। ब्रूहि राजेन्द्र किं भूयो वर्तयिष्यामि तेऽनघ।॥
en: Then that great ascetic, bringing another jar filled with ghee, placed the part into it for the purpose of daughter, O descendant of the Bharata race, thus have I narrated to you all about the birth of Dushala. O sinless one, tell me what more am I to narrate.

description: Narration of the names of Dhritarashtra's sons
sn: जनमेजय उवाच ज्येष्ठानज्येष्ठतां तेषां नामानि च पृथक् पृथक्। धृतराष्ट्रस्य पुत्राणामानुपूर्व्यात् प्रकीर्तय॥
en: Janamejaya said : O Lord, tell me the names of all the sons of Dhritarashtra beginning from the eldest, according to the order of their births. Vaishampayana said :

description: Narration of the names of Dhritarashtra's sons
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच दुर्योधनो युयुत्सुश्च राजन् दुःशासनस्तथा। दुःसहो दुःशलश्चैव जलसंधः समः सहः॥ विन्दानुविन्दौ दुर्धर्षः सुबाहुर्दुष्प्रधर्षणः। दुर्मर्षणो दुर्मुखश्च दुष्कर्णः कर्ण एव च॥ विविंशतिर्विकर्णश्च शलः सत्त्वः सुलोचनः। चित्रोपचित्रौ चित्राक्षश्चारुचित्रशरासनः॥ दुर्मदो दुर्विगाहश्च विवित्सुर्विकटाननः। ऊर्णनाभः सुनाभश्च तथा नन्दोपनन्दकौ॥५॥ चित्रबाणश्चित्रवर्या सुवर्मा दुर्विरोचनः। अयोबाहुर्महाबाहुश्चित्राङ्गश्चित्रकुण्डलः॥ भीमवेगो भीमबलो बलाकी बलवर्धनः। उग्रायुधः सुषेणश्च कुण्डोदरमहोदरौ॥ चित्रायुधो निषङ्गी च पाशी वृन्दारकस्तथा। दृढवर्मा दृढक्षत्रः सोमकीर्तिरनूदरः॥ दृढसंधो जरासंधः सत्यसंधः सदःसुवाक्। उग्रश्रवा उग्रसेनः सेनानीर्दुष्पराजयः॥ अपराजितः पण्डितको विशालाक्षो दुराधरः। दृढहस्तः सुहस्तश्च वातवेगसुवर्चसौ॥ आदित्यकेतुर्बह्वाशी नागदत्तोऽग्रयाय्यपि। कवची क्रथनः दण्डी दण्डधारो धनुर्ग्रहः॥ उग्रभीमरथौ वीरौ वीरबाहुरलोलुपः। अभयो रौद्रकर्मा च तथा दृढरथाश्रयः॥ अनाधृष्यः कुण्डभेदी विरावी चित्रकुण्डलः। प्रमथश्च प्रमाथी च दीर्घरोमश्च वीर्यवान्॥ दीर्घबाहुर्महाबाहु ढोरुः कनकध्वजः। कुण्डाशी विरजाश्चैव दुःशला च शताधिका॥ इति पुत्रशतं राजन् कन्या चैव शताधिका। नामधेयानुपूर्येण विद्धि जन्मक्रमं नृप॥
en: (Their names are). Duryodhana, Yuyutsu, Duhshasana, Duhsaha, Duhshala, Jalasandha, Vinda, Anuvinda, Durmarshana, Durmukha, Dushkarna, Karna, Vivinshati, Vikarna, Shala, Satva, Sulochana, Durdharsha, Subahu, Dushpradharshana, Durmarashana, Durmukha, Dushkarna, Karna, Chitra, Upachitra, Chitraksha, Charu, Chitrangada, Dhritarashtra, Durmada, Dushpraharsha, Vivitsu, Vikata, Sama, Umanabha, Padmanabha, Nanda, Upananda, Senapati, Sushena, Kundodara, Mandra, Chitrabahu, Chitravarmana, Suvarmana, Durvirochana, Ayobahu, Mahabahu, Chitrachapa, Sukundala, Bhimavega, Bhimabala, Balaki, Balavardhana, Ugrayudha, Bhimashara, Kanakaya, Drindahyudha, Drindavarmana, Drindakshetra, Somakirti, Anudara, Jarasandha, Dridhasandha, Satyasandha, Sadahsuvak, Ugrashrava, Ugrasena, Kshemamurti, Aparajita, Panditaka, Vishalaksha, Duradhara, Dridhahasta, Suhasta, Vatavega, Suvarcha, Adityaketu, Bahvashi, Nagadatta, Anuyayi, Nishangi, Kavachi, Dandi, Dandadhara, Dhanurgraha, Ugra, Bhimaratha, Virabahu, Alolupa, Abhaya, Raudrakarma, Dridharatha, Anadhrishya, Kundabhedi, Viravi, Dirghalochana, Dirghubahu, Mahabahu, Vyudhoru, Kanakadhvaja, Kundaja and Chitraksha. He (Dhritarashtra) had also a daughter, named Dushala, above and over these one hundred sons. The names of all the sons according to the order of their births.

description: Narration of the names of Dhritarashtra's sons
sn: सर्वे त्वतिरथाः शूराः सर्वे युद्धविशारदाः। सर्वे वेदविदश्चैव सर्वे सर्वास्त्रकोविदाः॥
en: They were all heroes and Atirathas, they were all learned in the science of war. They were all well acquainted with the Vedas and experts in using all kinds of weapons.

description: Narration of the names of Dhritarashtra's sons
sn: सर्वेषामनुरूपाश्च कृता दारा महीपते। धृतराष्ट्रेण समये परीक्ष्य विधिवत्रुप॥ दुःशलां चापि समये धृतराष्ट्रो नराधिपः। जयद्रथाय प्रददौ विधिना भरतर्षभ॥
en: O king, worthy wives were selected for them at the proper time and after due examinations by king Dhritarashtra. O best of the Bharata race, king Dhritarashtra bestowed Dushala at the proper time and with due rites on Jayadratha.

description: Curse of the deer on Pandu
sn: जनमेजय उवाच कथितो धार्तराष्ट्राणामार्षः सम्भव उत्तमः। अमनुष्यो मनुष्याणां भवता ब्रह्मवादिना॥
en: Janamejaya said : O utterer of Brahma, you have recited the excellent account of the extraordinary births of the sons of Dhritarashtra on earth, the result of the Rishi grace.

description: Curse of the deer on Pandu
sn: नामधेयानि चाप्येषां कथ्यमानानि भागशः। त्वत्तः श्रुतानि मे ब्रह्मन् पाण्डवानां च कीर्तय॥
en: O Brahmana, you have also told me their names according to their order of birth. I have heard all this from you. (Now) tell me all about the Pandavas.

description: Curse of the deer on Pandu
sn: ते हि सर्वे महात्मानो देवराजपराक्रमाः। त्वथैवांशावतरणे देवभागाः प्रकीर्तिताः॥
en: While reciting the incarnations of the celestials, the Asuras and beings of other classes on earth, you said that the illustrious men, the Pandavas, as powerful as the king of the celestials, were all incarnate portions of the celestials themselves.

description: Curse of the deer on Pandu
sn: एतदिच्छाम्यहं श्रोतुमतिमानुषकर्मणाम्। तेषामाजननं सर्वं वैशम्पायन कीर्तय॥
en: I desire to hear all about those beings of extraordinary achievements, beginning from the moments of their births. O Vaishampayana, narrate to me all their achievements.

description: Curse of the deer on Pandu
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच राजा पाण्डुर्महारण्ये मृगव्यालनिषेविते। चरन् मैथुनधर्मस्थं ददर्श मृगयूथपम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : O king, one day Pandu, while roaming in that great forest abounding in deer and other fierce animals, saw a large deer, the leader of its herd, coupling with its mate.

description: Curse of the deer on Pandu
sn: ततस्तां च मृगीं तं च रुक्मपुडखैः सुपत्रिभिः। निर्विभेद शरैस्तीक्ष्णैः पाण्डुः पञ्चभिराशुगैः॥
en: Seeing them, Pandu pierced both with five of his sharp and swift arrows, winged with golden feathers.

description: Curse of the deer on Pandu
sn: स च राजन् महातेजा ऋषिपुत्रस्तपोधनः। भार्यया सह तेजस्वी मृगरूपेण संगतः॥
en: O king, it was a greatly effulgent ascetic, the son of a Rishi (in the form of that deer) this effulgent man was with his wife who was a deer.

description: Curse of the deer on Pandu
sn: संसक्तश्च तया मृग्या मानुषीमीरयन् गिरम्। क्षणेन पतितो भूमौ विललापाकुलेन्द्रयः॥
en: Wounded by Pandu while with the mate, he fell down on the ground in a moment and uttered cries that were human. He began to weep bitterly.

description: Curse of the deer on Pandu
sn: मृग उवाच काममन्युपरीता हि बुद्ध्या विरहिता अपि। वर्जयन्ति नृशंसानि पापेष्वपि रता नराः॥ न विधिं ग्रसते प्रज्ञा प्रज्ञां तु ग्रसते विधिः। विधिपर्यागतानान् प्राज्ञो न प्रतिपद्यते॥
en: The deer said: Even men, who are slaves of lust and anger, who are devoid of reason and who are ever sinful, never commit such a cruel act. Man's individual judgment does not prevail against the ordinance; the ordinance (always) prevails against individual judgment. The wise men never sanction anything discountenanced by the ordinance.

description: Curse of the deer on Pandu
sn: शश्वद्धर्मात्मना मुख्ये कुले जातस्य भारत। कामलोभाभिभूतस्य कथं ते चलिता मतिः॥
en: O descendant of the Bharata race you are born in a dynasty that has ever been virtuous. How is it that you have lost your reason, over powered by passion.

description: Curse of the deer on Pandu
sn: पाण्डुरुवाच शत्रूणां या वधे वृत्तिः सा मृगाणां वधे स्मृता। राज्ञां मृग न मां मोहात् त्वं गर्हयितुमर्हसि॥
en: Pandu said : O deer, kings behave in the matter of killing the animals of your species (deer) as they do in the matter of killing their foes. Therefore, you should not, reprove me out of ignorance.

description: Curse of the deer on Pandu
sn: अच्छद्मना मायया च मृगाणां वध इष्यते। स एव धर्मो राज्ञां तु तद्धि त्वं किं नु गर्हसे॥
en: Animals of your species are killed by open or covert means. This is the practice of kings. Then why do you reprove me?

description: Curse of the deer on Pandu
sn: अगस्त्यः सत्रमासीनश्चकार मृगयामृषिः। आरण्यान् सर्वदेवेभ्यो मृगान् प्रेषन् महावने॥ प्रमाणदृष्टधर्मेण कथमस्मान् विगर्हसे। अगस्त्यस्याभिचारेण युष्माकं विहितो वधः॥
en: The Rishi Agastya, while engaged in a (great) sacrifice, hunted, he deer in the great forest and offered every one of them to the celestial. Agastya performed the Homa with the fat of the deer. You have been killed according to such precedents. Why then do you reprove me?

description: Curse of the deer on Pandu
sn: मृग उवाच न रिपून् वै समुद्दिश्य विमुञ्चन्ति नराः शरान्। रन्ध्र एषां विशेषेण वधः काले प्रशस्यते॥
en: The deer said : Man do not throw their arrows even at their enemies when they are unprepared. There is a time for doing it; to kill at such a time is not censurable.

description: Curse of the deer on Pandu
sn: पाण्डुरुवाच प्रमत्तमप्रमत्तं वा विवृतं जन्ति चौजसा। उपायैर्विविधैस्तीक्ष्णैः : कस्मान्मृग विगर्हसे॥
en: Pandu said: It is well known that men kill deer by various means, without (the least) regard whether they are prepared or unprepared; O deer, you should not, therefore, reprove me.

description: Curse of the deer on Pandu
sn: मृग उवाच नाहं जन्तं मृगान् राजन् विगर्हे चात्मकारणात्। मैथुनं तु प्रतीक्ष्यं मे त्वयेहाद्यानृशंस्यतः॥
en: The deer said: O king, I do not blame you, because you have killed a deer, or because you have done me an injury. Instead of doing such a cruel act, you should have waited till the completion of my intercourse.

description: Curse of the deer on Pandu
sn: सर्वभूतहिते काले सर्वभूतेप्सिते तथा। को हि विद्वान् मृगं हन्याच्चरन्तं मैथुनं वने॥
en: The intercourse is agreeable to all creatures; it is productive of good to all. What man of learning is there who kills a deer engage in intercourse in the forest?

description: Curse of the deer on Pandu
sn: अस्यां मृग्यां च राजेन्द्र हर्षान्मैथुनमाचरम्। पुरुषार्थफलं कर्तुं तत् त्वया विफलीकृतम्॥
en: O king, I was joyfully engaged in intercourse with this mate to beget offspring. You have made my that effort futile.

description: Curse of the deer on Pandu
sn: पौरवाणां महाराज तेषामक्लिष्टकर्मणाम्। वंशे जातस्य कौरव्य नानुरूपमिदं तव॥
en: O great king, being born in the Puru dynasty, ever famous for its pure acts and being a descendant of the Kuru race, you should not have committed such an act.

description: Curse of the deer on Pandu
sn: नृशंसं कर्म सुमहत् सर्वलोकविगर्हितम्। अस्वय॑मयशस्यं चाप्यधर्मिष्ठं च भारत॥
en: O descendant of the Bharata race, this act is yours is extremely cruel, it deserves universal excretion, it is infamous and sinful and will certainly lead (you) to hell.

description: Curse of the deer on Pandu
sn: स्त्रीभोगानां विशेषज्ञः शास्त्रधर्मार्थतत्त्ववित्। नार्हस्त्वं सुरसंकाश कर्तुमस्वय॑मीदृशम्॥
en: You are well acquainted with the pleasure of intercourse; you are also learned in the Shastras and the precepts of religion. You are like a celestial, you should not have committed such an act, unworthy of heaven.

description: Curse of the deer on Pandu
sn: त्वया नृशंसकर्तारः पापाचाराश्च मानवाः। निग्राह्याः पार्थिवश्रेष्ठ त्रिवर्गपरिवर्जिताः॥
en: O best of kings, your duty is to chastise those who act cruelly, who are engaged in sinful practices and who are devoid of the precepts of religion (Dharma, Artha and Kama.)

description: Curse of the deer on Pandu
sn: किं कृतं ते नरश्रेष्ठ मामिहानागसं जता। मुनिं मूलफलाहारं मृगवेषधरं नृप॥ वसमानमरण्येषु नित्यं शमपरायणम्। त्वयाहं हिंसितो यस्मात् तस्मात् त्वामप्यहं शपे॥
en: O best of men, O king, what have I done that you have killed me? I am a Rishi who lives on fruits and roots though in the form of a deer! I live in the forest always being disposed to peace. As you have killed me, I shall certainly curse you.

description: Curse of the deer on Pandu
sn: द्वयोर्नृशंसकर्तारमवशं काममोहितम्। जीवितान्तकरो भाव एवमेवागमिष्यति॥
en: Cruel as you have been to a couple, death shall certainly overtake you as soon as you will feel the influence of desire.

description: Curse of the deer on Pandu
sn: अहं कि किंदमो नाम तपसा भावितो मुनिः। व्यपत्रपन्मनुष्याणां मृग्यां मैथुनमाचरम्॥ मृगो भूत्वा मृगैः सार्धं चरामि गहने वने। न तु ते ब्रह्महत्येयं भविष्यत्यविजानतः॥
en: I am an ascetic Rishi, named Kindama. I was engaged in intercourse with this deer out of shame of men. Assuming the form of a deer I roam in the deep forest in company with other female deer. The sin of killing a Brahmana, (however), will not be yours, for you have done it not knowing me (to be Brahmana).

description: Curse of the deer on Pandu
sn: मृगरूपधरं हत्वा मामेवं काममोहितम्। अस्य तु त्वं फलं मूढ प्राप्स्यसीदृशमेव हि॥
en: As you have killed me in the form of a deer when I was full of desire, so you, O foolish man, will certainly meet with the fate that has befallen me.

description: Curse of the deer on Pandu
sn: प्रियया सह संवासं प्राप्य कामविमोहितः। त्वमप्यस्यामवस्थायां प्रेतलोकं गमिष्यसि॥
en: When you will go to your dear one, full of desire as was the case with me, you will, at that time, certainly go to the land of the dead.

description: Curse of the deer on Pandu
sn: अन्तकाले हि संवासं यया गन्तासि कान्तया। प्रेतराजपुरं प्राप्तं सर्वभूतदुरत्ययम्। भक्त्या मतिमतां श्रेष्ठ सैव त्वानुगमिष्यति॥
en: Your wife with whom you will join at your last moments will also go with you with reverence and affection to the ever unavoidable land of the dead.

description: Curse of the deer on Pandu
sn: वर्तमानः सुखे दुःखं यथाहं प्रापितस्त्वया। तथा त्वां च सुखं प्राप्तं दुःखमभ्यागमिष्यति॥
en: As I have been plunged into grief when I was happy, so you will also be afflicted with grief when in happiness.

description: Curse of the deer on Pandu
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्त्वा सुदुःखार्तो जीवितात् स व्यमुच्यत। मृगः पाण्डुश्च दुःखार्तः क्षणेन समपद्यत॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having said this, the deer, affected with grief, gave up his life; and Pandu also was plunged in grief in a moment.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तं व्यतीतमतिक्रम्य राजा स्वमिव बान्धवम्। सभार्यः शोकदुःखार्तः पर्यदेवयदातुरः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : After the death of the deer, the king (Pandu) like a friend (of his) wept bitterly with his wives, being much afflicted with grief.

sn: पाण्डुरुवाच सतामपि कुले जाताः कर्मणा वत दुर्गतिम्। प्राप्नुवन्त्यकृतात्मानः कामजालविमोहिताः॥
en: Pandu said: The wicked men, though born in virtuous families, being illuded with passions, become overwhelmed with misery as the fruit of their own acts.

sn: शश्वद्धर्मात्मना जातो बाल एव पिता मम। जीवितान्तमनुप्राप्तः कामात्मैवेति नः श्रुतम्॥ ।
en: I have heard that my father, though begotten by a virtuous man, died when he was still a youth, only because a slave of lust.

sn: तस्य कामात्मनः क्षेत्रे राज्ञः संयतवागृषिः। कृष्णद्वैपायन: साक्षाद् भगवान् मामजीजनत्॥
en: In the field of that lustful king, I was begotten by Krishna Dvaipayana of truthfull speech who was like Brahma himself.

sn: तस्याद्य व्यसने बुद्धिः संजातेयं ममाधमा। त्यक्तस्य देवैरनयान्मृगयां परिधावतः॥
en: (Being the son of such a man) with my heart devoted to sin I lead wandering life in pursuit of deer. The gods have all forsaken me.

sn: मोक्षमेव व्यवस्यामि बन्धो हि व्यसनं महत्। सुवृत्तिमनुवर्तिष्ये तामहं पितुरव्ययाम्॥
en: I shall now seek for salvation; my heart is a great slave of passion. The great impediments to salvation is the desire to beget children. I shall now adopt Brahmacharya, following the example of my father.

sn: अतीव तपसाऽऽत्मानं योजयिष्याम्यसंशयम्। तस्मादेकोऽहमेकाकी एकैकस्मिन् वनस्पतौ॥ चरन् भैक्ष्यं मुनिर्मुण्डश्चरिष्याम्याश्रमानिमान्। पांसुना समवच्छन्नः शून्यागारकृतालयः॥ वृक्षमूलनिकेतो वा त्यक्तसर्वप्रियाप्रियः।
en: I shall certainly bring my passions under complete control by severe asceticism. Forsaking my wives and other relatives and shaving my head, I shall alone wander over the earth, begging my food from the lords of the forests (tree). Forsaking every object of affection and aversion and covering my body with dust, I shall make the shelter of trees and deserted houses my home.

sn: न शोचन् न प्रहृष्यंश्च तुल्यनिन्दात्मसंस्तुतिः॥ निराशीर्निर्नमस्कारो निर्द्वन्द्वो निष्परिग्रहः।
en: I shall never yield to the influence of sorrow or joy; I shall regard praise and blame in the same light; I shall not seek benedictions or bows. I shall be in peace with all; I shall not accept gifts.

sn: न चाप्यवहसन् कच्चिन्न कुर्वन् भृकुटी क्वचित्॥ प्रसन्नवदनो नित्यं सर्वभूतहिते रतः।
en: I shall not mock any one; I shall not contract my brow at any body; I shall be ever cheerful; and I shall be devoted to the good of all creatures.

sn: जङ्गमाजङ्गमं सर्वमविहिंसंश्चतुर्विधम्॥ स्वासु प्रजास्विव सदा समः प्राणभृतां प्रति।
en: I shall not harm any of the four orders of the creation, either mobile or immobile. I shall treat them all equally, as if they are my own children.

sn: एककालं चरन् भैक्ष्यं कुलानि दश पञ्च वा॥ असम्भवे वा भक्ष्यस्य चरन्ननशनान्यपि।
en: I shall daily beg my food from only five or ten families. If it is impossible to get food thus, I shall remain fasting I shall rather go with little food then to ask a man twice.

sn: अल्पमल्पं च भुञ्जानः पूर्वालाभे न जातुचित्॥ अन्यान्यपि चरँल्लोभादलाभे सप्त पूरयन्। अलाभे यदि वा लाभे समदर्शी महातपाः॥
en: If I do not obtain food after completing my round of seven or ten houses, I shall not enlarge my round out of covetousness. Whether I obtain or fail to obtain alms, I shall remain a great ascetic equally unmoved.

sn: वास्यैकं तक्षतो बाहुं चन्दनेनैकमुक्षतः। नाकल्याणं न कल्याणं चिन्तयन्नुभयोस्तयोः॥ न जिजीविषुवत् किंचिन्न मुमूर्षुवदाचरन्। जीवितं मरणं चैव नाभिनन्दन् न च द्विषन्॥
en: The cutting off my one arm with an axe and the smearing of the other with sandal, both will be equally regarded by me as the same. I shall not desire good from one or evil from the other. I shall not be pleased with life or displeased with death. I shall neither wish to live or fear to die.

sn: याः काश्चिज्जीवता शक्याः कर्तुमभ्युदयक्रियाः। ताः सर्वाः समतिक्रम्य निमेषादिव्यवस्थिताः॥ तासु चाष्यनवस्थासु त्यक्तसर्वेन्द्रियक्रियः। सम्परित्यक्तधर्मार्थः सुनिर्णिक्तात्मकल्मषः॥
en: Washing my heart of all sins, I shall certainly transcend those sacred rites productive of happiness that men perform at inauspicious moments. I shall also abstain from all acts of Dharma and Artha and from all those acts those that lead to the gratification of senses.

sn: निर्मुक्तः सर्वपापेभ्यो व्यतीतः सर्ववागुराः। न वशे कस्यचित् तिष्ठन् सधर्मा मातरिश्वनः॥
en: Being freed from all sins and snares of the world, I shall be as free as the wind.

sn: एतया सततं धृत्या चरन्नेवंप्रकारया। देहं संस्थापयिष्यामि निर्भयं मार्गमास्थितः॥
en: Acting always in this way and treading in the path of fearlessness, I shall at last lay down my life.

sn: नाहं सुकृपणे मार्गे स्ववीर्यक्षयशोचिते। स्वधर्मात् सततापेते चरेयं वीर्यवर्जितः॥
en: I am destitute of the power of begetting children. I shall not certainly deviate from the line of duty, in order to tread in the vile path of the world which is full of misery.

sn: सत्कृतोऽसत्कृतो वापि योऽन्यं कृपणचक्षुषा। उपैति वृत्तिं कामात्मा स शुनां वर्तते पथि॥
en: Whether respected or disrespected by the world, that man, who, being desireless, becomes full of desire, behaves like a dog.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्त्वा सुदुःखार्तो निःश्वासपरमो नृपः। अवेक्षमाणः कुन्तीं च माद्रीं स समभाषत॥
en: Vaishampayana said : The king, having said this in sorrow, signed and looking at (his wives) Kunti and Madri said-

sn: कौसल्या विदुरः क्षत्ता राजा च सह बन्धुभिः। आर्या सत्यवती भीष्मस्ते च राजपुरोहिताः॥ ब्राह्मणाश्च महात्मानः सोमपाः संशितव्रताः। पौरवृद्धाश्च ये तत्र निवसन्त्यस्मदाश्रयाः। प्रसाद्य सर्वे वक्तव्याः पाण्डुः प्रव्रजितो वनम्॥
en: After gratifying all, tell the princess of Koshala, Vidura, the king with all his friends mother Satyavati, Bhishma, the royal priests, the high-souled, Soma drinking Brahmans of rigid vows and those old men who live under our protection that 'Pandu has retired into a forest'.

sn: निशम्य वचनं भर्तुर्वनवासे धृतात्मनः। तत्समं वचनं कुन्ती माद्री च समभाषताम्॥
en: Having heard these words of their husband who had fixed his mind to retire into a forest, both Kunti and Madri addressed him in these proper words.

sn: अन्येऽपि ह्याश्रमाः सन्ति ये शक्या भरतर्षभ। आवाभ्यां धर्मपत्नीभ्यां सह तप्तुं तपो महत्॥
en: “O best of the Bharata race, there are many other Ashramas (modes of life) in which you can perform with us, your lawfully wedded wives, great asceticism.

sn: शरीरस्यापि मोक्षाय स्वयं प्राप्य महाफलम्। त्वमेव भविता भर्ता स्वर्गस्यापि न संशयः॥
en: In which you can obtain the salvation of your body, you may obtain heaven as your reward. As the great fruit (of your action) you can certainly become the lord of heaven.

sn: प्रणिधायेन्द्रियग्रामं भर्तृलोकपरायणे। त्यक्तकामसुखे ह्यावां तप्स्यावो विपुलं तपः॥
en: We shall also perform great asceticism with our husband, controlling our passions and abandoning all desires and pleasures.

sn: यदि चावां महाप्राज्ञ त्यक्ष्यसि त्वं विशाम्पते। अद्यैवावां प्रहास्यावो जीवितं नात्र संशयः॥
en: O greatly learned man, if you abandon us, we shall then certainly give up our lives to day.

sn: पाण्डुरुवाच यदि व्यवसितं ह्येतद् युवयोधर्मसंहितम्। स्ववृत्तिमनुवर्तिष्ये तामहं पितुरव्ययाम्॥
en: Pandu said: If your this determination be conformable to virtue, then I shall with you both follow the imperishable path of my father.

sn: त्यक्त्वा ग्राम्यसुखाहारं तप्यमानो महत् तपः। वल्कली फलमूलाशी चरिष्यामि महावने॥
en: Abandoning the luxuries of village and towns, robed in barks of trees and living on fruits and roots and practicing the severest asceticism, I shall roam in the great forest.

sn: अग्नौ जुह्वन्नुभौ कालावुभौ कालावुपस्पृशन्। कृशः परिमिताहारश्चीरचर्मजटाधरः॥
en: Bathing in the morning and in the evening, I shall perform the Homa. I shall reduce my body by eating sparingly; I shall wear rags and skins; I shall carry matted hair on my head.

sn: शीतवातातपसहः क्षुत्पिपासानवेक्षकः। तपसा दुश्चरेणेदं शरीरमुपशोषयन्॥ एकान्तशीली विमृशन् पक्वापक्वेन वर्तयन्। पितॄन् देवांश्च वन्येन वाग्भिरद्धिश्च तर्पयन्।३५॥
en: Exposing myself to heat and cold and disregarding hunger and thirst, I shall reduce my body by performing most difficult asceticism. I shall live on fruits, ripe or unripe; I shall be in contemplation; I shall worship the Pitris and the celestial with speech and with the fruit of the forest.

sn: वानप्रस्थजनस्यापि दर्शनं कुलवासिनाम्। नाप्रियाण्याचरिष्यामि किं पुनर्गमवासिनाम्॥
en: I shall not see the dwellers of cities or the dwellers of forest. I shall not even harm them (the dwellers of forest), not to speak of the dwellers of villages.

sn: एवमारण्यशास्त्राणामुग्रमुग्रतरं विधिम्। काइक्षमाणोऽहमास्थास्ये देहस्यास्या समापनात्॥
en: I shall thus perform the severest practices of Vanaprastha, performing the severer ones gradually, till lay down my body.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच इत्येवमुक्त्वा भार्ये ते राजा कौरवनन्दनः। ततश्चूडामणि निष्कमङ्गदे कुण्डलानि च॥ वासांसि च महार्हाणि स्त्रीणामाभरणानि च। प्रदाय सर्वं विप्रेभ्यः पाण्डुः पुनरभाषत॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having said this to his wives, the descendant of Kuru, the king (Pandu), gave his jewel of the diadem, his necklace of precious gold, his bracelets, his car rings, his valuable robes and the ornaments of the ladies to the Brahmanas. He then said-

sn: गत्वा नागपुरं वाच्यं पाण्डुः प्रव्रजितो वनम्। अर्थ कामं सुखं चैव रतिं च परमात्मिकाम्॥ प्रतस्थे सर्वमुत्सृज्य सभार्यः कुरुनन्दनः। ततस्तस्यानुयातारस्ते चैव परिचारकाः॥
en: "Going to Hastinapur, inform all that Pandu, the descendant of Kuru, has retired into the forest with his wives, abandoning wealth, desires, happiness and sexual appetite.” Then assembled followers and attendants.

sn: श्रुत्वा भरतसिंहस्य विविधाः करुणा गिरः। भीममार्तस्वरं कृत्वा हाहेति परिचुक्रुशुः॥
en: Hearing these and other sorrowful words of that lion of the Bharata race, bewailed in grief and cried, "Alas! O!"

sn: उष्णमश्रु विमुञ्चन्तस्तं विहाय महीपतिम्। ययुर्नागपुरं तूर्णं सर्वमादाय तद् धनम्॥
en: They shed hot tears to leave the king. They left that forest and went to Hastinapur, taking all the wealth with them.

sn: ते गत्वा नगरं राज्ञो यथावृत्तं महात्मनः। कथयांचक्रिरे राज्ञस्तद् धनं विविधं ददुः॥
en: Going to the city, they told the illustrious king all that had happened and they gave him all the wealth.

sn: श्रुत्वा तेभ्यस्ततः सर्वं यथावृत्तं महावने। धृतराष्ट्रो नरश्रेष्ठः पाण्डुमेवान्वशोचत॥
en: Having heard all that had happened in the great forest, the best of men, king Dhritarashtra, wept for Pandu.

sn: न शय्यासनभोगेषु रतिं विन्दति कर्हिचित्। भ्रातृशोकसमाविष्टस्तमेवार्थं विचिन्तयन्॥
en: He derived no pleasure in the comforts of his beds, seats and luxuries. Afflicted with the loss of his brother, he continually brooded over it.

sn: राजपुत्रस्तु कौरव्य पाण्डुर्मूलफलाशनः। जगाम सह पत्नीभ्यां ततो नागशतं गिरिम्॥
en: The descendant of Kuru, the royal prince (Pandu), living on fruits and roots went with his two wives to the Nagashata mountains.

sn: स चैत्ररथमासाद्य कालकूटमतीत्य च। हिमवन्तमतिक्रम्य प्रययौ गन्धमादनम्॥
en: He then went to Chaitraratha and then to Kalakuta. Crossing the Himalayas, he went to Gandhamadana.

sn: रक्ष्यमाणो महाभूतैः सिद्धेश्च परमर्षिभिः। उवास स महाराज समेषु विषमेषु च॥ इन्द्रद्युम्नसरः प्राप्य हंसकूटमतीत्य च। शतशृङ्गे महाराज तापस: समतप्यत॥
en: Protected by Mahabhutas, Siddhas and great Rishis, that great king lived sometimes on the plain and sometimes on the hills. He then went to the lake Indradyumna; and then crossing the Hansakuta, the great king performed his penances on the mountain with hundred peaks.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तत्रापि तपसि श्रेष्ठे वर्तमानः स वीर्यवान्। सिद्धचारणसव्रनां बभूव प्रियदर्शनः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : That greatly powerful man (Pandu; was there engaged in the best of asceticism) and he soon became the favorite of all the Siddhas and Charanas.

sn: शुश्रूषुरनहंवादी संयतात्मा जितेन्द्रियः। स्वर्यं गन्तुं पराक्रान्तः स्वेन वीर्येण भारत॥
en: O descendant of the Bharata race, he was devoted to the service of his preceptors; he was free from vanity; he was self controlled and master over his passions. The powerful man went to heaven by his own prowess.

sn: केषांचिदभवद् भ्राता केषांचिदभवत् सखा। ऋषयस्त्वपरे चैनं पुत्रवत् पर्यपालयन्॥
en: He became the brother of some and the friend of others, the others again treated him as their own son.

sn: स तु कालेन महता प्राप्य निष्कलुषं तपः। ब्रह्मर्षिसदृशः पाण्डुर्बभूव भरतर्षभ।॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, after a long time Pandu acquired those great and sinless ascetic merits, by which he became like a Brahmarshi.

sn: अमावस्यां तु सहिता ऋषयः संशितव्रताः। ब्रह्मणं द्रष्टुकामास्ते सम्प्रतस्थुर्महर्षयः॥
en: On a new moon day the Rishis of rigid vows assembled together and were about to start with the desire of seeing Brahma.

sn: सम्प्रयातानृषीन् दृष्ट्वा पाण्डुर्वचनमब्रवीत्। भवन्तः क्व गमिष्यन्ति ब्रूत मे वदतां वराः॥
en: Seeing the Rishis about to start, Pandu said, "O best of eloquent men, tell me where you are going."

sn: ऋषयः ऊचुः समवायो महानद्य ब्रह्मलोके महात्मनाम्। देवानां च ऋषीणां च पितृणां च महात्मनाम्। वयं तत्र गमिष्यामो द्रष्टुकामाः स्वयम्भुवम्॥
en: The Rishi said : There will be a great assemblage of highsouled celestial Rishis and Pitris in the abode of Brahma. We shall go there; we are desirous of seeing the self created (Brahma).

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच पाण्डुरुत्थाय सहसा गन्तुकामो महर्षिभिः। स्वर्गपारं तितीर्घः स शतशृङ्गादुदङ्मुखः॥ प्रतस्थे सह पत्नीभ्यामब्रुवंस्तं च तापसाः। उपर्युपरि गच्छन्तः शैलराजमुदङ्मुखाः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Pandu suddenly rose with the desire of going with the Rishis and reaching the heaven. When he was about to start with his two wives in a northerly direction from the mountains with the hundred peaks, the ascetics addressed him thus.
