sn: दृष्टवन्तो गिरौ रम्ये दुर्गान् देशान् बहून् वयम्। विमानशतसम्बाधां गीतस्वरनिनादिताम्॥ आक्रीडभूमिं देवानां गन्धर्वाप्सरसां तथा। उद्यानानि कुबेरस्य समानि विषमाणि च॥
en: "In our northward march, ascending the king of mountains, higher and higher we have seen many delightful and inaccessible regions, on the breast of the hill. (We have seen) the retreats of the celestials, Gandharvas and Apsaras, with hundreds of places resounding with the sweet note of celestial music. (We have seen) the gardens of Kubera, laid out on even and uneven grounds.

sn: महानदीनितम्बांश्च गहनान् गिरिगह्वरान्। सन्ति नित्यहिमा देशा निर्वृक्षमृगपक्षिणः॥
en: (We have seen) the banks of great rivers and mountain caverns. There are regions (on that mountain) everlastingly covered with snow and devoid of birds and beasts and trees.

sn: सन्ति क्वचिन्महादर्यो दुर्गाः काश्चिद् दुरासदाः। नातिक्रामेत पक्षी यान् कुत एवेतरे मृगाः॥
en: There are some places, where are very dangerous caves that they are perfectly inaccessible and unfit for habitation. Not to speak of other creatures, even birds can not cross them.

sn: वायुरेको हि यात्यत्र सिद्धाश्च परमर्षयः। गच्छन्त्यौ शैलराजेऽस्मिन् राजपुत्र्यौ कथं त्विमे॥ न सीदेतामदुःखा मा गमो भरतर्षभ।
en: "The only thing that can go there is air and only beings, Siddhas and great Rishis. O best of the Bharata race, these princesses are unaccustomed to hardship; how will they ascend those heights of the king of mountains? Therefore, do not come with us.'

sn: पाण्डुरुवाच अप्रजस्य महाभागा न द्वारं परिचक्षते॥ स्वर्गे तेनाभितप्तोऽहमप्रजस्तु ब्रवीमि वः। पित्र्यादृणादनिर्मुक्तस्तेन तप्ये तपोधनाः॥
en: Pandu said: O greatly fortunate ones, it is said that there is no heaven for a sonless. I am sonless. I speak to you in sorrow. O great ascetics, I am sorry, because I have not been able to free myself from the debt I owe to my forefathers.

sn: देहनाशे ध्रुवो नाशः पितॄणामेष निश्चयः। ऋणैश्चतुर्भिः संयुक्ता जायन्ते मानवा भुवि॥
en: In the dissolution of my body, my ancestors are sure to perish. Men are born in this world with four debts.

sn: पितृदेवर्षिमनुजैर्देयं तेभ्यश्च धर्मतः। एतानि तु यथाकालं यो न बुध्यति मानवः॥ न तस्य लोकाः सन्तीति धर्मविद्भिः प्रतिष्ठितम्। यज्ञैस्तु देवान् प्रीणाति स्वाध्यायतपसा मुनीन्।॥
en: (The name of debts) namely the debts due to the ancestors, the celestials, the Rishis and other men. They must be discharged with virtue. It has been established by the learned men that no regions of bliss exist for those who neglect to pay in due time these debts. The celestial are paid (gratified) by sacrifices, the Rishis by study and meditation.

sn: पुत्रैः श्राद्धैः पितॄश्चापि आनृशंस्येन मानवान्। ऋषिदेवमनुष्याणां परिमुक्तोऽस्मि धर्मतः॥ त्रयाणामितरेषां तु नाश आत्मनि नश्यति। पित्र्यादृणादनिर्मुक्त इदानीमस्मि तापसाः॥
en: The Pitris by begetting children and performing Shraddha and the other men by humanity and kindness, I have virtuously discharged my debts to the celestials, Rishis and other men. But there are those (Pitris) who are sure to perish at the dissolution of my body. O ascetics, I am not as yet free from the debt I owe to my ancestors.

sn: इह तस्मात् प्रजाहेतोः प्रजायन्ते नरोत्तमाः। यथैवाहं पितुः क्षेत्रे जातस्तेन महर्षिणा॥ तथैवास्मिन् मम क्षेत्रे कथं वै सम्भवेत् प्रजा।
en: The best of men were born to beget children to discharge that debt. As I was begotten by the great Rishi on the field of my father, so should children be begotten on my soil (wives).

sn: ऋषयः ऊचुः अस्ति वै तव धर्मात्मान् विद्मो देवोपमं शुभम्॥ अपत्यमनघं राजन् वयं दिव्येन चक्षुषा। देवोद्दिष्टं नरव्याघ्र कर्मणेहोपपादय॥
en: The Rishis said : O virtuous minded man, O king, there is progeny for you that will be sinless, greatly fortunate and like the celestial themselves. We see this with our prophetic eyes. O best of kings, therefore, accomplish the purposes of the celestials by your acts.

sn: अक्लिष्टं फलमव्यग्रो विन्दते बुद्धिमान् नरः। तस्मिन् दृष्टे फले राजन् प्रयत्न कर्तुमर्हसि॥ अपत्यं गुणसम्पन्नं लब्धा प्रीतिकरं ह्यसि।
en: The intelligent man who acts with deliberation always obtains good fruits. Therefore, O king, you should exert yourself. The fruits you will obtain is visible. You will surely obtain accomplished and agreeable sons.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तच्छ्रुत्वा तापसवचः पाण्डुश्चिन्तापरोऽभवत्॥ आत्मनो मृगशापेन जानन्नुपहतां क्रियाम्। सोऽब्रवीद् विजने कुन्ती धर्मपत्नी यशस्विनीम्। अपत्योत्पादने यत्नमापदि त्वं समर्थय॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having heard these words of the ascetics and remembering the loss of his procreative power owing to the curse of the deer, Pandu began to reflect. He told his lawfully wedded wife, illustrious Kunti, in private, “Try to raise offspring at this emergency.

sn: अपत्यं नाम लोकेषु प्रतिष्ठा धर्मसंहिता। इति कुन्ति विदुर्धीराः शाश्वतं धर्मवादिनः॥ इष्टं दत्तं तपस्तप्तं नियमश्च स्वनुष्ठितः। सर्वमेवानपत्यस्य न पावनमिहोच्यते॥
en: O Kunti, the wise expounders of the eternal religion say that son is the source of virtuous fame in the three worlds, Sacrifices, gifts in charity, ascetic penances and carefully observed vows, do not free a sonless man from his sins.

sn: सोऽहमेवं विदित्वैतत् प्रपश्यामि शुचिस्मिते। अनपत्यः शुभाँल्लोकान् न प्राप्स्यामीति चिन्तयन्।३०।
en: O lady of sweet smiles, knowing all this, I am certain that sonless as I am, I shall not obtain the regions of felicity.

sn: मृगाभिशापान्नष्टं मे जननं ह्यकृतात्मनः। नृशंसकारिणो भीरु यथैवोपहतं पुरा॥
en: O timid lady, as I was formerly addicted to cruel acts and led a vicious life, I have lost my power of procreation by the curse of the deer.

sn: इमे वै बन्धुदायादाः षट् पुत्रा धर्मदर्शने। षडेवाबन्धुदायादाः पुत्रास्ताञ्छृणु मे पृथे।॥
en: O Pritha, the religious books mention of six kinds of sons who are both heirs and kinsmen and six kinds more who are not heirs, but kinsmen. I shall speak of them; listen to me.

sn: स्वयंजातः प्रणीतश्च तत्समः पुत्रिकासुतः। पौन वश्च कानीनः भगिन्यां यश्च जायते॥ दत्तः क्रीतः कृत्रिमश्च उपगच्छेत् स्वयं च यः। सहोढो ज्ञातिरेताच हीनयोनिधृतश्च यः॥
en: (They are), Aurasa (the son begotten by one's own self on his own wife), Pranita (the son begotten on one's own wife by an accomplished person), Parikrita (the son begotten on one's wife by a man for a pecuniary consideration), Paunarbhava (the son begotten on a wife after her husband's death), Kanin (the son born in the maidenhood), Kunda (the son born of a women who had intercourse with four persons), Datta (the son given by another), Krita (the son bought from another), Upakrita (the son coming to one out of gratitude), Svayam upagata (the son coming himself to give him away), Sahodha (the son born of a pregnant bride), Hina Yonidhrita (the son born of a wife of a lower caste.)

sn: पूर्वपूर्वतमाभावं मत्वा लिप्सेत वै सुतम्। उत्तमादवराः पुंसः काङ्क्षन्ते पुत्रमापदि॥
en: On the failure of getting offspring of the first class, the mother should try to get the offspring of the next class and so on. At the time of emergency (failure of offspring), men raise up sons by their accomplished younger brothers.

sn: अपत्यं धर्मफलदं श्रेष्ठं विन्दन्ति मानवाः। आत्मशुक्रादपि पृथे मनुः स्वायम्भुवोऽब्रवीत्॥
en: O Pritha, the self created Manu has said that men, failing to obtain son of their own, might raise up excellent virtue giving sons by others.

sn: तस्मात् प्रहेष्याम्यद्य त्वां हीनः प्रजननात् स्वयम्। सदृशाच्छ्रेयसो वा त्वं विद्ध्यपत्यं यशस्विनि॥
en: As I am destitute of the power of procreation, I command you to raise illustrious offspring by some men equal or superior to me.

sn: शृणु कुन्ति कथामेतां शारदण्डायिनी प्रति। सा वीरपत्नी गुरुणा नियुक्ता पुत्रजन्मनि॥
en: O Kunti, hear the history of that wife of a hero, the daughter of Sharadandayana, who raised offspring at the command of her lord.

sn: पुष्येण प्रयता स्नाता निशि कुन्ति चतुष्पथे। वरयित्वा द्विजं सिद्धं हुत्वा पुंसवनेऽनलम्।
en: O Kunti, after the bath when her season came, she went in the night to a place where four roads met. Worshipping a Brahmana who was crowned with ascetic success, she poured libations in the fire of Punsavana.

sn: कर्मण्यवसिते तस्मिन्सा तेनैव सहावसत्। तत्र त्रीञ्जनयामास दुर्जयादीन्महारथान्॥
en: After performing this, she lived with him; and thus were begotten on her three sons, Durjaya being the eldest.

sn: तथा त्वमपि कल्याणि ब्राह्मणात्तपसाधिकात्। मन्नियोगाद्यत क्षिप्रमपत्योत्पादनं प्रति॥
en: O greatly fortunate lady, like her you too at my command raise offspring by some Brahmana who is superior to me in ascetic merits.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्ता महाराज कुन्ती पाण्डुमभाषत। कुरूणामृषभं वीरं तदा भूमिपति पतिम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : O great king, having been thus assessed Kunti replied to her heroic lord, king Pandu, the best of the Kurus.

sn: न मामर्हसि धर्मज्ञ वक्तुमेवं कथंचना धर्मपत्नीमभिरतां त्वयि राजीवलोचने॥
en: Kunti said: O virtuous one, you should not say so to me. O lotus eyed one, I am your lawfully wedded wife, ever devoted to you.

sn: त्वमेव तु महाबाहो मय्यपत्यानि भारत। वीर वीर्योपपन्नानि धर्मतो जनयिष्यसि॥
en: O mighty armed descendant of the Bharata race, you should in righteousness beget on me greatly powerful children.

sn: स्वर्गं मनुजशार्दूल गच्छेयं सहिता त्वया। अपत्याय च मां गच्छ त्वमेव कुरुनन्दन।॥
en: O best of men, I shall go to heaven with you. O descendant of Kuru, embrace me to beget offspring

sn: न ह्यहं मनसाप्यन्यं गच्छेयं त्वदृते नरम्। त्वत्तः प्रतिविशिष्टश्च कोऽन्योऽस्ति भुवि मानवः॥
en: I shall not certainly, even in imagination, accept any other man except you in my embrace. Who is there in this world who could be superior to you?

sn: इमां च तावद् धर्मात्मन् पौराणीं शृणु मे कथाम्। परिश्रुतां विशालाक्ष कीर्तयिष्यामि यामहम्॥
en: O virtuous minded man, O large eyed one, hear the (following) Pauranika narrative which was heard by me and which I shall now narrate to you.

sn: व्युषिताश्व इति ख्यातो बभूव किल पार्थिवः। पुरा परमधर्मिष्ठः पूरोर्वंशविवर्धनः॥
en: "In ancient times there was a king known by the name of Vyushitashva, the expander of the Puru dynasty, who was exceedingly virtuous.

sn: तस्मिंश्च यजमाने वै धर्मात्मनि महाभुजे। उपागमस्ततो देवाः सेन्द्रा देवर्षिभिः सह॥
en: In the sacrifice which that virtuous and mighty armed man performed, the celestial with Indra and Devarshis came.

sn: अमाद्यदिन्द्रः सोमेन दक्षिणाभिर्द्विजातयः। व्युषिताश्वस्य राजर्षेस्ततो यज्ञे महात्मनः॥ देवा ब्रह्मर्षयश्चैव चक्रुः कर्म स्वयं तदा। व्युषिताश्वस्ततो राजन्नति मान् व्यरोचत॥
en: In the sacrifice of the illustrious royal sage Vyushitashva, Indra was so intoxicated with Soma drink and the Brahmanas with Dakshina (offerings) that the celestial and the Brahmana Rishis performed everything of it themselves. O king, thereupon Vyushitashva began to shine over all creatures.

sn: सर्वभूतान् प्रति यथा तपन: शिशिरात्यये। स विजित्य गृहीत्वा च नृपतीन् राजसत्तमः॥ प्राच्यानुदीच्या पाश्चान्यान् दाक्षिणात्यानकालयत्। अश्वमेधे महायज्ञे व्युषिताश्वः प्रतापवान्॥
en: O king, thereupon Vyushitashva began to shine over all creatures like the sun after the season of frost. O best of kings, he conquered all the monarchs of the east, west, north and south and he exacted tribute from them all.

sn: बभूव स हि राजेन्द्रो दशनागबलान्वितः। अप्यत्र गाथां गायन्ति ये पुराणविदो जनाः॥ व्युषिताश्वे यशोवृद्ध मनुष्येन्द्रे कुरूत्तम। व्युषिताश्वः समुद्रान्तां विजित्येमां वसुंधराम्॥ अपालयत् सर्ववर्णान् पिता पुत्रानिवौरसान्। यजमानो महायज्ञैर्ब्राह्मणेभ्यो धनं ददौ॥
en: O king, he was endued with the strength of ten elephants. Vyushitashva did all this in his great Horse sacrifice. O best of the Kurus, the men, learned in the Puranas, sing this verse in order to increase the fame of that king of men, Vyushitashva. Vyushitashva has conquered the whole earth as far as sea. He protects all classes of his subjects as a father protects his own sons. He performed many sacrifices and gave away much wealth to the Brahmanas,

sn: अनन्तरत्नान्यादाय स जहार महाक्रतून्। सुषाव च बहून् सोमान् सोमसंस्थास्ततान च॥
en: Collecting jewels and precious stones, he performed afterwards great sacrifices. Extracting a large quantity of Soma juice, he performed (the great sacrifice) Soma Sanstha.

sn: आसीत् काक्षीवती चास्य भार्या परमसम्मता। भद्रा नाम मनुष्येन्द्र रूपेणासदृशी भुवि॥
en: O king, his beloved wife was the daughter of Kakshivan, named Bhadra, unrivalled on earth for her beauty.

sn: कामयामासतुस्तौ च परस्परमिति श्रुतम्। स तस्यां कामसम्पन्नो यक्ष्मणा समपद्यत॥ तेनाचिरेण कालेन जगामास्तमिवांशुमान्। तस्मिन् प्रेते मनुष्येन्द्रे भार्यास्य भृशदुःखिता॥
en: We have heard, they deeply loved each other. He was seldom separated from his wife. Intercourse with her brought in consumption and he soon died sinking like the sun in its glory. She became, afflicted with great grief at her husband's death.

sn: अपुत्रा पुरुषव्याघ्र विललापेति नः श्रुतम्। भद्रा परमदुःखार्ता तन्निबोध जनाधिप॥
en: O best of men, O king, hear how Bhadra, being childless and afflicted with grief, bewailed for her husband. I shall recount it.

sn: भद्रोवाच नारी परमधर्मज्ञ सर्वा भर्तृविनाकृता। पतिं विना जीवति या न सा जीवति दुःखिता॥
en: Bhadra said: O greatly learned man in religious precepts, women serve no purpose when their husband is dead. She who lives without her husband lives a miserable life.

sn: पतिं विना मृतं श्रेयो नार्याः क्षत्रियपुङ्गव। त्वद्गतिं गन्तुमिच्छामि प्रसीदस्व नयस्व माम्॥ त्वया हीना क्षणमपि नाहं जीवितुमुत्सहे। प्रसादं कुरु मे राजनितस्तूर्णं नयस्व माम्॥
en: O best of Kshatriyas, death is preferable to one whom has her husband. I wish to follow the way you have gone. Be kind towards me and take me with you. I am unable in your absence to bear life for a moment. O kind to me and take me soon away.

sn: पृष्ठतोऽनुगमिष्यामि समेषु विषमेषु च। त्वामहं नरशार्दूल गच्छन्तमनिवर्तितुम्॥
en: O best of men, I shall follow you over even and uneven ground. Going with you, I shall never return again.

sn: छायेवानुगता राजन् सततं वशवर्तिनी। भविष्यामि नरव्याघ्र नित्यं प्रियहिते रता॥
en: O king, I shall follow you as a shadow. I shall be always obedient to you. O best of kings, I shall ever remain engaged in doing your favourite works,

sn: अद्यप्रभृति मां राजन् कष्टा हृदयशोषणः। आधयोऽभिभविष्यन्ति त्वामृते पुष्करेक्षण॥
en: O king, O lotus eyed, from this day the heart sucking affliction will always overwhelm me for your death.

sn: अभाग्यया मया नूनं वियुक्ताः सहचारिणः। तेन मे विप्रयोगोऽयमुपपन्नस्त्वया सह॥
en: Unfortunate am I! some loving couple had no doubt been separated by me in my former life. From this I am separated from you.

sn: विप्रयुक्ता तु या पत्या मुहूर्तमपि जीवति। दुःखं जीवति सा पापा नरकस्येव पार्थिव॥
en: O king, she, who lives even for a moment after being separated from her husband that sinful woman, lives in great misery and in hell.

sn: संयुक्ता विप्रयुक्ताश्च पूर्वदेहे कृता मया। तदिदं कर्मभिः पापैः पूर्वदेहेषु संचितम्॥ दुःखं मामनुसम्प्राप्तं राजंस्त्वद्विप्रयोगजम्। अद्यप्रभृत्यहं राजन् कुशसंस्तरशायिनी। भविष्याम्यसुखाविष्टा त्वदर्शनपरायणा॥
en: Some loving couple must have been separated by me in my former birth; from that sin, acquired in my former body. O king, I now suffer this great pain in consequence of your separation from me. O king, from this day I shall lie on Kusha grass.

sn: दर्शयस्व नरव्याघ्र शाधि मामसुखान्विताम्। कृपणां चाथ करुणं विलपन्ती नरेश्वर॥
en: I shall abstain from every luxury, being ever desirous of seeing you. O best of men, show yourself to me. O king of men, O lord, command your wretched and bitterly weeping wife, plunged in great misery.

sn: कुन्युवाच एवं बहुविधं तस्यां विलपन्त्यां पुनः पुनः। तं शवं सम्परिष्वज्य वाक् किलान्तर्हिताब्रवीत्॥
en: Kunti said: It was thus she bewailed again and again embracing the corpse (of her husband). She was then addressed by an invisible voice.

sn: उत्तिष्ठ भद्रे गच्छ त्वं ददानीह वरं तव। जनयिष्याम्यपत्यानि त्वय्यहं चारुहासिनि॥
en: The Voice said : O Bhadra, rise up and leave this place. I grant you this boon. O lady of sweet smiles, I shall beget offspring on you.

sn: आत्मकीये वरारोहे शयनीये चतुर्दशीम्। अष्टमी वा ऋतुस्नाता संविशेथा मया सह॥
en: O beautiful featured lady, lie down with me on your bed on the eighth or the fourteenth day of the moon after the bath of your season.

sn: एवमुक्ता तु सा देवी तथा चक्रे पतिव्रता। यथोक्तमेव तद्वाक्यं भद्रा पुत्रार्थिनी तदा॥
en: Kunti said : Having been thus addressed by the invisible voice, the chaste lady (Bhadra), desirous of offspring, did as she was directed.

sn: सा तेन सुषवे देवी शवेन भरतर्षभ। त्रीन् शाल्वांश्चतुरो मद्रान् सुतान् भरतसत्तम॥
en: O best of the Bharatas, O excellent descendant of the Bharata race, that lady gave birth of three Shalvas and four Madras by that corpse."

sn: तथा त्वमपि मय्येवं मनसा भरतर्षभ। शक्तो जनयितुं पुत्रांस्तपोयोगबलान्वितः॥
en: O best of the Bharatas, you too like him beget offspring by your ascetic power.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्तस्तया राजा तां देवीं पुनरब्रवीत्। धर्मविद् धर्मसंयुक्तमिदं वचनमुत्तमम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having been thus addressed, the king (Pandu), learned in the precepts of religious spoke these words of virtuous import to that lady (his wife).

sn: पाण्डुरुवाच एवमेतत् पुरा कुन्ति व्युषिताश्वश्चकार ह। यथा त्वयोक्तं कल्याणि स ह्यासीदमरोपमः॥
en: Pandu said: O Kunti, what you have said is true. Vyushitashva of old did exactly as you said; he was like a celestial.

sn: अथ त्विदं प्रवक्ष्यामि धर्मतत्त्वं निबोध मे। पुराणमृषिभिईष्टं धर्मविद्भिर्महात्मभिः॥
en: But I shall tell you the religious precepts which the illustrious Rishis, learned in the precepts of virtue, said in the Puranas.

sn: अनावृताः किल पुरा स्त्रिय आसन्वरानने। कामचारविहारिण्यः स्वतंत्राश्चारुहासिनी॥
en: O beautiful featured lady, O lady of sweet smiles, women were not formerly kept within the house. They used to go about freely and enjoyed as they liked.

sn: तासां व्युच्चरमाणानां कौमारात्सुभगे पतीन्। नाधर्मोऽभूद्वरारोहे स हि धर्मः पुराऽभवत्॥
en: O fortunate lady, O beautiful one, they had promiscuous intercourse form their maidenhood and they were not regarded sinful, for it was the custom of the age.

sn: तं चैव धर्म पौराणं तिर्यग्योनिगताः प्रजाः। अद्याप्यनुविधीयन्ते कामक्रोधविवर्जिताः॥
en: That very usage of the olden time is up to date followed by birds and beasts and they are free from anger and passions (for this promiscuous intercourse).

sn: प्रमाणदृष्टो धर्मोऽयं पूज्यते च महर्षिभिः। उत्तरेषु च रम्भोरु कुरुष्वद्यापि पूज्यते॥
en: O lady of tapering thighs, the practice, being sanctioned by presidents, is praised by great Rishis; it is still regarded with respect by the Northern Kurus.

sn: स्त्रीणामनुग्रहकरः स हि धर्मः सनातनः। अस्मिंस्तु लोके न चिरान्मर्यादेयं शुचिस्मिते॥ स्थापिता येन यस्माच्च तन्मे विस्तरतः शृणु।
en: O lady of sweet smiles, this eternal usage, very favourable to the women, had the sanction of antiquity; the present practice has been established only very lately. Hear, I shall narrate to you in detail who established it and why.

sn: बभूवोद्दालको नाम महर्षिरिति नः श्रुतम्॥ श्वेतकेतुरिति ख्यातः पुत्रस्तस्याभवन्मुनिः।
en: We have heard that there was a great Rishi, named Uddalaka. He had a son, known by the name of Svetaketu, who was also a Rishi.

sn: मर्यादेयं कृता तेन धा वै श्वेतकेतुना॥ कोपात्कमलपत्राक्षि यदर्थं तन्निबोध मे।
en: O lotus eyed one, the present virtuous practice was established by that Svetaketu in anger. I shall tell you why he did it.

sn: वेतकेतोः किल पुरा समक्षं मातरं पितुः॥ जग्राह ब्राह्मणः पाणौ गच्छाव इति चाब्रवीत्।
en: One day, in the time of yore, in the very presence of Shvetaketu's father, a Brahmana came and taking his (Shvetaketu's) mother by the hand said, “Let us go".

sn: ऋषिपुत्रस्ततः कोपं चकारामर्षचोदितः॥ मातरं तां तथा दृष्ट्वा नीयमानां बलादिव।
en: Having seen his mother taken away as if by force, the son of the Rishi grew angry and became very much affected with sorrow.

sn: क्रुद्धं तं तु पिता दृष्ट्वा श्वेतकेतुमुवाच ह॥ मा तात कोपं कास्त्विमेष धर्मः सनातनः।
en: Seeing him angry, his father told Shvetaketu, “O child, do not be angry. This is an eternal usage.

sn: अनावृता हि सर्वेषां वर्णानामङ्गना भुवि॥ यथा गावः स्थितास्तात स्वे स्वे वर्णे तथा प्रजाः।
en: The women of all the orders on earth are free. O son, men, in this matter as regards their respective orders, act as kine."

sn: ऋषिपुत्रोऽथ तं धर्मं श्वेतकेतुर्न चक्षमे॥ चकार चैव मर्यादामिमां स्त्रीपुंसयोर्भुवि।
en: The son of the Rishi, Svetaketu, disapproved of this usage and he established the following practice on earth as regards men and women.

sn: मानुषेषु महाभागे न त्वेवान्येषु जन्तुषु॥ तदाप्रभृति मर्यादा स्थितेयमिति नः श्रुतम्।
en: O greatly illustrious lady, we have heard that the present practice among men and women dates from that day but not among other animals.

sn: श्वेतकेतुरुवाच व्युच्चरन्त्याः पतिं नार्या अद्यप्रभृति पातकम्॥ भ्रूणहत्यासमं घोरं भविष्यत्यसुखावहम्।
en: Svetaketu said: The wife, not adhering to her husband, will be sinful from this date; she will commit as great and painful sin as the killing of an embryo.

sn: भार्यां तथा व्युच्चरतः कौमारब्रह्मचारिणीम्॥ पतिव्रतामेतदेव भविता पातकं भुवि।
en: The men who will go to other women neglecting a chaste and loving wife who has from her maidenhood observed a vow of purity, will commit the same sin.

sn: पत्या नियुक्ता या चैव पत्नी पुत्रार्थमेव च॥ न करिष्यति तस्याश्च भविष्यति तदेव हि।
en: The woman, who being commanded by her husband to raise offspring, will refuse to do it, will commit also the some sin.

sn: इति तेन पुरा भीरु मर्यादा स्थापिता बलात्॥ उद्दालकस्य पुत्रेण धा वै श्वेतकेतुना।
en: Pandu said: O timid lady, it was thus established by force in olden time the present virtuous usage by Uddalaka's son Shvetaketu.

sn: सौदासेन च रम्भोरु नियुक्ता पुत्रजन्मनि॥ मदयन्ती जगामर्षि वसिष्ठामिति नः श्रुतम्।
en: O lady of the tapering thighs, we have heard that Madayanti, being appointed by (her husband) Saudasa, went to Rishi Vasishtha to raise up offspring.

sn: तस्माल्लेभे च सा पुत्रमश्मकं नाम भाविनी॥ एवं कृतवती सापि भर्तुः प्रियचिकीर्षया।
en: That lady obtained from his a son, named Asmaka. She did this, moved by the desire of doing good to her husband.

sn: अस्माकमपि ते जन्म विदितं कमलेक्षण॥ कृष्णद्वैपायनाद्भीरु कुरूणां वंशवृद्धये।
en: O louts-eyed one, O timid girl, you know our birth, begotten by Krishna Dvaipayana, in order to expand the Kuru race.

sn: अत एतानि सर्वाणि कारणानि समीक्ष्य वै॥ ममैतद्वचनं धर्म्यं कर्तुमर्हस्यनिन्दिते।
en: O faultless one, seeing all these precedents, you should do my bidding which is not inconsistent with virtue.

sn: ऋतावृतौ राजपुत्रि स्त्रिया भर्ता पतिव्रते॥ नातिवर्तव्य इत्येवं धर्मं धर्मविदो विदुः। शेषष्वन्येषु कालेषु स्वातन्त्र्यं स्त्री किलार्हति॥
en: O princess, O devoted wife, the men learned in the precepts of virtue, said that a wife in her season must seek her husband, though she may be free at other times.

sn: धर्ममेवं जनाः सन्तः पुराणं परिचक्षते। भर्ता भार्यां राजपुत्रि धर्म्य वाधर्म्यमेव वा॥ यद् ब्रूयात् तत् तथा कार्यमिति वेदविदो विदुः।
en: The wise have said that this was the ancient practice. But, O princess, men, learned in the Vedas, have declared that whether the act be sinful or sinless, it is the duty of the wife to do what her husband commands.

sn: विशेषतः पुत्रगृध्नी हीन: प्रजननात् स्वयम्॥ यथाहमनवद्याङ्गि पुत्रदर्शनलालसः। तथा रक्ताङ्गुलितलः पद्मपत्रनिभः शुभे॥ प्रसादार्थं मया तेऽयं शिरस्यभ्युद्यतोऽञ्जलिः।
en: O lady of faultless features, especially I who am deprived of the power of procreation, having yet become desirous of seeing son, should more to be obeyed by you. O amiable girl, joining my palms furnished with rosy fingers like lotus-leaves, I place my hand on your head to propitiate you.

sn: मन्नियोगात् सुकेशान्ते द्विजातेस्तपसाधिकात्॥ पुत्रान् गुणसमायुक्तानुत्पादयितुमर्हसि। त्वत्कृतेऽहं पुथुश्रोणि गच्छेयं पुत्रिणां गतिम्॥
en: O lady of beautiful hair, you should raise accomplished sons at my command by the help of same Brahmanas possessed of great ascetic merits. O lady of beautiful hips, by your doing this, I shall go to the way reserved for those that are blessed with sons.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्ता ततः कुन्ती पाण्डुं परपुरंजयम्। प्रत्युवाच वरारोहा भर्तुः प्रियहिते रता॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having been thus addressed by that subjugator of hostile cities, Pandu, the beautiful Kunti, ever engaged in doing good to her husband, thus replied-

sn: पितृवेश्मन्यहं बाला नियुक्तातिथिपूजने। उग्रं पर्यचरं तत्र ब्राह्मणं संशितव्रतम्॥ निगूढनिश्चयं धर्मे यं तं दुर्वाससं विदुः। तमहं संशितात्मानं सर्वयत्नैरतोषयम्॥
en: O lord, I was engaged in my girlhood at my father's house in attending upon all guests. I attentively served the Brahmanas of rigid Vows. I gratified with all attentions that Brahmana, known as Durvasa, who had all his passions under control and who was acquainted with all the mysteries of religion.

sn: स मेऽभिचारसंयुक्तमाचष्ट भगवान् वरम्। मन्त्रं त्विमं च मे प्रादादब्रवीच्चैव मामिदम्॥
en: Pleased with the attention with which waited upon him, that illustrious (Brahmana) gave me a boon in the form of a Mantra. He told me-

sn: यं यं देवं त्वमेतेन मन्त्रेणावाहयिष्यसि। अकामो वा सकामो वा वशं ते समुपैष्यति॥
en: “Any of the celestials, whom you will call by this (Mantra), will be obedient to you, whether he likes it or not.

sn: तस्य तस्य प्रसादात् ते राज्ञि पुत्रो भविष्यति। इत्युक्ताहं तदानेन पितृवेश्मनि भारत॥
en: O princes, by each of their favour, you shall have offspring." descendant of the Bharata race, this was told to me by him at my father's house.

sn: ब्राह्मणस्य वचस्तथ्यं तस्य कालोऽयमागतः। अनुज्ञाता त्वया देवमाह्वयेयमहं नृप। तेन मन्त्रेण राजर्षे यथास्यान्नौ प्रजा हिता॥
en: O king, the words, uttered by the Brahmana, can never be false; the time has come when they may yield fruits. Commanded by you, I can call the celestial.

sn: आवाहयामि कं देवं ब्रूहि सत्यवतां वर। त्वत्तोऽनुज्ञाप्रतीक्षां मां विद्ध्यस्मिन् कर्मणि स्थिताम्॥
en: By that Mantra to rise up good offspring. O royal sage, O foremost of truthful men, tell me which of the celestials I shall call. Know, wait your commands in this matter.

sn: पाण्डुरुवाच अद्यैव त्वं वरारोहे प्रयतस्व यथाविधि। धर्ममावाहय शुभे स हि लोकेषु पुण्यभाक्॥
en: Pandu said : O beautiful lady, O amiable one try to do it today in the proper form. Call Dharma (the god of justice), for he is the most virtuous in the world.

sn: अधर्मेण न नो धर्मः संयुज्यति कथंचन। लोकश्चायं वरारोहे धर्मोऽयमिति मन्यते॥ धार्मिकश्च कुरूणां स भविष्यति न संशयः। धर्मेण चापि दत्तस्य नाधर्मे रंस्यते मनः॥ तस्माद् धर्मं पुरस्कृत्य नियता त्वं शुचिस्मिते। उपचाराभिचाराभ्यां धर्ममावाहयस्व वै॥
en: O beautiful lady, Dharma will ever be able to pollute us with sin and people will also consider that what we do is never sinful. There is no doubt the son thus begotten will be virtuous among the Kurus. Begotten by Dharma, his mind will never be in sin. Therefore, O lady of sweets smiles,, keeping virtue before your eyes and observing all vows, call Dharma by the help of your solicitations and incantations.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच सा तथोक्ता तथेत्युक्त्वा तेन भ; वराङ्गना। अभिवाद्याभ्यनुज्ञाता प्रदक्षिणमवर्तत॥
en: Vaishampayana said : That best of women, (Kunti), having been thus addressed, said-"Be it so". She then went round him (for seven times) and resolved to do his bidding.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच संवत्सरधृते गर्भे गान्धार्या जनमेजय। आह्वयामास वै कुन्ती गभार्थे धर्ममच्युतम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : O Janamejaya, when Gandhari was pregnant for a year, it was then that Kunti called the eternal Dharma for offspring.

sn: सा बलिं त्वरिता देवी धर्मायोपजहार ह। जजाप विधिवज्जष्यं दत्तं दुर्वाससा पुरा॥
en: That lady (Kunti) offered adorations to Dharma and repeated in the proper form the Mantra, formerly given to her by Durvasa.

sn: आजगाम ततो देवो धर्मो मन्त्रबलात् ततः। विमाने सूर्यसंकाशे कुन्ती यत्र जपस्थिता॥
en: The deity Dharma, being overpowered by the Mantra, came on his car resplendent as the sun to the place where Kunti was seated.

sn: विहस्य तां ततो ब्रूयाः कुन्ति किं ते ददाम्यहम्। सा तं विहस्यमानापि पुत्रं देह्यब्रवीदिदम्॥
en: Smiling he said to her, “O Kunti, what am I to give you?" Kunti also smilingly said, “You must give me offspring.'

sn: संयुक्ता सा हि धर्मेण योगमूर्तिधरेण ह। लेभे पुत्रं वरारोहा सर्वप्राणभृतां हितम्॥
en: She was united with Dharma in his Yoga (spiritual) form and that beautiful lady obtained a son devoted to the good of all creatures.

sn: ऐन्द्रे चन्द्रसमायुक्ते मुहूर्तेऽभिजितेऽष्टमे। दिवामध्यगते सूर्ये तिथौ पूर्णेऽतिपूजिते॥ समृद्धयशसं कुन्ती सुषाव प्रवरं सुतम्। जातमात्रे सुते तस्मिन् वागुवाचाशरीरिणी॥
en: She gave birth to an excellent son, who became afterwards greatly famous, at the eighth Muhurata called Abhijit of the hour of noon of that very auspicious day of the eight month, the fifth of the white fort-night, when the star Jyeshtha in conjunction with moon was in ascendant. As soon as the child was born, an invisible voice said-

sn: एष धर्मभृतां श्रेष्ठो भविष्यति नरोत्तमः। विक्रान्तः सत्यवाक् त्वेव राजा पृथ्व्यां भविष्यति॥
en: “This (child) will be the west of men and the foremost of all the virtuous. He will be truthful and (also) greatly powerful; he will be the ruler of the earth.

sn: युधिष्ठिर इति ख्यातः पाण्डोः प्रथमजः सुतः। भविता प्रथितो राजा त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतः॥
en: This eldest son of Pandu will be known as Yudhisthira: he bill be a famous king, known all over the three worlds.

sn: यशसा तेजसा चैव वृत्तेन च समन्वितः। धार्मिकं तं सुतं लब्ध्वा पाण्डुस्तां पुनरब्रवीत्॥
en: He will be endued with splendour, fame and vows. Having obtained this virtuous son, Pandu again told her.

sn: प्राहुः क्षत्रं बलज्येष्ठं बलज्येष्ठं सुतं वृणु। ततस्तथोक्ता भ; तु वायुमेवाजुहाव सा॥
en: "The wise say that Kshatriyas are the foremost in strength: therefore, ask for a son of great strength" having been thus addressed, she invoked Vayu.

sn: ततस्तामागतो वायुर्मुगारूढो महाबलः। किं ते कुन्ति ददाम्यद्य ब्रूहि यत् ते हृदि स्थितम्।१२।।
en: Thereupon the greatly strong Vayu came to her riding on a deer, (and he asked), “O Kunti, what am I to give you? Tell me what is in your mind."

sn: सा सलज्जा विहस्याह पुत्रं देहि सुरोत्तम। बलवन्तं महाकायं सर्वदर्पप्रभञ्जनम्॥
en: Smiling in bashfulness, she said, "O best of celestials, give me a son, who is strong, who is huge and how is capable of humbling the pride of everybody."

sn: तस्माज्जज्ञे महाबाहुर्भीमो भीमपराक्रमः। तमप्यतिबलं जातं वागुवाचाशरीरिणी॥ सर्वेषां बलिनां श्रेष्ठो जातोऽयमिति भारत। इदमत्यद्भुतं चासीज्जातमात्रे वृकोदरे॥ यदङ्कात् पतितो मातुः शिलां गात्रैर्व्यचूर्णयत्। कुन्ती व्याघ्रभयोद्विग्ना सहसोत्पतिता किल॥ नान्वबुध्यत संसुप्तमुत्सङ्गे स्वे वृकोदरम्। ततः स वज्रसंघातः कुमारो न्यपतद् गिरौ॥ पतता तेन शतधा शिला गात्रैर्विचूर्णिता। तां शिलां चूर्णितां दृष्ट्वा पाण्डुर्विस्मयमागतः॥
en: By him was born Bhima, endued with great strength: and on the birth of this greatly strong man, an invisible voice said, “This child will be foremost of all endued with strength." o descendant of the Bharata race, the following extraordinary incident happened as soon as Bhima was born. Falling from his mother's lap on the mountain, he broke into fragments the stone on which he fell. Kunti suddenly rose up from the fear of a tiger, forgetting that the child lay asleep on her lap. As she rose, the child, whose body was as hard as the thunder-bolt fell on the stone and broke it into a hundred pieces. Seeing the breaking of the stone, Pandu became very much astonished.

sn: यस्मिन्नहनि भीमस्तु जज्ञे भरतसत्तम। दुर्योधनोऽपि तत्रैव प्रजज्ञे वसुधाधिपः॥
en: O best of the Bharatas, the day on which Bhima was born, on that very bay, the king of the world, Duryodhana, was also born.

sn: जाते वृकोदरे पाण्डुरिदं भूयोऽन्वचिन्तयत्। कथं नु मे वरः पुत्रो लोकश्रेष्ठो भवेदिति॥
en: On the birth of Bhima, Pandu again began to reflect, “How can I obtain a very superior son who will be the best of men?

sn: दैवे पुरुषकारे च लोकोऽयं सम्प्रतिष्ठितः। तत्र दैवं तु विधिना कालयुक्तेन लभ्यते॥
en: This world depends on Daiva (Destiny) and Purushartha (exertion). But Destiny is gained in time by the grace of Providence,

sn: इन्द्रो हि राजा देवानां प्रधान इति नः श्रुतम्। अप्रमेयबलोत्साहो वीर्यवानमितद्युतिः॥ तं तोषयित्वा तपसा पुत्रं लप्स्ये महाबलम्। यं दास्यति स मे पुत्रं स वरीयान् भविष्यति॥ अमानुषान् मानुषांश्च संग्रामे स हनिष्यति। कर्मणा मनसा वाचा तस्मात् तप्स्ये महत् तपः॥
en: We have heard that Indra is the foremost (among the celestial) and the king of the Devas. He is endued with immeasurable might, energy, Prowess and glory. Gratifying him by my asceticism, I shall obtain a greatly powerful son. The son that he will give me will be superior to all. He will be capable of defeating the inhabitants of earth and those who are not of this earth. I shall, therefore practice severest asceticism with heart, deed and speech."

sn: ततः पाण्डुर्महाराजो मन्त्रयित्वा महर्षिभिः। दिदेश कुन्त्याः कौरव्यो व्रतंसांवत्सरं शुभम्॥
en: Thereupon the descendant of Kuru, the great king Pandu, after consulting with the great Rishis, commanded Kunti to observe an auspicious vow for one full year.

sn: आत्मना च महाबाहुरेकपादस्थितोऽभवत्। उग्रं च तप आस्थाय परमेण समाधिना॥ आरिराधयिषुर्देवं त्रिदशानां तमीश्वरम्। सूर्येण सह धर्मात्मा पर्यतप्यत भारत॥ तं तु कालेन महता वासवः प्रत्यपद्यता
en: That mighty-armed man (Pandu), himself stood upon his one leg and began to perform the severest asceticism and penances. He practiced severe austerities from morning to evening with his mind deep in meditation in order to gratify the lord of the celestials. It was after a long time that Indra appeared.

sn: शक्र उवाच पुत्रं तव प्रदास्यामि त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतम्॥
en: Indra said: I shall give you a son who will be famous all over the three worlds.

sn: ब्राह्मणानां गवां चैव सुहृदां चार्थसाधकम्। दुहृदां शोकजननं सर्वबान्धवनन्दनम्॥ सुतं तेऽत्र्यं प्रदास्यामि सर्वामित्रविनाशनम्।
en: Who will promote the welfare of the Brahmanas, kine and all honest men. The son that I shall give you will be the chastiser of the wicked and the delight of his friends and relations. He will the foremost of all and the slayer of all foes.

sn: इत्युक्तः कौरवो राजा वासवेन महात्मना॥ उवाच कुन्ती धर्मात्मा देवराजवचः स्मरन्। उदर्कस्तव कल्याणि तुष्टो देवगणेश्वरः॥ दातुमिच्छति ते पुत्रं यथा संकल्पितं त्वया। अतिमानुषकर्माणं यशस्विनीमरिंदमम्॥ नीतिमन्तं महात्मानमादित्यसतेजसम्। दुराधर्ष क्रियावन्तमतीवाद्भुतदर्शनम्॥
en: Having been thus addressed by the illustrious Indra, the virtuous Kuru king (Pandu), remembering the words of the king of the celestials said to Kunti, O fortunate one, your vow has been successful. The king of the celestials is gratified. He is willing to give you a son such as you desire to have (who will be) of superior human achievements and great fame (how will be) a chastiser of enemies and a greatly wise man, (who will possess) a great son, (who will be) invincible battle, (who will be) as effulgent as the sun (who will be) very handsome and endued with all the Kshatriya splendour.

sn: पुत्रं जनय सुश्रोणि धाम क्षत्रियतेजसाम्। लब्धः प्रसादो देवेन्द्रात् तभाह्वय शुचिस्मिते॥
en: O lady of beautiful thighs, O lady of sweet smiles, raise up a son. Call the lord of the celestials, I have gratified him.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्ताः ततः शक्रमाजुहाव यशस्विनी। अथाजगाम देवेन्द्रो जनयामास चार्जुनम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having been thus addressed, the illustrious Kunti invoked Indra. The lord of the celestials came begot Arjuna.

sn: जातमात्रे कुमारे तु वागुवाचाशरीरिणी। महागम्भीरनिर्घोषा नभो नादयती तदा॥
en: As soon as the prince was born, an invisible voice filled the whole sky with a laud and deep roar.

sn: शृण्वतां सर्वभूतानां तेषां चाश्रमवासिनाम्। कुन्तीमाभाष्य विस्पष्टमुवाचेदं शुचिस्मिताम्॥
en: Addressing Kunti, it said a distinct voice in the hearing of every creature dwelling in that hermitage,

sn: कार्तवीर्यसम: कुंन्ति शिवतुल्यपराक्रमः। एष शक्रः इवाजय्यो यशस्ते प्रथयिष्यति॥ अदित्या विष्णुना प्रीतिर्यथाभूदभिवर्धिता। तथा विष्णुसमः प्रीति वर्धयिष्यति तेऽर्जुनः॥
en: "O Kunti, (this child) will be equal to Kartavirya and Shiva in prowess he will be invincible like Indra himself. He will spread your fame everywhere. As Vishnu enhanced Aditi's joy, so Arjuna (this child) like Vishnu will enhance your joy.

sn: एष मद्रान् वशे कृत्वा कुरूंश्च सह सोमकैः। चेदिकाशिकरूपांश्च कुरुलक्ष्मी वहिष्यति॥
en: He will maintain the Lakshmi(goddess of prosperity) of the Kuru dynasty by subjugating Madra, the Somakas with the Kurus, Chedi, Kashi and Karusha.

sn: एतस्य भुजवीर्येण खाण्डवे हव्यवाहनः। मेदसा सर्वभूतानां तृप्तिं यास्यति वै पराम्॥
en: Agni will be greatly gratified with the fat of all creatures which will be burnt in the Khandava (forest) through the strength of arms of this (hero).

sn: ग्रामणीश्च महीपालानेष जित्वा महाबलः। भ्रातृभिः सहितो वीरस्त्रीन् मेधानाहरिष्यति॥
en: This greatly powerful hero with his brothers will conquer all the weak kings and perform three great horse-sacrifices.

sn: जामदग्न्यसमः कुन्ति विष्णुतुल्यपराक्रमः। एष वीर्यवतां श्रेष्ठो भविष्यति महायशाः॥
en: O Kunti, he will be equal to the son of Jamadagni (Parashurama)and Vishnu in prowess. He will be the foremost of all men endued with great strength he will be greatly famous.

sn: एष युद्धे महादेवं तोषयिष्यति शंकरम्। अस्त्रं पाशुपते नाम तस्मात् तुष्टादवाप्स्यति॥ निवातकवचा नाम दैत्या विबुधविद्विषः। शक्राज्ञया महाबाहुस्तान् वधिष्यति ते सुतः॥
en: He will gratify in battle the great god Shankara (Shiva) and he will receive from him a weapon, named Pashupata, which will he given to him with Pleasure. By command of Indra, your this mighty-armed son will kill those Daityas, called Nivatkavachas, who are enemies of the celestials.

sn: तथा दिव्यानि चास्त्राणि निखिलेनाहरिष्यति। विप्रणष्टां श्रियं चायमाहर्ता पुरुषर्षभः॥
en: He will also acquire all kinds of celestial weapons and this best of men will retrieve the lost fortunes of his race."

sn: एतामत्युद्धतां वाचं कुन्ती शुश्राव सूतके। वाचमुच्चारितामुच्चैस्तां निशम्य तपस्विनाम्॥ बभूव परमो हर्षः शतशृङ्गनिवासिनाम्। तथा देवनिकायानां सेन्द्राणां च दिवौकसाम्॥
en: Kunti heard these extraordinary words in her lying-in-room. Having heard these words, so loudly uttered, the ascetics, dwelling on that mountain with hundred peaks and the celestial with Indra sitting on their cars, became exceedingly happy.

sn: आकाशे दुन्दुभीनां च बभूव तुमुलः स्वनः। उदतिष्ठन्महाघोषः पुष्पवृष्टिभिरावृतः॥
en: The sounds of drums of drums rose in the sky and made a great noise; and the whole place was covered with the showers of flowers.

sn: समवेत्य च देवानां गणाः पार्थमपूजयन्। काद्रवेया वैनतेया गन्धर्वाप्सरसस्तथा। प्रजानां पतयः सर्वे सप्त चैव महर्षयः॥ भरद्वाजः कश्यपो गौतमक्ष विश्वामित्रो जमदग्निर्वसिष्ठः। यश्चोदितो भास्करेऽभूत् प्रणष्टे सोऽप्यत्रात्रिभगवानाजगाम॥
en: The various tribes of celestial assembled to adore Partha (Arjuna). The sons of Kadru, the son of Vinata, the Gandharvas. The seven great Rishis, namely, Bharadvaja, Kashyapa, Gautama, Vishvamitra, Jamadagni, Vasishtha and the illustrious Atri, who illuminated the world when the sun was lost came there.

sn: मरीचिरङ्गिराश्चैव पुलस्त्य: पुलहः क्रतुः। दक्षः प्रजापतिश्चैव गन्धर्वाप्सरसस्तथा॥
en: Marichi, Angira, Pulastya, Pulaha Kratu, the Prajapati Daksha, the Gandharvas and he Apsaras, all came there.

sn: दिव्यमाल्याम्बरधराः सर्वालंकारभूषिताः। उपगायान्ति वीभत्सुं नृत्यन्तेऽप्सरसां गणाः॥
en: The Apsara ladies, decked with celestial garlands and every ornament and attired in fine robes, began to dance chanting the Praises of Vibhatsa (Arjuna).

sn: तथा महर्षयश्चापि जेपुस्तत्र समन्ततः। गन्धर्वैः सहितः श्रीमान् प्रागायत च तुम्बरुः॥
en: The great Rishis began to utter the propitiatory Mantras every where and handsome Tumburu began to sing.

sn: भीमसेनोग्रसेनौ च ऊर्णायुरनधस्तथा। गोपतिधृतराष्ट्रश्च सूर्यवर्चास्तथाष्टमः॥ युगपस्तृणपः कार्पोिर्नन्दिश्चित्ररथस्तथा। त्रयोदशः शालिशिराः पर्जन्यश्च चतुर्दशः॥ कलिः पञ्चदशश्चैव नारदश्चात्र षोडशः। ऋत्वा बृहत्त्वा बृहकः करालश्च महामनाः॥ ब्रह्मचारी बहुगुणः सुवर्णश्चेति विश्रुतः। विश्वावसुर्भुमन्युश्च सुचन्द्रश्च शरुस्तथा॥ गतिमाधुर्यसम्पन्नौ विख्यातौ च हहाहुहू। इत्येते देवगन्धर्वा जग्मुस्तत्र नराधिप॥
en: Bhimasena, Ugrasena, Urnayus, Anagha, Gopati, Dhritarashtra, Suryavarcha, Yugapa, Trinapa, Krashni, Nandi, Chitraratha, Shalishira, Parjanya, Kali, Narada, Ritva, Brihattva, Brihaka, Karala, Brahmachari, Vahuguna, Suvarna, Vishvavasu, Bhumanyu, Suchandra, Sharu. the celebrated tribes of Haha and Huhu, gifted with sweet melody of voice, O king all these celestial and Gandharvas came there.

sn: तथैवाप्सरसो हृष्टाः सर्वालंकारभूषिताः। ननृतुर्वै महाभागा जगुश्चायतलोचनाः॥
en: Many famous Apsaras of large eyes, decked in every ornament, came there in joy to dance and sing.

sn: अनूचानानवद्या च गुणमुख्या गुणावरा। अद्रिका च तथा सोमा मिश्रकेशी त्वलम्बुषा॥ मरीचिः शुचिका चैव विद्युत्पर्णा तिलोत्तमा। अम्बिका लक्षणा क्षेमा देवी रम्भा मनोरमा॥ असिता च सुबाहुश्च सुप्रिया च वपुस्तथा। पुण्डरीका सुगन्धा च सुरसा च प्रमाथिनी॥ काम्या शारद्वती चैव ननृतुस्तत्र सङ्घशः। मेनका सहजन्या च कर्णिका पुञ्जिकस्थला॥ ऋतुस्थला घृताची च विश्वाची पूर्वचित्त्यपि। उम्लोचेति च विख्याता प्रम्लोचेति च ता दश॥ उर्वश्येकादशी तासां जगुश्चायतलोचनाः। धातार्यमा च मित्रश्च वरुणोंऽशो भगस्तथा॥ इन्द्रो विवस्वान् पूषा च त्वष्टा च सचिता तथा। पर्जन्यश्चैव विष्णुश्च आदित्या द्वादश स्मृताः। महिमानं पाण्डवस्य वर्धयन्तोऽम्बरे स्थिताः॥
en: Anuchana, Anavadhya, Gunamukha, Gunavara, Adrika, Soma, Mishrakeshi, Alambusha, Marichi, Suchika, Vidyutparna, Tilottama, Ambika, Lakshana, Kshema, Subahu, Supriya, Vapu, Pundarika, Sugandha, Surasa, Pramathini, Kamya and Sharadvati, all danced there together. Mainaka, Sahajanya, Karnika, Punjikasthala. Ritusthala, Ghritachi, Vishvachi, Purvachitti, Umlocha, Pramlocha and Urvashi, these large eyed dancing girls of heaven all came their and sang in chorus. Dhatri, Aryama, Mitra, Varuna, Angsha, Bhaga. Indra, Vivasvana, Pusha, Tvashta, Savita, Parjanya, alias Vishnu, these twelve Adityas glorified the son of Pandu remaining in the sky.

sn: मृगव्याधश्च सर्पश्च नितिश्च महायशाः। अजैकपादहिर्बुध्यः पिनाकी च परंतप॥ दहनोऽथेश्वरश्चैव कपाली च विशाम्पते। स्थाणुर्भगश्च भगवान् रुद्रास्तत्रावतस्थिरे॥
en: Mrigavyadha, Sarpa, illustrious Niriti. Ajaikapada, Ahiburdhnya, Pinaki, Dahana, Ishvara, Kapali, Sthanu and the illustrious Bhaga, these eleven Rudras also came there.

sn: अश्विनौ वसवश्चाष्टौ मरुतश्च महाबलाः। विश्वेदेवास्तथा साध्यास्तत्रासन परित: स्थिताः॥
en: The Ashvinis, the eight Vasus, the mighty Maruts, the Vishvadevas and the Saddhyas also came there.

sn: कर्कोटकोऽथ सर्पश्च वासुकिश्च भुजङ्गमः। कश्यपश्चाथ कुण्डश्च तक्षकश्च महोरगः॥ आययुस्तपसा युक्ता महाक्रोधा महाबलाः। एते चान्ये च बहवस्तत्र नागा व्यवस्थिताः॥
en: Karkotaka, Vasuki, Kashyapa, Kunda and the great Naga Takshaka, those mighty and wrathful Nagas possessed of ascetic merits and other Nagas also came there.

sn: ता_श्चारिष्टनेमिश्च गरुडश्चासितध्वजः। अरुणश्चारुणिश्चैव वैनतेया व्यवस्थिताः॥
en: Tarkshya, Arishtanemi, Garuda, Asitadhvaja, Aruna and Aruni of the race of Vinata also came there.

sn: तांश्च देवगणान् सर्वांस्तपःसिद्धा महर्षयः। विमानगिर्यग्रगतान् ददृशुर्नेतरे जनाः॥
en: Only the great Rishis, who were crowned with ascetic success, saw those celestial and others seated on their cars or standing on the mountain peaks. The others could not see them.

sn: तद् दृष्ट्वा महदाश्चर्यं विस्मिता मुनिसत्तमाः। अधिकां स्म ततो वृत्तिमवर्तन् पाण्डवान् प्रति॥
en: Those excellent Rishis were astonished to see that wonderful sight and their love and affection for Pandu's sons were enhanced.

sn: पाण्डुस्तु पुनरेवैनां पुत्रलोभान्महायशाः। वक्तुमैच्छद् धर्मपत्नी कुन्ती त्वेनमथाब्रवीत्॥
en: The illustrious Pandu, desirous of getting more sons, wished to speak again to his lawful wife, but Kunti addressed him thus-

sn: नातश्चतुर्थं प्रसवमापत्स्वपि वदन्त्युत। अतः परं स्वैरिणी स्याद् बन्धकी पञ्चमे भवेत्॥
en: “The learned men do not sanction a fourth delivery (conception) even in an emergency. The woman who holds intercourse with four different men is called Svairini; with five she becomes a harlot.

sn: स त्वं विद्वन् धर्ममिममधिगम्य कथं नु माम्। अत्यार्थं समुत्क्रम्य प्रमाददादिव भाषसे॥
en: O learned man, well-acquainted as you are with the scriptures, why being tempted by the desire of offspring, do you ask me again, forgetting the ordinance."

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच कुन्तीपुत्रेषु जातेषु धृतराष्ट्रमजेषु च। मद्रराजसुता पाण्डं रहो वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : After the birth of sons of Kunti and that of the sons of Dhritarashtra, the daughter of the king of Madra privately spoke to Pandu thus.

sn: न मेऽस्ति त्वयि संतापो विगुणेऽपि परंतप। नावरत्वे वराहयाः स्थित्वा चानघ नित्यदा॥ गान्धार्याश्चैव नृपते जातं पुत्रशतं तथा। श्रुत्वा न मे तथा दुःखमभवत् कुरुनन्दन॥
en: O chastiser of foes I can have on complaint, if you do not favourably look at me. O sinless one, I have no complaint that though I am by birth superior (to Kunti), yet I am inferior to her in status. O descendant of Kuru, O king, I do not grieve, hearing that Gandhari has obtained one hundred sons.

sn: इदं तु मे महद् दुःखं तुल्यतायामपुत्रता। दिष्ट्या त्विदानीं भर्तुर्मे कुन्त्यामप्यस्ति संततिः॥
en: This is my great grief (however) that though we are both equal, you should have sons by Kunti alone.

sn: यदि त्वपत्यसंतानं कुन्तिराजसुता मयि। कुर्यादनुग्रहो मे स्यात् तव चापि हितं भवेत्॥
en: If the princess Kunti so provide that I should have offspring, she would do me a great favour and she will also do you good.

sn: संरम्भो हि सपत्नीत्वाद् वक्तुं कुन्तुसुतां प्रति। यदि तु त्वं प्रसन्नो मे स्वयमेनां प्रचोदय॥
en: Kunti is my rival and therefore, I feel a delicacy in soliciting any favour from her, if you are favourably inclined towards me, ask her to grant me my desire.

sn: पाण्डुरुवाच ममाप्येष सदा माद्रि हृद्यर्थः परिवर्तते। न तु त्वां प्रसहे वक्तुमिष्टानिष्टविवक्षया॥
en: Pandu said: O Madri, I have often, reflected over this matter in my own mind. But I hesitated to tell you, not knowing whether you would like it or not.

sn: तव त्विदं मतं मत्वा प्रयतिष्याम्यतः परम्। मन्ये ध्रुवं मयोक्ता सा वचनं प्रतिपत्स्यते॥
en: Now that I know your mind, I shall certainly try to do it. I think, being asked by me, she (Kunti) will not refuse.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततः कुन्तीं पुनः पाण्डुर्विविक्त इदमब्रवीत्। कुलस्य मम संतानं लोकस्य च कुरु प्रियम्॥ मम चापिण्डनाशाय पूर्वेषामपि चात्मनः। मत्प्रियार्थं च कल्याणि कुरु कल्याणमुत्तमम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Thereupon Pandu again spoke to Kunti in private; (he said), “O blessed lady, great me some more offspring for the good of my race and of the whole world. Provide that I myself, my ancestors and you also, may always have the funeral cake.

sn: यशसोऽर्थाय चैव त्वं कुरु कर्म सुदुष्करम्। प्राप्याधिपत्यमिन्द्रेण यज्ञैरिष्टं यशोऽर्थिना॥
en: In order to gain fame, do this difficult work for me. Indra, through he has obtained the sovereignty of the celestials, performs sacrifices for fame alone.

sn: तथा मन्त्रविदो विप्रास्तपस्तप्त्वा सुदुष्करम्। गुरूनभ्युपगच्छन्ति यशसोऽर्थाय भाविनि॥
en: O handsome lady, Brahmanas, learned in Mantras, after having acquired ascetic merits most difficult to be achieved, still go to their preceptors for fame.

sn: तथा राजर्षयः सर्वे ब्राह्मणाश्च तपोधनाः। चक्रुरुच्चावचं कर्म यशसोऽर्थाय दुष्करम्॥
en: All the royal sages and Brahmanas, Possessed of ascetic wealth, have achieved the most difficult of feats for fame alone.

sn: सा त्वं माद्री प्लवेनैव तारयैनामनिन्दिते। अपत्यसंविभागेन परां कीर्तिमवाप्नुहि॥
en: O blameless one, rescue Madri with a raft of offspring; and achieve imperishable fame by making her a mother of children.”

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्त्वाब्रवीन्माद्रीं सकृच्चिन्तय दैवतम्। तस्मात् ते भवितापत्यमनुरूपमसंशयम्॥
en: Having been thus addressed, Kunti said to Madri, “Think of some celestials, from whom you will certainly get offspring."

sn: ततो माद्री विचार्यैवं जगाम मनसाश्चिनौ। तावागम्य सुतौ तस्यां जनयामासतुर्यमौ॥
en: Thereupon, Madri reflecting sometime, thought of the twin Asvinis. They came to her without delay and begot offspring on her.

sn: नकुलं सहदेवं च रूपेणाप्रतिमौ भुवि। तथैव तावपि यमौ वागुवाचाशरीरिणी॥
en: Namely Nakula and Sahadeva, matchless in beauty on earth. On the birth of that twin, the invisible voice said.

sn: सत्त्वरूपगुणोपेतौ भवतोऽत्यश्विनाविति। भासतस्तेजसात्यर्थं रूपद्रविणसम्पदा॥
en: “There virtuous and accomplished sons will transcend in energy and beauty even the twin Asvinis themselves. Possessed of great energy and beauty, they illuminated the whole region.

sn: नामानि चक्रिरे तेषां शतशृङ्गनिवासिनः। भक्त्या च कर्मणा चैव तथाशीभिर्विशाम्पते॥
en: The inhabitants (Rishi) of the mountain with the hundred parks, uttering blessings on them and performing the first rites of birth, named them.

sn: ज्येष्ठं युधिष्ठिरेत्येवं भीमसेनेति मध्यमम्। अर्जुनेति तृतीयं च कुन्तीपुत्रानकल्पयन्॥
en: The eldest of the Kunti's sons was called Yudhisthira, the second was named Bhimasena and the third was named Arjuna.

sn: पूर्वजं नकुलेत्येवं सहदेवेति चापरम्। माद्रीपुत्रावकथयंस्ते विप्राः प्रीतमानसाः॥
en: The first birth of the twins among Madri's sons was named Nakula and the next one Sahadeva. The Brahmanas with much pleasure named them thus.

sn: अनुसंवत्सरं जाता अपि ते कुरुसत्तमाः। पाण्डुपुत्रा व्यराजन्त पञ्च संवत्सरा इव॥
en: Those best of Kurus, the sons of Pandu, looked like five years old boys when they were only one year of age.

sn: महासत्त्वा महावीर्या महाबलपराक्रमाः। पाण्डुर्दृष्ट्वा सुतांस्तांस्तु देवरूपान् महौजसः॥ मुदं परमिकां लेभे ननन्द च नराधिपः ऋषीणामपि सर्वेषां शतशृङ्गनिवासिनाम्॥ प्रिया बभूवुस्तासां च तथैव मुनियोषिताम्। कुन्तीमथ पुनः पाण्डुर्माद्र्यर्थे समचोदयत्॥
en: Seeing his sons endued with celestial beauty and extraordinary strength, with super abundant energy, prowess and largeness of mind, Pandu. The king, became exceedingly glad obtaining such sons. To all the Rishis, inhabitants of the mountain with the hundred peaks. And to their wives, they became great favourites. Sometime after, Pandu again requested Kunti for Madri.

sn: तमुवाच पृथा राजन् रहस्युक्ता तदा सती। उक्ता सकृद् द्वन्द्वमेषा लेभे तेनास्मि वञ्चिता॥
en: In private, when the faithful Pritha replied to him thus, "Having given her the Mantra only for once, she has got two sons. I have been deceived by her.

sn: बिभेम्यस्याः परिभवात् कुस्त्रीणां गतिरीदृशी। नाज्ञासिषमहं मूढा द्वन्द्वाह्वाने फलद्वयम्॥ तस्मान्नाहं नियोक्तव्या त्वयैषोऽस्तु वरो मम। एवं पाण्डोः सुताः पञ्च देवदत्ता महाबलाः॥ सम्भूताः कीर्तिमन्तश्च कुरुवंशविवर्धनाः। शुभलक्षणसम्पन्नाः सोमवत् प्रियदर्शनाः॥
en: I fear she will surpass me in the number of her children. This is the way of all wicked women, fool l was, I did not know that by invoking the twin gods, I might get two sons all at once. Do not command me again, I ask from you this boon”. Thus were born to Pandu five sons, begotten by the celestials and endued with great strength. They achieved great fame and expanded the Kuru race. They were all as handsome as Soma and bore all the auspicious marks on their person.

sn: सिंहदर्पा महेष्वासाः सिंहविक्रान्तगामिनः। सिंहग्रीवा मनुष्येन्द्रा ववृधुर्देवविक्रमः॥ विवर्धमानास्ते तत्र पुण्ये हैमवते गिरौ। विस्मयं जनयामासुर्महर्षीणां समेयुषाम्॥
en: They were proud as lions; they were great bowmen; their necks were like those of lions and they were capable of going to the place frequented by lions. These kings of men endure with the prowess of the celestials daily grew up. Seeing them and their virtuous growth with years, the great Rishis, dwelling on the Himalaya mountains, were filled with astonishment and wonder.

sn: ते चे पञ्च शतं चैव कुरुवंशविवर्धनाः। सर्वे ववृधुरल्पेन कालेनाप्स्विव नीरजाः॥
en: These five (Pandavas) and the hundred (sons of Dhritarashtra), the extenders of the Kuru race, grew up rapidly like an assembly of lotuses in a lake.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच दर्शनीयांस्ततः पुत्रान् पाण्डुः पञ्च महावने। तान् पश्यन् पर्वते रम्ये स्वबाहुबलमाश्रितः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Seeing his five handsome sons before him in the great forest on the charming mountain slope, Pandu left that the old strength of his arms had come back.

sn: सुपुष्पितवने काले कदाचिन्मधुमाधवे। भूतसम्मोहने राजा सभार्यो व्यचरद् वनम्॥
en: One day in the season of spring which maddens all creatures, the king (Pandu) with his wife (Madri) roamed in the woods where every tree was blossomed.

sn: पलाशैस्तिलकैश्चतैश्चम्पकैः पारिभद्रकैः। अन्यैश्च बहुभिवृक्षैः फलपुष्पसमृद्धिभिः॥ जलस्थानैश्च विविधैः पद्मिनीभिश्च शोभितम्। पाण्डोर्वनं तत् सम्प्रेक्ष्य प्रजज्ञे हृदि मन्मथः॥
en: He saw Palashas, Tilakas, Mangoes, Champakas, Paribhadrakas and Karnikaras Kesharas, Atimuktas. There were also many other trees bent down with the weight of their flowers and fruits. There were many lakes overgrown with lotuses. Seeing all this, Pandu felt the influence of (the god of) love in his mind.

sn: प्रहृष्टमनसं तत्र विचरन्तं यथामरम्। तं मात्यनुजगामैका वसनं बिभ्रती शुभम्॥ समीक्षमाणः स तु तां वयःस्थां तनुवाससम्। तस्य कामः प्रववृधै गहनेऽग्निरिवोद्गतः॥
en: In a delightful heart he roamed there like a celestial, followed by (his wife) Madri, who was robed in a semi-transparent cloth.

sn: रहस्येकां तु तां दृष्ट्वा राजा राजीवलोचनाम्। न शशाक नियन्तुं तं कामं कामवशीकृतः॥
en: The king could not suppress his desire on seeing his lotus eyed wife and he was completely overcome by it in that solitude of the wood.

sn: तत एनां बलाद् राजा निजग्राह रहो गताम्। वार्यमाणस्तया देव्या विस्फुरन्त्या यथाबलम्॥
en: The king then sized her by force, but Madri, trembling in fear, resisted him to the best of her power.

sn: स तु कामपरीतात्मा तं शापं नान्वबुध्यत। माद्री मैथुनधर्मेण सोऽन्वगच्छद् बलादिव॥ जीवितान्ताय कौरव्य मन्मथस्य वशं गतः। शापजं भयमुत्सृज्य विधिना सम्प्रचोदितः॥
en: He (the king) was then overcome by desire; he did not remember the course (of the Rishi); he embraced Madri by force. O descendant of Kuru, unrestrained by the fear of curse and impelled by fate, the king, being overpowered by passion, forcibly sought the embraces of his wife, as if to put an end to his life.

sn: तस्य कामात्मनो बुद्धिः साक्षात् कालेन मोहिता। सम्प्रमथ्येन्द्रियग्रामं प्रणष्टा सह चेतसा॥
en: His reason, being clouded by the destroyer himself, after intoxicating his senses was itself lost with his life.

sn: स तया सह संगम्य भार्यया कुरुनन्दनः। पाण्डुः परमधर्मात्मा युयुजे कालधर्मणा॥
en: The descendant of Kuru, virtuous minded Pandu succumbed to the inevitable influence of Time while united with his wife.

sn: ततो माद्री समालिङ्गय राजानं गतचेतसम्। मुमोच दुःखजं शब्दं पुनः पुनरतीव हि॥
en: Then Madri, embracing the senseless (dead) king, began repeatedly to utter words of lament.

sn: सह पुत्रैस्ततः कुन्ती माद्रीपुत्रौ च पाण्डवौ। आजग्मुः सहितास्तत्र यत्र राजा तथागतः॥
en: Kunti with her sons and the sons of Madri, the Pandavas, came there where the king lay in that state.

sn: ततो मायब्रवीद् राजन्नार्ता कुन्तीमिदं वचः। एकैव त्वमिहागच्छ तिष्ठन्त्वयैव दारकाः॥
en: O king, Madri then crying piteously said to Kunti, “Come here alone and let the children stay there."

sn: तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं तस्यास्तत्रैवाधाय दारकान्। हताहमिति विक्रुश्य सहसैवाजगाम सा॥
en: Having heard her these words, Kunti bade the children to remain there came running and crying, "Woe to me!"

sn: दृष्ट्वा पाण्डं च माद्रीं च शयानौ धरणीतले। कुन्ती शोकपरीताङ्गी विललाप सुदुःखिता॥
en: Seeing both Pandu and Madri lying prostrate on the ground, she bewailed in grief and affliction, saying-

sn: रक्ष्यमाणो मया नित्यं वीरः सततमात्मवान्। कथं त्वामत्यतिक्रान्तः शापं जानन् वनौकसः॥
en: “Thus self controlled hero was always watched by me with care. How did he embrace you, knowing the curse of the Rishi.”

sn: ननु नाम त्वया माद्रि रक्षितव्यो नराधिपः। सा कथं लोभितवती विजने त्वं नराधिपम्॥
en: O Madri, this king ought to have been protected by you; but why did you tempt the king in solitude?

sn: कथं दीनस्य सततं त्वामासाद्य रहोगताम्। तं विचिन्तयतः शापं प्रहर्षः समजायत॥
en: He was always melancholy, thinking the curse of the Rishi. How did he become marry with you in solitude?

sn: धन्या त्वमसि बाह्रीकि मत्तो भाग्यतरा तथा। दृष्टवत्यसि यद् वक्त्रं प्रहृष्टस्य महीपतेः॥
en: "O princess of Valhika, greater fortunate you are than I. You have seen the face of the king in gladness and joy."

sn: मान्युवाच विलपन्त्या मया देवि वार्यमाणेन चासकृत्। आत्मा न वारितोऽनेन सत्यं दिष्टं चिकीर्षणा॥
en: Madri said : Sister, with tears in my eyes, I resisted the king, but he could not control himself, as if he was bent upon making the Rishi's curse true.

sn: कुन्त्युवाच अहं ज्येष्ठा धर्मपत्नी ज्येष्ठं धर्मफलं मम। अवश्यम्भाविनो भावान्मा मां माद्रि निवर्तय॥ अन्विष्यामीह भर्तारमहं प्रेतवशं गतम्। उत्तिष्ठ त्वं विसृज्यैनमिमान् पालय दारकान्॥ अवाप्य पुत्राँल्लोब्धात्मा वीरपत्नीत्वमर्थये।
en: Kunti said : I am the eldest of his wedded wives; the chief religious merit is mine. O Madri, therefore, prevent me not from what must come to pass. I must follow our lord to the region of the dead. Rise up, give me the body and you rear the children.

sn: मान्युवाच अहमेवानुयास्यामि भर्तारमपलायिनम्। न हि तृप्तास्मि कामानां ज्येष्ठा मामनुमन्यताम्॥
en: Madri said: I am still clasping our lord and here not allowed him to go away. Therefore, I shall follow him. I am not as yet satiated you are my eldest sister, give me permission (to go).

sn: मां चाभिगम्य क्षीणोऽयं कामाद् भरतसत्तमः। तमुच्छिन्द्यामस्य कामं कथं नु यमसादने॥
en: This best of the Bharata race came to me with the desire of having intercourse. His desire was not satiated, should I not go to the region of the Yama to gratify him?

sn: न चाप्यहं वर्तयन्ती निर्विशेषं सुतेषु ते। वृत्तिमार्ये चरिष्यामि स्पृशेदेनस्तथा च माम्॥
en: O revered sister, if I survive you, it is certain I shall not be able to rear up your and my own children (with equality) and thus sin will touch me.

sn: तस्मान्मे सुतयोः कुन्ति वर्तितव्यं स्वपुत्रवत्। मां च कामयमानोऽयं राजा प्रेतवशं गतः॥
en: O Kunti, you will be able to bring up my sons as if they are yours. The king, in seeking me with desire, has gone to the region of the dead.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच राज्ञः शरीरेण सह मामपीदं कलेवरम्। दग्धव्यं सुप्रतिच्छन्नमेतदार्ये प्रियं कुरु॥
en: Therefore, my body should be burned with that of the king. O revered abater, do not refuse me your permission to what is agreeable to me.

sn: दारकेष्वप्रमत्ता च भवेथाश्च हिता ममा अतोऽन्यन्न प्रपश्यामि संदेष्टव्यं हि किंचन॥
en: You will certainly bring up the children carefully. It would be doing the greatest good to me. I do not find anything more to tell you.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच इत्युक्त्वा तं चिताग्निस्थं धर्मपत्नी नरर्षभम्। मद्रराजसुता तूर्णमन्वारोहद् यशस्विनी॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having said this, the daughter of the king of Madra, the lawfully wedded wife of that best of men Pandu, ascended the funeral pyre of her lord.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच पाण्डोरुपरमं दृष्ट्वा देवकल्पा महर्षयः। ततो मन्त्रविदः सर्वे मन्त्रयांचक्रिरे मिथः॥
en: Vaishampayana said: The Rishis, who were all celestial like and wise in council, seeing the death of Pandu, consulted with one another.

sn: तापसा ऊचुः हित्वा राज्यं च राष्ट्रं च स महात्मा महायशाः। अस्मिन् स्थाने तपस्तप्त्वा तापसाशरणं गतः॥
en: The Rishis said: The high souled and the illustrious (Pandu), abandoning his sovereignty and kingdom, came here to practice asceticism and received the protection of the ascetics.

sn: स जातमात्रान् पुत्रांश्च दारांश्च भवतामिह। प्रादायोपनिधिं राजा पाण्डुः स्वर्गमितो गतः॥
en: The king Pandu has gone to heaven, leaving his wife and infant sons as a trust in our hands.

sn: तस्येमानात्मजान् देहं भार्यां च सुमहात्मनः। स्वराष्ट्रं गृह्य गच्छामो धर्म एष हि नः स्मृतः॥
en: It is now our duty to go to his kingdom with these his sons, his body (unburnt portion) and his wife.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ते परस्परममन्त्र्य देवकल्पा महर्षयः। पाण्डोः पुत्रान् पुरस्कृत्य नगरं नागसाह्वयम्॥ उदारमनसः सिद्धा गमने चक्रिरे मनः। भीष्माय पाण्डवान् दातुं धृतराष्ट्राय चैव हि॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Thus consulting with one another those god like Rishis of magnanimous hearts and of ascetic success resolved to go to the city of Hastinapur with the sons of Pandu in their front and to place them in the hands of Dhritarashtra and Bhishma.

sn: तस्मिन्नेव क्षणे सर्वे तानादाय प्रतस्थिरे। पाण्डोरांश्च पुत्रांश्च शरीरे ते च तापसाः॥
en: The ascetics started at that very moment, taking with them the boys, the two bodies and Kunti.

sn: सुखिनी सा पुरा भूत्वा सततं पुत्रवत्सला। प्रपन्ना दीर्घमध्वानं संक्षिप्तं तदमन्यत॥
en: The affectionate mother, Kunti, though she had all along led a most comfortable life, now regarded the long journey as being very short.

sn: सा त्वदीर्पण कालेन सम्प्राप्ता कुरुजाङ्गलम्। वर्धमानपुरद्वारमाससाद यशस्विनी॥
en: Arriving at Kurujangala within a very short time, the illustrious Kunti presented herself at the principal gate.

sn: द्वारिणं तापसा ऊचू राजानं च प्रकाशय। ते तु गत्वा क्षणेनैव सभायां विनिवेदिताः॥
en: The ascetics told the gate keepers "Go, inform the king.” They went in a moment to the royal court and informed the king.

sn: तं चारणसहस्राणां मुनीनामागमं तदा। श्रुत्वा नागपुरे नृणां विस्मयः समपद्यत॥
en: The citizens of Hastinapur were filed with wonder on hearing that thousands of Charanas and Rishis had arrived at their city.

sn: मुहूर्तेदित आदित्ये सर्वे बालपुरस्कृताः। सदारास्तापसान् द्रष्टुं निर्ययुः पुरवासिनः॥
en: It was soon after sunrise that the citizens all came with their wives and children, placing them in front, to see these ascetics.

sn: स्त्रीसङ्घाः क्षत्रसङ्घाश्च यानसङ्घसमास्थिताः। ब्राह्मणैः सह निर्जग्मुर्ब्राह्मणानां च योषितः॥
en: Seated on thousands of cars and conveyances, thousands of Kshatriyas and Brahmanas came out with their wives.

sn: तथा विट् शुद्रसङ्घानां महान् व्यतिकरोऽभवत्। न कश्चिदकरोदीर्ध्यामभवन धर्मबुद्धयः॥
en: The crowd of Vaishyas and Shudras was also very large. The vast crowd was very peaceful, because every one of them one of them was then inclined to piety.

sn: तथा भीष्मः शान्तनवः सोमदत्तोऽथ बाह्निकः। प्रज्ञाचक्षुश्च राजर्षिः क्षत्ता च विदुरः स्वयम्॥
en: The son of Shantanu, Bhishma, Somadatta or Balhika, the royal sage (Dhritarashtra) with the prophetic eyes and Vidura himself.

sn: सा च सत्यवती देवी कौसल्या च यशस्विनी। राजदारैः परिवृता गान्धारी चापि निर्ययौ॥
en: The venerable Satyavati, the illustrious princess of Kausalya and Gandhari surrounded by their maids, all came out to the royal gate.

sn: धृतराष्ट्रस्य दायादा दुर्योधनपुरोगमाः। भूषिता भूषणैश्चित्रैः शतसंख्या विनिर्ययुः॥
en: The hundred sons of Dhritarashtra, with Duryodhana at their head, all decked with various ornaments, also came out.

sn: तान् महर्षिगणान् दृष्ट्वा शिरोभिरभिवाद्य च। उपोपविविशुः सर्वे कौरव्याः सपुरोहिताः॥
en: Seeing the great Rishis, the Kauravas with their priests bowed down their heads in salutations and they all took their seats before them (Rishis).

sn: तथैव शिरसा भूमावभिवाद्य प्रणम्य च। उपोपविविशुः सर्वे पौरा जानपदा अपि॥
en: All the citizens also, bowing down their heads touching the ground in solutions, took their seats.

sn: तमकूजमभिज्ञाय जनौघं सर्वशस्तदा। पूजयित्वा यथान्यायं पायेनार्येण च प्रभो॥ भीष्मो राज्यं च राष्ट्रं च महर्षिभ्यो न्यवेदयत्। तेषामथो वृद्धतमः प्रत्युत्थाय जटाजिनी। ऋषीणां मतमाज्ञाय महर्षिरिदमब्रवीत्॥
en: O lord, Bhishma, seeing that vast crowd perfectly still, duly worshipped those ascetics by offering them water to wash their feet and the customary Arghya. He then spoke to them about the sovereignty and kingdom. Thereupon, the eldest of the ascetics with matted locks and skin cloth stood up. And with the concurrence of other great Rishis, he spoke thus-

sn: यः स कौरव्य दायादः पाण्डुर्नाम नराधिपः। कामभोगान् परित्यज्य शतशृङ्गमितो गतः॥
en: "The descendant of Kuru, the king, named Pandu, after abandoning pleasure and luxury, went to the mountain with the thousand peaks.

sn: ब्रह्मचर्यव्रतस्थस्य तस्य दिव्येन हेतुना। साक्षाद् धर्मादयं पुत्रस्तत्र जातो युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: He observed there the of Brahmacharya, but for some incrutable purpose of the celestials, this his eldest son, Yudhisthira, was born, begotten by Dharma himself.

sn: तथैनं बलिनां श्रेष्ठं तस्य राज्ञो महात्मनः। मातरिश्वा ददौ पुत्रं भीमं नाम महाबलम्॥
en: Then that high souled monarch was given another greatly powerful son by Vayu. This is that foremost of mighty men, who is called Bhishma.

sn: पुरुहूतादयं जज्ञे कुन्त्यामेव धनंजयः। यस्य कीर्तिर्महेष्वासान् सर्वानभिभविष्यति॥
en: This other son, begotten on Kunti by Indra, is Dhananjaya (Arjuna), whose achievements will humble all bow men in the world.

sn: यौ तु माद्री महेष्वासावसूत पुरुषोत्तमौ। अश्विभ्यां पुरुषव्याघ्राविमौ तावपि पश्यत॥
en: Look at these (two) best of men, the great bowmen, the twin boys, who were begotten by Ashvinis on Madri. VOW

sn: चरता धर्मनित्येन वनवासं यशस्विना। नष्टः पैतामहो वंशः पाण्डुना पुनरुद्धृतः॥
en: The almost extinct race of his forefathers was thus revived by the illustrious Pandu, leading in piety the life of a recluse.

sn: पुत्राणां जन्मवृद्धिं च वैदिकाध्ययनानि च। पश्यन्तः सततं पाण्डोः परां प्रीतिमवाप्स्यथ॥
en: The birth, growth and the Vedic studies of these sons of Pandu will no doubt give you much pleasure.

sn: वर्तमानः सतां वृत्ते पुत्रलाभमवाप्य च। पितृलोकं गतः पाण्डुरितः सप्तदशेऽहनि॥
en: Steadily adhering to the path of the virtuous and the wise and leaving behind him these children, Pandu has gone to the land of the Pitris.

sn: तं चितागतमाज्ञाय वैश्वानरमुखे हुतम्। प्रविष्टा पावकं माद्री हित्वा जीवितमात्मनः॥
en: Seeing him placed on the funeral pyre and about to be burnt down, his wife Madri entered the fire, thus sacrificing her life.

sn: सा गता सह तेनैव पतिलोकमनुव्रता। तस्यास्तस्य च यत् कार्यं क्रियतां तदनन्तरम्॥
en: She has thus gone with him to the land of Pati (reserved for chaste wives). Perform now those rites that should be performed for them.

sn: इमे तयोः शरीरे द्वे पुत्राश्चेमे तयोर्वराः। क्रियाभिरनुगृह्यन्तां सह मात्रा परंतपाः॥
en: These are their bodies (unburnt portions); here also are their sons, the chastisers of foes, with their mother; let them be received in due honour.

sn: प्रेतकार्ये निवृत्ते तु पितृमेधं महायशाः। लभतां सर्वधर्मज्ञः पाण्डुः कुरुकुलोद्वहः॥
en: After the completion of the first funeral rites, let the virtuous Pandu, the supporter of the dignity of the Kuru race, gain the Pitrimedha (the blissful region of the Pitris).

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्त्वा कुरून् सर्वान् कुरूणामेव पश्यताम्। क्षणेनान्तर्हिताः सर्वे तापसा गुह्यकैः सह॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having said this to the Kurus, the ascetics with the Rishi Guhyakas instantly disappeared in the very sight of the Kurus.

sn: गन्धर्वनगराकारं तथैवान्तर्हितं पुनः। ऋषिसिद्धगणं दृष्ट्वा विस्मयं ते परं ययुः॥
en: Seeing the Rishis disappear in their sight like the cities of the Gandharva (vapoury figures appearing and disappearing in the sky) the citizens was filled with wonder and astonishment and returned of their homes.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच पाण्डोर्विदुर सर्वाणि प्रेतकार्याणि कारय। राजवद् राजसिंहस्य मात्र्याश्चैव विशेषतः॥
en: Dhritarashtra said: O Vidura, perform the funeral ceremonies of that lion of kings, Pandu and also of Madri in all proper form.

sn: पशून् वासांसि रत्नानि धनानि विविधानि च। पाण्डोः प्रयच्छ मात्र्याश्च येभ्यो यावच्च वाञ्छितम्।२।। यथा च कुन्ती सत्कारं कुर्यान्मात्र्यास्तथा कुरु। यथा न वायुर्नादित्यः पश्येतां तां सुसंवृताम्॥
en: For the good of their souls, distribute cattle, cloths, gems and all kinds of wealth and give every one as much as he asks. Make arrangements also for Kunti's performance of the last rites of Madri in such a way as will please her. Let Madri's body be so carefully covered that neither the sun nor the wind may see it.

sn: न शोच्यः पाण्डुरनधः प्रशस्यः स नराधिपः। यस्य पञ्च सुता वीरा जाता: सुरसुतोपमाः॥
en: Do not lament for the sinless Pandu; he was a worthy king and has left behind him five sons like the celestial children.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच विदुरस्तं तथेत्युक्त्वा भीष्मेण सह भारत। पाण्डु संस्कारयामास देशे परमपूजिते॥
en: Vaishampayana said : O descendant of the Bharata race, Vidura said, “Be it so" and he with Bhishma performed the funeral ceremony of Pandu on a sacred spot.

sn: ततस्तु नगरात् तूर्णमाज्यगन्धपुरस्कृताः। निर्हताः पावका दीप्ताः पाण्डो राजन् पुरोहितैः॥
en: O king, without loss of time the priests went out of the city carrying with them, the last fire for Pandu the fragrant and blazing sacred fire, fed with ghee.

sn: अथैनामार्तवैः पुष्पैर्गन्धैश्च विविधैर्वरैः। शिविकां तामलंकृत्य वाससाऽच्छाद्य सर्वशः॥ तां तथा शोभितां माल्यैर्वासोभिश्च महाधनैः। अमात्या ज्ञातयश्चैनं सुहृदश्चोपतस्थिरे॥ नृसिंहं नरयुक्तेन परमालंकृतेन तम्। अवहन् यानमुख्येन सह माया सुसंयतम्॥
en: Friends, relatives and adherents, wrapping it up with cloth, decked the body of the king with the flowers of the season and sprinkled over it various perfumes. They decked the hearse also with garlands and rich hangings. Then placing the bodies of the king and the queen on the excellent heir, decked out so brightly, they caused it to be carried on the shoulders of men.

sn: पाण्डुरेणातपत्रेण चामरव्यजनेन च। सर्ववादित्रनादैश्च समलञ्चक्रिरे ततः॥
en: With the white umbrella held, over the hearse, with waving yak tails, with sounds of various musical instruments, the whole scene looked bright and grand.

sn: रत्नानि चाप्युपादाय बहूनि शतशो नराः। प्रददुः काङ्खमाणेभ्यः पाण्डोस्तस्यौर्ध्वदेहिके॥
en: Many hundreds of men began to distribute gems among the crowd at the time of the funeral ceremony of Pandu.

sn: अथच्छत्राणि शुभ्राणि चामराणि बृहन्ति च। आजह्वः कौरवस्यार्थे वासांसि रुचिराणि च॥
en: While umbrellas, large yak tails and beautiful robes were then brought for the dead Kaurava.

sn: याजकैः शुक्लवासोभिहूयमाना हुताशनाः। अगच्छन्नग्रतस्तस्य दीप्यमानाः स्वलंकृताः॥ ब्राह्मणाः क्षत्रिया वैश्याः शूद्राश्चैव सहस्रशः। रुदन्तः शोकसंतप्ता अनुजग्मुर्नराधिपम्॥
en: The priests clad in white, walked in the van of the procession, pouring libations of ghee on the sacred fire, blazing in an ornamental vessel. Thousands of Brahmanas, Kshatriyas Vaishyas and followed the king, weeping in grief.

sn: अयमस्मानपाहाय दुःखे चाधाय शाश्वते। कृत्वा चास्माननातांश्च क्व यास्यति नराधिपः॥
en: The Citizen said : O king, where do you go, leaving us behind and making us miserable and wretched forever?

sn: क्रोशन्तः पाण्डवाः सर्वे भीष्मो विदुर एव च। रमणीये वनोद्देशे गङ्गातीरे समे शुभे॥ न्यासयामासुरथ तां शिबिकां सत्यवादिनः। सभार्यस्य नृसिंहस्य पाण्डोरक्लिष्टकर्मणः॥
en: Bhishma, Vidura and the sons of Pandu all wept aloud. They at last came to a charming and holy wood on the banks of the Gangas. There they laid down the hearse on which the truthful, the lion hearted and the pious king and his wife lay.

sn: ततस्तस्य शरीरं तु सर्वगन्धाधिवासितम्। शुचिकालीयकादिग्धं दिव्यचन्दनरूषितम्॥ पर्यषिञ्चञ्जलेनाशु शातकुम्भमयैर्घटैः। चन्दनेन च शुक्लेन सर्वतः समलेपयन्॥ कालागुरुविमिश्रेण तथा तुङ्गरसेन च। अथैनं देशजैः शुक्लैर्वासोभिः समयोजयन्॥
en: They then besmeared the bodies with all kinds of perfumes; they brought water in may golden vessels and washed his body. They then again smeared at with white sandal. They then dressed it in a white dress made of national fabrics and smeared it with Kalaguru mixed with Tungarasa (sort of perfume).

sn: संछन्नः स तु वासोभिर्जीवन्निव नराधिपः। शुशुभे स नरव्याघ्रो महार्हशयनोचितः॥
en: With the new dress on, the king appeared like a living man, as if he was only sleeping on a costly bed.

sn: याजकैरभ्यनुज्ञाते प्रेतकर्मण्यनुष्ठिते। घृतावसिक्तं राजानं सह मान्या स्वलंकृतम्॥ तुङ्गपद्मकमिश्रेण चन्दनेन सुगन्धिना। अन्यैश्च विविधैर्गन्धैर्विधिना समदाहयन्॥
en: When the other funeral ceremonies were over, the Kauravas, with the direction of their priests, set fire to the bodies on the king and that of Madri which had been besmeared with ghee and decked with ornaments; and they burnt them with the fragrant Sandal woods which was besmeared with Tungapadma and other perfumes.

sn: ततस्तयोः शरीरे द्वे दृष्ट्वा मोहवशं गता। हा हा पुत्रेति कौसल्या पपात सहसा भुवि॥
en: Seeing the bodies in flame, Kausalya cried out, “O my son, O my son” and she fell senseless on the ground.

sn: तां प्रेक्ष्य पतितामा" पौरजानपदो जनः। सरोद दुःखसंतप्तो राजभक्त्या कृपान्वितः॥
en: Seeing her prostrate on the ground the citizens and the people wept in grief or the affection they for the king.

sn: कुन्त्याश्चैवार्तनादेन सर्वाणि च विचुक्रुशुः। मानुषैः सह भूतानि तिर्यग्योनिगतान्यपि॥
en: The beast and birds bewailed with men at the lamentations of Kunti.

sn: तथा भीष्मः शान्तनवो विदुरश्च महामतिः। सर्वशः कौरवाश्चैव प्राणदन् भृशदुःखिताः॥
en: Then the son of Shantanu, Bhishma, the high-souled Vidura and all the other Kurus became disconsolate in grief and sorrow.

sn: ततो भीष्मोऽथ विदुरोराजा च सह पाण्डवैः। उदकं चक्रिरे तस्य सर्वाश्च कुरुयोषितः॥ चुक्रशुः पाण्डवाः सर्वे भीष्मः शान्तनवस्तथा। विदुरो ज्ञातयश्चैव चक्रुश्चाप्युदकक्रियाः॥
en: Then Bhishma, Vidura, the king (Dhritarashtra), with the Pandavas and all the Kuru ladies, performed his (Pandu's) water ceremony. All Pandavas grieved for his father. Bhishma, Vidura and other relatives all are grieved. All of them performed the water ceremony.

sn: कृतोदकांस्तानादाय पाण्डवाञ्छोककर्शितान्। सर्वाः प्रकृतयो राजन् शोचमाना न्यवारयन्॥
en: When the water ceremony was over, the people, themselves filled with grief, began to console the bereaved sons of Pandu.

sn: यथैव पाण्डवा भूमौ सुषुपुः सह बान्धवैः। तथैव नागरा राजन् शिश्यिरे ब्राह्मणादयः॥ तद्गतानन्दमस्वस्थमाकुमारमहष्टवत्। बभूव पाण्डवैः सार्धं नगरं द्वादश क्षपाः॥
en: The Pandavas slept on the ground with their friends and relatives. O king, seeing this the Brahmanas and other citizens also gave their bed. Young and old, all men grieved with the sons of Pandu and passed twelve days in mourning.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततः कुन्ती च राजा च भीष्मश्च सह बन्धुभिः। ददुः श्राद्धं तदा पाण्डोः स्वधामृतमयं तदा॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Then Bhishma, the king (Dhritarashtra) and Kunti with their friends, celebrated the Shraddha of Pandu and offered the ambrosial Pinda.

sn: कुरूंश्च विप्रमुख्यांश्च भोजयित्वा सहस्रशः। रत्नौघान् विप्रमुख्येभ्यो दत्त्वा ग्रामवरांस्तथा॥
en: They feasted the Kurus and also many thousands of Brahmanas, whom they gave many gems and much wealth with many villages.

sn: कृतशौचांस्ततस्तु पाण्डवान् भरतर्षभान्। आदाय विविशुः सर्वे पुरं वारणसाह्वयम्॥
en: Thus being cleansed to Hastinapur with those best of the Bharata race, the sons of Pandu.

sn: सततं स्मानुशोचन्तस्तमेव भरतर्षभम्। पौरजानपदाः सर्वे मृतं स्वमिव बान्धवम्॥
en: All the citizens and the people bewailed for that best of the Bharata race (Pandu), as if they had lost their own relative.

sn: श्राद्धावसाने तु तदा दृष्ट्वा तं दुःखितं जनम्। सम्मूढां दुःखशोका” व्यासो मातरमब्रवीत्॥
en: After the completion of the Shraddha Vyasa, seeing all the people plunged in grief, spoke to his bereaved and greatly afflicted mother (Satyavati) thus,

sn: अतिक्रान्तसुखा: काला: पर्युपस्थितदारुणाः। श्वः श्वः पापिष्ठदिवसाः पृथिवी गतयौवना॥
en: “The days of happiness are gone; the days of misery have come. Sin begins to increase day by day; the world has lost its youth.

sn: बहुमायासमाकीर्णो नानादोषसमाकुलः। लुप्तधर्मक्रियाचारो घोरः कालो भविष्यति॥
en: The fearful Time, endued with many Mayas, full of various faults and loss of all virtuous acts, will now come.

sn: कुरूणामनयाच्चापि पृथिवी न भविष्यति। गच्छ त्वं योगमास्थाय युक्ता वस तपोवने॥
en: By the evil doings of the Kurus the world will be destroyed; (therefore) go into the forest of asceticism, devoting yourself to Yoga meditation.

sn: मा द्राक्षीस्त्वं कुलस्यास्य घोरं संक्षयमात्मनः। तथेति समनुज्ञाय सा प्रविश्याब्रवीत् स्नुषाम्॥
en: Do not be able witness of the terrible annihilation of your own race. Saying "Be it so," she entered the inner apartments and addressed her daughters-in-law thus.

sn: अम्बिके तव पौत्रस्य दुर्नयात् किल भारतः। सानुबन्धा विनक्ष्यन्ति पौराश्चैवेति नः श्रुतम्॥
en: "O Ambika, have heard that inconsequence of the evil deeds of your grandsons, this Bharata dynasty with its subjects will perish.

sn: तत् कौसल्यामिमामा" पुत्रशोकाभिपीडिताम्। वनमादाय भद्रं ते गच्छामि यदि मन्यसे॥
en: If you give me permission, I shall go to the forest with Kausalya, so grieved at the loss of her son."

sn: तथेत्युक्ता त्वम्बिकया भीष्ममामन्त्र्य सुव्रता। वनं ययौ सत्यवती स्नुषाभ्यां सह भारत॥
en: O descendant of the Bharata race, having said this to Ambika and taking the permission of Bhishma, Satyavati of excellent vows went to the forest with her daughter-in-law.

sn: ताः सुघोरं तपस्तप्त्वा देव्यो भरतसत्तम। देहं त्यक्त्वा महाराज गतिमिष्टां ययुस्तदा॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, she perforined severe asceticism. O great king, she then gave up her body and obtained heaven.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच अथाप्तवन्तो वेदोक्तान् संस्कारान् पाण्डवास्तदा। संव्यवर्धन्त भोगांस्ते भुञ्जानाः पितृवेश्मनि॥
en: Then the sons of king Pandu, after performing all the purifying rites mentioned in the Vedas, began to grow up in a royal style in the house of their father.

sn: धार्तराष्ट्रैश्च सहिताः क्रीडन्तो मुदिताः सुखम्। बालक्रीडासु सर्वासु विशिष्टास्तेजसाभवन्॥
en: They played in great joy with the sons of Dhritarashtra; and they excelled them all in the boyish sports with their superior strength.

sn: जवे लक्ष्याभिहरणे भोज्ये पांसुविकर्षणे। धार्तराष्ट्रान् भीमसेनः सर्वान् स परिमर्दति॥
en: In speed, in striking the object aimed at, in eating, in scattering dust, Bhimasena beat all the sons of Dhritarashtra.

sn: हर्षात् प्रक्रीडमानांस्तान् गृह्य राजन् निलीयते। शिरःसु विनिगृह्येतान् योधयामास पाण्डवैः॥ शतमेकोत्तरं तेषां कुमाराणां महौजसाम्। एक एव निगृहणाति नातिकृच्छ्राद् वृकोदरः॥ कचेषु च निगृह्येनान् विनिहत्य बलाद् बली। चकर्ष क्रोशतो भूमौ घृष्टजानुशिरोंऽसकान्॥
en: O king, that son of Pandu (Bhima), when they were all engaged in sports, pulled them by the hair and made them fight with one another, laughing all the while. Vrikodara (Bhima) easily defeated those one hundred and one (Dhritarashtra's) sons of great energy, as if they were but one instead of one hundred and one. He sized them by the hair and throwing them down, he dragged them along the ground; some breaking their knees, some their heads and some their shoulders.

sn: दश बालाञ्जले क्रीडन् भुजाभ्यां परिगृह्य सः। आस्ते स्म सलिले मग्नो मृतकल्पान् विमुञ्चति॥
en: When playing in the water, he sometimes seized ten of them by his arms and drowned them in the water. He left them off only when they were almost dead.

sn: फलानि वृक्षमारुह्य विचन्वन्ति च ते तदा। तदा पादप्रहारेण भीमः कम्पयते दुमान्॥
en: When they got upon a tree together fruits, Bhima shook the tree by striking it with his feet.

sn: प्रहारवेगाभिहता दुमा व्याधूर्णितास्ततः। सफलाः प्रपतन्ति स्म दुतं त्रस्ता: कुमारकाः॥
en: Being shaken and whirled by that shock, down came with all speed the princes with the fruits.

sn: न ते नियुद्धे न जवे न योग्यासु कदाचन। कुमारा उत्तरं चक्रुः स्पर्धमाना वृकोदरम्॥
en: In speed, in pugilistic encounters, or in speed, the princes could not excel Bhima in any way.

sn: एवं स धार्तराष्ट्रांश्च स्पर्धमानो वृकोदरः। अप्रियेऽतिष्ठदत्यन्तं बाल्यान्न द्रोहचेतसा॥
en: Bhima thus prided himself by tormenting the sons of Dhritarashtra out of boyish pranks. In fact he had no ill will towards them.

sn: ततो बलमतिख्यातं धार्तराष्ट्रः प्रतापवान्। भीमसेनस्य तज्ज्ञात्वा दुष्टभावमदर्शयत्॥
en: Seeing these extraordinary exhibitions of strength by Bhima, the mighty armed eldest of Dhritarashtra (Duryodhana), the conceived hostility towards him.

sn: तस्य धर्मादपेतस्य पापानि परिपश्यतः। मोहादैश्वर्यलोभाच्च पापा मतिर जायत॥
en: The wicked and unrighteous (Duryodhana), through ignorance and ambition (of possessing wealth), inclined to commit acts of sin. son

sn: अयं बलवतां श्रेष्ठः कुन्तीपुत्रो वृकोदरः। मध्यमः पाण्डुपुत्राणां निकृत्या संनिगृह्यताम्॥
en: (He thought), the son of Kunti, this Vrikodara (Bhima, this second Pandava, is the foremost in strength, I must destroy him by artifice.

sn: प्राणवान् विक्रमी चैव शौर्येण महतान्वितः। स्पर्धते चापि सहितानस्मानेको वृकोदरः॥
en: The greatly strong and powerful Bhima challenges one hundred of us in pride.

sn: तं तु सुतं पुरोद्याने गङ्गायां प्रक्षिपामहे। अथ तस्मादवरजं श्रेष्ठं चैव युधिष्ठिरम्॥ प्रसह्य बन्धने बद्ध्वा प्रशासिष्ये वसुंधराम्। एवं स निश्चयं पापः कृत्वा दुर्योधनस्तदा। नित्यमेवान्तरप्रेक्षी भीमस्यासीन्महात्मनः॥
en: Therefore, when he will be asleep in the gardens of the palace, we shall throw him into the Gangas. Afterwards confining his eldest brother Yudhisthira and his younger brother (Arjuna), I shall reign soie king over the earth.' Duryodhana, having determined to do this wicked act, watched for an opportunity to injure Bhima.

sn: ततो जलविहारार्थं कारयामास भारत। चैलकम्बलवेश्मानि विचित्राणि महान्ति च॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, he built for the purpose of water sport an extraordinary and beautiful palace.

sn: सर्वकामैः सुपूर्णानि पताकोच्छायवन्ति च। तत्र संजनयामास नानागाराण्यनेकशः॥
en: With many rooms filled with all sorts of luxuries, decorated with hangings of broad cloth and with banners flying from its top.
