en: Then the preceptor, clad in white attire, with white sacred thread, white locks, white bread, white garlands and white sandal-paste besmeared over his body, entered the arena with his son. It appeared as if the moon accompanied (the planet) Mars appeared in an unclouded sky.

sn: स यथासमयं चक्रे बलिं बलवतां वरः। ब्राह्मणांस्तु सुमन्त्रज्ञान् कारयामास मङ्गलम्॥
en: The best of strong men, the hero (Drona), entering at the proper time, caused Brahmanas versed in Mantras to celebrate the auspicious rites.

sn: सुखपुण्याहघोषस्य पुण्यस्य समनन्तरम्। विविशुर्विविधं गृह्य शस्त्रोपकरणं नराः॥
en: After auspicious and sweet-sounding musical instruments had struck up as propitiatory ceremony, men equipped with various weapons entered the arena.

sn: ततो बद्धाङ्गुलित्राणा बद्धकक्षा महारथाः। बद्धतूणाः सधनुषो विविशुर्भरतर्षभाः॥
en: Then the best of the Bharata race, (the princes), those mighty car-warriors, having girt up their lions, entered (the arena) equipped with bows, quivers and finger protectors.

sn: अनुज्येष्ठं तु ते तत्र युधिष्ठिरपुरोगमाः। चक्रुरस्त्रं महावीर्याः कुमाराः परमाद्भुतम्॥
en: With Yudhisthira, at their head, the greatly heroic princes, in the order of their age, began to show wonderful skill in their arms. a

sn: केचिच्छराक्षेपभयाच्छिरांस्यवननामिरे। मनुजा धृष्टमपरे वीक्षाञ्चक्रुः सुविस्मिताः॥
en: Some (spectators) lowered their heads out of fear of the falling arrows, while others not being afraid, looked on with wonder and astonishment.

sn: ते स्म लक्ष्याणि बिभिदुर्बाणैर्नामाङ्कशोभितैः। विविधैर्लाघवोत्सृष्टैरुह्यन्तो वाजिभिर्दुतम्॥
en: Riding swift horses and managing them dextrously, the princess hit marks with arrows engraved with their respective names.

sn: तत् कुमारबलं तत्र गृहीतशरकार्मुकम्। गन्धर्वनगराकारं प्रेक्ष्य ते विस्मिताभवन्।॥
en: On seeing the prowess of the princes in using bows and arrows, the spectators thought they were seeing the city of Gandharva. They were all filled with amazement.

sn: सहसा चुक्रुशुश्चान्ये नराः शतसहस्रशः। विस्मयोत्फुल्लनयनाः साधु साध्विति भारत॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, some hundreds and thousands of men, their eyes expanded with wonder, all at once cried out “Well done! Well done!"

sn: कृत्वा धनुषि ते मार्गान् स्थचर्यासु चासकृत्। गजपृष्ठेऽश्वपृष्ठे च नियुद्धे च महाबलः॥
en: After repeatedly displaying their skill and dexterity in the use of bow and arrows, in the management of cars, in the fight on horseback and on the back of elephants.

sn: गृहीतखड्गचर्माणस्ततो भूयः प्रहारिणः। त्सरुमार्गान् यथोद्दिष्टांश्चेसः सर्वासु भूमिषु॥
en: They took up their swords and buckles and began to attack one another and to walk around the arena displaying various modes of sword's play.

sn: लाघवं सौष्ठवं शोभा स्थिरत्वं दृढमुष्टिताम्। ददृशुस्तत्र सर्वेषां प्रयोगं खड्गचर्मणोः॥
en: They all saw their (great) agility, the beauty of the symmetry of their bodies, their grace, their calmness, the firmness of their grasp and the skill in the use of their swords and buckles.

sn: अथ तौ नित्यसंहृष्टौ सुयोधनवृकोदरौ। अवतीर्णौ गदाहतावेकशृङ्गाविवाचलौ॥
en: Then Vrikodara (Bhima) and Suyodhana (Duryodhana) entered the (arena)with secret mental delight like two single peaked mountains.

sn: बद्धकक्षौ महाबाहू पौरुषे पर्यवस्थितौ। बृहन्तौ वासिताहेतोः समदाविव कुञ्जरौ॥
en: Those mighty-armed heroes girt their lions and summoned all their strength; they roared like two infuriated elephants contending (for a female elephant).

sn: तौ प्रदक्षिणसव्यानि मण्डलानि महाबलौ। चेरतुर्मण्डलगतौ समदाविव कुञ्जरौ॥
en: Those two greatly strong (heroes) circled round the arena with faultless clubs and careered right and left in all the proper form.

sn: विदुरो धृतराष्ट्राय गान्धार्याः पाण्डवारणिः। न्यवेदयेतां तत् सर्वं कुमाराणां विचेष्टितम्॥
en: Vidura described to Dhritarashtra and the mother of the Pandavas (Kunti) to Gandhari all the feats of the princes.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच कुरुराजे हि रङ्गस्ये भीमे च बलिनां वरे। पक्षपातकृतस्नेहः स द्विधेवाभवज्जनः॥।॥
en: Vaishampayana said : On the appearance of the Kuru prince (Duryodhana) and the foremost of all strong men Bhima, the spectators were divided into two parties by their partiality swayed by the love (towards each of the contending heroes).

sn: वीर कुरुराजेति ही भीम इति जल्पताम्। पुरुषाणां सुविपुलाः प्रणादाः सहसोत्थिताः॥
en: Some cried, “Behold the heroic Kuru prince; some cried, “Behold the heroic Bhima.” Thus from these cries of the people rose a great uproar (in the arena).

sn: ततः क्षुब्धार्णवनिभं रङ्गमालोक्य बुद्धिमान्। भारद्वाजः प्रियं पुत्रमश्वत्थामानमब्रवीत्॥
en: On seeing the place become like a troubled ocean, the intelligent son of Bharadvaja, (Drona) spoke to his dear son Ashvathama.

sn: द्रोण उवाच वारयैतौ महावीरों कृतयोग्यावुभावपि। मा भूद् रङ्गप्रकोपोऽयं भीमदुर्योधनोद्भवः॥
en: Drona said: “Ştop these two mighty heroes, so expert in arms. Let not the anger of the assembled people be excited by this encounter between Bhima and Duryodhana.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततस्तावुद्यतगदौ गुरुपुत्रेण वारितौ। युगान्तानिलसंक्षुब्धौ महावेलाविवार्णवौ॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Thereupon the two combatants, with uplifted clubs, resembling two swollen oceans agitated by the winds that blow at the time of the world's dissolution, were stopped by the son of the preceptor.

sn: ततो रङ्गाङ्गणगतो द्रोणो वचनमब्रवीत्। निवार्य वादिगणं महामेघनिभस्वनम्॥
en: Then Drona entered the arena and sopping the musicians spoke thus in a voice deep as the roars of the clouds.

sn: यो मे पुत्रात् प्रियतरः सर्वशस्त्रविशारदः। ऐन्द्रिरिन्द्रानुजसमः स पार्थो दृश्यतामिति॥
en: “Behold all of you now that Partha who is dearer to me then my own son, who is the master of all arms, who is the son of Indra himself and who is like the younger brother of Indra."

sn: आचार्यवचनेनाथ कृतस्वस्त्ययनो युवा। बद्धगोधाङ्गुलित्राणः पूर्णतूणः सकार्मुकः॥ काञ्चनं कवचं बिभ्रत् प्रत्यदृश्यत फाल्गुनः। सार्कः सेन्द्रायुधतडित् ससंध्य इव तोयदः॥
en: At the command of the preceptor, the youthful Falguni (Arjuna), equipped with finger protector, his quiver full of arrows, with his bow in hand and with a golden armour on, after having performed the propitiatory rites, appeared in the arena like an evening cold reflecting the rays of the setting son and illumined by the hues of the rainbow and the flashes of lighting.

sn: ततः सर्वस्य रङ्गस्य समुत्पिञ्जलकोऽभवत्। प्रावाद्यन्त च वाद्यानि सशङ्खानि समन्ततः॥
en: On this a great cry of joy rose from all parts of the arena and musical instruments were played and conches were blown.

sn: एष कुन्तीसुतः श्रीमानेष मध्यमपाण्डवः। एष पुत्रो महेन्द्रस्य कुरूणामेष रक्षिता॥ एषोऽस्त्रविदुषां श्रेष्ठ एष धर्मभृतां वरः। एष शीलवतां चापि शीलज्ञाननिधिः परः॥ इत्येवं तुमुला वाचः शृण्वत्याः प्रेक्षकरिताः। कुन्त्याः प्रस्रवसंयुक्तैरनैः क्लिन्नमुरोऽभवत्॥
en: All cried, “This is the handsome son of Kunti, the middle (third) son of Pandu. This is the son of Indra. This the protector of the Kuru race. This is the best of the all name learned in arms. This is the best of all cherisher of virtue. This is the foremost of all well conducted persons. This is their great repository of the knowledge of all (good) manners.” Hearing these loud cries of the spectators, the tears of Kunti, mixing with the milk of her breast, drenched her bosom.

sn: तेन शब्देन महता पूर्णश्रुतिरथाब्रवीत्। धृतराष्ट्रो नरश्रेष्ठो विदुरं हृष्टमानसः॥
en: Having his ears filled with the uproar, the best of men, Dhritarashtra, asked Vidura with delight,

sn: क्षत्तः क्षुब्धार्णवनिभः किमेव सुमहास्वनः। सहसैवोत्थितो रङ्गे भिन्दन्निव नभस्तलम्॥
en: “O Kshatta, what is this great uproar, like that of the troubled sea, that rises in the arena all of sudden echoing the very heavens?"

sn: विदुर उवाच एष पार्थो महाराज फाल्गुनः पाण्डुनन्दनः। अवतीर्णः सकवचस्तत्रैष सुमहास्वनः॥
en: Vidura said: O great king, the son of Pritha and Pandu, Falguni (Arjuna), clad in armour; has entered, the arena; and therefore is this uproar.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच धन्योऽस्म्यनुगृहीतोऽस्मि रक्षितोऽस्मि महामते। पृथारणिसमुद्भूतैस्त्रिभिः पाण्डववह्निभिः॥
en: Dhritarashtra said : O high-souled man, I have indeed been blessed, favoured and protected by the three fire (sons) of Pritha (Kunti) who is like the sacred fuel.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तस्मिन् प्रमुदिते रङ्गे कथंचित् प्रत्युपस्थिते। दर्शयामास बीभत्सुराचार्यायास्त्रलाघवम्॥ आग्नेयेनासृजद् वह्नि वारुणोनासृजत् पयः। वायव्येनासृजद् वायुं पार्जन्येनासृजद् घनान्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : When the spectators some what regained their equanimity, Bibhatsu (Arjuna) displayed before his preceptor his lightness in the use of arins. He created fire by the Agneya weapon, by the Varuna weapon he created water. He created winds by the Vayavya weapon and by the Parjanya weapon, he created the clouds.

sn: भौमेन प्राविशद् भूमि पार्वतेनासृजद् गिरीन्। अन्तर्धानेन चास्त्रेण पुनरन्तर्हितोऽभवत्॥
en: He created land by the Bhima weapon and by the Parvata weapon he created the mountains. He made all this to disappear by the Antardhana weapon.

sn: क्षणात् प्रांशुः क्षणाद्धस्वः क्षणाच्च रथधूर्गतः। क्षणेन रथमध्यस्थः क्षणेनावतरन्महीम्॥
en: In a moment he appeared tail and in a moment short. He was now yoked in his car; he was in the next moment on the car itself; he was then again on the ground.

sn: सुकुमारं च सूक्ष्मं च गुरुं चापि गुरुप्रियः। सौष्ठवेनाभिसंक्षिप्तः सोऽविध्यद् विविधैः शरैः॥
en: The favourite (pupil) of the preceptor (Arjuna) shot by his arrows various marks, some tender, some fine and some of thick composition.

sn: भ्रमतश्च वराहस्य लोहस्य प्रमुखे समम्। पञ्च बाणानसंयुक्तान् सम्मुमोचैकबाणवत्॥
en: He let fly at one time five arrows from his bow stung into the mouth of a moving iron boar as if they were but one arrow.

sn: गव्ये विषाणकोषे च चले रज्ज्वलम्बिनि। निचखान महावीर्यः सायकानेकविंशतिम्॥
en: That greatly effulgent hero sent twenty one arrows into the hollow of a cow's horn hang upon a rope which was swinging to and fro.

sn: इत्येवमादि सुमहत् खड्गे धनुषि चानघ। गदायां शस्त्रकुशलो मण्डलानि ह्यदर्शयत्॥
en: O sinless one, in this manner he (Arjuna), walking round the arena, displayed his profound skill in the use of the sword, bow and club.

sn: तत: समाप्तभूयिष्ठे तस्मिन् कर्मणि भारता मन्दीभूते समाजे च वादित्रस्य च निःस्वने॥ द्वारदेशात् समुद्भूतो माहात्म्यबलसूचकः। वज्रनिष्पेषसदृशः सुश्रुवे भुजनिःस्वनः॥
en: O descendant of the Bharata race, when the tournament was alrnost ended, when the excitement of the spectators cooled down and the sound of music stopped. There was heard at the gate the slapping of arms, betokening power and strength, like the roars of thunder.

sn: दीर्यन्ते किं नु गिरयः किंस्विद् भूमिर्विदीर्यते। किंस्विदापूर्यते व्योम जलधाराघनैर्घनैः॥
en: "Are mountains splitting? Is the earth going to be rent asunder? Is the sky resounding with the roar of gathering clouds?”

sn: रङ्गस्यैवं मतिरभूत् क्षणेन वसुधाधिपः। द्वारं चाभिमुखाः सर्वे बभूवुः प्रेक्षकास्तदा।॥
en: O king, all the spectators in the arena thought thus and turned their eyes towards the gate.

sn: पञ्चभिर्धातृभिः पार्थैर्द्राणः परिवृतो बभौ। पञ्चतारेण संयुक्तः सावित्रेणेव चन्द्रमाः॥
en: Drona was surrounded by the five brothers, the sons of Pritha and looked like the moon surrounded by the five constellations.

sn: अश्वत्थाम्ना च सहितं भ्रातृणां शतमूर्जितम्। दुर्योधनममित्रनमुत्थितं पर्यवारयत्॥ स तैस्तदा भ्रातृभिरुद्यतायुधैर्गदाग्रपाणिः समवस्थितैर्वृतः। बभौ यथा दानवसंक्षये पुरा पुरन्दरो देवगणैः समावृतः॥
en: That chastiser of foes, Duryodhana, with his one hundred haughty brothers and with Ashvathama, stood up in haste. That prince (Duryodhana) with his club in his hand, surrounded by his one hundred brothers with uplifted weapons, looked like Indra in the days of yore when he stood surrounded by the celestial at the time of the battle with the Danavas.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच दत्तेऽवकाशे पुरुषैर्विस्मयोत्फुल्ललोचनैः। विवेश रङ्गं विस्तीर्णं कर्णः परपुरंजयः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : When the spectators, with eyes expended with wonder, made way for that subjugator of hostile cities; Karna, he entered the spacious arena.

sn: सहजं कवचं बिभ्रत् कुण्लोद्योतिताननः। सधनुर्वद्धनिस्त्रिंशः पादचारीव पर्वतः॥
en: He was armed in his natural coat of armour, his face was brightened with his earrings, his bow was in his hand and his sword in his lions, he entered like a walking cliff.

sn: कन्यागर्भः पृथुयशाः पृथायाः पृथुलोचनः। तीक्ष्णांशो स्करस्यांशः कर्णोऽरिगणसूदनः॥
en: The illustrious destroyer of enemies, the large eyed Karna was born of Pritha (Kunti) in her maidenhood. He was a portion of the hot beamed sun.

sn: सिंहर्षभगजेन्द्राणां बलवीर्यपराक्रमः। दीप्तिकान्तिद्युतिगुणैः सूर्येन्दुज्वलनोपमः॥
en: His power and energy were like those of lions, the bulls or the best of elephants. He was like the sun in splendour, moon in loveliness and fire in effulgence.

sn: प्रांशुः कनकतालाभः सिंहसंहननो युवा। असंख्येयगुणः श्रीमान् भास्करस्यात्मसम्भवः॥
en: Being born of the sun, he was tall like a golden palm; he was a youth who could slay lions. He was handsome and possessed countless accomplishments.

sn: स निरीक्ष्य महाबाहुः सर्वतो रङ्गमण्डलम्। प्रणाम द्रोणकृपयो त्यादृतमिवाकरोत्॥
en: The mighty armed (hero) looked all around the arena and bowed rather with indifference to Drona and Kripa.

sn: स समाजजन: सर्वो निश्चल: स्थिरलोचनः। कोऽयमित्यागतक्षोभः कौतूहलपरोऽभवत्॥
en: The entire assembly of people remain emotionless and stared in steadfast gaze. They were filled with great curiously and asked one another, "Who is he?"

sn: सोऽब्रवीन्मेघगम्भीरस्वरेण वदतां वरः। भ्राता भ्रातरमज्ञातं सावित्रः पाकशासनिम्॥
en: That foremost of eloquent men, the son of the sun, (Karna) in a voice deep as the roars of clouds, addressed his unknown brother thus-

sn: पार्थ यत् ते कृतं कर्म विशेषवदहं ततः। करिष्ये पश्यातं नृणां माऽऽत्मना विस्मयं गमः॥
en: "O Partha, I shall perform feats before this assembly excelling all that you have done. Behold them and will be amazed."

sn: असमाप्ते ततस्तस्य वचने वदतां वर। यन्त्रोत्क्षिप्त इवोत्तस्थौ क्षिप्रं वै सर्वतो जनः॥
en: O best of all eloquent men, when he had hardly finished his words, the spectators stood up all at once as if uplifted by some instrument.

sn: प्रीतिश्च मनुजव्याघ्र दुर्योधनमुपाविशत्। ह्रीश्च क्रोधश्च बीभत्सु क्षणेनान्वाविवेश ह॥
en: O best of men, Duryodhana was delighted, while Bibhatsa (Arjuna) was filled with abashment and anger.

sn: ततो द्रोणाभ्यनुज्ञात: कर्णः प्रियरणः सदा। यत् कृतं तत्र पार्थेन तच्चकार महाबलः॥
en: The greatly powerful Karna, ever fond of battle, displayed with the permission of Drona all that Partha had displayed before.

sn: अथ दुर्योधनस्तत्र भ्रातृभिः सह भारत। कर्णं परिष्वज्य मुदा ततो वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, Duryodhana with his brothers thereupon embraced Karna with delight and spoke to him thus-

sn: दुर्योधन उवाच स्वागतं ते महाबाहो दिष्ट्या प्राप्तोऽसि मानद। अहं च कुरुराज्यं च यथेष्टमुपभुज्यताम्॥
en: Duryodhana said : "O mighty armed hero welcome to you! man deserving of politeness, I have got you by good fortune. Command me and the Kuru kingdom at your pleasure.

sn: कर्ण उवाच कृतं सर्वमहं मन्ये सखित्वं च त्वया वृणे। द्वन्द्वयुद्धं च पार्थेन कर्तुमिच्छाम्यहं प्रभो॥
en: Karna said: When you have said this, I consider it as already accomplished. I only desire your friendship. O lord, I long for a single combat with Arjuna.

sn: दुर्योधन उवाच भुक्ष्व भोगान् मया साधु बन्धूनां प्रियकृद् भव। दुहृदां कुरु सर्वेषां मूर्ध्नि पादमरिंदम॥
en: Duryodhana said : Enjoy with me the good things of life. Be the benefactor of your friends. O oppressor of enemies, place your feet on the heads of all foes.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततः क्षिप्तमिवात्मानं मत्वा पार्थोऽभ्यभाषत। कर्ण भ्रातृसमूहस्य मध्येऽचलमिव स्थितम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Thereupon Partha considered himself disgraced and spoke to Karna who stood amidst the (Kuru) brothers like a hill.

sn: अर्जुन उवाच अनाहूतोपसृष्टानामनाहूतोपजल्पिनाम्। ये लोकास्तान् हत: कर्ण मया त्वं प्रतिपत्स्यसे॥
en: Arjuna said : O Karna, the path which the unwelcome intruder and the uninvited talker comes to shall be yours.

sn: कर्ण उवाच रङ्गोऽयं सर्वसामान्यः किमत्र तव फाल्गुन। वीर्यश्रेष्ठाश्च राजानो बलं धर्मोऽनुवर्तते॥
en: Karna said: This arena is meant for all; it is not for you alone. O Falguni, they are kings who are superior in power; Kshatriya Dharma depends on prowess alone.

sn: किं क्षेपैर्दुर्बलायासैः शरैः कथय भारत। गुरोः समक्षं यावत् ते हराम्यद्य शिरः शरैः॥
en: o descendant of Bharata, what need is their of altercation which is the habit of the weak! Speak in arrows, until I cut off your head today in the presence of the preceptor.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततो द्रोणाभ्यनुज्ञातः पार्थः परपुरंजयः। भ्रातृभिस्त्वरयाऽऽश्लिष्टो रणायोपजगाम तम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : The subduer of hostile cities, Partha, was embraced by his brothers and with the permission of Drona he advanced for the combat.

sn: ततो दुर्योधनेनापि सभ्रात्रा समरोद्यतः। परिष्वक्तः स्थितः कर्णः प्रगृह्य सशरं धनुः॥
en: Thereupon, Karna was embraced by Duryodhana with his brothers. Taking up his bow and arrows he stood ready for fight.

sn: ततः सविद्युत्स्तनितैः सेन्द्रायुधपुरोगमैः। आवृतं गगनं मेधैर्बलाकापङ्क्तिहासिभिः॥
en: The sky was covered in clouds emitting flashes of lightning and the coloured bow of Indra appeared shedding its effulgent rays. The clouds seemed to be laughing on account of the presence of white cranes that were then flying.

sn: ततः स्नेहाद्धरिहयं दृष्ट्वा रङ्गावलोकिनम्। भास्करोऽप्यनयन्नाशं समीपोपगतान् घनान्॥
en: Seeing that Indra was thus showing his affection (towards Arjuna), the sun dispersed the clouds over his son.

sn: मेघच्छायोपगूढस्तु ततोऽदृश्यत फाल्गुनः। सूर्यातपपरिक्षिप्तः कर्णोऽपि समदृश्यत॥
en: Falguni (Arjuna) was invisible under cover of the clouds, but Karna was visible on account of the clouds being dispersed from him by the sun.

sn: धार्तराष्ट्रा यतः कर्णस्तस्मिन् देशे व्यवस्थिताः। भारद्वाजः कृपो भीष्मो यतः पार्थस्ततोऽभवन्॥
en: The sons of Dhritarashtra stood by Karna and the son of Bharadvaja, (Drona) Kripa and Bhishma stood by Partha.

sn: द्विधा रङ्गः समभवत् स्त्रीणां द्वैधमजायत। कुन्तिभोजसुता मोहं विज्ञातार्था जगाम ह॥
en: The assembly was also divided into two parties, so were the ladies also. And on learning the affair the daughter of Bhoja, Kunti fainted away.

sn: तां तथा मोहमापन्नां विदुरः सर्वधर्मवित्। कुन्तीमाश्वासयामास प्रेष्याभिश्चन्दनोदकैः॥
en: The learned in all the precepts of virtue, Vidura, revived the insensible Kunti by sprinkling over (her face) water mixed with sandal-paste.

sn: ततः प्रत्यागतप्राणा तावुभौ परिदंशितौ। पुत्रौ दृष्ट्वा सुसम्भ्रान्ता नान्वपद्यत किंचन॥
en: O being revived she was seized with fear on seeing her two sons clad in armour, but she could do nothing.

sn: तावुद्यतमहाचापौ कृपः शारद्वतोऽब्रवीत्। द्वन्द्वयुद्धसमाचारे कुशलः सर्वधर्मवित्॥
en: When the two (heroes) were ready with their great bows raised up, the son of Sharadvana, Kripa, well versed in all the precepts of virtue and expert in the rules of duels, said-

sn: अयं पृथायास्तनयः कनीयान् पाण्डुनन्दनः। कौरवो भवता साधु द्वन्द्वयुद्धं करिष्यति॥ त्वमप्येवं महाबाहो मातरं पितरं कुलम्। कथयस्व नरेन्द्राणां येषां त्वं कुलभूषणम्॥
en: Kripa said : “This son of Pandu is the youngest child of Kunti. He is a Kuru and he will fight a duel with you. O mighty armed hero, you should also tell us the lineage of your father and mother and the royal line in which you are an ornament.

sn: ततो विदित्वा पार्थस्त्वां प्रतियोत्स्यति वा न वा। वृथाकुलसमाचारैर्न युध्यन्ते नृपात्मजाः॥
en: Knowing this, Partha will fight with you, or he will not fight (as he will think proper.) The sons of kings never fight a duel with men of inferior lineage.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्तस्य कर्णस्य व्रीडावनतमाननम्। बभौ वर्षाम्बुविक्लिन्नं पद्ममागलितं यथा॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Thus addressed, Karna's face was flushed! with the blushes of shame and it looked like the pale lotus torn and disfigured by the showers of rains.

sn: दुर्योधन उवाच आचार्य त्रिविधा योनी राज्ञां शास्त्रविनिश्चये। सत्कुलीनश्च शूश्च यश्च सेनां प्रकर्षति॥
en: Duryodhana said : O preceptor, it is said in the Shastras that three classes of men cam claim royalty, namely persons of noble birth, heroes and those that lead soldiers.

sn: यद्ययं फाल्गुनो युद्धे नाराज्ञा योद्भुमिच्छति। तस्मादेषोऽङ्गविषये मया राज्येऽभिषिच्यते॥
en: But if Falguni is unwilling to fight with one who is not a king, I install him (Karna) as the king of Anga.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततस्तस्मिन् क्षणे कर्णः सलाजकुसुमैर्घटैः। काञ्चनैः काञ्चने पीद्दे मन्त्रविद्भिर्महारथः॥ अभिषिक्तोऽङ्गराज्ये स श्रिया युक्तो महाबलः। सच्छत्रवालव्यजनो जयशब्दोत्तरेण च॥
en: Vaishampayana said : When the cheers cease at that very moment the greatly powerful car-warrior Karna, seated on a golden seat, the (royal) umbrella over his head and yak tails waved by his side, was installed king of Anga by the Brahmanas, learned in the Mantras, in the proper form, with paddy, flowers, Ghata (water pots) and much fold.

sn: उवाच कौरवं राजन् वचनं स वृषस्तदा। अस्य राज्यप्रदानस्य सदृशं किं ददानि ते॥ प्रब्रूहि राजशार्दूल कर्ता ह्यस्मि तथा नृप। अत्यन्तं सख्यमिच्छामीत्याह तं स सुयोधनः॥
en: O king, (Karna) said to the Kauravas (Duryodhana), "What shall I give you compared," your gift of a kingdom! O king O best of men, I shall do all you will command." Suyodhana (Duryodhana) replied, “I long for your friendship."

sn: एवमुक्तस्ततः कर्णस्तथेति प्रत्युवाच तम्। हर्षाच्चोभौ समाश्लिष्य परां मुदमवापतुः॥
en: Having been thus addressed, Karna replied. “Be it so." They thereupon embraced each other in joy and felt great happiness.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततः स्रस्तोत्तरपटः सप्रस्वेदः सवेपथुः। विवेशाधिरथो रङ्गं यष्टिप्राणो ह्वयन्निव॥
en: Vaishampayana said: Thereupon Adhiratha (Karna's father), with his sheet loosely hanging down, trembling and perspiring, supporting himself on a stuff, entered the arena.

sn: तमालोक्य धनुस्त्यक्त्वा पितृगौरवयन्त्रितः। कर्णोऽभिषेकाशिराः शिरसा समवन्दत॥
en: Seeing him, Karna left his bow and impelled by filial regard bowed his head, wet with the water of his coronation.

sn: ततः पादाववच्छाद्य पटान्तेन ससमम्भ्रमः। पुत्रेति परिपूर्णार्थमब्रवीत् रथसारथिः॥
en: The charioteer (Adhiratha) hurriedly covered his feet with the end of his sheet and addressed the successful Karna as his son.

sn: परिष्वज्य च तस्याथ मूर्धानं स्नेहविक्लवः। अङ्गराज्याभिषेकामश्रुभिः सिषिचे पुनः॥
en: He (Adhiratha) embraced him (Karna) and wetted his head with tears, his head which was still wet with the water sprinkled over it at his coronation as the king of Anga.

sn: तं दृष्ट्वा सूतपुत्रोऽयमिति संचिन्त्य पाण्डवः। भीमसेनस्तदा वाक्यमब्रवीत् प्रहसन्निव॥
en: Seeing him (Adhiratha) the Pandavas considered him to be a son of a charioteer and Bhishma jeeringly said,

sn: न त्वमर्हसि पार्थेन सूतपुत्र रणे वधम्। कुलस्य सदृशस्तूर्णं प्रतोदो गृह्यतां त्वया॥
en: O Charioteer's son, you deserve no to be killed by Partha in the battle. You should better take up the whip (instead of the sword) which befits your race.

sn: अङ्गराज्यं च नार्हस्त्वमुपभोक्तुं नराधम। श्वा हुताशमीपस्थं पुरोडाशमिवाध्वरे॥
en: O worst of men, you are not worthy of enjoying the kingdom of Anga, as a dog deserves not the ghee placed before the sacrificial fire."

sn: एवमुक्तस्ततः कर्णः किंचित्प्रस्फुरिताधरः। गगनस्थं विनिःश्वस्य दिवाकरमुर्दक्षत॥
en: Thus addressed Karna looked at the sun in the sky and with slightly quivering lips he heaved a deep sigh.

sn: कोपादुत्ययात महाबलः। भ्रातृपद्मवनात् तस्मान्मदोत्कट इव द्विपः॥
en: Like a mad elephant the greatly strong Duryodhana rose in anger from among his brothers, who were like an assemblage of lotuses.

sn: सोऽब्रवीद् भीमकर्माणं भीमसेनमवस्थितम्। वृकोदर न युक्तं ते वचनं वक्तुमीदृशम्॥
en: He said to that doer of fearful deeds, Bhimasena there present, “Vrikodara, you should not speak such words.

sn: ततो दुर्योधनः क्षत्रियाणां बलं ज्येष्ठं योद्धव्यं क्षत्रबन्धुना। शूराणां च नदीनां च दुर्विदाः प्रभवाः किल॥
en: The strength is the cardinal virtue of the Kshatriyas; even a man of inferior birth deserve to be fought with. The sources of heroes and rivers are the same, both the always unknown.

sn: सलिलादुत्थितो वह्निर्येन व्याप्तं चराचरम्। दधीचस्यास्थितो वज्रं कृतं दानवसूदनम्॥
en: The fore that covers the whole world rises from water. The Danava destroying thunder was made of Dadhichi's bone.

sn: आग्नेयः कृत्तिकापुत्रो रौद्रो गाङ्गेय इत्यपि। श्रूयते भगवान् देवः सर्वगुह्यमयो गुहः॥
en: It is heard that the birth of the illustrious god Guha (Kartikeya) is full of all mysteries. Some say he is the son of Agni, (some say) he is the son of Kirtika, (some again say) he is the son of Rudra and (other say) he is the son of Ganga.

sn: क्षत्रियेभ्यश्च ये जाता ब्राह्मणास्ते च ते श्रुताः। विश्वामित्रप्रभृतयः प्राप्ता ब्रह्मत्वमव्ययम्॥
en: It is also heard that those that were born Kshatriyas became Brahmanas. Vishvamitra and other attained to eternal Brahma.

sn: आचार्यः कलशाज्जातो द्रोणः शस्त्रभृतां वरः। गौतमस्यान्ववाये च शरस्तम्बाच्च गौतमः॥
en: The foremost of all wielders of arms, the preceptor (Drona), was born in a water vessel and the son of Gautama (Kripa) sprung from a clump of heath.

sn: भवतां च यथा जन्म तदप्यागमितं मया। सकुण्डलं सकवचं सर्वलक्षणलक्षितम्। कथमादित्यसदृशं मृगी व्याघ्नं जनिष्यति॥
en: I know also about your own birth. Can a deer give birth to this tiger, as effulgent as the sun, born with a natural armour and ear-rings and possessing all auspicious mark?

sn: पृथिवीराज्यमर्होऽयं नाङ्गराज्यं नरेश्वरः। अनेन बाहुवीर्येण मया चाज्ञानुवर्तिना॥
en: This lord of men deserves the sovereignty of not only Anga but of the whole world, by the prowess of his arms and by my obedience to him.

sn: यस्य वा मनुजस्येदं न क्षान्तं मद्विचेष्टितम्। रथमारुह्य पद्भ्यां स विनामयतु कार्मुकम्॥
en: If there is any one to whom all that I have done to him (Karna) has became intolerable, let him ascend his car and bend his bow with the help of his feet."

sn: ततः सर्वस्य रङ्गस्य हाहाकारो महानभूत्। साधुवादानुसम्बद्धः सूर्यश्चास्तमुपागमत्॥
en: Thereupon there arose a loud cheer among all the spectators, approving of Duryodhana's speech. At this time the sun went down.

sn: ततो दुर्योधनः कर्णमालम्ब्यागकरे नृपः। दीपिकाग्निकृतालोकस्तस्माद् रङ्गाद् विनिर्ययौ॥
en: Then king Duryodhana took Karna's hand and led him out of the arena lighted with countless lamps.

sn: पाण्डवाश्च सहद्रोणाः सकृपाश्च विशाम्पते। भीष्मेण सहिताः सर्वे ययुः स्वं स्वं निवेशनम्॥
en: The Pandavas also with Drona, Kripa and Bhishma returned to their own homes. All the people also went the respective houses.

sn: अर्जुनेति जनः कश्चित् कश्चित् कर्णेति भारत। कश्चिद् दुर्योधनेत्येवं ब्रुवन्तः प्रस्थितास्तदा॥
en: O descendant of the Bharata race, some of them named Arjuna), some Karna and some Duryodhana (as the victor of the day) as they went away.

sn: कुन्त्याश्च प्रत्यभिज्ञाय दिव्यलक्षणसूचितम्। पुत्रमङ्गेश्वरं स्नेहाच्छन्ना प्रीतिरजायत॥
en: Kunti also was much pleased out of her motherly love towards her son Karna, for he had various auspicious marks on his person and for he was installed as the king of Anga.

sn: दुर्योधनस्यापि तदा कर्णमासाद्य पार्थिवा भयमर्जुनसंजातं क्षिप्रमन्तरधीयत॥
en: O king, Duryodhana, having obtained Karna, banished his fears arising out of Arjuna)'s proficiency in arms.

sn: स चापि वीरः कृतशस्त्रनिश्रमः परेण साम्नाभ्यवदत् सुयोधनम्। युधिष्ठिरस्याप्यभवत् तदा मतिन कर्णतुल्योऽस्ति धनुर्धरः क्षितौ॥
en: And that hero, (Karna), accomplished in arms also began to gratify Duryodhana with sweet speeches; and Yudhisthira was impressed with the belief that there was no warrior like Karna on earth.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच पाण्डवान् धार्तराष्ट्रांश्च कृतास्त्रान् प्रसमीक्ष्य सः। गुर्वर्थं दक्षिणाकाले प्राप्तेऽमन्यत वै गुरुः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Seeing the sons of Pandu and Dhritarashtra accomplished in arms, Drona thought that the time had come when he could demand the preceptor's Dakshina (remuneration).

sn: ततः शिष्यान् समानीय आचार्योऽर्थमचोदयत्। द्रोणः सर्वानशेषेण दक्षिणार्थं महीपते॥
en: O king, one day assembling his pupils together, the preceptor Drona asked his Dakshina from them all, saying-

sn: पञ्चालराजं दुपदे गृहीत्वा रणमूर्धनि। पर्यानयत भद्रं वः सा ख्यात् परमदक्षिणा॥
en: "Seize the kind of Panchala, Drupada, in battle and bring him to me. That will be the most acceptable Dakshina to me".

sn: तथेत्युक्त्वा तु ते सर्वे रथेस्तूर्णं प्रहारिणः। आचार्यधनदानार्थं द्रोणेन सहिता ययुः॥
en: Saying “Be it so," they all ascended their chariots with their arms and marched out with Drona in order to pay the remuneration to their preceptor.

sn: ततोऽभिजग्मुः पञ्चालान् निघ्नन्तस्ते नरर्षभाः। ममृदुस्तस्य नगरं दुपदस्य महौजसः॥ दुर्योधनश्च कर्णश्च युयुत्सुश्च महाबलः। दुःशासनो विकर्णश्च जलसंध: सुलोचनः॥ एते चान्ये च बहवः कुमारा बहुविक्रमाः। अहं पूर्वमहं पूर्वमित्येवं क्षत्रियर्षभाः॥
en: Those best of man destroyed the Panchalas and went to the capital of the greatly powerful Drupada and attacked it. Duryodhana, Karna, greatly strong Yuyutsu, Dushasana, Vikarna, Jalasandha, Sulochana. These and many other princes of great prowess, all foremost of Kshatriyas, vied with one another to become foremost in the attack.

sn: ततो वररथारूढाः कुमारा: सादिभिः सह। प्रविश्य नगरं सर्वे राजमार्गमुपाययुः॥
en: The princes, riding on first class chariots and followed by cavalry, entered the hostile capital and proceeded along its streets.

sn: तस्मिन् काले तु पाञ्चालः श्रुत्वा दृष्ट्वा महद् बलम् भ्रातृभिः सहितो राजंस्त्वरया निर्ययौ गृहात्॥
en: At this time the king of the Panchalas, seeing the great army and hearing its roar, soon came out of his palace with all his brothers.

sn: ततस्तु कृतसंनाहा यज्ञसेनसहोदराः। शरवर्षाणि मुञ्चन्तः प्रणेदुः सर्व एव ते॥
en: The king Yajnasena (Drupada) was well armed, but he was assailed by them (Kurus) with a shower of arrows, all uttering their war cry.

sn: ततो रथेन शुभ्रेण समासाद्य तु कौरवान्। यज्ञसेनः शरान् घोरान् ववर्ष युधि दुर्जयः॥
en: The invincible warrior, Yajnasena, riding on his white chariot, attacked the Kurus and began to rain his fearful arrows.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच पूर्वमेव तु सम्मन्त्र्य पार्थो द्रोणमथाब्रवीत्। दद्रिकात् कुमाराणामाचार्यं द्विजसत्तमम्॥
en: Vaishampanya said : Seeing the pride of the princes, Partha (Arjuna) spoke thus to the preceptor, that excellent Brahmana Drona.

sn: एषां पराक्रमस्यान्ते वयं कुर्याम साहसम्। एतैरशक्यः पाञ्चालो ग्रहीतुं रणमूर्धनि॥
en: “We shall display our power when they would finish theirs. The are not capable of killing the king of the Panchalas in the battle."

sn: एवमुक्त्वा तु कौन्तेया भ्रातृभिः सहितोऽनघः। अर्धकोशे तु नगरादतिष्ठद् बहिरेव सः॥
en: Having said this, that sinless son of Kunti (Arjuna) with his brothers waited outside the city at a distance of a mile.

sn: दुपदः कौरवान् दृष्ट्वा प्राधावत समन्ततः। शरजालेन महता मोहयन् कौरवी चमूम्॥ तमुद्यतं रथेनैकमाशुकारिणमाहवे। अनेकमिव संत्रासान्मेनिरे तत्र कौरवाः॥
en: Seeing the Kauravas, Drupada rushed forward and afflicted the Kuru army with a shower of arrows. Such was his lightness of motion on the field of battle that though he was fighting alone on a single chariot, the Kurus thought in fear that there was more then one Drupada.

sn: दुपदस्य शरा घोरा विचेरुः सर्वतो दिशम्। ततः शङ्खाश्च भेर्यश्च मृदङ्गाश्च सहस्रशः॥ प्रावाद्यन्त महाराज पाञ्चालानां निवेशने। सिंहनादश्च संजज्ञे पाञ्चालानां महात्मनाम्॥
en: The fearful arrows of Drupada fell on all sides and thousands of conches, trumpets and drums began to be sounded by the Panchalas in their houses. O great king, a terrible roar, like that of the lion, rose from the mighty Panchalas. The great sound of the twang of their bow-strings seemed to rend the very sky.

sn: धनुातलशब्दश्च संस्पृश्य गगनं महान्। दुर्योधनो विकर्णश्च सुबाहुदीर्घलोचनः॥ दुःशासनश्च संक्रुद्धः शरवर्षैरवाकिरन्। सोऽतिविद्धो महेष्वासः पार्षतो युधि दुर्जयः॥ व्यधमत् तान्यनीकानि तत्क्षणादेव भारत। दुर्योधनं विकर्णं च कर्णं चापि महाबलम्॥ नानानृपसुतान् वीरान् सैन्यानि विविधानि च। अलातचक्रवत् सर्वं चरन् बाणैरतर्पयत्॥
en: (Thereupon) Duryodhana, Vikarna, Subahu, Dirghalochana and Dushasana, becoming furious, began to shower arrows upon the enemy. The mighty bow-man, the son of Prishata (Drupada), invincible in battle, though pierced with arrows. Instantly began to afflict the hostile army. O descendant of the Bharata race, careering over the field of battle like a fiery wheel, he smote with his arrows Duryodhana, Vikarna, even greatly powerful Karna and many other heroic princes and various other soldiers and slaked their thirst for battle.

sn: तत्तस्तु नागराः सर्वे मुसलैर्यष्टिभिस्तदा। अभ्यवर्षन्त कौरव्यान् वर्षमाणा घना इव॥
en: Then the citizens showered upon the Kurus club, maces and other missiles, like cloud's showering rains.

sn: सबालवृद्धास्ते पौराः कौरवानभ्ययुस्तदा। श्रुत्वा सुतुमुलं युद्ध कौरवा नेव भारत॥ द्रवन्ति स्म नदन्ति स्म क्रोशन्तः पाण्डवान् प्रति। पाड्वास्तु स्वयं श्रुत्वा आर्तानां लोमहर्षणम्॥ अभिवाद्य ततो द्रोणं रथानारुरुहुस्तदा। युधिष्ठिरं निवार्याशु मा युध्यस्वेति पाण्डवम्॥
en: O descendant of the Bharata race, young and old, all the citizens, hearing of the battle, rushed out and assailed the Kurus. They (Kurus) broke and fled, wailing towards the Pandavas; and the Pandavas, hearing their terrible wall. Ascended their cars after duly worshipping Drona. Then Arjuna, hastily asking Yudhisthira not to engage in the fight by saying "Don't fight".

sn: माद्रेयौ चक्ररक्षौ तु फाल्गुनश्च तदाकरोत्। सेनाग्रगो भीमसेनः सदाभूद गदया सह॥
en: At that time appointing the sons of Madri (Nakula and Sahadeva) as the protectors of his chariot wheels, rushed out. And Bhima, ever in the front, ran ahead with his club in his hand.

sn: तदा शत्रुस्वनं श्रुत्वा भ्रातृभिः सहितोऽनघः। अयाज्जवेन कौन्तेयो रथेनानादयन् दिशः॥
en: The sinless son of Kunti (Arjuna), thus accompanied by his brother, hearing the shouts of the enemy, advanced towards them, filling the whole region with the rattle of the wheels of his chariot.

sn: पाञ्चालानां ततः सेनामुद्भूतार्णवनिःस्वनाम्। भीमसेनो महाबाहुर्दण्डपाणिरिवान्तकः॥ प्रविवेश महासेनां मकरः सागरं यथा। स्वयमभ्यद्रवद् भीमो नागानीकं गदाधरः॥
en: As a Makara enters the sea, so the mightyarmed Yama-like Bhima with his club in his hand entered the Panchala ranks and roared as fiercely as the ocean in a tempest. Ever skillful in battle, Bhima, the son of Pritha, upraising his club, attacked the soldiers riding on elephants with the powers of his arms like the great destroyer himself.

sn: स युद्धकुशलः पार्थो बाहुवीर्येण चातुलः। अहनत् कुञ्जरानीकं गदया कालरूपधृत्॥
en: Those huge animals like mountains, struck with Bhima's club, had their heads broken into pieces and they fill covered with blood, like cliffs loosened by thunder.

sn: ते गजा गिरिसंकाशाः क्षरन्तो रुधिरं बहु। भीमसेनस्य गदया भिन्नमस्तकपिण्डकाः॥ पतन्ति द्विरदा भूमौ वज्रघातादिवाचलाः। गजानश्वान् रथांश्चैव पातयामास पाण्डवः॥ पदातींश्च रथांश्चैव न्यवधीदर्जुनाग्रजः। गोपाल इव दण्डेन यथा पशुगणान् वने॥ चालयन् रथनागांश्च संचचाल वृकोदरः।
en: The Pandava, the elder of Arjuna, (Bhima) felled to the ground elephants and horses and cars by thousands and killed many foot soldiers and car-warriors. As a herdsman drives the cattle with his stuff in the wood, so did Vrikodara drive before him the chariots and elephants (of the hostile force).

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच भारद्वाजप्रियं कर्तुमुद्यतः फाल्गुनस्तदा॥ पार्षतं शरजालेन क्षिपन्नागात् स पाण्डवः। हयौघांश्च रथौघांश्च गजौघांश्च समन्ततः॥ पातयन् समरे राजन् युगान्ताग्निरिव ज्वलन्।
en: Vaishampayana said : Falguni (Arjuna), eager to do the favourite work of the son of Bharadvaja, (Drona), felled the son of Prishata (Drupada) from his elephant, covering him with arrows. O king, like the fire at the end of a Yuga, he felled in the battle thousands of horses, car and elephants.

sn: पाञ्चाला: सृञ्जयास्तथा॥ शरैर्नानाविधैस्तूर्णं पार्थं संछाद्य सर्वशः। सिंहनादं मुखैः कृत्वा समयुध्यन्त पाण्डवम्॥ ततस्ते हन्यमाना
en: Thereupon all the Panchalas and the Shrinjyas, being thus attacked (by Arjuna), assailed Partha with a shower of weapons of various kinds.

sn: तद् युद्धमभवद् घोरं सुमहाद्भुतदर्शनम्। सिंहनादस्वनं श्रुत्वा नामृष्यत् पाकशासनिः॥
en: They uttered from their mouths great shorts like the roars of lions and they desperately attacked the Pandava (Arjuna). The battle became fearful and furious to be hold. Hearing their great leonine shouts, he (Arjuna) became illed with wrath.

sn: ततः किीटी सहसा पाञ्चालान् समरेऽद्रवत्। छादयन्निषुजालेन महता मोहयन्निव॥
en: Kirti (Arjuna) immediately assailed the Panchalas in the battle and covering them with a shower of arrows, he greatly confused them.

sn: शीघ्रमभ्यस्यतो बाणान् संदधानस्य चानिशम्। नान्तरं ददृशे किंचिन् कौन्तेयस्य यशस्विनः॥
en: They, that saw the son of Kunti (at that time), could not mark any interval between his fixing the arrows on the bowstring and letting them off.

sn: सिंहनादश्च संजज्ञे साधुशब्देन मिश्रितः। ततः पाञ्चालराजस्तु तथा सत्यनिता सह॥ त्वरमाणोऽभिदुद्राव महेन्द्रं शम्बरो यथा। महता शरवर्षेण पार्थः पाञ्चालमावृषोत्॥
en: The whole place was filled with leonine shouts mixed with cheers of approval. Thereupon the king of the Panchalas, accompanied with Satyajit (his commander-in-chief). Rushed towards him with speed, as Indra did towards (the Danava) Shambara, Partha covered the Panchala king with a thick shower of arrows.

sn: ततो हलहलाशब्द आसीत् पाञ्चालके बले। जिघृक्षति महासिंहो गजानामिव यूथपम्॥
en: Thereupon arose a great uproar among the Panchala-host like the roar of a great lion when springing on the leader of a heard of elephants.

sn: दृष्ट्वा पार्थं तदाऽऽयान्तं सत्यजित् सत्यविक्रमः। पाञ्चालं वै परिप्रेप्सुर्धनंजयमुपारवत्॥ ततस्त्वर्जुनपाञ्चालौ युद्धाय समुपागतौ। व्यक्षोभयेतां तौ सैन्यमिन्द्रवैरोचनाविव॥
en: Seeing Arjuna rush towards the Panchalaking for slaying him, greatly powerful Satyajit attacked him. The two heroes (Arjuna and the Panchala-king) rushed upon each other like Indra upon Virochanas; and they broke each other's ranks.

sn: ततः सत्यजितं पार्थो दशभिर्मर्मभेदिभिः। विव्याध बलवद् गाढं तदद्भुतमिवाभवत्॥
en: Thereupon Parth “pierced Satyajit with ten keen arrows" at which feat the spectators were all amazed.

sn: ततः शरशतैः पार्थं पाञ्चालः शीघ्रमार्दयत्। पार्थस्तु शरवर्षेण छाद्यमानो महारथः॥ वेगं चक्रे महावेगो धनुामवमृज्य च। ततः सत्यजितश्चापं छित्त्वा राजानमभ्ययात्॥
en: Thereupon the Panchala (Satyajit) covered Partha with one hundred arrows. That great car-warrior Arjuna rubbed his bow-string in order to increase the force and velocity of his arrows. Then covering the enemy with a shower of arrows, he cut off the bow of Satyajit and rushed upon the king (Drupada).

sn: अथान्यद् धनुरादाय सत्यजिद् वेगवत्तरम्। सावं ससूतं सरथं पार्थं विव्याध सत्वरः॥
en: But Satyajit immediately took up an other bow and he soon pierced with arrows Partha, with his chariot, charioteer and horses.

sn: स तं न ममृषे पार्थः पाञ्चालेनार्दितो युधि। ततस्तस्य विनाशार्थं सत्वरं व्यसृजच्छरान्॥
en: Thus being assailed, the hero Partha did not forgive the Panchala (Satyajit). In order to kill him soon, he (Arjuna) pierced with a number of arrows.

sn: हयान् ध्वजं धनुर्मुष्टिमुभौ तौ पार्णिसारथी। स तथा भिद्यमानेषु कार्मुकेषु पुनः पुनः॥ हयेषु विनियुक्तेषु विमुखोऽभवदाहवे। स सत्यजितमालोक्य तथा विमुखमाहवे॥ वेगेन महता राजन्नभ्यवर्षत पाण्डवम्। तदा चक्रे महद् युद्धमर्जुनो जयतां वरः॥ खगमुद्धृत्य कौन्तेयः
en: (His enemy's) horses, flags, bow, clenched fist, charioteer and the attendant at his back. Seeing his bow repeatedly cut down. And his horses slain as often, he (Satyajit) desisted from the fight. Secing Satyajit thus desisted from the fight. The king (Drupada) attacked the Pandava (Arjuna) with great speed. Then that foremost of victorious heroes. Arjuna, fought a wonderful battle.

sn: तस्य पार्थो धनुश्छित्त्वा ध्वज चोळमपातयत्। पञ्चभिस्तस्य विव्याध हयान् सूतं च सायकैः॥
en: Cutting off his bow and felling his flatstaff on the grounds he pierced his enemy's horses and charioteer with five arrows.

sn: तत उत्सृज्य तच्चापमाददानं शरावरम्। सिंहनादमथाकरोत्॥
en: Thereupon that son of Kunti (Arjuna), throwing aside his bow and taking off his quiver, took up a scimitar and sent forth a leonine shout.

sn: पाञ्चालस्य रथस्येषामाप्लुत्य सहसापतत्। पाञ्चालरथमास्थाय अवित्रस्तो धनंजयः॥ विक्षोभ्याम्भोनिधिं पार्थस्तं नागमिव सोऽग्रहीत्। ततस्तु सर्वपाञ्चाला विद्रवन्ति दिशो दश॥
en: He suddenly leaped from his chariot and fell on that of the Panchala-king. Dhananjaya (Arjuna) stood fearlessly on the chariot of the Panchala-king. He seized him (Drupada) as Garuda seized a huge snake after agitating the waters of the deep sea. Thereupon all the Panchalas ran away in all directions.

sn: दर्शयन् सर्वसैन्यानां स बाह्वोर्बलमात्मनः। सिंहनादस्वनं कृत्वा निर्जगाम धनंजयः॥
en: Showing the prowess of arms to all the hosts, Dhananjaya (Arjuna), sending forth a leonine shout, came out of the Panchala ranks).

sn: आयान्तमर्जुनं दृष्ट्वा कुमाराः सहितास्तदा। ममृदुस्तस्य नगरं द्रुपदस्य महात्मनः॥
en: Seeing him return (with his captive), the princes laid waste the capital of the illustrious Drupada.

sn: अर्जुन उवाच सम्बन्धी कुरुवीराणां दुपदो राजसत्तमः। मा वधीस्तद्बलं भीम गुरुदानं प्रदीयताम्॥
en: Arjuna said : This best of kings Drupada is a relative of the Kuru heroes. Therefore, O Bhima, do no: kill his soldiers. Let us only give out preceptor's remuneration.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच भीमसेनस्तदा राजन्नर्जुनेन निवारितः। अतृप्तो युद्धधर्मेषु न्यवर्तत महाबलः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : O king thus prevented by Arjuna, the greatly strong Bhima, though unsatiated with the battle, refrained from the act of slaughter.

sn: ते यज्ञसेनं दुपदं गृहीत्वा रणमूर्धनि। उपाजहः सहामात्यं द्रोणस्य भरतर्षभ।६३॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, thus seizing Yajnasena Drupada in the battle with his ministers, they offered him to Drona.

sn: भग्नदर्प हृतधनं तं तथा वशमागतम्। स वैरं मनसा ध्यात्वा द्रोणो. दुपदमब्रवीत्॥
en: (Seeing the king) humiliated and deprived of wealth and brought under his complete control, Drona remembered his former hostility towards him and he thus spoke to him.

sn: विमृद्य तरसा राष्ट्र पुरं ते मृदितं मया। प्राप्य जीवं रिपुवशं सखिपूर्वं किमिष्यते॥
en: "Your kingdom and your capital have been laid waste by me. Receiving your like at my hand, do you desire to revive our old friendship?".

sn: एवमुक्त्वा प्रहस्यैनं किंचित् स पुनरब्रवीत्। मा भैः प्राणभयाद् वीर क्षमिणो ब्राह्मणा वयम्॥
en: Having said this, he smiled a little and again said, "O hero, do not fear for your life. We are Brahmans that are ever-forgiving.

sn: आश्रमे क्रीडितं क्रीडितं यत् तु त्वया बाल्ये मया सह। तेन संवर्द्धितः स्नेहः प्रीतिश्च क्षत्रियर्षभ॥
en: O beast of Kshatriyas, from that day when in your boyhood you played with me in the ĀDI PARVA hermitage, my love and affection for you have grown up.

sn: प्रार्थयेयं त्वया सख्यं पुनरेव जनाधिप। वरं ददामि ते राजन् राज्यस्यार्धमवाप्नुहि॥
en: O king, I ask for your friendship again. O king, I grant you as a boon half of your kingdom.

sn: अराजा किल नो राज्ञः सखा भवितुमर्हसि। अतः प्रयतितं राज्ये यज्ञसेन मया तव॥
en: O Yajnasena, how can one be a friend of a king who is not a king? And therefore I retain half of your kingdom.

sn: राजासि दक्षिणे कूले भागीरथ्याहामुत्तरे। सखायं मां विजानीहि पाञ्चाल यदि मन्यसे॥
en: You became the king of the territory lying on the southern side of the Bhagirathi and I become that of the northern side. O Panchala, if it please you, know me henceforth as your friend."

sn: दुपद उवाच अनार्शयमिदं ब्रह्मन् विक्रान्तेषु महात्मसु। प्रीये त्वयाहं त्वत्तश्च प्रीतिमिच्छामि शाश्वतीम्॥
en: Drupada said : O Brahmana, this is not (at all) wonderful to the man of noble soul and great prowess. I am pleased with you and I desire to give you everlasting pleasure.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्तः स तं द्रोणो मोक्षयामास भारत। सत्कृत्य चैनं प्रीतात्मा राज्या) प्रत्यपादयत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : O descendant of Bharata, having been thus addressed, Drona released him (Drupadas); and cheerfully performing the usual offices of regard, he bestowed upon him the half of the kingdom.

sn: माकन्दीमथ गङ्गायास्तीरे जनपदायुताम्। सोऽध्यावसद् दीनमनाः काम्पिल्यं च पुरोत्तमम्॥ दक्षिणांश्चापि पञ्चालान् यावच्चर्मण्वती नदी। द्रोणेन चैवं द्रुपदः परिभूयाथ पालितः॥
en: (Receiving the territory named) Makandi with many towns and cities, situated on the banks of the Ganges, Drupada lived in the best of cities, called Kampilya. After his defeat by Drona, he (Drupada) also ruled over the southern Panchala upto the banks of the Charmanavati river.

sn: क्षात्रेण च बलेनास्य नापश्यत् स पराजयम्। हीनं विदित्वा चात्मानं ब्राह्मण स बलेन तु॥ पुत्रजन्म परीप्सन् वै पृथिवीमन्वसंचरत्। अहिच्छत्रं च विषयं द्रोणः समभिपद्यत॥
en: He was well convinced that his could not defeat Drona by Kshatriya might alone, he being very much inferior to him in Brahma (spiritual) power. He therefore wandered over the world to find the rneans of obtaining a son (who could defeat Drona). (Meanwhile) Drona lived at Ahichatra.

sn: एवं राजन्नहिच्छत्रा पुरी जनपदायुता। युधि निर्जित्य पार्थेन द्रोणारा प्रतिपादिता॥
en: Which was full of towns and cities and which was bestowed upon him by Partha after defeating the hero (Drupada).

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततः संवत्सारस्यान्ते यौवराज्याय पार्थिव। स्थापितो तराष्ट्रेण पाण्डुपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः॥ धृतिस्थैर्य सहिष्णुत्वादानृशंस्यात् तथार्जवात्। भृत्यानम्नुकम्पार्थं तथैव स्थिरसौहृदात्॥
en: Vaisha'mpayana said : O king, after the expiration of a year (from this), the son of Pandu, Yudhisthira, was installed as the heir-apparent. For he was noted for his firmness, fortitude, patience, benev olence, frankness and unswerving honesty of heart.

sn: ततोऽदीर्घेण कालेन कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः। पितुरन्तर्दधे कीर्ति शीलवृत्तसमाधिभिः॥
en: Thereupon, within a very short time, the son of Kunti, Yudhisthira, overshadowed the deeds of his faiher by his good behaviour, manners and close application to business.

sn: असियुद्धे गदायुद्धे रथयुद्धे च पाण्डवः। संकर्षणादशिक्षद् वै शश्वच्छिक्षां वृकोदरः॥
en: The Pandava Vrikodara began to receive lessons from Sankarshana (Balarama) in sword-fight, club-fight and car-fight.

sn: समाप्तशिक्षो भीमस्तु द्युमत्सेनसमो बले। पराक्रमेण सम्पन्नो भ्रातृणामचरद् वशे॥
en: At the end of his education (in arms), he became in strength equal to Duymutsena. He remained in harmony with his brothers, becoming great in prowess.

sn: प्रगाढदृढमुष्टित्वे लाघवे वेधने तथा। क्षुरनाराचभल्लानां विपादानां च तत्त्ववित्॥ ऋजुवक्रविशालानां प्रयोक्ता फाल्गुनोऽभवत्। लाघवे सौष्ठवे चैव नान्यः कश्चन विद्यते॥ बीभत्सुसदृशो लोके इति द्रोणो व्यवस्थितः। ततोऽब्रवीद् गुडाकेशं द्रोणः कौरवसंसदि॥
en: Arjuna became famous for the firmness of his grasp (of weapons), for his lightness of motion, his precision of aim and his proficiency in Kshura, Naracha, Bhalla, Vipatha and other straight, crooked and heavy weapons. And Drona said that there was none in the world who was equal to Bibhatsa (Arjuna) in lightness of hand and in general proficiency. Thereupon (one day) Drona thus spoke to Gudakesha (Arjuna) before the assembly of Kauravas.

sn: अगस्त्यस्य धनुर्वेद शिष्यों मम गुरुः पुरा। अग्निवेश इति ख्यातस्तस्य शिष्योऽस्मि भारत॥ तीर्थात् तीर्थं गमयितुमहमेतत् समुद्यतः। तपसा यन्मया प्राप्तममोघमशनिप्रभम्॥ अस्त्रं ब्रह्मशिरो नाम यद् दहेत् पृथिवीमपि। ददता गुरुणा चोक्तं न मनुष्येष्विदं त्वया॥ भारद्वाज विमोक्तव्यमल्पवीर्येष्वपि प्रभो। त्वया प्राप्तमिदं वीर दिव्यं नान्योऽर्हति त्विदम्॥ समयस्तु त्वया रक्ष्यो मुनिसृष्टो विशाम्पते। आचार्यदक्षिणां देहि ज्ञातिग्रामस्य पश्यतः॥
en: In the time of yore Agastya had a disciple in the science of arms. Who was known as Agnivesha. He was my preceptor and I was his disciple. O descendant of Bharata, I obtained from him by asceticism a weapon, known by the name of Brahmashira, which can never be futile and which is like thunder itself and capable of consuming the whole earth. That weapon from what I have done may now descend from disciple to disciple. Giving it to me, my preceptor said, “O son of Bharadvaja, do not hurl this weapon against any human being and against one who possess but little energy." O hero, (Arjuna), you have obtained that celestial weapon (from me); none else deserves it. But O Vishampata, obey the command of that best of Rishis (Agnivesha). Now give your preceptor's Dakshina before all your relatives and cousins.

sn: ददानीति प्रतिज्ञाते फाल्गुनेनाब्रवीद् गुरुः। युद्धेऽहं प्रतियोद्धव्यो युध्यमानस्त्वयानघ॥
en: Falguni (Arjuna) promised to the preceptor "To give (the Dakshina)." Drona said, O sinless one, you must fight with me when I fight with you.'

sn: तथेति च प्रतिज्ञाय द्रोणाय कुरुपुङ्गवः। उपसंगृह्य चरणौ स प्रायादुत्तरां दिशम्॥
en: That best of Kurus promised this also to Drona. Touching his feet, he went away northwards.

sn: स्वभावादगमच्छब्दो महीं सागरमेखलाम्। अर्जुनस्य समो लांके नास्ति कश्चिद् धनुर्धरः॥
en: There arose a great shout covering the whole earth, bounded by the belt of sea. “There was no bowman in the whole world equal to Arjuna.”

sn: गदायुद्धेऽसियुद्धे च रथयुद्धे च पाण्डवः। पारगश्च धनुयुद्धे बभूवाथ धनंजयः॥
en: Pandava Dhananjaya became proficient in club-fight, sword-fight, car-fight and bowfight.

sn: नीतिमान् सकलां नीति विबुधाधिपतेस्तदा। अवाप्य सहदेवोऽपि भ्रातृणां ववृते वशे॥ द्रोणेनैव विनीतश्च भ्रातृणां नकुलः प्रियः। चित्रयोधी समाख्यातो बभूवातिरथोदितः॥
en: Sahadeva, obtaining the whole science of morality and duties from the lord of all science Drona, remained obedient to his brothers. Nakula, the favourite of his brothers, taught by Drona, became known ass a skilful warrior and a car-warrior.

sn: त्रिवर्षकृतयज्ञस्तु गन्धर्वाणामुपप्लवे। अर्जुनप्रमुखैः पार्थैः सौवीरः समरे हतः॥ न शशाक वशे कर्तुं यं पाण्डुरपि वीर्यवान्। सोऽर्जुनेन वशं नीतो राजाऽऽसीद् यवनाधिपः॥
en: Arjuna and the other Pandava princes became so powerful that they killed in battle the great Sauvira who had performed a sacrifice extending for three years, (remaining) undaunted by the attacks of the Gandharvas. The Yavana king, whom the powerful Pandu could not bring under subjection, was (also brought by Arjuna under control.

sn: अतीव बलसम्पन्नः सदा मानी कुरून् प्रति। विपुलो नाम सौवीरः शस्तः पार्थेन धीमता॥ दत्तामित्र इति ख्यातं संग्रामे कृतनिश्चयम्। सुमित्रं नाम सौवीरमर्जुनोऽदमयच्छरैः॥
en: The great powerful and ever showing disregard for the Kurus. The king, named Vipula of the Sauviras was slain by the intelligent Partha. Arjuna also subjugated by means of his arrows king Sumitra of Sauvira, also known as Dattamitra, who always sought for an encounter with him.

sn: भीमसेनसहायश्च रथानामयुतं च सः। अर्जुनः समरे प्राच्यान् सर्वानेकरथोऽजयत्॥
en: The third of the Pandava princes, assisted by Bhima, on only one single car, subjugated all the kings of the East backed by ten thousand cars.

sn: तथैवैकरथो गत्वा दक्षिणामजयद् दिशम्। धनौघं प्रापयामास कुरुराष्ट्र धनंजयः॥ एवं सर्वे महामत्मानः पाण्डवा मनुजोत्तमाः। परराष्ट्राणि निर्जित्य स्वराष्ट्रं ववृधुः पुरा॥
en: In the same way Dhananjaya conquered on a single car the whole of the South; and he sent immense booty to the kingdom of the Kurus. Thus did the foremost of men, the illustrious Pandavas.Conquering the kingdoms of others, extended their own kingdom in the time of yore.

sn: ततो बलमतिख्यातं विज्ञाय दृढधन्विनाम्। दूषितः सहसा भावो धृतराष्ट्रस्य पाण्डुषु। स चिन्तापरमो राजा न निद्रामलभनिशि॥
en: Seeing the great prowess and strength of these mighty bow-men, King Dhritarashtra's mind became suddenly poisoned against the Pandavas. From that day that king became filled with so much anxiety that he could not sleep.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच श्रुत्वा पाण्डुसुतान् वीरान् बलोद्रिक्तान् महौजसः। धृतराष्ट्रो महीपालश्चिन्तामगमदातुरः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Hearing that the heroic sons of Pandu were endued with great energy and prowess, the king Dhritarashtra became very miserable with anxiety.

sn: तत आहूय मन्त्रज्ञं राजशास्त्रार्थवित्तमम्। कणिकं मन्त्रिणां श्रेष्ठं धृतराष्ट्रोऽब्रवीद् वचः॥
en: Thereupon summoning that best of ministers, Kanika, learned in politics and expert in counsels, Dhritarashtra said-

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच उत्सित्ताः पाण्डवा नित्यं तेभ्योऽसूये द्विजोत्तम। तत्र मे निश्चिततमं संधिविग्रहकारणम्। कणिक त्वं ममाचक्ष्व करिष्ये वचनं तव॥
en: Dhritarashtra said : O best of Brahmanas, the Pandavas are daily over-shadowing the earth. I am very jealous of them. Should I have peace or war with them? O Kanika, advise me truly; I shall do your bidding.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच स प्रसन्नमनास्तेन परिपृष्टो द्विजोत्तमः। उवाच वचनं तीक्ष्णं राजशास्त्रार्थदर्शनम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : That best of Brahmanas feel answered him in these pointed words, well-agreeing with the import of politics.

sn: शृणु राजन्निदं तत्र प्रोच्यमानं मयानघ। न मेऽभ्यसूया कर्तव्या श्रुत्वैव कुरुसत्तम।॥
en: Kanika said: O sinless king, listen to me as I answer. O best of the Kurus, you should not be angry with me on hearing what I say.

sn: नित्यमुद्यतदण्डः स्यान्नित्यं विवृतपौरुषः। अच्छिद्रश्छिद्रदर्शी स्यात् परेषां विवरानुगः॥
en: Kings should ever be ready with upraised scepter (to rule) and they should ever extend their prowess. Carefully avoiding all faults of theirs, they should ceaselessly watch for the faults of others.

sn: नित्यमुद्यतदण्डाद्धि भृशमुद्विजते जनः। तस्मात् सर्वाणि कार्याणि दण्डेनैव विधारयेत्॥
en: If the king is ever ready with his uplifted scepter, every one fears him. Therefore he should ever have recourse to his scepter (chastisement) in all he does.

sn: नास्यच्छिद्रं परः पश्येच्छिद्रेण परमन्वियात्। गृहेत् कूर्म इवाङ्गानि रक्षेद् विवरमात्मनः॥ नासम्यक्कृतकारी स्यादुपक्रम्य कदाचन। कण्टको ह्यपि दुश्छिन्न आसावं जनयेच्चिरम्॥
en: He should so act as others (his enemies) may not find any fault in him. But he should see the faults (defects) others. He should keep his resources concealed as does a tortoise his members of body. Having begun a particular act, he should ever completely accomplish it. A thorn, if not wholly extracted, produces a fostering sore.

sn: वधमेव प्रशंसन्ति शत्रूणामपकारिणाम्। सुविदीर्णं सुविक्रान्तं सुयुद्धं सुपलायितम्॥ आपद्यापदि काले च कुर्वीत न विचारयेत्। नावज्ञेयो रिपुस्तात दुर्बलौऽपि कथंचन।॥
en: The killing of a harmful foe is always praiseworthy. If he be powerful, if he be a great warrior, one should watch for the hour of his disaster and then kill him without any scruple. O son, if the enemy be weak, still he should not be scorned.

sn: अल्पोऽप्यग्निर्वनं कृत्स्नं दहत्याश्रयसंश्रयात्। अन्धः स्यादन्धवेलायां वाधिर्यमपि चाश्रयेत्॥
en: A spark of fire can consume a forest if it can spread from object to object. They (kings) should sometimes feign deafness and blindness; for if they are incapable of chastising, they should pretend not to notice the faults. They should then consider their bows as made of straw.

sn: कुर्यात् तृणमयं चापं शयीत मृगशायिकाम्। सान्त्वादिभिरुपायैस्तु हन्याच्छत्रु वशे स्थितम्॥
en: But they should be as watchful as a herd of deer sleeping (in the woods). When your enemy will be in your hands, destroy him by any means, open or secret. Do not show him any mercy, though he seeks your protection.

sn: दया न तस्मिन् कर्तव्या शरणागत इत्युत्। निरुद्विग्नो हि भवति नहताज्जायते भयम्॥
en: An old enemy should be killed even by winning him over by wealth. Thus you must be free of anxiety, for there is no fear from a dead man.

sn: हन्यादमित्रं दानेन तथा पूर्वापकारिणम्। हन्यात् त्रीन् पञ्च सप्तेति परपक्षस्य सर्वशः॥
en: Destroy all the three, five and seven resources of the enemy; you must destroy them (enemies) by completely uprooting them.

sn: मूलमेवादितीश्छिन्द्यात् परपक्षस्य नित्यशः। ततः सहायांस्तत्पक्षान् सर्वांश्च तदनन्तरम्॥
en: Then you should destroy their allies and partisans. If the root (principal) is destroyed, they (allies) can never exist.

sn: छिन्नमूले ह्यधिष्ठाने सर्वे तज्जीविनो हताः। कथं नु शाखास्तिष्ठेरंश्छिन्नमूले वनस्पतौ॥
en: If the root of the lord of the forest (tree) is uprooted, its branches and twigs can never exist as before. Carefully concealing your own weakness and watching those of your enemies.

sn: एकाग्रः स्यादविवृतो नित्यं विवरदर्शकः। राजन् नित्यं सपत्नेषु नित्योद्विग्नः समाचरेत्॥
en: O king, you should rule over your kingdom, ever being very watchful.

sn: अग्न्याधानेन यज्ञेन काषायेण जटाजिनैः। लोकान् विश्वासयित्वैव ततो लुम्पेद् यथा वृकः॥
en: By maintaining the perpetual fire by sacrifices, by brown clothes, by matted locks and skin cloth. You should first gain the confidence of men (your enemies); and then you should spring upon them like a wolf.

sn: असुशं शौचमित्याहुरर्थानामुपधारणे। आनाम्य फलितां शाखां पक्वं पक्वं प्रशातयेत्॥
en: It is said that in earning wealth, hypocrisy is a cheap means. As a hooked staff is used to bend down a bough of a tree of pluck the ripe fruits.

sn: फलार्थोऽयं समारम्भो लोके पुंसां विपश्चिताम्। वहेदमित्रं स्कन्धेन यावत् कालस्य पर्ययः॥
en: So this method should be adopted in destroying one's own enemies. Carry your enemy on your shoulder till the time comes.

sn: ततः प्रत्यागते काले भिन्द्याद् घटमिवाश्मनि। अमित्रो न विमोक्तव्यः कृपणं बपि ब्रुवन्॥ कृपा न तस्मिन् कर्तव्या हन्यादेवापकारिणम्। हन्यादमित्रं सान्त्वेन तथा दानेन वा पुनः॥ तथैव भेददण्डाभ्यां सर्वोपायैः प्रशातयेत्।
en: When the times come, you can throw him down and break him into pieces as a earthen vessel is broken being thrown on stones. An enemy should never be allowed to escape, even if he piteously addresses you. You ought not to show him any inercy; he must be slain at once. Enemies should be destroyed by the arts of conciliation or the expenditure of money or by producing disunion amongst his allies or by the employment of every means in your power.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच कथं सान्त्वेन दानेन भेदैर्दण्डेन वा पुनः॥ अमित्रः शक्यते हन्तुं तन्मे ब्रूहि यथातथम्।
en: Dhritarashtra said : Tell me in detail how can a foe be destroyed by the arts of conciliation, or the expenditure of money or by producing disunion or by the employment of force.

sn: कणिक उवाच शृणु राजन् यथावृत्तं वने निवसतः पुरा॥ जम्बुकस्य महाराज नीतिशास्त्रार्थदर्शिनः।
en: Kanika said: O king, hear what happened in the days of yore. O great king, there dwelt in the forest a jackal well-acquainted with the science of politics.

sn: अथ कश्चित् कृतप्रज्ञः शृगाल: स्वार्थपण्डितः॥ सखिभिय॑वसत् सार्धं व्याघ्राखुवृकबभ्रुभिः। तेऽपश्यन् विपिने तस्मिन् बलिनं मृगयूथपम्॥ अशक्ता ग्रहणे तस्य ततो मन्त्रममन्त्रयन्।
en: The Jackal was wise and mindful of his own interest. He lived in the company of four friends, namely a tiger, a wolf, a mouse and a mongoose. They saw in the woods a strong deer, the leader of a herd, whom however they could not seize for his fleetness and strength. Thereupon they held a consultation.

sn: जम्बुक उवाच असकृद् यतितो ह्येष हन्तुं व्याघ्र वने त्वया।॥ युवा वै जवसम्पन्नो बुद्धिशाली न शक्यते। मूषिकोऽस्य शयानस्य चरणौ भक्षयत्वयम्॥ यथैनं भक्षितैः पादैर्व्याघ्रो गृहणातु वै ततः। ततो वै भक्षयिष्यामः सर्वे मुदितमानसाः॥
en: The Jackal said : O tiger, you have made many attempts to seize this deer, but your efforts were in vain, for this deer is young, fleet and intelligent. Let the mouse go and eat into its feet when it is asleep. When his feet will be thus eaten, let the tiger go and seize it. Then we shall all eat it with a delightful heart.

sn: जम्बुकस्य तु तद् वाक्यं तथा चक्रुः समाहिताः। मूषिकाभक्षितैः पादैर्मृगं व्याघ्रोऽवधीत् तदा॥
en: Hearing these words of the jackal, they carefully did what he said. The feet of the deer being eaten up by the mouse, he was killed by the tiger.

sn: दृष्ट्वाचेष्टमानं तु भूमौ मृगकलवरम्। स्नात्वाऽऽगच्छत भद्रं वोरक्षामीत्याह जम्बुकः॥
en: The Jackal said, “ Blessed be you! Go and perform your ablutions. I shall look after it (the deer)".

sn: शृगालवचनात् तेऽपि गताः सर्वे नदी ततः। स चिन्तापरमो भूत्वा तस्थौ तत्रैव जम्बुकः॥
en: Hearing what the Jackal said, they all went to a river. The Jackal waited there, deeply meditating what he should do (next).

sn: अथाजगाम पूर्वं तु स्नात्वा व्याघ्रो महाबलः। ददर्श जम्बुकं चैव चिन्ताकुलितमानसम्॥
en: The greatly strong tiger came first after his bath and saw the Jackal sitting in a pensive mind.

sn: व्याघ्र उवाच किं शोचसि महाप्राज्ञ त्वं नो बुद्धिमतां वरः। अशित्वा पिशितान्यद्य विहरिष्यामहे वयम्॥
en: The Tiger said : O greatly wise one, what are you pondering over? You are the foremost of all intelligent persons. Let us enjoy ourselves (now) by feasting on this carcass.

sn: जम्वुक उवाच शृणु मे त्वं महाबाहो यद् वाक्यं मूषिकोऽब्रवीत्। धिग् बलं पृगराजस्य मयाद्यायं मृगो हतः॥
en: The Jackal said: O mighty armed one, hear what the mouse has said. (He said)" Fie on the strength of the king of beasts (tiger). The deer has been killed by me.

sn: माहुबलमाश्रित्य तृप्तिमद्य गमिष्यति। गर्जमानस्य तस्यैवमतो भक्ष्यं न रोचये॥
en: He will gratify his hunger today by the might of my arms.” When he has thus boasted, I, for my part, do not wish to touch this food.

sn: व्याघ्र उवाच ब्रवीति यदि स ह्येवं काले ह्यस्मिन् प्रबोधितः। स्वबाहुबलमाश्रित्य हनिष्येऽहं वनेचरान्॥ खादिष्ये तत्र मांसानि इत्युक्त्वा प्रस्थितो वनम्। एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु मूषिकोऽप्याजगाम ह॥ तमागतमभिप्रेत्य शृगालोऽप्यब्रववीद् वचः।
en: The Tiger said: If the mouse has really said this, my sense is awakened. I shall from this day kill with the might of my own arms the beasts of the forest and feast on their flesh. Having said this he went away into the forest. At this time the mouse came there. Seeing him come, the Jackal thus spoke to him.

sn: जम्बुक उवाच शृणु मूषिक भद्रं ते नकुलो यदिहाब्रवीत्॥
en: The Jackal said : Blessed by you, O mouse. Listen to what the mongoose has said.

sn: मृगमांसं न खादेयं गरमेतन्न रोचते। मूषिकं भक्षयिष्यामि तद् भवाननुमन्यताम्॥
en: (He said) "The flesh of this deer is poisoned (by the touch of the tiger). I shall not eat it. If you give me permission I shall eat the mouse."

sn: तच्छुत्वा मूषिको वाक्यं संत्रस्तः प्रगतो बिलम्। ततः स्नात्वा स वै तत्र आजगाम वृको नृप॥
en: Having heard this, the mouse became alarmed and he quickly entered his hole. O king, then after his bath came there the wolf.

sn: तमागतमिदं वाक्यमब्रवीज्जम्बुकस्तदा। मृगराजो हि संक्रुद्धो न ते साधु भविष्यति॥ सकलत्रस्त्विहायाति कुरुष्व यदनन्तरम्। एवं संचेदितस्तेन जम्बुकेन तदा वृकः॥ ततोऽवलुम्पनं कृत्वा प्रयात: पिशिताशनः। एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु नकुलोऽप्याजगाम ह॥
en: On his coming, the Jackal spoke to him thus. The king of the beasts (tiger) has become angry with you. No good will come to you. He will be soon here with his wife. Do now as you please. The wolf, ever fond of animal food, fled contracting his body into the smallest dimensions, and thus was he got rid of by the jackal. At this time the mongoose came.

sn: तमुवाच महाराज नकुलं जम्बुको वने। स्वबाहुबलमाश्रित्य निर्जितास्तेऽन्यतो गताः॥ मम दत्त्वा नियुद्धं त्वं भुड्क्ष्व मांसं यथेप्सितम्।
en: O great king, the jackal thus spoke to the mongoose in the forest. I have defeated others with the might of my arms and they have already fled away. Fight with me first and then eat this flesh as you please.

sn: नकुल उवाच मृगराजो वृक्श्चैव बुद्धिमानपि मूषिकः॥ निर्जिता यत् त्वया वीरास्तमाद् वीरतरो भवान्। न त्वयाप्युत्सहे योद्धमित्युक्त्वा सोऽप्युपागमत्॥
en: The Mongoose said : When the king of the beasts (tiger) the wolf and the intelligent mouse have all been defeated by you, heroes as they are, you seem to be a greater hero than they. I do not desire (therefore) to fight with you: Saying this he went away.

sn: कणिक उवाच एवं तेषु प्रयातेषु जम्बुको हृष्टमानसः। खादति स्म तदा मांसमेकः सन् मन्त्रनिश्चयात्॥
en: Kanika said: When thus they all went away, the jackal was much pleased in his heart for the success of policy and he alone ate the flesh (of that deer).

sn: एवं समाचरन्नित्यं सुखमेधते भूपतिः। भयेन भेदयेद् भीरुं शूरमञ्जलिकर्मणा॥ लुब्धमर्थप्रदानेन समं न्यूनं तथौजसा। एवं ते कथितं राजशृणु चाप्यपरं तथा॥
en: If kings act in this way, they can always be happy. Thus should the timid, by exciting their fears, the courageous by the arts of conciliation, the covetous by gift of wealth and the inferiors and the equals by the exhibition of prowess, be brought into subjugation. O king, besides what I have said, listen to something else that I say.

sn: पुत्रः सखा वा भ्राता वा पिता वा यदि वा गुरुः। रिपुस्थानेषु वर्तन्तो हन्तव्या भूतिमिच्छता॥
en: If your son, friend, brother and father, or even your preceptor, become your enemy. If you desire prosperity, you should.

sn: शपथेनाप्यरिं हन्यादर्थदानेन वा पुनः। विषेण मायया वापि नोपेक्षते कथंचन। उभौ चेत् संशयोपेतौ श्रद्धावांस्तत्र वर्द्धते॥
en: Destroy him by curses, by incantations, by gift of wealth, by poison or by deception. He should never be neglected out of scorn. If both the parties be equal and success uncertain, then he who acts with diligence grows in prosperity.

sn: गुरोरप्यविलप्तस्य कार्याकार्यमजानतः। उत्पथप्रतिपन्नस्य न्याय्यं भवति शासनम्॥
en: If the preceptor himself be vain, ignorant of what should be done and what should be left undone and vicious in his ways, even he should be chastised.

sn: क्रुद्धोऽप्यक्रुद्धरूपः स्यात् स्मितपूर्वाभिभाषिता। न चाप्यन्यमपध्वंसेत् कदाचित् कोपसंयुतः॥ प्रहरिष्यन् प्रियं ब्रूयात् प्रहरन्नपि भारत। प्रहत्य च कृपायीत शोचेत च रुदेत च॥
en: If you are angry, show yourself as if you are not so, speaking then with even smiles. O descendant of Bharatas, never reprove any one with indications of anger. Speak soft words before you hit (your enemy), (speak soft words) even when you are hitting (your enemy). After hitting (your enemy), pity the victim and grieve for him and even shed tears.

sn: आश्वासयेच्चापि परं सान्त्वधर्मार्थवृत्तिभिः। अथास्य प्रहरेत् काले यदा विचलिते पथि॥
en: Securing confidence (of the enemy) by conciliation, by gift of wealth and by long kind behaviour. You must destroy him if he does not walk aright.

sn: अपि घोरापराधस्य धर्ममाश्रित्य तिष्ठतः। स हि प्रच्छाद्यते दोषः शैलो मेघैरिवासितैः॥
en: The greatly sinful men live as if they are very virtuous. He conceals his sins, as black clouds cover the mountains.

sn: यः स्यादनुप्राप्तवधस्तस्यागारं प्रदीपयेत्। अधनान् नास्तिकांश्चौरान विषये स्वे न वासयेत्॥
en: You should burn the house of those that should be killed by you. You should never permit beggars, atheists and thieves to live in you kingdom.

sn: प्रत्युत्थानासनाद्येन सम्प्रदानेन केनचित्। प्रतिविश्रब्धघाती स्यात् तीक्ष्णदंष्ट्रो निमग्नकः॥
en: By a sudden sally or pitched battle, by poison, by gift of wealth, or by any means, you must destroy your enemy. You can act with the greatest cruelty. You should make your teeth sharp (enough) to bite with fatal effect.

sn: अशस्तेिभ्यः शङ्केत शख्तेिभ्यश्च सर्वशः। अशक्याद् भयमुत्पन्नमपि मूलं निकृन्तति॥
en: You must destroy him so effectually that he may not again raise up his head. You should always fear even those from whom you have no fear. If you do not fear a man, by your root may be destroyed (your ruin inay come).

sn: न विश्वसेदविश्वस्ते विश्वस्ते नातिविश्वसेत्। विश्वासाद् भयमुत्पन्नं मूलान्यपि निकृन्ततिः॥
en: You should never trust the faithless, nor should you trust too much those that are faithful. If fear (enmity) is engendered in a man whom you trust, your root may be destroyed (your total ruin may come).

sn: चारः सुविहित: कार्य आत्मनश्च परस्य वा। पाषण्डांस्तापसादींश्च परराष्ट्रेषु योजयेत्॥
en: The spies should be first carefully tested of their fidelity and then they should be appointed in your cwn (kingdom) or in (the kingdom of others). The spies in the kingdoms of others should be scoundrels and persons in the garbs of ascetic.

sn: उद्यानेषु विहारेषु देवतायतनेषु च। पानागारेषु रथ्यासुसर्वतीर्थेषु चाप्यथ॥ चत्वरेषु च कूपेषु पर्वतेषु वनेषु च। समवायेषु सर्वेषु सरित्सु च विचारयेत्॥
en: They should be (placed) in gardens. In place of amusements, in temples. In drinkingballs, in streets and with all the Tirthas (state officials), in place of sacrifice, near wells, on mountains, in forests. In all places where people congregate and on rivers. They should move about in these places.

sn: वाचा भृशं विनीतः स्याद्धदयेन तथा क्षुरः। स्मितपूर्वाभिभाषी स्यात् सृष्टो रौद्राय कर्मणे॥
en: They should be humble in speech, but their hearts must be as sharp as the razors. When you are engaged in doing a very cruel and terrible act, you should talk with smiles on your lips.

sn: अञ्जलिः शपथः सान्त्वं शिरसा पादवन्दनम्। आशाकरणमित्येवं कर्तव्यं भूतिमिच्छता॥
en: If you desire for prosperity, you must (adopt these acts narnely) fold your hands, be humble, take oath, use conciliation, worship the feet of others by lowering your head and inspire hope.

sn: सुपुष्पितः स्यादफलः फलवान् स्याद् दुरारुहः। आमः स्यात् पक्वसंकाशो न च जीर्येत कर्हिचित्।।
en: A man of policy should be like a tree decked with flowers but bearing no fruits. If there be any fruiti, it must be inaccessible and at a great height. If ripe, they must look raw. Such a man never fades.

sn: त्रिवर्गे त्रिविधा पीडा ह्यनुबन्धस्तथैव च। अनुबन्धाः शुभा ज्ञेयाः पीडास्तु परिवर्जयेत्॥
en: Trivarga, (Dharma, Artha and Kama) has three evils knit together (with three goods). Extracting the good from it, the evil should be avoided. He who practices virtue has also two diseases, (evil to cope with).

sn: धर्मं विचरतः पीडा सापि द्वाभ्यां नियच्छति। अर्थं चाप्यर्थलुब्धस्य कामं चातिप्रवर्तिनः॥
en: (Namely) the want of wealth and the neglect of pleasure. Those in pursuit of pleasure are made unhappy for the neglect of the two others. And those who pursue pleasure suffer for the want of virtue and wealth.

sn: अगर्वितात्मा युक्तश्च सान्त्वयुक्तोऽनसूयिता। अवेक्षितार्थः शुद्धात्मा मन्त्रयीत द्विजैः सह॥
en: Therefore you should pursue virtue, wealth and pleasure in such a way that you may not have to suffer in any way. With humiliation and attention, without jealousy and solicitations, you should in all sincerity consult with Brahmanas in accomplishing your purpose.

sn: कर्मणा येन केनैव मृदुना दारुणेन च। उद्धरेद् दीनमात्मानं समर्थो धर्ममाचरेत्॥
en: When you are fallen, you should raise yourself by any means, either gentle or violent. When you have raised yourself, you should practice virtue.

sn: न संशयमनारुह्य नरो भद्राणि पश्यति। संशयं पुनरारुह्य यदि जीवति पश्यति॥
en: The man who has never met with any calamity can never have prosperity. This is seen in the life of one who has passed through calamities.

sn: यस्य बुद्धिः परिभवेत् तमतीतेन सान्त्वयेत्। अनागतेन दुर्बुद्धिं प्रत्युत्पन्नेन पण्डितम्॥
en: He who is afflicted with sorrow should be consoled by the recitation of old history. The ignorant (should be consoled) by the hope of future prosperity and the learned by pleasing office. He who quietly responses after concluding a treaty with an enemy, considering himself crowned with success.

sn: योऽरिणा सह संधाय शयीत कृतकृत्यवत्। स वृक्षागे यथा सुप्तः पतितः प्रतिबुध्यते॥
en: Is like a person who awakes after having failen down from the top of a tree where he slept. Counsel should be kept concealed without the fear of calumny.

sn: मन्त्रसंवरणे यत्नः सदा कार्योऽनसूयता। आकारमभिरक्षेत चारेणाप्यनुपालितः॥ नाच्छित्त्वा परमर्माणि नाकृत्वा कर्म दारुणम्। नाहत्वा मत्स्यघातीव प्राणोति महतीं श्रियम्॥
en: And while seeing everything with the eyes of his spies, he should conceit his own thoughts before the spies of others like a fisherman who becomes rich by catching and killing fish, a king grc" vs prosperous by tearing the vitals of his enemy and by doing some violent acts.

sn: कर्शितं व्याधितं क्लिन्नमपानीयमघासकम्। परिविश्वस्तमन्दं च प्रहर्तव्यमरेबलम्॥
en: The strength of your enemy as represented by his force should always be completely destroyed, by ploughing it up, by moving it down or by afflicting it with disease, starvation and want of drink.

sn: नार्थिकोऽर्थिनमभ्येति कृतार्थे नास्ति संगतम्। तस्मात् सर्वाणि साध्यानि सावशेषाणि कारयेत्॥
en: A person in want never goes to a person in affluence. When your purpose has been fulfilled, you need not go to the man whom you have hitherto looked to for its accomplishment.

sn: संग्रहे विग्रहे चैव यत्नः कार्योऽनसूयता। उत्साहश्चापि यत्नेन कर्तव्यो भूतिमिच्छता॥
en: Therefore, when you do a thing, do it completely, leaving nothing to be done. He who desires prosperity, should diligently exert to seek for allies and means in order to conduct his war.

sn: नास्य कृत्यानि बुध्येरन् मित्राणि रिपवस्तथा। आरब्धान्येव पश्येरन् सुपर्यवसितान्यपि॥
en: He should act in such a way that both friends and foes may not know his intention before the commencement of the act. Let them know it when the act has been commenced or ended.

sn: भीतवत् संविधातव्यं यावद् भयमनागतम्। आगतं तु भयं दृष्ट्वा प्रहर्तव्यमभीतवत्॥
en: As long as danger does not come, so long only should you look as if you are afraid. Seeing the danger already come, you should grapple it courageously.

sn: दण्डेनोपनतं शत्रुमनुगृहणाति यो नरः। स मृत्युमुपगृहणीयाद् गर्भमश्वतरी यथाः॥
en: The man, who trusts his enemy who is already under his control, invites his own death as a mule by her conception.

sn: अनागतं हि बुध्येत यच्च कार्यं पुरः स्थितम्। न तु बुद्धिक्षयात् किंचिदतिक्रामेत् प्रयोजनम्॥
en: You should consider the future acts as already arrived. Else on account of the loss of reason, you may overlook an important point (in accomplishing the act). He who desires prosperity, should always exert himself with energy and prudence.

sn: उत्साहश्चापि यत्नेन कर्तव्यो भूतिमिच्छता। विभज्य देशकालौ च दैवं धर्मादयस्त्रयः। नैःश्रेयसौ तु तौ ज्ञेयौ देशकालाविति स्थितिः॥
en: Adopting his measures (suited) to time and place, destiny and Dharma, Artha and Kama. It is well known that time and place produce the greatest good.

sn: तालवत् कुरुते मूलं बालः शत्रुरुपेक्षितः। गहनेऽग्निरिवोत्सृष्टः क्षिप्रं संजायते महान्॥
en: If an enemy is despised and over looked, he may soon grow like a palm tree extending its roots, or like a spark of fire in the deep forest that may soon flame upto a great conflagration.

sn: अग्निं स्तोकमिवात्मानं संधुक्षयति यो नरः। स वर्धमानो ग्रसते महान्तमपि संचयम्॥
en: As a small fire, if fed with fagots, soon becomes capable of coming all, so a man who increase his power making alliances, soon becomes capable of vanquishing even the strongest foe.

sn: आशां कालवतीं कुर्यात् कालं विघ्नेन योजयेत्। विजं निमित्ततो ब्रूयानिमित्तं वापि हेतुतः॥
en: The hope, that you give to your enemy, should be long deferred to be fulfilled. When the time comes for fulfilling it, invent some pretext to defer it still. Let the pretext appear as founded on some reason and let that reason (also) appear as founded on some other reason.

sn: क्षुरो भूत्वा हरेत् प्राणान् निशितः कालसाधनः। प्रतिच्छन्नो लोमहारी द्विषतां परिकर्तनः॥
en: Unpitying and sharp, concealed in their leathern cases, striking when opportunity comes, sweeping of all hair, kings should resemble razors in the mater of destroying their enemy.

sn: पाण्डवेषु यथान्यायमन्येषु च कुरूद्वह। वर्तमानो न मज्जेस्त्वं तथा कृत्यं समाचर॥ सर्वकल्याणसम्पन्नो विशिष्ट इति निश्चयः। तस्मात् त्वं पाण्डुपुत्रेभ्यो रक्षात्मानं नराधिप।९।।
en: O supporter of the Kuru dignity, act with the Pandavas and others as policy dictates and (act) in such a way that you may not have to reput in futuic. I have not the least doubt that you are endued with every blessing and good fortune, O king, therefore, protect yourself frorn the sons of Pandu.

sn: भ्रातृव्या बलिनो यस्मात् पाण्डुपुत्रा नराधिप। पश्चात्तापो यथा न स्यात् तथा नीतिर्विधीयताम्॥
en: O king, the sons of Pandu are stronger than their cousins (your sons). O chastiser of foes, I tell you plainly what you ought to do.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्त्वा सम्प्रतस्थे कणिकः सवगृहं ततः। धृतराष्ट्रोऽपि कौरव्यः शोकार्तः समपद्यत॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having said this Kanika went away to his house and the descendant of Kuru Dhritarashtra become pensive and sad.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततः सुबलपुत्रस्तु राजा दुर्योधनश्च ह। दुःशासनश्च कर्णश्च दुष्टं मन्त्रममन्त्रयन्॥ ते कौरव्यमनुज्ञाप्य धृतराष्ट्र नराधिपम्। दहने तु सपुत्रायः कुन्त्या बुद्धिमकारयन्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Thereupon after consulting with one another the son of Subala (Sakuni) king Duryodhana, Dushasana and Karna formed and evil conspiracy. They resolved with the sanction of the descendant of Kuru the king Dhritarashtra to burn to death Kunti with her sons.

sn: तेषामिङ्गित्तभावज्ञो विदुरस्तत्त्वदर्शिवान्। आकारेण च तं मन्त्रं बुबुधे दुष्टचेतसाम्॥
en: The wise and learned Vidura, capable of reading the heart (of men) by external signs, came to know from their demeanours the intention of those wicked-minded men.

sn: ततो विदितवेद्यात्मा पाण्डवानां हिते रतः। पलायने मतिं चने कुन्त्याः पुत्रैः सहानघः॥
en: Thereupon, the sinless Vidura, whose soul was enlightened with true knowledge and who was ever devoted to the good of the Pandavas, resolved that Kunti should escape with her sons.

sn: ततो वातसहां नावं यन्त्रयुक्तां पातकिनीम्। ऊर्मिक्षमा दृढां कृत्वा कुन्तीमिदमुवाच ह॥
en: Thereupon he procured a boat with machinery and flats and which was strong enough to withstand wind and waves. He then spoke to Kunti thus.

sn: एष जातः कुलस्यास्य कीर्तिवंशप्रणाशनः। धृतराष्ट्रः परीतात्मा धर्मं त्यजति शाश्वतम्॥ इयं वारिपथे युक्ता तरङ्गपवनक्षमा। नौर्यया मृत्युपाशात् सपुत्रा मोक्ष्यसे शुभे॥
en: Vidura said: This Dhritarashtra is born to destroy the fame and offspring of your (Kuru) race. Being wicked-minded, he is going to cast off eternal virtue. O amiable lady, I have kept ready in the river a boat, capable of withstanding both wind and waves. By it escape with your sons from the net of death.

sn: तच्छ्रुत्वा व्यथिता कुन्ती पुत्रैः सह यशस्विनी। नावमारुह्य गङ्गायां प्रययौ भरतर्षभ॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, having heard this, Kunti became deeply grieved. She then with her sons got into the boat and went over the Ganges.

sn: ततो विदुरवाक्येन नावं विक्षिप्य पाण्डवाः। धनं चादाय तैर्दत्तमरिष्टं प्राविशन् वनम्॥
en: Then leaving the boat according to the advice of Vidura, the Pandavas entered a forest taking the wealth that was given to them.

sn: निषादी पञ्चपुत्रा तु जातुषे तत्र वेश्मनि। कारणाभ्यागता दग्धा सह पुत्रैरनागसा॥
en: For some reasons a Nishada woman came to the house of lac and though (she was) innocent, she was burnt to death with her five sons.

sn: स च म्लेच्छाधमः पापो दग्धस्तत्र पुरोचनः। वञ्चिताश्च दुरात्मानो धार्तराष्ट्रा: सहानुगाः॥
en: The worst of Mlecchas, the sinful Purochana, was also burnt to death. Thus were deceived the sons of Dhritarashtra with their counsellors.

sn: अविज्ञाता महात्मानो जनानामक्षतास्तथा। जनन्या सह कौन्तेया मुक्ता विदुरमन्त्रिताः॥
en: Thus also were the illustrious sons of Kunti with their mother saved by the advice of Vidura; but the people did not know that they were alive.

sn: ततस्तस्मिन् पुरे लोका नगरे वारणावते। दृष्ट्वा जतुगृहं दग्धमन्वशोचन्त दुःखिताः॥
en: Thereupon the citizens of Varanavata, seeing the house of lac burnt down, became exceedingly grieved.

sn: राज्ञे च प्रेषयामासुर्यथावृत्तं निवेदितुम्। संवृत्तस्ते महान् कामः पाण्डवान् दग्धवानसि॥ सकामो भव कौरव्य भुड्क्ष्व राज्यं सपुत्रकः। तच्छ्रुत्वा धृतराष्ट्रस्तु सह पुत्रेण शोचयन्॥
en: They sent messenger to the king to tell him all that had happened and they said, “Your great end has been achieved, you have burnt to death the Pandavas. O descendant of Kuru, your desire is (now) fulfilled; enjoy the kingdom with your sons." Having heard this, Dhritarashtra with his sons expressed their sorrow.

sn: प्रेतकार्याणि च तथा चकार सह बान्धवैः। पाण्डवानां तथा क्षत्ता भीष्मश्च कुरुसत्तमः :॥
en: He performed the last rites of the Pandavas with his friends and relatives, with Kshatta (Vidura) and that foremost of the Kurus, Bhishma.

sn: जनमेजय उवाच पुनर्विस्तरशः श्रोतुमिच्छामि द्विजसत्तम। दाहं जतुगृहस्यैव पाण्डवानां च मोक्षणम्॥
en: Janamejaya said : O best of the twice-born, I desire to hear in detail the account of the burning of the house of lac and the escape of the Pandavas.

sn: सुनृशंसमिदं कर्म तेषां क्रूरोपसंहितम्। कीर्तयस्व यथावृत्तं परं कौतूहलं मम॥
en: That was a cruel act of theirs, acting under the counsel of the wicked. Recite the history to me, all as it happened. I am full of great curiosity.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच शृणु विस्तरशो राजन् वदतो मे परंतप। दाहं जतुगृहस्यैतत् पाण्डवानां च मोक्षणम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : O chastiser of foes, o king, listen to me, I shall describe to you the burning of the lachouse and the escape of the Pandavas.

sn: प्राणाधिकं भीमसेनं कृतविद्यं धनंजयम्। दुर्योधनो लक्षयित्वा पर्यतप्यत दुर्मनाः॥
en: Seeing Bhimasena exceedingly strong and Dhananjaya (Arjuna) highly accomplished, Duryodhana became pensive and sad.

sn: ततो वैकर्तनः कर्णः शकुनिश्चापि सौबलः। अनेकैरभ्युपायैस्ते जिघांसन्ति स्म पाण्डवान्॥
en: Thereupon the son of the Sun, Karna and the son of Subala, Sakuni, tried by various means to cause the death of the Pandavas.

sn: पाण्डवा अपि तत् सर्वं प्रतिचक्रुर्यथागतम्। उद्भावनमकुर्वन्तो विदुरस्य मते स्थिताः॥
en: The Pandavas, however, counteracted them one after the other as they were made and in obedience to the counsel of Vidura, they never talked it afterwards.

sn: गुणैः समुदितान् दृष्ट्वा पौराः पाण्डुसुतांस्तदा। कथयांचक्रिरे तेषां गुणान् संसत्सु भारत॥
