en: O descendant of Bharata, seeing the sons of Pandu, endued with all accomplishments, the citizens began to speak to their accomplishments in every place of resort.

sn: राज्यप्राप्तिं च सम्प्राप्त ज्येष्ठं पाण्डुसुतं तदा। कथयन्ति स्म सम्भूय चत्वरेषु सभासु च॥
en: Assembling in court-yards and in other places of meeting, they talked of the eldest son of Pandu as the person fit for governing the kingdom.

sn: प्रज्ञाचक्षुरचक्षुष्ट्वाद् धृतराष्ट्रो जनेश्वरः। राज्यं न प्राप्तवान् पूर्वं स कथं नृपतिर्भवेत्॥
en: (They said), "The king Dhritarashtra, though possessed of the eye of knowledge, did not obtain "le kingdom, because he was blind. How can he be king (now)?

sn: तथा शांतनवो भीष्मः सत्यसंधो महाव्रतः। प्रत्याख्याय पुरा राज्यं न स जातु ग्रहीष्यति॥
en: And the son of Shantanu, Bhishma, is of rigid vows and devoted to truth; having son relinquished the kingdom before, he will never accept it now.

sn: ते वयं पाण्डवज्येष्ठं तरुण वृद्धशीलिनम्। अभिषिञ्चाम् साध्वद्य सत्यकारुण्यवेदिनम्॥
en: We shall therefore with all proper ceremonies, in all the eldest eldest Pandava (Yudhisthira) endued with youth, accomplished in battle, versed in the Vedas and is truthful and kind.

sn: स हि भीष्मं शांतनवं धृतराष्ट्रं च धर्मवित्। सपुत्रं विविधैर्भोगैर्योजयिष्यति पूजयन्॥
en: Worshipping the of Shantanu, Bhishma and virtuous Dhritarashtra, he (Yudhisthira) will certainly maintain Bhishma and Dhritarashtra with all his sons."

sn: तेषां दुर्योधनः श्रुत्वा तानि वाक्यानि जल्पताम्। युधिष्ठिरानुरक्तानां पर्यतप्यत दुर्मतिः॥
en: The wicked-minded Duryodhana, hearing these words of the men attached towards Yudhisthira, was exceedingly grieved.

sn: स तप्यमानो दुष्टात्मा तेषां वाचो न चक्षमे। ईय॑या चापि संतप्तो धृतराष्टमुपागमत्॥
en: The wicked-minded much afflicted and he could not bear their words. Being inflamed with jealousy, he went to Dhritarashtra.

sn: ततो विरहितं दृष्ट्वा पितरं प्रतिपूज्य सः। पौरानुरागसंतप्तः पश्चादिदमभाषत॥
en: Finding him alone, he duly saluted him with reverence and having been distressed by the partiality of the citizens (towards Yudhisthira), he spoke thus-

sn: दुर्योधन उवाच श्रुता मे जल्पतां तात पौराणामशिवा गिरः। त्वामनादृत्य भीष्मं च पतिमिच्छन्ति पाण्डवम्॥
en: Duryodhana said : o father, I have heard (the citizens) uttering words of ill-omen. Passing you and Bhishma by, they desire the son of Pandu to be their king.

sn: मतमेतच्च भीष्मस्य न स राज्यं बुभुक्षति। अस्माकं तु परां पीडां चिकीर्षन्ति पुरे जनाः॥
en: man was Bhishma will give his consent to this, for he will not desire to rule the kingdom. It seems the citizens are desiring to inflict a great injury on us. own

sn: पितृतः प्राप्तवान् राज्यं पाण्डुरात्मगुणैः पुरा। त्वमन्धगुणसंयोगात् प्राप्तं राज्यं न लब्धवान्॥
en: Pandu formerly obtained the ancestral kingdom by virtue of his accomplishments. Because you were blind, you did not get the kingdom, though you have every accomplishment to obtain it.

sn: स एष पाण्डोर्दायाद्यं यदि प्राप्नोति पाण्डवः। तस्य पुत्रो ध्रुवं प्राप्तस्तस्य तस्यापि चापरः॥
en: If the son of Pandu now obtains the kingdom as his inheritance from Pandu, then his son will obtain it after him; that son's son also and so on, it will thus for ever descend on Pandu's line.

sn: ते वयं राजवंशेन हीनाः सह सुतैरपि। अवज्ञाता भविष्यामो लोकस्य जगतीपते॥
en: We shall then with all our sons be excluded from the royal line. O lord of the world, we shall be disregarded and hated by all the people.

sn: सततं निरयं प्राप्ताः परपिण्डोपजीविनः। न भवेम यता राजंस्तथा नीतिविधीयताम्॥
en: Becoming defendants on others for our food, we shall suffer perpetual distress. O king, therefore, adopt such counsel that is consonant with statesmanship.

sn: यदि त्वं हि पुरा राजन्निदं राज्यमवाप्तवान्। ध्रुवं प्राप्स्याम च वयं राज्यमप्यवशे जने॥
en: O king, however the people might be unfavourable towards us if you had obtained the kingdom before, we would have certainly succeeded to it.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवं श्रुत्वा तु पुत्रस्य प्रज्ञाचक्षुर्नराधिपः। कणिकस्य च वाक्यानि तानि श्रुत्वा स सर्वशः॥ धृतराष्ट्रो द्विधाचित्तः शोकार्तः समपद्यत। दुर्योधनश्च कर्णश्च शकुनिः सौबलस्तथा॥ दुःशासनचतुर्थास्ते मन्त्रयामासुरेकतः। ततो दुर्योधनो राजा धृतराष्ट्रमभाषत॥
en: Vaishampayana said: Having heard these words of his son and also all that Kanika had said, the king possessed of the eye of knowledge. Dhritarashtra, became afflicted with sorrow and his mind was full of misgivings. Then Duryodhana, Karna, the son of Subala Sakuni. Dushasana, these four held a consultation together. Then Duryodhana spoke thus to the king Dhritarashtra.

sn: पाण्डवेभ्यो भयं न स्यात् तान् विवासयतां भवान्। निपुणेनाभ्युपायेन नगरं वारणावतम्॥
en: "Send the Pandavas by some contrivance to the city of Varanavata. Then we will have no fear of them."

sn: धृतराष्ट्रस्तु पुत्रेण श्रुत्वा वचनमीरितम्। मुहूर्तमिव संचिन्त्य दुर्योधनमथाब्रवीत्॥
en: Dhritarashtra having heard these words of his son, reflected for a moment and then spoke to Duryodhana thus-

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच धर्मनित्यः सदा पाण्डुस्तथा धर्मपरायणः। सर्वेषु ज्ञातिषु तथा मयि त्वासीद् विशेषतः॥
en: Dhritarashtra said : "Pandu was ever devoted to virtue; he always behaved dutifully towards all his relatives but particularly towards me.

sn: नासौ किंचिद् विजानाति भोजानादि चिकीर्षितम्। निवेदयति नित्यं हि मम राज्यं धृतव्रतः॥
en: He cared not for food or dress or the enjoyments of the world, he was devoted to me and gave me everything even the kingdom.

sn: तस्य पुत्रो यथा पाण्डुस्तथा धाईपरायणः। गुणवाँल्लोकविख्यातः पौरवाणां सुसम्मतः॥
en: His son (Yudhisthira) is as much devoted to virtue as he was; he is possessed of every accomplishment; he is illustrious; he is the favourite of the people. sons

sn: ते स कथं शक्यतेऽस्माभिरपाकर्तुं बलादितः। पितृपैतामहाद् राज्यात् ससहायो विशेषतः॥
en: How can we exile him by force from the kingdom of his fore-fathers, specially as he possesses allies?

sn: भृता हि पाण्डुनामात्या बलं च सततं भृतम्। भृताः पुत्राश्च पौत्राश्च तेषामपि विशेषतः॥
en: The counsellors and the soldiers and their and grandsons, all were specially cherished and maintained by Pandu.

sn: पुरा सत्कृतास्तात पाण्डुना नागरा जनाः। कथं युधिष्ठिरस्यार्थे न नो हन्युः सबान्धवान्॥
en: They being thus formerly benefited by Pandu, O son, why should not the people of the city kill us all with our relatives and friends for the sake of Yudhisthira?

sn: दुर्योधन उवाच एवमेतन्मया तात भावितं दोषमात्मनि। दृष्ट्वा प्रकृतयः सर्वा अर्थमानेन पूजिताः॥
en: Duryodhana said : O father, what you say is perfectly true. (But) on account of the evil that is likely in store for us in the future, we think we must conciliate the people by bestowing wealth and honours.

sn: ध्रुवमस्मत्सहायास्ते भविष्यन्ति प्रधानतः। अर्थवर्गः सहामात्यो मत्संस्थोऽद्य महीपते॥
en: Thus they would surely side with us for this proof of our power. O king, the ministers and the treasury are now under our control.

sn: स भवान् पाण्डवानाशु विवासयितुमर्हति। मृदुनैवाभ्युपायेन नगरं वारणावतम्॥
en: Therefore, you should banish the Pandavas to the city of Varanavata by some gentle means.

sn: यदा प्रतिष्ठितं राज्यं मयि राजन् भविष्यति। तदा कुन्ती सहापत्या पुनरेष्यति भारत॥
en: O king, when I shall be instalied as king, then, O descendant of Bharata, Kunti with her son may again come back.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच दुर्योधन ममाप्येतद्धदि सम्परिवर्तते। अभिप्रायस्य पापत्वान्नैवं तु विवृणोम्यहम्॥
en: Dhritarashtra said : O Duryodhana, this is the very thought that exists in my mind, but from its sinfulness, I could not give it out.

sn: न च भीष्मो न च द्रोणो न च क्षत्ता न गौतमः। विवास्यमानान् कौन्तेयाननुमंस्यन्ति कर्हिचित्॥
en: Neither Bhishma, nor Drona, nor Kshatta (Vidura), nor Gautama, (Kripa) will ever sanction the banishment of the sons of Kunti.

sn: समा हि कौरवेयाणां वयं ते चैव पुत्रक। नैते विषममिच्छेयुर्धर्मयुक्ता मनस्विनः॥
en: O son, in their eyes we (Kurus) and the Pandavas are equal. Those wise and virtuous men will make no difference between us,

sn: ते वयं कौरवेयाणामेतेषां च महात्मनाम्। कथं न बध्यतां तात गच्छाम जगतस्तथा॥
en: O son, (if we do this), why should we not deserve death at the hands of the Kurus and of those illustrious men (Bhishma and others), nay of the whole world?

sn: दुर्योधन उवाच मध्यस्थः सततं भीष्मो द्रोणपुत्रो मयि स्थितः। यतः पुत्रस्ततो द्रोणो भविता नात्र संशयः॥
en: Duryodhana said : Bhishma is always neutral; the son of Droua (Ashvathama) is in my side. There is no doubt Drona will also be in that side in which his son will be.

sn: कृपः शारद्वतश्चैव यत एतौ ततो भवेत्। द्रोणं च भागिनेयं च न स त्यक्ष्यति कर्हिचित्॥
en: The son of Sharadvan, Kripa, will surely be on the side in which these two will be. He will never abandon Drona and his nephew (sister's son, Ashvathama).

sn: क्षत्तार्थबद्धस्त्वस्माकं प्रच्छन्नं संयतः परैः। न चैकः स समर्थोऽस्मान् पाण्डवार्थेऽधिबाधितुम्।२२॥
en: Kshatta (Vidura) is dependent on us for his livelihood, although he is covertly on the side of the enemy (the Pandavas). He alone can do us no harm, (even) if he sides the Pandavas.

sn: स विस्रब्धः पाण्डुपुत्रान् सह मात्रा प्रवासय। वारणावतमद्यैव यथा यान्ति तथा कुरु॥
en: (Therefore) without any fear, exile the sons of Pandu with their mother to Varanavata. Take such steps as they may go there this very day.

sn: विनिद्रकरणं घोरं हृदि शल्यमिवार्पितम्। शोकपावकमुद्भूतं कर्मणैतेन नाशय॥
en: Extinguish by this act the grief that consumes me like a fire, that robs me of my sleep and that princes my heart like a terrible dart.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततो दुर्योधनो राजा सर्वाः प्रकृतयः शनैः। अर्थमानप्रदानाभ्यां संजहार सहानुजः॥ धृतराष्ट्रप्रयुक्तास्ते केचित् कुशलमन्त्रिणः। कथयांचक्रिरे रम्यं नगरं वारणावतम्॥ अयं समाजः सुमहान् रमणीयतमो भुवि। उपस्थितः पशुपतेनगरे वारणावते॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Thereupon King Duryodhana with his brothers began slowly to win over the people to his side by bestowing on them wealth and honours. One day in the (royal) Court, some clever ministers, as instructed by Dhritarashtra, described the city of Varanavata as a (most) charming place. (They said), "The festival of Pashupati (Siva) has begun in the city of Varanavata and the concourse of people there is now great.

sn: सर्वरत्नसमाकीर्णे पुंसां देशे मनोरमे। इत्येवं धृतराष्ट्रस्य वचनाच्चक्रिरे कथाः॥
en: The procession is the most grand in the world; and all gems and jewels (now) there delight the heart." Thus did they (counsellors) under instruction from Dhritarashtra, speak (of the city). O sons,

sn: कथ्यमाने तथा रम्ये नगरे वारणावते। गमने पाण्डुपुत्राणां जज्ञे तत्र मतिर्नुप॥
en: O king, while they were speaking of the charming city of Varanavata, the Pandavas desired in their mind to go there.

sn: यदा त्वमन्यत नृपो जातकौतूहला इति। उवाचैतानेत्य तदा पाण्डवानम्बिकासुतः॥
en: When the king Dhritarashtra knew that their (Pandavas) curiosity had been awakened, then the son of Ambika, (Dhritarashtra) spoke thus to the Pandavas.

sn: ममैते पुरुषा नित्यं कथयन्ति पुनः पुनः। रमणीयतमं लोके नगरं वारणावतम्॥
en: Dhritarashtra said: My men tell me daily again and again that the city of Varanavata is the most charming in the world.

sn: ते ताता यदि मन्यध्वमुत्सवं वारणावते। सगणाः सान्वयाश्चैव विहरध्वं यथामराः॥
en: if you desire to see the festival of Varanavata, go (there) with your friends and followers and enjoy yourselves like the celestial.

sn: ब्राह्मणेभ्यश्च रत्नानि गायकेभ्यश्च सर्वशः। प्रयच्छध्वं यथाकामं देवा इव सुवर्चसः॥ कंचित् कालं विहृत्यैवमनुभूय परां मुदम्। इदं वै हास्तिनपुरं सुखिनः पुनरेष्यत॥
en: Bestow gems and jewels on all the Brahmanas and the musicians (there), sport there as the effulgent celestial. Enjoy there for sometime as much happiness as you like at pleasure and then return to Hastinapur.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच धृतराष्ट्रस्य तं काममनुबुध्य युधिष्ठिरः। आत्मनश्चासहायत्वं तथेति प्रत्युवाच तम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Yudhisthira, understanding the motives of Dhritarashtra and knowing himself weak and friendless, said, “Be it so."

sn: ततो भीष्मं शान्तनवं विदुरं च महामतिम्। द्रोणं च बाह्निकं चैव सोमदत्तं च कौरवम्॥ कृपमाचार्यपुत्रं च भूरिश्रवसमेव च। मान्यानन्यानमात्यांश्च ब्राह्मणांश्च तपोधनान्॥ पुरोहितांश्च पौरांश्च गान्धारी च यशस्विनीम्। युधिष्ठिरः शनैर्दीन उवाचेदं वचस्तदा॥
en: Then addressing the son of Shantanu, Bhishma, the wise Vidura, Drona, Valhika, the Kaurava Somadatta, Kripa, Ashvathama, Bhurisrava and other respected counsellors, Brahmanas, ascetics, priests, citizens and the illustrious Gandhari, Yudhisthira slowly and humbly spoke thus-

sn: रमणीये जनाकीर्णे नगरे वारणावते। सगणास्तत्र यास्यामो धृतराष्ट्रस्य शासनात्॥
en: Yudhisthira said : We go with our friends and followers to the charming and populous city of Varanavata at the command of Dhritarashtra.

sn: प्रसन्नमनसः सर्वे पुण्या वाचो विमुञ्चत। आशीभिबृंहितानस्मान् न पापं प्रसहिष्यते॥
en: Give us cheerfully your benedictions, so that acquiring prosperity with it, we may not be touched by sin.

sn: एवमुक्तास्तु ते सर्वे पाण्डुपुत्रेण कौरवाः। प्रसन्नवदना भूत्वा तेऽन्ववर्तन्त पाण्डवान्॥ स्वस्त्यस्तु वः पथि सदा भूतेभ्यश्चैव सर्वशः। मा च वोऽस्त्वशुभं किंचित् सर्वशः पाण्डुनन्दनाः।१८।
en: Vaishampayana said : Having been thus addressed by the son of Pandu, all the Kauravas cheerfully pronounced blessings on them, saying, "O sons of Pandu, let all the elements bless you on your way and let not the slightest evil befall you."

sn: ततः कृतस्वस्त्ययना राज्यलम्भाय पार्थिवाः। कृत्वा सर्वाणि कार्याणि प्रययुर्वारणावतम्॥
en: Having performed propitiatory rites for obtaining the kingdom and making all other preparations, the princes (the Pandavas) started for Varanavata.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्तेषु राज्ञा तु पाण्डुपुत्रेषु भारत। दुर्योधनः परं हर्षमगच्छत् स दुरात्मवान्॥ स पुरोचनमेकान्तमानीय भरतर्षभ। गृहीत्वा दक्षिणे पाणौ सचिवं वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥ ममेयं वसुसम्पूर्णा पुरोचन वसुंधरा। यथेयं मम तद्वत् ते स तां रक्षितुमर्हसि॥ न हि मे कश्चिदन्योऽस्ति विश्वासिकतरस्त्वया। सहायो येन संधाय मन्त्रयेयं यथा त्वया॥
en: Vaishampayana said : O descendant of Bharata, when the king thus addressed the sons of Pandu, the wickedminded Duryodhana became exceedingly happy. O best of the Bharata race, he summoned in private, Purochana and taking up his right hand, he thus spoke to that counsellor. O Purochana, this world, full of wealth, is mine. It is equally yours with me. (Therefore), you should protect it. I have no other more trustworthy supporter and counsellor than you with whom I can consult.

sn: संरक्ष तात मन्त्रं च सपत्नांश्च ममोद्धर। निपुणेनाभ्युपायेन यद् ब्रवीमि तथा कुरु॥
en: O sire, keep my counsel (a secret) and destroy my enemy by some clever device. Accomplish, what I ask you to do.

sn: पाण्डवा धृतराष्ट्रेण प्रेषिता वारणावतम्। उत्सवे विहरिष्यन्ति धृतराष्ट्रस्य शासनात्॥
en: The Pandavas have been sent by Dhritarashtra to Varanavata. They will sport there in the festival at the command of Dhritarashtra.

sn: स त्वं रासभयुक्तेन स्पन्दनेनाशुगामिना। वारणावतमद्यैव यथा यासि तथा कुरु॥
en: Do that by with you can reach Varanavata this very day on a car drawn by swift asses.

sn: तत्र गत्वा चतुःशालं गृहं परमसंवृतम्। नगरोपान्तमाश्रित्य कारयेथा महाधनम्॥
en: Going there, erect a quadrangle palace at the outskirts of the city, (which should be) rich in materials and furniture. Guard it (also) well.

sn: शणसर्जरसादीनि यानि द्रव्याणि कानिचित्। आग्नेयान्युत सन्तीह तानि तत्र प्रदापय॥
en: Use in it (in erecting that house,) hemp, resin and all other inflammable materials that are procurable.

sn: सर्पिस्तैलवसाभिश्च लाक्षया चाप्यनल्पया। मृत्तिका मिश्रयित्वा त्वं लेपं कुड्येषु दापय॥
en: Mixing a little earth with ghee, oil, fat and a large quantity of lac, plaster the wall with it.

sn: शणं तैलं घृतं चैव जतु दारूणि चैव हि। तस्मिन् वेश्मनि सर्वाणि निक्षिपेथाः समन्ततः॥ यथा च तन्न पश्येरन् परीक्षन्तोऽपि पाण्डवाः। आग्नेयमिति तत् कार्यमपि चान्येऽपि मानवाः॥ वेश्मन्येवं कृते तत्र गत्वा तान् परमार्चितान्। वासयेथाः पाण्डवेयान् कुन्ती च ससुहृज्जनाम्॥
en: Place carefully all over that house hemp, oil, ghee, lac and wood. In such a way that the Pandavas and other men may not even with scrutiny see them or conclude that it is made of inflammable materials. Erecting such a house and worshipping the Pandavas with great reverence, make them live in it with Kunti and all their friends.

sn: आसगानि च दिव्यानि यानानि शयनानि च। विधातव्यानि पाण्डूनां यथा तुष्येत वै पिता॥ यथा च तन्न जानन्ति नगरे वारणावते। तथा सर्वं विधातव्यं यावत् कालस्य पर्ययः॥
en: Place there for the Pandavas seats, conveyances and beds of best workmanship, as ordered my father. Manage all this in a way so that none in the city of Varanavata may know it, till the end we have in view is accomplished.

sn: ज्ञात्वा च तान् सुविश्वस्ताशयानानकुतोभयान्। अग्निस्त्वया ततो देयो द्वारतस्तस्य वेश्मनः॥
en: Knowing that they are sleeping in that house in confidence and without fear, set fire to it, beginning from the gate.

sn: दह्यमाने स्वके गेहे दग्धा इति ततो जनाः। न गर्हयेयुरस्मान् वै पाण्डवार्थाय कर्हिचित्॥
en: The people will think that they have been burnt to death in that burning house; and therefore none will be able to blame us for the death of the Pandavas,

sn: स तथेति प्रतिज्ञाय कौरवाय पुरोचनः। प्रायाद् रासभयुक्तेन स्पन्दनेनाशुगामिना॥
en: Purochana promised to that Kaurava (Duryodhana) to carry out all by saying, “Be it so" and he then went (away) on a swift car drawn by asses.

sn: स गत्वा त्वरितं राजन् दुर्योधनमते स्थितः। यथोक्तं राजपुत्रेण सर्वं चक्रे पुरोचनः॥
en: O king, ever obedient to Duryodhana, he went without loss of time. Purochana did all that the prince said, (asked him to do).

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच पाण्डवास्तु रथान् युक्तान् सदश्वैरनिलोपमैः। आरोहमाणा भीष्मस्य पादौ जगृहुरार्तवत्॥ राज्ञश्च धृतराष्ट्रस्य द्रोणस्य च महात्मनः। अन्येषां चैव वृद्धानां कृपस्य विदुरस्य च॥ एवं सर्वान् कुरून् वृद्धानभिवाद्य यतव्रताः। समालिङ्गय समानान् वै बालैश्चाप्यभिवादितः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : The Pandavas got on their cars yoked with fine horses having the speed like that of the wind, When ascending (the car), they touched in grief the feet of Bhishma, of the king Dhritarashtra, of the high-souled Drona, Kripa and Vidura and of all the other old men. Thus duly saluting all the elders of the Kuru race, embracing the equals, being saluted by even the boys.

sn: सर्वा मातृस्तथाऽऽपृच्छ्य कृत्वा चैव प्रदक्षिणम्। सर्वाः प्रकृतयश्चैव प्रययुर्वारणावतम्॥
en: Taking leave of all the mothers (elderly ladies), walking round them respectfully and bidding farewell to the citizens, they (the Pandavas) started for Varanavata.

sn: विदुरच महाप्राज्ञस्तथान्ये कुरुपुङ्गवाः। पौराश्च पुरुषव्याघ्रानन्वीयुः शोककर्शिताः॥ तत्र केचिद् ब्रुवन्ति स्म ब्राह्मणा निर्भयास्तदा। दीनान् दृष्ट्वा पाण्डुसुतानतीव भृशदुःखिताः॥
en: The greatly intelligent Vidura and other best of the Kurus and also the citizens followed these best of men (for some distance) in sorrow. Seeing the sons of Pandu affected with sorrow and in grief, some of the men of the city spoke thus-

sn: विषमं पश्यते राजा सर्वथा स सुमन्दधीः। कौरव्यो धृतराष्ट्रस्तु न च धर्म प्रपश्यति॥
en: “The king (Dhritarashtra) sees not things with an equal eye. He is always wickedminded. The Kuru Dhritarashtra dose not cast his eye on virtue.

sn: न हि पापमपापात्मा रोचयिष्यति पाण्डवः। भीमो वा बलिनां श्रेष्ठः कौन्तेयो वा धनंजयः॥
en: The Pandava (Yudhisthira), the best of all strong men Bhima, or Dhananjaya (Arjuna) will never commit the sin of rebellion.

sn: कुत एव महात्मानौ माद्रीपुत्रौ करिष्यत। तान् राज्यं पितृतः प्राप्तान् धृतराष्टो न मृष्यते॥
en: What these illustrious (princes) would do, the two sons of Madri will also do. They have inherited the kingdom from their father, but Dhritarashtra can not beat them.

sn: अधर्म्यमिदमत्यन्तं कथं भीष्योऽनुमन्यते। विवास्यमानानस्थाने नगरे योऽभिमन्यते॥
en: How could Bhishma sanction such an act of great sin? How could he sanction their exile to that wretched city?

sn: पितेव हि नृपोऽस्माकमभूच्छांतनवः पुरा। विचित्रवीर्यो राजर्षिः पाण्डुश्च कुरुनन्दनः॥
en: The son of Shantanu, Vichitravirya and the descendant of Kuru, the royal sage Pandu, were to us like our fathers.

sn: स तस्मिन् पुरुषव्याघ्र देवभावं गते सति। राजपुत्रानिमान् बालान् धृतराष्ट्रो न मृष्यते॥
en: Now that best of men (Pandu), having gone to heaven, Dhritarashtra can not bear these princes, his sons.

sn: वयमेतदनिच्छन्तः सर्व एव पुरोत्तमात्। गृहान् विहाय गच्छामो यत्र गन्ता युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: We can not sanction this. Therefore leaving this excellent city and our houses, we shall go to the place where Yudhisthira is going.

sn: तांस्तथावादिनः पौरान् दुःखितान् दुःखकर्शितः। उवाच मनसा ध्यात्वा धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: The king of virtue, Yudhisthira reflected for some time and then addressed in sorrow the citizens who were talking thus in grief.

sn: पिता मान्यो गुरुः श्रेष्ठो यदाह पृथिवीपतिः। अशङ्कमानैस्तत् कार्यमस्माभिरिति नो व्रतम्॥
en: “The king of the world (Dhritarashtra) is our father, (he is) worthy of our regard, (he is) our preceptor and our superior. It is our duty, to accomplish with auspicious mind whatever he commands.

sn: भवन्तः सुहृदोऽस्माकमस्मान् कृत्वा प्रदक्षिणम्। प्रतिनन्द्य तथाशीभिर्निवर्तध्वं यथा गृहम्॥ यदा तु कार्यमस्माकं भवद्भिपपत्स्यते। तदा करिष्यथास्माकं प्रियाणि च हितानि च॥
en: "You are our friends; walking round us and making us happy with your blessings, return to your homes. When the time comes for anything to be done for us by you, then accomplish all that is agreeable and beneficial to us."

sn: एवमुक्तास्तदा पौराः कृत्वा चापि प्रदक्षिणम्। आशीभिश्चाभिनन्द्यैताञ्जग्मुर्नगरमेव हि॥
en: Having been thus addressed, the citizens walked round the Pandavas and offered them their blessings. They then returned to the city.

sn: पौरेषु विनिवृत्तेषु विदुरः सत्यधर्मवित्। बोधयन् पाण्डवश्रेष्ठमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: When the citizens had left (the Pandavas), Vidura, learned in all the precepts of virtue, thus spoke to the eldest Pandava in order to want him (of his danger.)

sn: प्राज्ञः प्राज्ञप्रलापज्ञः प्रलापज्ञमिदं वचः। प्राज्ञं प्राज्ञः प्रलापज्ञः प्रलापज्ञं वचोऽब्रवीत्॥
en: The learned man (Vidura) conversant with the (Mlecha) Jargon, spoke thus to the learned man (Yudhisthira), also conversant with the (Mlecha) jargon (in that Mlecha jargon)."

sn: यो जानाति परप्रज्ञा नीतिशास्त्रानुसारिणीम्। विज्ञायेह तथा कुर्यादापदं निस्तरेद् यथा॥
en: He who knows the schemes of others (enemies) according to the dictates of political science, knowing it, should act in such a way as to avoid all dangers.

sn: अलोहं निशितं शस्त्रं शरीरपरिकर्तनम्। यो वेत्ति न तु तं नन्ति प्रतिघातविदं द्विषः॥
en: He, who knows that there are sharp weapons capable of cutting the body though not made of iron and understands also the means of warding them off, can never be injured by the enemy.

sn: कक्षघ्नः शिशिरघ्नश्च महाकक्षे बिलौकसः। न देहदिति चात्मानं यो रक्षति स जीवति॥
en: He lives who protects himself by the knowledge that neither the consumer of straw and wood not the drier of dews burns the inmates of a hole in the deep forest.

sn: नाचक्षुर्वेति पन्थानं नाचक्षुर्विन्दते दिशः। नाधृतिर्बुद्धिमाप्नोति बुध्यस्वैवं प्रबोधितः॥
en: The blind man sees not his way, (for) the blind man has no knowledge of direction. He who has no firmness never acquires prosperity. Knowing this, keep yourself always alert.

sn: अनाप्तैर्दत्तमादत्ते नरः शस्त्रमलोहजम्। श्वाविच्छरणमासाद्य प्रमुच्येत हुताशनात्॥
en: The man, who takes a weapon (which is) not made of iron (and which is) given him by his enemy, can escape from fire by making his house like hole of a jackal.

sn: चरन् मार्गान् विजानाति नक्षत्रैर्विन्दते दिशः। आत्मना चात्मनः पञ्च पीडयन् नानुपीड्यते॥
en: By travelling a man may know the ways and by the star he can ascertain the direction. He that keeps his five (senses) under control can never be oppressed by his enemy."

sn: एवमुक्तः प्रत्युवाच धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः। विदुरं विदुषां श्रेष्ठं ज्ञातमित्येव पाण्डवः॥
en: Having been thus addressed, the king of virtue, the son of Pandu, Yudhishthira, thus replied to that foremost of learned men, the illustrious Vidura. "I have understood you."

sn: अनुशिक्ष्यानुगम्यैतान् कृत्वा चैव प्रदक्षिणम्। पाण्डवानभ्यनुज्ञाय विदुरः प्रययौ गृहान्॥
en: Vidura, thus having instructed the Pandavas, walked round them and bidding them farewell, returned to his house.

sn: निवृत्ते विदुरे चापि भीष्मे पौरजने तथा। अजातशत्रुमासाद्य कुन्ती वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Vidura, Bhishma and citizens having gone back, Kunti came to Ajatashatru (Yudhisthira) and spoke thus-

sn: क्षत्ता यदब्रवीद् वाक्यं जनमध्येऽब्रुवन्निव। त्वया च स तथेत्युक्तो जानीमो न च तद् वयम्॥
en: "What Khattwa (Vidura) said to you in the midst of many people, so indistinctly as if he said nothing and what you said similarly (in reply) is not understood by us.

sn: यदीदं शक्यमस्माभिर्ज्ञातुं न च सदोषवत्। श्रोतुमिच्छामि तत् सर्वं संवादं तव तस्य च॥
en: "If it is not improper for us to know it, I desire to hear all that passed between you and him."

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच गृहादग्निश्च बोद्धव्य इति मां विदुरोऽब्रवीत्। पन्थाश्च वो नाविदितः कश्चित् स्पादिति धर्मधीः॥
en: Yudhisthira said : The virtuous Vidura said to me that I must know that the house (at Varanavata) is made of inflammable materials. (He further said) the way of escape will also be known to you."

sn: जितेन्द्रियश्च वसुधां प्राप्स्यतीति च मेऽब्रवीत्। विज्ञातमिति तत् सर्वं प्रत्युक्तो विदुरो मया॥
en: He told me "The man who is self controlled wins (the sovereignty) of the whole world." I replied to Vidura. “I have understood you."

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच अष्टमेऽहनि रोहिण्यां प्रयाताः फाल्गुनस्य ते। वारणावतमासाद्य ददृशुर्नागरं जनम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : The Pandavas stared for Varanavata on the eighth day of the month of Falguni when the star Rohini was ascendant; and arriving there they saw the town and its people.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततः सर्वाः प्रकृतयो नगराद् वारणावतात्। सर्वमङ्गलसंयुक्ता यथाशास्त्रमतन्द्रिताः॥ श्रुत्वाऽऽगतान् पाण्डुपुत्रान् नानायानैः सहस्रशः। अभिजग्मुर्नरश्रेष्ठान् श्रुत्वैव परया मुदा॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Hearing that the sons of Pandu were coming, all the citizens came speedily by thousands, out of the town of Varanavata with joy, on various conveyances, taking with them all the auspicious things as directed by the Shastras in order to receive those best of men.

sn: ते समासाद्य कौन्तेयान् वारणावतका जनाः। कृत्वा जयाशिषः सर्वे परिवार्यावतस्थिरे॥
en: Coming to the sons of Kunti, the citizens of Varanavata surrounded them and blessed them by uttering the word Jaya (victory).

sn: तैर्वृतः पुरुषव्याघ्रो धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः। विबभौ देवसंकाशो वज्रपाणिरिवामरैः॥
en: Being thus surrounded by them, that best of men, the king of virtue, Yudhisthira, looked as effulgent as the thunderer (Indra) in the midst of the celestial.

sn: सत्कृताश्चैव पौरैस्ते पौरान् सत्कृत्य चानघ। अलंकृतं जनाकीर्णं विविशुर्वारणावतम्॥
en: Being welcomed by the citizens and welcoming them in return, those sinless ones (the Pandavas) entered the populous and ornamented Varanavata.

sn: ते प्रविश्य पुरी वीरास्तूर्णं जग्मुरथो गृहान्। ब्राह्मणानां महीपालं रतानां स्वेषु कर्मसु॥
en: Entering the town, O king, those heroes first went to the houses of the Brahmanas engaged in their proper duties.

sn: नगराधिकृतानां च गृहाणि रथिनां तदा। उपतस्थुर्नरश्रेष्ठा वैश्यशूद्रगृहाण्यपि॥
en: Then those best of men went to the houses of the officials in charge of the town; then they went to the houses of the car warriors, then to those of the Vaishyas and then even to those of the Shudras.

sn: अर्चिताश्च नरैः पौरैः पाण्डवा भरतर्षभ। जग्मुरावसथं पश्चात् पुरोचनपुरस्सराः॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, thus adored by the citizens, the Pandavas went to their house with Purochana walking at the head (of the possession).

sn: तेभ्यो भक्ष्याणि पानानि शयनानि शुभानि च। आसनानि च मुख्यानि प्रददौ स पुरोचनः॥
en: Purochana gave them first class food and drink, beds and carpets and seats.

sn: तत्र ते स्तकृतास्तेन सुमहार्हपरिच्छदाः। उपास्यमानाः पुरुषैरूषुः पुरनिवासिभिः॥
en: Being served by Purochana and adored by the citizens, they (the Pandavas,) attired in costly robes, lived there.

sn: दशरात्रोषितानां तु तत्र तेषां पुरोचनः। निवेदयामास गृहं शिवाख्यमशिवं तदा॥
en: When they had lived there for ten nights, Purochana spoke to them about the house, called "Blessed,” though really (it was) unblessed.

sn: तत्र ते पुरुषव्याघ्रा विविशुः सपरिच्छदाः। पुरोचनस्य वचनात् कैलासमिव गुह्यकाः॥
en: Thereupon those best of men, attired in (costly) garments, entered that house at the request of Purochana, as Guhyakas enter (those) in the Kailasa (mountain).

sn: तच्चागारमभिप्रेक्ष्य सर्वधर्मभृतां वरः। उवाचाग्नेयमित्येवं भीमसेनं युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Inspecting that house, that foremost of all virtuous men, Yudhisthira, said to Bhimasena that the house was made of inflammable materials.

sn: जिघ्राणोऽस्य वसागन्धं सर्पिर्जतुविमिश्रितम्। कृतं हि व्यक्तमाग्नेयमिदं वेश्म परंतप॥
en: Yudhisthira said : O chastiser of foes, from the smell of fat and ghee mixed with lac, it is event, his house is made of inflammable materials.

sn: शणसर्जरसंव्यक्तमानीय गृहकर्मणि। मुञ्जबल्वजवंशादि द्रव्यं सर्वं घृतोक्षितम्॥ शिल्पिभिः सुकृतं ह्याप्तैर्विनीतैर्वेश्मकर्मणि। विश्वस्तं मामयं पापो दग्धुकामः पुरोचनः॥ तथा हि वर्तते मन्दः सुयोधनवसे स्थितः। इमां तु तां महाबुद्धिर्विदुरो दृष्टवांस्तथा॥ आपदं तेन मां पार्थं स सम्बोधितवान् पुरा। ते वयं बोधितास्तेन नित्यमस्मद्धितैषिणा॥ पित्रा कनीयसा स्नेहाद् बुद्धिमन्तोऽशिवं गृहम्। अनार्यैः सुकृतं गूढैर्दुर्योधनवशानुगैः॥
en: By the help of trusted and well skilled artisans, the enemies have nicely built this house with hemp, health, straw and Purochana desires to burn me after inspiring me with confidence. The wicked man, therefore, lives here, obedient to (the instruction of) Duryodhana. The greatly intelligent Vidura, knew this danger. Therefore, O son of Pritha, he told me of it beforehand. Knowing this, that well-wiser of ours. The younger brother of our father, out of affection for us, has told us about this house, so full of danger and constructed by the wretches under Duryodhana (who is) acting secretly (from behind).

sn: भीमसेन उवाच यदीदं गृहमाग्नेयं विहितं मन्यते भवान्। तथैव साधु गच्छामो यत्र पूर्वोषिता वयम्॥
en: Bhima said: If this house is known to you inflammable, then let us go to the place where we lived first.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच इह यत्तैर्निराकारैर्वस्तव्यमिति रोचये। अप्रमत्तैर्विचिन्वद्भिर्गतिमिष्टां ध्रुवामितः॥
en: Yudhisthira said : I think we should rather live here, seeming unsuspicious, but we must remain very cautious and keep our senses wide awake and as at the same time we must seek for some means of escape. us

sn: यदि विन्देत चाकारमस्माकं स पुरोचनः। क्षिप्रकारी ततो भूत्वा प्रदह्यादपि हेतुतः॥
en: If Purochana finds from our demeanour that we have learnt his design, he may suddenly burn to death by taking immediately steps.

sn: नायं विभेत्युपक्रोशादधर्माद् वा पुरोचनः। तथा हि वर्तते मन्दः सुयोधनवशे स्थितः॥
en: Purochana cares very little for obloquy and sin. The wretch lives here in obedience to (the instructions) of Duryodhana.

sn: अपि चेह प्रदग्धेषु भीष्मोऽस्मासु पितामहः। कोपं कुर्यात् किमर्थं वा कौरवान् कोपयीत सः॥
en: If we are brunt, will grandfather Bhishma be angry? Why would he make the Kurus angry with him by showing his anger.

sn: अथवापीह दग्धेषु भीष्मोऽस्माकं पितामहः। धर्म इत्येव कुष्येरन् ये चान्ये कुरुपुङ्गवाः॥
en: It may be that if we are brunt, our grandfather Bhishma and other best men of the Kuru race may be indignant for the sake of virtue.

sn: वयं तु यदि दाहस्य बिभ्यतः प्रद्रवेमहि। स्पशैर्निर्घातयेत् सर्वान् राज्यलुब्धः सुयोधनः॥
en: If we fly from this place from the fear of being brunt, Duryodhana, covetous for kingdom, will surely bring about our death by means of spies.

sn: अपदस्थान् पदे तिष्ठन्नपक्षान् पक्षसंस्थितः। हीनकोशान् महाकोशः प्रयोगैर्घातयेद् ध्रुवम्॥ तदस्माभिरिमं पापं तं च पापं सुयोधनम्। वञ्चयद्भिर्निवस्तव्यं छन्नावासं क्वचित् क्वचित्॥
en: The wicked Duryodhana has rank, power, friends, allies and wealth, but we have none. He can certainly destroy us by adopting many means. Deceiving this wretch and that wretch also, let us live in disguise for some time.

sn: ते वयं मृगयाशीलाश्चराम वसुधामिमाम्। तथा नो विदिता मार्गा भविष्यन्ति पलायताम्॥
en: Let us lead a life of hunting, wandering over the earth. We shall then be aware of all the paths that exist for escape.

sn: भौमं च बिलमद्यैव करवाम सुसंवृतम्। गूढश्वासान्न नस्तत्र हुताशः सम्प्रधक्ष्यति॥
en: We shall dig in all secrecy, this very day a subterranean passage in our room. If we can keep it secret from others, fire will not able to consume us.

sn: वसतोऽत्र यथा चास्मान्न बुध्येत पुरोचनः। पौरो वापि जनः कश्चित् तथा कार्यमतन्द्रितैः॥
en: Therefore we shall live here (and act in such a way) as Purochana and the citizens of Varanavata may not know what we are doing.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच विदुरस्य सुहृत् कश्चित् खनकः कुशलो नरः। विविक्ते पाण्डवान् राजन्निदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : O king, a friend of Vidura, a person wellskilled in mining, came and spoke thus to the Pandavas in private.

sn: प्रहितो विदुरेणास्मि खनकः कुशलो ह्यहम्। पाण्डवानां प्रियं कार्यमिति किं करवाणि वः॥ प्रच्छन्नं विदुरेणोक्तः श्रेयस्त्वमिति पाण्डवान्। प्रतिपादय विश्वासादिति किं करवाणि वः॥
en: "I have been sent by Vidura; I am wellskilled in mining. Tell me what favourite works of the Pandavas I shall perform. He trusts me and has said to me in private, “Go to Pandavas and accomplish their good. what can I do for you?

sn: कृष्णपक्षे चतुर्दश्यां रात्रावस्यां पुरोचनः। भवनस्य तव द्वारि प्रदास्यति हुताशनम्॥
en: Purochana will set fire to the door of your house on the night of the fourteenth day of the black fortnight.

sn: मात्रा सह प्रदग्धव्याः पाण्डवाः पुरुषर्षभाः। इति व्यवसितं तस्य धार्तराष्ट्रस्य दुर्मतेः॥
en: The desire of the wicked-minded Dhritarashtra's son (Duryodhana) is to burn the best of men, the Pandavas, with their mother.

sn: किंचिच्च विदुरेणोक्तो म्लेच्छवाचासि पाण्डव। त्वया च तत् तथेत्युक्तमेतद् विश्वासकारणम्॥
en: O Pandavas, something was told to you by Vidura in the Mlecha language and you too replied in that language. I tell you this as a credential."

sn: उवाच तं सत्यधृतिः कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः। अभिजानामि सौम्य त्वां सुहृदं विदुरस्य वै॥ शुचिमाप्तं प्रियं चैव सदा च दृढभक्तिकम्। न विद्यते कवेः किंचिदविज्ञातं प्रयोजनम्॥
en: Yudhisthira said : Yudhisthira, the truthful son of Kunti, thus spoke to him. O amiable one, I now know you as a dear and trusted friend of Vidura, true and ever devoted to him. There is no necessity (of ours) which that learned man (Vidura) does not know.

sn: यथा तस्य तथा नस्त्वं निर्विशेषा वयं त्वयि। भवतश्च यथा तस्य पालयास्मान् यथा कविः॥
en: As you are his, so you ours. Do not make any difference between him and us. We are as much yours as his. Protects us as that learned man (Vidura) protects us.

sn: इदं शरणमाग्नेयं मदर्षमिति मे मतिः। पुरोचनेन विहितं धार्तराष्ट्रस्य शासनात्॥
en: I know this inflammable house was built for me by Purochana at the command of the son of Dhritarashtra (Duryodhana).

sn: स पापः कोषवांश्चैव ससहायश्च दुर्मतिः। अस्मानपि च पापात्मा नित्यकालं प्रबाधते॥
en: That sinful, vicious and wicked-minded man, commanding wealth and allies, pursues us always (with his persecutions).

sn: सभवान् मोक्षयत्वस्मान् यत्नेनास्माद्भुताशनात्। अस्मास्विह हि दग्धेषु सकामः स्यात् सुयोधनः॥
en: Save us with exertion from the impending conflagration. If we are brunt to death, the desire of Duryodhana will be fulfilled.

sn: समृद्धमायुधागारमिदं तस्य दुरात्मनः। वप्रान्तं निष्पतीकारमाश्रित्येदं कृतं महत्॥ इदं तदशुभं नूनं तस्य कर्म चिकीर्षितम्। प्रागेव विदुरो वेद तेनास्मानन्वबोधयत्॥
en: Here is that wicked man's well stocked arsenal. This large house has been built abutting the high walls of the arsenal, without having any out let. This most curse device which was made (for our destruction) was known to Vidura and I was told of it by him.

sn: सेयमापदनुप्राप्ता क्षत्ता यां दृष्टवान् पुरा। पुरोचनस्याविदितानस्मांस्त्वं प्रतिमोचय॥
en: The danger that Kshatta (Vidura) saw beforehand is now at our door, Save us from this without the knowledge of Purochana.

sn: स तथेति प्रतिश्रुत्य खनको यत्नमास्थितः। परिखामुत्किरन्नाम चकार च महाबिलम्॥
en: The miner promised to do it by saying "Be it so"; and he began with care the work of excavation and he (soon) made a subterranean passage.

sn: चक्रे च वेश्मनस्तस्य मध्येनातिमहद् बिलम्। कपाटयुक्तमज्ञातं समं भूम्याश्च भारत॥
en: He made that subterranean passage in the centre of the house. O descendant of Bharata, it was in a level with the floor and closed up by doors (planks).

sn: पुरोचनभयादेव व्यदधात् संवृत्तं मुखम्। स तस्य तु गृहद्वारि वसत्यशुभधीः सदा॥ तत्र ते सायुधाः सर्वे वसन्ति स्म क्षपां नृप॥ दिवा चरन्ति मृगयां पाण्डवेया वनाद् वनम्। विश्वस्तवदविश्वस्ता वञ्चयन्तः पुरोचनम्। अतुष्टा तुष्टवद् राजन्नूषुः परमविस्मिताः॥
en: For the fear of Purochana, its mouth was thus covered. He (Purochana) kept a constant watch at the gate of the house. O king, they the (Pandavas) lived in the night in it with arms ready for use; and in the day they hunted from forests to forests. Thus lived they very guardedly deceiving Purochana with a show of trustfulness and contentment while in reality they were trustless and discontented.

sn: न चैनानन्वबुध्यन्त नरा नगरवासिनः अन्यत्र विदुरामात्यात् तस्मात् खनकसत्तमात्॥
en: The people of the city also did not know anything of these plans (of the Pandavas). Except the friend of Vidura, that good miner, none else knew anything.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तांस्तु दृष्ट्वा सुमनसः परिसंवत्सरोषितान्। विश्वस्तानिव संलक्ष्य हर्षं चक्रे पुरोचनः॥ पुरोचने तथा हृष्टे कौन्तेयोऽथ युधिष्ठिरः। भीससेनार्जुनौ चोभौ यमौ प्रोवाच धर्मवित्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having seen them living cheerfully and without suspicious for a full year, Purochana became exceedingly glad. Seeing Purochana ili that state of mind, the virtuous son of Kunti, Yudhishthira, thus spoke to Bhima, Arjuna and the twins (Nakula and Sahadeva).

sn: अस्मानयं सुविश्वस्तान् वेत्ति पापः पुरोचनः। वञ्चितोऽयं नृशंसात्मा कालं मन्ये पलायने॥
en: Yudhisthira said: The cruel hearted and sinful Purochana thinks us very trustful and he has thus been well deceived. I think (therefore) that the time for our escape has come.

sn: आयुधागारमादीप्य दग्ध्वा चैव पुरोचनम्। षट् प्राणिनो निधायेह द्रवामोऽनभिलक्षिताः॥
en: Setting fire to the arsenal, burning Purochana to death and leaving six bodies here, let us escape from this place, unobserved by any.

sn: अथ दानापदेशेन कुन्ती ब्राह्मणभोजनम्। चक्रे निशि महाराज आजग्मुस्तत्र योषितः॥ ता विहृत्य यथाकामं भुक्त्वा पीत्वा च भारत। जग्मुर्निशि गृहानेव समनुज्ञाप्य माधवीम्॥
en: On the occasion of an alms giving, Kunti fed on a certain night a large number of Brahmanas. There came also a number of ladies. O descendant of Bharata, they ate and drank and enjoyed themselves as much as they pleased. And they all returned home with the permissions of Madhvi (Kunti).

sn: निषादी पञ्चपुत्रा तु तस्मिन् भोज्ये यदृच्छया। अन्नार्थिनी समभ्यागात् सपुत्रा कालचोदिता॥ सा पीत्वा मदिरां मत्ता सपुत्रा मदविह्वला। सह सर्वैः सुतै राजंस्तस्मिन्नेव निवेशने॥ सुष्वाप विगतज्ञाना मृतकल्पा नराधिप। अथ प्रवाते तुमुले निशि सुप्ते जने तदा॥ तदुपादीपयद् भीमः शेते यत्र पुरोचनः। ततो जदुगृहद्वारं दीपयामास पाण्डवः॥
en: Impelled by fate, a Nishada woman with her five sons came there with the desire of obtaining food and she enjoyed herself there at pleasure. She drank wine and became drunk and incapable with her sons. O king, she with her sons slept in that house more dead than alive. O king, when all the people fell asleep, a violent storm began to blow on that night. Bhima then set fire to the house where Purochana was asleep; then the Pandava set fire to the door of that lac house.

sn: समन्ततो ददौ पश्चादग्नि तत्र निवेशने। ज्ञात्वा तु तद् गृहं सर्वमादीप्तं पाण्डुनन्दनाः॥ सुरङ्गां विविशुस्तूर्णं मात्रा सार्धमरिंदमाः। ततः प्रतापः सुमहाञ्छब्दश्चैव विभावसोः॥ प्रादुरासीत् तदा तेन बुबुधे स जनवजः। तदवेक्ष्य गृहं दीप्तमाहुः पौराः कृशाननाः॥
en: Then he set fire to that house in several places. When the sons of Pandu were satisfied that the house had caught fire in all parts. Those chastisers of foes, then speedily entered the subterranean passage with their mother. Thereupon the intense heat and the great roar of the fire. Awakened the people of the city; and seeing the house ablaze, they said in sorrowful face.

sn: पौरा ऊचुः दुर्योधनप्रयुक्तेन पापेनाकृतबुद्धिना। गृहमात्मविनाशाय कारितं दाहितं च तत्॥ अहो धिग् धृतराष्ट्रस्य बुद्धिर्नातिसमञ्जसा। यः शुचीन् पाण्डुदायादान् दाहयामास शत्रुवत्॥
en: The Citizens said : The wicked minded (Purochana) built this house to destroy the relatives of his employer under the instructions of the Duryodhana and he has (now) set fire to it. Fire Fire on SO Dhritarashtra, whose understanding is partial! He has burnt to death the heirs of Pandu, as if they were his enemies?

sn: दिष्ट्या त्विदानी पापात्मा दग्धोऽयमतिदुर्मतिः। अनागसः सुविश्वस्तान् यो ददाह नरोत्तमान्॥
en: The wicked minded and sinful (Purochana), who has brunt those best of men (the Pandavas) innocent and unsuspicious, has himself been (also) burnt to death as fate would have it.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवं ते विलपन्ति स्म वारणावतका जनाः। परिवार्य गृहं तच्च तस्थू रात्रौ समन्ततः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Thus bewailed the citizens of Varanavata. Surrounding the house, they remained for the whole night there.

sn: पाण्डवाश्चापि ते सर्वे सह मात्रा सुदुःखिताः। बिलेन तेन निर्गत्य जग्मुर्दुतमलक्षिताः॥
en: The Pandavas however with their sorrowful mother came out of the subterranean passage and fled unobserved in haste.

sn: तेन निद्रोपरोधेन साध्वसेन च पाण्डवाः। न शेकुः सहसा गन्तुं सह मात्रा परंतपाः॥
en: Those chastisers of foes, the Pandavas, on account of sleeplessness and fear, could not proceed with speed with their mother.

sn: भीमसेनस्तु राजेन्द्र भीमवेगपराक्रमः। जगाम भ्रातृनादाय सर्वान् मातरमेव च॥ स्कन्धमारोप्य जननी यमावरून वीर्यवान्। पार्थी गृहीत्वा पाणिभ्यां भ्रातरौ सुमहाबलः॥
en: O king of kings, Bhimasena, educed with great speed and power, took upon his body his mother and all his brothers. The greatly strong and energetic Vrikodara took his mother on his shoulder, the twins on his sides and the two sons of Pritha, his brothers (Arjuna and Yudhisthira) on both his arms.

sn: उरसा पादपान् भञ्जन् महीं पद्भ्यां विदारयन्। स जगामाशु तेजस्वी वातरंहा वृकोदरः॥
en: He broke the trees by his breast and pressed the earth with his feet. He tius marched on.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु यथासम्प्रत्ययं कविः। विदुरः प्रेषयामास तद् वनं पुरुषं शुचिम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : In the meanwhile, the learned Vidura sent to that forest a man of pure character whom he much trusted.

sn: स गत्वा तु यधोद्देशं पाण्डवान् ददृशे वने। जनन्या सह कौरव्य मापयानान् नदीजलम्॥
en: He went to the place where he was directed to go; and he was the descendants of Kuru, the son of Pandu, with their mother, measuring the depth of the water of a river in the forest.

sn: विदितं तन्महाबुद्धेर्विदुरस्य महात्मनः। ततस्तस्यापि चारेण चेष्टितं पापचेतसः॥ ततः प्रवासितो विद्वान् विदुरेण नरस्तदा। पार्थानां दर्शयामास मनोमारुतगामिनीम्॥ सर्ववातसहां नावं यन्त्रयुक्तां पताकिनीम्। शिवे भागीरथीतीरे नरैर्विस्त्रम्भिभिः कृताम्॥
en: The design of the wicked minded (Duryodhana) was made kncwn by this spy to the high souled and greatly learned Vidura. Therefore that learned man was sent by Vidura and that person showed to the sons of Pritha a boat, as swift as mind or wind. With mechanism and flags, made by trusted artificers and capable of withstanding wind and waves. It was on the banks of the holy Bhagirathi.

sn: ततः पुनरथोवाच ज्ञापकं पूर्वचोदितम्। युधिष्ठिर निबोधेदं संज्ञार्थं वचनं कवेः॥
en: He said these word to show that he was really sent (by Vidura). (He said), "O Yudhishthira, listen to what the learned Vidura) said to you.

sn: कक्षघ्नः शिशिरघ्नश्च महाकक्षे विलौकसः। न हन्तीत्येवमात्मानं यो रक्षति स जीवति॥
en: 'Neither the consumer of straw and wood, nor the drier of the dews burns the inmates of a hole in the forest. He escapes from death who protects himself.'

sn: तेन मां प्रेषितं विद्धि विश्वस्तं संज्ञयानया! भूयश्चैवाह मां क्षत्ता विदुरः सर्वतोऽर्थवित्॥ कर्णं दुर्योधनं चैव भ्रातृभिः सहितं रणे। शकुनि चैव कौन्तेय विजेतासि न संशयः॥
en: By these credentials know me to have been sent by Vidura and also to be his trusted agent. Kshatta (Vidura), learned in the precepts of all religions, told me also. O son of Kunti, that you shall surely defeat in battle Karna, Duryodhana with his brothers and Sakuni.

sn: इयं वारिपथे युक्ता नौरप्सु सुखगामिनी। मोचयिष्यति वः सर्वानस्माद् देशान्न संशयः॥
en: "This boat is ready on the waters. It will glide pleasantly on. It will surely carry away from these regions."

sn: अथ तान् व्यथितान् दृष्ट्वा सह मात्रा नरोत्तमान्। नावमारोष्य गङ्गायां प्रस्थितानब्रवीत् पुनः॥
en: Seeing those best of men with their mother pensive and sad, he made them get on the boat that was on the Ganges. Going with them hiniself, he again said ..

sn: विदुरो मूर्युपाघ्राय परिष्वज्य वचो मुहुः। अरिष्टं गच्छताव्यग्राः पन्थानमिति चाब्रवीत्॥
en: "Vidura, having smelled your heads and embracing you, has said it again and again that in commencing your auspicious journey and going alone, you should never be careless."

sn: इत्युक्त्वा स तु तान् वीरान् पुमान् विदुरचोदितः। तारयामास राजेन्द्र गङ्गां नावा नरर्षभान्॥
en: O king, having said this, the man sent by Vidura took those heroes, those best of man, to the other side of the Ganges on his boat.

sn: तारयित्वा ततो गङ्गां पारं प्राप्तांश्च सर्वशः। जयाशिषः प्रयुज्याथ यथागतमगाद्धि सः॥
en: Having taken them over the waters and seen them all safe on the opposite bank, he uttered the word Jaya (Victory) and blessing them he went back to the place whence he came.

sn: पाण्डवाश्च महात्मानः प्रतिसंदिश्य वै कवेः। गङ्गामुत्तीर्य वेगेन जग्मुर्मूढमलक्षिताः॥
en: The illustrious Pandavas also, sending some message to the learned (Vidura) and having crossed the Ganges, proceeded in haste and in great secrecy, being your observed by all.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच अथ रात्र्यां व्यतीतायामशेषो नागरो जनः। तत्राजगाम त्वरितो दिदृक्षुः पाण्डुनन्दनान्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : When the night had passed away a large number of the people of the city came there to see the sons of Pandu.

sn: निर्वापयन्तो ज्वलनं ते जना ददृशुस्ततः। जातुषं तद् गृहं दग्धममात्यं च पुरोचनम्॥
en: Those men extinguished the fire and saw that the house was made of lac and that the counsellor Purochana had been burnt to death.

sn: नूनं दुर्योधनेनेदं विहितं पापकर्मणा। पाण्डवानां विनाशायेत्येवं ते चुक्रुशुर्जनाः॥
en: The Citizens said : Indeed this sinful act was contrived by the wicked Duryodhana to destroy the sons of Pandu.

sn: विदिते धृतराष्ट्रस्य धार्तराष्ट्रो न संशयः। दग्धवान् पाण्डुदायादान् न ह्येनं प्रतिषिद्धवान्॥
en: There is on doubt that the son of Dhritarashtra (Duryodhana ) has burnt to death the heirs of Pandu, with the full knowledge of Dhritarashtra, else he would have been prevented (by his father).

sn: नूनं शांतनवोऽपीह न धर्ममनुवर्तते। द्रोणश्च विदुरश्चैव कृपश्चान्ये च कौरवाः॥
en: Indeed, the son of Shantanu (Bhishma,) Drona. Vidura, Kripa and other Kurus have not followed the dictates of duty.

sn: ते वयं धृतराष्ट्रस्य प्रेषयामो दुरात्मनः। संवृत्तस्ते परः काम: पाण्डवान् दग्धवानसि॥
en: "Let us (now) send words to the wicked minded Dhritarashtra, (saying), "Your great desire is fulfilled; you have burnt to death the Pandavas."

sn: ततो व्यपोहमानास्ते पाण्डवार्थे हुताशनम्। निषादी ददृशुर्दग्धां पञ्चपुत्रामनागसम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said: They then began to extinguish the fire to find out the Pandavas. They saw the Nishada woman burnt to death with her five sons.

sn: खनकेन तु तेनैव वेश्म शोधयता बिलम्। पांसुभिः पिहितं तच्च पुरुषैस्तैर्न लक्षितम्॥
en: The miner, while removing the ashes, covered with it the hole he had dug in such a way that it remained unnoticed by all who had gone there. to

sn: ततस्ते ज्ञापयामासुधृतराष्ट्रस्य नागराः। पाण्डवानग्निना दग्धानमात्यं च पुरोचनम्॥
en: The citizens then sent words Dhritarashtra to inform that the Pandavas along with counsellor Purochana had been burnt to death.

sn: श्रुत्वा तु धृतराष्ट्रस्तद् राजा सुमहदप्रियम्। विनाशं पाण्डुपुत्राणां विललाप सुदुःखितः॥
en: Hearing the great evil news of the death of the sons of Pandu, the king Dhritarashtra bewailed in great sorrow.

sn: अद्य पाण्डुम॒तो राजा मम भ्राता महायशाः। तेषु वीरेषु दग्धेषु मात्रा सह विशेषतः॥
en: Dhritarashtra said: King Pandu, my illustrious brother, has (indeed) died to day, when those heroes (the Pandavas) with their mother have been burnt to death.

sn: गच्छन्तु पुरुषाः शीघ्रं नगरं वारणावतम्। सत्कारयन्तु तान् वीरान् कुन्तिराजसुतां च ताम्॥
en: O man, go quickly to the city of Varanavata and perform the funeral rites of those heroes and of the daughter of the king of Kunti (Bhoja).

sn: कारयन्तु च कुल्यानि शुभानि च बृहन्ति च। ये च तत्र मृतास्तेषां सुहृदो यान्तु तानपि॥
en: Let also the bones of the deceased be sanctified by the usual rites and let all the beneficial and great acts be performed. Let the friends and relatives of those that have been burnt to death also go there.

sn: एवं गते मया शक्यं यद् यत् कारयितुं हितम्। पाण्डवानां च कुन्त्याश्च तत् सर्वं क्रियतां धनैः॥ एवमुक्त्वा ततश्चक्रे ज्ञातिभिः परिवारितः। उदकं पाण्डुपुत्राणां धृतराष्ट्रोऽम्बिकासुतः॥
en: Let also all other beneficial acts that ought to be performed by us for the Pandavas and Kunti be accomplished by spending wealth. Having said this, the son of Ambika, Dhritarashtra, surrounded by his relatives, offered oblations of water to the manes of the sons of Pandu,

sn: रुरुदुः सहिताः सर्वे भृशं शोकपरायणाः। हा युधिष्ठिर कौरव्य हा भीम इति चापरे॥
en: Being greatly afflicted with sorrow, he wept with all others! (saying,) Yudhisthira!" "O descendant of Kuru!" others cried, “O Bhima!"

sn: हा फाल्गुनेति चाप्यन्ये हा यमाविति चापरे। कुन्तीमार्ताश्च शोचन्त उदकं चक्रिरे जनाः॥
en: Others again, “O Falguni!" some again, "O the twins!” “O mother Kunti!” They thus bewailed and gave oblations of water.

sn: अन्ये पौरजनाश्चैवमन्वशोचन्त पाण्डवान्। विदुरस्त्वल्पशश्चक्रे शोकं वेद परं हि सः॥
en: The other citizens also bewailed for the Pandavas. But Vidura did not bewail much, for he knew the truth.

sn: पाण्डवाश्चापि निर्गत्य नगराद् वारणावतात्। नदीं गङ्गामनुप्राप्ता मातृषष्ठा महाबलाः॥
en: Leaving the city of Varanavata, the greatly strong Pandavas, altogether six in number with their mother, reached the river Ganges.

sn: दाशानां भुजवेगेन नद्याः स्रोतोजवेन च। वायुना चानुकूलेन तूर्णं पारमवाप्नुवन्॥
en: Aided by the strength of arms of the boatmen and by the rapidity of the current and favourable wind, they then speedily reached the opposite bank.

sn: ततो नावं परित्यज्य प्रययुर्दक्षिणां दिशम्। विज्ञाय निशि पन्थानं नक्षत्रगणसूचितम्॥
en: They then left the boat and proceeded towards the south, fin ding their way in the dark by the light of the stars.

sn: यतमाना वनं राजन् गहनं प्रतिपेदिरे। ततः श्रान्ताः पिपासार्ता निद्रान्धाः पाण्डुनन्दनाः॥ पुनरूचुर्महावीर्यं भीमसेनमिदं वचः। इतः कष्टतरं किं नु यद् वयं गहने वने। दिशश्च न विजानीमो गन्तुं चैव न शक्नुमः॥
en: O king, afternoon much suffering, they at last reached a dense forest. The sons of Pandu became tired, thirsty and sleepy. Yudhisthira thus spoke to the greatly energetic Bhimasena, “What could be more painful then our being in a dense forest! We do not know the directions; we are incapable of proceeding further.

sn: तं च पापं न जानीमो यदि दग्धः पुरोचनः। कथं तु विप्रमुच्येम भयादस्मादलक्षिताः॥
en: We do not know whether the sinful Purochana has or has not been burnt to death. How shall we escape from the dangers unobserved by others!

sn: पुनरस्मानुपादाय तथैव व्रज भारत। त्वं हि नो बलवानेको यथा सततगस्तथा॥
en: "O descendant of Bharata, take us on you again and proceed as before. You alone amongst us are strong and (you are) as swift as wind."

sn: इत्युक्तो धर्मराजेन भीमसेनो महाबलः। आदाय कुन्तीं भ्रातूंश्च जगामाशु महाबलः॥
en: Having been thus addressed by the king of virtue (Yudhisthira), the greatly strong Bhimasena took his brothers and Kunti (on his body) and walked on.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तेन विक्रममाणेन ऊरुवेगसमीरितम्। वनं सवृक्षविटपं व्याघूर्णितमिवाभवत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : By the force of that mighty (heroes') breast, the forest with its trees and their branches appeared to tremble,

sn: जङ्घावातो ववौ चास्य शुचिशुक्रागमे यथा। आवर्जितलतावृक्षं मार्ग चक्रे महाबलः॥
en: The motion of his thighs raised a wind like that of the month of Jyeshtha and Asharda. The greatly strong (Bhima) made a road for himself by treading down the trees and creepers.

sn: स मृद्गन् पुष्पितांश्चैव फलितांश्च वनस्पतीन्। अवरुज्य ययौ गुल्मान् पथस्तस्य समीपजान्॥
en: He proceeded on, breaking the kings of the forest (big trees) and the plants with their flowers and fruits that stood on his way.

sn: स रोषित इव क्रुद्धो वने भञ्जन् महादुमान्। त्रिप्रस्त्रुतमदः शुष्मी षष्टिवर्षी मतङ्गराट्॥
en: Thus breaking large trees angrily goes through the forest the leader of a hard of elephants of sixty years of age, the liquid juice (at the season of rut) trickling down the three parts of his body.

sn: गच्छतस्तस्य वेगेन तार्क्ष्यमारुतरंहसः। भीमस्य पाण्डुपुत्राणां मूछेव समजायत।॥
en: So great was the force with which Bhima, endued with the speed of Garuda or Maruta, proceeded that the Pandavas seemed to be fainted.

sn: असकृच्चापि संतीर्य दूरपारं भुजप्लवैः। पथि प्रच्छन्नमासेदुर्धार्तराष्ट्रभयात् तदा॥
en: By the strength of his arms, he swam across many streams difficult to be crossed; and they (the Pandavas) disguised themselves from the fear of the sons of Dhritarashtra.

sn: कृच्छ्रेण मातरं चैव सुकुमारी यशस्विनीम्। अवहत् स तु पृष्ठेन रोधस्सु विषमेषु च॥
en: He carried his delicate and illustrious mother on his back over even and uneven grounds on the banks of rivers.

sn: अगमच्च वनोद्देशमल्पमूलफलोदकम्। क्रूरपक्षिमृगं घोरं सायाह्ने भरतर्षभ।॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, in the evening he reached a fearful forest where fruits and roots and water were scarce and (which was) full of terrible roars of birds and beasts.

sn: घोरा समभवत् संध्या दारुणा मृगपक्षिणः। अप्रकाशा दिशः सर्वा वातैरासन्ननार्तवैः॥
en: The twilight became fearfully bark and (the roars of) birds and beasts (grew) fiercer. All sides became invisible, (being covered with darkness).

sn: शीर्णपर्णफलै राजन् बहुगुल्मक्षुपैर्दुमैः। भग्नावभग्नभूयिष्ठेर्नानाद्रुमसमाकुलैः॥
en: A strong wind began to blow. It broke and laid low many large and small trees and many creepers with fruits and dry leaves.

sn: ते श्रमेण च कौरव्यास्तृष्णया च प्रपीडिताः। नाशक्नुवंस्तदा गन्तुं निद्रया च प्रवृद्धया॥
en: Those descendants of Kuru (the Pandavas), afflicted with fatigue and thirst and heavy with sleep, were unable to proceed further.

sn: न्यविशन्त हि ते सर्वे निरास्वादे महावने। ततस्तृषापरिक्लान्ता कुन्ती पुत्रानथाब्रवीत्॥
en: They then sat down in that great forest without food or water and Kunti, afflicted with thirst, then spoke thus to her sons-

sn: माता सती पाण्डवानां पञ्चानां मध्यतः स्थिता। तृष्णया हि परीतास्मि पुत्रान् भृशमथाब्रवीत्॥
en: "I am the mother of the five Pandavas though I am now in their midst, yet I am burning in thirst!” She repeatedly said this to her sons.

sn: तच्छ्रुत्वा भीमसेनस्य मातृस्नेहात् प्रजल्पितम्। कारुण्येन मनस्तप्तं गमनायोपचक्रमे॥
en: Having heard this, Bhimasena's heart was warmed with compassion from the affection (he bore) for his mother and he began to proceed again.

sn: ततो भीमो वनं घोरं प्रविश्य विजनं महत्। न्यग्रोधं विपुलच्छायं रमणीयं ददर्श ह॥
en: Then Bhima, entering a large fearful and terrible forest, saw a beautiful banian tree with wide spreading branches.

sn: तत्र निक्षिप्य तान् सर्वानुवाच भरतर्षभः। पानीयं मृगयामीह विश्रमध्वमिति प्रभो॥
en: Placing them all there (under the tree) that best of the Bharata race, (Bhima) said, “O lord, rest here; I shall go to bring water.

sn: एते रुवन्ति मधुरं सारसा जलचारिणः। ध्रुवमत्र जलस्थानं महच्चेति मतिर्मम॥
en: I hear the sweet notes of the water fowl Sarashas. I think there must be a big lake (somewhere here)."

sn: अनुज्ञातः स गच्छेति भ्रात्रा ज्येष्ठेन भारत। जगाम तत्र यत्र स्म सारसा जलचारिणः॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, commanded by his eldest brother who said, "Go," he went there where the aquatic Sarasas were.

sn: स तत्र पीत्वा पानीयं स्नात्वा च भरतर्षभ। तेषामर्थे च जग्राह भ्रातृणां भ्रातृवत्सलः। उत्तरीयेण पानीयमानयामास भारत॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, affectionate to his brothers he want for the sake of his bothers. He drank water and bathed there in that lake; he brought water for them by soaking his upper garment.

sn: गव्यूतिमात्रादागत्य त्वरितो मातरं प्रति। शोकदुःखपरीतात्मा निःशश्वासोरगो यथा॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, retracing his way with all speed, over four miles he came to his mother and began to sigh like a snake in sorrow and grief.

sn: स सुप्तां मातरं दृष्ट्वा भ्रातूंश्च वसुधातले। भृशं शोकपरीतात्मा विललाप वृकोदरः॥
en: Seeing his mother and brothers asleep on the ground, Vrikodara was greatly afflicted with grief and lamented thus-

sn: अतः कष्टतरं किं नु द्रष्टव्यं हि भविष्यति। यत् पश्यामि महीसुप्तान् भ्रातृनद्य सुमन्दभाक्॥
en: ever "Alas! what more painful sight can I see then what I see now, my brothers sleeping on the ground! O unfortunate am I!

sn: शयनेषु परार्येषु ये पुरा वारणावते। नाधिजग्मुस्तदा निद्रां तेऽद्य सुप्ता महीतले॥
en: They who could not formerly sleep at Varanavata on the softest and costliest bed are now asleep on the bare ground!

sn: स्वसारं वसुदेवस्य शत्रुसङ्घावमर्दिनः। कुन्तिराजसुतां कुन्तीं सर्वलक्षणपूजिताम्॥ स्नुषां विचित्रवीर्यस्य भार्यां पाण्डोर्महात्मनः। तथैव चास्मज्जननीं पुण्डरीकोदरप्रभाम्॥ सुकुमारतरामेनां महार्हशयनोचिताम्। शयानां पश्यतायेह पृथिव्यामतथोचिताम्॥
en: The sister of that chastiser of foes, Vasudeva, the daughter of the king of Kunti (Bhoja), Kunti, endued with all auspicious marks. The daughter-in-law of Vichitravirya and the wife of the illustrious Pandu and the mother of us (the Pandavas), resplendent as the filament of lotus. Delicate and tender, fit to sleep on the costliest beds, is now asleep as she could never do not the bare ground!

sn: धर्मादिन्द्राच्च वाताच्च सुषुवे या सुतानिमान्। सेयं भूमौ परिश्रान्ता शेते प्रासादशायिनी॥
en: She, who has given birth to these sons by Dharma, Indra, Maruta; and who has ever slept in palaces, is now asleep on the ground from fatigue!

sn: किं नु दुःखतरं शक्यं मया द्रष्टुमतः परम्। योऽहमद्य नरव्याघ्रान् सुप्तान् पश्यामि भूतले॥
en: What more painful sight shall I ever see than what I see (now) the best of men (the Pandavas) sleeping on the (bare) ground!

sn: त्रिषु लोकेषु यो राज्यं धर्मनित्योऽर्हते नृपः। सोऽयं भूमौ परिश्रान्तः शेते प्राकृतवत् कथम्॥
en: The ever virtuous (Yudhisthira) who deserves to be the king of the three worlds, now sleeps on the ground, fatigued and tired like on ordinary being.

sn: अयं नीलाम्बुदश्यामो नरेष्वप्रतिमोऽर्जुनः। शेते प्राकृतवद् भूमौ दुःखतरं नु किम्॥
en: (Arjuna) of the colour of the blue ocean who is matchless among men sleeps on the ground like ordinary mortals. What could be more painful then this!

sn: अश्विनाविव देवानां याविमौ रूपसम्पदा। तौ प्राकृतवदद्यमौ प्रसुप्तौ धरणीतले॥
en: The twins, who are handsome as the Asvinis among the celestial, are asleep on the ground like ordinary men!

sn: ज्ञातयो यस्य नैव स्युर्विषमाः कुलपांसनाः। स जीवेत सुखं लोके ग्रामद्रुम इवैकजः॥
en: He who has no jealous and wicked minded relatives lives like a single tree in a village.

sn: एको वृक्षो हि यो ग्रामे भवेत् पर्णफलान्वितः। चैत्यो भवति निर्मातिरर्चनीयः सुपूजितः॥
en: Where there is only one tree full of leaves and fruits in a village, it became sacred and is worshipped and venerated by all.

sn: येषां च बहवः शूरा ज्ञातयो धर्ममाश्रिताः। ते जीवन्ति सुखं लोके भवन्ति च निरामयाः॥
en: They, who have many relatives, who are heroic and virtuous, live happily in this world without any sorrow of any kind.

sn: बलवन्तः समृद्धार्था मित्रबान्धवनन्दनाः। जीवन्त्यन्योन्याश्रित्य दुमाः काननजा इव॥
en: Being powerful, growing in prosperity and making their friends and relatives happy, they live depending on one another like the trees of the forest.

sn: वयं तु धृतराष्ट्रेण सपुत्रेण दुरात्मना। विवासिता न दग्धाश्च कथंचिद् दैवसंश्रयात्॥
en: We are banished by the wicked minded Dhritarashtra and his sons and we escaped for our good fortune from a fiery death.

sn: तस्मान्मुक्तः वयं दाहादिमं वृक्षमुपाश्रिताः। कां दिशं प्रतिपत्स्यामः प्राप्ताः क्लेशमनुत्तमम्॥
en: Having escaped from that fire, we are now resting under this tree. Having suffering great afflictions, where are we now to go?

sn: सकामो भव दुर्बुद्धे धार्तराष्ट्राल्पदर्शन। नूनं देवाः प्रसन्नास्ते नानुज्ञां मे युधिष्ठिरः॥ प्रयच्छति वधे तुभ्यं तेन जीवसि दुर्मते। नन्वद्य त्वां सहामात्यं सकर्णानुजसौबलम्॥ गत्वा क्रोधसमाविष्टः प्रेषयिष्ये यमक्षयम्। किं नु शक्यं मया कर्तुं यत् ते न क्रुध्यते नृपः॥ धर्मात्मा पाण्डवश्रेष्ठः पापाचारः युधिष्ठिरः। एवमुक्त्वा महाबाहुः क्रोधसंदीप्तमानसः॥ करं करेण निष्षिष्य निःश्वसन् दीनमानसः। पुनर्दीनमना भूत्वा शान्तार्चिरिव पावकः॥ भ्रातृन् महीतले सुप्तानवैक्षत वृकोदरः। विश्वस्तानिव संविष्टान् पृथग्जनसमानिव॥
en: O fore sightless sons of Dhritarashtra, O wicked men, enjoy your success. The gods are certainly favourable to you. Because Yudhisthira does not order me, (to kill you) therefore, O wretched men, live till then. Else angry as I am, I would have even this very day sent you (Duryodhana) with your sons and ministers and with Karna and the son of Subala (Sakuni) to the land of the dead. What can I do, so long the king (Yudhisthira) is not angry. O vicious men, the eldest of the Pandavas, Yudhisthira, is a virtuous minded man." Having said this, the mighty armed (Bhima), his mind inflamed with wrath. Squeezed his palms and sighed with a sorrowful mind. Like an extinguished fire blazed up, again in sorrowful mind. Vrikodara saw his brothers sleeping like ordinary men in trustfulness on the ground.

sn: नातिदूरेग नगरं वनादस्माद्धि लक्षये। जागर्तव्ये स्वपन्तीमे हन्त जागर्म्यहं स्वयम्॥ पास्यन्तीमे जलं पश्चात् प्रतिबुद्धा जितक्लमाः। इति भीमो व्यवस्यैव जजागार स्वयं तदा॥
en: Then Bhima thought, “I think there are some towns not far off from this forest. We ought to remain awake here. But they are all asleep therefore, I myself will sit awake. When they will rise after having been refreshed by sleep, then they will quince their thirst.” having resolved this, Bhima said awake.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तत्र तेषु शयानेषु हिडिम्बो नाम राक्षसः। अविदूरे वनात् तस्माच्छालवृक्षं समाश्रितः॥श।
en: Vaishampayana said : Nor far from the place where they (the Pandavas) slept there was a Rakshasas, named Hidimba, living on a Sala tree.

sn: क्रूरो मानुषमांसादो महावीर्यपराक्रमः। प्रावृड्जलधरश्यामः पिङ्गाक्षो दारुणाकृतिः॥ दंष्ट्राकरालवदनः पिशितेप्सुः क्षुधादितः। लम्बस्फिग्लम्बजद्दरो रक्तश्मश्रुशिरोरुहः॥ महावृक्षगलस्कन्धः शरूको बिभीषणः। यदृच्छया तानपश्यत् पाण्डुपुत्रान् महारथान्॥
en: (He was) greatly energetic and powerful, black as the clouds of the rainy season, hungry and eager for human flesh of cruel and terrible visage, of long shanks and large belly, locks and beard, red in colour of shoulder broad as the neck of the large tree of ears like arrow and of features frightful and hideous. When casting his glance at pleasure all around (the place), he saw the great car warriors, the sons of Pandu.

sn: विरूपरूपः पिङ्गाक्षः करालो घोरदर्शनः। पिशितेप्सुः क्षुधार्तश्च तानपश्यद् यदृच्छया॥
en: Ugly featured, red eyed, fearful and terrible looking, hungry and thirsty he looked around at pleasure and he saw them in that state.

sn: ऊर्ध्वाङ्गुलिः स कण्डूयन् धुन्वन् रूक्षान् शिरोरुहान् जृम्भमाणो महावक्त्रः पुनः पुनरवेक्ष्य च॥ हष्टो मानुषमांसस्य महाकायो महाबलः। आघ्राय मानुषं गन्धं भगिनीमिदमब्रवीत्॥ उपपन्नश्चिरस्याद्य भक्षोऽयं मम सुप्रियः। स्नेहस्रवान् प्रस्रवति जिह्वा पर्येति मे सुखम्॥
en: Yawning wistfully, shaking his dry and grizzly locks pointed upwards and scratching them with his finger the large mouthed cannibal repeatedly looked at the sleeping sons of Pandu. Of huge body and great strength of complexion like a mass of clouds, of teeth long and sharp pointed, of face emitting a sort of lustre, he was ever pleased with the human food. Smelling the scent of man, he spoke thus to his sister, “It is after a long time that my most favourite food has come to me. My tongue is moist with saliva in anticipating the relish of such food.

sn: अष्टौ दंष्ट्राः सुतीक्ष्णाग्राश्चिरस्यापातदुस्सहाः। देहेषु मज्जयिष्यामि स्निग्धेषु पिशितेषु च।॥
en: My eight teeth are sharp pointed and incapable of being resisted by anything. I shall dip them into the most delicious meat.

sn: आक्रम्य मानुषं कण्द्दमाच्छिद्य धमनीमपि। उष्णं नवं प्रपास्यामि फेनिलं रुधिरं बहु॥
en: Attacking the human throat and (human) arteries also. I shall drink a plentiful quantity of hot, fresh and frothy blood.

sn: गच्छ जानीहि के त्वेते शेरते वनमाश्रिताः। मानुषो बलवान् गन्धो घ्राणं तर्पयतीव मे॥
en: Go and ascertain who these (men) are, lying asleep in this forest. The strong scent of man pleases my nostrils.

sn: हत्वैतान् मानुषान् सर्वानानयस्व ममान्तिकम्। अस्मद्विषयसुप्तेभ्यो नैतेभ्यो भयमस्ति ते॥
en: Killing all these men, bring them to me. They are asleep in my dominion. There is no fear for you.

sn: एषामुत्कृत्य मांसानि मानुषाणां यथेष्टतः। भक्षयिष्याव सहितौ कुरु तूर्णं वचो मम॥
en: Tearing a plentiful flesh from these men. We shall then both eat (the meat). You immediately obey my command.

sn: भक्षयित्वा च मांसानि मानुषाणां प्रकामतः। नृत्याव सहितावायां दत्ततालावनेकशः॥
en: Eating to our will the flesh of these men, we shall dance together to various tones.”

sn: एवमुक्ता हिडिम्बा तु हिडिम्बेन तदा वने। भ्रातुर्वचनमाज्ञाय त्वरमाणेव राक्षसी॥ जगाम तत्र यत्र स्म पाण्डवा भरतर्षभ। ददर्श तत्र सा गत्वा पाण्डवान् पृथया सह। शयानान् भीमसेनं च जाग्रतं त्वपराजितम्॥
en: Having been thus addressed by Hidimba in the forest, Hidimba. The female Rakshasas, went at the command of her brother, O best of the Bharata race, to the place where the Pandavas were. Going there she saw the Pandavas with Pritha asleep and the invincible Bhimasena sitting awake.

sn: दृष्टैव भीमसेनं सा शालपोतमिवोद्गतम्। राक्षसी कामयामास रूपेणाप्रतिमं भुवि॥
en: Seeing Bhimasena who resembled a Sala tree and who was matchless in beauty, the Rakshasi was filled with desire.

sn: अयं श्यामो महाबाहुः सिंहस्कन्धो महाद्युतिः। कम्बुग्रीवः पुष्कराक्षो भर्ता युक्तो भवेन्मम॥
en: She thought, “His colour is like the heated gold; he is mighty armed, he is leonine shouldered, he is greatly effulgent, he is conch necked and he is lotus eyed, he is fit to be my husband.

sn: नाहं भ्रातृवचो जातु कुर्यां क्रूरोपसंहितम्। पतिस्नेहोऽतिबलवान् न तथा भ्रातृसौहृदम्॥ मुहूर्तमेव तृप्तिश्च भवेद् भ्रातुर्ममैव च। हतैरेतैरहत्वा तु मोदिष्ये शाश्वतीः समाः॥
en: I shall not away the cruel commands of my brother. A woman's love for her husband is greater then that of her brother. If I kill him, my brother's and my pleasure will be momentary, but if I do not kill him, I shall for ever enjoy with hi.”

sn: सा कामरूपिणी रूपं कृत्वा मानुषमुत्तमम्। उपतस्थे महाबाहुं भीमसेनं शनैः शनैः॥ लज्जमानेव ललना दिव्याभरणभूषिता। स्मितपूर्वमिदं वाक्यं भीमसेनमथाब्रवीत्॥ कुतस्त्वमसि सम्प्राप्तः कश्चासि पुरुषर्षभ। क इमे शेरते चेह पुरुषा देवरूपिणः॥
en: She was capable of assuming any from at will. She assumed an excellent human form and came slowly to the mighty armed Bhimasena. Being decked with celestial ornaments, she came to Bhimasena in bashfui demeanour and with smiles on her lips. She said, "O best of men, whence have you come her and who are you? Who are these celestial like men that are asleep here?

sn: केयं वै बृहती श्यामा सुकुमारी तवानघ। शेते वनमिदं प्राप्य विश्वस्ता स्वगृहे यथा॥
en: O sinless one, who is this delicate lady of transcendent beauty sleeping so trustfully here in this forest, as if she is in her own house?

sn: नेदं जानाति गहनं वनं राक्षससेवितम्। वसति ात्र पापात्मा हिडिम्बो नाम राक्षसः॥
en: Do you not know that this dense forest is the abode of Rakshasas. Here dwells the wicked-minded Rakshasas named Hidimba.

sn: तेनाहं प्रेषिता भ्रात्रा दुष्टभावेन रक्षसा। बिभक्षयिषता मांसं युष्माकममरोपम॥
en: O celestial like man, I have been sent here by my brother, that Rakshasas, with the cruel intention of eating your flesh.

sn: साहं त्वामभिसम्प्रेक्ष्य देवगर्भसमप्रभम्। नान्यं भर्तारमिच्छामि सत्यमेतद् ब्रवीमि ते॥
en: I tell you truly that seeing you as effulgent as a celestial, I do not desire anybody else to be my husband except you.

sn: एतद् विज्ञाय धर्मज्ञ युक्तं मयि समाचर। कामोपहतचित्ताङ्गी भजमानां भजस्व माम्॥
en: O learned man in all the precepts of virtue, do to me what is proper. My heart and body are both pierced by Kama (god of love). I am desirous of making you mine; make me yours.

sn: त्रास्यामि त्वां महाबाहो राक्षसात् पुरुषादकात्। वत्स्यावो गिरिदुर्गेषु भर्ता भव ममानघ।॥
en: O mighty armed hero, I shall rescue you from the Rakshasas who eats human flesh. O sinless one, become my husband. we shall live on the breasts of mountains.

sn: अन्तरिक्षचरी ह्यस्मि कामतो विचरामि च। अतुलामाप्नुहि प्रीतिं तत्र तत्र मया सह॥
en: I can travel in the sky and I do so at pleasure. You may enjoy with incomparable pleasure in those place."

sn: भीमसेन उवाच मातरं भ्रातरं ज्येष्ठं सुखसुप्तान् कथं त्विमान्। परित्यजेत को वद्य प्रभवन्निह राक्षसि॥
en: me Bhima said: O Rakshasi, like a self controlled Rishi, who can leave his mother, elder and younger brothers, sleeping happily (here)?

sn: को हि सुप्तानिमान् भ्रातॄन् दत्त्वा राक्षसभोजनम्। मातरं च नरो गच्छेत् कामात इव मद्विधः॥
en: What man like me would leave his sleeping mother and brother and as food for a Rakshasas in order gratify his lust?

sn: राक्षस्युवाच यत् ते प्रियं तत् करिष्ये सर्वानेतान् प्रबोधय। मोक्षयिष्याम्यहं कामं राक्षसात् पुरुषादकात्॥
en: The Rakshasi said : Awake them all. I shall do what is agreeable to you. I shall rescue you all from my cannibal brother.

sn: भीमसेन उवाच सुखसुप्तान् वने भ्रातृन् मातरं चैव राक्षसि। न भयाद् बोधयिष्यामि भ्रातुस्तव दुरात्मनः॥
en: Bhima said: O Rakshasi, for the fear of your wicked minded brother, I shall not awaken my mother and brothers, sleeping comfortably in the forest.

sn: न हि मे राक्षसा भीरु सोढुं शक्ताः पराक्रमम्। न मनुष्या न गन्धर्वा न यक्षाश्चारुलोचने॥
en: O timid girl, the Rakshasas are never able to withstand my prowess. O beautiful eyed one, no man, no Gandharva and no Yaksha (can also withstand it.)

sn: गच्छ वा तिष्ठ वा भद्रे यद् वापीच्छसि तत् कुरु तं वा प्रेषय तन्वङ्गि भ्रातरं पुरुषादकम्॥
en: O amiable girl, go or stay or do what you like, or O delicate shaped lady, send your cannibal brother (to me.)

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तां विदित्वा चिरगतां हिडिम्बो राक्षसेश्वरः। अवतीर्य दुमात् तस्मादाजगामाशु पाण्डवान्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Seeing her delay (in returning), the king of the Rakshasas, Hidimba, got down from the tree and came where the Pandavas were.

sn: लोहिताक्षो महाबाहुरूर्ध्वकेशो महाननः। मेघसंघातवर्मा च तीक्ष्णदंष्ट्रो भयानकः॥
en: (He was) of red eyed and strong arms, of standing hair and large mouth, of colour like clouds, of sharp teeth and fearful appearance.

sn: तमापतन्तं दृष्टैव तथा विकृतदर्शनम्। हिडिम्बोवाच वित्रस्ता भीमसेनमिदं वचः॥
en: Seeing this frightful creature alike from the tree, Hidimba became alarmed and thus spoke

sn: आपतत्येष दुष्टात्मा संक्रुद्धः पुरुषादकः। साहं त्वां भ्रातृभिः सार्धं यद् ब्रवीमि तथा कुरु॥
en: "The wicked minded cannibal is coming in anger. Do with your brothers what I ask you.

sn: अहं कामगमा वीर रक्षोबलसमन्विता। आरुहेमां मम श्रोणि नेष्यामि त्वां विहायसा॥
en: O hero, endued as I am with the prowess of Rakshasas, I am capable of going anywhere at will. Get upon my hips; I shall carry you through the sky.

sn: प्रबोधयैतान् संसुप्तान् मातरं च परंतप। सर्वानेव गमिष्यामि गृहीत्वा वो विहायसा॥
en: O chastiser of foes, awake your mother and others, sleeping in comfort. Taking them all, I shall go through the sky".

sn: भीम उवाच मा भैस्त्वं पृथुसुश्रोणि नैष कश्चिन्मयि स्थिते। अहमेनं हनिष्यामि प्रेक्षन्त्यास्ते सुमध्यमे॥
en: Bhima said: O lady of fair hips, fear nothing. I am certain that so long I am here, there is no Rakshasa who can harm any of these (men). O lady of slender waist, I shall kill this (cannibal) before your very sight.

sn: नायं प्रतिबलो भीरू राक्षसापसदो मम। सोढुं युधि परिस्पन्दमथवा सर्वराक्षसाः॥
en: O timid girl, this worst of Rakshasas is not a worthy antagonist of mine, nay all the Rakshasas can never with stand my great prowess in battle.

sn: पश्य बाहू सुवृत्तौ मे हस्तिहस्तनिभाविमौ। ऊरू परिघसंकाशौ संहतं चाप्युरो महत्॥
en: Behold my arms each like a trunk of an elephant. (Behold) my thighs like two iron clubs. (Behold) my chest, broad and adamantine.

sn: विक्रमं मे यथेन्द्रस्य साद्य द्रक्ष्यसि शोभने। मावमंस्थाः पृथुश्रोणि मत्वा मामिह मानुषम्॥
en: O beautiful girl, you shall see to day my Indra like prowess. O lady of fair hips, do not consider me weak, thinking that I am a human being.

sn: हिडिम्बोवाच नावमन्ये नरव्याघ्र त्वामहं देवरूपिणम्। दृष्टप्रभावस्तु मया मानुषेष्वेव राक्षसः॥
en: Hidimba said: O best of men, you are like a celestial. I do not consider you weak. but I have seen the prowess that Rakshasas exert on men.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तथा संजल्पतस्तस्य भीमसेनस्य भारत। वाचः शुश्राव ताः क्रुद्धो राक्षसः पुरुषादकः॥
en: Vaishampayana said: O descendant of Bharata, the angry cannibal the Rakshasas hear these words of Bhima thus talking there.

sn: अवेक्षमाणस्तस्याश्च हिडिम्बो मानुषं वपुः। स्रग्दामपूरितशिखं समग्रेन्दुनिभाननम्॥ सुभूनासाक्षिकेशान्तं सुकुमारनखत्वचम्। सर्वाभरणसंयुक्तं सुसूक्ष्माम्बरवाससम्॥
en: He saw Hidimba in human form, her head decked with garlands of flowers and her face like the full moon. Her eyebrows, nose, eyes and ringlets were all of the handsome description and her nail and complexion were of the most delicate colour. She was decked with all kinds of ornaments and attired in fine transparent robes.

sn: तां तथा मानुषं रूपं बिभ्रती सुमनोहरम्। पुंस्कामा शरूमानस्च चुक्रोध पुरुषादकः॥
en: Seeing her in that charming human form the cannibal thought that she was lustful and became (very) angry.

sn: संक्रुद्धो राक्षसस्तस्या भगिन्याः कुरुसत्तम्। उत्फाल्य विपुले नेत्रे ततस्तामिदमब्रवीत्॥ को हि मे भोक्तुकामस्य विजं चरित दुर्मतिः। न विभेषि हिडिम्बे किं मत्कोपाद् विप्रमोहिता।१७।।
en: O best of the Kurus, becoming angry with his sister, the Rakshasas expanded his large eyes and thus spoke to her, "What foolish creature throws obstacle on my way when I am hungry; O Hidimba, have you become so senseless as not to fear my anger?

sn: धिक् त्वामसति पुंस्कामे मम विप्रियकारिणि। पूर्वेषां राक्षसेन्द्राणां सर्वेषामयशस्करि॥
en: O unchaste women, fie on you! you do me an injury out of lust! You are ready to sacrifice the honours of all the chief Rakshasas, your ancestors!

sn: यानिमानाश्रिताकार्षीर्विप्रियं सुमहन्मम। एष तानद्य वै सर्वान् हनिष्यामि त्वया सह॥
en: I shall kill you with all those for whose sake you are trying to do me a great injury."

sn: एवमुक्त्वा हिडिम्बां स हिडिम्बो लोहितेक्षणः। वधायाभिपपातैनान् दन्तैर्दन्तानुपस्पृशन्॥
en: Having addressed Hidimba thus Hidimba with red eyes, his teeth pressing against teeth, ran at her with the intention of killing her.

sn: तमापतन्तं सम्प्रेक्ष्य भीमः प्रहरतां वरः। भर्त्सयामास तेजस्वी तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति चाब्रवीत्॥
en: The best of all wielders of weapons Bhima, seeing him rush at her, reproached him by saying "stop, stop."

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच भीमसेनस्तु तं दृष्ट्वा राक्षसं प्रहसन्निव। भगिनीं प्रति संक्रुद्धमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥ किं ते हिडिम्ब एतैर्वा सुखसुप्तैः प्रबोधितैः। मामासादय दुर्बुद्धे तरसा त्वं नराशन॥
en: Vaishampayana said: Seeing the Rakshasas angry with his sister, Bhimasena smiled (in scom) and spoke thus, O Hidimba why do you awaken these (men) sleeping in comfort? O wicked-minded (Rakshasa), come to me first without loss of time.

sn: मय्येव प्रहरेहि त्वं न स्त्रियं हन्तुमर्हसि। विशेषतोऽनपकृते परेणापकृते सति॥
en: Smite me first; you should not kill woman, specially when she has been sinned against instead of sinning.

sn: न हीयं स्ववशा बाला कामयत्यद्य मामिह। चोदितैषा ह्यनङ्गेन शरीरान्तरचारिणा॥
en: This girl is not in her own control in becoming lustful towards me. She has been moved by the god of love who pervades every living form.

sn: भगिनी तव दुर्वृत्त रक्षसां वै यशोहर। त्वन्नियोगेन चैवेयं रूपं मम समीक्ष्य च॥ कामय.यद्य मां भीरुस्तव नैषापराध्यति। अनङ्गेन कृते दोघे नेमां गर्हितुमर्हसि॥
en: o wicked creature, O you the most infamous of your class, your sister came here at your command. Seeing my person, she desire me. The timid girl has done you no harm. It is the fault of the god of love and therefore, you should not injure her.

sn: मयि तिष्ठति दुष्टात्मन् न स्त्रियं हन्तुमर्हसि। संगच्छस्व मया सार्धमेकेनैको नराशन॥
en: O wicked wretch, you should not kill a woman when I am here. O cannibal, come with me (to a distance) and fight singly with me.

sn: अहमेको नयिष्यामि त्वामद्य यमसादनम्। अद्य मद्वलनिष्पिष्टं शिरो राक्षस दीर्यताम्। कुञ्जरस्येव पादेन विनिष्पिष्टं बलीयसः॥
en: I shall singly (fight with you) and send you to day to the land of the dead. O Rakshasa, your head will be pounded to pieces, being pressed by my strength.

sn: अद्य गात्राणि ते कङ्काः श्येना गोमायवस्तथा। कर्षन्तु भुवि संहृष्टा निहतस्य मया मृधे॥
en: As if pressed by the trend of a mighty elephant. When you will be killed by me in battle your body will be to day torn by hawks, herons and jackals, in glee.

sn: क्षणेनाद्य करिष्येऽहमिदं वनमराक्षसम्। पुरा यद् दूषितं नित्यं त्वया भक्षयता नरान्॥
en: I shall in a moment make this forest free of all Rakshasas, so long polluted by you by eating men.

sn: अद्य त्वां भगिनी रक्षः कृष्यमाणं मयासकृत्। द्रक्ष्यत्यद्रिप्रतीकाशं सिंहेनेव महाद्विपम्॥
en: O Rakshasas, your sister will see today that I shall drag you, huge though your are like a mountain, as a lion drags an elephant.

sn: निराबाधास्त्वयि हते मया राक्षसांसन। वनमेतच्चरिष्यन्ति पुरुषा वनचारिणः॥
en: O worst of Rakshasas, when you will be killed by me men frequenting this forest will live safely and without fear.

sn: हिडिम्ब उवाच गर्जितेन वृथा किं ते कत्थितेन च मानुष। कृत्वैतत् कर्मणा सर्वं कत्येथा मा चिरं कृथाः॥
en: Hidimba said : O man, what is the need of your this vaunting and boasting? Accomplish all this first and then you my vaunt. Therefore, do not make any delay.

sn: बलिनं मन्यसे यच्चाप्यात्मानं सपराक्रमम्। ज्ञास्यस्यद्य समागम्य मयाऽऽत्मानं बलाधिकम्॥ न तावदेतान् हिंसिष्ये स्वपन्त्वेते यथासुखम्। एष त्वामेव दुर्बुद्धे निहन्म्यद्याप्रियंवदम्॥ पीत्वा तवासृग् गात्रेभ्यस्ततः पश्चादिमानपि। हनिष्यामि ततः पश्चादिमां विप्रियकारिणीम्॥
en: You know yourself to be strong and endued with prowess. In your encounter with me to-day, you shall now rightly know with what is your (real) strength. I shall not kill these (your brothers) till then. Let them sleep at their pleasure. o foolish man, I shall first kill you who speaks such evil words. After drinking your blood, I shall then kill these (your brothers) and then kill this (my sister) who has done me an injury.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्त्वा ततो बाहुं प्रगृह्य पुरुषादकः। अभ्यद्रवत संक्रुद्धो भीमसेनमरिंदमम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having said this, the cannibal, outstretching his arms, ran in great wrath towards that chastiser of foes, Bhimasena.

sn: तस्याभिद्रवतस्तूर्णं भीमो भीमपराक्रमः। वेगेन प्रहितं बाहुं निजग्राह हसन्निव॥
en: The greatly powerful Bhima soon sized the extended arms (of the rushing Rakshasas) with great force, as if in sport.

sn: निगृह्य तं बलाद् भीमो विस्फुरन्तं चकर्ष ह। तस्माद् देशाद् धनूंष्यष्टौ सिंहः क्षुद्रमृगं यथा॥
en: Then seizing the struggling Rakshasas with violence, Bhima dragged him away from that place full thirty two cubits, as a lion drags a small deer.

sn: ततः स राक्षसः क्रुद्धः पाण्डवेन बलार्दितः। भीमेसनं समालिङ्ग्य व्यनदद् भैरवं रवम्॥
en: Thereupon the Rakshasas, becoming an angry, clasped the Pandava Bhima with great force and he sent forth a terrible yell.

sn: पुनर्भीमो बलादेनं विचकर्ष महाबलः। मा शब्दः सुखसुप्तानां भ्रातृणां मे भवेदिति॥
en: The greatly strong Bhima then dragged him again (further away) with (great) force, so that his comfortably sleeping brothers might not awake by his yell.

sn: अन्योन्यं तौ समासाद्य विचकर्षतुरोजसा। हिडिम्बो भीमसेनश्च विक्रमं चक्रतुः परम्॥
en: Clasping and dragging each other with great force, both Bhimasena and Hidimba displayed their great prowess.

sn: बभञ्जतुस्तदा वृक्षाल्लताश्चाकर्षतुस्तदा। मत्ताविव च संरब्धौ वारणौ षष्टिहायनौ॥
en: Fighting like two large elephants mad with rage, they broke down the trees and tore off the creepers that grew around.

sn: तयोः शब्देन महता विबुद्धास्ते नरर्षभाः। सह प्रात्रा च ददृशुर्हिडिम्बामग्रतः स्थिताम्॥
en: By the great noise (of the fight) those best of men (the Pandavas) woke up with their mother and they saw Hidimba sitting before them.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच प्रबुद्धास्ते हिडिम्बाया रूपं दृष्ट्वातिमानुषम्। विस्मिताः पुरुषव्याघ्रा बभूवुः पृथया सह॥
