en: Vaishampayana said : Rising from sleep, those best of men (the Pandavas) with their mother were filled with astonishment on seeing the extraordinary beauty of Hidimba.

sn: ततः कुन्ती समीक्ष्यैनां विस्मिता रूपसम्पदा। उवाच मधुरं वाक्यं सान्त्वपूर्वमिदं शनैः॥ कस्य त्वं सुरगर्भाभे का वासि वरवर्णिनि। केन कार्येण सम्प्राप्ता कुतश्चागमनं तव॥
en: Thereupon being astonished with her beauty, Kunti slowly addressed in sweet orders and give her all assurance. "O celestial beautiful maid, O beautiful one, who and whose are you? For what business have you come here and from what place have you come?

sn: यदि वास्य वनस्य त्वं देवता यदि वाप्सराः। आचक्ष्व मम तत् सर्वं किमर्थं चेह तिष्ठसि॥
en: Are you the deity of this forest or (are you) an Apsara? Tell me all why you are sitting here."

sn: हिडिम्बोवाच यदेतत् पश्यसि वनं नीलमेघनिभं महत्। निवासो राक्षसस्यैष हिडिम्बस्य ममैव च॥
en: Hidimba said: The blue cloud like great forest that you see is the abode of mine and that of my brother, Rakshasas Hidimba.

sn: तस्य मां राक्षसेन्द्रस्य भगिनीं विद्धि भाविनी। भ्रात्रा सम्प्रेषितामार्ये त्वां सपुत्रां जिघांसता॥
en: O amiable lady, know me as being the sister of the Rakshasas chief. O respected madarn, I was sent by my brother to kill you with your sons.

sn: क्रूरबुद्धेरहं तस्य वचनादागता त्विह। अद्राक्षं नवहेमाभं तव पुत्रं महाबलम्॥
en: Coming here at the command of that cruelminded (Rakshasas), I saw your greatly powerful son of the colour of pure gold.

sn: ततोऽहं सर्वभूतानां भावे विचरता शुभे। चोदिता तव पुत्रस्य मन्मथेन वशानुगा॥
en: O blessed lady, I was brought under the control of your son by the god of love who pervades the nature of everything.

sn: ततो वृतो मया भर्ता तव पुत्रो महाबलः। अपनेतुं च यतितो न चैव शकितो मया॥
en: I then chose your greatly powerful son as my husband. Through I tried to suppress this passion, I could not.

sn: चिरायमाणां मां ज्ञात्वा ततः स पुरुषादकः। स्वयमेवागतो हन्तुमिमान् सर्वांस्तवात्मजान्॥
en: Finding my delay, the cannibal, came in person here to kill all these your sons.

sn: स तेन मम कान्तेन तव पुत्रेण धीमता। बलादितो विनिष्पिष्य व्यपनीतो महात्मना॥
en: But he has been dragged away by your illustrious and intelligent son and my (chosen) husband.

sn: विकर्षन्तौ महावेगौ गर्जमानौ परस्परम्। पश्यैवं युधि विक्रान्तावेतौ च नरराक्षसौ॥
en: Behold the man and the Rakshasas, both endued with great strength and prowess, (now) engaged in combat, pressing each other with great force and filling the whole region with their roars.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तस्याः श्रुत्वैव वचनमुत्पपात युधिष्ठिरः। अर्जुनो नकुलश्चैव सहदेवश्च वीर्यवान्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Hearing her these words, Yudhisthira, Arjuna, Nakula and the powerful Sahadeva hastily rose up.

sn: तौ ते ददृशुरासक्तौ विकर्षन्तौ परस्परम्। काडक्षमाणौ जयं चैव सिंहाविव बलोत्कटौ॥
en: They saw those two (Bhima and Hidimba) already engaged in fight; they were dragging each other, (both) eager to overcome each other like two greatly strong lions.

sn: अथान्योन्यं समाश्लिष्य विकर्षन्तौ पुनः पुनः। दावाग्निधूमसदृशं चक्रतुः पार्थिवं रजः॥
en: They clasped and pressed each other again and again. The dust of the earth rose like the smoke of the forest fire.

sn: वसुधारेणुसंवीतौ वसुधाधरसंनिभौ। बभ्राजतुर्यथा शैलौ नीहारेणाभिसंवृतौ॥
en: Covered with the dust of the earth, they, who were like mountains looked like two cliffs enveloped in mists.

sn: राक्षसेन तदा भीमं क्लिश्यमानं निरीक्ष्य च। उवाचेदं वचः पार्थः प्रहसञ्छनकैरिव॥
en: Seeing Bhima oppressed by the Rakshasas, Partha, Arjuna, slowly said with smiles on his lips-

sn: भीम मा भैर्महाबाहो न त्वां बुध्यामहे वयम्। समेतं भीमरूपेण रक्षसा श्रमकर्शितम्॥
en: "O Bhima, O mighty armed (hero) fear nothing. we did not know that in the fight with the terrible Rakshasas you are tired.

sn: साहाय्येऽस्मि स्थितः पार्थ पातयिष्यामि राक्षसम्। नकुलः सहदेवश्च मातरं गोपयिष्यतः॥
en: O son of Pritha, I stand here to help you. I shall kill the Rakshasas. Nakula and Sahadeva will protect our mother.

sn: भीम उवाच उदासीनो निरीक्षस्व न कार्यः समभ्रमस्त्वया। न जात्वयं पुनर्जीवेन्मबाह्वन्तरमागतः॥
en: Bhima said: Look on this combat with unconcern. You need not take part in it. When he has come to my clutches, he will not escape with life.

sn: अर्जुन उवाच किमनेन चिरं भीम जीवता पापरक्षसा। गन्तव्ये न चिरं स्थातुमिह शक्यमरिंदम॥
en: Arjuna said : O Bhima, what need is there to keep this wicked Rakshasas alive any longer? O chastiser of foes, we are to go from this place as soon as possible; and therefore we can stay here no longer.

sn: पुरा संरज्यते प्राची पुरा संध्या प्रवर्तते। रौद्रे मुहूर्ते रक्षांसि प्रबलानि भवन्त्युत॥
en: The east is reddening; the morning twilight is about to set in. At Raudra Muhurata (just at the break of day), the Rakshasas become most powerful.

sn: त्वरस्व भीम मा क्रीड जहि रक्षो विभीषणम्। पुरा विकुरुते मायां भुजयोः सारमर्पय॥
en: O Bhima, be quick. Do not play (with him); kill the fierce Rakshasas. He can display Maya delusions, hereafter. Therefore, show the strength of you arms.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच अर्जुनेनैवमुक्तस्तु भीमो रोषाज्ज्वलन्निव। बलमाहारयामास यद् वायोर्जगतः क्षये॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having been thus addressed by Arjuna, Bhima blazed up in anger. He summoned the strength that Bahu puts forth at the time of the universal dissolution.

sn: ततस्तस्याम्बुदाभस्य भीमो रोषात् तु रक्षसः। उत्क्षिप्याभ्रामयद् देहं तूर्णं शतगुणं तदा॥
en: He quickly raised up the cloud like Rakshasas in anger and he then whirled him one hundred times.

sn: भीम उवाच वृथामांसैर्वृथापुष्टो वृथावृद्धो वृथमतिः। वृथामरणमर्हस्त्वं वृथाद्य न भविष्यसि॥
en: Bhima said: (O Rakshasas), your body has in vain grown and thriven on unsanctified meat. Your intelligence is in vain, your sense is in vain. You deserve, therefore, an unholy death. I shall reduce you today to nothing.

sn: क्षेममद्य करिष्यामि यथा वनमकण्टकम्। न पुनर्मानुषान् हत्वा भक्षयिष्यसि राक्षस॥
en: I shall make this forest blessed today, O Rakshasas, completely shorn of prickly plant (which you were in it); so that you shall no longer kill men in order to eat them.

sn: अर्जुन उवाच यदि वा मन्यसे भारं त्वमिमं राक्षसं युधि। करोमि तव साहाय्यं शीघ्रमेष निपात्यताम्॥
en: Arjuna said : If you think it a heavy task to kill the Rakshasas in battle, let me assist you. Kill him without (any further) loss of time.

sn: अथवाप्यहमेवैनं हनिष्यामि वृकोदर। कृतकर्मा परिश्रान्तः साधु तावदुपारम॥
en: O Vrikodara, let me kill him alone. You are tired and you have almost finished the work and you well deserve rest (now).

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा भीमसेनोऽत्यमर्षणः। निष्पिष्यैनं बलाद् भूमौ पशुमारममारयत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : having heard these words (of Arjuna) Bhimasena was inflamed with rage; and dashing him on the ground with all his might, he killed him like beast.

sn: स मार्यमाणो भीमेन ननाद विपुलं स्वनम्। पूरयंस्तद् वनं सर्वं जलाई इव दुन्दुभिः॥
en: When he was thus killed by Bhima, he sent forth a terrible roar like the sound of a wet drum which filled the whole forest.

sn: बाहुभ्यां योक्त्रयित्वा तं बलवान् पाण्डुनन्दनः। मध्ये भक्त्वाा महाबाहुर्हर्षयामास पाण्डवान्॥
en: Then the strong son of Pandu (Bhima), holding the body with his hands, broke it in the middle and the mighty armed hero greatly pleased the Pandavas (by his this great deed).

sn: हिडिम्बं निहतं दृष्ट्वा संहृष्टास्ते तरस्विनः। अपूजयन् नरव्याघ्रं भीमसेनमरिंदमम्॥
en: Seeing Hidimba slain, they were filled with joy and lost on time to congratulate that best of men, that chastiser of foes, Bhimasena.

sn: अभिपूज्य महात्मानं भीमं भीमपराक्रमम्। पुनरेवार्जुनो वाक्यमुवाचेदं वृकोदरम्॥ न दूरं नगरं मन्ये वनादस्मादहं विभो। शीघ्रं गच्छाम भद्रं ते न नो विद्यात् सुयोधनः॥
en: Thus congratulating the illustrious and greatly powerful Bhima, Arjuna thus again addressed Vrikodara, "O lord, I believe there is a town not far off from this forest. O blessed one, let us soon go from this place, so that Duryodhana may not trace us."

sn: ततः सर्वे तथेत्युक्त्वा सह मात्रा महारथाः। प्रययुः पुरुषव्याघ्रा हिडिम्बा चैव राक्षसी॥
en: Those best of men (the Pandavas), those great car warriors, saying “Be it so," proceeded with their mother. And Rakshasi Hidimba also (followed them.)

sn: भीमसेन उवाच स्मरन्ति वैरं रक्षांसि मायामाश्रित्य मोहिनीम्। हिडिम्बे व्रज पन्थानं त्वमिमं भ्रातृसेवितम्॥
en: Bhima said: woman even The Rakshasas revenge themselves on their enemy by alluring deceptions. Therefore, O Hidimba, go to the way that your brother has gone.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच क्रुद्धोऽपि पुरुषव्याघ्र भीम मा स्म स्त्रियं वधीः। शरीरगुप्त्यभ्यधिकं धर्मं गोपाय पाण्डव॥
en: Yudhisthira said: O best of men, O Bhima do not kill a in anger. O Pandava, the attainment of virtue is a higher duty than the protection of body.

sn: वधाभिप्रायमायान्तमधीस्त्वं महाबलम्। रक्षसस्तस्य भगिनी किं न: क्रुद्धा करिष्यति॥
en: You have killed the greatly powerful (Rakshasas) who came with the purpose of killing us. She is (but) his sister, what can she do to us, even if she is angry?

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच हिडिम्बा तु ततः कुन्तीमभिवाद्य कृताञ्जलिः। युधिष्ठिरं तु कौन्तेयमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥ आर्ये जानासि यद् दुःखमिह स्त्रीणामनङ्गजम्। तदिदं मामनुप्राप्तं भीमसेनकृतं शुभे॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Thereupon, Hidimba respectfully saluting Kunti and Yudhisthira with joined hands, spoke to Kunti thus, “O respected lady, you know the pangs that women suffer from the god of love. O blessed lady, I have received those (pangs) by Bhima.

sn: सोढं तत् परमं दुःखं मया कालप्रतीक्षया। सोऽयमभ्यागतः कालो भविता मे सुखोदयः॥
en: I have suffered these great pangs and I wait for the time (when it will be assuaged). That time has now come, when I expect that my happiness would come.

sn: मा ह्युयत्सृज्य सुहृदः स्वधर्म स्वजनं तथा। वृतोऽयं पुरुषव्याघ्रस्तव पुत्रः पतिः शुभे॥
en: O blessed lady, leaving my friends relatives and religion, I have chosen this best of men, this son of yours, as my husband.

sn: वीरेणाहं तथानेन त्वया चापि यशस्विनि। प्रत्याख्याता न जीवामि सत्यमेतद् ब्रवीमि ते॥
en: O illustrious lady, if forsaken by this hero and yourself I shall not live any longer, I tell you this truly.

sn: तदर्हसि कृपां कर्तुं मयि त्वं वरवर्णिनि। मत्वा मूढेति तन्मा त्वं भक्ता वानुगतेति वा॥
en: O greatly beautiful lady, you should show compassion towards me, considering me foolish or very obedient to you.

sn: भानेन महाभागे संयोजय सुतेन ह। तमुपादाय गच्छेयं यथेष्टं देवरूपिणम्। पुनश्चैवानयिष्यामि विस्रम्भं कुरु मे शुभे॥
en: O greatly fortunate lady, unite me with my husband, your son. Let me go away at pleasure (wherever I like), taking this celestial like (hero). Trust me, O blessed lady, I shall bring him back to you all.

sn: अहं हि मनसा ध्याता सर्वान् नेष्यामि वः सदा। वृजिनात् तारयिष्यामि दुर्गेषु विषमेषु च॥ पृष्ठेन वो वहिष्यामि शीघ्रं गतिमभीप्सतः। यूयं प्रसादं कुरुत भीमसेनो भजेत माम्॥
en: Whenever you will think of me I will immediately come to you and carry you wherever you will command. I shall rescue you from danger over even and uneven grounds. I shall carry you on my back whenever you will desire to proceed with speed. Be gracious to me and make Bhimasena accept me.

sn: आपदस्तरणे प्राणान् धारयेद् येन तेन वा। सर्वमावृत्य कर्तव्यं तं धर्ममनुवर्तता॥
en: It is consonant with the precepts of religion that one should protect his life by any means. He, who seeks to do it, should not scruple about the means.

sn: आपत्सु यो धारयति धर्म धर्मविदुत्तमः। व्यसनं ह्येव धर्मस्य धर्मिणामापदुच्यते॥
en: He who keeps his virtue (even) in distress in the foremost of all virtuous men. Distress is the greatest danger to virtue and virtuous men.

sn: पुण्यं प्राणान् धारयति पुण्यं प्राणदमुच्यते। येन येनाचरेद् धर्मं तस्मिन् गर्दा न विद्यते॥
en: 'It is virtue that protect life and therefore virtue is called the giver of life. The means by which virtue is secured be censurable.'

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच एवमेतद् यथाऽऽत्थ त्वं हिडिम्बे नात्र संशयः। स्थातव्यं तु त्वया सत्ये यथा ब्रूयां सुमध्यमे॥
en: Yudhisthira said: Hidimba, there is no doubt of that what you say is true. O lady of slender waist, you must act as you have said (you want to do).

sn: स्नातं कृताछिकं भद्रे कृतकौतुकमङ्गलम्। भीमसेनं भजेथास्त्वं प्रागस्तगमनाद् रवेः॥
en: O blessed lady, when Bhimasena will finished ablutions, twilight prayer and the usual propitiatory rites you will then be adored by him till the sun sets.

sn: अहस्सु विहरानेन यथाकामं मनोजवा। अयं त्वानयितव्यस्ते भीमसेनः सदा निशि॥
en: O lady of mind like speed, sport with him at pleasure during the day. You must always bring Bhimasena back every night. can never

sn: ॥ वैशम्पायन उवाच तथेति तत् प्रतिज्ञाय भीमसेनोऽब्रवीदिदम्। शृणु राक्षसि सत्येन समयं ते वदाम्यहम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having promised to do it by saying, “Be it so", Bhima said (to Hidimba), “O Rakshasi, listen to the agreement that I make with you.

sn: यावत् कालेन भवति पुत्रस्योत्पादन शुभे। तावत् कालं गमिष्यामि त्वया सह सुमध्यमे॥
en: O blessed lady, O lady of slender waist, I shall go (and stay) with you, so long you do not obtain a son."

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तथेति तत् प्रतिज्ञाय हिडिम्बा राक्षसी तदा। भीमसेनमुपादाय सोर्ध्वमाचक्रमे ततः॥
en: Having promised this by saying, “Be it so," the Rakshasi Hidimba took Bhima upon her body and went up to the sky.

sn: शैलशृङ्गेषु रम्येषु देवतायतनेषु च। मृगपक्षिविघुष्टेषु रमणीयेषु सर्वदा॥ कृत्वा च परमं रूपं सर्वाभरणभूषिता। संजल्पन्ती सुमधुरं रमयामास पाण्डवम्॥ तथैव वनदुर्गेषु पुष्पितदुमवल्लिषु। सरस्सु रमणीयेषु पद्मोत्पलयुतेषु च॥ नदीद्वीपप्रदेशेषु वैदूर्यसिकतासु च। सुतीर्थवनतोयासु तथा गिरिनदीषु च॥ काननेषु विचित्रेषु पुष्पितद्रुमवल्लिषु। हिमवद्गिरिकुञ्जेषु गुहासु विविधासु च॥ प्रफुल्लशतपत्रेषु सरस्खमलवारिषु। सागरस्य प्रदेशेषु मणिहेमचितेषु च॥ पल्वलेषु च रम्येषु महाशालवनेषु च। देवारण्येषु पुण्येषु तथा पर्वतसानुषु॥ गुह्यकानां निवासेषु तापसायतनेषु च। सर्वर्तुफलरम्येषु मानसेषु सरस्सु च॥ बिभ्रती परमं रूपं रमयामास पाण्डवम्। रमयन्ती तथा भीमं तत्र तत्र मनोजवा॥
en: Assuming the handsomest form, decked with all ornaments and pouring forth at times sweet music, she sported with the Pandava (Bhima) on the mountain peaks of picturesque scenery and in regions sacred to the celestial, abounding with beasts and birds. Also in forests and mountain fastness, overgrown with blossoming trees, in beautiful lake; resplendent with lotuses and lilies. On island of rivers, on the pebbled banks of streamlets, in sylvan streamlets with beautiful banks and also in mountain streams. In beautiful woods with blossoming trees, in the Himalayan bowers and in various mountains caves. In the crystal water of the lakes, smiling with lotuses, on the shores of the sea shinning with gold and pearls. In beautiful towns and fine gardens, in woods sacred to the gods and on the breast of hills. In the land of the Guhyakas and the hermitages of the ascetics on the banks of the Manasa lake, abounding with fruits and flowers of every season. Assuming the handsome form, she sported with the Pandava (Bhima). The lady with the mind like speed sported with Bhima in these places.

sn: प्रजज्ञे राक्षसी पुत्रं भीमसंनान्महाबलम्। विरूपाक्षं महावक्त्रं शरूकर्णं विभीषणम्॥
en: She then gave birth by Bhima a greatly strong son of terrible eyes and large mouth, of ears like arrows and of appearance fearful.

sn: भीमनादं सुताम्राष्ठं तीक्ष्णदंष्ट्रं महाबलम्। महेष्वासं महावीर्यं महासत्त्वं महाभुजम्॥ महाजवं महाकायं महामायमरिंदमम्। दीर्घघोणं महोरस्कं विकटोबद्धपिण्डिकम्॥ अमानुषं मानुषजं भीमवेगं महाबलम्। यः पिशाचनतीत्यान्यान् बभूवातीव राक्षसान्॥
en: Of roaring voice, of lips brown as copper, of teeth sharp and keen. He was mighty armed, greatly energetic, exceedingly powerful and a great car warrior. Having long nose, broad chest, frightfully swelling calves, celerity of motion and excessive strength, he had nothing human in him, though born of a man. He excelled all the Pishachas and other such creatures and also the Rakshasas.

sn: बालोऽपि यौवनं प्राप्तो मानुषेषु विशाम्पते। सर्वास्त्रेषु परं वीरः प्रकर्षमगमद् बली॥
en: He grew up to be a youth when he was a boy and that mighty hero soon acquainted high proficiency in all arms and weapons known amongst mankind.

sn: सद्यो हि गर्भान् राक्षस्यो लभन्ते प्रसवन्ति च। कामरूपधराश्चैव भवन्ति बहुरूपिकाः॥
en: The Rakshasas women give birth on the very day they conceive; they are capable of assuming any form at will and they change their forms (at will).

sn: प्रणम्य विकचः पादावगृहणात् स पितुस्तदा। मातुश्च परमेष्वासस्तौ च नामास्य चक्रतुः॥
en: That bad featured child, that mighty bowman, soon after his birth, bowed down to his mother and also to his father and touched their feet. They then named him.

sn: घटो हास्योत्कच इति माता तं प्रत्यभाषत। अब्रवीत् तेन नामास्य घटोत्कच इति स्म ह॥
en: His mother said, "This child's head is like a Ghata (water pot)." They then gave him the name of Ghatotkacha.

sn: अनुरक्तश्च तानासीत् पाण्डवान् स घटोत्कच। तेषां च दयितो नित्यमात्मनित्यो बभूव ह॥
en: Ghatotkacha was (very much) attached to the Pandavas. he became a great favourite with them, almost one of them.

sn: संवाससमयो जीर्ण इत्याभाष्य ततस्तु तान्। हिडिम्बा समयं कृत्वा स्वां गतिं प्रत्यपद्यत॥
en: Knowing that the period of her stay with the (Pandava) had come to an end, Hidimba making another agreement with them went away wherever she like.

sn: घटोत्कचो महाकायः पाण्डवान् पृथया सह। अभिवाद्य यथान्यायमब्रवीच्च प्रभाष्य तान्॥ किं करोम्यहमार्याणां निःशङ्कं वदतानघाः। तं ब्रुवन्तं भैमसेनि कुन्ती वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Thereafter giant Ghatotkacha bowed down to the Pandavas with Kunti, and told them, O sinless great men, you may tell me what I have to do. Thus addressed by him, Kunti spoke to the scn of Bhima.

sn: त्वं कुरूणां कुले जातः साक्षाद् भीमसमो ह्यसि। ज्येष्ठः पुत्रोऽसि पञ्चानां साहाय्यं कुरु पुत्रक॥
en: You are born in the race of Kuru and are the same as Bhima. You are the eldest son of five. O son! help us.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच पृथयाप्येवमुक्तस्तु प्रणम्यैव वचोऽब्रवीत्। यथा हि रावणो लोके इन्द्रजिच्च महाबलः। वर्मवीर्यसमो लोके विशिष्टश्चाभवं नृषु॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Thus addressed by Kunti, he replied respectfully-Just as there are in this world Ravana and Meghanada who were very strong, so also I am gigantic and valorous among the men of this world; in fact I am greater than any.

sn: कृत्यकाल उपस्थास्ये पितृनिति घटोत्कचः। आमन्त्र्य रक्षसां श्रेष्ठः प्रतस्थे चोत्तरां दिशम्॥
en: That best Rakshasas, Ghatotkacha, promising to come when required for business, went away towards the north.

sn: स हि सृष्टो मघवता शक्तिहेतोर्महात्मना। कर्णस्याप्रतिवीर्यस्य प्रतियोद्धा महारथः॥
en: That great car warrior (Ghatotkacha) was created by the illustrious Indra as a proper antagonist of Karna of matchless power in consequence of the weapon (he gave him).

description: Pandavas entered in Ekachakra city and meeting with Vyasa
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ते वनेन वनं गत्वा जन्तो मृगगणान् बहून्। अपक्रम्य ययू राजंस्त्वरमाणा महारथाः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : O king, hose mighty car-warriors the heroes (the Pandavas), went from forest of forest, killing many beasts. In course of their travel and they crossed many forests (came to).

description: Pandavas entered in Ekachakra city and meeting with Vyasa
sn: मत्स्यांस्त्रिगर्तान् पञ्चालान् कीचकानन्तरेण च। रमणीयान् वनोद्देशान् प्रेक्षमाणाः सरांसि च॥
en: The countries of the Matsyas, Trigartas and Panchalas, then to that of the Kichakas, where they saw mane beautiful woods and lakes.

description: Pandavas entered in Ekachakra city and meeting with Vyasa
sn: जटाः कृत्वाऽऽत्मनः सर्वे वल्कलाजिनवाससः। सह कुन्त्या महात्मानो बिभ्रतस्तापसं वपुः॥ क्वचिद् वहन्तो जननीं त्वरमाणा महारथाः। क्वचिच्छन्देन गच्छन्तस्ते जग्मुः प्रसभं पुनः॥
en: They all made matted locks and wore the barks of trees. Those illustrious (heroes) assumed the form of ascetics with their mother. Those car-warriors some times proceeded in haste, carrying their mother, (on their back) sometimes they proceeded slowly; they then went in great haste.

description: Pandavas entered in Ekachakra city and meeting with Vyasa
sn: ब्राह्यं वेदमधीयाना वेदाङ्गानि च सर्वशः। नीतिशास्त्रं च सर्वज्ञा ददृशुस्ते पितामहम्॥
en: They studied the Brahma (Rik) and the Vedangas and all other sciences of morals. (When they were thus engaged), they saw their grandfather (Vyasa).

description: Pandavas entered in Ekachakra city and meeting with Vyasa
sn: तेऽभिवाद्य महात्मानं कृष्णद्वैपायनं तदा। तस्थुः प्राञ्जल्यः सर्वे सह मात्रा परंतपाः॥
en: Having respectfully saluted the illustrious Krishna Dvaipayana those chastisers of foes with their mother stood before him with joined hands.

description: Pandavas entered in Ekachakra city and meeting with Vyasa
sn: व्यास उवाच मयेदं व्यसनं पूर्वं विदितं भरतर्षभाः। यथा तु तैरधर्मेण धात्रारष्टैर्विवासिताः॥ तद् विदित्वास्मि सम्प्राप्तश्चिकीर्षुः परमं हितम्। न विषादोऽन्न कर्तव्यः सर्वमेतत् सुखाय वः॥
en: Vyasa said : O best of the Bharata race, I knew beforehand of your this affection, your this unjust banishment by the sons of Dhritarashtra. Knowing this I have come to do you some great good. You ought not to grieve. Know all this is for your (future) happiness.

description: Pandavas entered in Ekachakra city and meeting with Vyasa
sn: समास्ते चैव मे सर्वे यूयं न संशयः। दीनतो बालतश्चैव स्नेहं कुर्वन्ति मानवाः। तस्मादभ्यधिकः स्नेहो युष्मासु मम साम्प्रतम्॥ स्नेहपूर्वं चिकीर्षामि हितं वस्तन्निबोधत। इदं नगरमभ्याशे रमणीयं निरामयम्। वसतह प्रतिच्छन्ना ममागमनकाक्षिणः॥
en: There is no doubt that you and they all are equal in my eyes; but men love more those that are in misfortune or in tender years. Therefore my love for you is now greater (then before) and in consequence of the love, I wish to do you some good. Listen to me. Not far from this place there is a beautiful town which is a safe place for you. There live you all in disguise, waiting for my return.

description: Pandavas entered in Ekachakra city and meeting with Vyasa
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवं स तान् समाश्वस्य व्यासः सत्यवतीसुतः। एकचक्रामभिगतः कुन्तीमाश्वासयत् प्रभुः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having thus comforted them, the son of a Satyavati, Vyasa, led them to (the town of) Ekachakra. The lord (Vyasa) comforted Kunti also.

description: Pandavas entered in Ekachakra city and meeting with Vyasa
sn: व्यास उवाच जीवत्पुत्रि सुतस्तेऽयं धर्मनित्यो युधिष्ठिरः। धर्मेण पृथिवीं जित्वा महात्मा पुरुषर्षभः। पृथिव्यां पार्थिवान् सर्वान् प्रशासिष्यति धर्मराट्॥
en: Vyasa said: O daughter, live your this son, the illustrious and the best of men, Yudhisthira, ever devoted to virtue, conquering the word by his virtue will virtuously rule over all the kings of the world.

description: Pandavas entered in Ekachakra city and meeting with Vyasa
sn: पृथिवीमखिलां जित्वा सर्वां सागरमेखलाम्। भीमसेनार्जुनबलाद् भोक्ष्यते नात्र संशयः॥
en: Conquering the whole earth bounded by the belt of the sea by the prowess of Bhima and Arjuna, there is no doubt (he will rule the world).

description: Pandavas entered in Ekachakra city and meeting with Vyasa
sn: पुत्रास्तव च माद्याश्च सर्व एव महारथाः। स्वराष्ट्रे विहरिष्यन्ति सुखं सुमनसः सदा॥
en: Your sons and those of Madri, all great car warriors, will sport in their own kingdom at pleasure.

description: Pandavas entered in Ekachakra city and meeting with Vyasa
sn: यक्ष्यन्ति च नरव्याघ्रा निर्जित्य पृथिवीमिमाम्। राजसूयाश्वमेधाद्यैः क्रतुभिर्भूरिदक्षिणैः॥
en: Conquering the whole world, these best of men will perform Rajasuya and Ashvamedha and other sacrifices in which Dakshina (presents to the Brahmanas) will be very large.

description: Pandavas entered in Ekachakra city and meeting with Vyasa
sn: अनुगृह्य सुहृद्वर्ग भोगैश्वर्यसुखेन च। पितृपैतामहं राज्यमिमे भोक्ष्यन्ति ते सुताः॥
en: Maintaining their friends and relatives in luxury and affluence, these your so will rule over the kingdom of their forefathers.

description: Pandavas entered in Ekachakra city and meeting with Vyasa
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्त्वा निवेश्यैनान् ब्राह्मणस्य निवेशने। अब्रवीत् पाण्डवश्रेष्ठमृषिद्वैपायनस्तदा॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having said this, he took them to the house of a Brahmana and then Rishi Dvaipayana spoke thus to the eldest Pandava-

description: Pandavas entered in Ekachakra city and meeting with Vyasa
sn: इह मासं प्रतीक्षध्वमागमिष्याम्यहं पुनः। देशकालौ विदित्वैव लप्स्यध्वं परमां मुदम्॥
en: “Wait here for me. I shall come back to you. You will be able to obtain great happiness by adopting yourself to the place and time (in which you are now).”

description: Pandavas entered in Ekachakra city and meeting with Vyasa
sn: स तैः प्राञ्जलिभिः सर्वैस्तथेत्युक्तो नराधिप। जगाम भगवान् व्यासो यथागतमृषिः प्रभुः॥
en: O king, they all said with joined hands, "Be it so." (Thereupon) the illustrious lord, the Rishi Vyasa, went away from whence he came.

sn: जनमेजय उवाच एकचक्रां गतास्ते तु कुन्तीपुत्रा महारथाः। अत ऊर्ध्वं द्विजश्रेष्ठ किमकुर्वत पाण्डवाः॥
en: Janamejaya said : O best of twice-born, what did the Pandavas, those great car-warriors, the sons of Kunti, do when they went to Ekachakra?

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एकचक्रां गतास्ते तु कुन्तीपुत्रा महारथाः। ऊषुर्नातिचिरं कालं ब्राह्मणस्य निवेशने॥
en: Vaishampayana said : These great car-warriors, the sons of Pandu, going to Ekachakra, lived for a short time in a Brahmana's house.

sn: रमणीयानि पश्यन्तो वनानि विविधानि च। पार्थिवानपि चोद्देशान् सरितश्च सरांसि च॥ चेसर्भेक्षं तदा ते तु सर्व एव विशाम्पते। बभूवुर्नागराणां च स्वैर्गुणैः प्रियदर्शनाः॥
en: O king, they saw many beautiful woods and countries, rivers and lakes, as they roamed about bagging their bread. O account of their many accomplishments they became (great) favourites of all men.

sn: निवेदयन्ति स्म तदा कुन्त्या भैक्षं सदा निशि। तया विभक्तान् भागांस्ते भुञ्जते स्म पृथक् पृथक्॥
en: They offered to Kunti every night all the food (that they got during the day) and it (the food) was divided (by Kunti) and they each ate separately the share of each.

sn: अर्धं ते भुञ्जते वीराः सह मात्रा परंतपाः। अर्धं सर्वस्य भैक्षस्य भीमो भुङ्क्ते महाबलः॥
en: Those heroes, those chastisers of foes, with their mother, ate half of the food collected, the greatly strong Bhima alone ate the other half.

sn: तथा तु तेषां वसतां तस्मिन् राष्ट्रे महात्मनाम्। अतिचक्राम सुमहान् कालोऽथ भरतर्षभ॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, the illustrious men thus passed some days in that country.

sn: ततः कदाचिद् भैक्षाय गतास्ते पुरुषर्षभाः। संगत्या भीमसेनस्तु तत्रास्ते पृथया सह॥
en: One day, when those best of men went out food, Bhima (alone) was (at home) with Pritha This mother.

sn: अथार्तिजं महाशब्दं ब्राह्मणस्य निवेशने। भृशमुत्पतितं घोरं कुन्ती शुश्राव भारत॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, Kunti heard loud and heart-rending lamentations in the house of the Brahmana.

sn: रोरूयमाणांस्तान् दृष्ट्वा परिदेवयतश्च सा। कारुण्यात् साधुभावाच्च कुन्ती राजन् न चक्षमे॥ मथ्यमानेन दुःखेन हृदयेन पृथा तदा। उवाच भीमं कल्याणी कृपान्वितमिदं वचः॥ वसाम सुसुखं पुत्र ब्राह्मणस्य निवेशने। अज्ञाता धार्तराष्ट्रस्य सत्कृता वीतमन्यवः॥
en: O king, seeing them weeping and piteously lamenting, she could not bear it from her compassion and form her goodness of heart. Being sorry in mind, the amiable Pritha spoke to Bhima these words full of compassion. "O son, our grief being gone we were happily living in this Brahmana's house, unknown to Dhritarashtra's son and much respected by him.

sn: सा चिन्तये सदा पुत्र ब्राह्मणस्यास्य किं न्वहम्। प्रियं कुर्यामिति गृहे यत् कुर्युरुषिताः सुखम्॥
en: O son, I always think what might be good for the Brahmana and what good I can do to him, as men who live in others, house (ought to) try to do.

sn: एतावान् पुरुषस्तात कृतं यस्मिन् न नश्यति। यावच्च कुर्यादन्योऽस्य कुर्यादभ्यधिकं ततः॥
en: O child, he is truly a man who pays back the benefit received. Such an act is never destroyed. One should do more (good) than others do him.

sn: तदिदं ब्राह्मणस्यास्य दुःखमापतितं ध्रुवम्। तत्रास्य यदि साहाय्यं कुर्यामुपकृतं भवेत्॥
en: This Brahmana has certainly fallen into a great distress. If we can be of any help to him (in his present distress), we should by (somewhat) repay his services.

sn: भीमसेन उवाच ज्ञायतामस्य यद् यतश्चैव समुत्थितम्। विदित्वा व्यवसिष्यामि यद्यपि स्यात् सुदुष्करम्॥
en: Bhima said: Learn what distress and from what cause that distress has befallen him. Having learnt it, I shall try to remove it (his distress), however difficult its achievement may be.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवं तौ कथयन्तौ च भूयः शुश्रुवतुः स्वनम्। आर्तिजं तस्य विप्रस्य सभार्यस्य विशाम्पते॥
en: Vaishampayana said : O king when those two (Kunti and Bhima) were thus talking, they heard a cry of sorrow proceeding from the Brahmana and his wife.

sn: अन्तःपुरं ततस्तस्य ब्राह्मणस्य महात्मनः। विवेश त्वरिता कुन्ती बद्धवत्सेव सौरभी॥
en: As the Kamadhenu (the all-boon giving cow) runs at her tethered calf, so Kunti ran in all hurry to the inner apartment of the highsouled Brahmana.

sn: ततस्तं ब्राह्मणं तत्र भार्यया च सुतेन च। दुहित्रा चैव सहितं ददर्शावनताननम्॥
en: She saw there the Brahmana, his wife, his son and his daughter, all sitting with cast-down faces.

sn: दुःखानामागमो ब्राह्मण उवाच धिगिदं जीवितं लोके गतसारमनर्थकम्। दुःखमूलं पराधीनं भृशमप्रियभागि च॥
en: The Brahmana said: Fie on the life in this world which is hollow as the read. It is full of misery; it is a slave to others; it is based on great sorrow.

sn: जीविते परमं दुःखं जीविते परमो ज्वरः। जीविते वर्तमानस्य ध्रुवः॥
en: To live is to suffer great misery; to live is to suffer great diseases. Life is certainly a record of sorrows.

sn: आत्मा ह्येको हि धर्मार्थो कामं चैव निषेवते। एतैश्च विप्रयोगोऽपि दुःखं परमनन्तकम्॥
en: The soul is one, but it has to serve Dharma, Artha and Kama. By simultaneous pursuit of these, great misery is occasioned.

sn: आहुः केचित् परं मोक्षं स च नास्ति कथंचन। अर्थप्राप्तौ तु नरकः कृत्स्न एवोपपद्यते॥
en: Some say salvation is our highest object of attainment, but it can never be attained. The acquisition of wealth is hell; it is attended with misery.

sn: अर्थेप्सुता परं दुःखमर्थप्राप्तौ ततोऽधिकम्। जातस्नेहस्य चार्थेषु विप्रयोगे महत्तरम्॥
en: Great misery is for those that desire wealth, greater for him who has (already) acquired it. Great affection is engendered on the acquired wealth; and when it goes away, the misery is great.

sn: न हि योगं प्रपश्यामि येन मुच्येयमापदः। पुत्रदारेण वा सार्धं प्राद्रवेयमनामयम्॥
en: I do not see by what means I can escape from this danger and how can I fiy away (from this place) with my son and wife?

sn: यतितं वै मया पूर्वं वेत्थ ब्राह्मणि तत् तथा। क्षेमं यतस्ततो गन्तुं त्वया तु मम न श्रुतम्॥
en: O Brahmani, (wife), remember, I tried to go to some other place where we could be happy, but you did not listen to my words.

sn: इह जाता विवृद्धास्मि पिता चापि ममेति वै। उक्तवत्यसि दुर्मेधे याच्यमाना मयासकृत्॥
en: When I repeatedly asked you to go, you, O foolish woman, said, "I am born here; I have grown old here; this is my ancestral homestead."

sn: स्वर्गतोऽपि पिता वृद्धस्तथा माता चिरं तव। बान्धवा भूतपूर्वाश्च तत्र वासे तु का रतिः॥
en: Your father is dead, your old mother died long ago. Your friends and relatives are also dead, why do you (then) desire to live here?

sn: सोऽयं ते बन्धुकामाया अशृण्वत्या वचो मम। बन्धुप्रणाशः सम्प्राप्तो भृशं दुःखकरो मम॥
en: From you affection towards your relatives and friends, you did not then listen to my words. The great misery for the loss of a relative and friend has now come to us.

sn: अथवा मद्विनाशोऽयं न हि शक्ष्यामि कंचन। परित्यक्तुमहं बन्धं स्वयं जीवन् नृशंसवत्॥
en: Oh, how can I bear it? The time has come for my own death. I shall not be able to live like a cruel wretch by abandoning my own relatives and friends.

sn: सहधर्मचरी दान्तां नित्यं मातृसमां मम। सखायं विहितां देवैर्नित्यं परमिकां गतिम्॥
en: You are always my heip-mate in all virtuous acts, you are like a mother to me. The gods have given you to me as my friend; you are my chief stay.

sn: पित्रा मात्रा च विहितां सदा गार्हस्थ्यभागिनीम्। वरयित्वा यथान्यायं मन्त्रवत् परिणीय च॥ कुलीनां शीलसम्पन्नामपत्यजननीमपि। त्वामहं जीवितस्यार्थे साध्वीमनपकारिणीम्॥ परित्यक्तुं न शक्ष्यामि भार्यां नित्यमनुव्रताम्। कुत एव परित्यक्तुं सुतं शक्ष्याम्यहं स्वयम्॥ बालमप्राप्तवयसमजातव्यञ्जनाकृतिम्। भर्तुरर्थाय निक्षिप्तां न्यासं धात्रा महात्मना॥ यया दौहित्रजॉल्लोकानाशंसे पितृभिः सह। स्वयमुत्पाद्य तां बालां कथमुत्स्रष्टुमुत्सहे॥
en: You were made by my parents as a partner of my domestic life; you are nobly-born and of good disposition; you are a mother of children; you are ever devoted to me; you are innocent, ever constant to your vows; you have chosen and wed me in due rites, how can I abandon you for the sake of saving my own life? How shall I be able to abandon my own son? (He is) a child of tender years, having no bcard (yet on his chin). How shall I sacrifice my daughter whom I have begotten myself, who has been given to me by the illustrious creator for bestowing her on a husband and through whom I am to enjoy, along with my ancestors, these regions attainable by those only who possess daughter's sons.

sn: मन्यते केचिदधिकं स्नेहं पुत्रे पितुर्नराः। कन्यायां केचिदपरे मम तुल्यावुभौ स्मृतौ॥
en: Some men think that father's affection for his son is greater; others (think that father's affection) for his daughter (is greater); but mine is equal.

sn: यस्यां लोकाः प्रसूतिश्च स्थिता नित्यमथो सुखम्। अपापां तामहं बालां कथमुत्स्रष्टुमुत्सहे॥
en: How can I abandon the innocent girl upon whom rests the region of internal bliss and my own lineage and perpetual happiness?

sn: आत्मानमपि चोत्सृज्य तप्स्यामि परलोकगः। त्यक्ता ह्येते मया व्यक्तं नेह शक्ष्यन्ति जीवितुम्॥
en: If I sacrifice myself and go to the other world, I shall still be repentant, for being abandoned by me, they would not be able to live.

sn: एषां चान्यतमत्यागो नृशंसो गर्हितो बुधैः। आत्मत्यागे कृते चेमे मरिष्यन्ति मया विना॥
en: To abandon any of these (my wife son or daughter) will be a cruel and most wicked act. If I sacrifice myself, they will (also) die without me.

sn: स कृच्छ्रामहमापन्नो न शक्तस्तर्तुमापदम्। अहो धिक् कां गतिं त्वद्य गमिष्यामि सबान्धवः। सर्वैः सह मृतं श्रेयो न च मे जीवितं क्षमम्॥
en: The distress into which I have fallen is great; I do not know the means of escape (from it). Alas! What means shall I adopt with my friends and relatives! It is better that I should die with them; I am unable to live (any longer).

sn: ब्राह्मण्युवाच न संतापस्त्वया कार्यः प्राकृतेनेव कर्हिचित्। न हि संतापकालोऽयं वैद्यस्य तव विद्यते॥
en: The Brahmani said: You should not grieve like ordinary men. This is not the time for lamentation. You are learned.

sn: अवश्यं निधनं सर्वैर्गन्तव्यमिह मानवैः। अवश्यम्भाविन्यर्थे वै संतापो नेह विद्यते॥
en: All men must die. None should grieve for that which is inevitable.

sn: भार्या पुत्रोऽथ दुहिता सर्वमात्मार्थमिष्यते। व्यथां जहि सुबुद्ध्या त्वं स्वयं यास्यामि तत्र च॥ एतद्धि परमं नार्याः कार्यं लोके सनातनम्। प्राणानपि परित्यज्य यद् भर्तृहितमाचरेत्॥
en: Man desires son, daughter and wife for himself. Therefore abandon grief, for you are greatly intelligent; I shall myself go there. It is the highest and eternal duty of women, namely to sacrifice their lives and to seek the good of their husbands.

sn: तच्च तत्र कृतं कर्म तवापीदं सुखावहम्। भवत्यमुत्र चाक्षय्यं लोकेऽस्मिंश्च यशस्करम्॥
en: Such an act done by me will give you pleasure; it will (also) bring me fame in this world and eternal bliss hereafter.

sn: एष चैव गुरुर्धर्मो यं प्रवक्ष्याम्यहं तव। अर्थश्च तव धर्मश्च भूयानत्र प्रदृश्यते॥
en: What I speak to you is the highest virtue. You can acquire by it (by my sacrificing myself) both virtue and profit.

sn: यदर्थमिष्यते भार्या प्राप्तः सोऽर्थस्त्वया मयि। कन्या चैका कुमारश्च कृताहमनृणा त्वया॥
en: The object for which one desires a wife has already been achieved by you from me. I have borne you a daughter and a son, by which I have been freed from the debt I owe you.

sn: समर्थः पोषणे चासि सुतयो रक्षणे तथा। न त्वहं सुतयोः शक्ता तथा रक्षणपोषणे॥
en: You are able to support and protect your children. I cannot support and protect the children as you can (do it).

sn: मम हि त्वद्विहीनायाः सर्वप्राणधनेश्वर। कथं स्यातां सुतौ बालौ भरेयं च कथं त्वहम्॥
en: You are my life, wealth and lord; having been abandoned by you, how these children to tender years and how myself, can live?

sn: कथं हि विधवानाथा बालुपत्रा विना त्वया। मिथुनं जीवयिष्यामि स्थिता साधुगते पथि॥
en: Being a helpless widow with two children of tender years depending on me how shall I be able to live leading my life in the path of virtue.

sn: अहंकृतावलिप्तैश्च प्रार्थ्यमानामिमां सुताम्। अयुक्तैस्तव सम्बन्धे कथं शक्ष्यामि रक्षितुम्॥
en: How shall I be able to protect the girl, if your this daughter is solicited by dishonourable and vain persons, unworthy of contracting an alliance with you?

sn: उत्सृष्टमामिषं भूमौ प्रार्थयन्ति यथा खगाः प्रार्थयन्ति जनाः सर्वे पतिहीनां तथा स्त्रियम्॥ साहं विचाल्यमाना वै प्रार्थ्यमाना दुरात्मभिः। स्थातुं पथि न शक्ष्यामि सज्जनेष्टे द्विजोत्तम्॥
en: As birds eagerly seek with avidity for the piece of) meat thrown on the ground, so men solicit women who have lost their husbands. O best of the twice-born, being solicited by wicked men, I might waver and I might not be able to keep myself on the path of virtue.

sn: कथं तव कुलस्यैकामिमां बालामनागसम्। पितृपैतामहे मार्गे नियोक्तुमहमुत्सहे॥
en: How shall I be able to place this only daughter of your house, this innocent girl, in the (virtuous) way in which her ancestors have always walked?

sn: कथं शक्ष्यामि बालेऽस्मिन् गुणानाधातुमीप्सितान्। अनाथे सर्वतो लुप्ते यथा त्वं धर्मदर्शिवान्॥
en: How shall I be able to teach this child (your son) every desirable accomplishment to make him as virtuous as yourself in that time of want I shall be helpless (without you)?

sn: इमामपि च ते बालामनाथां परिभूय माम्। अनर्हाः प्रार्थयिष्यन्ति शूद्रा वेदश्रुति यथा।॥
en: When I shall be in such helpless state, the unworthy persons will demand this orphan girl, like Shudras desiring to hear the Vedas.

sn: तां चेदहं न दित्सेयं त्वहगुणैरुपबृंहिताम्। प्रमथ्यैनां हरेयुस्ते हविर्खाङ्क्षा इवाध्वरात्॥
en: If I do not bestow this girl, endued with all qualities and possessing your blood, they may take her away by force as cows take the sacrificial ghee.

sn: सम्प्रेक्षमाणा पुत्रं ते नानुरूपमिवात्मनः। अनर्हवशमापन्नामिमां चापि सुतां तव॥ अवज्ञाता च लोकेषु तथाऽऽत्मानमजानती। अवलिप्तैनरैर्ब्रह्मन् मरिष्यामि न संशयः॥
en: Seeing your son (thoroughly) unlike yourself and your daughter under the control of unworthy person. I shall be despised in the world. I do not know what will happen to me. O Brahmana, there is no doubt I shall certainly die.

sn: तौ च हीनौ मया बालौ त्वया चैव तथाऽऽत्मजौ। विनश्येतां न संदेहो मत्स्याविव जलक्षये॥
en: There is no doubt these children of tender years, being bereft of me and you, will die as fish (in a tank) when the water is dried up.

sn: त्रितयं सर्वथाप्येवं विनशिष्यत्यसंशयम्। त्वया विहीनं तस्मात् त्वं मां परित्यक्तुमर्हसि॥
en: There is no doubt the three (myself, our son and daughter) will all die without you. Therefore you ought to abandon me.

sn: व्युष्टिरेषा परा स्त्रीणां पूर्वं भर्तुः परां गतिम्। गन्तुं ब्रह्मन् सपुत्राणामिति धर्मविदो दिदुः॥
en: O Brahmana, persons learned in the precepts of virtue have said that to predecease their husbands in an act of the highest merit for women who have borne children.

sn: परित्यक्तः सुतश्चायं दुहितेयं तथा मया। बान्धवाश्च परित्यक्तास्त्वदर्थं जीवितं च मे॥
en: I am ready to abandon this son and this daughter, these my relations, my this life itself.

sn: यज्ञैस्तपोभिर्नियमैर्दानैश्च विविधैस्तथा। विशिष्यते स्त्रिया भर्तुनित्यं प्रियहिते स्थितिः॥
en: To be ever engaged in serving her husband is a higher duty to a women than sacrifices, asceticism, vows and various charities.

sn: तदिदं यच्चिकीर्षामि धर्मं परमसम्मतम्। इष्टं चैव हितं चैव तव चैव कुलस्य च॥
en: Therefore the act I desire to perform is consonant with the highest virtue. It is for your good and for the good of your race.

sn: इष्टानि चाप्यपत्यानि द्रव्याणि सुहृदः प्रियाः। आपद्धर्मप्रमोक्षाय भार्या चापि सतां मतम्॥
en: The virtuous (men) say, that children, relatives, wives and all things dear in this world) are cherished for rescuing oneself from distress.

sn: आपदर्थे धनं रक्षेद् दारान् रक्षेद् धनैरपि। आत्मानं सततं रक्षेद् दारैरपि धनैरपि॥
en: Man cherishes wealth for (rescuing himself) from distress and danger. By wealth be cherishes his wife. He must always cherish himself both by his wealth and wife.

sn: दृष्टादृष्टफलार्थं हि भार्या पुत्रो धनं गृहम्। सर्वमेतद् विधातव्यं बुधानमेष निश्चयः॥
en: The wise men have said that wife, son, wealth or house is acquired to provide for foreseen or unforescen accidents.

sn: एकतो वा कुलं कृत्स्नमात्मा वा कुलवर्धनः। न समं सर्वमेवेति बुधानामेष निश्चयः॥
en: The wise men have said that one's all relations, weighed against one's own self, would not be equal to one's own self.

sn: स कुरुष्व मया कार्यं तारयात्मानमात्मना। अनुजानीहि मामार्य सुतौ मे परिपालय॥
en: Therefore, O respected Sir, accomplish your object by me. Protect yourself by abandoning me. Give me your permission cherish children.

sn: अवध्यां स्त्रियमित्याहुर्धर्मज्ञा धर्मनिश्चये। धर्मज्ञान् राक्षसानाहुन हन्यात् स च मामपि॥
en: In fixing moralities the men, learned in the precepts of virtue, have said that women should never be killed; and (they have also said that the Rakshasas are learned in the rules of morality. Therefore he (the Rakshasas) may not kill me.

sn: निस्संशयं वधः पुंसां स्त्रीणां संशयितो वधः। अतो मामेव धर्मज्ञ प्रस्थापयितुमर्हसि॥
en: It is certain that he will kill a man, but it is doubtful whether he will kill a woman. O virtuously learned man, you ought to send me.

sn: भुक्तं प्रियाण्यवाप्तानि धर्मश्च चरितो महान्। त्वत् प्रसूतिः प्रिया प्राप्ता न मां तप्स्यत्यजीवितम्।३३॥
en: I have enjoyed much happiness; I have obtained many things agreeable; I have earned much of religious merits; I have obtained from you beloved sons; I do not grieve to die.

sn: जातपुत्रा च वृद्धा च प्रियकामा च ते सदा। समीक्ष्यैतदहं सर्वं व्यवसायं करोम्यतः॥
en: I have borne son and I have grown old; I am ever desirous of doing good to you. Having considered all this, I have come to this resolution.

sn: उत्सृज्यापि हि मामार्य प्राप्स्यस्यन्यामपि स्त्रियम्। ततः प्रतिष्ठितो धर्मो भविष्यति पुनस्तव॥
en: O respected Sir, you can take another wife by abandoning me. You may be then again placed on the path of virtue.

sn: न चाप्यधर्मः कल्याण बहुपत्नीकृतां नृणाम्। स्त्रीणामधर्मः सुमहान् भर्तुः पूर्वस्य लङ्घने॥
en: To marry more than one wife is not sin among men. It is very sinful for a woman to take second husband after the first.

sn: एतत् सर्वं समीक्ष्य त्वमात्मत्यागं च गर्हितम्। आत्मानं तारयाद्याशु कुलं चेमौ च दारकौ॥
en: Having considered all this and knowing that your self-sacrifice is censurable, save today yourself, your race and your these two children without loss of time.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्तस्तया भर्ता तां समालिङ्गय भारत। मुमोच बाष्पं शनकैः सभार्यो भृशदुःखितः॥
en: O foremost of the Bharata race, when Brahmani told thus, her husband became griefstricken and, embracing her, shed copious tears along with her.

description: Words of Brahmana's daughter and son
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तयोर्दुःखितयोर्वाक्यमतिमात्रं निशम्य तु। ततो दुःखपरीताङ्गी कन्या तावभ्यभाषत॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having heard these words of her affected parents, the daughter was filled with grief and she thus spoke (to them.)

description: Words of Brahmana's daughter and son
sn: किमेवं भृशदुःखार्ती रोरूयेतामनाथवत्। ममापि श्रूयतां वाक्यं श्रुत्वा च क्रियतां क्षमम्॥
en: The Daughter said : Why are you so sorrowful? Why are you weeping, as if you have none. Listen to my words and hearing them, do what is proper.

description: Words of Brahmana's daughter and son
sn: धर्मतोऽहं परित्याज्या युवयोर्नात्र संशयः। त्यक्तव्यां मां परित्यज्य त्राहि सर्वं मयैकया।॥
en: There is no doubt that you will one time abandon me by the dictates of virtue. Abandon me who am to be abandoned and thus save all by (sacrificing) me alone.

description: Words of Brahmana's daughter and son
sn: इत्यर्थमिष्यतेऽपत्यं तारयिष्यति मामिति। अस्मिन्नुपस्थिते काले तरध्वं प्लवन्मया॥
en: Men desire for children hoping, they will save them. Cross this stream of your difficulty by me.

description: Words of Brahmana's daughter and son
sn: इह वा तारयेद् दुर्गादुत वा प्रेत्य भारत। सर्वथा तारयेत् पुत्रः पुत्र इत्युच्यते बुधैः॥
en: A child saves his presents in this world and in the next. Therefore, a child is called by the learmed Putra.

description: Words of Brahmana's daughter and son
sn: आकाङ्क्षन्ते च दौहित्रान् मयि नित्यं पितामहाः। तत् स्वयं वै परित्रास्ये रक्षन्ती जीवितं पितुः॥
en: My forefathers always desire to have daughter's son by me, (to save them from hell). I shall myself save them by saving the life of my father.

description: Words of Brahmana's daughter and son
sn: भ्राता च मम बालोऽयं गते लोकममुं त्वयि। अचिरेणैव कालेन विनश्यत न संशयः॥
en: My brother is but of tender years; there is no doubt he will die soon after your death.

description: Words of Brahmana's daughter and son
sn: तातेऽपि हि गते स्वर्ग विनष्टे च ममानुजे। पिण्डः पितॄणां व्युच्छिद्येत् तत् तेषां विप्रियं भवेत्॥
en: If you, my father, ascend to heaven, if my brother dies, the Pinda (funeral cake) for the Pitris (ancestors) will be stopped and it will be most unfavourite act of theirs.

description: Words of Brahmana's daughter and son
sn: पित्रा त्यक्ता तथा मात्रा भ्रात्रा चाहमसंशयम्। दुःखाद् दुःखतरं प्राप्य म्रियेयमतथोचिता॥
en: Having been abandoned by my father brother and also my mother, I shall fall from misery to greater misery and I shall finally perish in great distress.

description: Words of Brahmana's daughter and son
sn: त्वयि त्वरोगे निर्मुक्ते माता भ्राता च मे शिशुः। संतानश्चैव पिण्डश्च प्रतिष्ठास्यत्यसंशयम्॥
en: There is no doubt that if you can save yourself, my mother and my child brother, also the Pinda will be perpetuated.

description: Words of Brahmana's daughter and son
sn: आत्मा पुत्रः सखा भार्या कृच्छं तु दुहिता किला स कृच्छ्रान्मोचयात्मानं मां च धर्मे नियोजय॥
en: The son is one's own self; the wife is one's friend; the daughter is (however) a source of trouble. Save yourself by sacrificing that cause of trouble; and set me on the path of virtue.

description: Words of Brahmana's daughter and son
sn: अनाथा कृपणा बाला यत्रक्वचनगामिनी। भविष्यामि त्वया तात विहीना कृपणा सदा॥
en: O father, I am but a girl being abandoned by you, I shall be helpless and miserable and I shall have to go anywhere and everywhere.

description: Words of Brahmana's daughter and son
sn: अथवाहं करिष्यामि कुलस्यास्य विमोचनम्। फलसंस्था भविष्यामि कृत्वा कर्म सुदुष्करम्॥
en: I shall, therefore, save my race and I shall acquire the merit that such difficult work brings in.

description: Words of Brahmana's daughter and son
sn: अथवा यास्यसे तत्र त्यक्त्वा मां द्विजसत्तम्। पीडिताहं भविष्यामि तदवेक्षस्व मामपि॥
en: O best of the twice-born, leaving me behind, if you go there (to the Rakshasas) I shall be very much pained; therefore be kind to ine.

description: Words of Brahmana's daughter and son
sn: तदस्मदर्थं धर्मार्थं प्रसवार्थं स सत्तम। आत्मानं परिरक्षस्व त्यक्तव्यां मां च संत्यज॥
en: O excellent man, abandoning me who am to be (one day) abandoned, save yourself for our sake, for the sake of virtue and your race.

description: Words of Brahmana's daughter and son
sn: अवश्यकरणीये च मा त्वां कालोऽत्यगादयम्। किं त्वतः परमं दुःखं यद् वयं स्वर्गते त्वयि॥ याचमानाः परादन्नं परिधावेमहि श्ववत्। त्वयि त्वरोगे निर्मुक्ते क्लेशादस्मात् सबान्धवे। अमृते वसती लोके भविष्यामि सुखान्विता॥
en: There should not be may delay in doing that which is inevitable. What could be more painful to us than your ascending heaven. (Then) we shall have to beg our food from others like dogs. If you are saved with your friends (dear ones), I shall pass my time in heaven and bliss.

description: Words of Brahmana's daughter and son
sn: इतः प्रदाने देवाश्च पितरश्चेति न श्रुतम्। त्वया दत्तेन तोयेन भविष्यन्ति हिताय वै॥
en: We have heard that if after bestowing your daughter, you offer obtains to the celestial and forefathers, they will be propitious to you.

description: Words of Brahmana's daughter and son
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवं बहुविधं तस्या निशम्य परिदेवितम्। पिता माता च सा चैव कन्या प्ररुरुदुस्त्रयः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having heard her these piteous lamentations, the father, the brother and the daughter began to weep (together).

description: Words of Brahmana's daughter and son
sn: ततः प्ररुदितान् सर्वान् निशम्याथ सुतस्तदा। उत्फुल्लनयनो बाल: कलमव्यक्तमब्रवीत्॥
en: Thereupon seeing them all weep, their son of tender years, spoke thus in childish words, his eyes expanded with joy.

description: Words of Brahmana's daughter and son
sn: मा पिता रुद मा मातर्मा स्वसस्त्विति चाब्रवीत्। प्रहसन्निव सर्वांस्तानेकैकमनुसर्पति॥ ततः स तृणमादाय प्रहृष्टः पुनरब्रवीत्। अनेनाहं हनिष्यामि राक्षसं पुरुषादकम्॥
en: He said O father, o you mother, O sister also, do not weep.” Thus saying and smiling, he came to each of them. Then taking up a blade of glass, he said again in joy, “I shall kill the cannibal Rakshasas by it.

description: Words of Brahmana's daughter and son
sn: तथापि तेषां दुःखेन परीतानां निशम्य तत्। बालस्य वाक्यमव्यक्तं हर्षः समभवन्महान्॥
en: Through they were all in grief, yet hearing the lisping words of the child, they felt exceeding delight.

description: Words of Brahmana's daughter and son
sn: अयं काल इति ज्ञात्वा कुन्ती समुपसृत्य तान्। गतासूनमृतेनेव जीवयन्तीदमब्रवीत्॥
en: Thinking that to be the (proper) time (to appear before them), Kunti came to them and reviving them as nectar revives a dead man, she thus spoke (to them).

sn: कुन्त्युवाच कुतोमूलमिदं दुःखं ज्ञातुमिच्छामि तत्त्वतः। विदित्वाप्यपकर्षेयं शक्यं चेदपकर्षितुम्॥
en: Kunti said: I desire to learn from you what is the cause of this grief. Learning it, I shall remove it, if is capable of being removed.

sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच उपपन्नं सतामेतद् यद् ब्रवीषि तपोधने। न तु दुःखमिदं शक्यं पानुषेण व्यपोहितम्॥
en: The Brahmana said : O ascetic lady, what you say is no doubt worthy of virtuous men. But this grief cannot be removed by any human being.

sn: समीपे नगरस्यास्य बको वसति राक्षसः। ईशो जनपदस्यास्य पुरस्य च महाबलः॥ पुष्टो मानुषमांसेन दुर्बुद्धिः पुरुषादकः। रक्षत्यसुररानित्यमिमं जनपदं बली॥ नगरं चैव देशं च रक्षोबलसमन्वितः। तत्कृते परचक्राच्च भूतेब्यश्च न नो भयम्॥
en: A Rakshasas, named Baka, lives not far off from this town. That greatly powerful (cannibal) is the lord of this town and of this country. That wicked-minded and powerful cannibal, that chief of the Asuras, being fattened by (eating) human flesh, rules over this country. This country and town are protected by the strength of that Rakshasas; thus being protected, we have no fear of any enemy, nay of any living soul.

sn: वेतनं तस्य विहितं शालिवाहस्य भोजनम्। महिषौ पुरुषश्चैको यस्तदादाय गच्छति॥
en: His remuneration however is fixed to supply his food, which consists of one cart load of rice, two buffaloes and the man who takes them to him.

sn: एकैकश्चापि पुरुषस्तत् प्रयच्छति भोजनम्। स वारो बहुभिर्वर्भवत्यसुकरो नरैः॥
en: One after another all (men of this town) send him his food. Though it is very difficult to be kept, yet the turn comes to a particular family at intervals of many years.

sn: तद्विमोक्षाय ये केचिद् यतन्ति पुरुषाः क्वचित्। सपुत्रदारांस्तान् हत्वा तद् रक्षो भक्षयत्युत॥
en: If people try to avoid it, the Rakshasas then eats them up with their wives and children.

sn: वेत्रकीयगृहे राजा नायं नयमिहास्थितः। उपायं तं न कुरुते यत्नादपि स मन्दधीः। अनामयं जनस्यास्य येन स्यादद्य शाश्वतम्॥
en: There is a king in a place called Vetrakiyagriha, but that foolish man does not know how to govern (his kingdom) and he does not take any step by which this country may be rendered safe.

sn: एतदर्हा वयं नूनं वसामो दुर्बलस्य ये। विषये नित्यवास्तव्याः कुराजानमुपाश्रिताः॥
en: We certainly deserve it all, for we live in everlasting anxiety in the kingdom of a wretched and weak king.

sn: ब्राह्मणाः कस्य वक्तव्याः कस्य वाच्छन्दचारिणः। गुणैरेते हि वत्स्यन्ति कामगाः पक्षिणो यथा॥
en: The Brahmanas can never be made to live (permanently) in the house of any one, (for) they are free men. They depend upon their own accomplishments and roam (over the world) like a bird, free to fly at pleasure.

sn: राजानं प्रथमं विन्देत् ततो भार्यां ततो धनम्। त्रयस्य संचयेनास्य ज्ञातीन् पुत्रांश्च तारयेत्॥
en: It is said that a (good) king should be saved first, them a wife and then wealth, by the acquisition of the three, one can rescue his relatives and sons.

sn: विपरीतं मया चेदं त्रयं सर्वमुपार्जितम्। तदिमामापदं प्राप्य भृशं तप्यामहे वयम्॥
en: In the matter of the acquisition of these three, my course has been (quite) the reserve. Therefore falling into this danger, I am suffering great affections.

sn: सोऽयमस्माननुप्राप्तो वारः कुलविनाशनः। भोजनं पुरुषश्चैकः प्रदेयं वेतनं मया॥
en: The race destroying turn of (supplying food to the Rakshsasa) has come round to me. I shall have to give the food and a man as the remuneration of the (Rakshasas).

sn: न च मे विद्यते वित्तं संक्रेतुं पुरुषं क्वचित्। सुहज्जनं प्रदातुं च न शक्ष्यामि कदाचन॥
en: I have no wealth to buy a man. I shall not bu able to give one who is dear to me.

sn: गतिं चैव न पश्यामि तस्मान्मोक्षाय रक्षसः। सोऽहं दुःखार्णवे मग्नो महत्यसुकरे भृशम्॥
en: I do not see any means to save myself from the Rakshasas; therefore, I am plunged into a great ocean of grief, from which there is no escape.

sn: सहैवैतैर्गमिष्यामि बान्धवैरद्य राक्षसम्। ततो नः सहितान् क्षुद्रः सर्वानेवोपभोक्ष्यति॥
en: I shall today with all my family, go to that Rakshasas so that, that wretch may devour us all at once.

description: Promise of Bhima to kill Baka
sn: कुत्युवाच न विषादस्त्वया कार्यों भयादस्मात् कथंचन। उपायः परिदृष्टोऽत्र तस्मान्मोक्षाय रक्षसः॥
en: Kunti said : Do not grieve for this fear, I see a means by which you may be saved from the Rakshasas.

description: Promise of Bhima to kill Baka
sn: एकस्तव सुतो बालः कन्या चैका तपस्विनी। न चैतयोस्तथा पत्न्या गमनं तव रोचये।॥
en: You have only one son who is of tender years; you have only one daughter, who is engaged in vows. I do not like that any of these or yourself or your wife should go.

description: Promise of Bhima to kill Baka
sn: मम पञ्च सुता ब्रह्मस्तेषामेको गमिष्यति। त्वदर्थं वलिमादाय तस्य पापस्य रक्षसः॥
en: I have five sons; one of them will go carrying on your behalf your tribute to that sinful Rakshasas.

description: Promise of Bhima to kill Baka
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच नाहमेतत् करिष्यामि जीवितार्थी कथंचन। ब्राह्मणस्यातिथैश्चैव स्वार्थे प्राणान् वियोजयन्॥
en: The Brahmana said : I can never do this in order to live. I can not cause the death of a Brahmana and a guest for saving my own life.

description: Promise of Bhima to kill Baka
sn: न त्वेतदकुलीनासु नाधर्मिष्ठासु विद्यते। यद् ब्राह्मणार्थं विसृजेदात्मानमपि चात्मजम्॥
en: Even those that are lowly born and sinful refuse to do this; one should sacrifice himself and children for the sake of a Brahmana.

description: Promise of Bhima to kill Baka
sn: आत्मनस्तु मया श्रेयो बोद्धव्यमिति रोचते। ब्रह्मवध्याऽऽत्मवध्या वा श्रेयानात्मवधो मम॥ ब्रह्मवध्या परं पापं निष्कृति त्र विद्यते। अबुद्धिपूर्वं कृत्वापि वमात्मवधो मम॥
en: I consider this precept best for me and I like to follow it. Between the death of a Brahmana and of my own, I would prefer the latter. To kill a Brahmana is a great sin, of which there is no expiation. It is best for me to sacrifice myself reluctantly instead of sacrificing a Brahmana reluctantly.

description: Promise of Bhima to kill Baka
sn: न त्वहं वधमाकाक्षे स्वयमेवात्मनः शुभे। परैः कृते वधे पापं न किंचिन्मयि विद्यते॥
en: O blessed lady, in sacrificing myself, I do not commit the sin of self destruction. I shall commit no sin by being killed by another.

description: Promise of Bhima to kill Baka
sn: अभिसंधिकृते तस्मिन् ब्राह्मणस्य वधे मया। निष्कृतिं न प्रपश्यामि नृशंसं क्षुद्रमेव च॥ आगतस्य गृहं त्यागस्तथैव शरणार्थिनः। याचमानस्य च वधो नृशंसो गर्हितो बुधैः॥
en: But if I deliberately kill a Brahmana, I shall commit a cruel and sinful act, from which I shall never escape. The learned men have said that the abandonment of one who has come to your house or who has sought your protection and the killing of one who seeks death at your hands are both cruel and sinful.

description: Promise of Bhima to kill Baka
sn: कुर्यान्न निन्दितं कर्म न नृशंसं कथंचन। इति पूर्वे महात्मान आपद्धर्मविदो विदुः॥ श्रेयांस्तु सहदारस्य विनाशोऽद्य मम स्वयम्। ब्राह्मणस्य वधं नाहमनुमंस्ये कदाचन॥
en: The high-souled men, learned in the precepts that should be adopted in distress and danger, formerly said that one should never perform a cruel and censurable act. It is best for me that I should myself perish to day with my wife. I shall never cause the death of a Brahmana.

description: Promise of Bhima to kill Baka
sn: कुन्त्युवाच ममाप्येषा मतिर्ब्रह्मन् विप्रा रक्ष्या इति स्थिरा। न चाप्यनिष्टः पुत्रो मे यदि पुत्रशतं भवेत्॥ न चासौ राक्षसः शक्तो मम पुत्रविनाशने। वीर्यवान् मन्त्रसिद्धश्च तेजस्वी च सुतो मम॥
en: Kunti said: O Brahmana, my form opinion is that Brahmanas must be protected always. if I have one hundred sons, none of them would be less dear to me. But this Rakshasa will not be able to kill my son. my son is powerful energetic and learned in Mantras.

description: Promise of Bhima to kill Baka
sn: राक्षसाय च तत् सर्वं प्रापयिष्यति भोजनम्। मोक्षयिष्यति चात्मानमिति मे निश्चिता मतिः॥
en: He will reach the food of the Rakshasa, but he will be able to save himself; this is my firm belief.

description: Promise of Bhima to kill Baka
sn: समागताश्च वीरेण दृष्टपूर्वाश्च राक्षसाः। बलवन्तो महाकाया निहताश्चाप्यनेकशः॥
en: I had seen before that many powerful and huge Rakshasas came to my son and were killed at his hands.

description: Promise of Bhima to kill Baka
sn: न त्विदं केषुचिद् ब्रह्मन् व्याहर्तव्यं कथंचन। विद्यार्थिनो हि मे पुत्रान् विप्रकुर्युः कुतूहलात्॥
en: O Brahmana, do not by any means disclose this to anybody; for then people, being curious and desirous of learning (their power), will trouble my sons.

description: Promise of Bhima to kill Baka
sn: गुरुणा चाननुज्ञातो ग्राहयेद् यत् सुतो मम। न स कुर्यात् तथा कार्यं विद्ययेति सतां मतम्॥
en: The opinion of the learned men is that if my son gives this knowledge (to others) without the assent of his preceptor, he will no longer be able to profit by it.

description: Promise of Bhima to kill Baka
sn: एवमुक्तस्तु पृथया स विप्रो भार्यया सह। हृष्टः सम्पूजयामास तद्वाक्यममृतोपमम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having been thus addressed by Pritha (Kunti) the Brahmana and his wife became exceedingly glad and assented to those nectar like words (of Kunti).

description: Promise of Bhima to kill Baka
sn: ततः कुन्ती च विप्रश्च सहितावनिलात्मजम्। तमबूतां कुरुष्वेति स तथेत्यब्रवीच्च तौ॥
en: Thereupon Kunti and the Brahmana went to the son of Anila (Bhima) and told him "Do this"; and he replied by saying “Be it so."

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच करिष्य इति भीमेन प्रतिज्ञातेऽथ भारत। आजग्मुस्ते ततः सर्वे भैक्षमादाय पाण्डवाः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : O descendant of Bharata, when Bhima promised by saying, “I shall do it," the Pandavas all came there after collecting food,

sn: आकारेणैव तं ज्ञात्वा पाण्डुपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः। रहः समुपविश्यैकस्तत: पप्रच्छ मातरम्॥
en: The son of Pandu Yudhisthira learnt the affair by the appearance of Bhima and sitting by his mother, he spoke thus to her in private.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच किं चिकीर्षत्ययं कर्म भीमो भीमपराक्रमः। भवत्यनुमते कच्चित् स्वयं वा कर्तुमिच्छति॥
en: Yudhisthira said: What is the work that the greatly powerful Bhima wants to performs? Does he wish to do it by your command or of his own will?

sn: कुन्त्युवाच ममैव वचनादेष करिष्यति परंतपः। ब्राह्मणार्थे महत् कृत्यं मोक्षाय नगरस्य च॥
en: Kunti said: By my request the chastiser of foes (Bhima) will do this great deed for the sake of the Brahmana and in order to save the town (from the Rakshasa).

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच किमिदं साहसं तीक्ष्णं भवत्या दुष्करं कृतम्। परित्यागं हि पुत्रस्य न प्रशंसन्ति साधवः॥
en: Yudhisthira said : What rush act has been done by you! It is a very difficult work. The learned men never praise one's abandonment of his own son.

sn: कथं परसुतस्यार्थे स्वसुतं त्यक्तुमिच्छसि। लोकवेदविरुद्धं हि पुत्रत्यागात् कृतं त्वया॥
en: were Why do you wish to abandon your son for the sake of another's son? You have done this act of abandonment of your son which is not approved by both men and by the Vedas.

sn: यस्य बाहू समाश्रित्य सुखं सर्वे शयामहे। राज्यं चापहृतं क्षुद्रराजिहीर्षामहे पुनः॥
en: By the strength of whose arms we all sleep in comfort and hope to recovered the kingdom of which we have been deprived by the wretches (Duryodhana and others).

sn: यस्य दुर्योधनो वीर्यं चिन्तयन्नमितौजसः। न शेते रजनी: सर्वा दुःखाच्छकुनिना सह॥
en: Remembering whose great prowess, Duryodhana with Sakuni and all others do not sleep (for a moment) in the night in anxiety;

sn: यस्य वीरस्य वीर्येण मुक्ता जतुगृहाद् वयम्। अन्येभ्यश्चैव पापेभ्यो निहतश्च पुरोचनः॥
en: By whose heretic prowess we rescued from the burning house of lac and others dangers; by whom Purochana was killed.

sn: यस्य वीर्यं समाश्रित्य वसुपूर्णां वसुन्धराम्। इमां मन्यामहे प्राप्तां निहत्य धृतराष्ट्रजान्॥ तस्य व्यवसितस्त्यागो बुद्धिमास्थाय बुद्धिमास्थाय कां त्वया। कच्चिन्नु दुःखैर्बुद्धिस्ते विलुप्ता गतचेतसः॥
en: Relying on whose prowess we believe ourselves that we have already acquired this earth full of wealth and have killed the sons of Dhritarashira. On what consideration have you resolved upon abandoning him? have you lost your senses on account of the calamities?

sn: कुन्त्युवाच युधिष्ठिर न संतापस्त्वया कार्यो वृकोदरे। न चायं बुद्धिदौर्बल्याद् व्यवसायः कृतो मया॥
en: Kunti said: ( Yudhisthira, you need not be anxious for Vrikodara. I have not resolved (to do it) out of any weakness of my understanding.

sn: इह विप्रस्य भवने वयं पुत्र सुखोषिताः। अज्ञाता धार्तराष्ट्राणां सत्कृतः वीतमन्यवः॥ तस्य प्रतिक्रिया पार्थ मयेयं प्रसमीक्षिता। एतावानेव पुरुषः कृतं यस्मिन् न नश्यति॥
en: O son, our grief being assuaged, we live happily in the house of this Brahmana, unknown to the sons of Dhritarashtra and much respected by him. O Partha, I have resolved upon doing this in order to requite him, for he is a (true) man upon whom good service is never lost.

sn: यावच्च कुर्यादन्योऽस्य कुर्याद् बहुगुणं ततः। दृष्ट्वा भीमस्य विक्रान्तं तदा जदुगृहे महत्। हिडिम्बस्य वधाच्चैवं विश्वासो मे वृकोदरे॥
en: It is (always) proper that the requital should be greater than the service received. Seeing the great prowess of Bhima in the house of lac. And in killing Hidimba, my confidence on Vrikodara is great.

sn: बाह्वोर्बलं हि भीमस्य नागायुतसमं महत्। येन यूयं गजप्रख्या नियूँढा वारणावतात्॥
en: The strength of Bhima's arms is as great as that of ten thousand elephants. It was therefore that he was able to carry you, all as heavy as elephants from Varanavata.

sn: वृकोदरेण सदृशो बलेनान्यो न विद्यते। योऽभ्युदीयाद् युधि श्रेष्ठमपि वज्रधरं स्वयम्॥
en: There is none so strong as Vrikodara; he may even vanquish in battle the thunderer (Indra) himself.

sn: जातमात्रः पुरा चैव ममाङ्कात् पतितो गिरौ। शरीरगौरवादस्य शिला गात्रैविचूर्णिता॥
en: As soon as he was born, he fell from my lap on the stone. The mass of stone on which he fell was broken into pieces by the weight of his body.

sn: तदहं प्रज्ञया ज्ञात्वा बलं भीमस्य पाण्डव। प्रतिकार्ये च विप्रस्य ततः कृतवती मतिम्॥
en: O Pandaya, from that day I have come to know the (great) strength of Bhima. Therefore, I am desirous of requiting (the services) of the Brahmana.

sn: नेदं लोभान्न चाज्ञानान्न च मोहाद् विनिश्चितम्। बुद्धिपूर्वं तु धर्मस्य व्यवसायः कृतो मया॥
en: I have not done this from foolishness, from ignorance, or from any inotive of gain. I have deliberately resolved to do this virtuous act.

sn: अर्थों द्वावपि निष्पन्नौ युधिष्ठिर भविष्यतः। प्रतीकारश्च वासस्य धर्मश्च चरितो महान्॥
en: O Yudhisthira, two objects will be gained by this act, one is the requital of the Brahmana's services (to us) and the other is the acquisition of great religious merit.

sn: यो ब्राह्मणस्य साहाय्यं कुर्यादर्थेषु कहिचित्। क्षत्रियः स शुभाँल्लोकानाप्नुयादिति मे मतिः॥
en: It is my opinion that the Kshatriya who helps a Brahmana obtains the regions of bliss in after life.

sn: क्षत्रियस्यैव कुर्वाणः क्षत्रियो वधमोक्षणम्। विपुलां कीर्तिमाप्नोति लोकेऽस्मिंश्च परत्र च॥
en: A Kshatriya, who saves the life of a Kshatriya, acquires great fame in this and in the next world.

sn: वैश्यस्यार्थे च साहाय्यं कुर्वाणः क्षत्रियो भुवि। स सर्वेष्वपि लोकेषु प्रजा रञ्जयते ध्रुवम्॥
en: A Kshatriya, who helps a Vaishya on earth, certainly becomes popular among men.

sn: शूद्रं तु मोचयेद् राजा शरणार्थिनमागतम्। प्राप्नोतीह कुले जन्म सद्रव्ये राजपूजिते॥
en: The king should even protect a Shudra who seeks protection. If he does so, he is born in his next birth in a royal family, possessing property and being adored by other kings.

sn: एवं मां भगवान् व्यासः पुरा पौरवन्दना प्रोवाचासुकरप्रज्ञस्तस्मादेवं चिकीर्षितम्॥
en: O descendant of Kuru, the illustrious and wise Vyasa formerly told me this. Therefore I am resolved upon doing it.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच उपपन्नमिदं मातस्त्वया यद् बुद्धिपूर्वकम्। आर्तस्य ब्राह्मणस्यैतदनुक्रोशादिदं कृतम्॥
en: Yudhisthira said : O mother, what you have deliberately done, moved by the compassion for the affected Brahmana, is indeed excellent.

sn: ध्रुवमेष्यति भीमोऽयं निहत्य पुरुषादकम्। सर्वथा ब्राह्मणस्यार्थे यदनुक्रोशवत्यसि॥
en: Because you are compassionate for the Brahmana, Bhima will certainly come back after killing the cannibal.

sn: यथा त्विदं न विन्देयुनरा नगरवासिनः। तथायं ब्राह्मणो वाच्यः परिग्राह्यश्च यत्नतः॥
en: But tell the Brahmana that he must not to any thing by which the people of this town may know all about it. You must carefully make him promise it.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततो रात्र्यां व्यतीतायामन्नमादाय पाण्डवः। भीमसेनो ययौ तत्र यत्रासौ पुरुषादकः॥ आसाद्य तु वनं तस्य रक्षसः पाण्डवो बली। आजुहाव ततो नाम्ना तदनमुपपादयन्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : When the night passed away, the Pandava, Bhimasena, taking with him the food (for the Rakshasa) set out for the place where the cannibal dwelt. Reaching the forest in which the Rakshasas lived, the greatly strong Pandava (Bhima) began to eat himself the food and called loudly the Rakshasas by name.

sn: ततः स राक्षसः क्रुद्धो भीमस्य वचनात् तदा। आजगाम सुसंक्रुद्धो यत्र भीमो व्यवस्थितः॥
en: Thereupon the Rakshasas was inflamed with anger by Bhima's words. He came in wrath to the place where Bhima was.

sn: महाकायो महावेगो दारयन्निव मेदिनीम्। लोहिताक्षः करालश्च लोहितश्मश्रुमूर्धजः॥
en: Of huge body, of great strength, of fierce appearance, with red eyes, red beard, red hair, he pressed the earth (as he walked).

sn: आकर्णाद् भिन्नवक्त्रश्च शरूको विभीषणः। त्रिशिस्त्रां भ्रुकुटिं कृत्वा संदश्य दशनच्छदम्॥ भुञ्जानमन्नं तं दृष्ट्वा भीमसेनं स राक्षसः। विवृत्य नयने क्रुद्ध इदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: The opening of his mouth was from ear to ear, his ears were like arrows, his visage was grim and his forehead furrowed into three lines. Seeing Bhima engaged in eating his food the Rakshasas, thus spoke in anger and with eyes expanded and lips bitten.

sn: कोऽयमन्नमिदं भुङ्क्ते मदर्थमुपकल्पितम्। पश्यतो मम दुर्बुद्धिर्मियासुर्यमसादनम्॥
en: The Rakshasas said : Who is the fool that desires to go to the land of the dead by eating in my very sight the food intended for me!

sn: भीमसेनस्ततः श्रुत्वा प्रहसन्निव भारत। राक्षसं तमनादृत्य भुक्त एव पराङ्मुखः॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, hearing this Bhimasena smiled (in derision) and disregarding the Rakshasas and turning his head continued to eat.

sn: रवं स भैरवं कृत्वा समुद्यम्य करावुभौ। अभ्यद्रवद् भीमसेनं जिघांसुः पुरुषादकः॥
en: Uttering a fearful yell, the cannibal rushed on Bhima with two arms raised high and with the intention of killing Bhimasena.

sn: तथापि परिभूयैनं प्रेक्षमाणो वृकोदरः। राक्षसं भुक्त एवान्नं पाण्डवः परवीरहा॥ अमर्षेण तु सम्पूर्णः कुन्तीपुत्रं वृकोदरम्। जघान पृष्ठे पाणिभ्यामुभाभ्यां पृष्ठतः स्थितः॥
en: That slayer of hostile heroes, the son of Pandu (Bhima), even then disregarding him and casting on him only a single glance, continued to eat the food of the Rakshasas. Being filled with great displeasure, he (the Rakshasas) struck a heavy blow with both his hands on the back of the son of Kunti, Vrikodara.

sn: तथा बलवता भीमः पाणिभ्यां भृशमाहतः। नैवावलोकयामास राक्षसं भुङ्क्त एव सः॥
en: Though Bhima was struck in great force with the arms (of the Rakshasas), yet he did not even look at him, but he continued to eat.

sn: ततः स भूयः संक्रुद्धो वृक्षमादाय राक्षसः। ताडयिष्यंस्तदा भीमं पुनरभ्यद्रवद् बली॥
en: Thereupon he (the Rakshasas) became very angry, tore up a tree and ran at the strong Bhima to strike him again.

sn: ततो भीमः शनैर्भुक्त्वा तदन्नं पुरुषर्षभः। वायुपस्पृश्य संहृष्टस्तस्थौ युधि महाबलः॥
en: That best of men, the greatly strong Bhima, leisurely ate up all the food and then washing himself he stood up cheerfully to fight.

sn: क्षिप्तं क्रुद्धेन तं वृक्षं प्रतिजग्राह वीर्यवान्। सव्येन पाणिना भीमः प्रहसन्निव भारत॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, the greatly powerful Bhima smilingly caught in his left hand the tree hurled in anger (by the Rakshasas.)

sn: ततः स पुनरुद्यम्य वृक्षान् बहुविधान् बली। प्राहिणोद् भीमसेनाय तस्मै भीमश्च पाण्डवः॥
en: Then that mighty Rakshasas tearing up various trees, hurled them at Bhima and that Pandava also (hurled) many on the Rakshasas.

sn: तद् वृक्षयुद्धमभवन्महीरुहविनाशनम्। घोररूपं महाराज नरराक्षसराजयोः॥
en: O great king, the fight between the man and the Rakshasas with trees became devoid of all trees.

sn: नाम विश्राव्य तु बकः समभिदुत्य पाण्डवम्। भुजाभ्यां परिजग्राह भीमसेनं महाबलम्॥
en: Saying that 'He is no other than Baka,' he sprang upon the Pandava and clasped the greatly powerful Bhima by both his arms.

sn: भीमसेनोऽपि तद् रक्षः परिरभ्य महाभुजः। विस्फुरन्तं बलाद्
en: Bhimasena also clasped the Rakshasas by his strong arms. The mighty hero began to drag him violently.

sn: स कृष्यमाणो भीमेन कर्षमाणश्च पाण्डवम्। समयुज्यत तीव्रण क्लमेन पुरुषादकः॥
en: Being dragged by Bhima and dragging Bhima also, the cannibal was gradually overcome with great fatigue.

sn: तयोर्वेगेन महता पृथिवी समकम्पत। पादपांश्च महाकायांचूर्णयामासतुस्तदा॥
en: The earth trembled in consequence of their great strength and large trees that stood there were broken to pieces.

sn: महाबाहुं विचकर्ष बली॥ हीयमानं तु तद् रक्षः समीक्ष्य पुरुषादकम्। निष्पिप्य भूमौ जानुभ्यां समाजघ्ने वृकोदरः॥
en: Seeing that the cannibal was overcome with fatigue, Vrikodara pressed him down on the earth with his knees and he then began to strike him with great force.

sn: ततोऽस्य जानुना पृष्ठमवपीड्य बलादिव। बाहुना परिजग्राह दक्षिणेन शिरोधराम्॥ सव्येन च कटीदेशे गृह्य वाससि पाण्डवः। तद् रक्षो द्विगुणं चक्रे रुवन्तं भैरवं रवम्॥
en: Then placing one knee on the middle of his back, Bhima seized his neck with his right hand and his waist cloth with his left; he then broke him into two with great force. He (the cannibal) then uttered a fearful yell.

sn: ततोऽस्य रुधिरं वक्त्रात् प्रादुरासीद् विशाम्पते। भज्यमानस्य भीमेन तस्य घोरस्य रक्षसः॥
en: O Vishampata, then the Rakshasas, when he was thus fearfully broken by Bhima, vomited blood.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततः स भग्नपार्वाङ्गो नदित्वा भैरवं रवम। शैलराजप्रतीकाशो. गतासुरभवद् बकः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Baka, huge as a mountain, being thus broken by Bhima, died uttering fearful yells.

sn: तेन शब्देन वित्रस्तो जनस्तस्याथ रक्षसः। निष्पपात गृहाद् राजन् सहैव परिचारिभः॥ तान् भीतान् विगतज्ञानान् भीमः प्रहरतां वरः। सान्त्वयामास बलवान् समये च न्यवेशयत्॥ न हिंस्या मानुषा भूयो युष्माभिरिति कर्हिचित्। हिंसतां हि वधः शीघ्रमेवमेव भवेदिति॥
en: O king, terrified by that noise, the relatives of that Rakshasas with their attendants came out of their houses. Seeing them terrified and deprived of reason, that best of all wielders of arms, the strong Bhima, comforted them and made them promise (to give up cannibalism.) Bhima said: Do not again kill men. If you do it, you will be killed like this (Baka).

sn: तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा तानि रक्षांसि भारत। एवमस्त्विति तं प्राहुर्जगृहुः समयं च तम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : C descendant of Bharata, hearing his these words, those Rakshasas gave the desired promise by saying "Be it so."

sn: ततः प्रभृति रक्षांसि तत्र सौम्यानि भारत। नगरे प्रत्यदृश्यन्त नरनगरवासिभिः॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, from that day the people inhabiting that town saw the Rakshasas vary peaceful towards mankind.

sn: ततो भीमस्तमादाय गतासुं पुरुषादकम्। द्वारदेशे विनिक्षिप्य जगामानुपलक्षितः॥
en: Then Bhima took the dead cannibal and placed him at one of the gates (of the city) unobserved by anyone, he then went away.

sn: दृष्ट्वा भीमबलोद्भूतं बकं विनिहतं तदा। ज्ञातयोऽस्य भयोद्विग्नाः प्रतिजग्मुस्ततस्ततः॥
en: Seeing Baka killed by Bhima and his extraordinary strength, the kinsmen (of the Rakshasas) became frightened and ran away in different directions.

sn: ततः स भीमस्तं हत्वा गत्वा ब्राह्मणवेश्म तत्। आचचक्षे यथावृतं राज्ञः सर्वमशेषतः॥
en: Then Bhima, thus killing him (Baka), returned to the house of the Brahmana and described to the prince (Yudhisthira) in detail all that had happened.

sn: ततो नरा विनिष्क्रान्ता नगरात् कल्यमेव तु। ददृशुनिहतं भूमौ राक्षसं रुधिरोक्षितम्॥
en: The next morning the inhabitants of the town, in coming out, saw the Rakshasas lying dead on the ground, his body covered with blood.

sn: तमद्रिकूटसदृशं विनिकीर्णं भयानकम्। दृष्ट्वा संहृष्टरोमाणो बभूवुस्तत्र नागराः॥
en: The citizens' hair stood on end when they saw the fearful cannibal, as huge as a mountain cliff.

sn: एकचक्रां ततो गत्वा प्रवृत्तिं प्रददुः पुरे। ततः सहस्रशो राजन् नरा नगरवासिनः॥ तत्राजग्मुर्बकं दुष्टं सस्त्रीवृद्धकुमारकाः। ततस्ते विस्मिताः सर्वे कर्म दृष्ट्वातिमानुषम्। दैवतान्यर्चयांचक्रुः सर्व एव विशाम्पते॥
en: Going to Ekachakra, they soon gave the intelligence; thereupon, O king, thousands of the citizens. Accompanied by their wives both young and old, (all) went there to see Baka. They were all astonished at seeing the superhuman feat. O king they began to worship the gods.

sn: ततः प्रगणयामासुः कस्य वारोऽद्य भोजने। ज्ञात्वा चागम्य तं विप्रं पप्रच्छुः सर्व एव ते॥
en: They then began to calculate whose turn was to supply food (to the Rakshasas) on the previous day. Ascertaining this, they all came to that Brahmana and asked him (if he knew any thing about the matter).

sn: एवं पृष्टः स बहुशो रक्षमाणश्च पाण्डवान्। उवाच नागरान् सर्वानिदं विप्रर्षभस्तदा॥
en: Having been thus repeatedly asked by them that best of Brahmanas thus spoke to all the citizens in order to conceal the Pandavas.

sn: आज्ञापितं मामशने रुदन्तं सह बन्धुभिः। ददर्श ब्राह्मणः कश्चिन्मन्त्रसिद्धो महामनाः॥
en: Seeing me weeping with my friends when I was ordered to supply the food (for the Rakshasas ), a high-minded Brahmana, learned in Mantras, saw me.

sn: परिपृच्छ्य स मां पूर्वं परिक्लेशं पुरस्य च। अब्रवीद् ब्राह्मणश्रेष्ठो विश्वास्य प्रहसन्निव॥ प्रापयिष्याम्यहं तस्मा अन्मेतद् दुरात्मने। मन्निमित्तं भयं चापि न कार्यमिति चाब्रवीत्॥
en: Asking me the cause and knowing the calamity that hangs over the town, that best of Bra' manas ga e me every assurance and spoke to me with smiles, “I shall today carry the food to that wicked-minded wretch. "Do not fear for me." He said this.

sn: स तदन्नमुपादाय गतो बकवनं प्रति। तेन नूनं भवेदेतत् कर्म लोकहितं कृतम्॥
en: And taking the food, set out for the forest where Baka lived. This deed, so beneficial to us, must have been done by him.

sn: ततस्ते ब्राह्मणाः सर्वे क्षत्रियाश्च सुविस्मितः। वैश्याः शूद्राश्च मुदिताश्चक्रुर्ब्रह्ममहं तदा।॥
en: Thereupon all the Brahmanas and Kshatriyas became exceedingly astonished and the Vaishyas and Shudras became exceedingly glad.

sn: ततो जानपदाः सर्वे आजग्मुर्नगरं प्रति। तदद्भुततमं द्रष्टुं पार्थास्तत्रैव चावसन्॥
en: Thereupon all the citizens returned to the city after seeing that extraordinary feat. The Pandavas also lived there.

sn: जनमेजय उवाच ते तथा पुरुषव्याघ्रा निहत्य बकराक्षसम्। अत ऊर्ध्वं ततो ब्रह्मन् किमकुर्वत पाण्डवाः॥
en: Janamejaya said : O Brahmana, what did those best of men, the Pandavas, do after they had killed the, Rakshasas Baka.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तत्रैव न्यवसन् राजन् निहत्य बकराक्षसम्। अधीयानाः परं ब्रह्म ब्राह्मणस्य निवेशने॥
en: O king, after killing the Rakshasas Baka, they lived in the house of that Brahmana engaged in the study of the Vedas.

sn: ततः कतिपयाहस्य ब्राह्मणः संशितव्रतः। प्रतिश्रयार्थी तद् वेश्म ब्राह्मणस्य जगाम ह॥
en: A few days after, a Brahmana of rigid Vows came to the house of the Brahmana in order to live there.

sn: स सम्यक् पूजयित्वा तं विप्रं विप्रर्षभस्तदा। ददौ प्रतिश्रयं तस्मै सदा सर्वातिथिव्रतः॥
en: That best of Brahmanas, ever hospitable to hosts, after duly worshipping him, in his house, gave him quarters to live.

sn: ततस्ते पाण्डवाः सर्वे सह कुन्त्या नरर्षभाः। उपासांचक्रिरे विप्रं कथयन्तं कथा: शुभाः॥
en: Then all those, O best of men, the Pandavas, with Kunti requested the Brahmanas to narrate his interesting experiences.

sn: कथयामास देशांश्च तीर्थानि सरितस्तथा। राज्ञश्च विविधाश्चर्यान् देशांश्चैव पुराणि च॥
en: He spoke to them of various countries, pilgrimages, rivers, kingdoms, many wonderful provinces cities.

sn: स तत्राकथयन् विप्रः कथान्ते जनमेजय। पञ्चालेष्वद्भुताकारं याज्ञसेन्याः स्वयंवरम्॥ धृष्टद्युम्नस्य चोत्पत्तिमुत्पत्तिं च शिखण्डिनः। अयोनिजत्वं कृष्णाया द्रुपदस्य महामखे॥
en: O Janamejaya, when the narrations were over, that Brahmanas spoke to them of the wonderful Svayamvara of the daughter of Yajnasena, the princess of Panchala and the births of Dhrishtadyumna and Shikhandi and that of Krishna, born of no woman, in the sacrifice of Drupada.

sn: तदद्भुततमं श्रुत्वा लोके तस्य महात्मनः। विस्तरेणैव पप्रच्छुः कथान्ते पुरुषर्षभाः॥
en: When he concluded, those best of men (the Pandavas) hearing of these extraordinary affairs asked him to narrate it in detail.

sn: पाण्डवा ऊचुः कथं दुपदपुत्रस्य धृष्टद्युम्नस्य पावकात्। वेदीमध्याच्च कृष्णायाः सम्भवः कथमद्भुतः॥
en: The Pandavas said : O Brahmana, how did the birth of Dhrishtadyumna, the son of Drupada, take place from the (sacrificial) fire?

sn: कथं द्रोणान्महेष्वासात् सर्वाण्यस्त्राण्यशिक्षत। कथं विप्र सखायौ तौ भिन्नौ कस्य कृतेन वा॥
en: How did the wonderful birth of Krishna take place from the (sacrificial) after? How did (the sons of Drupada) learn all weapons from the great bowman Drona? How and for whom and for what reason was the friendship between Drona and Drupada broken?

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवं तैश्चोदितो राजन् स विप्रः पुरुषर्षभैः। कथयामास तत् सर्व द्रौपदीसम्भवं तदा॥
en: Vaishampayana said : O king, having been thus asked by those best of men, the Brahmana narrated in detail the account of the birth of Draupadi.

sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच गङ्गाद्वारं प्रति महान् बभूवर्षिर्महातपाः। भरद्वाजो महाप्राज्ञः सततं संशितव्रतः॥
en: The Brahmana said : There lived at the source of the Gangas a great Rishi of rigid vows and great wisdom and of severest austerities; his name was Bharadvaja.

sn: सोऽभिषेक्तं गतो गङ्गां पूर्वमेवागतां सतीम्। ददर्शाप्सरसं तत्र घृताचीमाप्लुतामृषिः॥
en: One day when the Rishi came to the Ganges to perform his ablutions, he saw the Apsara Gritachi who came before him and who now stood there after her ablutions.

sn: तस्या वायुर्नदीतीरे वसनं व्यहरत् तदा। अपकृष्टाम्बरां दृष्ट्वा तामृषिश्चकमे तदा॥
en: A wind rose on the banks of the river and made the cloth of the Apsara) fall from her body. Seeing her nude, the Rishi was filled with desire.

sn: तस्यां संसक्तमनसः कौमारब्रह्मचारिणः। चिरस्य रेतश्चस्कन्द तदृषिोण आदधे॥
en: He was a Brahmachari from his boyhood and (therefore) as soon as his mind felt the influence of desire, his vital fluid dropped down. The Rishi held it in a Drona (water-pot).

sn: तत समभवद् द्रोणः कुमारस्तस्य धीमतः। अध्यगीष्ट स वेदांश्च वेदाङ्गानि च सर्वशः॥
en: From that pot was born a son, the learned Drona and he studied all the Vedas and the Vedangas.

sn: भरद्वाजस्य तु सखा पृषतो नाम पार्थिवः। तस्यापि दुपदो नाम तदा समभवत् सुतः॥
en: Bharadvaja had a friend, who was a king by the name of Prishata. He had a son, called Drupada.

sn: स नित्यमाश्रमं गत्वा द्रोणेन सह पार्षतः। चिक्रीडाध्ययनं चैव चकार क्षत्रियर्षभः॥
en: That son of Prishata, that best of the Kshatriyas, went daily to the hermitage and played and studies with Drona.

sn: ततस्तु पृषतेऽतीते स राजा द्रुपदोऽभवत्। द्रोणोऽपि रामं शुश्राव दित्सन्तं वसु सर्वशः॥ वनं तु प्रस्थितं रामं भरद्वाजसुतोऽब्रवीत्। आगतं वित्तकामं मां विद्धि द्रोणं द्विजोत्तम॥
en: After Prishata's death, Draupada succeeded him as king. (About this time) Drona heard that (Parashu) Rama was going to distribute away all his wealth. Going from the forest, the son of Bharadvaja (Drona) thus spoke to Rama, O excellent Brahmana, know me to be Drona. I have come for obtaining wealth.

sn: राम उवाच शरीरमात्रमेवाद्य मया समवशेषितम्। अस्त्राणि वा शरीरं वा ब्रह्मन्नेकतमं वृणु॥
