en: Rama said: O Brahmana, after giving away all I have now left only my body. Ask from me either my body or weapons.

sn: द्रोण उवाच अस्त्राणि चैव सर्वाणि तेषां संहारमेव च। प्रयोगं चैव सर्वेषां दातुमर्हति मे भवान्॥
en: Drona said : You should give me all your weapons cugether with the knowledge of hurling and recalling them.

sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच तथेत्युक्त्वा ततस्तस्मै प्रददौ भृगुनन्दनः। प्रतिगृह्य तदा द्रोणः कृतकृत्योऽभवत् तदा॥
en: The Brahmana said: Saying “Be it so", the descendant of Bhrigu gave him (the weapons) and having received them, Drona considered himself crowned with success.

sn: सम्प्रहृष्टमना द्रोणो रामात् परमसम्मतम्। ब्रह्मास्त्रं समनुप्राप्य नरेष्वभ्यधिकोऽभवत्॥
en: Obtaining from Rama that great weapon called Brahmastra, Drona became exceeding glad and acquired superiority over all men.

sn: ततो द्रुपदमासाद्य भारद्वाजः प्रतापवान्। अब्रवीत् पुरुषव्याघ्रः सखायं विद्धि मामिति॥
en: Thereupon that powerful son of Bharadvaja went to that best of men Draupada and said, “Know me to be your friend."

sn: दुपद उवाच नाश्रोत्रियः श्रोत्रियस्य नारथी रथिनः सखा। नाराजा पार्थिवस्यापि सखिपूर्वं किमिष्यते॥
en: Drupada said : One of low birth can never be the friend of one whose lineage is pure. He who is not a carwarrior can never be the friend of one who is; he who is not a king can never be a friend one who is. Therefore why do you desire (to revived) our old friendship?

sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच स विनिश्चित्य मनसा पाञ्चाल्यं प्रति बुद्धिमान्। जगाम कुरुमुख्यानां नगरं नागसाह्वयम्॥
en: The Brahmana said: Being determined to humiliate the Panchala king, that intelligent man (Drona) went to the city of Hastinapur, the capital of the Kurus.

sn: तस्मै पौत्रान् समादाय वसूनि विविधानि च। प्राप्ताय प्रददौ भीष्मः शिष्यान् द्रोणाय धीमते॥
en: Thereupon Bhishma, taking with him his grandsons with much wealth, offered them to he intelligent Drona as his pupil.

sn: द्रोण: शिष्यांस्ततः पार्थानिदं वचनमब्रवीत्। समानीय तु ताशिष्यान् दुपदस्यासुखाय वै॥
en: With the intention of humiliating Draupada, Drona called together all his pupil and he spoke thus to them and to the sons of Kunti.

sn: आचार्यवेतनं किंचिद्धृदि यद् वर्तते मम। कृतास्त्रैस्तत् प्रदेयं स्यात् तदृतं वदतानघाः। सोऽर्जुनप्रमुखैरुक्तस्तथास्त्विति गुरुस्तदा॥
en: O sinless eyes, when you will be all experts in arms, you must give me as the preceptorial fee that which I cherish in my heart.” Arjuna and others said to the preceptor, "Be it so."

sn: यदा च पाण्डवाः सर्वे कृतास्त्राः कृतनिश्चयाः। ततो द्रोणोऽब्रवीद् भूयो वेतनार्थमिदं वचः॥
en: When all the Pandavas became experts in arms and sure in aim, then Drona thus spoke demanding his preceptorial fee.

sn: पार्षतो दुपदो नामच्छत्रवत्यां नरेश्वरः। तस्मादाकृष्य तद् राज्यं मम शीघ्रं प्रदीयताम्॥
en: Drona said: The son of Prishata, Drupada is the king of Chatravati. Take from him that kingdom and bestow it soon on me.

sn: ततः पाण्डुसुताः पञ्च निर्जित्य द्रुपदं युधि। द्रोणाय दर्शयामासुर्बद्ध्वा ससचिवं तदा।॥
en: The Brahmana said : Then the five sons of Pandu defeated Drupada in battle and taking him prisoner along with his ministers, they offered him to Drona.

sn: द्रोण उवाच प्रार्थयामि त्वया सख्यं पुनरेव नराधिप। अराजा किल नो राज्ञः सखा भवितुमर्हति॥ अतः प्रयतितं राज्ये यज्ञसेन त्वया सह। राजासि दक्षिणे कूले भागीरथ्याहमुत्तरे॥
en: Drona said: O king, I again solicit your friendship. He who is not a king should not be a friend of a king. Therefore, O Yajnasena, I shall divide this kingdom amongst ourselves. You will be the king of the country lying on the south banks of the Bhagirathi and I shall be that on the north banks.

sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच एवमुक्तो हि पाञ्चाल्यो भारद्वाजेन धीमता। उवाचास्त्रविदां श्रेष्ठो द्रोणं ब्राह्मणसत्तमम्॥ एवं भवतु भद्रं ते भारद्वाज महामते। सख्यं तदेव भवतु शश्वद् यदभिमन्यसे॥
en: The Brahmana said: Being thus addressed by the intelligent son of Bharadvaja, the Panchala king spoke thus to that excellent Brahmana, that best of all wielders of arms Drona, "O high-souled son of Bharadvaja, be blessed. Let it be. Let there be everlasting friendship between us as you desire."

sn: एवमन्योन्यमुक्त्वा तौ कृत्वा सख्यमनुत्तमम्। जग्मतुर्दोणपाञ्चाल्यौ यथागतमरिंदमौ॥
en: Thus addressing each other and establishing excellent friendship between themselves, Drona and the Panchala king those two chastisers of foes, went away to the place whence they came.

sn: असत्कारः स तु महान् मुहूर्तमपि तस्य तु। नापैति हृदयाद् राज्ञो दुर्मनाः स कृशोऽभवत्॥
en: The thought of that humiliation didnot (however) leave the king's mind for a single moment. Being miserable in mind, the king wasted away.

sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच अमर्षी दुपदो राजा कर्मसिद्धान् द्विजर्षभान्। अन्विच्छन् परिचक्राम ब्राह्मणावसथान् बहून्॥
en: The Brahmana said : Sorrowful in mind and afflicted with grief, the king Drupada wandered among the hermitages of many Brahmanas, all experts in sacrificial rites.

sn: पुत्रजन्म परीप्सन् वै शोकोपहतचेतनः। नास्ति श्रेष्ठमपत्यं मे इति नित्यमचिन्तयत्॥
en: Afflicted with grief and eagerly desirous of offspring, the daily thought, "Alas! I have no excellent son."

sn: जातान् पुत्रान् स निर्वेदाद् धिग् बन्धूनिति चाब्रवीत् निःश्वासपरमश्चासीद् द्रोणं प्रतिचिकीर्षया॥
en: He always said in despondency, "Fie on those children and relatives that I have!" He always sighed thinking of revenging himself of Drona.

sn: प्रभावं विनयं शिक्षा द्रोणस्य चरितानि च। क्षात्रेण च बलेनास्य चिन्तयन् नाध्यगच्छत्॥ प्रतिकर्तुं नृपश्रेष्ठो यतमानोऽपि भारत। अभितः सोऽथ कल्माषीं गङ्गाकूले परिभ्रमन्॥ ब्राह्मणावसथं पुण्यमाससाद महीपतिः। तत्र नास्नातकः कश्चिन्न चासीदव्रती द्विजः॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, even after much deliberation, that best of kings, (Drupada) did not find any means to overcome the prowess, the discipline, the raining and the accomplishments of Drona by his Kshatriya might. Wandering about the king came (at last) to the hermitage of a Brahmana situate on the banks of the holy Gangas. There was no Brahmana who was not a Snataka and none who was not of rigid vows.

sn: तथैव च महाभागः सोऽपश्यत् संशितव्रतौ। याजोपयाजौ ब्रह्मर्षी शाम्यन्तौ परमेष्ठिनौ॥
en: There saw that illustrious king two (Brahmanas) named Yaja and Upayaja, both were of rigid vows, both were self controlled and both belonged to the highest order.

sn: संहिताध्ययने युक्तौ गोत्रतश्चापि काश्यपौ। तारणेयौ युक्तरूपौ ब्राह्मणावृषिसत्तमौ॥
en: They belonged to the race of Kashyapa and they were engaged in studying the Institutes. Those two Brahmana Rishi were quite capable of helping the king.

sn: स तावामन्त्रयामास सर्वकामैरतन्द्रितः। बुद्धवा बलं तयोस्तत्र कनीयांसमुपह्वरे॥ प्रपेदे छन्दयन् कामैरुपयाजं धृतव्रतम्। पादशुश्रूषणे युक्तः प्रियवाक् सर्वकामदः॥ अर्चयित्वा यथान्यायमुपयाजमुवाच सः। येन मे कर्मणा ब्रह्मन् पुत्रः स्याद् द्रोणमृत्यवे॥ उपयाज कृते तस्मिन् गवां दातास्मि तेऽव॒दम्। यद् वा तेऽन्यद् द्विजश्रेष्ठ मनसः सुप्रियं भवेत्। सर्वं तत् ते प्रदाताहं न हि मे मेऽत्रास्ति संशयः॥
en: Having brought his senses under control, he with all earnestness worshipped and served them. Knowing the superiority of the younger of the two. The worshipped in private Upayaja of rigid vows, by offering him every desired object, by serving at his feet and by becoming sweet speeches. Worshipping him in due from, he (Drupada) said to Upayaja, “O Brahmana, if you perform that sacrifice which may give me a son who can kill Drona, O Upayaja, on your doing this, I shall give you ten crore kine. O best of Brahmanas, I am ready to bestow on you whatever else be in your mind and whatever which is agreeable to you. There is no doubt about it.

sn: इत्युक्तो नाहमित्येवं तमृषिः प्रत्यभाषत। आराधयिष्यन् दुपदः स तं पर्यचरत् पुनः॥
en: Having been thus addressed, the Rishi replied to him, “I cannot." Thereupon Drupada again began to worship and serve him.

sn: ततः संवत्सरस्यान्ते द्रुपदं स द्विजोत्तमः। उपयाजोऽब्रवीत् काले राजन् मधुरया गिरा॥ ज्येष्ठो भ्राता ममागृहणाद् विचरन् गहने वने। अपरिज्ञातशौचायां भूमौ निपतितं फलम्॥
en: O king, after the expiration of a year, that best of the twice born, Upayaja, spoke thus to Drupada in sweet words, "My eldest brother while roving in a dense forest took up a fruit that had fallen on the ground, not knowing that it was unclean.

sn: तदपश्यमहं भ्रातुरसाम्प्रतमनुव्रजन्। विमर्श संकरादाने नायं कुर्यात् कदाचन॥
en: I was following him and I saw this unworthy act of my brother. He never scruples to take impure things.

sn: दृष्ट्वा फलस्य नापश्यद् दोषान् पापानुबन्धकान्। विविनक्ति न शौचं यः सोऽन्यत्रापि कथं भवेत्॥
en: In taking that fruit he didnot see any impropriety of a sinful nature. One who does not observe purity (in one thing) is expected not to observe it in other things.

sn: संहिताध्ययनं कुर्वन् वसन् गुरुकुले च यः। भैक्ष्यमुत्सृष्टमन्येषां भुङ्क्ते स्म च यदा तदा॥ कीर्तयन् गुणमन्नानामघृणी च पुनः पुनः। तं वै फलार्थिनं मन्ये भ्रातरं तर्कचक्षुषा॥
en: When he lived in the preceptor's house reading in the Institutes, he used often to eat without any scruples in his mind the remnants of other people's food. He again and again speaks highly of food; and he has no hatred for anything. Arguing from this I see that he desires for earthly acquisitions.

sn: तं वै गच्छस्व नृपते स त्वां संयाजयिष्यति। जुगुप्समानो नृपतिर्मनसेदं विचिन्तयन्।॥ उपयाजवचः श्रुत्वा याजस्याश्रमभ्यगात्। अभिसम्पूज्य पूजार्हमथ याजमुवाच ह॥ अयुतानि ददान्यष्टौ गवां याजय मां विभो। द्रोणवैराभिसंतप्तं प्रह्लादयितुमर्हसि॥
en: "O king go to him, he will performs sacrifices for you.” Having heard those words of Upayaja, the king, though he entertained a low opinion of Yaja, went to his house. Worshipping him who was worthy of worship, he thus spoke to him, “O lord, I shall give you eighty thousand kine; perform my spatial actions. I am brunt by my feelings of enmity towards Drona. You should cool my heart.

sn: स हि ब्रह्मविदां श्रेष्ठो ब्रह्मास्त्रे चाप्यनुत्तमः। तस्माद् द्रोणः पराजैष्ट मां वै स सखिविग्रहे॥
en: That foremost of men, learned in the Vedas (Drona) is skilled in the Brahma weapon. Therefore, Drona has defeated me in a contest arising out of a quarrel on friendship.

sn: क्षत्रियो नास्ति तस्यास्यां पृथिव्यां कश्चिदग्रणीः। कौरवाचार्यमुख्यस्य भारद्वाजस्य धीमतः॥
en: The greatly intelligent son of Bharadvaja (Drona) is now the chief preceptor of the Kurus. There is no Kshatriya in the world who is superior to him.

sn: द्रोणस्य शरजालानि प्राणिदेहहराणि च। षडरनि धनुश्चास्य दृश्यते परमं महत्॥ स हि ब्राह्मणवेषेण क्षात्रं वेगमसंशयम्। प्रतिहन्ति महेष्वासो भारद्वाजो महामनाः॥
en: His arrows are capable of killing every living being, his bow is full six cubits long and it looks exceedingly great. That high-souled ' great bowman, that son of Bharadvaja (Drona,) attired in the Brahmanic garb, is destroying the Kshatriya might.

sn: क्षत्रोच्छेदाय विहितो जामदग्न्य इवास्थितः। तस्य ह्यस्त्रबलं घोरमप्रधृष्यं नरैर्भुवि॥
en: Like the son of Jamadagni, Parshurama, he is engaged in annihilating the Kshatriyas. There is no man on earth who can overcome the terrible force of his arms.

sn: ब्राह्यं संधारयंस्तेजो हुताहुतिरिवानलः। समेत्य स दहत्याजौ क्षात्रधर्मपुरस्सरः॥
en: Like blazing fire fed with ghee, Drona, possessing both the Brahma inight and the Kshatriya might consumes every antagonist in battle.

sn: ब्रह्मक्षत्रे च विहिते ब्राह्म तेजो विशिष्यते। सोऽहं क्षात्राद् बलाद्धीनो ब्राह्मं तेजः प्रपेदिवान्॥
en: Your Brahma might is superior to his Brahma might though his is amited with his Kshatriya might. As I am interior (to Drona) in consequence of my having only Kshatriya might, therefore, give me your Brahma might.

sn: द्रोणाद् विशिष्टमासाद्य भवन्तं ब्रह्मवित्तमम्। द्रोणान्तकमहं पुत्रं लभेयं युधि दुर्जयम्॥ तत् कर्म कुरु मे याज वितराम्यर्बुदं गवाम्। तथेत्युक्त्वा तु तं याजो याज्यार्थमुपकल्पयत्॥
en: As I have got you who is superior to Drona in Brahma might, O Yaja, perform that sacrifice by which I can obtain a son, who is invincible and who can kill Drona in battle. I am ready to give you ten crore kine.” Saying, "Be it so," Yaja recollected the various particulars of the sacrifice in question.

sn: गुर्वर्थ इति चाकाममुपयाजमचोदयत्। याजो द्रोणविनाशाय प्रतिजज्ञे तथा च सः॥ ततस्तस्य नरेन्द्रस्य उपयाजो महातपाः। भाचख्यौ कर्म वैतानं तदा पुत्रफलाय वै॥
en: Knowing the gravity of the matter, he asked the assistance of Upayaja who covered nothing. Then Yaja promised to perform the sacrifice for the destruction of Drona. Thereupon the great ascetic Upayaja spoke to the king (Drupada) all that is required for the sacrifice from which the king was to obtain offspring.

sn: स च पुत्रो महावीर्यो महातेजा महाबलः। इष्यते यद्धिधो राजन् भविता ते तथाविधः॥
en: Upayaja said: O king, a son will be born to you who will possess, as you desire. great prowess, great energy and great strength.

sn: भारद्वाजस्य हन्तारं सोऽभिसंधाय भूपतिः। आजहें तत् तथा सर्वं द्रुपदः कर्मसिद्धये॥
en: The Brahmana said : Then king Drupada, being desirous of obtaining a son who was to slay the son of Bharadvaja (Drona) began to make the necessary preparations for the success of his wish.

sn: याजस्तु हवनस्यान्ते देवीमाज्ञापयत् तदा। प्रेहि मां राज्ञि पृषति मिथुनं त्वामुपस्थितम्॥
en: Yaja then poured libations of ghee on the sacrificial fire and ordered the queen thus, “O daughter-in-law of Prishata, come here a son and a daughter have come for you.

sn: राज्युवाच अवलिप्तं मुखं ब्रह्मन् दिव्यान् गन्धान बिभर्मिच। सुतार्थे नोपलब्धास्मि तिष्ठ याज मम प्रिये॥
en: The Queen said: O Brahmana, my mouth is filled with saffron and other perfumes; my body bears many sweet scents; I am not now fit for accepting the sacrificial ghee which would give me offspring. O Yaja, wait for me a little, for that happy consummation.

sn: याज उवाच याजेन श्रपितं हव्यमुपयाजाभिमन्त्रितम्। कथं कामं न संदध्यात् सा त्वं विप्रेहि तिष्ठ वा॥
en: Yaja said : Whether you come or wait, why should not the object of this sacrifice be accomplished when the oblation has already been prepared by me and sanctified by Upayaja's invocations!

sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच एवमुक्त्वा तु याजेन हुते हविषि संस्कृते। उत्तस्थौ पावकात् तस्मात् कुमारो देवसंनिभः॥
en: The Brahmana said: Having said this, the sacrificial priest (Yaja) poured the sanctified libation on the fore, whereupon arose from those flames a celestials like boy.

sn: ज्वालावर्णो घोररूपः किरीटी वर्म चोत्तमम्। बिभ्रत् सखङ्गः सशरो धनुष्मान् विनदन् मुहुः॥
en: He was as effulgent as the fire; he was terrible to look at; he had a crown on his head; and his body was encased in an excellent armour; he had a sword in his hand, carried a bow and arrows and he frequently sent forth loud roars.

sn: सोऽध्यारोहद् रथवरं तेन च प्रययौ तदा। ततः प्रणेदुः पञ्चालाः प्रहृष्टाः साधु साध्विति॥
en: As soon as he was born, he got on an excellent car and went about. Thereupon the Panchalas should in great joy “Blessed, blessed."

sn: हर्षाविष्टांस्ततश्चैतान् नेयं सेहे वसुंधरा। भयापहो राजपुत्रः पाञ्चालानां यशस्करः॥ राज्ञः शोकापहो जात एष द्रोणवधाय वै। इत्युवाच महद् भूतमदृश्यं खेचरं तदा॥
en: The very earth appeared to be unable to bear the weight of the madly joyous Panchalas. “The price has been born for the destruction of Drona. He will dispel all the fears of the Panchalas and spread their fame. He will also remove the grief of the king.” Thus said the greatly wonderful voice of the sky managing beings.

sn: कुमारी चापि पाञ्चाली वेदमिध्यात् समुत्थिता। सुभगा दर्शनीयाङ्गी स्वसितायतलोचनाः॥ श्यामा पद्मपलाशाक्षी नीलकुञ्चितमूर्धजा। ताम्रतुङ्गनखी सुभ्रूश्चारुपीनपयोधरा॥
en: There rose from the (sacrificial alter) a daughter, called Panchali, who was blessed with good fortune; she was beautiful her eyes were smiling and large. Her complexion was dark, her eyes were like lotus leaves, her hair was blue and curly, her nails were beautifully carved and they were like bright copper, her eyebrows were fair, her breasts were rising and her things tapering.

sn: मानुषं विग्रहं कृत्वा साक्षादमरवर्णिनी। नीलोत्पलसमो गन्धो यस्याः क्रोशात् प्रधावति॥
en: She was veritable celestials maiden born among men. The sweet fragrance of the blue lotus emitted from her body and it was perceptible from a distance of full two miles,

sn: या बिभर्ति परं रूपं यस्या नास्त्युपमा भुवि। देवदानवयक्षाणामीप्सितां देवरूपिणीम्॥
en: Her beauty was such that she had no equal on earth. The Devas, the Danavas and the Yakshas could desire that celestials like beauty.

sn: तां चापि जातां सुश्रोणी वागुवाचाशरीरिणी। सर्वयाषिद्वरा कृष्णा निनीषुः क्षत्रियान् क्षयम्॥
en: When this beauty of fair hips was born, an invisible voice said, “This beauty of dark complexion will be the cause of the women and she will be the cause of the destruction of the Kshatriyas.

sn: सुरकार्यमियं काले करिष्यति सुमध्यमा। अस्या हेतोः कौरवाणां महदुत्पत्स्यते भयम्॥
en: "This lady of slender waist will in time accomplish the works of gods. From her will arise many fears (dangers) to the Kurus."

sn: तच्छ्रुत्वा सर्वपाञ्चालाः प्रणेदुः सिंहसङ्घवत्। न चैतान् हर्षसम्पूर्णानियं सेहे वसुंधरा॥
en: Hearing this all the Panchalas uttered a loud leonine roars. The earth was unable to bear the weight of the madly joyous Panchalas.

sn: तौ दृष्ट्वा पार्षती याज प्रपेदे वै सुतार्थिनी। न वै मदन्यां जननी जानीयातामिमाविति॥
en: The daughter-in-law of Prishata, seeing the two (the boy and the daughter) and being desirous of getting them, came to Yaja and said, “Let not these two know anyone else except myself as their mother."

sn: तथेत्युवाच तं याजो राज्ञः प्रियचिकीर्षया। तयोश्च नामनी चक्रुद्धिजाः सम्पूर्णमानसाः॥
en: Desiring to do good to the king (Drupada) Yaja said, “Be it so." Thereupon the Brahmanas whose wishes were completely gratified (by present) gave these two (children) names.

sn: धृष्टत्वादत्यमर्षित्वाद् द्युम्नाद्युत्सम्भवादपि। धृष्टद्युम्नः कुमारोऽयं दुपदस्य भवत्विति॥
en: (They said,) “Because this son of Drupada possesses excessive audacity and because he has been born like Dyumna with a natural armour of weapons, let him be called Dhrishtadyumna.

sn: कृष्णेत्येबाब्रुवन् कृष्णां कृष्णाभूत् सा हि वर्णतः। तथा तन्मिथुनं जज्ञे द्रुपदस्य महामखे।॥
en: Because this daughter is dark in complexion, let her be called Krishna.” Thus were born the son and daughter of Drupada in the great sacrifice.

sn: धृष्टद्युम्नं तु पाञ्चाल्यमानीय स्वं निवेशनम्। उपाकरोदस्त्रहेतोर्भारद्वाजः प्रतापवान्॥ अमोक्षणीयं दैवं हि भावि मत्वा महामतिः। तथा तत् कृतवान् द्रोण आत्मकीर्त्यनुरक्षणात्॥
en: Then Drona brought the Panchala prince Dhrishtadyumna to his own house and taught him all weapons as a requital of taking the half of the kingdom of Drupada. Regarding Destiny to be inevitable, the illustrious son of Bharadvaja did what would perpetuate his own deeds.

sn: वैशंपायन उवाच एतच्छ्रुत्वा तु कौन्तेया ब्राह्मणात् संशितव्रतात्। सर्वे चास्वस्थमनसो बभूवुस्ते महाबलाः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having heard this, son of Kunti appeared as if they were pieced with darts. Those mighty men lost their peace of mind.

sn: ततः कुन्ती सुतान् दृष्ट्वा सर्वास्तद्गतचेतसः। युधिष्ठिरमुवाचेदं वचनं सत्यवादिनी॥
en: Thereupon that truthful lady Kunti, seeing all his son's minds are in great anxiety, thus spoke to Yudhishthira.

sn: कुन्त्युवाच चिररात्रोषिताः स्मेह ब्राह्मणस्य निवेशने। रममाणाः पुरे रम्ये लब्धभैक्षा महात्मनः॥
en: Kunti said: We have now lived for many nights in the abode of this Brahmana; we have very pleasantly passed in this beautiful city, living on the alms of many high-souled men.

sn: यानीह रमणीयानि वनान्युपवनानि च। सर्वाणि तानि दृष्टानि पुनः पुनररिंदम॥
en: O chastiser of foes, we have seen again and again all the beautiful woods and forests in this part of the country.

sn: पुनर्द्रष्टुं हि तानीह प्रीणयन्ति न नस्तथा। भैक्षं च न तथा वीर लभ्यते कुरुनन्दन।॥
en: To see them again would give us no pleasure. O heroic descendant of Kuru, alms are not so easily obtainable now as before.

sn: ते वयं साधु पञ्चालान् गच्छाम यदि मन्यसे। अपूर्वदर्शनं वीर रमणीयं भविष्यति॥
en: O blessed one, if you wish to go to Panchala, let us go there. O hero, we have not seen it before it must be beautiful.

sn: सुभिक्षाश्चैव पञ्चालाः श्रूयन्ते शत्रुकर्शन। यज्ञसेनश्च राजासौ ब्रह्मण्य इति शुश्रुम॥
en: O destroyer of foes, we have heard that alms are easily obtainable in Panchala and the king Yajnasena is devoted to the Brahmanas.

sn: एकत्र चिरवासश्च क्षमो न च मतो मम। ते तत्र साधु गच्छामो यदि त्वं पुत्र मन्यसे॥
en: It is not my opinion that one should live long in one place. Therefore, O son, if you like it is well for us to go there.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच भवत्या यन्मतं कार्यं तदस्माकं परं हितम्। अनुजांस्तु न जानामि गच्छेयुर्नेति वा पुनः॥
en: Yudhishthira said: That which is your opinion and command is (always) to our great good. (But) I do not know whether my younger brothers are willing togo.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततः कुन्ती भीमसेनमर्जुनं यमजौ तथा। उवाच गमनं ते च तथेत्येवाब्रुवंस्तदा॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Thereupon Kunti spoke to Bhimasena, Arjuna and the twins (Nakula and Sahadeva) about the (proposed) journey and they said, “Be it so."

sn: तत आमन्त्र्य तं विप्रं कुन्ती राजन् सुतैः सह। प्रतस्थे नगरी रम्यां द्रुपदस्य महात्मनः॥
en: O king, then Kunti saluting the Brahmana started for the beautiful city of the illustrious Drupada. Thus ends hundred and sixty eighth chapter, the departure for the Panchala country, in the Chaitraratha of the Adi Parva.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच वसत्सु तेषु प्रच्छन्नं पाण्डवेषु महात्मसु। आजगामाथ तान् द्रष्टुं व्यास: सत्यवतीसुतः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : When the illustrious Pandavas were living in disguise, the son of Satyavati, Vyasa, once came to see them.

sn: तमागतमभिप्रेक्ष्य प्रत्युद्गम्य परंतपाः। प्रणिपत्याभिवाद्यैनं तस्थुः प्राञ्जलयस्तदा॥ समनुज्ञाप्य तान् सर्वानासीनान् मुनिरब्रवीत्। प्रच्छन्नं पूजितः पार्थः प्रीतिपूर्वमिदं वचः॥
en: Seeing him coming, those chastisers of foes advanced and bowed down their heads and worshipped him. Then they stood (before him) with hands. Then they all took their seats at the command (of the Rishi) and the Rishi being thus gratified by the son of Pritha living in disguise, cheerfuily spoke to them thus-

sn: अपि धर्मेण वर्तेध्वं शास्त्रेण च परंतपाः। अपि विप्रेषु पूजा वः पूजार्हेषु न हीयते॥
en: Vyasa said : "O chastisers of foes, are you following the path of virtue and scriptures? Do you worship the Brahmanas? You are not deficient in giving homage to those that deserve homage."

sn: अथ धर्मार्थवद् वाक्यमुक्त्वा स भगवानृषिः। विचित्राश्च कथास्तास्ताः पुनरेवेदमब्रवीत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : That illustrious Rishi thus spoke many worlds of virtuous import. Speaking on various subjects, he again spoke thus-

sn: व्यास उवाच आसीत् तपोवने काचिदृषेः कन्या महात्मनः। विलग्ममध्या सुश्रोणी सुभूः सर्वगुणान्विता॥
en: Vyasa said : There lived in a wood a certain illustrious Rishi who had a daughter of slender waist, fair hips, fine eye-brows and of all accomplishments.

sn: कर्मभिः स्वकृतैः सा तु दुर्भगा समपद्यत। नाध्यगच्छत् पतिं सा तु कन्या रूपवती सती॥
en: As a result of her own actions in her previous birth) she became very unfortunate. That beautiful chaste girl did not get a husband.

sn: ततस्तप्तुमथारेभे पत्यर्थमसुखा ततः। तोषयामास तपसा सा किलोग्रेण शंकरम्॥
en: Thereupon, she began with sorrowful heart to perform austere penances with the object of getting a husband. And she gratified Shankara (Shiva) by her severe ascetic.

sn: तस्या स भगवांस्तुष्टस्तमुवाच यशस्विनीम्। वरं वरय भद्रं ते वरदोऽस्मीति शरूरः॥
en: The high-souled (deity), being thus gratified, spoke thus to the illustrious girl, "ask the boon you desire to have. Be blessed; I am Shankara who is willing to give you a boon."

sn: अथेश्वरमुवाचेदमात्मनः सा वचो हितम्। पतिं सर्वगुणोपेतमिच्छामीति पुनः पुनः॥
en: Being desirous of benefiting herself, she again and again said to the supreme deity, "Give me an accomplished husband."

sn: तामथ प्रत्युवाचेदमीशानो वदतां वरः। पञ्च ते पतयो भद्रे भविष्यन्तीति भारताः॥
en: Then tnat foremost of all great speakers, Ishana (Shiva,) replied to her saying, “O blessed lady, you will have five husbands from among the Bharata princes."

sn: एवमुक्ता ततः कन्या देवं वरदमब्रवीत्। एकमिच्छाम्यहं देव त्वत्प्रसादात् पतिं प्रभो॥
en: Having been thus addressed the maiden thus spoke to the deity who gave her the boon, "O deity, O lord, I desire to have only one husband through your grace.”

sn: पुनरेवाब्रवीद् देव इदं वचनमुत्तमम्। पच्कृत्वस्त्वया ह्युक्तः पतिं देहीत्यहं पुनः॥
en: The deity addressed her again and said these excellent words, “You have said five times, "Give me a husband”.

sn: देहमन्यं गतायास्ते यथोक्तं तद् भविष्यति। दुपदस्य कुले जज्ञे सा कन्या देवरूपिणी॥
en: Therefore, you will have in another life, what I have said now.” That celestials like girl was born in the race of Drupada.

sn: निर्दिष्टा भवतां पत्नी कृष्णा पार्षत्यनिन्दिता। पाञ्चालनगरे तस्मान्निवसध्वं महाबलाः। सुखिनस्तामनुप्राप्य भविष्यथ न संशयः॥
en: That faultless Krishna, the descendant of Prishata; is destined to be the wife of all of you (the five Pandavas). O greatly powerful heroes, go to the city of the Panchalas and live there. There is no doubt you will all be very happy on obtaining her as your wife.

sn: एवमुक्त्वा महाभागः पाण्डवान् स पितामहः। पार्थानामन्त्र्य कुन्ती च प्रातिष्ठत महातपाः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having said this to the Pandavas, that greatly blessed grandfather, the great ascetic, after having been saluted by the sons of Pritha (the Pandavas) and Kunti, went to the place whence he came.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच गते भगवति व्यासे पाण्डवा हृष्टमानसाः। ते प्रतस्थुः पुरस्कृत्य मातरं पुरुषर्षभाः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : When the illustrious Vyasa went away, those best of men, the Pandavas, proceeded with joyous heart, (towards Panchala) placing their mother at the head (of the procession.)

sn: आमन्त्र्य ब्राह्मणं पूर्वमभिवाद्यानुमान्य च। समैरुदडमुखैर्मागैर्यथोद्दिष्टं परंतपाः॥
en: Those chastisers of foes proceeded in a northerly direction in order to reach their destination. They walked day and night and reached (the several) Somashrama.

sn: ते त्वगच्छन्नहोरात्रात् तीर्थं सोमाश्रयायणम्। आसेदुः पुरुषव्याघ्रा गङ्गायां पाण्डुनन्दनाः॥
en: Those best of men, the sons of Pandu, came to (the banks of) the Ganges. The great car-warriors Dhananjaya (Arjuna) walked before, carrying torch in his hand for showing them the way and for protecting them.

sn: उल्मुकं तु समुद्यम्य तेषामग्रे धनंजयः। प्रकाशार्थं ययौ तत्र रक्षार्थं च महारथः॥
en: There is the delightful waters of the Ganges was sporting in solitude the proud king of the Gandharvas (Chitraratha) with his wives.

sn: तत्र गङ्गाजले रम्ये विविक्ते क्रीडयन् स्त्रियः। ईर्युगन्धर्वराजो वै जलक्रीडामुपागतः॥
en: He heard the noise (of the footsteps of the Pandavas) approaching the river. The greatly strong (Gandharva) was inflamed with wrath by (hearing) the noise.

sn: शब्दं तेषां स शुश्राव नदी समुपसर्पताम्। तेन शब्देन चाविष्टश्चक्रोध बलवद् बली॥
en: Seeing there those chastisers of foes, the Pandavas, with their mother and drawing his fearful bow, he spoke thus,

sn: स दृष्ट्वा पाण्डवांस्तत्र सह मात्रा परंतपान्। विस्फारयन् धनुर्घोरमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥ संध्या संरज्यते घोरा पूर्वरात्रगमेषु या। अशीतिभिर्लवैीनं तन्मुहूर्तं प्रचक्षते॥
en: "It is known that excepting the first forty labas of the dark twilight that proceeds night, (the other portion of the night) is set apart for the Yakshas, the Gandharvas and the Rakshasas who are capable of going every where at will. The rest of the time is set apart for men.

sn: विहितं कामचाराणां यक्षगन्धर्वरक्षसाम्। शेषमन्यन्मनुष्याणा कर्मचारेषु वै स्मृतम्॥
en: Therefore, if any man out of greed wander during those moments and come near us, both we, (the Gandharvas) and the Rakshasas kill those fools.

sn: लोभात् प्रचारं चरतस्तासु वेलासु वै नरान्। उपक्रान्तानि गृहणीमो राक्षसैः सह बालिशान्॥
en: The men learned in the Vedas disapprove (the actions of) those men, nay even of the kings at the head of their enemies who come to any lake or river at such a time.

sn: अतो रात्रौ प्राप्नुवन्तो जलं ब्रह्मविदो जनाः। गर्हयन्ति नरान् सर्वान् बलस्थान् नृपतीनपि॥
en: Stay at a distance. Do not come near me. Know you not that I am (now) bathing in the waters of the Bhagirathi.

sn: आरात् तिष्ठत मा मह्यं समीपमुपसर्पत।। कस्मान्मां नाभिजानीत प्राप्तं भागीरथीजलम्॥
en: Know me to be the Gandharva, named Angarparna who depends only on his own strength of arms. I am proud and haughty; I am the friend of Kubera.

sn: अङ्गारपर्णं गन्धर्वं वित्त मां स्वबलाश्रयम्। अहं हि मानी चेर्युश्च कुबेरस्य प्रियः सखा॥
en: This my forest on the banks of the Ganges is known by the name of Angarparna in which I sport to gratify myself.

sn: अङ्गारपर्णमित्येवं ख्यातं चेदं वनं मम। अनुगङ्गं चरन् कामांश्चित्रं यत्र रमाम्यहम्॥
en: The Kapalikas, the Shringis or the Devas, dare not come here it appears you are human beings. How dare you (then) to approach me who is the brightest jewel in Kubera's crown?

sn: न कौणपाः शृङ्गिणो वा न देवा न च मानुषाः। इदं समुपसर्पन्ति तत् किं समनुसर्पथ॥ अर्जुन उवाच समुद्रे हिमवत्पार्श्व नद्यामस्यां च दुर्मते। रात्रावहनि संध्यायां कस्य गुप्तः परिग्रहः॥
en: Arjuna said : O wretch, to whom can the ocean, the sides of the Himalayas, or this river Ganges be barred, whether at night or day or at twilight?

sn: भुक्तो वाप्यथवाभुक्तो रात्रावहनि खेचर। न कालनियमो ह्यस्ति गङ्गां प्राप्य सरिद्वराम्॥
en: O sky ranger, whether the stomach be empty or full, there is no special time to come to this foremost of all rivers, the Ganges, whether it is night or day.

sn: वयं च शक्तिसम्पन्ना अकाले त्वामधृष्णुम्। अशक्ता हि रणे क्रूरयुष्मानन्ति मानवाः॥
en: We are endued with prowess, we care not when, we disturb you. O wicked being, those men that are incapable (of fighting) worship you.

sn: पुरा हिमवतश्चैषा हेमशृङ्गाद् विनिस्सृता। गङ्गा गत्वा समुद्राम्भः सप्तधा समपद्यतः। १९॥
en: This Ganges, issuing out of the golden peaks of the Himalayas, falls into the ocean by seven streams.

sn: गङ्गां च यमुनां चैव प्लक्षजातां सरस्वतीम्। रथस्थां सरयूं चैव गोमती गण्डकी तथा॥
en: (They are) Ganga, Yamuna, Sarasvati, Rathastha, Saraya, Gomti and Gandaki.

sn: अपर्युषितपाषास्ते नदीः सप्त पिबन्ति ये। इयं भूत्वा चैकवप्रा शुचिराकाशगा पुनः॥ देवेषु गङ्गा गन्धर्व प्राप्नोत्यलकनन्दताम्।
en: Those that drink the waters of these seven rivers are cleansed of their sins. O Gandharva, this sacred Ganga, following through the celestials regions, is called there Alaknanda,

sn: तथा पितृन् वैतरणी दुस्तरा पापकर्मभिः। गङ्गा भवति वै प्राप्य कृष्णद्वैपायनोऽब्रवीत्॥ असम्बाधा देवनदी स्वर्गसम्पादनी शुभा। कथमिच्छसि तां रोर्बु नैष धर्मः सनातनः॥
en: And in the region of Pitris, it is called Vaitarani, which is not crossable by the sinners, Krishna Dvaipayana has said that this auspicious and celestials river is accessible at all times by all. Why do you wish to bar us from it? It is not consonant with the eternal virtue.

sn: अनिवार्यमसम्बाधं तव वाचा कथं वयम्। न स्पृशेम यथाकामं पुण्यं भागीरथीजलम्॥
en: Why should we not, disregarding your words, touch at pleasure the sacred waters of the Bhagirathi which is ever accessible to all.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच अङ्गारपर्णस्तच्छ्रुत्वा क्रुद्ध आनप्य कार्मुकम्। मुमोच बाणान् निशितानहीनाशीविषानिव॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Hearing this, Angarparna became very angry and drawing his bow he shot at them his arrows which were like the poisonous snakes.

sn: उल्मुकं भ्रामयंस्तूर्णं पाण्डवश्चर्म चोत्तरम्। व्यपोहत शरांस्तस्य सर्वानेव धनंजयः॥
en: The Pandava Dhananjaya, who had an excellent shield, warded off all those arrows with it and with the torch in his hand.

sn: अर्जुन उवाच विभीषका वै गन्धर्व नास्त्रज्ञेषु प्रयुज्यते। अस्त्रज्ञेषु प्रयुक्तेयं फेनवत् प्रविलीयते॥
en: Arjuna said : O Gandharva, seek not to terrify those who are skilled in weapons, for weapons hurled at them vanish like froth.

sn: मानुषानति गन्धर्वान् सर्वान् गन्धर्व लक्षये। तस्मादस्त्रेण दिव्येन योत्स्येऽहं न तु मायया॥
en: O Gandharva, I know Gandharvas are superior to men (in prowess). I shall therefore fight with you by using the celestials weapons. I shall not use delusions.

sn: पुरास्त्रमिदमाग्नेयं प्रादात् किल बृहस्पतिः। भरद्वाजाय गन्धर्व गुरुर्मान्यः शतक्रतोः॥
en: The fire weapon that I hurl against you was formerly given by the preceptor of Indra, Brihaspati, to Bharadvaja.

sn: भरद्वाजादग्निवेश्यः अग्निवेश्याद् गुरुर्मम। साध्विदं मह्यमददद् द्रोणो ब्राह्मणसत्तमः॥
en: From Bharadvaja, it was obtained by Agnivaishya and from Agnivaishya by my preceptor, and that excellent Brahmana Drona gave it to mc.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच इत्युक्त्वा पाण्डवः क्रुद्धो गन्धर्वाय मुमोच ह। प्रदीप्तमस्त्रमाग्नेयं ददाहास्य रथं तु तत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having said this, the Pandava (Arjuna) angrily hurled at the Gandharva that blazing fire weapon which immediately brunt his chariot.

sn: विरथं विप्लुतं तं तु स गन्धर्वं महाबलः। अस्त्रतेजः प्रमूढ़ च प्रपतन्तमवाङ्मुखम्॥
en: Having fainted away by the force of the weapon, the greatly powerful Gandharva was falling headlong downwards from his chariot,

sn: शिरोरुहेषु जग्राह माल्यवत्सु धनंजयः। भ्रातृन् प्रति चकर्षाथ सोऽस्त्रपातादचेतसम्॥
en: But Dhananjaya sized him by the hair of his head which was adorned with garlands of flowers. He dragged towards his brother that (Gandharva), insonsible in consequence of (being wounded by) the weapon.

sn: युधिष्ठिरं तस्य भार्या प्रपेदे शरणार्थिनी। नाम्ना कुम्भीनसी नाम पतित्राणमभीप्सती॥
en: (Seeing this), his wife, named Kumbhinasi, being desirous of rescuing her husband, came to Yudhishthira and asked his protection.

sn: गन्धर्युवाच त्रायस्व मां महाभाग पतिं चेमं विमुञ्च मे। गन्धर्वी शरणं प्राप्ता नाम्ना कुम्भीनसी प्रभो॥
en: The Gandharvi said : O exalted one, extend your protection to me. Set my husband free. () Lord, I am a Gandharvi, named Kumbhinasi, I ask your protection.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच युद्धे जितं यशोहीनं स्त्रीनाथमपराक्रमम्। को निहन्याद् रिपुं तात मुञ्चेमं रिपुसूदन॥
en: Yudhishthira said : O chastiser of foes, who would kill an enemy who has been vanquished in the battle, who has been deprived of his fame, who is protected by a woman and who is incapable of defending himself), O child, set him free.

sn: अर्जुन उवाच जीवितं प्रतिपद्यस्व गच्छ गन्धर्व मा शुचः। प्रदिशत्यभयं तेऽद्य कुरुराजो युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Arjuna said : O Gandharva, take your life. Go hence and do not grieve. The king of the Kurus, Yudhishthira others me today to show you mercy.

sn: गन्धर्व उवाच जितोऽहं पूर्वकं नाम मुञ्चाम्यङ्गारपर्णताम्। न च श्लाघे बलेनाङ्गन नाम्ना जनसंसदि॥
en: The Gandharva said: I have been defeated by you, therefore, I shall give up my former name of Angarparna. In name only I shall not be boastful when really I am not strong in prowess like men.

sn: साध्विमं लब्धवाँल्लाभं योऽहं दिव्यास्त्रधारिणम्। गान्धर्व्या माययेच्छामि संयोजयितुमर्जुनम्॥
en: It is a great fortune to me that I have obtained a man who wields celestials weapons. I am desirous to impart to Arjuna the power of illusions of the Gandharvas.

sn: अस्त्राग्निना विचित्रोऽयं दग्धो मे रथ उत्तमः। सोऽहं चित्ररथो भूत्वा नाम्ना दग्धरथोऽभवम्॥
en: My excellent and beautiful chariot has been brunt by your fire weapon. I was (formerly) called Chitraratha having a beautiful chariot, I shall now be called Dagdharatha (having the chariot) burnt..

sn: सम्भृता चैव विद्येयं तपसेह मया पुरा। निवेदयिष्ये तामद्य प्राणदाय महात्मने॥
en: The science (of illusion) of which I spoke to you and which I formerly obtained by asceticism will be today given by me to that illustrious man who has given me my life.

sn: संस्तम्भयित्वा तरसा जितं शरणमागतम्। यो रिपुं योजयेत् प्राणैः कल्याणं किं न सोऽर्हति॥४२
en: What good fortune does he not deserve to obtain who after defeating an enemy gives him his life when he asks it from him?

sn: चाक्षुषी नाम विद्येयं यां सोमाय ददौ मनुः। ददौ स विश्वावसवे मम विश्वावसुर्ददौ॥
en: This science is called Chakshushi. It was taught by Manu to Soma. Soma taught it to Vishvavasu, Vishvavasu, taught it to me.

sn: सेयं कापुरुषं प्राप्ता गुरुदत्ता प्रणश्यति। आगमोऽस्या मया प्रोक्तो वीर्यं प्रतिनिबोध मे॥
en: Having been given by the preceptor to one who is a Kapurusha (without energy) it went to die out. I have spoken to you about its coming (origin and transmission); listen now to its prowess.

sn: यच्चक्षुषा द्रष्टुमिच्छेत् त्रिषु लोकेषु किंचन। तत् पश्येद् यादृशं चेच्छेत् तादृशं द्रष्टुमर्हति॥
en: Whatever you will desire to see by your eyes in this world and whatever its nature it will be seen by you (by the help of this science).

sn: एकपादेन षण्मासान् स्थितो विद्यां लभेदिमाम्। अनुनेष्याम्यहं विद्यां स्वयं तुभ्यं व्रतेऽकृते॥
en: One can acquire this (science) by standing on one leg for six months. I shall impart to you this science without your observing any vows.

sn: विद्यया ह्यनया राजन् वयं नृभ्यो विशेषिताः। अविशिष्टाश्च देवानामनुभावप्रदर्शिनः॥
en: O king, (only) on account of this science, we have a superiority over men. Because we are capable of seeing everything (by our spiritual eyes), we are equal to the celestials.

sn: गन्धर्वजानामश्वानामहं पुरुषसत्तम। भ्रातृभ्यस्तव तुभ्यं च पृथग्दाता शतं शतम्॥
en: O excellent man, I desire to give you and your brothers, cach separately, one hundred horses born in the regions of the Gandharvas.

sn: देवगन्धर्ववाहास्ते दिव्यवर्णा मनोजवाः। क्षीणाक्षीणा भवन्त्येते न हीयन्ते च रंहसः॥
en: They are employed in carrying the Devas and the Gandharvas; they are of the celestials colour, and they possess speed as that of the mind. They may be lean and thin in body, but they never feel tired and their speed never suffers for this reason.

sn: पुरा कृतं महेन्द्रस्य वज्रं वृत्रनिबर्हणम्। दशधा शतधा चैव तच्छीर्णं वृत्रमूर्धनि॥
en: The thunder was created by Indra in the days of yore in order to kill Vitra, (but) it broke into a thousand pieces when hurled on Vitra's head.

sn: ततो भागीकृतो देवैर्वज्रभाग उपास्यते। लोके यशो धनं किंचित् सैव वज्रतनुः स्मृता॥
en: Thereupon the celestials worshipped those fragments of the thunder thus broken into pieces. That which is known in the world as the wealth of fame is a portion of the thunder.

sn: वज्रपाणिर्ब्राह्मण: स्यात् क्षत्रं वज्ररथं स्मृतम्। वैश्या वै दानवज्राश्च कर्मवज्रा यवीयसः॥
en: The hands of Brahmanas are (the portion of) the thunder; the chariots of the Kshatriyas are (also the portions of) the thunder. The charity of the Vaishyas are (also the portions of) the thunder and the services of the Shudras are (also the portion of) the thunder.

sn: क्षत्रवज्रस्य भागेन अवध्या वाजिनः स्मृताः। रथाङ्ग वडवा सूते शूराश्चाश्वेषु ये मताः॥
en: The horses of the Kshatriyas being the portions of the thunder, it is said they are never to be killed. The portions of the chariots (the horses) are the offspring of Vadaba. Those amongst them that are Shuras.

sn: कामवर्णाः कामजवाः कामतः समुपस्थिताः। 'इति गन्धर्वजाः काम पूरयिष्यन्ति मे हयाः॥
en: Are capable of assuming any colour at pleasure, of going any where at will and of running at its owner's will. These horses of mine born in the Gandharva region will always fullfil your desire.

sn: अर्जुन उवाच यदि प्रीतेन मे दत्तं संशये जीवितस्य वा। विद्याधनं श्रुतं वापि न तद् गन्धर्व रोचये॥
en: Arjuna said : O Gandharva, if you give me out of your satisfaction for obtaining life in a crisis, these horses and the wealth of science shall not accept it.

sn: गन्धर्व उवाच संयोगो वे प्रीतिकरो महत्सु प्रतिदृश्यते। जीवितस्य प्रदानेन प्रीतो विद्यां ददामि ते॥
en: The Gandharva said : A meeting with an illustrious person is always a matter of gratification. Besides you have given me life. Thus being pleased with you, I give the science.

sn: त्वत्तोऽप्यहं ग्रहीष्यामि अस्त्रमाग्नेयमुत्तमम्। तथा योग्यं बीभत्सो चिराय भरतर्षभ॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, O Bibhatsa, so that the obligation may be not only on one side, I shall take from you your excellent and eternal fire-weapon.

sn: अर्जुन उवाच त्वत्तोऽस्त्रेण वृणोम्यश्वान् संयोगः शाश्वतोऽस्तु नौ सखे तद् ब्रूहि गन्धर्व युष्मभ्यो यद् भयं भवेत्।।५८।
en: Arjuna said : O Gandharva, I shall take your horses in exchange of my weapon. Let our friendship be ever-lasting. O friend, tell me that from which the danger of ours (human beings) arises from the Gandharvas.

sn: कारणं ब्रूहि गन्धर्व किं तद् येन स्म धर्षिताः। यान्तो वेदविदः सर्वे सन्तो रात्रावरिंदमाः॥
en: O Gandharva, we are all chastisers of foes; we are all learned in the Vedas and we are all) virtuous. Tell us why we were censured by you when travelling at night.

sn: गन्धर्व उवाच अनग्नयोऽनाहुतयो न च विप्रपुरस्कृताः। यूयं ततो धर्षिताः स्थ माया वै पाण्डुनन्दनाः॥
en: The Gandharva said : O sons of Pandu, you do not keep fire; you have no wives; you have no Brahmanas walking before you; therefore you were censured by me.

sn: यक्षराक्षसगन्धर्वाः पिशाचोरगदानवाः। विस्तरं कुरुवंशस्य धीमन्तः कथयन्ति ते॥
en: The Yakshas, the Rakshasas, the Gandharvas, the Pishachas, the Uragas and the Danavas are wise and intelligent. They speak much of the Kury race.

sn: नारदप्रभृतीनां तु देवर्षीणां मया श्रुतम्। गुणान् कथयतां वीर पूर्वेषां तव धीमताम्॥
en: O hero, I have heard from Narada and other Rishis the accomplishments of your intelligent ancestors.

sn: स्वयं चापि मया दृष्टश्चरता सागराम्बराम्। इमां वसुमती कृत्स्ना प्रभावः सुकुलस्य ते॥
en: While roaming over the earth attired in her ocean-cloth, I myself have seen the great prowess of your race.

sn: वेदे धनुषि चाचार्यमभिजानामि तेऽर्जुना विश्रुतं त्रिषु लोकेषु भारद्वाजं यशस्विनम्॥
en: O Arjuna, I personally know your preceptor, the illustrious son of Bharadvaja (Drona), who is celebrated in the three worlds for his learning in the Vedas and the science of archery.

sn: धर्मं वायुं च शक्रं च विजानाम्यश्विनौ तथा। पाण्डं च कुरुशार्दूल षडेतान् कुरुवर्धनान्। पितृनेतानहं पार्थ देवमानुषसत्तमान्॥
en: O best of the Kuru race, O Partha, I know also Dharma, Vayu, Indra, Ashvinis and Pandu, these six spreaders of the Kuru race. These (six) excellent celestials and man are your fathers.

sn: दिव्यात्मानो महात्मानः सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वराः। भवन्तो भ्रातरः शूराः सर्वे सुचरितव्रताः॥ उत्तमां च मनोबुद्धिं भवतां भावितात्मनाम्। जानन्नपि च वः पार्थ कृतवानिह धर्षणाम्॥
en: Knowing too that you are high-souled, you are illustrious, you are the foremost of all wielders of arms, you, all brothers, are great heroes, you are virtuous and observant of vows, your understandings and hearts are excellent and your behaviour faultless, I still censured you.

sn: स्त्रीसकाशे च कौरव्य न पुमान् क्षन्तुमर्हति। धर्षणामात्मनः पश्यन् बाहुद्रविणमाश्रितः॥
en: O descendant of Kuru, no man, possessing strength of arms, ought to bear with patience any ill usage before his wife.

sn: नक्तं च बलमस्माकं भूय एवाभिवर्धते। यतस्ततो मां कौन्तेय सदारं मन्युराविशत्॥
en: O son of Kunti, our strength specially increases at the time of night. As I was accompanied by my wife, I was filled with wrath.

sn: सोऽहं त्वयेह विजित: संख्ये तापत्यवर्धन। येन तेनेह विधिना कीर्त्यमानं निबोध मे॥
en: O best of all vow-observing men, I was vanquished by you in battle; hear from me the reasons for with I was discomfited.

sn: ब्रह्मचर्यं परो धर्मः स चापि नियतस्त्वयि। यस्मात् तस्मादहं पार्थ रणेऽस्मि विजितस्त्वया॥
en: Brahmacharya is a great virtue, you are in it (leAding that mode of life). O Partha it is for this that I was defeated by you in battle.

sn: यस्तु स्यात् क्षत्रियः कश्चित् कामवृत्तः परंतप। नक्तं च युधि युध्येत न स जीवेत् कथंचन॥
en: O chastiser of foes, if any Kshatriya, engaged in the exercise of his desire, fight with us at night, he can never escape form us with his life.

sn: यस्तु स्यात् कामवृत्तोऽपि पार्थ ब्रह्मपुरस्कृतः। जयेन्नक्तंचरान् सर्वान् स पुरोहितधूर्गतः॥
en: O Partha, a Kshatriya, engaged in the exercise of his desire, may defeat all the wanderers of night (as we are), if he is sanctified by Brahma and if he assigns the cares of his state to his priest.

sn: तस्मात् तापत्य यत्किंचिऋणां श्रेय इहेप्सितम्। तस्मिन् कर्मणि योक्तव्या दान्तात्मानः पुरोहिताः।७४। वेदे षडङ्गे निरताः शुचयः सत्यवादिनः। धर्मात्मानः कृतात्मानः स्युर्नृपाणां पुरोहिताः॥
en: O descendant of Tapati, men should, therefore, always employ learned and selfcontrolled priests for the acquisition of every good fortune that he desires (to get). That man an is fit to be the priest of kings who is engaged in the study of the Vedas and their six branches, who is pure and truthful and who is virtuousminded and self-controlled.

sn: जयश्च नियतो राज्ञः स्वर्गश्च तदनन्तरम्। यस्य स्याद् धर्मविद् वाग्मी पुरोधाः शीलवान् शुचिः।।
en: That king becomes ever victorious (in this world) and obtains heaven in the next, who has a priest, who is learned in the precepts of morals, who is a master of words and who is pure and well-behaved.

sn: लाभं लब्धुमलब्धं वा लब्धं वा परिरक्षितुम्। पुरोहितं प्रकुर्वीत राजा गुणसमन्वितम्॥
en: The king should always select accomplished priest who can protect what he has and acquires what he has not.

sn: पुरोहितमते तिष्ठेद् य इच्छेद् भूतिमात्मनः। प्राप्तुं वसुमती सर्वां सर्वशः सागराम्बराम्॥
en: He, who desires his own prosperity, should ever be guided by his priest; he may then acquire the whole earth attired in her oceancloth.

sn: न हि केवलशौर्येण तापत्याभिजनेन च। जयेदब्राह्मणः कश्चिद् भूमि भूमिपतिः क्वचित्॥
en: O descendant of Tapati, a king, who is without a Brahmana, can never acquire any land by his bravery or nobility of birth only.

sn: तस्मादेवं विजानीहि कुरूणां वंशवर्धन। ब्राह्मणप्रमुखं राज्यं शक्यं पालयितुं चिरम्॥
en: O spreader of the Kuru race, therefore, know that the kingdoms with Brahmanas at their heads can be retained for long.

sn: अर्जुन उवाच तापत्य इति यद् वाक्यमुक्तवानसि मामिह। तदहं ज्ञातुमिच्छामि तापत्यार्थं विनिश्चितम्॥
en: Arjuna said : You have addressed me as the descendant of Tapati. I wish to know what the precise signification of this word is.

sn: तपती नाम का चैषा तापत्या यत्कृते वयम्। कौन्तेया हि वयं साधो तत्त्वमिच्छामि वेदितुम्॥
en: O blessed being! we are the sons of Kunti, therefore, we are Kaunteyas, but who is Tapati that we should be called Tapatyas. I desire to hear about it.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्तः स गन्धर्वः कुन्तीपुत्रं धनंजयम्। विश्रुतां त्रिषु लोकेषु श्रावयामास वै कथाम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having been addressed by the son of Kunti, Dhananjaya, that Gandharva narrated the story who is celebrated in the three worlds.

sn: गन्धर्व उवाच हन्त तं कथयिष्यामि कथामेतां मनोरमाम्। यथावदखिलां पार्थ सर्वबुद्धिमतां वर॥
en: The Gandharva said : O Partha, o foremost of all intelligent men, I shall duly narrate to you in detail this interesting story.

sn: उक्तवानस्मि येन त्वां तापत्य इति यद् वचः। तत् तेऽहं कथयिष्यामि शृणुष्वैकमनां भव॥
en: Here with attention what I say about the reason for which I address you as Tapatya.

sn: य एष दिवि धिष्ण्येन नाकं व्याप्नोति तेजसा। एतस्य तपती नाम बभूव सदृशी सुता॥
en: He, who pervades the whole firmament by his light, had a daughter, named Tapati, equal to himself (in effulgence).

sn: विवस्वतो वै देवस्य सावित्र्यवरजा विभो। विश्रुता त्रिषु लोकेषु तपती तपसा युता॥
en: That daughter of the Vivasvata (Tapati) was the younger sister of Savitri. She was celebrated in the three worlds and devoted to asceticism.

sn: न देवी नासुरी चैव न यक्षी न च राक्षसी। नाप्सरा न च गन्धर्वी तथा रूपेण काचन॥
en: There was none equal to her in beauty amongst the Deva, the Aura, the Yaksha, the Rakshas, the Apsara and the Gandharva lAdies.

sn: सुविभक्तानवद्याङ्गी स्वसितायतलोचना। स्वाचारा चैव साध्वी च सुवेषा चैव भामिनी॥
en: She was perfectly semetrical in body and faultless in features; she had black and large eyes; she was attired in beautiful robes; she was chaste and exceedingly well conducted.

sn: न तस्याः सदृशं कंचित् त्रिषु लोकेषु भारत। भर्तारं सविता मेने रूपशीलगुणश्रुतैः॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, seeing her, Vivasvata thought, there was none who had beauty, accomplishments,, good behaviour and learning to be fit for her husband.

sn: सम्प्राप्तयौवनां पश्यन् देयां दुहितरं तु ताम्। नोपलेभे ततः शान्तिं सम्प्रदानं विचिन्तयन्॥
en: Seeing that his daughter had attained the age of puberty and that she was worthy of being bestowed on a husband, he had no peace of mind, for he always thought on whom he should bestow her.

sn: अथर्भपुत्र: कौन्तेय कुरूणामृषभो बली। सूर्यमाराधयामास नृपः संवरणस्तदा।॥
en: O son of Kunti, that best of the Kurus, the son of Riksha, the mighty king Samvarana, worshipped Surya

sn: अर्घ्यमाल्योपहाराद्यैर्गश्च नियतः शुचिः। नियमैरुपवासैश्च तपाभिर्विविधैरपि।॥
en: With due offers of Arghya, garlands and scents, with being always pure and holy and with vows, fasts and asceticism of various kinds.

sn: शुश्रूषुरनहंवादी शुचिः पौरवनन्दनः। अंशुमन्तं समुद्यन्तं पूजयामास भक्तिमान्॥
en: The descendant of Puru (Samvarana) worshipped the deity, effulgent in all his glory, with devotion, humanity and piety.

sn: ततः कृतज्ञं धर्मज्ञं रूपेणासदृशं भुवि। तपत्याः सदृशं मेने सूर्यः संवरणं पतिम्॥
en: Thereupon Surya, seeing Samvarana, learned in the precepts of region and matchless in the world for his beauty, considered him to be the fittest husband for (his daughter) Tapati.

sn: दातुमैच्छत् ततः कन्यां तस्मै संवरणाय ताम्। नृपोत्तमाय कौरव्य विश्रुताभिजनाय च॥
en: O descendant of Kuru, Surya then desired to bestow his daughter on that excellent king Samvarana of the Kuru race, who celebrated all over the world.

sn: यथा हि दिवि दीप्तांशुः प्रभासयति तेजसा। तथा भुवि महीपालो दीप्त्या संवरणोऽभवत्॥
en: As Surya in the heavens fills the firmament with his splendour, so did king Samvarana fill region on the earth with the splendour of his good achievements.

sn: यथार्चयन्ति चादित्यमुद्यन्तं ब्रह्मवादिनः। तथा संवरणं पार्थ ब्राह्मणावरजाः प्रजाः॥
en: O Partha, as men learned in the Vedas worship the sun manifests in all his glory, so did all men except the Brahmanas worship Samvarana.

sn: स सोममति कान्तत्वादादित्यमति तेजसा। बभूव नृपतिः श्रीमान् सुहृदां दुर्हदामपि।॥
en: Blessed with good fortune, the king (Samvarana) excelled Soma (moon) in soothing the hearts of friends and Surya (sun) scorching the hearts of the enemies.

sn: एवंगुणस्य नृपतेस्तथावृत्तस्य कौरव। तस्मै दातुं मनश्चक्रे तपतीं तपनः स्वयम्॥
en: O descendant of Kuru, Tapana himself resolved upon bestowing Tapati on the king (Samvarana) endued with such virtue and accomplishments.

sn: स कदाचिदथो राजा श्रीमानमितविक्रमः। चचार मृगयां पार्थ पर्वतोपवने किल॥
en: O Partha, once a time that king, blessed with good fortune and endued with great prowess, went out to hunt in the woods on the mountains.

sn: चरतो मृगयां तस्य क्षुत्पिपासासमन्वितः। ममार राज्ञः कौन्तेय गिरावप्रतिमो हयः॥
en: When thus hunting, the horse of that king of the Kuru race was overcome with hunger and thirst and he (horse) died on the mountains.

sn: स मृताश्वश्चरन् पार्थ पद्भ्यामेव गिरौ नृपः। ददर्शासदृशीं लोके कन्यामायतलोचनाम्॥
en: O Partha, abandoning the dead horse, the king walked on the mountain and saw a maiden of large eyes and matchless beauty.

sn: स एक एकामासाद्य कन्यां परबलार्दनः। तस्थौ नृपतिशार्दूलः पश्यन्नविचलेक्षणः॥
en: That chastiser of foes, that best of kings himself being alone and the maiden being also alone, stood motionless and he steadfastly gazed at her.

sn: स हि तां तर्कयामास रूपतो नृपतिः श्रियम्। पुनः संतर्कयामास रवर्धष्टामिव प्रभाम्॥
en: The king regarded her for her beauty as the goddess Lakshmi. He regarded her beauty to be the embodiment of the rays emanating from the sun.

sn: वपुषा वर्चसा चैव शिखामिव विभावसोः। प्रसन्नत्वेन कान्त्या च चन्द्ररेखामिवामलाम्॥
en: In splendour of body, she resembled a flame of fire and in benignity and loveliness she resembled the spotless disc of the moon.

sn: गिरिपृष्ठे तु सा यस्मिन् स्थिता स्वसितलोचना। विभ्राजमाना शुशुभे प्रतिमेव हिरण्मयी॥
en: The black eyed maiden, standing on the mountain breast, looked like a bright statue of gold.

sn: तस्या रूपेण स गिरिवेषण च विशेषतः। स सवृक्षक्षुपलतो हिरण्मय इवाभवत्॥
en: I consequence of the beauty and splendour of that maiden the mountain itself with its creepers and plants appeared as if it has been converted into gold.

sn: अवमेने च तां दृष्ट्वा सर्वलोकेषु योषितः। अवाप्तं चात्मनो मेने स राजा चक्षुषः फलम्॥
en: The sight of that maiden inspired the king with a contempt for all the women of the world that he had seen before. Seeing her, the king considered his eyes blessed.

sn: जन्मप्रभृति यत् किंचिद् दृष्टवान् स महीपतिः। रूपं न सदृशं तस्यास्तर्कयामास किंचन॥
en: Nothing that the king has seen from the day of his birth could equal, he argued, the beauty of that girl.

sn: तया बद्धमनुश्चक्षुः पाशैर्गुणमयैस्तदा। न चचाल ततो देशाद् बुबुधे न च किंचन॥ अस्या नूनं विशालाक्ष्याः सदेवासुरमानुषम्। लोकं निर्मथ्य धात्रेदं रूपमाविष्कृतं कृतम्॥
en: (He thought) “The creator has created the beauty of this beautiful eyed maiden after churning the whole world of the Devas and the Asuras and the human beings." The king's heart and eyes were captivated by that maiden, as if they became bound in ropes; he remained rooted to the spot deprived of his senses.

sn: एवं संतर्कयामास रूपद्रविणसम्पदा। कन्यामसदृशीं लोके नृपः संवरणस्तदा॥
en: Thus arguing, the king Samvarana considered that maiden as matchless in the wealth of her beauty in the three worlds.

sn: तां च दृष्ट्वैव कल्याणी कल्याणाभिजनो नृपः। जगाम मनसा चिन्तां कामबाणेन पीडितः॥
en: The king of the noble birth, seeing that blessed beauty, was pierced by the arrows of the god of love.

sn: दह्यमानः स तीवेण नृपतिर्मन्मथाग्निना। अप्रगल्भां प्रगल्भस्तां तदोवाच मनोहराम्॥
en: Having been brunt in the very scorching fire of Kama (desire), he (the king) thus spoke to that charming maiden, still innocent through in her full youth.

sn: कासि कस्यासि रम्भोस किमर्थं चेह तिष्ठसि। कथं च निर्जनेऽरण्ये चरस्येका शुचिस्मिते॥
en: The Samvarana said : O lady of tapering things, who and whose are you? Why are you staying here? O lady of sweet smiles, why do you wander alone in these solitary woods?

sn: त्वं हि सर्वानवद्याङ्गी सर्वाभरणभूषिता। विभूषणमिवैतेषां भूषणानामभीप्सितम्॥ न देवी नासुरां चैव न यक्षी न च राक्षसीम्। न च भोगवतीं मन्ये न गन्धर्वी न मानुषीम्॥
en: You are perfectly faultless in your every feature; decked in every ornament, you seem to be the coveted ornament of those ornaments themselves. You seem to be not a Devi or an Asuri, or a Lakshmi, or a Rakshasi; you are not a Nagini or a Gandharvi or a Manushi.

sn: या हि दृष्टा मया काश्चिच्छ्रुता वापि वराङ्गनाः। न तासां सदृशीं मन्ये मत्वामहं मत्तकाशिनि॥
en: O excellent lady, the best of women that I have seen or heard of can not equal you in beauty.

sn: दृष्ट्वैव चारुवदने चन्द्रात् कान्ततरं तव। वदनं पद्मपत्राक्षं मां मन्यातीव मन्मथः॥
en: O lady of beautiful feature, seeing your face which is lovelier than the moon and your eyes like the lotus leaves, I am oppressed by the god of love.

sn: एवं तां स महीपालो बभाषे न तु सा तदा। कामार्तं निर्जनेऽरण्ये प्रत्यभाषत किंचन॥
en: The Gandharva said : The king, oppressed desire, thus addressed her in the solitary woods, but the did not speak a word in reply.

sn: ततो लालप्यमानस्य पार्थिवस्यायतेक्षणा। सौदामिनीव चाभ्रेषु तत्रैवान्तरधीयत॥
en: When the king repeatedly asked her thus, the large-eyed maiden quickly disappeared in the very sight of the king like a flash of lightning.

sn: तामन्वेष्टुं स नृपतिः परिचक्राम सर्वतः। वनं वनजपत्राक्षीं भ्रमन्नुन्मत्तवत् तदा।॥
en: The king then, like one who has loss his reason, wandered through the whole forest in search of that lotus eyed maiden.

sn: अपश्यमानः स तु तां बहु तत्र विलप्य च। निश्चेष्टः पार्थिवश्रेष्ठो मुहूर्तं स व्यतिष्ठत॥
en: Having failed to find her, that best of kings gave vent to much lamentations and he remained motionless in grief for sometime.

sn: गन्धर्व उवाच अथ तस्यामदृश्यायां नृपतिः काममोहितः। पातनः शत्रुसङ्घानां पपात धरणीतले॥
en: The Gandharva said : On the disappearance of the maiden, that chastiser of foes the king, being deprived of his senses by desire, fell on the ground.

sn: तस्मिन् निपतिते भूमावथ सा चारुहासिनी। पुनः पीनायतश्रोणी दर्शयामास तं नृपम्॥
en: On his falling down on the ground, that maiden of sweet smiles and of swelling and round hips, appeared again before the king.

sn: अथाबभाषे कल्याणी वाचा मधुरया नृपम्। तं कुरूणां कुलकरं कामाभिहतचेतसम्॥
en: The blessed beauty (Tapati) then spoke to that king, the perpetuator of the Kuru race, these sweet words.

sn: उवाच मधुरं वाक्यं तपती प्रहसन्निव। उत्तिष्ठोत्तिष्ठ भद्रं ते न त्वमर्हस्यरिंदम्॥ मोहं नृपतिशार्दूल गन्तुमाविष्कृतः क्षितौ। एवमुक्तोऽथ नृपतिर्वाचा मधुरया गिरा॥
en: Sweetly smiling, Tapati spoke thus in sweet words, “Rise, rise, O chastiser of foes be blessed. O best of kings, you are celebrated in the word, it does not befit you to lose your senses.” Having been thus addressed by her in these sweet words,

sn: ददर्श विपुलश्रोणी तामेवाभिमुखे स्थिताम्। अथ तामसितापाङ्गीमाबभाषे स पार्थिवः॥
en: The king (opening his eyes) saw before him that maiden of swelling hips. The king then addressed that black eyed maiden thus,

sn: मन्मथाग्निपरीतात्मा संदिग्धाक्षरया गिरा। साधु त्वमसितापाङ्गि कामात मत्तकाशिनि॥ भजस्व भजमानं मां प्राणा हि प्रजहन्ति माम्। त्वदर्थं हि विशालाक्षि मामयं निशितैः शरैः॥ कामः कमलगर्भामे प्रतिविध्यन् न शाम्यति। दष्टमेवमनाक्रन्दे भद्रे काममहाहिना॥
en: In accents weak with emotion and his heart burning with the fire of desire, “O black eyed beauty. O excellent lady, be blessed. I am burning with desire; and I, therefore, solicit you. Accept me, my life is ebbing away. O lady of large eyes, O lotus eyed beauty, it is all for (not having obtained) you. The god of love pierces me day and night with his arrows. O blessed lady, I have been bitten by Kama (the god of love) who is like a large snake.

sn: सा त्वं पीनायतश्रोणि मामापनुहि वरानने। त्वदधीना हि मे प्राणाः किन्नरोद्गीतभाषिणि॥१०
en: O lady of faultless features, O lady of tapering things, O lady of sweet voice as that of the Kinnaris, have mercy on me; my life depends on you.

sn: चारुसर्वानवद्याङ्गि पद्येन्दुप्रतिमानने। न ह्यहं त्वदृते भीरु शक्ष्यामि खलु जीवितुम्॥
en: O lady of beautiful and faultless features, O lady with the face like the lotus or the moon, O timid lady, I shall certainly be unable to live without you.

sn: कामः कमलपत्राक्षि प्रतिविध्यति मामयम्। तस्मात् कुरु विशालाक्षि मय्यनुक्रोशमङ्गने॥
en: O lotus eyed lady, O lady of large eyes, the god of love is incessantly piercing me, be merciful towards me.

sn: भक्तं मामसितापाङ्गिन परित्यक्तुमर्हसि। त्वं हि मां प्रीतियोगेन त्रातुमर्हसि भाविनि॥
en: O black eyed lady, you should not abandon me. O handsome lady, you should relieve me from such affliction by giving me your love.

sn: त्वदर्शनकृतस्नेहं मनश्चलति मे भृशम्। न त्वां दृष्ट्वा पुनश्चान्यां द्रष्टुं कल्याणि रोचते॥
en: O blessed beauty, at the very first sight, my heart has been captivated by you. My mind wanders. Seeing you, I do not like to cast my eyes on any other woman.

sn: प्रसीद वशगोऽहं ते भक्तं मां भज भाविनि। दृष्ट्वैव त्वां वरारोहे मन्मथो भृशमङ्गने॥
en: O beautiful maiden, be merciful, I am your obedient (slave), (I am) your adorer; accept me. O beautiful lady, O large-eyed maiden, as soon as I saw you, he god of love,

sn: अन्तर्गतं विशालाक्षि विध्यति स्म पतत्रिभिः। मन्मथाग्निसमुद्धतं दाहं कमललोचने॥
en: Entered my heart and he is piercing me with his arrows. O large eyed lady, O lotuseyed beauty, the great fire of desire is burning within me.

sn: प्रीतिसंयोगयुक्ताभिरद्भिः प्रह्लादयस्व मे। पुष्पायुधं दुराधर्ष प्रचण्डशरकार्मुकम्॥ त्वदर्शनसमुद्भूतं विध्यन्तं दुस्सहैः शरैः। उपशामय कल्याणि आत्मदानेन भाविनि॥
en: Extinguish that fire by throwing on it the water of your love. O beautiful lady, pacify, by becoming mine, the irrepressible god of love that has appeared here (in my heart) armed with bow and arrows; he pierces me incessantly with his sharp arrows.

sn: गान्धर्वेण विवाहेन मामुपेहि वराङ्गने। विवाहानां हि रम्भोरु गान्धर्वः श्रेष्ठ उच्यते॥
en: O beautiful featured maiden, O lady of tapering hips, marry me according to the Gandharva form, for of all kinds of marriage the Gandharva form has been said to be the best."

sn: तपत्युवाच नाहमीशाऽऽत्मनो राजन् कन्या पितृमती ह्यहम्। मयि चेदस्ति ते प्रीतिर्याचस्व पितरं मम॥
en: Tapati said: O king, I am not the mistress of my ownself. Know me to be a maiden living under the control of my father. If you really love me, ask me of my father.

sn: यथा हि ते मया प्राणा: संगृहीता नरेश्वर। दर्शनादेव भूयस्त्वं तथा प्राणान् ममाहरः॥
en: O king, you say that your heart has been robbed by me; but you too have robbed my heart at the first sight.

sn: न चाहमीशा देहस्य तस्मान्नृपतिसत्तम। समीपं नोपगच्छामि न स्वतन्त्रा हि योषितः॥
en: O best of kings, I am not the mistress of my body; therefore I do not go near you. Women are never independent.

sn: का हि सर्वेषु लोकेषु विश्रुताभिजनं नृपम्। कन्या नाभिलषेन्नाथं भर्तारं भक्तवत्सलम्॥
en: Is there any girl in the three worlds who would not desire for her husband such a king as you, kind to all your dependents and born of a noble race.

sn: तस्मादेवं गते काले याचस्व पितरं मम। आदित्यं प्रणिपातेन तपसा नियमेन च॥
en: Therefore, when the opportunity comes, ask me of my father Aditya with due salutation, ascetic penances and vows.

sn: स चेत् कामयते दातुं तव मामरिसूदन। भविष्याम्यद्य ते राजन् सततं वशवर्तिनी॥
en: O king, O chastiser of foes, if my father bestows me on you then asked, I shall ever be your obedient (wife).

sn: अहं हि तपती नाम सावित्र्यवरजा सुता। अस्य लोकप्रदीपस्य सवितुः क्षत्रियर्षभ॥
en: My name is Tapati, I am the younger sister of Savitri. O best of Kshatriyas, I am the daughter of Surya, the illuminator of the Universe.

sn: गन्धर्व उवाच एवमुक्त्वा ततस्तूर्णं जगामोर्ध्वमनिन्दिता। स तु राजा पुनर्भूमौ तत्रैव निपपात ह॥
en: The Gandharva said : Having said this, that faultless (maiden) soon ascended the skies; on this the king again fell down on the ground.

sn: अन्वेषमाणः सबलस्तं राजानं नृपोत्तमम्। अमात्यः सानुयात्रश्च तं ददर्श महावने॥
en: In searching that best of kings, that monarch's ministers and attendants saw him there in that state in the great forest.

sn: क्षितौ निपतितं काले शक्रध्वजमिवोच्छ्रितम्। तं हि दृष्टवा महेष्वासं निरस्तं पतितं भुवि॥ बभूव सोऽस्य सचिवः सम्प्रदीप्त इवाग्निना। त्वरया चोपसंगम्य स्नेहादागतसम्भ्रमः॥
en: Seeing that excellent king, that great bowman, lying forsaken on the ground like a rain bow dropped from the sky, his chief minister became like one brunt by a flame of fire. Coming hastily to him with affection and respect,

sn: तं समुत्थापयामास नृपतिं काममोहितम्। भूतलाद् भूमिपालेशं पितेव पतितं सुतम्॥
en: As a father rises up the son fallen (on the ground) he raised up the king, lying senseless on the ground having been deprived of his senses by desire.

sn: प्रज्ञया वयसा चैव वृद्धः कीर्त्या नयेन च। अमात्यस्तं समुत्थाप्य बभूव विगतज्वरः॥
en: Old the wisdom as in age and in achievements as in policy, the minister became easy of mind when he raised him up.

sn: उवाच चैनं कल्याण्या वाचा मधुरयोत्थितम्। मा भर्मनुजशार्दूल भद्रमस्तु तवानघ॥
en: He spoke to him these words, both sweet and beneficial, “O best of men, do not fear, O sinless one,, be blessed."

sn: क्षुत्पिपासापरिश्रान्तं तर्कयामास वै नृपम्। पतितं पातनं संख्ये शात्रवाणां महीतले॥
en: The minister through the king, that destroyer of hostile forces, had been lying on the ground being overcome with hunger, thirst and fatigue.

sn: वारिणा च सुशीतेन शिरस्तस्याभ्यषेचयत्। अस्फुटन्मुकुटं राज्ञः पुण्डरीकसुगन्धिना॥
en: He sprinkled on the crewless head of the king cold water fragrant, with the perfume of lotus.

sn: ततः प्रत्यागतप्राणस्तद् बलं बलवान् नृपः। सर्वं विसर्जयामास तमेकं सचिवं विना॥
en: Thereupon, the mighty king regained his consciousness; he then sent away all his attendants except that one minister.

sn: ततस्तस्याज्ञया राज्ञो विप्रतस्थे महद् बलम् स तु राजा गिरिप्रस्थे तस्मिन् पुनरुपाविशत्॥
en: When that large number of attendants had gone away at the command of the king, the king again sat down on the mountain breast.

sn: ततस्तस्मिन् गिरिवरे शुचिर्भूत्वा कृताञ्जलिः। आरिराधयिषुः सूर्यं तस्थावर्ध्वमु तौ॥
en: Then the king becoming pure and folding his hands, worshipped Surya with his face turned upwards on that best of mountains.

sn: जगाम मनसा चैव वसिष्ठमृषिसत्तमम्। पुरोहितममित्रघ्नस्तदा संवरणो नृपः॥
en: That chastiser of foes, the king Samvarana, also mentally thought of his priest, that excellent Rishi, Vasishtha.

sn: नक्तं दिनमथैकत्र स्थिते तस्मिञ्जनाधिपे। अथाजगाम विप्रर्षिस्तदा द्वादशमेऽहनि॥
en: The king remained there four days and nights without intermission; and on the twelfth day the Brahmana Rishi (Vasishtha) came to him.

sn: स विदित्वैव नृपतिं तपत्या हृतमानसम्। दिव्येन विधिना ज्ञात्वा भावितात्मा महानृषिः॥
en: That great self-controlled Rishi knew by his ascetic power that the king's heart was stolen by Tapati.

sn: तथा तु नियतात्मानं तं नृपं मुनिसत्तमः। आबभाषे स धर्मात्मा तस्यैवार्थचिकीर्षया॥
en: As soon as that virtuous-minded and the best of Rishis knew this, he became desirous of benefiting the king and gave him his assurances.

sn: स तस्य मनुजेन्द्रस्य पश्यतो भगवानृषिः। अर्ध्वमाचक्रमे द्रष्टुं भास्करं भास्करद्युतिः॥
en: In the very sight of the king, the illustrious Rishi ascended the sky in order to see Surya, he himself being as effulgent as that luminary.

sn: सहस्रांशुं ततो विप्रः कृताञ्जलिरुपस्थितः। वसिष्ठोऽहमिति प्रीत्या स चात्मानं न्यवेदयत्॥
en: Thereupon, the Brahmana (Vasishtha) came with joined hands to the deity of one thousand rays and he then introduced himself by saying, “I am Vasishtha."

sn: तमुवाच महातेजा विवस्वान् मुनिसत्तमम्। महर्षे स्वागतं तेऽस्तु कथयस्व यथेप्सितम्॥
en: Then the greatly effulgent Vivasvata thus spoke to that excellent Brahmana, "O great Rishi, welcome to you. Tell me what is your desire.

sn: यदिच्छसि महाभाग मत्तः प्रवदतां वर। तत् ते दद्यामभिप्रेतं यद्यपि स्यात् सुदुष्करम्॥
en: O greatly fortunate man, O foremost of all eloquent men, whatever you desire to have, I shall give you however difficult it may be to give."

sn: एवमुक्तः स तेनर्षिर्वसिष्ठः प्रत्यभाषत। प्रणिपत्य विवस्वन्तं भानुमन्तं महातपाः॥
en: Having been thus addressed after duly bowing down his head to him the Rishi Vasishtha of great ascetic merit, thus replied to Vivasvata.

sn: वसिष्ठ उवाच यैषा ते तपती नाम सावित्र्यवरजा सुता। तां त्वां संवरणस्यार्थे वरयामि विभावसो॥
en: Vasishtha said: O Vivasvata, I ask to you for Samvarana your daughter, named Tapati, the younger sister of Savitri.

sn: स हि राजा बृहत्कीर्तिर्धमार्थविदुदारधीः। युक्तः संवरणो भर्ता दुहितुस्ते विहंगम॥
en: He (Samvarana) is a mighty king with great achievements; he is learned in the mysteries of religion and he is high-minded. O ranger of sky, Samvarana is the fittest husband for your daughter.

sn: इत्युक्तः स तदा तेन ददानीत्येव निश्चितः। प्रत्यभाषत तं विप्रं प्रतिनन्द्य दिवाकरः॥
en: The Gandharva said : Having been thus addressed, Divakara (Surya) resolved upon bestowing (his daughter on Samvarana) and saluting the Rishi thus replied,

sn: वरः संवरणो राज्ञां त्वमृषीणां वरो मुने। तपती योषितां श्रेष्ठा किमन्यदपवर्जनात्॥
en: "O Rishi! Samvarana is the best of kings; you are (also) the best of all Rishis; Tapati is (surely) the best of all women; what else could be done but to bestow her (on Samvarana)?

sn: ततः सर्वानवद्यागी तपती तपनः स्वयम्। ददौ संवरणस्यार्थे वसिष्ठाय महात्मने॥
en: Then Tapana himself gave to the illustrious Vasishtha (his daughter) Tapati of perfectly faultless features, so that she might be bestowed on Samvarana.

sn: प्रतिजग्राह तां कन्यां महर्षिस्तपती तदा। वसिष्ठोऽथ विसृष्टस्तु पुनरेवाजगाम ह॥
en: The great Rishi Vivasvata accepted that maiden Tapati and taking leave of Surya he came back to the place,

sn: यत्र विख्यातकीर्तिः स कुरूणामृषभोऽभवत्। स राजा मन्मथाविष्टस्तद्गतेनान्तरात्मना॥
en: Where that best of the Kurus, the king of celebrated achievements, was. That king who had been possessed of desire and whose heart was completely fixed on her (Tapati)

sn: दृष्ट्वा च देवकन्यां तां तपती चारुहासिनीम् वसिष्ठेन सहायान्तीं संहृष्टोऽभ्यधिकं बभौ॥
en: Became exceedingly glad on seeing that celestials maiden Tapati of sweet smiles led towards him by Vasishtha.

sn: रुरुचे साधिकं सुभूरापतन्ती नभस्तलात्। सौदामिनीव विभ्रष्टा द्योतयन्ती दिशस्त्विषा॥
en: That maiden of fair eye-brows came down from the sky as lighting comes down from the clouds illuminating the ten points of heaven.

sn: कृच्छ्राद् द्वादशरात्रे तु तस्य राज्ञः समाहिते। आजगाम विशुद्धात्मा वसिष्ठोः भगवानृषिः॥
en: The illustrious Rishi of pure soul Vasishtha came to that king when his vow of the twelfth night was over.

sn: तपसाऽऽराध्य वरदं देवं गोपतिमीश्वरम्। लेभे संवरणो भार्यां वसिष्ठस्यैव तेजसा॥
en: Thus Samvarana obtained (Tapati) as his wife by worshipping the propitious lord (Surya) by ascetic penances and by the help of the great effulgence of Vasishtha.

sn: ततस्तस्मिन् गिरिश्रेष्ठे देवगन्धर्वसेविते। जग्राह विधिवत् पाणिं तपत्याः स नरर्षभः॥
en: That best of kings accepted the hands of Tapati in due form on the breast of that mountain frequented by the celestials and the Gandharvas.

sn: वसिष्ठेनाभ्यनुज्ञातस्तस्मिन्नेव धराधरे। सोऽकामयत राजर्षिविहर्तुं सह भार्यया॥
en: The royal sage (Samvarana) with the permission of Vasishtha desired to sport with his wife on that mountain.

sn: ततः पुरे च राष्ट्रे च वनेषूपवनेषु च। आदिदेशे महीपालस्तमेव सचिवं तदा॥
en: He ordered the minister to rule over his capital, his kingdom, his woods and forests.

sn: नृपति त्वभ्यनुज्ञाप्य वसिष्ठोऽथापचक्रमे। सोऽथ राजा गिरौ तस्मिन् विजहारामरो यथा॥
en: Then bidding farewell to the king, Vasishtha left him and went away. Thereupon, the king sported on that mountain like a celestials.

sn: ततो द्वादश वर्षाणि काननेषु वनेषु च। रेमे तस्मिन् गिरौ राजा तथैव सह भार्यया॥
en: The king sported with his wife in the woods and forests on that mountain for twelve (long) years.

sn: तस्य राज्ञः पुरे तस्मिन् समा द्वादश सत्तम। न ववर्ष सहस्राक्षो राष्ट्रे चैवास्य भारत॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, for those twelve years the god of one thousand eyes (Indra) did nor pour any rains on the capital and the kingdom of that king.

sn: ततस्तस्यामनावृष्ट्यां प्रवृत्तायामरिंदम। प्रजाः क्षयमुपाजग्मुः सर्वाः सस्थाणुजङ्गमाः॥
en: O chastiser of foes, when that season of draught commenced, all the people together with plants, corns and animals began to die.

sn: तस्मिंस्तथाविधे काले वर्तमाने सुदारुणे। नावश्यायः पपातोल् ततः सम्यानि नारुहन्॥
en: During that terrible season (of draught) not even a drop of dew fell on the earth and (consequently) no corn was grown.

sn: ततो विभ्रान्तमनसो जनाः क्षुद्भयपीडिताः। गृहाणि सम्परित्यज्य वभ्रमुः प्रदिशो दिशः॥
en: Thereupon the people, affected with the fear of hunger, left their houses in despair and fled in all directions.

sn: ततस्तस्मिन् पुरे राष्ट्रे त्यक्तदारपरिग्रहाः। परस्परममर्यादाः क्षुधार्ता जजिरे जनाः॥
en: The famished people of the city and the country abandoned their wives and children and grew reckless of one another.

sn: तत् क्षुधातैर्निराहारैः शवभूतैस्तथा नरैः। अभवत् प्रेतराजस्य पुरं प्रेतैरिवावृतम्॥
en: The people being affected with hunger and starvation, became like dead skeletons, and the city looked like the land of the king of the dead full of ghostly beings.

sn: ततस्तत् तादृशं दृष्ट्वा स एव भगवानृषिः। अभ्यवर्षत धर्मात्मा वसिष्ठो मुनिसत्तमः॥
en: Thereupon, seeing the kingdom in such a state, the illustrious Rishi, the best of ascetics. the virtuous-minded Vasishtha, thought of remedying the evil.

sn: तं च पार्थिवशार्दूलमानयामास तत् पुरम्। तपत्या सहितं राजन् व्युषितं शाश्वतीः समाः। ततः प्रवृष्टस्तत्रासीद् यथापूर्वं सुरारिहा॥
en: O king, he brought back that best of kings (Samvarana) with his wife (Tapati) to that city, after he had passed many years with her.

sn: तस्मिन् नृपतिशार्दूले प्रविष्टे नगरं पुनः। प्रववर्ष सहस्राक्षः सस्यानि जनयन् प्रभुः॥ ततः सराष्ट्र मुमेदे तत् पुरं परया मुदा। तेन पार्थिवमुख्येन भावितं भावितात्मना॥
en: When that best of kings again entered his capital, the state of things became as before, the god of one thousand years, the slayer of Asuras, poured rain in abundance; and he caused corn to grow. Thus being revived by that virtuous-minded and that best of kings (Samvarana), the capital and the country became exceedingly glad.

sn: ततो द्वादश वर्षाणि पुनरीजे नराधिपः। तपत्या सहितः पल्या यथा शच्या मरुत्पतिः॥
en: Thereupon the king with his wife Tapati performed sacrifices for twelve years, as Indra did with (his wife) Shachi.

sn: गन्धर्व उवाच एवमासीन्महाभागा तपती नाम पौर्विकी। तव वैवस्वती पार्थ तापत्यस्त्वं यया मतः॥
en: O Partha, this is the history of the greatly blessed Tapati of old, the daughter of Vivasvata, It is for her you are Tapatya.

sn: तस्यां संजनयामास कुरुं संवरणो नृपः। तपत्यां तपतां श्रेष्ठ तापत्यस्त्वं ततोऽर्जुन॥
en: O Arjuna, the king Samvarana beget on Tapati a son, named Kuru. Born in the race of Tapati, you are called Tapatya.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच स गन्धर्ववचः श्रुत्वा तत् तदा भरतर्षभ। अर्जुनः परया भक्त्या पूर्णचन्द्र इवाबभौ॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Hearing these words of the Gandharva, that best of the Bharata race, Arjuna, was filled with devotion (towards him) and he stood as manifest as the full moon.

sn: उवाच च महेष्वासो गन्धर्वं कुरुसत्तमः। जातकौतूहलोऽतीव वसिष्ठस्य तपोबलात्॥
en: His curiosity being excited by what he heard of Vasishtha's ascetic power, that best of the Kurus, that great bowman, thus spoke to the Gandharva,

sn: वसिष्ठ इति तस्यैतदृषेर्नाम त्वयेरितम्। एतदिच्छाम्यहं श्रोतुं यथावत् तद् वदस्व मे॥
en: "I desire to hear the history of the Rishi whom you have mentioned by the name of Vasishtha. Tell me all about him in detail.

sn: य एष गन्धर्वपते पूर्वेषां नः पुरोहितः। आसीदेतन्ममाचक्ष्व क एष भगवानृषिः॥
en: O chief of the Gandharvas, tell me who this illustrious Rishi was, he who was the priest of our forefathers."

sn: गन्धर्व उवाच ब्रह्मणो मानसः पुत्रो वसिष्ठोऽरुन्धतीपतिः। तपसा निर्जितौ शश्वदजेयावमरैरपि॥ कामक्रोधावुभौ यस्य चरणौ संववाहतुः। इन्द्रियाणां वशकरो वशिष्ट इति चोच्यते॥
en: The Gandharva said : Vasishtha was the Brahma's son born of his mind; and he was the husband of Arundhati. Ever difficult of being conquered even by the celestials. Desire and Anger, having been conquered by his ascetic penances, shampooed his feet. He was so highsouled that he did not exterminate the Kushikas.

sn: यस्तु नोच्छेदनं चक्रे कुशिकानामुदारधीः। विश्वामित्रापराधेन धारयन् मन्युमुत्तमम्॥
en: Though the excellent Rishi's anger was excited by Vishvamitra, though he was afflicted at the loss of his sons, though he was powerful, yet he appeared to be powerless.

sn: पुत्रव्यसनसंतप्तः शक्तिमानप्यशक्तवत्। विश्वामित्रविनाशाय न चक्रे कर्म दारुणम्॥ मृतांश्च पुनराहर्तं शक्त पुत्रान् यमक्षयात्। कृतान्तं नातिचक्राम वेलामिव महोदधिः॥
en: He did not perform any dreadful deed for destroying Vishvamitra. Like the great ocean which does not cross its shore, he did not transgress the law of Yama by bringing back his sons from the land of the dead. It is by obtaining this self controlled and illustrious (Rishi), the kings,

sn: यं प्राप्य विजितात्मानं महात्मानं नराधिपाः। इक्ष्वाकवो महीपाला लेभिरे पृथिवीमिमाम्॥१०
en: (Namely) Ikshaku and others, became the lords over the whole earth. Getting the excellent Rishi Vasishtha as their priest,

sn: पुरोहितमिमं प्राप्य वसिष्ठमृषिसत्तमम्। ईजिरे क्रतुभिश्चैव नृपास्ते कुरुनन्दने।११॥
en: O descendant of Kuru, o best of the Pandavas, these kings performed many great sacrifices. That Brahmarshi performed the priestly duty of all these excellent kings, as Brihaspati did that of the celestials.

sn: स हि तान् याजयामास सर्वान् नृपतिसत्तमान्। ब्रह्मर्षिः पाण्डवश्रेष्ठ बृहस्पतिरिवामरान्॥
en: Therefore, seek to appoint as your priest an accomplished Brahmana in whose heart virtue predominates and who is learned in the Vedas.

sn: तस्माद् धर्मप्रधानात्मा वेदधर्मविदीप्सितः। ब्राह्मणो गुणवान् कश्चित् पुरोधाः प्रतिदृश्यताम्॥ क्षत्रियेणाभिजातेन पृथिवीं जेतुमिच्छता। पूर्वं पुरोहितः कार्यः पार्थ राज्याभिवृद्धये॥
en: O Partha, a Kshatriya of noble birth should first appoint a priest, if he is (at all) desirous of extending his dominions by conquering the earth. He, who is desirous of conquering the earth, should have a Brahmana before him.

sn: महीं जिगीषता राज्ञा ब्रह्म कार्यं पुरस्सरम्। तस्मात् पुरोहितः कश्चिद् गुणवान् विजितेन्द्रियः। विद्वान् भवतु वो विप्रो धर्मकामार्थतत्त्ववित्॥
en: Therefore, let an accomplished and learned Brahmana, who has conquered his senses and who is learned in Dharma, Artha and Kama, be your priest.

sn: अर्जुन उवाच किंनिमित्तमभूद वैरं विश्वामित्रवसिष्ठयोः। वसतोराश्रमे दिव्ये शंस नः सर्वमेव तत्॥
en: Arjuna said: How the hostility between Vishvamitra and Vasishtha, both of whom lived in celestials hermitages? Tell us all this in detail. arose

sn: गन्धर्व उवाच इदं वासिष्ठमाख्यानं पुराणं परिचक्षते। पार्थं सर्वेषु लोकेषु यथावत् तन्निबोध मे॥
en: The Gandharva said : O Partha, this history of Vasishtha is considered as a Purana in all the worlds. Listen to me as I recite it in detail.

sn: कान्यकुब्जे महानासीत् पार्थिवो भरतर्षभ। गाधीति विश्रुतो लोके कुशिकस्यात्मसम्भवः॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, there was a great king in Kanyakubja; known in the world by the name of Gadhi, he was the son of Kushika.

sn: तस्य धर्मात्मनः पुत्रः समृद्धबलवाहनः। विश्वामित्र इति ख्यातो बभूव रिपुमर्दनः॥
en: His son was know by the name of Vishvamitra. That chastiser of foes, Vishvamitra, was virtuous-minded; and he had a large army of troop and beasts of burdens.

sn: स चचार सहामात्यो मृगयां गहने वने। मृगान् विध्यन् वराहांश्च रम्येषु मरुधन्वसु॥
en: He wandered with his ministers in the deep forest for the purpose of hunting Killing deer and boars, he roamed through the charming marshes.

sn: व्यायामकर्शितः सोऽथ मृगलिप्सुः पिपासितः। आजगाम नरश्रेष्ठ वसिष्ठस्याश्रमं प्रति॥
en: Being (one day) fatigued and thirsty by the exercise of the hunt that best of men, came to the hermitage of Vasishtha.

sn: तमागतमभिप्रेक्ष्य वसिष्ठः श्रेष्ठभागृषिः। विश्वामित्रं नरश्रेष्ठं प्रतिजग्राह पूजया॥
en: Seeing him coming, the illustrious and blessed Rishi, Vasishtha, advanced to salute that best of men, Vishvamitra.

sn: पाद्यार्थ्याचमनीयैस्तं स्वागतेन च भारत। तथैव परिजग्राह वन्येन हविषा तदा॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, he (Vasishtha) worshipped him (Vishvamitra) by asking his welfare, by offering Arghya and water to wash his face and feet and by collected forest fruits and ghee.

sn: तस्याथ कामधुग् धेनुर्वसिष्ठस्य महात्मनः। उक्ता कामान् प्रयच्छेति सा कामान् दुह्यते सदा॥
en: The illustrious Rishi had a Kamadhenu, (a cow yielding every thing as desired.) when she was addressed by saying "Give” she always gave what was desired.

sn: ग्राम्यारण्याश्चौषधीश्च दुदुहे पय एव च। षड्रसं चामृतनिभं रसायनमनुत्तमम्॥ भोजनीयानि पेयानि भक्ष्याणि विविधानि च। लेह्यान्यमृतकल्पानि चोप्याणि च तथार्जुन॥ रत्नानि च महार्हाणि वासांसि विविधानि च। तैः कामैः सर्वसम्पूर्णैः पूजितश्च महीपतिः॥ सामात्यः सबलश्चैव तुतोष स भृशं तदा।
en: O Arjuna, the Rishi received from her various wild fruits and grown corn of gardens and fields, milk, many excellent nutritious was viands filled with six different kinds of juice which was like ambrosia itself, various other kinds of enjoyable things of ambrosial taste, things for drinking and eating, for lapping and sucking and many precious gems and various costly robes. With these desirable objects in profusion, the king (Vishvamitra) worshipped. And he with his ministers and troops was became exceedingly glad.

sn: षडुन्नतां सुपा.सं पृथुपञ्चसमावृताम्॥ मण्डूकनेत्रा स्वाकारां पीनोधसमनिन्दिताम्। सुबालधिं शकुकर्णां चारुशृङ्गां मनोरमाम्॥
en: He (Vishvamitra) became very much astonished to see that cow which had six elevated limbs, beautiful flanks and hips, fine broad limbs, limbs, frog-like prominent eyes, beautiful size, high udders, faultless make, straight and up-lifted ears, handsome horns and well-developed head and neck.

sn: पुष्टायतशिरोग्रीवां विस्मितः सोऽभिवीक्ष्य ताम्। अभिनन्द्य स तां राजा नन्दिनी गाधिनन्दनः॥
en: O prince, that king, the son of Gadhi, was exceedingly gratified with all that he saw and very much praising (the cow) Nandini he thus spoke to the Rishi (Vasishtha),

sn: अब्रवीच्च भृशं तुष्टः स राजा तमृषि तदा। अर्बुदेन गवां ब्रह्मन् मम राज्येन वा पुनः॥ नन्दिनी सम्प्रयच्छस्व भुक्ष्व राज्यं महामुने।
en: "O Brahmana, O great Rishi, give me (your) Nandini (cow) in exchange of ten thousand kine, or of my kingdom. Give her to me and enjoy my kingdom.

sn: वसिष्ठ उवाच देवतातिथिपित्रर्थं याज्यार्थं च पयस्विनी॥ अदेया नन्दिनीयं वै राज्येनापि तवानघ।
en: Vasishtha said: O sinless one, this milk-giving cow is kept by me for the purposes of the celestials, the Pitris and the guests and for my scarifies. Nandini cannot he given to you) in exchange of even your kingdom.

sn: विश्वामित्र उवाच क्षत्रियोऽहं भवान् विप्रस्तपस्स्वाध्यायसाधनः॥ ब्राह्मणेषु कुतो वीर्यं प्रशान्तेषु धृतात्मसु।
en: Vishvamitra said : I am a Kshatriya and your respected self is a Brahmana devoted to study and asceticism. Is there prowess in Brahmanas who are peaceful and have their souls under control?

sn: अर्बुदेन गवां यसत्वं न ददासि ममेप्सितम्॥ स्वधर्मं न प्रहास्यामि नेष्यामि च बलेन गाम्।
