en: When you do not give me what I desire to have in exchange of ten thousand kine, I shall not abandon the duty of my race (that of the Kshatriya). I will take your cow by force.

sn: वसिष्ठ उवाच बलस्थश्चासि राजा च बाहुवीर्यश्च क्षत्रियः॥ यथेच्छसि तथा क्षिप्रं कुरु मा त्वं विचारय।
en: Vasishtha said: You are a powerful king, you are a Kshatriya possessing great strength of arms; do what you desire without delay and without stopping to consider over it.

sn: गन्धर्व उवाच एवमुक्तस्तथा पार्थ विश्वामित्रो बलादिव॥ हंसचन्द्रप्रतीकाशां नन्दिनीं तां जहार गाम्।
en: The Gandharva said: O Partha, having been thus addressed, Vishvamitra then sized the cow Nandini as white as the swan or the moon.

sn: कशादण्डप्रणुदितां काल्यमानामितस्ततः॥ हम्भायमाना कल्याणी वसिष्ठस्याथ नन्दिनी।
en: He dragged her hither and thither and afflicted her by striking her with a stick. The blessed Nandini cried piteously and came near Vasishtha.

sn: आगम्याभिमुखी पार्थ तस्थौ भगवदुन्मुखी॥ भृशं च ताड्यमाना वै न जगामाश्रमात् ततः।
en: O Partha, she stood near him with up-lifted face staring at the illustrious Rishi. Though very much ill-treated, she did not quit the Rishi's hermitage.

sn: वसिष्ठ उवाच शृणोमि ते रवं भद्रे विनदन्त्याः पुनः पुनः॥ ह्रियसे त्वं बलाद् भद्रे विश्वामित्रेण नन्दिनि। किं कर्तव्यं मया तत्र क्षमावान् ब्राह्मणो ह्यहम्॥
en: Vasishtha said: O amiable Nandini, you are crying again and again and I hear your cries. But Vishvamitra is taking you away by force; what can I do? I am a forgiving Brahmana.

sn: गन्धर्व उवाच सा भयान्नन्दिनी तेषां बलानां भरतर्षभ। विश्वामित्रभयोद्विग्ना वसिष्ठं समुपागमत्॥
en: The Gandharva said : O best of the Bharata race, being alarmed at the sight of Vishvamitra's troops and being terrified by Vishvamitra himself, Nandini came closer to Vasishtha.

sn: गौरुवाच कशाग्रदण्डाभिहतां क्रोशन्ती मामनाथवत्। विश्वामित्रवलैोरैर्भगवन् किमुपेक्षसे॥
en: Nandini said: O illustrious Sir, I am afflicted by the : stripes of the fearful troops of Vishvamitra I am crying piteously like one who has none; why are you so indifferent to me?

sn: गन्धर्व उवाच नन्दिन्यामेवं क्रन्दन्त्यां धर्षितायां महामुनिः। न चुक्षुभे तदा धैर्यान्न चचाल धृतव्रतः॥
en: The Gandharva said : The great Rishi did not lose his patience, nor did he depart from his vow of forgiveness on hearing the words of the crying and persecuted Nandini.

sn: वसिष्ठ उवाच क्षत्रियाणां बलं तेजो ब्राह्मणानां क्षमा बलम्। क्षमा मां भजते यस्माद् गम्यतां यदि रोचते॥
en: Vasishtha said : The might of the Kshatriyas lies in their physical strength, that of the Brahmanas lies in their forgiveness. I cannot give up forgiveness. If you like, you can go.

sn: नु नन्दिन्युवाच कि त्यक्तास्मि भगवन् यदेवं त्वं प्रभाषसे। अत्यक्ताहं त्वया ब्रह्मन् नेतुं शक्या न वै बलात्॥
en: Nandini said : O illustrious Sir, have you abandoned me that you say so? O Brahmana, if you do not abandon me, I cannot be taken away by force.

sn: वसिष्ठ उवाच न त्वां त्यजामि कल्याणि स्थीयतां यदि शक्यते। दृढेन दाम्ना बद्धवैष वत्सस्ते ह्रियते बलात्॥
en: Vasishtha said : O blessed one, I do not abandon you. Stay if you can. Your calf, tied with a strong rope, is (even now) being carried away by force.

sn: गन्धर्व उवाच स्थायतामिति तच्छुत्वा वसिष्ठस्य पयस्विनी। अाञ्चितशिरोग्रीवा प्रबभौ रौद्रदर्शना॥
en: The Gandharva said : Having heard the word 'Stay,' that cow of Vasishtha (Nandini) raised up her head and neck and became fearful to look at.

sn: क्रोधरक्तेक्षणा सा गौहम्भारवधनस्वना। विश्वामित्रस्य तत् सैन्यं व्यद्रावयत सर्वशः॥
en: With eyes red in anger and with repeated roars, she then attacked Vishvamitra's troop on all sides.

sn: कशाग्रदण्डाभिहता काल्यमाना ततस्ततः। क्रोधरक्तेक्षणा क्रोधं भूय एव समादद॥
en: Afflicted with their stripes and being dragged hither and thither, her anger (doubly) ! increased and her eyes became red in wrath.

sn: आदित्य इव मध्याह्ने क्रोधदीप्तवपुर्बभौ। अङ्गारवर्षं मुञ्चन्ती मुहुर्बालधितो महत्॥
en: Blazing in anger, she soon become fearful to look at as the sun at mid day. She began incessantly to shower burning coals from her tail.

sn: असृजत् पह्लवान् पुच्छात् प्रस्रवाद् द्रविडाञ्छकान्। योनिदेशाच्च यवनान् शकृतः शबरान् बहून्॥
en: A few moments after she brought forth from her tail an army of Palhavas, from her udders an army of Dravidas and Shakas, from her womb an army of Yavanas, from her dung an army of Shabaras.

sn: मूत्रतश्चासृजत् कांश्चिच्छबरांश्चैव पार्श्वत:। पौण्ड्रान् किरातान् यवनान् सिंहलान् बर्बरान् खसान्॥ चिबुकांश्च पुलिन्दांश्च चीनान् हूणान् सकेरलान्। ससर्ज फेनतः सा गौम्लेंच्छान् बहुविधानायि॥
en: From her urine an army of Kanchis and from her sides an army of Saravanas; and from the froth of her mouth that cow created hosts of Kiratas, Yavanas, Singhalas, Barbaras, Chibuakas, Pulindas, Chinas, Hunas and Keralas and many other Mlecchas.

sn: तैर्विसृष्टर्महासैन्यैर्नानाम्लेच्छगणैस्तदा। नानावरणसंच्छन्नैर्नानायुधधरैस्तथा॥ अवाकीर्यत संरब्धैर्विश्वामित्रस्य पश्यतः। एकैकश्च तदा योधः पञ्चभिः सप्तभिर्वृतः॥
en: Those large armies of Mlecchas, cloud in various uniforms and armed with various weapons, as soon as they sprang into life, spre Ading all around attacked before his very sight the troops of Vishvamitra, five or seven attacking one.

sn: अस्त्रवर्षेण महता वध्यमानं बलं तदा। प्रभग्नं सर्वतस्त्रस्तं विश्वामित्रस्य पश्यतः॥
en: Assailed with a great shower of weapons, Vishvamitra's troops before his very sight broke and fled panic stricken in all directions.

sn: न च प्राणैर्वियुज्यन्ते केचित् तत्रास्य सैनिकाः। विश्वामित्रस्य संक्रुद्धैर्वासिष्ठैर्भरतर्षभ॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, though greatly excited with anger, the troops of Vasishtha did not take the life of any of Vishvamitra's troops.

sn: सा गौस्तत् सकलं सैन्यं कालयामास दूरतः। विश्वामित्रस्य तत् सैन्यं काल्यमानं त्रियोजनम्॥
en: That cow (Nandini) simply drove the troops (of Vishvamitra) to a distance. Being thus driven full seventy seven miles, the troops of Vishvamitra,

sn: क्रोशमानं भयोद्विग्नं त्रातारं नाध्यगच्छत। दृष्ट्वा तन्महदाश्चर्यं ब्रह्मतेजोभवे तदा॥
en: Becoming panic-stricken, cried aloud and did see none who could protect them. Seeing this great and wonderful feat of the Brahma might,

sn: विश्वामित्रः क्षत्रभावानिर्विण्णो वाक्यमब्रवीत्। धिग् बलं क्षत्रियबलं ब्रह्मतेजोबलं बलम्॥
en: Vishvamitra become disgusted with the Kshatriya might and spoke thus, "Fie on the Kshatriya prowess? The Brahma might is the true might.

sn: बलाबलं विनिश्चित्य तप एव परं बलम्। स राज्यं स्फीतमुत्सृज्यां तां च दीप्तां नृपश्रियम्॥
en: In judging of strength and weakness, I see asceticism is true strength.” Thereupon that best of kings abandoning his kingdom and regal splendour,

sn: भोगांश्च पृष्ठतः कृत्वा तपस्येव मनो दधे। स गत्वा तपसा सिद्धिं लोकान् विष्टभ्य तेजसा॥
en: And turning his back on all pleasures, set his mind on asceticism, he filled the world with his effulgence.

sn: तताप सर्वान् दीप्तौजा ब्राह्मणत्वमवाप्तवान्। अपिबच्च ततः सोममिन्द्रेण सह कौशिकः॥
en: Afflicted all with his effulgence, he became a Brahmana. The son of Kushika, (Vishvamitra) at last drank the Soma (ambrosia) with Indra himself.

sn: गन्धर्व उवाच कल्माषपाद इत्येवं लोके राजा बभूव ह। इक्ष्वाकुवंशजः पार्थ तेजसा सदृशो भुवि॥
en: The Gandharva said : O Partha there was a king named Kalmashapada in this world. He belonged to the race of Ikshaku and he was matchless in prowess.

sn: स कदाचिद् वनं राजा मृगयां निर्ययौ पुरात्। मृगान् विध्यन् वराहांश्च चचार रिपुमर्दनः॥
en: One day the king came out of his capital for the purpose of hunting. That chastiser of foes pierced (with his arrows) many deer and boars.

sn: तस्मिन् वने महाघोरे खगांश्च बहुशोऽहनत्। हत्वा च सुचिरं श्रान्तो राजा निववृते ततः॥
en: He also killed in that greatly fearful forest many rhinoceroses. Thus killing (animals) for a long period, the king became tried and refrained from it.

sn: अकामयत् तं याज्यार्थे विश्वामित्रः प्रतापवान्। स तु राजा महात्मानं वासिष्ठमृषिसत्तमम्॥ तृषार्तश्च क्षुधार्तश्च एकायनगतः पथि। अपश्यदजित: संख्ये मुनि प्रतिमुखागतम्॥ शक्तिं नाम महाभागं वसिष्ठकुलवर्धनम्। ज्येष्ठं पुत्रं पुत्रशताद् वसिष्ठस्य महात्मनः॥
en: (One day) when the king, whom the greatly powerful Vishvamitra desired to make his spiritual disciple, was proceeding through the forest afflicted with hunger and thirst he met with that best of Rishis, the high-souled son of Vasishtha, the illustrious perpetuator of Vasishtha's race, the eldest of the one hundred sons of the illustrious Rishi Vasishtha, known by the name of Shakti, coming along the same path from an opposite direction.

sn: अपगच्छ पथोऽस्माकमित्येवं पार्थिवोऽब्रवीत्। तथा ऋषिरुवाचैनं सान्त्वयश्लक्ष्णया गिरा॥
en: The king said, Stand out of our way." Thereupon the Rishi spoke thus in a conciliatory manner and in sweet words,

sn: मम पन्था महाराज धर्म एष सनातनः। राज्ञा सर्वेषु धर्मेषु देयः पन्था द्विजातये॥
en: “O great king, this is my way. This is eternal religion. The king should yield the way to the Brahmanas according to all the precepts of religion.”

sn: एवं परस्परं तौ तु पथोऽर्थं वाक्यमूचतुः। अपसर्पापसर्पति वागुत्तरमकुर्वताम्॥
en: Thus they addressed each other respected their right of way. "Stand aside,” “Stand aside,” were the words they said to each other.

sn: ऋषिस्तु नापचक्राम तस्मिन् धर्मपथे स्थितः। नापि राजा मुनेर्मानात् क्रोधाच्चाथ जगाम ह॥
en: The Rishi, being in the right, did not yield; the king also did not yield out of anger and pride.

sn: अमुञ्चन्तं तु पन्थानं तमृषि नृपसत्तमः। जघान कशया मोहात् तदा राक्षसवन्मुनिम्॥
en: Being enraged on seeing the Rishi decline to yield the way to him, that best of kings, acted like a Rakshasa and he struck him violently with his whips.

sn: कशाप्रहाराभिहतस्ततः स मुनिसत्तमः। तं शशाप नृपश्रेष्ठं वासिष्ठं क्रोधमूर्च्छितः॥
en: That best of Rishis, the son of Vasishtha, being thus struck by the whip, was deprived of his (good) senses and out of anger, cursed that best of kings.

sn: हंसि राक्षसवद् यस्माद् राजापसद तापसम्। तस्मात् त्वमद्यप्रभृति पुरुषादो भविष्यसि॥ मनुष्यपिशिते सक्तश्चरिष्यसि महीमिमाम्। गच्छ राजाधमेत्युक्तः शक्तिना वीर्यशक्तिना॥
en: The Rishi said: O worst of kings, as you injure an ascetic a Rakshasas, you shall from this day be a cannibal. O worst of kings, go hence. You shall wander over the world eating human flesh.

sn: ततो याज्यनिमित्ते तु विश्वामित्रवसिष्ठयोः। वैरमासीत् तदा तं तु विश्वामित्रोऽन्वपद्यत॥
en: At this time Vishvamitra, with whom Vasishtha had a great quarrel on the matter of becoming the priest (of the king Kalmashapada), came to the place (where Vasishtha's son and the king were.)

sn: तयोर्विवदतोरेवं समीपमुपचक्रमे। ऋषिरुग्रतपाः पार्थ विश्वामित्रः प्रतापवान्॥
en: O Partha, the Rishi of severe ascetic penances, the powerful Vishvamitra, came there where they were both quarrelling.

sn: ततः स बुबुधे पश्चात् तमृषि नृपसत्तमः। ऋषे पुत्रं वसिष्ठस्य वसिष्ठमिव तेजसा॥
en: Thereupon after the curse on the excellent king (had been uttered) he came to know that the Rishi was the son of Vasishtha as powerful as Vasishtha himself.

sn: अन्तर्धाय तदाऽऽत्मानं विश्वामित्रोऽपि भारत। तावुभावतिचक्रांम चिर्कीपन्नात्मनः प्रियम्॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, being desirous of benefiting himself, Vishvamitra remained there concealed from the sight of both by making himself invisible.

sn: स तु शप्तस्तदा तेन शक्तिना वै नृपोत्तमः। जगाम शरणं शक्तिं प्रसादयितुमर्हयन्॥
en: Then that best of kings, (Kalmashapada), having been thus cursed by Shakti, asked the protection of Shakti by humbly beseeching him.

sn: तस्य भावं विदित्वा स नृपतेः कुरुसत्तम। विश्वामित्रस्ततो रक्ष आदिदेश नृपं प्रति॥
en: O best of the Kuru race, knowing the disposition of the king, Vishvamitra ordered a Rakshasas to enter the king's body.

sn: शापात् तस्य तु विप्रपेर्विश्वामित्रस्य चाज्ञया। राक्षस: किंकरो नाम विवेश नृपतिं तदा॥
en: Obedient to Shakti's curse and Vishvamitra's order, a Rakshasas, named Kinkara, then entered the king body.

sn: रक्षसा तं गृहीतं तु विदित्वा मुनिसत्तमः। विश्वामित्रोऽप्यपाक्रामत् तस्माद् देशादरिंदम॥
en: O chastiser of foes, knowing that the Rakshasas had entered the body of the king, that best of Rishis, Vishvamitra, left the place and went away.

sn: ततः स नृपतिस्तेन रक्षसान्तर्गतेन वै। बलवत् पीडितः पार्थ नान्वबुध्यत किंचन॥
en: O Partha, then the king, being thus possessed by the Rakshasas and terribly afflicted by him, lost all his senses.

sn: ददर्शाथ द्विजः कश्चिद् राजानं प्रस्थितं वनम्। अयाचत क्षुधापन्नः समांसं भोजनं तदा॥
en: A certain Brahmana saw the king roaming in the forest. being hungry, he begged of the king some food with meat.

sn: तमुवाचाथ राजर्षिर्द्विजं मित्रसहस्तदा। आस्स्व ब्रह्मंस्त्वमत्रैव मुहूर्त प्रतिपालयन्॥
en: The royal sage (Kalmashapada) with his friends said to the Brahmana, “O Brahmana, Stay here for a moment,

sn: निवृत्तः प्रतिदास्यामि भोजनं ते यथेप्सितम्। इत्युक्तवा प्रययौ राजा तस्थौ च द्विजसत्तमः॥
en: On my return I shall give you whatever food you desire to have." Having said this, the king went away, but that excellent Brahmana remained there.

sn: ततो राजा परिक्रम्य यथाकामं यथासुखम्। निवृत्तौऽन्तःपुरं पार्थ प्रविवेश महात्मनाः॥
en: O Partha, that high-minded king, after roaming at pleasure and at will (for sometime), returned (to his palace) and entered the innerapartment.

sn: ततोऽर्धरात्र उत्थाय सूदमानाय्य सत्वरम्। उवाच राजा संस्मृत्य ब्राह्मणस्य प्रतिश्रुतम्॥
en: Waking at midnight and remembering his promise to the Brahmana, the king soon summoned his cook and spoke to him thus. The King said:

sn: गच्छामुष्मिन् वनोद्देशे ब्राह्मणो मां प्रतीक्षते। अन्नार्थी तं त्वमन्नेन समांसेनोपपादय॥
en: Go at once to the forest where a Brahmana is waiting for me in the hope of getting food. Go and entertain him with food and meat.

sn: गन्धर्व उवाच एवमुक्तस्तत: सूदः सोऽनासाद्यामिषं क्वचित्। निवेदयामास तदा तस्मै राज्ञे व्यथान्वितः॥
en: The Gandharva said : Having been thus addressed, the cook (went away in search of meat), but having failed to procure any meat, he sorrowfully informed the king (of his failure).

sn: राजा तु रक्षसाऽऽविष्टः सूदमाद गतव्यथः। अप्येनं नरमांसेन भोजयेति पुनः पुनः॥
en: The king, possessed as he was by the Rakshasas, again said to the cook without any scruple, “Feed him with human flesh."

sn: तथेत्युक्त्वा तत: सूदः संस्थानं वध्यघातिनाम्। गत्वाऽऽजहार त्वरितो नरमांसमपेतभीः॥
en: Saying "Be it so," the cook went to the place where the executioners were and he soon took from them human flesh.

sn: एतत् संस्कृत्य विधिवदन्नोपहितमाशु वै। तस्मै प्रादाद् ब्राह्मणाय क्षुधिताय तपस्विने॥
en: He washed it and then properly cooked it and then covering it with boiled rice, he gave it to the hungry ascetic Brahmana.

sn: स सिद्धचक्षुषा दृष्ट्वा तदन्नं द्विजसत्तमः। अभोज्यमिदमित्याह क्रोधपर्याकुलेक्षणः॥
en: That excellent Brahmana, seeing by his ascetic eye that the food was unworthy of being eaten, thus spoke with his eyes red in anger.

sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच यस्मादभोज्यमन्ने मे ददाति स नृपाधमः। तस्मात् तस्यैव मूढस्य भविष्यत्यत्र लोलुपा॥
en: The Brahmana said : Because that worst of kings offers me unworthy food, therefore that fool himself will be fond of such food.

sn: सक्तो मानुषभांसेषु यथोक्तः शक्तिना तथा। उद्वेजनीयो भूतानां चरिष्यति महीमिमाम्॥
en: Becoming fond of human flesh as cursed by Shakti before, he shall wander over the earth, persecuting all creatures.

sn: द्विरनुव्याहृते राज्ञः स शापो बलवानभूत्। रक्षोवलसमाविष्टो विसंज्ञश्चाभवन्नृपः॥
en: The Gandharva said : The curse on the king, thus repeated for the second time, became very strong. And the king being possessed of the Rakshasas disposition, soon lost all his senses.

sn: ततः स नृपतिश्रेष्ठो रक्षसापहतेन्द्रियः। उवाच शक्तिं तं दृष्ट्वा न चिरादिव भारत॥
en: Thereupon, O descendant of Bharata, that best of kings, having been deprived of all his senses by the Rakshasas within him and having seen before him Shakti who had cursed him, said,

sn: यस्मादसदृशः शापः प्रयुक्तोऽयं मयि त्वया। तस्मात् त्वत्तः प्रवर्तिष्ये खादितुं पुरुषानहम्॥
en: "Because you have inflicted upon me this extraordinary curse, therefore, shall commence my life of cannibalism by eating you.

sn: एवमुक्त्वा ततः सद्यस्तं प्राणैर्विप्रयुज्य च। शक्तिनं भक्षयामास व्याघ्रः पशुमिवेप्सितम्॥
en: Having said this, the king immediately killed Shakti and ate him up as a tiger eats up the animal it is fond of.

sn: शक्तिनं तु मृतं दृष्ट्वा विश्वामित्रः पुनः पुनः। वसिष्ठस्यैव पुत्रेषु तद् रक्षः संदिदेश ह॥
en: Having seen Shakti thus killed. Vishvamitra again urged that Rakshasas (within the king) to kill the other sons of Vasishtha.

sn: स ताञ्छक्त्यवरान् पुत्रान् वसिष्ठस्य महात्मनः। भक्षयामास संक्रुद्धः सिंहः क्षुद्रमृगानिव॥
en: He (the Rakshasas) devoured in anger all the sons of the illustrious Vasishtha, the younger brothers of Shakti as a lion devours smali animals.

sn: वसिष्ठो घातिताञ्छ्रुत्वा विश्वामित्रेण तान् सुतान्। धारयामास तं शोकं महाद्रिरिव मेदिनीम्॥
en: Having learnt that his sons had been caused to be killed by Vishvamitra, Vasishtha patiently bore his grief, as the great mountain bears the earth.

sn: चक्रे चात्मविनाशाय बुद्धि स मुनिसत्तमः। न त्वेव कौशिकोच्छेदं मेने मतिमतां वरः॥
en: That best of Rishis, that foremost of all intelligent men (Vasishtha), resolved rather to sacrifice his own life than to exterminate the race of the Kushikas.

sn: स मेरुकूटादात्मानं मुमोच भगवानृपिः। गिरेस्तस्य शिलायां तु तूलराशविवापतत्॥
en: The illustrious Rishi threw himself down from the summit of the Meru mountain, but he descended on the stony ground as if it was a heap of cotton.

sn: न ममार च पातेन स यदा तेन पाण्डव। तदाग्निमिद्धं भगवान् संविवेश महावने॥
en: O son of Pandu, when the illustrious (Rishi) found that he was not killed by that fall, he made a huge fire in that great forest and entered it.

sn: तं तदा सुसमिद्धोऽपि न ददाह हुताशनः । दीप्यमानोऽप्यमित्रघ्न शीतोऽग्निरभवत् ततः॥
en: The fire, through blazing fearfully, did not consume him. O chastiser of foes, that blazing fire seemed to him cool.

sn: स समुद्रमभिप्रेक्ष्य शोकविष्टो महामुनिः। बद्धवा कण्द्दे शिलां गुरु निपपात तदाम्भसि॥
en: Then seeing the sea (before him), the great Rishi, affected with grief, tied a heavy stone to his neck and threw himself into its waters.

sn: स समुद्रोर्मिवेगेन स्थले न्यस्तो महामुनिः। न ममार यदा विप्रः कथंचित् संशितव्रतः। जगाम स ततः खिन्नः पुनरेवाश्रमं प्रति॥
en: The great Rishi was with great force brought by the waves to the shore. He then returned to his hermitage with a sorrowful heart.

description: Birth of the son of Saudasya
sn: गन्धर्व उवाच ततो दृष्ट्वाऽऽश्रमपदं रहितं तैः सुतैर्मुनिः। निर्जगाम सुदुःखार्तः पुनरप्याश्रमात् ततः॥
en: The Gandharva said : Seeing his hermitage bereft of his children, the Rishi, afflicted with grief, again came out of it.

description: Birth of the son of Saudasya
sn: सोऽपश्यत् सरितं पूर्णां प्रावृटकाले नवाम्भसा। वृक्षान् बहुविधान् पार्थ हरन्ती तीरजान् बहून्॥
en: O Partha, (in course of his wandering), he saw a river swollen with the waters of the rainy season, it was sweeping away many trees and plants that grew on its banks.

description: Birth of the son of Saudasya
sn: अथ चिन्तां समापेदे पुनः कौरवन्दन। अम्भस्यस्या निमज्जेयमिति दुःखसमन्वितः॥
en: O descendant of Kuru, seeing this, the sorrowful Rishi began to ponder and thought that he would certainly be killed if he fell into its waters.

description: Birth of the son of Saudasya
sn: ततः पाशैस्तदाऽऽत्मानं गाढं बद्धवा महामुनिः। तस्या जले महानद्या निममज्ज सुदुःखितः॥
en: Thereupon the great Rishi tied himself with very strong cords and fell in grief into the waters of that great river.

description: Birth of the son of Saudasya
sn: अथ छित्त्वा नदी पाशांस्तस्यारिबलसूदन। स्थलस्थं तमृषि कृत्वा विपाशं समवासृजत्॥
en: O chastiser of hostile ranks, the river, having torn those cords and making him free of them, cast him on the land.

description: Birth of the son of Saudasya
sn: उत्ततार तत: पाशैर्विमुक्तः स महानृषिः। विपाशेति च नामास्या नद्याश्चक्रे महानृषिः॥
en: Having been freed from the cords, the great Rishi rose (from the shore) and he gave that river the name of Vipasha.

description: Birth of the son of Saudasya
sn: शोकबुद्धिं तदा चक्रे न चैकत्र व्यतिष्ठत। सोऽगच्छत पर्वतांश्चैव सरितश्च संरासि च॥
en: Being oppressed with grief, that Rishi could not from that time stay at one place. He went to the mountains, rivers and lakes.

description: Birth of the son of Saudasya
sn: दृष्ट्वा स पुनरेवर्निदीं हैमवतीं तदा। चण्डग्राहवती भीमां तस्याः स्रोतस्यपातयत्॥
en: Seeing once more the river Himavati of terrible appearance and full of fierce animals, the Rishi threw himself into its waters.

description: Birth of the son of Saudasya
sn: सा तमग्निसमं विप्रमनुचिन्त्य सरिद्वरा। शतधा विद्रुता यस्माच्छतदुरिति विश्रुता॥
en: That best of rivers, thinking the Brahmana to be fire, immediately fled away in a hundred different streams and thence was she called the Shatadru.

description: Birth of the son of Saudasya
sn: ततः स्थलगतं दृष्ट्वा तत्राप्यात्मानमात्मना। मर्तुं न शक्यमित्युक्त्वा पुनरेवाश्रमं ययौ॥
en: Thereupon, seeing himself again in dry land (he said), "(Alas)! I am not able to die by my own hands.” Saying this, (the Rishi) again went to (his own) hermitage.

description: Birth of the son of Saudasya
sn: स गत्वा विविधाञ्छैलान् देशान् बहुविधांस्तथा। अदृश्यन्त्याख्यया वध्वाथाश्रमेऽनुसृतोऽभवत्॥
en: When he was thus returning, crossing various mountains and countries, his daughterin-law Adrishyanti was following him.

description: Birth of the son of Saudasya
sn: अथ शुश्राव संगत्या वेदाध्ययननिः :स्वनम्। पृष्ठतः परिपूर्णार्थं षड्भिरङ्गैरलंकृतम्॥
en: He heard from behind, as she neared him, the sound of the well-explained recitations of the Vedas with its six ornaments (of elocution).

description: Birth of the son of Saudasya
sn: अनुव्रजति कोन्वेष मामित्येवाथ सोऽब्रवीत्। अहमित्यदृश्यन्तीमं सा स्नुषा प्रत्यभाषत। शक्तेर्भार्या महाभाग तपोयुक्ता तपस्विनी॥
en: He said, “Who is it that follows me?" His daughter-in-law replied, “I am Adrishyanti, the wife of Shakti. I am an ascetic woman, engaged in asceticism."

description: Birth of the son of Saudasya
sn: वसिष्ठ उवाच पुत्रि कस्यैष साङ्गम्य वेदस्याध्ययनस्वनः। पुरा साङ्गम्य वेदस्य शक्तेरिव मया श्रुतः॥
en: Vasishtha said: O daughter, whose is this sound of the recitations of the Vedas with their Angas, that is heard by me and (which is exactly) like the recitations of the Vedas and the Angas by Shakti?

description: Birth of the son of Saudasya
sn: अदृश्यन्त्युवाच अयं कुक्षौ समुत्पन्नः शक्तेर्गर्भः सुतस्य ते। समा द्वादश तस्येह वेदानभ्यस्यतो मुने॥
en: Adrishyanti said : In my womb is a child begotten by your son Shakti. He has been here (studying the Vedas) for twelve years. You have heard the recitations (of the Vedas) by that Rishi.

description: Birth of the son of Saudasya
sn: गन्धर्व उवाच एवमुक्तस्तया हृष्टो वसिष्ठः श्रेष्ठभागृषिः। अस्ति संतानमित्युक्त्वा मृत्योः पार्थ न्यवर्तत॥
en: The Gandharva said: Having been thus addressed by her, that best of Rishis, Vasishtha, became exceedingly glad. O Partha, saying, "There is a child (of my race)”, he refrained from self-destruction.

description: Birth of the son of Saudasya
sn: ततः प्रतिनिवृत्तः स तया वध्वा सहानघ। कल्माषपादमासीनं ददर्श विजने वने।॥
en: The sinless (Rishi), accomplished by his daughter-in-law, returned (to his hermitage). He saw (one day) Kalmashapada sitting in a solitary forest.

description: Birth of the son of Saudasya
sn: स तु दृष्टैव तं राजा क्रुद्ध उत्थाय भारत। आविष्टो रक्षसोग्रेण इयेषात्तुं तदा मुनिम्॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, on seeing him the king at once rose in anger and as he was possessed with the Rakshasas, he desired to devour the Rishi.

description: Birth of the son of Saudasya
sn: अदृश्यन्ती तु तं दृष्ट्वा क्रूरकर्माणमग्रतः। भयसंविग्नया वाचा वसिष्ठमिदमब्रवीत्॥
en: Seeing that that king of cruel of cruel deeds, Adrishyanti spoke thus to Vasishtha in anxiety and fear,

description: Birth of the son of Saudasya
sn: असौ मृत्युरिवोगेण दण्डेन भगवन्नितः। प्रगृहीतेन काष्ठेन राक्षसोऽभ्येति दारुणः॥
en: O illustrious Sir, the fearful Rakshasas (looking) like Death himself armed with his staff is coming towards us with a wooden club in his hand.

description: Birth of the son of Saudasya
sn: तं निवारयितुं शक्तो नान्योऽस्ति भुवि कश्चन। त्वदृतेऽद्य महाभाग सर्ववेदविदांवर॥
en: O illustrious Sir, O best of all learned men in the Vedas, there is none else except you in the world who can restrain him today.

description: Birth of the son of Saudasya
sn: पाहि मां भगवन् पापादस्माद् दारुणदर्शनात्। राक्षसोऽयमिहात्तुं वै नूनमावां समीहते॥
en: O illustrious Sir, save me from this cruel wretch of fearful appearance. The Rakshasas is certainly coming towards us to devour us.

description: Birth of the son of Saudasya
sn: वसिष्ठ उवाच मा भैः पुत्रि न भेतव्यं राक्षसात् तु कथंचन। नैतद् रक्षो भयं यस्मात् पश्यसि त्वमुपस्थितम्॥
en: Vasishtha said : O daughter, do not fear; there is nothing to be afraid of from any Rakshasas. There is no fear from Rakshasas whom you see coming.

description: Birth of the son of Saudasya
sn: राजा कल्माषपादोऽयं वीर्यवान् प्रथितो भुवि। स एषोऽस्मिन् वनोद्देशे निवसत्यतिभीषणः॥
en: He is the king Kalmashapada celebrated in the world as being a very powerful (monarch). That fearful man lives in this forest.

description: Birth of the son of Saudasya
sn: गन्धर्व उवाच तमापतन्तं सम्प्रेक्ष्य वसिष्ठो भगवानृषिः। वारयामास तेजस्वी हुकारेणैव भारत॥
en: The Gandharva said : O descendant of Bharata, the illustrious and the effulgent Rishi Vasishtha, seeing him advancing, stopped him by uttering a loud roar.

description: Birth of the son of Saudasya
sn: मन्त्रपूतेन च पुनः स तमभ्युक्ष्य वारिणा। मोक्षयामास वै शापात् तस्माद् योगान्नराधिपम्॥
en: Sprinkling over him water sanctified by Mantras (incantations), he freed the king from the terrible curse.

description: Birth of the son of Saudasya
sn: स हि द्वादश वर्षाणि वासिष्ठस्यैव तेजसा। ग्रस्त आसीद् ग्रेहणेव पर्वकाले दिवाकरः॥
en: He (the king) had been overwhelmed by the effulgence of Vasislitha's son as the sun by the planet (Rahu) at the time of an eclipse.

description: Birth of the son of Saudasya
sn: रक्षसा विप्रमुक्तोऽथ स नृपस्तददू वनं महत्। तेजसा रञ्जयामास संध्याभ्रमिव भास्करः॥
en: Having been thus freed froin the Rakshasas by that Brahmana (Vasishtha) the king illuminated the great forest by his splendour, as the sun illuminates the evening clouds.

description: Birth of the son of Saudasya
sn: प्रतिलभ्य ततः संज्ञामभिवाद्य कृताञ्जलिः। उवाच नृपतिः काले वसिष्ठमृषिसत्तमम्॥
en: Regaining his consciousness, the king saluted the Rishi with joined hands and he thus spoke to that best of Rishis Vasishtha.

description: Birth of the son of Saudasya
sn: सौदासोऽहं महाभाग याज्यस्ते मुनिसत्तम। अस्मिन् काले यदिष्टं ते ब्रूहि किं करवाणि ते॥
en: "O illustrious Sir, I am the son of Saudasa; O excellent Rishi, I am your disciple. Tell me what is your desire now and what I am to do."

description: Birth of the son of Saudasya
sn: वसिष्ठ उवाच वृत्तमेतद् यथाकालं गच्छ राज्यं प्रशाधि वै। ब्राह्मणं तु मनुष्येन्द्र भावमंस्थाः कदाचन।॥
en: Vasishtha said: o king of men, my desire has been fulfilled at the proper time. Return to your kingdom and rliic your subjects. Never (again) disregard the Brahmanas.

description: Birth of the son of Saudasya
sn: राजोवाच नावमंस्ये महाभाग कदाचिद् ब्राह्मणानहम्। त्वनिदेशे स्थितः सम्यक् पूजयिष्याम्यहं द्विजान्॥
en: The King said: O illustrious sir, I shall never again disregard the best Brahmanas. In obedience to your command, I shall properly worship the Brahmanas.

description: Birth of the son of Saudasya
sn: इक्ष्वाकूणां च येनाहमनृणः स्यां द्विजोत्तम। तत् त्वत्तः प्राप्तुमिच्छामि सर्ववेदविदां वर॥
en: O best of the twice-born, O best of all men learned in the Vedas. I desire to obtain from you that by which I may be freed from the debt I owe to the race of Ikshaku.

description: Birth of the son of Saudasya
sn: अपत्यमीप्सितं मह्यं दातुमर्हसि सत्तम। शीलरूपगुणोपेतमिक्ष्वाकुकुलवृद्धये॥
en: O excellent man, you should grant me a son, I desire to have, who will posses beauty, accomplishments and good behaviour.

description: Birth of the son of Saudasya
sn: गन्धर्व उवाच ददानीत्येव तं तत्र राजानं प्रत्युवाच ह। वसिष्ठः परमेष्वासं सत्यसंधो द्विजोत्तमः॥
en: The Gandharva said : The best of the twice born, ever devoted to truth Vasishtha, replied to that great bowman, the king saying, “I will give."

description: Birth of the son of Saudasya
sn: ततः प्रतिययौ काले वसिष्ठः सह तेन वै। ख्यातां पुरीमिमां लोकेष्वयोध्यां मनुजेश्वर॥
en: O king of men, after sometime, Vasishtha, accompanied by him (the king), went to his capital, known all over the world by the name of Ayodhya.

description: Birth of the son of Saudasya
sn: तं प्रजाः प्रतिमोदन्त्यः सर्वाः प्रत्युद्गतास्तदा। विपाप्मानं महात्मानं दिवौकस इवेश्वरम्॥
en: The people came out in joy to receive the sinless and the illustrious one, as the celestials do their chief (Indra).

description: Birth of the son of Saudasya
sn: सुचिराय मनुष्येन्द्रो नगरी पुण्यलक्षणाम्। विवेश सहिस्तेन वसिष्ठेन महर्षिणा॥
en: The accompanied by the great Rishi Vasishtha entered without delay his auspicious capital.

description: Birth of the son of Saudasya
sn: ददृशुस्तं महीपालमयोध्यावासिनो जनाः। पुरोहितेन सहितं दिवाकरमिवोदितम्॥
en: The citizens of Ayodhya saw the king accompanied by his priest (Vasishtha), as if he were the rising sun.

description: Birth of the son of Saudasya
sn: स च तां पूरयामास लक्ष्या लक्ष्मीवतां वरः। अयोध्यां व्योम शीतांशुः शरत्काल इवोदितः॥
en: The king, most handsome of all handsome men, filled Ayodhya with the whole sky with his splendour.

description: Birth of the son of Saudasya
sn: संसिक्तमृष्टपन्थानं पताकाध्वजशोभितम्। मनः प्रह्लादयामास तस्य तत् पुरमुत्तमम्॥
en: His (king's) mind was filled with joy on seeing that excellent city with its well-watered and well-swept streets and with banners and pendants flying all around.

description: Birth of the son of Saudasya
sn: तुष्टपुष्टजनाकीर्णा सा पुरी कुरुनन्दन। अशोभत तदा तेन शक्रेणेवामरावती॥
en: O descendant of Kuru, that city, full of well-fed and happy men, looked as gay as Amravati with the presence of Indra.

description: Birth of the son of Saudasya
sn: ततः प्रविष्टे राजर्षों तस्मिंस्तत् पुरमुत्तमम्। राज्ञस्तस्याज्ञया देवी वसिष्ठमुपचक्रमे॥
en: After the royal sage (the king Kalmashapada) had entered that excellent city, the queen at his command, came to Vasishtha.

description: Birth of the son of Saudasya
sn: ऋतावथ महर्षिः स सम्बभूव तया सह। देव्या दिव्येन विधिना वसिष्ठः श्रेष्ठभागृषिः॥
en: The best of Rishis, Vasishtha, made an agreement with her and he united himself with her according to the highest ordinance.

description: Birth of the son of Saudasya
sn: ततस्तस्यां समुत्पन्ने गर्भे स मुनिसत्तमः। राज्ञाभिवादितस्तेन जगाम मुनिराश्रमम्॥
en: Thereupon, when the queen conceived by him, that best of Rishis (Vasishtha), receiving the salutation of the king, went away to his hermitage.

description: Birth of the son of Saudasya
sn: दीर्घकालेन सा गर्भं सुषुवे न तुं तं यदा। तदा देव्यश्मना कुक्षिं निर्विभेद यशस्विनी॥
en: When she had borne the conception for a long time, the illustrious lady tore open her womb with a piece of stone.

description: Birth of the son of Saudasya
sn: ततोऽपि द्वादशे वर्षं स जज्ञे पुरुषर्षभः। अश्मको नाम राजर्षिः पौदन्यं यो न्यवेशयत्॥
en: Thus was born after a conception of twelve years that best of men, that royal sage, Ashmaka, who founded Pandava (a city).

sn: गन्धर्व उवाच आश्रमस्था ततः पुत्रमदृश्यन्ती व्यजायता शक्तेः कुलकरं राजन् द्वितीयमिव शक्तिनम्॥
en: The Gandharva said : o king, residing in the hermitage, Adrishyanti gave birth to a son who was the perpetuator of Shakti's race and who was like a second Shakti.

sn: जातकर्मादिकास्तस्य क्रियाः स मुनिसत्तमः। पौत्रस्य भरतश्रेष्ठ चकार भगवान् स्वयम्॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, that best of Rishis, that illustrious man (Vasishtha), himself performed the usual birth ceremonies of his grandson.

sn: परासुः स यतस्तेन वसिष्ठः स्थापितो मुनिः। गर्भस्तेन ततो लोके पराशर इति स्मृतः॥
en: Because the Rishi Vasishtha had determined to kill himself, but had refrained from doing it as soon as he heard of the conception, the child (when born) was known in the world by the name of Parashara.

sn: अमन्यत स धर्मात्मा वसिष्ठं पितरं मुनिः। जन्मप्रभृति तस्मिंस्तु पितरीवान्ववर्तत॥
en: That virtuous-minded man (Parashara) knew from the day of his birth Vasishtha as his father and behaved towards him as such.

sn: स तात इति विप्रर्षिर्वसिष्ठं प्रत्यभाषत। मातुः समक्षं कौन्तेय अदृश्यन्त्याः परंतपः॥
en: O son of Kunti, O chastiser of foes the child called the Brahmana Rishi Vasishtha as "father" before his mother Adrishyanti.

sn: तातेति परिपूर्णार्थं तस्य तन्मधुरं वचः। अदृश्यन्त्यश्रुपूर्णाक्षी शृण्वती तमुवाच ह॥
en: Hearing the well explained word "father" uttered sweetly by her son, Adrishyanti with tearful eyes thus spoke to him,

sn: मा तात तात तातेति ब्रूह्येनं पितरं पितुः। रक्षसा भक्षितस्तात तव तातो वनान्तरे॥
en: "O child, do not address your father's father as your father. O son, your father was devoured by a Rakshasas in another forest.

sn: मन्यसे यं त तातेति नैष तातस्तवानघ। आर्य एष पिता तस्य पितुस्तव यशस्विनः॥
en: O sinless one, he is not your father whom you consider to be (your father). The reverend man is the father of your illustrious father.”

sn: स एवमुक्तो दुःखार्तः सत्यवागृषिसत्तमः। सर्वलोकविनाशाय मतिं चक्रे महामनाः॥
en: Having been thus addressed, that truthful and excellent Rishi became grieved and that high-souled man resolved to destroy the whole creation.

sn: तं तथा निश्चितात्मानं स महात्मा महातपाः। ऋषिर्ब्रह्मविदां श्रेष्ठो मैत्रावरुणिरन्त्यधीः॥ वसिष्ठो वारयामास हेतुना येन तच्छृणु।
en: Seeing him resolved in doing this, that high-souled and greatly ascetic Rishi, that best of all men learned in the Vedas, that son of Mitravaruna, that Rishi acquainted with the positive truth, Vasishtha, prevented him (from accomplishing his desire by arguments). Hear them (now).

sn: वसिष्ठ उवाच कृतवीर्य इति ख्यातो बभूव पृथिवीपतिः॥ याज्यो वेदविदां लोके भृगूणां पार्थिवर्षभः।
en: Vasishtha said: There was a great king, known by the name of Kritavirya. That best of kings was in the world the disciple of the Veda knowing Bhrigus.

sn: स तानग्रभुजस्तात धान्येन च धनेन च॥ सोमान्ते तर्पयामास विपुलेन विशाम्पतिः।
en: O child, after performing the Soma sacrifice, the king gratified the revivers of the first portions of Yagna (Brahmanas) with large presents of rice and wealth.

sn: तस्मिन् नृपतिशार्दूले स्वर्यातेऽथ कथंचन॥ बभूव तत्कुलेयानां द्रव्यकार्यमुपस्थितम्। ते॥
en: some When that best of kings went to heaven, his descendants were in want of wealth.

sn: भृगूणां तु धनं ज्ञात्वा राजानः सर्व एव याचिष्णवोऽभिजग्मुस्तांस्ततो भार्गवसत्तमान्।
en: Knowing that the Bhrigus were rich, those kings all went in the grab of baggers to those best of Bhrigus.

sn: भूमौ तु निदधुः केचिद् भृगवो धनमक्षयम्॥ ददुः केचिद् द्विजातिभ्यो ज्ञात्वा क्षत्रियतोभयम्।
en: Some of the Bhrigus to save their wealth buried it under the earth and some from the fear of Kshatriyas gave away their wealth to the Brahmanas.

sn: भृगवस्तु ददुः केचित् तेषां वित्तं यथेप्सितम्॥ क्षत्रियाणां तदा तात कारणान्तरदर्शनात्।
en: O son, some of the Bhrigus, finding no other alternative, gave their wealth to the Kshatriyas as much as they desired.

sn: ततो महीतलं तात क्षत्रियेण यदृच्छया।॥ खनताधिगतं वित्तं केनचिद् भृगुवेश्मनि।
en: (It happened, however) that Kshatriyas, in digging at pleasure a certain house of a Bhrigu, came upon a large treasure.

sn: तद् वित्तं ददृशुः सर्वे समेताः क्षत्रियर्षभाः॥ अवमन्यः ततः क्रोधाद् भृगूस्ताञ्छरणागतान्। निजघ्नुः परमेष्वासाः सर्वास्तान् निशितैः शरैः॥
en: All those best of Kshatriyas assembled there saw that treasure. Enraged at the supposed deceitful conduct of the Bhrigu, those great men killed them all with their arrows, through they asked for protection. Roaming over the world, they killed even the embryos (that were in the wombs of the Bhriguwomen.)

sn: आगर्भादवकृन्तन्तश्चेरुः सर्वां वसुन्धराम्। तत उच्छिद्यमानेषु भृगुष्वेवं भयात् तदा॥
en: When they were thus killed, many Bhrigu Women fled in fear and took shelter in the inaccessible mountains of the Himalayas.

sn: भृगुपन्यो गिरिं दुर्गं हिमवन्तं प्रपेदिरे। तासामन्यतमा गर्भ भयाद् दधे महौजसम्॥
en: One among them, a lady of tapering things, desiring to perpetuate her husband's race, kept a greatly energetic embryo hidden in one of her things.

sn: ऊरुणैकेन वामोरुर्भर्तुः कुलविवृद्धये। तद् गर्भमुपलभ्याशु ब्राह्मणी या भयार्दिता॥
en: A Brahmana woman came to know this fact and she went to the Kshatriyas and out of fear reported it to thein.

sn: गत्वैका कथयामास क्षत्रियाणामुपहरे। ततस्ते क्षत्रिया जग्मुस्तं गर्भं हन्तुमुद्यता:॥
en: Thereupon the Kshatriyas went with the intention of destroying that embryo and saw the Brahmana lady blazing in her own splendour.

sn: ददृशुर्ब्राह्मणी तेऽथ दीप्यमानां स्वतेजसा। अथ गर्भः स भित्त्वोर्स ब्राह्मण्या निर्जगाम ह॥
en: On this the child in her thing came out tearing open the thigh came out tearing open the thigh and dazzling the eyes of the Kshatriyas like a mid day sun.

sn: मुष्णन् दृष्टी: क्षत्रियाणां मध्याह्न इव भास्करः। ततश्चक्षुर्विहीनास्ते गिरिदुर्गेषु बभ्रमुः॥
en: Thereupon they (the Kshatriyas), having been deprived of their sight, began to wander over those inaccessible hills. Being very much distressed for the protection of the faultless Brahmana lady in order to get back their sight.

sn: ततस्ते मोहमापन्ना राजानो नष्टदृष्टयः। ब्राह्मणी शरणं जग्मुर्दृष्ट्यर्थं तामनिन्दिताम्॥ ऊचुश्चैनां महाभागां क्षत्रियास्ते विचेतसः। ज्योतिःप्रहीणा दुःखार्ताः शान्तार्चिष इवाग्नयः॥
en: Afflicted with sorrow and looking like fire blown out on account of the loss of sight, those Kshatriyas addressed that illustrious lady with anxious heart.

sn: भगवत्याः प्रसादेन गच्छेत् क्षत्रं सचक्षुषम्। उपारम्य च गच्छेम सहिताः पापकर्मिणः॥
en: “When we shall be restored to sight by your grace, we shall go away together with our sinful acts.

sn: सपुत्रा त्वं प्रसादं नः कर्तुमर्हसि शोभने। पुनर्दृष्टिप्रदानेन राज्ञः संत्रातुमर्हसि॥
en: O handsome lady, you with your son should show mercy on us. You should favour these kings by granting them their sight.”

sn: ब्राह्मण्युवाच नाहं गृहणामि वस्ताता दृष्टी स्मि रुषान्विता। अयं तु भार्गवो नूनमूरुज: कुपितोऽद्य वः॥
en: The Brahmani said : O children, I have not taken your eyesight, nor am I angry with you. This child of the Bhrigu race is certainly angry with you.

sn: तेन चढूंषि वस्ताता व्यक्त कोपान्महात्मना। स्मरता निहतान् बन्धूनादत्तानि न संशयः॥
en: O children, there is no doubt your eyesight has been destroyed by this high-souled (Garbha) whose wrath has been kindled on remembering the massacre of his race.

sn: गर्भानपि यदा यूयं भृगूणां जत पुत्रकाः। तदायमूरुणा गर्भो मया वर्षशतं धृतः॥
en: O children, when you were destroying even the embryos of the Bhrigu race, this child was held by in my thigh for one hundred years.

sn: षडङ्गश्चाखिलो वेद इमं गर्भस्थमेव ह। विवेश भृगुवंशस्य भूयः प्रियचिकीर्षया॥
en: So that he may do good to the Bhrigu race, the entire Vedas with their six Angas came to him when he was in the womb.

sn: सोऽयं पितृवधान व्यक्तं क्रोधाद् वो हन्तुमिच्छति। तेजसा तस्य दिव्येन चढूंषि मुषितानि वः॥
en: Being enraged at the slaughter of his fathers; he desires to kill you, it is by his celestials effulgence that your eye-sight has been destroyed.

sn: तमेव यूयं याचध्वमौर्वं मम सुत्तोत्तमम्। अयं वः प्रणिपातेन तुष्टो दृष्टी: प्रमोक्ष्यति॥
en: O children, therefore, pray to my this excellent son, born of my thigh. Propitiated by your homage and by your bowing down your head to him, he may restore your eye-sight.

sn: एवमुक्तास्ततः सर्वे राजानस्ते तमूरुजम्। ऊचुः प्रसीदेति तदा प्रसादं च चकार सः॥
en: Having been thus addressed, all the kings addressed that thigh-born child, saying 'Be propitious"; and the child became propitious to them.

sn: अनेनैव च विख्यातो नाम्ना लोकेषु सत्तमः। स और्व इति विप्रर्षिरूकै भित्त्वा व्यजायत॥
en: As he was born after tearing open his mother's thigh, that excellent Brahmana came to be know throughout the world by the name of Aurva.

sn: चढूंषि प्रतिलस्वा च प्रतिजग्मुस्ततो नृपाः। भार्गवस्तु मुनिमेने सर्वलोकपराभवम्॥
en: Regaining their eye-sight, the kings returned to their homes) and that descendant of Bhrigu resolved in his mind to overcome the world.

sn: वसिष्ठ उवाच स चक्रे तात लोकानां विनाशाय महामनाः। सर्वेषामेव कात्स्न्येन मनः प्रवणमात्मनः॥ इच्छन्नपचितिं कर्तुं भृगूणां भृगुनन्दनः। सर्वलोकविनाशाय तपसा महतैधितः॥
en: Vasishtha said : O child, the high-souled man set his heart on the destruction of all creatures. In order to pay homage to his massacred ancestors, the descendant of the Bhrigu race engaged himself in the severest penances with the object of destroying the whole creation.

sn: तापयामास ताँल्लोकान् सदेवासुरमानुषान्। तपसोग्रेण महता नन्दयिष्यन् पितामहान्॥
en: He afflicted the worlds with the celestials, the Asuras and the men by his greatly serve penances; and he thus gratified his ancestors.

sn: ततस्तं पितरस्तात विज्ञाय कुलनन्दनम्। पितृलोकादुपागम्य सर्व ऊचुरिदं वचः॥
en: On learning what their son was doing in order to gratify their race, the Pitris all came to him from their region and said.

sn: पितर ऊचुः और्व दृष्टः प्रभावस्ते तपसोग्रस्य पुत्रका प्रसादं कुरु लोकानां नियच्छ क्रोधमात्मनः॥
en: The Pitris said : O Aurva, O son, fierce you have become by your asceticism. Your power has been seen by us. Be propitious to the worlds; control your anger.

sn: नानीशैर्हि तदा तात भृगुभिर्भावितात्मभिः। वधो ह्युपेक्षितः सर्वैः क्षत्रियाणां विहिंसताम्॥
en: O child, it was not from incapacity that the self-controlled Bhrigus were all indifferent to their own destruction caused by the murderous Kshatriyas.

sn: आयुषा विप्रकृष्टेन यदा नः खेद आविशत्। तदास्माभिर्वधस्तात क्षत्रियैरीप्सितः स्वयम्॥
en: O child, when we grew tried with our long life, then it was that we desired our own death at the hands of the Kshatriyas.

sn: निखातं यच्च वै वित्तं केनचिद् भृगुवेश्मनि। वैरायैव तदा न्यस्तं क्षत्रियान् कोपयिष्णुभिः॥
en: The wealth that the Bhrigus have kept hidden under the earth had been placed there with the object of enraging the Kshatriyas and creating a quarrel with them.

sn: किं हि वित्तेन नः कार्यं स्वर्गेप्सूनां द्विजोत्तम। यदस्माकं धनाध्यक्षः प्रभूतं धनमाहरत्॥
en: O best of the twice born, of what use could wealth be to us who were desirous of obtaining heaven? Our treasurer (in heaven) has kept large treasures for us.

sn: यदा तु मृत्युरादातुं न नः शक्नोति सर्वशः। तदास्माभिरयं दृष्ट उपायस्तात सम्मतः॥
en: When we found that death could by no means overtake us all, then, O child, we considered this to be the best means (of destroying us.)

sn: आत्महा च पुमांस्तात न लोकॉल्लभते शुभान्। ततोऽस्माभिः समीक्ष्यैवं नात्मनाऽऽत्मा निपातितः॥
en: O child, those that commit suicide never attain to the blessed regions. Considering this, we abstained from self-destruction.

sn: न चैतन्नः प्रियं तात यदिदं कर्तुमिच्छसि। नियच्छेदं मनः पापात् सर्वलोकपराभवात्॥
en: O child, that which you desire to do is not pleasing to us. Therefore, control your mind and abstain from overcoming the whole world.

sn: मा वधीः क्षत्रियांस्तात न लोकान् सप्त पुत्रका दूषयन्तं तपस्तेजः क्रोधमुत्पतितं जहि॥
en: O child, O son, do not destroy your this anger which stains your ascetic effulgence. i

sn: और्व उवाच उक्तवानस्मि यां क्रोधात् प्रतिज्ञां पितरस्तदा। सर्वलोकविनाशाय न सा मे वितथा भवेत्॥
en: Arjuna said : O Pitris, the vow I uttered in anger for the destruction of all the worlds must not be in vain.

sn: वृथारोषप्रतिज्ञो वै नाहं भवितुमुत्सहे। अनिस्तीर्णो हि मां रोषो दहेदग्निरिवारणिम्॥
en: I cannot to be one whose anger and vows are fruitless. This my anger will certainly consume me (if I do not accomplish my vow), as fire consumes the dry wood.

sn: यो हि कारणतः क्रोधं संजातं क्षन्तुमर्हति। नालं स मनुजः सम्यक् त्रिवर्गं परिरक्षितुम्॥
en: The men, who suppresses his anger excited by a just cause, becomes incapable of duly compassing the Three varga (Dharma, Artha and Kama.)

sn: अशिष्टानां नियन्ता हि शिष्टानां परिरक्षिता। स्थाने रोषः प्रयुक्तः स्यान्नृपैः सर्वजिगीषुभिः॥
en: The wrath, that the kings, desirous of subjugating the whole world, display, has its use. It serves to restrain the wicked and protect the honest.

sn: अश्रौषमहमूरुस्थो गर्भशय्यागतस्तदा। आरावं मातृवर्गस्य भृगूणां क्षत्रियैर्वधे॥
en: When I was lying unborn within my mother and other women of the Bhrigu race as they were being massacred by the Kshatriyas.

sn: संहारो हि यदा लोके भृगुणां क्षत्रियाधमैः। आगर्भोच्छेदनात् क्रान्तस्तदा मां मन्युराविशत्॥
en: O Pitris, when those wretches, the Kshatriyas, were exterminating the Bhrigus together with the unborn children to their race, anger filled my soul.

sn: सम्पूर्णकोशाः किल मे मातरः पितस्तथा। भयात् सर्वेषु लोकेषु नाधिजग्मुः परायणम्॥
en: My mother and the other women of our race, each in a state of advanced pregnancy and my father also, though exceedingly afflic did not get a protector in all the world.

sn: तान् भृगूणां यदा दारान् कश्चिन्नाभ्युपपद्यत। माता तदा दधारेयमूरुणैकेन मां शुभा॥
en: When the Bhrigu women did not find a single protector, my blessed mother held me (hidden) in one of her thighs.

sn: प्रतिषेद्वा हि पापस्य यदा लोकेषु विद्यते। तदा सर्वेषु लोकेषु पापकृन्नोपपद्यते॥
en: If there be a punisher of crimes in the world, no one in all the worlds could dare commit a crime.

sn: यदा तु प्रतिषेद्धारं पापो न लभते क्वचित्। तिष्ठन्ति बहवो लोकास्तदा पापेषु कर्मसु॥
en: If sin does not find any punisher, then many men live in sinful acts.

sn: जानन्नपि च यः पापं शक्तिमान् न नियच्छति। ईशः सन् सोऽपि तेनैव कर्मणा सम्प्रयुज्यते॥
en: The man who having power to punish sin, does not do so, knowing that a sin has been committed, is himself defiled by that sin.

sn: राजभिश्चैश्वरैश्चैव यदि वै पितरो मम। शक्तैर्न शकितास्त्रातुमिष्टं मत्वेह जीवितम्॥ अत एषामहं क्रुद्धो लोकानामीश्वरो ह्ययम्। भवतां च वचो नालमहं समभिवर्तितुम्॥
en: The kings and others, who were capable of protecting my fathers, did not protect them, neglecting to perform their duty by giving themselves up to the pleasures of life. Therefore, I have just cause to be enraged. I am the lord of creation, I am incapable of obeying your command.

sn: ममापि चेद् भवेदेवमीश्वरस्य सतो महत्। उपेक्षमाणस्य पुनर्लोकानां किल्बिषाद् भयम्॥
en: Capable as I am of punishing this crime, if I abstain from doing it, men will once more have to undergo a similar persecution.

sn: यश्चाहं मन्युजो मेऽग्निर्लोकानादातुमिच्छति। दहेदेष च मामेव निगृहीतः स्वतेजसा॥
en: The fire of my wrath, which is ready to consume the worlds, if suppressed, will certainly consume me by its own energy.

sn: भवतां च विजानामि सर्वलोकहितेप्सुताम्। तस्माद् विधध्वं यच्छ्रेयो लोकानां मम चेश्वराः॥
en: O masters, I know you always seek the good of the worlds. Therefore, instruct me as to what may be good to myself or to the worlds.

sn: पितर ऊचुः य एष मन्युजस्तेऽग्निर्लोकानादातुमिच्छति। अप्सु तं मुञ्च भद्रं ते लोका ह्यप्सु प्रतिष्ठिताः॥
en: The Pitris said : Throw this fire of your wrath which desires to consume the worlds into the waters. That will do you good. The worlds rest on water.

sn: आपोमयाः सर्वरसाः सर्वमापोमयं जगत्। तस्मादप्सु विमुञ्चमं क्रोधाग्निं द्विजसत्तम॥
en: Every juicy substance is full of water; indeed the whole universe is full of water. Therefore, O best of the twice born, throw this your anger into the waters.

sn: अयं तिष्ठतु ते विप्र यदीच्छसि महोदधौ। मन्युजोऽग्निर्दहन्नापो लोका ह्यापोमयाः स्मृताः॥
en: O Brahmana, if you desire it, let this fire of your wrath remain in the great ocean, consuming its water, for we have heard the worlds are made of water.

sn: एवं प्रतिज्ञा सत्येयं तवानघ भविष्यति। न चैवं सामरा लोंका गमिष्यन्ति पराभवम्॥
en: O sinless one, in this way your word will be made true and the worlds with the celestials will not be destroyed.

sn: वसिष्ठ उवाच ततस्तं क्रोधजं तात और्वोऽग्निं वरुणालये। उत्ससर्ज च चैवाप उपयुङ्क्ते महोदधौ॥
en: Vasishtha said: Thereupon Aurva threw the fire of his wrath into the abode of Varuna (sea) and that fire consumes the waters of the great ocean.

sn: महद्धयशिरो भूत्वा यत् तद् वेदविदो विदुः। तमग्निमुद्रिद् वक्त्रात् पिबत्यापो महोदधौ॥
en: Assuming a greatly fearful head (that of a horse) and emitting fire from its mouth, it consumes the waters of the great ocean. The men learned in the Vedas call it Vadabamukha.

sn: तस्मात् त्वमपि भद्रं ते न लोकान् हन्तुमर्हसि। पराशर पराँल्लोकान् जानज्ञानवतां वर॥
en: O Parashara, O foremost of all wise men, you are acquainted with the higher regions, you should not destroy the world.

sn: गन्धर्व उवाच एवमुक्तः स विप्रर्षिर्वसिष्ठेन महात्मना। न्ययच्छदात्मनः क्रोधं सर्वलोकपराभवात्॥
en: The Gandharva said : Having been thus addressed by the illustrious Vasishtha, the Brahmana Rishi (Parashara) controlled his word destroying wrath.

sn: ईजे च स महातेजाः सर्ववेदविदां वरः। ऋषी राक्षससत्रेण शाक्तेयोऽथ पराशरः॥
en: But the greatly effulgent Parashara, the son of Shakti, the foremost of all persons learned in the Vedas, performed a great Rakshasas sacrifice.

sn: ततो वृद्धांश्च बालांश्च राक्षसान् स महामुनिः। ददाह वितते यज्ञे शक्तेर्वधमनुस्मरन्॥
en: Remembering the slaughter of Shakti, the great Rishi began to consume the Rakshasas, young and old, in the sacrifice that he performed.

sn: न हि तं वारयामास वसिष्ठो रक्षसां वधात्। द्वितीयामस्य मा भाक्षं प्रतिज्ञामिति निश्चयात्॥
en: Vasishtha from his desire of not obstructing this second vow (of his grandson) did not prevent him from destroying the Rakshasas.

sn: त्रयाणां पावकानां च सत्रे तस्मिन् महामुनिः। आसीत् पुरस्ताद् दीप्तानां चतुर्थ इव पावकः॥
en: The great Rishi (Parashara) sat in that sacrifice before three blazing fires, himself looking a fourth fire.

sn: तेन यज्ञेन शुभ्रेण हूयमानेन शक्तिजः। तद्विदीपितमाकाशं सूर्येणेव धनात्यये॥
en: Like the sun emerged from the clouds, the firmament was illuminated by that stainless sacrifice in which large were the libation of ghee poured.

sn: तं वसिष्ठादयः सर्वे मुनयस्तत्र मेनिरे। तेजसा दीप्यमानं वै द्वितीयमिव भास्करम्॥
en: Then Vasishtha and the other Rishis regarded that Rishi, blazing with his own energy, as if he were a second sun.

sn: ततः परमदुष्प्रापमन्यैर्ऋषिरुदारधीः। समापिपयिषुः सत्रं तमत्रिः समुपागमत्॥
en: Then the great and the liberal-minded Rishi Atri came to that place with the desire of ending that sacrifice, a highly difficult act for any others.

sn: तथा पुलस्त्यः पुलहः क्रतुश्चैव महाक्रतुः। तत्राजग्मुरमित्रघ्न रक्षसां जीवितेप्सया॥
en: O chastiser of foes, there also came Pulaha, Kratu and Mahakratu with the desire of saving the Rakshasas.

sn: पुलस्त्यस्तु वधात् तेषां रक्षसां भरतर्षभ। उवाचेदं वचः पार्थ पराशरमरिंदमम्॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, O Partha, seeing that many Rakshasas had been already killed, Pulastya spoke thus to that chastiser of foes, Parashara,

sn: कच्चित् तातापविलं ते कच्चिन्नन्दसि पुत्रक। अजानतामदोषाणां सर्वेषां रक्षसां वधात्॥
en: “O child, I hope there is no obstruction to your this sacrifice. Do you take, Pleasure, O child, in destroying the Rakshasas who know nothing of your father's death.

sn: प्रजोच्छेदमिमं मह्यं न हि कर्तुं त्वमर्हसि। नैष तात द्विजातीनां धर्मो दृष्टस्तपस्विनाम्॥
en: You should not thus destroy all creatures. O sun, it is not a (proper) act for the Brahmanas devoted to asceticism.

sn: शम एव परो धर्मस्तमाचर पराशर। अधर्मिष्ठं वरिष्ठः सन् कुरुषे त्वं पराशर॥
en: O Parashara, peace is the highest virtue; therefore practice peace. O Parashara, being such a superior man, you (should not) consider sinful acts to be for your good.

sn: शक्तिं चापि हि धर्मज्ञं नातिक्रान्तुमिहार्हसि। प्रजायाश्च ममोच्छेदं न चैवं कर्तुमर्हसि॥
en: You should not transgress against Shakti who was learned in all the precepts of religion. You should not exterminate my creatures.

sn: शापाद्वि शक्तेर्वासिष्ठ तदा तदुपपादितम्। आत्मजेन स दोषेण शक्तिति इतो दिवम्॥
en: O son of Vasishtha, what befell your father all came upon him on account of his own curse. It was for his own fault that Shakti was taken to haven.

sn: न हि तं राक्षसः कश्चिच्छक्तो भक्षयितुं मुने। आत्मनैवात्मनस्तेन दृष्टो मृत्युस्तदाभवत्॥
en: O Rishi, on Rakshasas was capable of devouring him; he himself provided for his death.

sn: निमित्तभूतस्तत्रासीद् विश्वामित्रः पराशर। राजा कल्माषपादश्च दिवमारुह मोदते॥
en: O Parashara, Vishvamitra was mere an instrument in that matter. The king Kalmashapada, also ascending heaven, enjoy great happiness.

sn: ये च शक्त्यवराः पुत्रा वसिष्ठस्य महामुने। ते च सर्वे मुदा युक्ता मोदन्ते सहिताः सुरैः॥
en: Shakti and other sons of the great Rishi Vasishtha are all even now in great happiness enjoying themselves with the celestials.

sn: सर्वमेतद् वसिष्ठस्य विदितं वै महामुने। रक्षसां च समुच्छेद एष तात तपस्विनाम्॥ निमित्तभूतस्त्वं चात्र क्रतौ वासिष्ठनन्दन। तत् सत्रं मुञ्च भद्रं ते समाप्तमिदमस्तु ते॥
en: O great Rishi, all this was known to Vasishtha. O child, O grandson of Vasishtha, you have been in this sacrifice only an instrument in the destruction of those innocent Rakshasas. Be blessed. Give up this sacrifice. Let it come to an end.

sn: गन्धर्व उवाच एवमुक्तः पुलस्त्येन वसिष्ठेन च धीमता। तदा समापयामास सत्रं शाक्तो महामुनिः॥
en: The Gandharva said : Having been thus addressed by Pulastya and the intelligent Vasishtha, the great Rishi, the son of Shakti (Parashara), brought that sacrifice to an end.

sn: सर्वराक्षससत्राय सम्भृतं पावकं तदा। उत्तरे हिमवत्पार्श्वे उत्ससर्ज महावने॥
en: He (Parashara) threw away the fire that was kindled for the Rakshasas-sacrifice into the great forest on the north of the Himalayas.

sn: स तत्राद्यापि रक्षांसि वृक्षानश्मन एव च। भक्षयन् दृश्यते वह्निः सदा पर्वणि पर्वणि॥
en: There that fire may be seen to this day, always devouring in all seasons the Rakshasas, trees and stones.

sn: अर्जुन उवाच राज्ञा कल्माषपादेन गुरौ ब्रह्मविदां वरे। कारणं किं पुरस्कृत्य भार्या वै संनियांजिता॥
en: Arjuna said : Why did the king Kalmashapada command his to do to his preceptor, that foremost of all men learned in the Vedas?

sn: जानता वै परं धर्मं वसिष्ठेन महात्मना। अगम्यागमनं कस्मात् कृतं तेन महर्षिणा॥
en: Why did that great and illustrious Rishi Vasishtha, knowing as he knew all the great precepts of religion, went to a woman to whom he should not go?

sn: अधर्मिष्ठं वसिष्ठेन कृतं चापि पुरा सखे। एतन्मे संशयं सर्वं छेत्तुमर्हसि पृच्छतः॥
en: O friend, was this an act of sin on the part of Vasishtha? I ask, you should remove my these doubts.

sn: गन्धर्व उवाच धनंजय निबोधेदं यन्मां त्वं परिपृच्छसि। वसिष्ठं प्रति दुर्धर्ष तथा मित्रसहं नृपम्॥
en: The Gandharva said : O Dhananjaya, O irrepressible hero, listen to me as I answer the question you have asked me in respect of Vasishtha and that chastiser of foes the king (Kalmashapada).

sn: कथितं ते मया सर्वं यथा शप्तः स पार्थिवः। शक्तिना भरतश्रेष्ठ वासिष्ठेन महात्मना॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, I have told you how the king Kalmashapada was cursed by Shakti, the illustrious son of Vasishtha.

sn: स तु शापवशं प्राप्तः क्रोधपर्याकुलेक्षणः। निर्जगाम पुराद् राजा सहदारः परंतपः॥
en: Thus coming under the influence of that curse, that chastiser of foes, the king with his eyes whirling in anger came out of the city with his wife.

sn: अरण्यं निर्जनं गत्वा सदारः परिचक्रमे। नानामृगगणाकीर्णं नानासत्त्वसमाकुलम्॥ नानागुल्मलताच्छनं नानाद्रुमसमावृतम्। अरण्यं घोरसंनादं शापग्रस्तः परिभ्रमन्॥
en: Going to a solitary forest, he roamed with his wife. He roamed under the influence of the cures in the terribly resounding forest, abounding in various beasts and other animals, overgrown with numerous plants and creepers and full of many large trees.

sn: स कदाचित् क्षुधाविष्टो मृगयन् भक्ष्यमात्मनः। ददर्श सुपरिक्लिष्टः कस्मिंश्चिन्निर्जने वने।॥
en: One day becoming very much oppressed with exceeding hunger, he searched for some food. He saw in a certain solitary wood.

sn: ब्राह्मणं ब्राह्मणीं चैव मिथुनायोपसंगतौ। तौ तं वीक्ष्य सुवित्रस्तावकृतार्थी प्रधावितौ॥
en: A Brahmana and a Brahmani engaged in sexual intercourse. Seeing him they fled away in fear, their desire being unfulfilled.

sn: तयोः प्रद्रवतोर्विप्रं जग्राह नृपतिर्बलात्। दृष्ट्वा गृहीतं भर्तारमथ ब्राह्मण्यभाषत॥
en: Pursuing them the king seized the Brahmana by force. Seeing her husband thus seized, the Brahmani said,

sn: शृणु राजन् मम वचो यत् त्वा वक्ष्यामि सुव्रत। आदित्यवंशप्रभवस्त्वं हि लोके परिश्रुतः॥
en: “O king of excellent vows, listen to what I say; it is known all over the world that you are born in the solar dynasty.

sn: अप्रमत्तः स्थितो धर्म गुरुशुश्रूषणे रतः। शापोपहत दुर्धर्ष न पापं कर्तुमर्हसि॥
en: You are always steadily engaged in Performing virtuous acts, you are ever engaged in serving your superiors; O irresistible hero, though you are deprived of your senses by the curse, you should not commit sin.

sn: ऋतुकाले तु सम्प्राप्ते भर्तृव्यसनकर्शिता। अकृतार्था ह्यहं भर्ता प्रसवार्थं समागता॥
en: On my season's coming, I was united with my husband in order to get offspring; but I have not been successful.

sn: प्रसीद नृपतिश्रेष्ठ भर्तायं मे विसृज्यताम्। एवं विक्रोशमानायास्तस्यास्तु स नृशंसवत्॥ भर्तारं भक्षयामास व्याघ्रो मृगमिवेप्सितम्। तस्याः क्रोधाभिभूताया यान्यश्रूण्यपतन भुवि॥
en: O best of kings, be propitious to me, liberate my husband.” While she was thus crying, the king like a cruel wretch devoured her husband as a lion devours a deer. The tears that fell from eyes on the ground on account of her anger.

sn: सोऽग्निः समभवद् दीप्तस्तं च देशं व्यदीपयत्। ततः सा शोकसंतप्ता भर्तृव्यसनकर्शिता॥
en: Played up like a fire and consumed every thing in that place. Then afflicted with the death of her husband,

sn: कल्माषपादं राजर्षिमशपद् ब्राह्मणी रुषा। यस्मान्ममाकृतार्थायास्त्वया क्षुद्र नृशंसवत्॥ प्रेक्षन्त्या भक्षितो मेऽद्य प्रियो भर्ता महायशाः। तस्मात् त्वमपि दुर्बुद्धे मच्छापपरिविक्षतः॥ पत्नीमृतावनुप्राप्य सद्यस्त्यक्ष्यसि जीवितम्। यस्य चर्षेर्वसिष्ठस्य त्वया पुत्रा विनाशिताः॥
en: The Brahmani cursed the royal sage Kalmashapada in anger. “O wretch, because you have to day cruelly devoured in my very sight my illustrious and beloved husband when I was not gratified, therefore you shall by my curse meet with an instant death when you will unite yourself with your wife in season. That Rishi Vasishtha, whose son you have devoured,

sn: तेन संगम्य ते भार्या तनयं जनविष्यति। स ते वंशकरः पुत्रो भविष्यति नृपाधम॥
en: Will unite himself with your wife to beget a son . O worst of kings, that son will be the perpetuator of your race.

sn: एवं शप्त्वातु राजानं सा तमाङ्गिरसी शुभा। तस्यैव संनिधौ दीप्तं प्रविवेश हुताशनम्॥
en: Having thus cursed him, that blessed lady of the Angirasa race entered the blazing fire in his very presence.

sn: वसिष्ठश्च महाभागः सर्वमेतदवैक्षत। ज्ञानयोगेन महता तपसा च परंतप॥
en: O chastiser of foes, the illustrious Vasishtha immediately know all this by his great asceticism and spiritual sight.

sn: मुक्तशापश्च राजर्षिः कालेन महता ततः। ऋतुकालेऽभिपतितो मदयन्त्या निवारितः॥
en: After long time the royal sage (Kalmashapada) became freed from the curse. And (then one day) he went to his wife Madayanti in her season, but she prevented him.

sn: न हि सस्मार स नृपस्तं शापं काममोहितः। देव्याः सोऽथ वचः श्रुत्वा सम्भ्रान्तो नृपसत्तमः॥
en: Maddened by desire, the king had no recollection of the curse. Hearing the words of the lady (his wife), that best of kings become very much alarmed. a

sn: तं शापमनुसंस्मृत्य पर्यतष्यद् भृशं तदा। एतस्मात् कारणाद् राजा वसिष्ठं संन्ययोजयत्। स्वदारेषु नरश्रेष्ठ शापदोषसमन्वितः॥
en: O best of kings, recollecting the curse, he was very sorry for what he had done. It was for this reason and on account of the Brahmani's curse the king appointed Vasishtha to beget a son on his wife.

sn: अर्जुन उवाच अस्माकमनुरूपो वै यः स्याद् गन्धर्व वेदवित्। पुरोहितस्तमाचक्ष्व सर्वं हि विदितं तव॥
en: Arjuna said : O Gandharva, you are acquainted with every thing. Tell us therefore what Vedaknowing Brahmana is fit, to be appointed as our priest?

sn: गन्धर्व उवाच यवीयान् देवलस्यैष वने भ्राता तपस्यति। धौम्य उत्कोचके तीर्थे वृणुध्वं यदीच्छथ॥
en: The Gandharva said: There is a shrine in this forest, it is called Utkochaka. The younger brother of Devala, Dhaumya, is engaged there in ascetic penances. If you desire, you can appoint him as priest.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततोऽर्जुनोऽस्त्रमाग्नेयं प्रददौ तद् यथाविधि। गन्धर्वाय तदा प्रीतो वचनं चेदमब्रवीत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Then Arjuna, being highly pleased, gave the Gandharva his fire-weapon with due ceremonials; and he thus spoke to him,

sn: त्वय्येव तावत् तिष्ठन्तु हया गन्धर्वसत्तम। कार्यकाले ग्रहीष्यामः स्वस्ति तेऽस्त्विति चाब्रवीत्।।४।
en: "O best of the Gandharvas, let the horses you give us remain with you for sometime. When the time will come, we shall take them from you. Then he said to him, “Be blessed” "Be blessed."

sn: तेऽन्योन्यमभिसम्पूज्य गन्धर्वः पाण्डवाश्च ह। रम्याद् भागीरथीतीराद् यथाकामं प्रतस्थिरे॥
en: Then the Gandharva and the Pandavas, respectfully saluting one another, left the charming banks of the Bhagirathi and went away wherever they liked.

sn: तत उत्कोचकं तीर्थं गत्वा धौम्याश्रमं तु ते। तं वत्रुः पाण्डवा धौम्यं पौरोहित्याय भारत॥
en: Thereupon, O descendant of Bharata, the Pandavas went to the shrine of Utkochaka and to the hermitage of Dhaumya. They them installed Dhaumya as their priest.

sn: तान् धौम्यः प्रतिजग्राह सर्ववेदविदां वरः। वन्येन फलमूलेन पौरोहित्येन चैव ह॥
en: Dhaumya, the foremost of all men learned in the Vedas, received them with the offerings of wild fruits and roots and consented to be their priest.

sn: ते समाशंसिरे लब्धां श्रियं राज्यं च पाण्डवाः। ब्राह्मणं तं पुरस्कृत्य पाञ्चालीं च स्वयंवरे॥ पुरोहितेन तेनाथ गुरुणा संगतास्तदा। नाथवन्तमिवात्मानं मेनिरे भरतर्षभाः॥
en: Having obtained that Brahmana as their priest, the Pandavas with their mother, constituting the sixth of the Party, thought their wealth and kingdom had been already regained and the daughter of the Panchala king already obtained in the Svaimvara. Those best of the Bharata race, having obtained the preceptor Dhaumya as their priest, considered themselves as placed under a protector.

sn: स हि वेदार्थतत्त्वज्ञस्तेषां गुरुरुदारधीः। तेन धर्मविदा पार्था याज्या धर्मविदः कृताः॥
en: The preceptor (Dhaumya) was acquainted with the mystery of the Vedas; he was liberal minded, he made the virtue and all-knowing sons of Pritha his spiritual disciples.

sn: वीरांस्तुसहितान् मेने प्राप्तराज्यान् स्वधर्मतः। बुद्धिवीर्यबलोत्साहैर्युक्तान् देवानिव द्विजः॥
en: That Brahmana, seeing those heroes endued with intelligence, strength and perseverance like the celestials, considered that they were already restored to their wealth and sovereignty by virtue of their own accomplishments.

sn: कृतस्वस्त्ययनास्तेन ततस्ते मनुजाधिपाः। मेनिरे सहिता गन्तुं पाञ्चाल्यास्तं स्वयंवरम्॥
en: Benedictions having been uttered on them by that Brahmana, those kings of men resolved to go with him to the Svaimvara in the country of the Panchalas.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततस्ते नरशार्दूला भ्रातरः पञ्च पाण्डवाः। प्रययुर्दोपदी द्रष्टुं तं च देशं महोत्सवम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Then those best men, the five Pandava brothers, set out out to see Draupadi, the (Panchala) country and the festivities (of Svaimvara.)

sn: ते प्रयाता नरव्याघ्राः सह मात्रा परंतपाः। ब्राह्मणान् ददृशुर्मार्गे गच्छतः संगतान् बहून्॥
en: Those best of men, those chastisers of foes, saw with their mother many Brahmanas on their way going together (towards Panchala).

sn: त ऊचुर्ब्राह्मणा राजन् पाण्डवान् ब्रह्मचारिणः। क्व भवन्तो गमिष्यन्ति कुतो वाभ्यागता इह॥
en: O king, those Brahmacharis, those Brahmanas, asked the Pandavas, “Where are you going? Whence have you come?

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच आगतानेकचक्रायाः सोदर्यानेकचारिणः। भवन्तो वै विजानन्तु सह मात्रा द्विजर्षभाः॥
en: Yudhishthira said : O best of the twice born, know, Sirs, that we are five brothers travelling with our mother. We are now coming from Ekachakra.

sn: ब्राह्मणा ऊचुः गच्छताद्यैव पञ्चालान् दुपदस्य निवेशने। स्वयंवरो महांस्तत्र भविता सुमहाधनः॥
en: The Brahmanas said: Go even this very day to the house of the Panchala Drupada. There will be held a great Svaimvara, in which a large sum of money will be spent. with eyes

sn: एकसार्थं प्रयाताः स्म वयं तत्रैव गामिनः। तत्र ह्यद्भुतसंकाशो भविता सुमहोत्सवः॥
en: We are going there; let us go together. Extraordinary festivities will take place there.

sn: यज्ञसेनस्य दुहिता द्रुपदस्य महात्मनः। वेदीमध्यात् समुत्पन्ना पद्मपत्रनिभेक्षणा॥
en: The daughter of the illustrious Yajnasena Drupada was born from the sacrificial altar, like lotus leaves,

sn: दर्शनीयानवद्याङ्गी सुकुमारी मनस्विनी। धृष्टद्युम्नस्य भगिनी द्रोणशत्रोः प्रतापिनः॥
en: With features faultless and with beauty, youth and intelligence; she is the sister of the powerful Dhrishtadyuman, the (would be) slayer of Drona,

sn: यो जात: कवची खड्गी सशरः सशरासनः। सुसमिद्धे महाबाहुः पावके पावकोपमः॥
en: Who rose as a mighty-armed hero with natural armour, sword, bow and arrows from the blazing fire, himself looking like a second fire.

sn: स्वसा तस्यानवद्याङ्गी द्रौपदी तनुमध्यमा। नीलोत्पलसमो गन्धो यस्याः क्रोशात् प्रवाति वै॥
en: His sister is the slender wasted and faultless featured Draupadi, whose body emits the Perfume of lotus over full two miles around.

sn: यज्ञसेनस्य च सुतां स्वयंवरकृतक्षणाम्। गच्छामो वै वयं द्रष्टुं तं च दिव्यं महोत्सवम्॥
en: That daughter of Yajnasena will select a husband in a Svaimvara. We are going there to see her and witness the great celestials-like festivities.

sn: राजानो राजपुत्राश्च यज्वानो भूरिदक्षिणाः। स्वाध्यायवन्तः शुचयो महात्मानो यतव्रताः॥
en: The kings and princes who are performers of sacrifices in which Dakshina is large, who are devoted to study, who are pure, who are high-souled and vow-observing,

sn: तरुणा दर्शनीयाश्च नानादेशसमागताः। महारथा कृतास्त्राश्च समुपैष्यन्ति भूमिपाः॥
en: Who are young and handsome, who are great car warriors and accomplished in arms, will all be present there from various countries.

sn: ते तत्र विविधान् दायान् विजयार्थं नरेश्वराः। प्रदास्यन्ति धनं गाश्च भक्ष्यं भोज्यं च सर्वशः॥
en: Being desirous of victory (to be successful in obtaining Draupadi)those kings, will all give away much wealth, kine, food and other articles of enjoyments.

sn: प्रतिगृह्य च तत् सर्वं दृष्ट्वा चैव स्वयंवरम्। अनुभूयोत्सवं चैव गमिष्यामो यथेप्सितम्॥
en: Taking all that they will give, seeing the Svaimvara and enjoying the festivities, we shall then go wherever we like.

sn: नटा वैतालिकास्तत्र नर्तकाः सूतमागधाः। नियोधकाच देशेभ्यः समेष्यन्ति महावलाः॥
en: There will come in that Svaimvara) from many countries, the singers of king's penegeries, the dancers, the reciters of Puranas, the heralds and the powerful athletes.

sn: एवं कौतूहलं कृत्वा दृष्ट्वा च प्रतिगृह्य च। सहास्माभिर्महात्मानः पुनः प्रतिनिवर्व्यथ॥
en: O high-souled men seeing all these wonderful sights and taking what will be given away, you will also return with us.

sn: दर्शनीयांश्च वः सर्वान् देवरूपानवस्थितान्। समीक्ष्य कृष्णा वरयेत् संगत्यैकतमं वरम्॥
en: You are handsome, you look all like the celestials: it may be that seeing you, Krishna may chose some one amongst you, superior to the rest, ( as her husband),

sn: अयं भ्राता तव श्रीमान् दर्शनीयो महाभुजः। नियुज्यमानो विजये संगत्या द्रविणं बहु। आहरिष्यन्नयं नूनं प्रीतिं वो वर्धयिष्यति॥
en: Your this brother is handsome and is endued with beauty; he is also mighty-armed; engaged in (athletic) encounters,) he may by chance earn great wealth.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच परमं भो गमिष्यामो द्रष्टुं चैव महोत्सवम्। भवद्भिः सहिताः सर्वे कन्यायास्तं स्वयंवरम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said: We shall all go with you to see that great festivity, that Svaimvara of (the Panchala) maiden.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्ताः प्रयातास्ते पाण्डवा जनमेजय। राज्ञा दक्षिणपञ्चालान् दुपदेनाभिरक्षितान्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : OJanamejaya, having been thus addressed, the Pandavas proceeded towards the Southern Panchala country, uled over by the king Drupada.

sn: ततस्ते सुमहात्मानं शुद्धात्मानमकल्मषम्। ददृशुः पाण्डवा वीरा मुनि द्वैपायनं तदा॥
en: On their way of the heroic Pandavas saw the illustrious, the pure-souled and the perfectly sinless Rishi Dvaipayana.

sn: तस्मै यथावत् सत्कारं कृत्वा तेन च सत्कृताः। कथान्ते चाभ्यनुज्ञाताः प्रययुर्दुपदक्षयम्॥
en: Duly worshipping the Rishi and being saluted by him, when their conversation came to a close, they proceeded by his command to the palace of Drupada.

sn: पश्यन्तो रमणीयानि वनानि च सरांसि च। तत्र तत्र वसन्तश्च शनैर्जग्मुर्महारथाः॥
en: Those great car-warriors slowly walked on, stopping on forests and on (the banks of) lakes which they found to be charming.

sn: स्वाध्यायवन्तः शुचयो मधुराः प्रियवादिनः। आनूपूर्येण सम्प्राप्ताः पञ्चालान् पाण्डुनन्दनाः॥
en: The sons of Pandu, devoted in study, amiable, sweet-speeched and pure in acts, at last arrived in the country of the Panchalas.

sn: ते तु दृष्ट्वा पुरं तच्च स्कन्धावारं च पाण्डवाः। कुम्भकारस्य शालायां निवासं चक्रिरे तदा॥
en: After seeing the city and also the barracks, the Pandavas, took up there quarters in a potter's house.

sn: तत्र भैक्षं समाजहुर्ब्राह्मणी वृत्तिमाश्रिताः। तान् सम्प्राप्तांस्तथा वीराञ्जज्ञिरे न नराः क्वचित्॥
en: Adopting the life of the Brahmanas, they begged their food there (in that city). No man recognised those heroes when they stopped there.

sn: यज्ञसेनस्य कामस्तु पाण्डवाय किरीटिने। कृष्णां दद्यामिति सदा न चैतद् विवृणोति सः॥
en: Yajnasena always cherished the wish of bestowing (his daughter) Krishna on Kirit (Arjuna), the son of Pandu, but he never spoke it to any body.

sn: सोऽन्वेषमाणः कौन्तेयं पाञ्चाल्यो जनमेजय। दृढं धनुरनानम्यं कारयामास भारत॥
en: O Janamejaya, O descendant of Bharata, thinking of the son of Kunti (Arjuna), the Panchala king caused a very stiff bow to be made incapable of being bent by any man except Arjuna.

sn: यन्त्रं वैहायसं चापि कारयामास कृत्रिमम्। तेन यन्त्रेण समितं राजा लक्ष्यं चकार सः॥
en: Causing a machinery to be erected in the sky, the king set up a mark to be shot through that machinery.

sn: दुपद उवाच इदं सज्यं धनुः कृत्वा सज्जैरेभिश्च सायकैः। अतीत्य लक्ष्यं यो वेद्धा स लब्धा मत्सुतामिति॥
en: Drupada said : He, who will string this bow and he who will be able to shoot the mark above the machinery with these ornamented arrows, will obtain my daughter.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच इति स दुपदो राजा स्वयंवरमगोषयत्। तच्छ्रुत्वा पार्थिवाः सर्वे समीयुस्तत्र भारत॥
en: came Vaishampayana said : With these words, the king Drupada proclaimed the Svaimvara. O descendant of Bharata, having heard this, all the kings came there.

sn: ऋषयश्च महात्मानः स्वयंवरदिदृक्षवः। दुर्योधनपुरोगाश्च सकर्णाः कुरवो नृप।॥
en: There came also many illustrious Rishis desirous of seeing the Svaimvara. O king, Duryodhana and the Kurus, accompanied by Karna, also came there.

sn: ब्राह्मणाश्च महाभागा देशेभ्यः समुपागमन्। ततोऽर्चिता राजगणा द्रुपदेन महात्मना॥
en: There also many illustrious, Brahmanas from many countries. The kings and princes were duly worshipped by the illustrious Drupada.

sn: उपोपविष्टा मञ्चेषु द्रष्टुकामाः स्वयंवरम्। ततः पौरजनाः सर्वे सागरोद्भूतनि:स्वनाः॥
en: All the citizens, making a deep noise as that of the ocean, took their seats on the platforms with the desire of seeing the Svayamvara.

sn: शिशुमारशिरः प्राप्य न्यविशंस्ते स्म पार्थिवाः। प्रागुत्तरेण नगराद् भूमिभागे समे शुभे। समाजवाटः शुशुभे भवनैः सर्वतो वृतः॥ प्राकारपरिस्त्रोपेतो द्वारतोरणमण्डितः। वितानेन विचित्रेण सर्वतः समलंकृतः॥
en: The kings and princes entered the palace (of Svaimvara) through the north east gate. The arena was built on a plane and on an auspicious ground on the north east of the city. The Samajavata (arena) was surrounded by palaces and it was enclosed on all sides by a wall and a moat, it was ornamented with gates and arches and covered all over with a beautiful canopy.

sn: तूर्योघशतसंकीर्णः परार्ध्यागुरुधूपितः। चन्दनोदकसिक्तश्च माल्यदामोपशोभितः॥
en: It resounded with the notes of thousands of trumpets, it was scented with Aguru (back aloe), ornamented with garlands and sprinkled with the Sandal water paste.

sn: कैलासशिखरप्रख्यैर्नभस्तलविलेखिभिः। सर्वतः संवृतः शुभैः प्रासादैः सुकृतोच्छ्यैः॥
en: It was surrounded on all sides by high and white mansions looking like the cloud-kissing peaks of the Kailasa (mountain).

sn: सुवर्णजालसंवीतैर्मणिकुट्टिमभूषणैः। सुखारोहणसोपानैर्महासनपरिच्छदैः॥
en: Their windows were covered with networks of gold and their walls set with diamonds and precious stones. Their staircases were easy of ascent and the floors were covered with rich carpets and robes.

sn: स्रग्दामसमवच्छन्नैरगुरूत्तमवासितैः। हंसांशुवर्णैर्बहुभिरायोजनसुगन्धिभिः॥
en: They were scented with Aguru and adorned with wreaths and garlands of flowers; they were all white and spotless like the necks of the swans. Their fragrance could be perceived from a Yojana.

sn: असम्बाधशतद्वारैः शयनासनशोभितैः। बहुधा तु पिनद्धाङ्गैर्हिमवच्छिखरैरिव॥
en: Each of them contained one hundred doors wide enough to admit a crowd all at once; they were adorned with costly beds ornamented with various metals; they looked like the peaks of the Himalayas.

sn: तत्र नानाप्रकारेषु विमानेषु स्वलंकृताः। स्पर्धमानास्तदान्योन्यं निषेदुः सर्वपार्थिवाः॥
en: In them lived all the kings, adorned with various kinds of ornaments and each boasting to get possession of the maiden.

sn: तत्रोपविष्टान् ददृशुर्महासत्त्वपराक्रमान्। राजसिंहान् महाभागान् कृष्णागुरुविभूषितान्॥ महाप्रसादान् ब्रह्मण्यान् स्वराष्ट्रपरिरक्षिणः। प्रियान् सर्वस्य लोकस्य सुकृतैः कर्मभिः शुभैः॥ मञ्चेषु च पराध्र्येषु पौरजानपदा जनाः। कृष्णादर्शनसिद्ध्यर्थं सर्वतः समुपाविशन्॥
en: When those best of kings, who were adorned with the fragrant paste of Aguru, who were greatly powerful, noble minded, liberal, devoted to Brahmanas, beloved of the whole world for their good deeds and the protectors of their kingdoms, took their respective seats, the people of the city and the country who had come to see Krishna and who had already taken their seats on the excellent platforms all around saw them.

sn: ब्राह्मणैस्ते च सहिताः पाण्डवाः समुपाविशन्। ऋद्धिं पाञ्चालराजस्य पश्यन्तस्तामनुत्तमाम्॥
en: The Pandavas sat there in the arena with the Brahmanas and saw the great affluence of the Panchala king.

sn: ततः समाजो ववृधे स राजन् दिवसान् बहून्। रत्नप्रदानबहुलः शोभितो नटनर्तकैः॥
en: O king, that assemblage daily increased in bulk,) and it looked gay with (the performances of) actors and dancers. Large presents of wealth were also made.

sn: वर्तमाने समाजे तु रमणीयेऽछि घोडशे। आप्लुताङ्गी सुवसना सर्वाभरणभूषिता॥ मालां च समुपादाय काञ्चनीं समलंकृताम्। अवतीर्णा ततो रङ्गं द्रौपदी भरतर्षभ॥
en: When this grand assembly continued (for 15 days,) then on the sixteenth day, O best of the Bharata race, Draupadi, having bathed, attired in the best robes and adorned with all ornaments entered the arena carrying in her hand a golden dish on which there were a garland of flowers and other offerings of the Arghya.

sn: पुरोहितः सोमकानां मन्त्रविद् ब्राह्मणः शुचिः। परिस्तीर्य जुहावग्निमाज्येन विधिवत् तदा॥
en: The priest of the lunar race, that holy Brahmana learned in the Mantras, kindling the sacrificial fire in all due forms poured libations of ghee.

sn: संतर्पयित्वा ज्वलनं ब्राह्मणान् स्वस्त वाच्य च। वारयामास सर्वाणि वादित्राणि समन्ततः॥
en: Gratifying Agni and making the Brahmanas utter the formula of benediction, he stopped all the musical instruments (that were then being played) all around.

sn: निःशब्दे तु कृते तस्मिन् धृष्टद्युम्नो विशाम्पते। कृष्णामादाय विधिवन्मेघदुन्दुभिनिःस्वनः॥ मे समेताः। रङ्गमध्ये गतस्तत्र मेघगम्भीरया गिरा। वाक्यमुच्चैर्जगादेदं श्लक्ष्णमर्थवदुत्तमम्॥
en: O king, when they are became perfectly still, Dhrishtadyumna, possessing a voice like that of kettle-drums or clouds, taking hold of his sister's arm, stood in the midst of the assembly and spoke these sweet words of excellent import with a voice as that of the clouds.

sn: इदं धनुर्लक्ष्यमिमे च बाणाः शृण्वन्तु भूपतयः छिद्रेण यन्त्रस्य समर्पयध्वं शरैः शितैोमचरैर्दशाधैः॥
en: Dhrishtadyumna said: Hear, O you assembled kings, this is the bow, that is the mark and these are the arrows. Shoot the mark through the 'orifice of the machine with these fine sharp arrows.

sn: एतन्महत् कर्म करोति यो वै कुलेन रूपेणं बलेन युक्तः। तस्याद्य भार्या भगिनी ममेयं कृष्णा भवित्री न मृषा ब्रवीमि॥
en: Truly do I say, he who possessing noble birth, beauty and strength will achieve this great feat, shall obtain today for his wife this my sister Krishna.

sn: तानेवमुक्त्वा दुपदस्य पुत्रः पश्चादिदं तां भगिनीमुवाच। नाम्ना च गोत्रेण च कर्मणा च संकीर्तयन् भूमिपतीन् समेतान्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having thus addressed the assembled kings, Drupada's son (Dhrishtadyumna) then spoke thus to his sister, reciting to her the names and the lineage and the achievements of those assembled potentates.

sn: धृष्टद्युम्न उवाच दुर्योधनो दुर्विषहो दुर्मुखो दुष्प्रधर्षणः। विविंशतिर्विकर्णश्च सहो दुःशासनस्तथा॥
en: Dhrishtadyumna said : Duryodhana, Durvishaha, Durmukha, Dushpradharshana, Vivignshati, Vikarna, Saha, Dushasana,

sn: युयुत्सुर्वायुवेगश्च भीमवेगरवस्तथा। उग्रायुधो बलाकी च करकायुर्विरोचनः॥
en: Yuyutsu, Vayuvega, Bhima, Vegarava, Ugrayudha, Balaki, Karakayu, Virochana,

sn: कुण्डकश्चित्रसेनश्च सुवर्चाः कनकध्वजः। नन्दको बाहुशाली च तुहुण्डो विकटस्तथा॥
en: Sukundala, Chitrasena, Suvarcha, Kanakadhvaja, Nandaka, Bahushali, Tuhunda, Vikata,

sn: एते चान्ये च बहवो धार्तराष्ट्रा महाबलाः। कर्णेन सहिता वीरास्त्वदर्थं समुपागताः॥
en: These and others are the greatly powerful sons of Dhritarashtra. These heroes have all come with Karna for your hands.

sn: असंख्याता महात्मानः पार्थिवाः क्षत्रियर्षभाः। शकुनिः सौबलश्चैव वृषकोऽथ बृहद्बलः॥
en: Numerous other illustrious kings, the best of Kshatriyas,. (have also come for you). Shakuni, Saybala, Vrishaka, Brihadbala,

sn: एते गान्धारराजस्य सुताः सर्वे समागताः। अश्वत्थामा च भोजश्च सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वरौ॥
en: These sons of the king of Gandhara have also come. The foremost of all wielders of arms, Ashvathama and Bhoja.

sn: समवेतौ महात्मानौ त्वदर्थे समलंकृतौ। बृहन्तो मणिमांश्चैव दण्डधारश्च पार्थिवः॥
en: Have come hero adorned with every ornament. The kings, Brihanta, Manimana, Dandadhara,

sn: सहदेवजयत्सेनौ मेघसंधिश्च पार्थिवः। विराटः सह पुत्राभ्यां शड्वेनैवोत्तरेण च॥
en: Sahadeva, Jayatsena, Meghasandhi, Virata with his two sons, Sankhya and Uttara,

sn: वार्द्धक्षेमिः सुशर्मा च सेनाबिन्दुश्च पार्थिवः। सुकेतुः सह पुत्रेण सुनाम्ना च सुवर्चसा॥
en: Vardhakshemi, Susharma, Senabindu, Suketu with his two sons, Sunamana and Suvarcha,

sn: सुचित्रः सुकुमारश्च वृकः सत्यधृतिस्तथा। सूर्यध्वजो रोचमानो नीलचित्रायुधस्तथा॥
en: Suchitra, Sukumara, Vrika, Satyadhriti, Suryadhvaja, Rochamana, Nila, Chitrayudha,

sn: अंशुमांश्चेकितानश्च श्रेणिमांश्च महाबलः। समुद्रसेनपुत्रश्च चन्द्रसेनः प्रतापवान्॥
en: Angshumana, Chekitana, the mighty Srinimana, Chandrasena, the son of the mighty Subhadrasena both the father and the son,

sn: जलसंधः पितापुत्रौ विदण्डो दण्ड एव च। पौण्ड्रको वासुदेवश्च भगदत्तश्च वीर्यवान्॥
en: Jalasandha, Vidanda, Danda, Paundraka, Vasudeva, the mighty Bhagadatta,

sn: कालिङ्गस्ताम्रलिप्तश्च पत्तनाधिपतिस्तथा। मद्रराजस्तथा शल्यः सहपुत्रो महारथः॥
en: Kalinga, Tamralipta, the king of Pattana, the king of Madra, the great car-warrior Shalya with his son,

sn: रुक्माङ्गदेन वीरेण तथा रुक्मरथेन च। कौरव्यः सोमदत्तश्च पुत्राश्चास्य महारथाः॥
en: The heroic Rukmangada, Rukmaratha, Somadatta of the Kuru race with his three sons,

sn: समवेतास्त्रयः शूरा भूरिभूरिश्रवाः शलः। सुदक्षिणश्च काम्बोजो दृढधन्वा च
en: All great heroic and car-warriors, all these have assembled here. Bhuri, Bhurishrava, Sala, Sudakshina, Kamboja, the Paurava Dridadhnava,

sn: बृहद्बलः सुषेणश्च शिबिरौशीनरस्तथा। पटच्चरनिहन्ता च कारूषाधिपतिस्तथा॥
en: Brihadbala, Sushena, Shibi, the son of Ushinara, Pataccharnihanta, the king of Karusha,

sn: संकर्षणो वासुदेवो रौस्मिणेयश्च वीर्यवान्। साम्बश्च चारुदेष्णश्च प्राधुम्निः सगदस्तथा॥ पौरवः॥
en: Sankarshana, (Baladeva) Vasudeva (Krishna), the mighty son of Rukmini, Samba, Charudeshna, the son of Pradyumna, Gada,

sn: अक्रूरः सात्यकिश्चैव उद्धवश्च महामतिः। कृतकर्मा च हार्दिक्यः पृथुर्विपृथुरेव च॥
en: Akrura, Satyaki, the high-souled Uddhava, Kritavarma, the son of Hridika, Pritha, Vipritha,

sn: विदूरथश्च करुश्च शरुश्च सगवेषणः। आशावहोऽनिरुद्धश्च शमीकः सारिमेजयः॥
en: Viduratha, Kamka, Shanku, Gaveshna, Ashavaha, Aniruddha, Shamika, Sarimejaya,

sn: वीरो वातपतिश्चैव झिल्लीपिण्डारकस्तथा। उशीनरश्च विक्रान्तो वृष्णयस्ते प्रकीर्तिताः॥
en: Heroic Vatapati, Jhilli, Pindaraka, the powerful Ushinara, all these are known as Vrishnis,

sn: भागीरथो बृहत्क्षत्रः सैन्धवश्च जयद्रथः। बृहद्रथो बाह्निकश्च श्रुतायुश्च महारथः॥
en: Bhagiratha, Brihatkshatra, the son of Sindhu, Jayadratha, Brihadratha, Balhika, the great car-warrior Shrutayu,

sn: उलूकः कैतवो राजा चित्राङ्गदशुभाङ्गदौ। वत्सराजश्च मतिमान् कोसलाधिपतिस्तथा॥
en: Uluka, Kaitava, Chitrangada, Subhangada, the intelligent Vatsaraja, the king of Kosala,
