sn: तमब्रवीद् देवराजो ममेदं त्वं विद्धि विद्वन् भुवनं वशे स्थितम्। ईशोऽहमस्मीति समन्युरब्रवीद् दृष्ट्वा तमक्षैः सुभृशं प्रमत्तम्॥
en: The king of the celestials thus spoke to him, “O intelligent youth, know this universe to be under my sway." Seeing that the person take no notice of what he had said, he (Indra) again said, “I am the lord of the universe."

sn: क्रुद्धं च शक्रं प्रसमीक्ष्य देवो जहास शक्रं च शनैरुदैक्षत। स्तेनेक्षितः स्थाणुरिवावतस्थे।॥
en: Seeing Indra angry, the youth who was none else than Mahadeva cast a glance at him and smiled. At that glance the king of the celestials was at once paralysed and stood on that spot like a statue.

sn: यदा तु पर्याप्तमिहास्य क्रीडया तदा देवीं रुदतीं तामुत्राच! नैनं दर्पः पुनरप्याविशेत॥
en: When the game of dice came to an end, he (Shiva) spoke thus to the weeping woman, “Bring him (Indra) here. I shall so deal with him that pride may not again enter his heart."

sn: ततः शक्रः स्पृष्टमात्रस्तया तु सस्तैरङ्गैः पतितोऽभूद् धरण्याम्। तमब्रवीद् भगवानुग्रतेजा मैवं पुनः शक्र कृथाः कथंचित्॥
en: As soon as Indra was touched by that woman, the chief of the celestials with limbs paralysed by that touch fell down on the ground. The illustrious deity of fierce energy (Shiva) then said to him, "O Indra, never act thus again.

sn: निवर्तयैनं च महाद्रिराज बलं च वीर्यं च तवाप्रमेयम्। छिद्रस्य चैवाविश मध्यमस्य यत्रासते त्वद्धिधाः सूर्यभासः॥
en: Remove this huge stone, for your strength and energy are immeasurable. Enter the hole and wait with others who are all like you and the sun in splendour."

sn: स्तुल्याश्चितुरोऽन्यान् ददर्श। स तानभिप्रेक्ष्य बभूव दुःखितः कच्चिनाहं भविता वै यथेमे॥
en: He (Indra) removed that stone and saw a cave on the great mountain in which were four others resembling himself. Seeing them, he became very much grieved and exclaimed, "Shall I too meet with such fate?"

sn: ततो देवो गिरिशो वज्रपाणि विवृत्य नेत्रे कुपितोऽभ्युवाच। दरीमेतां प्रविश त्वं शतक्रतो यन्मां बाल्यादवमंस्थाः पुरस्तात्॥
en: Then looking at the wielder of thunder (Indra) with expanded eyes, the deity Girisha (Shiva), said in anger, "O Shatakratu, (Indra) enter this cave without delay, for out of folly you have insulted me before my very eyes."

sn: उक्तस्त्वेवं विभुना देवराजः प्रावेपता” भृशमेवाभिषङ्गात्। मश्वत्थपत्रं गिरिराजमूर्ध्नि॥
en: Thus addressed by the lord (Shiva), the chief of the celestials was deeply grieved in consequence of that imprecation; and with limbs weakened by fear he trembled like the wind shaken leaf of the tree on the breast of the king of mountains.

sn: स प्राञ्जलिः वृषवाहनेन प्रवेपमानः सहसैवमुक्तः। उवाच देवं बहुरूपमुग्रस्रष्टाशेषस्य भुवनस्य त्वं भवाद्यः॥
en: Thus unexpectedly cursed by the deity that rides the bull (Shiva), Indra trembled from head to foot; and with joined hands the thus head addressed the fearful god of many manifestations, "O Bhava, you are the on looker of the infinite universe."

sn: तमब्रवीदुग्रवर्चाः प्रहस्य नैवंशीला: शेषमिहाप्नुवन्ति। एतेऽप्येवं भवितारः पुरस्तात् तस्मादेतां दरीमाविश्य शेष्व॥
en: To him thus replied the deity of fiery energy with smiles, “Those that have your disposition never obtain my grace. These others (four in the cave) were like you at one lie there for some time.

sn: तत्र ह्येवं भवितारो न संशयो योनि सर्वे मानुषीमाविशध्वम्। तत्र यूयं कर्म कृत्वाविषह्यं बहूनन्यान् निधनं प्रापयित्वा॥ आगन्तारः पुनरेवेन्द्रलोकं स्वकर्मणा पूर्वजितं महार्हम्। सर्वं मया भाषितमेतदेवं कर्तव्यमन्यद् विविधार्थयुक्तम्॥
en: The fate of you all should certainly by the same. All of you shall have to take births in the world of men, where having achieved many difficult feats and killing large number of men, you shall again regain the valued region of Indra by the merits of your respective deeds. You shall accomplish all I have said and much more.

sn: पूर्वेन्द्रा ऊचुः गमिष्यामो मानुषं देवलोकाद् दुराधरो विहितो यत्र मोक्षः। देवास्त्वस्मानादधीरञ्जनन्यां धर्मो वायुर्मघावानश्विनौ च। अस्त्रैर्दिव्यैर्मानुषान् योधयित्वा आगन्तारः पुनरेवेन्द्रलोकम्॥
en: The Old Indras said : We shall go from our celestial region to the region of men where salvation is difficult to gain. But let the celestials, Dharma, Vayu, Maghavata (present Indra) and the twin Ashvinis beget us on our would be mother. After fighting with men with both hunian and celestial weapons, we shall again come back to the region of Indra.

sn: व्यास उवाच एतच्छ्रुत्वा वज्रपाणिर्वचस्तु देवश्रेष्ठं पुनरेवेदमाह। दद्यामेषां पञ्चमं मत्प्रसूतम्॥
en: Vyasa said : Having heard this, the wielder of thunder (Indra) again addressed that foremost of gods (Shiva) saying, "Instead of going myself, I shall create from myself with a portion of my energy a person able to accomplish the task; and he will be the fifth among these (old Indras)."

sn: विश्वभुग्भूतधामा च शिविरिन्द्रः प्रतापवान्। शातिश्चतुर्थस्तेषां वै तेजस्वी पञ्चमः स्मृतः॥
en: Vishvabhuga, Bhutadhamana, greatly effulgent Shibi, Shanti and Tejasvin, these are the five Indras of old.

sn: तेषां कामं भगवानुग्रधन्वा प्रादादिष्टं संनिसर्गाद् यथोक्तम्। तां चाप्येषां योषितं लोककान्तां श्रियं भार्यां व्यदधान्मानुषेषु॥
en: The illustrious deity of the formidable bow kindly granted to the five Indras the desire they cherished in their hearts and he appointed that exceedingly beautiful lady, who was none else than the celestial Lakshmi herself to be their common wife in the world of men.

sn: तैरेव सार्धं तु ततः स देवो जगाम नारायणमप्रमेयम्। अनन्तमव्यक्तमजं पुराणं सनातनं विश्वमरन्तरूपम्॥
en: Thereupon accompanied by all these Indras, he (Shiva) went to Narayana, who is immeasurably effulgent, infinite, immaterial, the self born, the old the eternal and the spirit of the infinite universe.

sn: स चापि तद् व्यदधात् सर्वमेव ततः सर्वे सम्बभूबुर्धरण्याम्। स चापि केशौ हरिरुद्धबह शुक्लमेकमपरं चापि कृष्णम्॥
en: He (Narayana) approved of everything and then they (Indras) all took births in the world of men. Hari (Narayana) took up two hairs from his body; one of then was white and the other black.

sn: तौ चापि केशौ निविशेतां यदूनां कुले स्त्रियौ देवकी रोहिणीं च। तयोरेको बलदेवो बभूव योऽसौ श्वेतस्तस्य देवस्य केशः। कृष्णो द्वितीयः केशवः सम्बभूव केशो योऽसौ वर्णतः कृष्ण उक्तः॥
en: Those two hairs entered the wombs of the two ladies of the Yadu race, named Devaki and Rohini. The hair of the deity that was white became Baladeva and the hair that was black became Keshava's self, Krishna.

sn: स्तस्यां दर्यां पर्वतस्योत्तरस्य। इहैव ते पाण्डवा वीर्यवन्तः शक्रस्यांशः पाण्डवः सव्यसाची॥
en: Those Indra-like ones who were kept confined in the cave of the mountain are none less then the five sons of Pandu, possessing great prowess. And the Pandava Savyasachi (Arjuna) is a portion of (the present) Indra.

sn: र्ये ते राजन् पूर्वमिन्द्रा बभूवुः। लक्ष्मीश्चैषां पूर्वमेवोपदिष्टा भार्या यैषा द्रौपदी दिव्यरूपा॥
en: O king, thus were born as the sons of Pandu those that were at one time Indras and the celestial Lakshmi herself who had appointed to be their wife is the exceedingly beautiful Draupadi.

sn: कथं हि स्त्री कर्मणा ते महीतलात् समुत्तिष्ठेदन्यतो दैवयोगात्। यस्या रूपं सोमसूर्यप्रकाशं गन्धश्चास्याः क्रोशमात्रात् प्रवाति॥
en: How could she whose effulgence is like that of the son of the moon, whose fragrance spreads over two miles around, take birth in any other but an extraordinary way? She rose from within the earth by virtue of your sacrifice.

sn: इदं चान्यत् प्रीतिपूर्वं नरेन्द्र ददानि ते वरमत्यद्भुतं च। दिव्यं चक्षुः पश्य कुन्तीसुतांस्त्वं पुण्यैर्दिव्यैः पूर्वदेहैरुपेतान्॥
en: O king, I cheerfully grant to you this boon, I give you spiritual sight. Behold the sons of Kunti now possessing their sacred and celestial forms of old.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततो व्यासः परमोदारकर्मा शुचिर्विप्रस्तपसा तस्य राज्ञः। चक्षुर्दिव्यै प्रददौ तांश्च सर्वान् राजाऽपश्यत् पूर्वदेहैर्यथावत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Thereupon, that holy Brahmana, Vyasa of greatly generous deeds, gave celestial sight to that king (Drupada) by his ascetic power. Then the king saw them (the Pandavas) all possessing their former forms.

sn: ततो दिव्यान् हेमकिरीटमालिनः शक्रप्रख्यान् पावकादित्यवर्णान्। बद्धापीडांश्चारुरूपांश्च यूनो व्यूढोरस्कांस्तालमात्रान् ददर्श॥
en: He saw them with celestial garlands, each of them resembling like a Indra himself, with complexion as effulgent as the fire or the sun, each adorned with every ornament, each handsome and youthful, each with broad chest and stature with a height of five cubits.

sn: र्माल्यैश्चावयैः शोभमानानतीव। नादित्यान् वा सर्वगुणोपपन्नान्॥
en: Possessing every accomplishment, attired in celestial robes of great beauty and adorned with fragrant garlands of excellent make, the king saw them as so many, three-eyed gods (Shiva) or Vasus, Rudras or Adityas.

sn: तान् पूर्वेन्द्रानभिवीक्ष्याभिरूपान् शक्रात्मजं चेन्द्ररूपं निशम्य। प्रीतो राजा दुपदो विस्मितश्च दिव्यां मायां तामवेक्ष्याप्रमेयाम्॥
en: Seeing the (four others) Pandavas in the forms of the (present) Indra sprang from Indra himself, the king Drupada was exceedingly pleased. He was greatly surprised on seeing the celestial manifestation of Maya.

sn: तां चैवावयां स्त्रियमतिरूपयुक्तां दिव्यां साक्षात् सोमवह्निप्रकाशाम्। योग्यां तेषां रूपतेजोयशोभिः पत्नी मत्वा दृष्टवान् पार्थिवेन्द्रः॥
en: Looking at his daughter, that foremost of women possessing great beauty as that of a celestial maiden and splendour as that of the fire or the moon, the king considered, that for her beauty, splendour and fame, she is really worthy to be th y wife of those celestial beings.

sn: स तद् दृष्ट्वा महदाश्चर्यरूपं जग्राह पादौ सत्यवत्याः सुतस्य। नैतच्चित्रं परमर्षे त्वयीति प्रसन्नचेताः स उवाच चैनम्॥
en: Seeing that wonderful sight, he touched the feet of the son of Satyavati, (Vyasa) and said, “O great Rishi, there is nothing wonderful in you."

sn: व्यास उवाच आसीत् तपोवने काचिदृषेः कन्या महात्मनः। नाध्ययगच्छत् पतिं सा तु कन्या रूपवती सती॥४४।
en: Vyasa said : There was in a certain wood a daughter of an illustrious Rishi, who though handsome and chaste, did not get a husband,

sn: तोषयामास तपसा सा किलोग्रेण शंकरम्। तामुवाचेश्वरः प्रीतो वृणु काममिति स्वयम्॥
en: She gratified by her asceticism the deity Shankara (Shiva). The deity being pleased with her, himself thus spoke to her “Tell me what you want."

sn: सैवमुक्ताब्रवीत् कन्या देवं वरदमीश्वरम्। पतिं सर्वगुणोपेतमिच्छामीति पुनः पुनः॥
en: Having been thus addressed, she repeatedly said to the boon-giving supreme lord, "I desire to have a husband endued with all accomplishments."

sn: ददौ तस्यै स देवेशस्तं वरं प्रीतमानसः। पञ्च ते पतयो भद्रे भविष्यन्तीति शंकरः॥
en: That deity Shankara gave her the boon in joyful heart (saying), "O amiable girl, you shall have five husbands."

sn: सा प्रसादयती देवमिदं भूयोऽभ्यभाषत। एकं पतिं गुणोपेतं त्वत्तोऽर्हामीति शंकर॥
en: She who had been able to please the deity said again, “O Shankara, I desire to have from you only one husband endued with all accomplishments."

sn: तां देवदेवः प्रीतात्मा पुनः प्राह शुभं वचः। पञ्चकृत्वस्त्वयोक्तोऽहं पतिं देहीति वै पुनः॥
en: The god of gods, being well-pleased with her, spoke again to her thus, “You have addressed me five times saying, “Give me a husband"

sn: तत् तथा भविता भद्रे वचस्तद् भद्रमस्तु ते। देहमन्यं गतायास्ते सर्वमेतद् भविष्यति॥
en: O amiable girl, therefore it shall be as you have asked. Be blessed. All this will happen in one of your future births.”

sn: दुपदैषा हि सा जज्ञे सुता वै देवरूपिणी। पञ्चानां विहिता पत्नी कृष्णा पार्षत्यनिन्दिता॥
en: This your daughter of celestial beauty is that maiden. The faultless Krishna of the Prishata race had been pre-ordained to be the wife of five (men).

sn: स्वर्गश्रीः पाण्डवार्थं तु समुत्पन्ना महामखे। सेह तप्त्वा तपो घोरं दुहितृत्वं तवागता॥
en: The celestial Lakshmi has risen in the great sacrifice to be the wife of the Pandavas. After serve penances she is born as your daughter.

sn: सैषा देवी रुचिरा देवजुष्टा पञ्चानामेका स्वकृतेनेह कर्मणा। सृष्टा स्वयं देवपत्नी स्वयम्भुवा श्रुत्वा राजन् दुपदेष्टं कुरुष्व॥
en: O king, that handsome goddess, who is waited upon by all the celestials, becomes the wife of five husbands. She has been created by the self-created (Brahma) for this purpose. Hearing all this, do what you desire.

sn: दुपद उवाच अश्रुत्वैवं वचनं ते महर्षे मया पूर्वं यतितं संविधातुम्। न वै शक्यं विहिस्यापयानं तदेवेदमुपपन्नं विधानम्॥
en: Drupada said : O great Rishi, it is only when I have not heard from you all this that I intended to act in the way I have already told you. I am now incapable of acting against what has been ordained by the celestials. I therefore desire to act as you have said.

sn: दिष्टस्य ग्रन्थिरनिवर्तनीयः स्वकर्मणा विहितं नेह किंचित् स्तदेवेदमुपपन्नं विधानम्॥
en: The knot of destiny cannot be untied. There is nothing which is the result of our own actions. That which was made to secure one husband (for my daughter) becomes now the source of this (new) ordinance.

sn: नैकं पतिं मे भगवान् ददातु। स चाप्येवं वरमित्यब्रवीत् तां देवो हि वेत्ता परमं यदत्र॥
en: As Krishna (Draupadi) had repeatedly asked (in her former life) for five times saying, “Give me a husband," the greatly deity had granted her the boon accordingly. The deity himself knows the right or the wrong of this.

sn: यदि चैवं विहितः शंकरेण धर्मोऽधर्मो वा नात्र ममापराध:। गृहणन्त्विमे विधिवत् पाणिमस्या यथोपजोषं विहितैषां हि कृष्णा॥
en: When Shankara has fixed this ordinance, sinful or virtuous, I can have no fault. Therefore, let these (heroes) take as ordained the hand of Krishna according to all due rites.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच मद्यैव पुण्याहमुत वः पाण्डवेया अद्य पौष्यं योगमुपैति चन्द्रमाः पाणिं कृष्णायास्त्वं गृहाणाद्य पूर्वम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : The illustrious Rishi then spoke thus to Dharamraja (Yudhishthira), "O son of Pandu today is an auspicious day. Today the Moon has entered the constellation Paushya. You first take the hand of Krishna today.”

sn: ततो राजा यज्ञसेनः सपुत्रो जन्यार्थमुक्तं बहु तत् तदग्र्यम्। माप्लाव्य रत्नैर्बहुभिर्विभूष्य॥
en: Thereupon the king Yajnasena with his son made preparations for the marriage. Keeping ready many costly marriage presents, he brought out his daughter Krishna adorned after a bath, with many jewels and pearls.

sn: ततस्तु सर्वे सुहदो नृपस्य समाजग्मुः सहिता मन्त्रिणश्च। द्रष्टुं विवाहं परमप्रतीता द्विजाश्च पौराश्च यथा प्रधाना॥
en: All the friends and the relatives of the king with the state ministers and many Brahmanas and citizens according to their precedence of ranks, came there in joy to witness the marriage ceremony.

sn: ततोऽस्य वेश्मावयजनोपशोभितं विस्तीर्णपद्मोत्पलभूषिताजिरम्। बलौघररत्नौघविचित्रमाबभौ नभो यथा निर्मलतारकान्वितम्॥
en: Adorned with that concourse of chief men, with its court-yards decked with lotuses and lilies and beautified with the lines of troops and fastened round with diamonds and precious stones, his (Drupada's) palace looked like the sky studded with the brilliant stars.

sn: ततस्तु ते कौरवराजपुत्रा विभूषिताः कुण्डलिनो युवानः। महार्हवस्त्राम्बरचन्दनोक्षिताः कृताभिषेकाः कृतमङ्गलक्रियाः॥
en: Then those Kuru Princes, those young (heroes) bathed; adorned with ear-rings, attired in costly robes and perfumed by Sundal paste, they performed the Abhisheka (preparatory ceremony) and all other usual auspicious rites.

sn: पुरोहितेनाग्निसमानवर्चसा सहैव धौम्येन यथाविधि प्रभो। क्रमेण सर्वे विविशुस्ततः सदो महर्षभा गोष्ठमिवाभिनन्दितः॥
en: O lord, like mighty bulls entering their r 'n, they !..en accompanied by their priest Dhaumya, as effulgent as fire, entered in joy and in due order (the wedding place) one after the other.

sn: ततः समाधाय स वेदपारगो जुहाव मन्त्रैर्ध्वलितं हुताशनम्। ततोऽभ्यनुज्ञाय नियोजयामास सहैव कृष्णया॥
en: Then that Veda-knowing priest (Dhaumya) kindled the sacred fire and poured the libations of ghee in that blazing fire with proper Mantras. That Mantra knowing Brahmana then called Yudhisthira and united him with Krishna (Draupadi).

sn: प्रदक्षिणं तौ प्रगृहीतपाणी समानयामास स वेदपारगः। तमाजिशोभिनं पुरेहितो राजगृहाद् विनिर्ययौ॥
en: Walking round the fire (for seven times), the bride and the bridegroom took each other's hands. Thus they were married by the Vedaknowing (Dhaumya). Then taking leave of that ornament of battle (Yudhishthira), he (Dhaumya) went out of the palace.

sn: क्रमेण चानेन नराधिपात्मजा वरस्त्रियस्ते जगृहस्तदा करम्। अहन्यहन्युत्तमरूपधारिणो महारथाः कौरववंशवर्धनाः॥
en: Then those mighty car-warriors, the perpetuators of the Kuru race, those princes, attired in costly robes, took the hand of that best of women (Draupadi) day by day in succession.

sn: इदं च तत्राद्भुतरूपमुत्तम जगाद देवर्षिरतीतमानुषम्। महानुभावा किल सा सुमध्यमा बभूव कन्यैव गते गतेऽहनि॥
en: The celestial Rishi told me of a very wonderful incident, namely that the highsouled lady of slender waist (Draupadi) regained her virginity day after day (i.e., every day after her previous marriage).

sn: कृते विवाहे द्रुपदो धनं ददौ महारथेभ्यो बहुरूपसमुत्तमम्। शतं रथानां वरहेममालिनां चतुर्युजां हेमखलीनमालिनाम्॥
en: After the wedding was over, Drupada gave to those great car-warriors various kind of excellent wealth. (He gave them) one hundred chariots with golden standards, each drawn by four horses with golden bridles;

sn: शतं गजानामपि पद्मिनां तथा शतं गिरीणामिव हेमशृङ्गिणाम्। तथैव दासीशतमग्र्ययौवनं महार्हवेषाभरणाम्बरस्रजम्॥
en: One hundred elephants all possessing auspicious marks on their temples and faces and all looking like so many mountains with golden peaks; and one hundred young maidservants attired in costly robes and adorned with ornaments and floral wreaths.

sn: पृथक् पृथग् दिव्यदृशां पुनर्ददौ तदा धनं सौमकिरग्निसाक्षिकम्। तथैव वस्त्राणि विभूषणानि प्रभावयुक्तानि महानुभावः॥
en: Making fire his witness, the high-souled king of the lunar race, (Draupada), gave separately each of those celestials-like heroes much wealth, various brilliant ornaments and many costly robes.

sn: कृते विवाहे च ततस्तु पाण्डवाः। प्रभूतरत्नामुपलभ्यं तां श्रियम्। विजहरिन्द्रप्रतिमा महाबलाः पुरे च पाञ्चालनृपस्य तस्य ह॥
en: When the wedding was over and after they had obtained that maiden, like Lakshmi herself, along with great wealth, those greatly powerful sons of Pandu like so many Indras passed their days in joy, in the capital of the Panchala king.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच पाण्डवैः सह संयोगं गतस्य दुपदस्य ह। न बभूव भयं किंचिद् देवेभ्योऽपि कथंचन॥
en: Vaishampayana said : After his alliance with the Pandavas, Drupada had all his fears dispelled; and he did not fear even the celestials.

sn: कुन्तीमासाद्य ता नार्यो द्रुपदस्य महात्मनः। नाम संकीर्तयन्त्योऽस्या जग्मुः पादौ स्वमूर्धभिः॥
en: The ladies of the illustrious Draupada's (household) all came to Kunti; and mentioning their respective names, they saluted her with their heads touching the ground.

sn: कृष्णा च क्षौमसंवीता कृतकौतुकमङ्गला। कृताभिवादना श्वश्र्वास्तस्थौ प्रह्वा कृताञ्जलिः॥
en: Krishna, attired in red silk and with her wrists still encircled with auspicious thread, saluted her mother-in-law with reverence; and she then stood before her contentedly with joined hands.

sn: रूपलक्षणसम्पन्नां शीलाचारसमन्विताम्। द्रौपदीमवदत् प्रेम्णा पृथाऽऽशीवर्चनं स्नुषाम्॥
en: Out of affection Pritha (Kunti) pronounced a blessing on Draupadi, endued with beauty and auspicious marks and with sweet disposition and good character.

sn: यथेन्द्राणी हरिहये स्वाहा चैव विभावसो। रोहिणी च यथा सोमे दमयन्ती यथा नले॥
en: Kunti said : As Sachi is to Indra, as Svaha to Vibhavasu, as Rohini to Soma, as Damayanti to Nala.

sn: यथा वैश्रवणे भद्रा वसिष्ठे चाप्यरुन्धती। यथा नारायणे लक्ष्मीस्तथा त्वं भव भर्तृषु॥
en: As Bhadra to Vaishravana, as Arundhati to Vasishtha and as Lakshmi to Narayana, so be you to your husbands.

sn: जीवसूर्वीरसूर्भद्रे बहुसौख्यसमन्विता। सुभगा भोगसम्पन्ना यज्ञपत्नी पतिव्रता॥
en: Oamiable girl, be the mother of long-lived and heroic children and possess every thing that can make you happy. Be lucky and prosperous, be faithful to your husbands and a performer of great sacrifices.

sn: अतिथीनागतान् साधून् वृद्धान् बालांस्तथा गुरून्। पूजयन्त्या यथान्यायं शश्वद् गच्छन्तु ते समाः॥
en: Let your time be ever passed in duly entertaining your guests, the strangers that come to your house, the pious men, the old men, the children and the superiors.

sn: कुरुजाङ्गलमुख्येषु राष्ट्रेषु नगरेषु च। अनु त्वमभिषिच्यस्व नृपति धर्मवत्सला॥
en: Be installed with the virtue-loving king (Yudhishthira) as the queen of the kingdom and the capital of Kurujangala.

sn: पतिभिर्निर्जितामुर्वी विक्रमेण महाबलैः। कुरु ब्राह्मणसात् सर्वामश्वमेधे महाक्रतौ॥
en: Let the whole earth, conquered by your greatly powerful husbands, be given to the Brahmanas in a great Ashvamedha sacrifice.

sn: पृथिव्यां यानि रत्नानि गुणवन्ति गुणान्विते। तान्याप्नुहि त्वं कल्याणि सुखिनी शरदां शतम्॥
en: O accomplished girl, what gems of great qualities are in the world, let them all belong to you. O blessed girl, be happy for (full) one hundred years.

sn: यथा च त्वाभिनन्दामि वध्वद्य क्षौमसंवृताम्। तथा भूयोऽभिनन्दिष्ये जातपुत्रां गुणान्विताम्॥
en: O daughter-in-law, as I rejoice to-day on seeing you in red silk, so I shall rejoice when you will give birth to an accomplished son.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततस्तु कृतदारेभ्यः पाण्डुभ्यः प्राहिणोद्वरिः। वैदूर्यमणिचित्राणि हैमान्याभरणानि च॥
en: Vaishampayana said : After the Pandavas had been married, Hari (Krishna) sent them various golden ornaments set with pearls and Vaidurya gems.

sn: वासांसि च महार्हाणि नानादेश्यानि माधवः। कम्बलाजिनरत्नानि स्पर्शवन्ति शुभानि च॥
en: Madhava (Krishna) also sent (to them) costly robes of various countries, many beautiful and soft blankets and skins,

sn: शयनासनयानानि विविधानि महान्ति च। वैदूर्यवज्रचित्राणि शतशो भाजनानि च॥
en: Various costly beds, carpets and conveyance and hundreds of vessels set with diamonds and Vaidurya gems. to

sn: रूपयौवनदाक्षिण्यैरुपेताश्च स्वलंकृताः। प्रेष्याः सम्प्रददौ कृष्णो नाना देश्याः स्वलंकृताः।।१६।
en: Krishna gave them thousands of maidservants, all young, beautiful and accomplished and adorned with all ornaments and brought from various countries.

sn: गजान् विनीतान् भद्राश्च सदश्वांश्च स्वलंकृतान्। रथांश्च दान्तान् सौवर्णैः शुभैः पट्टैरलंकृतान्॥
en: He also gave them many well-trained elephants of the country of the Madras, many excellent horses adorned with ornaments and many chariots drawn by heroes of excellent colours and large teeth.

sn: कोटिशश्च सुवर्णं च तेषामकृतकं तथा। वीथीकृतममेयात्मा प्राहिणोन्मधुसूदनः॥
en: Madhusudan (Krishna) of immeasurable soul sent to them also in separate heaps millions of coins of pure gold.

sn: तत् सर्वं प्रतिजग्राह धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः। मुदा परमया युक्तो गोविन्दप्रियकाम्यया॥
en: Wishing to please Govinda (Krishna), Dharmaraja Yudhishthira, being himself filled with great joy, accepted all those presents.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततो राज्ञां चरैराप्तैः प्रवृत्तिरुपनीयत। पाण्डवैरुपसम्पन्ना द्रौपदी पतिभिः शुभा॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Thereupon the kings knew from their trusted spies that the beautiful Draupadi had got the Pandavas her husbands;

sn: येन तद् धनुरादाय लक्ष्यं विद्धं महात्मना। सोऽर्जुनो जयतां श्रेष्ठो महाबाणधनुर्धरः॥
en: The illustrious man who had best the bow and shot the mark was Arjuna, that foremost of all victorious warriors and the great wielder of bow and arrows;

sn: यः शल्यं मद्रराजं वै प्रोक्षिप्यापातयद् बली। त्रासयामास संक्रुद्धो वृक्षेण पुरुषान् रणे॥ न चास्य सम्भ्रमः कश्चिदासीत् तत्र महात्मनः। स भीमो भीमसंस्पर्शः शत्रुसेनाङ्गपातनः॥
en: The greatly strong man who had hurled away the Madra king Shalya, he who had in anger frightened all men in the battle by the tree. He who had stood in perfect fearlessness, whose touch was death to all, that illustrious hero, was no other than Bhima, that grinder of hostile ranks.

sn: ब्रह्मरूपधराज्छ्रुत्वा प्रशान्तान् पाण्डुनन्दनान्। कौन्तेयान् मनुजेन्द्राणां विस्मयः समजायत॥
en: The monarchs were very much astonished to learn that the sons of Kunti, the Pandavas, had assumed the guise of the peaceful Brahmanas.

sn: सपुत्रा हि पुरा कुन्ती दग्धा जतुगृहे श्रुता। पुनर्जातानिव च तांस्तेऽमन्यन्त नराधिपाः॥
en: They heard that Kunti with her sons had been formerly burnt to death in the lac house; therefore those kings regarded the Pandavas as men who had come back from the dead.

sn: धिगकुर्वंस्तदा भीष्मं धृतराष्ट्रं च कौरवम्। कर्मणातिनृशंसेन पुरोचनकृतेन वै॥
en: Remembering the greatly cruel dead of Purochana, they said, “Fie on Bhishma! Fie on Dhritarashtra of the Kuru race!"

sn: वृत्ते स्वयंवरे चैव राजानः सव्र एव ते। यथागतं विप्रजग्मुर्विदित्वा पाण्डवान् वृतान्॥
en: When the Svyaimvara was over, all the kings, learning that Draupadi had been wedding to the Pandavas, went away to therefore respective kings.

sn: अथ दुर्योधनो राजा विमना भ्रातृभिः सह। अश्वत्थाम्ना मातुलेन कर्णेन च कृपेण च॥ विनिवृत्तो वृतं दृष्ट्वा द्रौपद्या श्वेतवाहनम्। तं तु दुःशासनो वीडन मन्दं मन्दमिवाब्रवीत्॥
en: Having heard that Draupadi had been married to the rider of the white horse (Arjuna), Duryodhana, became greatly depressed; and accompanied by his brothers,। Ashvathama, his maternal uncle (Shakuni), Karna and Kripa, he started for his capital. Then Dushashana, being full of shame, thus slowly spoke to him.

sn: यद्यसौ ब्राह्मणो न स्याद् विन्देत द्रौपदी न सः। न हि तं तत्त्वतो राजन् वेद कश्चिद् धनंजयम्॥
en: "O king, if Arjuna had not disguised himself as a Brahmana, he could have never succeeded in obtaining Draupadi. On that account, none could recognise as Dhananjaya.

sn: दैवं च परमं मन्ये पौरुषं चाप्यनर्थकम्। धिगस्तु पौरुषं तात ध्रियन्ते यत्र पाण्डवाः॥
en: I believe that Destiny is supreme and human exertion is useless. O brother, fie on our exertions, when the Pandavas are still alive!"

sn: एवं सम्भाषमाणास्ते निन्दन्तश्च पुरोचनम्। विविशुहा॑स्तिनपुरं दीना विगतचेतसः॥
en: Thus talking to one another and blaming Purochana, they entered Hastinapur in misery and sorrow.

sn: जस्ता विगतसंकल्पा दृष्ट्वा पार्थान् महौजसः। मुक्तान् हव्यभुजश्चैव संयुक्तान् द्रुपदेन च॥ धृष्टद्युम्नं तु संचिन्त्य तथैव च शिखण्डिनम्। दुपदस्यात्मजांश्चान्यान् सर्वयुद्धविशारदान्॥
en: Seeing the greatly powerful sons of Pritha escaped from the house of lac and allied with Drupada and thinking of Dhrishtaduymna, Shikhandin and also other sons of Drupada who were all learned in every art of war, he (Duryodhana) became depressed and alarmed.

sn: विदुरस्त्वथ तां श्रुत्वा द्रौपदीं पाण्डवैर्वृतान्। वीडितान् धार्तराष्ट्रांश्च भग्नदर्पानुपागतान्॥ ततः प्रीतमनाः क्षत्ता धृतराष्ट्र विशाम्पते। उवाच दिष्ट्या कुरवो वर्धन्त इति विस्मितः॥ १७
en: Having learnt that Draupadi had been won by the Pandavas and that the sons of Dhritarashtra, their pride being broken, had returned in shame, Vidura became exceedingly glad; and coming to Dhritarashtra, O king, Kshatta, (Vidura) said to him, “The Kurus are prospering from good luck."

sn: वैचित्रवीर्यस्तु वचो निशम्य विदुरस्य तत्। अब्रवीत् परमप्रीतो दिष्ट्या दिष्ट्येति भारत॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, the son of Vichitravirya, the king Dhritarashtra, becoming astonished, said in great joy, "What good luck! What good luck!"

sn: मन्यते स वृतं पुत्रं ज्येष्ठं दुपदकन्यया। दुर्योधनमविज्ञानात् प्रशाचक्षुर्नरेश्वरः॥
en: That king, possessing the eye of knowledge, thought from ignorance that his eldest son Duryodhana had been chosen by the daughter of Drupada.

sn: अथ त्वाज्ञापयामास द्रौपद्या भूषणं बहु। आनीयतां वै कृष्णेति पुत्रं दुर्योधनं तदा॥
en: He ordered various ornaments to be made for Draupadi and he ordered that both Krishna and his son Duryodhana should be (brought in great pomp.)

sn: अथास्य पश्चाद् विदुर आचख्यौ पाण्डवान् वृतान्। सर्वान् कुशलिनो वीरान् पूजितान् द्रुपदेन ह॥
en: It was then that Vidura said that Draupadi had chosen the Pandavas for her husbands and they were all in good health and peace and those heroes had been duly received by Drupada.

sn: तेषां सम्बन्धिनश्चान्यान् बहून् बलसमन्वितान्। समागतान् पाण्डवेयैस्तस्मिन्नेव स्वयंवरे॥
en: And that the Pandavas had been allied with the many relatives and friends of Drupada, each possessing large armies and also with many others that had come to the Svyaimvara.

sn: यथैव पाण्डोः पुत्रास्तु तथैवाभ्यधिका मम। यथा चाभ्यधिका बुद्धिर्मम तान् प्रति तच्छृणु॥
en: Dhritarashtra said: Those children are dearer to me then they were to Pandu, know that my affection for them is now greater then before.

sn: यत् ते कृशलिनो वीरा मित्रवन्तश्च पाण्डवाः। तेषां सम्बन्धिनश्चान्ये बहवश्च महाबलाः॥
en: Those heroes, the sons of Pandu, are in good health and peace and they have now friends. Their friends and others (with whom they have allied) are all greatly powerful.

sn: को हि द्रुपदमासाद्य मित्रं क्षत्तः सबान्धवम्। न बुभूषेद् भवेनार्थी गतश्रीरपि पार्थिवः॥
en: O Kshatta, who among kings does not desire to have Drupada with his relatives as his friends in weal or in woe?

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तं तथा भाषमाणं तु विदुरः प्रत्यभाषत। नित्यं भवतु ते बुद्धिरेषा राजञ्छतं समाः। इत्युक्तवा प्रययौ राजन् विदुरः स्वं निवेशनम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : When he said this, Vidura replied “O king, let your understanding remain so for one hundred years."

sn: ततो दुर्योधनश्चापि राधेयश्च विशाम्पते। धृतराष्ट्रमुपागम्य वचोऽब्रूतामिदं तदा॥ संनिधौ विदुरस्य त्वां वक्तुं न शक्नुवः। विविक्तमिति वक्ष्याव: किं तवेदं चिकीर्षितम्॥ सपत्नवृद्धिं यत् तात मन्यसे वृद्धिमात्मनः। अभिष्टौषि च यत् क्षत्तुः समीपे द्विषतां वर॥
en: O king, then there came to Dhritarashtra Duryodhana and the son of Radha (Karna) and they thus spoke to him, “We are incapable of speaking wicked designs before Vidura, We have now found you alone; we shall, therefore, speak to you all that we desire to say. O father, are you considering the prosperity of the enemy as your own? O best of men, you were applauding the Pandavas before Kshatta.

sn: अन्यस्मिन् नृप कर्तव्ये त्वमन्यत् कुरुषेऽनघ। तेषां बलविधातो हि कर्तव्यस्तात नित्यशः॥
en: O sinless one, you are not acting as you should. You ought to act every day in a way as to weaken their (the Pandavas') strength.

sn: ते वयं प्राप्तकालस्य चिकीर्षा मन्त्रयामहे। यथा नो न गसेयुस्ते सपुत्रवलबान्धवान्॥
en: The time has come when we should consult together, so that they (the Pandavas) may not swallow us all with our sons, forces, friends and relatives.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच अहमप्येवमेवैतच्चिकीर्षामि यथा युवाम्। विवेक्तुं नाहमिच्छामि त्वाकारं विदुरं प्रति॥
en: Dhritarashtra said : I desire to act exactly as you desire, but I do not wish to show my mental thoughts to Vidura even by my demeanour.

sn: ततस्तेषां गुणानेव कीर्तयामि विशेषतः। नावबुध्येत विदुरो ममाभिप्रायमिङ्गितैः॥
en: Therefore, I was highly applauding them, (the Pandavas), so that Vidura may not know my real desire even by a sign.

sn: यच्च त्वं मन्यसे प्राप्तं तद् ब्रवीहि सुयोधन। राधेय मन्यसे यच्च प्राप्तकालं वदाशु मे॥
en: O Duryodhana, as this is the (proper) time, tell me, therefore, what is in your mind and also, in the mind of the son of Radha (Karna.)

sn: दुर्योधन उवाच अद्य तान् कुशलैर्विप्रैः सुगुप्तैराप्तकारिभिः। कुन्तीपुत्रान् भेदयामो माद्रीपुत्रौ च पाण्डवौ॥
en: Duryodhana said : Let us by the help of trusted and skillful Brahmanas privately create dissensions amongst the Pandavas, a quarrel between the sons of Kunti and those of Madri.

sn: अथवा द्रुपदो राजा महद्भिर्वित्तसंचयैः। पुत्राश्चास्य प्रलोभ्यन्ताममात्याश्चैव सर्वशः॥ परित्यजेद् यथा राजा कुन्तीपुत्रं युधिष्ठिरम्। अथ तत्रैव वा तेषां निवासं रोचयन्तु ते॥ इहैषां दोषवद्वासं वर्णयन्तु पृथक् पृथक्। ते भिद्यमानास्तत्रैव मनः कुर्वन्तु पाण्डवाः॥
en: Or let the king Drupada with his sons and ail his ministers of state be tempted by the presents of large wealth, so that they may abandon the cause of the son of Kunti, Yudhishthira. Or let them (our spies) speak to each of them separately the inconvenience of this place (Hastinapur) and induce them to live there (in Panchala.) Thus separated from the Kurus, they may live permanently there.

sn: अथवा कुशलाः केचिदुपायनिपुणा नराः। इतरेतरतः पार्थान् भेदयन्त्वनुरागतः॥
en: O let some clever men, full of resources, sow the seed of disunion among the sons of Pritha and make them jealous of one another.

sn: व्युत्थापयन्तु वा कृष्णां बहुत्वात् सुकरं हि तत्। अथवा पाण्डवांस्तस्यां भेदयन्तु ततश्च ताम्॥
en: Or let them incite Krishna (Draupadi) against her husbands; as she has many husbands, it will not at all be difficult. Let some make the Pandavas dissatisfied with her, so that she may be displeased with them.

sn: भीमसेनस्य वा राजन्नुपायकुशलैनरैः। मृत्युर्विधीयतां छन्नैः स हि तेषां बलाधिकः॥
en: O king, let some clever spies, full of resources, go there and secretly bring about the death of Bhimasena, he is the strongest of them all.

sn: तमाश्रित्य हि कौन्तेयः पुरा चास्मान् न मन्यते। स हि तीक्ष्णाश्च शूरश्च तेषां चैव परायणम्॥
en: Relying on him the son of Kunti formerly disregarded us. He is fierce, brave and the main-stay of the Pandavas.

sn: तस्मिंस्त्वभिहते राजन् हतोत्साहा हतौजसः। यतिष्यन्ते न राज्याय स हि तेषां व्यपाश्रयः॥
en: O king, on his death all the others (the Pandavas) will be deprived of strength and energy. Deprived of him, who is their mainstay, they will not attempt to regain their kingdom.

sn: अजेयो ह्यर्जुनः संख्ये पृष्ठगोपे वृकोदरे। तमृते फाल्गुनो युद्धे राधेयस्य न पादभाक्॥
en: If Arjuna is supported from behind by Vrikodara (Bhima), he is invincible in battle. But if Bhima is not there, he (Arjuna) is not a match for even the forth part of the son of Radha (Karna).

sn: जानानास्तु दौर्बल्यं भीमसेनमृते महत्। अस्मान् बलवतो ज्ञात्वा न यतिष्यन्ति दुर्बलाः॥ ते
en: In consequence of the death of Bhimasena, they (the Pandavas) would know themselves weak and ourselves strong; and they will not attempt to recover the kingdom.

sn: इहागतेषु वा तेषु निदेशवशवर्तिषु। प्रवर्तिष्यामहे राजन् यथाशास्त्रं निबर्हणम्॥
en: O king, if coming here, they prove themselves docile and obedient to us, we would then try to repress them according to the Shastras (Political science).

sn: अथवा दर्शनीयाभिः प्रमदाभिर्विलोभ्यताम्। एकैकस्तत्र कौन्तेयस्ततः कृष्णा विरज्यताम्॥
en: We may tempt them with handsome girls; and on sceing which Krishna (Draupadi) will surely be annoyed with the sons of Kunti.

sn: प्रेष्यतां चैव राधेयस्तेषामागमनाय वै। तैस्तैः प्रकारैः संनीय पात्यन्तामाप्तकारिभिः॥
en: Or, O son of Radha, send messengers to bring them here, so that getting them here, we might kill them by some means or other.

sn: एतेषामप्युपायानां यस्ते निर्दोषवान् मतः। तस्य प्रयोगमातिष्ठ पुरा कालोऽतिवर्तते॥ यावद्ध्यकृतविश्वासा दुपदे पार्थिवर्षभे। तावदेव हि ते शक्या न शक्यास्तु ततः परम्॥
en: O father, employ any of these means which appear to you faultless. Time passes away, we should not make any further delay. So long their confidence in that best of kings Drupada is not established, we may succeed, but not after (when it has been established).

sn: एषा मम मतिस्तात निग्रहाय प्रवर्तते। साध्वी वा यदि वासाध्वी किं वा राधेय मन्यसे॥
en: O father, these are my views for their suppression. Judge whether they are good or bad. What, O son of Radha (Karna), do you think?

sn: कर्ण उवाच दुर्योधन तव प्रज्ञा न सम्यगिति मे मतिः। न ह्युपायेन ते शक्याः पाण्डवाः कुरुवर्धन॥
en: Karna said: O Duryodhana, in my opinion your reasoning are not well-founded. O perpetuator of the Kuru race, no machinations will succeed against the Pandavas.

sn: पूर्वमेव हि ते सूक्ष्मैरुपायैर्यतितास्त्वया। निग्रहीतुं तदा वीर न चैव शकितास्त्वया।॥
en: O hero, you have formerly tried to accomplish your wishes by various subtlc means, but you have not been successful in killing them.

sn: इहैव वर्तमानास्ते समीपे तव पार्थिव। अजातपक्षाः शिशवः शकिता नैव बाधितुम्॥
en: O. king, they were then living near you, they were then mere children, they were then without allies and friends, still you could nor injure them.

sn: जातपक्षा विदेशस्था विवृद्धाः सर्वशोऽद्य ते। नोपायसाध्याः कौन्तेया ममैषा मतिरच्युत॥
en: They are now living at a distance, they are now grown up and they are now stronger by securing allies. It is my firm belief that you will not be able to injure them now with any subtle machinations.

sn: न च ते व्यसनैर्योक्तुं शक्या दिष्टकृतेन च। शकिताश्चेप्सवश्चैव पितृपैतामहं पदम्॥
en: They are aided by Fate. When they are desirous of regaining the place of their fathers and grandfathers, we can never succeed to injure them by any means of ours.

sn: परस्परेण भेदश्च नाधातुं तेषु शक्यते। एकस्यां ये रताः पन्यां न भिद्यन्ते परस्परम्॥
en: It is impossible to create disunion amongst them. They can never be disunited who have taken a common wife.

sn: न चापि कृष्णा शक्येत तेभ्यो भेदयितुं परैः। परियूनान् वृतवती किमुताद्य मृजावतः॥
en: We can never succeed in estranging Krishna (Draupadi) from them by any spies. she choose them as her husband when they were in adversity, they are now in prosperity.

sn: ईप्सितश्च गुणः स्त्रीणामेकस्या बहुभर्तृता। तं च प्राप्तवती कृष्णा न सा भेदयितुं क्षमा॥
en: Women generally desire to have many husbands, Krishna has got it; she can never be estranged from them.

sn: आर्यव्रतश्च पाञ्चाल्यो न स राजा धनप्रियः। न संत्यक्ष्यति कौन्तेयान् राज्यदानैरपि ध्रुवम्॥
en: The Panchala king is honest and virtuous, he is not covetous for wealth. Even if we offer him our whole kingdom, he will certainly not abandon the sons of Kunti.

sn: यथास्य पुत्रो गुणवाननुरक्तश्च पाण्डवान्। तस्मान्नो पायसाध्यांस्तानहं मन्ये कथंचन॥
en: His son is also well-accomplished and has become attached to the Pandavas; therefore, I think by no subtle machinations that are in your power, you will be able to injure them.

sn: इदं त्वद्य क्षमं कर्तुमस्माकं पुरुषर्षभ। यावन्न कृतमूलास्ते पाण्डवेया विशाम्पते॥ तावत् प्रहरणीयास्ते तत् तुभ्यं तात रोचताम्। अस्मत्पक्षो महान् यावद् यावत् पाञ्चालको लघुः। तावत् प्रहरणं तेषां क्रियतां मा विचारय॥
en: O best of men, this is what is good and advisable for us to-day, namely, O king, to attack and smite them till the Pandavas are exterminated. O sire, consent to this. As long as our party is strong and that of the Panchalas weak, so long let us strike them without scruple.

sn: वाहनानि प्रभूतानि मित्राणि च कुलानि च। यावन्न तेषां गान्धारे तावद् विक्रम पार्थिव॥
en: O son of Gandhari, O king, as long as their innumerable conveyances, their friends and relatives, do not gather together, so long continue to display your prowess.

sn: यावच्च राजा पाञ्चाल्यो नोद्यमे कुरुते मनः। सह पुत्रैर्महावीर्य स्तावद् विक्रम पार्थिव॥
en: O king, as long as the Panchala king with his greatly powerful son does not resolve to fight with us, so long display your prowess.

sn: यावन्नायाति वार्ष्णेयः कर्षन् यादववाहिनीम्। राज्यार्थे पाण्डवेयानां पाञ्चाल्यसदनं प्रति॥
en: As long as Vasudeva, Krishna, does not march with the Yadava hosts into the city of the Panchala king in order to restore the Pandavas to their kingdom, so long display your prowess.

sn: वसूनि विविधान् भोगान् राज्यमेव च केवलम्। नात्याज्यमस्ति कृष्णस्य पाण्डवार्थं कथंचन॥
en: Wealth, articles of enjoyments, kingdom, nay their is nothing which Krishna may not sacrifice for the Pandavas,

sn: विक्रमेण मही प्राप्ता भरतेन महात्मना। विक्रमेण च लोकांस्त्रीञ्जितवान् पाकशासनः॥
en: The whole earth was acquired by the illustrious Bharata by his prowess. Indra has obtained the sovereignty of three worlds by prowess alone.

sn: विक्रमं च प्रशंसन्ति क्षत्रियस्य विशाम्पते। स्वको हि धर्मः शूराणां विक्रमः पार्थिवर्षभ॥
en: O king, prowess is always admired in a Kshatriya. O best of kings, prowess is the cardinal virtue of the heroes.

sn: ते बलेन वयं राजन् महता चतुरङ्गिणा। प्रमथ्य दुपदं शीघ्रमानयामेह पाण्डवान्॥
en: O king, therefore, without any further delay let us with our large army of four kinds of troops vanquish Drupada and bring here the Pandavas.

sn: न हि साम्ना न दानेन न भेदेन च पाण्डवाः। शक्याः साधयितुं तस्माद् विक्रमेणैव ताञ्जहि॥
en: The Pandavas cannot be defeated by any policy of conciliation, of gift, of wealth, of bribery or of disunion. Therefore, vanquish them by your prowess.

sn: तान् विक्रमेण जित्वेमामखिलां भुक्ष्व मेदिनीम्। अतो नान्यं प्रपश्यामि कार्योपायं जनाधिप॥
en: O king, after defeating them by your prowess, rule over the wide world. I do not see any other means of becoming successful in our object.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच श्रुत्वा तु राधेयवचो धृतराष्ट्रः प्रतापवान्। अभिपूज्य ततः पश्चादिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Hearing what the son of Radha (Karna) said, the powerful Dhritarashtra gave him high praise and he then spoke to him thus-

sn: उपपन्नं महाप्राज्ञे कृतास्त्रे सूतनन्दने। त्वयि विक्रमसम्पन्नमिदं वचनमीदृशम्॥
en: "O son of Suta, you are gifted with great wisdom and you are highly accomplished in arms. Such words breathing the spirit of heroism are surely worthy of you.

sn: भूय एव तु भीष्मश्च द्रोणो विदुरएव च। युवां च कुरुतं बुद्धिं भवेद् या नः सुखोदया॥
en: But let Bhishma, Drona and Vidura and also you two, consult together and then adopt that means which may lead to our good."

sn: तत आनाय्य तान् सर्वान् मन्त्रिणः सुमहायशाः। धृतराष्ट्रो महाराज मन्त्रयामास वै तदा॥
en: Thereupon, the greatly illustrious king Dhritarashtra summoned to him all those councillors and consulted with them.

sn: भीष्म उवाच न रोचते विग्रहो मे पाण्डुपुत्रैः कथंचन। यथैव धृतराष्ट्रो मे तथा पाण्डुरसंशयम्॥
en: Bhishma said: O Dhritarashtra, I can never consent to a quarrel with the sons of Pandu. There is no doubt Pandu was to me as you are to me.

sn: गान्धार्याश्च यथा पुत्रास्तथा कुन्तीसुता मम। यथा च मम ते रक्ष्या धृतराष्ट्र तथा तव॥
en: The sons of Gandhari are (as dear) to me as the sons of Kunti. O Dhritarashtra, they are to be protected as much by me as you.

sn: यथा च मम राज्ञश्च तथा दुर्योधनस्य ते। तथा कुरूणां सर्वेषामन्येषामपि पार्थिव॥
en: O king, they are as much dear to me as prince Duryodhana and other Kurus.

sn: एवं गते विग्रहं तैर्न रोचे संधाय वीरैर्दीयतामर्धभूमिः। तेषामपीदं प्रपितामहानां राज्यं पितुश्चैव कुरूत्तमानाम्॥
en: Therefore, I can never like a quarrel with them. Conclude a treaty with those heroes and give them the half of the kingdom. There is no doubt that this is the ancestral kingdom of those best of the Kurus (the Pandavas).

sn: दुर्योधन यथा राज्यं त्वमिदं तात पश्यसि। मम पैतृकमित्येवं तेऽपि पश्यन्ति पाण्डवाः॥
en: O Duryodhana, as you consider this kingdom as your paternal property, so do the Pandavas consider this their paternal property.

sn: यदि राज्यं न ते प्राप्ताः पाण्डवेया यशस्विनः। कुत एव तवापीदं भारतस्यापि कस्यचित्॥
en: If the illustrious sons of Pandu do not get the kingdom, how can it be yours or of any descendant of the Bharata race?

sn: अधर्मेण च राज्यं त्वं प्राप्तवान् भरतर्षभ। तेऽपि राज्यमनुप्राप्ताः पूर्वमेवेति मे मतिः॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, if you think you have rightfully come into the possession of the kingdom, I think, they can consider also that they have rightfully come to the possession of the kingdom before you.

sn: मधुरेणैव राज्यस्य तेषामधु प्रदीयताम्। एतद्धि पुरुषव्याघ्र हितं सर्वजनस्य च॥
en: Give them in peace the half of the kingdom. O best of men, this is for the good of all.

sn: अतोऽन्यथा चेत् क्रियते न हितं नो भविष्यति। तवाप्यकीर्तिः सकला भविष्यति न संशयः॥
en: If you act otherwise, no good will come to any of us. There is no doubt we all will be covered with dishonour.

sn: कीर्तिरक्षणमातिष्ठ कीर्तिर्हि परमं बलम्। नष्टकीर्तेर्मनुष्यस्य जीवितं ह्यफलं स्मृतम्॥
en: Try to maintain your good name. A good name is the source of one's strength. It is said that a man, whose reputation is gone, lives in vain.

sn: यावत्कीर्तिर्मनुष्यस्य न प्रणश्यति कौरव। तावज्जीवति गान्धारे नष्टकीर्तिस्तु नश्यति॥
en: O descendant of Kuru, O son of Gandhari, a man not die so long his reputation exists. One lives as long as his fame lasts; he dies when his reputation is gone.

sn: तमिमं समुपातिष्ठ धर्मं कुरुकुलोचितम्। अनुरूपं महाबाहो पूर्वेषामात्मनः कुरु॥
en: Therefore, follow the practice that is worthy of the Kuru race. O mighty-armed hero, act as your forefathers did before you.

sn: दिष्ट्या ध्रियन्ते पार्था हि दिष्ट्या जीवति सा पृथा। दिष्ट्या पुरोचनः पापो न सकामोऽत्ययं गतः॥
en: It is fortunate for us that the sons of Pritha are alive; It is fortunate that the sinful Purochana, without being successful (in his evil design), himself perished.

sn: यदा प्रभृति दग्धास्ते कुन्तिभोजसुतासुताः। तदा प्रभृति गान्धारे न शक्नोम्यभिवीक्षितुम्॥ लोके प्राणभृतां कंचिच्छ्रुत्वा कुन्ती तथागताम्। न चापि दोषेण तथा लोको मन्येत् पुरोचनम्। यथा त्वां पुरुषव्याघ्र लोको दोषेण गच्छति॥
en: O son of Gandhari, from that time when I heard that the sons of Kunti Bhoja's daughter had been burnt to death, I could not meet with any living creatures. O best of men, hearing the way in which Kunti was killed, men do not consider Purochana so much guilty as they consider you.

sn: तदिदं जीवितं तेषां तव किल्विपनाशनम्। सम्मन्तव्यं महाराज पाण्डवानां च दर्शनम्॥
en: O king, therefore the escape of the sons of Pandu from that conflagration and their present reappearance remove your bad repute.

sn: न चापि तेषां वीराणां जीवतां कुरुनन्दन। पित्र्योंऽशः शक्य आदातुमपि वज्रभृता स्वयम्॥
en: O descendant of Kuru, know that as long as those heroes (the Pandavas) live, the wielder of thunder (Indra) himself cannot deprive them of their paternal property.

sn: ते सर्वेऽवस्थिता धर्मे सर्वे चैवैकचेतसः। अधर्मेण निरस्ताश्च तुल्ये राज्ये विशेषतः॥
en: They are virtuous and united; they are unjustly kept out of their equal share in the kingdom.

sn: यदि धर्मस्त्वया कार्यो यदि कार्यं प्रियं च मे। क्षेमं च यदि कर्तव्यं तेषामधु प्रदीयताम्॥
en: If you want to act justly, if you want to act what is pleasing to me, if you want to seek the welfare of all, then give them the half of the kingdom.

sn: द्रोण उवाच मन्त्राय समुपानीतैर्धराष्ट्र हितैर्नृप। धर्म्यमर्थ्य यशस्यं च वाच्यमित्यनुशुश्रुम्॥
en: Drona said: O king Dhritarashtra, it has been heard that friends summoned for consultation should always speak what is right, true and conductive of fame.

sn: ममाप्येषा मतिस्तात या भीष्मस्य महात्मनः। संवभिज्यास्तु कौन्तेया धर्म एष सनातनः॥
en: O Sire, my opinion is as that of the illustrious Bhishma. Let the sons of Kunti have a share in the kingdom. It is eternal virtue.

sn: प्रेष्यतां द्रुपदायाशु नरः कश्चित् प्रियंवदः। बहुलं रत्नमादाय तेषामर्थाय भारत।॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, send a sweetspeeched man to Drupada; let him carry for them (the Pandavas) a large treasure with him.

sn: मिथः कृत्यं च तस्मै च आदाय वसु गच्छतु। वृद्धिं च परमां ब्रूयात् त्वत्संयोगोद्भवां तथा॥ सम्प्रीयमाणं त्वां ब्रूयाद् राजन् दुर्योधनं तथा। असकृद् द्रुपदे चैव धृष्टद्युम्ने च भारत॥
en: Let him take costly presents with him for both the bridegroom and the bride and let him speak to him (Draupada) the increase of your power and dignity that has been secured by this alliance. O king, let him say to Draupada and Dhrishtadyumna that both you and Duryodhana have become exceedingly glad by all that has happened.

sn: उचितत्वं प्रियत्वं च योगस्यापि च वर्णयेत्। पुनः पुनश्च कौन्तेयान् माद्रीपुत्रौ च सान्त्वयन्॥
en: Let him say that the alliance has been exceedingly proper and it has become very picasing to you and that you are quite worthy of it. Let him repeatedly propitiate the sons of Kunti and the two sons of Madri.

sn: हिरण्मयानि शुभ्राणि बहून्याभरणानि च। वचनात् तव राजेन्द्र द्रौपद्याः सम्प्रयच्छतु॥
en: O king, let many brilliant golden ornaments at your command be given to Draupadi.

sn: तथा दुपदपुत्राणां सर्वेषां भरतर्षभ। पाण्डवानां च सर्वेषां कुन्त्या युक्तानि यानि च॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, let proper presents be given to all the sons of Drupada and all the Pandavas with (their mother) Kunti.

sn: एवं सान्त्वसमायुक्तं द्रुपदं पाण्डवैः सह। उक्त्वा सोऽनन्तरं ब्रूयात् तेषामागमनं प्रति॥
en: Thus propitiating Drupada with the Pandavas, he should then propose their return (10 Hastinapur).

sn: अनुज्ञातेषु वीरेषु बलं गच्छतु शोभनम्। दुःशासनो विकर्णश्चाप्यानेतुं पाण्डवानिह॥
en: When those heroes will get the permission (of Drupada) to come here, let Dushasana and Vikarna go with a magnificent army to receive the Pandavas.

sn: ततस्ते पाण्डवाः श्रेष्ठाः पूज्यमानाः सदा त्वया। प्रकृतीनामनुमते पदे स्थास्यन्ति पैतृके॥
en: Let those best of the Kurus, the sons of Pandu, always be treated by you with affection and let them be installed in their paternal kingdoin as desired by the people.

sn: एतत् तव महाराज पुत्रेषु तेषु चैव हि। वृत्तयौपयिकं मन्ये भीष्मेण सह भारत॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, in my opinion and that of Bhishma, this should be your conduct towards the Pandavas, who stand to you in the relation of your own sons.

sn: कर्ण उवाच योजितावर्थमानाभ्यां सर्वकार्येष्वनन्तरौ। न मन्त्रयेतां त्वच्छ्रेयः किमद्भुततरं ततः॥
en: Karna said : These two (Bhishma and Drona) are supported by your wealth and favours. They are supposed to be your best friends. What can be more surprising than they should give you advice that is not for your good!

sn: दुष्टेन मनसा यो वै प्रच्छन्नेनान्तरात्मना। ब्रूयान्निःश्रेयसं नाम कथं कुर्यात् सतां मतम्॥
en: How can the wise accept the advice which is pronounced good by the man who speaks with wicked intention, taking care to conceal the wickedness of his heart?

sn: न मित्राण्यर्थकृच्छ्रेषु श्रेयसे चेतराय वा। विधिपूर्वं हि सर्वस्य दुःखं वा यदि वा सुखम्॥
en: Friends can neither do good nor harm in distress. man's happiness or misery depends on Destiny alone.

sn: कृतप्रज्ञोऽकृतप्रज्ञो बालो वृद्धश्च मानवः। ससहायोऽसहायश्च सर्वं सर्वत्र विन्दति॥
en: He who is wise, or he who is a fool, he who is old or he who is a child, he who has friends or he who has no friends, becomes happy or unhappy everywhere.

sn: श्रूयते हि पुरा कश्चिदम्बुवीच इतीश्वरः। आसीद् राजगृहे राजा मागधानां महीक्षिताम्॥
en: We have heard that there was a king of old, named Ambuvich, who was the king at Rajgriha over the Magadhas.

sn: स हीनः करणैः सर्वैरुच्छ्वासपरमो नृपः। अमात्यसंस्थ: सर्वेषु कार्येष्वेवाभवत् तदा॥
en: He was a king who never looked to his affairs. All he did was to inhale and exhale the air. All his affairs were in the hands of his ministers.

sn: तस्यामात्यो महाकर्णिर्बभूवैकेश्वरस्तदा। स लब्धवलमात्मानं मन्यमानोऽवमन्यते॥
en: He had a minister, named Mahakarni, who became the supreme lord of his kingdom Regarding that all authority had been gained, he even disregarded the king.

sn: स राज्ञ उपभोग्यानि स्त्रियो रत्नधनानि च। आददे सर्वशो मूढ ऐश्वर्यं च स्वयं तदा॥
en: The fool himself appropriated everything belonging to the king, including his articles of luxury, his women, his jewels and his sovereignty.

sn: तदादाय च लुब्धस्य लोभाल्लोभोऽप्यवर्धत। तथा हि सर्वमादाय राज्यमस्य जिहीर्षति॥
en: Having secured them all, that avaricious man's avarice only increased; and having appropriated all, he coveted his kingdom.

sn: हीनस्य करणैः सर्वैरुच्छ्वासपरमस्य च। यतमानोऽपि तद् राज्यं न शशाकेति नः श्रुतम्॥
en: We have heard that with all his endeavours he did not succeed to get the kingdom, although the king did not look to his affairs and only breathed the air.

sn: किमन्यद् विहिता नूनं तस्य सा पुरुषेन्द्रता। यदि ते विहितं राज्यं भविष्यति विशाम्पते॥ मिषतः सर्वलोकस्य स्थास्यते त्वयि तद् ध्रुवम्। अतोऽन्यथा चेद् विहितं यतमानो न लप्स्यसे॥
en: O king, what else human exertion can be said to have been in him than that the kingdom was dependent on his Destiny. If this kingdom be fixed in you by destiny. It will certainly remain in you, notwithstanding the enmity of all the worlds. If otherwise, however you may try, it will never remain in you.

sn: एवं विद्वन्नपादत्स्व मन्त्रिणां साध्वसाधुताम्। दुष्टानां चैव बोद्धव्यमदुष्टानां च भाषितम्॥
en: You are learned, therefore, remembering all this, judge of the honesty and dishonesty of your ministers. Ascertain also who amongst them are wicked and who have spoken wisely and well.

sn: द्रोण उवाच विद्म ते भावदोषेण यदर्थमिदमुच्यते। दुष्ट पाण्डवहेतोस्त्वं दोषमाख्यापयस्युत॥
en: Drona said: Wicked as you are, you say so out of the wickedness of your intentions. It is to injure the Pandavas, you find fault with us.

sn: हितं तु परमं कर्ण ब्रवीमि कुलवर्धनम्। अथ त्वं मन्यसे दुष्टं ब्रूहि यत् परमं हितम्॥
en: O Karna, know that what I have said is good for all. This is for the prosperity of the Kuru race. If you consider it as productive of evil, tell yourself what is the great good.

sn: अतोऽन्यथा चेत् क्रियते यद् ब्रवीमि परं हितम्। कुरवो वै विनक्षयन्ति नचिरेणैव मे मतिः॥
en: If the advice, productive of great good that I have given, is not followed, my opinion is that the Kurus will be exterminated.

sn: विदुर उवाच राजन् नि:संशयं श्रेयो वाच्यस्त्वमसि बान्धवैः। न त्वशुश्रूषमाणे वै वाक्यं सम्प्रतिष्ठिति॥
en: Vidura said : O king, there is no doubt your friends have spoken to you what is good for you. But as you don't listen to their words, they find no place here,

sn: प्रियं हितं च तद् वाक्यमुक्तवान् कुरुसत्तमः। भीष्मः शांतनवो राजन् प्रतिगृहणसि तन्न च॥ तथा द्रोणेन बहुधा भाषितं हितमुत्तमम्। तच्च राधासुतः कर्णो मन्यते न हितं तव॥
en: O king, the best of Kurus, the son of Shantanu (Bhishma) has said what is for your great good, but you do not accept it (his advice). What has been said by Drona is for your good, but the son of Radha, Karna, does not consider it for your good.

sn: चिन्तयंश्च न पश्यामि राजंस्तव सुहृत्तमम्। आभ्यां पुरुषसिंहाभ्यं यो वा स्यात् प्रज्ञयाधिकः॥
en: O king, after (due) reflection I do not find there is any who is a better friend of your than these two best of men (Bhishma and Drona) or who excels them in wisdom.

sn: इमौ हि वृद्धौ वयसा प्रज्ञया च श्रुतेन च। समौ च त्वयि राजेन्द्र तथा पाण्डुसुतेषु च॥
en: These two are old in age, in wisdom and in Shastras. O king, they look at the sons of Pandu with equal eyes.

sn: धर्मे चानवरौ राजन् सत्यतायां च भारत। रामाद् दाशरथेश्चैव गयाच्चैव न संशयः॥
en: O descendant of the Bharata, O king they are not certainly inferior to Rama, the son of Dasharatha and Gaya in the virtue and truthfulness.

sn: न चोक्तवन्तावश्रेय पुरस्तादपि किंचन। न चाप्यपकृतं किंचिदनयोर्लक्ष्यते त्वयि॥ तावभौ पुरुषव्याघ्रावनागसि नृपे त्वयि। न मन्त्रयेतां त्वच्छ्रेयः कथं सत्यपराक्रमौ॥
en: It is not seen that they have ever given you evil advice. O king, you too have never injured them. Why should, therefore, these best of men, who are ever truthful, give you wicked advice?

sn: प्रज्ञावन्तौ नरश्रेष्ठावस्मॅिल्लोके नराधिप। त्वन्निमित्तपतो नेमौ किंचिज्जिा वदिष्यतः॥
en: O king, these foremost of men are endued with wisdom; they will never give you evil advises or say any thing that is crooked.

sn: इति मे नैष्ठिकी बुद्धिवर्तते कुरुनन्दन। न चार्थहेतोर्धर्मौ वक्ष्यतः पक्षसंश्रितम्॥
en: O descendant of Kuru, this is my firm conviction that being tempted by wealth these, learned as they are in the precepts of morality, will never utter anything savouring partisanship.

sn: एतद्धि परमं श्रेयो मन्येऽहं तव भारत। दुर्योधनप्रभृतयः पुत्रा राजन् यथा तव॥ तथैव पाण्डवेयास्ते पुत्रा राजन् न संशयः। तेषु चेदहितं किंचिन्मन्त्रयेयुरतद्विदः॥ मन्त्रिणस्ते न च श्रेयः प्रपश्यन्ति विशेषतः। अथ ते हृदये राजन् विशेष: स्वेषु वर्तते। ते॥ अन्तरस्थं वितृण्वानाः श्रेयः कुर्युर्न ते ध्रुवम्॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, I consider what they have said is highly beneficial to you. O king, the Pandavas are certainly your sons as much as Duryodhana and others. Therefore, those ministers who give you any advice that is fraught with evil intentions towards the Pandavas do not really look after your interest. O king, if there is any partiality (for your sons) in your heart, it is certain that they who seek to excite it do you no good.

sn: एतदर्थमिमौ राजन् महात्मानौ महाद्युती। नोचतुर्विवृतं किंचिन्न ह्येष तव निश्चयः॥
en: Therefore, O king, I think these illustrious and effulgent persons have not certainly said anything that leads to evil. You however do not understand it.

sn: यच्चाप्यशक्यतां तेषामहतुः पुरुषर्षभौ। तत् तथा पुरुषव्याघ्र तव तद् भद्रमस्तु
en: O best of kings, what these excellent men have said regarding the invincibility of the Pandavas is perfectly true. Do not think otherwise. Be blessed.

sn: कथं हि पाण्डवः श्रीमान् सव्यसाची धनंजयः। शक्यो विजेतुं संग्रामे राजन् मघवतापि हि॥
en: O king, can the handsome Pandavas Savyasachi Dhananjaya be ever vanquished in battle even by Maghavata (Indra) himself?

sn: भीमसेनो महाबाहुर्नागायुतबलो महान्। कथं स्म युधि शक्येत विजेतुममरैरपि॥
en: Can the powerful Bhimsena of strong arms possessing the might of ten thousand elephants be vanquished in battle even by the immortals?

sn: तथैव कृतिनौ युद्धे यमौ यमसुताविव। कथं विजेतुं शक्यौ तौ रणे जीवितुमिच्छता॥
en: Who having the desire of living can vanquish in battle the twins (Nakula and Sahadeva), who are like the sons of Yama himself and who are both well-skilled in battle?

sn: यस्मिन् धृतिरनुक्रोशः क्षमा सत्यं पराक्रमः। नित्यानि पाण्डवे ज्येष्ठे स जीयेत रणे कथम्॥
en: How the eldest Pandavas (Yudhishthira) in whom patience, mercy, can son forgiveness, truth and prowess are always present, be ever vanquished?

sn: येषां पक्षधरो रामो येषां मन्त्री जनार्दनः। किं न तैरजितं संख्ये येषां पक्षे च सात्यकिः॥
en: Is there any whom they have not already vanquished in battle, who who have have Rama (Baladeva) as their ally, Janardana (Krishna) as their counsellor, Satyaki as their supporter.

sn: द्रुपदः श्वशुरो येषां येषां श्यालाश्च पार्षताः। धृष्टद्युम्नमुखा वीरा भ्रातरो द्रुपदात्मजाः॥ सोऽशक्यतां च विज्ञाय तेषामग्रे च भारता दायाद्यतां च धर्मेण सम्यक् तेषु समाचर॥
en: Drupada as their father-in-law and the descendant of Prishata, Drupada's Dhrishtadyumna and his other heroic brothers as their brother-in-law? O descendant of Bharata, remembering this and knowing that their claim to the kingdom is even prior to yours, behave virtuous towards them.

sn: इदं निर्दिष्टमयशः पुरोचनकृतं महत्। तेषामनुग्रहेणाद्य राजन् प्रक्षालयात्मनः॥
en: O king, the stain of calumny is on you on account of the act of Purochana. Wash yourself off it by kindly behaving towards them (the Pandavas).

sn: तेषामनुग्रहश्चायं सर्वेषां चैव नः कुले। जीवितं च परं श्रेयः क्षत्रस्य च विवर्धनम्॥
en: Your kindly behaviour towards them will be for our great good. It will protect the lives of all of us of the Kuru race and it will lead to the growth of the whole Kshatriya race.

sn: दुपदोऽपि महान् राजा कृतवैस्च नः पुरा। तस्य संग्रहणं राजन् स्वपक्षस्य विवर्धनम्॥
en: O king, we have formerly waged a great war with the king of Drupada; if we can now secure him as an ally, it will strengthen our party.

sn: बलवन्तश्च दाशार्हा बहवश्च विशाम्पते। यतः कृष्णस्ततः सर्वे यतः कृष्णस्ततो जयः॥
en: O king, the Dasharahas are numerous and powerful. They will be all there where Krishna will be. Where Krishna is, victory is certainly there.

sn: यच्च साम्नैव शक्येत कार्यं साधयितुं नृप। को दैवशप्तस्तत् कार्यं विग्रहेण समाचरेत्॥
en: O king, unless cursed by the celestials, who would seek to effect by means of war that which can be effected by conciliation?

sn: श्रुत्वा च जीवतः पार्थान् पौरजानपदा जनाः। बलवद् दर्शने हृष्टास्तेषां राजन् प्रियं कुरु॥
en: O king, having heard that the sons of Pritha are alive, the men of the city and the country have become exceedingly glad; and they are all eager to see them. Do what will be agreeable to them.

sn: दुर्योधनश्च कर्णश्च शकुनिश्चापि सौबलः। अधर्मयुक्ता दुष्प्रज्ञा बाला मैषां वचः कृथाः॥
en: Duryodhana, Karna and the son of Subala, Shakuni, are sinful, foolish and young. Do not listen to their words.

sn: उक्तमेतत् पुरा राजन् मया गुणवतस्तव। दुर्योधनापराधेन प्रजेयं वै विनक्ष्यति॥
en: O king, endued with all accomplishments as you are, I have told you long ago that for the fault of Duryodhana, the subjects of this kingdom will be annihilated.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच भीष्मः शांतनवो विद्वान् द्रोणश्च भगवानृषिः। हितं च परमं वाक्यं त्वं च सत्यं ब्रवीषि माम्॥
en: The learned Bhishma, the son of Shantanu and the illustrious Rishi Drona and you yourself, have said the truth and what is good for me.

sn: यथैव पाण्डोस्ते वीराः कुन्तीपुत्रा महारथाः। तथैव धर्मतः सर्वे मम पुत्रा न संशयः॥
en: There is no doubt that as those great carwarriors, the heroic sons of Kunti, are the sons of Pandu, so they are my sons also according to ordinance.

sn: यथैव मम पुत्राणामिदं राज्यं विधीयते। तथैव पाण्डुपुत्राणामिदं राज्यं न संशयः॥
en: As my sons are entitled to this kingdom, so certainly are the sons of Pandu entitled to it.

sn: क्षत्तरानय गच्छैतान् सह मात्रा सुसत्कृतान्। तया च देवरूपिण्या कृष्णया सह भारत॥
en: O Kshatta, go and in due affectionate way, bring them (the Pandavas) here along with their mother. O descendant of Bharata, bring also with them Krishna (Draupadi) of celestials beauty.

sn: दिष्ट्या जीवन्ति ते पार्था दिष्ट्या जीवति सा पृथा। दिष्ट्या दुपदकन्यां च लब्धवन्तो महारथाः॥
en: From our good fortune the sons of Pritha are alive; from our good fortune Pritha is alive. From our good fortune those great car-warriors have obtained the daughter of Drupada.

sn: दिष्ट्या वर्धामहे सर्वे दिष्ट्या शान्तः पुरोचनः । दिष्ट्या मम परं दुःखमपनीतं महाद्युते॥
en: From our good fortune our strength is increased; and from our good fortune Purochana is dead. O greatly effulgent one, from our good fortune my great grief is also removed.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततो जगाम विदुरो धृतराष्ट्रस्य शासनात्। सकाशं यज्ञसेनम्य पाण्डवानां च भारत॥ समुपादाय रत्नानि वसूनि विविधानि च। द्रौपद्याः पाण्डवानां च यज्ञसेनस्य चैव ह॥
en: Vaishampayana said : O descendant of Bharata, thereupon Vidura at the command of Dhritarashtra went to Yajnasena and the Pandavas. He carried with him numerous jewels and various kinds of wealth for Draupadi, for the Pandavas and for Yainasena.

sn: तत्र गत्वा स धर्मज्ञः सर्वशास्त्रविशारदः। दुपदं न्यायतो राजन् संयुक्तमुपतस्थिवान्॥
en: O king, having arrived there, that virtuous man, learned in all the Shastras, properly addressed Drupada and waited upon him.

sn: स चापि प्रतिजग्राह धर्मेण विदुरं ततः। चक्रतुश्च यथान्यायं कुशलप्रश्नसंविदम्॥
en: He (Drupada) too received Vidura in proper form and they both enquire after each other's welfare.

sn: ददर्श पाण्डवांस्तत्र वासुदेवं च भारत। स्नेहात् परिष्वज्य स तान् पप्रच्छानामयं ततः॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, he saw there the Pandavas and Vasudeva (Krishna). He embraced them from affection and inquired after their welfare.

sn: तैश्चाप्यमितबुद्धिः स पूजितो हि यथाक्रमम्। वचनाद् धृतराष्ट्रस्य स्नेहयुक्तं पुनः पुनः॥ पप्रच्छानामयं राजंस्ततस्तान् पाण्डुनन्दनान्। प्रददौ चापि रत्नानि विविधानि वसूनि च॥ पाण्डवानां च कुन्त्याश्च द्रौपद्याश्च विशाम्पते। द्रुपदस्य च पुत्राणां यथा दत्तानि कौरवैः॥
en: They too worshiped in due order Vidura of immeasurable intelligence. According the command of Dhritarashtra, he (Vidura) spoke to the sons of Pandu again and again words of affection. O king, he then gave to the Pandavas, Kunti, Draupadi, Drupada and Drupada's sons, the gems and various kinds of wealth, sent through him by the Kurus.

sn: प्रोवाच चामितमतिः प्रश्रितं विनयान्वितः। द्रुपदं पाण्डुपुत्राणां संनिधौ केशवस्य च॥
en: The immeasurably intelligent Vidura then, in the presence of the Pandavas and Keshava (Krishna), thus modestly addressed Drupada in words of affection.

sn: विदुर उवाच राजञ्छृणु सहामात्यः सपुत्रश्च वचो मम। धृतराष्ट्रः सपुत्रस्त्वां सहामात्यः सबान्धवः॥ अब्रवीत् कुशलं राजन् प्रीयमाणः पुनः पुनः। प्रीतिमांस्ते दृढं चापि सम्बन्धेन नराधिप॥
en: Vidura said: O king, listen to my words with your sons and ministers. Dhritarashtra with his ministers, sons and friends. Has again and again joyously inquired after your welfare. O king, he has been pleased by the alliance with you.

sn: तथा भीष्मः शांतनवः कौरवैः सह सर्वशः। कुशलं त्वां महाप्राज्ञः सर्वतः परिपृच्छति॥
en: The son of Shantanu, the greatly wise Bhishma with all the Kurus has enquired after your welfare in every respect.

sn: भारद्वाजो महाप्राज्ञो द्रोणः प्रियसखस्तव। समाश्लेषमुपेत्य त्वां कुशलं परिपृच्छति॥
en: The son of Bharadvaja, the greatly, wise Drona, your beloved friend, embracing you mentally, has enquired after your welfare.

sn: धृतराष्ट्रश्च पाञ्चाल्य त्वया सम्बन्धमीयिवान्। कृतार्थं मन्यतेऽत्मानं तथा सर्वेऽपि कौरवाः॥
en: Panchala king, Dhritarashtra and all the Kurus regard themselves very blessed by this alliance with you.

sn: न तथा राज्यसम्प्राप्तिस्तेषां प्रीतिकरी मता। यथा सम्बन्धकं प्राप्य यज्ञसेन त्वया सह॥
en: Yajnasena, this alliance with you has made them more happy than if they had acquired a new kingdom.

sn: एतद् विदित्वा तुभवान् प्रस्थापयतु पाण्डवान्। द्रष्टुं हि पाण्डुपुत्रांश्च त्वरन्ति कुरवो भृशम्॥
en: Knowing all this, O Sir, permit the Pandavas to go there. The Kurus exceedingly eager to see the sons of Pandu.

sn: विप्रोषिता दीर्घकालमेते चापि नरर्षभाः। उत्सुका नगरं द्रष्टुं भविष्यन्ति तथा पृथा॥
en: These best of men (the Pandavas) are long absent (from Hastinapur). They and Pritha (Kunti) must be very eager to see their own city.

sn: कृष्णामपि च पाञ्चालीं सर्वाः कुरुवरस्त्रियः। द्रष्टुकामाः प्रतीक्षन्ते पुरं च विषयाश्च नः॥
en: All the Kuru Ladies, all the citizens and our subjects are eagerly waiting to see the Panchala princess Krishna.

sn: स भवान् पाण्डुपुत्राणामाज्ञापयतु मा चिरम्। गमनं सहदाराणामेतदत्र मतं मम॥
en: Therefore, O Sir, my opinion is that you should permit the Pandavas to go there with their wife without any further delay. are

sn: निसृष्टेषु त्वया राजन् पाण्डवेषु महात्मसु। ततोऽहं प्रेषयिष्यामि धृतराष्ट्रस्य शीघ्रगान्। आगमिष्यन्ति कौन्तेयाः कुन्ती च सह कृष्णया॥
en: O king, when the illustrious Pandavas will get your permission, I shall then send information to Dhritarashtra by quick messengers. Then, O king, the Pandavas will set out with Kunti and Krishna (Draupadi.)

sn: दुपद उवाच एवमेतन्महाप्राज्ञ यथाऽऽत्थ विदुराद्य माम्। ममापि परमो हर्षः सम्बन्धेऽस्मिन् कृते प्रभो॥
en: Drupada said: O Vidura, O greatly learned man, it is as you say. O lord, I too have been exceedingly happy by this alliance.

sn: गमनं चाप युक्तं स्याद् दृढमेषां महात्मनाम्। न तु तावन्मया युक्तमेतद् वक्तुं स्वयं गिरा।॥ यदा तु मन्यते वीरः कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः। भीमसेनार्जुनो चैव यमौ च पुरुषर्षभौ॥ रामकृष्णौ च धर्मज्ञो तदा गच्छन्तु पाण्डवाः। एतौ हि पुरुषव्याघ्रावेषां प्रियहिते रतौ॥
en: It is highly proper for these illustrious princess to return to their ancestral kingdom. But it is not proper for me to say this myself. If the hero, Yudhishthira, the son of Kunti, if Bhima and Arjuna, if these best of men the twins (Nakula and Sahadeva) and if Rama and Krishna, both learned in the precepts of religion, wish it, then let the Pandavas go there. These two best of men (Rama and Krishna) are ever engaged in doing what is agreeable and beneficial to them (the Pandavas).

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच परवन्तो वयं राजंस्त्वयि सर्वे सहानुगाः। यथा वक्ष्यसि नः प्रीत्या तत् करिष्यामहे वयम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said: O king, I with all my brothers, am now dependent on you. We shall all gladly do what you will command us to do.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततोऽब्रवीद् वासुदेवो गमनं रोचते मम। यथा वा मन्यते राजा दुपदः सर्वधर्मवित्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Thereupon Vasudeva said, “I am of opinion that they should go. But we must all abide by the opinion of the king Drupada who is learned in all the precepts of virtue."

sn: दुपद उवाच यथैव मन्यते वीरो दाशार्हः पुरुषोत्तमः। प्राप्तकालं महाबाहुः सा बुद्धिनिश्चिता मम॥ यथैव हि महाभागाः कौन्तेया मम समाप्रतम्। तथैव वासुदेवस्य पाण्डुपुत्रा न संशयः॥
en: Drupada said : Having considered all the circumstances, I certainly agree with the foremost of men, the heroic and mighty armed Dasharaha (Krishna). There is no doubt the illustrious sons of Kunti, the Pandavas, are now to me as they are to Vasudeva.

sn: न तद् ध्यायति कौन्तेयः पाण्डुपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः। यथैषां पुरुषव्याघ्रः श्रेयो ध्यायति केशवः॥
en: The son of Kunti, Yudhishthira, himself does not seek the welfare of the Pandavas so much as this foremost of men Keshava (Krishna) does.

sn: वैशाम्पायन उवाच ततस्ते समनुज्ञाता दुपदेन महात्मना। पाण्डवाश्चैव कृष्णश्च विदुरश्च महीपते॥ आदाय द्रौपदी कृष्णां कुन्तीं चैव यशस्विनीम्। सविहारं सुर जग्मुर्नगरं नागसाह्वयम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : O king, having been commanded by the illustrious Drupada, the Pandavas, Krishna and Vidura. Taking with them the daughter of Drupada, Krishna and the illustrious Kunti, journeyed in pleasure towards the city of Hastinapur.

sn: श्रुत्वा चाप्यागतान् वीरान् धृतराष्ट्रो जनेश्वरः। प्रतिग्रहाय पाण्डूनां प्रेषयामास कौरवान्॥
en: The king, Dhritarashtra, learning that those heroes (the Pandavas) had arrived, sent out the Kurus to receive them.

sn: विकर्णं च महेष्वासं चित्रसेनं च भारत। द्रोणं च परमेष्वासं गौतमं कृपमेव च।॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, Vikarna, the great bowmen Chitrasena, the foremost of bowmen Drona and the son of Gautama Kripa (went out to receive them).

sn: तैस्ते परिवृता वीराः शोभमाना महाबलाः। नगरं हास्तिनपुरं शनैः प्रविविशुस्तदा॥ कौतूहलेन नगरं दीप्यमानमिवाभवत्। तत्र ते पुरुषव्याघ्राः शोकदुःखविनाशनाः॥ तत उच्चावचा वाचः पौरैः प्रियचिकीर्षुभिः। उदीरिता अशृण्वंस्ते पाण्डवा हृदयंगमाः॥
en: Surrounded by those (illustrious men), those mighty heroes (the Pandavas), their splendour (many times) increased, slowly entered the city of Hastinapur. The city became radiant with the curious sight-seers of the city. Those foremost of men, the dispelled of grief and sorrow. The Pandavas, dear to the hearts of the people, heard as they proceeded, various exclamations which the citizens, ever desirous of obeying the wishes of those princes, loudly uttered.

sn: अयं स पुरुषव्याघ्रः पुनरायाति धर्मवित्। यो नः स्वानिव दायादान् धर्मेण परिरक्षति॥
en: They exclaimed, “Here return that best of men (Yudhishthira), learned in the precepts of virtue. He always protects us as if we are his nearest relatives.

sn: अद्य पाण्डुर्महाराजो वनादिव जनप्रियः। आगतः प्रियमस्माकं चिकीर्षुर्नात्र संशयः॥
en: It seems as if the great king Pandu, ever beloved of his subjects, returns to-day from the forest to do what is agreeable to us.

sn: किं नु नाद्य कृतं तात सर्वेषां नः परं प्रियम्। यन्नः कुन्तीसुता वीरा नगरं पुनरागताः॥
en: What good is not done to us today when the heroic sons of Kunti returns to our city?

sn: यदि दत्तं यदि हुतं विद्यते यदि नस्तपः। तेन तिष्ठन्तु नगरे पाण्डवाः शरदां शतम्॥ ततस्ते धृतराष्र्ण्य भीष्मस्य च महात्मनः। अन्येषां च तदर्हाणां चक्रुः पादाभिवन्दनम्॥
en: If we have ever given away in charity, if we have ever poured libations of ghee on the (sacrificial) fire, if we have any ascetic merit, let the Pandavas live in our city for one hundred years." They (the Pandavas) worshipped the feet of Dhritarashtra, as also those of Bhishma and also the feet of every body else that deserved the honour.

sn: कृत्वा तु कुशलप्रश्नं सर्वेण नगरेण च। न्यविशन्ताथ वेश्मानि धृतराष्ट्रस्य शासनात्॥
en: They inquired after the welfare of all the citizens. They then entered the palace assigned to them at the command of Dhritarashtra.

sn: विश्रान्तास्ते महात्मान: कंचित् कालं महाबलाः। आहूता धृतराष्ट्रेण राज्ञा शांतनवेन च॥
en: When those illustrious and greatly strong heroes had taken rest for some time, they were summoned by the king Dhritarashtra and the son of Shantanu (Bhishma.)

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच भ्रातृभिः सह कौन्तेय निबोध गदतो मम। पुनर्वो विग्रहो मा भूत् खाण्डवप्रस्थमाविश॥
en: Dhritarashtra said: O sun of Kunti, (Yudhishthira), listen with your brothers to what I say. Go to Khandavaprastha, so that no difference may arise again.

sn: न च वो वसतस्तत्र कश्चिच्छक्तः प्रबाधितुम्। संरक्ष्यमाणान् पार्थेन त्रिदशानिव वज्रिणा॥ अर्धं राज्यस्य सम्प्राप्य खाण्डवप्रस्थमाविश।
en: If you live there, none will be able to injure you. Taking half of the kingdom, live at Khandavaprastha protected by Partha (Arjuna), as the celestials are by the wielder of the thunder (Indra).

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच प्रतिगृह्य तु तद् वाक्यं नृपं सर्वे प्रणम्य च॥ प्रतस्थिरे ततो घोरं वनं तन्मनुजर्षभाः। अर्धं राज्यस्य सम्प्राप्य खाण्डवप्रस्थमाविशन्॥ ततस्ते पाण्डवास्तत्र गत्वा कृष्णपुरोगमाः। मण्डयां चक्रिरे तद् वै परं स्वर्गवदच्युताः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Agreeing to what the king said, those best of men worshipped the kings and started for that fearful forest. Receiving half of the kingdom, the Pandavas entered the Khandavaprastha, Krishna being at the head of the procession. Thereafter, the infallible Pandavas accompanied by Krishna, and by going to that place made it as glorious as heaven.

sn: ततः पुण्ये शिवे देशे शान्तिं कृत्वा महारथाः। नगरं मापयामासुद्वैपायनपुरोगमाः॥
en: Those great car-warriors, selecting with the assistance of Dvaipayana a sacred and auspicious place, performed the propitiatory ceremonies and measured out a piece of land to found a city.

sn: सागरप्रतिरूपाभिः परिखाभिरलंकृतम्। प्राकारेण च सम्पन्नं दिवमावृत्य तिष्ठता॥ पाण्डुराभ्रप्रकाशेन हिमरश्मिनिभेन च। शुशुभे तत् पुरश्रेष्ठं नागैर्भोगवती यथा॥
en: It was surrounded by a most as wide as the sea and by wall rising high up to the sky. It was as white as the white clouds or the rays of the moon. Those foremost of cities looked resplendent like the city of Bhogavati of the Nagas.

sn: द्विपक्षगरुडप्रख्यारैः सौधैश्च शोभितम्। गुप्तमभ्रचयप्रख्यैर्गोपुरैर्मन्दरोपमैः॥ विविधैरपि निर्विः शस्त्रोपेतैः सुसंवृतैः। शक्तिभिश्चावृतं तद्धि द्विजिलैरिव पन्नगैः॥ तल्पैश्चाभ्यासिकैर्युक्तं शुशुभे योधरक्षितम्। तीक्ष्णारूशशतघ्नीभिर्यन्त्रजालैश्च शोभितम्॥
en: It was adorned with mansions having windows like the out-stretched wings of Garuda. It was protected with gates looking like the clouds and they were as high as the Mandara mountain; the weapons of the enemy could not make any impression on them. They were almost covered with darts and other missiles like the double tongued snakes. The turrets were filled with armed men and the walls were lined with warriors. It was wellstocked with various weapons of attack; there were thousands of sharp hooks and Shataghanis (a sort of weapon) and numerous other machines; there were also many iron wheels planted on them. With these were adorned that best of cities.

sn: आयसैश्च महाचक्रैः शुशुभे तत् पुरोत्तमम्। सुविभक्तमहारथ्यं देवतावाधवर्जितम्॥ विरोचमानं विविधैः पाण्डुरैर्भवनोत्तमैः। तत् त्रिविष्टपसंकाशमिन्द्रप्रस्थं व्यरोचत॥
en: The streets were all wide and excellently laid out. Adorned with innumerable white mansions, the city looked like Amaravati (the celestials city); it looked like a mass clouds charged with lightings. It came to be called Indraprastha.

sn: मेघवृन्दमिवाकाशे विद्धं विद्युत्समावृतम्। तत्र रम्ये शिवे देशे कौरव्यस्य निवेशनम्॥
en: In a delightful and auspicious place stood the palace of those descendants of Kuru (the Pandavas). It was full of every kind of wealth like the palace of the celestials) treasurer (Kubera) himself.

sn: शुशुभे धनसम्पूर्ण धनाध्यक्षक्षयोपमम्। तत्रागच्छन् द्विजा राजन् सर्ववेदविदां वराः॥ निवासं रोचयन्ति स्म सर्वभाषाविस्तथा। वणिजश्चाययुस्तत्र नानादिग्भ्यो धनार्थिनः॥
en: O king, there came with the desire of living (in that city) numerous Brahmanas learned in all the Vedas and conversant with every language. There came also from every direction numerous merchants with the desire of earning wealth.

sn: सर्वशिल्पविदस्तत्र वासायाभ्यागमंस्तदा। उद्यानानि च रम्याणि नगरस्य समन्ततः॥ आप्रैराम्रातकैनीपैरशोकैश्चम्पकैस्तथा। पुन्नागैर्नागपुष्पैश्च लकुचैः पनसैस्तथा॥ शालतालतमालैश्च बकुलैश्च सकेतकैः। मनोहरैः सुपुष्पैश्च फलभारावनामितैः॥
en: There also came with the desire of living (in that city) numerous men well-skilled in all arts. Around the city were laid out many charming gardens with Amras, Amratakas, Kadambas, Ashokas, Champakas, Punnagas, Nagas, Lakuchas, Panasas, Salas, Talas, Tamalas, Bakulas and Ketakas. They were all beautiful and blossoming; they bent down with the weight of their fruits.

sn: प्राचीनामलकैलॊधेरकोलैश्च सुपुष्पितैः। जम्बूभिः पाटलाभिश्च कुब्जकैरतिमुक्तकैः॥ करवीरैः पारिजातैरन्यैश्च विविधैर्दुमैः। नित्यपुष्पफलोपेते नाद्विजगणायुतैः॥
en: The Amlokas, Lodhras, blossoming Ankolas, Jambus, Patalas, Kubjakas, Atimuktakas, Karaviras, Parijatas and various other tress were there. All adorned with flowers and fruits and thronged with birds of various kinds.

sn: मत्तवहिणसंघुष्टकोकिलैश्च सदामदैः। गृहैरादर्शविमलैर्विविधैश्च लतागृहैः॥ मनोहरैचित्रगृहैस्तथाजगतिपर्वतैः। वापीभिर्विविधाभिश्च पूर्णाभिः परमाम्भसा॥ सरोभिरतिरम्यैश्च पद्मोत्पलसुगन्धिभिः। हंसकारण्डवयुतैश्चक्रवाकोपशोभितैः॥ रम्याश्च विविधास्तत्र पुष्करिण्यो वनावृताः। तडागानि च रम्याणि बृहन्ति सुबहूनि च॥
en: These verdant groves were resounded with the notes of the maddened peacocks and Kokilas. There were various pleasure houses bright as mirrors and innumerable bowers of creepers, charming artificial hillocks, many lakes full to the brim with crystal water and delightful tanks fragrant with lotuses and lilies and adorned with swans, ducks and Chakravakas. There many tanks overgrown with fine aquatic plants and various large and beautiful pounds. were

sn: तेषां पुण्यजनोपेतं राष्ट्रमाविशतां महत्। पाण्डवानां महाराज शश्वत् प्रीतिरवर्धत्॥
en: O great king, the joy of the Pandavas increased from day to day in consequence of their residence in that large kingdom which was inhabited by pious men.

sn: तत्र भीष्मेण राज्ञा च धर्मप्रणयने कृते। पाण्डवाः समपद्यन्त खाण्डवप्रस्थवासिनः॥
en: Thus inconsequence of the virtuous conduct of Bhishma and the king (Dhritarashtra) the Pandavas became the dwellers of Khandavaprastha.

sn: पञ्चभिस्तैर्महेष्वासैरिन्द्रकल्पैः समन्वितम्। शुशुभे तत् पुरश्रेष्ठं नागैर्भोगवती यथा॥
en: Adorned with those excellent and great bow-men, each like an Indra himself, that best of cities looked like Bhogavati with the Nagas.

sn: तां निवेश्य ततो वीरो रामेण सह केशवः। ययौ द्वारवती राजन् पाण्डवानुमते तदा॥
en: O king, having settled the Pandavas there, the heroic Krishna, on obtaining their leave, came back with Rama to Dvaravati.

sn: जनमेजय उवाच एवं सम्प्राप्य राज्यं तदिन्द्रप्रस्थं तपोधन। अत ऊर्ध्वं महात्मानः किमकुर्वत पाण्डवाः॥ सर्व एव महासत्त्वा मम पूर्वपितामहाः। द्रौपदी धर्मपत्नी च कथं तानन्ववर्तत।॥
en: Janamejaya said : O ascetic, what did those illustrious men, the high-souled ones, my grandsires, the Pandavas, do after obtaining the kingdom of Indraprastha? How did their wedded wife Draupadi obey them all?

sn: कथं च पञ्च कृष्णायामेकस्यां ते नराधिपाः। वर्तमाना महाभागा नाभिद्यन्त परस्परम्॥
en: How was it that no dissension arose amongst those illustrious rulers of men, though attached to one wife Krishna?

sn: श्रोतुमिच्छाम्यहं सर्वं विस्तरेण तपोधन। तेषां चेष्टितमन्योन्यं युक्तानां कृष्णया सह॥
en: O ascetic Rishi, I desire to hear everything in detail as regards their conduct towards one another after their union with Krishna.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच धृतराष्ट्राभ्यनुज्ञाता: कृष्णया सह पाण्डवाः। रेमिरे खाण्डवप्रस्थे प्राप्तराज्या: परंतपाः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having obtained their kingdom at the command of Dhritarashtra, those chastisers of foes, the Pandavas, sported with Krishna at Indraprastha.

sn: प्राप्य राज्यं महातेजाः सत्यसंधो युधिष्ठिरः। पालयामास धर्मेण पृथिवीं भ्रातृभिः सह॥
en: Having obtained the kingdom, the ever truthful greatly effulgent Yudhishthira with his brothers virtuously ruled the kingdom.

sn: जितारयो महाप्रज्ञाः सत्यधर्मपरायणाः। मुदं परमिकां प्राप्तास्तत्रोषुः पाण्डुनन्दनाः॥
en: Having defeated all their foes, the greatly wise and ever devoted to truth and virtue, the sons of Pandu lived there in great happiness.

sn: कुर्वाणां पौरकार्याणि सर्वाणि पुरुषर्षभाः। आसांचक्रुर्महार्हेषु पार्थिवेष्वासनेषु च॥
en: Those of men, seated on costly royal seats, discharged all the duties of government.

sn: अथ तेषूपविष्टेषु सर्वेष्वेव महात्मसु। नारदस्त्वथ देवर्षिराजगाम यदृच्छया॥
en: When (one day) those illustrious heroes so seated, there came to them the celestials Rishi Narada in course of his travels.

sn: तमागतमृर्षि दृष्ट्वा प्रत्युद्गम्याभिवाद्यच। आसनं रुचिरं तस्मै प्रददौ स्वं युधिष्ठिरः। देवर्षेरुपविष्टस्य स्वयमर्थ्य यथाविधि॥ प्रादाद् युधिष्ठिरो धीमान् राज्यं तस्मै न्यवेदयत्। प्रतिगृह्य तु तां पूजामृषिः प्रीतमनास्तदा॥
en: Yudhishthira gave him his own excellent seat. When the celestials Rishi was seated, the wise Yudhishthira duly offered him the Arghya with his own hands. The Rishi accepted the worship and became very much pleased.

sn: आशीभिर्वर्धयित्वा च तमुवाचास्यतामिति। निषसादाभ्यनुज्ञातस्ततो राजा युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Uttering benedictions on him, he (the Rishi) asked him (Yudhishthira) to take his seat. Thus commanded, the king Yudhishthira took his seat.

sn: कथयामास कृष्णायै भगवन्तमुपस्थितम्। श्रुत्वैतद् द्रौपदी चापि शुचिर्भूत्वा समाहिता॥
en: He sent words to Krishna informing her of the arrival of the high-souled (Rishi). Hearing it, Draupadi, after properly purifying herself.

sn: जगाम तत्र यत्रास्ते नारदः पाण्डवैः सह। तस्याभिवाद्य चरणौ देवर्षेर्धर्मचारिणी॥
en: Went there where Narada was with the Pandavas. And that lady of virtuous deeds worshipped his feet.

sn: कृताञ्जलिः सुसंवीता स्थिताथ दुपदात्मजा। तस्याश्चापि स धर्मात्माः सत्यवागृषिसत्तमः॥
en: Then the daughter of Drupada, being properly covered with her veil, stood before him with joined hands. That virtuous, truthful and excellent Rishi.

sn: आशिषो विविधाः प्रोच्य राजपुत्र्यास्तु नारदः। गम्यतामिति होवाच भगवांस्तामनिन्दिताम्॥
en: The illustrious Rishi Narada, after uttering various benedictions on the princess and saying that faultless lady, “Go," sent her away.
