sn: सुभद्रा त्वथ शैलेन्द्रमभ्ययैव रैवतम्। दैवतानि च सर्वाणि ब्राह्मणान् स्वस्ति वाच्य च॥ प्रदक्षिणं गिरेः कृत्वा प्रययौ द्वारका प्रति। तामभिदुत्य कौन्तेयः प्रसह्यारोपयद् स्थम्। सुभद्रां चारुसर्वाङ्गी कामबाणप्रपीडितः॥
en: Subhadra, having worshipped that king of hills, Raivataka and the celestials and having been blessed by all the Brahmanas, and having walked round the hill, was returning towards Dwarka. The son of Kunti, struck by the arrows of the god of love, suddenly rushed towards that faultless featured Subhadra and forcibly took her upon his chariot.

sn: ततः स पुरुषव्याघ्रस्तामादाय शुचिस्मिताम्। रथेन काञ्चना न प्रययौ स्वपुरं प्रति॥
en: Thereupon that best of men, having seized that lady of sweet-smiles, proceeded (in haste) on his golden car towards his own city (Indraprastha).

sn: ह्वियमाणां तु तां दृष्ट्वा सुभद्रां सैनिका जनाः। विक्रोशन्तोऽद्रवन् सर्वे द्वारकामभितः पुरीम्॥
en: Seeing Subhadra thus forcibly carried away, her armed attendants all ran crying towards the city of Dvarka.

sn: ते समासाद्य सहिताः सुधर्मामभितः सभाम्। सभापालस्य तत् सर्वमाचख्युः पार्थविक्रमम्॥
en: Having arrived all together to that (Yadava) court, called Sudharma, they represented to the Sabhapala (the chief officer of the court), all about the prowess of Partha.

sn: तेषां श्रुत्वा सभापालो भेरी सांनाहिकी ततः। समाजघ्ने महाघोषां जाम्बूनदपरिष्कृताम्॥
en: Having heard this, the Sabhapala blew his golden decked trumpet of loud blare, calling every one to arms.

sn: क्षुब्धास्तेनाथ शब्देन भोजवृष्ण्यन्धकास्तदा। अन्नपानमपास्याथ समापेतुः समन्ततः॥
en: Alarmed by that sound, the Bhojas the Vrishnis and the Andhakas poured in from all directions, even those who were eating and drinking came leaving their food and drink,

sn: तत्र जाम्बूनदाङ्गानि स्पर्ध्यास्तरणवन्ति च। मणिविदुमचित्राणि ज्वलिताग्निप्रभाणि च॥ भेजिरे पुरुषव्याघ्रा वृष्ण्यन्धकमहारथाः। सिंहासनानि शतशो धिष्ण्यानीव हुताशनाः॥
en: Like blazing fires taking faggots to increase their splendour, those best of men, the great car-warriors of the Vrishni and the Andhaka races, possessing the lustre of the blazing fire, took their seats on thousands of golden thrones, covered with excellent carpets and adorned with gems and corals.

sn: तेषां समुपविष्टानां देवानामिव संनये। आचख्यौ चेष्टितं जिष्णोः सभापाल: सहानुगः॥
en: When they were all seated like an assembly of celestials, the Sabhapala with his followers narrated all about the conduct of Jishnu (Arjuna).

sn: तच्छ्रुत्वा वृष्णिवीरास्ते मदसंरक्तलोचनाः। अमृष्यमाणाः पार्थस्य समुत्पेतुरहंकृताः॥
en: Having heard it, the proud heroes of the Vrishni, with their eyes red with wine, rose up from their seats, being unable to brook the conduct of Partha.

sn: योजयवं रथानाशु प्रासानाहरतेति च। धनूंषि च महार्हाणि कवचानि बृहन्ति च॥ सूतानुच्चुक्रुशुः केचिद् रथान् योजयतेति च। स्वयं च तुरगान् केचिदयुञ्जन् हेमभूषितान्॥
en: Some cried, “Yoke our cars", some “Bring our weapons, “some” Bring our costly bows and strong armours," some loudly called their charioteers to yoke their horses adorned with gold to their cars.

sn: रथेष्वानीयमानेषु कवचेषु ध्वजेषु च। अभिक्रन्दे नृवीराणां तदासीत् तुमुलं महत्॥
en: While their cars, their armours and their standards were being brought, the uproars of those heroes became exceedingly great.

sn: वनमाली ततः क्षीबः कैलासशिखरोपमः। नीलवासा मदोसिक्त इदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Then proud and intoxicated with wine, Baladeva, who was like the Kailasa mountain, adorned with the garlands of wild flowers and attired in blue robes, thus spoke to all.

sn: किमिदं कुरुथाप्रज्ञास्तूष्णीभूते जनार्दने। अस्य भावमविज्ञाय संक्रुद्धा मोघगर्जिताः॥
en: "O senseless men, what are you doing when Janardana (Krishna) is sitting silent? Without knowing what is in his heart, you are vainly roaring in wrath.

sn: एष तावदभिप्रायमाख्यातु स्वं महामतिः। यदस्य रुचिरं कर्तुं तत् कुरुध्वमतन्द्रिताः॥
en: Let the high-minded (Krishna) speak out what he proposes to do. Accomplish with all alacrity what he desires to do."

sn: ततस्ते तद् वचः श्रुत्वा ग्राह्यरूपं हलायुधात्। तूष्णीम्भूतास्ततः सर्वे साधु साध्विति चाब्रुवन्॥
en: Having heard these words of Halayudha (Baladeva) which deserved, to be accepted, they all exclaimed, “Excellent,” “Excellent.” They then became silent.

sn: समं वचो निशम्यैव बलदेवस्य धीमतः। पुनरेव सभामध्ये सर्वे ते समुपाविशन्॥
en: Silence have been restored by the words of the intelligent Baladeva, they again all took their seats in that court.

sn: ततोऽब्रवीद् वासुदेवं वचो रामः परंतपः। किमवागुपविष्टोऽसि प्रेक्षमाणो जनार्दन॥
en: Then the chastiser of foes Rama (Baladeva) thus spoke to Vasudeva (Krishna), "O Janardana, why do you not speak, why are you silently gazing?

sn: सत्कृतस्त्वत्कृते पार्थः सर्वैरस्माभिरच्युत। न च सोऽर्हति तां पूजां दुर्बुद्धिः कुलपांसनः॥
en: O Achyuta, it was for your sake that Partha had been welcomed and received with all honour by us. It appears that wretch, that fool, does not deserve our welcome and honour.

sn: को हि तत्रैव भुक्त्वान्नं भाजनं भेत्तुमर्हसि। मन्यमानः कुले जातमात्मानं पुरुषः क्वचित्॥
en: Is there a man born of a respectable family who will break the very plate after having dined off it?

sn: इच्छन्नेव हि सम्बन्धं कृतं पूर्वं च मानयन्। को हि नाम भवेनार्थी साहसेन समाचरेत्॥
en: Even if one desires to have such an alliance, who is there who desiring happiness will act so rashly remembering the services he has received?

sn: सोऽवमन्य तथास्माकमनादृत्य च केशवम्। प्रसह्य हृतवानद्य सुभद्रां मृत्युमात्मनः॥
en: By insulting us and disregarding Keshava (Krishna) he has carried away Subhadra by force wishing to compass his own death.

sn: कथं हि शिरसो मध्ये कृतं तेन पदं मम। मर्षयिष्यामि गोविन्द पादस्पर्शमिवोरगः॥
en: He has placed his foot on my head. O Govinda, how shall I bear it, (shall I not resent it) like a snake trodden by foot?

sn: अद्य निष्कौरवामेकः करिष्यामि वसुंधराम्। न हि मे मर्षणीयोऽयमर्जुनस्य व्यतिक्रमः॥
en: I shall alone to-day make the earth free of all Kauravas. Never shall I put up with this insult offered to us by Arjuna."

sn: तं तथा गर्जमानं तु मेघदुन्दुभिनिःस्वनम्। अन्वपद्यन्त ते सर्वे भोजवृष्ण्यन्धकास्तदा॥
en: Thereupon all the Bhojas, Vrishnis and the Andhakas, assembled there approved of every thing that Baladeva said and they roared like the sounds of kettledrum or the clouds.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच उक्तवन्तो यथा वीर्यमसकृत् सर्ववृष्ण्यः। ततोऽब्रवीद् वासुदेवो वाक्यं धर्मार्थसंयुतम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : When the powerful Vrishnis all began to speak in this strain, then Vasudeva (Krishna) spoke these words of deep import and true morality.

sn: नावमानं कुलस्यास्य गुडाकेशः प्रयुक्तवान्। सम्मानोऽभ्यधिकस्तेन प्रयुक्तोऽयं न संशयः॥
en: Gudakesha (Arjuna) has not insulted our family by what he has done. There is no doubt he has enhanced our glory.

sn: अर्थलुब्धान् न वः पार्थो मन्यते सात्वतान् सदा। स्वयंवरमनाधृष्यं मन्यते चापि पाण्डवः॥
en: Partha knows that we are never mercenary. The Pandava (Arjuna) also regards Svyaimvara as doubtful in its results.

sn: प्रदानमपि कन्यायाः पशुवत् कोऽनुमन्यते। विक्रयं चाप्यपत्यस्य कः कुर्यात् पुरुषो भुवि॥
en: Who also would approved of accepting a bride in gift as if she were an animal? What man again is there on earth who would sell his offsprings?

sn: एतान् दोषांस्तु कौन्तेयो दृष्टवानिति मे मतिः। अतः प्रसह्य हृतवान् कन्यां धर्मेण पाण्डवः॥
en: I think the son of Kunti (Arjuna) saw these faults in all other methods, therefore the Pandava took the maiden away by force according to ordinance.

sn: उचितश्चैव सम्बन्धः सुभद्रां च यशस्विनीम्। एष चापीदृशः पार्थः प्रसह्य हृतवानिति॥
en: This alliance is very proper. Subhadra is an illustrious girl and so is Partha. Thinking all this, he has taken her away by force. a

sn: भरतस्यान्वये जातं शान्तनोश्च यशस्विनः। कुन्तिभोजात्मजापुत्रं को बुभूषेत नार्जुनम्॥
en: Who is there that would not desire to have Arjuna as a friend? He is born in the race of Bharata and the illustrious Shantanu and he is also the son of the daughter of Kuntibhoja.

sn: न च पश्यामि यः पार्थं विजयेत रणे बलात्। वर्जयित्वा विरूपाक्षं भगनेत्रहरं हरम्॥ अपि सर्वेषु लोकेषु सेन्द्ररुद्रेषु मारिष। स च नाम रथस्तादृङ्मदीयास्ते च वाजिनः॥ योद्धा पार्थश्च शीघ्रास्त्रः को नु तेन समो भवेत्। तमभिद्रुत्य सान्त्वेन परमेण धनंजयम्॥ न्यवर्तयत् संहृष्टा ममैषा परमा मतिः।
en: I do not see such a man in all the worlds, even with Indra and the Rudras, who can vanquish him in battle except the three eyed deity Shiva. His car is well known; my steeds are now yoked to it. Partha as a warrior is also well known and his lightness of hand too is well known. Who shall be equal to him? Go cheerfully to Dhananjaya; stop him by conciliation and bring him back. This is my opinion.

sn: यदि निर्जित्य वः पार्थो बलाद् गच्छेत् स्वकं पुरम्।।११ प्रणश्येद् वो यशः सद्यो न तु सान्त्वे पराजयः।
en: If Partha goes away to his city (Indraprastha) by defeating us, our fame will be destroyed. But there is no disgrace in conciliation.

sn: तच्छ्रुत्वा वासुदेवस्य तथा चक्रुर्जनाधिप॥
en: O king, having heard these words of Vasudeva, they did as he directed.

sn: निवृत्तश्चार्जुनस्तत्र विवाहं कृतवान् प्रभुः। उषित्वा तत्र कौन्तेयः संवत्सरपराः क्षपाः॥
en: Stopped by them, the lord Arjuna returned to Dvarka and he was then united with Subhadra in marriage.

sn: विहत्य च यथाकामं पूजितो वृष्णिनन्दनैः। पुष्करे तु ततः शेषं कालं वर्तितवान् प्रभुः॥ पूर्णे तु द्वादशे वर्षे खाण्डवप्रस्थमागतः।
en: Having worshipped by the Vrishnis, the son of Kunti remained for a year in Dvarka, sporting there at pleasure. The lord (Arjuna) passed the last portion of his excite at Pushkara. When twelve years were thus complete, he came back of Khandavaprastha.

sn: अभिगम्य च राजानं नियमेन समाहितः॥ अभ्यर्च्य ब्राह्मणान् पार्थो द्रौपदीमभिजग्मिवान्।
en: He went to Yudhishthira and worshipped him first; he then worshipped the Brahmanas and at last he went to Draupadi.

sn: तं द्रौपदी प्रत्युवाच प्रणयात् कुरुनन्दनम्॥ तत्रैव गच्छ कौन्तेय यत्र सा सात्वतात्मजा।
en: Draupadi, out of jealousy, thus spoke to that descendant of Kuru, Arjuna, “O son of Kunti, go there where the daughter of the Satvata race is.

sn: सुबद्धस्यापि भारस्य पूर्वबन्धः श्लथायते॥ तथा बहुविधं कृष्णां विलपन्ती धनंजयः सान्त्वयामास भूयश्च क्षमयामास चासकृत्॥ सुभद्रां त्वरमाणश्च रक्तकौशेयवासिनीम्। पार्थः प्रस्थापयामास कृत्वा गोपालिकावपुः॥ साधिकं तेन रूपेण शोभमाना यशस्विनी।
en: A second always relaxes the first one, however strong it might be.” Thus Krishna (Draupadi) lamented in various strains and Dhananjaya (Arjuna) comforted her, asking again and again her forgiveness. Coming to Subhadra attired in red silk, Partha sent her (into the inner apartments) dressed in the grab of a cow-herd women. The illustrious lady looked handsome even in that dress.

sn: भवनं श्रेष्ठमासाद्य वीरपत्नी वराङ्गना।॥ ववन्दे पृथुताम्राक्षी पृथां भद्रा यशस्विनी।
en: Arriving at that best of houses, that wife of a hero, the best of women, the illustrious Bhadra (Subhadra) of large and radish eyes worshipped Pritha.

sn: तां कुन्ती चारुसर्वाङ्गीमुपाजिघ्रत मूर्धनि॥ प्रीत्या परमया युक्ता आशीर्भिर्युञ्जतातुलाम्।
en: Out of excessive affection Kunti sinelt the head of that maiden of perfectly charming features and she then pronounced infinite blessings upon her.

sn: ततोऽभिगम्य त्वरिता पूर्णेन्दुसदृशानना॥ ववन्दे द्रौपदी भद्रा प्रेष्याहमिति चाब्रवीत्।
en: Then that damsel of the face like the full moon, Bhadra, soon went to Draupadi and worshipped her saying, "I am your maid."

sn: प्रत्युत्थाय तदा कृष्णा स्वसारं माधवस्य च॥ परिष्वज्यावदत् प्रीत्या निःसपत्नोऽस्तु ते पतिः।
en: Krishna hastily rose and embraced the sister of Madhava; and out of affection she then said, “Let you husband be without a rival."

sn: तथैव मुदिता भद्रा तामुवाचैवमस्त्विति॥ ततस्ते हृष्टमनसः पाण्डवेया महारथाः। कुन्ती च परमप्रीता बभूव जनमेजय॥ श्रुत्वा तु पुण्डरीकाक्षः सम्प्राप्तं स्वं पुरोत्तमम्। अर्जुनं पाण्डवश्रेष्ठमिन्द्रप्रस्थगतं तदा॥ आजगाम विशुद्धात्मा सह रामेण केशवः।
en: Bhadra then with a delightful heart said to her, “But it so." O Janamejaya, from that time, those great car-warriors the Pandavas, lived happily and Kunti also became vary happy. Having heard that the best of the Pandavas Arjuna, had reached that excellent city, Indraprastha, the lotus-eyed and pure-souled Keshava (Krishna) came there with Rama (Baladeva),

sn: वृष्ण्यन्धकमहामात्रैः सह वीरैर्महारथैः॥ भ्रातृभिश्च कुमारैश्च योधैश्च बहुभिर्वृतः।
en: And the other heroes and great carwarriors of the Vrishni and the Andhaka races and his brothers and sons and many other warriors.

sn: सैन्येन महता शौरिरभिगुप्तः परंतपः॥ तत्र दानपतिर्धीमानाजगाम महायशाः। अक्रूरो वृष्णिवीराणां सेनापतिररिंदमः॥ अनाधृष्टिर्महातेजा उद्धवश्च महायशाः।
en: That chastiser of foes, Shauri, came with a large army and there also came that chastiser of foes, that exceedingly liberal, greatly intelligent and illustrious commander-in-chief of the Vrishni heroes, Akrura. (There also came) the greatly illustrious Uddhava.

sn: साक्षाद् बृहस्पतेः शिष्यो महाबुद्धिर्महामनाः॥ सत्यकः सात्यकिश्चैव कृतवर्मा च सात्वतः।
en: Who was a man of great soul and great intelligence, like a disciple of Brihaspati himself. (There also came) Satyaka and Satyaki and Kritavarmana and Satvata,

sn: प्रद्युम्नश्चैव साम्बश्च निशद्दः शरुरेव च॥ चारुदेष्णश्च विक्रान्तो झिल्ली विपृथुरेव च। सारणश्च महाबाहुर्गदश्च विदुषां वरः॥
en: Pradyumna, Samba, Nishatha and Shanku, Chandrasena, the greatly powerful Jhilli, Vipritha, the mighty armed Sarana the foremost of all learned men Gada.

sn: एते चान्ये च बहवो वृष्णिभोजान्धकास्तथा। आजग्मुः खाण्डवप्रस्थमादाय हरणं बहु॥
en: These and many other Vrishni, Bhojas and Andhakas came to Indraprastha, bringing with them many bridal presents.

sn: ततो युधिष्ठिरो राजा श्रुत्वा माधवमागतम्। प्रतिग्रहार्थं कृष्णस्य यमौ प्रास्थापयत् तदा॥
en: Hearing that Madhava (Krishna) had come, the king Yudhishthira sent the twins (Nakula and Sahadeva) to receive him.

sn: ताभ्यां प्रतिगृहीतं तु वृष्णिचक्रं महर्द्धिमत्। विवेश खाण्डवप्रस्थं पताकाध्वजशोभितम्॥
en: Having been welcomed by them, the Vrishni heroes of great prosperity entered Khandavaprastha which was well-adorned with flags and standards.

sn: सम्मृष्टसिक्तपन्थानं पुष्पप्रकरशोभितम्। चन्दनस्य रसैः शीतैः पुण्यगन्धैनिषेवितम्॥
en: The street were well-swept and waters; they were adorned with floral wreathes and bunches, sprinkled over with cooling and fragrant Sandal-wood-water.

sn: दह्यतागुरुणा चैव देशे देशे सुगन्धिना। हृष्टपुष्टजनाकीर्णं वणिम्भिरुपशोभितम्॥
en: Every part of the town was full of the sweet scent of burning aloes. The whole city was full of happy and healthy people and adorned with traders and merchants.

sn: प्रतिपेदे महाबाहुः सह रामेण केशवः। वृष्ण्यन्धकैस्तथा भोजैः समेतः पुरुषोत्तमः॥ सम्पूज्यमानः पौरेश्च ब्राह्मणैश्च सहस्रशः। विवेश भवनं राज्ञः पुरन्दरगृहोपमम्॥
en: That best of men, the mighty-armed Keshava (Krishna) with Rama and many of the Vrishni, Bhoja and Andhaka races entered the town and was worshipped by thousands of citizens and Brahmanas. He then entered the king's palace which was like the palace of Indra hiinself.

sn: युधिष्ठिरस्तु रामेण समागच्छद् यथाविधि। मूर्षि केशवमाघ्राय बाहुभ्यां परिषस्वजे॥
en: Yudhishthira received Rama with all due ceremonies and the king embraced Keshava with both his arms ad smelt his head.

sn: तं प्रीयमाणो गोविन्दो विनयेनाभिपूजयन्। भीमं च पुरुषव्याघ्रं विधिवत् प्रत्यपूजयत्॥
en: Being much pleased with the reception, Govinda (Krishna) worshipped him (Yudhishthira) with all humility. He duly worshipped that best of men Bhima.

sn: तांश्च वृष्ण्यन्धक श्रेष्ठान् कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः। प्रतिजग्राह सत्कारैर्यथाविधि यथागतम्॥
en: The son of Kunti, Yudhishthira, then welcomed with all due ceremonies all the other chief men of the Vrishni and the Andhaka races.

sn: गुरुवत् पूजयामास कांश्चित् कांश्चिद् वयस्यवत्। कांश्चिदभ्यवदत् प्रेम्णा कैश्चिदप्यभिवादितः॥
en: He worshipped some as his superiors, he welcomed others as his equals; he received some with affection and he worshipped others with reverence.

sn: तेषां ददौ हृषीकेशो जन्यार्थे धनमुत्तमम्। हरणं वै सुभद्राया ज्ञातिदेयं महायशाः॥
en: Then the illustrious Hrishikesha (Krishna) gave much wealth to the bridge groom's party. He gave to the illustrious Subhadra all the bridal presents given to her by her relatives.

sn: रथानां काञ्चनाङ्गानां किरूिणीजालमालिनाम्। चतुर्युजामुपेतानां सूतैः कुशलशिक्षितैः॥
en: (He gave the Pandavas) one thousand golden cars adorned with rows of bells, to each of which were yoked four steeds driven by well-trained charioteers.

sn: सहस्रं प्रददौ कृष्णो गवामयुतमेव च। श्रीमान् माधुर देश्यानां दोग्ध्रीणां पुण्यवर्चसाम्॥
en: Ten thousand well complexioned kine, belonging to the country of Mathura and yielding much milk were also presented (o the Pandavas) by Krishna.

sn: वडवानां च शुद्धानां चन्द्रांशुसमवर्चसाम्। ददौ जनार्दनः प्रीत्या सहस्रं हेमभूषितम्॥
en: Being very much pleased, Janardana (Krishna) gave them one thousand moon-like with golden harnesses.

sn: तथैवाश्वतरीणां च दान्तानां वातरंहसाम्। शतान्यञ्जनकेशीनां श्वेतानां पञ्च पञ्च च॥
en: (He also gave them) one thousand mules of white colour with black manes, all possessing the speed of wind and all well trained.

sn: स्नानपानोत्सवे चैव प्रयुक्तं वयसान्वितम्। स्त्रीणां सहस्रं गौरीणां सुवेषाणां सुवर्चसाम्॥ सुवर्णशतकण्द्दीनामरोमाणां स्वलंकृताम्। परिचर्यासु दक्षाणां प्रददौ पुष्करेक्षणः॥
en: (He gave them also) one thousand of skin perfectly polished, all young and virgin, all well-attired and of excellent complexion, each wearing one hundred pieces of gold round her neck, adorned with all ornaments and wellskilled in saving at bath and at drink and in every kind of service.

sn: पृष्ठ्यनामपि चाश्वानां बालिकानां जनार्दनः। ददौ शतसहस्राख्यं कन्याधनमुत्तमम्॥
en: Janardana (Krishna) also gave them as an excellent dowry of the bride, hundreds of thousands of horses, brought from the country of Balhikas.

sn: कृताकृतस्य मुख्यस्य कनकस्याग्निवर्चसः। मनुष्यभारान् दाशार्हो ददौ दश जनार्दनः॥
en: Janardana gave her (Subhadra) as her dowry ten loads of first class gold, possessing the splendour of fire; some portions of were purified and some portions in original state.

sn: गजानां तु प्रभिन्नानां त्रिधा प्रस्रवतां मदम्। गिरिकूटनिकाशानां समरेष्वनिवर्तिनाम्॥ क्लृप्तानां पटुघण्टानां चारूणां हेममालिनाम्। हस्त्यारोहैरुपेतानां सहस्रं साहसप्रियः॥ रामः पाणिग्रहणिकं ददौ पार्थाय लागली। प्रीयमाणो हलधरः सम्बन्धं प्रतिमानयन्॥ स महाधनरत्नौघौ वस्त्रकम्बलफेनवान्। महागजमहाग्राहः पताकाशैवलाकुलः॥
en: The wielder of plough his weapon, the lover of heroism, Rama, gave Partha as his nuptial present one thousand elephants with secretions flowing in three streams from the thrce parts of their bodies, each as large as a mountain., each irresistible in battle, each decked with coverlets. Well adorned with everringing bells and other golden ornaments and cach equipped with excellent haudhas on its back. The large number of gems and the large quantity of wealth presented by the Yadavas looked like a sea, of which the cloths and blankets were the foams, the elephants were the alligators and sharks and the flags the floating weeds.

sn: पाण्डुसागरमाविद्धः प्रविवेश महाधनः। पूर्णमापूरयंस्तेषां द्विषच्छोकावहोऽभवत्॥ प्रतिजग्राह तत् सर्वं धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः। पूजयामास तांश्चैव वृष्ण्यन्धकमहारथान्॥
en: The sea, thus swelling into large proportions, mingled with the ocean of wealth of the Pandavas. It was filled to the brim to the great sorrow of all their foes. Dharmaraja Yudhishthira accepted all these presents and worshipped all those great warriors of the Vrishni and Andhaka raccs.

sn: ते समेता महात्मानः कुरुवृष्ण्यन्धकोत्तमाः। विजह्वरमरावासे नराः सुकृतिनो यथा॥
en: Those illustrious of the Kuru, Vrishni and Andhaka races passed their time all in merriment and in pleasure, as do the virtuous inen in heaven (after their death).

sn: तत्र तत्र महानादैरुत्कृष्टतलनादितैः। यथायोगं यथाप्रीति विजह्वः कुरुवृष्णयः॥
en: The Kurus and the Vrishnis sported there with joyous hearts, often shouting and clapping their hands.

sn: एवमुत्तमवीर्यास्ते विहृत्य दिवसान् बहून्। पूजिताः कुरुभिर्जग्मुः पुनरवती प्रति॥
en: Thus passing many days in pleasure and worshipped and entertained by the Kurus, the greatly effulgent Vrishni heroes then returned to the city of Dvaravati.

sn: राम पुरस्कृत्य ययुर्वृष्ण्यन्धकमहारथाः। रत्नान्यादाय शुभ्राणि दत्तानि कुरुसत्तमैः॥
en: The great warriors of the Vrishni and the Andhaka races, placing Rama at their head and carrying with them all those brilliant gems presented to them by the excellent Kuru, set out (for their own city).

sn: वासुदेवस्तु पार्थेन तत्रैव सह भारत। उवास नगरे रम्ये शक्रप्रस्थे महात्मना॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, the high-souled Vasudeva (Krishna however) remained with Arjuna in the charming city of Indraprastha.

sn: व्यचरद् यमुनातीरे मृगयां स महायशाः। मृगान् विध्यन् वराहांश्च रेमे सार्धं किरीटिना॥
en: That greatly illustrious hero roamed along the banks of Yamuna in search of deer. he sported and hunted with Kiriti (Arjuna), piercing deer and wild boars with his arrows.

sn: ततः सुभद्रा सौभद्रं केशवस्य प्रिया स्वसा। जयन्तमिव पौलोमी ख्यातिमन्तमजीजनत्॥
en: Then Subhadra, the beloved sister of Krishna, gave birth to an illustrious son, like Pauloma's daughter (Sachi) giving birth to Jayanta (son of Indra).

sn: दीर्घबाहुं महोरस्कं वृषभाक्षमरिंदमम्। सुभद्रा सुषुवे वीरमभिमन्युं नरर्षभम्॥
en: He was of long arms, broad chest and bulllike eyes; that chastiser of focs, that best of men, that hero, the son of Subhadra, was named Abhimanyu.

sn: अभिश्च मन्युमांश्चैव ततस्तमरिमर्दनम्। अभिमन्युमिति प्राहुरार्जुनि पुरुषर्षभम्॥
en: That best of the Bharata race, that chastiser of foes, that son of Arjuna, was called Abhimanyu, because he was fearless and wrathful.

sn: स सात्वत्यामतिरथः सम्बभूव धनंजयात्। मखे निर्मथनेनेव शमीगर्भाद्भुतासनः॥
en: That great hero was begotten by Dhananjaya on the maiden of the Satvata race, like fire produced by rubbing in a sacrifice from within the Sami wood.

sn: यस्मिञ्जाते महातेजाः कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः। अयुतं गा द्विजातिभ्यः प्रादान्निष्कांश्च भारत॥
en: O descendant of Bharata on the birth of this child the powerful son of Kunti, Yudhishthira, gave away to the Brahmanas ten thousand kine and many thousand gold coins.

sn: दयितो वासुदेवस्य बाल्यात् प्रभृति चाभवत्। पितृणामिव सर्वेषां प्रजानामिव चन्द्रमाः॥
en: The child became a favourite of Vasudeva from his earliest years and of his father and uncles. He shone like the moon become and the favourite of all the people.

sn: जन्मप्रभृति कृष्णाश्च चक्रे तस्य क्रियाः शुभाः। स चापि ववृधे बालः शुक्लपक्षे यथा शशी॥
en: Krishna performed all the usual rites of infancy on his birth. The child began to grow up like the moon in the white fortnight.

sn: चतुष्पादं दशविधं धनुर्वेदमरिंदमः। अर्जुनाद् वेद वेदज्ञः सकलं दिव्यमानुषम्॥
en: That chastiser of foes learnt from Arjuna the science of arms with its four branches and ten divisions, both human and celestials; and he also became in the Vedas.

sn: विज्ञानेष्वपि चास्त्राणां सौष्ठवे च महाबलः। क्रियास्वपि च सर्वासु विशेषानभ्यशिक्षयत्॥ आगमे च प्रयोगे च चक्रे तुल्यमिवात्मना। तुतोष पुत्रं सौभद्रं प्रेक्षमाणो धनंजयः॥
en: That powerful boy (Abhimanyu) became equal to his father in counteracting the weapons hurled upon him, in great lightness of hands, in fleetness of inotion, forward and backward and in traversing and wheeling. Seeing his son, the son of Subhadra, (so skillful in arms), Dhananjaya became exceedingly happy.

sn: सर्वसंहननोपेतं सर्वलक्षणलक्षितम्। दुर्धर्षमृषभस्कन्धं व्यात्ताननमिवोरगम्॥
en: He possessed the power of crushing all his enemies-he had every auspicious mark on his body; he was invincible in battle and as broad shouldered as a bull; he had a face like that of a snake,

sn: सिंहदष महेष्वासं मत्तमातङ्गविक्रमम्। मेघदुन्दुभिनिर्घोषं पूर्णचन्द्रनिभाननम्॥
en: He was as proud as the lion, he was a great powerful as a mad elephant. His voice was like that of the roars of clouds and his face was like that of the full moon.

sn: कृष्णस्य सदृशं शौर्ये वीर्य रूपे तथाऽकृतौ। ददर्श पुत्रं बीभत्सुर्मघवानिव तं यथा॥
en: He was equal to Krishna in bravery, in energy, in beauty and in features. Vivatsu (Arjuna) saw his son as if he was Maghavata himself.

sn: पाञ्चाल्यपि तु पञ्चभ्यः पतिभ्यः शुभलक्षणा। लेभे पञ्च सुतान् वीराश्रेष्ठान् पञ्चाचलानिव॥
en: The auspicious Panchala princess also obtained five heroic, excellent and mountainsons from the five Pandavas.

sn: युधिष्ठिरात् प्रतिविन्ध्यं सुतसोमं वृकोदरात्। अर्जुनाच्छुतकर्माणं शतानीकं च नाकुलिम्॥ सहदेवाच्छ्रुतसेनमेतान् पञ्च महारथान्। पाञ्चाली सुषुवे वीरानादित्यानदितिर्यथा॥
en: Prativindhya begotten by Yudhishthira, Sutasoma by Vrikodara, Shrutakarmana by Arjuna, Shatanika by Nakula and Shrutasena by Sahadeva; they were all great car-warriors. The Panchala princess gave birth to these five heroes, as Aditi gave birth to the Adityas.

sn: शास्त्रतः प्रतिविन्ध्यं तमूचुर्विप्रा युधिष्ठिरम्। परप्रहरणज्ञाने प्रतिविध्यो भवत्वयम्॥
en: The Brahmanas from their for-knowledge said to Yudhishthira, that because that son of his would be capable of bring like the Vindhya mountains the weapons of the foe, he should be called Prativindhyas. was

sn: सुते सोमसहस्रे तु सोमार्कसमतेजसम्। सुतसोमं महेष्वासं सुषुवे भीमसेनतः॥
en: Because the child that Draupadi bore to Bhimsena was born after Bhima had performed one thousand Soma sacrifices, he should be called the great bow-man Sutasoma.

sn: श्रुतं कर्म महत् कृत्वा निवृत्तेन किरीटिना। जातः पुत्रस्तथेत्येवं श्रुतकर्मा ततोऽभवत्॥
en: Because Arjuna's son was born on his relurn from exile during which he had achieved many celebrated feats, that child came to be called Shrutakarma.

sn: शतानीकस्य राजर्षेः कौरव्यस्य महात्मनः। चक्रे पुत्रं सनामानं नकुलः कीर्तिवर्धनम्॥
en: Nakula's son was named Shatanika after a royal sage of that name in the illustrious race of Kuru.

sn: ततस्त्वजजनत् कृष्णा नक्षत्रे वह्निदैवते। सहदेवात् सुतं तस्माच्छ्रुतसेनेति यं विदुः॥
en: And because the son, Draupadi bore to Sahadeva, was born under the constellation, called Vahni Daivata, therefore he was called after the commander-in-chief of the celestials ariny, Shrutasena.

sn: एकवर्षान्तरास्वेते द्रौपदेया यशस्विनः। अन्वजायन्त राजेन्द्र परस्परहितैषिणः॥
en: The sons of Draupadi were all born each at the interval of year. all of them became renowned and was much attached to one another.

sn: जातकर्माण्यानुपूर्व्याच्चूडोपनयनानि च। चकार विधिवद् धौम्यस्तेषां भरतसत्तम॥
en: O king, all their rites of infancy and childhood according to the ordinance, such as Chudakarana and Upanayana, were duly performed by Dhaumya.

sn: कृत्वा च वेदाध्ययनं ततः सुचरितव्रताः। जगृहुः सर्वमिष्वस्त्रमर्जुनाद् दिव्यमानुषम्॥
en: After having studied the Vedas, those princes of excellent behaviour and vow learnt from Arjuna the use of all the weapons, both celestials and human.

sn: दिव्यगर्भोपमैः पुत्रैयूंढोरस्कैर्महारथैः। अन्वितो राजशार्दूल पाण्डवा मुदमाप्नुवन्॥
en: O best of kings, having obtained sons, all of whom were celestials, all of whom possessed broad chests and all whom became great warriors, the Pandavas became exceedingly happy.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच इन्द्रप्रस्थे वसन्तस्ते जघ्नुरन्यान् नराधिपान्। शासनाद् धृराष्ट्रस्य राज्ञः शान्तनवस्य च॥
en: Vaishampayana said : When at the command of the king, Dhritarashtra and the son of Shantanu, (Bhishma), the Pandavas had taken up their abode at Indraprastha, they brought under their sway many other kings and monarchs.

sn: आश्रित्य धर्मराजानं सर्वलोकोऽवसत् सुखम्। पुण्यलक्षणकर्माणं स्वदेहमिव देहिनः॥
en: As a soul lives happily depending on the body blessed with auspicious marks and pious deeds, so all the subjects lived most happily, depending on Dharmaraja (Yudhishthira).

sn: स समं धर्मकामार्थान् सिषेवे भरतर्षभ। त्रीनिवात्मसमान् बन्धून नीतिमानिव मानयन्॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, he (Yudhishthira) served equally Dharma, Artha and Kama, as if each of them was a friend as dear to him as his own soul.

sn: तेषां समविभक्तानां क्षितौ देहवतामिव। बभौ धर्मार्थकामानां चतुर्थ इव पार्थिवः॥
en: It appeared as if the three pursuits, Dharma, Artha and Kama, became personified on earth; and with them the king shined as the fourth (pursuit).

sn: अध्येतारं परं वेदान् प्रयोक्तारं महाध्वरे। रक्षितारं शुभाँल्लोकान् लेभिरे तं जनाधिपम्॥
en: Having obtained him as their king, they obtained a monarch who was devoted to the study of the Vedas, who was a performer of great sacrifices and who was the protector of all good works.

sn: अधिष्ठानवती लक्ष्मीः परायणवती मतिः। वर्धमानोऽखिलो धर्मस्तेनासीत् पृथिवीक्षिताम्॥
en: (During his reign) Lakshmi became stationary and hearts became devoted to the Supreme Spirit. Virtue itself began to grow all over the world.

sn: भ्रातृभिः सहितो राजा चतुर्भिराधिकं बभौ। प्रयुज्यमानैर्विततो वेदैरिव महाध्वरः॥
en: Surrounded by his four brothers the king looked as resplendent as a great sacrifice depending upon and assisted by the four Vedas.

sn: तं तु धौम्यादयो विप्राः परिवार्योपतस्थिरे। बृहस्पतीसमा मुख्याः प्रजापतिमिवामराः॥
en: Many learned Brahmanas with Dhaumya at their head, each equal to Brihaspati, waited upon the king, as the celestial wait upon the Lord of creation.

sn: धर्मराजे ह्यतिप्रीत्या पूर्णचन्द्र इवामले। प्रजानां रेमिरे तुल्यं नेत्राणि हृदयानि च॥
en: On account of the excessive affection of the people, both their hearts and eyes equally took great delight in Dharmaraja (Yudhishthira) who was like a full moon without a stain.

sn: न त केवलदैवेन प्रजा भावेन रेमिरे। यद् बभूव मन:कान्तं कर्मणा स चकार तत्॥
en: The people took delight in him, not only because he was their king, but because they bore for him a great affection. The king also did not was agreeable to them.

sn: न ह्ययुक्तं न चासत्यं नासह्यं न च वाप्रियम्। भाषितं चारुभाषस्य जज्ञे पार्थस्य धीमतः॥
en: The sweet-speeched and greatly intelligent son of Pritha (Yudhishthira) never uttered any was improper, or untrue unbearable or disagreeable.

sn: स हि सर्वस्य लोकस्य हितमात्मन एव च। चिकीर्षन् सुमहातेजा रेमे भरतसत्तम।॥
en: or That greatly powerful and best king of the Varata race happily passed his days in seeking the good of every body, as if every one was his own self.

sn: तथा तु मुदिताः सर्वे पाण्डवा विगतज्वराः। अवसन् पृथिवीपालांस्तापयन्तः स्वतेजसा॥
en: (His brothers) the Pandavas brought by their great powers many kings under their sway; they passed their days in happiness, having nothing to disturb their peace.

sn: ततः कतिपयाहस्य बीभत्सुः कृष्णमब्रवीत्। उष्णानि कृष्ण वर्तन्तं गच्छावो यमुनां प्रति॥
en: After a few days, Vivatsu (Arjuna) thus spoke to Krishna, “O Krishna, the summer is come, let us go to the Yamuna.

sn: सुहृज्जनवृतौ तत्र विहृत्य मधुसूदन। सायाह्ने पुनरेष्यावो रोचतां ते जनार्दना॥
en: O Janardana, O slayer of Madhu, if you like, let us sport their with out friends and then return in the evening.

sn: वासुदेव उवाच कुन्तीमातर्ममाप्येतद् रोचते यद् वयं जले। सुहज रनवृतः पार्थ विहरेम यथासुखम्॥
en: Krishna said : O son of Kunti, this is also my wish. O Partha, let us sport with our friends in the waters( of the Yamuna).

sn: वैशंपायन उवाच आमन्त्र्य तौ धर्मराजमनुज्ञाष्य च भारत। जग्मतुः पार्थगोविन्दौ सुहृज्जनवृतौ ततः॥
en: Vaishampayana said: O descendant of Bharata, having consulted with each other and after receiving Yudhishthira's permission, Partha (Arjuna) and Govinda (Krishna) in company with their friends set out (for the Yamuna).

sn: विहारदेशं सम्प्राप्य नानाद्रुममनुत्तमम्। गृहैरुच्चावचैयुक्तं पुरन्दरपुरोपमम्॥ भक्ष्यैर्भोज्यैश्च पेयैश्च रसवद्भिर्महाधनैः। माल्यैश्च विविधैर्गधैर्युक्तं वार्ष्णेयपार्थयोः॥ विवेशान्तःपुरं तूर्णं रत्नैरुच्चावचैः शुभैः। यथोपजोषं सर्वश्च जनश्चिनीड भारत॥
en: And arrived at a charming spot, fitted for the purpose of pleasure, overgrown with numerous tall trees and adorned with high mansions and looking like the city of Indra. O descendant of Bharata, in these houses were collected for the descendants of Vrishni and Pritha (Arjuna and Krishna) numerous wellflavoured and costly viands, drinks and other articles of enjoyments and floral wreathes and various perfumes. The party soon entered the inner apartments (of the house), adorned with many precious gems of pure brilliancy. Entering these apartments, every one of them began to sport at his pleasure.

sn: स्त्रियश्च विपुलश्रोण्यश्चारुपीनपयोधराः। मदस्खलितगामिन्यश्चिक्रीडुर्वामलोचनाः॥
en: The women with beautiful full hips and rising breasts with handsome eyes and unsteady gait for drink began to sport.

sn: वने काश्चिज्जले काश्चित् काश्चिद् वेश्मनु चाङ्गनाः। यथायोग्यं यथाप्रीति चिक्रीडुः पार्थकृष्णयोः॥
en: Some sported at their pleasure in the woods, some in the waters and some within the houses as directed and commanded by Krishna and Partha (Arjuna).

sn: द्रौपदी च सुभद्रा च वासांस्याभरणानि च। प्रायच्छतां महाराज ते तु तस्मिन् मदोत्कटे॥
en: O king, Draupadi and Subhadra, exhilarated with wine, gave away costly robes and ornaments to the women that were sporting there.

sn: काश्चित् प्रहृष्टा ननृतुश्चक्रुशुश्च तथापराः। जगुश्चान्या वरस्त्रियः॥
en: Some amongst them danced in joy and some began to sing; some laughed and jested and some drank excellent wines.

sn: रुरुधुश्चापरास्तत्र प्रजघ्नुश्च परस्परम्। मन्त्रयामासुरन्याश्च रहस्यानि परस्परम्॥
en: Some obstructed one another's progress, some fought with one another and some again talked with one another in private and some cut jokes at one another.

sn: जहसुश्च परा नार्यो वेणुवीणामृदङ्गानां मनोज्ञानां च सर्वशः। शब्देन पूर्यते हh तद् वनं सुमहर्द्धिमत्॥
en: Those woods, filled with the charming music of the flute, guitars and drums, became the scene of prosperity itself.

sn: तस्मिंस्तदा वर्तमाने कुरुदाशार्हनन्दनौ। समीपं जग्मतुः कंचिदुद्देशं सुमनोहरम्॥
en: When such was the state of things there, the descendants of Kuru and Dasharha (Krishna and Arjuna) went to a certain charming spot near by.

sn: तत्र गत्वा महात्मानौ कृष्णौ परपुरंजयौ। महार्हासनयो राजंस्ततस्तौ संनिषीदतुः॥
en: O king, after having gone there, the two illustrious Krishna, the two subjugators of the hostile cities, (Krishna and Arjuna) sat themselves down on two very costly seats.

sn: तत्र पूर्वव्यतीतानि विक्रान्तानीतराणि च। बहूनि कथयित्वा तौ रेमाते पार्थमाधवौ॥
en: Partha and Madhava amused themselves there by talking over their past achievements and discoursing on heroism and various other topics.

sn: तत्रोपविष्टौ मुदितौ नाकपृष्ठेऽश्विनाविव। अभ्यागच्छत् तदा विप्रो वासुदेवधनंजयौ॥
en: When Vasudeva and Dhananjaya were thus happily sitting together (in that charming spot), like the twin Ashvinis in heaven, a certain Brahmanas came to them.

sn: बृहच्छालप्रतीकाशः प्रतप्तकनकप्रभः। हरिपिङ्गोज्जवलश्मश्रुः प्रमाणायामतः समः॥
en: He looked like an old Shala tree, his complexion was like that of heated gold, his beard with bright yellow tinged with green, the height and thickness of his body were in just proportion.

sn: तरुणादित्यसंकाशश्चीरवासा जटाधरः। पद्मपत्राननः पिङ्गस्तेजसा प्रज्वलन्निव॥
en: He had matted locks, he was attired in rags, he was as effulgent as the morning sun, his eyes were like lotus-leaves, his colour was tawny and he appeared to be blazing in splendour.

sn: उपसृष्टं तु तं कृष्णौ भ्राजमानं द्विजोत्तमम्। अर्जुनो वासुदेवश्च तूर्णमुत्पत्य तस्थतुः॥
en: Seeing that foremost of Brahmanas blazing with splendour coming towards them, Arjuna and Vasudeva hastily rose up and stood waiting (to receive command).

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच सोऽब्रवीदर्जुनं चैव वासुदेवं च सात्वतम्। लोकप्रवीरौ तिष्ठन्तौ खाण्डवस्य समीपतः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Thereupon that Brahmana thus spoke to Arjuna and Vasudeva of Satvata race," You two, who are now staying so near the Khandava, are two foremost of men.

sn: ब्राह्मणो बहुभोक्तास्मि भुञ्जेऽपरिमितं सदा। भिक्षे वार्ष्णेयपार्थो वामेकां तृप्तिं प्रयच्छतम्॥
en: I am a voracious Brahmana that eats much. o descendants of Vrishni and Pritha, I ask you to gratify me by giving me sufficient foot.”

sn: एवमुक्तौ तमब्रूतां ततस्तौ कृष्णपाण्डवौ। केनान्नेन भवांस्तृप्येत् तस्यान्नस्य यतावहे॥
en: Having been thus addressed, Krishna and the Pandava (Arjuna) thus spoke to him, “ Tell us what food will gratify you. We shall try to give it to you."

sn: एवमुक्तः स भगवानब्रवीत् तावुभौ ततः। भाषमाणौ तदा वीरौ किमन्नं क्रियतामिति॥
en: Having been thus addressed, the illustrious Brahmana thus spoke to those two heroes who were enquiries what kind of food he wanted.

sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच नाहमन्नं बुभुक्षे वै पावकं मां निबोधतम्। यदन्नमनुरूपं मे तद् युवां सम्प्रयच्छतम्॥
en: The Brahmana said ; I do not wish to eat ordinary food. Know that I am Agni (fire). Give me that food which suits me.

sn: इदमिन्द्रः सदा दावं खाण्डवं परिरक्षति। न च शक्रोम्यहं दग्धुं रक्ष्यमाणं महात्मना॥
en: This Khandava (forest) is every protected by Indra. I always fail to consume it, because it is ever protected by that illustrious god.

sn: वसत्यत्र सखा तस्य तक्षकः पन्नगः सदा। सगणस्तत्कृते दावं परिरक्षति वज्रभृत्॥
en: There lives in this forest) his friend the Naga Takshaka with his relatives and followers. It is for him that the wilder of thunder (Indra) protects it.

sn: तत्र भूतान्यनेकानि रक्षतेऽस्य प्रसङ्गतः। तं दिधक्षुर्न शक्नोमि दग्धुं शक्रस्य तेजसा॥
en: Many other creatures are also protected by him (in this forest) for the sake of Takshaka. Although I am ever desirous of consuming it, I cannot do it for Indra's prowess.

sn: स मां प्रज्वलितं दृष्ट्वा मेघाम्भोभिः प्रवर्षति। ततो दग्धुं न शक्नोमि दिधक्षुर्दावमीप्सिताम्॥
en: Whenever he sees me blazing up in this forest), he pours upon me waters from the clouds. I cannot thus succeed to consume it, though very much desirous of doing it.

sn: स युवाभ्यां सहायाभ्यामस्त्रविद्भ्यां समागतः। दहेयं खाण्डवं दावमेतदन्नं वृतं मया॥
en: I have now come to you, you are both great experts in arms. I shall be able to consume Khandava with your help. This is the food I desire to have from you.

sn: युवां ह्यदकधारास्ता भूतानि च समन्ततः। उत्तमास्त्रविदौ सम्यक् सर्वतो वारयिष्यथः॥
en: Expert as you are in excellent weapons, I pray you to prevent the showers of rain from coming down upon me and to prevent also any creatures from escaping when I begin to consume it (the forest).

sn: जनमेजय उवाच किमर्थं भगवानग्निः खाण्डवं दग्धुमिच्छति। रक्ष्यमाणं महेन्द्रेण नानासत्त्वसमायुतम्॥
en: Janamejaya said : Why did the high-souled Agni desire to consume the forest of Khandava, abounding in various living creatures and protected by Indra?

sn: न ह्येतत् कारणं ब्रह्मन्नल्पं सम्प्रतिभाति मे। यद् ददाह सुसंक्रुद्धः खाण्डवं हव्यवाहनः॥ एतद् विस्तरशो ब्रह्मञ्छ्रोतुमिच्छामि तत्त्वतः। खाण्डवस्य पुरा दाहो यथा समभवन्मुने॥
en: When Agni consumed the Khandava in wrath, there was certainly a grave cause for it. I desire to hear from you all this in detail. O Rishi, tell me why the Khandava (forest) was consumed (by fire) in the days of yore.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच शृणु मे ब्रुवतो राजन् सर्वमेतद् यथातथम्। यनिमित्तं ददाहाग्निः खाण्डवं पृथिवीपते॥
en: O king, hear I am telling you the whole story of why Khandava forest was consumed by the fire.

sn: हन्त ते कथयिष्यामि पौराणीमृषिसंस्तुताम्। कथामिमां नरश्रेष्ठ खाण्डवस्य विनाशिनीम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : O best of men, I shall narrate to you the story of the destruction of the Khandavas as told by the Rishis in the Puranas.

sn: पौराणः श्रूयते राजन् राजा हरिहयोपमः। श्वेतकिर्नाम विख्यातो बलविक्रमसंयुतः॥
en: O king, it has been heard in the Puranas that there was a king named Shvetaki who was endued with both strength and prowess and who was a rival to Indra himself.

sn: यज्वा दानपतिर्थीमान् यथा नान्योऽस्ति कञ्चन। ईजे च स महायज्ञैः क्रतुभिश्चाप्तदक्षिणैः॥
en: None has equalled him in sacrifices, charity and intelligence. He performed five great sacrifices and many other smaller ones, in all of which Dakshinas (presents to Brahmanas) were very large.

sn: तस्य नान्याभवद् बुद्धिर्दिवसे दिवसे नृप। सत्रे क्रियासमारम्भे दानेषु विविधेषु च॥ ऋत्विग्भिः सहितो धीमानेवमीजे स भूमिपः। ततस्तु ऋत्विजश्चास्य धूमव्याकुललोचनाः॥ कालेन महता खिन्नास्तत्यजुस्ते नराधिपम्। ततः प्रचोदयामास ऋत्विजस्तान् महीपतिः॥ चक्षुर्विकलतां प्राप्ता न प्रपेदुश्च ते क्रतुम्।
en: O king, the heart of that monarch was always set upon sacrifices, religious rites and gifts of all kind. That greatly intelligent king performed sacrifices for many years, assisted by the Ritvijas till they, becoming weak and their eyes afflicted with smoke, left that king, wishing never more to assist him at his sacrifices. The king, however, again and again asked them to come to him, but on account of their sore eyes, they did not come.

sn: ततस्तेषामनुमते तद् विप्रैस्तु नराधिपः॥ सत्रं समापयामास ऋत्विग्भिपरैः सह।
en: Thereupon the king with the permission of the Ritvijas completed his sacrifices with the assistance of other Ritvijas.

sn: तस्यैवं वर्तमानस्य कदाचित् कालपयये॥ सत्रमाहर्तुकामस्य सवंत्सरशतं किल। ऋत्विजो नाभ्यपद्यन्त समाहर्तुं महात्मनः॥
en: Some days after, he desired to perform another sacrifice which would extend for one hundred years. But the illustrious king did not get any Ritvijas.

sn: स च राजाकरोद् यत्नं महान्तं ससुहृज्जनः। प्रणिपातेन सान्त्वेन दानेन च महायशाः॥ ऋत्विजोऽनुनयामास भूयो भूयस्त्वतन्द्रितः। ते चास्य तमभिप्रायं न चक्रुरमितौजसः॥
en: They high-souled king with his friends and relatives again and again courted them by bowing down to them, by conciliatory speeches and by the gifts of wealth. But they refused to accomplish the purpose of that greatly effulgent (king).

sn: स चाश्रमस्थान् राजर्षिस्तानुवाच रुषान्वितः। यद्यहं पतितो विप्राः शुश्रूषायां न च स्थितः॥ आशु त्याज्योऽस्मि युष्माभिर्ब्राह्मणैश्च जुगुप्सितः। तन्नार्हथ क्रतुश्रद्धां व्याघातयितुमद्य ताम्॥
en: Thereupon that royal sage thus spoke to them in anger, sitting in their own hermitage, “O Brahmanas, if I were a fallen person, if I were in wanting in service to you, I should then deserve to be abandoned by you and other Brahmanas.

sn: अस्थाने वा परित्यागं कर्तुं मे द्विजसत्तमाः। प्रपन्न एव वो विप्राः प्रसादं कर्तुमर्हथ॥ सान्त्वदानादिभिर्वाक्येस्तत्त्वतः कार्यवत्तया। प्रसादयित्वा वक्ष्यामि यन्नः कार्यं द्विजोत्तमाः॥ अथवाहं परित्यक्तो भवद्भिदे॒षकारणात्। ऋत्विजोऽन्यान् गमिष्यामि याजनार्थं द्विजोत्तमाः॥
en: O excellent Brahmanas, as I am neither degraded, nor wanting in homage to you, you should not obstruct sacrifice performed by me and abandon me thus without sufficient reason. O Brahmanas, I seek your protection, you should be propitious to me. () excellent Brahmanas, if you abandon me from enmity alone, I shall go to other Brahmanas and I shall ask for their assistance at my sacrifice. Conciliating them with sweet words and speeches, I shall tell them what is my business to be done so that they may accomplish it."

sn: एतावदुक्त्वा वचनं विरराम स पार्थिवः। यदा न शेकू राजानं याजनार्थं परंतपः॥ ततस्ते याजकः क्रुद्धास्तमूचुर्नृपसत्तमम्। तव कर्माण्यजस्रं वै वर्तन्ते पार्थिवोत्तम॥
en: Having said this, the king became silent. The Brahmanas knew well that they could not assist that chastiser of foes at his sacrifice; therefore they pretended to be angry with that best of kings and they said, "O best of kings, your sacrifices are incessant.

sn: ततो वयं परिश्रान्ताः सततं कर्मवाहिनः। श्रमादस्मात् परिश्रान्तान् स त्वं नस्त्यक्तुमर्हसि॥ बुद्धिमोहं समास्थाय त्वरासम्भावितोऽनघ। गच्छ रुद्रसकाशं त्वं स हि त्वां याजयिष्यति॥
en: We have been fatigued by assisting you (at your sacrifices). We are tried in consequence of this labour; therefore, you should give us leave (to go away). O sinless one, from your loss of judgement only you cannot wait. Go to Rudra (Shiva); he will assist you at your sacrifice."

sn: साधिक्षेपं वचः श्रुत्वा संक्रुद्धः श्वेतकिर्नृपः। कैलास पर्वतं गत्वा तप उग्रं समास्थितः॥ आराधयन् महादेवं नियतः संशितव्रतः। उपवासपरो राजन् दीर्घकालमतिष्ठत॥
en: Having heard these words of censure and wrath, the king Shvetaki became angry. Going to the Kailasa mountain, he begin to worship the God (Shiva), observing rigid vows and performing austere penances. Giving up all food, he passed many years.

sn: कदाचिद् द्वादशे काले कदाचिदपि षोडशे। आहारमकरोद् राजा मूलानि च फलानि च॥
en: He only ate fruits and roots sometimes at the twelfth and sometimes at the sixteenth hour of the day.

sn: ऊर्ध्वबाहुस्त्वनिमिषस्तिष्ठन् स्थाणुरिवाचलः। षण्मासानभवद् राजा श्वेतकिः सुसमाहितः॥
en: He stood like the trunk of a tree. For six months with upraised arms and eyes fixed, the king performed the severest penances there (on the Kailasa mountain).

sn: तं तथा नृपशार्दूलं तप्यमानं महत् तपः। शंकरः परमप्रीत्या दर्शयामास भारत॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, Shankara (Shiva) was greatly pleased; and he at last appeared before him.

sn: उवाच चैनं भगवान् स्निग्धगम्भीरया गिरा। प्रीतोऽस्मि नरशार्दूल तपसा ते परंतप॥
en: He said," O chastiser of foes, O best of men, I have been much pleased with your asceticism.

sn: वरं वृणीष्व भद्रं ते यं त्वमिच्छसि पार्थिव। एतच्छ्रुत्वा तु वचनं रुद्रस्यामिततेजसः॥
en: O king, now ask the boon you desire," Hearing these words of the immeasurably effulgent Rudra (Shiva). The royal sage bowed to him and thus replied to him,

sn: प्रणिपत्य महात्मानं राजर्षिः प्रत्यभाषत। यदि मे भगवान् प्रीतः सर्वलोकनमस्कृतः॥ स्वयं मां देवदेवेश याजयस्व सुरेश्वर। एतच्छ्रुत्वा तु वचनं राज्ञा तेन प्रभाषितम्॥
en: "O illustrious one, O chief of the celestial, O god of gods, if you are pleased with me, assist me then in my sacrifices.” Having heard these words of the king, the deity was pleased and smilingly replied,

sn: उवाच भगवान् प्रीतः स्मितपूर्वमिदं वचः। नास्माकमेष विषयो वर्तते याजनं प्रति॥ त्वया च सुमहत् तप्तं तपो राजन् वरार्थिना। याजयिष्यामि राजांस्त्वां समयेन परंपत॥
en: "We ourselves do not assist at scarifics. But O king, O chastiser of foes, as you have undergone the severest of penances with the desire of obtaining a boon, I shall assist you at your sacrifice on this condition.

sn: रुद्र उवाच समा द्वादश राजेन्द्र ब्रह्मचारी समाहितः। सततं त्वाज्यधाराभिर्यदि तर्पयसेऽनलम्॥ कामं प्रार्थयसे यं त्वं मत्तः प्राप्स्यसि तं नृप।
en: Rudra said: O king of kings, if for full twelve years you can incessantly pour libations of ghee into the sacrificial fire, you yourself leading all the while the life of a Brahmachari. Then, o king, you can obtain me, for the purpose for which you ask me."

sn: एवमुक्तश्च रुद्रेण श्वेतकिर्मनुजाधिपः॥ तथा चकार तत् सर्वं यथोक्तं शूलपाणिना। पूर्णे तु द्वादशे वर्षे पुनरायान्महेश्वरः॥
en: Having been thus addressed by Rudra, the king Shvetaki did what he was asked to do by the wielder of Shula (Shiva). When twelve years were completed, he again came to Maheshwara (Shiva).

sn: दृष्ट्वैव च स राजानं शंकरो लोकभावनः। उवाच परमप्रीतः श्वेतकिं नृपसत्तमम्॥
en: On seeing the king and being much pleased with him, the creator of the world Shankara (Shiva) spoke thus to that best of monarchs, Shvetaki.

sn: तोषितोऽहं नृपश्रेष्ठ त्वयेहाद्येन कर्मणा। याजनं ब्राह्मणानां तु विधिदृष्टं परंतप॥
en: "O best of kings, I have been pleased with your (great) act. O chastiser of foes, the duty of assisting at scarifies belongs to the Brahmanas.

sn: अतोऽहं त्वां स्वयं नाद्य याजयामि परंतय। ममांशस्तु क्षितितले महाभागो द्विजोत्तमः॥
en: O chastiser of foes, therefore, I shall not myself assist you at your sacrifice today. There is one earth a greatly illustrious and best of Brahmanas who is a portion of my own self.

sn: दुर्वासा इति विख्यातः स हि त्वां याजयिष्यति। मन्नियोगान्महातेजाः सम्भाराः सम्भ्रियन्तु ते॥
en: He is known by the name of Durvasa. He will assist you at your sacrifice. He is endued with ascetic powers, he will assist you. Therefore, let every preparation be made (by you)".

sn: एतच्छ्रुत्वा तु वचनं रुद्रेण समुदाहृतम्। स्वपुरं पुनरागम्य सम्भारान् पुनरार्जयत्॥
en: Having heard these words of Rudra, the king returned to his capital and begin to collect all that were necessary for his sacrifice.

sn: ततः सम्भृतसम्भारो भूयो रुद्रमुपागमत्। सम्भृता मम सम्भारा: सर्वोपकरणानि च॥ त्वत्प्रसादान्महादेव श्वो मे दीक्षा भवेदिति। एतच्छ्रुत्वा तु वचनं तस्य राज्ञो महात्मनः॥ दुर्वाससं समाहूय रुद्रो वचनमब्रवीत्। एष राजा महाभागः श्वेतकिर्द्विजसत्तम॥ एनं याजय विप्रेन्द्र मन्नियोगेन भूमिपम्। बाढमित्येव वचनं रुद्रं त्वृषिरुवाच ह॥
en: When every thing had been collected, the king again appeared before Shankara and said, “Every necessary things has been collected. And through your grace all my preparations are ready. O god of gods, let me, therefore be installed in the sacrifices tomorrow.” Having heard these words of the illustrious king. Rudra summoned Durvasa and spoke to him thus, O best of Brahmanas, this is the high-souled king Shvetaki. O chief of Brahmanas assist him at his sacrifice at my command." The Rishi said to Rudra, “Be it so."

sn: ततः सत्रं समभवत् तस्य राज्ञो महात्मनः। यथाविधिः यथाकालं यथोक्तं बहुदक्षिणम्॥
en: Thereupon the sacrifice for which the illustrious king made preparations who performed according to the ordinance, at the proper season and a with large amount of Dakshinas.

sn: तस्मिन् परिसमाप्ते तु राज्ञः सत्रे महात्मनः। दुर्वाससाभ्यनुज्ञाता विप्रतस्थुः स्म याजकः॥ ये तत्र दीक्षिताः सर्वे सदस्याश्च महौजसः। सोऽपि राजन् महाभागः स्वपुरं प्राविशत् तदा॥
en: When the sacrifice of that illustrious king came to an end, all the other priests that assisted at it went away with the permission of Durvasa. All other greatly effulgent Sadasyas also, who had been installed in that sacrifice, went away. O king, then that high-souled (royal sage) entered his own palace.

sn: पूज्यमानो महाभागैाह्मणैर्वेदपारगैः। वन्दिभिः स्तूयमानश्च नागरैश्चाभिनन्दितः॥
en: The Brahmanas well-versed in the Vedas adorned him and singers praised him. The people of the city welcomed him.

sn: एवंवृत्तः स राजर्षिः श्वेतकिर्नृपसत्तमः। कालेन महता चापि ययौ स्वर्गमभिष्टुतः॥ ऋत्विग्भिः सहितः सर्वैः सदस्यैश्च समन्वितः। तस्य सत्रे पपौ वह्निर्हविदश वत्सरान्॥
en: The great king Shvetaki was always righteous. After a long time, adorning by all, he went to the herven accompanied by all members and Ritvijas of the sacrifice. Agni drank ghee for twelve years in his sacrifice.

sn: सततं चाज्यधाराभिरैकात्म्ये तत्र कर्मणि। हविषा च ततो वह्निः परां तृप्तिमगच्छत॥
en: In that unique sacrifice Agni drank large quantity of Ghee, which provided him enormous satisfaction.

sn: न चैच्छत् पुनरादातुं हविरन्यस्य कस्यचित्। पाण्डुवर्णो विवर्णश्च न यथावत् प्रकाशते॥
en: Now, he had no desire to take more oblation from others. Thereupon the illustrious Agni became pale, (because he drank a very large quantity of ghee in that sacrifice). He could not shine as before.

sn: ततो भगवतो वह्नर्विकारः समजायत। तेजसा विप्रहीणश्च ग्लानिश्चैनं समाविशत्॥
en: Then the lord Agni brought some mistransformations in his stomach. Being lusterless he felt hatred.

sn: स लक्षयित्वा चात्मानं तेजोहीनं हुताशनः। जगाम सदनं पुण्यं ब्रह्मणो लोकपूजितम्॥
en: Seeing himself pale, Agni went to the sacred abode of Brahma ever adorned by all.

sn: तत्र ब्रह्माणमासीनमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्। भगवन् परमा प्रीतिः कृता मे श्वेतकेतुना॥ अरुचिश्चाभवत् तीव्रा तां न शक्नोभ्यपोहितुम्। तेजसा विप्रहीणोऽस्मि बलेन च जगत्पते॥ इच्छेय त्वत्प्रसादेन स्वात्मनः प्रकृति स्थिराम्।
en: Coming to Brahma seated (on his throne), he spoke to him thus, King Svetaki satisfied me by his sacrifice. O lord of the universe, I am reduced both in splendour and strength. I desire to regain my own permanent nature through your grade."

sn: एतच्छ्रुत्वा हुतवहाद् भगवान् सर्वलोककृत॥ हव्यवाहमिदं वाक्यमुवाच प्रहसन्निव। त्वया द्वादश वर्षाणि वसोर्धाराहुतं हविः॥ उपयुक्तं महाभाग तेन त्वां ग्लानिराविशत्। तेजसा विप्रहीणत्वात् सहसा हव्यवाहन॥ मा गमस्त्वं यथा वह्ने प्रकृतिस्थो भविष्यसि। अरुचिं नाशयिष्येऽहं समयं प्रतिपद्य ते॥
en: Having heard these words of Agni, the illustrious creator of all the worlds. Smilingly thus spoke to Agni, “You have drunk continuously for twelve years a very large quantity of ghee poured into your mouth. O exalted Deity, it is for this you have been affected with illness. O Agni, you have, therefore, suddenly lost both your splendour strength. O Agni, do not grieve for it. You shall soon regain your own nature. I shall dispel you this malady.

sn: पुरा देवनियोगेन यत् त्वया भस्मसात् कृतम्। आलयं देवशत्रूणां सुघोरं खाण्डवं वनम्॥ तत्र सर्वाणि सत्त्वानि निवसन्ति विभावसो। तेषां त्वं मेदसा तृप्तः प्रकृतिस्थो भविष्यसि॥
en: O Agni, the abode of the enemies of the celestial, the fearful forest of Khandava, which at the request of the celestial you reduced to washes in the days of yorc has again been filled with numerous creatures. When you will eat the fat of all those creatures (now living in the Khandava), you will then regain your own nature.

sn: गच्छ शीघ्रं प्रदग्धुं त्वं ततो मोक्ष्यसि किल्बिषात्। एतच्छ्रुत्वा तु वचनं परमेष्ठिमुखाच्च्युतम्॥ उत्तमं जवमास्थाय प्रदुद्राव हुताशनः। आगम्य खाण्डवं दावमुत्तमं वीर्यमास्थितः। सहसा प्राज्वलच्चाग्निः क्रुद्धो वायुसमीरितः॥
en: Go there soon to consume it with all its living creatures. You will then certainly be cured of your malady." Having heard these words that were uttered by the Supreme Deity, Agni proceeded with great speed (towards that great forest). Arriving at the fearful Khandava forest in full vigour, he suddenly blazed up with the help of the wind.

sn: प्रदीप्तं खाण्डवं दृष्ट्वा ये स्युस्तत्र निवासिनः। परमं यत्नमातिष्ठन् पावकस्य प्रशान्तये॥
en: Seeing the Khandava on fire, the dwellers of that forest made great efforts to extinguish it.

sn: करैस्तु करिणः शीघ्रं जलमादाय सत्वराः। सिषिचुः पावकं क्रुद्धाः शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः॥
en: Hundreds and thousands of elephants speedily brought water in their trunks and they scattered it over the fire in great wrath.

sn: बहुशीर्षास्ततो नागाः शिरोभिर्जलसंततिम्। मुमुचुः पावकाभ्याशे सत्वराः क्रोधमूर्च्छिताः॥
en: Many-headed snakes, becoming mad with anger, speedily scattered on the fire water from their many hoods.

sn: तथैवान्यानि सत्त्वानि नानाप्रहरणोद्यमैः। विलयं पावकं शीघ्रमनयन् भरतर्षभ॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, they and the other creatures that lived in that forest soon extinguished the fire by various means and efforts.

sn: अनेन तु प्रकारेण भूयो भूयश्च प्रज्वलन्। सप्तकृत्वः प्रशमितः खाण्डवे हव्यवाहनः॥
en: Thus Agni blazed forth again and again in the Khandava (forest), but the blazing fire was again and again extinguished by the dwellers of that forest.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच स तु नैराश्यमापन्नः सदा ग्लानिसमन्वितः। पितामहमुपागच्छत् संक्रुद्धो हव्यवाहनः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Then Agni in despair and his malady (uncured) came to the grandsire in anger.

sn: तच्च सर्वं यथान्यायं ब्रह्मणे संन्यवेदयत्। उवाच चैनं भगवान् मुहूर्तं स विचिन्त्य तु॥
en: He told Brahma all that had happened. The illustrious one, then reflecting for a moment, spoke thus to him,

sn: उपायः परिदृष्टो मे यथा त्वं धक्ष्यसेऽनघ। कालं च कंचित् क्षमतां ततस्त्वं धक्ष्यसेऽनल॥
en: “O sinless one, I see a means by which you may consume Khandava today. O Agni! wait for some time, then you will consume.

sn: भविष्यतः सहायौ ते नरनारायणौ तदा। ताभ्यां त्वं सहितो दावं धक्ष्यसे हव्यवाहन॥
en: O Fire! Nara and Narayana will assist you. Accompanied by both of them you will burn Khandava.

sn: एवमस्त्विति तं वह्निर्ब्रह्माणं प्रत्यभाषत। सम्भूतौ तौ विदित्वा तु नरनारायणावृषी॥ कालस्य महतो राजंस्तस्य वाक्यं तस्य वाक्यं स्वयम्भुवः। अनुस्मृत्य जगामाथ पुनरेव पितामहम्॥
en: Agni said to Brahma 'so it be'. Thereafter knowing the incernation of Nara and Narayana he remembered the words of Brahma and he went to him.

sn: अब्रवीच्च तदा ब्रह्मा यथा त्वं धक्ष्यसेऽनल। खाण्डवं दावमद्यैव मिषतोऽस्य शचीपतेः॥
en: Then Brahma addressed him that I see a mcans by which you may consume Khandava today even before the very sight of the husband of Sachi (Indra).

sn: नरनारायणौ यौ तौ पूर्वदेवौ विभावसो। सम्प्राप्तौ मानुषे लोके कार्यार्थं हि दिवौकसाम्॥
en: O Vibhavasu, the two old dcities Nara and Narayana have become incarnates in the world of men to accomplish the purposes of the dwellers of heaven (the celestial).

sn: अर्जुनं वासुदेवं च यौ तौ लोकोऽभिमन्यते। तावेतौ सहितावेहि खाण्डवस्य समीपतः॥ तौ त्वं याचस्व साहाय्ये दाहार्थं खाण्डवस्य च। ततो धक्ष्यसि तं दावं रक्षितं त्रिदशैरपि॥
en: They are called on earth Vasudeva (Krishna) and Arjuna. They are now staying near the Khandava (forest). Ask those two (heroes) to help you in consuming the Khandava. You will then be able to consume it, even if it be protected by the celestial.

sn: तौ तु सत्त्वानि सर्वाणि यत्नतो वारयिष्यतः। देवराजं च सहितौ तत्र मे नास्ति संशयः॥
en: They will certainly prevent the dwellers of the Khandava to escape; and they will thwart Indra also. I have not the least doubt in this."

sn: एकच्छ्रुत्वा तु वचनं त्वरितो हव्यवाहनः। कृष्णपार्थावुपागम्य यमर्थं त्वभ्यभाषत॥ अब्रवीनृपशार्दूल तत्कालसदृशं वचः। दिधएं खाण्डवं दावमकामस्य शतक्रतोः॥ तं ते कथितवानस्मि पूर्वमेव नृपोत्तम। तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं तवग्नेर्बीभत्सुर्जातवेदसम्॥
en: Having heard his words, Agni speedily came to Krishna and Arjuna. What he said to those illustrious pair, I have already told you. O best of kings, hearing these words of Agni who desired to consume the foes of Pandava against the wishes of Indra, Vivatsu (Arjuna) said to him these words will suited to the occasion.

sn: अर्जुन उवाच उत्तमास्त्राणि मे सन्ति दिव्यानि च बहूनि च। यैरहं शक्नुयां योद्धुमपि वज्रधरान् बहून्॥
en: "I have numberless excellent celestial weapons with which I can fight even with many wielders of thunder(Indra).

sn: धनुर्मे नास्ति भगवन् बाहुवीर्येण सम्मितम्। कुर्वतः समरे यत्नं वेगं यद् विषहेन्मम॥
en: But, O illustrious one, I have no bow suited to the strength of my arms and capable of bearing the might I put fourth in battle.

sn: शरैश्च मेऽर्थो बहुभिरक्षयैः क्षिप्रमस्यतः। न हि वोढुं रथः शक्तः शरान् मम यथेप्सितान्॥
en: In consequence of the great lightness of my hands, I require arrows that will be inexhaustible (in the quiver). My car also is hardly able to bear the load of arrows that I desire to keep by me.

sn: अश्वांश्च दिव्यानिच्छेयं पाण्डुरान् वातरंहसः। रथं च मेघनिर्घोषं सूर्यप्रतिमतेजसम्॥
en: I desire to have (some) celestial horses of pure white colour, possessing the speed of the wind and (I also desire to have) a car, possessing the splendour of the sun; the clatter of its wheels should resemble the roars of clouds.

sn: तथा कृष्णस्य वीर्येण नायुधं विद्यते समम्। येन नागान् पिशाचांश्च निहन्यान्माधवो रणे॥
en: Then there is no weapon suited to Krishna's prowess. He requires weapon like the one with which Mahadeva (Shiva) kills Nagas and Pishachas in the battle.

sn: उपायं कर्मसिद्धौ च भगवन् वक्तुमर्हसि। निवारयेयं येनेन्द्रं वर्षमाणं महावने॥
en: O illustrious one, you should give us the means by which we may gain success; and we can prevent Indra from pouring rains on that extensive forest.

sn: पौरुषेण तु यत् कार्यं तत् कर्तारौ स्व पावक। करणानि समर्थानि भगवन् दातुमर्हसि॥
en: O Agni, we are ready to do what is possible to be done by manliness and prowess. O illustrious one, but you should give us the proper means.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्तः स भगवान् धूमकेतुर्हताशनः। चिन्तयामास वरुणं लोकपालं दिदृक्षया॥ आदित्यमुदके देवं निवसन्तं जलेश्वरम्। स च तच्चिन्तितं ज्ञात्वा दर्शयामास पावकम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having been thus addressed, the illustrious smoke-banned (deity) Agni recollected Varuna, the protector of the world, the son of Aditi and the lord of waters having his home in the waters, He too knowing that he was thought of, appeared before Agni.

sn: तमब्रवीद् धूमकेतुः प्रतिगृह्य जलेश्वरम्। चतुर्थं लोकपालानां देवदेवं सनातनम्॥
en: The smoke-banned deity (Agni) with reverence welcomes the lord of the waters, the foremost of the Lokapalas, the eternal god of gods and he then thus spoke to him,

sn: सोमेन राज्ञा यद् दत्तं धनुश्चैवेषुधी च ते। तत् प्रयच्छोभयं शीघ्रं रथं च कपिलक्षणम्॥
en: "Give me without delay the bow and the quiver and also the ape-banned chariot which were obtained from the king Soma.

sn: कार्यं च सुमहत् पार्थो गाण्डीवेन करिष्यति। चक्रेण वासुदेववश्च तन्ममाद्य प्रदीयताम्॥
en: Partha will (today) accomplish a great deed with the Gandiva (the bow in question) and Vasudeva also with the discus. Therefore, give them both to me today."

sn: ददानीत्येव वरुणः पावकं प्रत्यभाषत। तदद्भुतं महावीर्यं यश:कीर्तिविवर्धनम्॥ सर्वशस्त्रैरनार सर्वशस्त्रप्रमाथि च। सर्वायुधमहामात्रं परसैन्यप्रधर्षणम्॥ एकं शतसहस्रेण सम्मितं राष्ट्रवर्धनम्। चित्रमुच्चावचैर्वर्णैः शोभितं श्लक्ष्णमव्रणम्॥ देवदानवगन्धर्वैः पूजितं शाश्वतीः समाः। प्रादाच्चैव धनूरत्नमक्षय्ये च महेषुधी॥
en: Varuna said to Agni, “I am giving." He then gave him that jewel of a bow, Gandiva, a bow endued with great energy. It was a great enhancer of fame and achievements, it was incapable of being injured by any weapon, it was the chief of all weapons and the gem of them all, it was the smiter of hostile armies and it was alone equal to one hundred thousand bow; it was the enhancer of kingdoms and it was variegated with excellent colours; it was well-adorned and beautiful to look at without a mark of weakness and injury anywhere and it was always worshipped both by the celestial and the Gandharvas.

sn: रथं च दिव्याश्वयुजं कपिप्रवरकेतनम्। उपेतं राजतैरश्वैर्गान्धर्हममालिभिः॥ पाण्डुराभ्रप्रतीकाशैर्मनोवायुसमैर्जवे। सर्वोपकरणैर्युक्तमजय्यं देवदानवैः॥
en: He also gave him a chariot filled with celestial weapons and having a large ape as its standard. Yoked to that chariot were steeds as white as the silver or the fleecy clouds, they were born in the regions of the Gandharvas and they were all adorned with golden harness. They had the speed of the wind or the mind. The chariot was equipped with every instruments of war and was incapable of being vanquished by the celestial or the Asuras.

sn: भानुमन्तं महाघोषं सर्वरत्नमनोरमम्। ससर्ज यं सुतपसा भौमनो भुवनप्रभुः॥ प्रजापतिरनिर्देश्यं यस्य रूपं रवेरिव। यं स्म सोमः समारुह्य दानवानजयत् प्रभुः॥
en: Its splendour was very great and the sound of its wheels were tremendous; it delighted the heart of every creature that looked at it. It was created by Prajapati after severe ascetic mediation. It was as effulgent as the sun and its splendour was so great that none could gaze at it. It was that very chariot riding on which the lord Soma defeated the Danavas.

sn: नवमेघप्रतीकाशं ज्वलन्तमिव च श्रिया। आश्रितौ तं रथश्रेष्ठं शक्रायुधसमावुभौ॥ तापनीया सुरुचिरा ध्वजयष्टिरनुत्तमा। तस्यां तु वानरो दिव्यः सिंहशार्दूलकेतनः॥
en: Resplendent with beauty, it looked like an evening could reflecting the splendour of the sun. It was furnished with an excellent flagstaff of golden colour and beauty. And there sat upon that staff a fierce-looking celestial ape which looked like a lion or a tiger.

sn: दिधक्षन्निव तत्र स्म संस्थितो मूर्ध्यशोभत। ध्वजे भूतानि तत्रासन् विविधानि महान्ति च॥
en: Stationed on high the ape seemed bent upon burning everything it saw. There were other creatures also on other flags.

sn: नादेन रिपुसैन्यानां येषां संज्ञा प्रणश्यति। स तं नानापताकाभिः शोभितं रथसत्तमम्॥ प्रदक्षिणमुपावृत्य दैवतेभ्यः प्रणम्य च। संनद्धः कवची खङ्गी बद्धगोधाङ्गुलित्रकः॥
en: Whose roars caused the soldiers of the enemy's army to faint away. Then walking round that excellent car adorned with various flags and banners and bowing to the celestial, Arjuna, attired in armour, armed with sword and his fingers increased in leather, ascended it as a virtuous man (on a celestial car that takes him to heaven).

sn: आरुरोह तदा पार्थो विमानं सुकृती यथा। तच्च दिव्यं धनुः श्रेष्ठं ब्रह्मणा निर्मितं पुरा॥ गाण्डीवमुपसंगृह्य बभूव मुदितोऽजुनः। हुताशनं पुरस्कृत्य ततस्तदपि वीर्यवान्॥ जग्राह बलमास्थाय ज्यया च युयुजे धनुः। मौ। तु योज्यमानायां बलिना पाण्डवेन ह॥ येऽशृण्वन् कूजितं तत्र तेषां वै व्यथितं मनः।
en: Taking upto that celestial and the best of all bows, that which was created by Brahma in days of yore and which was called Gandiva, Arjuna became exceedingly glad. Bowing down to Agni, the greatly powerful hero took up the bow with force and stringed it. His heart trembled who heard the noise that was made while the bow was stringed by the mighty Pandava (Arjuna).

sn: लब्ध्वा रथं धनुश्चैव तथाक्षय्ये महेषुधी॥ बभूव कल्यः कौन्तेयः प्रहृष्टः साह्यकर्मणि। वज्रनाभं ततश्चक्रं ददौ कृष्णाय पावकः॥
en: Having obtained that chariot and bow and the two inexhaustible quivers the son of Kunti became exceedingly glad; and he then thought that he was competent to assist Agni in the task. Then (Agni) gave Krishna a discuss with a piece of iron attached to its centre.

sn: आग्नेयमस्त्रं दयितं स च कल्योऽभवत् तदा। अब्रवीत् पावकश्चैवमेतेन मधुसूदन।॥ अमानुषानपि रणे जेष्यसि त्वमसंशयम्। अनेन तु मनुष्याणां देवानामपि चाहवे॥ रक्षःपिशाचदैत्यानां नागानां चाधिकस्तथा। भविष्यसि न संदेहः प्रवरोऽपि निबर्हणे॥
en: It was a desirable fiery weapon and on receiving it, he too became competent to assist Agni. Then Agni said, “O slayer of Madhu Krishna, you shall certainly, with the help of this weapon, be able to defeat you enemies, even if they are not human. O Madhava, with this weapon you shall certainly be superior to men and gods, to Rakshasas and Pishachas, to Daityas and Nagas. You shall certainly be able to kill all creatures with this weapon.

sn: क्षिप्तं क्षिप्तं रणे चैतत् त्वया माधव शत्रुषु। हत्वाप्रतिहतं संख्ये पाणिमेष्यति ते पुनः॥
en: Being hurled at your enemy by you in battle, it will irresistibly kill the enemy and it will then again come back to your hands."

sn: वरुणश्च ददौ तस्मै गदामशनिनिःस्वनाम्। दैत्यान्तकरणी घोरां नाम्ना कौमोदकी प्रभुः॥
en: Then lord Varuna gave him (Krishna) a club, named Kaumodaki, capable of killing every Daityas and producing a roar like that of the thunder.

sn: ततः पावकमबूतां प्रहृष्टावर्जुनाच्युतौ। कृतास्त्रौ शस्त्रसम्पन्नौ रथिनौ ध्वजिनावपि॥ कल्यौ स्वो भगवन् योद्धमपि सर्वैः सुरासुरैः। किं पुनर्वज्रिणैकेन पन्नगार्थे युयुत्सता॥
en: Then Arjuna and Achyuta (Krishna) thus spoke to Agni in joy, “O illustrious one, furnished ass we are now with great weapons and well conversant with their use and possessed as we are of cars with flats and flatstaff, we are now able to fight even with all the celestial and the Asuras put together, not to speak of the wielder of thunder (Indra) who desire to fight for the sake of the Naga Takshaka.

sn: अर्जुन उवाच चक्रपाणिर्हषीकेशो विचरन् युधि वीर्यवान्। चक्रेण भस्मसात् सर्वं विसृष्टेन तु वीर्यवान्। त्रिषु लोकेषु तन्नास्ति यन्न कुर्याज्जनार्दनः॥ गाण्डीवं धनुरादाय तथाक्षय्ये महेषुधी। अहमप्युत्सहे लोकान् विजेतुं युधि पावक॥
en: Arjuna said : O Agni, when the greatly powerful Hrishikesha Krishna moves on the field of battle with this discuss in hand, there is nothing in the three worlds which he is not able to consume by hurling his weapon. Having obtained the bow Gandiva and these two inexhaustible quivers, I am also ready to vanquish the three worlds.

sn: सर्वतः परिवायैवं दावमेतं महाप्रभो। कामं सम्प्रज्वलाद्यैव कल्यौ स्वः साह्यकर्मणि॥
en: Therefore, O lord, blaze as much as you like. Surround this large forest with fire. We are quite capable of helping you. Vaishampayana said :

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्तः स भगवान् दाशार्हेणार्जुनेन च। तैजसं रूपमास्थाया दावं दग्धुं प्रचक्रमे॥
en: Having been thus addressed by Dasharha (Krishna) and Arjuna, the illustrious (Agni) put forth his most energetic form and he then prepared himself to consume that forest.

sn: सर्वतः परिवार्याथ सप्ताचिर्खलनस्तथा। ददाह खाण्डवं दावं युगान्तमिव दर्शयन्॥
en: Having sur Sunded it from all sides with his seven flames and appearing as fearful as he appears at the end of a Yuga, he begin to consume the Khandava.

sn: प्रतिगृह्य समाविश्य तद् वनं भरतर्षभ। मेघस्तनितनिर्घोषः सर्वभूतान्यकम्पयत्॥
en: best of the Bharata race, having surrounded that forest and catching it on all sides, he roared like that of the clouds and made every creature within it tremble (with fear).

sn: दह्यतस्तस्य च बभौ रूपं दावस्य भारत। मेरोरिव नगेन्द्रस्य कीर्णस्यांशुमर्तोऽशुभिः॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, that burning forest looked like, the resplendent Meru, the king of the mountains, blazing with the rays of the sun falling on it.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तौ रथाभ्यां रथश्रेष्ठौ दावस्योभयतः स्थितौ। दिक्षु सर्वासु भूतानां चक्राते कदनं महत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Then those two foremost of car warriors (Krishna and Arjuna), riding on their cars and placing themselves each on one side of the burning forest, began a great slaughter of all creatures.

sn: यत्र यत्र च दृश्यन्ते प्राणिनः खाण्डवालयाः। पलायन्तः प्रवीरौ तौ तत्र तत्राभ्यधावताम्॥
en: Wherever and whenever they saw any creature, any dweller of the Khandava, escaping from the fire, those two great heroes immediately shot it down.

sn: छिद्रं न स्म प्रपश्यन्ति रथयोराशुचारिणोः। आविद्धावेव दृश्येते रथिनौ तौ रथोत्तमौ॥
en: There cars moved so fast round the forest that the creatures dwelling in it saw not the smallest space between the two rushing cars (so that they might escape by that way). Those two excellent cars seemed to be one car and those two heroes also seemed as if they were one man.

sn: खाण्डवे दह्यमाने तु भूताः शतसहस्रशः। उत्पेतुर्भेरवान् नादान् विनदन्तः समन्ततः॥
en: When the Khandava was on fire, hundreds and thousands of living creatures, uttering fearful yells, ran in all directions.

sn: दग्धैकदेशा बहवो निष्टप्ताश्च तथापरे। स्फुटिताक्षा विशीर्णाश्च विप्लुताश्च तथापरे॥
en: Some had their limbs burnt, some were scorched with the excessive heat, some had their eyes burst out, some were withered away and some ran about in fear.

sn: समालिङ्गय सुतानन्ये पितॄन् भ्रातृनथापरे। त्यक्तं न शेकुः स्नेहेन तत्रैव निधनं गताः॥
en: Some died calmly within the forest clasping their children and some their parents and brothers; they were unable to abandon those that were dear to them out of excessive affection.

sn: संदष्टदशनाश्चान्ये समुत्पेतुरनेकशः। ततस्तेऽतीव घूर्णन्तः पुनरग्नौ प्रपेदिरे॥
en: Many rose high upwards, biting their nether lips, but they soon again fell below whirling into the blazing fire.

sn: दग्धपक्षाक्षिचरणा विचेष्टन्तो महीतले। तत्र तत्र स्म दृश्यन्ते विनश्यन्तः शरीरिणः॥
en: Some were seen rolling on the ground with their wings, eyes and feet scorched and burnt. They were soon after found to be dead.

sn: जलाशयेषु तप्तेषु काथ्यमानेषु वह्निना। गतसत्त्वाः स्म दृश्यन्ते कूर्ममत्स्याः समन्ततः॥
en: The tanks and the ponds that lay within that forest were heated with the fire and they began to boil. The fishes and tortoises that were in their waters were all seen to perish.

sn: शरीरैरपरे दीप्तैर्देहवन्त इवाग्नयः। अदृश्यन्त वने तत्र प्राणिनः प्राणिसंक्षय॥
en: In that great massacre of creatures in that forest, the burning bodies of various animals looked as if Agni had assumed to many forms.

sn: कांश्चिदुत्पततः पार्थः शरैः संछिद्य खण्डशः। पातयामास विहगान् प्रदीप्ते वसुरेतसि॥
en: The birds that took to their wings to escape from that fire were soon pierced by Arjuna's arrows; and being cut down to pieces, they again fell into the burning fire.

sn: ते शराचितसर्वाङ्गा निनदन्तो महारवान्। ऊर्ध्वमुत्पत्य वेगेन निपेतुः खाण्डवे पुनः॥
en: Being pierced by Arjuna's arrows the flying birds again fell into the Khandava with great speed and uttering loud cries.

sn: शरैरभ्याहतानां च संघशः स्म वनौकसाम्। विरावः शुश्रुवे घोरः समुद्रस्येव मथ्यतः॥
en: Being pierced by the arrows, the dwellers of that forest begin to cry and the noise they made was like the fearful noise that rose at the churning of the ocean.

sn: वह्वेश्चापि प्रदीप्तस्य खमुत्पेतुर्महार्चिषः। जनयामासुरुद्वेगं सुमहान्तं दिवौकसाम्॥
en: The great flame of the blazing fire rose to the sky and created a great anxiety in the minds of the dwellers of heavens the Devas.

sn: तेनार्चिषा सुसंतप्ता देवा: सर्षिपुरोगमाः। ततो जग्मुर्महात्मानः सर्व एव दिवौकसः। शतक्रतुं सहस्राक्षं देवेशमसुरार्दनम्॥
en: Thereupon all the illustrious celestial went in a body to their chief of one hundred sacrifices and one thousands eyes the grinder of the Asuras, Indra.

sn: देवा ऊचुः तच्छ्रुत्वा वृत्रहा किं विमे मानवाः सर्वे दह्यन्ते चित्रभानुना। कच्चिन्न संक्षयः प्राप्तो लोकानाममरेश्वर॥
en: The Celestial said: O lord of the immortals, who does Agni burn all the creatures below? Has the time for the destruction of the world come?

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तेभ्यः स्वयमेवान्ववेक्ष्य च। खाण्डवस्य विमोक्षार्थं प्रययौ हरिवाहनः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having heard this and himself seeing what Agni was doing, the slayer of Vitra (Indra) set out to save the creatures from the fire.

sn: महता रथवृन्देन नानारूपेण वासवः। आकाशं समवाकीर्य प्रववर्ष सुरेश्वरः॥
en: The lord of the celestial, Vasava soon covered the sky with masses of clouds of various kinds; he then began to pour fain.

sn: ततोऽक्षमात्रा व्यसृजन धाराः शतसहस्रशः। चोदिता देवराजेन जलदाः खाण्डवं प्रति॥
en: As soon as commanded by the king of the celestial, those hundreds and thousands of clouds begin to shower on the Khandava forest in as thick drops as the flag-staffs of warchariots.

sn: असम्प्राप्तास्तु ता धारास्तेजसा जातवेदसः। ख एव समशुष्यन्त न काश्चित् पावकं गताः॥
en: But the showers were all dried up even in the sky by the heat of the fire; and they could not reach the fire below.

sn: ततो नमुचिहा क्रुद्धो भृशमर्चिष्मतस्तदा। पुनरेव महामेधैरम्भांसि व्यसृजद् बहु॥
en: The slayer of Namuchi (Indra) becoming very angry with Agni, again collected many more masses of clouds and made them shower a heavy down-pour.

sn: अचिर्धाराभिसम्बद्धं धूमविद्युत्समाकुलम्। बभूव तद् वनं घोरं स्तनयित्नुसमाकुलम्॥
en: Then the flames fought with that heavy shower and those masses of clouds overhead. The forest, being filled with smoke and lightings, became fearful to look at.

description: Battle between the celestial and Krishna and Arjuna
sn: तस्याथ वर्षतो वारि पाण्डव: प्रत्यवारयत्। शरवर्षेण बीभत्सुरुत्तमास्त्राणि दर्शयन्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : The son of Pandu, Vivatsu (Arjuna), calling his excellent weapons to his help, stopped that shower of rain by means of a shower of his own.

description: Battle between the celestial and Krishna and Arjuna
sn: खाण्डवं च वनं सर्वं पाण्डवो बहुभिः शरैः। आच्छादयदमेयात्मा नीहारेणेव चन्द्रमाः॥
en: The high-souled Pandava covered the Khandava forest with innumerable arrows, as the atmosphere is filled with a thick fog.

description: Battle between the celestial and Krishna and Arjuna
sn: न च स्म किंचिच्छक्नोति भूतं निश्चरितुं ततः। संछाद्यमाने खे बाणैरस्यता सव्यसाचिना॥
en: When the sky over the forest was thus covered with the arrows of Savyasachi (Arjuna), not a single creature could escape (from that forest).

description: Battle between the celestial and Krishna and Arjuna
sn: तक्षकस्तु न तत्रासीन्नागराजो महाबलः। दह्यमाने वने तस्मिन् कुरुक्षेत्रं गतो हि सः॥
en: The greatly powerful king of the Nagas Takshaka, was not there. When the forest was on fire, he was absent in Kurukshetra where he had gone.

description: Battle between the celestial and Krishna and Arjuna
sn: निगीर्य च। अश्वसेनोऽभवत् तत्र तक्षकस्य सुतो बली। स यत्नमकरोत् तीव्र मोक्षार्थं जातवेदसः॥
en: But the powerful son of Takshaka, named Ashvasena, was there (in the forest); and he made great efforts to escape from the fire.

description: Battle between the celestial and Krishna and Arjuna
sn: न शशाक स निर्गन्तुं निरुद्धोऽर्जुनपत्रिभिः। मोक्षयामास तं माता निगीर्य भुजगात्मजा॥
en: Confined by Arjuna's arrows, he could not succeed to come out (of the forest), but the snakes lady, his mother, determined to save his life.

description: Battle between the celestial and Krishna and Arjuna
sn: तस्य पूर्वं शिरो ग्रस्तं पुच्छमस्य निगीर्यमाणा साक्रामत् सुतं नागी मुमुक्षया॥
en: She first swallowed his head and then she began to swallow his tail; in that state she then attempted to save her son and rose to the sky.

description: Battle between the celestial and Krishna and Arjuna
sn: तस्याः शरेण तीक्ष्णेन पृथुधारेण पाण्डवः। शिरश्चिच्छेद गच्छन्त्यास्तामपश्यच्छचीपतिः॥ तं मुमोचयिषुर्वज्री वातवर्षेण पाण्डवम्। मोहयामास तत्कालमश्वसेनस्त्वमुच्यत॥
en: As soon as the Pandava (Arjuna) saw her escaping, he cut off her head by means of sharp arrows, but the husband of Sachi, the wielder of thunder, Indra, saw all this; and he resolved to save the son of his friend. He raised a violent wind and deprived Arjuna of his consciousness. In the meantime Ashvasena succeeded in effecting his escape.

description: Battle between the celestial and Krishna and Arjuna
sn: तां च मायां तदा दृष्ट्वा घोरां नागेन वञ्चितः। द्विधा त्रिधा चखगतान् प्राणिनः पाण्डवोऽच्छिनत्।१०।।
en: Having seen this fearful delusion and having been deceived by the Nagas, the Pandava cut down all creatures into two three or more pieces.

description: Battle between the celestial and Krishna and Arjuna
sn: शशाप तं च संक्रुद्धो बीभत्सुर्जिह्यगामिनम्। पावको वासुदेवश्चाप्यप्रतिष्ठो भविष्यसि॥
en: Vivatsu (Arjuna) cursed in anger the Naga that had so deceitfully escaped; so did Vasudeva (Krishna) and Agni. They said, "Never shall you be able to win fame or position.”

description: Battle between the celestial and Krishna and Arjuna
sn: ततो जिष्णुः सहस्राक्षं स्वं वितत्याशुगैः शरैः। योधयामास संक्रुद्धो वञ्चनां तामनुस्मरन्॥
en: Then remembering the deception practised on him, Jishnu (Arjuna) became very much angry and covering the sky with a cloud of arrows, he sought to fight with the god of thousand eyes(Indra).

description: Battle between the celestial and Krishna and Arjuna
sn: देवराजोऽपि तं दृष्ट्वा संरब्धं समरेऽर्जुनम्। स्वमस्त्रमसृजत् तीव्र छादयित्वाखिलं नभः॥
en: Seeing Arjuna in wrath, the king of the celestial also sought to fight with him. He hurled his very fearful weapons and covered whole of the sky.

description: Battle between the celestial and Krishna and Arjuna
sn: ततो वायुर्महाघोषः क्षोभयन् सर्वसागरान्। वियत्स्थो जनयन् मेघाञ्जलधारासमाकुलान्॥
en: Then greatly roaring winds, agitating all the oceans, gathered together masses of clouds charged with torrents of rains.

description: Battle between the celestial and Krishna and Arjuna
sn: ततोऽशनिमुचो घोरांस्तडित्स्तनितनि:स्वनान्। तद्विघातार्थमसृजदर्जुनोऽप्यस्त्रमुत्तमम्॥ वायव्यमभिमन्याथ प्रतिपत्तिविशारदः। तेनेन्द्राशनिमेघानां वीर्योजस्तद् विनाशितम्॥ जलधाराश्च ताः शोषं जग्मुर्नेशुश्च विद्युतः। क्षणेन चाभवद् व्योम समप्रशान्तरजस्तमः॥
en: Thereupon those clouds, charged with thunder-rattle, vomited thunder and flashes of lightings; but to dispel them Arjuna hurled and excellent weapon. Named Vayavya (wind weapon) with proper Mantras. In a moment it destroyed the force and the energy of Indra's thunder and it dried up the water that was in those masses of clouds; it then destroyed the lightings that played amongst them.

description: Battle between the celestial and Krishna and Arjuna
sn: सुखशीतानिलवहं प्रकृतिस्थार्कमण्डलम्। निष्प्रतीकारहृष्टश्च हुतभुग विविधाकृतिः॥ सिच्यमानो वसौघैस्तैः प्राणिनां देहनिःसृतैः। प्रजज्वालाथ सोऽर्चिष्मान् स्वनादैः पूरयञ्जगत्॥
en: (In a moment) the sky was cleared off dust and darkness; delicious and cool breeze began to blow and the sun regained its normal state. Then Agni, sprinkled over with the fat that came out of the burning bodies of the various creatures, blazed up with all his flames and filled the universe with his roars.

description: Battle between the celestial and Krishna and Arjuna
sn: कृष्णाभ्यां रक्षितं दृष्ट्वा तं च दावमहंकृताः। खमुत्पेतुर्महाराज सुपर्णाद्याः पतत्रिणः॥ गरुत्मान् वज्रसदृशैः पक्षतुण्डनखैस्तथा। प्रहर्तुकामो न्यपतदाकाशात् कृष्णपाण्डवौ॥
en: O great king, seeing that the forest was protected by the two Krishnas, many feathery creatures of the Garuda race proudly came down from the sky with the desire of striking those two heroes Krishna and the Pandava (Arjuna) with their thunder like strong wings, breaks and claws.

description: Battle between the celestial and Krishna and Arjuna
sn: तथैवोरगसङ्घाताः पाण्डवस्य समीपतः। उत्सृजन्तो विषं घोरं निपेतुर्खलिताननाः॥
en: Many Nagas also came down upon the Pandava (Arjuna), all with faces emitting most virulent poisons.

description: Battle between the celestial and Krishna and Arjuna
sn: तांश्चकर्त शरैः पार्थः सरोषाग्निसमुक्षितैः। विविशुश्चापि तं दीप्तं देहाभावाय पावकम्॥
en: Partha cut them to pieces by his arrows which appeared as if they had been steeped in the fire of his wrath. They (those birds and snakes) all fell into the burning fire below.

description: Battle between the celestial and Krishna and Arjuna
sn: ततोऽसुराः सगन्धर्वा यक्षराक्षसपन्नगाः। उत्पेतुर्नादमतुलमुत्सृजन्तो रणार्थिनः॥
en: Wishing to fight, there also came innumerable Asuras, Gandharvas, Yakshas, Rakshasas and Nagas, all uttering fearful yells.

description: Battle between the celestial and Krishna and Arjuna
sn: अयः कणपचक्राश्मभुशुण्ड्युद्यतबाहवः। कृष्णपार्थो जिघांसन्तः क्रोधसम्मूर्छितौजसः॥
en: Armed with instruments which vomited iron balls and bullets from their throats and with machines and propelled huge stones and rockets, they rushed forward to strike Krishna and Partha.

description: Battle between the celestial and Krishna and Arjuna
sn: तेषामतिव्याहरतां शस्त्रवर्षं प्रमुञ्चताम्। प्रममाथोत्तमाङ्गानि बीभत्सुनिशितैः शरैः॥
en: Though they rained a fearful shower of weapons, Vivatsu (Arjuna) cut off their heads with his sharp arrows,

description: Battle between the celestial and Krishna and Arjuna
