sn: ततः स भगवान् सूर्यो मामुपादाय वीर्यवान्। आगच्छत् तां सभां ब्राह्मीं विपाप्मा विगतक्लमः॥
en: (When I completed my vow), then the illustrious and powerful and sinless Surya who knows no fatigue came and took me to the Sabha of Brahma.

sn: एवंरूपेति सा शक्या न निर्देष्टुं नराधिप। क्षणेन हि बिभर्त्यन्यदनिर्दैश्यं वपुस्तथा॥
en: O king, none is able to describe it by saying “It is such"; for it assumes an indescribable form with a moment.

sn: न वेद परिमाणं वा संस्थानं चापि भारत। न च रूपं मया तादृग् दृष्टपूर्वं कदाचन॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, it is impossible to indicate its dimensions or shape. I have never seen any this like it before.

sn: सुसुखा सा सदा राजन् न शीता न च धर्मदा। न क्षुत्पिपासे न ग्लानिं प्राप्य तां प्राप्नुवन्त्युत॥
en: O king, it ever contributes to the happiness of those that live within it. It is neither cold nor hot; hanger, thirst and all kinds of uneasiness disappear from one as soon as one enters into it.

sn: नानारूपैरिव कृता मणिभिः सा सुभास्वरैः। स्तम्भैर्न च धृता सा तु शाश्वती न च सा क्षरा॥ दिव्यैर्नानाविधैर्भावैर्भासद्भिरमितप्रभैः॥ अति चन्द्रं च सूर्यं च शिखिनं च स्वयम्प्रभा। दीप्यते नाकपृष्ठस्था भर्सयन्तीव भास्करम्॥
en: It is made of brilliant gems of many kinds, it does not seem to be supported on any pillars, it knows no deterioration, it is eternal. That self effulgent Sabha seems to surpass the moon, the sun, and the fire by its numerous matchless and blazing celestials indications.

sn: तस्यां स भगवानास्ते विदधद् देवमायया। स्वयमेकोऽनिशं राजन् सर्वलोकपितामहः॥ उपतिष्ठन्ति चाप्येनं प्रजानां पतयः प्रभुम्। दक्षः प्रचेताः पुलहो मरीचिः कश्यपः प्रभुः॥
en: O king, in this (Sabha) sits the supreme deity, the Grandsire of all created things, having himself alone created everything, having himself alone created every thing by his own Maya. Daksha, Pracheta, Pulaha, Marichi, Lord Kashyapa,

sn: भृगुरत्रिर्वसिष्ठच गौतमोऽथ तथाङ्गिराः। पुलस्त्यश्च क्रुतश्चैव प्रहादः कर्दमस्तथा॥ अथर्वाङ्गिरसश्चैव बालखिल्या मरीचिपाः। मनोऽन्तरिक्षं विद्याश्च वायुस्तेजो जलं मही॥
en: Bhrigu, Atri, Vasishtha, Gautama, Angirasa, Pulastya, Kratu, Prahlada, Kardama, the Prajapati, Angirasa of the Atharva, Veda, the Balkhilyas, the Marichipas, Mind, Space Knowledge, Air, Heat water, Earth.

sn: शब्दस्पर्शी तथा रूपं रसो गन्धश्च भारत। प्रकृतिश्च विकारच यच्चान्यत् कारणं भुवः॥
en: Sound, Touch, Form, Taste, Scent, Nature, the Modes, the Elemental and Prime causes of the world, O descendant of Bharata, (all these sit there).

sn: अगस्त्यश्च महातेजा मार्कण्डेयश्च वीर्यवान्। जगमदग्निर्भरद्वाजः संवर्तश्च्यवनस्तथा॥ दुर्वासाश्च महाभाग ऋष्यशृङ्गश्च धार्मिकः। सनत्कुमारो भगवान् योगाचार्यो महातपाः॥ असितो देवलश्चैव जैगीषव्यश्च तत्त्ववित्। ऋषभो जितशत्रुश्च महावीर्यस्तथा मणिः॥
en: The greatly effulgent Agastya, the great ascetic Markandeya, Jamadagni, Bharadvaja, Samvarata, Chyavana, the illustrious Durvasa, the pious Rishyashringa, the high souled Sanatkumara, who is a great ascetic and the preceptor of Yoga, Asita, Devala, Jaigishavya, learned in all truths, Rishabha, Ajitsatan, greatly resplendent Mani,

sn: आयुर्वेदस्तथाष्टाङ्गो देरवांस्तत्र भारत। चन्द्रमाः सह नक्षत्रैरादित्यश्च गभस्तिमान्॥
en: The Science of Healing with its eight branches, all these in their personified forms, O descendant of Bharata, wait there (in that assembly-hall). Moon with stars and constellations, sun with its rays.

sn: वायवः क्रतवश्चैव संकल्पः प्राण एव च। मूर्तिमन्तो महात्मानो महाव्रतपरायणाः॥ एते चान्ये च बहवो ब्रह्माणं समुपस्थिताः। अर्थो धर्मश्च कामश्च हर्षो द्वेषस्तपो दमः॥
en: Declaration of purpose in sacrifices, the Ritual principles, these illustrious and vow observing beings in their personified forms, and many others too numerous to mention, all wait upon Brahma. Artha Dharma, Kama, Joy, Aversion, Asceticism and Peace of Mind,

sn: आयान्ति तस्यां सहिता गन्धर्वाप्सरसां गणाः। विंशतिः सप्त चैवान्ये लोकपालाश्च सर्वशः॥
en: With them come the twenty seven different tribes of the Gandharvas and of the Apsaras and others also, and also the Lokapalas,

sn: शुक्रो बृहस्पतिश्चैव बुधोऽङ्गारक एव च। शनैश्चरच राहुश्च ग्रहाः सर्वे तथैव च॥ मन्त्रो स्थन्तरं चैव हरिमान् वसुमानपि। आदित्याः साधिराजानो नामद्वन्द्वैरुदाहृताः॥
en: Shukra, Brihaspati, Budha, Angaraka, Shani, Rahu, and the other planets the Mantras, the special Mantras, Hasimaat, Vasumat, Adityas with Indra, the two Agnis,

sn: मरुतो विश्वकर्मा च वसवश्चैव भारत। तथा पितृगणाः सर्वे सर्वाणि च हवींष्यथ।॥ ऋग्वेदः सामवेदश्च यजुर्वेदच पाण्डव। अथर्ववेदश्च तथा सर्वशास्त्राणि चैव ह॥
en: The Vishvakarma, the Vasus, the Pitris, all kinds of sacrificial libations, the four Vedas, namely Rig, Sama, Yaju and Atharva, all Sciences and branches of learning,

sn: इतिहासोपवेदाश्च वेदाङ्गानि च सर्वशः। ग्रहा यज्ञाश्च सोमश्च देवताचापि सर्वशः॥
en: Histories and all minor branches of learning, all the Vedangas, the Planets, the Sacrifices, the Soma, all the celestials,

sn: सावित्री दुर्गतरणी वाणी सप्तविधा तथा। मेधा धृतिः श्रुतिश्चैव प्रज्ञा बुद्धिर्यशः क्षमा॥
en: Savitri, the seven kinds of Speech, Understanding, Patience, Memory, Wisdom, Intelligence, Fame, Forgiveness,

sn: सामानि स्तुतिगीतानि गाथाश्च विविधास्तथा। भाष्याणि तर्कयुक्तानि देहवन्ति विशाम्पते।॥ नाटका विविधाः काव्याः कथाख्यायिककारिकाः। तत्र तिष्ठन्ति ते पुण्या ये चान्ये गुरुपूजकाः॥
en: The hymns of the Sama Veda, the Science of hymns, various kinds of verses and songs, various commentaries with arguments, various dramas, poems and stories, abridged glosses, these and other holy worshipers of Brahma, all in their personified forms, O king, stay there,

sn: क्षणा लवा मुहूर्ताश्च दिवारात्रिस्तथैव च। अर्धमासाश्च मासाश्च ऋतवः षट् च भारत॥ संवत्सराः पञ्च युगमहोरात्रश्चतुर्विधः। कालचक्रं च तद् दिव्यं नित्यमक्षयमव्ययम्॥ धर्मचक्रं तथा चापि नित्यमास्ते युधिष्ठिर। अदितिर्दितिर्दनुश्चैव सुरसा विनता इरा॥ कालिका सुरभी देवी सरमा चाथ गौतमी॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, O Yudhishthira, Kshanas, Lavas, Muhurattas (part of time), the day, the night, the fortnights, the months, the six seasons, the years, the Yugas, the four kinds of days. and nights, the eternal, indestructible, and undeteriorating, excellent Wheel of Time, the Wheel of Virtue, all of them stay there. Aditi, Diti, Danu, Shurasas, Vinata, Ira, Kalika, Shurabhidevi, Sarama, Gautami,

sn: प्रभा कश्च वै देव्यौ देवतानां च मातरः। रुद्राणी श्रीश्च लक्ष्मीश्च भद्रा षष्ठी तथापराः॥
en: Prabha, Kadru, all these goddesses, the mothers of the celestials, Rudrani, Sree, Lakshmi, Bhadra,

sn: पृथ्वी गां गता देवी ह्रीः स्वाहा कीतिरेव च। सुरा देवी शची चैव तथा पुष्टिररुन्धती॥ संवृत्तिराशा नियति: सृष्टिर्देवी रतिस्तथा। एताश्चान्याश्च वै देव्य उपतस्थुः प्रजापतिम्॥
en: Shashthi, the earth, Ganga, Hri, Svaha, Krita, Shura, Sachi, Pushti, Arundhati, Samvriti, Asha, Niyati, Srishti, Rati, these and other goddesses wait upon the Prajapati (Brahma).

sn: आदित्या वसवो रुद्रा मरुतश्चाश्विनावपि। विश्वेदेवाश्च साध्याश्च पितरश्च मनोजवाः॥
en: The Adityas, the Vasus, the Rudras, the Marutas, the Ashvinis, the Vishvadevas, the Sadhyas, the Pitris, all possessing the speed of mind, (wait upon the Grandsire).

sn: पितॄणां च गणान् विद्धि सप्तैव पुरुषर्षभ। मूर्तिमन्तो हि चत्वारस्त्रयश्चाप्यशरीरिणः॥
en: O best of men, know that there are seven classes of Pitris, of which four classes have embodied forms, the three remaining classes have no forms.

sn: वैराजाश्च महाभागा अग्निष्वात्ताश्च भारत। गार्हपत्या नाकचराः पितरो लोकविश्रुताः॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, it is well known amongst men that the illustrious Vairajas, Agnishvattas and Garhapatyas (three classes of the Pitris) roam in heaven.

sn: सोमपा एकशृङ्गाश्च चतुर्वेदाः कलास्तथा। एते चतुर्पु वर्णेषु पूज्यन्ते पितरो नृप।॥
en: O king, the Sompas, the Ekashringas, the Chaturvedas, and the Kalas (the four classes of the Pitris) are always worshipped amongst the four orders of men (namely Brahmanas, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas and Shudras).

sn: एतैराप्यायितैः पूर्वं सोमश्चाप्याय्यते पुनः। त एते पितरः सर्वे प्रजापतिमुपस्थिताः॥
en: Being first gratified by Soma, these (Pitris) gratify Soma next. All these Pitris wait upon the Prajapati.

sn: उपासते च संहृष्टा ब्रह्माणममितौजसम्। राक्षसाश्च पिशाचाश्च दानवा गुह्यकास्तथा॥
en: They cheerfully worship the immeasurably effulgent Brahma. The Rakshasas, the Pishachas, the Danavas, the Guhyakas,

sn: नागाः सुपर्णाः पशवः पितामहमुपासते। स्थावरा जङ्गमाश्चैव महाभूतास्तथापरे॥
en: The Nagas, the birds, the various other animals, all other mobile and immobile great beings, worship the Grandsire.

sn: पुरंदश्च देवेन्द्रो वरुणो धनदो यमः। महादेवः सहोमोऽत्र सदा गच्छति सर्वशः॥
en: The lord of the celestials, Purandara (Indra), Varuna, Kubera, Yama, Mahadeva with Uma (his wife), all often go there (to that Sabha).

sn: महासेनश्च राजेन्द्र सदोपास्ते पितामहम्। देवो नारायणस्तस्यां तथा देवर्षयश्च ये॥ ऋषयो बालखिल्याश्च योनिजायोनिचास्तथा। यच्च किंचित् त्रिलोकेऽस्मिन् दृश्यते स्थाणु जङ्गमम्। सर्वं तस्यां मया दृष्टमिति विद्धि नराधिप।॥
en: O king of kings, Mahasena also worship the Grandsire, know, O king, that Narayana himself, the celestials Rishis, the Rishis named Balkhilyas, all beings born of females or not born of females, nay whatever else is seen in the three worlds, mobile and immobile, were all seen by me there in that assembly-hall (of Brahma).

sn: अष्टाशीतिसहस्राणि ऋषीणामूर्ध्वरेतसाम्। प्रजावतां च पञ्चाशदृशीणामपि पाण्डव॥
en: O son of Pandu, eighty thousand Rishis who have gained complete control over their sexual passions, and fifty thousand Rishis who have begotten offspring were also seen by me there.

sn: ते स्म तत्र यथाकामं दृष्ट्वा सर्वे दिवौकसः। प्रणम्य शिरसा तस्मै सर्वे यान्ति यथाऽऽगतम्॥
en: All the dwellers of heaven see him (Brahma) there at their pleasure, and worshipping him by bowing down their heads all go back to the place from which they come.

sn: अतिथीनागतान् देवान् दैत्यान् नागांस्तथा द्विजान्। यक्षान् सुपर्णान् कालेयान् गन्धर्वाप्सरसस्तथा॥ महाभागानमितधीब्रह्मा लोकपितामहः। दयावान् सर्वभूतेषु यथार्ह प्रतिपद्यते॥ प्रतिगृह्य तु विश्वात्मा सवयम्भूरमितद्युतिः। सान्त्वमानार्थसम्भोगैर्युनक्ति मनुजाधिप॥
en: O king of men, the immeasurably intelligent Brahma, the Grandsire of all created things, the self-reacted Supreme Deity of immeasurable effulgence, is ever kind equally on all creatures, honours each as each deserves and gratifies with sweet speech gifts of wealth and other enjoyable things all those Devas, Daityas, the Nagas, the Yakshas, the Brahmanas, the birds, the Kaleyas, the Gandharvas, the Apsaras and all other illustrious beings that come to him as his guests.

sn: तथा तैरुपयातैश्च प्रतियद्भिश्च भारत। आकुला सा सभा तात भवति स्म सुखप्रदा॥
en: o descendant of Bharata, O child that charming Sabha is always being agitated with crowds of beings coming and going.

sn: सर्वतेजोमयी दिव्या ब्रह्मर्षिगणसेविता। ब्राझ्या श्रिया दीप्यमाना शुशुभे विगतक्लमा॥
en: Filled with every splendour and worshipped by the Brahmarshis, that celestials Sabha, the dispeller of all fatigue and misery, looks extremely beautiful, it being brightened with the wealth of Brahma.

sn: सा सभा तादृशी दृष्टा मया लोकेषु दुर्लभा। सभेयं राजशार्दूलं मनुष्येषु यथा तव॥
en: O best of kings, as your Sabha is matchless in the world of men, so is matchless in all the worlds that Sabha which was seen by me before.

sn: एता मया दृष्टपूर्वाः सभा देवेषु भारत। सभेयं मानुषे लोके सर्वश्रेष्ठतमा तव॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, I saw these Sabhas before in the region of the celestials. Your this Sabha is the foremost in the world of men.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच प्रायशो राजलोकस्ते कथितो वदतां वर। वैवस्वतसभायां तु यथा वदसि मे प्रभो॥
en: Yudhishthira said O best of eloquent men, O lord, from your descriptions it appears that all the monarchs (of the earth) are in the Sabha of the son of Vaivasvata (Yama).

sn: वरुणस्य सभायां तु नागास्ते कथिता विभो। दैत्येन्द्राश्चापि भूयिष्ठाः सरितः सागरास्तथा॥
en: O lord, you have said that in the Varuna's Sabha are the Nagas, the chief Daityas, the rivers, and the oceans,

sn: तथा धनपतेर्यक्षा गुह्यका राक्षसास्तथा। गन्धर्वाप्सरसश्चैव भगवांश्च वृषध्वजः॥
en: And in that of the lord of wealth (Kubera) the Yakshas, Guhyakas, Guhyakas, Rakshasas, Gandharvas, Apsaras, and the exalted Vishvadeva (Shiva).

sn: पितामहसभायां तु कथितास्ते महर्षयः। सर्वे देवनिकायाश्च सर्वशास्त्राणि चैव ह॥
en: You have said that in the Sabha of the Grandsire are the great Rishis, all the celestials, and all the Shastras.

sn: शक्रस्य तु सभायां तु देवाः संकीर्तिता मुने। उद्देशतश्च गन्धर्वा विविधाश्च महर्षयः॥
en: O Rishi, you have said that in the Sabha of Shakra (Indra) are the celestials, the Gandharvas and the various great Rishis.

sn: एक एव तु राजर्षिर्हरिश्चन्द्रो महामुने। कथितस्ते सभायां वै देवेन्द्रस्य महात्मनः॥
en: O great Rishi, you have said that one king namely the royal sage Harishchandra, is in the Sabha of the illustrious lord of the celestials.

sn: किं कर्म तेनाचरितं तपो वा नियतव्रतः। येनासौ सह शक्रेण स्पर्द्धते सुमहायशाः॥
en: What act, what asceticism, what steady vows were performed by that greatly famous (king) that he has alone become equal to Indra? are

sn: पितृलोकगतश्चैव त्वया विप्र पिता मम। दृष्टः पाण्डुर्महाभागः कथं वापि समागतः॥
en: O Brahmana, how did you meet with my father, the illustrious Pandu, now living in the region of the Pitris?

sn: किमुक्तवांश्च भगवंस्तन्ममाचक्ष्व सुव्रतः। त्वत्तः श्रोतुं सर्वमिदं परं कौतूहलं हि मे॥
en: O exalted one, O Rishi of excellent vows, what did he tell you? Tell me all. I am filled with great curiosity to hear all this.

sn: नारद उवाच यन्मां पृच्छसि राजेन्द्र हरिश्चन्द्रं प्रति प्रभो। तत् तेऽहं सम्प्रवक्ष्यामि माहात्म्यं तस्य धीमतः॥
en: Narada said O king of kings, O lord, I shall tell you all about the greatness of the greatly intelligent Harishchandra which you ask me to narrate.

sn: (इक्ष्वाकूणां कुले जातस्त्रिशङ्कुर्नाम पार्थिवः। अयोध्याधिपतिर्वीरो विश्वामित्रेण संस्थितः।। तस्य सत्यवती नाम पत्नी केकयवंशजा। तस्यां गर्भः समभवद् धर्मेण कुरुनन्दन॥ सा च काले महाभागा जन्ममासं प्रविश्य वै। कुमारं जनयामास हरिश्चन्द्रमकल्मषम्॥ वै राजा हरिश्चन्द्रस्त्रैशङ्कव इति स्मृतः।) स राजा बलवानासीत् सम्राट् सर्वमहीक्षिताम्। तस्य सर्वे महीपालाः शासनावनताः स्थिताः॥
en: That king (Harishchandra) was very powerful and an Emperor over all the monarchs of the earth. All the kings of the world were under his sway.

sn: तेनैकं रथमास्थाय जैत्रं हेमविभूषितम्। शस्त्रप्रतापेन जिता द्वीपाः सप्त जनेश्वर॥
en: O king of men, riding alone on his car adorned with gold, he conquered all the seven islands (of the world) by the prowess of his weapons.

sn: स निर्जित्यमहीं कृत्स्ना सशैलवनकाननाम्। आजहार महाराज राजसूयं महाक्रतुम्॥
en: O great king, having conquered the whole of the earth with her mountains, forests and woods, he made preparation to perform a great Rajasuya sacrifice.

sn: तस्य सर्वे महीपाला धनान्याजह्वराज्ञया। द्विजानां परिवेष्टारस्तस्मिन् यज्ञे च तेऽभवन्॥
en: All the monarchs at his command brought wealth to that sacrifice. They became the distributors of food to the Brahmanas in that sacrifice.

sn: प्रादाच्च द्रविणं प्रीत्या याचकानां नरेश्वरः। यथोक्तवन्तस्ते तस्मिंस्ततः पञ्चगुणाधिकम्॥
en: The king (Harishchandra) in that sacrifice cheerfully gave away to the sacrificial Brahmanas wealth five times more than what each asked.

sn: अतर्पयच्च विविधैर्वसुभिर्ब्राह्मणांस्तदा। प्रसर्पकाले सम्प्राप्ते नानादिग्भ्यः समागतान्॥
en: At the conclusion of the sacrifice, the king gratified the Brahmanas that assembled there from various quarters with large presents of various kinds of wealth.

sn: भक्ष्यभोज्यैश्च विविधैर्यथाकामपुरस्कृतैः। रत्नौघतर्पितैस्तुष्टैर्द्विजैश्च समुदाहृतम्। तेजस्वी च यशस्वी च नृपेभ्योऽभ्यधिकोऽभवत्॥
en: Having been gratified by various kinds of food and enjoyable things given to them to their fill and by the heaps of jewels distributed amongst them, the Brahmanas said: “The king Harishchandra has became superior to all the kings in energy and in renown".

sn: एतस्मात् कारणाद् राजन् हरिश्चन्द्रो विराजते। तेभ्यो राजसहस्रेभ्यस्तद् विद्धि भरतर्षभा॥
en: O king, O best of the Bharata race, know that for this reason, Harishchandra has shone more brightly than thousands of other kings.

sn: समाप्य च हरिश्चन्द्रो महायज्ञं प्रतापवान्। अभिषिक्तश्च शुशुभे साम्राज्येन नराधिप॥
en: O king, having concluded his great sacrifice, the mighty Harishchandra, being installed in his Empire, looked resplendent.

sn: ये चान्ये च महीपाला राजसूयं महाक्रतुम्। यजन्ते ते सहेन्द्रेण मोदन्ते भरतर्षभ।॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, all the kings that perform the great Rajasuya sacrifices pass their time in bliss in company with Indra.

sn: ये चापि निधनं प्राप्ताः संग्रामेष्वपलायिनः। ते तत् सदनमासाद्य मोदन्ते भरतर्षभ॥ ते
en: O best of the Bharata race, those kings, that give their lives on the field of battle without turning their backs, go to the abode (of Indra) and pass their time in felicity.

sn: तपसा ये च तीव्रण त्यजन्तीह कलेवरम्। तत् स्थानं समासाद्य श्रीमन्तो भान्ति नित्यशः॥२२
en: Those also that give up their lives after undergoing severe ascetic penances go to the same region and shine brightly there for ages.

sn: पिता च त्वाऽऽह कौन्तेय पाण्डुः कौरवनन्दन। हरिश्चन्द्रे श्रियं दृष्ट्वा नृपतौ जातविस्मयः॥
en: O son of Kunti, O descendant of Kuru, seeing the good fortune of Harishchandra and being much astonished at it, your father Pandu has told you something (through me).

sn: विज्ञाय मानुषं लोकमायान्तं मां नराधिप। प्रोवाच प्रणतो भूत्वा वदेथास्त्वं युधिष्ठिरम्॥
en: O king of men, knowing that I was coming to the world of men, he bowed to me and said, "Tell this to Yudhishthira,

sn: समर्थोऽसि महीं जेतुं भ्रातरस्ते स्थिता वशे। राजसूयं क्रतुश्रेष्ठमाहरस्वेति भारत॥
en: That he can subjugate the whole earth as his brothers are obedient to him". O descendant of Bharata, he said, “Let him perform the great Rajasuya sacrifice.

sn: त्वयीष्टवति पुत्रेऽहं हरिश्चन्द्रवदाशु वै। मोदिष्ये बहुलाः शश्वत् समाः शक्रस्य संसदि॥
en: He is my son, if he performs that sacrifice, I can go like Harishchandra to the region of Indra and pass my time there in everlasting bliss in company with Indra in his Sabha."

sn: एवं भवतु वक्ष्येऽहं तव पुत्रं नराधिपम्। भूलोकं यदि गच्छेयमिति पाण्डुमथाब्रवम्॥
en: O king, I told him thus (in reply), “If I go to the world of men, I shall speak to your son." I have told you what Pandu told me.

sn: पुरुषव्याघ्र संकल्पं कुरु पाण्डव। गन्तासि त्वं महेन्द्रस्य पूर्वैः सह सलोकताम्॥
en: O best of men, O son of Pandu, accomplish then the intentions of your father. If you do this, you will go with your ancestors to the region of Indra.

sn: तस्य त्वं बहुविघ्नश्च नृपते क्रतुरेष स्मृतो महान्। छिद्राण्यस्य तु वाञ्छन्ति यज्ञना ब्रह्मराक्षसाः॥
en: O king, it is said that this sacrifice is full of many obstacles. The Brahma Rakshasas who always harm sacrifices search for holes when this sacrifice is begun.

sn: युद्धं च क्षत्रशमनं पृथिवीक्षयकारणम्। किंचिदेव निमित्तं च भवत्यत्र क्षयावहम्॥
en: On the commencement of such a sacrifice a war may break out which may destroy the Kshatriyas, and which may be the cause of the total destruction of the whole world. A slight obstacle (to it) may cause the ruin of the whole earth.

sn: एतत् संचिन्त्य राजेन्द्र यत् क्षेमं तत् समाचर। अप्रमत्तोत्थितो नित्यं चातुर्वर्ण्यस्य रक्षणे॥
en: O king of kings, reflecting on all this, do what is beneficial to you. Be always watchful in protecting the four orders (of your subjects).

sn: भव एधस्व मोदस्व धनैस्तर्पय च द्विजान्। एतत् ते विस्तरेणोक्तं यन्मां त्वं परिपृच्छसि। आपृच्छे त्वां गमिष्यामि दाशार्हनगरी प्रति॥
en: Grow in prosperity, enjoy felicity gratify the Brahmans with wealth. I have thus answered in detail all that you have asked me. With your permission, I shall now go towards the city of the Dasharahas (Dwarka).

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमाख्याय पार्थेभ्यो नारदो जनमेजय। जगाम तैर्वृतो राजनृषिभिर्यैः समागतः॥
en: Vaishampayana said O Janamejaya, O king, having said this to the son of Pritha, Narada went away with those Rishis with whom he had come.

sn: गते तु नारदे पार्थो भ्रातृभिः सह कौरवः। राजसूयं क्रतुश्रेष्ठं चिन्तयामास पार्थिवः॥
en: O descendants of Kuru, on the departure of Narada, the King (Yudhishthira), the son of Pritha, began to think with his brothers (how to perform) that best of sacrifice Rajasuya.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ऋषेस्तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा निशश्वास युधिष्ठिरः। चिन्तयन् राजसूयेष्टिं न लेभे शर्म भारत॥
en: Vaishampayana said O descendant of Bharata, having heard these words of the Rishi (Narada) Yudhishthira heaved sight. Full of the thought of the Rajasuya, (sacrifice), the king did not get any peace of mind.

sn: राजर्षीणां च तं श्रुत्वा महिमानं महात्मनाम्। यज्वनां कर्मभिः पुण्यैर्लोकप्राप्ति समीक्ष्य च॥ हरिश्चन्द्रं च राजर्षि रोचमानं विशेषतः। यज्वानं यज्ञमाहर्तुं राजसूयमियेष सः॥
en: Having heard the glory of the illustrious kings of old and having known their acquisition of regions of felicity by the performance of sacrifices and scared deeds, and having also thought the great sacrifice performed by the royal sage Harishchandra, the king Yudhishthira desired to make preparations for the Rajasuya sacrifice.

sn: युधिष्ठिरस्ततः सर्वानर्चयित्वा सभासदः। प्रत्यर्चितश्च तैः सर्वैर्यज्ञायैव मनो दधे॥
en: Having worshipped all his Sabhasadas (counsellors and officers) and having been worshipped by them in return, he consulted with them about the sacrifice.

sn: स राजसूयं राजेन्द्र कुरूणामृषभस्तदा। आहर्तुं प्रवणं चक्रे मनः संचिन्त्य चासकृत्॥
en: O king of kings, having reflected much, the best of the Kurus, (Yudhishthira) resolved to make preparations to perform that sacrifice.

sn: भूयश्चाद्भुतवीर्यौजा धर्ममेवानुचिन्तयन्। किं हितं सर्वलोकानां भवेदिति मनो दधे॥
en: Reflecting upon virtue and righteousness, that king of wonderful energy and prowess set his heart to find out what should be beneficial to all his people.

sn: अनुगृह्णन् प्रजाः सर्वाः सर्वधर्मभृतां वरः। अविशेषेण सर्वेषां हितं चक्रे युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: The foremost of all virtuous men Yudhishthira, ever kind to all his subjects, always acted without any distinction for the good of all.

sn: सर्वेषां दीयतां देयं मुञ्चन् कोपमदावुभौ। साधु धर्मेति धर्मेति नान्यच्छ्रयेत भाषितम्॥
en: Dispelling all anger and vengeance he always said, “Give to each what each is to have.” The only sounds that could be heard (in his kingdom) were, "Blessed be Dharma, blessed be Dharma."

sn: एवंगते ततस्तस्मिन् पितरीवाश्वसञ्जनः। न तस्य विद्यते द्वेष्टा ततोऽस्याजातशत्रुता॥
en: Having thus conducted himself and having given every one paternal assurance, he had none in his kingdom who entertained any hostile feelings towards him. He therefore came to be called Ajatasatru (enemy-less).

sn: परिग्रहान्नरेन्द्रस्य भीमस्य परिपालनात्। शत्रूणां क्षपणाच्चैव बीभत्सोः सव्यसाचिनः॥
en: The king treated every one as if he was one of his own family; and Bhima ruled them all justly and impartially. Vibhatsu Savyasachi (Arjuna) by using both his hands protected all from their enemies.

sn: धीमतः सहदेवस्य धर्माणामनुशासनात्। वैनत्यात् सर्वतश्चैव नकुलस्य स्वभावतः। अविग्रहा वीतभयाः स्वधर्मनिरताः सदा॥
en: The intelligent Sahadeva administered justice with all impartiality, and Nakula treated all with humility which was natural to his character. (For all this the kingdom became) free from quarrels and fear of all kinds. All people were engaged in their respective works.

sn: निकामवर्षाः स्फीताश्च आसञ्जनपदास्तथा। वार्धषी यज्ञसत्त्वानि गोरक्षं कर्षणं वणिक्॥
en: The rains were as much as could be desired and the kingdom became full of prosperity. Persons living on usury, things necessary for sacrifices, cattle-rearing, tillage, and trades, all and everything grew in prosperity.

sn: विशेषात् सर्वमेवैतत् संजज्ञे राजकर्मणा। अनुकर्षं च निष्कर्ष व्याधिपावकमूर्च्छनम्॥
en: In consequence of the good deeds of the kings, there was in his kingdom no extortion, no oppression in the realisation of rents, and no fear of disease, of fire, of death by poisoning, and of incantations,

sn: सर्वमेव न तत्रासीद् धर्मनित्ये युधिष्ठिरे। दस्युभ्यो वञ्चकेभ्यश्च राज्ञः प्रति परस्परम्॥ राजवल्लभतश्चैव नाश्रूयत मृषा कृतम्। प्रियं कर्तुमुपस्थातुं बलिकर्म स्वकर्मजम्॥ अभिहर्तुं नृपाः षट्सु पृथग् जात्यैश्च नैगमैः। ववृधे विषयस्तत्र धर्मनित्ये युधिष्ठिरे॥
en: In consequence of Yudhishthira being ever devoted to virtue, it was never heard that thieves or cheats or royal favourites did not wrong towards one another. In consequence of Yudhishthira's devotion to virtue his tributary chiefs always waited upon him to render him good service on the six occasions (of war, treaty etc.); and the traders and merchants of different classes paid him their dues taxes liveable on their respective trades. Thus the kingdom grew in prosperity.

sn: कामतोऽप्युपयुञ्जानै राजसैलॊभजैर्जनैः। सर्वव्यापी सर्वगुणी सर्वसाहः सह सर्वराट्॥
en: The prosperity of the kingdom increased even by greatly voluptuous and luxurious persons. The king possessed every accomplishment and he bore every thing in patience. His sway extended over all.

sn: यस्मिन्नधिकृतः सम्राट् भ्राजमानो महायशाः। यत्र राजन् दश दिशः पितृतो मातृतस्तथा। अनुरक्ताः प्रजा आसन्नागोपाला द्विजातयः॥
en: O king whichever countries this renowned and the illustrious king conquered the people of them, from Brahmanas to peasants, were all more attached to him than to their own parents.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच स मन्त्रिणः समानाय भ्रातूंश्च वदतां वरः। राजसूयं प्रति तदा पुनः पुनरपृच्छत॥
en: That foremost of speakers (Yudhishthira) summoned together his brothers and ministers and asked them again and again about the Rajasuya sacrifice.

sn: ते पूच्छमानाः सहिता वचोऽर्थ्य मन्त्रिणस्तदा। युधिष्ठिरं महाप्राज्ञं यियक्षुमिदमब्रुवन्॥
en: Having been thus asked by the greatly wise Yudhishthira eager to perform the sacrifice, they spoke to him these words of grave import.

sn: येनाभिषिक्तो नृपतिर्वारुणं गुणमृच्छति। तेन राजापि तं कृत्स्नं सम्राङ्गुणमभीप्सति॥
en: The Ministers said A king already in possession of a kingdom wishes to acquire all the attributes of an emperor by means of the sacrifice, (Rajasuya) a sacrifice that helps to acquire the attributes of Varuna.

sn: तस्य सम्राङ्गुणार्हस्य भवतः कुरुनन्दन। राजसूयस्य समयं मन्यन्ते सुहृदस्तव।॥
en: O descendant of Kuru, you are worthy the attributes of an emperor; therefore your friends consider that the time has come for you to perform the Rajasuya sacrifice.

sn: तस्य यज्ञस्य समयः स्वाधीनः क्षत्रसम्पदा। साम्ना षडग्नयो यस्मिश्चीयन्ते शंसितव्रतैः॥
en: In consequence of your Kshatriya possessions, the time for the performance of that sacrifice has come, the sacrifice in which the Rishis of rigid vows establish the six fires with the Mantras of the Sama Veda.

sn: दर्वीहोमानुपादाय सर्वान् यः प्राप्नुते क्रतून्। अभिषेकं च यस्यान्ते सर्वजित् तेन चोच्यते॥
en: At the conclusion of a Rajasuya sacrifice, the performer is said to be installed in the sovereignty of an empire; he is then rewarded with the fruits of all sacrifices including the Agnihotra sacrifice. It is for this he is called the conqueror of all.

sn: समर्थोऽसि महाबाहो सर्वे ते वशगा वयम्। अचिरात् त्वं महाराज राजसूयमवाप्स्यसि॥
en: O mighty armed hero, O great king, you are quite capable of performing this sacrifice. We are all obedient to you. You will soon be able to perform the Rajasuya.

sn: अविचार्य महाराज राजसूये मनः कुरु। सर्वे पृथक् च सह चाब्रुवन्।॥
en: O great king, set your mind to perforin the Rajasuya without any further discussion." Vaishampayana said Thus spoke to the king all his friends and counsellors separately and together.

sn: इत्येवं सुहदः स धर्म्यं पाण्डवस्तेषां वचः श्रुत्वा विशाम्पते। धृष्टमिष्टं वरिष्ठं च जग्राह मनसारिहा॥
en: O king, having heard their these virtuous, bold, agreeable and weighty words, the son of Pandu (Yudhishthira), accepted them in is mind.

sn: श्रुत्वा सुहृद्वचस्तच्च जाश्चाप्यात्मनः क्षमम्। पुनः पुनर्मनो दधे राजसूयाय भारत॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, having heard these words of his friends and having known his own strength also, the king again thought in his mind about the Rajasuya.

sn: स भ्रातृभिः पुन/मानृत्विग्भिश्च महात्मभिः। मन्त्रिभिश्चापि सहितो धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः। धौम्यद्वैपायनाद्यैश्च मन्त्रयामास मन्त्रवित्॥
en: The intelligent Dharmaraja Yudhishthira, ever wise in counsel, again consulted with his brothers, with his ministers, his Ritvijas, his priest, Dhaumya and Dvaipayana and others.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच इयं या राजसूयस्य सम्राडर्हस्य सुक्रतोः। श्रद्दधानस्य वदतः स्पृहा मे सा कथं भवेत्॥
en: Yudhishthira said How can this Rajasuya sacrifice, which is worthy of an emperor and which my mind is desirous to perform, be accomplished only by my faith and speech?

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्तास्तु राजीवलोचन। इदमूचुर्वचः काले धर्मराज युधिष्ठिरम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said O lotus-eyed hero, having been thus asked by the king, they thus spoke to the Dharmaraja Yudhishthira at that time.

sn: अर्हस्त्वमसि धर्मज्ञ राजसूयं महाक्रतुम्। अथैवमुक्ते नृपतावृत्विग्भिर्ऋषिभिस्तथा॥
en: "O king, learned in the precepts of virtue, you are worthy of performing the great sacrifice of Rajasuya.” When the Ritvijas and the Rishis told these words.

sn: मन्त्रिणो भ्रातरश्चान्ये तद्वचः प्रत्यपूजयन्। स तु राजा महाप्राज्ञः पुनरेवात्मनाऽऽत्मवान्॥ ते तेन राज्ञा भूयो विममृशे पार्थो लोकानां हितकाम्यया। सामर्थ्ययोगं सम्प्रेक्ष्य देशकालौ व्ययागमौ॥
en: His ministers and his brothers highly approved of his words. The greatly wise and self-controlled son of Pritha (Yudhishthira), ever desirous to do good to the world, again thought over the matter in his mind, taking into his consideration his won strength and means, the time and the place, his income and expenditure.

sn: विमृश्य सम्यक् च धिया कुर्वन् प्राज्ञो न सीदति। न हि यज्ञसमारम्भः केवलात्मविनिश्चयात्॥
en: He knew that the wise never come to grief, because they always act after due deliberation, He thought that the sacrifice should not be commenced pursuant to his own resolution only.

sn: भवतीति समाज्ञाय यत्नतः कार्यमुद्वहन्। स निश्चयार्थ कार्यस्य कृष्णमेव जनार्दनम्॥
en: Carefully bearing on his shoulder the weight of affairs, he (Yudhishthira) thought of Krishna Janardana as the fittest person to decide the matter.

sn: सर्वलोकात् परं मत्वा जगाम मनसा हरिम्। अप्रमेयं महाबाहुं कामाज्जातमजं नृषु॥
en: knowing his (Krishna) to be the foremost of all persons, the possessor of immeasurable; energy, the mighty-armed, (hero), being without birth and was born among men only out of his pleasure, he (Yudhishthira) thought of Hari (Krishna) in his mind.

sn: पाण्डवस्तर्कयामास कर्मभिर्देवसम्मतैः। नास्य किंचिदविज्ञातं नास्य किंचिदकर्मजम्॥ न स किंचिन्न विषहेदिति कृष्णममन्यत। स तु तां नैष्ठिकी बुद्धिं कृत्वा पार्थो युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Having reflected upon his God-like feats, the son of Pandu (Yudhishthira) thought that there could be nothing unknown to him nothing unachievable by him and nothing that he could not bear. Having argued thus, he remembered Krishna. Having come to this settled conclusion, the of Pritha Yudhishthira.

sn: गुरुवद् भूतगुरवे प्राहिणोद् दूतमञ्जसा। शीघ्रगेन रथेनाशु स दूतः प्राप्य यादवान्॥
en: son Soon sent a messenger to that lord of all beings, sending through him (the messenger) blessings and agreeable words such as the elder should send to his younger. Riding on a swift car, that messenger soon reached the Yadavas.

sn: द्वारकावासिनं कृष्णं द्वारवत्यां समासदत्। धर्मनाकाक्षिणं पार्थं दर्शनाकाक्षयाच्युतः॥
en: He arrived at Dvaravati in which Dvaravati city Krishna was living. Having heard that the son of Pritha (Yudhishthira) was eager to see him, Achyuta (Krishna) also became eager to see him.

sn: इन्द्रसेनेन सहित इन्द्रप्रस्थमगात् तदा। व्यतीत्य विविधान् देशांस्त्वरावान् क्षिप्रवाहनः॥
en: Passing quickly through various countries on (the car yoked with his swift horses, he arrived at Indraprastha with Indrasena.

sn: इन्द्रप्रस्थगतं पार्थमभ्यगच्छज्जनार्दनः। स गृहे पितृवद् भ्रात्रा धर्मराजेन पूजितः। भीमेन च ततोऽपश्यत् स्वसारं प्रीतिमान् पितुः॥
en: Having arrived at Indraprastha, Janardana (Krishna) came to son of Pritha (Yudhishthira). He was worshipped by his cousin Dharmaraja (Yudhishthira) in his house with paternal affection.

sn: प्रीतः प्रीतेन सुहृदा रेमे स सहितस्तदा। अर्जुनेन यमाभ्यां च गुरुवत् पर्युपासितः॥ तं विश्रान्तं शुभे देशे क्षणिनं कल्पमच्युतम्। धर्मराजः समागम्याज्ञापयत् स्वप्रयोजनम्॥
en: He was also received by Bhima as affectionately. He then went cheerfully to see the sister of his father (Kunti). He was worshipped by the twins (Nakula and Sahadeva) their superiors. superiors. He then conversed with his friend Arjuna with joy; Arjuna was very glad to see him. Then when he had rested for sometime in that pleasant place and become fully refreshed, Yudhishthira came to him and spoke to him his business.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच प्रार्थितो राजसूयो मे न चासौ केवलेप्सया। प्राप्यते येन तत् ते हि विदितं कृष्ण सर्वशः॥
en: Yudhishthira said. O Krishna, I have desired to perform the Rajasuya sacrifice, but it cannot be performed as by my simply wishing to perform it. You know every thing by which it may be accomplished.

sn: यस्मिन् सर्वं सम्भवति यश्च सर्वत्र पूज्यते। यश्च सर्वेश्वरो राजा राजसूयं स विन्दति॥
en: He in whom every thing is possible he who is worshipped every where and he who is the king of all kings can alone perform this sacrifice.

sn: तं राजसूयं सुहृदः कार्यमाहुः समेत्य मे। तत्र मे निश्चिततमं तव कृष्ण गिरा भवेत्॥
en: O Krishna, my friends and ministers have said that I should perform it, but your words will be my guide in this matter.

sn: केचिद्धि सौहृदादेव न दोषं परिचक्षते। स्वार्थहेतोस्तथैवान्ये प्रियमेव वदन्त्युत॥
en: Some (counsellors) do not notice faults (difficulties) out of friendship. Some out of self interest say only that which will be agreeable to the hearer.

sn: प्रियमेव परीप्सन्ते केचिदात्मनि यद्धितम्। एवमप्रायाश्च दृश्यन्ते जनवादाः प्रयोजने॥
en: Some again consider that which is beneficial to them as the fittest thing to be adopted, Men are seen to advice thus in business.

sn: त्वं तु हेतूनतीत्यैतान् कामक्रोधौ व्युदस्य च। परमं यत् क्षमं लोके यथावद् वक्तुमर्हसि॥
en: You are above all motives; you have conquered anger and desire; you should tell me which is most beneficial to the world.

sn: कृष्ण उवाच सर्वैर्गुणैर्महाराज राजसूयं त्वमर्हसि। जानतस्त्वेव ते सर्वं किंचिद् वक्ष्यामि भारत॥
en: Krishna said O great king, you are endued with all accomplishments, and you are worthy of performing the Rajasuya. O descendant of Bharata, you know everything, (therefore) I shall tell you only something. were

sn: जामदग्न्येय रामेण क्षत्रं यदवशेषितम्। तस्मादवरजं लोके यदिदं क्षत्रसंज्ञितम्॥
en: The men now know as Kshatriyas are inferior to those Kshatriyas that exterminated by Rama, the son of Jamadagni.

sn: कृतोऽयं कुलसंकल्पः क्षत्रियैर्वसुधाधिप। निदेशवाग्भिस्तत् ते ह विदितं भरतर्षभ॥
en: O lord of earth, O best of the Bharata race, you are aware of the rules that those Kshatriyas established amongst their order, guided by the traditions (coming down from generations to generations).

sn: ऐलस्येक्ष्वाकुवंशस्य प्रकृतिं परिचक्षते। राजानः श्रेणिबद्धाश्च तथान्ये क्षत्रिया भुवि॥
en: All the numerous royal dynasties and other Kshatriyas in the world claim to be descended from Aila and Ikshaku,

sn: ऐलवंश्याश्च ये राजंस्तथैवेक्ष्वाकवो नृपाः। तानि चैकशतं विद्धि कुलानि भरतर्षभ।॥
en: O king, O best of the Bharata race the monarchs (the descendants) of Aila and those of Ikshaku became divided into one hundred separate dynasties.

sn: ययातेस्त्वेव भोजानां विस्तरो गुणतो महान्। भजतेऽद्य महाराज विस्तरं स चतुर्दिशम्॥
en: O great king, the descendants of Yayati and the Bhoja are also great in birth number and accomplishments. They are scattered in all directions.

sn: तेषां तथैव तां लक्ष्मी सर्वक्षत्रमुपासते। इदानीमेव वै राजञ्जरासंधो महीपतिः॥
en: O king, all the Kshatriyas worship the wealth and prosperity of all these kings. At the present time the king Jarasandha,

sn: अभिभूय श्रियं तेषां कुलानामभिषेचितः। स्थितो मूर्ध्नि नरेन्द्राणामोजसाऽऽक्रम्य सर्वशः॥
en: Having overcome that prosperity ever revered by the whole (Kshatriya) order, and also having overcome them by his prowess, has set himself up over the heads of all the kings.

sn: सोऽवनिं मध्यामां भुक्त्वा मिथोभेदममन्यत। प्रभुर्यस्तु परो राजा यस्मिन्नेकवशे जगत्॥ स साम्राज्यं महाराज प्राप्तो भवति योगतः। तं स राजा जरासंधं संश्रित्य किल सर्वशः॥ राजन् सेनापतिर्जातः शिशुपालः प्रतापवान्। तमेव च महाराज शिष्यवत् समुपस्थितः॥ वक्रः करूषाधिपतिर्मायायोधी महाबलः। अपरौ च महावीरों महात्मानौ समाश्रितौ॥
en: Enjoying the sovereignty of the middle portion of thirteenth, he tried to create disunion among ourselves. O great-king, the monarch, who is the lord of all kings and whose sway extends over the whole earth, is the proper person to be an Emperor. O king, the powerful Shisupala having every way placed himself under his protection, has become his commander-in-chief. great king, the powerful king of the Karushas, Vakra, who fight with the power of illusion, also waits upon him as his disciple. The two other greatly powerful and illustrious monarchs have taken the protection.

sn: जरासंधं महावीर्यं तौ हंसडिम्भकावुभौ। दन्तवक्रः करूषश्च करभो मेघवाहनः। मूर्धा दिव्यमणिं बिभ्रद् यमद्भुतमणि विदुः॥
en: Of the greatly powerful Jarasandha, namely Hansa and Dimbhaka. Dantavakra, Karusha, Karabha (also wait upon Jarasandha). He who bears on his head the gem which is knows as the most wonderful gem in the world.

sn: मुरं च नरकं चैव शास्ति यो यवनाधिपः। अपर्यन्तबलो राजा प्रतीच्यां वरुणो यथा।॥
en: That king of the Yavanas who is chastised Mura and Naraka and who is the matchlessly powerful king of the west like a (second) Varuna.

sn: भगदत्तो महाराज वृद्धस्तव पितुः सखा। स वाचा प्रणतस्तस्य कर्मणा च विशेषतः॥
en: O great king, who is called Bhagadatta and who was your father's old friend, has also lowered his head (to Jarasandha) by his speech and specially by his acts.

sn: स्नेहबद्धश्च मनसा पितृवद् भक्तिमांस्त्वयि। प्रतीच्या दक्षिणं चान्तं पृथिव्याः प्रति यो नृपः॥
en: But he is in his heart tied to you by affection. He loves you as a father loves his son. The king, who has his kingdom on the west and south of the earth,

sn: मातुलो भवतः शूरः पुरुजित् कुन्तिवर्धनः। स ते सन्नतिमानेकः स्नेहतः शत्रुसूदनः॥
en: Who is your maternal uncle, that heroic Purujit, the spreader of the Kunti race, that chastiser of foes, is the only one king who is on your side.

sn: जरासंधं गतस्त्वेव पुरा यो न मया हतः। पुरुषोत्तमविज्ञातो योऽसौ चेदिषु दुर्मतिः॥ आत्मानं प्रतिजानाति लोकेऽस्मिन् पुरुषोत्तमम्। आदत्ते सततं मोहाद् यः स चिह्नं च मामकम्॥
en: That wicked wreath amongst the Chedis, whom I did not kill before, who has become known in the world as the Supreme Being, who gives himself out as such and who out of foolishness always bears all my signs, has gone over to the side of Jarasandha.

sn: वङ्गपुण्ड्रकिरातेषु राजा बलसमन्वितः। पौण्ड्रको वासुदेवेति योऽसौ लोकेऽभिविश्रुतः॥
en: The powerful king of Vanga, Pundra and the Kiratas who is known by the name of Pundraka and Vasudeva, (also waits upon Jarasandha).

sn: चतुर्थभाग महाराज भोज इन्द्रसखो बली। विद्याबलाद् यो व्यजयत् सपाण्ड्यक्रथकैशिकान्॥२१ भ्राता यस्याकृतिः शूरो जामदग्न्यसमोऽभवत्। स भक्तो मागधं राजा भीष्मकः परवीरहा।॥
en: O great king, that mighty king of the Bhojas, Bhishmaka, who is a friend of Indra, that chastiser of foes, who governs a fourth part of the world, who has conquered by his learning the Pandayas and Krathakaishikas, and whose brother Atri is like the son of Jamadagni Rama has (also) become a servitor to the king of Magadha (Jarasandha).

sn: प्रियाण्याचरतः प्रह्वान् सदा सम्बन्धिनस्ततः। भजतो न भजत्यस्मानप्रियेषु व्यवस्थितः॥
en: We are his (Bhishmaka's) relatives and therefore, we are always engaged in doing what is agreeable to him. But though we respect and regard him much yet he doesn't at all regard us. He is always doing us ill.

sn: न कुलं स बलं राजन्नभ्यजानात् तथाऽऽत्मनः। एश्यमानो यशो दीप्तं जरासंधमुपस्थितः॥
en: O king, without knowing his own strength and the dignity of the race to which he belongs, he (Bhishmaka) has placed himself under Jarasandha's shelter only seeing his blazing fame.

sn: उदीच्याश्च तथा भोजाः कुलान्यष्टादश प्रभो। जरासंधभयादेव प्रतीची दिशमास्थिताः॥ शूरसेना भद्रकारा बोधाः शाल्वाः पटच्चराः। सुस्थलाश्च सुकुटाश्च कुलिन्दाः कुन्तिभिः सह॥
en: O lord, the eighteen tribes of the Bhojas from the fear of Jarasandha, have fled to the west; so also have fled the Shurasenas, the Bhadrakas, the Bodhas, the Shalvas, the patachharas, the Susthalas the Sukuttas, the Kulindas and the Kuntis.

sn: शाल्वायनाश्च राजानः सोदर्यानुचरैः सह। दक्षिणाये च पञ्चालाः पूर्वाः कुन्तिषु कोशलाः॥ तथोत्तरां दिशं चापि परित्यज्य भयार्दिताः। मत्स्याः संन्यस्तपादाश्च दक्षिणां दिशमाश्रिताः॥
en: The kings of the Shalvayana, with their brothers and followers, the southern Panchalas and the eastern Kosalas have also fled to the country of the Kuntis. So also the Matsyas and the Samyastapadas have left their kingdoms in the north and have all fled from fear to the Southern country.

sn: तथैव सर्वपञ्चाला जरासंधभयार्दिताः। स्वराज्यं सम्परित्यज्य विद्रुताः सर्वतो दिशम्॥
en: Afflicted with the fear of Jarasandha all the Panchalas have left their own Kingdoms and fled in all directions.

sn: कस्यचित् त्वथ कालस्य कंसो निर्मथ्य यादवान्। बार्हद्रथसुते देव्यावुपागच्छद् वृथामतिः॥
en: Sometime before, the foolish minded Kansa, having persecuted the Yadavas married two of the daughters of the son of Brihadratha (Jarasandha).

sn: अस्तिः प्राप्तिश्च नाम्ना ते सहदेवानुजेऽबले। बलेन तेन स्वज्ञातीनभिभूय वृथामतिः॥
en: They are named Asti and Prapti and they are the sisters of Sahadeva. Strengthened by such an alliance, the fool (Kansa) persecuted his relatives and gained an ascendancy over them all.

sn: श्रेष्ठ्यं प्राप्तः स तस्यासीदतीवापनयो महान्। भोजराजन्यवृद्धैश्च पीड्यमानैर्दुरात्मना॥
en: By his such acts he earned a very bad repute. The wicked wretch persecuted the old chiefs of the Bhoja race.

sn: ज्ञातित्राणमभीप्सद्भिरस्मत्सम्भावना कृता। दत्त्वाक्रूराय सुतनुं तामाहुकसुतां तदा॥
en: These chiefs sought our protection from the persecution of their relative (Kansa). Having bestowed upon Akrura the beautiful daughter of Ahuka, Satrinka.

sn: संकर्षणद्वितीयेन ज्ञातिकार्यं मया कृतम्। हतौ कंससुनामानौ मया रामेण चाप्युत॥
en: I did a service to my relatives. Making Samkarasiana (Baladeva) my second, I killed both Kansa and Sunama with the assistance of Rama.

sn: भये तु समतिक्रान्ते जरासंधे समुद्यते। मन्त्रोऽयं मन्त्रितो राजन् कुलैरष्टादशावरैः॥
en: O king, though the immediate cause of our fear was thus removed, yet Jarasandha (Kansa's father-in-law) took up arms. We eighteen branches of the Yadavas consulted together;

sn: अनारभन्तो निघ्नन्तो महास्त्रैः शत्रुघातिभिः। न हन्यामो वयं तस्य त्रिभिर्वर्षशतैर्बलम्॥
en: And we came to the conclusion that even if we continually strike at our enemy with weapons capable of killing the foe, we shall not be able to do any thing of him in three hundred years.

sn: तस्य ह्यमरसंकाशौ बलेन बलिनां वरौ। नामभ्यां हंसडिष्भकावशस्त्रनिधनावुभौ॥ तावुभौ सहितौ वीरौ जरासंधश्च वीर्यवान्। त्रयस्त्रयाणां लोकानां पर्याप्ता इति मे मतिः॥
en: He had two friends, who were like the two immortals; and they were as powerful as the foremost men of all powerful men. They were named Hansa and Dimbhaka who were incapable of being slain by any weapons. When the powerful Jarasandha was united with them, he was incapable of being defeated by the weapons of all the world. This was my opinion.

sn: न हि केवलमस्माकं यावन्तोऽन्ये च पार्थिवाः। तथैव तेषामासीच्च बुद्धिर्बुद्धिमतां वर॥
en: O foremost of all intelligent men, this was not only our opinion, but all the other kings were of the same opinion.

sn: अथ हंस इति ख्यातः कश्चिदासीन्महान् नृपः। रामेण स हतस्तत्र संग्रामेऽष्टादशावरे॥
en: There was a great king named Hansa, he was killed by Rama in a battle which lasted for eighteen days.

sn: हतो हंस इति प्रोक्तमथ केनापि भारत। तच्छ्रुत्वा डिम्भको राजन् यमुनाम्भस्यमज्जत॥ विना हंसेन लोकेऽस्मिन् नाहं जीवितुमुत्सहे। इत्येतां मतिमास्थाय डिम्भको निधनं गतः॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, O king, hearing people say that Hansa had been killed, Dimbhaka thought that he could not live without Hansa. He went to the Yamuna, jumped into its water and thus killed himself.

sn: तथा तु डिम्भकं श्रुत्वा हंसः परपुरंजयः। प्रपेदे यमुनामेव सोऽपि तस्यां न्यमज्जत॥
en: Thereupon when that subjugator of hostile cities, Hansa heard what Dimbhaka had done, he too went to the Yamuna, jumped into its water and drowned himself.

sn: तौ स राजा जरासंधः श्रुत्वा च निधनं गतौ। पुरं शून्येन मनसा प्रययौ भरतर्षभ॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, when Jarasandha heard of the death of the two heroes, he returned to his city with an empty heart.

sn: ततो वयममित्रघ्न तस्मिन् प्रतिगते नृपे। पुनरानन्दिनः सर्वे मथुरायां वसामहे॥
en: O slayer of all foes, on the departure of the King (Jarasandha), we were filled with great joy, and we continued to live at Mathura.

sn: यदा त्वभ्येत्य पितरं सा वै राजीवलोचना। कंसभार्या जरासंधं दुहिता मागधं नृपम्। चोदयत्येव राजेन्द्र पतिव्यसनदुःखिता॥ पतिनं मे जहीत्येवं पुनः पुनररिंदम। ततो वयं महाराज तं मन्त्रं पूर्वमन्त्रितम्॥
en: But when the wife of Kansa and the daughter of Jarasandha, that lotus-eyed lady (Prapti) went to her father lamenting for the death of her husband, and when, O king, she again and again urged the king of Magadha, saying, “O chastiser of foes, kill the murderer of my husband," then, O great king, we thought of acting according to the conclusion we came to before.

sn: संस्मरन्तो विमनसो व्यपयाता नराधिप। पृथक्त्वेन महाराज संक्षिप्य महतीं श्रियम्॥ पलायामो भयात् तस्य ससुतज्ञातिबान्धवाः। इति संचिन्त्य सर्वे स्म प्रतीची दिशमाश्रिताः॥
en: We became exceedingly cheerless and we became ready to fly. We divided our great wealth into small portions to make it portable. We then fled from the fear of Jarasandha with out sons, cousins and relatives. After reflecting thus over every thing, we flew towards the west.

sn: कुशस्थली पुरीं रम्यां रैवतेनोपशोभिताम्। ततो निवेशं तस्यां च कृतवन्तो वयं नृप॥
en: O king, there is a charming city, named Kushasthali, adorned by the adorned by the Raivatake (mountain). In this city we took up our abode.

sn: तथैव दुर्गसंस्कारं देवैरपि दुरासदम्। स्त्रियोऽपि यस्यां युध्येयुः किमु वृष्णिमहारथाः॥
en: We repaired its fort and made it so strong that it became impregnable even to the celestialss. Even women could fight from within it, not to speak of the great car-warriors of the Vrishni race.

sn: तस्यां वयममित्रघ्न निवसामोऽकुतोभयाः। आलोच्य गिरिमुख्यं तं मागधं तीर्णमेव च॥ माधवाः कुरुशार्दूलं परां मुदमवाप्नुवन्। एवं वयं जरासंधादभितः कृतकिल्बिधाः॥
en: O slayer of all foes, we are now living in that city without fear of any kind. O best of the Kuru race, thinking of the inaccessibility of that foremost of hills (Raivataka), and considering that they had no longer any fear of Jarasandha, the descendants of Madhu (Yadavas) have become exceedingly glad.

sn: सामर्थ्यवन्तः सम्बन्धाद् गोमन्तं समुपाश्रिताः। त्रियोजनायतं सद्म त्रिस्कन्धं योजनावधि॥
en: Though we were capable of defending ourselves (from the attacks of Jarasandha), yet we have taken shelter on the Gomanta mountain which is three Yojanas in length. Within its each Yojana have been placed twenty one posts of armed men.

sn: योजनान्ते शतद्वारं वीरविक्रमतोरणम्। अष्टादशावरैर्नद्धं क्षत्रियैर्युद्धदुर्मदैः॥
en: At the intervals of each Yojana have been made one hundred gates, the heroism of the Vrishni heroes are the arches of these gates. They are always) protected by the heroes of the eighteen branches of the Yadavas.

sn: अष्टादश सहस्राणि भ्रातृणां सन्ति नः कुले। आहुकस्य शतं पुत्रा एकैकस्त्रिदशावरः॥
en: There are eighteen thousand brothers and cousins in our race. Ahuka has been hundred sons, each of whom is like the best of the celestialss.

sn: चारुदेष्णः सह भ्रात्रा चक्रदेवोऽथ सात्यकिः। अहं च रौहिणेयश्च साम्बः प्रद्युम्न एव च॥
en: Charudeshna with his brother Chakradeva, Satyaki, myself, the son of Rohini(Baladeva), Samba, as heroic as myself.

sn: एवमतिरथाः सप्त राजन्नन्यान् निबोध मे। कृतवर्मा ह्यनाधृष्टिः समीकः समिर्तिजयः॥
en: O king, these seven are Atirathas, Besides these there are others, whom I shall (Presently) mention. Kritavarma, Anadhrishti, Samika, Samitinajaya.

sn: कङ्कः शङ्कुच कुन्तिश्च सप्तैते वै महारथाः। पुत्रौ चान्धकभोजस्य वृद्धो राजा च ते दश॥
en: Kanka, Shanku, Kunti these seven are Maharathas. The old king Andhakabhoja has two sons, and the king himself, these ten (arc Maharathas).

sn: वज्रसंहनना वीरा वीर्यवन्तो महारथाः। स्मरन्तो मध्यमं देशं वृष्णिमध्ये व्यवस्थिताः॥
en: Possessing great prowess, all these heroes are as mighty as the thunderbolt. These Maharathas, choosing the middle country, now live among the Vrishnis.

sn: स त्वं सम्राड्गुणैर्युक्तः सदा भरतसत्तम। क्षत्रे सम्राजमात्मानं कर्तुमर्हसि भारत॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, O descendant of Bharata, you alone are worthy of becoming an emperor. You should establish your empire over all Kshatriyas.

sn: न तु शक्यं जरासंधे जीवमाने महाबले। राजसूयस्त्वयावाप्तुमेषा राजन् मतिर्मम॥
en: O king, but it is my opinion that you will not be able to perform the Rajasuya (Sacrifice), so long the greatly powerful Jarasandha remains alive.

sn: तेन रुद्धा हि राजानः सर्वे जित्वा गिरिव्रजे। कन्दरे पर्वतेन्द्रस्य सिंहनेव महाद्विपाः॥
en: Many kings have been kept imprisoned in Girivraja(his city), as dead carcasses of elephants are kept in the cave of a great mountains by the lion.

sn: स हि राजा जरासंधो यियक्षुर्वसुधाधिपैः। महादेवं महात्मानमुमापतिमरिंदम॥ आराध्य तपसोग्रेण निर्जितास्तेन पार्थिवाः। प्रतिज्ञायाश्च पारं स गतः पार्थिवसत्तम॥
en: Chastiser of foes, having been desirous of performing a great sacrifice by (offering) kings (to the sacrificial fire), the king Jarasandha, has adored with fierce ascetic penances the illustrious god of gods, the husband of Uma (Shiva). He has by this means been able to defeat many kings of the earth and to fulfill his VOW.

sn: स हि निर्जित्य निर्जित्य पार्थिवान् पृतनागतान्। पुरमानीय बद्धवा च चकार पुरुषव्रजम्॥
en: By defeating all the kings, one after the other and their soldiers, he has brought them all as prisoners to his city; and he has thus daily swelled the crowd (of kings).

sn: वयं चैव महाराज जरासंधभयात् तदा। मथुरां सम्परित्यज्य गता द्वारवतीं पुरीम्॥
en: O great kings, we too from the fear of Jarasandha left Mathura and fled to the city of Dvaravati.

sn: यदि त्वेनं महाराज यज्ञं प्राप्तुमभीप्ससि। यतस्व तेषां मोक्षाय जरासंधवधाय च॥
en: O great king, if you desire to perform the sacrifice, try to release those (the kings) kept prisoners by Jarasandha and try to kill him.

sn: समारम्भो न क्योऽयमन्यथा कुरुनन्दन। राजसूयश्च कात्स्येंन कर्तुं मतिमतां वर॥
en: O descendant of Kuru, O foremost of all intelligent men, if you do not try to do it, your undertaking can never be successful. If you wish to perform Rajasuya (sacrifice), you must do it.

sn: इत्येषा मे मती राजन् यथा वा मन्यसेऽनघ। एवंगते ममाचक्ष्व स्वयं निश्चित्य हेतुभिः॥
en: O king, O sinless one, this is my opinion. Do as you think (proper)after reflecting over everything, nothing the causes and effects of all. Tell us what you yourself think proper to do.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच उक्तं त्वया बुद्धिमता यन्नान्यो वक्तुमर्हति। संशयानां हि निर्मोक्ता त्वन्नान्यो विद्यते भुवि॥
en: Yudhishthira said Intelligent as you are, you have said what none else is capable of saying. There is none else in the world but you who can settle all doubts.

sn: गृहे गृहे हि राजानः स्वस्य स्वस्य प्रियंकराः। न च साम्राज्यमाप्तास्ते सम्राट्छन्दो हि कृच्छ्रभाक्॥
en: There are kings in every province engaged in doing good to their respective selves. But none of them has been able to become an Emperor. The title of Emperor is difficult to be achieved.

sn: कथं परानुभावज्ञः स्वं प्रशंसितुमर्हति। परेण समवेतस्तु यः प्रशस्यः स पूज्यते॥
en: He who knows the velour and the strength of others never applauds himself. He is really worthy of praise who even in fighting with his enemies bear himself with all commendation.

sn: विशाला बहुला भूमिर्बहुरत्नसमाचिता। दूरं गत्वा विजानाति श्रेयो वृष्णिकुलोद्वह॥
en: O supporter of the Vrishni dignity, man's desires and propensities are varied and extensive like the wide earth adorned with various gems and jewels. As by travelling in distant places experiences is gained, so man can get the highest good by the highest culture of his understanding.

sn: शममेव परं मन्ये शमात् क्षेमं भवेन्मम। आरम्भे पारमेष्ठ्ये तु न प्राप्यमिति मे मतिः॥
en: I consider peace of mind as the highest quality, for from peace of mind proceeds prosperity. In my opinion, if I undertake to perform this sacrifice, I shall not win the highest reward.

sn: एवमेते हि जानन्ति कुले जाता मनस्विनः। कश्चित् कदाचिदेतेषां भवेच्छ्रेष्ठो जनार्दन॥
en: O Janardana, these intelligent and powerful men born in our race think that one amongst them will at one time become the foremost man amongst all the Kshatriyas.

sn: वयं चैव महाभाग जरासंधभयात् तदा। शङ्किताः स्म महाभाग दौरात्म्यात् तस्य चानघ॥ अहं हि तव दुर्द्धर्ष भुजवीर्याश्रयः प्रभो। नात्मानं बलिनं मन्ये त्वयि तस्माद् विशङ्किते॥
en: But, O exalted one, O sinless being, we also were all alarmed at the prowess and the wickedness of the king Jarasandha, O hero, invincible in battle, O lord, the prowess of your arms in our refuge. When you are alarıned at Jarasandha's might, how should I consider my self strong (enough to cope with him)?

sn: त्वत्सकाशाच्च रामाच्च भीमसेनाच्च माधव। अर्जुनाद् वा महाबाहो हन्तुं शक्यो न वेति वै। एवं जानन् हि वार्ष्णेय विमृशामि पुनः पुनः॥ त्वं मे प्रमाणभूतोऽसि सर्वकार्येषु केशव। तच्छ्रुत्वा चाब्रवीद् भीमो वाक्यं वाक्यविशारदः॥
en: O Madhava, O descendant of the Vrishni race, I have often become dispersed at the thought whether Jarasandha is at all capable of being killed by you, by Rama, or by Arjuna. O Keshava, what shall I say? You are my highest authority in everything. Having heard this, the able speaker Bhima then spoke these words:

sn: भीम उवाच अनारम्भपरो राजा वल्मीक इव सीदति। दुर्बलश्चानुपायेन बलिनं योऽधितिष्ठति॥
en: Bhima said The king, who is without any exertion, or the king who being himself weak and without resources, enter into hostility with one who is strong, perishes like an anthill.

sn: अतन्द्रितश्च प्रायेण दुर्बलो बलिनं रिपुम्। जयेत् सम्यक् प्रयोगेण नीत्यार्थानात्मनो हितान्॥
en: It is often seen that even weak king may defeat a strong enemy; and he may be come successful in his attempts by his wakefulness and by using policy.

sn: कृष्णे नयो मयि बलं जयः पार्थे धनञ्जये। मागधं साधयिष्याम इष्टिं त्रय इवाग्नयः॥
en: (We have) in Krishna policy, in me strength, and in Partha (Dhananjaya) victory. Like the three (sacrificial) fires, we shall bring about the death of the king of Magadha (Jarasandha)

sn: कृष्ण उवाच अर्थानारभते बालो नानुबन्धमवेक्षते। तस्मादरिं न मृष्यन्ति बालमर्थपरायणम्॥
en: Krishna said Men of immature understanding begin an act without having an eye to what may happen in future. It is, therefore, not a self-seeking enemy with immature understanding is ever forgiven by a sensible man.

sn: जित्वा जय्यान् यौवनाश्विः पालनाच्च भगीरथः। कार्तवीर्यस्तपोवीर्याद् बलात्तु भरतो विभुः॥ ऋद्ध्या मरुत्तस्तान् पञ्च सम्राजस्त्वनुशुश्रुम। साम्राज्यमिच्छतस्ते तु सर्वाकारं युधिष्ठिर।॥ निग्राह्यलक्षणं प्राप्तिर्धर्मार्थनयलक्षणैः॥
en: It has been heard by us that in the Satya Yuga, Yuvanashva brought every one under his sway, by the remission of taxes, Bhagiratha by kind treatment of his subjects, Kartavirya by his great asceticism, the lord Bharata by his extra ordinary prowess and Maruta by his prosperity, and thus they became emperors. O Yudhishthira, you who wish to acquire the imperial dignity, have the above mentioned) five qualities.

sn: बार्हद्रथो जरासंधस्तद् विद्धि भरतर्षभ। न चैनमनुरुद्ध्यन्ते कुलान्येकशतं नृपाः। तस्मादिह बलादेव साम्राज्यं कुरुते हि सः॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, the son of Brihadratha, Jarasandha, is (also) one such (a candidate for the imperial dignity). One hundred families of kings have failed to oppose him.

sn: रत्नभाजो हि राजानो जरासंधमुपासते। न च तुष्यति तेनापि वाल्यादनयमास्थितः॥
en: He is ruling over an empire by his own great prowess. The monarchs that wear jewels wait upon and worship Jarasandha. Wicked from his childhood, he is not satisfied even such worship.

sn: मूर्धाभिषिक्तं नृपतिं प्रधानपुरुषो बलात्। आदत्ते न च नो हृष्टोऽभागः पुरुषतः क्वचित्॥
en: Having become the foremost of all be attacks with force the kings that wear crowns. There is not to be found a single king who does not pay tributes to him.

sn: एवं सर्वान् वशे चक्रे जरासंधः शतावरान्। तं दुर्बलतरो राजा कथं पार्थ उपैष्यति॥
en: O son of Pritha, thus has be brought under his sway one hundred kings. How can then a weak king approach him with hostile intentions?

sn: प्रोक्षितानां प्रमृष्टानां राज्ञां पशुपतेर्गृहे। पशूनामिव का प्रीतिर्जीविते भरतर्षभ॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, kept as they are prisoners in the temple of Shiva like so many animals to be offered to the sacrifice, do not these kings feel the greatest possible misery?

sn: क्षत्रियः शस्त्रस्मरणो यदा भवति सत्कृतः। ततः स्म मागधं संख्ये प्रतिबाधेम यद् वयम्॥
en: A Kshatriya who is killed by weapons (on the field of battle) is ever considered to be blessed. Why shall we not then assemble together and oppose the king of Magadha?

sn: षडशीतिः समानीताः शेषा राजश्चतुर्दश। जरासंधेन राजानस्ततः क्रूरं प्रवय॑ते॥
en: He has already brought under his sway eighty-six kings, only fourteen (more) are wanted to make the number of one hundred complete. As soon as he will collect them (the fourteen others), he will begin his cruel act(sacrificing them before Shiva).

sn: प्राप्नुयात् स यशो दीप्तं तत्र यो विघ्नमाचरेत्। जयेद् यश्च जरासंधं स सम्रानियतं भवेत्॥
en: He, who will be able to prevent him from doing this act, will surely earn blazing fame. He, who will defeat Jarasandha, will certainly become the emperor of all the world.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच सम्राङ्गणमभीप्सन् वै युष्मान् स्वार्थपरायणः। कथं प्रहिणुयां कृष्ण सोऽहं केवलसाहसात्॥
en: Yudhishthira said O Krishna, depending only on courage, how can I send you (to Jarasandha) out of selfish motives and out of the desire of the imperial dignity?

sn: भीमार्जुनावुभौ नेत्रे मनो मन्ये जनार्दनम्। मनश्चक्षुर्विहीनस्य कीदृशं जीवितं भवेत्॥
en: I consider Bhima and Arjuna as my eyes and you Jarasandha as my mind. How shall I able to live without my eyes and mind?

sn: जरासन्धबलं प्राप्य दुष्पारं भीमविक्रमम्। यमोऽपि न विजेताऽऽजौ तत्र वः किं विचेष्टितम्॥
en: Even Yama cannot defeat the powerful army of Jarasandha who himself is endued with terrible velour. What velour can you show against him?

sn: अस्मिंस्त्वर्थान्तरे युक्तमनर्थः प्रतिपद्यते। तस्मान्न प्रतपत्तिस्तु कार्या युक्ता मता मम॥
en: This affair that promises to terminate Otherwise may lead to a great mischief. It is my opinion, therefore, that the proposed task should not be undertaken.

sn: यथाहं विमृशाम्येकस्तत् तावच्छूयतां मम। संन्यासं रोचये साधु कार्यस्यास्य जनार्दन। प्रतिहन्ति मनो मेऽद्य राजसूयो दुराहरः॥
en: O Jarasandha, O excellent man, listen to what I think. To desist from this act seems to be beneficial to me. My heart is full of misery to-day. The Rajasuya sacrifice seems to me very difficult to be accomplished.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच पार्थः प्राप्य धनुः श्रेष्ठमक्षय्ये च महेषुधी। रथं ध्वजं सभां चैव युधिष्ठिरमभाषत॥
en: Vaishampayana said Partha (Arjuna who had the excellent bow(Gandiva), the couple of inexhaustible quivers and the car with the (Ape) standard and also that Sabha, spoke thus to Yudhishthira.

sn: अर्जुन उवाच धनुः शस्त्रं शरा वीर्यं पक्षो भूमिर्यशो बलम्। प्राप्तमेतन्मया राजन् दुष्प्रापं यदभीप्सितम्॥
en: Arjuna said O king, I have obtained the bow, the weapons and the arrows, and also energy, allies, dominions, fame and strength. They are all difficult to be obtained, though they may be often desired.

sn: कुले जन्म प्रशंसन्ति वैद्याः साधु सुनिष्ठिता। बलेन सदृशं नास्ति वीर्यं तु मम रोचते॥
en: All famous men of learning always praise in good society the nobleness of descent; but nothing is equal to prowess. There is nothing I like more thari prowess.

sn: कृतवीर्यकुले जातो निर्वीर्यः किं करिष्यति। निर्वीर्य तु कुले जातो वीर्यवांस्तु विशिष्यते॥
en: One, born in a race famous for velour, but without velour, is scarcely worthy of regard. One who is born in a race noted for velour and also possesses valour is much superior to the former.

sn: क्षत्रियः सर्वशो राजन् यस्य वृत्तिर्दिषज्ज्ये। सर्वैर्गुणैर्विहीनोऽपि वीर्यवान् हि तरेद् रिपून्॥
en: O king, he is in every way a real Kshatriya who increases his fame and possessions by the subjugation of his enemies. He who is possessed of velour, though he has no other merits, will vanquish his enemies.

sn: सर्वैरपि गुणैर्युक्तो निर्वीयः किं करिष्यति। गुणीभूता गुणाः सर्वे तिष्ठन्ति हि पराक्रमे॥
en: One, who is endued with all accomplishments, but who is destitute of velour, can hardly ever accomplish any thing. Every merit exists by the side of velour in an incipient state.

sn: जयस्य हेतुः सिद्धिर्हि कर्म दैवं च संश्रितम्। संयुक्तो हि बलैः कश्चित् प्रमादान्नोपयुज्यते॥ तेन द्वारेण शत्रुभ्यः क्षीयते सबलो रिपुः॥ दैन्यं यथा बलवति तथा मोहो बलान्विते। तावुभौ नाशकौ हेतू राज्ञा त्याज्यौ जयार्थिना॥
en: Concentration of mind, exertion and destiny, (these three) exist as the three causes of victory. One who possesses velour, but does act with carelessness can never win victory; It is for this that a many endued with strength sometimes suffers death at the hands of his enemies. As meanness overtakes the weak, so folly sometimes overtakes the strong. A king therefore, who is desirous of victory, should forsake both these causes of destruction.

sn: जरासंधविनाशं च राज्ञां च परिरक्षणम्। यदि कुर्याम यज्ञार्थं किं ततः परमं भवेत्॥
en: If for the purpose of performing out sacrifice, we try to kill Jarasandha and to rescue the kings kept prisoners by him for his cruel purpose, there could be no act higher than this in which we could employ ourselves.

sn: अनारम्भे हि नियतो भवेदगुणनिश्चयः। गुणानिः संशया राजन् नैर्गुण्यं मन्यसे कथम्॥
en: If we do not undertake the task, the world will always regard us as worthless. O king, we have certainly the ability, why should we then be regarded (by the people) as worthless?

sn: काषायं सुलभं पश्चान्मुनीनां शममिच्छताम्। साम्राज्यं तु भवेच्छक्यं वयं योत्स्यामहे परान्॥
en: Those that have become Rishis with the desire of obtaining peace of mind get the red clothes with ease. Therefore, if we defeat the enemy, the imperial dignity will be easily obtained by us. We should, therefore, fight with the enemy.

sn: वासुदेव उवाच जातस्य भारते वंशे तथा कुन्त्याः सुतस्य च। या वै युक्ता मतिः सेयमर्जुनेन प्रदर्शिता॥
en: Krishna said Arjuna has shown what should be the inclination of one born in the Bharata race, specially of one who is the son of Kunti.

sn: न स्म मृत्यु विद्म रात्रौ वा यदि वा दिवा। न चापि कंचिदमरमयुद्धेनानुशुश्रुम॥
en: We do not know when death will overtake us, whether in the night or in the day; nor have we heard the immortality has been obtained by desisting from battle.

sn: एतावदेव पुरुषैः कार्य हृदयतोषणम्। नयेन विधिदृष्टेन यदुपक्रमते परान्॥
en: Therefore, the duty of a man (a hero) is to attack all enemies with the help of the policy indicated in the ordinance. This always gives satisfaction to the heart.

sn: सुनयस्यानपायस्य संयोगे परमः क्रमः। संगत्या जायतेऽसाम्यं साम्यं च न भवेद् द्वयोः॥
en: If aided by good policy, and if not frustrated by destiny, an undertaking is sure to be crowned with success. If both the parties are aided by such means, and if they fight with each other, one must get the better of the other, for both cannot win or lose.

sn: अनयस्यानुपायस्य संयुगे परमः क्षयः। संशयो जायते साम्याज्जयश्च न भवेद् द्वयोः॥
en: If aided by bad policy which is destitute of all well-known arts, a man is sure to be defeated and meet with destruction. If, however, both parties are equally circumstance, the result becomes doubtful, but booth cannot win.

sn: ते वयं नयमास्थाय शत्रुदेहसमीपगाः। कथमन्तं न गच्छेम वृक्षस्येव नदीरयाः। पररन्ध्र पराक्रान्ताः स्वरन्ध्रावरणे स्थिताः॥
en: When such is the case, why should we not, with the aid of good policy, go to the enemy and kill him as a river uproots a tree? if hiding our own drawbacks and taking advantage of his holes (faults), we attack the enemy, why should we not be successful?

sn: व्यूढानीकैरतिबलैर्न युद्ध्येदरिभिः सह। इति बुद्धिमतां नीतिस्तन्ममापीह रोचते॥
en: It is the policy of all intelligent men that one should fight with enemies who are exceedingly powerful and who stand at the head of their well-arrayed forces. It is my opinion also.

sn: अनवद्या ह्यसम्बुद्धाः प्रविष्टाः शत्रुसद्म तत्। शत्रुदेहमुपाक्रम्य तं कामं प्राप्नुयामहे॥
en: If we can accomplish our purpose by secretly entering the abode of our enemy and attacking his person, we shall never meet with obloquy.

sn: एको ह्येव श्रियं नित्यं बिभर्ति पुरुषर्षभः। अन्तरात्मेव भूतानां तत्क्षणं नैव लक्षये॥
en: That best of men (Jarasandha) alone enjoys unfading prosperity like him who is inner-soul of every created being. But I see his destruction (before me).

sn: अथवैनं निहत्याजौ शेषेणापि समाहताः। प्राप्नुयाम ततः स्वर्ग ज्ञातित्राणपरायणाः॥
en: Desirous as we are of protecting our relatives we shall either kill him, in battle or being ourselves killed by him we shall ascend to heaven.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच कृष्ण कोऽयं जरासंधः किंवीर्यः किम्पराक्रमः। यस्त्वां स्पृष्टवाग्निसदृशं न दग्धः शलभो यथा॥
en: Yudhishthira said O Krishna, who is this Jarasandha? What is his might, and what is his prowess that he has not been burnt by touching you as a insect is burnt at the touch of fire?

sn: कृष्ण उवाच शृणु राजञ्जरासंधो यद्वीर्यो यत्पराक्रमः। यथा चोपेक्षितोऽस्माभिबहुशः कृतविप्रियः॥
en: Krishna said O king, hear who is Jarasandha, what is his might and prowess, and why he has been spared by us, though he repeatedly offended us.

sn: अक्षौहिणीनां तिसृणां पतिः समरदर्पितः। राजा बृहद्रथो नाम मगधाधिपतिर्बली॥
en: There was a king, named Brihadratha who was the heroic lord of Magadha. He was proud in battle battle and had any army of three Akshauhinis of soldiers,

sn: रूपवान् वीर्यसम्पन्नः श्रीमानतुलविक्रमः। नित्यं दीक्षाङ्किततनुः शतक्रतुरिवापरः॥
en: He was handsome, mighty, wealthy and matchlessly powerful. He always bore (sacrificial) marks on his person and looked like a second Shakra (Indra).

sn: तेजसा सूर्यसंकाशः क्षमया पृथिवीसमः। यमान्तकसमः क्रोधे श्रिया वैश्रवणोयमः॥
en: He was like Surya in glory, like earth in patience, like the destroyer Yama in anger and like Vaishravana (Kubera) in wealth.

sn: तस्याभिजनसंयुक्तैर्गुणैर्भरतसत्तम। व्याप्तेयं पृथिवी सर्वा सूर्यस्येव गभस्तिभिः॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, as the rays of the sun (covers the whole earth), so the whole carth was covered by his merits which descended to him from a long line of ancestors.

sn: स काशिराजस्य सुते यमजे भरतर्षभ। उपयेमे महावीर्यो रूपद्रविणसंयुते। तयोश्चकार समयं मिथः स पुरुषर्षभः॥ नातिवर्तिष्य इत्येवं पत्नीभ्यां संनिधौ तदा। स ताभ्यां शुशुभे राजा पत्नीभ्यां वसुधाधिपः॥ प्रियाभ्यामनुरूपाभ्यां करेणुभ्यामिव द्विपः। तयोर्मध्यगतश्चापि रराज वसुधाधिपः॥ गङ्गायमुनयोर्मध्ये मूर्तिमानिव सागरः। विषयेषु निमग्नस्य तस्य यौवनमभ्यगात्॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, that greatly powerful hero married the two beautiful twindaughters of the king of Kashi. That best of men made an engagement in secret with his two wives, namely that he would equally love them both, and that he would never show a preference for any of them. Like a mighty elephant in the company of two femaleelephants, or like the ocean in his personified form in the company of the Ganga and the Yamuna, that lord of the earth passed his days in joy in the company of his two wives, both of whom suited him well. His youth passed away in the enjoyment of his wealth.

sn: न च वंशकरः पुत्रस्तस्याजायत कश्चन। मङ्गलैर्बहुभिर्होमैः पुत्रकामाभिरिष्टिभिः। नाससाद नृपश्रेष्ठः पुत्रं कुलविवर्धनम्॥
en: No son was (however) born to him to perpetuate his line; though he performed many auspicious rites, Homas, and sacrifices with the desire of getting a son, yet that best of men did not get a son who could perpetuate his line.

sn: अथ काक्षीवतः पुत्रं गौतमस्य महात्मनः। शुश्राव तपसि श्रान्तमुदारं चण्डकौशिकम्॥ यदृच्छयाऽऽगतं तं तु वृक्षमूलमुपाश्रितम्। पत्नीभ्यां सहितो राजा सर्वरत्नैरतोषयत्॥
en: He heard one day that the illustrious Chandakaushika, the son of Kakshivana of the Goutama race, having been tired of ascetic penances, have come to his city in his wandering at pleasure, and that he sat under a tree. The king with his wives gratified the Rishi with presents of Jewels.

sn: तमब्रवीत् सत्यधृतिः सत्यवागृषिसत्तमः। परितुष्टोऽस्मि राजेन्द्र वरं वरय सुव्रत॥
en: That best of Rishis ever truthful in speech and firmly devoted to truth, thus spoke to him (the king), “O king of kings I have been much gratified. O hero of excellent vows, ask from me a boon.

sn: ततः सभार्यः प्रणतस्तमुवाच बृहद्रथः। पुत्रदर्शननैराश्याद् वाष्पसंदिग्धया गिरा॥
en: Thereupon Brihadratha with his wives bowed down to the Rishi, and he spoke thus to him, his voice being choked with tears in consequences of his despair to obtain a son.

sn: राजोवाच भगवन् राज्यमुत्सृज्य प्रस्थितोऽहं तपोवनम्। किं वरेणाल्पभाग्यस्य किं राज्येनाप्रजस्य मे॥
en: The king said O exalted one, I am about to give up my kingdom and to go into the forest to lead an ascetic life. I am unfortunate, (for not having a son), what shall I do with the kingdom or with a boon?

sn: कृष्ण उवाच एतच्छ्रुत्वा मुनिर्ध्यानमगमत् क्षुभितेन्द्रियः। तस्यैव चाम्रवृक्षस्यच्छायायां समुपाविशत्॥
en: Krishna said Having heard this the Rishi, sitting in the shade of that every mangoes tree where he was, controlled his outer senses and entered into the Yoga meditation.

sn: तस्योपविष्टस्य मुनेरुत्सङ्गे निपपात ह। अवातमशुकादष्टमेकमाम्रफलं किल॥
en: There fell in the lap of the seated Rishi a juicy mango, untouched by the beak of parrots or other birds.

sn: तत् प्रगृह्य मुनिश्रेष्ठो हृदयेनाभिमन्त्र्य च। राज्ञे ददावप्रतिमं पुत्रसम्प्राप्तिकारणम्॥
en: That best of Rishis, taking up the fruit and mentally pronouncing some mantras over it, gave it to the king as the means of his obtaining a son.

sn: उवाच च महाप्राज्ञस्तं राजानं महामुनिः। गच्छ राजन् कृतार्थोऽसि निवर्तस्व नराधिप॥
en: That greatly learned Rishi spoke thus to the king, “O king, go, your wish is fulfilled. O king, desist from going to the forest."

sn: एतच्छ्रुत्वा मुनेर्वाक्यं शिरसा प्रणिपत्य च। मुनेः पादौ महाप्राज्ञः स नृपः स्वगृहं गतः॥
en: Having heard these words of the Rishi, the greatly intelligent king bowed down his head before the Rishi and returned to his own house.

sn: यथासमयमाज्ञाय तदा स नृपसत्तमः। द्वाभ्यामेकं फलं प्रादात् पत्नीभ्यां भरतर्षभ॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, recollecting his former promise, that best of kings gave that one fruit to his two wives.

sn: ते तदानं द्विधा कृत्वा भक्षयामासतुः शुभे। भावित्वादपि चार्थस्य सत्यवाक्यतया मुनेः॥ गर्भः फलप्राशनसम्भवः। ते च दृष्ट्वा स नृपतिः परां मुदमवाप ह॥
en: His two beautiful wives ate the mango, dividing it into two equal parts. In consequence of the certainty of the Muni's words and his truthfulness both of them conceived as an effect of their having eaten that fruit. Seeing them in that state, the king was filled with great joy.

sn: अथ काले महाप्राज्ञ यथासमयमागते। प्रजायेतामुभे राजञ्छरीरशकले तदा॥
en: O greatly wise (king), sometime after when the (proper) season came, each of the two queens brought forth two fragmentary bodies.

sn: एकाक्षिबाहुचरणे अर्धेदरमुखस्फिचे। दृष्ट्वा शरीरकाले प्रवेपतुरुभे भृशम्॥
en: Each of those two bodies had one eye, one arm, one leg, half a stomach, half a face, and half an anus. Seeing the fragmentary bodies, they (the queens) trembled much.

sn: तयोः समभवद् उद्विग्ने सह सम्मन्त्र्य ते भगिन्यौ तदाबले। सजीवे प्राणिशकले तत्यजाते सुदुःखिते॥
en: The helpless sisters then a great anxiety consulted with each other, and they abandoned in sorrow the fragments that had life in them.

sn: तथोर्धात्र्यौ सुसंवीते कृत्वा ते गर्भसम्प्लवे। निर्गम्यान्तः पुरद्वारात् समुत्सृज्याभिजग्मतुः॥
en: The two midwives then carefully wrapped up those still-born fragments and went out of the inner apartments (of the palace), by the back door. Throwing away the bodies, they returned in haste.

sn: ते चतुष्पथनिक्षिप्ते जरा नामाथ राक्षसी। जग्राह मनुजव्याघ्र मांसशोणितभोजना॥
en: O best of men, sometime after a Rakshasas woman, named, Jara who lived on flesh and blood, took up the fragments that lay on a crossing (or roads).

sn: कर्तुकामा सुखवहे शकले सा तु राक्षसी। संयोजयामास तदा विधानबलचोदिता॥४०
en: Being impelled by fate, that Rakshasas woman united the fragments to make them easier to carry.

sn: ते समानीतमात्रे तु शकले पुरुषर्षभ। एकमूर्तिधरो वीरः कुमारः समपद्यत॥
en: O best of men, as soon as the fragments were united, they formed into a heroic child of one body.

sn: ततः सा राक्षसी राजन् विस्मयोत्फुल्ललोचना। न शशाक समुद्वोढुं वज्रसारमयं शिशुम्॥
en: O king, the Rakshasas woman, with her cyes wide opened in wonder, found herself unable to carry that child who had a body as hard and strong as the thunderbolt.

sn: बालस्ताम्रतलं मुष्टिं कृत्वा चास्ये निधाय सः। प्राक्रोशदतिसंरब्धः सतोय इव तोयदः॥
en: Closing his coppery red fists and inserting it into its mouth, that child roared as terribly as the clouds charged with rains.

sn: तेन शब्देन सम्भ्रान्तः सहसान्तःपुरे जनः। निर्जगाम नरव्याघ्र राज्ञा सह परंतप॥
en: O best of men, O chastiser of foes, being much alarmed by the sound, the inmates of the palace along with the king all came out (to see what was the matter).

sn: ते चाबले परिम्लाने पयःपूर्णपयोधरे। निराशे पुत्रलाभाय सहसैवाभ्यगच्छताम्॥
en: The helpless, disappointed and the sad queens also, with their breasts full of milk suddenly came out to get back their child.

sn: अथ दृष्ट्वा तथाभूते राजानं चेष्टसंततिम्। तं च बालं सुबलिनं चिन्तयामास राक्षसी॥
en: Seeing them (the queens) in that condition and the king also, who was so much desirous of getting a son, and also the child which was so very strong, the Rakshasas woman reflected thus.

sn: नार्हामि विषये राज्ञो वसन्ती पुत्रगृद्धिनः। बालं पुत्रमिमं हन्तुं धार्मिकस्य महात्मनः॥
en: “I live in the kingdom of the king who is so eager to get a son. I should not therefore, kill the child so such a virtuous and illustrious king.

sn: सा तं बालमुपादाय मेघलेखेव भास्करम्। कृत्वा च मानुषं रूपमुवाच वसुधाधिपम्॥
en: Then hiding the child in her arms as the clouds envelope the sun, and assuming a human form, she thus spoke to the lord of earth (Brihadratha).

sn: राक्षस्युवाच बृहद्रथ सुतस्तेऽयं मया दत्तः प्रगृह्यताम्। तव पत्नीद्वये जातो द्विजातिवरशासनात्। धात्रीजनपरित्यक्तो मयायं परिरक्षितः॥
en: The Rakshasi Said O Brihadratha, this is your son. It is given to you by me. Take it. It is born in the wombs of your two wives in consequence of the boon granted to you by the Brahmana. It was abandoned by the midwives, but it was protected by me.

sn: श्रीकृष्ण उवाच ततस्ते भरतश्रेष्ठ काशिराजसुते शुभे। तं बालमभिपद्याशु प्रस्रवैरभ्यषिञ्चताम्॥
en: Krishna said O best of the Bharata race, having obtained the child, the handsome daughters of the king of Kashi drenched it with their lacteal streams.

sn: ततः स राजा संहृष्टः सर्वं तदुपलभ्य च। अपृच्छद्धेगर्भाभां राक्षसी तामराक्षसीम्॥
en: having ascertained everything, the king was filled with joy. He then spoke thus to the Rakshasas woman who was in the guise of a human female possessing the complexion of gold.

sn: राजोवाच का त्वं कमलगर्भाभे मम पुत्रप्रदायिनी। कामया ब्रूहि कल्याणि देवता प्रतिभासि मे॥
en: “O lotus-complexioned lady, who are you that give me the child? O blessed lady, you appear to me as a goddess roaming (over the earth) at pleasure."

sn: राक्षस्युवाच जरा नामास्मि भद्रं ते राक्षसी कामरूपिणी। तव वेश्मनि राजेन्द्र पूजिता न्यवसं सुखम्॥
en: The Rakshasi said O king of kings, be blessed, I am a Rakshasas woman, called Jara. I am capable of going everywhere at will. Worshipped by all, I live in your house in joy.

sn: गृहे गृहे मनुष्याणां नित्यं तिष्ठामि राक्षसी। गृहदेवीति नाम्ना वै पुरा सृष्टा स्वयंभुवा॥
en: I am a Rakshasi who always wander from house to house of men. I was formerly created by the self-create (Brahma) and was named Grihadevi (household goddess).

sn: दानवानां विनाशाय स्थापिता दिव्यरूपिणी। यो मां भक्त्या लिखेत् कुड्ये सपुत्रां यौवनान्विताम्॥३। गृहे तस्य भवेद् वृद्धिरन्यथा क्षयमाप्नुयात्। त्वद्गृहे तिष्ठमानाहं पूजिताहं सदा विभो॥ लिखिता चैव कुड्येषु पुत्रैर्बहुभिरावृता। गन्धपुष्पैस्तथा धूपैर्भक्ष्यभोज्यैः सुपूजिता॥
en: I was endued with celestials beauty and I was placed (in the world) for the destruction of the Danavas. He, who with devotion paints on the walls (of his house) and likeness of myself who am young and who have children, must have prosperity in his house. He, who does not do it, must meet with decay and destruction. O lord, a likeness of myself surrounded by many children, is painted on the walls of your house. Placed their, I am daily worshipped with scents, flowers, incense, edibles and various objects of enjoyments.

sn: साहं प्रत्युपकारार्थं चिन्तयाम्यनिशं तव। तवेमे पुत्रशकले दृष्टवत्यस्मि धार्मिक॥
en: Therefore, O virtuous man, I always think of doing some good to you. It happened that I chanced to see the fragments of the body of you son.

sn: संश्लेषिते मया दैवात् कुमारः समपद्यत। तव भाग्यान्महाराज हेतुमात्रमहं त्विह॥
en: On my accidentally uniting them, a boy was born. O great king, it has so happened only out of your good fortune. I have been mere an instrument (in reviving the child).

sn: मेरुं वा खादितुं शक्ता किं पुनस्त्व बालकम्। गृहसम्पूजनात् तुष्ट्या मया प्रत्यर्पितस्तव॥
en: I can swallow (even) the mountain of Meru, what I speak of your child. I am gratified with the worship that I receive in your house; therefore the child is returned to you,

sn: श्रीकृष्ण उवाच एवमुक्त्वा तु सा राजंस्तत्रैवान्तरधीयत। स संगृह्य कुमारं तं प्रविवेश गृहं नृपः॥
en: Krishna said O king having said this, she disappeared there and then. Obtaining the child the king then entered his own house.

sn: तस्य बालस्य यत् कृत्यं तच्चकार नृपस्तदा। आज्ञापयच्च राक्षस्या मगधेषु महोत्सवम्॥
en: The 'king then caused all the rites and ceremonies of infancy to be performed on the child; he ordered a festival to be observed in Magadha (by his subjects) in honour of the Rakshasas woman.

sn: तस्य नामाकरोच्चैव पितामहसम: पिता। जरया संधितो यस्माज्जरासंधो भवत्वयम्॥
en: The father (the king) who was equal to the Grandsire, then bestowed a name on that child. As the (fragments of the body of the child) was united by Jara, he was named Jarasandha.

sn: सोऽवर्धत महातेजा मगधाधिपतेः सुतः। प्रमाणबलसम्पन्नो हुताहुतिरिवानलः। मातापित्रोर्नन्दिकरः शुक्लपक्षे यथा शशी॥
en: The greatly powerful son of the Magadha king begin to grow up in bulk and in strength, like a fire into which libations of Ghee have been poured. He delighted the heart of his father and mother, increasing day by day like the moon in the white-fortnight.

sn: श्रीकृष्ण उवाच कस्यचित् त्वथ कालस्य पुनरेव महातपाः। मगधेषूपचक्राम भगवांश्चण्डकौशिकः॥
en: Krishna said Sometime after, the great ascetic the illustrious Chandakaushika came again to the kingdom of Magadha

sn: तस्यागमनसंहृष्टः सामात्यः पुरःसरः। सभार्य: सह पुत्रेण निर्जगाम बृहद्रथः॥
en: Being overjoyed at the arrival of the Rishi, Brihadratha with his ministers, priest, his son and wives went out to receive him.

sn: पाद्यार्थ्याचमनीयैस्तमर्चयामास भारत। स नृपो राज्यसहितं पुत्रं तस्मै न्यवेदयत्॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, worshipping the Rishi with water to wash his feet and with Arghya, the king offered him his on with the whole of his kingdom.

sn: प्रतिगृह्य च तां पूजां पार्थिवाद् भगवानृषिः। उवाच मागधं राजन् प्रहृष्टेनान्तरात्मना॥
en: O king, the illustrious Rishi accepted the worship of the king and thus spoke to the king of Magadha with a delightful heart.

sn: सर्वमेतन्मया ज्ञातं राजन् दिव्येन चक्षुषा। पुत्रस्तु शृणु राजेन्द्र यादृशोऽयं भविष्यति॥
en: O king, everything is known to me thought my spiritual sight. O king of kings, hear what this your son will be.

sn: अस्य रूपं च सत्त्वं च बलमूर्जितमेव च। एष श्रिया समुदितः पुत्रस्तव न संशयः॥ प्रापयिष्यति तत् सर्वं विक्रमेण समन्वितः। अस्य वीर्यवतो वीर्यं नानुयास्यन्ति पार्थिवाः॥
en: (Hear also) what will be his beauty, excellence, strength and courage. There is not the least doubt that your this son will grow in prosperity and will obtain them, endued as he is with great prowess. No king will be able to equal your greatly powerful son in prowess,

sn: पततो वैनतेयस्य गतिमन्ये यथा खगाः। विनाशमुपयास्यन्ति ये चास्य परिपन्थिनः॥
en: As other birds, can never equal the speed of Vainata's son (Garuda). All those that will stand in his way will meet with certain destruction.

sn: देवैरपि विसृष्टानि शस्त्राण्यस्य महीपते। न रुजं जनयिष्यन्ति गिरेरिव नदीरयाः॥
