en: O king, as the river can make no impression on the mountain, so the weapons hurled upon him even by the celestials will not be able to make any impression on him.

sn: सर्वमूर्धाभिषिक्तानामेष मूनि ज्वलिष्यति। प्रभाहरोऽयं सर्वेषां ज्योतिषामिव भास्करः॥
en: He will blaze forth above the heads of all that wear crowns on their heads. Like the sun he will rob all other kings of their splendour.

sn: एनमासाद्य राजानः समृद्धबलवाहनाः। विनाशमुपयास्यन्ति शलभा इव पावकम्॥
en: The kings who are rich in their armies and troops will meet with destruction at the hand of your son like insects in the fire.

sn: एष श्रियः समुदिताः सर्वराज्ञां ग्रहीष्यति। वर्षास्विवोदीर्णजला नदीनदनदीपतिः॥
en: He will seize the growing prosperity of all the kings, as the ocean receives the rivers swollen with the waters of the rainy season.

sn: एष धारयिता सम्यक् चातुर्वण्र्यं महाबलः। शुभाशुभमिव स्फीता सर्वसस्यधरा धरा॥
en: As the wide earth bears all kinds of produce and supports those that are both good and bad, your this greatly powerful son will support all the people of the four orders.

sn: अस्याज्ञावशगाः सर्वे भविष्यन्ति नराधिपाः। सर्वभूतात्मभूतस्य वायोरिव शरीरिणः॥
en: All the kings will remain obedient to him, as all embodied beings remain obedient to the wind, which is as dear to beings as the self.

sn: एष रुद्र महादेवं त्रिपुरान्तकरं हरम्। सर्वलोकेष्वतिबलः साक्षाद् द्रक्ष्यति मागधः॥
en: This Magadha prince, this mightiest of all mighty men in the world, will see with his physical eyes the god of gods, Rudra, the slayer of Tripura, Hara.”

sn: एवं ब्रुवन्नेव मुनिः सवकार्यमिव चिन्तयन्। विसर्जयामास नृपं बृहद्रथमथारिहन्॥
en: Having said this, the Rishi, thinking of his own business, dismissed that layer of foes, the king Brihadratha.

sn: प्रविश्य नगरीं चापि ज्ञातिसम्बन्धिभिर्वृतः। अभिषिच्य जरासंधं मगधाधिपतिस्तदा॥
en: The Magadha king then re-entered his capital; and summoning all his friends and relatives, he installed Jarasandha on the throne.

sn: बृहद्रथो नरपतिः परां निर्वृतिमाययौ। अभिषिक्ते जरासंधे तदा राजा बृहद्रथः। पत्नीद्वयेनानुगतस्तपोवनचरोऽभवत्॥
en: The king Brihadratha became greatly disgusted with all worldly pleasures. After the installation of Jarasandha, the king Brihadratha followed by his two waives went into a forest to lead the life of an ascetic.

sn: ततो वनस्थे पितरि मात्रोश्चैव विशाम्पते। जरासंध स्ववीर्येण पार्थिवानकरोद् वशे॥
en: O king, after his father and mother had retired into the forest, Jarasandha brought numerous kings under his sway by his velour.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच अथ दीर्घस्य कालस्य तपोवनचरो नृपः। सभार्यः स्वर्गमगमत् तपस्तप्त्वा बृहद्रथः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having lived for a long time in the forest and practiced asceticism, (the king) Brihadratha ascended to heaven with his wives.

sn: जरासंधोऽपि नृपतिर्यथोक्तं कौशिकेन तत्। वरप्रदानमखिलं प्राप्य राज्यमपालयत्॥
en: As told by Kaushika, the king Jarasandha received the boons and ruled the kingdom after obtaining the (sovereignty of the) whole world.

sn: निहते वासुदेवेन तदा कंसे महीपतौ। जातो वै वैरनिर्बन्धः कृष्णेन सह तस्य वै॥
en: Sometime after, when the king Kansa was killed by Vasudeva (Krishna), an enmity arose between him and Krishna.

sn: भ्रामयित्वा शतगुणमेकोनं येन भारत। गदा क्षिप्ता बलवता मागधेन गिरिव्रजात्॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, the greatly powerful king of Magadha whirled a club ninety nine times and he hurled it towards Mathura from Girivraja (his capital).

sn: तिष्ठतो मथुरायां वै कृष्णस्याद्भुतकर्मणः। एकोनयोजनशते सा पपात गदा शुभा॥
en: Krishna of wonderful deeds was then living in Mathura. That excellent club fell at a distance of ninety-nine Yojanas.

sn: दृष्ट्वा पौरैस्तदा सम्यग् गदा चैव निवेदिता। गदावसानं तत् ख्यातं मथुरायाः समीपतः॥
en: Seeing well all the circumstances the citizens (of Mathura) all went to Krishna and told him all about the fall of the club. The place where the club fell was near Mathura, and it was known by the name of Gadavasana.

sn: तस्यास्तां हंसडिम्भकावशस्त्रनिधनावुभौ। मन्त्रे मतिमतां श्रेष्ठौ नीतिशास्त्रे विशारदौ॥
en: He (Jarasandha) had two supporters named Hansa and Dimbhaka, both incapable of being killed by any weapons, both were learned in the science of politics and morality, and both were in counsel foremost of all intelligent men.

sn: यौ तौ मया ते कथितौ पूर्वमेव महाबलौ। त्रयस्त्रयाणां लोकानां पर्याप्ता इति मे मतिः॥
en: I have already told you before every thing about these two greatly powerful heroes. My opinion is that these two heroes and Jarasandha were more than a match for the three worlds.

sn: एवमेव तदा वीर बलिभिः कुकुरान्धकैः। वृष्णिभिश्च महाराज नीतिहेतोरुपेक्षितः॥
en: O hero, O great king, it was for this reason that the powerful Akrura, Andhaka and Vrishni tribes, acting from policy, did not fight with him (Jarasandha).

sn: वासुदेव उवाच पतितौ हंसडिम्भकौ कंसश्च सगणो हतः। जरासंधस्य निधने कालोऽयं समुपागतः॥
en: Krishna said Hansa and Dimbhaka have fallen Kansa also with his followers has been killed; the time has, therefore, come for killing Jarasandha.

sn: न शक्योऽसौ रणे जेतुं सर्वैरपि सुरासुरैः। बाहुयुद्धेन जेतव्यः स इत्युपलभामहे॥
en: He is incapable of being vanquished in battle by all the celestials and the Asuras. Therefore, my opinion is to defeat him in a single combat.

sn: मयि नीतिर्बलं भीमे रक्षिता चावयोर्जयः। मागधं साधयिष्याम इष्टिं त्रय इवाग्नयः॥
en: In me is policy, and in Bhima is strength, and we are both protected by Arjuna. We shall vanquish the Magadha king like three (sacrifice) fires.

sn: त्रिभिरासादितोऽस्माभिर्विजने स नराधिपः। न संदेहो यथा युद्धमेकेनाप्युपयास्यति॥
en: If we three go secretly to that king, there is no doubt he will be engaged in a single combat with one of us.

sn: अवमानाच्च लोभाच्च बाहुवीर्याच्च दर्पितः। भीमसेनेन युद्धाय ध्रुवमप्युपयास्यति॥
en: From the fear of disgrace, from covetousness, and from the pride of strength of arms, he will certainly challenge Bhima to a single combat.

sn: अलं तस्य महाबाहुर्भीमसेनो महाबलः। लोकस्य समुदीर्णस्य निधनायान्तको यथा॥
en: Like death himself who kills a person however proud he might be, the mighty armed and the greatly powerful Bhima will surely bring about the destruction of the king (Jarasandha).

sn: यदि मे हृदयं वेत्सि यदि ते प्रत्ययो मयि। भीमसेनार्जुनौ शीघ्रं न्यासभूतौ प्रयच्छ मे॥
en: If you know my heart, if you have any faith in me, then without any further loss of time, give me as a pledge Bhima and Arjuna.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्तो भगवता प्रत्युवाच युधिष्ठिरः। भीमार्जुनौ समालोक्य सम्प्रहृष्टमुखौ स्थितौ॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having been thus addressed by that exalted being (Krishna), and having seen Bhima and Arjuna standing there with cheerful face, Yudhishthira thus replied.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच अच्युताच्युत मा मैवं व्याहरामित्रकर्शन। पाण्डवानां भवान् नाथो भवन्तं चाश्रिता वयम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said O Achyuta, O chastiser of foes, do not say so, You are the lord of the Pandavas. We are all dependent on you.

sn: यथा वदसि गोविन्द सर्वं तदुपपद्यते। न हि त्वमग्रतस्तेषां येषां लक्ष्मी: पराङ्मुखी॥
en: O Govinda, what you say is (always) consistent with wise counsel. You never lead those on whom Lakshmi (the goddess of prosperity) has turned her back.

sn: निहतश्च जरासंधो मोक्षिताश्च महीक्षितः। राजसूयश्च मे लब्धो निदेशे तव तिष्ठतः॥
en: I am, who always at your command, consider that Jarasandha is already killed, that the kings kept prisoner by him have already been liberated and that the Rajasuya sacrifice is already accomplished by me.

sn: क्षिप्रमेव यथा त्वेतत् कार्यं समुपपद्यते। अप्रमत्तो जगन्नाथ तथा कुरु नरोत्तम॥
en: O lord of the universe, O best of men, act soon with care in such a way as this task may be accomplished.

sn: त्रिभिर्भवद्भिर्हि विना नाहं जीवितुमुत्सहे। धर्मकामार्थरहितो रोगात इव दुःखितः॥
en: Like a sorrowful man afflicted with disease and like a man without Dharma, Artha and Kama, I dare not live without you.

sn: न शौरिणा विना पार्थो न शौरिः पाण्डवं विना। नाजेयोऽस्त्यनयोलोक कृष्णयोरिति मे मतिः॥
en: Partha (Arjuna) cannot live without Shauri (Krishna), and Shauri cannot live without Partha. My opinion is that there is nothing unconquerable by these two, namely Shauri and Partha.

sn: अयं च बलिनां श्रेष्ठः श्रीमानपि वृकोदरः। युवाभ्यां सहितो वीरः किं न कुर्यान्महायशाः॥
en: This handsome Vrikodara (Bhima) is the foremost of all strong men. Greatly famous as he is, what may not be achieved by him with you.

sn: सुप्रणीतो बलौधो हि कुरुते कार्यमुत्तमम्। अंधं बलं जडं प्राहुः प्रणेतव्यं विचक्षणैः॥ :॥
en: Troops when led properly do excellent service. The wise men say that troops without a leader is useless. Therefore, troops should be (always) led by experienced leaders.

sn: यतो हि निम्नं भवति नयन्ति हि ततो जलम्। यतश्छिद्रं ततश्चापि नयन्ते धीवरा जलम्॥
en: The wise always conduct the water to place that are low. The fisherman take the water through the place where there are holes.

sn: तस्मान्नयविधानज्ञं पुरुषं लोकविश्रुतम्। वयमाश्रित्य गोविन्दं यतामः कार्यसिद्धये॥
en: We shall, therefore, try to accomplish our object by following the leadership of Govinda (Krishna), who is learned in the science of politics, and whose fame has spread all over the world.

sn: एवं प्रज्ञानयबलं क्रियोपायसमन्वितम्। पुरस्कुर्वीत कार्येषु कृष्णं कार्यार्थसिद्धये॥
en: If one desires to have a successful end of his purpose, he should always place Krishna at the head, he is the foremost of all men whose strength consists in wisdom and policy; he is the man who possesses the knowledge of both the means and the methods.

sn: एवमेव यदुश्रेष्ठ यावत्कार्यार्थसिद्धये। अर्जुनः कृष्णमन्वेतु भीमोऽन्वेतु धनंजयम्। नयो जयो बलं चैव विक्रमे सिद्धिमेष्यति॥
en: For the accomplishment of our purpose, let the son of Pritha (Arjuna) follow the best of the Yadava, Krishna and let Bhima follow Dhananjaya (Arjuna). Policy, victory and prowess will bring about success in a matter requiring velour.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्तास्ततः सर्वे भ्रातरो विपुलौजसः। वार्ष्णेयः पाण्डवेयौ च प्रतस्थुर्मागधं प्रति॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having been thus addressed (by Yudhishthira) all the three brothers, the two Pandavas and the Varshneya (Krishna), all possessing great prowess, started for the kingdom of Magadha.

sn: वर्चस्विनां ब्राह्मणानां स्नातकानां परिच्छदम्। आच्छाद्य सुहृदां वाक्यैर्मनोहरभिनन्दिताः॥
en: They were attired in the grab of Snataka Brahmanas of effulgent bodies; they were blessed by the agreeable speeches of friends and relatives, (when they started).

sn: अमर्षादभितप्तानां ज्ञात्यर्थं मुख्यतेजसाम्। रविसोमाग्निवपुषां दीप्तमासीत् तदा वपुः॥
en: They possessed great prowess, and their bodies were like the sun, the moon and the fire. Being inflamed by the wrath wrath for the persecution that was perpetrated by Jarasandha on their relatives), their bodies now looked more blazing than before.

sn: हतं मेने जरासंधं दृष्ट्वा भीमपुरोगमौ। एककार्यसमुद्यन्तौ कृष्णौ युद्धेऽपराजितौ॥
en: Seeing the two Krishnas (Krishna and Arjuna) who are invincible in battle, and seeing Bhima at their head, all the three bent upon performing the same act, the people considered that Jarasandha was already killed.

sn: ईशौ हि तौ महात्मानौ सर्वकार्यप्रवर्तिनौ। धर्मकामार्थलोकानां कार्याणां च प्रवर्तकौ॥
en: The illustrious pair (Krishna and Arjuna) were the masters that directed the every operation of the universe; they directed all acts relating Dharma, Artha and Kama.

sn: कुरुभ्यः प्रस्थितास्ते तु मध्येन कुरुजाङ्गलम्। रम्यं पद्मसरो गत्वा कालकूटमतीत्य च॥
en: Having started from the Kuru country, they passed through the Kurujangala. They then arrived at the (lake) Padmasara, whence they went to the Kalakuta (mountains). Crossing it,

sn: गण्डकी च महाशोणं सदानीरां तथैव च। एकपर्वतके नद्यः क्रमेणैत्याव्रजन्त ते॥
en: They (finally) crossed the (rivers) Gandaki, the Sadanira and the Ekaparavata and others rivers, all these (rivers) taking either rise from the same mountain.

sn: उत्तीर्य सरयूं रम्यां दृष्ट्वा पूर्वांच कोसलान्। अतीत्य जग्मुर्मिथिलां पश्यन्तो विपुला नदीः॥
en: They then crossed the charming Sarayu and saw the eastern Kosalas. Crossing through it, they went to Mithila; and then crossing the rivers Mala and Charmanvati,

sn: अतीत्य गङ्गां शोणं च त्रयस्ते प्राङ्मुखास्तदा। कुशचीरच्छदा जग्मुर्मागधं क्षेत्रमच्युताः॥
en: The Ganges, and the Shone, they proceeded eastwards, Going to the heart of the Kusamva (country), the matchlessly effulgent heroes arrived at Magadha.

sn: ते शश्वद् गोधनाकीर्णमम्बुमन्तं शुभदुमम्। गोरथं गिरिमासाद्य ददृशुर्मागधं पुरम्॥
en: Getting on the (hill) Goratha, they saw the city of the Magadha king, full of kine, wealth and water. It was very beautiful with the trees that stood everywhere in it.

sn: वासुदेव उवाच एष पार्थ महान् भाति पशुमान् नित्यमम्बुमान्। निरामयः सुवेश्माढ्यो निवेशो मागधः शुभः॥
en: Krishna said O Partha, behold the great city of Magadha standing in all its beauty. It is full of cattle and other beasts of burden; its stock of water is inexhaustive; it is adorned with fine mansions; and it is (entirely) free from all dangers.

sn: वैहारो विपुलः शैलो वराहो वृषभस्तथा। तथा ऋषिगिरिस्तात शुभाश्चैत्यकपञ्चमाः॥
en: The five large hills, namely Vaihara, Varaha, Vrishabha, Rishigiri and the beautiful fifth hill Chaityaka.

sn: एते पञ्च महाशृङ्गाः पर्वताः शीतलद्रुमाः। रक्षन्तीवाभिसंहत्य संहताङ्गा गिरिव्रजम्॥
en: These five hills, all with high peaks and with tall trees with cool shades, all being connected with one another, seem jointly to protect the city of Girivraja.

sn: पुष्पवेष्टितशाखाग्रैर्गन्धवद्भिर्मनोहरैः। निगूढा इव लोध्राणां वनैः कामिजनप्रियैः॥
en: They are concealed by the forest of charming and fragrant Lodhra trees with their branches covered with flowers.

sn: शूद्रायां गौतमो यत्र महात्मा संशितव्रतः। औशीनर्यामजनयत् काक्षीवाद्यान् सुतान् मुनिः॥
en: This was the place where the illustrious Gotama of the rigid vows begot on the daughter of Ushinara, s Shudra woman Kakshivana and other famous sons.

sn: गौतमः प्रणयात् तस्माद् यथासौ तत्र सद्मनि। भजते मागधं वंशं स नृपाणामनुग्रहात्॥
en: The race sprung from such a man as Goutama worships the sway of ordinary human race, it shows the great kindness of Goutama towards kings.

sn: अङ्गवङ्गादयश्चैव राजानः सुमहाबलाः। गौतमक्षयमभ्येत्य रमन्ते स्म पुरार्जुन॥
en: O Arjuna, it was here that in olden times the powerful kings of Anga, Vanga and other countries came to the hermitage of Goutama and lives in joy and happiness.

sn: वनराजीस्तु पश्येमाः पिप्पलानां मनोरमाः। पार्थ गौतमौकः समीपजाः॥
en: O Partha, behold the charming forest of Pipalas and beautiful Lodhras standing near the place where Goutama lived.

sn: अर्बुदः शक्रवापी च पन्नगौ शत्रुतापनौ। स्वस्तिकस्यालयश्चात्र मणिनागस्य चोत्तमः॥
en: Here were the abodes of the chastisers of foes, the Nagas, Arbuda, Chakrapani and Swastika, and also that of the excellent Naga, called Mani.

sn: अपिहरार्या मेघानां मागधा मनुना कृताः। कौशिको मणिमांश्चैव चक्राते चाप्यनुग्रहम्॥
en: Manu himself had made the country of the Magadhas to be free from draught Kaushika and Maniman also have favoured and blessed this country.

sn: एवं प्राप्य पुरं रम्यं दुराधर्षं समन्ततः। अर्थसिद्धिं त्वनुपमा जरासंधोऽभिमन्यते॥ लोध्राणां च शुभाः
en: Having secured such a charming and impregnable city, Jarasandha does not fear to accomplish all his unrivalled purposes. We shall, however, today humble his pride by attacking him.

sn: वयमासादने तस्य दर्पमद्य हरेमहि। वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्तवा ततः सर्वे भ्रातरो विपुलौजसमः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having said this, those brothers of matchless effulgence the Varshneya (Krishna) and the two Pandavas (Bhima and Arjuna) entered the city of Magadha.

sn: वार्ष्णेयः पाण्डवौ चैव प्रतस्थुर्मागधं पुरम्। हृष्टपुष्टजनोपेतं चातुर्वर्ण्यसमाकुलम्॥
en: Then they went towards the impregnable city of Girivraja, full of cheerful and well-fed inhabitants belonging to all the four orders of men. The city was ever enlivened with perennial festivities.

sn: स्फीतोत्सवमनाधृष्यमासेदुश्च गिरिव्रजम्। ततो द्वारमनासाद्य पुरस्य गिरिमुच्छ्रितम्॥ बार्हद्रथैः पूज्यमानं तथा नगरवासिभिः। मगधानां सुरुचिरं चैत्यकान्तं समाद्रवन्॥
en: Going to the gate of the city (they did not enter through it); the brothers pierced the heart of the high Chaityaka (hill) which was ever worshipped by there of Brihadratha and by the citizens (of Girivraja), the hill that delighted the hearts of all the Magadhas.

sn: यत्र मांसादमृषभमाससाद बृहद्रथः। तं हत्वा मासतालाभिस्तिस्रो भेरीरकारयत्॥ स्वपुरे स्थापयामास तेन चानह्य चर्मणा। यत्र ताः प्राणदन् भेर्यो दिव्यपुष्पावचूर्णिताः॥ भङ्क्त्वा भेरीत्रयं तेऽपि चैत्यप्राकारमाद्रवन्। द्वारतोऽभिमुखाः सर्वे ययुर्नानाऽऽयुधास्तदा।॥ मागधानां सुरुचिरं चैत्यकं तं समाद्रवन्। शिरसीव समाघ्नन्तो जरासंधं जिघांसवः॥
en: Here (on this Chaityaka hill) Brihadratha had killed a cannibal, called Rishava,. Having killed the monster, he caused three drums to be made of his skin. He then kept these drums in his city. They were such that if once played upon their sound lasted for full one month. The brothers (Krishna & c.) broke down the Chaityaka, ever charming to all the people, at the place where these drums, covered with celestials flowers, sent forth their continuous sound. Desirous Desirous as they as they were to kill Jarasandha, they seemed to place their feet on the head of their foe by their this act.

sn: स्थिरं सुविपुलं शृङ्गं सुमहत् तत् पुरातनम्। अर्चितं गन्धमाल्यैश्च सततं सुप्रतिष्ठितम्॥ विपुलैर्बाहुभिर्वीरास्तेऽभिहत्याभ्यपातयन्। ततस्ते मागधं हृष्टाः पुरं प्रविविशुस्तदा॥
en: Attacking with their powerful arms that immovable, huge, high, old and famous peak, ever worshipped with perfumes and garlands, those heroes broke it down. They then with joyful hearts entered the city.

sn: एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु ब्राह्मणा वेदपारगाः। दृष्ट्वा तु दुर्निमित्तानि जरासंधमदर्शयन्॥
en: At that very time the Veda-knowing Brahmanas inhabiting the city saw many evil omens which they duly reported to Jarasandha.

sn: पर्यग्न्यकुर्वश्च नृपं द्विरदस्थं पुरोहिताः। ततस्तच्छान्तये राजा जरासंधः प्रतापवान्। दीक्षितो नियमस्थोऽसावुपवासपरोऽभवत्॥
en: The priest made the king mount on an elephant; and he then sanctified him by whirling lighted woods about him. The greatly powerful king Jarasandha commenced a fasting with proper vows to wards off these evils.

sn: स्नातकव्रतिनस्ते तु बाहुशस्त्रा निरायुधाः। युयुत्सवः प्रविविशुर्जरासंधेन भारत॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, they (the brothers) in the meantime, unarmed and with their bare arms as their only weapons, entered the city in the guise of Snataka Brahmanas in order to fight with Jarasandha.

sn: भक्ष्यमाल्यापणानां च ददृशुः श्रियमुत्तमाम्। स्फीतां सर्वगुणोपेतां सर्वकामसमृद्धिनीम्॥
en: They saw many beautiful shops, full of v...ious eataoles and garlands, every shop swelling with every article and every wealth that man can ever desire.

sn: तां तु दृष्ट्वा समृद्धि ते वीथ्यां तस्यां नरोत्तमाः। राजमार्गेण गच्छन्तः कृष्णभीमधनंजयाः। बलाद् गृहीत्वा माल्यानि मालाकारान्महाबलाः॥
en: Seeing the great wealth of those shops, those best of men, Krishna, Bhima and Dhananjaya (Arjuna), proceeded along the public streets. Those greatly powerful heroes snatched garlands from the flower vendors.

sn: विरागवसनाः सर्वे स्रग्विणो मृष्टकुण्डलाः। निवेशनमथाजग्मुर्जरासंधस्य धीमतः॥ गोवासमिव वीक्षन्तः सिंहा हैमवता यथा। शालस्तम्भनिभास्तेषां चन्दनागुरुरूषिताः॥ अशोभन्त महाराज बाहवो युद्धशालिनाम्। तान् दृष्ट्वा द्विरदप्रख्याशालस्कन्धानिवोद्गतान्। व्यूढोरस्कान् मागधानां विस्मयः: समपद्यत॥
en: Having attired in robes of various colours and adorned with garlands and earrings, the heroes entered the palace of the greatly intelligent Jarasandha as Himalayan lions longingly look at the pen of cattle. The arms of those warriors, smeared sandal and aloe paste, looked like the trunks of Sala trees, O great king, when the people of Magadha saw those heroes with necks and broad as those of Sala trees and with wide chests, they began to be very much astonished.

sn: तेत्वतीत्य जनाकीर्णाः कक्षास्तिस्रो नरर्षभाः। अहंकारेण राजानमुपतस्थुर्गतव्यथाः॥
en: Passing through three rooms crowded with men those best of men, with pride and cheerfulness came to the king.

sn: तान् पाद्यमधुपर्कार्हान् गवार्हान् सत्कृतिं गतान्। प्रत्युत्थाय जरासंध उपतस्थे यथाविधि॥ उवाच चैतान् राजासौ स्वागतं वोऽस्त्विति प्रभुः। मौनमासीत् तदा पार्थभीमयोर्जनमेजय॥
en: Jarasandha rose up in haste saying “Welcome to you”. He received his visitors with proper ceremonies, with water to wash their feet, with honey, with Arghya, with gift of kine and with the other forms of respect. O Janamejaya, both Partha and Bhima remained silent.

sn: तेषां मध्ये महाबुद्धिः कृष्णो वचनमब्रवीत्। वक्तुं नायाति राजेन्द्र एतयोर्नियमस्थयोः॥
en: Amongst them the greatly intelligent Krishna thus spoke to him, “O king of kings, these two are observing a vow. They will not therefore speak.

sn: अर्वानिशीथात् परतस्त्वया सार्धं वदिष्यतः। यज्ञागारे स्थापयित्वा राजा राजगृहं गतः॥
en: They will remain silent till midnight. After that hour they will talk with you." The king quartered them in the sacrificial apartments, and he then went to his own royal apartments.

sn: ततोऽर्धरात्रे सम्प्राप्ते यातो यत्र स्थिता द्विजाः। तस्य ह्येतद् व्रतं राजन् बभूव भुवि विश्रुतम्॥ स्नातकान् ब्राह्मणान् प्राप्ताञ्छ्रुत्वा स समितिंजयः। अत्यर्धरात्रे नृपतिः प्रत्युद्गच्छति भारत॥
en: O king, at midnight he(Jarasandha) came to the place where the Brahmanas (Krishna & c.) were. O descendant of Bharata, that ever victorious king observed the vow which was known all over the earth that as soon as he should hear of the arrival of any Snataka Brahmanas in his palace-even if it be midnight, he would immediately come out and grant them an interview.

sn: तांस्त्वपूर्वेण वेषेण दृष्ट्वा स नृपसत्तमः। उपतस्थे जरासंधो विस्मिताश्चाभवत् तदा॥
en: Seeing the strange attire (of his guests), that best of kings, Jarasandha, be came, very much astonished, but he waited upon them with all respect.

sn: ते तु दृष्ट्वैव राजानं जरासंधं नरर्षभाः। इदमूचुरमित्रघ्नाः सर्वे भरतसत्तम।॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, seeing the king Jarasandha, those best of men, those slayers of foes (Krishna etc.) thus spoke to him,

sn: स्वस्त्यस्तु कुशलं राजनिति तत्र व्यवस्थिताः। तं नृपं नृपशार्दूल प्रेक्षमाणाः परस्परम्॥
en: "O king, let salvation be attained by you without any difficulty.” And O best of king, having said this to the king, they stood looking at one another.

sn: तानब्रवीज्जरासंधस्तथा पाण्डवयादवान्। आस्यतामिति राजेन्द्र ब्राह्मणच्छद्मसंवृतान्॥
en: O king of kings, then Jarasandha said to the Pandavas (Bhima and Arjuna) and the Yadava (Krishna), who were all disguised as Brahmanas, “Take your seat.”

sn: अथोपविविशुः सर्वे त्रयस्ते पुरुषर्षभाः। सम्प्रदीप्तास्त्रयो लक्ष्या महाध्वर इवाग्नयः॥
en: Blazing forth in their own beauty like the three fires of a great sacrifice, these three best of men then took their seats.

sn: तानुवाच जरासंधः सत्यसंधो नराधिपः। बिगर्हमाणः कौरव्य वेषग्रहणवैकृतान्। न स्नातकव्रता विप्रा बहिर्माल्यानुलेपनाः॥ भवन्तीति नृलोकेऽस्मिन् विदितं मम सर्वशः। के यूयं पुष्पवन्तश्च भुजाकृतलक्षणैः॥
en: O descendant of Kuru, the firmly truthful king Jarasandha spoke to them thus, “It is wellknown to me that no where in the whole world the Brahmanas engaged in observing the Snataka vows ever adorn themselves with garlands or with fragrant paste. Who are you then, thus adorned with flowers and with hands that bear the marks of the bow-string?

sn: बिभ्रतः क्षात्रमोजश्च ब्राह्मण्यं प्रतिजानथ। एवं विरागवसना बहिर्माल्यानुलेपनाः॥
en: Attired in ascetic robes and adorned unseasonably with flowers and fragrant paste, you give me to understand that you are Brahmanas, though you bear all the signs of the Kshatriyas. Tell me truly who you are. Truth adorns (even) kings.

sn: चैत्यकस्य गिरेः शृङ्गं भित्त्वा किमिह छद्मना। अद्वारेण प्रविष्टाः स्थ निर्भया राजकिल्बिषात्॥
en: Breaking down the peak of the Chaityaka hill, why in disguise have you entered (the city) by the other ways than the gates without fearing the royal anger?

sn: वदध्वं वाचि वीर्यं च ब्राह्मणस्य विशेषतः। कर्म चैतद् विलिङ्गस्थं किं वोऽद्य प्रसमीक्षितम्॥
en: The prowess of a Brahmana rests mainly in his speech. Your action does not suit the order you profess to belong. Tell me what is your object today.

sn: एवं च मामुपास्थाय कस्माच्च विधिनार्हणाम्। प्रतीतां नानुगृहणीत कार्य किं वास्मदागमे॥
en: Though you have arrived by such an improper way, why do you not accept the worship, I offer to you? What is your object in coming to me?

sn: एवमुक्ते ततः कृष्णः प्रत्युवाच महामनाः। स्निग्धगम्भीरया वाचा वाक्यं वाक्यविशारदः॥
en: Having been thus addressed, the high minded Krishna, well-skilled in speech, thus replied to him in a calm and grave voice.

sn: श्रीकृष्ण उवाच स्नातकान् ब्राह्मणान् राजन् विद्ध्यस्मांस्त्वं नराधिप। स्नातकव्रतिनो राजन् ब्राह्मणाः क्षत्रिया विशः॥
en: Krishna said O king, know us for Snataka Brahmanas. O king of men, O monarch, Brahmanas, Kshatriyas and Vaishyas are all competent to observe the Snataka vow.

sn: विशेषनियमाश्चैषामविशेषाश्च सन्त्युज। विशेषवांश्च सततं क्षत्रियः श्रियमृच्छति॥
en: This vow has both special and general rules. A Kshatriya who observes this vow with special rules always obtains (great) prosperity.

sn: पुष्पवत्सु ध्रुवा श्रीश्च पुष्पवन्तस्ततो वयम्। क्षत्रियो बाहुवीर्यस्तु न तथा वाक्यवीर्यवान्। अप्रगल्भं वचस्तस्य तस्माद् बार्हद्रथेरितम्॥
en: Persons who adorn themselves with flowers always gain prosperity, therefore we have adorned ourselves with flowers. The Kshatriyas are powerful in their prowess of arms and in the prowess of speech. O son of Brihadratha it is therefore the speeches of the Kshatriyas are never audacious.

sn: स्ववीर्यं क्षत्रियाणां तु बाह्वोर्धाता न्यवेशयत्। तद् दिदृक्षसि चेद् राजन् द्रष्टास्यद्य न संशयः॥
en: O king, the creator has placed his own energy in the arms of the Kshatriya. If you desire to see it, you will certainly see it today.

sn: अद्वारेण रिपोर्गेहं द्वारेण सुहृदो गृहान्। प्रविशन्ति नरा धीरा द्वाराण्येतानि धर्मतः॥
en: The intelligent men enter the house of the enemy through a way which is not the general gate; but in the house of a friend they enter by the right gate. This is the rule of the ordinance.

sn: कार्यवन्तो गृहानेत्य शत्रुतो नार्हणां वयम्। प्रतिगृह्णीम तद् विद्धि एतन्नः शाश्वतं व्रतम्॥
en: O king, know that this is our eternal vow that having entered the house of the enemy for the purpose of accomplishing an object, we do not accept the worship offered by him.

sn: जरासंध उवाच न स्मरामि कदा वैरं कृतं युष्माभिरित्युत। चिन्तयंश्च न पश्यामि भवतां प्रति वैकृतम्॥
en: Jarasandha said I do not recollect when I have ever done you any injury. After careful reflection, I cannot recollect the injury I have done you.

sn: वैकृते वासति कथं मन्यध्वं मामनागसम्। अरिं वै ब्रूत हे विप्राः सतां समय एष हि॥
en: O Brahmanas, when I have never done you any harm, why do you consider me, who am innocent, as your enemy? Tell me truly, for this is the rule followed by the honest.

sn: अथ धर्मोपघाताद्धि मनः समुपतप्यते। योऽनागसि प्रसजति क्षत्रियो हि न संशयः॥ अतोऽन्यथा चरँल्लोके धर्मज्ञः सन् महारथः। वृजिनां गतिमाप्नोति श्रेयसोऽप्युपहन्ति च।॥
en: If injury is done to one's Dharma and Artha, the mind feels pain. Even a great carwarrior, well versed in all the precepts of morality, gets the fate of sinners and falls off from prosperity, if he injures an innocent man.

sn: त्रैलोक्ये क्षत्रधर्मो हि श्रेयान् वै साधुचारिणाम्। नान्यं धर्मं प्रशंसन्ति ये च धर्मविदो जनाः॥
en: For honest men the practices of the Kshatriyas are the best in the three worlds. The men that are learned in the precepts of virtue praise nothing else (then the practices of the Kshatriyas).

sn: तस्य मेऽद्य स्थितस्येह स्वधर्मे नियतात्मनः। अनागसं प्रजानां च प्रमादादिव जल्पथ॥
en: I adhere to the practices of my order with a steadily soul. I never injure any of my subjects. In bringing this charge against me, it appears you speck in error.

sn: श्रीकृष्ण उवाच कुलकार्यं महाबाहो कश्चिदेकः कुलोद्वहः। वहते यस्तन्नियोगाद् वयमभ्युद्यतास्त्वयि॥
en: Krishna said O mighty-armed (hero), there is one who upholds the dignity of a (royal) line. We have come against you at his command.

sn: त्वया चोपहृता राजन् क्षत्रिया लोकवासिनः। तदागः क्रूरमुत्पाद्य मन्यसे किमनागसम्॥
en: O king, the Kshatriyas of the world have been brought captive by you. Having done this cruel wrong, how do you consider yourself innocent?

sn: राजा राज्ञः कथं साधून् हिंस्यानृपतिसत्तम। तद् राज्ञः संनिगृह्य त्वं रुद्रायोपजिहीर्षसि॥
en: O best of kings, how can a man, being a king himself, act cruelly against other virtuous kings? After persecuting them, you want to offer them as sacrifices to Rudra.

sn: अस्मांस्तदेनो गच्छेद्धि कृतं वार्हद्रथ त्वया। वयं हि शक्ता धर्मस्य रक्षणे धर्मचारिणः॥
en: O son of Brihadratha, this sin, committed by you, may even touch us. We practise virtue, and we are capable of protecting virtue.

sn: मनुष्याणां समालम्भो न च दृष्टः कदाचन। स कथं मानुषैर्देवं यष्टुमिच्छसि शङ्करम्॥
en: The slaughter of human beings as sacrifice to the gods is never seen. Why do you then desire to sacrifice human beings to the god Sankara?

sn: सवर्णो हि सवर्णानां पशुसंज्ञां करिष्यसि। कोऽन्य एव यथा हि त्वं जरासंध वृथामतिः॥
en: You are calling all men belonging to your own orders as beasts. O Jarasandha, foolish as you are, who else is capable of doing it?

sn: यस्यां यस्यामवस्थायां यद्यत् कर्म करोति यः। तस्यां तस्यामवस्थायां तत्फलं समवाप्नुयात्॥
en: Whatever actions are performed by a man under whatever circumstances, he gets the fruits of those those actions under whatever circumstances they may be performed.

sn: ते त्वां ज्ञातिक्षयकरं वयमार्तानुसारिणः। ज्ञातिवृद्धिनिमित्तार्थं विनिहन्तुमिहागताः॥
en: We are desirous of helping all distiessed people. For the Prosperity of our race, we have come here to kill you, the slayer of our relatives.

sn: नास्ति लोके पुमानन्यः क्षत्रियेष्विति चैव तत्। मन्यसे स च ते राजन् सुमहान् बुद्धिविप्लवः॥
en: O king, you consider there is not a Kshatriya equal to you in the world; it is a great error of your judgement.

sn: को हि जानन्नभिजनमात्मवान् क्षत्रियो नृप। नाविशेत् स्वर्गमतुलं रणानन्तरमव्ययम्॥
en: O king, what Kshatriya is there who, possessing greatness of mind and recollecting the dignity of his own parentage, would not ascend the unrivalled heaven by falling on the field of battle?

sn: स्वर्गं ह्येव समास्थाय रणयज्ञेषु दीक्षिताः। जयन्ति क्षत्रिया लोकांस्तद् विद्धि मनुजर्षभ॥
en: O best of men, know that Kshatriyas, being installed in the sacrifice of war with the view of heaven before them, conquer the whole world.

sn: स्वर्गयोनिर्महद् ब्रह्म स्वर्गयोनिर्महद् यशः। स्वर्गयोनिस्तपो युद्धे मृत्युः सोऽव्यभिचारवान्॥
en: The study of Brahma, great fame ascetic penances and death in battle are acts that lead men to heaven. The attainment of heaven by the three other acts may be uncertain, but death in battle has heaven for its certain result.

sn: एष न्द्रिो वैजयन्तो गुणैर्नित्यं समाहितः। येनासुरान् पराजित्य जगत् पाति शतक्रतुः॥
en: It is graced with many merits; it is through this, Shatakratu (Indra) has became what he is; he rules the universe by vanquishing the Asuras.

sn: स्वर्गमार्गाय कस्य स्याद् विग्रहो वै यथा तव। मागधैर्विपुलैः सैन्यैर्बाहुल्यबलदर्पितः॥
en: Fighting with you is the certain path to heaven, for you are proud of your prowess of arms and of the excessive might of your large Magadha army.

sn: मावमंस्थाः परान् राजन्नस्ति वीर्यं नरे नरे। समं तेजस्त्वया चैव विशिष्टं वा नरेश्वर॥
en: O king, do not disregard others; velour exists in every man. O king of men, there are men whose velour is equal or superior to yours.

sn: यावदेतदसम्बुद्धं तावदेव भवेत् तव। विषह्यमेतदस्माकमतो राजन् ब्रवीमि ते॥
en: So long it is not known (to the world) so long only you are famous. O king, I tell you, your prowess can be borne by us.

sn: जहि त्वं सदृशेष्वेव मानं दर्पं च मागध। मा गमः ससुतामात्य सबलश्च यमक्षयम्॥
en: O Magadha king, throw away your superiority and pride in the presence of those that are your equals. Do not go to the abode of Yama with your sons, ministers, and troops.

sn: दम्भोद्भवः कार्तवीर्य उत्तरश्च बृहद्रथः। श्रेयसो ह्यवमन्येह विनेशुः सबला नृपाः॥
en: Dambhodhva, Kartavirya, Uttara, and Brihadratha, all these kings met with their destruction, along with all their troops for disregarding their superiors.

sn: युयुक्षमाणास्त्वत्तो हि न वयं ब्राह्मणा ध्रुवम्। शौरिरस्मि हृषिकेशो नृवीरौ पाण्डवाविमौ। अनयोर्मातुलेयं च कृष्णं मां विद्धि ते रिपुम्॥
en: We are desirous of liberating the captive monarchs from you. Know that we are certainly not Brahmanas. I am Hrishikesha Shauri, and these two are the Pandavas.

sn: त्वामाह्वयामहे राजन् स्थिरो युध्यस्व मागध। मुञ्च वा नृपतीन् सर्वान् गच्छ वा त्वं यमक्षयम्॥
en: O king, O monarch of the Magadha kingdom, we challenge you (to a. single combat). Fight with us with steadiness. Either liberate the kings (now kept prisoner by you) or go the abode of Yama.

sn: जरासंध उवाच नाजितान् वै नरपतीनहमाददि कांश्चन। अजितः पर्यवस्थाता कोऽत्र यो न मया जितः॥
en: Jarasandha said I never make a king prisoner without first defeating him. Who is kept prisoner here who has not been defeated (by me)?

sn: क्षत्रियस्यैतदेवाहुर्धर्म्य कृष्णोपजीवनम्। विक्रम्य वशमानीय कामतो यत् समाचरेत्॥
en: O Krishna, it has been said that the duty of the Kshatriya is to bring others under his sway by displaying his own prowess, and then to treat them in the way he likes.

sn: देवतार्थमुपाहत्य राज्ञः कृष्ण कथं भयात्। अहमद्य विमुच्येयं क्षात्रं व्रतमनुस्मरन्।॥
en: O Krishna, recollecting the duty of a Kshatriya, how can I from fear to day liberate the kings collected by me for the purpose of the god?

sn: सैन्यं सैन्येन व्यूढेन एक एकेन वा पुनः। द्वाभ्यां त्रिभिर्वा योत्स्येऽहं युगपत् पृथगेव वा॥
en: I am ready to fight with troops against troops placed in a battle array, or alone against (you) one, two or three, either at the sometime or separately.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्त्वा जरासंधः सहदेवाभिषेचनम्। आज्ञापयत् तदा राजा युयुत्सुर्भीमकर्मभिः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having said this, and being willing to fight with those heroes of fearful deeds (Krishna etc.), Jarasandha ordered his son Sahadeva to be installed on the throne.

sn: स तु सेनापति राजा सस्मार भरतर्षभ। कौशिकं चित्रसेनं च तस्मिन् युद्ध उपस्थिते॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, when the day for the combat came, the king thought of his commanders-in-chief, Kaushika and Chitrasena.

sn: ययोस्ते नामनी राजन् हंसेति डिम्भकेति च। पूर्वं संकथितं पुम्भिर्नृलोके लोकसत्कृते॥
en: O king, they were formerly called by the ever renowned names of Hansa and Dimbhaka by every body in the world.

sn: तं तु राजन् विभुः शौरी राजानं बलिनां वरम्। स्मृत्वा पुरुषशार्दूल: शार्दूलसमविक्रमम्॥ सत्यसंधो जरासंधं भुवि भीमपराक्रमम्। भागमन्यस्य निर्दिष्टमवध्यं मधुभिर्मधे॥ नात्मनाऽऽत्मवतां मुख्य इयेष मधुसूदनः। ब्राह्मीमाज्ञां पुरस्कृत्य हन्तुं हलधरानुजाः॥
en: O king, that foremost of all powerful men, the self-controlled lord Shauri (Krishna), that best of men, that slayer of Madhu, ever de:oted to truth, the younger brother of Haladhara, knowing that the king of Magadha was destined to be killed in battle by Bhima and not by the destroyer of Madhu, did not at the command of Brahma desire to kill that foremost of all powerful men, that hero as powerful as the tiger, that warrior of terrible valour, king Jarasandha.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततस्तं निश्चितात्मानं युद्धाय यदुनन्दनः। उवाच वाग्मी राजानं जरासंधमधोक्षजः॥
en: Vaishampayana said The excellent speaker, the descendant of Yadu (Krishna), then thus addressed the king Jarasandha who was resolved upon fight.

sn: श्रीकृष्ण उवाच त्रयाणां केन ते राजन् योद्धमुत्सहते मनः। अस्मदन्यतमेनेह सज्जीभवतु को युधि॥
en: Krishna said O king, with whom amongst us three you have the mind to fight? Who amongst us should be ready for battle (with you)?

sn: एवमुक्तः स नृपतिर्युद्धं वने महाद्युतिः। जरासंधस्ततो राजा भीमसेनेन मागधः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having been thus addressed, the king of Magadha, the greatly effulgent Jarasandha, desired to fight with Bhimasena.

sn: आदाय रोचनां माल्यं मङ्गल्यान्यपराणि च। धारयन्नगदान् मुख्यान् निर्वृतीवेदनानि च। उपतस्थे जरासंधं युयुत्सं वै पुरोहितः॥
en: The priest brought the yellow pigment obtained from the cow, garlands of flowers, and other auspicious articles, and also various excellent medicines for restoring lost consciousness and for alleviating pains. He came (with these articles) to the king Jarasandha who was panting for fight.

sn: कृतस्वस्त्ययनो राजा ब्राह्मणेन यशस्विना। समनह्यज्जरासंधः क्षात्रं धर्ममनुस्मरन्॥
en: The king's propitiatory ceremonies with benedictions having been performed by an illustrious Brahmana, Jarasandha, remembering the duty of a Kshatriya, dressed himself for battle.

sn: अवमुच्य किरीटं स केशान् समनुगृह्य च। उदतिष्ठज्जरासंधो वेलातिग इवार्णवः॥
en: Removing his crown and properly binding his hair, Jarasandha stood up like an ocean bursting through its shore.

sn: उवाच मतिमान् राजा भीमं भीमपराक्रमः। भीम योत्स्ये त्वया सार्धं श्रेयसा निर्जितं वरम्॥
en: The terribly powerful and intelligent king then thus spoke to Bhima, “O Bhima, I shall fight with you. It is better to be vanquished by a superior man."

sn: एवमुक्त्वा जरासंधो भीमसेनमरिंदमः। प्रत्युद्ययौ महातेजाः शक्रं बल इवासुरः॥
en: Having said this, the greatly effulgent Jarasandha, that chastiser of foes, rushed at Bhimasena like the Asura Bala at Shakra (Indra).

sn: ततः सम्मन्त्र्य कृष्णेन कृतस्वस्त्ययनो बली। भीमसेनो जरासंधमाससाद युयुत्सया॥
en: After having consulted with Krishna and having his propitiatory ceremonies with benedictions been performed by him (Krishna), the powerful Bhimasena also advanced towards Jarasandha with the desire of fight.

sn: ततस्तौ नरशार्दूलौ बाहुशस्त्रौ समीयतुः। वीरौ परमसंहृष्टावन्योन्यजयकाक्षिणौ॥
en: Then those two best of men, those two greatly powerful heroes with their bare arms as their only weapons, being each eagerly desirous of defeating the other, cheerfully engaged in the fight.

sn: करग्रहणपूर्वं तु कृत्वा पादाभिवन्दनम्। कक्षैः कक्षां विधुन्वानावास्फोटं तत्र चक्रतुः॥
en: Seizing each other's arms and twining each other's legs, they slapped their arm-pits. They caused the arena to tremble with that sounds.

sn: स्कन्धे दो• समाहत्य निहत्य च मुहुर्मुहुः। अङ्गमङ्गैः समाश्लिष्य पुनरास्फालनं विभो॥
en: O lord, seizing each other's necks with their hands now and again, and dragging and pushing them with great force, each pressed every limb of the other's body and began to roar.

sn: चित्रहस्तादिकं कृत्वा कक्षाबन्धं च चक्रतुः। गलगण्डाभिघातेन सस्फुलिङ्गेन चाशनिम्॥
en: Sometimes stretching their arms, sometimes drawing them close, sometimes raising them up and sometimes dropping them down, they began to seize each other. Striking neck against neck and forehead against forehead, they caused fiery sparks to emit like the flashes of lightning.

sn: बाहुपाशादिकं कृत्वा पादाहतशिरावुभौ। उरोहस्तं ततश्चक्रे पूर्णकुम्भो प्रयुज्य तौ॥ करसम्पीडनं कृत्वा गर्जन्तौ वारणाविव। नर्दन्तौ मेघसंकाशौ बाहुप्रहरणावुभौ॥
en: Grasping each other by arms in various ways and kicking each other with such force as to impress the innermost nerves, they struck at cach other's breast with clenched fists and with their bare arms at their only weapons. Roaring like clouds, they grasped and struck each other like two mad elephants fighting with their trunks.

sn: तलेनाहन्यमानौ तु अन्योन्यं कृतवीक्षणौ। सिंहाविव सुसंक्रुद्धावाकृष्याकृष्य युध्यताम्॥
en: Becoming angry at each other's blow they dragged and pushed each other, and they fought on, looking fiercely at each other like two angry lions.

sn: अङ्गेनाङ्गं समापीड्य बाहुभ्यामुभयोरपि। आवृत्य बाहुभिश्चापि उदरं च प्रचक्रतुः॥
en: Each striking every limb of the other, and each catching hold of the other's waist, they hurled each other to a great distance.

sn: उभौ कट्यां सुपार्श्वे तु तक्षवन्तौ च शिक्षितौ। अधोहस्तं स्वकण्द्दे तूदरस्योरसि चाक्षिपत्॥
en: Both the heroes were greatly accomplished in wrestling; each clasping the other with arms and each dragging the other to himself, they began to press each other with great force.

sn: सर्वातिक्रान्तमर्यादं पृष्ठभङ्गं च चक्रतुः। सम्पूर्णमूर्छा बाहुभ्यां पूणकुम्भं प्रचक्रतुः॥
en: They then performed the grandest of all feats in wrestling namely Prishthabhanga, they also performed the feats, called Sampurva Nemcha and Purnakumbha.

sn: तृणपीडं यथाकामं पूर्णयोगं समुष्टिकम्। एवमादीनि युद्धानि प्रकुर्वन्तौ परस्परम्॥
en: They also performed the feats Trinapida at pleasure, and then the feat Purna yoga with fists. Thus did not two heroes fight with each other.

sn: तयोर्युद्धं ततो द्रष्टुं समेताः पुरवासिनः। ब्राह्मणा वणिजश्चैव क्षत्रियाश्च सहस्रशः॥ शूद्राश्च नरशार्दूल स्त्रियो वृद्धाश्च सर्वशः। निरन्तरमभूत् तत्र जनौधैरभिसंवृतम्॥
en: O best of men, thousands of citizens, consisting of Brahmanas, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas and Shudras, and also women and even old men, came out and assembled there to witness the fight. The crowed became so great that it grew to be a solid mass of human beings with no space between two persons.

sn: तयोरथ भुजाधातान्निग्रहप्रग्रहात् तथा। आसीत् सुभीमसम्पातो वज्रपर्वतयोरिव॥
en: The sound they made by the slapping of arins by the seizing of each other's necks, and by the grasping of each other's legs became so loud that if resembled the roar of thunder or the noise of a falling cliff.

sn: उभौ परमसंहृष्टौ बलेन बलिनां वरौ। अन्योन्यस्यान्तरं प्रेप्सू परस्परजयैषिणौ॥
en: Both of them were foremost of strong and powerful men, and both took great delight in such fights. Each was eager to vanquish the other, and each was on the alert to take advantage of the slightest carelessness of the other.

sn: तद् भीममुत्सार्यजनं युद्धमासीदुपप्लवे। बलिनोः संयुगे राजन् वृत्रवासवयोरिव॥
en: O king, the powerful Bhima and Jarasandha, like Vitra and Vasava of old, terribly fought on in the arena, driving the people at times by the motions of their hands.

sn: प्रकर्षणाकर्षणाभ्यामनुकर्षविकर्षणैः। आचकर्षतुरन्योन्यं जानुभिश्चावजघ्नतुः॥ ततः शब्देन महता भर्त्सयन्तौ परस्परम्। पाषाणसंघातनिभैः प्रहारैरभिजघ्नतुः॥ व्यूढोरस्कौ दीर्घभुजौ नियुद्धकुशलावुभौ। बाहुभिः समसज्जेतामायसैः परिचैरिव॥
en: Pressing each other forward and dragging each other backward, throwing each other's face downwards and side ways with sudden jerks, they dreadfully mangled each other. They struck each other with keen joints. They loudly addressed each other in stinging words; they struck each other with keen joints. They loudly addressed each other in stinging words; they struck each other with clenched fists, the blow descending like a mass of stone on another mass of stone. With broad shoulders and long arms the two well-skilled wrestlers struck each other with their long arms which were like clubs made of iron.

sn: कार्तिकस्य तु मासस्य प्रवृत्तं प्रथमेऽहनि। अनाहारं दिवारात्रमविश्रान्तमवर्तत॥ तद् वृत्तं तु त्रयोदश्यां समवेतं महात्मनोः। चतुर्दश्यां निशायां तु निवृत्तो मागध: क्लमात्॥
en: The fight began on the first day of the month of Kartika, and those two illustrious heroes fought on continuously without food, and without intermission of day or night till the thirteenth day. It was on the night of the fourteenth day, the Magadha king stopped from fatigue.

sn: तं राजानं तथा क्लान्तं दृष्ट्वा राजञ्जनार्दनः। उवाच भीमकर्माणं भीमं सम्बोधयन्निव॥
en: O king, seeing the monarch (Jarasandha) tried, Janardana (Krishna) thus spoke to Bhima of terrible deeds to encourage him.

sn: क्लान्तः शत्रुर्न कौन्तेय लभ्यः पीडयितुं रणे। पीड्यमानो हि कात्स्न्येन जह्याज्जीवितमात्मनः॥
en: Krishna said O son of Kunti, the foe that has become tried in the fight.cannot be pressed. If pressed at such a time, he may even die.

sn: तस्मात् ते नैव कौन्तेय पीडनीयो जनाधिपः। सममेतेन युध्यस्व बाहुभ्यां भरतर्षभ॥
en: Therefore, O son of Kunti, you should not oppress this king (now). O best of the Bharata race, fight with your arms only in such a way as your antagonist may be equal to you.

sn: एवमुक्तः स कृष्णेन पाण्डवः परवीरहा। जरासंधस्य तद् रूपं ज्ञात्वा चक्रे मतिं वधे॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having been thus addressed by Krishna, and knowing the state of Jarasandha, the Pandava (Bhima), the slayer of hostile heroes, determined to kill him.

sn: ततस्तमजितं जेतुं जरासंधं वृकोदरः। संरम्भं बलिनां श्रेष्ठो जग्राह कुरुनन्दनः॥
en: That foremost of all strong men, that descendant of Kuru, Vrikodara (Bhima), mustered all his strength and courage with the desire of now vanquishing the hitherto unvanquished Jarasandha.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच भीमसेनस्ततः कृष्णमुवाच यदुनन्दनम्। बुद्धिमास्थाय विपुलां जरासंधवधेप्सया॥ नायंपापो मया कृष्ण युक्तः स्यादनुरोधितुम्। प्राणेन यदुशार्दूल बद्धकक्षेण वाससा॥
en: Vaishampayana said Thereupon Bhimsena, his mind firmly set on the desire of killing Jarasandha, thus spoke to the descendant of Yadu, Krishna, "O Krishna, O best of the Yadu race, this wretch is still before me with girded loins and with sufficient strength. He should not be excused by me,”

sn: एवमुक्तस्ततः कृष्णः प्रत्युवाच वृकोदरम्। त्वरयन् पुरुषव्याघ्रो जरासंधवधेप्सया॥ यत् ते दैवं परं सत्त्वं यच्च ते मातरिश्वनः। बलं भीम जरासंधे दर्शयाशु तदद्य नः॥
en: Having been thus addressed, Krishna, that best of men, with the desire of seeing soon an end of Jarasandha, thus replied to Vrikodara (Bhima), “O Bhima, the strength that you have derived from the celestials, the might that you have obtained from Maruta, display them today towards Jarasandha."

sn: एवमुक्तास्तदा भीमो जरासंधमरिंदमः। उत्क्षिप्य भ्रामयामास बलवन्तं महाबलः॥
en: Having been thus addressed, that chastiser of foes, that greatly strong (hero), Bhima, raised up the strong Jarasandha and whirled him on high.

sn: भ्रामयित्वा शतगुणं जानुभ्यां भरतर्षभ। बभञ्ज पृष्ठं संक्षिप्य निष्पिष्य विननाद च॥ करे गृहीत्वा चरणं द्वेधा चक्रे महाबलः॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, having thus whirled him high for one hundred times, he (Bhima) pressed his knee against his (Jarasandha's) backbone and broke his body, into two parts. (Having thus killed him), he roared aloud.

sn: तस्य निष्यिष्यमाणस्य पाण्डवस्य च गर्जतः। अभवत् तुमुलो नादः सर्वप्राणिभंयकरः॥
en: The roar of the Pandava (Bhima), mingled with that of Jarasandha while he was being broken by Bhima's knee, raised such a loud roar that it struck fear into the heart of every creature.

sn: चित्रेसुर्मागधाः सर्वे स्त्रीणां गर्भाश्च सुस्रुवुः। भीमसेनस्य नादेन जरासंधस्य चैव ह॥
en: The people of Magadha becaine dumb with fear; and even many women were prematurely delivered by the roars of Bhima and Jarasandha.

sn: किं नु स्याद्धिमवान् भिन्नः किं नु स्विद् दीर्यते मही। इति वै मागधा जजुर्भीमसेनस्य नि:स्वनात्॥
en: Hearing the roars of Bhima, the people of Magadha thought that either Himalayas were coming down or the earth is being rent asunder.

sn: ततो राज्ञः कुलद्वारि प्रसुप्तमिव तं नृपम्। रात्रौ गतासुमुत्सृज्य निश्चक्रमररिंदमाः॥
en: The chastiser of foes (Krishna) left at night the dead body of the king at the palace gate, as if he was but asleep. They then came out (of the palace).

sn: जरासंधरथं कृष्णो योजयित्वा पताकिनम्। आरोप्य भ्रातरौ चैव मोक्षयामास बान्धवान्॥
en: Krishna made ready the chariot of Jarasandha with the excellent standard and he then placed on it the two brothers (Bhima and Arjuna). He then liberated the friends (the captive kings).

sn: ते वै रत्नभुजं कृष्णं रत्नार्हाः पृथिवीश्वराः। राजानश्चक्रुरासाद्य मोक्षिता महतो भयात्॥
en: Having been freed from their great fear, those monarchs, those kings, those possessors came of gems came to Krishna and presented him with many gems and jewels.

sn: अक्षतः शस्त्रसम्पन्नो जितारिः सह राजभिः। रथमास्थाय तं दिव्यं निर्जगाम गिरिव्रजात्॥
en: Unwounded, (now) with (many) weapons, vanquishing the foe, he (Krishna), riding on the celestials car (of Jarasandha) came out with the kings from the city of Girivraja.

sn: यः स सोदर्यवान् नाम द्वियोधी कृष्णसारथिः। अभ्यासघाती संदृश्यो दुर्जयः सर्वराजभिः॥
en: He, who wielded the bow with both hands, who was invincible to all kings, and who was exceedingly handsome and well skilled in killing the enemy, out with that possessors of great strength Bhima, and Krishna drove the car.

sn: भीमार्जुनाभ्यां योधाभ्यामास्थितः कृष्णसारथिः। शुशुभे रथवर्योऽसौ दुर्जयः सर्वधन्विभिः॥
en: That celestials car, invincible to all warriors, ridden by the heroes, Bhima and Arjuna, and driven by Krishna, looked exceedingly beautiful.

sn: शक्रविष्णू हि संग्रामे चेरतुस्तारकामये। रथेन तेन वै कृष्ण उपारुह्य ययौ तदा॥
en: It was in this very car that Indra and Vishnu fought in the battle of old (with the Asuras) in which Taraka (the wife of Brihaspati) was cause, and the result of which was a great slaughter. Riding on that very car, Krishna now came out.

sn: तप्तचामीकराभेण किङ्किणीजालमालिना। मेघनिर्घोषनादेन जैत्रेणामित्रघातिना॥
en: It possessed the splendour of heated gold, it was adorned with rows of jingling bells, it had wheels that made the clatter like the roars of the clouds, it was ever victorious in battle and it always killed the foes.

sn: येन शक्रो दानवानां जघान नवतीनव। तं प्राप्य समहृष्यन्त रथं ते पुरुषर्षभाः॥
en: Riding on it, Shakra (Indra) killed ninety nine Danavas of old. Those best of men (Krishna & c.) were exceedingly pleased on obtaining this car.

sn: ततः कृष्णं महाबाहुं भ्रातृभ्यां सहितं तदा। रथस्थं मागधा दृष्ट्वा समपद्यन्त विस्मिताः॥
en: Seeing the long-armed Krishna on the chariot with the two brothers, (Bhima and Arjuna), the people of Magadha became very much astonished.

sn: हयैर्दिव्यैः समायुक्तो रथो वायुसमो जवे। अधिष्ठितः स शुशुभे कृष्णेनातीव भारत॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, that car, with which were yoked celestials horses with the speed of the wind and which was driven by Krishna, looked exceedingly beautiful.

sn: असङ्गो देवविहितस्तस्मिन् रथवरे ध्वजः। योजनाद् ददृशे श्रीमानिन्द्रायुधसमप्रभः॥
en: On this best of cars there was a flag-staff without being visibly attached thereto. It was the product of celestials art. That beautiful flat staff could be seen from a distance of a Yojana, and it had the splendour of the rainbow.

sn: चिन्तयामास कृष्णोऽथ गरुत्मन्तं स चाभ्ययात्। क्षणे तस्मिन् स तेनासीच्चैत्यवृक्ष इवोत्थितः॥
en: When coming out, Krishna thought of Garuda. As soon as thought of, he came there like a large tree worshipped by all.

sn: व्यादितास्यैर्महानादैः सह भूतैर्ध्वजालयैः। तस्मिन् रथवरे तस्थौ गरुत्मान् पन्नगाशनः॥
en: The eater of snakes, Garuda of iminense weight of body, sat on that excellent car along with innumerable other open-mouthed and fearfully roaring creatures on its flag-staff.

sn: दुर्निरीक्ष्यो हि भूतानां तेजसाभ्यधिकं बभौ। आदित्य इव मध्याह्ने सहस्रकिरणावृतः॥
en: Thereupon that best of cars be came more dazzling than before; and like the sun in midday, surrounded by thousand rays, it became incapable of being looked at by any living creature.

sn: न स सज्जति वृक्षेषु शस्त्रैश्चापि न रिष्यते। दिव्यो ध्वजवरो राजन् दृश्यते चेह मानुषैः॥
en: O king, such was that celestialsly made and the best flagstaff that it never struck against a tree. The weapons could not any way injure it, although it was visible to the human eye.

sn: तमास्थाय रथं दिव्यं पर्जन्यसमनिःस्वनम्। निर्ययौ पुरुषव्याघ्रः पाण्डवाभ्यां सहाच्युतः॥
en: That best of men, Achyuta (Krishna), riding with the two Pandava (Bhima and Arjuna) on that celestials car, the wheels of which made a clatter like the roars of the clouds, came out (of Girivraja).

sn: यं लेभे वासवाद् राजा वसुस्तस्माद् बृहद्रथः। बृहद्रथात् क्रमेणैव प्राप्तो बार्हद्रथं नृप॥
en: It (the car) was obtained by the king Vasu from Vasava (Indra), From Vasu it was obtained by Brihadratha; from Brihadratha it was in due course obtained by the king (Jarasandha), the son of Brihadratha.

sn: स निर्याय महाबाहुः पुण्डरीकेक्षणस्ततः। गिरिव्रजाद् बहिस्तस्थौ समदेशे महायशाः॥
en: The long armed, the lotus-eyed and the greatly famous (Krishna), coming out (of Girivraja), stopped on a level plain outside the city.

sn: तत्रैनं नागराः सर्वे सत्कारेणाभ्ययुस्तदा। ब्राह्मणप्रमुखा राजन् विधिदृष्टेन कर्मणा॥
en: O king, all the citizens with the Brahmans at their head then hastened there to adore him according to the due rites of the ordinance.

sn: बन्धनाद् विप्रमुक्ताश्च राजानो मधुसूदनम्। पूजयामासुरूचुश्च स्तुतिपूर्वमिदं वचः॥
en: The kings, who had been liberated from their confinement, worshipped the slayer of Madhu; and they thus spoke to him eulogistic words.

sn: नैतच्चित्रं महाबाहो त्वयि देवकिनन्दने। भीमार्जुनबलोपेते धर्मस्य प्रतिपालनम्॥ जरासंधहदे घोरे दुःखपङ्के निमज्जताम्। राज्ञां समभ्युद्धरणं यदिदं कृतमद्य वै॥
en: O mighty armed (hero), O son of Devaki, such an act of virtue is not (at all) wonderful in you. Assisted as you are by the prowess of Bhima and Arjuna, you have to-day rescued the kings who sank in the fearful mire of sorrow in the lake of Jarasandha.

sn: विष्णो समवसन्नानां गिरिदुर्गे सुदारुणे। दिष्ट्या मोक्षाद् यशो दीप्तमाप्तं ते यदुनन्दन॥
en: O Vishnu, O descendant of Yadu, we were languishing in the fearful hill-fort (of Jaransandha); from our good fortune alone, you have rescued us and earned a great renown.

sn: किं कुर्मः पुरुषव्याघ्र शाधि नः प्रणतिस्थितान्। कृतमित्येव तद् विद्धि नृपैर्यद्यपि दुष्करम्॥
en: O best of men, we bow to you, command us what we shall do. However difficult it may be to carry out your command, know, it is already carried out by the kings (ourselves)”.

sn: तानुवाच हृषीकेशः समाश्वास्य महामनाः। युधिष्ठिरो राजसूयं क्रतुमाहर्तुमिच्छति॥
en: Giving them every assurance, thus replied to them Hrishikesha (Krishna), "Yudhishthira is desirous of performing the Rajasuya (sacrifice).

sn: तस्य धर्मप्रवृत्तस्य पार्थिवत्वं चिकीर्षतः। सर्वैर्भवद्भिर्विज्ञाय साहाय्यं क्रियतामिति॥
en: That king, ever devoted to virtue, is solicitous to acquire the imperial dignity. Knowing this from me, help him in his attempt."

sn: ततः सुप्रीतमनसस्ते नृपा नृपसत्तम। तथेत्येवाब्रुवन् सर्वे प्रतिगृह्यास्य तां गिरम्॥
en: O best of kings, thereupon all those monarchs, saying "Be it so, “accepted with joyous heart all that Krishna said.

sn: रत्नभाजं च दाशार्हं चक्रुस्ते पृथिवीश्वराः। कृच्छ्राज्जग्राह गोविन्दस्तेषां तदनुकम्पया॥
en: The monarchs made presents of jewels to the hero of Dasarha race (Krishna). Govinda (Krishna), out of kindness towards them, only took a portion of those presents.

sn: जरासंधात्मजश्चैव सहदेवो महामनाः। निर्ययौ सजनामात्यः पुरस्कृत्यः पुरोहितम्॥
en: The son of Jarasandha, the high-minded Sahadeva, came out there with his relatives and his ministers, his priest being at the head of the procession.

sn: स नीचैः प्रणतो भूत्वा बहुरत्नपुरोगमः। सहदेवो नृणां देवं वासुदेवमुपस्थितः॥
en: Sahadeva bowed low before the god among men, Vasudeva; and presenting him many gems and jewels, he worshipped him.

sn: भयार्ताय ततस्तस्मै कृष्णो दत्त्वाभयं तदा। आददेऽस्य महार्हाणि रत्नानि पुरुषोत्तमः॥
en: That best of men (Krishna) gave every assurance to that very much frightened prince and accepted his very valuable presents.

sn: अभ्यषिञ्चत तत्रैव जरासंधात्मजं मुदा। गत्वैकत्वं च कृष्णेन पार्थाभ्यां चैव सत्कृतः॥ विवेश राजा द्युतिमान् बार्हद्रथपुरं नृप। अभिषिक्तो महाबाहुर्जारासंधिर्महात्मभिः॥
en: He (Krishna) gladly installed there the son of Jarasandha; and thus being installed on the throne of Magadha by those exalted men and having been obtained the friendship of Krishna and being treated with respect and kindness by the two sons of Pritha, the mighty armed and the illustrious son of Jarasandha (Sahadeva) entered the city of the son of Brihadratha (Jarasandha).

sn: कृष्णस्तु सह पार्थाभ्यां श्रिया परमया युतः। रत्नान्यादाय भूरीणि प्रययौ पुरुषर्षभः॥
en: That best of men (Krishna), accompanied by the sons of Pritha and enriched with much wealth and laden with numerous jewels, went away (from Girivraja).

sn: इन्द्रप्रस्थमुपागम्य पाण्डवाभ्यां सहाच्युतः। समेत्य धर्मराजानं प्रीयमाणोऽभ्यभाषत॥
en: Achyuta (Krishna), accompanied by the two Pandavas (Bhima and Arjuna), arrived at Indraprastha and went to Yudhishthira. He joyfully addressed the king and said,

sn: दिष्ट्या भीमेन बलवाञ्जरासंधो निपातितः। राजानो मोक्षिताश्चैव बन्धनान्नृपसत्तम॥
en: "O best of kings, the powerful Jarasandha has been killed by Bhima from good fortune. The kings, confined at Girivraja, have all been liberated.

sn: दिष्ट्या कुशलिनौ चेमौ भीमसेनधनंजयौ। पुनः स्वनगरं प्राप्तावक्षताविति भारत॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, from good fortune, these two Bhima and Dhananjaya (Arjuna), are well. They have arrived at their own city unwounded”.

sn: ततो युधिष्ठिरः कृष्णं पूजयित्वा यथार्हतः। भीमेनार्जुनौ चैव प्रहृष्टः परिषस्वजे॥
en: Then Yudhishthira worshipped Krishna as he deserved; and he embrace Bhima and Arjuna in joy.

sn: ततः क्षीणे जरासंधे भ्रातृभ्यां विहितं जयम्। अजातशत्रुरासाद्य मुमुदे भ्रातृभिः सह॥
en: Having obtained victory through the agency of his brothers by the death of Jarasandha, Ajatashatru (Yudhishthira) passed his time with his brothers in great merriment.

sn: यथावयः समागम्य भ्रातृभिः सह पाण्डवः। सत्कृत्य पूजयित्वा च विसर्सज नराधिपान्॥
en: The Pandava (Yudhishthira) with his brothers came to the kings (who had come to Indraprastha). Entertaining and worshipping them each according to his age, he sent them away.

sn: युधिष्ठिराभ्यनुज्ञातास्ते नृपा हृष्टमानसाः। जग्मुः स्वेदशास्त्वरिता यानरुच्चावचैस्ततः॥
en: Having been commanded by Yudhishthira, those kings with joyful hearts and without any further loss of time started on their excellent vehicles for their own respective kingdoms.

sn: एवं पुरुषशार्दूलो महाबुद्धिर्जनार्दनः। पाण्डवैर्घातयामास जरासंधमरिं तदा॥
en: O king, thus did that best of men, the greatly intelligent Janardana (Krishna) cause his foe Jarasandha to be killed through the instrumentality of the Pandavas.

sn: घातयित्वा जरासंधं बुद्धिपूर्वमरिंदमः। धर्मराजनमनुज्ञाप्य पृथां कृष्णां च भारत॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, having caused the death of Jarasandha by policy, that chastiser of foes, (Krishna) took leave of Yudhishthira, Pritha, (Kunti), Krishna (Draupadi).

sn: सुभद्रां भीमसेनं च फाल्गुनं यमजौ तथा। धौम्यमामन्त्रयित्वा च प्रययौ स्वां पुरीं प्रति॥
en: Subhadra, Bhimasena, Falguni (Arjuna), and the twins (Nakula and Sahadeva). Taking leave of Dhaumya, he started for his own city (Dwarka).

sn: तेनैव स्थमुख्येन मनसस्तुल्यगामिना। धर्मराजविसृष्टेन दिव्येनानादयन् दिशः॥
en: On that celestialsly-made and the best of cars, which possessed the speed of mind, and which was given to him by Dharmaraja (Yudhishthira), and which filled the ten points of the horizon with the rattle of his wheels.

sn: ततो युधिष्ठिरमुखाः पाण्डवा भरतर्षभ। प्रदक्षिणमकुर्वन्त कृष्णमक्लिष्टकारिणम्॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, when Krishna was about to start, the Pandavas with Yudhishthira at their head walked round that best of men (Krishna) who was never fatigued with exertion.

sn: ततो गते भगवति कृष्णे देवकिनन्दने। यं लब्ध्वा सुविपुलं राज्ञां दत्त्वाभयं तदा॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, having acquired that great victory and having also dispelled the fears of the kings, when the illustrious Krishna, the son of Devaki went away,

sn: संवर्धितं यशो भूयः कर्मणा तेन भारत। द्रौपद्याः पाण्डवा राजन् परां प्रीतिमवर्धयन्॥
en: That feat of his increased the fame of the Pandavas. O descendant of Bharata, O king, the Pandavas (thus) increased the great happiness of Draupadi.

sn: तस्मिन् काले तु यद् युक्तं धर्मकामार्थसंहितम्। तद् राजा धर्मतश्चक्रे प्रजापालनकीर्तनम्॥
en: Whatever is consistent with Dharma. Artha and Kama continued at that time to be properly performed by king Yudhishthira in the exercise of his duties in protecting his subjects.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच पार्थः प्राप्य धनुः श्रेष्ठमक्षय्यौ च महेषुधी। रथं ध्वजं सभां चैव युधिष्ठिरमभाषत॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having obtained that best of bows (Gandiva) and the couple of inexhaustible quivers and the car and the (ape standard) flagstaff, Arjuna spoke to Yudhishthira thus.

sn: अर्जुन उवाच धनुरस्त्रं शरा वीर्यं पक्षो भूमिर्यशो बलम्। प्राप्तमेतन्मया राजन् दुष्प्रापं यदभीप्सितम्॥
en: Arjuna said O king, bow, weapons, great prowess, allies, dominions, fame, troops, all these have been obtained by me, though they are all difficult to be gained, however a man may desire to have them.

sn: तत्र कृत्यमहं मन्ये कोशस्य परिवधनम्। करमाहारयिष्यामि राज्ञः सर्वान् नृपोत्तम॥
en: O best of kings, I think we should now do that by which we shall be able to increase our treasury. I desire to make the (other) kings pay tribute to us.

sn: विजयाय प्रयास्यामि दिशं धनदपालिताम्। तिथावथ मुहूर्ते च नक्षत्रे चाभिपूजिते॥
en: I shall start, in an auspicious moment of a holy day of the moon under a favourable constellation, to conquer the kingdoms situated in the quarter protected by the lord of wealth (Kubera).

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच धनंजयवचः श्रुत्वा धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः। स्निग्धगम्भीरनादिन्या तं गिरा प्रत्यभाषत।॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having heard the words of Dhananjaya (Arjuna), Dharmaraja Yudhishthira thus replied to him in a grave and calm voice.

sn: स्वस्तिवाच्याहतो विप्रान् प्रयाहि भरतर्षभ। दुर्हदामप्रहर्षाय सुहृदां नन्दनाय च॥
en: Yudhishthira said O best of the Bharata race, start but first cause the holy Brahmanas to utter benedictions on you, so that you may plunge your enemies into grief and make your friends happy.

sn: विजयस्ते ध्रुवं पार्थ प्रियं काममवाप्स्यसि। इत्युक्तः प्रययौ पार्थः सैन्येन महताऽऽवृतः॥
en: O Partha, victory will surely be yours. Your desires will surely be fulfilled. Vaishampayana said Having been thus addressed, Arjuna, surrounded by a large number of troops, started (for conquest).

sn: अग्निदत्तेन दिव्येन रथेनाद्भुतकर्मणा। तथैव भीमसेनोऽपि यमौ च पुरुषर्षभौ॥ ससैन्याः प्रययुः सर्वे धर्मराजेन पूजिताः। दिशं धनपतेरिष्टामजयत् पाकशासनिः॥
en: He started on the celestials car of great deeds which he has obtained from Agni. Bhimasena, and those best of men the longarmed twins Nakul and Sahadeva, also having been affectionately worshipped by Dharmaraja Yudhishthira, started (for conquest). The son of the chastiser of Paka (Arjuna) conquered all the countries situated in the direction protected by the lord of wealth (Kubera).

sn: भीमसेनस्तथा प्राची सहदेवस्तु दक्षिणाम्। प्रतीची नकुलो राजन् दिशं व्यजयतास्त्रवित्॥
en: O king, Bhimasena conquered the East, Sahadeva, the South, and well skilled in arms, Nakula, conquered the west.

sn: खाण्डवप्रस्थमध्यस्थो धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः। आसीत् परमया लक्ष्म्या सुहृद्गणवृतः प्रभुः॥
en: Surrounded by his friends and relatives, the lord Dharmaraja Yudhishthira lived in the enjoyment of great affluence with in Khandavaprastha.

sn: जनमेजय उवाच दिशामभिजय ब्रह्मन् विस्तरेणानुकीर्तय। न हि तृप्यामि पूर्वेषां शृण्वानश्चरितं महत्॥
en: Janamejaya said O Brahmana, narrate to me in full the history of the conquests of the various directions (by the Pandavas). I am not satiated with listening to the great history of my ancestors.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच धनंजयस्य वक्ष्यामि विजयं पूर्वमेव ते। यौगपद्येन पार्हि निर्जितेयं वसुन्धरा॥
en: Vaishampayana said The earth was conquered simultaneously by all the sons of Pritha. I shall first describe the conquest of Dhannajaya (Arjuna).

sn: पूर्वं कुलिन्दविषये वशे चक्रे महीपतीन्। धनंजयो महाबाहु तितीव्रण कर्मणा॥
en: The mighty armed Dhananjaya, by the greatest courageous feats first, conquered the king of the Kulindas.

sn: आनर्तान् कालकूटांश्च कुलिन्दांश्च विजित्य सः। सुमण्डलं च विजितं कृतवान् सहसैनिकम्॥
en: Having conquered the Kulindas, the Anartas and the Kalakutas, he conquered Sumandala with his troops.

sn: स तेन सहितो राजन् सव्यसाची परंतपः। विजिग्ये शाकलं द्वीपं प्रतिविन्ध्यं च पार्थिवम्॥
en: O king, the chastiser of foes, Savyasachi (Arjuna) conquered with him (Sumandala) the island of Shakala, and also the king Prativindhya.

sn: शाकलद्वीपवासाश्च सप्तद्वीपेषु ये नृपाः। अर्जुनस्य च सैन्यैस्तैर्विग्रहस्तुमलोऽभवत्॥
en: Shakala was one of the seven islands of the earth, and there were many kings o that island. A fearful battle took place between them and their troops and Arjuna.

sn: स तानपि महेष्वासान् विजिग्ये भरतर्षभ। तैरेव सहितः सर्वैः प्राग्ज्योतिषमुपाद्रवत्॥
en: But O best of the Bharata race, those great bowmen were all defeated by Arjuna. With them all, he then attacked the kingdom of Pragjyotisha.

sn: तत्र राजा महानासीद् भगदत्तो विशाम्पते। तेनासीत् सुमहद् युद्धं पाण्डवस्य महात्मनः॥
en: O king, the king of that country was Bhagadatta. A great battle was fought by the illustrious Pandava with him.

sn: स किरातैश्च चीनैश्च वृतः प्राग्ज्योतिषोऽ ऽभवत्। अन्यैश्च बहुभिर्योधैः सागरानूपवासिभिः॥
en: The king of Pragjyotisha was supported by hosts of Kiratas and Chins and by numerous other warriors that dwelt on the sea-coast.

sn: ततः स दिवसानष्टौ योधयित्वा धनंजयम्। प्रहसन्नब्रवीद् राजा संग्रामविगतक्लमम्॥
en: Having fought with Dhananjaya (Arjuna) continuously for eight days and having found him not the least tired in the battle, the king Bhagadatta smilingly said to him.

sn: उपपन्नं महाबाहो त्वयि कौरवनन्दन। पाकशासनदायादे वीर्यमाहवशोभिनि॥
en: "O mighty-armed (hero), O descendant of Kuru, this energy in battle is well-suited to you, (for) you are the son of the chastiser of Paka (Indra) and an ornament in battle.

sn: अहं सखा महेन्द्रस्य शक्रादनवरो रणे। न शक्ष्यामि च ते तात स्थातुं प्रमुखतो युधि॥
en: O child, I am the friend of Indra, I am scarcely inferior to him in battle, (but) I cannot stand before you.

sn: त्वमीप्सितं पाण्डवेय ब्रूहि किं करवाणि ते। यद् वक्ष्यसि महाबाहो तत् करिष्यामि पुत्रक॥
en: O son of Pandu, tell me what is your desire? What can I do for you? O mightyarmed hero, O son, I shall do what you will tell me to do.

sn: अर्जुन उवाच कुरूणामृषभो राजा धर्मपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः। धर्मज्ञः सत्यसंधश्च यज्वा विपुलदक्षिणः॥
en: Arjuna said That foremost of the Kurus, the king Dharmaraja Yudhishthira, learned in the precepts of all virtues, devoted to truth and a performer of sacrifices in which Dakshina is very large, (desires to obtain imperial dignity).

sn: तस्य पार्थिवतामीप्से करस्तस्मै प्रदीयताम्। भवान् पितृसखा चैव प्रीयमाणो मयापि च। ततो नाज्ञापयामि त्वां प्रीतिपूर्वं प्रदीयताम्॥
en: I desire to see him acquire (it) the imperial dignity. Let tribute be paid by you to him. You are my father's friend, and you have been also gratified by me. I cannot command you. Therefore, let the tribute be paid by you with cheerfulness and at your own (free) will.

sn: भगदत्त उवाच कुन्तीमातर्यथां मे त्वं तथा राजा युधिष्ठिरः। सर्वमेतत् करिष्यामि किं चान्यत् करवाणि ते॥
en: Bhagadatta said O son of Kunti, as you are to me, so is also the king Yudhishthira. I shall do all this; tell me what else I can do for you.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्तः प्रत्युवाच भगदत्तं धनंजयः। अनेनैव कृतं सर्वमनुजानीहि याम्यहम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having been thus addressed, Dhananjaya (Arjuna) thus replied to Bhagadatta. "If you give me your promise to do it, you will have done all that I desire."

sn: तं विजित्य महाबाहुः कुन्तीपुत्रो धनंजयः। प्रययावुत्तरां तस्माद् दिशं धनदपालिताम्॥
en: Having thus conquered him, the mighty armed son of Kunti, Dhananjaya, then went towards the north, the direction presided over by the lord of wealth (Kubera).

sn: अन्तर्गिरिं च कौन्तेयस्तथैव च बहिर्गिरिम्। तथैवोपगिरिं चैव विजिग्ये पुरुषर्षभः॥
en: The son of Kunti, that best of men, conquered the inner-mountains, the outer mountains and the smaller mountains.

sn: विजित्य पर्वतान् सर्वान् ये च तत्र नराधिपाः। तान् वशे स्थापयित्वा स धनान्यादाय सर्वशः॥
en: Having conquered all the mountains and all the kings that lived on them and having brought them under his sway, he exacted tribute from them all.

sn: तैरेव सहितः सर्वैरनुरज्य च तान् नृपान्। उलक्वासिनं राजन् बृहृतमुपजग्मिवान्॥
en: O king, having won the affection of those kings, and having united himself with them, he next marched against Brihanta (who was) the king of Uluka.

sn: मृदङ्गवरनादेन रथनेमिस्वनेन च। हस्तिनां च निनादेन कम्पयन् वसुधामिमाम्॥
en: Trembling the earth with the sound of his drums, with the clatter of his chariot wheels and with the roar of the elephants that were with his troops.

sn: ततो बृहन्तस्त्वरितो बलेन चतुरङ्गिणा। निष्क्रम्य नगरात् तस्माद् योधयामास फाल्गुनम्॥
en: Brihanta soon came out of his city with his five kinds of troops and gave battle to Falguni (Arjuna).

sn: सुमहान् संनिपातोऽभूद् धनंजयबृहन्तयोः। न शशाक बृहन्तस्तु सोढुं पाण्डवविक्रमम॥
en: The battle that took place between Brihanta and Dhananjaya was a terrible one. But Brihanta was not able to stand against the prowess of the son of Pandu (Arjuna).

sn: सोऽविषह्यतमं मत्वा कौन्तेयं पर्वतेश्वरः। उपावर्तत दुर्धर्षो रत्नान्यादाय सर्वशः॥
en: Thinking that the son of Kunti was incapable of being withstood, that invincible mountain-king came to him with all his wealth.

sn: स तद्राज्यमवस्थाप्य उलूकसहितो ययौ। सेनाबिन्दुमथो राजन् राज्यादाशु समाक्षिपत्॥
en: O king, having made peace with him and having placed him in his kingdom, he (Arjuna) marched against Senabindu whom he expelled from his kingdom.

sn: मोदापुरं वामदेवं सुदामानं सुसंकुलम्। उलूकानुत्तरांश्चैव तांश्च राज्ञः समानयत्॥
en: He then subjugated Modapura, Vamadeva, Sudamana, Susankula, the northern Ulukas and the kings and the people of those countries.

sn: तत्रस्थः पुरुषैरेव धर्मराजस्य शासनात्। किरीटी जितवान् राजन् देशान् पञ्चगणांस्ततः॥
en: O king, at the command of Yudhishthira, Kirti (Arjuna) brought under his sway all these five countries and their people by sending only his troops against them and not moving himself from the city (of Senavindu).

sn: स देवप्रस्थमासाद्य सेनाविन्दोः पुरं प्रति। बलेन चतुरङ्गेण निवेशमकरोत् प्रभुः॥
en: After his arrival at Devaprastha, the city of Senavindu, the lord (Arjuna) took up his quarters there with his five kinds of troops.

sn: स तैः परिवृतः सर्वैर्विष्वगंश्वं नराधिपम्। अभ्यगच्छन्महातेजाः पौरवं पुरुषर्षभ॥
en: Surrounded by the kings and all the people whom he subjugated, he marched against that best of men, the descendant of Puru, Vishvagashva.

sn: विजित्य चाहवे शूरान् पर्वतीयान् महारथान्। जिगाय सेनया राजन् पुरं पौरवरक्षितम्॥
en: king, having subjugated in battle the brave mountaineers who were all great warriors, the son of Pandu (Arjuna) conquered with the help of his troops the city protected by the Puru King.

sn: पौरवं युधि निर्जित्य दस्यून् पर्वतवासिनः। गणानुत्सवसंकेतानजयत् सप्त पाण्डवः॥
en: Having vanquished the Puru king, and also the robber tribes of the mountains, the son of Pandu brought under his sway the seven tribes, called Utsavasanketa.

sn: ततः काश्मीरकान् वीरान् क्षत्रियान् क्षत्रियर्षभः। व्यजयल्लोहितं चैव मण्डलैर्दशभिः सह॥
en: That best of Kshatriyas (Arjuna) then vanquished the brave Kshatriyas of Kashmira and also the king Lohita, as well as ten minor chiefs.

sn: ततस्त्रिगर्ताः कौन्तेयं दार्वाः कोकनदास्तथा। क्षत्रिया बहवो राजन्नुपावर्तन्त सर्वशः॥
en: O king, then the Trigartas, the Danavas, the Kokanadas and various other Kshatriyas advanced against the son of Kunti.

sn: अभिसारी ततो रम्यां विजिग्ये कुरुनन्दनः। उरगावासिनं चैव रोचमानं रणेऽजयत्॥
en: That descendant of Kuru (Arjuna) then conquered the charming city, named Abhisari. He then vanquished Rochamana, who ruled in urga.

sn: ततः सिंहपुरं रम्यं चित्रायुधसुरक्षितम्। प्राधमद् बलमास्थाय पाकशासनिराहवे॥
en: The son of the chastiser of Paka (Arjuna) then conquered the charming city of Singhapura which was well protected by all kinds of weapons.

sn: ततः सुह्मांश्च चोलांश्च किरीटी पाण्डवर्षभः। सहितः सर्वसैन्येन प्रामथत् कुरुनन्दनः॥
en: Then that best of the Pandavas the descendant of Kuru, Kirti (Arjuna) marched against the countries, called Sumba and Sumala, and attacked them.

sn: ततः परमविक्रान्तो बाह्रीकान् पाकशासनिः। महता परिमर्दैन वशे चक्रे दुरासदान्॥
en: Then after attacking with great force, the son of Indra (Arjuna), subjugated the Valhikas, ever difficult to vanquish.

sn: गृहीत्वा तु बलं सारं फाल्गुनः पाण्डुनन्दनः। दरदान् सह काम्बोजैरजयत् पाकशासनिः॥
en: The son of Pandu, and the son of Indra, Falguni (Arjuna), then took with him a select force and defeated the Daradas along with the Kambojas.

sn: प्रागुत्तरां दिशं ये च वसन्त्याश्रित्य दस्यवः। निवसन्ति वने ये च तान् सर्वानजयत् प्रभुः॥
en: The lord (Arjuna) vanquished the robber tribes that lived in the north eastern frontier, and those also that lived in the forest.

sn: लोहान् परमकाम्बोजानृषिकानुत्तरानपि। सहितांस्तान् महाराज व्यजयत् पाकशासनिः॥
en: O great king, the son of Indra also subjugated the allied tribes of the Lokas, the eastern Kambojas and the northern Rishikas.

sn: ऋषिकेष्वपि संग्रामो बभूवातिभयंकरः। तारकामयसंकाशः परस्त्वृषिकपार्थयोः॥
en: The battle with the Rishikas was very fearful. The battle that took place between them and the son of Pritha (Arjuna) was equal to the between the gods and the Danavas, the immediate cause of which was Taraka (the wife of Brihaspati).

sn: स विजित्य ततो राजऋषिकान् रणमूर्धनि। शुकोदरसमांस्तत्र हयानष्टौ समानयत्॥
en: O king, having vanquished the Rishikas on the field of battle, he took from them as tribute eight horses that were of the colour of the parrot's breast.

sn: मयूरसदृशानन्यानुत्तरानपरानपि। जवनानाशुगांश्चैव करार्थं समुपानयत्॥
en: And some other horses also which had the colour of peacocks, these horses were all born in northern and other countries, and possessed great speed.

sn: स विनिर्जित्य संग्रामे हिमवन्तं सनिष्कुटम्। श्वेतपर्वतमासाद्य न्यविशत् पुरुषर्षभः॥
en: Thus having conquered all the Himalayas and the Nishkuta mountains, he at last arrived at the white mountains and encamped on it.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच स श्वेतपर्वतं वीरः समतिक्रम्य वीर्यवान्। देशं किम्पुरुषावासं दुमपुत्रेण रक्षितम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said After having crossed the white mountains, that greatly powerful hero conquered the country of the Kimpurushas which was ruled by Drumaputra.

sn: महता संनिपातेन क्षत्रियान्तकरेण ह। अजयत् पाण्डवश्रेष्ठः करे चैनं न्यवेशयत्॥
en: After a great battle in which great was the slaughter of Kshatriyas, that best of the Pandavas brought the country under his complete control.

sn: तं जित्वा हाटकं नाम देशं गुह्यकरक्षितम्। पाकशासनिरव्यग्रः सहसैन्यः समासदत्॥
en: Having conquered this country the son of Indra with a determined mind and with a large number of troops, subjugated the country, named Hataka, ruled by the Guhyakas.

sn: तांस्तु सान्त्वेन निर्जित्य मानसं सर उत्तमम्। ऋषिकुल्यास्तथा सर्वा ददर्श कुरुनन्दनः॥
en: Having subjugated them by a policy of conciliation, that descendant of Kuru saw that excellent lake, called Manasa. He saw also various other lakes and tanks sacred to the Rishis.

sn: सरो मानसमासाद्य हाटकानभितः प्रभुः। गन्धर्वरक्षितं देशमजयत् पाण्डवस्ततः॥
en: Having arrived at the Manasa (lake), the lord Pandava (Arjuna) conquered the regions, ruled by the Gandharvas the regions that lay around the Hataka countries.

sn: तत्र तित्तिरिकल्माषान् मण्डूकाख्यान् हयोत्तमान्। लेभे स करमत्यन्तं गन्धर्वनगरात् तदा॥
en: The victor (Arjuna) took from the city of the Gandharvas as his tribute many excellent horses, called Tittiri, Kalmasha and Manduka.

sn: उत्तरं कुरुवर्षं तु समासाद्य पाण्डवः। इयेष जेतुं तं देशं पाकशासननन्दनः॥
en: Wishing to conquer that country, the son of Indra, the Pandava (Arjuna), came to the country of North Harivarsha.

sn: तत एनं महावीर्यं महाकाया महाबलाः। द्वारपाला: समासाद्य हृष्टाः वचनमब्रुवन्॥
en: Thereupon some greatly powerful strong and huge-bodied frontier guards came to him and his cheerfully spoke to him.

sn: पार्थ नेदं त्वया शक्यं पुरं जेतुं कथंचन। उपावर्तस्व कल्याण पर्याप्तमिदमच्युत॥
en: "O Partha, this country cannot be conquered by you. If you seek your good return from this place. O Achyuta, your conquests are already enough.

sn: इदं पुरं यः प्रविशेद् ध्रुवं न स भवेन्नरः। प्रीयामहे त्वया वीर पर्याप्तो विजयस्तव॥
en: He that enters this country, if he is human, is sure to perish. We are pleased with you, your conquests are (already) too many.

sn: न चात्र किंचिज्जेतव्यमजुनात्र प्रदृश्यते। उत्तराः कुरवो ह्येते नात्र युद्धं प्रवर्तते॥
en: O Arjuna, there is nothing to be seen here, there is nothing to be conquered here by you. The Northern Kurus live here, there cannot be any war here.

sn: प्रविष्टोऽपि हि कौन्तेय नेह द्रक्ष्यसि किंचन। न हि मानुषदेहेन शक्यमत्राभिवीक्षितुम्॥
en: O son of Kunti, even if you enter this country, you will not be able to seen any thing, for nothing can be seen here with human eyes.

sn: अथेह पुरुषव्याघ्र किंचिदन्यच्चिकीर्षसि। तत् प्रब्रूहि करिष्यामो वचनात् तव भारत॥
en: O best of men, O descendant of Bharata, if however, you desire to have any thing else, tell us, we may do your bidding."

sn: ततस्तानब्रवीद् राजन्नर्जुनः प्रहसन्निवा पार्थिवत्वं चिकीर्षामि धर्मराजस्य धीमतः॥
en: Having been thus addressed, Arjuna smilingly thus spoke to them, “I desire the acquisition of the imperial dignity for the intelligent Dharamaraja Yudhishthira.

sn: न प्रवेक्ष्यामि वो देशं विरुद्धं यदि मानुषैः। युधिष्ठिराय यत् किंचित् करपण्यं प्रदीयताम्॥
en: If this country is shut against human beings, I shall not enter it. Let something be given by you as tribute to Yudhishthira.

sn: ततो दिव्यानि वस्त्राणि दिव्यान्याभरणानि च। क्षौमाजिनानि दिव्यानि तस्य ते प्रददुः करम्॥
en: Thereupon they gave him as tribute many celestials clothes and ornaments and many celestials silks and celestials skins.

sn: एवं स पुरुषव्याघ्रो विजित्य दिशमुत्तराम्। संग्रामान् सुबहून् कृत्वा क्षत्रियैर्दस्युभिस्तथा॥
en: It was thus that best of men (Arjuna) conquered the northern countries, and all the kings (of those countries); and he fought many battles both with the Kshatriyas and the robber tribes.

sn: स विनिर्जित्य राज्ञस्तान् करे च विनिवेश्य तु। धनान्यादाय सर्वेभ्यो रत्नानि विविधानि च॥
en: Having thus vanquished and subjugated many kings and countries, he exacted tributes from them all, and (he thus) obtained much wealth and many gems and jewels.

sn: हयांस्तित्तिरिकल्माषाञ्छुकपत्रनिभानपि। मयूरसदृशानन्यान् सर्वाननिलरंहसः॥
en: And many swift horses of the species called Tittiri and Kalmasha, and also many others with the colour of peacocks.

sn: वृतः सुमहता राजन् बलेन चतुरङ्गिणा। आजगाम पुनर्वीरः शक्रप्रस्थं पुरोत्तमम्॥
en: O king, surrounded by a large army of the four kinds of troops, the hero (at last) returned to the city of Indraprastha.

sn: धर्मराजाय तत् पार्थो धनं सर्वं सवाहनम्। न्यवेदयदनुज्ञातस्तेन राज्ञा गृहान् ययौ॥
en: Partha (Arjuna) offered to Dharmaraja all the wealth and the animals brought by him. Commanded by the king, the hero went to his chamber to take rest.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु भीमसेनोऽपि वीर्यवान्। धर्मरजमनुप्राप्य ययौ प्राची दिशं प्रति॥
en: Vaishampayana said In the meantime, having received the permission of Dharmaraja (Yudhishthira), the powerful Bhimasena marched towards the east.

sn: महता बलचक्रेण परराष्ट्रावमर्दिना। हस्त्यश्वरथपूर्णेन दंशितेन प्रतापवान्॥ वृतो भरतशार्दूलो द्विषच्छोकविवर्द्धनः। स गत्वा नरशार्दूल: पञ्चालानां पुरं महत्॥
en: That best of the Bharata race (Bhima), that hero of great velour and enhancer of the enemy's sorrow, was accompanied by a powerful army with the full compliment of elephants, horses and cars, an army well-armed and capable of grinding all hostile kingdoms, that best of men (Bhima) first went to thereat country of the Panchalas.

sn: पञ्चालान् विविधेपायैः सान्त्वयामास पाण्डवः। ततः स गण्डकाञ्छूरो विदेहान् भरतर्षभः॥ विजित्याल्पेन कालेन दशार्णानजयत् प्रभुः। तत्र दाशार्णको राजा सुधर्मा लोमहर्षणम्। कृतवान् भीमसेनेन महद् युद्धं निरायुधम्॥
en: The Pandava (Bhima) began to conciliate the Panchalas by various means. Then that best of the Bharata race soon defeated the Gandakas and Videhas. The Lord (Bhima) then subjugated the Dasarnas. The king of the Dasarnas, Sudharma.

sn: भीमसेनस्तु तद् दृष्ट्वा तस्य कर्म महात्मनः। अधिसेनापतिं चक्रे सुधर्माणं महाबलम्॥
en: Fought a fearful battle with Bhima without any arms. Seeing the feat of that illustrious (king), Bhimasena installed installed the mighty Sudharma as the generalissimo (of his army).

sn: ततः प्राची दिशं भीमो ययौ भीमपराक्रमः। सैन्येन महता राजन् कम्पयन्निव मेदिनीम्॥
en: O king, causing the earth itself to tremble with the tread of the mighty army that followed him, then Bhima of fearful velour marched towards the east.

sn: सोऽश्वमेधेश्वरं राजन् रोचमानं सहानुगम्। जिगाय समरे वीरो बलेन बलिनां वरः॥
en: O king, that hero, the foremost of all mighty men, then defeated in battle Rochaman, the king of Ashvamedha, with all his troops.

sn: स तं निर्जित्य कौन्तेयो नातितीव्रण कर्मणा॥ पूर्वदेशं महावीर्यो विजिग्ये कुरुनन्दन॥
en: Having vanquished that king by performing feats that excelled in fierceness, the greatly powerful descendant of Kuru subjugated the eastern region.

sn: ततो दक्षिणमागम्य पुलिन्दनगरं महत्। सुकुमारं वशे चक्रे सुमित्रं च नराधिपम्॥
en: He then went to the south in the great city of the Pulindas and subjugated Sukumara and the king Sumitra.

sn: ततस्तु धर्मराजस्य शासनाद् भरतर्षभः। शिशुपालं महावीर्यमभ्यगाज्जनमेजय॥
en: O Janamejaya, then at the command of Dharmaraja Yudhishthira, that best of the Bharata race marched against the greatly powerful Shishupala.
