sn: चेदिराजोऽपि तच्छ्रुत्वा पाण्डवस्य चिकीर्षितम्। उपनिष्क्रम्य नगरात् प्रत्यगृहणात् परंतप॥
en: Having heard the intentions of the Pandava (Bhima), the king of Chedi came out of his city. That chastiser of foes then received the son of Pritha with all respects.

sn: तौ समेत्य महाराज कुरुचेदिवृषौ तदा। उभयोरात्मकुलयोः कौशल्यं पर्यपृच्छताम्॥
en: O great king, those two best of the Kuru and the Chedi race then met together and inquired after each other's welfare.

sn: ततो निवेद्य तद् राष्ट्र चेदिराजो विशाम्पते। उवाच भीमं प्रहसन् किमिदं कुरुषेऽनघ॥
en: O king, the king of Chedi offered his kingdom to Bhima, and he smilingly said "O sinless one, what are you bent upon to do?

sn: तस्य भीमस्तदाऽचख्यौ धर्मराजचिकीर्षितम्। स च तं प्रतिगृह्येव तथा चक्रे नराधिपः॥
en: Thereupon Bhima told him all about the intentions of the king Yudhishthira. That king acted as desired (by the Pandava).

sn: ततो भीमस्तत्र राजन्नुषित्वा त्रिदश क्षपाः। सत्कृत: शिशुपालेन ययौ सबलवाहनः॥
en: O king, having been duly entertained by Shishupala, Bhima lived there for thirty nights. He then set out from Chedi with his troops and vehicles.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततः कुमारविषये श्रेणिमन्तमथाजयत्। कोसलाधिपतिं चैव बृहद्बलमरिंदमः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Thereupun that chastiser of foes vanquished (king) Shrenimana of the country of Kumara, and then Vrihadvala, the king of Koshala.

sn: अयोध्यायां तु धर्मज्ञं दीर्घयज्ञं महाबलम्। अजयत् पाण्डवश्रेष्ठो नातितीव्रण कर्मणा॥
en: The best of the Pandavas (Bhima) then vanquished the greatly powerful and virtuous (king) Dirghayajna of Ayodhya by performing greatly fearful deeds.

sn: ततो गोपालकक्षं च सोत्तरानपि कोसलान्। मल्लानामधिपं चैव पार्थिवं चाजयत् प्रभुः॥
en: The lord (Bhima) then subjugated the country of Gopalakaksha and the northern Kosalas, and then the king of the Malla.

sn: ततो हिमवतः पार्श्व समभ्येत्य जलोद्भवम्। सर्वमल्पेन कालेन देशं चक्रे वशं बली॥
en: The powerful (hero), then arrived at the damp country at the foot of the Himalayas and soon subjugated the whole of that country.

sn: एवं बहुविधान् देशान् विजिग्ये भरतर्षभः। भल्लाटमभितो जिग्ये शुक्तिमन्तं च पर्वतम्॥
en: That best of the Bharata race (Bhima) thus brought under his sway various country of Bhallata and also the mountains of Shuktimanta.

sn: पाण्डवः सुमहावीर्यो बलेन बलिनां वरः। स काशिराजं समरे सुबाहुमनिवर्तिनम्॥
en: The foremost of all powerful men, the greatly mighty Pandava (Bhima), then vanquished in battle Subahu, the king of Kashi, who never retreated (from the field).

sn: वशे चक्रे महाबाहुर्भीमो भीमपराक्रमः। ततः सुपार्श्वमभितस्तथा राजपतिं क्रथम्॥ युध्यमानं बलात् संख्ये विजिग्ये पाण्डवर्षभः। ततो मत्स्यान् महातेजा मलदांश्च महाबलान्॥
en: And the mighty armed Bhima of fearful prowess brought him also under his sway. Then that best of the Pandavas by great force vanquished in battle Kratha who reigned (over and kingdom) near Suparshva. Then the greatly effulgent (hero) vanquished the Matsyas and the mighty Malavas.

sn: अनघानभयांश्चैव पशुभूमिं च सर्वशः। निवृत्य च महाबाहुर्मदधारं महीधरम्॥
en: And all the countries, called Pashubhumi, which were free from all fear of oppression. Returning (from these places), that mighty armed (hero) vanquished Madadhara and Mahidhara.

sn: सोमधेयांश्च निर्जित्य प्रययावुत्तरामुखः। वत्सभूमिं च कौन्तेयो विजिग्ये बलवान् बलात्॥
en: And the Somadheyas. He then marched towards the north. The mighty son of Kunti (Bhima) then by force conquered the country, named Vatsabhumi.

sn: भर्गाणामधिपं चैव निषदाधिपति तथा। विजिग्ये भूमिपालांश्च मणिमत्प्रमुखान् बहून्।॥
en: He then conquered the king of the Bhargas, the king of the Nishadas, and many other rulers, Maniman being at their head.

sn: ततो दक्षिणमल्लांश्च भोगवन्तं च पर्वतम्। तरसैवाजयद् भीमो नातितीव्रण कर्मणा॥
en: Then Bhima without any very great effort soon vanquished the southern Mallas and the mountain Bhogavanta.

sn: शर्मकान् वर्मकांश्चैव व्यजयत् सान्त्वपूर्वकम्। वैदेहकं च राजानं जनकं जगतीपतिम्॥ विजिग्ये पुरुषव्याघ्रो नातितीव्रण कर्मणा। शकांश्च बर्बरांश्चैव अजयगच्छद्मपूर्वकम्॥
en: He then vanquished the Sharmakas and the Varmakas by a policy of conciliation. That best of men then without any very great exertion vanquished the king of Videha, the lord of the universe, Janaka. He then by craftiness vanquished the Shakas and the barbarians.

sn: वैदेहस्थस्तु कौन्तेय इन्द्रपर्वतमन्तिकात्। किरातानामधिपतीनजयत् सप्त पाण्डव॥
en: The son of Kunti, the Pandava (Bhima), sent forth expeditions from Videha and conquered the seven kings of the Kiratas, living on the Indra Parvata (imountains).

sn: ततः सुह्मान् प्रसुह्मांश्च सपक्षानतिवीर्यवान्। विजित्य युधि कौन्तेयो मागधानभ्यधाद् बली॥ दण्डं च दण्डधारं च विजित्य पृथिवीपतीन्। तैरेव सहितैः सर्वैर्गिरिव्रजमुपाद्रवत्॥
en: Thereupon the greatly energetic and powerful hero, the son of Kunti (Bhima), vanquished the Suhamas and the Prasuhmas, winning over to his his side Danda and Dandadhara. Being accompanied by all other kings, the Pandava (Bhima) then marched towards Girivraja.

sn: जारासंधिं सान्त्वयित्वा करे च विनिवेश्य ह। तैरेव सहितैः सर्वैः कर्णमभ्यद्रवद् बली॥
en: Having subjugated the son of Jarasandha by conciliation and having made him pay tribute, the hero, accompanied by all the kings he had vanquished, marched against Karna.

sn: स कम्पयन्निव महीं बलेन चतुरङ्गिणा। युयुधे पाण्डवश्रेष्ठः कर्णेनामित्रघातिना॥
en: Making the earth tremble by his troops of four kinds, that best of the Pandavas fought (a battle) with that slayer of foes Karna.

sn: स कर्णं युधि निर्जित्य वशे कृत्वा च भारत। ततो विजिग्ये बलवान् राज्ञः पर्वतवासिनः॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, having vanquished and brought under his away Karna, he then vanquished the powerful kings who lived on the mountains.

sn: अथ मोदागिरौ चैव राजानं बलवत्तरम्। पाण्डवो बाहुवीर्येण निजघान महामृधे॥
en: The Pandava (Bhima) then in a fearful fight killed by the strength of his arms the mighty king who dwelt in Madagiri.

sn: ततः पुण्ड्राधिपं वीरं वासुदेवं महाबलम्। कौशिकीकच्छनिलयं राजानं च महौजसम्॥
en: O king, he then subjugated the heroic and greatly powerful Vasudeva, the king of Pundra, and the king Mahaujasa who lived in Kaushikacha.

sn: उभौ बलभृतौ वीरावुभौ तीव्रपराक्रमौ। निर्जित्याजी महाराज वङ्गराजमुपाद्रवत्॥
en: O great king, having vanquished both these heroic and greatly powerful kings, the son of Pritha (Bhima), then attacked the king of Vanga.

sn: समुद्रसेनं निर्जित्य चन्द्रसेनं च पार्थिवम्। ताम्रलिप्तं च राजानं कर्वटाधिपतिं तथा॥
en: Having vanquished Samudarasena and the king Chandrasena, the king of Tamralipta and the king of Karvata.

sn: सुह्यानामधिपं चैव ये च सागरवासिनः। सर्वान् म्लेच्छगणांश्चैव विजिग्ये भरतर्षभः॥
en: The ruler of the Suhamas and also the kings that lived on the sea coast, the best of the Bharata race (Bhima) subjugated all the Mlecchas.

sn: एवं बहुविधान् देशान् विजित्य पवनात्मजः। वसु तेभ्य उपादाय लौहित्यमगमद् बली॥
en: Having thus conquered various countries and having taken much wealth from them all, the powerful son of Pavana (wind), came to Lohitya.

sn: स सर्वान् म्लेच्छनृपतीन् सागरानूपवासिनः। करमाहारयामास रत्नानि विविधानि च॥
en: From all the kings of the Mlecchas who lived on the coast of these, he exacted tribute in the shape of various gems and jewels.

sn: चन्दनागुरुवस्त्राणि मणिमौक्तिककम्बलम्। काञ्चनं रजत चैव विद्रुमं च महाधनम्॥
en: Sandalwood, ales, clothes, gems, pearls, blankets, gold, silver and valuable corals.

sn: ते कोटिशतसंख्येन कौन्तेयं महता तदा। अभ्यवर्षन् महात्मानं धनवर्षेण पाण्डवम्॥
en: They (the Mleccha kings) showered upon the illustrious son of Kunti, the Pandava (Bhima), every thick shower of wealth counted by hundreds of millions.

sn: इन्द्रप्रस्थमुपागम्य भीमो भीमपराक्रमः। निवेदयामास तदा धर्मराजाय तद् धनम्॥
en: Have arrived at Indraprastha, Bhima of fearful prowess offered all those wealth to Dharmaraja (Yudhishthira).

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तथैव सहदेवोऽपि धर्मराजेन पूजितः। महत्या सेनया राजन् प्रययौ दक्षिणां दिशम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said O king, having been sent away with affection by Dharmaraja (Yudhishthira), with a very large army Sahadeva, was marched towards the south.

sn: स शूरसेनान् कात्स्न्र्येन पूर्वमेवाजयत् प्रभुः। मत्स्यराजं च कौरव्यो वशे चक्रे बलाद् बली॥
en: That powerful descendant of Kuru, the lord (Sahadeva), strong in his own strength, vanquished the Shurasenas at the very outset. He then subjugated the king of Matsya.

sn: अधिराजाधिपं चैव दन्तवक्रं महाबलम्। जिगाय करदं चैव कृत्वा राज्ये न्यवेशयत्॥
en: Having vanquished the powerful king of the Adhirajas, Dantavakra, and having made him pay tribute, the hero (Sahadeva) then replaced him on his throne.

sn: सुकुमारं वशे चक्रे सुमित्रं च नराधिपम्। तथैवापरमत्स्यांश्च व्यजयत् स पटच्चरान्॥
en: He then subjugated Sukumara and the king Sumitra, and then the other Matsyas, and then the Patachharas.

sn: निषादभूमि गोशृङ्गं पर्वतप्रवरं तथा। तरसैवाजयद् धीमान् श्रेणिमन्तं च पार्थिवम्॥
en: The greatly intelligent (Sahadeva) then soon conquered the country of the Nishadas and also the best of hills, called Goshringa, and the king, called Shrenimana.

sn: नरराष्ट्रं च निर्जित्य कुन्तिभोजमुपाद्रवत्। प्रीतिपूर्वं च तस्याजौ प्रतिजग्राह शासनम्॥
en: Having then conquered the country, named Nararashtra, he marched against Kuntibhoja. He (the king of Kuntibhoja) very willingly accepted the sway (of the Pandavas).

sn: तत्तश्चर्मण्वतीकूले जम्भकंस्यात्मजं नृपम्। ददर्श वासुदेवेन शेषितं पूर्ववैरिणा॥
en: Then on the banks of the Charmanvati, he met the son of the king Jambhaka who had been formerly defeated by Vasudeva for some old hostilities.

sn: चक्रे तेन स संग्राम सहदेवेन भारत। स तमाजौ विनिर्जित्य दक्षिणाभिमुखो ययौ॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, he fought a battle with Sahadeva, but he (Sahadeva) defeated him and then marched towards the south.

sn: सेकानपरसेकांश्च व्यजयत् सुमहाबलः। करं तेभ्य उपादाय रत्नानि विविधानि च॥
en: The greatly powerful hero then subjugated the Sekas and the other Sekas, and exacted tribute from them in the shape of various gems and jewels.

sn: ततस्तेनैव सहितो नर्मदामभितो ययौ। विन्दानुविन्दावावन्त्यौ सैन्येन महताऽऽवृतौ। जिगाय समरे वीरावाश्चिनेयः प्रतापवान्॥ ततो रत्नान्युपादाय पुरं भोजकटं ययौ।
en: With them all, he then went to wards the country watered by the Narmada. The mighty son of Ashvinis (Sahadeva) then vanquished in a battle the two heroic kings of Avanti, named Vinda and Anuvinda who were surrounded by a large number of soldiers. Having exacted much wealth from them, he went towards the city of Bhojakata.

sn: तत्र युद्धमभूद् राजन् दिवसद्वयमच्युत्॥ स विजित्य दुराधर्ष भीष्मकं माद्रिनन्दनः।
en: O king, O Achyuta (unfolding glory), a great battle was fought there for two days. But the son of Madri, Sahadeva, defeated the invincible Bhishmaka.

sn: कोसलाधिपतिं चैव तथा वेणातटाधिपम्॥ कान्तारकांश्च समरे तथा प्राक्कोसलान् नृपान्।
en: He then defeated in battle the king of Kosala, the king of Venatatha, the Kantarakas, and the kings of the eastern Kosalas.

sn: नाटकेयांश्च समरे तथा हेरम्बकान् युधि॥ मारुधं च विनिर्जित्य रम्यग्राममथो बलात्। नाचीनानर्धकांश्चैव राज्ञश्चैव महाबलः॥ तांस्तानाटविकीन् सर्वानजयत् पाण्डुनन्दनः। वाताधिपं च नृपति वशं चक्रे महाबलः॥
en: Having then defeated in battle the Natakeyas and the Herambakas, and having subjugated the Marudhas, he conquered Munjagrama by force. He then vanquished the kings of the Nachinas, the Arbukas and the various other forest kings who ruled in that part of the country. The greatly powerful son of Pandu then subjugated the king Vatadhipa.

sn: पुलिन्दांश्च रणे जित्वा ययौ दक्षिणतः पुरः। युयुधे पाण्ड्यराजेन दिवसं नकुलानुजः॥
en: Having defeated in battle the Pulindas, he marched towards the south. The younger brother of Nakula (Sahadeva) then fought for a day with the king of Pandya.

sn: तं जित्वा स महाबाहुः प्रययौ दक्षिणापथम्। गुहामासादयामास किष्किन्धां लोकविश्रुताम्॥
en: Having vanquished him, the mighty armed (hero) went (further) towards the south. He then came to the world-renowned caves of Kishkindhya.

sn: तत्र वानरराजाभ्यां मैन्देन द्विविदेन च। युयुधे दिवसान् सप्त न च तौ विकृतिं गतौ॥
en: Here fought he for seven days with the monkey kings, named Mainda and Dvivida. They too, however, did not at all feel fatigued (in the fight).

sn: ततस्तुष्टौ महात्मानौ सहदेवाय वानरौ। ऊचतुश्चैव संहृष्टौ प्रीतिपूर्वमिदं वचः॥
en: Those two illustrious monkey-kings (were much) pleased with Sahadeva, and they thus joyfully spoke to him these affectionate words.

sn: गच्छ पाण्डवशार्दूल रत्नान्यादाय सर्वशः। अविघ्नमस्तु कार्याय धर्मराजाय धीमते॥
en: "O best of the Pandavas, go (back) on receiving wealth from us. Let the work of the intelligent Dharmaraja be accomplished without any hindrance."

sn: ततो रत्नान्युपादाय पुरी माहिष्मती ययौ। तत्र नीलेन राज्ञा स चक्रे युद्धं नरर्षभः॥
en: Thereupon, having received wealth that best of men, (Sahadeva), marched towards the city of Mahishmati. He fought there a battle with king Nila.

sn: पाण्डवः परवीरनः सहदेवः प्रतापवान्। ततोऽस्यं सुमहद् युद्धमासीद् भीरुभयंकरम्॥
en: The battle between the chastiser of foes, the powerful Pandava, Sahadeva, and the king (Nila) was very fearful.

sn: सैन्यक्षयकरं चैव प्राणानां संशयावहम्। चक्रे तस्य हि साहाय्यं भगवान् हव्यवाहनः॥
en: It destroyed many soldiers, and it endangered the life (of the hero Sahadeva), for the lord, the carrier of sacrificial libation (fire), was helping him (the king Nila).

sn: ततो रथा हया नागाः पुरुषाः कवचानि च। प्रदीप्तानि व्यदृश्यन्त सहदेवबले तदा॥
en: The cars, horses, elephants, and the wellarmoured of Sahadeva's army all appeared as if they were on fire.

sn: ततः सुसम्भ्रान्तमना बभूव कुरुनन्दनः। नोत्तरं प्रतिवक्तुं च शक्तोऽभूज्जनमेजय॥
en: Seeing this, that descendant of Kuru was filled with great anxiety. O Janamejaya, seeing this, the hero could not resolve upon what he should do. inen was

sn: जनमेजय उवाच किमर्थं भगवान् वह्निः प्रत्यमित्रोऽभवद् युधि। सहदेवस्य यज्ञार्थं घटमानस्य वै द्विज॥
en: Janamejaya said O exalted one, O Brahmana, why was it that the deity Agni became hostile in battle to Sahadeva who fighting for the accomplishment of a sacrifice?

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तत्र माहिष्मतीवासी भगवान् हव्यवाहनः। श्रूयते हि गृहीतो वै पुरस्तात् पारदारिकः॥
en: Vaishampayana said It is heard that Agni, living in the city of Mahishmati, was formerly taken for an adulterer.

sn: नीलस्य राज्ञो दुहिता बभूवातीवशोभना। साग्निहोत्रमुपातिष्ठद् बोधनाय पितुः सदा॥
en: The daughter of the king Nila was exceedingly handsome. She always used to stay near her father's Agnihotra (sacred fire) to stir it up.

sn: व्यजनै—यमानोऽपि तावत् प्रज्वलते न सः। यावच्चारुपुटौष्ठेन वायुना न विधूयते॥
en: Being fanned as much as was possible, the fire did not blaze up, till it was not blown by the breaths of the sweet lips of that girl

sn: ततः स भगवानाग्निश्चकमे तां सुदर्शनाम्। नीलस्य राज्ञः सर्वेषामुपनीतश्च सोऽभवत्॥
en: It was said in the king Nila's palace and in the houses of all (men) that the illustrious Agni wanted to marry that beautiful maiden; and he was (in fact) accepted by her.

sn: ततो ब्राह्मणरूपेण रममाणो यदृच्छया। चकमे तां वरारोहां कन्यामुत्पललोचनाम्। तं तु राजा यथाशास्त्रमशासद् धार्मिकस्तदा॥
en: One day when he (Agni), assuming the form of a Brahmana, was enjoying at pleasure in the company of that handsome girl, he was discovered by the king. The virtuous monarch then ordered the Brahmana to be punished according to law.

sn: प्रजज्वाल ततः कोपाद् भगवान् हव्यवाहनः। तं दृष्ट्वा विस्मितो राजा जगाम शिरसावनिम्॥
en: Thereupon the illustrious carrier of sacrificial libations (Agni) blazed up in wrath. Seeing this, the king was filled with astonishment, and he bent his head to the ground.

sn: ततः कालेन तां कन्यां तथैव हि तदा नृपः। प्रददौ विप्ररूपाय वह्नये शिरसा ततः॥
en: After sometime, bending his head low, the king bestowed his that daughter on Agni who was in the disguise of a Brahmana.

sn: प्रतिगृह्य च तां सुबूं नीलराज्ञः सुतां तदा। चक्रे प्रसादं भगवांस्तस्य राज्ञो विभावसुः॥
en: The illustrious Vibhavasu (Agni) accepted that fire-browed daughter of the king Nila, and he bestowed on the king his favours.

sn: वरेणच्छन्दयामास तं नृपं स्विष्टकृत्तमः। अभयं च स जग्राह स्वसैन्ये वै महीपतिः॥
en: The illustrious gratifier of all purposes (Agni) also asked the king to solicit a boon from him. The king asked the boon by which he with the troops while engaged in battle might never be struck with panic.

sn: ततः प्रभृति ये केचिदज्ञानात् तां पुरी नृपाः। जिगीषन्ति बलाद् राजंस्ते दह्यन्ते स्म वह्निना॥
en: O king, from that day he, who out of ignorance of this, desires to subjugate the city of the king (Nila), is consumed by fire.

sn: तस्यां पुर्यां तदा चैव माहिष्मत्यां कुरूद्वह। बभूवुरनतिग्राह्या योषितश्छन्दतः किल॥ एवमग्निर्वरं प्रादात् स्त्रीणामप्रतिवारणे। वरिण्यस्तत्र नार्यो हि यथेष्टं विचरन्त्युत॥
en: O perpetuator of the Kuru race, from that day the girls of the city of Mahishmati became rather unacceptable to others (as wives). Agni by his boon granted them sexual liberty. The women of that city, being not confined to a particular husband, always roamed as Sairini at will.

sn: वर्जयन्ति च राजानस्तत् पुरं भरतर्षभ। भयादग्नेर्महाराज तदाप्रभृति सर्वदा॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, O great king, from that day all the kings avoid this city for the fear of fire.

sn: सहदेवस्तु धर्मात्मा सैन्यं दृष्ट्वा भयादितम्। परीतमग्निना राजन् नाकम्पत यथाचलः। उपस्पृश्य शुचिर्भूत्वा सोऽब्रवीत् पावकं ततः॥
en: O king, the virtuous-minded Sahadeva also, seeing his troops afflicted with fear and encircled with flames, stood motionless as a mountain. Touching water and purifying himself, he thus spoke to Pavaka (fire).

sn: सहदेव उवाच त्वदर्थोऽयं समारम्भः कृष्णवर्त्मन् नमोऽस्तु ते। मुखं त्वमसि देवानां यज्ञस्त्वमसि पावक॥
en: Sahadeva said O Pavaka, O Krishnavartman, (having) smoke for marking your track, I bow to you. You are the mouth of the celestials; you are the sacrifice itself.

sn: पावनात् पावकश्चासि वहनाद्धव्यवाहनः। वेदास्त्वदर्थं जाता वै जातवेदास्ततो ह्यसि॥
en: You are called Pavaka, because you sanctify every thing; thing; you are called Havyavahana, because you carry the sacrificial libation of Ghee. The Vedas have all sprung from you, and therefore, you are called Jatavedas.

sn: चित्रभानुः सुरेशश्च अनलस्त्वं विभावसो। स्वर्गद्वारस्पृशश्चासि हुताशो ज्वलनः शिखी॥
en: You are Suresha (chief of the celestials), you Chitrabhanu, Anala, Svargadvarsparshi, Vibhavasu, Hutasha, Jvalana, Shikhi.

sn: वैश्वानरस्त्वं पिङ्गेशः प्लवङ्गो भूरितेजसः। कुमारसूस्त्वं भगवान् रुद्रगर्भो हिरण्यकृत्॥
en: Vaishvanara, Pingesha, Plavanga and Bhuritejas. You are the origin of Kumara (Kartikeya). O exalted one, you are called Rudragarbha and Hiranyakrit.

sn: अग्निर्ददातु मे तेजो वायुः प्राणं ददातु मे। पृथिवी बलमादध्याच्छिवं चापो दिशन्तु मे॥
en: O Agni, let yourself grant me energy and let Vayu grant me life. Let earth grant me nourishment and strength, and let water grant me prosperity.

sn: अपांगर्भ महासत्त्व जातवेदः सुरेश्वर। देवानां मुखमग्ने त्वं सत्येन विपुनीहि माम्॥
en: O the first cause of waters, O great purity, O the origin of the Vedas, Othe chief of the are celestials, O the mouth of the celestials, purify me by your truly.

sn: ऋषिभिर्ब्राह्मणैश्चैव दैवतैरसुरैरपि। नित्यं सुहुत यज्ञेषु सत्येन विपुनीहि माम्॥
en: The Rishis, the Brahmanas, the celestials and the Asuras every day pour Ghee in the sacrifice according to the ordinance. Let the rays of truth emanate from you as you exhibit yourself in sacrifices. Purify me,

sn: धूमकेतुः शिखी च त्वं पापहानिलसम्भवः। सर्वप्राणिषु नित्यस्थः सत्येन विपुनीहि माम्॥
en: O smoke-bannered deity, O possessor of flames, O deity born of Vayu, O god who is present in all creatures. Purify me by your rays of truth.

sn: एवं स्तुतोऽसि भगवन् प्रीतेन शुचिना मया। तुष्टिं पुष्टिं श्रुतिं चैव प्रीतिं चाग्ने प्रयच्छ मे॥
en: O exalted one having cheerfully cleansed myself, I do pray to you, O Agni, grant me now contentment and prosperity, knowledge and gladness.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच इत्येवं मन्त्रमाग्नेयं पठन् यो जुहुयाद् विभुम्। ऋद्धिमान् सततं दान्तः सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते॥
en: Vaishampayana said He, who will pour Ghee into Agni reciting these Mantras, will be ever blessed with prosperity. Having his souls under his complete control, he will be cleansed of all his sins.

sn: सहदेव उवाच यज्ञविजमिमं कर्तुं नार्हस्त्वं हव्यवाहन। एवमुक्त्वा तु माद्रेयः कुशैरास्तीर्य मेदिनीम्॥
en: Sahadeva said O carrier of sacrificial libation (Agni), you should not put obstacle to a sacrifice. Having said this, the son of Madri (Sahadeva) spread some Kusha grass of the ground.

sn: विधिवत् पुरुषव्याघ्रः पावकं प्रत्युपाविशत्। प्रमुखे तस्य सैन्यस्य भीतोद्विग्नस्य भारत॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, that best of men in expectation of the approaching fire then sat himself down in front of his terrified and anxious troops.

sn: न चैनमत्यगाद् वह्निर्वेलामिव महोदधिः। तमुपेत्य शनैर्वह्निरुवाच कुरुनन्दनम्॥
en: Like the ocean that never pass beyond its shore, Agni did not pass over his (Sahadeva). Agni quietly came to him, and he thus spoke to that descendant of the Kuru.

sn: सहदेवं नृणां देवं सान्त्वपूर्वमिदं वचः। उत्तिष्ठोत्तिष्ठ कौरव्य जिज्ञासेयं कृता मया। वेदि सर्वमभिप्रायं तद धर्मसुतस्य च॥
en: Sahadeva, that god among men, these words of assurance, "O descendant of Kuru rise up, rise up. I was only trying you.

sn: मया तु रक्षिताव्येयं पुरी भरतसत्तम। यावद् राज्ञो हि नीलस्य कुले वंशधरा इति॥
en: I know all your purposes as well as those of the son of Dharma (Yudhishthira). O best of the Bharata race, this city will be protected by me.

sn: ईप्सितं तु करिष्यामि मनसस्तव पाण्डव॥ तत उत्थाय हृष्टात्मा प्राञ्जलिः शिरसा नतः।
en: So long as there will be a scion in the King Nila's dynasty. O son of Pandu, I shall, however, accomplish the desire of your heart.”

sn: पूजयामाय माद्रेयः पावकं भरतर्षभ॥ पावके विनिवृत्ते तु नीलो राजाभ्यगात् तदा।
en: O best of the Bharata race, the son of Madri rose up with a cheerful heart and bowing down his head with joined hands, he worshipped Pavaka (Agni).

sn: पावकस्याज्ञया चैनमर्चयामास पार्थिवः॥ सत्कारेण नरव्याघ्रं सहदेवं युधाम्पतिम्। प्रतिगृह्य च तां पूजां करे च विनिवेश्य च॥
en: On the disappearance of Pavaka king Nila came there, and at the command of that deity (Agni), the king worshipped with due rites that best of men and that master in war, Sahadeva, He accepted his worship and made him pay tribute.

sn: माद्रीसुतस्ततः प्रायाद विजयी दक्षिणां दिशम्। त्रैपुरं स वशे कृत्वा राजानममितौजसम्॥
en: Thereupon the victorious son of Madri went further towards the south. Having subjugated the immeasurably effulgent Tripura.

sn: निजग्राह महाबाहुस्तरसा पौरवेश्वरम्। आकृति कौशिकाचार्य यत्नेन महता ततः॥
en: The mighty armed (hero) soon vanquished and subjugated the Paurava King; and he then with great deal of effort subjugated the preceptor of Kaushika, Akriti.

sn: वशे चक्रे महाबाहुः सुराष्ट्राधिपतिं तदा। सुराष्ट्रविषयस्थश्च प्रेषयामास रुक्मिणे॥ राजे भोजकटस्थाय महामात्राय धीमते। भीष्मकाय स धर्मात्मा साक्षादिन्द्रसखाय वै॥
en: The mighty armed (hero) then subjugated the king of Shurashtra. He sent an ambassador to king Rukmin of Bhishmaka in the territories of Bhojakata, who, rich in wealth and intelligence, was the friend of Indra.

sn: स चास्य प्रतिजग्राह ससुतः शासनं तदा। प्रीतिपूर्वं महाराज वासुदेवमवेक्ष्य च॥
en: O great king, remembering his friendship with Vasudeva (Krishna), that king with his son cheerfully accepted their (the Pandavas) sway.

sn: ततः स रत्नान्यादाय पुनः प्रायाद् युधाम्पतिः। ततः शूर्पारकं चैव तालाकटमथापि च॥
en: Taking many jewels and much wealth from him (Rukmin), that master of war (Sahadeva) then subjugated Shuparaka and Talakata.

sn: वशे चक्रे महातेजा दण्डकांश्च महाबलः। सागरद्वीपवासांश्च नृपतीन् म्लेच्छयोनिजान्॥
en: The greatly powerful (hero) then brought under his sway the exceedingly energetic Dandaka. Then he subjugated many kings born of the Mleccha race and living in the island in the sea;

sn: निषादान् पुरुषादांश्च कर्णप्रावरणानपि। ये च कालमुखा नाम नरराक्षसयोनयः॥
en: Then the Nishadas, the cannibals, the Karnapravanas, those tribes called Kalamukhas who were a cross race between the men and Rakshasas,

sn: कृत्स्नं कोलागिरिं चैव सुरभीपत्तनं तथा। द्वीपं ताम्राह्वयं चैव पर्वतं रामकं तथा॥
en: The whole of the Cole mountains, also Shurabhipattna, the island called Copper Island and the mountain called Ramaka.

sn: तिमिङ्गिलं च स नृपं वशे कृत्वा महामतिः। एकपादांश्च पुरुषान् केरलान् वनवासिनः॥
en: Having brought under subjection, king Timingila, the illustrious warrior subjugated a wild tribe, named the Keralas who were men with one leg.

sn: नगरी संजयन्ती च पाखण्डं करहाटकम्। दूतैरेव वशे चक्रे करं चैनानदापयत्॥
en: The son of Pandu also subjugated the city of Sanjayanti and the country of the Pakhandas and Karahatakas by means of his messengers alone; and he made them all pay tribute to him.

sn: पाण्ड्यांश्च द्रविडांश्चैव सहितांश्चोण्ड्रकेरलैः। आन्ध्रांस्तालवनांश्चैव कलिङ्गानुष्ट्रकर्णिकान्॥
en: The hero also subjugated and exacted tribute from the Pandyas, the Dravidas the Udrakeralas, the Andhras, the Talavanas the Kalinga, and the Ushtrakarnikas.

sn: आटवीं च पुरी रम्यां यवनानां पुरं तथा। दूतैरेव वशे चक्रे करं चैनानदापयत्॥
en: He brought under his away the charming city of Atavi and also the city of the Yavanas by sending messengers and by exacting tribute.

sn: तत: कच्छगतो धीमान् दूतं माद्रवतीसुतः। प्रेषयामास हैडिम्बं पौलस्त्याय महात्मने। विभीषणाय धर्मात्मा प्रीतिपूर्वमरिंदमः॥ स चास्य प्रतिजग्राह शासनं प्रीतिपूर्वकम्। तच्च कालकृतं धीमानभ्यमन्यत स प्रभुः॥
en: O king of kings, that slayer of foes, the virtuous and intelligent son of Madri (Sahadeva), having (at last) arrived at the sea coast, sent ambassadors to the illustrious Vibhishana, the grandson of Pulastya. He also cheerfully accept his sway.

sn: ततः सम्प्रेषयामास रत्नानि विविधानि च। चन्दनागुरुकाष्ठानि दिव्यान्याभरणानि च॥
en: He (Vibhishana) sent to him (Sahadeva) various kinds of jewels and gems, sandal and aloe-woods, many celestials ornaments.

sn: वासांसि च महार्हाणि मणींश्चैव महाधनान्। न्यवर्तत ततो धीमान् सहदेवः प्रतापवान्॥
en: Many costly apparels and many valuable pearls. Thereupon the intelligent Sahadeva returned to his kingdom.

sn: एवं निर्जित्य तरसा सान्त्वेन विजयेन च। करदान् पार्थिवान् कृत्वा प्रत्यागच्छदरिंदमः॥
en: Having vanquished by war and by, conciliation many kings and having also made them pay tribute to him, that chastiser of foes returned (to his own city).

sn: धर्मराजाय तत् सर्व निवेद्य भरतर्षभ। कृतकर्मा सुखं राजन्नुवास जनमेजय॥
en: O king, O Janamejaya, the best of the Bharata race (Sahadeva) presented all, that wealth to Dharmaraja (Yudhishthira) and regarded himself crowned with success, and he became very happy.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच नकुलस्य तु वक्ष्यामि कर्माणि विजयं तथा। वासुदेवजितामाशां यथासावजयत् प्रभुः॥
en: Vaishampayana said I shall now describe to you the conquests of Nakula and how that lord conquered the countries one subjugated by Vasudeva (Krishna).

sn: निर्याय खाण्डवप्रस्थात् प्रतीचीमभितोदिशम्। उद्दिश्य मतिमान् प्रायान्महत्या सेनया सह॥
en: The intelligent (Nakula), surrounded by a large ariny, started from the Khandavaprastha and marched towards the west.

sn: सिंहनादेन महता योधानां गर्जितेन च। रथनेमिनिनादैश्च कम्पयन् वसुधामिमाम्॥
en: The earth trembled with the shouts and the leonine roars of the warriors and the rattle of the chariot wheels.

sn: ततो बहुधनं रम्यं गवाढ्यं धनधान्यवत्। कार्तिकेयस्य दयितं रोहीतकमुपाद्रवत्॥
en: He first attacked the hilly countries called Rohitaka which was dear to Kartikeya, and which was delightful, prosperous, and full of kine and every king of wealth.

sn: तत्र युद्धं महच्चासीच्छूरैर्मत्तमयूरकैः। मरुभूमि स कात्स्र्थेन तथैव बहुधान्यकम्॥ च प्रतस्थे शैरीषकं महोत्थं च वशे चक्रे महाद्युतिः। आक्रोशं चैव राजर्षि तेन युद्धमभून्महत्॥
en: The battle between him and the heroic Mattamayurakas was a great one. The greatly effulgent (hero) then conquered the desert country and then the country, called Shairishaka which was full of wealth and paddy, then also that country, called Mahottha. a great battle was then fought with the royal saga, Akrosha.

sn: तान् दशार्णान् स जित्वा पाण्डुनन्दनः। शिबींस्त्रिगर्तानम्बष्ठान् मालवान् पञ्चकर्पटान्॥ तथा माध्यमिकांश्चैव वाटधानान् द्विजानथ। पुनश्च परिवृत्याथ पुष्करारण्यवसिनः॥ गणानुत्सवसंकेतान् व्यजयत् पुरुषर्षभः। सिन्धुकूलाश्रिता ये च ग्रामणीया महाबलाः॥
en: Having subjugated the Dasharnas, the Shiva, the Trigartas, the Ambashthas, the Malavas, the five tribes of Karpatavas the twice-born tribes called Madhyamikas and Vatadhanas, the son of Pandu (Nakula) marched onwards. They turning back, that best of men (Nakula) subjudged all the tribes named Utsavasanketas, the greatly powerful Gramaniyas living on the sea coast,

sn: शूद्राभीरगणाश्चैव ये चाश्रित्य सरस्वतीम्। वर्तयन्ति च ये मत्स्यैर्ये च पर्वतवासिनः॥
en: The Shudras, the Abhiras living on the banks of the Sarasvati, and all those tribes that lived on fishing and those that lived on the mountains.

sn: कृत्स्नं पञ्चनदं चैव तथैवामरपर्वतम्। उत्तरज्योतिषं चैव तथा दिव्यकटं पुरम्॥ द्वारपालं च तरसा वशे चक्रे महाद्युतिः। रामठान् हारहूणांश्च प्रतीच्याश्चैव ये नृपाः॥
en: The whole country, called after the five rivers, the mountains called Amara, the country called Uttarajyotisha, the city of Divyakata and the tribe called Dvarapala, the Ramathas, the Harahunas, and the various other kings of the west were all subjugated by the greatly effulgent hero.

sn: तान् सर्वान् स वशे चक्रे शासनादेव पाण्डवः। तत्रस्थः प्रेषयामास वासुदेवाय भारत॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, having brought them all under his sway, the Pandava Nakula then sent messengers to Vasudeva (Krishna).

sn: स चास्य गतभी राजन् प्रतिजग्राह शासनम्। ततः शाकलमभ्येत्य मद्राणां पुटभेदनम्॥
en: He (Krishna) with all the Yadavas accepted the sway (of the Pandavas). He then went to Shakala, the city of the Madras.

sn: मातुलं प्रीतिपूर्वेण शल्यं चक्रे वशे बली। स तेन सत्कृतो राज्ञा सत्कारार्हो विशाम्पते॥
en: The hero made his uncle Shalya to accept cheerfully their (the Pandava's) sway, o king, deserving as he was of his uncle's hospitality and entertainment, he was well entertained by him.

sn: रत्नानि भूरीण्यादाय सम्प्रतस्थे युधाम्पतिः। ततः सागरकुक्षिस्थान् म्लेच्छान् परमदारुणान्॥
en: The well-skilled hero in war (Sahadeva), taking a large amount of wealth and gems and jewels, marched onwards. He then subjugated the greatly fearful Mlecchas living in the Ocean.

sn: पह्नवान् बर्बरांश्चैव किरातान् यवनाञ्छकान्। ततो रत्नान्युपादाय वशे कृत्वा च पार्थिवान्। न्यवर्तत कुरुश्रेष्ठो नकुलचित्रमार्गवित्॥
en: Also the barbarians called Palhavas, the Kiratas, the Yavanas and the Shakas. Having thus subjugated and exacted tribute from all the kings.

sn: करभाणां सहस्राणि कोशं तस्य महात्मनः। ऊहुर्दश महाराज कृच्छ्रादिव महाधनम्॥
en: That best of the Kuru race, Nakula of great resources, then returned (to Indraprastha). So great was the treasure that he brought that ten thousand camels carried the treasure of that illustrious prince.

sn: इन्द्रप्रस्थगतं वीरमभ्येत्य स युधिष्ठिरम्। ततो माद्रीसुतः श्रीमान् धनं तस्मै न्यवेदयत्॥
en: O great king, having arrived Indraprastha, the hero offered all the wealth of Yudhishthira.

sn: एवं विजित्य नकुलो दिशं वरुणपालिताम्। प्रतीची वासुदेवेन निर्जितां भरतर्षभ॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, thus did Nakula conquer the west, presided over by Varuna, the at countries that had been once before conquered by Vasudeva (Krishna).

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच रक्षणाद् धर्मराजस्य सत्यस्य परिपालनात्। शत्रूणां क्षपणाच्चैव स्वकर्मनिरताः प्रजाः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Protected by Dharmaraja (Yudhishthira) and supported by Truth and also all their enemies being kept in check, all subjects (of the Pandava king) were always engaged in their respective business.

sn: बलीनां सम्यगादानाद् धर्मतश्चानुशासनात्। निकामवर्षी पर्जन्यः स्फीतो जनपदोऽभवत्॥
en: In consequence of the equitable taxation and the virtuous and the just rule of the king, the clouds poured as much rain as desired, and the country became prosperous.

sn: सर्वारम्भाः सुप्रवृत्ता गोरक्षा कर्षणं वणिक्। विशेषात् सर्वमेवैतत् संजज्ञे राजकर्मणः॥
en: As the result of the king's (virtuous) acts every thing of the kingdom, specially the breeding of cattle, agriculture and trade, greatly flourished.

sn: दस्युभ्यो वञ्चकेभ्यो वा राजन् प्रति परस्परम्। राजवल्लभतश्चैव नाश्रूयन्त मृषा गिरः॥
en: O king, even cheats and thieves, nay even the king's favourites, were never heard to speak lies amongst themselves,

sn: अवर्षं चातिवर्षं च व्याधिपावकमूर्च्छनम्। सवमेतत् तदा नासीद् धर्मनित्ये युधिष्ठिरे॥
en: During the reign of Yudhishthira, who was ever devote to virtue, there were no draughts, or floods, or plagues, or fires, or premature deaths.

sn: प्रियं कर्तुमुपस्थातुं बलिकर्म स्वभाजवम्। अभिहर्तुं नृपा जग्मुर्नान्यैः कार्यैः कथंचन॥
en: The (other) kings used to come to him only for agreeable services, or for paying their respects to him, or for offering to him tribute that did not (any way) impoverish them. They never used to come for any other purpose (such as conquests).

sn: धय॑र्धनागमैतस्य ववृधे निचयो पहान्। कर्तुं यस्य न शक्येत क्षयो वर्षशतैरपि॥
en: The large treasury of the King became so much filled with the hoards of wealth virtuously obtained that it could not be emptied even in one hundred years.

sn: स्वकोष्ठस्य परीमाणं कोशस्य च महीपतिः। विज्ञाय राजा कौन्तेयो यज्ञायैव मनो दधे॥
en: Having ascertained the state of his treasury and the extent of his possessions, the son of Kunti (Yudhishthira) set his heart upon performing the (Rajasuya) sacrifice.

sn: सुहृदयश्चैव ये सर्वे पृथक् च सह चाब्रुवन्। यज्ञकालस्तव विभो क्रियतामत्र साम्प्रतम्॥
en: His friends and relatives all separately and jointly said, "O lord, the time for the sacrifice has come. Let it be now performed without delay.”

sn: अथैव ब्रुवतामेव तेषामभ्याययौ हरिः। ऋषिः पुराणो वेदात्मादृश्यश्चैव विजानताम्॥ जगतस्तस्थुषां श्रेष्ठः प्रभवश्चाप्ययश्च ह। भूतभव्यभन्नाथः केशवः केशिसूदनः॥
en: When they were thus talking, there came that omniscient and ancient one, that soul of the Vedas, that invincible one as described by the learned, that foremost of all lasting existences in the universe, that origin of all things, that receptacle in which every thing is destroyed, that slayer of Keshi, Hari (Krishna).

sn: प्राकारः सर्ववृष्णीनामापत्स्वभयदोऽरिहा। बलाधिकारे निक्षिप्य सम्यगानकदुन्दुभिम्॥ उच्चावचमुपादाय धर्मराजाय माधवः। धनौघं पुरुषव्याघ्रो बलेन महताऽऽवृतः॥ तं धनौघमपर्यन्तं रत्नसागरमक्षयम्। नादयन् स्थघोषेण प्रविवेश पुरोत्तमम्॥
en: Having appointed Vasudeva command of the army and having brought with him for Dharmaraja Yudhishthira a large amount of wealth, the bulwark of all the Vrishnis, the dispelled of all fears in danger, the grinder of all foes, that best of men, Madhava, entered the excellent city (Indraprastha), surrounded with a large army to the was and filling, the atmosphere with the rattle of his chariot's wheels. The inexhaustible ocean of gems, that the Pandavas possessed.

sn: पूर्णमापूरयंस्तेषां द्विषच्छोकावहोऽभवत्। असूर्यमिव सूर्येण निवातमिव वायुना।। कृष्णेन समुपेतेन जहषे भारतं पुरम्॥
en: Was brought to a full limit by the wealth that he (Krishna) brought, and thus all their (the Pandava's) griefs were removed. By the arrival of Krishna, the capital of the Bharata race was gladdened like a sunless region by the sun, or a region of still air by gentle breeze.

sn: तं मुदाभिसमागम्य सत्कृत्य च यथाविधि। स पृष्ट्वा कुशलं चैव सुखासीनं युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Coming to him with joy and receiving him with all dues respect, Yudhishthira asked him his welfare. When he (Krishna) comfortably seated.

sn: धौम्यद्वैपायनमुखैर्ऋत्विग्भिः पुरुषर्षभ। भीमार्जुनयमैश्चैव सहितः कृष्णमब्रवीत्॥
en: That best of men (Yudhishthira) with the Ritvikas, Dhaumya and Dvaipayana being at their head, and also with Bhima, Arjuna and the twins (Nakula and Sahadeva) thus spoke to Krishna.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच त्वत्कृते पृथिवी सर्वा मद्वशे कृष्ण वर्तते। वार्ष्णेय त्वत्प्रसादादुपार्जितम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said O Krishna, it is for you that the whole earth has come rinder my sway. O descendant of the Vrishni race, it is through your favour that this vast wealth has been earned by me.

sn: सोऽहममिच्छामि तत् सर्वं विधिवद् देवकीसुत। उपयोक्तुं द्विजायेभ्यो हव्यवाहे च माधव॥
en: O Madhava, O son of Devaki, I desire to devote all this wealth to the Brahmanas and to the. carrier of sacrificial libations (Agni) according to the ordinance.

sn: तदहं यष्टुमिच्छामि दाशार्ह सहितस्त्वया। अनुजैश्च महाबाहो तनमानुज्ञातुमर्हसि॥
en: O prince of the Dasarha race, O mighty armed hero, you should grant me permission to celebrate the Rajasuya sacrifice along with you and with my brothers.

sn: धनं च बहु तद् दीक्षाप गोविन्द त्वमात्मानं महाभुजा त्वयीष्टवति दाशार्ह विपाप्मा भविता ह्यहम्॥
en: O Govinda, O long-armed hero, O prince of the Dasarha race, install yourself in that sacrifice. If you perform the sacrifice, I shall be cleansed from sin.

sn: मां वाप्यभ्यनुजानीहि स हैमिरनुजैविभो। अनुज्ञातस्त्वया कृष्ण प्राप्नुयां क्रतुमुत्तमम्॥
en: O lord, O Krishna, grant permission to me that I may be installed in the sacrifice along with my these younger brothers, for if permitted by you, I shall be able to enjoy the fruit of that excellent sacrifice.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तं कृष्णः प्रत्युषाचेदं बहूक्त्वा गुणविस्तरम्।
en: Vaishampayana said To him replied Krishna after extolling his many virtues.

sn: त्वमेव राजशार्दूल सम्राडो महाक्रतुम्। सम्प्राप्नुहि त्वया प्राप्ते कृतकृत्यास्ततो वयम्॥ यजस्वाभीप्सितं यज्ञं मयि श्रेयस्यवस्थिते। नियुक्ष्व त्वं च मां कृत्ये सर्वं कर्तास्मि ते वचः॥
en: Krishna said O best of kings, you deserve the imperial dignity. Let therefore the great (Rajasuya) sacrifice be performed. If you perform that sacrifice, and if you obtain its fruit, we shall all consider ourselves as crowned with success. I am always engaged in seeking your good. Perform the sacrifice you desire. Appoint me in some office in that sacrifice. I shall obey all your commands.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच सफलः कृष्ण संकल्पः सिद्धिश्च नियता मम। यस्य मे त्वं हृषीकेश यथेप्सितमुपस्थितः॥
en: Yudhishthira said O Krishna, O Hrishikesha, when you have come here agreeably to my wish, my resolve is fulfilled; success is sure to come to my work.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच अनुज्ञातस्तु कृष्णेन पाण्वो भ्रातृभिः सह। ईजितुं राजसूयेन साधनान्युपचक्रमे॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having been commanded by Krishna, the son of Pandu (Yudhishthira) with his brothers employed himself to collect the necessary materials for the Rajasuya (sacrifice).

sn: ततस्त्वाज्ञापयामास पाण्डवोऽरिनिबर्हणः। सहदेव युधां श्रेष्ठं मन्त्रिणश्चैव सर्वशः॥
en: That chastiser of foes, the son of Pandu (Yudhishthira), commanded that foremost of all warriors, Sahadeva, and also all his ministers, saying.

sn: अस्मिन् क्रतौ यथोक्तानि यज्ञाङ्गानि द्विजातिभिः। तथोपकरणं सर्वं मङ्गलानि च सर्वशः॥ अधियज्ञांश्च सम्भारान् धौम्योक्तान् क्षिप्रमेव हि। समानयन्तु पुरुषा यथायोगं यथाक्रमम्॥
en: “Let men be appointed to collect without loss of time all those articles which the Brahmanas will direct as necessary for the performance of this sacrifice, and also all auspicious necessaries and things that Dhaumya may order to be collected; each of the king required and one after the other in due order.

sn: इन्द्रसेनो विशोकश्च पूस्चार्जुनसारथिः। अन्नाद्याहरणे युक्ताः सन्तु मत्प्रियकाम्यया॥
en: Let Indrasena and Vishoka and the charioteer of Arjuna, Puru, if, they desire to please me, be employed in collecting them.

sn: सर्वकामाश्च कार्यन्तां रसगन्धसमन्विताः। मनोरथप्रीतिकरा द्विजानां कुरुसत्तम॥
en: O best of the Kuru race (Sahadeva) let them gather every article agreeable to taste and smell, articles which may delight and attract the hearts of the Brahmanas."

sn: तद्वाक्यसमकालं च कृतं सर्वं न्यवेदयत्। सहदेवो युधां श्रेष्ठो धर्मराजे युधिष्ठिरे॥
en: As soon as these words were uttered by Dharmaraja Yudhishthira, that foremost of all warriors, Sahadeva, informed the king that they had been all done.

sn: ततो द्वैपायनो राजन्नृत्विजः समुपानयत्। वेदान्व महाभागान् साक्षान्मूर्तिमतो द्विजान्॥
en: O king, Dvaipayana then appointed the Ritvijas, who were high-souled, and who were like the Vedas in their personified forms.

sn: स्वयं ब्रह्मत्वमकरोत् तस्य सत्यवतीसुतः। धनंजयानामृषभः सुसामा सामगोऽभवत्॥
en: The son of Satyavati (Vyasa) himself became the Brahma in that sacrifice, the best of the Dhananjaya race, Susama, became the chaunter of the Sama Veda.

sn: याज्ञवल्क्यो बभूबाथ ब्रह्मिष्ठोऽध्वर्युसत्तमः। पैलो होता वसोः पुत्रो धोम्येन सहितोऽभवत्॥
en: The Brahma-knowing Yajnavalkya became the Adhvaryu, the son of Vasu Paila, with Dhaumya, became the Hotas.

sn: एतेषां पुत्रवर्गाश्च शिष्याश्च भरतर्षभ। बभूवर्होत्रगाः सर्वे वेदवेदाङ्गपारगाः॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, the disciples and the sons of these men, all well-acquainted with the Vedas, became Hotragas,

sn: ते वाचयित्वा पुण्याहमूहयित्वा च तं विधिम्। शास्त्रोक्तं पूजयामासुस्तद् देवयजनं महत्॥
en: Having uttered benedictions, and having recited the objects of the sacrifice, all of them worshipped the large (sacrificial) ground according to the ordinance.

sn: तत्र चक्रुरनुज्ञाताः शरणान्युत शिल्पिनः। गन्धवन्ति विशालानि वेश्मानीव दिवौकसाम्॥
en: Commanded by the Brahmanas, the builders and the artifices erected their many houses that were specious and that were well perfumed like the temples of gods.

sn: तत आज्ञापयामास स राजा राजसत्तमः। सहदेवं तदा सद्यो मन्त्रिणं पुरुषर्षभः॥
en: Thereupon that best of kings, and that best of men, the king (Yudhishthira) immediately commanded his minister Sahadeva saying.

sn: आमन्त्रणार्थं दूतांस्त्वं प्रेषयस्वाशुगान् द्रुतम्। उपश्रुत्य वचो राज्ञः स दूतान् प्राहिणोत् तदा॥ आमन्त्रयध्वं राष्ट्रेषु ब्राह्मणान् भूमिपानथ। विशश्च मान्यान् शूद्रांश्च सर्वानानयतेति च॥
en: “Dispatch soon (some-swift messengers to invite all. “Having heard the royal command, he (Sahadeva) soon sent messengers saying. “Invite all the Brahmanas of the kingdom, all the owners of land (Kshatriyas). All the Vaishyas, and all the respectable Shudras. Bring them all here (in this sacrifice)".

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच समाज्ञप्तास्ततो दूताः पाण्डवेयस्य शासनात्। आमन्त्रयाम्बभूवुश्च आनयंश्चापरान् द्रुतम्। तथा परानपि नरानात्मनः शीघ्रगामिनः॥
en: At the command of the Pandavas those swift messengers invited every one without any loss of time, and they brought with them many persons both friends and strangers.

sn: ततस्ते तु यथाकालं कुन्तीपुत्रं युधिष्ठिरम्। दीक्षयाञ्चक्रिरे विप्रा राजसूयाय भारत॥
en: o descendant of Bharata, at the proper time the Brahmanas installed the son of Kunti, Yudhishthira, in the sacrifice,

sn: दीक्षितः स तु धर्मात्मा धर्मराजो युधिष्ठरः। जगाम यज्ञायतनं वृतो विप्रैः सहस्रशः॥
en: When the virtuous Dharmaraja Yudhishthira was installed in the sacrifice, he went to the sacrificial ground, surrounded by thousands of Brahmanas.

sn: भ्रातृभििितभिश्चैव सुहृद्भिः सचिवैः सह। क्षत्रियैश्च मनुष्येन्द्रैर्नानादेशसमागतैः॥
en: And accompanied by his brothers, relatives, friends and ministers, and also by many best of men among the Kshatriyas who had assembled from various countries.

sn: अमात्यैश्च नरश्रेष्ठो धर्मो विग्रहवानिव। आजग्मुर्ब्राह्मणास्तत्र विषयेभ्यस्ततस्ततः॥ सर्वविद्यासु निष्णाता वेदवेदाङ्गपारगाः। तेषामावसथांश्चक्रुर्धर्मराजस्य शासनात्॥
en: And also by many counsellors. Many Brahmanas, learned in all the branches of knowledge and well versed in the Vedas and the Vedangas, began to assemble there from various directions. At the command of the Dharmaraja, habitations were erected for them.

sn: बह्वन्नाच्छादनैयुक्तान् सगणानां पृथक् पृथक्। सर्वर्तुगुणसम्पन्नान् शिल्पिनोऽथ सहस्रशः॥
en: And their attendants, separately for each by thousands of artisans who were endued with all qualifications, they were filled with much food and many clothes.

sn: तेषु ते न्यवसन् राजन् ब्राह्मणानृपसत्कृताः। कथयन्तः कथां बह्वीः पश्यन्तो नटनर्तकान्॥
en: O king, having been duly worshipped by the king, Brahmanas continued to live there, passing their time in conversation on various topics and seeing the performance of actors and dancers.

sn: भुञ्जतां चैव विप्राणां वदतां च महास्वनः। अनिशं श्रूयते तत्र मुदितानां महात्मनाम्॥
en: The noise of these illustrious Brahmanas eating and talking cheerfully was continuously heard.

sn: दीयतां दीयतामेषां भुज्यतां भुज्यतामिति। एवम्प्रकाराः संजल्पाः श्रूयन्ते स्मात्र नित्यशः॥
en: "Give, Give", "Eat, Eat", were the words that were continuously and every day heard there.

sn: गवां शतसहस्राणि शयनानां च भारत। रुक्मस्य योषितां चैव धर्म राजः पृथग् ददौ॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, Dharmaraja separately gave to each of those Brahmanas thousands of kine, beds, golden coins and damsels.

sn: प्रावर्ततैवं यज्ञः स पाण्डवस्य महात्मनः। पृथिव्यामेकवीरस्य शक्रस्येव त्रिविष्टपे॥
en: Thus like the sacrifice formerly performed by Shakra (Indra) in heaven, began the sacrifice of that matchless hero, the illustrious Pandava (Yudhishthira), on earth.

sn: ततो युधिष्ठिरो राजा प्रेषयामास पाण्डवम्। नकुलं हास्तिनपुरं भीष्माय पुरुषर्षभः॥ द्रोणाय धृतराष्ट्राय विदुराय कृपाय च। भ्रातृणां चैव सर्वेषां येऽनुरक्ता युधिष्ठिरे॥
en: Then that best of men, the king Yudhishthira, sent the Pandava Nakula to Hastinapur to Bring Bhishma, Drona, Dhritarashtra, Vidura, Kripa, and all those cousins who were attached to him.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच स गत्वा हास्तिनपुरं नकुलः समितिंजयः। भीष्ममामन्त्रयाञ्चक्रे धृतराष्ट्रं च पाण्डवः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having gone to Hastinapur the ever victorious son of Pandu Nakula at their head, invited Bhishma and Dhritarashtra.

sn: सत्कृत्यामन्त्रतास्तेन आचार्यप्रमुखास्ततः। प्रययुः प्रीतमनसो यज्ञं ब्रह्मपुरः सराः॥
en: Having (thus) been invited by due ceremonies, the elders of the Kuru race, with the preceptor at their head and with Brahmanas walking in front came joyfully to sacrifice.

sn: संश्रुत्य धर्मराजस्य यज्ञं यज्ञविदस्तदा। अन्ये च शतशस्तुष्टैर्मनोभिर्भरतर्षभ॥ द्रष्टकामाः सभां चैव धर्मराजं च पाण्डवम्। दिग्भ्यः सर्वे समापेतुः क्षत्रियास्तत्र भारत॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, O descendant of Bharata, having heard of the sacrifice of king Yudhishthira, and wishing to see the son of Pandu Dharamaraja (Yudhishthira) and his Sabha, hundreds of other Yajna-knowing Kshatriyas joyfully came there from various countries.

sn: समुपादाय रत्नानि विविधानि महान्ति च। धृतराष्ट्रश्च भीष्मश्च विदुरश्च महामतिः॥
en: They brought with them various costly gems and jewels. The high-minded Bhishma, Dhritarashtra and Vidura,

sn: दुर्योधनपुरोगाश्च भ्रातरः सर्व एव ते। गान्धारराजः सुबलः शकुनिश्च महाबलः॥
en: All the (Kuru) brothers with Duryodhana at their head, the king of Gandharva Subala, the greatly strong Shakuni.

sn: अचलो वृषकश्चैव कर्णश्च राथिनां वरः। तथा शल्यश्च बलवान् बाह्निकश्च महाबलः॥
en: Achala, Vrishaka, that best of all carwarriors, Karna, the greatly powerful Shalya, the exceedingly strong Valhika.

sn: सोमदत्तोऽथ कौरव्यो भूरिभूरिश्रवाः शलः। अश्वत्थामा कृपो द्रोणः सैन्धवश्च जयद्रथः॥
en: Somadatta, Bhuri of the Kuru race, Bhurisrava, Sala, Ashvathama, Kripa, Drona, the king of Sindhu, Jayadratha.

sn: यक्षसेनः सपुत्रश्च शाल्वश्च वसुधाधिपः। प्राग्ज्योतिषश्च नृपतिर्भगदत्तो महारथः॥
en: Yakshasena with his sons, that lord of the earth Shalva, the great car-warrior, Bhagadatta, the king of Pragjyotisha.

sn: स तु सर्वैः सहम्लेच्छैः सागरानूपवासिभिः। राजानो राजा चैव बृहद्बलः॥ पर्वतीयाच
en: With all the Mlecchas living in the marshy regions along the sea coast, many mountain kings, king Vrihadvala.

sn: पौण्ड्रको वासुदेवश्च वङ्गः कालिङ्गकस्तथा। आकर्षाः कुन्तलाश्चैव मालवाश्चान्ध्रकास्तथा॥
en: The king of the Paundrakas, Vasudeva the king of Vanga and Kalinga, Akarsha, Kuntala, the kings of the Malavas and the Andhakas,

sn: द्राविडाः सिंहलाश्चैव राजा काश्मीरकस्तथा। कुन्तिभोजो महातेजाः पार्थिवो गौरवाहनः॥
en: And of the Dravidas and the Singhalas, the king of Kashmira, the greatly effulgent king Kuntibhoja, the king Gauravahana.

sn: वालिकाश्चापरे शूरा राजानः नः सर्व एव ते। विराटः सह पुत्राभ्यां मावेल्लश्च महाबलः॥
en: Balhika, and many other heroic kings, Virata with his two sons, the greatly powerful Mavella,

sn: राजानो राजपुत्राश्च नानाजनपदेश्वराः। शिशुपालो महावीर्यः सह पुत्रेण भारत॥ आगच्छत् पाण्डवेयस्य यज्ञं समरदुर्मदः। रामश्चैवानिरुद्धश्च कश्च सहसारण:॥
en: Various other kings and potentates ruling over various countries the greatly effulgent and invincible in battle king Sisupala with his son, o descendant of Bharata, (all these kings) came to the sacrifice of the Pandavas, Rama, Aniruddha, Kanaka, Sarana.

sn: गदप्रद्युम्नसाम्बाश्च चारुदेष्णश्च वीर्यवान्। उल्मुको निशद्दश्चैव वीरश्चाङ्गावहस्तथा॥
en: Gada, Pradyumna, Samba, the greatly energetic Charudeshna Ulmuka, Nishatha, the brave Angavaha.

sn: वृष्णयो निखिलाश्चान्ये समाजग्मुर्महारथाः। एते चान्ये च बहवो राजानो मध्यदेशजाः॥
en: And numerous other Vrishnis, all great car-warriors, came to that sacrifice. These and many other kings of the middle country

sn: आजग्मुः पाण्डुपुत्रस्य राजसूयं महाक्रतुम्। ददुस्तेषामावसथान् धर्मराजस्य शासनात्॥
en: Came to that great Rajasuya sacrifice of the son of Pandu. At the command of Dharmaraja (Yudhishthira), houses assigned to them all. were

sn: बहुभक्ष्यान्वितान् राजन् दीर्घिकावृक्षशोभितान्। तथा धर्मात्मजः पूजां चक्रे तेषां महात्मनाम्॥
en: O king! (these houses) were full of various kinds of eatables; they were adorned with tanks and tall trees. There is those houses the son of Dharma (Yudhishthira) worshipped all those illustrious (monarchs).

sn: सत्कृताश्च यथोद्दिष्टाञ्जग्मुरावसथान् नृपाः। कैलासशिखर प्रख्यान् मनोज्ञान् द्रव्यभूषितान्॥
en: Having been duly worshipped by the king, they retired to the houses assigned to them. Those houses were like the cliffs of Kailasa, they were delightful and adorned with every king of furniture.

sn: सर्वतः संवृतानुच्चैः प्राकारैः सुकृतैः सितैः। सुवर्णजालसंवीतान् मणिकुट्टिमभूषितान्॥
en: They were enclosed on all sides with wellbuilt, high and white-washed walls. Their windows were cover with net works of gold and their interior was adorned with strings of pearls.

sn: सुखारोहणसोपानान् महासनपरिच्छदान्। स्रग्दामसमवच्छन्नानुत्तमागुरुगन्धिनः॥
en: Their stairs were easy of ascent, and their floors were all covered with costly carpets. They were all adorned with garlands of flowers and perfumed with excellent aloes.

sn: हंसेन्दुवर्णसदृशानायोजनसुदर्शनान्। असम्बाधान् समद्वारान् युतानुच्चावचैर्गुणैः॥
en: Being white as the snow or the moon, they looked exceedingly beautiful even from the distance of a Yojana. Their doors were all uniformly made, and they were wide enough to admit a crowd of persons (all at once).

sn: बहुधातुनिबद्धाङ्गान् हिमवच्छिखरानिव। विश्रान्तास्ते ततोऽपश्यन् भूमिपा भूरिदक्षिणम्॥ वृतं सदस्यैर्बहुभिर्धर्मराज युधिष्ठिरम्। तत् सदः पार्थिवैः कीर्णं ब्राह्मणैश्च महर्षिभिः। भाजते स्म तट राजन् नाकपृष्ठं यथामरैः॥
en: Made of many metals, they looked like the peaks of the Himalayas. After resting for a while (in these mansions) all those kings saw the great. Dakshina giving Dharmaraja Yudhishthira, surrounded by numerous Sadasyas. O king, the sacrificial ground, crowded with kings, (Brahmanas and great Rishis, looked as beautiful as heaven crowded with the celestials.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच पितामहं गुरुं चैव प्रत्युद्गम्य युधिष्ठिरः। अभिवाद्यः ततो राजन्निदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said O king, having approached and worshipped his grandfather (Bhishma) and his preceptor (Drona), Yudhishthira thus spoke to,

sn: भीष्मं द्रोणं कृपं द्रौणिं दुर्योधनविविंशती। अस्मिन् यज्ञे भवन्तो मामनुगृहणन्तु सर्वशः॥
en: Bhishma, Drona, Kripa, the son of Drona (Ashvathama), Duryodhana and Vivanshati. “But all of you gracious to me in my this sacrifice.

sn: इदं वः सुमहच्चैव यदिहास्ति धनं मम। प्रणयन्तु भवन्तो मां यथेष्टमभिमन्त्रिताः॥
en: All this my great wealth is yours. Consult you all with one another, and guide me as you desire."

sn: एवमुक्त्वा स तान् सर्वान् दीक्षितः पाण्डवाग्रजः। युयोज स यथायोगमधिकारेष्वनन्तरम्॥
en: Having thus spoken to all, the eldest of the Pandavas (Yudhishthira), who had been already installed in the sacrifice, appointed every one of them in suitable office.

sn: भक्ष्यभोज्याधिकारेषु दुःशासनमयोजयत्। परिग्रहे ब्राह्मणानामश्वत्थामानमुक्तवान्॥
en: He appointed Dushasana to superintend the department of food and other enjoyable articles. Ashvathama was solicited to look after the Brahmanas.

sn: राज्ञां तु प्रतिपूजार्थं संजयं स न्ययोजयत्। कृताकृतपरिज्ञाने भीष्मद्रोणौ महामती॥
en: Sanjaya was appointed to return worship to all (invited kings). The high-minded Bhishma and Drona were employed to see what was done and what was left undone.

sn: हिरण्यस्य सुवर्णस्य रत्नानां चान्ववेक्षणे। दक्षिणानां च वै दाने कृपं राजा न्ययोजयत्॥
en: The king (Yudhishthira) appointed Kripa to look after the diamonds, the gold the pearls and the gems, and he was also appointed to distribute Dakshina (gift) to the Brahmanas.

sn: तथान्यान् पुरुषव्याघ्रांस्तस्मिंस्तस्मिन् न्ययोजयत्। वाह्निको धृतराष्ट्रश्च सोमदत्तो जयद्रथः। नकुलेन समानीताः स्वामिवत् तत्र रेमिरे॥
en: Thus other best of men were all appointed in various other offices. Having been brought there by Nakula, Valhika, Dhritarashtra, Somadatta, and Jayadratha enjoyed there as the lords (of the sacrifice).

sn: क्षत्ता व्ययकरस्त्वासीद् विदुरः सर्वधर्मावेत्। दुर्योधनस्त्वर्हणानि प्रतिजग्राह सर्वशः॥
en: Kshatta (Vidura), learned in all the precepts of virtue, became the master of exchequer. Duryodhana became the receiver of tributes brought by the kings.

sn: चरणक्षालने कृष्णो ब्राह्मणानां स्वयं ह्यभूत। सर्वलोकसमावृत्तः पिप्रीषुः फलमुत्तमम्॥
en: Krishna, the centre of all men, with the desire of gaining the excellent fruit, him-self willingly took the task of washing the feet of the Brahmanas.

sn: द्रष्टुकामाः सभां चैव धर्मराजं युधिष्ठिरम्। न कश्चिदाहरत् तत्र सहस्रावरमर्हणम्॥
en: Wishing to see that Sabha and also Dharmaraja Yudhishthira, no one came there with less tribute than one thousand (in kind) number of quantity).

sn: रत्नैश्च बहुभिस्तत्र धर्मराजमवर्धयत् कथं तु मम कौरव्यो रत्नदानैः समाप्नुयात्॥ यज्ञमित्येव राजनः स्पर्धमाना ददुर्धनम्। भवनैः सविमानाप्रैः सोदर्बलसंवृतैः॥ लोकराजविमानैश्च ब्राह्मणावसथैः सह। कृतैरावसथैर्दिव्यैर्विमानप्रमिमैस्तथा।॥ विचित्रै रत्नवद्भिश्च ऋद्ध्या परमया युतैः। राजभिश्च समावृत्तैरतीव श्रीसमृद्धिभिः। अशोभत सदो राजन् कौन्तेयस्य महात्मनः॥
en: All (the assembled kings) honoured Dharmaraja with large presents of jewels, Every one of those kings proudly said, “Let the Kuru king complete his sacrifice with the gems and wealth that I present to him,(without taking any presents from any other king)”. O king, the sacrificial ground of the illustrious son of Kunti, crowded with guards and warriors, with the cars of the celestialss and with the kings, all possessing beauty and wealth, looked extremely handsome with the numerous palaces, so built as to last for ever, and so high that their tops touched the car of the celestialss who came to see that sacrifice, with the dwellings of the Brahmanas, and the mansions that were built for the king which resembled the cars of the celestialss, and adorned with gems and filled with every king of wealth.

sn: ऋद्ध्या तु वरुणं देवं स्पर्धमानो युधिष्ठिरः। षडग्निनाथ यज्ञेन सोऽयजद् दक्षिणावता॥
en: Yudhishthira, as if vying with the deity Varuna himself in wealth, commenced the (Rajasuya) sacrifice which was distinguished by large Dakshinas to Brahmanas and emblazoned with the six fires.

sn: सर्वाञ्जनान् सर्वकामैः समृद्धैः समतर्पयत्। अन्नवान् बहुभक्ष्यश्च भुक्तवज्जनसंवृतः। रत्नोपहारसम्पन्नो बभूव स समागमः॥
en: The king gratified every body with present of great value and with every object that one could desire, with abundance of rice and of every kind of food, and also with a large quantity of jewels brought as tribute. Every one of that vast concourse of people was fed to his fill.

sn: इडाज्यहोमाहुतिभिर्मत्रशिक्षाविशारदैः। तस्मिन् हि ततृपुर्देवास्तते यज्ञे महर्षिभिः॥
en: The celestialss were gratified in that sacrifice by the Ida, Ghee, Homa and libations poured by the great Rishis, learned in Mantras and pronunciations.

sn: यथा देवास्तथा विप्रा दक्षिणान्नमहाधनैः। ततृपुः सर्ववर्णाश्च तस्मिन् यज्ञे मुदान्विताः॥
en: Like the celestialss, the Brahmanas were also gratified with the sacrificial gifts, food and great wealth. Men of all the orders were gratified and were filled with joy.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततोऽभिषेचनीयेऽछि ब्राह्मणा राजभिः सह। अन्तर्वेदी प्रविविशुः सत्कारार्हा महर्षयः॥
en: Vaishampayana said On the last day of the sacrifice when the king (Yudhishthira) was to be sprinkled over with sacred water, the great Brahmana Rishis with (all) the monarchs(present there) entered the inner enclosure (of the sacrificial ground).

sn: नारदप्रमुखास्तस्यामन्तवेद्यां महात्मनः। समासीनाः शुशुभिरे सह राजर्षिभिस्तदा॥ समेता ब्रह्मभवने देवा देवर्षयस्तथा। कर्मान्तरमुपासन्तो जजल्पुरमितौजसः॥
en: Those illustrious and Mantra-knowing Rishis, with Narada at their head and with the royal sages seated at their ease looked like the celestialss seated in the mansion of Brahma in the company of the celestials Rishis, those Rishis of immeasurable energy, having then obtained leisure, started various topics of conversation.

sn: एवमेतन्न चाप्येवमेवं चैतन्न चान्यथा। इत्यूचुर्बहवस्तत्र वितण्डा वै परस्परम्॥
en: "This is so," "This is not so." "This is even so," "This cannot be other wise," thus did many of them engage in arguments with one another.

sn: कृशानार्थांस्ततः केचिदकृशांस्तत्र कुर्वते। अकृशांश्च कृशाश्चर्हेतुभिः शास्त्रानिश्चयैः॥
en: Some amongst the disputants made the weaker arguments to appear stronger, and the stronger ones the weaker by their arguments based on Shastras.

sn: तत्र मेधाविनः केचिदर्थमन्यैरुदीरितम्। टिचिक्षिपुर्यथा धेना नमोगतमिवामिषम्॥
en: Some greatly intelligent disputants fell upon the position urged by others as hawks dart at meat thrown into the air.

sn: केचिद् धर्मार्थकुशलाः केचित् तत्र महाव्रताः। रेमिरे कथयन्तश्च सर्वभाष्यविदां वरा:॥
en: Some amongst them, learned in the interpretations of Shastras, and some others of rigid vows, well acquainted with every commentary and gloss, engaged themselves in pleasant conversations.

sn: सा वेदिर्वेदसम्पन्नैवद्विजमहर्षिभिः। आबभासे समाकीर्णा नक्षत्रैद्यौरिवायता॥
en: That (sacrificial) plate for, crowded with the celestialss, Brahmanas and the great Rishis, all endued with the Vedas, looked as beautiful as the sky studded with the stars.

sn: न तस्यां संनिधौ शूद्रः कश्चिदासीन चाव्रती। अन्तर्वेद्यां तदा राजन् युधिष्ठिरनिवेशने॥
en: O king, there was no Shudra or any man without vows near the inner (sacrificial) platform of Yudhishthira's palace.

sn: तां तु लक्ष्मीवतो लक्ष्मी तदा यज्ञविधानजाम्। तुतोष नारदः पश्यन् धर्मराजस्य धीमतः॥
en: Seeing the prosperity of the prosperous and intelligent Dharamraja which was the result of that sacrifice, Narada became exceedingly happy.

sn: अथ चिन्तां समापेदे च मुनिर्मनुजाधिप। नारदस्तु तदा पश्यन् सर्वक्षत्रसमागमम्॥
en: O ruler of men, seeing the assemblage of all Kshatriyas, (in that sacrifice), the Rishi Narada became thoughtful.

sn: सस्मार च पुरा वृत्तां कथां तां पुरुषर्षभ। अंशावतरणे यासौ ब्रह्मणो भवनेऽभवत्॥
en: O best of men, he recollected the words he had heard in the abode of Brahma; regarding the Angshavatarana, (incarnations of portions of every deity).

sn: देवानां संगमं तं तु विज्ञाय कुरुनन्दन। नारदः पुण्डरीकाक्षं सस्मार मनसा हरिम्॥
en: O descendant of Kuru, knowing that assembly was an assembly of the celestialss, Narada thought in his mind the lotus-eyed Hari.

sn: साक्षात् स विबुधारिघ्नः क्षत्रे नारायणो विभुः। प्रतिज्ञां पालयंश्चमां जातः परपुरंजयः॥ संदिदेश पुरायोऽसौ विबुधान् भूतकृत् स्वयम्। अन्योयमभिनिघ्नन्तः पुनर्लोकानवाप्स्यथ॥
en: He knew that the creator of every object, the exalted god of all gods, Narayana, who had formerly commanded the celestialss saying, “Take your births on earth and kill one another and then come back to heaven," that chastiser of all the enemies of the celestialss, that subjugator of all hostile towns, had taken his birth in the Kshatriya order to fulfil his own purpose.

sn: इति नारायणः शम्भुर्भगवान् भूतभावनः। आदित्यविबुधान् सर्वानजायत यदुक्षये॥
en: The illustrious lord of the universe, Shambhu, Narayana, having thus commanded all the celestialss, had taken his birth in the race of Yadu.

sn: क्षितावन्धकवृष्णीनां वंशे वंशभूतां वरः। परया शुशुभे लक्ष्या नक्षत्राणामिवोडुराट्॥
en: Having been born in the Andhaka Vrishni race on earth, that foremost of all perpetuator of races was graced with great good fortune and was shinning like the moon among the stars.

sn: यस्य बाहुबलं सेन्द्राः सुराः सर्व उपासते। सोऽयं मानुषवन्नाम हरिरास्तेऽरिमर्दनः॥
en: He whose prowess of arms was adored by the celestialss with Indra, that Hari, that chastiser of foes, was then living in the world of men in a human form.

sn: अहो बत महद्भूतं स्वयंभूर्यदिदं स्वयम्। आदास्यति पुनः क्षत्रमेवं बलसमन्वितम्॥
en: "Oh! what could be greater wonder than that the self-creates himself will take away (from earth) all these Kshatriyas endued with great strength.

sn: इत्येतां नारदश्चिन्तां चिन्तयामास सर्ववित्। हरि नारायणं ध्यात्वा यज्ञैरीज्यन्तमीश्वरम्॥
en: Thus reflected the omniscient Narada who knew that Hari, Narayana, (Krishna) was no other than the Supreme Being, whom every body worships with sacrifices.

sn: तस्मिन् धर्मविदां श्रेष्ठो धर्मराजस्य धीमतः। महाध्वरे महाबुद्धिस्तस्थौ स बहुमानतः॥
en: That foremost of all men, learned in the precepts of virtue, that greatly intelligent man (Narada), (thinking of all this), sat in the sacrifice of the intelligent Dharmaraja (Yudhishthira) with feelings of awe.

sn: ततो भीष्मोऽब्रवीद् राजन् धर्मराज युधिष्ठिरम्। क्रियतामहणं राज्ञां यथाहमिति भारत॥
en: O king, Bhishma then thus spoke to Dharmaraja Yudhishthira, “O descendant of Bharata, now offer Arghyas to the kings as each deserves".

sn: आचार्यमृत्विजं चैव संयुजं च युधिष्ठिर। स्नातकं च प्रियं प्राहुः षडार्हान् नृपं तथा॥ एतानानभिगतानाहुः संवत्सरोषितान्। त इमे कालपूगस्य महतोऽस्मानुपागताः॥
en: O Yudhishthira, hear, the preceptor, the sacrificial priest, the relative,, the Snataka, the friend and the king, these are the six (classes of persons) who deserve to get the Arghya. The wise men have said that when any of there live with one for a full one year, he deserves to be worshipped with the presentation of Arghya. These kings have been staying with us for a very long time,

sn: एषामेकैकशो राजन्नय॑मानीयतामिति। अथ चैषां वरिष्ठाय समायोपनीयताम्॥
en: Therefore, O king, bring Arghya for each of them; and let the Arghya be first presented to him who is the foremost of all of them.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच कस्मै भवान् मन्यतेऽर्घ्यमेकस्मै कुरुनन्दन। उपनीयमानं युक्तं च तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह॥
en: Yudhishthira said O descendant of Kuru, O grandsire, whom do you consider to be the foremost of these (men present here), and to whom should the Arghya be presented first. Tell me this.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततो भीष्मः शान्तनवो बुद्ध्याद् निश्चित्य वीर्यवान्। अमन्यत तदा कृष्णमहणीयतमं भुवि॥
en: Vaishampayana said O Descendant of Bharata, the son of Shantanu, Bhishma, settled it by his great intelligence that Krishna was the foremost of all on earth.

sn: भीष्म उवाच एष ह्येषां समस्तानां तेजोवलपराक्रमः। मध्ये तपन्निवाभाति ज्योतिषामिव भास्करः॥
en: Bhishma said As sun shines among all luminous objects, so shines this (Krishna) among all (these kings and potentates) by his effulgence, strength and prowess.

sn: असूर्यमिव सूर्येण निर्वातमिव वायुना। भासितं ह्लादितं चैव कृष्णेनेदं सदो हि नः॥
en: This sacrificial ground is illuminated and gladdened by Krishna like a sunless region by the sun and a airless region by the air.

sn: तस्मै भीष्माभ्यनुज्ञातः सहदेवः प्रतापवान्। उपजह्वेऽथ विधिवद् वार्ष्णेयायार्घ्यमुत्तमम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Then commanded by Bhishma, the powerful Sahadeva proceeded to present in due form the excellent Arghya to the prince of the Vrishni race, (Krishna).

sn: प्रतिजग्राह तत् कृष्णः शास्त्रदृष्टेन कर्मणा। शिशुपालस्तु तां पूजां वासुदेवे न चक्षमे॥
en: Krishna also (agreed to) accept that worship according to the forms of the ordinance. But Shishupala could not bear that worship (proposed to be) offered to Vasudeva (Krishna),

sn: स उपालभ्य भीष्मं च धर्मराजं च संसदि। अपाक्षिपद् वासुदेवं चेदिराजो महाबलः॥
en: The greatly powerful Chedi-king (Shishupala), after reproving Bhishma and Dharmaraja (Yudhishthira) in the presence of that assembly, began to censure Vasudeva (Krishna).

sn: शिशुपाल उवाच नायमर्हति वार्ष्णेयस्तिष्ठत्स्विह महात्मसु महीपतिषु कौरव्य राजवत् पार्थिवाहणम्॥
en: Shishupala said O descendant of Kuru, when so many illustrious kings are present here, this man of the Vrishni race does not deserve a royal worship like a king.

sn: नायं युक्तः समाचार: पाण्डवेषु महात्मसु। यत् कामात् पुण्डरीकाक्षं पाण्डवार्चितवानसि॥
en: Your this conduct in willfully making this lotus-eyed hero worshipped by the Pandavas is not worthy of the illustrious Pandavas.

sn: बाला यूयं न जानीध्वं धर्मः सूक्ष्मो हि पाण्डवाः। अयं च स्मृत्यतिक्रान्तो ह्यापगेयोऽल्पदर्शनः॥
en: O sons of Pandu, you are children; you do now know what Dharma is, for it (the ways of Dharma) is very subtle. This son of the river (Bhishma) has but little knowledge, and therefore he has transgressed the Smriti (rules of morality).

sn: त्वादृशो धर्मयुक्तो हि कुर्वाणः प्रियकाम्यया। भवत्यभ्यधिकं भीष्म लोकेष्ववमत: सताम्॥
en: O Bhishma, if a man like you, possessing virtue and morality, acts from motives of pleasing others, he (surely) becomes worthy of censure among all the honest and wise men.

sn: कथं डराजा दाशार्हो मध्ये सर्वमहीक्षिताम्। अर्हणामर्हति तथा यथा युष्माभिरर्चितः॥
en: How does this man of the Dasarha race, who is not a king, deserve to be worshipped among these kings that you have worshipped him?

sn: अथ वा मन्यसे कृष्णं स्थविरं कुरुपुङ्गव। वसुदेवे स्थिते वृद्धे कथमर्हति तत्सुतः॥
en: O foremost man of the Puru race, if you consider him to be the eldest, why, here is Vasudeva. How can his son be worshipped before him?

sn: अथ वा वासुदेवोऽपि प्रियकामोऽनुवृत्तवान्। दुपदे तिष्ठति कथं माधवोऽर्हति पूजनम्॥
en: If you consider him your well-wisher and supporter, why, when Drupada is here, how can he get the (first) worship?

sn: आचार्यं मन्यसे कृष्णमथ वा कुरुनन्दन। द्रोणे तिष्ठति वार्ष्णेयं कस्मादर्चितवानसि॥
en: O descendant of Kuru, if you consider Krishna your preceptor, when Drona is here, how have you worshipped the Vrishni prince?

sn: ऋत्विजं मन्यसे कृष्णमथ या कुरुनन्दन। द्वैपायने स्थिते वृद्धे कथं कृष्णोऽर्चितस्त्वया॥
en: O descendant of Kuru, if you consider Krishna as the Ritvija, when old Dvaipayana is here, how have you worshipped Krishna?

sn: भीष्मे शान्तनवे राजन् स्थिते पुरुषसत्तमे। स्वच्छन्दमृत्युके राजन् कथं कृष्णोऽर्चितस्त्वया॥
en: O king, when that best of men, the son of Shantanu, old Bhishma, who can die only at his will, is here, why have you worshipped Krishna?

sn: अश्वत्थाम्नि स्थिते वीरे सर्वशास्त्रविशारदे। कथं कृष्णस्त्वया राजन्नर्चितः कुरुनन्दन॥
en: O king, O descendant of Kuru, when the hero Ashvathama who is learned in every branch of knowledge is here, why has Krishna been worshipped by you.

sn: दुर्योधने च राजेन्द्रे स्थिते पुरुषसत्तमे। कृपे च भारताचार्ये कथं कृष्णस्त्वयार्चितः॥
en: When that best of men, that king of kings, Duryodhana, and also that preceptor of the Kuru race, Kripa, are present here, why Krishna has been worshipped?

sn: दुमं किम्पुरुषाचार्यमतिक्रम्य तथार्चितः। भीष्मके चैव दुर्धर्षं पाण्डुवत् कृतलक्षणे॥
en: Passing over the preceptor of the Kimpurushas, he (Krishna) has been worshipped by you. When the invincible Bhishmaka, auspicious marked king of Paundrya.

sn: नृपे च रुक्मिणि श्रेष्ठे एकलव्ये तथैव च। शल्ये मद्राधिपे चैव कथं कृष्णस्त्वयार्चितः॥
en: That best of kings, Rukmi, and Ekalavya, and the king of the Madras, Shalya, are present, why Krishna has been worshipped?

sn: अयं च सर्वराज्ञां वै बलश्लाघी महाबलः। जामदग्न्यस्य दयितः शिष्यो विप्रस्य भारत॥ येनात्मबलमाश्रित्य राजानो युधि निर्जिताः। तं च कर्णमतिक्रम्य कथं कृष्णस्त्वयार्चितः॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, this greatly powerful hero whose prowess is the pride amongst all kings, who is the favourite disciple of the son of the Brahmana Jamadagni, the hero who defeated all the kings by his prowess alone, that Karna being present here, passing over him, why Krishna has been worshipped?

sn: नैवविंग् नैव चाचार्यो न राजा मधुसूदनः। अर्चितश्च कुरुश्रेष्ठ किमन्यत्प्रियकाम्यया॥
en: O best of the Kuru race, the slayer of Madhu (Krishna) is neither a sacrificial priest, nor a preceptor, nor a king, why have you worshipped Krishna with the motive of pleasing others?

sn: अथ वाभ्यर्चनीयोऽयं युष्माकं मधुसूदनः। किं राजभिरिहानीवैरवमानाय भारत॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, if it was your intention to offer the first worship to the slayer of Madhu, why were these kings brought here to be insulted?

sn: वयं तु न भयादस्य कौन्तेयस्य महात्मनः। प्रयच्छामः करान्सर्वे न लोभान्न च सान्त्वनात्॥
en: We have not paid tribute to the illustrious son of Kunti out of fear of temptation (the desire of gain) or conciliation:

sn: अस्य धर्मप्रवृत्तस्य पार्थिवत्वं चिकीर्षतः। करानस्मै प्रयच्छामः सोऽयमस्मान् न मन्यते॥
en: We have paid him tribute only because he was desirous of obtaining the imperial dignity from the motive of virtue. He it is who is now insulting us.

sn: किमन्यदवमानाद्वि यदेनं राजसंसदि। अप्राप्तलक्षणं कृष्णमयेणार्चितवानसि॥
en: What else could be your motive, except that of insult, that in the midst of this assembly of kings, you have worshipped Krishna, who does not possess the insignia of royalty, with the Arghya?

sn: अकस्माद् धर्मपुत्रस्य धर्मात्मेति यशो गतम्। को हि धर्मच्युत पूजामेवं युक्तां नियोजयेत्॥
en: The tile of "virtuous" achieved by the son of Dharma (Yudhishthira), has been obtained without any cause. Who will offer such unworthy worship to one who has failed from religion?

sn: योऽयं वृष्णिकुले जातो राजानं हतवान् पुरा। जरासंधं महात्मानमन्यायेन दुरात्मवान्॥
en: This wretch, born in the Vrishni race, formerly most unrighteously killed the illustrious king Jarasandha.

sn: अद्य धर्मात्मता चैव व्यपकृष्टा युधिष्ठिरात्। दर्शितं कृपणत्वं च कृष्णेऽय॑स्य निवेदनात्॥
en: Righteousness has today left Yudhishthira, and his meanness only has been displayed by his offering the Arghya to Krishna.

sn: यदि भीताश्च कौन्तेयाः कृपणाश्च तपस्विनः। ननु त्वयापि बोद्धव्यं यां पूजां माधवार्हसि॥
en: O Janardana, if the helpless sons of Kunti are frightened, and if they have become mean for their asceticism, you ought to have enlightened them as to your claim to the first worship.

sn: अथ वा कृपणैरेतामुपनीतां जनार्दना। पूजामनर्हः कस्मात् त्वमभ्यनुज्ञातवानसि॥
en: O Janardana, why did you accept the worship of which you are not worthy, although it was offered to you by these mean-minded princes?

sn: अयुक्तामात्मनः पूजां त्वं पुनर्बहु मन्यसे। हविषः प्राप्य निष्यन्दं प्राशिता श्वेव निर्जने॥
en: You (surely) think much of the worship so unworthy of freed to you, as a dog (joyfully) licks in solitude a quantity of Ghee which he has obtained.

sn: न त्वयं पार्थिवेन्द्राणामपमानः प्रयुज्यते। त्वामेव कुरवो व्यक्तं प्रलम्भन्ते जनार्दन॥
en: OJanardana, this is no insult to the kings, but it is you whom the Kurus have insulted.

sn: क्लीबे दारक्रिया यादृगन्धे वा रूपदर्शनम्। अराज्ञो राजवत् पूजा तथा ते मधुसूदन॥.
en: O slayer of Madhu, as a wife is to an impotent man and a beautiful sight to a blind man, so is this worship to you who are not a king (at all).

sn: दृष्टो युधिष्ठिरो राजा दृष्टो भीष्मश्च यादृशः। वासुदेवोऽप्ययं दृष्टः सर्वमेतद् यथातथम्॥
en: What (sort of man) Yudhishthira is, it has been (well) seen today; what (sort of man) Bhishma is, it has (also) been seen: what (sort of man) Vasudeva is, it has been also seen. all these men have been seen as they (really) are.

sn: इत्युक्त्वा शिशुपालस्तानुत्थाय परमासनात्। निर्ययौ सदसस्तस्मात् सहितो राजभिस्तदा॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having said this, Shishupala rose from the excellent seat (on which he was seated). He then went out of the assembly accompanied by the kings.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततो युधिष्ठिरो राजा शिशुपालमुपाद्रवत्। उवाच चैनं मधुरं सान्त्वपूर्वमिदं वचः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Thereupon king Yudhishthira ran after Shishupala and spoke thus to him in sweet and conciliating tone.

sn: नेदं युक्तं महीपाल यादृशं वै त्वमुक्तवान्। अधर्मश्च परो राजन् पारुष्यं च निरर्थकम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said O lord of the earth, what you have said does not suit you, O king, it is highly sinful and needlessly cruel.

sn: न हि धर्मं परं जातु नावबुध्येत पार्थिवः। भीष्मः शान्तनवस्त्वेनं मावमंस्थास्त्वमन्यथा॥
en: O king, do not insult the son of Shantanu, Bhishma, by erroneously thinking that he does not know what is the great Dharma.

sn: पश्य चैतान् महीपालांस्त्वत्तो वृद्धतरान् बहून्। मृष्यन्ते चार्हणां कृष्णे तद्वत् त्वं क्षन्तुमर्हसि॥
en: Look, these many kings, who are all older than you, approve the worship offered to Krishna. You should also approve it.

sn: वेद तत्त्वेन कृष्णं हि भीष्मश्चेदिपते भृशम्। न ह्येनं त्वं तथा वेत्थ यथैनं वेद कौरवः॥
en: O king of Chedi, the descendant of Kuru, Bhishma, knows truly and well what Krishna is. You do not know him so well as he knows.

sn: भीष्म उवाच नास्मै देयो ह्यनुनयो नायमर्हति सान्त्वनम्। लोकवृद्धतमे कृष्णे योऽर्हणां नाभिमन्यते॥
en: Bhishma said He, who does not approve of the worship offered to Krishna, who is the oldest in the universe, deserves neither soft words nor conciliation.

sn: क्षत्रियः क्षत्रियं जित्वा रणे रणकृतां वरः। यो मुञ्चति वशे कृत्वा गुरुर्भवति तस्य सः॥
en: That chief of warriors in the Kshatriya race, who, having overcome a Kshatriya in battle and brought him under his power, sets him free, becomes his preceptor.

sn: अस्यां हि समितौ राज्ञामेकमप्यजितं युधि। न पश्यामि महीपालं सात्वतीपुत्रतेजसा॥
en: I do not see any king in this assembly of monarchs who has not been defeated by the prowess of this descendant of Satvata race (Krishna).

sn: न हि केवलमस्माकमयमर्च्यतमोऽच्युतः। त्रयाणामपि लोकानामर्चनीयो महाभुजः॥
en: This mighty-armed hero of unfading glory deserve to be worshipped not only by us alone, but by all the three worlds.

sn: कृष्णेन हि जिता युद्धे बहवः क्षत्रियर्षभाः। जगत् सर्वं च वार्ष्णेय निखिलेन प्रतिष्ठितम्॥
en: Many best of Kshatriyas have been defeated by Krishna in battle. The infinite universe is established in this Vrishni hero.

sn: तस्मात् सत्स्वपि वृद्धेषु कृष्णमर्चाम नेतरान्। एवं वक्तुं न चार्हस्त्वं मा ते भूद् बुद्धिरीदृशी॥
en: Therefore, we worship Krishna. Amongst the best and the oldest, we do not worship any other. you should not say so, your understanding should not be so.

sn: ज्ञानवृद्धा मया राजन् बहवः पर्युपासिताः। तेषां कथयतां शौरेरहं गुणवतो गुणान्॥ समागतानामश्रौषं बहून् बहुमतान् सताम्। कर्माण्यपि च यान्यस्य जन्मप्रभृति धीमतः॥ बहुशः कथ्यमानानि नरैर्भूयः श्रुतानि मे। न केवलं वयं कामाच्चेदिराज जनार्दनम्॥
en: O king, I have worshipped many men who are old in knowledge. I have heard from all those wise men when they came and talked to me what are the many accomplishments of Shauri (Krishna). I have heard many times narrated by the people all the acts which greatly intelligent Krishna performed since his birth. O king of Chedi, we do not worship Janardana only from caprice,

sn: न सम्बन्धं पुरस्कृत्य कृतार्थं वा कथंचन। अर्चामहेऽर्चितं सद्भिर्भुवि भूतसुखावहम्॥
en: Or from keeping in view our relationship with him, or from expected benefits (to be received from him). He is worshipped by all the pious men on earth, and he is the source of all happiness.

sn: यशः शौर्यं जयं चास्य विज्ञायार्चा प्रयुञ्जमहे। न च कश्चिदिहास्माभिः सुबालोऽप्यपरीक्षितः॥
en: We have offered him the first worship in consideration of his fame, his heroism and his success. There is none here, even if he is a child, whom we have not taken into our consideration (when offering the Arghya to Krishna).

sn: गुणवृद्धानतिक्रम्य हरिरर्च्यतमो मतः। ज्ञानवृद्धो द्विजातीनां क्षत्रियाणां बलाधिकः॥
en: Passing over many persons who are accomplished and learned, we have thought Hari as deserving of the first worship. Amongst Brahmanas he, who is old in knowledge, amongst Kshairiyas he, who is great in strength.

sn: वैश्यानां धान्यधनवाञ्छूद्राणामेव जन्मतः। पूज्यतायां च गोविन्दे हेतू द्वावपि संस्थितौ॥
en: Amongst Vaishyas, he, who is rich in possessions and wealth; and amongst the Shudras he, who is old in age, deserves to be worshipped. There are two reasons for offering the worship to Govinda (Krishna).

sn: वेदवेदाङ्गविज्ञानं बलं चाभ्यधिकं तथा। नृणां लोके हि कोऽन्योऽस्ति विशिष्टः केशवादृते॥
en: He is vastly learned in the Vedas and the Vedangas, and he is also very great in prowess. Who else is there in the world of men except Keshava (Krishna) who is so distinguished?

sn: दानं दाक्ष्यं श्रुतं शौर्यं ह्रीः कीर्तिर्बुद्धिरुत्तमा। सन्नतिः श्रीकृतिस्तुष्टिः पुष्टिश्च नियताच्युते॥
en: Liberality, cleverness, knowledge of the Shruti (Veda), bravery, modesty, achievements, excellent intelligence, humility, beauty, firmness, contentment and prosperity, all live for ever in Achyuta (Krishna).

sn: तमिमं गुणसम्पन्नमार्यं च पितरं गुरुम्। अर्घ्यमर्चितमर्चाहँ सर्वे संक्षन्तुमर्हथ॥
en: Therefore, you should approve the worship offered to one who is endued with such accomplishments, who is (our) preceptor, father, and Guru, and who is worthy of the Arghya and of the worship.

sn: ऋत्विग् गुरुस्तथाऽऽचार्यः स्नातको नृपतिः प्रियः। सर्वमेतद्धृषीकेशस्तस्मादभ्यर्चितोऽच्युतः॥
en: Hrishikesha (Krishna) is the Ritvija, preceptor, worthy of being solicited to marry one's daughter, the Snataka, the king and the friend. Therefore, Achyuta (Krishna) has been worshipped.

sn: कृष्ण एव हि लोकानामुत्पत्तिरपि चाप्ययः। कृष्णस्य हि कृते विश्वमिदं भूतं चराचरम्॥
en: Krishna is the origin of the universe, and he is that in which the universe is to dissolve. This universe of mobile and immobile creatures has sprung into existence from Krishna alone.

sn: एष प्रकृतिरव्यक्ता कर्ता चैव सनातनः। परश्च सर्वभूतेभ्यस्तस्मात् पूज्यतमोऽच्युतः॥
en: He is unmanifest primal nature, he is the creator, he is eternal, and he is beyond all creatures. Therefore, Achyuta deserves the highest worship.

sn: बुद्धिर्मनो महद् वायुस्तेजोऽम्भः खं मही च या। चतुर्विधं च यद् भूतं सर्वं कृष्णे प्रतिष्ठितम्॥
en: The intellect, the seat of sensibility, the primal elements, air, heat, water, space, earth and the four kings of life, are all established in Krishna.

sn: आदित्यश्चन्द्रमाश्चैव नक्षत्राणि ग्रहाश्च ये। दिशश्च विदिशश्चैव सर्वं कृष्णे प्रतिष्ठितम्॥
en: The sun, the moon, the stars, the planets, the chief directions and the intermediate directions are all established in Krishna.

sn: अग्निहोत्रमुखा वेदा गायत्री छन्दसां मुखम्। राजा मुखं मनुष्याणां नदीनां सागरो मुखम्॥ नक्षत्राणां मुखं चन्द्र आदित्यस्तेजसां मुखम्। पर्वतानां मुखं मेरुर्गरुडः पततां मुखम्॥
en: As the Agnihotra is the foremost of all Vedic rites, as Gayatri is that of the metres, as the king is that of men as the ocean is that of all rivers, as the moon is the foremost of all constellations, as the sun is that of luminous bodies, as the Meru is that of all mountains, as Garuda is that of all birds.

sn: ऊर्ध्वं तिर्यगधश्चैव यावती जगतो गतिः। सदेवकेषु लोकेषु भगवान् केशवो मुखम्॥
en: So is the illustrious Keshava, (Krishna) the foremost in all the worlds including that of the celestials, so he is as long as the upward, downward and sideways course of the universe lasts.

sn: अयं तु पुरुषो बालः शिशुपालो न बुध्यते। सर्वत्र सर्वदा कृष्णं तस्मादेवं प्रभाषते॥
en: This Shishupala is a mere child. He does not know who Krishna is, and therefore every where and always he speaks of Krishna thus.

sn: यो हि धर्मं विचिनुयादुत्कृष्टं मतिमन् नरः। स वै पश्येद् यथा धर्मं न तथा चेदिराडयम्॥
en: This ruler of Chedi cannot see virtue in that light in which those intelligent men who desire to acquire high merits sees it.

sn: सवृद्धबालेष्वथवा पार्थिवेषु महात्मसु। को नाईं मन्यते कृष्णं को वाप्येनं न पूजयेत्॥
en: Who is there among the young or the old or among these illustrious kings who does not consider Krishna worthy of worship, or who does not worship Krishna?

sn: अथैनां दुष्कृतां पूजां शिशुपालो व्यवस्यति। दुष्कृतायां यथान्यायं तथायं कर्तुमर्हति॥
en: If Shishupala considers this worship undeserved, in this undeserved worship he should do that which is proper in this matter

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्त्वा ततो भीष्मो विरराम् महाबलः। व्याजहारोत्तरं तत्र सहदेवोऽर्थवद् वचः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having said this, the greatly strong Bhishma stopped. Then Sahadeva gave this reply(to Shishupala) of grave import.

sn: केशवं केशिहन्तारमप्रमेयपराक्रमम्। पूज्यमानं मया यो वः कृष्णं न सहते नृपाः॥
en: "If there is any king(present here) who cannot bear the worship offered by me to Keshava, the slayer of Keshi, and the possessor of immeasurable energy.

sn: सर्वेषां बलिनां मूर्ध्नि भयेदं निहितं पदम्। एवमुक्ते मया सम्यगुत्तरं प्रब्रवीतु सः॥
