en: On the head of such heroes I place my foot. When I say this, let that one give me the proper reply.

sn: स एव हि मया वध्यो भविष्यति न संशयः। मतिमन्थश्च ये केचिदाचार्यं पितरं गुरुम्॥ अर्घ्यमर्चितम_हमनुजानन्तु ते नृपाः। ततो न व्याजहारैषां कश्चिद् बुद्धिमतां सताम्॥ मानिनां बलिनां राज्ञां मध्ये वै दर्शिते पदे। ततोऽपतत् पुष्पवृष्टिः सहदेवस्य मूर्धनि॥
en: Let those kings who possess intelligence approve the worship of the preceptor, the father, and the Guru (Krishna) who (fully) deserves the Arghya and the worship.” When Sahadeva thus showed his foot, no one among those intelligent, wise, proud and powerful kings said anything. Thereupon, showers of flowers fell upon the head of Sahadeva.

sn: अदृश्यरूपा वचाश्चाप्यब्रुवन् साधु साध्विति। आविध्यदजितं कृष्णं भविष्यद्भूतजल्पकः॥
en: An invisible voice said, “Excellent, Excellent!" Clad in a black deer skin, the speaker of both the past and the future,

sn: सर्वसंशयनिर्मोक्ता नारदः सर्वलोकवित्। उवाचाखिलभूतानां मध्ये स्पष्टतरं वचः॥
en: The dispeller of all doubts, Narada learned in(the mysteries) of all the world, then said in the midst of innumerable creatures these words of the clearest import.

sn: कृष्णं कमलपत्राक्षं नार्चयिष्यन्ति ये नराः। जीवन्मृतास्तु ते ज्ञेया न सम्भाष्याः कदाचन॥
en: Those men, who will not worship the lotus-eyed Krishna, should be considered as dead though living. He should never be talked to."

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच पूजयित्वा च पूजार्हान् ब्रह्मक्षत्रविशेषवित्। सहदेवो नृणां देवः समापद्यत कर्म तत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having worshipped those that deserved worship, then that god among men, Sahadeva, well-acquainted with the difference between a Brahmana and a Kshatriya competed the ceremony.

sn: तस्मिन्नभ्यर्चिते कृष्णे सुनीथः शत्रुकर्षणः। अतिताप्रेक्षणः कोपादुवाच मनुजाधिपान्॥
en: When Krishna received the first worship, that slayer of foes, Sunitha (Shishupala), with eyes red as copper in anger, thus addressed the kings (present there).

sn: स्थित: सेनापतिर्योऽहं मन्यध्वं किं तु साम्प्रतम्। युधि तिष्ठाम संना समेतान् वृष्णिपाण्डवान्॥
en: “When I am here to be the generalissimo, what are you thinking now? In battle array let us stand against the assembled Vrishnis and the Pandavas".

sn: इति सर्वान् समुत्साह्य राज्ञस्तांश्चेदिपुङ्गवः। यज्ञोपघाताय ततः सोऽमन्त्रयत राजभिः॥
en: Having thus stirred up the kings, that best of the Chedis (Shishupala) began to consult with them how to obstruct the completion of the sacrifice.

sn: तत्राहूता गताः सर्वे सुनीथप्रमुखा गणाः। समदृश्यन्त संक्रुद्धा विवर्णवदनास्तथा॥
en: The invited kings, who had come to the sacrifice, all with Sunitha (Shishupala) at their head, looked angry, and their face became pale.

sn: युधिष्ठिराभिषेकं च वासुदेवस्य चाहणम्। न स्याद् यथा तथा कार्यमेवं सर्वे तदाब्रुवन्॥
en: They all said, “We must act in such a way as the final sacrificial rites to be performed by Yudhishthira and this worship of Krishna may not be supposed to have our acquiescence”.

sn: निष्कर्षानिश्चयात् सर्वे राजानः क्रोधमूर्छिताः। अब्रुवंस्तत्र राजानो निर्वेदादात्मनिश्चयात्॥
en: Having been impelled by a belief in their great power and confidence, and having been also deprived of all sense by anger, all the kings began to talk in this way.

sn: सुहृद्भिर्वार्यमाणानां तेषां हि वपुराबभौ। आमिषादपकृष्टानां सिंहानामिव गर्जताम्॥
en: Though they were appeased by their friends, their faces glowed with anger, and they roared like lions driven away from their prey.

sn: तं बलौघमपर्यन्तं राजसागरमक्षयम्। कुर्वाणं समयं कृष्णो युद्धाय बुबुधे तदा॥
en: Krishna understood that the undeteriorating great sea of kings with its countless waves of soldiers was making preparation for a fight.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततः सागरसंकाशं दृष्ट्वा नृपतिमण्डलम्। संवर्तवाताभिहतं भीमं क्षुब्धमिवार्णवम्॥ रोषात् प्रचलितं सर्वमिदमाह युधिष्ठिरः। भीष्मं मतिमतां मुख्यं वृद्धं कुरुपितामहम्। बृहस्पतिं बृहत्तेजाः पुरुहूत इवारिहा॥ असौ रोषात् प्रचलितो महान् नृपतिसागरः। अत्र यत् प्रतिपत्तव्यं तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह॥
en: Vaishampayana said Seeing that assembly of kings agitated by anger, as the fearful ocean is agitated by the winds at the time of the universal dissolution, Yudhishthira thus spoke to that foremost of all intelligent men, the grandsire of the Kurus, the aged Bhishma, as that slayer of foes, Purohita (Indra) of extraordinary prowess, speaks to Brihaspati. “This.vast ocean of kings have been agitated by wrath. O grandsire, tell me what should be done now.

sn: यज्ञस्य च न विघ्नः स्यात् प्रजानां च हितं भवेत्। यथा सर्वत्र तत् सर्वं ब्रूहि मेऽद्य पितामह॥
en: O grandsire, tell me what I should do now that my sacrifice may not be obstructed and my subjects may not be injured”.

sn: इत्युक्तवति धर्मज्ञे धर्मराजे युधिष्ठिरे। उवाचेदं वचो भीष्मस्ततः कुरुपितामहः॥
en: When Dharmaraja Yudhishthira, learned in morality, said this, the grandsire of the Kurus Bhishma thus spoke to him.

sn: मा भैस्त्वं कुरुशार्दूल श्वा सिंहं हन्तुमर्हति। शिवः पन्थाः सुनीतोऽत्र मया पूर्वतरं वृतः॥
en: "O best of the Kurus, do not be alarmed. can the dog kill the lion? I have already settled some means that is both beneficial and conformable to policy.

sn: प्रसुप्ते हि यथा सिंहे श्वानस्तस्मिन् समागताः। भषेयुः सहिताः सर्वे तथेमे वसुधाधिपाः॥
en: As a pack of dogs bark all together at a sleeping lion, so do all these rulers of the earth.

sn: वृष्णिसिंहस्य सुप्तस्य तथामी प्रमुखे स्थिताः। भषन्ते तात संक्रुद्धाः श्वान: सिंहस्य संनिधौ॥
en: O child, like the dogs at the lion, these (kings) are angrily barking before the sleeping lion of the Vrishni race (Krishna).

sn: न हि सम्बुध्यते यावत् सुप्तः सिंह इवाच्युतः। तेन सिंहीकरोत्येतान् नृसिंहश्चेदिपुङ्गवः॥
en: Achyuta (Krishna) is now like a lion that is asleep. So long he does not wake up this king of the Chedis, this foremost of men, makes these monarchs look like the lions.

sn: पार्थिवान् पार्थिवश्रेष्ठः शिशुपालोऽप्यचेतनः। सर्वान् सर्वात्मना तात नेतुकामो यमक्षयम्॥
en: O best of kings, O child, this Shishupala possesses but little intelligence. He is desirous of taking along (with him) all these monarchs to the abode of Yama through the agency of him who is the soul of this universe.

sn: नूनमेतत् समादातुं पुनरिच्छत्यधोक्षजः। यदस्य शिशुपालस्य तेजस्तिष्ठति भारत॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, Krishna has been surely desirous of taking back to himself the effulgence and prowess that now lives in Shishupala.

sn: विप्लुता चास्य भद्रं ते बुद्धिर्बुद्धमतां वर। चेदिराजस्य कौन्तेय सर्वेषां च महीक्षिताम्॥
en: O son of Kunti, O foremost of all intelligent men, the intelligence of this wicked king of the Chedis, as well as that of all these kings, have become perverse.

sn: आदातुं च नरव्याघ्रो यं यमिच्छत्ययं तदा। तस्य विप्लवते बुद्धिरेवं चेदिपतेर्यथा॥
en: The intelligence of all men whom this best of men (Krishna) desires to take to himself become as perverse as that of this Chedi king.

sn: चतुर्विधानां भूतानां त्रिषु लोकेषु माधवः। प्रभवश्चैव सर्वेषां निधनं च युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: O Yudhishthira, Madhava is the creator and destroyer of all the four kinds of beings existing in the three worlds.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच इति तस्य वचः श्रुत्वा ततश्चेदिपतिनृपः। भीष्मं रुक्षाक्षरा वाचः श्रावयामास भारत॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, having heard his words, the king of the Chedis spoke thus to Bhishma in stem and harsh words.

sn: शिशुपाल उवाच विभीषिकाभिर्बह्वीभिर्भीषयन् सर्वपार्थिवान्। न व्यपत्रपसे कस्माद् वृद्धः सन् कुलपांसन॥
en: Shishupala said Old and infamous wretch of your race, are you not ashamed to frighten all these kings by these false terrors?

sn: युक्तमेतत् तृतीयायां प्रकृतौ वर्तता त्वया। वक्तुं धर्मादपेतार्थं त्वं हि सर्वकुरूत्तमः॥
en: You are the foremost of the Purus-living as you do in the third state (celibacy), it is but fit that you should give such advice, which is so void of morality.

sn: नावि नौरिव सम्बद्धा यथान्धो वान्धमन्वियात्। तथाभूता हि कौरव्या येषां भीष्म त्वमग्रणीः॥
en: O Bhishma, when you are their leader the Purus are like a boat tied to a boat, or like a blind man following a blind man.

sn: पूतनाघातपूर्वाणि कर्माण्यस्य विशेषतः। त्वया कीर्तयतास्माकं भूयः प्रव्यथितं मनः॥
en: You have once again given pains to our hearts by reciting the deeds of this (Krishna), such as his killing Putana and others.

sn: अवलिप्तस्य मूर्खस्य केशवं स्तोतुमिच्छतः। कथं भीष्म न ते जिह्वा शतधेयं विदीर्यते॥
en: O Bhishma, arrogant and fool as you are, and also desirous of praising Krishna, why does not your tongue split into a hundred parts?

sn: यत्र कुत्सा प्रयोक्तव्या भीष्म बालतरैनरैः। तमिमं ज्ञानवृद्धः सन् गोपं संस्तोतुमिच्छसि॥
en: O Bhishma, how do you, superior as you are in knowledge, desire to praise the cowherd (Krishna) whose evil repute is told even by men with childish intelligence,

sn: यद्यनेन हतो बाल्ये शकुनिश्चित्रमत्र किम्। तौ वाश्ववृषभौ भीष्म यौ न युद्धविशारदौ॥
en: O Bhishma, if he (Krishna) has killed a vulture in his childhood, what is there to praise in that feat? What is there also in his killing of Ashva and Vrishabha, both of whom were ignorant of the science of war?

sn: चेतनारहितं काष्ठं यद्यनेन निपातितम्। पादेन शकटं भीष्म तत्र किं कृतमद्भुतम्॥
en: O Bhishma, what is there wonderful if this (Krishna) threw down by a kick an inanimate piece of wood, namely a car?

sn: वल्मीकमात्रः सप्ताहं यद्यनेन धृतोऽचलः। तदा गोवर्धनो भीष्म न तच्चित्रं मतं मम॥
en: O Bhishma, in my opinion there was nothing remarkable in this one's holding for a week the Govardhana hill which is like an anthill.

sn: भुक्तमेतेन बह्वन्नं क्रीडता नगमूर्धनि। इति ते भीष्म शृण्वानाः परे विस्मयमागताः॥
en: O Bhishma, "while sporting on the hills, this one ate a large quantity of food,” hearing these words of yours, many have been much astonished.

sn: यस्य चानेन धर्मज्ञ भुक्तमन्नं बलीयसः। स चानेन हतः कंस इत्येतन्न महाद्भुतम्॥
en: O (Bhishma) learned in the precepts of religion, what could be more wonderful than this one's killing Kansa, by whose food he became fattened and strong.

sn: न ते श्रुतमिदं भीष्म नूनं कथयतां सताम्। यद् वक्ष्ये त्वामधर्मज्ञं वाक्यं कुरुकुलाधम॥
en: O Bhishma, O wretch of the Puru race, you are ignorant of the precepts of religion. You have not heard from the pious men what I would now tell you.

sn: स्त्रीषु गोषु न शस्त्राणि पातयेद् ब्राह्मणेषु च। यस्य चान्नानि भुञ्जीत यत्र च स्यात् प्रतिश्रयः॥ इति सन्तोऽनुशासन्ति सज्जनं धर्मिणः सदा। भीष्म लोके हि तत् सर्वं वितथं त्वयि दृश्यते॥
en: The pious men always instruct good men not to use weapons against women, kine, Brahmanas and the men whose food has been partaken, and also those whose shelter has been enjoyed. O Bhishma, it appears all this teaching has been thrown away on you.

sn: ज्ञानवृद्धं च वृद्धं च भूयांसं केशवं मम। अजानत इवाख्यासि संस्तुवन् कौरवाधम॥
en: Owretch of the Kuru race, wishing to praise Keshava (Krishna), you describe him before me as great and superior in knowledge and age, as if I know nothing.

sn: गोनः स्त्रीनश्च सन् भीष्म त्वद्वाक्याद् यदि पूज्यते। एवंभूतश्च यो भीष्म कथं संस्तवमर्हति॥
en: O Bhishma, if at your word one who has killed women and kine be worshipped, what then is to become of this teaching? O Bhishma, how can he deserve praise who is such?

sn: असौ मतिमतां श्रेष्ठो य एथ जगतः प्रभुः। सम्भावयति चाप्येवं त्वद्वाक्याच्च जनार्दनः। एवमेतत् सर्वमिति तत् सर्वं वितथं ध्रुवम्॥
en: "This one is the foremost of all wise men," and "This one is the lord of the universe," hearing these words of yours, Janardana (Krishna) believes that they are all true. But they are surely all false.

sn: न गाथागाथिनं शास्ति बहु चेदपि गायति। प्रकृति यान्ति भूतानि भूलिङ्गशकुनिर्यथा॥
en: The verses that a chaunter chaunts, though he chants them often, would produce no impression on him. every creature acts according to his own disposition like the bird Bhulinga.

sn: नूनं प्रकृतिरेषा ते जघन्या नात्र संशयः। अति पापीयसी चैषा पाण्डवानामपीष्यते॥ येषामर्थ्यतमः कृष्णस्त्वं च येषां प्रदर्शकः। धर्मवांस्त्वमधर्मज्ञः सतां मार्गादवप्लुतः॥
en: There is not the least doubt that your disposition is very mean. It appears the Pandavas also who consider Krishna as deserving of worship and who have you for their leader are of sinful dispositions. Though you possess the knowledge of virtue, yet you have fallen from the path of virtue.

sn: को हि धर्मिणमात्मानं जानज्ञानविदां वरः। कुर्याद् यथा त्वया भीष्म कृतं धर्ममवेक्षता॥
en: O Bhishma, who will so act as you have from the motives of virtue, knowing himself to be virtuous and superior in knowledge?

sn: चेत् त्वं धर्मं विजानासि यदि प्राज्ञा मतिस्तव। अन्यकामा हि धर्मज्ञा कन्यका प्राज्ञमानिना। अम्बा नामेति भद्रं ते कथं सापहृता त्वया॥ तां त्वयापि हृतां भीष्म कन्यां नैषितवान् यतः। भ्राता विचित्रवीर्यस्ते सतां मार्गमनुष्ठितः॥
en: O Bhishma, if you know Dharına, if your mind is guided by wisdom, why was that virtuous maiden Amba, who desired to have another for her husband, was forcibly carried away by you? Your brother Vichitravirya who followed the path of the pious men,

sn: दारयोर्यस्य चान्येन मिषतः प्राज्ञमानिनः। तव जातान्यपत्यानि सज्जनाचरिते पथि।॥
en: Knowing her state of mind, did not marry her, though she was brought by you. Proud as you are of your virtue, in your very sight sons were begotten by another on the widow of your brother according to the ways of the pious.

sn: को हि धर्मोऽस्ति ते भीष्म ब्रह्मचर्यमिदं वृथा। यद् धारयसि मोहाद् वा क्लीबत्वाद् वा न संशयः।।
en: O Bhishma, where is your virtue? your Brahmacharya is in vain. Your celibacy is no doubt the result of your ignorance or impotence.

sn: न त्वहं तव धर्मज्ञ पश्याम्युपचयं क्वचित्। न हि ते सेविता वृद्धा य एवं धर्ममब्रवीः॥
en: O (Bhishma), learned in Dharma, I do not see your prosperity. You who thus preach moralịty does not seem to have ever waited upon the old.

sn: इष्टं दत्तमधीतं च यज्ञाश्च बहुदक्षिणाः। सर्वमेतदपत्यस्य कलां नार्हन्ति षोडशीम्॥
en: Worship, gift, study, large-Dakshina giving sacrifices, these all are not equal to sixteenth part of that merit which is obtained by the possession of a son.

sn: व्रतोपवासैर्बहुभिः कृतं भवति भीष्म यत्। सर्वं तदनपत्यस्य मोघं भवति निश्चयात्॥
en: O Bhishma, the merit that is obtained by observing many vows and fasts surely goes all in vain if one is childless.

sn: सोऽनपत्यश्च वृद्धश्च मिथ्याधर्मानुसारकः। हंसवत् त्वमपीदानीं ज्ञातिभ्यः प्राप्नुया वधम्॥
en: You are childless, you are old, you are an expounder of false morality. Like the swan in ne the story, you shall now be killed by your own relatives.

sn: एवं हि कथयन्त्यन्ये नरा ज्ञानविदः पुरा। भीष्म यत् तदहं सम्यग् वक्ष्यामि तव शृण्वतः॥
en: O Bhishma, the learned men have said this (story) of old. I shall presently narrate it in full in your hearing.

sn: वृद्धः किल समुद्रान्ते कश्चिद्वंसोऽभवत् पुरा। धर्मवागन्यथावृत्तः पक्षिणः सोऽनुशास्ति च॥
en: In the days of yore there lived an old swan on the coast of the sea. He always spoke of morality and used to instruct all the birds, but his conduct was otherwise.

sn: धर्मं चरत माधर्ममिति तस्य वचः किल। पक्षिणः शुश्रुवुर्भीष्म सततं सत्यवादिनः॥
en: O Bhishma, “Practice virtue and forego sin", these were the words that the truthful (birds) heard him say.

sn: अथास्य भक्ष्यमाजहः समुद्रजलचारिणः। अण्डजा भीष्म तस्मान्ये धर्मार्थमिति शुश्रुम॥
en: O Bhishma, it has been heard by us that oviparous creatures, (all) dwelling in the sea, brought him food for the sake of virtue.

sn: ते च तस्य समभ्याशे निक्षिप्याण्डानि सर्वशः। समुद्राम्भस्यमज्जन्त चरन्तो भीष्म पक्षिणः। तेषामण्डानि सर्वेषां भक्षयामास पापकृत्॥
en: O Bhishma, all those birds left their eggs with him, ranged and dived in the waters of the sea. But that sinful wretch ate them (eggs) all.

sn: स हंसः सम्प्रमत्तानामप्रमत्तः स्वकर्मणि। ततः प्रक्षीयमाणेषु तेषु तेष्वण्डजोऽपरः। अशङ्कत महाप्राज्ञः स कदाचिद् ददर्श ह॥
en: That swan, always attentive to his own purpose, ate the eggs foolishly trusted to him, Some time after seeing the eggs decreased in number, another greatly intelligent bird suspected him, and one day he saw him (eat those eggs).

sn: ततः स कथयामास दृष्ट्वा हंसस्य किल्बिषम्। तेषां परमदुःखार्तः स पक्षी सर्वपक्षिणाम्॥
en: Having witnessed the sinful act of the swan, that bird spoke of it to all the other birds in great sorrow.

sn: ततः प्रत्यक्षतो दृष्ट्वा पक्षिणस्ते समीपगाः। निजघ्नुस्तं तदा हंसं मिथ्यावृत्तं कुरूद्वह॥
en: O excellent Puru, then all those birds, witnessing with their own eyes the act of the (old), swan, came to him, and they then killed that wretch of false conduct.

sn: ते त्वां हंससधर्माणमपीमे वसुधाधिपाः। निहन्युर्भीष्म संक्रुद्धाः पक्षिणस्तं यथाण्डजम्॥
en: O Bhishma, your conduct is like that of the old swan. These kings might kill you in anger as the birds killed the old swan.

sn: गाथामप्यत्र गायन्ति ये पुराणविदो जनाः। भीष्म यां तां च ते सम्यक् कथयिष्यामि भारत॥३९।
en: 0. Bhishma, the Purana-knowing men mention a proverb as regard this occurrence. O descendant of Bharata, I shall repeat it to you in detail.

sn: अन्तरात्मन्यभिहते रौषि पत्ररथाशुचि। अण्डभक्षणकर्मैतत् तव वाचमतीयते॥
en: It is this “O bird, though your heart is affected, yet you preach. But your this sinful act of eating the eggs transgresses of your speeches".

sn: शिशुपाल उवाच स मे बहुमतो राजा जरासंधो महाबलः। योऽनेन युद्धं नेयेष दासोऽयमिति संयुगे॥
en: Shishupala said The greatly powerful king Jarasandha, who did not desire to fight with Krishna, saying that he was but a “servant”, was (surely) worthy of my greatest esteem.

sn: केशवेन कृतं कर्म जरासंधवधे तदा। भीमसेनार्जुनाभ्यां च कस्तत् साध्विति मन्यते॥
en: Who will consider praiseworthy the act of killing Jarasandha which was done by Keshava (Krishna), as also by Bhima and Arjuna?

sn: अद्वारेण प्रविष्टेन छद्मना ब्रह्मवादिना। दृष्टः प्रभावः कृष्णेन जरासंधस्य भूपतेः॥
en: Entering (the city) by a way which was not the (public) gate, and disguised as a Vedaknowing (Brahmana), this Krishna saw the prowess of king Jarasandha.

sn: येन धर्मात्मनाऽऽत्मानं ब्रह्मण्यमविजानता। नेषितं पाद्यमस्मै तद् दातुमग्रे दुरात्मने।॥
en: When that illustrious king offered this wretch water to wash his feet, it was then he said from seeming motives of virtue that he was not a Brahmana.

sn: भुज्यतामिति तेनोक्ताः कृष्णभीमधनंजयाः। जरासंधेन कौरव्य कृष्णेन विकृतं कृतम्॥
en: O descendant of Kuru, when Bhima, Dhananjaya and Krishna were asked by Jarasandha to eat, that request was refused by this Krishna.

sn: यद्ययं जगतः कर्ता यथैनं मूर्ख मन्यसे। कस्मान्न ब्राह्मणं सम्यगात्मानमवगच्छति॥
en: If this one (Krishna) is the lord of the universe, as this fool thinks himself to be, why does he not then consider himself a Brahmana?

sn: इदं त्वाश्चर्यभूतं मे यदिमे पाण्डवास्त्वया। अपकृष्टाः सतां मार्गान्प्रन्यन्ते तच्च साध्विति॥
en: It is greatly surprising that though you often lead the Pandavas away from the path of the pious, yet they consider you (Bhima) to be honest.

sn: अथ वा नैतदाश्चर्यं येषां त्वमसि भारत। स्त्रीसधर्मा च वृद्धश्च सर्वार्थानां प्रदर्शकः॥
en: Odescendant of Bharata (Bhishma), there is nothing to be surprising (perhaps) in those who have got you, who is no better than a woman and who is old, to be their counsellor in all things.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा रूक्षं रूक्षाक्षरं बहु। चुकोप बलिनां श्रेष्ठो भीमसेनः प्रतापवान्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Hearing his these harsh words-harsh both in import and sound, that foremost of all strong men, the powerful Bhimasena, became angry.

sn: तथा पद्मप्रतीकाशे स्वभावायतविस्तृते। क्रोधाभिताम्राक्षे रक्ते नेत्रे बभूवतुः॥
en: Under the influence of anger, his lotus-like eyes, naturally large and expanding, became still more extended, and also as red as the copper.

sn: त्रिशिखां भृकुटीं चास्य ददृशुः सर्वपार्थिवाः। भूयः ललाटस्थां त्रिकूटस्थां गङ्गां त्रिपथगामिव॥
en: The assembled kings saw on his forehead three lines of wrinkles like the Ganges with her three currents on the three peaked mountain.

sn: दन्तान् संदशतस्तस्य कोपाद् ददृशुराननम्। युगान्ते सर्वभूतानि कालस्येव जिघत्सतः॥
en: When he began to grind his teeth in anger, the kings saw his face resemble like that of the Death preparing to swallow every creature at the end of the Yuga.

sn: उत्पतन्तं तु वेगेन जग्राहैनं मनस्विनम्। भीष्म एव महाबाहुर्महासेनमिवेश्वरः॥
en: As the strong-minded (hero) was about to jump up with great impetuosity, the mighty armed Bhishma caught him (by the hand), as if Mahadeva seized Mahasena.

sn: तस्य भीमस्य भीष्मेण वार्यमाणस्य भारत। गुरुणा विविधैर्वाक्यैः क्रोधः प्रशममागतः॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, Bhima's anger was soon appeased by Bhishma with various words of sound counsels.

sn: नातिचक्राम भीष्मस्य स हि वाक्यमरिंदमः। समुवृत्तो घनापाये वेलामिव महोदधिः॥
en: That chastiser of foes could not disobey Bhishma's words, as the ocean never goes beyond its shore, though swollen with the waters of the rainy season.

sn: शिशुपालस्तु संक्रुद्धे भीमसेने जनाधिप। नाकम्पत तदा वीरः पौरुषे स्वे व्यवस्थितः॥
en: O king, though Bhima was angry, the heroic Shishupala, depending on his own valour, did not tremble in fear.

sn: उत्पतन्तं तु वेगेन पुन: पुनररिंदमः। न स तं चिन्तयामास सिंहः क्रुद्धो मृगं यथा।॥
en: Though Bhima every moment jumping up (from his seat) with great impetuosity, yet Shishupala did not bestow a single thought on him, as a lion does not mind a small animal who leaps up in rage.

sn: प्रहसंश्चाब्रवीद् वाक्यं चेदिराजः प्रतापवान्। भीमसेनमभिक्रुद्धं दृष्ट्वा भीमपराक्रमम्॥
en: Seeing Bhima of terrible prowess in such great rage, the mighty kings of Chedi laughingly spoke thus. was

sn: मुञ्चैनं भीष्म पश्यन्तु यावदेनं नराधिपाः। मत्प्रभावविनिर्दग्धं पतङ्गमिव वह्निना॥
en: "O Bhishma, release his. Let all these kings see him burnt down by my prowess like an insect by fire".

sn: ततश्चेदिपतेर्वाक्यं श्रुत्वा तत् कुरुसत्तमः। भीमसेनमुवाचेदं भीष्मो मतिमतां वरः॥
en: Having heard these words of the king of the Chedis, that foremost of the Kurus, that best of all intelligent men, Bhishma thus spoke to Bhima.

sn: भीष्म उवाच चेदिराजकुले जातस्त्र्यक्ष एष चतुर्भुजः। रासभारावसदृशं ररास च ननाद च॥
en: Bhishma said This Shishupala was born with three eyes and four hands in the dynasty of the kings of Chedi. As soon as he was born, he screamed and brayed like an ass.

sn: तेनास्य मातापितरौ त्रेसतुस्तौ सबान्धवौ। वैकृतं तस्य तौ दृष्ट्वा त्यागायाकुरुतां मतिम्॥
en: His father and mother along with all their relatives were struck with fear (on seeing this fearful phenomenon). seeing these evil omens, they resolved to abandon him.

sn: ततः सभार्यं नृपतिं सामात्यं सपुरोहितम्। चिन्तासम्मूढहृदयं वागुवाचाशरीरिणी॥
en: But at that time an invisible voice (thus) said to the king and his wife with their ministers and priest, all of whose hearts were paralysed by anxiety.

sn: एष ते नृपतेः पुत्रः श्रीमाञ्जातो बलाधिकः। तस्मादस्मान्न भेतव्यमव्यगः पाहि वै शिशुम्॥
en: The Voice said. O king, this your son, who has been (just) born, will become fortunate and superior in strength. Therefore you have no fear from him. Cherish this child without (any) anxiety.

sn: न च वै तस्य मृत्युर्वै न कालः प्रत्युपस्थितः। मृत्युहन्तास्य शस्त्रेण स चोत्पन्नो नराधिप।॥
en: O king, he will not die. His time is not yet come. He that will kill him with weapons has also been born.

sn: संश्रुत्योदाहृतं वाक्यं भूतमन्तर्हितं ततः। पुत्रस्नेहाभिसंतप्ता जननी वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
en: Bhishma said. Having heard these words, the mother becoming anxious by affection for her son, spoke thus to the invisible being.

sn: येनेदमीरितं वाक्यं ममैतं तनयं प्रति। प्राञ्जलिस्तं नमस्यामि ब्रवीतु स पुनर्वचः॥ याथातथ्येन भगवान् देवो वा यदि वेतरः। श्रोतुमिच्छामि पुत्रस्य कोऽस्य मृत्युभविष्यति॥
en: "I bow with joined hands to him that has uttered these words regarding my son. Let him (the invisible being), whether he is an exalted god or any other being, tell me another word. I desire to hear who will be the slayer of this my son".

sn: अन्तर्भूतं ततो भूतमुवाचेदं पुनर्वचः। यस्योत्सङ्गे गृहीतस्य भुजावभ्यधिकावुभौ॥ पतिष्यतः क्षितितले पञ्चशीर्षाविवोरगौ। तृतीयमेतद् बालस्य ललाटस्थं तु लोचनम्॥ निमज्जिष्यति यं दृष्ट्वा सोऽस्य मृत्युभविष्यति। त्र्यक्षं चतुर्भुजं श्रुत्वा तथा च समुदाहृतम्॥
en: The invisible being then again said, "He, upon whose lap this child being taken, his extra arms will fall down on the ground like a pair of five headed snakes, and observing whom his third eyes on the forehead will disappear, will be his slayer." Having heard of the child's three eyes and five arms and also of the words of the invisible being.

sn: पृथिव्यां पार्थिवाः सर्वे अभ्यागच्छन् दिदृक्षवः। तान् पूजयित्वा सम्प्राप्तान् यथार्ह स महीपतिः॥
en: All the kings of the world came to see him. The (Chedi) king worshipped the monarchs that came as each deserved.

sn: एकैकस्य नृपस्याङ्के पुत्रमारोपयत् तदा। एवं राजसहस्राणां पृथक्त्वेन यथाक्रमम्॥ शिशुरङ्कसमारूढो न तत् प्राप निदर्शनम्। एतदेव तु संश्रुत्य द्वारवत्यां महाबलौ॥
en: And gave his child upon their laps one after the other. Thus the child was placed on the laps of one thousand kings one after the other. But what was heard (from the invisible being) did not come to pass. having heard this (about the child) at Dvaravati, the two greatly powerful heroes.

sn: ततश्चेदिपुरं प्राप्तौ संकर्षणजनार्दनौ। यादवी यादवीं द्रष्टुं स्वसारं तौ पितुस्तदा॥
en: The Yadu princes, Sankarashans (Valadeva) and Janarddana (Krishna) went to the capital of the Chedi (king) to see their aunt, the princess of the Yadu race (the queen of the Chedi king).

sn: अभिवाद्य यथान्यायं यथाश्रेष्ठं नृपं च ताम्। कुशलानामयं पृष्ट्वा निषण्णौ रामकेशवौ।॥
en: Saluting every body according to his rank and saluting also the king and the queen and inquiring after every body's welfare, Rama and Keshava (Balaram and Krishna) took their seats.

sn: साभ्यर्च्य तौ तदा वीरौ प्रीत्या चाभ्यधिकं ततः। पुत्रं दामोदरोत्सङ्गे देवी संन्यदधात् स्वयम्॥
en: When those two heroes were duly worshipped, the queen with great pleasure and joy herself placed the child on the lap of Damodara (Krishna).

sn: न्यस्तमात्रस्य तस्याङ्के भुजावभ्यधिकावुभौ। पेततुस्तच्च नयनं न्यमज्जत ललाटजम्॥
en: As soon as the child was placed on his lap, his extra arms fell down and the eye on his forehead disappeared.

sn: तद् दृष्ट्वा व्यथिता जस्ता वरं कृष्णमयाचत। दद व मे वरं कृष्ण भयार्ताया महाभुज॥
en: Seeing this, the queen became alarmed and aggrieved, she begged Krishna to grant her a boon. (She said), O mighty armed hero, I am afflicted with fear; grant me a boon.

sn: त्वं वार्तानां समाश्वासो भीतानामभयप्रदः। एवमुक्तस्ततः कृष्णः सोऽब्रवीद् यदुनन्दनः॥
en: You are the assuager of all men afflicted with grief; you are the dispeller of every body's fear". Having been thus addressed, the : descendant of Yadu, Krishna replied.

sn: मा भैस्त्वं देवि धर्मज्ञे न मत्तोऽस्ति भयं तव। ददामि कं वरं च करवाणि पितृष्वसः॥
en: "O lady, do not be alarmed. O virtuous queen, you have no fear from me. O aunt, what boon shall I give you? What shall I do?

sn: शक्यं वा यदि वाशक्यं करिष्यामि वचस्तव। एवमुक्ता ततः कृष्णमब्रवीद् यदुनन्दनम्॥
en: Whether I am able or not, I shall do what you will say." Having been thus addressed, she thus spoke to the descendant of Yadu, Krishna.

sn: शिशुपालस्यापराधान् क्षमेथास्त्वं महाबला मत्कृते यदुशार्दूल विद्ध्येनं मे वरं प्रभो॥
en: "O greatly powerful hero, O best of the Yadu race, you will have to pardon for my sake the offence committed by Shishupala. O lord, know, this is the boon I ask”.

sn: श्रीकृष्ण उवाच अपराधशतं क्षाम्यं मया ह्यस्य पितृष्वसः। पुत्रस्य ते वधार्हस्य मा त्वं शोके मनः कृथाः॥
en: Krishna Said O Aunt, even when he will deserve to be killed, in such one hundred (occasions of) offences of this (Shishupala), I will pardon him. Do not be (therefore) aggrieved.

sn: भीष्म उवाच एवमेष नृपः पापः शिशुपालः सुमन्दधीः। त्वां समाह्वयते वीर गोविन्दवरदर्पितः॥
en: Bhishma said. O Bhima, such is this wretch Shishupala, a king with a wicked heart. Being proud for the boon granted by Govinda (Krishna), he now calls you to battle.

sn: भीष्म उवाच नैषा चेदिपतेर्बुद्धिर्यया त्वाऽऽह्वयतेऽच्युतम्। नूनमेष जगद्धर्तुः कृष्णस्यैव विनिश्चयः॥
en: Bhishma said The desire, that cause the Chedi king to call you, whose strength deterioration to fight, is hardly is his own wish. knows no This is surely the purpose of Krishna himself, who is the lord of the universe.

sn: को हि मां भीमसेनाद्य क्षितावर्हति पार्थिवः। क्षेप्तुं कालपरीतात्मा यथैष कुलपांसनः॥
en: O Bhimasena, what king was there on earth who could abuse me as this wretch of his race, who has been already taken for his own by Death, has done today.

sn: एष ह्यस्य महाबाहुस्तेजोऽशश्च हरेधुंवम्। तमेव पुनरादातुमिच्छत्युत तथा विभुः॥
en: This mighty armed (hero) is certainly a portion of Hari's (Krishna) energy. The lord (Krishna) wishes to take back to himself his that energy.

sn: येनेष कुरुशार्दूल शार्दूल इव चेदिराट्। गर्जत्यतीव दुर्बुद्धिः सर्वानस्मानचिन्तयन्।॥
en: O best of the Kuru race, for this reason (only) this wicked-minded and tiger like Chedi king roars in this way without caring little for any of us.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततो न ममृषे चैद्यस्तद् भीष्मवचनं तदा। उवाच चैनं संक्रुद्धः पुनर्भीष्ममथोत्तरम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having heard these words of Bhishma, the Chedi king could not brook them. He thus replied to Bhishma in great wrath.

sn: शिशुपाल उवाच द्विषतां नो भीष्मैष प्रभावः केशवस्य यः। यस्य संस्तववक्ता त्वं वन्दिवत् सततोत्थितः॥
en: Shishupala said O Bhishma, when always rising from your seat you are praising his like a (professional) chaunter, let our enemies possess that prowess which is possessed by this Keshava (Krishna).

sn: संस्तवे च मनो भीष्मे परेषां रमते यदि। तदा संस्तौषि राज्ञस्त्वमिमं हित्वा जनार्दनम्॥
en: O Bhishma, if your mind takes pleasure in praising others, then praise these kings (present) here, and leave of Janarddana (Krishna).

sn: दरदं स्तुहि बाह्रीकमिमं पार्थिवसत्तमम्। जायमानेन येनेयमभवद् दारिता मही॥
en: Praise this best of kings Danda, the monarch of Valhika, who, as soon as he was born, rent this earth.

sn: वङ्गाङ्गविषयाध्यक्षं सहस्राक्षसमं बले। स्तुहि कर्णमिमं भीष्म महाचापविकर्षणम्॥
en: O Bhishma, praise this Karna, the king of Anga and Banga, who is like Indra in strength, who draws the great bow.

sn: यस्येमे कुण्डले दिव्ये सहजे देवनिर्मिते। कवचं च महाबाहो बालार्कसदृशप्रभम्॥
en: Who is adorned with the celestials earrings of heavenly make and with the armour possessing the splendour of the rising sun, with (both of) which he was born.

sn: वासवप्रतिमो येन जरासंधोऽतिदुर्जयः। विजितो बाहुयुद्धेन देहभेदं च लम्भितः॥
en: And who vanquished and mangled in a wrestling match the greatly invincible Jarasandha equal to Vasava (Indra).

sn: द्रोणं द्रौणिं च साधु त्वं पितापुत्रौ महारथौ। स्तुहि स्तुत्यावुभौ भीष्म सततं द्विजसत्तमौ॥
en: O Bhishma, praise always Drona and his son (Ashvathama),who are, both father and son, worthy of praise, who are great carwarriors, and who are best of Brahmanas.

sn: ययोरन्यतरो भीष्म संक्रुद्धः सचराचराम्। इमां वसुमती कुर्यान्निःशेषामिति मे मतिः॥
en: O Bhishma, it is my opinion that if they are enraged, either of the two can annihilate this earth with all its mobile and immobile creatures.

sn: द्रोणस्य हि समं युद्धे न पश्यामि नराधिपम्। नाश्वत्थाम्न: समं भीष्म न च तौ स्तोतुमिच्छसि।।१४।
en: O Bhishma, I do not see any king who is equal to Drona or Ashvathama in battle. Why do you not desire to praise them?

sn: पृथिव्यां सागरान्तायां यो वै प्रतिसमो भवेत्। दुर्योधनं त्वं राजेन्द्रमतिक्रम्य महाभुजम्॥
en: Passing over Duryodhana who is the mighty-armed king of kings, and who is unrivalled on earth girt with the seas.

sn: जयद्रथं च राजानं कृतास्त्रं दृढविक्रमम्। दुमं किम्पुरुषाचार्यं लोके प्रथितविक्रमम्। अतिक्रम्य महावीर्यं किं प्रशंससि केशवम्॥
en: Also king Jayadratha, who is accomplished in weapons and who is of great prowess; and also Druma, the preceptor of the Kimpurushas, who is renowned on earth for his prowess.

sn: वृद्धं च भारताचार्यं तथा शारद्वतं कृपम्। आत्क्रम्य महावीर्यं किं प्रशंससि केशवम्॥
en: And also old Kripa, the son of Sharadvata, who is the preceptor of the Bharata race, passing over these greatly powerful men, why do you praise Keshava (Krishna)?

sn: धनुर्धराणां प्रवरं रुक्मिणं पुरुषोत्तमम्। आत्क्रम्य महावीर्यं किं प्रशंससि केशवम्॥
en: Passing over that foremost of bowmen, that excellent man,, the greatly powerful Rukmin, why do you praise Keshava?

sn: भीष्मकं च महावीर्यं दन्तवनं च भूमिपम्। भगदत्तं यूपकेतुं जयत्सेनं च मागधम्॥
en: Passing over the greatly energetic Bhishmaka, and the king Dantavakra, and also Bhagadatta celebrated for his many sacrificial stakes, the king of Magadha Jayacsena.

sn: विराटदुपदौ चोभौ शकुनि च बृहद्बलम्। विन्दानुविन्दावावन्त्यौ पाण्ड्यं श्वेतमथोत्तरम्॥
en: And also Drupada and Virata, Shakuni and Brihadbala, Vinda and Anuvinda of Avanti, Pandya, Shveta, Uttama.

sn: शङ्ख च सुमहाभागं वृषसेनं च मानिनम्। एकलव्यं च विक्रान्तं कालिङ्गं च महारथम्॥
en: The greatly prosperous Shankha, the proud Vrishasena, the powerful Ekalavya, the great car-warrior the king of Kalinga, passing over all these powerful men, why do you praise Keshava?

sn: अतिक्रम्य महावीर्यं किं प्रशंससि केशवम्। शल्यादीनपि कस्मात् त्वं न स्तौषि वसुधाधिपान्। स्तवाय यदि ते बुद्धिवर्तते भीष्म सर्वदा॥
en: O Bhishma, if your mind is always eager to praise others, why do you not praise Shalya and other rulers of the earth?

sn: क हि शक्यं मया कर्तुं यद् वृद्धानां त्वया नृप। पुरा कथयतां नूनं न श्रुतं धर्मवादिनाम्॥
en: O king, what am I capable of doing (giving you good advice) when you have never before heard any thing from the virtuous men who are learned in the precepts of virtue?

sn: आत्मनिन्दाऽऽत्मपूजा च परनिन्दा परस्तवः। अनाचरितमार्याणां वृत्तमेतच्चतुर्विधम्॥
en: O Bhishma, have you not heard that reproach and glorification of self and reproach and glorification of others are not the practices of those who are respectable?

sn: यदस्त्वयमिमं शश्वन्मोहात् संस्तौषि भक्तितः। कंशवं तच्च ते भीष्म न कश्चिदनुमन्यते॥
en: O Bhishma, there is none who approves your conduct in thus continually praising this Keshava, who is unworthy of any praise; you (surely) do it from ignorance alone.

sn: कथं भोजस्य पुरुषे वर्गपाले दुरात्मनि। समावेशयसे सर्वं जगत् केवलकाम्यया॥
en: How can you from your desire alone establish the whole universe in this wicked minded slave and cow-heard of Vraja.

sn: अथ चैषा न ते बुद्धिः प्रकृतिं याति भारत। मयैव कथितं पूर्वं भूलिङ्गशकुनिर्यथा।॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, perhaps your inclination is not conformable to your true nature, like that of the bird Bhulinga, the story of which has been already told by me.

sn: भूलिङ्गशकुनि म पार्श्वे हिमवतः परे। भीष्म तस्या सदा वाचः श्रूयन्तेऽर्थविगर्हिताः॥
en: O Bhishma, there was a bird, called Bhulinga living on the other side of the Himalayas. His words were always without any meaning.

sn: मा साहसमितीदं सा सततं वाशते किल। साहसं चात्मनातीव चरन्ती नावगुध्यते॥
en: "Never act rashly” was what he always said, but he never knew that he himself always acted rashly.

sn: सा हि मांसार्गलं भीष्म मुखात् सिंहस्य खादतः। दन्तान्तरविलग्नं यत् तदादत्तेऽल्पचेतना॥
en: O Bhishma, that foolish bird used to pick from the lion's mouth the pieces of flesh sticking between its teeth when the lion was engaged in eating.

sn: इच्छतः सा हि सिंहस्य भीष्म जीवत्यसंशयम्। तद्वत् त्वमप्यधर्मिष्ठ सदा वाचः प्रभाषसे॥
en: O Bhishma, that bird surely lived at the pleasure of the lion. O sinful wretch, you always speak like that bird.

sn: इच्छतां भूमिपालानां भीष्म जीवस्य संशयम्। लोकविद्विष्टकर्मा हि नान्योऽस्ति भवता समः॥
en: O Bhishma, surely you live at the pleasure of these kings. There is none else like you who is engaged in doing things contrary to the opinions of all.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततश्चेदिपते: श्रुत्वा भीष्मः स कटुकं वचः। उवाचेदं वचो राजश्चेदिराजस्य शृण्वतः॥
en: Vaishampayana said O king, having heard these rude and harsh words of the Chedi king, Bhishma spoke thus in the hearing of the king of Chedi.

sn: इच्छतां किल नामाहं जीवाम्येषां महीक्षितान्। सोऽहं न गणयाम्येतांस्तृणेनापि नराधिपान्॥
en: Bhishma said Truly am I alive at the pleasure of these rulers of earth. But I do not consider these kings as equal to even straws.

sn: एवमुक्ते तु भीष्मेण ततः संचक्रुशुर्नृपाः। केचिज्जहषिरे तत्र केचिद् भीष्मं जगहिरे॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having been thus addressed by Bhishma, the kings became full of anger. Some amongst them stood erect and some began to reproach Bhishma.

sn: केचिदूचुर्महेष्वासाः श्रुत्वा भीष्मस्य तद् वचः। पापोऽवलिप्तो वृद्धश्च नायं भीष्मोऽर्हति क्षमाम्॥
en: Having heard these words of Bhishma, some of these great bowmen said, “This sinful wretch, Bhishma, though old, is exceedingly boastful. He deserves no pardon.

sn: हन्यतां दुर्मतिर्भीष्मः पशुवत् साध्वयं नृपाः। सर्वैः समेत्य संरब्धैर्दह्यता वा कटाग्निना॥
en: Therefore, O kings, let this wicked minded Bhishma be killed like an animal, or let us master all together, and let him be burnt in a fire made of straw".

sn: इति तेषां वचः श्रुत्वा ततः कुरुपितामहः। उवाच मतिमान् भीष्मस्तानेव वसुधाधिपान्॥
en: Having heard their these words, the grandsire of the Kurus, the intélligent Bhishma, then thus spoke to the kings.

sn: उक्तस्योक्तस्य नेहान्तमहं समुपलक्षये। यत् तु वक्ष्यामि तत् सर्वं शृणुध्वं वसुधाधिपाः॥
en: Bhishma said O rulers of earth, I do not see the ends of our speeches, for words may be answered with words. Therefore, listen to what I say.

sn: पशुवद् घातनं वा मे दहनं वा कटाग्निना। क्रियतां मूर्ध्नि वो न्यस्तं मयेदं सकलं पदम्॥
en: Whether I may be killed by you like an animal or be burnt in a fire made of straw, say, I place my foot on the head of all.

sn: एष तिष्ठति गाविन्दः पूजितोऽस्माभिरच्युतः। यस्य वस्त्वरते बुद्धिर्मरणाय स माधवम्॥ कृष्णमाह्वयतामद्य युद्धे चक्रगदाधरम्। यादवस्यैव देवस्य देहं विशतु पातितः॥
en: Here is Govinda (Krishna) who knows no deterioration. Him have we worshipped. Let him, who is willing to meet a speedy death call today to battle Madhava, Krishna, the wielder of discus and club, falling (in the battle), let him enter and mix with the body of this Deity.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततः श्रुत्वैव भीष्मस्य चेदिराडुरुविक्रमः। युयुत्सुर्वासुदेवेन वासुदेवमुवाच हः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having heard these words of Bhishn:a, the greatly powerful Chedi King, being desirous of fighting with Vasudeva (Krishna), thus spoke to Vasudeva.

sn: आह्वये त्वां रणं गच्छ मया साधु जनार्दन। यावदद्य निहन्मि त्वां सहितं सर्वपाण्डवैः॥
en: Shishupala said O Janardana, I challenge you. Come, fight me with till I kill you today with all the Pandavas.

sn: सह त्वया हि मे वध्याः सर्वथा कृष्ण पाण्डवाः। नृपतीन् समतिक्रम्य यैरराजा त्वमर्चितः॥
en: O Krishna, the Pandavas also deserve to be killed by me with you, for they having passed over all these kings, have worshipped you who are not a king.

sn: ये त्वां दारमराजानं बाल्यादर्चन्ति दुर्मतिम्। अनर्हमर्हवत् कृष्ण वध्यास्त इति मे मतिः॥
en: O Krishna, it is my opinion that those, that have from childishness worshipped you, as if you deserve it, although you are unworthy of worship, you being only a slave and a wretch and not a king, deserve to be killed by me.

sn: इत्युक्त्वा राजशार्दूलस्तस्थौ गर्जनमर्षणः। एवमुक्तस्ततः कृष्णो मृदुपूर्वमिदं वचः। उवाच पार्थिवान् सर्वान् स समक्षं च वीर्यवान्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having said this, that best of men (Shishupala) stood up and roared in anger. When he ceased (talking), Krishna spoke these words in a soft voice to all the kings in the presence of the Pandavas.

sn: एष नः शत्रुरत्यन्तं पार्थिवाः सात्वतीसुतः। सात्वतानां नृशंसात्मा न हितोऽनपकारिणाम्॥
en: Krishna said O kings, this cruel-hearted man who is the son of a lady of the Satvata race is a great enemy of the Satvata race. Though we never seek to injure him, yet he always seek to do us injury.

sn: प्राग्ज्योतिषपुरं यातानस्माज्ञात्वा नृशंसकृत्। अदहद् द्वारकामेष स्वस्रीयः सन् नराधिपाः॥
en: O king, hearing that we had gone to the city of Pragjyotisha, this wretch of cruel deeds came and burnt Dwarka, though he is the son of my aunt (father's sister).

sn: क्रीडतो भोजराजस्य एष रैवतके गिरौ। हत्वा बद्ध्वा च तान् सर्वानुपायात् स्वपुरं पुरा॥
en: When the Bhoja king was sporting on the Raivataka hill, he killed many of that king''. attendant and carried away many in chains to his own city.

sn: अश्वमेधे हयं मेध्यमुत्सृष्टं रक्षिभिर्वृतम्। पितुर्मे यज्ञविघ्नार्थमहरत् पापनिश्चयः॥
en: This wretch, sinful in all his purposes, in order to obstruct my father's sacrifice, stole the horse of the horse-sacrifice which was let loose under armed guards.

sn: सौवीरान् प्रति यातां च बभ्रोरेष तपस्विनः। भार्यामभ्यहरन्मोहादकामां तामितो गताम्॥
en: This wretch, prompted by sinful motives, though she was unwilling, stole the wife of saintly Babhru (Akura), when she was on her way from Dwarka to the country of the Sauviras.

sn: एष मायाप्रतिच्छन्नः करूषार्थं तपस्विनीम्। जहार भद्रां वैशाली मातुलस्य नृशंसकृत्॥
en: This wretch, ever intent to injure his maternal uncle, ravished in the disguise of the king of Karusha the saintly Bhadra, the princess of Vishala, who was the intended bride of the

sn: पितृष्वसुः कृते दुःखं सुमहन्मर्षयाम्यहम्। दिष्ट्या हीदं सर्वराज्ञां संनिधावद्य वर्तते॥
en: I have patiently born all these for the sake of my father's sister. It is, however, very fortunate that (today) all this has happened before all these kings.

sn: पश्यन्ति हि भवन्तोऽद्य मय्यतीव व्यतिक्रमम्। कृतानि तु परोक्षं मे यानि तानि निबोधत॥
en: Look, Sirs, at the hostility that he bears towards me. Known also all that he has done against me at my back.

sn: इमं त्वस्य न शक्ष्यामि क्षन्तुमद्य व्यतिक्रमम्। अवलेपाद् वधार्हस्य समग्रे राजमण्डले॥
en: He deserves to be killed by me only on account of the great pride that he has displayed today before all these kings. I am hardly able to pardon him to day for the injuries he has done me.

sn: रुक्मिण्यामस्य मूढस्य प्रार्थनाऽऽसीन्मुमूर्षतः। न च तां प्राप्तवान् मूढः शूद्रो वेदश्रुतीमिव॥
en: Desirous as he was of a speedy death, this fool had (once) desired to possess Rukmani (Krishna's wife), but the fool did not obtain her, as a Shudra cannot get a hearing of the Vedas.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमादि ततः सर्वे सहितास्ते नराधिपाः। वासुदेववचः श्रुत्वा चेदिराजं व्यगर्हयन्॥ जातु त्वदन्यो
en: Vaishampayana said Having heard these words of Vasudeva, all the kings assembled there, began to reproach the Chedi King.

sn: तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा शिशुपाल् प्रतापवान्। जहास स्वनवद्धासं वाक्यं चेदमुवाच ह॥
en: Having heard these words, the powerful Shishupala laughed aloud and spoke these words.

sn: मत्पूर्वां रुक्मिणी कृष्ण संसत्सु परिकीर्तयन्। विशेषतः पार्थिवेषु व्रीडां न कुरुषे कथम्॥
en: Shishupala said O Krishna, are you not ashamed to talk in this assembly, specially before all these kings, of Rukinani who had been intended for me.

sn: मन्यमानो हि कः सत्सु पुरुषः परिकीर्तयेत्। अन्यपूर्वां स्त्रियं मधुसूदनः॥
en: O slayer of Madhu, who else is there but you who, regarding himself a man, would say in the midst of respectable men that his wife was intended for some body else?

sn: क्षम वा यदि ते श्रद्धा मा वा कृष्ण मम क्षम। क्रुद्धाद् वापि प्रसन्नाद् वा किं मे त्वत्तो भविष्यति।।२०।
en: O Krishna, if you please pardon me or pardon me not. Angry of friendly, what can you do to me?

sn: तथा ब्रवुत एवास्य भगवान् मधुसूदनः। मनसाचिन्तयच्चक्रं दैत्यवर्गनिषूदनम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said When he (Shishupala) was thus talking, the high-souled slayer of Madhu, (Krishna), thought in his mind of the discus that humbles the pride of the Daityas.

sn: एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु चक्रे हस्तगते सति। उवाच भगवानुच्चैर्वाक्यं वाक्यविशारदः॥
en: As soon as the discus came into his hands, the skillful speaker, the high-souled (Krishna), spoke loudly these words.

sn: शृण्वन्तु मे महीपाला येनैतत् क्षमितं मया। अपराधशतं क्षाम्यं मातुरस्यैव याचने॥
en: Krishna said O rulers of earth, hear why this man has been hither to pardoned by me. Asked by his mother, I promised to pardon his one hundred offences.

sn: दत्तं मया याचितं च तानि पूर्णानि पार्थिवाः। अधुना वधयिष्यामि पश्यतां वो महीक्षिताम्॥
en: This was the boon that she asked me and this was the boon that I granted to her. O kings, that number has (now) become full. I shall now kill him in the presence of the kings.

sn: एवमुक्त्वा यदुश्रेष्ठश्चेदिराजस्य तत्क्षणात्। व्यपाहरच्छिरः क्रुद्धश्चक्रेणामित्रकर्षणः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having said this, the chief of the Yadu race, that chastiser chastiser of foes (Krishna), immediately cut off in anger by his discus, the head of the Chedi king.

sn: स पपात महाबाहुर्वजाहत इवाचलः। ततश्चेदिपतेर्दैहात् तेजोऽयं ददृशुर्नृपाः॥
en: The mighty armed hero fell like a cliff struck by thunder. The kings saw a fearful effulgence from the body of the Chedi king.

sn: उत्पतन्तं महाराज गगनादिव भास्करम्। ततः कमलपत्राक्षं कृष्णं लोकनमस्कृतम्। तेजो विवेश च नराधिप।॥
en: Issuing like that of the sun in the sky. O great king, that effulgence then adorned the lotus-eyed Krishna, ever worshipped by all the worlds, and it then entered his (Krishna's ) body.

sn: तदद्भुतममन्यन्त दृष्ट्वा सर्वे महीक्षितः। यद् विवेश महाबाहुं तत् तेजः पुरुषोत्तमम्॥
en: Seeing the effulgence (of Shishupala) enter (the body of) that mighty armed and excellent of men (Krishna), all the kings thought (the phenomenon) as very wonderful.

sn: अनभ्रे प्रववर्ष द्यौः पपात ज्वलिताशनिः। कृष्णेन निहते चैद्ये चचाल च वसुंधरा॥
en: When the Chedi king was killed by Krishna, the cloudless sky poured showers of rain, blasting thunders were hurled and the earth itself began to tremble.

sn: ततः केचिन्महीपाला नाब्रुवंस्तत्र किंचन। अतीतवाक्पथे काले प्रेक्षमाणा जनार्दनम्॥
en: Some amongst those kings did not speak a word during those unspeakable moments; they sat gazing at Janardana (Krishna).

sn: ववन्दे तत् तदा "प्तैर्हस्ताग्रमपरे प्रत्यर्पिषन्नमर्षिताः। र दशनैरोष्ठानदशन् क्रोधमूर्छिताः॥
en: Some rubbed in anger their palms with their fore fingers, others, being deprived of their senses by anger, bit their lips with their teeth,

sn: रहश्च केचिद् वार्ष्णेयं प्रशशंसुर्नराधिपाः। केचिदेव सुसंरब्धा मध्यस्थास्त्वपरेऽभवन्॥
en: Some kings praised the Vrishni hero in private, some became exited with anger, while others became mediators.

sn: प्रहृष्टाः केशवं जग्मुः संस्तुवन्तो महर्षयः। ब्राह्मणाश्च महात्मानः पार्थिवाश्च महाबलाः॥ शशंसुर्निर्वृताः सर्वे दृष्ट्वा कृष्णस्य विक्रमम्। पाण्डवस्त्वब्रबीद् भ्रातॄन् सत्कारेण महीपतिम्॥
en: The great Rishis became much pleased and praised Keshava (Krishna), and the high-souled Brahmanas and the greatly powerful kings, seeing the prowess of Krishna, became glad at heart and praised him. The Pandava (Yudhishthira) then commanded his brothers to perform the funeral ceremony of the king (Shishupala).

sn: दमघोषात्मजं वीरं संस्कारयत मा चिरम्। तथा च कृतवन्तस्ते भ्रातु शासनं तदा॥ चेदीनामाधिपत्ये च पुत्रमस्य महीपतेः। अभ्यषिञ्चत् तदा पार्थः सह तैर्वसुधाधिपः॥
en: The heroic son of Damaghosha without delay and with all proper respect. They obeyed (their brother's command). Then the son of Pritha (Yudhishthira), with his brothers and with all the kings, installed the son of the king Shishupala in the kingdom of Chedi.

sn: ततः स कुरुराजस्य क्रतुः सर्वसमृद्धिमान्। यूनां प्रीतिकरो राजन् स बभौ विपुलौजसः॥ शान्तविघ्नः सुखारम्भः प्रभूतधनधान्यवान्! अन्नवान् बहुभक्ष्यश्च केशवेन सुरक्षितः॥
en: O king, furnished with plentiful of corn, rice and every king of food and with abundance of wealth that sacrifice of the greatly effulgent king of the Kurus, blessed with every king of prosperity, and well protected by Keshava, commenced with all auspicious ceremonies and became exceedingly beautiful and pleasing to all young men.

sn: समापयामास च तं राजसूयं महाक्रतुम्। तं तु यज्ञं महाबाहुरासमाप्तेर्जनार्दनः। ररक्ष भगवाञ्छौरिः शाईचक्रगदाधरः॥
en: So long the great Rajasuya sacrifice was not completed, the mighty armed Janardana, the illustrious Shauri (Krishna), guarded it with his bow, called Sharanga, and with his discus and club, and thus in due time it was completed.

sn: ततस्त्ववभृथस्नातं धर्मात्मानं युधिष्ठिरम्। समस्तं पार्थिवं क्षत्रमुपगम्येदमब्रवीत्॥
en: Thereupon all the Kshatriya kings came to the virtuous minded Yudhishthira who had bathed (after the completion of the sacrifice) and thus spoke to him.

sn: दिष्टया वर्धसि धर्मज्ञ साम्राज्यं प्राप्तवानसि। आजमीढाजमीढानां यशः संवर्धितं त्वया॥
en: "O virtuous man, you have grown in prosperity by good fortune. You have acquired the imperial dignity. The fame of the Ajamida race has been greatly increased by (you) the descendant of Ajamida.

sn: कर्मणैतेन राजेन्द्र धर्मश्च सुमहान् कृतः। आपृच्छामो नरव्याघ्र सर्वकामैः सुपूजिताः॥
en: O king of kings, you have acquired great religious nerit by your this act. O best of kings, we tell you we have been worshipped by you to the full extent of our desires.

sn: स्वराष्ट्राणि गमिष्यामस्तदनुज्ञातुमर्हसि। श्रुत्वा तु वचनं राज्ञां धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: We now desire to return to our own kingdoms. You should give us permission”. Having heard the words of the kings, Dharmaraja Yudhishthira.

sn: यथार्ह पूज्य नृपतीन् भ्रातृन् सर्वानुवाच ह। राजानः सर्व एवैते प्रीत्यास्मान् समुपागताः॥
en: Worshipped them as each deserved, and then commanded his brother; thus, "All these kings have come to us at their own pleasure;

sn: प्रस्थिता: स्वानि राष्ट्राणि मामापृच्छ्य परंतपाः। अनुव्रजत भद्रं वो विषयान्तं नृपोत्तमान्॥
en: These chastisers of foes are now desirous of returning to their kingdoms after bidding me farewell. Blessed (brothers), follow these excellent kings to the confines of our kingdom".

sn: भ्रातुर्वचनमाज्ञाय पाण्डवा धर्मचारिणः। यथार्ह नृपतीन् सर्वानेककैकं समनुव्रजन्॥
en: Having been thus commanded by their brothers, the virtuous Pandava princes followed the kings one after the other as each deserved.

sn: विराटमन्वयात् तूर्णं धृष्टद्युम्नः प्रतापवान्। धनंजयो यज्ञसेनं महात्मानं महारथम्॥
en: The powerful Dhristadyumna followed the king of Virata. Dhananjaya (Arjuna) followed the great car-warrior and high-souled Yajnasena.

sn: भीष्मं च धृतराष्ट्रं च भीमसेनो महाबलः। द्रोणं तु ससुतं वीरं सहदेवो युधाम्पतिः॥
en: The mighty Bhimasena followed Bhishma and Dhritarashtra. The lord of battle, Sahadeva, followed the heroic Drona and his son.

sn: नकुलः सुबलं राजन् सहपुत्रं समन्वयात्। द्रौपदेयाः ससौभद्राः पर्वतीयान् महारथान्॥
en: O king, Nakula followed Subala and his son, the sons of Draupadi and the son of Subhadra followed the great car-warrior, the mountain kings.

sn: अन्वगच्छंस्तथैवान्यान् क्षत्रियान् क्षत्रियर्षभाः। एवं सुपूजिताः सर्वे जग्मुर्विप्राः सहस्रशः॥
en: The other best of Kshatriyas followed others Kshatriyas; and thousands of Brahmanas also, after being duly worshipped, went away.

sn: गतेषु पार्थिवेन्द्रेषु सर्वेषु ब्राह्मणेषु च। युधिष्ठिरमुवाचेदं वासुदेवः प्रतापवान्॥
en: On the departure of all the kings and the Brahmanas, the powerful Vasudeva (Krishna) thus spoke to Yudhishthira.

sn: आपृच्छे त्वां गमिष्यामि द्वारकां कुरुनन्दन। राजसूयं क्रतुश्रेष्ठं दिष्ट्या त्वं प्राप्तवानसि॥
en: Krishna said. o descendant of Kuru, of Kuru, with permission I shall now go to Dwarka. By good fortune you have accomplished the best of sacrifices, Rajasuya. with your

sn: तमुवाचैवमुक्तस्तु धर्मराजो जनार्दनम्। तव प्रसादाद् गोविन्द प्राप्तः क्रतुवरो मया॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having been thus addressed Dharmaraja (Yudhishthira) thus replied to Janardana (Krishna), "O Govinda, through your grace I have accomplished the great sacrifice.

sn: क्षत्रं समग्रमपि च त्वत्प्रसादाद् वशे स्थितम्। उपादाय बलिं मुख्यं मामेव समुपस्थितम्॥
en: Through your grace, all the Kshatriya (kings) came under my sway and brought here for me valuable tribute.

sn: कथं त्वद्गमनार्थं मे वाणी वितरतेऽनघ। न ह्यहं त्वामृते वीर रतिं प्राप्नोमि कर्हिचित्॥
en: O sinless one, O hero, how can I give you permission to go? Without you my heart never feels any delight.

sn: अवश्यं चैव गन्तव्या भवता द्वारकापुरी। एवमुक्तः स धर्मात्मा युधिष्ठिरसहायवान्॥ अभिगम्याब्रवीत् प्रीतः पृथां पृथुयशा हरिः। साम्राज्यं समनुप्राप्ताः पुत्रास्तेऽद्य पितृष्वसः॥
en: But (I know) you must have to go to the city of Dwarka”. Having been thus addressed, the virtuous-minded and the world renowned Hari (Krishna), accompanied by Yudhishthira, went to Pritha and cheerfully said, “O Aunt, your sons have today obtained the imperial dignity.

sn: सिद्धार्था वसुमन्तश्च सा त्वं प्रीतिमवाप्नुहि। अनुज्ञातस्त्वया चाहं द्वारकां गन्तुमुत्सहे॥
en: They have obtained vast wealth, and they have been crowned with success. Be pleased with all this; with your permission I shall now to go to Dwarka.

sn: सुभद्रां द्रौपदीं चैव सभाजयत केशवः। निष्क्रम्यान्तःपुरात् तस्माद् युधिष्ठिर सहायवान्॥
en: Keshava (Krishna) then bade farewell to Subhadra and Draupadi. Then he came out of the inner apartments accompanied by Yudhishthira.

sn: सातश्च कृतजप्यश्च ब्राह्मणान् स्वस्ति वाच्य च। ततो मेघवपुःप्रख्यं स्यन्दनं च सुकल्पितम्। योजयित्वा महाबाहुर्दारुकः समुपस्थितः॥ उपस्थितं रथं दृष्ट्वा तायप्रवरकेतनम्। प्रदक्षिणमुपावृत्य समारुह्य महामनाः॥ प्रययौ पुण्डरीकाक्षस्ततो द्वारवती पुरीम्॥
en: He performed his ablutions and went through the daily rites of worship. The Brahmanas uttered benedictions. Then the mighty armed Daruka came with the car of excellent make and the body resembling the clouds. Seeing that the Garuda-bannered car had arrived, the high-souled and lotus-eyed (Krishna) walked round it respectfully and ascending on it, started for the city of Dvaravati.

sn: तं पद्भ्यामनुवव्राज धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः। भ्रातृभिः सहितः श्रीमान् वासुदेवं महाबलम्॥
en: The blessed Dharmaraja Yudhishthira, accompanied by his brothers followed on foot the greatly powerful Vasudeva (Krishna).

sn: ततो मुहूर्तं संगृह्य स्यन्दनप्रवरं हरिः। अब्रवीत् पुण्डरीकाक्षः कुन्तीपुत्रं युधिष्ठिरम्॥
en: Then the lotus-eyed Hari (Krishna) stopped for a moment that excellent chariot; and thus spoke to the son of Kunti, Yudhishthira.

sn: अप्रमत्तः स्थितो नित्यं प्रजाः पाहि विशाम्पते। पर्जन्यमिव भूतानि महाद्रुममिव द्विजाः॥
en: "O kings, cherish your subjects with ceaseless vigilance and patience. As the clouds are to all creatures, as the large tree to the birds.

sn: बान्धवास्त्वोपजीवन्तु सहस्राक्षमिवामराः। कृत्वा परस्परेणैवं संविदं कृष्णपाण्डवौ॥
en: And as the thousand-eyed deity (Indra) to the immortals, so you also become the refuge of all your friends and relatives". Krishna and the Pandava (Yudhishthira), thus talking with each other,

sn: अन्योन्यं समनुज्ञाप्य जग्मतुः स्वगृहान् प्रति। गते द्वारवती कृष्णे सात्वतप्रवरे नृप॥
en: Took each other's leave and went towards their respective homes. O king, when the foremost of the Satvata race, Krishna, had gone away to Dvaravati.

sn: एको दुर्योधनो राजा शकुनिश्चापि सौबलः। तस्यां सभायां दिव्यायामूषतुस्तौ नरर्षभौ॥
en: King Duryodhana and the son of Subala, Shakuni, these two best of men only remained in that celestials Sabha (assembly-hall).

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच समाप्ते राजसूये तु क्रतुश्रेष्ठे सुदुर्लभे। शिष्यैः परिवृतो व्यासः पुरस्तात् समपद्यत॥
en: Vaishampayana said When that best of sacrifices, Rajasuya, ever difficult of accomplishment, completed, Vyasa, surrounded by his disciples, came before him (Yudhishthira).

sn: सोऽभ्ययादासनात् तूर्णं भ्रातृभिः परिवारितः। पाद्येनासनदानेन पितामहमपूजयत्॥
en: On his arrival he soon rose from his seat, surrounded by his brothers, and worshipped his grandfather (Vyasa) with offering him a seat and water to wash his feet.

sn: अथोपविश्य भगवान् काञ्चने परमासने। आस्तामिति चोवाच धर्मराज युधिष्ठिरम्॥
en: When the illustrious (Rishi) took his seat on a best seat made of gold, he said to Dharmaraja Yudhishthira "to take his seat".

sn: अथोपविष्टं राजानं भ्रातृभिः परिवारितम्। उवाच भगवान् व्यासस्तत्तद्वाक्यविशारदः॥
en: When the king was seated surrounded by his brothers, the illustrious Vyasa, the skillful speaker, thus spoke.

sn: दिष्ट्या वर्धसि कौन्तेय साम्राज्यं प्राप्य दुर्लभम्। वर्धिताः कुरवः सर्वे त्वया कुरुकुलोद्वह॥
en: “O son of Kunti, you grow in prosperity for good fortune; you have acquired the imperial dignity which is very difficult to be acquired. O perpetuator of the Kuru race, all the Kurus have grown in prosperity for your sake.

sn: आपृच्छे त्वां गमिष्यामि पूजितोऽस्मि विशाम्पते। एवमुक्तः स कृष्णेन धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: O king, with your permission I shall (now) go. I have been duly worshipped”. Having been thus addressed by Krishna (Vyasa), Dharmaraja Yudhishthira,

sn: अभिवाद्योपसंगृह्य पितामहमथाब्रवीत्। युधिष्ठिर उवाच संशयो द्विपदां श्रेष्ठ ममोत्पन्नः सुदुर्लभः॥
en: Saluted his grandfather by touching his feet and thus spoke to him, “O foremost of all men, a very great doubt has arisen in my mind.

sn: तस्य नान्योऽस्ति वक्ता वै त्वामृते द्विजपुङ्गव। उत्पातांस्त्रिविधान् प्राह नारदो भगवानृषिः॥ दिव्यांश्चैवान्तरिक्षांश्च पार्थिवांश्च पितामह। अपि चैद्यस्य पतनाच्छन्नमौत्पातिकं महत्॥
en: O best of the twice-born, there is none else except you who can remove it. The illustrious Rishi Narada said that three kinds of portents, namely celestials, atmospherical and terrestrial, happen (if Rajasuya sacrifice is performed). O grandsire, have these portents been removed by the fall of the Chedi king?

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच राज्ञस्तु वचनं श्रुत्वा पराशरसुतः प्रभुः। कृष्णद्वैपायनो व्यास इदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having heard these words from the king, the son of Parashara, the lord Krishna Dvaipayana, Vyasa, thus spoke to him.

sn: त्रयोदश समा राजन्नुत्पातानां फलं महत्। सर्वक्षत्रविनाशाय भविष्यति विशाम्पते॥
en: "O king, for thirteen years those portents will produce great results. O king, they may even cause the destruction of all the Kshatriyas.

sn: त्वामेकं कारणं कृत्वा कालेन भरतर्षभ। समेतं पार्थिवं क्षत्रं क्षयं यास्यति भारत। दुर्योधनापराधेन भीमार्जुनबलेन च॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, O descendant of Bharata, in course of time, making you the sole cause, the assembled Kshatriya kings will all be destroyed for the fault of Duryodhana and the prowess of Bhima and Arjuna.

sn: स्वप्ने द्रक्ष्यसि राजेन्द्र क्षपान्ते त्वं वृषध्वजम्। नीलकण्दं भवं स्थाणुं कपालं त्रिपुरान्तकम्॥ उग्रं रुद्रं पशुपति महादेवमुमापतिम्। हरं शर्वं वृषं शूलं पिनाकिं कृत्तिवाससम्॥ कैलासकूटप्रतिमं वृषभेऽवस्थितं शिवम्। निरीक्षमाणं सततं पितृराजाश्रितां दिशम्॥
en: O king of kings, in your dream you will see towards the end of this night Vrishadhvaja (Bull-marked), Nilkantha (blue throated), Bhava, Sthanu, (deep in mediation) Kapali, (drinking from human skull), Tripurantaka (slayer to Tripura), fierce and terrible Pashupati (the lord of creatures), Mahadeva (the god of gods), Umapati, (the husband of Uma) Hara, Sharva, Vrisha, Shuli, (holding the trident) Pinaki (armed with Pinaka bow), attired in skin, Shiva, tall and white as the cliff of the Kailasa, seated on his bull and always gazing towards the direction, presided over by the Pitris (South).

sn: एवमीदृशकं स्वप्नं द्रक्ष्यसि त्वं विशाम्पते। मा तत्कृते ह्यनुध्याहि कालो हि दुरतिक्रमः॥
en: O king, you will see such a dream (today). Do not be grieved for it, for none can rise superior of Time.

sn: स्वस्ति तेऽस्तु गमिष्यामि कैलास पर्वतं प्रति। अप्रमत्तः स्थितो दान्तः पृथिवीं परिपालय॥
en: Be blessed. I shall now (go towards the Kailasa mountain). Rule the earth with vigilance and steadiness and bear patiently all privations".

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्त्वा स भगवान् कैलासं पर्वतं ययौ। कृष्णद्वैपायनो व्यासः सह शिष्यैः श्रुतानुगैः॥
en: Having said this, the illustrious Krishna Dvaipayana, Vyasa, accompanied by his disciples, who always followed the dictates of the Vedas, went towards the Kailasa mountain.

sn: गते पितामह राजा चिन्ताशोकसमन्वितः। निःश्वसन्नुष्णमसकृत् तमेवार्थं विचिन्तयन्॥
en: On the departure of the grandfather (Vyasa), the king became afflicted with grief and anxiety. He continuously sighed and reflected on what the Rishi said.

sn: कथं तु दैवं शक्येत पौरुषेण प्रबाधितुम्। अवश्यमेव भविता यदुक्तं परमर्षिणा॥
en: He said to himself, "what the great Rishi has said must came to pass. How can fates be warded off by human exertions?

sn: ततोऽब्रवीन्महातेजाः सर्वान् भ्रातृन् युधिष्ठिरः। श्रुतं वै पुरुषव्याघ्रा यन्मां द्वैपायनोऽब्रवीत्॥
en: Thereupon, the greatly effulgent Yudhishthira thus spoke to all his brothers. "O best of men, you have heard what Dvaipayana (Vyasa) has said.

sn: तदा तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा मरणे निश्चिता मतिः। सर्वक्षत्रस्य निधने यद्यहं हेतुरीप्सितः॥
en: Hearing his words, my firm resolve is to die, when I have been ordained to be the cause of the destruction of all the Kshatriyas.

sn: कालेन निर्मितस्तात को ममार्थोऽस्ति जीवतः। एवं ब्रुवन्तं राजानं फाल्गुनः प्रत्यभाषत।॥
en: O children, if Time has willed it, what need is there for me to live?” To the king who was thus speaking replied Falguni (Arjuna),

sn: मा राजन् कश्मलं घोरं प्रविशो बुद्धिनाशनम्। सम्प्रधार्य महाराज यत् क्षेमं तत् समाचर॥
en: "O king, do not yield yourself to the great depression which destroys one's reason. O great king, mustering fortitude, do what is beneficial".

sn: ततोऽब्रवीत् सत्यधृतिर्धातॄन् सर्वान् युधिष्ठिरः। द्वैपायनस्य वचनं ह्येवं समनुचिन्तयन्॥
en: Thereupon Yudhishthira, ever devoted to truth, thinking all the while the words of Dvaipayana (Vyasa), spoke thus to all his brothers.

sn: अद्यप्रभृति भद्रं वः प्रतिज्ञां मे निबोधत। त्रयोदश समास्तात को ममार्थोऽस्ति जीवतः॥
en: "O children, O blessed ones, listen to the vow I make from this day. For what other purpose am I to live for thirteen years?

sn: न प्रवक्ष्यामि परुषं भ्रातृनन्यांश्च पार्थिवान्। स्थितो निदेशे ज्ञातीनां योक्ष्ये तत् समुदाहरन्॥
en: I shall not speak a harsh word to my brothers or to any of the kings of the earth. I shall remain obedient to my relatives and practice virtue.

sn: एवं मे वर्तमानस्य स्वसुतेष्वितरेषु च। भेदो न भविता लोके भेदमूलो हि विग्रहः॥
en: If I live in this way, making no distinction between my own sons and those of others, there will be no disagreement in the world. Disagreement is the cause of war.

sn: विग्रहं दूरतो रक्षन् प्रियाण्येव समाचरन्। वाच्यतां न गमिष्यामि लोकेषु मनुजर्षभाः॥
en: O best of men, I shall keep war at a distance, and I shall ever do what is agreeable to others. Thus no evil reputation will touch me in the world."

sn: भ्रातुर्येष्ठस्य वचनं पाण्डवाः संनिशम्य तत्। तमेव समवर्तन्त धर्मराजहिते रताः॥
en: Having heard these words of their elder brother, the Pandavas, ever engaged in doing what is agreeable to Dharmaraja (Yudhishthira), approved of them.

sn: संसत्सु समयं कृत्वा धर्मराड् भ्रातृभिः सह। पितॄस्तर्प्य यथान्यायं देवताश्च विशाम्पते॥
en: O king, Dharmaraja (Yudhishthira), having thus taken the vow with his brothers in that assembly, gratified the Pitris and the celestial.

sn: कृतमङ्गलकल्याणो भ्रातृभिः परिवारितः। गतेषु क्षत्रियेन्द्रेषु सर्वेषु भरतर्षभ॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, on the departure of all the Kshatriya kings, he (Yudhishthira), surrounded by his brothers, performed the usual auspicious rites.

sn: युधिष्ठिरः सहामात्यः प्रविवेश पुरोत्तमम्। दुर्योधनो महाराज शकुनिश्चापि सौबलः। सभायां रमणीयायां तत्रैवास्ते नराधिप॥
en: Yudhishthira then with his ministers entered his excellent palace. O great king, Duryodhana and the son of Subala, Shakuni, (then) lived in that charming Sabha (assembly hall).

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच वसन् दुर्योधनस्तस्यां सभायां पुरुषर्षभ। शनैर्ददर्श तां सर्वां सभां शकुनिना सह॥
en: Vaishampayana said O best of men, Duryodhana lived in their (the Pandava's) that Assembly-Hall. He slowly examined the whole of that mansion with Shakuni.

sn: तस्यां दिव्यानभिप्रायान् ददर्श कुरुनन्दनः। न दृष्टपूर्वा ये तेन नगरे नागसाह्वये॥
en: The Kuru prince saw in it many celestials designs which he had never seen before in the city of Hastinapur.

sn: स कदाचित् सभामध्ये धार्तराष्ट्रो महीपतिः। स्फाटिकं स्थलमासाद्य जलमित्यभिशङ्कया॥ स्ववस्त्रोत्कर्षणं राजा कृतवान् बुद्धिमोहितः। दुर्मना विमुखश्चैव परिचक्राम तां सभाम्॥ ततः स्थले निपतितो दुर्मना वीडितो नृपः। निःश्वसन् विमुखश्चापि परिचक्राम तां सभाम्॥
en: One day the son of Dhritarashtra, king (Duryodhana) coming to a place made of crystal, mistook it for water and drew up his clothes. Finding his mistake out, he wandered over the Sabha in great sorrow.

sn: ततः स्फाटिकतोयां वै स्फाटिकाम्बुजशोभिताम्। वापी मत्वा स्थलमिव सवासाः प्रापतज्जले॥
en: Some after, he mistook a lake of crystal water, adorned with crystal water flowers for land and fell into it with all his clothes on.

sn: जले निपतितं दृष्ट्वा भीमसेनो महाबलः। जहास जहसुश्चैव किंकराश्च सुयोधनम्॥
en: Seeing him fallen into the water, the greatly strong Bhima laughed aloud, the servants also laughed at Suyodhana (Duryodhana).

sn: वासांसि च शुभान्यस्मै प्रददू राजशासनात्। तथागतं तु तं दृष्ट्वा भीमसेनो महाबलः॥
en: Other handsome and dry clothes were soon given to him at the command of the king (Yudhishthira). Seeing his this plight the mighty Bhimasena.

sn: अर्जुनश्च यमौ चोभौ सर्वे ते प्राहसंस्तदा। नामर्षयत् ततस्तेषामवहासममर्षणः॥
en: Arjuna, and the twins (Nakula and Sahadeva) all laughed aloud. Ever incapable of putting up with insults, he (Duryodhana) could not bear their laughter.

sn: आकारं रक्षमाणस्तु न स तान् समुदैक्षत। पुनर्वसनमुत्क्षिप्य प्रतरिष्यन्निव स्थलम्॥ आरुरोह ततः सर्वे जहसुश्च पुनर्जनाः। द्वारं तु पिहिताकारं स्फाटिकं प्रेक्ष्य भूमिपः। प्रविशन्नाहतो मूनि व्याघूर्णित इव स्थितः॥
en: Concealing his emotions, he even did not cast his eyes on them. Seeing him again draw up his clothes to cross a piece of land (made of crystal), mistaking it for water, all men laughed aloud. Then king (Duryodhana) mistook a closed door made of crystal as open.

sn: तादृशं न परं द्वारं स्फाटिकोरुकपाटकम्। विघट्टयन् कराभ्यां तु निष्क्रम्याग्रे पपात ह॥
en: And he hurt his head to pass it and stood with his brains swimming. In this way mistaking another open door made of crystal as closed, he attempted to open it with outstretched hands and tumbled down.

sn: द्वारं तु वितताकारं समापेदे पुनश्च सः। तद्वत्तं चेति मन्वानो द्वारस्थानादुपारमत्॥
en: Coming upon another door that was really open, the king, thinking it closed, went away from it.

sn: एवं प्रलम्भान् विविधान् प्राप्य तत्र विशाम्पते। पाण्डवेयाभ्यनुज्ञातस्ततो दुर्योधनो नृपः॥ अप्रहृष्टेन मनसा राजसूये महाक्रतौ। प्रेक्ष्य तामद्धतामृद्धिं जगाम गजसाह्वयम्॥
en: O king, having thus become the victim of various mistakes there (in that Assembly-hall) and having seen the vast wealth (that was collected) in the great Rajasuya sacrifice, the king Duryodhana, with the permission of the Pandavas, returned to the city of Hastinapur.

sn: पाण्डवश्रीप्रतप्तस्य ध्यायमानस्य गच्छतः। दुर्योधनस्य नृपतेः पापा मतिरजायत॥
en: As he proceeded (towards the city), reflecting (on all he had seen), the heart of the king Duryodhana, having been afflicted with the sight of the prosperity of the Pandavas, became inclined to sin.

sn: पार्थान् सुमनसो दृष्ट्वा पार्थिवांश्च वशानुगान्। कृत्स्नं चापि हितं लोकमाकुमारं कुरूद्वह॥ महिमानं परं चापि पाण्डवानां महात्मनाम्। दुर्योधनो धार्तराष्ट्रो विवर्णः समपद्यत॥
en: O perpetuator of the Kuru race, seeing the sons of Pritha happy and all the kings of the world obedient to them, and (seeing also) that every body (both) young and old engaged in son doing good to them, reflecting also on the splendour and prosperity of the illustrious Pandavas, the of Dhritarashtra, Duryodhana, became pale.

sn: स तु गच्छन्ननेकाग्रः सभामेकोऽन्वचिन्तयत्। श्रियं च तामनुपमां धर्मराजस्य धीमतः॥
en: In proceeding (towards his city) with an afflicted heart, he only reflected on the matchless Assembly-hall and the great prosperity of the intelligent Dharmaraja (Yudhishthira).

sn: प्रमत्तो धृतराष्ट्रस्य पुत्रो दुर्योधनस्तदा। नाभ्यभाषत् सुबलजं भाषमाणं पुनः पुनः॥
en: The son of Dhritarashtra, Duryodhana, was so much taken up with his own thoughts that he did not speak a word to Subala's son (Shakuni), though he repeatedly spoke to him.

sn: अनेकाग्रं तु तं दृष्ट्वा शकुनिः प्रत्यभाषत। दुर्योधन कुतोमूलं निःश्वसनिव गच्छसि॥
en: Seeing him very much agitated (in heart), Shakuni thus spoke to him, "O Duryodhana, why are you proceeding, sighing (all the while)?

sn: दुर्योधन उवाच दृष्ट्वेमां पृथिवीं कृत्स्नां युधिष्ठिरवशानुगाम्। जितामस्त्रप्रतापेन श्वेताश्वस्य महात्मनः॥ तं च यज्ञं तथाभूतं दृष्ट्वा पार्थस्य मातुला यथा शक्रस्य देवेषु तथाभूतं महाद्युतेः॥
en: Duryodhana said O uncle, seeing the whole earth brought under Yudhishthira's sway by the force of the illustrious Arjuna's weapons, and seeing also the sacrifice of the son of Pritha like that of the greatly effulgent Shakra (Indra) among the celestials,

sn: अमर्षेण तु सम्पूर्णो दह्यमानो दिवानिशम्। शुचिशुक्रागमे काले शुष्येत् तोयमिवाल्पकम्॥
en: I have been filled with jealousy, and I am burning day and night. I am being dried up like a shallow tank in the summer season.

sn: पश्य सात्वतमुख्येन शिशुपालो निपातितः। न च तत्र पुमानासीत् कश्चित् तस्य पदानुगः॥
en: Behold, when Shishupala was killed by the chief of the Satvata race, there was none to take his side.

sn: दह्यमाना हि राजानः पाण्डवोत्थेन वह्निना। क्षान्तवन्तोऽपराधं ते को हि तत् क्षन्तुमर्हति॥
en: The kings appeared (as if) they were consumed by the Pandava fire; therefore they were forgiving, for else who could pardon such an offence?

sn: वासुदेवेन तत् कर्म यथायुक्तं महत् कृतम्। सिद्धं च पाण्डुपुत्राणां प्रतापेन महात्मनाम्॥
en: That greatly improper act of Vasudeva was only successful on account of the prowess of the illustrious sons of Pandu.

sn: तथा हि रत्नान्यादाय विविधानि नृपा नृपम्। उपातिष्ठन्त कौन्तेयं वैश्या इव करप्रदाः॥
en: Various kings brought with them various kinds of wealth to the son of Kunti, king (Yudhishthira) and worshipped him like the tribute-paying Vaishyas.

sn: श्रियं तथाऽऽगतां दृष्ट्वा ज्वलन्तीमिव पाण्डवे। अमर्षवशमापन्नो दह्यामि न तथोचितः॥
en: Seeing the splendour of the Pandava's prosperity, and being afflicted with jealousy, I am as if on fire although I should not be jealous.

sn: एवं स निश्चयं कृत्वा ततो वचनमब्रवीत्। पुनर्गान्धारनृपतिं दह्यमान इवाग्निना॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having been burnt as if by fire and having made the (following) resolve, he (Duryodhana) thus again spoke to the king of Gandhara (Shakuni).

sn: वह्निमेव प्रवक्ष्यामि भक्षयिष्यामि वा विषम्। अपो वापि प्रवेक्ष्यामि न हि शक्ष्यामि जीवितुम्॥
en: Duryodhana said I shall throw myself into the fire, or I shall drink the poison, or I shall drown myself in water. I am unable to live.

sn: को हि नाम पुमाँल्लोके मर्पयिष्यति सत्त्ववान्। सपत्नानृङ्ख्यतो दृष्ट्वा हीनमात्मामेव च॥
en: What man is there in the world possessing manliness who can bear to see his foes in prosperity and himself in destitution?

sn: सोऽहं न स्त्री न चाप्यस्त्री न पुमान्नापुमानपि। योऽहं तां मर्षयाम्यद्य तादृशीं श्रियमागताम्॥
en: Therefore, I who bear the sight of the prosperity and fortune of my foes, am neither a woman nor on who is not a woman, neither a man nor one who is not a man.

sn: ईश्वरत्वं पृथिव्याश्च वसुमत्तां च तादृशीम्। यज्ञं च तादृशं दृष्ट्वा मादृशः को न संज्वरेत्॥
en: Seeing their lordship over the world, their such vast wealth, and also their that sacrifice, who is there like me that will not smart under it?

sn: अशक्तश्चैव एवाहं तामाहर्तुं नृपश्रियम्। सहायांश्च न पश्यामि तेन मृत्यु विचिन्तये॥
en: I am alone incapable of acquiring such royal prosperity. I do not also see any one who can help me in doing it. Therefore I think of death.

sn: दैवमेव परं मन्ये पौरुषं च निरर्थकम्। दृष्ट्वा कुन्तीसुते शुद्धां श्रियं तामहतां तथा॥
en: Seeing the great and serene prosperity of the son of Kunti, I consider Fate to be supreme and exertion useless.

sn: कृतो यत्नो मया पूर्वं विनाशे तस्य सौबल। तच्च सर्वमतिक्रम्य संवृद्धोऽप्स्विव पङ्कजम्॥
en: O son of Subala, I forinerly tried to destroy hiin, but baffling all my efforts, he has grown in prosperity like the lotus (in the tank).

sn: तेन दैवं परं मन्ये पौरुषं च निरर्थकम्। धार्तराष्ट्राश्च हीयन्ते पार्था वर्धन्ति नित्यशः॥
en: Therefore, I consider fate to be supreme and (all) exertions useless. The sons of Dhritarashtra are decaying, (but) the sons of Pritha are prospering.

sn: सोऽहं श्रियं च तां दृष्ट्वा सभां तां च तथाविधाम्। रक्षिभिश्चावहासं तं परितप्ये यथाग्निना॥
en: Seeing their prosperity and their that Assembly-hall, and also the laughter of their servants, I am burning (in my heart), as if I am on fire.

sn: स मामभ्यनुजामीहि मातुलाद्य सुदुःखितम्। अमर्षं च समाविष्टं धृतराष्ट्र निवेदय॥
en: O uncle, know me now to be in great grief and full of jealousy, of jealousy, speak of it to Dhritarashtra.

sn: शकुनिरुवाच दुर्योधन न तेऽमर्षः कार्यः प्रति युधिष्ठिरम्। भागधेयानि हि स्वानि पाण्डवा भुञ्जते सदा॥
en: Shakuni said O Duryodhana, you should not be jealous of Yudhishthira. the Pandavas are enjoying what their good fortune yields them.

sn: विधानं विविधाकारं परं तेषां विधानत: । अनेकैरभ्युपायैश्च त्वया न शकिताः पुरा॥ आरब्धाश्च महाराज पुनः पुनरिंदम। विमुक्ताश्च नरव्याघ्रा भागधेयपुरस्कृताः॥
en: O Chastiser of foes, O great king, you were unable to destroy them by repeatedly adopting various plans, many of which you reduced to practice. These best of men for their good fortune escaped (all) your machinations.

sn: तैर्लब्धा द्रौपदी भार्या द्रुपदश्च सुतैः सह। सहायः पृथिवीलाभे वासुदेवश्च वीर्यवान्॥
en: They obtained Draupadi as wife and Drupada with his two sons (as allies); and also the greatly powerful Vasudeva (Krishna) as a help to acquire the whole world.

sn: लब्धश्चानभिभूतार्थैः पित्र्योंऽशः पृथिवीपते। विवृद्धस्तेजसा तेषां तत्र का परिदेवना॥
en: O ruler of earth, having obtained their paternal share of the kingdom and not being deprived of it, they have grown (in prosperity) by their own energy. What is there to make you sorry in all this?

sn: धनञ्जयेन गाण्डीवमक्षय्यौ च महेषुधी। लब्धान्यस्त्राणि दिव्यानि तोषयित्वा हुताशनम्॥
en: Having worshipped Hutashana (Fire) Dhananjaya (Arjuna) has obtained the Gandiva (bow), the two inexhaustible quivers and many celestial weapons.

sn: तेन कार्मुकमुख्येन बाहुवीर्येण चात्मनः। कृता वशे महीपालास्तत्र का परिदेवना॥
en: With that best of bow and by the prowess of his arins, he has brought all the rulers of earth under his sway. What is there to be sorry at?

sn: अग्निदाहान्मयं चापि मोक्षयित्वा स दानवम्। सभां तां कारयामास सव्यसाची परंतपः॥
en: Having saved the Danava Maya from the conflagration of fire, the chastiser of foes, Savyasachi (Arjuna) made him build that Assembly-hall.

sn: तेन चैव मयेनोक्ताः किंकरा नाम राक्षसाः। वहन्ति तां सभां भीमास्तत्र का परिदेवना॥
en: At the command of Maya, those fearful Rakshasas, named Kinkaras, guard that Assembly-hall. What is there then be sorry at?

sn: यच्चासहायतां राजन्नुक्तवानसि भारत। तन्मिथा भ्रातरो हीमे तव सर्वे वशानुगा॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, O king, you have said that you have no one to help you. This is not true. These your brothers are all obedient to you.

sn: द्रोणस्तव महेष्वासः सह पुत्रेण वीर्यवान्। सूतपुत्रश्च राधेयो गौतमश्च महारथः॥
en: The wielder of the great bow the greatly powerful Drona with his son, the Suta's son, Radheya (Karna), the great car-warrior, Goutama (Kripa),

sn: अहं च सह सोदर्यैः सौमदत्तिश्च पार्थिवः। एतैस्त्वं सहितः सर्वैर्जय कृत्स्ना वसुन्धराम्॥
en: I with my brothers, the king Somadatti, these are all your allies. Conquer the whole earth with them.

sn: दुर्योधन उवाच त्वया च सहितो राजन्नेतैश्चान्यैर्महारथैः। एतानेव विजेष्यामि यदि त्वमनुमन्यसे॥
en: Duryodhana said O king, if it please you, I shall conquer the Pandavas with you and with these great carwarriors.

sn: एतेषु विजितेष्वद्य भविष्यति मही मम। सर्वे च पृथिवीपालाः सभा सा च महाधना॥
en: If I can conquer them, the whole world will be mine; as also the kings and the Assembly hall which is so full of wealth.

sn: शकुनिरुवाच धनंजयो वासुदेवो भीमसेनो युधिष्ठिरः। नकुलः सहदेवश्च दुपदश्च सहात्मजैः॥ नैते युधि पराजेतुं शक्या देवगणैरपि। महारथा महेष्वासाः कृतास्त्रा युद्धदुर्मदाः॥
en: Shakuni Said Dhananjaya, Vasudeva, Bhimasena, Yudhishthira, Nakula, Sahadeva, Drupada, and his two sons, these (heroes) cannot be conquered in a battle even by the celestials. They are all great car-warriors, and the wielders of great bows; they are accomplished in arms and invincible in war.

sn: अहं तु तद् विजानामि विजेतुं येन शक्यते। युधिष्ठिरं स्वयं राजंस्तन्निबोध जुषस्व च॥
en: But I know the means by which Yudhishthira may be vanquished. O king, listen to it and adopt it.

sn: दुर्योधन उवाच अप्रमादेन सुहृदामन्येषां च महात्मनाम्। यदि शक्या विजेतुं ते तन्ममाचक्ष्व मातुल॥
en: Duryodhana said O uncle, without any danger to our friends and other illustrious men, if there is means to conquer him, tell it to me.

sn: शकुनिरुवाच द्यूतप्रियश्च कौन्तेयो न स जानाति देवितुम्। समाहूतश्च राजेन्द्रो न शक्ष्यति निवर्तितुम्॥
en: Shakuni Said The son of Kunti (Yudhishthira) is very much fond of gambling, but he does now know how to play. That king of kings, (Yudhishthira) if asked to play, will not be able to refuse.

sn: देवने कुशलश्चाहं न मेऽस्ति सदृशो भुवि। त्रिषु लोकेषु कौरव्य तं त्वं द्यूते समाह्वय॥
en: I am skillful in the play at dice. There is none equal to me (in this play), on earth, may, not even in the three worlds. O descendant of Kuru, (therefore) ask him to play.

sn: तस्याक्षकुशलो राजन्नादास्येऽहमसंशयम्। राज्यं श्रियं च तां दीप्तां त्वदर्थं पुरुषर्षभ॥
en: O king, O best of men, expert as I am in the play at dice, I am certain to win for you his kingdom and his greatly effulgent prosperity.

sn: इदं तु सर्वं त्वं राज्ञे दुर्योधन निवेदय। अनुज्ञातस्तु ते पित्रा विजेष्ये तान् न संशयः॥
en: But, O Duryodhana, tell all this to the king (Dhritarashtra). At the command of your father, I will win the whole of Yudhishthira's possessions without the least doubt.

sn: दुर्योधन उवाच त्वमेव कुरुमुख्याय धृतराष्ट्राय सौबल। निवेदय यथान्यायं नाहं शक्ष्ये निवेदितुम्॥
en: Duryodhana said O son of Subala, tell yourself all this to the chief of the Kurus, Dhritarashtra, I shall not be able to do it.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच अनुभूय तु राज्ञस्तं राजसूयं महाक्रतुम्। युधिष्ठिरस्य नृपतेर्गान्धारीपुत्रसंयुतः॥ प्रियकृन्मतमाज्ञाय पूर्वं दुर्योधनस्य तत्। प्रज्ञाचक्षुषमासीनं शकुनिः सौबलस्तदा।॥ दुर्योधनवचः श्रुत्वा धृतराष्ट्रं जनाधिपम्। उपगम्य महाप्राज्ञं शकुनिर्वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said O king, having been impressed with the great Rajasuya sacrifice of king Yudhishthira and having also learnt the intentions of Duryodhana, from what he said, and also in order to do what was pleasing to him (Duryodhana), the son of Subala, Shakuni, accompanied by Gandhari's son (Duryodhana) to the king Dhritarashtra whose knowledge was his eye, seated (on this throne). Approaching that greatly intelligent (king), Shakuni thus spoke to him.

sn: शकुनिरुवाच दुर्योधनो महाराज विवर्णो हरिणः कृशः। दीनश्चिन्तापरचैव तं विद्धि मनुजाधिप॥
en: Shakuni said O great king, O best of the Bharata race, know that Duryodhana has become colourless, pale, and emaciated with anxiety. came

sn: न वै परीक्षसे सम्यगसह्यं शत्रुसम्भवम्। ज्येष्ठपुत्रस्य हृच्छोकं किमर्थं नावबुध्यसे॥
en: Why do you not after due enquiry ascertain the cause of the grief that is in the heart of your eldest son, the grief caused by the enemy?

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच दुर्योधन कुतोमूलं भृशमार्तोऽसि पुत्रक। श्रोतव्यश्चन्मया सोऽर्थो ब्रूहि मे कुरुनन्दन॥
en: Dhritarashtra said O Duryodhana, O son, what is the cause of your grief? O Kuru prince, if it is fit for me to hear, tell it to me.

sn: अयं त्वां शकुनिः प्राह विवर्णं हरिणं कृशम्। चिन्तयंश्च न पश्यामि शोकस्य तव सम्भवम्॥
en: This Shakuni says you are colourless, pale and emaciated. After reflection I can not find any cause for your grief.

sn: ऐश्वर्यं हि महत् पुत्र त्वयि सर्वं प्रतिष्ठितम्। भ्रातरः सुहृदश्चैव नाचरन्ति तवाप्रियम्॥
en: O son, all my vast wealth is at your command. Your brothers and our relatives and friends never do anything injurious to you.

sn: आच्छादयसि प्रावारानश्नासि विशदौदनम्। आजानेया वहन्त्यश्वाः केनासि हरिणः कृशः॥
en: You wear the best robes, you eat food prepared with meat, you ride the best horses, why then are you pale and emaciated?

sn: शयनानि महार्हाणि योषितश्च मनोरमाः। गुणवन्ति च वेश्मानि विहाराश्च यथासुखम्॥
en: Costly beds, the charming damsels finely furnished mansions and grounds of sport are at pleasure (when you amuse).

sn: देवानामिव ते सर्वं वाचि बुद्धं न संशयः। स दीन इव दुर्धर्ष कस्माच्छोचसि पुत्रकः॥
en: All these certainly wait your command as do they in the case of the celestials. () invincible hero, O son, why do you grieve (then) like a destitute person?

sn: दुर्योधन उवाच अश्नाम्याच्छादये चाहं यथा कुपुरुषस्तथा। अमर्षं धारये चोग्रं निनिषुः कालपर्ययम्॥
en: Duryodhana said I, no doubt, eat and dress but I pass my time all the while like a wretch, for I am a prey to jealousy.

sn: अमर्षण: स्वाः प्रकृतीरभिभूयः परं स्थितः। क्लेशान् मुमुक्षुः परजान् स वै पुरुष उच्यते॥
en: He is called a (true) man who lives after having vanquished his enemy in order to liberate his own subjects from the tyranny of that enemy.

sn: संतोषो वै श्रियं हन्ति हभिमानं च भारत। अनुक्रोशभये चोभे यैर्वृतो नाश्नुते महत्॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, contentment and pride destroy (one's) prosperity. Being engrossed with compassion and fear he can never rise.

sn: न मां प्रीणाति मद्भुक्तं श्रियं दृष्ट्वा युधिष्ठिरे। अति ज्वलन्तीं कौन्तेये विवर्णकरणी मम॥
