en: Seeing the prosperity of Yudhishthira, whatever I enjoy does not gratify or please me. The great and splendid prosperity of the son of Kunti makes me pale.

sn: सपत्नानृध्यतोऽऽत्मानं हीयमानं निशम्य च । अदृश्यामपि कौन्तेयश्रियं पश्यन्निवोद्यताम्॥
en: Though I am not now seeing the greatly effulgent prosperity of the son of Kunti, yet knowing the affluence of the foe and my destitution, I (feel as if I) see it before me. For this reason I am colourless melancholy, pale and emaciated.

sn: तस्मादहं विवर्णश्च दीनश्च हरिणः कृशः। अष्टाशीतिसहस्राणि सातका गृहमेधिनः॥
en: Yudhishthira supports by giving thirty servant maids to each of eighty eight thousands Snataka Brahmanas who lead domestic life.

sn: त्रिंशदासीक एकैको यान् बिभर्ति युधिष्ठिरः। दशान्यानि सहस्राणि नित्यं तत्रानमुत्तमम्। भुञ्जते रुक्मपात्रीभिर्युधिष्ठिरनिवेशने॥
en: Besides these, ten thousand other B:ahmanas daily eat well cooked food from golden plates at the palace of Yudhishthira.

sn: कदलीमृगमोकानि कृष्णश्यामारुणानि च। काम्बोजः प्राहिणोत् तस्मै परार्ध्यानपि कम्बलान्। गजयोषिद्गवाश्वस्य शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः॥ त्रिशतं चोष्ट्रवामीनां शतानि विचरन्त्युत। राजन्या बलिमादाय समेता हि नृपक्षये॥
en: The king of Kamboja sent to him hundreds and thousands of black darkish and red skins of the deer called Kadali, and also blankets of excellent texture. Hundreds and hundreds and thousands and thousands of female elephants, horses and cows and thirty thousand female camels wander (within his palace); the kings brought them all as tribute when they assembled there.

sn: पृथग्विधानि रत्नानि पार्थिवाः पृथिवीपते। आहरन् ऋतुमुख्येऽस्मिन् कुन्तीपुत्राय भूरिशः॥
en: O lord of earth, the kings brought to that foremost of sacrifice heaps of gems and jewels for the son of Kunti,

sn: न क्वचिद्धि मया तादृग् दृष्टपूर्वो न च श्रुतः। यादृग् धनागमो यज्ञे पाण्डुपुत्रस्य धीमतः॥
en: I never heard or saw such enormous wealth as was brought to the sacrifice of the intelligent (son) of Pandu (Yudhishthira).

sn: अपर्यन्तं धनौघं तं दृष्ट्वा शत्रोरहं नृपा शमं नैवाभिगच्छामि चिन्तयानो विशाम्पते।॥
en: O king, seeing that enormous collection of wealth belonging to the enemy. I cannot enjoy peace of mind. 'I am afflicted with their thoughts. O king.

sn: ब्राह्मणा वाटधानाश्च गोमन्तः शतसङ्घशः। त्रिखर्वं बलिमादाय द्वारि तिष्ठन्ति वारिताः॥
en: Being stopped there by the gatekeepers hundreds of Brahmanas, supported by the land presented to them (by Yudhishthira) and possessing wealth of kine, waited at the palace gate with three thousands of millions of tribute.

sn: कमण्डलूनुपादाय जातरूपमयाञ्छुभान्। एतद् धनं समादाय प्रवेशं लेभिरे न च॥
en: Even having brought with them Ghee in golden Kamandalus (sort of water pot), they could not get admission into the palace.

sn: यथैव मधु शक्राय धारयन्त्यमरस्त्रियः। तदस्मै कांस्यमाहार्षीद् वारुणं कलशोदधिः॥
en: Ocean himself brought to him in vessels of white copper Ambrosia which was generated within his waters and which was superior to that which the wives of the immortal (Soma, i.e. flowers and annual plants) produce for Shakra (Indra)

sn: शैक्यं रुक्मसहस्रस्य बहुरत्नविभूषितम्। शङ्खप्रवरमादाय वासुदेवोऽभिषिक्तवान्॥
en: Having brought an excellent conch, Vasudeva bathed him (Yudhishthira at the conclusion of the sacrifice) with they holy water brought in one thousand golden jars inlaid with numerous gems.

sn: दृष्ट्वा च मम तत् सर्वं ज्वररूपमिवाभवत्। गृहीत्वा तत् तु गच्छन्ति समुद्रौ पूर्वदक्षिणौ॥ तथैव पश्चिमं यान्ति गृहीत्वा भरतर्षभ। उत्तरं तु न गच्छन्ति विना तात पतत्रिणः॥
en: Seeing all this, I felt myself as if attacked with fever. O best of men, O sire, they (jars) were taken to the eastern and the southern seas. They were also taken to the western sea. But none can go to the northern sea except birds.

sn: तत्र गत्वार्जुनो दण्डमाजहारामितं धनम्। इदं चाद्भुतमत्रासीत् तन्मे निगदतः शृणु॥
en: Arjuna, however, went there and exacted as tribute a vast quantity of wealth. There happened another wonderful incident, which I shall describe to you. Listen to it.

sn: पूर्णे शतसहस्रे तु विप्राणां परिविष्यताम्। स्थापिता तत्र संज्ञाभूच्छलो ध्मायति नित्यशः॥
en: When (full) one lac Brahmanas were every day fed, it was arranged (to notify) the fact by blowing conchs in a chorus.

sn: मुहुर्मुहुः प्रणदतस्तस्य शङ्खस्य भारत। अनिशं शब्दमश्रौषं ततो रोमाणि मेऽहषन्॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, I continually heard (choruses of) conchs blown; and that too often repeatedly. It each time indicated that one lac Brahmanas had been fed. Having heard these sounds, my hairs stood on end.

sn: पार्थिवैर्बहुभिः कीर्णमुपस्थानं दिदृक्षुभिः। अशोभत महाराज नक्षत्रै?रिवामला॥
en: O great king, that palatial grounds crowded with many kings who came there as spectators, looked as beautiful as the cloudless sky studded with stars.

sn: सर्वरत्नान्युपादाय पार्थिवा वै जनेश्वर। यज्ञे तस्य महाराज पाण्डुपुत्रस्य धीमतः॥
en: O ruler of men, O great king, the monarchs came to the sacrifice of the wise son of Pandu, bringing with them every king of wealth.

sn: वैश्या इव महीपाला द्विजातिपरिवेषकाः। न सा श्रीर्देवराजस्य यमस्य वरुणस्य च। गुह्यकाधिपतेर्वापि या श्री राजन् युधिष्ठिरे॥
en: Like the Vaishyas the kings became the distributors of food to the Brahmanas. Such wealth does not belong even to the king of the celestials (Indra) or to Yama or to Varuna,

sn: तां दृष्ट्वा पाण्डुपुत्रस्य श्रियं परमिकामहम्। शान्ति न परिगच्छामि दह्यमानेन चेतसा॥
en: Or to the lord of the Guhyakas, as belongs to Yudhishthira. O king, seeing that great prosperity of the son of Pandu, my heart is burning. I cannot get peace (of mind).

sn: शकुनिरुवाच यामेतामतुलां लक्ष्मी दृष्टवानसि पाण्डवे। तस्याः प्राप्तावुपायं मे शृणु सत्यपराक्रम॥
en: Shakuni said O hero whose prowess is truth, hear the means by which you can obtain the matchless prosperity that you have seen in the Pandava.

sn: अहमक्षेष्वभिज्ञातः पृथिव्यामपि भारत। हृदयज्ञः पणज्ञश्च विशेषज्ञश्च देवने॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, I am an adept in dice, superior to all in the world. I can ascertain the success or otherwise of every throw, and also when to stake and when not to stake. I have special knowledge of the play.

sn: द्यूतप्रियश्च कौन्तेयो न च जानाति देवितुम्। आहूतश्चैष्यति व्यक्तं द्यूतादपि रणादपि॥
en: The son of Kunti (Yudhishthira) is also fond of the play, although he possesses little skill in it. He is sure to come, if challenged to pay or to fight.

sn: नियतं तं विजेष्यामि कृत्वा तु कपटं विभो। आनयामि समृद्धिं तां दिव्यां चोपाह्वयस्व तम्॥
en: O lord, I shall always defeat him at every throw by practising deception. I shall win all.. his celestial-like wealth; and you will (then) be able to enjoy it.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्तः शकुनिना राजा दुर्योधनस्ततः। धृतराष्ट्रमिदं वाक्यमपदान्तरमब्रवीत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having been thus addressed by Shakuni, the king Duryodhana, without allowing a moment to elapse, spoke thus to Dhritarashtra.

sn: अयमुत्सहते राजच्छियमाहर्तुमक्षवित्। द्यूतेन पाण्डुपुत्रस्य तदनुज्ञातुमर्हसि॥ .
en: O king, this (Shakuni) is an adept in dice; he is ready to win at dice the wealth of the sons of Pandu. You should grant him permission.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच क्षत्ता मन्त्री महाप्राज्ञः स्थितो यस्यास्मि शासने। तेन संगम्य वेत्स्यामि कार्यस्यास्य विनिश्चयम्॥
en: Dhritarashtra says I always follow the counsel of greatly intelligent Khattwa (Vidura), my minister. Having consulted with him, I shall inform you my decision (in this matter).

sn: स हि धर्मं पुरस्कृत्य दीर्घदर्शी परं हितम्। उभयोः पक्षयोर्युक्तं वक्ष्यत्यर्थविनिश्चयम्॥
en: He is endued with great foresight; keeping the rules of morality before his eyes, he will point out what is good and what is proper for both parties and what should be done in this matter.

sn: दुर्योधन उवाच निवर्तयिष्यति त्वासौ यदि क्षत्ता समेष्यति। निवृत्ते त्वयि राजेन्द्र मरिष्येऽहमसंशयम्॥
en: Duryodhana said If you consult with Kshatta (Vidura) he will make you desist (from it). O king of kings, if you desist (from this), I will certainly kill myself.

sn: स त्वं मयि मृते राजन् विदुरेण सुखी भव। भोक्ष्यसे पृथिीं कृत्स्ना किं मया त्वं करिष्यसि॥
en: O king, when I am dead, be happy with Vidura. Enjoy then the whole earth. What need you have with me?

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच आर्तवाक्यं तु तत् तस्य प्रणयोक्तं निशम्य सः। धृतराष्ट्रोऽब्रवीत् प्रेष्यान् दुर्योधनमते स्थितः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Hearing his (Duryodhana's) words of affection. Dhritarashtra, ever ready to do what Duryodhana said, commanded his servant thus.

sn: स्थूणासहस्रैर्वृहतीं शतद्वारा सभां मम। मनोरमां दर्शनीयामाशु कुर्वन्तु शिल्पिनः॥
en: Dhritarashtra said. Let artifices be employed to crect without delay a delightful, charming and spacious Sabha with one hundred doors and with one thousand pillars.

sn: ततः संस्तीर्य रत्नस्तां तक्ष्ण आनाय्य सर्वशः। सुकृतां सुप्रवेशां च निवेदयत मे शनैः॥
en: Having brought carpenters and joiners, set jewels and precious stones all over its walls. Make it handsome and easy of access; and then inform me when every thing is complete.

sn: दुर्योधनस्य शान्त्यर्थमिति निश्चित्य भूमिपः। धृतराष्ट्रो महाराज प्राहिणोद् विदुराय वै॥
en: Vaishampayana said O great king, having resolved to pacify Duryodhana the ruler of earth, Dhritarashtra, sent men to Vidura to summon him (before his presence).

sn: अपृष्ट्वा विदुरं स्वस्य नासीत् कश्चिद् विनिश्चयः। द्यूते दोषांश्च जानन् स पुत्रस्नेहादकृष्यत॥
en: Because without asking Vidura, he (Dhritarashtra) never framed any resolution. Knowing (full well) the evils of gambling, he was still attracted towards it out of his fondness for his son.

sn: तच्छ्रुत्वा विदुरो धीमान् कलिद्वामुपस्थितम्। विनाशमुखमुत्पन्नं धृतराष्ट्रमुपाद्रवत्॥
en: Having heard this, the intelligent Vidura knew that the arrival of Kali (Yuga) is near at hand. Seeing also the way to destruction (of the Kuru race) about to the opened, he soon came to Dhritarashtra.

sn: सोऽभिगम्य महात्मानं भ्राता भ्रातरमग्रजम्। मूर्धा प्रणम्य चरणाविदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Coming to his illustrious eldest brother and bowing his head to his feet, he thus spoke to him.

sn: विदुर उवाच नाभिनन्दामि ते राजन् व्यवसायमिमं प्रभो। पुत्रैर्भेदो यथा न स्याद् द्यूतहेतोस्तथा कुरु॥
en: Vidura said O king, O lord, I do not approve of the resolution you have formed. You should act in such a way that no dispute may arise amongst your sons on account of this gambling.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच क्षत्तः पुत्रेषु पुत्रैर्मे कलहो न भविष्यति। यदि देवाः प्रसादं नः करिष्यन्ति न संशयः॥
en: Dhritarashtra said O Khattwa, there is no doubt that if the gods are propitious to us, no dispute will ever arise amongst my children.

sn: अशुभं वा शुभं वापि हितं वा यदि वाहितम्। प्रवर्ततां सुहृद्यूतं दिष्टमेतन्न संशयः॥
en: Auspicious or not auspicious, beneficial or not beneficial, let this friendly gambling match be held. This is certainly what Fate has ordained (for us).

sn: मयि संनिहिते द्रोणे भीष्मे त्वयि च भारत। अनयो दैवविहितो न कथंचिद् भविष्यति॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, when Drona, Bhishma, you and I will be near at hand, no evil, can possible happen, even if Fate has ordained it.

sn: गच्छ त्वं रथमास्थाय हयैर्वातसमैर्जवे। खाण्डवप्रस्थमद्यैव समानय युधिष्ठिरम्॥
en: Go ascending a car yoked with horses possessing the speed of wind, so that you may reach Khandavaprastha day. Bring Yudhishthira with you.

sn: न वाच्यो व्यवसायो मे विदुरैतद् ब्रवीमि ते। दैवमेव परं मन्ये येनैतदुपपद्यते॥
en: O Vidura, I tell you, this is my resolution. Do not tell me any thing. I regard Fate as supreme; she brings all this.

sn: इत्युक्तो विदुरो धीमान् नेदमस्तीति चिन्तयन्। आपगेयं महाप्राज्ञमभ्यगच्छत् सुदुःखितः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having heard this, and having concluded that his race was doomed, the intelligent to Vidura went to the greatly wise Bhishma in great sorrow.

sn: जनमेजय उवाच कथं समभवद् द्यूतं भ्रातृणां तन्महात्ययम्। यत्र तद् व्यसनं प्राप्तं पाण्डवैर्म पितामहैः॥
en: Janamejaya said How did that gambling take place, the play which was full of such evils to the brothers and which plunged my grandsires into such sorrow?

sn: के च तत्र सभास्तारा राजानो ब्रह्मवित्तम। के चैनमन्वमोदन्त के चैनं प्रत्यषेधयन्॥
en: O best of all Veda-knowing men, who were the kings that were present in that Sabha and who amongst them approved of the play and who forbade it?

sn: विस्तरेणैतदिच्छामि कथ्यमानं त्वया द्विजा मूलं ह्येतद् विनाशस्य पृथिव्या द्विजसत्तम॥
en: O sinless one, O foremost of the twice borne. I desire to hear narrated by you in detail all this which became the cause of the destruction of all the world.

sn: सौतिरुवाच एवमुक्तस्ततो राजा व्यासशिष्यः प्रतापवान्। आचचक्षेऽथ यद् वृत्तं तत् सर्वं वेदतत्त्ववित्॥
en: Sauti said Having been thus addressed by the king, the powerful disciple of Vyasa, (Vaishampayana), learned in all the Vedas, narrated every thing as it happened.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच शृणु मे विस्तरेणेमां कथां भारतसत्तम। भूय एव महाराज यदि ते श्रवणे मतिः॥
en: Vaishampayana said O best of the Bharata race, O great king, if you desire to hear it, listen to it. I narrate all this in detail.

sn: विदुरस्य मतिं ज्ञात्वा धृतराष्ट्रोऽम्बिकासुतः। दुर्योधनमिदं वाक्यमुवाच विजने पुनः॥
en: Knowing the opinion of Vidura, the son of Ambika, Dhritarashtra, thus spoke to Duryodhana in private.

sn: अलं द्यूतेन गान्धारे विदुरो न प्रशंसति। न ह्यसौ सुमहाबुद्धिरहितं नो वदिष्यति॥
en: Dhritarashtra said O son of Gandhara, there is no need of playing dice. Vidura does not praise it. That greatly intelligent man will never give me advice that is not good for me.

sn: हितं हि परमं मन्ये विदुरो यत् प्रभाषते। क्रियतां पुत्र तत् सर्वमेतन्मन्ये हितं तव॥
en: I consider that what Vidura said is greatly beneficial to me. O son, do it; for I consider it to be for your good also.

sn: देवर्षिर्वासवगुरुर्देवराजाय धीमते। यत् प्राह शास्त्रं भगवान् बृहस्पतिरुदारधीः। तद् वेद विदुरः सर्वं सरहस्यं महाकविः॥
en: The greatly learned man, Vidura, knows all the sciences with their mysteries which the illustrious, learned and wise Brihaspati, the great Rishi who is the preceptor of Vasava (Indra), taught to the intelligent king of the immortals.

sn: स्थितस्तु वचने तस्य सदाहमपि पुत्रका विदुरो वापि मेधावी कुरूणां प्रवरो मतः॥
en: O son, I always follow his counsel. The greatly wise Vidura is considered to be the foremost of the Kurus.

sn: उद्धवो वा महाबुद्धिवृष्णीनामर्चितो नृप। तदलं पुत्र द्यूतेन छूते भेदो हि दृश्यते॥
en: As the greatly intelligent Udhava (is considered to be the foremost) of the Vrishnis. O son, O prince, have nothing with gambling. Dissension is the evident result of gambling.

sn: भेदे विनाशो राज्यस्य तत् पुत्र परिवर्जय। पित्रा मात्रा च पुत्रस्य यद् वै कार्यं परं स्मृतम्॥ प्राप्तस्त्वमसि तन्नाम पितृपैतामहं पदम्। अधीतवान् कृती शास्त्रे लालितः सततं गृहे॥
en: Dissension causes ruin to a kingdom. O son, therefore, abandon (the idea of gambling). O son, you have obtained all that is hard to be obtained from the father and the mother. You have obtained the rank and the possessions of your ancestors, you are taught, you are made learned in the Shastras, you were carefully brought up in the house.

sn: भ्रातृज्येष्ठः स्थितो राज्ये विन्दसे किं न शोभनम्। पृथग्जनैरलभ्यं यद् भोजनाच्छादनं परम्॥
en: You are the eldest amongst all your brothers, you are placed over the kingdom; why do you not consider yourself fortunate and happy? You get the very best kind of food and robes, unobtainable by ordinary men.

sn: तत् प्राप्तोऽसि महाबाहो कस्माच्छोचसि पुत्रका स्फीतं राष्ट्रं महाबाहो पितृपैतामहं महत्॥ नित्यमाज्ञापयन् भासि दिवि देवेश्वरो यथा। तस्य ते विदितप्रज्ञ शोकमूलमिदं कथम्। समुत्थितं दुःखकरं यन्मे शंसितुमर्हसि॥
en: O mighty armed hero, O son, having obtained all this, why do you grieve? O mighty armed hero, ruling over your large ancestral kingdom swelling with people and wealth, you shine as splendidly as the chief of the celestials in heaven. O possessor of knowledge, you should tell me what can be the root of your grief which has made you so melancholy.

sn: दुर्योधन उवाच अश्नाम्याच्छादयामीति प्रपश्यन् पापपूरुषः। नामर्षं कुरुते यस्तु पुरुषः सोऽधमः स्मृतः॥
en: Duryodhana said I am a sinful wretch that I eat and dress, though see the prosperity of the enemy. It has been said that a man is a wretch who does not feel jealousy at the sight of his enemy's prosperity.

sn: न मां प्रीणाति राजेन्द्र लक्ष्मी: साधारणी विभो। ज्वलितामेव कौन्तेये श्रियं दृष्ट्वा च विव्यथे॥
en: O king of kings, O lord, this ordinary prosperity does not please me. I am greatly pained on seeing the burning prosperity of the son of Kunti.

sn: सर्वां च पृथिवीं चैव युधिष्ठिरवशानुगाम्। स्थिरोऽस्मि योऽहं जीवामि दुःखादेतद् ब्रवीमि ते।।
en: I tell you, my life must be very hard to be parted with from my body, and therefore I am still alive after seeing all the kings of the world enduring the sway of Yudhishthira.

sn: आवर्जिता इवाभान्ति नीपाश्चित्रककौकुराः। कारस्कारा लोहजङ्घा युधिष्ठिरनिवेशने॥
en: The Nipas, the Chitrakas, the Kukuras, the Karaskaras and the Lohajanghas are living in the Yudhishthira's palace like bondsmen.

sn: हिमवत्सागरानूपाः सर्वे रत्नाकरास्तथा। अन्त्याः सर्वे पर्युदस्ता युधिष्ठिरनिवेशने॥
en: The Himalayas, the ocean, the regions on the sea-shore and the numberless other regions that yield gems and jewels have all acknowledged their inferiority to the palace of Yudhishthira.

sn: ज्येष्ठोऽयमिति मां मत्वा श्रेष्ठश्चेति विशाम्पते। युधिष्ठिरेण सत्कृत्य युक्तो रत्नपरिग्रहे॥
en: O king, on consideration of my being the eldest and the foremost. I was engaged in receiving the gems and jewels (brought as tribute by the kings).

sn: उपस्थितानां रत्नानां श्रेष्ठानामर्घहारिणाम्। नादृश्यत परः पारो नापरस्तत्र भारत॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, the limit and the like of the excellent and the invaluable jewels that were brought there have never been seen.

sn: न मे हस्तः समभवद् वसु तत् प्रतिगृहणतः। अतिष्ठन्त मयि श्रान्ते गृह्य दूराहृतं वसु॥
en: O king, my hands were tired to receive that wealth. When I became tired they that brought that wealth from distant places waited (till I could resume my task).

sn: कृतां विन्दुसरोरत्नैर्मयेन स्फाटिकच्छदाम्। अपश्यं नलिनी पूर्णामुदकस्येव भारत॥
en: Having brought jewels from Bindu lake, Maya built a lake-like ground made of crystal. O descendant of Bharata, seeing the place full of lotuses, I mistook it for waster.

sn: वस्त्रमुत्कर्षति मयि प्राहसत् स वृकोदरः। शत्रोर्ऋद्धिविशेषेण विमूढं रत्नवर्जितम्॥
en: Seeing me draw up my clothes, Vrikodara (Bhima) laughed at me, considering me as destitute of jewels and deprived of my reason at the affluence of the enemy.

sn: तत्र स्म यदि शक्तः स्यां पातयेऽहं वृकोदरम्। यदि कुर्यां समारम्भं भीमं हन्तुं नराधिप।॥
en: "O king, if I had the ability, I would have instantly killed Vrikodara (for his laughter), O king, if we now try to kill Bhima.

sn: शिशुपाल इवास्माकं गतिः स्यान्नात्र संशयः। सपनेनावहासो मे स मां दहति भारत॥
en: Our fate will be certainly as that of Shishupala. O descendant of Bharata, that insult by the enemy burns me.

sn: पुनश्च तादृशीमेव वापी जलजशालिनीम्। मत्वा शिलासमां तोये पतितोऽस्मि नराधिप॥
en: O king, again seeing a similar lake full of water, I mistook it for a crystal surface, and I fell into it.

sn: तत्र मां प्राहसत् कृष्णः पार्थेन सह सुस्वरम्। द्रौपदी च सह स्त्रीभिर्व्यथयन्ती मनो मम॥
en: At this Bhima with Partha (Arjuna) laughed aloud, and Draupadi with other females laughed also. This greatly pains my heart.

sn: क्लिन्नवस्त्रस्य तु जले किंकरा राजनोदिताः। ददुर्वासांसि मेऽन्यानि तच्च दुःखं परं मम॥
en: My robes having been wet, the servants gave me other clothes at the command of the king (Yudhishthira). That also is my great sorrow.

sn: प्रलम्भं च शृणुष्वान्यद् वदतो मे नराधिप। अद्वारेण विनिर्गच्छन् द्वारसंस्थानरूपिणा। अभिहत्य शिलां भूयो ललाटेनास्मि विक्षतः॥ तत्र मां यमजौ दूरादालोक्याभिहतं तदा। बाहुभिः परिगृह्णीतां शोचन्तौ सहितावुभौ॥
en: O king, listen to another mistake (I made) which I speak of. In attempting to pass through what was exactly of the shape of a door, but which was not really a door, I struck my forehead against it and injured myself. Thereupon the twins (Nakula and Sahadeva), seeing from a distance that I was struck, came and supported me in their arms, and expressed great concern (for my injury).

sn: उवाच सहदेवस्तु तत्र मां विस्मयन्निव। इदं द्वारमितो गच्छ राजनिति पुनः पुनः॥
en: Sahadeva then again and again told me with smiles, “O king, this is the door, Go this way.”

sn: भीमसेनेन तत्रोक्तो धृतराष्टात्मजेति च। सम्बोध्य प्रहसित्वा च इतो द्वारं नराधिप॥
en: O king, Bhimasena laughed aloud, and addressing me, he spoke thus to me. "O son of Dhritarashtra, this is the doer".

sn: नामधेयानि रत्नानां पुरस्तान्न श्रुतानि मे। यानि दृष्टानि मे तस्यां मनस्तपति तच्च मे॥
en: I had not even heard the names of the gems that I saw in that palace. It is for this reason my heart is so much burning.

sn: दुर्योधन उवाच यन्मया पाण्डवेयानां दृष्टं तच्छृणु भारत। आहृतं भूमिपालैहि वसु मुख्यं ततस्ततः॥
en: Duryodhana said O descendant of Bharata hear about all the best of wealth that belongs to the Pandavas and that was brought by the kings of earth one after another.

sn: नाविदं मूढमात्मानं दृष्ट्वाहं तदरेर्धनम्। फलतो भूमितो वापि प्रतिपद्यस्व भारत॥ और्णान् बैलान् वार्षदंशाञ्जातरूपपरिष्कृतान्। प्रावाराजिनमुख्यांश्च काम्बोजः प्रददौ बहून्॥
en: Seeing that wealth of the enemy. I lost my reason, and I scarcely knew myself O descendant of Bharata, hear as I describe that wealth consisting of both manufactures and the produce of land. The king of Kamboja gave many of the best kinds of skins, woollen blankets, blankets made of the soft fur of mice and other animals living in holes and blankets made of the wool of cats, all inlaid with threads of gold;

sn: अश्वांस्तित्तिरिकल्माषांस्त्रिशतं शुकनासिकान्। उष्ट्रवामीस्त्रिंशतं च पुष्टाः पीलुशमीीङ्गुदैः॥
en: Also three hundred horses of the Tittiri and Kalmasha kinds, all possessing nose like the parrots; also three hundred camels, three hundred female asses, all fattened with olive and Pilusha.

sn: गोवासना ब्राह्मणाश्च दासनीयाश्च सर्वशः। प्रीत्यर्थं ते महाराज धर्मराज्ञो महात्मनः॥
en: O great king, many Brahmanas, who rear cattle and who are fit to be engaged in menial service, in order to gratify the illustrious Dharmaraja (Yudhishthira) waited,

sn: त्रिखर्वं बलिमादाय द्वारि तिष्ठन्ति वारिताः। ब्राह्मणा वाटधानाच गोमन्तः शतसङ्घशः॥ कमण्डलूनुपादाय जातरूपमयाञ्छुभान्। एवं बलिं समादाय प्रवेशं लेभिरे न च॥ शतं दासीसहस्राणां कासिकनिवासिनाम्॥
en: At the gate with hundred millions of tribute and were denied admittance. Hundreds of Brahmanas, possessing wealth of kine and living upon the lands that Yudhishthira gave them, came there with their handsome golden Kamandalus (water-pot) filled with Ghee. Though they brought such tribute, yet they were refused admittance. Hundred thousands of serving maids of the Karpasika country.

sn: श्यामास्तन्व्यो दीर्घकेश्यो हेमाभरणभूषिताः। शूद्रा विप्रोत्तमाएणि राङ्कवाण्यजिनानि च॥ बलिं च कृत्स्नमादाय भरुकच्छनिवासिनः। उपनिन्युर्महाराज हयान् गान्धारदेशजान्॥
en: All of beautiful features of slender waist, and of long hair, and all adorned with golden ornaments, also many skins of Ranku deer worthy of the best Brahmanas, and also horses of the Gandhara country, were brought by the Shudra kings who lived in the regions on the coast of the sea. O great king,

sn: इन्द्रकृष्टैर्वतयन्ति धान्यैर्ये च नदीमुखैः। समुद्रनिष्कुटे जाताः पारेसिन्धु च मानवाः॥ ते वैरामां: पारदाश्च आभीराः कितवैः सह। विविधं बलिमादाय रत्नानि विविधानि च॥ अजाविकं गोहिरण्यं खरोष्ट्र फलजं मधु। कम्बलान् विविधांश्चैव द्वारि तिष्ठन्ति वारिताः॥
en: The Vairamas, the Paradas, the Tungas and the Kitavas who lived upon crops that depended on water from the sky or of the river, and those who were born in regions on these shore, in woodlands or in countries on the other side of the sea, being refused admittance waited at the gate, though they brought with them goats and kine, asses and camels, vegetable honey and blankets, jewels and gems of various kinds.

sn: प्राग्ज्योतिषाधिपः शूरो म्लेच्छानामधिपो बली। यवनैः सहितो राजा भगदत्तो महारथः॥ आजानेयान् हयाञ्छीघ्रानादायानिलरंहसः। बलिं च कृत्स्नमादाय द्वारि तिष्ठति वारितः॥
en: The brave ruler of Pragjyotisha, and the powerful king of the Mlecchas the car-warrior king Bhagadatta, waited at the gate at the head of a large number of Yavanas. He too was unable to enter, though he brought a large tribute comprising of horses of the best breed and of the speed of the wind.

sn: अश्मसारमयं भाण्डं शुद्धदन्तत्सरूनसीन्। प्राग्ज्योतिषाधिपो दत्त्वा भगदत्तोऽव्रजत् तदा॥
en: Thereupon the king of Pragjyotisha Bhagadatta had to go away from the gate, giving away a number of swords with handles made of the purest ivory and well-adorned with diamonds and every kind of gems.

sn: व्यक्षांस्त्र्यक्षाल्ललाटाक्षान् नानादिग्भ्यः समागतान् औष्णीकानन्तवासांश्च रोमकान् पुरुषादकान्॥
en: Many races, coming from various regions, some with eyes on the forehead, and also the Aushnikas, the Nishadas, the Romakas, also those that were cannibals.

sn: एकपादांश्च तत्राहमपश्यं द्वारि वारितान्। राजानो बलिमादाय नानावर्णाननेकशः॥ कृष्णग्रीवान् महाकायान् रासभान् दूरपातिनः। आजहुर्दशसाहस्रान् विनीतान् दिक्षु विश्रुतान्॥
en: And also those that possessed only one leg. I saw, were refused admittance at the gate. These kings brought as tribute ten thousand celebrated asses of various and innumerable colours, with black necks and huge bodies, with great speed and much docility.

sn: प्रमाणरागसम्पन्नान् वक्षुतीरसमुद्भवान्। बल्यर्थं ददतस्तस्मै हिरण्यं रजतं बहु॥
en: They were all of good size and delightful colour; they were all born on the coast and shore the Vanku, of all these kings gave much gold and silver.

sn: दत्त्वा प्रवेशं प्राप्तास्ते युधिष्ठिरनिवेशने। इन्द्रगोपकवर्णाभाञ्छुकवर्णान् मनोजवान्॥ तथैवेन्द्रायुधनिभान् संध्याभ्रसदृशानपि। अनेकवर्णानारण्यान् गृहीत्वाश्वान् महाजवान्॥ जातरूपमनर्घ्यं च ददुस्तस्यैकपादकाः। चीनाञ्छकांस्तथा चौड्रान् बर्बरान् वनवासिनः॥
en: Having given so much, tribute they got admission to the palace of Yudhishthira. the one legged people who came there gave him (Yudhishthira) many wild horses, some red as coccinella (a sort of red insect) and some white, some of the rain-bow colour, some looking like evening clouds and some of variegated colour, and all possessing the speed of mind. They also gave to the king much gold of superior quality. Innumerable chins, Shakas, Aodaras and many barbarians and dwellers of forest,

sn: वार्ष्णेयान् हारहूणांश्च कृष्णान् हैमवतांस्तथा। नीपानूपानधिगतान् विविधान् द्वारवारितान्॥
en: The Vrishnis, the Harahunas, the dark people of the Himalayas, the Nipas and the people living on the sea coast, were all refused admittance at the gate.

sn: बल्यर्थं ददतस्तस्य नानारूपाननेकशः। कृष्णग्रीवान् महाकायान् रासभाञ्छतपातिनः। अहार्पर्दशसाहस्रान् विनीतान् दिक्षु विश्रुतान्॥ प्रमाणरागस्पर्शाढ्यं बाल्हीचीनसमुद्भवम्। और्णं च राङ्कवं चैव कीटजं पट्टजं तथा॥
en: They gave as tribute ten thousand various asses of good size and black necks and capable of daily running two thousand miles, all of many shapes and all well-trained and celebrated over the world, all possessing symmetrical proportion and excellent colour, they skins being pleasant to the touch, also many woollen blankets made in chin, also many skins of Ranku deer, and also many clothes made of Jute and many others made of the threads of insects.

sn: कुटीकृतं तथैवात्र कमलाभं सहस्रशः। श्लक्ष्णं वस्त्रमकार्पासमाविकं मृदु चाजिनम्॥ निशितांश्चैव दीर्घासीनृष्टिशक्तिपरश्वधान्। अपरान्तसमुद्भूतांस्तथैव परशूञ्छितान्॥ रसान् गन्धांश्च विविधान् रत्नानि च सहस्रशः। बलिं च कृत्स्नमादाय द्वारि तिष्ठन्ति वारिताः॥
en: They also gave thousands of other cloths not made of cotton and all possessing the colour of the lotus, being made of smooth and soft texture. They also gave thousands of soft sheepskins, also many sharp and long swords and scimitars, hatches and fine-edged battleaxes, manufactured in the western countries also thousands of perfumes, jewels and gems. But being refused admittance they all waited at the gate.

sn: शकास्तुषाराः कङ्काश्च रोमशाः शृङ्गिणो नराः। महागजान् दूरगमान् गणितानर्बुदान् हयान्॥ शतशश्चैव बहुशः सुवर्णं पद्मसम्मितम्। बलिमादाय विविधं द्वारि तिष्ठन्ति वारिताः॥
en: The Shakas, the Tusharas, the Kankas, the Romakas and the men with horns, bringing with them (as tribute) many large elephants which could go long distance, and also ten thousand horses and also hundreds of millions of gold, waited at the gate being refused admittance.

sn: आसनानि महार्हाणि यानानि शयनानि च। मणिकाञ्चनचित्राणि गजदन्तमयानि च॥ कवचानि विचित्राणि शस्त्राणि विविधानि च। रथांश्च विविधाकाराञ्जातरूपपरिष्कृतान्॥
en: Costly carpets, vehicles and beds, armours of various colours, decked with jewels, gems and ivory, and also weapons of various kinds and cars of various shapes handsomely made and adorned with gold.

sn: हयैर्विनीतैः सम्पन्नान् वैयाघ्रपरिवारितान्। विचित्रांश्च परिस्तोमान् रत्नानि विविधानि च॥
en: Well-trained horses covered with the tiger skins, rich and variegated blankets for covering elephants, various kinds of gems and jewels,

sn: नाराचानर्धनाराचाज्छस्त्राणि विविधानि च। एतद् दत्त्वा महद् द्रव्यं पूर्वदेशाधिपा नृपाः। प्रविष्टा यज्ञसदनं पाण्डवस्य महात्मनः॥
en: Long and short arrows, and various other kinds of weapons such valuable things were presented by the eastern kings. They then entered the sacrificial palace of the illustrious Pandava.

sn: दुर्योधन उवाच दायं तु विविधं तस्मै शृणु मे गदतोऽनघ। यज्ञार्थं राजभिर्दत्तं महान्तं धनसंचयम्॥
en: Duryodhana said O sinless one, listen to me as I describe that large mass of wealth, consisting of various kinds of tributes presented to him (Yudhishthira) by the kings of the earth.

sn: मेरुमन्दरयोर्मध्ये शैलोदामभितो नदीम्। ये ते कीचकवेणूनां छायां रम्यामुपासते॥
en: Those, that live on the banks of the river Shailoda flowing between the mountains Meru and Mandara and enjoy the delicious shade of the groves of Kichaka bamboo,

sn: खसा एकासना ह्यर्हाः प्रदरा दीर्घवेणवः। पारदाश्च कुलिन्दाश्च तङ्गणाः परतङ्गणाः॥
en: Namely (the kings) of the khasas, the Ekasanas, the Arhas, the Pradaras, the Dirghavenus, the Paradas, the Kulindas, the Tanganas, and the other Tanganas,

sn: तद् वै पिपीलिकं नाम उद्धृतं यत् पिपीलिकैः। जातरूपं द्रोणमेयमहायुः पुञ्जशो नृपाः॥
en: Brought as tribute heaps of gold measured in Dronas (jars) and raised from underneath the earth by ants, and therefore called after the ants.

sn: कृष्णाल्ललामांश्चमराज्छुक्लांश्चान्याञ्छशिप्रभान्। हिमवत्पुष्पजं चैव स्वादु क्षौद्रं तथा बहु॥ उत्तरेभ्यः कुरुभ्यश्चाप्यपोढं माल्यमम्बुभिः। उत्तरादपि कैलासादोषधीः सुमहाबलाः॥ पर्वतीया बलिं चान्यमाहृत्य प्रणताः स्थिताः। अजातशत्रोपतेरि तिष्ठन्ति वारिताः॥
en: The powerful mountain tribes, having brought as tribute many soft and black Chamaras and many others as white as the moon-beam, and also sweet honey extracted from the flowers growing on the Himalayas and also from the Mechelia champaka, and also garlands of flowers brought from the land of the northern Kurus, and also various kinds of plants from the north, even from the Kailasa (mountain), waited at the gate with their heads down, being refused admittance.

sn: ये परार्धे हिमवतः सूर्योदयगिरौ नृपाः। कारूषे च समुद्रान्ते लौहित्यमभितश्च ये॥ फलमूलाशना ये च किराताश्चर्मवाससः। क्रूरशस्त्रा: क्रूरकृतस्तांश्च पश्याम्यहं प्रभो॥
en: O lord, I also saw many Kirata kings, armed with cruel weapons and ever engaged in cruel deeds, living on fruits and roots and wearing skins, who live on the slopes of the Himalayas and the mountain from behind which the sun rises and in the Karusha country on the sea coast and on the both sides of the Lohitya mountain.

sn: चन्दनागुरुकाष्ठानां भारान् कालीयकस्य च। चर्मरत्नसुवर्णानां गन्धानां चैव राशयः॥ कैरातकीनामयुतं दासीनां च विशाम्पते। आहृत्य रमणीयार्थान् दूरजान् मृगपक्षिणः॥
en: O king, having brought loads of Chandana and alone and also black aloes and heaps of valuable skins and much wealth and perfumes, and also ten thousand serving maids of the Kirata race, and many beautiful birds and animals of remote countries.

sn: निचितं पर्वतेभ्यश्च हिरण्यं भूरिवर्चसम्। बलिं च कृत्स्नमादाय द्वारि तिष्ठन्ति वारिताः॥
en: And also much gold of great splendour procured from the mountains, waited at the gate, being refused admittance.

sn: कैराता दरदा दर्वाः शूरा वै यमकास्तथा। औदुम्बरा दुर्विभागाः पारदा बाह्निकैः सह॥
en: The Kiratas, the Daradas, the Darvas, the Shiras, the Vaiamakas, the Audumbaras, the Durvibhagas, the Paradas the Valhikas.

sn: काश्मीराश्च कुमाराश्च घोरका हंसकायनाः। शिवित्रिगर्तयौधेया राजन्या भद्रकेकयाः॥
en: The Kashmiras, the Kumaras, the Ghorakas, the Hansakayanas, the Shibis the Trigartas, the Yaudheyas, the rulers of the Madras, the Kaikeyas,

sn: अम्बष्ठाः कौकुरास्ताा वस्त्रपाः पह्नवैः सह। वशातलाश्च मौलेयाः सह क्षुद्रकमालवैः॥
en: The Ambashthas, the Kaukuras, the Tarkshyas, the Vastrapas, with the Pahlvas the Vashatalas, the Mauleyas, the Kshudrakas, the Malavas,

sn: शौण्डिकाः कुकुराश्चैव शकाश्चैव विशाम्पते। अङ्गा वङ्गाश्च पुण्ड्राश्च शाणवत्या गयास्तथा॥
en: O king, the Paundrayas, the Kukkuras, the Shakas, the Angas, the Vangas, the Pundras, the Shanavatyas and the Gayas,

sn: सुजातयः श्रेणिमन्तः श्रेयांसः शस्त्रधारिणः। अहार्षुः क्षत्रिया वित्तं शतशोऽजातशत्रवे॥
en: These well-born, greatly fortunate excellent and well-skilled in arms Kshatriyas brought tribute by hundreds and thousands.

sn: वङ्गाः कलिङ्गा मगधास्ताम्रलिप्ताः सपुण्ड्रकाः। दौवालिकाः सागरकाः पत्रोर्णाः शैशवास्तथा।॥
en: The Vangas, the Kalingas, the Magadhas, the Tamraliptas, the Sapundrakas the Dauvalikas, the Sagarakas, the Patrornas, the Shaishavas,

sn: कर्णप्रावरणाश्चैव बहवस्तत्र भारता तत्रस्था द्वारपालैस्ते प्रोच्यन्ते राजशासनात्। कृतकालाः सुबलयस्ततो द्वारमवाप्स्यथ॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, innumerable Karnapravaranas who came to the gate were told by the gate-keepers at the command of the king (Yudhishthira) that if they could wait and bring good tribute, they would (then) get admittance.

sn: ईषादन्तान् हेमकक्षान् पद्मवर्णान् कुथावृतान्। शैलाभान् नित्यमत्तांश्चाप्यभितः काम्यकं सरः॥ दत्त्वैकैको दश शतान् कुञ्जरान् कवचावृतान्। क्षमावन्त: कुलीनाश्च द्वारेण प्राविशंस्तदा॥
en: They (therefore) each gave one thousand elephants with tusks like the shafts of plough and girdles made of gold and with coverlets of fine blankets of the colour of lotus. They were darkish like rocks and they were always rusty, they were all procured from the banks of the Kamyaka lake and they were covered with defensive armour. They were also very patient and they were all of the best breed. Having made these presents, the kings were admitted (into the sacrificial ground).

sn: एते चान्ये च बहवो गणा दिग्भ्यः समागताः। अन्यैश्चोपाहतान्यत्र रत्नानीह महात्मभिः॥
en: These and many other (kings), coming from various regions, and also others who brought a great mass of gems and jewels, all assembled there.

sn: राजा चित्ररथो नाम गन्धर्वो वासवानुगः। शतानि चत्वार्यददद्धयानां वातरंहसाम्॥
en: The king, named Chitraratha, the friend of Indra, gave five hundred horses with the spread of wind.

sn: तुम्बुरुस्तु प्रमुदितो गन्धर्वो वाजिनां शतम्। आम्रपत्रसवर्णानामददाद्धेममालिनाम्॥
en: The Gandharva Tumburu cheerfully gave one hundred horses of the colour of the mango leaf, all adorned with gold (ornaments).

sn: कृती राजा च कौरव्य शूकराणां विशाम्पते। अददाद् गजरत्नानां शतानि सुबहून्यथ॥
en: O king, O descendant of Kuru, the renowned king of the Shukaras gave many hundreds of valuable elephants.

sn: विराटेन तु मत्स्येन बल्यर्थं हेममालिनाम्। कुञ्जराणां सहस्रे द्वे मत्तानां समुपाहते॥
en: The king of Matsya, Virata, gave as tribute two thousand elephants adorned with gold (ornaments).

sn: पांशुराष्ट्राद् वसुदानो राजा षड्विंशतिं गजान्। अश्वानां च सहस्र द्वे राजन् काञ्चनमालिनाम्॥
en: O monarch, king Vasudana from the kingdom of Pánshu gave twenty six elephants and two thousand horses all adorned with gold (ornaments).

sn: जवसत्त्वोपपन्नानां वयस्थानां नराधिप। बलिं च कृत्स्नमादाय पाण्डवेभ्यो न्यवेदयत्॥
en: O king, they were all endued with speed and strength and they were all in the full vigour of their youth. These and many other wealth he offered to the Pandavas.

sn: यज्ञसेनेन दासीनां सहस्राणि चतुर्दश। दासानामयुतं चैव सदाराणां विशाम्पते। गजयुक्ता महाराज रथाः षड्विंशतिस्तथा॥ राज्यं च कृत्स्नं पार्थेभ्यो यज्ञार्थं वै निवेदितम्। वासुदेवोऽपि वार्ष्णेयो मानं कुर्वन् किरीटिनः॥
en: O king, Yajnasena presented to the sons of Pritha for their sacrifice fourteen thousand serving maids and ten thousands serving men with their wives. O great king, also many hundreds of excellent elephants, twenty six cars with elephants yoked to them and also his whole kingdom. Vasudeva of the Vrishni race (Krishna) in order to increase the dignity of Kiriti Arjuna.

sn: अददाद् गजमुख्यानां सहस्राणि चतुर्दश। आत्मा हि कृष्णः पार्थस्य कृष्णस्यात्मा धनंजयः॥
en: Gave fourteen thousand excellent elephants. Krishna is the soul of Partha (Arjuna), and Dhananjaya (Arjuna) is the soul of Krishna.

sn: यद् ब्रूयादर्जुनः कृष्णं सर्वं कुर्यादसंशयम्। कृष्णो धनंजयस्यार्थे स्वर्गलोकमपि त्यजेत्॥
en: Whatever Arjuna may say Krishna is certain to accomplish. Krishna can abandon heaven itself for the sake of Dhananjaya (Arjuna).

sn: तथैव पार्थः कृष्णार्थे प्राणानपि परित्यजेत्। सुरभीश्चन्दनरसान् हेमकुम्भसमास्थितान्॥
en: Partha also can sacrifice his life for the sake of Krishna. Though, numberless golden jars filled with fragrant Chandana.

sn: मलयाद् दर्दुराच्चैव चन्दनागुरुसंचयान्। मणिरत्नानि भास्वन्ति काञ्चनं सूक्ष्मवस्त्रकम्॥
en: From the Malaya hills and loads of sandals and alone woods from the Daraduras hills, many very costly gems and many fine cloths inlaid with gold.

sn: चोलपाण्ड्यावपि द्वारं न लेभाते ह्युपस्थितौ। समुद्रसारं वैदूर्यं मुक्तासङ्घांस्तथैव च॥
en: Were brought by the kings of Chola and Pandya yet they could not get admittance. That best of sea-born gems, Vaidurya and heap of pearls.

sn: शतशश्च कुथांस्तत्र सिंहलाः समुपाहरन्। संवृता मणिचीरैस्तु श्यामास्ताम्रान्तलोचनाः॥
en: And hundreds of coverlets for elephants were presented by the kings of the Singhalas. Innumerable dark-coloured men with copper coloured eyes, attired with robes adorned with gems.

sn: ता गृहीत्वा नरास्तत्र द्वारि तिष्ठन्ति वारिताः। प्रीत्यर्थं ब्राह्मणाचैव क्षत्रियाच विनिर्जिताः॥ उपाजहुर्विशश्चैव शूद्राः शुश्रूषवस्तथा। प्रीत्या च बहुमानाच्चाप्युपागच्छन् युधिष्ठिरम्॥ सर्वे म्लेच्छाः सर्ववर्णा आदिमध्यान्तजास्तथा। नानादेशसमुत्यैश्च नानाजातिभिरेव च॥
en: Waited at the gate with their presents being refused admittance. In order to gratify (Yudhishthira) many Brahmanas and many Kshatriyas who have been vanquished, Vaishyas and serving Shudras brought tribute from the love and respect of Yudhishthira even all the Mlecchas came to his palace. Men of all orders, good, indifferent and low belonging to various tribes came from various regions.

sn: पर्यस्त इव लोकोऽयं युधिष्ठिरनिवेशने। उच्चावचानुपग्राहान् राजभिः प्रापितान् बहून्॥ शत्रूणां पश्यतो दुःखान्मुमूर्षा मे व्यजायत। भृत्यास्तु ये पाण्डवानां तांस्ते वक्ष्यामि पार्थिव॥
en: And made the palace of Yudhishthira an epitom of all the world. seeing the king offer such excellent and valuable presents, I wish for death from grief. O king, I shall now tell you about the servants of the Pandavas,

sn: येषामामं च पक्वं च संविधत्ते युधिष्ठिरः। अयुतं त्रीणि पद्मानि गजारोहाः ससादिनः॥
en: To whom Yudhishthira supplies both cooked and uncooked food. There are hundred thousand billions of soldiers mounted on elephants, and also horsemen.

sn: रथानामर्बुदं चापि पादाता बहवस्तथा। प्रमीयमाणमामं च पच्यमानं तथैव च॥
en: And also a hundred million of cars and numberless foot-soldiers. At one place raw food grains are being measured out and at another they all being cooked.

sn: विसृज्यमानं चान्यत्र पुण्याहस्वन एव च। नाभुक्तवन्तं नापीतं नालङ्कृतमसत्कृतम्॥ अपश्यं सर्ववर्णानां युधिष्ठिरनिवेशने। अष्टाशीतिसहस्राणि स्नातका गृहमेधिनः॥
en: At another place they are distributed; the sound of festivity is heard every where. I have not seen a single man amongst the four orders who had not got in Yudhishthira's palace food, drink, ornament and reception. Eighty eight thousand Snatakas leading domestic life.

sn: त्रिंशद्दासीक एकैको यान् बिभर्ति युधिष्ठिरः। सुप्रीताः परितुष्टाश्च ते ह्याशंसन्त्यरिक्षयम्॥
en: Were all supported by Yudhishthira who presented each with thirty serving girls. They being thus gratified always pray for the destruction of his foe.

sn: दशान्यानि सहस्राणि यतीनामूर्ध्वरेतसाम्। भुञ्जते रुक्मपात्रीभिर्युधिष्ठिरनिवेशने॥
en: Ten thousand Ascetics with their passions under complete control daily cat in golden plates in Yudhishthira's palace.

sn: अभुक्तं भुक्तवद् वापि सर्वमाकुब्जवामनम्। अबुञ्जाना याज्ञसेनी प्रत्यवैक्षद् विशाम्पते॥
en: O king, Yajnaseni (Draupadi) without herself taking any food, daily sees whether everybody, including even the dwarfs and the deformed has eaten.

sn: द्वौ करौ न प्रयच्छेतां कुन्तीपुत्राय भारत। सम्बन्धिकेन पञ्चालाः सख्येनान्धकवृष्णयः॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, only two (race) do not pay tribute to the son of Kunti, the Panchalas on account of their relationship by marriage and the Andhakas and the Vrishnis on account of their friendship (with the Pandavas).

sn: दुर्योधन उवाच आर्यास्तु ये वै राजानः सत्यसंधा महाव्रताः। पर्याप्तविद्या वक्तारो वेदोक्तावभृथप्लुताः॥
en: Duryodhana Said Those high-souled kings, who are devoted to truth, who are greatly observant of vows, who are vastly learned, who are eloquent, who are learned in the Vedas and their branches and in sacrifices.

sn: धृतिमन्तो ह्रीनिषेवा धर्मात्मानो यशस्विनः। मूर्धाभिषिक्तास्ते चैनं राजानः पर्युपासते॥
en: Who have piety and modesty, who are virtuous-minded, who are renowned and on whom the grand rites of coronation have been performed, all these worship the king.

sn: दक्षिणार्थं समानीता राजभिः कांस्यदोहनाः। आरण्या बहुसाहस्रा अपश्यंस्तत्र तत्र गाः॥
en: As I saw many thousands of wild kine with as many vessels of white copper for milking them, brought there by the kings of the earth to be given away Dakshina (sacrificial presents) by Yudhishthira.

sn: आजहस्तत्र सत्कृत्य स्वयमुद्यम्य भारत। अभिषेकार्थमव्यग्रा भाण्डमुच्चावचं नृपाः॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, many kings with greatest alacrity themselves brought there many excellent jars(of water) for the purpose of bathing the king at the end of the sacrifice.

sn: बाह्रीको रथमाहार्षीज्जाम्बूनदविभूषितम्। सुदक्षिणस्तु युयुजे श्वेतैः काम्बोजजैर्हयैः॥
en: Valhika himself brought there a car decked with gold. Sudakshina himself yoked to it four white horses of the Kamboja kind.

sn: सुनीथः प्रीतिमांश्चैव ह्यनुकर्षं महाबलः। ध्वजं चेदिपतिश्चैवमहार्षीत् स्वयमुद्यतम्॥
en: The greatly strong Sunitha gladly fitted its lower pole and the ruler of Chedi with his own hands took up and fitted its flag-staff.

sn: दाक्षिणात्यः संनहनं स्रगुष्णीषे च मागधः। वसुदानो महेष्वासो गजेन्द्रं षष्टिहायनम्॥ मत्स्यस्त्वक्षान् हेमनद्धानेकलव्य उपानहौ। आवन्त्यस्त्वभिषेकार्थमापो बहुविधास्तथा॥
en: The king of the southern country stood ready with the coat of mail and the Magadha king with garlands of flowers and the headsdress. The great bow-man Vasudeva stood with a sixty years old elephant, the king of Matsya with side-fittings of the cars decked with gold, Ekalavya with the shoes, the king of Avanti with various kinds of water for the final bath.

sn: चेकितान उपासङ्गे धनुः काश्य उपाहरत्। असिं च सुत्सरूं शल्यः शैक्यं काञ्चनभूषणम्॥
en: Chekitana with the Quiver, the king of Kashi with the bow, Shalya with a sword, the hilt and straps of which were inlaid with gold.

sn: अभ्यषिञ्चत् ततो धौम्यो व्यासश्च सुमहातपाः। नारदं च पुरस्कृत्य देवलं चासितं मुनिम्॥
en: Dhaumya and greatly ascetic Vyasa with Narada and Asita's son, Rishi Devala at the head, performed the ceremony of sprinkling sacred water over the king.

sn: प्रीतिमन्त उपातिष्ठन्नभिषेकं महर्षयः। जामदग्न्येन सहितास्तथान्ये वेदपारगाः॥ अभिजग्मुर्महात्मानो मन्त्रवद् भूरिदक्षिणम्। महेन्द्रमिव देवेन्द्रं दिवि सप्तर्षयो यथा॥
en: The great Rishis sat with cheerful heart at the place where the sprinkling ceremony took place. As the seven Rishis approached the chief of the celestials Indra in heaven, so the illustrious Rishis, learned in the Vedas, with the son of Jamadagni, came uttering Mantras to the great Dakshina-giving (Yudhishthira).

sn: अधारयच्छत्रमस्य सात्यकिः सत्यविक्रमः। धनंजयश्च व्यजने भीमसेनश्च पाण्डवः॥
en: The greatly powerful Satyaki held the umbrella and Dhananjaya (Arjuna) and Bhima fanned the Pandava (Yudhishthira).

sn: चामरे चापि शुद्ध द्वे यमौ जगृहतुस्तथा। उपागृहणाद् यमिन्द्राय पुराकल्पे प्रजापतिः॥
en: The twins (Nakula and Sahadeva) held two excellent chamaras in their hands which was presented by Prajapati to Indra in a former Kalpa.

sn: तमस्मै शङ्खमाहादि वारुणं कलशोदधिः। शैक्यं निष्कसहस्रेण सुकृतं विश्वकर्मणा॥
en: That big conch of Varuna which Vishvakarma had constructed with a thousand Nishkas of gold was brought by the Ocean himself.

sn: तेनाभिषिक्तः कृष्णेन तत्र मे कश्मलोऽभवत्। गच्छन्ति पूर्वादपरं समुद्रं चापि दक्षिणम्॥
en: With it Krishna bathed Yudhishthira after the conclusion of the sacrifice. Seeing this I partly lost my senses. People go to the eastern and the western and also the southern seas;

sn: उत्तरं तु न गच्छन्ति विना तात पतत्रिभिः। तत्र स्म दध्मुः शतशः शङ्खान् मङ्गलकारकान्॥ प्राणदन्त समाध्मातास्ततो रोमाणि मेऽहषन्। प्रापतन् भूमिपालाश्च ये तु हीनाः स्वतेजसा॥
en: But, O father, except birds none can go the northern seas. They have spread their dominion even there-for I heard hundreds of conches that had been brought from that region blown indicating auspicious rejoicing. While those conches were simultaneously blown, my hair stood on end; and those among the kings who were weak in strength fell down in a swoon.

sn: धृष्टद्युम्नः पाण्डवाश्च सात्यकिः केशवोऽष्टमः। सत्त्वस्था वीर्यसम्पन्ना ह्यन्योन्यप्रियदर्शनाः॥ विसंज्ञान् भूमिपान् दृष्ट्वा मां च ते प्राहसंस्तदा। ततः प्रहृष्टो बीभत्सुः प्रादाद्धेमविषाणिनाम्॥ शतान्यनडुहां पञ्च द्विजमुख्येषु भारत। न रन्तिदेवो नाभागो यौवनाश्वो मनुर्न च॥
en: O descendant of Bharata Dhrishtadyumna, Satyaki, the Pandavas and Keshava (Krishna), these eight handsome and greatly powerful men having seen the kings deprived of consciousness and myself in that state, laughed aloud. Then Bibhatsu (Arjuna) gave to the foremost of Brahmanas with a cheerful heart five hundred bullocks with their horns covered with gold, Rantideva, Nabhaga, Yauvanashva, Manu.

sn: न च राजा पृथुर्वैन्यो न चाप्यासीद् भगीरथः। ययातिर्नहुषो वापि यथा राजा युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: King Pritha, the son of Vena, Bhagiratha, Yayati or Nahusha was not like the king Yudhishthira.

sn: यथातिमात्रं कौन्तेयः श्रिया परमया युतः। राजसूयमवाप्यैवं हरिचन्द्र इव प्रभुः॥
en: The son of Kunti (Yudhishthira), having completed the Rajasuya sacrifice, obtained the prosperity as was obtained by the lord Harishchandra.

sn: एतां दृष्ट्वा श्रियं पार्थे हरिचन्द्रे यथा विभो। कथं त जीवितं श्रेयो मम पश्यसि भारत॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, o lord, seeing such prosperity in the son of Pritha as that of Harishchandra, I do not find any good in my living any longer.

sn: अन्धेनेव युगं नद्धं विपर्यस्तं नराधिप। कनीयांसो विवर्धन्ते ज्येष्ठा हीयन्त एव च।॥
en: O king, a yoke tied by a blind man becomes loosened. Such is the case with us. The younger ones are growing, while the elder ones are decaying.

sn: एवं दृष्ट्वा नाभिविन्दामि शर्म समीक्षमाणोऽपि कुरुप्रवीर। तेनाहमेवं कृशतां गतश्च विवर्णतां चैव सशोकतां च॥
en: O chief of the Kurus, seeing all this, however, I try to console my mind by thoughts. I cannot enjoy peace. It is for this I am plunged into grief, and I am becoming pale and emaciated.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच त्वं वै ज्येष्ठो ज्यैष्ठिनेयः पुत्र मा पाण्डवान् द्विषः। द्वेष्टा ह्यसुखमादत्ते यथैव निधनं तथा॥
en: Dhritarashtra said You are my eldest son, born of my eldest wife. Therefore, O son, be not jealous of the Pandavas, He who is jealous is always unhappy and suffer the death pangs.

sn: अव्युत्पन्नं समानार्थं तुल्यमित्रं युधिष्ठिरम्। अद्विषन्तं कथं द्विष्यात् त्वादृशो भरतर्षभ॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, Yudhishthira does not know what deception is; he possesses wealth equal to yours; he has your friends for his; and he is not jealous of you. Why then are you jealous of him?

sn: तुल्याभिजनवीर्यश्च कथं भ्रातुः श्रियं नृप। पुत्र कामयसे मोहान्मैवं भूः शाम्य मा शुचः॥
en: O prince, you are equal to Yudhishthira in friends and allies. Why should you then out of folly covet the property of your cousin? Be not so. Cease to be jealous. Do not grieve.

sn: अथ यज्ञविभूतिं तां काङ्क्षसे भरतर्षभ। ऋत्विजस्तव तन्वन्तु सप्ततन्तुं महाध्वरम्॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, if you desire to possess the dignity of performing a sacrifice, let Ritvijas arrange for you the great sacrifice, called Saptatantu.

sn: आहरिष्यन्ति राजानस्तवापि विपुलं धनम्। प्रीत्या च बहुमानाच्च रत्नान्याभरणानि च।॥
en: The kings will then gladly bring (for you) much wealth and many gems and ornaments.

sn: अनार्याचरितं तात परस्वस्पृहणं भृशम्। स्वसंतुष्टः स्वधर्मस्थो यः स वै सुखमेधते॥
en: O son, to covet other's property is exceedingly mean. He, who is contended and is engaged in the practices of his own order, enjoys happiness.

sn: अव्यापारः परार्थेषु नित्योद्योगः स्वकर्मसु। रक्षणं समुपात्तानामेतद् वैभवलक्षणम्॥
en: Not to try to get the wealth of others, to perseveres in one's own affairs and to protect what has been earned, these are the indications of true greatness.

sn: विपत्तिष्वव्यथो दक्षो नित्यमुत्थानवान् नरः। अप्रमत्तो विनीतात्मा नित्यं भद्राणि पश्यति॥
en: He who is unmoved in calamity, is skilled in his own business, is ever exerting, vigilant, and humble will always meet with prosperity.

sn: बाहूनिवैतान् मा छेत्सीः पाण्डुपुत्रास्तथैव ते। भ्रातृणां तद्धनार्थं वै मित्रद्रोहं च मा कुरु॥
en: The Pandavas are like your arms; do not chop off your those arms. do not plunge yourself into internal dissensions coveting the wealth of your brothers.

sn: स्तथैव ते भ्रातृधनं समग्रम्। मित्रद्रोहे तात महानधर्मः पितामहा ये तव तेऽपि तेषाम्॥
en: O prince, do not be jealous of the Pandavas. Your wealth is equal to that of your cousins. To quarrel with one's own friends is a great sin. They who are your grandsires are their grandsires also.

sn: अन्तर्वेद्यां ददद् वित्तं कामाननुभवन् प्रियान्। क्रीडन् स्त्रीभिर्निरातङ्कः प्रशाम्य भरतर्षभ॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, give away (wealth) in charity on the occasions of sacrifices; gratify every dear object of your desire; sport freely in the company of women, and enjoy peace.

sn: दुर्योधन उवाच यस्य नास्ति निजा प्रज्ञा केवलं तं बहुश्रुतः। न स जानाति शास्त्रार्थं दर्वी सूपरसानिव॥
en: Duryodhana said He, who has not personal knowledge, but has merely heard of many things cannot understand the real meaning of the Shastras, like the spoon which has no perception of the taste of the soup it touches.

sn: जानन् वै मोहयसि मां नावि नौरिव संयता। स्वार्थे किं नावधानं ते उताहो द्वेष्टि मां भवान्॥
en: You know everything, but you still confound me. Like a boat tied to another boat, you and I are tied to each other. Are you unmindful of your own interest? Do you entertain hostile feelings towards me?

sn: न सन्तीमे धार्तराष्ट्रा येषां त्वमनुशासिता। भविष्यमर्थमाख्यासि सर्वदा कृत्यमात्मनः॥
en: The sons of Dhritarashtra are doomed to destruction in as much as they are ruled by you. That which should be done at once, you say should be done in future.

sn: परनेयोऽग्रणीर्यस्य स मार्गान् प्रति मुह्यति। पन्थानमनुगच्छेयुः कथं तस्य पदानुगाः॥
en: He often loses his way whose guide follows the instruction of others. How can those who follow him obtain the right path?

sn: राजन् परिणतप्रज्ञो वृद्धसेवी निजेन्द्रियः। प्रतिपन्नान् स्वकार्येषु सम्मोहयसि नो भृशम्॥
en: O king, you are of mature wisdom; you wait on the old, and your passions are also under complete control. You should not confound us, when we are ready to seek our own interest.

sn: लोकवृत्ताद् राजवृत्तमन्यदाह बृहस्पतिः। तस्माद् राज्ञाप्रमत्तेन स्वार्थश्चिन्त्यः सदैव हि॥
en: Brihaspati has said that the usage of kings are different from those of common people. Therefore, kings should always look to their interest with vigilance.

sn: क्षत्रियस्य महाराज जये वृत्तिः समाहिता। स वै धर्मस्त्वधर्मो वा स्ववृत्तौ का परीक्षणा॥
en: O great king, the character of a Kshatriya is to be known from (his) success. Whether sinful or virtuous, what scruples can there be in performing the duties of one's own (caste).

sn: प्रकालयेद् दिशः सर्वाः प्रतोदेनेव सारथिः। प्रत्यमित्रश्रियं दीप्तां जिघृक्षुर्भरतर्षभ।॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, he, who is desirous of securing the blazing prosperity of his enemy, should bring all directions under his subjection, as the charioteer does his steeds with his whip.

sn: प्रच्छन्नो वा प्रकाशो वा योगो योऽरिं प्रबाधते। तद् वै शस्त्रं शस्त्रविदां न शस्त्रं छेदनं स्मृतम्॥
en: The men, skilled in arms, say that the means, either covered or open, which can vanquish the enemy, is to be called the (true) weapon and not that which cuts.

sn: शत्रुश्चैव हि मित्रं च न लेख्यं न च मातृका। यो वै संतापयति यं स शत्रुः प्रोच्यते नृप॥
en: O king, there is no figure or dimension to know who is one's friend and who is one's foe. He who gives pain to the other is to be called by him his enemy.

sn: असंतोषः श्रियो मूलं तस्मात् तं कामयाम्यहम्। समुच्छ्रये यो यतते स राजन् परमो नयः॥
en: O king, discontent is the root of prosperity. Therefore, I desire to have it. O king, he who tries to acquire prosperity is truly a man of policy.

sn: ममत्वं हि न कर्तव्यमैश्वर्ये वा धनेऽपि वा। पूर्वावाप्तं हरन्त्यन्ये राजधर्मं हि तं विदुः॥
en: None should love his wealth and affluence, for the wealth, that has been earned and hoarded, might be plundered. This (such plundering) is the usage of the kings.

sn: अद्रोहसमयं कृत्वा चिच्छेद नमुचेः शिरः। शक्रः साभिमता तस्य रिपौ वृत्तिः सनातनी॥
en: It was during an armistice and also at the time when a pledge was given (not to fight) that Shakra (Indra) cut off the head of Namuchi. As he approved of this eternal usage towards the enemy, he did act in this way.

sn: द्वावेतौ ग्रसते भूमिः सर्पो बिलशयानिव। राजानं चाविरोद्धारं ब्राह्मणं चाप्रवासिनम्॥
en: Like a snake that swallows up frogs and other animals living in holes, the earth swallows up a king who is peaceful and (also) a Brahmana who does not stir out of his house.

sn: नास्ति वै जातितः शत्रुः पुरुषस्य विशाम्पते। येन साधारणी वृत्तिः स शत्रुर्नेतरो जनः॥
en: O king, none can by nature by any person's foe. He, and none else, is one's enemy who has common pursuits with another.

sn: शत्रुपक्षं समृध्यन्तं यो मोहात् समुपेक्षते। व्याधिराज्यायित इव तस्य मूलं छिनत्ति सः॥
en: He who foolishly neglects a growing foe cuts off his root, as a disease which he keeps without treatment (destroys his body).

sn: अल्पोऽपि शरिरत्यर्थं वर्धमानः पराक्रमैः। वल्मीको मूलज इव ग्रसते वृक्षमन्तिकात्॥
en: If a foe, however insignificant he is, be allowed to grow in prowess, he swallows one as the white ants at the root of a tree eat up the tree itself.

sn: आजमीढ रिपोर्लक्ष्मीर्मा ते रोचिष्ट भारत। एष भारः सत्त्ववतां नयः शिरसि विष्ठितः॥
en: O descendant of Ajamida, O descendant of Bharata, let not the enemy's prosperity be acceptable to you. The wise men should carry on their heads this policy like a load.

sn: जन्मवृद्धिमिवार्थानां यो वृद्धिमभिकाडक्षते। एधते ज्ञातिषु स वै सद्यो वृद्धिर्हि विक्रमः॥
en: He, who always wishes for the increase of his wealth, grows and prospers amongst his relatives, as the body naturally grows from the day of birth. Prowess brings speedy growth.

sn: नाप्राप्य पाण्डवैश्वर्यं संशयो मे भविष्यति। अवाप्स्ये वा श्रियं तां हि शयिष्ये वा हतो युधि॥
en: Covet as much as I do the wealth and prosperity of the Pandavas, they have not as yet become my own. I am doubtful about my ability; I am, however, determined to remove my doubt. I will either obtain their wealth or lay my own life in battle.

sn: एतादृशस्य किं मेऽद्य जीवितेन विशाम्पते। वर्धन्ते पाण्डवा नित्यं वयं त्वस्थिरवृद्धयः॥
en: O king, when the state of my mind is such, when the Pandavas are daily growing in prosperity and our possessions are daily decreasing, what do I care for life?

sn: शकुनिरुवाच यां त्वमेतां श्रियं दृष्ट्वा पाण्डुपुत्रे युधिष्ठिरे। तप्यसे तां हरिष्यामि द्यूतेन जयतां वर॥
en: Shakuni said O foremost of all virtuous men, I shall win by dice the prosperity of the son of Pandu, Yudhishthira, seeing which you so much grieve.

sn: आहूयतां परं राजन् कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः। अगत्वा संशयमहमयुद्ध्वा च चमूमुखे॥ अक्षान् क्षिपन्नक्षतः सन् विद्धानविदुषो जये। ग्लहान् धनूंषि मे विद्धि शरानक्षांश्च भारत॥ अक्षाणां हृदयं मे ज्या रथं विद्धि ममास्तरम्॥
en: O king, let the son of Kunti, Yudhishthira, be summoned. A skilfull man, keeping himself uninjured, and by throwing dice may vanquish one that has no skill. O descendant of Bharata, know that betting is my bow, the dice are my arrows, the marks of them (dice) are my bow-strings, and the dice-board is my car.

sn: दुर्योधन उवाच अयमुत्सहते राजञ्छ्यिमाहर्तुमक्षवित्। द्यूतेन पाण्डुपुत्रेभ्यस्तदनुज्ञातुमर्हसि॥
en: Duryodhana said O king, this expert in dice (Shakuni) is ready to win the prosperity of the son of Pandu by means of dice. you ought to give him permission.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच स्थितोऽस्मि शासने भ्रातुर्विदुरस्य महात्मनः। तेन संगम्य वेत्स्यामि कार्यस्यास्य विनिश्चयम्॥
en: Dhritarashtra said I am always obedient to the counsel of my brother, the high-souled Vidura. After consulting with him, I shall settle what should be done in this matter.

sn: दुर्योधन उवाच व्यपनेष्यति ते बुद्धिं विदुरो मुक्तसंशयः। पाण्डवानां हिते युक्तो न तथा मम कौरव॥
en: Duryodhana said O descendant of Kuru, Vidura is always engaged in doing good to the Pandavas. His feelings towards me is not so.

sn: नारभेतान्यसामर्थ्यात् पुरुषः कार्यमात्मनः। मतिसाम्यं द्वयोर्नास्ति कार्येषु कुरुनन्दन॥
en: O descendant of Kuru, he is sure to withdraw your mind from the proposed act. No man should engage in doing a thing by depending on the counsel of another, for the minds of two persons seldom agree in any thing.

sn: भयं परिहरन् मन्द आत्मानं परिपालयन्। वर्षासु क्लिन्नकटवत् तिष्ठन्नेवावसीदति॥
en: The fool who cherishes himself by shunning all causes of fear destroys himself like an insect in the rainy season.

sn: न व्याधयो नापि यमः प्राप्तुं श्रेयः प्रतीक्षते। यावदेव भवेत् कल्पस्तावच्छ्रेयः समाचरेत्॥
en: Neither disease nor Yama (Death) waits till one is in prosperity. Therefore, so long there is life and breath, let us accomplish this purpose.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच सर्वथा पुत्र बलिभिर्विग्रहो मे न रोचते। वैरं विकारं सृजति तद् वै शस्त्रमनायसम्॥
en: Dhritarashtra said O son, enmity with those that are strong is never liked by me. Enmity brings about a change of feelings, and it is itself a weapon, though not made of steel.

sn: अनर्थमर्थं मन्यसे राजपुत्र संग्रन्थनं कलहस्याति घोरम्। तद् वै प्रवृत्तं तु तथा कथंचित् सृजेदसीन् निशितान् सायकांच॥
en: O prince, you consider an act, which will bring in its train the fearful consequences of war and which is really fraught with mischief, as a great blessing. If it once begins, it will produce sharp swords and pointed arrows.

sn: दुर्योधन उवाच स्तत्रात्ययो नास्ति न सम्प्रहारः। तद् रोचतां शकुनेर्वाक्यमद्य सभां क्षिप्रं त्वमिहाज्ञापयस्व॥
en: Duryodhana said The dice has been created and used by the men of ancient time. There is neither destruction nor striking with weapons in it. Therefore, let the counsel of Shakuni be accepted by you today. Let your commands be soon issued for the construction of the Assembly-hall.

sn: स्वर्गद्वारं दीव्यतां नो विशिष्टं तद्वर्तिनां चापि तथैव युक्तम्। भवेदेवं ह्यात्मना तुल्यमेव दुरोदरं पाण्डवैस्त्वं कुरुष्व॥
en: The door of heaven will be opened to us by gambling. It will lead us to great happiness. They that be take to gambling (truly) deserve such good fortune. The Pandavas will be then our equal therefore (allow us to) gamble with them.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच वाक्यं न मे रोचते यत् त्वयोक्तं यत् ते प्रियं तत् क्रियतां नरेन्द्र। पश्चात् तप्स्यसे तदुपाक्रम्य वाक्यं न हीदृशं भावि वचो हि धर्म्यम्॥
en: Dhritarashtra said The words uttered by you do not recommend themselves to me. (However) O ruler of men, do what is agreeable to you. You shall have to repent for acting according to these words, for words fraught with such impiety cannot bring.in prosperity.

sn: दृष्टं ह्येतद् विदुरेणैव सर्वं विपश्चिता बुद्धिविद्यानुगेन। तदेवैतदवशस्याभ्युपैति महद् भयं क्षत्रियजीवधाति॥
en: All this has been foreseen by the learned Vidura, who follows the path of learning end wisdom. the great calamity which would cause the destruction of the Kshatriya-lives comes as willed by Fate.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्त्वा धृतराष्ट्रो मनीषी दैवं मत्वा परमं दुस्तरं च। शशासोच्चैः पुरुषान् पुत्रवाक्ये स्थितो राजा दैवसम्मूढचेताः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having said this the weak-minded Dhritarashtra considered that Fate was supreme (in this world). The king (Dhritarashtra), deprived of his (good) sense by Fate and obedient to the words of his son, loudly commanded his men (saying),

sn: सहस्रस्तम्भां हेमवैदूर्यचित्रां शतद्वारां तोरणस्फाटिकाख्याम्। सभामग्यां क्रोशमात्रायतां मे तद्विस्तारामाशु कुर्वन्तु युक्ताः॥
en: “Build with all care as soon as possible an Assembly-hall of the most beautiful description to be called” crystal-gate palace” with one thousand pillars and one thousand gates, decked with gold and Vaidurya gems and extending two miles in length and two miles in breadth".

sn: श्रुत्वा तस्य त्वरिता निर्विशङ्काः प्राज्ञा दक्षास्तां तदा चक्रुराशु। सर्वद्रव्याण्युपजह्वः सभायां सहस्रशः शिल्पिनश्चैव युक्ताः॥
en: Hearing (the command), thousands of wise and skillful artificial soon built the palace with the greatest alacrity. Having built it, they brought there every king of article.

sn: कालेनाल्पेनाथ निष्ठां गतां तां सभां रम्यां बहुरत्नां विचित्राम्। माचख्युस्ते तस्य राज्ञः प्रतीताः॥
en: They (then) gladly informed the king that the Sabha was ready, it has been made delightful and beautiful, and it had been furnished with every king of gems and covered with many coloured carpets inlaid with gold.

sn: मुवाचेदं धृतराष्ट्रो नरेन्द्रः। युधिष्ठिरं राजपुत्रं च गत्वा मद्वाक्येन क्षिप्रमिहानयस्व॥
en: Thereupon the ruler of men, Dhritarashtra, thus spoke to his chief minister, the learned Vidura, “Going (to Indraprastha), soon bring the prince Yudhishthira here at my command.

sn: सभेयं मे बहुरत्ना विचित्रा शय्यासनैरुपपन्ना महाहैः। सा दृश्यतां भ्रातृभिः सार्धमेत्य सुहृद्यूतं वर्ततामत्र चेति॥ :।
en: Coming here with his brothers, let him see my this beautiful Assembly-hall furnished with countless gems and jewels and with costly beds and carpets. Let then a friendly match at dice by played in that Hall."

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच मतमाज्ञाय पुत्रस्य धृतराष्ट्रो नराधिपः। मत्वा च दुस्तरं दैवमेतद् राजश्चकार ह॥
en: Vaishampayana said The king Dhritarashtra, knowing the inclinations of his son and considering also that Fate was unavoidable, acted in this way.

sn: अन्यायेन तथोक्तस्तु विदुरो विदुषां वरः। नाभ्यनन्दद् वचो भ्रातुर्वचनं चेदमब्रवीत्॥
en: The foremost of all learneu men, Vidura, did not approve the words of his brothers so unjustly uttered; and he then thus spoke to him.

sn: विदुर उवाच नाभिनन्दे नृपते प्रैषमेतं मैवं कृथाः कुलनाशाद् बिभेमि। देतच्छङ्के द्यूतकृते नरेन्द्र॥
en: Vidura said O king, I do not approve of your this command. Do not act thus. I am afraid this will bring about the destruction of our race. O ruler of men, I apprehend that your sons will lose unity from this match at dice; and dissension will certainly arise amongst them.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच नेह क्षत्तः कलहस्तप्स्यते मां न चेद् दैवं प्रतिलोमं भविष्यत्। धाग तु दिष्टस्य वशे किलेदं सर्वं जगच्चेष्टति न स्वतन्त्रतम्॥
en: Dhritarashtra said O Khattwa, if fate be not unfavourable to me, this quarrel will not certainly grieve me. The whole universe moves at the will of its creator, but (it moves) under the controlling influence of Fate. It is not free.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच महाजवैर्बलिभिः साधुदान्तैः। बलान्नियुक्तो धृतराष्ट्रेण राज्ञा मनीषिणां पाण्डवानां सकाशे॥
en: Vaishampayana said Thus commanded against his will by king Dhritarashtra, Vidura started for (the palace of) the wise Pandavas by means of quiet and patient horses of best species, possessing great speed and strength.

sn: सोऽभिपत्य तदध्वानमासाद्य नृपतेः पुरम्। प्रविवेश महाबुद्धिः पूज्यमानो द्विजातिभिः॥
en: The greatly intelligent (Vidura) proceeded by the way leading to the city of the Pandavas; and having arrived there, he, being duly worshipped by the Brahmanas, entered the city.

sn: स राजगृहमासाद्य कुबेरभवनोपमम्। अभ्यगच्छत धर्मात्मा धर्मपुत्रं युधिष्ठिरम्॥
en: Coming to the royal palace which was like the palace of Kubera, the virtuous minded (Vidura) went to the son of Dharma, Yudhishthira.

sn: तं वै राजा सत्यधृतिर्महात्मा अजातशत्रुर्विदुरं यथावत्। स्ततोऽपृच्छद् धृतराष्ट्र सपुत्रम्॥
en: The illustrious and enemiless descendant of Ajamida, ever devoted to truth, reverentially saluted Vidura and asked him about the welfare of Dhritarashtra and his sons.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच विज्ञायते ते मनसोऽप्रहर्षः कच्चित् क्षत्तः कुशलेनागतोऽसि। कच्चित् पुत्राः स्थविरस्यानुलोमा वशानुगाश्चापि विशोऽथ कच्चित्॥
en: Yudhishthira said O Khattwa, your mind seems to be cheerless. Do you come in peace? Are the sons (of Dhritarashtra) obedient to their old father? Are the people obedient to his (Dhritarashtra's) rule?

sn: विदुर उवाच राजा महात्मा कुशलौ सपुत्र आस्ते वृतो ज्ञातिभिरिन्द्रकल्पः। विशोक एवात्मरतिर्महात्मा।॥
en: Vidura said The illustrious king with his sons is well. Surrounded by his relatives, he reigns like Indra. O king, the illustrious monarch is happy with his sons who are all obedient to him. But he is bent upon his own aggrandisement.

sn: इदं तु त्वां कुरुराजोऽभ्युवाच पूर्वं पृष्ट्वा कुशलं चाव्ययं च। इयं सभा त्वत्सभातुल्यरूपा भ्रातृणां ते दृश्यतामेत्य पुत्र॥
en: The Kuru king has commanded me first to enquire after your peace and prosperity, and then to tell you on his behalf the following. (He says to you), "The Assembly-hall of your cousin (built by me) is equal to your Sabha. Therefore, (come) and see it.

sn: समागम्य भ्रातृभिः पार्थ तस्यां सुहृद्यूतं क्रियतां रम्यतां च। प्रीयामहे भवतां संगमेन समागताः कुरवश्चापि सर्वे॥
en: O son of Pritha, coming there enjoy the palace and play a friendly match at dice with your cousins. We shall be very happy at your arrival, so will be all the Kurus assembled there."

sn: दुरोदरा विहिता ये तु तत्र महात्मना धृतराष्ट्रेण राज्ञा। नित्यागतोऽहं नृपते तज्जुषस्व॥
en: O king, you will see there all those gamblers, those cheats who have been brought there by the illustrious king Dhritarashtra. I have come here for this. Let the king's command be approved by you.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच द्यूते क्षत्तः कलहो विद्यते नः को वै द्यूतं रोचयेद् बुध्यमानः। किं वा भवान् मन्यते युक्तरूपं भवद्वाक्ये सर्व एव स्थिताः स्म॥॥
en: Yudhishthira said o Khattwa, gambling may produce quarrel. Knowing this, who is there who will consent to gamble? What do you think proper for us to do? We are all obedient to your advice,

sn: विदुर उवाच जानाम्यहं द्यूतमनर्थमूलं कृतश्च यत्नोऽस्य मया निवारणे। राजा च मां प्राहिणोत् त्वत्सकाशं श्रुत्वा विद्वच्छ्रेय इहाचरस्व॥
en: Vidura said I know gambling is the root of all misery. I tried to dissuade the king from it. The king, however, has sent me to you. O learned man, knowing all this, do what is good.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच के तत्रान्ये कितवा दीव्यमाना विना राज्ञो धृतराष्ट्रस्य पुत्रैः। पृच्छामि त्वां विदुर ब्रूहि न स्तान् यैर्दीव्यामः शतशः संनिपत्य॥
en: Yudhishthira said Besides the sons of king Dhritarashtra who are the other dishonest gamblers that are present there to play? O Vidura, I ask you, tell us who are the men with whom we shall have to play staking hundreds upon hundreds.

sn: विदुर उवाच गान्धारराजः शकुनिर्विशाम्पते। राजातिदेवी कृतहस्तो मताक्षः। विविंशतिश्चित्रसेनश्च राजा सत्यव्रतः पुरुमित्रो जयश्च॥
en: Vidura said. O king, expert in dice, with great skill of hand, even desperate at stakes the Gandhara king, Shakuni, Vivingshati, Chitrasena, king Satyavrata, Purumitra and Jaya (these are present there).

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच महाभयाः कितवाः संनिविष्टा मायोपधा देवितारोऽत्र सन्ति। धात्रा तु दिष्टस्य वशे किलेदं सर्वं जगत् तिष्ठति न स्वतन्त्रतम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said It appears that some of the most desperate and terrible gamblers who always depend on deceit (in their play) are present there. The whole universe, however, is at the will of its creator under the control of Fate. It is not free.

sn: त्र गन्तुमिच्छामि कवे दुरोदरम्। इष्टो हि पुत्रस्य पिता सदैव तदस्मि कर्ता विदुरात्थ मां यथा॥
en: O leaned man, I do not desire to engage in gambling at the command of king Dhritarashtra, for a father always Wishes to benefit his son. You are our master, OVidura, tell me what is proper (for us to do).

sn: न चाकाम: शकुनिना देविताहं न चेन्मां जिष्णुराहयिता सभायाम्। आहूतोऽहं न निवर्ते कदाचित् तदाहितं शाश्वतं वै व्रतं मे॥
en: I am unwilling to gamble. I will not do it (gamble) unless the wicked Shakuni does not challenge me in the Sabha. If however he challenges me, I will never refuse. This is my settled and eternal vow.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्त्वा विदुरं धर्मराजः प्रायात्रिकं सर्वमाज्ञाप्य तूर्णम्। प्रायाच्छ्वोभूते सगणः सानुयात्रः सह स्त्रीभिद्रौपदीमादि कृत्वा॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having said this to Vidura, Dharmaraja (Yudhishthira) commanded that preparations for his journey might be soon made. The next day accompanied by his relatives and attendants and taking with his Draupadi and the women of the household he started (for Hastinapur).

sn: दैवं हि प्रज्ञां मुष्णाति चक्षुस्तेज इवापतत्। धातुश्च वशमन्वेति पाशैरिव नरः सितः॥
en: “As a brilliant body falling before the eye deprives the power of seeing so does Fate our reason. Man, tied as it were with a cord, submits to the sway of providence”.

sn: इत्युक्तवा प्रययौ राजा सह क्षत्रा युधिष्ठिरः। अमृष्यमाणस्तस्याथ समाह्वानमरिंदमः॥
en: Having said this, the chastiser of foes Yudhishthira, went with Khattwa (Vidura) without deliberating over the summons (of Dhritarashtra).

sn: बाह्रीकेन रथं यत्तमास्थाय परवीरहा। परिच्छन्नो ययौ पार्थो भ्रातृभिः सह पाण्डवः॥
en: The slayer of hostile hosts, the son of Pritha, the Pandava (Yudhishthira) attired in. royal robes and riding on the car presented to him by the Valhika king started with his brothers.

sn: राजश्रिया दीप्यमानो ययौ ब्रह्मपुरःसरः। धृतराष्ट्रेण चाहूतः कालस्य समयेन च॥
en: Summoned by Dhritarashtra and impelled by what has been ordained by Time and blazing with royal prosperity, the king with the Brahmanas walking before him went (from his city).

sn: स हास्तिनपुरं गत्वा धृतराष्ट्रगृहं ययौ। समियाय च धर्मात्मा धृतराष्ट्रेण पाण्डवः॥
en: Arriving at Hastinapur he went in the Dhritarashtra's palace. The high-souled Pandava (Yudhishthira) then that Dhritarashtra,

sn: तथा भीष्मेण द्रोणेन कर्णेन च कृपेण च। समियाय यथान्यायं द्रौणिना च विभुः सह॥
en: Bhishma, Drona, Karna and Kripa, the lord (Yudhishthira) also met the son of Drona (Ashvathama) he duly saluted and embraced all of them and was saluted and embraced by them in return.

sn: समेत्य च महाबाहुः सोमदत्तेन चैव ह। दुर्योधनेन शल्येन सौबलेन च वीर्यवान्॥
en: The greatly powerful and mighty armed (hero) them met Somadatta, Duryodhana, Shalya the son of Subala (Shakuni).

sn: ये चान्ये तत्र राजानः पूर्वमेव समागताः। दुःशासनेन वीरेण सर्वैभ्रातृभिरेव च।॥
en: And the other monarchs that had arrived there before him; and also the brave Dushasana and all his other cousins;

sn: जयद्रथेन च तथा कुरुभिश्चापि सर्वशः। ततः सर्वैर्महाबाहुभ्रातभिः परिवारितः॥
en: Also Jayadratha and all other Kurus. Then the mighty armed hero, surrounded by all his brothers,

sn: प्रविवेश गृहं राज्ञो धृतराष्ट्रस्य धीमतः। ददर्श तत्र गान्धारी देवी पतिमनुव्रताम्॥
en: Entered the palace of the wise king Dhritarashtra, and saw there lady Gandhari ever obedient to her husband.

sn: स्नुषाभिः संवृतां शश्वत् तारा भिरिव रोहिणीम्। अभिवाद्य स गान्धारी तया च प्रतिनन्दितः॥ ददर्श पितरं वृद्धं प्रज्ञाचक्षुषमीश्वरम्॥
en: Surrounded by her daughters-in-law like Rohini by the stars. Having saluted Gandhari and having been blessed by her in return. He his old father (uncle, Dhritarashtra), the great lord whose knowledge was his eye.

sn: राज्ञा मूर्धन्युपाघ्रातास्ते च कौरवनन्दनाः। चत्वारः पाण्डवा राजन् भीमसेनपुरोगमा:॥
en: O king, the monarch (Dhritarashtra) smelt his head as also those of the four other Kuru princes, the Pandavas, Bhima being at their head.

sn: ततो हर्षः समभवत् कौरवाणां विशाम्पते। तान् दृष्ट्वा पुरुषव्याघ्रान् पाण्डवान् प्रियदर्शनान्॥
en: O king, seeing those best of men, the handsome Pandavas, all the Kurus became exceedingly glad.

sn: विविशुस्तेऽभ्यनुज्ञाता रत्नवन्ति गृहाणि च। ददृशुश्चोपयातांस्तान् दुःशलाप्रमुखाः स्त्रियः॥
en: Commanded by the king Dhritarashtra, the Pandavas retired to rooms, adorned with gems saw and jewels. Here the ladies of the household with Dushala (Duryodhana' sister) at their head visited them.

sn: याज्ञसेन्याः परामृद्धिं दृष्ट्वा प्रज्वलितामिव। स्नुषास्ता धृतराष्ट्रस्य नातिप्रमनसोऽभवन्॥
en: Seeing the blazing and splendid beauty and prosperity of Yajnaseni (Draupadi), Dhritarashtra's daughters-in-law were filled with jealousy and became cheerless.

sn: ततस्ते पुरुषव्याघ्रा गत्वा स्त्रीभिस्तु संविदम्। कृत्वा व्यायामपूर्वाणि कृत्यानि प्रतिकर्म च॥
en: Having conversed with the ladies, those best of men (then) went through their daily physical exercises, and they then performed the usual daily religious rites.

sn: ततः कृताछिकाः सर्वे दिव्यचन्दनभूषिताः। कल्याणमनसश्चैव ब्राह्मणान् स्वस्ति वाच्य च॥
en: Having performed their daily rites and decked their body with excellent Chandana and having desired to secure good luck and prosperity they caused Brahmanas to utter benedictions. Then having eaten best food, they retired to the sleeping apartments.

sn: मनोज्ञमशमनं भुक्त्वा विविशुः शरणान्यथा उपगीयमाना नारीभिरस्वपन् कुरुपुङ्गवाः॥ जगाम तेषां सा रात्रिः पुण्या रतिविहारिणाम्। स्तूयमानाश्च विश्रान्ताः काले निद्रामथात्यजन्॥
en: Those best of the Kurus, those subjugators of hostile towns, were sung into sleep by beautiful damsels. Receiving what came in due succession, they passed that delicious night in pleasure and sport. Having awakened by the sweet music of the bards, they rose from their bed after rest.

sn: सुखोषितास्ते रजनी प्रातः सर्वे कृताछिकाः। सभां रम्यां प्रविविशुः कितवैरभिनन्दिताः॥
en: Having passed the day in happiness, they rose in the morning and having performed the usual rites, they entered the Sabha and were saluted by those who assembled there for gambling.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच प्रविश्य तां सभां पार्था युधिष्ठिरपुरोगमाः। समेत्य पार्थिवान् सर्वान् पूजार्हानभिपूज्य च॥ यथावयः समेयाना उपविष्टा यथार्हतः। आसनेषु विचित्रेषु स्पर्ध्यास्तरणवत्सु च॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having entered the Sabha, the sons of Pritha with Yudhishthira at their head met all the kings that were present there. Worshipping all those that deserved to be worshipped and saluting others as each deserved according to his age, they took their seats on pure seats covered with costly carpets.

sn: तेषु तत्रोपविष्टेषु सर्वेष्वध नृपेषु च। शकुनिः सौबलस्तत्र युधिष्ठिरमभाषत॥
en: When they were seated, and when the kings took their seats also, the son of Subala, Shakuni, thus spoke to Yudhishthira.

sn: शकुनिरुवाच उपस्तीर्णा सभा राजन् सर्वे त्वयि कृतक्षणाः। अक्षानुप्त्वा देवनस्य समयोऽस्तु युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Shakuni said O king, the Assembly is full. All was waiting for you. O Yudhishthira, let now the dice be cast and the rules of play be fixed.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच निकृतिर्देवनं पापं न क्षात्रोऽत्र पराक्रमः। न च नीति_वा राजन् किं त्वं द्यूतं प्रशंससि॥
en: Yudhishthira said O king, deceitful gambling is a sin. there is no Kshatriya prowess (to be found) in it. There is certainly no moraliiy in it; why then are you praising gambling?

sn: न हि मानं प्रशंसन्ति निकृतौ कितवस्य हि। शकुने मैव नो जैषीरमार्गेण नृशंसवत्॥
en: O Shakuni, the wise men do not praise the pride that gamesters feel in deceitful play. Do not like a cruel man defeat us by deceitful means.

sn: शकुनिरुवाच चेष्टास्वखिन्नः कितवोऽक्षजासु। महामतिर्यश्च जानाति द्यूतं स वै सर्वं सहते प्रक्रियासु॥ स्तेनैव दोषो भवतीह पार्थ। दीव्यामहे पार्थिव मा विशङ्कां कुरुष्व पाणं च चिरं च मा कृथाः॥
en: Shakuni said. That high minded player, who knows the secrets of winning and losing, who is skilled in baffling the deceitful arts of those with whom he plays, and who is united with the various operations which gambling consists of, knows truly the play and suffers all in course of it. O son of Pritha, it is the staking of dice that may be lost and won, and which may injure us. And it is for this reason gambling is considered to be a fault. Therefore, O king, let us begin the play. Fear not, let the stakes be fixed. Do not make any further delay.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच एवमाहायमसितो देवलो मुनिसत्तमः। इमानि लोकद्वाराणि यो वै भ्राम्यति सर्वदा॥ इदं वै देवनं पापं निकृत्या कितवैः सह। धर्मेण तु जयो युद्धे तत्परं न तु देवनम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said That best of Rishis, the son of Asita, Devala, who always instructs us about all those acts that may lead(men) to heaven, hell or to the other regions, has said this it is sinful to play deceitfully with a gamester. The best sport is to obtain victory in a righteous battle. Gambling is not a sport.

sn: नार्या म्लेच्छन्ति भाषाभिर्मायया न चरन्त्युत। अजिह्ममशठं युद्धमेतत् सत्पुरुषव्रतम्॥
en: Those that are respectable do not use the Mleccha language, nor do they adopt deceitfulness in their behaviours. The act of honest men is to carry on a war without crookedness of cunning.

sn: शक्तितो ब्राह्मणान् नूनं रक्षितुं प्रयतामहे। तद् वै वित्तं मातिदेवीर्मा जैषीः शकुने परान्॥
en: O Shakuni, by playing disparately do not deceitfully win from us that wealth with which according to our ability we try to benefit the Brahmanas. Even enemies should not be vanquished by desperate stakes in a deceitful play.

sn: निकृत्या कामये नाहं सुखान्युत धनानि वा। कितवस्येह कृतिनो वृत्तमेतन्न पूज्यते॥
en: I do not desire to have happiness or wealth by means of cunning. The conduct of one that is a gamester, even if his playing be without deceitfulness, should still never be praised.

sn: शकुनिरुवाच श्रोत्रियः श्रोत्रियानेति निकृत्यैव युधिष्ठिर। विद्वानविदुषोऽभ्येति नाहुस्तां निकृतिं जनाः॥
en: Shakuni said O Yudhishthira, it is with the desire of vanquishing, which is (of course) not a very honest motive, that a high-born man approaches another (like him); so does a learned man an ignorant one;

sn: अक्षैर्हि शिक्षितोऽभ्येति निकृत्यैव युधिष्ठिरः। विद्वानविदुषोऽभ्येति नाहुस्तां निकृति जनाः॥
en: O Yudhishthira, so also a man skilled in dice approaches one who is not so from the desire of vanquishing (his opponent). One who is conversant with the truths of science approaches another that is not from the desire of victory, which is scarcely an honest motive.

sn: अकृतास्त्रं कृतास्त्रश्चं दुर्बलं बलवत्तरः। एवं कर्मसु सर्वेषु निकृत्यैव युधिष्ठिर। विद्वानविदुषोऽभ्येति नाहुस्तां निकृति जनाः॥
en: O Yudhishthira, so also a man skilled in weapons approaches one who is not so; so does a strong man a weak one. This is the practice in every contest. The victory is(always)the motive.

sn: एवं त्वं मामिहाभ्येत्य निकृति यदि मन्यसे। देवनाद् विनिवर्तस्व यदि ते विद्यते भयम्॥
en: If, therefore, in approaching me to play, you consider that I am actuated by dishonest motives, and if you are afraid then desist from the play.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच आहूतो न निवर्तेयमिति मे व्रतमाहितम्। विधिश्च बलवान् राजन् दिष्टस्यामि वशे स्थितः॥
en: Yudhishthira said. O king, challenged, I do not withdraw; this is my established vow. (I know) fate is (all) powerful. We are all under the sway of Fate.

sn: अस्मिन् समागमे केन देवनं मे भविष्यति। प्रतिपाणश्च कोऽन्योऽस्ति ततो द्यूतं प्रवर्तताम्॥
en: In this assembly with whom am I to play? Who is there who can stake equally with me? Let the play begin (with him).

sn: दुर्योधन उवाच अहं दातास्मि रत्नानां धनानां च विशाम्पते॥ मदर्थे देविता चायं शकुनिर्मातुलो मम।
en: Duryodhana said O king, I shall supply gems and jewels and wealth, and my uncle, Shakuni, will play the dice on my behalf.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच अन्येनान्यस्य वै द्यूतं विषमं प्रतिभाति मे। एतद् विद्वन्नुपादत्स्व काममेवं प्रवर्तताम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said Gambling by one on another's behalf seems to me to be contrary to rule. O learned man, you too will admit this. If however, you still desire it, let the play begin.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच उपोह्यमाने द्यूते तु राजानः सर्व एव ते। धृतराष्ट्र पुरस्कृत्य विविशुस्तां सभां ततः॥
en: Vaishampayana said When the play commenced, all the kings, Dhritarashtra being at their head, took their seats in that Assembly hall.

sn: भीष्मो द्रोणः कृपश्चैव विदुश्च महामतिः। नातिप्रीतेन मनसा तेऽन्ववर्तन्त भारत॥
