en: O descendant of Bharata, Bhishma, Drona, Kripa, the high-souled Vidura followed their example with cheerless heart.

sn: ते द्वन्द्वशः पृथक् चैव सिंहग्रीवा महौजसः। सिंहासनानि भूरीणि विचित्राणि च भेजिरे॥
en: Those lion-necked and greatly effulgeit (kings) took their seats separately and in praise on may high (royal) seats of various make and colour.

sn: शुशुभे सा सभा राजन् राजभिस्तैः समागतः। देवैरिव महाभागैः समवेतैस्त्रिविष्टपम्॥
en: O king, that Assembly-hall looked beautiful with the assembled monarchs like the heaven with a conclave of greatly fortunate celestials.

sn: सर्वे वेदविदः शूराः सर्वे भास्वरमूर्तयः। प्रावर्तत महाराज सुहृद्यूतमनन्तरम्॥
en: O great king, they were all heroes, they were all learned in the Vedas, and they all bore resplendent countenances. The friendly match at dice then commenced (in due form).

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच अयं बहुधनो राजन् सागरावर्तसम्भवः। मणिर्हारोत्तरः श्रीमान् कनकोत्तमभूषणः॥
en: Yudhishthira said O king, this excellent and most valuable chain of pearls, so beautiful and adorned with gold and procured from the ocean by churning it,

sn: एतद् राजन् मम धनं प्रतिपाणोऽस्ति कस्तव। येन मां त्वं महाराज धनेन प्रतिदीव्यसे॥
en: O king, is my stake. O great king, what is your counter stake, the wealth with which you wish to play with me?

sn: दुर्योधन उवाच सन्ति मे मणयश्चैव धनानि सुबहूनि च। मत्सरश्च न मेऽर्थेषु जयस्वैनं दुरोदरम्॥
en: Duryodhana said I have many jewels and much wealth, but I am not proud of them. However, let yourself win this stake.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततो जग्राह शकुनिस्तानक्षानक्षतत्त्ववित्। जितमित्येव शकुनियुधिष्ठिरमभाषत॥
en: Vaishampayana said Thereupon Shakuni, well-skilled in dice, took up the dice and said to Yudhishthira, “Lo, I have won it".

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच मत्तः कैतवकेनैव यज्जितोऽस्मि दुरोदरे। शकुने हन्त दीव्यामो ग्लहमानाः परस्परम्॥ सन्ति निष्कसहस्रस्य भाण्डिन्यो भरिताः शुभाः।
en: Yudhishthira said O Shakuni, you have won this stake by unfair means. Do you feel pride for it? Let us play, staking thousands and thousands.

sn: कोशो हिरण्यमक्षय्यं जातरूपमनेकशः। एतद् राजन् मम धनं तेन दीव्याम्यहं त्वया।॥
en: O king, I have many beautiful jars each filled with one thousand Nishkas (gold coins) I have in my treasury inexhaustible gold, and much silver and other minerals. this is the wealth with which I shall (now) stake with you.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच कौरवाणां कुलकरं ज्येष्ठं पाण्डवमच्युतम्। इत्युक्तः शकुनिः प्राह जितमित्येव तं नृपम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having been thus addressed, Shakuni thus spoke to the perpetuator of the Kuru race, the eldest Pandava of undeteriorating glory, “Lo, I have whom?"

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच अयं सहस्रसमितो वैयाघ्रः सुप्रतिष्ठितः। सुचक्रोपस्करः श्रीमान् किङ्किणीजालमण्डितः॥ संहादनो राजरथो य इहास्मानुपावहत्। जैत्रो रथवरः पुण्यो मेघसागरनिःस्वनः।। अष्टौ यं कुररच्छायाः सदश्वा राष्ट्रसम्मताः॥ वहन्ति नैषां मुच्येत पदाद् भूमिमुपस्पृशन्। एतद् राजन् धनं मह्यं तेन दीव्याम्यहं त्वया॥
en: Yudhishthira said. This my sacred, victorious and royal car, which gladdens the heart and which brought us here, which is equal to one thousand cars, which is symmetrical in make and covered with tiger's skins, which is furnished with excellent wheels and flag-staff, which is beautiful and adorned with small bells, the clatter of the wheel of which is like the roars of clouds or the ocean and which is drawn by eight noble steeds renowned all over the kingdom, (the steeds) that are white as the moon-beam and from whose hoofs no earthly being can escape, this, O king, is my wealth with which I shall (now) stake with you.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवं श्रुत्वा व्यवसितो निकृतिं समुपाश्रितः। जितमित्येव शकुनियुधिष्ठिरमभाषत।॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having heard this, and adopting unfair means, Shakuni, ever ready with the dice said to Yudhishthira, “Lo, I have won?"

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच शतं दासीसहस्राणि तरुण्यो हेमभद्रिकाः। कम्बुकेयूरधारिण्यो निष्ककण्ठ्यः स्वलंकृताः॥
en: Yudhishthira said I have one hundred thousand serving girls, who are all you and all adorned with golden bracelets on their wrists and upper arms, who have Nishkanthas and other ornaments,

sn: महार्हमाल्याभरणाः सुवस्त्राश्चन्दनोक्षिताः। मणीन् हेम च बिभ्रत्यश्चतुःषष्टिविशारदाः॥ अनुसेवां चरन्तीमाः कुशला नृत्यसामसु। स्नातकानाममात्यानां राज्ञां च मम शासनात्। एतद् राजन् मम धनं तेन दीव्याम्यहं त्वया॥
en: And also costly garlands round their necks, who are attired in rich garments and anointed with sandal paste, who are well-skilled in sixty four elegant arts, specially in dancing and singing, and who wait upon and serve at my command the celestials, the snatakas and the kings. With this wealth, I shall (now) stake with you.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एतच्छ्रुत्वा व्यवसितो निकृतिं समुपाश्रितः। जितमित्येव शकुनियुधिष्ठिरमभाषत॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having heard this and adopting unfair means, Shakuni, ever ready with the dice, sand to Yudhishthira, “Lo, I have won?"

sn: युधिष्टिर उवाच एतावन्ति च दासानां सहस्राण्युत सन्ति मे। प्रदक्षिणानुलोमाश्च प्रावारवसनाः सदा॥
en: Yudhishthira said I have thousands of serving men, skilled in waiting upon guests, who are always attired in silken robes.

sn: प्राज्ञा मेधाविनो दान्ता युवानो मृष्टकुण्डलाः। पात्रीहस्ता दिवारात्रमतिथीन् भोजयन्त्युत। एतद् राजन् मम धनं तेन दीव्याम्यहं त्वया॥
en: Who possess wisdom and intelligence, who are self-controlled, young, adorned with ear-rings and who feed all guests with plates and dishes in hand. With this wealth, O king, I shall (now) stake with you.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एतच्छ्रुत्वा व्यवसितो निकृतिं समुपाश्रितः। जितमित्येव शकुनियुधिष्ठिरमभाषत॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having heard this and adopting unfair means, Shakuni, ever ready with the dice, sand to Yudhishthira, “Lo, I have won?"

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच सहस्रसंख्या नागा मे मत्तास्तिष्ठन्ति सौबल। हेमकक्षाः कृतापीडाः पद्मिनो हेममालिनः॥
en: Yudhishthira said O son of Subala, I have one thousand musty elephants with golden girdles, who are adorned with ornaments, who have the marks of the lotus on their temples necks and other parts and who are adorned with golden garlands.

sn: सुदान्ता राजवहनाः सर्वशब्दक्षमा युधि। ईषादन्ता महाकायाः सर्वे चाष्टकरेणवः॥ सर्वे च पुरभेत्तारो नवमेघनिभा गजाः। एतद् राजन् मम धनं तेन दीव्याम्यहं त्वया॥
en: Who possess fine(white) tusks, tusks like plough-shafts, who are worthy of carrying kings and capable of withstanding every kind of noise on the field of battle, who have huge bodies, who are capable of battering down the walls of the hostile cities, who are of the colour of newly formed clouds and each of whom possesses eight female elephants. With this wealth, O king, I shall (now) stake with you.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच इत्येवंवादिनं पार्थं प्रहसन्निव सौबलः। जितमित्येव शकुनियुधिष्ठिरमभाषत॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having heard this and adopting unfair means, Shakuni, ever ready with the dice, said to Yudhishthira, “Lo, I have won?"

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच रथास्तावन्त एवेमे हेमदण्डाः पताकिनः। हयैर्विनीतैः सम्पन्ना रथिभिश्चित्रयोधिभिः॥
en: Yudhishthira said I have as many cars as elephants, all furnished with golden poles and flat-staffs, and also well trained horses and car-warriors who fight wonderfully.

sn: एकैको ह्यत्र लभते सहस्रपरमां भृतिम्। युध्यतोऽयुध्यतो वापि वेतनं मासकालिकम्। एतद् राजन् मम धनं तेन दीव्याम्यहं त्वया॥
en: And each of whom receives one thousand coins as his monthly salary whether he fights or not. With this wealth, O king, I shall (now) stake with you.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच इत्येवमुक्ते वचने कृतवैरो दुरात्मवान्। जितमित्येव शकुनियुधिष्ठिरमभाषत॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having heard this and adopting unfair means, Shakuni, ever ready with the dice, said to Yudhishthira, “Lo, I have won?" was

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच अश्वास्तित्तिरिकल्माषान् गान्धर्वान् हेममालिनः। ददौ चित्ररथस्तुष्टो यांस्तान् गाण्डीवधन्वने॥ युद्धे जितः पराभूतः प्रीतिपूर्वमरिंदमः। एतद् राजन् मम धनं तेन दीव्याम्यहं त्वया॥
en: Yudhishthira said The steeds of the Tittiri, Kalmasha and Gandharva breeds, adorned with golden garlands, all of whom were gladly presented to the wielder of the Gandiva (Arjuna) by the chastiser of foes, Chitraratha, who vanquished and subdued in battle, with this wealth, O king, I shall (now) stake with you.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एतच्छ्रुत्वा व्यवसितो निकृति समुपाश्रितः। जितमित्येव शकुनियुधिष्ठिरमभाषत॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having heard this and adopting unfair means, Shakuni, ever ready with the dice, said to Yudhishthira, "Lo, I have won?”

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच स्थानां शकटानां च श्रेष्ठानां चायुतानि मे। युक्तान्येव हि तिष्ठन्ति वाहैरुच्चावचैस्तथा॥
en: Yudhishthira said I have ten thousand wagons and vehicles to which are yoked draught animals of the foremost breed.

sn: एवं वर्णस्य वर्णस्य समुच्चीय सहस्रशः। यथा समुदिता वीराः सर्वे वीरपराक्रमाः॥
en: I have soldiers picked up by thousands from each order who are all brave and who are endued with the prowess of (great) heroes.

sn: क्षीरं पिबन्तस्तिष्ठन्ति भुञ्जानाः शालितण्डुलान्। षष्टिस्तानि सहस्राणि सर्वे विपुलवक्षसः। एतद् राजन् मम धनं तेन दीव्याम्यहं त्वया।॥
en: And who drink milk and eat good rice. They are sixty thousands in number, and all of them possess broad cheats. With this wealth, O king, I shall (now stake with you.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एतच्छ्रुत्वा व्यवसितो निकृतिं समुपाश्रितः। जितमित्येव शकुनिथुधिष्ठिरमभाषत॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having heard this and adopting unfair means Shakuni, ever ready with the dice, said to Yudhishthira, "Lo, I have won?"

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच ताम्रलोहैः परिवृता निधयो ये चतुःशताः। पञ्चद्रौणिक एकैकः सुवर्णस्याहतस्य वै॥ जातरूपस्य मुख्यस्य अनर्धेयस्य भारत। एतद् राजन् मम धनं तेन दीव्याम्यहं त्वया॥
en: Yudhishthira said I have four hundred Nidhis (very valuable jewels) encased in sheets of copper and iron; each one of them is equal to five Draunikas of the costliest and purest gold leaf of the Jatarupa kind. With this wealth, o king, I shall (now) stake with you.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एतच्छ्रुत्वा व्यवसितो निकृति समुपाश्रितः। जितमित्येव शकुनियुधिष्ठिरमभाषत॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having heard this and adopting unfair means, Shakuni, ever ready with the dice, said to Yudhishthira, "Lo, I have won?”

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवं प्रवतिते द्यूते घोरे सर्वापहारिणि। सर्वसंशयनिर्मोक्ता विदुरो वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said During the course of this fearful gambling, which was certain to bring about utter twin, that dispeller of all doubts, Vidura, thus spoke (to Dhritarashtra).

sn: विदुर उवाच महाराज विजानीहि यत् त्वां वक्ष्यामि भारत। मुमूर्षोरौषधमिव न रोचेतापि ते श्रुतम्॥
en: Vidura Said O great, O descendant of Bharata, attend to what I say, although it may not be agreeable to you like medicine to one who is at the point of death.

sn: यद् वै पुरा जातमात्रो रुराव गोमायुवद् विस्वरं पापचेताः दुर्योधनो भरतानां कुलनः सोऽयं युक्तो भरथां कालहेतुः॥
en: When this sinful wretch Duryodhana, this destroyer of the Bharata race, cried like jackal immediately after his, it was well-known that he had been ordained to bring about the destruction of you all.

sn: गृहे वसन्तं गोमायुं त्वं वै मोहान्न बुध्यसे। दुर्योधनस्य रूपेण शृणु काव्यां गिरं मम॥
en: A jackal is in your house in the form of Duryodhana. You do not know this out of folly. Listen to what Kavya (Shukra) said.

sn: मधु वै माध्विको लब्ध्वा प्रपातं नैव बुध्यते। आरुह्य तं मज्जति वा पतनं चाधिगच्छति॥
en: Those that collect honey, having received what they seek, do not (at all) mark that they are about to fall (down from the tree). Ascending dangerous heights and being deeply engaged in what they seek, they fall down and perish.

sn: सोऽयं मत्तोऽक्षयूतेन मधुवन्न परीक्षते। प्रपातं बुध्यते नैव वैरं कृत्वा महारथैः॥
en: He (Duryodhana) too maddened with the gambling, is absent-indeed (in the pursuit of the play) like the collector of honey. he dose not mark its (future) consequences. Creating hostilities with these great car-warriors, he dose not see the fall (which is before him).

sn: विदितं मे महाप्राज्ञ भोजेष्वेवासमञ्जसम्। पुत्रं संत्यक्तवान् पूर्वं पौराणां हितकाम्यया॥
en: O greatly wise one, it is known to you, that amongst the Bhojas, (there is a custom) of abandoning a son who is unworthy of there race, for (the sake of the general) good of the people.

sn: अन्धका यादवा भोजाः समेताः कंसमत्यजन्। नियोगात् तु हते तस्मिन् कृष्णेनामित्रघातिना॥
en: The Andhakas, the Yadavas the Bhojas, uniting together, abandoned Kansa. At the request (of the whole tribe) Kansa was kill by that slayer of foes, Krishna.

sn: एवं ते ज्ञातयः सर्वे मोदमानाः शतं समाः। त्वन्नियुक्तः सव्यसाची निगृह्णातु सुयोधनम्॥
en: Knowing this all became exceedingly happy for one hundred years. Let Savyasachi (Arjuna) kill Suyodhana (Duryodhana) at your command.

sn: निग्रहादस्य पापस्य मोदन्तां कुरवः सुखम्। काकेनेमांश्चित्रबर्हान् शार्दूलान् क्रोष्टकेन च। क्रीणीष्व पाण्डवान् राजन् मा मज्जी: शोकसागरे॥१०
en: Let the Kurus be glad and pass their time in happiness by the death of this wrench. O king, purchase these peacocks (Pandavas) at the exchange of this crow (Duryodhana); and buy these tiger, the Pandavas, at the exchange of this jackal (Duryodhana). Do not sink into the ocean of grief.

sn: त्यजेत् कुलार्थे पुरुषं ग्रामस्यार्थे कुलं त्यजेत्। ग्रामं जनपदस्यार्थे आत्मार्थे पृथिवीं त्यजेत्॥
en: For the sake of a family a member (of that family) may be sacrificed; for the sake of a village, a family may be scarified; for the sake of a town, village may be sacrificed; and for the sake of one's own soul, the earth may be sacrificed.

sn: सर्वज्ञः सर्वभावज्ञः सर्वशत्रुभयंकरः। इति स्म भाषते काव्यो जम्भत्यागे महासुरान्॥
en: The omniscient, the knower of all creatures' thoughts, the terror to all foes, Kavya, thus spoke to the great Asuras (to induce them) to abandon Jambha (Asura).

sn: हिरण्यष्ठीविनः कांश्चित् पक्षिणो वनगोचरान्। गृहे किल कृतावासान् लोभाद् राजा न्यपीडयत्। स चोपभोगलोभान्धो हिरण्यार्थी परंतप॥ आयतिं च तदात्वं च उभे सद्यो व्यनाशयत्। तदर्थकामस्तद्वत् त्वं मा दुहः पाण्डवान् नृप॥
en: It is said that a (certain) king, having (first) made some wild birds which used to vomit gold to take up their quarters in his own house, killed them afterwards from temptation. O chastiser of foes, blinded by temptation and by the desire of enjoyinent he destroyed both his present and future for the sake of the gold. O king, O monarch like that king, do not persecute the Pandavas from the desire of gain.

sn: मोहात्मा तप्स्यसे पश्चात् पत्रिहा पुरुषो यथा। जातं जातं पाण्डवेभ्यः पुष्पमादत्स्व भारत॥ मालाकार इवारामे स्नेहं कुर्वन् पुनः पुनः। वृक्षानङ्गारकारीव मैनान् धाक्षी: समूलकान्। मा गमः ससुतामात्यः सबलश्च यमक्षयम्॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, from (this) folly you will have to repent afterwards like the man who killed the birds. Like the flower-seller who plucks (flowers) from trees that he cherishers with affection from day to day, continue. O king, to pluck flowers from the Pandavas. Do not burn them to their roots like the fire-producing wind which reduces every thing to charcoal. Do not go to the abode of Yama with your sons, ministers, and forces.

sn: समवेतान् हि कः पार्थान् प्रतियुध्येत भारत। मरुद्भिः सहितो राजन्नपि साक्षान्मरुत्पतिः॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, who is capable of fighting with the sons of Pritha if they stand together? O king, not to speak of others, even the chief of the celestial with all the celestial cannot do it.

sn: विदुर उवाच द्यूतं मूलं कलहस्याभ्युपैति मिथो भेदं महते दारुणाय। यदास्थितोऽयं धृतराष्ट्रस्य पुत्रो दुर्योधनः सृजते वैरमुग्रम्॥
en: Vidura said Gambling is the root of dissensions. It brings about disunion. Its consequences are frightful. Taking recourse to it, Dhritarashtra's son creates for himself fearful hostility.

sn: प्रातीपेयाः शान्तनवा भैमसेनाः सबाह्निकाः। दुर्योधनापराधेन कृच्छ्रे प्राप्स्यन्ति सर्वशः॥
en: The descendants of Pratipa and Shantanu with the Valhikas and their fearful troops all will be destroyed for the fault of Duryodhana.

sn: दुर्योधनो मदेनैष क्षेमं राष्ट्रादपोहति। विषाणं गौरिव मदात् स्वयमारुजतेऽऽत्मनः॥
en: In consequence of this intoxication, Duryodhana forcibly drives away luck and prosperity from his kingdom like an infuriated bull who breaks his own hours.

sn: यश्चित्तमन्वेति परस्य राजन् वीरः कविः स्वामवमन्य दृष्टिम्। मारुह्य घोरे व्यसने निमज्जेत्॥
en: O king, that brave and learned man, who follows another man's heart disregarding his own foresight, sinks into terrible affliction like the man who goes into the sea in a boat guided by a child.

sn: दुर्योधनो ग्लहते पाण्डवेन प्रियायसे त्वं जयतीति तच्च। अतिनर्मा जायते सम्प्रहारो यतो विनाशः समुपैति पुंसाम्॥
en: Duryodhana is gambling with the Pandava (Yudhisthira), and you are in ecstasy of joy that he is winning. It is such success that begets war which (finally) ends in the destruction of men.

sn: आकर्षस्तेऽवाक्फलः सुप्रणीतो हृदि प्रौढो मन्त्रपदः समाधिः। मचिन्तितोऽनभिमतः स्वबन्धुना॥
en: This fascination that you have welldevised will lead to fearful results. You have by these counsels brought on great affliction to your heart. This quarrel with Yudhisthira, who is so nearly related to you, even if you have not foreseen it, is still approved by you.

sn: प्रातीपेयाः शान्तनवाः शृणुध्वं काव्यां वाचं संसदि कौरवाणाम्। वैश्वानरं प्रज्वलितं सुघोरं मा यास्यध्वं मन्दमनुप्रपन्नाः॥
en: O descendant of Shantanu, O descendant of Pratipa, listen in this assembly of the Kurus, to the words of wisdom. By following a wretch, do not enter into the terrible fire that has blazed forth.

sn: र्न संयच्छेदक्षमदाभिभूतः। वृकोदरः सव्यसाची यमौ च कोऽत्र द्वीप: स्यात् तुमुले वस्तदानीम्॥
en: When the Pandava, Ajatashatru (Yudhisthira), intoxicated with dice, will be angry, so will be Bhima, Arjuna and the twins (Nakula and Sahadeva), who (I say) will be your island (refuse) in that hour of confusion?

sn: महाराज प्रभवस्त्वं धनानां पुरा द्यूतान्मनसा यावदिच्छेः। बहुवित्तान् पाण्डवांश्चेज्जयस्त्वं किं ते तत् स्याद् वसु विन्देह पार्थान्॥
en: O great king, you are yourself a mine of wealth. You can earn as much wealth as you desire to earn by not taking recourse to gambling. What will you gain by winning the vast wealth of the Pandavas? Win the sons of Pritha, who will be more than all the wealth they have?

sn: जानीमहे देवितं सौबलस्य वेद द्यूते निकृति पर्वतीयः। यतः प्राप्तः शकुनिस्तत्र यातु मा यूयुधो भारत पाण्डवेयान्॥
en: We all know the skill of the son of Subala (Shakuni) in play. This mountain king knows many nefarious methods of gambling. Let Shakuni go back to the place whence he has come. O descendant of Bharata, do not rage a war with the Pandavas.

sn: दुर्योधन उवाच परेषामेव यशसा श्लाघसे त्वं सदा क्षत्तः कुत्सयन् धार्तराष्ट्रान्। जानीमहे विदुर यत् प्रियस्त्वं बालानिवास्मानवमन्यसे नित्यमेव॥
en: Duryodhana said O Khattwa, you are always boasting of the fame of our foes. You always depreciate the sons of Dhritarashtra. O Vidura, we know whose friend you really are. You always disregard us as if we are children.

sn: स विज्ञेयः पुरुषोऽन्यत्रकामो निन्दाप्रशंसे हि तथा युनक्ति। जिह्वा कथं ते हृदयं व्यनक्ति यो न ज्यायसः कृथा मनसः प्रातिकूल्यम्॥
en: That man who wishes for the success of those that are dear to him and defeat of those that are not dear to him stands confessed. He is known by his praise and blame. Your tongue and mind betray your heart.

sn: उत्सङ्गे च व्याल इवाहितोऽसि मार्जारवत् पोषकं चोपहंसि। स्तस्मात् क्षत्तः किं न बिभेषि पापात्॥
en: You are kept by us on our lap as a serpent. Like a cat you wish to injure him who cherishes you. The wise men have said that there is no sin greater than that of injuring one's supporter. O Khattwa, how is it that you do not fear sin?

sn: जित्वा शत्रून् फलमाप्तं महद् वै मास्मान् क्षत्तः परुषाणीह वोचः। द्विषद्भिस्त्वं सम्प्रयोगाभिनन्दी मुहुर्द्वषं यासि नः सम्प्रयोगात्॥
en: O Khattwa, having vanquished our enemies we have gained great advantage. Do not use harsh words towards us. You are always willing to make friendship with the foes, and it is for this reason that you always hate us.

sn: अमित्रतां याति नरोऽक्षमं ब्रुवन् निगूहते गुह्यममित्रसंस्तवे। तदाश्रितोऽपत्रप किं नु बाधसे यदिच्छसि त्वं तदिहाभिभाषसे॥
en: A man becomes a foe by speaking words that are unpardonable. In praising the enemy, the secrets of one's own party is never to be divulged. Therefore, O shameless man, why do you obstruct us in this way? You are speaking whatever comes to your mind.

sn: मा नोऽवमंस्था विद्म मनस्तवेदं शिक्षस्व बुद्धिं स्थविराणां सकाशात्। यशो रक्षस्व विदुर सम्प्रणीतं मा व्यापृतः परकार्येषु भूस्त्वम्॥
en: O Vidura, do not disregard us; we know your mind. Go, learn sitting at the feet of the old. Save the reputation that you have won. Do not middle with other men's affairs.

sn: अहं कर्तेति विदुर मा च मंस्था मा नो नित्यं परुषाणीह वोचः। न त्वां पृच्छामि विदुर यद्धितं मे स्वस्ति क्षत्तर्मा तितिक्षून् क्षिणु त्वम्॥
en: O Vidura, do not disregard us. Imagining that you are our master, do not always tell us harsh words. O Vidura, we do not ask you (to say) what is for our good. O Khattwa, do not irritate those that have already suffered much (at your hand),

sn: एकः शास्ता न द्वितीयोऽस्ति शास्ता गर्भे शयानं पुरुषं शास्ति शास्ता। तेनानुशिष्टः प्रवणादिवाम्भो यथा नियुक्तोऽस्मि तथा भवामि॥
en: There is but one controller (of men's Destiny), and there is no second. He controls even (the Destiny of the child which is in its mother's womb. I am controlled by Him. Like water that always flows in a downward course, I am acting in the way. He is directing me.

sn: भिनत्ति शिरसा शैलमहिं भोजयते च यः। धीरेव कुरुते तस्य कार्याणामनुशासनम्। यो बलादनुशास्तीह सोऽमित्रं तेन विन्दति॥
en: He also breaks his head against a stonewall and he that feeds a serpent, is guided in those acts of his by his own reason. He who wants to control another by force becomes his enemy.

sn: मित्रतामनुवृत्तं तु समुपेक्षेत पण्डितः। प्रदीप्य यः प्रदीप्ताग्नि प्राक् चिरं नाभिधावति। भस्मापि न स विन्देत शिष्टं क्वचन भारत॥
en: When advice is offered in a friendly spirit, the learned man does not (very much) mind it. O descendant of Bharata, he who sets fire to such a highly inflammable object as camphor, can not see its ashes, if he does not hasten to extinguish the fire.

sn: न वासयेत् पारवर्यं द्विषन्तं विशेषतः क्षत्तरहितं मनुष्यम्। स यत्रेच्छसि विदुर तत्र गच्छ सुसान्त्विता ह्यसती स्त्री जहाति॥
en: O be should not give shelter to one who is a friend of his enemy, or to one who is always jealous of his protector. O Vidura, therefore go away wherever you like. An unchaste wife, however well-treated, (always) forsakes her husband.

sn: विदुर उवाच एतावता पुरुषं ये त्यजन्ति तेषां वृत्तं साक्षिवद् ब्रूहि राजन्। राज्ञां हि चित्तानि परिप्लुतानि सान्त्वं दत्त्वा मुसलैर्घातयन्ति॥
en: Vidura said O king, tell us (impartially) like a witness what you think of the conduct of those who abandon men that give them such instruction (as I give you). The hearts of kings are unsteady. Granting protection first, they strike with clubs afterwards.

sn: अबालत्वं मन्यसे राजपुत्र बालोऽहमित्येव सुमन्दबुद्धे। यः सौहदे पुरुषं स्थापयित्वा पश्चादेनं दूषयते स बालः॥
en: O princes, you regard yourself as mature in intellect. O wicked hearted man, you consider me a child. But consider him a child who, having first accepted one as a friend, afterwards finds fault with him.

sn: न श्रेयसे नीयते मन्दबुद्धिः स्त्री श्रोत्रियस्येव गृहे प्रदुष्टा। ध्रुवं न रोचेद् भरतषभस्य पतिः कुमार्या इव षष्टिवर्षः॥
en: Like an unchaste wife in the house of a well-born man, a wicked-minded man can never be brought to the path of rectitude. As a husband of sixty years can never be agreeable to a young wife, so instruction is not agreeable to this chief of the Bharata race.

sn: अतः प्रियं चेतदनुकाक्षसे त्वं सर्वेषु कार्येषु हिताहितेषु। स्त्रियश्च राजञ्जडपङ्गुकांच पृच्छ त्वं वै तादृशांश्चैव सर्वान्॥
en: O king, if you hereafter wish to hear words that are agreeable to you as regards all good or bad acts, you should ask (for it to) women, idiots, cripples or all persons of such descriptions.

sn: लभ्यते खलु पापीयान् नरो नु प्रियवागिह। अप्रियस्य हि पथ्यस्य वक्ता श्रोता च दुर्लभः॥
en: Many sinful men who speak agreeable words may be had in this world, but a man, who will speak words that are disagreeable through fit as regimen or a man who will hear such words, is very rare.

sn: यस्तु धर्मपरश्च स्याद्धित्वा भर्तुः प्रियाप्रिये। अप्रियाण्याह पथ्यानि तेन राजा सहायवान्॥
en: He is a king's true friend who, disregarding what is agreeable or disagreeable to his master, conducts himself virtuously and utters what may be disagreeable, but what may be required as regimen.

sn: अव्याधिजं कटुजं तीक्ष्णमुष्णं यशोमुषं परुषं पूतिगन्धि। सतां पेयं यन्न पिबन्त्यसन्तो मन्युं महाराज पिब प्रशाम्य॥
en: O great king, drink that which is drunk by the honest and shunned by the dishonest, that (drink of) humility which is like a medicine that is bitter, pungent, burning, unintoxicating, disagreeable and revolting. Drinking it (humility), regain your sobriety.

sn: वैचित्रवीर्यस्य यशो धनं च वाञ्छाम्यहं सहपुत्रस्य शश्वत्। यथा तथा तेऽस्तु नमश्च तेऽस्तु ममापि च स्वस्ति दिशन्तु विप्राः॥
en: I always wish prosperity and affluence to the son of Vichitravirya (Dhritarashtra) and his sons. Happen what may to you, here I bow to you. Let the Brahmanas wish me sell.

sn: आशीविषान् नेत्रविषान् कोपयेन च पण्डितः। एवं तेऽहं वदामीदं प्रयतः कुरुनन्दन॥
en: O descendant of Kuru, this is the moral I carefully inculcate, that the learned men should never enrage such adders as have venom in their eyes.

sn: शकुनिरुवाच बहु वित्तं पराजैषीः पाण्डवानां युधिष्ठिर। आचक्ष्व वित्तं कौन्तेय यदि तेऽस्त्यपराजितम्॥
en: Shakuni said O Yudhisthira, you have lost much wealth of the Pandavas. O son of Kunti, if you have any other wealth which is not yet lost, tell us.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच मम वित्तमसंख्येयं यदहं वेद सौबल। अथ त्वं शकुने कस्माद् वित्तं समनुपृच्छसि॥
en: Yudhisthira said O Shakuni, O son of Subala, I know my wealth is untold. Why do you ask me of my wealth?

sn: अयुतं प्रयुतं चैव शङ्ख पद्मं तथार्बुदम्। खर्वं शनिखर्वं च महापद्मं च कोटयः॥ मध्यं चैव परार्धं च सपरं चात्र पण्यताम्। एतन्मम धनं राजंस्तेन दीव्याम्यहं त्वया॥
en: You can bet (with me) tens of thousands, and millions, tens of millions and billions, hundreds of billions and trillions, tens of trillions and hundreds of trillions, tens of quadrillions and hundreds of quadrillions and even more. O king, I will bet such wealth. With this wealth at stake I shall play with you.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एतच्छ्रुत्वा व्यवसितो निकृतिं समुपाश्रितः। जितमित्येव शकुनियुधिष्ठिरमभाषत॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having heard this and adopting unfair means, Shakuni, ever ready with the dice said to Yudhisthira, “Lo, I have won!"

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच गवाश्वं बहुधेनूकमसंख्येयमजाविकम्। यत् किंचिदनुपर्णाशां प्राक् सिन्धोरपि सौबल। एतन्मम धनं सर्वं तेन दीव्याम्यहं त्वया॥
en: Yudhisthira said O son of Subala, I have innumerable kine, horses, milch cows with claves, goats and shee; in the country extending from the Parnasha to the eastern bank of the Sindhu (river). With this wealth I shall (now) play with you.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एतच्छ्रुत्वा व्यवसितो निकृति समुपाश्रितः। जितमित्येव शकुनियुधिष्ठिरमभाषत॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having heard this and adopting unfair means, Shakuni, ever ready with the dice, said to Yudhisthira, “Lo, I have won!"

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच पुरं जनपदो भूमिरब्राह्मणधनैः सह। अब्राह्मणाश्च पुरुषा राजञ्छिष्टं धनं मम। एतद् राजन् मम धनं तेन दीव्याम्यहं त्वया॥
en: Yudhisthira said O king, I have my city, the country, land, the wealth of horses thereon, except those belonging to the Brahmanas, and also all those persons, except Brahmanas living therein-the wealth which still belongs to me. With all this wealth, O king, I shall (now) play with you.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एतच्छ्रुत्वा व्यवसितो निकृतिं समुपाश्रितः। जितमित्येव शकुनियुधिष्ठिरमभाषत॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having heard this and adopting unfair means, Shakuni, ever ready with the dice; said to Yudhisthira; “Lo, I have won!”

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच राजपुत्रा इमे राजञ्छोभन्ते यैर्विभूषिताः। कुण्डलानि च निष्काश्च सर्वं राजविभूषणम्। एतन्मम धनं राजंस्तेन दीव्याम्यहं त्वया॥
en: Yudhisthira said O_king, these princes here, who look resplendent in their ornaments and their earrings, and Nishkas and the royal ornaments on their persons are still my wealth. With this wealth, O king, I shall (now) play with you.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एतच्छ्रुत्वा व्यवसितो निकृतिं समुपाश्रितः। जितमित्येव शकुनियुधिष्ठिरमभाषत॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having heard this and adopting unfair means, Shakuni, ever ready with the dice, said to Yudhisthira, Lo, I have won?”

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच श्यामो युवा लोहिताक्षः सिंहस्कन्धो महाभुजः। नकुलो ग्लह एवैको विद्ध्येतन्मम तद्धनम्॥
en: Yudhisthira said This youthful, fair-coloured Nakula with mighty arms, with lion-like necks, and with red eyes is now one of my stakes.

sn: शकुनिरुवाच प्रियस्ते नकुलो राजन् राजपुत्रो युधिष्ठिर। अस्माकं वशतां प्राप्तो भूयः केनेह दीव्यसे॥
en: Shakuni said O king, O Yudhisthira, the prince Nakula is dear to you. (Know) he is already under our subjection (won by us). With what will you now play?

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्त्वा तु तानक्षाञ्छकुनिः प्रत्यदीव्यत। जितमित्येव शकुनियुधिष्ठिरमभाषत॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having said this, Shakuni cast the dice and thus spoke to Yudhisthira, Lo, I have won!"

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच अयं धर्मान् सहदेवोऽनुशास्ति लोके ह्यस्मिन् पण्डिताख्यां गतश्च। अनर्हता राजपुत्रेण तेन दीव्याम्यहं चाप्रियवत् प्रियेण॥
en: Yudhisthira said This Sahadeva administers justice, he has acquired a reputation for learning in this world. Though this prince does not deserve to be staked in play, yet with such dear object as my stake, I shall play, as if he is not so.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एतच्छ्रुत्वा व्यवसितो निकृतिं समुपाश्रितः। जितमित्येव शकुनियुधिष्ठिरमभाषत॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having heard this and adopting unfair means, Shakuni, ever ready with the dice, said to Yudhisthira, “Lo, I have won!"

sn: शकुनिरुवाच माद्रीपुत्रौ प्रियौ राजंस्तवेमौ विजितौ मया। गरीयांसौ त ते मन्ये भीमसेनधनंजयौ॥
en: Shakuni said O king, the two sons of Madri are dear to you; but (know it for certain,) they have already) been won by me. It appears Bhimasena and Dhananjaya (Arjuna), are more loved by you (than these two).

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच अधर्मं चरसे नूनं यो नावेक्षसि वै नयम्। यो नः सुमनसां मूढ विभेदं कर्तुमिच्छसि॥
en: Yudhisthira said Fool, disregarding morality you sinfully act in thus trying to create disunion amongst us who are all of one heart.

sn: शकुनिरुवाच गर्ने मत्तः प्रपतते प्रमत्तः स्थाणुमृच्छति। ज्येष्ठो राजन् वरिष्ठोऽसि नमस्ते भरतर्षभ॥
en: Shakuni said O king, one who is intoxicated falls into a pit and remains there, being deprived of his power of motion. O best of the Bharata race, you are senior to us in age and in everything, I bow to you.

sn: स्वप्ने तानि न दृश्यन्ते जाग्रतो वा युधिष्ठिर। कितवा यानि दीव्यन्तः प्रलपन्त्युत्कटा इव।॥
en: O Yudhisthira, know, gamesters in the excitement of the play utter such raving as they would never do in their waking moments or in their dreams.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच यो नः संख्ये नौरिव पारनेता जेता रिपूणां राजपुत्रस्तरस्वी। अनर्हता लोकवीरेण तेन दीव्याम्यहं शकुने फाल्गुनेन॥
en: Yudhisthira said He who takes us like a boat to the other shore of the sea of battle, who is ever victorious over foes, who is endued with great activity and who is the only one hero in this world (in Arjuna). With that Falguni as stake, O Shakuni, though he does not deserve it, I shall (now) play.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एतच्छ्रुत्वा व्यवसितो निकृति समुपाश्रितः। जितमित्येव शकुनिर्युधिष्ठिरमभाषत।॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having heard this and adopting unfair means, Shakuni, ever ready with the dice, said to Yudhisthira, "Lo, I have won?”

sn: शकुनिरुवाच अयं मया पाण्डवानां धनुर्धरः। पराजितः पाण्डवः सव्यसाची। भीमेन राजन् दयितेन दीव्य यत् कैतवं पाण्डव तेऽवशिष्टम्॥
en: Shakuni said This foremost of all wielders of bows, this Pandava Savyasachi (Arjuna) has been won by me. O king, O Pandava play now with (staking) your beloved Bhima, the only wealth that is now left to you.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच यो नो नेता युधि नः प्रणेता यथा वज्री दानवशत्रुरेकः। तिर्यक्प्रेक्षी संनतभूर्महात्मा सिंहस्कन्धो यश्च सदात्यमर्षी॥ बलेन तुल्यो यस्य पुमान् न विद्यते गदाभृतामय इहारिमर्दनः। अनर्हता राजपुत्रेण तेन दीव्याम्यहं भीमसेनेन राजन्॥
en: Yudhisthira said Though he does not deserve to be made a stake, I shall now play with staking Bhimasena, the prince who is our leader, who is foremost in fight like the wielder of thunder (Indra), the enerny of the Danavas, who is the illustrious hero with lion-like neck, arched eye-brows and expansive eyes, who is incapable of putting up with an insult, who is matchless in prowess in all the world, who is the foremost of all wielders of clubs and who grinds all foes.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एतच्छ्रुत्वा व्यवसितो निकृतिं समुपाश्रितः। जितमित्येव शकुनियुधिष्ठिरमभाषत॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having heard this and adopting unfair means, Shakuni, ever ready with the dice, said to Yudhisthira, "Lo I have won?"

sn: शकुनिरुवाच बहु वित्तं पराजैषीर्धातूंश्च सहयद्विपान्। आचक्ष्व वित्तं कौन्तेय यदि तेऽस्त्यपराजितम्॥
en: Shakuni said O son of Kunti, you have lost much wealth, heroes and elephants with your brothers. Tell us if you have anything else which you have not as yet lost.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच अहं विशिष्टः सर्वेषां भ्रातॄणां दयितस्तथा। कुर्यामहं जित: कर्म स्वयमात्मन्युपप्लुते॥
en: Yudhisthira said I alone, the eldest of my brothers and beloved of all of them, am still not won (by you). If won by you, I shall do that which one who is won is bound to do.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एतच्छ्रुत्वा व्यवसितो निकृति समुपाश्रितः। जितामित्येव शकुनियुधिष्ठिरमभाषत॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having heard this and adopting unfair means, Shakuni even ready with the dice, said to Yudhisthira; “Lo I have won!”

sn: शकुनिरुवाच एतत् पापिष्ठमकरोर्यदात्मानमहारयः। शिष्टे सति धने राजन् पाप आत्मपराजयः॥
en: Shakuni said O king, you have allowed yourself to be won, an act which is worthy of a sinful man. When there is still wealth belonging to you, it is sinful to lose one's own self.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्त्वा मताक्षस्तान् ग्लहे सर्वानवस्थितान्। पराजयं लोकवीरानुक्त्वा राज्ञां पृथक् पृथक्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having said this, (Shakuni), well-skilled in dice, spoke to all the brave kings present there of having won all the Pandavas one after the other.

sn: शकुनिरुवाच अस्ति ते वै प्रिया राजन् ग्लह एकोऽपराजितः। पणस्व कृष्णां पाञ्चालीं तयाऽत्मानं पुनर्जय॥
en: Shakuni said O king, there is still one stake dear to you which is not yet won. Bet Krishna, (Draupadi), the princess of Panchala. By her, win yourself back.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच नैव ह्रस्वा न महती न कृष्णा नातिरोहिणी। नीलकुञ्चितकेशी च तया दीव्याम्यहं त्वया॥
en: Yudhisthira said I shall (now) play with you staking her who is neither short nor tall, neither lean nor corpulent, who possesses blue curly hair,

sn: शारदोत्पलपत्राझ्या शारदोत्पलगन्धया। शारदोत्पलसेविन्या रूपेण श्रीसमानया॥
en: And eyes are like the leaves of the autumn lotus, and fragrance like that of the lily, who is like Sree herself in symmetry and grace,

sn: तथैव स्यादानृशंस्यात् तथा स्याद् रूपसम्पदा। तथा स्याच्छीलसम्पत्त्या यामिच्छेत् पुरुषः स्त्रियम्॥३५
en: Who is such that for her softness of heart, wealth of beauty and virtue, one may desire her for a wife.

sn: सर्वैगुणैर्हि सम्पन्नामनुकूलां प्रियंवदाम्। यादृशी धर्मकामार्थसिद्धिमिच्छेन्नरः स्त्रियम्॥
en: Who possesses every accomplishment, who is compassionate and sweet speeched, who is such that for the acquisition of Dharma, Artha and Kama one may desire her for his wife.

sn: चरमं संविशति या प्रथमं प्रतिबुध्यते। आगोपालाविपालेभ्यः सर्वं वेद कृताकृतम्॥
en: Who, retiring to bed last and rising from bed first, looks after the comforts of the cowherds and shepherds,

sn: आभाति पद्मवद् वक्त्रं सस्वेदं मल्लिकेव च। वेदिमध्या दीर्घकेशी ताम्रास्या नातिलोमशा॥
en: Whose face when covered with sweat looks like the lotus or the wasp, who possesses flowing hair, red lips and body without down;

sn: तयैवंविधया राजन् पाञ्चाल्याहं सुमध्यया। ग्लहं दीव्यामि चावल्या द्रौपद्या हन्त सौबल॥
en: O king, O son of Subala, making that princess of Panchala, the slender-waisted Draupadi, as my stake, I shall (now) play with you.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्ते तु वचने धर्मराजेन धीमता। धिग्धिगित्येव वृद्धानां सभ्यानां निःसृता गिरः॥
en: Vaishampayana said When this was said by the wise Dharmaraja (Yudhisthira), “Fie! Fie!" were the words uttered by all the elders that were present in the assembly.

sn: चुक्षुभे सा सभा राजन् राज्ञां संजज्ञिरे शुचः। भीष्मद्रोणकृपादीनां स्वेदश्च समजायत॥
en: O king, the whole assembly was agitated. The kings began to grieve. Bhisma, Drona and Kripa were covered with perspiration.

sn: शिरो गृहीत्वा विदुरो गतसत्त्व इवाभवत्। आस्ते ध्यायन्नधोवक्त्रो निःश्वसन्निव पन्नगः॥
en: Vidura, holding his head between his hands, sat like one who has lost his reason. He sat with down cast face giving away to his own thoughts and sighing like a snake.

sn: धृतराष्ट्रस्तु तं हृष्टः पर्यपृच्छत् पुनः पुनः। किं जितं किं जितमिति ह्याकारं नाभ्यरक्षत॥
en: (But) Dhritarashtra, being glad at heart, could not conceal his emotions and asked again and again, "is the stake won?” “Is the stake won???

sn: जहर्ष कर्णोऽतिभृशं सह दुःशासनादिभिः। इतरेषां तु सभ्यानां नेत्रेभ्यः प्राप्तज्जलम्॥
en: Karna with Dushasana and others laughed aloud, but tears began to flow from the eyes of all those that were present in the assembly.

sn: सौबलस्त्वभिधायैवं जितकाशी मदोत्कटः। जितमित्येव तानक्षान् पुनरेवान्वपद्यत॥
en: The son of Subala (Shakuni), proud of success, and flurried with excitement, repeating “You have still one stake dear to you” said, "Lo, I have won!” He then took up the dice that had been cast.

sn: दुर्योधन उवाच एहि क्षत्तौपदीमानयस्व प्रियां भार्यां सम्मतां पाण्डवानाम्। सम्मार्जतां वेश्म परैतु शीघ्रं तत्रास्तु दासीभिरपुण्यशीला॥
en: Duryodhana said Come Khattwa, bring here Draupadi, the dear and the beloved wife of the Pandavas. Let her be forced to sweep the chambers, and let the unfortunate women remain where our serving women are.

sn: विदुर उवाचदुर्विभाष भाषितं त्वादृशेन न मन्द सम्बुध्यसि पाशबद्धः।प्रपाते त्वं लम्बमानो न वेत्सि व्याघ्रान् मृगः कोपयसेऽतिवेलम्॥
en: Vidura said O wicked man, do you not know that by uttering such words you are tying yourself with cords? Do you not feel that you are standing on the edge of the precipice? Do you not know that being but a deer you are provoking to anger so many tigers? ?

sn: आशीविषास्ते शिरसि पूर्णकोपा महाविषाः। मा कोपिष्ठाः सुमन्दात्मन् मा गमस्त्वं यमक्षयम्॥
en: O greatly wicked-minded man, deadly venomous and angry snakes are on your head. Do not provoke them any further and go to the land of Yama.

sn: न हि दासीत्वमापन्ना कृष्णा भवितुमर्हति। अनीशेन हि राज्ञैषा पणे न्यस्तेति मे मतिः॥
en: In my opinion the slavery cannot attach to Krishna (Draupadi), as she was staked by the king (Yudhisthira) after he lost himself and ceased to be his own master.

sn: अयं धत्ते वेणुरिवात्मघाती फलं राजा धृतराष्ट्रस्य पुत्रः। द्यूतं हि वैराय महाभयाय मत्तो न बुध्यत्ययमन्तकालम्॥
en: Like bamboo which bears fruits when it is about to die, this king, this son of Dhritarashtra, wins this treasure at play. Intoxicated (in play), he does not perceive in his these last moments what enmity and frightful terrors the dice bring in.

sn: नारुन्तुदः स्यान्न नृशंसवादी न हीनतः परमभ्याददीत। ययास्य वाचा पर उद्विजेत न तां वदेदुषती पापलोक्याम्॥
en: No man should utter harsh words, and thus pierce the heart of others. No man should subjugate his enemies by dice and by such other foul means. No one should utter such words, as give pain and lead men to hell and annoys others.

sn: समुच्चरन्त्यतिवादाश्च वक्त्राद् पैराहतः शोचति रात्र्यहानि। परस्य नामर्मसु ते पतन्त तान् पण्डितो नावसृजेत् परेषु॥
en: One man utters from his lips words that are harsh. Stung by them the other burns day and night. Those words pierce the very heart of another. Therefore, the learned men should never utter such (harsh) words towards others.

sn: अजो हि शस्त्रमगिलत् किलैकः शस्त्रे विपन्ने शिरसास्य भूमौ। निकृन्तनं स्वस्य कण्दस्य घोरं तद्वद् वैरं मा कृथाः पाण्डुपुत्रैः॥
en: Once at a time a goat swallowed a hook, and when it was pierced with it, the hunter placed its head on the ground and frightfully tore its throat in drawing it out. Like it do not create a terrible enmity with the Pandavas.

sn: न किंचिदित्थं प्रवदन्ति पार्था वनेचरं वा गृहमेधिनं वा। तपस्विनं वा परिपूर्णविद्यं भषन्ति हैवं श्वनराः सदैव।॥
en: The sons of Pritha never use such words. It is only low men who are like dogs that use harsh words towards all classes of people, namely towards those that live in the forest, those that lead domestic life, those that are employed in asceticism, and those that are greatly learned.

sn: द्वारं सुघोरं नरकस्य जिह्यं न बुध्यते धृतराष्ट्रस्य पुत्रः। तमन्वेतारो बहवः कुरूणां द्यूतोदये सह दुःशासनेन॥
en: The son of Dhritarashtra does not know that dishonesty is one of the fearful doors of hell. Many Kurus with Dushasana amongst them have followed him in the path of dishonesty in this play at dice.

sn: मज्जन्त्यलावूनि शिलाः प्लवन्ते मुह्यन्ति नावोऽम्भसि शश्वदेव। मूढो राजा धृतराष्ट्रस्य पुत्रो न मे वाचः पथ्यरूपाः शृणोति॥
en: Even grounds may sink and stone may float and boats may always sink in water, but still this foolish king (Duryodhana) the son of Dhritarashtra, will not listen to my words which are like regimen to him.

sn: अन्तो नूनं भवितायं कुरूणां सुदारुणः सर्वहरो विनाशः। वाचः काव्याः सुहृदां पथ्यरूपा न श्रूयन्ते वर्धते लोभ एव॥
en: He will certainly be the cause of the destruction of the Kurus. When the worlds of wisdom spoken by friends, words of wisdom spoken by friends, words that are like the proper regimen, are not listened to, when temptation is on the increase, a fearful and universal destruction is sure to overtake all the Kurus.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच धिगस्तु क्षत्तारमिति ब्रुवाणो दर्पण मत्तो धृतराष्ट्रस्य पुत्रः। मुवाच चैनं परमार्यमध्ये॥
en: Vaishampayana said Intoxicated with pride, the son of Dhritarashtra (Duryodhana) spoke. “Fie on Khattwa.” Casting his eye on the Pratikamin, he spoke thus in the Sabha and in the midst of (all) the revered elders.

sn: दुर्योधन उवाच प्रातिकामिन् द्रौपदीमानयस्व न ते भयं विद्यते पाण्डवेभ्यः। क्षत्ता ह्ययं विवदत्येव भीतो न चास्माकं वृद्धिकामः सदैव॥
en: Duryodhana said Go, Pratikamin and bring Draupadi here. You have no fear from the Pandavas. It is only Khattwa (Vidura) who savers in fear. He never wishes for our prosperity.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्तः प्रातिकामी स सूतः प्रायाच्छीघ्रं राजवचो निशम्य। प्रविश्य च श्वेव हि सिंहगोष्ठं समासदन्महिषीं पाण्डवानाम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having been thus commanded and having heard the words of the king, the Pratikamin, the man of the Suta caste, went with (great haste). As a dog enters a lion's den, he (entered the house) and came to the queen of the Pandavas.

sn: प्रातिकाम्युवाच युधिष्ठिरो द्यूतमदेन मत्तो दुर्योधनो द्रौपदि त्वामजैषीत्। सा त्वं प्रपद्यस्व धृतराष्ट्रस्य वेश्म न यामि त्वां कर्मणे याज्ञसेनि॥
en: Pratikamin said O Draupadi, Yudhisthira having been intoxicated with dice you have been won by Duryodhana. Therefore, O Yajnaseni, come now to the house of Dhritarashtra. I shall ' menial work.

sn: द्रौपद्युवाच कथं त्वेवं वदसि प्रातिकामिन् को हि दीव्येद् भार्यया राजपुत्रः। मूढो राजा द्यूतमदेन मत्तो ह्यभूनान्यत् कैतवमस्य किंचित्॥
en: Duryodhana said O Pratikamin, why do you say so? Is there any prince who plays staking his (own) wife? The king was certainly intoxicated with dice, or else could he not find any other object or stake?

sn: प्रातिकाम्युवाच यदा नाभूत् कैतवमन्यदस्य तदादेवीत् पाण्डवोऽजातशत्रुः। न्यस्ताः पूर्वं भ्रातरस्तेन राज्ञा स्वयं चात्मा त्वमथो राजपुत्रि॥
en: Pratikamin said When he had nothing else to stake, it was then that Ajatasatru (Yudhisthira), the son of Pandu, staked you. The king had first staked his brothers, then himself, and then, O princess, he staked you.

sn: द्रौपद्युवाच गच्छ त्वं कितवं गत्वा सभायां पृच्छ सूतजा किं नु पूर्वं पराजैषीरात्मानमथवा नु माम्॥
en: Draupadi said O son of Suta, go (back) to the Sabha and ask that gambler (Yudhisthira) whom he lost first, himself or me.

sn: एतज्ज्ञात्वा समागच्छ ततो मां नय सूतज। ज्ञात्वा चिकीर्षितमहं राज्ञो यास्यामि दुःखिता॥
en: Ascertaining. this, O son of Suta, come here and then take me with you. Knowing the desire of the king (Yudhisthira), I shall go with a sorrowful heart.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच सभां गत्वा स चोवाच द्रौपद्यास्तद् वचस्तदा। युधिष्ठिरं नरेन्द्राणां मध्ये स्थितमिदं वचः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having returned to the Sabha, he (Pratikamin) told all present there the words of Draupadi. He spoke these words to Yudhisthira sitting in the midst of the kings.

sn: कस्येशो नः पराजैषीरिति त्वामाह द्रौपदी। किं नु पूर्वं पराजैषीरात्मानमथवापि माम्॥
en: Pratikamin said Draupadi has asked you, "Whose lord were you at the time when you lost me in play? Did you lose yourself first or me?

sn: युधिष्ठिरस्तु निश्चेता गतसत्त्व इवाभवत्। न तं सूतं प्रत्युवाच वचनं साध्यसाधु वा॥
en: Vaishampayana said Yudhishthira sat like one demented and deprived of reason. He did not five any reply to the Suta, good or ill.

sn: दुर्योधन उवाच इहैवागत्य पाञ्चाली प्रश्नमेनं प्रभाषताम्। इहैव सर्वे शृण्वन्तु तस्याश्चैतस्य यद् वचः॥
en: Duryodhana said Let the princess of Panchala come here and put her question. Let every one here in this Sabha hear the worlds that pass between them (her and Yudhisthira).

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच स गत्वा राजभवनं दुर्योधनवशानुगः। उवाच द्रौपदी सूतः प्रातिकामी व्यथान्वितः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Going back to the palace, himself much distressed, the Suta, Pratikamin obedient to the command of Duryodhana, spoke thus to Draupadi.

sn: प्रातिकाम्युवाच सभ्यास्त्वमी राजपुत्र्याह्वयन्ति मन्ये प्राप्तः संक्षयः कौरवाणाम्। न वै समृद्धिं पालयते लघीयान् यस्त्वां सभां नेष्यति राजपुत्रि॥
en: Pratikamin said O princess, those that are in the assembly are summoning you. It seems the destruction of the Kurus is near at hand. O princess, when the weak-brained (Duryodhana) is for taking you before the assembly, he will no longer be able to protect his prosperity.

sn: द्रौपद्युवाच एवं नूनं व्यदधात् संविधाता स्पर्शावुभौ स्पृशतो वृद्धबालौ। धर्मं त्वेकं परमं प्राह लोके स नः शमं धास्यति गोप्यमानः॥
en: Draupadi said The great ordainer of the world has ordained this. Happiness and misery come to both the old and the young (the wise and the unwise). Dharma has been said to be the highest object in the world. If cherished, it certainly pours blessings on us.

sn: सोऽयं धर्मो मात्यगात् कौरवान् वै सभ्यान् गत्वा पृच्छ धर्म्यं वचो मे। ते मां ब्रूयुनिश्चितं तत् करिष्ये धर्मात्मानो नीतिमन्तो वरिष्ठाः॥
en: Let not Dharma now abandon the Kurus. Going back to the Sabha, speak these my words conformable to virtue and morality. I am ready to do what those virtuous-minded elder conversant with the precepts of morality, definitely tell me (to do).

sn: श्रुत्वा सूतस्तद्वचो याज्ञसेन्याः सभां गत्वा प्राह वाक्यं तदानीम्। निर्बन्धं तं धार्तराष्ट्रस्य बुद्ध्वा॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having heard these words of Yajnaseni (Draupadi), the Suta returned to the Sabha and repeated her words. But all sat with downcast faces, knowing the eagerness and resolution of the son of Dhritarashtra (Duryodhana).

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच युधिष्ठिरस्तु तच्छ्रुत्वा दुर्योधनचिकीर्षितम्। द्रौपद्याः सम्मतं दूतं प्राहिणोद् भरतर्षभ।॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, having heard of the intentions of Duryodhana, Yudhisthira sent a trusted messenger to Draupadi,

sn: एकवस्त्रा त्वधोनीवी रोदमाना रजस्वला। सभामागम्य पाञ्चालि श्वशुरस्याग्रतो भव॥
en: (Saying) "Panchali should appear before her father-in-law by coming to the Sabha, though she is weeping and attired in one piece of cloth with her naval exposed in consequence of her season having came.”

sn: अथ त्वामागतां दृष्ट्वा राजपुत्रीं सभां तदा। सभ्याः सर्वे विनिन्देरन् मनोभिधृतराष्ट्रजम्॥
en: O king, having gone to Krishna's (Draupadi's) house in great speed, the intelligent (messenger) informed her of the intentions of Dharmaraja (Yudhisthira).

sn: स गत्वा त्वरितं दूतः कृष्णाया भवनं नृप। न्यवेदयन्मतं धीमान् धर्मराजस्य निश्चितम्॥
en: The illustrious Pandavas, distressed and sorrowful and bound by promise, could not settle what they should do.

sn: पाण्डवाश्च महात्मानो दीना दुःखसमन्विताः। सत्येनातिपरीताङ्गा नोदीक्षन्ते स्म किंचन॥
en: Looking at their countenance, the king Duryodhana with cheerful heart thus addressed the Suta, “O Pratikamin, bring her here. Let the Kurus give their answer before her presence."

sn: ततस्त्वेषां मुखमालोक्य राजा दुर्योधन: सूतमुवाच हृष्टः। इहैवैतामानय प्रातिकामिन् प्रत्यक्षमस्या: कुरवो ब्रुवन्तु॥
en: Thereupon the Suta, ever obedient to his command and at the same time afraid of the anger of Drupada's daughter, giving up his pride, again spoke thus in the assembly, "What shall I say to Krishna (Draupadi)?

sn: ततः सूतस्तस्य वशानुगामी भीतश्च कोपाद् दुपदात्मजायाः. नुवाच कृष्णां किमहं ब्रवीमि॥
en: Duryodhana said O Dushasana, this foolish son of Suta is afraid of Vrikodara (Bhima). Go you yourself and forcibly bring Yajnaseni (Draupadi) here. Our enemies are now dependant on our will. What can they do?

sn: दुर्योधन उवाच दुःशासनैष मम सूतपुत्रो वृकोदरादुद्विजतेऽल्पचेताः। स्वयं प्रगृह्यानय याज्ञसेनी किं ते करिष्यन्त्यवशाः सपत्नाः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having heard the command of his brother, that prince (Dushasana) rose with blood red eyes. Entering the house of those great carwarriors (the Pandavas), he thus spoke to the princess, Draupadi.

sn: ततः समुत्थाय स राजपुत्रः श्रुत्वा भ्रातुः शासनं रक्तदृष्टिः। मित्यब्रवीद् द्रौपदी राजपुत्रीम्॥
en: Dushasana said O Panchali, O Krishna, come you have been won by us. Behold Duryodhana (now) casting aside your modesty. O lady of eyes like the wide lotus leaves, accept the Kurus as your lords. You have been virtuously won by us, therefore come to the Sabha.

sn: एह्येहि पाञ्चालि जितासि कृष्णे दुर्योधनं पश्य विमुक्तलज्जा। कुरून् भजस्वायतपत्रनेत्रे धर्मेण लब्धासि सभां परैहि॥
en: Vaishampayana said Thereupon she, being (much) distressed, rose up in great affliction, and covering her pale face with her hands, ran to the place where were the ladies of the old king, the foremost of the Kurus (Dhritarashtra.)

sn: ततः समुत्थाय सुदुर्मनाः सा विवर्णमामृज्य मुखं करेण। आर्ता प्रदुद्राव यतः स्त्रियस्ता वृद्धस्य राज्ञः कुरुपुङ्गवस्य॥
en: Thereupon Dushasana, roaring in anger, ran after her and seized the queen (Draupadi) by her long, blue and wavy hair.

sn: ततो जवेनाभिससार रोषाद् दुःशासनस्तामभिगर्जमानः। दीर्येषु नीलेष्वथ चोर्मिमत्सु जग्राह केशेषु नरेन्द्रपत्नीम्॥
en: The hair that was (once) sprinkled with the water sanctified with Mantras in the great Rajasuya sacrifice were now forcibly seized by the son of Dhritarashtra who disregarded the prowess of the Pandavas.

sn: ये राजसूयावभृथे जलेन महाक्रतौ मन्त्रपूतेन सिक्ताः। ते पाण्डवानां परिभूय वीर्य बलात् प्रमृष्टा धृतराष्ट्रजेन॥
en: Dragging the greatly long-haired Krishna (Draupadi) as if she was protectorless, although she had great protectors, Dushasana brought her into the Sabha trembling like the banian tree in a storm.

sn: मानीय कृष्णामतिदीर्घकेशीम्। च्चकर्ष वायुः कदलीमिवार्ताम्॥
en: Having been thus dragged by him, she best her body down and spoke in a low voice “O wretch, O rude one, you should not take me before the assembly. I am in my season. I am attired only in one cloth."

sn: सा कृष्यमाणा नमिताङ्गयष्टिः शनैरुवाचाथ रजस्वलास्मि एकं च वासो मम मन्दबुद्धे सभां नेतुं नार्हसि मामनार्य॥
en: While she was piteously praying to Krishna and Vishnu (Arjuna) who were Hari (Narayana) and Nara (on earth), he (Dushasana) dragged her forcibly by her black hair.

sn: ततोऽब्रवीत् तां प्रसभं निगृह्य केशेषु कृष्णेषु तदा स कृष्णाम्। कृष्णं च जिष्णुं च हरिं नरं च त्राणाय विक्रोशति याज्ञसेनी॥
en: Dushasana said O Yajnaseni, whether you are in your season, whether you are attired in one cloth, or whether you are naked, when you have been won (by us) at dice and made our slave, you are to live amongst our serving women as you best can.

sn: दुःशासन उवाच रजस्वला वा भव याज्ञसेनि एकाम्बरा वाप्यथवा विवस्त्रा। द्यूते जिता चासि कृतासि दासी दासीषु वासश्च यथोपजोषम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said With dishevelled hair and her attire half loosened on account of the cruel dragging of Dushasana, the modest Krishna (Draupadi), being consumed as it were by anger, thus spoke in a low voice.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच प्रकीर्णकेशी पतितार्धवस्त्रा दुःशासनेन व्यवधूयमाना। ह्रीमत्यमर्षेण च दह्यमाना। शनैरिदं वाक्यमुवाच कृष्णा॥
en: Draupadi said All these persons in this assembly are men learned in all the Shastras, all devoted to the performances of sacrifices and other rites and all equal to Indra (in prowess). Some of them are my Gurus (superiors) and some who stand to me as such. I cannot stay before them in this state.

sn: द्रौपद्युवाच इमे सभायामुपनीतशास्त्राः क्रियावन्तः सर्व एवेन्द्रकल्पाः। गुरुस्थाना गुरवश्चैव सर्वे तेषामग्रे नोत्सहे स्थातुमेवम्॥
en: O Wretch, O man of cruel deeds, do not make me uncovered. Do not drag me in this way. The princes (the Pandavas) will not pardon you, even if the celestial with Indra become your allies.

sn: नृशंसकर्मंस्त्वमनार्यवृत्त मा मा विवस्त्रां कुरु मा विकर्षीः। न मर्षयेद्युस्तव राजपुत्राः सेन्द्राश्च देवा यदि ते सहायाः॥ धर्मे स्थितो धर्मसुतो महात्मा धर्मश्च सूक्ष्मो निपुणोपलक्ष्यः। मिच्छामि दोषं न गुणान् विसृज्य॥
en: The high-souled of Dharma (Yudhisthira) is (now) bound by the obligation of the rules of morality. The ways of Dharma is subtle. Those only can ascertain them who son possess great clearness of vision. Forgetting his virtue, I am unwilling to admit even an atom of fault in my husband (Yudhisthira.)

sn: इदं त्वकार्यं कुरुवीरमध्ये रजस्वलां यत् परिकर्षसे माम्। न चापि कश्चित् कुरुतेऽत्र कुत्सां ध्रुवं तवेदं मतमभ्युपेताः॥
en: It is a most unworthy act that you are dragging me before these Kuru heroes, though I am in my season. But none rebukes you here; they are certainly of the same mind with you.

sn: धिगस्तु नष्टः खलु भारतानां धर्मस्तथा क्षत्रविदां च वृत्तम्। यत्र ह्यतीतां कुरुधर्मवेलां प्रेक्षन्ति सर्वे कुरवः सभायाम्॥
en: O Fie! When all the Kurus in this assembly look silently on this act which transgresses the shore of the Kuru morality; the morality of the Bharatas have certainly been destroyed and the usage of those conversant with the Kshatriya practices have surely disappeared.

sn: द्रोणस्य भीष्मस्य च नास्ति सत्त्वं क्षत्तुस्तथैवास्य महात्मनोऽपि। राज्ञस्तथा हीममधर्ममुग्रं न लक्षयन्ते कुरुवृद्धमुख्याः॥
en: Drona and Bhisma, Khattwa and also the king (Dhritarashtra) have lost their greatness, else why do these best of the Kuru elders look silently on this great crime.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तथा ब्रुवन्ती करुणं सुमध्यमा भर्तृन् कटाक्षैः कुपितानपश्यत्। सा पाण्डवान् कोपपरीतदेहान् संदीपयामास कटाक्षपातैः॥
en: Vaishampayana said The slender-waisted (Draupadi) thus cried in distress in that Sabha and cast a glance on her enraged husbands, the Pandavas, who were filled with fearful wrath. She inflamed them more by her that glance.

sn: हतेन राज्येन तथा धनेन रत्नैश्च मुख्यैर्न तथा बभूव। यथा त्रपाकोपसमीरितेन कृष्णाकटाक्षेण बभूव दुःखम्॥
en: They were not so much pained at the robbing of their kingdom, their wealth, and their costly gems, as they were by that glance of Krishna (Draupadi), full of modesty and anger.

sn: मवेक्षमाणां कृपणान् पतीस्तान्। मुवाच दासीति हसन् सशब्दम्॥
en: Seeing Krishna (Draupadi) looking at her helpless husbands, Dushasana dragged her more forcibly and repeatedly called her "slave" "slave," and he laughed aloud.

sn: कर्णस्तु तद्वाक्यमतीव हृष्टः सम्पूजयामास हसन् सशब्दम्। गान्धारराजः सुबलस्य पुत्र स्तथैव दुःशासनमभ्यनन्दत्॥
en: At these words, Karna became vary glad and approved them by laughing aloud. The Gandhara king, the son of Subala (Shakuni), similarly applauded Dushasana.

sn: सभ्यास्त ये तत्र बभूवुरन्ये ताभ्यामृते धार्तराष्ट्रेण चैवा तेषामभूद् दुःखमतीव कृष्णां दृष्ट्वा सभायां परिकृष्यमाणाम्॥
en: Amongst all those that were present in the assembly, except these three and the son of Dhritarashtra (Duryodhana), every one was filled with great sorrow on seeing Krishna (Draupadi) thus dragged in the Sabha.

sn: भीष्म उवाच न धर्मसौक्ष्यात् सुभगे विवेक्तु शक्नोमि ते प्रश्नमिमं यथावत्। अस्वाम्यशक्तः पणितुं परस्वं स्त्रियाश्च भर्तुर्वशतां समीक्ष्य।॥
en: Bhisma said O blessed lady, knowing that one who has no wealth of his own cannot stake the wealth belonging to others and (knowing also) that wives are always at the command and disposals of their husbands, I am unable to decide properly the point put forward by you. The ways of morality is subtle.

sn: त्यजेत सर्वां पृथिवीं समृद्धां युधिष्ठिरो धर्ममथो न जह्यात्। उक्तं जितोऽस्मीति च पाण्डवेन तस्मान्न शक्नोमि विवेक्तुमेतत्॥
en: Yudhishthira can abandon the whole world full of wealth, but he will never sacrifice morality. The Pandavas (Yudhisthira) himself has said, "I am won'. Therefore, I am unable to decide this matter.

sn: द्यूतेऽद्वितीयः शकुनि रेषु कुन्तीसुतस्तेन निसृष्टकामः। स्तस्मान्न ते प्रश्नमिमं ब्रवीमि॥
en: Shakuni is matchless in dice. The son of Kunti has still willfully staked with him. The illustrious (Yudhisthira) does not consider that Shakuni played with him deceitfully. Therefore, I am unable to decide this matter.

sn: द्रौपद्युवाच र्दुष्टात्मभिरैंकृतिकैः सभायाम्। द्यूतप्रियैर्नातिकृतप्रयत्नः कस्मादयं नाम निसृष्टकामः॥
en: Draupadi said The king (Yudhisthira) was summoned to this assembly, and through he does not possess any skill in dice, yet he was made to play with skillful, wicked, deceitful and desperate gamblers. How then can he be said to have staked voluntarily?

sn: रबुध्यमानः कुरुपाण्डवायः। सम्भूय सर्वेश्च जितोऽपि यस्मात् पश्चादयं कैतवमभ्युपेतः॥
en: The chief of the Kurus and the Pandavas was deprived of his senses by the wretches of deceitful conduct and unholy instincts acting in concert. He could not understand their tricks through vanquished, but he has now understood all.

sn: मीशाः सुतानां च तथा स्नुषाणाम्। समीक्ष्य सर्वे मम चापि वाक्यं विब्रूत मे प्रश्नमिमं यथावत्॥
en: Here in this assembly are present the Kurus who are the lords of their sons and daughter-in-law. Let all of them, after duly reflecting on my words, properly answer me the question I have asked.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच मवेक्षमाणां कृपणान् पतीस्तान्। दुःशासनः परुषाण्यप्रियाणि वाक्यान्युवाचामधुराणि चैव॥
en: Vaishampayana said Dushasana spoke many disagreeable and harsh words to Krishna (Draupadi) who was thus piteously weeping and bewailing and casting glances on her helpless husbands.

sn: तां कृष्यमाणां च रजस्वलांच स्रस्तोत्तरीयामतदहमाणाम्। वृकोदरः प्रेक्ष्य युधिष्ठिरं च चकार कोयं परमार्तरूपः॥
en: Seeing her who was in her season thus dragged and her upper garments loosened, seeing her in that condition which she did not deserve, Vrikodara (Bhima), afflicted beyond endurance, cast his eyes on Yudhisthira and gave vest to his anger.

sn: भीम उवाच भवन्ति गेहे बन्धक्यः कितवानां युधिष्ठिर। न ताभिरुत दीव्यन्ति दया चैवास्ति तास्वपि॥
en: Bhima said O Yudhisthira, the gamblers have in their house many loose women. They do not play staking even those women. They have kindness even towards them.

sn: काश्यो यद् धनमाहार्षीद् द्रव्यं यच्चान्यदुत्तमम्। तथान्ये पृथिवीपाला यानि रत्नान्युपाहरन्॥ वाहनानि धनं चैव कवचान्यायुधानि च। राज्यमात्मा वयं चैव कैतवेन हृतं परैः॥
en: Whatever wealth and other excellent articles which the king of Kashi gave, and the gems and jewels, animals, wealth, armours, and weapons which the other kings, presented, nay even our kingdom, yourself and ourselves, have all been won by our enemies at play.

sn: न च मे तत्र कोपोऽभूत् सर्वस्येशो हि नो भवान्। इमं त्वतिक्रमं मन्ये द्रौपदी यत्र पण्यते॥
en: Even at all this, my anger was not excited, for you are our lord. But I consider it a highly improper act, this your staking Draupadi.

sn: एषा ह्यनहती बाला पाण्डवान् प्राप्य कौरवैः। त्वत्कृते क्लिश्यते क्षुदैर्नृशंसैरकृतात्मभिः॥
en: Having obtained the Pandavas as her husband, this innocent girl does not deserve this (treatment). It is only for you that she is persecuted by these low, despicable, cruel and mean-minded Kurus.

sn: अस्याः कृते मन्युरयं त्वयि राजन् निपात्यते। बाहू ते सम्प्रधक्ष्यामि सहदेवाग्निमानय॥
en: O king, it is for her sake that my anger falls on you. I shall burn your hands. Sahadeva, bring some fire?

sn: अर्जुन उवाच न पुरा भीमसेन त्वमीदृशीर्वदिता गिरः। परैस्ते नाशितं नूनं नृशंसैर्धर्मगौरवम्॥
en: Arjuna said O Bhimasena, you have never before uttered such swords as these. Your high morality has certainly been destroyed by these cruel foes.

sn: न सकामाः परे कार्या धर्ममेवाचरोत्तमम्। भ्रातरं धार्मिकं ज्येष्ठं कोऽतिवर्तितुमर्हति॥
en: You should not fulfill the wishes of the enemy. Practise the highest morality. Should any body transgress his virtuous elders brother?

sn: आहूतो हि परै राजा क्षात्रं व्रतमनुस्मरन्। दीव्यते परकामेन तन्नः कीर्तिकरं महत्॥
en: Having been summoned by the Kurus and having remembered the Kshatriyas Dharma (usage), the king played at dice against his will. This is certainly conductive to one's great fame.

sn: भीमसेन उवाच एवमस्मिन् कृतं विद्यां यदि नाहं धनंजय। दीप्तेऽग्नौ सहितौ बाहू निर्दहेयं बलादिव॥
en: Bhima said O Dhananjaya, if I had not know what the king did, he did according to the Kshatriyas usage, I would have long ago snatched his arms by force and brunt them in a blazing fire.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तथा तान् दुःखितान् दृष्ट्वा पाण्डवान् धृतराष्ट्रजः। कृष्यमाणां च पाञ्चालीं विकर्ण इदमब्रवीत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Seeing the Pandavas thus distressed and the Panchala princess thus afflicted, the son of Dhritarashtra, Vikarna, thus spoke.

sn: विकरण उवाच याज्ञसेन्या यदुक्तं तद् वाक्यं विबूत पार्थिवाः। अविवेकेन वाक्यस्य नरकः सद्य एव नः॥
en: Vikarna said O kings, answer the question that has been asked by Yajnaseni (Draupadi). If we do not decide a matter referred to us, we shall certainly have to go to hell without delay.

sn: भीष्मश्च धृतराष्ट्रश्च कुरुवृद्धतमावुभौ। समेत्य नाहतुः किंचिद् विदुरश्च महामतिः॥
en: Bhisma and Dhritarashtra, the two eldest of the Kurus, and the high-souled Vidura, uniting together, do not say any thing.

sn: भारद्वाजश्च सर्वेषामाचार्यः कृप एव च। कुत एतावपि प्रश्नं नाहतुर्द्विजसत्तमौ॥
en: The son of Bharadvaja (Drona), the preceptor of all of us and also Kripa, why these best of Brahmanas do not answer her question?

sn: ये त्वन्ये पृथिवीपालाः समेताः सर्वतो दिशः। कामक्रोधौ समुत्सृज्य ते ब्रुवन्तु यथामति॥
en: Let the kings that have assembled here from all directions, leaving aside all motives of anger and desire, speak our according to their judgement.

sn: यदिदं द्रौपदीवाक्यमुक्तवत्यसकृच्छुभा। विमृश्य कस्य कः पक्षः पार्थिवा वदतोत्तरम्॥
en: O kings, answer the question asked by Draupadi and say after due reflection on which side each of you is.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवं स बहुशः सर्वानुक्तवांस्तान् सभासदः। न च ते पृथिवीपालास्तमूचुः साध्वसाधु वा॥
en: Vaishampayana said Thus did he (Vikarna) repeatedly appeal to those that were present in the assembly to answer Draupadi's question. But the kings present did not say a word good or ill.

sn: उक्त्वा सकृत् तथा सर्वान् विकर्णः पृथिवीपतीन्। पाणौ पाणिं विनिष्पिष्य निःश्वसन्निदमब्रवीत्॥
en: Repeatedly appealing to the kings, rubbing his palms and sighing like a snake, Vikarna thus (again) spoke.

sn: विकरण उवाच विद्वत पृथिवीपाला वाक्यं मा वा कथंचन। मन्ये न्याय्यं यदत्राहं तद्धि वक्ष्यामि कौरवाः॥
en: Vikarna said O kings, O Kurus, whether you answer this question or not, I shall say what I consider just and proper.

sn: चत्वार्याहुनश्रेष्ठा व्यसनानि महीक्षिताम्। मृगयां पानमक्षांश्च ग्राम्ये चैवातिरक्तताम्॥
en: O best of men, it has been said that hunting, drinking, gambling, and enjoying women are the four vices of the kings.

sn: एतेषु हि नरः सक्तो धर्ममुत्सृज्य वर्तते। यथायुक्तेन च कृतां क्रियां लोको न मन्यते॥
en: The man who is addicted to those vices lives by forsaking virtue. People do not consider the acts done by a person who is thus improperly engaged as of any authority.

sn: तदयं पाण्डुपुत्रेण व्यसने वर्तता भृशम्। समाहूतेन कितवैरास्थितौ द्रौपदीपणः॥
en: This son of Pandu (Yudhisthira), white madly engaged in one of these vicious acts (namely gambling) and urged thereto by dec sitful gamblers, staked Draupadi.

sn: साधारणी च सर्वेषां पाण्डवानामनिन्दिता। जितेन पूर्वं चानेन पाण्डवेन कृतः पणः॥
en: The faultness Draupadi is the common wife of all the sons of Pandu. Having first lost himself, the Pandava (Yudhisthira) offered her as a stake.

sn: इयं च कीर्तिता कृष्णा सौबलेन पणार्थिना। एतत् सर्वं विचार्याहं मन्ये न विजितामिमाम्॥
en: The son of Subala (Shakuni), himself being desirous of a stake, prevailed upon the king to stake Krishna (Draupadi). Considering all these circumstances, I consider Draupadi as not won.

sn: एतच्छ्रुत्वा महान् नादः सभ्यानामुदतिष्ठत। विकर्णं शंसमानानां सौबलं चापि निन्दताम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Hearing these words, a loud uproar rose from those present in the assembly. They all applauded Vikarna and censured the son of Subala (Shakuni).

sn: तस्मिन्नुपरते शब्दे राधेयः क्रोधमूर्च्छितः। प्रगृह्य रुचिरं बाहुमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: The son of Radha (Karna) became out of sense from anger. Waving his well sapped arms he spoke thus.

sn: कर्ण उवाच दृश्यन्ते वै विकर्णेह वैकृतानि बहून्यपि। तज्जातस्तद्विनाशाय यथाग्निररणिप्रजः॥
en: Karna said O Vikarna, I observed many opposite and inconsistent conditions in this assembly. As the fire, produced from a faggot, itself, so you will be consumed by you this anger.

sn: एते न किंचिदप्याहुश्चोदिता ह्यपि कृष्णया। धर्मेण विजितामेतां मन्यन्ते दुपदात्मजाम्॥
en: These (great) personages (present) here, through (repeatedly) urged by Krishna (Draupadi), have not uttered a single word. They all consider that the daughter of Drupada has been righteously won.

sn: त्वं तु केवलबाल्येन धार्तराष्ट्र विदीर्यसे। यद् ब्रवीषि सभामध्ये बालः स्थविरभाषितम्॥
en: O son of Dhritarashtra, you alone for your boyish age are bursting into rage. Though you are but a boy, you speak as if you are an old man.

sn: न च धर्मं यथावत् त्वं वेत्सि दुर्योधनावर। यद् ब्रवीषि जितां कृष्णां न जितेति सुमन्दधीः॥
en: O younger brother of Duryodhana, you know not what really the rules of morality are. You say like a fool that this Krishna (Draupadi), who has been won, as not won (at all).

sn: कथं ह्यविजितां कृष्णां मन्यसे धृतराष्ट्रज। यदा सभायां सर्वस्वं न्यस्तवान् पाण्डवाग्रजः॥
en: o son of Dhritarashtra, how do you consider that Krishna (Draupadi) is not won, when the eldest of the Pandavas have staked all his possessions in this assembly?

sn: अभ्यन्तरा च सर्वस्वे द्रौपदी भरतर्षभ। एवं धर्मजितां कृष्णां मन्यसे न जितां कथम्॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, Draupadi is (surely) included in his possessions. Why do you consider that Krishna (Draupadi) who has been righteously won as not won?

sn: कीर्तिता द्रौपदी वाचा अनुज्ञाता च पाण्डवैः। भवत्यविजिता केन हेतुनैषा मता तव॥
en: Draupadi was mentioned (by Shakuni) in conversation, and she was approved of as a stake by the Pandava, why is it (then) your opinion that she is not won?

sn: मन्यसे वा सभामेतामानीतामेकवाससम्। अधर्मेणेति तत्रापि शृणु मे वाक्यमुत्तमम्॥
en: If you consider it wrong to bring her in the Sabha attired in only one piece of cloth, listen to the excellent words I say.

sn: एको भर्ता स्त्रिया देवैर्विहितः कुरुनन्दन। इयं त्वनेकवशगा बन्धकीति विनिश्चिता॥
en: O descendant of Kuru, it has been ordained by the gods that a woman should have only one husband; she (Draupadi) has (however) many husbands; therefore it is certain that she is an unchaste woman.

sn: अस्याः सभामानयनं च चित्रमिति मे मतिः। एकाम्बरध रत्वं वाप्यथ वापि विवस्त्रता॥
en: In my opinion there is nothing surprising if she is brought before the assembly in one cloth or if she be made naked.

sn: यच्चैषां द्रविणं किंचिद् या चैषा ये पाण्डवाः। सौबलेनेह तत् सर्वं धर्मेण विजितं वसु॥
en: Whatever wealth the Pandavas had, including her and also the Pandavas themselves, have been righteously won by the son of Subala (Shakuni).

sn: दुःशासन सुबालोऽयं विकर्णः प्राज्ञवादिकः। पाण्डवानां च वासांसि द्रौपद्याश्चाप्युहर॥
en: O Dushasana, this Vikarna, speaking words of wisdom, is but a boy. Take off the robes of the Pandavas and also that of Draupadi.

sn: तच्छ्रुत्वा पाण्डवाः सर्वे स्वानि वासांसि भारत। अवकीर्योत्तरीयाणि सभायां समुपाविशन्॥
en: Vaishampayana said O descendant of Bharata, having heard this, the Pandavas took off their upper garments, and throwing them down, they sat (silently) in the Sabha.

sn: ततो दुःशासनो राजन् द्रौपद्या वसनं बलात्। सभामध्ये समाक्षिप्य व्यपाक्रष्टुं प्रचक्रमे॥
en: O king, thereupon Dushasana, in the sight of all (present) in the assembly, began to drag forcibly the cloth of Draupadi.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच आकृष्यमाणे वसने द्रौपद्याश्चिन्तितो हरिः। गोविन्द द्वारकावासिन् कृष्ण गोपीजनप्रियः॥
en: When the cloth of Draupadi was being thus dragged, she thought of Hari. Draupadi said O Govinda, O dweller of Dwarika, O Krishna, O favourite of the milk maids,

sn: कौरवैः परिभूतां मां किं न जानासि केशव हे नाथ हे रमानाथ व्रजनाथार्तिनाशन। कौरवार्णवमग्नां मामुद्धरस्व जनार्दन॥
en: O Keshava, do you not see that I am persecuted by the Kurus. O lord, O husband of Lakshmi O lord of Vraja, O destroyer of all affliction, O Janardana, save me who am sinking in the Kuru ocean!

sn: कृष्ण कृष्ण महायोगिन् विश्वात्मन् विश्वभावन। प्रपन्नां पाहि गोविन्द कुरुमध्येऽवसीदतीम्॥
en: O Krishna, O great Yogi, O soul of the universe, O creator of the world, O Govinda, save me who am distressed, who am losing her senses in the midst of the Kurus!

sn: इत्यनुस्मृत्य कृष्णं सा हरिं त्रिभुवनेश्वरम्। प्रारुदद् दुःखिता राजन् मुखमाच्छाद्य भामिनी॥
en: Vaishampayana said O king, thus being afflicted, the lady, covering her face, cried aloud thinking of Krishna (Hari), the lord of the three worlds.

sn: याज्ञसेन्या वचः श्रुत्वा कृष्णो गह्वरितोऽभवत्। त्यक्त्वा शय्याऽऽसनं पद्भ्यां कृपालुः कृपयाभ्यगात्॥४५
en: Hearing the words of Yajnaseni (Draupadi), Krishna was deeply moved. Leaving his seat, the kind Deity froni compassion came there on foot.

sn: कृष्णं च विष्णु च हरिं नरं च त्राणाय विक्रोशति याज्ञसेनी। ततस्तु धर्मोऽन्तरितो महात्मा समावृणोद् वै विविधैः सुवस्त्रैः॥
en: When Yajnaseni (Draupadi) was crying for protection to Krishna, Vishnu and Hari and also Nara, the illustrious (Deity) Dharma, remaining unseen, covered her with many excellent cloths.

sn: आकृष्यमाणे वसने द्रौपद्यास्तु विशाम्पते। तद्रूपमपरं वस्त्रं प्रादुरासीदनेकशः॥
en: O king, as the cloth of Draupadi was being dragged, after one was taken off, another of the same kind appeared and covered her.

sn: नानारागविरागाणि वसनान्यथ वै प्रभो। प्रादुर्भवन्ति शतशो धर्मस्य परिपालनात्॥
en: O lord, in consequence of the protection (extended towards Draupadi) by Dharma, hundreds and hundreds of cloths of many colour appeared.

sn: ततो हलहलाशब्दस्तत्रासीद् घोरदर्शनः। तदद्भुततमं लोको वीक्ष्य सर्वे महीभृतः। शशंसुद्रौपदीं तत्र कुत्सन्तो धृतराष्ट्रजम्॥
en: Thereupon there rose a great uproar. All the kings (present there), seeing this most extraordinary sight in the world, applauded Draupadi and endured the son of Dhritarashtra.

sn: शशाप तत्र भीमस्तु राजमध्ये बृहत्स्वनः। क्रोधाद् विस्फुरमाणौष्ठो विनिष्पिष्य करे करम्॥
en: Thereupon Bhima, squeezing his palms, and his lips quivering in anger, took a terrible oath in a loud voice in the midst of the kings.

sn: भीम उवाच इदं मे वाक्यमादध्वं क्षत्रिया लोकवासिनः। नोक्तपूर्वं नरैरन्यैर्न चान्यो यद् वदिष्यति॥
en: Bhima said O Kshatriyas, O men of the world, listen to my these words, words never before uttered by any man or will be (ever) uttered by any man in future.

sn: यद्येतदेवमुक्त्वाहं न कुर्यां पृथिवीश्वराः। पितामहानां पूर्वेषां नाहं गतिमवाप्नुयाम्॥ अस्य पापस्य दुर्बुद्धेर्भारतापसदस्य च। न पिबेयं बलाद् वक्षो भित्त्वा चेद् रुधिरं युधि॥
en: O lords of earth, if having spoken these words, I do not accomplish them hereafter, and if I do not forcibly tearing open the breast of this sinful wretch, this wicked minded scoundrel of the Bharata race, drink his life blood in the field of battle, let me not obtain the path of my ancestors.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तस्य ते तद् वचः श्रुत्वा रौद्रं लोमप्रहर्षणम्। प्रचक्रुर्बहुलां पूजां कुत्सन्तो धृतराष्ट्रजम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Hearing his these terrible and hair stirring words, every one present there applauded him and censured the son of Dhritarashtra.

sn: यदा तु वाससां राशिः सभामध्ये समाचितः। ततो दुःशासनः श्रान्तो वीडितः समुपाविशत्॥
en: When a mass of cloths were heaped in the assembly, Dushasana, becoming fatigued and ashamed, sat down.

sn: धिक्शब्दस्तु ततस्तत्र समभूल्लोमहर्षणः। सभ्यानां नरदेवानां दृष्ट्वा कुन्तीसुतांस्तथा॥
en: Seeing the sons of Kunti in that state, all those gods among men who were present there cried hair stirring words of "Fie!” “Fie!” (on the son of Dhritarashtra).

sn: न विब्रुवन्ति कौरव्याः प्रश्नमेतमिति स्म ह। स जनः क्रोशति स्मात्र धृतराष्ट्र विगर्हयन्॥
en: All the good men who were present there exclaimed, “Alas, the Kurus do not answer the question asked to them." They all censured Dhritarashtra.

sn: ततो बाहू समुच्छ्रित्य निवार्य च सभासदः। विदुरः सर्वधर्मज्ञ इदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Thereupon Vidura, learned in all the precepts of religion, waving his hands and silencing every one in the assembly, spoke these words.

sn: विदुर उवाच द्रौपदी प्रश्नमुक्त्वैवं रोरवति हयनाथवत्। न च विब्रूत तं प्रश्न सभ्या धर्मोऽत्र पीड्यते॥
en: Vidura said O men present in the assembly Draupadi, having put her question, is piteously weeping. You do not answer her question. Dharma is here persecuted.

sn: सभां प्रपद्यते ह्यातः प्रज्वलन्निव हव्यवाट्। तं वै सत्येन धर्मेण सभ्याः प्रशमयन्त्युत॥
en: A person in distress comes to an assembly of good men like a man in a blazing fire. Those that are in the assembly extinguish that fire and cool him by means of truth and morality.

sn: धर्मप्रश्नमतो ब्रूयादार्य: सत्येन मानवः। विब्रूयस्तत्र तं प्रश्न कामक्रोधबलातिगाः॥
en: The person in distress asks the assembly about his rights as sanctioned by morality. Those that are in the assembly should answer his question without being unmoved by anger of desire.

sn: विकर्णेन यथाप्रज्ञःमुक्तः प्रश्नो नराधिपाः। भवन्तोऽपि हि तं प्रश्न विब्रुवन्तु यथामति॥
en: O kings, Vikarna has answered the question according to his knowledge and judgement. You should also answer it as you think proper.

sn: यो हि प्रश्न न विब्रूयाद धर्मदर्शी सभां गतः। अनृते या फलावाप्तिस्तस्याः सोऽधू समश्नुते॥
en: The man who knows the rules of morality and sits in an assembly, incurs half the demerit that attaches to a lie, if he does not answer a question put to him.

sn: यः पुनर्वितथं ब्रूयाद् धर्मदर्शी सभां गतः। अनृतस्य फलं कृत्स्नं सम्प्राप्नोतीति निश्चयः॥
en: The man who knows the rules of morality and sits in an assembly, certainly incurs the sin of lie, if he answers falsely a question put to him.

sn: अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। प्रह्लादस्य च संवादं मुनेराङ्गिरसस्य च॥
en: The learned men quote as an example in connection with this matter the old history of Prahlada and the son of Angirasa.

sn: प्रह्लादो नाम दैत्येन्द्रस्तस्य पुत्रो विरोचनः। कन्याहेतोराङ्गिरसं सुधन्वानमुपाद्रवत्॥
en: There was a chief of the Daityas named Prahlada, whose son was Virochana. He (Virochana) quarrelled with Sudhanva, the son of Angirasa, for the sake of a bride.

sn: अहं ज्यायानहं ज्यायानिति कन्येप्सया तदा। तयोर्देवनमत्रासीत् प्राणयोरिति नः श्रुतम्॥
en: We have heard that they wagered even their own lives saying “I am superior,” “I am superior,” for the sake of obtaining a bride,

sn: तयोः प्रश्नविवादोऽभूत् प्रह्लादं तावपृच्छताम्। ज्यायान् क आवयोरेकः प्रश्नं प्रब्रूहि मा मृषा॥
en: When they thus quarrelled with each other, they hoth asked Prahlada, saying "Who amongst us is superior? Answer this question, don't speak falsely,"

sn: स वै विवदनाद् भीत: सुधन्वानं विलोकयन्। तं सुधन्वाब्रवीत् क्रुद्धो ब्रह्मदण्ड इव ज्वलन्॥
en: He (Prahlada), being alarmed at their quarrel, looked at Sudhanva. (Thereupon) Sudhanva thus spoke to him burning in rage as the Brahmadanda (club of Brahma).

sn: यदि वै वक्ष्यसि मृषा प्रह्लादाथ न वक्ष्यसि। शतधा ते शिरो वज्री वज्रेण प्रहरिष्यति॥
en: O Prahlada, if you answer falsely, or do not answer at all, your head will then be spilt into a hundred pieces by the wielder of thunder (Indra) with his thunder.

sn: सुधन्वना तथोक्तः सन् व्यथितोऽश्वत्थपर्णवत्। जगाम कश्यपं दैत्यः परिप्रष्टुं महौजसम्॥
en: When Sudhanva thus spoke, the Daitya (Prahlada) trembling like a leaf of the fig tree went to the greatly effulgent Kashyapa, to consult with him.

sn: प्रह्लाद उवाच त्वं वै धर्मस्य विज्ञाता दैवस्येहासुरस्य च। ब्राह्मणस्य महाभाग धर्मकृच्छ्रमिदं शृणु॥
en: Prahlada said O exalted one, you are learned in the precepts of morality which should guide the celestial, the Asuras and the Brahmanas. Here is a great dilemma in respect of a duty. Hear it.

sn: यो वै प्रश्नं न विब्रूयाद् वितथं चैव निर्दिशेत्। के वै तस्य परे लोकास्तन्ममाचक्ष्व पृच्छतः॥
en: Tell me, I ask you, what regions are obtained by men who, being asked a question, does not give answer to it or answer it falsely.

sn: कश्यप उवाच जाननविब्रुवन् प्रश्नान् कामात् क्रोधाद् भयात् तथा। सहस्रं वारुणान् पाशानात्मनि प्रतिमुञ्चति॥
en: Kashyapa said He, who knows but answers not a question from temptation, anger or fear, brings upon himself one thousand Pashas a sort of weapons) of Varuna upon his person.

sn: साक्षी वा विब्रुवन् साक्ष्यं गोकर्णशिथिलश्चरन्। सहस्रं वारुणान् पाशानात्मनि प्रतिमुश्चति॥
en: A man, who is cited as a witness with respect to any matter of ocular or auricular knowledge, speaks falsely, brings upon him one thousand Pashas of Varuna,

sn: तस्य संवत्सरे पूर्णे पाश एकः प्रमुच्यते। तस्मात् सत्यं तु वक्तव्यं जानता सत्यमञ्जसा॥
en: On the completion of one full year, one such Pasha is loosened (from his body). Therefore, he, who knows, should speak the truth without concealment.

sn: विद्धो धर्मो हाधर्मेण सभां यत्रोपपद्यते। न चास्य शल्यं कृन्तन्ति विद्धास्तत्र सभासदः॥
en: If virtue, pierced with sin, goes to an assembly, it is the duty of every man in that assembly to take off the dart. If they fail to do it, they themselves are pierced with it.

sn: अर्धं हरति वै श्रेष्ठः पादो भवति कर्तृषु। पादश्चैव सभासत्सु ये न निन्दन्ति निन्दितम्॥
en: In an assembly where a truly censurable act is not rebuked, half the demerit of that act attaches to the head of that assembly, fourth to the person who acts censurably, and fourth to all men present there.

sn: अनेना भवति श्रेष्ठों मुच्यन्ते च सभासदः। एनो गच्छति कर्तारं निन्दा) यत्र निन्द्यते॥
en: On the other hand, in an assembly in which he that deserves censure is rebuked, the head of that assembly becomes freed from all sins, and others that are present there incurs none. It is only the perpetrator of the (sinful) act, who becomes responsible for it.

sn: वितथं तु वदेयुर्ये धर्म प्रह्लाद पृच्छते। इष्टापूर्तं च ते नन्ति सप्त सप्त परावरान्॥
en: O Prahlada, those who, being asked about morality, answer falsely, destroy the meritorious acts of their ancestors seven generations upwards and downwards.

sn: हृतस्वस्य हि यद् दुःखं हतपुत्रस्य चैव यत्। ऋणिनः प्रति यच्चैव स्वार्थाद् भ्रष्टस्य चैव यत्॥ स्त्रियाः पत्या विहीनाया राज्ञा ग्रस्तस्य चैव यत्। अपुत्रायाश्च यद् दुःखं व्याघ्राघातस्य चैव यत्॥ अध्यूढायाश्च यद् दुःखं साक्षिभिर्विहतस्य च। एतानि वै समान्याहुर्दुःखानि त्रिदिवेश्वराः॥
en: The grief of one who has lost all his wealth, of one who has lost a son, of one who is in debt, of one who is separated from his companions, of a woman who has lost her husband, of one who has lost all in consequence of the king's demand, of a woman who is sterile, of one who is being devoured by a tiger, of one who is a co-wife, and of one who has been deprived of his property by false witnesses, is said by the celestial to be uniform in degree.

sn: तानि सर्वाणि दुःखानि प्राप्नोति वितथं ब्रुवन्। समक्षदर्शनात् साक्षी श्रवणाच्चेति धारणात्॥
en: He who speaks false gets all these sorts of grief. A man becomes a witness in consequence of his having seen, heard and understood a thing.

sn: तस्मात् सत्यं ब्रुवन् साक्षी धर्मार्थाभ्यां न हीयते। कश्यपस्य वचः श्रुत्वा प्रह्लादः पुत्रमब्रवीत्॥
en: Therefore a witness should always tell the truth. A witness should always tell the truth never loses his religious merits and earthly possessions.

sn: विदुर उवाच श्रेयान् सुधन्वा त्वत्तो वै मत्तः श्रेयांस्तथाङ्गिराः। माता सुधन्वनश्चापि मातृतः श्रेयसी तव। विरोचन सुधन्वायं प्राणानामीश्वरस्तव॥
en: Vidura said Having heard the words of Kashyapa, Prahlada thus spoke to his son.

sn: सुधन्वोवाच पुत्रस्नेहं परित्यज्य यस्त्वं धर्मे व्यवस्थितः। अनुजानामि ते पुत्रं जीवत्वेष शतं समाः॥
