en: Prahlada said Sudhanva is superior to you as Angirasa (his father) is to me. The mother of Sudhanva is superior to your mother. Therefore, O Virochana, Sudhanva is now the lord of your life. Sudhanva said As without being moved by affection for your son you have adhered to virtue, I command that your this son will live for one hundred years.

sn: विदुर उवाच एवं वै परमं धर्मं श्रुत्वा सर्वे सभासदः। यथाप्रश्नं तु कृष्णाया मन्यध्वं तत्र किं परम्॥
en: Vidura said Hearing these great truths of Dharma, let all persons present in this Sabha reflect upon what should be the answer to the question asked by Krishna (Draupadi).

sn: वैशंपायन उवाच विदुरस्य वचः श्रुत्वा नोचुः किंचन पार्थिवाः। कर्णो दुःशासनं त्वाह कृष्णां दासीं गृहान् नय॥
en: Vaishampayana said Even hearing the words of Vidura, the kings did not answer a word. Karna said to Dushasana, “Take away the servant woman Krishna in the inner apartment.”

sn: तां वेपमानां सवीडां प्रलपन्तीं स्म पाण्डवान्। दुःशासनः सभामध्ये विचकर्ष तपस्विनीम्॥
en: Thereupon Dushasana began to drag in the assembly the helpless, modest and ascetic Draupadi who was trembling and weeping piteously to the Pandavas.

sn: द्रौपद्युवाच पुरस्तात् करणीयं मे न कृतं कार्यमुत्तरम्। विह्वलास्मि कृतानेन कर्षता बलिना बलात्॥
en: Draupadi said I have a duty to perform. I have not as yet performed that great work. Forcibly dragged by this strong man (Dushasana), I am deprived of my senses.

sn: अभिवादं करोम्येषां कुरूणां कुरुसंसदि। न मे स्यादपराधोऽयं यदिदं न कृतं मया।॥
en: I salute all my superiors in this assembly of the Kurus. It is not my fault if I have not done it before.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच सा तेन च समाधूता दुःखेन च तपस्विनी। पतिता विललापेदं सभायामतथोचिता॥
en: Vaishampayana said Dragged with greater force the afflicted and ascetic lady (Draupadi) who did not deserve such treatment, fell on the ground and wept in the assembly.

sn: द्रौपद्युवाच स्वयंवरे यास्मि नृपैदृष्टा रङ्गे समागतैः। न दृष्टपूर्वा चान्यत्र साहमद्य सभां गता॥
en: Draupadi said I was once seen on the occasion of my Svamavara by the assembled kings in the arena. I was never before seen (by them) any where else. I am to day been brought before the assembly.

sn: यां न वायुर्न चादित्यो दृष्टवन्तौ पुरा गृहे। साहमद्य सभामध्ये दृश्यास्मि जनसंसदि॥
en: She, who is never before seen by even the wind and the sun in her house, is seen to day in the assembly and is exposed before all men.

sn: यां न मृष्यन्ति वातेन स्पृश्यमानां गृहे पुरा। स्पृश्यमानां सहन्तेऽद्य पाण्डवास्तां दुरात्मना॥
en: We have never heard before that a wedded wife is brought before an assembly. That old and eternal rule is to day destroyed by the Kurus.

sn: मृष्यन्ति कुरवश्चमे मन्ये कालस्य पर्ययम्। सुषां दुहितरं चैव क्लिश्यमानामनर्हतीम्॥
en: She, whom the Pandavas did not suffer to be touched (even) by the wind before, is to day suffered by them to be persecuted by the wicked men.

sn: किं न्वतः कृपणं भूयो यदहं स्त्री सती शुभा। सभामध्यं विगाहेऽद्य क्व नु धर्मो महीक्षिताम्॥
en: It appears the time has became out of joint, when the Kurus suffer their daughter and daughter-in-law, who is so unworthy of such treatment, to be thus persecuted.

sn: धर्म्या स्त्रियं सभा पूर्वे न नयन्तीति नः श्रुतम्। स नष्टः कौरवेयेषु पूर्वो धर्मः सनातनः॥
en: What could be more digressing to me than that through I am high born and chaste, yet I should be brought into the assembly. Where is the Dharma of these kings?

sn: कथं हि भार्या पाण्डूनां पार्षतस्य स्वसा सती। वासुदेवस्य च सखी पार्थिवानां सभामियाम्॥
en: How is it that the chaste wife of the Pandavas, the sister of the son of Prishata, the friend of Vasudeva (Krishna), is brought before the assembly of the kings?

sn: तामिमां धर्मराजस्य भार्यां सदृशवर्णजाम्। बूत दासीमदासीं वा तत् करिष्यामि कौरवाः॥
en: O Kauravas, I am the wife of Dharmaraja (Yudhisthira), born in the same order to which the king belongs. Tell me whether I am a servant woman or not. I shall cheerfully do what you would say.

sn: अयं मां सुदृढं क्षुद्रः कौरवाणां यशोहरः। क्लिश्नाति नाहं तत् सोढुं चिरं शक्ष्यामि कौरवाः॥
en: O Kurus, this low man, this destroyer of the Kuru fame, is cruelly persecuting me. I cannot bear it any longer.

sn: जितां वाप्यजितां वापि मन्यध्वं मां यथा नृपाः। तथा प्रत्युक्तमिच्छामि तत् करिष्यामि कौरवाः॥
en: O kings, O Kurus, I desire you to answer whether you consider me as won or unwon. I shall do what you would say.

sn: भीष्म उवाच उक्तवानस्मि कल्याणि धर्मस्य परमा गतिः। लोके न शक्यते ज्ञातुमपि विज्ञैर्महात्मभिः॥
en: Bhisma said O blessed lady, I have said the course of Dharma is subtle. Even the illustrious wise men cannot understand it in the world.

sn: बलवांश्च यथा धर्म लोके पश्यति पूरुषः। स धर्मो धर्मवेलायां भवत्यभिहतः परः॥
en: What a powerful man says morality in the world is regarded as such by others, however otherwise it may really be. What a weak man says, however morality it may be, is not regarded as such.

sn: न विवेक्तुं च ते प्रश्नमिमं शक्नोमि निश्चयात्। सूक्ष्मत्वाद् गहनत्वाच्च कार्यस्यास्य च गौरवात्॥
en: From the importance of the issue involved, from its intricacy and subtility, I am unable to answer with certainly the question you have asked.

sn: नूनमन्तः कुलस्यायं भविता नचिरादिव। तथा हि कुरवः सर्वे लोभमोहपरायणाः॥
en: It is certain that as all the Kurus have become the slaves of covetousness and folly, the destruction of this our race will happen on no distant date.

sn: कुलेषु जाताः कल्याणि व्यसनैराहता भृशम्। धर्म्यान्मार्गान्न च्यवन्ते येषां नस्त्वं वधूः स्थिता॥
en: O blessed one, the family into which you have been admitted as a daughter-in-law is such that there are men and women born in it, however they might be afflicted by calamities, they never deviate from the path of virtue.

sn: उपपन्नं च पाञ्चालि तवेदं वृत्तमीदृशम्। यत् कृच्छ्रमपि सम्प्राप्ता धर्ममेवान्ववेक्षसे॥
en: O Panchali, your this conduct, namely through persecuted, you still cast your eyes on Dharma, is certainly worthy of you.

sn: एते द्रोणादयश्चैव वृद्धा धर्मविदो जनाः। शून्यैः शरीरैस्तिष्ठन्ति गतासव इवानताः॥
en: These men of mature years, learned in the precepts of morality, (namely) Drona and others, sit with down cast heads like men who are dead and whose lives have departed from their bodies.

sn: युधिष्ठिरस्तु प्रश्नेऽस्मिन् प्रमाणमिति मे मतिः। अजितां वा जितां वेति स्वयं व्याहर्तुमर्हति॥
en: My opinion is that Yudhisthira himself is an authority in this question. He should say whether you are won or not won.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तथा तु दृष्ट्वा बहु तत्र देवीं रोरूयमाणां कुररीमिवार्ताम्। नोचुर्वचः साध्वथ वाप्यसाधु महीक्षितो धार्तराष्ट्रस्य भीताः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Through the kings present there saw the lady (Draupadi) crying piteously in affliction like a female osprey, yet they, out of the fear for the son of Dhritarashtra (Duryodhana), did not utter a word good or evil.

sn: स्तूष्णीभूतान् धृतराष्ट्रस्य पुत्रः। स्मयन्निवेदं वचनं बभाषे पाञ्चालराजस्य सुतां तदानीम्॥
en: Seeing the sons and grandsons of kings sitting silent, the son of Dhritarashtra (Duryodhana) smiled and spoke thus to the daughter of the Panchala king.

sn: दुर्योधन उवाच तिष्ठत्वयं प्रश्न उदारसत्त्वे भीमेऽर्जुने सहदेवे तथैव। पत्यौ च ते नकुले याज्ञसेनि वदन्त्वेते वचनं त्वत्प्रसूतम्॥
en: Duryodhana said O Yajnaseni, the question you have asked depends on the greatly powerful Bhima, on Arjuna, on Nakula and on Sahadeva. Let them answer your question.

sn: अनीश्वरं विब्रुवन्त्वार्यमध्ये युधिष्ठिरं तव पाञ्चालि हेतोः। कुर्वन्तु सर्वे चानृतं धर्मराज पाञ्चालि त्वं मोक्ष्यसे दासभावात्॥
en: O Panchali, let them for them for your sake declare in the midst of these most noblemen (present here) that Yudhisthira is not their lord and that he is a liar; you will then be freed from the slavery.

sn: धर्मे स्थितो धर्मसुतो महात्मा स्वयं चेदं कथयत्विन्द्रकल्पः। ईशो वा ते ह्यनीशोऽथ वैष वाक्यादस्य क्षिप्रमेकं भजस्व॥
en: Let the illustrious son of Dharma (Yudhisthira), ever devoted to virtue, who is like Indra himself, declare whether he is or is not your lord. At his words, accept us or accept the Pandavas without (further) delay.

sn: सर्वे हीमे कौरवेयाः सभायां दुःखान्तरे वर्तमानास्तवैव। न विब्रुवन्त्यार्यसत्त्वा यथावत् पतींश्च ते समवेक्ष्याल्पभाग्यान्॥
en: All the Kurus present in this assembly are floating in the sea of your affliction. They are endued with magnanimity and looking at your husbands they are unable to answer your question.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततः सभ्याः कुरुराजस्य तस्य वाक्यं सर्वे प्रशशंसुस्तथोच्चैः। चेलावेधांश्चापि चक्रुर्नदन्तो हाहेत्यासीदपि चैवार्तनादः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Hearing these words of the Kuru king (Duryodhana), all persons present in the assembly loudly applauded him. Some shouting approvingly made signs to one another by motions of their eyes and lips and some made sounds of distress such as "Oh," "Alas."

sn: द्धर्षश्चासीत् कौरवाणां सभायाम्। सर्वे चासन् पार्थिवाः प्रीतिमन्तः कुरुश्रेष्ठं धार्मिकं पूजयन्तः॥
en: Hearing his these delightful words, the Kurus present in the assembly become exceedingly glad. All the kings, becoming much pleased, applauded the virtuous chief of the Kurus.

sn: युधिष्ठिरं च ते सर्वे समुदैक्षन्त पार्थिवाः। किं नु वक्ष्यति धर्मज्ञ इति साचीकृताननाः॥
en: All the kings, turning their faces sideways, looked at Yudhisthira, learned in the precepts of morality, and they all became curious to learn what he would say,

sn: किं नु वक्ष्यति बीभत्सुरजितो युधि पाण्डवः। भीमसेनो यमौ चोभौ भृशं कौतूहलान्विताः॥
en: And they became curious to learn also invincible Pandavas, Bibhatsa (Arjuna), Bhimasena and the twins (Nakula and Sahadeva) would say.

sn: तस्मिन्नपरते शब्दे भीमसेनोऽब्रवीदिदम्। प्रगृह्य रुचिरं दिव्यं भुजं चन्दनचर्चितम्॥
en: When the noise was silenced, Bhimasena, waving his strong and well armed arms smeared with sandal paste, thus spoke (in the assembly).

sn: भीमसेन उवाच योष गुरुरस्माकं धर्मराजो महामनाः। न प्रभुः स्यात् कुलस्यास्य न वयं मर्षयेमहि॥
en: Bhima said If our this Guru (superior), this high-souled Dharmaraja, were not our lord, we would not have pardoned this (Kuru) race.

sn: ईशो नः पुण्यतपसां प्राणानामपि चेश्वरः। मन्यतेऽजितमात्मानं यद्येष विजिता वयम्॥
en: He is the lord of our all religions and ascetic merits, he is the lord even of our lives. If he considers himself won, then we are all won.

sn: न हि मुच्येत मे जीवन् पदा भूमिमुपस्पृशन्। मर्त्यधर्मा परामृश्य पाञ्चाल्या मूर्धजानिमान्॥
en: If it were not so, who is there amongst creatures that touch the earth with his feet or amongst the mortals that would escape from me with life after having touched the hair of the Panchala princess?

sn: पश्यध्वं ह्यायतौ वृत्तौ भुजौ मे परिघाविव। तयोरन्तरं प्राप्य मुच्येतापि शतक्रतुः॥
en: Look at my powerful and well formed arms like two iron clubs, if once within them, even Shatakratu (Indra) cannot escape.

sn: धर्मपाशसितस्त्वेवं नाधिगच्छामि संकटम्। गोरवेण विरुद्धश्च निग्रहादर्जुनस्य च॥
en: Bound by the ties of virtue, for the reverence that is due to our elder brother and repeatedly urged by Arjuna to remain silent, I am doing nothing awful.

sn: धर्मराजनिसृष्टस्तु सिंहः क्षुद्रमृगानिव। धार्तराष्ट्रानिमान् पापान् निष्पिधेयं तलासिभिः॥
en: If I am once commanded by Dharmaraja (Yudhisthira), I would, by making my slaps do the work of swords, kill these sinful sons of Dhritarashtra as a lion kills a number of small animals.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तमुवाच तदा भीष्मो द्रोणो विदुर एव च। क्षम्यतामिदमित्येवं सर्वं सम्भाव्यते त्वयि॥
en: Vaishampayana said Thereupon Bhisma, Drona, and Vidura spoke thus to Bhima, “Forbear, everything is possible in you."

sn: कर्ण उवाच त्रयः किलेमे ह्यधना भवन्ति। दासः पुतश्चास्वतन्त्रा च नारी। दासस्य पत्नी त्वधनस्य भद्रे हीनेश्वरा दासधनं च सर्वम्॥
en: Karna said Of all the persons in this assembly, Bhisma, Khattwa (Vidura) and the preceptor of the Kurus (Droria) appear to be independent (men), for they always speak of their master as wicked, they always censure him and never wish for his prosperity.

sn: प्रविश्य राज्ञः परिवारं भजस्व तत् ते कार्यं शिष्टमादिश्यतेऽत्र। ईशास्तु सर्वे तव राजपुत्रि। भवन्ति वै धार्तराष्ट्रा न पार्थाः॥
en: The slave, the son, and the wife, (these three) are always dependent. They can have no wealth, for whatever they possess belong to their master. You are (now) the wife of a slave incapable of possessing anything of her own.

sn: अन्यं वृणीष्व पतिमाशु भाविनि यस्माद् दास्यं न लभसि देवनेन। नित्यं दास्ये विदितं तत् तवास्तु॥
en: Go to the inner apartments of the king and serve his relatives. This is the work that is now justify assigned to you. O princess, the sons of Dhritarashtra, and not the sons of Pritha (the Pandavas), are now your masters.

sn: पराजितो नकुलो भीमसेनो युधिष्ठिरः सहदेवार्जुनौ च। दासीभूता त्वं हि वै याज्ञसेनि पराजितास्ते पतयो नैव सन्ति।॥
en: O beautiful lady, select now another husband who will not make you a slave by gambling. It is well known that it is not censurable in a slave to proceed with freedom in selecting her husband.

sn: प्रयोजनं जन्मनि किं न मन्यते पराक्रमं पौरुषं चैव पार्थः। पाञ्चाल्यस्य दुपदस्यात्मजामिमां सभामध्ये यो व्यदेवीद् ग्लहेषु॥
en: O Yajnaseni, Nakula, Bhimasena, Yudhisthira, Sahadeva and Arjuna are all won (by us). You are (also) now a slave. Your husbands who are slaves cannot be now your masters.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तद् वै श्रुत्वा भीमसेनोऽत्यमर्षी भृशं निशश्वास तदाऽऽर्तरूपः। राजानुगो धर्मपाशानुबद्धो दहन्निवैनं क्रोधसंरक्तदृष्टिः॥
en: Did not the son of Pritha (Yudhisthira) consider life as useless, did he not care for prowess and manhood, that he offered the daughter of Drupada, the Panchala king, as a stake at dice in the presence of all this assembly.

sn: भीम उवाच नेष सत्यं दासधर्मः प्रदिष्टः। र्नादेवीस्त्वं यद्यनया नरेन्द्र॥
en: Vaishampayana said Hearing these words, the wrathful Bhima breathed hard; he became a very picture of woe. But obedient to the king (Yudhisthira) and bound by the ties of virtue and duty, (he still did nothing awful). But as if burning every thing with his eyes inflamed with anger, he thus spoke.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच भीमसेनवचः श्रुत्वा राजा दुर्योधनस्तदा। युधिष्ठिरमुवाचेदं तूष्णीम्भूतमचेतनम्॥
en: Bhima said I cannot be angry at these words of the Suta's son (Karna), for we have really entered the state not played staking this princess, could our enemies ever dare to speak thus to me?

sn: भीमार्जुनौ यमौ चैव स्थितौ ते नृप शासने। प्रश्नं ब्रूहि च कृष्णां त्वमजितां यदि मन्यसे॥
en: Vaishampayana said Hearing these words of Bhimasena, king Duryodhana thus addressed Yudhisthira who was sitting silent as one who is deprived of his senses.

sn: एवमुक्त्वा तु कौन्तेयमपोह्य वसनं स्वकम्। स्मयन्नवेक्ष्य पाञ्चालीमैश्वर्यमदमोहितः॥
en: "O king, Bhima, Arjuna, and the twins (Nakula and Sahadeva) are ever under your seat. Answer this question. Say whether you regard Krishna as won".

sn: कदलीस्तम्भसदृशं सर्वलक्षणसंयुतम्। गजहस्तप्रतीकाशं वज्रप्रतिमगौरवम्॥ अभ्युत्स्मयित्वा राधेयं भीममाधर्षयन्निव। द्रौपद्याः प्रेक्षमाणायाः सव्यमूरुमदर्शयत्॥
en: Having spoken thus to the son of Kunti, Duryodhana proud of his affluence, and desirous of encouraging the son of Radha (Karna) and of insulting Bhima, uncovered his right thigh, which was like a stem of the plantain tree or like the trunk of an elephant and which was graced with every auspicious mark, and endued with the strength of thunder; he showed it to Draupadi in her very sight.

sn: भीमसेनस्तमालोक्य नेत्रे उत्फाल्य लोहिते। प्रोवाच राजमध्ये तं सभां विश्रावयन्निव॥
en: Seeing this Bhimasena, expanding his red eyes, thus spoke to him (Duryodhana) in the midst of the kings, as if piercing them (with his words).

sn: पितृभिः सह सालोक्यं मा स्म गच्छेद् वृकोदरः। यद्येतमूरूं गदया न भिन्द्यां ते महाहवे॥
en: "Let not Vrikodara go to the regions obtained by his ancestors, if he does not break that thigh in a great battle."

sn: क्रुद्धस्य तस्य सर्वेभ्यः स्रोतोभ्यः पावकर्चिषः। वृक्षस्येव विनिश्चेरुः कोटरेभ्यः प्रदह्यतः॥
en: Like the fire that comes out of every crevice of a burning tree, sparkles of fire emitted from every part of angry Bhima's body.

sn: विदुर उवाच परं भयं पश्यत भीमसेनात्। तद् बुध्यस्वं धृतराष्ट्रस्य पुत्राः। दैवेरितो नूनमयं पुरस्तात् परोऽनयो भरतेषूदपादि॥
en: Vidura said O kings of Pratipa's race, look at the great danger that arise from Bhimasena. Know for certain that this great calamity that threatens to overtake the descendants of Bharata has been sent by Destiny itself.

sn: अतिद्यूतं कृतमिदं धार्तराष्ट्रा यस्मात् स्त्रियं विवदध्वं सभायाम्। योगक्षेमौ नश्यतो वः समग्रौ पापान् मन्त्रान् कुरवो मन्त्रयन्ति॥
en: The sons of Dhritarashtra have gambled disregarding every proper consideration. They are now quarrelling in the Sabha over a lady. Your kingdom's prosperity is at an end. Alas! The Kurus are engaged in sinful consultation.

sn: इमं धर्मं कुरवो जानताशु ध्वस्ते धर्मे परिषत् सम्प्रदुष्येत्। दीशोऽभविष्यदपराजितात्मा॥
en: O Kurus, take to your heart this high precept that I declare to you. If virtue is persecuted (in · an assembly,) the whole assembly becomes polluted. If he (Yudhisthira) had staked her before he was himself won, he would have certainly been regarded as her master.

sn: देवं मन्ये यस्य दीव्यत्यनीशः। गान्धारराजस्य वचो निशम्य धर्मादस्मात् कुरवो मापयात॥
en: If a man stakes any thing at a time when he has no wealth, to win from him any wealth (then) is like obtaining wealth in a dream. O Kurus, listening to the words of the Gandhara king, do not fall from the path of virtue.

sn: दुर्योधन उवाच भीमस्य वाक्ये तद्वदेवार्जुनस्य स्थितोऽहं वै यमयोश्चैवमेव। मथो दास्यान्मोक्ष्यसे याज्ञसेनि॥
en: Duryodhana said I am willing to abide by the words of Bhima, Arjuna and the twins. Let them say that Yudhisthira is not their master; and Yajnaseni will (then) be freed from slavery.

sn: अर्जुन उवाच ईशो राजा पूर्वमासीद् ग्लहे नः कुन्तीसुतो धर्मराजो महात्मा। ईशस्त्वयं कस्य पराजितात्मा तज्जानीध्वं कुरवः सर्व एव॥
en: Arjuna said This illustrious son of Kunti, Dharmaraja (Yudhisthira) was certainly our lord and master before he began to play. But having lost himself, let all the Kurus decide whose master he is now.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततो राज्ञो धृतराष्ट्रस्य गेहे गोमायुरुच्चाहरदग्निहोत्रे। तं रासभाः प्रत्यभाषन्त राजन् समन्ततः पक्षिणश्चैव रौद्राः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Thereupon a jackal cried in the Homa chamber of king Dhritarashtra. O king asses began to bray responsively (with the jackal), and fearful birds from all quarters joined with them in their cries.

sn: तं वै शब्दं विदुरस्तत्त्ववेदी शुश्राव घोरं सुबलात्मजा च। भीष्मो द्रोणो गौतमश्चापि विद्धान् स्वस्ति स्वस्तीत्यपि चैवाहुरुच्चैः॥
en: At this sound, Vidura, learned in everything, and also the daughter of Subala (Gandhari), knew what it meant. Bhisma, Drona, and the learned Goutama (Kripa) also knowing it, loudly cried, "Svasti" "Svasti" (peace).

sn: स्तमुत्पातं घोरमालक्ष्य राज्ञे। निवेदयामासतुरातवत् तदा ततो राजा वाक्यमिदं बभाषे॥
en: Seeing that fearful omen, Gandhari and the learned Vidura told everything in great affliction to the king (Dhritarashtra). Then the king thus spoke.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच हतोऽसि दुर्योधन मन्दबुद्धे यस्त्वं सभायां कुरुपुङ्गवानाम्। स्त्रियं समाभाषसि दुर्विनीत विशेषतो द्रौपदी धर्मपत्नीम्॥
en: Dhritarashtra said O wicked minded Duryodhana, O wretch, destruction has already overtaken you when you insult in such language a wife of the Kuru chief, especially this wedded wife (of the Pandavas) Draupadi.

sn: एवमुक्त्वा धृतराष्ट्रो मनीषी। हितान्वेषी बान्धवानामपायात्। कृष्णां पाञ्चालीमब्रवीत् सान्त्वपूर्व विमृश्यैतत् प्रज्ञया तत्त्वबुद्धिः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having said this, the wise Dhritarashtra, who possessed great knowledge, reflecting (on the matter) with the aid of his wisdom and being desirous of saving his relatives and friends from destruction, consoled the Panchala princes Krishna and thus spoke to her.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच वरं वृणीष्व पाञ्चालि मत्तो यदभिवाञ्छसि। वधूनां हि विशिष्टा मे त्वं धर्मपरमा सती॥
en: Dhritarashtra said O Panchali ask from me any boon you desire. Chaste and devoted to virtue, you are the foremost of all my daughters-in-law.

sn: द्रौपद्युवाच ददासि चेद् वरं मह्यं वृणोमि भरतर्षभ। सर्वधर्मानुगः श्रीमानदासोऽस्तु युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Draupadi said O best of the Bharata race, if you grant me a boon, I say, let the handsome Yudhisthira, ever obedient to all duties, be freed from slavery.

sn: मनस्विनमजानन्तो मैवं ब्रूयः कुमारकाः। एष वै दासपुत्रो हि प्रतिविन्ध्यं ममात्मजम्॥
en: Let not unthinking children speak of my greatly intelligent son Prativindhya as the son of a slave.

sn: राजपुत्रः पुरा भूत्वा यथा नान्यः पुमान् क्वचित्। राजभिालितस्यास्य न युक्ता दासपुत्रता॥
en: Having been born a prince, to whom there is no man superior, and nurtured by kings, it is not proper that he should be called the son of a slave.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच एवं भवतु कल्याणि यथा त्वमभिभाषसे। द्वितीयं ते वरं भद्रे ददानि वरयस्व ह। मनो हि मे वितरति नैकं त्वं वरमर्हसि॥
en: Dhritarashtra said O blessed girl, what you have said, let it be so. O excellent one, ask for a second boon. I shall grant it to you. My heart desires to give you a second boon. You do not deserve to get only one boon. me

sn: द्रौपद्युवाच सरथौ सधनुष्कौ च भीमसेनधनेजयौ। यमौ च वरये राजन्नदासान् स्ववशानहम्॥
en: Draupadi said O king, grant this boon that Bhimasena, Arjuna and the twins with their bows and cars be freed from slavery and gain their liberty.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच तथास्तु ते महाभागे यथा त्वं नन्दिनीच्छसि। तृतीयं वरयास्मत्तो नासि द्वाभ्यां सुसत्कृता। त्वं हि सर्वस्नुषाणां मे श्रेयसी धर्मचारिणी॥
en: Dhritarashtra said O greatly blessed girl, let it be what you say. O daughter, ask for a third boon, you have not been sufficiently honoured with two boons. Ever trading the path of virtue, you are the foremost of all my daughters-in-law.

sn: द्रौपद्युवाच लोभो धर्मस्य नाशाय भगवन् नाहमुत्सहे। अनर्हा वरमादातुं तृतीयं राजसत्तम॥
en: Draupadi said O illustrious one, covetousness destroys virtue. O foremost of kings, I do not deserve a third boon; I dare not ask any.

sn: एकमाहुर्वैश्यवरं द्वौ तु क्षत्रस्त्रिया वरौ। त्रयस्तु राज्ञो राजेन्द्र ब्राह्मणस्य शतं वराः॥
en: O king of kings, it is ordained that a Vaisya may ask one boon, a Kshatriya woman two, a Kshatriya three and a Brahmana one hundred.

sn: पापीयांस इमे भूत्वा संतीर्णाः पतयो मम। वेत्स्यन्ति चैव भद्राणि राजन् पुण्येन कर्मणा॥
en: O king, these my husbands, freed from the wretched state of slavery, will be able to achieve prosperity by their own virtuous acts.

sn: कर्ण उवाच या नः श्रुता मनुष्येषु स्त्रियो रूपेण सम्मताः। तासामेतादृशं कर्म न कस्याश्चन शुश्रुम॥
en: Karna said We have not heard of such an act performed by any woman who are noted in this world for their beauty.

sn: क्रोधाविष्टेषु पार्थेषु धार्तराष्ट्रेषु चाप्यति। द्रौपदी: पाण्डुपुत्राणां कृष्णा शान्तिरिहाभवत्॥
en: When the sons of Pandu and Dhritarashtra were excited with anger, this Krishna, the daughter of Drupada, become their salvation.

sn: अप्लवेऽम्भसि मग्नानामप्रतिष्ठे निमज्जताम्। पाञ्चाली पाण्डुपुत्राणां नौरेषा पारगाभवत्॥
en: The sons of Pandu were sinking boatless in an ocean of distress, this Panchali, becoming a boat to them, brought them safely to the shore.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तद् वै श्रुत्वा भीमसेनः कुरुमध्येऽत्यमर्षणः। स्त्रीगतिः पाण्डुपुत्राणामित्युवाच सुदुर्मनाः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Hearing the words, "A woman is the refuge for the sons of Pandu, "uttered in the midst of the Kurus (by Karna), the angry Bhima in great affliction said:

sn: भीम उवाच त्रीणि ज्योतींषि पुरुष इति वै देवलोऽब्रवीत्। अपत्यं कर्म विद्या.च यतः सृष्टाः प्रजास्ततः॥
en: Bhima said (O Arjuna), Devala has said that offspring, acts and learning, these are the three lights that is in every person, for from these (three) has sprung the creation,

sn: अमेध्ये वै गतप्राणे शून्ये ज्ञातिभिरुज्झिते। देहे त्रितयमेवैतत् पुरुषस्योपयुज्यते॥
en: When life becomes extinct and the body becomes impure and is cast off by the relatives, these three (offspring, acts and learning) become of service to every person,

sn: तन्नो ज्योतिरिहतं दाराणामभिमर्शनात्। धनंजय कथंस्विन् स्यादपत्यमभिमृष्टजम्॥
en: But the light that is in us has been dimmed by this act of insult done to our wife. O Dhananjaya, how can a son born from this insulted wife of ours prove serviceable to us?

sn: अर्जुन उवाच न चैवोक्ता न चानुक्ता हीनत: परुषाः गिरः। भारत प्रतिजल्पन्ति सदा तूत्तमपूरुषाः॥ स्मरन्ति सुकृतान्येव न वैराणि कृतान्यपि। सन्तः प्रतिविजानन्तो लब्धसम्भावनाः स्वयम्॥
en: Arjuna said O descendant of Bharata, great men never care about the harsh words that may or may not be uttered by inferior men. Persons that have earned respects for themselves, even if they are able to retaliate, do not remember the acts of hostility done by their enemies, but they treasure up only their good deeds.

sn: भीम उवाच इहैवैतांस्त्वहं सर्वान् हन्मि शत्रून् समागतान्। अथ निष्क्रम्य राजेन्द्र समूलान् हन्मि भारत॥
en: Bhima said O king of kings, shall I here at once kill all these foes assembled together, or o descendant of Bharata, shall I destroy them all by the roots outside the palace?

sn: किं नो विवदितेनेह किमुक्तेन च भारत। अद्यैवैतान् निहन्मीह प्रशाधि पृथिवीमिमाम्॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, what need is there for discussion in this matter) or what need is there for (your) command? I shall kill all these (men) even now, and O king, (then) rule the whole earth without a rival,

sn: इत्युक्त्वा भीमसेनस्तु कनिष्ठैर्धातृभिः सह। मृगमध्ये यथा सिंहो मुहुर्मुहुरुदैक्षत॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having said this Bhima with his younger brothers repeatedly cast his angry glances around as a lion does towards a herd of small animals.

sn: सान्त्व्यमानो वीक्षमाणः पार्थेनाक्लिष्टकर्मणा। खिद्यत्येव महाबाहुरन्तर्दाहेन वीर्यवान्॥
en: Partha (Arjuna) of pure deeds pacified him with appealing looks, but the mighty armed and powerful (Bhima) began to burn in the fire of his anger.

sn: क्रुद्धस्य तस्य स्रोताभ्यः कर्णादिभ्ये नराधिप। सधूमः सस्फुलिङ्गज्रिर्चः पावकः समजायत॥
en: O king, fire with smokes, sparks and flames began to issue out of his ears and other senses, so much angry he became.

sn: भृकुटीकृतदुष्प्रेक्ष्यमभवत् तस्य तन्मुखम्। युगान्तकाले सम्प्राप्ते कृतान्तस्येव रूपिणः॥
en: His face became terrible to look at in consequence of his furrowed brows as that of Yama himself at the time of universal destruction.

sn: युधिष्ठिरस्तमावार्य बाहुना बाहुशालिनम्। मैवमित्यब्रवीच्चैनं जोषमास्स्वेति भारत॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, thereupon Yudhisthira embracing him with his arms asked the mighty armed hero to forbear, telling him “Be not so. Remain in silence and peace." And

sn: निवार्य च महाबाहुं कोपसंरक्तलोचनम्। पितरं समुपातिष्ठद् धृतराष्ट्रं कृताञ्जलिः॥
en: Having pacified the mighty armed (Bhima) with eyes red in anger, the king (Yudhisthira) approached his sire Dhritarashtra.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच राजन् किं करवामस्ते प्रशाध्यस्मांस्त्वमीश्वरः। नित्यं हि स्थातुमिच्छामस्तव भारत शासने॥
en: Yudhisthira said O king, you are our lord. Command us what we shall do. O descendant of Bharata, we desire to remain always under your swa

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच अजातशत्रो भद्रं ते अरिष्टं स्वस्ति गच्छत। अनुज्ञाताः सहधनाः स्वराज्यमनुशासत॥
en: Dhritarashtra said O Ajatasatru, be blessed. Go in peace and safety. Rule your kingdom with your wealth at my command.

sn: इदं चैवावबोद्धव्यं वृद्धस्य मम शासनम्। मया निगदितं सर्वं पथ्यं निःश्रेयसं परम्॥
en: Take to heart the command of an old man, the wholesome advice that I give and which is like a nutritive regimen.

sn: वेत्थ त्वं तात धर्माणां गतिं सूक्ष्मां युधिष्ठिर। विनीतोऽसि महाप्राज्ञ वृद्धानां पर्युपासिता॥
en: O child, O greatly wise Yudhisthira, you are full of humility, and you wait upon the old. You know the path of Dharma is subtle.

sn: यतो बुद्धिस्ततः शान्तिः प्रशमं गच्छ भारत। नादारुणि पतेच्छस्त्रं दारुण्येतन्निपात्यते॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, where there is intelligence there is forbearance. Therefore follow the path of peace. Axe falls upon wood, it does not fall upon stone.

sn: न वैराण्यभिजानन्ति गुणान् पश्यन्ति नागुणान्। विरोधं नाधिगच्छन्ति ये त उत्तमपूरुषाः॥
en: Those are superior men who do not remember the acts of hostility of their enemies, who see only the merits and not the faults of their enemies, and who themselves never enter into hostilities.

sn: स्मरन्ति सुकृतान्येव न वैराणि कृतान्यपि। सन्तः परार्थं कुर्वाणा नावेक्षन्ते प्रतिक्रियाम्॥
en: Those that are good remember only the good deeds of their enemies and not any act of hostility that their enemies might do. The good men do good to others without any expectation of getting a return.

sn: संवादे परुषाण्याहुर्युधिष्ठिर नराधमाः। प्रत्याहुर्मध्यामास्त्वेतेऽनुक्ताः परुषमुत्तरम्॥
en: O Yudhisthira, only the worst of men use harsh words in quarrel. Men of indifferent character reply to such words when spoken by others. But superior men do not think of such words or recapitulate them.

sn: न चोक्ता नैव चानुक्तास्त्वहिताः परुषा गिरः। प्रतिजल्पन्ति वै धीराः सदा तूत्तमपूरुषा॥ स्मरन्ति सुकृतान्येव न वैराणि कृतान्यपि। सन्तः प्रतिविजानन्तो लब्ध्वा प्रत्ययमात्मनः॥ असम्भिन्नार्थमर्यादाः साधवः प्रियदर्शनाः। तथा चरितमार्येण त्वयास्मिन् सत्समागमे॥
en: Those that are good, taking their own feelings under consideration, can understand the feelings of others. Therefore, they remember only the good deeds and not the acts of hostility, of their enemies. You have acted, as is done by good men of possessing appearance who does not transgress Dharma, Artha and Kama.

sn: दुर्योधनस्य पारुष्यं तत् तात हृदि मा कृथाः। मातरं चैव गान्धारी मां च त्वं गुणकाझ्या॥
en: O child, do not remember the harshness of Duryodhana. If you desire to remember what is only good look at your mother Gandhari and myself.

sn: उपस्थितं वृद्धमन्धं पितरं पश्य भारत। प्रेक्षापूर्वं मया द्यूतमिदमासीदुपेक्षितम्॥ मित्राणि द्रष्टुकामेन पुत्राणां च बलाबलम्। अशोच्याः कुरवो राजन् येषां त्वमनुशासिता॥ मन्त्री च विदुरो धीमान् सर्वशास्त्रविशारदः। त्वयि धर्मोऽर्तुने धैर्यं भीमसेने पराक्रमः॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, look at me, your father, present here who am old, and blind. It was for meeting with our friends, and also for examination the strength and weakness of my children that I allowed out of policy this match at dice to proceed. O king, there is no fear for those Kurus who are under your sway and who follow the counsel of the greatly intelligent Vidura learned in all Shastras. In you is virtue, in Arjuna is patience, and in Bhimasena is prowess,

sn: श्रद्धा च गुरुशुश्रूषा यमयोः परुषग्ययोः। अजातशत्रो भद्रं ते खाण्डवप्रस्थमाविश। भ्रातृभिस्तेऽस्तु सौभ्रानं धर्मे ते धीयतां मनः॥
en: And in those foremost of men, the twins (Nakula and Sahadeva), are pure reverence and service to superiors. O Ajatasatru, be blessed. Return to Khandavaprastha. Let there be brotherly love between you and your cousins. Let your mind be always fixed in virtue.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच इत्युक्तो भरतश्रेष्ठ धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः। कृत्वाऽऽर्यसमयं सर्वं प्रतस्थे भ्रातृभिः सह॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having been thus addressed, and performing all the ceremonies of politeness, the best of the Bharata race, Dharmaraja Yudhisthira, started with his brothers.

sn: ते रथान् मेघसंकाशानास्थास सह कृष्णया। प्रययुर्हष्टमनस इन्द्रप्रस्थं पुरोत्तमम्॥
en: Accompanied with Krishna, and ascending their cars of colour of clouds, (Draupadi), they started for that best of cities, Indraprastha.

sn: जनमेजय उवाच अनुज्ञातांस्तान् विदित्वा सरत्नधनसंचयान्। पाण्डवान् धार्तराष्ट्राणां कथमासीन्मनस्तदा॥
en: Janamejaya said How did the sons of Dhritarashtra feel when they came to know that the Pandavas had with Dhritarashtra's permission left Hastinapur with all their wealth and jewels?

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच अनुज्ञातांस्तान् विदित्वा धृतराष्ट्रेण धीमता। राजन् दुःशासनः क्षिप्रं जगाम भ्रातरं प्रति॥
en: Vaishampayana said O king, having learnt that the Pandavas had been commanded by the wise Dhritarashtra to return to their capital Dushasana soon went to his brother.

sn: दुर्योधनं समासाद्य सामात्यं भरतर्षभ। दुःखार्तो भरतश्रेष्ठमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, having come before Duryodhana (sitting) with his counsellors he spoke thus in a sorrowful heart.

sn: दुःशासन उवाच दुःखेनैतत् समानीतं स्थविरो नाशयत्यसौ। शत्रुसाद् गमयद् द्रव्यं तद् बुध्यध्वं महारथाः॥
en: Dushasana said O great car-warrior, the old man has thrown away, what we earned with so much trouble. Know that he had made over the whole of that wealth to our enemies.

sn: अथ दुर्योधनः कर्णः शकुनिश्चापि सौबलः। मिथः संगम्य सहिताः पाण्डवान् प्रति मानिनः॥ वैचित्रवीर्यं राजानं धृतराष्ट्र मनीषिणम्। अभिगम्य त्वरायुक्ताः श्लक्ष्णं वचनमब्रुवन्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Thereupon, Duryodhana, and Karna, all exceedingly proud and vain-being united together and wishing to counteract the Pandavas went in haste and saw the king Dhritarashtra, the son of Vichitravirya. They spoke to him these smooth and artful words.

sn: दुर्योधन उवाच न त्वयेदं श्रुतं राजन् यज्जगाद् बृहस्पतिः। शक्रस्य नीतिं प्रवदन् विद्वान् देवपुरोहितः॥
en: Duryodhana said O king, have you not heard what the learned Brihaspati, the preceptor of the celestial, said on morals and politics when advising Shakra (Indra).

sn: सर्वोपायैर्निहन्तव्याः शत्रवः शत्रुसूदन। पुरा युद्धाद् बलाद् वापि प्रकुर्वन्ति तवाहितम्॥
en: O chastiser of foes, (he said), “Those enemies who always harm by force or stratagem should be destroyed by every means".

sn: ते वयं पाण्डवधनैः सर्वान् सम्पूज्य पार्थिवान्। यदि तान् योधयिष्यामः किं वै नः परिहास्यति॥
en: If we gratify with the wealth of his Pandavas, the kings of the world and then fight with the sons of Pandu, what reverse can overtake us?

sn: अहीनाशीविषान् क्रुद्धान् नाशाय समुपस्थितान्। कृत्वा कण्द्दे च पृष्ठे च कः समुत्स्रष्टुमर्हति॥
en: When one places on his neck and back angry snakes full of venom, which has come to bring about his destruction, is it possible for him to take them off?

sn: आत्तशस्त्रा रथगताः कुपितास्तात पाण्डवाः। निःशेषं वः करिष्यन्ति क्रुद्धा ह्याशीविषा इव॥
en: O father, equipped with weapons and seated on cars, the Pandavas will annihilate us like angry and poisonous snakes.

sn: संनद्धो ह्यर्जुनो याति विधृत्य परमेषुधी। गाण्डीवं मुहुरादत्ते निःश्वसंश्च निरीक्षते॥
en: Even now Arjuna, attired in armour and furnished with couple of quivers, is proceeding, frequently taking up the Gandiva (bow) and breathing hard and casting angry glances around.

sn: गदां गुर्वी समुद्यम्य त्वरितश्च वृकोदरः। स्वस्थं योजयित्वाऽऽशु निर्यात इति नः श्रुतम्॥
en: We are told that Vrikodara (Bhima), hastily ordering his chariot to be made ready and then riding on it, frequently whirling his heavy club is proceeding along.

sn: नकुलः खड्गमादाय चर्म चाप्यर्धचन्द्रवत्। सहदेवश्च राजा च चक्रुराकारमिङ्गितैः॥
en: Nakula also is proceeding with the sword in his grasp and the semicircular shield in his hand; Sahadeva and the king (Yudhisthira) have made signs clearly indicating their intentions.

sn: ते त्वास्थाय रथान् सर्वे बहुशस्त्रपरिच्छदान्। अभिघ्नन्तो रथवातान् सेनायोगाय निर्ययुः॥
en: Having ascended their cars which were full of all kings of weapons, they are all whipping their horses, (so that they might soon reach their capital) to assemble their forces.

sn: न क्षस्यन्ते तथास्माभिर्जातु विप्रकृता हि ते। द्रौपद्याश्च परिक्लेशं कस्तेषां क्षन्तुमर्हति॥
en: Persecuted (as) they are (by us), they cannot forgive us for those injuries. Who is there amongst them who will be able to forgive the insult to Draupadi?

sn: पुनर्दीव्या भद्रं ते वनवासाय पाण्डवैः। एवमेतान् वशे कर्तुं शक्ष्याः पुरुषर्षभः॥
en: O foremost of all men, be blessed. We shall again gamble with the Pandavas in order to send them to exile in the forest. We are able to bring them under our sway in this way.

sn: ते वा द्वादश वर्षाणि वयं वा द्यूतनिर्जिताः। प्रविशमे महारण्यमजिनैः प्रतिवासिताः॥
en: Attired in skins, either they or we, having (first) been defeated at dice, shall go into the forest for twelve years.

sn: त्रयोदशं च सजने अज्ञाता: परिवत्सरम्। ज्ञाताश्च पुनरन्यानि वने वर्षाणि द्वादश॥
en: The thirteenth year shall have to be spent in some inhabited country without being recognised. If recognised, an exile for another twelve years shall be the consequence(of such recognition).

sn: निवसेन वयं ते वा तथा द्यूतं प्रवर्तताम्। अक्षानुप्त्वा पुन तमिदं कुर्वन्तु पाण्डवाः॥
en: Either they or we shall live (according to this engagement). Let therefore the game begin. Throwing the dice, let the Pandavas once more play.

sn: एतत् कृत्यतमं राजन्नस्माकं भरतर्षभ। अयं हि शकुनिर्वेद सविद्यामक्षसम्पदम्॥
en: O best of Bharata race, O king, this is our highest duty. This Shakuni is highly proficient in the whole science of dice-playing.

sn: दृढमूला वयं राज्ये मित्राणि परिगृह्य च। सारवद् विपुलं सैन्यं सत्कृत्य च दुरासदम्॥
en: We shall in the meantime be firmly rooted in the kingdom and making alliances (with other kings), we shall be able to get together a vast and invincible army and to keep them content.

sn: ते च त्रयोदशं वर्षं पारयिष्यन्ति चेद् व्रतम्। जेष्यामस्तान् वयं राजन् रोचतां ते परंतप॥
en: O king, O chastiser of foes, we shall then be able to defeat the Pandavas if they reappear. Let this plan recommend itself to you.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच तूर्णं प्रत्यानयस्वैतान् कामं व्यध्वगतानपि। आगच्छन्तु पुन तमिदं कुर्वन्तु पाण्डवाः॥
en: Dhritarashtra said Then bring back the Pandavas, even if they have gone a great way off. Let them come and throw dice once again.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततो द्रोणः सोमदत्तो बाह्रीकश्चैव गौतमः। विदुरो द्रोणपुत्रश्च वैश्यापुत्रश्च वीर्यवान्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Thereupon, Drona, Somadatta, Vahlika, Goutama, the son of Drona, the powerful son of Vaishya (Vidura).

sn: भूरिश्रवाः शान्तनवो विकर्णश्च महारथः। मा द्यूतमित्यभाषन्त शमोऽस्त्विति च सर्वशः॥
en: Bhurisrava,, Bhisma, and the mighty carwarrior Vikarna all said, “Let not the play commence. Let there be peace.”

sn: अकामानां च सर्वेषां सुहृदामर्थदर्शिनाम्। अकरोत् पाण्डवाह्वानं धृतराष्ट्रः सुतप्रियः॥
en: But disregarding the counsels of all his wise friends and relatives, Dhritarashtra ever partial to his sons, (again) summoned the Pandavas.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच अथाब्रवीन्महाराज धृतराष्ट्रं जनेश्वरम्। पुत्रहार्दाद् धर्मयुक्ता गान्धारी शोककर्षिता॥
en: Vaishampayana said O great king, it was then the virtuous Gandhari, afflicted with grief on account of her sons, addressed king Dhritarashtra and said.

sn: जाते दुर्योधने क्षत्ता महामतरभाषत। नीयतां परलोकाय साध्वयं कुलपांसनः॥
en: Gandhari said When Duryodhana was born, the highsouled Khattwa (Vidura) said, “It is better to send this disgrace of the race (Duryodhana) to the other world".

sn: व्यनदज्जातमात्रो हि गोमायुरिव भारत। अन्तो नूनं कुलस्यास्य कुरवस्तन्निबोधत॥
en: For he (Duryodhana) cried repeatedly and dissonantly like a jackal when he was born. It is certain he will prove the destruction of our race. Take this (the words of Vidura) to heart.

sn: मा निमज्जीः स्वदोषेण महाप्सु त्वं ह भारत। मा बालानामशिष्टानामभिमंस्था मतिं प्रभो॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, do not sink for your own fault in the ocean of calamity. O lord, do not approve the counsel of these wickedminded ones who are but boys.

sn: मा कुलस्य क्षये घोरे कारणं त्वं भविष्यसि। बद्धं सेतुं को नु भिन्द्याद् धमेच्छान्तं च पावकम्॥
en: Do not be the cause of the fearful destruction of this race. Who is there that will break an embankment which has been completed or re-kindle a conflagration which has been extinguished?

sn: शमे स्थितान् को नु पार्थान् कोपयेद् भरतर्षभ। स्मरन्तं त्वामाजमीढ स्मारयिष्याम्यहं पुनः॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, who is there that will provoke the peaceful sons of Pritha (Kunti)? O descendant of Ajamida, you remember everything, but I shall still call your attention to this.

sn: शास्त्रं न शास्ति दुर्बुद्धिं श्रेयसे चेतराय च। न वै वृद्धो बालमतिर्भवेद् ग़जन् कथंचन॥
en: The Shastras can never control the wickedminded men, either in good or in evil acts. A man of boyish intelligence can never act as an old man.

sn: त्वन्नेत्राः सन्तु ते पुत्रा मा त्वां दीर्णाः प्रहासिषुः। तस्मादयं मद्वचनात् त्यज्यतां कुलपांसनः॥
en: Let your sons follow you as their leader. Let them not for ever be separated from you (by death). Therefore, abandon at my word this disgrace of our race.

sn: तथा ते न कृतं राजन् पुत्रस्नेहान्नराधिप। तस्य प्राप्तं फलं विद्धि कुलान्तकरणाय यत्॥
en: O king, O ruler of men, you could not do it before from the affection you bear for your son. Know that the time has come for the destruction of our race through him.

sn: शमेन धर्मेण नयेन युक्ता या ते बुद्धिः सास्तु ते मा प्रमादीः। {दुप्रौढा गच्छति पुत्रपौत्रान्॥
en: Let your mind, guided by counsels of peace, virtue and true policy, be what it naturally is. Do not err. The prosperity which is acquired by the aid of wicked acts is soon destroyed, while that which is won by honest means takes root and descends from generation to generation.

sn: अथाब्रवीन्महाराजो गान्धारी धर्मदर्शिनीम्। अन्तः कामं कुलस्यास्तु न शक्नोमि निवारितुम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having been thus addressed by Gandhari who pointed out to him the path of virtue, the king replied to her saying, “If the destruction of our race has came, let it take place without any hindrance. I cannot prevent it.

sn: यथेच्छन्ति तथैवास्तु प्रत्यागच्छन्तु पाण्डवाः। पुन तं च कुर्वन्तु मामकाः पाण्डवैः सह॥
en: Let it be what they desire. Let the Pandavas return. Let my sons again gamble with the sons of Pandu".

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततो व्यध्वगतं पार्थं प्रातिकामी युधिष्ठिरम्। उवाच वचनाद् राज्ञो धृतराष्ट्रस्य धीमतः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Thereupon at the command of the intelligent Dhritarashtra Pratikamin, thus spoke to the son of Pritha, king Yudhisthira who had gone (by this time) to a great distance from Hastinapur.

sn: उपास्तीर्णा सभा राजन्नक्षानुप्त्वा युधिष्ठिर। एहि पाण्डव दीव्येति पिता त्वाऽऽहेति भारत॥
en: Pratikamin said O descendant of Bharata, your father has said, “O Yudhisthira, the assembly is ready. O son of Pandu, O king, O Yudhisthira, come and throw the dice.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच धातुर्नियोगाद् भूतानि प्राप्नुवन्ति शुभाशुभम्। न निवृत्तिस्तयोरस्ति देवितव्यं पुनर्यदि॥
en: Yudhisthira said All creatures obtain good or evil fruits according to the appointment of the Ordainer of the creation. Whether I play or I do not play, those fruits are inevitable.

sn: अक्षयूते समाह्वानं नियोगात् स्थविरस्य च। जानन्नपि क्षयकरं नातिक्रमितुमुत्सहे॥
en: This is a summons to dice, it is also the command of the old king. Though I know it will prove destructive to me, yet I cannot refuse.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच स्तथापि रामो लुलुभे मृगाय। प्रायः समासन्नपराभवाणां धियो विपर्यस्ततरा भवन्ति॥
en: Though (a living) animal made of gold was an impossibility, yet Rama suffered himself to be tempted by a (golden) deer. the mind of men over whom calamities hang become deranged and out of order.

sn: इति ब्रुवन् निववृते भ्रातृभिः सह पाण्डवः। जानंश्च शकुनेर्मायां पार्थो द्यूतमियात् पुनः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having said this, the Pandava (Yudhisthira) with his brothers retraced his steps (towards Hastinapur). Knowing full well the deception practised by Shakuni, the son of Pritha (Yudhisthira) came back to sit at dice with him again.

sn: विविशुस्ते सभां तां तु पुनरेव महारथाः। व्यथयन्ति स्म चेतांसि सुहृदां भरतर्षभाः॥
en: O best of the Bharata race,, giving great pain to the hearts of all their friends those great car-warriors again entered that assembly.

sn: यथोपजोषमासीनाः पुन तप्रवृत्तये। सर्वलोकविनाशाय दैवेनोपनिपीडिताः॥
en: Guided by Fate, they once more sat down at ease for gambling in order to bring about the destruction of men.

sn: शकुनिरुवाच अमुञ्चत् स्थविरो यद् वो धनं पूजितमेव तत्। महाधनं ग्लहं त्वेकं शृणु भो भरतर्षभ।॥
en: Shakuni said O best of the Bharata race the old king has given you back all your wealth. That is well. But listen to me, there is a stake of great value.

sn: वयं वा द्वादशाब्दानि युष्माभि तनिर्जिताः। प्रविशेम महारण्यं रौरवाजिनवाससः॥ त्रयोदशं च सजने अज्ञाताः परिवत्सरम्। ज्ञाताश्च पुनरन्यानि वने वर्षाणि द्वादश॥
en: (It is this), If we are defeated by you at dice, we shall enter the great forest attired in deer skins and live there for twelve years and pass the thirteenth years in some inhabited place unrecognised. If recognised, we shall return to the exile of another twelve years.

sn: अस्माभिर्निर्जिता यूयं वने द्वादश वत्सरान्। वसध्वं कृष्णया सार्धमजिनैः प्रतिवासिताः॥ त्रयोदशं च सजने अज्ञाताः परिवत्सरम्। ज्ञाताश्च पुनरन्यानि वने वर्षाणि द्वादश॥ त्रयोदशे च निर्वृत्ते पुनरेव यथोचितम्। स्वराज्यं प्रतिपत्तव्यमितरैरथवेतरैः॥
en: (On the other hand), if you be defeated by us, you shall with Krishna (Draupadi) live for twelve years in the forest and pass the whole of the thirteenth year unrecognised in an inhabited country. If recognised, an exile of another twelve years is to be the consequence. On the expiry of the thirteenth year, each is to have his kingdom surrendered to the other.

sn: अनेन व्यवसायेन सहास्माभिर्युधिष्ठिर। अक्षानुप्त्वा पुन तमेहि दीव्यस्व भारत॥
en: O Yudhishthira, O descendant of Bharata, with such stake, play with us again by throwing the dice.

sn: अथ सभ्याः सभामध्ये समुच्छ्रितकरास्तदा। ऊचुरुद्विग्नमनसः संवेगात् सर्व एव हि॥
en: Vaishampayana said Thereupon those that were present in the Sabha raising up their arms, said in great anxiety of mind and in great emotion.

sn: सभ्या ऊचुः अहो धिग बान्धवा नैनं बोधयन्ति महद् भयम्। बुद्ध्या बुध्येन्न वा बुध्येदयं वै भरतर्षभः॥
en: "Alas! Fie on the friends of Dhritarashtra that they do not tell him of his great danger! O best of the Bharata race (Dhritarashtra), whether he understand or not out of his own sense, it is your duty to tell him plainly.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच जनप्रवादान् सुबहूण्वन्नपि नराधिपः। हिया च धर्म संयोगात् पार्थो द्यूतमियात् पुनः॥
en: The king, the son of Pritha (Yudhisthira) even hearing these various remarks again sat at dice from shame and sense of (Kshatriyas) duty.

sn: जानन्नपि महाबुद्धिः पुन तमवर्तयत्। अप्यासन्नो विनाशः स्यात् कुरूणामिति चिन्तयन्॥
en: Full you knowing the consequence, the greatly intelligent one (Yudhisthira) again began to play, as if he was fully aware that the destruction of the Kurus were inevitably near at hand.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच कथं वै मद्विधो राजा स्वधर्ममनुपालयन्। आहूतो विनिवर्तेत दीव्यामि शकुने त्वया॥
en: Yudhisthira said. O Shakuni, how can a king like me who always observe the duty of his order refuse when challenged to dice? Therefore, I shall (again) play with you.

sn: शकुनिरुवाच गवावं बहुधेनूकमपर्यन्तमजाविकम्। गजाः कोशो हिरण्यं च दासीदासाश्च सर्वशः॥ एष नो ग्लह एवैको वनवासाय पाण्डवाः। यूयं वयं वा विजिता वसेम वनमाश्रिताः॥ त्रयोदशं च वै वर्षमज्ञाताः सजने तथा। अनेन व्यवसायेन दीव्याम पुरुषर्षभाः॥
en: Shakuni said. O son of Pandu, we have many kine and horse and milch cows and innumerable goats and sheep and elephants, treasures, gold and servants, both male and female. All these have been staked by us before. But now let this be our stake, namely exile into forest (for twelve years) and then living in the thirteenth year unrecognised in an inhabited place. O foremost of men, with this stake let us (now ) play.

sn: समुत्क्षेपेण चैकेन वनवासाय भारत। प्रतिजग्राह तं पार्थो ग्लहं जग्राह सौबलः। जितमित्येव शकुनियुधिष्ठिरमभाषत॥
en: Vaishampayana said O descendant of Bharata, when this proposa about going to the forest was but once uttered, the of Pritha (Yudhisthira) accepted it; and the son of Subala (Shakuni) (then) took up the dice. (Finally) Shakuni said to Yudhisthira, "Lo! I have won!" son

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततः पराजिताः पार्था वनवासाय दीक्षिताः। अजिनान्युत्तरीयाणि जगृहुश्च यथाक्रमम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Thereupon the vanquished sons of Pritha, preparing for their exile in the forest, attired themselves in deer skins and Uttriya (upper garment).

sn: अजिनैः संवृतान् दृष्ट्वा हृतराज्यानरिंदमान्। प्रस्थितान् वनवासाय ततो दुःशासनोऽब्रवीत्॥
en: Seeing those chastisers of foes attired in deer skins and robbed of their kingdom at point of going the forest, Dushasana exclaimed.

sn: प्रवृत्तं धार्तराष्ट्रस्य चक्रं राज्ञो महात्मनः। पराजिताः पाण्डवेया विपत्तिं परमां गताः॥
en: Dushasana Said The absolute sovereignty of son of Dhritarashtra, the high-souled king, (Duryodhana) has (now) commenced. The Pandavas are vanquished, and they have been plunged into great misery.

sn: अद्यैव ते सम्प्रयाताः समैर्वर्त्मभिरस्थलैः। गुणज्येष्ठास्तथा श्रेष्ठाः श्रेयांसो यद् वयं परैः॥
en: The gods are propitious to us, whether or not we have proceeded in the very narrow path (of sin); for we are today superior to our enemy in wealth and in every thing.

sn: नरकं पातिताः पार्था दीर्घकालमनन्तकम्। सुखाच्च हीना राज्याच्च विनष्टाः शाश्वती: समाः॥
en: The sons of Pritha are plunged into eternal hall. They are deprived of happiness and kingdom for ever-lasting days.

sn: धनेन मत्ता ये ते स्म धार्तराष्ट्रान् प्रहासिषुः। ते निर्जिता हृतधना वनमेष्यन्ति पाण्डवाः॥
en: Those Pandavas, who being intoxicated with the pride of wealth, laughed at the son of Dhritarashtra, will now have to go to the forest defeated and deprived of their wealth.

sn: चित्रान् सन्नाहानवमुच्य पार्था वासांसि दिव्यानि च भानुमन्ति। विवास्यन्तां रुरुचर्माणि सर्वे यथा ग्लहं सौबलस्याभ्युपेताः॥
en: Let them abandon their variegated armours, and their resplendent robes of celestial make. Let them all put on deer skins according to the stake they had accepted of the son of Subala (Shakuni).

sn: न सन्ति लोकेषु पुमांस ईदृशा इत्येव ये भावितबुद्धयः सदा। ज्ञास्यन्ति तेऽऽत्मानमिमेऽद्य पाण्डवा विपर्यये षण्ढतिला इवाफलाः॥
en: The Pandavas, who always boasted that they had no equals in all the world, will now know and regard themselves in this their calamity as grains of sesame without kernal.

sn: इदं हि वासो यदि वेदृशानां मनस्विनां रौरवमाहवेषु। अदीक्षितानामजिनानि यद्वद् बलीयसां पश्यत पाण्डवानाम्॥
en: Though in this dress, the Pandavas appear like wise and powerful men installed in a sacrifice, but see (consider) them as persons not entitled to perform sacrifices.

sn: महाप्राज्ञः सौमकिर्यज्ञसेनः कन्यां पाञ्चालीं पाण्डवेभ्यः प्रदाय। अकार्षीद् वै सुकृतं नेह किंचित् क्लीबाः पार्थाः पतयो याज्ञसेन्याः॥
en: The greatly wise descendant of Somaka, Yajnasena (Drupada), having bestowed the Panchala princess on the Pandavas, did not act well. The husbands of Yajnaseni (Draupadi) are impotent.

sn: सूक्ष्मप्रावारानजिनोत्तरीयान् दृष्टवारण्ये निर्धनानप्रतिष्ठान्। कां त्वं प्रीति लप्स्यसे याज्ञसेनि पतिं वृणीष्वेह यमन्यमिच्छसि॥
en: O Yajnaseni, what joy will you get in seeing these your husbands in the forest attired in skins and rags and deprived of their wealth and possessions. Select a husband from these present.

sn: एते हि सर्वे कुरवः समेताः क्षान्ता दान्ताः सुद्रविणोपपन्नाः। एषां वृणीष्वैकतमं पतित्वे न त्वां तपेत् कालविपर्ययोऽयम्॥
en: These Kurus, assembled here, are all forbearing and self-controlled. They are all vastly wealthy. Select one amongst these as your husband, so that this calamity may not drag you(in its train).

sn: यथाफलाः षण्ढतिला यथा चर्ममया मृगाः। तथैव पाण्डवाः सर्वे यथा काकयवा अपि॥
en: All the Pandavas are now like grains of sesame that are without kernal or toy animals incased in skins, or the grains of paddy without kernal.

sn: किं पाण्डवांस्ते पतितानुपास्य मोघः श्रमः षण्ढतिलानुपास्य। नश्रावयद् धृतराष्ट्रस्य पुत्रः॥
en: Why do you wait any longer upon the fallen sons of Pandu? The labour is thrown away that is bestowed on pressing the sesame grain that is without the kernal. Vaishampayana said The son of Dhritarashtra (Dushasana) uttered such cruel and harsh words in the hearing of the Pandavas.

sn: तद् वै श्रुत्वा भीमसेनोऽत्यमर्षी निर्भत्र्योच्चैः संनिगृह्मैव रोषात्। उवाच चैनं सहसैवोपगम्य सिंहो यथा हैमवतः शृगालम्॥
en: Having heard them, the unforbearing Bhimasena suddenly rushed towards that prince in anger like a Himalayan lion does towards a jackal. He loudly rebuked him in these words.

sn: भीमसेन उवाच क्रूर पापजनैर्जुष्टमकृतार्थं प्रभाषसे। गान्धारविद्यया हि त्वं राजमध्ये विकत्थसे॥
en: Bhima said O crooked-minded wretch, you rave in words that are uttered only by the sinful. Being advanced by the skill of the Gandhara king, you (dare to) boast in the midst of these kings.

sn: यथा तुदसि मर्माणि वाक्शरैरिह नो भृशम्। तथा स्मारयिता तेऽहं कृन्तन् मर्माणि संयुगे॥
en: As you pierce our hearts with these your words like arrows, so will I pierce your heart in battle, making you recollect all this.

sn: ये च त्वामनुवर्तन्ते क्रोधलोभवशानुगाः! गोप्तारः सानुबन्धास्तान् नेतास्मि यमसादनम्॥
en: I shall send to the abode of Yama all those with their descendants and relatives who are from anger or covetousness walking behind you as your protectors.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवं ब्रुवाणमजिनैर्विवासितं दुःशासनस्तं परिनृत्यति स्म। मध्ये कुरूणां धर्मनिबद्धमार्ग गौौरिति स्माह्वयन् मुक्तलज्जः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Dushasana, abandoning all sense of shame, danced around in the midst of the Kurus and loudly said, "O cow," "O cow”. Bhima uttered these words of wrath, but did nothing, for he could not deviate from the path of virtue.

sn: भीमसेन उवाच नृशंस परुषं वक्तुं शक्यं दुःशासन त्वया। निकृत्या हि धनं लब्ध्वा को विकस्थितुमर्हति॥
en: Bhima said Wretch, do you dare use harsh words ass these? O Dushasana, who should boast having thus won wealth by foul means?

sn: मैव स्म सुकृताल्लोकान् गच्छेत् पार्थो वृकोदरः। यदि वक्षो हि ते भित्त्वा न पिबेच्छोणितं रणे॥
en: I tell you, if Vrikodara, the son of Pritha, does not drink your life-blood piercing open your breast in battle, let him not attain to regions of blessedness.

sn: धार्तराष्ट्रान् रणे हत्वा मिषतां सर्वधन्विनाम्। शां गन्तास्मि नवरात् सत्यमेतद् ब्रवीमि ते॥
en: I tell you truly that killing the sons of Dhritarashtra in battle in the presence of all the warriors, I shall without the least delay pacify my this anger.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तस्य राजा सिंहगतेः सखेलं दुर्योधनो भीमसेनस्य हर्षात्। गतिं स्वगत्यानुचकार मन्दो निर्गच्छतां पाण्डवानां सभायाः॥
en: Vaishampayana said When the Pandavas were going out of the Sabha, the wicked king Duryodhana from excess of joy mimicked by his own steps the playful and lion-like movements of Bhimasena.

sn: नैतावता कृतमित्यब्रवीत् तं वृकोदरः संनिवृत्तार्धकायः। शीघ्रं हि त्वां निहतं सानुबन्ध संस्मार्याहं प्रतिवक्ष्यामि मूढ॥
en: Thereupon, Vrikodara(Bhima), half turning towards him, said. “O fool, do not think that by this you gain any ascendancy over me. I shall soon kill you with all your followers and answer you recalling all this to your mind”.

sn: एवं समीक्ष्यात्मनि चावमानं नियम्य मन्युं बलवान् स मानी। राजांनुगः संसदि कौरवाणां विनिष्क्रामन् वाक्यमुवाच भीमः॥
en: Seeing this insult offered to him, the powerful and proud Bhima, suppressing his rising anger and following the king (Yudhisthira) spoke these words when going out of the Kuru court.

sn: भीमसेन उवाच अहं दुर्योधनं हन्ता कर्णं हन्ता धनंजयः। शकुनि चाक्षकितवं सहदेवो हनिष्यति॥
en: Bhima said I shall be the slayer of Duryodhana, Dhananjaya (Arjuna) will be the slayer of Karna. Sahadeva will kill the gambler Shakuni.

sn: इदं च भूयो वक्ष्यामि सभामध्ये बृहद् वचः। सत्यं देवाः करिष्यन्ति यन्नो युद्धं भविष्यति॥
en: I repeat in the midst of this assembly these proud words which the celestial will surely make good, if ever we engage in battle (with the Kurus).

sn: सुयोधनमिमं पापं हन्तास्मि गदया युधि। शिरः पादेन चास्याहमधिष्ठास्यामि भूतले॥
en: I shall kill this sinful wretch Suyodhana (Duryodhana) in a club-fight. Felling him on the ground, I shall place my foot on his head.

sn: वाक्यशूरस्य चैवास्य परुषस्य दुरात्मनः। दुःशासनस्य रुधिरं पातास्मि मृगराडिव॥
en: As regards this wicked-minded man Dushasana, who is bold in speech, I will drink his blood like a lion.

sn: अर्जुन उवाच नैवं वाचा व्यवसितं भीम विज्ञायते सताम्। इतश्चतुर्दशे वर्षे द्रष्टारो यद् भविष्यति॥
en: Arjuna said Bhima, the resolutions of superior men are not known only in words. On the fourteenth year, they will see what will happen.

sn: भीमसेन उवाच दुर्योधनस्य कर्णस्य शकुनेश्च दुरात्मनः। दुःशासनचतुर्थानां भूमिः पास्यति शोणितम्॥
en: Bhima said The earth will drink the blood of Duryodhana, Karma, the wicked-minded Shakuni and the fourth Dushasana.

sn: अर्जुन उवाच असूयितारं द्रष्टारं प्रवक्तारं विकत्थनम्। भीमसेन नियोगात् ते हन्ताहं कर्णमाहवे॥
en: Arjuna said O Bhimasena, I will as you direct, kill in battle this Karna so malicious, jealous, harshspecched and vain.

sn: अर्जुनः प्रतिजानीते भीमस्य प्रियकाम्यया। कर्णं कर्णानुगांश्चैव रणे हन्तास्मि पत्रिभिः॥
en: For doing what is agreeable to Bhima, Arjuna vows that he will kill in battle with his arrows this Karna with all his followers.

sn: ये चान्ये प्रतियोत्स्यन्ति बुद्धिमोहेन मां नृपाः। तांश्च सर्वानहं बाणैर्नेतास्मि यमसादनम्॥
en: I will send to the abode of Yama with my arrows also those other kings that will from foolishness fight against me.

sn: चलेद्धि हिमवान् स्थानानिष्प्रभः स्याद् देवाकरः। शैत्यं सोमात् प्रणश्येत मत्सत्यं विष नेद् यदि॥
en: If my this vow be not carried out, then the Himalaya mountains might be removed from where they are, the maker of the day (sun) might lose his rays and the Moon his coolness.

sn: न प्रदास्यति चेद् राज्यमितो वर्षे चतुर्दशे। दुर्योधनोऽभिसत्कृत्य सत्यमेतद् भविष्यति॥
en: All this will surely happen if on the fourteenth year from this, Duryodhana does not return us our kingdom with proper respect.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच इत्युक्तवति पार्थे तु श्रीमान् माद्रवतीसुतः। प्रगृह्य विपुलं बाहुं सहदेवः प्रतापवान्॥
en: Vaishampayana said When Arjuna said this, the handsome and powerful son of Madri, Sahadeva, waving his mighty arms,

sn: सौबलस्य वधं प्रेप्सुरिदं वचनमब्रवीत्। क्रोधसंरक्तनयनो निःश्वसन्निव पन्नगः॥
en: And sighting like a snake and desiring to kill Shakuni, spoke thus with eyes red with anger.

sn: सहदेव उवाच अक्षान् यान् मन्यसे मूढ गान्धाराणां यशोहर। नैतेऽक्षा निशिता बाणास्त्वयैते समरे वृताः॥
en: Sahadeva said O fool, O destroyer of the fame of the Gandhara kings, what you are thinking as dice is not dice. They are sharp-pointed arrows which you have invited in battle.

sn: यथा चैवोक्तवान् भीमस्त्वामुद्दिश्य सबान्धवम्। कर्ताहं कर्मणस्तस्य कुरु कार्याणि सर्वशः॥
en: I shall certainly accomplish all which Bhima has said as regards you with all your followers. If you have anything to do, do it before that day comes.

sn: हन्तास्मि तरसा युद्धे त्वामेवेह सबान्धवम्। यदि स्थास्यसि संग्रामे क्षत्रधर्मेण सौबल॥
en: O son of Subala, I shall certainly kill you with all your friends and relatives if you stay in the fight according to the usage of the Kshatriyas.

sn: सहदेववचः श्रुत्वा नकुलोऽपि विशाम्पते। दर्शनीयतमो नृणामिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said O king, hearing the words of Sahadeva, Nakula, the handsomest of men, spoke thus.

sn: नकुल उवाच सुतेयं यज्ञसेनस्य द्यूतेऽस्मिन् धृतराष्ट्रजैः। यैर्वाचः श्राविता रूक्षाः स्थितैर्दुर्योधनप्रिये॥ तान् धार्तराष्ट्रान् दुर्वृत्तान् मुमूर्षुन् कालनोदितान्। गमयिष्यामि भूयिष्ठानहं वैवस्वतक्षयम्॥
en: Nakula said I shall certainly send to the abode of Yama all those wicked-minded sons of Dhritarashtra, who being desirous of death and impelled by Fate, and also moved by the wish of doing what would please Duryodhana, have used harsh and insulting words towards this Yajnaseni, (Draupadi) at the gambling match.

sn: निदेशाद् धर्मराजस्य द्रौपद्याः पदवीं चरन्। निर्धार्तराष्ट्रां पृथिवीं कर्तास्मि नचिरादिव॥
en: At the command of the king (Yudhisthira) and remembering the wrongs done to (Draupadi), I shall soon make the earth freed from the sons of Dhritarashtra.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवं ते पुरुषव्याघ्राः सर्वे व्यायतबाहवः। प्रतिज्ञा बहुलः कृत्वा धृतराष्ट्रमुपागमन्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having thus taken many vows, those mighty armed and foremost of men (the Pandavas) went to Dhritarashtra.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच आमन्त्रयामि भरतांस्तथा वृद्धं पितामहम्। राजानं सोमदत्तं च महाराजं च बाह्निकम्॥
en: Yudhisthira said I bid farewell to all the descendants of Bharata, to my old grandsire (Bhisma) to king Somadatta, the great king Valhika.

sn: द्रोणं कृपं नृपांश्चान्यानश्वत्थामानमेव च। विदुरं धृतराष्ट्रं च धार्तराष्ट्रांश्च सर्वशः॥
en: To Drona, to Kripa, to all the other kings, to Ashvathama, Vidura, Dhritarashtra, and to all the sons of Dhritarashtra.

sn: युयुत्सुं संजयं चैव तथैवान्यान् सभासदः। सर्वानामन्त्र्य गच्छामि द्रष्टास्मि पुनरेत्य वः॥
en: To Yuyutsu, Sanjaya, and all the Sabhasadas (court-officials). I bed you all farewell. I shall see you (again) on my return.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच न च किंचिदथोचुस्तं ह्रिया सन्ना युधिष्ठिरम्। मनोभिरेव कल्याणं दध्युस्ते तस्य धीमतः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Those that were present there could not out of shame tell anything to Yudhisthira, but they all prayed for the welfare of the intelligent (king).

sn: विदुर उवाच आर्या पृथा राजपुत्री नारण्यं गन्तुमर्हति। सुकुमारी च वृद्धा च नित्यं चैव सुखोचिता॥
en: Vidura said The reversed Pritha (Kunti) is a princess. She should not go to the forest. She is delicate and old, and she is ever in happiness.

sn: इह वत्स्यति कल्याणी सत्कृता मम वेश्मनि। इति पार्था विजानीध्वमगदं वोऽस्तु सर्वशः॥
en: The blessed lady will remain in my house (well) respected by me. O sons of Pritha, know this, and let safety by yours in every way.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तथेत्युक्त्वाब्रुवन् सर्वे यथा नो वदसेऽनघ। त्वं पितृव्यः पितृसमो वयं च त्वत्परायणाः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Thereupon they (the Pandavas) all said, “O sinless one, let it be as you say. You are our uncle, and (therefore) you are the same as our father. We are all obedient to you.

sn: यथाऽऽज्ञापयसे विद्वंस्त्वं हि नः परमो गुरुः। यच्चान्यदपि कर्तव्यं तद् विधत्स्व महामते॥
en: O learned man, you are our most respected Guru (superior). O high-souled one, command us what else is there to be done".

sn: विदुर उवाच युधिष्ठिर विजानीहि ममेदं भरतर्षभ। नाधर्मेण जितः कश्चिद् व्यथते वै पराजय॥
en: Vidura said O Yudhisthira, O best of the Bharata race, know this to be my opinion that he who is defeated by sinful means need not be pained for such defeat.

sn: त्वं वै धर्मं विजानीषे युद्धे जेता धनंजयः। हन्तारीणां भीमसेनो नकुलस्त्वर्थसंग्रही॥
en: You know every rule of Dharma. Dhananjaya (Arjuna) is ever victorious in battle. Bhimsena is the slayer of foes, Nakula is the gatherer of wealth.

sn: संयन्ता सहदेवस्तु धौम्यो ब्रह्मविदुत्तमः। धर्मार्थकुशला चैव द्रौपदी धर्मचारिणी॥
en: Sahadeva has administrative talents, Dhaumya is the best of all men learned in the Vedas, and the virtuous Draupadi is learned in Dharma and Artha.

sn: अन्योन्यस्य प्रियाः सर्वे तथैव प्रियदर्शनाः। परैरभेद्याः संतुष्टाः को वो न स्पृहयेदिह॥
en: You are all attached to one another and you all feel delight at one another's presence; enemies cannot separate you from one another, and you are all contented.

sn: एष वै सर्वकल्याणः समाधिस्तव भारत। नैनं शत्रुर्विषहते शक्रेणापि समोऽप्युत॥
en: O descendent of Bharata, for this patient abstraction from the worldly possessions will be great benefit to you. No enemy, even if he be like Shakra (Indra), will be able to stand it.

sn: हिमवत्यनुशिष्टोऽसि मेरुसावर्णिना पुरा। द्वैपायनेन कृष्णेन नगरे वारणावते॥
en: You were instructed on the mountains of Himalaya by Meru-Savarani. You were instructed in Varanavata by Krishna Dvaipayana (Vyasa).

sn: भृगुतुङ्गे च रामेण दृषद्वत्यां च शम्भुना। अश्रौषीरसितस्यापि महर्षेरञ्जनं प्रति॥
en: On the Bhrigu mountain by Rama, on the banks of the Drishadvati by Shambhu (Shiva). You have also received instructions from the great Rishi Asita on the Anajna mountains.

sn: कल्माषीतीरसंस्थस्य गतस्त्वं शिष्यतां भृगोः। द्रष्टा सदा नारदस्ते धौम्यस्तेऽयं पुरोहितः॥
en: You became a disciple of Bhrigu on the banks of the Kalmashi. Narada and your this priest Dhaumya will be now your instructors.

sn: मा हासीः साम्पराये त्वं बुद्धि तामृषिपूजिताम्। पुरूरवसमैलं त्वं बुद्ध्या जयसि पाण्डव॥
en: Do not abandon the excellent lessons, ever adored by the Rishis, as regards the next world. O sons of Pandu, you surpass in intelligence even Pururava, the son of Ila.

sn: शक्त्या जयसि राज्ञोऽन्यानृषीन् धर्मोपसेवया। ऐन्द्रे जये धृतमना याम्ये कोपविधारणे॥
en: In strength all other kings, and in virtue even the Rishis. Resolve earnestly to win the victory which is the attribute of Indra, to control anger which is the attribute of Yama.

sn: तथा विसर्गे कौबेरे वारुणे चैव संयमे। आत्मप्रदानं सौम्यत्वमद्भ्यश्चैवोपजीवनम्॥
en: To give in charity which is the attribute of Kuvera, and to control all passions which is the attribute of Varuna. Obtain the power of gladdening from the moon, the power of sustaining all from the water.

sn: भूमेः क्षमा च तेजश्च समग्रं सूर्यमण्डलात्। वायोर्बलं प्राप्नुहि त्वं भूतेभ्यश्चात्मसम्पदम्॥
en: Forbearance from earth, energy from the whole of the solar disc, strength from the winds, and affluence from the creatures.

sn: अगदं वोऽस्तु भद्रं वो द्रष्टास्मि पुनरागतान्। आपद्धर्मार्थकृच्छ्रेषु सर्वकार्येषु वा पुनः॥ यथावत् प्रतिपद्येथाः काले काले युधिष्ठिर। आपृष्टोऽसीह कौन्तेय स्वस्ति प्राप्नुहि भारत॥
en: Welfare and immunity from disease by yours. I hope to see you return (in all safety). O Yudhisthira, act properly and duly in all seasons-in the time of distress, in that of difficulty, and in respect of every thing, O son of Kunti, O descendant of Bharata, with our permission depart. Blessings be on you.

sn: कृतार्थं स्वस्तिमन्तं त्वां द्रक्ष्यामः पुनरागतम्। न हि वो वृजिनं किंचिद् वेद कश्चित्पुरा कृतम्।।
en: None can say that you have done any thing sinful before. We hope to see you return in safety and crowned with success.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्तस्तथेत्युक्त्वा पाण्डवः सत्यविक्रमः। भीष्मद्रोणौ नमस्कृत्य प्रातिष्ठत युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Thus addressed the greatly powerful Pandava (Yudhisthira), saying, “Be it so" and bowing low to Bhisma and Drona, went away.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तस्मिन् सम्प्रस्थिते कृष्णा पृथां प्राप्य यशस्विनीम्। अपृच्छद् भृशदुःखार्ता याश्चान्यास्तत्र योषितः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Thereupon, when Krishna (Draupadi) was about to start, she went to the illustrious Pritha (Kunti) and asked her leave and that of the other ladies who were all plunged in grief.

sn: यथार्ह वन्दनाश्लेषान् कृत्वा गन्तुमियेष सा। ततो निनादः सुमहान् पाण्डवान्तःपुरेऽभवत्॥
en: Saluting and embracing every one of them as each deserved, she desired to go away. Thereupon loud lamentations rose within the inner apartments of the Pandavas.

sn: कुन्ती च भृशसंतप्ता द्रौपदी प्रेक्ष्य गच्छतीम्। शोकविह्वलया वाचा कृच्छ्राद् वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Kunti, being greatly afflicted on seeing Draupadi on the eve of her journey, uttered these words in a voice choked with grief.

sn: कुन्त्युवाच वत्से शोको न ते कार्यः प्राप्येदं व्यसनं महत्। स्त्रीधर्माणामभिज्ञासि शीलाचारवती तथा॥
en: Kunti said O child, do not grieve that this great calamity has overtaken you. You are well aware of all the duties of the female sex. Your character and conduct are as they should be.

sn: न त्वां संदेष्टुमर्हासि भर्तृन् प्रति शुचिस्मिते। साध्वीगुणसमापन्ना भूषितं ते कुलद्वयम्॥
en: O lady of sweet smiles, I need not instruct you as to your duties towards your lords. You are chaste and accomplished; your qualifications and accomplishments have adorned our two races (those of the Kurus and the Pandavas).

sn: सभाग्याः कुरवश्चमे ये न दग्धास्त्वयानचे। अरिष्टं व्रज पन्थानं मदनुध्यानबृंहिता॥
en: The Kurus are (very) fortunate that they have not been burnt by your wrath. O siniess one, go away in safety, blessed by my prayer.

sn: भाविन्यर्थे हि सत्स्त्रीणां वैकृतं नोपजायते। गुरुधर्माभिगुप्ता च श्रेयः क्षिप्रमवाप्स्यसि॥
en: The hearts of good woman never moved by what is inevitable. Protected by great virtue, you will soon obtain good fortune.

sn: सहदेवश्च मे पुत्रः सदावेक्ष्योः वने वसन्। यथेदं व्यसनं प्राप्य नायं सीदेमहामतिः॥
en: While living in the woods, keep your eyes always on my child Sahadeva, so that his mind may not sink under this great calamity.

sn: तथेत्युक्त्वा तु सा देवी स्रवन्नेत्रजलाविला। शोणिताक्तैकवसना मुक्तकेशी विनिर्ययौ॥
en: Vaishampayana said Saying, "so be it,” the lady Draupadi clad in one cloth stained with blood, and with dishevelled hair, came out (of the inner apartment in tears.

sn: तां क्रोशन्तीं पृथा दुःखादनुवव्राज गच्छतीम्। अथापश्यत् सुतान् सर्वान् हृताभरणवाससः॥
en: As she went away weeping and lamenting, Pritha (Kunti) herself in grief, followed her. She saw her sons, shorn of their ornaments and robes.

sn: रुरुचर्मावृततनून् ह्रिया किंचिदवाङ्मुखान्। परैः परीतान् संहृष्टैः सुहृद्धिश्चानुशोचितान्॥
en: Their body clad in deer skins and their heads cast down. They were surrounded by rejoining foes and they were pitied by friends.

sn: तदवस्थान् सुतान् सर्वानुपसृत्यातिवत्सला। स्वजमानावदच्छोकात् तत्तद् विलपती बहु॥
en: Kunti, possessing excess of parental affection, approached her sons who were in that state. Embracing them all, she spoke thus her voice choked with grief.

sn: कुन्त्युवाच कथं सद्धर्मचारित्रान् वृत्तस्थितिविभूषितान्। अक्षुद्रान् दृढभक्तांश्च दैवतेज्यापरान् सदा॥
en: Kunti said You are virtuous and well-conducted; you are adorned with all excellent qualities; your behaviours is (always) respectful. You are all high minded, you are (always).

sn: व्यसनं वः समभ्यागात् कोऽयं विधिविपर्ययः। कस्यापध्यानजं चेदं धिया पश्यामि नैव तत्॥
en: Engaged in the service of your superiors; you are ever devoted to the gods and the performance of sacrifices, why then this calamity has overtaken you? Whence in this your reverse of fortune? I do not see whose wickedness and sin have fallen on you.

sn: स्यात् तु मद्भाग्यदोषोऽयं याहं युष्मानजीजनम्। दुःखायासभुजोऽत्यर्थं युक्तानप्युत्तमैर्गुणैः॥
en: All this must be due to my bad fortune, for I have given birth to you. It is for this you have been overtaken by this calamity, notwithstanding your possessing excellent accomplishments.

sn: कथं वत्स्यथ दुर्गेषु वने ऋद्धिविनाकृताः। वीर्यसत्त्वबलोत्साहतेजोभिरकृशाः कृशाः॥
en: Your are not wanting in energy prowess, strength, firmness and might. How will you live in great wilderness shorn of your wealth and possession?

sn: यद्येतदेवमज्ञास्यं वने वासो हि वि ध्रुवम्। शतशृङ्गन्मृते पाण्डौ नागमिष्यं गजाह्वयम्॥
en: If I had known before that you were destined to live in the forest, I would not have (then) come after Pandu's death from the mountains of Shatashringa to Hastinapur.

sn: धन्यं वः पितरं मन्ये तपोमेधान्वितं तथा। यः पुत्राधिमसम्प्राप्य स्वर्गेच्छाम करोत् प्रियाम्॥
en: Fortunate was your father; I consider it now, for he recapped the fruit of asceticism and there fore did not meet with the misery appertaining to one's sons. He considered the desire to attain to heaven as the most delightful.

sn: धन्यां चातीन्द्रियज्ञानामिमां प्राप्तां परां गतिम्। मन्ये तु माद्रीं धर्मज्ञां कल्याणी सर्वथैव तु॥
en: I consider today the virtuous and the blessed Madri as very fortunate, for she had, a fore-knowledge of what would happen and had thus obtained the great emancipation,

sn: रत्या मत्या च गत्या च ययाहमभिसन्धिता। जीवितप्रियतां मह्यं धिमां संक्लेशभागिनीम्॥
en: Madri looked upon me as her stay and her mind and her affections were ever fixed on me. Fie on my desire of life? I suffer all this woe for it.

sn: पुत्रकान विहास्ये वः कृच्छ्रलब्धान् प्रियान् सतः। साहं यास्यामि हि वनं हा कृष्णे किं जहासि माम्॥
en: O sons, you are all excellent; and you are all dear to me. I have obtained you after much suffering. I cannot leave you; I will go with you. O Krishna, alas, why do you leave me so?

sn: अन्तवत्यसुधर्मेऽस्मिन् धात्रा किं नु प्रमादतः। ममान्तो नैव विहितस्तेनायुर्न जहाति माम्॥
en: Everything possessing life is sure to perish. Has Dhatra (creator) forgotten to ordain my death? Perhaps it is so; and that is why life does not quit me.

sn: हा कृष्ण द्वारकावासिन् क्वासि संकर्षणानुज। कस्मान्न त्रायसे दुःखान्मां चेमांश्च नरोत्तमान्॥
en: O Krishna, O dweller of Dwarka, O younger brother of Sankarshana (Baladeva), where are you? Why do you not save me and these best of men (the Pandavas)?

sn: अनादिनिधनं ये त्वामनुध्यायन्ति वै नराः। तांस्त्वं पासीत्ययं वादः स गतो व्यर्थतां कथम्॥
en: The men say that you are without beginning and without end and that you save those who think of you. Why does this saying now turn to be false?

sn: इमे सद्धर्ममाहात्म्ययशोवीर्यानुवर्तिनः। नार्हन्ति व्यसनं भोक्तुं नन्वेषां क्रियतां दया!॥
en: These my sons are ever attached to virtue, nobility, good fame and prowess. They do not deserve to suffer afflictions. Show kindness towards them.

sn: सेयं नीत्यर्थविज्ञेषु भीष्मद्रोणकृपादिषु। स्थितेषु कुलनाथेषु कथमापदुपागता॥
en: When such leaders of our race as Bhisma, Drona, and Kripa, all learned in morality and Artha, are present how could such a calamity (at all) happen?

sn: हा पाण्डो हा महाराज क्वासि किं समुपेक्षसे। पुत्रान् विवास्यतः साधूनरिभि तनिर्जितान्॥
en: Alas Pandu! Alas, lord where are you? How could you see your good children sent into exile thus persecuted by gambling?

sn: सहदेव निवर्तस्व ननु त्वमसि मे प्रियः। शरीरादपि माद्रेय मा मा त्याक्षीः कुपुत्रवत्॥
en: Sahadeva, you do not go. You are dearer to me than my own body. O son of Madri, do not forsake me; you should be kind to me.

sn: व्रजन्तु भ्रातरस्तेऽमी यदि सत्याभिसंधिनः। मत्परित्राणजं धर्ममिहैव त्वमवाप्नुहि॥
en: If they are bound by the dictates of virtue, let these your (elder) brothers go. You earn that virtue which is the fruit of waiting upon me (a mother).

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवं विलपती कुन्तीमभिवाद्य प्रणम्य च। पाण्डवा विगतानन्दा वनायैव प्रवव्रजुः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Consoling their weeping (mother) Kunti and bowing to her, the Pandavas set for the forest in great grief.

sn: विदुरश्चापि तामा" कुन्तीमाश्वास्य हेतुभिः। प्रावेशयद् गृहं क्षत्ता स्वयमार्ततरः शनैः॥
en: Vidura, himself greatly grieved, consoled the afflicted Kunti with reasons, and Khattwa (Vidura) then led her slowly to his house.

sn: धार्तराष्ट्रस्त्रियस्ताश्च निखिलेनोपलभ्य तत्। गमनं परिकर्षं च कृष्णाया द्यूतमण्डले॥
en: The ladies of Dhritarashtra's house hold, hearing every thing as it had happened namely the exile (of the Pandavas) and the dragging of Krishna (Draupadi) in the assembly of gambling.

sn: रुरुदुः सुस्वनं सर्वा विनिन्दन्त्यः कुरून् भृशम्। दध्युश्च सुचिरं कालं करासक्तमुखाम्बुजाः॥
en: Loudly wept, all greatly censuring the Kurus. The ladies of the royal household sat silent for a long time covering their lotus like faces with their hands.

sn: राजा च धृतराष्ट्रस्तु पुत्राणामनयं तदा। ध्यायन्नुद्विग्नहृदयो न शान्तिमधिजग्मिवान्॥
en: King Dhritarashtra, thinking of the dangers that threatened his sons, became a prey to anxiety and could not get any peace of mind.

sn: स चिन्तयन्ननेकाग्रः शोकव्याकुलचेतनः। क्षत्तुः सम्प्रेषयामास शीघ्रमागम्यतामिति॥
en: Anxious meditating on everything and with mind deprived of its equanimity by grief, he sent for Khattwa (Vidura) asking him to come (to him) without delay.

sn: ततो जगाम विदुरो धृतराष्ट्रनिवेशनम्। तं पर्यपृच्छत् संविग्नो धृतराष्ट्रो जनाधिपः॥
en: Thereupon Vidura went to Dhritarashtra's palace and the ruler of men Dhritarashtra asked him in great anxiety.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तमागतमथो राजा विदुरं दीर्घदर्शिनम्। साशरू इव पप्रच्छ धृतराष्ट्रोऽम्बिकासुतः॥
en: Vaishampayana said As soon as Vidura of great foresight came, the king Dhritarashtra, the son of Ambika, asked him timidly.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच कथं गच्छति कौन्तेयो धर्मपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः। भीमसेनः सव्यसाची माद्रीपुत्रौ च पाण्डवौ॥
en: Dhritarashtra said How does the son of Kunti, and Dharma, Yudhisthira, proceed along? How does Bhimasena also Savyasachi (Arjuna) and the two Pandavas, the sons of Madri?

sn: धौम्यश्चैव कथं क्षत्तद्रौपदी च यशस्विनी। श्रोतुमिच्छाम्यहं सर्वं तेषां शंस विचेष्टितम्॥
en: O Khattwa, how does Dhaumya? How does the illustrious Draupadi (proceed along)? I desire to hear everything. Describe to me all their acts.

sn: विदुर उवाच वस्त्रेण संवृत्य मुखं कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः। बाहू विशालौ सम्पश्यन् भीमो गच्छति पाण्डवः॥
en: Vidura said The son of Kunti (has gone away), covering his face with cloth, the Pandava Bhima has proceeded along looking at his mighty arms.

sn: सिकता वपन् सव्यसाची राजानमनुगच्छति। माद्रीपुत्रः सहदेवो मुखमालिप्य गच्छति॥
en: Savyasachi (Arjuna) has followed the king, (Yudhisthira) scattering sands along. The son of Madri, Sahadeva proceeds (the way) besmearing his face.

sn: पांसूपलिप्तसर्वाङ्गो नकुलश्चित्तविह्वलः। दर्शनीयतमो लोके राजानमनुगच्छति॥
en: That handsomest of men in the world, Nakula, has gone following the king in great grief, staining himself with dust.

sn: कृष्णा तु केशैः प्रच्छाद्य मुखमायतलोचना। दर्शनीया प्ररुदती राजानमनुगच्छति॥
en: The large eyed and beautiful Krishna (Draupadi) has followed the king, covering her face with her dishevelled hair and bathing in tears.

sn: धौम्यो रौद्राणि सामानि याम्यानि च विशाम्पते। गायन् गच्छति मार्गेषु कुशानादाय पाणिना॥
en: O king, Dhaumya proceeds along with Kusha grass in hand, uttering the fearful Mantras of the Sama Veda relating to Yama.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच विविधानीह रूपाणि कृत्वा गच्छन्ति पाण्डवाः। तन्ममाचक्ष्व विदुर कस्मादेवं व्रजन्ति ते॥
en: Dhritarashtra said The Pandavas are going assuming various guise. O Vidura, tell me why they are going in this way.

sn: विदुर उवाच निकृतस्यापि ते पुत्रैर्हते राज्ये धनेषु च। न धर्माच्चलते बुद्धिर्धर्मराजस्य धीमतः॥
en: Vidura said Through persecuted by your sons, and robbed off his kingdom and wealth, the mind of the wise Dharmaraja (Yudhisthira) has not deviated from the path of virtue.

sn: योऽसौ राजा घृणी नित्यं धार्तराष्ट्रेषु भारत। निकृत्या भ्रंशितः क्रोधान्नोन्मीलयति लोचने।॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, the king (Yudhisthira) is always kind to the sons of Dhritarashtra. Deprived of kingdom by foul means, he does not open his eyes in anger.

sn: नाहं जनं निर्दहेयं दृष्ट्वा घोरेण चक्षुषा। स पिधाय मुखं राजा तस्माद् गच्छति पाण्डवः॥१२।
en: "I shall not consume men by looking at them with fearful eyes," thinking this, the Pandava king proceeds along with covered face.

sn: यथा च भीमो व्रजति तन्मे निगदतः शृणु। बाह्वोर्बले नास्ति समो ममेति भरतर्षभ।॥
en: Hear, I tell you, why Bhima goes in this way. O best of the Bharata race, thinking “There is none equal to me in strength of arms."

sn: बाहू विशालौ कृत्वासौ तेन भीमोऽपि गच्छति। बाहू विदर्शयन् राजन् बाहुद्रविणदर्पितः॥ चिकीर्षन् कर्म शत्रुभ्यो बाहुद्रव्यानुरूपतः। प्रदिशञ्छरसम्पातान् कुन्तीपुत्रोऽर्जुनस्तदा॥
en: O king Bhima ever proud of his strength of arms, goes repeatedly stretching forth his mighty arms and exhibiting them and desiring to do to his enemies, deeds worthy of those arms. The son of Kunti, Arjuna, capable of using both his arms (in throwing weapon),

sn: सिकता वपन् सव्यसाची राजानमनुगच्छति। असक्ताः सिकतास्तस्य यथा सम्प्रति भारत। असक्तं शरवर्षाणि तथा मोक्ष्यति शत्रुषु॥ न मे कश्चिद् विजानीयान्मुखमद्येति भारत।
en: That Savyasachi, O descendant of Bharata, follows the king, scattering dust emblematical of the arrows he will shower in the battle. O descendant of Bharata, it indicated that as the sand grains are scattered by him with ease, so will he rain arrows with ease on the enemy. O lord, thinking “None may recognise me in this day of calamity,"

sn: मुखमालिप्य तेनासौ सहदेवोऽपि गच्छति॥ नाहं मनांस्याददेयं मार्गे स्त्रीणामिति प्रभो। पांसूपलिप्तसर्वाङ्गो नकुलस्तेन गच्छति॥
en: Sahadeva proceeds along besmearing his face. Nakula goes with his body besmeared with ashes, thinking, “I may steal the hearts of the ladies that may look at me."

sn: एकवस्त्रा प्ररुदती मुक्तकेशी रजस्वला। शोणितेनाक्तवसना द्रौपदी वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
en: Draupadi, attired in one piece of cloth, stained with blood, and her hair dishevelled (proceeds along) weeping and saying.

sn: यत्कृतेऽहमिदं प्राप्ता तेषां वर्षे चतुर्दशे। हतपत्यो हतसुता हतबन्धुजनप्रियाः॥ बहुशोणितदिग्धाङ्गयो मुक्तकेशयो रजस्वलः। एवं कृतोदका भार्याः प्रवेक्ष्यन्ति गजाह्वयम्॥
en: “The wives of those for whom I have been reduced to such a plight shall, on the fourteenth year hence, deprived of their husbands, sons, relatives and dear ones smeared all over with blood, all in their seasons, and with hair dishevelled enter Hastinapur having offered oblations of water to the manes of their dead husbands.

sn: कृत्वा तु नैर्ऋतान् दर्भान् धीरो धौम्यः पुरोहितः। सामानि गायन् याम्यानि पुरतो याति भारत॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, the learned and self controlled priest Dhaumya, holding the Kusha (grass) in his hand and pointing them towards the south west, walk before (the Pandavas) singing the Mantras of the Samaveda.

sn: हतेषु भारतेष्वाजौ कुरूणां गुरवस्तदा। एवं सामानि गास्यन्तीत्युक्त्वा धौम्योऽपि गच्छति॥२३
en: Dhaumya is preceding, saying "When the descendant of Bharata will be killed in battle, the priests and preceptors of the Kurus will thus sing the Sama Mantras."

sn: हा हा गच्छन्ति नो नाथाः समवेक्षध्वमीदृशम्। अहो धिक् कुरुवृद्धानां बालानामिव चेष्टितम्॥
en: “Alas, alas, our lords are going away! O fie on the Kuru chiefs who have acted like children.

sn: राष्ट्रेभ्यः पाण्डुदायादाँल्लोभान्निर्वासयन्ति ये। अनाथाः स्म वयं सर्वे वियुक्ताः पाण्डुनन्दनैः॥
en: In thus banishing the heirs of Pandu from covetousness! We shall be masterless, being thus separated from the Pandavas,
