sn: दुर्विनीतेषु लुब्धेषु का प्रीतिः कौरवेषु नः। इति पौराः सुदुःखार्ताः क्रोशन्ति स्म पुनः पुनः॥२६
en: What love can we bear for the wicked and covetous Kurus”? The citizens repeatedly bewailed thus in great grief.

sn: एवमाकारलिङ्गैस्ते व्यवसायं मनोगतम्। कथयन्तश्च कौन्तेया वनं जग्मुर्मनस्विनः॥
en: The son of Kunti, all possessing great energy of mind, has gone away to the forest indicating by signs the resolution that were in their minds.

sn: एवं तेषु नरावयेषु निर्यत्सु गजसाह्वयात्। अनभ्रे विद्युतश्चासन् भूमिश्च समकम्पत॥
en: At the departure of those foremost of men from Hastinapur, lightning flashed in the cloudless sky, earth began to tremble,

sn: राहुरग्रसदादित्यमपर्वणि विशाम्पते। उल्का चाप्यपसव्येन पुरं कृत्वा व्यशीर्यत॥
en: Rahu came to devour the sun, although it was not the day of an eclipse, meteors began to fall, keeping the city to their right.

sn: प्रत्याहरन्ति क्रव्यादा गृध्रगोमायुवायसाः। देवायतनचैत्येषु प्राकाराट्टालकेषु च॥
en: Jackals, vultures, ravens, and other carnivorous beasts and birds began to shriek from the temples of the gods, from the tops of sacred trees and from walls and housetops.

sn: एवमेते महोत्पाताः प्रादुरासन् दुरासदाः। भरतानामभावाय राजन् दुर्मन्त्रिते तव॥
en: O king, thus extraordinary and fearful protents were seen and heard, indicating the destruction of the Bharata race the consequence of your evil counsels;

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवं प्रवदतोरेव तयोस्तत्र विशाम्पते। धृतराष्ट्रस्य राज्ञश्च विदुरस्य च धीमतः॥
en: Vaishampayana said O king, when the king Dhritarashtra and the intelligent Vidura were thus talking, there as came.

sn: स्थितः। नारदश्च सभामध्ये कुरूणामग्रतः महर्षिभिः परिवृतो रौद्रं वाक्यमुवाच ह॥
en: To the Sabha (and stood) in the midst of the Kurus, Narada surrounded by great Rishis. He then uttered these terrible words.

sn: इतश्चतुर्दशे वर्षे विनक्ष्यन्तीह कौरवाः। दुर्योधनापराधेन भीमार्जुनबलेन च॥
en: Narada said On the fourteenth year hence, for the fault of Duryodhana will be destroyed the Kurus by the prowess of Bhima and Arjuna.

sn: इत्युक्त्वा दिवमाक्रम्य क्षिप्रमन्तरधीयत। ब्राह्मीं श्रियं सुविपुलां बिभ्रद् देवर्षिसत्तमः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having said this, that foremost of all celestial Rishis, adorned with surprising Vedic grace, disappeared from the scene, passing into the sky.

sn: ततो दुर्योधनः कर्णः शकुनिश्चापि सौबलः। द्रोणं द्वीपममन्यन्त राज्यं चास्मै न्यवेदयन्॥
en: Thereupon Duryodhana, Karna and the son of Subala, Shakuni, considering Drona as the island (refuse) offered him the kingdom.

sn: अथाब्रवीत् ततो द्रोणो दुर्योधनममर्षणाम्। दुःशासनं च कर्णं च सर्वानेव च भारतान्॥
en: Then Drona spoke thus to the wicked Duryodhana, Dushasana, Karna and all the other Bharatas.

sn: अवध्यान् पाण्डवान् प्राहुर्देवपुत्रान् द्विजातयः। अहं वै शरणं प्राप्तान् वर्तमानो यथाबलम्॥ गन्ता सर्वात्मना भक्त्या धार्तराष्ट्रान् सराजकान्। नोत्सहेयं परित्यक्तुं दैवं हि बलवत्तरम्॥
en: Drona said The Brahmanas have said that the Pandavas of celestial origin are incapable of being killed. The sons of Dhritarashtra, with all their forces, heartily and with reverence have sought my protection; I shall look after them to the best of my power. I cannot abandon them. Destiny is Supreme.

sn: धर्मतः पाण्डुपुत्रा वै वनं गच्छन्ति निर्जिताः। ते च द्वादश वर्षाणि वने वत्स्यन्ति पाण्डवाः॥
en: The sons of Pandu, being defeated at dice, are going to the forest to save their virtue. The Pandavas will live for twelve years in the forest.

sn: चरितब्रह्मचर्याश्च क्रोधामर्षवशानुगाः। वैरं निर्यातयिष्यन्ति महद् दुःखाय पाण्डवाः॥
en: Practising Brahmacharya. The Pandavas will to our great grief return in anger (at the end of the thirteenth) to take great ngeanceve on their foes.

sn: मया च भ्रंशितो राजन् दुपदः सखिविग्रहे। पुत्रार्थमयजद् राजा वधाय मम भारत॥
en: I formerly deprived Drupada of his kingdom in a quarrel over friendship. O descendant of Bharata, robbed of his kingdom, the king (Drupada) performed a sacrifice to obtain a son who would kill me.

sn: याजोपयाजतपसा पुत्रं लेभे स पावकात्। धृष्टद्युम्नं द्रौपदी च वेदीमध्यात् सुमध्यमाम्॥
en: By the ascetic power of Yaja and Upayaja, he has obtained a son from (the sacrificial) fire, (namely) Dhristadyumna and (a daughter) the faultless Krishna (Draupadi), both risen from the sacrificial alter.

sn: धृष्टद्युम्नस्तु पार्थानां श्यालः सम्बन्धतो मतः। पाण्डवानां प्रियरतस्तस्मान्मां भयमाविशत्॥
en: Dhristadyumna is the brother-in-law of the sons of Pritha by marriage; he is ever engaged in doing the favourite works of the Pandavas. I have, therefore, a great fear.

sn: ज्वालावर्णो देवदत्तो धनुष्मान् कवची शरी। मर्त्यधर्मतया तस्मादद्य मे साध्वसो महान्॥
en: Of celestial origin and of effulgence as that of fire, he was born with bow, arrows and armour. I have great fear from him.

sn: गतो हि पक्षतां तेषां पार्षतः परवीरहा। स्थातिरथसंख्यायां योऽग्रणीरर्जुनो युवा॥
en: The slayer of hostile heroes, the son of Prishata (Drupada), has taken the side of that your hero who stands at the head of all great car warriors.

sn: सृष्टप्राणो भृशतरं तेन चेत् संगमो मम। किमन्यद् दुःखमधिकं परमं भुवि कौरवाः॥
en: I shall have to lose my life if he and I have ever to meet each other in battle. O Kurus, what could be a greater grief to me than this in the world?

sn: धृष्टद्युम्नो द्रोणमृत्युरिति विप्रथितं वचः। मद्वधाय श्रुतोऽप्यष लोके चाप्यति विश्रुतः॥
en: “Dhristadyumna is the slayer of Drona" is the general belief. I have heard that he is born to kill me. This is also widely known in the world.

sn: सोऽयं नूनमनुप्राप्तस्त्वत्कृते काल उत्तमः। त्वरितं कुरुत श्रेयो नैतदेतावता कृतम्॥
en: For your sake, that fearful time of destruction has come, Do without any loss of time what may be beneficial to you.

sn: मुहूर्तं सुखमेवैतत् तालच्छायेव हैमनी। यजध्वं च महायज्ञैर्भोगानश्नीत दत्त च॥
en: Your happiness will last but for a moment as the shadow of the top of the palm tree rests in winter only but a moment at its base. Perform various sacrifices; enjoy and give away every thing at your heart's content.

sn: इतश्चतुर्दशे वर्षे महत् प्राप्यस्यथ वैशसम्। द्रोणस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा धृतराष्ट्रोऽब्रवीदिदम्॥
en: On the fourteenth year a great calamity will overwhelm you. (Vaishampayana said) Having heard the words of Drona, Dhritarashtra said.

sn: सम्यगाह गुरुः क्षत्तरुपावर्तय पाण्डवान्। यदि ते न निवर्तन्ते सत्कृता यान्तु पाण्डवाः। सशस्त्ररथपादाता भोगवन्तश्च :॥ पुत्रकाः
en: Dhritarashtra said O Kshatta (Vidura), the preceptor has said what is true. Go and back the Pandavas. If they do not come back, let them go, but after being treated with respect and affection; let my these children (the Pandavas) go with arms, soldiers and cars, enjoying every good thing.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच वनं गतेषु पार्थेषु निर्जितेषु दुरोदरे। धृतराष्ट्र महाराज तदा चिन्ता समाविशत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said At the departure of the Pandavas to the forest after being defeated at dice, the great king Dhritarashtra was afflicted with great anxiety.

sn: तं चिन्तयानमासीनं धृतराष्ट्रं जनेश्वरम्। निःश्वसन्तमनेकाग्रमिति होवाच संजयः॥
en: When the ruler of men, Dhritarashtra was thus seated in anxiety and restlessness and sighing in grief, Sanjaya came to him and spoke thus.

sn: संजय उवाच अवाप्य वसुसम्पूर्णां वसुधां वसुधाधिप। प्रव्राज्य पाण्डवान् राज्याद् राजन् किमनुशोचसि॥
en: Sanjaya said O lord of the world, you have (now) obtained the whole earth with all its wealth; you have banished the Pandavas, why then do you grieve so?

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच अशोच्यत्वं कुतस्तेषां येषां वैरं भविष्यति। पाण्डवैर्युद्धशौण्डैर्हि बलवद्भिर्महारथैः॥
en: Dhritarashtra said What have they not to grieve for who will have to meet in battle those foremost of heroes, the Pandavas those great car warriors aided by allies.

sn: संजय उवाच तवेदं स्वकृतं राजन् महद् वैरमुपस्थितम्। विनाशो येन लोकस्य सानुबन्धो भविष्यति॥
en: Sanjaya said O king, this is assuredly a great act of yours, this great hostility which is inevitable and which will cause the destruction of the whole world.

sn: वार्यमाणो हि भीष्मेण द्रोणेन विदुरेण च। पाण्डवानां प्रियां भार्यां द्रौपदी धर्मचारिणीम्॥ प्राहिणोदानयेहेति पुत्रो दुर्योधनस्तव। सूतपुत्रं सुमन्दात्मा निर्लज्जः प्रातिकामिनम्॥
en: Forbidden by Bhisma, Drona, and Vidura, your wicked minded and shameless son, Duryodhana sent his Pratikamin, born in the Suta caste, commanding him to bring into the Sabha the beloved and virtuous wife of the Pandavas.

sn: यस्मै देवाः प्रयच्छन्ति पुरुषाय पराभवम्। बुद्धिं तस्यापकर्षन्ति सोऽवाचीनानि पश्यति॥
en: The celestial first deprive that man of his reason to whom they ordain defeat and disgrace. It is for this, he sees every thing in a strange light.

sn: बुद्धौ कलुषभूतायां विनाशे समुपस्थिते। अनयो नयसंकाशो हृदयानापसर्पति॥ अनर्थाश्चार्थरूपेण अर्थाश्चानर्थरूपिणः। उत्तिष्ठन्ति विनाशाय नूनं तच्चास्य रोचते॥
en: When destruction is at hand, evil, appearing as good to the mind polluted by sin, remains stuck to it. That which is improper appears as proper, and that which is proper appears as improper to a man overwhelmed by destruction. And this he (always) likes.

sn: न कालो दण्डमुद्यम्य शिरः कृन्तति कस्यचित्। कालस्य बलमेतावद् विपरीतार्थदर्शनम्॥
en: The Time that brings on destruction does not come with upraised club to smash one's head. Peculiarity of Time is this that it makes a man see evil in good and good in evil.

sn: आसादितमिदं घोरं तुमुलं लोमहर्षणम्। पाञ्चालीमपकर्षद्भिः सभामध्ये तपस्विनीम्॥
en: The wretches have brought on themselves this fearful, wholesale and horrible destruction by dragging into the Sabha the ascetic princess of Panchala.

sn: अयोनिजां रूपवती कुले जातां विभावसोः। को नु तां सर्वधर्मज्ञां परिभूय यशस्विनीम्॥ पर्यानयेत् सभामध्ये विना दुर्दूतदेविनम्। स्त्रीधर्मिणी वरारोहा शोणितेन परिप्लुता॥
en: Who else than that false player at dice (Duryodhana) could bring into the Sabha with insults the daughter of Drupada, possessing beauty and intelligence, being conversant with every rule of morality and duty, and sprung not from any woman's womb but from the sacred fire. That beautiful lady was in her season covered with blood.

sn: एकवस्त्राथ पाञ्चाली पाण्डवानभ्यवेक्षता हतस्वान् हतराज्यांश्च हृतवस्त्रान् हृतश्रियः॥ विहीनान् सर्वकामेभ्यो दासभावमुपागतान्। धर्मपाशपरिक्षिप्तानशक्तानिव विक्रमे॥ क्रुद्धां चानर्हती कृष्णां दु:खितां कुरुसंसदि।
en: And in one cloth. Panchali (Draupadi) saw the Pandavas, plunged in slavery and robbed of their wealth, of their kingdom, of their attire, of their beauty, and of every object of enjoyment. Bound by the tie of virtue, they were then unable to exert their prowess.

sn: दुर्योधनश्च कर्णश्च कटुकान्यभ्यभाषताम्॥ इति सर्वमिदं राजन्नाकुलं प्रतिभाति मे।
en: In the midst of the Kuru assembly, Duryodhana and Karna spoke cruel and harsh words to the distressed and enraged Krishna (Draupadi) who did not deserve such treatment.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच तस्याः कृपणचक्षुर्त्यां प्रदह्येतापि मेदिनी॥ अपि शेषं भवेदद्य पुत्राणां मम संजय।
en: Dhritarashtra said O Sanjaya, the glances of the affected Draupadi may consume the whole world. Is their any chance of any of my son's living?

sn: भरतानां स्त्रियः सर्वा गान्धार्या सह संगताः॥ प्राक्रोशन् भैरवं तत्र दृष्ट्वा कृष्णां सभागताम्। धर्मिष्ठां धर्मपत्नी च रूपयौवनशालिनीम्॥
en: The ladies of the Bharata race, with Gandhari, seeing the virtuous, young and beautiful Krishna (Draupadi), the wedded wife (of the Pandavas), dragged into court wept aloud. They are even now weeping every day along with all (my) subjects.

sn: प्रजाभिः सह संगम्य ह्यनुशोचन्ति नित्यशः। अग्निहोत्राणि सायाहे न चाहूयन्त सर्वशः॥
en: Enraged at the persecution on Draupadi, all the Brahmanas refrained from performing the Agnihotra in the evening.

sn: ब्राह्मणाः कुपिताश्चासन् द्रौपद्याः परिकर्षणे। आसीनिष्ठानको घोरो निर्घातश्च महानभूत्॥ दिव उल्काश्चापतन्त राहुश्चार्कमुपाग्रसत्। अपर्वणि महाघोरं प्रजानां जनयन् भयम्॥ तथैव रथशालासु प्रादुरासीद्भुताशनः।
en: The winds frightful begun to blow as they do at the universal destruction. A fearful thunder storm raged, Metros fell from the sky and devoured the sun, and unseasonably and fearfully alarmed all the people. The fire came blazing out from the chariot house.

sn: ध्वजाश्चापि व्यशीर्यन्त भरतानामभूतये॥ दुर्योधनस्याग्निहोत्रे प्राक्रोशन भैरवं शिवाः।
en: All their flag staffs fell down, foreboding evil to the Bharatas. Jackals fearfully cried out within the sacred fire chamber of Duryodhana.

sn: तास्तदा प्रत्यभाषन्त रासभाः सर्वतो दिशः॥ प्रातिष्ठत ततो भीष्मो द्रोणेन सह संजय।
en: Asses from all directions began to bray in response (to the jackal). O Sanjaya, then left the assembly Bhisma, Drona with

sn: कृपश्च सोमदत्तश्च बाह्रीकश्च महामनाः॥ ततोऽहमब्रुवं तत्र विदुरेण प्रचोदितः।
en: Kripa, Somadatta, and the high souled Valhika. It was then at the advice of Vidura, I spoke thus (to Draupadi).

sn: वरं ददानि कृष्णायै काक्षितं यद् यदिच्छति॥ अवृणोत् तत्र पाञ्चाली पाण्डवानामदासताम्।
en: "O Krishna, I shall grant you boons whatever you desire to have." Panchali (Draupadi) begged of me the liberation of the Pandavas.

sn: सरथान् सधनुष्कांश्चाप्यनुज्ञासिषमप्यहम्॥ अथाब्रवीन्महाप्राज्ञो विदुरः सर्वधर्मवित्।
en: I then set free the Pandavas and commanded them to go away with their cars, bows and arrows. It was then the greatly intelligent Vidura spoke thus.

sn: एतदन्तास्तु भरता यद् वः कृष्णा सभां गता॥ यैषा पाञ्चालराजस्य सुता सा श्रीरनुत्तमा।
en: Vidura said This will prove the destruction of the Bharata race, namely the dragging of Krishna into the Sabha. This excellent daughter of the Panchala is Sree (the goddess of wealth) herself.

sn: पाञ्चाली पाण्डवानेतान् दैवसृष्टोपसर्पति॥ तस्याः पार्थाः परिक्लेशं न ऑस्यन्ते घमर्षणाः।
en: Of celestial origin, Panchali is the wedded wife of the Pandavas. The wrathful sons of Pritha will never forgive the insult offered to her.

sn: वृष्णयो वा महेष्वासाः पाञ्चाला वा महारथाः॥ तेन सत्याभिसंधेन वासुदेवेन रक्षिताः।
en: The mighty bowmen of the Vrishni race, and the mighty Panchala car warriors will not suffer this in silence. Supported by Vasudeva (Krishna),

sn: आगमिष्यति बीभत्सुः पाञ्चालैः परिवारितः॥ तेषां मध्ये महेष्वासो भीमसेनो महाबलः।
en: Vivatsu (Arjuna) will certainly come back surrounded by the Panchala heroes. Among them, the great bowman and greatly powerful Bhimsena.

sn: आगमिष्यति धुन्वानो गदां दण्डमिवान्तकः॥ ततो गाण्डीवनिर्घोषं श्रुत्वा पार्थस्य धीमतः। गदावेगं च भीमस्य नालं सोढुं नराधिपाः॥ तत्र मे रोचते नित्यं पार्थैः साम न विग्रहः।
en: Will also come back whirling his club like Yama himself his mace. There will be no kings who will be able to stand the sound of the Govinda (bow) of the intelligent Partha (Arjuna) and the terrible force of the club of Bhima. Therefore it seems to me to be the best to have peace and not hostility with the sons of Pritha.

sn: कुरुभ्यो हि सदा मन्ये पाण्डवान् बलवत्तरान्॥ तथा हि बलवान् राजा जरासंधो महाद्युतिः।
en: The Pandavas are always stronger than the Kurus. The greatly effulgent king Jarasandha.

sn: बाहुप्रहरणेनैव भीमेन निहतो युधि॥ तस्य ते शम एवास्तु पाण्डवैर्भरतर्षभ।
en: Was killed in battle in Bhima with his bare arms. O best of the Bharata race, you should therefore make peace with the Pandavas.

sn: उभयोः पक्षयोर्युक्तं क्रियतामविशङ्कया॥
en: O great king, without scruples of any kind, unite the two parties. If it is done, you are sure to obtain good fortune."

sn: एवं कृते महाराज परं श्रेयस्त्वमाप्स्यसि। एवं गावल्गणे क्षत्ता धर्मार्थसहितं वचः॥ उक्तवान् न गृहीतं वै मया पुत्रहितैषिणा॥
en: Dhritarashtra said The son of Gavalgana, Khattwa (Vidura) spoke in words replete with Dharma and Artha. I did not accept his words moved by the affection I bear for my sons.

sn: नारायणं नमस्कृत्य नरं चैव नरोत्तमम्। देवी सरस्वतीं व्यासं ततो जयमुदीरयेत्।।
en: Having saluted the Supreme Deity (Narayana) and the highest of all male beings (Nara) and also the Goddess of Learning (Sarasvati), Let us cry "success!"

sn: जनमेजय उवाच एवं द्यूतजिताः पार्थाः कोपिताश्च दुरात्मभिः। धार्तराष्ट्र: सहामात्यैनिकृत्या द्विजसत्तम॥ श्राविता: परुषा वाचः सृजद्भिर्वैरमुत्तमम्। किमकुर्वत कौरव्य मम पूर्वपितामहाः॥
en: Janamejaya said : O best of Brahmanas, having been deceitfully defeated at dice by the sons of Dhritarashtra with their counsellors and having been provoked by the wicked-minded ones (the Kuru princes), who thus brought about a fearful hostility by addressing them in cruel words, what did the Kurus, my grandsires do?

sn: कथं चैश्वर्यविभ्रष्टाः सहसा दुःखमेयुषः। वने विजहिरे पार्थाः शक्रप्रतिमतेजसः॥
en: How did the sons of Pritha (the Pandavas), equal to Shakra (Indra) in effulgence, thus suddenly robbed of their affluence and overwhelmed with misery, pass their days in the forest?

sn: के वै तानन्ववर्तन्त प्राप्तान् व्यसनमुत्तमम्। किमाचाराः किमाहाराः क्व च वासो महात्मनाम्॥
en: Who are the men that followed them, (the Pandavas) that were plunged in great affliction. What was their conduct, what was their food and where did those illustrious ones live?

sn: कथं च द्वादश समा वने तेषां महामुने। व्यतीयुर्ब्राह्मणश्रेष्ठ शूराणामरिघातिनाम्॥
en: O great Rishi, O best of the Brahmanas, how did the twelve years of those heroes, those slayers of foes, pass away in the forest?

sn: कथं च राजपुत्री सा प्रवरा सर्वयोषिताम्। पतिव्रता महाभागा सततं सत्यवादिनी॥ वनवासमदुःखार्हा दारुणं प्रत्यपद्यत। एतदाचक्ष्व मे सर्वं विस्तरेण तपोधन॥
en: How did that foremost of all women, the royal princess (Draupadi), ever devoted to her husbands, greatly fortunate and truthful, undeserving of suffering misery, endure that painful exile in the forest? O great ascetic, tell me all this in detail.

sn: श्रोतुमिच्छामि चरितं भूरिद्रविणतेजसाम्। कथ्यमानं त्वया विप्र परं कौतूहलं हि मे॥
en: O Brahmana, I desire to hear the history of those greatly effulgent heroes narrated by you. I am in great curiosity.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवं द्यूतजिताः पार्थाः कोपिताश्च दुरात्मभिः। धार्तराष्ट्रैः सहामात्यैर्निर्ययुर्गजसाह्वयात्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having been thus defeated at dice and provoked by the wicked-minded sons of Dhritarashtra with their counsellors, the sons of Pritha (the Pandavas) set out from Hastinapur.

sn: वर्धमानपुद्वारदभिनिष्क्रम्य पाण्डवाः। उदङ्मुखाः शस्त्रभृतः प्रययुः सह कृष्णया॥
en: Coming out through the Vardhamana gate of the city, the Pandavas with Krishna and with their arms went away in a northerly direction.

sn: इन्द्रसेनादयश्चैव भृत्याः परि चतुर्दश। रथैरनुययुः शी।ः त्रिय आदाय सर्वशः॥
en: Indrasena and others, taking with them their fourteen servants with all their wives, followed them on their swift cars.

sn: गतानेतान् विदित्वा तु पौराः शोकाभिपीडिताः। गर्हयन्तोऽसकृद् भीष्मविदुरद्रोणगौतमान्॥ ऊचुर्विगतसंत्रासाः समागम्य परस्परम्।
en: Having learnt that they had gone away, the citizens were overwhelmed with great grief; and having all met together, they began without fear to censure among themselves Bhishma, Drona, Vidura and the son of Gautama (Kripa).

sn: पौरा ऊचुः नेदमस्ति कुलं सर्वं न वयं न च नो गृहाः॥ यत्र दुर्योधनः पापः सौबलेनाभिपालितः। कर्णदुःशासनाभ्यां च राज्यमेतच्चिकीर्षति॥
en: The citizens said : When the sinful Duryodhana, helped by the son of Subala (Shakuni), (Shakuni), Karna and Dushasana, aspires to this kingdom, our families, our homes, nay we ourselves are all gone.

sn: न तत् कुलं न चाचारो न धर्मोऽर्थः कुतः सुखम्। यत्र पापसहायोऽयं पापो राज्यं चिकीर्षति॥
en: When this sinful man with the help of other sinful men aspires to the kingdom, our families, usages, virtue and prosperity are all doomed. How can there be happiness (where these are destroyed)?

sn: दुर्योधनो गुरुद्वेषी त्यक्ताचारसुहृज्जनः। अर्थलुब्धोऽभिमानी च नीचः प्रकृतिनिघृणः॥
en: Duryodhana is malicious towards his superiors; he has abandoned all good conduct; he is covetous, vain, mean and by nature cruel.

sn: नैयमस्ति मही कृत्स्ना यत्र दुर्योधनो नृपः। साधु गच्छामहे सर्वे यत्र गच्छन्ति पाण्डवाः॥
en: Where Duryodhana is the king, there the whole earth is doomed. Let us proceed there where the virtuous Pandavas are going.

sn: सानुक्रोशा महात्मानो विजितेन्द्रियशत्रवः। श्रीमन्तः कीर्तिमन्तश्चधर्माचारपरायणाः॥
en: They are self-controlled, high-souled, victorious over foes, endued with modesty and renown and devoted to virtue.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्त्वानुजग्मुस्ते पाण्डवांस्तान् समेत्य च। ऊचुः प्राञ्जलयः सर्वे कौन्तेयान् माद्रिनन्दनान्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having said this, they all went together after the Pandavas. With joined hands, they thus spoke to the sons of Kunti and Madri.

sn: क्व गमिष्यथ भद्रं वस्त्यक्तवास्मान् दुःखभागिनः। वयमप्यनुयास्यामो यत्र यूयं गमिष्यथ॥
en: The citizens said : Be blessed. Where will you go leaving us (behind) who are in great grief? We shall go where you will go.

sn: अधर्मेण जिताञ्छूवा युष्मांस्त्यक्तघृणैः परैः। उद्विग्नाः स्मो भृशं सर्वे नास्मान् हातुमिहार्हथ॥ भक्तानुरक्तान् सुहृदः सदा प्रियहिते रतान्। कुराजाधिष्ठिते राज्ये न विनश्येम सर्वशः॥
en: We have been greatly distressed in learning that you have been defeated with sinful means by the cruel enemies. You should not forsake us. Who are your devoted and loving friends and who are ever engaged in doing your good and seeking your welfare. We all do not desire to meet destruction by living in the kingdom of a bad king.

sn: श्रूयतां चाभिधास्यामो गुणदोषान् नरर्षभाः। शुभाशुभाधिवासेन संसर्गः कुरुते यथा॥
en: O foremost of men, listen to the merits and demerits, as we indicate, that respectively arise from associating with what is good and what is bad.

sn: वस्त्रमापस्तिलान् भूमिं गन्धो वासयते यथा। पुष्पाणामधिवासेन तथा संसर्गजा गुणाः॥
en: As cloth, water, sesame-seeds and ground are perfumed by their association with flowers, so qualities are derived from association.

sn: मोहजालस्य योनिर्हि मूढेरेव समागमः। अहन्यहनिधर्मस्य योनिः साधुसमागमः॥
en: Association with the fools produces delusion, as daily association with the honest and good produces virtue.

sn: तस्मात् प्राज्ञैश्च वृद्धैश्च सुस्वभावैस्तपस्विभिः। सद्भिश्च सह संसर्गः कार्यः शमपरायणैः॥
en: Therefore those who are virtuously inclined should associate with men who are wise, old, honest and pure in conduct and who are ascetics.

sn: येषां त्रीण्यवदातानि विद्या योनिश्च कर्म च। ते सेव्यास्तैः समास्या हि शास्त्रेभ्योऽपि गरीयसी। निरारम्भा ह्यपि वयं पुण्यशीलेषु साधुषु। पुण्यमेवाप्नुयामेह पापं पापोपसेवनात्॥
en: Those whose triple possessions, namely knowledge, birth and acts, are pure, should be waited upon. To associate with them is superior to the study of the Shastras. Without performing any special virtuous act, we shall be able to reap religious merits by associating with the righteous. We shall (assuredly) get sin by serving the sinful (Duryodhana and others).

sn: असतां दर्शनात् स्पर्शात् संजल्पाच्च सहासनात् धर्माचाराः प्रहीयन्ते सिद्ध्यन्ति च न मानवाः॥
en: The very sight and the touch of the sinful and conversation and association with them, cause diminution of virtue. Men (who act thus) never attain purity of soul.

sn: बुद्धिश्च हीयते पुंसां नीचैः सह समागमात्। मध्यमैर्मध्यतां याति श्रेष्ठतां याति चोत्तमैः॥
en: Association with the mean and the low inakes one's understanding mean and low; association with the indifferent makes it indifferent and association with the good makes it good.

sn: अनीचैर्नाप्यविषयैर्नाधर्मिष्ठैर्विशेषतः। ये गुणाः कीर्तिता लोकेधर्मकामार्थसम्भवाः। लोकाचारेषु सम्भूता वेदोक्ताः शिष्टसम्मताः॥ ते युष्मासु समस्ताश्च व्यस्ताश्चैवेह सद्गुणाः। इच्छामो गुणवन्मध्ये वस्तुं श्रेयोऽभिकाक्षिणः।।
en: All those attributes, which are spoken of in the world as the source of religious merit, worldly prosperity and sensual pleasure, which are highly regarded by men, extolled in the Vedas and approved by the good, exist in you separately and jointly. Desiring our own welfare, we wish to live among men who possess such attributes.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच धन्या वयं यदस्माकं स्नेहकारुण्ययन्त्रिताः। असतोऽपि गुणानाहुर्ब्राह्मणप्रमुखाः प्रजाः॥
en: Yudhishthira said: Blessed are we, since moved by affection and compassion, our subjects, headed by the Brahmanas, credit us with merits we do not possess.

sn: तदहं भ्रातृसहितः सर्वान् विज्ञापयामि वः। नान्यथा तद्धि कर्तव्यमस्मत्स्नेहानुकम्पया॥
en: I with my brothers, would ask all of you to do one thing. For the sake of the love you bear for us; you should not act otherwise.

sn: भीष्म पितामहो राजा विदुरो जननी च में। सुहृज्जनश्च प्रायो मे नगरे नागसाह्वये॥
en: Our grandfather Bhishma, the king (Dhritarashtra), Vidura, our mother (Kunti) and our other friends are all in Hastinapur.

sn: ते त्वस्मद्धितकामार्थं पालनीयाः प्रयत्नतः। युष्माभिः सहिताः सर्वे शोकसंतापविह्वलाः॥
en: They are overwhelmed with sorrow and afflictions; if you want to please me, uniting all together, (go and) cherish them with care.

sn: निवर्ततागता दूरं समागमनशापिताः। स्वजने न्यासभूते मे कार्या स्नेहान्विता मतिः॥
en: Grieved at my departure, you have come far away. Go back. heart be affectionately directed towards the relatives whom we leave behind as our pledges to you.

sn: एतद्धि मम कार्याणां परमं हृदि संस्थितम्। कृता तेन तु तुष्टिर्मे सत्कारच भविष्यति॥
en: This is the one act on which my heart is set. If you do it, you will give me the greatest satisfaction and pay your best regards.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तथानुमन्त्रितास्तेनधर्मराजेन ताः प्रजाः। चक्रुरार्तस्वरं घोरं हा राजनिति संहताः॥
en: Vaishampayana said: Let your Having been thus exhorted by Dharmaraja (Yudhishthira), the subjects raised up all together a fearful wail, exclaiming “Alas, O king!”

sn: गुणान् पार्थस्य संस्मृत्य दुःखार्ताः परमातुराः। अकामाः संन्यवर्तन्त समागम्याथ पाण्डवान्।॥
en: Afflicted and overwhelmed with grief, they unwillingly retraced their steps after asking leave of the Pandavas and remembering the virtues of Pritha's sons.

sn: निवृत्तेषु तु पौरेषु स्थानास्थाय पाण्डवाः। आजग्मुर्जाह्नवीतीरे प्रमाणाख्यं महावटम्॥
en: At the departure of the citizens, the Pandavas ascended their cars and came to a great banian tree, named Prirnana, on the banks of the Ganges.

sn: ते तं दिवसशेषेण वटं गत्वा तु पाण्डवाः। ऊषुस्तां रजनीं वीराः संस्पृश्य सलिलं शुचि॥
en: Coming to the banian tree at the close of the day, the heroic Pandavas became purified by touching the water. They then passed the night there.

sn: उदकेनैव तां रात्रिमूषुस्ते दुःखकर्षिताः। अनुजग्मुश्च तत्रैतान् स्नेहात् केचिद् द्विजातयः॥ साग्नयोऽनग्नयश्चैव सशिष्यगणबान्धवाः। स तैः परिवृतो राजा शुशुभे ब्रह्मवादिभिः॥
en: Afflicted with grief, they passed that night, living on water only. Some Brahmanas, both those that maintained fire and those that did not, followed the Pandavas there for the love they bore for them. Surrounded by those Brahma-knowing men, the king (Yudhishthira) shone resplendent.

sn: तेषां प्रादुष्कृताग्नीनां मुहूर्ते रम्यदारुणे। ब्रह्मघोषपुरस्कारः संजल्प: समजायत॥
en: That terrible evening hours became in a moinent delightful on account of those Brahmana's lighting their fire, chanting the Vedas and holding mutual conversations.

sn: राजानं तु कुरुश्रेष्ठं ते हंसमधुरस्वराः। आश्वासयन्तो विप्राण्याः क्षपां सर्वां व्यनोदयन्॥
en: Those foremost of Brahmanas with their swan-like sweet voices spent the night in comforting that best of Kurus, the king (Yudhishthira). son

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच प्रभातायां तु शर्वर्यां तेषामक्लिष्टकर्मणाम्। वनं यियासतां विप्रास्तस्थुर्भिक्षाभुजोऽचतः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : When that night passed away and morning appeared, those Brahmanas, who supported themselves by alms, stood before those doers of exalted deeds (the Pandavas) who were on the point of entering the forest.

sn: तानुवाच ततो राजा कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठरः। वयं हि हृतसर्वस्वा हृतराज्या हृतश्रियः॥ फलमूलाशनाहारा वनं गच्छाम दुःखिताः। वनं च दोषबहुलं बहुव्यालसरीसृपम्॥
en: Thereupon the of Kunti, king Yudhishthira, thus spoke to them, “We are robbed to our kingdom, prosperity and everything. Living on fruits, roots and meat we go to the forest in sorrow. The forest is full of dangers and it abounds in reptiles and beasts of prey.

sn: परिक्लेशश्च वो मन्येध्रुवं तत्र भविष्यति। ब्राह्मणानां परिक्लेशो दैवतान्यपि सादयेत्। किं पुनर्मामितो विप्रा निवर्तध्वं यथेष्टतः॥
en: It appears to me that you will have to suffer much privations and misery there. The sufferings of the Brahmanas may overwhelm even the celestials, what to speak of me! O Brahmanas, go back wherever you like.

sn: ब्राह्मणा ऊचु: गतिर्या भवतां राजस्तां वयं गन्तुमुद्यताः। नार्हस्यस्मान् परित्यक्तुं भक्तान् सद्धर्मदर्शिनः॥
en: The Brahmanas said: O king, we are ready to go where you are going. You should not abandon us who are devoted to you and who follow the path of the true religion.

sn: अनुकम्पां हि भक्तेषु देवता ह्यपि कुर्वते। विशेषतो ब्राह्मणेषु सदाचारावलम्बिषु॥
en: The celestials have compassion on their devotees, specially on the Brahmanas whose conduct is pure.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच ममापि परमा भक्तिर्ब्राह्मणेषु सदा द्विजाः। सहायविपरिभ्रंशस्त्वयं सादयतीव माम्॥ आहरेयुरिमे येऽपि फलमूलमधूनि च। त इमे शोकजैर्दुःखैर्धातरो मे विमोहिताः॥ द्रौपद्या विप्रकर्षण राज्यापहरणेन च। दुःखार्दितानिमान् क्लेशैर्नाहं योक्तुमिहोत्सहे॥
en: Yudhishthira said : O Brahmanas, I have always great devotion towards the Brahmanas. But this destitution has overwhelmed me. My these brothers who are to procure fruits and roots and the deer are stupified with grief for the afflictions that have overtaken them and for the distress of Draupadi and for the loss of our kingdom. Alas, as they are distressed, I cannot employ them in painful tasks!

sn: ब्राह्मणा ऊचुः अस्मत्पोषणजा चिन्ता मा भूत् ते हृदि पार्थिव। स्वयमाहत्य चान्नानि त्वानुयास्यामहे वयम्॥
en: The Brahmanas said : O king, do not allow any anxiety for our maintenance to find a place in your heart. Procuring our food ourselves, we shall follow you.

sn: अनुध्यानेन जप्येन विधास्यामः शिवं तव। कथाभिश्चाभिरम्याभिः सह रंस्यामहे वयम्॥
en: And we shall do you good by meditation and prayers and we shall entertain you with pleasant conversation and we shall ourselves be cheered in return.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच एवमेतत्र संदेहो रमेऽहं सततं द्विजैः। न्यूनभावात् तु पश्यामि प्रत्यादेशमिवात्मनः॥
en: Yudhishthira said: There is no doubt that it must be as you say. I am ever pleased with the company of Brahmanas. But my fallen condition makes me regard myself as an object of reproach.

sn: कथं द्रक्ष्यामि वः सर्वान् स्वयमाहृतभोजनान्। मद्भक्त्या क्लिश्यतोऽनर्हान् धिक् पापान्धृतराष्ट्रजान्।
en: How shall I see you all, my well-wishers, who do not deserve to suffer any trouble, subsist on food procured by yourselves? O fie on the sons of Dhritarashtra!

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच इत्युक्त्वा स नृपः शोचन निषसाद महीतले। यात्मरतो विद्वाञ्छौनको नाम वै द्विजः॥ योगे सांख्ये च कुशलो राजानमिदमब्रवीत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having said this, that king (Yudhishthira) sat down weeping on the ground. Then a learned Brahmana, named Shaunaka, who was learned in the philosophy of the soul and in the Sankhya and Yoga, thus spoke to the king.

sn: शोकस्थानसहस्राणि भयस्थानशतानि च। दिवसे दिवसे मूढमाविशन्ति न पण्डितम्॥
en: Shaunaka said : Thousand causes of grief and hundred causes of fear overwhelm the ignorant day after day, but not the learned.

sn: न हि ज्ञानविरुद्धेषु बहुदोषेषु कर्मसु। श्रेयोघातिषु सज्जन्ते बुद्धिमन्तो भवद्विधाः॥
en: Intelligent men like you never allow themselves to be deluded by acts which are opposed to true knowledge, which is fought with every kind of evil and which is destructive of salvation.

sn: अष्टाङ्गां बुद्धिमाहुर्यां सर्वाश्रेयोऽभिघातिनीम्। श्रुतिस्मृतिसमायुक्तां राजन् सा त्वय्यवस्थिता॥
en: O king, the understanding with the eight attributes, which is said to be capable of providing against all evils which results from the study of the Shrutis, is in you.

sn: अर्थकृच्छ्रेषु दुर्गेषु व्यापत्सु स्वजनस्य च। शारीरमानसैर्दुःखैन सीदन्ति भवद्विधाः॥
en: Men like you are never stupified by poverty or by meeting with difficult ways or by afflictions that overtake his friends or by bodily or mental miseries.

sn: श्रूयतां चाभिधास्यामि जनकेन यथा पुरा। आत्मव्यवस्थानकरा गीताः श्लोका महात्मना॥
en: Hear, I shall recite to you the slokas which were chanted by the high-souled Janaka of old on the subject of controlling the soul.

sn: मनोदेहसमुत्थाभ्यां दुःखाभ्यमर्दितं जगत्। त्योर्व्याससमासाभ्यां शमोपायमिमं शृणु॥
en: This world is afflicted with both bodily and mental sufferings. Listen to the means of allaying them as I indicate them both briefly and in detail.

sn: व्याधेरनिष्टसंस्पर्शाच्छ्रमादिष्टविर्वजनात्। दुःखं चतुर्भिः शारीरं कारणैः सम्प्रवर्तते॥
en: Disease, contact with painful things, toil and want of objects desired, these are the four causes of the sufferings of the body.

sn: तदा तत्प्रतिकाराच्च सततं चाविचिन्तनात्। आधिव्याधिप्रशमनं क्रियायोगद्वयेन तु॥
en: Disease may be allayed by the application of medicine, but mental ailments, are cured by Yoga meditation.

sn: मतिमन्तो ह्यतो वैद्याः शमं प्रागेव कुर्वते। मानसस्य प्रियाख्यानैः सम्भोगोपनयैर्नृणाम्॥
en: Therefore, intelligent physicians first seek to allay the mental sufferings of their patients by agreeable conversations and by the offer of desirable objects.

sn: मानसेन हि दुःखेन शरीरमुपतप्यते। अय:पिण्डेन तप्तेन कुम्भसंस्थमिवोदकम्॥
en: As a hot iron ball makes the water of a jar hot, so mental grief brings in bodily pains.

sn: मानसं शमयेत् तस्माज्ज्ञानेनाग्निमिवाम्बुना। प्रशान्ते मानसे ह्यस्य शारीरमुपशाम्यति॥
en: As water quenches fire, so knowledge allays mental ailments. When mind enjoys' peace, body also enjoys peace.

sn: मनसो दुःखमूलं तु स्नेह इत्युपलभ्यते। स्नेहात् तु सज्जते जन्तुर्दुःखयोगमुपैति च॥
en: It appears attachment is the root of all mental agonies; it is attachment that makes every creature miserable and brings on every kind of woe.

sn: स्नेहमूलानि दुःखानि स्नेहजानि भयानि च। शोकहर्षों तथाऽऽयासः सर्वं स्नेहात् प्रवर्तते॥ स्नेहाद् भावोऽनुरागश्च प्रजज्ञे विषये तथा। अश्रेयस्कावुभावेतौ पूर्वस्तत्र गुरुः स्मृतः॥
en: Attachment is the root of all misery and of all fear. Attachment produces joy and grief of every kind. From attachment spring all worldly desires and it is from attachment that springs the love of worldly goods. Both of these are evils, but the first is worse than the second.

sn: कोटराग्निर्यथाशेषं समूलं पादपं दहेत्। धर्मार्थो तु तथाल्पोऽपि रागदोषो विनाशयेत्॥
en: As fire in the hollow of a tree consumes the tree itself to its roots, so attachment, however little it may be, destroys both Dharma and Artha,

sn: विप्रयोगे न तु त्यागी दोषदर्शी समागमे। विरागं भजते जन्तुर्निवैरो निरवग्रहः॥
en: He, who has merely withdrawn from possessions, cannot be regarded as to have renounced the world. He, however, who remains in contact with the world, but sees its faults, may be said to have truly renounced the world. Such a man becomes freed from all evil passions and his soul is dependent on nothing.

sn: तस्मात् स्नेहं न लिप्सेत मित्रेभ्योधनसंचयात्। स्वशरीरसमुत्थं च ज्ञानेन विनिवर्तयेत्॥
en: Therefore none should place his attachment on either friends or on wealth which he has carned. The attachment towards one's own body is destroyed by knowledge.

sn: ज्ञानान्वितेषु युक्तेषु शास्त्रज्ञेषु कृतात्मसु। न तेषु सज्जते स्नेहः पद्मपत्रेष्विवोदकम्॥
en: Like the lotus leaf which is never drenched by water, souls of those men who are capable of knowing the everlasting and of men who are devoted to the pursuit of the eternal, learned in the Shastras and purified by knowledge, can never be touched by attachment.

sn: रागाभिभूतः पुरुषः कामेन परिकृष्यते। इच्छा संजायते तस्य ततस्तृष्णा विवर्धते॥ तृष्णा हि सर्वपापिष्ठा नित्योद्वेगकरी स्मृता। अधर्मबहुला चैव घोरा पापानुबन्धिनी॥
en: The man that is influenced by itachment is tortured by desire and from the desire that springs up in his heart, his thirst for worldly possessions increases. This thirst is sinful and is regarded as the source of all anxieties. It is this terrible thirst, fraught with sin, that leads to unrighteous acts.

sn: या दुस्त्यजा दुर्मतिभिर्या न जीर्यति जीर्यतः। योऽसौ प्राणान्तिको रोगस्तां तृष्णां त्यजतः सुखम्॥३६
en: Those men, who can renounce this thirst, which can never be renounced by the wicked, which decays not with the decay of the body and which is a fatal disease, can be freed from misery.

sn: अनाद्यन्ता तु सा तृष्णा अन्तर्देहगता नृणाम्। विनाशयति भूतानि अयोनिज इवानलः॥
en: This thirst has neither beginning nor end. Like the fire of incorporeal origin, it destroys creatures by living within their hearts.

sn: यथैधः स्वसमुत्थेन वह्निना नाशमृच्छति। तथाकृतात्मा लोभेन सहजेन विनश्यति॥
en: As a faggot of wood is consumed by the fire that is fed by that faggot, so a person of impure soul meets with destruction from the covetousness born in his own heart.

sn: राजतः सलिलादग्नेश्चोरतः स्वजनादपि। भयमर्थवतां नित्यं मृत्योः प्राणभृतामिव॥
en: Creatures endued with life have always a dread of death; so men having wealth are in constant dread of the king, the water, the fire, the thief and his relatives.

sn: यथा ह्यामिषमाकाशे पक्षिभिः श्वापदैर्भुवि। भक्ष्यते सलिले मत्स्यैस्तथा सर्वत्र वित्तवान्॥
en: If a piece of meat be in the air, it may be devoured by the birds, if it is on the grounds, it may be devoured by beasts of prey and if in the water, by the fishes, so a man having wealth is exposed to dangers wherever he might be.

sn: अर्थ एव हि केषांचिदनर्थं भजते नृणाम्। अर्थश्रेयसि चासक्तो न श्रेयो विन्दते नरः॥
en: To many men, the wealth they possess is their bane. The man, who sees happiness in wealth and becomes attached to it, knows not what true happiness is.

sn: तस्मादर्थागमाः सर्वे मनोमोहविवर्धनाः। कार्पण्यं दर्पमानौ च भयमुद्वेग एव च॥ अर्थजानि विदुः प्राज्ञा दुःखान्येतानि देहिनाम्। अर्थस्योत्पादने चैव पालने च तथा क्षये।॥ सहन्ति च महद् दुःखं प्रन्ति चैवार्थकारणात्। अर्था दुःखं परित्यक्तुं पालिताश्चैव शत्रवः॥
en: Therefore, the accession of wealth is what increases covetousness and folly. It is the root of niggardliness, boastfulness, pride, fear and anxiety. These are the miseries that wise men see in wealth. Men have to suffer infinite miseries in the acquisition and retention of wealth. Its expenditure also is painful. Sometimes men are even killed for the sake of wealth. To abandon wealth is painful; even those men who are cherished become enemies for the sake of wealth.

sn: दुःखेन चाधिगम्यन्ते तस्मान्नाशं न चिन्तयेत्। असंतोषपरा मूढाः संतोषं यान्ति पण्डिताः॥
en: As the possession of wealth is fraught with such misery, one should not (at all) mind its loss. Ignorant men alone are discontented, but the wise men are always contented.

sn: अन्तो नास्ति पिपासायाः संतोषः परमं सुखम्। तस्मात् संतोषमेवेह परं पश्यन्ति पण्डिताः॥
en: The thirst for wealth can never be assuaged. Contentment is the highest happiness, therefore the wise men consider contentment to be the highest object to attain.

sn: अनित्यं यौवनं रूपं जीवितं रत्नसंचयः। ऐश्पर्य प्रियसंवासो गृध्येत् तत्र न पण्डितः॥
en: The learned men, knowing youth, beauty, life, treasure, prosperity and association with beloved ones to be (all) unstable, never covet them.

sn: त्यजेत संचयांस्तस्मात्तज्जान् क्लेशान् सहेत च। न हि संचयवान् कश्चिद् दृश्यते निरुपद्रवः। अतश्चधार्मिकैः पुंभिरनीहार्थः प्रशस्यते॥
en: Therefore one should refrain from the acquisition of wealth and thus avoid the sufferings of misery. The man of wealth can never be without dangers. For this reason virtuous men praise those who have no desire for wealth.

sn: धर्मार्थं यस्य वित्तेहा वरं तस्य निरीहता। प्रक्षालनाद्धि पंकस्य श्रेयो न स्पर्शनं नृणाम्॥
en: As regards those that acquire wealth for the virtuous purposes, it is better for them not to do it at all. It is better not to touch mud than to wash it off after being besmeared with it.

sn: युधिष्ठिरैवं सर्वेषु न स्पृहां कर्तुमर्हसि। धर्मेण यदि ते कार्यं विमुक्तेच्छो भवार्थतः॥
en: O Yudhishthira, you should not covet anything. It you want to acquire virtue, free yourself from all desires for the possession of wealth.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच नार्थोपभोगलिप्सार्थमियमर्थेप्सुता मम। भरणार्थं तु विप्राणां ब्रह्मन् काझे न लोभतः॥
en: Yudhishthira said: O Brahmana, this my desire for wealth is not for the purpose of enjoying it when obtained. I do not desire it through avarice. I desire it only for the support of the Brahmanas.

sn: कथं ह्यस्मद्विधो ब्रह्मन् वर्तमानो गृहाश्रमे। भरणं पालनं चापि न कुर्यादनुयायिनाम्॥
en: O Brahmana, for what purpose would one like to lead a domestic life, if he cannot cherish and support those that follow him?

sn: संविभागो हि भूतानां सर्वेषामेव दृश्यते। तथैवापचमानेभ्यः प्रदेयं गृहमेधिना॥
en: All creatures are seen to divide their food among those that depend on them. So should person leading a domestic life give a share of his food to Brahmacharis who have given up cooking.

sn: तृणानि भूमिरुदकं वाक् चतुर्थी च सूनृता। सतामेतानि गेहेषु नोच्छिद्यन्ते कदाचन॥ देयमार्तस्य शयनं स्थितश्रान्तस्य चासनम्। तृषितस्य च पानीयं क्षुधितस्य च भोजनम्॥
en: "The houses of good men can never be in want of grass, space, water and sweet words, the fourth. Bed to the tired, seat to one who is fatigued by standing, water to on who is thirsty and food to one who is hungry should be always given.

sn: चक्षुर्दद्यान्मनो दद्याद् वाचं दद्यात् सुभाषिताम्। उत्थाय चासनं दद्यादेषधर्मः सनातनः। प्रत्युत्थायाभिगमनं कुर्यात्र्यायेन चार्चनम्॥ अग्निहोत्रमनड्वांश्च ज्ञातयोऽतिथिबान्धवाः। पुत्रा दाराश्च भृत्याश्च निर्दहेयुरपूजिताः॥ आत्मार्थं पाचयेन्नान्नं न वृथा घातयेत् पशून्। न च तत् स्वयमश्नीयाद् विधिवद् यन्न निर्वपेत्॥
en: Pleasant looks, cheerful heart and sweet words are due to a guest. Rising up, the host should advance towards the guest; he should offer him a seat and duly worship him. This is the eternal Dharma. They who do not perform Agnihotra, they who do not wait upon bulls and cherish their kinsmen, guest, friends, sons, wives and servants, for such negligence are consumed with sin. None should cook his food for himself, none should kill any animal for nothing. Non should eat that food which is not duly dedicated.

sn: श्वभ्यश्च श्वपचेभ्यश्च वयोभ्यश्चावपेद् भुवि। वैश्वदेवं हि नामैतत् सायं प्रातश्च दीयते॥
en: By scattering morning and evening food on the earth for dogs, Chandalas and birds, a person should perform the Vishvadeva (sacrifice).

sn: विघसाशी भवेत् तस्मान्नित्यं चामृतभोजनः। विघसो भुक्तशेषं तु यज्ञशेषं तथामृतम्॥
en: He who eats Vighasa eats ambrosia. That, which remains after dedication in a sacrifice, is (also) regarded as ambrosia.

sn: चक्षुर्दघान्मनो दद्याद् वाचं दद्याच्च सूनृताम्। अनुव्रजेदुपासीत स यज्ञः पञ्चदक्षिणः॥
en: The pleasant looks (one casts on his guests), the attention he devotes to him, the sweet words with which he addresses him, the respect with which he follows him and the food and drink with which he treats him, are the five Dakshinas in that sacrifice.

sn: यो दद्यादपरिक्लिष्टमध्वनि वर्तते। श्रान्तायदृष्टपूर्वाय तस्य पुण्यफलं महत्॥
en: He, who gives food freely to a fatigued way. farer, whom he has never seen before, obtains grcat virtuous merit.

sn: एवं यो वर्तते वृत्तिं वर्तमानो गृहाश्रमे। तस्यधर्म परं प्राहुः कथं वा विप्र मन्यसे॥
en: He, who leading domestic life, follows such practices, obtains, it is said, great religious merit. O Brahmana, what is your opinion?

sn: शौनक उवाच अहो वत महत् कष्टं विपरीतमिदं जगत्। येनापत्रपते साधुरसाधुस्तेन तुष्यति॥
en: Shaunaka said: Alas, alas this worlds is full of contradictions! That which makes the good and the honest ashamed gratifies the wicked.

sn: शिश्नोदरकृतेऽप्राज्ञः करोति विघसं बहु। मोहरागवशाक्रान्त इन्द्रियार्थवशानुगः॥
en: Move by ignorance and passions and becoming slaves to their senses, ignorant men perform many acts to gratify their stomachs an sexual organs.

sn: ह्रियते बुध्यमानोऽपि नरो हारिभिरिन्द्रियैः। विमूढसंज्ञो दुष्टाश्वैरुद्धान्तैरिव सारथिः॥
en: Men are lcd astray by their seducing senses, as a charioteer who has lost his senses (is led। astray) by wicked horses.

sn: षडिन्द्रियाणि विषयं समागच्छन्ति वै यदा। तदा प्रादुर्भवत्येषां पूर्वसंकल्पजं मनः॥
en: When any of the six senses finds its ! particular object, the desire springs up in the heart to enjoy that particular object.

sn: मनो यस्येन्द्रियस्येह विषयान् याति सेवितुम्। तस्यौत्सुक्यं सम्भवति प्रवृत्तिश्चोपजायते॥
en: Thus when one's mind proceeds to enjoy the objects of any particular sense, a wish is entertained; that wish in its turn gives birth to a resolve.

sn: ततः संकल्पबीजेन कामेन विषयेषुभिः। विद्धः पतति लोभाग्नौ ज्योतिर्लोभात् पतङ्गवत्॥
en: As an insect falls into a flame from love of light, man falls into the fire of temptation, as it were pierced by the arrows of the objects of enjoyments) which are discharged by the desire which is the seed of resolve.

sn: ततो विहारैराहारैर्मोहितश्च यथेप्सया। महामोहे सुखे मग्नो नात्मानमवबुध्यते॥ एवं पतति संसारे तासु तास्विह योनिषु। अविद्याकर्मतृष्णाभिर्धाम्यमाणोऽथ चक्रवत्॥ ब्रह्मादिषु तृणान्तेषु भूतेषु परिवर्तते। जले भुवि तथाऽऽकाशे जायमानः पुनः पुनः॥
en: Blinded by sensual pleasure which he freely seeks and steeped in dark ignorance and folly which he mistakes for happiness, he thenceforth knows not himself. Like a wheel that is incessantly whirling, every creature, from ignorance, acts and desire, roves in various states in the world, wandering from one birth to another, ranging from Brahma to a blade of grass, an taking birth again and again now in water, now in earth and now in the sky.

sn: अबुधानां गतिस्त्वेषा बुधानामपि मे शृणु। येधर्मे श्रेयसि रता विमोक्षरतयो जनाः॥
en: This is the career of those that are without knowledge. Listen to that of the wise, the men who are intent on virtue and who are desirous of Moksha (emancipation).

sn: तदिदं वेदवचनं कुरु कर्म त्यजेति च। तस्माद्धर्मानिमान् सर्वान् नाभिमानात् समाचरेत्।७४॥
en: This is the word of the Vedas, act, but act with renunciation. Therefore you should act renouncing Abhimana.

sn: इज्याध्ययनदानानि तपः सत्यं क्षमा दमः। अलोभ इति मार्गोऽयंधर्मस्याष्टविधः स्मृतः॥
en: Performances of sacrifices, study, gifts, penance, truth, forgiveness, subduing the senses and renunciation of desire, these are the eight Dharmas declared by the Smriti.

sn: अब पूर्वश्चतुर्वर्गः पितृयाणपथे स्थितः। कर्तव्यमिति यत् कार्यं नाभिमानात् समाचरेत्॥
en: Of these the first four pave the way to the regions of Pitris. Therefore it is the duty of all to act by renouncing Abhimana.

sn: उत्तरो देवयानस्तु सद्भिराचरितः सदा। अष्टाङ्गेनैव मार्गेण विशुद्धात्मा समाचरेत्॥
en: The last four are always observed by the pious who aspire to attain to the region of the celestials. The men of pure soul should observe these eight (paths).

sn: सम्यक्संकल्पसंबन्धात् सम्यक् चेन्द्रियनिग्रहात् सम्यग्व्रतविशेषाच्च सम्यक च गुरुसेवनात्॥ सम्यगाहारयोगाच्च सम्यक् चाध्ययनागमात्। सम्यक्कर्मोपसंन्यासात् सम्यक्चित्तनिरोधनात्॥ एवं कर्माणि कुर्वन्ति संसारविजिगीषवः। रागद्वेषविनिर्मुक्ता ऐश्वर्यं देवता गताः॥
en: Those, who wish to subdue the world for the purposes of salvation, should always act by fully renouncing all motives and by subduing their senses, rigidly observing vows, devotedly serving their preceptors, austerely regulating their food, diligently studying the Vedas, renouncing action as mean and restraining their heart. By renouncing desire and aversions, the celestials have obtained prosperity.

sn: रुद्राः साध्यास्तथाऽऽदित्या वसवोऽथ तथाश्विनौ। योगैश्वर्येण संयुक्ताधारयन्ति प्रजा इमाः॥
en: It is for the virtue of their wealth of Yoga, that the Rudras, the Sadhyas, the Adityas, the Vasus and the Ashvins support all these creatures (of the world).

sn: तथा त्वमपि कौन्तेय शममास्थाय पुष्कलम्। तपसा सिद्धिमन्विच्छ योगसिद्धिं च भारत॥
en: O son of Kunti, O descendant of Bharata, therefore you too like them, entirely renouncing actions with motive, try to obtain success in Yoga and austerities.

sn: पितृमातृमयी सिद्धिः प्राप्ता कर्ममयी च ते। तपसा सिद्धिमन्विच्छ द्विजानां भरणाय वै॥
en: You have already obtained success as far as your debts to the Pitris, both male and female are concerned and you have obtained that success also which is derived from action. Try now to obtain success in from action. Try now to obtain success in penances in order to support the Brahmanas.

sn: सिद्धा हि यद् यदिच्छन्ति कुर्वते तदनुग्रहात्। तस्मात्तपः समास्थाय कुरुष्वात्ममनोरथम्॥
en: Those that are crowned with ascetic success can by virtue of that success do whatever they like. Therefore practising asceticism, realise all your wishes.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच शौनकेनैवमुक्तस्तु कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः। पुरोहितमुपागम्य भ्रातृमध्येऽब्रवीदिदम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having been thus addressed by Shaunaka, the son of Kunti, Yudhishthira, conting to his priest, thus spoke to him in the midst of his brothers.

sn: प्रस्थितं मानुयान्तीमे ब्राह्मणा वेदपारगाः। न चास्मि पोषणे शक्तो बहुदुःखसमन्वितः॥
en: Yudhishthira said: The Brahmanas, learned in the Vedas, are following me who am departing. Afflicted with many calamities, I am unable to support them.

sn: परित्यक्तुं न शक्तोऽस्मि दानशक्तिश्च नास्ति मे। कथमत्र मया कार्यं तद् ब्रूहि भगवन् मम॥
en: I cannot forsake them, but I have no power to provide them with their sustenance. O exalted one, tell me what should be now done by me.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच मुहूर्तमिव सध्यात्वाधर्मेणान्विष्य तां गतिम्। युधिष्ठिरमुवाचेदंधौम्योधर्मभृतां वरः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : After reflecting for a moment to seek out the (proper) course by the help of his Yoga prowess, that foremost of all virtuous men, Dhaumya, thus spoke to Yudhishthira.

sn: धौम्य उवाच ततोऽनुकम्पया पुरा सृष्टानि भूतानि पीड्यन्ते क्षुधया भृशम्। तेषां सविता स्वपिता यथा॥ गत्वोत्तरायणं तेजो रसानुद्धृत्य रश्मिभिः। दक्षिणायनमावृत्तो महीं निविशते रविः॥
en: Dhaumya said : In the days of yore, all living beings that had been created were greatly afflicted with hunger. Thereupon Savita (sun) took compassion on them, as a father (does to his children). Going to the Northern declension, the sun drew up water by his rays and then coming back to the Southern declension and having centered his heat in himself, he stayed over the earth.

sn: क्षेत्रभूते ततस्तस्मिन्नोषधीरोषधीपतिः। दिवस्तेजः समुद्धृत्य जनयामास वारिणा॥
en: While the sun so stayed, the lord of the vegetable world (moon), converting the effects of the sun's heat (vapours) created the clouds.

sn: निषिक्तश्चन्द्रतेजोभिः स्वयोनौ निर्गते रविः। ओषध्यः षड्रसा मेध्यास्तदन्नं प्राणिनां भुवि॥
en: Thus it is the sun himself who, being drenched by the lunar influence, is transformed from the sprouting of seeds into holy vegetables furnished with the six tastes. It is this which constitutes the food of all creatures on carth.

sn: एवं भानुमयं ह्यन्नं भूतानां प्राणधारणम्। पितैष सर्वभूतानां तस्मात् तं शरणं व्रज॥
en: Thus the food which supports the lives of creatures is the sun and therefore he is the father of all creatures. Therefore take shelter in him.

sn: राजानो हि महात्मानो योनिकर्मविशोधिताः। उद्धरन्ति प्रजाः सर्वास्तप आस्थाय पुष्कलम्॥
en: All illustrious kings of noble birth and great deeds are known to have delivered their people by practising high asceticism.

sn: भीमेन कार्तवीर्येण वैन्येन नहुषेण च। तपोयोगसमाधिस्थैरुद्धता ह्यापदः प्रजाः॥
en: Dhaumya, Kartavirya, Vainya and Nahusha all protected their subjects from dangers by virtue.of ascetic meditation and vows.

sn: तथा त्वमपिधर्मात्मन् कर्मणा च विशोधितः। तप आस्थायधर्मेण द्विजातीन् भर भारत॥
en: Therefore, O descendant of Bharata, O virtuous one, as you are purified by acts, you too, like like them, support virtuously the Brahmanas by entering upon a life of austerities.

sn: जनमेजय उवाच कथं कुरूणामृषभः स तु राजा युधिष्ठिरः। विप्रार्थमाराधितवान् सूर्यमद्भुतदर्शनम्॥
en: Janamejaya said : How does, for the sake of the Brahmanas, that foremost of the Kurus, king Yudhishthira, worshipped the sun of wonderful appearance?

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच शृणुष्वावहितो राजशुचिर्भूत्वा समाहितः! क्षणं च कुरु राजेन्द्र सम्प्रवक्ष्याम्यशेषतः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : O king, (first) purify yourself and (then) withdrawing your mind from all (the worldly) objects, (at that appointed hour) hear it with all attention. O king of kings, appoint a time. I shall (then) tell you everything in detail.

sn: धौम्येन तु यथा पूर्वं पार्थाय सुमहात्मने। नामाष्टशतमाख्यातं तच्छृणुष्व महामते॥
en: O high souled one, listen to the one hundred and eight names (of the sun), as they were told by Dhaumya to the greatly illustrious son of Pritha (Yudhishthira).

sn: धौम्य उवाच सूर्योऽर्यमा भगस्त्वष्टा पूषार्कः सविता रविः। गभस्तिमानजः कालो मृत्युर्धाता प्रभाकरः॥ पृथिव्यापश्च तेजश्च खं वायुश्च परायणम्। सोमो बृहस्पतिः शुक्रो बुधोऽङ्गारक एव च॥ इन्द्रो विवस्वान् दीप्तांशुः शुचिः शौरिः शनैश्चरः ब्रह्मा विष्णुश्च रुद्रश्च स्कन्दो वै वरुणो यमः॥ वैद्युतो जाठरश्चाग्निरैन्धनस्तेजसां पतिः। धर्मध्वजो वेदकर्ता वेदाङ्गो वेदवाहनः॥ कृतं त्रेता द्वापरश्च कलिः सर्तमलाश्रयः। कला काष्ठा मुहूर्ताश्च क्षपा यामस्तथा क्षणः॥ संवत्सरकरोऽश्वत्थः कालचक्रो विभावसुः। पुरुषः शाश्वतो योगी व्यक्ताव्यक्तः सनातनः॥ कालाध्यक्षः प्रजाध्यक्षो विश्वकर्मा तमोनुदः। वरुणः सागरोंऽशुश्च जीमूतो जीवनोऽरिहा॥ भूताश्रयो भूतपतिः सर्वलोकनमस्कृतः। स्रष्टा संवर्तको वह्निः सर्वस्यादिरलोलुपः। :॥ अनन्तः कपिलो भानुः कामदः सर्वतोमुखः। जयो विशालो वरदः सर्वधातुनिषेचिता॥ मन:सुपर्णो भूतादिः शीघ्रगः प्राणधारकः। धन्वन्तरिधूमकेतुरादिदेवोऽदितेः सुतः॥ द्वादशात्मारविन्दाक्षः पिता माता पितामहः। स्वर्गद्वारं प्रजाद्वारं मोक्षद्वारं त्रिविष्टपम्॥ देहकर्ता प्रशान्तात्मा विश्वात्मा विश्वतोमुखः। चराचरात्मा सूक्ष्मात्मा मैत्रेयः करुणान्वितः॥
en: Dhaumya said : Surya, Aryama, Bhaga, Tvashta, Pusha, Arka, Savita, Ravi, Gabhastiman, Aja, Kala, Mrityu, Dhata, Prabhakara, Prithivi, Apa, Teja, Kha, Vayu, Parayana, Soma, Brihaspati, Shukra, Budha, Angaraka, Indra, Vivashvana, Dirtangshu, Suchi, Souri, Sanaichara, Brahma, Vishnu, Rudra, Skanda, Vaishravana, Yama, Vaidyutagni, Jatharagni, Aindhana, Tejaspati, Dharmadhvaja, Vedakarta, Vedanga, Vedavahana, Krita, Treta, Dvapara, Kali, Kala, Kastha, Muhurta, Kashyapa, Yama, Kshana, Samvatsarakara, Ashvatha, Kalachakra, Vibhavasu, Purusha, Sashvata, Yogin, Vyakta, Avyakta, Sanatana, Kaladhyaksha, Prajadhakshya, VishBakarman, Tamanooda, Varuna, Sagara, Ansa, Jimuta, Jivana, Ariha, Bhutashraya, Bhutapati, Srashta, Samvartaka, Vanhi, Sarvadi, Alolupa, Ananta, Kapila, Bhanu, Karmaprada, Sarvatamukha, Jaya, Vishala, Varada, Manas, Suparna, Bhutadi, Sighraga, Pranadharna, Dhanvantari, Dhumaketu, Adideva, Aditisuta, Dvadasatma, Aravindaksha, Pitri, Matri, Pitamaha, Svargadara, Prajadvara, Mokshadara, Prasanatma, Vishvatima, Vishvatamukha, Characharatman, Sukshatma and the merciful Maitra.

sn: एतद् वै कीर्तनीयस्य सूर्यस्यामिततेजसः। नामाष्टशतकं चेदं प्रोक्तमेतत् स्वयंभुवा॥
en: These are the one hundred and eight names of immeasurably effulgent Surya as told by the self-created (Brahma).

sn: सुरगणपितृयक्षसेवितं ह्यसुरनिशाचरसिद्धवन्दितम्। वरकनकहुताशनप्रभं प्रणिपतितोऽस्मि हिताय भास्करम्॥
en: O Bhaskara (sun), who blazes like gold or fire, who is worshipped by the celestials, the Pitris, the Yakshas and who is adored by Asuras, Nishacharas and Siddhas, I bow you for the acquisition of prosperity.

sn: सूर्योदये यः सुसमाहितः पठेत् स पुत्रदारान्धनरत्नसंचयान्। लभेत जातिस्मरतां नरः सदा धृतिं च मेधां च स विन्दते पुमान्॥
en: He who recites with fixed attention this hymn at sunrise, obtains wife, offspring, riches and the memory of his former existence. Men always get patience and memory (by reciting it).

sn: इमं स्तवं देववरस्य यो नरः प्रकीर्तयेच्छुचिसुमना: समाहितः ल्लभेत कामान् मनसा यथेप्सितान्॥
en: Let a man, concentrating his mind, recite this hymn of the foremost of gods (the sun). He will be proof against grief, forest-fire and ocean; and he will obtain every object of desire as he will wish for.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्तस्तुधौम्येन तत्कालसदृशं वचः। विप्रत्यागसमाधिस्थः संयतात्मा दृढव्रतः॥ धर्मराजो विशुद्धात्मा तप आतिष्ठदुत्तमम्। पुष्पोपहारैलिभिरर्चयित्वा दिवाकरम्॥ सोऽवगाह जलं राजा देवस्याभिमुखोऽभवत्। योगमास्थायधर्मात्मा वायुभक्षो जितेन्द्रियः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having, heard these words uttered by Dhaumya suitable to the occasion, Dharmaraja (Yudhishthira), moved by the desire of supporting the Brahmanas of controlled and pure souls and of austere vows, began to observe excellent asceticism. Worshipping the sun with flowers and other articles and turning his face towards the lord of day (the sun), he bathed in the water. That virtuous minded man became rapt in Yoga, living on air ard becoming a victor over his passions.

sn: गाङ्गेयं वार्युपस्पृश्य प्राणायामेन तस्थिवान्। शुचिः प्रयतवाग् भूत्वा स्तोत्रमारब्धवांस्ततः॥
en: Purifying himself with the touch of the Ganges water and restraining his speech, he practised Pranayama (one of the processes of Yoga) for some time and he then recite this hymn of praise.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच त्वं भानो जगतश्चक्षुस्त्वमात्मा सर्वदेहिनाम्। त्वं योनिः सर्वभूतानां त्वमाचारः क्रियावताम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said: O sun, you are the eye of the universe. You are the soul of all corporeal existence. You are the creative organ of all things. You are the acts of all religious men.

sn: त्वं गतिः सर्वसांख्यानां योगिनां त्वं परायणम्। अनावृतार्गलद्वारं त्वं गतिस्त्वं मुमुक्षुताम्॥
en: You are the refuge of all Sankhyas (the followers of Sankhya philosophy) and you are the support of all Yogins (the followers of Yoga philosophy). You are the door with bolts : unfastened, you are the refuge of men aspiring to salvation.

sn: त्वया संधार्यते लोकस्त्वया लोकः प्रकाश्यते। त्वया पवित्रीक्रियते निर्व्याजं पाल्यते त्वया॥
en: You support the world, you make it manifest; you purify it and support it from compassion.

sn: त्वामुपस्थाय काले तु ब्राह्मणा वेदपारगाः। स्वशाखाविहितैर्मन्त्रैरर्चन्त्यषिगणार्चितम्॥
en: The Brahmanas, learned in the Vedas, adore you by coming to you in proper time and by reciting the hymns from the respective branches (of the Vedas what each of them follows). You are the adored of the Rishis.

sn: तव दिव्यं रथं यान्तमनुयान्ति वरार्थिनः। सिद्धचारणगन्धर्वा यक्षगुह्यकपन्नगाः॥
en: The Siddhas, the Charanas, the Gandharvas, the Yakshas, the Guhyakas and the Nagas, being desirous of obtaining boons, follow your moving celestials car.

sn: त्रयस्त्रिंशच्च वै देवास्तथा वैमानिका गणाः। सोपेन्द्राः समहेन्द्राश्च त्वामिष्ट्वा सिद्धिमागताः॥
en: Thirty three gods, with Upendra (Vishnu) and Mahendra (Indra) and the Vaimanikas (an order of celestials) have all attained success by worshipping you.

sn: उपयान्त्यर्चयित्वा तु त्वां वै प्राप्तमनोरथाः। दिव्यमन्दारमालाभिस्तूर्णं विद्याधरोत्तमाः॥ गुह्याः पितृगणाः सप्त ये दिव्या ये च मानुषाः। ते पूजयित्वा त्वामेव गच्छन्त्याशु प्रधानताम्॥ वसवो मरुतो रुद्रा ये च साध्या मरीचिपाः। वालखिल्यादयः सिद्धाः श्रेष्ठत्वं प्राणिनां गताः॥
en: By offering you garlands of the celestials Mandaras (celestials flowers), the best of the Vidyadharas have obtained all their desires. The Guhyakas and the seven orders of the Pitris, both divine and human, have attained superiority by adoring you. The Vasus, the Marutas, the Rudras the Saddhyas, the Marichipas, the Valkhilyas and the Siddhas have (all) attained prominence by bowing to you.

sn: सब्रह्मकेषु लोकेषु सप्तस्वष्यखिलेषु च। न तद्भूतमहं मन्ये यदर्कादतिरिच्यते॥ सन्ति चान्यानि सत्त्वानि वीर्यवन्ति महान्ति च। न त तेषां तथा दीप्तिः प्रभावो वा यथा तव॥ ज्योतीषिं त्वयि सर्वाणि त्वं सर्वज्योतिषां पतिः। त्वयि सत्यं च सत्त्वं च सर्वे भावाश्च सात्त्विका:।४७॥ त्वत्तेजसा कृतं चक्रं सुनाभं विश्वकर्मणा। देवारीणां मदो येन नाशितः शार्ङ्गधन्वना॥
en: There is nothing that I know in the whole of the seven worlds including that of Brahma which is beyond you. There are other beings both powerful and great, but none of them possesses lustre and prowess as you do. All light is in you. You are the lord of all light. In you are the elements, you are knowledge and you are all the ascetic properties. The discuss, by which the wielder of the Saranga (the bow of Vishnu) humble the pride of the Asuras and which is furnished with a beautiful have, was made by Vishvakarma with your effulgence.

sn: त्वमादायांशुभिस्तेजो निदाघे सर्वदेहिनाम्। सौषधिरसानां च पुनर्वर्षासु मुञ्चसि॥
en: You draw by your rays moisture from all corporeal existence and from plants and liquid substances in summer. You pour it down (on the earth as rain) in the rainy season.

sn: तपन्त्यन्ये दहन्त्यन्ये गर्जन्त्यन्ये तथा घनाः। विद्योतन्ते प्रवर्षन्ति तव प्रावृषिः रश्मयः॥
en: Your rays are warm and they scorch (things). Becoming clouds they roar and flash lightning; they pour down showers when the scason comes.

sn: न तथा सुखयत्यग्निर्न प्रावारा न कम्बलाः। शीतवातार्दितं लोकं यथा तव मरीचयः॥
en: Neither fire, nor shelter, nor woolen blankets give greater comfort to one in cold than what is got from your rays.

sn: त्रयोदशद्वीपवतीं गोभिर्भासयसे महीम्। त्रयाणामपि लोकानां हितायैकः प्रवर्तसे॥
en: You illuminate by your rays the whole earth with her thirteen islands. You alone are (ever) engaged in doing good to the three worlds.

sn: तव यादयो न स्यादन्धं जगदिदं भवेत्। न चधर्मार्थकामेषु प्रवर्तेरन् मनीषिणः॥
en: If you do not rise, the universe becomes blind. The learned men cannot employ themselves in the attainment of Dharma, Artha and Kama.

sn: आधानपशुबन्धेष्टिमन्त्रयज्ञतपःक्रियाः। त्वत्प्रसादादवाप्यन्ते ब्रह्मक्षत्रविशां गणैः॥
en: It is through your grace that the Brahmanas, Kshatriyas and Vaisyas are able to perform Adhana, Pashabandha, Ishti, Mantra, Yajona and Tapakrya (names of various duties, sacrifices and vows.)

sn: यदहर्ब्रह्मणः प्रोक्तं सहस्रयुगसम्मितम्। तस्य त्वमादिरन्तश्च कालज्ञैः परिकीर्तितः॥
en: Those that know all about the Time say that you are the beginning and the end of the Brahma day which consists of full one thousand Yugas.

sn: मनूनां मनुपुत्राणां जगतोऽमानवस्य च। मन्वन्तराणां सर्वेषामीश्वराणां त्वमीश्वरः॥
en: You are the lord of the Manus, of the sons of Manus, of the universe, of mankind, of the Manvantaras and of all lords.

sn: संहारकाले सम्प्राप्ते तव क्रोधविनिःसृतः। संवर्तकाग्निस्त्रैलोक्यं भस्मीकृत्यावतिष्ठते॥
en: When the time for final dissolution comes, the Samvartaka fire, born of your anger, only exists and reduces the three worlds to ashes.

sn: त्वद्दीधितिसमुत्पन्न नानावर्णा महाघनाः। सैरावता: साशनयः कुर्वन्त्याभूतसम्लवम्॥
en: Clouds of various colors, born of your rays, accompanied by Airavata (Indra's elephant) and the thunder, produce the appointed deluges.

sn: कृत्वा द्वादशधाऽऽत्मानं द्वादशादित्यतां गतः। संहृत्यैकार्णवं सर्वं त्वं शोषयसि रश्मिभिः॥
en: Dividing yourself into twelve parts and becoming as many suns, you then drink up the ocean with your rays.

sn: त्वामिन्द्रमाहुस्त्वं रुद्रस्त्वं विष्णुस्त्वं प्रजापतिः। त्वमग्निस्त्वं मनः सूक्ष्म प्रभुस्त्वं ब्रह्म शाश्वतम्॥
en: You are called Indra, you are Vishnu, you are Rudra, (you are) Prajapati, you are fire, you are the subtle mind, you are the lord and the eternal Brahma.

sn: त्वं हंसः सविता भानुरंशुमाली वृषाकपिः। विवस्वान् मिहिरः पूषा मित्रोधर्मस्तथैव च॥ सहस्ररश्मिरादित्यस्तपनस्त्वं गवाम्पतिः। मार्तण्डोऽर्को रविः सूर्यः शरण्यो दिनकृत् तथा॥ दिवाकरः सप्तसप्तिर्धामकेशी विरोचनः। आशुगामी तमोघ्नश्च हरिताश्वश्च कीर्त्यसे॥
en: You are Hansa, you are Savitri, you are Bhanu, Anshumali, Vrishakapi, Vivasvana, Mihira, Pusha, Mitra and Dharma. You are thousand-rayed sun, you are Tapana, the lord of rays. You are Martanda, Arka, Ravi, Surya, Sharanga, the maker of the day. Dibakara, Saptasapti, Dhamakeshin, Virochana, Ashugami, Tamoghna and Haritashva.

sn: सप्तम्यामथवा षष्ठ्यां भक्त्या पूजां करोति यः। अनिविण्णोऽनहंकारी तं लक्ष्मीर्भजते नरम्॥
en: He who reverentially worships you on the sixth or the seventh lunar day with humility of mind obtains the grace of Lakshmi (goddess of wealth.)

sn: न तेषामापदः सन्ति नाधयो व्याधयस्तथा। ये तवानन्यमनसः कुर्वन्त्यर्चनवन्दनम्॥
en: Those that adore and worship you with undivided attention are delivered from all dangers, agonies and afflictions.

sn: सर्वरोगविरहिताः सर्वपापविवर्जिताः। तवद्भावभक्ताः सुखिनो भवन्ति चिरजीविनः॥
en: Those that believe you in everything becoming freed from all disease and all sins, grow happy in all their life.

sn: त्वं ममापनकामस्य सर्वातिथ्यं चिकीर्षतः। अन्नमन्नपते दातुमभितः श्रद्धयाहसि॥
en: O lord of all food, you should grant me abundance of food to entertain all my guests with reverence.

sn: ये च तेऽनुचराः सर्वे पादोपान्तं समाश्रिताः। माठरारुणदण्डाद्यास्तांस्तान् वन्देऽशनिक्षुभान्॥ क्षुभया सहिता मैत्री याश्चान्या भूतमातरः। ताश्च सर्वा नमस्यामि पान्तु मां शरणागतम्॥
en: I bow to all your followers that have taken your feet, (namely) Mathara, Aruna, Danda and others including Asani, Kshubha and others. I also bow to the celestials mothers of all creatures, namely Kshubha and Maitri and to the others of the class. Let them deliver me who am suppliant (at their feet).

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवं स्तुतो महराजा भास्करो लोकभावनः। ततो दिवाकरः प्रीतो दर्शयामास पाण्डवम्। दीप्यमानः स्ववपुषा ज्वलनिव हुताशनः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Thereupon the sun became gratified and that maker of day, self-luminous and blazing like fire, appeared before the Pandava (Yudhishthira).

sn: विवस्वानुवाच यत् तेऽभिलषितं किंचित् तत् त्वं सर्वमवाप्स्यसि। अहमन्नं प्रदास्यामि सप्त पञ्च च ते समाः॥
en: The Sun said: You shall get all that you desire to have. I shall provide you with food for all the twelve years (of your exile).

sn: गृहणीष्व पिठरं तानं मया दत्त नराधिप। यावद् वय॑ति पाञ्चाली पात्रेणानेन सुव्रत॥ फलमूलामिषं शाकं संस्कृतं यन्महानसे। चतुर्विधं तदन्नाद्यमक्षय्यं ते भविष्यति॥ इतश्चतुर्दशे वर्षे भूयो राज्यमवाप्स्यसि।
en: O king, accept this copper vessel that I present you. O man of excellent vows, so long the Panchala excellent vows, so long the Panchala Princess (Draupadi) will hold this vessel without partaking of it contents-fruits, roots, meat and vegetables, cooked in your kitchen-the four kinds of food, shall from this day be (there) inexhaustible. You shall regain your kingdom on the fourteenth year from this.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्त्वा तु भगवांस्तत्रैवान्तरधीयत॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having said this, the deity (Sun) then and there vanished away.

sn: इमं स्तवं प्रयतमनाः समाधिना पठेदिहान्योऽपि वरं समर्थयन्। तत् तस्य दद्याच्च रविर्मनीषितं तदाप्नुयाद् यद्यपि तत् सुदुर्लभम्॥
en: He, who with the desire of obtaining a boon, recites this hymn concentrating his mind with ascetic abstraction, obtains it from the sun, however difficult of acquisition it may be.

sn: यश्चेदंधारयेन्नित्यं शृणुयाद् वाप्यभीक्ष्णशः। पुत्रार्थी लभते पुत्रंधनार्थी लभतेधनम्। विद्यार्थी लभते विद्यां पुरुषोऽप्यथवा स्त्रियः॥
en: A man or a woman that recites or hears this hymn day after day, if he or she is desirous of a son, obtains one; if desirous of wealth, cbtains it; and if desirous of learning, obtains it. The man or woman who always reads it in the two twlights (early morning and evening).

sn: उभे संध्ये पठेन्नित्यं नारी वा पुरुषो यदि। आपदं प्राप्य मुच्यते बद्धो मुच्येत बन्धनात्॥
en: Is delivered from danger and is freed from the bonds. This hymn was given of old to the high-souled Shakra.

sn: एतद् ब्रह्मा ददौ पूर्वं शक्राय सुमहात्मने। शक्राच्च नारदः प्राप्तोधौम्यस्तु तदनन्तरम्। धौम्याद् युधिष्ठिरः प्राप्य सर्वान् कामानवाप्तवान्।७८।।
en: From Shakra it was obtained by Narada and from Narada by Dhaumya. Receiving it from Dhaumya, Yudhishthira obtained all that he desired.

sn: संग्रामे च जयेन्नित्यं विपुलं चाप्नुयाद् वसु। मुच्यते सर्वपापेभ्यः सूर्यलोकं स गच्छति॥
en: It is by the virtue of the hymn one may win victory in a war and acquire immense wealth. Making one freed from all sins, it leads a man to the region of the sun.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच लब्ध्वा वरं तु कौन्तेयो जलादुत्तीर्यधर्मवित्। जचाद पादौधौम्यस्य भ्रातुंश्च परिषस्वजे॥
en: The virtuous son of Kunti (Yudhishthira), having obtained the boon, rose from the water. He then took hold of Dhaúmya's feet and then embraced his brothers.

sn: द्रौपद्या सह संगम्य वन्द्यमानस्तया प्रभुः। महानसे तदानीं तु साधयामास पाण्डवः॥
en: O lord, the Pandava (Yudhishthira), going to the kitchen with Draupadi and being duly worshipped by her, began to cook food.

sn: संस्कृतं प्रसवं याति स्वल्पमन्नं चतुर्विधम्। अक्षय्यं वर्धते चान्नं तेन भोजयते द्विजान्॥
en: The food, however little that was cooked, becoming four kinds increased and become inexhaustible. Who them he (Yudhishthira) fed the Brahman.

sn: भुक्तवत्सु च विप्रेषु भोजयित्वानुजानपि। शेषं विघससंज्ञं तु पश्चाद् भुङ्क्ते युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: After the Brahmanas had been fed and his younger brothers also, Yudhishthira himself ate the food that remained and which was called Vighasa.

sn: युधिष्ठिरं भोजयित्वा शेषमश्नाति पार्षती। द्रौपद्यां भुज्यमानायां तदन्नं क्षयमेति च। एवं दिवाकरात् प्राप्य दिवाकरसमप्रभः॥ कामान् मनोऽभिलषितान् ब्राह्मणेभ्योऽददात् प्रभुः। पुरोहितपुरोगाश्च तिथिनक्षत्रपर्वसु। यज्ञियार्थाः प्रवर्तन्ते विधिमन्त्रप्रमाणतः॥
en: After Yudhishthira had partaken his food, the daughter of Prishata (Draupadi) took what remained. After Draupadi had taken her meal, the food became exhausted. The lord (Yudhishthira) as resplendent as the sun thus obtaining the boon from the sun, entertained the Brahmanas agrecable to their wishes. Obedient to his priest, he performed sacrifices with due Mantras and according to the ordinances and Shastras on auspicious lunar days, constellations and conjunctions.

sn: ततः कृतस्वस्त्ययनाधौम्येन सह पाण्डवाः। द्विजसबै परिवृताः प्रययुः काम्यकं वनम्॥
en: Thereupon the Pandavas, blessed by the auspicious rites and, accompained by Dhaumya and surrounded by the Brahmanas, set out for the forest of Kamyaka.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच वनं प्रविष्टष्वथ पाण्डवेषु प्रज्ञाचक्षुस्तप्यमानोऽम्बिकेयः। धर्मात्मानं विदुरमगाधबुद्धिं सुखासीनो वाक्यमुवाच राजा॥
en: Vaishampayana said: After the departure of the Pandavas to the forest, the son of Ambika (Dhritarashtra) whose knowledge was his eye, became exceedingly sorrowful. The King, seated at his case, thus spoke to the virtuous minded and highly intelligent Vidura.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच प्रज्ञा च ते भार्गवस्येव शुद्धा धर्म च त्वं परमं वेत्थ सूक्ष्मम्। समश्च त्वं सम्मतः कौरवाणां पथ्यं चैषां मम चैव ब्रवीहि॥
en: Dhritarashtra said: Your intelligence is as great as that of Bhargava (Shukra), you know all the subtleties of holy Dharma. You look on all the Kurus with and equal eye. Tell me what is good for me and for them (the Kurus).

sn: एवंगते विदुर यदद्य कार्य पौराश्च मे कथमस्मान् भजेरन्। स्तत्त्वं ब्रूयाः साधु कार्याणि वेत्सि॥
en: O Vidura, things having taken this course, what should be done by us? I low can we secure the adoration of the citizens? How can we avoid the danger of total annihilation? Tell us what we should do); for you are conversant with all excellent expedients.

sn: विदुर उवाच त्रिवर्गोऽयंधर्ममूलो नरेन्द्र राज्यं चेदंधर्ममूलं वदन्ति। धर्मे राजन् वर्तमानः स्वशक्त्या पुत्रान सर्वान् पाहि पाण्डोः सुतांश्च॥
en: Vidura said: O king, Trivarga (Dharma, Artha and Kama) has its foundation on virtue and the sages says that a kingdom also stands on virtue as its basis. O king, therefore cherish with virtue and to your best power on your own sons and those of Pandu.

sn: स वैधर्मो विप्रलब्धः सभायां पापात्मभिः सौबलेयप्रधानैः। आहूय कुन्तीसुतमक्षवत्यां पराजैषीत् सत्यसंधं सुतस्ते॥
en: Virtue was destroyed by the wicked souls (the Kuru princes) with Subala's son (Shakuni) at their head when your sons invited the virtuous Yudhishthira to play and defeated him at dice.

sn: छेषस्याहं परिपश्याम्युपायम्। मुक्तो लोके प्रतितिष्ठेत साधु॥
en: I see this expiation of this dead of utter iniquity. O chief of the Kurus, your son (Duryodhana) may win by it a praise among good men.

sn: तद् वै सर्वं पाण्डुपुत्रा लभन्तां यत् तद् राजन्नभिसृष्टं त्वयाऽऽसीत्। एषधर्मः परमो यत् स्वकेन राजा तुष्येन्न परस्वेषु गृध्येत्॥
en: Let the Pandavas have what is to may given to them by you. The king's morality is that a king should remain content with his own and never covet the possessions of others.

sn: यशो न नश्येज्ज्ञातिभेदश्च न स्याद् धर्मो न स्यानैव चैवं कृते त्वाम्। एतत् कार्यं तव सर्वप्रधान तेषां तुष्टिः शकुनेश्चावमानः॥
en: Your good name would not thus suffer; family dissension's would not thus ensue; you will have then no unrighteous act. This is your first duty, (namely) to grace the Pandavas and to disgrace Shakuni.

sn: देतद् राजंस्त्वरमाणः कुरुष्व। तथैतदेवं न करोषि राजन् ध्रुवं कुरूणां भविता विनाशः॥
en: O king, if you wish to restore to you sons the good fortune they have lost this speedily act as I say, O king, if you do not act thus, the Kurus will be soon destroyed.

sn: न हि क्रुद्धो भीमसेनोऽर्जुनो वा शेषं कुर्याच्छात्रवाणामनीके। येषां योद्धा सव्यसाची कृतास्त्रो धनुर्येषां गाण्डिवं लोकसारम्॥ येषां भीमो बाहुशाली च योद्धा तेषां लोके किं नु न प्राप्यमस्ति। उक्तं पूर्वं जातमात्रे सुते ते मया यत् ते हितमासीत् तदानीम्॥
en: For neither Bhimasena nor Arjuna, if angry, will leave any of the enemies unslain. What is there in the world which is unattainable to those who have amongst their warriors Savyasachi Arjuna well-skilled in war, who possesses the Gandiva, the most powerful of all weapons in the world and who have the mighty Bhimasena warrior.

sn: पुत्रं त्यजेममहितं कुलस्य हितं परं न च तत् त्वं चकर्थ। मेवं कर्ता परितप्तासि पश्चात्॥
en: I told you formerly as soon as the son was born, “Abandon this inauspicious child of yours. The good of your race is in it (abandoning).” But you did not accept my advice, if you did as I advised to do, you would not have repented.

sn: यद्येतदेवमनुमन्ता सुतस्ते सम्प्रीयमाणः पाण्डवैरेकराज्यम्। न चेन्निगृहणीष्व सुतं सुखाय॥
en: If your son consent to reign just and in peace with the sons of Pandu, you will thus pass your days in happiness and you will not have to repent.

sn: दुर्योधनं त्वहितं वै निगृह्य पाण्डोः पुत्रं कुरुष्वाधिपत्ये। अजातशत्रुर्हि विमुक्तरागो धर्मेणेमां पृथिवीं शास्तु राजन्॥ दुःशासनो
en: Putting aside Duryodhana invite the son of Pandu (Yudhishthira) in the sovereignty. Let Ajatashatru (Yudhishthira) who is free from passion, rule the earth virtuously.

sn: ततो राजन् पार्थिवाः सर्व एव वैश्या इवास्मानुपतिष्ठन्तु सद्यः। दुर्योधनः शकुनिः सूतपुत्रः प्रीत्या राजन् पाण्डुपुत्रान् भजन्तु॥
en: O king, all the monarchs of the world then like Vaisyas will pay homage to us. O king, let Duryodhana, Shakuni and Suta's son (Karna) gladly wait upon the sons of Pandu.

sn: याचतु भीमसेनं सभामध्ये दुपदस्यात्मजां च। युधिष्ठिरं त्वं परिसान्त्वयस्व राज्ये चैनं स्थापयस्वाभिपूज्य॥
en: Let Dushasana ask pardon of Bhimasena and of the daughter of Draupada (Draupadi) in open court. After pacifying Yudhishthira, place him on the throne with all respects.

sn: मेतत् कृत्वा कृतकृत्योऽसि राजन्॥
en: O king, asked by you, who else can I advise? If you do this, you will do what is proper.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच मिह प्रोक्तं पाण्डवान् प्राप्य मां च। मेतत् सर्वं मम नावैति चेतः॥
en: Dhritarashtra said: O Vidura, the worlds you have spoken in this assembly with reference to the Pandavas and myself are for their and not my good. My mind does not approve this.

sn: इदं त्विदानी गत एव निश्चितं तेषामर्थे पाण्डवानां यदास्थ! तेनाद्य मन्ये नासि हितो ममेति कथं हि पुत्रं पाण्डवार्थे त्यजेयम्॥
en: How have you settled all this in your mind. When you have spoken all this on behalf of the Pandavas. I perceive you are not at all friendly to me. How can I leave my son for the sake of sons of Pandu?

sn: असंशयं तेऽपि ममैव पुत्रा दुर्योधनस्तु मम देहात् प्रसूतः। स्वं वै देहं परहेतोस्त्यजोत को नु ब्रूयात् समतामन्ववेक्ष्य॥
en: There is no doubt they (the Pandavas) too are my sons, but Duryodhana has spring from my (own) body. Speaking partially how will you advise me to replace my own body for the sake of others?

sn: स मां जिह्यं विदुर सर्वं ब्रवीषि मानं च तेऽहमधिकंधारयामि। यथेच्छकं गच्छ वा तिष्ठ वा त्वं सुसान्त्व्यमानाप्यसती स्त्री जहाति॥
en: Vidura, though I hold you in great esteem, (yet I must say) all that you have said is crooked. Stay (here) or go (away) as you please. However an unchaste wife is assured, she forsakes her husband.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच दन्तर्वेश्म सहसोत्थाय राजन्। नेदमस्तीत्यथ विदुरो भाषमाणः सम्प्राद्रवद् यत्र पार्था बभूवुः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : O king, having said this, Dhritarashtra suddenly rose and went into the inner apartments. Saying "this race is doomed", Vidura (also) went away where the sons of Fandu were.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच पाण्डवास्तु वने वासमुद्दिश्य भरतर्षभाः। प्रययुर्जाह्नवीकूलात् कुरुक्षेत्रं सहानुगाः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Being desirous of living in the forest, the foremost men of the Bharata race, the sons of Pandu with their followers to the banks of the Ganges to the Kurukshetra.

sn: सरस्वतीदृषद्वत्यौ यमुनां च निषेव्य ते। ययुर्वनेनैव वनं सततं पश्चिमां दिशम्॥
en: Performing their ablutions in the Sarasvati, the Drisadvati and the Yamuna and went from one forest to another travelling in the westerly direction.

sn: ततः सरस्वतीकूले समेषु मरुधन्वसु। काम्यकं नाम ददृशुर्वनं मुनिजनप्रियम्॥
en: Then (at last) they saw before them the forest of Kamyaka on the banks of Sarasvati and on a level and wild plain which was ever charming to the ascetics.

sn: तत्र ते न्यवसन् वीरा वने बहुमृगद्विजे। अन्वास्यमाना मुनिभिः सान्त्व्यमानाश्च भारत॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, entertained and comforted by the Munis, there did they live in that forest abounding in birds and animals.

sn: विदुरस्त्वथ पाण्डूनां सदा दर्शनलालसः। जगामैकरथेनैव काम्यकं वनमृद्धिमत्॥
en: Vidura, ever longing to see the Pandavas went (alone) in a single car to the forest of Kamyaka abounding in every good thing.

sn: च्छीढरश्चैर्वाहिना स्यन्दनेन। ददर्शासीनंधर्मात्मानं विविक्ते सार्धं द्रौपद्या भातृभिर्ब्राह्मणैश्च॥
en: Thereupon going to the Kamyaka forest on a car drawn by swift horses, he saw Dharmaraja (Yudhishthira) at a retired part (of the forest) sitting with Draupadi and surrounded by his brothers and the Brahmanas.

sn: दभ्यायान्तं सत्यसंधः स राजा। अथाब्रवीद् भ्रातरं भीमसेनं किं नु क्षत्ता वक्ष्यति नः समेत्य॥
en: Thereupon seeing Vidura coming in speed, the virtuous king spoke thus to his brother Bhimsena. “With what message Khattva (Vidura) comes to us?”

sn: कच्चिन्नायं वचनात् सौबलस्य समाह्वाता देवनायोपयातः। कच्चित् क्षुद्रः शकुनि युधानि जेष्यत्यस्मान् पुनरेवाक्षवत्याम्॥
en: Does he come here, having been despatched by the son of Subala (Shakuni) to invite us again to a game at dice? Does the meanminded Shakuni desire to win our weapons by playing again at dice?

sn: समाहूतः केनचिदाद्रवेति नाहं शक्तो भीमसेनापयातुम्। गाण्डीवे च संशयिते कथं नु राज्यप्राप्तिः संशयिता भवेन्नः॥
en: O Bhimasena, if challenged by one who says “Come," I am unable to stay, if our possessions of the Gandiva (bow) be doubtful, then the acquisition of our kingdom again will be (equally) doubtful.”

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तत उत्थाय विदुरं पाण्डवेयाः प्रत्यगृहणन् नृपते सर्व एव। तैः सत्कृतः स च तानाजमीढो यथोचितं पाण्डुपुत्रान् समेयात्॥
en: Then the Pandavas all rose up and welcomed Vidura with all respects. Received by them, that descendant of Ajamira (Vidura) sat in their midst and made to the sons of Pandu the usual enquiries.

sn: स्ततोऽपृच्छन्नागमनाय हेतुम्। स चापि तेभ्यो विस्तरतः शशंस यथावृत्तोधृतराष्ट्रोऽम्बिकेयः॥
en: After Vidura had taken some rest, those foremost of men (the Pandavas) asked him the reason of his coming and he related to them in detail everything with regard to the conduct of the son of Ambika, Dhritarashtra.

sn: विदुर उवाच मजातशत्रो परिगृह्याभिपूज्य। एवं गते समतामभ्युपेत्य पथ्यं तेषां मम चैव ब्रवीहि॥
en: Vidura said: O Ajatashatru, Dhritarashtra summoned me, his dependent and honouring me duly, he said, “Things have thus fared. Tell me what is good for me as well as for them (the Pandavas)."

sn: मयाप्युक्तं यत् क्षेमं कौरवाणां हितं पथ्यंधृतराष्ट्रस्य चैव।। तद् वै तस्मै न रुचामभ्युपैति ततश्चाहं क्षेममन्यन्न मन्ये॥
en: I told him what was good for the Kurus and for Dhritarashtra. But he did not relish what I said. I did not consider any other course to the beneficial.

sn: परं श्रेयः पाण्डवेया मयोक्तं न मे तच्च श्रुतवानाम्बिकेयः। यथाऽऽतुरस्येव हि पथ्यमन्नं न रोचते स्मास्य तदुच्यमानम्॥
en: O Pandavas, what I advised was highly beneficial, but the of Ambika, (Dhritarashtra), did not care to accept it. As medicine is not acceptable to a man who is ill, so my advice failed to please the king.

sn: न श्रेयसे नीयतेऽजातशत्रो स्त्री श्रोत्रियस्येव गृहे प्रदुष्टा। ध्रुवं न रोचेद् भरतर्षभस्य पतिः कुमार्या इव षष्टिवर्षः॥
en: O Ajatashatru, as an unchaste wife of a man of noble birth can never be brought back to the path of virtue, so is the case with Dhritarashtra, As a young damsel does not certainly like a husband of sixty years, so that foremost of Bharata race did not like my words.

sn: ध्रुवं विनाशो नृप कौरवाणां न वै श्रेयोधृतराष्ट्रः परैति। यथाच पणे पुष्करस्यावसिक्तं जलं न तिष्ठेत् पथ्यमुक्तं तथास्मिन्॥
en: O king, the destruction of the Kurus is certain; Dhritarashtra will never meet with good fortune. As water dropped on a lotus leaf son does not remain there, so my counsels failed to have any effect on him.

sn: ततः क्रुद्धोधृतराष्ट्रोऽब्रवीन्मां यस्मिन् श्रद्धा भारत तत्र याहि। नाहं भूयः कामये त्वां सहायं महीमिमां पालयितुं पुरं वा॥
