en: Thereupon angry Dhritarashtra told me saying, “O descendant of Bharata, go away wherever you like. I shall never more seek your aid in ruling the earth or in ruling the city."

sn: सोऽहं त्यक्तोधृतराष्ट्रेण राज्ञा प्रशासितुं त्वामुपयातो नरेन्द्र। तद् वै सर्वं यन्मयोक्तं सभायां तद्धार्यतां यत् प्रवक्ष्यामि भूयः॥
en: O ruler of men, having been (thus) abandoned by the king Dhritarashtra, I have come to you for giving you good counsel. What I said in the Sabha I shall now repeat to you. Hear and bear them in mind.

sn: क्लेशैस्तीत्रैर्युज्यमानः सपत्नैः क्षमां कुर्वन् कालमुपासते यः। संवर्धयन् स्तोकमिवाग्निमात्मवान् स वै भुङ्क्ते पृथिवीमेक एव॥
en: That wise man, who patiently bearing all the wrongs done to him by his enemies, bides his time and multiplies his resources by degrees as a man makes a small fire a large one, rules alone this entire earth.

sn: स्तस्य दुःखेऽप्यंशभाजः सहायाः। सहायानामेष संग्रहणेऽध्युपायः सहायाप्तौ पृथिवीप्राप्तिमाहुः॥
en: O king, he who enjoys his wealth with his adherents finds them sharers of his adversity. This is the best means of securing adherents. It is said he that has adherents wins the sovereignity of the whole world.

sn: सत्यं श्रेष्ठं पाण्डव विप्रलापं तुल्यं चान्नं सह भोज्यं सहायैः। आत्मा चैषामग्रतो न स्म पूज्य एवंवृत्तिवर्धते भूमिपालः॥
en: O son of Pandu, share your wealth with your adherents; behave truthfully towards them and talk with them agreeably. Share also your food with them and never boast in their presence. This conduct increases the prosperity of kings.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच एवं करिष्यामि यथा ब्रवीषि परां बुद्धिमुपगम्याप्रमत्तः। यच्चाप्यन्यद्देशकालोपपन्नं तद् वै वाच्यं तत् करिष्यामि कृत्स्नम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said : Having the aid of such intelligence (as yours), undisturbed by passion as you advise in respect of time and place, I will carefully and entirely follow (your advice).

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच गते तु विदुरे राजन्नाश्रमं पाण्डवान् प्रति! धृतराष्ट्रो महाप्राज्ञः पर्यतप्यत् भारत॥
en: Vaishampayana said: O king, O descendant of Bharata, after Vidura had gone to the hermitage of the Pandavas, the greatly wise Dhritarashtra repented for his actions.

sn: विदुरस्य प्रभावं च संधिविग्रहकारितम्। विवृद्धिं च परां मत्वा पाण्डवानां भविष्यति॥ स सभाद्वारमागम्य विदुरस्मारमोहितः। समक्षं पार्थिवेन्द्राणां पपाताविष्टचेतनः॥
en: Remembering the great intelligence of Vidura in war and in peace and thinking of the future prosperity of the the Pandavas, he (Dhritarashtra), having been pained at the recollection of Vidura and having come to the door of the Assembly-Hall, fell down senseless in the presence of the kings.

sn: स तु लङ्वा पुनः संज्ञां समुत्थाय महीतलात्। समीपोपस्थितं राजा संजयं वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
en: Regaining consciousness, the king rose from the ground and spoke thus to Sanjaya who was standing by.

sn: भ्राता मम सुहृच्चैव साक्षाद्धर्म इवापरः। तस्य स्मृत्याद्य सुभृशं हृदयं दीर्यतीव मे॥
en: Dhritarashtra said : My brother and my friend (Vidura) is like the God of Justice himself. Remembering him, my heart burns in grief.

sn: तमानयस्वधर्मज्ञं मम भ्रातरमाशु वै। इति ब्रुवन् स नृपतिः कृपणं पर्यदेवयत्॥
en: Go bring to me soon my brother, learned in the precepts of morality. Saying this, the king wept bitterly.

sn: पश्चात्तापाभिसंतप्तो विदुरस्मारमोहितः। भ्रातृस्नेहादिदं राजा संजयं वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
en: Burning in repentance and being overwhelmed with sorrow at the recollection of Vidura, the king, from the brotherly love again spoke to Sanjaya thus-

sn: गच्छ संजय जानीहि भ्रातरं विदुरं मम। यदि जीवति रोषेण मया पापेन निथुतः॥
en: Dhritarashtra said : O Sanjaya, go and ascertain whether my brother, Vidura, expelled by my wretched self through anger, still lives or not.

sn: न हि तेन मम भ्रात्रा सुसूक्ष्ममपि किंचन। व्यलीकं कृतपूर्वं वै प्राज्ञेनामितबुद्धिना॥ स व्यलीकं परं प्राप्तो मत्तः परमबुद्धिमान्। त्यक्ष्यामि जीवितं प्राज्ञ तं गच्छानय संजय॥
en: That greatly wise and immeasurably intelligent brother of mine has never done me the slightest wrong. It is that greatly wise man who has suffered wrong at my hands. O Sanjaya, seek him and bring him here or else I shall not live.

sn: तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा राज्ञस्तमनुमान्य च। संजयो बाढमित्युक्त्वा प्राद्रवत् काम्यकं प्रति॥ सोऽचिरेण समासाद्य तद् वनं यत्र पाण्डवाः। रौरवाजिनसंवीतं ददर्शाथ युधिष्ठिरम्॥ विदुरेण सहासीनं ब्राह्मणैश्च सहस्रशः। भ्रातृभिश्चाभिसंगुप्तं देवैरिव पुरंदरम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having heard these words of the king, Sanjaya respectfully approved them and saying “Be it so", he set out for the Kamyaka (forest). He soon arrived at the forest where were the Pandavas, He saw Yudhishthira, clad in deer skin, guarded by his brothers and seated with Vidura and thousands of Brahmanas, like Purandara (Indra) in the midst of the celestials.

sn: युधिष्ठिरमुपागम्य पूजयामास संजयः। भीमार्जुनयमाश्चापि तद्युक्तं प्रतिपेदिरे॥
en: Coming to Yudhishthira, Sanjaya duly worshipped him. He was received with due respect by Bhima, Arjuna and the twins (Nakula and Sahadeva).

sn: राज्ञा पृष्टः स कुशलं सुखासीनश्च संजयः। शशंसागमने हेतुमिदं चैवाब्रवीद् वचः॥
en: He was asked by the king about the welfare of all. When he was comfortably seated, he told the reason of his coming in these words.

sn: संजय उवाच राजा स्मरति ते क्षत्तद्धृतराष्ट्रोऽम्बिकासुतः। तं पश्य गत्वा त्वं क्षिप्रं संजीवय च पार्थिवम्॥
en: Sanjaya said: O Vidura, the son of Ambika, king Dhritarashtra, has remembered you. Returning soon, revive that king.

sn: सोऽनुमान्य नरश्रेष्ठान् पाण्डवान् कुरनन्दनान्। नियोगाद् राजसिंहस्य गन्तुमर्हसि सत्तम॥
en: O descendant of Kuru, O excellent one, with the permission of these best of men, the Pandavas, you should at the command of that lion among kings (Dhritarashtra) return to him.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्तस्तु विदुरोधीमान् स्वजनवल्लभः। युधिष्ठिरस्यानुमते पुनरायाद् गजाह्वयम्॥ तमब्रवीन्महातेजाधृतराष्ट्रोऽम्बिकासुतः। दिष्ट्या प्राप्तोऽसिधर्मज्ञ दिष्ट्या स्मरसि मेऽनघ॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having been thus addressed, the intelligent Vidura, ever attached to his relatives, returned to Hastinapur with the permission of Yudhishthira. The greatly powerful and energetic Dhritarashtra thus spoke to him, “O virtuous man, O sinless one, by good luck alone I have got you. By good luck alone, you have remembered me.

sn: अद्य रात्रौ दिवा चाहं त्वत्कृते भरतर्षभ। प्रजागरे प्रपश्यामि विचित्रं देहमात्मनः॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, I was sleepless through the day and through the night. I was suing myself as one that has been lost on earth.

sn: सोऽङ्कमानीय विदुरं मूर्धन्याघ्राय चैव ह। क्षम्यतामिति चोवाच यदुक्तोऽसि मयानघ॥
en: He then took Vidura on his lap and smelt his head. He said, "O sinless one, forgive me for the words that I spoke to you.

sn: विदुर उवाच क्षान्तमेव मया राजन् गुरुर्मे परमो भवान्। एषोऽहमागतः शीघ्रं त्वदर्शनपरायणः॥ भवन्ति हि नरव्याघ्र पुरुषाधर्मचेतसः। दीनाभिपातिनो राजन् नात्र कार्या विचारणा॥
en: Vidura said: O king, I have forgiven you. You are my Guru (superior), worthy of my highest respect, I have speedily come here, being eagerly desirous of seeing you. O best of men, all virtuous men are partial to those that are distressed. O king, this is scarcely the result of deliberations.

sn: पाण्डोः सुता यादृशा मे तादृशास्तव भारत। दीना इतीव मे बुद्धिरभिपन्नाद्य तान् प्रति॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, your sons are as dear to me as those of Pandu. But as they are now in distress, my mind yarns for them.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच अन्योन्यमनुनीयैवं भ्रातरौ द्वौ महाद्युती। विदुरोधृतराष्ट्रश्च लेभाते परमां मुदम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Addressing each other thus in apologetic words, the two illustrious brothers, Vidura and Dhritarashtra, became greatly happy.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच श्रुत्वा च विदुरं प्राप्तं राज्ञा च परिसान्त्वितम्। धृतराष्ट्रात्मजो राजा पर्यतप्यत दुर्मतिः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having heard that Vidura had returned and minded son of Dhritarashtra (Duryodhana) began to burn in grief.

sn: स सौबलेयमानाय्य कर्णदुःशासनौ तथा। अब्रवीद् वचनं राजा प्रविश्याबुद्धिजं तमः॥
en: His intelligence, (fully) clouded by ignorance, he summoned the son of Subala (Shakuni), Karna and Dushashana and thus spoke to them.

sn: एष प्रत्यागतो मन्त्रोधृतराष्ट्रस्यधीमतः। विदुरः पाण्डुपुत्राणां सुहृद् विद्वान् हिते रतः॥
en: Duryodhana said : The intelligent minister of Dhritarashtra (Vidura) has returned. The learned Vidura is the friend of the sons of Pandu and he is ever engaged in doing good to them.

sn: यावदस्य पुनर्बुद्धिं विदुरो नापकर्षति। पाण्डवानयने तावन्मन्त्रयध्वं हितं मम॥
en: So long Vidura does not succeed to induce him (Dhritarashtra) to bring back the Pandavas, let us think what may benefit us.

sn: अथ पश्याम्यहं पार्थान् प्राप्तानिह कथंचन। पुनः शोषं गमिष्यामि निरम्बुर्निरवग्रहः॥
en: If ever I see the sons of Pritha (the Pandavas) returned to the city, I shall again be emaciated by abandoning food and drink.

sn: विषमुद्बन्धनं चैव शस्त्रमग्निप्रवेशनम्। करिष्ये न हि तानृद्धान् पुनर्द्रष्टुमिहोत्सहे॥
en: I shall either take poison or hang myself; (I shall) either enter a pyre or kill myself with my own weapon. I shall not be able to see (endure) their (the Pandavas') prosperity.

sn: शकुनिरुवाच किं बालिशमतिं राजन्नास्थितोऽसि विशाम्पते। गतास्ते समयं कृत्वा नैतदेवं भविष्यति॥
en: Shakuni said: O king, O ruler of the world, what folly has taken possession of you? They have gone (to the forest) after making a pledge. Therefore what you fear can never take place.

sn: सत्यवाक्यस्थिताः सर्वे पाण्डवा भरतर्षभ। पितुस्ते वचनं तात न ग्रहीष्यन्ति कर्हिचित्॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, all the Pandavas follow the path of truth. They will never accept your father's words.

sn: अथवा ते ग्रहीष्यन्ति पुनरेष्यन्ति वा पुरम्। निरस्य समयं सर्वे पणोऽस्माकं भविष्यति॥
en: If however they accept thein (the words of your father) and again come to the city, violating their vow, this will be our conduct.

sn: सर्वे भवामो मध्यस्था राज्ञश्छन्दानुवर्तिनः। छिद्रं बहु प्रपश्यन्तः पाण्डवानां सुसंवृताः॥
en: Assuming an aspect of neutrality and in apparent obedience to the will of the king (Dhritarashtra), we, keeping our counsels to ourselves, will closely watch the Pandavas.

sn: दुःशासन उवाच एवमेतन्महाप्राज्ञ यथा वदसि मातुल। नित्यं हि मे कथयतस्तव बुद्धिर्विरोचते॥
en: Dushashana said: O greatly intelligent uncle, it is exactly as you say. The words of wisdom you utter always recommend themselves to me.

sn: कर्ण उवाच काममीक्षामहे सर्वे दुर्योधन तवेप्सितम्। ऐकमत्यं हि नो राजन् सर्वेषामेव लक्षये।॥
en: Karna said: O Duryodhana, all of us scek to accomplish your wish. O king, I observe unanimity of opinion amongst us all.

sn: नाममिष्यन्ति तेधीरा अकृत्वा कालसंविदम्। आगमिष्यन्ति चेन्मोहात् पुन तेन ताञ्जय॥
en: These self-controlled men (the Pandavas) will never return without living in the exile) the promised period. If however they come from delusion, defeat them again at dice.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्तस्तु कर्णेन राजा दुर्योधनस्तदा। नातिहृष्टमनाः क्षिप्रेमभवत् स पराङ्मुखः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having been thus addressed by Karna, king Duryodhana with cheerless heart turned his face (from them).

sn: उपलभ्य ततः कर्णो विवृत्य नयने शुभे। रोषाद् दुःशासनं चैव सौबलं च तमेव च॥ उवाच परमक्रुद्ध उद्यम्यात्मानमात्मना। अथो मम मतं यत् तु तन्निबोधत भूमिपाः॥
en: Marking all this, Karna expanding his beautiful eyes and vehemently moving his arms and limbs, spoke, thus in great anger to Dushashana, to the son of Subala (Shakuni) and to him (Duryodhana) "O ruler of land, know what is my opinion.

sn: प्रियं सर्वे करिष्यामो राज्ञः किङ्करपाणयः। न चास्य शक्नुमः स्थातुं प्रिये सर्वे ह्यतन्द्रिताः॥
en: We all wait with joined hands like the servants of the king (Duryodhana). We must do what is agreeable to him. But we are not always able to seek his welfare with promptness and activity.

sn: वयं तु शस्त्राण्यादाय रथानास्थाय दंशिताः। गच्छामः सहिता हन्तुं पाण्डवान् वनगोचरान्॥
en: Let us now, attired in our armours and armed with our weapons, mount on our chariot and go in a body to kill the Pandavas now living in the forest.

sn: तेषु सर्वेषु शान्तेषु गतेष्वविदितां गतिम्। निर्विवादा भविष्यन्तिधार्तराष्ट्रास्तथा वयम्॥
en: When they (the Pandavas) will be rooted out and when will go to the unknown journey, both ourselves and the sons of Dhritarashtra will be in (eternal) peace.

sn: यावदेव परिघूना यावच्छोकपरायणाः। यावन्मित्रविहीनाश्च तावच्छक्या मतं मम॥
en: As long as they are in distress, as long as they are in sorrow and as long as they are destitute of allies and friends, so long we will be able to destroy them. This is my opinion."

sn: तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा पूजयन्तः पुनः पुनः। बाढमित्येव ते सर्वे प्रत्यूचुः सतजं तदा॥
en: Having heard his these words, they repeatedly applauded him and they all replied to the Suta's son (Karna) saying “Excellent”, "Excellent".

sn: एवमुक्त्वा सुसंरब्धा रथैः सर्वे पृथक्पृथका निर्ययुः पाण्डवान् हन्तुं सहिताः कृतनिश्चयाः॥
en: Having said this, each of them being full of hopes of success separately mounted their chariots. They then started in a body with the resolve of killing the Pandavas.

sn: तान् प्रस्थितान् परिज्ञाय कृष्णद्वैपायनः प्रभुः। आजगाम विशुद्धात्मा दृष्ट्वा दिव्येन चक्षुषा॥
en: Knowing by his spiritual eyes that they had gone away (to kill the Pandavas), that lord, the pure-souled Krishna Dvaipayana (Vyasa), came.

sn: प्रतिषिध्याथ तान् सर्वान् भगवाँल्लोकपूजितः। प्रज्ञाचक्षुषमासीनमुवाचाभ्येत्य सत्वरम्॥
en: The illustrious lord, ever worshipped by all the world, commanded them to stop. He then soon appeared before the king whose knowledge was his eye sitting at his ease.

sn: व्यास उवाच धृतराष्ट्र महाप्राज्ञ निबोध वचनं मम। वक्ष्यामि त्वां कौरवाणां सर्वेषां हितमुत्तमम्॥
en: Vyasa said: O greatly wise Dhritarashtra, hear my words. I shall tell you what will be the great good of all the Kurus.

sn: न मे प्रियं महाबाहो यद् गताः पाण्डवा वनम्। निकृत्या निकृताश्चैव दुर्योधनपुरोगमैः॥
en: O mighty-armed hero, it has not pleased me that the Pandavas have gone to the forest, having been dishonestly defeated by Duryodhana and others.

sn: ते स्मरन्तः परिक्लेशान् वर्षे पूर्णे त्रयोदशे। विमोक्ष्यन्ति विषं क्रुद्धाः कौरवेयेषु भारत॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, on the expiration of the thirteenth year, recollecting all their woes, they may shower virulent poisons on the Kurus.

sn: तदयं किं नु पापात्मा तव पुत्रः सुमन्दधी। पाण्डवान् नित्यसंक्रुद्धो राज्यहेतोर्जिघांसति॥
en: Why does your wicked-minded and sinful son angrily want to kill the Pandavas for the sake of the kingdom?

sn: वार्यतां साध्वयं मूढः शमं गच्छतु ते सुतः। वनस्थांस्तानयं हन्तुमिच्छन् प्राणान् विमोक्ष्यति॥
en: Let the fool be checked; let your son remain quiet. In attempting to kill them (the Pandavas) now living in the forest, he will loose his own life.

sn: यथा हि विदुर: प्राज्ञो यथा भीष्मो यथा वयम्। यथा कृपश्च द्रोणश्च तथा साधुर्भवानपि॥
en: You are as pious as the wise Vidura, Bhishma, myself, Kripa or Drona.

sn: विग्रहो हि महाप्राज्ञ स्वजनेन विगर्हितः। अधर्म्यमयशस्यं च मा राजन् प्रतिपद्यताम्॥
en: O greatly intelligent man, dissension with relatives is improper. It is sinful and reprehensible. O king, you should desist from it.

sn: समीक्षा यादृशी ह्यस्य पाण्डवान् प्रति भारत। उपेक्ष्यमाणा स राजन् महान्तमनयं स्पृशेत्॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, he (Duryodhana) looks towards the Pandavas with such jealousy that unless you interfere, great harm will be the consequence.

sn: अथवायं सुमन्दात्मा वनं गच्छतु ते सुतः। पाण्डैवः सहितो राजन्नेक एवासहायवान्॥ ततः संसर्गजः स्नेहः पुत्रस्य तव पाण्डवैः। यदि स्यात् कृतकार्योऽद्य भवेस्त्वं मनुजेश्वर।॥
en: Or let this wicked son of yours go to the forest alone and unaccompanied. O king, O lord of men, if the Pandavas, from association with him, feel an attachment for your son, then good fortune will be yours.

sn: अथवा जायमानस्य यच्छीलमनुजायते। श्रूयते तन्महाराज नामृतस्यापसर्पति॥ कथं वा मन्यते भीष्मो द्रोणोऽथ विदुरोऽपि वा। भवान् वात्र क्षमं कार्य पुरा वोऽर्थोऽभिवर्धते॥
en: O great king, it has been heard that a man's nature derived from his birth does not leave him till death. What do Bhishma, Drona and Vidura think? What do you think? What id proper should be done at once, else your purpose will ever remain unrealised.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच भगवन् नाहमप्येतद् रोचये द्यूतसम्भवम्। मन्ये तद्विधिनाऽऽकृष्य कारितोऽस्मीति वै मुने॥
en: Dhritarashtra said: O illustrious one, I did not like this business of gambling. O Rishi, I think I was made to give my consent having been drawn by Fate.

sn: नैतद् रोचयते भीष्मो न द्रोणो विदुरो न च। गान्धारी नेच्छति द्यूतं तत्र मोहात् प्रवर्तिमम्॥
en: Neither Bhishma, nor Drona, nor Vidura, nor Gandhari, liked this game at dice. There is no doubt it was begot by Moha (delusion).

sn: परित्यक्तुं न शक्नोमि दुर्योधनमचेतनम्। पुत्रस्नेहेन भगवञ्जानन्नपि प्रियव्रत॥
en: O illustrious one, O (Rishi), who delights in observing vows, knowing everything, but yet for the sake of paternal love. I was unable to abandon the senseless Duryodhana.

sn: व्यास उवाच वैचित्रवीर्य नृपते सत्यमाह यथा भवान्। दृढं विद्मः परं पुत्रं परं पुत्रान्न विद्यते॥
en: Vyasa said : O king, O son of Vichitravirya, what you say is right. We too know it for certain that the son is the greatest of all things. I here is nothing greater than the son.

sn: इन्द्रोऽप्यश्रुनिपातेन सुरभ्या प्रतिबोधितः। अन्यैः समृद्धैरप्यर्थैर्न सुतान्मन्यते परम्॥
en: Instructed by the Surabhi (celestials cow), Indra came to know that the son surpasses in worth other valuable possessions.

sn: अत्र ते कीर्तयिष्यामि महदाख्यानमुत्तमम्। सुरभ्याश्चैव संवादमिन्द्रस्य च विशाम्पते।॥
en: O king, I shall relate to you in this connection that excellent and best of stories, the conversation between Indra and Surabhi.

sn: त्रिविष्टपगता राजन् सुरभी प्रारुदत् किल। गवां माता पुरा तात तामिन्द्रोऽन्वकृपायत॥
en: O king, O child, in the days of yore Surabhi, the mother of cows, was once weeping in the celestials regions. Indra took compassion on her.

sn: इन्द्र उवाच किमिदं रोदिषि शुभे कच्चित् क्षेमं दिवौकसाम्। मानुषेष्वथ वा गोषु नैतदल्पं भविष्यति॥
en: Indra said: O blessed one, why do you weep? Is everything well with the celestials? Has any misfortune, however so little, befallen on the world of men or of the Nagas.

sn: सुरभिरुवाच विनिपातो न वः कश्चिद् दृश्यते त्रिदशाधिप। अहं तु पुत्रं शोचामि तेन रोदिमि कौशिक॥
en: Surabhi said: O lord of heaven, I do not see any evil that has befallen you. I am aggrieved on account of my son. O Vasava, therefore I weep.

sn: पश्यैनं कर्षकं क्षुद्रं दुर्बलं मम पुत्रकम्। प्रतोदेनाभिनिघ्नन्तं लागलेन च पीडितम्॥ निषीदमानं सोत्कण्ठं वध्यमानं सुराधिप। कृपाविष्टास्मि देवेन्द्र मनश्चोद्विजते मम। एकस्तत्र बलोपेतोधुरमुद्वहतेऽधिकाम्॥ अपरोऽप्यबलप्राणः कृशोधमनिसंततः। कृच्छ्रादुद्वहते भारं तं वै शोचामि वासव॥ वध्यमानः प्रतोदेन तुद्यमानः पुनः पुनः। नैव शक्नोति तं भारमुद्वोढुं पश्य वासव॥
en: O chief of the gods, O lord of the celestials, see the (your) cruel husband-man belabouring my weak son with the wooden stick and oppressing him with the stick, for which my son is afflicted with agony and he is falling on the ground and is at the point of death. I am filled with compassion and my mind is agitated. One of those (in the plough) is the stronger (of the pair) and bears his burden of greater weight (with ease), but the other (my son) is lean and weak and but a mass of veins and arteries. O Vasava, he bears his burden with difficulty. Therefore, I am weeping. Being whipped again and again harassed exceedingly.

sn: ततोऽहं तस्य शोकार्ता विरौमि भृशदुःखिता। अश्रूण्यावर्तयन्ती च नेत्राभ्यां करुणायती॥
en: O Vasava, look, he is unable to bear the burden. Therefore, afflicted with grief for his sake, I weep in agony; and tears of sorrow roll down my eyes.

sn: शक्र उवाच तव पुत्रसहस्रेषु पीड्यमानेषु शोभने। किं कृपायितवत्यत्र पुत्र एकत्र हन्यति॥
en: Indra said: O handsome one, thousands of your sons are oppressed (all over the world), why do you then grieve for one who is under inflictions?

sn: सुरभिरुवाच यदि पुत्रसहस्राणि सर्वत्र समतैव मे। दीनस्य तु सतः शक्र पुत्रस्याभ्यधिका कृपा॥
en: Surabhi said: Though I have thousands of offspring, yet my affection flows equally towards them all. But, O Shakra, I feel greater compassion for one who is weak and honest.

sn: व्यास उवाच तदिन्द्रः सुरभीवाक्यं निशम्य भृशविस्मित;। जीवितेनापि कौरव्य मेनेऽभ्यधिकमात्जम्॥
en: Vyasa said: Having heard the words of Surabhi, Indra was much surprised. O descendant of Kuru, he became convinced that a son is dearer than one's own life.

sn: प्रववर्ष च तत्रैव सहसा तोयमुल्बणम्। कर्षकस्याचरन् विघ्नं भगवान् पाकशासनः॥
en: Thereupon the illustrious chastiser of Paka (Indra) suddenly poured a very great shower of rains. Thus he caused obstruction to the husband man's work.

sn: तद् यथा सुरभिः प्राह समवेतास्तु ते तथा। सुतेषु राजन् सर्वेषु हीनेष्वभ्यधिका कृपा॥
en: O king, as Surabhi said, your affection flows equally towards all your sons. Let it be greater towards those that are weak.

sn: यादृशो मे सुतः पाण्डुस्तादृशो मेऽसि पुत्रका विदुरश्च महाप्राज्ञः स्नेहादेतद् ब्रवीम्यहम्॥
en: O son, as my son Pandu is to me, so are you and also greatly wise Vidura. It is out of affection I tell you all this.

sn: चिराय तव पुत्राणां शतमेकश्च भारत। पाण्डोः पञ्चैव लक्ष्यन्ते तेऽपि मन्दाः सुदुःखिताः।
en: O descendant of Bharata, You possess one hundred and one children. Pandu has only five. They are in misery and they are greatly afflicted.

sn: कथं जीवेयुरत्यन्तं कथं वर्धयुरित्यपि। इति दीनेषु पार्थेषु मनो मे परितप्यते॥
en: "How might they save their lives how might they thrive?" Such thoughts about the distressed sons of Pritha make me aggrieved.

sn: यदि पार्थिव कौरव्याञ्जीवमानानिहेच्छसि। दुर्योधनस्तव सुतः शमं गच्छतु पाण्डवैः॥
en: O king, if you wish to keep all the Kurus alive, let your son Duryodhana make peace with the Pandavas.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच एवमेतन्महाप्राज्ञ यथा वदसि नो मुने। अहं चैव विजानामि सर्वे चेमे नराधिपाः॥
en: Dhritarashtra said: O greatly intelligent Rishi, it is exactly as you say. I know it well, as do all these kings.

sn: भवांश्च मन्यते साधु यत् कुरूणां महोदयम्। तदेव विदुरोऽप्याह भीष्मो द्रोणश्च मां पुने॥
en: O Rishi, what you consider beneficial for the Kurus was pointed out to me by Vidura, Bhishma and Drona.

sn: यदि त्वहमनचाह्यः कौरव्येषु दया यदि। अन्वशाधि दुरात्मानं पुत्रं दुर्योधनं मम॥
en: If I deserve your grace and if you have kindness for the Kurus, then teach my wicked son Duryodhana (to be good).

sn: व्यास उवाच अयमायाति वै राजन् मैत्रेयो भगवानृषिः। अन्विष्य पाण्डवान् भ्रातृनिहैत्यस्मद्दिदृक्षया॥
en: Vyasa said: O king, after having seen the Pandava brothers, there comes the illustrious. Rishi Maitreya with the desire of seeing us.

sn: एष दुर्योधनं पुत्रं तव राजन् महानृषिः। अनुशास्ता यथान्यायं शमायास्य कुलस्य च॥
en: O king, this great Rishi will admonish your son Duryodhana for the sake of the welfare of this race.

sn: ब्रूयाद् यदेष कौरव्य तत् कार्यमविशङ्कया। अक्रियायां तु कार्यस्य पुत्रं ते शप्स्यते रुषा॥
en: O descendant of Kuru, what he will advise should be done without any hesitation, for if what he will recommend is not done, the Rishi will curse your son in anger.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्त्वा ययौ व्यासो मैत्रेयः प्रत्यदृश्यता पूजया प्रतिजग्राह सपुत्रस्तं नराधिपः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having said this, Vyasa went away and Maitreya came there. The king with his sons received with all respect.

sn: अर्ध्याद्याभिः क्रियाभिर्वै विश्रान्तं मुनिसत्तमम्। प्रश्रयेणाब्रवीद् राजाधृतराष्ट्रोऽम्बिकासुतः॥
en: That way-worn chief of the Rishis, by offering him Arghya and performing other rites. The son of Ambika, king Dhritarashtra, then asked him these questions.

sn: सुखेनागमनं कच्चिद् भगवन् कुरुजाङ्गलान्। कच्चित् कुशलिनो वीरा भ्रातरः पञ्च पाण्डवाः॥
en: Dhritarashtra said: O illustrious one, has your journey from the Kurujangal been a pleasant one? Are the heroes, the five Pandava brothers, living happily (there)?

sn: समये स्थातुमिच्छन्ति कच्चिच्च भरतर्षभाः। कच्चित् कुरूणां सौभ्रात्रमव्युच्छिन्नं भविष्यति॥
en: Do those foremost (heroes) of the Kuru race intend to pass all the time (they have pledged?) Will the brotherly affection of the Kurus remain unimpaired?

sn: मैत्रेय उवाच तीर्थयात्रामनुकामन् प्राप्तोऽस्मि कुरुजाङ्गलान्। यदृच्छयाधर्मराजं दृष्टवान् काम्यके वने॥
en: Maitreya said : Setting out on a pilgrimage, I arrived at the Kurujangala. I suddenly met there Dharmaraja (Yudhishthira) in the forest of Kamyaka.

sn: तं जटाजिनसंवीतं तपोवननिवासिनम्। समाजग्मुर्महात्मानं द्रष्टुं मुनिगणाः प्रभो॥
en: Attiring himself in deer skin and wearing matted locks, he is living in the forest in asceticism. O lord, many Rishis have assembled there to see him.

sn: तत्राश्रौषं महाराज पुत्राणां तव विभ्रमम्। अनयं द्यूतरूपेण महाभयमुपस्थितम्॥
en: O great king, it was there that I heard of the grave errors that your sons liave committed and also of the approaching) calamity and fearful danger that have arisen from gambling.

sn: कौरवाणामवेक्षया। सदा ह्यभ्यधिकः स्नेहः प्रीतिश्च त्वयि मे प्रभो॥
en: Therefore, I have come to you for the good of the Kurus. O lord, my affection for you is great and I am always pleased with you.

sn: ततोऽहं त्वामनुप्राप्तः नैतदौपयिकं राजंस्त्वयि भीष्मे च जीवति। यदन्योन्येन ते पुत्रा विरुध्यन्ते कथंचन॥
en: O king, when yourself and Bhishma are (still) alive, it is not proper that your sons should quarrel amongst themselves.

sn: मेढीभूतः स्वयं राजन् निग्रहे प्रग्रहे भवान्। किमर्थमनयं घोरमुत्पद्यन्तमुपेक्षसे॥
en: O king, you are (as it were) the stake at which bulls are tied. You are competent to punish and reward. Why do you then overlook this great evil that is about to overtake all?

sn: दस्यूनामिव यद् वृत्तं सभायां कुरुनन्दन। तेन न भ्राजसे राजस्तापसानां समागमे॥
en: O descendant of Kuru, O king, as these wrongs have been perpetrated in your Sabha, wrongs that are like the acts of thieves, you cannot shine in the assembly of ascetics.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततो व्यावृत्य राजानं दुर्योधनममर्षणम्। उवाच श्लक्ष्णया वाचा मैत्रेयो भगवानृषिः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Thereupon turning to the angry Duryodhana, the illustrious Rishi Maitreya spoke to him thus in soft words.

sn: मैत्रेय उवाच दुर्योधन महाबाहो निबोध वदतां वर। वचनं मे महाभाग ब्रुवतो यद्धितं तव॥
en: Maitreya said : O mighty-armed Duryodhana, O best of all eloquent me.l, O blessed one, listen to the words I utter for your good.

sn: मा दुहः पाण्डवान् राजन् कुरुष्व प्रियमात्मनः। पाण्डवानां कुरूणां च लोकस्य च नरर्षभ॥
en: O king, do not quarrel with the Pandavas. O best of men, thus accomplish the good of your own, of the Pandavas, of the Kurus and of all the world.

sn: ते हि सर्वे नरव्याघ्राः शूरा विक्रान्तयोधिनः। सर्वे नागायुतप्राणा वज्रसंहनना दृढाः॥
en: All these foremost of men (the Pandavas) are heroes of great prowess in war. They are endued with strength of ten thousand elephants; their bodies are as hard as the thunder.

sn: सत्यव्रतधराः सर्वे सर्वे पुरुषमानिनः। हन्तारो देवशत्रूणां रक्षसां कामरूपिणाम्॥ हिडिम्बबकमुख्यानां किर्मीरस्य च रक्षसः।
en: They are all truthful and proud of their manliness. They have killed the enemies of the celestials, the Rakshasas, who are able to assume.any from at will. (The Rakshasas) such as were headed by Hidimba, Baka and Kirmira.

sn: इतः प्रद्रवतां रात्रौ यः स तेषां महात्मनाम्॥ आवृत्य मार्ग रौद्रात्मा तस्थौ गिरिरिवाचलः। तं भीमः समरश्लाघी बलेन बलिनां वरः॥ जघान पशुमारेण व्याघ्रः क्षुद्रमृगं यथा। पश्य दिग्विजये राजन् यथा भीमेन पातितः॥ जरासंधो महेष्वासो नागायुतबलो युधि। सम्बन्धी वासुदेवश्च श्याला: सर्वे च पार्षताः॥
en: When departing from this place, he (Kirmira) of fearful soul obstructed in the night the path of those high-souled ones like an immovable hill, that foremost of all strong men, Bhima, ever delighting in fight. Killed him like a beast, as a tiger kills a small deer. O king, see how Bhima, when out for conquest, killed. The great bow-man Jarasandha who possessed the strength of ten thousand elephants. Related (as they are) with Vasudeva (Krishna) and having sons of Prishata (Draupada) as their brother-in-law.

sn: कस्तान् युधि समासीत जरामरणवान् नरः। तस्य ते शम एवास्तु पाण्डवैर्भरतर्षभ॥ कुरु मे वचनं राजन् मा मन्युवशमन्वगाः।
en: Who is there such a hero who being subject to old age and death will cope with them? O best of the Bharata race, let there be peace between you and the Pandavas. Follow my advice; surrender not yourself to danger.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवं तु ब्रुवतस्तस्य मैत्रेयस्य विशाम्पते॥ ऊरूं गजकराकारं करेणाभिजधान सः। दुर्योधनः स्मितं कृत्वा चरणेनोल्लिखन् महीम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : O king, having been thus addressed by Maitreya, Duryodhana slapped his thigh which resembled the trunk of an elephant and he then smilingly began to scratch the ground with his foot.

sn: न किंचिदुक्त्वा दुर्मेधास्तस्थौ किंचिदवाङ्मुखः तमशुश्रूषमाणं तु विलिखन्तं वसुंधराम्॥ दृष्ट्वा दुर्योधनं राजन् मैत्रेयं कोप आविशत्। स कोपवशमापनो मैत्रेयो मुनिसत्तमः॥
en: That wicked wretch (Duryodhana) did not speak a word, but he hung down his head. O king, seeing Duryodhana thus offer an insult to him by silently scratching the earth (by his foot), Maitreya became angry. That best of Rishis, Maitreya, overwhelmed with anger.

sn: विधिना सम्प्रणुदितः शापायास्य मनो दधे। ततः स वार्युपस्पृश्य कोपसंरक्तलोचनः। मैत्रेयोधार्तराष्ट्रं तमशपद् दुष्टचेतसम्॥ यस्मात् त्वं मामनादृत्य नेमां वाचं चिकीर्षसि। तस्मादस्याभिमानस्य सद्यः फलमवाप्नुहि॥
en: And, as if commissioned by fate set his mind to curse him. Thereupon touching water and with eyes red in anger. Maitreya cursed the evil-minded son of Dhritarashtra, saying, "Since slighting my words you decline to follow my advice, you shall soon reap the fruit of your this insolence.

sn: त्वदभिद्रोहसंयुक्तं युद्धमुत्पत्स्यते महत्। तत्र भीमो गदाधातैस्तवोरुं भेत्स्यते बली॥
en: In the great war which will spring out of the wrongs perpetrated by you (on the Pandavas) the mighty Bhima shall smash your that thigh with a blow of his club.

sn: इत्येवमुक्ते वचनेधृतराष्ट्रो महीपतिः। प्रसादयामास मुनि नैतदेवं भवेदिति॥
en: When the Rishi had thus spoken, the ruler of earth, Dhritarashtra, began to gratify the Rishi, so that what he had said may not happen.

sn: मैत्रेय उवाच शमं यास्यति चेत् पुत्रस्तव राजन् यदा तदा। शापो न भविता तात विपरीते भविष्यति॥ मैत्रेयं प्राह
en: Maitreya said : O king, if your son make peace (with the Pandavas) then, O child, my curse will not take effect. Otherwise it would.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच विलक्षयंस्तु राजेन्द्रो दुर्योधनपिता तदा। किर्मीरः कथं भीमेन पातितः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : The king of kings, the father of Duryodhana (Dhritarashtra), thus averting the curse, asked Maitreya (to tell him) how Kirmira had been kiiled by Bhima.

sn: मैत्रेय उवाच नाहं वक्ष्यामि ते भूयो न ते सुश्रूषते सुतः। एष ते विदुरः सर्वमाख्यास्यति गते मयि॥
en: Maitreya said: I shall not again speak to you as my words are not accepted by your son. When I shall go away. Vidura will tell you all.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच इत्येवमुक्त्वा मैत्रेयः प्रातिष्ठत यथाऽऽगतम्। किर्मीरवधसंविग्नो बहिर्दुर्योधनो ययौ॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having said this, Maitreya went away whence he came. Duryodhana (also) went away much agitated by the thought of the death of Kirmira.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच किर्मीरस्य वधं क्षत्तः श्रोतुमिच्छामि कथ्यताम्। रक्षसा भीमसेनस्य कथमासीत् समागमः॥
en: Dhritarashtra said: O Khattva, I desire to hear (the account) of the destruction of Kirmira. Tell me how the encounter between Bhimasena and the Rakshasa (Kirmira) took place.

sn: विदुर उवाच शृणु भीमस्य कर्मेदमतिमानुषकर्मणः। श्रुतपूर्वं मया तेषां कथान्तेषु पुनः पुनः॥
en: Vidura said: Hear that feat of Bhimasena of superhuman deeds. I have heard of it in my conversation with them.

sn: इतः प्रयाता राजेन्द्र पाण्डवा द्यूतनिर्जिताः। जग्मुस्त्रिभिरहोरात्रैः काम्यकं नाम तद् वनम्॥
en: O king of kings, having been defeated at dice, the Pandavas departed from this place. Travelling for three days and three nights, they arrived at a forest, called Kamyaka.

sn: रात्रौ निशीथे त्वाभीले गतेऽर्धसमये नृप। प्रचारे पुरुषादानां रक्षसां घोरकर्मणाम्॥ तद् वनं तापसा नित्यं गोपाश्च वनचारिणः। दूरात् परिहरन्ति स्म पुरुषादभयात् किल॥
en: O king, after the dreadful hours of midnight were passed and when all nature fell asleep, then man-eating Rakshasass of fearful deeds began to wander. (Therefore) the ascetics, the cowherds and other rangers of forest used to shun that forest for the fear of the cannibals.

sn: तेषां प्रविशतां तत्र मार्गमावृत्य भारत। दीप्ताक्षं भीषणं रक्षः सोल्मुकं प्रत्यपद्यत॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, as they (the Pandavas) were entering that forest, a fearful Rakshasas with flaming eyes stood before them with a lighted brand and obstructed their path.

sn: बाहू महान्तौ कृत्वा तु तथाऽऽस्यं च भयानकम् स्थितमावृत्य पन्थानं येन यान्ति कुरूद्वहाः॥
en: With out-stretched arms and terrible face he stood obstructing the way on which those perpetuators of the Kuru race (the Pandavas) were proceeding.

sn: स्पष्टाष्टदंष्ट्रं ताम्राक्षं प्रदीप्तोर्ध्वशिरोरुहम्। सार्करश्मितडिच्चक्रं सबलाकमिवाम्बुदम्॥
en: With his eight teeth stretching out, with his copper-coloured eyes, with the hair of his head blazing and standing erect, he looked like a mass of clouds, mingled with the rays of the sun, charged with lightning and adorned with a flock of cranes (flying underneath those clouds).

sn: सृजन्तं राक्षसी मायां महानादनिनादितम्। मुञ्चन्तं विपुलान् नादान् सतोयमिव तोयदम्॥
en: Uttering fearful yells and roaring like clouds charged with rain, he spread the Rakshasas illusion.

sn: तस्य नादेन संत्रस्ताः पक्षिण: सर्वतोदिशम्। विमुक्तनादाः सम्पेतुः स्थलजा जलजैः सह॥
en: Being terrified by his yells, birds along with other creatures that live on land or in water utterring cries of fear dropped down in all directions.

sn: सम्प्रद्रुतमृगद्वीपिमहिषर्भसमाकुलम्। तद् वनं तस्य नादेन सम्प्रस्थितमिवाभवत्॥
en: In consequence of the deers, the leopards and the buffaloes and the bears flying in all directions, it appeared as if the forest itself was in motion.

sn: तस्योरूवाताभिहतास्ताम्रपल्लवबाहवः। विदूरजाताश्च लताः समाश्लिष्यन्ति पादपान्॥
en: Blown by the wind raised by his thighs, creepers growing at a great distance from that place seemed to embrace in alarm the tree of coppery leaves.

sn: तस्मिन् क्षणेऽथ प्रववौ मारुतो भृशदारुणः। रजसा संवृतं तेन नष्टज्योतिरभून्नभः॥
en: At that time a violent wind began to blow and the sky became darkened with the dust that covered it.

sn: पञ्चानां पाण्डुपुत्राणामविज्ञातो महारिपुः। पञ्चानामिन्द्रियाणां तु शोकावेश इवातुलः॥
en: As grief is the greatest enemy of the objects of the five senses, so that unknown foe appeared to the five Pandavas.

sn: स दृष्ट्वा पाण्डवान् दूरात् कृष्णाजिनसमावृतान् आवृणोत् तद्वनद्वारं मैनाक इव पर्वतः ॥
en: Seeing from a distance the Pandavas clad in black deer skin, he obstructed their path through the forest like the Mainaka mountain.

sn: तं समासाद्य वित्रस्ता कृष्णा कमललोचना। अदृष्टपूर्वं संत्रासान्यमीलयत लोचने॥
en: At the sight of that fearful creature rever seen by her before, the lotus-eyed Krishna (Draupadi), being much terrified, closed her eyes.

sn: दुःशासनकरोत्सृष्टविप्रकीर्णशिरोरुहा। पञ्चपर्वतमप्यस्था नदीवाकुलतां गता॥
en: She whose hair was dishevelled by the hand of Dushashana stood in the midst of the Pandavas like an agitated river amid five hills.

sn: मोमुह्यमानां तां तत्र जगृहुः पञ्च पाण्डवाः। इन्द्रियाणि प्रसक्तानि विषयेषु यथा रतिम्॥
en: Seeing her overwhelmed with fear, the five Pandavas supported her, as the (five) senses influenced by desire are supported by the worldly objects.

sn: अथ तां राक्षसी मायामुत्थितां घोरदर्शनाम्। रक्षोनैर्विविधैर्मन्त्रैर्बोम्यः सम्यक्प्रयोजितैः॥ पश्यतां पाण्डुपुत्राणां नाशयामास वीर्यवान्। स नष्टमायोऽतिबलः क्रोधविस्फारितेक्षणः॥ काममूर्तिधरः क्रूरः कालकल्पो व्यदृश्यत। तमुवाच ततो राजा दीर्घप्रज्ञो युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: (Thereupon) the greatly powerful Dhaumya destroyed in the presence of the sons of Pandu, the fearful Rakshasas illusion by applying various Mantras calculated to destroy the Rakshasass. Seeing his illusion destroyed, that Rakshasas of crooked ways, who was capable of assuming any form at will, expanded his eyes in anger and he appeared like Death himself. Then the greatly intelligent Yudhishthira thus spoke to him.

sn: को भवान् कस्य वा किं ते क्रियता कार्यमुच्यताम्। प्रत्युवाचाथ तद् रक्षोधर्मराज युधिष्ठिरम्॥
en: “Who and whose are you? Say what we shall do. “That Rakshasas thus replied to Dharmaraja Yudhishthira.

sn: अहं बकस्य वै भ्राता किसर इति विश्रुतः। वनेऽस्मिन् काम्यके शून्ये निवसामि गतज्वरः॥
en: I am the brother of Baka and I am known by the name of Kirmira. I live in this uninhabited Kamyaka forest in comfort and ease.

sn: युधि निर्जित्य पुरुषानाहारं नित्यमाचरन्। के यूयमभिसम्प्राप्ता भक्ष्यभूता ममान्तिकम्। युधि निर्जित्य वः सर्वान् भक्षयिष्ये गतज्वरः॥
en: Defeating men in battle I always eat them. Who are you that have come before me as my food? Defeating you all in battle, I shall eat you in comfort.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच युधिष्ठिरस्तु तच्छ्रुत्वा वचस्तस्य दुरात्मनः। आचचक्षे ततः सर्वं गोत्रनामादि भारत॥
en: Vaishampayana said : O descendant of Bharata, having heard the words of that wretch, Yudhishthira told him his name and lineage.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच पाण्डवोधर्मराजोऽहं यदि ते श्रोत्रमागतः। सहितो भ्रातृभिः सर्वैर्भीमसेनार्जुनादिभिः॥ हृतराज्यो वने वासं वस्तुं कृतमतिस्ततः। वनमभ्यागतो घोरमिदं तव परिग्रहम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said : I am the son of Pandu, Dharmaraja (Yudhishthira); you may have heard of me. Deprived of my kingdom, I with my brothers, Bhima, Arjuna and others have come in my wanderings to this fearful forest which is your dominion. I desire to pass the period of my exile here.

sn: विदुर उवाच किर्मीरस्तवब्रवीदेनं दिष्ट्या देवैरिदं मम। उपपादितमोह चिरकालान्मनोगतम्॥ भीमसेनवधार्थं हि नित्यमभ्युद्यतायुधः। चराम पृथिवीं कृत्स्नां नैनं चासादयाम्यहम्॥
en: Vidura said: Kirmira replied, “By good luck, Fate has accomplished today my long cherished desire. With weapons upraised, I have been continually wandering over the earth with the object of killing Bhima. But I did not find him.

sn: सोऽयमासादितो दिष्ट्या भ्रातृहा काक्षितश्चिरम् अनेन हि मम भ्राता बको विनिहतः प्रियः॥ वैत्रकीयवने राजन् ब्राह्मणच्छद्मरूपिणा। विद्याबलमुपाश्रित्य न ह्यस्त्यस्यौरसं बलम्॥
en: By good luck that slayer of my brother (Baka) whom I have been seeking so long has come before me. O king, it is he who, in the disguise of a Brahmana, killed my beloved brother Baka in the Vetrakeja forest. Through his knowledge of skill only. He has no strength of arms.

sn: हिडिम्बश्च सखा मह्यं दयितो वनगोचरः। हतो दुरात्मनानेन स्वसा चास्य हृता पुरा॥
en: My friend Hidimba, who lived in the forest. Was forinerly killed by this wretch; and he then took possession of his sister.

sn: सोऽयमभ्यागतो मूढो ममेदं गहनं वनम्। प्रचारसमयेऽस्माकमर्धरात्रे स्थिते स मे॥
en: That fool has now come to my this deep forest. At a time when the night is half-spent and when we wander about.

sn: अद्यास्य यातयिष्यामि तद् वैरं चिरसम्भृतम्। तर्पयिष्यामि च बकं रुधिरेणास्य भूरिणा॥
en: I shall today kill him; and (I shall now) wreak my vengeance on my old enemy. I shall gratify (the manes) of Baka with plentiful blood of his (body).

sn: अद्याहमनृणो भूत्वा भ्रातुः सख्युस्तथैव च। शान्तिं लब्धास्मि परमां हत्वा राक्षसकण्टकम्॥
en: I shall today be freed from my debts which I owe to my friend and brother. I shall obtain great peace by killing today this enemy of the Rakshasas.

sn: यदि तेन पुरा मुक्तो भीमसेनो बकेन वै। अद्यैनं भक्षयिष्यामि पश्यतस्ते युधिष्ठिर॥
en: If Bhima was formerly allowed to escape from the hands of Baka. O Yudhishthira, I shall today devour him in your presence.

sn: एनं हि विपुलप्राणमद्य हत्वा वृकोदरम्। सम्भक्ष्य जरयिष्यामि यथागस्त्यो महासुरम्॥
en: Killing this huge bodied Vrikodara (Bhima) today. I shall eat him up and digest him as Agasta did the great Asura (Vatapi).

sn: एवमुक्तस्तुधर्मात्मा सत्यसंधो युधिष्ठिरः। नैतदस्तीति सक्रोधो भर्त्सयामास राक्षसम्॥
en: Having been thus addressed, the virtuousminded and stead-fast in his pledges, Yudhishthira, saying “It cannot be," rebuked the Rakshasas in anger.

sn: ततो भीमो महाबाहुरारुज्य तरसा दुमम्। दशव्याममथोद्विद्धं निष्पत्रमकरोत् तदा॥
en: Thereupon the mighty armed Bhima soon tore up a tree. Of the length of ten Vyamas and stripped it of its leaves.

sn: चकार सज्यं गाण्डीवं वज्रनिष्पेषगौरवम्। निमेषान्तरमात्रेण तथैव विजयोऽर्जुनः॥
en: Within a twinkle of an eye the ever victorious Arjuna stringed the Gandiva (bow) of the force of the thunder.

sn: निवार्य भीमो जिष्णुं तं तद् रक्षो मेघनि:स्वनम्। अभिद्रुत्याब्रवीद् वाक्यं तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति भारत॥
en: Making Vishnu (Arjuna) desist, Bhima said to that Rakshasas in a voice as that of the roaring louds “Stay, Stay."

sn: इत्युक्त्वैनमतिक्रुद्धः कक्ष्यामुत्पीड्य पाण्डवः। निष्पिष्य पाणिना पाणिं संदष्टौष्ठपुटो बली॥ तमभ्यधावद् वेगेन भीमो वृक्षायुधस्तदा। यमदण्डप्रतीकाशं ततस्तं तस्य मूर्धनि॥ पातयामास वेगेन कुलिशं मघवानिव। असम्भ्रान्तं तु तद् रक्षः समरे प्रत्यदृश्यत॥
en: Saying this, the Pandava Bhima tightened the cloth round his waist in anger. Rubbing his palms and biting his nether lips, the heroic Bhima, armed with the tree, rushed towards him. As Maghavata (Indra) hurls his thunderbolt, so he (Bhima) made it (the tree), which was like the mace of Yama, descend with force on his (Kirmira's) head. The Rakshasas was seen to stand in the battle unmoved.

sn: चिक्षेप चोल्मुकं दीप्तमशनिं ज्वलितामिव। तदुदस्तमलातं तु भीमः प्रहरतां वरः॥ पदा सव्येन चिक्षेप तद् रक्षः पुनराव्रजत्। किर्मीरश्चापि सहसा वृक्षमुत्पाट्य पाण्डवम्॥ दण्डपाणिरिव क्रुद्धः समरे प्रत्यधावत। तद् वृक्षयुद्धमभवन्महीरुहविनाशनम्॥ वालिसुग्रीवयोर्धात्रोर्यथा स्त्रीकाक्षिणोः पुरा।
en: He hurled his lighted brand (at Bhima) which was as flaming as the lightning. But that foremost of all warriors (Bhima) turned it off with his left foot and it then went back towards Rakshasas. Kirmira also, suddenly tearing up a tree, himself angrily rushed to fight with the Pandava (Bhima) like mace bearing Yama. That battle, so destructive to the trees, looked like that of the old one which was fought for the sake of a woman between Bali and Sugriva.

sn: शीर्षयोः पतिता वृक्षा बिभिदु:कधा तयोः॥ यथैवौत्पलपत्राणि मत्तयोर्द्विपयोस्तथा।
en: The trees, struck at the heads (of the two combatants), were broken into minute pieces, like lotus-stalks thrown on the temples of mad elephants.

sn: मुञ्जवज्जर्जरीभूता बहवस्तत्र पादपाः॥ चीराणीव व्युदस्तानि रेजुस्तत्र महावने। तद् वृक्षयुद्धमभवन्मुहूर्तं भरतर्षभ। राक्षसानां च मुख्यस्य नराणामुत्तमस्य च॥
en: In that great forest innumerable trees, crushed like reeds, lay scattered like rags. O best of the Bharata race, that fight with trees between that foremost of Rakshasass (Kirmira) and that best of men (Bhima) lasted but for a moment.

sn: ततः शिलां समुक्षिप्य भीमस्य युधि तिष्ठतः। प्राहिणोद् राक्षसः क्रुद्धो भीमश्च न चचाल ह॥
en: Thereupon the angry Rakshasas hurled a stone at Bhima standing in the fight, but Bhima did not waver.

sn: तं शिलाताडनजडं पर्यधावत राक्षसः। बाहुविक्षिप्तकिरणः स्वर्भानुरिव भास्करम्॥
en: Thereupon as Rahu goes to devour the sun, shadowing his rays with out-stretched arms, so did the Rakshasas rush upon Bhima who had remained firm under the blow that was inflicted by the (Rakshasass) with the stone.

sn: तावन्योन्यं समाश्लिष्य प्रकर्षन्तौ परस्परम्। उभावपि चकाशेते प्रवृद्धौ वृषभाविव॥
en: Grappling and dragging each other in various ways, they appeared like two infuriated bulls struggling with each other.

sn: तयोरासीत् सुतुमुलः सम्प्रहारः सुदारुणः। नखदंष्ट्रायुधवतोर्व्याघ्रयोरिव दृप्तयोः॥
en: Or like two mighty tigers armed with teeth and claws. The fight between them was fierce and hard.

sn: दुर्योधननिकाराच्च बाहुवीर्याच्च दर्पितः। कृष्णानयनदृष्टश्च व्यवर्धत वृकोदरः॥
en: Vrikodara (Bhima), being proud of his strength of arms and conscious of Krishna's (Draupadi's) looking at him and remembering their disgrace at the hand of Duryodhana, began to swell in vigour.

sn: अभिपद्य च बाहुभ्यां प्रत्यगृहणादमर्षितः। मातङ्गमिव मातङ्गः प्रभिन्नकरटामुखम्॥ स चाप्येनं ततो रक्षः प्रतिजग्राह वीर्यवान्। तमाक्षिपद् भीमसेनो बलेन बलिनां वरः॥
en: Inflamed with wrath, Bhima seized the Rakshasas by his arms as one elephant in rut seizes another. The mighty Rakshasas also in his turn seized his adversary, but that foremost of all warriors Bhimasena threw the cannibal down with violence.

sn: तयोर्भुजविनिष्पेषादुभयोर्बलिनोस्तदा। शब्दः समभवद् घोरो वेणुस्फोटसमो युधि॥ अथैनमाक्षिप्य बलाद् गृह्य मध्ये वृकोदरः। धूनयामास वेगेन वायुश्चण्ड इव दुमम्॥
en: The sounds that rose from those mighty combatants pressing each others hands were fearful. They resembled the sounds of splittering bamboo's. Hurling the Rakshasas down. Vrikodar seized him forcibly by the waist and he then began to shake him, as trees are shaken by the wind.

sn: स भीमेन परामृष्टो दुर्बलो बलिना रणे। व्यस्पन्दत यथाप्राणं विचकर्ष च पाण्डवम्॥
en: Having been thus seized by the mighty Bhima, he became weakened in the fight with that strong man. But thus being shaken he still pressed the Pandava (Bhima) with all his strength.

sn: तत एनं परिश्रान्तमुपलक्ष्य वृकोदरः। योक्त्रयामास बाहुभ्यां पशुं रशनया यथा॥
en: Finding him (the Rakshasas) fatigued, Vrikodara (Bhima) twined his own arm round the body of the enemy, as one binds a beast with a cord.

sn: विनदन्तं महानादं भिन्नभेरीस्वनं बली। भ्रामयामास सुचिरं विस्फुरन्तमचेतसम्॥
en: The monster then roared fearfully like a trumpet out of order. But the hero (Bhima) whirled him for a long time, till he became insensible.

sn: तं विषीदन्तमाज्ञाय राक्षसं पाण्डुनन्दनः। प्रगृह्य तरसा दो• पशुमारममारयत्॥
en: Finding the Rakshasas exhausted the son of Pandu, (Bhima) took him up on his arms without loss of time and he then killed him like a beast.

sn: आक्रम्य च कटीदेशे जानुना राक्षसाधमम्। पीडयामास पाणिभ्यां कण्ठं तस्य वृकोदरः॥
en: Placing his knees on the breast of that wretch of Rakshasass and seizing his throat, Vrikodara (Bhima) began to press his neck.

sn: अथ जर्जरसर्वाङ्गं व्यावृत्तनयनोल्वणम्। भूतले भ्रामयामास वाक्यं चेदमुवाच ह॥
en: Then dragging along on the earth the bruised body of the Rakshasas whose eye-lids were about to close, Bhima spoke thus.

sn: हिडिम्बबकयोः पाप न त्वमश्रुप्रमार्जनम्। करिष्यसि गतश्चापि यमस्य सदनं प्रति॥
en: “O sinful wretch, you will no more have to wine away the tears of Hidimba and Baka, for you too are going to the abode of Yama.”

sn: स्तं राक्षसं क्रोधपरीतचेताः। मुद्घान्तचित्तं व्यसुमुत्ससज॥
en: Having said this and seeing the Rakshasas destitute of clothes and ornaments and insensible, that foremost of men, his heart filled with wrath left him dead.

sn: तस्मिन् हते तोयदतुल्यरूपे कृष्णां पुरस्कृत्य नरेन्द्रपुत्राः। भीमं प्रशरयाथ गुणैरनेकैहृष्टास्ततो द्वैतवनाय जग्मुः॥
en: When that cloud-coloured Rakshasas was killed, the son of the great king (Pandu i.e. Yudhishthira) praised Bhima for his many qualities. And then placing Krishna (Draupadi) in their front, they set out for the forest of Daitya.

sn: विदुर उवाच एवं विनिहतः संख्ये किर्मीरो मनुजाधिप। भीमेन वचनात् तस्यधर्मराजस्य कौरव॥
en: O ruler of men, O descendant of Kuru, it was thus that Kirmira was killed by Bhima at the command of Dharmaraja (Yudhishthira).

sn: ततो निष्कण्टकं कृत्वा वनं तदपराजितः। द्रौपद्या सहधर्मज्ञो वसतिं तामुवास ह॥
en: Having made the forest free from its pest, the invincible and virtuous man (Yudhishthira) lived with Draupadi there in their abode.

sn: समाश्वास्य च ते सर्वे द्रौपदीं भरतर्षभाः। प्रहृष्टमनसः प्रीत्या प्रशशंसुर्वृकोदरम्॥
en: Comforting Draupadi, those foremost of heroes of the Bharata race with glad hearts praised Vrikodara cheerfully.

sn: भीमबाहुबलोत्पिष्टे विनष्टे राक्षसे ततः। विविशुस्ते वनं वीराः क्षेमं निहतकण्टकम्॥
en: After the Rakshasas had been killed by the strength of arms of Bhima, the heroes. (the Pandavas) entered that peaceful forest (now) being free from its pest.

sn: स मया गच्छता मार्गे विनिकीर्णो भयावहः। वने महति दुष्टात्मा दृष्टो भीमबलाद्धतः॥
en: Passing through that great forest, I saw the body of the wicked and fearful Rakshasas lying killed by Bhima's prowess.

sn: तत्राश्रौषमहं चैतत् कर्म भीमस्य भारत। ब्राह्मणानां कथयतां ये तत्रासन् समागताः॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, I heard there (in the forest) of this great deed of Bhima from the Brahmanas who had assembled there (round the Pandavas).

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवं विनिहतं संख्ये किर्मीरं रक्षसां वरम्। श्रुत्वाध्यानपरो राजा निशश्वासार्तवत् तदा॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having thus heard of the account of the destruction of that foremost of Rakshasas, Kirinira, the king (Dhritarashtra) sighed in sorrow and became absorbed in thought.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच भोजाः प्रव्रजिताञ्छ्रुत्वा वृष्णयश्चान्धकैः सह। पाण्डवान् दुःखसंतप्तान् समाजग्मुर्महावने॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having heard that the Pandavas had been banished, the Bhojas with the Vrishnis and the Andhakas went to the afflicted Pandavas in the great forest.

sn: पाञ्चालस्य च दायादोधृष्टकेतुश्च चेदिपः। केकयाश्च महावीर्या भ्रातरो लोकविश्रुताः॥ वने द्रष्टुं ययुः पार्थान् क्रोधामर्षसमन्विताः। गर्हयन्तोधार्तराष्ट्रान् किं कुर्म इति चाब्रुवन्॥
en: The relatives of (the king) Panchala, Dhristadyumna, the king of Chedi and the greatly powerful and renowned brothers, the Kaikeyas. Went to see the sons of Pritha in the forest. Their heart inflamed with wrath, they reproaching the sons of Dhritarashtra said, “What should we do?”

sn: वासुदेवं पुरस्कृत्य सर्वे ते क्षत्रियर्षभाः। परिवार्योपविविशुर्धर्मराज युधिष्ठिरम्।। अभिवाद्य कुरुश्रेष्ठं विषण्णः केशवोऽब्रवीत्॥
en: All those foremost of Kshatriyas with Vasudeva (Krishna) at their head sat around Dharmaraja Yudhishthira. Saluting that chief of the Kurus, Keshava (Krishna) spoke thus in sorrow.

sn: वासुदेव उवाच दुर्योधनस्य कर्णस्य शकुनेश्च दुरात्मनः। दुःशासनचतुर्थानां भूमिः पास्यति शोणितम्॥
en: Krishna said: The earth will drink the will drink the blood of Duryodhana, Karna, Shakuni and the fourth (of their allies) Dushashana.

sn: एतान् निहत्य समरे ये च तस्य पदानुगाः। तांश्च सर्वान् विनिर्जित्य सहितान् सनराधिपान्॥ ततः सर्वेऽभिषिञ्चामोधर्मराज युधिष्ठिरम्। निकृत्योपचरन् वध्य एषधर्मः सनातनः॥
en: Killing all these and defeating all their followers and royal allies. We shall all install Dharmaraja Yudhishthira (on the throne). The crafty men deserve to be slain. This is 'eternal morality.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच पार्थानामभिषङ्गेण तथा क्रुद्धं जनार्दनम्। अर्जुनः शमयामास दिधक्षन्तमिव प्रजाः॥ संक्रुद्धं केशवं दृष्ट्वा पूर्वदेहेषु फाल्गुनः। कीर्तयामास कर्माणि सत्यकीर्तेर्महात्मनः॥ पुरुषस्याप्रमेयस्य सत्यस्यामिततेजसः। प्रजापतिपतेविष्णोर्लोकनाथस्यधीमतः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Jarsardana (Krishna) became angry for the wrongs done to the sons of Pritha and he seemed bent upon consuming all created things. But Arjuna tried to pacify him. Seeing Keshava (Krishna) angry, Falguni (Arjuna) began to recite the feats achieved in his former lives by that soul of all things who is immeasurable, who is the eternal one of infinite energy, the lord of Prajapati, the supreme ruler of the world and the greatly wise Vishnu.

sn: अर्जुन उवाच दश वर्षसहस्राणि यत्रसायंगृहो मुनिः। व्यचरस्त्वं पुरा कृष्ण पर्वते गन्धमादने॥
en: Arjuna said: O Krishna, in the days of yore, you had wandered on the Gandhamadana mountain for ten thousand years as a Fatrashayanagriha Rishi.

sn: दश वर्षसहस्राणि दश वर्षशतानि च। पुष्करेष्ववसः कृष्ण त्वमपो भक्षयन् पुरा॥
en: O Krishna, living on water alone, you passed eleven thousand years in the days of yore by the side of the Pushkara (lake).

sn: ऊर्ध्वबाहुर्विशालायां बदर्यां मधुसूदन। अतिष्ठ एकपादेन वायुभक्षः शतं समाः॥
en: O slayer of Madhu, you with your arms upraised and standing on one leg, living all the while on air, passed one hundred years on the high hills of Badari.

sn: अवकृष्टोत्तरासङ्गः कृशोधमनिसंततः। आसीः कृष्ण सरस्वत्यां सत्रे द्वादशवार्षिके॥
en: O Krishna, leaving aside your upper garment and looking like a bundle of veins, with your body emaciated you lived on the banks of the Sarasvati, employed in your sacrifice extending for twelve years.

sn: प्रभासमप्यथासाद्य तीर्थं पुण्यजनोचितम्। तथा कृष्ण महातेजा दिव्यं वर्षसहस्रकम्॥ अतिष्ठस्त्वमथैकेन पादेन नियमस्थितः। लोकप्रवृत्तिहेतुस्त्वमिति व्यासो ममाब्रवीत्॥
en: O greatly effulgent Krishna, in observance of your vow, you stood on one leg for one thousand celestials years on the plains of Pravasha which the virtuous ought to visit. Vyasa has told me that you are the cause of the creation and its course.

sn: क्षेत्रज्ञः सर्वभूतानामादिरन्तश्च केशव। निधानं तपसां कृष्णा यज्ञस्त्वं च सनातनः॥
en: O Keshava, the lord of Kshetra, you are the mover of all minds and the beginning and the end of all things. O Krishna, all asceticism rests in you; you are the embodiment of all sacrifices and you are the eternal one.

sn: निहत्य नरकं भौममाहत्य मणिकुण्डले। प्रथमोत्पतितं कृष्णा मेध्यमश्वमवासृजः॥
en: O Krishna, killing the fearful Naraka, the first begotten offspring of the earth, you have obtained his ear-rings by the performance of the first horse sacrifice.

sn: कृत्वा तत् कर्म लोकानामृषभः सर्वलोकजित्। अवधीस्त्वं रणे सर्वान् समेतान् दैत्यदानवान्॥
en: O foremost of all the worlds, having performed that feat, you have become victorious over all. You have killed all the Daityas and the Danavas mustered in battle.

sn: ततः सर्वेश्वरत्वं च सम्प्रदाय शचीपतेः। मानुषेषु महाबाहो प्रादुर्भूतोऽसि केशव॥
en: O mighty-armed Keshava, giving the lord of Sachi (Indra) the sovereignty of the universe, you have taken your birth among men.

sn: स त्वं नारायणो भूत्वा हरिरासीः परंतप। ब्रह्मा सोमश्च सूर्यश्चधर्मोधाता यमोऽनलः॥ वायुर्वैश्रवणो रुद्रः कालः खं पृथिवी दिशः। अजश्चराचरगुरुः स्रष्टा त्वं पुरुषोत्तम॥
en: O chastiser of foes, having floated on Primordial waters, you subsequently became Hari, Brahma, Surya, Dharma, Dhatri, Yama, Anala. Vayu, Vaisravana, Rudra, Kala and the sky, the earth, the air and the directions. O foremost of Purushas, you are your own creator, you are the lord of all mobile and immobile universe.

sn: परायणं देवमूर्धा क्रतुभिर्मधुसूदन। अयजो भूरितेजा वै कृष्ण चैत्ररथे वने॥
en: O slayer of Madhu, O greatly effulgent one, O Krishna, you gratified with your sacrifice in the forest of Chitraratha the chief of the celestials, the highest of the high.

sn: शतं शतसहस्राणि सुवर्णस्य जनार्दन। एकैकस्मिंस्तदा यज्ञे परिपूर्णानि भागशः॥
en: O Janardana, at each sacrifice you offered, according to (each one's) shares, gold by hundred and thousands.

sn: अदितेरपि पुत्रत्वमेत्य यादवनन्दन। त्वं विष्णुरिति विख्यात इन्द्रादवरजो विभुः॥
en: O descendant of Yadu, becoming the son of Aditi you have been known as the younger brother of Indra, though you are the exalted one of the supreme attributes.

sn: शिशुर्भूत्वा दिवं खं च पृथिवीं च परंतप। त्रिभिर्विक्रमणैः कृष्ण क्रान्तवानसि तेजसा॥
en: O chastiser of foes, O Krishna while you are but a child, you filled by three steps the heaven, the sky and the earth in consequences of your energy.

sn: सम्प्राप्य दिवमाकाशमादित्यस्यन्दने स्थितः। अत्यरोचश्च भूतात्मन् भास्करं स्वेन तेजसा॥
en: O soul of all creatures, covering the heaven and the sky, you dwell in the body of the sun and afflict him with your own effulgence.

sn: प्रादुर्भावसहस्रेषु तेषु तेषु त्वया विभो। अधर्मरुचयः कृष्ण निहताः शतशोऽसुराः॥
en: O exalted one, O Krishna, in your incarnations on three thousand occasions, you have killed the sinful Asuras by thousands.

sn: सादिता मौरवाः पाशा निसुन्दनरको हतौ। कृतः क्षेमः पुनः पन्थाः पुरं प्राग्ज्योतिषं प्रति॥
en: By destroying the Mansavas and the Pashas and killing Nishunda and Naraka, you have again made the road to Pragjotisha safe.

sn: जारूथ्यामाहुतिः क्राथः शिशुपालो जनैः सह। जरासंधश्च शैब्यश्च शतधन्वा च निर्जितः॥
en: You killed Ahuti at Jarutha, Kratha and Shishupala with his followers and allies, Jarasandha, Saivya and Shatadhanvan.

sn: तथा पर्जन्यघोषेण रथेनादित्यवर्चसा। अवाप्सीमहिषीं भोज्यां रणे निर्जित्य रुक्मिणम्॥
en: You defeated on your car which is as effulgent as the sun and as roaring a the clouds, Rukmi in battle and then obtained for your queen the daughter of Bhoja.

sn: इन्द्रद्युम्नो हतः कोपाद् यवनश्च कसेरुमान्। हतः सौभपतिः शाल्वस्त्वया सौभं च पातितम्॥
en: You killed in fury Indradyumna and the Yavana called Kaseruman. Killing Shalva, the king of Saivya, you destroyed his city.

sn: एवमेते युधि हता भूयश्चान्याञ्छृणुष्व ह। इरावत्यां हतो भोजः कार्तवीर्यसमो युधि।॥
en: At Irvati, you killed king Bhoja, who was equal to Kartavirya in battle.

sn: गोपतिस्तालकेतुश्च त्वया विनिहतावुभौ। तां च भोगवतीं पुण्यामृषिकान्तां जनार्दन॥ द्वारकामात्मसात् कृत्वा समुद्रं गमयिष्यसि।
en: Both Gopati and Taluketu also have been killed by you. O Janardana, you have also obtained for yourself the sacred city of Dvarka which abounds in wealth and which is agreeable to all Rishis. You will submerge it into the ocean at the end.

sn: न क्रोधो न च मात्सर्यं नानृतं मधुसूदन। त्वयि तिष्ठति दाशार्ह न नृशंस्यं कुतोऽनृजु॥ आसीनं चैत्यमध्ये त्वां दीप्यमानं स्वतेजसा। आगम्य ऋषयः सर्वेऽयाचन्ताभयमच्युत॥
en: O slayer of Madhu, O descendant of Dasahara race, how can crookedness be in you, devoid as you are of anger, envy, untruth and cruelty? O undeteriorating one, all the Rishis come to you when seated in your glory on the sacrificial ground and seek your protection.

sn: युगान्ते सर्वभूतानि संक्षिप्य मधुसूदन। आत्मनैवात्मसात् कृत्वा जगदासीः परंतप॥
en: O slayer of Madhu. O chastiser of foes, contracting all things and withdrawing this universe into your own self, you stay at the end of Yuga.

sn: युगादौ तव वार्ष्णेय नाभिपद्मादजायत। ब्रह्मा चराचरगुरुर्यस्येदं सकलं जगत्॥
en: O descendant of the Vrishni race, there at the beginning of the Yuga, sprang from your lotus-like navel Brahma himself who is the lord of all mobile and immobile things and whose is this entire universe.

sn: तं हन्तुमुद्यतौ घोरौ दानवौ मधुकैटभौ। तयोर्व्यतिक्रमं दृष्ट्वा क्रुद्धस्य भवतो हरेः॥ ललाटाज्जातवाञ्छम्भुः शूलपाणिस्त्रिलोचनः। इत्थं तावपि देवेशौ त्वच्छरीरसमुद्भवौ॥४०
en: O Hari, when the fearful Danavas Madhu and Kaitava were bent on killing Brahma, seeing their impious endevour you grew angry and from your head then sprang Sambhu, the holder of trident, the deity of three eyes. Thus have these two foremost of the deities sprung from your body to accomplish your work.

sn: त्वन्नियोगकरावेताविति मे नारदोऽब्रवीत्। तथा नारायण पुरा क्रतुभिर्भूरिदक्षिणैः॥ इष्टवांस्त्वं महासत्रं कृष्ण चैत्ररथे वने। नैवं परे नापरे वा करिष्यन्ति कृतानि वा॥ कृतवान् पुण्डरीकाक्ष बलदेवसहायवान्। कैलासभवने चापि ब्राह्मणैर्व्यवस: सह॥
en: It was Narada who has told me (all) this. O Narayana, you performed in the forest of Chaitraratha a grand sacrifice with multitudes of rites and plentiful of gifts. O lotus-eyed deity the feats you accomplished with your prowess aided by Baladeva have never before been done by others. They are not capable of being done by others in future. You dwelt even in Kailasa accompanied by Brahmanas.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्त्वा महात्मानमात्मा कृष्णस्य पाण्डवः। तूष्णीमासीत् ततः पार्थमित्युवाच जनार्दनः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having spoken thus to Krishna, the highsouled Pandava (Arjuna) who was his (Krishna's) soul became dumb. Janardana (Krishna) then thus replied to Partha (Arjuna).

sn: ममैव त्वं तवैवाहं ये मदीयास्तवैव ते। यस्त्वां द्वेष्टि स मां द्वेष्टि यस्त्वामनु समामनु॥
en: You are mine and I am yours. All that is mine is yours also. He who hates you hates me and he who follows you follows me.

sn: नरस्त्वमसि दुर्धर्ष हरिर्नारायणो ह्यहम्। काले लोकमिमं प्राप्तौ नरनारायणावृषी॥
en: O irrepressible hero, you are Nara and I am Narayana (Hari). We are the Rishis Nara and Narayana born in the world of men for a special purpose.

sn: अनन्यः पार्थ मत्तस्तवं त्वत्तश्चाहं तथैव च। नावयोरन्तरं शक्यं वेदितुं भरतर्षभ॥
en: O Partha, you are from me and I am from you. O best of the Bharata race, none can understand the difference that exists between us.

sn: एवमुक्ते तु वैशम्पायन उवाच वचने केशवेन महात्मना। तस्मिन् वीरसमावाये संरब्धेष्वथ राजसु॥ धृष्टद्युम्नमुखैवीरैर्धातृभिः परिवारिता। पाञ्चाली पुण्डरीकाक्षमासीनं भ्रातृभिः सह। अभिगम्याब्रवीत् क्रुद्धा शरण्यं शरणैषिणी॥
en: Vaishampayana said: When the high-souled Krishna said this in the midst of that assembly of the heroic kings, who were all excited with anger. The Panchala princess (Draupadi), surrounded by Dhristadyumna and her other heroic brothers, came to the lotus-eyed one (Krishna) who was seated with his cousins. Desirous of getting protection, she spoke thus to the refuge of all (Krishna) in angry words.

sn: द्रौपद्युवाच पूर्वे प्रजाभिसर्गे त्वामाहुरेकं प्रजापतिम्। स्रष्टारं सर्वलोकानामसितो देवलोऽब्रवीत्॥
en: Draupadi said : Asita and Devala have said that in the matter of creation of things you have been indicated as the only Prajapati and the creator of all the worlds.

sn: विष्णुस्त्वमसि दुर्धर्ष त्वं यज्ञो मधुसूदन। यष्टा त्वमसि यष्टव्यो जामदग्न्यो यथाब्रवीत्॥
en: O irrepressible one, Jamadagni says you are Vishnu. O slayer of Madhu, you are the sacrifice, you are the sacrificer and you are he for whom the sacrifice is performed.

sn: ऋषयस्त्वां क्षमामाहुः सत्यं च पुरुषोत्तम। सत्याद् यज्ञोऽसि सम्भूतः कश्यपस्त्वां यथाब्रवीत्।
en: O best of Purushas (male beings), the Rishis call you Forgiveness and Truth. Kashyapa has said that you are the sacrifice sprung from Truth.

sn: साध्यानामपि देवानां शिवानामीश्वरेश्वर। भूतभावन भूतेश यथा त्वां नारदोऽब्रवीत्॥
en: O lord, Narada says that you are the God of the Sadhyas and of the Shivas, you are the creator and the lord of all.

sn: ब्रह्मशंकरशक्राद्यैर्दैववृन्दैः पुनः पुनः। क्रीडसे त्वं नरव्याघ्र बालः क्रीडनकैरिव॥
en: O foremost of men, as children sport with their toys, you repeatedly sport with the celestials including Brahma, Shankara (Shiva) and Shakra (Indra).

sn: द्यौश्च ते शिरसा व्याप्ता पद्भ्यां च पृथिवी प्रभो। जठरं त इमे लोकाः पुरुषोऽसि सनातनः॥
en: O lord, the firmament is covered by your head and the earth by your feet. These worlds are your womb and you are the Eternal one.

sn: विद्यातपोऽभितप्तानां तपसा भावितात्मनाम्। आत्मदर्शनतृप्तानामृषीणामसि सत्तमः॥
en: You are the best of all objects to those Rishis who have been sanctified by ine Vedic lore and asceticism, whose souls have been purified by penance and who are contended with some visions.

sn: राजर्षीणां पुण्यकृतामाहवेष्वनिवर्तिनाम्। सर्वधर्मोपपन्नानां त्वं गतिः पुरुषर्षभ। त्वं प्रभुस्त्वं विभुश्च त्वं भूतात्मा त्वं विचेष्टसे॥
en: O best of Purushas, you are the refuge of all royal sages, who are devoted to piety, who never turn their looks on the field of battle and who possess every accomplishment. You are the lord of all; you are omnipresent, you are the soul of all things, you are the active power pervading everything.

sn: लोकपालाश्च लोकाच नक्षत्राणि दिशो दश। नभश्चन्द्रश्च सूर्यश्च त्वयि सर्वं प्रतिष्ठितम्॥
en: The rulers of the several worlds, those worlds themselves, the steller-conjunctions, the ten points of horizon, the firmament, the moon and the sun are all established in you.

sn: मर्त्यता चैव भूतानाममरत्वं दिवौकसाम्। त्वयि सर्वं महाबाहो लोककार्यं प्रतिष्ठितम्॥
en: O mighty armed hero, the mortality of all creatures and the immortality of the universe are established in you.

sn: सा तेऽहं दुःखमाख्यास्ये प्रणयान्मधुसूदन। ईशस्त्वं सर्वभूतानां ये दिव्या ये च मानुषाः॥
en: O slayer of Madhu, impelled by the affection, you bore for me, I shall relate to you my grief's. You are the supreme lord of all creatures, both celestials and human.

sn: कथं नु भार्या पार्थानां तव कृष्ण सखी विभो। धृष्टद्युम्नस्य भगिनी सभां कृष्येत मादृशी॥
en: O Krishna, how could one like me, the wife of Pritha's sons (the Pandavas), the sister of Dhristadyumna and the friend of yours, be dragged to the assembly?

sn: स्त्रीधर्मिणी वेपमाना शोणितेन समुक्षिता। एकवस्त्रा विकृष्टास्मि दुःखिता कुरुसंसदि॥
en: Alas, in my season,. stained with blood, with but a single cloth on, trembling and weeping, I was dragged into the court of the Kurus!

sn: राज्ञां मध्ये सभायां तु रजसातिपरिप्लुता। दृष्ट्वा च मांधार्तराष्ट्रा प्राहसन् पापचेतसः॥
en: Seeing me stained with blood (standing) in the presence of the kings in that assembly, the wicked-minded sons of Dhritarashtra laughed at me.

sn: दासीभावेन मां भोक्तुमीषुस्ते मधुसूदन। जीवत्सु पाण्डुपुत्रेषु पञ्चालेषु च वृष्णिषु॥
en: O slayer of Madhu, though the Pandavas, the Panchalas and the Vrishnis were present, yet they (the sons of Dhritarashtra) dared express their desire of making me their slave.

sn: नन्वहं कृष्ण भीष्मस्यधृतराष्ट्रस्य चोभयोः। स्नुषा भवामिधर्मेण साहं दासीकृता बलात्॥
en: O Krishna, I am the daughter-in-law of both Bhishma and Dhritarashtra according to the ordinance, yet, О slayer of Madhu, they wished to make me their slave by force.

sn: गर्हये पाण्डवांस्त्वेव युधि श्रेष्ठान् महाबलान्। यत्क्लिश्यमानां प्रेक्षन्तेधर्मपत्नी यशस्विनीम्॥
en: I blame the Pandavas who are mighty and the foremost (heroes) in battle, for they (silently) looked at the cruel treatment that was offered to their renowned wedded wife.

sn: धिग् बलं भीमसेनस्य धिक् पार्थस्य च गाण्डिवम्। यौ मां विप्रकृतां क्षुद्रमर्षयेतां जनार्दन॥
en: O Janardana, fie to the prowess of Bhimasena and fie to the Gandiva of Arjuna, for they both suffered me to be thus disgraced by men of no importance!

sn: शाश्वतोऽयंधर्मपथः सद्भिराचरितः सदा। यद् भार्यां परिरक्षन्ति भर्तारोऽल्पबला अपि॥
en: This eternal course of morality is ever followed by the pious men, namely the husband, however weak he might be, should protect his wedded wife.

sn: भार्यायां रक्ष्यमाणायां प्रजा भवति रक्षिता। प्रजायां रक्ष्यमाणायामात्मा भवति रक्षितः॥
en: By protecting his wife one protects his offspring and by protecting the offspring one protects his own self.

sn: आत्मा हि जायते तस्यां तस्माज्जाया भवत्युत। भर्ता च भार्यया रक्ष्यः कथं जायान्ममोदरे॥
en: One's own self is begotten on one's wife and therefore wife is called Jaya. A wife should also protect her husband, remembering that he would take his birth in her womb.

sn: नन्विमे शरणं प्राप्तं न त्यजन्ति कदाचन। ते मां शरणमापन्नां नान्वपद्यन्त पाण्डवाः॥
en: The Pandavas never forsake the persons who ask for their protection, but they abandoned me who asked for their protection.

sn: पञ्चभिः पतिभिर्जाताः कुमारा मे महौजसः। एतेषामप्यवेक्षार्थं त्रातव्यास्मि जनार्दन॥
en: Five greatly powerful sons have been born of me by my five husbands; O Janardana, for their sake it was necessary to protect me.

sn: प्रतिविन्ध्यो युधिष्ठिरात् सुतसोमो वृकोदरात्। अर्जुनाच्छ्रुतकीर्तिश्च शतानीकस्तु नाकुलिः॥ कनिष्ठाच्छुतकर्मा च सर्वे सत्यपराक्रमाः। प्रद्युम्नो यादृशः कृष्ण तादृशास्ते महारथाः॥
en: Prativindhya (was begotten) by Yudhishthira, Satasoma by Vrikodara (Bhima), Shrutakirti by Arjuna, Satanika by Nakula. Shrutakarman by the youngest (of my husbands) Sahadeva. They are all of irrepressible prowess. O Krishna, they are all as great car-warriors as Pradyumna (Krishna's son).

sn: नन्विमेधनुषि श्रेष्ठा अजेया युधि शात्रवैः। किमर्थंधार्तराष्ट्राणां सहन्ते दुर्बलीयसाम्॥
en: They are all foremost of all bowmen and they are all invincible in battle by any foe. Why do they (silently) bear the wrongs inflicted (on me) by the weak sons of Dhritarashtra?

sn: अधर्मेण हृतं राज्यं सर्वे दासाः कृतास्तथा। सभायां परिकृष्टाहमेकवस्त्रा रजस्वला॥
en: Having been deprived of their kingdom by deception, the Pandavas were made slaves and I myself in my season and in one cloth was dragged into the Sabha.

sn: नाधिज्यमपि यच्छक्यं कर्तुमन्येन गाण्डिवम्। अन्यत्रार्जुनभीमाभ्यां त्वया वा मधुसूदन॥
en: O slayer of Madhu, fie to the Gandiva, which none else can string except Arjuna; Bhima and yourself!

sn: धिग् बलं भीमसेनस्य धिक् पार्थस्य च पौरुषम् यत्र दुर्योधनः कृष्ण मुहूर्तमपि जीवति॥
en: O Krishna, fie to the strength of Bhima and to the prowess to Partha (Arjuna) for Duryodhana lived for even a moment (after what he did).

sn: य एतानाक्षिपद् राष्ट्रात् सह मात्राविहिंसकान्। अधीयानान् पुरा बालान् व्रतस्थान् मधुसूदन॥
en: O slayer of Madhu, it was he who formerly drove the guileless Pandavas with their mother from the kingdom while they were but boys engaged in study and in the observance of their VOWS.

sn: भोजने भीमसेनस्य पापः प्राक्षेपयद् विषम्। कालकूटं नवं तीक्ष्णं सम्भूतं लोमहर्षणम्॥
en: It was that sinful wretch who mixed fresh, virulent, horrible and excessive poison with the food of Bhimasena.

sn: तज्जीर्णमविकारेण सहान्नेन जनार्दन। सशेषत्वान्महाबाहो भीमस्य पुरुषोत्तम॥
en: O Janardana, but Bhima without sustaining any injury digested that poison with the food. O mighty armed hero, O best of men, Bhima's days had not (then) ended.

sn: प्रमाणकोट्यां विश्वस्तं तथा सुप्तं वृकोदरम्। बद्ध्वैनं कृष्ण गङ्गायां प्रक्षिप्य पुरमाव्रजत्॥
en: O Krishna, it was Duryodhana, who at the house that stood by the banian tree, called Pramana, bound the sleeping and unsuspecting Bhima; and then throwing him into the Ganges, he returned to the city,

sn: यदा विबुद्धः कौन्तेयस्तदा संच्छिद्य बन्धनम्। उदतिष्ठन्महाबाहुर्भीमसेनो महाबलः॥
en: But the son of Kunti, the greatly strong and mighty armed Bhima, on waking from his sleep, tore his bonds and rose from the water.

sn: आशीविषैः कृष्णसीमसेनपदंशयत्। सर्वेष्वेवाङ्गदेशेषु च ममार च शत्रुहा॥
en: It was he (Duryodhana) who caused venomous snakes to bite all over the body of Bhimasena, but that slayer of foes did not die.

sn: प्रतिबुद्धस्तु कौन्तेयः सर्वान् सर्पानपोथयत्। सारथिं चास्य दयितमपहस्तेन जनिवान्॥
en: Awaking, the son of Kunti (Bhima) killed all the serpents with his left hand; and he killed his (Duryodhana's) favorite charioteer (also).

sn: पुनः सुप्तानुपाधाक्षीद् बालकान् वारणावते। शयानानार्यया साधु को नु तत् कर्तुमर्हति॥
en: Again, while the children (the Pandavas) were sleeping unsuspicious with the revered one (their mother), he set fire to the house (Jatugriha). Who is there who is capable of doing such an act?

sn: यत्रार्या रुदती भीता पाण्डवानिदमब्रवीत्। महद् व्यसनमापन्ना शिखिना परिवारिता॥
en: It was then the revered madam (Kunti), overtaken by this calamity and surrounded by the flames, began to cry in terrors.

sn: हा हतास्मि कुतोन्वद्य भवेच्छान्तिरिहानलात्। अनाथा विनशिष्यामि बालकैः पुत्रकैः सह॥
en: Kunti said: Alas, I am undone! How shall we today escape from this fire! Alas, I shall meet with detraction my sons who are but children!

sn: तत्र भीमो महाबाहुर्वायुवेगपराक्रमः। आर्यामाश्वासयामास भ्रातूंश्चापि वृकोदरः॥ वैनतेयो यथा पक्षी गरुत्मान् पततां वरः। तथैवाभिपतिष्यामि भयं वो नेह विद्यते॥
en: Draupadi said : Thereupon the mighty-armed Bhima Vrikodara whose prowess is like that of wind, comforted the revered madam (Kunti) and his brothers. I will spring up into the air like the son of Vinata that best of birds, Garuda. We have no fear from this fire.

sn: आर्यामथेन वामेन राजानं दक्षिणेन च। अंसयोश्च यमौ कृत्वा पृष्ठे बीभत्सुमेव च॥ सहसोत्पत्य वेगेन सर्वानादाय वीर्यवान्। भ्रातृनार्यां च बलवान् मोक्षयामास पावकात्॥
en: Then taking the revered lady (his mother) on his left flank and the king (Yudhishthira) on the right, the twins on each shoulder and Vivatsu (Arjuna) on his back. The powerful hero (Bhima), taking all of them, cleared off the fire at one leap and thus delivered his mother and brothers from the conflagration.

sn: ते रात्रौ प्रस्थिताः सर्वे सह मात्रा यशस्विनः। अभ्यगच्छन्महारण्ये हिडिम्बवनमन्तिकात्॥
en: Setting out that night with their illustrious mother, they (the Pandavas) came near the great forest, the forest of Hidimba.

sn: श्रान्ताः प्रसुप्तास्तत्रेमे मात्रा सह सुदुःखिताः। सुप्तांश्चैनानभ्यगच्छद्धिडिम्बा नाम राक्षसी॥
en: Fatigued and distressed they fell asleep with their mother. A Rakshasas woman, named Hidimba then came to them.

sn: सा दृष्ट्वा पाण्डवांस्तत्र सुप्तान् मात्रा सह क्षितौ हृच्छयेनाभिभूतात्मा भीमसेनमकामयत्॥
en: Seeing the Pandavas asleep on the ground with their mother and being influenced by desire, she sought to have Bhimasena as her lord.

sn: भीमस्य पादौ कृत्वा तु स्व उत्सङ्गे ततोऽबला। पर्यमर्दत् संहृष्टा कल्याणी मृदुपाणिना॥
en: That weak and blessed one (the Rakshasas woman), thereupon taking up Bhima's feet on her lap, began to press them with her soft hands.

sn: तामबुध्यदमेयात्मा बलवान् सत्यविक्रमः। पर्यपृच्छत तां भीमः किमिहेच्छस्यनिन्दिते॥
en: The immeasurably energetic, irrepressibly powerful and greatly strong Bhima then awoke and asked, “O faultless one, what do you wish (here)?"

sn: एवमुक्ता तु भीमेन राक्षसी कामरूपिणी। भीमसेनं महात्मानमाह चैवमनिन्दित॥
en: Having been thus addressed by Bhima, the faultless Rakshasas woman, who could assume any form at will, thus replied to the high-souled Bhimasena.

sn: पलायध्वमितः क्षिप्रं मम भ्रातैष वीर्यवान्। आगमिष्यति वो हन्तुं तस्माद् गच्छत मा चिरम्॥
en: "Speedily fly from this place; my powerful brother will (soon) come to kill you. Therefore speed away, do not stay here any longer."

sn: अथ भीमोऽभ्युवाचैनां साभिमानमिदं वचः। नोद्धिजेयमहं तस्मानिहनिष्येऽहपागतम्॥
en: Thereupon Bhima spoke thus in haughtiness, "I do not fear him. If he comes here, I shall kill him."

sn: तयोः श्रुत्वा तु संजल्पमागच्छद् राक्षसाधमः। भीमरूपो महानादान् विसृजन् भीमदर्शनः॥
en: Having heard their conversations, that worst of Rakshasas of fearful form and dreadful appearance uttered a loud cry as he came.

sn: राक्षस उवाच केन सार्धं कथयसि आनयैनं ममान्तिकम्। हिडिम्बे भक्षयिष्यामो न चिरं कर्तुमर्हसि॥
en: The Rakshasas said: O Hidimba, with whom are you talking? Bring him to me; I will eat hin up. You ought not to tarry.

sn: सा कृपासंगृहीतेन हृदयेन मनस्विनी। नैनमैच्छत् तदाख्यातुमनुक्रोशादनिन्दिता॥
en: Draupadi said : But move I by compassion. the faultless featured and pure hearted Rakshasas woman did not speak a word out of pity.

sn: स नादान् विनदन् घोरान् राक्षस: पुरुषादकः। अभ्यद्रवत वेगेन भीमसेनं तदा किल॥
en: Then the man-eating Rakshasas, uttering dreadful cries, rushed with great force at Bhimasena.

sn: तमभिदुत्त्य संक्रुद्धो वेगेन महता बली। अगृहणात् पाणिना पाणिं भीमसेनस्य राक्षसः॥ इन्द्राशनिसमस्पर्श वज्र संहननं दृढम्। संहत्य भीमसेनाय व्याक्षिपत् सहसा करम्॥
en: Coming furiously and angrily at him, the mighty Rakshasas caught hold of Bhimasena's hand by his own. Catching hold of his other hand and making it as hard as the thunder of Indra, he suddenly struck Bhima a blow that descended with the force of lightning.

sn: गृहीतं पाणिना पाणि भीमसेनस्य रक्षसा। नामृष्यत महाबाहुस्तत्राक्रुध्यद् वृकोदरः॥
en: His hand having been seized by the Rakshasas, the mighty-armed Vrikodara (Bhima), without being able to brook it, flew into rage.

sn: तदाऽऽसीत् तुमुलं युद्धं भीमसेनहिडिम्बयोः। सर्वास्त्रविदुषो?रं वृत्रवासवयोरिव॥
en: Then a fearful combat took place between Bhimasena and Hidimba, both skilled in all sorts of weapons, like the battle between Vasava (Indra) and Vritra.

sn: विक्रीड्य सुचिरं भीमो राक्षसेन सहानघ। निजघान महावीर्यस्तं तदा निर्बलं बली॥
en: O sinless one, after playing with (the strength of) the Rakshasas for a long time, the powerful and greatly energetic Bhima killed him when he became exhausted and weak.

sn: हत्वा हिडिम्बं भीमोऽथ प्रस्थितो भ्रातृभिः सह। हिडिम्बामग्रतः कृत्वा यस्यां जातो घटोत्कचः॥
en: Having thus killed Hidimba, Bhima proceeded with his brothers, placing Hidimba in their front, (Hidimba) of whom Ghatotkacha was born.

sn: ततः सम्प्राद्रवन् सर्वे सह मात्रा परंतपाः। एकचक्रामभिमुखाः संवृता ब्राह्मणव्रजैः॥
en: Thereupon all those chastisers of foes, accompanied by their mother and surrounded by many Brahmanas, proceeded towards Ekachakra.

sn: प्रस्थाने व्यास एषां च मन्त्री प्रियहिते रतः। ततोऽगच्छन्नेकचक्रां पाण्डवाः संशितव्रताः॥
en: In their this journey, Vyasa, ever engaged in their welfare, became their counsellor. Then the Pandavas of rigid vows, arriving at Ekachakra.

sn: तत्राप्यासादयामासुर्बकं नाम महाबलम्। पुरुषादं प्रतिभयं हिडिम्बेनैव सम्मितम्॥
en: Killed there a greatly strong man eating monster, named Baka, who was as terrible as Hidimba.

sn: तं चापि विनिहत्योचं भीमः प्रहरतां वरः। सहितो भ्रातृभिः सर्दुपदस्य पुरं ययौ॥
en: Having killed him, that foremost of smiters, Bhima, with all his brothers went to the capital of Drupada.

sn: लब्धाहमपि तत्रैव वसता सव्यसाचिना। यथा त्वया जिता कृष्ण रुक्मिणी भीष्मकात्मजा।११५॥
en: O Krishna, as you have obtained Rukmani, the daughter of Bhishmaka, so Savyasachi (Arjuna) obtained me while he lived there (at Draupada's capital).

sn: एवं सुयुद्धे पार्थेन जिताहं मधुसूदन। स्वयंवरे महत् कर्म कृत्वा न सुकरं परैः॥
en: O slayer of Madhu, I was thus obtained in the Saimvara by Partha (Arjuna) who performed a feat difficult of achievment by others and who fought with the assembled kings.

sn: एवं क्लेशैः सुबहुभिः क्लिश्यमाना सुदुःखिता। निवसाम्यार्यया हीना कृष्णधौम्यपुरःसरा॥
en: O Krishna, thus afflicted with numerous grief's, I am living in sorrow and in great distress with Dhaumya at our head, but deprived of the company of the revered lady (Kunti).

sn: त इमे सिंहविक्रान्ता वीर्येणाभ्यधिकाः परैः। विहीनैः परिक्लिश्यन्ती समुपैक्षन्त म कथम्॥
en: Why do these (Pandavas), who are gifted with strength and who possess the prowess of the lion, sit silently on seeing me afflicted by so despicable enemies (as the Kurus).

sn: एतादृशानि दुःखानि सहन्ती दुर्बलीयसाम्। दीर्घकालं प्रदीप्तास्मि पापानां पापकर्मणाम्॥
en: Suffering such wrongs at the hands of the sinful, evil-doing and weak foes, am I to suffer misery so long?

sn: कुले महति जातास्मि दिव्येन विधिना किला पाण्डवानां प्रिया भार्या स्नुषा पाण्डोर्महात्मनः॥
en: I was born in a great race and I came to the world in an extraordinary way. I am the beloved wife of the Pandavas and the daughterin-law of the illustrious Pandu.

sn: कचग्रहमनुप्राप्ता सास्मि कृष्ण वरा सती। पञ्चानां पाण्डुपुत्राणां प्रेक्षतां मधुसूदन॥
en: O Krishna, O slayer of Madhu, being the foremost of women and devoted to my husbands, even I was seized by the hair in the very sight of the Pandavas, each of whom was like an Indra.

sn: इत्युक्त्वा प्रारुदत् कृष्णा मुखं प्रच्छाद्य पाणिना। पद्मकोशप्रकाशेन मृदुना मृदुभाषिणी॥
en: Having said this, the mild-speeched Krishna (Draupadi) hid her face with her soft hands which were like the buds of lotus and began to weep.

sn: स्तनावपतितौ पीनौ सुजातौ शुभलक्षणौ। अभ्यवर्षत पाञ्चाली दुःखजैरश्रुबिन्दुभिः॥
en: The tears of the Panchala princess, the outpourings of her grief, washed her deep, plump and graceful breasts, which were crowned with auspicious marks.

sn: चक्षुषी परिमार्जन्ती निःश्वसन्ती पुनः पुनः। बाष्पपूर्णेन कण्ठेन क्रुद्धा वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Wiping her eyes and sighing frequently she thus spoke in anger and in a choked voice.

sn: नैव मे पतयः सन्ति न पुत्रा न च बान्धवाः। न भ्रातरो न च पिता नैव त्वं मधुसूदन॥
en: Draupadi said : O slayer of foes, husbands, sons, friends, brothers, father or you, I have none.

sn: ये मां विप्रकृतां क्षुद्रसपेक्षध्वं विशोकवत्। न च मे शाम्यते दुःखं कर्णो यत् प्राहसत् तदा।
en: For you all, seeing me treated so cruelly, by inferior foes, (still) sit unmoved in silence. My grief at Karna's ridicule is capable of being assuaged.

sn: चतुर्भिः कारणैः कृष्ण त्वया रक्ष्यास्मि नित्यशः। सम्बन्धाद् गौरवात् सख्यात् प्रभुत्वेनैव केशव॥
en: O Keshava, O Krishna, I always deserve to be protected by you for four reasons, namely for our relationship, for the respect you bear for me, for our friendship and for your lordship over me.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच अथ तामब्रवीत् कृष्णस्तस्मिन् वीरसमागमे।
en: Thereupon Krishna thus spoke to her in that assembly of heroes.

sn: वासुदेव उवाच रोदिष्यन्ति स्त्रियो ह्येव येषां क्रुद्धासि भाविनि। बीभत्सुशरसंच्छन्नाञ्छोणितौघपरिप्लुतान्॥ निहतान् वल्लभान् वीक्ष्य शयानान् वसुधातले। यत् समर्थं पाण्डवानां तत् करिष्यामि मा शुचः।।
en: Krishna said: O fair lady, the wives of those with whom you are angry will weep like you on seeing their husbands lying dead on the ground, their bodies covered with the arrows of Vivatsu and weltering in blood. Do not grieve; I shall do for the Pandavas whatever lies in my power.

sn: सत्यं ते प्रतिजानामि राज्ञां राज्ञी भविष्यसि। पतेद् द्यौर्हिमवाञ्छीर्येत् पृथिवी शकलीभवेत्॥ शुष्येत् तोयनिधिः कृष्णे न मे मोघं वचो भवेत्। तच्छ्रुत्वा द्रौपदी वाक्यं प्रतिवाक्यमथाच्युतात्॥ साचीकृतमवेक्षत् सा पाञ्चाली मध्यमं पतिम्। आबभाषे महाराज द्रौपदीमर्जुनस्तदा॥
en: I tell you the truth; you shall be the queen of kings. The heavens might fall and the Himalayas might split, the earth might be rent. And the waters of the ocean might be dried up, but, O Krishna (Draupadi), my words shall never be futile. Having heard these words of Achyuta (Krishna), as a reply to her, Draupadi. The princess of Panchala, glanced obliquely at her third husband (Arjuna). O great king, Arjuna then thus spoke to Draupadi.

sn: मा रोदीः शुभताम्राक्षि यदाह मधुसूदनः। तथा तद् भविता देवि नान्यथा वरवर्णिनी॥
en: O copper-colour-eyed lady, do not weep. What the slayer of Madhu (Krishna) has said will (surely) happen. O lady, O beautiful one, it cannot be otherwise.

sn: धृष्टद्युम्न उवाच अहं द्रोणं हनिष्यामि शिखण्डी तु पितामहम्। दुर्योधनं भीमसेनः कर्णं हन्ताधनंजयः॥ रामकृष्णौ व्यपाश्रित्य अजेयाः स्म रणे स्वसः। अपि वृत्रहणा युद्धे किं पुनधृतराष्ट्रजे॥
