en: You know also, O king, what conduces to our well-being; and wherever you wish, O great king, we shall fix our habitation.

description: The Pandava's entrance into the Dvaitavana
sn: इदं द्वैतवनं नाम सरः पुण्यजलोचितम्। बहुपुष्पफलं रम्यं नानाद्विजनिषेवितम्॥
en: Here is the lake called Dvyaitavana, resorted to by the pious, abounding in many flowers and fruits, charming and inhabited by birds of diverse species.

description: The Pandava's entrance into the Dvaitavana
sn: अत्रेपा द्वादश समा विहरेमेति रोचये। यदि तेऽनुमतं राजन् किमन्यन्मन्यते भवान्॥
en: If you please, O king, we would like to live here for twelve years; do you think otherwise?

description: The Pandava's entrance into the Dvaitavana
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच ममाप्येतन्मतं पार्थ त्वया यत् समुदाहृतम्। गच्छामः पुण्यविख्यातं महद् द्वैतवनं सरः॥
en: Yudhishthira said : I do fully approve of what you have said. O Partha, let us repair to that sacred and celebrated lake Dvyaitavana.

description: The Pandava's entrance into the Dvaitavana
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततस्ते प्रययुः सर्वे पाण्डवाधर्मचारिणः। ब्राह्मणैर्बहुभिः सार्धं पुण्यं द्वैतवनं सरः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Thereupon the pious sons of Pandu, followed by numberless Brahmanas all repaired to the holy lake Dvyaitavana.

description: The Pandava's entrance into the Dvaitavana
sn: ब्राह्मणाः साग्निहोत्राश्च तथैव च निरग्नयः। स्वाध्यायिनो भिक्षवश्च तथैव वनवासिनः॥ बहवो ब्राह्मणास्तत्र परिवव॒र्युधिष्ठिरम्। तप:सिद्धा महात्मानः शतशः संशितव्रताः॥
en: The Brahmanas, some offering sacrifice to the fire, some without it, some engaged in the study of the Vedas, some depending upon alms and some living in the forest, all these numberless Brahmanas as well as hundreds of Mahatamas of accomplished ascetic piety and hard austerities surrounded Yudhishthira.

description: The Pandava's entrance into the Dvaitavana
sn: ते यात्वा पाण्डवास्तत्र ब्राह्मणैर्बहुभिः सह। पुण्यं द्वैतवनं रम्यं विविशुर्भरतर्षभाः॥
en: And setting out with these numberless Brahmanas the Bharata chiefs, the sons of Pandu, entered the holy and the charming forest of Dvyaita.

description: The Pandava's entrance into the Dvaitavana
sn: कदम्बसर्जार्जुनकर्णिकारैः। तपात्यये पुष्पधरैरुपेतं महावनं राष्ट्रपतिर्ददर्श॥
en: The king saw that huge forest covered, at the end of summer, with Shalas palms, mangoes, Madhukas, Nipas, Kadambas, Sarjas, Arjunas, Karnikaras clothed with flowers;

description: The Pandava's entrance into the Dvaitavana
sn: मनोरमां वाचमुदीरयन्तः। स्तस्मिन् वने बर्हिणकोकिलाश्च॥
en: And peacocks, Datyuhas, Chakoras, Barhins and Kokilas sat on the top of the highest trees and emitted their sweet notes. saw

description: The Pandava's entrance into the Dvaitavana
sn: करेणुयूथैः सह यूथपानां मदोत्कटानामचलप्रभाणाम्। महान्ति यूथानि महाद्विपानां तस्मिन् वने राष्ट्रपतिर्ददर्श॥
en: In that forest the king (also) saw the leaders of elephant-herds, gigantic like hills with temporal juice trickling down in the season of rut and accompanied by herds of she-elephants.

description: The Pandava's entrance into the Dvaitavana
sn: मनोरमां भोगवतीमुपेत्य पूतात्मनां चीरजटाधराणाम्। तस्मिन् वनेधर्मभृतां निवासे ददर्श सिद्धर्षिगणाननेकान्॥
en: And approaching the picturesque Bhagavati (Sarasvati) he many ascetics of accomplished piety in that forest in the hermitages of pious (Rishis) of purified souls and wearing bark and matted-locks.

description: The Pandava's entrance into the Dvaitavana
sn: ततः स यानादवरुहा राजा सभ्रातृकः सजनः काननं तत्। स्त्रिविष्टपं शक्र इवामितौजाः॥
en: Thereupon descending from his chariot, the king, the foremost of the pious, with his brothers and followers, entered the forest like Indra of mincasurable prowess entering heaven.

description: The Pandava's entrance into the Dvaitavana
sn: दिदृक्षवश्चारणसिद्धसङ्घाः। वनौकसचापि नरेन्द्रसिंह मनस्विनं तं परिवार्य तस्थुः॥
en: With a view of seeing the truthful king many Charanas and Siddhas approached him; and the dwellers of the forest stood encircling that highly intelligent chief of kings.

description: The Pandava's entrance into the Dvaitavana
sn: स तत्र सिद्धानभिवाद्य सर्वान् प्रत्यर्चितो राजवद् देववच्च। विवेश सर्वैः सहितो द्विजावयैः कृताञ्जलिर्धर्मभृतां वरिष्ठः॥
en: Then saluting all the Siddhas and being adored by them in return like a king or a god, that foremost of the pious, accompanied by all the leading twice-born, entered (the forest).

description: The Pandava's entrance into the Dvaitavana
sn: स पुण्यशीलः पितृवन्महात्मा तपस्विभिर्धर्मपरैरुपेत्य प्रत्यर्चितः पुष्पधरस्य मूले महाद्रुमस्योपविवेश राजा॥
en: And being worshipped in return by those pious ascetics who had approached him that pious and high-souled king, sat down with them at the foot of a huge tree covered with flowers like her father Pandu in the days of yore.

description: The Pandava's entrance into the Dvaitavana
sn: भीमश्च कृष्णा चधनंजयश्च यमौ च ते चानुचरा नरेन्द्रम्। विमुच्य वाहानवशाश्च सर्वे तत्रोपतस्थुर्भरतप्रबर्हाः॥
en: Bhima, Krishna (Draupadi), Dhananjaya, the twins and all their retinue all wearied and leaving conveyances sat on all sides of that foremost of kings.

description: The Pandava's entrance into the Dvaitavana
sn: महाद्रुमः पञ्चभिरेवधन्विभिः। महागिरिर्वारणयूथपैरिव॥
en: The huge tree, bent down with the weight of creepers, with those five illustrious bowmen sitting under it for rest, appeared like a mountain with five gigantic elephants resting at its side.

description: The Pandava's entrance into the Dvaitavana
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तत् काननं प्राप्य नरेन्द्रपुत्राः सुखोचिता वासमुपेत्य कृच्छ्रम्। विजह्वरिन्द्रप्रतिमाः शिवेषु सरस्वतीशालवनेषु तेषु॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having arrived at that forest those princes resembling Indra, (formerly) used to happiness, (but now) labouring under misfortune, began to sport in that sacred forest of Shala trees washed by Sarasvati.

description: The Pandava's entrance into the Dvaitavana
sn: स्तस्मिन् वने मूलफलैरुदगः। द्विजातिमुख्यानृषभः कुरूणां संतर्पयामास महानुभावः॥
en: In that forest, that king, the foremost of the Kurus, began to please all the Yatis, Munis and all the leading Brahmanas by offering them excellent fruits and roots.

description: The Pandava's entrance into the Dvaitavana
sn: इष्टीश्च पित्र्याणि तथा क्रियाश्च महावने वसतां पाण्डवानाम्। पुरोहितस्तत्र समृद्धतेजाश्चकारधौम्यः पितृवन्नृपाणाम्॥
en: And their highly energetic priest Dhaumya, like a father, began to perforin for those Pandavas living in the forest, the sacrificial rites (in honour of their departed manes) of Ishti and Paitreya.

description: The Pandava's entrance into the Dvaitavana
sn: मृषिः पुराणोऽतिथिराजगाम। तमाश्रमं तीव्रसमृद्धतेजा मार्कण्डेयः श्रीमतां पाण्डवानाम्॥
en: The old Rishi Markandeya, of profuse and increasing energy, approached as a guest to the hermitage of the illustrious Pandavas who had repaired there on the loss of their kingdom.

description: The Pandava's entrance into the Dvaitavana
sn: तमागतं ज्वलितहुताशनप्रभं महामनाः कुरुवृषभो युधिष्ठिरः। अपूजयत् सुरऋषिमानवार्चितं महामुनि ह्यनुपमसत्त्ववीर्यवान्॥
en: The high-minded Kuru chief Yudhishthira of incomparable energy and prowess welcomed that great ascetic, who had come there gifted with the effulgence of blazing fire and worshipped by the celestials.

description: The Pandava's entrance into the Dvaitavana
sn: स सर्वविद् द्रौपदी वीक्ष्य कृष्णां युधिष्ठिरं भीमसेनार्जुनौ च। संस्मृत्य रामं मनसा महात्मा तपस्विमध्येऽस्मयतामितौजाः॥
en: Seeing Draupadi, Yudhishthira, Bhima and Arjuna in the midst of the ascetics, that illustrious and omniscient ascetic of incomparable prowess, smiled thinking of Rama in his mind.

description: The Pandava's entrance into the Dvaitavana
sn: तंधर्मराजो विमना इवाब्रवीत् सर्वे ह्रिया सन्ति तपस्विनोऽमी। स्तपस्विनां पश्यतां मामुदीक्ष्य॥
en: The pious Yudhishthira who was beside himself (with grief) said, “All these ascetics are sorry for seeing me here; why is it that you alone smile, as if in delight, before all these?"

description: The Pandava's entrance into the Dvaitavana
sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच न तात हृष्यामि न च स्पयामि प्रहर्षजो मां भजते न दर्पः। तवापदं त्वद्य समीक्ष्य राम सत्यव्रतं दाशरथिं स्मरामि॥
en: Markandeya said : I am not delighted, O my child, but I am struck with amazement; nor does haughtiness begotten of delight, possess me. Seeing your calamity to day I think of Dasharatha's son Rama of truthful vows.

description: The Pandava's entrance into the Dvaitavana
sn: स चापि राजा सह लक्ष्मणेन वने निवासं पितुरेव शासनात्। धन्वी चरन् पार्थ मयैव दृष्टो गिरेः पुरा ऋष्यमूकस्य सानौ॥
en: O son of Pritha, at the behest of his sire he (Rama) resided in the forest; I saw him in the days of yore wandering with his bow, at the summit of the mount Rishyamuka.

description: The Pandava's entrance into the Dvaitavana
sn: सहस्रनेत्रप्रतिमो महात्मा यमस्य नेता नमुचेश्च हन्ता। पितुर्निदेशादनघः स्वधर्म वासं वने दाशरथिश्चकार॥
en: The high-souled and innocent son of Dasharatha, resembling the thousand-eyed Deity, the lord of Yama and the slayer of Namuchi, lived in the forest at the command of his father and for the satisfaction of his duty.

description: The Pandava's entrance into the Dvaitavana
sn: स चापि शक्रस्य समप्रभावो महानुभावः समरेष्वजेयः। विहाय भोगानचरद् वनेषु नेशे बलस्येति चरेदधर्मम्॥
en: He was equal to Shakra in prowess, highminded and invincible in warfare, still he had to range the forest, renouncing pleasure; therefore none should act unrighteously thinking "I am powerful."

description: The Pandava's entrance into the Dvaitavana
sn: भूपाश्च नाभागभगीरथादयो महीमिमां सागरान्तां विजित्य। सत्येन तेऽप्यजयंस्तात लोकान् नेशे बलस्येति चरेदधर्मम्॥
en: Having conquered by truth this earth bounded by seas the kings headed by Nabhaga and Bhagiratha obtained, O my son, all the regions hereafter. Therefore, none should act unrighteously thinking "I am powerful."

description: The Pandava's entrance into the Dvaitavana
sn: अलर्कमाहुर्नरवर्य सन्तं सत्यव्रतं काशिकरूपराजम्। विहाय राज्यानि वसूनि चैव नेशे बलस्येति चरेदधर्मम्॥
en: O foremost of men, for forsaking his kingdom and wealth, the pious and truthful king of Kashi and Karusha was called a maddog. Therefore, none should act unrighteously thinking “I am powerful."

description: The Pandava's entrance into the Dvaitavana
sn: स्तं पूजयन्तो नरवय सन्तः। सप्तर्षयः पार्थ दिवि प्रभान्ति नेशे बलस्येति चरेदधर्मम्॥
en: O best of men, O son of Pritha, for satisfying the ordinances, laid down by the Creator himself in the Vedas, the seven pious Rishis shone brilliantly in the sky. Therefore, none should act unrighteously, thinking "I am powerful.”

description: The Pandava's entrance into the Dvaitavana
sn: महाबलान् पर्वतकूटमात्रान् विषाणिनः पश्य गजान् नरेन्द्र। नेशे बलस्येति चरेदधर्मम्॥
en: Behold, O king, O foremost of men, (even) the powerful elephants, having tusks as huge as the mountain tops, do not pass by the laws of the Creator. Therefore none should act unrighteously, thinking, 'I am powerful.'

description: The Pandava's entrance into the Dvaitavana
sn: सर्वाणि भूतानि नरेन्द्र पश्य तथा यथावद् विहितं विधात्रा। स्वयोनितः कर्म सदा चरन्ति नेशे बलस्येति चरेदधर्मम्॥
en: Behold, O king of men, all creatures act according to the laws (of their species) as laid down by the Creator. Therefore none should act unrighteously thinking, "I am powerful.”

description: The Pandava's entrance into the Dvaitavana
sn: सत्येनधर्मेण यथार्हवृत्त्या ह्रिया तथा सर्वभूतान्यतीत्य। यशश्च तेजश्च तवापि दीप्तं विभावसो स्करस्येव पार्थ॥
en: O son of Pritha, you have excelled all men in truth, piety, decorum and modesty; your fame and energy are brilliant as fire or the sun.

description: The Pandava's entrance into the Dvaitavana
sn: यथाप्रतिज्ञं च महानुभाव कृच्छ्रे वने वासमिमं निरुष्य। मादास्यसे पार्थिव कौरवेभ्यः॥
en: O great king, having spent the painful days of your exile in the forest as promised, you shall again snatch from the Kauravas your blazing prosperity by dint of your own energy.

description: The Pandava's entrance into the Dvaitavana
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच स्तपस्विमध्ये सहितं सुहृद्भिः। स्ततः प्रतस्थे दिशमुत्तरां सः॥
en: Vaishampayana said: Having addressed these words to him in the midst of the ascetics with friends the great Rishi saluting Dhaumya and all the Pandavas, proceeded towards the north.

description: The Pandava's entrance into the Dvaitavana
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच वसत्सु वै द्वैतवने पाण्डवेषु महात्मसु। अनुकीर्णं महारण्यं ब्राह्मणैः समपद्यत॥
en: Vaishampayana said : The high-minded Pandavas while residing in the forest of Dvaita that great forest was filled with Brahmanas.

description: The Pandava's entrance into the Dvaitavana
sn: ईर्यमाणेन सततं ब्रह्मघोषेण सर्वशः। ब्रह्मलोकसमं पुण्यमासीद् द्वैतवनं सरः॥
en: Resounding always and all over with the recitations of the Veda, the lake of the forest became as holy as the region of Brahma.

description: The Pandava's entrance into the Dvaitavana
sn: यजुषामृचां साम्नां च गद्यानां चैव सर्वशः। आसीदुच्चार्यमाणानां नि:स्वनो हृदयङ्गमः॥
en: The sounds of Yajus, Riks, Saman and other words uttered by the Brahmanas, were exceedingly charming.

description: The Pandava's entrance into the Dvaitavana
sn: ज्याघोषश्चैव पार्थानां ब्रह्मघोषश्चधीमताम्। संसृष्टं ब्रह्मणा क्षत्रं भूय एव व्यरोचत्॥
en: The Vedic recitations of the high-minded Brahmanas, mingling with twang of the bows of the sons of Pritha brought about a delightful union of the Brahmana and Kshatriya customs.

description: The Pandava's entrance into the Dvaitavana
sn: अथाब्रवीद् बको दालभ्योधर्मराज युधिष्ठिरम्। सध्यां कौन्तेयमासीनमृषिभिः परिवारितम्॥
en: Thereupon one evening (the Rishi) Baka of the Dalvya family addressed the son of Kunti, the pious king Yudhishthira seated in the midst of the Rishis.

description: The Pandava's entrance into the Dvaitavana
sn: पश्य द्वैतवने पार्थ ब्राह्मणानां तपस्विनाम्। होमवेलां कुरुश्रेष्ठ सम्प्रज्वलितपावकाम्॥
en: “Behold, O Partha, O Kuru chief, in this forest Dvaita the hour of the ascetic Brahmanas for performing Homa when the (sacred) fires have all been enkindled.

description: The Pandava's entrance into the Dvaitavana
sn: चरन्तिधर्मं पुण्येऽस्मिंस्त्वया गुप्ताधृतव्रताः। भृगवोऽङ्गिरसश्चैव वासिष्ठाः काश्यपैः सह॥ आगस्त्याश्च महाभागा आत्रेयाश्चोत्तमव्रताः। सर्वस्य जगतः श्रेष्ठा ब्राह्मणाः संगतास्त्वया।॥
en: Being protected by you, they of firm vows, are observing their religious rites in this sacred (forest). Bhrigu and Angiras together with Vasishtha and Kashyapa, the renowned sons of Agastya, the offspring of Atri, all of excellent vows, in face, all the leading Brahmanas of the world are united with you.

description: The Pandava's entrance into the Dvaitavana
sn: इदं तु वचनं पार्थ शृणुष्व गदतो मम। भ्रातृभिः सह कौन्तेय यत् त्वा वक्ष्यामि कौरव॥
en: O son of Pritha, O son of Kunti, O descendant of Kuru, hear along with your brothers what I speak to you.

description: The Pandava's entrance into the Dvaitavana
sn: ब्रह्म क्षत्रेण संसृष्टं क्षत्रं च ब्रह्मणा सह। उदीर्णे दहतः शत्रून् वनानीवाग्निमारुतौ॥
en: Brahima-energy combined with Kshatriyaenergy, Brahma-prowess united with Kshatriya-prowess, when rendered strong, might consume the enemies as fire united with the wind consumes the forest.

description: The Pandava's entrance into the Dvaitavana
sn: दिच्छन्निमं लोकममुं च जेतुम्। विनीतधर्मार्थमपेतमोहं लब्ध्वा द्विजं नुदति नृपः सपत्नान्॥
en: O my son, O king, one should never be without a Brahmana, if he wished to conquer this world and the next for long. Having got a Brahmana, well-versed in religion and worldly affairs and cleansed of passion and folly a king destroys his enemies.

description: The Pandava's entrance into the Dvaitavana
sn: चरन् नैःश्रेयसंधर्म प्रजापालनकारितम्। नाध्यगच्छद् बलिलकि तीर्थमन्यत्र वै द्विजात्॥
en: Having governed his subjects, the King Bali performed those duties that lead to salvation and did not know of any other means in this world than the Brahmanas.

description: The Pandava's entrance into the Dvaitavana
sn: वैरोचनेः श्रीरपि चाक्षयाऽऽसीत्। लब्वा महीं ब्राह्मणसम्प्रयोगात् तेष्वाचरन् दुष्टमथो व्यनश्यत्॥
en: It was for this, that all the desires of the Asura (Bali) Virochana's son, were satisfied and his wealth was even inexhaustible. Having obtained (the entire) carth through the instrumentality of the Brahmanas, he met with destruction when he began to oppress (people).

description: The Pandava's entrance into the Dvaitavana
sn: वर्णं द्वितीयं भजते चिराय। समुद्रनेमिनमते तु तस्मै यं ब्राह्मणः शास्ति नयैर्विनीतम्॥
en: The earth with her wealth, never worships him for long, as her lord, who is without a Brahmana. The earth however surrounded by the sea worships him who is governed by a Brahmana and is instructed by him regarding his duties.

description: The Pandava's entrance into the Dvaitavana
sn: कुञ्जरस्येव संग्रामे परिगृह्याङ्कुशग्रहम्। ब्राह्मणैर्विप्रहीणस्य क्षत्रस्य क्षीयते बलम्॥
en: Like an elephant without a driver in battle, the strength of a Kshatriya, without a Brahmana, decreases.

description: The Pandava's entrance into the Dvaitavana
sn: ब्राह्मण्यनुपमा दृष्टिः क्षात्रमप्रतिमं बलम्। तौ यदा चरतः सार्धं तदा लोकः प्रसीदति॥
en: Incomparable is the sight of a Brahmana and the might of a Kshatriyas; when they proceed in unision the whole world is delighted.

description: The Pandava's entrance into the Dvaitavana
sn: यथा हि सुमहानग्निः कक्षं दहति सानिलः। तथा दहति राजन्यो ब्राह्मणेन समं रिपुम्॥
en: As fire rendered stronger by the win destroys straw and woo, so kings united with Brahmanas destroy (all their) enemies.

description: The Pandava's entrance into the Dvaitavana
sn: ब्राह्मणेष्वेव मेधावी बुद्धिपर्येषणं चरेत्। अलब्धस्य च लाभाय लब्धस्य परिवृद्धये॥
en: An intelligent man, for acquiring what he has not got and for multiplying what he has got, should take the advice of the Brahmanas.

description: The Pandava's entrance into the Dvaitavana
sn: अलब्धलाभाय च लब्धवृद्धये यथार्हतीर्थप्रतिपादनाय यशस्विनं वेदविदं विपश्चितं बहुश्रुतं ब्राह्मणमेव वासय॥
en: Therefore for obtaining what you have not got and multiplying what you have got and for spending that on proper objects and persons, do keep with you a Brahmana of fame, wise, experienced and well-versed in the knowledge of the Vedas.

description: The Pandava's entrance into the Dvaitavana
sn: ब्राह्मणेषूत्तमा वृत्तिस्तव नित्यं युधिष्ठिर। तेन ते सर्वलोकेषु दीप्यते प्रथितं यशः॥
en: O Yudhishthira, you have always highly respected the Brahmanas, it is for this that your reputation shines brilliantly in the three worlds.

description: The Pandava's entrance into the Dvaitavana
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततस्ते ब्राह्मणाः सर्वे बकं दाल्भ्यमपूजयन्। युधिष्ठिरे स्तूयमाने भूयः सुमनसोऽभवन्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Then all the Brahinanas, who were with Yudhishthira, adored Baka of Dalvya family; and hearing him eulogize Yudhishthira they were greatly delighted.

description: The Pandava's entrance into the Dvaitavana
sn: द्वैपायनो नारदश्च जामदग्न्यः पृथुश्रवाः। इन्द्रद्युम्नो भालुकिश्च कृतचेताः सहस्रपात्॥ कर्णश्रवाश्च मुञ्जश्च लवणाश्वश्च काश्यपः। हारीतः स्थूणकर्णश्च अग्निवेश्योऽथ शौनकः॥ कृतवाक् च सुवाक् चैव बृहदश्वो विभावसुः। ऊर्ध्वरेतो वृषामित्रः सुहोत्रो होत्रवाहनः॥ एते चान्ये च बहवो ब्राह्मणाः संशितव्रतः। अजातशत्रुमानचुः पुरंदरमिवर्षयः॥
en: Dvaipayana, Narada, Jamadagni, Pithushrava, Indradyumna, Bhalaki, Kritachetas, Sahasrapat, Karnasravas, Munja, Lavanashva, Kashyapa, Harita, Sthulakarna, Agnivishya, Saunaka, Kritavak, Suvak, Vrihadashya, Vibhavasu, Urdharetas, Vrishamitra, Suhotra, Hotravahana, all these and many other Brahmanas of firm vows worshipped Yudhishthira like celestials sages worshipping Purandara in the celestials region.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततो वनगता: पार्थाः सायाह्ने सह कृष्णया। उपविष्टाः कथाश्चक्रुर्दुःखशोकपरायणाः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Thereupon the sons of Pritha with Draupadi banished to the forest, sat one evening, stricken with grief and sorrow and began to talk with one another.

sn: प्रिया च दर्शनीया च पण्डिता च पतिव्रता। अथ कृष्णाधर्मराजमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: The beloved, beautiful, learned and faithful Draupadi addressed, the following words to the pious king (Yudhishthira).

sn: द्रौपद्युवाच न नूनं तस्य पापस्य दुःखमस्मासु किंचन। विद्यतेधार्तराष्ट्रस्य नृशंसस्य दुरात्मनः॥
en: Draupadi said : No feeling for us exists in the mind of that vile, vicious-souled and cruel son of Dhritarashtra.

sn: यस्त्वां वां राजन् मया सार्धमजिनैः प्रतिवासितम्। वनं प्रस्थाप्य दुष्टात्मा नान्वतप्यत दुर्मतिः॥
en: For, that vicious-minded one, O king, having sent you along with me to the forest clad in deer-skin, feels no mortification.

sn: आयसं हृदयं नूनं तस्य दुष्कृतकर्मणः। यस्त्वांधर्मपरं श्रेष्ठं रूक्षाण्यश्रावयत् तदा॥
en: For, the heart of that one of impious deed is made of steel since he could address harsh words to his pious eldest brother.

sn: सुखोचितमदुःखाहँ दुरात्मा ससुहृद्गणः। ईदृशं दुःखमानीय मोदते पापपूरुषः॥
en: Having brought you, who are used to happiness, to such a miserable plight that vicious-souled wretch delights with his friends.

sn: चतुर्णामेव पापानामा न पतितं तदा। त्वयि भारत निष्क्रान्ते वनायाजिनवाससि॥ दुर्योधनस्य कर्णस्य शकुनेश्च दुरात्मनः। दुर्धातुस्तस्य चोचस्य राजन् दुःशासनस्य च॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, O king, when clad in deer-skin you set out for the forest, only four vicious wights did not shed tears; Duryodhona, Karna, the evil-minded Shakuni and the fierce and vicious brother Dushashana.

sn: इतरेषां तु सर्वेषां कुरूणां कुरुसत्तम्। दुःखेनाभिपरीतानां नेत्रेभ्यः प्राप्तज्जलम्॥
en: O foremost of the Kurus, the other Kurus filled with sorrow, shed tears from their eyes.

sn: इदं च शयनं दृष्ट्वा यच्चासीत् ते पुरातनम्। शोचामि त्वां महाराज दुःखान/ सुखोचितम्॥
en: O great king, seeing this your bed and recollecting what you had before I grieve for you, who do not deserve misery and have been brought up in every luxury.

sn: दान्तं यच्च सभामध्य आसनं रत्नभूषितम्। दृष्ट्वा कुशवृषी चेमा शोको मां प्रदहत्ययम्॥
en: Thinking of that ivory seat in your court crested with jewels and seeing this scat of Kusha grass grief assails me.

sn: यदपश्यं सभायां त्वां राजभिः परिवारितम्। तच्च राजन्नपश्यन्त्याः का शान्तिर्हदयस्य मे॥
en: I saw you in your court surrounded by the kings; seeing you without kings how can my mind have peace?

sn: या त्वाहं चन्दनादिग्धमपश्यं सूर्यवर्चसम्। सा त्वां पङ्कमलादिग्धं दृष्ट्वा मुह्यामि भारत॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, I am beside myself on seeing you pasted with mud, you, gifted with the effulgence of sun whom I saw before pasted with sandal.

sn: या त्वाहं कौशिकैर्वस्त्रैः शुभैराच्छादितं पुरा। दृष्टवत्यस्मि राजेन्द्र सा त्वां पश्यामि चीरिणम्॥
en: O king of kings, I see you now clad in bark, whom I saw before clothed in white silken raiment.

sn: यच्च तदुक्मपात्रीभिर्ब्राह्मणेभ्यः सहस्रशः। ह्रियते ते गृहादन्नं संस्कृतं सार्वकामिकम्॥
en: (Formerly) pure food of every kind was taken from your house, on golden plates to thousands of Brahmanas.

sn: यतीनामगृहाणां ते तथैव गृहमेधिनाम्। दीयते भोजनं राजन्नतीवगुणवत् प्रभो॥
en: O lord, best food was given by you to ascetics, the houseless and those leading domestic lives, like an accomplished king.

sn: सत्कृतानि सहस्राणि सर्वकामैः पुरा गृहे। सर्वकामैः सुविहितैर्यदपूजयथा द्विजान्॥
en: Formerly living in your palace you had thousands of plates filled with every kind of food and used to worship the Brahmana, satisfying every desire of theirs.

sn: तच्च राजन्नपश्यन्त्याः का शान्तिर्हदयस्य मे। यत् ते भ्रातृन् महाराज युवानो मृष्टकुण्डलाः॥ अभोजयन्त मिष्टान्नैः सूदाः परमसंस्कृतैः। सर्वांस्तानद्य पश्यामि वने वन्येन जीविनः॥ अदुःखार्हान् मनुष्येन्द्र नोपशाम्यति मे मनः। भीमसेनमिमं चापि दुःखितं वनवासिनम्॥ ध्यायत: किं न मन्युस्ते प्राप्ते काले विवर्धते। भीमसेनं हि कर्माणि स्वयं कुर्वाणमन्युतम्॥ सुखा/ दुःखितं दृष्ट्वा कस्मान्मन्युर्न वर्धते।
en: Not beholding all these, how can my heart, O king have peace! Thy youthful brothers, adorned with ear-rings, were formerly treated by cooks with sweat and skillfully prepared dishes-I now behold them all, unused to misery, in the forest living on the produces of the forest. My mind finds no peace, O lord of men. Beholding this Bhimasena sorry and living in forest and thinking over this, does not your mind in proper time become wrathful, Bhimasena who used to perforin all actions unaided.

sn: सत्कृतं विविधैर्यानैर्वस्त्रैरुच्चावचैस्तथा॥ तं ते वनगतं दृष्ट्वा कस्मान्मन्युर्न वर्धते।
en: Beholding him stricken with sorrow who was used to all happiness, surrounded by numerous conveyances and clothed in costly raiment, why does not your anger blaze up?

sn: अयं कुरून् रणे सर्वान् हन्तुमुत्सहते प्रभुः॥ त्वत्प्रतिज्ञा प्रतीक्षस्तु सहतेऽयं वृकोदरः।
en: Beholding him in the forest why does not your anger blaze up, this great one is prepared to slay all Kurus in battle. In honour of your promise Vrikodara bears all this.

sn: योऽर्जुनेनार्जुनस्तुल्यो द्विबाहुर्बहुबाहुना॥ शरावमर्दे शीघ्रत्वात् कालान्तकयमोपमः। यस्य शस्त्रप्रतापेन प्रणताः सर्वपार्थिवाः॥ यज्ञे तव महाराज ब्राह्मणानुपतस्थिरे। तमिमं पुरुषव्याघ्र पूजितं देवदानवैः॥ ध्यायन्तमर्जुनं दृष्ट्वा कस्माद् राजन् न कुप्यसि।
en: O King, this Arjuna though possessed of two hands is equal to Arjuna of a thousand arms for light handedness in discharging arrows; he is equal to Yama at the end of Yuga; humbled by the prowess of whose weapons all the kings. Waited upon the Brahmanas in your sacrifice, O great king, beholding this foremost of men worshipped of Devas and Danavas. Arjuna stricken with anxiety, does not your mind become worked with anger?

sn: दृष्ट्वा वनगतं पार्थमदुःखार्ह सुखोचितम्॥ न च ते वर्धते मन्युस्तेन मुह्यामि भारत।
en: O king, beholding Partha used to happiness and unworthy of misery, living in the forest. Your anger is not excited, I am stricken with wonder for this.

sn: यो देवांश्च मनुष्यांश्च सर्वांश्चैकरथोऽजयत्॥ तं ते वनगतं दृष्ट्वा कस्मान्मन्युर्न वर्धते।
en: O Bharata, who mounted on a single car, vanquished men and serpents. Beholding him in the forest why is not your anger excited?

sn: यो यानैरद्धृताकारैर्हयैर्नागैश्च संवृतः॥ प्रसह्य वित्तान्यादत्त पार्थिवेभ्यः परंतप। क्षिपत्येकेन वेगेन पञ्चबाणशतानि यः॥ तं ते वनगतं दृष्ट्वा कस्मान्मन्युर्न वर्धते।
en: He was honoured with the present of various vehicles, horses and elephants; he, the slayer of foes, wrested wealth by force from various other kings and discharges with one velocity hundreds of shafts; is not your mind worked up with ire beholding him in exile?

sn: श्यामं बृहन्तं तरुणं चर्मिणामुत्तमं रणे॥ दृष्ट्वा कस्मान्मन्युर्न वर्धते। नकुलं ते वने
en: Beholding him fair, able-bodied, youthful and the best of swordsmen. Nakula in exile does not your anger blaze up?

sn: दर्शनीयं च शूरं च माद्रीपुत्रं युधिष्ठिर॥ सहदेवं वने दृष्ट्वा कस्मात् क्षमसि पार्थिव।
en: Beholding, O Yudhishthira, O king, the heroic and handsome son of Madri, Sahadeva, in exile do you forgive (them)?

sn: नकुलं सहदेवं च दृष्ट्वा ते दुःखितावुभौ॥ अदुःखार्ही मनुष्येन्द्र कस्मान्मन्युर्न वर्धते।
en: Beholding, O king of men, these Nakula and Sahadeva, unworthy of misery, stricken with grief does not your anger blaze up?

sn: दुपदस्य कुले जातां स्नुषां पाण्डोर्महात्मनः॥ धृष्टद्युम्नस्य भगिनीं वीरपत्नीमनुव्रताम्। मां वै वनगतां दृष्ट्वा कस्मात् क्षमसि पार्थिव॥
en: Beholding me in the forest born in the race of Drupada, the daughter-in-law of the great Pandu, sister of Dhristadyumna, the devoted spouse of a heroes, do you forgive them, O king?

sn: नूनं च तव वै नास्ति मन्युर्भरतसत्तम्। यत् ते भ्रातूंश्च मां चैव दृष्ट्वा न व्यथते मनः॥
en: Forsooth, O foremost of Bharatas, you have no anger, since beholding me and your brothers your mind is not pained.

sn: न निर्मन्युः क्षत्रियोऽस्ति लोके निर्वचनं स्मृतम्। तदद्य त्वयि पश्यामि क्षत्रिये विपरीतवत्॥
en: This is the saying of Smriti, that in this world there is not a Kshatriya who is without anger, but in you do I behold today the contradiction.

sn: यो न दर्शयते तेजः क्षत्रियः काल आगते। सर्वभूतानि तं पार्थ सदा परिभवन्त्युत॥
en: The Kshatriya who does not manifest his energy in proper hour is disregarded by all creatures, O son of Pritha.

sn: तत् त्वया न क्षमा कार्या शत्रुन् प्रति कथंचन। तेजसैव हि ते शक्या निहन्तुं नात्र संशयः॥
en: Therefore you should by no means, vouchsafe your forgiveness to the enemies; forsooth, by your energy you may destroy them all.

sn: तथैव यः क्षमाकाले क्षत्रियो नोपशाम्यति। अप्रियः सर्वभूतानां सोऽमुत्रेह च नश्यति॥
en: So that Kshatriya too becomes unpopular with all and meets with destruction both in this world and in the next, whose anger is not appeased when the time for forgiveness comes.

sn: द्रौपद्युवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। प्रह्लादस्य च संवादं बलेर्वैरोचनस्य च।।।।
en: Draupadi said : On this is cited as an example the ancient history relating to the conversation between Prahlada and Vali the son of Virochana.

sn: असुरेन्द्रं महाप्राज्ञंधर्माणामागतागमम्। बलिः पप्रच्छ दैत्येन्द्र प्रह्लादं पितरं पितुः॥
en: One day, Bali accosted his grandfather Prahlada, the king of Asuras and Danava, endued with great wisdom and well-versed in duties (saying).

sn: बलिरुवाच क्षमा स्विच्छ्रेयसी तात उताहो तेज इत्युत। एतन्मे संशयं तात यथावद् ब्रूहि पृच्छते॥
en: Vali said : Does forgiveness lead to well-being, O father or prowess or energy? I have great doubt in this; father, tell me who am asking you.

sn: श्रेयो यदत्रधर्मज्ञ ब्रूहि मे तदसंशयम्। करिष्यामि हि तत् सर्वं यथावदनुशासनम्॥
en: Tell me, without any doubt, O you conversant with duties, whatever leads to wellbeing. I shall obey duly all your commands.

sn: तस्मै प्रोवाच पृष्टः पितामहः। सर्वनिश्चयवित् प्राज्ञः संशयं परिपृच्छते॥
en: Draupadi said : Being thus accosted the wise grandfather, conversant with all truths, replied at length for the removal of his doubts.

sn: तत् सर्वमेवं प्रह्लाद उवाच न श्रेयः सततं तेजो न नित्यं श्रेयसी क्षमा। इति तात विजानीहि द्वयमेतदसंशयम्॥
en: Prahlada said: Do you learn, my son, these two truths without any doubt neither does prowess always lead to well-being nor does forgiveness.

sn: यो नित्यं क्षमते तथा बहून् दोषान् स विन्दति। भृत्याः परिभवन्त्येनमुदासीनास्तथारयः॥ सर्वभूतानि चाप्यस्य न नमन्ति कदाचन। तस्मान्नित्यं क्षमा तात पण्डितैरपि वर्जिता।।।
en: He who forgives always, O my son, suffers many evils-servants, strangers and enemies always disregard him. No one does ever bow to him; perpetual forgiveness therefore, O my son, is avoided by the learned.

sn: अवज्ञाय हि तं भृत्या भजन्ते बहुदोषताम्। आदातुं चास्य वित्तानि प्रार्थयन्तेऽल्पचेतसः॥
en: Disregarding him his servants contract many vicious habits; all those evil-minded men try to deprive him of his wealth.

sn: यानं वस्त्राण्यलंकाराञ्छयनान्यासनानि च। भोजनान्यथ पानानि सर्वोपकरणानि च॥ आददीरनधिकृता यथाकाममचेतसः। प्रदिष्टानि च देयानि न दद्युभर्तृशासनात्॥ न चैनं भर्तृपूजाभिः पूजयन्ति कथंचन। अवज्ञानं हि लोकेऽस्मिन् मरणादपि गर्हितम्॥१२
en: Those vicious servants also appropriate to themselves nis conveyances, clothes ornaments, dress, beds, seats, food, drink and other articles of use. They do not at the behest of their master, give to others things they are commanded to do, Nor do they treat their master with that respect which is his due. Disregard in this world is worse than death.

sn: क्षमिणं तादृशं तात ब्रुवन्ति कटुकान्यपि। प्रेष्याः पुत्राश्च भृत्याश्च तथोदासीनवृत्तयः॥
en: O my child, sons, servants attendants and even strangers use harsh words to such a forgiving person.

sn: अथास्य दारानिच्छन्ति परिभूय क्षमावतः। दाराश्चास्य प्रवर्तन्ते यथाकाममचेतसः॥
en: Disregarding him even they wish to have the wife of a forgiving person and his wife too does whatever she likes.

sn: तथा च नित्यमुदिता यदि नाल्पमपीश्वरात्। दण्डमर्हन्ति दुष्यन्ति दुष्टाश्चाप्यपकुर्वते॥
en: The pleasure-loving servants, if a slight punishment is not meted out to them, contract all sorts of vices and the wicked always injure such a master.

sn: एते चान्ये च बहवो नित्यं दोषाः क्षमावताम्। अथ वैरोचने दोषानिमान् विद्वयक्षमावताम॥
en: These and various other evils attend always upon the forgiving. Listen, O son of Virochana, to (other) evils that beset a person that never forgives.

sn: अस्थाने यदि वा स्थाने सततं रजसाऽऽवृतः। क्रुद्धो दण्डान् प्रणयति विविधान् स्वेन तेजसा॥ मित्रैः सह विरोधं प्राप्नुते तेजसाऽऽवृतः। आप्नोति द्वेष्यतां चैव लोकात् स्वजनतस्तथा॥
en: If an angry person, always beset by the quality of darkness, inflicts punishments, by this own energy, upon deserving and nondeserving persons, he is alienated from his friends and hated by outsiders as well as his own relations.

sn: सोऽवमानादर्थहानिमुपालम्भमनादरम्। संतापद्वेषमोहांश्च शत्रूश्च लभते नरः॥
en: Such a man who insults others is subject to loss of wealth, disregard, misery and hatred and creates enemies.

sn: क्रोधाद् दण्डान्मनुष्येषु विविधान् पुरुषोऽनयात्। भ्रश्यते शीघ्रमैश्वर्यात् प्राणेभ्यः स्वजनादपि॥
en: A man, in anger, inflicts various punishments upon people and is soon deprived of his wealth, life and even kinsmen.

sn: योपकर्तश्च हर्तश्च तेजसैवोपगच्छति। तस्मादुद्विजते लोकः सर्पाद् वेश्मगतादिव॥
en: People are afraid of him who abuses his power equally upon his benefactor and enemy, as the inmates of a house are of a snake.

sn: यस्मादुद्विजते लोकः कथं तस्य भवो भवेत्। अन्तरं तस्य दृष्टैव लोको विकुरुतेध्रुवम्॥
en: How can good betide him of whom the people are afraid-forsooth do the people injure him as soon as they find a hole.

sn: तस्मान्नात्युत्सृजेत् तेजो न च नित्यं मृदुर्भवेत्। काले काले तु सम्प्राप्ते मृदुस्तीक्ष्णोऽपि वा भवेत्।२३।।
en: Therefore people should not be always angry or mild; they should exhibit their anger or mildness in proper hours.

sn: काले मृदुर्यो भवति काले भवति दारुणः। स वै सुखमवाप्नोति लोकेऽमुष्मिन्निहैव च॥
en: He, who is forgiving in proper hour and angry when the occasion arises, attains to happiness both in this world and in the next.

sn: क्षमाकालांस्तु वक्ष्यामि शृणु मे विस्तरेण तान्। ये ते नित्यमसंत्याज्या यथा प्राहुर्मनीषिणः॥
en: Hear, I shall now describe to you the hours of forgiveness as pointed out by the learned and which should always be followed.

sn: पूर्वोपकारी यस्ते स्यादपराधे गरीयसि। उपकारेण तत् तस्य क्षन्तव्यमपराधिनः॥
en: If your former benefactor commits a heinous offence you should forgive him considering his former benefaction.

sn: अबुद्धिमाश्रितानां तु क्षन्तव्यमपराधिनाम्। न हि सर्वत्र पाण्डित्यं सुलभं पुरुषेण वै॥
en: Those that commit an offence out of ignorance or foolishness should be forgiven-for people cannot always easily attain to learning.

sn: अथ चेद् बुद्धिजं कृत्वा ब्रूयुस्ते तदबुद्धिजम्। पापान् स्वल्पेऽपि तान् हन्यादपराधे तथानृजून्॥
en: Those crooked men, who having committed an offence wittingly plead ignorance should be punished even if their offence by trifling.

sn: सर्वस्यैकोऽपराधस्ते क्षन्तव्यः प्राणिनो भवेत्। द्वितीये सति वध्यस्तु स्वल्पेऽप्यपकृते भवेत्॥
en: The first offence of all men should be forgiven; when they commit the second, however insignificant it might be they should be punished.

sn: अजानता भवेत् कश्चिदपराधः कृतो यदि। क्षन्तव्यमेव तस्याहुः सुपरीक्ष्य परीक्षया॥
en: If a person unknowingly commits an offence-he should be pardoned, it is said, after having made a proper enquiry.

sn: मृदुना दारुणं हन्ति मृदुना हन्त्यदारुणम्। नासाध्यं मृदुना किंचित् तस्मात् तीव्रतरं मृदु॥
en: Strength might be vanquished by forgiveness, weakness might be vanquished by forgiveness; there is nothing which forgiveness cannot accomplish, therefore forgiveness is truly fiercer.

sn: देशकालौ तु सम्प्रेक्ष्य बलाबलमथात्पनः। नादेशकाले किंचित् स्याद् देशकालौ प्रतीक्षताम् तथा लोकभयाच्चैव क्षन्तव्यमपराधिनः॥
en: Considering his own strength or weakness one should act with reference to time or place; nothing is successful that is not taken in hand with reference to time or place; therefore wait for place or time; sometimes, offenders should be forgiven for fear of people.

sn: एत एवंविधाः कालाः क्षमायाः परिकीर्तिताः। अतोऽन्यथानुवर्तत्सु तेजसः काल उच्यते॥
en: These have been described as the proper hours of forgiveness; and at other times besides these one should exhibit his prowess.

sn: तदहं तेजसः कालं तव मन्ये नराधिप। धार्तराष्ट्रेषु लुब्धेषु सततं चापकारिषु॥
en: I therefore consider, O king, this to be the time when you should display your might to the avaricious sons of Dhritarashtra who always injure others.

sn: न हि कश्चित् क्षमाकालो विद्यतेऽद्य कुरून् प्रति। तेजसश्चागते काले तेज उत्स्रष्टुमर्हसि॥
en: This is not the time for showing forgiveness towards the Kurus; when the hour for showing might arrives, it behoves you to display it.

sn: मृदुर्भवत्यवज्ञातस्तीक्ष्णादुद्विजते जनः। काले प्राप्ते द्वयं चैतद् यो वेद स महीपतिः॥
en: The humble and forgiving person is always neglected; while those that are powerful assail others; he is the king who takes recourse to both in proper time.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच क्रोधो हन्ता मनुष्याणां क्रोधो भावयिता पुनः। इति विद्धि महाप्राज्ञे क्रोधमूलौ भवाभवौ॥
en: Yudhishthira said: Anger is the destroyer of mankind and anger again places them in prosperity; consider, therefore, O highly-intelligent lady, that anger is the root of prosperity and adversity.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: यो हि संहरते क्रोधं भवस्तस्य सुशोभने। वः पुनः पुरुषः क्रोधं नित्यं न सहते शुभे। तस्याभावाय भवथि क्रोधः परमदारुणः॥
en: Prosperity crown him, O beautiful lady, who destroys anger; and the greatly terrible anger brings on his adversity who cannot always control it, O fair one.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: क्रोधमूलो विनाशो हि प्रजानामिह दृश्यते। तत् कथं मादृशः क्रोधमुत्सृजेल्लोकनाशनम्॥
en: Anger is in this world, the root of the destruction of mankind; how can, one like me indulge in anger which brings about the destruction of the world?

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: क्रुद्धः पापं नरः कुर्यात् क्रुद्धो हन्याद् गुरूनपि। क्रुद्धः परुषया वाचा श्रेयसोऽप्यवमन्यते॥
en: The angry man commits a sin; the angry man murders his preceptor; the angry man insults his elders with harsh words.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: वाच्यावाच्ये हि कुपितो न प्रजानाति कर्हिचित्। नाकार्यमस्ति क्रुद्धस्य नावाच्यं विद्यते तथा॥
en: The angry man cannot distinguish what should be and should not be said by him; there is nothing which cannot be said or done by an angry man.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: हिंस्यात् क्रोधादवध्यांस्तु वध्यान् सम्पूजयीत च आत्मानमपि च क्रुद्धः प्रेषयेद् यमसादनम्॥
en: From anger a man may kill one who should not be killed and adore one that should be slain, an angry man may even dispatch his own self to the abode of Yama.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: एतान् दोषान् प्रपश्यद्भिर्जितः क्रोधो मनीषिभिः। इच्छद्भिः परमं श्रेय इह चामुत्र चोत्तमम्॥
en: Beholding these evils, anger is conquered by one desirous of excellent well-being both in this world and in the next.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: तं क्रोधं वर्जितंधीरैः कथमस्मद्विधश्चरत्। एतद् द्रौपदि संधाय न मे मन्युः प्रवर्धते॥
en: Why should persons like myself indulge in that anger which has been controlled by persons of tranquil mind; thinking this, O Draupadi, my anger is not excited.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: आत्मानं च परांश्चैव त्रायते महतो भयात्। क्रुध्यन्तमप्रतिक्रुध्यन् द्वयोरेष चिकित्सकः॥
en: One, that does not act against a person whose anger has been excited, saves himself and others from great fear-in fact he is the physician of both.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: मूढो यदि क्लिश्यमानः क्रुध्यतेऽशक्तिमान् नरः। बलीयसां मनुष्याणां त्यजत्यात्मानमात्मना॥
en: When a weak man when oppressed by others is angry with those that are more powerful, he brings about his own ruin.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: तस्यात्मानं संत्यजतो लोका नश्यन्त्यनात्मनः। तस्माद् द्रौपद्यशक्तस्य मन्योर्नियमनं स्मृतम्॥
en: There is no region hereafter for such a man who deliberately brings about his own destruction; therefore it is said, O Draupadi, that a weak man should control his anger.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: विद्वांस्तथैव यः शक्तः क्लिश्यमानो न कुप्यति। अनाशयित्वा क्लेष्टारं परलोके च नन्दति॥
en: And the wise man too, who though oppressed does not allow his anger to be excited, rejoices in the next world for having treated his persecutor with indifference.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: तस्माद् बलवता चैव दुर्बलेन च नित्यदा। क्षन्तव्यं पुरुषेणाहुरापत्स्वपि विजानता॥
en: For this, it is said that a wise man whether he be strong or weak, should always forgive his persecutor, even if he is in difficulty.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: मन्योर्हि विजयं कृष्णे प्रशंसन्तीह साधवः। क्षमावतो जयो नित्यं साधोरिह सतां मतम्॥
en: The pious always praise him, O Krishna (Draupadi), who has conquered his anger; it is held by the pious that the honest and forgiving man is always victorious.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: सत्यं चानृततः श्रेयो नृशंस्याच्चानृशंसता। तमेवं बहुदोषं तु क्रोधं साधुविवर्जितम्॥ मादृशः प्रसृजेत् कस्मात् सुयोधनवधादपि। तेजस्वीति यमा हुर्वै पण्डिता दीर्घदर्शिनः॥ न क्रोधोऽभ्यन्तरस्तस्य भवतीति विनिश्चितम्। यस्तु क्रोधं समुत्पन्नं प्रज्ञया प्रतिबाधते॥ तेजस्विनं तं विद्वांसो मन्यन्ते तत्त्वदर्शिनः क्रुद्धो हि कार्यं सुश्रोणि न यथावत् प्रपश्यति। नाकार्यं न च मर्यादां नरः क्रुद्धोऽनुपश्यति॥
en: Truth is superior to untruth and gentle to cruel conduct; why should I, for slaying Suyodhana, display that anger of many evils, renounced by the virtuous? The far-sceing sages regard him as a man of character in whom anger does not exist; the learned men, seeing the real things, always regard him as a man of character who restrains his rising wrath. O you of fair hips, the angry man does not observe the real state of things; the angry man does not see his way nor regard persons.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: हन्त्यवध्यानपि क्रुद्धो गुरून् क्रुद्धस्तुदत्यपि। तस्मात् तेजसि कर्तव्यः क्रोधो दूरे प्रतिष्ठितः॥
en: The angry man kills those who should not be killed; he even slays his preceptor; therefore a man of character should always leave off anger at a distance.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: दाक्ष्यं घमर्ष: शौर्यं च शीघ्रत्वमिति तेजसः। गुणाः क्रोधाभिभूतेन न शक्याः प्राप्तुमञ्जसा॥
en: The man that is possessed by anger does not easily acquire generosity, dignity, bravery, skill and other accomplishments of a real man of character.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: क्रोधं त्यक्त्वा तु पुरुषः सम्यक् तेजोऽभिपद्यते। कालयुक्तं महाप्राज्ञे क्रुद्धस्तेज: सुदुःसहम्॥
en: Renouncing anger a man can display his true energy, whereas it is difficult, O highly wise one, for an angry man to display energy at the proper hour.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: क्रोधस्त्वपण्डितैः शश्वत् तेज इत्यभिनिश्चितम्। रजस्तु लोकनाशाय विहितं मानुषं प्रति॥
en: Anger is regarded by the illiterate as equivalent to energy, anger has been given to mankind for the destruction of the world.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: तस्माच्छश्वत् त्यजेत् क्रोधं पुरुषः सम्यगाचरन्। श्रेयान् स्वधर्मानपगो न क्रुद्ध इति निश्चितम्॥
en: The person, who wishes to behave with decorum, should renounce anger; even one who has forsaken the virtues of his own order, docs not indulge in anger.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: यदि सर्वमबुद्धीनामतिक्रान्तमचेतसाम्। अतिक्रमो मद्विधस्य कथंस्वित् स्यादनिन्दिते॥
en: Light-minded fools might transgress all these, but O faultless damsel, how can persons like myself (transgress).

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: यदि न स्युर्मानुषेषु क्षमिणः पृथिवीसमाः। न स्यात् संधिर्मनुष्याणां क्रोधमूलो हि विग्रहः॥
en: If there were not persons amongst mankind equal to the earth in forgiveness there would be no peace amongst them but perpetual dissension's engendered by anger.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: अभिषक्तो ह्यभिषजेदाहन्याद् गुरुणा हतः। एवं विनाशो भूतानामधर्मः प्रथितो भवेत्॥
en: If the injured persons were to return their injuries; if one admonished by his superiors were to chastise his superiors in return, the result would be the destruction of all creatures and sin would take its root firm.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: आक्रुष्टः पुरुषः सर्वं प्रत्याक्रोशेदनन्तरम्। प्रतिहन्याद्धतश्चैव तथा हिंस्याच्च हिंसितः॥ हंन्युर्हि पितरः पुत्रान् पुत्राश्चापि तथा पितृन्। हन्युश्च पतयो भार्याः पतीन् भार्यास्तथैव च॥ एवं संकुपिते लोके शमः कृष्णे न विद्यते। प्रजानां संधिमूलं हि शमं विद्धि शुभानने॥
en: If the man when vilified by another vilifies him in return; if the injured man returns his injuries; if the chastised man chastises in return; if fathers kill their sons and sons their fathers; and if husbands destroy their wives and wives their husbands; then, how can, O Krishna, births take place in this world where anger so predominates? Know you, O fair damsel, that birth of creatures in this world, is dependent upon peace.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: ताः क्षिपेरन् प्रजाः सर्वाः क्षिप्रं द्रौपदि तादृशे। तस्मान्मन्युर्विनाशाय प्रजानामभवाय च॥
en: If the kings yield to anger, O Draupadi, their subjects soon meet with ruin. Thus anger brings on destruction and distress of mankind.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: यस्मात् तु लोके दृश्यन्ते क्षमिणः पृथिवीसमाः। तस्माज्जनम् च भूतानां भवश्च प्रतिपद्यते॥
en: Because persons forgiving like the earth are seen in this world, it is therefore that creatures are born and enjoy prosperity.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: क्षन्तव्यं पुरुषेणेह सर्वापत्सु सुशोभने। क्षमावतो हि भूतानां जन्म चैव प्रकीर्तितम्॥
en: O fair damsel, in every form of injury, persons should forgive; it is said that the birth of creatures is due to the forgiveness of mankind.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: आक्रुष्टस्ताडितः क्रुद्धः क्षमते यो बलीयसा। यश्च नित्यं जितक्रोधो विद्वानुत्तमपूरुषः॥
en: He is considered as an excellent and learned person who, having conquered his anger, always shows his forgiveness even when insulted, oppressed and excited by a strong man.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: प्रभाववानपि नरस्तस्य लोकाः सनातनाः। क्रोधनस्त्वल्पविज्ञानः प्रेत्य चेह न नश्यति॥
en: Eternal regions are for that person, who, though powerful (conquers his anger), while he that is angry, is foolish and meets with ruin both in this world and in the next.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीमा गाथा नित्यं क्षमावताम्। गीताः क्षमावता कृष्णे काश्यपेन महात्मना॥
en: As an illustration of this, the following hymn, O Krishna, in honor of the forgiving has been sung by the high-souled and everforgiving Kashyapa.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: क्षमाधर्मः क्षमा यज्ञः क्षमा वेदाः क्षमा श्रुतम्। य एतदेवं जानाति स सर्वं क्षन्तुमहति॥
en: Forgiveness is virtue, forgiveness is sacrifice, forgiveness is the Vedas, forgiveness is Shruti; he who knows all this is capable of forgive all.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: क्षमा ब्रह्म क्षमा सत्यं क्षमा भूतं च भावि च। क्षमा तपः क्षमा शौचं क्षमयेदंघृतं जगत्॥
en: Forgiveness is Brahma, forgiveness is truth, forgiveness is the accumulated and future (ascetic) merit, forgiveness is the devout penance and forgiveness is purity; and by forgiveness the universe is sustained.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: अति यज्ञविदां लोकान् क्षमिणः प्राप्नुवन्ति च। अति ब्रह्मविदां लोकानति चापि तपस्विनाम्॥
en: Forgiving persons attain to the regions of those conversant with the rituals, of those wellversed with the knowledge of Brahman and those of ascetics.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: अन्ये वै यजुषां लोकाः कर्मिणामपरे तथा। क्षमावतां ब्रह्मलोके लोकाः परमपूजिताः॥
en: Persons performing Vedic rites as well as those performing other rituals attain to other regions; whereas forgiving persons attain to the highly adored regions in the world of Brahma.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: क्षमा तेजस्विनां तेजः क्षमा ब्रह्म तपस्विनाम्। क्षमा सत्यं सत्यवतां क्षमा यज्ञः क्षमा शमः॥
en: Forgiveness is the energy of the energetic; forgiveness is the sacrifice and forgiveness is the control of mind; forgiveness is the truth of the truthful; forgiveness is the control of mind.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: तां क्षमा तादृशीं कृष्णे कथमस्मद्विधस्त्यजेत्। यस्यां ब्रह्म च सत्यं च यज्ञा लोकाश्च धिष्ठिताः॥
en: How can, O Krishna, the persons like me renounce such forgiveness in which are established Brahma, truth, wisdom and the three worlds.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: क्षन्तव्यमेव सततं पुरुषेण विजानता। यदा हि क्षमते सर्वं ब्रह्म सम्पद्यते तदा।॥
en: Even, knowing all, person should always forgive; whoever forgives everything attains to Brahma.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: क्षमावतामयं लोकः परश्चैव क्षमावताम्। इह सम्मानमृच्छन्ति परत्र च शुभां गतिम्॥
en: This world belongs to the forgiving, the other world also belongs to the forgiving, they obtain honors here and holy blessedness in the next.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: येषां मन्युर्मनुष्याणां क्षमयाभिहतः सदा। तेषां परतरे लोकास्तस्मात् क्षान्तिः परा मता॥
en: Those persons, whose anger is overpowered by forgiveness, attain to the higher regions; therefore forgiveness is considered the highest (virtue).

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: इति गीताः काश्यपेन गाथा नित्यं क्षमावताम्। श्रुत्वा गाथाः क्षमायास्त्वं तुष्य द्रौपदि मा क्रुधः।४५॥
en: These verses were always chanted by Kashyapa in honor of the forgiving; hearing these verses of forgiveness, be pleased and be not angry, O Draupadi.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: पितामहः शान्तनवः शमं सम्पूजयिष्यति। कृष्णाश्च देवकीपुत्रः शमं सम्पूजयिष्यति॥
en: Our grandfather, the son of Shantanu, worships peace, as well as Krishna, the son of Devaki.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: आचार्यो विदुरः क्षत्ता शममेव वदिष्यतः। कृपश्च संजयश्चैव शममेव वदिष्यतः॥
en: The preceptor and Vidura, (known as) Khattva both speak of peace; Kripa as well as Sanjaya also speak of peace.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: सोमदत्तो युयुत्सुश्च द्रोणपुत्रस्तथैव च। पितामहाश्च नो व्यासः शमं वदति नित्यशः॥
en: Somadatta, Yuyutsu, Drona's son as well as our grandfather Vyasa daily speak of peace.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: एतैर्हि राजा नियतं चोद्यमानः शमं प्रति। राज्यं दातेति मे बुद्धिर्न चेल्लोभान्नशिष्यति॥
en: Being led by all these towards peace the king will return us the kingdom; if he yields to temptation he will meet with destruction.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: कालोऽयं दारुणः प्राप्तो भरतानामभूतये। निश्चितं मे सदैवैतत् पुरस्तादपि भाविनि॥
en: A dreadful time has set in to bring about the misfortune of the Bharatas; from some time before this has been settled conclusion, O fair damsel.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: सुयोधनो नाहतीति क्षमामेवं न विन्दति। अर्हस्तत्राहमित्येवं तस्मान्मां विन्दते क्षमा॥
en: Suyodhana does not deserve kingdom and therefore he does not know forgiveness; I deserve it and therefore forgiveness has taken possession of me.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: एतदात्मवतां वृत्तमेषधर्मः सनातनः। क्षमा चैवानृशंस्यं च तत् कर्तास्म्यहमञ्जसा॥
en: Forgiveness and humility are the qualities of the self-controlled and constitute the eternal virtue and I shall therefore adopt them.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: द्रौपद्युवाच नमोधात्रे विधाने च यौ मोहं चक्रतुस्तव। पितृपैतामहे वृत्ते वोढव्ये तेऽन्यथा मतिः॥
en: Draupadi said: I bow to Dhatri and Vidhatri who have thus bewildered my sense; you think otherwise from your father and grandfather regarding what you have got to bear.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: कर्मभिश्चिन्तितो लोको गत्यां गत्यां पृथग्विधः। तस्मात् कर्माणि नित्यानि लोभान्मोक्षं यियासति॥ नेहधर्मानृशंस्याभ्यां च क्षान्त्या नार्जवेन च। पुरुषः श्रियमाप्नोति न घृणित्वेन कर्हिचित्॥
en: By actions men are placed in different situations of life; consequences of action are inevitable, from ignorance people desire for the liberation from action. A man does not even attain prosperity in this world by virtue, gentleness, forgiveness, straight-forwardness and fear of censure.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: त्वां च व्यसनमभ्यागादिदं भारत दुःसहम्। यत् त्वं नार्हसि नापीमे भ्रातरस्ते महौजसः॥
en: Or else, O descendant of Bharata, this unbearable misfortune would not have befallen you, who are so unworthy of it and your brothers of great energy.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: न हि तेऽध्यगमञ्जानु तदानीं नाद्य भारत। धर्मात् प्रियतरं किंचिदपि चेज्जीवितादिह॥
en: Neither then, nor even now, O descendant of Bharata, has anything appeared to you dearer than virtue, which is dearer to you even than your life.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: धर्मार्थमेव ते राज्यधर्मार्थं जीवितं च ते। ब्राह्मणा गुरुवश्चैव जानन्त्यपि च देवताः॥
en: That your kingdom is for virtue and your life even is for virtue, is known by Brahmanas, superiors and even celestials.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: भीमसेनार्जुनौ चोभौ माद्रेयौ च मया सह। त्यजेस्त्वमिति मे बुद्धिर्न तुधर्मं परित्यजेः॥
en: You can abandon Bhimasena, Arjuna these twin sons of Madri along with myself, I think, but you can never renounce virtue.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: राजानंधर्मगोप्तारंधर्मो रक्षति रक्षितः। इति में श्रुतमार्याणां त्वां तु मन्ये न रक्षति॥
en: I have heard from elders that a king protects virtue and virtue in return protects him-but methinks it does not protect you.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: अनन्या हि नरव्याघ्र नित्यदाधर्ममेव ते। बुद्धिः सततमन्वेतिच्छायेव पुरुषं निजा॥
en: O best of men, like a shadow following a man, you with a singleness of purpose always follow virtue.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: नावमंस्था हि सदृशान् नावराञ्छ्रेयसः कुतः। अवाप्य पृथिवीं कृत्स्नां न ते शृङ्गमवर्धत॥
en: You have never disregarded your equals, inferiors and superiors; obtaining even the entire universe your pride never increased.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: स्वाहाकारैः स्वधाभिश्च पुजाभिरपि च द्विजान्। दैवतानि पितॄश्चैव सततं पार्थ सेवसे।॥
en: O son of Pritha, with Yvahas and Svaddhas and other forms of worship you ever adore the Brahmanas, the celestials and the Pitris.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: ब्राह्मणाः सर्वकामैस्ते सततं पार्थ तर्पिताः। यतयो मोक्षिणश्चैव गृहस्थाश्चैव भारत॥ भुञ्जते रुक्मपात्रीभिर्यत्राहं परिचारिका। आरण्यकेभ्यो लौहानि भाजनानि प्रयच्छसि। नादेयं ब्राह्मणेभ्यस्ते गृहे किंचन विद्यते॥
en: O son of Pritha, you have always pleased the Brahmanas by granting all their desires; the Yatis, the ascetics, the householder ascetics, have always been fed by you on golden plates where (myself) have distributed food. You always give food and gold to Vanaprasthas; there is nothing in your house which you cannot bestow upon the Brahmanas.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: यदिदं वैश्वदेवं ते शान्तये क्रियते गृहे। तद् दत्त्वातिथिभूतेभ्यो राजञ्छिष्टेन जीवसि॥
en: Having distributed duly, O king, all to the guests in the Vishvadeva sacrifice that is solemnized in your house for your peace you live upon what remains.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: इष्टयः पशुबन्धाश्च काम्यनैमित्तिकाश्च ये। वर्तन्ते पाकयज्ञाश्च यज्ञकर्म च नित्यदा॥
en: Ishtis, Pashubandhas, sacrifice for obtaining the gratification of desires and ordinary household ceremonies, Paka sacrifices and various other rites are daily performed in your house.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: अस्मिन्नपि महारण्ये विजने दस्युसेविते। राष्ट्रादपेत्य वसतोधर्म स्तेनावसीदति॥
en: Even in this huge solitary forest frequented by robbers, living in banishment, deprived of your kingdom your virtue has suffered no decrease.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: अश्वमेधो राजसूयः पुण्डरीकोऽथ गोसवः। एतैरपि महायज्ञैरिष्टं ते भूरिदक्षिणैः॥
en: The Ashvamedha, the Rajasuya, Pundarika, the Gosava-all these great sacrifices requiring large gifts have been celebrated by you.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: राजन् परीतया बुद्ध्या विषमेऽक्षपराजये। राज्यं वसून्यायुधानि भ्रातृन् मां चासि निर्जितः॥
en: O king, by your perverse understanding, in your defeat at the gambling match you lost your kingdom, wealth, weapons your brothers and even myself.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: ऋजोर्मदोर्वदान्यस्य ह्रीमतः सत्यवादिनः। कथमक्षव्यसनजा बुद्धिरापतिता तव॥
en: How could your mind, siinple, gentle, liberal, modest and truthful as you are, be drawn to the vice of gambling?

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: अतीव मोहमायाति मनश्च परिभूयते। निशाम्य ते दुःखमिदमिमां चापदमीदृशीम्॥
en: Beholding this your calamity and misfortune my sense is bewildered and mind overwhelmed.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। ईश्वरस्य वशे लोकास्तिष्ठन्ते नात्यनो यथा॥
en: I shall cite here an old historical incident as an illustration that men are subject to the will of Providence and not to themselves.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: धातैव खलु भूतानां सुखदुःखे प्रियाप्रिये। दधाति सर्वमीशानः पुरस्ताच्छुक्रमुच्चरन्॥
en: The Lord Ishana ordains beforehand, with reference to weal and woe, happiness and misery, of all creatures like a seed.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: यथा दारुमयी योषा नरवीर समाहिता। ईरयत्यङ्गमङ्गानि तथा राजनिमा: प्रजाः॥
en: O hero among men, O king, as a wooden figure is made to move its limbs by the wirepuller so are all these creatures (made to act by the lord.)

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: आकाश इव भूतानि व्याप्य सर्वाणि भारत। ईश्वरो विदधातीह कल्याणं यच्च पापकम्॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, pervading all creatures, like ethereal space the Providence ordains its happiness or misery.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: शकुनिस्तन्तुबद्धो वा नियतोऽयमनीश्वरः। ईश्वरस्य वशे तिष्ठेन्नान्येषां नात्मनः प्रभुः॥
en: Like a bird tied with a string all creatures depend upon God; they all live in dependence upon God not upon others; nor are they their own masters.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: मणिः सूत्र इव प्रोतो नस्योत इव गोवृषः। स्रोतसो मध्यमापन्नः कूलाद् वृक्ष इव च्युतः॥ धातुरादेशमन्वेति तन्मयो हि तदर्पणः। आत्माधीनो मनुष्योऽयं कालं भजति कंचन॥
en: Like a pearl set on a string, a bull tied by a rope passing through its nose or a tree fallen from the bank into the middle of a river. All creatures follow the ordinances of the Creator for they are identical with Him and live in Him; they are not subject to themselves and cannot pass an hour independently.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: अज्ञो जन्तुरनीशोऽयमात्मनः सुखदुःखयोः। ईश्वरप्रेरितो गच्छेत् स्वर्ग नरकमेव च॥
en: Ignorant as they are, creatures are not masters of their own happiness or misery; dispatched by the Providence they either go to heaven or hell.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: यथा वायोस्तृणाचाणि वशं यान्ति बलीयसः। धातुरेवं वशं यान्ति सर्वभूतानि भारत॥
en: As light straws are brought to the subjugation of the strong wind, so all creatures, O descendant of Bharata, depend upon the Creator.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: आर्ये कर्मणि युञ्जानः पापे वा पुनरीश्वरः। व्याप्य भूतानि चरते न चायमिति लक्ष्यते॥
en: Again, performing actions right or wrong and pervading the universe, the Lord exists but is not perceived by any (who can say) "This is God."

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: हेतुमात्रमिदंधातुः शरीरं क्षेत्रसंज्ञितम्। येन कारयते कर्म शुभाशुभफलं विभुः॥
en: This physical body is merely the instrument of God by which the Lord engages them in actions, the fruits of which are cither good or bad.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: पश्य मायाप्रभावोऽयमीश्वरेण यथा कृतः। यो हन्ति भूतैर्भूतानि मोहयित्वाऽऽत्ममायया॥
en: Behold the power of the illusive energy by which he makes them kill their fellows.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: अन्यथा परिदृष्टानि मुनिभिस्तत्त्वदर्शिभिः। अन्यथा परिवर्तन्ते वेगा इव नभस्वतः॥
en: This is seen in a different light by the sages seeing the real truths; they appear to them in a different light like the rays of the sun.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: अन्यथैव ही मन्यन्ते पुरुषास्तानि तानि च। अन्यथैव प्रभुस्तानि करोति विकरोति च॥
en: Ordinary people see all those things in a different view; the Lord create and destroy them in a different way.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: यथा काष्ठेन वा काष्ठमश्मानं चाश्मना पुनः। अयसा चाप्ययश्छिन्द्यानिर्विचेष्टमचेतनम्॥ एवं स भगवान् देवः स्वयम्भूः प्रपितामहः। हिनस्ति भूतैर्भूतानिच्छद्म कृत्वा युधिष्ठिर॥
en: As one can break a piece of inactive senseless wood with wood, stone with stone and iron with iron. So, O Yudhishthira the Self-create, divinc Grandsire spreading his illusive energy destroys creatures, with creatures.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: सम्प्रयोज्य वियोज्यायं कामकारकरः प्रभुः। क्रीडते भगवान् भूतैर्बालः क्रीडनकैरिव॥
en: Like a child playing with his creatures, creating and destroying them.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: न मातृपितृवद् राजन्धाता भूतेषु वर्तते। रोषादिव प्रवृत्तोऽयं यथायमितरो जनः॥
en: O king, the Providence behaves towards the creatures, like a father or mother, like an ordinary person he (sometimes) seems to be angry towards them.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: आर्याञ्छोलवतो दृष्ट्वा ह्रीमतो वृत्तिकर्शितान्। अनार्यान् सुखिनश्चैव विह्वलामीव चिन्तया।॥
en: Sceing elderly, well behaved and modest persons, in distress and the vicious, in happiness, I am beside myself with thought.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: तवेमामापदं दृष्ट्वा समृद्धिं च सुयोधने। धातारं गर्हये पार्थ विषमं योऽनुपश्यति॥
en: O son of Pritha, seeing your misfortune and the prosperity of Suyodhana, I blame the Providence who sees such an inequality.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: आर्यशास्त्रातिगे क्रूर लुब्धेधर्मापचायिनि। धार्तराष्ट्र श्रियं दत्त्वाधाता किं फलमश्नुते॥
en: Conferring prosperity prosperity upon the wily avaricious of Dhritarashtra, who transgresses the sacred scriptures and injures virtue, what fruit shall the Creator reap?

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: कर्म चेत् कृतमन्वेति कर्तारं नान्यमृच्छति। कर्मणा तेन पापेन लिप्यते नूनमीश्वरः॥
en: If the act done follows the performer then forsooth, the God himself is contaminated with the sin of every action.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: अथ कर्म कृतं पापं न चेत् कर्तारमृच्छति। कारणं बलमेवेह जनाञ्छोचामि दुर्बलान्॥
en: If the sin consequent upon actions does not touch the doer then the individual power is the cause and I grieve for those who are weak. son

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच वल्गु चित्रपदं श्लक्ष्णं याज्ञसेनि त्वया वचः। उक्तं तच्छ्रुतमस्माभिर्नास्तिक्यं तु प्रभाषसे॥
en: Yudhishthira said : O Yajnaseni, your speech is sweet, clear and full of nice expressions; we have listened to it; you speak of atheism.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: नाहं कर्मफलान्वेषी राजपुत्रि चराम्युत। ददामि देयमित्येव यजै यष्टव्यमित्युत॥
en: O princess, I never act being desirous of the fruits thereof; I distribute (a thing) which should be distributed and I perform a sacrifice which should be performed.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: अस्तु वात्र फलं मा वा कर्तव्यं पुरुषेण यत्। गृहे वा वसता कृष्णे यथाशक्ति करोमि तत्॥
en: I perform, as best as I can, O Krishna, what a householder should do, not caring for the fruits (of my actions).

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: धर्मं चरामि सुश्रोणि नधर्मफलकारणात्। आगमाननतिक्रम्य सतां वृत्तमवेक्ष्य च॥
en: O fair-lady, I act piously not for getting the fruits of virtue but for not transgressing the Vedas and seeing the conduct of the pious.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: धर्म एव मनः कृष्णे स्वभावाच्चैव मेधृतम्। धमवाणिज्यको हीनो जघन्योधर्मवादिनाम्॥ नधर्मफलमाप्नोति योधर्मं दोग्धुमिच्छति। यश्चैनं शङ्कते कृत्वा नास्तिक्यात् पापचेतनः॥
en: My mind and nature, O Krishna, are naturally bent upon virtue; that vile trader of virtue, the worst of the virtuous, who wishes to reap the fruits of virtue, does never obtain them; nor does a vicious-minded person, for his scepticism, who doubts a virtuous act, having accomplished it.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: अतिवादाद् वदाम्येष माधर्ममभिशङ्किथाः। धर्माभिशङ्की पुरुषस्तिर्यग्गतिपरायणः॥
en: From the evidence of the Vedas I say, “You should never doubt virtue; the person doubting virtue is destined to be born among the brutes."

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: धर्मो यस्याभिशक्यः स्यादाष वा दुर्बलात्मनः। वेदाच्छूद्र इवापेयात् स लोकादजरामरात्॥
en: A weak-minded man who doubts religion, virtue and the words of the Rishis, is precluded form the regions of immortality and bliss as the Shudras are from the Vedas.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: वेदाध्यायीधर्मपरः कुले जातो मनस्विनि। स्थविरेषु स योक्तव्यो राजर्षिर्धर्मचारिभिः॥
en: O large-minded lady, one studying the Vedas, virtuous and born in a high race, (though young) is considered aged by the pious royal saints.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: पापीयान् स हि शूद्रेभ्यस्तस्करेभ्यो विशिष्यते। शास्त्रातिगो मन्दबुद्धिर्योधर्ममभिशङ्कते॥
en: That vicious-minded one, who transgresses the scriptures and doubts virtue is regarded as lower even than the Shudras and robbers.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: प्रत्यक्षं हि त्वया दृष्ट ऋषिर्गच्छन् महातपाः। मार्कण्डेयोऽप्रमेयात्माधर्मेण चिरजीविता॥
en: You have seen with your own eyes the great ascetic Markandeya of incomparable magnanimity come to us who has been rendered immortal by virtue.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: व्यासो वसिष्ठो मैत्रेयो नारदो लोमशः शुकः। अन्ये च ऋषयः सर्वेधर्मेणैव सुचेतसः॥
en: Vyasa, Vasishtha, Maitreya, Narada Lomasha, Shuka and all other Rishis have become of pure souls by virtue.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: प्रत्यक्षं पश्यसि ह्येतान् दिव्ययोगसमन्वितान्। शापानुग्रहणे शक्तान् देवेभ्योऽपि गरीयसः॥
en: You yourself see all these endued with celestials asceticism capable of cursing or blessing and superior even to the celestials,

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: एते हिधर्ममेवादौ वर्णयन्ति सदानघे। कर्तव्यममरप्रख्याः प्रत्यक्षागमबुद्धयः॥
en: O sinless lady, these sages, equal to the Rishis and who can see what is written in the Vedas, describe virtue as the foremost duty.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: अतो नार्हसि कल्याणिधातारंधर्ममेव च। राज्ञि मूढेन मनसा क्षेप्तुं शङ्कितुमेव च।॥
en: You should not, O blessed queen, with a foolish mind either doubt or censure the Providence or (His act).

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: उन्मत्तान् मन्यते बाल: सर्वानागतनिश्चयान्। धर्माभिशङ्को नान्यस्मात् प्रमाणमधिगच्छति॥ आत्मप्रमाण उन्नद्धः श्रेयसो ह्यवमन्यकः। इन्द्रियप्रीतिसम्बद्धं यदिदं लोकसाक्षिकम्। एतावन्मन्यते बालो. मोहमन्यत्र गच्छति॥
en: The fool, who doubts religion and disregards virtue and being proud of the proof of his own reasoning, does not receive it from others, considers all these sages who look upon the future as present, like mad man. He considers the external world as conducive to the gratification of senses and is blind to everything else.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: प्रायश्चित्तं न तस्यास्ति योधर्ममभिशङ्कते। ध्यायन् स कृपणः पापो न लोकान् प्रतिपद्यते॥
en: Whoever, doubts religion has no expatiation of his sin; that wretched and vile person feels anxicty (here) and does not attain to the regions (of bliss) hereafter.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: प्रमाणाद्धि निवृत्तो हि वेदशास्त्रार्थनिन्दकः। कामलोभातिगो मूढो नरकं प्रतिपद्यते॥
en: That stupid person, who does not regard evidences, who vilifics the interpretation of the Vedic texts and who commits sin under the influence of lust and covetousness, is doomed to hell.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: यस्तु नित्यं कृतमतिर्धर्ममेवाभिपद्यते। अशङ्कमानः कल्याणि सोऽमुत्रानन्त्यमश्नुते॥
en: O blessed lady, he however, who, with faith and without any doubt follows religion, attains to eternal bliss in the next world.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: आर्षं प्रमाणमुत्क्रम्यधर्मं न प्रतिपालयन्। सर्वशास्त्रातिगो मूढः शं जन्मसु न विन्दति॥
en: That stupid person, who transgresses the evidences of the Rishis, who does not follow religion and who transgresses all the scriptures, never obtains bliss in any life.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: यस्य नार्षं प्रमाणं स्याच्छिष्टाचारच भाविनि। न वै तस्य परो लोको नायमस्तीति निश्चयः॥
en: For him, O fair lady, who disregards the words of the Rishis and does not care for the evidence of the pious, neither this world nor the next exists.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: शिष्टैराचरितंधर्मं कृष्णे मा स्माभिशङ्किथाः। पुराणमृषिभिः प्रोक्तं सर्वज्ञैः सर्वदर्शिभिः॥
en: Doubt not, O Krishna, the ancient religion which is followed by the good and formulated by the omniscient and omnipotent Rishis.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: धर्म एव प्लवो नान्यः स्वर्ग द्रौपदि गच्छताम्। सैव नौः सागरस्येव वणिजः पारमिच्छतः॥
en: O Draupadi, virtue is the only raft and nothingelse to those who wish to go to heaven, like a ship to the merchant wishing to cross the Ocean.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: अफलो यदिधर्मः स्याच्चरितोधर्मचारिभिः। अप्रतिष्ठे तमस्येतज्जगन्मज्जेदनिन्दिते॥
en: O blameless lady, if the pieties practised by the virtuous had no fruits then this world would been enshrouded by infamous darkness.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: निर्वाणं नाधिगच्छेयुर्जीवेयुः पशुजीविकाम्। विद्यां ते नैव युज्येयुर्न चार्थ केचिदाप्नुयुः॥
en: None would have followed emancipation, none would have cared for the acquisition of knowledge or even of wealth and people would have lived like beasts.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: तपश्च ब्रह्मचर्यं च यज्ञः स्वाध्याय एव च। दानमार्जवमेतानि यदि स्युरफलानि वै॥ नाचरिष्यन् परेधर्म परे परतरे च ये। विप्रलम्भोऽयमत्यन्तं यदि स्युरफलाः क्रियाः॥ ऋषयश्चैव देवाश्च गन्धर्वासुरराक्षसाः। ईश्वराः कस्य हेतोस्ते चरेयुर्धर्ममादृताः॥
en: If devout penances, life of celibacy, sacrifice, the study of the Vedas, charity and honesty-these were fruitless then people would not have practised virtues, generation after generation. If all the action had been fruitless a terrible confusion would have set in. Why do the Rishis, the gods the Gandharvas, the Asuras and the Rakshasas who are lords of themselves, with love practise virtues?

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: फलदं त्विह विज्ञायधातारं श्रेयसिध्रुवम्। धर्मं ते व्यचरन् कृष्णे तद्धि श्रेयः सनातनम्॥
en: Considering for certain that Providence is the giver of fruits in virtue, they practise virtues; O Krishna, for them is eternal bliss.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: ह नायमफलोधर्मो नाधर्मोऽफलवानपि। दृश्यन्तेऽपि हि विद्यानां फलानि तपसां तथा॥ त्वमात्मनो विजानीहि जन्म कृष्णेयथा श्रुतम्। वेत्थ चापि यथा जातोधृष्टद्युम्नः प्रतापवान्॥
en: Whereas the fruits of knowledge and ascetic observances are seen, virtue and vice can never be devoid of fruits. Recollect, O Krishna, the circumstances of your birth, as you have heard and also the manner in which the powerful Dhristadyumna was born.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: एतावदेव पर्याप्तमुपमानं शुचिस्मिते। कर्मणां फलमाप्नोतिधीरोऽल्पेनापि तुष्यति॥
en: These are sufficient proofs, O you of sweet smiles; the self-controlled reap the fruits of acts and are satisfied with a little.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: बहुनापि ह्यविद्वांसो नैव तुष्यन्त्यबुद्धयः। तेषां नधर्मजं किंचित् प्रेत्य शर्मास्ति वा पुनः॥
en: Ignorant and stupid persons are not satisfied even with much and they have no happiness begotten of virtue for them in the next world.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: कर्मणां श्रुतपुण्यानां पापानां च फलोदयः। प्रभवश्चात्ययश्चैव देवगुह्यानि भाविनि॥
en: The fruits of the holy acts laid down in the Vedas as well as of sinful acts, the root and the destruction of actions, O fair lady, are mysteries even to the celestials,

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: नैतानि वेद यः कश्चिन्मुह्यन्तेऽत्र प्रजा इमाः। अपि कल्पसहस्रेण न स श्रेयोऽधिगच्छति॥
en: These are not known to all; ordinary people are ignorant of these; he does not follow in a thousand Kalpa the well-being of the celestials.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: रक्ष्यान्येतानि देवानां गूढमाया हि देवताः। कृताशाश्च व्रताशाश्च तपसा दग्धकिल्बिषाः। प्रसादैर्मानसैर्युक्ताः पश्यन्त्येतानि वै द्विजाः॥
en: These are kept (in secrecy) by the celestials for their illusive energy is mysterious; those Brahmanas that have conquered their aspirations, those that have built up their hopes, those whose sins have been burnt down by ascetic observances, those who have got contented minds, can observe these.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: न फलादर्शनाद्धर्मः शङ्कितव्यो न देवताः। यष्टव्यं च प्रयत्नेन दातव्यं चानसूयता॥
en: For not seeing the fruit you should not doubt religion or the gods; you should perform sacrifices assiduously and charities without any insolence.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: कर्मणां फलमस्तीह तथैतद्धर्मशासनम्। ब्रह्मा प्रोवाच पुत्राणां यदृषिर्वेद कश्यपः॥
en: Acts have their fruits in this world and virtue is eternal; as said by Kashyapa, Brahma told all this to his sons.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: तस्मात् ते संशयः कृष्णे नीहार इव नश्यतु। व्यवस्य सर्वमस्तीति नास्तिक्यं भावमुत्सृज॥
en: O Krishna, let your doubt be destroyed like dews meditating upon all this. Let your scepticism yield to faith.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: ईश्वरं चापि भूतानांधातारं मा च वै क्षिप। शिक्षस्वैनं नमस्वैनं मा तेऽभूद् बुद्धिरीदृशी॥
en: Do not speak ill of God who is the lord of all creatures; learn to know him; bow to him; let not your understanding be such.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: यस्य प्रसादात् तद्भक्तो मर्यो गच्छत्यमर्त्यताम्। उत्तमां देवतां कृष्णे मावमंस्थाः कथंचन॥
en: Never disregard that Supreme being, Krishna, by whose mercy the mortals, by pious observances, become immortals.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: द्रौपद्युवाच नावमन्ये न गर्हे चधर्मं पार्थ कथंचन। ईश्वरं कुत एवाहमवमस्ये प्रजापतिम्॥
en: Draupadi said : I never disregard or speak ill of religion, O son of Pritha; why should I disregard God, the lord of creations?

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: आर्ताहं प्रलपामीदमिति मां विद्धि भारत। भूयश्च विलपिष्यामि सुमनास्त्वं निबोध मे॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, consider me raving as being stricken with misery, listen to me, I shall again bewail.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: कर्म खल्विह कर्तव्यं जानतामित्रकर्शन। अकर्माणो हि जीवन्ति स्थावरा नेतरे जनाः॥
en: O represser of enemies, forsooth every conscious being should engage in actions in this world; it is only the immobile and not even other creatures that can live without action.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: यावद्गोस्तनपानाच्च यावच्छायोपसेवनात्। जन्तवः कर्मणा वृत्तिमाप्नुवन्ति युधिष्ठिर॥
en: Immediately after the birth the calf sucks the mother's teat. (People feel distress) as soon as incantations are performed on their statues; the creatures, O Yudhishthira, deserve the character of their lives according to pristine actions.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: जङ्गमेषु विशेषेण मनुष्या भरतर्षभ। इच्छन्ति कर्मणा वृत्तिमवाप्तुं प्रेत्य चेह च॥
en: O foremost of Bharatas, this is the difference of man from mobile creatures, that he aspires to like his course of life both in this world and in the next by means of his acts.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: उत्थानमभिजानन्ति सर्वभूतानि भारत। प्रत्यक्षं फलमश्नन्ति कर्मणां लोकसाक्षिकम्॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, all creatures perceive the impression of the pristine life and they visibly reap in this world the fruits of their acts.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: सर्वे हि स्वं समुत्थानमुपजीवन्ति जन्तवः। अपिधाता विधाता च यथायमुदके बकः॥
en: All creatures live according to the impression of the pristine life, even the creatures and the ordainers of the universe like a crane that lives on the water.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: अकर्मणां वै भूतानां वृत्तिः स्यान्न हि काचन। तदेवाभिप्रपद्येत न विहन्यात् कदाचन॥
en: The course of life for a creatures that does not act is impossible; for them there is action and never inaction.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: स्वकर्म कुरु मा ग्लासी: कर्मणा भव दंशितः। कृतं हि योऽभिजानाति सहस्रे सोऽस्ति नास्ति च॥
en: You should therefore act and never incur censure by leaving affection; cover yourself with action as with an armour. There might not be one in a thousand who does not truly understand the utility of work.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: तस्य चापि भवेत् कार्यं विवृद्धौ रक्षणे तथा। भक्ष्यमाणो ह्यनादानात् क्षीयेत् हिमवानपि॥
en: One should act either for increasing or protecting his wealth; if spent without being earned it vanishes although it be like (the mount) Himavana.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: उत्सीदेरन् प्रजाः सर्वा न कुर्युः कर्म चेद् भुवि। तथा ह्येता न वधैरन् कर्म चेदफलं भवेत्॥
en: All creatures would have been exterminated if there were no action; if acts had born no fruits they would not have multiplied.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: अपि चाप्यफलं कर्म पश्यामः कुर्वतो जनान्। नान्यथा ह्यपि गच्छन्ति वृत्ति लोकाः कथंचन॥
