en: It is sometimes observed that creatures perform acts that give them no fruits; for without action the course of life would be an impossibility.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: यश्च दिष्टपरो लोके यश्चापि हठवादिकः। उभावपि शठावेतौ कर्मबुद्धिः प्रशस्यते॥
en: Whoever in this world believe in Destiny and whoever in chance are both the worst of people; those only are praiseworthy who believe in the efficacy of acts.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: यो हि दिष्टमुपासीनो निर्विचेष्टः सुखं शयेत्। अवसीदेत् स दुर्बुद्धिरामो घट इवोदके॥
en: He, who has been at ease without any action and believing in Destiny, is soon consumed like an unburnt earthen pot in water.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: तथैव हठदुर्बुद्धिः शक्तः कर्मण्यकर्मकृत्। आसीत न चिरं जीवेदनाथ इव दुर्बलः॥
en: So also that man, who believes in chance and who, though capable of work, does not work, does not live long, for his life is one of weakness and helplessness.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: अकस्मादिह यः कश्चिदर्थं प्राप्नोति पूरुषः। तं हठेनेति मन्यन्ते स हि यत्नो न कस्यचित्॥
en: If a person in the world attains, by accident, to an accession of wealth-people consider it derived from chance for none has tried for it.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: यच्चापि किंचित् पुरुषो दिष्टं नाम भजत्युत। दैवेन विधिना पार्थ तद् दैवमिति निश्चितम्॥
en: O son of Pritha, whatever good fortune a person acquires in consequence of religious rites is called Providential.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: यत् स्वयं कर्मणा किंचित् फलमाप्नोति पूरुषः। प्रत्यक्षमेतल्लोकेषु तत् पौरुषमिति श्रुतम्॥
en: The fruit, that a person reaps by acting himself and which is the direct outcome of his actions, is considered as a proof of manliness.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: स्वभावतः प्रवृत्तो यः प्राप्नोत्यर्थं न कारणात्। तत् स्वभावात्मकं विद्धि फलं पुरुषसत्तम॥
en: Of best of men, know that the riches acquired spontaneously and without cause are considered as a spontaneous acquisition.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: एवं हठाच्च दैवाच्च स्वभावात् कर्मणस्तथा। यानि प्राप्नोति पुरुषस्तत् फलं पूर्वकर्मणाम्।।२
en: Whatever is thus acquired accidentally, providentially or spontaneously by a person is the outcome of his pristine actions.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: धातापि हि स्वकर्मैव तैस्तैर्हेतुभिरीश्वरः। विदधाति विभज्येह फलं पूर्वकृतं नृणाम्॥
en: And judging according to their pristine actions, the good and bad, the ordainer of the universe distributes among men, their portions in this world.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: यद्ध्ययं पुरुषः किंचित् कुरुते वै शुभाशुभम्। तद्धातृविहितं विद्धि पूर्वकर्मफलोदयम्॥
en: Know that whatever actions, either good or bad, that a person performs are the outcome of God's arrangements with reference to their pristine actions.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: कारणं तस्य देहोऽयंधातुः कर्मणि वर्तते। स यथा प्रेरयत्येनं तथायं कुरुतेऽवशः॥
en: This body is the instrument of God for actions; inert in itself, it performs what is urged on by God.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: तेषु तेषु हि कृत्येषु विनियोक्ता महेश्वरः। सर्वभूतानि कौन्तेय कारयत्यवशान्यपि॥
en: O son of Kunti, it is the supreme Lord of all who makes all creatures do what they do, though they themselves are all inert.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: मनसार्थान् विनिश्चित्य पश्चात् प्राप्नोति कर्मणा। बुद्धिपूर्वं स्वयं वीर पुरुषस्तत्र कारणम्॥
en: O hero, having settled upon some object in mind, a man carries it out into action aided by his intelligence; man is himself therefore the cause.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: संख्यातुं नैव शक्यानि कर्माणि पुरुषर्षभ। अगारनगराणां हि सिद्धिः पुरुषहैतुकी॥ तिले तैलं गवि क्षीरं काष्ठे पावकमन्ततः। धियाधीरो विजानीयादुपायं चास्य सिद्धये॥
en: O best of men, the number of actions cannot be ascertained for towns and palaces are the result of man's acts. By the aid of their intelligence, intelligent men know that oil may be had from sesame, curds from milk and that food may be cooked by means of igniting fuel; they know the means for accomplishing them.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: ततः प्रवर्तते पश्चात् कारणैस्तस्य सिद्धये। तां सिद्धिमुपजीवन्ति कर्मजामिह जन्तवः॥
en: Thereupon they set themselves, by instruinents, to accomplishing them; and creatures maintain their lives by the results acquired in these directions by their own acts.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: कुशलेन कृतं कर्म क; साधु स्वनुष्ठितम्। इदं त्वकुशलेनेति विशेषादुपलभ्यते॥
en: If a work is done by a clever work-man it is done well; from the difference in execution another work may be said to be that of an unskilled hand.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: इष्टापूर्तफलं न स्यान्न शिष्यो न गुरुर्भवेत्। पुरुषः कर्मसाध्येषु स्याच्चेदयमकारणम्॥
en: If a person were not himself the instrument of his acts, the sacrifices would not bear any fruits in his case nor would anybody be a disciple or preceptor.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: कर्तृत्वादेव पुरुषः कर्मसिद्धौ प्रशस्यते। असिद्धौ निन्द्यते चापि कर्मनाशात् कथं त्विह॥
en: It is because a person is himself the instrument of his action that he is praised when or he acquires success, so the doer is censured when he is unsuccessful; nothing else exists.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: सर्वमेव हठेनैके दैवेनैके वदन्त्युत। पुंसः प्रयत्न केचित्त्रैधमेतन्निरुच्यते॥ न चैवेतावता कार्यं मन्यन्त इति चापरे। अस्ति सर्वमदृश्यं तु दिष्टं चैव तथा हठः॥
en: Some say that everything is the outcome of chance, some say everything is providential, whereas others hold that this, is not so, but everything that is said to be the outcome of Destiny or chance is the result of pristine actions.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: दृश्यते हि हठाच्चैव दिष्टाच्चार्थस्य संततिः। किंचिद् दैवाद्धठात् किंचित् किंचिदेव स्वभावतः।३४॥ पुरुषः फलमाप्नोति चतुर्थं नात्र कारणम्। कुशलाः प्रतिजानन्ति ये वै तत्त्वविदो जनाः॥
en: It is seen that wealth proceeds from chance Destiny; something accidental and something natural. In the acquisition of fruits for a man, there is not the fourth cause; this is said by those who are cognizant of truth and well-versed in knowledge.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: तथैवधाता भूतानामिष्टानिष्टफलप्रदः। यदि न स्यान्न भूतानां कृपणो नाम कश्चन॥
en: If God himself were not the bestower of good or bad fruits then among creatures there would not be any miserable being.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: यं यमर्थमभिप्रेप्सुः कुरुते कर्म पूरुषः। तत्तत् सफलमेव स्याद् यदि न स्यात् पुरा कृतम्।
en: If pristine actions had no existence then all purposes for which a man would work should prove successful.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: त्रिद्वारामर्थसिद्धिं तु नानुपश्यन्ति ये नराः। तथैवानर्थसिद्धिं च यथा लोकास्तथैव ते॥
en: Those persons, who do not observe these three doors for the accomplishment of objects as well as for the failure, are dull and exist like the body itself.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: कर्तव्यमेव कर्मेति मनोरेष विनिश्चयः। एकान्तेन ह्यनीहोऽयं पराभवति पूरुषः॥
en: Man should always act; for this is the conclusion of Manu; a person that does not act is always defeated.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: कुर्वतो हि भवत्येव प्रायेणेह युधिष्ठिर। एकान्तफलसिद्धिं तु न विन्दत्यलसः क्वचित्॥
en: A man of action in this world, O Yudhishthira, generally meets with success; the idle however never acquire success.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: असम्भवे त्वस्य हेतुः प्रायश्चित्तं तु लक्षयेत्। कृते कर्मणि राजेन्द्र तथानृण्यमवाप्नुते॥
en: If success becomes impossible a person should remove the difficulties; when engaged in action, O king, he is freed from debts (whether he is successful or not).

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: अलक्ष्मीराविशत्येनं शयानमलसं नरम्। नि:संशयं फलं लब्ध्वा दक्षो भूतिमुपाश्नुते॥
en: Adversity overpowers a person who is idle and lies down, whereas whoever is active reaps success and enjoys prosperity.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: अनर्थाः संशयावस्थाः सिद्ध्यन्ते मुक्त संशयाः। धीरा नराः कर्मरता ननु निःसंशयाः क्वचित्॥
en: Intelligent persons engaged confidently in acts consider all who are diffident as doubting and unsuccessful.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: एकान्तेन ह्यनर्थोऽयं वर्ततेऽस्मासु साम्प्रतम्। स तु निःसंशयं न स्यात् त्वयि कर्मण्यवस्थिते॥
en: Now we are overtaken by misfortune and if you engage in action this misfortune will certainly be removed.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: अथवा सिद्धिरेव स्यादभिमानं तदेव ते। वृकोदरस्य बीभत्सोमा॑त्रोश्च यमयोरपि॥
en: Even if you are unsuccessful it shall be proved to you. Vrikodara, Vivatsu and the twins (that you are unable to take the kingdom).

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: अन्येषां कर्म सफलमस्माकमपि वा पुनः। विप्रकर्षण बुध्येत कृतकर्मा यथाफलम्।॥
en: The actions of others have been seen crowned with success and ours might be as well; how can one, performing action, perceive beforehand what would be the result?

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: पृथिवीं लागलेनेह भित्त्वा बीजं वपत्युत। आस्तेऽथ कर्षकस्तूष्णीं पर्जन्यस्तत्र कारणम्॥
en: Having tilled the ground with plough one sows the seeds; the tiller then sits silent (for) the clouds are the next cause.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: वृष्टिश्चेन्नानुगृहणीयादनेनास्तत्र कर्षकः। यदन्यः पुरुषः कुर्यात् तत् कृतं सफलं मया॥
en: If however the clouds do not favour him the cultivator is not to blame-he says :-"I have done what others do."

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: तच्चेदं फलमस्माकमपराधो न मे क्वचित्। इतिधीरोऽन्ववेक्ष्यैव नात्मानं तत्र गर्हयेत्।।
en: If however I do not meet with success I am not to blame thinking this he contents himself and does not reproach himself.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: कुर्वतो नार्थसिद्धिर्मे भवतीति ह भारत। निर्वेदो नात्र कर्तव्यो द्वावन्यौ ह्या कारणम्॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, no one should despair saying, “I am working still I do not succeed," for besides exertion there are two other ause for success.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: सिद्धिर्वाप्यथवासिद्धिरप्रवृत्तिरतोऽन्यथा। बहूनां समवाये हि भावानां कर्म सिद्ध्यति॥
en: Success or failure, no one should despair, for success in action depends upon the union of many circumstances.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: गुणाभावे फलं न्यूनं भवत्यफलमेव च। अनारम्भे हि न फलं न गुणो दृश्यते क्वचित्॥
en: One element wanting proportionate success does not come or nothing at all; if however no exertion is made no success is acquired, nor any quality is seen.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: देशकालावुपायांश्च मङ्गलं स्वस्तिवृद्धये। युनक्ति मेधयाधीरो यथाशक्ति यथाबलम्॥
en: The man is by his intelligence and according to his might and power, brings place, time, means and auspicious rites for the acquisition of prosperity.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: अप्रमत्तेन तत् कार्यमुपदेष्टा पराक्रमः। भूयिष्ठं कर्मयोगेषु दृष्ट एव पराक्रमः॥
en: One should assiduously engage in action, his guide being his prowess; among the qualities necessary for action energy is the foremost.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: यत्रधीमानवेक्षेत श्रेयांसं बहुभिर्गुणैः। साम्नैवार्थं ततो लिप्सेत् कर्म चास्मै प्रयोजयेत्॥
en: If an intelligent man finds his enemy superior to him in many qualities he should accomplish his object by the arts of conciliation and proper appliances.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: व्यसनं वास्य काक्षेत विवासं वा युधिष्ठिर। अपि सिन्धोगिरेर्वापि किं पुनर्मर्त्यधर्मिणः॥
en: O Yudhishthira, he should wish for the calamity and banishment (of his foe), what of mortal men, even he be an ocean or a mountain.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: उत्थानयुक्तः सततं परेषामन्तरैषौ। आनृण्यमाप्नोति नरः परस्यात्मन एव च॥
en: A person, by actively praying into the holes of his enemy, satisfies a debt to himself as well as to his enemies.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: न त्वेवात्मावमन्तव्यः पुरुषेण कदाचन। न ह्यात्मपरिभूतस्य भूतिर्भवति शोभना॥
en: A man should never think ill of himself; whoever thinks ill of himself never earnis splendid prosperity.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: एवंसंस्थितिका सिद्धिरियं लोकस्य भारत। तत्र सिद्धिर्गतिः प्रोक्ता कालावस्थाविभागतः॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, the success of persons is thus situated; it is said that the course of success depends upon time and situation.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: ब्राह्मणं मे पिता पूर्वं वासयामास पण्डितम्। सोऽपि सर्वामिमां प्राह पित्रे मे भरतर्षभ॥ नीति बृहस्पतिप्रोक्ता भ्रातृन् मेऽचाहयत् पुरा। तेषां सकाशादौषमहमेतां तदा गृहे॥
en: In the days of yore my father housed a learned Brahmana; he said all this to my father, O foremost of Bharatas. My brothers, formerly accept from Brihaspati inoral precepts and then in our house I heard all this from them.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Yudhishthira
sn: स मां राजन् कर्मवतीमागतामाह सान्त्वयन्। शुश्रूषमाणामासीनां पितुरङ्के युधिष्ठिर॥
en: O king, O Yudhishthira, he said this to me, consoling, who had approached my father for some work and who for serving was seated on my father's lap.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच याज्ञसेन्या वचः श्रुत्वा भीमसेनो झमर्षणः। निःश्वसन्नुपसंगम्य क्रुद्धो राजानमब्रवीत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having heard these words of Yajnaseni (Draupadi), Bhimasena came to the king (Yudhishthira). And sighing in wrath, he thus spoke to him.

sn: राज्यस्य पदवीधयां व्रज सत्पुरुषोचिताम्। धर्मकामार्थहीनानां किं नो वस्तुं तपोवने॥
en: Bhima said: O king, walk as regards kingdoms in the customary path trodden by good men. What do you gain by living in the hermitage of the ascetics, thus deprived of Dharma, Artha and Kama?

sn: नैवधर्मेण तद् राज्यं नार्जवेन न चौजसा। अक्षकूटमधिष्ठाय हृतं दुर्योधनेन वै॥
en: Your kingdom has been robbed by Duryodhana by an unfair gambling at dice and not by virtue or by honesty or by prowess.

sn: गोमायुनेव सिंहानां दुर्बलेन बलीयसाम्। आमिषं विघसाशेन तद्वद् राज्यं हि नो हृतम्॥
en: He has robbed our kingdom like a weak offal-eating jackal that steals the prey from mighty lions.

sn: धर्मलेशप्रतिच्छन्नः प्रभवंधर्मकामयोः। अर्थमुत्सृज्य किं राजन् दुःखेषु परितप्यसे॥
en: O king, why do you, abandoning the wealth which is the source of both virtue and pleasures and in obedience of the (mere) trifling virtue of keeping one's promise, suffer such afflictions?

sn: भवतोऽनवधानेन राज्यं नः पश्यतां हृतम्। अहार्यमपि शक्रेण गुप्तं गाण्डीवधन्वना॥
en: Our kingdom, protected by the wielder of Gandiva (Arjuna) and incapable of being snatched from us by (even) Shakra (Indra), was robbed from us in our very sight (only) on account of your carelessness.

sn: कुणीनामिव बिल्वानि पशूनामिवधेनवः। हृतमैश्वर्यमस्माकं जीवतां भवतः कृते॥
en: It was for you, that notwithstanding we were alive, our prosperity was wrested from use like a fruit from one who is unable to use his arms or like kine from one who cannot use his legs.

sn: भवत: प्रियमित्येवं महद् व्यसनमीदृशम्। धर्मकामे प्रतीतस्य प्रतिपन्नाः स्म भारत॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, you are firin in the desire of acquiring virtue. It was to please you that we suffered ourselves to be overwhelmed with such calamities.

sn: कर्शयामः स्वमित्राणि नन्दयामश्च शात्रवान्। आत्मानं भवतां शास्त्रैर्नियम्य भरतर्षभ।॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, it was because we are at your command that we are giving pain to our friends and joy to our enemies.

sn: यद् वयं न तदैवैतान्धार्तराष्ट्रान् निहन्महि। भवतः शास्त्रमादाय तन्नस्तपति दुष्कृतम्॥
en: It was on our part an act of folly which gives me great pain that we did not, obeying your command, kill the sons of Dhritarashtra then and there.

sn: अथैनामन्ववेक्षस्व मृगचर्यामिवात्मनः। दुर्बलाचरितां राजन् न बलस्थैनिषेविताम्॥
en: O king, this your living in the forest like an wild animal is an act which only a weak man alone would submit to.

sn: यां न कृष्णो न बीभत्सु भिमन्युर्न संजयाः। न चाहमभिनन्दामि न च माद्रीसुतावुभौ॥
en: Your this act is approved of neither by Krishna, nor by Vivatsu (Arjuna), nor by Abhimanyu, nor by the Srinjayas, nor by myself, nor by the sons of Madri.

sn: भवान्धर्मोधर्म इति सततं व्रतकर्शितः। कच्चिद् राजन् न निर्वेदादापन्नः क्लीबजीविकाम्।।
en: Afflicted with your vow you always cry, "Virtue, virtue."O king, have you from despair become a man of no manliness?

sn: दुर्मनुष्या हि निर्वेदमफलं स्वार्थघातकम्। अशक्ताः श्रियमाहर्तुमात्मनः कुर्वते प्रियम्॥
en: Cowards only, being unable to win back their prosperity, cherish despair which is fruitless and destructive of one's own purpose.

sn: स भवान् दृष्टिमाञ्छक्तः पश्यन्नस्मासु पौरुषम्। आनृशंस्यपरो राजन् नानर्थमवबुध्यसे॥
en: You have ability and cyes. You see that we possess manliness. O king, it is because you have adopted a peaceful life that you do not feel (the pain of) this distress.

sn: अस्मानमीधार्तराष्ट्राः क्षममाणानलं सतः। अशक्तानिव मन्यन्ते तद् दुःखं नाहवे वधः॥
en: The sons of Dhritarashtra consider us, who are only forgiving, as men really incompetent and weak. O king, this gives me more pain than death in battle would have given me.

sn: तत्र चेद् युध्यमानानामजिह्ममनिवर्तिनाम्। सर्वशो हि वधः श्रेयान् प्रेत्य लोकान् लभेमहि॥
en: If we all die in a fair fight without turning our backs on our foes, even that would be better than this exile, for we shall then obtain regions of bliss.

sn: अथवा वयमेवैतान् निहत्य भरतर्षभ। आददीमहि गां सर्वां तथापि श्रेय एव नः॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, on the other hand if we become the ruler of the whole earth by killing them, that would be doing us a great good.

sn: सर्वथा कार्यमेतन्नः स्वधर्मनुतिष्ठताम्। काक्षतां विपुलां कीर्तिं वैरं प्रतिचिकीर्षताम्॥
en: This is our bounded duty, we who ever adhere to the duties of our own order, who are ever desirous of great achievements and who wish to take revenge on our enemies.

sn: आत्मार्थं युध्यमानानां विदिते कृत्यलक्षणे। अन्यैरपि हृते राज्ये प्रशंसैव न गर्हणा॥
en: Our kingdom having been robbed from us, if we (under the circumstances) engage in a war, our that act, when it well be known in the world, will bring praise and no condemnation.

sn: कर्शनार्थो हि योधर्मो मित्राणामात्मनस्तथा। व्यसनं नाम तद् राजन् नधर्मः स कुधर्म तत्॥
en: O king, the virtue, that produces affliction on one's ownself and on one's own friends, is no virtue, at all. It is vice that produces calamities.

sn: सर्वथाधर्मनित्यं तु पुरुषंधर्मदुर्बलम्। त्यजतस्तात्धर्मार्थों प्रेतं दुःखसुखे यथा॥
en: O sire, virtue is sometimes (the indirect cause of) the weakness of men. Dharina and Artha forsake such men, as pain and pleasure forsake a dead man.

sn: यस्यधर्मो हिधर्मार्थं क्लेशभाङ् न स पण्डितः। न सधर्मस्य वेदार्थं सूर्यस्यान्धः प्रभामिव॥
en: He who practices virtue only for the sake of virtue always suffers afflictions. He can never be called a wise man. He cannot know the (real) purpose of virtue, as a blind man is incapable of seeing the light of the sun.

sn: यस्य चार्थार्थमेवार्थः स च नार्थस्य कोविदः। रक्षेत भृतकोऽरण्ये यथा गास्तादृगेव सः॥
en: He who considers that his wealth exists for himself alone does not at all understand the purpose of wealth. He is like the servant tending kine in the forest.

sn: अतिबेलं हि योऽर्थार्थी नेतरावनुतिष्ठति। स वध्यः सर्वभूतानां ब्रह्महेव जुगुप्सितः॥
en: He, again, who pursues Artha (profit or wealth) too much without pursuing Dharma (virtue) and Kama (pleasure) deserves to be censured and killed by all creatures.

sn: सततं यश्च कामार्थी नेतरावनुतिष्ठति। मित्राणि तस्य नश्यन्तिधर्मार्थाभ्यां च हीयते॥
en: He who always pursues Kama without pursuing Dharma and Artha loses his friends and also loses virtue and profit.

sn: तस्यधर्मार्थहीनस्य कामान्ते निधनंध्रुवम्। कामतो रममाणस्य मीनस्येवाम्भसः क्षये॥
en: Such a man, indulging in pleasure at will becoming destitute of virtue and profit, meets with certain death at the expiration of the period of enjoyment, as the fish dies when the water is dried up.

sn: तस्माद्धर्मार्थयोर्नित्यं न प्रमाद्यन्ति पण्डिताः। प्रकृतिः सा हि कामस्य पावकस्यारणिर्यथा॥
en: It is for this, those that are wise always pursue both virtue and profit, for the union of virtue and profit is the essential requisite of pleasure, as wood is of fire.

sn: सर्वथाधर्ममूलोऽर्थोधर्मश्चार्थपरिग्रहः। इतरेतरयो तौ विद्धि मेघोदधी यथा॥
en: Pleasure has always virtue for its root and virtue is always united with pleasure. Know that both are dependent on one another, as the ocean and the clouds (depend on each other).

sn: द्रव्यार्थस्पर्शसंयोगे या प्रीतिरुपजायते। स कामश्चित्तसंकल्पः शरीरं नास्य दृश्यते॥
en: The sensation that one feels in consequence of the contact with the objects of touch or in consequence of the possession of wealth is called pleasure. It exists in the mind and has no corporeal existence.

sn: अर्थार्थी पुरुषो राजन् बृहन्तंधर्ममिच्छति। अर्थमिच्छति कामार्थी न कामादन्यमिच्छति॥
en: O king, he that wishes to have Artha should seek a large share of virtue. Those that wish Karma should seek (also) Artha, but Kama does not yield any thing in return.

sn: न हि कामेन कामोऽन्यः साध्यते फलमेव तत्। उपयोगात् फलस्यैव काष्ठाद् भस्मेव पण्डितैः॥
en: Pleasure brings its own fruit; it cannot lead to another (pleasure). Ashes may be had from wood, but nothing could be had from ashes.

sn: इमाञ्छकुनकान् राजन् हन्ति वैतंसिको यथा। एतद् रूपमधर्मस्य भूतेषु हि विहिंसता॥ कामाल्लोभाच्चधर्मस्य प्रकृति यो न पश्यति। स बध्यः सर्वभूतानां प्रेत्य चेह च दुर्मतिः॥
en: O king, as a fowler kills the birds, so does sin kill all the creatures of the world. He who, being misled by pleasure and covetousness, does not understand the nature of virtue, deserves to be killed by all. He becomes a wretch here and hereafter (after death).

sn: व्यक्तं ते विदितो राजत्रों द्रव्यपरिग्रहः। प्रकृतिं चापि वेत्थास्य विकृतिं चापि भूयसीम्॥
en: O king, it is evident that you know that pleasure is to be derived from virtuous objects of enjoyments. You also know (what) their ordinary states as well as their great changes (are).

sn: तस्य नाशे विनाशे वा जरया मरणेन वा। अनर्थ इति मन्यन्ते सोऽयमस्मासु वर्तते॥
en: From their (objects of enjoyment's) loss, destruction, decrepitude and death, arises what is called affliction. That affliction has overtaken us.

sn: इन्द्रियाणां च पञ्चानां मनसो हृदयस्य च। विषये वर्तमानानां या प्रीतिरुपजायते॥ स काम इति मे बुद्धिः कर्मणां फलमुत्तमम्।
en: The pleasure that is produce by the five senses, by the mind and by the heart being directed to the objects proper to each, is in my opinion, one of the best fruits of our actions.

sn: एवमेव पृथग् दृष्ट्वाधर्मार्थो काममेव च।॥ नधर्मपर एव स्यान्न चार्थपरमो नरः। न कामपरमो वा स्यात् सर्वान् सेवेत सर्वदा॥ धर्म पूर्वेधनं मध्ये जघन्ये काममाचरेत्। अहन्यनुचरेदेवमेष शास्त्रकृतो विधिः॥
en: Thus Dharma, Artha and Kama should be taken into one's consideration one after the other. One should not pursue virtue alone. No man should consider profit or pleasure as the highest object of his desire. All the three should always be (equally) pursued. The Shastras ordain that one should pursue virtue in the morning, profit at noon and pleasure in the evening.

sn: काम पूर्वेधनं मध्ये जघन्येधर्ममाचरेत्। वयस्यनुचरेदेवमेष शास्त्रकृतो विधिः॥
en: The Shastras ordain that one should pursue pleasure in the first, profit in the second and virtue in the last portion of his life.

sn: धर्मं चार्थं च कामं च यथावद् वदतां वर। विभज्य काले कालज्ञः सर्वान् सेवेत पण्डितः॥
en: O foremost of eloquent men, those that are learned and fully conversant with the proper divisions of time, dividing their time properly, pursue all three, Dharma Artha and Kama.

sn: मोक्षो वा परमं श्रेय एष राजान् सुखार्थिनाम्। प्राप्तिर्वा बुद्धिमास्थाय सोपायां कुरुनन्दन॥ तद् वाऽऽशु क्रियतां राजन् प्राप्तिर्वाप्यधिगम्यताम्। जीवितं ह्यातुरस्येव दुःखमन्तरवर्तिनः॥
en: O king, O descendant of Kuru, whether freedom from all these three (Dharma, Artha and Kama) or possession of them is the better course for those that desire happiness, should be settled by you after careful thought. O king, you should then without the least hesitation act either to achieve them or to abandon them, for he who lives wavering between the two becomes most miserable.

sn: विदितश्चैव मेधर्मः सततं चरितश्च ते। जानन्तस्त्वयि शसन्ति सुहृदः कर्मचोदनाम्॥
en: It is well that your conduct is ever regulated by virtue. Knowing this, your sensible friends advise you to act (thus).

sn: दानं यज्ञाः सतां पूजा वेदधारणमार्जवम्। एषधर्मः परो राजन् बलवान् प्रेत्य चेह च॥
en: O king, gift, sacrifice, adoration to the honest, study of the Vedas and honesty, these are the highest virtues strong both here and hereafter.

sn: एष नार्थविहीनेन शक्यो राजन् निषेवितुम्। अखिलाः पुरुषव्याघ्र गुणाः स्युर्यद्यपीतरे॥
en: But, O foremost of men, these virtues, cannot be attained by one that has no wealth, even if he possess infinite other accomplishments.

sn: धर्ममूलं जगद् राजन् नान्यद्धर्माद् विशिष्यते। धर्मश्चार्थेन महता शक्यो राजन् निषेवितुम्॥
en: O king, the universe depends on virtue. There is nothing higher than virtue. O king, virtue is attainable (only) by those who possess wealth.

sn: न चार्थो भैक्ष्यचर्येण नापि क्लैब्येन कर्हिचित्। वेत्तुं शक्यः सदा राजन् केवलंधर्मबुद्धिना॥
en: But wealth cannot be acquired by leading the life of a mendicant nor by bearing a life of weakness. O king, wealth can be earned by virtuous intelligence.

sn: प्रतिषिद्धा हि ते याचा यया सिद्ध्यति वै द्विजः। तेजसैवार्थलिप्सायां यतस्व पुरुषर्षभ॥
en: O best of men, in your case, begging, which is a success to the Brahmanas, has been forbidden. Therefore try to acquire wealth by prowess and energy.

sn: भैक्ष्यचर्या न विहिता न च विट्शूद्रजीविका। क्षत्रियस्य विशेषेणधर्मस्तु बलमौरसम्॥
en: It is not proper for you to lead a life of mendicancy or the life of Shudra. Prowess and energy constitute the special virtue of the Kshatriya.

sn: स्वधर्म प्रतिपद्यस्व जहि शत्रून् समागतान्। धार्तराष्ट्रवनं पार्थ मया पार्थेन नाशय॥
en: Therefore, O son of Pritha, perform the duty of your own (order) and destroy the enemies. Destroy the prowess of the sons of Dhritarashtra with my help and with that of Partha (Arjuna).

sn: उदारमेव विद्वांसोधर्मं प्राहुर्मनीषिणः। उदारं प्रतिपद्यस्व नावरे स्थातुमर्हसि॥
en: The wise and learned man says that prosperity is virtue. Therefore, acquire prosperity, for you ought not to be in frivolity.

sn: अनुबुध्यस्व राजेन्द्र वेत्थधर्मान् सनातनान्। क्रूरकर्माभिजातोऽसि यस्मादुद्विजते जनः॥
en: O king of kings, awake and understand the eternal virtues (of one's own order). You belong by birth to an order the acts of which are cruel and are the sources of pain to others.

sn: प्रजापालनसम्भूतं फलं तव न गर्हितम्। एष ते विहितो राजन्धानाधर्मः सनातनः॥
en: O king, cherish your subjects and reap the fruits (of that good act) that can never be wrong. This is the eternal duty ordained (for us the Kshatriyas) by the Creator himself.

sn: तस्मादपचितः पार्थ लोके हास्यं गमिष्यसि। स्वधर्माद्धि मनुष्याणां चलनं न प्रशस्यते॥
en: O son of Pritha, if you fall off from it, you will be the laughing stock (of all men). Deviation from the duties of one's own (order) is never praised.

sn: स क्षात्रं हृदयं कृत्वा त्यक्तवेदं शिथिलं मनः। वीर्यमास्थाय कौरव्यधुरमुबहधुर्यवत्॥
en: O descendant of Kuru, therefore, making your heart as the order in which you belong requires it and abandoning this your course of weakness, summon prowess an bear your weight (of duty) like one that bears it manfully.

sn: न हि केवलधर्मात्मा पृथिवीं जातु कश्चन। पार्थिवो व्यजयद् राजन् न भूतिं न पुनः श्रियम्॥
en: O king, no monarch can acquire the sovereignty of earth or prosperity or affluence by means of being only virtuous-minded.

sn: जिह्वां दत्त्वा बहूनां हि क्षुद्राणां लुब्धचेतसाम्। निकृत्या लभते राज्यमाहारमिव शल्यकः॥
en: As a fowler catches a flock of very easilytempled games by offering them some attractive food, so does an intelligent man acquire a kingdom by offering bribes to his enemy's men and covetous enemies.

sn: भ्रातरः पूर्वजाताश्च सुसमृद्धाश्च सर्वशः। निकृत्या निर्जिता देवैरसुराः पार्थिवर्षभ॥
en: O foremost of monarchs, the Asuras, though they were elder brothers of the Devas and though they in affluence were, vanquished by the Devas by mean of Stratagem.

sn: एवं बलवतः सर्वमिति बुद्ध्वा महीपते। जहि शत्रून् महाबाहो परां निकृतिमास्थितः॥
en: O mighty armed hero, O ruler of the world, thus everything belongs to those that possess might. Destroy enemy by means of stratagem.

sn: न ह्यर्जुनसमः कश्चिद् युधि योद्धाधनुर्धरः। भविता वा पुमान् कश्चिन्मत्समो वा गदाधरः॥
en: There is none equal to Arjuna in wielding the bow in battle. There is none equal to me in wielding the mace.

sn: सत्त्वेन कुरुते युद्धं राजन् सुबलवानपि। अप्रमादी महोत्साही सत्त्वस्थो भव पाण्डव॥
en: O king, men of prowess engage in battle depending on their prowess alone and not on the strength of numbers and not on information of the enemy' plan through spies. O son of Pandu, therefore exert your prowess. were

sn: ते सत्त्वं हि मूलमर्थस्य वितथं यदतोऽन्यथा। न तु प्रसक्तं भवति वृक्षच्छायेव हैमनी॥
en: Prowess is the root of wealth; whatever else is called its root is not so. As the shade of the tree in winter is useless, so is everything fruitless without prowess.

sn: अर्थत्यागोऽपि कार्यः स्यादर्थं श्रेयांसमिच्छता। बीजौपम्येन कौन्तेय मा भूदन्न संशयः॥
en: O son of Kunti, wealth should be spent in the way that seeds are scattered on the ground by one who wishes to increase it. Let there be no doubt (about it) in your mind.

sn: अर्थेन तु समो नार्थो यत्र लभ्येत नोदयः। न तत्र विपणः कार्यः खरकण्डूयनं हि तत्॥
en: But where wealth is more than sufficient, there should be no expenditure of wealth. In such cases investment of wealth is like the scratching of an ass, which is first pleasurable and then painful.

sn: एवमेव मनुष्येन्द्रधर्मं त्यक्त्वाल्पकं नरः। बृहन्तंधर्ममाप्नोति स बुद्ध इति निश्चितम्॥
en: O king of men, a man, who in order to earn a greater measure of virtue casts away like seeds the little virtue that he is sticking to, is certainly considered to be wise.

sn: अमित्रं मित्रसम्पन्नं मित्रैर्भिन्दन्ति पण्डिताः। भिन्नैर्मित्रैः परित्यक्तं दुर्बलं कुर्वते वशम्॥
en: Those, that are learned, alienate the friends of the foe that possesses friends. Having thus weakened him by making his friends abandon him, they bring him to subjugation.

sn: सत्त्वेन कुरुते युद्धं राजन् सुबलवानपि। नोद्यमेन न होत्राभिः सर्वाः स्वीकुरुते प्रजाः॥
en: O king, those that are strong engage in battle by depending on their own courage. They do not conquer people by continued efforts or by the arts of conciliation.

sn: सर्वथा संहतैरेव दुर्बलैर्बलवानपि। अमित्रः शक्यते हन्तुं मधुहा भ्रमरैरिव॥
en: O king, sometimes those that are weak kill a powerful enemy by combination, as bees kill the spoiler of their honey by the force of their numbers.

sn: यथा राजन् प्रजाः सर्वाः सूर्यः पति गभस्तिभिः। अत्ति चैव तथैव त्वं सदृशः सवितुर्भव॥
en: O king, like the sun that sustains as well as destroys all creatures by this rays, you too adopt the ways of the sun.

sn: एतच्चापि तपो राजन् पुराणमिति नः श्रुतम्। विधिना पालनं भूमेर्यत् कृतं न पितामहैः॥
en: O king, it has been heard by us in the Puranas that to protect one's own kingdom and cherish one's own subjects, as was done by our forefathers, is a kind of Tapa (austerities).

sn: न तथा तपसा राजैल्लोकान् प्राप्नोति क्षत्रियः। यथा सृष्टेन युद्धेन विजयेनेतरेण वा॥
en: O king, a Kshatriya cannot acquire those regions of blessedness which he can by fair fight, whether (that fight) ends in victory or defeat.

sn: अपेयात् किल भाः सूर्याल्लक्ष्मीश्चन्द्रमसस्तथा। इति लोको व्यवसितो दृष्ट्वेमां भवतो व्यथाम्॥
en: Seeing your this affliction, (the people of) the world have come to this conclusion that light may (some day) forsake the sun and beauty may (some day) forsake the moon.

sn: भवतश्च प्रशंसाभिर्निन्दाभिरितरस्य च। कथायुक्ताः परिषदः पृथग राजन् समागताः॥
en: O king, the learned men, both separately and assembling together, talk with one another by praising you and blaming the other (Duryodhana).

sn: इदमभ्यधिकं राजन् ब्राह्मणाः कुरवश्च ते। समेताः कथयन्तीह मुदिताः सत्यसंधताम्॥
en: O king, over and above this the Brahmanas and the Kurus assembling together talk cheerfully of your great adherence to truth.

sn: यन्न मोहान्न कार्पण्या लोभान भयादपि। अनृतं किंचिदुक्तं ते न कामानार्थकारणात्॥
en: They say that you have never from delusion, from meanness, from covetousness, from fear, from desire or from wealth, uttered an untruth.

sn: यदेनः कुरुते किंचिद् राजा भूमिमवाप्नुवन्। सर्वं तन्नुदते पश्चाद् यज्ञैर्विपुलदक्षिणैः॥
en: Whatever sin a king commits in acquiring dominions, he consumes it all by means of performing sacrifices in which large Dakshinas are given away.

sn: ब्राह्मणेभ्यो ददद् ग्रामान् गाश्च राजन् सहस्रशः। मुच्यते सर्वपापेभ्यस्तमोभ्य इव चन्द्रमाः॥
en: O king, as the moon emerges from the clouds, so does a king emerge from all sins by bestowing thousands of villages and kine on the Brahmanas.

sn: पौरजानपदाः सर्वे प्रायशः कुरुनन्दन। सवृद्धबालसहिताः शंसन्ति त्वां युधिष्ठिर॥
en: O descendant of Kuru, O Yudhishthira, all the citizens and the inhabitants of the country, both young and old, praise you.

sn: श्वदृतौ क्षीरमासक्तं ब्रह्म वा वृषले यथा। सत्यं स्तेने बलं नार्यो राज्यं दुर्योधने तथा॥
en: "As milk in a bag made of a boar's hide, as the Vedas in a Shudra, as truth in a robber and as strength in a woman, so is sovereignty in Duryodhana.

sn: इति लोके निर्वचनं पुरश्चरति भारत। अपि चैताः स्त्रियो बाला: स्वाध्यायमधिकुर्वते॥
en: Thus talk the people among one another. O descendant of Bharata, even women and children are repeating it, as if it were a lesson they wanted to commit to memory.

sn: इमामवस्थां च गते सहास्माभिररिंदम। हन्त नष्टाः स्म सर्वे वै भवतोपद्रवे सति॥
en: O chastiser of foes, you have fallen into this state along with me. Alas! we too are lost with you on account of your this calamity.

sn: स भवान् रथमास्थाय सर्वोपकरणान्वितम्। त्वरमाणोऽभिनिर्यातु विप्रेभ्योऽर्थविभावकः॥ वाचयित्वा द्विजश्रेष्ठानद्यैव गजसाह्वयम्। अस्त्रविद्भिः परिवृतो भ्रातृभिर्दृढधन्विभिः॥ आशीविषसमैवीरैर्मरुद्भिरिव वृत्रहा। अमित्रांस्तेजसा मृद्गन्नसुरानिव वृत्रहा। श्रियमादत्स्व कौन्तेयधार्तराष्ट्रान् महावल॥
en: Therefore, ascending on your chariot, furnished with every implement of war and making the chief Brahmanas utter benedictions on you, march at once, even this very day, against Hastinapur, so that you may be able to give to the Brahmanas the spoils of your victory. Surrounded by your brothers, who are all great wielders of bows and by (other) heroes, who are all skilled in weapons and all like virulent snakes, start (at once) like the slayer of Vritra (Indra) surrounded by the Marutas. Destroy with your prowess your weak enemies as the slayer of Vritra (Indra) destroyed the Asuras. O son of Kunti, snatch away from the son of Dhritarashtra (Duryodhana) the prosperity he (now) enjoys.

sn: न हि गाण्डीवमुक्तानां शराणां गार्धवाससाम्। स्पर्शमाशीविषाभानां मर्त्यः कश्चन संसहेत्॥
en: There is no mortal who can withstand the touch of the arrows which are equipped with the feathers of vulture and which are like the snakes of virulent poison when these are shot from the Gandiva (bow).

sn: न स वीरो न मातङ्गो न च सोऽश्वोऽस्ति भारत। यः सहेत गदावेगं मम क्रुद्धस्य संयुगे॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, there is not a warrior, nor an elephant, nor an horse that can withstand the force of my mace when I am angry in battle.

sn: सृञ्जयैः सह कैकेयैर्वृष्णीनां वृषभेण च। कथंस्विद् युधि कौन्तेय न राज्यं प्राप्नुयामहे॥
en: O son of Kunti, why should we not snatch back our kingdom from our foe after fighting a great battle with the help of the Srinjayas the Kaikeyas and the chief of the Vrishnis.

sn: शत्रुहस्तगतां राजन् कथंस्विन्नाहरेर्महीम्। इह यत्नमुपाहृत्य बलेन महतान्वितः॥
en: O king, why should we not succeed in Snatching away the (sovereignty of the) earth from the hands of our enemy? Let us but try with the help of a large army.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच स एवमुक्तस्तु महानुभावः सत्यव्रतो भीमसेनेन राजा। अजातशत्रुस्तदनन्तरं वै धैर्यान्वितो वाक्यमिदं बभाषे॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having been thus addressed by Bhimasena, the high-souled and ever devoted to truth, Ajatashatru (Yudhishthira), mastering his patience, thus spoke after a few moments.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच असंशयं भारत सत्यमेतद् यन्मां तुदन् वाक्यशल्यैः क्षिणोषि। न त्वां विगहें प्रतिकूलमेव ममानयाद्धि व्यसनं व आगात्॥
en: Yudhishthira said: O descendant of Bharata, no doubt all this is true. I cannot reproach you for giving me pain by piercing me with your arrow words. From my folly alone this great calamity has overtaken you all.

sn: अहं ह्यक्षानन्वपद्यं जिहीर्षन् राज्यं सराष्ट्रधृतराष्ट्रस्य पुत्रात्। तन्मां शठः कितवः प्रत्यदेवीत् सुयोधनार्थं सुबलस्य पुत्रः॥
en: I was engaged to play at dice with the desire of snatching from Dhritarashtra's son his kingdom with its sovereignty. It was thus that the cunning gambler, the son of Subala (Shakuni), played with me on behalf of Suyodhana (Duryodhana).

sn: महामायः शकुनिः पर्वतीयः सभामध्ये प्रवपन्नक्षपूगान्। अमायिनं मायया प्रत्यजैषीत् ततोऽपश्यं वृजिनं भीमसेन॥
en: Bhimasena, that dweller of the mountainous country, Shakuni, is exceedingly artful. Plying at dice in the midst of the assembly-unacquainted as I am with the artifices of any kind, he defeated me by adopting all possible artful means. It is therefore we have been overwhelmed with this c:lamity.

sn: अक्षांश्च दृष्ट्वा शकुनेर्यथावत् कामानुकूलानयुजो युजश्च। शक्यो नियन्तुमभविष्यदात्मा मन्युस्तु हन्यात् पुरुषस्यधैर्यम्॥
en: Seeing the dice obedient to the wishes of Shakuni in Ayuja and Yuja (odds and evens), I could have controlled my mind, but anger (you know) drives off a person's patience.

sn: यन्तुं नात्मा शक्यते पौरुषेण मानेन वीर्येण च तात नद्धः। न ते वाचो भीमसेनाभ्यसूये मन्ये तथा तद् भवितव्यमासीत्॥
en: O child, the mind cannot be controlled when it is influenced by manliness, pride and prowess. O Bhimasena, I do not reproach you for what you have said. I consider that what have happened was preordained.

sn: स नो राजाधृतराष्ट्रस्य पुत्रो न्यपातयद् व्यसने राज्यमिच्छन्। दास्यं च नोऽगमयद् भीमसेन यत्राभवच्छरणं द्रौपदी नः॥
en: O Bhimasena, when the king (Duryodhana) the son of Dhritarashtra, wishing to get possession of our kingdom, plunged us into misery and even slavery, it was Draupadi who rescued us.

sn: त्वं चापि तद् वेत्थधनंजयश्च पुन तायागतानां सभां नः। यन्माऽब्रवीद्धृतराष्ट्रस्य पुत्र एकग्लहार्थं भरतानां समक्षम्॥
en: When summoned again to the Sabha for playing once more, you as well as Arjuna know what the son of Dhritarashtra told me in the presence of the Bharatas.

sn: वने समा द्वादश राजपुत्र यथाकामं विदितमजातशत्रो। अथापरं चाविदितं चरेथाः। सर्वैः सह भ्रातृभिश्छद्मगूढः॥
en: (He said), "O prince Ajatashatru, you shall have to live for twelve years with all your brothers (if defeated in the play) in the forest which you will chose to dwell in, but which must be known to all men; you shall have to spend the thirteenth year in disguise without your whereabouts being known to anybody.

sn: मवभोत्स्यन्ते भरतानां चराश्च। अन्यांश्चरेथास्तावतोऽब्दांस्तथा त्वं निश्चित्य तत् प्रतिजानीहि पार्थ॥
en: O sire, O son of Pritha, (if during that period) spies of the Bharatas, hearing of you, become successful in discovering you, you shall then have again to live in the forest for the same period passing once more the last year in secrecy. Reflecting on this, pledge yourself to it.

sn: चरेश्चेन्नोऽविदितः कालमेतं युक्तो राजन् मोहयित्वा मदीयान्। ब्रवीमि सत्यं कुरुसंसदीह तवैव ता. भारत पञ्च नद्यः॥
en: O king, as regards myself, I pledge myself in this assembly of the Kurus, if you can pass this period of time evading the vigilance of my spies and if you can remain undiscovered by them, then O descendant of Bharata, this kingdom of the five rivers will be once more yours.

sn: वयं चैतद् भारत सर्व एव त्वया जिताः कालमपास्य भोगान्। वसेम इत्याह पुरा स राजा मध्ये कुरूणां स मयोक्तस्तथेति॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, we also, if defeated by you at play, shall all of us, abandoning all our wealth, pass other same period according to the same rules." Thus said that king in the midst of the Kurus; and I said "So Be it."

sn: तत्र द्यूतमभवन्नो जघन्यं तस्मिञ्जिताः प्रव्रजिताश्च सर्वे। इत्थं तु देशाननुसंचरामो वनानि कृच्छ्राणि च कृच्छ्ररूपाः॥
en: The hateful play then began. We were defeated and we were all exiled. We are thus wandering miserably over difficult forests full of discomforts.

sn: सुयोधनश्चापि न शान्तिमिच्छन् भूयः स मन्योर्वशमन्वगच्छत्। उद्योजयामास कुरूंश्च सर्वान् ये चास्य केचिद् वशमन्वगच्छन्॥
en: Suyodhana (Duryodhana), however, having been not satisfied (with what he had done), gave himself up to anger and urged the Kurus and all those who were under his away to express their joy at our distress.

sn: को नाम जह्यादिह राज्यहेतोः। आर्यस्य मन्ये मरणाद् गरीयो यद्धर्ममुत्क्रम्य महीं प्रशासेत्॥
en: Having entered into such a pledge in the presence of all the pious and good men, who can now dare break it for the sake of a kingdom in this world? For in my opinion, to a respectable person death is not more serious than an act of transgression in order to gain a kingdom.

sn: तदैव चेद् वीर कर्माकरिष्यो यदा द्यूते परिघं पर्यमृक्षः। बाहू दिधक्षन् वारितः फाल्गुनेन किं दुष्कृतं भीम तदाभविष्यत्॥
en: O hero, you desired to burn my hand at the time of the play; you were, however, prevented by Arjuna and you only squeezed your mace. O Bhima, if you had done it, this calamity could not then befall us.

sn: प्रागेव चैवं समयक्रियायाः किं नाब्रवीः पौरुषमाविदानाः। प्राप्तं तु कालं त्वभिपद्य पश्चात् किं मामिदानीमतिवेलमात्य॥
en: O Bhima, conscious as you are of your prowess, why did you not say so before we entered into such an agreement? Having already burdened myself with the pledge made at that time what is the use of your speaking to me these harsh words (now)?

sn: भूयोऽपि दुःखं मम भीमसेन दूये विषस्येव रसं हि पीत्वा। यद् याज्ञसेनी परिक्लिश्यमानां संदृश्य तत् क्षान्तमिति स्म भीम॥
en: O Bhimasena, this was my great grief that I could not do anything when I saw Yajnaseni (Draupadi) persecuted in that way. O Bhima, my heart burns on account of this, as if I have drunk some poisonous liquid.

sn: न त्वद्य शक्यं भरतप्रवीर कृत्वा यदुक्तं कुरुवीरमध्ये। कालं प्रतीक्षस्व सुखोदयस्य पक्तिं फलानामिव बीजवापः॥
en: O foremost of the Bharata race, having made the pledge in the presence of the Kurus there, I am unable (now) to violate it. Wait for the return of our better days, as scatterers of seed wait for the harvest.

sn: यदा हि पूर्वं निकृतो निकृन्तेद् वैरं सपुष्पं सफलं विदित्वा। महागुणं हरति हि पौरुषेण तदा वीरो जीवति जीवलोके॥ श्रियं च लोके लभते समग्रां मन्ये चास्मै शत्रवः संनमन्ते। मित्राणि चैनमचिराद् भजन्ते देवा इवेन्द्रमुपजीवन्ति चैनम्॥
en: When one that has been first injured succeeds in revenging himself upon his enemy at a time when the latter's enmity has borne fruits and flowers, he is regarded as one who has accomplished a great deed by his prowess. Such a brave man earns undying fame. Such a man obtains great prosperity. His enemies bow down to him and his friends gather round him, as the celestials cluster round Indra for protection.

sn: मम प्रतिज्ञां च निबोध सत्यां वृणेधर्मममृताज्जीविताच्च। राज्यं च पुत्राश्च यशोधनं च सर्वं न सत्यस्य कलामुपैति॥
en: Know my promise cannot be made false. I regard Dharma as superior to life itself and divinity. Kingdoms, sons, fame and wealth all these do not come up even to a sixteenth part of truth.

sn: भीमसेन उवाच संधिं कृत्वैव कालेन ह्यन्तकेन पतत्त्रिणा। अनन्तेनाप्रमेयेण स्रोतसा सर्वहारिणा॥ प्रत्यक्षं मन्यसे कालं मर्त्यः सन् कालबन्धनः। फेनधर्मा महाराज फलधर्मा तथैव च॥
en: Bhima said : O great king, being mortal and unsubstantial as froth, unstable as fruit and dependant on time, how can you consider of any avail your having made an agreement in respect of Time, which is infinite and immeasurable, which passes as quickly as an arrow or a stream, carrying everything before it like death itself?

sn: निमेषादपि कौन्तेय यस्यायुरपचीयते। सूच्येवाञ्जनचूर्णस्य किमिति प्रतिपालयेत्॥
en: O son of Kunti, how can he wait whose life is shortened every moment, as a quantity of collyrium is lessened each time, a grain is taken up by the needle?

sn: यो नूनममितायुः स्यादथवापि प्रमाणवित्। स कालं वै प्रतीक्षेत सर्वप्रत्यक्षदर्शिवान्॥
en: Only he whose life has no limit or he who knows with certainty what the period of his life (really) is or he who knows the future as if it were placed before his eyes can wait for the arrival of (a certain fixed) time.

sn: प्रतीक्ष्यमाणः कालो न: समा राजस्त्रयोदश। आयुषोऽपचयं कृत्वा मरणायोपनेष्यति।॥
en: O king, if we wait for thirteen years, that period of time will shorten our lives and bring us nearer to death.

sn: शरीरिणां हि मरणं शरीरे नित्यमाश्रितम्। प्रागेव मरणात् तस्माद् राज्यायैव घटामहे॥
en: Wealth is ever established in every creature having corporeal body. Therefore we should try to get possession of our kingdom before we meet with death.

sn: यो न याति प्रसंख्यानमस्पष्टो भूमिवर्धनः। अयातयित्वा वैराणि सोऽवसीदति गौरिव॥
en: He who fails to achieve fame by not chastising his enemies is like a thing unclean. He is an useless burden of the earth as a brute is and perishes with ignominy.

sn: यो न यातयते वैरमल्पसत्त्वोद्यमः पुमान्। अफलं जन्म तस्याहं मन्ये दुर्जातजायिनः॥
en: The man, who being destitute of strength and courage, fails to chastise his enemies lives in vain. I consider such a man as low-born.

sn: हैरण्यौ भवतो बाहू श्रुतिर्भवति पार्थिवी। हत्वा द्विषन्तं संग्रामे भुड्क्ष्व बाहुजितं वसु॥
en: Your hand can shower gold; your fame spreads over the whole earth. Therefore, killing your enemies in battle, enjoy the wealth acquired by the strength of your arms.

sn: हत्वा वै पुरुषो राजन् निकर्तारमरिदम्। अह्राय नरकं गच्छेत् स्वर्गेणास्य स सम्मितः॥
en: O king, O chastiser of foes, if a man goes to hell on the very day he kills his injurer, that hell at once becomes heaven to him.

sn: अमर्षजो हि संतापः पावकाद् दीप्तिमत्तरः। येनाहमभिसंतप्तो न नक्तं न दिवा शये॥
en: The pain that one feels in suppressing his anger is more burning than fire itself. I burn with it even now and I cannot sleep either in the night or in the day.

sn: अयं च पार्थो बीभत्सुर्वरिष्ठो ज्याविकर्षणे। आस्ते परमसंतप्तो नूनं सिंह इवाशये॥
en: This son of Pritha, Vivatsu (Arjuna) is foremost in drawing the bow-string. He is certainly much aggrieved, though he lives (quietly) like a lion in its den.

sn: योऽयमेकोऽभिमनुते सर्वान् लोकेधनुर्भृतः। सोऽयमात्मजमूष्माणं महाहस्तीव यच्छति॥
en: This one (Arjuna) who desires to kill all the wielders of bow of the world without any body's) help, suppresses his wrath within his breast like a great elephant.

sn: नकुलः सहदेवश्च वृद्धा माता च वीरसूः। तवैव प्रियमिच्छन्त आसते जडमूकवत्॥
en: Nakula, Sahadeva, the old mother of heroes (Kunti) are all sitting like dumb people in order to please you.

sn: सर्वे ते प्रियमिच्छन्ति बान्धवाः सह सृञ्जयैः। अहमेकश्च संतप्तो माता च प्रतिविन्ध्यतः॥
en: All our friends with the Srinjayas wish to , please you. Only I and the mother of Prativindhya, (Draupadi) are greatly aggrieved.

sn: प्रियमेव तु सर्वेषां यद् ब्रवीम्युत किंचन। सर्वे हि व्यसनं प्राप्ताः सर्वे युद्धाभिनन्दिनः॥
en: And speak to you. Whatever I speak is (surely) agreeable to them all, for they plunged in great affliction eagerly wish for the battle.

sn: नातः पापीयसी काचिदापद् राजन् भविष्यति। यन्नो नीचरैल्पबलै राज्यमाच्छिद्य भुज्यते॥
en: O king, what greater calamity would befall us than that our kingdom should be snatched away from us and enjoyed by weak and contemptible foes!

sn: शीलदोषाद् घृणाविष्ट आनृशंस्यात् परंतप। क्लेशांस्तितिक्षसे राजन् नान्यः कश्चित् प्रशंसति॥
en: O chastiser of foes, (only) from the weakness of your character you feel shame to violate the pledge you made. But O king, none praises you for your this kindly disposition.

sn: श्रोत्रियस्येव ते राजन् मन्दकस्याविपश्चितः। अनुवाकहता बुद्धिर्नैषा तत्त्वार्थदर्शिनी॥
en: O king, your intellect cannot see the truth like that of a foolish and ignorant man, though of high birth, who has committed to memory the Vedas without understanding them. sons

sn: घृणी ब्राह्मणरूपोऽसि कथं क्षत्रेऽभ्यजायथाः। अस्यां हि योनौ जायन्ते प्रायशः क्रूरबुद्धयः॥
en: You are kind as a Brahmana; how have you been born in the Kshatriya order? Those born in it (the Kshatriya order) are generally crooked-minded.

sn: अश्रौषीस्त्वं राजधर्मान् यथा वै मनुरब्रवीत्। क्रूरान् निकृतिसम्पन्नान् विहितानशमात्मकान्॥ धार्तराष्ट्रान् महाराज क्षमसे किं दुरात्मनः। कर्तव्ये पुरुषव्याघ्र किमास्से पीठसर्पवत्॥ बुद्ध्या वीर्येण संयुक्तः श्रुतेनाभिजनेन च।
en: You have heard the duties of kings told by Manu, they are fraught with crookedness and unfairness, they are perfectly opposed to peace and virtue. O great king, why do you then forgive the wicked-minded of Dhritarashtra. O foremost of men, why are you silent in performing your duties being a man of ' high birth?

sn: तृणानां मुष्टिनैकेन हिमवन्तं च पर्वतम्॥ छन्नमिच्छसि कौन्तेय योऽस्मान् संवर्तुमिच्छसि।
en: O son of Kunti, who wishes to conceal the Himalayas by means of a handful of grass.

sn: अज्ञातचर्या गूढेन पृथिव्यां विश्रुतेन च॥ दिवीव पार्थ सूर्येण न शक्याचरितं त्वया।
en: Known as you are all over the world, you will hardly be able to live unknown and undiscovered. O son of Pritha, the sun can never pass through the sky unknown to men.

sn: बृहच्छाल इवानूपे शाखापुष्यपलाशवान्॥ हस्ती श्वेत इवाज्ञातः कथं जिष्णुश्चरिष्यति।
en: A large tree with spreading branches; flowers and with leaves in a well watered place (can never remain hidden). Nor can the Airavat (Indra's elephant). How will Jishnu (Arjuna) be able to live undiscovered and unknown?

sn: इमौ च सिंहसंकाशौ भ्रातरौ सहितौ शिशू॥ नकुलः सहदेवश्च कथं पार्थ चरिष्यतः।
en: How will these lion-like young children, together with the two brothers. Nakula and Sahadeva, O son of Pritha, be able to live in secrecy?

sn: पुण्यकीर्ती राजपुत्री द्रौपदी वीरसूयिरम्॥ विश्रुता कथमज्ञाता कृष्णा पार्थ चरिष्यति।
en: The mother of heroes, the princess Draupadi of virtuous deeds. O son of Pritha, how will this Krishna be able to live undiscovered and unknown?

sn: मां चापि राजञ्जानन्ति ह्याकुमारमिमाः प्रजाः॥ नाज्ञातचर्यां पश्यामि मेरोरिव निगूहनम्।
en: O king, all the people know me from my childhood. I do not see how I shall be able to live undiscovered and unknown. The Meru (mountains) might as well be concealed!

sn: तथैव बहवोऽस्माभी राष्ट्रेभ्यो विप्रवासिताः॥ राजानो राजपुत्राश्चधृतराष्ट्रमनुव्रताः। न हि तेऽप्युपशाम्यन्ति निकृता वा निराकृताः॥
en: Then again many kings have been driven away from their kingdoms. These kings and princes will all follow the wicked son of Dhritarashtra. For robbed and exiled by us, they cannot be friendly towards us.

sn: अवश्यं तैर्निकर्तव्यमस्माकं तत्प्रियैषिभिः। तेऽप्यस्मासु प्रयुञ्जीरन् प्रच्छन्नान् सुबहूंश्चरान्। आचक्षीरंश्च नो ज्ञात्वा तत: स्यात् सुमहद् भयम्।३१।।
en: They will certainly seek to injure us with the desire of doing good to him (Duryodhana); and they will certainly set against us many spies in disguise. If they discover us and report it, a great calamity will (then) befall us.

sn: अस्माभिरुषिताः सम्यग्वने मासास्त्रयोदश। परिमाणेन तान् पश्य तावतः परिवत्सरान्॥
en: We have already lived in the forest for full thirteen months. Consider them for their length as full thirteen years.

sn: अस्ति मास: प्रतिनिधिर्यथा प्राहुर्मनीषिणः। पूतिकामिव सोमस्य तथेदं क्रियतामिति॥
en: The wise men have said that a month is (but) a substitute for a year, as Pritika is considered as a substitute for the Soma.

sn: अथवानडुहे राजन् साधवे साधुवाहिने। सौहित्यदानादेतस्मादेनसः प्रतिमुच्यते॥
en: O king, (if you violate the pledge) you may free yourself from its sin by offering good food to a well-conducted bull which carries sacred burdens.

sn: तस्माच्छत्रुवधे राजन् क्रियतां निश्चयस्त्वया। क्षत्रियस्य हि सर्वस्य नान्योधर्मोऽस्ति संयुगात्॥
en: O king, therefore make up your mind to kill your enemies. There is no virtue higher to a Kshatriya than battle.

description: Pandavas entrance into the Kamyaka forest
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच भीमसेनवचः श्रुत्वा कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः। निःश्वस्य पुरुषव्याघ्रः सम्प्रदध्यौ परंतपः॥ श्रुता मे राजधर्माश्च वर्णानां च विनिश्चयाः। आयत्यां च तदात्वे च यः पश्यति स पश्यति॥
en: Vaishampayana said : O foremost of men, having heard the words of Bhima, that chastiser of foes, the son of Kunti, Yudhishthira, sighed and reflected in silence. (He thought in his mind) “I have heard the duties of king recited to me. I have heard also the duties of the different orders. He sees truly who sees how to regulate his conduct both in the present and in the future.

description: Pandavas entrance into the Kamyaka forest
sn: धर्मस्य जानमानोऽहं गतिमवयां सुदुर्विदाम्। कथं बलात् करिष्यामि मेरोरिव विमर्दनम्॥
en: Knowing as I do the true course of Dharma, which is so difficult to be known, how can I forcibly grind it, which would be like my grinding the Meru (mountain)."

description: Pandavas entrance into the Kamyaka forest
sn: स मुहूर्तमिवध्यात्वा विनिश्चत्येतिकृत्यताम्। भीमसेनमिदं वाक्यमपदान्तरमब्रवीत्॥
en: Having thus reflected for a moment and having also settled in his mind) what he should do, he thus spoke to Bhimasena without allowing him to say anything.

description: Pandavas entrance into the Kamyaka forest
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच एवमेतन्महाबाहो यथा वदसि भारत। इदमन्यत् समादत्स्व वाच्यं मे वाक्यकोविद॥
en: Yudhishthira said: O descendant of Bharata, O mighty-armed hero, what you say is true. O best of speakers, listen (also) to what I say.

description: Pandavas entrance into the Kamyaka forest
sn: महापापानि कर्माणि यानि केवलसाहसात्। आरभ्यन्ते भीमसेन व्यथन्ते तानि भारत॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, O Bhimasena, the greatly sinful deeds that one wants to perforin depending only on his courage become a source of pain to him.

description: Pandavas entrance into the Kamyaka forest
sn: समुन्त्रिते सुविक्रान्ते सुकृते सुविचारिते। सिध्यन्त्यर्था महाबाहो दैवं चात्र प्रदक्षिणम्॥
en: But, O mighty-armed hero, whatever is performed with (due) deliberation, with welldirected prowess, with all (necessary) appliances and with much previous thought, is (always) seen to be successful (at the end.) The celestials themselves favour such acts.

description: Pandavas entrance into the Kamyaka forest
sn: यत् तु केवचापल्याद् बलदपोत्थितः स्वयम्। आरब्धव्यमिदं कार्यं मन्यसे शृणु तत्र मे॥
en: Hear something about the act which you think should be at once done from your pride of strength and restlessness of mind.

description: Pandavas entrance into the Kamyaka forest
sn: भूरिश्रवाः शलश्चैव जलसंधश्च वीर्यवान्। भीष्मो द्रोणश्च कर्णश्च द्रोणपुत्रश्च वीर्यवान्॥ धार्तराष्ट्रा दुराधर्षा दुर्योधनपुरोगमाः। सर्व एव कृतास्त्राश्च सततं चाततायिनः॥ राजानः पार्थिवाश्चैव येऽस्माभिरुपतापिताः। संश्रिताः कौरवं पक्षं जातस्नेहाश्च तं प्रति॥
en: Bhurishrava, Shalva, the powerful Jarasandha, Bhishma, Drona, Karna, the mighty son of Drona (Ashvathama). The invincible sons of Dhritarashtra Duryodhana and others, all are accomplished in arms and ever ready for battle. Those kings and the rulers of the world, who have been injured by us, have all taken the side of the Kurus; and their affection has grown towards them.

description: Pandavas entrance into the Kamyaka forest
sn: दुर्योधनहिते युक्ता न तथास्मासु भारत। पूर्णकोशा बलोपेताः प्रयतिष्यन्ति संगरे॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, they are engaged in seeking to do good to Duryodhana and not to us. With their treasury full and large army, they will try their best in the war (to defeat us).

description: Pandavas entrance into the Kamyaka forest
sn: सर्वे कौरवसैन्यस्य सपुत्रामात्यसैनिकाः। संविभक्ता हि मात्राभिर्भोगैरपि च सर्वशः॥
en: All the officers of the Kuru army with their sons and relatives have been honoured by Duryodhana with the presentation of wealth according to proper divisions.

description: Pandavas entrance into the Kamyaka forest
sn: दुर्योधनेन ते वीरा मानिताश्च विशेषतः। प्राणांस्त्यक्ष्यन्ति संग्रामे इति मे निश्चिता मतिः॥
en: These heroes have been much honored by Duryodhana. My firm conviction is that they will give their lives in battle for him,

description: Pandavas entrance into the Kamyaka forest
sn: समा यद्यपि भीष्मस्य वृत्तिरस्मासु तेषु च। द्रोणस्य च महाबाहो कृपस्य च महात्मनः॥ अवश्यं राजपिण्डस्तैर्निर्वेश्य इति मे मतिः। तस्मात् त्यक्ष्यन्ति संग्रामे प्राणानपि सुदुस्त्यजान्॥
en: O mighty-armed hero, though the behaviour of Bhishma, Drona and the high-souled Kripa is the same (to both parties). Yet it is my firin conviction that they would sacrifice in battle their lives, then which there is nothing dearer in this world, so that they might pay off (their debt) in the shape of royal favours which they enjoy.

description: Pandavas entrance into the Kamyaka forest
sn: सर्वे दिव्यास्त्रविद्वांसः सर्वेधर्मपरायणाः। अजेयाश्चेति मे बुद्धिरपि देवैः सवासवैः॥
en: They are all masters in celestials weapons and they are all devoted to virtue. My opinion is that they cannot be vanquished even by the celestials with Vasava (Indra) at their head.

description: Pandavas entrance into the Kamyaka forest
sn: अमर्षी नित्यसंरब्धस्तत्र कर्णो महारथः। सर्वास्त्रविदनाधृष्यो ह्यभेद्यकवचावृतः॥
en: There is Karna, the great car-warrior, who is impetuous. ever angry, invincible, accomplished in all weapons and encased in impenetrable armour.

description: Pandavas entrance into the Kamyaka forest
sn: अनिर्जित्य रणे सर्वानेतान् पुरुषसत्तमान्। अशक्यो ह्यसहायेन हन्तुं दुर्योधनस्त्वया॥
en: Without first defeating in battle all these foremost of men, you cannot, unaided as you are, kill Duryodhana.

description: Pandavas entrance into the Kamyaka forest
sn: न निद्रामधिगच्छामि चिन्तयानो वृकोदर। अतिसर्वान्धनुाहान् सूतपुत्रस्य लाघवम्॥
en: O Vrikodara, I cannot sleep as I ponder upon the lightness of hand that the Suta's son (Karna) possesses. I consider him to be the foremost of all wielders of bows.

description: Pandavas entrance into the Kamyaka forest
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एतद् वचनमाज्ञाय भीमसेनोऽत्यमर्षणः। बभूव विमनास्त्रस्तो न चैवोवाच किंचन॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having heard these words, the impetuous Bhimasena became alarmed and pensive; and he did not utter a word.

description: Pandavas entrance into the Kamyaka forest
sn: तयोः संवदतोरेवं तदा पाण्डवयोर्द्वयोः। आजगाम महायोगी व्यास: सत्यवतीसुतः॥
en: When the Pandavas were talking one another, there came to that place the great ascetic Vyasa, the son of Satyavati.

description: Pandavas entrance into the Kamyaka forest
sn: सोऽभिगम्य यथान्यायं पाण्डवैः प्रतिपूजितः। युधिष्ठिरमिदं वाक्यमुवाच वदतां वरः॥
en: When he arrived, he was duly worshipped by the sons of Pandu. That best of speakers then thus spoke to Yudhishthira.

description: Pandavas entrance into the Kamyaka forest
sn: व्यास उवाच युधिष्ठिर महाबाहो वेद्मि ते हृदयस्थितम्। मनीषया ततः क्षिप्रमागतोऽस्मि नरर्षभ॥
en: Vyasa said : O mighty-armed Yudhishthira, O best of men, knowing by my intelligence what is passing in your mind, I have speedily come to this place.

description: Pandavas entrance into the Kamyaka forest
sn: भीष्माद् द्रोणात् कृपात् कर्णाद् द्रोण पुत्राच्च भारत। दुर्योधनान्नृपसुतात् तथा दुःशासनादपि॥ यत् ते भयममित्रघ्न हृदि सम्परिवर्तते। तत् तेऽहं नाशयिष्यामि विधिदृष्टेन कर्मणा॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, O slayer of foes, I shall destroy the fever that is in your mind and I shall tell you, by means of what act according to the ordinance you will be able to kill Bhishma, Kripa, Karna, Drona, the son of Drona, Duryodhana and the other princes and Dushasana.

description: Pandavas entrance into the Kamyaka forest
sn: तच्छुत्वाधृतिमास्थाय कर्मणा प्रतिपादय। प्रतिपाद्य तु राजेन्द्र ततः क्षिप्रं ज्वरं जहि॥
en: O king of kings, hearing it from me, accomplish the act with patience. Having accomplished it, soon destroy your this (mental) fever.

description: Pandavas entrance into the Kamyaka forest
sn: तत एकान्तमुन्नीय पाराशर्यो युधिष्ठिरम। अब्रवीदुपपन्नार्थमिदं वाक्यविशारदः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : That foremost of all eloquent men, the son of Parasara (Vyasa), taking him aside thus spoke to Yudhishthira in words of deep import.

description: Pandavas entrance into the Kamyaka forest
sn: श्रेयसस्ते परः कालः प्राप्तो भरतसत्तम। येनाभिभविता शत्रून् रणे पार्थोधनुर्धरः॥
en: Vyasa said: O best of the Bharatas, that prosperous time has come when the son of Pritha, Dhananjaya (Arjuna), will kill your enemies in battle.

description: Pandavas entrance into the Kamyaka forest
sn: गृहाणेमां मया प्रोक्तां सिद्धिं मूर्तिमतीमिव। विद्यां प्रतिस्मृति नाम प्रपन्नाय ब्रवीमि ते॥
en: Accept from me this knowledge, called Pratismriti. Uttered by me it is like success personified. You are capable of accepting it; I shall tell it to you.

description: Pandavas entrance into the Kamyaka forest
sn: यामवाप्य महाबाहुरर्जुनः साधयिष्यति। अस्त्रहेतोर्महेन्द्रं च रुद्रं चैवाभिगच्छतु॥ वरुणं च कुबेरं चधर्मराजं च पाण्डव। शक्तो ह्येष सुरान् द्रष्टुं तपसा विक्रमेण च॥
en: Receiving it, the mighty-armed Arjuna will be able to accomplish his desire. O son of Pandu, let him go for the acquisition of weapons to Mahendra. Rudra, Varuna, Kubera and Yama. He is competent to see the celestials on account of his asceticism and prowess.

description: Pandavas entrance into the Kamyaka forest
sn: ऋषिरेष महातेजा नारायणसहायवान्। पुराणः शाश्वतो देवस्त्वजेयी जिष्णुरच्युतः॥ अस्त्राणीन्द्राच्च रुद्राच्च लोकपालेभ्य एव च। समादाय महाबाहुर्महत् कर्म करिष्यति॥
en: He is a Rishi of great effulgence; he is the friend of Narayana (Krishna); he is ancient, eternal celestials, invincible, ever successful and undeteriorating. O mighty-armed hero, he will achieve great deeds by receiving weapons from Indra, Rudra and the Lokapalas.

description: Pandavas entrance into the Kamyaka forest
sn: वनादस्माच्च कौन्तेय वनमन्यद् विचिन्त्यताम्। निवासार्थाय यद् युक्तं भवेद् वः पृथिवीपते॥
en: O son of Kunti, O ruler of the world, think of going from this forest to another (forest) that may be fit for your abode.

description: Pandavas entrance into the Kamyaka forest
sn: एकत्र चिरवासो हि न प्रीतिजननो भवेत्। तापसानां च सर्वेषां भवेदुद्वेगकारकः॥
en: To reside in one place for a length of time is never pleasant. It might produce anxieties to the ascetics.

description: Pandavas entrance into the Kamyaka forest
sn: मृगाणामुपयोगश्च वीरुदोषधिसंक्षयः। बिभर्षि च बहून् विप्रान् वेदवेदाङ्गपारगान्॥
en: As you support numerous Brahmanas, learned in the Vedas, your continued residence here (in this forest) may exhaust the deer of the forest and may be destructive of the creepers and plant.

description: Pandavas entrance into the Kamyaka forest
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्त्वा प्रपन्नाय शुचये भगवान् प्रभुः। प्रोवाच लोकतत्त्वज्ञो योगी विद्यामनुत्तमाम्॥ धर्मराजायधीमान् स व्यासः सत्यवतीसुतः। अनुज्ञाय च कौन्तेयं तत्रैवान्तरधीयत॥
en: Vaishampayana said: Having thus addressed by that illustrious lord, the ascetic of great wisdom, the intelligent Vyasa, the son of Satyavati, learned in the mysteries of the world, then imported that foremost of knowledge to the willing Dharmaraja (Yudhishthira) who had meanwhile purified himself. Bidding farewell to the son of Kunti, he then disappeared.

description: Pandavas entrance into the Kamyaka forest
sn: युधिष्ठिरस्तुधर्मात्मा तद् ब्रह्म मनसा यतः। धारयामास मेधावी काले काले सदाभ्यसन्॥
en: Having received that knowledge, the virtuous-minded and the intelligent Yudhishthira carefully retained it in his memory and always repeated it at the proper times.

description: Pandavas entrance into the Kamyaka forest
sn: स व्यासवाक्यमुदितो बनाद् द्वैतवनात् ततः। ययौ सरस्वतीकूले काम्यकं नाम काननम्॥
en: Being glad at the words of Vyasa, he, leaving the Dvaiytavana, went to the forest of Kamyaka on the banks of the Sarasvati.

description: Pandavas entrance into the Kamyaka forest
sn: तमन्वयुर्महाराज शिक्षाक्षरविशारदाः। ब्राह्मणास्तपसा युक्ता देवेन्द्रमृषयो यथा॥
en: O great king, the Brahmanas, possessing ascetic merits and versed in the science of ortheopy and orthography, followed him, as the Rishis follow the king of the celestials (Indra).

description: Pandavas entrance into the Kamyaka forest
sn: ततः काम्यकमासाद्य पुनस्ते भरतर्षभ। न्यविशन्त महात्मानः सामात्याः सपरिच्छदाः॥
en: Thereupon arriving at Kamyaka, those highsouled chief's of the Bharata race took up their residence there with their friends and followers.

description: Pandavas entrance into the Kamyaka forest
sn: तत्र ते न्यवसन् राजन् किंचित् कालं मनस्विनः। धनुर्वेदपरा वीराः शृण्वन्तो वेदमुत्तमम्॥
en: O king, those intelligent heroes then lived there for some time, devoting themselves to the science of archery and hearing the excellent Vedas.

description: Pandavas entrance into the Kamyaka forest
sn: चरन्तो मृगयां नित्यं शुद्धैर्बाणैर्मृगार्थिनः। पितृदैवतविप्रेभ्यो निर्वपन्तो यथाविधि॥
en: They went about the forest every day with non-poisoned arrows in search of deer. They duly performed all the rites in honour of the Pitris, the celestials and the Brahmanas.

description: The meeting of Indra and Arjuna
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच कस्यचित् त्वथ कालस्यधर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः। संस्मृत्य मुनिसंदेशमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥ विविक्ते विदितप्रज्ञमर्जुनं पुरुषर्षभ। सान्त्वपूर्वं स्मितं कृत्वा पाणिना परिसंस्पृशन्॥ स मुहूर्तमिवध्यात्वा वनवासमरिंदमः। धनंजयधर्मराजो रहसीदमुवाच॥
en: Vaishampayana said : After sometime, Dharmaraja Yudhishthira, remembering the words of the Muni (Vyasa), spoke these words. Calling to himself in private that foremost of men, the greatly wise Arjuna and taking hold of his hands. That chastiser of foes, Dharmaraja, reflecting for a moment over their exile, smilingly spoke these words to Dhananjaya (Arjuna).

description: The meeting of Indra and Arjuna
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच भीष्मे द्रोणे कृपे कर्णे द्रोणपुत्रे च भारत। धनुर्वेदश्चतुष्पाद एतेष्वद्य प्रतिष्ठितः॥
en: Yudhishthira said: O descendant of Bharata, the four divisions of the science of arms always dwell in Bhishma, Drona, Kripa, Karna and the son of Drona (Ashvathama).

description: The meeting of Indra and Arjuna
sn: दैवं ब्राह्मं मानुषं च संयलं सचिकित्सितम्। सर्वास्त्राणां प्रयोगं च अभिजानन्ति कृत्स्नशः॥
en: They fully know all sorts of Brahma, celestials, human, Vayavya weapons, together with the mode of using them and warding them off.

description: The meeting of Indra and Arjuna
sn: ते सर्वेधृतराष्ट्रस्य पुत्रेण परिसान्त्विताः। संविभक्ताश्च तुष्टाश्च गुरुवत् तेषु वर्तते॥
en: They are all conciliated honoured and gratified by the son of Dhritarashtra (Duryodhana) who behaves to them as one does towards his preceptor.

description: The meeting of Indra and Arjuna
sn: सर्वयोधेषु चैवास्य सदा प्रीतिरनुत्तमा। आचार्या मानितास्तुष्टाः शान्तिं व्यवहरन्त्युत॥
en: Towards all his warriors he behaves with great affection. All the revered ones, thus honoured and gratified, seek to do him good.

description: The meeting of Indra and Arjuna
sn: शक्तिं न हापयिष्यन्ति ते काले प्रतिपूजिताः। अद्य चेयं मही कृत्स्ना दुर्योधनवशानुगा॥ सग्रामनगरा पार्थ ससागरवनाकरा। भवानेव प्रियोऽस्माकं त्वयि भारः समाहितः॥
en: Thus honoured by him, they will not fail to exert their might. The whole world is today under the sway of Duryodhana. With villages and cities, with all the seas and forests and mines. O Partha, you are our sole favourite refuge. On you rests a great burden.

description: The meeting of Indra and Arjuna
sn: अत्र कृत्यं प्रपश्यामि प्राप्तकालमरिदम। कृष्णद्वैपायनात् तात गृहीतोपनिषन्मया।॥
en: O chastiser of foes, I shall tell you what you should do now. O child, I have received a knowledge from Krishna Dvaipayana (Vyasa).

description: The meeting of Indra and Arjuna
sn: तया प्रयुक्तया सम्यग् जगत् सर्वं प्रकाशते। तेन त्वं ब्रह्मणा तात संयुक्तः सुसमाहितः॥ देवतानां यथाकालं प्रसादं प्रतिपालय। तपसा योजयात्मानमुग्रेण भरतर्षभ॥ धनुष्मान् कवची खड्गी मुनिः साधुव्रते स्थितः। न कस्यचिद् ददन्मार्गं गच्छ तातोत्तरां दिशम्॥
en: O child, if used by you, the whole universe will be brought to your view by that knowledge, Having attentively received that Brahma-knowledge. Attain in due time the grace of the celestials. O best of the Bharata race, devotes yourself to auster asceticism. Armed with the bow and the sword and clad in armour, devote yourself to austere asceticism and deep meditation. O child, without giving way to any body, go towards the north.

description: The meeting of Indra and Arjuna
sn: इन्द्रे ह्यस्त्राणि दिव्यानि समस्तानिधनंजय। वृत्राद् भीतैर्बलं देवैस्तदा शक्रे समर्पितम्॥
en: O Dhananjaya, all celestials weapons are with Indra. The celestials at one time gave all their strength to Shakra (Indra) from the fear of Vitra.

description: The meeting of Indra and Arjuna
sn: तान्येकस्थानि सर्वाणि ततस्त्वं प्रतिपत्स्यसे। शक्रमेव प्रपद्यस्व स तेऽस्त्राणि प्रदास्यति॥ दीक्षितोऽद्यैव गच्छ त्वं द्रष्टुं देवं पुरंदरम्।
en: They are all collected together in one place. And he will (surely) give you all his weapons. Go to Shakra (Indra); he will give you all his weapons. Be initiated and go this very day to the god Purandara (Indra).

description: The meeting of Indra and Arjuna
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्त्वाधर्मराजस्तमध्यापयत प्रभुः॥ दीक्षितं विधिनानेनधृतवाक्कायमानसम्। अनुजज्ञे तदा वीरं भ्राता भ्रातरमग्रजः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having said this, the lord Dharmaraja (Yudhishthira) imparted to him (Arjuna) the knowledge. The elder brother communicated with due rites the knowledge to his heroic brother whose speech, body and mind were all under complete control. He then commanded him to go.

description: The meeting of Indra and Arjuna
sn: निदेशाधर्मराजस्य द्रष्टुकामः पुरंदरम्। धनुर्गाण्डीवमादाय तथाक्षय्ये महेषुधी॥ कवची सतलत्राणो बद्धगोधाङ्गुलित्रवान्। हुत्वाग्निं ब्राह्मणान्निष्कैः स्वस्ति वाच्यं महाभुजः।१९।। प्रातिष्ठत महाबाहुः प्रगृहीतशरासनः। वधायधार्तराष्ट्राणां निःश्वस्योर्ध्वमुदीक्ष्य च॥
en: At the command of Dharmaraja (Yudhishthira), the mighty-armed (Arjuna), clad in mail and incased with gauntlets and furnished with finger protectors made of the guana skin, taking up the Gandiva (bow) and also his inexhaustible quivers; and having poured oblations into the fire and made the Brahmanas utter benediction on receipts of gifts, started to see Purandara (Indra). Armed with bow and arrows the mighty-armed hero heaved a sigh and cast a look upwards, when he set out for the destruction of Dhritarashtra's sons.

description: The meeting of Indra and Arjuna
sn: तं दृष्ट्वा तत्र कौन्तेयं प्रगृहीतशरासनम्। अब्रुवन् ब्राह्मणाः सिद्धा भूतान्यन्तर्हितानि च॥
en: Seeing the son of Kunti, about to start, thus armed with bow and arrows, the Brahmanas, the Siddhas and the invisible spirits said.

description: The meeting of Indra and Arjuna
sn: क्षिप्रमाप्नुहि कौन्तेय मनसा यद् यदिच्छसि। अब्रुवन् ब्राह्मणाः पार्थमिति कृत्वा जयाशिषः॥ संसाधयस्व कौन्तेयध्रुवोऽस्तु विजयस्तव।
en: "O son of Kunti, soon obtain what you wish for in your mind.” The Brahmanas blessed him with benedictions and said to Partha (Arjuna). "O son of Kunti, engage yourself in achieving the object you have in view. Victory is sure to come to you."

description: The meeting of Indra and Arjuna
sn: तं तथा प्रस्थितं वीरं शालस्कन्धोरुमर्जुनम्॥ मनांस्यादाय सर्वेषां कृष्णा वचनमब्रवीत्।
en: Then when the heroic Arjuna of thighs like the trunks of the Sala tree was about to start, taking away the hearts of all, Krishna (Draupadi) thus spoke.

description: The meeting of Indra and Arjuna
sn: कृष्णोवाच यत् ते कुन्ती महाबाहो जातस्यैच्छद्धनंजय॥ तत् तेऽस्तु सर्वं कौन्तेय यथा च स्वयमिच्छसि।
en: Draupadi said : O mighty-armed Dhananjaya, O son of Kunti, let all that Kunti desired at your birth and all that you yourself (always) desire be accomplished.

description: The meeting of Indra and Arjuna
sn: आस्माकं क्षत्रियकुले जन्म कश्चिदवाप्नुयात्॥ ब्राह्मणेभ्यो नमो नित्यं येषां भैक्ष्येण जीविका।
en: Let none of us again be born in the order of Kshatriya. Daily salutation to the Brahmanas whose mode of life is mendicancy.

description: The meeting of Indra and Arjuna
sn: इदं मे परमं दुःखं यः स पापः सुयोधनः॥ दृष्ट्वा मां गौरिति प्राह प्रहसन् राजसंसदि।
en: This is my great grief that the sinful wretch Suyodhana (Duryodhana). Seeing me in the assembly of the kings, mockingly called me a COW.

description: The meeting of Indra and Arjuna
sn: तस्माद् दुःखादिदं दुःखं गरीय इति मे मतिः॥ यत् तत् परिषदो मध्ये बह्वयुक्तमभाषत।
en: Besides this, other harsh words were spoken by him. But this is my opinion, that the grief I now feel in parting with you is greater than any I felt then at his words.

description: The meeting of Indra and Arjuna
sn: नूनं ते भ्रातरः सर्वे त्वत्कथाभिः प्रजागरे॥ रंस्यन्ते वीर कर्माणि कथयन्तः पुनः पुनः। नैव नः पार्थ भोगेषु नधने नोत जीविते॥ तुष्टिबुद्धिर्भवित्री वा त्वयि दीर्घप्रवासिनि। त्वयि नः पार्थ सर्वेषां सुखदुःखे समाहिते।॥ जीवितं मरणं चैव राज्यमैश्चर्यमेव च। आपृष्टो मेऽसि कौन्तेय स्वस्ति प्राप्नुहि भारत॥
en: Your brothers will while away their waking moments in repeatedly talking over your great deeds. O hero, O Partha, if you stay away (from us) for a long period of time, we shall derive no pleasure from enjoyments or luxury. Life itself would be distasteful to us. O son of Kunti, our weal and woe, our life and death, our kingdom and prosperity all depend on you. O descendant of Bharata, I bless you. Let success be yours. to

description: The meeting of Indra and Arjuna
sn: बलवद्भिर्विरुद्धं न कार्यमेतत् त्वयानघ। प्रयाह्यविघ्नेनैवाशु विजयाय महाबला नमोधात्रे विधात्रे च स्वस्ति गच्छ ह्यनामयम्॥
en: O mighty hero, O sinless one, you will be able to perform your this task even against powerful enemies. Go with speed to win success. Let there be no danger to you. I bow Dhatri and Vidhatri; undeteriorating blessings be to you.

description: The meeting of Indra and Arjuna
sn: ह्रीः श्रीः कीर्तिर्युतिः पुष्टिरुमा लक्ष्मीः सरस्वती। इमा वै तव पान्थस्य पालयन्तुधनंजय॥
en: O Dhananjaya, let Hri, Shri, Kirti, Dhriti, Pushti, Uma, Lakshmi and Sarasvati, all protect you on your way.

description: The meeting of Indra and Arjuna
sn: ज्येष्ठापचायी ज्येष्ठस्य भ्रातुर्वचनकारकः। प्रपद्येऽहं वसून् रुद्रानादित्यान् समरुद्गणान्॥ विश्वेदेवांस्तथा साध्याञ्छान्त्यर्थं भरतर्षभ। स्वस्ति तेऽस्त्वान्तरिक्षेभ्यः पार्थिवेभ्यश्च भारत॥ दिव्येभ्यश्चैव भूतेभ्यो ये चान्ये परिपन्थिनः।
en: For you always worship your elder brother and always obey his commands. I bow to the Vasus, the Rudras, the Adityas, the Marutas. The Vishvadevas and the Siddhas for your welfare. O best of the Bharata race, O descendant of Bharata, be safe from all mischievous spirits belonging to the firmament, the earth. And the heaven and also from other such ones generally.

description: The meeting of Indra and Arjuna
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्त्वाऽऽशिषः कृष्णा विरराम यशस्विनी॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having uttered these benedictions, the illustrious Krishna (Draupadi) stopped.

description: The meeting of Indra and Arjuna
sn: ततः प्रदक्षिणं कृत्वा भ्रातृन्धौम्यं च पाण्डवः। प्रातिष्ठत महाबाहुः प्रगृह्य रुचिरंधनुः॥
en: Having then walked round his brothers and Dhaumya, the mighty-armed Pandava (Arjuna), taking up his beautiful bow, started.

description: The meeting of Indra and Arjuna
sn: तस्य मार्गादपाक्रामन् सर्वभूतानि गच्छतः। युक्तस्यैन्द्रेण योगेन पराक्रान्तस्य शुष्मिणः॥
en: All creatures left the path that the greatly energetic and powerful (hero) took with the desire of seeing Indra.

description: The meeting of Indra and Arjuna
sn: सोऽगच्छत् पर्वतांस्तात तपोधननिषेवितान्। दिव्यं हैमवतं पुण्यं देवजुष्टं परंतपः॥
en: O child, that chastiser of foes passed over many mountains inhabited by the ascetics; and (at last) he reached the sacred and the celestials Himalayas.

description: The meeting of Indra and Arjuna
sn: अगच्छत् पर्वतं पुण्यमेकाद्वैव महामनाः। मनोजवगतिर्भूत्वा योगयुक्तो यथानिलः॥
en: The high-minded hero reached the sacred mountain in one day, for he, being a great ascetic, possessed the speed like that of the mind.

description: The meeting of Indra and Arjuna
sn: हिमवन्तमतिक्रम्य गन्धमादनमेव च। अत्यक्रामत् स दुर्गाणि दिवारात्रमतन्द्रितः॥
en: Having cross the Himalayas and also the Gandhamadana and many other uneven and dangerous passes by walking day and night.

description: The meeting of Indra and Arjuna
sn: इन्द्रकीलं समासाद्य ततोऽतिष्ठद्धनंजयः। अन्तरिक्षेऽतिशुश्राव तिष्ठेति स वचस्तदा॥
en: He reached Indrakila and Dhananjaya (Arjuna) stopped there. He then heard a voice in the sky. It said, “stop."

description: The meeting of Indra and Arjuna
sn: तच्छ्रुत्वा सर्वतो दृष्टिं चारयामास पाण्डवः। अथापश्यत् सव्यसाची वृक्षमूले तपस्विनम्॥
en: Having heard it, the Pandava (Arjuna) looked at all sides and Savyasachi (Arjuna) then saw an ascetic sitting at the foot of a tree.

description: The meeting of Indra and Arjuna
sn: ब्राह्मया श्रिया दीप्यमानं पिङ्गलं जटिलं कृशम्। सोऽब्रवीदर्जुनं तत्र स्थितं दृष्ट्वा महातपाः॥
en: (He was) blazing with Brahma-effulgence. With brawny colour and matted-locks, (he was) thin and lean. Seeing him (Arjuna) stopped there. The great ascetic then thus spoke to Arjuna,

description: The meeting of Indra and Arjuna
sn: कस्त्वं तातेह सम्प्राप्तोधनुष्मान् कवची शरी। निबद्धासितलत्राणः क्षत्रधर्ममनुव्रतः॥ नेह शस्त्रेण कर्तव्यं शान्तानामेष आलयः। विनीतक्रोधहर्षाणां ब्राह्मणानां तपस्विनाम्॥
en: “O child, who are you that have come here with bow and arrows, clad in armour, scabbard and gauntlet and devoted to the Kshatriya usage? There is no necessity for weapons here. This is the abode of peaceful Brahmana ascetics (who are all) without either joy or anger.

description: The meeting of Indra and Arjuna
sn: नेहास्तिधनुषा कार्यं न संचामोऽत्र कर्हिचित्। निक्षिपैतद्धनुस्तात प्राप्तोऽसि परमां गतिम्॥
en: O child, there is no use of the bow here. There is no sort of fight here. Therefore throw away your bow. You have obtained the highest state of life.

description: The meeting of Indra and Arjuna
sn: ओजसा तेजसा वीर यथा नान्यः पुमान् क्वचित् तथा हसन्निवाभीक्ष्णं ब्राह्मणोऽर्जुनमब्रवीत्। न चैनं चालयामासधैर्यात् सुधृतनिश्चयम्॥
en: O hero, there is no man who is equal to you in energy and prowess." The Brahmana smilingly thus spoke to Arjuna. But he could not move him, who was so firm in his purpose.

description: The meeting of Indra and Arjuna
sn: तमुवाच ततः प्रीतः स द्विजः प्रहसन्निवा वरं वृणीष्व भद्रं ते शक्रोऽहमरिसूदन॥
en: Thereupon that Brahmana, being much pleased with him, again spoke to him with smiles, “O slayer of foes, be blessed. I am Shakra (Indra). Ask the boon you desire to have."

description: The meeting of Indra and Arjuna
sn: एवमुक्तः सहस्राक्षं प्रत्युवाचधनंजयः। प्राञ्जलिः प्रणतो भूत्वा शूरः कुरुकुलोद्वहः॥
en: Having been thus addressed by the deity of one thousand eyes (Indra), that perpetuator of the Kuru race, the heroic Dhananjaya (Arjuna) with joined hands and bowing head said,

description: The meeting of Indra and Arjuna
sn: ईप्सितो ह्येष वै कामो वरं चैनं प्रयच्छ मे। त्वत्तोऽद्य भगवन्नस्त्रं कृत्स्नमिच्छामि वेदितुम्॥
en: “O exalted one, this is the object of my wishes; grant me this boon, (namely) I desire to learn from you all weapons."

description: The meeting of Indra and Arjuna
sn: प्रत्युवाच महेन्द्रस्तं प्रीतात्मा प्रहसन्निव। इह प्राप्तस्य किं कार्यमस्त्रैस्तवधनंजय॥ कामान् वृणीष्व लोकांस्त्वं प्राप्तोऽसि परमां गतिम्। एवमुक्तः प्रत्युवाच सहस्राक्षंधनंजयः॥ न लोभान्न पुनः कामान्न देवत्वं पुनः सुखम्। न च सर्वामरैश्वर्यं कामये त्रिदशाधिप।॥ भ्रार्तृस्तान् विपिने त्यक्त्वा वैरमप्रतियात्य च। अकीर्तिं सर्वलोकेषु गच्छेयं शाश्वतीः समाः॥
