en: Mahendra (Indra), being much please with him smilingly replied, “O Dhananjaya, when you have reached this region, what need is there of you to get weapons? You have already obtained the highest state of life. Ask for other regions of bliss you desire to obtain.” Having been thus addressed, Dhananjaya thus replied to the deity of one thousand eyes (Indra), “O lord of heaven, I do not desire to obtain regions of bliss, nor objects of enjoyment, nor the celestials state, what to speak of (other) pleasures. I do not desire to obtain the prosperity of all the celestials. Having left my brothers behind me in the forest and having been unable to avenge myself on the enemy, shall I incur the opprobrium of all the world for everlasting time?"

description: The meeting of Indra and Arjuna
sn: एवमुक्तः प्रत्युवाच वृत्रहा पाण्डुनन्दनम्। सान्त्वयञ्छ्लक्ष्णया वाचा सर्वलोकनमस्कृतः॥
en: Having been thus addressed, the slayer of Vritra, the worshipped of all the worlds (Indra), consoling him with sweet words, thus spoke to the son of Pandu (Arjuna),

description: The meeting of Indra and Arjuna
sn: यदा द्रक्ष्यसि भूतेशं त्र्यक्षं शूलधरं शिवम्। तदा दातास्मि ते तात दिव्यान्यस्त्राणि सर्वशः॥
en: “O child, when you will be able to meet the three-eyes deity, Shiva, the wielder of trident and the lord of all creatures, it is then I shall bestow on you all my weapons.

description: The meeting of Indra and Arjuna
sn: क्रियतां दर्शने यत्नो देवस्य परमेष्ठिनः। दर्शनात् तस्य कौन्तेय संसिद्धः स्वर्गमेष्यसि॥
en: O son of Kunti, try to meet the greatest of all gods, for it is only when you have seen him that you would have your desire fulfilled.”

description: The meeting of Indra and Arjuna
sn: इत्युक्त्वा फाल्गुनं शक्रो जगामादर्शनं पुनः। अर्जुनोऽप्यथ तत्रैव तस्थौ योगसमन्वितः॥
en: Having thus spoken to Falguni (Arjuna), Shakra (Indra) disappeared. Arjuna remained at that spot, devoting himself asceticism. to severe

description: The colloquy between the Rishis and Shiva
sn: जनमेजय उवाच भगवञ्छ्रोतुमिच्छामि पार्थस्याक्लिष्टकर्मणः। विस्तरेण कथामेतां यथास्त्राण्युपलब्धवान्॥
en: Janamejaya said : O exalted onc, I desire to hear in detail the account of the acquisition of weapons by Partha (Arjuna) of spotless deeds.

description: The colloquy between the Rishis and Shiva
sn: यथा च पुरुषव्याघ्रो दीर्घबाहुर्धनंजयः। वनं प्रविष्टस्तेजस्वी निर्मनुष्यमभीतवत्॥
en: How did that foremost of men, the mightyarmed and the greatly energetic Dhananjaya enter that solitary forest without having felt (any) fear?

description: The colloquy between the Rishis and Shiva
sn: किं च तेन कृतं तत्र वसता ब्रह्मवित्तम। कथं च भगवान् स्थाणुर्देवराजश्च तोषितः॥
en: O foremost of all men, learned in the Vedas, what did he do when he lived there? O exalted one, how did he gratify Sthanu (Shiva) and the chief of the celestials (Indra)?

description: The colloquy between the Rishis and Shiva
sn: एतदिच्छाभ्यहं श्रोतुं त्वत्प्रसादाद् द्विजोत्तम। त्वं हि सर्वज्ञ दिव्यं च मानुषं चैव वेत्थ ह॥
en: O best of the twice-born, I desire to hear all this through your favour. O omniscient one, you are acquainted with everything regarding men and gods.

description: The colloquy between the Rishis and Shiva
sn: अत्यद्भुततमं ब्रह्मन् रोमहर्षणमर्जुनः। भवेन सह संग्रमं चकाराप्रतिम किल॥ पुरा प्रहरतां श्रेष्ठः संग्रमेष्वपराजितः। यच्छ्रुत्वा नरसिंहानां दैन्यहर्षातिविस्मयात्॥ शूराणामपि पार्थानां हृदयानि चकम्पिरे। यद् यच्च कृतवानन्यत् पार्थस्तदखिलं वद॥
en: O Brahmana, the battle that was formerly fought between that best of smiters, who had never been defeated in war and Bhava (Shiva) was without a parallel and was extraordinary and was also hair-stirring. Having heaard which the hearts of those foremost of men, the sons of Pritha, trembled in wonder and joy, thinking of their own inferiority. Tell me what other acts Partha (Arjuna), performed.

description: The colloquy between the Rishis and Shiva
sn: न ह्यस्य निन्दितं जिष्णोः सुसूक्ष्ममपि लक्षये। चरितं तस्य शूरस्य तन्मे सर्वं प्रकीर्तय॥
en: I do not find the most trivial thing in Jishnu (Arjuna) which might be called censurable. (Therefore) narrate the history of that hero to me.

description: The colloquy between the Rishis and Shiva
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच कथयिष्यामि ते तात कथामेतां महात्मनः। दिव्यां पौरवशार्दूल महतीमद्भुतोपमाम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : O foremost of the Kurus, O child, I shall narrate to you the excellent, the extensive and greatly unrivalled history of that illustrious hero.

description: The colloquy between the Rishis and Shiva
sn: गात्रसंस्पर्शसम्बद्धां त्र्यम्बकेण सहानघ। पार्थस्य देवदेवेन शृणु सम्य समागमम्॥
en: O sinless, one, hear in detail the account of Partha's meting with the three-eyed, god of gods and his contact with his body.

description: The colloquy between the Rishis and Shiva
sn: युधिष्ठिरनियोगात् स जगामामितविक्रमः। शक्रं सुरेश्वरं द्रष्टुं देवदेवं च शंकरम्॥ दिव्यं तद्धनुरादाय खङ्गं च कनकत्सरुम्। महाबलो महाबाहुरर्जुनः कार्यसिद्धये॥ दिशं [दीची कौरव्यो हिमवच्छिखरं प्रति। ऐन्द्रिः स्थिरमना राजन् सर्वलोकमहारथः॥
en: At the command of Yudhishthira that immeasurably powerful hero set out to meet the chief of the celestials, Shakra and the god of gods, Shankara (Shiva). Taking up the excellent bow and the sword with the golden hit, in order to accomplish his purpose, the greatly powerful and the mighty-armed Arjuna. That descendant of Kuru, set out northward towards the summit of the Himalayas. O king, that son of Indra (Arjuna) of calm mind, that greatest car-warrior of all the world.

description: The colloquy between the Rishis and Shiva
sn: त्वरया परया युक्तस्तपसेधृतनिश्चयः। वनं कण्टकितं घोरमेक एवान्वपद्यत॥
en: Firmly adhering to his purpose, soon engaged himself in austere asceticism. He entered that fearful and thorny forest alone.

description: The colloquy between the Rishis and Shiva
sn: नानापुष्पफलोपेतं नानापक्षिनिषेवितम्। नानामृगगणाकीर्णं सिद्धचारणसेवितम्॥
en: It abounded in various flowers and fruits, it was inhabited by birds of various species, it was full of various animals and it was frequented by the Siddhas and Charanas.

description: The colloquy between the Rishis and Shiva
sn: ततः प्रयाते कौन्तेये वनं मानुषवर्जितम्। शङ्खानां पटहानां च शब्दः समभवद् दिवि॥
en: When the son of Kunti, Arjuna, entered that forest, which was destitute of human beings, conchs and drums from heaven were sounded.

description: The colloquy between the Rishis and Shiva
sn: पुष्पवर्षं च सुमहन्निपपात महीतले। मेघजालं च विततं छादयामास सर्वतः॥ सोऽतीत्य वनदुर्गाणि संनिकर्षे महागिरेः। शुशुभे हिमवत्पृष्ठे वसमानोऽर्जुनस्तदा॥
en: Great showers of flowers fell on the earth; and the clouds spreading out covered every place with a shade. Passing the forest-paths at the foot of the great mountain Arjuna shone in his own effulgence by dwelling on the breast of the Himalayas.

description: The colloquy between the Rishis and Shiva
sn: तत्रापश्यद् दुमान् फुल्लान् विहगैर्वल्गुनादितान् नदीश्च विपुलावर्ता वैदूर्यविमलप्रभाः॥
en: He saw there many trees blooming in green verdure and resounding with the sweet notes of the birds, abounding in great rivers with great eddies and currents of the color of Vaidurya gems.

description: The colloquy between the Rishis and Shiva
sn: हंसकारण्डवोद्गीताः सारसाभिरुतास्तथा। पुस्कोकिलरुताश्चैव क्रौञ्चबर्हिणनादिताः॥
en: And echoing with the sweet notes of the swans, ducks and cranes. The banks of those rivers were resounded with melodious strains of male Kokilas, of peacocks and of cranes.

description: The colloquy between the Rishis and Shiva
sn: मनोहरत्नोपेतास्तस्पितिरथोऽर्जुनः। पुण्यशीतामलजलाः पश्यन् प्रीतमनाभवत्॥
en: Seeing those rivers of sacred, pure and delicious water and also their charming banks, thc great car-warrior Arjuna became very much delighted.

description: The colloquy between the Rishis and Shiva
sn: रमणीये वनोद्देशे रममाणोऽर्जुनस्तदा। तपस्युचे वर्तमान उग्रतेजा महामनाः॥
en: The greatly energetic and high-minded Arjuna then engaged himself in asceticism in that charming forest.

description: The colloquy between the Rishis and Shiva
sn: दर्भचीरं निवस्याथ दण्डाजिनविभूषितः। शीर्णं च पतितं भूमौ पर्णं समुपयुक्तवान्।॥
en: Clad in cloth made of grass and with deerskin and holding the Danda (stick), he ate withered leaves fallen on the ground.

description: The colloquy between the Rishis and Shiva
sn: पूर्णे पूर्णे त्रिरात्रे तु मासमेकं फलाशनः। द्विगुणेन हि कालेन द्वितीयं मासमत्ययात्॥
en: He ate fruits in the first month (of his asceticism) at the interval of three nights, in the second (month) at the interval of six nights.

description: The colloquy between the Rishis and Shiva
sn: तृतीयमपि मासं स पक्षणाहारमाचरन्। चतुर्थे त्वथ सम्प्राप्ते मासे भरतसत्तमः॥ वायुभक्षो महाबाहुरभवत् पाण्डुनन्दनः। ऊर्ध्वबाहुर्निरालम्बः पादाङ्गुष्ठाचविष्ठितः॥
en: In the third (month) at the interval of a fortnight. When the fourth month came, that foremost of the Bharata race. That mightyarmed son of Pandu lived (simply) on air, with his arms upraised and with nothing to lean upon, standing only on the tips of his toes.

description: The colloquy between the Rishis and Shiva
sn: सदोपस्पर्शनाच्चास्य बभूवुरमितौजसः। विद्युदम्भोरुहनिभा जटास्तस्य महात्मनः॥
en: In consequences of frequent bathing the hair of that high-souled and immeasurably energetic hero became as bright as the lightning or the lotus.

description: The colloquy between the Rishis and Shiva
sn: ततो महर्षयः सर्वे जग्मुर्देवं पिनाकिनम्। निवेदयिषवः पार्थं तपस्युचे समास्थितम्॥
en: Thereupon all the great Rishis went to the god, the wielder of trident (Shiva) and told him that the son of Pritha (Arjuna) was engaged in austere asceticism.

description: The colloquy between the Rishis and Shiva
sn: तं प्रणम्य महादेवं शशंसुः पार्थकर्म तत्। एष पार्थो महातेजा हिमवत्पृष्ठमास्थितः॥ उग्रे तपसि दुष्पारे स्थितोधूमाययन् दिशः। तस्य देवेश न वयं विद्मः सर्वे चिकीर्षितम्॥
en: Bowing to the great god (Shiva), they told him all about the action of Partha. (They said), “The greatly effulgent Partha is engaged in austere asceticism on the breast of the Himalayas. Heated with his asceticism the earth is sending forth smokes. O chief of gods, we do not know with what object he undergoes this asceticism.

description: The colloquy between the Rishis and Shiva
sn: संतापयति नः सर्वानसौ साधु निवार्यताम्। तेषां तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा मुनीनां भावितात्मनाम्॥ उमापतिर्भूतपतिर्वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह।
en: He causes us pain. O exalted one, you ought to stop him." Having heard these words of those self-controlled Rishis. The husband of Uma, the lord of creatures, thus spoke.

description: The colloquy between the Rishis and Shiva
sn: महादेव उवाच न वो विषादः कर्तव्यः फाल्गुनं प्रति सर्वशः॥ शीघ्रं गच्छत संहृष्टा यथागतमतन्द्रिताः। अहमस्य विजानामि संकल्पं मनसि स्थितम्॥
en: Shiva said : You all ought not feel any anxiety on account of Falguni (Arjuna). Go away soon with cheerfulness and alacrity to the place whence you have come. I know what is the determination of his mind.

description: The colloquy between the Rishis and Shiva
sn: नास्य स्वर्गस्पृहा काचिन्नैश्वर्यस्य तथाऽऽयुषः। यत् तस्य काक्षितं सर्वं तत् करिष्येऽहमद्य वै॥
en: His desire is not for heaven, not for prosperity, nor for long life. What is desired by him, will be done by me even today.

description: The colloquy between the Rishis and Shiva
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तच्छ्रुत्वा शर्ववचनमृषयः सत्यवादिनः। प्रहृष्टमनसो जग्मुर्यथा स्वान् पुनरालयान्॥
en: Vaishampayana said: Having heard all this, the truthful Rishis with cheerful heart returned to their respective abodes.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच गतेषु तेषु सर्वेषु तपस्विषु महात्मसु। पिनाकपाणिर्भगवान् सर्वपापहरो हरः॥ कैरातं वेषमास्थाय काञ्चनदुमसंनिभम्। विभ्राजमानो विपुलो गिरिर्मेरुरिवापरः॥
en: When all those high-souled ascetics went away, the wielder of trident, the exalted lord Hara, the destroyer of all sins. Assuming the form of a Kirata (hunter), blazing like a golden tree, appearing like a second huge Meru mountain.

sn: श्रीमद्धनुरुपादाय शरांश्चाशीविषोपमान्। निष्पपात महावेगो दहनो देहवानिव॥
en: And taking a handsome bow and many virulently poisonous snake-like arrows, came down with great speeds an embodiment of fire.

sn: देव्या सहोमया श्रीमान् समानव्रतवेषया। नानावेषधरैर्हष्टैर्भूतैरनुगतस्तदा॥ किरातवेषसंच्छन्नः स्त्रीभिश्चापि सहस्रशः। अशोभत तदा राजन् स देशोऽतीव भारत॥
en: The auspicious deity was accompanied by Uma who was in the same custom and with the same purpose (as those of her husband Shiva) and also by many merry goblins of various forms and attires. And also by thousands of female (goblins). O king, O descendant of Bharata, the place blazed forth with beauty (as Shiva appeared).

sn: क्षणेन तद् वनं सर्वं निःशब्दमभवत् तदा। नादः प्रस्रवणानां च पक्षिणां चाप्युपारमत्॥
en: And in a moment all the forest was pervaded with silence. The sounds of springs, water-falls and birds ceased.

sn: स संनिकर्षमागम्य पार्थस्याक्लिष्टकर्मणः। मूकं नाम दनोः पुत्रं ददर्शाद्भुतदर्शनम्॥ वाराहं रूपमास्थाय तर्कयन्तमिवार्जुनम्। हन्तुं परं दीप्यमानं तमुवाचाथ फाल्गुनः॥ गाण्डीवं धनुरादाय शरांचाशीविषोपमान्। सज्यंधनुर्वरं कृत्वा ज्याघोषेण निनादयन्॥
en: Coming near Partha of spotless deeds, he (Shiva) saw that a son of a Danava, named Muka of wonderful appearance. Assuming the form of a boar, intended to kill Arjuna. Seeing him in the attempt to kill him. (At once) taking up his Gandiva bow and virulently poisonous snake-like arrows and also stringing them to the bow and having filled all sides with its twang, Falguni said to him.

sn: यन्मां प्रार्थयसे हन्तुमनागसमिहागतम्। तस्मात् त्वां पूर्वमेवाहं नेताद्य यमसादनम्॥
en: Arjuna said : I have come here, but, done you no harm. As you seek to kill me, I shall certainly today send you to the abode of Yama,

sn: दृष्ट्वा तं प्रहरिष्यन्तं फाल्गुनं दृढधन्विनम्। किरातरूपी सहसा वारयामास शङ्करः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Seeing that firm wielder of bow Falguni (Arjuna) about to kill him, (the Danava), Shankara (Shiva) in the disguise of the Kirata suddenly asked him to stop.

sn: मयैष प्रार्थितः पूर्वमिन्द्रकीलसमप्रभः। अनादृत्य च तद् वाक्यं प्रजहाराथ फाल्गुनः॥
en: (He said), “This boar like the Indrakila in colour has been first aimed by me." But disregarding his word, Falguni (Arjuna) struck it.

sn: किरातश्च समं तस्मिन्नेकलक्ष्ये महाद्युतिः। प्रमुमोचाशनिप्रख्यं शरमग्निशिखोपमम्॥
en: At that very moment the greatly effulgent Kirata also shot an arrow like the flaming fire or the blazing thunderbolt.

sn: तौ मुक्तौ सायको ताभ्यां समं तत्र निपेततुः। मूकस्य गात्रे विस्तीर्णे शैलसंहनने तदा॥
en: The two arrows thus shot by the two (men) fell at the same time on the huge and adamantine body of Muka.

sn: यथाशनेर्विनिर्घोषो वज्रस्येव च पर्वते। तथा तयोः संनिपातः शरयोरभवत् तदा॥
en: The two arrows fell on him with a loud sound as that of lightning or as that of the thunder falling on a mountain.

sn: स विद्धो बहुभिर्बाणैर्दीप्तास्यैः पन्नगैरिव। ममार राक्षसं रूपं भूयः कृत्वा बिभीषणम्॥
en: Thus struck by the two arrows which were like flaming-mouthed snakes, Muka, assuming his fearful Rakshasas form, gave up his life.

sn: स ददर्श ततो जिष्णुः पुरुषं काञ्चनप्रभम्। किरातवेषसंच्छन्नं स्त्रीसहायममित्रहा॥ तमब्रवीत् प्रीतमनाः कौन्तेयः प्रहसन्निव। को भवानटते शून्ये वने स्त्रीगणसंवृतः॥
en: Thereupon Jishnu (Arjuna), that slayer of foes, saw before him the person with the form of blazing gold, disguised as a Kirata and accompanied by many women. The son of Kunti then with a cheerful heart smilingly asked him. “Who are you wandering in this solitary forest surrounded by women?

sn: न त्वमस्मिन् वने घोरे बिभेषि कनकप्रभा किमर्थं च त्वया विद्वो वराहो मत्परिग्रहः॥
en: O golden-splendoured one, are you not afraid of this fearful forest? Why have you pierced the boar that was first aimed by me.

sn: मयाभिपन्नः पूर्वं हि राक्षसोऽयमिहागतः। कामात् परिभवाद् वापि न मे जीवन् विमोक्ष्यसे।२०॥
en: This Rakshasas either listlessly or with the intention of killing me came here and he was first aimed by me, therefore you cannot escape from me with your life.

sn: न ह्येष मृगयाधर्मो यस्त्वयाद्य कृतो मयि। तेन त्वां भ्रंशयिष्यामि जीवितात् पर्वताश्रयम्॥
en: What you have done towards me is quite contrary to the usage of the chase. O mountaineer, therefore, I shall take your life.”

sn: इत्युक्तः पाण्डवेयेन किरातः प्रहसन्निव। उवाच श्लक्ष्णया वाचा पाण्डवं सव्यसाचिनम्॥
en: Having been thus addressed by the Pandava, the Kirata spoke to the son of Pandu, Savyasachi (Arjuna), in these sweet words.

sn: न मत्कृते त्वया वीर भी: कार्या वनमन्तिकात्। इयं भूमिः सदास्माकमुचिता वसतां वने।॥
en: "O hero, you need not be anxious for my dwelling in the forest. This forest-land is the proper abode for us who (always) dwell in the forest.

sn: त्वया तु दुष्करः कस्मादिह वासः प्ररोचितः। वयं तु बहुसत्त्वेऽस्मिन् नवसामस्तपोधन॥
en: O ascetic, why have you selected to live here amidst these difficulties and dangers? We always live in these forests full of various sorts of animals.

sn: भवांस्तु कृष्णवाभः सुकुमार: सुखोचितः। कथं शून्यमिमं देशमेकाकी विचरिष्यति॥
en: You are delicate; you are brought up in luxury; and you are as effulgent as the fire, why do you wander alone in this solitary forest?"

sn: अर्जुन उवाच गाण्डीवमाश्रयं कृत्वा नाराचांश्चाग्निसंनिभान्। निवसामि महारण्ये द्वितीय इव पावकिः॥
en: Arjuna said: Depending on my Gandiva(bow) and my arrows as blazing as the fire, I live in this great forest like a second son of fire (Kartikeya).

sn: एष चापि मया जन्तुर्मंगरूपं समाश्रितः। राक्षसो निहतो घोरो हन्तुं मामिह चागतः॥
en: See, this great beast, this fearful Rakshasas, who came here in the form of an animal, has been killed by me.

sn: किरात उवाच मयैषधन्वनिर्मुक्तैस्ताडितः पूर्वमेव हि। बाणैरभिहतः शेते नीतश्च यमसादनम्॥
en: The Kirata said: This one (the Rakshasas) was first struck with the arrow shot from my bow. He was killed and sent to the abode of Yama by me.

sn: ममैष लक्ष्यभूतो हि मम पूर्वपरिग्रहः। ममैव च प्रहारेण जीविताद् व्यपरोपितः॥
en: He was first aimed by me, he was first claimed by mc and it is from my shot that he has lost his life.

sn: दोषान् स्वान् नार्हसेऽन्यस्मै वक्तुं स्वबलदर्पितः। अविलप्तोऽसि मन्दात्मन् न मे जीवन् विमोक्ष्यसे।३०।।
en: Being proud of your strength, you should not blame others for your own fault. O wickedminded wretch, you are yourself in fault and therefore you will not escape from me with life.

sn: स्थिरो भवस्व मोक्ष्यामि सायकानशनीनिव। घटस्व परया शक्त्या मुञ्च त्वमपि सायकान्॥
en: Stop, I shall shoot at you arrows like the thunder. Try your best if you can and shoot at me your arrows.

sn: तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा किरातस्यार्जुनस्तदा। रोषमाहारयामास ताडयामास चेषुभिः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having heard these words of the Kirata, Arjuna, grew angry and began to strike him with numerous arrows.

sn: ततो हृष्टेन मनसा प्रतिजग्राह सायकान्। भूयो भूय इति प्राह मन्दमन्देत्युवाच ह॥
en: Thereupon he (the Kirata) received upon himself all those arrows with a cheerful heart, He again and again said "O wretch, Owretch,

sn: प्रहरस्व शरानेतान् नाराचान् मर्मभेदिनः। इत्युक्तो बाणवर्षं स मुमोच सहसार्जुनः॥
en: Shoot at me your best arrows that are capable of piercing to the very heart." Having been thus addressed, Arjuna poured a shower of arrows upon him.

sn: ततस्तौ तत्र संरब्धौ राजमानौ मुहुर्मुहुः। शरैराशीविषाकारैस्ततक्षाते परस्परम्॥
en: Thereupon both of thein became angry. Engaging in a fearful fight, they hurled again and again at each other showers of poisonous snake-like arrows.

sn: ततोऽर्जुनः शरवर्षं किराते समवासृजत्। तत् प्रसन्नेन मनसा प्रतिजग्राह शङ्करः॥
en: Arjuna poured a shower of arrows on the Kirata, but Shankara (Shiva) received them all upon him with a cheerful heart.

sn: मुहूर्तं शरवर्षं तत् प्रतिगृह्य पिनाकधृक्। अक्षतेन शरीरेण तस्थौ गिरिरिवाचलः॥ स दृष्ट्वा बाणवर्ष
en: Having born that shower of arrows for a moment, the wiclder of Pinaka, (Shiva) stood there in unwounded body like an immovable mountain.

sn: तु मोघीभूतंधनंजयः। परमं विस्मयं चक्रे साधु साध्विति चाब्रवीत्॥
en: Seeing his shower of arrows had no effects (on his adversary), Dhananjaya (Arjuna) became greatly surprised; and he exclaimed "Excellent" "Excellent."

sn: अहोऽयं कुसुमाराङ्गो हिमवच्छिखराश्रयः। गाण्डीवमुक्तान् नाराचान् प्रतिगृहणात्यविह्वलः॥
en: "Alas, this delicate bodied mountaincer of the Himalayas bear unmoved the arrows shot from the Gandiva.

sn: कोऽयं देवो भवेत् साक्षाद् रुद्रो यक्षः सुरोऽसुरः विद्यते हि गिरिश्रेष्ठे त्रिदशानां समागमः॥
en: Who is he? Is he the deity Rudra (Shiva) himself? Is he a Yaksha or a celestials or a Asura? The celestials often come to this best of mountains.

sn: न हि मद्वाणजालानामुत्सृष्टानां सहस्रशः। शक्तोऽन्यः सहितुं वेगमते देवं पिनाकिनम्॥
en: Except the deity, the wielder of Pinaka, there is none else that can with stand the force of the thousands of arrows shot by me from the Gandiva.

sn: देवो वा यदि वा यक्षो रुद्रादन्यो व्यवस्थितः। अहमेनं शरैस्तीक्ष्णैर्नयामि यमसादनम्॥
en: Whether he is a celestials or a Yaksha, any body cxcept Rudra (Shiva), I Shall soon send him to the abode of Yama with my these sharp arrows."

sn: ततो हृष्टमना जिष्णुाराचान् मर्मभेदिनः। व्यसृजच्छतधा राजन् मयूखानिव भास्करः॥
en: O king, thereupon Jishnu, (Arjuna) with a chcerful heart began to hurl thousands of arrows, (each) capable of piercing to the very heart, as the sun spreads his rays (all over the world).

sn: तान् प्रसन्नेन मनसा भगवाल्लोकभावनः। शूलपाणिः प्रत्यगृहणाच्छिलावर्षमिवाचलः॥
en: The exalted Creator of the world, the wielder of trident, with a cheerful heart bore that shower of arrows, as a mountain does a shower of rocks.

sn: क्षणेन क्षीणबाणोऽथ संवृत्तः फाल्गुनस्तदा। भीश्चैनमाविशत् तीव्रा तं दृष्ट्वा शरसंक्षयम्॥
en: The arrows of Falguni were soon exhausted; and seeing that all his arrows were exhausted, he was seized with great fear.

sn: चिन्तयामास जिष्णुस्तु भगवन्तं हुताशनम्। पुरस्तादक्षयौ दत्तौ तूणौ येनास्य खाण्डवे॥
en: Jishnu (Arjuna) then thought of the exalted Agni who had forinerly given him two inexhaustible quivers at the burning of the Khandava.

sn: किं नु मोक्ष्यामिधनुषा यन्मे बाणाः क्षयं गताः। अयं च पुरुषः कोऽपि बाणान् चसति सर्वशः॥ हत्वा चैनंधनुष्कोट्या शूलाचेणेव कुञ्जरम्। नयामि दण्डधारस्य यमस्य सदनं प्रति॥
en: (He inentally said), "Alas, my arrows are exhausted! What shall I shoot now from my bow? Who is this person who swallows up my arrows. Killing him by striking with the end of my bow as elephants are killed by clubs, I shall then send him to the wielder of mace, Yama."

sn: प्रगृह्याथधनुष्कोट्या ज्यापाशेनावकृष्य च। मुष्टिभिश्चापि हतवान् वज्रकल्पैर्महाद्युतिः॥
en: Taking up the bow and dragging him (the Kirata) with his bow-string, the greally effulgent (Arjuna) struck him some fearful blows which descended upon him as thunderbolis.

sn: सम्प्रयुद्धोधनुष्कोट्या कौन्तेयः परवीरहा। तदप्यस्यधनुर्दिव्यं जग्राह गिरिगोचरः॥
en: When that slayer of hostile heroes the son of Kunti, began to fight with the end of the bow, that mountaineer snatched (from his hand) that excellent bow.

sn: ततोऽर्जुनो चस्तधनुः खङ्गपाणिरतिष्ठत। युद्धस्यान्तमभीप्सन् वै वेगेनाभिजगाम् तम्॥
en: His bow having been snatched away from his hand, Arjuna, with the desire of ending the fight, rushed with great force at his adversary with sword in hand.

sn: तस्य मूर्ध्नि शितं खङ्गमसक्तं पर्वतेष्वपि। मुमोच भुजवीर्येण विक्रम्य कुरुनन्दनः॥
en: Then that prince of the Kuru race struck that sharp weapon in his (Kirata's) head with the whole strength of his arms, a weapon which could not be resisted even by solid rocks.

sn: तस्य मूर्धानमासाद्य पफालासिवरो हि सः। ततो वृक्षः शिलाभिश्च योधयामास फाल्गुनः॥
en: But that best of swords on falling on his head broke into pieces. Thereupon Falguni began to fight with trees and stones.

sn: तदा वृक्षान् महाकायः प्रत्यगृहणादथो शिलाः। किरातरूपी भगवांस्ततः पार्थो महाबलः॥
en: Then the exalted deity in the disguise of the huge-bodied Kirata bore that shower of trees and stones too. The greatly strong Partha (Arjuna).

sn: मुष्टिभिर्वज्रसंकाशै—ममुत्पादयन् मुखे। प्रजहार दुराधर्षे किरातसमरूपिणि॥
en: His mouth smoking with wrath, struck (again) that irrepressible (deity) in the form of the Kirata with fists which were like thunderbolts.

sn: ततः शक्राशनिसमैर्मुष्टिभिर्भृशदारुणैः। किरातरूपी भगवानर्दयामास फाल्गुनम्॥
en: The exalted deity in the form of the Kirata then struck at Falguni with fists which were (also) like the thunder-bolt of Indra.

sn: ततश्चटचटाशब्दः सुघोरः समपद्यत। पाण्डवस्य च मुष्टीनां किरातस्य च युध्यतः॥
en: In consequence of the fight with fists between the son of Pandu (Arjuna) and the Kirata, great sounds arose in that place.

sn: सुमुहूर्तं तु तद् युद्धमभवल्लोमहर्षणम्। भुजप्रहारसंयुक्तं वृत्रवासवयोरिव॥
en: That fearful and hair-stirring fight with fists, resembling that of Vasava (Indra) and Vitra, lasted only for a moment.

sn: जघानाथ ततो जिष्णुः किरातमुरसा बली। पाण्डवं च विचेष्टं किरातोऽप्यहनद् बली॥
en: The powerful Jishnu (Arjuna), clasping the Kirata (with his both arms) began to press him with his breast. The greatly strong Kirata (also) pressed the insensible son of Pandu.

sn: तयोर्भुजविनिष्पेषात् संघर्षणोरसोस्तथा। समजायत गात्रेषु पावकोऽङ्गारधूमवान्॥
en: In consequence of pressure of their arms and of their breasts, their bodies emitted smokes, as charcoal does in fire.

sn: तत एनं महादेवः पीड्य गात्रैः सुपीडितम्। तेजसा व्यक्रमद् रोषाच्चेतस्तस्य विमोहयन्॥
en: Thereupon the great god pressed his (Arjuna's) body and attacking him in anger with all his might, he deprived him of his consciousness.

sn: ततोऽभिपीडितैर्गात्रैः पिण्डीकृत इवाबभौ। फाल्गुनो गात्रसंरुद्धो देवदेवेन भारत॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, Falguni (Arjuna) thus pressed by the god of gods and his body bruised, became almost like a ball of flesh.

sn: निरुच्छ् वासोऽभवच्चैव संनिरुद्धो महात्मना। पपात भूम्यां निश्चेष्टो गतसत्त्व इवाभवत्॥
en: Pressed by the high-souled deity, he became breathless and falling on the ground without the power of moving, he looked like one who was dead.

sn: स मुहूर्तं तथा भूत्वा सचेताः पुनरुत्थितः। रुधिरेणाप्लुताङ्गस्तु पाण्डवो भृशदुःखितः॥
en: He soon however regained consciousness. Rising up from the ground, his body being covered with blood, the Pandava (Arjuna) becanie overwhelmed with sorrow

sn: शरण्यं शरणं गत्वा भगवन्तं पिनाकिनम्। मृन्मयं स्थण्डिलं कृत्वा माल्येनापूजयद् भवम्॥
en: Mentally bowing before the exalted deity of the Pinaka and making a clay image of that deity, he worshipped it with garlands of flowers.

sn: तच्च माल्यं तदा पार्थः किरातशिरसि स्थितम्। अपश्यत् पाण्डवश्रेष्ठो हर्षेण प्रकृतिं गतः॥
en: Seeing the garlands that he had offered to the (clay image) adorning the head of the Kirata, that best of the Pandava, Partha (Arjuna), was filled with joy and he then regained his ease.

sn: पपात पादयोस्तस्य ततः प्रीतोऽभवद् भवः। उवाच चैनं वचसा मेघगम्भीरगीहरः। जातविस्मयमालोक्य तपःक्षीणाङ्गसंहतिम्॥
en: Thereupon he prostrated himself at his feet and Vava (Shiva) became gratified. Seeing his astonishment and his body emaciated with ascetic austerities, the deity thus spoke to his in the voice as that of the roaring clouds.

sn: भव उवाच भो भोः फाल्गुन तुष्टोऽस्मि कर्मणाप्रतिमेन ते। शौर्येणानेनधृत्या च क्षत्रियो नास्ति ते समः॥
en: Shiva said: O Falguni, I am pleased with you for your matchless deeds. There is no Kshatriya who is equal to you in courage and patience.

sn: समं तेजश्च वीर्यं च ममाद्य तव चानघ। प्रीतस्तेऽहं महाबाहो पश्य मां भरतर्षभ॥
en: O mighty-armed hero, O best of the Bharata race, O sinless one, your strength and prowess are almost equal to mine. I have been pleased with you. Behold me.

sn: ददामि ते विशालाक्ष चक्षुः पूर्वऋषिर्भवान्। विजेष्यसि रणे शत्रू नपि सर्वान् दिवौकसः॥
en: O large-eyed hero, I will give you eyes, (so that you may see me in my real form). You were formerly a Rishi. You will vanquish all your enemies, even (if they be) the dwellers of heaven.

sn: प्रीत्या च तेऽहं दास्यामि यदस्त्रमनिवारितम्। त्वं हि शक्तो मदीयं तदस्त्रंधारयितुं क्षणात्॥
en: Being pleased with you, I shall give you an irrerestible weapon; you shall soon acquire (great) weapons.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततो देवं महादेवं गिरिशं शूलपाणिनम्। ददर्श फाल्गुनस्तत्र सह देव्या महाद्युतिम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said: Thereupon Falguni (Arjuna) saw that greatly effulgent deity, the great god, the dweller of the mountain, the wielder of the Pinaka, with his wife.

sn: स जानुभ्यां महीं गत्वा शिरसा प्रणिपत्य च। प्रसादयामास हरं पार्थः परपुरंजयः॥
en: Kneeling (before him) and bowing down his head to him, that conqueror of enemy's cities, Partha, gratificd Hara (Shiva).

sn: अर्जुन उवाच कपर्दिन् सर्वदेवेश भगनेत्रनिपातन। देवदेव महादेव नीलग्रीव जटाधर॥
en: Arjuna said : O Kapardin, O chief of all the celestials, O destroyer of Vaga's eyes, O god of gods, O great god, O blue throated deity of mattedlocks.

sn: कारणानां च परमं जाने त्वां त्र्यम्बकं विभुम्। देवानां च गतिं देव त्वत्प्रसूतमिदं जगत्॥
en: O three-eyed god, O lord of all, I know you to be the cause of all causes. You are the refuge of all the celestials. The universe has sprung from you.

sn: अजेयस्त्वं त्रिभिर्लोकः सदेवासुरमानुषैः। शिवाय विष्णुरूपाय विष्णवे शिवरूपिणे॥
en: You are incapable of being vanquished by the three worlds of the celestials, of the Asuras and of men. You are Shiva in the form of Vishnu and Vishnu in the form of Shiva.

sn: दक्षयज्ञविनाशाय हरिरुद्राय वै नमः। ललाटाक्षाय शर्वाय मीढुषे शूलपाणये॥
en: You destroyed the sacrifice of Daksha. O Hari, O Rudra, I bow to you. You have an eye on your forehead. O Sharva, O Medrusha, O wielder of trident.

sn: पिनाकगोप्जे सूर्याय मङ्गल्याय च वेधसे। प्रसादये त्वां भगवन् सर्वभूतमहेश्वर॥
en: O wielder of the Pinaka, O Surya, O pure bodied deity, O exalted one, O lord of all creatures, I adore you.

sn: गणेशं जगतः शम्भुं लोककारणकारणम्। प्रधानपुरुषातीतं परं सूक्ष्मतरं हरम्॥
en: O lord of the Ganas, O source of Universal blessings, O (first) cause of the causes of the universe, the foremost of Purusha, the highest and the sublimes Hara.

sn: व्यतिक्रमं मे भगवन् क्षन्तुमर्हसि शंकर। भगवन् दर्शनाकाक्षी प्राप्तोऽस्मीमं महागिरिम्॥
en: O exalted one, O Shankara, you should pardon my fault. It was to get a sight of yourself that I came to this great mountain.

sn: दयितं तव देवेश तापसालयमुत्तमम्। प्रसादये त्वां भगवन् सर्वलोकनमस्कृतम्॥
en: Which is dear to you and which is the excellent abode of ascetics. O chief of the celestials, you are adored by all the worlds and I adore you.

sn: न मे स्यादपराधोऽयं महादेवातिसाहसात्। कृतो मयायमज्ञानाद् विमर्दो यस्त्वया सह। शरणं प्रतिपन्नाय तत् क्षमस्वाद्य शंकर॥
en: Let not my rashness in the combat that I have fought with you from ignorance be considered by you as a fault. O Shankara, I ask your protection. Pardon me for all I have done.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाचत तमुवाच महातेजाः प्रहस्यवृषभध्वजः। प्रगृह्य रुचिरं बाहुं क्षान्तमित्येव फाल्गुनम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : The greatly effulgent Vrishabdhvaja (Shiva), taking hold of the handsome hands of Arjuna, smilingly said to him, “I have pardoned you."

sn: परिष्वज्य च बाहुभ्यां प्रीतात्मा भगवान् हरः। पुनः पार्थं सान्त्वपूर्वमुवाच वृषभध्वजः॥
en: The exalted Hara, whose sign was the bull, (Shiva), cheerfully embracing Arjuna with his arins, again consoled him and thus spoke to him.

sn: देवदेव उवाच नरसवं पूर्वदेहे वै नारायणसहायवान्। बदाँ तप्तवानुचं तपो वर्षायुतान् बहून्॥
en: Shiva said: You were in your former life Nara, the friend of Narayana, You passed many thousands of years in fearful and austere asceticism.

sn: त्वयि वा परमं तेजो विष्णौ वा पुरुषोत्तमे। युवाभ्यां पुरुषाच्याभ्यां तेजसाधार्यते जगत्॥
en: Great prowess exists in you and in Vishnu, that foremost of Purushas. You two by your prowess hold the Universe.

sn: शक्राभिषेके सुमहद्धनुर्जलदनिःस्वनम्। प्रगृह्य दानवाः शस्तास्त्वया कृष्णेन च प्रभो॥
en: O lord, taking up that fearful bow whose twang resembled the deep roars of clouds, you as well as Krishna chastised the Danavas at the coronation of Indra.

sn: तदेतदेव गाण्डीवं तव पार्थ करोचितम्। मायामास्थाय यद् चस्तं मया पुरुषसत्तम॥
en: O Partha this Gandiva which is fit for (only) your hands is that very bow (with which you chastised the Danavas). O foremost of men. I snatched it from you by means of my power of illusion.

sn: तूणौ चाप्यक्षयौ भूयस्तव पार्थ यथोचितौ। भविष्यति शरीरं च नीरुजं कुरनन्दन॥
en: O Partha, these two quivers which is fit only for you, will again be inexhaustible. O descendant of Kuru, your body will be free from pain and disease.

sn: प्रीतिमानस्मि ते पार्थ भवान् सत्यपराक्रमः! गृहाण वरमस्मत्तः काक्षितं पुरुषोत्तम्॥
en: O Partha, your prowess will be incapable of being ever baffled. I have been pleased with you. O foremost of men, ask from me, what you desire to get.

sn: न त्वया पुरुषः कश्चित् पुमान् मर्येषु मानद। दिवि वा वर्तते क्षत्रं त्वत्प्रधानमरिंदम्॥
en: O giver of proper respect (to all men), O chastiser of foes, there is no man either here on earth or in heaven who is cqual to you (in prowess). Nor there is any Kshatriya who is superior to you.

sn: अर्जुन उवाच भगवन् ददासि चेन्मह्यं कामं प्रीत्या वृषध्वज। कामये दिव्यमस्त्रं तद् घोरं पाशुपतं प्रभो॥ यत् तद् ब्रह्मशिरो नाम रौद्रं भीमपराक्रमम्। युगान्ते दारुणे प्राप्ते कृत्स्नं संहरते जगत्॥
en: Arjuna said : O exalted one, O Vrishabdhvaja. O lord, if you will grant me what I desire to possess, I ask from you that fearful weapon which is wielded by you and which is called Brahmashira, that weapon of fearful prowess, which destroys at the end of Yuga the entire universe.

sn: कर्णभीष्मकृपद्रोणैर्भविता तु महाहवः। त्वत्प्रसादान्महादेव जयेयं तान् यथा युधि॥
en: That weapon, with the help of which, O great god, I may through your grace obtain victory in the great battle that will be fought by me with Karna, Bhishma, Kripa and Drona,

sn: दहेयं थेन संग्रमे दानवान् राक्षसांस्तथा। भूतानि च पिशाचाश्च गन्धर्वानथ पन्नगान्॥ यस्मिञ्छूलसहस्राणि गदाश्चोचप्रदर्शनाः। शराश्चाशीविषाकारा: सम्भवन्त्यनुमन्त्रिते॥
en: The weapon by which I may destroy in battle the Danavas, the Rakshasas, the evil spirits, the Pishachas, the Gandharvas and the Nagas. The weapon which when hurled with Mantras produces thousands of darts, maces and virulently poisonous snake-like arrows.

sn: युध्येयं येन भीष्मेण द्रोणेन च कृपेण च। सूतपुत्रेण च रणे नित्यं कटुकभाषिणा॥
en: The weapon by the help of which I may fight with Bhishma, Drona, Kripa and the ever abusive son of Suta (Karna).

sn: एष कामो मे प्रथमः भगवन् भगनेत्रहन्। त्वत्प्रसादाद् विनिर्वृत्तः समर्थः स्यामहं यथा॥
en: O exalted destroyer of Vaga's eyes, my chief desire is that I may be able to fight with them and finally obtain victory.

sn: भव उवाच ददामि तेऽस्त्रं दयितमहं पाशुपतं विभो। समर्थोधारणे मोक्षे संहारे चासि पाण्डव॥
en: Shiva said: O exalted Pandava, I shall give you my favourite weapon called Pashupata. You are capable of holding, hurling and withdrawing it.

sn: नैतद् वेद महेन्द्रोऽपि न यमो न च यक्षराट्। वरुणोऽप्यथवा वायुः कुतो वेत्स्यन्ति मानवाः॥
en: Neither Indra, nor Yama, nor the king of the Yakshas, nor Varuna, nor Vayu knows it, how could it (then) be known to human beings?

sn: न त्वेतत् सहसा पार्थ मोक्तव्यं पुरुषे क्वचित्। जगद् विनाशयेत् सर्वमल्पतेजसि पातितम्॥
en: O Partha, this weapon should not be discharged without proper reason, for if discharged at a weak enemy, it would destroy the whole universe.

sn: अवध्यो नाम नास्त्यत्र त्रैलोक्ये सचराचरे। मनसा चक्षुषा वाचाधनुषा च निपातयेत्॥
en: There is none in the three worlds of mobile and immobile creatures who is incapable of being killed by this weapon. It might be discharged by the mind, by the eyes, by words or by the bow.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तच्छ्रुत्वा त्वरितः पार्थः शुचिर्भूत्वा समाहितः। उपसंगम्य विश्वेशमधीष्वेत्यथ सोऽब्रवीत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having heard this, the son of Pritha (Arjuna) purified himself. Coming to the lord of the universe with rapt attention, he said, "Instruct me.”

sn: ततस्त्वध्यापयामास सरहस्यनिवर्तनम्। तदस्त्रं पाण्डवश्रेष्ठं मूर्तिमन्तमिवान्तकम्॥ उपतस्थे च तत् पार्थं यथा त्र्यक्षमुमापतिम्। प्रतिजग्राह तच्चापि प्रीतिमानर्जुनस्तदा॥
en: He (Shiva) then imparted to that best of Pandavas the knowledge of that weapon which looked like the embodiment of Yama and (also) all the mysteries as regards its method of discharging and withdrawing. That weapon then waited upon Partha as it did before upon Traksha, the lord of Uma. Arjuna with cheerful heart accepted it.

sn: ततश्चचाल पृथिवी सपर्वतवनद्रुमा। ससागरवनोद्देशा संग्रमनगराकरा॥
en: Thereupon the whole earth with its mountains, forests, trees, seas, woods, villages, towns and mines, began to tremble.

sn: शङ्खदुन्दुभिघोषाश्च भेरीणां च सहस्रशः। तस्मिन् मुहूर्ते सम्प्राप्ते निर्घातश्च महानभूत्॥
en: Sounds of thousands of conchs, drums and trumpets were heard. Hurricanes and whirlwinds began to blow.

sn: अथास्त्रं जाज्वलद् घोरं पाण्डवस्यामितौजसः। मूर्तिमद् वै स्थितं पार्वे ददृशुर्देवदानवाः॥
en: The celestials and the Danavas saw that fearful weapon in its embodied from standing at the side of the immeasurably energetic and heroic Pandava.

sn: स्पृष्टस्य त्र्यम्बकेणाथ फाल्गुनस्यामितौजसः। यत् किंचिदशुभं देहे तत् सर्वं नाशमीयिवत्॥
en: Whatever evil there was in the body of the immeasuraely energetic Falguni (Arjuna) was all dispelled by his touch with the three-eyed deity.

sn: स्वर्ग गच्छेत्यनुज्ञातस्त्र्यम्बकेण तदार्जुनः। प्रणम्य शिरसा राजन् प्राञ्जालर्देवमैक्षत॥
en: Then Arjuna was commanded by the threeeyed deity to "Go to heaven." O king, bowing down his head, he gazed at him with joined hands.

sn: ततः प्रभुस्त्रिदिवनिवासिनां वशी महामतिर्गिरिश उमापतिः शिवः। धनुर्महद दितिजपिशाचसूदनं ददौ भवः पुरुषवराय गाण्डिवम्॥
en: Then the lord of all the dwellers of heaven, the deity of blazing splendour, the dweller of mountain, the husband of Uma, Shiva, the source of all blessings. Bhava, gave to Arjuna, that foremost of men, the great bow called Gandharva, capable of destroying the Danavas and the Pishachas.

sn: ततः शुभं गिरिवरमीश्वरस्तदा। सहोमया सिततटसानुकन्दरम्। विहाय तं पतगमहर्षिसेवितं जगाम खं पुरुषवरस्य पश्यत॥
en: The god of gods, accompanied by Uma then leaving that blessed mountain of snowy plateaus and valleys and caves, the favourite resort of the sky-ranging Rishis, went up to the skies in the very sight of that foremost of men (Arjuna).

description: The departure of Indra and other deities
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तस्य सम्पश्यतस्त्वेव पिनाकी वृषभध्वजः। जगामादर्शनं भानुलॊकस्येवास्तमीयिवान्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : The wielder of Pinaka, having the bull for his emblem, then disappeared before the gazing son of Pandu like the sun setting in the sight of the world.

description: The departure of Indra and other deities
sn: ततोऽर्जुनः परं चक्रे विस्मयं परवीरहा। मया साक्षान्महादेवो दृष्ट इत्येव भारत॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, thereupon Arjuna, the slayer of hostile heroes, wondered much at it, saying, "O I have seen the great god of gods.

description: The departure of Indra and other deities
sn: धन्योऽस्म्यनुगृहीतोऽस्मि यन्मया त्र्यम्बको हरः। पिनाकी वरदो रूपी दृष्टः स्पृष्टश च पाणिना॥
en: Fortunate and favoured am I for I have both seen and touched with my hand the three-eyed Hara, the wielder of Pinaka in his boon giving form.

description: The departure of Indra and other deities
sn: कृतार्थं चावगच्छामि परमात्मानमाहवे। शत्रूश्च विजितान् सर्वान् निर्वृत्तं च प्रयोजनम्॥
en: I consider myself greatly blessed; I have already vanquished all my enemies in battle and my object has been accomplished.”

description: The departure of Indra and other deities
sn: इत्येवं चिन्तयानस्य पार्थस्यामिततेजसः। ततो वैदूर्यवर्णाभो भासयन् सर्वतो दिशः। यादोगणवृतः श्रीमानाजगाम जलेश्वरः॥
en: While Partha, of incomparable prowess, was thus meditating, there came the effulgent lord of waters, brilliant like Vaidurya, dazzling all the quarters and accompanied by aquatic animals.

description: The departure of Indra and other deities
sn: नागैर्नदैर्नदीभिश्च दैत्यैः साध्यैश्च दैवतैः। वरुणो यादसां भर्ता वशी तं देशमागमत्॥
en: Accompanied by rivers both male and female, Nagas, Daityas, Siddhas and inferior deities, the self-possessed Varuna, the lord of waters, arrived there.

description: The departure of Indra and other deities
sn: अथ जाम्बूनदवपुर्विमानेन महार्चिषा। कुबेरः समनुप्राप्तो यक्षैरनुगतः प्रभुः॥
en: There came also the lord Kubera, having a body resembling pure gold, seated on a highly splendid car and accompanied by numberless Yakshas.

description: The departure of Indra and other deities
sn: विद्योतयन्निवाकाशमद्भुतोपमदर्शनः। धनानामीश्वरः श्रीमानर्जुनं द्रष्टुमागतः॥
en: The effulgent lord of wealth, most wonderfully beautiful, came there to see Arjuna illuminating the the sky with his effulgence.

description: The departure of Indra and other deities
sn: तथालोकान्तकृच्छ्रीमान् यमः साक्षात् प्रतापवान् मर्त्यमूर्तिधरैः सार्धं पितृभिर्लोकभावनैः॥
en: As also (came) the graceful and powerful Yama, the destroyer of the worlds accompanied by the lords of creations, the manes, both embodied and disembodied.

description: The departure of Indra and other deities
sn: दण्डपाणिरचिन्त्यात्मा सर्वभूतविनाशकृत्। वैवस्वतोधर्मराजो विमानेनावभासयन्॥ त्री ल्लोकान् गुह्यकांश्चैव गन्धर्वांश्च सपन्नगान्। द्वितीय इव मार्तण्डो युगान्ते समुपस्थिते॥
en: The god of justice, the son of Vivasvat, whose soul cannot be meditated upon and who is the destroyer of all creatures, came there in his chariot, mace in hand, lighting the three worlds, with the regions of Guhyakas, Gandharvas and the Nagas like a second sun at the end of a Yuga.

description: The departure of Indra and other deities
sn: ते भानुमन्ति चित्राणि शिखराणि महागिरेः। समास्थायार्जुनं तत्र ददृशस्तपसान्वितम्॥
en: They beheld there from the shinning and variegated summits of the mountains Arjuna engaged in devout penances.

description: The departure of Indra and other deities
sn: ततो मुहूर्ताद् भगवानरावतशिरोगतः। आजगाम सहेन्द्राण्या शक्रः सुरगणैर्वृतः॥
en: Immediately came there also the great Shakra accompanied by his queen, seated on the back of Airavata and encircled by all the celestials.

description: The departure of Indra and other deities
sn: पाण्डुरेणातपत्रेण ध्रियमाणेन मूर्धनि। शुशुभे तारकाराजः सितमभ्रमिव स्थितः॥
en: And the white umbrella being held over his head he shone like the moon in the midst of fleecy clouds.

description: The departure of Indra and other deities
sn: संस्तूयमानो गन्धर्वैर्ऋषिभिश्च तपोधनैः। शृङ्गं गिरेः समासाद्य तस्थौ सूर्य इवोदितः॥
en: Eulogised by Gandharvas and greatly ascetic Rishis, he, attaining to a summit of a mountain, stood there like the rising sun.

description: The departure of Indra and other deities
sn: अथ मेघस्वनोधीमान् व्याजहार शुभां गिरम्। यमः परमधर्मज्ञो दक्षिणां दिशमास्थितः॥
en: Thereupon the highly intelligent and pious Yama, having voice deep as the muttering of clouds, who was stationed on the southern (summit) gave vent to the following auspicious words.

description: The departure of Indra and other deities
sn: अर्जुनार्जुन पश्यास्माल्लोकपालान् समागतान्। दृष्टिं ते वितरामोऽद्य भवानर्हति दर्शनम्॥ पूर्वर्षिरमितात्मा त्वं नरो नाम महाबलः। नियोगाद् ब्रह्मणस्तात मर्त्यतां समुपागतः॥
en: "Behold, O Arjuna, all the protectors of the world have come here; we will give you vision for you are worthy of seeing us. You were in your former life a highly powerful Rishi of immeasurable mental caliber named Nara; by the behest of Brahma, O son, you have been born as a mortal.

description: The departure of Indra and other deities
sn: त्वया च वसुसम्भूतो महावीर्यः पितामहः। भीष्मः परमधर्मात्मा संसाध्यश्च रणेऽनघ॥ क्षत्रं चाग्निसमस्पर्श भारद्वाजेन रक्षितम्। दानवाश्च महावीर्या ये मनुष्यत्वमागताः॥ निवातकवचाश्चैव दानवाः कुरुनन्दन। पितुर्ममांशु देवस्य सर्वलोकप्रतापिनः॥ कर्णश्च सुमहावीर्यस्त्वया वध्योधनंजय।
en: O sinless one, by you shall be vanquished in battle the highly virtuous and powerful grandsire Bhishma, born of Vasus. (You shall also defeat) Kshatriyas of fiery energy protected by the son of Baradvaja as also the highly powerful Danavas who have been born among men. The Danavas named Nivatakavachas, O descendant of Kuru; and the highly powerful Karna, who is a portion of my father who lights all the regions, shall be slain by you.

description: The departure of Indra and other deities
sn: अंशाच क्षितिसम्प्राप्ता देवदानवरक्षसाम्॥ त्वया निपातिता युद्धे स्वकर्मफलनिर्जिताम्। गतिं प्राप्स्यन्ति कौन्तेय यथास्वमरिकर्षण॥
en: O Dhananjaya; the portions of the celestials, Danavas and Rakshasas who have been born on earth. Shall be slain by you in battle; O son of Kunti, O slayer of foes, they shall attain to regions as destined by their acts.

description: The departure of Indra and other deities
sn: अक्षया तव कीर्तिश्च लोके स्थास्यति फाल्गुन। त्वया साक्षान्महादेवस्तोषितो हि महामृधे॥
en: O Falguni; your game shall remain eternal on the earth; you have pleased Mahadeva himself in encounter.

description: The departure of Indra and other deities
sn: लध्वी वसुमती चापि कर्तव्या विष्णुना सह। गृहाणास्त्रं महाबाहो दण्डमप्रतिवारणम्। अनेनास्त्रेण सुमहत् त्वं हि कर्म करिष्यसि॥
en: The earth shall be lightened of her burden by you along with Vishnu; O large-armed hero, accept this weapon of mine-this mace, incapable of being baffled and with it you will accomplish great deeds.

description: The departure of Indra and other deities
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच प्रतिजग्राह तत् पार्थो विधिवत् कुरुनन्दनः। समन्त्रं सोपचारं च समोक्षविनिवर्तनम्॥
en: O descendant of Kuru, the son of Pritha received that weapon duly along with Mantras and rites and the means of hurling and withdrawing it.

description: The departure of Indra and other deities
sn: ततो जलधरश्यामो वरुणो यादसां पतिः। पश्चिमो दिशमास्थाय गिरमुच्चारयन् प्रभुः॥
en: Thereupon stationed in the western quarter, Varuna, the lord of waters and yellow as the clouds gave vent to the following words.

description: The departure of Indra and other deities
sn: पार्थ क्षत्रियमुख्यस्त्वं क्षत्रधर्मे व्यवस्थितः। पश्य मां पृथुताम्राक्ष वरुणोऽस्मि जलेश्वरः॥
en: "O Partha, you are the foremost of Kshatriyas and observe the duties of the Kshatriyas; behold me, O you having coppery eyes, I am Varuna, the lord of waters.

description: The departure of Indra and other deities
sn: मया समुद्यतान् पाशान् वारुणानविारितान्। प्रतिगृहणेष्व कौन्तेय सरहस्यनिवर्तनम्॥
en: When discharged by me my nooses are incapable of being resisted; accept from me, O son of Kunti, these Varuni weapons, along with the means of discharging and withdrawing them.

description: The departure of Indra and other deities
sn: एभिस्तदा मया वीर संग्रामे तारकामये। दैतेयानां सहस्राणि संयतानि महात्मनाम्॥
en: O hero, in the battle on account of Taraka, with these (weapons) thousands of powerful Daityas were bound by me.

description: The departure of Indra and other deities
sn: तस्मदिमान् महासत्त्व मत्प्रसादसमुत्थितान्। गृहाण न हि ते मुच्येदन्तकोऽप्याततायिनः॥
en: O you of great energy, accept all these from me, as given to you out of favour; even if Death be your enemy he will not be able to escape from you.

description: The departure of Indra and other deities
sn: अनेन त्वं यदास्त्रेण संग्रामे विचरिष्यसि। तदा निःक्षत्रिया भूमिर्भविष्यति न संशयः॥
en: When armed with this you will range in the battle-field, forsooth the earth shall be devoid of Kshatriyas.

description: The departure of Indra and other deities
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततः कैलासनिलयोधनाध्यक्षोऽभ्यभाषत। दत्तेष्वस्त्रेषु दिव्येषु वरुणेन यमेन च॥ प्रीतोऽहमपि ते प्राज्ञ पाण्डवेय महाबल। त्वया सह समागम्य अजितेन तथैव च॥
en: Vaishampayana said : After the celestials weapons had been given away by both Varuna and Yama, the lord of wealth having his abode on the summit of Kailasa thus said, “O wise and highly powerful son of Pandu, I am pleased with you; and meeting with you is tantamount to that with Ajita.

description: The departure of Indra and other deities
sn: सव्यसाचिन् महाबाहो पूर्वदेव सनातन। सहास्माभिर्भवाञ्छ्रान्तः पुराकल्पेषु नित्यशः॥ दर्शनात् ते त्विदं दिव्यं प्रदिशामि नरर्षभ। अमनुष्यान् महाबाहो दुर्जयानपि जेष्यसि॥
en: O you who hold the bow with your left hand, O mighty-armed one, O you who were a god before, O eternal one, in the days of yore you were always tired with devout penances along with us. O best of men, I shall grant you celestials vision, by which, O mighty-armed hero, you shall conquer the invincible Daityas and Danavas.

description: The departure of Indra and other deities
sn: मत्तश्चैव भवानाशु गृहणात्वस्त्रमनुत्तमम्। अनेन त्वमनीकानिधार्तराष्ट्रस्यधक्ष्यसि॥
en: Take from me immediately an excellent weapon by which you shall be able to burn done the soldiers of the son of Dhritarashtra.

description: The departure of Indra and other deities
sn: तदिदं प्रतिगृहणीष्व अन्तर्धानं प्रियं मम। ओजस्तेजोद्युतिकरं प्रस्वायनमरातिनुत्॥
en: Take this favourite weapon of mine called Antardhana; this effulgent, mighty and powerful weapon is capable of sending the enemy to sleep.

description: The departure of Indra and other deities
sn: महात्मना शङ्करेण त्रिपुरं निहतं यदा। तदैतदस्त्रं निर्मुक्तं येन दग्धा महासुराः॥
en: When Tripura was slain by the high-souled Shankara this weapon was discharged by which many a mighty Asura were consumed.

description: The departure of Indra and other deities
sn: त्वदर्थमुद्यतं चेदं मया सत्यपराक्रम। त्वम)धारणे चास्य मेरुप्रतिमगौरव॥
en: O you of invincible prowess, this has been taken up by me to give you; O you gifted with the dignity of Meru, you are capable of holding this weapon." son

description: The departure of Indra and other deities
sn: ततोऽर्जुनो महाबाहुर्विधिवत् कुरुनन्दनः। कौबेरमधिजग्राह दिव्यमस्त्रं महाबलः॥
en: Thereupon the mighty-armed and the highly powerful descendant of Kuru, Arjuna duly received that celestials weapon of Kubera.

description: The departure of Indra and other deities
sn: ततोऽब्रवीद् देवराजः पार्थमक्लिष्टकारिणम्। सान्त्वयश्लक्ष्णया वाचा मेघदुन्दुभिनि:स्वनः॥
en: Thereupon consoling, Pritha's of unwearied action, in sweet words, the king of the celestials, having a voice like the sound of clouds of kettle-drum, said,

description: The departure of Indra and other deities
sn: कुन्तीमातर्महाबाहो त्वमीशान: पुरातनः। परां सिद्धिमनुप्राप्तः साक्षाद् देवगतिं गतः॥
en: "O mighty-armed son of Kunti, you are the ancient Ishana; you have already attained to the highest success and dignity of a god.

description: The departure of Indra and other deities
sn: देवकार्यं तु सुमहत् त्वया कार्यमरिंदम आरोढव्यस्त्वया स्वर्गः सज्जीभव महाद्युते॥
en: O subduer of enemies, you of great effulgence, a great work for gods should be performed by you; you are to ascend heaven, prepare yourself.

description: The departure of Indra and other deities
sn: रथो मातलिसंयुक्त आगन्ता त्वत्कृते महीम्। तत्र तेऽहं प्रदास्यामि दिव्यान्यस्त्राणि कौरव॥
en: The car, having Matali as its charioteer, shall come down to the earth for you; O Kaurava, I shall give you these celestials weapons."

description: The departure of Indra and other deities
sn: तान् दृष्ट्वा लोकपालांस्तु समेतान् गिरिमूर्धनि। जगाम विस्मयंधीमान् कुन्ती पुत्रोधनंजयः॥
en: Beholding all the protectors of the world assembled on the summit of the mountain, the intelligent son of Kunti, Dhananjaya, was amazed.

description: The departure of Indra and other deities
sn: ततोऽर्जुनो महातेजा लोकपालान् समागतान्। पूजयामास विधिवद् वाग्भिरद्भिः फलैरपि॥
en: Thereupon the highly effulgent Arjuna duly worshipped the assembled protectors with words, water and fruits.

description: The departure of Indra and other deities
sn: ततः प्रतिययुर्देवाः प्रतिमान्यधनंजयम्। यथागतेन विबुधाः सर्वे काममनोजवाः॥
en: Honouring Dhananjaya in return the celestials went back; all the deities capable of coursing at will went back from where they came.

description: The departure of Indra and other deities
sn: ततोऽर्जुनो मुदं लेभे लब्धास्त्रः पुरुषर्षभः। कृतार्थमथ चात्मानं स मेने पूर्णमानसम्॥
en: Thereupon having obtained that weapon that best of men, Arjuna attained to delight; he then considered himself blessed and as having his desire fulfilled.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच गतेषु लोकपालेषु पार्थः शत्रुनिबर्हणः। चिन्तयामास राजेन्द्र देवराजरथं प्रति।।।।
en: Vaishampayana said : O king of kings, after the Lokapalas had gone away, Partha, the repressor of enemies, began to think of the chariot of the king of celestials.

sn: ततश्चिन्तयमानस्य गुडाकेशस्यधीमतः। रथो मातलिसंयुक्त आजगाम महाप्रभः॥
en: While the intelligent (Arjuna) of controlled senses was thinking, the highly-effulgent car having Matali as its charioteer came there.

sn: नभो वितिमिरं कुर्वञ्जलदान् पाटयन्निव। दिशः सम्पूरयन् नादैर्महामेघरवोपमैः॥
en: Making the sky devastated of darkness, dividing the clouds and filling the quarters with a sound resembling that of huge clouds.

sn: असयः शक्तयो भीमा गदाश्चोग्रप्रदर्शनाः। दिव्यप्रभावाः प्रासाश्च विद्युतश्च महाप्रभाः॥ तथैवाशनयश्चैव चक्रयुक्तास्तुलागुडाः। वायुस्फोटाः सनिर्घाता महामेघस्वनास्तथा॥
en: Dreadful swords and missiles, terriblelooking maces, Prasas of celestials prowess and highly effulgent lightning. Thunder-bolts, Tulagudas (canon) furnished with wheels and worked with atmospheric expansion and emitting sounds resembling that of huge clouds were on the car.

sn: तत्र नागा महाकाया ज्वलितास्याः सुदारुणाः। सिताभ्रकूटप्रतिमाः संहताश्च तथोपलाः॥
en: There (were) huge-bodied and fierce Nagas having fiery mouths heaps of stones white as the fleecy clouds.

sn: दशवाजिसहस्राणिः हरीणां वातरंहसाम्। वहन्ति यं नेत्रमुषं दिव्यं मायामयं रथम्॥
en: Ten thousand horses of golden colour gifted with the speed of wind drew that celestials car full of illusion (with such velocity) that hardly could the eye see it.

sn: तत्रापश्यन्महानीलं वैजयन्तं महाप्रभम्। ध्वजमिन्दीवरश्यामं वंशं कनकभूषणम्॥
en: There he saw the greatly effulgent and blue flag-staff called Vaijayanta resembling the dark blue lotus and adorned with gold and straight as bamboo.

sn: तस्मिन् रथे स्थितं सूतं तप्तहेमविभूषितम्। दृष्ट्वा पार्थो महाबाहुर्देवमेवान्वतर्कयत्॥
en: Beholding seated on that car a charioteer adorned with burning gold, the mighty-armed son of Pritha, considered it as belonging to the celestials.

sn: तथा तर्कयतस्तस्य फाल्गुनस्याथ मातलिः। संनतः प्रस्थितो भूत्वा वाक्यमर्जुनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Thereupon while Falguni was thus thinking about the car, Matali, descending and bending himself low, said to Arjuna.

sn: मातलिरुवाच भो भोः शक्रात्मज श्रीमाञ्छक्रस्त्वां द्रष्टुमिच्छति आरोहतु भवाञ्छीघ्रं रथमिन्द्रस्य सम्मतम्॥
en: Matali said: O lucky one, O son of Shakra, Shakra wants to see you, ascend speedily this car sent by Indra.

sn: आह माममरश्रेष्ठः पिता तव शतक्रतुः। कुन्तीसुतमिह प्राप्तं पश्यन्तु त्रिदशालयाः॥ एष शक्रः परिवृतो देवैर्ऋषिगणैस्तथा। गन्धर्वैरप्सरोभिश्च त्वां दिदृक्षुः प्रतीक्षते॥
en: Your father, the foremost of the immortals and the performer of a thousand sacrifices said to me, “Bring the son of Kunti here and let the celestials see him.” Shakra encircled by the celestials and Rishis, Gandharvas and Apsaras, is waiting to see you.

sn: अस्माल्लोकाद् देवलोकं पाकशासनशासनात्। आरोह त्वं मया साधु लब्धास्त्रः पुनरेष्यसि॥
en: By the command of the chastiser of Paka ascend with me from this region to that of the celestials and having obtained the weapon return therefrom.

sn: अर्जुन उवाच मातले गच्छ शीघ्रं त्वमारोहस्व रथोत्तमम्। राजसूयाश्वमेधानां शतैरपि सुदुर्लभम्॥
en: Arjuna said : O Matali, go soon and make me ascend this best of cars that cannot be obtained even by a hundred Rajasuya and horse-sacrifices.

sn: पार्थिवैः सुमहाभागैर्यज्वभिर्भूरिदक्षिणैः। दैवतैर्वा समारोढुं दानवैर्वा रथोत्तमम्॥
en: Even kings, rendered illustrious by scarifies accompanied with proper gifts, celestials of Danavas are not capable of riding this excellent car.

sn: नातप्ततपसा शक्य एष दिव्यो महारथः। द्रष्टुं वाप्यथवा स्प्रष्टुमारोढुं कुत एव च॥
en: He who has not acquired ascetic merit is not capable of seeing and touching this excellent car far from riding it.

sn: त्वयि प्रतिष्ठिते साधो रथस्थे स्थिरवाजिनि। पश्चादहमथारोक्ष्ये सुकृती सत्पथ यथा।॥
en: O sage, after you have mounted it, after horses have become quiet, I will mount it like a pious man following the road of honesty.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा मातलिः शक्रसारथिः। आरुरोह रथं शीघ्रं हयान् येमे च रश्मिभिः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Hearing his words, Matali, Shakra charioteer, speedily mounted the chariot and controlled the steeds with reins.

sn: ततोऽर्जुनो हृष्टमना गङ्गायामाप्लुतः शुचिः। जजाप जप्यं कौन्तेयो विधिवत् कुरुनन्दनः॥
en: Thereupon Arjuna, the descendant of Kuru and the son of Kunti bathing in the Ganges and becoming purified and with a contented mind, duly repeated his customary prayers.

sn: ततः पितृन् यथान्यायं तर्पयित्वा यथाविधि। मन्दरं शैलराजं तमाप्रष्टुमुपचक्रमे॥
en: Thereupon duly and according to the ordinances offering oblation to the manes he began to invoke Mandara the king of mountains.

sn: साधूनां पुण्यशीलानां मुनीनां पुण्यकर्मणाम्। त्वं सदा संश्रयः शैल स्वर्गमार्गाभिकाक्षिणाम्॥
en: “O you mountain, you are always the refuge of the pious and god-charactered sages seek in heaven.

sn: त्वत्प्रसादात् सदा शैल ब्राह्मणाः क्षत्रिया विशः। स्वर्ग प्राप्ताश्चरन्ति स्म देवैः सह गतव्यथा।॥
en: By your favour, mountain, the Brahmanas, Kshatriyas and Vaishyas attain to heaven and rid of afflictions sport with the celestials.

sn: अद्रिराज महाशैल मुनिसंश्रय तीर्थवन्। गच्छाम्यामन्त्रयामि त्वां सुखमस्म्युषितस्त्वयि॥
en: O king of mountains, O great mountain, O you that contain sages and sacred shrines, I lived happily on you; I go today bidding you farewell.

sn: तव सानूनि कुञ्जाश्च नद्यः प्रस्रवणानि च। तीर्थानि च सुपुण्यानि मया दृष्टान्यनेकशः॥
en: Many a time and often have I seen your table-lands and bowers, your springs and rivulets and your sacred shrines.

sn: फलानि च सुगन्धीनि भक्षितानि ततस्ततः। सुसुगन्धाश्च वार्योधास्त्वच्छरीरविनिःसृताः॥ अमृतास्वादनीया मे पीताः प्रस्रवणोदकाः।
en: I have eaten you savoury fruits and have satisfied my thirst with draughts of perfumed water coming out from your body. I have drunk the water of your spring tasting like nectar.

sn: शिशुर्यथा पितुरङ्के सुसुखं वर्तते नग॥ तथा तवाङ्के ललितं शैलराज मया प्रभो।
en: O mountain, As a child happily lives on the lap of his sire, so I have sported on your lap

sn: अप्सरोगणसंकीर्णे ब्रह्मघोषानुनादिते॥ सुखमस्म्युषितः शैल तव सानुषु नित्यदा।
en: O king of mountains, on your lap filled with Apsaras and resounding with the recitations of the Vedas. I always lived happily on your table-lands

sn: एवमुक्त्वार्जुनः शैलमामन्त्र्य परवीरहा॥ आरुरोह रथं दिव्यं द्योतयन्निव भास्करः।
en: Having thus welcomed and said to the mountain, Arjuna, the slayer of hostile heroes, blazing like the sun, ascended the celestials car.

sn: स तेनादित्यरूपेण दिव्येनाद्भुतकर्मणा॥ ऊर्ध्वमाचक्रमेधीमान् प्रहृष्टः कुरुनन्दनः। सोऽदर्शनपथं यातो मानांधर्मचारिणाम्॥
en: And that intelligent descendant of Kuru, with a delighted heart coursed through the welkin in that car of wonderful deeds resembling the sun in its form. And coming within the view of pious mortals.

sn: ददर्शाद्भुतरूपाणि विमानानि सहस्रशः। न तत्र सूर्यः सोमो वा द्योतते न च पावकः॥
en: He espied thousands of chariots of wondrous make. There did not shine the sun, the nioon or the fire.

sn: स्वयैव प्रभया तत्र द्योतन्ते पुण्यलब्धया। तारारूपाणि यानीह दृश्यन्ते द्युतिमन्ति वै॥ दीपवद् विप्रकृष्टत्वात् तनूनि सुमहान्त्यपि। तानि तत्र प्रभास्वन्ति रूपवन्ति च पाण्डवः॥ ददर्श स्वेषु धिष्ण्येषु दीप्तिमन्तः स्वयार्चिषा। तत्र राजर्षयः सिद्धा वीराश्च निहता युधि॥
en: But it blazed in its own light begotten of virtue and ascetic merit. And those brilliant regions that are seen from the earth in the form of stars. Like lamps, too small on account of the distance, though very large, were seen in their own spheres, by the son of Pandu full of beauty and brilliance and shinning in their native splendour. (There he saw) royal sages of accomplished piety, heroes who had been slain in battle.

sn: तपसा च जितं स्वर्गं सम्पेतुः शतसङ्घशः। गन्धर्वाणां सहस्राणि सूर्यज्वलिततेजसाम्॥ गुह्यकानामृषीणां च तथैवाप्सरसां गणान्। लोकानात्मप्रभान् पश्यन् फाल्गुनो विस्मयान्वितः।३७॥
en: And those who had obtained heaven by their devout penances, hundreds and hundreds of thousands of Gandharvas shinning in effulgence like the sun and also Guhyakas, Rishis and various Apsaras. Beholding those self-effulgent regions, Falguni, stricken with wonder.

sn: पप्रच्छ मातलिं प्रीत्या स चाप्येनमुवाच ह। एते सुकृतिनः पार्थ स्वेषु धिष्ण्येष्ववस्थिताः॥ तान् दृष्टवानसि विभो तारारूपाणि भूतले।
en: Accosted Matali, who gladly replied, saying, "These are pious persons, O son of Pritha, stationed in their respective spheres, whom, you have seen, O lord, from the earth in the form of stars."

sn: ततोऽपश्यत् स्थितं द्वारि शुभं वैजयिनं गजम्॥ ऐरावतं चतुर्दन्तं कैलासमिव शृङ्गिणम्। स सिद्धमार्गमाक्रम्य कुरुपाण्डवसत्तमः॥ व्यरोचत यथापूर्वं मान्धाता पार्थिवोत्तमः। अभिचक्राम लोकान् स राज्ञां राजीवलोचनः॥
en: Then he saw standing at the gate, the white and ever victorious elephant, Airavata, having four tusks resembling the mount Kailasa with its summits. And passing along the path of the Siddhas that foremost of Kurus and Pandavas shone like Mandhata, the best of kings in the days of yore. And he, having lotus eyes, passed through (various) regions set apart for the kings.

sn: एवं स संक्रमंस्तत्र स्वर्गलोके महायशाः। ततो ददर्श शक्रस्य पुरी ताममरावतीम्॥
en: Having thus passed through the celestials regions, the highly illustrious (Arjuna) at last beheld India's city Amaravati.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ददर्श स पुरी रम्यां सिद्धचारणसेविताम्। सर्वर्तुकुसुमैः पुण्यैः पादपैरुपशोभिताम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : He saw the beautiful city resorted to by Siddhas and Charanas, filled with flowers of all seasons and adorned with sacred trees.

sn: तत्र सौगन्धिकानां च पुष्पाणां पुण्यगन्धिनाम्। उद्वीज्यमानो मिश्रेण वायुना पुण्यगन्धिना॥ नन्दनं च वनं दिव्यमप्सरोगणसेवितम्। ददर्श दिव्यकुसुमैराह्वयद्भिरिव दुमैः॥
en: Here as if fanned by the fragrant breezes charged with the fragrance of sweet scented flowers and invited by the celestials flowers and trees he saw the celestials garden Nandana resorted to by the Apsaras.

sn: नातप्ततपसा शक्यो द्रष्टुं नानाहिताग्निना। स लोकः पुण्यकर्तृणां नापि युद्धे पराडमुखैः॥
en: None but those who have gone through devout penances and poured libations on fire, could behold it; that region was for the performers of pious deeds and not for them who had turned their back on the field of battle.

sn: नायज्वभिर्नावतिकैर्न वेदश्रुतिवर्जितैः। नानाप्लुताङ्गैस्तीर्थेषु यज्ञदानबहिष्कृतैः॥
en: (It was not to be seen) by them who had not celebrated sacrifices observed rigid penances or who had been divorced from the Vedas and Shrutis or who had not bathed in sacred waters who had not been distinguished for sacrifices and gifts.

sn: नापि यज्ञहनैः क्षुद्रैर्द्रष्टुं शक्यः कथंचन। पानपैर्गुरुतल्पैश्च मांसादैर्वा दुरात्मभिः॥
en: Those, who had put obstacles in the performance of sacrifices, who were mean, who were addicted to drinking, who had violated the preceptor's bed, who had taken or or meat and who were wicked-minded, were not capable of seeing it.

sn: स तद् दिव्यं वनं पश्यन् दिव्यगीतनिनादितम्। प्रविवेश महाबाहुः शक्रस्य दयितां पुरीम्॥
en: Beholding that celestials garden resounding with celestials music that mighty-armed hero entered the beloved city of Shakra.

sn: तत्र देवविमानानि कामगानि सहस्रशः। संस्थितान्यभियातानि ददर्शायुतशस्तदा॥ संस्तूयमानो गन्धर्वैरप्सरोभिश्च पाण्डवः। पुष्पगन्धवहैः पुण्यैर्वायुभिश्चानुवीजितः॥
en: He beheld their thousands of celestials cars coursing at will stationed in their proper places and Ayutas of such moving every where. The son of Pandu was eulogised by Gandharvas and Apsaras and fanned by the delightful wind carrying the fragrance of flowers.

sn: ततो देवाः सगन्धर्वाः सिद्धाश्च परमर्षयः। हृष्टाः सम्पूजयामासुः पार्थमक्लिष्टकारिणम्॥
en: Thereupon the celestials, accompanied by Gandharvas, Siddhas and great Rishis, delighted, adored the son of Pritha of unwearied actions.

sn: आशीर्वादैः स्तूयमानो दिव्यवादिनि:स्वनैः। प्रतिपेदे महाबाहुः शङ्खदुन्दुभिनादितम्॥ नक्षत्रमार्ग विपुलं सुरवीथीति विश्रुतम्। इन्द्राज्ञया ययौ पार्थः स्तूयमानः समन्ततः॥
en: He (adored) by benedictions accompanied by the sounds of celestials music; the mighty-armed hero heard (on all sides) the music of conchs and drums. Eulogised on all sides and commanded by Indra, the son of Pritha went to that large and extensive starry way named Surabhithi (probably the milk way).

sn: तत्र साध्यास्तथा विश्वे मरुतोऽथाश्चिनौ तथा। आदित्या वसवो रुद्रास्तथा ब्रह्मर्षयोऽमलाः॥ राजर्षयश्च बहवो दिलीपप्रमुखा मृपाः। तुम्बुरुर्नारदचैव गन्धर्वी च ह हाहुहूः॥
en: There he met with Sadhyas, Vishvas, the Maruts, the twin Ashvins, the Adityas, the was Vasus, the Rudras and the pure Brahmana saints. Many a royal saint, many kings headed by the king Dilipa, Tumbaru, Narada and the two Gandharvas named Haha and Huhu.

sn: तान् स सर्वान् समागम्य विधिवत् कुरुनन्दनः। ततोऽपश्यद् देवराजं शतक्रतुमरिंदम्॥
en: Having duly saluted them all, that descendant of Kuru, the slayer of enemies, beheld the king of celestials, the performer of hundred sacrifices.

sn: ततः पार्थो महाबाहुरवतीर्य रथोत्तमात्। ददर्श साक्षाद् देवेशं पितरं पाकशासनम्॥
en: Thereupon descending from the excellent car, the mighty-armed son of Pritha, saw his father, the king of gods and the chastiser of Paka.

sn: पाण्डुरेणातपत्रेण हेमदण्डेन चारुणा। दिव्यगन्धाधिवासेन व्यजनेन विधूयता॥
en: A beautiful white umbrella having a golden staff, was held over his head; he was fanned by a chamara perfumed with celestials fragrance.

sn: विश्वावसुप्रभृतिभिर्गन्धर्वैः स्तुतिवन्दनैः। स्तूयमानं द्विजावयैश्च ऋग्यजुः सामसम्भवैः॥
en: He was eulogised by many Gandharvas headed by Vishvavasu and others, by bards and singers and leading Brahmanas chanting Rig and Yaju hymns.

sn: ततोऽभिगम्य कौन्तेयः शिरसाभ्यगमद् बली। स चैनं वृत्तपीनाभ्यां बाहुभ्यां प्रत्यगृहणत॥
en: Thereupon approaching him the powerful son of Kunti saluted him bending his head low; he (Indra) too embraced him with his round and plump arms.

sn: ततः शक्रासने पुण्ये देवर्षिगणसेविते। शक्रः पाणौ गृहीत्वैनमुपावेशयदन्तिके॥
en: Taking him by hand Shakra made him sit on a portion of his own sacred seat resorted to by the celestials and Rishis.

sn: मूर्ध्नि चैनमुपाघ्राय देवेन्द्रः परवीरहा। अङ्कमारोपयामास प्रश्रयावनतं तदा॥
en: Smelling his head bent low in humility, the king of gods, the slayer of hostile heroes, made him sit on his lap.

sn: सहस्राक्षनियोगात् स पार्थः शक्रासनं गतः। अध्यक्रामदमेयात्मा द्वितीय इव वासवः॥
en: Seated on Shakra's seat, at the command of the thousand-eyed deity, the son of Pritha, of immeasurable prowess appeared like the second Vasava (Indra).

sn: ततः प्रेम्णा वृत्रशत्रुरर्जुनस्य शुभं मुखम्। पस्पर्श पुण्यगन्धेन करेण परिसान्त्वयन्॥
en: Thereupon consoling him and out of affection, the enemy of Vritra touched the beautiful face of Arjuna with his perfumed hands.

sn: प्रमार्जमानः शनकैर्बाहू चास्यायतौ शुभौ। ज्याशरक्षेपकठिनौ स्तम्भाविव हिरण्मयौ॥ वज्रग्रहणचिह्नन करेण परिसान्त्वयन्। मुहुर्मुहुर्वज्रधरो बाहू चास्फोटयच्छनैः॥
en: Patting and gently rubbing again and again with his own hands which bore the marks of the thunder-bolt the handsome and large arms of Arjuna like two golden columns and hard on account of drawing bow-string and arrows, the wielder of thunderbolt began to console him.

sn: स्मयन्निव गुडाकेशं प्रेक्षमाणः सहस्रदृक्। हर्षेणोत्फुल्लनयनो न चातृप्यत वृत्रहा।॥
en: Seeing the smiling Gudakesha (Arjuna) the thousand-eyed deity, the slayer of Vritra, with his eyes expanded with delight, seemed not to be gratified.

sn: एकासनोपविष्टौ तौ शोभयांचक्रतुः सभाम्। सूर्याचन्द्रमसौ व्योम चतुर्दश्यामिवोदितौ॥
en: Seated on one seat, they beautified the assembly like the sun and moon beautifying the sky on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight.

sn: तत्र स्म गाथा गायन्ति साम्ना परमवल्गुना। गन्धर्वास्तुम्बुरुश्रेष्ठाः कुशला गीतसामसु॥
en: Gandharvas headed by Tumbaru, skilled in music sacred and profane, sang hymns in sweet and melodious notes.

sn: घृताची मेनका रम्भा पूर्वचित्तिः स्वयंप्रभा। उर्वशी मिश्रकेशी च दण्डगौरी वरूथिनी॥ गोपाली सहजन्या च कुम्भयोनिः प्रजागरा। चित्रसेना चित्रलेखा सहा च मधुरस्वरा॥ एताश्चान्याश्च ननृतुस्तत्र तत्र सहस्रशः। चित्तप्रसादने युक्ताः सिद्धानां पद्मलोचनाः॥ महाकटितटश्रोण्यः कम्पमानैः पयोधरैः। कटाक्षहावमाधुर्यैश्चेतोबुद्धिमनोहरैः॥
en: Ghritachi, Menaka, Rambha, Purvachithi, Sayamprabha, Urvashi, Misrakeshi, Dandagauri, Varuthini, Gopali, Sahajanya, Kumbhayoni, Prajagara, Chitrasena, Chitralekha, Saha, Saha, Madhurasvara, these and thousands of others having lotus-eyes, engaged in captivating the minds of the sages of accomplished piety, danced there. Having slim waists and fair, large hips they began to make various gestures shaking their breasts, casting their side-long looks and displaying other motions capable of captivating heart and mind of the spectators.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततो देवाः सगन्धर्वाः समादायार्घ्यमुत्तमम्। शक्रस्य मतमाज्ञाय पार्थमानचुरञ्जसा॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Thereupon the celestials and the Gandharvas, knowing the opinion of Shakra (Indra) procured an excellent Arghya and they presented it to Partha (Arjuna) as soon as possible.

sn: पाद्यमाचमनीयं च प्रतिग्राह्य नृपात्मजम्। प्रवेशयामासुरथो पुरन्दरनिवेशनम्॥
en: Having given him water to wash his foe and feet, they made the prince enter the palace of Purandara (Indra).

sn: एवं सम्पूजितो जिष्णुरुवास भवने पितुः। उपशिक्षन महास्त्राणि ससंहाराणि पाण्डवः॥
en: Having been thus worshipped, Jishnu (Arjuna) lived in the house of his father (Indra). The Pandava (Arjuna) then began to learn the great weapons together with the mode of withdrawing them.

sn: शक्रस्य हस्ताद् दयितं वज्रमस्त्रं च दुःसहम्। अशनीश्च महानादा मेघबर्हिणलक्षणाः॥
en: He received from the hands of Shakra (Indra) his favourite Vajra (thunder) weapon of irresistible force and also those lightning of tremendous roars, fashes of which bespoken (by the appearance) of clouds and (the dancing) of peacocks.

sn: गृहीतास्त्रस्तु कौन्तेयो भ्रातन् सस्मार पाण्डवः। पुरन्दरनियोगाच्च पञ्चाब्दानवसत् सुखी॥
en: The son of Kunti, the Pandava (Arjuna), after receiving the weapons, remembered his brothers. At the command of Purandara (Indra) he lived there for five years in (great) happiness.

sn: ततः शक्रोऽब्रवीत् पार्थं कृतास्त्रं काल आगते। नृत्यं गीतं च कौन्तेय चित्रसेनादवाप्नुहि॥
en: When the proper time came, Shakra (Indra) said to Partha (Arjuna), “O son of Kunti, iearn from Chitrasena singing and dancing.

sn: वादित्रं देवविहितं नृलोके यन्न विद्यते। तदर्जयस्व कौन्तेय श्रेयो वै ते भविष्यति॥
en: Learn (instrumental) music known only to the celestials which does not exist in the world of men. O son of Kunti, if you learn all this, it will be for your good.”

sn: सखायं प्रददौ चास्य चित्रसेनं पुरन्दरः। स तेन सह संगम्य रेमे पार्थो निरामयः॥
en: Purandara then gave him to Chitrasena as his friend. Partha (Arjuna) then lived with him in happiness and peace.

sn: गीतवादित्रनृत्यानि भूय एवादिदेश ह। तथापि नालभच्छर्म तपस्वी द्यूतकारितम्॥
en: He (Chitrasena) taught him vocal and instrumental music and dancing. But remembering the game at dice the active (Arjuna) did not obtain any peace of mind.

sn: दुःशासनवधामर्षी शकुनेः सौबलस्य च। ततस्तेनातुलां प्रीतिमुपागम्य क्वचित् क्वचित्। गान्धर्वमतुलं नृत्यं वादित्रं चोपलब्धवान्॥
en: Thinking of Shakuni, the son of Subala and thinking also with anger of Dushasana's death (he got no peace). But as he derived unrivalled pleasure from the matchless singing and dancing of the Gandharvas he was able to learn their arts.

sn: स शिक्षितो नृत्यगुणाननेकान्। वादित्रगीतार्थगुणांश्च सर्वान्। न शर्म लेभे परवीरहन्ता भ्रातृन् स्मरन् मातरं चैव कुन्तीम्॥
en: Having learnt various kinds of dance and various sorts of vocal and instrumental music, that slayer of hostile heroes, (Arjuna) did not (still) obtain any peace of mind, remembering his brothers and (his mother) Kunti.

description: The colloquy between Chitrasena and Urvashi
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच आदावेवाथ तं शक्रश्चित्रसेनं रहोऽब्रवीत्। पार्थस्य चक्षुरुर्वश्यां सक्तं विज्ञाय वासवः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : One day Vasava (Indra), knowing that the glances of Partha were cast on Urvashi, called Chitrasena, spoke to him in private.

description: The colloquy between Chitrasena and Urvashi
sn: गन्धर्वराज गच्छाद्य प्रहितोऽप्सरसां वराम्। उर्वशी पुरुषव्याघ्र सोपातिष्ठतु फाल्गुनम्॥
en: Indra said: O chief of the Gandharvas, sent by me go today to that foremost of Apsaras, Urvashi, so that she might wait upon that best of men, Falguni.

description: The colloquy between Chitrasena and Urvashi
sn: यथार्चितो गृहीतास्त्रो विद्यया मन्नियोगतः। तथा त्वया विधातव्यं स्त्रीषु संगविशारदः॥
en: As you have, at my command, made him learned in all the weapons worshipped by all, so you should also make him learned in all the arts of mixing with the females.

description: The colloquy between Chitrasena and Urvashi
sn: एवमुक्तस्तथेत्युक्त्वा सोऽनुज्ञां प्राप्य वासवात्। गन्धर्वराजोऽप्सरसमभ्यगादुर्वशी वराम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having been thus addressed, he said, "So be it.” And receiving the command of Vasava (Indra), the chief of the Gandharvas went to that foremost of Apsaras, Urvashi.

description: The colloquy between Chitrasena and Urvashi
sn: तां दृष्ट्वा विदितो हृष्टः स्वागतेनार्चितस्तया। सुखासीनः सुखासीनां स्मितपूर्वं वचोऽब्रवीत्॥
en: Seeing him she recognised and being delighted worshipped him by inquiring after his welfare. Having been comfortably seated, he smilingly thus spoke to her who was also comfortably seated.

description: The colloquy between Chitrasena and Urvashi
sn: विदितं तेऽस्तु सुश्रोणि प्रहितोऽहमिहागतः। त्रिदिवस्यैकराजेन त्वत्प्रसादाभिनन्दिना॥
en: Chitrasena said : O lady of fair hips, know that I have come here being sent by the one sole king of heaven who asks from you a favour.

description: The colloquy between Chitrasena and Urvashi
sn: वस्तु देवमनुष्येषु प्रख्यातः सहजैर्गुणैः। श्रिया शीलेन रूपेण व्रतेन च दमेन च। प्रख्यातो बलवीर्येण सम्मतः प्रतिभानवान्॥
en: He, who is known among good men for his grace, behaviour, beauty, vows and selfcontrol, who is famous for his might and prowess, who is respected by the pious, who is endued with presence of mind.

description: The colloquy between Chitrasena and Urvashi
sn: वर्चस्वी तेजसा युक्तः क्षमावान् वीतमत्सरः। साङ्गोपनिषदान् वेदांश्चतुराख्यानपञ्चमान्॥
en: Who is a genius and who possesses great energy, who is forgiving and who is without any sort of malice, who has studied the four Vedas and the Upanishadas with all their branches and also the Puranas.

description: The colloquy between Chitrasena and Urvashi
sn: योऽधीते गुरुशुश्रूषां मेधां चाष्टगुणाश्रयामा ब्रह्मचर्येण दाक्ष्येण प्रसवैर्वयसापि च॥
en: Who is endued with devotion to his preceptors, who possesses intellect that stands on the eight attributes, who by his Brahmacharya, ability origin and age.

description: The colloquy between Chitrasena and Urvashi
sn: एको वै रक्षिता चैव त्रिदिवं मघवानिव। अकत्यनो मानयिता स्थूललक्ष्यः प्रियंवदः॥
en: Who is alone capable of protecting heaven like Maghabat himself, who is never boastful, who shows (proper) respects to all, who clearly sees even the minutes thing as if they are large and gross, who is sweet-speeched.

description: The colloquy between Chitrasena and Urvashi
sn: सुहृदश्चान्नपानेन विविधेनाभिवर्षति। सत्यवाक् पूजितो वक्ता रूपवाननहंकृतः॥
en: Who showers on his friends and dependents various kinds of foods and drinks, who is truthful, who is worshipped by all, who is eloquent, handsome and without pride.

description: The colloquy between Chitrasena and Urvashi
sn: भक्तानुकम्पी कान्तश्च प्रियश्च स्थिरसंगरः। प्रार्थनीयैर्गुणगणैर्महेन्द्रवरुणोपमः॥
en: Who is kind to those devoted to him, who is pleasing and dear to all, who is firm in promise, who is like Mahendra and Varuna in every desirable attribute.

description: The colloquy between Chitrasena and Urvashi
sn: विदितस्तेऽर्जुनो वीरः स स्वर्गफलमाप्नुयात्। त्वं तु शक्राभ्यनुज्ञाता तस्य पादान्तिकं व्रज। तदेवं कुरु कल्याणि प्रसन्नस्त्वांधनंजयः॥
en: Is the heroic Arjuna, thus known to you. O blessed lady, he is made to taste the fruits (pleasure) of heaven. At the command of Shakra (Indra) let him today obtain your feet. Do this, for Dhananjaya (Arjuna) is inclined to you.

description: The colloquy between Chitrasena and Urvashi
sn: एवमुक्ता स्मितं कृत्वा सम्मानं बहु मन्य च। प्रत्युवाचोर्वशी प्रीता चित्रसेनमनिन्दिता॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having been thus addressed, Urvashi of faultless feature received the words of Chitrasena with high respect. She then smiled and replied to him thus with cheerfulness.

description: The colloquy between Chitrasena and Urvashi
sn: यस्त्वस्य कथित: सत्यो गुणोद्देशस्त्वया मम। तं श्रुत्वाव्यथयं पुंसो वृणुयां किमतोऽर्जुनम्॥
en: Urvashi said: Having heard the virtues that should adorn men, as told by you I would bestow my favours upon any man, why should I not then choose Arjuna?

description: The colloquy between Chitrasena and Urvashi
sn: महेन्द्रस्य नियोगेन त्वत्तः सम्प्रणयेन च। तस्य चाहं गुणौघेन फाल्गुने जातमन्मथा। गच्छ त्वं हि यथाकाममागमिष्याम्यहं सुखम्॥
en: At the command of Indra and for my friendship for you and also moved by the many virtues of Falguni (Arjuna), I am already full of the god of love. Go therefore wherever you like to go I shall go to him.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततो विसृज्य गन्धर्वं कृतकृत्यं शुचिस्मिता। उर्वशी चाकरोत् स्नानं पार्थदर्शनलालसा॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having sent away the Gandharva successful (in his mission), the smiling Urvashi, moved by the desire of possessing Partha (Arjuna), bathed.

sn: स्नानालंकरणैर्हद्यैर्गन्धमाल्यैश्च सुप्रभैः। धनंजयस्य रूपेण शरैर्मन्मथचोदितैः॥
en: After the both she adorned herself with charming and greatly splendid ornaments and sweet scented garlands. Her heart was pierced by the arrows of the god of love on account of the beauty and grace of Dhananjaya (Arjuna).

sn: अतिविद्धेन मनसा मन्मथेन प्रदीपिता। दिव्यास्तरणसंस्तीर्णे विस्तीर्णे शयनोत्तमे॥ चित्तसंकल्पभावेन सुचित्तानन्यमानसा। मनोरथेन सम्प्राप्तं रमन्त्येनं हि फाल्गुनम्॥
en: Being greatly pierced by (the arrows of the) god of love and being excited by him, she withdrew her mind from any other object; and with her imagination highly inflamed, she mentally sported with him (Arjuna) on a wide and excellent bed laid over with celestials sheets.

sn: निर्गस्य चन्द्रोदयने विगाढे रजनीमुखे। प्रस्थिता सा पृथुश्रोणी पार्थस्य भवनं प्रति॥
en: Starting at the time when the moon rose and the twilight deepened, that lady of high hips went towards the abode of Partha (Arjuna).

sn: मृदुकुञ्चितदीर्घेण कुमुदोत्करधारिणा। केशहस्तेन ललना जगामाथ विराजती॥
en: That lady went looking extremely beautiful, with her crisp, soft and long veni (braids of hair) adorned with bunches of flowers.

sn: भ्रक्षेपालापमाधुपैः कान्त्या सौम्यतया पे च। शशिनं वक्त्रचन्द्रेण साऽऽह्वयन्तीव गच्छति॥
en: With her beauty, grace and the charm of the motions of her eye-brows, with her soft accents and moon-like face, she walked on defying the moon.

sn: दिव्याङ्गरागौ सुमुखो दिव्यचन्दनरूषितौ। गच्छन्त्या हाररुचिरौ स्तनौ तस्या ववल्गतुः॥
en: As she proceeded along, her two welldevoted and finely tapering breasts, adorned with a golden chain and celestials unguent and also with fragrant sandal paste, began to tremble.

sn: स्तनोद्वहनसंक्षोभान्नम्यमाना पदे पदे। त्रिवलीदामचित्रेण मध्येमातीवशोभिना।॥
en: In consequence of the weight of her two breasts, she had to slightly stoop forward at every step; it displayed the beauty of her waist lined with the three-folds.

sn: अधो भूधरविस्तीर्णं नितम्बोन्नतपीवरम्। मन्मथायतनं शुभं रसनादामभूषितम्॥ ऋषीणामपि दिव्यानां मनोव्याघातकारणम्। सूक्ष्मवस्त्रधरं रेजे जघनं निरवद्यवत्॥
en: He fair, high, round and matchless hip which was wide as two hillocks, which was the charming abode of the god of love, which was decked with the chains of gold and which was capable of shaking the saint-ship of the celestials Rishis, being covered with thin attire, looked highly beautiful.

sn: गूढगुल्फधरौ पादौ ताम्रायततलाङ्गुली। कूर्मपृष्ठोन्नतौ चापि शोभेते किङ्किणीकिणौ॥
en: Her feet, with beautiful ankles, with flat soles and bright copper-colored toes high and carved like the back of a tortoise, looked extremely charming with the ornaments with rows of little bells.

sn: सीधुपानेन चाल्पनं तुष्ट्याथ मदनेन च। विलासनैश्च विविधैः प्रेक्षणीयतराभवत्॥
en: Exhilarated with the little liquor she had drunk and excited also by desire she moved in many attitudes and looked more beautiful than ever.

sn: सिद्धचारणगन्धर्वैः सा प्रयाता विलासिनी। बह्वाश्चर्येऽपि वै स्वर्गे दर्शनीयतमाकृतिः॥
en: Not withstanding there were many wonderful sights in heaven the Siddhas, the Charanas and the Gandharvas considered her to be the most beautiful object as that beautiful lady went on.

sn: सुसूक्ष्मणोत्तरीयेण मेघवर्णेन राजता। तनुरभ्रावृता व्याम्नि चन्द्रलेखेव गच्छति॥
