en: The upper half of her body being clad in an attire of fine texture and of cloud colour, she looked like the digit of the moon moving on in the sky covered over by the (passing) fleecy clouds.

sn: ततः प्राप्ता क्षणेनैव मन:पवनगामिनी। भवनं पाण्डुपुत्रस्य फाल्गुनस्य शुचिस्मिता॥
en: That lady of the speed of mind or the wind, that beauty of charming siniles reached the abode of the son of Pandu Falguni (Arjuna) in a moment.

sn: तत्र द्वारमनुप्राप्ता द्वारस्थेश्व निवेदिता। अर्जुनस्य नरश्रेष्ठ उर्वशी शुभलोचना॥
en: O foremost of men, having arrived at the gate (of Arjuna's abode), Urvashi of charming eyes sent words (to Arjuna) through the gatekeeper.

sn: उपातिष्ठत तद् वेश्म निर्मलं सुमनोहरम्। स शङ्कितमना राजन् प्रत्युद्गच्छत तां निशि॥
en: O king, she entered that brilliant and charming house. Seeing her at night, Arjuna with fear-stricken heart went forward to receive her.

sn: दृष्ट्वैव चोर्वशी पार्थो लज्जासंवृतलोचनः। तदाभिवादनं कृत्वा गुरुपूजां प्रयुक्तवान्॥
en: Seeing Urvashi, Partha closed his eyes form modesty. Then saluting her, he offered her the worship usually offered to a superior.

sn: अर्जुन उवाच अभिवादये त्वां शिरसा प्रवराप्सरसां वरे। किमाज्ञापयसे देवि प्रेष्यस्तेऽहमुपस्थितः॥
en: Arjuna said : O foremost of all the foremost of Apsaras, I salute you by bowing my head. O celestials lady, what is your command? I wait upon you as a servant.

sn: फाल्गुनस्य वचः श्रुत्वा गतसंज्ञा तदोर्वशी। गन्धर्ववचनं सर्वं श्रावयामास तं तदा॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having heard the words of Falguni (Arjuna) Urvashi became deprived of her senses. She then told him all that was told to her by the Gandharva (Chitrasena).

sn: उर्वश्युवाच यथा ते चित्रसेनेन कथितं मनुजोत्तम। तत् तेऽहं सम्प्रवक्ष्यामि यथा चाहमिहागता॥
en: Urvashi said: O best of men, I shall tell you all that was told to me by Chitrasena and the reason why I have come here.

sn: उपस्थाने महेन्द्रस्य वर्तमाने मनोरमे। तवागमनतो वृत्ते स्वर्गस्य परमोत्सवे॥ रुद्राणां चैव सांनिध्यमादित्यानां च सर्वशः। समागमेऽश्विनोश्चैव वसूनां च नरोत्तम॥ महर्षीणां च संघेषु राजर्षिप्रवरेषु च। सिद्धचारणयक्षेषु महोरगगणेषु च॥ उपविष्टेषु सर्वेषु स्थानमानप्रभावतः। ऋद्ध्या प्रज्वलमानेषु अग्निसोमार्कवर्मसु॥ वीणासु वाद्यमानासु गन्धर्वैः शक्रनन्दन। दिव्ये मनोरमे गेये प्रवृत्ते पृथुलोचन॥ सर्वाप्सरःसु मुख्यासु प्रनृत्तासु कुरूद्वह। त्वं किलानिमिषः पार्थ मामेकां तत्र दृष्टवान्।॥
en: On account of your coming here, Mahendra had convened a large and charming assembly in which great festivities of heaven were held. O best of men, there came all the Rudras, the Adityas. A large member of great Rishis, also royal sages, the Siddhas, the Charanas, the Yakshas and the great Nagas. When all those (celestials) as effulgent as the fire or the sun or the moon took their seats according to their rank, honour and prowess. The Gandharvas, O son of Shakra (Indra), O large-eyed hero, began to play on the Vinas and to sing the charming songs of celestials melody. O perpetuator of the Kuru race, the chief Apsaras also began to dance. O Partha, you had looked at me only once with a steadfast gaze.

sn: तत्र वावभृथे तस्मिन्नुपस्थाने दिवौकसाम्। तव पित्राभ्यनुज्ञाता गताः स्वं स्वं गृहं सुराः॥ तथैवाप्सरसः सर्वा विशिष्टाः स्वगृहं गताः। अपि चान्याश्च शत्रुघ्न तव पित्रा विसर्जिताः।॥
en: When that assembly of the celestials broke, the celestials at the command of your father (Indra) went away to their respective homes. O slayer of foes, the chief Apsaras also and other too at the command of your father went away to their own abodes.

sn: ततः शक्रेण संदिष्टश्चित्रसेनो ममान्तिकम्। प्राप्तः कमलपत्राक्ष स च मामब्रवीदथ॥
en: O lotus-eyed one, therefore at the command of Shakra. (Indra), Chitrasena came to me; and arriving at my house, he then thus spoke to me.

sn: त्वत्कृतेऽहं सुरेशेन प्रेषितो वरवर्णिनि। प्रियं कुरु महेन्द्रस्य मम चैवात्मनश्च ह॥
en: O charming lady, I have been sent to you by the chief of the celestials. Do the favourite work of Mahendra and of myself and also of yourself.

sn: शक्रतुल्यं रणे शूरं सदौदार्यगुणान्वितम्। पार्थ प्रार्थय सुश्रोणि त्वमित्येवं तदाब्रवीत्॥
en: O lady of fair hips, desire (to possess) him who is as heroic in battle as Indra and who is always endued with the virtue of magnanimity.” He thus spoke to me.

sn: ततोऽहं समनुज्ञाता तेन पित्रा च तेऽनघ। तवान्तिकमनुप्राप्ता शुश्रूषितुमरिदम्॥
en: O sinless one, thus commanded by him and also by your father, O chastiser of foes, I have come to wait upon you.

sn: त्वद्गुणाकृष्टचित्ताहमनङ्गवशमागता। चिराभिलषितो वीर ममाप्येष मनोरथः॥
en: O hero, my heart has been fascinated with your virtues. I am under the influence of the god of love. This is my wish and I have cherished it for ever.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तां तथा ब्रुवतीं श्रुत्वा भृशं लज्जाऽऽवृतोऽर्जुनः उवाच कर्णौ हस्ताभ्यां पिधाय त्रिदशालये॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Hearing her speak there in that heaven in this way, Arjuna was filled with great shame. He shut his ears with his hands and said.

sn: दुःश्रुतं मेऽस्तु सुभगे यन्मां वदसि भाविनि। गुरुदारैः समाना मे निश्चयेन वरानने॥
en: Arjuna said : O blessed lady, O charming featured one, it is not proper for me to hear what you have said to me. You are considered by me as the wife of my superior.

sn: यथा कुन्ती महाभागा यथेन्द्राणी शची मम। तथा त्वमपि कल्याणी नात्र कार्या विचारणा॥
en: As the illustrious Kunti is to me, as the wife of Indra, Sachi, is to me. O blessed lady, so are you to me. There is no doubt about it.

sn: यच्चेक्षितासि विस्पष्टं विशेषेण मया शुभे। तच्च कारणपूर्वं हि शृणु सत्यं शुचिस्मिते॥
en: O blessed one, O lady of charming smiles, I did gaze specially at you is true. By there was a reason for it. I shall truly tell it to you, hear.

sn: इयं पौरववंशस्य जननी मुदितेति ह। त्वामहं दृष्टवांस्तत्र विज्ञायोत्फुल्ललोचनः॥ न मामर्हसि कल्याणि अन्यथाध्यातुमप्सरः। गुरोर्गुरुतरा मे त्वं मम त्वं वंशवर्धिनी॥
en: I gazed at you with wide expanded eyes in delight, thinking, “This is the mother of the Puru dynasty." O blessed one, O Apsara, you should not entertain any other feeling towards me, for you are superior to my superior, you are perpetuator of my race.

sn: उर्वश्युवाच अनावृताश्च सर्वाः स्म देवराजाभिनन्दन। गुरुस्थाने न मां वीर नियोक्तुं त्वमिहार्हसि॥
en: Urvashi said: O son of the celestials king, O hero, we (Apsaras) are free and unfettered in our choice. You should not therefore place me in the position of our superior.

sn: पूरोर्वशे हि ये पुत्रा नप्तारो वा त्विहागताः। तपसा रमयन्त्यस्मान्न च तेषां व्यतिक्रमः॥ तत् प्रसीद न मामात विसर्जयितुमर्हसि। हृच्छयेन च संतप्तं भक्तां च भज मानद॥
en: The sons and grandsons of the Puru dynasty, who have come her from their asceticism, all sport with us; and they do not incur any sin by doing it. Therefore be favourable towards me. You ought not send me away. O giver of proper respect, I am burning with desire. I am devoted to you, therefore accept me.

sn: अर्जुन उवाच शृणु सत्यं वरारोहे यत् त्वां वक्ष्याम्यनिन्दिते। शृण्वन्तु मे दिशश्चैव विदिशश्च सदेवताः॥
en: Arjuna said: O beautiful lady, beauty of faultless features, hear what I truly tell you and also let the four directions and the four transverse directions and also the celestials hear.

sn: यथा कुन्ती च माद्री च शची चैव ममानघे। तथा च वंशजननी त्वं हि मेऽद्य गरीयसी॥
en: O sinless one, as Kunti, Madri and Sachi is to me, so are you to me, an object of respect, the mother of our race.

sn: गच्छ मूर्धा प्रपन्नोऽस्मि पादौ ते वरवर्णिनि। त्वं हि मातृवत् पूज्या रक्ष्योऽहं पुत्रवत् त्वया॥
en: O beautiful complexioned one, go away, I bow my head to you, I prostrate myself at your feet. You are worthy of my worship as my mother. Protect me as your son.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्ता तु पार्थेन उर्वशी क्रोधमूर्च्छिता। वेपन्ती भृकुटीवक्रा शशापाथधनंजयम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having been thus addressed by Partha, Urvashi lost her senses out of anger. Trembling in anger and contracting her brows, she thus cursed Dhananjaya (Arjuna).

sn: उर्वश्युवाच तव पित्राभ्यनुज्ञातां स्वयं च गृहमागताम्। यस्मान्मां नाभिनन्देथाः कामबाणवशंगताम्॥ तस्मात् त्वं नर्तनः पार्थ स्त्रीमध्ये मानवर्जितः। अपुमानिति विख्यातः षण्ढवद् विचरिष्यसि॥
en: Urvashi said: As you insult a woman who come to you at the command of your father and at her own desire, (a woman) who is pierced with the arrows of the god of love. O Partha, you shall have to live among women, losing all respect becoming a dancer and being deprived of manhood.

sn: एवं दत्त्वार्जुने शापं स्फुरदोष्ठी श्वसन्त्यथ। पुन: प्रत्यागता क्षिप्रमुर्वशी गृहमात्मनः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having thus cursed Arjuna, with her lips quivered and her breaths heavily drawn, Urvashi speedily returned to her own abode.

sn: ततोऽर्जुनस्त्वरमाणश्चित्रसेनमरिंदमः। सम्प्राप्य रजनीवृत्तं तदुर्वश्या यथातथम्॥ निवेदयामास तदा चित्रसेनाय पाण्डवः। तत्र चैवं यथावृत्तं शापं चैव पुनः पुनः॥
en: Thereupon that chastiser of foes Arjuna soon went to Chitrasena. Having got him, the son of Pandu (Arjuna) told him all that had happened in the night and also what had happened between himself and Urvashi, especially mentioning ihe curse again and again.

sn: अवेदयच्च शक्रस्य चित्रसेनोऽपि सर्वशः। तत आनाय्य तनयं विविक्ते हरिवाहनः॥ सान्त्वयित्वा शुभैर्वाक्यैः स्मयमानोऽभ्यभाषत। सुपुत्राद्य पृथा तात त्वया पुत्रेण सत्तम॥
en: Chitrasena also told everything to Shakra (Indra). Then Harivahana (Indra), calling his son in private. And consoling him in sweet words, thus smilingly spoke to him, "O excellent man, O child, having obtained you, Pritha (Kunti) has today became a true mother.

sn: ऋषयोऽपि हिधैर्येण जिता वै ते महाभुजा यत् तु दत्तवती शापमुर्वशी तव मानद॥ स चापि तेऽर्थकृत् तात साधकश्च भविष्यति॥ अज्ञातवासो वस्तव्यो भवद्भिर्भूतलेऽनघ। वर्षे त्रयोदशे वीर तत्र त्वं क्षपयिष्यसि॥
en: O mighty-armed hero, O giver of proper respects, you have defeated even the Rishis by your patience. Urvashi's curse will be to your good. O child, it will come very much to your use. O sinless one, O hero, you shall have to pass on earth the thirteenth year (of your exile) disguised and undiscovered. It will then the curse will be much to your benefit.

sn: तेन नर्तनवेषेण अपुंस्त्वेन तथैव च। वर्षमेकं विहृत्यैव ततः पुंस्त्वमवाप्स्यसि॥
en: Having passed one year as a dancer without manhood, you shall again regain your power.

sn: एवमुक्तस्तु शक्रेण फाल्गुनः परवीरहा। मुदं परमिकां लेभे न च शापं व्यचिन्तयत्॥
en: Having been thus addressed by Shakra (Indra), that slayer of hostile heroes, Falguni, became exceedingly glad and ceased to think of the curse.

sn: चित्रसेनेन सहितो गन्धर्वेण यशस्विना। रेमे स स्वर्गभवने पाण्डुपुत्रोधनंजयः॥
en: The son of Pandu, Dhananjaya, sported in his celestials abode with the illustrious Gandharva Chitrasena.

sn: इदं यः शृणुयाद् वृत्तं नित्यं पाण्डुसुतस्य वै। न तस्य कामः कामेषु पापकेषु प्रवर्तते॥
en: The desires of the man, who often hears this history of the son of Pandu (Arjuna), never runs after lustful ends.

sn: इदममरवरात्मजस्य घोरं शुचि चरितं विनिशम्य फाल्गुनस्य। स्त्रिदिवगता विरमन्ति मानवेन्द्राः॥
en: Those foremost of men, who listen to this history of greatly pure conduct of Falgunii (Arjuna), becoming freed from pride, arrogance, wrath an other faults, ascend to heaven and they (merrily) sport there.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच कदाचिदटमानस्तु महर्षिरुत लोमशः। जगाम शक्रभवनं पुरन्दरदिदृक्षया॥ स समेत्य नमस्कृत्य देवराज महामुनिः। ददर्शार्धासनगतं पाण्डवं वासवस्य हि॥
en: Vaishampayana said : One day the great Rishi Lomasha, in the course of his wanderings, went to the abode of Shakra (Indra) with the intention of seeing Purandara (Indra). Having come to him, the great Rishi bowed to the king of the celestials. He saw that the son of Pandu (Arjuna) occupying the half of the seat of Vasava (Indra).

sn: ततः शक्राभ्यनुज्ञात आसने विष्टरोत्तरे। निषसाद द्विजश्रेष्ठः पूज्यमानो महर्षिभिः॥
en: Having been worshipped by the great Rishis, that best of the twice-born sat at the . desire of Shakra (Indra) on an excellent seat.

sn: तस्य दृष्ट्वाभवद् बुद्धिः पार्थमिन्द्रासने स्थितम् कथं नु क्षत्रियः पार्थः शक्रासनमवाप्तवान्॥
en: Seeing Arjuna seated on the seat of Indra, he pondered as to how Partha had attained to the seat of Shakra, he being (but) a Kshatriya.

sn: किं त्वस्य सुकृतं कर्म के लोका वै विनिर्जिताः। स एवमनुसम्प्राप्तः स्थानं देवनमस्कृतम्॥
en: What act of merit had been performed by him and what regions had been conquered by him that he had obtained a seat which was worshipped by the celestials themselves?

sn: तस्य विज्ञाय संकल्पं शक्रो वृत्रनिषूदनः। लोमशं प्रहसन् वाक्यमिदमाह शचीपतिः॥
en: Having known his thoughts, the slayer of Vritra, Shakra, the husband of Sachi, smilingly spoke these words to Lomasha.

sn: ब्रह्मर्षे श्रूयतां यत् ते मनसैतद् विवक्षितम्। नायं केवलमर्यो वै मानुषत्वमुपागतः॥
en: Indra said: O Brahmarshi, hear all about what is now passing in your mind. This one (Arjuna) is not a mortal, though he has taken his birth among men.

sn: महर्षे मम पुत्रोऽयं कुन्त्यां जातो महाभुजः। अस्त्रहेतोरिह प्राप्तः कस्पाच्चित् कारणान्तरात्॥ अहो नैनं भवान् वेत्ति पुराणमृषिसत्तमम्। शृणु मे वदतो ब्रह्मन् योऽयं यच्चास्य कारणम्॥
en: O great Rishi, this mighty-armed hero is my son, born (in the womb) of Kunti. He has come here to obtain weapons. For what wonderful reason. Alas, you do not recognise him as the excellent Rishi of old! O Brahmana, listen to me, I shall tell you who he is and for what reason he has come here.

sn: नरनारायणौ यौ तौ पुराणावृषिसत्तमौ। ताविमावनुजानीहि हृषीकेशधनंजयौ॥
en: Know, those two excellent and ancient Rishis, known by the name of Nara and Narayana, are none else than Hrishikesha (Krishna) and Dhananjaya (Arjuna).

sn: विख्यातौ त्रिषु लोकेषु नरनारायणावृषी। कार्यार्थमवतीर्णौ तौ पृथ्वीं पुण्यप्रतिश्रयाम्॥
en: The Rishis Nara and Narayana are renowned all over the three worlds; they have descended (on earth) for the accomplishment of certain purpose on earth, which is the region for the acquisition of virtue.

sn: यन्न शक्यं सुरैर्द्रष्टुमृषिभिर्वा महात्मभिः। तदाश्रमपदं पुण्यं बदरीनाम विश्रुतम्॥ स निवासोऽभवद् विप्र विष्णोर्जिष्णोस्तथैव च। यत् प्रववृते गङ्गा सिद्धचारणसेविता॥
en: The sacred hermitage, which even the celestials and the high-souled Rishis adore, which is known by the name of Badarika, which is situate at the source of the Ganges and which is frequented by the Siddhas and the Charanas, O Brahmana, was the abode of Vishnu (Krishna) and Jishnu (Arjuna).

sn: तौ मन्नियोगाद् ब्रह्मर्षे क्षितौ जातौ महाद्युती। भूमे रावतरणं महावीरों करिष्यतः॥
en: O Brahmarshi, those two effulgent ones have at my request taken their birth on earth. Those two greatly powerful ones will remove the burden of the earth.

sn: उद्धृत्ता ह्यसुराः केचिन्निवातकवचा इति। विप्रियेषु स्थितास्माकं वरदानेन मोहिताः॥
en: Besides, there are certain Asuras, called Nivatkavachas who, being proud of the boon they have acquired, are (now) engaged in doing us injuries.

sn: तर्कयन्ते सुरान् हन्तुं बलदर्पसमन्विताः। देवान् न गणयन्त्येते तथा दत्तवरा हि ते॥
en: Proud of their great prowess, they are planning the destruction of the celestials, for having received the boon, they do not at all regard the celestials.

sn: पातालवासिनो रौद्रा दनोः पुत्रा महाबलाः। सर्वदेवनिकाया हि नालं योधयितुं हि तान्॥ योऽसौ भूमिगतः श्रीमान् विष्णुर्मधुनिषूदनः। कपिलो नाम देवोऽसौ भगवानजितो हरिः॥
en: Those fearful and greatly powerful sons of Dano live in the nether regions. Even all the celestials put together are in capable of fighting with them. The blessed Vishnu, the slayer of Madhu, he who was known on earth as Kapila,

sn: येन पूर्वं महात्मानः खनमाना रसातलम्। दर्शनादेव निहताः सगरस्यात्मजा विभो॥
en: O exalted one, who destroyed by his glance alone the high-souled sons of Sagara when they came roaring towards him, that illustrious and invincible.

sn: तेन कार्यं महत् कार्यमस्माकं द्विजसत्तम। पार्थेन च महायुद्धे समेताभ्यां न संशयः॥
en: O foremost of Brahmanas, Hari (Krishna) is capable alone or with Partha both together, of doing us a great good in a great battle. There is no doubt about it.

sn: सोऽसुरान् दर्शनादेव शक्तो हन्तुं सहानुगान्। निवातकवचान् सर्वान् नागानिव महाह्रदे॥
en: Like the snakes in a great lake he (Krishna) is capable of destroying at the very first sight all those Asuras, the Nivatkavachas, with all their followers.

sn: किं तु नाल्पेन कार्येण प्रबोध्यो मधुसूदनः। तेजसः सुमहाराशिः प्रबुद्धः प्रदहेज्जगत्॥
en: But the slayer of Madhu should not be requested to perform an insignificant task. He can consume the Universe by the great mass of his effulgence, if he minds to increase it.

sn: अयं तेषां समस्तानां शक्तः प्रतिसमासने। तान् निहत्य रणे शूरः पुनर्यास्यति मानुषान्॥
en: This one (Arjuna) also is quite competent to fight with them all. This hero, having destroyed them all in a battle, will again go back to the earth.

sn: भवानस्मन्नियोगेन यातु तावन्महीतलम्। काम्यके द्रक्ष्यसे वीरं निवसन्तं युधिष्ठिरम्॥
en: At my request go back to the earth. You will find the heroic Yudhishthira living in the Kamyaka (forest).

sn: स वाच्यो मम संदेशाद्धर्मात्मा सत्यसंगरः। नोत्कण्ठा फाल्गुने कार्या कृतास्त्रः शीघ्रमेष्यति॥
en: On my behalf tell that invincible and virtuous hero that he should not be anxious for Falguni. He will soon return acquiring all weapons.

sn: नाशुद्धबाहुवीर्येण नाकृतास्त्रेण वा रणे। भीष्मद्रोणादयो युद्धे शक्याः प्रतिसमासितुम्॥
en: For without the sacred prowess of arms and without the skill in weapons and in war, he will not be able to meet Bhishma, Drona and others in battle. Tell him.

sn: गृहीतास्त्रो गुडाकेशो महाबाहुर्महामनाः। नृत्यवादित्रगीतानां दिव्यानां पारमीयिवान्॥
en: That the high-minded and the mighty-armed Gudakesha Arjuna has acquired all weapons and has mastered the arts of celestials dancing and vocal and instrumental music.

sn: भवानपि विविक्तानि तीर्थानि मनुजेश्वर। भ्रातृभिः सहितः सर्वैर्द्रष्टुमर्हत्यरिंदम॥ तीर्थेष्वाप्लुत्य पुण्येषु विपाप्मा विगतज्वरः। राज्यं भोक्ष्यसि राजेन्द्र सुखी विगतकल्मष।॥
en: (You should also tell him) saying, “O foremost of men, O chastiser of foes, you too with all your brothers should see the various sacred shrines. O king of kings, having bathed in various sacred waters, you will be cleansed of your sins and the fever of your heart will abate. You will then be able to enjoy your kingdom in happiness."

sn: भवांश्चैनं द्विजश्रेष्ठ पर्यटन्तं महीतलम्। त्रातुमर्हति विप्राक्य तपोबलसमन्वितः।॥
en: O best of Brahmanas, O foremost of the twice-born, endued with the prowess of asceticism, you should protect him (Yudhishthira) in his wandering over the earth.

sn: गिरिदुर्गेषु च सदा देशेषु विषमेषु च। वसन्ति राक्षसा रौद्रास्तेभ्यो रक्षां विधास्यति॥
en: Fearful Rakshasas always live in mountain passes and in rugged steppes. Protect him from them.

sn: एवमुक्तो महेन्द्रेण बीभत्सुरपि लोमशम्। उवाच प्रयतो वाक्यं रक्षेथाः पाण्डुनन्दनम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having been thus addressed by Mahendra, Vibhatsu also spoke to Lomasha with all reverence, saying, “Protect the son of Pandu (Yudhishthira).

sn: यथा गुप्तस्त्वया राजा चरेत् तीर्थानि सत्तम। दानं दद्याद् यथा चैव तथा कुरु महामुने॥
en: O excellent man, O great Rishi, let the king, protected by you, visit the various sacred shrines and give away (much wealth) to the Brahmanas in charity."

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तथेति सम्प्रतिज्ञाय लोमशः सुमहातपाः। काम्यकं वनमुद्दिश्य समुपायान्महीतलम्॥
en: The greatly ascetic Lomasha, saying, “Be it So," went to the earth with the intention of going to the Kamyaka forest.

sn: ददर्श तत्र कौन्तेयंधर्मराजमरिदमम्। तापसै भ्रातभिश्चैव सर्वतः परिवारितम्॥
en: He saw there the son of Kunti, that chastiser of foes, Dharmaraja (Yudhishthira) surrounded by the ascetics and by his brothers.

sn: जनमेजय उवाच अत्यद्भुतमिदं कर्म पार्थस्यामितेजसः। धृतराष्ट्रो महाप्राज्ञः श्रुत्वा विप्र किमब्रवीत्॥
en: Janamejaya said : These acts of the immeasurably effulgent Partha (Arjuna) are (no doubt) wonderful. O Brahmana, what did greatly wise Dhritarashtra say on hearing (all this)?

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच शक्रलोकगतं पार्थं श्रुत्वा राजाम्बिकासुतः। द्वैपायनादृषिश्रेष्ठात् संजयं वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having heard from the foremost of Rishis, Krishna Dvaipayana, that Partha (Arjuna) had gone to the abode of Indra, the son of Ambika, the king Dhritarashtra, thus spoke to Sanjaya.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच श्रुतं मे सूत कात्स्न्र्येन कर्म पार्थस्यधीमतः। कच्चित् तवापि विदितं याथातथ्येन सारथे॥
en: Dhritarashtra said : O charioteer, O Suta, do you know in detail the acts of the wise Arjuna which I have heard from the beginning to end?

sn: प्रमत्तो ग्राम्यधर्मेषु मन्दात्मा पापनिश्चयः। मम पुत्रः सुदुर्बुद्धिः पृथिवीं घातयिष्यति॥
en: Mad in performing acts of the most vulgar kind, my wicked-minded and ever sinful son of wicked policies will destroy the earth.

sn: यस्य नित्यमृता वाचः स्वैरेष्वपि महात्मनः। त्रैलोक्यमपि तस्य स्याद् योद्धा यस्यधनंजयः॥
en: That high-souled one (Yudhishthira) whose words are ever true and who has Dhananjaya (Arjuna) to fight for him will certainly conquer the three worlds.

sn: अस्यतः कर्णिनाराचांसतीक्ष्णाग्रांश्च शिलाशितान्। कोऽर्जुनस्याग्रतस्तिष्ठेदपि मृत्युर्जरातिगः॥
en: Is there any one who is even beyond the influence of death and decrepitude, that will be able to stand before Arjuna when he will shower his barbed and sharp-pointed arrows sharpened on the stone?

sn: मम पुत्रा दुरात्मानः सर्वे मृत्युवशानुगाः। येषां युद्धं दुराधर्षेः पाण्डवैः प्रत्युपस्थितम्॥
en: My wicked-minded sons, who will have to fight with the invincible Pandavas are all under the influence of Death.

sn: तथैव च न पश्यामि युधि गाण्डीवधन्वनः। अनिशं चिन्तयानोऽपि य एनमुदियाद् रथी।॥
en: Reflecting day and night I do not see amongst us that warrior who will be able to stand in battle before the wielder of the Gandiva (Arjuna).

sn: द्रोणकर्णी प्रतीयातां यदि भीष्मोऽपि वा रणे। महान् स्यात् संशयो लोके तत्र पश्यामि नो जयम्।९॥
en: Even if Drona, Karna or Bhishma advance against him in battle, there will befall a great calamity over the world. But I do not see even there any chance of our Victory.

sn: घृणी कर्णः प्रमादी च आचार्यः स्थविरो गुरुः। अमर्षी बलवान् पार्थः संरम्भी दृढविक्रमः॥ सम्भवेत् तुमुलं युद्धं सर्वशोऽप्यपराजितम्। सर्वे शस्त्रविदः शूराः सर्वं प्राप्ता महद् यशः॥
en: Karna is kind and forgetful, the preceptor (Drona) is old and he is (also Arjuna's) tutor. But Arjuna is wrathful, strong, proud and greatly powerful. As all these heroes are invincible, all skilled in weapons and all illustrious, a fearful battle will take place between thein.

sn: अपि सर्वेश्वरत्वं हि ते वाञ्छन्त्यपराजिताः। वधे नूनं भवेच्छान्तिरेतेषां फाल्गुनस्य वा॥
en: They will not desire even the sovereignty of the whole world, if it is at all to be had by defeat; peace will be established only at the death of either of these (Bhishma etc.) or Falguni (Arjuna).

sn: न तु हन्तार्जुनस्यास्ति जेता वास्य न विद्यते। मन्युस्तस्य कथं शाम्येन्मन्दान् प्रति समुत्थितः॥
en: But he, who will be able to kill Arjuna, does not exist, nor even he who will defeat him. How shall that wrath of his which has myself for its object be appeased?

sn: त्रिदशेशसमो वीरः खाण्डवेऽग्निमतर्पयत्। जिगाय पार्थिवान् सर्वान् राजसूये महाक्रतौ॥
en: That hero, equal to the lord of the celestials gratified Agni at Khandava. He vanquished all the rulers of the earth at the time of the great Rajasuya sacrifice.

sn: शेषं कुर्याद् गिरेर्वज्रो निपतन् मूर्ध्नि संजय। न तु कुर्युः शराः शेषं क्षिप्तास्तात किरीटिना॥
en: O Sanjaya, O child, even the thunderbolt, that falls on the mountain peak, leaves a portion unburnt, but the arrows, shot by Kirti (Arjuna) do not leave anything behind.

sn: यथा हि किरणा भानोस्तपन्तीह चराचरम्। तथा पार्थभुजोत्सृष्टाः शरास्तप्यन्ति मत्सुतान्॥
en: As the rays of the sun scorch mobile and immobile universe, so will the arrows, shot by the arins of Partha, scorch all my sons.

sn: अपि तद्रथघोषेण भयार्ता सव्यसाचिनः। प्रतिभाति विदीर्णेव सर्वतो भारती चमूः॥
en: It seems to me that the Chamus (armies) of the Bharatas have already run away in all directions, being terrified at the clatter of Arjuna's chariot wheels.

sn: यदोद्वहन् प्रवपंश्चैव बाणान् स्थाताऽऽततायी समरे किरीटी। सृष्टोऽन्तकः सर्वहरो विधात्रा भवेद् यथा तद्वदपारणीयः॥
en: Vidhata (creator) has created Kirti (Arjuna) as our all-destroying, destroyer. He stands as a foe in the battle, scattering and vomiting swarms of arrows. Who is there that will defeat him?

sn: संजय उवाच यदेतत् कथितं राजंस्त्वया दुर्योधनं प्रति। सर्वमेतद् यथात्त्वं नैतन्मिथ्या महीपते।।शा
en: Sanjaya said : O king, what you have said as regards, Duryodhana is true. O ruler of earth, nothing what you have said is untrue.

sn: मन्युना हि समाविष्टाः पाण्डवास्ते महौजसः। दृष्ट्वा कृष्णां सभां नीतांधर्मपत्नी यशस्विनीम्॥ दुःशासनस्य ता वाचः श्रुत्वा ते दारुणोदयाः। कर्णस्य च महाराज जुगुप्सन्तीति मे मतिः॥
en: The immeasurably effulgent Pandavas were filled with wrath seeing their illustrious wedded wife, Krishna, brought into the Sabha. O great king, hearing the cruel words of Dushashana and Karna, they have become so angry that I believe they would not forgive.

sn: श्रुतं हि मे महाराज यथा पार्थेन संयुगे। एकादशतनुः स्थाणुर्धनुषा परितोषितः॥
en: O great king, I have heard how Arjuna has gratified in battle by means of his bow the god of gods, Sthanu of eleven forms.

sn: कैरातं वेषमास्थाय योधयामास फाल्गुनम्। जिज्ञासुः सर्वदेवेशः कपर्दी भगवान् स्वयम्॥
en: The exalted lord of all the gods, Kapardin (Shiva) himself, having assumed the disguise of a Kirata, fought with Falguni (Arjuna) to test his prowess.

sn: तत्रैनं लोकपालास्ते दर्शयामासुरर्जुनम्। अस्त्रहेतोः पराक्रान्तं तपसा कौरवर्षभम्॥
en: It was then that the Lokapalas appeared before that hero of undeterioating ascetic prowess in order to give away their weapons to that chief of the Kuru race.

sn: नैतदुत्सहते चान्यो लब्धुमन्यत्र फाल्गुनात्। साक्षाद् दर्शनमेतेषामीश्वराणां नरो भुवि।॥
en: What other man, on earth except Falguni canı ever attempt to get a sight of these gods in their own real forms?

sn: महेश्वरेण यो राजन् न जीर्णो ह्यष्टमूर्तिना। कस्तमुत्सहते वीरो युद्धे जरयितुं पुमान्॥
en: O king, who is there who will be able to weaken that hero who was not weakened by Maheswara (Shiva) himself with eight forms?

sn: आसादितमिदं घोरं तुमुलं लोमहर्षणम्। द्रौपदी परिकर्षद्भिः कोपयद्धिश्च पाण्डवान्॥
en: Having dragged Draupadi (into the Sabha) and thus provoked the Pandavas, your sons have brought upon themselves this terrible, fearful and hair-stirring calamity.

sn: यत् तु प्रस्फुरमाणौष्ठौ भीमः प्राह वचोऽर्थवत्। दृष्ट्वा दुर्योधनेनोरू द्रौपद्या दर्शितावुभौ॥
en: Seeing Duryodhana in the act of displaying his both thighs to Draupadi. Bhima, with quivering lips, spoke these words.

sn: ऊरू भेत्स्यामि ते पाप गदया भीमवेगया। त्रयोदशानां वर्षाणामन्ते दुर्दूतदेविनः॥
en: "O sinful wretch, as you are a great gambler, I will smash with the fearfully forcible maces, your these two thighs on the expiration of the thirteenth year."

sn: सर्वे प्रहरतां श्रेष्ठाः सर्वे चामिततेजसः। सर्वे सर्वास्त्रविद्वांस देवैरपि सुदुर्जयाः॥
en: All (the Pandavas) are the foremost of smiters, all immeasurably effulgent, all skilled in every weapon, all invincible even before the celestials.

sn: पन्ये मन्यु समुद्भूताः पुत्राणां तव संयुगे। अन्तं पार्थाः करिष्यन्ति भार्यामर्षसमन्विताः॥
en: I am sure, the sons of Pritha, angry as they are at the insult offered to their wedded wife, will kill all your sons in battle.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच किं कृतं सूत कर्णेन वदता परुषं वचः। पर्याप्तं वैरमेतावद् यत् कृष्णा सा सभां गता॥
en: Dhritarashtra said: O charioteer, what (great) mischief has been done by Karna by his uttering cruel words? Was it not enmity to the extreme by bringing Krishna (Draupadi) to the assembly-hall?

sn: अपीदानीं मम सुतास्तिष्ठेरन् मन्दचेतसः। येषां भ्राता गुरुज्येष्ठो विनये नावतिष्ठते॥
en: How can my wicked minded sons live when their eldest brother and superior does not walk in the path of righteousness?

sn: ममापि वचनं सूत न शुश्रूषति मन्दभाक्। दृष्ट्वा मां चक्षुषा हीनं निर्विचेष्टमचेतसम्॥
en: O Suta, seeing me blind and incapable of taking any active steps, my wicked son considers me a fool and does not listen to what I say. are

sn: ये चास्य सचिवा मन्दाः कर्णसौबलकादयः। ते तस्य भूयसो दोषान् वर्धयन्ति विचेतसः॥
en: Those wretches also, who his counsellors, namely, Karna, the son of Subala (Shakuni) and others, always encourage him in his course of vice; he is incapable of understanding things.

sn: स्वैरमुक्ता ह्यपि शरा: पार्थेनामिततेजसा। निर्दहेयुर्मम सुतान् किं पुनर्मन्युनेरिताः॥
en: The arrows, that the immeasurably powerful Arjuna shoots in playfulness are able to consume all my sons, what to speak of his those arrows which are shot by him in anger!

sn: पार्थबाहुबलोत्सृष्टा महाचापविनिःसृताः। दिव्यास्त्रमन्त्रमुदिताः सादयेयुः सुरानपि॥
en: The arrows, pulled by the strength of Arjuna's arms and shot from his bows and also inspired with mantras which convert them to celestials weapons, can chastise even the celestials.

sn: यस्य मन्त्री च गोप्ता च सुहच्चैव जनार्दनः। हरिस्त्रैलोक्यनाथः स किं नु तस्य न निर्जितम्॥
en: What is there which is unconquerable by him who has for his protector, counsellor and friend, the Lord of the three worlds, Hari, Janardana (Krishna).

sn: इदं हि सुमहच्चित्रमर्जुनस्येह संजय। महादेवेन बाहुभ्यां यत् समेत इति श्रुति॥ प्रत्यक्षं सर्वलोकस्य खाण्डवे यत् कृतं पुरा। फाल्गुनेन सहायार्थे वह्नर्दामोदरेण च॥
en: O Sanjaya, this is most wonderful in Arjuna as we have heard that he clasped Mahadeva (Shiva) with his arms. That act also which Falguni (Arjuna) did of old aided by Damodara (Krishna) in order to help Agni to consume the Khandava (forest) was witnessed by all the world.

sn: सर्वथा न हि मे पुत्राः सहामात्याः ससौबलाः। क्रुद्ध पार्थे च भीमे च वासुदेवे च सात्वते॥
en: When these Bhima, Partha (Arjuna) and Vasudeva (Krishna) of the Satvata race are angry, my sons with their friends and the son of Subala are surely not at all capable to fight with them.

description: The description of the food of the Pandavas
sn: जनमेजय उवाच यदिदं शोचितं राज्ञाधृतराष्ट्रेण वै मुरे। प्रव्राज्य पाण्डवान् वीरान् सर्वमेतन्निरर्थकम्॥
en: Janamejaya said : O (Muni), king Dhritarashtra must uselessly have lamented after having sent the heroic sons of Pandu into exile.

description: The description of the food of the Pandavas
sn: कथं च राजा पुत्रं तमुपेक्षेताल्पचेतसम्। दुर्योधनं पाण्डुपुत्रान् कोपयानं महारथान्॥
en: Why did the king thus permit his narrowminded son Duryodhana to excite the anger of those mighty warriors, the sons of Pandu?

description: The description of the food of the Pandavas
sn: किमासीत् पाण्डुपुत्राणां वने भोजनमुच्यताम्। वानेयमथवा कृष्टमेतदाख्यातु नो भवान्॥
en: What was the food of the sons of Pandu while they lived in the woods? You explain to me-was it obtained from the woods or was it the product of cultivation?

description: The description of the food of the Pandavas
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच वानेयांश्च मृगांश्चैव शुद्धैर्बाणैर्निपातितान्। ब्राह्मणानां निवेद्याचमभुञ्जन् पुरुषर्षभाः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : The best of men ate the produce of the wilderness and the (meat of) deer killed with pure arrows, which they first dedicated to the Brahmanas.

description: The description of the food of the Pandavas
sn: तांस्तु शूरान् महेष्वासांस्तदा निवसतो वने। अन्वयुाह्मणा राजन् साग्नयोऽनग्नयस्तथा॥
en: O king, both classes of Brahmanas (those worshipping with fire and those worshipping without it) followed these heroes wielding large bows while they lived in the wilderness.

description: The description of the food of the Pandavas
sn: ब्राह्मणानां सहस्राणि स्रातकानां महात्मनाम्। दश मोक्षविदां तत्र यान् बिभर्ति युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: There were ten thousand most illustrious Snataka Brahmanas, who had perfect knowledge in the matter and means of salvation and whom Yudhishthira fed in the woods.

description: The description of the food of the Pandavas
sn: रुरून् कृष्णमृगांश्चैव मेध्यांश्चान्यान् वनेचरान्। बाणैरुन्मथ्य विविधैर्ब्राह्मणेभ्यो न्यवेदयत्॥
en: He dedicated the black and other kinds of deer and clean animals of the forest to those Brahmanas, after having killed them with his arrows.

description: The description of the food of the Pandavas
sn: न तत्र कश्चिद् दुर्वर्णो व्याधितो वापि दृश्यते। कृशो वा दुर्बलो वापि दीनो भीतोऽपि वा पुनः॥
en: None of those who lived with Yudhishthira in the woods looked either pale or diseased, lean or weak and timid or terrified.

description: The description of the food of the Pandavas
sn: पुत्रानिव प्रियान् भ्रातृज्ञातीनिव सहोदरान्। पुपोष कौरवश्रेष्ठोधर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: The best of the Kurus, the most virtuous Yudhishthira, supported his dear brothers as if they were his sons; and maintained his relatives, as if they were his own brothers.

description: The description of the food of the Pandavas
sn: पतींश्च द्रौपदी सर्वान् द्विजातींश्च यशस्विनी। मातृवद् भोजयित्वाचे शिष्टमाहारयत् तदा॥
en: The famous Draupadi first supplied her husband and the Brahmanas with food like their mother and at last she took her food herself.

description: The description of the food of the Pandavas
sn: प्राची राजा दक्षिणां भीमसेनो यमौ प्रतीचीमथ वाप्युदीचीम्। धनुर्धराणां सहितो मृगाणां क्षयं चक्रुर्नित्यमेवोपगम्य॥
en: The king going towards the east and Bhima towards the south and the twins towards the west or the north, put an end to the race of the deer in the forest (by daily killing them with their bows) for the sake of meat.

description: The description of the food of the Pandavas
sn: तथा तेषां वसतां काम्यके वै विहीनानामर्जुनेनोत्सुकानाम्। रधीयतां जपतां जुह्वतां च॥
en: Thus the Pandavas lived in the forest of Kamyaka for five years; but all the while they remained very anxious on account of the absence of Arjuna and were always busy with study, prayers and sacrifices.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तेषां तच्चरितं श्रुत्वा मनुष्यातीतमद्भुतम्। चिन्ताशोकपरीतात्मा मन्युनाभिपरिप्लुतः॥ दीर्घमुष्णं च निःश्वस्यधृतराष्ट्रोऽम्बिकासुतः। अब्रवीत् संजयं सूतमामन्त्र्य पुरुषर्षभ॥
en: Vaishampayana said : The foremost of men, Dhritarashtra, the son of Ambika, having heard this most extraordinary and wonderful account (the mode of life of the Pandava king in the Kamyaka forest) became filled with grief and anxiety; and overwhelmed with melancholy and breathing hot and long he addressing his charioteer Sanjaya said,

sn: न रात्रौ न दिवा सूत शान्ति प्राप्नोमि वै क्षणम्। संचिन्त्य दुर्नयं घोरमतीतं द्यूतजं हि तत्॥
en: “O charioteer, I do not enjoy a moment's rest either during the day or in the night, thinking of the terrible misconduct of my sons resulting from their past gambling;

sn: तेषामसह्यवीर्याणां शौर्यधैर्यधृति पराम्। अन्योन्यमनुरागं च भ्रातृणामतिमानुषम्॥
en: And thinking of the heroism, patience superior fortitude and the extraordinary mutual love of those brothers of unbearable prowess.

sn: देवपुत्रौ महाभागौ देवराजसमद्युती। नकुलः सहदेवश्च पाण्डवौ युद्धदुर्मदौ॥ दृढायुधौ दूरपातौ युद्धे च कृतनिश्चयौ। शीघ्रहस्तौ दृढक्रोधौ नित्ययुक्तौ तरस्विनौ॥ भीमार्जुनौ पुरोधाय यदा तौ रणमूर्धनि। स्थास्येते सिंहविक्रान्तावश्विनाविव दुःसहौ॥ न शेषमिह पश्यामि मम सैन्यस्य संजय। तौ ह्यप्रतिरथौ युद्धे देवपुत्रौ महारथौ॥
en: When the two Pandavas, Nakula and Sahadeva who are of divine origin, most exalted, equal to the king of the gods in splendour, invincible in battle, steady in management of weapons, able to shoot at a great distance indefatigable in battle, lighthanded, of inextinguishable wrath, persevering, of untiring activity, mighty as the lions, unbearable as the Ashvins themselves will come to the field of battle placing Bhima and Arjuna in the front, then I see, O Sanjaya, that my soldiers will be slain to a mass; and those mighty and matchless warriors of divine origin will not show mercy.

sn: द्रौपद्यास्तं परिक्लेशं न ऑस्यते त्वमर्षिणौ। वृष्णयोऽथ महेष्वासाः पञ्चाला वा महौजसः॥ युधि सत्याभिसंधेन वासुदेवेन रक्षिताः। प्रधक्ष्यन्ति रणे पार्थाः पुत्राणां मम वाहिनीम्॥
en: As they are very angry at the insult upon Draupadi. And the most powerful warriors of the Vrishni race and the Panchalas of great strength and the sons of Pritha themselves guarded by Vasudeva of indomitable strength, will defeat my son's legions.

sn: रामकृष्णप्रणीतानां वृष्णीनां सूतनन्दन। न शक्यः सहितुं वेगः सर्वैस्तैरपि संयुगे॥
en: O son of charioteer, my assembled forces are incapable of standing the push as given by the Vrishnis, when commanded by Rama and Krishna.

sn: तेषां मध्ये महेष्वासो भीमो भीमपराक्रमः। शैक्यया वीरघातिन्या गदया विचरिष्यति॥ तथा गाण्डीवनिर्घोषं विस्फूर्जितमिवाशनेः। गदावेगं च भीमस्य नालं सोढुं नराधिपाः॥
en: The mighty-warrior Bhima of terrible prowess, armed with his uplifted mace, capable of crushing every hero, will rove about in their midst. The kings on my side will not be able to stand against the twang of Gandiva, as loud as the thunder of heaven and the push of the mace of Bhima.

sn: ततोऽहं सुहृदां वाचो दुर्योधनवशानुगः। स्मरणीयाः स्मरिष्यामि मया या न कृताः पुरा॥
en: It is then that I, ever obedient to the counsels of Duryodhana, shall call to my memory the advices of my friends, which, I should have listened to beforehand.

sn: संजय उवाच व्यतिक्रमोऽयं सुमहांस्त्वया राजन्नुपेक्षितः। समर्थेनापि यन्मोहात् पुत्रस्ते न निवारितः॥
en: Sanjaya said : O king, you did not care for this, your great fault was that though capable you did not prevent out of affection your son from doing what he had done.

sn: श्रुत्वा हि निर्जितान् द्यूते पाण्डवान् मधुसूदनः। त्वरितः काम्यके पार्थान् समभावयदच्युतः॥
en: Having heard the defeat at dice of the Pandavas, the slayer of Madhu, that hero of imperishable fame, went at once to the forest of Kamyaka.

sn: द्रुपदस्य तथा पुत्राधृष्टद्युम्नपुरोगमाः। विराटोधृष्टकेतुश्च केकयाश्च महारथाः॥
en: So also Dhristadyumna at the head of the sons of Drupada and Virata and Dhristaketu and those mighty warriors, the Kaikeyas.

sn: तैश्च यत् कथितं राजन् दृष्ट्वा पार्थान् पराजितान् चारेण विदितं सर्वं तन्मयाऽऽवेदितं च ते॥
en: O king, I have learnt through the spies whatever they talked of after they had seen the sons of Pandu defeated at dice.

sn: समागम्य वृतस्तत्र पाण्डवैर्मधुसूदनः। सारथ्ये फाल्गुनस्याजौ तथेत्याह च तान् हरिः॥
en: Having advanced towards the slayer of Madhu, the Pandavas appointed him to the charioteership of Falguni in battle; and Hari in response to their request said-"So be it."

sn: अमर्षितो हि कृष्णोऽपि दृष्ट्वा पार्थांस्तथा गतान्। कृष्णाजिनोत्तरासंगानब्रवीच्च युधिष्ठिरम्॥
en: And Krishna, beholding the sons of Pritha, gone to the woods and dressed in the skins of black deer, became greatly annoyed and addressing Yudhishthira, said,

sn: या सा समृद्धिः पार्थानामिन्द्रप्रस्थे बभूव ह। राजसूये मया दृष्टा नृपैरन्यैः सुदुर्लभा॥
en: “I beheld the prosperity of the sons of Pritha at Indraprastha, on the occasion of the Rajasuya sacrifice, which could not even painfully be obtained by other kings.

sn: यत्र सर्वान् महीपालाञ्छस्त्रतेजोभयातिान्। सवङ्गाङ्गान् सपौण्ड्रोड्रान् सचोलद्रवाडिा-ध्रकान्॥ सागरानूपकांश्चैव ये च प्रान्ताभिवासिनः। सिंहलान् बर्बरान् म्लेच्छान् ये च लङ्कानिवासिनः।। पश्चिमानि च राष्ट्राणि शतशः सागरान्तिकान्। पह्नवान् दरदान् सर्वान् किरातान् यवनाञ्छकान्॥ हारहूणांश्च चीनांश्च तुषारान् सैन्धवांस्तथा। जागुडान् रामठान् मुण्डान् स्त्रीराज्यमथ तङ्गणान्॥ केकयान् मालवांश्चैव तथा काश्मीरकानपि। अद्राक्षमहमाहूतान् यज्ञे ते परिवेषकान्॥
en: At the Rajasuya I saw also all the kings those of the Bangas and Angas, Paundras and Odras, Cholas and Dravidas and Andhakas; and the rulers of several islands and the countries on the sea-coast and the kings of the frontier dominions i.e. the chiefs of the Sinhalas, the barbarians Mlechchhas, the aboriginal tribes of Lanka and hundreds of the kings of the west and the chiefs of the sea-coast principalities and all those of the Pahlavas and the Daradas. The various tribes of the Kiratas, the Yavanas, the Cakras, the Harahunas, the Chinas, the Thukharas, the Sindavas, the Jugudas, the Ramathas and the Mundas; and the natives of the kingdom of women, the Tanganas, the Kaikeyas, the Malavas and the inhabitants of Kashmira, who were greatly afflicted with the terror of your weapons, strength and who, having been present as you had invited them, performed various offices.

sn: सा ते समृद्धिरात्ता चपला प्रतिसारिणी। आदाय जीवितं तेषामहरिष्यामि तामहम्॥
en: That prosperity, so very ephemeral was taken away by your enemies and now rests upon them, which I shall recover from them for you by depriving them of their very life.

sn: रामेण सह कौरव्य भीमार्जुनयमैस्तथा। अक्रूरगदसाम्बैश्च प्रद्युम्नेनाहुकेन च।॥ धृष्टद्युम्नेन वीरेण शिशुपालात्मजेन च। दुर्योधनं रणे हत्वा सद्यः कर्णं च भारत॥ दुःशासनं सौबलेयं यश्चान्यः प्रतियोत्स्यते। ततस्त्वं हास्तिनपुरे भ्रातृभिः सहितो वसन्।॥ धार्तराष्ट्रीं श्रियं प्राप्य प्रशाधि पृथिवीमिमाम्।
en: O chief of the Kurus, I shall, with the help of Rama, Bhima and Arjuna and the twins and of Akrura, Gada and Samba and Pradyumna and Ahuka and also with the assistance of the heroic Dhristadyumna and the of Shishupala, kill Duryodhana and Karna in a day and so also Dushasana, Subala's son and all others who will stand against us in battle. And thereafter you shall, O Bharata, live in Hastinapur with your brothers and having in possession the prosperity that is now being enjoyed by the sons of Dhritarashtra, govern this earth."

sn: अथैनमब्रवीद् राजा तस्मिन् वीरसमागमे॥ शृण्वत्स्वेतेषु वीरेषुधृष्टद्युम्नमुखेषु च।
en: Thereupon the king (Yudhishthira) spoke unto Krishna in the hearing of those heroes at the head of whom was Dhristadyumna whilst they were listening to him.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच प्रतिगृहणामि ते वाचमिमां सत्यां जनार्दन॥
en: Yudhishthira said : O Janardana, I accept these words of your to be true. son

sn: अमित्रान् मे महाबाहो सानुबन्धान् हनिष्यसि। वर्षात् त्रयोदशादूर्ध्वं सत्यं मां कुरु केशव॥ प्रतिज्ञातो वने वासो राजमध्ये मया ह्ययम्।
en: O mighty-armed one, slay my enemies with their followers subsequent to the expiration of the thirteen years. O Keshava, swear this to me. I really promised in the assembly of the kings to live in the woods as I am now doing.

sn: तद्धर्मराजवचनं प्रतिश्रुत्य सभासदः॥ धृष्टद्युम्नपुरोगास्ते शमयामासुरञ्जसा। केशवं मधुरैर्वाक्यैः कालयुक्तैरमर्षितम्॥
en: Sanjay Said: Hearing these words of the most righteous, Yudhishthira his courtiers headed by Dhristadyumna instantly pacified the indignant Keshava with sweet words most suitable to the occasion.

sn: पाञ्चालीं प्राहुरक्लिष्टां वासुदेवस्य शृण्वतः। दुर्योधनस्तव क्रोधाद् देवि त्यक्ष्यति जीवितम्॥
en: They, (the courtiers) in the hearing of Vasudeva, said to the daughter of Panchala (Draupadi), “O lady, Duryodhana shall certainly give up his life on account of your wrath.

sn: प्रतिजानीमहे सत्यं मा शुचो वरवर्णिनी। ये स्म तेऽक्षजितां कृष्णे दृष्ट्वा त्वां प्राहसंस्तदा मांसानि तेषां खादन्तो हरिष्यन्ति वृकद्विजाः॥
en: O fair-complexioned one, we make this promise unto you and therefore grieve no more. O Krishna, the flesh of those that laughed on beholding the victory at dice will be devoured by the wolves and birds.

sn: पास्यन्ति रुधिरं तेषां गृध्रा गोमायवस्तथा। उत्तमाङ्गानि कर्षन्तो यैः कृष्टासि सभातले॥ तेषां द्रक्ष्यसि पाञ्चाली गात्राणि पृथिवीतले। क्रव्यादैः कृष्यमाणानि भक्ष्यमाणानि चासकृत्॥
en: They themselves will be mocked; and their blood will be drunk by the jackals and vultures. ( daughter of Panchala, you shall see the bodies of those that dragged you by the hair at once dragged and devoured by the carnivorous animals.

sn: परिक्लिष्टासि यैस्तत्र यैश्चासि समुपेक्षिता। तेषामुत्कृत्तशिरसां भूमिः पास्यति शोणितम्॥
en: Krishna, the blood, of those with severed heads, by whom you were much aggrieved and neglected, will be drunk by the earth.”

sn: एवं बहुविधा वाचस्त ऊचुर्भरतर्षभ। सर्वे तेजस्विनः शूराः सर्वे चाहतलक्षणाः॥ तेधर्मराजेन वृता वर्षादूर्ध्वं त्रयोदशात्। पुरस्कृत्योपयास्यन्ति वासुदेवं महारथाः॥
en: The foremost ones of the Bharata race uttered these and various other speeches (in order to console Draupadi). Yudhishthira made this request to those brave heroes who were all impressed with the marks of battle, that they should after the expiration of the thirteenth year (of life in the forest), come to the field (of battle) keeping Vasudeva at their head.

sn: रामश्च कृष्णश्चधनंजयश्च प्रद्युम्नसाम्बौ युयुधानभीमौ। माद्रीसुतौ केकयराजपुत्राः पाञ्चालपुत्राः सह मत्स्यराज्ञा॥ एतान् सर्वान् लोकवीरानजेयान् महात्मनः सानुबन्धान ससैन्यान्। को जीवितार्थी समरेऽभ्युदीयात् क्रुद्धान् सिंहान् केसरिणो यथैव॥
en: Who is there that, desiring to have his existence in earth, will appear in the field of battle and encounter these most illustrious and invincible heroes (like the furious lions with erect manes) viz. Rama and Krishna and Dhananjaya, Pradyumna and Samba and Yuyudhana and Bhima and the sons of Madri and the Kaikeya and Panchala princes, attended by the king of Matsya, who will come to the battle with all their troops and attendants.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच यन्माब्रवीद विदुरो द्यूतकाले त्वं पाण्डवाञ्जेष्यसि चेन्नरेन्द्र। ध्रुवं कुरूणामयमन्तकालो महाभयो भविता शोणितौघः॥
en: Dhritarashtra said: Vidura in the occasion of the past gambling told me this “O king, you shall surely defeat the Pandavas at dice; but certainly there will ensue a terrible bloodshed, resulting in the total destruction of the Kurus."

sn: मन्ये तथा तद् भवितेति सूत यथा क्षत्ता प्राह वचः पुरा माम्। असंशयं भविता युद्धमेतद् गते काले पाण्डवानां यथोक्तम्॥
en: O charioteer, I think it is now almost certain what Vidura had told me of old, that undoubtedly you would happen, a most fearful battle with the Pandavas just after the expire of the said period of thirteen years.

description: NALOPAKHYANA PARVA The colloquy between Brihadashva and Yudhishthira
sn: जनमेजय उवाच अस्त्रहेतोर्गते पार्थे शक्रलोकं महात्मनि। युधिष्ठिरप्रभृतयः किमकुर्वत पाण्डवाः॥
en: Janamejaya said : When the illustrious son of Pritha (Arjuna) had gone to the region of Indra with a view of obtain the arms, what did Yudhishthira and the other Pandavas do?

description: NALOPAKHYANA PARVA The colloquy between Brihadashva and Yudhishthira
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच अस्त्रहेतोर्गते पार्थे शक्रलोकं महात्मनि। आवसन् कृष्णया साधु काम्यके भरतर्षभाः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : When the illustrious son of Pritha had gone to the region of Indra for obtaining the arms then those foremost ones of the Bharata race lived with Krishna (Draupadi) in the forest of Kamyaka.

description: NALOPAKHYANA PARVA The colloquy between Brihadashva and Yudhishthira
sn: ततः कदाचिदेकान्ते विविक्त इव शाद्वले। दुःखार्ता भरतश्रेष्ठा निषेदुः सह कृष्णया॥ धनंजयं शोचमानाः साश्रुकण्ठाः सुदुःखिताः। तद्वियोगार्दितान् सर्वाञ्छोकः समभिपुप्लुवे॥
en: Thereupon those excellent ones of the seated one day with Krishna on a clean and solitary turf (in the forest). They were greatly afflicted with grief; their voices were choked up with the tears and also they were overwhelmed with sorrow on account of the absence of Dhananjaya. A flood of grief passed over them, tormented as they were by his separation.

description: NALOPAKHYANA PARVA The colloquy between Brihadashva and Yudhishthira
sn: धनंजयवियोगाच्च राज्यभ्रंशाच्च दुःखिताः। अथ भीमो महाबाहुर्युधिष्ठिरमभाषत॥
en: Thereupon the heroic Bhima, afflicted with sorrow for the separation of Dhananjaya and the loss of kingdom, addressed Yudhishthira in the following terms.

description: NALOPAKHYANA PARVA The colloquy between Brihadashva and Yudhishthira
sn: निदेशात् ते महाराज गतोऽसौ भरतर्षभः। अर्जुनः पाण्डुपुत्राणां यस्मिन् प्राणाः प्रतिष्ठिताः॥
en: "O great king, this chief of the Bharata race Arjuna, has gone away in obedience to your command. On him depend the very lives of the sons of Pandu.

description: NALOPAKHYANA PARVA The colloquy between Brihadashva and Yudhishthira
sn: यस्मिन् विनष्टे पाञ्चालाः सह पुत्रैस्तथा वयम्। सात्यकिर्वासुदेवश्च विनश्येयुर्न संशयः॥
en: Losing Arjuna, we with all our sons, the Panchalas, as also the Satyaki and Vasudeva, are sure to die.

description: NALOPAKHYANA PARVA The colloquy between Brihadashva and Yudhishthira
sn: योऽसौ गच्छतिधर्मात्मा बहून् क्लेशान् विचिन्तयन् भवन्नियोगाद् बीभत्सुस्ततो दुःखतरं नु किम्॥
en: For what can we grieve more than this, that the righteous Vibhatsu goes away at your behest, thinking upon the various sorrows?

description: NALOPAKHYANA PARVA The colloquy between Brihadashva and Yudhishthira
sn: यस्य बाहू समाश्रित्य वयं सर्वे महात्मनः। मन्यामहे जिताना तौ परान् प्राप्ता च मेदिनीम्॥
en: Relying upon the strength of arms of that illustrious hero, we can take for granted that our enemies are already vanquished and the possession of the earth is ours,

description: NALOPAKHYANA PARVA The colloquy between Brihadashva and Yudhishthira
sn: यस्य प्रभावान्न मया सभामध्येधनुष्मतः। नीता लोसममुं सर्वेधार्तराष्ट्राः ससौबलाः॥
en: But for the intervention of that mightyarmed hero in the meeting of warriors, I could not send the descendants of Dhritarashtra with

description: NALOPAKHYANA PARVA The colloquy between Brihadashva and Yudhishthira
sn: ते वयं बाहुबलिनः क्रोधमुत्थितमात्मनः। सहामहे भवन्मूलं वासुदेवेन पालिताः॥
en: We are supported by Vasudeva and are the mightiest warriors. We were constrained to suppress the wrath that had been awakened in ourselves, because you are the cause of that anger.

description: NALOPAKHYANA PARVA The colloquy between Brihadashva and Yudhishthira
sn: वयं हि सह कृष्णेन हत्वा कर्णमुखान् परान्। स्वबाहुविजितां कृत्स्ना प्रशासेम वसुन्धराम्॥
en: As a matter of fact, assisted by Krishna, having slain all our foes with Karna at their head, we are in a position to rule the whole rld, conquered by the might of our own arms.

description: NALOPAKHYANA PARVA The colloquy between Brihadashva and Yudhishthira
sn: भवतो द्यूतदोषेण सर्वे वयमुपप्लुताः। अहीनपौरुषा बाला बलिभिर्बलवत्तराः॥
en: Although we are not devoid of manliness yet we are the most unfortunate and that is for the reason of your gambling vice. Meanwhile the foolish sons of Dhritarashtra are growing very strong with the tributes (collected from the dependant chiefs).

description: NALOPAKHYANA PARVA The colloquy between Brihadashva and Yudhishthira
sn: क्षात्रधर्म महाराज त्वमवेक्षितुमर्हसि। न हिधर्मो महाराज क्षत्रियस्य वनाश्रयः॥
en: O great king, it is necessary for you to keep in view the duties of a Kshatriya. O great king, to live in the forest should not be his duty.

description: NALOPAKHYANA PARVA The colloquy between Brihadashva and Yudhishthira
sn: राज्यमेव परंधर्मं क्षत्रियस्य विदुर्बुधाः। स क्षत्रधर्मविद् राजा माधर्म्यान्नीनशः पथः॥
en: The sages have said that the duty of a Kshatriya is to rule the kingdom. O king, you, are versed in the Kshatriya moralities, should not go astray from the path of your duty, the most righteous as you are.

description: NALOPAKHYANA PARVA The colloquy between Brihadashva and Yudhishthira
sn: प्राग् द्वादशसमा राजन्धार्तराष्ट्रान् निहन्महि। निवर्त्य च वनात् पार्थमानाय्य च जनार्दनम्॥
en: Calling back Partha and Janardana, let us, O king, go away from the forest and slay the descendants of Dhritarashtra even before the expiry of pledged period of twelve years.

description: NALOPAKHYANA PARVA The colloquy between Brihadashva and Yudhishthira
sn: व्यूढानीकान् महाराज जवनेव महामते। धार्तराष्ट्रानमुं लोकं गमयामि विशाम्पते।॥ सर्वानहं हनिष्यामिधार्तराष्ट्रान् ससौबलान्। दुर्योधनं च कर्णं च यो वान्यः प्रतियोत्स्यते॥
en: O great monarch, O high-souled one, O king of kings, I shall send the sons of Dhritarashtra to the other world (even if they are encircled by their soldiers in battle-array) by the very push of our arms. I shall slay all the sons of Dhritarashtra accompanied by the Subalas, Duryodhana and Karna and others who will encounter me (or us) in battle.

description: NALOPAKHYANA PARVA The colloquy between Brihadashva and Yudhishthira
sn: मया प्रशमिते पश्चात् त्वमेष्यसि वनात् पुनः। एवं कृते न ते दोषा भविष्यन्ति विशाम्पते॥
en: The enemies thus being slain by me, you may come back to the forest again, O king of kings, there will be no fault of yours if thus acted.

description: NALOPAKHYANA PARVA The colloquy between Brihadashva and Yudhishthira
sn: यज्ञैश्च विविधैस्तात कृतं पापमरिंदम। अवधूय महाराज गच्छेम स्वर्गमुत्तमम्॥
en: O sir, O chastiser of foes, if thus a sin be committed, we are able to wash it off by the performance of various sacrifices and we may ascend a superior heaven.

description: NALOPAKHYANA PARVA The colloquy between Brihadashva and Yudhishthira
sn: एवमेतद् भवेद् राजन् यदि राजा न बालिशः। अस्माकं दीर्घसूत्रः स्याद् भवान्धर्मपरायणः॥
en: O monarch, such may happen, if our king be not foolish or procrastinating. Indeed you are, O king, righteous.

description: NALOPAKHYANA PARVA The colloquy between Brihadashva and Yudhishthira
sn: निकृत्या निकृतिप्रज्ञा हन्तव्या इति निश्चयः। न हि नैकृतिकं हत्वा निकृत्या पापमुच्यते॥
en: Undoubtedly the deceitful persons should be done away with deceitful means. Surely it is no sin. to destroy them by frauds.

description: NALOPAKHYANA PARVA The colloquy between Brihadashva and Yudhishthira
sn: तथा भारतधर्मेषुधर्मज्ञैरिह दृश्यते। अहोरात्रं महाराज तुल्यं संवत्सरेण ह॥
en: O Bharata, O great prince, the pious, who are conversant in morality, have regarded a day and a night as equivalent to an entire year.

description: NALOPAKHYANA PARVA The colloquy between Brihadashva and Yudhishthira
sn: तथैव वेदवचनं श्रूयते नित्यदा विभो। संवत्सरो महाराज पूर्णो भवति कृच्छ्रतः॥
en: O illustrious one, the Veda text is often heard to signify that a year, O great monarch, passes away like a day, if one is engaged in strict devotion.

description: NALOPAKHYANA PARVA The colloquy between Brihadashva and Yudhishthira
sn: यदि वेदाः प्रमाणास्ते दिवसादूर्ध्वमच्युत। त्रयोदश समाः कालो ज्ञायतां परिनिष्ठितः॥
en: Therefore regard, O one of unfading glory, accepting the authority of the Vedas, the period of thirteen years equal to a day or so.

description: NALOPAKHYANA PARVA The colloquy between Brihadashva and Yudhishthira
sn: कालो दुर्योधनं हन्तुं सानुबन्धमरिंदम। एकाचां पृथिवीं सर्वां पुरा राजन् करोति सः॥
en: O chastiser of foes, this is the (proper) time to kill Duryodhana with all his attendants. Otherwise, O prince, he will bring the whole world under his subjection.

description: NALOPAKHYANA PARVA The colloquy between Brihadashva and Yudhishthira
sn: द्यूतप्रियेण राजेन्द्र तथा तद् भवता कृतम्। प्रायेणाज्ञातचर्यायां वयं सर्वे निपातिताः॥
en: O most excellent of princes, this has been the out-come of your love for gambling. We are almost ruined by your promise to live one year undiscovered.

description: NALOPAKHYANA PARVA The colloquy between Brihadashva and Yudhishthira
sn: न तं देशं प्रपश्यामि यत्र सोऽस्मान् सुदुर्जनः। न विज्ञास्यति दुष्टात्मा चारैरिति सुयोधनः॥
en: I do not find a country where, if we live, that wicked and evil-natured Suyodhana will not be able to discover us by his spies.

description: NALOPAKHYANA PARVA The colloquy between Brihadashva and Yudhishthira
sn: अधिगम्य च सर्वान् नो वनवासमिमं ततः। प्रव्राजयिष्यति पुनर्निकृत्याधमपूरुषः॥
en: And having thus traced us, that stupid one will again deceitfully banish us (to live in exile) into the woods.

description: NALOPAKHYANA PARVA The colloquy between Brihadashva and Yudhishthira
sn: यद्यस्मानभिगच्छेत पापः स हि कथंचन। अज्ञातचर्यामुत्तीर्णान् दृष्ट्वा च पुनराह्वयेत्॥
en: If that sinful wretch beholds us to return from the woods after the expiration of that period of our undiscovered life, he will again invite us to game at dice.

description: NALOPAKHYANA PARVA The colloquy between Brihadashva and Yudhishthira
sn: द्यूतेन ते महाराज पुन तमवर्तत। भवांश्च पुनराहतो द्यूते नैवापनेष्यति॥
en: O great prince, the game of chance will once more begin. And then being again summoned at dice, we are sure to be banished.

description: NALOPAKHYANA PARVA The colloquy between Brihadashva and Yudhishthira
sn: स तथाक्षेषु कुशलो निश्चितो गतचेतनः। चरिष्यसि महाराज वनेषु वसतीः पुनः॥
en: He (the king) is unskilled at dice and beyond doubt he looses his senses when at dice. Therefore, O great monarch, you shall have again to live in the woods.

description: NALOPAKHYANA PARVA The colloquy between Brihadashva and Yudhishthira
sn: यद्यस्मान् सुमहाराज कृपणान् कर्तुमर्हसि। यावज्जीवमवेक्षस्व वेदधर्मांश्च कृत्स्नशः॥ निकृत्या निकृतिप्रज्ञो हन्तव्य इति निश्चयः। अनुज्ञातस्त्वया गत्वा यावच्छक्ति सुयोधनम्॥ यथैव कक्षमुत्सृष्टो दहेदनिलसारथिः। हनिष्यामि तथा मन्दमनुजानातु मे भवान्॥
en: O great prince, if it behoves you not to make us miserable for life, observe fully the teaching of the Vedas, which lay down, that verily the deceitful ought to be destroyed by the deceitful means. If I but have your command, I would go forth (to Hastinapur) and even as fire consumes heap of grass, would slay that wicked Suyodhana with all my power. It behoves you therefore, O charioteer, to grant me permission."

description: NALOPAKHYANA PARVA The colloquy between Brihadashva and Yudhishthira
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवं ब्रुवाणं भीमं तुधर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः। उवाच सान्त्वयन् राजा मूर्युपाघ्राय पाण्डवम्॥
en: And king Dharmaraja Yudhishthira, having consoled and smelling the crown of the head of that son of Pandu, Bhima, who thus (as above) addressed, spoke thus.

description: NALOPAKHYANA PARVA The colloquy between Brihadashva and Yudhishthira
sn: असंशयं महाबाहो हनिष्यसि सुयोधनम्। वर्षात् त्रयोदशादूर्ध्वं सह गाण्डीवधन्वना॥
en: “You shall, O mighty-armed warrior, assisted by the wielder of the Gandiva, slay, without doubt, Suyodhana after the expiration of the pledged period of thirteen years.

description: NALOPAKHYANA PARVA The colloquy between Brihadashva and Yudhishthira
sn: यत् त्वमाभाषसे पार्थ प्राप्तः काल इति प्रभो। अनृतं नोत्सहे वक्तुं न ह्येतन्मम विद्यते॥
en: O son of Pritha, as for what you say, that “O Lord, the period is complete," I dare not tell a lie, for it never finds place in my heart.

description: NALOPAKHYANA PARVA The colloquy between Brihadashva and Yudhishthira
sn: अन्तरेणापि कौन्तेय निकृति पापनिश्चयम्। हन्ता त्वमसि दुर्धर्ष सानुबन्धं सुयोधनम्॥
en: O son of Kunti, you shall without the help of deceit, which is doubtlessly a sin, slay that irrepressible Suyodhana with all his adherents."

description: NALOPAKHYANA PARVA The colloquy between Brihadashva and Yudhishthira
sn: एवं ब्रुवति भीमं तुधर्मराजे युधिष्ठिरे। आजगाम महाभागो बृहदश्वो महानृषिः॥
en: Whilst Dharmaraja Yudhishthira, was thus speaking to Bhima, there came before him that great and most illustrious sage, Brihadashva.

description: NALOPAKHYANA PARVA The colloquy between Brihadashva and Yudhishthira
sn: तमभिप्रेक्ष्यधर्मात्मा सम्प्राप्तधर्मचारिणम्। शास्त्रवन्मधुपर्केण पूजयामासधर्मराट्॥
en: That righteous and high-souled monarch, Yudhishthira, worshipped the virtuous ascetic with the respectful offerings of Madhuparka (made of honey, curd clarified-butter, sugar and milk in a small cup made of some metal) whom he beheld standing before him.

description: NALOPAKHYANA PARVA The colloquy between Brihadashva and Yudhishthira
sn: आश्वस्तं चैनमासीनमुपासीनो युधिष्ठिरः। अभिप्रेक्ष्य महाबाहुः कृपणं बह्वभाषत॥
en: When the great sage was seated, the mightyarmed Yudhishthira, having supplied him with the refreshments, sat before him, looking and spoke to him in the most piteous terms.

description: NALOPAKHYANA PARVA The colloquy between Brihadashva and Yudhishthira
sn: अक्षयूते च भगवन्धनं राज्यं च मे हृतम्। आहूय निकृतिप्रज्ञैः कितवैरक्षकोविदैः॥
en: "O almighty one, summoned by those evilminded and mischievous but skillful gamblers at dice. I have been deprived of my wealth and kingdom (through gambling).

description: NALOPAKHYANA PARVA The colloquy between Brihadashva and Yudhishthira
sn: अनक्षज्ञस्य हि सतो निकृत्या पापनिश्चयैः। भार्या च मे सभां नीता प्राणेभ्योऽपि गरीयसी॥
en: I am not an expert at dice, the sinful men, having recourse to the foul means, defeated me at dice and even brought my wife, who is dearer to me that life itself, into the midst of the assembly (of herocs).

description: NALOPAKHYANA PARVA The colloquy between Brihadashva and Yudhishthira
sn: पुन तेन मां जित्वा वनवासं सुदारुणम्। प्रावाजयन् महारण्यमजिनैः परिवारितम्॥
en: And defeating me at dice a second time, they have exiled me into the fearful woods, where I lead a disastrous life, clad in deer-skin.

description: NALOPAKHYANA PARVA The colloquy between Brihadashva and Yudhishthira
sn: अहं वने दुर्वसतीर्वसन् परमदुःखितः। अक्षयूताधिकारे च गिरः शृण्वन् सुदारुणाः॥ आतोनां सुहृदां वाचो द्यूतप्रभृति शंसताम्। अहं हृदि श्रिताः स्मृत्वा सर्वरात्रीविचिन्तयन्॥
en: Greatly afflicted with sorrow, I am at present leading a very distressful life in the woods. The cruel speeches which I heard uttered (by my enemies) on the occasion of the past. Gambling and the expressions of my afflicted friends regarding the game and other subjects, live still fresh in my heart and when remembered, they put me into serious thinking during the whole night.

description: NALOPAKHYANA PARVA The colloquy between Brihadashva and Yudhishthira
sn: यस्मिश्चैव समस्तानां प्राणा गाण्डीवधन्वनि। विना महात्मना तेन गतसत्त्व इवाभवम्॥
en: I am, even as deprived of my life, as I am in destitute of that high-souled wielder of the Gandiva, on whom depend the very lives of us all.

description: NALOPAKHYANA PARVA The colloquy between Brihadashva and Yudhishthira
sn: कदा द्रक्ष्यामि बीभत्सुं कृतास्त्रं पुनरागतम्। प्रियवादिनमक्षुद्रं दयायुक्तमतन्द्रितः॥
en: Ah! when shall I see the swift-speaking and liberal Vibhatsu, who is so full of the milk of human kindness and aptitude, coming back to us with all the arms collected from heaven!

description: NALOPAKHYANA PARVA The colloquy between Brihadashva and Yudhishthira
sn: अस्ति राजा मया कश्चिदल्पभाग्यतरो भुवि। भवता दृष्टपूर्वो वा श्रुतपूर्वोऽपि वा क्वचित्। न मत्तो दुःखिततरः पुमानस्तीति मे मतिः॥
en: Is there a prince, on the earth, who is more wretched than I am? Have you ever heard of or seen such a one before. So far as I think, there is no such person, who is more afflicted with grief than myself."

description: NALOPAKHYANA PARVA The colloquy between Brihadashva and Yudhishthira
sn: बृहदश्व उवाच यद् ब्रवीषि महाराज न मत्तो विद्यते क्वचित्। अल्पभाग्यतरः कश्चित् पुमानस्तीति पाण्डव॥ अत्र ते वर्णयिष्यामि यदि शुश्रूषसेऽनघ। यस्त्वत्तो दुःखितारो राजाऽऽसीत् पृथिवीपते॥
en: Brihadashva said: O great prince, O son of Pandu, you say that on this earth there is no such a person more wretched than yourself. O sinless monarch, I will narrate to you if you would listen to me, the history of a king who was (really) more miserable than yourself.

description: NALOPAKHYANA PARVA The colloquy between Brihadashva and Yudhishthira
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच अथैनमब्रवीद् राजा ब्रवीतु भगवानिति। इमामवस्थां सम्प्राप्तं श्रोतुमिच्छामि पार्थिवम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said: Thereupon the king spoke to the great sage, "O most glorious one, relate as I am desirous to hear, the history of the king who had fallen in the most distressful condition of life.”

description: NALOPAKHYANA PARVA The colloquy between Brihadashva and Yudhishthira
sn: बृहदश्व उवाच शृणु राजन्नवहितः सह भ्रातृभिरच्युत। यस्त्वत्तो दुःखिततरो राजाऽऽसीत् पृथिवीपते॥
en: Brihadashva said : O prince, O you that never lapse hear attentively, with your brothers the history of the king who was more miserable than yourself.

description: NALOPAKHYANA PARVA The colloquy between Brihadashva and Yudhishthira
sn: निषधेषु महीपालो वीरसेन इति श्रुतः। तस्य पुत्रोऽभवन्नामा नलोधर्मार्थकोविदः॥
en: O great king, there lived a famous prince among the Nishadhas, who was known by the name of Virasena. He had a son, named Nala, who was versed in religion (virtue) and (in the knowledge of acquiring) wealth).

description: NALOPAKHYANA PARVA The colloquy between Brihadashva and Yudhishthira
sn: स निकृत्या जितो राजा पुष्करेणेति नः श्रुतम्। वनवासं सुदुःखार्तो भार्यया न्यवसत् सह॥
en: We have heard that the king was deceitfully defeated by Pushkara; and in consequence defeated by Pushkara; and in consequence thereof he dwelt in the forest with his spouse, pressed with distress.

description: NALOPAKHYANA PARVA The colloquy between Brihadashva and Yudhishthira
sn: न तस्य दासा न रथो न भ्राता न च बान्धवाः। वने निवसतो राजच्छिष्यन्ते स्म कदाचन॥
en: O king, while living in the forest, Nala had neither servants nor chariots, (nor charioteers), neither he had a brother or friends with him.

description: NALOPAKHYANA PARVA The colloquy between Brihadashva and Yudhishthira
sn: भवान् हि संवृतो वीरैर्धातृभिर्देवसम्मितैः। ब्रह्मकल्पैर्द्विजावयैश्च तस्मान्नार्हसि शोचितुम्॥
en: But you are encircled by your war-like brothers, who are equal to the celestials and also by the best of the twice-born Brahmanas, who arelike unto Brahma himself. Consequently, O king, you should not lament.

description: NALOPAKHYANA PARVA The colloquy between Brihadashva and Yudhishthira
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच विस्तरेणाहमिच्छामि नलस्य सुमहात्मनः। चरितं वदतां श्रेष्ठ तन्ममाख्यातुमर्हसि॥
en: Yudhishthira said: O foremost of the story-tellers, I am very desirous of hearing in detail the history of that illustrious king, Nala. It behoves you therefore, to tell me.

description: The words of the swan's speeches
sn: बृहदश्व उवाच आसीद् राजा नलो नाम वीसेनसुतो बली। उपपन्नो गुणैरिष्टै रूपवानश्वकोविदः॥
en: Brihadashva said: There was a heroic king, named Nala the son of Virasena. He was possessed of desirable attainments, handsome and well-acquainted with the management of horses.

description: The words of the swan's speeches
sn: अतिष्ठन्मनुजेन्द्राणां मूर्ध्नि देवपतिर्यथा। उपर्युपरि सर्वेषामादित्य इव तेजसा॥ ब्रह्मण्यो वेदविच्छूरो निषधेषु महीपतिः। अक्षप्रियः सत्यवादी महानक्षौहिणीपतिः॥
en: He stood at the head of all the princes, even as the king of the celestials; and exalted above all, was equal to the sun in splendour. He was the well-wisher of the Brahmanas and the lord of the Nishadhas. He was truthful, the commander of a mighty force, consisting of cavalry and infantry and a large number of chariots and elephants but fond of gaming at dice,

description: The words of the swan's speeches
sn: ईप्सितो वरनारीणामुदारः संयतेन्द्रियः। रक्षिताधन्विनां श्रेष्ठः साक्षादिव मनुः स्वयम्॥
en: He was beloved of women, high-souled and with all passions checked. He was also the refuge of all and the best of bowmen and was like Manu himself.

description: The words of the swan's speeches
sn: तथैवासीद् विदर्भेषु भीमो भीमपराक्रमः। शूरः सर्वगुणैर्युक्तः प्रजाकामः स चाप्रजः॥
en: Like him (Nala) there was a king among the Vidarbhas, named Bhima, who was warlike, possessor of immense power and all accomplishments and beloved of his subjects. But with all these virtues he was without an issue.

description: The words of the swan's speeches
sn: स प्राजर्थे परं यत्नमकरोत् सुसमाहितः। तमभ्यगच्छद् ब्रह्मर्षिर्दमनो नाम भारत॥
en: He, with a fixity of purpose, made great endeavour for obtaining issue. O Bharata, there came before him, a Brahmarishi named Damana.

description: The words of the swan's speeches
sn: तं स भीमः प्रजाकामस्तोषयामासधर्मवित्। महिष्या सह राजेन्द्र सत्कारेण सुवर्चसम्॥ तस्मै प्रसन्नो दमनः सभार्याय वरं ददौ। कन्यारत्नं कुमारांश्च त्रीनुदारान् महायशाः॥
en: Thereupon, O king of kings, the virtuous prince, Bhima, assisted by his wife, satisfied that reverened sage with the most respectful offerings. Damana, thus pleased, conferred upon the king and his spouse a boon of a daughter like unto a jewel and three sons possessed of liberal heart and great fame.

description: The words of the swan's speeches
sn: दमयन्ती दमं दान्तं दमनं च सुवर्चसम्। उपपन्नान् गुणैः सर्वैर्भीमान् भीमपराक्रमान्॥
en: The daughter and the three sons were named Damayanti and Dama, Danta and the illustrious Damana. The latter were possessed of all the virtues, most fearful and of terrible might.

description: The words of the swan's speeches
sn: दमयन्ती तु रूपेण तेजसा यशसा श्रिया। सौभाग्येन च लोकेषु यशः प्राप्त सुमध्यमा॥
en: But Damayanti of slender waist, obtained celebrity all ever the world in beauty and brightness and in good name, luck and glory.

description: The words of the swan's speeches
sn: अथ तां वयसि प्राप्ते दासीनां समलंकृताम्। शतं शतं सखीनां च पर्युपासच्छचीमिव॥
en: And when she attained to age, hundreds and hundreds of female servants and hand-raids, decked in ornaments, waited on her like Sachi herself.

description: The words of the swan's speeches
sn: तत्र स्म राजते भैमी सर्वाभरणभूषिता। सखीमध्येऽनवद्याङ्गी विद्युत्सौदामनी यथा॥
en: There shone in the midst of her hand-maids the daughter of Bhima, of beautiful features and decked with all ornaments like the bright lightning of the sky.

description: The words of the swan's speeches
sn: अतीव रूपसम्पन्ना श्रीरिवायतलोचना। न देवेषु न यक्षेषु तादृग् रूपवती क्वचित्॥
en: The damsel was possessed of extra-ordinary beauty and large eyes and was like Lakshmi (the goddess of riches) herself. Indeed, there was none among the celestials or the Yakshasa who could be compared with her.

description: The words of the swan's speeches
sn: मानुषेष्वपि चान्येषु दृष्टपूर्वाथवा श्रुता। चित्तप्रसादनी बाला देवानामपि सुन्दरी॥
en: No body among men or others, was possessed of such beauty, seen or heard of. In fact, the damsel was most pleasant to look at and more handsome than the celestials.

description: The words of the swan's speeches
sn: नलश्च नरशार्दूलो लोकेष्वप्रतिमो भुवि। कन्दर्प इव रूपेण मूर्तिमानभवत् स्वयम्॥
en: That foremost of men, Nala, was peerless in the worlds; because on earth he resembled in beauty Kandarpa (the god of love) himself in his embodied form.

description: The words of the swan's speeches
sn: तस्याः समीपे तु नलं प्रशशंसुः कुतूहलात्। नैषधस्य समीपे तु दमयन्तीं पुनः पुनः॥
en: Moved with admiration, they (the heralds) again and again uttered the praises of Nala before her (Damayanti) and those of Damayanti before the king of the Nishadhas, Nala.

description: The words of the swan's speeches
sn: तयोरदृष्टः कामोऽभूच्छृण्वतोः सततं गुणान्। अन्योन्यं प्रति कौन्तेय स व्यवर्धत हृच्छयः॥
en: Although they had not seen each other, yet they conceived a love (for each other) produced by their repeatedly hearing each other's accomplishments. O son of Kunti, that mutual attachment began to grow very strong.

description: The words of the swan's speeches
sn: अशक्नुवन् नलः कामं तदाधारयितुं हृदा। अन्तःपुरसमीपस्थे वन आस्ते रहोगतः॥
en: And then Nala, incapable of holding it in his bosom, passed much of his time in solitude in the gardens adjacent to the inner apartments (of his palace).

description: The words of the swan's speeches
sn: न ददर्श ततो हंसान् जातरूपपरिष्कृतान्। वने विचरतां तेषामेकं जचाह पक्षिणम्॥
en: There he saw, one day, a lot of swans, with golden wings, roving in those woods. Of them he caught one with his hands.

description: The words of the swan's speeches
sn: ततोऽन्तरिक्षगो वाचं व्याजहार नलं तदा। हन्तव्योऽस्मि न ते राजन् करिष्यामि तव प्रियम्।२०॥
en: Thereupon that sky-roving one spoke unto Nala. "O king, it behoves you not to kill me. I will render some good to you.

description: The words of the swan's speeches
sn: दमयन्तीसकाशे त्वां कथयिष्यामि नैषध। यथा त्वदन्यं पुरुषं न सा मंस्यति कर्हिचित्॥
en: O prince of the Nishadhas, I will speak of you before Damayanti and in such a manner that she will never mind to have any other person (for her lord) but yourself."

description: The words of the swan's speeches
sn: एवमुक्तस्ततो हंसमुत्ससर्ज महीपतिः। ते तु हंसाः समुत्पत्य विदर्भानगमंस्ततः॥
en: Thus spoken, the king liberated the swan. Thereafter the swans, spreading their wings, betook themselves to the country of the Vidharbhas.

description: The words of the swan's speeches
sn: विदर्भनगरौं गत्वा दमयन्त्यास्तदान्तिके। निपेतुस्ते गरुत्मन्तः सा ददर्श च तान् खगान्॥
en: Arriving at the city of the Vidharbhas the birds alighted from heaven before Damayanti, who also beheld them.

description: The words of the swan's speeches
sn: सा तानद्भुतरूपान् वै दृष्ट्वा सखिगणावृता। हृष्टा ग्रहीतुं खगमांस्त्वरमाणोपचक्रमे॥
en: Damayanti surrounded by her hand-maids, having seen those birds of extraordinary beauty, desired to catch those rovers of the skies without loss of time.

description: The words of the swan's speeches
sn: अथ हंसा विससृपुः सर्वतः प्रमदावने। एकैकशस्तदा कन्यास्तान् हंसान् समुपाद्रवन्॥
en: Thereupon the swans fled in all directions in that charming forcst; and the ladies ran after them, each pursuing one.

description: The words of the swan's speeches
sn: दमयन्ती तु यं हंसं समुपाधावदन्तिके। स मानुषी गिरं कृत्वा दमयन्तीमथाब्रवीत्॥
en: The swan which Damayanti pursued, led her into a solitary corner of the gardens and addressed her a human speech the following words,

description: The words of the swan's speeches
sn: दमयन्ति नलो नाम निषधेषु महीपतिः। अश्विनोः सदृशो रूपे न समास्तस्य मानुषाः॥
en: “O Damayanti, there is a prince among the Nishadhas, named Nala, who is in beauty, like the Ashvins; and he has not his equal among men.

description: The words of the swan's speeches
sn: कन्दर्प इव रूपेण मूर्तिमानभवत् स्वयम्। तस्य वै यदि भार्या त्वं भवेथा वरवर्णिनी॥ सफलं ते भवेज्जन्म रूपं चेदं सुमध्यमे। वयं हि देवगन्धर्वमनुष्योरगराक्षसान्॥ दृष्टवन्तो न चास्माभिर्दृष्टपूर्वस्तथाविधः। त्वं चापि रत्नं नारीणां नरेषु च नलो वरः॥ विशिष्टया विशिष्टेन संगमो गुणवान् भवेत्।
en: In beauty he is like Kandarpa (the god of love) himself in his embodied form. O fair complexioned one, if you becomes his wife. O you of slender waist, your birth and also your beauty may be of some avail. We have, as a matter of fact, seen celestials, Gandharvas, men, Nagas and Rakshasas; but never have we seen one like him (Nala). As you are a jewel among the maidens, so Nala is the best among men. The best united with the best is of merit.

description: The words of the swan's speeches
sn: एवमुक्ता तु हंसेन दमयन्ती विशांपते॥ अब्रवीत् तत्र तं हंसं त्वमप्येवं नले वद। तथेत्युक्त्वाण्डजः कन्या विदर्भस्य विशाम्पते। पुनरागम्य निषधान् नले सर्वं न्यवेदयत्॥
en: O Prince, Damayanti, was in the above way addressed by the swan. She (Damayanti) in retum said to the swan, “you also thus speak unto Nala."O Prince, the bird having uttered to the daughter of Vidharbha "So be it" returned to the country of the Nishadhas and described everything to Nala himself.

sn: बृहदश्च उवाच दमयन्ती तु तच्छ्रुत्वा वचो हंसस्य भारत। ततः प्रभृति न स्वस्था नलं प्रति बभूव सा॥
en: Brihadashva said: O Bharata hearing the words of the swan, Damayanti thence forth became restless on account of her anxiety for Nala.

sn: ततश्चिन्तापरा दीना विवर्णवदना कृशा। बभूव दमयन्ती तु निःश्वासपरमा तदा॥
en: For this reason, Damayanti became filled with great anxiety and grief; and sighning heavily became lean and pale-faced.

sn: ऊर्ध्वदृष्टिानपरा बभूवोन्मत्तदर्शना। पाण्डुवर्णा क्षणेनाथ हृच्छयाविष्टचेतना॥
en: She always gazed on high with contemplative turn of mind and looked like a dementate. Possessed by the god of love, she also became pale and slender.

sn: न शय्यासनभोगेषु रतिं विन्दति कर्हिचित्। न नक्तं न दिवा शेते हाहेति रुदती पुनः॥
en: She had no desire for the enjoyments, either of beds or seats. And she did not lie down either during the day or night and lamented again and again with the exclamations of Ah and Alas.

sn: तामस्वस्थां तदाकारां सख्यस्ता जजुरिङ्गितः। ततो विदर्भपतये दमयन्त्याः सखीजनः॥ न्यवेदयत् तामस्वस्थां दमयन्ती नरेश्वरे। तच्छ्रुत्वा नृपतिर्भीमो दमयन्ती सखीगणात्॥ चिन्तयामास तत् कार्यं सुमहत् स्वां सुतां प्रति। किमर्थं दुहिता मेऽद्य नातिस्वस्थेव लक्ष्यते॥
en: O King, the hand-maids, of Damayanti beholding her that condition and features, represented them to the ruler of Vidharbha. The king Bhima hearing all from the handmaids was set to serious thinking regarding the affair of his daughter; the thought within, himself why was it that his daughter scemed to be so uncasy at present.

sn: स समीक्ष्य महीपाल: स्वां सुतां प्राप्तयौवनाम्। अपश्यदात्मना कार्यं दमयन्त्याः स्वयंवरम्॥
en: The king, secing his daughter had attained to puberty, observed in his mind that it was his Own duty to make arrangements for Damayanti's Svayamvara (marriage).

sn: तेषां भीमो महाबाहुः स संनिमन्त्रयामास महीपालान् विशाम्पतिः। एषोऽनुभूयतां वीरा: स्वयंवर इति प्रभो॥
en: O exalted one, the king united all the rulers of the earth saying, “O heroes, the Svayamvara ceremony of Damayanti is going to be held.”

sn: श्रुत्वा तु पार्थिवाः सर्वे दमयन्त्याः स्वयंवरम्। अभिजग्मुस्ततो भीमं राजानो भीमशासनात्॥ हस्त्यश्वरथघोषेण पूरयन्तो वसुन्धराम्। विचित्रमाल्याभरणैर्बलैर्दृश्यैः स्वलंकृतैः॥ पार्थिवानां महात्मनाम्। यथार्हमकरोत् पूजां तेऽवसंस्तत्र पूजिताः॥
en: Having learnt of Damayanti's Svayamvara (marriage), all the kings, the rulers of the earth, in obedience to the invitation of Bhima, came to him. The earth was filled with the noise caused by the clatter of the cars, the neighing of horses and the roars of elephants; and those high-souled rulers of the earth, who came with their fair-complexioned battalions decked in ornaments and handsome garlands, were received by that heroic Bhima with the most suitable offerings. Thus honoured by a respectful reception, the kings took up their abodes (in the city of Bhima).

sn: एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु सुराणामृषिसत्तमौ। अटमानौ महात्मानाविन्द्रलोकमितो गतौ॥ नारदः पर्वतश्चैव महाप्राज्ञौ महाव्रतौ। देवराजस्य भवनं विविशाते सुपूजितौ॥
en: At this juncture, those most exalted of the divine sages, the illustrious, greatly wise and austere Narada and Parvata, having arrived at the regions of Indra, obtained admittance into his palace with a respectful reception.

sn: तावर्चयित्वा मघवा ततः कुशलमव्ययम्। पप्रच्छानामयं चापि तयोः सर्वगतं विभुः॥
en: The illustrious Maghavat (Indra), having offered them proper worship, inquired after their everlasting welfare and peace regarding all matters.

sn: नारद उवाच आवयोः कुशलं देव सर्वत्रगतमीश्वर। लोके च मघवन् कृत्स्ने नृपाः कुशलिनो विभो॥
en: Narada said: O Lord, O God, we enjoy peace as regards all matters; and O Maghavat, O illustrious one, so also the beings of the entire world.

sn: बृहदश्व उवाच नारदस्य वचः श्रुत्वा पप्रच्छ बलवृत्रहा। धर्मज्ञाः पृथिवीपालास्त्यक्तजीवितयोधिनः॥ शस्त्रेण निधनं काले ये गच्छन्त्यपराङ्मुखाः। अयं लोकोऽक्षयस्तेषां यथैव मम कामधुक्॥ क्व नु ते क्षत्रियाः शूरा न हि पश्यामि तानहम्। आगच्छतो महीपालान् दयितानतिथीन् मम॥ एवमुक्तस्तु शक्रेण नारदः प्रत्यभाषत।
en: Brihadashva said : Hearing the speeches of Narada the slayer of Bala and Vitra, asked, “Where are those warlike Kshatriyas and why do I not find those princes, coming to me, as they are my most favourite guests? They are the virtuous rulers of the earth, renouncing their life in battle. Your meet death by weapons, when time is come; and never turn their faces away from the battle; their is this world, eternal unto them and bestowing upon them all the objects of enjoyments, even as it does to me. Narada, thus addressed by Shakra, said in reply.

sn: नारद उवाच शृणु मे मघवन् येन न दृश्यन्ते महीक्षितः॥ विदर्भराज्ञो दुहिता दमयन्तीति विश्रुता। रूपेण समतिक्रान्ता पृथिव्यां सर्वयोषितः॥
en: Narada said : O Maghavat, listen to me, why the rulers of the earth are not being seen by you now. The king of the Vidharbhas has a daughter the famous Damayanti; who, in beauty, surpasses all the women of the earth.

sn: तस्याः स्वयंवरः शक्र भविता न चिरादिव। तत्र गच्छन्ति राजानो राजपुत्राश्च सर्वशः॥
en: O Shakra, her Svayamvara will shortly take place. There the kings and princes are going from all directions.

sn: तां रत्नभूतां लोकस्य प्रार्थयन्तो महीक्षितः। काक्षन्ति स्म विशेषेण बलवृत्रनिषूदन॥ सर्वे
en: O slayer of Bala and Vitra, the kings, desirous of getting that pearl of the earth, all desire to have her most eagerly.

sn: एतस्मिन् कथ्यमाने तु लोकपालाश्च साग्निकाः। आजग्मुर्देवराजस्य समीपममरोत्तमाः॥
en: While they were discoursing thus, the most excellent of the immortals, the Lokapalas, (with Agni among them) came before the king of heaven, Indra.

sn: ततस्ते सुश्रुवुः नारदस्य वचो महत्। श्रुत्वैव चाब्रुवन् हृष्टा गच्छामो वयमप्युत।॥
en: They then all heard the speeches of Narada pregnant with lofty ideas and becoming greatly delighted to hear them said that they would also go there.

sn: ततः सर्वे महाराज सगणा: सहवाहनाः। विदर्भानभिजग्मुस्ते यतः सर्वे महीक्षितः॥
en: O great king, mounted on their vehicles, accompanied by their attendants, they all betook themselves to the country of the Vidharbhas where all the rulers of the earth had gone.

sn: नलोऽपि राजा कौन्तेय श्रुत्वा राज्ञां समागमम्। अभ्यगच्छददीनात्मा दमयन्तीमनुव्रतः॥
en: O son of Kunti, the lofty-minded king, Nala, hearing of the assembly of the kings, set out, thinking of Damayanti.

sn: अथ देवाः पथि नलं ददृशुर्भूतले स्थितम्। साक्षादिव स्थितं मूर्त्या मन्मथं रूपसम्पदा॥
en: The celestials saw Nala on the way walking on the earth. In beauty he resembled even the god of love himself in his embodied form.

sn: तं दृष्ट्वा लोकपालास्ते भ्राजमानं यथा रविम्। तस्युर्विगतसंकल्पा विस्मिता रूपसम्पदा॥
