en: The Lokapalas, having seen him resplendent as the sun, were struck with astonishment at his wealth of beauty; and they, therefore, abandoned their idea (of getting her).

sn: ततोऽन्तरिक्षे विष्टभ्य विमानानि दिवौकसः। अब्रुवन् नैषधं राजन्नवतीर्य नभस्तलात्॥
en: The celestials, leaving their cars, alighted from heaven and (then) addressed the king of the Nishadhas thus.

sn: भो भो निषधराजेन्द्र नल सत्यव्रतो भवान्। अस्माकं कुरु साहाय्यं दूतो भव नरोत्तम॥
en: "O the most exalted of the rulers of the Nishadhas, O Nala, O you who do observe the vow of truth, O the foremost of men, help us; be our messenger."

sn: बृहदश्व उवाच तेभ्यः प्रतिज्ञाय नल: करिष्य इति भारत। अर्थतान् परिपप्रच्छ कृताञ्जलिरुपस्थितः॥ के वै भवन्तः कश्चासौ यस्याहं दूत ईप्सितः। किं च तद् वो मया कार्यं कथयध्वं यथातथम्॥
en: Brihadashva said: O Bharata, Nala promised to them (the celestials) saying that he would do it; and then, approaching with folded hands, asked them, “Who are you? And who is he, by whom I am desired to be his inessenger? what further shall I render to you; tell me what really is."

sn: एवमुक्तो नैषधेन मघवानभ्यभाषत। अमरान् वै निबोधास्मान् दमयन्त्यर्थमागतान्॥
en: Maghavat, being thus addressed by the king of the Nishadhas, said in reply, “Be informed that we, the celestials, come here for Damayanti.

sn: अहमिन्द्रोऽयमग्निश्च तथैवायमपां पतिः। शरीरान्तकरो नृणां यमोऽयमपि पार्थिव॥
en: O king I am Indra, this one is Agni; he is the lord of the waters and this is even Yama, the destroyer of human bodies.

sn: त्वं वै समागतानस्मान् दमयन्त्यै निवेदय। लोकपाला महेन्द्राधाः समायान्ति दिदृक्षवः॥
en: Do you inform Damayanti that we, Lokapalas with Mahendra at our head, are all come and going to the assembly (of the heroes), filled with the desire of witnessing (the Svayamvara).

sn: प्राप्तुमिच्छन्ति देवास्त्वां शक्रोऽग्निर्वरुणो यमः। तेषामन्यतम् देवं पतित्वे वरयस्व ह॥
en: And the gods-Shakra, Agni, Vasava and Yama, all desire to win you. Hence choose one of them for your husband."

sn: एवमुक्तः स शक्रेण नलः प्राञ्जलिरब्रवीत्। एकार्थं समुपेतं मां न प्रेषयितुमर्हथ॥
en: Nala, being thus spoken to by Shakra, requested them with folded hands not to send him, as he also has come with the same purpose.

sn: कथं तु जातसंकल्प: स्त्रियमुत्सृजते पुमान्। परार्थमीदृशं वक्तुं तत् क्षमन्तु महेश्वरराः॥
en: "O gods, pardon me; and how it is that a person, who is in the same way determined (to get Damayanti), can dare speak to the damsel on behalf of others."

sn: देवा ऊचुः करिष्य इति संश्रुत्य पूर्वमस्मासु नैषध। न करिष्यसि कस्मात् त्वं व्रज नैषध मा चिरम्॥
en: The Gods said : O king of the Nishadhas, you promised to us beforehand that you would do it. O king of the Nishadhas, why, therefore will you not act up to it? Tell us without (a moment's) hesitation.

sn: वृहदश्व उवाच एवमुक्तः स देवैस्तैर्नैषधः पुनरब्रवीत्। सुरक्षितानि वेश्मानि प्रवेष्टुं कथमुत्सहे॥
en: Brihadashva said : The king of the Nishadhas, being thus spoken by the gods, said again to them: "How can I dare enter those palaces so well-guarded."

sn: प्रवेक्ष्यसीति तं शक्रः पुनरेवाभ्यभाषत। जगाम स तथेत्युक्त्वा दमयन्त्या निवेशनम्॥
en: Indra again said to him in reply "you shall get access." Nala, saying “so be it," repaired to the mansion of Damayanti.

sn: ददर्श तत्र वैदर्भी सखीगणसमावृताम्। श्रिया च वरवर्णिनीम्॥
en: There he saw the daughter of the ruler of Vidharbhas, who was encircled by her handsminds, effulgent in beauty and forin and of fair color.

sn: देदीप्यमानां वपुषा अतीवसुकुमाराङ्गीं तनुमध्यां सुलोचनाम्। आक्षिपन्तीमिव प्रभां शशिनः स्वेन तेजसा॥
en: She also possessed extraordinarily symmetrical handsome limbs, slender waist and fair eyes; her splendour was supposed to ecclipse the light of the moon.

sn: तस्य दृष्ट्वैव बवृधे कामस्तां चारुहासिनीम्। सत्यं चिकीर्षमाणस्तुधारयामास हच्छयम्॥
en: His (Nala's) love increased at the very sight of that sweet smiling one (Damayanti). But being desirous of carrying out the truth, he repressed the love (that was aroused in him).

sn: ततस्ता नैषधं दृष्ट्वा सम्भ्रान्ताः परमाङ्गनाः। आसनेभ्यः समुत्पेतुस्तेजसा तस्यधर्षिताः॥
en: Then beholding the king of the Nishadhas, all the respectable and beautiful ladies sprang up from their seats, possessed as they were by the splendour (of his beauty).

sn: प्रशशंसुश्च सुप्रीता नलं ता विस्मयान्विताः। न चैनमभ्यभाषन्त मनोभिस्त्वभ्यपूजयन्॥
en: Filled with amazement and highly gratified, they praised Nala; but they spoke nothing to him, only worshipped him in the mind.

sn: अहो रूपमहो कान्तिरहोधैर्य महात्मनः। कोऽयं देवोऽथवा यक्षो गन्धर्वो वा भविष्यति॥
en: Oh! what beauty, what effulgence and what patience are possessed by this high-souled one! Who is he! Is he a god or a Yaksha or a Gandharva?

sn: न तास्तं शक्नुवन्ति स्म व्याहर्तुमपि किंचन। तेजसाधर्षितास्तस्य लज्जावत्यो वराङ्गनाः॥
en: Those most excellent women, over-powered by his splendour and out of bashfulness, were not at all able to go near or address him.

sn: अथैनं स्मयमानं तु स्मितपूर्वाभिभाषिणी। दमयन्ती नलं वीरमभ्यभाषत विस्मिता॥
en: Filled as she was with amazement, yet Damayanti, smilingly addressed the heroic Nala, who, also gently smiled at her. She smilingly said thus.

sn: कस्त्वं सर्वानवद्याङ्ग मम हृच्छयवर्धन। प्राप्तोऽस्यमरवद् वीर ज्ञातुमिच्छामि तेऽनघ।॥ कथमागमनं चेह कथं चासि न लक्षितः। सुरक्षितं हि मे वेश्म राजा चैवोचशासनः॥ एवमुक्तस्तु वैदा नलस्तां प्रत्युवाच ह।
en: "Who are you, O you of beautiful form, you have aroused love in me. O warlike one, O sinless one, I desire to know how have you come here. Why have you come here! And how is it you have not been perceived by any body? Indeed, my palace is so well-guarded; and so strict are the commands of the king." Being thus addressed by the daughter of

sn: नल उवाच नलं मां विद्धि कल्याणि देवदूतमिहागतम्॥ देवास्त्वां प्राप्तुमिच्छन्ति शक्रोऽचिर्वरुणो यमः। तेषामन्यतमं देवं पतिं वरय शोभने।॥
en: Nala said: "O handsome damsel, know me by the name of Nala; I have come here as the messenger of the gods. The gods, Shakra, Agni, Varuna and Yama, all desire to have you. O beauteous one, choose one of the celestials as your husband.

sn: तेषामेव प्रभावेण प्रविष्टोऽहमलक्षितः। प्रविशन्तं न मां कश्चिदपश्यन्नाप्यवारयत्॥
en: It is through the influence of those celestials I have entered the palace undiscovered and for this reason also that none has perceived me, nor put obstacles in my way.

sn: एतदर्थमहं भद्रे प्रेषितः सुरसत्तमैः। एतच्छ्रुत्वा शुभे बुद्धिं प्रकुरुष्व यथेच्छसि॥
en: O respected one, I have been sent by the illustrious gods on this errand. O lucky one, form your opinion by hearing this, as you please.

sn: बृहदश्व उवाच सा नमस्कृत्य देवेभ्यः प्रहस्य नलमब्रवीत्। प्रणयस्व यथाश्रद्धं राजन् किं करवाणि ते॥
en: Brihadashva said: Saluting the celestials, (Damayanti) smilingly said to Nala, "O king! love me with due respect and say what shall I do for you.

sn: अहं चैव हि यच्चान्यन्ममास्ति वसु किंचन। तत् सर्वं तव विश्रब्धं कुरु प्रणयमीश्वर॥
en: Myself and whatever riches that I have got are all yours. O lord, make love with full confidence.

sn: हंसानां वचनं यत् तु तन्मां दहति पार्थिव। त्वत्कृते हि मया वीर राजानः संनिपातिता:॥
en: O prince, the speeches of the swans are burning me out. It is for you indeed, O lord I have caused the kings assemble here.

sn: यदि त्वं भजमानां मां प्रत्याख्यास्यसि मानद। विषमग्नि जलं रज्जुमास्थास्ये तव कारणात्॥
en: O the bestower of honor, if you forsake me who worship you, I must have recourse to either poison or fire, water or the rope for your sake."

sn: एवमुक्तस्तु वैदा नलस्तां प्रत्युवाच हा तिष्ठत्सु लोकपालेषु कथं मानुषमिच्छसि॥
en: Thus addressed by the daughter of the king of the Vidharbhas, Nala said to her in reply: “How is it that you choose a man rejecting the Lokapalas (guardians of the worlds) who are present?

sn: येषामहं लोककृतामीश्वराणां महात्मनाम्। न पादरजसा तुल्यो मनस्ते तेषु वर्तताम्॥
en: Do you lead your heart towards those illustrious cclestials, who are the creators of the worlds and even with the dust of whose feet I aim not equal.

sn: विप्रियं ह्याचरन् मयों देवानां मृत्युमृच्छति। त्राहि मामनवद्याङ्गि वरयस्व सुरोत्तमान्॥
en: By offending the celestials, the mortals receive death. Therefore, O beauteous lady, save me by choosing one of the gods for your lord.

sn: विरजांसि च वासांसि दिव्याश्चित्रा: स्रजस्तथा। भूषणानि तु मुख्यानि देवान् प्राप्य तु भुक्ष्व वै॥
en: By choosing the celestials you will enjoy garments unsullied with dust, gaudy garlands of variegated color and superior ornaments.

sn: य इमां पृथिवीं कृत्स्नां संक्षिप्य चसते पुनः। हुताशमीशं देवानां का तं न वरयेत् पतिम्॥
en: What lady will not accept as her husband Hutasha, who, by reducing the dimensions of this entire earth, swallows it also?

sn: यस्य दण्डभयात् सर्वे भूतग्रमाः समागताः। धर्ममेवानुरुध्यन्ति का तं न वरयेत् पतिम्॥
en: What lady will not accept him as her husband, by the terror of whose club all the assembled creatures are propelled to walk in the path of virtue!

sn: धर्मात्मानं महात्मानं दैत्यदानवमर्दनम्। महेन्द्रं सर्वदेवानां का तं न वरयेत् पतिम्॥
en: What lady will not accept as her husband Mahendra, who is the lord of the gods and who is the most virtuous and illustrious and who is also the repressor of the Daityas and the Danavas.

sn: क्रियतामविशङ्केन मनसा यदि मन्यसे। वरुणं लोकपालानां सुहृद्वाक्यमिदं शृणु॥
en: Should you cherish in you heart (the love of Varuna among the guardians of the worlds, do so without delay. Hear this my friendly advice.

sn: नैषधेनैवमुक्ता सा दमयन्ती वचोऽब्रवीत्। समाप्लुताभ्यां नेत्राभ्यां शोकजेनाथ वारिणा॥
en: Thus addressed by the king of the Nishadhas, Damayanti spoke to him with eyes overflowed by the tears produced by sorrow.

sn: देवेभ्योऽहं नमस्कृत्य सर्वेभ्यः पृथिवीपते। वृणे त्वामेव भर्तारं सत्यमेतद् ब्रवीमि ते॥
en: O the ruler of the carth, to tell you the truth, I accept you for my lord after I have saluted all the celestials,

sn: तामुवाच ततो राजा वेपमानां कृताञ्जलिम्। दौत्येनागत्य कल्याणि तथा भद्रे विधीयताम्॥
en: The king, who had come on the mission of the gods, answered her thus who was trembling (with fear), standing with joined hands, 'O blessed one, O gentle one, do what you please.

sn: कथं ह्यहं प्रतिश्रुत्य देवतानां विशेषतः। परार्थे यत्नमारभ्य कथं स्वार्थमिहोत्सहे॥
en: Having promised the celestials specially and come in their interest, how can I venture to look to my own (interest).

sn: एषधर्मो यदि स्वार्थो ममापि भविता ततः। एवं स्वार्थं करिष्यामि तथा भद्रे विधीयताम्॥
en: If virtue be consistent with the seeking of one's own interest, I will surely look to it and so also do you, O gentle one, act according to this (principle).

sn: ततो बाष्पाकुलां वाचं दमयन्ती शुचिस्मिता। प्रत्याहरन्ती शनकैर्नलं राजानमब्रवीत्॥
en: Thereupon Damayanti, whose words were choked up with tears, spoke to Nala with blameless smiles.

sn: उपायोऽयं मया दृष्टो निरपायो नरेश्वर। येन दोषो न भविता तव राजन् कथंचन॥
en: "O the most supreme among men, I find out this sinless way, following which no sin, whatever, O king, will hang upon you.

sn: त्वं चैव हि नरश्रेष्ठ देवाश्चन्द्रपुरोगमाः। आयान्तु सहिताः सर्वे मम यत्र स्वयंवरः॥
en: O the foremost of men, yourself and the celestials with Indra at their head, all come together when my Svayamvara takes place.

sn: ततोऽहं लोकपालानां संनिधौ त्वां नरेश्वर। वरयिष्ये नरव्याघ्र नैवं दोषो भविष्यति॥
en: O the best of men, there I will accept you for my lord among the guardians of the world. Thus, O foremost of men, there will be no blame hanging upon you.

sn: एवमुक्तस्तु वैदा नलो राजा विशाम्पते। आजगाम पुनस्तत्र यत्र देवाः समागताः॥
en: O ruler of the earth! thus addressed by the daughter of the king of the Vidarbhas, king Nala returned where the assembled celestials took their quarters.

sn: तमपश्यंस्तथाऽऽयानं लोकपाला महेश्वराः। दृष्ट्वा चैनं ततोऽपृच्छन् वृत्तान्तं सर्वमेव तम्॥
en: Thereupon the great lords, who are the guardians of the world, seeing him approach, to them, inquired of him about all that had taken place there.

sn: कच्चिद् दृष्टा त्वया राजन् दमयन्ती शुचिस्मिता। किमब्रवीच्च नः सर्वान् वद भूमिप तेऽनघ॥
en: "O Prince, did you see Damayanti of blameless smiles? O blameless one, O Prince, tell us all whatever she pronounced.

sn: नल उवाच भवद्भिरहमादिष्टो दमयन्त्या निवेशनम्। प्रविष्टः सुमहाकक्षं दण्डिभिः स्थविरैर्वृतम्॥
en: Nala said: At your behest, I entered the mansion of Damayanti consisting of large and beautiful chambers and guarded by old guards with bludgeons in their hands.

sn: प्रविशन्तं च मां तत्र न कश्चिद् दृष्टवान् नरः। ऋते तां पार्थिवसुतां भवतामेव तेजसा॥
en: When I entered, no man, through your influence, discovered me there except the daughter of the king.

sn: सख्यश्चास्या मया दृष्टास्ताभिश्चाप्युपलक्षितः। विस्मिताश्चाभवन् सर्वा दृष्ट्वा मां विबुधेश्वराः॥
en: I was preceived by her hand-maids, whom I saw too. O the foremost of the gods, beholding me they were all struck with ainazement.

sn: वर्ण्यमानेषु च मया भवत्सु रुचिरानना। मामेव गतसंकल्पा वृणीते सा सुरोत्तमाः॥
en: O the most excellent of the celestials, although I related all about you, yet the faircomplexioned one settled her mind to choose me for her lord.

sn: अब्रवीच्चैव मां बाला आयान्तु सहिताः सुराः। त्वया सह नरव्याघ्र मम यत्र स्वयंवरः॥
en: The Maiden said: O the foremost of men, I wish the assembled celestials would come with you where my Svayamvara will take place.

sn: तेषामहं संनिधौ त्वां वरयिष्यामि नैषध। एवं तव महाबाहो दोषो न भवितेति ह॥
en: O king of Nishadhas, I will choose you among those celestials. O you mighty-armed warrior, if this be done, no blame will surely touch you.

sn: एतावदेव विबुधा यथावृत्तमुपाहृतम्। मयाशेषे प्रमाणं तु भवन्तस्त्रिदशेश्वराः॥
en: O the exalted of gods, this is all, I relate to you what happened there. O the lords of the gods, it behoves, you therefore, to settle everything finally

sn: बृहदश्व उवाच अथ काले शुभे प्राप्ते तिथौ पुण्ये क्षणे तथा। आजुहाव महीपालान् भीमो राजा स्वयंवरे॥
en: Brihadashva said: When the auspicious hour, the sacred lunar day and the propitious season set in the king Bhima summoned all the rulers of the earth to the Svayamvara.

sn: तच्छ्रुत्वा पृथिवीपाला: सर्वे हृच्छयपीडिताः। त्वरिताः समुपाजग्मुर्दमयन्तीमभीप्सवः॥
en: Hearing this, all the rulers of the carth, repressed by her love and filled with the desire for Damayanti, repaired (to the Svayamvara).

sn: कनकस्तभरुचिरं तोरणेन विराजितम्। विविशुस्ते नृपा रङ्गं महासिंहा इवाचलम्॥
en: Those kings entered the amphi-thcater furnished with golden pillars and adorned with beautiful gates even as the furious lions force their way into the mountain caves.

sn: तत्रासनेषु विविधेष्वासीनाः पृथिवीक्षितः। सुरभिस्रग्धराः सर्वे प्रमृष्टमणिकुण्डलाः॥
en: There all the rulers of the earth decked in fragrant garlands and adorned with ornaments set with gems suspended from their cars, took their respective seats.

sn: तां राजसमिति पुण्यां नागैर्भोगवतीमिव। सम्पूर्णां पुरुषव्याङ्ग्रा।गिरिगुहामिव॥
en: That sacred conclave of the rulers of the earth abounded in the foremost of men even as Bhogavati abounds in the Nagas or as the mountain caves in tigers.

sn: तत्र स्म पीना दृश्यन्ते बाहवः परिघोपमाः। आकारवर्णसुश्लक्ष्णाः पञ्चशीर्षा इवोरगाः॥
en: Their arms were sincwy looking like maces; and they were well-shaped and smooth, even as the five-headed snakes.

sn: सुकेशान्तानि चारुणि सुनासाक्षिभ्रुवाणि च। मुखानि राज्ञां शोभन्ते नक्षत्राणि यथा दिवि॥
en: The countenance of the kings, embellished with beautiful locks and fine noses and brows, glittered even as the stars shine in the firmament.

sn: दमयन्ती ततो रङ्गं प्रविवेश शुभानना। मुष्णन्ती प्रभया राज्ञां चढूंषि च मनांसि च॥
en: Thereupon the fair-complexioned Damayanti entered the amphi-theater; and thus attracted the eyes and hearts of the assembled princes.

sn: तस्या गात्रेषु पतिता तेषां दृष्टिर्महात्मनाम्। तत्र तत्रैव सक्ताभून चचाल च पश्यताम्॥
en: When the kings beheld her, their cyes, unmoved, were finally fixed upon those parts of her body, wherever they had fallen first.

sn: ततः संकीर्त्यमानेषु राज्ञां नामसु भारत। ददर्श भैमी पुरुषान् पञ्चतुल्याकृतीनिह॥
en: Thereupon, ( Bharata, the names of the kings having been ultered, the daughter of Bhima beheld five persons all alike in their form.

sn: तान् समीक्ष्य ततः सर्वान् निर्विशेषाकृती स्थितान। संदेहादथ वैदर्भी नाभ्यजानान्नलं नृपम्॥
en: Thereafter the daughter of the king of the Vidharbhas, having seen all of them of similar forms could not make out which one was prince Nala; for doubts had already arisen in her mind.

sn: यं यं हि ददृशे तेषां तं तं मेने नलं नृपम्। सा चिन्तयन्ती तर्कयामास भाविनी॥
en: Whomsoever she saw among the kings, she supposed him to be the prince Nala; and thus the thoughtful lady pondered and deliberated in her mind.

sn: बुद्ध्याथ कथं हि देवाञ्जानीयां कथं विद्यां नलं नृपम्। एवं संचिन्तयन्ती सा वैदर्भी भृशदुःखिता॥
en: 'How shall I discern the gods and how shall I ascertain prince Nala?' This thought engrossed the mind of the daughter of the king of the Vidarbhas and also afflicted her with great grief.

sn: श्रुतानि देवलिङ्गानि तर्कयामास भारत। देवानां यानि लिङ्गानि स्थविरेभ्यः श्रुतानि मे॥ तानीह तिष्ठतां भूमावेकस्यापि न लक्षये। सा विनिश्चित्य बहुधा विचार्य च पुनः पुनः॥ शरणं प्रति देवानां प्राप्तकालममन्यत।
en: O Bharata, she deliberated in her mind upon the marks of which she heard, as appertaining to the gods, I have heard from the old men whatever marks belong to the celestials and indeed those are never seen to appertain to any one of these assembled in this earth.' Thus she thought on this subject over and over in several ways and came to the conclusion, viz., that she should, after saluting the celestials.

sn: वाचा च मनसा चैव नमस्कारं प्रयुज्य सा॥ देवेभ्यः प्राञ्जलिर्भूत्वा वेपमानेदमब्रवीत्। हंसानां वचनं श्रुत्वा यथा मे नैषधो वृतः। पतित्वे तेन सत्येन देवास्तं प्रदिशन्तु मे॥
en: After that with the mind and words and with joined hands, resolve upon obtaining the assistance of the gods themselves. Trembling with fear she spoke to the celestials thus, "On hearing the words of the swans I accepted the prince of the Nishadhas as my husband. For the sake of that vow of mine, O celestials, point him out to me.

sn: मनसा वचसा चैव यथा नाभिचराम्यहम्। तेन सत्येन विबुधास्तमेव प्रदिशन्तु मे॥
en: As I am always firm to him either in speech or thought, so for the sake of that truth, it beloves the celestials to point him out to me.

sn: यथा देवैः स मे भर्ता विहितो निषधाधिपः। तेन सत्येन मे देवास्तमेव प्रदिशन्तु मे॥
en: When it was settled to me by the celestials that the prince of the Nishadhas should be my husband; for the sake of that truth it behoves the celestials to point him to me.

sn: यथेदं व्रतमारब्धं नलस्याराधने मया। तेन सत्येन मे देवास्तमेव प्रदिशन्तु मे॥
en: When I have commenced my vow for the worship of king Nala; for the sake of that truth, it behoves the celestials to reveal him to me.

sn: स्वं चैव रूपं कुर्वन्तु लोकपाला महेश्वराः। यथाहमभिजानीयां पुण्यश्लोकं नराधिपम्॥
en: It behoves the Lokapalas, the most excellent of the gods, therefore, to assume their respective forms, that I may ascertain that virtuous prince (Nala).

sn: निशम्य दमयन्त्यास्तत् करुणं प्रतिदेवितम्। निश्चयं परमं तथ्यमनुरागं च नैषधे॥ मनोविशुद्धिं बुद्धिं च भक्तिं रागं च नैषधे। यथोक्तं चक्रिरे देवाः सामर्थ्य लिङ्गधारणे॥
en: The celestials, having heard the words of Damayanti full of compassion and known for certain that her love for the prince of the Nishadhas was most fervent and also realizing her fixed will, purity of heart and mind and her passion for that prince, fulfilled what they had been prayed for by assuming their proper forms.

sn: सापश्यद् विबुधान् सर्वानस्वेदान् स्तब्धलोचनान्। हृषितस्रग्रजोहीनान् स्थितानस्पृशतः क्षितिम्॥
en: She then beheld all the gods, not perspiring, with fixed eyes and spotless garlands (round their neck) and seated without touching the earth.

sn: छायाद्वितीयो म्लानस्रग्रजः स्वेदसमन्वितः। भूमिष्ठो नैषधश्चैव निमेषेण च सूचितः॥
en: She, on the other hand, saw Nala standing pre-eminent with his own shadow and (unlike the gods) full of perspiration and with floral wreaths stained with dust and the king of the Nishadhas was also seated on the ground with staring eyes.

sn: सा समीक्ष्य तु तान् देवान् पुण्यश्लोकं च भारत। नैषधं वरयामास भैमीधर्मेण पाण्डव॥
en: O Bharata, she saw both the celestials and that righteous king. But, O descendant of Pandu, the daughter of Bhima accepted (as her husband) the prince of the Nishadhas in accordance with her vow.

sn: विलज्जमाना वस्त्रान्तं जग्राहायतलोचना। स्कन्ध देशेऽसृजत् तस्य स्रजं परमशोभनाम्॥ वरयामास चैवैनं पतित्वे वरवर्णिनी।
en: The bashful and larged-eyed maiden held the flying-end of her cloth and put a most handsome garland round his neck. Thus the . fair-faced damsel had chosen him as his lord.

sn: ततो हाहेति सहसा मुक्तः शब्दो नराधिपः॥
en: Thereupon all the celestials suddenly gave utterance to their woe by saying, Ah! Alas!!

sn: देवैर्महर्षिभिस्तत्र साधु साध्विति भारत। विस्मितैरीरितः शब्दः प्रशंसद्भिर्नलं नृपम्॥
en: O Bharata! all the celestials and the great sages became struck with amazement and uttered the cry. “Excellent and Excellent” while at the same time they were praising king Nala.

sn: दमयन्तीं तु कौरव्य वीरसेनसुतो नृपः। आश्वासयद् वरारोहां प्रहृष्टेनान्तरात्मना।॥
en: O Kauravya! the prince-the son of Virasena, with the gladness of heart, consoled that faircomplexioned maiden thusयत् त्वं भजसि कल्याणि पुमांसं देवसंनिधौ।

sn: तस्मान्मां विद्धि भर्तारमेवं ते वचने रतम्॥
en: O blessed one, as you rejecting all the gods, choose a man to be your lord; so know me, therefore, for your husband, ever ready to obey your words (of command).

sn: यावच्च मेधरिष्यन्ति प्राणा देहे शुचिस्मिते। तावत् त्वयि भविष्यामि सत्यमेतद् ब्रवीमि ते॥
en: O you of blameless smiles, I truly promise to you that as long as my life will reside in my body, till then I will continue to be yours.

sn: दमयन्ती तथा वाग्भिरभिनन्द्य कृताञ्जलिः। तौ परस्परतः प्रीतौ दृष्ट्वा त्वग्निपुरोगमान्॥ तानेव शरणं देवाञ्जग्मतुर्मनसा तदा।
en: Damayanti, with joined hands, showed due respect to him (Nala) by similar expressions. Thereupon the happy pair, each having seen those celestials headed by Agni, mentally prayed for their protection.

sn: वृते तु नैषधे भैम्या लोकपाला महौजसः॥ प्रहृष्टमनसः सर्वे नलायाष्टौ वरान् ददुः।
en: Then the guardians of the worlds of great splendour, beholding the prince of the Nishadhas accepted by the daughter of Bhima, became greatly gratified; and they all granted to Nala eight boons.

sn: प्रत्यक्षदर्शनं यज्ञे गतिं चानुत्तमां शुभाम्॥ नैषधाय ददौ शक्रः प्रीयमाणः शचीपतिः।
en: At first Shakra, the husband of Sachi, well pleased, bestowed upon the king of the Nishadhas a boon. viz., that in the sacrifices he should attain to divinity and thence to each of the extraordinarily great and happy abodes.

sn: अग्निरात्मभवं प्रादाद् यत्र वाञ्छति नैषधः॥ लोकानात्मप्रभांश्चैव ददौ तस्मै हुताशनः।
en: Agni gave assurance of his own presence wherever the king of the Nishadhas would wish. Hutashana also granted to him regions as resplendent as himself.

sn: यमस्त्वन्नरसं प्रादाद्धर्म च परमां स्थितिम्॥
en: Then again Yama lent him a superior taste for food, as well as a highest place in virtue.

sn: अपां पतिरपां भावं यत्र वाञ्छति नैषधः। स्रजश्चोत्तमगन्धाढ्याः सर्वे च मिथुनं ददुः॥
en: The presiding god of the water granted to Nala the boon of his own presence wherever he would wish, as well a floral wreaths of superior fragrance. Thus each one of the assembled gods had given Nala a couple of boons.

sn: वरानेवं प्रदायास्य देवास्ते त्रिदिवं गताः। पार्थिवाश्चानुभूयास्य विवाहं विस्मयान्विताः॥ दमयन्त्याश्च मुदिताः प्रतिजग्मुर्यथागतम्।
en: Having granted these boons to him, all the celestials returned to heaven. And the monarchs also, having witnessed this choicemarriage of Damayanti with Nala, became filled with astonishment; and highly gratified, went away wherever they came from.

sn: गतेषु पार्थिवेन्द्रेषु भीमः प्रीतो महामनाः॥ विवाहं कारयामास दमयन्त्या नलस्य च।
en: And after the departure of the best rulers of the earth, the lofty-minded and well-pleased Bhima celebrated the marriage ceremony of Damayanti and Nala.

sn: उष्य तत्र यथाकामं नैषधो द्विपदां वरः॥ भीमेन समनुज्ञातो जगाम नगरं स्वकम्।
en: The foremost of men, the prince of the Nishadhas, having passed there some time his in-laws house, then return to his own city with the permission of the king Bhima.

sn: अवाप्य नारीरत्नं तु पुण्यश्लोकोऽपि पार्थिवः॥ रेमे सह तया राजञ्छच्येव बलवृत्रहा।
en: O king, that righteous prince, having obtained a maiden like a gem, began to enjoy her sweet company, even as the slayer of Bala and Vritra enjoys the company of Sachi.

sn: अतीव मुदितो राजा भ्राजमानोंऽशुमानिव॥ अरञ्जयत् प्रजा वीरोधर्मेण परिपालयन्।
en: The warlike monarch, resplendent as the sun, was exceedingly glad to rule and maintain his subjects most righteously.

sn: ईजे चाप्यश्वमेधेन ययातिरिव नाहुषः॥ अन्यैश्च बहुभिर्धीमान् क्रतुभिश्चातदक्षिणैः।
en: That talented one like Yayati the son of Nahusha held the horse and several other sacrifices, offering abundant gifts of the Brahmanas.

sn: पुनश्च रमणीयेषु वनेषूपवनेषु च॥ दमयन्त्या सह नलो विजहारामरोपमः।
en: Then again Nala passed his days in joy in the company of Damayanti in the woods and the pleasure gardens, even as the immortals themselves.

sn: जनयामास च ततो दमयन्त्यां महामनाः। इन्द्रसेनं सुतं चापि इन्द्रसेनां च कन्यकाम्॥
en: Thereupon the illustrious prince begot upon Damayanti a son named Indrasena and a daughter named Indrasenā.

sn: एवं स यजमानश्च विहरंश्च नराधिपः। ररक्ष वसुसम्पूर्णां वसुधां वसुधाधिपः॥
en: Thus the ruler of the earth, the fore-most of men having celebrated the sacrifices and passed his days in joy (with Damayanti), governed the earth abounding in wealth.

description: The colloquy between Kali and the celestials
sn: बृहदश्व उवाच वृते तु नैषधे भैम्या लोकपाला महौजसः। यान्तो ददृशुरायान्तं द्वापरं कलिना सह॥
en: Brihadashva said: After the daughter of Bhima had accepted the king of the Nishadhas as her husband, the protectors of the worlds, of great energy, met, when they were returning, Dvapara accompanied by Kali, approaching towards them.

description: The colloquy between Kali and the celestials
sn: अथाब्रवीत् कलिं शक्रः सम्प्रेक्ष्य बलवृत्रहा। द्वापरेण सहायेन कले ब्रूहि क्व यास्यसि॥
en: Shakra, the slayer of Vala and Vritra, beholding Kali, said to him, 'O Kali, tell me, whither are you going with Dvapara as your companion?'

description: The colloquy between Kali and the celestials
sn: ततोऽब्रवीत् कलिः शक्रं दमयन्त्याः स्वयंवरम्। गत्वा हि वरयिष्ये तां मनो हि मम तां गतम्॥
en: Thereupon Kali replying to Shakra's words said, 'Hearing the Svayamvara of Damayanti, I am going there. I shall take her to be my wife; for my heart has been captivated by her?'

description: The colloquy between Kali and the celestials
sn: तमब्रवीत् प्रहस्येन्द्रो निर्वृत्तः स स्वयंवरः। वृतस्तया नलो राजा पतिरस्मत्समीपतः॥
en: Indra smilingly said to him, “That Svayamvara is now over; king Nala has been accepted by her as her husband even in our presence.

description: The colloquy between Kali and the celestials
sn: एवमुक्तस्तु शक्रेण कलिः कोपसमन्वितः। देवानामन्त्र्य तान् सर्वानुवाचेदं वचस्तदा॥
en: Thus spoken to by Shakra, Kali, the viler among the celestials, waxing worth, said to them (celestials) all, the following words:

description: The colloquy between Kali and the celestials
sn: देवानां मानुषं मध्ये यत् सा पतिमविन्दत। ततस्तस्या भवेन्न्याय्यं विपुलं दण्डधारणम्॥
en: "In as much as neglecting the divinities she has accepted a man for her husband, it is but severe cquitable that she shall suffer punishment?”

description: The colloquy between Kali and the celestials
sn: एवमुक्ते तु कलिना प्रत्यूचुस्ते दिवौकसः। अस्माभिः समनुज्ञाते दमयन्त्या नलो वृतः॥
en: When Kali had spoken in the above manner, the celestials replied, “With our permission, Nala has been chosen by Damayanti.

description: The colloquy between Kali and the celestials
sn: का च सर्वगुणोपेतं नाश्रयेत नलं नृपम्। यो वेदधर्मानखिलान् यथावच्चरितव्रतः॥ योऽधीते चतुरो वेदान् सर्वानाख्यानपञ्चमान्। नित्यं तृप्ता गृहे यस्य देवा यज्ञेषुधर्मतः। अहिंसानिरतो यश्च सत्यवादी दृढव्रतः॥ यस्मिन् दाक्ष्यंधृतिर्ज्ञानं तपः शौचं दमः शमः। ध्रुवाणि पुरुषव्याने लोकपालसमे नृपे॥ एवंरूपं नलं यो वै कामयेच्छपितुं कले। आत्मानं स शपेन्मूढो हन्यादात्मानमात्मना॥
en: Also what maiden would not accept Nala as her lord, who is endued with all (excellent) qualities, who is acquainted with all systems of religion, who is a strict observer of vows, who has studied the four Vedas as also the Puranas that are styled the fifth; in whose house the deities are always satisfied by Sacrifices performed in accordance with the rules prescribed for their observance; who never docs any harm to any one, who is truthful and of unshaken vows; in whom truthfulness, forgiveness, knowledge, rigid austerities, purity, self-control and quiescence are ever present; who is the foremost of kings, like the guardians of the worlds. O Kali, that foolish creature, that desires to imprecate Nala of this description, does surely curse his own self and does kill himself by his own agency.

description: The colloquy between Kali and the celestials
sn: एवंगुणं नलं यो वै कामयेच्छपितुं कले। कृच्छ्रे स नरके मज्जेदगाधे विपुले ह्रदे। एवमुक्त्वा कलिं देवा द्वापरं च दिवं ययुः॥
en: O Kali, he that wishes to pronounce malediction on Nala of such qualities, sinks into the vast, unfathomable, lake of hell replete with various torments. "Thus speaking to Kali and Dvapara the celestials repaired to heaven.

description: The colloquy between Kali and the celestials
sn: ततो गतेषु देवेषु कलिपरमब्रवीत्। संहर्तुं नोत्सहे कोपं नले वत्स्यामि द्वापर॥ भ्रंशयिष्यामि तं राज्यान्न भैम्या सह रंस्यते। त्वमप्यक्षान् समाविश्य साहाय्यं कर्तुमर्हसि॥
en: After the celestials had disappeared, Kali said to Dvapara, 'O Dvapara, I cannot restrain my wrath, I will enter into the Nala and disposes him of his kingdom. He shall not any longer hold any dalliance with the daughter of Bhima. Placing yourself at the dice, you ought to help me.

description: On the subject of Nala's gambling
sn: बृहदश्व उवाच एवं स समयं कृत्वा द्वापरेण कलिः सह। आजगाम ततस्तत्र यत्र राजा स नैषधः॥
en: Brihadashva said : Having entered into this agreement with Dvapara, Kali came to the place where the king of the Nishadhas was.

description: On the subject of Nala's gambling
sn: स नित्यमन्तरप्रेप्सुनिषधेष्ववसच्चिरम्। अथास्य द्वादशे वर्षे ददर्श कलिरन्तरम्॥
en: Always intent on detecting a flaw in Nala, he resided in the country of the Nishadhas. In the twelfth vear Kali found out a fault of his.

description: On the subject of Nala's gambling
sn: कृत्वा मूत्रमुपस्पृश्य संध्यामन्वास्त नैषधः। अकृत्वा पादयोः शौचं तत्रै कलिराविशत्॥
en: Naishadha, after having with water, rinsed his mouth, performed the Sandhya ceremony, without having previously washed his two feet. Thereupon Kali possessed him.

description: On the subject of Nala's gambling
sn: स समाविश्य च नलं समीपं पुष्करस्य च। गत्वा पुष्करमाहेदमेहि दीव्य नलेन वै॥
en: He, having entered into Nala, went to Pushkara and said to the latter, “Come, play at dice with Nala?

description: On the subject of Nala's gambling
sn: अक्षयूते नलं जेता भवान् हि सहितो मया। निषधान् प्रतिपद्यस्व जित्वा राज्यं नलं नृपम्॥
en: With my help you shall conquer Nala at a game of dice; and vanquishing king Nala and wining his kingdom, do you govern the Nishadhas?"

description: On the subject of Nala's gambling
sn: एवमुक्तस्तु कलिना पुष्करो नलमभ्ययात्। कलिश्चैव वृषो भूत्वा गवां पुष्करमभ्ययात्॥
en: Thus spoken to by Kali, Pusłıkara went to Nala; Kali also repaired to Pushkara becoming the principal die.

description: On the subject of Nala's gambling
sn: आसाद्य तु नलं वीरं पुष्करः परवीरहा। दीव्यावेत्यब्रवीद् भ्राता वृषेणेति मुहुर्मुहुः।।
en: Pushkara, the chastiser of hostile heroes, having approached the warlike Nala, repeatedly asked him to game together at dice.

description: On the subject of Nala's gambling
sn: न चक्षमे ततो राजा समाह्वानं महामनाः। वैदाः प्रेक्षमाणायाः पणकालममन्यत॥
en: Thereupon the illustrious monarch could not desire to reject the summons. For the reason of Damayanti's presence there, he fixed the time for game also.

description: On the subject of Nala's gambling
sn: हिरण्यस्य सुवर्णस्य यानयुग्यस्य वाससाम्। आविष्टः कलिना द्यूते जीयते स्म नलस्तदा॥ तमक्षमदसम्मत्तं सुहृदां न तु कश्चन। निवारणेऽभवच्छतो दीव्यमानमरिदमम्॥
en: Being taken up by Kali, the prince Nala lost at dice his gold and silver statues, his cars with their teams and also the valuable garments. The illustrious chastiser of the foes was maddened at the game, from which none of his friends could make him desist.

description: On the subject of Nala's gambling
sn: ततः पौरजनाः सर्वे मन्त्रिभिः सह भारत। राजानं द्रष्टुमागच्छन् निवारयितुमातुरम्॥
en: Thereupon, O Bharata, all the inhabitants of the city with the ministers came to see the troubled prince and also to dissuade him (from the play).

description: On the subject of Nala's gambling
sn: तत: सूत उपागम्य दमयन्त्यै न्यवेदयत्। पौरजनो देवि द्वारि तिष्ठति कार्यवान्॥
en: Then the charioteer, having approached Damayanti, said to her" 'O auspicious one, all the citizens and the state officers are staying at the gate."

description: On the subject of Nala's gambling
sn: निवेद्यतां नैषधाय सर्वाः प्रकृतयः स्थिताः। अमृष्यमाणा व्यसनं राज्ञोधर्मार्थदर्शिनः॥
en: O lady, do you inform the king of the Nishadhas that all his citizens have come here, who cannot rcally bear with the calamitous game of their monarch, who is so very well versed in virtue and in the acquisition or wealth.

description: On the subject of Nala's gambling
sn: ततः सा बाष्पकलया वाचा दुःखेन कर्शिता। उवाच नैषधं भैमी शोकोपहतचेतना॥
en: Thereupon the daughter of Bhima, overpowered by grief and deprived of scnses by distresses, said to the prince of the Nishadhas in terins chocked with tears-

description: On the subject of Nala's gambling
sn: राजन् पौरजनो द्वारि त्वां दिदृक्षुरवस्थितः। मन्त्रिभिः सहितः सर्वे राजभक्तिपुरस्कृतः॥ तं द्रष्टुमर्हसीत्येवं पुनः पुनरभाषत। तां तथा रुचिरापाङ्गी विलपन्तीं तथाविधाम्॥ आविष्टः कलिना राजा नाभ्यभाषत किंचन। ततस्ते मन्त्रिणः सर्वे ते चैव पुरवासिनः॥ नायमस्तीति दुःखार्ता वीडिता जग्मुरालयान्। तथा तदभवद् द्यूतं पुष्करस्य नलस्य च। युधिष्ठिर बहून् मासान् पुण्यश्लोकस्त्वजीयत॥
en: 'O king! foremost in loyalty, all the citizens accompanied by the ministers, are waiting at the gate with the desire of seeing you.' She repeatedly told him to grant them an interview. But as the king was possessed by Kali, he answered nothing to them or his queen of handsome looks, who gave utterance to her sorrows thus: And the counselors and all the citizens, overwhelmed with grief and shame and having uttered (unto themselves) that he would never stand, went back to their homes; and thence forward. O Yudhishthira, the gambling of Pushkara and Nala continued for several months, while the righteous king was always defeated.

sn: बृहदश्व उवाच दमयन्ती ततो दृष्ट्वा पुण्यश्लोकं नराधिपम्। उन्मत्तवदनुन्मत्ता देवने गतचेतसम्॥ भयशोकसमाविष्टा राजन् भीमसुता ततः। चिन्तयामास तत् कार्यं सुमहत् पार्थिवं प्रति॥
en: Brihadshava said : Damayanti beheld the righteous king to be maddened at the gambling and deprived of his reason. Thereupon, O Monarch, the daughter of Bhima was overwhelmed with terror and grief and meditated upon the seriousness of the matter regarding the king, her husband.

sn: सा शङ्कमाना तत् पापं चिकीर्षन्ती च तत्प्रियम्। नलं च हृतसर्वस्वमुपलभ्येदमब्रवीत्॥ बृहत्सेनामतियशां तांधात्री परिचारिकाम्। हितां सर्वार्थकुशलामनुरक्तां सुभाषिताम्॥
en: Beholding Nala deprived of all his possessions and being afraid of the calamity that had befallen her husband and desirous of doing good to him, Damayanti addressed to her nurse and maid-servant who was most noted, well-meaning beloved and intent upon doing good to all and well-speaking-these words-

sn: बृहत्सेने व्रजामात्यानानाय्य नलशासनात्। आचक्ष्व यद्भूतं द्रव्यमवशिष्टं च यद् वसु॥
en: 'O Brihadsena! inviting all the ministers in the name of king Nala, go and inform them what things are lost and what wealth still remains.

sn: ततस्ते मन्त्रिणः सर्वे विज्ञाय नलशासनम्। अपि नो भागधेयं स्यादित्युक्त्वा नलमाव्रजन्॥
en: Thereupon all the ministers, having been informed of the summons of the king, uttered"O this was most unfortunate for them all” and advanced to Nala,

sn: तास्तु सर्वाः प्रकृतयो द्वितीयं समुपस्थिताः। न्यवेदयद् भीमसुता न च तत् प्रत्यनन्दत॥
en: When again the daughter of Bhima informed Nala, that all his subjects came there in a body for the second time, the king said nothing to her in reply.

sn: वाक्यमप्रतिनन्दन्तं भर्तारमभिवीक्ष्य सा। दमयन्ती पुनर्वेश्म वीडिता प्रविवेश ह॥ निशम्य सततं चाक्षान् पुण्यश्लोकपराङ्मुखान्। नलं च हृतसर्वस्वंधात्री पुनरुवाच ह॥ बृहत्सेने पुनर्गच्छ वार्ष्णेयं नलशासनात्। सूतमानय कल्याणि महत् कार्यमुपस्थितम्॥
en: Damayanti, beholding that her lord uttered not a word to her in reply, felt shame and entered her own apartments. And also hearing that the virtuous Nala was always defeated at dice and deprived of all his possessions, she spoke again unto her nurse, Brihadsena! O blessed one do you go and summon, in the name of Nala, Varshneya, the charioteer, as a very serious matter is near at hand.

sn: बृहत्सेना तु सा श्रुत्वा दमयन्त्याः प्रभाषितम्। वार्ष्णेयमानयामास पुरुषैराप्तकारिभिः॥ वार्ष्णेयं तु ततो भैमी सान्त्वयश्लक्ष्णया गिरा। उवाच देशकालज्ञा प्राप्तकालमनिन्दिता॥
en: Hearing the words of Damayanti, Brihadsena brought Varshneya summoned by faithful servants. Thereupon the daughter of Bhima, who was unblameable and was never out of place or season, consoled Varshneya by sweet speeches and said to him words suitable to the occasion-

sn: जानीषे त्वं यथा राजा सम्यग् वृत्तः सदा त्वयि। तस्य त्वं रिषमस्थस्य साहाय्यं कर्तुमर्हसि॥
en: It is known to you how always you were treated by the monarch. Now it is necessary for you therefore, to remember this and help him in his distress.

sn: यथा यथा हि नृपतिः पुष्करेणैव जीयते। तथा तथास्य वै छूते रागो भूयोऽभिवर्धते॥
en: The more the king is defeated by Pushkara in the game, the greater becomes his earnestness for it.

sn: यथा च पुष्करस्याक्षाः पतन्ति वशवर्तिनः। तथा विपर्ययश्चापि नलस्याक्षेषु दृश्यते॥
en: As the dice fall in accordance with the commands of Pushkara, so it is seen they are adverse to the interests of Nala in the play.

sn: सुहृत्स्वजनवाक्यानि यथावन्न शृणोति च। ममापि च तथा वाक्यं नाभिनन्दति मोहितः॥ नूनं मन्ये न दोषोऽस्ति नैषधस्य महात्मनः। यत् तु मे वचनं राजा नाभिनन्दति मोहितः॥
en: Deeply engaged in the game, as he is deaf regarding the advices of his friends and relatives, so he does not accept my counsel. Surely me-seems, the high-souled Naishadha is not to be blamed for his not listening to my words, absorbed as he is in the game.

sn: शरणं त्वां प्रपन्नास्मि सारथे कुरु मद्वचः। न हि मे शुध्यते भावः कदाचिद् विनशेदपि॥
en: O charioteer! I seek your protection. Act according to my commands. My mind is not very sanguine. King Nala may come to danger.

sn: नलस्य दयितानश्वान् योजयित्वा मनोजवान्। इदमारोप्य मिथुनं कुण्डिनं यातुमर्हसि॥
en: Yoking the favourite steeds of Nala, fleet as the glance of mind and placing my twins (a son and a daughter) on the car, you should repair to Kundina in all haste.

sn: मम ज्ञातिषु निक्षिप्य दारको स्यन्दनं तथा। अश्वांश्चमान् यथाकामं वस वान्यत्र गच्छ वा॥
en: Leaving the children and the car and these horses with my relatives, do you go there or go away wherever it pleases you to go,'

sn: दमयन्त्यास्तु तद् वाक्यं वार्ष्णेयो नलसारथिः। न्यवेदयशेषेण नलामात्येषु मुख्यशः॥
en: Varshneya the charioteer of Nala, told in detail these words of Damayanti to the chief counsellors of Nala.

sn: तैः समेत्य विनिश्चित्य सोऽनुज्ञातो महीपते। ययौ मिथुनमारोग्य विदर्भास्तेन वाहिना॥
en: O lord of earth! deciding (the matter) with their aid and with their permission placing the children on the chariot the charioteer hastened towards Vidarbha.

sn: हयांस्तत्र विनिक्षिप्य सूतो रथवरं च तम्। इन्द्रसेनां च तां कन्यामिन्द्रसेनं च बालकम्॥ आमन्त्र्य भीमं राजानमार्तः शोचन् नलं नृपम्। अटमानस्ततोऽयोध्या जगाम नगरी तदा॥
en: There leaving the horses, the excellent of cars and the boy Indrasena and the girl Indrasena and saluting king Bhima and afflicted and grieving for Nala, the charioteer started from that place and repaired to the town of Ayodhya.

sn: ऋतुपर्णं स राजानमुपतस्थे सुदुःखितः। भृति चोपययौ तस्य सारथ्येन महीपते॥
en: He approached king Rituparna with a sorrowful heart and entered into the service of the monarch as a charioteer.

sn: बृहदश्व उवाच ततस्तु याते वार्ष्णेये पुण्यश्लोकस्य दीव्यतः। पुष्करेण हृतं राज्यं यच्चान्यद् वसु किंचन॥
en: Brihadashva said: After Varshneya had gone away, his kingdom and what else of wealth he possessed, were won by Pushkara from Nala of good fame, who was engaged at dice.

sn: हृतराज्यं नलं राजन् प्रहसन् पुष्करोऽब्रवीत्। द्यूतं प्रवर्ततां भूयः प्रतिपाणोऽस्ति कस्तव॥
en: O king! Pushkara said to Nala whose kingdom had been won from him, with a (sinister) smile:-'Let our game at dice commence anew, but what else to stake you have got now?'

sn: शिष्टा ते दमयन्त्येका सर्वमन्यज्जितं मया। दमयन्त्याः पणः साधु वर्ततां यदि मन्यसे॥
en: Damayanti alone is left to you; everything else has been won by me. Well if you think it right hold Damayanti as your stake now?

sn: पुष्करेणैवमुक्तस्य पुण्यश्लोकस्य मन्युना। व्यदीर्यतेव हृदयं न चैनं किंचिदब्रवीत्॥
en: Thus spoken to by Pushkara Nala of holy fame felt as if his heart would burst in grief. Neither did he speak a syllable to him.

sn: ततः पुष्करमालोक्य नलः परममन्युमान्। उत्सृज्य सर्वगात्रेभ्यो भूषणानि महायशाः॥ एकवासा ह्यसंवीतः सुहृच्छोकविवर्धनः। निश्चक्राम ततो राजा त्यक्त्वा सुविपुलां श्रियम्॥
en: Thereafter Nala of high renown, possessed with extreme anguish, looking at Pushkara, began to take all the ornaments off every part of his body. Then wearing a single piece of cloth, with his person uncovered enhancing the gricſ of his friends and forsaking his vast wealth the king went out.

sn: दमयन्त्येकवस्त्राथ गच्छन्तं पृष्ठतोऽन्वगात्। स तया बाह्यतः सार्धं त्रिरात्रं नैषधोऽवसत्॥
en: Also Damayanti, attired in a single piece of cloth, followed the departing king behind. With her the king of Naishadha, passed three nights outside the precincts of the town.

sn: पुष्करस्तु महाराज घोषयामास वै पुरे। नले यः सम्यगातिष्ठेत् स गच्छेद् वध्यतां मम॥
en: O mighty king in the meantime Pushkara had it proclaimed within the city, that any body that should regardfully (hospitably) behave towards Nala would become his victim.

sn: पुष्करस्य तु वाक्येन तस्य विद्वेषणेन च। पौरा न तस्य सत्कारं कृतवन्तो युधिष्ठिर॥
en: O Yudhishthira! in consequence of this proclamation of Pushkara and his malice towards Nala, the citizens offered no respectful conduct towards him.

sn: स तथा नगराभ्याशे सत्कारार्हो न सत्कृतः। त्रिरात्रमुषितो राजा जलमात्रेण वर्तयन्॥
en: Thus unregarded, though worthy of their (citizen's) regards, that king stayed three nights outside the precincts of the city living, all the while solely on water.

sn: पीड्यमानः क्षुधा तत्र फलमूलानि कर्षयन्। प्रातिष्ठत ततो राजा दमयन्ती तमन्वगात्॥
en: Oppressed with hunger, the king started from the vicinity of the city with the object of collecting fruits and roots while Damayanti followed him (closely).

sn: क्षुधया पीड्यमानस्तु नलो बहुतिथेऽहनि। अपश्यच्छकुनान् कांश्चिद्धिरण्यसदृशच्छदान्॥
en: Afflicted sore with (the pangs of) hunger, after the lapse of many days, Nala saw some birds, the colour of whose plumage resembled that of gold.

sn: स चिन्तयामास तदा निषधाधिपतिर्बली। अस्ति भक्ष्यो ममाद्यायं वसु चेदं भविष्यति॥
en: Thereupon the powerful ruler of the Nishadhas, thought (within himself)-My food today will consist of these and afterwards their plumage shall be my wealth.

sn: ततस्तान् परिधानेन वाससा स समावृणोत्। तस्य तद् वस्त्रामादाय सर्वे जग्मुर्विहायसा॥
en: Then he covered them with the piece of cloth he was wearing. Taking on their back that piece of cloth belonging to him, those rangers of the sky flew to the heavens.

sn: उत्पदन्तः खगा वाक्यमेतदाहुस्ततो नलम्। दृष्ट्वा दिग्वाससं भूमौ स्थितं दीनमधोमुखम्॥
en: When rising up (to the sky) the birds of the earth seeing Nala sorrowful and seated on the car with his person nude and countenance down towards the ground, addressed these words to him.

sn: वयमक्षाः सुदुर्बुद्धे तव वासो जिहीर्षवः। आगता न हि नः प्रीतिः सवाससि गते त्वयि॥
en: 'O greatly foolish one! we are even those dice. We had come hither desirous of robbing your cloth. For surely we feel no pleasure, even if you depart wearing your cloth.'

sn: तान् समीपगतानक्षानात्मानं च विवाससम्। पुण्यश्लोकस्तदा राजन् दमयन्तीमथाब्रवीत्॥ येषां प्रकोपादैश्वर्यात् प्रच्युतोऽहमनिन्दिते। प्राणयात्रां न विन्देयं दुःखितः क्षुधयान्वितः॥ येषां कृते न सत्कारमकुर्वन् मयि नैषधाः। इमे ते शकुना भूत्वा वासो भीरु हरन्ति मे॥
en: O king! then Nala of holy fame beholding the dice depart and himself naked, thus spoke of Damayanti. O unblameable lady! they, in consequence of whose wrath I have been deprived of my (royal) fortune and being distressed and oppressed with hunger I cannot procure my livelihood, they through whose (malign) influence the citizens of Naishadha paid me no regard, O timid one! those very dice have assumed the form of birds and are even now fiying away with my cloth.

sn: वैषम्यं परमं प्राप्तो दुःखितो गतचेतनः। भर्ता तेऽहं निबोधेदं वचनं हितमात्मनः॥
en: I, your husband, have met with a great catastrophe. I am afflicted with sorrow and am devoid of my consciousness. Listen to my words, which (when acted upon) shall conduce to your good.

sn: एते गच्छन्ति बहवः पन्थानो दक्षिणापथम्। अवन्तीमृक्षवन्तं च समतिक्रम्य पर्वतम्॥
en: These various roads before you, passing by the (city of) Avanti and crossing the Rikshavat mountain lead to the Deccan.

sn: एष विन्ध्यो महाशैलः पयोष्णी च समुद्रगा। आश्रमाश्च महर्षीणां बहुमूलफलान्विताः॥ एष पन्था विदर्भाणामसौ गच्छति कोसलान्। अतः परं च देशोऽयं दक्षिणे दक्षिणापथः॥
en: Yonder is the mighty range of mountains known under the name of Vindhya; there is the river Payashini flowing toward the sea and you lie the hermitages of the illustrious sages replete with many kinds of fruits and roots. This road leads to Vidharbha, the other one proceeds towards the country of the Kosalas; beyond them in the southern direction lies the Deccan.

sn: बृहदश्व उवाच एतद् वाक्यं नलो राजा दमयन्तीं समाहितः। उवाचासकृदातॊ हि भैमीमुद्दिश्य भारत।॥
en: Brihdashva said: O descendant of Bharata's race! addressing the daughter of Bhima, king Nala sorely afflicted with grief, carefully spoke these words to Damayanti, over and over again.

sn: ततः सा बाष्पकलया वाचा दुःखेन कर्शिता। उवाच दमयन्ती तं नैषधं करुणं वचः॥
en: Thereupon distressed with sorrow and in a voice choked with the vapour of grief, Damayanti spoke to Nala these piteous words.

sn: उद्वेजते मे हृदयं सीदन्त्यङ्गानि सर्वशः। तव पार्थिव संकल्पं चिन्तयन्त्याः पुनः पुनः॥ हृतराज्यं हृतद्रव्यं विवस्त्रं क्षुच्छ्रमान्वितम्। कथमुत्सृज्य गच्छेयमहं त्वां निर्जने वने।॥
en: Damayanti said : O ruler of the earth! on continuous thinking of your intention, my heart trembles and all my limbs are sinking. How can I depart leaving you in this lonely forest, deprived of your kingdom despoiled of your wealth, yourself not covered even with a single piece of cloth and afflicted with hunger and toil?

sn: श्रान्तस्य ते क्षुधार्तस्य चिन्तयानस्य तत् सुखम्। वने घोरे महाराज नाशयिष्याम्यहं क्लमम्॥
en: O illustrious sovereign! when fatigued with toil and oppressed with hunger in the midst of this dreary wilderness, you shall remember your former happiness, then shall I solace you in your troubles.

sn: न च भार्यासमं किंचिद् विद्यते भिषजां मतम्। औषधं सर्वदुःखेषु सत्यमेतद् ब्रवीमि ते॥
en: 'In all descriptions of misery there is no medicine similar to a wife, this is the opinion of all the physicians, I tell the forsooth.

sn: नल उवाच एवमेतद् यथाऽऽत्य त्वं दमयन्ति सुमध्यमे। नास्ति भार्यासमं मित्रं नरस्यार्तस्य भेषजम्॥
en: Nala said: O you of delicate loins! O Damayanti, what you have said, is indeed true; to a man aggrieved there is no friend equal to a wife that serves as a remedy.

sn: न चाहं त्यक्त कामस्त्वां किमलं भीरु शङ्कसे। त्यजेयमहमात्मानं न चैव त्वामनिन्दिते॥
en: O timid one! why are you afraid? I do not intend to forsake you; O faultless one, I can part with myself, but not with you.

sn: दमयन्त्युवाच यदि मां त्वं महाराज न विहातुमिहेच्छसि। तत् किमर्थं विदर्भाणां पन्थाः समुपदिश्यते॥
en: Damayanti said : O great monarch! if you seek not to desert me, why then do you instruct, (point out to) me, about the road that leads to the dominion of the Vidharbhas?

sn: अवैमि चाहं नृपते न तु मां त्यक्तुमर्हसि। चेतसा त्वपकृष्टेन मां त्यजेथा महीपते।॥
en: O protector of your subjects! I know also that you cannot leave me. But, O ruler of the earth! you may renounce me, as your mind (reason) is spoiled (distracted) by Kali.

sn: पन्थानं हि ममाभीक्ष्णमाख्यासि च नरोत्तम। अतो निमित्तं शोकं मे वर्धयस्यमरोपम॥
en: O foremost of men! you are repeatedly instructing me about the road. O divine one! it is in this way that you are adding to my sorrow.

sn: यदि चायमभिप्रायस्तव ज्ञातीन् व्रजेदिति। सहितावेव गच्छावो विदर्भान् यदि मन्यसे॥
en: If it be your wish that I should go back to my kinsmen, then if it list you, we both together shall repair to the kingdom of Vidharbha.

sn: विदर्भराजस्तत्र त्वां पूजयिष्यति मानद। तेन त्वं पूजितो राजन् सुखं वत्स्यसि नो गृहे॥
en: O bestower of honor! there, the king of the Vidharbhas shall worship you. Thus held in great respect by him, you shall live in happiness in our residence.

description: The desertion of Damayanti by Nala
sn: नल उवाच यथा राज्यं तव पितुस्तथा मम न संशयः। न तु तत्र गमिष्यामि विषमस्थः कथंचन॥
en: Nala said: No doubt, your father's kingdom is the same as mine own. But thither by any means I will not go, being in embarrassed circumstances.

description: The desertion of Damayanti by Nala
sn: कथं समृद्धो गत्वाहं तव हर्षविवर्धनः। परिच्युतो गमिष्यामि तव शोकविवर्धनः॥
en: There was a time when repairing there in all my prosperity, I enhanced your delight. Shorn of it (prosperity) how can I now repair there to add to your sorrow?

description: The desertion of Damayanti by Nala
sn: बृहदश्व उवाच इति ब्रुवन् नलो राजा दमयन्तीं पुनः पुनः। सान्त्वयामास कल्याणी वाससोऽर्धेन संवृताम्॥ तावेकवस्त्रसंवीतावटमानावितस्ततः। क्षुत्पिपासापरिश्रान्तौ सभां कांचिदुपेयतुः॥
en: Brihadhsava said: Thus repeatedly speaking unto Damayanti, used to all happiness, king Nala tried to console her, now clad only in half of her cloth. Both of them wrapped in a single piece of cloth, when wandering this way and that, arrived at an inn, worn out with hunger and thirst.

description: The desertion of Damayanti by Nala
sn: तां सभामुपसम्प्राप्य तदा स निषधाधिपः। वैदा सहितो राजा निषसाद महीतले॥
en: Then on reaching that inn, the ruler of the Nishadhas seated himself on the surface of the earth with the daughter of the king of Vidharbha.

description: The desertion of Damayanti by Nala
sn: स वै विवस्त्रो विकटो मलिनः पांसुगुण्ठितः। दमयन्त्या सह श्रान्तः सुष्वापधरणीतले॥
en: Destitute of his garments, unsightly, with his person unclean, covered with dust, he laid himself down with Damayanti on the surface of the earth in fatigue.

description: The desertion of Damayanti by Nala
sn: दमयन्त्यपि कल्याणी निद्रयापहृता ततः। सहसा दुःखमासाद्य सुकुमारी तपस्विनी॥
en: Then ever used to happiness, the comcly and innocent Damayanti, too, suddenly visited with misfortune, became unconscious in sleep.

description: The desertion of Damayanti by Nala
sn: सुप्तायां दमयन्त्यां तु नलो राजा विशाम्यते। शोकोन्मथितचित्तात्मा न स्म शेते तथा पुरा॥
en: O lord of your subjects! when Damayanti fell asleep, king Nala, owing to his heart and mind being agitated with grief, could not sleep as before (in his days of happiness).

description: The desertion of Damayanti by Nala
sn: स तद् राज्यापहरणं सुहृत्त्यागं च सर्वशः। वने च तं परिध्वंसं प्रेक्ष्य चिन्तामुपेयिवान्॥
en: He, musing over the loss of his kingdom, his abandonment by his friends, the disaster he met with in the forest and over his other misfortunes, began to reflect (in the following manner).

description: The desertion of Damayanti by Nala
sn: नु किं मे स्यादिदं कृत्वा किं नु मे स्यादकुर्वतः। किं नु मे मरणं श्रेयः परित्यागो जनस्य वा॥
en: “What will accrue from my doing this? And what from my not doing this? Which is preferable to me now, my death or the desertion of my wife?

description: The desertion of Damayanti by Nala
sn: मामियं हनुरक्तवं दुःखमाप्नोति मत्कृते। मद्विहीना त्वियं गच्छेत् कदाचित् स्वजनं प्रति॥
en: She is (fondly) attached unto myself. For this reason she suffer these afflictions for me. But (when) forsaken by me, she may possibly repair to her relatives.

description: The desertion of Damayanti by Nala
sn: मयि नि:संशयं दुःखमियं प्राप्स्यत्यनुव्रता। उत्सर्गे संशयः स्यात् तु विन्देतापि सुखं क्वचित्।।
en: Devoted as she is to me, she is sure to suffer distress if she accompanies me; but it is doubtful, whether she would suffer them or not, were I to forsake her. Perchance, she may sometime attain to happiness."

description: The desertion of Damayanti by Nala
sn: स विनिश्चित्य बहुधा विचार्य च पुनः पुनः। उत्सर्ग मन्यते श्रेयो दमयन्त्या नराधिप॥
en: O Monarch! thus repeatedly cogitating over this subject and reflecting again and again about it, he (at last) decided the desertion of Damayanti to be the best course open to him.

description: The desertion of Damayanti by Nala
sn: न चैषा तेजसा शक्या कैश्चिद्धर्षयितुं पथि। यशस्विनी महाभागा मद्भक्तेयं पतिव्रता॥
en: For her spiritedness, nobody will be able to insult, on the way, this high-souled, chaste and illustrious lady who is (fondly) devoted to me.'

description: The desertion of Damayanti by Nala
sn: एवं तस्य तदा बुद्धिर्दमयन्त्यां न्यवर्तत। कलिना दुष्टभावेन दमयन्त्या विसर्जने।॥
en: Thus through the instrumentality of the wicked Kali, his mind then ceased to dwell on Damayanti and he settled his purpose of abandoning her.

description: The desertion of Damayanti by Nala
sn: सोऽवस्त्रताममात्मनश्च तस्याश्चाप्येकवस्त्रताम्। चिन्तयित्वाध्यगाद् राजा वस्त्रार्धस्यावकर्तनम्॥
en: Thinking of his own want of garment and of Damayanti's being clad in a single piece of cloth, the King intended to pair off half of her cloth.

description: The desertion of Damayanti by Nala
sn: कथं वासो विकर्तेयं न च बुध्येत मे प्रिया। विचिन्त्यैवं नलो राजा सभां पर्यचरत्तदा॥
en: 'How shall I cut off her cloth, so that my beloved may not awake.' Thus thinking, king Nala then began to wander about that inn.

description: The desertion of Damayanti by Nala
sn: परिधावनथ नल इतश्चेतश्च भारत। आससाद सभोद्देशे विकोशं खङ्गमुत्तमम्॥
en: O descendant of Bharata's race! walking with hasty steps up and down, Nala obtained, near the inn, an excellent unsheathed sword.

description: The desertion of Damayanti by Nala
sn: तेनार्धं वाससश्छित्त्वा निवस्य च परंतपः। सुप्तामुत्सृज्य वैदर्भी प्राद्रवद् गतचेतनाम्॥
en: That chastiser of his enemies, having with this sword cut off one half of her cloth, wore it. And then leaving the daughter of the Vidharbha king asleep and unconscious, he hurriedly went away.

description: The desertion of Damayanti by Nala
sn: ततो निवृत्तहृदयः पुनरागम्य तां सभाम्। दमयन्तीं तदा दृष्ट्वा सरोद निषधाधिपः॥
en: But then his heart being attracted towards Damayanti, the ruler of the Nishadhas, came back to that inn; and finding her in that condition he began to lament:

description: The desertion of Damayanti by Nala
sn: यां न वायुर्न चादित्यः पुरा पश्यति मे प्रियाम्। सेयमद्य सभामध्ये शेते भूमावनाथवत्॥
en: ‘My dear-loved wife, whom even the winds or the sun could not sce before, is even now lying asleep like one helpless on the ground of this inn.

description: The desertion of Damayanti by Nala
sn: इयं वस्त्रावकर्तेन संवीता चारुहासिनी। उन्मत्तेव वरारोहा कथं बुद्ध्वा भविष्यति॥
en: How will this sweet smiling and slenderwaisted Damayanti live, when awaking, she shall find herself clothed, like one mad, in half a piece of cloth?

description: The desertion of Damayanti by Nala
sn: कथमेका सती भैमी मया विरहिता शुभा। चरिष्यति वने घोरे मृगव्यालनिषेविते॥
en: How will this blessed daughter of Bhima, the chaste Damayanti, roam, without me and all alone, in this dreary wilderness, inhabited by beasts and serpents.

description: The desertion of Damayanti by Nala
sn: आदित्या वसवो रुद्रा अश्विनौ समरुद्गणौ। रक्षन्तु त्वां महाभागेधर्मेणासि समावृता॥
en: O noble-hearted one! may the Adityas, the Vasus, the Rudras, the twin Asvinis together with the wind-gods, protect you! Or you are protected by yours own virtue!'

description: The desertion of Damayanti by Nala
sn: एवमुक्तवा प्रियां भार्यां रूपेणाप्रतिमां भुवि। कलिनापहतज्ञानो नलः प्रातिष्ठदुद्यतः॥
en: Thus speaking unto his dear-loved wife matchless on carih in beauty, king Nala, deprived of his senses by Kali, endeavoured to go away.

description: The desertion of Damayanti by Nala
sn: गत्वा गत्वा नलो राजा पुनरेति सभां मुहुः। आकृष्यमाणः कलिना सौहृदेनावकृष्यते॥
en: The royal Nala departing again and again, returned again and again to the inn, once dragged away by Kali and again drawn back by his love (to his wife).

description: The desertion of Damayanti by Nala
sn: द्विधेव हृदयं तस्य दुःखितस्याभवत् तदा। दोलेव मुहुरायाति याति चैव सभां प्रति॥
en: It seemed as if the heart of the distressed king was divided in twain, who like a rocking cradle repeatedly went away from and came back into the inn,

description: The desertion of Damayanti by Nala
sn: अवकृष्टस्तु कलिना मोहितः प्राद्रवन्नलः। सुप्तामुत्सृज्य तां भार्यां विलप्य करुणं बहु॥
en: Befooled and deprived of his reason by Kali, Nala ran away deserting his sleeping wife and lainenting profusely and plaintively for her.

description: The desertion of Damayanti by Nala
sn: नष्टात्मा कलिना स्पृष्टस्तत् तद् विगणयन् नृपः। जगामैकां वने शून्ये भार्यामुत्सृज्य दुःखितः॥
en: Losing his senses through the influence of Kali and ruminating over a variety of thoughts, the king went away with his heart full of sorrow, forsaking his wife, alone, in that solitary wilderness.

description: The curse of Damayanti on the hunter
sn: वृहदश्व उवाच अपक्रान्ते नले राजन् दमयन्ती गतक्लमा। अबुध्यत वरारोहा संत्रस्ता विजने वने॥ अपश्यमाना भर्तारं शोकदुःखसमन्विता। प्राक्रोशदुच्चैः संत्रस्ता महाराजेति नैषधम्॥
en: Brihadashva said: O king, after Nala, had gone away, the slender-waisted Damayanti, getting over her fatigue, awoke in terror in that solitary wilderness. Terrified at not finding her husband and oppressed with grief and troubles, she called aloud for Naishadha, saying: O Maharaja.

description: The curse of Damayanti on the hunter
sn: हा नाथ हा महाराज हा स्वामिन् किं जहासि माम् हा हतास्मि विनष्टास्मि भीतास्मि विजने वने॥
en: O master! O mighty sovereign! O husband! why have you forsaken me? Alas! I am done for, I ain lost, I am (greatly) terrified in this lonely forest.

description: The curse of Damayanti on the hunter
sn: ननु नाम महाराजधर्मज्ञः सत्यवागसि। कथमुक्त्वा तथा सत्यं सुप्तामुत्सृज्य कानने॥
en: O mighty monarch! you are virtuous and truthful. How then, promising not to do so you have forsaken me asleep, in the woods?

description: The curse of Damayanti on the hunter
sn: कथमुत्सृज्य गन्तासि दक्षां भार्यामनुव्रताम्। विशेषतोऽनपकृते परेणापकृते सति॥
en: Why have you gone away forsaking your able and devoted, wife, specially when she had done you no harın, but you have been wronged by others?

description: The curse of Damayanti on the hunter
sn: शक्यसे ता गिरः सम्यक् कर्तुं मयि नरेश्वर। यास्तेषां लोकपालानां संनिधौ कथिताः पुरा॥
en: O lord of your people! you ought faithfully to fulfill those words of yours in respect of mc, that you had uttered in days gone by, before the guardian deities of the worlds.

description: The curse of Damayanti on the hunter
sn: नाकाले विहितो मृत्युर्मानां पुरुषर्षभ। तत्र कान्ता त्वयोत्सृष्टा मुहूर्तमपि जीवति॥
en: O best of men! because mortals are not ordained to die before their appointed time, therefore, it is, that your beloved wife live even a moment after your abandonment of her.

description: The curse of Damayanti on the hunter
sn: पर्याप्तः परिहासोऽयमेतावान् पुरुषर्षभ। भीताहमतिदुर्धर्ष दर्शयात्मानमीश्वर॥
en: O foremost of men! enough of this joke, let us have no more of it. O invincible one! I am awfully frightened. O lord! show yourself.

description: The curse of Damayanti on the hunter
sn: दृश्यसे दृश्यसे राजन्नेष दृष्टोऽसि नैषध। आवार्य गुल्मैरात्मानं किं मां न प्रतिभाषसे॥
en: You are discovered O king! you discovered! O ruler of the Nishadhas I have scen you! concealing yourself behind the corpses, why do you not answer me?

description: The curse of Damayanti on the hunter
sn: नृशंसं बत राजेन्द्र यन्मामेवंगतामिह। विलपन्तीं समागम्य नाश्वासयसि पार्थिव॥
en: Alas, O king of kings! it is very cruel of you. For sceing me in this and so bewailing, you do not, O king, come near to console me.

description: The curse of Damayanti on the hunter
sn: न शोचाम्यहमात्मानं न चान्यदपि किंचन। कथं नु भवितास्येक इति त्वां नृप शोचिमि॥
en: I lament not for myself, nor for any thing else. But, O king, I only grieve thinking, how you will live alone.

description: The curse of Damayanti on the hunter
sn: कथं नु राजंस्तृषितः क्षुधितः श्रमकर्षितः। सायाह्ने वृक्षमूलेषु मामपश्यन् भविष्यसि॥
en: O king! when, in the evening you will sit thirsty, hungry and worn out with toils under the trees, how will you live without seeing ine (by your side)?

description: The curse of Damayanti on the hunter
sn: ततः सा तीव्रशोकार्ता प्रदीप्तेव च मन्युना। इतश्चेतश्च रुदती पर्यधावत दुःखिता॥
en: Then oppressed with poignant grief and burning with anger, the miserable Damayanti began to run hither and thither bewailing.

description: The curse of Damayanti on the hunter
sn: मुहुरुत्पतते बाला मुहुः पतति विह्वला। मुहुरालीयते भीता मुहुः क्रोशति रोदिति॥
en: At times the youthful princess would stand up suddenly. At other times she would sink down bewildered. Now she would conceal herself alarmed and the next moment, she would cry and wail aloud.

description: The curse of Damayanti on the hunter
sn: अतीव शोकसंतप्ता मुहुनि:श्वस्य विह्वला। उवाच भैमी निःश्वस्य रुदत्यथ पतिव्रता॥
en: Then the chaste daughter of Bhima, bewildered and afflicted with heavy grief and sighing again and again, spoke weeping:

description: The curse of Damayanti on the hunter
sn: यस्याभिशापाद् दुःखार्तो दुःखं विन्दति नैषधः। तस्य भूतस्य नो दुःखाद् दुःखमप्यधिकं भवेत्॥
en: ‘May that being suffer grief greater than ours, through whose curse the afflicted king of the Nishadhas bear this woc!'

description: The curse of Damayanti on the hunter
sn: अपापचेतसं पापो य एवं कृतवान् नलम्। तस्माद् दुःखतरं प्राप्य जीवत्वसुखजीविकाम्॥
en: May that sinful wretch, who has reduced Nala of pious heart into this plight, live a more miserable life than his (Nala's) own, fraught with such greater woes.'

description: The curse of Damayanti on the hunter
sn: एवं तु विलपन्ती सा राज्ञो भार्या महात्मनः। अन्वेषमाणा भर्तारं वने श्वापदसेविते॥ उन्मत्तवद् भीमसुता विलपन्ती इतस्ततः। हा हा राजनिति मुहुरितश्चेतश्चधावति॥
en: Thus bewailing, the consort of that highsouled monarch began to search her dear lord in that forest, infested with wild beasts. Thus continuously lamenting, the daughter of Bhima ran hither and thither like an insane person, crying aloud, 'alas alas O king.'

description: The curse of Damayanti on the hunter
sn: तां क्रन्दमानामत्यर्थं कुररीमिव वाशतीम्। करुणं बहु शोचन्तीं विलपन्तीं मुहुर्मुहुः सहसाभ्यागतां भैमीमभ्याशपरिवर्तिनीम्। जग्राहाजगरो ग्राहो महाकायः क्षुधान्वितः॥
en: As she was crying aloud and bitterly lamenting like a female osprey, grieving profusely in piteous words and bewailing again and again, a huge and hungry serpent suddenly scized the daughter of Bhima, who camc and rolled near it.

description: The curse of Damayanti on the hunter
sn: सा ग्रस्यमाना ग्राहेण शोकेन च परिप्लुता। नात्मानं शोचति तथा यथा शोचति नैषधम्॥
en: Being devoured by the monster and swelling with sorrow, she grieved not so much for herself, as for the king of the Nishadhas.

description: The curse of Damayanti on the hunter
sn: हा नाथ मामिह वने ग्रस्यामानामनाथवत्। ग्राहेणानेन विजने किमर्थं नानुधावसि॥
en: 'O lord! why do you not run after me, seeing that I am swallowed by this huge serpent like one helpless, in this desolate wilderness?

description: The curse of Damayanti on the hunter
sn: कथं भविष्यसि पुनर्मामनुस्मृत्य नैषधा कथं भवाञ्जगामाद्य मामुत्सृज्य वने प्रभो॥
en: O king of the Nishadhas! how will you live, when you shall remember me (when I am gone)? O master! how have you gone away today forsaking me in the woods?

description: The curse of Damayanti on the hunter
sn: पापान्मुक्तः पुनर्लब्ध्वा बुद्धिं चेतोधनानि च। श्रान्तस्य ते क्षुधार्तस्य परिग्लानस्य नैषध। कः श्रमं राजशार्दूल नाशयिष्यति तेऽनघ॥
en: How will you live without me, when liberated from your curse, you will regain your mind, senses and wealth? O lord of the Nishadhas! O sinless one! O foremost of kings! who will remove your fatigue when you will be worn out with toil, oppressed with hunger and depressed with grief?'

description: The curse of Damayanti on the hunter
sn: ततः कश्चिन्मृगव्याधो विचरन् गहने वने। आक्रन्दमानां संश्रुत्य जवेनाभिससार ह॥
en: Then a hunter who was roaming in the deep forest, hearing the sound of her loud wailing's speedily came near her.

description: The curse of Damayanti on the hunter
sn: तां तु दृष्ट्वा तथा ग्रस्तामुरगेणायतेक्षणाम्। त्वरमाणो मृगव्याधः समभिक्रम्य वेगतः॥ मुखतः पाटयामास शस्त्रेण निशितेन च। निर्विचेष्टं भुजङ्गं तं विशस्य मृगजीवनः॥ मोक्षयित्वा स तां व्याधः प्रक्षाल्य सलिलेन ह। समाश्वास्य कृताहारामथ पप्रच्छ भारत॥
en: The hunter, who live upon the proceeds of hunting, seeing that large-eyed one swallowed up by a serpent, came up with haste and speed and dispatching that inert snake with a sharpedged weapon, tore it open from its mouth. Then O Bharata! the hunter freeing her from the coils of the serpent and washing her with water and consoling her, asked her when she had taken some food.

description: The curse of Damayanti on the hunter
sn: कस्य त्वं मृगशावाक्षि कथं चाभ्यागता वनम्। कथं चेदं महत् कृच्छ्रे प्राप्तवत्यसि भाविनि॥
en: 'O you having cyes like those of a young gazelle! whose are you! Why also have you entered into this forest? O handsome one! how have you fallen in this great predicament?'

description: The curse of Damayanti on the hunter
sn: दमयन्ती तथा तेन पृच्छ्यमाना विशाम्यते। सर्वमेतद् यथावृत्तमाचचक्षेऽस्य भारत॥
en: O lord of your people! O descendant of Bharata's race! thus questioned by him, Damayanti, related unto him precisely, all that had occurred.

description: The curse of Damayanti on the hunter
sn: तामर्धवस्त्रसंवीतां पीनश्रोणिपोधराम्। सुकुमारानवद्याडी पूर्णचन्द्रनिभाननाम्॥ अरालपक्ष्मनयनां तथा मधुरभाषिणीम्। लक्षयित्वा मृगव्याधः कामस्य वशमीयिवान्॥
en: The huntsman, seeing her, covered with half a piece of a cloth, with heaving breasts and shapely lips, with delicate and faultless limbs, with countenance resembling the full moon, with cyes furnished with graceful eye-lashes and with words very pleasing, was made the slave of the god of love.

description: The curse of Damayanti on the hunter
sn: तामेवं श्लक्ष्णया वाचा लुब्धको मृदुपूर्वया। सान्त्वयामास कामार्तस्तदबुध्यत भाविनी॥
en: Inflamed with lust, the hunter comforted her mildly and in smooth words. But the graceful Damayanti soon saw through his purposes.

description: The curse of Damayanti on the hunter
sn: दमयन्त्यपि तं दुष्टमुपलभ्य पतिव्रता। तीव्ररोषसमाविष्टा प्रजज्वालेव मन्युना॥
en: The chaste Damayanti then understanding the intentions of this evil-minded one, possessed with fierce rage, seemed to blaze forth in anger.

description: The curse of Damayanti on the hunter
sn: स तु पायमतिः क्षुद्रः प्रधर्षयितुमातुरः। दुर्धर्षां तर्कयामासा दीप्तामग्निशिखामिव॥
en: That evil minded one, having waxed irascible and fired with desire, endeavoured to insult her (by force) who was unconquerable even as a flame of blazing fire.

description: The curse of Damayanti on the hunter
sn: दमयन्ती तु दुःखार्ता पतिराज्यविनाकृता। अतीतवाक्पथे काले शशापैनं रुषान्विता॥
en: Then Damayanti afflicted with sorrow and deprived of her husband and kingdom, bursting with rage, cursed the huntsman when he had passed the limit of being checked by words.

description: The curse of Damayanti on the hunter
sn: यद्यहं नैषधादन्यं मनसापि न चिन्तये। तथायं पततां क्षुद्रो परासुर्मुगजीवनः॥
en: 'If even in my mind I have never thought of any other person than the king of the Nishadhas, then let this puny one living by। hunting, fall down devoid of life.

description: The curse of Damayanti on the hunter
sn: उक्तमात्रे त वचने तथा स मृगजीवनः। व्यसुः पपात मेदिन्यामग्निदग्ध इव दुमः॥
en: No sooner did she utter these words, than that one subsisting on chase, fell down dead on the ground, even as a tree consumed by fire.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: बृहदश्व उवाच सा निहत्य मृगव्याधं प्रतस्थे कमलेक्षणा। वनं प्रतिभयं शून्यं झिल्लिकागणनादितम्॥
en: Brihadashva said: Thus having slain the huntsman she, of eyes resembling lotus leaves, entered deeper and deeper into that desolate and dreadful forest, echoing with the jingling of crickets.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: सिंहद्वीपिरुरुव्याघ्रमहिषर्क्षगणैर्युतम्। नानापक्षिगणाकीर्णं म्लेच्छतस्करसेवितम्॥
en: That forest full of lions, leopards, Rurus tigers, buffaloes, bear and deer; swarming with various kinds of birds; inhabited by robbers and low hybrid tribes.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: शालवेणुधवाश्वत्थतिन्दुकेगदकिंशुकैः। अर्जुनारिष्टसंछन्नं स्यन्दनैश्च सशाल्मलैः॥ जम्ब्वाम्रलोध्रखदिरसालवेत्रसमाकुलम्। पद्मकामलकप्लक्षकदम्बोदुम्बरावृतम्॥ बदरीबिल्वसंछन्नं न्यग्रोधैश्च समाकुलम्। प्रियालतालखर्जूरहरीतकबिभीतकैः॥
en: Containing Salas bamboos, Dhabas, Asavathas. Tindukas Ingudas Kinsukas, Arjunas, Aristhas Sundanas together with Salmalas; abounding in Tumbus, mango trees, Lodras the catechu, the cane and Salas; overgrown with Padmakas, Amlakas, Plakhas, Kadamvas, Uduinvaras; covered with Badaris, Vilvas and banians, Piyalas, palms, date-trees, Haritakis and Vivitakas.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: नानाधानुशतैर्नद्धान् विविधानपि चाचलान्। निकुञ्जान् परिसंघुष्टान् दरीश्चाद्भुतदर्शनाः॥
en: She (Damayanti) saw, many mountains containing mines of different kinds of metals, groves singing with the notes of birds; many valleys of beautiful sight.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: नदीः सरांसि वापीश्च विविधांश्च मृगद्विजान्। सा बहून् भीमरूपांश्च पिशाचोरगराक्षसान्॥ पल्वलानि तडागानि गिरिकूटानि सर्वशः। सरितो निर्झराश्चैव ददर्शाद्भुतदर्शनान्॥
en: Many rivers, lakes, expanses of water and various kinds of birds and beasts; large number of serpents, Rakshasas and goblins of frightful figures; and pools, tanks, mountain-peaks on all sides; and streams and cataracts of picturesque appearance.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: यूथशो ददृशे चात्र विदर्भाधिपनन्दिनी। महिषांश्च वराहांश्च ऋक्षांश्च वनपन्नगान्॥ तेजसा यशसा लक्ष्म्या स्थित्या च परया युता। वैदर्भी विचरत्येका नलमन्वेषती तदा॥
en: There the daughter of the king of the Vidharbhas, saw, herd after herd, of buffaloes, boars and bears and numberless wild snakes. Possessed of energy, glory, beauty and high dignity, the princess of the Vidharbhas then began to roam alone in that wilderness, in quest of Nala.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: नाबिभ्यत् सा नृपसुता भैमी तत्राथ कस्यचित्। दारुणामटवीं प्राप्य भर्तृव्यसनपीडिता॥
en: Afflicted at her husband's calamity and having entered into that fearful forest, that princess, the daughter of Bhima, was not afraid of anything.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: विदर्भतनया राजन् विललाप सुदुःखिता। भर्तृशोकपरीताङ्गी शिलातलमथाश्रिता॥
en: O King! the royal daughter of the king of the Vidharbhas, seating herself down on the surface of a stone, greatly aggrieved and with her limbs trembling with sorrow for her husband, thus lamented.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: दमयन्त्युवाच व्यूढोरस्क महाबाहो नैषधानां जनाधिप। क्व नु राजन् गतोऽस्यद्य विसृज्यविजने वने॥ अश्वमेधादिभिर्वीर क्रतुभिर्भूरिदक्षिणैः। कथमिष्ट्वा नरव्याघ्र मयि मिथ्या प्रवर्तसे॥
en: Damayanti said “O you of expanded breast! O you of long arms! O protector of the Nishadha people! O king! whither have you gone today forsaking me in this desolate wilderness? O hero! O foremost of men! it does not behove you, who have performed the horse-sacrifice and various other sacrifices accompanied by profuse Dakshinas, to play false with myself.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: यत् त्वयोक्तं नरश्रेष्ठ तत् समक्षं महाद्युते। स्मर्तुमर्हसि कल्याणा वचनं पार्थिवर्षभ॥
en: O foremost of men! O auspicious one! O your of blazing lustre! O excellent of kings! you ought to remember the words you did utter in my presence.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: यच्चोक्तं विहगैर्हसैः समीपे तव भूभिप। मत्समक्षं यदुक्तं च तदवेक्षितुमर्हसि॥
en: O ruler of earth! you ought also to remember what the sky-ranging swans said before you and also what they declared before me.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: चत्वार एकतो वेदाः साङ्गोपाङ्गाः सविस्तराः। स्वधीता मनुजव्याघ्र सत्यमेकं किलैकतः॥
en: O foremost of men! surely the performance of one single promise on one side, weighs equal with the study of the four Vedas in all their extent and the Angas and Upangas taken together, on the other.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: तस्मादर्हसि शत्रुघ्न सत्यं कर्तुं नरेश्वर। उक्तवानसि यद् वीर मत्सकाशे पुरा वचः॥
en: "Therefore, O slayer of your adversaries! O lord of men! O brave one! you ought to fulfill your promise, that you did make before, in my presence.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: हा वीर नल नामाहं नष्टा किल तवानघा अस्यामटव्यां घोरायां किं मां न प्रतिभाषसे॥
en: Alas O hero! O Nala! verily am I done for in this wood, although I belong to you. O sinless one! wherefore do you not answer me lost in this dreary forest?

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: कर्षयत्येष मां रौद्रो व्यात्तास्यो दारुणाकृतिः। अरण्यराट् क्षुधाविष्टः किं मां न त्रातुमर्हसि॥
en: This fearful sylvan sovereign, of expanded jaws and frightful figure and oppressed with hunger, is distressing me. Do it not befit you to save me?

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: न मे त्वदन्या काचिद्धि प्रियास्तीत्यब्रवीः सदा। तामृतां कुरु कल्याण पुरोक्तां भारती नृप॥
en: You did always use to say, 'Except yourself, there is none dear unto me' O auspicious one! O king! prove the truth of that assertion you did make previously.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: उन्मत्तां विलपन्ती मां भार्यामिष्टां नराधिप। ईप्सितामीप्सितोऽसि त्वं किं मां न प्रतिभाषसे॥
en: O ruler of men! wherefore do you not answer me, your dear wife, raft of reason and bewailing you, although you love her and are loved in return?

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: कृशां दीनां विवर्णां च मलिनां वसुधाधिय। वस्त्रार्धप्रावृतामेकां विलपन्तीमनाथवत॥ यूथभ्रष्टामिवैकां मां हरिणीं पृथुलोचन। न मानयसि मामार्य रुदन्तीमरिकर्शन॥
en: O monarch! O respected one, O repressor of your enemies! wherefore do you not behold me, O large-eyed one, lean, emaciated, distressed, discolored desolate, bewailing like one helpless, weeping, covered with one piece of cloth and resembling a lovely does strayed out of the herd.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: महाराज महारण्ये अहमेकाकिनी सती। दमयन्त्यभिभाषे त्वां किं मां न प्रतिभाषसे।॥
en: O mighty monarch! in this vast wilderness I, your best-loved Damayanti, now forlorn and forsaken, am calling out your name; why do you not answer me?

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: कुलशीलोपसम्पन्न चारुसर्वाङ्गशोभन। नाद्य त्वां प्रतिपश्यामि गिरावस्मिन् नरोत्तम॥
en: O foremost of men! I do not find you, this day, on this mountain, who are possessed of a noble lineage and an excellent) character and shapely limbs enhancing your personal beauty.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: वने चास्मिन् महाघोरे सिंहव्याघ्रनिषेविते। शयानमुपविष्टं वा स्थितं वा निषधाधिय॥ प्रस्थितं वा नरश्रेष्ठ मम शोकविवर्धन। कं नु पृच्छामि दुःखार्ता त्वदर्थे शोककर्शिता॥
en: O ruler of the Nishadhas! O foremost of men! ( you who are adding to my grief in this fearful wilderness infested by lions and tigers, of whom shall I, woeful and distressed with grief on your account, enquire whether you are sitting or lying down or staying or gone?

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: कच्चिद् दृष्टस्त्वयारण्ये संगत्येह नलो नृपः। को नु मे वाथ प्रष्टव्यो वनेऽस्मिन् प्रस्थितं नलम्॥
en: Whom shall I ask, 'Have you seen king Nala ranging in these woods? Of whom shall I enquire about the royal Nala lost in this wilderness?

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: अभिरूपं महात्मानं परव्यूहविनाशनम्। यमन्वेषसि राजानं नलं पद्मनिभेक्षणम्॥ अयं स इति कस्याद्य श्रोष्यामि मधुरां गिरम्।
en: From whose lips shall I this day hear these honeyed words viz. 'That graceful and highsouled king Nala of eyes resembling lotus leaves, the slayer of hostile troops, in quest of whom you are wandering in this forest, is staying even here.'

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: अरण्यराडयं श्रीमांश्चतुर्दष्ट्रो महाहनुः॥ शार्दूलोऽभिमुखोऽभ्येति व्रजाम्येनमशङ्किता। भवान् मृगाणामधिपस्त्वमस्मिन् कानने प्रभुः॥
en: Yonder come the handsome sovereign of the forests, the tiger having four teeth and protruding jaws. Even unto him shall I repair fearlessly. You are the lord of beasts. You are the king of this forest.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: विदर्भराजतनयां दमयन्तीति विद्धि माम्। निषधाधिपतेर्भार्यां नलस्यामित्रघातिनः॥
en: Damayanti said : Know me for Damayanti, the daughter of the king of the Vidharbhas and the wife of Nala the king of the Nishadhas and the slayer of his foes.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: पतिमन्वेषतीमेकां कृपणां शोककर्शिताम्। आश्वासय मृगेन्द्रेह यदि दृष्टस्त्वया नलः॥
en: O lord of animals! console me-who am, alone seeking my husband, distressed and woestricken-with the news of Nala if you have at all seen him.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: अथवा त्वं वनपते नलं यदि न शंससि। मां खादय मृगश्रेष्ठ दुःखादस्माद् विमोचय॥
en: O lord of this forest! on the other hand, if you know nothing of Nala, then, O foremost of animals, devour me up and thereby relieve me from this misery.'

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: श्रुत्वारण्ये विलपितं न मामाश्वासयत्ययम्। यात्येतां स्वादुसलिलामापगां सागरंगमाम्॥
en: Hearing me bewailing in this wilderness, this forest king himself, is wending towards the rivulet containing tasteful water that is rolling towards the sea.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: इमं शिलोच्चयं पुण्यं शृङ्गैर्बहुभिरुच्छ्रितैः। विराजद्भिरिवानेकै कवणमनोरमैः॥
en: I shall now for the tidings of the kings, ask yonder king of mountains, adorned with various beautiful and many hued peaks reaching the skies.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: नानाधातुसमाकीर्णं विविधोपलभूषितम्। अस्यारण्यस्य महतः केतुभूतमिवोत्थितम्॥
en: Containing heaps of sacred rocks; replete with many kinds of metals; decked with diverse pieces of stones; flowing like streamer over this wide wilderness.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: सिंहशार्दूलमातङ्गवराह‘मृगायुतम्। पतत्रिभिर्बहुविधैः समन्तादनुनादितम्॥
en: Haunted by lions, tigers, elephants, boars, bears and deers; ringing on all sides with the notes of various kinds of birds.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: किंशुकाशोकबकुलपुन्नागैरुपशोभितम्। कर्णिकारधवप्लक्षैः सुपुष्पैरुपशोभितम्॥
en: The mountain graced with Kinsukas, Asokas, Bakulas and Tannagas; beautified with, Karnikaras Dhabas and Plakshas bearing blossoms.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: सरिद्भिः सविहङ्गाभिः शिखरैश्च समाकुलम्। गिरिराजमिमं तावत् पृच्छामि नृपतिं प्रति॥
en: The mountain abounding in rivers infested by water fowls; and decorated with crested summits. Now I ask about king Nala from the king of mountain.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: भगवनचलश्रेष्ठ दिव्यदर्शन विश्रुत्। शरण्य बहुकल्याण नमस्तेऽस्तु महीधर॥
