en: Damayanti said : O mighty and foremost of mountains! O you of picturesque appearance! O highly famous hill! O you shelter (of the distressed)! O highly blessed hill! O you pillar of the Earth! I salute you.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: प्रणमाम्यभिगम्याहं राजपुत्रीं निबोध माम्। राज्ञः स्नुषां राजभार्यां दमयन्तीति विश्रुताम्॥
en: Approaching I bow down unto you. Know me for a kings' daughter, a king's daughter-inlaw, a king's wife and for Damayanti by name.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: राजा विदर्भाधिपति: पिता मम महारथः। भीमो नाम क्षितिपतिश्चातुर्वर्ण्यस्य रक्षिता॥
en: The royal Bhima, the ruler of the Vidharbhas, the great warrior, the lord of the Earth and the protector of the four different orders, is my sire.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: राजसूयाश्वमेधानां क्रतूनां दक्षिणावताम्। आहर्ता पार्थिवश्रेष्ठः पृथुचार्वञ्चितेक्षणः॥ ब्रह्मण्यः साधुवृत्तश्च सत्यवागनसूयकः। शीलवान् वीर्यसम्पन्नः पृथुश्रीधर्मविच्छुचिः॥ सम्यग् गोप्ता विदर्भाणां निर्जितारिगणः प्रभुः। तस्य मां विद्धि तनयां भगवंस्त्वामुपस्थिताम्॥
en: That foremnost of the descendants of Prithu, performed the Rajasuya sacrifice and the horse-sacrifice accompanied by profuse Dakshinas. Possessing large and beautiful eyes graced with arching brows, well-versed in the Vedas, of pious nature, true-speaking, free from jealously, of good character, endued with prowess, of immense prosperity, acquainted with all morality and pure, that lord defeating all his adversaries completely protect the people of Vidharbha. O mighty one! know me to be his daughter thus approaching you.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: निषधेषु महाराजः श्वशुरो मे नरोत्तमः। गृहीतनामा विख्यातो वीरसेन इति स्म ह॥
en: My father-in-law, the foremost of men, was the illustrious sovereign ruling over the Nishadhas. He was known under the name of Virasena and was of high renown.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: तस्य राज्ञः सुतो वीरः श्रीमान् सत्यपराक्रमः। क्रमप्राप्तं पितुः स्वं यो राज्यं समनुशास्ति ह॥ नलो नामारिहा श्यामः पुण्यश्लोक इति श्रुतः। ब्रह्मण्यो वेदविद् वाग्मी पुण्यकृत् सोमपोऽग्निमान्।। यष्टा दाता च योद्धा च सम्यक् चैव प्रशासिता। तस्य मामबलां श्रेष्ठां विद्धि भार्यामिहागताम्॥ त्यक्तश्रियं भर्तृहीनामनाथां व्यसनान्विताम्। अन्वेषमाणां भर्तारं त्वं मां पर्वतसत्तम॥
en: The son of this king, a mighty warrior, possessed of prosperity and of infallible prowess, who govern well the kingdom that he had inherited from his father, is known under the name of Nala of holy fame, of complexion like molten gold. He is respectful towards Brahmanas, versed in the Vedas, eloquent and performer of meritorious deeds; he is used to the drinking of Soma and the worship of Fire; he celebrates sacrifices, is immensely charitable and heroic and a just chastiser (of sinful) men. Know me for his principal consort now helpless and come unto you. O excellent of mountains! devoid of prosperity, deprived of the company of my husband, helpless and distressed with affliction, in quest of my lord I have approached you.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: समुल्लिखद्भिरेतैर्हि त्वया शृङ्गशतैर्नृपः। कच्चिद् दृष्टोऽचलश्रेष्ठ वनेऽस्मिन् दारुणेनलः॥
en: O foremost of mountains! by means of your hundred peaks reaching the skies, have you seen anywhere in this dreary wilderness the royal Nala?

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: गजेन्द्रविक्रमोधीमान् दीर्घबाहुरमर्षणः। विक्रान्तः सत्त्ववान् वीरो भर्ता मम महायशाः॥ निषधानामधिपतिः कच्चिद् दृष्टस्त्वया नलः। विपलतीं किमेकां मां पर्वतश्रेष्ठ विह्वलाम्॥
en: Have you anywhere seen the heroic and unconquerable Nala, my husband, the ruler of the Nishadhas, with the gait of an elephant of great intelligence, having long arms, of illustrious renown, endued with prowess and possessed of energy? O best of mountains! seeing me desolate and lamenting and fainting (with grief) wherefore do you not console me by speaking to me as your own afflicted daughter.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: गिरानाश्वासयस्यद्य स्वां सुतामिव दुःखिताम्। वीर विक्रान्तधर्मज्ञ सत्यसंध महीपते॥
en: O hero! O you of great prowess! O you versed in righteousness! O veracious one! O lord of the earth! if you are present in this forest then, O king! show yourself unto me?

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: यद्यस्यस्मिन् वने राजन् दर्शयात्मानमात्मना। कदा सुस्निग्धगम्भीरां जीमूतस्वनसंनिभाम्॥ श्रोष्यामि नैषधस्याहं वाचं ताममृतोपमाम्। वैदर्भीत्येव विस्पष्टां शुभां राज्ञो महात्मनः॥ आम्नायसारिणीमृद्धां मम शोकविनाशिनीम्। भीतामाश्वासयत मां नृपतेधर्मवत्सल॥
en: When shall I again hear the words of the royal and high-souled Nala, sweet and sonorous and resembling the rumbling of clouds and delicious like nectar and calling me the “princess of the Vidharbhas" with distinct and holy accents and spoken according to the precepts of the Vedas and eloquent and soothing all my grief. O king! O righteous one, it behoove you to comfort me, who am greatly terror-stricken."

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: इति सा तं गिरिश्रेष्ठमुक्त्वा पार्थिवनन्दिनी। दमयन्ती ततो भूयो जगाम दिशमुत्तराम्॥
en: Having spoken in the above manner to the foremost of mountains, the princess Damayanti again roamed towards the northern quarters.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: सा गत्वा तीनहोरात्रान् ददर्श परमाङ्गना। तापसारण्यमतुलं दिव्यकाननशोभितम्॥ वसिष्ठभृग्वत्रिसमैस्तापसैरुपशोभितम्। नियतैः संयताहारैर्दमशौचसमन्वितैः॥ अब्भक्षैर्वायुभक्षैश्च पत्राहारैस्तथैव च। जितेन्द्रियैर्महाभागैः स्वर्गमार्गदिदृक्षुभिः॥ वल्कलाजिनसंवीतैर्मुनिभिः संयतेन्द्रियैः। तापसाध्युषितं रम्यं ददर्शाश्रममण्डलम्॥ नानामृगगणैर्जुष्टं शाखामृगगणायुतम्। तापसैः समुपेतं च सा दृष्ट्वैव समाश्वसत्॥
en: That supremely beautiful damsel, after having wandered for three whole days and nights, saw an incomparable woody retreat of ascetics, furnished with beautiful gardens, inhabited by anchorites, like Vasishtha, Bhrigu and Atri, self-governed and abstemious, performing the ten prescribed purifactory rites; some living on water, some on air and some on (fallen) leaves, with passions under thorough control, of eminent parts, secking the way to Heaven, wearing barks of trees and skins of deer and with senses held in check. She saw that charming hermitage inhabited by the ascetics and abounding in various species of animals and swarming with monkeys and graced by the presence of hermits and she was comforted (with the sight).

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: सुभूः सुकेशी सुश्रोणी सुकुचा सुद्विजानना। वर्चस्विनी सुप्रतिष्ठा स्वसितायतलोचना॥ सा विवेशाश्रमपदं वीरसेनसुतप्रिया। योषिद्रत्नं महाभागा दमयन्ती तपस्विनी॥
en: That dear-loved spouse of the son of Virasena; that best of damsels, the pitiable Damayanti of eminent parts, of black and large eyes, of beaming splendour and pure fame, having long tresses, a dainty waist, heaving breasts, graceful eye-brows and a face adorned with pearly teeth, then entered into that asylum of ascetics.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: साभिवाद्य तपोवृद्धान् विनयावनता स्थिता। स्वागतं त इति प्रोक्ता तैः सर्वैस्ताप्रसोत्तमैः॥
en: She, saluting those sages grown old in the practice of austerities, stood in an attitude of humility. In that forest she was offered 'welcome' by those ascetics.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: पूजां चास्या यथान्यायं कृत्वा तत्र तपोधनाः। आस्यतामित्यथोचुस्ते ब्रूहि किं करवामहे॥
en: Then those ascetics, offering due adoration unto her, said, 'Sit yourself down and speak what shall we do for you?”

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: तानुवाच वरारोहा कच्चिद् भगवतामिह। तपःस्वग्निषुधर्मेषु मृगपक्षिषु चानघाः॥ कुशलं वो महाभागाः स्वधर्माचरणेषु च। तैरुक्ता कुशलं भद्रे सर्वत्रेति यशस्विनि॥
en: That damsel of delicate loins replied unto them saying, 'O sinless ones! O you of eminent parts! is everything progressing well regarding your rigid austerities, (sacrificial). Fires, your righteousness, the religious rites of your own sect and the birds and beasts of this herinitage?” And they answered her saying, 'O illustrious lady! O blessed one! prosperity attend us in every respect.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: ब्रूहि सर्वानवद्याङ्गि का त्वं किं च चिकीर्षसि। दृष्ट्वैव ते परं रूपं द्युतिं च परमामिह॥ विस्मयो नः समुत्पन्न: समाश्वसिहि मा शुचः। अस्यारण्यस्य देवी त्वमुताहोऽस्य महीभृतः॥
en: O you of faultless limbs! tell us who are you and what do you scek? We are amazed seeing your great beauty and your extreme splendour. Be consoled and do not grieve. O faultless one! O blessed one! say whether you are the presiding deity of this forest or of this mountain or of this rivulet? Speak the truth!”

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: अस्याश्च नद्याः कल्याणि वद सत्यमनिन्दिते। साव्रवीत् तानृपीन् नाहमरण्यस्यास्य देवता॥ न चाप्यस्य गिरेविप्रा नैव नद्याश्च देवता। मानुषीं मां विजानीत यूयं सर्वे तपोधनाः॥
en: She said unto the sages, “O twice-born ones! neither am I the deity of this forest, nor the goddess of this mountain, nor of this river. Know me for a daughter of human beings, O you sages of ascetic wealth! I am relating my history in detail, do you listen attentively to me.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: विस्तरेणाभिधास्यामि तन्मे शृणुत सर्वशः। विदर्भेषु महीपालो भीमो नाम महीपतिः॥
en: The ruler of the carth, Bhima by name, is the sovercign of the Vidharbhas, O foremost of twice-born ones! know me for his daughter.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: तस्य मां तनयां सर्वे जानीत द्विजसत्तमाः। निषधाधिपतिर्धीमान् नलो नाम महायशाः॥
en: The heroic, the ever-victorious (in battle), the learned lord of the Nishadhas, Nala by name, of illustrious fame, great intelligence and the ruler of men, is my husband.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: वीरः संचामजिद् विद्वान् मम भर्ता विशाम्पतिः। देवताभ्यर्चनपरो द्विजातिजनवत्सलः॥ गोप्ता निषधवंशस्य महातेजा महाबलः। सत्यवान्धर्मवित् प्राज्ञः सत्यसंधोऽरिमर्दनः॥ ब्रह्मण्यो दैवतरपरः श्रीमान् परपुरंजयः। नलो नाम नृपश्रेष्ठो देवराजसमद्युतिः॥ मम भर्ता विशालाक्षः पूर्णेन्दुवदनोऽरिहा। आहर्ता क्रतुमुख्यानां वेदवेदाङ्गपारगः॥
en: That foremost of kings named Nala, of splendour like unto that of the lord of the celestials, of large eyes and of face resembling the full moon, the destroyer of his foes, the worshipper of the gods, devoted to the Vedas, of great prosperity, the captor of his enemies' towns, the repressor of his foes, that veracious and wise being, acquainted with all religions, of truthful promise, of eminent energy and great prowess, the protector of the race of the Nishadhas, occupied in the adoration of the celestials, kind towards the regenerate ones is my husband. He is the celebrator of principal sacrifices and is versed in the Vedas and their branches and the slayer of his adversaries in battle. He resemble in lustre the sun and the moon.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: सपत्नानां मृधे हन्ता रविसोमसमप्रभः। स कैश्चिनिकृतिप्रज्ञैरनार्यैरकृतात्मभिः॥ आहूय पृथिवीपालः सत्यधर्मपरायणः। देवने कुशलैर्जिर्हितं राज्यं वसूनि च॥
en: This king devoted to truthfulness and ruler of the earth, was one day challenged to play a game at dice, by some mean-minded, vile and deceitful men of uncultivated soul and skillful in gambling. He was defeated and lost his wealth and kingdom.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: तस्य मामवगच्छध्वं भार्यां राजर्षभस्य वै। दमयन्तीति विख्यातां भर्तुर्दर्शनलालसाम्॥
en: Know me to be the consort of that foremost of kings, famous under the name of Damayanti and anxious to enjoy a sight of my missing husband.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: सा वनानि गिरीश्चैव सरांसि सरितस्तथा। पल्वलानि च सर्वाणि तथारण्यानि सर्वशः॥ अन्वेषमाणा भर्तारं नलं रणविशारदम्। महात्मानं कृतास्त्रं च विचरामीह दुःखिता॥
en: I am wandering through the length and breadth of this wood, over mountains, among rivers, lakes, tanks and expanses of water and forests, with a sorrowful heart, in quest of my lord Nala, versed in the tactics of war, skilled in the use of weapons and of high soul.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: कच्चिद् भगवतां रम्यं तपोवनमिदं नृपः। भवेत् प्राप्तो नलो नाम निषधानां जनाधिपः॥ यत्कृतेऽहमिदं ब्रह्मन् प्रपन्ना भृशदारुणम्। वनं प्रतिभयं घोरं शार्दूलमृगसेवितम्॥
en: Has the royal Nala, the ruler of the Nishadha people, for whom, O Brahmanas! afflicted, I am roaming in this dreadful and deep wilderness, full of terrible things and infested by tigers and other beasts of prey-visited this charming hermitage of your almighty selves!

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: यदि कैश्चिदहोरात्रैर्न द्रक्ष्यामि नलं नृपम्। आत्मानं श्रेयसा योक्ष्ये देहस्यास्य विमोचनात्॥
en: If within a few days and nights I do not see king Nala, I will secure my own welfare by renouncing this body.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: को नु मे जीवितेनार्थस्तमृते पुरुषर्षभम्। कथं भविष्याम्यद्याहं भर्तृशोकाभिपीडिता॥
en: What is the use of my life, separated as I have been, from that foremost of men? How shall I live today, afflicted with sorrow for my husband?"

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: तथा विलपतीमेकामरण्ये भीमनन्दिनीम्। दमयन्तीमथोचुस्ते तापसा: सत्यदर्शिनः॥
en: Those truth-seeing ascetics then said unto the forlorn Damayanti, the daughter of Bhima, who had been bewailing for her lord in the forest.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: उदर्कस्तव कल्याणि कल्याणो भविता शुभे। वयं पश्याम तपसा क्षिप्रं द्रक्ष्यसि नैषधम्॥
en: "O auspicious and blessed one! you shall attain to happiness in future. We see by our power of asceticism, that ere long you shall see Naishadha.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: निषधानामधिपति नलं रिपुनिपातिनम्। भैमिधर्मभृतां श्रेष्ठं द्रक्ष्यसे विगतज्वरम्॥ विमुक्तं सर्वपापेभ्यः सर्वरत्नसमन्वितम्। तदेव नगरं श्रेष्ठं प्रशासतमरिंदमम्॥ द्विषतां भयकर्तारं सुहृदां शोकनाशनम्। पतिं द्रक्ष्यसि कल्याणि कल्याणाभिजनं नृपम्॥
en: O daughter of king Bhima! you shall meet Nala, the Ruler of the Naishadhas, the slayer of his foes and the foremost of those who protect righteousness, with his fever of misery subsided. O blessed one! you shall see your royal husband purged of all sins, adorned with diverse kings' of gems, ruling the self-same excellent of towns, the subduer of his foes, the terror of his enemies, the destroyer of the grief of his friends and crowned with all blessings."

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: एवमुक्त्वा नलस्येष्टां महिषी पार्थिवात्मजाम्। अन्तर्हितास्तापसास्ते साग्निहोत्राश्रमास्तथा॥
en: Having thus spoken to that daughter of a king, the dear-loved queen of Nala, the ascetics, with their sacrificial fires and with the asylum itself, disappeared from sight.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: सा दृष्ट्वा महदाश्चर्यं विस्मिता ह्यभवत् तदा। दमयन्त्यनवद्याङ्गी वीरसेननृपस्नुषा॥
en: Seeing this wondrous phenomenon, Damayanti of faultless shape and limbs and the daughter-in-law of king Virasena became greatly amazed.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: किं नु स्वपो मया दृष्टः कोऽयं विधिरिहाभवत्। क्व नु ते तापसा: सर्वे क्व तदाश्रममण्डलम्॥
en: Did I dream a dream! what an event have occurred even now? Where are all those ascetics and where is that asylum (gone).

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: क्व सा पुण्यजला रम्या नदी द्विजनिषेविता। क्व नु ते ह नगा हृद्याः फलपुष्पोपशोभिताः॥
en: Where is that enchanting rivulet of holy waters, inhabited by water-fowls of various species? Where again are those delightful trees adorned with flowers and fruits?

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: ध्यात्वा चिरं भीमसुता दमयन्ती शुचिस्मिता। भर्तृशोकपरा दीना विवर्णवदनाभवत्॥१००।
en: Thus thinking for a while, Damayanti of pure smiles, the daughter of Bhima, indulging in grief for her husband and miserable, grew pale-faced.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: सा गत्वाथापरां भूमि बाष्पसंदिग्धया गिरा। विललापाश्रुपूर्णाक्षी दृष्ट्वाशोकतरुं ततः॥ ।
en: Thereafter wandering to another part of the forest and beholding there an Ashoka tree, she began to lament, her voice choked with the vapour of grief and her eyes overflowing with tears.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: उपगम्य तरुश्रेष्ठमशोकं पुष्पितं वने। पल्लवापीडितं हृद्यं विहङ्गैरनुनादितम्॥
en: She in that forest approached that foremost of trees, the Ashoka, bedecked with flowers, charming, loaded with thick foliage and echoing all round with the notes of birds.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: अहो बतायमगमः श्रीमानस्मिन् वनान्तरे। आपीडैर्बहुभिर्भाति श्रीमान् पर्वतराडिव॥
en: Oh! this charming tree in the heart of this wilderness ornamented with fruits and flowers, is shining like a glorious king of mountains.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: विशोकां कुरु मां क्षिप्रमशोक प्रियदर्शन। वीतशोकभयाबाधं कच्चित् त्वं दृष्टवान् नृपम्॥
en: "O Ashoka (this tree is fabled to discard the grief of those, who have a view of it)! do you speedily relieve me from my grief, O you of graceful appearance! Have you anywhere in this forest seen king Nala, freed from all grief and fear and unobstructed by any hindrance?

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: नलं नामारिदमनं दमयन्त्याः प्रियं पतिम्। निघधानामधिपतिं दृष्टवानसि मे प्रियम्॥ एकवस्त्रार्धसंवीतं सुकुमारतनुत्वचम्। व्यसनेनार्दितं वीरमरण्यमिदमागतम्॥
en: Have you seen the dear-loved husband of Damayanti, my best beloved one, by name Nala, the king of the Nishadhas, the subduer of his foes, wearing half a piece of cloth, of delicate body and skin and that warrior who, crushed under calamity, has repaired into this forest?

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: यथा विशोका गच्छेयमशोकनग तत् कुरु। सत्यनामा भवाशोक अशोकः शोकनाशनः॥
en: O Ashoka tree! so manage that I may go away from you relieved from all grief. O Ashoka! vindicate your denomination of Ashoka, which mean the destroyer of grief?"

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: एवं साशोकवृक्षं तमार्ता वै परिगम्य ह। जगाम दारुणतरं देशं भैमी वराङ्गना॥
en: That excellent of damsels the afflicted daughter of Bhima, then three-times going round the Ashoka tree, entered a more dreary part of the wilderness.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: सा ददर्श नगान् नैकान् नैकाश्च सरितस्तथा। नैकांश्च पर्वतान् रम्यान् नैकांश्च मृगपक्षिणः॥
en: She beheld many trees and many streams, many charming mountains and various kinds of birds and beasts.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: कन्दरांश्च नितम्बांश्च नदीश्चाद्भुतदर्शनाः। ददर्श तान् भीमसुता पतिमन्वेषती तदा॥
en: That daughter of Bhima saw, when roaming in quest of her husband, many caverns and ridges and rivulets of amazing sight.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: गत्वा प्रकृष्टमध्वानं दमयन्ती शुचिस्मिता। ददर्शाथ महासार्थं हस्त्यश्वरथसंकुलम्॥ उत्तरन्तं नदी रम्यां प्रसन्नसलिलां शुभाम्। सुशीततोयां विस्तीर्णां ह्रदिनीं वेतसैर्वृताम्॥ प्रो ष्टां क्रौञ्चकुररैश्च क्रवाकोपकूजिताम्। कूर्मचाहझषाकीर्णां विपुलद्वीपशोभिताम्॥
en: After Damayanti of pure smiles had proceeded a long way, she saw a large caravan of trades together with their horses cars and elephants landing on the banks of a broad, lovely, charming and delightful river, containing cool and clear water, covered with cane-bushes, resounding with cries of cranes and ospreys and ringing with the notes of the Chacrabaka and abounding in tortoises, alligators and fishes and adorned with a large number of small islands.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: सा दृष्ट्वैव महासार्थं नलपत्नी यशस्विनी। उपसर्प्य वरारोहा जनमध्यं विवेश ह॥ उन्मत्तरूपा शोकार्ता तथा वस्त्रार्धसंवृता। कृशा विवर्णा मलिना पांसुध्वस्तशिरोरुहा॥
en: As soon as the illustrious and delicatewaisted spouse of Nala, roving like an insane person, afflicted with grief, wearing half a piece of cloth, lean, discoloured and pale and with hair soiled with dust saw this great caravan, she approached it and entered into the midst of its people.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: तां दृष्ट्वा तत्र मनुजाः केचिद् भीताः प्रदुद्रुवुः। केचिच्चिन्तापरा जग्मुः केचित् तत्र विचुक्रुशुः॥
en: Seeing her in their midst, some people of the caravan began to fly in fear, some became greatly anxious and some began to cry aloud.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: प्रहसन्ति स्म तां केचिदभ्यसूयन्ति चापरे। अकुर्वत दयां केचित् पप्रच्छुश्चापि भारत॥
en: Some laughed at her, some began to hate her. Some showed kindness towards her and some, O Bharata, questioned her in the following manner.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: कासि कस्यासि कल्याणि किं वा मृगवसे वने। त्वां दृष्ट्वा व्यथिताः स्मेह कच्चित् त्वमसि मानुषी।
en: 'O blessed one! who are you and whom do you belong to? What seek you in this forest? Seeing you among us we are greatly anxious! Are you human?

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: वद सत्यं वनस्यास्य पर्वतस्याथवा दिशः। देवता त्वं हि कल्याणि त्वां वयं शरणं गताः॥
en: O blessed one! speak the truth, as to whether you are the deity presiding over this forest or the goddess of this mountain or of the cardinal quarters? We seek your shelter.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: यक्षी वा राक्षसी वा त्वमुताहोऽसि वराङ्गना। सर्वथा कुरु नः स्वस्ति रक्ष वास्माननिन्दिते॥ यथायं सर्वथा सार्थः क्षेमी शीघ्रमितो व्रजेत्। तथा विधत्स्व कल्याणि यथा श्रेयो हि नो भवेत्।।
en: Be you a female Yaksha or a female Rakshasa or a heavenly damsel, do good unto us and O blaimeless one! protect us completely. O blessed one! do you so ordain that, ere long, this caravan may start from this place attended with prosperity in every direction, as also that poor personal property may be secured.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: तथोक्ता तेन सार्थेन दमयन्ती नृपात्मजा। प्रत्युवाच ततः साध्वी भर्तृव्यसनपीडिता॥
en: Thus spoken to by the men of the caravan, the princess Damayanti, devoted to her husband and greatly oppressed with sorrow replied to them thus..

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: सार्थवाहं च सार्थं च जना ये चात्र केचन। युवस्थविरबालाश्च सार्थस्य च पुरोगमाः॥ मानुषीं मां विजानीत मनुजाधिपतेः सुताम्। नृपस्नुषां राजभार्यां भर्तृदर्शनलालसाम्॥
en: "O leader of the caravan, You traders, You men that belong to this caravan! You youths, you guides of this caravan! Know me for a female human being, a daughter of a royal parent, a daughter-in-law of a sovereign, spouse of a king and as one cager to have a sight of her husband.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: विदर्भराण्मम पिता भर्ता राजा च नैषधः। नलो नाम महाभागस्तं मृग्याम्यपराजितम्॥
en: The sovereign of Vidharbhas is my father, the illustrious Ruler of the Nishadhas is my husband, known under the name of Nala. Even now I am wandering in quest of that unconquerable one.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: यदि जानीत नृपतिं क्षिप्रं शंसत मे प्रियम्। नलं पुरुषशार्दूलममित्रगणसूदनम्॥
en: Tell me without delay if you have seen my beloved husband, king Nala, the foremost of men and the slayer of his enemies."

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: तामुवाचानवद्याङ्गीं सार्थस्य महतः प्रभुः। सार्थवाहः शुचिर्नाम शृणु कल्याणि मद्वचः॥
en: Thereupon the lord of that great caravan, the leader of it, by name Suchi, said unto that damsel of faultless limbs. "O blessed one! listen to my words."

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: अहं सार्थस्य नेता वै सार्थवाहः शुचिस्मिते। मनुष्यं नलनामानं न पश्यामि यशस्विनि॥
en: O you of pure smiles, I am a merchant and the guide of this caravan. O renowned lady, I have not seen any man bearing the name of Nala.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: कुञ्जरद्वीपिमहिषशार्दूलर्भमृगानपि। पश्याम्यस्मिन् वने कृत्स्ने ह्यमनुष्यनिषेविते॥
en: In this extensive wilderness, uninhabited by men, I see only elephants, leopards and buffaloes, as also tigers birds and other animals.

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: ऋते त्वां मानुषी मर्यं न पश्यामि महावने। तथा नो यक्षराडद्य मणिभद्रः प्रसीदतु॥
en: Save and except yourself I do not find any mortal in this terrible forest. So, may Manibhadra, the king of the Yakshas, be propitious on us this day!

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: साब्रवीद् वणिज: सर्वान् सार्थवाहं च तं ततः। क्व नु यास्यति सार्थोऽयमेतदाख्यातुमर्हसि॥
en: Thereupon she asked the merchants and the leader of the caravan, “You ought to tell me wither the caravan is going.'

description: In Damayanti's meeting with the caravan
sn: सार्थवाह उवाच सार्थोऽयं चेदिराजस्य सुबाहोः सत्यदर्शिन: क्षिप्रं जनपदं गन्ता लाभाय मनुजात्मजे॥
en: The leader of the Caravan said: O daughter of the foremost of men! for purposes of profit this caravan is going in haste 1O the rerritory of Subahu the truth-seeing king of the Chedis.

description: Damayanti's living in the house of the King of the Chedis
sn: बृहदश्व उवाच सा तच्छ्रुत्वानवद्याङ्गी सार्थवाहवचस्तदा। जगाम सह तेनैव सार्थेन पतिलालसा॥
en: Brihadashva said: Thereupon that beauteous lady, hearing the words of the leader of the caravan, went away with the company of travellers, hoping to find out her lord.

description: Damayanti's living in the house of the King of the Chedis
sn: अथ काले बहुतिथे वने महति दारुणे। तडागं सर्वतोभद्रं पद्मसौगन्धिकं महत्॥ ददृशुर्वणिजो रम्यं प्रभूतयवसेन्धनम्। बहुपुष्पफलोपेतं नानापक्षिनिषेवितम्॥ निर्मलस्वादुसलिलं मनोहारि सुशीतलम्। सुपरिश्रान्तवाहास्ते निवेशाय मनो दधुः॥
en: Thus many days passed over, when the merchants saw in the midst of that fearful and extensive forest a very large lake, which was all-beautiful, pregnant with lotuses, most delight-some, containing abundant grasses and fuels and also various sorts of delicious fruits and flowers (on its banks) and inhabited by several kinds of birds; and also finding the water of the lake to be pure and tasteful, most charming and cool, these tired traverllers made up their mind up stop there.

description: Damayanti's living in the house of the King of the Chedis
sn: सम्मते सार्थवाहस्य विविशुर्वनमुत्तमम्। उवास सार्थः सुमहान् वेलामासाद्य पश्चिमाम्॥
en: The caravan dispersed itself into the forest at the behest of its leader. But when the day (i.e., the sun) slanted down the west, that great company took its quarters there.

description: Damayanti's living in the house of the King of the Chedis
sn: अथार्धरात्रसमये नि:शब्दस्तिमिते तदा। सुप्ते सार्थे परिश्रान्ते हस्तियूथमुपागमत्॥ पानीपार्थं गिरिनदीं मदप्रस्रवणाविलाम्। अथापश्यत सार्थं तं सार्थजान् सुबहून् गजान्॥
en: Then, at midnight, when cverything was hushed and silence prevailed, the travellers fell into sleep, while there came a multitude of elephants. And while going to the mountain stream to drink its water, soiled by their own exudations, they saw the merchants as well as a good number of other elephants possessed by them.

description: Damayanti's living in the house of the King of the Chedis
sn: तान् चाम्यगजान् दृष्ट्वा सर्वे वनगजास्तदा। समाद्रवन्त वेगेन जिघांसन्तो मदोत्कटाः॥
en: Beholding those domesticated elephants, the wild ones, maddened at the fury, rushed towards them with the object of killing them, while the juice was exuding from their temples.

description: Damayanti's living in the house of the King of the Chedis
sn: तेषामापततां वेग: करिणां दुःसहोऽभवत्। नगाचादिव शीर्णानां शृङ्गाणां पततां क्षितौ।॥
en: The violence of the forward rush of these elephants became intolerable, even as the fall of the peaks, broken from the mountain tops, directed towards the ground.

description: Damayanti's living in the house of the King of the Chedis
sn: स्पन्दतामपि नागानां मार्गा नष्टा वनोद्भवाः। मार्ग संस्थ्य संसुप्तं पद्मिन्याः सार्थमुत्तमम्॥
en: The course of the rushing elephants through the paths of the woods was hindered, as the good caravan was sleeping, obstructing the way to the lake filled with lotuses.

description: Damayanti's living in the house of the King of the Chedis
sn: ते तं ममर्दुः सहसा चेष्टमानं महीतले। हाहाकारं प्रमुञ्चन्तः सार्थिकाः शरणार्थिनः॥ ते वनगुल्मांश्चधावन्तो निद्राधा बहवोऽभवन्। केचिद् दन्तैः करैः केचित् केचित् पद्भ्यां हता गजैः।।
en: The elephants, all on a sudden, crushed the caravan, which was sleeping in the ground. Then the merchants, uttering the cries of Ah! and Alas! sought for protection. Blinded by sleep, they all rushed towards the bushes and the forest (for protection). But some of them were killed by the tusks of those elephants and some by trunks, as also some were killed by their legs.

description: Damayanti's living in the house of the King of the Chedis
sn: निहतोष्ट्राश्वबहुलाः पदातिजनसंकुलाः। भयादाधावमानाश्च परस्परहतास्तदा॥ घोरान् नादान विमुञ्चन्तो निपेतुर्धरणीतले। वृक्षेष्वारुह्य संरब्धाः पतिता विषमेषु च॥
en: Thus a large number of camels and horses was killed; as also the countless men, who were on their legs, killed one another, as they were all rushing in terror. Several of the merchants, who were crying loudly, fell down on the surface of the earth; several others climbed on trees; and some again fell down on uneven ground.

description: Damayanti's living in the house of the King of the Chedis
sn: एवं प्रकारैर्बहुभिर्दैवेनाक्रम्य हस्तिभिः। राजन् विनिहतं सर्वं समृद्धं सार्थमण्डलम्॥
en: O king! thus accidentally attacked by a large number of elephants, the good merchants underwent a great loss.

description: Damayanti's living in the house of the King of the Chedis
sn: आराव: सुमहांश्चासीत् त्रैलोक्यभयकारकः। एषोऽग्निरुत्थितः कष्टस्त्रायध्वंधावताधुना॥ रत्नराशिर्विशीर्णोऽयं गृहणीध्वं की प्रधावत।
en: Then there arose a great uproar, terrifying the three worlds, and also there broke out a fire. "O! save us from this trouble. Do you now fly away? These heaps of gems are scattered on all sides. Take them. Why do you fly?

description: Damayanti's living in the house of the King of the Chedis
sn: सामान्यमेतद् द्रविणं न मिथ्यावचनं मम॥
en: These riches are nothing. My words are not untrue.

description: Damayanti's living in the house of the King of the Chedis
sn: एवमेवाभिभाषन्तो विद्रवन्ति भयात् तदा। पुनरेवाभिधास्यामि चिन्तयध्वं सुकातराः॥
en: You terror-stricken ones! think upon the words that I tell you again. Exclaiming in the way as above, they all ran about in fright.

description: Damayanti's living in the house of the King of the Chedis
sn: तस्मिंस्तथा वर्तमाने दारुणे जनसंक्षये। दमयन्ती च बुबुधे भयसंत्रस्तमानसा॥
en: While that terrible slaughter prevailed, Damayanti rose up with a mind agitated by terror and anxiety.

description: Damayanti's living in the house of the King of the Chedis
sn: अपश्यद् वैशसं तत्र सर्वलोकभयंकरम्। अदृष्टपूर्वं तद् दृष्ट्वा बाला पद्मनिभेक्षणा॥ संसक्तवदनाश्वासा उत्तस्थौ भयविह्वला। ये तु तत्र विनिर्मुक्ताः सार्थात् केचिदविक्षताः॥ तेऽब्रुवन् सहिताः सर्वे कस्येदं कर्मणः फलम्। नूनं न पूजितोऽस्माभिर्मणिभद्रो महायशाः॥ तथा यक्षाधिपः श्रीमान् न वै वैश्रवणः प्रभुः। न पूजा विघ्नकर्तृणामथवा प्रथमं कृता॥ शकुनानां फलं वाथ विपरीतमिदंध्रुवम्। ग्रहा न विपरीतास्तु किमन्यदिदमागतम्॥
en: There the maiden, possessing eyes like the lotus-leaves, saw the effects of that unforeseen accident. viz., the slaughter, which meant to frighten all the worlds. On her awakening, she became insensible with fear; and also with an affected countenance, she became out of breath. Those of the caravan, who escaped from the slaughter unhurt, all assembled together and talked on the action of which that (the slaughter) was the result. 'Surely we have not worshipped that well-reputed Maharudra or that auspicious and magnanimous king of the Yakshas, Vaisravana. Or it might be that we have not worshipped the deities that cause distresses. Or perhaps we have not paid them the first offerings. 'Or this unnatural circumstance is the sure result of the birds (we beheld). Our presiding stars unfavourable; what else there is, from which this calamity has ensued?'

description: Damayanti's living in the house of the King of the Chedis
sn: अपरे त्वब्रुवन् दीना ज्ञातिद्रव्यविनाकृताः। यासावध महासार्थे नारी हुन्मत्तदर्शना॥ प्रविष्टा विकृताकारा कृत्वा रूपममानुषम्। तयेयं विहिता पूर्वं माया परमदारुणा॥
en: Other again, distressed and deprived of wealth and friends as they were, said, 'That mad-like woman of unnatural look came are not among this mighty company of merchants, assuming an inhuman appearance. It is by her that this terrible illusion had been prearranged.

description: Damayanti's living in the house of the King of the Chedis
sn: राक्षसी वाध्रुवं यक्षी पिशाची वा भयंकरी। तस्याः सर्वमिदं पापं नात्र कार्या विचारणा॥ पश्यामो यदि तां पापां सार्थनीं नैकदुःखदाम्। लोष्टभिः पांसुभिश्चैव तृणैः काष्ठैश्च मुष्टिभिः॥
en: This woman must surely be a Rakshasi or a Yakshi or a dreadful Pishachni. All this evil has been wrought by her, regarding which there should be no scruples. 'Should I again find out that vicious woman, who is the slayer of merchants, giving innumerable sufferings to them, I must kill her by either (throwing) stones or dust or grass or wood or by strokes of the hand.'

description: Damayanti's living in the house of the King of the Chedis
sn: अवश्यमेव हन्यामः सार्थस्य किल कृत्यकाम्। दमयन्ती तु तच्छ्रुत्वा वाक्यं तेषां सुदारुणम्॥ ह्रीता भीता च संविग्ना प्राद्रवद् यत्र काननम्। आशङ्कमाना तत्पापमात्मानं पर्यदेवयत्॥
en: Damayanti, hearing their words, afflicted with fright and shame; and she on suspicion of their evil designs fled into the forest, greatly terrified. She also upbraided herself, saying-

description: Damayanti's living in the house of the King of the Chedis
sn: अहो ममोपरि विधेः संरम्भो दारुणो महान्। नानुबध्नाति कुशलं कस्येदं कर्मणः फलम्॥
en: 'Oh! the god's anger is violent and great upon me; and hence it is that peace never follows me. Of what deed (or misdeed) is this the result?

description: Damayanti's living in the house of the King of the Chedis
sn: न स्मराम्यशुभं किचित् कृतं कस्यचिदण्वपि। कर्मणा मनसा वाचा कस्येदं कर्मणः फलम्॥
en: I do not remember that I have ever done any harm to any body, either by actions or thought or by speeches. Of what deed (or misdeed) is this, therefore, the result?

description: Damayanti's living in the house of the King of the Chedis
sn: नूनं जन्मान्तरकृतं पापमापतितं महत्। अपश्चिमामिमां कष्टामापदं प्राप्तवत्यहम्॥
en: I have met with these sufferings, which are the results of that great calamity that has befallen me. Certainly all these are owing to was my perpetrating a cruel deed during my past existence.

description: Damayanti's living in the house of the King of the Chedis
sn: भर्तृराज्यापहरणं स्वजनाच्च पराजयः। भ! सह वियोगश्च तनयाभ्यां च विच्युतिः॥ निर्नाथता वने वासो बहुव्यालनिषेविते। अथापरेयुः सम्प्राप्ते हतशिष्टा जनास्तदा॥ देशात् तस्माद् विनिष्क्रम्य शोचन्ते वैशसं कृतम्। भ्रातरं पितरं पुत्रं सखायं च नराधिप।॥
en: The consequence of that calamity are the loss of kingdom by my husband; his defeat (at dice) by his relatives; my separation from my husband, son and my daughter, and also this my unprotected condition; and my exile in these woods abounding in all classes of beasts of prey.' O king! thereupon the next day the rest of the merchants, who survived the slaughter, departed from the country, lamenting for the loss of their brothers, fathers, sons and relatives.

description: Damayanti's living in the house of the King of the Chedis
sn: अशोचत् तत्र वैदर्भी किं नु मे दुष्कृतं कृतम्। योऽपि मे निर्जनेऽरण्ये सम्प्राप्तोऽयं जनार्णवः॥ स हतो हस्तियूथेन मन्दभाग्यान्ममैव तत्। प्राप्तव्यं सुचिरं दुःखं नूनमद्यापि वै मया॥
en: The daughter of the king of the Vidharbhas again lamented, saying, 'What a misdeed I had committed in the past! As the result of my misfortune, the crowd of men, whose company I have found in this solitary wood, was all destroyed by elephants. As it seems, surely I shall have to suffer certain distresses for a pretty long period.

description: Damayanti's living in the house of the King of the Chedis
sn: नाप्राप्तकालो म्रियते श्रुतं वृद्धानुशासनम्। या नाहमद्य मृदिता हस्तियूथेन दुःखिता।॥
en: I have heard from old men that none dies before his time. Had this not been true, my afflicted self would surely have been crushed to death this day by the herd of elephants.

description: Damayanti's living in the house of the King of the Chedis
sn: न ह्यदैवकृतं किंचिन्नराणामिह विद्यते। न च मे बालभावेऽपरि किंचित् पापकृतं कृतम्॥ कर्मणा मनसा वाचा यदिदं दुःखमागतम्।
en: Indeed, there exists nothing of men that does not fall within the category of destiny. I had committed no crime even in my childhood, either in action, thought or speech, for which reason this great calamity might befall me.

description: Damayanti's living in the house of the King of the Chedis
sn: मन्ये स्वयंवरकृते लोकपालाः समागताः॥ प्रत्याख्याता मया तत्र नलस्यार्थाय देवताः। नूनं तेषां प्रभावेण वियोगं प्राप्तवत्यहम्॥ एवमादीनि दुःखार्ता सा विलप्य वराङ्गना। प्रलापानि तदा तानि दमयन्ती पतिव्रता॥
en: On the occasion of the Svayamvara, the assembled divine guardians of the worlds were neglected by me, for the sake of king Nala; and surely I think. it is through their potent interference, that I have been suffering from this separation.' That fair complexioned Damayanti, devoted to her husband, uttering these words of grief, became greatly afflicted with sorrows and looked pale.

description: Damayanti's living in the house of the King of the Chedis
sn: हतशेषैः सह तदा ब्राह्मणैर्वेदपारगैः। अगच्छद् राजशार्दूल चन्द्रलेखेव शारदी॥ गच्छन्ती साचिराद् बाला पुरमासादयन्महत्। सायाह्ने चेदिराजस्य सुबाहोः सत्यदर्शिनः॥
en: O foremost of kings! even as the autumnal moon herself, she then went away with the Brahmanas, conversant with the texts of the Vedas, who survived that terrible slaughter. In the course of her going with haste, the maiden arrived in the evening at the great city of truthful Subahu, the king of the Chedis.

description: Damayanti's living in the house of the King of the Chedis
sn: अथ वस्त्रार्धसंवीता प्रविवेश पुरोत्तमम्। तां विह्वलां कृशां दीनां मुक्तकेशीममार्जिताम्॥ उन्मत्तामिव गच्छन्तीं ददृशुः पुरवासिनः। प्रविशन्तीं तु तां दृष्ट्वा चेदिराजपुरीं तदा॥ अनुजग्मुस्तत्र बाला चामिपुत्राः कुतूहलात्। सा तैः परिवृतागच्छत् समीपं राजवेश्मनः॥
en: When she entered that good city, half dressed, the citizens saw her terror-stricken, very weak and helpless, of loosened hairs, unbathed and faring even as a mad woman. Through curiosity the boys of the city pursued her, while they saw her enter into the city of the king of the Chedis. Then the damsel, thus surrounded by the boys, came to the front of the palace.

description: Damayanti's living in the house of the King of the Chedis
sn: तां प्रासादगतापश्यद् राजमाता जनैर्वृताम्। धात्रीमुवाच गच्छैनामानयेह ममान्तिकम्॥
en: From the palace the Queen-mother beheld her surrounded by a large number of persons; and asked her nurse to go and bring her before her Highness.

description: Damayanti's living in the house of the King of the Chedis
sn: जनेन क्लिश्यते बाला दुःखिता शरणार्थिनी। तादृग् रूपं च पश्यामि विद्योतयति मे गृहम्॥
en: The Queen-mother also saw her, vexed by the people, helpless, overpowered by sorrows and seeking for protection, but the splendour of her beauty was such that it illumined the whole palace.

description: Damayanti's living in the house of the King of the Chedis
sn: उन्मत्तवेषा कल्याणी श्रीरिवायतलोचना। सा जनं वारयित्वा तं प्रासादतलमुत्तमम्॥ आरोग्य विस्मिता राजन् दमयन्तीमपृच्छत। एवमप्यसुखाविष्टा बिभर्षि परमं वपुः॥
en: That beautiful and large-eyed lady, even as Sri herself, looked like a mad woman. Then, O king, the nurse ordering the crowd to disperse, took her into the palace and, struck with amazement, inquired of Damayanti, saying: 'How do you, oppressed with sorrow, bear a graceful form.

description: Damayanti's living in the house of the King of the Chedis
sn: भासि विद्युदिवाभ्रेषु शंस मे कासि कस्य वा। न हि ते मानुषं रूपं भूषणैरपि वर्जितम्॥
en: Do you blaze like lightning in the midst of clouds? O! tell me who are you and to whom do you belong? Surely your beauty is not human, although you are not decked in ornaments.

description: Damayanti's living in the house of the King of the Chedis
sn: असहाया नरेभ्यश्च नोद्विजस्यमरप्रभे। तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं तस्या भैमी वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: you effulgent one like unto the celestials! although you are helpless, yet you are unmoved by these (outraging) persons?' Hearing these words of the nurse, the daughter of king Bhima spoke the (following) words to her,

description: Damayanti's living in the house of the King of the Chedis
sn: मानुषीं मां विजानीहि भर्तारं समनुव्रताम्। सैरन्ध्रीजातिसम्पन्नं भुजिष्यां कामवासिनीम्॥ फलमूलाशनामेकां यत्रसायंप्रतिश्रयाम्। असंख्येयगुणो भर्ता मां च नित्यमनुव्रतः॥
en: 'Know that I am a woman, devoted to my husband; and a female-servant, belonging to a high caste. Know also that I stay wherever I like and subsist on fruits and roots. I am lonely; and I stop when evening draws nigh. My lord possesses innumerable virtues; and he was ever devoted to me.

description: Damayanti's living in the house of the King of the Chedis
sn: भक्तामहपि तं वीरं छायेवानुगता पथि। तस्य दैवात् प्रसङ्गोऽभूदतिमात्रं सुदेवने॥ द्यूते स निर्जितश्चैव वनमेक उपेयिवान्। तमेकवसनं वीरमुन्मत्तमिव विह्वलम्॥ आश्वासयन्ती भर्तारमहमप्यगमं वनम्। स कदाचिद् वने वीरः कस्मिंश्चित् कारणान्तरे॥
en: I was also attached to that heroic one, following him in his course even as a shadow. It so happened that once he was engaged in the play at dice, at which he was defeated; and in consequence thereof he came alone into the wood. Beholding my heroic husband, wearing a single piece of cloth, maniac-like and afflicted with grief, I also followed him into the forest with a view to console him. Once on a time, that warlike one, for some reason go to in forest.

description: Damayanti's living in the house of the King of the Chedis
sn: क्षुत्परीतस्तु विमनास्तदप्येकं व्यसर्जयत्। तमेकवसना नग्नमुन्मत्तवदचेतसम्॥ अनुव्रजन्ती बहुला न स्वपामि निशास्तदा। ततो बहुतिथे काले सुप्तामुत्सृज्य मां क्वचित्॥ वाससोऽर्धं परिच्छिद्य त्यक्तवान् मामनागसम्। तं मार्गमाणा भर्तारं दह्यमाना दिवानिशम्॥
en: He oppressed with hunger, lost, in the woods, that single piece of cloth out of carelessness. Following him, naked, maniaclike and devoid of all his senses as he was, I, with a single piece of cloth on, could not sleep for several nights. Thus many days passed away when I fell asleep. He then tore off onehalf of my garment and forsook me there, although I had not done to him any harm. Hence it is that I fare about seeking my husband and burn day and night in distress.

description: Damayanti's living in the house of the King of the Chedis
sn: साहं कमलगर्भाभमपश्यन्ती हृदि प्रियम्। न विन्दाम्यमरप्रख्यं प्रियं प्राणेश्वरं प्रभुम्॥
en: Thus afflicted, I am unable to find out my lord, who is the darling of my heart and whose splendour is like the filaments of the lotuses. I do not see my lord, who is the delight of my heart, my own presiding god, most beloved of me and who again is like the celestials in appearance.

description: Damayanti's living in the house of the King of the Chedis
sn: तामश्रुपरिपूर्णाक्षीं विलपन्ती तथा बहु। राजमाताब्रवीदार्ता भैमीमार्तस्वरां स्वयम्॥ वसस्व मयि कल्याणि प्रीतिमें परमा त्वयि। मृगयिष्यन्ति ते भद्रे भर्तारं पुरुषा मम॥
en: The Queen-mother herself addressed the daughter of Bhima, whose eyes were full of tears, bewailing in the above manner and whose voice was choked up in sorrow. O blessed lady! O gentle one! stay here with me. I am much pleased with you. Mymen will seek your husband in the woods.

description: Damayanti's living in the house of the King of the Chedis
sn: अपि वा स्वयमागच्छेत् परिधावन्नितस्ततः। इहैव वसती भद्रे भर्तारमुपलप्स्यसे॥
en: It may so happen that he shall come here of himself in course of his roving about in the forest. O gentle one! do you live here now; and you shall get your husband back.'

description: Damayanti's living in the house of the King of the Chedis
sn: राजमातुर्वचः श्रुत्वा दमयन्ती वचोऽब्रवीत्। समयेनोत्सहे वस्तुं त्वयि वीरप्रजायिनि॥ उच्छिष्टं नैव भुञ्जीयां न कुर्यां पादधावनम्। न चाहं पुरुषानन्यान् प्रभाषेयं कथंचन॥
en: Hearing these words of the Queen-mother, Damayanti spoke to her; 'O mother of heroes! I dare reside with you, provided that I shall not have to eat the remnants of a dish, nor I shall have ever to speak with other men.

description: Damayanti's living in the house of the King of the Chedis
sn: प्रार्थयेद् यदि मां कश्चिद् दण्ड्यस्ते स पुमान् भवेत्। वध्यश्च तेऽसकृन्मन्द इति मे व्रतमाहितम्॥
en: If any body shall solicit me (to be his wife), that person must be punished by you. Or should he solicit me repeatedly, that criminal person shall be punished with death. This is the vow that I have prearranged.

description: Damayanti's living in the house of the King of the Chedis
sn: भर्तुरन्वेषणार्थं तु पश्येयं ब्राह्मणानहम्। यद्येवमिह वत्स्यामि त्वत्सकाशे न संशयः॥
en: 'I will find out those Brahmanas, who will search for my husband. Should you arrange all this, I shall no doubt live with you.'

description: Damayanti's living in the house of the King of the Chedis
sn: अतोऽन्यथा न मे वासो वर्तते हृदये क्वचित्। तां प्रहष्टेन मनसा राजमातेदमब्रवीत्॥
en: If it is otherwise, to live does not find place in my heart.' The Queen-mother said to her:

description: Damayanti's living in the house of the King of the Chedis
sn: सर्वमेतत् करिष्यामि दिष्ट्या ते व्रतमीदृशम्। एवमुक्त्वा ततो भैमी राजमाता विशाम्पते॥ उवाचेदं दुहितरं सुनन्दा नाम भारत। सैरन्ध्रीमभिजानीष्व सुनन्दे देवरूपिणीम्॥
en: 'I will do all this. Very good is this your vow.' O monarch! the daughter of king Bhima was thus addressed by the Queen-mother. O Bharata! she called her daughter Sunanda and spoke to her this: 'O Sunanda! know well that this maiden is a goddess, even as your Shairindhri (a high class maid-servant).

description: Damayanti's living in the house of the King of the Chedis
sn: वयसा तुल्यतां प्राप्ता सखी तव भवत्वियम्। एतया सह मोदस्व निरुद्विग्नमनाः सदा॥
en: As she is of the same age with yourself, do you take the lady as your companion and also play with her always without any apprehension in the mind.'

description: Damayanti's living in the house of the King of the Chedis
sn: ततः परमसंहष्टा सुनन्दा गृहमागमत्। दमयन्तीमुपादाय सखीभिः परिवारिता॥
en: Thereupon Sunanda, having received Damayanti with the greatest delight, conducted her into her own apartinents, attended by all her companions.

description: Damayanti's living in the house of the King of the Chedis
sn: स तत्र पूज्यमाना वै दमयन्ती व्यनन्दत। सर्वकामैः सुविहितैर्निरुद्वेगावसत् तदा॥
en: Damayanti was highly gratified with the respectful behaviour of her companion; and she lived there for some time, because all her desires were excellently satisfied.

description: The discourse between king Nala and Karkotaka
sn: बृहदश्व उवाच उत्सृज्य दमयन्ती तु नलो राजा विशाम्पते। ददर्श दावं दह्यन्तं महान्तं गहने वने।॥
en: Brihadashava said : O king! king Nala, having forsaken Damayanti, beheld a great fire breaking out in that dreadful forest.

description: The discourse between king Nala and Karkotaka
sn: तत्र शुश्राव शब्दं वै मध्ये भूतस्य कस्यचित्। अभिधाव नलेत्युच्चैः पुण्यश्लाकेति चासकृत्॥ मा भैरिति नलश्चोक्त्वा मध्यमग्नेः प्रविश्य तम्। ददर्श नागराजानं शयानं कुण्डलीकृतम्॥
en: There in the midst of that great fire he heard the voice of some living object, which cried over and over again unto the righteous Nala, Saying-Come hither. Nala answered him, saying-do not fear. Thus saying, he entered into the conflagration and saw there the king of the snakes lying in coils.

description: The discourse between king Nala and Karkotaka
sn: स नागः प्राञ्जलिर्भूत्वा वेपमानो नलं तदा। उवाच मां विद्धि राजन् नागं कर्कोटकं नृप।॥ मया प्रलब्धो ब्रह्मर्षिर्नारदः सुमहातपाः। तेन मन्युपरीतेन शप्तोऽस्मि मनुजाधिप।॥ तिष्ठ त्वं स्थावर इव यावदेव नल: क्वचित्। इतो नेता हि तत्र त्वं शापान्मोक्ष्यसि मत्कृतात्॥
en: Thereupon the Naga (the king of the snakes), with folded hands and trembling with fear, addressed Nala. 'O king! know me that I am Naga (snake), Karkotaka by name. O lord of men! the great sage, Narada, observing rigid austerity, was once deceived by me; and who, again, filled with rage, coursed me, saying: Remain here like some immovable thing, until king Nala leads you hence. And, indeed, wherever shall he take you, there shall you be released from my curse.'

description: The discourse between king Nala and Karkotaka
sn: तस्य शापान शक्तोऽस्मि पदाद् विचलितुं पदम् उपदेक्ष्यामि ते श्रेयस्त्रातुमर्हति मां भवान्॥
en: It is owing to his curse that I am unable to move even a step-father. It behoves you, therefore, to release me; and then I will instruct you as regards your welfare.

description: The discourse between king Nala and Karkotaka
sn: सखा च ते भविष्यामि मत्समो नास्ति पन्नगः। लघुश्च ते भविष्यामि शीघ्रमादाय गच्छ माम्॥
en: I have not a peer among the snakes; I will be your companion. I am very light. So do you carry me in your hands and spcedily go.'

description: The discourse between king Nala and Karkotaka
sn: एवमुक्त्वा स नागेन्द्रो बभूवाङ्गुष्ठमात्रकः। तं गृहीत्वा नलः प्रायाद् देशं दावविवर्जितम्॥
en: Having thus addressed the king, the prince of the snakes assumed the size of the thumb. King Nala, having thus taken him up, repaired to a country, free from the conflagration.

description: The discourse between king Nala and Karkotaka
sn: आकाशदेशमासाद्य विमुक्तं कृष्णवर्मना। उत्स्रष्टुकामं तं नागः पुन: कर्कोटकोऽब्रवीत्॥
en: Having approached an open ground, free from the fire, Nala was desirous of leaving him, whereupon the Naga (king of the snakes) again said to him:

description: The discourse between king Nala and Karkotaka
sn: पदानि गणयन् गच्छ स्वानि नैषध कानिचित्। तत्र तेऽहं महाबाहो श्रेयोधास्यामि यत् परम्॥
en: “O king of the Nishadhas! do you proceed counting your own steps. O mighty-armed warrior! I will render great good to you."

description: The discourse between king Nala and Karkotaka
sn: तत: संख्यातुमारब्धमदशद् दशमे पदे। तस्य दष्टस्य तद् रूपं क्षिप्रमन्तरधीयत॥
en: Thereupon the king commenced counting his own steps, and at the tenth step he was bit. Having thus bitten him, the snake soon assumed a speedy change, viz., his original form.

description: The discourse between king Nala and Karkotaka
sn: स दृष्ट्वा विस्मितस्तस्थावात्मानं विकृतं नलः। स्वरूपधारिणं नागं ददर्श स महीपतिः॥
en: Beholding the change of form, Nala became struck with astonishment. The ruler of the earth also behold the snake to assume his real form,

description: The discourse between king Nala and Karkotaka
sn: ततः कर्कोटको नागः सान्त्वयन् नलमब्रवीत्। मया तेऽन्तर्हितं रूपं न त्वां विद्युर्जना इति॥
en: Thereupon the snake, Karkotaka, consoling him, spoke to Nala: "I have wrought this change of your beauty for the reason that the people will not recognise you."

description: The discourse between king Nala and Karkotaka
sn: यत्कृते चासि निकृतो दुःखेन महता नल। विषेण स मदीयेन त्वयि दुःखं निवत्स्यति॥
en: As I have done this, O Nala, the person, by whom have you been cast into great distress, will dwell within yourself, oppressed by my venom."

description: The discourse between king Nala and Karkotaka
sn: विषेण संवृतैर्गात्रैर्यावत् त्वां न विमोक्ष्यति। तावत् त्वयि महाराज दुःखं वै स निवत्स्यति॥
en: O foremost of the kings! as long as the person will not leave you, he shall have to miserably reside in yourself with the whole body filled with my poison.

description: The discourse between king Nala and Karkotaka
sn: अनागा येन निकृतस्त्वमन) जनाधिप। क्रोधादसूययित्वा तं रक्षा मे भवतः कृता॥
en: O king of men! from the person by whom, out of anger or hate, have you been cast into distress, I ilave saved you.

description: The discourse between king Nala and Karkotaka
sn: न ते भयं नरव्याघ्र दंष्ट्रिभ्यः शत्रुतोऽपि वा। ब्रह्मविद्भ्यश्च भविता मत्प्रसादान्नराधिप॥
en: O best of kings! O ruler of men! (hitherto fore) you shall have no fear either from the animals with fangs or from your cnemies or the Brahmanas conversant with the texts of the Vedas; for I am most graceful to you.

description: The discourse between king Nala and Karkotaka
sn: राजन् विषनिमित्ता च न ते पीडा भविष्यति। संग्रमेषु च राजेन्द्र शश्वज्जयमवाप्स्यसि॥
en: O king! you shall feel no uneasiness owing to my venom. O best of kings! you shall ever gain victory in battles.

description: The discourse between king Nala and Karkotaka
sn: गच्छ राजनित: सूतो बाहुकोऽहमिति ब्रुवन्। समीपमृतुपर्णस्य स हि चैवाक्षनैपुणः॥ अयोध्या नगरी रम्यामद्य वै निषधेश्वर। स तेऽक्षहृदयं दाता राजाश्चहृदयेन वै॥
en: O monarch! O the prince of the Nishadhas! do you go from here this day to the city of Ayodhya before Rituparna, who is most sk in the game at dice, calling yourself that you are the charioteer, Bahuka by name. That king will exchange his skill at dice for your knowledge in the management of horses.

description: The discourse between king Nala and Karkotaka
sn: इक्ष्वाकुकुलजः श्रीमान् मित्रं चैव भविष्यति। भविष्यसि यदाक्षज्ञः श्रेयसा योक्ष्यसे तदा।॥
en: That prosperous one, descended from the line of Ikshvaku, will be your friend. Then shall you obtain skillfulness at dice and meet your prosperity.

description: The discourse between king Nala and Karkotaka
sn: सममेष्यसि दारैस्त्वं मा स्म शोके मनः कृथाः। राज्येन तनयाभ्यां च सत्यमेतद् ब्रवीमि ते॥
en: I tell you the truth that you shall find your wife, son and daughter and also obtain your kingdom back and so be not filled with grief.

description: The discourse between king Nala and Karkotaka
sn: स्वं रूपं च यदा द्रष्टुमिच्छेथास्त्वं नराधिप। संस्मर्तव्यस्तदा तेऽहं वासश्चेदं निवासयेः॥
en: O king of men! when shall you desire to witness your own form, call me back to your mind; and put on these pieces of cloth.

description: The discourse between king Nala and Karkotaka
sn: अनेन वाससाच्छन्नः स्वं रूपं प्रतिपत्स्यसे। इत्युक्त्वा प्रददौ तस्मै दिव्यं वासोयुगं तदा॥
en: Wearing these pieces of cloth, you shall recover your proper form. Having said this, the king of the snakes then gave to him (Nala) two pieces of cloth of superior worth."

description: The discourse between king Nala and Karkotaka
sn: एवं नलं च संदिश्य वासो दत्त्वा च कौरव। नागराजस्ततो राजंस्तत्रैवान्तरधीयत।॥
en: O descendant of Kuru! O king! having thus advised Nala and given to him the celestials garment, the monarch of the snakes disappeared then and there.

sn: वृहदश्व उवाच तस्मिन्नन्तहिते नागे प्रययौ नैषधो नलः। ऋतुपर्णस्य नगरं प्राविशद् दशमेऽहनि॥
en: Brihadashva said : After the disappearance of the Naga, Nala, the prince of the Nishadhas, repaired to the city of Rituparna on the tenth day.

sn: स राजानमुपातिष्ठद् बाहुकोऽहमिति ब्रुवन्। अश्वानां वाहने युक्तः पृथिव्यां नास्ति मत्समः॥
en: He approached the king with these words: “I am Bahuka, skilled in the management of horses. I have not a peer in this earth.

sn: अर्थकृच्छ्रेषु चैवाहं प्रष्टव्यो नैपुणेषु च। अन्नसंस्कारमपि च जानाम्यन्यैर्विशेषतः॥
en: I may be referred to on the matters of pecuniary difficulty, as well as on those of skill. I know the art of cooking, in which I am unsurpassed by others.

sn: यानि शिल्पानि लोकेऽस्मिन् यच्चैवान्यत् सुदुष्करम् सर्वं यतिष्ये तत् कर्तुमृतुपर्ण भरस्व माम्॥
en: O Rituparna, I will take care to bring under operation all the arts, that rest in the world and also other matters difficult of accomplishment. Therefore, do you maintain me.”

sn: ऋतुपर्ण उवाच वस बाहुक भद्रं ते सर्वमेतत् करिष्यसि। शीघ्रयाने सदा बुद्धिर्धियते मे विशेषतः॥
en: Rituparna said : O Bahuka! stay with me! All hail unto you! Shall you perform all this. Always my mind particularly turns to this, viz., to be driven very fast.

sn: स त्वमातिष्ठ योगं तं येन शीघ्रा हया ममा भवेयुरश्वाध्यक्षोऽसि वेतनं ते शतं शतम्॥
en: Do you adopt some such means that my horses may become very fast. Be then the superintendent of my stables, on a salary of ten thousand coins.

sn: त्वामुपस्थास्यतश्चैव नित्यं वार्ष्णेयजीवलौ। एताभ्यां रंस्यसे सार्धं वस वै मयि बाहुक॥
en: Varshneya and Jivala shall always be guided by you; and in whose company shall you pass your days in joy. O Bahuka! do you, therefore, stay with me.

sn: बृहदश्व उवाच एवमुक्तो नलस्तेन न्यवसत् तत्र पूजितः। ऋतुपर्णस्य नगरे सहवार्ष्णेयजीवलः॥
en: Brihadashya said : Having been thus addressed, Nala, thus received, lived there in the city of Rituparna in company with Varshneya and Jivala.

sn: स वै तत्रावसद् राजा वैदर्भीमनुचिन्तयन्। सायं सायं सदा चेमं श्लोकमेकं जगाद ह॥
en: That king continued to live there in anxiety for the daughter of the king of the Vidharbhas; and every evening he repeated a verse which runs thus:

sn: क्व नु सा क्षुत्पिपासार्ता श्रान्ता शेते तपस्विनी। स्मरन्ती तस्य मन्दस्य कं वा साद्योपतिष्ठति॥
en: Where does lie that glorious one, oppressed with hunger and thirst and fatigued with toil; and always meditating upon that miserable one, to whom does she now attach herself?"

sn: एवं ब्रुवन्तं राजानं निशायां जीवलोऽब्रवीत्। कामेनां शोचसे नित्यं श्रोतुमिच्छामि बाहुक॥
en: Jivala asked the king, while he was muttering the above verse in the night, saying: 'O Bahuka! I desire to learn about the person, for whom do you mourn every day.

sn: आयुष्मन् कस्य वा नारी यामेवमनुशोचसि। तमुवाच नलो राजा मन्दप्रज्ञस्य कस्यचित्॥ आसीद् बहुमता नारी तस्यादृढतरं वचः। स वै केनचिदर्थेन तया मन्दो व्ययुज्यत॥
en: O you blessed with longevity! whose is that lady, for whom do you lament every day?” Thus spoken, king Nala answered him, saying, There was a wretch, who had lost all his senses. He had a spouse known to many. He was false in his promises (to her). For a certain cause he was separated from her.

sn: विप्रयुक्तः स मन्दात्मा भ्रमत्यसुखपीडितः। दह्यमानः स शोकेन दिवारानमतन्द्रितः॥
en: Being thus separated (from her), that wicked person roved about. He was repressed with sorrow; and burning with grief, he never slept either by day or night.

sn: निशाकाले स्मरंस्तस्याः श्लोकमेकं स्म गायति। स विभ्रमन् महीं सर्वां क्वचिदासाद्य किंचन॥ वसत्यनहर्हस्तद् दुःखं भूय एवानुसंस्मरन्।
en: Remembering her during the night, he sings the above verse. Then having wandered over the whole world and at last coming to a place where he, undeserving of the calamity that has overtaken him, resides always remembering his wife.

sn: सा तु तं पुरुषं नारी कृच्छ्रेऽप्यनुगता वने।॥ त्यक्ता तेनाल्पपुण्येन दुष्करं यदि जीवति। एका बालानभिज्ञा च मार्गाणामतथोचिता॥
en: Having fallen into distress, the person was followed by his wife into the forest. Forsaken by that man of little virtue, the lady, aftlicted with sorrow, hardly lives. That solitary girl, having no knowledge of the forest paths, saves her life with difficulty.

sn: क्षुत्पिपासापरीताङ्गी दुष्करं यदि जीवति। श्वापदाचरिते नित्यं वने महति दारुणे॥ त्यक्ता तेनाल्पभाग्यन मन्दप्रज्ञेन मारिष। इत्येवं नैषधो राजा दमयन्तीमनुस्मरन्। अज्ञातवासं न्यवसद् राज्ञस्तस्य निवेशने॥
en: As she, fatigued with hunger and thirst, is quite unfit to wander about in that dreadful and dense forest, always haunted by fierce animals. Cfriend! having left her in that dreadful forest, the stupid king of the Nishadhas of little fortune thus remembered Damayanti, while he was living an unknown life in the house of that king.''

description: The parley between Damayanti and Sudeva
sn: बृहदश्व उवाच हृतराज्ये नले भीमः सभार्ये च वनं गते। द्विजान् प्रस्थापयामास नलदर्शनकाझया।।।।
en: Brihadashva said : When Nala, deprived of his kingdom, turned himself to a servant with his wife, then king Bhima sent away Brahmanas, with the object of seeing Nala.

description: The parley between Damayanti and Sudeva
sn: संदिदेश च तान् भीमो वसु दत्त्वा च पुष्कलम्। मृगयध्वं नलं चैव दमयन्तीं च मे सुताम्॥
en: Bhima, having given immense wealth to the Brahmanas, asked them to go in quest of Nala and his daughter, Damayanti.

description: The parley between Damayanti and Sudeva
sn: अस्मिन् कर्मणि सम्पन्ने विज्ञाते निषधाधिपे। गवां सहस्रं दास्यामि यो वस्तावानयिष्यति॥ अग्रहारांश्च दास्यामि ग्राम नगरसम्मितम्। न चेच्छक्याविहानेतुं दमयन्ती नलोऽपि वा॥ ज्ञातमात्रेऽपि दास्यामि गवां दशशतं धनम्।
en: “To him, who will perform this deed, viz., learning the place where at the king of the Nishadhas does live now or bringing him hither with his wife, will I give a thousand kine, fields and a village like a city. Should he fail to bring hither Nala as well as Damayanti, his very knowledge of them would be rewarded by my giving him wealth in the shape of a ten thousand kine."

description: The parley between Damayanti and Sudeva
sn: इत्युक्तास्ते ययुर्हष्टा ब्राह्मणाः सर्वतो दिशम्॥ पुरराष्ट्राणि चिन्वन्तो नैषधं सह भार्यया। नैव क्वापि प्रपश्यन्ति नलं वा भीमपुत्रिकाम्॥ ततश्चेदिपुरी रम्यां सुदेवो नाम वै द्विजः। विचिन्वानोऽथ वैदर्भीमपश्यद् राजवेश्मनि॥
en: Having been thus addressed, the Brahmanasa went out in all directions, searching for Nala and Damayanti in the various cities and provinces. But they could not see Nala or the daughter of Bhima anywhere. While at last a Brahmana, Sudeva by name, was searching in the city of the king of the Chedis, he saw the daughter of the king of the Vidarbhas, Damayanti.

description: The parley between Damayanti and Sudeva
sn: पुण्याहवाचने राज्ञः सुनन्दासहितां स्थिताम्। मन्दं प्रख्यायमानेन रूपेणाप्रतिमेन ताम्॥ निबद्धां धूमजालेन प्रभामिव विभावसोः। तां समीक्ष्य विशालाक्षीमधिकं मलिनां कृशाम्। तर्कयामास भैमीति कारणैरुपपादयन्॥
en: She seated with Sunanda, in the house of that monarch, who at the time was repeating his prayers. She was faintly seen, on account of the great luminosity of her extraordinary beauty. Even as her splendour was like the blazing of a fire enveloped by smokes. Thus beholding that lady, with large eyes, colorless and weak, he, after arguing from various reasons, decided her to be the daughter of Bhima.

description: The parley between Damayanti and Sudeva
sn: सुदेव उवाच यथेयं मे पुरा दृष्टा तथारूपेयमङ्गना। कृतार्थोऽस्म्यद्य दृष्ट्वेमा लोककान्तामिव श्रियम्॥
en: Sudeva said: As I saw the lady beforehand, she seems to be the self-same in appearance at present. This day I think myself blessed by the very sight of her, who is like Sree herself, delighting all the worlds.

description: The parley between Damayanti and Sudeva
sn: पूर्णचन्द्रनिभां श्यामां चारुवृत्तपयोधराम्। वन्तीं प्रभया देवी सर्वा वितिमिरा दिशः॥
en: Also, the lady is like the full moon in splendour. She looks ever youthful, possessing a handsome breast; and dispelling darkness from all the directions by virtue of her effulgence.

description: The parley between Damayanti and Sudeva
sn: चारुपद्मविशालाक्षी मन्मथस्य रतीमिव। इष्टां समस्तलोकस्य पूर्णचन्द्रप्रभामिव॥
en: She again looks even as Kama's Rati herself, having eyes as large as the handsome lotusleaves. She is the delight of all the worlds like the rays of the full moon.

description: The parley between Damayanti and Sudeva
sn: विदर्भसरसस्तस्माद् दैवदोषादिवोद्धताम्। मलपङ्कानुलिप्ताङ्गी मृणालीमिव चोद्धृताम्॥ पौर्णमासीमिव निशां राहुग्रस्तनिशाकराम्। पतिशोकाकुलां दीनां शुष्कस्रोतां नदीमिव॥
en: Separated on account of her adverse fortune from that Vidarbha lake, she looks like the transplanted lotus-stalk, besmeared with mire. Or also, she looks like the night of the full moon, when that nocturnal god is swallowed up by Rahu. Repressed by sorrow for her, husband, she looks slender like the river with all its current dried up.

description: The parley between Damayanti and Sudeva
sn: विध्वस्तपर्णकमलां वित्रासितविहंगमाम्। हस्तिहस्तपरामृष्टां व्याकुलामिव पद्मिनीम्॥
en: She looks (in her present condition) like a ravaged lake, with the leaves of its lotuses crushed by the trunks of elephants and with its birds all flying away from fear.

description: The parley between Damayanti and Sudeva
sn: सुकुमारी सुजाताङ्गी रत्नगर्भगृहोचिताम्। दह्यमानामिवार्केण मृणालीमिव चोद्धृताम्॥
en: Possessed of slender constitution and handsome limbs and fit to dwell in a jewelled palace, she looks like a transplanted lotus-stalk burnt by the rays of the sun.

description: The parley between Damayanti and Sudeva
sn: रूपौदार्यगुणोपेतां मण्डनार्हाममण्डिताम्। चन्द्रलेखामिव नवां व्योम्नि नीलाभ्रसंवृताम्॥
en: Endued with beauty and liberality and undecked in ornaments, although befitting thein, she looks like the crescent of the moon, newly appearing in heaven and enveloped with the dark clouds.

description: The parley between Damayanti and Sudeva
sn: कामभोगैः प्रियीनां हीनां बन्धुजनेन च। देहं संधारयन्ती हि भर्तृदर्शनकाझ्या॥
en: Deprived of all the delightful objects of enjoyments and separated from friends and relatives, she lives a miserable life, cherishing the hope of beholding her husband again.

description: The parley between Damayanti and Sudeva
sn: भर्ता नाम परं नार्या भूषणं भूषणैर्विना। एषा हि रहिता तेन शोभमाना न शोभते॥
en: The best ornament of a woman, who is without the ornaments, is (the accompaniment of) her husband. Destitute so such an ornament (as the husband), she does not shine, although she is beautiful.

description: The parley between Damayanti and Sudeva
sn: दुष्करं कुरुतेऽत्यन्तं हीनो यदनया नलः। धारयत्यात्मनो देहं न शोकेनापि सीदति॥
en: Nala performs a very arduous task by holding his life without his dear wife and also without succumbing to sorrow.

description: The parley between Damayanti and Sudeva
sn: इमामसितकेशान्तां शतपत्रायतेक्षणाम्। सुखाहाँ दुःखितां दृष्ट्वा ममापि व्यथते मनः॥
en: My heart aches to behold that maiden, possessing black hairs and eyes as large as the lotus leaves and afflicted with sorrow, although she is most deserving of prosperity.

description: The parley between Damayanti and Sudeva
sn: कदा नु खलु दुःखस्य पारं यास्यति वै शुभा। भर्तुः समागमात् साध्वी रोहिणी शशिनो यथा॥
en: When, after sometime, the auspicious lady will surely have bridged over this ocean of woe, then she, devoted to her husband as ever, will, in company with her lord, look like Rohini in company with the Moon.

description: The parley between Damayanti and Sudeva
sn: अस्या नूनं पुनर्लाभान्नैषधः प्रीतिमेष्यति। राजा राज्यपरिभ्रष्टः पुनर्लब्ध्वा च मेदिनीम्॥
en: Certainly the king of the Nishadhas will obtain great delight by regaining his wife, even as the monarch, deprived of his kingdom, does by recovering his lost territories.

description: The parley between Damayanti and Sudeva
sn: तुल्यशीलवयोयुक्तां तुल्याभिजनसंवृताम्। नैषधोऽर्हति वैदर्भी तं चेयमसितेक्षणा॥
en: The king of the Nishadhas deserves the daughter of Vidharbha, who is like Nala in disposition, age and birth; as also the daughter of Vidharbha with black eyes is quite becoming to him.

description: The parley between Damayanti and Sudeva
sn: युक्तं तस्याप्रमेयस्य वीर्यसत्त्ववतो मया। समाश्वासयितुं भार्यां पतिदर्शनलालसाम्॥
en: It is my duty to console the wife of that immensely powerful one who is gifted with prowess and goodness, as she is most anxious for beholding her lord.

description: The parley between Damayanti and Sudeva
sn: अहमाश्वासयाम्येनां पूर्णचन्द्रनिभाननाम्। अदृष्टपूर्वां दुःखस्य दुःखाध्यिानतत्पराम्॥
en: I will (rather must) comfort the lady the splendour of whose face is like that of the full moon; and who is oppressed with such an woe that she had never experienced before, and also who is ever in fervid devotion for her husband.

description: The parley between Damayanti and Sudeva
sn: बृहदश्व उवाच एवं विमृश्य विविधैः कारणैर्लक्षणैश्च ताम्। उपागम्य ततो भैमी सुदेवो ब्राह्मणोऽब्रवीत्॥ अहं सुदेवो वैदर्भि भ्रातुस्ते दयितः सखा। भीमस्य वचनाद् राज्ञस्त्वामन्वेष्टुमिहागतः॥
en: Brihadashva said: Thereupon the Brahmana, Sudeva by name, having recognised the daughter of Bhima by observing the various circumstances and signs of hers, advanced to her and addressed her thus, O the daughter of Vidharbha! I am Sudeva, the intimate friend of your brother. Enjoined by king Bhima, I have come here searching for yourself. came

description: The parley between Damayanti and Sudeva
sn: कुशली ते पिता राज्ञि जननी भ्रातरश्च ते। आयुष्मन्तौ कुशलिनौ तत्रस्थौ दारकौ च तौ॥
en: O princess! your father is at peace, as also your mother and brothers. Those, your son and daughter, are enjoying length of days and living in peace.

description: The parley between Damayanti and Sudeva
sn: त्वत्कृते बन्धुवर्गाश्च गतसत्त्वा इवासते। अन्वेष्टारो ब्राह्मणाश्च भ्रमन्ति शतशो महीम्॥
en: Your friends and relatives, though living, are like the dead on your account; and hundreds of Brahmanas are wandering about over the whole world in quest of you.

description: The parley between Damayanti and Sudeva
sn: बृहदश्व उवाच अभिज्ञाय सुदेवं तं दमयन्ती युधिष्ठिर। पर्यपृच्छत तान् सर्वान् क्रमेण सुहृदः स्वकान्॥
en: Brihadashva said: O Yudhishthira! Damayanti to recognize Sudeva; and then asked him about all her friends and relatives in succession.

description: The parley between Damayanti and Sudeva
sn: रुरोद च भृशं राजन् वैदर्भी शोककर्शिता। दृष्ट्वा सुदेवं सहसा भ्रातुरिष्टं द्विजोत्तमम्॥
en: O king! crushed with misery as she was, the daughter of the king of the Vidharbhas began to lament most bitterly at the unexpected sight of that best of the Brahmanas, Sudeva, who is the friend of her brother.

description: The parley between Damayanti and Sudeva
sn: रुदतीं तामथो दृष्ट्वा सुनन्दा शोककर्शिता। सुदेवेन सहैकान्ते कथयन्तीं च भारत॥ जनित्र्यै कथयामास सैरन्ध्री रोदितीति च। ब्राह्मणेन सहागम्य तां वेद यदि मन्यसे॥
en: Thereupon, O Bharata! Sunanda, seeing her (Damayanti) conversing in private with a Brahmana and weeping most bitterly, was hard pressed with sorrow and informed her mother, saying: 'Sairindhri is most bitterly lamenting. Know this, if should you like.'

description: The parley between Damayanti and Sudeva
sn: अथ चेदिपतेर्माता राज्ञश्चान्तःपुरात् तदा। जगाम यत्र सा बाला ब्राह्मणेन सहाभवत्॥
en: Thereafter the mother of the king of the Nishadhas, having left the inner apartments of the palace, repaired to the place where that lady (Damayanti) was waiting with the Brahmana.

description: The parley between Damayanti and Sudeva
sn: ततः सुदेवमानाय्य राजमाता विशाम्यते। पप्रच्छ भार्या कस्येयं सुता वा कस्य भाविनी॥ कथं च नष्टा ज्ञातिभ्यो भर्तुर्वा वामलोचना। त्वया च विदिता विप्र कथमेवगंता सती॥
en: O the ruler of the earth! the Queen-mother summoned Sudeva before her and asked him, saying, 'whose wife is this lady? and whose daughter? and how this damsel, possessing handsome eyes has been separated from her husband as well as her relatives? O Brahmana! how have you come to know her, falling in this great distress?

description: The parley between Damayanti and Sudeva
sn: एतदिच्छाम्यहं श्रोतुं त्वत्तः सर्वमशेषतः। तत्त्वेन हि ममाचक्ष्व पृच्छन्त्या देवरूपिणीम्॥
en: I desire to hear from you all about her in detail. Do you surely relate to me, as I am asking of that lady of celestials splendour.”

description: The parley between Damayanti and Sudeva
sn: एवमुक्तस्तया राजन् सुदेवो द्विजसत्तमः। सुखोपविष्ट आचष्ट दमयन्त्या यथातथम्॥
en: O monarch! Sudeva, the foremost of the Brahmanas, thus addressed by the Queenmother, sat at his ease and began to relate the true account of Damayanti.

sn: सुदेव उवाच विदर्भराजोधर्मात्मा भीमो नाम महाद्युतिः। सुतेयं तस्य कल्याणी दमयन्तीति विश्रुता॥
en: Sudeva said: There is a virtuous and illustrious king of the Vidharbhas, named Bhima, whose daughter is this blessed lady, known by the name of Damayanti.

sn: राजा तु नैषधो नाम वीरसेनसुतो नलः। भार्येयं तस्य कल्याणी पुण्यश्लोकस्यधीमतः॥
en: Also there is the king of the Nishadhas, named Nala, who is the son of Virasena. This blessed damsel is the daughter of that virtuous and intelligent monarch.

sn: स घृतेन जितो भ्रात्रा हृतराज्यो महीपतिः। दमयन्त्या गतः सार्धं न प्राज्ञायत कस्यचित्॥
en: That ruler of the earth was defeated at dice by his brother; and, thereby deprived of his kingdom, went away with Damayanti without the knowledge of any body.

sn: ते वयं दमयन्त्यर्थे चरामः पृथिवीमिमाम्। सेयमासादिताः बाला तव पुत्रनिवेशने॥
en: We (the Brahmanas) are roving over the whole world for the sake of Damayanti, which lady is at last discovered in the palace of your son.

sn: अस्या रूपेण सदृशी मानुषी न हि विद्यते। अस्या ह्येष भ्रवोर्मध्ये सहज: पिप्लुरुत्तमः॥ श्यामाया: पद्मसंकाशो लक्षितोऽन्तर्हितो मया। मलेन संवृतो ह्यस्याश्छन्नोऽभ्रेणेव चन्द्रमाः॥
en: There exists no woman like her in beauty. This maiden of unchanging youth has a beautiful mark, from her birth, resembling a lotus. This freckle was seen by me; but now it has disappeared, owing to its being soiled with dust, even as the moon seems to vanish when covered over with clouds.

sn: चिह्नभूतो विभूत्यर्थमयंधात्रा विनिर्मितः। प्रतिपत्कलुषस्येन्दोर्लेखा नातिविराजते॥ न चास्य नश्यते रूपं वपुर्मलसमाचितम्। असंस्कृतमभिव्यक्तं भाति काञ्चनसंनिभम्॥ अनेन वपुषा बाला पिप्लुनानेन सूचिता। लक्षितेयं मया देवी निभृतोऽग्निरिवोष्मणा॥
en: That mark of prosperity and wealth, made and given to her by God, is now faintly seen, even as the crescent of the new moon does faintly shine, in the evening of the first day. Although her body is soiled with dust, yet her beauty has not suffered. And again her person, though not washed, is conspicuous and shines like gold. This celestials lady was ascertained by me by my identifying her form as well as that mark (between the eye-brows), even as fire though hid (in ashes) is ascertained by its heat.

sn: तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं तस्य सुदेवस्य विशाम्पते। सुनन्दा शोधयामास पिप्लुप्रच्छादनं मलम्॥
en: O monarch! Sunanda, having heard the words of Sudeva, cleaned the dust that soiled ile freckle (between the eye-brows of Damayanti).

sn: स मलेनापकृष्टेन पिप्लुस्तस्या व्यरोचत। दमयन्त्या यथा व्यभ्रे नभसीव निशाकरः॥
en: The mole of Damayanti, having been cleared of the bad dust, became conspicuous like the moon, which appears in the sky when the clouds are dispersed.

sn: पिप्लुं दृष्ट्वा सुनन्दा च राजमाता च भारत। रुदत्यौ तां परिष्वज्य मुहूर्तमिव तस्थतुः॥
en: O Bharata! seeing that mark, Sunanda as well as the mother of the king, wept; and, embracing her, stood there for some time.

sn: उत्सृज्य बाष्पं शनकै राजमातेदमब्रवीत्। भगिन्या दुहिता मेऽसि पिप्लुनानेन सूचिता॥
en: Shedding tcars and in a low voice, the Queen-mother said, 'Know by this your mole, you are the daughter of my sister.

sn: अहं च तव माता च राज्ञस्तस्य महात्मनः। सुते दशार्णाधिपतेः सुदाम्नश्चारुदर्शने॥
en: O handsome looking one! myself and your mother are the daughters of that illustrious king, Sudaman, who is the ruler of the Dasharnas.

sn: भीमस्य राज्ञः सा दत्ता वीरबाहोरहं पुनः। त्वं जाता मया दृष्टा दशार्णेषु पितुहे॥
en: She was given to king Bhima and myself was given to Virabahu. I saw you were born at our father's palace in the country of the Dasharmas.

sn: यथैव ते पितुर्गेहं तथैव मम भामिनि। यथैव च ममैश्वर्यं दमयन्ति तथा तव॥
en: O beauteous lady! as is your father's house, so is mine, to you. O Damayanti! my wealth is to you, cven as your own.

sn: तां प्रहप्टेन मनसा दमयन्ती विशाम्पते। प्रणम्य मातुर्भगिनीमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: O monarch! thereupon Damayanti, having bowed down unto her with a delightful heart,

sn: अज्ञायमानापि सती सुखमसम्युषिता त्वयि। सर्वकामैः सुविहिता रक्ष्यमाणा सदा त्वया॥ तु
en: “Although I stayed here unrecognised, still I lived with your happily and supplied with all the objects of my desire and ever protected by you.

sn: सुखात् सुखतरो वासो भविष्यति न संशयः। चिरविप्रोषितां मातामनुज्ञातुमर्हसि॥
en: Undoubtedly I shall have a happier abode than this. Therefore, O mother, grant permission unto me, who am ever living in exile.

sn: दारकौ च हि मे नीतौ वसतस्तत्र बालकौ। पित्रा विहीनौ शोकातॊ मया चैव कथं नु तौ॥
en: My children, the son and daughter, were led to my father's palace, where they are living now, hard pressed with sorrow on account of their separation from their father and mother.

sn: यदि चापि प्रियं किंचिन्मयि कर्तुमिहेच्छसि। विदर्भान् यातुमिच्छामि शीघ्रं मे यानमादिश॥ बाढमित्येव तामुक्त्वा हृष्टा मातृष्वसा नृप। गुप्तां बलेन महता पुत्रस्यानुमते ततः॥ प्रास्थापयद् राजमाता श्रीमती नरवाहिना। यानेन भरतश्रेष्ठ स्वन्नपानपरिच्छदाम्॥
en: Should you wish to do me some good order at once a vehicle; for I am desirous to go to the country of the Vidharbhas.” Thereupon, O monarch, saying, “So be it,” the sister of Damayanti's mother, the queen-mother highly satisfied and with the permission of her son, sent away Damayanti in a beautiful vehicle conveyed by men and guarded by a strong force, as also the lady, O the foremost of the descendants of Bharata, was provided with tasteful food and drink and valuable dresses.

sn: ततः सा न चिरादेव विदर्भानगमत् पुनः। तु बन्धुजनः सर्वः प्रहृष्टः समपूजयत्॥
en: Then the lady immediately went away to the country of the Vidharbhas, where all her friends and relatives, satisfied with her arrival, offered praises to her.

sn: सर्वान् कुशलिनो दृष्ट्वा बान्धवान् दारकौ च तौ मातरं पितरं चोभौ सर्वं चैव सखीजनम्॥ देवताः पूजयामास ब्राह्मणांश्च यशस्विनी। परेण विधिना देवी दमयन्ती विशाम्यते॥
en: O king, beholding that her relatives, her son and daughter, father and mother and all her companions were at peace, the goddess-like and all-glorious Damayanti worshipped the gods and the Brahmanas in the best way.

sn: अतर्पयत् सुदेवं च गोसहस्रेण पार्थिवः। प्रीतो दृष्ट्वैव तनयां ग्रामेण द्रविणेन च॥
en: The king, beholding his daughter, became gratified and presented to Sudeva a thousand kine, immense fortune and a village.

sn: सा व्युष्टा रजनीं तत्र पितुर्वेश्मनि भाविनी। विश्रान्ता मातरं राजन्निदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: O monarch! the handsome lady having spent there the whole night at her father's palace and taken perfect rest, addressed her mother thus:

sn: दमयन्त्युवाच मां चेदिच्छसि जीवन्ती मातः सत्यं ब्रवीमि ते। नलस्य नरवीरस्य यतस्वानयने पुनः॥
en: Damayanti said : O mother! should you desire me to live, I tell the truth, take care to bring here that hero among men, viz., Nala.

sn: दमयन्त्या तथोक्ता सा देवी भृशदुःखिता। बाष्पेणापिहिता राज्ञी नोत्तरं किंचिदब्रवीत्॥
en: Thus addressed by Damayanti,"the goddesslike queen became greatly afflicted with grief and was suffused with tears and spoke nothing to her in reply.

sn: तदवस्थां तु तां दृष्ट्वा सर्वमन्तःपुरं तदा। हाहाभूतमतीवासीद् भृशं च प्ररुरोद ह॥
en: Thereupon all the inmates of the king's harem uttered the exclamations of 'Oh'! and 'Alas'! at this dangerous situation of Damayanti and also wept most bitterly.

sn: ततो भीमं महाराजं भार्या वचनमब्रवीत्। दमयन्ती तव सुता भर्तारमनुशोचति॥
en: Then the queen spoke to the illustrious king, Bhima, thus: 'Your daughter, Damayanti, is lamenting, for her husband.

sn: अपकृष्य च लज्जां सा स्वयमुक्तवती नृप। प्रयतन्तां तव प्रेष्याः पुण्यश्लोकस्य मार्गणे॥
en: O monarch! unblushed with shame, Damayanti herself said that my men should try to find out the whereabouts of that virtuous king (Nala).

sn: तया प्रदेशितो राजा ब्राह्मणान् वशवर्तिनः। प्रास्थापयद् दिशः सर्वा यतध्वं नलमार्गणे॥
en: Thus urged by the queen, the king sent out the dependant Brahmanas in all directions; and enjoined them to strive to find out the whereabouts of king Nala.

sn: ततो विदर्भाधियतेर्नियोगाद् ब्राह्मणास्तदा। दमयन्तीमथो सृत्वा प्रस्थिता:स्मेत्यथाब्रुवन्।॥
en: Thereupon, at the injunction of the king of the Vidharbhas, all the Brahmanas approached Damayanti and told her that they were going away (for searching Nala).

sn: अथ तानब्रवीद् भैमी सर्वराष्ट्रेष्विदं वचः। ब्रुवध्वं जनसंसत्सु तत्र तत्र पुनः पुनः॥
en: Then the daughter of Bhima asked them to repeat, in all countries and before all crowds of men, these words.

sn: क्व नु त्वं कितवच्छित्त्वा वस्त्रार्धं प्रस्थितो मम। उत्सृज्य विपिने सुप्तामनुरक्तां प्रियां प्रिय॥
en: 'O gambler, O beloved one, did you tear off a half of my cloth and flee away forsaking your dear and devoted wife sleeping in the forest?

sn: सा वै यथा त्वया दृष्टा तथाऽऽस्ते त्वत्प्रतीक्षिणा दह्यमाना भृशं वाला वस्त्रार्थेनाभिसंवृता॥
en: 'Indeed, in obedience to your command that lady, covered in half a piece of cloth and greatly burning with woe, is ever expecting you.

sn: तस्या रुदत्याः सततं तेन शोकेन पार्थिव। प्रसादं कुरु वै वीर प्रतिवाक्यं ददस्व च॥
en: 'O monarch, O mighty one, do you answer; and do you show favour to her, who is ever weeping on account of that woe.'

sn: एवमन्यच्च वक्तव्यं कृपां कुर्याद् यथा मयि) वायुनाधूयमानो हि वनं दहति पावकः॥
