en: Do you cry, saying this and the like, viz., fire (here compared with grief of Damayanti), led by the wind (compared with time), consumes the forest (compared with the body of Damayanti); and then the lord will pity me.

sn: भर्तव्या रक्षणीया च पत्नी पत्या हि सर्वदा। तन्नष्टमुभयं कस्माद्धर्मज्ञस्य सतस्तव॥
en: Further do you cry, saying: "The wife is always to be maintained and protected by the husband. You are righteous and honest as well. Why, therefore, these virtues of yours are being neglected by you.

sn: ख्यातः प्राज्ञः कुलीनश्च सानुक्रोशो भवान् सदा। संवृत्तो निरनुक्रोशः शङ्के मद्भाग्यसंक्षयात्॥
en: You are well reputed, wise, respectable and always kind. But why now have you become unkind; and that is perhaps for the reason of my adverse fortune.

sn: तत् कुरुष्व नरव्याघ्र दयां मयि नरर्षभ। आनृशंस्यं परोधर्मस्त्वत्त एव हि मे श्रुतः॥
en: O foremost of men, O the most excellent of persons, be you kind to me. For I have heard from you, that kindness is the chief virtue.”

sn: एवं ब्रुवाणान् यदि वः प्रतिब्रूयात् कथंचन। स नरः सर्वथा ज्ञेयः कश्चासौ क्व नु वर्तते॥
en: If anybody answer you, as you would speak in this way, that man should be known by you in every way; and also it should be learnt what is he and where does he live.

sn: यश्चैवं वचनं श्रुत्वा ब्रूयात् प्रतिवचो नरः। तदादाय वचस्तस्य ममावेद्यं द्विजोत्तमाः॥
en: O excellent of the regenerate ones! do you convey to me the words of that man who, hearing these words of yours, will answer you.

sn: यथा च वो न जानीयाद् ब्रुवतो मम शासनात्। पुनरागमनं चैव तथा कार्यमतन्द्रितैः॥
en: Do you take care that no body should know that these words are uttered by you at my behest; neither do you do such to return to me.

sn: यदि वासौ समृद्धः स्याद् यदि वाप्यधनो भवेत्। यदि वाप्यसमर्थः स्याज्ज्ञेयमस्य चिकीर्षितम्॥
en: You should know whether the man is rich or poor or powerless; and know also his desires.

sn: एवमुक्तास्त्वगच्छंस्ते ब्राह्मणाः सर्वतो दिशम्। ते पुराणि नलं मृगयितुं राजंस्तदा व्यसनिनं तथा॥ सराष्ट्राणि ग्रामान् घोषांस्तथाऽऽश्रमान्। अन्वेषन्तो नलं राजन् नाधिजग्मुर्द्विजातयः॥
en: O king, thus advised, the Brahmanas departed in all directions in order to search for Nala, who had fallen into such great calamity. O monarch, the regenerate ones wandered in the cities, kingdoms, villages, the dwellings of the cowherds and the retreats of he sages in search of king Nala.

sn: तच्च वाक्यं तथा सर्वे तत्र तत्र विशाम्यते। श्रावयांचक्रिरे विप्रा दमयन्त्या यथेरितम्॥
en: O ruler of the earth, all the Brahmanas repeated the words, wherever they wandered, which Damayanti had enjoined them to do.

description: The declaration of Damayanti's second Svayamvara
sn: बृहदश्व उवाच अथ दीर्घस्य कालस्य पर्णादो नाम वै द्विजः। प्रत्येत्य नगरं भैमीमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Brihadashva said : After a very long time, a Brahmana, Parnada by name, came back to the city of the king of the Vidharbhas and spoke to the daughter of king Bhima these words:

description: The declaration of Damayanti's second Svayamvara
sn: नैषधं मृगयानेन दमयन्ति मया नलम्। अयोध्या नगरी गत्वा भाङ्गासुरिमुपस्थितः॥
en: “O Damayanti, searching Nala, the king of the Nishadhas, at last I went to the city of the Ayodhya and presented myself to Vangasuri.

description: The declaration of Damayanti's second Svayamvara
sn: श्रावितश्च मया वाक्यं त्वदीयं स महाजने। ऋतुपर्णो महाभागो यथोक्तं वरवर्णिनि॥ तच्छुत्वा नाब्रवीत् किंचिदृतुपर्णो नराधिपः। न च पारिषदः कश्चिद् भाष्यमाणो मयासकृत्॥
en: O fair-complexioned one, O best of women, I recited the very words of yours before that illustrious Rituparna. Hearing these words, which I had repeatedly uttered to them, neither king Rituparna, nor any one of his courtiers, said anything in reply.

description: The declaration of Damayanti's second Svayamvara
sn: अनुज्ञातं तु मां राज्ञा विजने कश्चिदब्रवीत्। ऋतुपर्णस्य पुरुषो बाहुको नाम नामतः॥
en: When I was dismissed by the king, some person in the service of Rituparna, Bahuka by name, told me in private.

description: The declaration of Damayanti's second Svayamvara
sn: सूतस्तस्य नरेन्द्रस्य विरूपो ह्रस्वबाहुकः। शीघ्रयानेषु कुशलो मृष्टकर्ता च भोजने॥
en: That Bahuka is the charioteer of that foremost of monarchs. He is also possessed of extraordinary appearance and short arms; and is skilled in driving with speed and also in cooking sweet food.

description: The declaration of Damayanti's second Svayamvara
sn: स विनिःश्वस्य बहुशो रुदित्वा च पुनः पुनः। कुशलं चैव मां पृष्ट्वा पश्चादिदमभाषत।॥
en: Sighing heavily and frequently and weeping incessantly, he asked about my welfare; and then addressed me with these words:

description: The declaration of Damayanti's second Svayamvara
sn: वैषम्यमपि सम्प्राप्ता गोपायन्ति कुलस्त्रियः। आत्मानमात्मना सत्यो जित: स्वर्गो न संशयः॥
en: 'Although fallen into great calamity, the chaste women guard themselves by their own efforts; and thus undoubtedly obtain heaven (heavenly blessings).

description: The declaration of Damayanti's second Svayamvara
sn: रहिता भर्तृभिश्चैव न कुप्यन्ति कदाचन। प्राणांश्चारित्रकवचान्धारयन्ति वरस्त्रियः॥
en: Again, chaste women, even if they be forsaken by their husbands, do never become angry (with them); rather they hold their lives shielded by virtuous behaviours.

description: The declaration of Damayanti's second Svayamvara
sn: विषमस्थेन मूढेन परिभ्रष्टसुखेन च। यत् सा तेन परित्यक्ता तत्र न क्रोद्भुमर्हति॥
en: She should not be angry, forsaken as she was by a person, who himself was foolish, overtaken by distress and also destitute of all happiness.

description: The declaration of Damayanti's second Svayamvara
sn: प्राणयात्रां परिप्रेप्सोः शकुनैर्हतवाससः। आधिभिर्दह्यमानस्य श्यामा न क्रोद्भुमर्हति॥
en: It behoves the lady of unchanging youth not to be angry with a person, who was deprived to his cloth by a bird while trying for sustenance (in the forest); and also who was burning with woe.

description: The declaration of Damayanti's second Svayamvara
sn: सत्कृतासत्कृता वापि पतिं दृष्ट्वा तथागतम्। भ्रष्टराज्यं श्रिया हीनं क्षुधितं व्यसनाप्लुतम्॥
en: Also, it behoves the lady, treated fairly or unfairly, not to be angry with her husband, seeing him in that miserable condition, in which he was deprived of both wealth and kingdom and oppressed with hunger and overwhelmed with distress.

description: The declaration of Damayanti's second Svayamvara
sn: तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा त्वरितोऽहमिहागतः। श्रुत्वा प्रमाणं भवती राज्ञश्चैव निवेदय॥
en: Hearing these words of his, I instantly came here. Do you, therefore, inform the king all about these words, which you have heard.”

description: The declaration of Damayanti's second Svayamvara
sn: एतच्छ्रुत्वाश्रुपूर्णाक्षी पर्णादस्य विशाम्पते। दमयन्ती रहोऽभ्येत्य मातरं प्रत्यभाषत॥
en: O monarch, hearing these words of Parnada, Damayanti, with her eyes filled with tears, repaired to her mother and said to her these words,

description: The declaration of Damayanti's second Svayamvara
sn: अयमर्थो न संवेद्यो भीमे मातः कदाचन। त्वत्संनिधौ नियोक्ष्येऽहं सुदेवं द्विजसत्तमम्॥ यथा न नृपतिर्भीमः प्रतिपद्येत मे मतम्। तथा त्वया प्रकर्तव्यं मम चेत् प्रियमिच्छसि॥
en: "O mother, let not king Bhima, by any means, know my object. I like to employ that foremost of the Brahmanas, Sudeva, in your presence. Should you desire my welfare, do you act in such a manner that king Bhima will not come to know this purpose of mine.

description: The declaration of Damayanti's second Svayamvara
sn: यथा चाहं समानीता सुदेवेनाशु बान्धवान्। तेनैव मङ्गलेनाशु सुदेवो यातु मा चिरम्॥ समानेतुं नलं मातरयोध्यां नगरीमितः।
en: Let Sudeva go at once, with the performance of the same auspicious ceremonies, by the doing of which I was brought to my relatives instantly by him. O mother, let him go hence to the city of Ayodhya in order to bring Nala here."

description: The declaration of Damayanti's second Svayamvara
sn: विश्रान्तं तु ततः पश्चात् पर्णादं द्विजसत्तमम्॥ अर्चयामास वैदर्भाधनेनातीव भाविनी। नले चेहागते तत्र भूयो दास्यामि ते वसु॥
en: Thereupon the beauteous lady, the daughter of the king of the Vidharbhas, worshipped, with the bestowal of immense riches, the foremost of the regenerate ones, who has now taken perfect rest. And she said to him, “O Brahmana, I will, again, give you much wealth at the arrival of Nala here.

description: The declaration of Damayanti's second Svayamvara
sn: त्वया हि मे बहु कृतं यदन्यो न करिष्यति। यद् भाहं समेष्यामि शीघ्रमेव द्विजोत्तम॥
en: O foremost of the regenerate ones, indeed you have done much for me, which none else will do; and for this reason only that I will soon regain my husband.”

description: The declaration of Damayanti's second Svayamvara
sn: स एवमुक्तोऽथाश्वास्य आशीर्वादैः सुमङ्गलैः। गृहानुपययौ चापि कृतार्थः सुमहामनाः॥
en: Thus addressed by her, that high-souled Brahmana solaced Damayanti by the expression of auspicious benedictions, and then he returned home, thinking himself successful in his endeavours.

description: The declaration of Damayanti's second Svayamvara
sn: ततः सुदेवमाभाष्य दमयन्ती युधिष्ठिर। अब्रवीत् संनिधौ मातुर्दुःखशोकसमन्विता॥
en: Thereupon, O Yudhishthira, Damayanti summoned Sudeva; and overwhelmed with grief and calamity, she addressed him in the presence of her mother thus,

description: The declaration of Damayanti's second Svayamvara
sn: गत्वा सुदेव नगरीमयोध्यावासिनं नृपम्। ऋतुपर्णं वचो ब्रूहि सम्पतन्निव कामगः॥
en: “O Sudeva, like a bird which falls straight, do you at once depart to the city of Ayodhya and tell king Ritupara, Who dwells in it, these words:

description: The declaration of Damayanti's second Svayamvara
sn: आस्थास्यति पुनर्भमी दमयन्ती स्वयंवरम्। तत्र गच्छन्ति राजानो राजपुत्राश्च सर्वशः॥
en: 'Damayanti, the daughter of king Bhima, will again hold the Svayamvara, to which all the kings and princes are rushing from all directions.

description: The declaration of Damayanti's second Svayamvara
sn: तथा च गणितः कालः श्वोभूते स भविष्यति। यदि सम्भावनीयं ते गच्छ शीघ्रमरिंदम्॥
en: Calculating the time, this will beheld tomorrow. So, if possible, O chastiser of foes, go at once.

description: The declaration of Damayanti's second Svayamvara
sn: सूर्योदये द्वितीयं सा भर्तारं वरयिष्यति। न हि स ज्ञायते वीरो नलो जीवति वा न वा॥
en: At the next sun-rise she will accept a second husband; as it is not known whether heroic Nala is still living or otherwise.'

description: The declaration of Damayanti's second Svayamvara
sn: एवं तया यथोक्तो वै गत्वा राजानमब्रवीत्। ऋतुपर्ण महाराज सुदेवो ब्राह्मणस्तदा।॥
en: O monarch, thus addressed by her, the Brahmana, Sudeva by name, started at once. He spoke to king Rituparna what he was ordered by her to do.

description: The departure of Rituparna for the Vidharbhas
sn: बृहदश्व उवाच श्रुत्वा वचः सुदेवस्य ऋतुपर्णो नराधिपः। सान्त्वयश्लक्ष्णया वाचा बाहुकं प्रत्यभाषत॥
en: Brihadashva said : Hearing these words of Sudeva, king Rituparna comforted Bahuka with sweet speeches and addressed him thus,

description: The departure of Rituparna for the Vidharbhas
sn: विदर्भान् यातुमिच्छामि दमयन्त्याः स्वयंवरम्। एकाला हयतत्त्वज्ञ मन्यसे यदि बाहुक॥
en: "O Bahuka, O you who are well-versed in the knowledge of horses, if you are willing, I desire to go, in course of a day, to the country of the Vidharbhas, where will be held the Svayamvara of Damayanti."

description: The departure of Rituparna for the Vidharbhas
sn: एवमुक्तस्य कौन्तेय तेन राज्ञा नलस्य ह। व्यदीर्यत मनो दुःखात् प्रदध्यौ च महामनाः॥
en: O descendant of Kunti, thus addressed by that king, Nala had his mind bursting with grief and that lofty-minded one also burned with sorrow.

description: The departure of Rituparna for the Vidharbhas
sn: दमयन्ती वदेदेतत् कुर्याद् दुःखेन मोहिता। अस्मदर्थे भवेद् वायमुपायश्चिन्तितो महान्॥
en: He thought “It may be that Damayanti, afflicted by sorrow, does this; or, perhaps, by doing this, she has conceived a great policy for my sake.

description: The departure of Rituparna for the Vidharbhas
sn: नृशंसं बत वैदर्भी भर्तृकामा तपस्विनी। मया क्षुद्रेण निकृता कृपणा पापबुद्धिना॥ स्त्रीस्वभावश्चलो लोके मम दोषश्च दारुणः। स्यादेवभपि कुयात् सा विवासाद् गतसौहृदा॥
en: That virtuous lady, the daughter of the king of the Vidharbhas, is willing to do this, is, indeed, very cruel; and that is for the reason of my deceiving her, who am an insignificant, sinful and senseless one. In this world, the nature of women is very subtle. My fault is also very great. She works out this end; for she no longer entertains any love for me, on account of my long separation from her.

description: The departure of Rituparna for the Vidharbhas
sn: मम शोकेन संविग्ना नैराश्यात् तनुमध्यमा। नैवं सा कर्हिचित् कुर्यात् सापत्या च विशेषतः॥
en: The lady, possessing slender waist, oppressed as she is by sorrow for me, will, as a matter of fact, not be able to do this; especially because she has got children (by me).

description: The departure of Rituparna for the Vidharbhas
sn: यदत्र सत्यं वासत्यं गत्वा वेत्स्यामि निश्चयम्। ऋतुपर्णस्य वै काममात्मार्थं च करोम्यहम्॥
en: I will go there and know for certain whether there is any truth in this; or the fact is unreal. I will surely fulfill the desire of Rituparna; for in doing this I will serve my own purpose."

description: The departure of Rituparna for the Vidharbhas
sn: इति निश्चित्य मनसा बाहुको दीनमानसः। कृताञ्जलिरुवाचेदमृतुपर्णं जनाधिपम्॥ प्रतिजानामि ते वाक्यं गमिष्यामि नराधिप। एकाह्रा पुरुषव्याघ्र विदर्भनगरी नृप॥
en: Having thus settled his mind, Bahuka, whose mind was filled with sorrow, folded his hands and said these words to king Rituparna, "O best of kings, O foremost of men, O monarch, I am determined at your command to go to the city of Ayodhya in course of a single day.”

description: The departure of Rituparna for the Vidharbhas
sn: ततः परीक्षामश्वानां चक्रे राजन् स बाहुकः। अश्वशालामुपागम्य भागासुरिनृपाज्ञया॥
en: O king, thereupon Bahuka went, at the behest of the royal son of Vangasura, to the stables; and there he examined the horses.

description: The departure of Rituparna for the Vidharbhas
sn: स त्वर्यमाणो बहुश ऋतुपर्णेन बाहुकः। अश्वाञ्जिज्ञासमानो वै विचार्य च पुनः पुनः। अभ्यगच्छत् कृशानश्वान् समर्थानध्वनि क्षमान्॥ तेजोबलसमायुक्तान् कुलशीलसमन्वितान्। वर्जिताँल्लक्षणैर्हनिः पृथुप्रोथान् महाहनून्॥
en: Bahuka, having been repeatedly asked by Rituparna, examined the horses and balanced in his mind over and over again. Then, at last, he selected such horses that were very lean but able; and also that are capable of bearing hardhips of a long journey and endued with strength and energy; well bred and gentle and unmarked by inauspicious marks; possessed of broad nostrils and swelling cheeks.

description: The departure of Rituparna for the Vidharbhas
sn: शुद्धान् दशभिरावर्तेः सिन्धुजान् वातरंहसः। दृष्ट्वा तानब्रवीद् राजा किंचित् कोपसमन्वितः॥
en: These horses were also faultless as regards 'the ten hairy curls' and born in the country called) Sindhu and swift as the wind. The king, seeing these steeds, became a little angry and said,

description: The departure of Rituparna for the Vidharbhas
sn: किमिदं प्रार्थितं कर्तुं प्रलब्धव्या न ते वयम्। कथमल्पबलप्राणा वक्ष्यन्तीमे हया मम। महदध्वानमपि च गन्तव्यं कथमीदृशैः॥
en: "What do you want to do? You should not jest with me. How these weak and breathless steeds will carry us? How this long way we would travel with the help of these horses?"

description: The departure of Rituparna for the Vidharbhas
sn: बाहुक उवाच एको ललाटे द्वौ मूर्ध्नि द्वौ द्वौ पार्थोपपार्श्वयोः। द्वौ द्वौ वक्षसि विज्ञेयौ प्रयाणे चैक एव तु॥ एते हया गमिष्यन्ति विदर्भान् नात्र संशयः॥ यानन्यान् मन्यसे राजन् ब्रूहि तान् योजयामि ते॥
en: Bahuka said: These horses, respectively bearing one curl on the forehead, two on the temples, four on the sides, four on the breast and one on the back, will, without doubt, reach the country of the Vidharbhas. But, O monarch, should you like others, tell me and I will yoke them for you.

description: The departure of Rituparna for the Vidharbhas
sn: ऋतुपर्ण उवाच त्वमेव हयतत्त्वज्ञः कुशलो ह्यसि बाहुक। यान् मन्यसे समर्थांस्त्वं क्षिप्रं तानेव योजय॥
en: Rituparna said: O Bahuka, you are well conversant with the knowledge and guiding of horses. Soon yoke those that you think fit.

description: The departure of Rituparna for the Vidharbhas
sn: ततः सदश्वांश्चतुरु कुलशीलसमन्वितान्। योजयामास कुशलो जवयुक्तान् रथे नलः॥
en: Thereupon clever and skillful Nala yoked to the car high-bred, gentle and swift steeds.

description: The departure of Rituparna for the Vidharbhas
sn: ततो युक्तं रथं राजा समारोहत् त्वरान्वितः। अथ पर्यपतन् भूमौ जानुभिस्ते हयोत्तमाः॥
en: Then the monarch most speedily mounted the car, to which such horses had been yoked. But these best of horses fell down upon the ground on their knees.

description: The departure of Rituparna for the Vidharbhas
sn: ततो नरवरः श्रीमान् नलो राजा विशाम्पते। सान्त्वयामास तानश्वांस्तेजोबलसमन्वितान्॥
en: O monarch, thereupon that most auspicious and best of men, king Nala, comforted the horse, that were endued with strength and energy.

description: The departure of Rituparna for the Vidharbhas
sn: रश्मिभिश्च समुद्यम्य नलो यातुमियेष सः। सूतमारोप्य वार्ष्णेयं जवमास्थाय वै परम्॥ ते चोद्यमाना विधिवद् बाहुकेन हयोत्तमाः। समुत्पेतुरथाकाशं रथिनं मोहयन्निव॥
en: Nala, then raising the steeds by the reins and making Varshneya, the charioteer, sit on the car, commanded great speed and set out. Thereafter those foremost of horses, having been conducted by Bahuka according to the rules, rose to the sky and confounded the occupant of the car.

description: The departure of Rituparna for the Vidharbhas
sn: तथा तु दृष्ट्वा तानश्वान् वहतो वातरंहसः। अयोध्याधिपतिः श्रीमान् विस्मयं परमं ययौ॥
en: The blessed king of Ayodhya, having seen these horses carrying him with the speed of winds, was struck with great astonishment.

description: The departure of Rituparna for the Vidharbhas
sn: रथघोषं तु तं श्रुत्वा हयसंग्रहणं च तत्। वार्ष्णेयश्चिन्तयामास बाहुकस्य हयज्ञताम्॥ किं नु स्यान्मातलिरयं देवराजस्य सारथिः। तथा तल्लक्षणं वीरे बाहुके दृश्यते महत्॥
en: Varshneya, hearing the sound of the car (of its wheels) and witnessing the management of the horses, was set to thinking on the knowledge of Bahuka in the science of steeds. He said, “Was he not Matali, the charioteer of the king of the gods? That auspicious mark is seen in heroic Bahuka.

description: The departure of Rituparna for the Vidharbhas
sn: शालिहोत्रोऽथ किं नु स्याद्धयानां कुलतत्त्ववित्। मानुषं समनुप्राप्तो वपुः परमशोभनम्॥
en: Is he not Salihotra, who is conversant with the knowledge of horses? Or Salihotra has taken this beautiful human form?"

description: The departure of Rituparna for the Vidharbhas
sn: उताहोस्विद् भवेद् राजा नल: परपुरंजयः। सोऽयं नृपतिरायात इत्येवं समचिन्तयत्॥
en: He continued to think, “That he might be king Nala, the reducer of hostile cities, who has come here.

description: The departure of Rituparna for the Vidharbhas
sn: अथ चेह नलो विद्यां वेत्ति तामेव बाहुकः। तुल्यं हि लक्षये ज्ञानं बाहुकस्य नलस्य च॥
en: Or it might be that Bahuka knew the science with which Nala was conversant; for Nala's knowledge seemed to be identical with that of Bahuka.

description: The departure of Rituparna for the Vidharbhas
sn: अपि चेदं वयस्तुल्यं बाहुकस्य नलस्य च। नायं नलो महावीर्यस्तद्धिद्यश्च भविष्यति॥
en: Again, both Nala and Bahuka seem to be of the same age. This person may not be identical with Nala of great energy; but he must be somebody of equal knowledge.

description: The departure of Rituparna for the Vidharbhas
sn: प्रच्छन्ना हि महात्मानश्चरन्ति पृथिवीमिमाम्। दैवेन विधिना युक्ताः शास्त्रोक्तैश्च निरूपणैः॥
en: Sometimes, indeed, great men rove over this world in disguise either ordained by mishap or in obedience to the dictates of the Shastras.

description: The departure of Rituparna for the Vidharbhas
sn: भवेन्न मतिभेदो मे गात्रवैरूप्यतां प्रति। प्रमाणात् परिहीनस्तु भवेदिति मतिर्मम॥
en: There should be no change of my opinion on account of his ugly appearance; rather my opinion is that this one has under gone some change in the body.

description: The departure of Rituparna for the Vidharbhas
sn: वय:प्रमाणं तत्तुल्यं रूपेण तु विपर्ययः। नलं सर्वगुणैर्युक्तं मन्ये बाहुकमन्ततः॥
en: This one is of the same age with him but there is some difference in the form. Again, he Bahuka gifted with all the accomplishments? Therefore I think he is Nala."

description: The departure of Rituparna for the Vidharbhas
sn: एवं विचार्य बहुशो वार्ष्णेयः पर्यचिन्तयत्। हृदयेन महाराज पुण्यश्लोकस्य सारथिः॥
en: O the foremost of kings, having deliberated upon this over and over again, Varshneya, the charioteer of virtuous Nala, went on thinking in his mind.

description: The departure of Rituparna for the Vidharbhas
sn: ऋतुपर्णश्च राजेन्द्रो बाहुकस्य हयज्ञताम्। चिन्तयन् मुमुदे राजा सहवार्ष्णेयसारथिः॥
en: Along with his charioteer, Varshneya, the excellent king Rituparna, highly delighted, was absorbed in the thought, regarding Bahuka's knowledge in the management of horses.

description: The departure of Rituparna for the Vidharbhas
sn: ऐकाग्र्यं च तथोत्साहं हयसंग्रहणं च तत्। परं यत्नं च सम्प्रेक्ष्य परां मुदमवाप ह॥
en: Also he was greatly delighted to behold the attentiveness and zeal of Bahuka, as also his manner of holding the reins and his skill in it. nin TCY ATT VTTTTTTTTTTT

sn: बृहदश्व उवाच स नदी: पर्वतांश्चैव वनानि च सरांसि च। अचिरेणातिचक्राम खेचरः खे चरनिव॥
en: Brihadashva said: As the bird course through the sky, so he (king Nala) speedily crossed the rivers, mountains, woods and lakes.

sn: तथा प्रयाते तु रथे तदा भाङ्गासुरिर्नृपः। उत्तरीयमधोऽपश्यद् भ्रष्टं परपुरजयः॥
en: While the car was thus coursing, the conqueror of hostile towns, the king Vangasura, saw his sheet drop down upon the ground.

sn: ततः स त्वरमाणस्तु पटे निपतिते तदा। ग्रहीष्यामीति तं राजा नलमाह महामनाः॥ निगृहणेष्व महाबुद्धे हयानेतान् महाजवान्। वार्ष्णेयो यावदेनं मे पटमानयतामिह॥
en: When the garinent had thus dropped down, then the lofty-minded king instantly expressed to Nala his desire to recover it. O you of profound intelligence, do you restrain these horses of great swiftness, until Varshneya bring me back my upper garment here.

sn: नलस्तं प्रत्युवाचाथ दूरे भ्रष्टः पटस्तवा योजनं समतिक्रान्तो नाहर्तुं शक्यते पुनः॥
en: Thereupon, Nala said to him in reply, “Your garment had dropped down far away; that is, we had advanced about eight miles from that place. It is, therefore, impossible to recover it.”

sn: एवमुक्तो नलेनाथ तदा भाङ्गासुरिर्नृपः। आससाद वने राजन् फलवन्तं बिभीतकम्॥
en: O monarch, having been thus addressed by Nala, the royal son of Vangasura came near a tree, called Vibhitaka with fruits, in the wood.

sn: तं दृष्ट्वा बाहुकं राजा त्वरमाणोऽभ्यभाषत। ममापि सूत पश्य त्वं संख्याने परमं बलम्॥
en: Beholding the tree, the king instantly said to Bahuka: “O charioteer, do you also see my great power of calculation.

sn: सर्वः सर्वं न जानाति सर्वज्ञो नास्ति कश्चन। नैकत्र परिनिष्ठास्ति ज्ञानस्य पुरुषे क्वचित्॥
en: All men do not know all things; in fact, there is none, who is acquainted with all the branches of knowledge. In one person, the knowledge in its entirety, is not centered.

sn: वृक्षेऽस्मिन् यानि पर्णानि फलान्यपि च बाहुक। पतितान्यपि यान्यत्र तत्रैकमधिकं शतम्॥ एकपत्राधिकं चात्र फलमेकं च बाहुका पञ्चकोट्योऽथ पत्राणां द्वयोरपि च शाखयोः॥ प्रचिनुगुह्यस्य शाखे द्वे याश्चाप्यन्याः प्रशाखिकाः। आभ्यां फलसहस्रे द्वे पञ्चोनं शतमेव च॥
en: O Bahuka, the leaves and fruits that have fallen from the tree (respectively) exceed the leaves and fruits, that are on the tree itself, by one hundred and one. O Bahuka, these two branches of the tree contain five millions of leaves. Examine the two branches and all their boughs and their fruits will number two thousand and ninety-five."

sn: ततो रथमवस्थाप्य राजानं बाहुकोऽब्रवीत्। परोक्षमिव मे राजन् कत्थसे शत्रुकर्शन॥ प्रत्यक्षमेतत् कर्तास्मि शातयित्वा विभीतकम्। अथात्र गणिते राजन् विद्यते न परोक्षता॥ प्रत्यक्षं ते महाराज शातयिष्ये बिभीतकम्। अहं हि नाभिजानामि भवेदेवं न वेति वा॥
en: Thereupon Bahuka stopped the car and addressed the king, “O monarch, O the chastiser of foes, you are saying to me what is beyond my power of perception. O king, I will make this matter perceptible (by my sense) by cutting down the tree Vibhitaka; and when I will really count, there nothing will remain to be supposed. O foremost of kings, I will hew down the tree Vibhitaka in your presence. I do not know whether what you say will really come to pass or not.

sn: संख्यास्यामि फलान्यस्य पश्यतस्ते जनाधिप। मुहूर्तमपि वार्ष्णेयो रश्मीन् यच्छतु वाजिनाम्॥
en: O ruler of men, I will number the fruits of the tree, while you will see it. Let Varshneya pull up the reins of the horses for a moment."

sn: तमब्रवीनृपः सूतं नायं कालो विलम्बितुम्। बाहुकस्त्वब्रवीदेनं परं यत्नं समास्थितः॥ प्रतीक्षस्व मुहूर्तं त्वमथवा त्वरते भवान्। एष याति शिवः पन्था याहि वार्ष्णेयसारथिः॥
en: The monarch asked the charioteer not to lose any time. But Bahuka, with great humility, answered him, saying, "Do you wait for a moment; or, if you are in a hurry, go then with Varshneya, as your charioteer. The way goes smooth and straight."

sn: अब्रवीदूतुपर्णस्तु सान्त्वयन् कुरुनन्दन। त्वमेव यन्ता नान्योऽस्ति पृथिव्यामपि बाहुक॥
en: O descendant of the Kuru race, king Rituparna, having comforted Bahuka, addressed him, saying: "O Bahuka, there is none else in this world, who is like you, as a charioteer.

sn: त्वत्कृते यातुमिच्छामि विदर्भान् हयकोविदा शरणं त्वां प्रपन्नोऽस्मि न विघ्नं कर्तुमर्हसि॥
en: O you versed in the equestrian science, I desire to go to the country of the Vidharbhas with your assistance. May I obtain your protection. It is necessary for you not to cause any obstacle.

sn: कामं च ते करिष्यामि यन्मां वक्ष्यसि बाहुक। विदर्भान् यदि यात्वाद्य सूर्यं दर्शयितासि मे॥
en: O Bahuka, I shall fulfill your desire, (that is, whatever you will tell me) if you take me today to the country of the Vidharbhas and make me see the sun-rise."

sn: अथाब्रवीद् बाहुकस्तं संख्याय मे बिभीतकम्। ततो विदर्भान् यास्यामि कुरुष्वैवं वचो मम॥
en: Thereupon Bahuka answered him, saying: "Having counted the (leaves and fruits of) Vibhitaka tree. I shall go to the country of the Vidharbhas. Act up to my words."

sn: अकाम इव तं राजा गणयस्वेत्युवाच ह। एकदेशं च शाखायाः समादिष्टं मयानघ॥ गणयस्वाश्वतत्त्वज्ञ ततस्त्वं प्रीतिमावह। सोऽवतीर्य रथात् तूर्णं शातयामास तं दुमम्॥
en: Surely the king most unwillingly said to him count. (He also said), “O unblameable one, O you versed in the knowledge of horses, having counted (the leaves and fruits of) one portion of this branch, you will be satisfied of the truth of my affirmation." He (Nala) then dismounted from the car with all haste and cut down the tree.

sn: ततः स विस्मयाविष्टो राजानमिदमब्रवीत्। गणयित्वा यथोक्तानि तावन्त्येव फलानि तु॥
en: Then again he numbered all the fruits; and found out the truth of what the king had said; and, thus struck with astonishment, he addressed the monarch, saying,

sn: अत्यद्भुतमिदं राजन् दृष्टवानस्मि ते बलम्। श्रोतुमिच्छामि तां विद्यां ययैतज्ज्ञायते नृप॥ तमुवाच ततो राजा त्वरितो गमने नृप। विद्ध्यक्षहदयज्ञं मां संख्याने च विशारदम्॥
en: "O king, this is most wonderful. I found your high proficiency (in calculation), O monarch, I desire to be informed of your art, by (virtue of) which you have known all this." Thereupon the prince, as he was most desirous to go speedily, said to him this" "Do you know that I am conversant with the play at dice and versed in calculation as well."

sn: बाहुकस्तमुवाचाथ देहि विद्यामिमां मम। मत्तोऽपि चाश्चहृदयं गृहाण पुरुषर्षभ॥
en: Then Bahuka said to him" "O foremost of men, do you impart this art to me and take from me my knowledge, regarding the management of horses."

sn: ऋतुपर्णस्ततो राजा बाहुकं कार्यगौरवात्। हयज्ञानस्य लोभाच्च तं तथेत्यब्रवीद् वचः॥
en: Thereupon king Rituparna, for the reason of the great importance of his business and also for his extreme desire to acquire the knowledge of horses, agreed to what Bahuka had said.

sn: यथोक्तं त्वं गृहाणेदमक्षाणां हृदयं परम्। निक्षेपो मेऽश्वहृदयं त्वयि तिष्ठतु बाहुका एवमुक्त्वा ददौ विद्यामृतुपर्णो नलाय वै॥
en: "As you have asked, do you take from me my great skill at dice. O Bahuka, let my knowledge of horses remain with you in trust. Thus saying, king Rituparna gave Nala his knowledge of the play at dice.

sn: तस्याक्षहृदयज्ञस्य शरीरानि:सृतः कलिः। कर्कोटकविषं तीक्ष्णं मुखात् सततमुद्वमन्॥ कलेस्तस्य तदार्तस्य शापाग्निः स विनिःसृतः। स तेन कर्शिता राजा दीर्घकालमनात्मवान्॥
en: When he (Nala) thus acquired the knowledge of this art of playing at dice Kali came out of his body; while he continued to vomit from his mouth the most virulent poison of Karkotaka. Then that fire of curse (by Damayanti), by which Kali had greatly been afflicted, also came out of his body. In fact, the king, like one of unregenerate soul, had long remained repressed by him (Kali).

sn: ततो विषविमुक्तात्मा स्वं रूपमकरोत् कलिः। तं शप्तुमैच्छत् कुपितो निषधाधिपतिर्नलः॥
en: Thereupon Kali, with his soul freed from the poison, assumed his own form. Then Nala, the prince of the Nishadhas, became angry and was intent upon cursing him.

sn: तमुवाच कलि तो वेपमानः कृताञ्जलिः। कोपं संयच्छ नृपते कीर्तिं दास्यामि ते पराम्॥
en: Kali became frightened; and, trembling with fear, folded his hands; and said to him this: “O king, restrain your anger and, in return, I will impart you great fame.

sn: इन्द्रसेनस्य जननी कुपिता माशपत् पुरा। यदा त्वया परित्यक्ता ततोऽहं भृशपीडितः॥
en: The mother of Indrasena cursed ine in wrath long ago, that is, at the time when she had been left by you. From that time forward I have greatly been oppressed (by that curse).

sn: अवसं त्वयि राजेन्द्र सुदुःखमपराजित। विषेण नागराजस्य दह्यमानो दिवानिशम्॥
en: O foremost of kings, O unconquered one, burning day and night in the poison of the prince of the snakes, I most miserably resided within you.

sn: शरणं त्वां प्रपन्नोऽस्मि शृणु चेदं वचो मम! ये च त्वां मनुजा लोके कीर्तयिष्यन्त्यतन्द्रिताः। मत्प्रसूतं भयं तेषां न कदाचिद् भविष्यति॥ भयार्तं शरणं यातं यदि मां त्वं न शप्स्यसे। एवमुक्तो नलो राजा न्ययच्छत् कोपमात्मनः॥
en: I place myself under your protection. Do you listen to these my words. Should you not curse me, who am seeking your protection and greatly terrified by you, then the men of this world, attentively repeating your story, will never have any fear on my account.” Having been thus said, king Nala suppressed his own wrath.

sn: ततो भीतः कलिः क्षिप्रं प्रविवेश बिभीतकम्। कलिस्त्वन्यैस्तदादृश्यः कथयन् नैषधेन वै॥
en: Thereupon Kali became terrified and instantly entered into the three Vibhitaka. While Kali, thus conversing with the king of the Nishadhas, was invisible to others.

sn: ततो गतज्वरो राजा नैषधः परवीरहा। सम्प्रणष्टे कलौ राजा संख्यायास्य फलान्युत॥ मुदा परमया युक्तस्तेजसाथ परेण वै। रथमारुह्य तेजस्वी प्रययौ जवनैर्हयैः॥
en: Thenceforth the king became freed from all afflictions; and, having numbered the fruits of the tree, he was filled with great joy and was endued with great energy. Then the mighty one mounted on the car; and, urging the swift steeds, proceeded onwards.

sn: बिभीतकश्चाप्रशस्तः संवृत्तः कलिसंश्रयात्। हयोत्तमानुत्पततो द्विजानिव पुनः पुनः॥ नलः संचोदयामास प्रहृष्टेनान्तरात्मना। विदर्भाभिमुखो राजा प्रययौ स महायशाः॥
en: Having been possessed by Kali, the Vibhitaka tree grew worthless. Highly satisfied at the very core of his heart, Nala urged the excellent horses which, like the birds, mounted again and again into the air. Thus the glorious monarch proceeded in the direction of the country of the Vidharbhas.

sn: नले त समतिक्रान्ते कलिरप्यगमद् गृहम्। ततो गतज्वरो राजा नलोऽभूत् पृथिवीपतिः। विमुक्तः कलिना राजन् रूपमात्रवियोजितः॥
en: When Nala went a long way off, Kali too returned home. Thus prince Nala, having been left by Kali, became delivered from all afflictions. But, O monarch, that ruler of the earth did not regain his native form.

description: Rituparna's entering the city of Bhima
sn: बृहदश्व उवाच ततो विदर्भान् सम्प्राप्तं सायाह्ने सत्यविक्रमम्। ऋतुपर्णं जना राज्ञे भीमाय प्रत्यवेदयन्॥
en: Brihadashva said: Thereupon king Rituparna of undaunted courage had, in the evening, arrived at the city of the Vidharbhas. The people then brought to prince Bhima the intelligence of his arrival.

description: Rituparna's entering the city of Bhima
sn: स भीमवचनाद् राजा कुण्डिनं प्राविशत् पुरम्।। नादयन् रथघोषेण सर्वाः स विदिशो दिशः॥
en: The king (of Ayodhya), at the request of Bhima, entered the city of Kundina, filling all the directions (the points of the horizon) with the rattle of his car.

description: Rituparna's entering the city of Bhima
sn: ततस्तं रथनिर्घोषं नलाश्वास्तत्र शुश्रुवुः। श्रुत्वा तु समहृष्यन्त पुरेव नलसंनिधौ॥
en: Thereupon the horses of Nala, that were there, heard the rattle of his car; and, having heard it, they felt great pleasure, which they had really done before in the presence of Nala himself.

description: Rituparna's entering the city of Bhima
sn: दमयन्ती तु शुश्राव रथघोषं नलस्य तम्। यथा मेघस्य नदतो गम्भीरं जलदागमे॥
en: Damayanti also heard the rattle of Nala's car, which was like the sound of the deeply rumbling clouds during the rains.

description: Rituparna's entering the city of Bhima
sn: परं विस्मयमापन्ना श्रुत्वा नादं महास्वनम्। नलेन संगृहीतेषु पुरेव नलवाजिषु। सदृशं स्थनिर्घोषं मेने भैमी तथा हयाः॥
en: She was struck with great astonishment to hear that sound. The daughter of king Bhima, the horses of Nala as well, supposed that chattering sound to be like one, which they heard in the days gone by, while Nala himself urged his own horses.

description: Rituparna's entering the city of Bhima
sn: प्रासादस्थाश्च शिखिनः शालास्थाश्चैव वारणाः। हयाश्च शुश्रुवुस्तस्य रथघोषं पहीपतेः॥
en: The peacocks of the palace, the elephants in the stables and also the horses, all heard the rattle of the car of that monarch (Rituparna).

description: Rituparna's entering the city of Bhima
sn: तच्छुत्वा रथनिर्घोषं वारणा: शिखिनस्तथा। प्रणेदुरुन्मुखा राजन् मेघनाद् इवोत्सुकाः॥
en: O king, hearing the chattering sound of the car, the elephants as well as the peacocks, began to cry aloud with their faces in that direction; and they became very glad, even as they heard the rumbling of the clouds themselves.

description: Rituparna's entering the city of Bhima
sn: दमयन्त्युवाच यथासौ रथनिर्घोषः पूरयन्निव मेदिनीम्। ममाह्लादयते चेतो नल एष महीपतिः॥
en: Damayanti said : As the rattle of this car fills the entire earth and highly delights my heart, it must be king Nala, who comes from that direction.

description: Rituparna's entering the city of Bhima
sn: अद्य चन्द्राभवक्त्रं तं न पश्यामि नलं यदि। असंख्येगुणं वीरं विनश्यामि न संशयः॥
en: If I do not see Nala, that hero of innumerable virtues and whose face is like the moon, surely I will die.

description: Rituparna's entering the city of Bhima
sn: यदि वै तस्य वीरस्य बाह्वोर्नाद्याहमन्तरम्। प्रविशामि सुखस्पर्श न भविष्याम्यसंशयम्॥
en: If I am not to enter within the arms of that hero and not to feel the pleasurable touch of his embrace, I will doubtlessly cease to exist.

description: Rituparna's entering the city of Bhima
sn: यदि मां मेघनिर्घोषो नोपगच्छति नैषधः। अद्य चामीकरप्रख्यं प्रवेक्ष्यामि हुताशनम्॥
en: If the king of the Nishadhas do not come to me with his voice as deep as the rumbling of the cloud, today I will surely enter into the fire of golden brilliance.

description: Rituparna's entering the city of Bhima
sn: यदि मां सिंहविक्रान्तो मत्तवारणविक्रमः। नाभिगच्छति राजेन्द्रो विनइक्ष्यामि न संशयः॥
en: If that foremost of kings, of prowess like that of a lion and of courage like that of a furious elephant, do not come to me, there will be no doubt that I will die.

description: Rituparna's entering the city of Bhima
sn: न स्मराम्यनृतं किंचिन्न स्मराम्यपकारताम्। न च पर्युषितं वाक्यं स्वैरेष्वपि कदाचन॥
en: I do not remember a little untruth in him; neither I remember any injury committed by him to others, nor he ever told a lie even in jest.

description: Rituparna's entering the city of Bhima
sn: प्रभुः क्षमावान् वीरश्च दाता चाप्यधिको नृपः। रहोऽनीचानुवर्ती च क्लीबवन्मम नैषधः॥
en: My Naishadha is illustrious forgiving, warlike and liberal. He is supcrior to other monarchs; and he never behaves with low persons regarding private matters; and he is like an eunuch respecting other women than myself.

description: Rituparna's entering the city of Bhima
sn: गुणांस्तस्य स्मरन्त्या मे तत्पराया दिवानिशम्। हृदयं दीर्यत इदं शोकात् प्रियविनाकृतम्॥
en: Remembering his virtues day and night, my mind is always directed towards him; and my heart is about to burst in grief on account of the absence of that beloved one.

description: Rituparna's entering the city of Bhima
sn: एवं विलपमाना सा नष्टसंज्ञेव भारत। आरुरोह महद् वेश्म पुण्यश्लोकदिदृक्षया॥
en: O descendant of the Bharata race, thus lamenting, the lady, as if senseless, mounted the (terrace of the) large palace with the desire of seeing that righteous king.

description: Rituparna's entering the city of Bhima
sn: ततो मध्यमकक्षायां ददर्श रथमास्थितम्। ऋतुपर्णं महीपालं सहवार्ष्णेयबाहुकम्॥ वै
en: From the central portion of the mansion she saw on the car king Rituparna, with Varshneya and Bahuka.

description: Rituparna's entering the city of Bhima
sn: ततोऽवतीर्य वार्ष्णेयो बाहुकश्च रथोत्तमात्। हयांस्तानवमुच्याथ स्थापयामास रथम्॥
en: Thereupon Varshneya, as well as Bahuka, alighted from that excellent car; and then loosened the steeds; and at last kept the car apart.

description: Rituparna's entering the city of Bhima
sn: सोऽवतीर्य रथोपस्थादृतुपर्णो नराधिपः। उपतस्थे महाराज भीमं भीमपराक्रमम्॥
en: Having alighted from the car, car, king Rituparna appeared before that excellent monarch, Bhima, of terrible prowess.

description: Rituparna's entering the city of Bhima
sn: तं भीमः प्रतिजग्राह पूजया परया ततः। स तेन पूजितो राज्ञा ऋतुपर्णो नराधिपः॥
en: Thereupon king Bhima received him with respectful offerings. Thus the best of the kings, Rituparna, was highly honoured by that inonarch.

description: Rituparna's entering the city of Bhima
sn: स तत्र कुण्डिने रम्ये वसमानो महीपतिः। न च किंचित् तदापश्यत् प्रेक्षमाणो मुहुर्मुहुः। स तु राज्ञा समागम्य विदर्भपतिना तदा॥ अकस्मात् सहसा प्राप्तं स्त्रीमन्त्रं न स्म विन्दति। किं कार्यं स्वागतं तेऽस्तु राजा पृष्टः स भारत॥
en: While residing in that beautiful city of Kundina, that ruler of the earth saw nothing (no signs of the Svayamvara) there, although he looked about all again and again. Then, at last, the lord of the Vidharbhas presented himself before that monarch and welcomed him. O descendant of the Bharata race, Bhima asked him on what business he was pleased to come there; for, in the absence of a proper occasion, an illustrious personage can not be had.

description: Rituparna's entering the city of Bhima
sn: नाभिजज्ञे स नृपतिर्दुहित्रर्थे समागतम्। ऋतुपर्णोऽपि राजा सधीमान् सत्यपराक्रमः॥ राजानं राजपुत्रं वा न स्म पश्यति कंचन। नैव स्वयंवरकथां न च विप्रसमागमम्॥ ततो व्यगणयद् राजा मनसा कोसलाधिपः। आगतोऽस्मीत्युवाचैनं भवन्तमभिवादकः॥
en: In fact Bhima did not know that he (Rituparna) had come to win the hands of his daughter. The intelligent king Rituparna, possessed of unbaffled power, beheld that there was neither a king nor a prince; nor he saw any gathering of Brahmanas; nor he heard any talk regarding the Svayamvara. Thereupon the ruler of Koshala ineditated in his mind and after a while addressed him, saying, "I have como here to pay you homage?"

description: Rituparna's entering the city of Bhima
sn: राजापि च स्मयन् भीमो मनसा समचिन्तयन्। अधिकं योजनशतं तस्यागमनकारणम्॥ ग्रमान् बहूनतिक्रम्य नाध्यगच्छद् यथातथम्। अल्पकार्य विनिर्दिष्टं तस्यागमनकारणम्॥
en: Struck with amazement, king Bhima reflected on the cause of Rituparna's visit, who had travelled more than a hundred yojanas. Bhima supposed, “That simply to pay him respects was not the reason of his coming there, after having passed over so many monarchs and crossed over countless villages.

description: Rituparna's entering the city of Bhima
sn: पश्चादुदर्के ज्ञास्यामि कारणं यद् भविष्यति। नैतदेवं स नृपतिस्तं सत्कृत्य व्यसर्जयत्॥
en: He attributes his arrival to a very slight cause. Be what it may. I will find out the reason in the future time.” Thus thinking, Bhima did not dismiss the monarch at once; rather he honoured him.

description: Rituparna's entering the city of Bhima
sn: विश्राम्यतामित्युवाच क्लान्तोऽसीति पुनः पुनः। स सत्कृतः प्रहृष्टात्मा प्रीतः प्रीतेन पार्थिवः॥ राजप्रेष्यैरनुगतो दिष्टं वेश्म समाविशत्। ऋतुपर्णे गते राजन् वार्ष्णेयसहिते नृपे॥ बाहुको रथमादाय रथशालामुपागमत्। स मोचयित्वा तानश्वानुपचर्य च शास्त्रतः॥
en: He also said to him again and again, “Do you take rest, as you are very weary.” Thus regarded by the pleased monarch, the ruler of the earth (Rituparna) was highly satisfied at the mind; and, with the gladness of his heart, repaired to his appointed quarters, accompanied by the servants of the royal household. O king, after king Rituparna had gone away with Varshneya, Bahuka caught hold of the car and took it to the stables. He then unyoked the horses and looked after them according to the rules.

description: Rituparna's entering the city of Bhima
sn: स्वयं चैतान् समाश्वास्य रथोपस्थ उपविशत्। दमयन्त्यपि शोकार्ता दृष्ट्वा भागासुरिं नृपम्॥ सुतपुत्रं च वार्ष्णेय बाहुकं च तथाविधम्। चिन्तयामास वैदर्भी कस्यैष रथनिःस्वनः॥
en: Thereafter Bahuka comforted the horses and seated himself on a side of the car; while Damayanti, the daughter of the king of the Vidharbhas, afflicted with grief, saw prince Vangasura and Varshneya, the son of the charioteer, as also Bahuka in that posture; and she continued to meditate upon, "Of whose car was the rattle?

description: Rituparna's entering the city of Bhima
sn: नलस्येव महानासीन च पश्यामि नैषधम्। वार्ष्णेयेन भवेन्नूनं विद्या सैवोपशिक्षिता॥ तेनाद्य रथनिर्घोषो नलस्येव महानभूत्। आहोस्विदूतुपर्णोऽपि यथा राजा नलस्तथा। यथायं स्थनिर्घोषो नैषधस्येव लक्ष्यते॥
en: This loud sound is like that of Nala's.car. But I do not find that prince of the Nishadhas. It is surely then that this are (of driving) was learnt by Varshneya. It is for this reason that the clattering sound of the car has been as loud as that of Nala. Or it may be, that king Rituparna is equal to Nala (in driving). Hence this rattle appears to be like that of the king of the Nishadhas."

description: Rituparna's entering the city of Bhima
sn: एवं सा तर्कयित्वा तु दमयन्ती विशाम्पत। दूतीं प्रस्थापयामास नैषधान्वेषणे शुभा॥
en: O lord of the earth, thus meditating, blessed Damayanti sent a female messenger in search of the king of the Nishadhas.

description: The colloquy between Nala and Keshini
sn: दमयन्त्युवाच गच्छ केशिनि जानीहि क एष रथवाहकः। उपविष्टो रथोपस्थे विकृतो हस्वबाहुकः॥
en: Damayanti said : OKeshini, do you go; and know who that charioteer is, sitting down on a side of the car, most unsightly and with short arms.

description: The colloquy between Nala and Keshini
sn: अभ्येत्य कुशलं भद्रे मृदुपूर्वं समाहिता। पृच्छेथाः पुरुषं ह्येनं यथातत्त्वमनिन्दिते॥
en: O gentle one, O blameless one, approaching him and becoming careful, do you ask his welfare; and do you enquire all the particulars about this person.

description: The colloquy between Nala and Keshini
sn: अत्र मे महती शङ्का भवेदेष नलो नृपः। यथा च मनसस्तुष्टिर्हदयस्य च निर्वृतिः॥
en: I am greatly afraid, lest this person be king Nala himself. For so great is the satisfaction of my mind, as also the easiness of my heart regarding this matter.

description: The colloquy between Nala and Keshini
sn: ब्रूयाश्चैनं कथान्ते त्वं पर्णादवचनं यथा। प्रतिवाक्यं च सुश्रोणि बुद्ध्येथास्त्वमनिन्दिते॥
en: O one of beautiful waist, unblameable one, after you have finished your enquiry, tell him the words of Parnada and understand his reply to them.

description: The colloquy between Nala and Keshini
sn: ततः समाहिता त्वा दूती बाहुकमब्रवीत्। दमयन्त्यपि कल्याणी प्रासादस्था [पैक्षत॥
en: Brihadashva said: Thereupon the female messenger carefully approached Bahuka and addressed him, while blessed Damayanti looked from her palace what would come to pass.

description: The colloquy between Nala and Keshini
sn: केशिन्युवाच स्वागतं ते मनुष्येन्द्र कुशलं ते ब्रवीम्यहम्। दमयन्त्या वचः साधु निबोध पुरुषर्षभ॥
en: Keshini said: O best of men, O excellent of persons, you are welcome! I wish you prosperity! Now listen to the words of Damayanti with attention.

description: The colloquy between Nala and Keshini
sn: कदा वै प्रस्थिता यूयं किमर्थमिह चागताः। तत् त्वं ब्रूहि यथान्यायं वैदर्भी श्रोतुमिच्छति॥
en: When did you start! What did you come here for? Tell me all the particulars; for the daughter of the king of the Vidharbhas wishes to hear all about these.

description: The colloquy between Nala and Keshini
sn: बाहुक उवाच राज्ञा कोसलेन श्रुतः स्वयंवरो महात्मना। द्वितीयो दमयन्त्या वै भविता श्व इति द्विजात्॥
en: Bahuka said: The high-souled monarch of Koshala had learnt from a Brahmana that there would be held a second Svayamvara of Damayanti.

description: The colloquy between Nala and Keshini
sn: श्रुत्वैतत् प्रस्थितो राजा शतयोजनयायिभिः। हयैर्वातजवैर्मुख्यैरहमस्य च सारथिः॥
en: Hearing this, the monarch and myself as his charioteer, set out with excellent steeds, that are capable of travelling one hundred yojanas and that are as fleet as the wind itself.

description: The colloquy between Nala and Keshini
sn: केशिन्युवाच अथ योऽसौ तृतीयो व: स कुतः कस्य वा पुनः। त्वं च कस्य कथं चेदं त्वयि कर्म समाहितम्॥
en: Keshini said: Whence is the third among you come? And, again, whose (son) is he? Whose (son) are you and how has this work been performed by you?

description: The colloquy between Nala and Keshini
sn: बाहुक उवाच पुण्यश्लोकस्य वै सूतो वार्ष्णेय इति विश्रुतः। स नले विद्रुते भद्रे भाङ्गासुरिमुपस्थितः॥
en: Bahuka said : Indeed, he is the charioteer of righteous Nala; and is known by the name of Varshneya. O blessed one, after Nala had been deprived of his kingdom, he came to the royal son of Vangasura.

description: The colloquy between Nala and Keshini
sn: अहमण्यश्वकुशलः सूतत्वे च प्रतिष्ठितः। ऋतुपर्णेन सारथ्ये भोजने च वृतः स्वयम्॥
en: I am too, well versed in the management of horses, and hence I have been appointed as a charicteer. King Rituparna himself appointed me to be his charioteer as well as his cook.

description: The colloquy between Nala and Keshini
sn: केशिन्युवाच अथ जानाति वार्ष्णेयः क्व नु राजा नलो गतः। कथं च त्वयि वा तेन कथितं स्यात् तु बाहुक॥
en: Keshini said: O Bahuka, Varshneya perhaps knows where has king Nala gone. He also may have told you about him.

description: The colloquy between Nala and Keshini
sn: बाहुक उवाच इहैव पुत्रौ निक्षिप्य नलस्य शुभकर्मणः। गतस्ततो यथाकाम नैष जानाति नैषधम्॥
en: Bahuka said: Having brought here the children of Nala, of golden deeds, he (Varshneya) then repaired to wherever he wished. Indeed, he does not know where the king of the Nishadhas is.

description: The colloquy between Nala and Keshini
sn: न चान्यः पुरुषः कश्चिन्नलं वेत्ति यशस्विनि। गूढश्चरति लोकेऽस्मिन् नष्टरूपे महीपतिः॥
en: O glorious one, no other person knows the whereabouts of king Nala; for a king (in distress) roves about in the world unawares and with an unsightly appearance.

description: The colloquy between Nala and Keshini
sn: आत्मैव त नलं वेद या चास्य तदनन्तरा। न हि वै स्वानि लिङ्गानि नलः शंसति कर्हिचित्॥
en: Nala's self only knows Nala; and she also knows him, who is his second self. Indeed, Nala never shows his own marks anywhere.

description: The colloquy between Nala and Keshini
sn: केशिन्युवाच योऽसावयोध्यां प्रथमं गतोऽसौ ब्राह्मणस्तदा। इमानि नारीवाक्यानि कथयानः पुनः पुनः॥
en: Keshini said : The Brahmana, who had first gone to the city of Ayodhya, uttered again and again these expressions, suitable to the lips of a female:

description: The colloquy between Nala and Keshini
sn: क्व नु त्वं कितवच्छित्त्वा वस्त्रार्धं प्रस्थितो मम। उत्सृज्य विपिने सुप्तामनुरक्तां प्रियां प्रिय॥
en: "O gambler, O dear one, where have you gone, tearing off half my garment and forsaking me, your devoted and beloved wife, asleep in the forest.

description: The colloquy between Nala and Keshini
sn: सा वै यथा समादिष्टा तथाऽऽस्ते त्वत्प्रतीक्षिणी दह्यमाना दिवा रात्रौ वस्त्रार्धेनाभिसंवृता॥
en: Indeed, she herself, enjoined by you, remains there, expecting to receive you, clad only in half a piece of cloth and burning whole day and night in sorrow.

description: The colloquy between Nala and Keshini
sn: तस्या रुदन्त्याः सततं तेन दुःखेन पार्थिव। प्रसादं कुरु मे वीर प्रतिवाक्यं वदस्व च॥
en: O monarch, O mighty one, as she is incessantly lamenting for that distress; so be you kind and give answer to her words.

description: The colloquy between Nala and Keshini
sn: तस्यास्तत् प्रियमाख्यानं प्रवदस्व महामते। तदेव वाक्यं वैदर्भी श्रोतुमिच्छत्यनिन्दिता॥
en: O high-minded one, do you recite that story agreeable to her, which words that blameless daughter of Vidharbha wishes to hear.”

description: The colloquy between Nala and Keshini
sn: एतच्छ्रुत्वा प्रतिवचस्तस्य दत्तं त्वया किल। यत् पुरा तत् पुनस्त्वत्तो वैदर्भी श्रोतुमिच्छति॥
en: Hearing these words (as above), you formerly gave answer to the Brahmanas. As you did before, so do now; for the daughter of the king of the Vidharbhas wishes to hear them in detail.

description: The colloquy between Nala and Keshini
sn: बृहदश्व उवाच एवमुक्तस्य केशिन्या नलस्य कुरुनन्दन। हृदयं व्यथितं चासीदश्रुपूर्णे च लोचने॥
en: Brihadashva said : O descendant of the Kuru race, hearing these words of Keshini, Nala's heart became afflicted with grief; and his eyes, too, were filled with tears.

description: The colloquy between Nala and Keshini
sn: स निगृह्यात्मनो दुःखं दह्यमानो महीपतिः। वाष्पसंदिग्धया वाचा पुनरेवेदपद्रवीत्॥
en: Having suppressed his grief and burning with sorrow, the lord of the earth uttered again these words in a voice choked with tears.

description: The colloquy between Nala and Keshini
sn: बाहुक उवाच वैषम्यमपि सम्प्राप्ता गोपायन्ति कुलस्त्रियः। आत्मानमात्मना सत्यो जितः स्वर्गो न संशयः॥
en: Bahuka said: Chaste women, falling in distress, protect themselves by their own efforts and thus doubtlessly obtain heaven.

description: The colloquy between Nala and Keshini
sn: रहिता भर्तृभिश्चापि न क्रुध्यन्ति कदाचन। प्राणांश्चारित्रकवचान्धारयन्ति वरस्त्रियः॥
en: The women, that are the best, become never angry and hold their lives, protected by the armour of good character, even if they be left by their husbands.

description: The colloquy between Nala and Keshini
sn: विषमस्थेन मूढेन परिभ्रष्टसुखेन च। यत् सा तेन परित्यक्ता तत्र न क्रोधुमर्हति॥
en: Because she has been abandoned by one, who himself has fallen in distress and who is foolish and deprived of all happiness. She, therefore, should not be angry.

description: The colloquy between Nala and Keshini
sn: प्राणयात्रां परिप्रेप्सोः शकुनैर्हतवाससः। आधिभिर्दह्यमानस्य श्यामा न क्रोद्भुमर्हति॥
en: The lady of unchanging youth should not be angry with one, who deprived of his cloth by the birds, while seeking his food in the forest, is ever burning in grief.

description: The colloquy between Nala and Keshini
sn: सत्कृतासत्कृता वापि पतिं दृष्ट्वा तथाविधम्। राज्य भ्रष्टं श्रिया हीनं क्षुधितं व्यसनाप्लुतम्॥
en: Behaved well or badly, the lady should not be angry with her husband, when he is in that miserable condition (that he is deprived of his kingdom and happiness); and also he is overtaken by hunger and distress.

description: The colloquy between Nala and Keshini
sn: एवं ब्रुवाणस्तद् वाक्यं नलः परमदुर्मनाः। न वाष्यमशकत् सोढुं प्ररुरोद च भारत।॥
en: O Bharata, while speaking these words, Nala, afflicted with calamity, could not check the flow of his tears and began to weep bitterly.

description: The colloquy between Nala and Keshini
sn: ततः सा केशिनी गत्वा दमयन्त्यै न्यवेदयत्। तत् सर्वं कथितं चैव विकारं तस्य चैव तम्॥
en: Thereupon Keshini went away and informed everything to Damayanti regarding that discourse (between herself and Nala), as also the overtaking of his calamity.

sn: बृहदश्व उवाच दमयन्ती तु तच्छ्रुत्वा भृशं शोकपरायणा। शङ्कमाना नलं तं वै केशिनीमिदमब्रवीत्॥
en: Brihadashva said : Having heard all these, Damayanti became afflicted with sorrow; and, suspecting that le must be Nala, addressed Keshini, saying,

sn: गच्छ केशिनि भूयस्त्वं परीक्षां कुरु बाहुके। अब्रुवाणा समीपस्था चरितान्यस्य लक्षय॥
en: "O Keshini, do you go again and scrutinize the conduct of Bahuka; and keeping yourself in silence at his side, behold all his bevaviours.

sn: यदा च किंचित् कुर्यात् स कारणं तत्र भामिनि। तत्र संचेष्टमानस्य लक्षयन्ती विचेष्टितम्॥
en: O beautiful one, find out the cause, whenever he does anything; and marks well whenever he performs anything skillful.

sn: न चास्य प्रतिबन्धेन देयोऽग्निरपि केशिनि। याचते न जलं देयं सर्वथा त्वरमाणया॥
en: O Keshini, whenever he may ask fire or water, you will not be in a hurry to give it; and thus obstruct him.

sn: एतत् सर्वं समीक्ष्य त्वं चरितं मे निवेदया निमित्तं यत् त्वया दृष्टं बाहुके दैवमानुषम्॥ यच्चान्यदपि पश्येथास्तच्चाख्येयं त्वया मम।
en: "Seeing all these, do you let me know his conduct, as also what human or super-human will be seen in Bahuka. Do you also report to me what else you will see in him."

sn: दमयन्त्यैवमुक्ता सा जगामाथ च केशिनी॥ निशम्याथ हयज्ञस्य लिङ्गानि पुनरागमत्।
en: Thus spoken by Damayanti, Keshini went away. Having learnt the behaviours of that person, who was versed in the knowledge of horses, Keshini returned.

sn: सा तत् सर्वं यथावृत्तं दमयन्त्यै न्यवेदयत्। निमित्तं यत् तया दृष्टं बाहुके दैवमानुषम्॥
en: She reported to Damayanti the whole history, mentioning what human superhuman she saw in Bahuka.

sn: केशिन्युवाच दृढं शुच्युपचारोऽसौ न मया भानुषः क्वचित्। दृष्टपूर्वः श्रुतो वापि दमयन्ति तथाविधः॥
en: Keshini said: O Damayanti, I have never heard or seen before any person of his character, having so great a 'power over the elements.'

sn: ह्रस्वमासाद्य संचारं नासौ विनमते क्वचित्। तं तु दृष्ट्वा यथासंगमुत्सर्पति यथासुखम्॥
en: Whenever he comes to a narrow hole, he never stoops low; rather the hole opens wide at his touch; and he easily passes through it.

sn: संकटेऽप्यस्य सुमहान् विवरो जायतेऽधिकः। ऋतुपर्णस्य चार्थाय भोजनीयमनेकशः॥ प्रेषितं तत्र राज्ञा तु मांसं चैव प्रभूतवत्। तस्य प्रक्षालनार्थाय कुम्भास्तत्रोपकल्पिताः॥
en: Thus a small hole grows largely wide at his coming. There were sent by the king (Bhima) various sorts of food, as also flesh of many animals, for Rituparna. There were also many vessels sent for washing the flesh.

sn: ते तेनावेक्षिताः कुम्भाः पूर्णा एवाभवंस्ततः। ततः प्रक्षालनं कृत्वा समधिश्रित्य बाहुकः॥ तृणमुष्टिं समादाय सवितुस्तं समादधत्। अथ प्रज्वलितस्तत्र सहसा हव्यवाहनः॥
en: Those vessels, whenever looked at by him (Bahuka), became at once filled with water. Thereupon Bahuka washed them and set himself to cooking. Then again he grasped a handful of grass and held it to the sun, where suddenly fire blazed up.

sn: तदद्भुततमं दृष्ट्वा विस्मिताहमिहागता। अन्यच्च तस्मिन् सुमहदाश्चर्यं लक्षितं मया।॥
en: Beholding that greatest wonder, I was struck with astonishment and have come hither. Also another great wonder was marked by me in him.

sn: यदग्निमपि संस्पृश्य नैवासौ दह्यते शुभे। छन्देन चोदकं तस्य वहत्यावर्जितं दुतम्॥
en: O beautiful one, although he touched fire, still he was not burnt. The water, falling at his command, flowed rapidly.

sn: अतीव चान्यत् सुमहदाश्चर्यं दृष्टवत्यहम्। यत् स पुष्पाण्युपादाय हस्ताभ्यां ममृदे शनैः॥ मृद्यमानानि पाणिभ्यां तेन पुष्पाणि नान्यथा। भूय एव सुगन्धीनि हृषितानि भवन्ति हि। एतान्यद्भुतलिङ्गानि दृष्ट्वाहं दुतमागता॥
en: I have marked another wonder, which was extraordinarily great, that he took some flowers in his hands and pressed them slowly. Although these flowers were pressed by him with the hands, yet they, instead of losing their original forms, became more fragrant and beautiful than before. Observing those marks of wonder, I have hastily come here.

sn: बृहदश्व उवाच दमयन्ती तु तच्छ्रुत्वा पुण्यश्लोकस्य चेष्टितम्। अमन्यत नलं प्राप्तं कर्मचेष्टाभिसूचितम्॥
en: Brihadashva said : Having heard of those wonderful behaviours of that righteous one and having known him by his acts, Damayanti considered that Nala was obtained.

sn: सा शङ्कमाना भर्तारं बाहुकं पुनरिङ्गितैः। केशिनीं श्लक्ष्णया वाचा रुदती पुनरब्रवीत्॥ पुनर्गच्छ प्रमत्तस्य बाहुकस्योपसंस्कृतम्। महानसाद् द्रुतं मांसमानयस्वेह भाविनि॥ सा गत्वा बाहुकस्याचे तन्मांसमपकृष्य च। अत्युष्णमेव त्वरिता तत्क्षणात् प्रियकारिणी॥
en: Again, by these marks suspecting Bahuka to be her husband, Damayanti wept and again addressed Keshini in a sweet speech, "O handsome one, do you go again and fetch here from the kitchen, without the knowledge of Bahuka, some meat cooked by him." The beneficent lady instantly went to Bahuka; and immediately returned, taking some hot meat therefrom.

sn: दमयन्त्यै ततः प्रादात् केशिनी कुरुनन्दन। सो चिता नलसिद्धस्य मांसस्य बहुशः पुरा॥
en: O descendant of the Kuru race, thereupon Keshini gave the meat to Damayanti, who had, during the past days, very often tasted meat boiled by Nala.

sn: प्राश्य मत्वा नलं सूतं प्राक्रोशद् भृशदुःखिता। वैक्लव्यं परमं गत्वा प्रक्षाल्य च मुखं ततः॥ मिथुनं प्रेषयामास केशिन्या सह भारत। इन्द्रसेनां सह भ्रात्रा समभिज्ञाय बाहुकः॥ अभिद्रुत्य ततो राजा परिष्वज्याङ्कमानयत्। बाहुकस्तु समासाद्य सुतौ सुरसुतोपमौ॥ भृशं दुःखपरीतात्मा सुस्वरं प्ररुरोद ह। नैषधो दर्शयित्वा तु विकारमसकृत् तदा। उत्सृज्य सहसा पुत्रौ केशिनीमिदमब्रवीत्॥
en: Thus tasting the meat brought by her female servant, she decided the charioteer to be Nala himself; and, inuch aggrieved, she wept bitterly. Overtaken by great calamity, she then washed her face. O Bharata, thereafter she sent her two children with Keshini. Bahuka recognised Indrasena with her brother. Thereupon the monarch (in the guise of Bahuka) came up speedily and, embracing his children, placed them on his lap. Then again, embracing his children, who were like the children of the celestials, Bahuka became filled with the greatest misery and wept bitterly in a soft voice. Thus having cxprcsscd his mental derangement over and over again, the prince of the Nishadhas left the children all on a sudden and spoke Keshini there words,

sn: इदं च सदृशं भद्रे मिथुनं मम पुत्रयोः। अतो दृष्ट्वैव सहसा बाष्पमुत्सृष्टवानहम्॥
en: "O beauteous one, these twins are like iny own children. Hence seeing them suddenly, I shed tears.

sn: बहुशः सम्पतन्तीं त्वां जनः संकेतदोषतः। वयं च देशातिथयो गच्छ भद्रे यथासुखम्॥
en: If you come to me very often, people may think evil; because we are men of other country. So, O handsome one, do you go away hence with ease."

description: The union of Nala and Damayanti
sn: बृहदश्व उवाच सर्वं विकारं दृष्ट्वा तु पुण्यश्लोकस्यधीमतः। आगत्य केशिनी सर्वं दमयन्त्यै न्यवेदयत्॥
en: Brihadashva said: Having learnt all about the mental agony of that righteous and wise one, Keshini came back and spoke everything to Damayanti.

description: The union of Nala and Damayanti
sn: दमयन्ती ततो भूयः प्रेषयामास केशिनीम्। मातुः सकाशं दुःखार्ता नलदर्शनकाक्षया॥
en: Thereupon Damayanti sent again Keshini to her mother; as she, sorely aggrieved, was most desirous to see Nala.

description: The union of Nala and Damayanti
sn: परीक्षितो मे बहुशो बाहुको नलशङ्कया। रूपे मे संशयस्त्वेकः स्वयमिच्छामि वेदितुम्॥
en: Damayanti said: “Suspecting Bahuka to be Nala, I have examined him several times; but I have some doubt about his appearance, which I like to know myself.

description: The union of Nala and Damayanti
sn: स वा प्रवेश्यतां माताँ वानुज्ञातुमर्हसि। विदितं वाथवा ज्ञातं पितुर्मे संविधीयताम्॥
en: O mother, with or without the knowledge of my father, make this arrangement for me; either allow him to enter my mansion or give me permission to go to him.”

description: The union of Nala and Damayanti
sn: एवमुक्ता तु वैदा सा देवी भीममब्रवीत्। दुहितुस्तमभिप्रायमन्वजानात् स पार्थिवः॥
en: Thus spoken by Vaidharbhi, that lady told king Bhima the intention of his daughter, which the king learned.

description: The union of Nala and Damayanti
sn: सा वै पित्राभ्यनुज्ञाता मात्रा च भरतर्षभ। नलं प्रवेशयामास यत्र तस्याः प्रतिश्रयः॥ तां स्म दृष्ट्वैव सहसा दमयन्ती नलो नृपः। आविष्टः शोकदुःस्वाभ्यां बभूवाश्रुपरिप्लुतः॥
en: O foremost of men, Damayanti obtained the permission of both her father and mother; and thus she caused Nala to enter her own apartments. Unexpectedly beholding Damayanti, prince Nala became oppressed with grief and calamity; as also she was overwhelmed with tears.

description: The union of Nala and Damayanti
sn: तं तु दृष्ट्वा तथायुक्तं दमयन्ती नलं तदा। तीव्रशोकसमाविष्टा बभूव वरवर्णिनी॥
en: Then that excellent of women, Damayanti, beholding Nala is that plight, was greatly afflicted with sorrow.

description: The union of Nala and Damayanti
sn: ततः काषायवसना जटिला मलपङ्किनी। दमयन्ती महाराज बाहुकं वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
en: Thereupon, O great king, Damayanti, who was dressed in a red garment, wearing matted hairs and tainted with clay and dust, spoke these words do Bahuka:

description: The union of Nala and Damayanti
sn: पूर्वं दृष्टस्त्वया कश्चिद्धर्मज्ञो नाम बाहुका सुप्तामृत्सृज्य विपिने गतो यः पुरुषः स्त्रियम्॥
en: "O Bahuka, did you ever see any men, who, known as virtuous, had gone away leaving his wife asleep in the woods?

description: The union of Nala and Damayanti
sn: अनागसं प्रियां भार्यां विजने श्रममोहिताम्। अपहाय तु को गच्छेत् पुण्यश्लोकमृते नलम्॥
en: Who excepts that righteous Nala, could go away, abandoning his beloved hand unoffending wife in the woods, when she was overtaken by fatigue?

description: The union of Nala and Damayanti
sn: किमु तस्य मया बाल्यादपराद्धं महीपतेः। यो मामुत्सृज्य विपिने गतवान् निद्रयार्दिताम्॥
en: What offence did I give to that ruler of the earth since my youth, for which he had gone away forsaking me in the woods; while I was overpowered by sleep?

description: The union of Nala and Damayanti
sn: साक्षाद् देवानपाहाय वृतो यः स पुरा मया। अनुव्रतां साभिकामां पुत्रिणीं त्यक्तवान् कथम्॥
en: Formerly I had selected him as my lord, rejecting the very celestials. Therefore how it was that he should abandon his wife, who am ever devoted and dear to him as also the mother of his children?

description: The union of Nala and Damayanti
sn: अग्नौ पाणिं गृहीत्वा तु देवानामग्रतस्तथा। भविष्यामीति सत्यं तु प्रतिश्रुत्य क्व तद् गतम्॥
en: He had taken my hand; and, before the fire and in the presence of all the gods, he had pledged that he would truly be mine. But where now was that pledge gone?"

description: The union of Nala and Damayanti
sn: दमयन्त्या ब्रुवन्त्यास्तु सर्वमेतदरिंदम्। शोकजं वारि नेत्राभ्यामसुखं प्रास्रवद् बहु॥
en: O chastiser of foes, while Damayanti was speaking all these, tears of sorrow flowed copiously from her eyes.

description: The union of Nala and Damayanti
sn: अतीव कृष्णसाराभ्यां रक्तान्ताभ्यां जलं तु तत्। परिस्रवन् नलो दृष्ट्वा शोकार्तामिदमब्रवीत्।॥
en: When Nala saw her thus oppressed with sorrow, he also shed tears from his eyes, which were black like those of the gazelle, with red extremities; and addressed her, saying:

description: The union of Nala and Damayanti
sn: मम राज्यं प्रणष्टं यन्नाहं तत् कृतवान् स्वयम्। कलिना तत् कृतं भीरु यच्च त्वामहमत्यजम्॥
en: "O timid one, the loss of my kingdom was not wrought by me. It was done by Kali, on whose account I had abandoned you in the woods.

description: The union of Nala and Damayanti
sn: यत् त्वयाधर्मकृच्छ्रे तु शापेनाभिहतः पुरा। वनस्थया दुःखितया शोचन्त्या मां दिवानिशम्॥ स मच्छरीरे त्वच्छापाद् दह्यमानोऽवसत् कलिः। त्वच्छापदग्धः सततं सोऽग्नावग्निरिवाहितः॥
en: O best of virtuous ladies, long ago you cursed Kali, while you were living in the forest, greatly afflicted with sorrow and burning in grief for me day and night. Since then Kali, burning with that curse, was living in my body. As a matter of fact, Kali, burning with your curse, was always dwelling within me, as fire dwells within fire.

description: The union of Nala and Damayanti
sn: मम च व्यवसायेन तपसा चैव निर्जितः। दुःखस्यान्तेन चानेन भवितव्यं हि नौ शुभे॥
en: Now he had been vanquished by my observances and devotion. Therefore, auspicious one, there will be an end of our sorrows.

description: The union of Nala and Damayanti
sn: विमुच्य मां गतः पापस्ततोऽहमिह चागतः। त्वदर्थं विपुलश्रोणि न हि मेऽन्यत् प्रयोजनम्॥
en: O you of round hips, leaving me, the wretched one had gone away. It is for this that I could come here. Indeed, in my coming here I have no other object than to get you back.

description: The union of Nala and Damayanti
sn: कथं नु नारी भर्तारमनुरक्तमनुव्रतम्। उत्सृज्य वरयेदन्यं यथा त्वं भीरु कर्हिचित्॥
en: O timid one, is it possible that a lady, forsaking her dear and devoted lord, will ever select a second husband like yourself?

description: The union of Nala and Damayanti
sn: दूताश्चरन्ति पृथिवीं कृत्स्नां नृपतिशासनात्। भैमी किल स्म भर्तारं द्वितीयं वरयिष्यति॥
en: At the command of the monarch, the messengers are roving all over the world, proclaiming that the daughter of king Bhima would surely choose a second husband.

description: The union of Nala and Damayanti
sn: स्वैरवृत्ता यथाकाममनुरूपमिवात्मनः। श्रुत्वैव चैवं त्वरितो भाङ्गासुरिरुपस्थितः॥
en: And like an unchaste woman, she would choose one, worthy of her, whomever she likes. Hearing this, the royal son of Vangasura had arrived here with all speed."

description: The union of Nala and Damayanti
sn: दमयन्ती तु तच्छ्रुत्वा नलस्य परिदेवितम्। प्राञ्जलिर्वेपमाना च भीता वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Hearing these weeping of Nala, Damayanti became greatly terrified; and she, trembling with fear and with folded hands, spoke these words.

description: The union of Nala and Damayanti
sn: दमयन्त्युवाच न मामर्हसि कल्याण दोषेण परिशङ्कितुम्। मया हि देवानुत्सृज्य वृतस्त्वं निषधाधिप॥
en: Damayanti said : O ruler of the Nishadhas, O blessed one, it behoves you not to suspect any fault in me; for I have selected you as my husband, discarding all the celestials.

description: The union of Nala and Damayanti
sn: तवाभिगमनार्थं तु सर्वतो ब्राह्मणा गताः। वाक्यानि मम गाथाभिर्गायमाना दिशो दश॥
en: With a view to bring you here, the Brahmanas had gone away in all directions, (to the ten points of the horizon) singing my words, composed in ballads.

description: The union of Nala and Damayanti
sn: ततस्त्वां ब्राह्मणो विद्वान् पर्णादो नाम पार्थिव। अभ्यगच्छत् कोसलायामृतुपर्णनिवेशने॥
en: At length, a learned Brahmana, known by the name of Parnada, found you out, O monarch, in the palace of Rituparna in the kingdom of Koshala.

description: The union of Nala and Damayanti
sn: तेन वाक्ये कृते सम्यक् प्रतिवाक्ये तथाऽऽहते। उपायोऽयं मया दृष्टो नैषधानयने तव॥
en: It was after hearing his words and your proper answer thereto, that I devised this project in order to receive the king of the Nishadhas back.

description: The union of Nala and Damayanti
sn: त्वामृते न हि लोकेऽन्य एकाह्ना पृथिवीपते। समर्थो योजनशतं गन्तुमश्चैवर्नराधिप॥
en: O ruler of the earth, O'foremost of the kings, there is none else in this world, who is able to journey, with the help of steeds, a hundred yojanas in a single day.

description: The union of Nala and Damayanti
sn: स्पृशेयं तेन सत्येन पादावेतौ महीपते। यथा नासत्कृतं किंचिन्मनसापि चराम्यहम्॥
en: O lord of the earth, touching these your feet, I can truly swear that even in thought I have not committed any sort of crime.

description: The union of Nala and Damayanti
sn: अयं चरति लोकेऽस्मिन् भूतसाक्षी सदागतिः। एव मे मुञ्चतु प्राणान् यदि पापं चराम्यहम्॥
en: Let the all-seeing air, that always moves about the whole world, take away my life, if I have committed any sin.

description: The union of Nala and Damayanti
sn: यथा चरति तिग्मांशुः परेण भुवनं सदा। स मुञ्चतु मम प्राणान् यदि पापं चराम्यहम्॥
en: Let the sun of bright rays, that always travels over the sky, take away, my life, if I have committed any sin.

description: The union of Nala and Damayanti
sn: चन्द्रमाः सर्वभूतानामन्तश्चरति साक्षिवत्। स मुञ्चतु मम प्राणान् यदि पापं चराम्यहम्॥
en: Let the moon, that lives in the heart of all creatures as a witness, take away my life, if I have committed any sin.

description: The union of Nala and Damayanti
sn: एते देवास्त्रयः कृत्स्नं त्रैलोक्यंधारयन्ति वै। विब्रुवन्तु यथा सत्यमेतद् देवास्त्यजन्तु माम्॥
en: Let the three gods, that preside over the whole of the three worlds, relate the whole history truly; or let them abandon me today.

description: The union of Nala and Damayanti
sn: एवमुक्तस्तथा वायुरन्तरिक्षादभाषत। नैषा कृतवती पापं नल सत्यं ब्रवीमि ते॥
en: Brihadashva said : Thus spoken the wind-god addressed from above, saying, “O Nala, I tell you the truth that she had not committed any sin.

description: The union of Nala and Damayanti
sn: राजज्छीलनिधिः स्फीतो दमयन्त्या सुरक्षितः साक्षिणो रक्षिणश्चास्या वयं त्रीन् परिवत्सरान्॥
en: O monarch, protected by Damayanti, the honour of your family, even as the wealth, has much increased. We bear testimony to this, as we have been her protectors for the last three years.

description: The union of Nala and Damayanti
sn: उपायो विहितश्चायं त्वदर्थमतुलोऽनया। न ह्यकोछा शतं गन्ता त्वामृतेऽन्यः पुमानिह॥
en: This unrivalled project was planned by her for your sake: for, except you, there is no other person in this world who can clear in a single day an hundred yojanas.

description: The union of Nala and Damayanti
sn: उपपन्ना त्वया भैमी त्वं च भैम्या महीपते। नात्र शङ्का त्वया कार्या संगच्छ सह भार्यया॥
en: O ruler of the earth, the daughter of king Bhima has been obtained by you; as also you have been obtained by Bhaimi. You should hold no doubt about her conduct. Be you united with your consort."

description: The union of Nala and Damayanti
sn: तथा ब्रुवति वायौ तु पुष्पवृष्टिः पपात ह। देवदुन्दुभयो नेदुर्ववौ च पवनः शिवः॥
en: While the wind-god was thus speaking, there was a downfall of floral showers; as also the divine kettle-drum played and auspicious breezes began to blow.

description: The union of Nala and Damayanti
sn: तदद्भुतमयं दृष्ट्वा नलो राजाथ भारत। दमयन्त्यां विशङ्कां तामुपाकर्षदरिंदमः॥
en: O son of the Bharata race, seeing this greatest wonder, king Nala, the chastiser of foes, threw away all doubts regarding the character of Damayanti.

description: The union of Nala and Damayanti
sn: ततस्तद् वस्त्रमजरं प्रावृणोद् वसुधाधिपः। संस्मृत्य नागराजं तं ततो लेभे स्वकं वपुः॥
en: Thereupon the ruler of the earth put on a fresh garment; and, then remembering that king of serpents, assumed his original form.

description: The union of Nala and Damayanti
sn: स्वरूपिणं तु भर्तारं दृष्ट्वा भीमसुता तदा। प्राक्रोशदुच्चैरालिङ्गय पुण्यश्लोकमनिन्दिता॥
en: Beholding her husband in his original form, the faultless daughter of king Bhima embraced the righteous one and wept bitterly.

description: The union of Nala and Damayanti
sn: भैमीमपि नलो राजा भ्राजमनो यथा पुरा। सस्वजे स्वसुतौ चापि यथावत् प्रत्यनन्दत॥
en: King Nala, again, embraced the daughter of Bhima, who was attached to him as before; as well as he embraced his two children; and thus felt great satisfaction.

description: The union of Nala and Damayanti
sn: ततः स्वोरसि विन्यस्य वक्त्रं तस्य शुभानना। परीता तेन दुःखेन निशश्वासायतेक्षणा॥
en: Thereupon the lady, of beautiful face and of large eyes, hiding her face in his bosom, became overwhelmed with grief and began to sigh heavily.

description: The union of Nala and Damayanti
sn: तथैव मलदिग्धाङ्गी परिष्वज्य शुचिस्मिताम्। सुचिरं पुरुषव्याघ्रस्तस्थौ शोकपरिप्लुतः॥
en: That foremost of men, overwhelmed as he was with grief, stood in silence for some time, while embracing that lady of blameless smiles, who herself was covered with dust.

description: The union of Nala and Damayanti
sn: ततः सर्वं यथावृत्तं दमयन्त्या नलस्य च। भीमायाकथयत् प्रीत्या वैदा जननी नृप॥
en: O monarch, thereupon the mother of Vaidharbhi, with a glad heart, informed king Bhima all that had passed between Nala and Damayanti.

description: The union of Nala and Damayanti
sn: ततोऽब्रवीन्महाराजः कृतशौचमहं नलम्। दमयन्त्या सहोपेतं कल्ये द्रष्टा सुखोषितम्॥
en: The great king said in reply: “Tomorrow I shall see Nala with Damayanti by his side, after he shall have sanctified himself (by bath and prayers). Let him dwell in peace this day."

description: The union of Nala and Damayanti
sn: ततस्तौ सहितौ रात्रिं कथयन्तौ पुरातनम्। वने विचरितं सर्वमूषतुर्मुदितौ नृप॥
en: O king, thercupon the happy pair passed the night at ease, relating to each other the past events of their wanderings in the forest.

description: The union of Nala and Damayanti
sn: गृहे भीमस्य नृपतेः परस्परसुखैषिणौ। वसेतां हृष्टसंकल्पौ वैदर्भी च नलश्च ह॥
en: Both the princess of Vidharbha and Nala began to dwell most happily in the palace of king Bhima, desirous to make each other happy.

description: The union of Nala and Damayanti
sn: स चतुर्थे ततो वर्षे संगम्य सह भार्यया। सर्वकामैः सुसिद्धार्थो लब्धवान् परमां मुदम्॥
en: Then in the fourth year, (after his exile) king Nala, regained his wife and had all his desires satisfied; and thus once more he enjoyed the highest pleasure.

description: The union of Nala and Damayanti
sn: दमयन्त्यपि भर्तारमासाद्याप्यायिता भृशम्। अर्धसंजातसस्येव तोयं प्राप्य वसुंधरा॥
en: Damayanti on the other hand, exceedingly satisfied to recover her husband, was even as the fields of half-born seedlings are highly benefited to receive a shower.

description: The union of Nala and Damayanti
sn: सैवं समेत्य व्यपनीय तन्द्रां शान्तज्वरा हर्षविवृद्धसत्त्वा। रराज भैमी समवाप्तकामा शीतांशुना रात्रिरिवोदितेन॥
en: When the daughter of the king and thus egained her husband, all her weariness had disappeared, as well as all her anxieties. She herself became elated with joy and blazed forth in her native beauty like the night, that is favoured by the uninterrupted rising of the moon.

description: The returning of Rituparna to his own City
sn: बृहदश्व उवाच अथ तां व्युषितो रात्रि नलो राजा स्वलंकृतः। वैदा सहितः काले ददर्श वसुधाधिपम्॥
en: Brihadashva said : The king Nala, having passed that night in peace, decked himself in gay ornaments; and, with Damayanti by his side, appeared before the king in due time.

description: The returning of Rituparna to his own City
sn: ततोऽभिवादयामास प्रयतः श्वशुरं नलः। ततोऽनु दमयन्ती च ववन्दे पितरं शुभा॥
en: Thereupon Nala saluted his father-in-law; and, after him, blessed Damayanti also saluted her father.

description: The returning of Rituparna to his own City
sn: तं भीमः प्रतिजग्राह पुत्रवत् परया मुदा। यथार्ह पूजयित्वा च समाश्वासयत प्रभुः॥ नलेन सहितां तत्र दमयन्ती पतिव्रताम्।
en: Illustrious Bhima received him as a son with the greatest delight; as also he offered him due respects and consoled him with his devoted wife in words suited to the occasion.

description: The returning of Rituparna to his own City
sn: तामहणां नलो राजा प्रतिगृह्य यथाविधि॥ परिचर्यां स्वकां तस्मै यथावत् प्रत्यवेदयत्। ततो बभूव नगरे सुमहान् हर्षजः स्वनः॥ जनस्य सम्प्रहृष्टस्य नलं दृष्ट्वा तथाऽऽगतम्।
en: King Nala, on the other hand, acknowledged the honour according to rules and offered his proper services to him (father-in-law). The citizens felt great delight to see Nala returned. Thereupon there was a great uproar of joy in the city.

description: The returning of Rituparna to his own City
sn: अशोभयच्च नगरं पताकाध्वजमालिनम्॥ सिक्ताः सुमृष्टपुष्पाढ्या राजमार्गाः स्वलंकृताः। द्वारि द्वारि च पौराणां पुष्पभङ्गः प्रकल्पितः॥
en: The city also was gorgeously decorated by hoisting flags, standards and floral wreaths. Moreover the streets of the town were well watered, and were decorated with the garlands of flowers and various other ornaments; as also flowers were piled at the doors of the houses.

description: The returning of Rituparna to his own City
sn: अर्चितानि च सर्वाणि देवतायतनानि च। ऋतुपर्णोऽपि सुश्राव बाहुकच्छद्मिनं नलम्॥ दमयन्त्या समायुक्तं जहषे च नराधिपः। तमानाय्य नलं राजा क्षमयामास पार्थिवम्॥
en: The temples of gods, too, were adorned with flowers. While all this had happened, the foremost king Rituparna became highly gratified to hear that Nala, in the guise of Bahuka, was united with Damayanti. He then called Nala, the ruler of the earth, before him; and begged his pardon.

description: The returning of Rituparna to his own City
sn: स च तं क्षमयामास हेतुभिर्बुद्धिसम्मितः। स सत्कृतो महीपालो नैषधं विस्मिताननः॥ उवाच वाक्यं तत्त्वज्ञो नैषधं वदतां वरः। दिष्ट्या समेतो दारैः स्वैर्भवानित्यभ्यनन्दत॥
en: He again, intelligent as he was, asked his forgiveness for reasons more than one. Thus regarded, the ruler of the earth, Rituparna, who was excellent in speech and acquainted with the real nature of things and who had his face struck with amazement, addressed the prince of the Nishadhas, saying, “That you, by recovering the company of your consort, have obtained greatest delight.

description: The returning of Rituparna to his own City
sn: किंचित् तु नापराधं ते कृतवानस्मि नैषध। अज्ञातवासे वसतो मद्गृहे वसुधाधिप॥
en: O prince of the Nishadh..s, O lord of the earth, perhaps I had not donc any wrong to you, while you were living in my house in disguise.

description: The returning of Rituparna to his own City
sn: यदिवाबुद्धिपूर्वाणि यदि बुद्ध्यापि कानिचित्। मया कृतान्यकार्याणि तानि त्वं क्षन्तुमर्हसि॥
en: If I have done any wrong to you, with or without my knowledge, pardon me for all this,”

description: The returning of Rituparna to his own City
sn: नल उवाच न मेऽपराधं कृतवांस्त्वं स्वल्पमपि पार्थिव। कृतेऽपि च न मे कोपः क्षन्तव्यं हि मया तव॥
en: Nala said: O monarch, you have not done me the slightest wrong. Even if you have done any, you should be pardoned in every way; for it excited no worth in me.

description: The returning of Rituparna to his own City
sn: पूर्वं ह्यपि सखा मेऽसि सम्बन्धी च जनाधिप। अत ऊर्ध्वं तु भूयस्त्वं प्रीतिमाहर्तुमर्हसि॥
en: O prince, formerly you had been my friend and relative; and hence that I should find enough of enjoyments in you. Indeed, I lived with you most happily with all my desires gratified.

description: The returning of Rituparna to his own City
sn: सर्वकामैः सुविहितैः सुखमसम्युषितस्त्वयि। न तथा स्वगृहे राजन् यथा तव गृहे सदा॥
en: O king, I always lived in your house most happily, not even in my own house. This your knowledge about horses now rests with me.

description: The returning of Rituparna to his own City
sn: इदं चैव हयज्ञानं त्वदीयं मयि तिष्ठति। तदुपाकर्तुमिच्छामि मन्यसे यदि पार्थिवा एवमुक्त्वा ददौ विद्यामृतुपर्णाय नैषधः॥
en: O monarch, if you like, I may give it to you.” Saying this, the prince of the Nishadhas made over that equestrian learning to king Rituparna.

description: The returning of Rituparna to his own City
sn: स च तां प्रतिजग्राह विधिदृष्टेन कर्मणा। गृहीत्वा चाश्वहदयं राजन् भागासुरिर्नृपः॥ निषधाधिपतेश्चापि दत्त्वाक्षहृदयं नृपः। सूतमन्यमुपादाय ययौ स्वपुरमेव ह॥
en: O king, the royal son of Vangasura accepted that horse-learning, performing all the acts, as ordained by fate. And having thus received this horse-knowledge and also having made over his skill in the game at dice to the prince of the Nishadhas, he went to his own city, appointing another charioteer in the place of Bahuka.

description: The returning of Rituparna to his own City
sn: ऋतुपर्णे गते राजन् नलो राजा विशाम्पते। नगरे कुण्डिने कालं नातिदीर्घमिवावसत्॥
en: O monarch, O lord of the earth, after Rituparna had thus gone away, prince Nala did not remain long in the city Kundina.

description: Nala's victory over Pushkara at dice and Pushkara's arrival at his own City
sn: बृहदश्व उवाच स मासमुष्य कौन्तेय भीममामन्त्र्य नैषधः। पुरादल्पपरीवारो जगाम निषधान् प्रति॥
en: Brihadashva said: O son of Kunti, the prince of the Nishadhas, having lived there for about a month, obtained permission of Bhima and went, with a small number of attendants, to the country of the Nishadhas.

description: Nala's victory over Pushkara at dice and Pushkara's arrival at his own City
sn: रथेनैकेन शुभ्रेण दन्तिभिः परिषोडशैः। पञ्चाशद्भिर्हयैश्चैव षट्शतैश्च पदातिभिः॥ स कम्पयन्निव महीं त्वरमाणो महीपतिः। प्रविवेशाथ संरब्धस्तरसैव महामनाः॥
en: That agile and lofty-minded monarch, who was swelled with rage, entered the country of the Nishadhas speedily, with a single white car, sixteen elephants, fifty horse and six hundred infantry and thereby he trembled the whole earth.

description: Nala's victory over Pushkara at dice and Pushkara's arrival at his own City
sn: ततः पुष्करमासाद्य वीरसेनसुतो नलः। उवाच दीव्याव पुनर्बहुवित्तं मयार्जितम्॥ दमयन्ती च यच्चान्यन्मम किंचन विद्यते। एष वै मम संन्यासस्तव राज्यं तु पुष्कर॥ पुनः प्रवर्ततां द्यूतमिति मे निश्चिता मतिः। एकपाणेन भद्रं ते प्राणयोश्च पणावहे॥
en: Thereupon the heroic son of Virasena, advancing towards Pushkara (his brother), expressed his intention to play at dice; because he again earned vast wealth.
