Nal Said, "O Pushkara, let Damayanti and everything else, that I have, by my stake; and let your kingdom be yours. Let the game at dice begin again; for this is my firm resolution. Be you happy. Let us stake all that we possess, as well as our lives.

description: Nala's victory over Pushkara at dice and Pushkara's arrival at his own City
sn: जित्वा परस्वमाहृत्य राज्यं वा यदि वा बसु। प्रतिपाणः प्रदातव्यः परमोधर्म उच्यते॥
en: To stake back other's possessions, that is, wealth and kingdom, that are already won, is said to be the chief virtue.

description: Nala's victory over Pushkara at dice and Pushkara's arrival at his own City
sn: न चेद् वाञ्छसि त्वं युद्धद्यूतं प्रवर्तताम्। द्वैरथेनास्तु वै शान्तिस्तव वा मम वा नृप॥
en: If you do not like the game at dice, do you then engage yourself in the play at weapons. Really, O king, let us have peace by fighting out a duel.

description: Nala's victory over Pushkara at dice and Pushkara's arrival at his own City
sn: वंशभोज्यमिदं राज्यमर्थितव्यं यथा तथा। येन केनाप्युपायेन वृद्धानामिति शासनम्॥
en: The sages have laid down their authority by saying, that the ancestral kingdom should be obtained under any circumstance or by any means.

description: Nala's victory over Pushkara at dice and Pushkara's arrival at his own City
sn: द्वयोरेकतरे बुद्धिः क्रियतामद्य पुष्कर। कैतवेनाक्षवत्यां तु युद्धे वा नाम्यतांधनुः॥
en: O Pushkara, do you choose today one of these two; that is, do you either game at dice or bend the bow in battle.

description: Nala's victory over Pushkara at dice and Pushkara's arrival at his own City
sn: नैषधेनैवमुक्तस्तु पुष्करः प्रहसन्निवा ध्रुवमात्मजयं मत्वा प्रत्याह पृथिवीपतिम्॥
en: Brihadashva said: Having been thus addressed by the prince of the Nishadhas, Pushkara, with the assurance of his own success, answered the king smilingly.

description: Nala's victory over Pushkara at dice and Pushkara's arrival at his own City
sn: दिष्ट्या त्वयार्जितं वित्तं प्रतिपाणाय नैषध। दिष्ट्या च दुष्कृतं कर्म दमयन्त्याः क्षयं गतम्॥
en: “O Naishadha, by good fortune you have acquired the vast wealth, in order to stake it back again. Most fortunately the adversity of Damayanti has come to an end.

description: Nala's victory over Pushkara at dice and Pushkara's arrival at his own City
sn: दिष्ट्या च ध्रियसे राजन् सदारोऽद्य महाभुज। धनेनानेन वै भैमी जितेन समलंकृता।॥ देवनेन मम मामुपस्थास्यति व्यक्तं दिवि शक्रमिवाप्सराः। नित्यशो हि स्मरामि त्वां प्रतीक्षेऽपि च नैषध॥
en: O monarch, O mighty-armed one, that you are still living with your wife, is owing to your good luck. Indeed, the daughter of king Bhima, decked in ornaments, will attend me with all the wealth, that I will gain from you, even as the Apsaras wait upon Shakra in heaven. O prince of the Nishadhas, do I, therefore, recollect you and expect you always.

description: Nala's victory over Pushkara at dice and Pushkara's arrival at his own City
sn: प्रीतिर्न भवत्यसुहृद्गणैः। जित्वा त्वद्य वरारोहां दमयन्तीमनिन्दिताम्॥ कृतकृत्यो भविष्यामि सा हि मे नित्यशो हृदि।
en: To play at dicc with those that are not my relatives, gives me no pleasure. Having this day obtained the hand of Damayanti, who is most beautiful and possessed of blameless features, I shall think myself very lucky, for she is, as ever, the darling of my heart.”

description: Nala's victory over Pushkara at dice and Pushkara's arrival at his own City
sn: श्रुत्वा तु तस्य ता वाचो बह्वबद्धप्रलापिनः॥ इयेष स शिरश्छेत्तुं खड्नेन कुपितो नलः। स्मयंस्तु रोषताम्राक्षस्तमुवाच नलो नृपः॥
en: Having heard these expressions of that infatuated braggart, king Nala became filled with rage and desired to sever his head by the sword. King Nala smilingly, though his eyes were red with anger, addressed him, saying,

description: Nala's victory over Pushkara at dice and Pushkara's arrival at his own City
sn: पणावः किं व्याहरसे जितो न व्याहरिष्यसि। ततः प्रावर्तत द्यूतं पुष्करस्य नलस्य च॥ एकपाणेन वीरेण लेन स पराजितः। स रत्नकोशनिचयैः प्राणेन पणितोऽपि च॥
en: "Let us begin the play. Why do you speak thus now? You will speak in any way you like, after you shali have defeated me at dice.” Thereupon the gambling began between Pushkara and Nala. Pushkara, who had even staked his own life, was defeated at a single throw by Nala; and thus he lost all his wealth and treasures.

description: Nala's victory over Pushkara at dice and Pushkara's arrival at his own City
sn: जित्वा च पुष्करं राजा प्रहसन्निदमब्रवीत्। मम सर्वमिदं राज्यमव्यग्रं हतकण्टकम्॥ वैदर्भी न त्वया शक्या राजापसद वीक्षितुम्। तस्यास्त्वं सपरीवारो मूढ दासत्वमागतः॥
en: The king, having defeated Pushkara, laughingly saidto him: "This entire kingdom is now undisputedly mine. The thorns (the enemies) are all destroyed. O worst of kings, now you are not able even to have a look of Vaidharbhi. O foolish one, you are now reduced to her slave with your family.

description: Nala's victory over Pushkara at dice and Pushkara's arrival at his own City
sn: न त्वया तत् कृतं कर्म येनाहं विजितः पुरा। कलिना तत् कृतं कर्म त्वं च मूढ न बुध्यसे॥
en: That formerly I was defeated by you, was not wrought by you. That act was done by Kali; and it was not you, that did so. O stupid one, this you do not understand.

description: Nala's victory over Pushkara at dice and Pushkara's arrival at his own City
sn: नाहं परकृतं दोषं त्वय्याधास्ये कथंचन। यथासुखं वै जीव त्वं प्राणानवसृजामि ते॥
en: I will never attribute the faults, committed by others, to you. Indeed, do you live happily. I grant you your life.

description: Nala's victory over Pushkara at dice and Pushkara's arrival at his own City
sn: तथैव सर्वसम्भारं स्वमंशं वितरामि ते। तथैव च मम प्रतिस्त्वयि वीर न संशयः॥
en: As before, I give you your portion of the whole kingdom. O hero, the amount of my love for you is doubtlessly the same as before.

description: Nala's victory over Pushkara at dice and Pushkara's arrival at his own City
sn: सौहार्द चापि मे त्वत्तो न कदाचित् प्रहास्यति। पुष्कर त्वं हि मे भ्राता संजीव शरदः शतम्॥
en: O Pushkara, the fraternal love, that I entertain for you, will never decrease. You are my brother. Do you live for a hundred years.

description: Nala's victory over Pushkara at dice and Pushkara's arrival at his own City
sn: एवं नल: सान्त्वयित्वा भ्रातरं सत्यविक्रमः। स्वपुरं प्रेषयामास परिष्वज्य पुनः पुनः॥
en: Having thus accosted his brother, Nala of undaunted courage embraced him repeatedly and asked him to go to his own city.

description: Nala's victory over Pushkara at dice and Pushkara's arrival at his own City
sn: सान्त्वितो नैषाधेनैवं पुष्करं प्रत्युवाच तम्। पुण्यश्लोकं तदा राजन्नभिवाद्य कृताञ्जलिः॥ कीर्तिरस्तु तवाक्षय्या जीव वर्षशतं सुखी। यो मे वितरसि प्राणानधिष्ठानं च पार्थिव॥
en: O king, having been thus consoled by the prince of the Nishadhas, Pushkara then, with folded hands, saluted and answered that virtuous prince, saying, “O prince, let your fame be immortal; and do you live at peace for hundred years, for you have give to me both life and shelter."

description: Nala's victory over Pushkara at dice and Pushkara's arrival at his own City
sn: स तथा सत्कृतो राज्ञा मासमुष्य तदा नृप। प्रययौ पुष्करो हृष्टः स्वपुरं स्वजनावृतः॥ महत्या सेनया साधू विनीतैः परिचारकैः। भ्राजमान इवादित्यो वपुषा पुरुषर्षभ॥
en: O monarch, having been thus honoured by the king (his brother, Nala). Pushkara, gratified at heart, then repaired to his own city attended by his relatives, after he has passed about a month with his brother. O foremost of men, also attended by a great force and humble servants, Pushkara went away; and he looked like the resplendent sun in appearance.

description: Nala's victory over Pushkara at dice and Pushkara's arrival at his own City
sn: प्रस्थाप्य पुष्करं राजा वित्तवन्तमनामयम्। प्रविवेश पुरं श्रीमानत्यर्थमुपशोभिताम्॥
en: After having settled Pushkara and enriched and delivered him from all anxieties, the blessed prince entered his own palace, most gorgeously decorated.

description: Nala's victory over Pushkara at dice and Pushkara's arrival at his own City
sn: प्रविश्य सान्वयामास पौरांश्च निषधाधिपः। पौरा जानपदाश्चापि सम्प्रहृष्टतनूरुहाः॥
en: After having entered the palace, the prince of the Nishadhas consoled all the citizens, who, as well as the subjects from the country, again, greatly expressed their satisfaction,

description: Nala's victory over Pushkara at dice and Pushkara's arrival at his own City
sn: ऊचुः प्राञ्जलयः सर्वे सामात्यप्रमुखा जनाः। अद्य स्म निर्वृता राजन् पुरे जनपदेऽपि च। उपासितुं पुन: प्राप्ता देवा इव शतक्रतुम्॥
en: All the officers of government, headed by their minister, addressed him with folded hands, saying, "O king, really we are all glad today both in the city and the country, even as the gods themselves, after having obtained their chief of a hundred sacrifices for worship."

sn: बृहदश्व उवाच प्रशान्ते तु पुरे हृष्टे सम्प्रवृत्ते महोत्सवे। महत्या सेनया राजा दमयन्तीमुपानयत्॥
en: Brihadashva said: When the great festivities began in the city which was full of joy, the king with a large army brought Damayanti (back to his capital).

sn: दमयन्तीमपि पिता सत्कृत्य परवीरहा। प्रास्थापयदमेयात्मा भीमो भीमपराक्रमः॥
en: Her father, that slayer of hostile heroes Bhima of great prowess and of high soul, also having honoured her duly, sent Damayanti (tc her husband's palace).

sn: अगतायां तु वैदर्त्यां सपुत्रायां नलो नृपः। वर्तयामास मुदितो देवराडिव नन्दने॥ तथा प्रकाशतां यातो जम्बुद्वीपे स राजसु। पुनः शशास तद् राज्यं प्रत्याहृत्य महायशाः॥
en: On the arrival of the Vidharbha princess accompanied by her son and daughter, king Nala passed his days in great happiness, like the chief of the celestials in the Nandana (garden). The greatly illustrious king, having regained his kingdom and becoming famous among the kings of the Jambudvipa, began once more to rule it.

sn: ईजे च विविधैर्यज्ञैर्विधिवच्चाप्तदक्षिणैः। तथा त्वमपि राजेन्द्र ससुहृद् यक्ष्यसेऽचिरात्॥
en: He duly performed many sacrifices with large Dakshinas to the Brahmanas. O great king, you, too, with your relatives and friends, will soon perform many sacrifices.

sn: दुःखमेतादृशं प्राप्तो नल: परपुरंजयः। देवनेन नरश्रेष्ठ सभार्यो भरतर्षभ।॥
en: foremost of meu, O best of the Bharata race that conqueror of the hostile cities, Nala, thus fell into great distress in consequence of his playing at dice.

sn: एकाकिनैव सुपहन्नलेन पृथिवीपते। दुःखमासादितं घोरं प्राप्तश्चाभ्युदयः पुनः॥
en: O ruler of the earth, Nala alone suffered such great and terrible distress, but he regained his lost glory.

sn: त्वं पुनर्धातृसहितः कृष्णाया चैव पाण्डव। रमसेऽस्मिन् महारण्येधर्ममेवानुचिन्तयन्॥
en: O son of Pandu, you, however, with Krishna (Draupadi) and your brothers, sport here in this great forest, with your heart fixed on virtue.

sn: ब्राह्मणैश्च महाभागैर्वेदवेदाङ्गपारगैः। नित्यमन्वास्यसे राजंस्तत्र का परिदेवना॥
en: O king, what cause is there for your sorrow, when you are always mixing with the greatly exalted Brahmanas learned in the Vedas?

sn: कर्कोटकस्य नागस्य दमयन्त्या नलस्य च। ऋतुपर्णस्य राजर्षेः कीर्तनं कलिनाशनम्॥
en: To recite the history of Naga Karkotaka, of Damayanti, of Nala and of the royal sage Rituparna, is destructive of evil (Kali).

sn: इतिहासमिमं चापि कलिनाशनमच्युत। शक्यमाश्वसितुं श्रुत्वा त्वद्विधेन विशाम्यते॥
en: O undeteriorating one, O ruler of men, this history, which is destructive of evil (Kali), is capable of comforting persons like you, when they hear it.

sn: अस्थिरत्वं च संचिन्त्य पुरुषार्थस्य नित्यदा। तस्योदये व्यये चापि न चिन्तयितुमर्हसि॥
en: Considering that human exertion is always futile, you should joy or grieve at prosperity or adversity.

sn: श्रुत्वेतिहासं नृपते समाश्वसिहि मा शुचः। व्यसने त्वं महाराज न विषीदितुमर्हसि॥
en: O great king, hearing this history, be comforted. Do not grieve. You should not be aggrieved at calamity.

sn: विषमावस्थिते दैवे पौरुषेऽफलतां गते। विषादयन्ति नात्मानं सत्त्वोपाश्रयिणो नराः॥
en: Reflecting on the caprice of fate and futileness of human exertions, men of selfpossession never allow themselves to be aggrieved.

sn: ये चेदं कथयिष्यन्ति नलस्य चरितं महत्। श्रोष्यन्ति चाप्यभीक्ष्णं वै नालक्ष्मीस्तान् भजिष्यति।१५।।
en: Those who recite the great history of Nala and those who often hear it are never touched by calamity.

sn: अर्थास्तस्योपपत्स्यन्तेधन्यतां च गमिष्यति। इतिहासमिमं श्रुत्वा पुराणं शश्वदुत्तमम्॥
en: He, who hears this excellent and old history, gets all his desires fulfilled and obtains wealth and

sn: पुत्रान् पौत्रान् पशृंश्चापि लभते नृषु चावयताम्। आरोग्यप्रीतिमांश्चैव भविष्यति न संशयः॥
en: Sons, grandsons, animals, a high position, health and joy. There is no doubt in this.

sn: भयात् त्रस्यसि यच्च त्वमाह्वयिष्यति मां पुनः। अक्षज्ञ इति तत् तेऽहं नाशयिष्यामि पार्थिव॥
en: O king, the fear, that you entertain that some one would again summon you to play, I shall dispel.

sn: वेदाक्षहृदयं कृत्स्नमहं सत्यपराक्रम। उपपद्यस्व कौन्तेय प्रसन्नोऽहं ब्रवीमि ते॥
en: O greatly powerful hero, O son of Kunti, I am an expert in the science of dice. I am pleased with you; learn it from me, I shall tell it to you.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततो हृष्टमना राजा वृहदश्वमुवाच ह। भगवन्नक्षहृदयं ज्ञातुमिच्छामि तत्त्वतः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Thereupon with great joy the king (Yudhishthira) thus spoke to Brihadashva, “O exalted one. I desire to learn the science of dice from you."

sn: ततोऽक्षहृदयं प्रादात् पाण्डवाय महात्मने। दत्त्वा चाश्वशिरोऽगच्छदुपस्प्रष्टुं महातपाः॥
en: Thereupon he taught the science to the illustrious son of Pandu. Having taught it, the great ascetic went to Asvasira to bathe.

sn: बृहदश्वे गते पार्थमश्रौषीत् सव्यसाचिनम्। वर्तमानं तपस्युग्रे वायुभक्षं मनीषिणम्॥ ब्राह्मणेभ्यस्तपस्विभ्यः सम्पतझ्यस्ततस्ततः। तीर्थशैलवनेभ्यश्च समेतेभ्यो दृढव्रतः॥ इति पार्थो महावाहुर्दुरापं तप आस्थितः। न तथा दृष्टपूर्वोऽन्यः कश्चिदुग्रतपा इति॥
en: When Brihadashva had gone away, he (Yudhishthira) heard that the son of Pritha Savyasachi (Arjuna) was engaged in severe asceticism, living on air. He heard this from the greatly intelligent Brahmanas and ascetics who came to him from various directions and from places of pilgrimage, from mountains and forests. He heard that the mighty Partha (Arjuna) was engaged in such fearful asceticism that none else, before him, had done it.

sn: यथाधनंजयः पार्थस्तपस्वी नियतव्रतः। मुनिरेकचरः श्रीमान्धर्मो विग्रहवानिव॥
en: He heard that Dhananjaya Partha (Arjuna) engaged in asceticism, observing vows of silence and deep in meditation, appeared like the blazing deity, Dharma.

sn: तं श्रुत्वा पाण्डवो राजंस्तव्यमानं महावने। अन्वशोचत कौन्तेयः प्रियं वै भ्रातरं जयम्॥
en: O king, having heard that his beloved brother, the son of Kunti, Yaja (Arjuna) was thus undergoing asceticism in the great forest Yudhishthira began to grieve.

sn: दह्यमानेन तु हृदा शरणार्थी महावने। ब्राह्मणान् विविधज्ञानान् पर्यपृच्छद् युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Thus burning in grief, Yudhishthira sought consolation in the great forest and talked with the Brahmanas learned in all Shastras.

sn: जनमेजय उवाच भगवन् काम्यकात् पार्थे गते मे प्रपितामहे। पाण्डवाः किमकुर्वंस्ते तमृते सव्यसाचिनम्॥
en: Janamejaya said : O exalted one, when my great-grandfather, the son of Pritha (Arjuna) had gone away from the Kamyaka, what did the Pandavas do in the absence of Savyasachi (Arjuna)?

sn: स हि तेषां महेष्वासो गतिरासीदनीकजित्। आदित्यानां यथा विष्णुस्तथैव प्रतिभाति मे॥
en: It appears to me that great bowman and the victor of armies (Arjuna) was their refuge, as Vishnu was that of the Adityas.

sn: तेनेन्द्रसमवीर्येण संग्रामेष्वनिवर्तिना। विनाभूता वने वीराः कथमासन् पितामहाः॥
en: How did my great-grand-fathers pass their time in the forest deprived as they were of the company of that hero who was equal to Indra in prowess and who never turned his back in a field of battle?

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच गते तु पाण्डवे तात काम्यकात् सत्यविक्रमे। बभूवुः पाण्डवेयास्ते दुःखशोकपरायणाः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : O child, when the greatly powerful Pandava, (Arjuna) had gone away from the Kamyaka, the sons of Pandu were filled with sorrow and grief.

sn: आक्षिप्तसूत्रा मणयश्छिन्नपक्षा इव द्विजाः। अप्रीतमनसः सर्वे बभूवुरथ पाण्डवाः॥
en: The Pandavas all became depressed and looked like pearls unstrung from a garland or like birds shorn of their wings.

sn: वनं तु तदभूत् तेन हीनमक्लिष्टकर्मणा। कुबेरेण यथा हीनं वनं चैत्ररथं तथा॥
en: Without the presence of that hero of spotless deeds, that forest looked like the Chaitraratha forest deprived of the presence of Kubera.

sn: तमृते ते नरव्याघ्राः पाण्डवा जनमेजय। मुदमप्राप्नुवन्तो वै काम्यके न्यवसंस्तदा॥
en: O Janamejaya, in his absence, those foremost of men, the Pandavas, continued to live in the Kamyaka in great cheerlessness.

sn: ब्राह्मणार्थे पराक्रान्ता: शुद्धैर्बाणैर्महारथाः। निघ्नन्तो भरतश्रेष्ठ मेध्यान् बहुविधान् मृगान्॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, those powerful, great car-warriors killed with pure (nonpoisonous) arrows various kinds of sacrificial animals for the Brahmanas.

sn: नित्यं हि पुरुषव्याघ्रा वन्याहारमरिदमाः। उपाकृत्य उपाहृत्य ब्राह्मणेभ्यो न्यवेदयन्॥
en: Those chastisers of foes, those foremost of men daily killed wild animals and after properly sanctifying them, they offered them to the Brahmanas.

sn: सर्वे संन्यवसंस्तत्र सोत्कण्ठाः पुरुषर्षभाः। अहृष्टमनसः सर्वे गते राजन्धनंजये।॥
en: O king, after the departure of Dhananjaya (Arjuna) thus did they live there, filled with sorrow and with cheerless heart.

sn: विशेषतस्तु पाञ्चाली स्मरन्ती मध्यमं पतिम्। उद्विग्नं पाण्डवश्रेष्ठमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Panchali (Draupadi) in particular remembered her third husband and she thus spoke to the anxious chief of the Pandavas (Yudhishthira).

sn: योऽर्जुनेनार्जुनस्तुल्यो द्विवाहुबहुबाहुना। तमृते पाण्डवश्रेष्ठ वनं न प्रतिभाति मे॥
en: Draupadi said : Arjuna with two hands, is equal to Arjuna of many hands; in the absence of that foremost of the Pandavas, this forest does not at all look charming to me.

sn: शून्यामिव प्रपश्यामि तत्र तत्र महीमिमाम्। बह्लाश्चर्यमिदं चापि वनं कुसुमितदुमम्॥
en: Wherever I cast my eyes, I see this earth as if it is empty. This forest, with its blossoming trees and with its so many wonders.

sn: न तथा रमणीयं वै तमृते सव्यसाचिनम्। नीलाम्बुदसमप्रख्यं मत्तमातङ्गगामिनम्॥
en: Does not appear to me charming in the absence of Savyasachi (Arjuna). He is (in color) like a mass of blue clouds, he is in prowess like a mad elephant.

sn: तमृते पुण्डरीकाक्षं काम्यकं नातिभाति मे। यस्य वाधनुषो घोषः श्रूयते चाशनिस्वनः। न लभे शर्म वै राजन् स्मरन्ती सव्यसाचिनम्॥
en: In the absence of that lotus-eyed hero, the Kamyaka does not at all look charming to me. Remembering Savyasachi, the twang of whose bow sounds like the roars of thunder, I do not feel any peace of mind.

sn: तथा लालप्यमानां तां निशम्य परवीरहा। भीमसेनो महाराज द्रौपदीमिदमब्रवीत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : O great king, hearing her thus lament, that slayer of hostile heroes Bhimasena, thus spoke to Draupadi.

sn: भीम उवाच मनःप्रीतिकरं भद्रे यद् ब्रवीषि सुमध्यमे। तन्मे प्रीणाति हृदयममृतप्राशनोपमम्॥
en: Bhima said: O blessed lady, O beauty of slender waist the pleasing words you say are as delightful to my mind, as the drinking of ambrosia.

sn: यस्य दी? समौ पीनौ भुजौ परिघसंनिभौ। मौर्वीकृतकिणौ वृत्तौ खङ्गायुधधनुर्धरौ॥ निष्काइदकृतापीडौ पञ्चशीर्षाविवोरगौ। तमृते पुरुषव्याघ्रं नष्टसूर्यमिवाम्बरम्॥
en: (Without him), whose arms are long, symmetrical, stout and mace-like, which are round and marked with the scars of the bowstrings, which are ground with the bow, the sword and the other weapons, encircled with golden bracelets, like two five-headed snakes, without that foremost of men, the sky seems to have lost the sun.

sn: यमाश्रित्य महाबाहुं पाञ्चालाः कुरवस्तथा। सुराणामपि मत्तानां पृतनासुन बिभ्यति॥
en: (Without him), relying on which mightyarmed hero the Panchalas and the Kurus do not fear even the various powerful celestials.

sn: यस्य बाहू समाश्रित्य वयं सर्वे महात्मनः। मन्यामहे जितानाजौ परान् प्राप्तां च मेदिनीम्॥
en: Relying on the prowess of the arms of which illustrious here, we all consider our enemies vanquished and the earth (already) acquired.

sn: तमृते फाल्गुनं वीरं न लभे काम्यकेधृतिम्। पश्यामि च दिशः सर्वास्तिमिरेणावृता इव। ततोऽब्रवीत् साश्रुकण्ठो नकुलः पाण्डुनन्दनः॥
en: Without that heroic Falguni (Arjuna), I do not get peace of mind in the Kamyaka. I behold all directions as empty and covered with darkness. Wherever I cast my eyes, I see the earth as if she is empty. Thereupon the son of Pandu, Nakula, thus spoke with his voice choked with tears.

sn: नकुल उवाच यस्मिन् दिव्यानि कर्माणि कथयन्ति रणाजिरे। देवा अपि युधां श्रेष्ठं तमृते का रतिर्वने॥
en: Nakula said: (Without him) whose excellent deeds in battle are talked about even by the gods, without that best of warriors, what pleasure can be here in this forest?

sn: उदीची यो दिशं गत्वा जित्वा युधि महाबलान्। गन्धर्वमुख्याञ्छतशो हयाँल्लेभे महाद्युतिः॥
en: (Without him) who, going to the northern regions, conquered in battle hundreds of greatly powerful Gandharva chiefs and obtained greatly effulgent horses.

sn: राज्ञे तित्तिरिकल्माषाञ्छ्रीमतोऽनिलरंहसः। प्रादाद् भ्रात्रे प्रियः प्रेम्णा राजसूये महाक्रतौ॥
en: Of the Tittiri and Kalamasha species, all possessing the speed of the wind, which were all presented by him to his brother out of the love he bore for him at the great Rajasuya sacrifice.

sn: तमृते भीमधन्वानं भीमादवरजं वने। कामये काम्यके वासं नेदानीममरोपमम्॥
en: Without that great bowman, the younger brother of Bhima, without that celestials-like hero, I do not any longer desire to dwell in this Kamyaka.

sn: सहदेव उवाच योधनानि च कन्याश्च युधि जित्वा महारथः। आजहार पुरा राजे राजसूये महाक्रतौ॥ यः समेतान् मृधे जित्वा यादवानमितद्युतिः। सुभद्रामाजहारैको वासुदेवस्य सम्मते॥ तस्य जिष्णोतसीं दृष्ट्वा शून्यामिव निवेशने। हृदयं मे महाराज न शाम्यति कदाचन॥ वनादस्माद् विवासं तु रोचयेऽहमरिंदम्। न हि नस्तमृते वीरं रमणीयमिदं वनम्॥
en: Sahadeva said: O king, O descendant of Bharata, seeing his bed of grass empty in our hermitage without that Jishnu, who, having vanquished powerful warriors in battle, won wealth and virgins and brought them to the king at the time of the great sacrifice, without that immeasurably effulgent hero who having vanquished singlehanded all the Yadavas took possession of Subhadra with the consent of Vasudeva (Krishna), who having invaded the kingdom of the illustrious Drupada, gave to the preceptor Drona his tuition-fee by securing for him half of Drupada's kingdom, my mind by no means gets any consolation. O chastiser of foes, to go away from this forest to some other forest is what I would prefer, for in the absence of that hero this forest can by no means be delightful.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच धनंजयोत्सुकानां तु भ्रातृणां कृष्णया सह। श्रुत्वा वाक्यानि विमनाधर्मराजोऽप्यजायत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having heard these words of his brothers and Krishna (Draupadi) who were all anxious for Dhananjaya, Dharmaraja became absentminded.

sn: अथापश्यन्महात्मानं देवर्षि तत्र नारदम्। दीप्यमानं श्रिया ब्राह्मया हुतार्चिषमिवानलम्॥
en: (At that time) he saw (before him) .ne celestials Rishi Narada, blazing with Brahma effulgence and resembling a fire flaming up for the sacrifice.

sn: तमागतमभिप्रेक्ष्य भ्रातृभिः सहधर्मराट्। प्रत्युत्थाय यथान्यायं पूजां चक्रे महात्मने॥
en: Seeing him arrived, Dharmaraja (Yudhishthira) with his brothers and stoop up and duly worshipped the illustrious one.

sn: स तैः परिवृतः श्रीमान् भ्रातृभिः कुरुसत्तमः। विबभावतिदीप्तौजा देवैरिव शतक्रतुः॥
en: Endued with blazing effulgence the handsome chief of the Kurus, surrounded by his brothers, shone like Shatakratu (Indra) surrounded by the celestials.

sn: यथा च वेदान् सावित्री याज्ञसेनी तथा पतीन्। न जहौधर्मतः पार्थान् मेरुमर्कप्रभा यथा॥
en: In obedience to the dictates of Dharma Yajnaseni (Draupadi) did not abandon the sons of Pritha and is adhered to her husband, as to Savitri to the Vedas or the rays of the sun to the Meru (mountain).

sn: प्रतिगृह्य च तां पूजां नारदो भगवानृषिः। आश्वासयद् धर्मसुतं युक्तरूपमिवानघ॥
en: O sinless one, having received their worship, the exalted Rishi Narada comforted the son of Dharma (Yudhishthira) in proper words.

sn: उवाच च महात्मानंधर्मराज युधिष्ठिरम्। ब्रूहिधर्मभृतां श्रेष्ठ केनार्थः किं ददानि ते॥
en: He thus spoke the high-souled Dharmaraja Yudhishthira, “O foremost of virtuous men, tell me what you seek and what I can give you."

sn: अथधर्मसुता राजा प्रणम्य भ्रातृभिः सह। उवाच प्राञ्जलिर्भूत्वा नारदं देवसम्मितम्॥
en: Then the son of , the king (Yudhishthira), bowing (to the Rishi) with his brothers, thus spoke with joined hands to Narada, the revered of the celestials.

sn: त्वयि तुष्टे महाभाग सर्वलोकाभिपूजिते। कृतमित्येव मन्येऽहं प्रसादात् तव सुव्रत॥
en: Yudhishthira said: O highly exalted one, O worshipped of all the worlds, O Rishi of excellent vows, when you are pleased with me, I consider that all my wishes are gratificd through your grace.

sn: यदि त्वहमनुग्राह्यो भ्रातृभिः सहितोऽनघ। संदेहं मे मुनिश्रेष्ठ तत्त्वतश्छेत्तुमर्हसि॥
en: O sinless one, O foremost of Rishis, I and my brothers deserve (to receive) your favours. You ought to dispel my doubt.

sn: प्रदक्षिणां यः कुरुते पृथिवीं तीर्थतत्परः। किं फलं तस्य कात्स्येन तद्भवान् वक्तुमर्हति॥
en: You should tell me in detail what merit is obtained by him who travels over the world with the desire of seeing the Tirthas and sacred shrines.

sn: नारद उवाच शृणु राजन्नवहितो यथा भीष्मेणधीमता। पुलस्त्यस्य सकाशाद् वै सर्वमेतदुपश्रुतम्॥
en: Narada said: O king, hear with attention what was heard by the intelligent Bhishma from Paulastya. Hear all that in detail.

sn: पुरा भागीरथीतीरे भीष्मोधर्मभृतां वरः। पित्र्यं व्रतं समास्थाय न्यवसन्मुनिभिः सह॥ शुभे देशे तथा राजन् पुण्ये देवर्षिसेविते। गङ्गाद्वारे महाभाग देवगन्धर्वसेविते॥
en: Formerly that foremost of virtuous men Bhishma, when observing the Pitrya vow, lived on the banks of the Bhagirathi with the Rishis. O king, O highly exalted one, it was a delightful and sacred region, situated on the source of the Ganges and frequented by the celestials and the Gandharvas.

sn: स पितॄस्तर्पयामास देवांश्च परमद्युतिः। ऋषींश्च तर्पयामास विधिदृष्टेन कर्मणा॥
en: That greatly effulgent hero (Bhishma) gratified the Pitris, the celestials and the Rishis with offering oblations to them according to the rites ordained in the Shastras.

sn: कस्यचित् त्वथ कालस्य जपन्नेव महायशाः। ददर्शाद्भुतसंकाशं पुलस्त्यमृषिसत्तमाम्॥
en: One day when the greatly illustrious one was thus engaged (in observing his vow), he saw that foremost of Rishis, Pulastya of wonderful appearance.

sn: स तं दृष्ट्वोग्रतपसं दीप्यमानमिव श्रिया। प्रहर्षमतुलं लेभे विस्मयं परमं ययौ॥
en: Seeing that austere ascetic, as if blazing with prosperity, he became exceedingly glad and was filled with great wonder.

sn: उपस्थितं महाभागं पूजयामास भारता भीष्मोधर्मभृतां श्रेष्ठो विधिदृष्टेन कर्मणा॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, then that foremost of virtuous men, Bhishma, worshipped according to the rites of the ordinance that highly exalted Rishi who had already arrived.

sn: शिरसा चार्घ्यमादाय शुचिः प्रयतमानसः। नाम संकीर्तयामास तस्मिन् ब्रह्मर्षिसत्तमे॥
en: Purifying himself and making his mind exceedingly attentive and also taking the Arghya on his head, he loudly uttered his name near that foremost of Rishis.

sn: भीष्मोऽहमस्मि भद्रं ते दासोऽस्मि तव सुव्रत। तव संदर्शनादेव मुक्तोऽहं सर्वकिल्बिषैः॥
en: "O Rishi of excellent vows, be blessed; I am Bhishma, your servant. At the very sight of yours I am cleansed of all my sins."

sn: एवमुक्त्वा महाराज भीष्मोधर्मभृतां परः। वाग्यतः प्राञ्जलिर्भूत्वा तृष्णीमासीद् युधिष्ठिर॥
en: O great king, O Yudhishthira, having said this, that foremost of virtuous men, Bhishma restraining his speech, stood (before the Rishi) in silence and with joined hands.

sn: तं दृष्ट्वा नियमेनाथ स्वाध्यायाम्नायकर्शितम्। भीष्मं कुरुकुलश्रेष्ठ मुनिः प्रीतमनाभवत्॥
en: Seeing that foremost of the Kuru race, Bhishma, rendered emaciated by the observance of vows and the study of the Vedas, the Rishi became exceedingly pleased.

sn: पुलस्त्य उवाच अनेन तवधर्मज्ञ प्रश्रयेण दमेन च। सत्येन च महाभाग तुष्टोऽस्मि तव सुव्रत॥
en: Pulastya said: O hero of excellent vows, learned in the precepts of virtue, O greatly exalted one, I am much pleased with your humility, self-control and truth.

sn: यस्येदृशस्तेधर्मोऽयं पितृभक्त्याश्रितोऽनघ। तेन पश्यसि मां पुत्र प्रीतिश्च परमा त्वयि॥
en: O sinless one, O son, it is for the virtue which you have acquired from your great regard and respect for your forefathers that you have been able to see me and that I have been so pleased with you.

sn: अमोघदर्शी भीष्माहं ब्रूहि किं करवाणि ते। यद् वक्ष्यसि कुरुश्रेष्ठ तस्य दातास्मि तेऽनघ॥
en: O Bhishma, my eyes can penetrate into everything. Tell me what I can do for you. O foremost of the Kuru race, O sinless one, I shall grant you whatever you will ask from me.

sn: भीष्म उवाच प्रीते त्वयि महाभाग सर्वलोकाभिपूजिते। कृतमेतावता मन्ये यदहं दृष्टवान् प्रभुम्॥
en: Bhishma said: O greatly exalted one, () worshipped of all the world, when you are pleased with me and when I have got a sight of you. I consider myself crowned with success.

sn: यदि त्वहमनुग्राह्यस्तवधर्मभृतां वर। संदेहं ते प्रवक्ष्यामि तन्मे त्वं छेत्तुमर्हसि॥
en: O foremost of all virtuous men, if I have deserved your favour, you will kindly dispel my doubts; I shall describe them to you.

sn: अस्ति मे हृदये कश्चित् तीर्थेभ्योधर्मसंशयः। तमहं श्रोतुमिच्छामि तद् भवान् वक्तुमर्हति॥
en: O exalted one, I have some religious doubts regarding Tirthas. I desire to hear you. Tell me separately of (each) in detail.

sn: प्रदक्षिणां यः पृथिवीं करोत्यमरसंनिभ। किं फलं तस्य विप्रर्षे तन्मे ब्रूहि सुनिश्चितम्॥
en: O celestials-like one, O Brahmana Rishi, what virtue is derived by him who travels over the earth, (seeing sacred places)? Tell me this with certainty.

sn: पुलस्त्य उवाच हन्त ते कथयिष्यामि यदृषीणां परायणम्। तदेकाग्रमनाः पुत्र शृणु तीर्थेषु यत् फलम्॥
en: Pulastya said: O son, listen to me with an attentive mind. I shall tell you the virtues which are derived in Tirthas that are the refuge of the Rishis.

sn: यस्य हस्तौ च पादौ च मनश्चैव सुसंयतम्। विद्या तपश्च कीर्तिश्च स तीर्थफलमश्नुते॥
en: He, whose hands, feet, mind, learning, asceticism and deeds are under proper control, enjoys the fruits of Tirthas.

sn: प्रतिग्रहादपावृत्तः संतुष्टो येन केनचित्। अहंकारनिवृत्तश्च स तीर्थफलमश्नुते॥
en: He, who has ceased to accept gifts, who is contented with little and who is free from pride, enjoys the fruits of Tirthas.

sn: अकल्कको निरारम्भो लघ्वाहारो जितेन्द्रियः। विमुक्तः सर्वपापेभ्यः स तीर्थफलमश्नुते॥
en: He who is free from sins, who acts without desire, who eats light food, who has conquered his passions and who is free from all sins, enjoys the fruits of Tirthas.

sn: अक्रोधनश्च राजेन्द्र सत्यशीलो दृढव्रतः। आत्मोपमश्च भूतेषु स तीर्थफलमश्नुते॥
en: O king of kings, he who is free from anger, who is truthful, who is firm in his vows and who considers all creatures as his own self, enjoys the fruits of Tirthas.

sn: ऋषिभिः क्रतवः प्रोक्ता देवेष्विह यथाक्रमम्। फलं चैव यथातथ्यं प्रेत्य चेह च सर्वशः॥
en: The Rishis have told in due order the sacrifices and also their fruits to be obtained here (in this birth) and hereafter (in the next birth).

sn: न ते शक्या दरिद्रेण यज्ञाः प्राप्तुं महीपते। बहूपकरणा यज्ञा नानासम्भारविस्तराः॥
en: O ruler of earth, the poor cannot perform these sacrifices, for the sacrifices require many materials and various things in large quantities.

sn: प्राप्यन्ते पार्थिवैरेते समृद्धैर्वा नरैः क्वचित्। नार्थन्यूनै वगणैरेकात्मभिरसाधनैः॥
en: These (sacrifices) therefore be performed by the kings and also by the men of wealth and affluence. They cannot be performed by men without wealth and without friends and by men destitute of means and destitute of friends.

sn: यो दरिद्रैरपि विधिः शक्यः प्राप्तुं नरेश्वर। तुल्यो यज्ञफलैः पुण्यैस्तुं निबोध युधां वर॥
en: O ruler of men, best of warriors, I shall now tell you about that which can be performed by the poor and the fruits of which are equal to those sacred ones of sacrifices.

sn: ऋषीणां परमं गुह्यमिदं भरतसत्तम। तीर्थाभिगमनं पुण्यं यज्ञैरपि विशिष्यते॥
en: foremost of the Bharata race, visiting Tirthas, which are sacred and which are a great mystery of the Rishis, is even superior to the sacrifices. can

sn: अनुपोष्य त्रिरात्राणि तीर्थान्यनभिगम्य च। अदत्त्वा काञ्चनं गाश्च दरिद्रो नाम जायते॥
en: He is called poor who, having gone to a Tirtha, does not fast for three nights and who does not give away gold and kine (in charity).

sn: अग्निष्टोमादिभिर्यज्ञैरिष्ट्वा विपुलदक्षिणैः। न तत् फलमवाप्नोति तीर्थाभिगमनेन यत्॥
en: One does not acquire so much virtue in Agnihotra and other sacrifices full of large Dakshinas, as he acquires by visiting a Tirtha.

sn: नृलोके देवदेवस्य तीर्थं त्रैलोक्यविश्रुतम्। पुष्करं नाम विख्यातं महाभागः समाविशेत्॥
en: There is in the world of men that Tirtha of the god of gods which is celebrated all over the three worlds and which is known by the name of Pushkara. One (who goes there) becomes equal to that greatly exalted deity (the god of gods).

sn: दशकोटिसहस्राणि तीर्थानां वै महामते। सांनिध्यं पुष्करे येषां त्रिसंध्यं कुरुनन्दन॥
en: O high-ininded one, O descendant of Kuru, at the three Sandhyas, there are always present hundred thousand millions of Tirthas in Pushkara.

sn: आदित्या वसवो रुद्राः साध्याश्च समरुद्गणाः। गन्धर्वाप्सरसश्चैव नित्यं संनिहिता विभो॥
en: O lord, the Adityas, the Vasus, the Rudras, the Sadhyas, the Maruts, the Gandharvas and the Apsaras are always present there.

sn: यत्र देवास्तपस्तत्त्वा दैत्या ब्रह्मर्षयस्तथा। दिव्ययोगा महाराज पुण्येन महतान्विताः॥
en: O great king, it was there that the Devas, the Danavas and the Brahmarshi, after performing their ascetic devotions, acquired great virtues and final divinity.

sn: मनसाप्यभिकामस्य पुष्कराणि मनस्विनः। पूयन्ते सर्वपापानि नाकपृष्ठे च पूज्यते॥
en: The sins of the intelligent man are all cleansed, even if he mentally thinks of Pushkara. He is adored even in heaven.

sn: तस्मिंस्तीर्थे महाराज नित्यमेव पितामहः। उवास परमप्रीतो भगवान् कमलासनः॥
en: O great king, the lotus-seated, illustrious Grand-Sire always dwells in great pleasure in this Tirtha.

sn: पुष्करेषु महाभाग देवाः सर्षिगणाः पुरा। सिद्धिं समभिसम्प्राप्ताः पुण्येन महतान्विताः॥
en: O greatly exalted one, is war formerly in Pushkara, that the celestials with the Rishis, having acquired great virtue, finally obtained the highest success.

sn: तत्राभिषेकं यः कुर्यात् पितृदेवार्चने रतः। अश्वमेधाद् दशगुणं फलं प्राहुर्मनीषिणः॥
en: The wise men say that those that bathe in it in honour of the Pitris and the celestials obtain ten times the fruits of the Ashvamedha sacrifice.

sn: अप्येकं भोजयेद् विप्रं पुष्करारण्यमाश्रितः। तेनासौ कर्मणा भीष्म प्रेत्य चेह च मोदते॥
en: O Bhishma, he, who, going to the forest of Pushkara, feeds but only one Brahmana, becomes by his that act happy here and hereafter.

sn: शाकैर्मूलैः फलैर्वापि येन वर्तयते स्वयम्। तद् वै दद्याद् ब्राह्मणाय श्रद्धावाननसूयकः॥
en: He, who supports himself on vegetables, roots and fruits, may very well offer such food to the Brahmanas with due regard and without any disrespect.

sn: तेनैव प्राप्नुयात् प्राज्ञो हयमेधफलं नरः। ब्राह्मणाः क्षत्रिया वैश्याः शूद्रा वा राजसत्तम॥ न वै योनौ प्रजायन्ते सघतास्तीर्थे महात्मनः।
en: O foremost of kings, the wise men obtain by it the fruits of the Ashvamedha sacrifice. Among the Brahmanas, Kshatriyas, Vaisyas and Sudras, those that are high-souled are freed from the bondage of rebirth, if they bathe in it.

sn: कार्तिकी तु विशेषेण योऽभिगच्छति पुष्करम्॥ प्राप्नुयात् स नरो लोकान् ब्रह्मणः सदनेऽक्षयान्।
en: Especially he who goes to Pushkara in the full-moon on the (month) of Kartikeya, that man, obtains everlasting regions in the abode of Brahma.

sn: सायं प्रातः स्मरेद् यस्तु पुष्कराणि कृताञ्जलिः॥ उपस्पृष्टं भवेत् तेन सर्वतीर्थेषु भारत।
en: O descendant of Bharata, he who thinks of Pushkara, morning and evening with joined hands, practically bathes in all the Tirthas.

sn: जन्मप्रभृति यत् पापं स्त्रिया वा पुरुषेण वा॥ पुष्करे स्नातमात्रस्य सर्वमेव प्रणश्यति।
en: Whatever sins a man or a woman commits from his and her birth, are all destroyed at the very moment he or she bathes in Pushkara.

sn: यथा सुराणां सर्वेषामादिस्तु मधुसूदनः॥ तथैव पुष्करं राजंस्तीर्थानामादिरुच्यते।
en: O king, as the slayer of Madhu is the origin of all the celestials, so is, Pushkara called the origin of all the Tirthas.

sn: उष्ट्वा द्वादश वर्षाणि पुष्करे नियतः शुचिः॥ क्रतून् सर्वानवाप्नोति ब्रह्मलोकं स गच्छति।
en: He who lives at Pushkara for twelve years in purity. Acquires all the merits of performing sacrifices and goes to the region of Brahma.

sn: यस्तु वर्षशतं पूर्णमग्निहोत्रमुपासते।॥ कार्तिकी वा वसेदेकां पुष्करे सममेव तत्॥
en: He who performs the sacred Agnihotra for one hundred years acquires the same mcrit as he who lives only one month of Kartikeya in Pushkara.

sn: त्रीणि शृङ्गाणि शुभ्राणि त्रीणि प्रस्रवणानि च। पुष्कराण्यादिसिद्धानि न विद्मस्तत्र कारणम्॥
en: There are three white hills and three springs (in Pushkara). We do not know why they are known by the name of Pushkara from the remotest time.

sn: दुष्करं पुष्करे गन्तुं दुष्करं पुष्करे तपः। दुष्करं पुष्करे दानं वस्तुं चैव सुदुष्करम्॥
en: It is very difficult to go to Pushkara; it is very difficult to undergo asceticism Pushkara; it is very difficult to give away in charity at Pushkara.

sn: उष्य द्वादशरात्रं तु नियतो नियताशन:। प्रदक्षिणमुपावृत्य जम्बूमार्गं समाविशेत्॥
en: Having lived for twelve nights at Pushkara with regulated diet and regulated food and having walked round it, one goes to Jambu marga. at

sn: जम्बूमार्ग समाविश्य देवर्षिपितृसेवितम्। अश्वमेधमवाप्नोति सर्वकामसमन्वितः॥
en: He who goes to the Jambu marga which is frequented by the celestials Rishis and the Pitris, obtains the fruits of a horse-sacrifice and fulfillment of all his wishes.

sn: तत्रोष्य रजनी: पञ्च पूतात्मा जायते नरः। न दुर्गतिमवाप्नोति सिद्धिं प्राप्नोति चोत्तमाम्॥
en: He who lives there for five nights has his soul cleansed of all sins. He does not meet with any distress; he obtains the highest success.

sn: जम्बूमार्गादुपावृत्य गच्छेत् तन्दुलिकाश्रमम्। न दुर्गतिमवाप्नोति ब्रह्मलोकं च गच्छति॥
en: O great king, leaving Jambu marga one goes to the Tandulikasrama. He who goes there never meets with any disaster, but goes to the region of Brahma.

sn: आगस्त्यं सर आसाद्य पितृदेवार्चने रतः। त्रिरात्रोपोषितो राजन्नाग्निष्टोमफलं लभेत्॥
en: O king, he who goes to Agastya's lake and engages himself in the worship of the Pitris and the celestials, fasting there for three nights, obtains the fruits of performing Agnishtoma.

sn: शाकवृत्तिः फलैर्वापि कौमारं विन्दते परम्। कण्वाश्रमं ततो गच्छेच्छ्रीजुष्टं लोकपूजितम्॥
en: He who (going there) lives on vegetables or fruits acquires the state of Kumara. One should then go to the hermitage of Kansa, worshipped by the whole world.

sn: धर्मारण्यं हि तत् पुण्यमाद्यं च भरतर्षभ। यत्र प्रविष्टमात्रो वै सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, it was a sacred and holy forest from the remotest time. As soon as one enters it, he is cleansed of all his sins.

sn: अर्चयित्वा पितॄन् देवान् नियतो नियताशनः। सर्वकामसमृद्धस्य यज्ञस्य फलमश्नुते॥
en: He, who with regulated diet and vows worships here the Pitris and the celestials, obtains the fruits of performing sacrifices and fulfillment of all his wishes.

sn: प्रदक्षिणं ततः कृत्वा ययातिपतनं व्रजेत्। हयमेधस्य यज्ञस्य फलं प्राप्नोति तत्र वै॥
en: Having walked round it, one should go where Yayati fell. This gives that man fruits, obtained by the performance of a horsesacrifice.

sn: महाकालं ततो गच्छेन्नियतो नियताशनः। कोटितीर्थमुपस्पृश्य हयमेधफलं लभेत्॥
en: One should then go to Mahakala with regulated diet and vows. Having bathed in the Kati Tirtha he obtains the fruit of a horsesacrifice.

sn: ततो गच्छेत्धर्मज्ञः स्थाणोस्तीर्थमुमापतेः। नाम्ना भद्रवटं नाम त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतम्॥
en: The virtuous man then should go to the Tirtha of Sthanu, the husband of Uma, which is known all over the three worlds by the name of Bhadravata.

sn: तत्राभिगम्य चेशानं गोसहस्रफलं लभेत्। महादेवप्रसादाच्च गाणपत्यं च विन्दति॥ समृद्धमसपत्नं च श्रिया युक्तं नरोत्तमः।
en: Going there he beholds Ishana and obtains the fruit of (giving away) one thousand kine. Through the grace of Mahadeva (Shiva), he obtains the state of Ganapatya. That foremost of man becomes blessed with prosperity, peace and highest grace.

sn: नर्मदां तु समासाद्य नदीं त्रैलोक्यविश्रुताम्॥ तर्पयित्वा पितॄन् देवानग्निष्टोमफलं लभेत्।
en: Going to the river Narmada which is celebrated all over the three worlds, he obtains the fruit of Agnishtoma by offering oblations to the Pitris and the celestials.

sn: दक्षिणं सिन्धुमासाद्य ब्रह्मचारी जितेन्द्रियः॥ अग्निष्टोममवाप्नोति विमानं चाधिरोहति।
en: Going to the southern sea, he who practices Brahmacharya and conquers his passions obtains the fruit of Agnishtoma and ascends to heaven.

sn: चर्मण्वतीं समासाद्य नियतो नियताशनः। रन्तिदेवाभ्यनुज्ञातमग्निष्टोमफलं लभेत्॥
en: Going to Charmanvati with regulated diet and vows, he obtains at the command of Rantideva the fruit of Agnishtoma sacrifice.

sn: ततो गच्छेतधर्मज्ञ हिमवत्सुतमर्बुदम्। पृथिव्यां यत्र वै छिद्रं पूर्वमासीद् युधिष्ठिर॥
en: O virtuous king, O Yudhishthira, he should then go to the son of Himavata, named Arvuda, where there is a hole through the earth from ancient days.

sn: तत्राश्रमो वसिष्ठस्य त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतः। तत्रोष्य रजनीमेकां गोसहस्रफलं लभेत्॥
en: There is the hermitage of Vasishtha, celebrated over the three worlds. He who lives there only for one night obtains the merit of giving away one thousand kine.

sn: पिङ्गतीर्थमुपस्पृश्य ब्रह्मचारी जितेन्द्रियः। कपिलानां नरश्रेष्ठ शतस्य फलमश्नुते॥
en: O ruler of men, O foremost of men, he who leading the life of a Brahmachari bathes in the Pinga Tirtha obtains the merit of giving away one hundred Kapila kine.

sn: ततो गच्छेत राजेन्द्र प्रभासं तीर्थमुत्तमम्। तत्र संनिहितो नित्यं स्वयमेव हुताशनः॥ देवतानां मुखं वीर ज्वलनोऽनिलसारथिः।
en: O King of kings, thence one should go to that excellent Tirtha called Pravasha; Hutashana (Agni) himself is always present there. O hero, he is the mouth of the celestials and has wind for his chariot.

sn: तस्मिंस्तीर्थे नरः स्नात्वा शुचिः प्रयतमानसः॥ अग्निष्टोमातिरात्राभ्यां फलं प्राप्नोति मानवः।
en: If a man bathes in this Tirtha with subdued mind, he becomes pure. That man obtains the fruits of performing Agnishtoma and Atiratha sacrifices.

sn: ततो गत्वा सरस्वत्याः सागरस्य च संगमे॥ गोसहस्रफलं तस्य स्वर्गलोकं च विन्दति। प्रभया दीप्यते नित्यमग्निवद् भरतर्षभ॥
en: One should then go to the place where river Sarasvati mixes with the ocean. He who goes there obtains the fruit giving away one thousand kine and acquires also heaven. O best of the Bharata race, he always blazes like the fire.

sn: तीर्थ सलिलराजस्य स्नात्वा प्रयतमानसः। त्रिरात्रमुषित: स्नातस्तर्पयेत् पितृदेवताः॥
en: He who bathes in the Tirtha of the chief of water with subdued mind and lives there three nights and offers oblations to the Pitris and the celestials.

sn: प्रभासते यथा सोमः सोऽश्वमेधं च विन्दति। वरदानं ततो गच्छेत् तीर्थं भरतसत्तम॥
en: Blazes forth like the Moon and obtains the fruits of Ashvamedha sacrifice. O best of the Bharata race, one should then go to the Tirtha named Vasudeva,

sn: विष्णोर्दुर्वाससा यत्र वरो दत्तो युधिष्ठिर। वरदाने नरः स्नात्वा गोसहस्रफलं लभेत्॥
en: Where Durvasha bestowed a boon on Vishnu. The man who bathes in Vardana obtains the fruits of giving away one thousand kine.

sn: ततो द्वारवतीं गच्छेन्नियतो नियताशनः। पिण्डारके नरः स्नात्वा लभेद् बहु सुवर्णकम्॥
en: Then one should go to Daravati with regulated diet and vows. The man who bathes in the Pindaraka obtains (the merit of giving away) much gold.

sn: तस्मिंस्तीर्थे महाभाग पद्मलक्षणलक्षिताः। अद्यापि मुद्रा दृश्यन्ते तदद्भुतमरिंदम्॥
en: O greatly exalted one, O chastiser of foes, it is wonderful that in that Tirtha even today coins are found with the marks of lotus;

sn: त्रिशूलाङ्कानि पानि दृश्यन्ते कुरुनन्दन। महादेवस्य सांनिध्यं तत्र वै पुरुषर्षभ॥
en: And lotuses are seen with the marks of trident. O descendant of Kuru, O foremost of men, Mahadeva is always present there.

sn: सागरस्य च सिन्धोश्च संगम प्राप्य भारत। तीर्थे सलिलराजस्य स्नात्वा प्रयतमानसः॥ तर्पयित्वा पितॄन् देवानृषीश्च भरतर्षभ। प्राप्नोति वारुणं लोकं दीप्यमानं स्वतेजसा॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, going to the place where the Sindhu mixes with the sea and bathing in the Tirtha of the chief of the water with subdued mind, O best of the Bharata, race and also offering oblations to the Pitris, the Rishis and the celestials, one obtains the region of Varuna and blazes forth in his own effulgence.

sn: शकुकर्णेश्वरं देवमर्चयित्वा युधिष्ठिर। अश्वमेधाद् दशगुणं प्रवदन्ति मनीषिणः॥
en: O Yudhishthira, the wise men say that by worshipping the deity, Sankhakarneshvara, one obtains ten times the merit of Ashvamedha (sacrifice).

sn: प्रदक्षिणमुपावृत्य गच्छेत् भरतर्षभ। तीर्थं कुरुवरश्रेष्ठ त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतम्॥ दमीति नाम्ना विख्यातं सर्वपापप्रणाशनम्। तत्र ब्रह्मादयो देवा उपासन्ते महेश्वरम्॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, O foremost of the Kurus, having walked round it, one should go to the Tirtha, celebrated all over the three worlds. It is known by the name of Drimi, which is capable of cleansing off all sins and where the celestials including including Brahma worshipped Maheshvara (Shiva).

sn: तत्र स्नात्वा च पीत्वा च रुद्रं देवगणैर्वृतम्। जन्मप्रभृति यत् पापं तत् स्नातस्य प्रणश्यति॥
en: Bathing in it and worshipping here Rudra surrounded by the celestials, all the sins committed from one's birth are cleansed off.

sn: दमी चात्र नरश्रेष्ठ सर्वदेवैरभिष्टुतः। तत्र स्नात्वा नरव्याघ्र हयमेधमवाप्नुयात्॥
en: O foremost of men, it was here that Drimi was worshipped by all the celestials. Bathing here one obtains the fruits of Ashvamedha (sacrifice).

sn: गत्वा यत्र महाप्राज्ञ विष्णुना प्रभविष्णुना। पुरा शौचं कृतं राजन् हत्वा दैतेयदानवान्॥
en: O greatly wise man, O king, here did Vishnu, the creator of the universe, after killing the Daityas and the Danavas, purify himself.

sn: ततो गच्छेतधर्मज्ञ वसोर्धारामभिष्टुताम्। गमनादेव तस्यां हि हयमेधफलं लभेत्॥
en: O virtuous king, one should then go to Vasudhara which is worshipped by all. He who goes there obtains the fruits of Ashvamedha (sacrifice).

sn: स्नात्वा कुरुवरश्रेष्ठ प्रयतात्मा समाहितः। तर्घ्य देवान् पितॄश्चैव विष्णुलोके महीयते॥
en: O foremost of the Kurus, bathing there with subdued soul and rapt attention and offering oblations to the Pitris and the celestials one is adored in the regions of Vishnu.

sn: तीर्थे चात्र सरः पुण्यं वसूनां भरतर्षभ। तत्र स्नात्वा च पीत्वा च वसूनां सम्मतो भवेत्॥ सिन्धूत्तममिति ख्यातं सर्वपापप्रणाशनम्। तत्र स्नात्वा नरश्रेष्ठ लभेद् बहु सुवर्णकम्॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, in that Tirtha there is a lake of the Vasus. Bathing in it and drinking its water, one becomes respected of the Vasus. O foremost of men, it is known by the name of Sindhuttama and it destroys all sins. Bathing in it one obtains (the fruits of giving away) much gold.

sn: भद्रतुङ्गं समासाद्य शुचिः शीलसमन्वितः। ब्रह्मलोकमवाप्नोति गतिं च परमां व्रजेत्॥
en: Going to Bharutunga, with purity of conduct, one goes to the region of Brahma and obtains the highest state.

sn: कुमारिकाणां शक्रस्य तीर्थं सिद्धनिषेवितम्। तत्र स्नात्वा नरः क्षिप्रं स्वर्गलोकमवाप्नुयात्॥
en: Then is the Tirtha, called Kumariak of Sakra (Indra), frequented by the Siddhas. O foremost of men, bathing there one obtains the region of Sakra (Indra).

sn: रेणुकायाश्च तत्रैव तीर्थं सिद्धनिषेवितम्। तत्र स्नात्वा भवेद् विप्रो निर्मलश्चन्द्रमा यथा॥
en: There is another Tirtha called Renuka, frequented by the Siddhas. Bathing in it, a Brahmana becomes as pure as the moon.

sn: अथ पञ्चनदं गत्वा नियतो नियताशनः। पञ्चयज्ञानवाप्नोति क्रमशो येऽनुकीर्तिताः॥
en: Then going to the five rivers with regulated food and vows, one obtains the fruits of the five sacrifices as described in order in the Shastras).

sn: ततो गच्छेत राजेन्द्र भीमायाः स्थानमुत्तमम्। तत्र सषत्वा तु योन्यां वै नरो भरतसत्तम॥ देव्याः पुत्रो भवेद् राजंस्तप्तकुण्डलविग्रहः। गवां शतसहस्रस्य फलं प्राप्नोति मानवः॥
en: O king of kings, one should then go to the excellent region of Bhima. O best of the Bharata race, bathing there in Yoni (Tirtha) a man. Becomes, O king, a son of a goddess, adorned with earring set with pearls. That man also obtains the fruits of giving away one thousand kine.

sn: श्रीकुण्डं तु समासाद्य त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतम्। पितामहं नमस्कृत्य गोसहस्रफलं लभेत्॥
en: Going to Srikunda, celebrated over the three worlds and bowing there to the Grandsire, one obtains the fruit of giving away one thousand kine.

sn: ततो गच्छेतधर्मज्ञ विमलं तीर्थमुत्तमम्। अद्यापि यत्र दृश्यन्ते मत्स्याः सौवर्णराजताः॥
en: O virtuous man, one should then go to that excellent Tirtha called Simala, where even today are to be seen fishes of silver and golden colour.

sn: तत्र स्नात्वा नरः क्षिप्रं वासवं लोकमाप्नुयात्। सर्वपापविशुद्धात्मा गच्छेत परमां गतिम्॥
en: Bathing in it a man soon obtains the region of Vashava (Indra) and his soul becomes pure with all his sins destroyed; he also obtains the highest state.

sn: वितस्तां च समासाद्य संतर्घ्य पितृदेवताः। नरः फलमवाप्नोति वाजपेयस्य भारत॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, going to Vitasta and offering oblations to the Pitris and the celestials a man obtains the fruits of the Vajapeya (sacrifice).

sn: काश्मीरेष्वेव नागस्य भवनं तक्षकस्य च। वितस्ताख्यमिति ख्यातं सर्वपापप्रमोचनम्॥
en: The Tirtha known by the name of Vitasta is situated in Kashmira and it is the abode of Naga and Takshaka. It is capable of destroying all sins.

sn: तत्र स्नात्वा नरो नूनं वाजपेयमवाप्नुयात्। सर्वपापविशुद्धात्मा गच्छेच्च परमां गतिम्॥
en: Bathing there a man is certain to obtain the fruits of the Vajapeya sacrifice. His soul becoming pure with all his sins destroyed, he obtains the highest state.

sn: ततो गच्छेत वडवां त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुताम्। पश्चिमायां तु संध्यायामुपस्पृश्य यथाविधि॥ चरूं सप्तार्चिषे राजन् यथाशक्ति निवेदयेत्। पितृणामक्षयं दानं प्रवदन्ति मनीषिणः॥
en: O king, one should then go to the Vadaba, celebrated all over the three worlds. Bathing there with due rites in the evening, one should offer Charu (rice boiled in butter and milk) according to the best of his means to the deity of seven flames (fire). The learned men say that gift to the Pitris (offered there) becomes inexhaustible.

sn: ऋषयः पितरो देवा गन्धर्वापसरसां गणाः। गुह्यकाः किन्नरा यक्षाः सिद्धा विद्याधरा नराः॥ राक्षसा दितिजा रुद्रा ब्रह्मा च मनुजाधिप। नियतः परमां दीक्षामास्थायाब्दसहस्रिकीम्॥ विष्णोः प्रसादनं कुर्वश्चरुं च श्रपयंस्तथा। सप्तभिः सप्तभिश्चैव ऋग्भिस्तुष्टाव केशवम्॥
en: The Rishis, the Pitris, the Devas, the Gandharvas, the Apsaras, the Guhyakas, the Siddhas, the Vidyadharas, the men. The Rakshashas, the Daityas, the Rudras, the Brahma himself, O ruler of men, having their senses subdued and having performed austere asceticism for one thousand years. In order to secure the grace of Vishnu, cooked Charu here and gratified Keshava (Vishnu) with oblation (offered), each time uttering seven Riks (the verse of three Vedas).

sn: ददावष्टगुणैश्वर्यं तेषां तुष्टस्तु केशवः। यथाभिलषितानन्यान् कामान् दत्त्वा महीपते॥ तत्रैवान्तरर्दधे देवो विद्युदभ्रेषु वै यथा। नाम्ना सप्तचरूं तेन ख्यातं लोकेषु भारत॥ गवां शतसहस्रेण राजसूयशतेन च। अश्वमेधसहस्रेण श्रेयान् सप्तार्चिषे चरुः॥ ततो निवृत्तो राजेन्द्र रुद्रं पदमथाविशेत्। अर्चयित्वा महादेवमश्वमेधफलं लभेत्॥
en: O ruler of earth, Keshava, being thus gratified, bestowed on them the eight-fold attributes, called Aishvarya and other objects which they had desired to obtain. O descendant of Bharata, having bestowed these on them the one deity disappeared before their very sight as a flash of lightning in a cloud. Thus did it become known on earth by the name of Sapta Charu. If seven Charus are offered here, it secures greater merit than that of giving away one thousand kine, that of one hundred Rajasuyas and that of thousand Ashvamedhas (sacrifices). O king of kings, leaving that Tirtha, one should go to the Raudra Pada and worshipping Mahadeva there, one obtains the fruit of Ashvamedha sacrifice.

sn: मणिमन्तं समासाद्यं ब्रह्मचारी समाहितः। एकरात्रोषितो राजन्नग्निष्टोमफलं लभेत्॥
en: O king, going to Manimanta and practising Brahmacharya and subduing one's mind and living there for (only) one night, one obtains the fruits of Agnishtoma (sacrifice).

sn: अथ गच्छेत राजेन्द्र देविकां लोकविश्रुताम्। प्रसूतिर्यत्र विप्राणां श्रूयते भरतर्षभ॥
en: O king of kings, O best of the Bharata race, one should then go to Davika, celebrated all over the world. It is heard that the Brahmana first came into existence in that place.

sn: त्रिशूलपाणे: स्थानं च त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतम्। देविकायाः नरः स्नात्वा समभ्यर्च्य महेश्वरम्॥ यथाशक्ति चरूं तत्र निवेद्य भरतर्षभ। सर्वकामसमृद्धस्य यज्ञस्य लभते फलम्॥
en: Here is situated the region of the wielder of the trident (Shiva) which is celebrated all over the world. Bathing in the Davika and worshipping Maheshvara and by offering Charu to the best of the deities, O best of the Bharata race, one obtains the fruit of sacrifices that is capable of fulfilling every desire.

sn: कामाख्यं तत्र रुद्रस्य तीर्थं देवनिषेवितम्। तत्र स्नात्वा नरः क्षिप्रं सिद्धिं प्राप्नोति भारत॥
en: There is another Tirtha of Rudra, called Kamakya frequented by the celestials. Bathing in it, a man soon obtains salvation.

sn: यजनं याजनं चैव तथैव ब्रह्म वालुकाम्। पुष्पाम्भश्च उपस्पृश्य न शोचेन्मरणं गतः॥
en: By touching the water of Yajana, Yojana, Branka, Valuka and Pushpama one becomes freed from grief and death.

sn: अर्धयोजनविस्तारा पञ्चयोजनमायता। एतावती वेदिका तु पुण्या देवर्षिसेविता॥
en: It is said that the sacred Dabhika (Tirtha), frequented by the celestials and Rishis, is five yojanas in length and half a yojana in breadth.

sn: ततो गच्छेतधर्मज्ञ दीर्घसत्रं यथाक्रमम्। तत्र ब्रह्मादयो देवाः सिद्धाश्च परमर्षयः॥
en: O king, one should then go in due order to Dirghasatra. There did Brahma and the celestials, the Siddhas and the great Rishis.

sn: दीर्घसत्रमुपासन्ते दीक्षिता नियतव्रताः॥
en: Being installed performed the longextending sacrifice with regulated vows.

sn: गमनादेव राजेन्द्र दीर्घसत्रमरिंदम्। राजसूयाश्वमेधाभ्यां फलं प्राप्नोति भारत॥
en: O king of kings, O chastiser of foes, O descendant of Bharata, going to Dirghasatra, one obtains the fruits of Rajasuya and Ashvamedha.

sn: ततो विनशनं गच्छेनियतो नियताशनः। गच्छत्यन्तर्हिता यत्र मेरुपृष्ठे सरस्वती।१११॥
en: Then one should go with regulated diet and subdued soul to Vinasana, where the Sarasvati, disappeared on the breast of the Meru (mountain).

sn: चमसेऽथ शिवोद्भेदे नागोद्भेदे च दृश्यते। स्नात्वा तु चमसोद्भेदे अग्निष्टोमफलं लभेत्॥
en: And then again reappeared at Chamasha, Sivodveda and Nagaveda. Bathing in Ckamashveda one obtains the fruits of Agnishtoma.

sn: शिवोद्भेदे नरः स्नात्वा गोसहस्रफलं लभेत्। नागोद्भेदे नरः स्नात्वा नागलोकमवाप्नुयात्॥
en: Bathing in Sivodveda a man obtains the fruits of giving away one thousand kine. Bathing in Nagaveda a man goes to the region of the Nagas.

sn: शशयानं च राजेन्द्र तीर्थमासाद्य दुर्लभम्। शशरूपप्रतिच्छन्नाः पुष्करा यत्र भारत॥ सरस्वत्यां महाराज अनुसंवत्सरं च ते। दृश्यन्ते भरतश्रेष्ठ वृत्तां वै कार्तिकी सदा॥ तत्र स्नात्वा नरव्याघ्र द्योतते शशिवत् सदा। गोसहस्रफलं चैव प्राप्नुयाद् भरतर्षभ॥
en: O king of kings, going to the inaccessible Tirtha, called Sashyana, where the cranes disappear in the forms of Susas and reappear every year in the month of Kartikeya and bathe in the Sarasvati. O descendant of Bharata, O best of the Bharata race, O greatly exalted one. O chief of men, one, bathing there, becomes like the moon and obtains the fruits of giving away one thousand kine.

sn: कुमारकोटिमासाद्य नियत: कुरुनन्दन। तत्राभिषेकं कुर्वीत पितृदेवार्चने रतः॥
en: O descendant of Kuru, going next to Kumarkoti with subdued soul, one should bathe there and engage himself in worshipping the celestials and the Pitris.

sn: गवामयुतमाप्नोति कुलं चैव समुद्धरेत्। ततो गच्छेतधर्मज्ञ रुद्रकोटि समाहितः॥ पुरा यत्र महाराज मुनिकोटिः समागता। हर्षेण महताविष्टा रुद्रदर्शनकाझ्या॥ अहं पूर्वमहं पूर्वं द्रक्ष्यामि वृषभध्वजम्। एवं सम्प्रस्थिता राजऋषयः किल भारत॥
en: He thus obtains the fruits of giving away ten thousand kine and raises his race to the highest state. O virtuous man, one should then go to Rudrakati with subdued soul. Here, O great king, in olden days ten millions of Rishis were assembled and were filled with great joy at the prospect of seeing Rudra (Shiva). O descendant of Bharata, O king, “I have first seen (the deity) Vrishadhvaja" "I have first seen (the deity) Vrishadhvaja” thus the Rishis spoke to one another.

sn: ततो योगेश्वरेणापि योगमास्थाय भूपते। तेषां मन्युप्रणाशार्थमृषीणाां भावितात्मनाम्॥ सृष्टा कोटीति रुद्राणामृषीणामग्रतः स्थिता। मया पूर्वतरं दृष्ट इति ते मेनिरे पृथक्॥ तेषां तुष्टो महादेवो मुनीनां भावितात्मनाम्। भक्त्या परमया राजन् वरं तेषां प्रदिष्टवान्॥
en: O ruler of earth, thereupon in order to prevent disputes among those self-controlled Rishis, the lord of Yoga (Shiva) by his Yoga powers, multiplied himself into ten millions of forms and appeared before the Rishis. Then they all separately thought, “I have seen him first.” () king, being (nuch) pleased with the great devotion of those Rishis of subdued soul, Mahadeva granted them a boon.

sn: अद्यप्रभृति युप्माकंधर्मवृद्धिर्भविष्यति। तत्र स्नात्वा नरव्याघ्र रुद्रकोट्यां नरः शुचिः॥ अश्वमेधमवाप्नोति कुलं चैव समुद्धरेत्।
en: (Saying) “From today your virtues will increase." ( foremost of men, bathing with purity in Raudrakota a inan obtains the fruits of the Ashvamedha (sacrifice) and saves his race.

sn: ततो गच्छेत राजेन्द्र संगमं लोकविश्रुतम्॥ सरस्वत्या महापुण्यं केशवं समुपासते। यत्र ब्रह्मादयो देवा ऋषयश्च तपोधनाः॥
en: O king of kings, one should then go to the Sangama, celebrated all over the world. A region of great sacredness, where the Sarasvati mixes with the sea. Here Keshava is worshipped by Brahma and other celestials, by Rishis and by ascetics.

sn: अभिगच्छन्ति राजेन्द्र चैत्रशुक्लचतुर्दशीम्। तत्र स्नात्वा नरव्याघ्र विन्देद् बहुसुवर्णकम्। सर्वपापविशुद्धात्मा ब्रह्मलोकं च गच्छति॥
en: On the fourteenth day of the white fortnight of Chaitra, O king of kings, O foremost of men, bathing there one obtains the fruits of giving away much wealth. His sins being all destroyed and his soul becoming pure, he goes to the region of Brahma.

sn: ऋषीणां यत्र सत्राणि समाप्तानि नराधिप। तत्रावसानमासाद्य गोसहस्रफलं लभेत्॥
en: O ruler of men, it is there that the Rishis completed many sacrifices. Going to this Satravasana one obtains the fruits of giving away one thousand kine.

sn: पुलस्त्य उवाच ततो गच्छेत राजेन्द्र कुरुक्षेत्रमभिष्टुतम्। पापेभ्यो यत्र मुच्यन्ते दर्शनात् सर्वजन्तवः॥
en: Pulastya said: O king of kings, one should then go to Kurukshetra, adored by all and at the sight of which sins of all creatures are destroyed.

sn: कुरुक्षेत्रं गमिष्यामि कुरुक्षेत्रे वसाम्यहम्। य एवं सततं ब्रूयात् सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते॥
en: He who always says, “I shall go to Kurukshetra, I shall live in Kurukshetra" is cleansed off all his sins.

sn: पांसवोऽपि कुरुक्षेत्रे वायुना समुदीरिताः। अपि दुष्कृतकर्माणं नयन्ति परमां गतिम्॥
en: The very dust of Kurukshetra carried by the wind leads even the man of sinful deeds to the highest state.

sn: दक्षिणेन सरस्वत्या दृषद्वत्युत्तरेण च। ये वसन्ति कुरुक्षेत्रे ते वसन्ति त्रिविष्टपे॥
en: He who lives in Kurukshetra which is situated south of the Sarasvati and the north of the Drishadvati (really) lives in heaven.

sn: तत्र मासं वसेद्धीरः सरस्वत्यां युधिष्ठिर। यत्र ब्रह्मादयो देवा ऋषयः सिद्धचारणाः॥
en: O hero ever stcady in battle and should live there for a month where flows the Sarasvati. Brahma and other celestials, the Rishis, the Siddhas, the Charans.

sn: गन्धर्वाप्सरसो यक्षाः पन्नगाश्च महीपते। ब्रह्मक्षेत्रं महापुण्यमभिगच्छन्ति भारत॥
en: The Gandharvas, the Apsaras the Yakshas, the Nagas, O ruler of earth, O descendant of Bharata, all often go to that greatly sacred Brahmakshetra.

sn: मनसाप्यभिकामस्य कुरुक्षेत्रं युधिष्ठिर। पापानि विप्रणश्यन्ति ब्रह्मलोकं च गच्छति॥
en: O hero steady in battle, even the sins of him who only mentally desires to go to Kurukshetra are all destroyed; and he goes to the region of Brahma.

sn: गत्वा हि श्रद्धया युक्तः कुरुक्षेत्रं कुरूद्वह। फलं प्राप्नोति च तदा राजसूयाश्वमेधयोः॥
en: O perpetuator of the Kuru race, he who goes to Kurukshetra with due respect, obtains the fruits of Rajasuya and Ashvamedha sacrifices,

sn: ततो मङ्खनकं नाम द्वारपालं महाबलम्। यक्षं समभिवाद्यैव गोसहस्रफलं लभेत्॥
en: Then saluting the greatly powerful gatekeeper, the Yaksha, Mankanaka, one obtains the fruits of giving away one thousand kine.

sn: ततो गच्छेतधर्मज्ञ विष्णो: स्थानमनुत्तमम्। सततं नाम राजेन्द्र यत्र संनिहितो हरिः॥
en: O virtuous man, O king of kings, one should then go to the excellent region of Vishnu, called Satata, where Hari is always present.

sn: तत्र स्नात्वा च नत्वा च त्रिलोकप्रभवं हरिम्। अश्वमेधमवाप्नोति विष्णुलोकं च गच्छति॥ ततः पारिप्लवं गच्छेत् तीर्थं त्रैलोक्यविश्रुतम्। अग्निष्टोमातिरात्राभ्यां फलं प्राप्नोति भारत॥
en: Bathing there and bowing to Hari, the creator of the three worlds, one obtains the fruits of Ashvamedha sacrifice and goes to the region of Vishnu. Then one should go to the Tirtha named Pariplava, celebrated all over the three worlds. O descendant of Bharata, he obtains greater fruits than those of the Agnishtoma and Atiratha (sacrifices).

sn: पृथिवीतीर्थमासाद्य गोसहस्रफलं लभेत्। ततः शालूकिनी गत्वा तीर्थसेवी नराधिप।॥ दशाश्वमेधे स्नात्वा च तदेव फलमाप्नुयात्। सर्पदेवीं समासाद्य नागानां तीर्थमुत्तमम्॥ अग्निष्टोममवाप्नोति नागलोकं च विन्दति। ततो गच्छेतधर्मज्ञ द्वारपालं तरन्तुकम्॥ तत्रोष्य रजनीमेकां गोसहस्रफलं लभेत्। ततः पञ्चनदं गत्वा नियतो नियताशनः॥ कोटितीर्थमुपस्पृश्य हयमेधफलं लभेत्। अश्विनोस्तीर्थमासाद्य रूपवानभिजायते॥
en: Then going to the Tirtha, called Prithivi one obtains the fruits of giving away one thousand kine. O ruler of men, going to the Salukini, the pilgrim, bathing there in the Dasashvamedha obtains the fruits of ten Ashvamedha sacrifice. Then going to the excellent Tirtha of the Nagas, called Sarpadevi. One obtains fruits of the Agnishtoma (sacrifice) and goes to the region of the Nagas. O virtuous man, one should then go to the gate-keeper, Tarantuka. Living there for only one night, one obtains the fruits of giving away one thousand kine. Then going to the five rivers with regulated diet and subdued soul and bathing in the Koti Tirtha, one obtains the fruits of Ashvamedha sacrifice. Going to the Tirtha called Ashvins one acquires personal beauty.

sn: ततो गच्छेतधर्मज्ञ वाराहं तीर्थमुत्तमम्। विष्णुर्वाराहरूपेण पूर्वं यत्र स्थितोऽभवत्॥ तत्र स्नात्वा नरश्रेष्ठ अग्निष्टोमफलं लभेत्।
en: O virtuous man, one should then go to the excellent Tirtha, called Varaha, where Vishnu formerly in his boar form lived. O foremost of men, bathing there one obtains the fruits of Agnishtoma.

sn: ततो जयन्त्यां राजेन्द्र सोमतीर्थं समाविशेत्॥ स्नात्वा फलमवाप्नोति राजसूयस्य मानवः।
en: O king of kings, one should then go to the Soma Tirtha, situated in Jayanti, Bathing in it a man obtains the fruits of the Rajasuya sacrifice.

sn: एकहंसे नरः स्नात्वाः गोसहस्रफलं लभेत्॥ कृताशौचं समासाद्य तीर्थसेवी नराधिप। पुण्डरीकमवाप्नोति कृतशौतो भवेच्च सः॥
en: Bathing in Ekahansa a man obtains the fruits of giving away one thousand kine. O ruler of men, going to Kritashocha, the pilgrim obtains the lotus-eyed deity (Vishnu) and becomes pure in soul.

sn: ततो मुञ्जवटं नाम स्थाणोः स्थानं महात्मनः। उपोष्य रजनीमेकां गाणपत्यमवाप्नुयात्॥
en: Then going to the region of the illustrious Sihanu (Shiva, called Manjabata and living there for one night, one acquires the state of Ganapathya.

sn: तत्रैव च महाराज यक्षिणी लोकविश्रुताम्। स्नात्वाभिगम्य राजेन्द्र सर्वान् कामानवाप्नुयात्॥
en: O great king, there is the celebrated Tirtha called Yakshini; O king of kings, going and bathing in that Tirtha one's all desires are fulfilled.

sn: कुरुक्षेत्रस्य तद् द्वारं विश्रुतं भरतर्षभ। प्रदक्षिणमुपावृत्य तीर्थसेवी समाहितः॥ सम्मितं पुष्कराणां च स्नात्वार्य पितृदेवताः। जामदग्न्येन रामेण कृतं तत् सुमहात्मना॥ कृतकृत्यो भवेद् राजन्नश्वमेधं च विन्दति। ततो रामह्रदान गच्छेत् तीर्थसेवी समाहितः॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, it is known as the gate of Kurukshetra. The pilgrim with subdued soul should walk round it. It was created by the illustrious son of Jamadagni, Rama. It is equal to the Pushkara. O king, bathing in it and worshipping the Pitris and the celestials, he becomes successful in everything and obtains the fruits of Ashvamedha sacrifice. Then the pilgrim should go with subdued soul to Ramahrada.

sn: तत्र रामेण राजेन्द्र तरसा दीप्ततेजसा। क्षत्रमुत्साद्य वीरेण ह्रदाः पञ्च निवेशिताः॥
en: O king of kings, the greatly effulgent and heroic Rama, exterminating the Kastrayas dug five lakes.

sn: पूरयित्वा नरव्याघ्र रुधिरेणेति विश्रुतम्। पितरस्तर्पिताः सर्वे तथैव प्रपितामहाः॥
en: foremost of men, we have heard that he filled them with their blood. He offered that (blood) as oblations to all his sires and grandsires.

sn: ततस्ते पितर: प्रीता राममूचुर्नराधिप।
en: O ruler of men, thereupon the Pitris, being passed with him, thus spoke to Rama.

sn: पितर ऊचुः राम राम महाभाग प्रीताः स्म तव भार्गव॥ अनया पितृभक्त्या च विक्रमेण च ते विभो। वरं वृणीष्व भद्रं ते किमिच्छसि महाद्युते॥
en: The Pitris said: O greatly exalted Rama, O Rama, O descendant of Bhrigu, we are pleased. O lord, with your filial piety and with your great prowess. O greatly effulgent one, be blessed. Ask the boon you desire to get.

sn: पुलस्त्य उवाच एवमुक्तः स राजेन्द्र रामः प्रहरतां वरः। अब्रवीत् प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यं पितॄन् स गगने स्थितान्॥ भवन्तो यदि मे प्रीता यद्यनुचाह्यता मयि। पितृप्रसादमिच्छेयं तप आप्यायनं पुनः॥
en: Pulastya said : O king, having been thus addressed, that foremost of smiters, Rama, thus spoke with joined hands to the Pitris who were in the sky. If you are pleased with me and if I have deserved your favour, I desire to get this favour from the Pitris that I may again derive pleasure in asceticism.

sn: यच्च रोषाभिभूतेन क्षत्रमुत्सादितं मया। ततश्च पापान्मुच्येयं युष्माकं तेजसाप्यहम्॥ ह्रदाश्च तीर्थभूता मे भवेयुर्भुवि विश्रुताः।
en: With your power let the sin I have incurred by exterminating the Kashtriyas from wrath be all destroyed. Let also my these lakes becomes Tirthas, celebrated all over the earth.

sn: एतच्छ्रुत्वा शुभं वाक्यं रामस्य पितरस्तदा॥ प्रत्यूचुः परमप्रीता राम हर्षसमन्विताः। तपस्ते वर्धतां भूयः पितृभक्त्या विशेषतः॥
en: Having heard these blessed words of Rama, the Pitris. Becoming highly pleased and filled with joy, thus replied to Rama, “Let your asceticism increase for your great filial piety.

sn: यच्च रोषाभिभूतेन क्षत्रमुत्सादितं त्वया। ततश्च पापान्मुक्तस्त्वं पतितास्ते स्वकर्मभिः॥
en: You have exterminated the Kashtriyas from wrath, but you are already freed from that sin, for they have fallen for their own (mis) deeds.

sn: ह्रदाश्च तव तीर्थत्वं गमिष्यन्ति न संशयः। ह्रदेषु तेषु यः स्नात्वा पितृन् संतर्पयिष्यति॥ पितरस्तस्य वै प्रीता दास्यन्ति भुवि दुर्लभम्। ईप्सितं च मन:कामं स्वर्गलोकं च शाश्वतम्॥
en: Without the least doubt your these lakes w. be Tirthas, he who will bathe in these lakes and offer oblations to the Pitris. Will make his Pitris pleased with him. They will grant him the desired objects so difficult to be obtained in this world and lead him to the celestials region."

sn: एवं दत्त्वा वरान् राजन् रामस्य पितरस्तदा। आमन्त्र्य भार्गवं प्रीत्या तत्रैवान्तर्हितास्ततः॥
en: O king, having granted this boon, the Pitris saluted Rama, the descendant of Bhrigu and disappeared then and there.

sn: एवं रामहदाः पुण्या भार्गवस्य महात्मनः। स्नात्वा हृदेषु रामस्य ब्रह्मचारी शुभवतः॥ राममभ्यर्च्य राजेन्द्र लभेद् बहुसुवर्णकम्। वंशमूलकमासाद्य तीर्थसेवी कुरूद्वह॥
en: It was thus the lakes of the illustrious descendant of Bhrigu became sacred. Leading the life of a Brahmachari and observing sacred vows, if one bathes in these lakes of Rama and worships Rama, O king of kings, he obtains the fruits of giving away much wealth. O perpetuator of the Kuru race, going to Vanshamulaka, the pilgrim.

sn: स्ववंशमुद्धरेद् राजन् स्नात्वा वै वंशमूलके। कायशोधनमासाद्य तीर्थं भरतसत्तम॥ शरीरशुद्धिः स्नातस्य तस्मिंस्तीर्थे न संशयः। शुद्धदेहच संयाति शुभाँल्लोकाननुत्तमान्॥
en: Saves his own race by bathing in Vanshamulaka. O best of the Bharata race, going to Kayashodhana and bathing in that Tirtha one purifies his body without the least doubt. Acquiring a purified body, one goes to the excellent regions of bliss.

sn: ततो गच्छेतधर्मज्ञ तीर्थं त्रैलोक्यविश्रुतम्। लोका यत्रोद्धताः पूर्वं विष्णुना प्रभविष्णुना॥ लोकोद्धारं समासाद्य तीर्थं त्रैलोक्यपूजितम्। स्नात्वा तीर्थवरे राजैल्लोकानुद्धरते स्वकान्॥
en: O virtuous man, one should then go to that Tirtha, called Lokodvara which is celebrated all over the three worlds and where greatly effulgent Vishnu had formerly created the world. O king, going to the Lokodvara Tirtha, celebrated over the three worlds and bathing in that foremost of Tirthas one acquires many worlds for himself.

sn: श्रीतीर्थं च समामाद्य स्नात्वा नियतमानसः। अर्चयित्वा पितॄन् देवान् विन्दते श्रियमुत्तमाम्॥
en: Going with subdued mind to the Tirtha called Sri and bathing in it and worshipping the Pitris and the celestials there, one obtains great affluence.

sn: कपिलातीर्थमासाद्य ब्रह्मचारी समाहितः। तत्र स्नात्वार्चयित्वा च पितृन् स्वान् दैवतान्यपि॥ कपिलानां सहस्रस्य फलं विन्दति मानवः।
en: Leading the life of a Brahmachari and having one's soul subdued, he who goes to the Tirtha, called Kapila and bathes in it and worships the Pitris and the celestials, that man, obtains the fruit of giving away one thousand Kapila kine.

sn: सूर्यतीर्थं समासाद्य स्नात्वा नियमानसः॥ अर्चयित्वा पितॄन् देवानुपवासपरायणः। अग्निष्टोममवाप्नोति सूर्यलोकं च गच्छति॥
en: Going with subdued soul to the Tirtha, called Surya and bathing in it. And worshipping the Pitris and the celestials with fasting, one obtains the fruits of Agnishtoma and goes to he region of Surya.

sn: गवां भवनमासाद्य तीर्थसेवी यथाक्रमम्। तत्राभिषेकं कुर्वाणो गोसहस्रफलं लभेत्॥
en: Going in due order to the Gobhavana and bathing in it, the pilgrim obtains the fruits of giving away one thousand kine.

sn: शङ्खिनीतीर्थमासाद्य तीर्थसेवी कुरूद्वह। देव्यास्तीर्थे नरः स्नात्वा लभते रूपमुत्तमम्॥
en: O perpetuator of the Kuru race, going to Tirth called Shankhini and bathing in the Divitirtha man acquires great prowess.

sn: ततो गच्छेत राजेन्द्र द्वारपालमरन्तुकम्। तच्च तीर्थं सरस्वत्यां यक्षेन्द्रस्य महात्मनः॥ तत्र स्नात्वा नरो राजन्नग्निष्टोमफलं लभेत्।
en: O king of kings, one should then go to the gatc-keeper, Arantuka, which is in the Sarasvati and which belongs to the illustrious chief of the Yakshas (Kubera). O king, bathing one in it, a man obtains the fruits of Agnishtoma (sacrifice).

sn: ततो गच्छेत राजेन्द्र ब्रह्मावर्तं नरोत्तमः॥ ब्रह्मावर्ते नरः स्नात्वा ब्रह्मलोकमवाप्नुयात्।
en: O virtuous king, one should then go to Brahmavarta. Bathing in the Brahmavarta a man, obtains the regions of Brahma.

sn: ततो गच्छेत राजेन्द्र सुतीर्थकमनुत्तमम्॥ तत्र संनिहिता नित्यं पितरो दैवतैः सह। तत्राभिषेकं कुर्वीत पितृदेवार्चने रतः॥ अश्वमेधमवाप्नोति पितृलोकं च गच्छति।
en: O king of kings, one should then go to the excellent Tirthas called Su. There the Pitris are always present with the celestials. Bathing there and worshipping the Pitris and the celestials, obtains thc fruits of Ashvamedha (sacrifice) and goes to the region of Brahma.

sn: ततोऽम्बुमत्यांधर्मज्ञ सुतीर्थकमनुत्तमम्॥
en: O virtuous man, it is therefore that Sutirtha situated in Ambumati is so very excellent.

sn: काशीश्वरस्य तीर्थेषु स्नात्वा भरतसत्तम। सर्वव्याधिविनिर्मुक्तो ब्रह्मलोके महीयते॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, bathing in the Tirtha of Kashishvara, one is freed from all diseases; and he is adored in the region of Brahma.

sn: मातृतीर्थं च तत्रैव यत्र स्नातस्य भारत। प्रजा विवर्धते राजन्नतन्वीं श्रियमश्नुते॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, O king, there is also Matri Tirtha, bathing in which one obtains large progeny and great prosperity.

sn: ततः सीतवनं गच्छेन्नियतो नियताशनः। तीर्थं तत्र महाराज महदन्यत्र दुर्लभम्॥
en: O great king, one should then go with regulated diet and subdued soul to Sitavana. There is one thing there which is not to be seen anywhere else.

sn: पुनाति गमनादेव दृष्टमेकं नराधिप। केशानभ्युक्ष्य वै तस्मिन् पूतो भवति भारत॥
en: O ruler of men, man obtains virtue by only going there. O descendant of Bharata, shaving there one's hair, a man becomes sanctified.

sn: तीर्थं तत्र महाराज श्वाविल्लोमापहं स्मृतम्। यत्र विप्रा नरव्याघ्र विद्वांसस्तीर्थतत्पराः॥ प्रीतिं गच्छन्ति परमां स्नात्वा भरतसत्तम। वाविल्लोमापनयने तीर्थे भरतसत्तम॥ प्राणायामैर्निर्हरन्ति स्वलोमानि द्विजोत्तमाः। पूतात्मानश्च राजेन्द्र प्रयान्ति परमां गतिम्॥
en: O great king, in that spot there is a Tirtha called Shvaillomapaha. O foremost of men, learned Brahmanas who always visit Tirthas. Get great pleasure by bathing in it. O best of the Bharata race, shaving their heads at the Shvaillomapaha Tirtha, the excellent Brahmanas acquire holiness by Pranayama; and becoming pure-souled they obtain the highest state.

sn: दशाश्वमेधिकं चैव तस्मिंस्तीर्थे महीपते। तत्र स्नात्वा नरव्याघ्र गच्छेत परमां गतिम्॥
en: O ruler of earth, O foremost of men, there is in that spot another Tirtha called Dashashvamedha. Bathing in it, one obtains the highest state.

sn: ततो गच्छेत राजेन्द्र मानुषं लोकविश्रुतम्। यत्र कृष्णमृगा राजन् व्याधेन शरपीडितः॥ विगाह्य तस्मिन् सरसि मानुषत्वमुपागताः। तस्पिस्तीर्थे नरः स्नात्वा ब्रह्मचारी समाहितः॥
en: O king of kings, one should then go to Manusha, celebrated all over the world, O king, where some black deer, pierced by the arrows of a hunter. Jumped into its water and were transformed into human beings. Bathing in that Tirtha with leading the life of a Brahmachari and having one's soul subdued.

sn: सर्वपापविशुद्धात्मा स्वर्गलोके महीयते। मानुषस्य तु पूर्वेण क्रोशमात्रे महीपते॥ आपगा नाम विख्याता नदी सिद्धनिषेविता। श्यामाकं भोजने तत्र यः प्रयच्छन्ति मानवः॥ देवान् पितृन् समुद्दिश्य तस्यधर्मफलं महत्। एकस्मिन् भोजिते विप्रे कोटिर्भवति भोजिता॥
en: One is freed from all sins; and becoming pure souled he is adored in the region of Brahma. O ruler of men, in the east of Manusha, only a kosa from it. There is a celebrated river named Apaga which is ever frequented by the Siddhas. The man who offers there Shyamaka food. To the celestials and the Pitris secures great virtuous merit. One Brahmana svd there is equal to million of Brahmanas fed.

sn: तत्र स्नात्वार्चयित्वा च पितॄन् वै दैवतानि च। उषित्वा रजनीमेकामग्निष्टोमफलं लभेत्॥
en: Bathing in it and worshipping the Pitris and the celestials and living there only for a night, one obtains the fruit of Agnishtoma (sacrifice).

sn: ततो गच्छेत राजेन्द्र ब्रह्मणः स्थानमुत्तमम्। ब्रह्मोदुम्बरमित्येव प्रकाशं भुवि भारत॥
en: O king of kings, O descendant of Bharata, one should then go to that excellent region of Brahma which is celebrated on earth by the name of Brahmodumbara.

sn: तत्र सप्तर्षिकुण्डेषु स्नातस्य नरपुङ्गव। केदारे चैव राजेन्द्र कपिलस्य महात्मनः॥ ब्रह्माणमधिगम्याथ शुचिः प्रयतमानसः। सर्वपापविशुद्धात्मा ब्रह्मलोकं प्रपद्यते॥ कपिलस्य च केदारं समासाद्य सुदुर्लभम्। अन्तर्धानमवाप्नोति तपसा दग्धकिल्बिषः॥
en: O foremost of men, bathing in the lakes of the seven Rishis and also in the Kedara of the high-souled Kapila. With pure mind and subdued soul and going to Brahma, one's all sins are destroyed; and his soul being made pure, he goes to the region of Brahma. Going the inaccessible (Tirtha) Kedara of Kapisthala and having his sins all burnt by asceticism, obtains the power of disappearance at will.

sn: ततो गच्छेत राजेन्द्र सरकं लोकविश्रुतम्। कृष्णपक्षे चतुर्दश्यामभिगम्य वृषध्वजम्॥ लभेत सर्वकामान् हि स्वर्गलोकं च गच्छति।
en: O king of kings, one should then go to Saraka, celebrated over the three worlds. Seeing there Vrishadhvaja (Mahadeva) on the fourteenth day of the black fortnight. One obtains all that he desires and goes to the celestials region. to one

sn: तिस्रः कोट्यस्तु तीर्थानां सरके कुरुनन्दन॥
en: O descendant of Kuru, thirty millions of Tirthas are in Saraka.

sn: रुद्रकोट्यां तथा कूपे ह्रदेषु च महीपते। इलास्पदं च तत्रैव तीर्थं भरतसत्तम॥ तत्र स्नात्वार्चयित्वा च दैवतानि पितृनथ। न दुर्गतिमवाप्नोति वाजपेयं च विन्दति॥
en: And in Rudrakoti and also in the wells and lakes that are there. O ruler of earth, O best of the Bharata race, there is also the Tirtha called Ilaspada. Bathing in it and worshipping there the Pitris and the celestials, one does not meet with any calamity. He obtains the fruits of Vajapeya (sacrifice).

sn: किंदाने च नरः स्नात्वा किंजप्ये च महीपते। अप्रमेयमवाणोति दानं जप्यं च भारत॥
en: O ruler of earth, O descendant of Bharata, bathing in Kindana and Kinjapya, one obtains the fruits of measureless gifts and of infinite recitation of prayers.

sn: कलश्यां वार्युपस्पृश्य श्रद्दधानो जितेन्द्रियः। अग्निष्टोमस्य यज्ञस्य फलं प्राप्नोति मानवः॥
en: Bathing in Kalasa with devotion and with one's passions subdued, a man obtains the fruits of Agnishtoma sacrifice.

sn: सरकस्य तु पूर्वेण नारदस्य महात्मनः। तीर्थं कुरुकुलश्रेष्ठ अम्बाजन्मेति विश्रुतम्॥
en: O best of the Kurus, in the east of Saraka is the sacred Tirtha of the illustrious Narada, known by the name of Ambajanma.

sn: तत्र तीर्थे नरः स्नात्वा प्राणानुत्सृज्य भारत। नारदेनाभ्यनुज्ञातो लोकान् प्राप्नोत्यनुत्तमान्॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, a man, bathing in that Tirtha, obtains excellent regions (after death) at the command of Narada.

sn: शुक्लपक्षे दशम्यां च पुण्डीरकं समाविशेत्। तत्र स्नात्वा नरो राजन् पुण्डरीकफलं लभेत्॥
en: O king, one should go on the tenth of the white fortnight to Pundarika. Bathing there, a man obtains the fruits of Pundarika sacrifice.

sn: ततस्त्रिविष्टपं गच्छेत् त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतम्। तत्र वैतरणी पुण्या नदी पापप्रणाशिनी॥
en: One should then go to Trivistapa, celebrated all over the three worlds. There flows the sacred and the sin-destroying Vaitarani river.

sn: तत्र स्नात्वार्चयित्वा च शूलपाणिं वृषध्वजम्। सर्वपापविशुद्धात्मा गच्छेत परमां गतिम्॥
en: Bathing in it and worshipping there the wielder of trident, Vrishadhvaja (Shiva), one obtains the highest state, all his sins being destroyed and his soul being purified.

sn: ततो गच्छेत राजेन्द्र फलकीवनमुत्तमम्। तत्र देवाः सदा राजन् फलकीवनमाश्रिताः॥ तपश्चरन्ति विपुलं बहु वर्षसहस्रकम्। दृषद्वत्यां नरः स्नात्वा तर्पयित्वा च देवताः॥ अग्निष्टोमातिरात्राभ्यां फलं विन्दति भारत। तीर्थे च सर्वदेवानां स्नात्वा भरतसत्तम॥ गोसहस्रस्य राजेन्द्र फलं विन्दति मानवः। पाणिखाते नरः स्नात्वा तर्पयित्वा च देवताः॥ अग्निष्टोमातिरात्राभ्यां फलं विन्दति भारत। राजसूयमवाप्नोति ऋषिलोकं च विन्दति॥
en: O king of kings, one should then go to the excellent Tirtha of Falaki. O king, there the celestials are always present in Falakivana. And they undergo there great asceticism for many years together. Bathing then in the Drishadvati and worshipping the celestials, a man obtains fruits superior to those of both the Agnishtoma and Atiratha (sacrifices). O descendant of Bharata, bathing in the Tirtha called Sarvadeva a man obtains the fruits of giving away one thousand kine. O king of kings, Bathing in the Panikhata and worshipping there the celestials, a mano descendant of Bharata, obtains fruits superior to those of Agnishtoma and Atiratha. He also obtains the fruits of Rajasuya and goes to the region of the Rishis.

sn: ततो गच्छेत राजेन्द्र मिश्रकं तीर्थमुत्तमम्। तत्र तीर्थानि राजेन्द्र मिश्रितानि महात्मना॥ व्यासेन नृपशार्दूल द्विजार्थमिति नः श्रुतम्। सर्वतीर्थेषु स स्नाति मिश्रके स्नाति यो नरः॥
en: virtuous man, one should then go to the excellent Tirtha, called Mishraka. O king of kings, in that Tirtha of the illustrious Mishrita. It has been heard by us that the Vyasa for the sake of the Brahmans mixed up all the Tirthas. The man who bathes in Mishraka bathes in all the Tirthas.

sn: ततो व्यासवनं गच्छेत्रियतो नियताशनः। मनोजवे नरः स्नात्वा गोसहस्रफलं लभेत्॥
en: One should then go with regulated diet and subdued soul to Vyasavana. Bathing there in the Mancjava one obtains the fruits of giving away one thousand kine.

sn: गत्वा मधुवटीं चैव देव्यास्तीर्थे नरः शुचिः। तत्र स्नात्वार्चयित्वा च पितॄन् देवांश्च पूरुषः॥ स देव्या समनुज्ञातो गोसहस्रफलं लभेत्।
en: Going to the Devi Tirtha in Madhuvati, the man who bathes with purity and worships the Pitris and the celestials. Obtains at the command of the celestials the fruit of giving away one thousand kine.

sn: कौशिक्याः संगमे यस्तु दृषद्वत्याश्च भारत॥ स्नाति वै नियताहारः सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते।
en: O descendant of Bharata, he who at the confluence of the Kaushiki and the Drishadvati bathes with regulated diet is freed from all sins.
