sn: प्रयागं जघनस्थानमुपस्थमृषयो विदुः। प्रयागं सप्रतिष्ठानं कम्बलाश्वतरौ तथा॥ तीर्थं भोगवती चैव वेदिरेषा प्रजापतेः। तत्र वेदाश्च यज्ञाश्च मूर्तिमन्तो युधिष्ठिर॥ प्रजापतिमुपासन्ते ऋषयश्च तपोधनाः। यजन्ते क्रतुभिर्देवास्तथा चक्रधरा नृपाः॥ तत: पुण्यतमं नाम त्रिषु लोकेषु भारत। प्रयागं सर्वतीर्थभ्यः प्रवदन्त्यधिकं विभो॥ गमनात् तस्य तीर्थस्य नामसंकीर्तनादपि। मृत्युकालभयाच्चापि नर: पापात् प्रमुच्यते॥
en: And Prayaga is known as the foremost point of that region. Prayaga, Sapratishanta, Kamvala, Asvatari and the Tirtha Bhogavati are the sacrificial altars of Prajapati (Brahma). O hero steady in war, the Vedas and the sacrifices in their embodied forms and also ascetic Rishis adore here Prajapati (Brahma). Here the celestials and the rulers of kingdoms perform their sacrifices. O descendant of Bharata, O lord, therefore Prayaga is the most sacred of all the Tirthas, in fact it is the foremost of all the Tirthas in the three worlds. Going to that Tirtha and singing its name and taking a little carth from it, one is cleansed of all his sins.

sn: तत्राभिषेकं यः कुर्यात् संगमे लोकविश्रुते। पुण्यं स फलमाप्नोति राजसूयाश्वमेधयोः॥
en: He who bathes in this celebrated confluence obtains all the merits of Ashvamedha and Rajasuya (sacrifices).

sn: एषा यजनभूमिर्हि देवानामभिसंस्कृता। तत्र दत्तं सूक्ष्ममपि महद् भवति भारत॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, this sacrificial place is worshipped by the celestials themselves. If a man gives away here only a little, it increases thousand-fold.

sn: न वेदवचनात् तात न लोकवचनादपि। मतिरुत्क्रमणीया ते प्रयागमरणं प्रति॥
en: O child, let not the texts of the Veda or the opinions of men dissuade your mind from the desire of dying at Prayaga.

sn: दश तीर्थसहस्राणि षष्टिः कोट्यस्तथापराः। येषां सांनिध्यमत्रैव कीर्तितं कुरुनन्दन॥ चतुर्विद्ये च यत् पुण्यं सत्यवादिषु चैव यत्। स्नात एव तदाप्नोति गङ्गायमुनसंगमे॥
en: O descendant of Kuru, the wise men say that six hundred millions and ten thousand Tirthas exist at Prayaga. Bathing in the confluence of the Ganges and the Yamuna, one obtains the merit of the four kinds of knowledge and the merits also of those that are truthful.

sn: तत्र भोगवती नाम वासुकेस्तीर्थमुत्तमम्। तत्राभिषेकं यः कुर्यात् सोऽश्वमेधफलं लभेत्॥
en: There is an excellent Tirtha of Vasuki, called Bhogavati. He who bathes in it obtains the fruits of Ashvamedha.

sn: तत्र हंसप्रपतनं तीर्थं त्रैलोक्यविश्रुतम्। दशाश्वमेधिकं चैव गङ्गायां कुरुनन्दन॥
en: O descendant of Kuru, there in the Ganges is a Tirtha, celebrated all over the three worlds, called Hansaprapatana which gives one the fruits of ten sacrifices.

sn: कुरुक्षेत्रसमा गङ्गा यत्र तत्रावगाहिता। विशेषो वै कनखले प्रयागे परमं महत्॥
en: Wherever a man bathes in the Ganges he obtains the fruits of going to Kurukshetra, except the place named Kanakhala while the merit attaching to Prayaga is the greatest.

sn: यद्यकार्यशतं कृत्वा कृतं गङ्गाभिषेचनम्। सर्वं तत् तस्य गङ्गाम्भो दहत्यग्निरिवेन्धनम्॥ सर्वं कृतयुगे पुण्यं त्रेतायां पुष्करं स्मृतम्। द्वापरेऽपि कुरुक्षेत्रं गङ्गा कलियुगे स्मृता॥ पुष्करे तु तपस्तप्येद् दानं दद्यान्महालये। मलये त्वग्निमारोहेद् भृगुतुङ्गे त्वनाशनम्॥
en: Having committed one hundred sins he who bathes in the Ganges has all his sins burnt off by the waters of the Ganges) as fuel is consumed by fire. It has been said that in the Satya Yuga all the Tirthas were sacred. In the Treta Pushkara alone was sacred. In the Dvapara Kurukshetra was sacred. In the Kaliyuga the Ganges alone is sacred. In Pushkara, one should practices asceticism, in Mahalaya one should give away (in charity); in the Malaya (mountains) one should ascend the funeral pyre, in Bhrigutunga, one should give up his body by fasting.

sn: पुष्करे तु कुरुक्षेत्रे गङ्गायां मध्यमेषु या स्नात्वा तारयते जन्तुः सप्तसप्तावरांस्तथा॥
en: Bathing in Pushkara in Kurukshetra and in the Ganges and in the confluence of the Ganges and the Yamuna), one saves ten generations of his race upwards and downwards.

sn: पुनाति कीर्तिता पापं दृष्टा भद्रं प्रयच्छति। अवगाढा च पीता च पुनात्यासप्तमं कुलम्॥
en: He who recites the name (of the Ganges) is purified. He who beholdsher obtains prosperity. He who bathes in her and drinks her water saves seven generations of his race upwards and downwards.

sn: यावदस्थि मनुष्यस्य गङ्गाया स्पृशते जलम्। तावत् स पुरुषो राजन् स्वर्गलोके महीयते॥
en: O king, so long a man's bones lie in the waters of the Ganges, so long that man is adored in the celestials region,

sn: यथा पुण्यानि तीर्थानि पुण्यान्यायतनानि च। उपास्य पुण्यं लब्ध्वा च भवत्यमरलोकभाक्॥
en: As is the man who earns virtues by visiting the Tirthas and by drinking their sacred water and thus by earning virtue adored in the celestials region.

sn: न गङ्गासदृशं तीर्थं न देवः केशवात् परः। ब्राह्मणेभ्यः परं नास्ति एवमाह पितामहः॥
en: There is no Tirtha like the Ganges, there is no god like Keshava (Krishna), there is none superior to Brahmanas thus said the Grandsire (Brahma).

sn: यत्र गङ्गा महाराज स देशस्तत् तपोवनम्। सिद्धिक्षेत्रं च तज्ज्ञेयं गङ्गातीरसमाश्रितम्॥
en: O great king, where there is the Ganges and the place on the banks of the Ganges, is the wood fit for asceticism. The region through which the Ganges flows is a favourite hermitage.

sn: इदं सत्यं द्विजातीनां साधूनामात्मजस्य च। सुहृदां च जपेत् कर्णे शिष्यस्यानुगतस्य च॥
en: This truth (about Tirthas) should be recited to the ears of only Brahmanas, of the pious men, one's of own sons, friends, disciples and dependants.

sn: इदंधन्यमिदं मेध्यमिदं स्वर्ग्यमनुत्तमम्। इदं पुण्यमिदं रम्यं पावनधर्म्यमुत्तमम्॥
en: It (this narrative of Tirthas) is unrivalled, it is blessed, it is holy and it leads men to heaven, it is holy, entertaining, sanctifying and it is productive of high merit.

sn: महर्षीणामिदं गुह्यं सर्वपापप्रमोचनम्। अधीत्य द्विजमध्ये च निर्मलः स्वर्गमाप्नुयात्॥
en: It is a mystery of the great Rishis, it cleanses all sins. By reciting this holy history in the midst of Brahmanas, one goes to heaven.

sn: श्रीमत् स्वयँ तथा पुण्यं सपत्नशमनं शिवम्। मेधाजननमवयं वै तीर्थवंशानुकीर्तनम्॥
en: It is auspicious, heaven-giving, sacred, it is ever blessed and it destroys one's cnemies. This narrative of Tirtha is the foremost of all narratives and it increases one's intellect.

sn: अपुत्रो लभते पुत्रमधनोधनमाप्नुयात्। महीं विजयते राजा वैश्योधनमवाप्नुयात्॥
en: (By reciting it) the sonless obtain sons, the poor obtain wealth, the king conquers the world and the Vaisyas obtain affluence.

sn: शूद्रोः यथेप्सितान् कामान् ब्राह्मणः पारगः पठन्। यश्चेदं शृणुयान्नित्यं तीर्थपुण्यं नरः शुचिः॥ जाती: स स्मरते बह्वी कपृष्ठे च मोदते। गम्यान्यपि च तीर्थानि कीर्तितान्यगमानि च॥
en: The Shudra cbtains all his desires and the Brahmana crosses the ocean (of world). The man who daily hears it with purity. Becomes abic to remember the incidents of his former births and rejoices in heaven. Some of the Tirthas that have been narrated here are accessible and some inaccessible.

sn: मनसा तानि गच्छेत सर्वतीर्थसमीक्षया। एतानि वसुभिः साध्यैरादित्यैर्मरुदश्विभिः॥
en: But he who is eagerly desirous to see them should go to them even in his mind (with the help of imagination). The Vasus, the Sadhyas, the Adityas, the Marutas, the Ashvins.

sn: ऋषिभिर्देवकल्पैश्च स्नातानि सुकृतैषिभिः। एवं त्वमपि कौरव्य विधिनानेन सुव्रत॥
en: And the Rishis equal to the celestials all bathed in them by performing good deeds. O descendant of Kuru, O vow observing hero, you too, acting according to the rites.

sn: व्रज तीर्थानि नियतः पुण्यं पुण्येन वर्धयन्। भावितैः करणैः पूर्वमास्तिक्याच्छ्रुतिदर्शनात्॥ प्राप्यन्ते तानि तीर्थानि सद्भिः शास्त्रानुदर्शिभिः। नाव्रती नाकृतात्मा च नाशुचिर्न च तस्करः॥ स्नाति तीर्थेषु कौरव्य न च वक्रमतिर्नरः। त्वया तु सम्यग्वृत्तेन नित्यंधर्मार्थदर्शिना॥
en: Should with subdued senses, visit these Tirthas by increasing your virtue. The man of honesty and those who understand the Shastras are able to visit these Tirthas by reason of their purified soul, by their belief in Godhead and by their study of the Vedas. He who does not observe vows, whose soul is not under control, who is impure, who is a thief and who is crooked-minded cannot bathe in these Tirthas. O descendant of Kuru, you are ever observant of virtue and you are of pure character.

sn: पिता पितामहश्चैव सर्वे च प्रपितामहाः। पितामहपुरोगाश्च देवाः सर्षिगणा नृप॥ तवधर्मेणधर्मज्ञ नित्यमेवाभितोषिताः। अवाप्स्यसि त्वं लोकान् वै वसूनां वासवोपम्। कीर्तिं च महतीं भीष्म प्राप्स्यसे भुवि शाश्वतीम्।१११।।
en: O king, you have always gratified by your virtue your father, your grandfather, your great grandfather and also the celestials with Grandsire (Brahma) at their head and also the Rishis, O virtuous man, O Vasava-like hero, O Bhishma, you will attain to the region of the Vasus and you will acquire eternal fame on earth.

sn: नारद उवाच एवमुक्त्वाभ्यनुज्ञाय पुलस्त्यो भगवानृषिः। प्रीतः प्रीतेन मनसा तत्रैवान्तरधीयत॥
en: Narada said: Having thus spoken with cheerfulness and bidding farewell to him (Bhishma) the exalted Rishi Pulastya with his mind well pleased, disappeared then and there.

sn: भीष्मश्च कुरुशार्दूल शास्त्रतत्त्वार्थदर्शिवान्। पुलस्त्यवचनाच्चैव पृथिवीं परिचक्रमे॥
en: O foremost of the Kurus, Bhishma also who well understood the true import of the Shastras travelled over the world at the command of Pulastya.

sn: एवमेषा महाभाग प्रतिष्ठाने प्रतिष्ठिता। तीर्थयात्रा महापुण्या सर्वपापप्रमोचनी॥
en: O greatly exalted one, he (Bhishma) ended here (at Prayaga) his highly meritorious visits to the Tirthas which are ever capable of destroying all sins.

sn: अनेन विधिना यस्तु पृथिवीं संचरिष्यति। अश्वमेधशतस्याङ्वयं फलं प्रेत्य स भोक्ष्यति॥
en: He who travels over the earth according to these rules obtains the great fruits of one hundred horse-sacrifices and finally obtains salvation.

sn: ततश्चाष्टगुणं पार्थ प्राप्स्यसेधर्ममुत्तमम्। भीष्मः कुरूणां प्रवरो यथापूर्वमवाप्तवान्॥
en: O son of Pritha, you will get eight times superior merit to those that the foremost of the Kurus, Bhima formerly obtained.

sn: नेता च त्वमृषीन् यस्मात् तेन तेऽष्टगुणं फलम्। रक्षोगणविकीर्णानि तीर्थान्येतानि भारत! न गतानि मनुष्येन्द्रस्त्वामृते कुरुनन्दन॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, as you will take all these Rishis to those Tirthas, your merit will be eight times greater. The Tirthas are infested with Rakshashas. O descendant of Kuru, none else except you can go there.

sn: इदं देवर्षिचरितं सर्वतीर्थाभिसंवृत्तम्। यः पठेत् कल्यमुत्थाय सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते॥
en: He who recites this narrative of all the Tirthas told by the celestials Rishi (Pulastya) by rising early in the morning is cleansed of all his sins.

sn: ऋषिमुख्याः सदा यत्र वाल्मीकिस्त्वथ कश्यपः। आत्रेयः कुण्डजठरो विश्वामित्रोऽथ गौतमः॥ असितो देवलश्चैव मार्कण्डेयोऽथ गालवः। भरद्वाजो वसिष्ठश्च मुनिरुद्दालकस्तथा॥ शौनकः सह पुत्रेण व्याश्च तपतां वरः। दुर्वासाश्च मुनिश्रेष्ठो जावालिश्च महातपाः॥ एते ऋषिवराः सर्वे त्वत्प्रतीक्षास्तपोधनाः। एभिः सह महाराज तीर्थान्येतान्यनुव्रज॥
en: There always dwell those foremost of Rishis, Valmiki and Kashyapa, Atrya, Kundayatra Vishvamitra, Gautama, Asita, Devala, Markandeya, Galava, Bharadvaja, Vasishtha, Uddalaka, Shaunaka with his son, that best of ascetics Vyasa, that foremost of Rishis Durvasa, the greatly ascetic Jabali, these foremost of Rishis are all waiting for of you. O great king, by visiting the Tirthas meet them.

sn: एष ते लोमशो नाम महर्षिरमितद्युतिः। समेष्यति महाराज तेन सार्धमनुव्रज॥
en: O great king, a greatly effulgent Rishi named Lomasha will come to you. Go with him (to the Tirthas).

sn: मयापि सहधर्मज्ञ तीर्थान्येतान्यनुक्रमात्। प्राप्स्यसे महतीं कीर्तिं यथा राजा महाभिषः।।१२४
en: You can go with me O virtuous man, to visit some of the Tirthas. You will by this obtain great fame as did king Mahavisha,

sn: यथा ययातिधर्मात्मा यथा राजा पुरूरवाः। तथा त्वं राजशार्दूल स्वेनधर्मेण शोभसे॥ यथा भगीरथो राजा यथा रामश्च विश्रुतः। तथा त्वं सर्वराजभ्यो भ्राजसे रश्मिवानिव॥
en: As did virtuous minded Yayati, as did king Pururava. O foremost of kings, you too will blaze forth with your own virtue; as did king Bhagiratha as did the celebrated Rama, so would you shine among kings like the Sun.

sn: यथा मनुर्यथेक्ष्वाकुर्यथा पूरुर्महायशाः। यथा वैन्यो महाराज तथा त्वमपि विश्रुतः॥ यथा च वृत्रहा सर्वान् सपत्नान् निर्दहन् पुरा। त्रैलोक्यं पालयामास देवराड् विगतज्वरः॥ तथा शत्रुक्षयं कृत्वा त्वं प्रजाः पालयिष्यसि। स्वधर्मविजितामुर्वी प्राप्य राजीवलोचन॥ ख्यातिं यास्यसिधर्मेण कार्तवीर्यार्जुनो यथा॥
en: As were Manu, Ikshvaku the greatly famous Puru and Vena so, O great king, would you become celebrated and as in the days of yore, the slayer of Vitra, the king of the celestials after, having burnt his enemies and having his mind freed from all anxieties ruled over the three worlds, so will you destroying your enemies rule over your subjects. O lotus-eyed hero, having conquered the earth according to the custom of your own order (Kshatriya), you will acquire renown by your own virtue as did Krittaviryarjuna.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमाश्वास्य राजानं नारदो भगवानृषिः। अनुज्ञाप्य महाराज तत्रैवान्तरधीयत॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having thus comforted the king, O great king, the exalted Rishi Narada, bidding firewell disappeared then and there.

sn: युधिष्ठिरोऽपिधर्मात्मा तमेवार्थं विचिन्तयन्। तीर्थयात्राश्रितं पुण्यमृषीणां प्रत्यवेदयत्॥
en: And the virtuous-minded Yudhishthira also, reflecting on the subject, recited before the Rishis the merits that are derived from visiting the Tirthas.

description: The colloquy between Dhaumya and Yudhishthira
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच भ्रातृणां मतमाज्ञाय नारदस्य चधीमतः। पितामहसमंधौम्यं प्राह राजा युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Vaishampayana said: Having ascertained the opinion of his brothers and that of the intelligent Narada, Yudhishthira thus spoke to the grandfather like Dhaumya.

description: The colloquy between Dhaumya and Yudhishthira
sn: मया स पुरुषव्याघ्रो जिष्णुः सत्यपराक्रमः। अस्त्रहेतोर्महाबाहुरमितात्मा विवासितः॥
en: Yudhishthira said : I have sent away for the acquisition of weapons, that foremost of men, that irresistibly powerful and the mighty-aried Vishnu (Arjuna) of immeasurable intelligence.

description: The colloquy between Dhaumya and Yudhishthira
sn: स हि वीरोऽनुरक्तश्च समर्थश्च तपोधनः। कृती च भृशमप्यस्त्रे वासुदेव इव प्रभुः॥
en: O ascetic, that hero (Arjuna) is devoted to me; he is able, he is well-skilled in weapons, he is like the lord Vasudeva (Krishna) himself.

description: The colloquy between Dhaumya and Yudhishthira
sn: अहं ह्येतावुभौ ब्रह्मन् कृष्णावरिविघातिनौ। अभिजानामि विक्रान्तौ तथा व्यासः प्रतापवान्॥
en: O Brahmana, I know them both, Krishna and Arjuna, those greatly powerful destroyers of enemies as much as the mighty Vyasa knows them.

description: The colloquy between Dhaumya and Yudhishthira
sn: त्रियुगौ पुण्डरीकाक्षौ वासुदेवधनंजयौ। नारदोऽपि तथा वेद योऽप्यशंसत् सदा मम॥
en: I know Vasudeva (Krishna) and Dhananjaya (Arjuna) to be none else than Vishnu himself of six attributes. Narada also knows them to be such, for he has always spoken so to me.

description: The colloquy between Dhaumya and Yudhishthira
sn: तथाहमपि जानामि नरनारायणावृषी। शक्तोऽयमित्यतो मत्वा मया स प्रेषितोऽर्जुनः॥ इन्द्रादनवरः शक्रं सुरसूनुः सुराधिपम्। द्रष्टुमस्त्राणि चादातुमिन्द्रादिति विवासितः॥ भीष्मद्रोणावतिरथौ कृपो द्रौणिश्च दुर्जयः। धृतराष्ट्रस्य पुत्रेण वृता युधि महारथाः॥
en: I also know them to be Rishis Nara and Narayana. Knowing him to be able, I have sent Arjuna away. He is not inferior to Indra and he is fully competent; I have sent him, that son of god (Arjuna) to see the king of the celestials and obtain weapons from him. Bhishma and Drona are mighty car-warriors; Kripa and the son of Drona are invincible. These great carwarriors have been installed by the son of Dhritarashtra (Duryodhana) in the command of his army.

description: The colloquy between Dhaumya and Yudhishthira
sn: सर्वे वेदविदः शूराः सर्वास्त्रविदुषस्तथा। योद्धुकामाश्च पार्थेन सततं ये महाबलाः। स च दिव्यास्त्रवित् कर्णः सूतपुत्रो महारथः॥
en: All of them are learned in the Vedas, all are heroic, all possess the knowledge of every weapon. Those greatly powerful heroes always eagerly desire to fight with Arjuna. Karna, the son of Suta, that great car-warrior, is well skilled in the celestials weapons.

description: The colloquy between Dhaumya and Yudhishthira
sn: योऽस्त्रवेगानिलबलः शरार्चिस्तलनिःस्वनः। रजोधूमोऽस्त्रसम्पातोधार्तराष्ट्रानिलोद्धतः॥ निसृष्ट इव कालेन युगान्ते ज्वलनो महान्। मम सैन्यमयं कक्षं प्रधक्ष्यति न संशयः॥
en: In respect of the impetus of his weapons, he possesses the strength of Vayu. He being a flame of fire, his arrows are its tongue. The dust (of the battle field) is its smoke and the slaps of his left hand cased in leather are the crackling of that flame. Urged by the son of Dhritarashtra, as the fire, urged by the wind, Karna, fix like the all consuming fire at the end of Yuga, sent forth by the destroyer death himself, will certainly consume my troops like straw.

description: The colloquy between Dhaumya and Yudhishthira
sn: तं स कृष्णानिलोद्भूतो दिव्यास्त्रज्वलनो महान्। श्वेतवाजिबलाकाभृद् गाण्डीवेन्द्रायुधोल्बणः॥ संरब्धः शरधाराभिः सुदीप्तं कर्णपावकम्। अर्जुनोदीरितो मेघः शमयिष्यति संयुगे॥ स साक्षादेव सर्वाणि शक्रात् परपुरंजयः। दिव्यान्यस्त्राणि बीभत्ससुस्ततश्च प्रतिपत्स्यते॥
en: Only that mass of clouds, namely Arjuna assisted by Krishna, who is like the powerful wind, his celestials weapons representing fearful lightning (in that cloud) his white steeds representing white cranes flying underneath (those clouds) his unbearable Gandiva representing the rainbow, (that Arjuna only) is capable of extinguishing that blazing flame, namely Karna, by means of the shower of his arrows shot with unflagging steadiness. That conqueror of hostile heroes, Vibhatsu (Arjuna) will certainly succeed in obtaining all the celestials weapons with their fullness and life from Indra.

description: The colloquy between Dhaumya and Yudhishthira
sn: अलं स तेषां सर्वेषामिति मेधीयते मतिः। नास्ति त्वतिकृतार्थानां रणेऽरीणां प्रतिक्रिया॥
en: In my opinion he alone is equal to them all; it is impossible otherwise to vanquish in battle all those foes who have all attained great success in all those purposes.

description: The colloquy between Dhaumya and Yudhishthira
sn: ते वयं पाण्डवं सर्वे गृहीतास्त्रमरिंदमम्। द्रष्टारो न हि बीभत्सुर्भारमुद्यम्य सीदति॥
en: We the Pandavas shall all see that chastiser of foes (Arjuna) fully equipped with celestials weapons, for Vibhatsu (Arjuna) (Arjuna) when undertaking a task never droops down under its weight.

description: The colloquy between Dhaumya and Yudhishthira
sn: वयं तु तमृते वीरं वनेऽस्मिन् द्विपदां वर। अवधानं न गच्छामः काम्यके सह कृष्णया।॥
en: In the absence of that hero, that foremost of men, we shall never have peace of mind with Krishna (Draupadi) in this forest of Kamyaka.

description: The colloquy between Dhaumya and Yudhishthira
sn: भवानन्यद् वनं साधु बह्वन्नं फलवच्छुचि। आख्यातु रामणीयं च सेवितं पुण्यकर्मभिः॥
en: Therefore, you, (O Rishis), speak of some other forest which is sacred and delightful and which abounds in fruits and food and which is inhabited by men of pious deeds,

description: The colloquy between Dhaumya and Yudhishthira
sn: यत्र कंचिद् वयं कालं वसन्तः सत्यविक्रमम्। प्रतीक्षामोऽर्जुनं वीरं वृष्टिकामा इवाम्बुदम्॥
en: And where we may pass some time waiting for the heroic and invincible Arjuna, as Chataka (bird) expects rain from the gathering clouds.

description: The colloquy between Dhaumya and Yudhishthira
sn: विविधानाश्रमान् कांश्चिद् द्विजातिभ्यः प्रतिश्रुतान्। सरांसि सरितश्चैव रमणीयांश्च पर्वतान्॥ आचक्ष्व न हि मे ब्रह्मन् रोचते तमृतेऽर्जुनम्। वनेऽस्मिन् काम्यके वासो गच्छामोऽन्यां दिशं प्रति॥
en: Tell us of various hermitages, lakes, rivers and beautiful mountains which are open to the twice-born. O Brahmana, in the absence of Arjuna, I do not like to live in this forest of Kamyaka We shall go somewhere else.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तान् सर्वानुत्सुकान् दृष्ट्वा पाण्डवान् दीनचेतसः। आश्वासयंस्तथाधौम्यो बृहस्पतिसमोऽब्रवीत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Seeing all the Pandavas afflicted with anxiety and depressed in spirits, Dhaumya who was like Brihaspati himself, thus comforted them and spoke to them.

sn: ब्राह्मणानुमतान् पुण्यानाश्रमान् भरतर्षभ। दिशस्तीर्थानि शैलांश्च शृणु मे वदतोऽनघ॥
en: Dhaumya said : O best of the Bharata race, O sinless one, listen to me as I mention some of the sacred hermitages, regions and Tirthas and mountains that are approved of by the Brahmanas.

sn: याञ्छ्रुत्वा गदतो राजन् विशोको भवितासि हो द्रौपद्या चानया सार्धं भ्रातृभिश्च नरेश्वर॥
en: O king, O ruler of men, hearing which you with Draupadi and your brothers will be freed from all grief.

sn: श्रवणाच्चैव तेषां त्वं पुण्यमाप्स्यसि पाण्डव। गत्वा शतगुणं चैव तेभ्य एव नरोत्तम॥
en: O son of Pandu, only hearing of them you will acquire great merit. But going to them, O foremost of men, you will get merit hundred times greater.

sn: पूर्वं प्राची दिशं राजन् राजर्षिगणसेविताम्। रम्यां ते कथयिष्यामि युधिष्ठिर यथास्मृति॥
en: O king, O Yudhishthira, I shall first speak of the charming eastern country ever frequented by the royal Rishis, as far as I recollect.

sn: तस्यां देवर्षिजुष्टायां नैमिषं नाम भारत। यत्र तीर्थानि देवानां पुण्यानि च पृथक् पृथक्॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, in that country there is a Tirtha ever frequented by the celestials Rishis called Naimisha. In that Tirtha there are several separate Tirthas sacred to the celestials.

sn: यत्र सा गोमती पुण्या रम्या देवर्षिसेविता। यज्ञभूमिश्च देवानां शामित्रं च विवस्वतः॥
en: Here flows the charming and sacred Gomati, ever adored by the celestials Rishis; here is the sacrificial ground of the celestials and the sacrificial stake of Vivasvata (sun).

sn: तस्यां गिरिवरः पुण्यो गयो राजर्षिसत्कृतः। शिवं ब्रह्मसरो यत्र सेवितं त्रिदशर्षिभिः॥
en: Here there is also that foremost of hills, the sacred Gaya, adored by the celestials Rishis, where there is the auspicious lake of Brahma, frequented by the celestials.

sn: यदर्थे पुरुषव्याघ्र कीर्तयन्ति पुरातनाः। एष्टव्या बहवः पुत्रा योकोऽपि गयां व्रजेत्॥ यजेत वाश्वमेधेन नीलं वा वृषमुत्सृजेत्। उत्तारयति संतत्या दशपूर्वान् दशावरान्॥
en: O foremost of men, it is for this reason the ancients say that inen should desire for many sons, so that one (son) at least among them may go to Gaya. May perform the horsesacrifice and may give away a Nila bull and thus deliver ten generations of his race upwards and downwards.

sn: महानदी च तत्रैव तथा गयशिरो नृप। यत्रासौ कीर्त्यते विगैरक्षय्यकरणो वटः॥
en: O king, there is a great river and there is also Gayashira and there is a banian tree called by the Brahmanas eternal.

sn: यत्र दत्तं पितृभ्योऽन्नमक्षय्यं भवति प्रभो। सा च पुण्यजला तत्र फल्गु म महानदी॥ बहुमूलफला चापि कौशिकी भरतर्षभ। विश्वामित्रोऽध्यगाद् यत्र ब्राह्मणत्वं तपोधनः॥
en: O lord, food offered here to the Pitris becomes everlasting. There flows the great river of sacred water called by the name of Falgu. O best of Bharata race, there is also in this place the Kaushika abounding in various fruits and roots where the great ascetic Vishvamitra attained to Brahmanhood.

sn: गङ्गा यत्र नदी पुण्या यस्यास्तीरे भगीरथः। अयजत् तत्र बहुभिः क्रतुभिर्भूरिदक्षिणैः॥
en: Here there is the river, the sacred Ganges; on the banks of Bhagirathi were performed many sacrifices with large Dakshinas (gift).

sn: पञ्चालेषु च कौरव्य कथयन्त्युत्पलावनम्। विश्वामित्रोऽयजद् यत्र पुत्रेण सह कौशिकः॥
en: O descendant of Kuru, they say that in the country of Panchala, there is a forest, called Utpala, in which the descendant of Kaushika, Vishvamitra with his son performed his sacrifices.

sn: यत्रानुवंशं भगवाञ्जामदग्न्यस्तथा जगौ। विश्वामित्रस्य तां दृष्ट्वा विभूतिमतिमानुषीम्॥
en: And where seeing the relics of Vishvamitra's superhuman power, Rama, the son of Jamadagni, recited the praises of his ancestor.

sn: कान्यकुब्जेऽपिबत् सोममिन्द्रेण सह कौशिकः। ततः क्षत्रादपाक्रामद् ब्राह्मणोऽस्मीति चाब्रवीत्॥
en: At Kanyakubja, the descendant of Kaushika (Vishvamitra) drank the Soma with Indra. Then abandoning Kshatriya order, he said "I am a Brahmana."

sn: पवित्रमृषिभिर्जुष्टं पुण्यं पावनमुत्तमम्। गङ्गायमुनयोर्वीर संगमं लोकविश्रुतम्॥
en: O hero, there is the sacred confluence of the Ganges and the Yamuna celebrated all over the world. Sacred and sin destroying it is ever adored by the holy Rishis.

sn: यत्रायजत भूतात्मा पूर्वमेव पितामहः। प्रयागमिति विख्यातं तस्माद् भरतसत्तम॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, in this place, the soul of creatures, the Grandsire (Brahma) formerly performed his sacrifices. It is hence called Prayaga.

sn: अगस्त्यस्य तु राजेन्द्र तत्राश्रमवरो नृप। तत् तथा तापसारण्यं तापसैरुपशोभितम्॥
en: O king of kings, O ruler, there is that foremost of hermitages of Agastya and also the forest called Tapasa graced by the presence of ascetics.

sn: हिरण्यबिन्दुः कथितो गिरौ कालञ्जरे महान्। आगस्त्यपर्वतो रम्यः पुण्यो गिरिवरः शिवः॥
en: There is also Hiranyabindu on the great Kalanjara mountain and also that foremost of hills Agastya which is charming sacred and auspicious.

sn: महेन्द्रो नाम कौरव्य भार्गवस्य महात्मनः। अयजत् तत्र कौन्तेय पूर्वमेव पितामहः॥
en: O descendant of Kuru, there is also the hill called Mahendra, sacred to the high-souled descendant of Bhrigu (Rama), where in the days of yore the Grandsire (Brahma) performed his sacrifices.

sn: यत्र भागीरथी पुण्या सरस्यासीद् युधिष्ठिर। यत्र सा ब्रह्मशालेति पुण्या ख्याता विशाम्पते॥ धूतपाप्मभिराकीर्णा पुण्यं तस्याश्च दर्शनम्।
en: O king, O Yudhishthira, in this place the Bhagirathi enters a lake, where there is also the sacred river known by the name of Brahmashala. The very sight of which produces great virtue and the banks of which are inhabited by men whose sins are destroyed.

sn: पवित्रो मङ्गलीयश्च ख्यातो लोके महात्मनः॥ केदारश्च मतङ्गस्य महानाश्रम उत्तमः। कुण्डोदः पर्वतो रम्यो बहुमूलफलोदकः॥ नैषधस्तृषितो यत्र जलं शर्म च लब्धवान्।
en: There is also the sacred, auspicious, celebrated, great and excellent hermitage of the high-souled Matanga, called Kedara. There is also the charming Kundoda mountain which abounds in many fruits, roots and water, where the king of the Nishadas (Nala) had satisfied his thirst and rested for a while.

sn: यत्र देववनं पुण्यं तापसैरुपशोभितम्॥ बाहुदा च नदी यत्र नन्दा च गिरिमूर्धनि।
en: In this place is also the charming Devavana, grand with the presence of ascetics. In this place also are rivers Bahuda and Nanda on the top of the mountains.

sn: तीर्थानि सरितः शैलाः पुण्यान्यायतनानि च॥ प्राच्यां दिशि महाराज कीर्तितानि मया तव। तिसृष्वन्यानि पुण्यानि दिक्षु तीर्थानि मे शृणु। सरितः पर्वतांश्चैव पुण्यान्यायतनानि च॥
en: O great king, I have described to you all the Tirthas, the rivers, the mountains and sacred spots. that are to be seen in the eastern country. Now hear of the sacred Tirthas, rivers, mountains and holy spots in the other three quarters.

sn: धौम्य उवाच दक्षिणस्यां तु पुण्यानि शृणु तीर्थानि भारत। विस्तरेण यथाबुद्धि कीर्त्यमानानि तानि वै॥
en: Dhaumya said: O descendant of Bharata, I shall describe to you in detail according to my knowledge the sacred Tirthas of the south. Listen to them.

sn: यस्यामाख्यायते पुण्या दिशि गोदावरी नदी। बहरामा बहुजला तापसाचरिता शिवा॥
en: In this quarter lies the sacred and auspicious river Godavari which is full of much water, which abounds in groves and which is frequented by the ascetics.

sn: वेणा भीमरथी चैव नद्यौ पापभयापहे। मृगद्विजसमाकीर्णे तापसालयभूषिते॥
en: In this place also are the rivers Vena and Bhimarathi, both capable of destroying sin and fear, both abounding in birds and deer and are graced with the abodes of ascetics.

sn: राजर्षेस्तस्य च सरिनृगस्य भरतर्षभ। रम्यतीर्था बहुजला पयोष्णी द्विजसेविता॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, in this region, is also the Tirtha of the royal ascetic, called Nriga, namely the river Payashini which is charming and which is full of water and which is frequented by Brahmanas.

sn: अपि चात्र महायोगी मार्कण्डेयो महायशाः। अनुवंश्यां जगौ गाथां नृगस्यधरणीपतेः॥ मृगस्य यजमानस्य प्रत्यक्षमिति नः श्रुतम्। अमाद्यदिन्द्रः सोमेन दक्षिणाभिर्द्विजातयः॥ पयोष्ण्यां यजमानस्य वाराहे तीर्थ उत्तमे। उद्धृतं भूतलस्थं वा वायुना समुदीरितम्। पयोष्ण्या हरते तोयं पापमामरणान्तिकम्॥
en: In this place the greatly illustrious and mighty Yogi, Markandeya sang the praises of the king Nriga and of his family. We have heard of the sacrificing king Nriga; we have heard also that which really took place when he was perforining a sacrifice in the excellent Tirtha called Varaha on the Payoshini. In that sacrifice Indra became intoxicated with Soma and the Brahmanas with the gifts which they received. The water of the Payaoshini, taken up (in vessel) or flowing along the ground or conveyed by the wind, can cleanse a person from whatever sins he may commit till the day of his death.

sn: स्वर्गादुत्तुङ्गममलं विषाणं यत्र शूलिनः। स्वमात्मविहितं दृष्ट्वा मर्त्यः शिवपुरं व्रजेत्॥
en: Higher than heaven itself, created and bestowed by the trident wielding deity (Shiva) there in that pure Tirtha, seeing the image of the deity one goes to the region of Shiva.

sn: गङ्गाद्याः सलिलोच्चयाः। पयोष्णी चैकतः पुण्या तीर्थेभ्यो हि मता मम॥ एकतः सरितः सर्वा
en: Placing on the one scale Ganga and all the other rivers with their waters and on the other, the Payoshini, the latter in my opinion would be superior in point of merit to all the Tirthas put together.

sn: माठरस्य वनं पुण्यं बहुमूलफलं शिवम्। यूपश्च भरतश्रेष्ठ वरुणस्रोतसे गिरौ॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, on the mountain, called Varuna Srotasa is the sacred and auspicious forest of Mathara abounding in fruits and roots and containing a sacrificial stake.

sn: प्रवेण्युत्तरमार्गे तु पुण्ये कण्वाश्रमे तथा। तापसानामरण्यानि कीर्तितानि यथाश्रुति॥
en: It is said that in the region north of it (Payoshini) and near the sacred hermitage of Kanva are many forests inhabited by the ascetics.

sn: वेदी शूर्पारके तात जगदग्नेर्महात्मनः। रम्या पाषाणतीर्था च पुनश्चन्द्रा च भारत॥
en: O child, O descendant of Bharata, in the charming Tirtha called Shurparaka, are the two sacrificial platforms of the high-souled son of Jamadagni called Pashana and Punashchandra.

sn: अशोकतीर्थं तत्रैव कौन्तेय बहुलाश्रयम्। अगस्त्यतीर्थं पाण्ड्येषु वारुणं च युधिष्ठिर॥ कुमार्यः कथिताः पुण्याः पाण्ड्येष्वेव नरर्षभ। ताम्रपर्णी तु कौन्तेय कीर्तयिष्यामि तां शृणु॥
en: O son of Kunti, in this place, is the Tirtha called Ashoka abounding in many hermitages. O Yudhishthira, in the Pandya country are the Tirthas called Agastya and Varuna. O foremost of men, O son of Kunti, among the Pandyas, there is the Tirtha called Kumari, Hear, I shall now describe Tamraparia.

sn: यत्र देवैस्तपस्तप्तं महदिच्छद्भिराश्रमे। गोकर्ण इति विख्यातस्त्रिषु लोकेषु भारत॥
en: In this hermitage, the celestials had undergone penances with the desire of obtaining salvation. In this region is also Gokarna celebrated over the three worlds.

sn: शीततोयो बहुजलः पुण्यस्तात शिव: शुभः। ह्रदः परमदुष्प्रापो मानुषैरकृतात्मभिः॥
en: O child, it is full of cool water, it is auspicious, sacred and capable of giving great merit. That lake is inaccessible to men of unpurified souls.

sn: तत्र वृक्षतृणाद्यैश्च सम्पन्नः फलमूलवान्। आश्रमोऽगस्त्यशिष्यस्य पुण्यो देवसमो गिरिः॥
en: Near to that Tirtha is the sacred hermitage of Agastya's disciple, the mountain Devasama which abounds in trees and grass and fruits and roots.

sn: वैदूर्यपर्वतस्तत्र श्रीमान् मणिमयः शिवः। अगस्त्यस्याश्रमश्चैव बहुमूलफलोदकः॥
en: There is also the Vaidurya mountain which is delightful and which abounds in gems and which is capable of bestowing great merit. There (on that mountain) is the hermitage of Agastya abounding in fruits, roots and water.

sn: सुराष्ट्रेष्वपि वक्ष्यामि पुण्यान्यायतनानि च। आश्रमान् सरितश्चैव सरांसि च नराधिप॥
en: O ruler of men, I shall now describe the sacred spots and hermitages, rivers and lakes, situated in the Saurashtra country.

sn: चमसोद्भेदनं विप्रास्तत्रापि कथयन्त्युत। प्रभासं चोदधौ तीर्थं त्रिदशानां युधिष्ठिर॥
en: O Yudhishthira, the Brahmanas say that on the sea-coast is the Chamasodbhedana and also Prabhasa, the Tirtha which is adored by the celestials.

sn: तत्र पिण्डारकं नाम तापसाचरितं शिवम्। उज्जयन्तश्च शिखरी क्षिप्रं सिद्धिकरो महान्॥
en: There is also the Tirtha called Pindarka, frequented by ascetics and capable of producing great merit. In this region is the great mountain Ujjyayanta which produces great success.

sn: तत्र देवर्षिवर्येण नारदेनानुकीर्तितः। पुराणः श्रूयते श्लोकस्तं निबोध युधिष्ठिर॥
en: O Yudhishthira, the celestials Rishi Narada of great intelligence has recited an ancient sloka about it. Listen to it.

sn: पुण्ये गिरौ सुराष्ट्रेषु मृगपक्षिनिषेविते। उज्जयन्ते स्म तप्ताङ्गो नाकपृष्ठे महीयते॥
en: He who performs austerities on the sacred hill, Ujjyayanta in Saurashtra, abounding in birds and beasts, is adored in the celestials region.

sn: पुण्या द्वारवती तत्र यत्रासौ मधुसूदनः। साक्षाद् देवः पुराणोऽसौ स हिधर्मः सनातनः॥
en: There is also Daravati which produces great merit and in which lives the slayer of Madhu who is the ancient one in embodied form and who is eternal virtue.

sn: ये च वेदविदो विप्रा ये चाध्यात्मविदो जनाः। ते वदन्ति महात्मानं कृष्णंधर्म सनातनम्॥
en: The Brahmanas, learned in the Vedas and persons verscd in the philosophy of the soul say that the illustrious Krishna is eternal virtue.

sn: पवित्राणां हि गोविन्दः पवित्रं परमुच्यते। पुण्यानामपि पुण्योऽसौ मङ्गलानां च मङ्गलम्। त्रैलोक्ये पुण्डरीकाक्षो देवदेवः सनातनः॥ अव्ययात्मा व्ययात्मा च क्षेत्रज्ञः परमेश्वरः। आस्ते हरिरचिन्त्यात्मा तत्रैव मधुसूदनः॥
en: Govinda is said to be the pure of all pure things, the righteous of the righteous and the auspicious of the auspicious. In all the three worlds, the lotus-eyed god of gods is eternal. He is the pure soul; he is the supreme Brahma and he is the lord of all. That slayer of Madhu of inconceivable soul lives there.

sn: धौम्य उवाच आनर्तेषु प्रतीच्यां वै कीर्तयिष्यामि ते दिशि। यानि तत्र पवित्राणि पुण्यान्यायतनानि च॥
en: Dhaumya said : I shall (now) describe to you those sacred spots capable of producing merit that lie on the west, in the country of the Anartas.

sn: प्रियङ्ग्वाम्रणोपेता वानीरफलमालिनी। प्रत्यक्स्रोता नदी पुण्या नर्मदा तत्र भारत॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, there flows in a westward course the sacred river Narmada, graced by Priyangu and adorned with mango trees and engar-landed by cranes.

sn: त्रैलोक्ये यानि तीर्थानि पुण्यान्यायतनानि च। सरिद्वनानि शैलेन्द्रा देवाश्च सपितामहाः॥ नर्मदायां कुरुश्रेष्ठ सह सिद्धर्षिचारणैः। स्नातुमायान्ति पुण्यौघैः सदा वारिषु भारत॥
en: All the Tirthas, sacred spots, rivers, forests and those best of the mountains that are in the three worlds, all the celestials with the Grandsire, with the Siddhas, the Rishis and the Charanas. O foremost of Kurus, O descendant of Bharata, always come to bathe in the sacred waters of the Narmada.

sn: निकेतः श्रूयते पुण्ये यत्र वश्रवसो मुनेः। जज्ञेधनपतिर्यत्र कुबेरो नरवाहनः॥
en: It has been heard by us that the sacred hermitage of Rishi Vishvasrava stood there and there the lord of wealth, Kubera, having man as his vehicle, was born.

sn: वैदूर्यशिखरो नाम पुण्यो गिरिवरः शिवः। नित्यपुष्पफलास्तत्र पादपा हरितच्छदाः॥
en: There is also that foremost of hills, the sacred and auspicious Vaidurya mountain, which is always abounding in trees that are green and that are always adorned with flowers and fruits.

sn: तस्य शैलस्य शिखरे सरः पुण्यं महीपते। फुल्लपद्मं महाराज देवगन्धर्वसेवितम्॥
en: O ruler of men, O great king, on the top of the mountain there is a sacred lake adorned with full blossomed lotuses and frequented by the celestials and the Gandharvas.

sn: बह्वाश्चर्यं महाराज दृश्यते तत्र पर्वते। पुण्ये स्वर्गोपमे चैव देवर्षिगणसेविते॥
en: O great king, many wonders are to be seen on that sacred mountain which is like heaven itself and which is visited by the celestials Rishis.

sn: ह्रदिनी पुण्यतीर्था च राजर्षेस्तत्र वै सरित्। विश्वामित्रनदी राजन् पुण्या परपुरंजय॥ यस्यास्तीरे सतां मध्ये ययातिर्नहुषात्मजः। पपात स पुनर्लोकॉल्लेभेधर्मान् सनातनान्॥
en: O king, O conqueror of hostile cities, there is the sacred river called Vishvamitra belonging to the royal sage of that name and which abounds in many sacred Tirthas. It was on the banks of this river, the son of Nahusha, Yayati, fell (from heaven) among the pious and obtained again the eternal region of the virtuous.

sn: तत्र पुण्यो ह्रदः ख्याते मैनाकश्चैव पर्वतः। बहुमूलफलोपेतस्त्वसिते नाम पर्वतः॥
en: There is also the sacred lake known by the name of Punya, the mountain called Mainaka and that other mountain called Asita abounding in fruits and roots.

sn: आश्रमः कक्षसेनस्य पुण्यस्तत्र युधिष्ठिर। च्यवनस्याश्रमश्चैव विख्यातस्तत्र पाण्डव॥
en: O Yudhishthira, O son of Pandu, there is also the sacred hermitage of Kakshasena and also the hermitage of Chyavana known every where.

sn: तत्राल्पेनैव सिध्यन्ति मानवास्तपसा विभो। जम्बूभार्गो महाराज ऋषीणां भावितात्मनाम्॥ आश्रमः शाम्यतां श्रेष्ठ मृगद्विजनिषेवितः।
en: O lord, here men obtain success in their asceticism with less austerities. O great king, here also is Jambumarga, the herinitage of Rishis of subdued soul. O foremost of selfcontrolled men, the hermitage is frequented by birds and deer.

sn: ततः पुण्यतमा राजन् सततं तापसैर्युता॥ केतुमाला च मेध्या च गङ्गद्वारं च भूमिप। ख्यातं च सैन्धवारण्यं पुण्यं द्विजनिषेवितम्॥
en: O king, there is the very sacred and ascetic surrounded, Ketumela, Medhaya also Gangadvara and the celebrated forest of Saindhava, frequented by the Brahmanas.

sn: पितामहसरः पुण्यं पुष्करं नाम नामतः। वैखानसानां सिद्धानामृषीणामाश्रमः प्रियः॥
en: Then there is the sacred lake of the Grandsire, known by the name of Pushkara, the favourite hermitage of Valkhilyas, the Siddhas and the Rishis.

sn: अप्यत्र संश्रयार्थाय प्रजापतिरथो जगौ। पुष्करेषु कुरुश्रेष्ठ गाथां सुकृतिनां वर॥
en: O foremost of Kurus, O best of all virtuous men, moved by the desire to get its shelter, the lord of creatures recited this verse at Pushkara.

sn: मनसाप्यभिकामस्य पुष्कराणि मनस्विनः। विप्रणश्यन्ति पापानि नाकपृष्ठे च मोदते॥
en: "If a pure souled man wishes to go to the Pushkara even in his imagination, he is cleansed of all his sins and he rejoices in heaven.

sn: धौम्य उवाच उदीच्यां राजशार्दूल दिशि पुण्यानि यानि वै। तानि ते कीर्तयिष्यामि पुण्यान्यायतनानि च।॥ शृणुष्वावहितो भूत्वा मम मन्त्रयतः प्रभो। कथाप्रतिग्रहो वीर श्रद्धां जनयते शुभाम्॥
en: Dhaumya said : O foremost of men, I shall (now) describe those Tirthas and sacred spots that lie in the northern country. O lord, hear of them with all attention. O hero, hearing this narrative one obtains reverence which does him much good.

sn: सरस्वती महापुण्या ह्रदिनी तीर्थमालिनी। समुद्रगा महावेगा यमुना यत्र पाण्डव॥
en: O son of Pandu, here flows the greatly sacred Sarasvati abounding in Tirthas and banks, easy of ascent. Here also flows the ocean going and impetuous Yamuna.

sn: यत्र पुण्यतरं तीर्थं प्लक्षावतरणं शुभम्। यत्र सारस्वतैरिष्टवा गच्छन्त्यवभृथैर्द्विजाः॥
en: And here is also the very sacred and auspicious Tirtha called Plakshavatarana where the Brahmanas after performing the Sarasvati sacrifice made their ablutions.

sn: पुण्यं चाख्यायते दिव्यं शिवमग्निशिरोऽनघ। सहदेवोऽयजद् यत्र शम्याक्षेपेण भारत॥
en: O sinless one, O descendant of Bharata, here is also the celebrated celestials and auspicious Tirtha called Agnisshira, where Sahadeva performed a sacrifice by measuring out the ground by a throw of Shamya.

sn: एतस्मिन्नेव चार्थेऽसाविन्द्रगीता युधिष्ठिर। गाथा चरति लोकेऽस्मिन् गीयमाना द्विजातिभिः॥
en: O Yudhishthira, it is for this reason Indra sang the praises (of Sahadeva) in a verse which is still current in the world and sung by the Brahmanas.

sn: अग्नयः सहदेवेन सेविता यमुनामनु। ते तस्य कुरुशार्दूल सहस्रशतदक्षिणा:॥
en: O foremost of the Kurus, on the Yamuna, Agni was worshipped by Sahadeva when Dakshinas (gifts) in hundreds and thousands were made.

sn: तत्रैव भरतो राजा चक्रवर्ती महायशाः। विंशतिः सप्त चाष्टौ च हयमेधानुपाहरत्॥
en: Here the greatly illustrious king, the emperor Bharata performed thirty five horse-sacrifices.

sn: कामकृद् यो द्विजातीनां श्रुतस्तात यथा पुरा। अत्यन्तमाश्रमः पुण्यः शरभङ्गस्य विश्रुतः॥
en: O child, we have heard that Sharabhanga who in the days of yore used to gratify much the Brahmanas, had his sacred and celebrated hermitage here.

sn: सरस्वती नदी सद्भिः सततं पार्थ पूजिता। बालखिल्यैर्महाराज यत्रेष्टमृषिभिः पुरा॥
en: O son of Pritha, O great king, here is also the river Sarasvati which is ever worshipped by the pious and (on the bank of which) the Balkhilayas performed sacrifices in the days of yore.

sn: दृषद्वती महापुण्या यत्र ख्याता युधिष्ठिर। न्यचोधाख्यस्तु पुण्याख्यः पाञ्चाल्यो द्विपदांवर॥ दाल्भ्यघोषश्च दाल्भ्यश्चधरणीस्थो महात्मनः। कौन्तेयानन्तयशसः सुव्रतस्यामितौजसः॥ आश्रमः ख्यायते पुण्यस्त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतः।
en: O Yudhishthira, O foremost of men, here is also the highly sacred and greatly famous Drishadvati. Here are Nyagrodhya, Panchalya, Punya, Dalbhayaghosa and Dalbhya which are the sacred hermitage on earth of the illustrious Anantasas of excellent vows and great energy and which are all celebrated over the three worlds.

sn: एतावर्णाववर्णौ च विश्रुतौ मनुजाधिप॥
en: O ruler of men, here also the celebrated Etavarna and Avavarna.

sn: वेदज्ञौ वेदविद्वांसौ वेदविद्याविदावुभौ। ईजाते क्रतुभिर्मुख्यैः पुण्यैर्भरतसत्तम॥
en: Learned in the Vedas, versed in the Vedic lore and proficient in Vedic rites, O best of the Bharata race, performed many sacred and best sacrifices.

sn: समेत्य बहुशो देवाः सेन्द्राः सवरुणाः पुरा। विशाखयूपेऽतप्यन्त तेन पुण्यतमश्च सः॥
en: Here is also Vishakhayupa to which in the days of yore came the celestials with Indra and Varuna and practised asceticism; and thus it became so sacred.

sn: ऋधिर्महान् महाभागो जमदग्निर्महायशाः। पलाशकेषु पुण्येषु रम्येष्वयजत प्रभुः॥
en: Here also is the sacred and charming Palasaka where the greatly exalted, the highly illustrious great Rishi lord Jamadagni performed sacrifices.

sn: यत्र सर्वाः सरिच्छेष्ठाः साक्षात् तमृषिसत्तमम्। स्वं स्वं तोयमुपादाय परिवार्योपतस्थिरे॥
en: Here all the chief rivers in their embodied forms, taking their respective waters, stood round that foremost of Rishis.

sn: अपि चात्र महाराज स्वयं विश्वांवसुर्जगौ। इमं श्लोकं तदा वीर प्रेक्ष्य दीक्षां महात्मनः॥
en: O great king, O hero, here also Vibhavasu (fire) himself, going there and seeing that highsouled Rishis' initiation, recited the following sloka.

sn: यजमानस्य वै देवाञ्जमदग्नेर्महात्मनः। आगम्य सरितो विप्रान् मधुना समतर्पयन्॥
en: "When the illustrious Jamadagni was worshipping the celestials, the rivers, coming to the Brahmanas, offered them honey."

sn: गन्धर्वयक्षरक्षोभिरप्सरोभिश्च सेवितम्। किरातकिन्नरावासं शैलं शिखारेणां वरम्॥ विभेद तरसा गङ्गा गङ्गाद्वारं युधिष्ठिर। पुण्यं तत् ख्यायते राजन् ब्रह्मर्षिगणसेवितम्॥
en: O Yudhishthira, the spot where the Ganga rushes onward clearing that foremost of mountains (the Himalayas) frequented by the Gandharvas, the Yakshas, the Rakshasas, the Apsaras and inhabited by the Kiratas and the Kinnaras is called Gangadvara. O king this spot frequented by the celestials Rishis is considered very sacred.

sn: सनत्कुमारः कौरव्य पुण्यं कनखलं तथा। पवर्तश्च पुरुर्नाम यत्र यातः पुरूरवाः॥
en: O descendant of Kuru, by Sanatkumar, as also the sacred Kankhala. Here is also the mountain called Puru on which was born Pururava,

sn: भृगुर्यत्र तपस्तेपे महर्षिगणसेविते। राजन् स आश्रमः ख्यातो भृगुतुङ्गो महागिरिः॥
en: And where Bhrigu practised his austerities. O king that hermitage has thus become known by the name of mountain Bhrigutunga.

sn: यः स भूतं भविष्यच्च भवच्च भरतर्षभ। नारायणः प्रभुर्विष्णुः शाश्वतः पुरुषोत्तमः॥ तस्यातियशसः पुण्यां विशालां बदरीमनु। आश्रमः ख्यायते पुण्यस्त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतः॥
en: O best of Bharata race, here is the sacred and extensive Badari, celebrated all over the worlds, which is the highly holy hermitage of him who is the Present, the Past and the Future, who is called Narayana, the lord Vishnu, who is eternal and who is the foremost of Purushas.

sn: उष्णतोयवहा गङ्गां शीततोयवहा पुरा। सुवर्णसिकता राजन् विशालां बदरीमनु॥
en: O king, near Badari the cool waters of Ganga were formerly hot and her banks were over-spread with sands of gold.

sn: ऋषये यत्र देवाश्च महाभागा महौजसः। प्राप्य नित्यं नमस्यन्ति देवं नारायणं प्रभुम्॥ यत्र नारायणो देवः परमात्मा सनातनः। तत्र कृत्स्नं जगत् सर्वं तीर्थान्यायतनानि च।॥
en: Here the greatly exalted and highly effulgent Rishis and the celestials come daily to worship the deity, the lord Vishnu. The whole universe, with all its Tirthas and sacred places is there where dwells the deity Narayana, the eternal Supreme soul.

sn: तत् पुण्यं परमं ब्रह्म तत् तीर्थं तत् तपोवनम्। तत् परं परमं देवं भूतानां परमेश्वरम्॥
en: He is virtue, he is the supreme Brahma, he is the Tirtha, he is the ascetic retreat, he is the first, he is the foremost of gods, he is the great lord of all creatures.

sn: शाश्वतं परमं चैवधातारं परमं पदम्। यं विदित्वा न शोचन्ति विद्वांसः शास्त्रदृष्टयः॥ तत्र देवर्षयः सिद्धाः सर्वे चैव तपोधनाः।
en: He is the great creator, he is the highest state. By knowing him, learned men versed in the Shastras never meet with grief. The celestials Rishis, the Siddhas, may all the ascetics live ther.

sn: आदिदेवो महायोगी यत्रास्ते मधुसूदनः॥ पुण्यानामपि तत् पुण्यमत्र ते संशयोऽस्तु मा। एतानि राजन् पुण्यानि पृथिव्यां पृथिवीपते॥ कीर्तितानि नरश्रेष्ठ तीर्थान्यायतनानि च। एतानि वसुभिः साध्यैरादित्यैर्मरुदश्विभिः॥ ऋषिभिर्देवकल्पैश्च सेवितानि महात्मभिः। चरन्नेतानि कौन्तेय सहिता ब्राह्मणर्षभैः। भ्रातृभिश्च महाभागैरुत्कण्ठां विहरिष्यसि॥
en: Where the primeval deity, that Supreme Yogi, the slayer of Madhu lives. O king, let not any doubt come to your mind about the sacredness of that place. O ruler of earth, these are the sacred spots on earth and the Tirthas that I have mentioned to you. O foremost of men, they are all frequented by the Vasus, the Sadhyas, the Adityas, the Marutas, the Ashvins and the high-souled. Celestialss like Rishis. O son of Kunti, visit all these (Tirthas) with the Brahmanas and with your greatly exalted brothers and thus be relieved from all anxiety.

description: The colloquy between Yudhishthira and Lomasha
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवं सम्भाषमाणे तुधौम्ये कौरवनन्दन। लोमशः स महातेजा ऋषिस्तत्राजगाम ह॥ तं पाण्डवाचजो राजा सगणो ब्राह्मणाश्च ते। उपातिष्ठन्महाभागं दिवि शक्रमिवामराः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : O descendant of Kuru, when Dhaumya was thus talking, at that very time the greatly effulgent Rishi Lomasha came here. Thereupon the eldest Pandava, the king (Yudhishthira) with his followers and other Brahmanas sat round that greatly exalted one (Lomasha), as Shakra (Indra) is surrounded by the celestials.

description: The colloquy between Yudhishthira and Lomasha
sn: समभ्यर्च्य यथान्यायंधर्मपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः। पप्रच्छागमने हेतुमटने च प्रयोजनम्॥
en: Having duly adored him, the son of Dharma Yudhishthira asked the reason of his arrival and the object of his wandering.

description: The colloquy between Yudhishthira and Lomasha
sn: स पृष्टः पाण्डुपुत्रेण प्रीयमाणो महामनाः। उवाच श्लक्ष्णया वाचा हर्षयन्निव पाण्डवान्॥
en: Having been asked by the son of Pandu, the high-minded (Rishi), being well pleased, spoke in sweet words and delighted the Pandavas.

description: The colloquy between Yudhishthira and Lomasha
sn: संचरन्नस्मि कौन्तेय सर्वाल्लँकोकान् यदृच्छया। गतः शक्रस्य भवनं तत्रापश्यं सुरेश्वरम्॥
en: Lonmasha said: O son of Kunti, travelling over all the worlds at pleasure I went to the abode of Sakra (Indra) and there I saw the king of the celestials.

description: The colloquy between Yudhishthira and Lomasha
sn: तव च भ्रातरं वीरमपश्यं सव्यसाचिनम्। शक्रस्यार्धासनगतं तत्र मे विस्मये महान्॥
en: saw your brother also, the heroic Savyasachi (Arjuna) sitting on the half of Shakra's seat and I became very much astonished,

description: The colloquy between Yudhishthira and Lomasha
sn: आसीत् पुरषशार्दूल दृष्टवा पार्थं तथागतम्। आह मां तत्र देवेशो गच्छ पाण्डुसुतान् प्रति॥
en: On seeing Partha sitting in that way. O foremost of men, then the chief of the celestials said to me, “Go to the sons of Pandu."

description: The colloquy between Yudhishthira and Lomasha
sn: सोऽहमभ्यागतः क्षिप्रं दिदृक्षुस्त्वां सहाजुनम्। वचनात् पुरुहूतस्य पार्थस्य च महात्मनः॥
en: At the request of Indra and the high-souled Partha. I have speedily come here to see you with your younger brothers.

description: The colloquy between Yudhishthira and Lomasha
sn: आख्यास्ये ते प्रियं तात महत् पाण्डवनन्दन। ऋषिभिः सहितो राजन् कृष्णया चैव तच्छृणु॥ यत् त्वयोक्तो महाबाहुरस्त्रार्थं भरतर्षभ। तदस्त्रमाप्तं पार्थेन रुद्रादप्रतिमं विभो॥
en: O child, O descendant of Pandu, O king, I shall tell you something which will give you great pleasure. Listen to it with Krishna (Draupadi) and with the Rishis that are with you. O lord, O best of the Bharata race, Partha has obtained from Rudra that matchless weapon for which you had sent that mighty armed hero to the celestials region.

description: The colloquy between Yudhishthira and Lomasha
sn: यत् तद् ब्रह्मशिरो नाम तपसा रुद्रमागमत्। अमृतादुत्थितं रौद्रं तल्लब्धं सव्यसाचिना॥
en: That fearful weapon, known by the name of Brahinashira which rose after the Ambrosia (in the churning of the ocean) and which Rudra obtained after great asceticism, has been obtained by Savyasachi (Arjuna).

description: The colloquy between Yudhishthira and Lomasha
sn: तत् समन्त्रं ससंहारं सप्रायश्चित्तमङ्गलम्। वज्रमस्त्राणि चान्यानि दण्डादीनि युधिष्ठिर॥
en: Together with the Mantras for hurling and withdrawing it and also the rites of expiation and revival. O Yudhishthira, the weapon Vajra, Dandas and other weapons,

description: The colloquy between Yudhishthira and Lomasha
sn: यमात् कुबेराद् वरुणादिन्द्राच्च कुरुनन्दन। अस्त्राण्यधीतवान् पार्थो दिव्यान्यमितविक्रमः॥
en: O descendant of Kuru, have been obtained by the immeasurably powerful Partha from Yama, Kubera, Varuna and Indra.

description: The colloquy between Yudhishthira and Lomasha
sn: विश्वावसोस्तु तनयाद् गीतं नृत्यं च साम च। वादित्रं च यथान्यायं प्रत्यविन्दद् यथाविधि॥
en: He has learnt from Vishvavasu's son both vocal and instrumental music and also singing and also the reciting of the Sama (Veda) as thoroughly as they should be learnt.

description: The colloquy between Yudhishthira and Lomasha
sn: एवं कृतास्त्रः कौन्तेयो गान्धर्वं वेदमाप्तवान्। सुखं वसति बीभत्सुरनुजस्यानुजस्तव॥
en: Having thus acquired all weapons and learnt the Gandharva Veda (knowledge) your third brother Vivatsu (Arjuna) lives happily in (heaven).

description: The colloquy between Yudhishthira and Lomasha
sn: यदर्थं मां सुरश्रेष्ठ इदं वचनमब्रवीत्। तच्च ते कथयिष्यामि युधिष्ठिर निबोध मे॥
en: O Yudhishthira, I shall now tell you what the chief of the celestials spoke to me. Listen to me.

description: The colloquy between Yudhishthira and Lomasha
sn: भवान् मनुष्यलोकेऽपि गमिष्यति न संशयः। ब्रूयाद् युधिष्ठिरं तत्र वचनान्मे द्विजोत्तम॥
en: (He said), “You will certainly go to the world of men. O foremost of men, tell Yudhishthira my these words.

description: The colloquy between Yudhishthira and Lomasha
sn: आगमिष्यति ते भ्राता कृतास्त्रः क्षिप्रमर्जुनः। सुरकार्यं महत् कृत्वा यदशक्यं दिवौकसाम्॥
en: Your brother will soon came back to you after having obtained all weapons and after having accomplished a great deed for the celestials which is incapable of being done by them.

description: The colloquy between Yudhishthira and Lomasha
sn: तपसापि त्वमात्मानं योजय भ्रातृभिः सह। तपसो हि परं नास्ति तपसा विन्दते महत्॥
en: Devote yourself with your brothers to asceticism; there is nothing superior to asceticism and asceticism produces great results.

description: The colloquy between Yudhishthira and Lomasha
sn: अहं च कर्णं जानामि यथावद् भरतर्षभ। सत्यसंधं महोत्साहं महावीर्यं महाबलम्॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, I know very well that Karna possesses great ardour, energy, strength and prowess.

description: The colloquy between Yudhishthira and Lomasha
sn: महाहवेष्वप्रतिमं महायुद्धविशारदम्। महाधनुर्धरं वीरं महास्त्रं वरवर्णिनम्॥
en: He is matchless in great battle, highly learned in the science of war, a great wielder of bow, a hero clad in the best of armour and skilled in the best of weapons.

description: The colloquy between Yudhishthira and Lomasha
sn: महेश्वरसुतप्रख्यमादित्यतनयं प्रभुम्। तथार्जुनमतिस्कन्दं सहजोल्बणपौरुषम्॥
en: That exalted son of Aditya resembles the son of Maheshvara himself. I know also very well and naturally great prowess of the broadshouldered Arjuna.

description: The colloquy between Yudhishthira and Lomasha
sn: न स पार्थस्य संग्रमे कलामर्हति षोडशीम्। यच्चापि ते भयं कर्णान्मनसिस्थमरिंदम॥
en: In battle Karna is not equal even to a sixteenth part of Partha (Arjuna). The fear that you bear in your mind from Karna, O chastiser of foes.

description: The colloquy between Yudhishthira and Lomasha
sn: तच्चाप्यपहरिष्यामि सव्यसाचिन्युपागते। यच्च ते मानसं वीर तीर्थयात्रामिमां प्रति। स महर्षिर्लोमशस्ते कथयिष्यत्यसंशयम्॥
en: Will be dispelled when Savyasachi (Arjuna) would come here from heaven. O Hero and as regards your desire to go to visit the Tirthas, the great Rishi Lomasha will no doubt speak to you.

description: The colloquy between Yudhishthira and Lomasha
sn: यच्च किंचित् तपोयुक्तं फलं तीर्थेषु भारत! ब्रह्मर्षिरेष ब्रूयात् ते तच्छ्रद्धेयं न चान्यथा॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, whatever that Brahmana Rishi would speak about the fruits of asceticism and Tirthas, should be accepted by you with all respect and never otherwise.

sn: लोमश उवाच धनंजयेन चाप्युक्तं यत् तच्छृणु युधिष्ठिर। युधिष्ठिरं भ्रातरं मे योजयेर्धर्म्यया श्रिया॥ त्वं हिधर्मान् परान् वेत्थ तपांसि च तपोधन। श्रीमतां चापि जानासिधर्मं राज्ञां सनातनम्॥
en: Lomasha said : O Yudhishthira, listen to now what Dhananjaya (Arjuna) has said. He said, "Make my brother Yudhishthira to practice excellent religion. O ascetic, you know the highest religion, ascetic austerities and the eternal religion of prosperous kings.

sn: स भवान् परमं वेद पावनं पुरुषं प्रति। तेन संयोजयेथास्त्वं तीर्थपुण्येन पाण्डवान्॥
en: You know the great means by which men are purified. Therefore, persuade the Pandavas to acquire the virtue which is obtained by visiting Tirthas.

sn: यथा तीर्थानि गच्छेत गाश्च दद्यात् स पार्थिवः। तथा सर्वात्मना कार्यमिति मामर्जुनोऽब्रवीत्॥
en: Do that with all your heart by which that king Yudhishthira may visit all the Tirthas and give away (in charity). Arjuna said this to ine.

sn: भवता चानुगुप्तोऽसौ चरेत् तीर्थानि सर्वशः। रक्षोभ्यो रक्षितव्यश्च दुर्गेषु विषमेषु च॥
en: (He said), “Let him go to all the Tirthas protected by you. You should protect him from the Rakshasas in inaccessible and rugged places.

sn: दधीच इव देवेन्द्रं यथा चाप्यङ्गिरा रविम्। तथा रक्षस्व कौन्तेयान् राक्षसेभ्यो द्विजोत्तम॥
en: O foremost of Brahmanas, as Dadhichi has protected the chief of the celestials and as Angiras has protected the sun, so do you protect the sons of Kunti from the Rakshasas.

sn: यातुधाना हि बहवो राक्षसाः पर्वतोपमाः। त्वयाभिगुप्तं कौन्तेयं न विवर्तेयुरन्तिकम्॥
en: The way is beset with many Rakshasas, huge as mountains. If protected by you, they will not be able to approach the sons of Kunti.

sn: सोऽहमिन्द्रस्य वचनान्नियोगादर्जुनस्य च। रक्षमाणो भयेभ्यस्त्वां चरिष्यामि त्वया सह॥
en: At the request of Indra and also being appointed by Arjuna, I shall travel with you protecting you from all dangers.

sn: द्विस्तीर्थानि मया पूर्वं दृष्टानि कुरुनन्दन। इदं तृतीयं द्रक्ष्यामि तान्येव भवता सह॥
en: O descendant of Kuru, I have seen the Tirthas twice before. I shall for the third time see them with you.

sn: इयं राजर्षिभिर्याता पुण्यकृद्भिर्युधिष्ठिर। मन्वादिभिर्महाराज तीर्थयात्रा भयापहा॥
en: O great king Yudhishthira, Manu and other Rishis of virtuous deeds had visited the Tirthas, for a visit to them dispels all fears.

sn: नानृजुर्नाकृतात्मा च नाविद्यो न च पापकृत्। स्नाति तीर्थेषु कौरव्य न च वक्रमतिर्नरः॥
en: O descendant of Kuru, men, who are crooked-minded, who have not souls under control, who are illiterate and who are sinful, do not bathe in Tirthas.

sn: त्वं तुधर्ममतिर्नित्यंधर्मज्ञः सत्यसंगरः। विमुक्तः सर्वसङ्गेभ्यो भूय एव भविष्यसि॥
en: But your mind is always fixed on virtue; you are versed in the precepts of religion and you are truthful, you will surely be freed from all fears.

sn: यथा भागीरथो राजा राजानश्च गयादयः। यथा ययातिः कौन्तेय तथा त्वमपि पाण्डव॥
en: O son of Pandu and O Yudhishthira, you are like the king Bhagiratha or king Gaya or Yayati or any one else like them,

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच न हर्षात् सम्प्रपश्यामि वाक्यस्यास्योत्तरं क्वचित्। स्मरेद्धि देवराजो यं को नामाभ्यधिकस्ततः॥
en: Yudhishthira said : I am so overwhelmed with joy that I cannot find words to answer you. Who can be more fortunate than he who is remembered by the king of the celestials?

sn: भवता संगमो यस्य भ्राता चैवधनंजयः। वासवः स्मरते यस्य को नामाभ्यधिकस्ततः॥
en: Who can be more fortunate than he who has you for his company, who has Dhananjaya (Arjuna) as his brother, nay who is remembered by Vasava (Indra) himself.

sn: यच्च मां भगवानाह तीर्थानां दर्शनं प्रति। धौम्यस्य वचनादेषा बुद्धिः पूर्वं कृतव मे॥
en: What your exalted self has said to me as regards seeing the Tirthas I have already made up my mind to do it) at the words of Dhaumya.

sn: तद् यदा मन्यसे ब्रह्मन् गमनं तीर्थदर्शने। तदैव गन्तास्मि तीर्थान्येष मे निश्चयः परः॥
en: O Brahmana, I shall start to visit the Tirthas at whatever hour you are pleased to appoint. This is my firm resolve.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच गमने कृतबुद्धिं तु पाण्डवं लोमशोऽब्रवीत्। लघुर्भव महाराज लघुः स्वैरं गमिष्यसि॥
en: Vaishampayana said: Lomasha then thus spoke to the Pandava (Yudhishthira) who had made up his mind, "O great king, be light (as regards your retinue), for if you be thus light, you will be able to go more easily.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच भिक्षाभुजो निवर्तन्तां ब्राह्मणा यतयश्च ये। क्षुत्तृडध्वश्रमायासशीतार्तिमसहिष्णवः॥
en: Yudhishthira said : Let the mendicants, Brahmanas and Yogis who are incapable of bearing hunger and thirst, the fatigues of travel and toil and also the severity of winter desist (from following me).

sn: ते सर्वे विनिवर्तन्तां ये च मिष्टभुजो द्विजाः। पक्वान्नलेह्यपानानां मांसानां च विकल्पकाः॥
en: Let those Brahmanas also that live on sweet meats, that desire cooked food and the food that is sucked or drunk and meat desist (from following me).

sn: तेऽपि सर्वे निवर्तन्ता ये च सूदानुयायिनः। मया यथोचिताजीव्यैः संविभक्ताश्च वृत्तिभिः॥ चाप्यनुरताः पौरा राजभक्तिपुरः सराः। धृतराष्ट्र महाराजमभिगच्छन्तु ते च वै॥
en: Let all those that depend on cooks also desist (from. following me). Let those citizens that have followed me from loyalty and whom I have hitherto supported properly go back to the great king Dhritarashtra.

sn: स दास्यति यथाकालमुचिता यस्य या भृतिः। स चेद् यथोचितां वृत्तिं न दद्यान्मनुजेश्वरः॥ अस्मत्प्रियहितार्थाय पाञ्चाल्यो वः प्रदास्यति॥
en: He will give them in due time their proper allowance. If that ruler of men does not give them their proper allowances. The king of Panchala will give them the allowance for our satisfaction and welfare.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततो भूयिष्ठशः पौरा गुरुभारप्रपीडिताः। विप्राश्च यतयो मुख्या जग्मुर्नागपुरं प्रति॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Thereupon being exceedingly aggrieved the Brahmanas, the Yogis and the citizens went towards Hastinapur.

sn: तान् सर्वान्धर्मराजस्य प्रेम्णा राजाम्बिकासुतः। प्रतिजग्राह विधिवद्धनैश्च समतर्पयत्॥
en: Out of affection for Dharmaraja (Yudhishthira), the king (Dhritarashtra) the son of Ambika, received them properly and gratified them with proper allowances.

sn: ततः कुन्तीसुतो राजा लघुभिाह्मणैः सह। लोमशेन च सुप्रीतस्त्रिरात्रं काम्यकेऽवसत्॥
en: Thereupon, the son of Kunti, the king (Yudhishthira) with only a few Brahmanas lived in the Kaimyaka (forest) for three nights, much cleared by Lomasha.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततः प्रयान्तं कौन्तेयं ब्राह्मणा वनवासिनः। अभिगम्य तदा राजन्निदं वचनमबृदन्॥
en: Vaishampayana said: O king, thereupon those dwellers of the forest, those Brahmanas, seeing that the son of Kunti was about to, came to him and spoke these words.

sn: राजस्तीर्थानि गन्तासि पुण्यानि भ्रातृभिः सह। ऋषिणा चैव सहितो लोमशेन महात्मना॥
en: “O king, you are going to the sacred Tirthas with your brothers and with the illustrious Rishi Lomasha.

sn: अस्मानपि महाराज नेतुमर्हसि पाण्डव। अस्माभिर्हि न शक्यानि त्वदृते तानि कौरव॥
en: O great king, O Pandava, O descendant of Kuru, you should take us with you. Without you we shall never able to visit them.

sn: श्वापदैरुपसृष्टानि दुर्गाणि विषमाणि च। अगम्यानि नरैरल्पैस्तीर्थानि मनुजेश्वर॥
en: O ruler of men, they are full of dangers and abound in wild beasts; they are inaccessible and are to be reached through dragged ways. Men in small parties cannot reach these Tirthas.

sn: भवतो भ्रातरः शूराधनुर्धरवसः सदा। भवद्भिः पालिताः शूरैर्गच्छामो वयमप्युत॥
en: O undeteriorating one, your brothers are heroes, they are foremost wielders of bows. Protected by you who are all heroes, we shall also be able to go.

sn: भवत्प्रसादाद्धि वय प्राप्नुयाम सुखं फलम्। तीर्थानां पृथिवीपाल वनानां च विशाम्पते॥
en: O ruler of earth, O king, through your favour we shall acquire the happy fruits of Tirthas and (sacred) forests.

sn: तव वीर्यपरित्राताः शुद्धास्तीर्थपरिप्लुताः। भवेमधूतपाप्मानस्तीर्थसंदर्शनानृप॥
en: O king, protected by your prowess, let us be cleansed of all our sins by visiting those Tirthas and by purifying ourselves by bathing therein,

sn: भवानपि नरेन्द्रस्य कार्तवीर्यस्य भारत। अष्टकस्य च राजर्लोमपादस्य चैव ह॥ भरतस्य च वीरस्य सार्वभौमस्य पार्थिव। ध्रुवं प्राप्स्यसि दुष्प्रापॉल्लोकांस्तीर्थपरिप्लुतः॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, O king, having bathed in these Tirthas you too will certainly obtain those inaccessible regions obtained by Kartavirya, Ashtaka, the royal sage Lomapada and the imperial and heroic Bharata.

sn: प्रभासादीनि तीर्थानि महेन्द्रादींश्च पर्वतान्। गङ्गाद्याः सरितश्चैव प्लक्षादींश्च वनस्पतीन्॥ त्वया सह महीपाल द्रष्टुमिच्छामहे वयम्। यदि ते ब्राह्मणेष्वस्ति काचित् प्रीतिर्जनाधिप।॥
en: Prabhasa and other Tirthas, Mahendra and other mountains, Ganga and other rivers, Plaksha and other lords of forests (trees). O great king, we desire to see all these with you. O ruler of men, if you have any regard of the Brahmanas. Then speedily do what we say. You will obtain prosperity through it.

sn: कुरु क्षिप्रं वचोऽस्माकं ततः श्रेयोऽभिपत्स्यसे। तीर्थानि हि महाबाहो तपोविघ्नकरैः सदा॥
en: O mighty armed hero, Tirthas are infested by Rakshasas ever prone to obstruct ascetic austerities. You should protect us from them.

sn: अनुकीर्णानि रक्षोभिस्तेभ्यो नस्त्रातुमर्हसि। तीर्थान्युक्तानिधौम्येन नारदेन चधीमता॥ यान्युवाच च देवर्षिर्लोमशः सुमहातपाः। विधिवत् तानि सर्वाणि पर्यटस्व नराधिप॥ धूतपाप्मा सहास्माभिर्लोमशेनाभिपालितः। स राजा पूज्यमानस्तैर्हर्षादश्रुपरिप्लुतः॥ भीमसेनादिभिवीरैर्धातृभिः परिवारितः। बाढमित्यब्रवीत् सर्वांस्तानृषीन् पाण्डवर्षभः॥
en: O ruler of men visit all the Tirthas spoken of by the greatly intelligent Dhaumya and also those spoken of by the greatly ascetic celestials Rishi Lomasha. Protected by Lomasha and accompanied by us, be cleansed of all sins.” Having been thus addressed by them, the king (Yudhishthira) was filled with tears of joy. Surrounded by his heroic brothers headed by Bhimasena that foremost of Pandavas (Yudhishthira) said to all those Rishis “So be it."

sn: लोमशं समनुज्ञाप्यधौम्यं चैव पुरोहितम्। ततः स पाण्डवश्रेष्ठो भ्रातृभिः सहितो वशी॥
en: With the permission of Lomasha and also with that of the priest Dhumya that selfcontrolled eldest Pandava with his brothers,

sn: द्रौपद्या चानवद्याझ्या गमनाय मनो दधे। अथ व्यासो महाभागस्तथा पर्वतनारदौ॥ काम्यके पाण्डवं द्रष्टुं समाजग्मुर्मनीषिणः। तेषां युधिष्ठिरो राजा पूजां चक्रे यथाविधि। सत्कृतास्ते महाभागा युधिष्ठिरमथाब्रुवन्॥
en: And with faultless featured Draupadi made up his mind to start. At that very time the greatly exalted Vyasa, Parvata and Narada, all endued with great intelligence, came to the Kamyaka (forest) with the desire of seeing the Pandavas. the king Yudhishthira worshipped them all in due form. When the exalted ones were all duly worshipped, they thus spoke to Yudhishthira,

sn: ऋषय ऊचुः युधिष्ठिर यमौ भीम मनसा कुरुतार्जवम्। मनसा कृतशौचा वै शुद्धास्तीर्थानि यास्यथ॥
en: "O Yudhishthira, O the twins, O Bhima, banish all evil thoughts from your minds. Purify your hearts and thus being purified go to the Tirthas.

sn: शरीरनियमं प्राहुर्ब्राह्मणा मानुषं व्रतम्। मनोविशुद्धां बुद्धिं च दैवमाहुव्रतं द्विजाः॥
en: The Brahmanas have said that to regulate one's body is the observance of human vows and to purify one's mind and understanding is the observance of celestials vows.

sn: मनो ह्यदुष्टं शौचाय पर्याप्तं वै नराधिप। मैत्री बुद्धिं समास्थाय शुद्धास्तीर्थानि द्रक्ष्यथ॥
en: O ruler of men, the mind which is free from all evil thoughts is highly pure. Therefore bearing friendly feelings towards all the purifying yourselves, visit the Tirthas.

sn: ते यूयं मानसैः शुद्धाः शरीरनियमव्रतैः। दैवं व्रतं समास्थाय यथोक्तं फलमाप्स्यथ॥
en: Observing human vows in respect of your body and purifying your mind by observing the celestials vows, acquire the fruits of Tirthas as recited (to you).

sn: ते तथेति प्रतिज्ञाय कृष्णया सह पाण्डवाः। कृतस्वस्त्ययनाः सर्वे मुनिभिर्दिव्यमानुषैः।।२१
en: Saying “So be it," the Pandavas with Krishna (Draupadi) caused all those celestials and human Rishis to perform propitiatory rites.

sn: लोमशस्योपसंगृह्य पादौ द्वैपायनस्य च। नारदस्य च राजेन्द्र देवर्षेः पर्वतस्य च॥
en: O king of kings, then touching the feet of Lomasha, of Dvaipayana (Vyasa) of Narada and of the celestials Rishi Parvata.

sn: ॥ धौम्येन सहिता वीरास्तथा तैर्वनवासिभिः। मार्गशीर्ध्यामतीतायां पुष्येण प्रययुस्ततः॥
en: Those heroes, accompanied by Dhaumya and other dwellers of the forest, started on their journey on the day following the full moon of Agrahayana in which the constellation Pausha was in ascendance.

sn: कठिनानि समादाय चीराजिनजटाधराः। अभेद्यैः कवचैर्युक्तास्तीर्थान्यन्वचरंस्ततः॥ इन्द्रसेनादिभिर्भूत्यै रथैः परिचतुर्दशैः। महानसव्यापृतैश्च तथान्यैः परिचारकैः॥ सायुधा बद्धनिस्त्रिशास्तूणवन्तः समार्गणाः। प्राङ्मुखाः प्रययुर्वीराः पाण्डवा जनमेजय॥
en: Clad in barks and skins, putting on impenetrable armours the heroic sons of Pandu with matted-locks on their heads, with quivers, arrows swords and other weapons, accompanied by Indrasena and other attendants, with fourteen chariots, with a number of cooks and servants of other classes, O Janamejaya, started with their faces turned towards the east.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच न वै निगुणमात्मानं मन्ये देवर्षिसत्तम। तथास्मि दुःखसंतप्तो यथा नान्यो महीपतिः॥
en: Yudhishthira said : O foremost of celestials Rishis, I do not think that I am not endued with some merit. But I am still afflicted with so much sorrow that (I believe) there is no other king like me.

sn: परांश्च निर्गुणान् मन्ये न चधर्मगतानपि। ते च लोमश लोकेऽस्मिन्नृध्यन्ते केन हेतुना॥
en: O Lomasha, I think my enemies have no merit and no virtuous tendencies. Why then do they proper in this world?

sn: लोमश उवाच नात्र दुःखं त्वया राजन् कार्यं पार्थ कथंचन। यदधर्मेण वर्धेयुरधर्मरुचयो जनाः॥
en: Lomasha said : O king, O Partha, never grieve that sinful men should prosper in consequence of the sins they commit.

sn: वर्धत्यधर्मेण नरस्ततो भद्राणि पश्यति। ततः सपत्नाञ्जयति समूलस्तु विनश्यति॥
en: A man may be seen to prosper by his sins, obtain good fruits or vanquish his enemies, but he is finally destroyed to the root.

sn: मया हि दृष्टा दैतेया दानवाश्च महीपते। वर्धमाना ह्यधर्मेण क्षयं चोपगताः पुनः॥
en: O ruler of earth, I have seen many Daityas and Danavas prosper by sin, but I have also seen that destruction has again ever taken them.

sn: पुरा देवयुगे चैव हृष्टं सर्वं मया विभो। अरोचयन् सुराधर्मधर्म तत्यजिरेऽसुराः॥
en: O lord, I have seen all this formerly in the Deva Yuga. The celestials practised virtue whereas the Asuras practised sin.

sn: तीर्थानि देवा विविशु विशन् भारतासुराः। तानधर्मकृतो दर्पः पूर्वमेव समाविशत्॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, the celestials visited the Tirthas whereas the Asuras did not visit them. Those sinful ones were first filled with pride.

sn: दर्पान्मानः समभवन्मानात् क्रोधो व्यजायत। क्रोधादह्रीस्ततोऽलज्जा वृत्तं तेषां ततोऽनशत्॥
en: Pride begot vanity and vanity begot wealth. From wealth arose every king of evil propensity and from evil propensities arose shamelessness.

sn: तानलज्जान् गतह्रीकान् हीनवृत्तान् वृथाव्रतान्। क्षमा लक्ष्मीः स्वधर्मश्च न चिरात् प्रजहुस्ततः॥
en: From shamelessness good behaviour disappeared from among them. From their shamelessness, from their evil propensities, from their want of good conduct and virtuous vows, forgiveness, propensity and morality all forsook them.

sn: लक्ष्मीस्तु देवानगमदलक्ष्मीरसुरान् नृप। तानलक्ष्मी समाविष्टान् दर्पोपहतचेतसः॥
en: O king, Lakshmi (the goddess of prosperity) then sought the celestials while a Lakshmi (goddess of adversity) sought the Asuras. When they were possessed by adversity they became senseless out of pride.

sn: दैतेयान् दानवांश्चैव कलिरप्याविशत् ततः। तानलक्ष्मीसमाविष्टान् दानवान् कलिना हतान्॥
en: Then Kali possessed the Daityas and the Danavas. Being thus possessed by adversity, the Danavas were destroyed by Kali.

sn: दभिभूतान् कौन्तेय क्रियाहीनानचेतसः। मानाभिभूतानचिराद् विनाशः समपद्यत॥
en: O son of Kunti, as they were filled with pride they became destitute of rites and sacrifices, devoid of reason, overwhelmed with vanity and they soon met with their destruction.

sn: निर्यशस्कास्तथा दैत्याः कृत्स्नशो विलयं गताः। देवास्तु सागरांश्चैव सरितश्च सरांसि च॥ अभ्यगच्छन्धर्मशीला: पुण्यान्यायतनानि च। तपोभिः क्रतुभिर्दानैराशीर्वादैश्च पाण्डव॥ प्रजहुः सर्वपापानि श्रेयश्च प्रतिपेदिरे। एवमादानवन्तश्च निरादानाश्च सर्वशः॥
en: Covered with infamy the Daityas were soon destroyed. O son of Pandu, the celestials, however, who were all of virtuous character, going to the seas, rivers and lakes and other sacred places, cleansed themselves of all their sins by means of asceticism and sacrifices, by gifts and blessings; and O Pandava, they obtained great prosperity. Because they thus abandoned all evil deeds and practised all good deeds,

sn: तीर्थान्यगच्छन् विबुधास्तेनापुभूतिमुत्तमाम्। तथा त्वमपि राजेन्द्र स्नात्वा तीर्थेषु सानुजः॥ पुनर्वेत्स्यसि तां लक्ष्मीमेष पन्थाः सनातनः।
en: And visited all the Tirthas, they obtained great good fortune. O king of kings, you will too therefore, bathing with your younger brothers in the Tirthas, obtain again great good fortune. This is the eternal road.

sn: यथेव हि नृगो राजा शिबिरौशीनरो यथा॥ भगीरथो वसुमना गयः पूरुः पुरूरवाः। चरमाणास्तपो नित्यं स्पर्शनादम्भसश्च ते॥ तीर्थाभिगमनात् पूता दर्शनाच्च महात्मनाम्। अलभन्त यशः पुण्यंधनानि च विशाम्पते॥
en: As kings, Nriga, Shibi, Ushinara, Bhagiratha, Vasumana, Gaya, Puru and Pururava, by always practising austerities and touching the sacred waters and visiting the Tirthas and seeing the illustrious holy men, O king, obtained fame, virtue and great wealth.

sn: तथा त्वमपि राजेन्द्र लब्धासि विपुलां श्रियन्त। यथा चेक्ष्वाकुरभवत् सपुत्रजनबान्धवः॥ मुचुकुन्दोऽथ मान्धाता मरुत्तश्च महीपतिः। कीर्ति पुण्यामविन्दन्त यथा देवास्तपोबलात्॥ देवर्षयश्च कात्स्न्येन तथा त्वमपि वेत्स्यसि। धार्तराष्ट्रास्त्वधर्मेण मोहेन च वशीकृताः। न चिराद् वै विनइक्ष्यन्ति दैत्या इव न संशयः॥
en: So will you obtain by acquiring exceedingly great prosperity. As Ikshvaku with his sons, friends and followers, Muchukunda, Mandhata and king Maruta, as the celestials through their power of asceticism, as the celestials Rishis also have obtained fame, so will you also obtain great fame. The sons of Dhritarashtra, enslaved as they are by sin and ignorance, will certainly be destroyed like Daityas. as

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ते तथा सहिता वीरा वसन्तस्तत्र तत्र ह। क्रमेण पृथिवीपाल नैमिषारण्यमागताः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : O ruler of earth, those heroes, (the Pandavas) accompanied by their followers, going from place to place, at last reached Naimisha forest.

sn: ततस्तीर्थेषु पुण्येषु गोमत्याः पाण्डवा नृप। कृताभिषेकाः प्रददुर्गाश्च वित्तं च भारत॥ तत्र देवान् पितॄन् विप्रांस्तर्पयित्वा पुनः पुनः। कन्यातीर्थेऽश्वतीर्थे च गवां तीर्थे च भारत। कालकोट्यां वृषप्रस्थे गिरावुष्य च पाण्डवाः॥ बाहुदायां महीपाल चक्रुः सर्वेऽभिषेचनम्। प्रयागे देवयजने देवानां पृथिवीपते॥ ऊषुराप्लुत्य गात्राणि तपश्चातस्थुरुत्तमम्। गङ्गयामुनयोश्चैव संगमे सत्यसंगराः॥
en: O king, O descendant of Bharata, the Pandavas bathed in the sacred Tirtha of Gomati and gave away kine and wealth (in charity). O descendant of Bharata, again and again offering oblations there to the Pitris and the celestials and the Brahmanas and living in Kalkoti and Brishaprastha hills, these descendants of Kuru, O ruler of earth, reached Vahuda and all performed there oblations. O king, going then to the sacrificial ground of the celestials. Those truth-observing men purified their bodies by bathing in the confluence of the Ganges and the Yamuna and performed excellent austerities.

sn: विपाप्मानो महात्मानो विप्रेभ्यः प्रददुर्वसु। तपस्विजनजुष्टां च ततो वेदी प्रजापतेः॥ जग्मुः पाण्डुसुता राजन् ब्राह्मणैः सह भारत। तत्र ते न्यवसन् वीरास्तपश्चातस्थुरुत्तमम्॥ संतर्पयन्तः सततं वन्येन हविषा द्विजान्।
en: Having been thus cleansed of all their sins, those high-souled heroes gave much wealth to the Brahmanas. O descendant of Bharata, then the son of king, O Pandu went to the (sacrificial altar) Vedi of the Creator, ever adored by the ascetics. There lived those heroes and performed excellent asceticism. Always gratifying the Brahmanas with the offer of fruits and ghee.

sn: ततो महीधरं जग्मुर्धर्मज्ञेनाभिसंस्कृतम्॥ राजर्षिणा पुण्यकृता गयेनानुपमद्युते। नगो गयशिरो यत्र पुण्या चैव महानदी॥ वानीरमालिनी रम्या नदी पुलिनशोभिता। दिव्यं पवित्रकूटं च पवित्रंधरणीधरम्॥ ऋषिजुष्टं सुपुण्यं तत् तीर्थं ब्रह्मसरोत्तमम्। अगस्त्यो भगवान् यत्र गतो वैवस्वतं प्रति॥
en: Then they went to Mahidhara, consecrated by the virtuous. Royal sage Gaya of matchless effulgence. Here stands the hill called Gayasira and where flows the sacred great river. With charming banks adorned with bushes of cane plants. On that celestials and sacred hill of holy peaks. Is the highly sacred Tirtha called Brahmasara adored by the Rishis, where Agastya went to the high-souled Vivasvata.

sn: उवास च स्वयं तत्रधर्मराजः सनातनः। सर्वासां सरितां चैव समुद्भेदो विशाम्पते॥
en: And where dwelt the eternal king of justice (Yama) himself. O king, all the rivers have taken their rise from it.

sn: यत्र संनिहितो नित्यं महादेवः पिनाकधृक्। तत्र ते पाण्डवा वीराश्चातुर्मास्यैस्तदेजिरे॥ ऋषियज्ञेन महता यत्राक्षयवटो महान्।
en: The wielder of Pinaka, the great god (Shiva) is always near it. The heroic Pandavas performed there the vow called Chaturmasa, according to the rites of the Rishi Jagma. Here is also the great banian tree called Akshayavata.

sn: अक्षये देवयजने अक्षयं यत्र वै फलम्॥
en: Any sacrifice performed there produces ever-lasting merit.

sn: ते तु तत्रोपवासांस्तु चक्रुनिश्चितमानसाः। ब्राह्मणास्तत्र शतशः समाजग्मुस्तपोधनाः॥
en: They (the Pandavas) began to fast there with subdued mind. And there came to them hundreds of ascetic Brahmanas.

sn: चातुर्मास्येनायजन्त आर्षेण विधिना तदा। तत्र विद्यातपोवृद्धा ब्राह्मणा वेदपारगाः। कथां प्रचक्रिरे पुण्यां सदसिस्था महात्मनाम्॥
en: Those Brahmanas, learned in the Vedas and old in knowledge, also performed the vow called Chaturmasa according to the rites ordained by the Rishis and they, becoming he court of the illustrious heroes talked on various subjects.

sn: तत्र विद्याव्रतस्तातः कौमारं व्रतमास्थितः। शमथोऽकथयद् राजन्नामूर्तरयसं गयम्॥
en: O king, the learned and vow-observing and celebrated Samatha spoke of Gaya, the son of Amurtaya.

sn: शमथ उवाच अमूर्तरयसः पुत्रो गयो राजर्षिसत्तमः। पुण्यानि यस्य कर्माणि तानि मे शृणु भारत॥
en: Samatha said: The son of Amurtaya is Gaya, the foremost of royal sages. O descendant of Bharata, listen to me, as I recite his virtuous deeds.

sn: यस्य यज्ञो बभूवेह बह्वन्नो बहुदक्षिणः। यत्रानपर्वता राजशतशोऽथ सहस्रशः॥ घृतकुल्याश्च दध्नश्च नद्यो बहुशतास्तथा। व्यञ्जनानां प्रवाहाश्च महार्हाणां सहस्रशः॥
en: O king, here it was that he performed many sacrifices, in which food and gifts were in abundance and in which cooked rice was in hundreds and thousands of mountains. Ghee and curds were in hundreds of lakes and rivers and richly cooked curries in thousands of streams.

sn: अहन्यहनि चाप्येवं याचतां सम्प्रदीयते। अन्ये च ब्राह्मणा राजन् भुञ्जतेऽन्नं सुसंस्कृतम्॥
en: O king, day after they were given away to all that asked for them. Besides Brahmanas were fed with food which was pure.

sn: तत्र वै दक्षिणाकाले ब्रह्मघोषो दिवं गतः। न च प्रज्ञायते किंचिद् ब्रह्मशब्देन भारत॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, when the time for distributing Dakshina (gift) came, the chanting of the Vedas reached heaven. Nothing else could be heard for that chanting of the Vedas.

sn: पुण्येन चरता राजन् भूर्दिशः खं नभस्तथा। आपूर्णमासीच्छब्देन तदप्यासीन्महाद्भुतम्॥ यत्र स्म गाथा गायन्ति मनुष्या भरतर्षभ। अन्नपानैः शुभैस्तृप्ता देशे देशे सुवर्चसः॥
en: O king, those sacred sounds filled earth, the points of the firmament, the sky and the heaven itself; and great wonders were seen. O best of Bharata race, greatly gratified with the food and the drink, men went about singing the following verse in various countries.

sn: गयस्य यज्ञे के त्वद्य प्राणिनो भोक्तुमीप्सवः। तत्र भोजनशिष्टस्य पर्वताः पञ्चविंशतिः॥
en: “Who is there among creatures that desires to day to eat more in the sacrifice of Gaya? There are still twenty-five mountains of food (uneaten).

sn: न तत् पूर्वे जनाचक्रुर्न करिष्यन्ति चापरे। गयो यदकरोद् यज्ञे राजर्षिरमितद्युतिः॥
en: What the immeasurably effulgent royal sage Gaya has done was never done by any man before or will be done by any man in future.

sn: कथं तु देवा हविषा गयेन परितर्पिताः। पुनः शक्ष्यन्त्युपादातुमन्यैर्दत्तानि कानिचित्॥
en: The celestials have been so very much fed with the Ghee that Gaya has offered them that they are not able to take anything more offered by any one else.

sn: सिकता वा यथा लोके यथा वा दिवि तारकाः। यथा वा वर्षतोधारा असंख्येयाः स्म केनचित्। तथा गणयितुं शक्या गययज्ञे न दक्षिणाः॥
en: As sand-grains on earth, as stars in the sky, as the drops of falling rains cannot be counted by any body, so will none be able to count the Dakshina given away in Gaya's sacrifice.”

sn: एवंविधा: सुबहवस्तस्य यज्ञा महीपतेः। बभूवुरस्य सरसः समीपे कुरुनन्दन॥
en: O descendant of Kuru, O king, many such sacrifices of his were performed on the banks of this lake.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततः सम्प्रस्थितो राजा कौन्तेयो भूरिदक्षिणः। अगस्त्याश्रममासाद्य दुर्जयायामुवास हा॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Then the of Kunti, the king (Yudhishthira), distinguished for his large gifts, son came to the hermitage of Agastya and lived at Durjaya.

sn: तत्रैव लोमशं राजा पप्रच्छ वदतां वरः। अगस्त्येनेह वातापिः किमर्थमुपशामितः॥
en: That foremost of eloquent men, the king (Yudhishthira) asked Agastya why Vatapi was killed there by him,

sn: आसीद्वा किं प्रभावश्च स दैत्यो मानवान्तकः। किमर्थं चोदितो मन्युरगस्त्यस्य महात्मनः॥
en: And what was the prowess of that meneating Daitya and why the anger of that highsouled (Rishi) was excited against him.

sn: लोमश उवाच इल्वलो नाम दैतेय आसीत् कौरवनन्दन। मणिमत्यां पुरि पुरा वातापिस्तस्य चानुजः॥
en: Lomasha said: O descendant of Kuru, there was a Daitya, named Ilvala in the days of yore in the city of Manimati. He had a younger brother, called Vatapi.

sn: स ब्राह्मणं तपोयुक्तमुवाच दितिनन्दनः। पुत्रं मे भगवानेकमिन्द्रतुल्यं प्रयच्छतु॥
en: That son of Diti (one day) spoke to an ascetic Brahmana, (saying), “O exalted one, give me a son equal to Indra.”

sn: तस्मै स ब्राह्मणो नादात् पुत्रं वासवसम्मितम्। चुक्रोध सोऽसुरस्तस्य ब्राह्मणस्य ततो भृशम्॥
en: As that Brahmana did not give him a son equal to Indra, that Asura got exceedingly angry against that Brahmana.

sn: तदाप्रभृति राजेन्द्र इल्वलो ब्रह्महासुरः। मन्युमान् भ्रातरं छागं मायावी ह्यकरोत् ततः॥
en: O king of kings, from that day the Asura Ilvala became a destroyer of Brahmanas. Endued as he was with the power of illusion, he made his brother a goat.

sn: मेघरूपी च वातापि: कामरूप्यभवत् क्षणात्। संस्कृत्य च भोजयति ततो विप्रं जिघांसति॥
en: Vatapi who was capable of assuming any form at will at once assumed the form of a goat. After being cooked that food was given to the Brahmanas in order to kill them.

sn: स चाह्वयति यं वाचा गतं वैवस्वतक्षयम्। स पुनर्देहमास्थाय जीवन् स्म प्रत्यदृश्यत॥
en: For he, whom he (Ilvala) summoned with his voice, would at once come back to him if he had gone even to the abode of Yama.

sn: ततो वातापिमसुरं छागं कृत्वा सुसंस्कृतम्। तं ब्राह्मणं भोजयित्वा पुनरेव समाह्वयत्॥
en: Thus having transformed Vatapi into a goat and after having cooked his flesh, he fed the Brahmanas and summoned him (back) again.

sn: तामिल्वलेन महता स्वरेण वाचमीरिताम्। श्रुत्वातिमायो बलवान् क्षिप्रं ब्राह्मणकण्टकः॥
