en: That powerful (Asura) endued with great power of illusion, that thorn to the Brahmanas, hearing the words loudly uttered by Ilvala,

sn: तस्य पार्श्व विनिर्भिद्य ब्राह्मणस्य महासुरः। वातापिः प्रहसन् राजन् निश्चक्राम विशाम्पते॥
en: That great Asura Vatapi, O king, O ruler of earth, would laughingly come out ripping open the sides of these Brahmanas.

sn: एवं स ब्राह्मणान् राजन् भोजयित्वा पुनः पुनः। हिंसयामास दैतेय इल्वलो दुष्टचेतनः॥
en: O king, having thus fed the Brahmanas again and again, the wicked-minded Daitya Ilvala destroyed the Brahmanas.

sn: अगस्त्यश्चापि भगवानेतस्मिन् काल एव तु। . पितृन् ददर्श गर्ने वै लम्बमानानधोमुखान्॥
en: The exalted Agastya in the mean-while saw his (dead) ancestors hanging in a pit with their head downwards.

sn: सोऽपृच्छल्लम्बमानांस्तान् भवन्त इव कम्पिताः। संतानहेतोरिति ते प्रत्यूचुर्ब्रह्मवादिनः॥
en: He asked them who were thus hanging, "What is the matter with you?" And those Brahmanas replied, “It is for the want offspring.”

sn: ते तस्मै कथयामासुर्वयं ते पितरः स्वकाः। गर्तमेतमनुप्राप्ता लम्बामः प्रसवार्थिनः॥
en: They told him, “We are your forefathers. We are thus hanging in this pit for the want of offspring.

sn: यदि नो जनयेथास्त्वमगस्त्यापत्यमुत्तमम्। स्यान्नोऽस्मान्निरयान्मोक्षस्त्वं च पुत्राप्नुया गतिम्॥
en: O Agastya, if you beget an excellent son for us, we may then be saved from this hell and you too can acquire the blessed state obtainable by begetting offspring."

sn: स तानुवाच तेजस्वी सत्यधर्मपरायणः। करिष्ये पितरः कामं व्येतु वो मानसो जवरः॥
en: To them replied that powerful Rishi observant of truth and morality, "O Pitris. I shall accomplish your desire and remove the fever of your mind.”

sn: ततः प्रसवसंतानं चिन्तयन् भगवानृषिः। आत्मनः प्रसवस्यार्थे नापश्यत् सदृशी स्त्रियम्॥
en: Then that illustrious Rishi began to think how to perpetuate his race. He did not find a fit wife in whom he can take his birth as his son.

sn: स तस्य तस्य सत्त्वस्य तत् तदङ्गमनुत्तमम्। संगृह्य तत्समैरङ्गैर्निर्मिमे स्त्रियमुत्तमाम्॥
en: He then, taking those parts of creatures that are considered beautiful, created an excellent woman with them.

sn: स तां विदर्भराजस्य पुत्रार्थं तप्यतस्तपः। निर्मितामात्मनोऽर्थाय मुनिः प्रादान्महातपाः॥
en: That greatly ascetic Rishi then gave that woman created for him to the king of Vidarbha who was performing great asceticism to beget an offspring.

sn: सा तत्र जज्ञे सुभगा विद्युत् सौदामनी यथा। विभ्राजमाना वपुषा व्यवर्धत शुभानना।॥
en: Taking her birth there, that exalted girl of beautiful face, as effulgent as the lightning, began to grow in body day after day.

sn: जातमात्रां च तां दृष्ट्वा वैदर्भः पृथिवीपतिः। प्रहर्षेण द्विजातिभ्यो न्यवेदयत भारत॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, as soon as she was born, seeing her, that ruler of earth, the king of Vidharbha communicated it to the Brahmanas in great joy.

sn: अभ्यनन्दन्त तां सर्वे ब्राह्मणा वसुधाधिप। लोपामुद्रेति तस्याश्च चक्रिरे नाम ते द्विजाः॥
en: O ruler of earth, all those Brahmanas blessed her and those twice born ones gave her the name of Lopamudra.

sn: ववृधे सा महाराज बिभ्रती रूपमुत्तमम्। अप्स्विवोत्पलिनी शीघ्रमग्नेरिव शिखा शुभा।॥
en: O king, possessed with great beauty that blessed girl began to grow quickly like a lotus in water or the blazing flame in a fire.

sn: तां यौवनस्थां राजेन्द्र शतं कन्याः स्वलंकृताः। दास्यः शतं च कल्याणीमुपातस्थुर्वशानुगाः॥
en: O king of kings, when she grew youthful, one hundred damsels adorned with ornaments and also one hundred maid-servants, remaining at her command always, waited upon that blessed girl.

sn: सा स्म दासीशतवृता मध्ये कन्याशतस्य च। आस्ते तेजस्विनी कन्या रोहिणीव दिवि प्रभा॥
en: Surrounded by these one hundred maidservants and remaining in the midst of these one hundred damsels, that effulgent damsel shone, as the brilliant Rohini (star) in the sky.

sn: यौवनस्थामपि च तां शीलाचारसमन्विताम्। न वव्रे पुरुषः कश्चिद् भयात् तस्य महात्मनः॥
en: When she grew youthful, even then for the fear of the illustrious king none dared ask for her hand, endued as she was with good and excellent manners.

sn: सा तु सत्यवती कन्या रूपेणाप्सरसोऽप्यति। तोषयामास पितरं शीलेन स्वजनं तथा॥
en: That truthful maiden possessed of beauty like that of an Apsara pleased her father and relatives with her good conduct.

sn: वैदर्भी तु तथायुक्तां युवतीं प्रेक्ष्य वै पिता। मनसा चिन्तयामास कस्मै दद्यामिमां सुताम्॥
en: Seeing her attain to puberty, her father, the king of Vidharbha thought in his mind, "To whom shall I give my this daughter?”

sn: लोमश उवाच यदा त्वमन्यतागस्त्यो गार्हस्थ्ये तां क्षमामिति। तदाभिगम्य प्रोवाच वैदर्भ पृथिवीपतिम्॥
en: Lomasha said : When Agastya thought that she had become fit for leading a domestic life, he went to the ruler of the earth, the king of Vidarbha and spoke to him thus.

sn: राजन् निवेशे बुद्धिर्मे वर्तते पुत्रकारणात्। वरये त्वां महीपाल लोपामुद्रां प्रयच्छ मे॥
en: O king, I have a mind to lead a domestic life for the sake of begetting offspring. O ruler of carth, therefore bestow on me Lopamudra; I solicit her.

sn: एवमुक्तः स मुनिना महीपालो विचेतनः। प्रत्याख्यानाय चाशक्तः प्रदातुं चैव नैच्छत॥
en: Having been thus addressed by the Rishi, that king fainted away. He was unable to refuse, though he was unwilling to give.

sn: ततः स भार्यामभ्येत्य प्रोवाच पृथिवीपतिः। महर्षिर्वीर्यवानेष क्रुद्धः शापाग्निना दहेत्॥
en: That ruler of earth then, going to his wife, said, "The great Rishi possesses great power. If angry, he can consumne us by the fire of his curse.

sn: तं तथा दुःखितं दृष्ट्वा सभार्यं पृथिवीपतिम्। लोपामुद्राभिगम्येदं काले वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Seeing the king with his wife afflicted with sorrow, Lopamudra coming to them at that time spoke these words.

sn: न मत्कृते महीपाल पीडामभ्येतुमर्हसि। प्रयच्छ मामगस्त्याय वाह्यात्मानं मया पितः॥
en: "O ruler of earth, you should not grieve on my account. O father, bestow me on Agastya and save yourself by giving me away."

sn: दुहितुर्वचनाद् राजा सोऽगस्त्याय महात्मने। लोपामुद्रां ततः प्रादाद् विधिपूर्वं विशाम्पते॥
en: O king, at the request of his daughter that king then bestowed Lopamudra on the illustrious Agastya with all due rites.

sn: प्राप्य भार्यामगस्त्यस्तु लोपामुद्रामभाषत। महार्हाण्युत्सृजैतानि वासांस्याभरणानि च॥
en: Having received Lopamudra as his wife, Agastya thus spoke to her. “Throw away these costly robes and ornaments."

sn: ततः सा दर्शनीयानि महार्हाणि तनूनि च। समुत्ससर्ज रम्भोरुर्वसनान्यायतेक्षणा॥ ततश्चीराणि जग्राह वल्कलान्यजिनानि च। समानवतचर्या च बभूवायतलोचना॥
en: Thereupon that large-eyed damsel of Rambha-like thighs threw away her costly and handsome robes of fine texture. That largeeyed lady then dressing herself in bark, skin and rags, became equal to her husband in vows and acts.

sn: गङ्गाद्वारमथागम्य भगवानृषिसत्तमः। उग्रमातिष्ठत तपः सह पल्यानुकूलया॥
en: Coming to the source of the Ganges that exalted one, that foremost of Rishis, began to perform severe austerities with his helpful wife.

sn: सा प्रीता बहुमानाच्च पतिं पर्यचरत् तदा। अगस्त्यश्च परां प्रीति भार्यायामचरत् प्रभुः॥
en: She being much pleased began to serve her. husband with great respect and the exalted Agastya also showed great love towards his wife.

sn: ततो बहुतिथे काले लोपामुद्रां विशाम्पते। तपसा द्योतितां स्नातां ददर्श भगवानृषिः॥ स तस्याः परिचारेण शौचेन च दमेन च। श्रिया रूपेण च प्रीतो मैथुनायाजुहाव ताम्॥
en: After a long time, O king, the illustrious Rishi one day saw Lopamudra, blazing in ascetic splendour, coming after a bath in her season. Being pleased with her service, with her purity, with her self-control, with her grace and beauty, he summoned her for the purpose of living with her.

sn: ततः सा प्राञ्जलिर्भूत्वा लज्जमानेव भाविनी। तदा सप्रणयं वाक्यं भगवन्तमथाब्रवीत्॥
en: Thereupon that lady in love and bashfulness spoke thus with joined hands to the exalted one.

sn: असंशयं प्रजाहेतोर्भार्यां पतिरविन्दत। या तु त्वयि मम प्रीतिस्तामृषे कर्तुमर्हसि॥
en: "The husband certainly narries a wife for the purpose of offspring. But O Rishi, you should show towards me that love which I bear for you.

sn: यथा पितुर्गृहे विप्र प्रासादे शयनं मम। तथाविधे त्वं शयने मामुपैतुमिहार्हसि॥
en: O Brahmana, you should come to me on a bed like the one in which I used to lie in my father's house, his palace.

sn: इच्छामि त्वां स्रग्विणं च भूषणैश्च विभूषितम्। उपसर्तुं यथाकामं दिव्याभरणभूषिता॥
en: I desire that you should be adorned with garlands of flowers and I too should be adorned with those celestials ornaments that I like.

sn: अन्यथा नोपतिष्ठेयं चीरकाषायवासिनी। नैवापवित्रो विप्रर्षे भूषणोऽयं कथंचन॥
en: O foremost of Brahmanas, I can not go to you with these rags dyed in red; to wear ornaments is never unholy.

sn: अगस्त्य उवाच न तेधनानि विद्यन्ते लोपामुद्रे तथा मम। यथाविधानि कल्याणि पितुस्तव सुमध्यमे॥
en: Agastya said: O Lopamudra, O blessed girl, O slenderwaisted maiden, I have not wealth like what your father possesses.

sn: लोपामुद्रोवाच ईशोऽसि तपसा सर्वं समाहर्तुं तपोधन। क्षणेन जीवलोके यद् वसु किंचन विद्यते॥
en: Lopamudra said : O great ascetic, by your ascetic prowess you can in a moment bring here all the wealth that exists in the world of men.

sn: अगस्त्य उवाच एवमेतद् यथाऽऽत्य त्वं तपोव्ययकरं तु तत्। यथा तु मे न नश्येत तपस्तन्मां प्रचोदय।॥
en: Agastya said: It is true what you say. But it would (simply) waste my ascetic merit. Bid me so do that which may not waste my ascetic merit.

sn: लोपामुद्रोवाच अल्पावशिष्टः कालोऽयमृतोर्मम तपोधन। न चान्यथाहमिच्छामि त्वामुपैतुं कथंचन॥
en: Lopamudra said : O great ascetic, my season will not last long. I do not desire to live with you at any other time.

sn: न चापिधर्ममिच्छामि विलोप्तुं तु कथंचन। एवं तु मे यथाकाम सम्पादयितुमर्हसि॥
en: I never also desire to diminish your virtue in any way. You should therefore do what I desire without injuring your virtue.

sn: अगस्त्य उवाच यद्येष कामः सुभगे तव बुद्ध्या विनिश्चितः। हर्तुं गछाम्यहं भद्रे चर काममिह स्थिता॥
en: Agastya said: O blessed girl, O fortunate one, if you make this resolve in your mind, then I will go out in search of wealth. Mean-while here as you like.

sn: लोमश उवाच ततो जगाम कौरव्य सोऽगस्त्यो भिक्षितुं वसु। श्रुतर्वाणं महीपालं यं वेदाभ्यधिकं नृपः॥
en: Lomasha said: O descendant of Kuru, then Agastya wept out to beg wealth from the king Shrutarvana who was considered to be richer than other kings.

sn: स विदित्वा तु नृपतिः कुम्भयोनिमुपागतम्। विषयान्ते सहामात्यः प्रत्यगृहणात् सुसत्कृतम्॥
en: Having learnt of the arrival of the pot-born Rishi on the frontier of his kingdom, the king went out with his ministers and received the holy man with all respects.

sn: तस्मै चार्घ्यं यथान्यायमानीय पृथिवीपतिः। प्राञ्जलिः प्रयतो भूत्वा पप्रच्छागमनेऽर्थिताम्॥
en: Having duly offered the Arghya, the king with joined hands, submissively inquired the reason of the Rishi's arrival.

sn: अगस्त्य उवाच वित्तार्थिनमनुप्राप्तं विद्धि मां पृथिवीपते। यथाशक्त्यविहिंस्यान्यान् संविभागं प्रयच्छ मे॥
en: Agastya said : O lord of earth, know, I have come to you for wealth. Give me a portion of your wealth according to your ability.

sn: लोमश उवाच तत आयव्ययौ पूर्णौ तस्मै राजा न्यवेदयत्। अतो विद्वन्नुपादत्स्व यदत्र वसु मन्यसे॥
en: Lomasha said: Telling him that his income and expenditure were the same, that king said "Take from my wealth whatever you please to take."

sn: तत आयव्ययौ दृष्ट्वा समौ सममतिर्द्विजः। सर्वथा प्राणिनां पीडामुपादानादमन्यत॥
en: Having seen that his income and expenditure are the same, that Rishi who always saw both sides with equal eyes thought that if he took anything (from that king's wealth), he would injure creatures.

sn: स श्रुतर्वाणमादाय नश्वमगमत् ततः। स च तौ विषयस्यान्ते प्रत्यगृहणाद् यथाविधि॥ तयोरय॑ च पाद्यं च ब्रनश्वः प्रत्यवेदयत्। अनुज्ञाप्य च पप्रच्छ प्रयोजनमुपक्रमे॥
en: Taking therefore Shrutarvana with him, he went to Bradhnashva. Having learnt of their arrival at the frontier of his kingdom he received them duly by offering them Arghya and water to wash their feet. He then with their permission inquired the reason of their coming.

sn: अगस्त्य उवाच वित्तकामाविह प्राप्तौ विद्ध्यावां पृथिवीपते। यथाशक्त्यविहिस्यान्यान् संविभागं प्रयच्छ नौ॥
en: Agastya said : O ruler of earth, know, I have come to you for wealth. Give me a portion of your wealth according to your ability,

sn: लोमश उवाच तत आयव्ययौ पूर्णौ ताभ्यां राजा न्यवेदयत्। अतो ज्ञात्वा तु गृहणीतं यदत्र व्यतिरिच्यते॥
en: Lomasha said: Thereupon the king, telling them that his income and the expenditure are the same, said “Knowing this, take from my wealth whatever you please to take."

sn: तत आयव्ययौ दृष्ट्वा समौ सममतिर्द्विजः। सर्वथा प्राणिनां पीडामुपादानामन्यत॥
en: Having seen that his income and expenditure were the same, the Rishi who always saw both sides with equal eyes thought if he took any thing from him he would injure other creatures.

sn: पौरुकुत्सं ततो जग्मुस्त्रसदस्युं महाधनम्। अगस्त्यश्च श्रुतर्वा च ब्रधनश्वश्च महीपतिः॥
en: Then Agastya, Shrutarvana and the king Bradnashva all went to Purukutsa's son Trasadasya of great wealth.

sn: त्रसदस्युस्तु तान् दृष्ट्वा प्रत्यगृहणाद् यथाविधि। अभिगम्य महाराज विषयान्ते महामनाः॥ अर्चयित्वा यथान्यायमिक्ष्वाकू राजसत्तमः। समस्तांश्च ततोऽपृच्छत् प्रयोजनमुपक्रमे॥
en: O great king, having learnt of their arrival at the frontier of his kingdom, the high-minded Trasadasyu went out and received them duly. That foremost of kings of the Ikshvaku race, having duly worshipped them, asked the reason of their coming.

sn: अगस्त्य उवाच वित्तकामानिह प्राप्तान् विद्धि नः पृथिवीपते। यथाशक्त्यविहिंस्यान्यान् संविभागं प्रयच्छ नः॥
en: Agastya said: O ruler of earth, know, that I have come to you for wealth. Give me a portion of your wealth according to your ability.

sn: लोमश उवाच तत आयव्ययौ पूर्णौ तेषां राजा न्यवेदयत्। एतज्ज्ञात्वा ह्यपादध्वं यदत्र व्यतिरिच्यते॥ तत् आयव्ययौ दृष्ट्वा समौ सममतिर्द्विजः। सर्वथा प्राणिनां पीडामुपादानादमन्यत॥
en: Lomasha said: Telling them that his income and expenditure were the same that king said, “knowing this take from my wealth whatever you please to take. Having seen that his income and expenditure were the same, the Rishi who saw both sides with equal eyes thought that if he took anything, he would injure other creatures.

sn: ततः सर्वे समेत्याथ ते नृपास्तं महामुनिम्। इदमूचुर्महाराज समवेक्ष्य परस्परम्॥
en: O great king, then all those monarchs looking at one another and speaking all together thus spoke to the great Rishi.

sn: अयं वै दानवो ब्रह्मन्निल्वलो वसुमान् भुवि। तमतिक्रम्य सर्वेऽद्य वयं चार्थामहे वसु॥
en: O Brahmana, there is a Danava on earth named Ilvala who of all persons possesses the largest wealth. Let us all go to day to him and ask wealth from him.

sn: लोमश उवाच तेषां तदासीदुचितमिल्वलस्यैव भिक्षणम्। ततस्ते सहिता राजनिल्वलं समुपाद्रवन्॥
en: O king, the suggestion to beg wealth from Ilyala appeared to them proper; and they all then went to Ilvala.

sn: लोमश उवाच इल्वलस्तान् विदित्वा तु महर्षिसहितान् नृपान्। उपस्थितान् सहामात्यो विषयान्ते ह्यपूजयत्॥
en: Lomasha said: Having learnt that those kings with the great Rishi had arrived at the frontier of his kingdom. Ilvala with all his relatives went out and worshipped them duly.

sn: तेषां ततोऽसुरश्रेष्ठस्त्वातिथ्यमकरोत् तदा। सुसंस्कृतेन कौरव्य भ्रात्रा वातापिना यदा॥
en: O descendant of Kuru, that foremost of Asuras received them with hospitality and entertained them with well cooked meat of his brother Vatapi (in the form of a goat).

sn: ततो राजर्षयः सर्वे विषण्णा गतचेतसः। वातापिं संस्कृतं दृष्ट्वा मेषभूतं महासुरम्॥
en: Thereupon seeing Vatapi, the great Asura cooked, all the royal sages were filled with grief and became as senseless.

sn: अथाब्रवीदगस्त्यस्तान् राजर्षीनृषिसत्तमः। विषादो वो न कर्तव्यो ह्यहं भोक्ष्ये महासुरम्॥ धुर्यासनमथासाद्य निषसाद महानृषिः। तं पर्यवेषद् दैत्येन्द्र इल्वलः प्रहसन्निव॥
en: Thereupon that foremost of Rishis Agastya said to those royal sages. “You ought not to grieve. I shall eat up the great Asura." When the great Rishi sat on an excellent seat in order to eat, the great Daitya Ilvala laughingly began to distribute the food.

sn: अगस्त्य एव कृत्स्नं तु वातापिं वुभुजे ततः। भुक्तवत्यसुरोऽऽह्वानमकरोत् तस्य चेल्वलः॥
en: Then Agastya eat up all the cooked meat of Vatapi. When the dinner was over the Asura Alluvial began to summon him (Vatapi).

sn: ततो वायुः प्रादुरभूदधस्तस्य महात्मनः। शब्देन महता तात गर्जन्निव यथा घनः॥
en: Thereupon, a child, (only a quantity of) wind came out of the stomach of the high-souled one with great a sound as that of the roaring clouds.

sn: वातापे निष्क्रमस्वेति पुनः पुनरुवाच ह। तं प्रहस्याब्रवीद् राजन्नगस्त्यो मुनिसत्तमः॥
en: He (Ilvala) again and again cried, “Vatapi,O Vatapi, come out.” Then that foremost of Rishis, Agastya laughingly said,

sn: कुतो निष्क्रमितुं शक्तो मया जीर्णस्तु सोऽसुरः। इल्वलस्तु विषण्णोऽभूद् दृष्ट्वा जीर्ण महासुरम्॥
en: "How can he come out? I have already digested that Asura." Seeing that great Asura digested, Ilvala became sad.

sn: प्राञ्जलिश्च सहामात्यैरिदं वचनमब्रवीत्। किमर्थमुपयाताः स्थ ब्रूत किं करवाणि वः॥
en: Joining his hands along with his ministers, he thus spoke, “What for have you come here? And what can I do for you?”

sn: प्रत्युवाच ततोऽगस्त्यः प्रहसन्निल्वलं तदा। ईशं सुर विद्मस्त्वां वयं सर्वेधनेश्वरम्॥
en: Thereupon Agastya smilingly thus replied, "O Asura, we know you to be possessed of great power and also enormous wealth.

sn: एते च नातिधनिनोधनार्थश्च महान् मम। यथाशक्त्यविहिंस्यान्यान् संविभागं प्रयच्छ नः॥
en: These kings are not very wealthy, but my necessity of wealth is great. Give us what you can without injuring any other.

sn: ततोऽभिवाद्य तमृषिमिल्वलो वाम्यमब्रवीत्। दित्सितं यदि वेत्सि त्वं ततो दास्यामि ते वसु॥
en: Thereupon (having been thus addressed) Ilvala saluted the Rishi and thus spoke to him, "If you can say what it is that I mean to give, then I shall give you wealth.

sn: अगस्त्य उवाच गवां दशसहस्राणि राज्ञामेकैकशोऽसुर। तावदेव सुवर्णस्य दित्सितं ते महासुर॥
en: Agastya said : O Asura, you have intended to give to each of these kings ten thousand kine and as many gold coins.

sn: मां ततो वै द्विगणं रथश्चैव हिरण्मयः। मनोजवौ वाजिनौ च दित्सितं ते महासुर॥
en: O great Asura, to me you have intended to give twice as much and a golden chariot and a couple of horses with the speed of mind.

sn: लोमश उवाच जिज्ञास्यमानः स रथः कौन्तेयासीद्धिरण्मयः। ततः प्रव्यथितो दैत्यो ददावभ्यधिकं वसु॥
en: Lomasha said: O son of Kunti, he (Ilvala) made inquired and learnt that the car was really made of gold. The Daitya then with a sad heart gave away much wealth.

sn: विरावश्च सुरावश्च तस्मिन् युक्तौ रथे हयौ। ऊहतुः सवसूनाशु तावगस्त्याश्रमं प्रति॥ अगस्त्येनाभ्यनुज्ञाता जग्मू राजर्षयस्तदा। कृतवांश्च मुनिः सर्वं लोपामुद्राचिकीर्षितम्॥
en: That car which are yoked the two horses, called Virava and Surava. O descendant of Bharata, these horses took those kings and Agastya and also all the wealth to the hermitage of Agastya within twinkling of an eye. Then obtaining Agastya's permission the royal sages went away to their respective cities. That Rishi (Agastya) did all that his wife Lopamudra had desired.

sn: लोपामुद्रोवाच कृतवानसि तत् सर्वं भगवन् मम काक्षितम्। उत्पादय सकृन्मह्यमपत्यं वीर्यवत्तरम्॥
en: Lopamudra said : O exalted one, you have accomplished all my desires. (Now) beget on me a greatly powerful and virtuous son.

sn: अगस्त्य उवाच तुष्टोऽहमस्मि कल्याणि तव वृत्तन शोभने। विचारणामपत्ये तु तव वक्ष्यामि तां शृणु।॥
en: Agastya said : O blessed one, O beautiful lady, I am pleased with your conduct. Listen to me as regards the proposal I make in respect of your son.

sn: सहस्रं तेऽस्तु पुत्राणां शतं वा दशसम्मितम्। दश वा शततुल्याः स्युरेको वापि सहस्रजित्॥
en: Do you desire to have one thousand sons or one hundred sons, each equal to one hundred or only one such who can conquer one thousand.

sn: लोपामुद्रोवाच सहस्रसम्मितः पुत्र एकोऽप्यस्तु तपोधन। एकोहि बहुभिः श्रेयान् विद्वान् साधुरसाधुभिः॥
en: Lopamudra said : O great ascetic, let me have one son equal to one thousand. One learned and good son is preferable to many bad ones.

sn: लोमश उवाच स तथेति प्रतिज्ञाय तया सम्भवन्मुनिः। समये समशीलिन्या श्रद्दावाञ्छ्रद्दधानया॥ तत आधाय गर्भं तमगमद् वनमेव सः। तस्मिन् वनगते गर्भो ववृधे सप्त शारदान्॥
en: Lomasha said: O King, saying “So be it”, that Rishi lived with reverence with his devoted wife of equal behaviour and then the Rishi) went away into the forest. After he had gone away to the forest, that conception grew on for seven years.

sn: सप्तमेऽब्दे गते चापि प्राच्यवत् स महाकविः। ज्वलन्निव प्रभावेण दृढस्युर्नाम भारत॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, when the seventh year passed, that highly learned man, called Dridasya came out of the womb blazing like fire.

sn: साङ्गोपनिषदान् वेदाञ्जपन्निव महातपाः। तस्य पुत्रोऽभवदृषेः स तेजस्वी महाद्विजः॥
en: That highly effulgent Brahmana, that great ascetic, took birth as that Rishi's (Agastya's) son, as if uttering the Vedas, Vedangas and the Upanishadas.

sn: स बाल एव तेजस्वी पितुस्तस्य निवेशने। इध्मानां भारमाजहे इध्मवाहस्ततोऽभवत्॥
en: Greatly powerful even in his childhood, he used to carry loads of sacrificial fuel to his father's house and hence he was called Idhmavaha.

sn: तथायुक्तं तु तं दृष्ट्वा मुमुदे स मुनिस्तदा। एवं स जनयामास भारतापत्यमुत्तमम्॥
en: Seeing him endued with such (prowess) that Rishi became very much pleased. O descendant of Bharata, thus did he beget that excellent son.

sn: लेभिरे पितरश्चास्य लोकान् राजन् यथेप्सितान्। तत अर्ध्वमयं ख्यातस्त्वगस्त्यस्याश्रमो भुवि॥
en: O king, by this his ancestors obtained the region they desired. From that time this place has become famous on earth as the hermitage of Agastya.

sn: प्राह्लादिरेवं वातापिरगस्त्येनोपशामितः। तस्यायमाश्रमो राजन् रमणीयैर्गुणैर्युतः॥
en: O king, this is that hermitage of Agastya who had killed Vatapi of the Prahrada race, the hermitage adorned with charming beauties.

sn: एषा भागीरथी पुण्या देवगन्धर्वसेविता। वातेरिता पताकेव विराजति नभस्तले॥
en: This sacred Bhagirathi frequented by the celestials and the Gandharvas rolls in like a person in the sky shaken by the gentle breeze.

sn: प्रतार्यमाणा कूटेषु यथा निम्नेषु नित्यशः। शिलातलेषु संत्रस्ता पन्नगेन्द्रवधूरिव॥
en: She flows onward on draggy crests (of hills), descending lower and lower, looking like a frightened female snake lying along the slopes of the hills.

sn: दक्षिणां वै दिशं सर्वां प्लावयन्ती च मातृवत्। पूर्वं शम्भोर्जटाभ्रष्टा समुद्रमहिषी प्रिया। अस्यां नद्यां सुपुण्यायां यथेष्टमवगाह्यताम्॥
en: Issuing first from the matted locks of Sambhu (Shiva), this favourite queen of the ocean floods the southern country, (thereby benefiting it) as a mother. Bathe freely in this highly sacred river.

sn: युधिष्ठिर निबोधेदं त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतम्। भृगोस्तीर्थं महाराज महर्षिगणसेवितम्॥
en: O Yudhishthira, O great king, behold the Bhrigu Tirtha, celebrated over the three worlds and frequented by the great Rishi.

sn: यत्रोपस्पृष्टवान् रामो हृतं तेजस्तदाऽऽप्तवान्। अत्र त्वां भ्रातृभिः सार्धं कृष्णया चैव पाण्डव॥
en: Bathing in it, Rama regained his lost prowess. O son of Pandu, bathing here with your brothers and Krishna (Draupadi).

sn: दुर्योधनहृतं तेजः पुनरादातुमर्हसि। कृतवैरेण रामेण यथा चोपहृतं पुनः॥
en: You should regain that effulgence which had been robbed from you by Duryodhana, as Rama regained his lost splendour by a hostile encounter (with Dashratha's son).

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच स तत्र भ्रातृभिश्चैव कृष्णाया चैव पाण्डवः। स्नात्वा देवान् पितॄश्चैव तर्पयामास भारत॥
en: Vaishampayana said : O descendant of Bharata, the Pandava (Yudhishthira) bathed there with his brothers and Krishna (Draupadi) and offered oblations to the Pitris and the celestials.

sn: तस्य तीर्थस्य रूपं वै दीप्ताद् दीप्ततरं बभौ। अप्रधृष्यतरवासीच्छात्रवाणां नरर्षभ॥
en: O foremost of men, after he had bathed there, his body blazed forth in brighter effulgence. and he became invincible to all foes,

sn: अपृच्छच्चैव राजेन्द्र लोमशं पाण्डुनन्दनः। भगवन् किमर्थं रामस्य हृतमासीद् वपुः प्रभो। कथं प्रत्याहृतं चैव एतदाचक्ष्व पृच्छतः॥
en: O king of kings, the son of Pandu (Yudhishthira) then thus spoke to Lomasha, "O exalted one, for what reason Rama's effulgence was robbed? How did he again regain it? I ask you, tell me everything.

sn: लोमश उवाच शृणु रामस्य राजेन्द्र भार्गवस्य चधीमतः। जातो दशरथस्यासीत् पुत्रो रामो महात्मनः॥ विष्णुः स्वेन शरीरेण रावणस्य वधाय वै। पश्यामस्तमयोध्यायां जातं दाशरथिं ततः॥
en: Lomasha said : O king of kings, listen to the history of Rama (Dasharatha's son) and also that of the intelligent (Parshurama), the descendant of Bhrigu. For the destruction of Ravana, Vishnu in his own body took his birth as the son of the illustrious Dasharatha. We then saw that son of Dasharatha when he had been born in Ayodhya.

sn: ऋचीकनन्दनो रामो भार्गवो रेणुकासुतः। तस्य दाशरथेः श्रुत्वा रामस्याक्लिष्टकर्मणः॥ कौतूहलान्वितो रामस्त्वयोध्यामगमत् पुनः। धनुरादाय तद् दिव्यं क्षत्रियाणां निबर्हणम्॥
en: Being impelled by curiosity, Rama, the descendant of Bhrigu, the son of Richika and Renuka, hearing of Rama, the son of Dasharatha of spotless deeds, went to Ayodhya, taking with him the bow so fatal to the Kshatriyas.

sn: जिज्ञासमानो रामस्य वीर्यं दाशरथेस्तदा। तं वै दशरथः श्रुत्वा विषयान्तमुपागतम्॥ प्रेषयामास रामस्य रामं पुत्रं पुरस्कृतम्। स तमभ्यागतं दृष्ट्वा उद्यतास्त्रमवस्थितम्॥ प्रहसनिव कौन्तेय रामो वचनमब्रवीत्। कृतकालं हि राजेन्द्रधनुरेतन्मया विभो॥
en: (With the intention of) ascertaining the prowess of Rama, the son of Dasharatha. Hearing that he had arrived at the frontier of his dominion, Dasharatha, sent his own son Rama to receive (Parshu) Rama with respect. Seeing him (Dasharatha's son) arrived and standing before him with upraised weapons, Rama, smilingly spoke these words to him, “O king of kings, O lord, O ruler of earth, string, if you can with all your strength, this bow in my hand which was made to destroy the Kshatriyas."

sn: समारोपय यत्नेन यदि शक्नोषि पार्थिव। इत्युक्तस्त्वाह भगवंस्त्वं नाधिक्षेप्तुमर्हसि॥
en: Having been thus addressed, he (Dasharatha's son) said, “O exalted one, you should not insult me thus.

sn: नाहमप्यधमोधर्मे क्षत्रियाणां द्विजातिषु। इक्ष्वाकूणां विशेषेण बाहुवीर्ये न कत्थनम्॥
en: I am amongst the twice-born not deficient in the virtue of the Kshatriya order. But the descendants of Ikshvaku never boast of their prowess of arms,

sn: तमेवंवादिनं तत्र रामो वचनमब्रवीत्। अलं वै व्यपदेशेनधनुरायच्छ राघव॥
en: To him who spoke thus, Rama replied in these words, “O descendant of Raghu, stop all your crafty speech. Take this bow."

sn: ततो जग्राह रोषेण क्षत्रियर्षभसूदनम्। रामो दाशरथिर्दिव्यं हस्ताद् रामस्य कार्मुकम्॥ धनुरारोपयामास सलील इव भारत। ज्याशब्दमकरोच्चैव स्मयमानः स वीर्यवान्॥
en: Thereupon the son of Dasharatha Rama took up in anger from the hands of (Parshu) Rama that celestials bow which destroyed the foremost of Kshatriyas. O descendant of Bharata, that greatly powerful hero stringed that bow without the least exertion and then he twanged it.

sn: तस्य शब्दस्य भूतानि वित्रसन्त्यशनेरिव। अथाब्रवीत् तदा रामो रामं दाशरथिस्तदा॥ इदमारोपितं ब्रह्मन् किमन्यत् करवाणि ते। तस्य रामो ददौ दिव्यं जामदग्न्यो महात्मनः। शरमाकर्णदेशान्तमयमाकृष्यतामिति॥
en: With its twang like that of the thunder he frightened all creatures. Thereupon Rama, the son of Dasharatha, thus spoke to (Parshu) Rama, “O Brahmana, here I have stringed the bow. What else shall I do for you?” Then the illustrious son of Jamadagni (Parshurama) gave to Rama a celestials arrow and said, “Please this to the bow-string and draw it to your ear.

sn: लोमश उवाच एतच्छ्रुत्वाब्रवीद् रामः प्रदीप्त इव मन्युना। श्रूयते क्षम्यते चैव दर्पपूर्णोऽसि भार्गव॥
en: Having heard this, Rama, blazing up in wrath, thus spoke to him, “O descendant of Bhrigu, I have heard what you have said and I have also pardoned you. You are full of vanity.

sn: त्वया ह्यधिगतं तेजः क्षत्रियेभ्यो विशेषतः। पितामहप्रसादेन तेन मां क्षिपसिध्रुवम्॥
en: You have acquired prowess superior to the Kshatriyas through the grace of the Grandsire (Brahma) and therefore you certainly insult me.!

sn: पश्य मां स्वेन रूपेण चक्षुस्ते वितराम्यहम्। ततो रामशरीरे वै रामः पश्यति भार्गवः॥ आदित्यान् सवसून् रुद्रान् साध्यांश्च समरुद्गणान्। पितरो हुताशनश्चैव नक्षत्राणि ग्रहास्तथा॥ गन्धर्वा राक्षसा यक्षा नद्यस्तीर्थानि यानि च। ऋषयो बालखिल्याश्च ब्रह्मभूताः सनातनाः॥ देवर्षयश्च कात्स्न्र्येन समुद्राः पर्वतास्तथा। वेदाश्च सोपनिषदो वषट्कारैः सहाध्वरैः॥ चेतोमन्ति च सामानिधनुर्वेदश्च भारत। मेघवृन्दानि वर्षाणि विद्युतश्च युधिष्ठिर॥
en: Behold me in my own original form; I give you sight.” Then the descendant of Bhrigu Rama saw in the body of Rama (Dasharatha's son). The Adityas, the Vasus, the Rudras, the Sadhyas, the Marutas, the Pitris, Hutashana (Fire), constellations, the planets. The Gandharvas, the Rakshashas, the Yakshas, the rivers, the Tirthas, those eternal Rishis who have become Brahma-like, namely Valakhilyas. The celestials Rishis, the seas, the mountains, the Vedas, the Upanishadas, the Vasishthas, the sacrifices, the Samas in their living forms. O descendant of Bharata Yudhishthira, the science of arms, the clouds with rain and lightning to saw in the body of Rama (Dasharatha's son).

sn: ततः स भगवान् विष्णुस्तं वै बाणं मुमोच ह। शुष्काशनिसमाकीर्णं महोल्काभिश्च भारत॥ पांसुवर्षेण महता मेघवर्षेश्च भूतलम्। भूमिकम्पैश्च निर्घातै दैश्च विपुलैरपि॥
en: Then the exalted Vishnu (Rama) shot that arrow. O descendant of Bharata at this the whole earth was filled with sounds of thunder and burning meteors flashed through the sky. Showers of dust and rain fell on the earth, earthquakes, whirl-winds of fearful sounds convulged everything.

sn: स रामं विह्वलं कृत्वा तेजश्चाक्षिष्य केवलम्। आगच्छज्ज्वलितो बाणो रामबाहुप्रचोदितः॥
en: Confounding (Parshu) Rama by the effulgence of the arrow shot by the hand of Rama, it came back blazing into his hand.

sn: स तु विह्वलतां गत्वा प्रतिलभ्य च चेतनाम्। रामः प्रत्यागतप्राणः प्राणमद् विष्णुतेजसम्॥ विष्णुना सोऽभ्यनुज्ञातो महेन्द्रमगमत् पुनः। भीतस्तु तत्र न्यवसद् व्रीडितस्तु महातपाः॥
en: (Parshu) Rama who had been thus deprived of his senses, then regaining his consciousness and receiving back (as it were) his life, bowed to the greatly effulgent Vishnu (Rama). Commanded by Vishnu he again went to the Mahendra mountain. The great ascetic lived there in fear and in shame.

sn: ततः संवत्सरेऽतीते हतौजसमवस्थितम्। निर्मदं दुःखितं दृष्ट्वा पितरो राममब्रुवन्॥
en: When one year passed away, seeing (Parshu) Rama deprived of prowess, his pride gone and himself in great affliction, the Pitris thus spoke to him,

sn: पितर ऊचुः न वै सम्यगिदं पुत्र विष्णुमासाद्य वै कृतम्। स हि पूज्यश्च मान्यश्च त्रिषु लोकेषु सर्वदा॥
en: “O son, in going to Vishnu, your conduct was not proper. He deserves to be worshipped and respected by the three worlds.

sn: गच्छ पुत्र नदी पुण्यां वधूसरकृताह्वयाम्। तत्रोपस्पृश्य तीर्थेषु पुनर्वपुरवाप्स्यसि॥
en: O son, go to the sacred river which is known by the name of Vadhusara. Bathing in all the Tirthas in that river, you will regain your old effulgence.

sn: दीप्तोदं नाम तत् तीर्थं यत्र ते प्रपितामहः। भृगुर्देवयुगे राम तप्तवानुत्तमं तपः॥
en: O Rama, therein is the Tirtha called Diptodaka where your grand father Bhrigu in the celestials age practised excellent austerities."

sn: तत् तथा कृतवान् रामः कौन्तेय वचनात् पितुः। प्राप्तवांश्च पुनस्तेजस्तीर्थेऽस्मिन् पाण्डुनन्दन॥
en: O son of Kunti, Rama did all that his ancestors had said. O son of Pandu, he regained his lost effulgence in this Tirtha.

sn: एतदीदृशकं तात रामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा। प्राप्तमासीन्महाराज विष्णुमासाद्य वै पुरा॥
en: O child, O great king, this was what happened in the days of yore to Rama of spotless deeds when he met with Vishnu.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच भूय एवाहमिच्छामि महर्षेस्तस्यधीमतः। कर्मणां विस्तरं श्रोतुमगस्त्यस्य द्विजोत्तम॥
en: Yudhishthira said: O foremost of Brahmanas, I desire to hear in detail more of the achicvements of the highly intelligent great Rishi Agastya.

sn: लोमश उवाच शृणु राजन् कथां दिव्यामद्भुतामतिमानुषीम्। अगस्त्यस्य महाराज प्रभावममितौजसः॥
en: Lomasha said : O king, O great monarch, listen to the excellent, wonderful and extraordinary account of Agastya and also about his immeasurably effulgent prowess.

sn: आसन् कृतयुगे घोरा दानवा युद्धदुर्मदाः। कालकेया इति ख्याता गणाः परमदारुणाः॥
en: There in the Treta Yuga were some fearful Danavas who were invincible in battle. They were known by the name of Kalkeyas and they possessed fearful prowess.

sn: ते तु वृत्रं समाश्रित्य नानाप्रहरणोद्यताः। समन्तात् पर्यधावन्त महेन्द्रप्रमुखान् सुरान्॥
en: Placing themselves under the command of) Vritra and arming themselves with various weapons, they pursued the celestials with Indra at their head to all directions.

sn: ततो वृत्रवधे यत्नमकुर्वंस्त्रिदशाः पुरा। पुरंदरं पुरस्कृत्य ब्रह्माणमुपतस्थिरे॥
en: Thereupon the celestials resolved upon the destruction of Vritra and they all went to Brahma with Purandra (Indra) at their head.

sn: कृताञ्जलींस्तु तान् सर्वान् परमेष्ठीत्युवाच ह। विदितं मे सुराः सर्वं यद् वः कार्यं चिकीर्पितम्॥
en: Seeing them all standing before him with joined hands. Parameshti (Brahma) thus spoke to them, “O celestials, I know all that you desire.

sn: तमुपायं प्रवक्ष्यामि यथा वृत्रं वधिष्यथा दधीच इति विख्यातो महानृषिरुदारधीः॥ तं गत्वा सहिताः सर्वे वरं वै सम्प्रयाचत। स वो दास्यतिधर्मात्मा सुप्रीतेनान्तरात्मना॥
en: I shall tell you the means by which Vritra will be killed. There is a highly intelligent great Rishi, well-known by the name of Dadhichi. Go to him all together and ask from him a boon. That Rishi, of virtuous mind and well pleased heart, will grant you the boon.

sn: स वाच्यः सहितैः सर्वैर्भवद्भिर्जयकाक्षिभिः । स्वान्यस्थीनि प्रयच्छेति त्रैलोक्यस्य हिताय वै॥
en: Desirous as you are of victory, go all together to him and tell him, "Give us your bones for the good of the three worlds."

sn: स शरीरं समुत्सृज्य स्वान्यस्थीनि प्रदास्यति। तस्यास्थिभिर्महाघोरं वज्रं संस्क्रियतां दृढम्॥
en: Giving up his body, he will give his bones to you. With those bones make a greatly fearful and strong weapon (to be called) Vajra (thunder).

sn: महच्छत्रुहणं घोरं षडधे भीमनिःस्वनम्। तेन वज्रेण वै वृत्रं वधिष्यति शतक्रतुः॥
en: It will have six sides, it will be fearful, it will make terrible roars, it will be able to destroy even the greatest enemies . With that Vajra, Shatakratu (Indra) will kill Vitra.

sn: एतद् वः सर्वमाख्यातं तस्माच्छीघ्रं विधीयताम्। एवमुक्तास्ततो देवा अनुज्ञाप्य पितामहम्॥ नारायणं पुरस्कृत्य दधीचस्याश्रमं ययुः। सरस्वत्याः परे पारे नानादुमलतावृतम्॥
en: I have told you all. Do all this without delay." Having been thus addressed, the celestials bidding farewell to the Grandsire (Brahima). Went to the hermitage of Dadhichi with Narada at their head. It (hermitage) stood on the opposite bank of the Sarasvati, covered with various plants and creepers.

sn: षट्पदोद्गीतनिनदैविघुष्टं सामगैरिव। पुंस्कोकिलरवोन्मिश्रं जीवं जीवकनादितम्॥
en: It resounded with the hum of bees as if they were reciting Samas. It echoed with the melodious notes of males Kokilas and Chakoras.

sn: महिषैश्च वराहैश्च सृमरैश्चमरैरपि। तत्र तत्रानुचरितं शार्दूलभयवर्जितैः॥
en: Buffaloes, bears, deer and Chamaras (cows) wandered there at pleasure without having any fear of tigers.

sn: करेणुभिर्वारणैश्च प्रभिन्नकरटामुखैः। सरोऽवगाडैः क्रीडद्भिः समन्तादनुनादितम्॥
en: Male elephants with juice trickling down from their rent temples sported with the female elephants in the streams and filled the place with their roars.

sn: सिंहव्यात्रैर्महानादानदगिरनुनादितम्। अपरैश्चापि संलीनैर्गुहाकन्दरशायिभिः॥ तेषु तेष्ववकाशेषु शोभितं सुमनोरमम्। त्रिविष्टपसमप्रख्यं दधीचाश्रममागमन्॥
en: The place echoed with the roars of lions and tigers. And here and there might be seen lions with grisly manes lying stretched in caves and glens, thus beautifying them with their presence. They then (celestials) came to the hermitage of Dadhichi which was like heaven itself.

sn: तत्रापश्यन् दधीचं ते दिवाकरसमद्युतिम्। जाज्वल्यमानं वपुषा यथा लक्ष्या पितामहम्॥
en: They saw there Dadhichi as effulgent as the sun and as blazing in the grace of person as the Grandsire (Brahma).

sn: तस्य पादौ सुरा राजन्नभिवाद्य प्रणम्य च। अयाचन्त वरं सर्वं यथोक्तं परमेष्ठिना॥
en: O king, bowing at his feet and saluting him, the celestials all together asked from him for the boon as directed by Parameshti (Brahma).

sn: ततो दधीचः परमप्रतीतः सुरोत्तमांस्तानिदमभ्युवाच। करोमि यद् वो हितमद्य देवाः स्वं चापि देहं स्वयमुत्सृजामि॥
en: Thereupon Dadhichi, becoming very much pleased and addressing those foremost of celestials said, “O celestials, I shall do today what is to your benefit. I shall even give up my body myself."

sn: स एवमुक्त्वा द्विपदां वरिष्ठः प्राणान् वशी स्वान् सहसोत्ससर्ज। ततः सुरास्ते जगृहुः परासोरस्थीनि तस्याथ यथोपदेशम्॥
en: Having said this, that foremost of men of subdued soul suddenly gave up his life. Thereupon the celestials took the bones of the dead Rishi, as they had been directed.

sn: स्त्वष्टारमागम्य तमर्षमूचुः। त्वष्टा तु तेषां वचनं निशम्य प्रहृष्टरूपः प्रयतः प्रयत्नात्॥
en: Then the celestials with glad heart went to Tvashtri (Vishwakarma) and told him the means of their victory. Tyashtri also hearing their words was filled with joy; and with great attention and care.

sn: चकार वज्रं भृशमुचरूपं कृत्वा च शक्रं स उवाच हृष्टः। अनेन वज्रप्रवरेण देव भस्मीकुरुष्वाद्य सुरारिमुचम्॥
en: He made the Vajra of greatly fearful, appearance. Having made it he cheerfully said to Sakra (Indra), “O god, with this best of weapons Vajra reduce today the fearful enemies of the celestials to ashes.

sn: ततो हतारिः सगणः सुखं वै प्रशाधि कृत्स्नं त्रिदिवं दिविष्ठः। त्वष्ट्रा तथोक्तस्तु पुरंदरस्तद् वज्रं प्रहृष्टः प्रयतो ह्यगृहणात्॥
en: O chief of the celestials, killing the foe rule happily the kingdom of heaven with your own friends." Having been thus addressed by Tvashtri Purandara (Indra) cheerfully took the Vajra from his hands with proper respects.

sn: लोमश उवाच ततः स वज्री बलिभिर्दैवतैरभिरक्षितः। आससाद ततो वृत्रं स्थितमावृत्य रोदसी॥
en: Lomasha said : Thereupon that wielder of Vajra (Indra) supported by the powerful celestials came to Vritra who was then occupying both the earth and the heaven.

sn: कालकेयैर्महाकायैः समन्तादभिरक्षितम्। समुद्यतप्रहरणैः सशृङ्गैरिव पर्वतैः॥
en: He was guarded on all sides by the huge bodied Kalkeyas with upraised weapons, looking like great mountains with towering peaks.

sn: ततो युद्धं समभवद् देवानां दानवैः सह। मुहूर्तं भरतश्रेष्ठ लोकत्रासकरं महत्॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, then a great battle appalling on the three worlds was fought by the celestials with the Danavas for a short while.

sn: उद्यतप्रतिपिष्टानां खङ्गानां वीरबाहुभिः। आसीत् सुतुमुलः शब्दः शरीरेष्वभिपात्यताम्॥
en: Loud was the clashing of swords upraised and warded off by the heroic hands, those that were aimed at one another's bodies.

sn: शिरोभिः प्रपतद्भिश्चाप्यन्तरिक्षान्महीतलम्। तालैरिव महाराज वृन्ताद् भ्रष्टैरदृश्यत॥
en: The heads began to fall from the sky on the earth like fruits of palmyra palm, falling on the ground loosened from their stalks.

sn: ते हेमकवचा भूत्वा कालेयाः परिघायुधाः। त्रिदशानभ्यवर्तन्त दावदग्धा इवाद्रयः॥
en: The Kaleyas, clad in golden armour and armed with iron mounted in aces rushed towards the celestials like moving mountains on fire.

sn: तेषां वेगवतां वेगं साभिमानं प्रधावताम्। न शेकुस्त्रिदशाः सोढुं ते भग्नाः प्राद्रवन् भयात्॥
en: Being unable to stand the onrush of those impetuous heroes, the celestials broke (their ranks) and fled away from fear.

sn: तान् दृष्ट्वा द्रवतो भीतान् सहस्राक्षः पुरंदरः। वृत्रे विवर्धमाने च कश्मलं महदाविशत्॥
en: Seeking them (the celestials) flying in fear and Vritra growing in boldness, the thousand eyed Purandra (Indra) was greatly confounded with fear.

sn: कालेयभयसंत्रस्तो देवः साक्षात् पुरंदरः। जगाम शरणं शीघ्रं तं तु नारायणं प्रभुम्॥
en: Filled with the fear of the Kalkeyas the deity Purandra (Indra) himself asked protection from the lord Narayana without delay.

sn: तं शक्रं कश्मलाविष्टं दृष्ट्वा विष्णुः सनातनः। स्वतेजो व्यदधाच्छने बलमस्य विवर्धयन्॥
en: The eternal Vishnu, seeing Sakra (Indra) confounded with fear and grief, enhanced his prowess by importing to him a portion of his own might.

sn: विष्णुना गोपितं शक्रं दृष्ट्वा देवगणास्ततः। सर्वे तेजः समादध्युस्तथा ब्रह्मर्षयोऽमलाः॥
en: Having seen Sakra (Indra) thus protected by Vishnu, all the celestials and the Brahmana Rishis of spotless deeds imparted to him their own might.

sn: स समाप्यायितः शक्रो विष्णुना दैवतैः सह। ऋषिभिश्च महाभागैर्बलवान् समपद्यता॥
en: Thus favoured by Vishnu by all the celestials and by the highly-blessed Rishis Sakra (Indra) became more powerful than before.

sn: ज्ञात्वा बलस्थं त्रिदशाधिपं तु ननाद वृत्रो महतो निनादान। तस्य प्रणादेनधरा दिशश्च खं द्यौर्नगाश्चापि चचाल सर्वम्॥
en: Knowing that the chief of the celestials had been filled with the prowess of others, Vitra sent forth fearful roars. The earth, the directions, the heaven and the mountains all began to tremble.

sn: ततो महेन्द्रः परमाभितप्तः श्रुत्वा रवं घोररूपं महान्तम्। भये निमग्नस्त्वरितो मुमोच वज्रं महत् तस्य वधाय राजन्॥
en: O king, thereupon hearing that fearful and loud roar, Indra was filled with grief and fear and in order to kill the Asura he hurled the great Vajra.

sn: स शक्रवज्राभिहतः पपात महासुरः काञ्चनमाल्यधारी। यथा महाशैलवरः पुरस्तात् स मन्दरो विष्णुकराद् विमुक्तः॥
en: Struck with Vajra, that great Asura adorned with garlands of gold, fell down as the great Mandara mountain did in the days of yore when hurled from the hand of Vishnu.

sn: तस्मिन् हते दैत्यवरे भयातः शक्रः प्रदुद्राव सरः प्रवेष्टुम्। वज्रं स मेने न कराद् विमुक्तं वृत्रं भयाच्चापि हतं न मेने॥
en: When that foremost of Daityas was killed, even then Sakra (Indra) fled away in fear to take shelter in a lake, thinking that the Vajra had not been hurled from his hands and that Vitra had not (really) been killed.

sn: सर्वे च देवा मुदिताः प्रहृष्टा महर्षयश्चेन्द्रभिष्टुवन्तः। सर्वांश्च दैत्यांस्त्वरिताः समेत्य जघ्नुः सुरा वृत्रवधाभितप्तान्॥
en: The celestials and the great Rishis were all filled with joy and they cheerfully sang the praise of Indra. Then the celestials mustering together began to kill all the Daityas who grew dejected by the death of Vitra.

sn: तैस्त्रास्यमानास्त्रिदशैः समेतैः समुद्रमेवाविविशुर्भयार्ताः। प्रविश्य चैवोदधिमप्रमेयं झषाकुलं नक्रसमाकुलं च॥
en: Struck with panic at the sight of the assembled celestials, they entered the fathomless ocean, full of fishes and alligators. They (the Danavas) assembled together with pride began to conspire for the destruction of the three worlds.

sn: स्त्रैलोक्यनाशार्थमभिस्मयन्तः। स्तांस्तानुपायानुपवर्णयन्ति॥
en: Some among them who were wise suggested some courses of action, each according to his own judgment.

sn: तेषां तु तत्र क्रमकालयोगाद् घोरा मतिश्चिन्तयतां बभूव। स्तेषां विनाशः प्रथमं तु कार्यः॥
en: In course of time they made the fearful resolution that they should first destroy all persons' knowledge and ascetic virtues.

sn: लोका हि सर्वे तपसा ध्रियन्ते तस्मात् त्वरध्वं तपसः क्षयाय। ये सन्ति केचिच्च वसुंधरायां तपस्विनोधर्मविदश्च तज्ज्ञाः॥
en: "The worlds are all supported by asceticism, therefore lose no time to destroy asceticism. All those men who are on earth endued with ascetic virtues and with the knowledge of the precepts of virtue and that of Brahma.

sn: तेषां वधः क्रियतां क्षिप्रमेव तेषु प्रणष्टेषु जगत् प्रणष्टम्। एवं हि सर्वे गतबुद्धिभावा जगद्विनाशे परमप्रहृष्टाः॥
en: Should be soon destroyed, for when they are destroyed, the whole universe will be destroyed.” Having arrived at this resulting for the destruction of the universe, they became exceedingly glad.

sn: दुर्गं समाश्रित्य महोमिमन्तं रत्नाकरं वरुणस्यालयं स्म॥
en: Then they made the ocean, with the mountain, like waves, the abode of Varuna, their fort.

sn: लोमश उवाच समुद्रं ते समाश्रित्य वारुणं निधिसम्भसः। कालेयाः सम्प्रवर्तन्त त्रैलोक्यस्य विनाशने॥
en: Lomasha said : Living in the ocean, the abode of Varuna, the Kalkeyas began their operations for the destruction of the worlds.

sn: ते रात्रौ समभिक्रुद्धा भक्षयन्ति सदा मुनीन्। आश्रमेषु च ये सन्ति पुण्येष्वायतनेषु च॥
en: They began to devour in the night in anger the Rishis (they found) in the hermitages and in the holy spots.

sn: वसिष्ठस्याश्रमे विप्रा भक्षितास्तैर्दुरात्मभिः। अशीतिः शतमष्टौ च नव चान्ये तपस्विनः॥
en: Those wicked-minded Daityas devoured one hundred and eighty Brahmanas and also ascetics in the hermitage of Vasishtha.

sn: च्यवनस्याश्रमं गत्वा पुण्यं द्विजनिषेवितम्। फलमूलाशनानां हि मुनीनां भक्षितं शतम्॥
en: Going to the sacred hermitage hermitage of Chayavana, frequented by the Brahmanas, they devoured one hundred Rishis who lived on fruits and roots.

sn: एवं रात्रौ स्म कुर्वन्ति विविशुश्चार्णवं दिवा। भरद्वाजाश्रमे चैव नियता ब्रह्मचारिणः॥ वाय्वाहाराम्बुभक्षाश्च विंशतिः संनिषूदिताः। एवं क्रमेण सर्वांस्तानाश्रमान् दानवास्तदा॥
en: They thus acted during the night and during the day they entered into the sea. They devoured in the hermitage of Bharadvaja two Brahmanas of subdued soul and of Brahmachari life, living on air and water only. In this way did the Danavas one after another (invade) all the hermitages.

sn: निशायां परिबाधन्ते मत्ता भुजबलाश्रयात्। कालोपसृष्टाः कालेया घ्नन्तो द्विजगणान् बहून्॥
en: Being intoxicated with prowess of arms and their lives nearly run out, the Kalkeyas destroyed many Brahmanas.

sn: न चैनानन्वबुध्यन्त मनुजा मनुजोत्तम। एवं प्रवृत्तान् दैत्यांस्तांस्तापसेषु तपस्विषु॥
en: O foremost of men, the Danavas acted in this way towards the ascetics in their ascetic retreats. Yet men could not discover them.

sn: प्रभाते समदृश्यन्त नियताहारकर्शिताः। महीतलस्था मुनयः शरीरैर्गतजीवितैः॥
en: Every morning people saw lying on the ground the dead bodies of Rishis who were emaciated for living on frugal diet.

sn: क्षीणमांसैविरुधिरैर्विमज्जान्त्रैविसंधिभिः। आकीर्णैराबभौ भूमिः शङ्खानामिव राशिभिः॥
en: Many of those bodies were without flesh or blood. without entrails and with limbs separated from one another. Here and there lay heaps of bones like heaps of conch-shells.

sn: कलशैविप्रविबैश्च सुवैर्भग्नैस्तथैव च। विकीर्णैरग्निहोत्रैश्च भूर्बभूव समावृता॥
en: The earth was scattered over with the (sacrificial) contents of broken jars and shattered ladles for pouring libations of ghee and with the sacred fires kept with care by the ascetics.

sn: नि:स्वाध्यायवषट्कारं नष्टयज्ञोत्सवक्रियम्। जगदासीनिरुत्साहं कालेयभयपीडितम्॥
en: The universe, being afflicted with the terror of the Kalkeyas and being destitute of the Vedic studies, of the Vashats and the sacrificial festivals and religious rites, became very fearless.

sn: एवं संक्षीयमाणाश्च मानवा मनुजेश्वर। आत्मत्राणपराभीताः प्राद्रवन्त दिशो भयात्॥
en: O ruler of men, when men began to perish in this way, the survivors fled for their lives in all directions.

sn: केचिद् गुहा: प्रविविशुर्निर्झरांश्चापरे तथा। अपरे मरणोद्विग्ना भयात् प्राणान् समुत्सृजन्॥
en: Some fled to caverns and some behind mountain streams and springs and some through fear of death gave up their lives.

sn: केचिदत्र महेष्वासाः शूराः परमहर्षिताः। मार्गमाणाः परं यत्नं दानवानां प्रचक्रिरे॥
en: Those among them who were bow-men and heroes cheerfully went out and took great trouble of find out the Danavas.

sn: न चैतानधिजग्मुस्ते समुद्रं समुपाश्रितान्। श्रमं जग्मुश्च परममाजग्मुः क्षयमेव च॥
en: Failing to find them, for the Asuras had taken shelter in the bottom of the ocean, they came back to their homes greatly aggrieved.

sn: जगत्युपशमं याते नष्टयज्ञोत्सवक्रिये। आजग्मुः परमामाति त्रिदशा मनुजेश्वर॥
en: O ruler of men, when the universe was being thus destroyed and when sacrificial festivals and religious rites were all destroyed, the celestials were filled with great afflictions.

sn: समेत्य समहेन्द्राश्च भयान्मन्त्रं प्रचक्रिरे। शरण्यं शरणं देवं नारायणमजं विभुम्॥
en: Assembling all together with Indra in their midst, they consulted with one another out of fcar. They asked protection from the increate and exalted deity, Narayana.

sn: तेऽभिगम्य नमस्कृत्य वैकुण्ठमपराजितम्। ततो देवाः समस्तास्ते तदोचुर्मधुसूदनम्॥
en: Going to that unvanquished lord of Vaikuntha and bowing to that slayer of Madhu, the celestials thus addressed him,

sn: त्वं न स्रष्टा च भर्ता च हर्ता च जगतः प्रभो। त्वया सृष्टमिदं विश्वं यच्चेङ्गं यच् नेङ्गति॥
en: “O lord, you are the creator, the protector and the destroyer of the universe as well as of ourselves. It is you who have created this universe with all its mobile creatures.

sn: त्वया भूमिः पुरा नष्टा समुद्रात् पुष्करेक्षण। वाराहं वपुराश्रित्य जगदर्थे समुद्धृता॥
en: O lotus-eyed deity, it is you who in the days of yore assuming the form of a boar raised the sunken earth from the sea for the benefit of all creatures.

sn: आदिदैत्यो महावीर्यो हिरण्यकशिपुः पुरा। नारसिंहं वपुः कृत्वा सूदितः पुरुषोत्तम॥
en: O foremost of Purushas, assuming the form of Narasimha (half man and half lion) you killed in the days of yore the ancient and greatly powerful Daityas, called Hiranayakashipu.

sn: अवध्यः सर्वभूतानां बलिश्चापि महासुरः। वामनं वपुराश्रित्य त्रैलोक्याद् भ्रंशितस्त्वया॥
en: There was a great Asura named Bali, incapable of being killed by any crcature. Assuming the form of a dwarf, you exiled him from the three worlds.

sn: असुरश्च महेष्वासो जम्भ इत्यभिविश्रुतः। यज्ञक्षोभकरः क्रूरस्त्वयैव विनिपातितः॥
en: It is by you that wicked Asura called Jambha who was a powerful bow-man and v.ho always obstructed sacrifices was killed.

sn: एवमादीनि कर्माणि येषां संख्या न विद्यते। अस्माकं भयभीतानां त्वं गतिर्मधुसूदन॥
en: Your acts are like those which, O slayer of Madhu, cannot be counted. You are the refuge of all who are afflicted with fear.

sn: तस्मात् त्वां देवदेवेश लोकार्थं ज्ञापयामहे। रक्ष लोकांश्च देवांश्च शक्रं च महतो भयात्॥
en: O god of gods, it is for this we tell you what is our present trouble. Save the worlds, the celestials and Indra also from this great fear.

sn: देवा ऊचुः तव प्रसादाद् वर्धन्ते प्रजाः सर्वाश्चतुर्विधाः। ता भाविता भावयन्ति हव्यकव्यैर्दिवौकसः।१।।
en: The celestials said : All the four orders of creatures increase through your favour. They propitiate the dwellers of heaven with the offering of Habya and Kabya (sacrificial libations to the gods and oblations to the Pitris).

sn: लोका ह्येवं विवर्धन्ते ह्यन्योन्यं समुपाश्रिताः। त्वत्प्रसादान्निरुद्विग्नास्त्वयैव परिरक्षिताः॥ इदं च समनुप्राप्तं लोकानां भयमुत्तमम्। न च जानीम केनेमे रात्रौ वध्यन्ति ब्राह्मणाः॥
en: Thus being protected by you and freed from troubles, people through your favour increase depending on one arrother. Now this great fear has overtaken the people. We do not know by whom the Brahmanas are killed at night.

sn: क्षीणेषु च ब्राह्मणेषु पृथिवी क्षयमेष्यति। ततः पृथिव्यां क्षीणायां त्रिदिवं क्षयमेष्यति॥
en: If the Brahmanas are destroyed, the world will be also destroyed. If the world is destroyed, heaven itself will be destroyed.

sn: त्वत्प्रसादान्महाबाहो लोकाः सर्वे जगत्पते। विनाशं नाधिगच्छेयुस्त्वया वै परिरक्षिताः॥
en: O mighty armed lord of the universe, let not, through your favour, people, protected as they are by you, meet with destruction.

sn: विष्णुरुवाच विदितं मे सुराः सर्वं प्रजानां क्षयकारणम्। भवतां चापि वक्ष्यामि शृणुध्वं विगतज्वराः॥
en: Vishnu said: O celestials, I know the reason of the destruction of all creatures. I shall tell you all about it. Having your mind freed form anxiety listen to it.

sn: कालेय इति विख्यातो गणः परमदारुणः। तैश्च वृत्रं समाश्रित्य जगत् सर्वं प्रमाथितम्॥
en: There are a fearful class (of Danavas) wellknown by the name of Kalkeyas. Placing Vritra at their head, they devasted the Universe.

sn: ते वृत्रं निहतं दृष्ट्वा सहस्राक्षेणधीमता। जीवितं परिरक्षन्तः प्रविष्टा वरुणालयम्॥
en: Having seen Vritra killed by the greatly intelligent deity of one thousand eyes (Indra), they entered into the ocean) the abode of Varuna, to save their lives,

sn: ते प्रविश्योदधिं घोरं नक्रग्राहसमाकुलम्। उत्सादनार्थं लोकानां रात्रौ घ्नन्ति ऋषीनिह॥
en: Having entered the fearful ocean full of sharks and crocodiles, they (now) kill the Rishis at night with the intention of exterminating all creatures.

sn: न तु शक्या: क्षयं नेतुं समुद्राश्रयगा हि ते। समुद्रस्य क्षये बुद्धिर्भवद्भिः सम्प्रधार्यताम्॥
en: But they cannot be killed, as they have taken shelter under the sea. You should therefore find out some means to dry up the ocean.

sn: अगस्त्येन विना को हि शक्तोऽन्योऽर्णवशोषणे। अन्यथा हि न शक्यास्ते विना सागरशोषणम्॥
en: Except Agastya, who else is capable of drying up the ocean? Without drying up the ocean, they cannot be assailed by any other ineans.

sn: एतच्छ्रुत्वा तदा देवा विष्णुना समुदाहृतम्। परमेष्ठिनमाज्ञाप्य अगस्त्यस्याश्रमं ययुः॥
en: Having heard these words of Vishnu about the drying up of the ocean, they took the permission of Parameshti (Brahma) and went to the hermitage of Agastya.

sn: तत्रापश्यन् महात्मानं वारुणिं दीप्ततेजसम्। उपास्यमानमृषिभिर्देवैरिव पितामहम्॥
en: There they saw the high-souled son of Varuna, of blazing effulgence, waited upon by the Rishis, as Brahma is waited upon by the celestials.

sn: तेऽभिगम्य महात्मानं मैत्रावरुणिमच्युतम्। आश्रमस्थं तपोराशि कर्मभिः स्वैरभिष्टुवन्॥
en: Going to the high-souled and undeteriorating son of Mitra and Varuna (Agastya) Seated in his hermitage as a man of ascetic merits, they sang his glory by reciting his deeds.

sn: देवा ऊचुः नहुषेणाभितप्तानां त्वं लोकानां गतिः पुरा। भ्रंशितश्च सुरैश्वार्यात् स्वर्लोकाल्लोककण्टकः॥
en: The celestials said: You became in the days of yore the refuge of creatures when they were oppressed by Nahusha. Deprived of his heaven's affluence, he was thrown down, a thorn of the heaven as he was, from the celestials region.

sn: क्रोधात् प्रवृद्धः सहसा भास्करस्य नगोत्तमः। वचस्तवानतिक्रामन् विन्ध्यः शैलो न वर्धते॥
en: That foremnost of mountains Vindhya being angry with the sun, suddenly in the days of yore) began to increase its height, but he has ceased to increase, as he could not disobey your command.

sn: तमसा चावृते लोके मृत्युनाभ्यर्दिताः प्रजाः। त्वामेव नाथमासाद्य निर्वृत्तिं परमां गताः॥
en: When darkness covered the world, creatures were oppressed by death; but having got you as a protector, they obtained the greatest security.

sn: अस्माकं भयभीतानां नित्यशो भगवान् गतिः। ततस्त्वार्ताः प्रयाग्रमो वरं त्वां वरदो ह्यसि॥
en: O exalted one, whenever we are beset with danger, it is you from whom we ask for a boon, for you always grant the boon asked of you.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच किमर्थं सहसा विथ्यः प्रवृद्धः क्रोधमूर्छितः। एतदिच्छाम्यहं श्रोतुं विस्तरेण महामुने॥
en: Yudhishthira said : O great Rishi, I am desirous of hearing why Vindhya (mountain), made senseless with anger, suddenly began to increase its bulk.

sn: लोमश उवाच अद्रिराजं महाशैलं मेरुं कनकपर्वतम्। उदयास्तमने भानुः प्रदक्षिणमवर्तत॥
en: Lomasha said : The sun between his rising and setting went round that king of mountains, that great golden mountain named Meru.

sn: तं तु दृष्ट्वा विध्यः शैल: सूर्यमथाब्रवीत्। यथा हि मेरुर्भवता नित्यशः परिगम्यते॥ प्रदक्षिणश्च क्रियते मामेवं कुरु भास्कर। एवमुक्तस्ततः सूर्यः शैलेन्द्र प्रत्यभाषत॥ नाहमात्मेच्छया शैलं करोम्येनं प्रदक्षिणम्। एष मार्गः प्रदिष्टो मे यैरिदं निर्मितं जगत्॥
en: Seeing this, the Vindhya inountain spoke thus to the sun, “As you every day go round Meru and honour him, O sun, so do you the sarne by going round me.” Having been thus addressed, the sun thus replied to that king of mountains. "O mountain, I do not walk round it out of my own desire. He who has created this universe has assigned this path to me.”

sn: एवमुक्तस्ततः क्रोधात् प्रवृद्धः सहसाचलः। सूर्याचन्द्रमसोर्मागं रोद्भुमिच्छन् परंतप॥
en: Having been thus addressed, the mountain, O chastiser of foes, desiring to obstruct the path of the sun and the moon, suddenly began to increase its bulk in anger.

sn: ततो देवाः सहिताः सर्व एव विन्ध्यं समागम्य महाद्रिराजम्। निवारयामासुरुपायतस्तं न च स्म तेषां वचनं चकार॥
en: Thereupon all the assembled celestials came to Vindhya, the great king of mountains and tried to dissuade him from what he was doing. But he did not heed their words.

sn: अथाभिजग्मुर्मुनिमाश्रमस्थं तपस्विनधर्मभृतां वरिष्ठम्। अगस्त्यमत्यद्भुतवीर्यवन्तं तं चार्थमूचुः सहिताः सुरास्ते॥
en: Then the assembled celestials all went to the Rishi living in his hermitage, that ascetic, that foremost of virtuous men, the wonderfully powerful Agastya; and they told him all.

sn: देवा ऊचुः सूर्याचन्द्रमसोर्मागं नक्षत्राणां गतिं तथा। शैलराजो वृणोत्येष विन्ध्यः क्रोधवशानुगः॥ तं निवारयितुं शक्तो नान्यः कश्चिद् द्विजोत्तम्। ऋते त्वां हि महाभाग तस्मादेनं निवारय॥
en: The celestials said: The king of mountains, Vindhya, giving way to anger, is obstructing the path of the sun and the moon and the course of the stars. O best of Brahimanas, O greatly exalted one, except you there is none who can prevent him from doing it.

sn: तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं विप्रः सुराणां शैलमभ्यगात्। सोऽभिगम्याब्रवीद् विन्ध्यं सदारः समुपस्थितः॥
en: Lomasha said : Having heard the words of the celestials, the Brahmana went to the mountain. Going there with his wife, he spoke thus to Vindhya.

sn: मार्गमिच्छाम्यहं दत्तं भवता पर्वतोत्तम। दक्षिणामभिगन्तास्मि दिशं कार्येण केनचित्॥
en: "O foremost of mountains, I wish to have a path given to me by you, as I intend to go to the southern country for some purpose.

sn: यावदागमनं मह्यं तावत् त्वं प्रतिपालय। निवृत्ते मयि शैलेन्द्र ततो वर्धस्व कामतः॥
en: O king of mountains, wait till I return, you can then increase your bulk as much as you like."

sn: एवं स समयं कृत्वा विन्ध्येनामित्रकर्शन। अद्यापि दक्षिणाद् देशाद् वारुणिर्न निवर्तते॥
en: O chastiser of foes, having made this agreement with Vindhya, (he went away) and up to the present day the son of Varuna (Agastya) has not returned from the southern country.

sn: एतत् ते सर्वमाख्यातं यथा विन्ध्यो न वर्धते। अगस्त्यस्य प्रभावेण यन्मां त्वं परिपृच्छसि॥
en: Thus have I narrated to you, as you asked me to do, why Vindhya does not increase its bulk on account of the prowess of Agastya.

sn: कालेयास्तु यथा राजन् सुरैः सर्वैर्निषूदिताः। अगस्त्याद् वरमासाद्य तन्मे निगदतः शृणु॥
en: O king, now hear how the Kalkeyas were destroyed by the celestials when they obtained their prayer from Agastya.

sn: त्रिदशानां वचः श्रुत्वा मैत्रावरुणिरब्रवीत्। किमर्थमभियाताः स्थ वरं मत्तः कमिच्छथा एवमुक्तास्ततस्तेन देवता मुनिमब्रुवन्॥
en: Having heard the words of the celestials, the son of Mitra and Varuna said, “Why have you come? What boon do you solicit from me?” Having been thus addressed, the celestials said to the Rishi.

sn: एवं त्वयेच्छाम कृतं हि कार्य महार्णवं पीयमानं महात्मन्। ततो वधिष्याम सहानुबन्धान् कालेयसंज्ञान् सुरविद्विषस्तान्॥
en: O "high-souled one, we desire this act to be done by you, namely to drink up the ocean. Then we shall be able to kill these enemies of the celestials, known by the name of Kalkeyas, along with their followers."

sn: त्रिदशानां वचः श्रुत्वा तथेति मुनिरब्रवीत्। करिष्ये भवतां कामं लोकानां च महत् सुखम्।।१९।
en: Having heard the words of the celestials, the Rishi said, "So be it. I shall do what you desire and also that which would be beneficial to the world."

sn: एवमुक्त्वा ततोऽगच्छत् समुद्रं सरितां पतिम्। ऋषिभिश्च तपःसिद्धैः सार्धं देवैश्च सुव्रत॥ समुद्रं भीमनिः
en: O vow-observing man, having said this, he then went to the lord of rivers, the ocean, accompanied by the Rishis who had become successful in asceticism and by the celestials.

sn: मनुष्योरगगन्धर्वयक्षकिंपुरुषास्तथा। अनुजग्मुर्महात्मानं द्रष्टुकामास्तदद्भुतम्॥
en: Men, snakes, Gandharvas, Yakshas and Kinnaras followed the high-souled (Rishi), with the desire of seeing that wonderful feat.

sn: ततोऽभ्यगच्छन् सहिताः :स्वनम्। नृत्यन्तमिव चोर्मीभिर्वल्गन्तमिव वायुना॥ हसन्तमिव फेनौधैः स्खलन्तं कन्दरेषु च। नानाग्राहसमाकीर्णं नानाद्विजगणान्वितम्॥
en: They then all came to the fearfully roaring ocean which was as it were dancing with billows made by the winds and was, as it were laughing with masses of froth, created by the dashing of waves at the mountain cave. It was full of different water animals and birds.

sn: अगस्त्यसहिता देवाः सगन्धर्वमहोरगाः। ऋषयश्च महाभागाः समासेदुर्महोदधिम्॥
en: The celestials, the Gandharvas, the great Nagas, the greatly exalted Rishis, all came with Agastya to the great ocean.

description: Consultations about the refilling of the Ocean
sn: लोमश उवाच समुद्रं स समासाद्य वारुणिर्भगवानृषिः। उवाच सहितान् देवानृषींश्चैव समागतान्॥
en: Lomasha said: Coming to the ocean, the exalted Rishi, the son of Varuna thus spoke to the assembled celestials and the Rishis, who had come with him.

description: Consultations about the refilling of the Ocean
sn: अहं लोकहितार्थं वै पिबामि वरुणालयम्। भवद्भिर्यदनुष्ठेयं तच्छीघ्रं संविधीयताम्॥
en: "For the good of the world, I shall drink up this abode of Varuna (ocean). You should at once make the preparations which devolves upon you to make."

description: Consultations about the refilling of the Ocean
sn: एतावदुक्त्वा वचनं मैत्रावरुणिरच्युतः। समुद्रमपिबत् क्रुद्धः सर्वलोकस्य पश्यतः॥
en: Having spoken these few words, the undeteriorating son of Mitra and Varuna began in wrath to drink up the ocean in the sight of all the world.

description: Consultations about the refilling of the Ocean
sn: पीयमानं समुद्रं तं दृष्ट्वा सेन्द्रास्तदामराः। विस्मयं परमं जग्मुः स्तुतिभिश्चाप्यपूजयन्॥
en: Seeing how the ocean was being drunk up, Indra and the other immortals were filled with great astonishment; and they began to adore him by reciting his praises.

description: Consultations about the refilling of the Ocean
sn: त्वं नस्त्राता विधाता च लोकानां लोकभावना त्वत्प्रसादात् समुच्छेदं न गच्छेत् सामरं जगत्॥
en: (They said) “O protector of the world you our Saviour and you are the creator of the world. Through your favour the universe with the immortals may be saved from extermination."

description: Consultations about the refilling of the Ocean
sn: स पूज्यमानस्त्रिदशैर्महात्मा गन्धर्वतूर्येषु नदत्सु सर्वशः। दिव्यैश्च पुष्पैरवकीर्यमाणो महार्णवं नि:सलिलं चकार॥
en: Being thus worshipped by the celestials while the musical instruments of the Gandharvas played all around and celestials blossoms were showered on him, that highsouled (Rishi) made the great ocean waterless.

description: Consultations about the refilling of the Ocean
sn: दृष्ट्वा कृतं नि:सलिलं महार्णवं सुराः समस्ताः परमप्रहृष्टाः। प्रगृह्य दिव्यानि वरायुधानि तान् दानवाञ्जनुरदीनसत्त्वाः॥
en: Seeing the great ocean made waterless, all the celestials were filled with joy; and taking up various celestials weapons they began to kill the Danayas with courageous hearts.

description: Consultations about the refilling of the Ocean
sn: महाबलैर्वेगिभिरुन्नदद्भिः। न सेहिरे वेगवतां महात्मनां वेगं तदाधारयितुं दिवौकसाम्॥
en: Being attacked by the high-souled and greatly powerful, swift-coursing and loudly roaring celestials, they (the Danavas) were unable to withstand the on set of those swift and courageous dwellers of heaven.

description: Consultations about the refilling of the Ocean
sn: ते वध्यमानास्त्रिदशैर्दानवा भीमनि:स्वनाः। चक्रुः सुतुमुलं युद्धं मुहूर्तमिव भारत॥
en: O descendant of the Bharata, those loudly roaring Danavas, being thus attacked by the celestials, fought a great battle for a moment.

description: Consultations about the refilling of the Ocean
sn: ते पूर्वं तपसा दग्धा मुनिभिर्भावितात्मभिः। यतमानाः परं शक्त्या त्रिदशैर्विनिषूदिताः॥
en: But they had been already burnt by the force of the penances of pure-souled Rishis (whom they had killed). Therefore though they tried their utmost, they were all killed by the celestials.

description: Consultations about the refilling of the Ocean
sn: ते हेमनिष्काभरणा: कुण्डलाङ्गदधारिणः। निहता बह्वशोभन्त पुष्पिता इव किंशुकाः॥
en: Adorned as they were with golden ornaments and earrings, they (the Danavas), when killed, looked as beautiful as the Palasha tree when full of blossoms.

description: Consultations about the refilling of the Ocean
sn: हतशेषास्ततः केचित् कालेया मनुजोत्तम। विदार्य वसुधां देवीं पातालतलमास्थिताः॥
en: O best of men, the remnant of those Kalkeyas that were not killed, took shelter in the nether regions after having rent the goddess Earth.

description: Consultations about the refilling of the Ocean
sn: निहतान् दानवान् दृष्ट्वा त्रिदशा मुनिपुङ्गवम्। तुष्टुवुर्विविधैर्वाक्यैरिदं वचनमब्रुवन्॥
en: Seeing the Danavas destroyed, the celestials gratified that foremost of Rishis (Agastya) with various speeches; and they then thus spoke,

description: Consultations about the refilling of the Ocean
sn: त्वत्प्रसादान्महाभागलोकैः प्राप्तं महत् सुखम्। त्वत्तेजसा च निहताः कालेयाः क्रूरविक्रमाः॥
en: “O mighty-armed one, through your favour the world has obtained great happiness. The greatly powerful Kalkeyas are all destroyed by your might.

description: Consultations about the refilling of the Ocean
sn: पूरयस्व महाबाहो समुद्रं लोकभावन। यत् त्वया सलिलं पीतं तदस्मिन् पुनरुत्सृज्॥
en: O mighty-armed one and O saviour of the world, fill up the Ocean (again). Give up the water drunk by you."

description: Consultations about the refilling of the Ocean
sn: एवमुक्तः प्रत्युवाच भगवान् मुनिपुङ्गवः। जीर्णं तद्धि मया तोयमुपायोऽन्यः प्रचिन्त्यताम्॥ पूरणार्थं समुद्रस्य भवद्भिर्यत्नमास्थितैः। एतच्छ्रुत्वा तु वचनं महर्षे वितात्मनः॥ विस्मिताश्च विषण्णाश्च बभूवुः सहिताः सुराः। परस्परमनुज्ञाप्य प्रणम्य मुनिपुङ्गवम्॥
en: Having been thus addressed, the exalted great Rishi thus replied. “The water has been digested by me. Think of other means, if you are willing to fill up the ocean with water." Having heard those words of that high-souled grcat Rishi, the assembled celestials, were all filled with wonder and also with sorrow, Bidding farewell to one another and bowing to the great Rishi.

description: Consultations about the refilling of the Ocean
sn: प्रजाः सर्वा महाराज विप्रजग्मुर्यथागतम्। त्रिदशा विष्णुना साधुमुपजग्मुः पितामहम्॥
en: All creatures went away whence they came. The celestials with Vishnu went to the Grandsire (Brahma).

description: Consultations about the refilling of the Ocean
sn: पूरणार्थं समुद्रस्य मन्त्रयित्वा पुनः पुनः। ऊचुः प्राञ्जलय: सर्वे सागरस्याभिपूरणम्॥
en: Having again and again held consultations in order to fill up again the ocean, they thus spoke with joined hands about the refilling of the ocean.

sn: लोमश उवाच तानुवाच समेतांस्तु ब्रह्मा लोकपितामहः। गच्छध्वं विबुधाः सर्वे यथाकामं यथेप्सितम्॥
en: Lomasha said: The Grandsire of creatures Brahma thus spoke to the assembly (of celestials) “O gods, go wherever you like and desire to go.

sn: महता कालयोगेन प्रकृतिं यास्यतेऽर्णवः। ज्ञातीश्च कारणं कृत्वा महाराजो भगीरथः॥ पूरयिष्यति तोयौघैः समुद्र निधिमम्भसाम्।
en: A very long time must pass before the ocean would be able to resume its natural state by making the relatives of the great king Bhagiratha as its cause."

sn: पितामहवचः श्रुत्वा सर्वे विबुधसत्तमाः। कालयोगं प्रतीक्षन्तो जग्मुश्चापि यथागतम्॥
en: Having heard the words of the Grandsire, all those foremost of celestials went away where they liked and they waited for the time (when the ocean would be refilled).

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच कथं वै ज्ञातयो ब्रह्मन् कारणं चात्र किं मुने। कथं समुद्रः पूर्णश्च भगीरथप्रतिश्रयात्॥
en: Yudhishthira said : O Brahmana, O Rishi, why and how did the relations (of Bhagiratha) become the cause (of refilling the ocean)? How was the ocean refilled by the interference of Bhagiratha?

sn: एतदिच्छाम्यहं श्रोतुं विस्तरेण तपोधन। कथ्यमानं त्वया विप्र राज्ञां चरितमुत्तमम्॥
en: O ascetic, O Brahmana, I desire to hear all this in detail, the excellent history of that king (Bhagiratha) narrated by you.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्तस्तु विप्रेन्द्रोधर्मराज्ञा महात्मना। कथयामास माहात्म्यं सगरस्य महात्मनाः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having been thus addressed by the highsouled Dharmaraja, Yudhishthira, that foremost of Brahmanas narrated the glory of the illustrious Sagara.

sn: लोमश उवाच इक्ष्वाकूणां कुले जातः सगरो नाम पार्थिवः। रूपसत्त्वबलोपेतः स चापुत्रः प्रतापवान्॥
en: Lomasha said: In the race of the Ikshvaku there was born a king, named Sagara, possessing beauty of person and prowess. That mighty king was son-less.

sn: स हैहयान् समुत्साद्य तालजङ्घांश्च भारत। वशे च कृत्वा राजन्यान् स्वराज्यमन्वशासत॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, exterminating the Haihayas and Talrangas and subjugating many kings, he ruled over his own kingdom.

sn: तस्य भार्ये त्वभवतां रूपयौवनदर्पिते। वैदर्भी भरतश्रेष्ठ शैब्या च भरतर्षभ॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, he had two wives, proud of their beauty and of their youth, one a princess of Vaidarbhi and the other a princess of Shaibya.

sn: स पुत्रकामो नृपतिस्तप्यते स्म महत्तपः। पत्नीभ्यां सह राजेन्द्र कैलासं गिरिमाश्रितः॥
en: O king of kings, desiring to get a son, that king practised great austerities with his two wives on the Kailasa mountain.

sn: स तप्यमानः सुमहत् तपो योगसमन्वितः। आससाद महात्मानं त्र्यक्षं त्रिपुरमर्दनम्॥ शंकरं भवमीशानं शूलपाणिं पिनाकिनम्। त्र्यम्बकं शिवमुग्रेशं बहुरूपमुमापतिम्॥
en: Being engaged in great austerities and in Yoga and in contemplation, he saw the illustrious three-eyed deity, the chastiser of Tripura, Shankara, Bhava, Ishana, Pinaki, Shulapani, Traymbaka, Shiva, Ugresha of many forms, the husband of Uma.

sn: स तं दृष्ट्वैव वरदं पत्नीभ्यां सहितो नृपः। प्रणिपत्य महाबाहुः पुत्रार्थे समयाचत॥ तं प्रीतिमान् हरः प्राह सभार्यं नृपसत्तमम्। यस्मिन् वृतो मुहूर्तेऽहं त्वयेह नृपते वरम्॥
en: As soon as he saw that giver of boons, that mighty-armed king bowed to him along with his two wives and prayed for a son. Hara (Shiva) being pleased said to that best of kings with his wives. “O king, considering the moment in which you have asked the boon.

sn: षष्टिः पुत्रसहस्राणि शूराः परमदर्पिताः। एकस्यां सम्भविष्यन्ति पल्यां नरवरोत्तम॥ ते चैव सर्वे सहिताः क्षयं यास्यन्ति पार्थिव। एको वंशधरः शूर एकस्यां सम्भविष्यति॥
en: O foremost of men, sixty thousand heroic and proud sons will be born in one of your two wives. O ruler of men, they will all together meet with destruction. In the other wife will be born a heroic son who will perpetuate your race."

sn: एवमुक्त्वा तु तं रुद्रस्तत्रैवान्तरधीयत। स चापि सगरो राजा जगाम स्वं निवेशनम्॥
en: Having said this, Rudra (Shiva) then and there disappeared. The king Sagara also went back to his own abode.

sn: पत्नीभ्यां सहितस्तत्र सोऽतिहृष्टमनास्तदा। तस्य ते मनुजश्रेष्ठ भार्ये कमललोचने॥ वैदर्भी चैव शैब्या च गर्भिण्यौ सम्बभूवतुः। ततः कालेन वैदर्भी गर्भालावं व्यजायत॥
en: Accompanied by his two wives who were exceedingly glad at heart. O foremost of men, he returned' home. His two lotus-eyed wives, the princesses of Vaidarbhi and of Shaibya conceived. In due time, the Vidarbha princess gave birth to a gourd.

sn: शैब्या च सुषुवे पुत्रं कुमारं देवरूपिणम्। तदालावू समुत्स्रष्टुं मनश्चक्रे स पार्थिवः॥
en: The princess of Shaibya gave birth to a son as handsome as a celestials. That king then thought of throwing away the gourd.

sn: अथान्तरिक्षाच्छुश्राव वाचं गम्भीर निःस्वनाम्। राजन् मा साहसं कार्षीः पुत्रान् न त्यक्तुमर्हसि॥
en: But he heard a voice in the sky uttered in a grave and solcinn voice; it said "O king, do not be guilty of this hasty acts. You should not abandon your sons.

sn: अलावुमध्यान्निष्कृष्य बीजं यलेन गोप्यताम्। सोपस्वेदेषु पात्रेषु घृतपूर्णेषु भागशः॥
en: Take out the seeds from the gourd and let inem be preserved with care in họt vessels partly filled with Ghee.

sn: ततः पुत्रसहस्राणि षष्टिं प्राप्स्यसि पार्थिव। महादेवेन दिष्टं ते पुत्रजन्म नराधिप। अनेन क्रमयोगेन मा ते बुद्धिरतोऽन्यथा।॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, you will then get sixty thousand sons in this manner. Let not your mind be diverted.

sn: लोमश उवाच एतच्छ्रुत्त्वान्तरिक्षाच्च स राजा राजसत्तमः। यथोक्तं तच्चकाराथ श्रद्दधद् भरतर्षभ॥
en: Lomasha said : O best of the Bharata race, having heard these words uttered in the sky, that foremost of kings reverentially did all that he was directed to do.

sn: एकैकशस्ततः कृत्वा बीजं बीजं नराधिपः। घृतपूर्णेषु कुम्भेषु तान् भागान् विदधे ततः॥
en: That ruler of men took out separately each one of the seeds and he then kept these divisions (of the gourd) in vessels filled with Ghee.

sn: धात्रीश्चैकैकशः प्रादात् पुत्ररक्षणतत्परः। ततः कालेन महता समुत्तस्थुर्महाबलाः॥ षष्टिः पुत्रसहस्राणि तस्याप्रतिमतेजसः। रुद्रप्रसादाद् राजर्षेः समजायन्त पार्थिव॥
en: Being anxious to save the son, he placed one nurse in charge of one vessel. Then after a long time there were born greatly powerful and exceedingly effulgent sixty thousand sons. O king, they were born to that royal sage through the favour of Rudra (Shiva).

sn: ते घोराः क्रूरकर्माण आकाशपरिसर्पिणः। बहुत्वाच्चावजानन्तः सर्वांल्लोकान् सहामरान्।।५
en: They were fierce, they were prone to do wicked acts, they were able to ascend to and roam about in the sky. Being numerous themselves, they disturbed all creatures including the immortals.

sn: त्रिदशांश्चाप्यबाधन्त तथा गन्धर्वराक्षसान्। सर्वाणि चैव भूतानि शूराः समरशालिनः॥
en: Those heroes, ever fond of fight, chased even the celestials, the Gandharvas the Rakshashas and all other creatures.

sn: वध्यमानास्ततो लोकाः सागरैर्मन्दबुद्धिभिः। ब्रह्माणं शरणं जग्मुः सहिताः सर्वदैवतैः॥
en: Persecuted by the wicked-minded sons of Sagara, all creatures with all the celestials went to ask protection from Brahma.

sn: तानुवाच महाभागः सर्वलोकपितामहः। गच्छध्वं त्रिदशा: सर्वे लोकैः सार्धं यथागतम्॥
en: To them said the greatly cxalted Grandsire of all creatures, “O celestials, go back whence you came with all these creatures.

sn: नातिदीर्पण कालेन सागराणां क्षयो महान्। भविष्यति महाघोरः स्वकृतैः कर्मभिः सुराः॥
en: Within a very short time, exceedingly fearful destruction of Sagara's heroic sons will take place through their own misdeeds.

sn: एवमुक्तास्तु ते देवा लोकाश्च मनुजेश्वर। पितामहमनुज्ञाप्य विप्रजग्मुर्यथागतम्॥
en: O ruler of men, having been thus addressed, the celestials and the other creatures, bidding farewell to the Grandsire, went back to the place whence they had come.

sn: ततः काले बहुतिथे व्यतीते भरतर्षभ। दीक्षितः सगरो राजा हयमेधेन वीर्यवान्॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, after a long time, the mighty king Sagara installed himself for the performance of a horse-sacrifice.

sn: तस्याश्वो व्यचरद् भूमिं पुत्रैः स परिरक्षितः। समुद्रं स समासाद्य निस्तोयं भीमदर्शनम्॥ रक्ष्यमाणः प्रयत्नेन तत्रैवान्तरधीयत। ततस्ते सागरास्तात हृतं मत्वा हयोत्तमम्॥ आगम्य पितुराचख्युरदृश्यं तुरगं हृतम्। तेनोक्ता दिक्षु सर्वासु सर्वे मार्गत वाजिनम्॥
en: His horse, guarded by his sons, roamed over the world. Going to the fearful and waterless ocean. It disappeared there, though it was guarded with all care. O child, they thought that the excellent horse had been robbed. Going (back) to their father, they told him how the horse had disappeared and had been stolen. He (Sagara) said, “Go and search the horse in all directions."

sn: ततस्ते पितुराज्ञाय दिक्षु सर्वासु तं हयम्। अमार्गन्त महाराज सर्वं च पृथिवीतलम्॥
en: O great king, at the command of their father, they searched for the horse in all directions and all over the world.

sn: ततस्ते सागराः सर्वे समुपेत्य परस्परम्। नाध्यगच्छन्त तुरगमश्वहर्तारमेव च॥
en: Thereupon the sons of Sagara mutually united together could not find the horse nor the person who had stolen it.

sn: आगम्य पितरं चोचुस्ततः प्राञ्जलयोऽग्रतः। ससमुद्रवनद्वीपा सनदीनदकन्दरा॥ सपर्वतवनोद्देशा निखिलेन मही नृप। अस्माभिर्विचिता राजञ्छासनात् तव पार्थिव॥ न चाश्वमधिगच्छामो नाश्वहर्तारमेव च। श्रुत्वा तु वचनं तेषां स राजा क्रोधमूछितः॥
en: Coming to their father, they spoke to him with joined hands, "O king, O ruler of earth, O protector of men, at your command we have searched the whole earth with its seas, forests, islands, with its rivers and caves, with its mountains and forest lands, but we could not find cither the horse or the thief who had stolen it.” Having heard their words, the king grew senseless in anger.

sn: उवाच वचनं सर्वांस्तदा दैववशानृप। अनागमाय गच्छध्वं भूयो मार्गत वाजिनम्॥
en: O king, impelled by Destiny, he spoke to them thus, “Go away, never return. O sons, search again for the horse in all directions.

sn: यज्ञियं तं विना ह्यश्वं नागन्तव्यं हि पुत्रकाः। प्रतिगृह्य तु संदेशं पितुस्ते सगरात्मजाः॥ भूय एव महीं कृत्स्ना विचेतुमुपचक्रमुः। अथापश्यन्त ते वीराः पृथिवीमवदारिताम्॥
en: Without that sacrificial horse never return again." Accepting the command of their father, those sons of Sagara, once more began to search for the horse all over the world. The heroes saw a pit on the surface of the earth.

sn: समासाद्य बिलं तच्चाप्यखनन् सगरात्मजाः। कुद्दालैर्तेषुकैश्चैव समुद्रं यत्नमास्थिताः॥
en: Having seen that pit, the sons of Sagara axes they dug on in the sea with the greatest efforts.

sn: स खन्यमानः सहितैः सागरैर्वरुणालयः। अगच्छत् परमामार्ति दीर्यमाण: समन्ततः॥
en: That abode of Varuna (ocean), being thus dug by the united sons of Sagara and also rent and cut on all sides, found itself in the greatest possible distress.

sn: असुरोरगरक्षांसि सत्त्वानि विविधानि च। आर्तनादमकुर्वन्त वध्यमानानि सागरैः॥
en: Being killed by the sons of Sagara, the Asuras, the Nagas, the Rakshashas and various other living creatures raised up distressful cries.

sn: छिन्नशीर्षा विदेहाश्च भिन्नवगस्थिसंधयः। प्राणिनः समदृश्यन्त शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः॥
en: Hundreds and thousands of living creatures were seen with severed heads, with separated trunks, with their skin, bones and joints rent asunder.

sn: एवं हि खनतां तेषां समुद्रं वरुणालयम्। व्यतीत: सुमहान् कालो न चाश्वः समदृश्यत॥
en: Thus they dug on the ocean, the abode of Varuna, but a long period of time passed away and still the horse was not found.

sn: ततः पूर्वोत्तरे देशे समुद्रस्य महीपते। विदार्य पातालमथ संक्रुद्धाः सगरात्मजाः॥
en: O ruler of men, the sons of Sagara then dug the sea in anger on its north eastern region till they reached the nether region.

sn: अपश्यन्त हयं तत्र विचरन्तं महीतले। कपिलं च महात्मानं तेजोराशिमनुत्तमम्। तेजसा दीप्यमानं तु ज्वालाभिरिव पावकम्॥
en: They then saw that the horse was roaming there on the surface of the ground. (They also saw) the illustrious Kapila, a perfect mass of great effulgence. He was blazing in splendour like a blazing fire.

sn: ते तं दृष्ट्वा हयं राजन् सम्प्रहृष्टतनूरुहाः। अनादृत्य महात्मानं कपिलं कालचोदिताः॥
en: Having seen him and the horse, they were flushed with delight. Being impelled by Fate, they did not care the presence of the illustrious Kapila.

sn: संक्रुद्धाः सम्प्रधावन्त अश्वग्रहणकाक्षिणः। ततः क्रुद्धो महाराज कपिलो मुनिसत्तमः॥
en: Being eager to get the horse, they ran towards it in anger. O great king, thereupon that foremost of Rishis, Kapila, grew angry.

sn: वासुदेवेति यं प्राहुः कपिलं मुनिपुङ्गवम्। स चक्षुर्विकृतं कृत्वा तेजस्तेषु समुत्सृजन्॥
en: Kapila whom the great Rishis called Vasudeva assumed a fiery look and shot flames from his eyes.

sn: ददाह सुमहातेजा मन्दबुद्धीन् स सागरान्। तान् दृष्ट्वा भस्मसाद् भूतान् नारदः सुमहातपाः॥ सगरान्तिकमागच्छत् तच्च तस्मै न्यवेदयत्। स तच्छ्रुत्वा वचो घोरं राजा मुनिमुखोद्गतम्॥ मुहूर्तं विमना भूत्वा स्थाणोर्वाक्यमचिन्तयत्। अंशुमन्तं समाहूय असमञ्जःसुतं तदा॥ पौत्रं भरतशार्दूल इदं वचनमब्रवीत्। षष्टिस्तानि सहस्राणि पुत्राणाममितौजसाम्॥ कापिलं तेज आसाद्य मत्कृते निधनं गताः। तव चापि पिता तात परित्यक्तो मयानघ। धर्म संरक्षमाणेन पौराणां हितमिच्छता॥
en: That greatly effulgent one burnt down those foolish-minded sons of Sagara. Having seen them reduced to ashes, the great ascetic Narada came to Sagara and told him all that had happened. Having heard those terrible words, uttered from the lips of the Rishi, the king (Sagara) remained unconscious for some time; he then thought of the words of Sthanu (Shiva). Then calling Anshuman, the son of Asamanjasa his grandson, O best of Bharata race, he spoke these words. "My sixty thousands immeasurably powerful sons, falling under the effulgence of Kapila, has met with their death on my account. O child, O sinless one, your father also has been abandoned by me from my desire to protect the citizens and to save my virtue.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच किमर्थं राजशार्दुल: सगरः पुत्रमात्मजम्। त्यक्तवान् दुस्त्यजं वीरं तन्मे ब्रूहि तपोधन॥
en: Yudhishthira said : O great ascetic, tell me why that foremost of kings, Sagara abandoned his own heroic son, a son who was not fit to be abandoned?

sn: लोमश उवाच असमञ्जा इति ख्यातः सगरस्य सुतो ह्यभूत्। यं शैब्या जनयामास पौराणां स हि दारकान्॥ गलेषु क्रोशतो गृह्य नद्यां चिक्षेप दुर्बलान्। ततः पौरा: समाजग्मुर्भयशोकपरिप्लुताः॥ सगरं चाभ्यभाषन्त सर्वे प्राञ्जलयः स्थिताः। त्वं नस्त्राता महाराज परचक्रादिभिर्भयात्॥
en: Lomasha said: The son of Sagara who was born of Shaibya and who was called Asamanjasa used to seize by the throat the weak children of the citizens and to throw them into the river while screaming. Thereupon the citizens overwhelmed with grief and fear all met together and with joined hands they thus prayed to Sagara, "O great king, you are our protector from the fear of an attack from the hostile force.
