sn: अत्र वै भरतो राजा राजन् क्रतुभिरिष्टवान्। हयमेधेन यज्ञेन मेध्यमश्वमवासृजत्॥ असकृत् कृष्णसारङ्गंधर्मेणाप्य च मेदिनीम्। अत्रैव पुरुषव्याघ्र मरुत्तः सत्रमुत्तमम्॥ प्राप चैवर्षिमुख्येन संवर्तेनाभिपालितः। अत्रोपस्पृश्य राजेन्द्र सर्वा ल्लोकान् प्रपश्यति। पूयते दुष्कृताच्चैव अत्रापि समुपस्पृश॥
en: O monarch, king Bharata performed sacrifices here. To perform a horse-sacrifice, he here set free the horse which was the intended victim and which was marked with black strips. He ruled the earth with righteousness. O foremost of men, here did Maruta, protected by Samvarata the foremost of Rishis, succeed in performing excellent sacrifices. O king of kings, bathing here one obtains all the regions. He is purified from all his evil deeds. Therefore bathe at this place.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तत्र सभ्रातृकः स्नात्वा स्तूयमानो महर्षिभिः। लोमशं पाण्डवश्रेष्ठ इदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said: Being praised by the great Rishis he (Yudhishthira) bathed there with his brothers. Then that foremost of the Pandavas thus spoke to Lomasha.

sn: सर्वाल्लोकान् प्रपश्यामि तपसा सत्यविक्रम। इहस्थः पाण्डवश्रेष्ठं पश्यामि श्वेतवाहनम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said: O greatly powerful Rishis, I see all the worlds by virtue of asceticism. I also see that foremost of the Pandavas Svetavahana (Arjuna).

sn: लोमश उवाच एवमेतन्महाबाहो पश्यन्ति परमर्षयः। सरस्वतीमिमां पुण्यां पुण्यैकशरणावृताम्॥
en: Lomasha said: O mighty-armed hero, it is as you say. Thus do great Rishis see (all the worlds). Yonder is the sacred Sarasvati, thronged by persons who consider her to be their sole refuge.

sn: यत्र स्नात्वा नरश्रेष्ठधूतपाप्मा भविष्यसि। इह सारस्वतैर्यज्ञैरिष्टवन्तः सुरर्षयः। ऋषयश्चैव कौन्तेय तथा राजर्षयोऽपि च॥
en: O foremost of men, bathing in it, you will be freed from all your sins. O son of Kunti, the celestials Rishis performed here the Sarasvata sacrifice; so did the Rishis and the royal sages.

sn: वेदी प्रजापतेरेषा समन्तात् पञ्चयोजना। कुरोर्वै यज्ञशीलस्य क्षेत्रमेतन्महात्मनः॥
en: This is the altar of the Prajapati; it is five yojanas in extent on all sides round. This is the field of the high-souled Kurus who always performed sacrifices.

description: History of the hawk and pigeon
sn: लोमश उवाच इह मास्तनूस्त्यक्तवा स्वर्गं गच्छन्ति भारता मर्तुकामा नरा राजनिहायान्ति सहस्रशः॥
en: Lomasha said: O descendant of Bharata, if men give up their bodies here, they go to heaven. O king, thousands of men come here with the desire to die.

description: History of the hawk and pigeon
sn: एवमाशीः प्रयुक्ता हि दक्षेण यजता पुरा। इह ये वै मरिष्यन्ति ते वै स्वर्गजितो नराः॥
en: A blessing was pronounced here by Daksha when in the days of yore he was performing sacrifice at this spot. (It was as follows), “The men that will die here will go to heaven.”

description: History of the hawk and pigeon
sn: एषा सरस्वती रम्या दिव्या चौघवती नदी। एतद् विनशनं नाम सरस्वत्या विशाम्पते॥
en: O king, here is the charming celestials river full of water, named Sarasvati. It is here Vinasana of the Sarasvati (where she disappeared).

description: History of the hawk and pigeon
sn: द्वारं निषादराष्ट्रस्य येषां दोषात् सरस्वती। प्रविष्टा पृथिवीं वीर मा निषादा हि मां विदुः॥
en: O hero, here is the gate of the kingdom of the Nishadas; it is from the hatred of the Nishadhas that the Sarasvati entered the earth so that she might not be seen by the Nishadas.

description: History of the hawk and pigeon
sn: एष वै चमसोद्देदो यत्र दृश्या सरस्वती। यौनामभ्यवर्तन्त सर्वाः पुण्याः समुद्रगाः॥
en: Here is also Chamashodbheda where the Sarasvati again reappeared. Here she was joined by all the other sacred ocean-going currents.

description: History of the hawk and pigeon
sn: एतत् सिन्धोर्महत् तीर्थं यत्रागस्त्यमरिंदम्। लोपामुद्रा समागम्य भर्तारमवृणीत वै॥
en: O chastiser of foes, here is the greatly sacred place called Sindhu, where Lopamudra accepted the great Rishi Agastya as her husband.

description: History of the hawk and pigeon
sn: एतत् प्रकाशते तीर्थं प्रभासं भास्कराते। इन्द्रस्य दयितं पुण्यं पवित्रं पापनानम्॥
en: O sun-like effulgent hero, here is the sacred Tirtha called Pravasha which is truly sacred, sin-destroying and a favourite place of Indra.

description: History of the hawk and pigeon
sn: एतद् विष्णुपदं नाम दृश्यते तीर्थमुत्तमम्। एषा रम्या विपाशा च नदी परमपावनी॥
en: Yonder appears the excellent Tirtha called Vishnupada. Here also is the charming river and greatly purifying Vipasa.

description: History of the hawk and pigeon
sn: अत्र वै पुत्रशोकेन वसिष्ठो भगवानृषिः। बद्ध्वाऽऽत्मानं निपतितो विपाशः पुनरुत्थितः॥
en: Here from the grief at his son's death, the great Rishi Vasishtha threw himself into the Vipasa after first binding himself, but he rose again.

description: History of the hawk and pigeon
sn: काश्मीरमण्डलं चैतत् सर्वपुण्यमरिंदम्। महर्षिभिश्चाध्युषितं पश्येदं भ्रातृभिः सह॥
en: O chastiser of foes, behold with your brothers the sacred region of Kashmira, ever frequented by the holy Rishis.

description: History of the hawk and pigeon
sn: यत्रोत्तराणां सर्वेषामृषीणां नाहुषस्य च। अग्नेश्चैवात्र संवादः काश्यपस्य च भारत॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, here a conference took place between Agni and the Rishi Kashyapa and between the son of Nahusha (Yayati) and the Rishis of the north.

description: History of the hawk and pigeon
sn: एतद् द्वारं महाराज मानसस्य प्रकाशते। वर्षमस्य गिरेमध्ये रामेण श्रीमता कृतम्॥
en: O great king, yonder appears the gate of Manaka. A gap was opened by Rama in the midst of this mountain.

description: History of the hawk and pigeon
sn: एष वातिकपण्डो वै प्रख्यातः सत्यविक्रमः। नात्यवर्तत यद्द्वारं विदेहादुत्तरं च यः॥
en: O greatly powerful hero, here is the celebrated Vatikakhanda, which although near the gate of Vedika, lies on the north of it.

description: History of the hawk and pigeon
sn: इदमाश्चर्यमपरं देशेऽस्मिन् पुरुषर्षभ। क्षीणे युगे तु कौन्तेय शर्वस्य सह पार्षदैः॥ सहोमया च भवति दर्शनं कामरूपिणः। अस्मिन् सरसि सत्रैर्वै चैत्रे मासि पिनाकिनम्॥
en: O foremost of men, there is another very remarkable thing in connection with this place. It is this that at the end of every Yuga the deity Shiva who is capable of assuming every form at will may be seen here with Uma and his followers. In the yonder lake men, desirous of securing welfare to them, cheerfully gratify the wielder of Pinaka in the month of Chaitra by performing sacrifices.

description: History of the hawk and pigeon
sn: यजन्ते याजकाः सम्यक् परिवारं शुभार्थिनः। अत्रोपस्पृश्य सरसि श्रद्दधानो जितेन्द्रियः॥ क्षीणपापः शुभाँल्लोकान् प्राप्नुते नात्र संशयः। एष उज्जानको नाम पावकिर्यत्र शान्तवान्। अरुन्धतीसहायश्च वसिष्ठो भगवानृषिः॥
en: The religious-minded and self-controlled men perform their ablations in this lake and become free from all sins. They certainly obtain the blessed regions. Here is the sacred Tirtha called Ujjanaka where the holy Rishi Vasishtha with his wife Arundhati lived.

description: History of the hawk and pigeon
sn: ह्रदश्च कुशवानेष यत्र पद्मं कुशेशयम्। आश्रमश्चैव रुक्मिण्या यत्राशाम्यदकोपना॥ समाधीनां समासस्तु पाण्डवेय श्रुतस्त्वया। तं द्रक्ष्यसि महाराज भृगुतुझं महागिरिम्॥
en: Yonder is the lake called Kushavanisha in which grow the lotuses called Kushashaya. Here also is the hermitage of Rukmini where she attained peace by conquering her anger. O son of Pandu, O great king, you must have heard of the great hill Bhrigutunga. Behold it (now).

description: History of the hawk and pigeon
sn: वितस्तां पश्य राजेन्द्र सर्वपापप्रमोचनीम्। महर्षिभिश्चाध्युषितां शीततोयां सुनिर्मलाम्॥
en: O king of kings, behold Vitasta which cleanses all sins. The water of it is very cool and transparent and it is frequented by the great Rishis.

description: History of the hawk and pigeon
sn: जलां चोपजलां चैव यमुनामभितो नदीम्। उशीनरो वै यत्रेष्ट्वा वासवादत्यरिच्यत॥
en: (Behold) Jala and Upjala the rivers on both the sides of the Yamuna. Ushinara surpassed Vasava (Indra in greatness) by performing a sacrifice here.

description: History of the hawk and pigeon
sn: तां देवसमिति तस्य दासवश्च विशाम्पते। अभ्यागच्छन्नृपवरं ज्ञातुमग्निश्च भारत॥
en: O king, O descendant of Bharata, being desirous of testing the merit of that great king, Vasava (Indra) and Agni came to his celestialslike Sava.

description: History of the hawk and pigeon
sn: जिज्ञासमानौ वरदौ महात्मानमुशीनरम्। इन्द्रःश्येनः कपोतोऽग्निर्भूत्वा यज्ञेऽभिजग्मतुः॥
en: Being inquisitive to know Ushinara and being willing to bestow boons on him, those two celestials Indra and Agni, came to his sacrificial ground, Indra becoming a hawk and Agni a pigeon.

description: History of the hawk and pigeon
sn: ऊरू राज्ञः समासाद्य कपोतः श्येनजाद् भयात्। शरणार्थी तदा राजन् निलिल्ये भयपीडितः॥
en: O king, the pigeon from the fear of the hawk fell upon the king's thighs for protection; and it became almost dead from the great fear.

description: History of the hawk and pigeon
sn: श्येन उवाच धर्मात्मानं त्वाहुरेकं सर्वे राजन् महीक्षितः। सर्वधर्मविरुद्धं त्वं कस्मात् कर्म चिकीर्षसि॥
en: The Hawk said: All the kings of earth call you virtuous. Therefore why do you perform an act which is not in accordance with Dharma?

description: History of the hawk and pigeon
sn: विहितं भक्षणं राजन् पीड्यमानस्य मे क्षुधा। मा रक्षीधर्मलोभेनधर्ममुत्सृष्टवानसि॥
en: O king, I am oppressed by hunger; do not withhold from me my ordained food on the belief that you are thus gaining virtue, whereas you are not.

description: History of the hawk and pigeon
sn: राजोवाच संत्रस्तरूपस्त्राणार्थी त्वत्तो भीतो महाद्विज। मत्सकाशमनुप्राप्तः प्राणगृनुरयं द्विजः॥
en: The King said: O great bird, this one is afflicted with the fear of you; and desirous of escaping from you it has come in a fury to me for protection.

description: History of the hawk and pigeon
sn: एवमभ्यागतस्येह कपोतस्याभयार्थिनः। अप्रदाने परंधर्मं कथं श्येन न पश्यसि॥
en: O hawk, why do you not see that it is a great virtue for me not to give up this pigeon which has thus come to me?

description: History of the hawk and pigeon
sn: प्रस्पन्दमानः सम्भ्रान्तः कपोतः श्येन लक्ष्यते। मत्सकाशं जीवितार्थी तस्य त्यागो विगर्हितः॥
en: O hawk, this pigeon is seen to tremble with fear; it is agitated, it has come to me for protection of its life. It is not proper for me to forsake it.

description: History of the hawk and pigeon
sn: यो हि कश्चिद् द्विजान् हन्याद् गां वा लोकस्य मातरम् शरणागतं च त्यजते तुल्यं तेषां हि पातकम्॥
en: He who kills a Brahmana and the mother of men (cow) and he who forsakes one who seeks his protection, both commit equal sin.

description: History of the hawk and pigeon
sn: श्येन उवाच आहारात् सर्वभूतानि सम्भवन्ति महीपते। आहारेण विवर्धन्ते तेन जीवन्ति जन्तवः॥
en: The Hawk said : O ruler of earth, all creatures exist on food. The animals are nourished and sustained by food.

description: History of the hawk and pigeon
sn: शक्यते दुस्त्यजेऽप्यर्थे चिररात्राय जीवितुम्। न तु भोजनमुत्सृज्य शक्यं वर्तयितुं चिरम्॥
en: A man can live many days even after forsaking his dear ones, but be cannot live long after abstaining from food.

description: History of the hawk and pigeon
sn: भक्ष्याद् वियोजितस्याद्य मम प्राणा विशाम्पते। विसृज्य कायमेष्यन्ति पन्थानमकुतोभयम्॥
en: O king, my life will depart today if deprived of food. Leaving my body it would fearlessly go away to other ways.

description: History of the hawk and pigeon
sn: प्रमृते मयिधर्मात्मन् पुत्रदारादि नक्ष्यति। रक्षमाणः कपोतं त्वं बहून् प्राणान् न रक्षसि॥
en: O virtuous-minded one, at my death my wife and children will perish. By protecting the pigeon you do not (at all) protect many lives.

description: History of the hawk and pigeon
sn: धर्मं यो बाधतेधर्मो न सधर्मः कुधर्म तत्। अविरोधात् तु योधर्मः सधर्मः सत्यविक्रम॥
en: The virtue, that stands in the way of another virtue, is (really) unrighteousness. O truthful king, that virtue true virtue which is not conflicting.

description: History of the hawk and pigeon
sn: विरोधिषु महीपाल निश्चित्य गुरुलाघवम्। न बाधा विद्यते यत्र तंधर्म समुपाचरेत्॥ गुरुलाघवमादायधर्माधर्मविनिश्चये। यतो भूयास्ततो राजन् कुरुष्वधर्मनिश्चयम्॥
en: O ruler of earth, after comparing the opposing virtues and weighing their comparative merits, one ought to espouse that which is not opposing. Where there is no confliction, one should adopt that virtue which preponderates.

description: History of the hawk and pigeon
sn: राजोवाच बहुकल्याणसंयुक्तं भाषसे विहगोत्तम। सुपर्णः पक्षिराट् किं त्वंधर्मज्ञश्चास्यसंशयम्॥
en: The King said : O excellent bird, as you speak words fraught with good, (may I ask) are you the king of birds, Suparna (Garuda)? I have not the least doubt that you are learned in all the precepts of virtue.

description: History of the hawk and pigeon
sn: तथा हिधर्मसंयुक्तं बहु चित्रं च भाषसे। न तेऽस्त्यविदितं किंचिदिति त्वां लक्षयाम्यहम्॥
en: As you speak many and various words of virtue, I do not see there is anything in respect with it which you do not know.

description: History of the hawk and pigeon
sn: शरणैषिपरित्यागं कथं साध्विति मन्यसे। आहारार्थं समारम्भस्तव चायं विहंगम॥
en: O bird, why do you consider, it virtuous to forsake one who seeks one's protection? Your attempt is only to search for food.

description: History of the hawk and pigeon
sn: शक्यश्चाप्यन्यथा कर्तुमाहारोऽप्यधिकस्त्वया। गोवृषो वा वराहो वा मृगो वा महिषोऽपि वा। त्वदर्थमद्य क्रियतां यच्चान्यदिह काक्षसि॥
en: You can appease you hunger with some other food which would be more plentiful. I am perfectly willing to procure for you any sort of food that would be palatable to you, whether it be an ox or a boar or a deer or a buffalo.

description: History of the hawk and pigeon
sn: श्येन उवाच न वराहं न चोक्षाणं न मृगान् विविधांस्तथा। भक्षयामि महाराज किं ममान्येन केनचित्॥
en: The Hawk said: O great king, I am not desirous of eating a boar or an ox or any other kind of beasts. What have I to do with any other food?

description: History of the hawk and pigeon
sn: यस्तु मे देवविहितो भक्षः क्षत्रियपुङ्गव। तमुत्सृज महीपाल कपोतमिममेव मे॥
en: O ruler of earth, O best of Kshatriyas, give me therefore this pigeon which is the food ordained to me by the celestials.

description: History of the hawk and pigeon
sn: श्यनेः कपोतानत्तीति स्थितिरेषा सनातनी। मा राजन् सारमज्ञात्वा कदलीस्कन्धमाश्रया२०॥
en: O king, that the hawks eat the pigeons, is an eternal law. Do not get on a plantain tree not knowing its want of strength (to support you).

description: History of the hawk and pigeon
sn: राजोवाच राष्ट्र शिबीनामृद्धं वै ददानि तव खेचर। यं वा कामयसे कामं श्येन सर्वं ददानि ते॥
en: The King said : Oranger of skies, I am willing to give you this kingdom of my dynasty and all wealth and also all that you desire to have,

description: History of the hawk and pigeon
sn: विनेनं पक्षिणं श्येन शरणार्थिनमागतम्। येनेमं वर्जयेथास्त्वं कर्मणा पक्षिसत्तम। तदाचक्ष्व करिष्यामि न हि दास्ये कपोतकम्॥
en: O hawk, O excellent bird, with the exception of giving up this pigeon which has come to me for protection. Tell me what I shall have to do for the deliverance of this bird, I shall not give you this pigeon.

description: History of the hawk and pigeon
sn: श्येन उवाच उशीनर कपोते ते यदि स्नेहो नराधिप। आत्मनो मांसमुत्कृत्य कपोततुलयाधृतम्॥
en: The Hawk said : O Ushinara, O ruler of men, if you have so much affection for the pigeon, then cut a portion of your flesh and weigh it against this pigeon.

description: History of the hawk and pigeon
sn: यदा समं कपोतेन तव मांसं नृपोत्तम। तदा देयं तु तन्मह्यं सा मे तुष्टिर्भविष्यति॥
en: O excellent king, when you flesh would be equal in weight with this pigeon, give it then to me and I shall be then satisfied.

description: History of the hawk and pigeon
sn: राजोवाच अनुग्रहमिमं मन्ये श्येन यन्माभियाचसे। तस्मात् तेऽद्य प्रदास्यामि स्वमांसं तुलयाधृतम्॥
en: The King said : O hawk, I consider your this request as a favour. I shall give you my own flesh weighing it against the pigeon.

description: History of the hawk and pigeon
sn: लोमश उवाच उत्कृत्य स स्वयं मांसं राजा परमधर्मवित्। तोलयामास कौन्तेय कपोतेन समं विभो॥
en: Lomasha said: O son of Kunti, O lord, cutting off his own flesh, that virtuous king weighed it against the pigeon.

description: History of the hawk and pigeon
sn: ध्रियमाणः कपोतस्तु मांसेनात्यतिरिच्यते। पुनश्चोत्कृत्य मांसानि राजा प्रादादुशीनरः॥
en: But when he found that the pigeon was more heavy than this flesh (thus cut and placed in the scale), the king Ushinara again cut (some more) flesh (from his body) and placed it (in the scale).

description: History of the hawk and pigeon
sn: न विद्यते यदा मांसं कपोतेन समंधृतम्। तत उत्कृत्तमांसोऽसावारुरोह स्वयं तुलाम्॥
en: When portion after portion of his flesh had been added to weigh against the pigeon and no more flesh was left on his body, he then himself mounted on the scale.

description: History of the hawk and pigeon
sn: श्येन उवाच इन्द्रोऽहमस्मिधर्मज्ञ कपोतो हव्यवाडयम्। जिज्ञासमानौधर्म त्वां यज्ञवाटमुपागतौ॥
en: The Hawk said : O virtuous king, I am Indra. The pigeon is the carrier of the sacrificial Ghee (Agni). In order to test your virtuous merit, we came to your sacrificial grounds,

description: History of the hawk and pigeon
sn: यत् ते मांसानि गात्रेभ्य उत्कृत्तानि विशाम्पते। एषा ते भास्वती कीर्तिर्लोकानभिभविष्यति॥
en: O king, as you have cut off your flesh from your body, your glory will be resplendent.

description: History of the hawk and pigeon
sn: यावल्लोके मनुष्यास्त्वां कथयिष्यन्ति पार्थिव। तावत् कीर्तिश्च लोकाश्च स्थास्यन्ति तव शाश्वताः।।
en: O king, as long as men will speak of you on earth, so long will your glory endure and eternal region would be reserved for you.

description: History of the hawk and pigeon
sn: इत्येवमुक्त्वा राजानमारुरोह दिवं पुनः। उशीनरोऽपिधर्मात्माधर्मेणावृत्य रोदसी॥ विभ्राजमानो वपुषाप्यारुरोह त्रिविष्टपम्। तदेतत् सदनं राजन् राज्ञस्तस्य महात्मनः॥
en: Lomasha said: Having said this to the king, he (Indra) again went to heaven. And the virtuous Ushinara also, after filling heaven and earth with the merit of his pious deeds, went to heaven in an effulgent form. O king, yonder is the residence of that illustrious king.

description: History of the hawk and pigeon
sn: पश्यस्वैतन्मया सार्धं पुण्यं पापप्रमोचनम्। तत्र वै सततं देवा मनुयश्च सनातनाः। दृश्यन्ते ब्राह्मणै राजन् पुण्यवद्भिर्महात्मभिः॥
en: Behold it which is holy and capable of cleansing sins. O king, here are always seen the celestials and eternal Rishis and also virtuous and high-souled Brahmanas.

sn: लोमश उवाच रौद्दालकिः श्वेतकेतुः पृथिव्याम्। तस्याश्रमं पश्य नरेन्द्र पुण्यं सदाफलैरुपपन्नं महीजैः॥
en: Lomasha said: O ruler of men, behold the sacred hermitage of Shvatakatu, the son of Uddalka, whose fame as an expert in Mantras is so widely spread all over the world. It always abounds in fruit trees.

sn: साक्षादत्र श्वेतकेतुर्ददर्श सरस्वतीं मानुषदेहरूपाम्। वेत्स्यामि वाणीमिति सम्प्रवृत्तां सरस्वतीं श्वेतकेतुर्बभाषे।॥
en: Here did Shvatakatu see Sarasvati herself in her heavenly form. Shvatakatu said to Sarasvati when she appeared, “Make me endued with the gift of speech.”

sn: वास्तां मुनी मातुलभागिनेयौ। रौद्दालकिः श्वेतकेतुः पृथिव्याम्॥
en: In that Yuga, Shvatakatu, the son of Uddalaka and Ashtavakra, the son of Kahoda, who were uncle and nephews, were the foremost men learned in the Vedas.

sn: विदेहराजस्य महीपतेस्तौ विप्रावुभौ मातुलभागिनेयौ। प्रविश्य यज्ञायतनं विवादे बन्दिं निजग्राहतुरप्रमेयौ॥
en: These two Brahmanas of matchless energy went to the sacrificial ground of the king of Videha and defeated Bandi (in a controversy).

sn: उपास्व कौन्तेय सहानुजस्त्वं तस्याश्रमं पुण्यतमं प्रविश्य। योऽसौ बन्दिं जनकस्याथ यज्ञे॥ वादी विप्रायो बाल एवाभिगम्य वादे भक्त्वा मज्जयामास नद्याम्॥
en: O son of Kunti, worship with your younger brothers the sacred hermitage of him who had for his grandson Ashtavakra, who when he was but a child had caused Bandi to be drowned in a river after having defeated him in a controversy).

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच स्तथाभूतं यो निजग्राह बन्दिम्। अष्टावक्र: केन चासौ बभूव तत् सर्वं मे लोमश शंस तत्त्वम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said : O Lomasha, tell me all about the power of this Brahmana who had thus defeated Bandi. Why was he born as Ashtavakra (crooked in cight parts of his body)?

sn: लोमश उवाच उद्दालकस्य नियतः शिष्य एको नाम्ना कहोड इति विश्रुतोऽभूत्। शुश्रूषुराचार्यवशानुवर्ती दीर्घ कालं सोऽध्ययनं चकार॥
en: Lomasha said : Udhalaka had a self-controlled disciple who was known by the name of Kohada. He was entirely devoted to the service of his preceptor and he continued his studies for a long time.

sn: स्तां च ज्ञात्वा परिचर्यां गुरुः सः। तस्मै प्रादात् सद्य एव श्रुतं च भार्यां च वै दुहितरं स्वां सुजाताम्॥
en: That Brahmana served his preceptor for a long time. Recognising it his preceptor gave him a mastery over the Shastras and also bestowed upon him his own daughter Sujata.

sn: तस्या गर्भः समभवदग्निकल्प: सोऽधीयानं पितरं चाप्युवाच। सर्वां रात्रिमध्ययनं करोषि नेदं पितः सम्यगिवोपवर्तते॥
en: She became with child as cffulgent as fire and the child while engaged in study spoke thus to his father, “O father, you have been reading for the whole night, but your reading does not seem to me correct.

sn: उपालब्धः शिष्यमध्ये महर्षिः स तं कोपादुदरस्थं शशाप। यस्मात् कुक्षौ वर्तमानो ब्रवीषि तस्माद् वक्रो भवितास्यष्टकृत्वः॥
en: Through your grace I have become even in my this fatal state learned in all the Shastras and in the Vedas and in the Vedangas. But O father, I tell you what proceeds from your lips is not correct."

sn: दष्टावक्रः प्रथितो वै महर्षिः। अस्यासीद् वै मातुलः श्वेतकेतुः स तेन तुल्यो वयसा बभूव॥
en: Having been thus insulted before his disciples, the great Rishi cursed in anger the child in the womb. “As you speak from the womb, so will you be crooked in eight parts of your body." Thus the child was born crooked and the great Rishi was ever afterwards known by the name of Ashtavakra. He had an uncle, named Shvatakatu who was of the same age as himself.

sn: सम्पीड्यमाना तु तदा सुजाता सा वर्धमानेन सुतेन कुक्षौ। उवाच भर्तारमिदं रहोगता प्रसाद्य हीनं वसुनाधनार्थिनी॥
en: Having been much oppressed for the growth of the child in the womb, Sujata, who was desirous of obtaining wealth, conciliating her husband who had no wealth, spoke to him thus in private.

sn: कथं करिष्याम्यधुना महर्षे मासश्चायं दशमो वर्तते मे। नैवास्ति ते वसु किंचित् प्रजाता येनाहमेतामापदं निस्तरेयम्॥
en: "O great king, what shall I do now, as the tenth month of my pregnancy has come! Neither you nor I possess any wealth with which we can be delivered from this distress."

sn: उक्तस्त्वेवं भार्यया वै कहोडो वित्तस्यार्थे जनकमथाभ्यगच्छत्। वै तदा वादविदा निगृह्य निमज्जितो बन्दिनेहाप्सु विप्रः॥
en: Having been thus addressed by his wife, Kohada went to Janaka for wealth. That Brahmana was defeated (in a controversy) by Bandi who was learned in the science of arguments. The result was that he was drowned.

sn: उद्दालकस्तं तु तदा निशम्य सूतेन वादेऽप्सु निमज्जितं तथा। उवाच तां तत्र ततः सुजातामष्टावक्रे गृहितव्योऽयमर्थः॥
en: Having heard that his sin-in-law had been defeated by Bandi and that he had been drowned, Udhalaka thus spoke to Sujata, “You must keep it a secret from Ashtavakra.”

sn: ररक्ष सा चापि तमस्य मन्त्रं जातोऽप्यसौ नैव शुश्राव विप्रः। उद्दालकं पितृवच्चापि मेने तथाष्टावक्रो भ्रातृवच्छ्वेतकेतुम्॥
en: She (accordingly) kept it a secret (from Ashtavakra). Thus that Brahmana heard nothing of it when he was born. He regarded Udhalaka as his father and Shvataketu as his brother.

sn: रष्टावक्रं पितुरङ्के निषण्णम्। अपाकर्षद् गृह्य पाणौ रुदन्तं नायं तवारू: पितुरित्युक्तवांश्च॥
en: When Ashtavakra was in his twelfth year, Shvataketu one day saw him on his father's lap. He dragged Ashtavakra by catching hold of his hand and when he (Ashtavakra) began to cry, he said, “This is not your father's lap.”

sn: यत् तेनोक्तं दुरुक्तं तत् तदानीं हृदि स्थितं तस्य सुदुःखिमासीत्। गृहं गत्वा मातरं सोऽभिगम्य पप्रच्छेदं क्व नु तातो ममेति॥
en: These cruel word went to his heart and he became greatly aggrieved. Going home and coming to his mother, he asked “Where is my father?"

sn: ततः सुजाता परमार्तरूपा शापाद् भीता सर्वमेवाचचक्षे। वित्यब्रवीच्छ्वेतकेतुं स विप्रः॥
en: Thereupon Sujata greatly afflicted and afraid of his curse told him all that had happened. Having heard all, that Brahmana (Ashtavakra) spoke in the night thus to Shvataketu.

sn: गच्छाव यज्ञं जनकस्य राज्ञो बह्वाश्चर्यः श्रूयते तस्य यज्ञः। मर्थं चायं तत्र भोक्ष्यावहे च॥
en: “Let us go to the sacrifice of the king Janaka. We hear of many wonderful things in that sacrifice. We shall hear controversies there among the Brahmanas and (we shall also) eat excellent food.

sn: विचक्षणत्वं च भविष्यते नौ शिवश्च सौम्यश्च हि ब्रह्मघोषः॥
en: We shall also gain experience. The recitation of the Vedas is charming to hear and it is fraught with blessings."

sn: तौ जग्मतुर्मातुलभागिनेयौ यज्ञं समृद्ध जनकस्य राज्ञः। अष्टावक्रं पथि राज्ञा समेत्य प्रोत्सार्यमाणो वाक्यमिदं जगाद॥
en: Thereupon the uncle and the nephew went to the splendid sacrifice of the king Janaka. Having been driven away from the path, Ashtavakra on meeting the king thus spoke to him.

sn: अष्टावक्र उवाच अन्धस्य पन्था बधिरस्य पन्थाः स्त्रियः पन्था भारवाहस्य पन्थाः। राज्ञः पन्था ब्राह्मणेनासमेत्य समेत्य तु ब्राह्मणस्यैव पन्थाः॥
en: Ashtavakra said: When no Brahmana passes along a path, it then belongs first to the blind, then to the deaf, then to women, then to the carriers of burden and then (last of all) to the king But when a Brahmana is met on the way, it solely belongs to him.

sn: राजोवाच पग्था अयं तेऽद्य मयातिदिष्टो येनेच्छसि तेन कामं व्रजस्व। निन्द्रोऽपि नित्यं नमते ब्राह्मणानाम्॥
en: The king said : I leave the path, go in whatever way you like. Even the smallest fire is not to be slighted. Indra himself always bows down to a Brahmana.

sn: अष्टावक्र उवाच प्राप्तौ स्व यज्ञं नृप संदिद्दसू कौतूहलं नौ बलवन्नरेन्द्र। प्राप्ताविहावामतिथी प्रवेशं काक्षावहे द्वारपतेस्तवाज्ञाम्॥
en: Ashtavakra said : O king, O ruler of men, we have come to see the sacrifice, our curiosity was very great. We have come as Athithis (guests). We ask your order on the gate-keeper.

sn: ऐन्द्रद्युम्ने यज्ञदृशाविहावां विवक्षू वै जनकेन्द्रं दिदृक्षा वयं च नौ द्वारपालो रुणद्धि॥
en: O son of Indradumnya, we have come here with the desire of seeing the sacrifice and to see and to speak with king Janaka. We are burning with anger, for the gate-keeper stops us.

sn: द्वारपाल उवाच बन्देः समादेशकरा वयं स्म निबोध वाक्यं च मयेर्यमाणम्। न वै बालाः प्रविशन्त्यत्र विप्रा वृद्धा विदग्धाः प्रविशन्त्यत्र विप्राः॥
en: The gate-keeper said : We carry out the word of Bandi. Hear what I say. The boy are not permitted to enter here; only old and learned Brahmanas are allowed to enter.

sn: अष्टावक्र उवाच यद्यत्र वृद्धेषु कृतः प्रवेशो युक्तं प्रवेष्टुं मम द्वारपाल। वयं हि वृद्धाश्चरितव्रताश्च वेदप्रभावेण समन्विताश्च॥
en: Ashtavakra said: O gate-keeper, if this be the order that only old men can enter here, then we can enter. We also are old and we have observed severe vows. We are endued with the effulgence of the Vedas,

sn: शुश्रूषवश्चापि जिन्द्रियाश्च ज्ञानागमे चापि गताः स्म निष्ठाम्। र्बालोऽप्यग्निहति स्पृश्यमानः॥
en: We have served our preceptor and we have subdued our passions and we have also obtained proficiency in knowledge. It is said that even boys must not be slighted; for the smallest fire if touched burns.

sn: द्वारपाल उवाच मेकाक्षरां बहुरूपां विराजम्। अङ्गात्मानं समवेक्षस्व बालं किं श्लाघसे दुर्लभो वै मनीषी॥
en: The gate-keeper said: O boy, if you know, recite the verse demonstrating the existence of the Supreme Being, adored by the celestials sages and composed of one letter though multifarious. Do not indulge in vain boasting. Learned men are very rare.

sn: अष्टावक्र उवाच र्यथाष्ठीला शाल्मलेः सम्प्रवृद्धा। ह्रस्वोऽल्पकायः फलितो विवृद्धो यश्चाफलस्तस्य न वृद्धभावः॥
en: Ashtavakra said: True growth can not be inferred from the mere growth of the body, as the growth of the knots of Salmali tree cannot tell its age. That tree is called full grown, which, though slender and short, bears fruits.

sn: द्वारपाल उवाच वृद्धेभ्य एवेह मतिं स्म बाला गृहणन्ति कालेन भवन्ति वृद्धाः। न हि ज्ञानमल्पकालेन शक्यं कस्माद् बालः स्थविर इव प्रभाषसे॥
en: The gate-keeper said : Boys receive instruction from the old and they thus in due time grow old. Knowledge cannot be obtained in a short time. Therefore why being but a child do you talk like an old man?

sn: अष्टावक्र उवाच । न तेन स्थविरे भवति येनास्य पलितं शिरः। बालोऽपि यः प्रजानाति तं देवा: स्थविरं विदुः॥
en: Ashtavakra said : One is not old, because his hair has turned white. Even boys who possess knowledge are considered to be old by the celestials.

sn: न हायनैर्न पलितैर्न वित्तेन न बन्धुभिः। ऋषयश्चक्रिरेधर्मं योऽनूचान: स नो महान्॥
en: The Rishis have not ordained that a man's merit depends on years or on gray hair or wealth or friend. To us one who is versed in the Vedas is great.

sn: दिदृक्षुरस्मि सम्प्राप्तो वन्दिनं राजसंसदि। निवेदयस्व मां द्वा:स्थ राज्ञे पुष्करमालिने।॥
en: O gate-keeper, I have come with the desire of secing Bandi. Go, inform the king (Janaka) adorned with the garlands of lotuses.

sn: द्रष्टास्यद्य वदतोऽस्मान् द्वारपाल मनीषिभिः। सह वादे विवृद्धे तु बन्दिनं चापि निर्जितम्॥
en: O gate-keeper, you will today see me engaged in a controversial fight with all the learned men and also with Bandi and you will (also) find him defeated by me.

sn: पश्यन्तु विप्राः परिपूर्णविद्याः सहैव राज्ञा सपुरोधमुख्याः। उताहो वाप्युच्चतां नीचता वा तूष्णीभूतेष्वेव सर्वेष्वथाद्य॥
en: When others will be silenced, then the learned men and the king with his chief priests will judge my superiority or inferiority.

sn: द्वारपाल उवाच कथं यज्ञं दशवर्षो विशेस्त्वं विनीतानां विदुषां सम्प्रवेशम्। उपायतः प्रयतिष्ये तवाहं प्रवेशने कुरु यत्नं यथावत्॥
en: The gate-keeper said : How can you, who are but in your tenth year, hope to enter into the grounds of this sacrifice into which only learned and educated men are admitted? I shall however try some means to admit you. You too make an attempt.

sn: अष्टावक्र उवाच भो भो राजञ्जनकानां वरिष्ठ त्वं वै सम्राट् त्वयि सर्वं समृद्धम्। त्वं वा कर्ता कर्मणां यज्ञियानां ययातिरेको नृपतिर्वा पुरस्तात्॥
en: Ashtavakra said: O king, O best of Janaka's race, you are an emperor and all wealth rest in you. In the days of yore, Yayati was the (great) performer of sacrifices and in the modern age you are the great performer of sacrifices.

sn: वृद्धान् बन्दी वादविदो निगृह्य वादे भग्नानप्रतिशङ्कमानः। जले सर्वान् मज्जयतीति नः श्रुतम्॥
en: We have heard that the learned Bandi, after defeating (in controversy), men who are experts in discussion, causes them to be drowned by faithful servants employed by you.

sn: सोऽहं श्रुत्वा ब्राह्मणानां सकाशाद् ब्रह्माद्वैत कथयितुमागतोऽस्मि। क्वासौ बन्दी यावदेनं समेत्य नक्षत्राणीव सविता नाशयामि॥
en: Having heard this from the Brahmanas, I have come to expound the doctrine of the Supreme Being. Where is that Bandi? Tell me, so that I may destroy him, as the sun destroys the stars.

sn: राजोवाच मविज्ञाय त्वं वाक्यबलं परस्य। विज्ञातवीर्यैः शक्यमेवं प्रवक्तुं दृष्टचासौ ब्राह्मणैर्वेदशीलैः॥
en: The King said: You hope to defeat Bandi, because you do not know his power. Can they, who know him, speak as you do? He had been tested by the Brahmanas who were experts in discussion.

sn: मविज्ञाय तु बलं बन्दिनोऽस्य। समागता ब्राह्मणास्तेन पूर्वं न शोभन्ते भास्करेणेव ताराः॥
en: You hope to defeat Bandi, only because you do not know his powers. Many Brahmanas that assembled did not shine before him as the stars do not shine before the sun.

sn: स्तस्यान्तिकं प्राप्य विलुप्तशोभाः। विज्ञानमत्ता नि:सृताश्चैव तात कथं सदस्यैर्वचनं विस्तरेयुः॥
en: Being desirous of defeating him, they proud of their learning, have lost their glory on simply appearing before him. They have retired from his presence without even venturing to speak with the members of the assembly.

sn: अष्टावक्र उवाच विवादितोऽसौ न हि मादृशैर्हि सिंहीकृतस्तेन वदत्यभीतः। समेत्य मां निहतः शेष्यतेऽद्य मार्गे भग्नं शकटमिवाचलाक्षम्॥
en: Ashtavakra said : Bandi has never had an occasion to hold a discussion with a man like me. It is only for this reasor, that he considers himself as a lion and goes about roaring like one. But when he will meet me today, he will lie down (dead) as a cart breaks down on the road when its wheels have been deranged.

sn: राजोवाच त्रिंशकद्वादशांशस्य चतुर्विंशतिपर्वणः। यस्त्रिषष्टिशतारस्य वेदार्थं स परः कविः॥
en: The King said : He alone is a really learned man who understands the thing that has thirty divisions, twelve parts, twenty-four joints and three hundred and sixty spokes.

sn: अष्टावक्र उवाच चतुर्विंशतिपर्व त्वां षण्नाभि द्वादशप्रधि। तत् त्रिषष्टिशतारं वै चक्रं पातु सदागति॥
en: Ashtavakra said: May that ever-revolving wheel (Time) that has twenty-four joints, six naves twelve peripheries and sixty spokes protect you.

sn: राजोवाच वडवे इव संयुक्ते श्येनपाते दिवौकसाम्। कस्तयोर्गर्भमाधत्ते गर्भं सुषुवतुश्च कम्॥
en: The King said : Who among the celestials gives birth to those who which go together like two yoked mares and swoop down like hawks; and to what also do they give birth?

sn: अष्टावक्र उवाच मा स्म ते ते गृहे राजञ्छात्रवाणामपिध्रुवम्। वातसारथिरागन्ता गर्भं सुषुवतुश्च तम्॥
en: Ashtavakra said : O king, may God keep away from your house those two (thunder and lightning), nay cven from the house of your enemies. He who appears with the wind as his charioteer (cloud or mind) gives, birth to them and they also produce him.

sn: राजोवाच किंस्वित् सुप्तं न निमिषति किंस्विज्जातं न चोपति। कस्य स्विद्धृदयं नास्ति किं स्विद् वेगेन वर्धते॥
en: The King said: What is it that does not close its eyes even when it is asleep? What is it that does not move when born? What is it that has no heart and what is it that increases in its speed?

sn: अष्टावक्र उवाच मत्स्यः सुप्तो न निमिषत्यण्डं जातं न चोपति। अश्मनो हृदयं नास्ति नदी वेगेन वर्धते॥
en: Ashtavakra said: It is a fish that does not close its eyes when asleep. It is an egg that does not move even when born. It is stone that has no heart. It is a river that increases in its speed.

sn: राजोवाच न त्वां मन्ये मानुषं देवसत्त्वं न त्वं बाल: स्थविरः सम्मतो मे। न ते तुल्यो विद्यते वाक्प्रलापे तस्माद् द्वारं वितराम्येष बन्दी॥
en: The King said : Opossessor of divine energy, it appears that you are not a human being. I do not consider that you are a boy. I consider you to be a grown up man. There is none who can be compared with you in learning. Therefore I give you admittance. Yonder is Bandi.

sn: अष्टावक्र उवाच अत्रोग्रसेन समितेषु राजन् समागतेष्वप्रतिमेषु राजसु। नावैमि बन्दिं वरमत्र वादिनां महाजले हंसमिवाददामि॥
en: Ashtavakra said : O king, O commander of large army, cannot find Bandi, this chief of controversialists in that assembly of these kings of matchless power who have met together. I search for him as one searches for a swan on a vast expanse of water.

sn: न मेऽद्य वक्ष्यस्यतिवादिमानिन् ग्लहं प्रपन्नः सरितामिवागमः। हुताशनस्येव समिद्धतेजसः स्थिरो भवस्वेह ममाद्य बन्दिन्॥
en: O Bandi, you consider that you are the foremost of all controversialists. When you will engage with me to argue, you will then not be able to flow like the current of a river. I am like a flaming fire. Be silent before me.

sn: बन्धुवाच व्याघ्र शयानं प्रति मा प्रबोधय आशीविषं सृक्किणी लेलिहानम्। पदाहतस्येह शिरोऽभिहत्य नादष्टो वै मोक्ष्यसे तन्निबोध॥
en: Do not awaken a sleeping tiger. Know that you will not escape biting when you will trample on the head of a poisonous snake, which is licking the corner of its mouth with its tongue and which has been hurt by your foot.

sn: यो वै दर्पात् संहननोपपन्नः। सुदुर्बलः पर्वतमाविहन्ति। तस्यैव पाणिः सनखो विदीर्यते न चैव शैलस्य हि दृश्यते व्रणः॥
en: That weak man, who in the pride of his strength strikes a blow at a mountain, only hurts his hands and nails. He can not wound the mountains.

sn: अष्टावक्र उवाच सर्वे राज्ञो मैथिलस्य मैनाकस्येव पर्वताः। निकृष्टभूता राजानो वत्सा अनडुहो यथा॥
en: As all other mountains are inferior to the Mainakas, as calves are inferior to the ox, so are all the others kings of the earth inferior to the king of Mithila.

sn: यथा महेन्द्रः प्रवरः सुराणां नदीषु गङ्गा प्रवरा यथैव। तथा नृपाणां प्रवरस्त्वमेको बन्दिं समभ्यानय मत्सकाशम्॥
en: As Indra is the foremost of the celestials, as Ganga is the foremost of all rivers so are you the foremost of all kings. Cause Bandi to appear before me.

sn: लोमश उवाच जातक्रोधो बन्दिनमाह राजन्। उक्ते वाक्ये चोत्तरं मे ब्रवीहि वाक्यस्य चाप्युत्तरं ते ब्रवीमि॥
en: Lomasha said: O king, having said this and becoming greatly angry with Bandi, Ashtavakra began to roar in the assembly. He said, “Answer my questions, I shall answer yours.”

sn: बन्धुवाच एक एवग्निर्बहुधा समिध्यते एकः सूर्यः सर्वमिदं विभाति। एको वीरो दोवराजऽरिन्ता यमः पितृणामीश्वरश्चैक एव॥
en: Bandi said: Fire is only one which blazes in various forms, One is the sun that illuminates the universe, One is the hero, Indra, the lord of the celestials who destroys all enemies, One is Yama, the sole lord of the Pitris.

sn: अष्टावक्र उवाच द्वाविन्द्राग्नी चरतो वै सखायौ द्वौ देवर्षी नारदपर्वतौ च। द्वावश्विनौ द्वे रथस्यापि चक्रे भार्यापती द्वौ विहितौ विधात्रा॥
en: Ashtavakra said : The two friends, Agni and Indra, move together; the celestials sages are Two Narada and Parvata, the Ashvins are Two, the wheels of a car are two. It is Two, husband and wife, that live together as ordained by the deity.

sn: बन्धुवाच त्रिः सूयते कर्मणा वै प्रजेयं त्रयो युक्ता वाजपेयं वहन्ति। अध्वर्यवस्त्रिसवनानि तन्वते त्रयो लोकास्त्रीणि ज्योतींषि चाहुः॥
en: Bandi said: Three kinds of being are born as the results of their acts, Three are the Vedas that perform the Vajapeya sacrifice; at three different times the Adhvaryus commence sacrifice, three also are the divine lights.

sn: अष्टावक्र उवाच चतुष्टयं ब्राह्मणानां निकेतं चत्वारो वर्णा यज्ञमिमं वहन्ति। दिशश्चतस्रो वर्णचतुष्टयं च चतुष्पदा गौरपि शश्वदुक्ता॥
en: Ashtavakra said: Four are the Ashrams of the Brahmanas; four orders perform sacrifices; four are the cardinal points; four is the number of letters and four also are the legs of a cow.

sn: बन्धुवाच र्यज्ञाः पञ्चैवाप्यथ पञ्चेन्द्रियाणि। दृष्टा वेदे पञ्चचूडाप्सराश्च लोके ख्यातं पञ्चनदं च पुण्यम्॥
en: Bandi said: Five is the number of fires; five are the feet of Punkti (a meter); five are the sacrifices; it is said in the Vedas that five locks are on the heads of the Apsaras and five are the sacred rivers in the world.

sn: अष्टावक्र उवाच षडाधाने दक्षिणामाहुरेके षट् चैवेमे ऋतवः कालचक्रम्। षडिन्द्रियाण्युत षट् कृत्तिकाश्च षट् साद्यस्काः सर्ववेदेषु दृष्टाः॥
en: Ashtavakra said: Six cows are paid as Dakshina on establishing the sacred fire; six are the seasons belonging to the wheel of time, six stars constitute the constellation Kirtika and the Vedas say six the number of Sadyaska sacrifice.

sn: बन्धुवाच सप्त ग्राम्याः पशवः सप्त वन्याः सप्तच्छन्दांसि क्रतुमेकं वहन्ति। सप्तर्षयः सप्त चाप्यर्हणानि सप्ततन्त्री प्रथिता चैव वीणा॥
en: Bandi said : Seven is the number of domestic animals, seven also is the number of wild animals; seven meters are used in completing a sacrifice; seven are the Rishis, seven are the forms of paying homage and seven, are the strings of the Binda.

sn: अष्टावक्र उवाच अष्टौ शाणाः शतमानं वहन्ति तथाष्टपादः शरभः सिंहघाती। अष्टौ वसूशुश्रुम देवतासु यूपश्चाष्टास्त्रिर्विहितः सर्वयज्ञे।॥
en: Ashtavakra said: Eight are the bags that hold hundred-fold, eight is the number of the Sarava, which preys upon lions, eight are the Vasus among the celestials and eight are the angles of a Yupa (stake) in a sacrifice.

sn: बन्धुवाच नवैवोक्ताः सामिधेन्यः पितृणां तथा प्राहुर्नवयोगं विसर्गम्। नवाक्षरा बृहती सम्प्रदिष्टा नवयोगो गणनामेति शश्वत्॥
en: Bandi said: Nine is the number of the Mantras used in kindling the fire in a sacrifice to the Pitris: nine are the fixed functions in the progresses of creation, nine letters compose the foot of Vrihati (a meter) and nine also are numbers (in calculation).

sn: अष्टावक्र उवाच दिशो दशोक्ताः पुरुषस्य लोके सहस्रमाहुर्दशपूर्णं शतानि। दशैव मासान् बिभ्रति गर्भवत्यो दशैरका दश दाशा दशार्हाः॥
en: Ashtavakra said : Ten is the number of the cardinal points; ten times hundred make a thousand; ten is the number of months of a woman's conception, ten are the teachers of true knowledge and ten are the haters of knowledge and ten again who are capable of obtaining it.

sn: बन्धुवाच मेकादशैवात्र भवन्ति यूपाः। एकादश प्राणभृतां विकारा एकादशोक्ता दिवि देवेषु रुद्राः॥
en: Eleven are the enjoyable objects, eleven is the number of Yupas (sacrificial stake), eleven are the natural states of all living creatures, eleven are the Rudras among the celestials in heaven.

sn: अष्टावक्र उवाच जगत्याः पादो द्वादशैवाक्षराणि। द्वादशाहः प्राकृतो यज्ञ उक्तो द्वादशादित्यान् कथयन्तीहधीराः॥
en: Twelve are the months in a year; twelve letters compose a foot of Yayati (a meter) twelve are the sacrifices and the learned say twelve is the number of the Adityas.

sn: बन्धुवाच त्रयोदशी तिथिरुक्ता प्रशस्ता त्रयोदशद्वीपवती मही च।
en: Bandi said : Thirteen lunar days are most auspicious and thirteen islands exist on earth.

sn: लोमश उवाच एतावदुक्त्वा विरराम बन्दी। श्लोकस्यार्धं व्याजहाराष्टवक्रः।
en: Lomasha said : Having said this Bandi stopped. Thereupon Ashtavakra supplied the other half of the Sloka.

sn: अष्टावक्र उवाच त्रयोदशाहानि ससार केशी त्रयोदशादीन्यतिच्छन्दांसि चाहुः॥
en: Ashtavakra said: Thirteen sacrifices are presided over by Keshi and thirteen are devoured by Atichandas of the Vedas.

sn: स्तूष्णीभूतं सूतपुत्रं निशम्या मष्टावक्रं चाप्युदीर्यन्तमेव॥ तस्मिंस्तथा संकुले वर्तमाने स्फीते यज्ञे जनकस्योत राज्ञः। विप्राः सर्वे प्राञ्जलयः प्रतीताः॥
en: Lomasha said: Having seen Ashtavakra speaking and Suta's son sitting silent and pensive and with head down-cast, all men raised up great uproar in the assembly. When the tumult thus rose in the king Janaka's great sacrifice, the Brahmanas i became very much pleased and with joined hands they came to Ashtavakra and paid him homage.

sn: अष्टावक्र उवाच अनेनैव ब्राह्मणाः शुश्रुवांसो वादे जित्वा सलिले मज्जिताः प्राक्। तानेवधर्मानयमद्य बन्दी प्राप्नोतु गृह्याप्सु निमज्जयैनम्॥
en: Defeating the Brahmanas in controversy Bandi threw them into the waters. Let Bandi meet with the same fate to day. Seize him and drown him in the water.

sn: बन्धुवाच स्तत्रास सत्रं द्वादशवार्षिकं वै। सत्रेण ते जनक तुल्यकालं तदर्थं ते प्रहिता मे द्विजाच्याः॥
en: O Janaka, I am the son of king Varuna. Simultaneously with your sacrifice, there (underneath the sea) has been commenced (by Varuna) a sacrifice extending over twelve years. Therefore I have sent there those chief Brahmanas.

sn: ते तु सर्वे वरुणस्योत यज्ञं द्रष्टुं गता इह आयान्ति भूयः। अष्टावक्रं पूजये पूजनीयं यस्य हेतोर्जनितारं समेष्ये॥
en: They had all gone to see Varuna's sacrifice. Behold they are (all) coming. I pay homage to the revered Ashtavakra by whose favour I shall today join him who has begotten me.

sn: अष्टावक्र उवाच विप्राः समुद्राम्भसि मज्जिता ये वाचा जिता मेधया वा विदानाः। तां मेधया वाचमथोज्जहार यथा वाचमवचिन्वन्ति सन्तः॥
en: Ashtavakra said: Defeating the Brahmanas either by words or subtlety, he has thrown them into the waters of the sea. By dint of my intellect I have to day have rescued them.

sn: अग्निर्दहञ्जातवेदाः सतां गृहान् विसर्जयस्तेजसा न स्मधाक्षीत्। बालेषु पुत्रेषु कृपणं वदत्सु तथा वाचमवचिन्वन्ति सन्तः॥
en: As Agni (fire) who knows the character of both the good and the bad, leaves unscorched those that are honest, so do good men judge the assertions of even boys, though they lack in the power of speech.

sn: श्लेष्मातकी क्षीणवर्चाः शृणोषि उताहो त्वां स्तुतयो मादयन्ति। हस्तीव त्वं जनक विनुद्यमानो न मामिकां वाचमिमां शृणोषि।॥
en: O Janaka, you are hearing my words as if you have been stupified by eating the fruit of Sleshmataki tree. You have been robbed of your sense by flattery. Therefore though you are pierced by my words as an elephant by the goad, you do not heed them.

sn: जनक उवाच ममानुषी दिव्यरूपोऽसि साक्षात्। अजैषीर्यद् बन्दिनं त्वं विवादे निसृष्ट एष तव कामोऽद्य बन्दी॥
en: Janaka said: I listen to your words which are excellent and superhuman. Your appearance also appears to me as superhuman. As you "have to day defeated Bandi, I place even him at your disposal.

sn: अष्टावक्र उवाच नानेन जीवता कश्चिदर्थो मे बन्दिना नृप। पिता यद्यस्व वरुणो मज्जयैनं जलाशये॥
en: Ashtavakra said : O king, if Bandi remains alive, he would come to no use of mine. If his father is really Varuna, let him be drowned in the sea.

sn: बन्धुवाच अहं पुत्रो वरुणस्योत राज्ञो न मे भयं विद्यते मज्जितस्य। मष्टावक्रश्चिरनष्टं कहोडम्॥
en: Bandi said: I am the son of the king Varuna. I have therefore no fear to be drowned. Even at this very moment Ashtavakra would see his longlost father Kahoda.

sn: लोमश उवाच ततस्ते पूजिता विप्रा वरुणेन महात्मना। उदतिष्ठंस्ततः सर्वे जनकस्य समीपतः॥
en: Lomasha said : Then rose before Janaka all the Brahmanas, after they been duly worshipped by the illustrious Varuna.

sn: कहोड उवाच इत्यर्थमिच्छन्ति सुताञ्जना जनक कर्मणा। यदहं नाशकं कर्तुं तत् पुत्रः कृतवान् मम॥
en: Kahoda said: O Janaka, it is for this reason men desire for sons by performing virtuous acts. That in which I failed has been done by my son.

sn: उताबलस्य बलवानुत बालस्य पण्डितः। उत वाविदुषो विद्धान् पुत्रो जनक जायते॥
en: O Janaka, weak men may have strong sons, fools may have intelligent sons and the illiterate may have learned sons.

sn: शितेन ते परशुना स्वयमेवान्तको नृप। शिरांस्यपाहरत्वाजौ रिपूणां भद्रमस्तु ते॥
en: Bandi said: O king, it is with your sharp axe that Yama severs the heads of his enemies. May prosperity attend you.

sn: महदौक्थ्यं गीयते साम चावयं सम्यक् सोमः पीयते चात्र सत्रे। शुचीन् भगान् प्रतिजगृहुश्च हृष्टाः साक्षाद् देवा जनकस्योत राज्ञः॥
en: In this sacrifice of king Janaka, the chief hymns relating to the Uktha rites are sung and the Soma juice is properly drunk. The celestials themselves with cheerful hearts accept their sacred portions.

sn: लोमश उवाच समुत्थितेष्वथ सर्वेषु राजन् विप्रेषु तेष्वधिकं सुप्रभेषु। अनुज्ञातो जनकेनाथ राज्ञा विवेश तोयं सागरस्योत बन्दी॥
en: Lomasha said: O king, when all the Brahmanas rose (from the waters), their splendour was much enhanced; Bandi with the permission of king Janaka then entered the ocean.

sn: अष्टावक्र: पितरं पूजयित्वा सम्पूजितो ब्राह्मणैस्तैर्यथावत्। प्रत्याजगामाश्रममेव चावयं जित्वा सौतिं सहितो मातुलेन॥
en: Ashtavakra then worshipped his father and he himself was (also) worshipped by the Brahmanas. Having thus defeated Suta's son, he returned with his uncle to his excellent hermitage.

sn: ततोऽष्टावक्रमातुरथान्तिके पिता नदीं समङ्गां शीघ्रमिमां विशस्व। प्रोवाच चैनं स तथा विवेश समैरङ्गैश्चापि बभूव सद्यः॥
en: Thereupon in the presence of his mother, his father said, "Speedily enter into the water of this river Samanga." Being thus told, he entered. And immediately all his (crooked) limbs were made straight.

sn: नदी समङ्गा च बभूव पुण्या यस्यां स्नातो मुच्यते किल्बिषाद्धिा त्वमप्येनां स्नानपानावगाहैः सभ्रातृकः सहभार्यो विशस्व॥
en: From that day that river became known by the name of Samanga and it became capable of cleansing sins. He who bathes in it is cleansed of all sins. Therefore enter with your brothers and wife into its water.

sn: अत्र कौन्तेय सहितो भ्रातृभिस्त्वं सुखोषितः सह विप्रैः प्रतीतः। र्मया साधू चरितस्याजमीढ॥
en: O son of Kunti, O descendant of Ajamira, being intent on good deeds, you will perform many other virtuous acts by living happily here with your brothers and the Brahmanas.

sn: लोमश उवाच एषा मधुविला राजन् समङ्गा सम्प्रकाशते। एतत् कर्दमिलं नाम भरतस्याभिषेचनम्॥
en: Lomasha said: O king, here is visible the river Samanga which is also called Madhubela. Yonder is Kardamela, the bathing place of Bharata.

sn: अलक्ष्म्या किल संयुक्तो वृत्रं हत्वा शचीपतिः। आप्लुतः सर्वपापेभ्यः समझायां व्यमुच्यत॥
en: When the lord of Sachi, (Indra) became devoid of his prosperity in consequence of killing Vritra, he was cleansed of his sins by bathing in the Samanga.

sn: एतद् विनशनं कुक्षौ मैनाकस्य नरर्षभ। अदितिर्यत्र पुत्रार्थं तदन्नमपचत् पुरा॥
en: O foremost of men, here is the spot where the Mainaka has sunk into the interior of the earth. It is therefore called Vinasana. In order to obtain sons Aditi in the days of yore cooked his famous food.

sn: एनं पर्वतराजानमारुह्य भरतर्षभाः। अयशस्यामसंशब्द्यामलक्ष्मी व्यपनोत्स्यथ॥
en: O foremost of men, ascend this lofty mountain and put an end to your inglorious misery which is not worthy of uttering.

sn: एते कनखला राजन्तृषीणां दयिता नगाः। एषा प्रकाशते गङ्गा युधिष्ठिर महानदी।॥
en: O king, yonder is the Kanakhala mountain, the favourite resort of the Rishis, O Yudhishthira, yonder is the great river Ganga.

sn: सनत्कुमारो भगवानत्र सिद्धिमगात् पुरा। आजमीढावगायैनां सर्वपापैः प्रमोक्ष्यसे॥
en: Here in the days of yore the holy sage Sanatkumara attained ascetic auccess. O descendant of Ajmira, if you bathe in it, you will be cleansed of all your sins.

sn: अपां ह्रदं च पुण्याख्यं भृगुतुङ्गं च पर्वतम्। उष्णीगङ्गे च कौन्तेय सामात्यः समुपस्पृश॥
en: O son of Kunti, touch with your ministers this lake, called Punya and this Bhrigutunga (mountain) and also these two rivers called Tashniganga.

sn: आश्रमः स्थूलशिरसो रमणीयः प्रकाशते। अत्र मानं च कौन्तेय क्रोधं चैव विवर्जय॥
en: O son of Kunti, yonder is the charming hermitage of Sulasherasha. Abandon your anger and sense of self-importance.

sn: एष रैभ्याश्रमः श्रीमान् पाण्डवेय प्रकाशते। भारद्वाजो यत्र कविर्यवक्रीतो व्यनश्यत॥
en: O son of Pandu, yonder is the beautiful hermitage of Raivya where died the son of Bharadvaja, Yavakrit, learned in the Vedas.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच कथं युक्तोऽभवदृषिर्भरद्वाजः प्रतापवान्। किमर्थं च यवक्रीतः पुत्रोऽनश्यत वै मुनेः॥
en: Yudhishthira said: How did the mighty sage Yavakrit, the son of the ascetic Bharadvaja, acquire profound knowledge in the Vedas. How also did he die?

sn: एतत् सर्वं यथावृत्तं श्रोतुमिच्छामि तत्त्वतः। कर्मभिर्देवकल्पानां कीर्त्यमानै शं रमे॥
en: I desire to learn all this as they happened. I take delight in hearing the accounts of the celestials-like men.

sn: लोमश उवाच भरद्वाजश्च रैभ्यश्च सखायौ सम्बभूवतुः। तावूषतुरिहात्यन्तं प्रीयमाणावनन्तरम्॥
en: Lomasha said : Bharadvaja and Raivya were two friends. They both lived here always taking the greatest pleasure in each other's company.

sn: रैभ्यस्य तु सुतावास्तामर्वावसुपरावसू। आसीद् यवक्रीः पुत्रस्तु भरद्वाजस्य भारत॥
en: Raivya had two sons, named Arvavasu and Pravashu. O descendant of Bharata, Bharadvaja had only one son named Yavakrit.

sn: रैभ्यो विद्वान् सहापत्यस्तपस्वी चेतरोऽभवत्। तयोश्चाप्यतुला कीर्तिर्बाल्यात् प्रभृति भारत॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, Raivya and his sons became learned and the other (Bharadvaja) became an ascetic. From their childhood their friendship was matchless.

sn: यवक्री: पितरं दृष्ट्वा तपस्विनमसत्कृतम्। दृष्ट्वा च सत्कृतं विप्रै रैभ्यं पुत्रैः सहानघ॥ पर्यतप्यत तेजस्वी मन्युनाभिपरिप्लुतः। तपस्तेपे ततो घोरं वेदज्ञानाय पाण्डव॥
en: O sinless one, seeing that his father who practised asceticism was slighted by the Brahmanas, while Raivya with his sons was greatly respected by them, the high-spirited Yavakrit was overwhelmed with sorrow and became pale. O son of Pandu, he underwent severe austerities in order to get the knowledge of the Vedas.

sn: स समिद्धे महत्यग्नौ शरीरमुपतापयन्। जनयामास संतापमिन्द्रस्य सुमहातपाः॥
en: He exposed his body to a flaming fire. By thus practising great asceticism he filled Indra with great anxiety.

sn: तत इन्द्रो यवक्रीतमुपगम्य युधिष्ठिर। अब्रवीत् कस्य हेतोस्त्वमास्थितस्तप उत्तमम्॥
en: O Yudhishthira, thereupon Indra went to him and thus spoke to him, 'Why have you been engaged in the severe austerities?

sn: यवक्रीत उवाच द्विजानामनधीत वै वेदाः सुरगणार्चित। प्रतिभान्त्विति तप्येऽहमिदं परमकं तपः॥
en: Yavakrit said : O worshipped of the celestials, I am engaged in the severe asceticism, because I desire to possess such knowledge of the Vedas as has never been acquired by any Brahmana.

sn: स्वाध्यायार्थ समारम्भो ममायं पाकशासन। तपसा ज्ञातुमिच्छामि सर्वज्ञानानि कौशिक॥
en: O chastiser of Paka, O Kaushika, my this attempt is for obtaining the knowledge of the Vedas. By the force of my asceticism, I desire to acquire all sorts of knowledge.

sn: कालेन महता वेदाः : शक्या गुरुमुखाद् विभो। प्राप्तुं तस्मादयं यत्नः परमो मे समास्थितः॥
en: O lord, the knowledge of the Vedas that are to be learnt from teachers, requires long time to acquire. Therefore I am engaged in this great attempt.

sn: इन्द्र उवाच अमार्ग एष विप्रर्षे येन त्वं यातुमिच्छसि। किं विघातेन ते विप्र गच्छाधीहि गुरोर्मुखात्॥
en: Indra said: O Brahmana Rishi, the way you have adopted is not the proper way. O Brahmana, why will you destroy yourself? Go and learn (the Vedas) from a preceptor.

sn: लोमश उवाच एवमुक्त्वा गतः शक्रो यवक्रीरपि भारत। भूय एवाकरोद् यत्नं तपस्यमितविक्रमः॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, having said this, Sakra (Indra) departed and Yavakrit of immeasurable prowess again engaged himself in asceticism.

sn: घोरेण तपसा राजस्तप्यमानो महत् तपः। संतापयामास भृशं देवेन्द्रमिति नः श्रुतम्॥
en: O king we have heard that by thus undergoing severe asceticism, he again greatly agitated the lord of the celestials.

sn: तं तथा तप्यमानं तु तपस्तीव्र महामुनिम्। उपेत्य बलभिद् देवो वारयामास वै पुनः॥
en: The slayer of Bala, the deity (Indra) again came to that great Rishi who was engaged in that great austerity and forbade him to do it.

sn: अशक्योऽर्थः समारब्धो नैतद् बुद्धिकृतं तव। प्रतिभास्यन्ति वै वेदास्तव चैव पितुश्च ते॥
en: Indra said: You are doing all this with the intention that the knowledge of the Vedas might be manifest in you and in your father, but your attempt can never be successful. Your this act is not welladvised.

sn: यवक्रीत उवाच न चैतदेवं क्रियते देवराज ममेप्सितम्। महता नियमेनाहं तप्स्ये घोरतरं तपः॥
en: Yavakrit said : O king of the celestials, if you will not do what I desire, I shall, then, by observing stricter vows, practise still more severe austerities.

sn: समिद्धेऽग्नावुपकृत्याङ्गमङ्गं होष्यामि वा मघवंस्तन्निबोध। यद्येतदेवं न करोषि कामं ममेप्सितं देवराजेह सर्वम्॥
en: O king of the celestials, know that if you do not fulfill all my desires, I shall then cut off my limbs and offer them as a sacrifice to a blazing fire.

sn: लोमश उवाच निश्चयं तमभिज्ञाय मुनेस्तस्य महात्मनः। प्रतिवारणहेत्वर्थं बुद्ध्या संचिन्त्य बुद्धिमान्॥
en: Lomasha said: Having known the firın resolution of that high-souled Rishi, that intelligent deity (Indra) reflected (for a moment) and hit upon a means by which to dissuade him.

sn: तत इन्द्रोऽकरोद् रूपं ब्राह्मणस्य तपस्विनः। अनेकशतवर्षस्य दुबर्लस्य सयक्ष्मणः॥
en: Thereupon Indra assumed the garb of an ascetic Brahmana, who was many hundred years of age and who was weak and consumptive.

sn: यवक्रीतस्य यत् तीर्थमुचितं शौचकर्मणि। भागीरथ्यां तत्र सेतुं बालुकाभिश्चकार स:॥
en: He began to construct a dam of sands at thai spot of the Bhagirathi where Yavakrit used to go to perform his ablutions.

sn: यदास्य वदतो वाक्यं न स चक्रे द्विजोत्तमः। बालुकाभिस्ततः शक्रो गङ्गां समभिपूरयन्॥
en: As that foremost of Brahmanas paid no heed to the words of Sakra (Indra), he therefore began to fill Ganga with sands.

sn: वालुकामुष्टिमनिशं भागीरथ्यां व्यसर्जयत्। सेतुमभ्यारभच्छको यवक्रीतं निदर्शयन्॥
en: Without stopping for a moment, he threw handfuls of sands into the Bhagirathi and to construct the dam thus attracting the notice of the Rishi.

sn: तं ददर्श यवक्रीतो यत्नवन्तं निबन्धने। प्रहसंश्चाब्रवीद् वाक्यमिदं स मुनिपुङ्गवः॥
en: When that foremost of Rishis, Yavakrit, saw him thus earnestly engaged in bridging (the Ganges), he broke out into a loud laughter and thus spoke.

sn: किमिदं वर्तते ब्रह्मन् किं च ते ह चिकीर्षितम्। अतीव हि महान् यत्नः क्रियतेऽयं निरर्थकः॥
en: Yavakrit said: O Brahmana, what are you doing? What is your intention? Why are you in vain making this great attempt?

sn: इन्द्र उवाच बन्धिष्ये सेतुना गङ्गां सुखः पन्था भविष्यति। क्लिश्यते हि जनस्तात तरमाणः पुनः पुनः॥
en: Indra said: O sire, I am trying to bridge the Ganga, so that a comfortable way may be made across it. People meet with great inconvenience in again and again crossing and recrossing it.

sn: यवक्रीत उवाच नायं शक्यस्त्वया बड़े महानोघस्तपोधन। अशक्याद् विनिवर्तस्व शक्यमर्थं समारभ॥
en: Yavakrit said : O ascetic, you cannot bridge this mighty river. O Brahmana, desist from what is impracticable; attempt some thing practicable.

sn: इन्द्र उवाच यथैव भवता चेदं तपो वेदाथमुद्यतम्। अशक्यं तद्वदस्माभिरयं भारः समाहितः॥
en: Indra said: I have undertaken this heavy task, as you have engaged yourself in these great austerities to obtain the knowledge of the Vedas, an attempt which can never be successful.

sn: यवक्रीत उवाच यथा तव निरर्थोऽयमारम्भस्त्रिदशेश्वर। तथा यदि ममापीदं मन्यसे पाकशासन॥
en: Yavakrit said : O lord of the celestials, O chastiser of Paka, if you consider these my attempts as fruitless, as yours are,

sn: क्रियतां यद् भवेच्छक्यं त्वया सुरगणेश्वर। वरांश्च मे प्रयच्छान्यान् यैरन्यान् भवितास्म्यति॥
en: O lord of the celestials, be pleased to do for me what is practicable. Favour me with boons by which I may excel all other men.

sn: लोमश उवाच तस्मै प्रादाद् वरानिन्द्र उक्तवान् यान् महातपाः। प्रतिभास्यन्ति ते वेदाः पित्रा सह यथेप्सिताः॥
en: Lomasha said : Indra granted him boons as was asked by the great ascetic. He said, "as you desire it, the Vedas will be manifest in you as well as in your father.

sn: यच्चान्यत् काक्षसे कामं यवक्रीर्गम्यतामिति। स लब्धकामः पितरं समेत्याथेदमब्रवीत्॥
en: Your all other desires also will be fulfilled." Having thus obtained all that he desired, he came to his father and said,

sn: यवक्रीत उवाच प्रतिभास्यन्ति वै वेदा मम तातस्य चोभयोः। अति चान्यान् भविष्यावो वरा लब्धास्तदा मया॥
en: O father, the Vedas will be manifest in you as well as in me. In have obtained boons by which we shall excel all other men.

sn: भरद्वाज उवाच दपस्ते भविता तात वसल्लब्ध्वा यथेप्सितान्। स दर्पपूर्णः कृपणः क्षिप्रमेव विनक्ष्यसि॥
en: Bharadvaja said : O son, as you have obtained all that you desired, you (as a matter of course) will (now) be proud. And when you will be filled with pride, destruction will soon overtake you.

sn: अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीमा गाथा देवैरुदाहृताः। मुनिरासीत् पुरा पुत्र बालधिर्नाम वीर्यवान्॥
en: O son, there is a story told by the celestials as an instance (of this). In the days of yore there was a greatly powerful Rishi, named Valadhi.

sn: स पुत्रशोकादुद्विग्नस्तपस्तेपे सुदुष्करम्। भवेन्मम सुतोऽमर्त्य इति तं लब्धवांश्च सः॥
en: Being afflicted with grief for the death of his son, he performed great asceticism, to get a child who would be immortal. He obtained such a son.

sn: तस्य प्रसादो वै देवैः कृतो न त्वमरैः समः। नामयो विद्यते मर्यो निमित्तायुर्भविष्यति॥
en: But the celestials, though very much favourably disposed towards him, did not still make his son immortal like the celestials. They said that on no condition a mortal can be made immortal.

sn: बालधिरुवाच यथेमे पर्वताः शश्वत् तिष्ठन्ति सुरसत्तमाः। अक्षयास्तन्निमित्तं मे सुतस्यायुभविष्यति॥
en: Valadhi said: O foremost of the celestials, these mountains are existing for an ever-lasting time; indestructible as they are, they will be the instrumental of my son's immortality.

sn: भरद्वाज उवाच तस्य पुत्रस्तदा जज्ञे मेधावी क्रोधनस्तदा। स तच्छ्रुत्वाकरोद् दर्पमृषींश्चैवावमन्यत॥
en: Bharadvaja said : Afterwards a son was born to that Rishi, named Medhavi, who was of very wrathful temper. Having heard all about his birth he grew haughty and began to insult the Rishis.

sn: विकुर्वाणो मुनीनां च व्यचरत् स महीमिमाम्। आससाद महावीर्यं धनुषाक्षं मनीषिणम्॥
en: He roamed over the earth committing various mischiefs to the Rishis. He one day met with the intelligent and greatly powerful (Rishi) Dhanushakha.

sn: तस्यापचने मेधावी तं शशाप स वीर्यवान्। भव भस्मेति चोक्तः स न भस्म समपद्यत॥
en: Medhavi maltreated him; therefore that greatly powerful Rishi cursed him saying, "Be reduced to ashes.” But he was not reduced to ashes.

sn: धनुषाक्षस्तु तं दृष्ट्वा मेधाविनमनामयम्। निमित्तमस्य महिषैर्भेदयामास वीर्यवान्॥
en: Thereupon having seen this, Dhanushakha caused the mountain which was the instrumental cause of his life to be shattered by buffaloes.

sn: स निमित्त विनष्टे तु ममार सहसा शिशुः। तं मृतं पुत्रमादाय विललाप ततः पिता।॥
en: When the instrumental cause of his life was destroyed, the child (Medhavi) suddenly died. Thereupon taking up his dead son the father began to lament.

sn: लालप्यमानं तं दृष्ट्वा मुनयः परमार्तवत्। ऊचुर्वेदविदः सर्वे गाथां यां तां निबोध मे॥
en: Now hear from me the verse that was recited by the Rishis learned in the Vedas when they saw the Rishi thus mourning.

sn: न दिष्टमर्थमत्येतुमीशो मर्त्यः कथंचन। महिषैर्भेदयामासधनुषाक्षो महीधरान्॥
en: "On no condition can a mortal overcome what has been ordained by Fate. Dhanushakha shattered even mountain by buffaloes.”

sn: एवं लब्ध्वा वरान् बाला दर्पपूर्णास्तपस्विनः। क्षिप्रमेव विनश्यन्ति यथा न स्यात् तथा भवान्॥
en: Thus having obtained boons, young ascetics are (generally) filled with pride and perish in no time. Do not become one of them.

sn: एष रेभ्यो महावीर्यः पुत्रौ चास्य तथाविधौ। तं यथा पुत्र नाभ्येषि तथा कुर्यास्त्वतन्द्रितः॥
en: O son, this Raibhya is greatly powerful, so are his two sons. Therefore, be careful never to approach him.

sn: स हि क्रुद्धः समर्थस्त्वां पुत्र पीडयितुं रुषा। रैभ्यश्चापि तपस्वी च कोपनश्च महानृषिः॥
en: O son, this Raibhya is a great Rishi and an ascetic of wrathful temper. If wrathful he can do you harm in anger.

sn: यवक्रीत उवाच एवं करिष्ये मा तापं तात कार्षीः कथंचन। यथा हि मे भवान् मान्यस्तथा रैथ्यः पिता मम॥५९।
en: Yavakrit said : O father, I shall do as you command me. Never be in anxiety for it. As you, my father, deserve to be respected by me, so is Raibhya.

sn: लोमश उवाच उक्त्वा स पितरं श्लक्ष्णं यवक्रीरकुतोभयः। विप्रकुर्वनृषीनन्यानतुष्यत् परया मुदा॥
en: Lomasha said: Having thus replied to his father in sweet words, Yavakrit began fearlessly to take pleasure in wantonly injuring the Rishis.

sn: लोमश उवाच चक्रम्यमाणः स तदा यवक्रीरकुतोभयः। जगाम माधवे मासि रैभ्याश्रमपदं प्रति॥शा
en: Lomasha said: One day in the month of Vaisaka Yavakrit, while fearlessly wandering about, came to the hermitage of Raibhya.

sn: स ददर्शाश्रमे रम्ये पुष्पितदुमभूषिते। विचरन्तीं स्नुषां तस्य किन्नरीमिव भारत॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, he saw in that charming hermitage adorned with blossoming trees the daughter-in-law of Raibhya who was like a Kinnari.

sn: यवक्रीस्तामुवाचेदमुपातिष्ठस्व मामिति। निर्लज्जो लज्जया युक्तां कामेन हतचेतनः॥
en: Having lost his sense through desire, he shamelessly spoke to that bashful maiden saying, “Be attached to me."

sn: सा तस्य शीलमाज्ञाय तस्माच्छापाच्च बिभ्यती। तेजस्वितां च रैभ्यस्य तथेत्युक्त्वाऽऽजगाम ह॥
en: Knowing his character and fearing his course and thinking (also) of the great power of Raibhya, she said, “Be it so" (then) and she went to him.

sn: तत एकान्तमुन्नीय मज्जयामास भारत। आजगाम तदा रैभ्यः स्वमाश्रममरिदमा।५।।
en: O descendant of Bharata, then taking him in private, she kept him hidden. O chastiser of foes, (some time after) Raibhya returned to his hermitage.

sn: रुदतीं च स्नुषां दृष्ट्वा भार्यामाः परावसोः। सान्त्वयश्लक्ष्णया वाचा पर्यपृच्छद् युधिष्ठिर॥
en: O Yudhishthira, seeing his daughter-in-law, Paravasu's wife in tears, he consoled her with sweet words and asked her the cause of her grief,

sn: सा तस्मै सर्वमाचष्ट यवक्रीतभाषितं शुभा। प्रत्युक्तं च यवक्रीतं प्रेक्षापूर्वं तथाऽऽत्मना॥
en: That blessed damsel told him all that Yavakrit had spoken to her and also what she herself had cleverly said to him.

sn: शृण्वानस्यैव रैभ्यस्य यवक्रीत विचेष्टितम्। दहन्निव तदा चेतः क्रोधः समभवन्महान्॥
en: Having heard of this gross misbehaviour of Yavakrit, Raibhya's heart burnt as if in fire and he was filled with great anger.

sn: स तदामन्युनाऽऽविष्टस्तपस्वी कोपनो भृशम्। अवलुच्य जटामेकां जुहावाग्नौ सुसंस्कृते॥
en: Thereupon that great ascetic of wrathful temper, inflamed with anger, tore off a matted lock of his head and with proper rites offered it to the fire.

sn: ततः समभवन्नारी तस्या रूपेण सम्मिता। अवलुच्यापरां चापि जुहावाग्नौ जटां पुनः॥
en: Thereupon rose out of it a female exactly resemble his daughter-in-law. He then again tore off another lock and offered it to the fire.

sn: ततः समभवद् रक्षो घोराक्षं भीमदर्शनम्। अब्रूतां तौ तदा रैभ्यं किं कार्यं करवावहै॥
en: Thereupon rose out of it a fearful Rakshasha of fearful eyes. Those two then spoke thus to Raivya, “What are we to do?"

sn: तावब्रवीदृषिः क्रुद्धो यवक्रीर्वध्यतामिति। जग्मतुस्तौ तथेत्युक्त्वा यवक्रीतजिघांसया॥
en: Thereupon the Rishi said to them in anger, “Go and kill Yavakrit.” (Having been thus ordered) those two said, “Be it to” and went away with the intention of killing Yavakrit.

sn: ततस्तं समुपास्थाय कृत्या सृष्टा महात्मना। कमण्डलुं जहारास्य मोहयित्वेव भारत॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, the female whom the high-souled Rishi created robbed with her charms the sacred water-pot of Yavakrit.

sn: उच्छिष्टं तु यवक्रीतमपकृष्टकमण्डलुम्। तत उद्यतशूलः स राक्षसः समुपाद्रवत्॥
en: The Rakshasha with uplifted spear rushed upon Yavakrit who was robbed of his waterpot and who had thus become unclean.

sn: तमापतन्तं सम्प्रेक्ष्य शूलहस्तं जिघांसया। यवक्री: सहसोत्थाय प्राद्रवद् येन वै सरः॥
en: Seeing him coming with the uplifted spear with the intention of killing him, Yavakrit suddenly rose and ran towards a tank.

sn: जलहीनं सरो दृष्ट्वा यवक्रीस्त्वरितः पुनः। जगाम सरितः सर्वास्ताश्चाप्यासन् विशोषिताः॥
en: Having seen that tank to be without water, Yavakrit went to all the rivers, but they too all were dried up.

sn: स काल्यमानो घोरेण शूलहस्तेन रक्षसा। अग्निहोत्रं पितुर्भीत: सहसा प्रविवेश ह॥
en: Being pursued by the fearful Rakshasha with the uplifted spear, he in great fear, tried to enter his father's room of the sacred fire.

sn: स वै प्रविशमानस्तु शूद्रेणान्धेन रक्षिणा। निगृहीतो बलाद् द्वारि सोऽवातिष्ठत पार्थिव॥
en: O king, he was there repulsed by a blind Shudra door-keeper; and he was stopped at the door and grasped by the man.

sn: निगृहीतं तु शूद्रेण यवक्रीतं स राक्षसः। ताडयामास शूलेन स भिन्नहृदयोऽपतत्॥
en: Having been thus stopped by the Shudra, (he stood motionless) and that Rakshasha hurled his spear at Yavakrit who then fell down pierced in the heart.

sn: यवक्रीतं स हत्वा तु राक्षसो रैम्यमागमत्। अनुज्ञातंस्तु रैभ्येण तया नार्या सहावसत्॥
en: Having killed Yavakrit, that Rakshasha came back to Raivya; and being ordered by Raivya, he lived (there) with his wife (that female).

sn: लोमश उवाच भरद्वाजस्तु कौन्तेय कृत्वा स्वाध्यायमाछिकम्। समित्कलापमादाय प्रविवेश स्वमाश्रयम्॥
en: Lomasha said: O son of Kunti, having collected the sacrificial fuel and after performing the ritual duties of the day Bharadvaja entered his hermitage.

sn: तं स्म दृष्टवा सर्वे प्रत्युत्तिष्ठन्ति पावकाः। न त्वेनमुपतिष्ठन्ति हतपुत्रं तदाग्नथः॥
en: As his son was killed, the (sacrificial) fire, which used to welcome him every day, did not come that day to welcome him.

sn: वैकृतं त्वग्निहोत्रे स लक्षयित्वा महातपाः। तमन्धं शूद्रमासीनं गृहपालमथाब्रवीत्॥
en: Having seen this change in the Agnihotra, that great ascetic thus spoke to that blind Shudra gate-keeper who was seated there.

sn: किं नु मे नाग्नयः शूद्र प्रतिनन्दन्ति दर्शनम्। त्वं चापि न यथापूर्वं कच्चित् क्षेममिहाश्रमे॥
en: "O Shudra, why does not the fire delight on seeing me? You too do not express delight as you always do? Is everything well in the hermitage?

sn: कम्चिन्न रैभ्यं पुत्रो मे गतवानल्पचेतनः। एतदाचक्ष्व मे शीघ्रं न हि शुद्ध्यति मे मनः॥
en: I hope my foolish son had not gone to Raivya? Tell me all this quickly; misgivings fill my mind

sn: शूद्र उवाच रैभ्यं यातो नूनमयं पुत्रस्ते मन्दचेतनः। तथा हि निहतः शेते राक्षसेन बलीयसा॥
en: Shudra said: Your foolish son went to the great sage and therefore he lies prostrate being killed by a powerful Rakshasha.

sn: प्रकाल्यमानस्तेनायं शृलहप्तेन रक्षसा। अग्न्यागारं प्रति द्वारि मया दोऱ्यां निवारितः॥
en: He was pursued by a Rakshasha with uplifted spear; and he attempted to enter this room, but he was stopped at the door by me.

sn: ततः स विहताशोऽत्र जलकामोऽशुचिर्भुवम्। निहतः सोऽतिवेगेन शूलहस्तेन रक्षसा॥
en: Thereupon being desirous to obtain water (in this room) in an unclean state, (he tried to force a passage, but his way being barred with my arms), he stood hopeless and (at that state) he was killed by the Rakshasha who held a spear in his hand.

sn: भरद्वाजस्तु तच्छ्रुत्वा शूद्रस्य विप्रियं महत्। गतासुं पुत्रमादाय विललाप सुदुःखितः॥
en: Lomasha said: Having hcard from the Shudra, of this great calamity, Bharadvaja, embracing his dead son, began to lament for him.

sn: भरद्वाज उवाच ब्राह्मणानां किलार्थाय ननु त्वं तप्तवांस्तपः। द्विजानामनधीता वै वेदाः सम्प्रतिभान्त्विति॥
en: Bharadvaja said : For the good of the Brahmana you performed the severe austerities, so that the Vedas unstudied by any Brahmanas might be manifest in you.

sn: तथा कल्याणशीलस्त्वं ब्राह्मणेषु महात्मसु। अनागाः सर्वभूतेषु कर्कशत्वमुपेयिवान्॥
en: Your conduct towards the Brahmanas had always been for their good and you had been always innocent in regard to all creatures. But at last you turned to be rude.

sn: प्रतिषिद्धो मया तात रैभ्यावसथदर्शनात्। गतवानेव तं द्रष्टुं कालान्तकयमोपमम्॥
en: O child, I prohibited you from visiting the residence of Raivya, but you went there to visit it which was like the all-destroying death.

sn: यः स जानन महातेजा वृद्धस्यैकं ममात्मजम्। गतवानेव कोपस्य वशं परमदुर्मतिः॥
en: That greatly effulgent one knows me to be old and (he knew also) that I had only one son. But that wicked-minded one still became subject to anger.

sn: पुत्रशोकमनुप्राप्त एष रैभ्यस्य कर्मणा। त्यक्ष्यामि त्वामृते पुत्र प्राणानिष्टतमान् भुवि॥
en: I have been afflicted with the grief at my son's death on account of Raivya. O son, for your death I shall give up my life which is the most precious thing in the world.

sn: यथाहं पुत्रशोकेन देहं त्यक्ष्यामि किल्विषी। तथा ज्येष्ठः सुतो रैभ्यं हिंस्याच्छीघ्रमनागसम्॥
en: As I give up my life on account of the gricf at the death of my son, so will the eldest son of Raivya kill him, though he would be innocent.

sn: सुखिनो वै नरा येषां जात्या पुत्रो न विद्यते। ते पुत्रशोकमप्राप्य विचरन्ति यथासुखम्॥
en: Happy are those to whom children are never born! Without experiencing the grief at their son's death, they happily move about.

sn: ये तु पुत्रकृताच्छोकाद् भृशं व्याकुलचेतसः। शपन्तीष्टान् सखीनार्तास्तेभ्यः पापतरो नु कः॥
en: Who can in this world be more sinful than those, who from the grief at their son's death and thus becoming deprived of their sense, curse their dearest friends?

sn: परासुश्च सुतो दृष्टः शप्तश्चेष्टः सखा मया। ईदृशीमापदं कोऽत्र द्वितीयोऽनुभविष्यति॥
en: Having seen my son dead, I have cursed my dearest friend. What second man is there who mects with such a (grcat) calamity.

sn: लोमश उवाच विलप्यैवं बहुविधं भरद्वाजोऽदहत् सुतम्। सुसमिद्धं ततः पश्चात् प्रविवेश हुताशनम्॥
en: Lomasha said : Having thus variously lamented for his son, Bharadvaja cremated him and then he himself entered a blazing fire.

sn: लोमश उवाच एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु बृहद्युम्नो महीपतिः। सत्रं तेने महाभागो रैभ्ययाज्य: प्रतापवान्॥
en: Lomasha said: About this time, the highly blessed ruler of earth, the greatly powerful Brihadyumna, the Yajamana of Raivya performed a sacrifice.

sn: तेन रैभ्यस्य वै पुत्रावर्वावसुपरावसू। वृतौ संहायौ सत्रार्थं बृहद्द्युम्नेनधीमता॥
en: The two sons of Raivya, named Arvavasu and Paravasu, were employed by the intelligent Brihadyumna to assist him in the sacrifice.

sn: तत्र तौ समनुज्ञातौ पित्रा कौन्तेय जग्मतुः। आश्रमे त्वभवद् रैभ्यो भार्या चैव परावसोः॥
en: O son of Kunti, thercupon those two, taking the permission of their father, went away. Raivya remained in the hermitage with Paravasu's wife.

sn: अथावलोककोऽगच्छद् गृहानेकः परावसुः। कृष्णाजिनेन संवीतं ददर्श पितरं वने।॥
en: One day in order to see his wife, Paravasu alone went to the hermitage and he saw his father in the forest, covered with black dcerskin.

sn: जघन्यरात्रे निद्रान्धः सावशेषे तमस्यपि। चरन्तं गहनेऽरण्ये मेने स पितरं मृगम्॥
en: The night was far advanced and dark and he was drowsy with sleep. When roaming in the forest, he took his father for a deer.

sn: मृगं तु मन्यमानेन पिता वै तेन हिंसितः। अकामयानेन तदा शरीरत्राणमिच्छता॥
en: Mistaking his father for a dcer, he unintentionally killed him with the desire of protecting his own body.

sn: करोतु वै भवान् सत्रं तस्य स प्रेतकार्याणि कृत्वा सर्वाणि भारत। पुनरागम्य तत् सत्रमब्रवीद् भ्रातरं वचः॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, after performing all his funeral rites, he came again to the sacrifice and spoke these words to his brother.

sn: इदं कर्म न शक्तस्त्वं वोढुमेकः कथंचन। मया तु हिंसितस्तातो मन्यमानेन तं मृगम्॥
en: Paravasu said: You will never be able to perform this act alone. I have killed our father, mistaking him for a deer.

sn: सोऽस्मदर्थे व्रतं तात चर त्वं ब्रह्महिंसनम्। समर्थोऽप्यहमेकाकी कर्म कर्तुमिदं मुने॥
en: O brother, on my behalf, observe a vow prescribed in the case of killing a Brahmana. O Rishi, I shall alone be able to perform this act.

sn: अर्वावसुरुवाच बृहद्युम्नस्यधीमतः। ब्रह्मवध्यां चरिष्येऽहं त्वदर्थं नियतेन्द्रियः॥
en: Arvavasu said: Then perform the sacrifice of the intelligent Brihadyumna. On your behalf, I shall observe the vow prescribed in the case of killing a Brahmana by subduing my senses.

sn: लोमश उवाच स तस्य ब्रह्मवध्यायाः पारं गत्वा युधिष्ठिर। अर्वावसुस्तदा सत्रमाजगाम पुनर्मुनिः॥
en: Lomasha said : ( Yudhishthira, having observed the vow prescribed in the case of killing a Brahmana, Arvavasu, the Rishi, again came back to the sacrifice.

sn: ततः परावसुर्दृष्ट्वा भ्रातरं समुपस्थितम्। बृहद्युम्नमुवाचेदं वचनं हषगद्गदम्॥
en: Thereupon having seen his brother come back again, Paravasu spoke these words, his voice choked with delight.

sn: एष ते ब्रह्महा यज्ञं मा द्रष्टुं प्रविशेदिति। ब्रह्महा प्रेक्षितेनापि पीडयेत् त्वामसंशयम्॥
en: "See that this killer of a Brahmana may not enter your sacrifice. Do not also look at him, for even a glance at a killer of a Brahmana can certainly do you harm."

sn: लोमश उवाच तच्छ्रुत्वैव तदा राजा प्रेष्यानाह स विट्यते। प्रेष्यैरुत्सार्यमाणस्तु राजन्नर्वावसुस्तदा॥ न मया ब्रह्महत्येयं कृतेत्याह पुनः पुनः। उच्यमानोऽसकृत्प्रेष्यैर्ब्रह्महन्निति भारत॥
en: ruler of earth, O descendant of Bharata, as soon as the king heard this, he ordered his men (to turn him out). Being driven out by the king's men and being repeatedly called by thein as the slayer of Brahmana, Arvavasu again and again cried, “It is not I that killed a Brahmana.'

sn: नैव स्म प्रतिजानाति ब्रह्मवध्यां स्वयंकृताम्। मम भ्रात्रा कृतमिदं मया स परिमोक्षितः॥
en: He did not also admit, that he had observed the vow for his own sake. (He said), “My brother did it and I have freed him from that sin."

sn: स तथा प्रवदन् क्रोधात् तैश्च प्रेष्यैः प्रभाषितः। तूष्णीं जगाम ब्रह्मर्षिर्वनमेव महातपाः॥
en: Having said this in anger and having been reprimanded by the king's men, that Brahmana Rishi, that great ascetic, became silent; and he then went away to the forest.

sn: उग्रं तप: समास्थाय दिवाकरमथाश्रितः। रहस्यवेदं कृतवान् सूर्यस्य द्विजसत्तमः॥ मूर्तिमांस्तं ददर्शाथ स्वयमग्रभुगव्ययः। लोमश उवाच प्रीतास्तस्याभवन् देवाः कर्मणार्वावसोनूप॥
en: Performing severe austerities, he took protection in the sun. Thereupon the mystery of the sun revealed in him and that eternal deity appeared before him in an embodied form. O king, the celestials were exceedingly pleased with that act of Arvavasu.

sn: तं ते प्रवरयामासुर्निरासुश्च परावसुम्। ततो देवा वरं तस्मै ददुरग्निपुरोगमाः॥
en: They appointed him as the chief priest of the sacrifice and caused Paravasu to be dismissed. Then the celestials with Agni at the head, bestowed upon him boons.

sn: स चापि वरयामास पितुरुत्थानमात्मनः। अनागस्त्वं ततो भ्रातुः पितुश्चास्मरणं वधे॥
en: He too asked the boons that his father might be restored to life. He also prayed that his brother might be freed from the sin of killing his father;

sn: भरद्वाजस्य चोत्थानं यवक्रीतस्य चोभयोः। प्रतिष्ठां चापि वेदस्य सौरस्य द्विजसत्तमः। एवमस्त्विति तं देवाः प्रोचुश्चापि वरान् ददुः॥
en: (And also) that Bharadvaja and Yavakrit, both might be restored to life and that the Solar revelation might be famous.

sn: ततः प्रादुर्बभूवुस्ते सर्व एव युधिष्ठिर। अथाब्रवीद् यवक्रीतो देवाग्निपुरोगमान्॥
en: O Yudhishthira, the celestials said, “Be it so"; and they bestowed on him the boons. Thereupon all of them were restored to life. Then Yavakrit spoke thus to the celestials with Agni at their head.

sn: समधीतं मया ब्रह्म व्रतानि चरितानि च। कथं च रैभ्यः शक्तो मामधीयानं तपस्विनम्॥
en: “I have obtained the knowledge of all the Vedas, I have also observed vows. How came it then that Raivya killed me who am an ascetic!

sn: तथायुक्तेन विधिना निहन्तुममरोत्तमाः। देवा ऊचुः मैवं कृथा यवक्रीत यथा वदसि वै मुने। ऋते गुरुमधीता हि सुखं वेदास्त्वया पुरा॥ अनेन तु गुरून् दुःखात् तोषयित्वाऽऽत्मकर्मणा। कालेन महता क्लेशाद् ब्रह्माधिगतमुत्तमम्॥
en: O foremost of the celestials, how could he then kill me in that way?" "O Yavakrit, O Rishi, do not think in the way you speak, thinking that you easily learnt the Vedas without the help of a preceptor and Raivya obtained the excellent Vedas after great exertions and long time.

sn: लोमश उवाच यवक्रीतमथोक्त्वैवं देवाः साग्निपुरोगमाः। संजीवयित्वा तान् सर्वान् पुनर्जग्मुस्त्रिविष्टपम्॥
en: Having said this to Yavakrit, the celestials with Indra at their head restored them all to life and went away to heaven.

sn: आश्रमस्तस्य पुण्योऽयं सदापुष्पफलद्रुमः। अत्रोष्य राजशादूल सर्वं पापं प्रमोक्ष्यसि॥
en: O foremost of kings, here is the sacred hermitage of that Rishi) adorned with trees full of flowers and fruits (that grow) at all seasons. It cleanses all sins.

sn: लोमश उवाच उशीरबीजं मैनाकं गिरि श्वेतं च भारत। समतीतोऽसि कौन्तेय कालशैलं च पार्थिव।।।।
en: Lomasha said: O descendant of Bharata, O son of Kunti, O ruler of earth, you have now left behind the mountains Ushinara, Mainaka, Shveta and Kala.

sn: एषा गङ्गा सप्तविधा राजते भरतर्षभ। स्थानं विरजसं पुण्यं यत्राग्निर्नित्यमिध्यते॥
en: O foremost of the Bharata race, here flow before you the seven Ganges. This spot is (very) pure and holy. Here Agni unceasingly blazes forth.

sn: एतद् वै मानुषेणाद्य न शक्यं द्रष्टुमद्भुतम्। समाधि कुरुताव्यग्रास्तीर्थान्येतानि द्रक्ष्यथ॥
en: No man is able to get a sight of this wonder. Therefore concentrate your mind, so that you may with rapt attention see these Tirthas.

sn: एतद् द्रक्ष्यसि देवानामाक्रीडं चरणाङ्कितम्। अतिक्रान्तोऽसि कौन्तेय कालशैलं च पर्वतम्॥
en: O son of Kunti, as we have passed the Kaola mountains you will now see the play-grounds of the celestials, marked with their foot-prints.

sn: श्वेतं गिरि प्रवेक्ष्यामो मन्दरं चैव पर्वतम्। यत्र माणिवरो यक्षः कुबेरचैव यक्षराट्॥
en: We shall now ascend Shveta Giri and the Mandara mountain, where dwell Manivadra, Yaksha and Kubera, the king of the Yakshas.

sn: अष्टाशीतिसहस्राणि गन्धर्वाः शीघ्रगामिनः। तथा किंपुरुषा राजन् यक्षाश्चैव चतुर्गुणाः॥ अनेकरूपसंस्थाना नानाप्रहरणाश्च ते। यक्षेन्द्रं मनुजश्रेष्ठ माणिभद्रमुपासते॥
en: O king, O foremost of men, here at this place eight thousand swift-going Gandharvas and as many Kimpurushes and four times as many Yakshas of various shapes, wielding many weapons, wait upon the chief of Yaksha Manivadra.

sn: तेषामृद्धिरतीवात्र गतौ वायुसमाश्च ते। स्थानात् प्रच्यावयेयुर्ये देवराजमपि ध्रुवम्॥
en: In this place their power is very great and their speed is that of the wind. They are certainly capable of displacing the king of the celestials from his seat.

sn: तैस्तात बलिभिर्गुप्ता यातुधानैश्च रक्षिताः। दुर्गमाः पर्वताः पार्थ समाधि परमं कुरु॥
en: O child, O son of Pritha, protected by them and watched over by the Rakshashas, these mountains have become inaccessible. Therefore perform the great concentration of mind.

sn: कुबेरसचिवाश्चान्ये सैद्रा मैत्राश्च राक्षसाः। तैः समेष्याम कौन्तेय संयतो विक्रमेण च॥
en: O son of Kunti, here are the ministers of Kubera and his other friends who are all fearful Rakshashas. We shall have to meet them therefore gather up all your prowess.

sn: कैलासः पर्वतो राजन् षड्योजनसमुच्छ्रितः। यत्र देवा समायान्ति विशाला यत्र भारत॥
en: O king, the Kailasa mountain is six yojanas in height. O descendant of Bharata, there is a large Jujube tree. Here often are the celestials,

sn: असंख्येयास्तु कौन्तेय यक्षराक्षसकिनराः। नागाः सुपर्णा गन्धर्वाः कुबेरसदनं प्रति॥
en: In great members, also the Yakshas, the Rakshasha, the Kinnaras, the Nagas, the Suparnas, the Gandharvas when they go to the palace of Kubera.

sn: तान् विगाहस्व पार्थाद्य तपसा च दमेन च। रक्ष्यमाणो मया राजन् भीमसेनबलेन च॥
