en: O king, protected by me, as well as by the prowess of Bhimasena and also in consequence of your own asceticism and sclf-command, do mix with them today.

sn: स्वस्ति ते वरुणो राजा यमश्च समितिंजयः। गङ्गा च यमुना चैव पर्वतश्च दधातु ते॥ मरुतश्च सहाश्विभ्यां सरितश्च सरांसि च। त्वस्ति देवासुरेभ्यश्च वसुभ्यश्च महाद्युते॥
en: May king Varuna, that conqueror in battles, Yama, Ganga and Yamuna, this mountain, the Marutas, the Ashinas, all rivers and lakes, vouchsafe to you safety. () greatly effulgent one, may you have safety from the celestials, the Asuras and the Vasus.

sn: इन्द्रस्य जाम्बूनपर्वताद् वै शृणोमि घोषं तव देवि गङ्गे। गोपायैनं त्वं सुभगे गिरिभ्यः। सर्वाजमीढापचितं नरेन्द्रम्॥
en: "O Goddess Ganga, I hear your roar from this golden mountain which is sacred to Indra. (O blessed one, protect, in this mountain, this ruler of men adored of all the Ajamira race.

sn: ददस्व शर्म प्रविविक्षतोऽस्य शैलानिमाछैलसुते नृपम्य। उक्त्वा तथा सागरगां स विप्रो यत्तो भवस्वेति शशास पार्थम्॥
en: O daughter of the mountain, this king is about to enter this mountainous regions. Therefore confer upon him your protection." Having thus addressed that ocean-going river, that Brahinana said to the son of Pritha to be careful.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच अपूर्वोऽयं सम्भ्रमो लोमशस्य कृष्णां सर्वे रक्षत मा प्रमादम्। देशो ह्ययं दुर्गतमो मतोऽस्य तस्मात् परं शौचमिहाचरध्वम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said : This confusion of Lomasha is astonishing. Therefore of you protect Krishna (Draupadi). Do not be careless. He knows very well this place as being difficult of access. Therefore practise here the greatest purity.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततोऽब्रवीद् भीममुदारवीर्य कृष्णां यत्तः पालय भीमसेन। शून्येऽर्जुनेऽसंनिहिते च तात त्वामेव कृष्णा भजते भयेषु॥
en: Vaishampayana said : He then thus spoke to the greatly powerful Bhima, "O Bhimasena, protect protect Krishna (Draupadi) with all care. O child, whether Arjuna be near or away, Krishna (Draupadi) always seeks your protection when in fear.”

sn: ततो महात्मा स यमौ समेत्य मूर्धन्युपाघ्राय विमृज्य गात्रे। उवाच तौ बाप्पकलं स राजा मा भैष्टमागच्छतमप्रमत्तौ।॥
en: Thereupon the high-souled, king (Yudhishthira), coming to the twins (Nakula and Sahadeva) and smelling their heads and rubbing their body, said, "Do not fear. Proceed with caution."

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच अन्तर्हितानि भूतानि बलवन्ति महान्ति च। अग्निना तपसा चैव शक्यं गन्तुं वृकोदर।॥
en: Yudhishthira said: O Vrikodara, there are in this place, many invisible beings who are all powerful and huge. We shall however be able to pass through them by the merit of our Agnihotra and asceticism.

sn: संनिवतय कौन्तेय क्षुत्पिपासे बलाश्रयात्। ततो बलं च दाक्ष्यं च संश्रयस्व वृकोदर॥
en: O son of Kunti, by collecting your prowess, restrain your hunger and thirst, O Vrikodara, have recourse to your strength and cleverness,

sn: ऋषेस्त्वया श्रुतं वाक्यं कैलास पर्वतं प्रति। बुद्ध्या प्रपश्य कौन्तेय कथं कृष्णा गमिष्यति॥
en: O son of Kunti, you have heard what the Rishi (Lomasha) has said about the Kailasa mountain. After due deliberation think, how Krishna (Draupadi) should pass through is place.

sn: अथवा सहदेवेनधौम्येन च समं विभो। सूतैः पौरोगवैश्चैव सर्वेश्च परिचारकैः॥ रथैरश्चैश्च ये चान्ये विप्राः क्लेशासहाः पथि। सर्वैस्त्वं सहितो भीम निवर्तस्वायतेक्षण॥
en: Or, O exalted Bhima of large eyes, you should better return with Sahadeva, with Dhaumya, with all our charioteers, cooks, scrvants, cars, horses and also the Brahmanas who are worn out with travel.

sn: त्रयो वयं गमिष्यामो लध्वाहारा यतव्रताः। अहं च नकुलश्चैव लोमशश्च महातपाः॥
en: The great ascetic Lomasha, Nakula and I shall proceed living on light food and observing vows.

sn: ममागमनमाकाङ्क्षन् गङ्गाद्वारे समाहितः। वसेह द्रौपदी रक्षन् यावदागमनं मम॥
en: In expectation of my return, wait carefully at the source of the Ganges and protect Draupadi till I come back.

sn: भीम उवाच राजपुत्री श्रमेणार्ता दुःखार्ता चैव भारत। व्रजत्येव हि कल्याणी श्वेतवाहदिदृक्षया॥
en: Bhima said: O descendant of Bharata, although this blessed princess is afflicted with toil she easily proceeds along in the hope of seeing Shvetavahana (Arjuna).

sn: तव चाप्यरतिस्तीता वर्तते तमपश्यतः। गुडाकेशं महात्मानं संग्रामेष्वपलायिनम्॥
en: Your dejection also is very great at not seeing the high-souled Gudukesha (Arjuna) who never retreats from battle.

sn: किं पुनः सहदेवं च मां च कृष्णां च भारत। द्विजाः कामं निवर्तन्तां सर्वे च परिचारकाः॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, you will be more dejected if you do not see Sahadeva, Krishna (Draupadi) and myself. Let the Brahmanas return with our servants,

sn: सूताः पौरोगवाश्चैव यं च मन्येत नो भवान्। न ह्यहं हातुमिच्छामि भवन्तमिह कर्हिचित्॥
en: Charioteers, cooks and others whom you may command. I shall never leave you here.

sn: शैलेऽस्मिन् राक्षसाकीर्णे दुर्गेषु विषमेषु च। इयं चापि महाभागा राजपुत्री पतिव्रता।॥
en: In these rugged and inaccessible mountainous regions infested by Rakshashas. This greatly blessed princess, ever devoted to her husbands,

sn: त्वामृते पुरुषव्याघ्र नोत्सहेद् विनिवर्तितुम्। तथैव सहदेवोऽयं सततं त्वामनुव्रतः॥
en: O foremost of men, will not return without you. This Sahadeva is always devoted to you;

sn: न जातु विनिवर्तेत मनोज्ञो ह्यहमस्य वै। अपि चात्र महाराज सव्यसाचिदिदृक्षया॥ सर्वे लालसभूताः स्म तस्माद् यास्यामहे सह। यद्यशक्यो स्थैर्गन्तुं शैलोऽयं बहुकन्दरः॥
en: O great king, I know his character well; he will never return (without you). We are all cager to see Savyasachi (Arjuna) and therefore we will all go together. If we cannot go on our cars over this mountain of many defiles,

sn: पद्भिरेव गमिष्यामो मा राजन् विमना भव। अहं वहिष्ये पाञ्चालीं यत्र यत्र न शक्ष्यति॥
en: We shall walk on foot. O King, you need not trouble yourself about it. I shall carry the Panchala Princess, wherever and whenever she will be incapable of walking.

sn: इति मे वर्तते बुद्धिर्मा राजन् विमना भव। सुकुमारौ तथा वीरौ माद्रीनन्दिकरावुभौ। दुर्गे संतारयिष्यामि यत्राशक्तौ भविष्यतः॥
en: I have decided upon this; therefore do not trouble yourself about it. I shall carry these two heroes, the tender sons of Madri, the delight of their mother, over difficult tracts, wherever they will be incapable of walking.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच एवं ते भाषमाणस्य बलं भीमाभिवर्धताम्। यत् त्वमुत्सहसे वोढुं पाञ्चालीं च यशस्विनीम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said: O Bhima, let your strength increase for your speaking thus. You boldly undertake to carry the illustrious Panchala princess.

sn: यमजौ चापि भद्रं ते नैतन्यत्र विद्यते। बलं तव यशश्चैवधर्मः कीर्तिश्च वर्धताम्॥
en: And also the twins (Nakula and Sahadeva). Be blessed; such courage does not exist in others. May your strength, fame and virtue increase.

sn: यत् त्वमुत्सहसे नेतुं भ्रातरौ सह कृष्णया। मा ते ग्लानिर्महाबाहो मा च तेऽस्तु पराभवः॥
en: O mighty-armed hero, as you propose to carry our two brothers will Krishna (Draupadi), let not exhaustion or defeat come to you.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततः कृष्णाब्रवीद् वाक्यं प्रहसन्ती मनोरमा। गमिष्यामि न संतापः कार्यो मां प्रति भारत॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Thereupon the charming Krishna (Draupadi) smilingly said, “O descendant of Bharata, I shall go, you need not be anxious for me."

sn: लोमश उवाच तपसा शक्यते गन्तुं पर्वतो गन्धमादनः। तपसा चैव कौन्तेय सर्वे योक्ष्यामहे वयम्॥
en: Lomasha said: O son of Kunti, one can go to Gandamadana by asceticism; therefore we shall all practise asceticism,

sn: नकुलः सहदेवश्च भीमसेनश्च पार्थिवा अहं च त्वं च कौन्तेय द्रक्ष्यामः श्वेतवाहनम्॥
en: O king, O son of Kunti, Nakula, Sahadeva, Bhimsena, you and myself then shall see Shvetavahana (Arjuna).

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवं सम्भाषमाणास्ते सुबाहुविषयं महत्। ददृशुर्मुदिता राजन् प्रभूतगजवाजिमत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : O king, having thus conversed, they saw with delight the extensive kingdom of Suvaka abounding in horses and elephants.

sn: किराततङ्गणाकीर्णं पुलिन्दशतसंकुलम्। हिमवत्यमरैर्जुष्टं बह्वाश्चर्यसमाकुलम्। सुबाहुश्चापि तान् दृष्ट्वा पूजया प्रत्यगृहणत॥ विषयान्ते कुलिन्दानामीश्वरः प्रीतिपूर्वकम्। ततस्ते पूजितास्तेन सर्व एव सुखोषिताः॥
en: Densely inhabited by the Kiratas and the Tanganas, crowded by hundred of Pulindas, frequented by the celestials and full of wonders. Seeing them Suvaka, the king of the Pulindas, received them in due honour and with great cheerfulness, on the frontier of his kingdom. They, too being thus received, lived there (for some time) with great comfort.

sn: प्रतस्थुर्विमले सूर्ये हिमवन्तं गिरि प्रति। इन्द्रसेनमुखांश्चापि भृत्यान् पौरोगवांस्तथा॥ सूदांश्च पारिबहाँश्च द्रौपद्याः सर्वशो नृप। राज्ञः कुलिन्दाधिपते: परिदाय महारथाः॥ पद्भिरेव महावीर्या ययुः कौरवनन्दनाः। ते शनैः प्राद्रवन् सर्वे कृष्णया सह पाण्डवाः। तस्माद् देशात् सुसंहृष्टा द्रष्टुकामाधनंजयम्॥
en: They started for the Himalaya mountain when the sun shone brightly in the sky. Having left in the care of the king of the Pulindas all their servants, Indrasena and others, also the cooks and stewards and also all accoutrements of Draupadi and also everything else, those mighty car-warriors, those greatly powerdescendants of Kuru started for that country. They proceeded cautiously with Krishna (Draupadi); they were all cheerful in the expectation of seeing Arjuna.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच भीमसेन यमौ चोभौ पाञ्चालि च निबोधत। नास्ति भूतस्य नाशो वै पश्यतास्मान् वनेचरान्॥
en: Yudhishthira said: O Bhimasena, O Panchala princess, O twins, hear. Nothing of creatures perishes. Behold, we are now rangers of forest.

sn: दुर्बला: क्लेशिताः स्मेति यद् ब्रुवामेतरेतरम्। अशक्येऽपि व्रजामो यद्धनंजयदिदृक्षया।॥
en: Weak and fatigued as we are, we have to help one another and pass over difficult places. Though incapable, yet we must proceed in order to see Dhananjaya (Arjuna).

sn: तन्मे दहति गात्राणि तूलराशिमिवानलः। यच्च वीरं न पश्यामिधनंजयमुपान्तिकात्॥
en: It (his absence) burns my body as fire does a heap of cotton. I do not see the heroic Dhananjaya at my side.

sn: तस्य दर्शनतृष्णं मां सानुजं वनमास्थितम्। याज्ञसेन्याः परामर्श स च वीर दहत्युत॥
en: With the thirst for seeing him, I live with my younger brothers in the forest. O hero, the great oppression committed on Yajnaseni (Draupadi) also burns me.

sn: नकुलात् पूर्वजं पार्थं न पश्याम्यमितौजसम्। अजेयमुग्रधन्वानं तेन तप्ये वृकोदर॥
en: O Vrikodara, I do not see the immediate elder of Nakula, the immeasurably powerful Partha (Arjuna) who is invincible and who is the wielder of the strongest bow. For this, O Vrikodara, I am miserable.

sn: तीर्थानि चैव रम्याणि वनानि च सरांसि चा चरामि सह युष्माभिस्तस्य दर्शनकाझया।॥ पञ्चवर्षाण्यहं वीरं सत्यसंधंधनंजयम्। यन्न पश्यामि बीभत्सुं तेन तप्ये वृकोदर॥
en: In order to see that hero, Dhananjaya firm in truthfulness, I have been wandering with you for these five years in various Tirthas, in charming forests and lakes. As I do not still see Vibhatsu (Arjuna)O Vrikodara I am miserable.

sn: तं वै श्यामं गुडाकेशं सिंहविक्रान्तगामिनम्। न पश्यामि महाबाहुं तेन तप्ये वृकोदर॥
en: As I do not see the long armed, black, curlyhaired, lion-like (Arjuna), O Vrikodara, I am miserable.

sn: कृतास्त्रं निपुणं युद्धेऽप्रतिमानधनुष्मताम्। न पश्यामि कुरुश्रेष्ठ तेन तप्ये वृकोदर॥
en: As I do not see that foremost of the Kurus, accomplished in arms, skillful in fight and matchless among bowmen, O Vrikodara I am miserable.

sn: चरन्तमरिसंघेषु काले क्रुद्धमिवान्तकम्। प्रभिन्नमिव मातङ्गं सिंहस्कन्धंधनंजयम्॥ यः स शक्रादनवरो वीर्येण द्रविणेन च। यमयोः पूर्वजः पार्थः श्वेताश्वोऽमितविक्रमः॥ दुःखेन महताविष्टस्तं न पश्यामि फाल्गुनम्। अजेयमुग्रधन्वानं तेन तप्ये वृकोदर॥
en: As I, though very much distressed, do not see that son of Pritha, Dhananjaya who was born under the influence of the constellation Falguni, who ranges amidst enemies like angry Yama at the time of the universal dissolution, who possesses the prowess of an elephant with the juice trickling down its temple, who has lion-like shoulder, who is in no way inferior to Sakra (Indra) in energy and prowess, who is elder of the twins, who rides on white horses, who is immeasurably powerful, invincible and the wielder of the strongest bow, O Vrikodara, I am miserable.

sn: सततं यः क्षमाशीलः क्षिप्यमाणोऽप्यणीयसा। ऋजुमार्गप्रपन्नस्य शर्मदाताभयस्य च॥
en: He is forgiving, even when he is insulted by the meanest foe. He confers benefit and protection upon the men who follow the righteous path.

sn: स तु जिह्मप्रवृत्तस्य माययाभिजिघांसतः। अपि वज्रधरस्यापि भवेत् कालविषोपमः॥
en: To crafty men who want to injure him, even if he be the wielder of thunder (Indra), he is like a virulently poisonous snake.

sn: शत्रोरपि प्रपन्नस्य सोऽनृशंसः प्रतापवान्। दाताभयस्य बीभत्सुरमितात्मा महाबलः॥
en: The high-souled and Immeasurably powerful Vivatsu shows mercy and extends protection even to an enemy when he is fallen.

sn: सर्वेषामाश्रयोऽस्माकं रणेऽरीणां प्रमर्दिता। आहर्ता सर्वरत्नानां सर्वेषां नः सुखावहः॥
en: He is the refuge of us all and he destroys his enemies in battle. He can gather all wealth and he keeps us all happy.

sn: रत्नानि यस्य वीर्येण दिव्यान्यासन् पुरा मम। बहूनि बहुजातीनि यानि प्राप्तः सुयोधनः॥
en: It was through his prowess I formerly possessed various kinds of precious jewels which Suyodhana (Duryodhana) has now got.

sn: यस्य बाहुबलाद् वीर सभा चासीत् पुरा मम। सर्वरत्नमयी ख्याता त्रिषु लोकेषु पाण्डव॥
en: O hero, O son of Pandu, it was through his prowess I formerly possessed the Assembly Hall adorned with all sorts of jewels and celebrated over the three worlds.

sn: वासुदेवसमं वीर्ये कार्तवीर्यसमं युधि। अजेयममितं युद्धे तं न पश्यामि फाल्गुनम्॥
en: He is like Vasudeva in prowess, he is invincible and matchless in battle like Kartavirya. I do not (now) see that Falguni.

sn: संकर्षणं महावीर्यं त्वां च भीमापराजितम्। अनुयातः स्ववीर्येण वासुदेवं च शत्रुहा।॥
en: That chastiser of foes (Arjuna) is equal to the invincible and most powerful Sankarsana (Baladeva) and Vasudeva (Krishna).

sn: यस्य बाहुबले तुल्यः प्रभावे च पुरंदरः। जवे वायुर्मुखे सोमः क्रोधे मृत्युः सनातनः॥
en: He is equal to Purandara (Indra) in strength of arms and prowess; he is equal to the wind in speed, to the moon in beauty and to the eternal Death in anger.

sn: ते वयं तं नरव्याघ्रं सर्वे वीर दिदृक्षवः। प्रवेक्ष्यामो महाबाहो पर्वतं गन्धमादनम्॥
en: O mighty armed one, in order to see that hero, that foremnost of men, we shall all go to the Gandainadana mountain.

sn: विशाला बदरी यत्र नरनारायणाश्रमः। तं सदाध्युषितं यःक्ष्यामो गिरिमुत्तमम्॥
en: In which is situated the hermitage Nara and Narayana and on which stands the great Badari tree. It is inhabited by the Yakshas. We shall see that excellent mountain.

sn: कुबेरनलिनी रम्यां राक्षसैरभिसेविताम्। पद्भिरेव गमिष्यामस्तप्यमाना महत् तपः॥
en: Practising great asceticism, we shall go walking to the charming lake of Kubera guarded by the Rakshashas.

sn: न च यानवता शक्यो गन्तुं देशो वृकोदर। न नृशंसेन लुब्धेन नाप्रशान्तेन भारत॥
en: O Vrikodara, no vehicle can go to that place. O descendant of Bharata, no cruel, avaricious and hot-tempered man can go there.

sn: तत्र सर्वे गमिष्यामो भीमार्जुनगवेषिणः। सायुधा बद्धनिस्त्रिंशाः सार्धं विप्रैर्महाव्रतैः॥
en: O Bhima, in order to see Arjuna, we shall all go there guiding on our swords and wielding our bows. We shall be accompanied by Brahmanas of strict vows.

sn: मक्षिकादंशमशकान् सिंहान् व्याघ्रान् सरीसृपान्। प्राप्नोत्यनियतः पार्थ नियतस्तान् न पश्यति॥
en: O son of Pritha, the sinful men meet there flies, gad-flies, mosquitoes, tigers, lions and reptiles, but pure-souled men do not meet them.

sn: ते वयं नियतात्मानः पर्वतं गन्धमादनम्। प्रवेक्ष्यामो मिताहाराधनंजयदिदृक्षवः॥
en: Therefore with regulated diet and with subdued passions, we to the Gandamadana with the desire of seeing Dhananjaya. shall go

sn: लोमश उवाच द्रष्टारः पर्वताः सर्वे नद्यः सपुरकाननाः। तीर्थानि चैव श्रीमन्ति स्पृष्टं च सलिल करैः॥
en: Lomasha said: You have seen many mountains and rivers, towns and forests and also many charming Tirthas, the sacred water of which you have touched with your hands.

sn: पर्वतं मन्दरं दिव्यमेष पन्थाः प्रयास्यति। समाहिता निरुद्विग्नाः सर्वे भवत पाण्डवाः॥
en: O sons of Pandu, this way leads to the celestials Mandara mountain; therefore be attentive and free from all anxieties.

sn: अयं देवनिवासो वै गन्तव्यो वो भविष्यति। ऋषीणां चैव दिव्यानां निवासः पुण्यकर्मणाम॥
en: You will now go to the abode of the celestials Rishis of virtuous deeds.

sn: एषा शिवजला पुण्या याति सौम्य महानदी। बदरीप्रभवा राजन् देवर्षिगणसेविता॥
en: O king, here flows the great and beautiful river (Alakananda) of sacred water rising from the Badari tree. It is ever adored by the celestials Rishis,

sn: एषा वैहायसैनित्यं बालखिल्यैर्महात्मभिः। अर्चिता चोपयाता च गन्धर्वैश्च महात्मभिः॥
en: It is always adored by the high-souled. Vaihayasa, Valakhilyas and the Gandharvas,

sn: अत्र साम स्म गायन्ति सामगाः पुण्यनि:स्वनाः। मरीचिः पुलहश्चैव भृगुश्चैवाङ्गिरास्तथा॥
en: And the singers of the Sama (Veda) the Rishis, Marichi, Pulaha, Bhrigu and Angirasa chant the hymns in this place.

sn: अत्राछिकं सुरश्रेष्ठो जपते समरुद्गणः। साध्याश्चैवाश्विनौ चैव परिधावन्ति तं तदा॥
en: Here does the lord of the celestials with the Marutas perform his daily prayers. The Siddhas and the Ashvins wait upon him.

sn: चन्द्रमाः सह सूर्येण ज्योतीषि च ग्रहैः सह। अहोरात्रविभागेन नदीमेनामनुव्रजन्॥
en: The moon with the sun and with all the luminaries and with the planets always go to this river by day and by night.

sn: एतस्याः सलिलं मूर्ध्नि वृषाङ्कः पर्यधारयत्। गङ्गाद्वारे महाभाग येन लोकस्थितिर्भवेत्॥
en: O greatly blessed one, that protector of the world, Vrishanka (Shiva) received on his head the all of the waters of this river at the source of the Ganges.

sn: एतां भगवती देवीं भवन्तः सर्व एव हि। प्रयतेनात्मना तात प्रतिगम्याभिवादत॥
en: O child, now come to this goddess of six attributes and bow down before her with concentrated mind.

sn: तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा लोमशस्य महात्मनः। आकाशगङ्गां प्रयताः पाण्डवास्तेऽभ्यवादयन्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having heard the words of the illustrious Lomasha the Pandavas reverentially worshipped the river which flows from the sky.

sn: अभिवाद्य च ते सर्वे पाण्डवाधर्मचारिणः। पुनः प्रयाताः संहृष्टाः सर्वैर्ऋषिगणैः सह॥
en: Having worshipped her, all the virtuous Pandavas accompanied by the Rishis again cheerfully proceeded.

sn: ततो दूरात् प्रकाशन्तं पाण्डुरं मेरुसंनिभम्। ददृशुस्ते नरश्रेष्ठा विकीर्णं सर्वतोदिशम्॥
en: Those best of men then saw at a distance some white objects of vast proportions which looked like the Meru (mountain) stretching in all directions.

sn: तान् प्रष्टुकामान् विज्ञाय पाण्डवान् स तु लोमशः। उवाच वाक्यं वाक्यज्ञः शृणुध्वं पाण्डुनन्दनाः॥
en: Seeing the Pandavas eager to ask him about it, Lomasha, skillful in speech, thus spoke. “Hear, O sons of Pandu.

sn: एतद् बिकीर्णं सुश्रीमत् कैलासशिखरोपमम्। यत् पश्यसि नरश्रेष्ठ पर्वतप्रतिमं स्थितम्॥ एतान्यस्थीनि दैत्यस्य नरकस्य महात्मनः। पर्वतप्रतिमं भाति पर्वतप्रस्तराश्रितम्॥
en: O foremost of men, what you see before you and what is of vast proportions looking like a mountain and appearing as beautiful as the Kailasa, is the collection of bones of the greatly powerful Daitya Naraka. As they have been kept on a mountain one mistakes it for a mountain.

sn: पुरातनेन देवेन विष्णुना परमात्मना। दैत्यो विनिहतस्तेन सुरराजहितैषिणा॥
en: In the days of yore, this Daitya was killed by the Supreme Soul, the eternal deity Vishnu, for the good of the king of the celestials.

sn: दशवर्षसहस्राणि तपस्तप्यन् महामनाः। ऐन्द्रं प्रार्थयते स्थानं तप:स्वाध्यायविक्रमात्॥
en: That high-souled Daitya performed great asceticism for ten thousand years with the desire of getting possession of Indra's kingdom.

sn: तपोबलेन महता बाहुवेगबलेन च। नित्यमेव दुराधर्षोधर्षयन् स दितेः सुतः॥
en: That son of Diti, becoming thus unrivalled by the power of his asceticism, as well as, that of arms, always harassed (Indra).

sn: स तु तस्य बलं ज्ञात्वाधर्मे च चरितव्रतम्। भयाभिभूतः संविग्नः शक्र आसीत् तदानघ॥
en: O sinless one, Sakra (Indra) became agitated. Afflicted with fear by learning his prowess, asceticism and observance of religious vows,

sn: तेन संचिन्तितो देवो मनसा विष्णुरव्ययः। सर्वत्रगः प्रभुः श्रीमानागतश्च स्थितौ बभौ॥
en: He mentally thought of the eternal deity Vishnu; and the graceful lord of the universe who is present everywhere appeared and stood before him.

sn: ऋषयश्चापि तं सर्वे तुष्टुवुश्च दिवौकसः। तं दृष्ट्वा ज्वलमानश्रीभगवान् हव्यवाहनः॥ नष्टतेजाः समभवत् तस्य तेजोऽभिभर्त्सितः। तं दृष्ट्वा वरदं देवं विष्णुं देवगणेश्वरम्॥
en: The Rishis and the celestials propitiated Vishnu with prayers. In his presence even the exalted and blazing Havyavahana (fire), lost his effulgence. Seeing that giver of boons, the deity Vishnu, the lord of all the celestials,

sn: प्राञ्जलिः प्रणतो भूत्वा नमस्कृत्य च वज्रभृत्। प्राह वाक्यं ततस्तत्त्वं यतस्तस्य भयं भवेत्॥
en: The wielder of thunder (Indra) with joined hands and bowed down head, told him soon the cause of his fear.

sn: विष्णुरुवाच जानामि ते भयं शक्र दैत्येन्द्रान्नरकात् ततः। ऐन्द्रं प्रार्थयते स्थानं तप:सिद्धेन कर्मणा॥
en: Vishnu said: “O Sakra, I know your fear originates from the lord of the Daityas, Naraka. By his successful asceticism he desires to obtain Indra's kingdom.

sn: सोऽहमेनं तव प्रीत्या तप:सिद्धमपिध्रुवम्। वियुनज्मि देहाद् देवेन्द्र मुहूर्त प्रतिपालय॥
en: O lord of the celestials, although he has achieved success in asceticism. I shall sever his soul from his body to do you good. Wait for a moment."

sn: तस्य विष्णुर्महातेजाः पाणिना चेतनां हरत्। स पपात ततो भूमौ गिरिराज इवाहतः॥
en: Lomasha said: Thereupon the greatly powerful Vishnu deprived him (Naraka) of his senses by striking him with his hands. He (Naraka) the fell down on the ground dead, like a great mountain.

sn: तस्यैतदस्थिसंघातं मायाविनिहतस्य वै। इदं द्वितीयमपरं विष्णोः कर्म प्रकाशते॥
en: He was thus killed by a miracle and his bones were then gathered at this spot. Here thus is manifest another great deed of Vishnu.

sn: नष्टा वसुमती कृत्स्ना पाताले चैव मज्जिता। पुनरुद्धरिता तेन वाराहेणैकङ्गिणा॥
en: Once the whole earth was lost, it sunk into the nether regions. But she was again lifted up by him (Vishnu) who had assumed the form of a boar.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच भगवन् विस्तरेणेमां कथां कथय तत्त्वतः। कथं तेन सुरेशेन नष्टा वसुमती तदा॥ योजनानां शतं ब्रह्मन् पुनरुद्धरिता तदा। केन चैव प्रकारेण जगतोधरणीध्रुवा॥ शिवा देवी महाभागा सर्वसस्यप्ररोहिणी। कस्य चैव प्रभावाद्धि योजनानां शतं गता॥ केन तद् वीर्यसर्वस्वं दर्शितं परमात्मनः। एतत् सर्वं यथातत्त्वमिच्छामि द्विजसत्तम। श्रोतुं विस्तरशः सर्वं त्वं हि तस्य प्रतिश्रयः॥
en: Yudhishthira said: O exalted one, narrate in detail how Vishnu, the lord of the celestials, raised up the earth sunk down one hundred yojanas. How was also that support of all created things, the greatly blessed Earth, who dispenses blessings and produces all sorts of course, made stable? By whom she was forced to sink one hundred yojanas and under what circumstances was this greatest exploit of the Supreme Being exhibited? O foremost of Brahmanas, I desire to hear all this in detail as it happened. You know all about it.

sn: लोमश उवाच यत् तेऽहं परिपृष्टोऽस्मि कथामेतां युधिष्ठिर। तत् सर्वमखिलेनेह श्रूयतां मम भाषतः॥ पुरा कृतयुगे तात वर्तमाने भयंकरे। यमत्वं कारयामास आदिदेवः पुरातनः॥
en: Lomasha said: O Yudhishthira, hear all in detail as I narrate the story which you have asked me to relate. O child, in the days of yore, in a terrible time in the Treta Yuga the ancient and primeval deity performed the duties of Yama.

sn: यमत्वं कुर्वतस्तस्य देवदेवस्यधीमतः। न तत्र म्रियते कश्चिज्जायते वा तथाप्युत॥
en: O undeteriorating one, when the god of gods began to perform the duties of Yama, there was no death (on earth), but births were numerous.

sn: वर्धन्ते पक्षिसंघाश्च तथा पशुगवेडकम्। गवांश्वं च मृगाश्चैव सर्वे ते पिशिताशनाः॥
en: Birds, beasts, kine, sheep, deer and all kinds of wild animals began to multiply.

sn: तथा पुरुषशार्दूल मानुषाश्च परंतप। सहस्रशो ह्ययुतशो वर्धन्ते सलिलं यथा।॥
en: O foremost of men, O chastiser of foes, men also began to multiply by thousands and tens of thousands like water.

sn: एतस्मिन् संकुले तात वर्तमाने भयंकरे। अतिभाराद् बसुमती योजनानां शतं गता॥
en: O child, by this terrible increase of creatures, the Earth sank down one thousand yojanas.

sn: सा वै व्यथतसर्वाङ्गी भारेणाक्रान्तचेतना। नारायणं वरं देवं प्रपन्ना शरणं गता॥
en: Being afflicted with pain all over her body and being deprived of her senses by this excessive weight (on her), she sought the protection of the foremost of deities NaraNarayana.

sn: पृथिव्युवाच भगवंस्त्वत्प्रसादाद्धि तिष्ठेयं सुचिरं त्विह। भारेणास्मि समाक्रान्ता न शक्नोमि स्म वर्तिमुम्॥
en: The Earth said: O exalted deity, it is through your favour I was able to remain so long in my position. But (now) I have been overcome with (a heavy) burden and I am now unable to hold myself any longer.

sn: ममेमं भगवन् भारं व्यपनेतुं त्वमर्हसि। शरणागतास्मि ते देव प्रसादं कुरु मे विभो॥
en: O exalted deity, you should remove this burden. O deity, O lord, I ask your protection. Extend your favour towards me.

sn: तस्यास्तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा भगवानक्षरः प्रभुः। प्रोवाच वचनं हृष्टः श्रव्याक्षरसमीरितम्॥
en: Lomasha said: Having heard her these words, the eternal deity of six attributes, cheerfully spoke these words to her with great distinctness.

sn: विष्णुरुवाच न ते महि भयं कार्यं भारार्ते वसुधारिणि। अहमेवं तथा कुर्मि यथा लघ्वी भविष्यसि॥
en: Vishnu said: O Earth, O holder of treasures, O burdened earth, do not be afraid; I shall act in the way by which you will be relieved of your burden.

sn: लोमश उवाच स तां विसर्जयित्वा तु वसुधां शैलकुण्डलाम्। ततो वराहः संवृत्त एकशृङ्गो महाद्युतिः॥
en: Lomasha said : Having thus sent away the earth adorned with mountains as her ear-rings, he then became a greatly effulgent boar with one tusk.

sn: रक्ताभ्यां नयनाभ्यां तु भयमुत्पादयन्निव। धूमं च ज्वलयल्ल्क्ष्म्या तत्र देशे व्यवर्धत॥
en: Causing terror with his red eyes and ernitting smokes from his blazing lustre, he began to swell in magnitude in that place.

sn: स गृहीत्वा वसुमती शृङ्गेणेकेन भास्वता। योजनानां शतं वीर समुद्धरति सोऽक्षरः॥
en: O hero, then holding the earth with his single tusk that eternal one raised her up one hundred yojanas.

sn: तस्यां चोद्धार्यमाणायां संक्षोभः समजायत। देवाः संक्षुभिताः सर्वे ऋषयश्च तपोधनाः॥ हाहाभूतमभूत् सर्वं त्रिदिवं व्योम भूस्तदा। न पर्य वस्थितः कश्चिद् देवो वा मानुषोऽपि वा॥
en: When she was thus raised up, a great agitation was created. All the celestials the Rishis and the ascetics were agitated; and the earth, the sky and the heaven were filled with “Alas! Oh!". Neither the celestials nor men could find peace.

sn: ततो ब्राह्मणामासीनं ज्वलमानमिव श्रिया। देवाः सर्षिगणाश्चैव उपतस्थुरनेकशः॥
en: Then the celestials and the Rishis all approached Brahma who was seated as if blazing in his own prosperity.

sn: उपसर्प्य च देवेशं ब्रह्माणं लोकसाक्षिकम्। भूत्वा प्राञ्जलयः सर्वे वाक्यमुच्चारयंस्तदा।॥
en: Coming to the deity Brahma, the witness of the acts of all beings, they with joined hands thus said to these words.

sn: लोकाः संक्षुभिताः सर्वे व्याकुलं च चराचरम्। समुद्राणां च संक्षोभस्त्रिदशेश प्रकाशते।॥
en: The Celestialss said: "O lord of heaven, all created beings have become agitated; all the mobile and immobile creatures have become restless. The ocean are also in great agitation.

sn: सैषा वसुमती कृत्स्ना योजनानां शतं गता। किमेतद् किं प्रभावेण येनेदं व्याकुलं जगत्। आख्यातु नो भवाशीघ्रं विसंज्ञाः स्मेह सर्वशः॥
en: This whole earth has gone one hundred yojanas down. What is the cause of all this? By whom the whole universe has been agitated? Kindly explain the cause to us without delay; we are all bewildered.

sn: ब्रह्मोवाच असुरेभ्यो भयं नास्ति युष्माकं कुत्रचित् क्वचित्। श्रूयतां यत्कृतेष्वेष संक्षोभो जायतेऽमराः॥
en: Brahma said: O immortals, there is no fear from the Asuras in any matter or in any place. Hear why all this agitation has taken place.

sn: योऽसौ सर्वत्रगः श्रीमानक्षरात्मा व्यवस्थितः। तस्य प्रभावात् संक्षोभस्त्रिदिवस्य प्रकाशते॥
en: This heaven has been agitated from the prowess of the illustrious being, who is omnipresent, eternal and the never-perishing soul.

sn: यैषा वसुमती कृत्स्ना योजनानां शतं गता। समुद्धता पुनस्तेन विष्णुना परमात्मना।॥
en: That supreme soul, Vishnu, has lifted up again the earth which sank down one hundred yojanas.

sn: तस्यामुद्धार्यमाणायां संक्षोभः समजायत। एवं भवन्तो जानन्तु छिद्यतां संशयश्च वः॥
en: On account of thus raising her up, this agitation has taken place. Know this to be the cause and dispel your doubts.

sn: देवा ऊचुः क्व तद् भूतं वसुमती समुद्धरति हृष्टवत्। तं देशं भगवन् ब्रूहि तत्र यास्यामहे वयम्॥
en: The Celestialss said : O exalted deity, where is that God, who so easily raises up the earth? Tell us the place; we shall all go there.

sn: ब्रह्मोवाच हन्त गच्छत भद्रं वो नन्दने पश्यत स्थितम्। एषोऽत्र भगवाश्रीमान् सुपर्णः सम्प्रकाशते॥
en: Brahma said: Go there. Be blessed, you will find him in the Nandana. Yonder is the exalted and adored Suparna (Garuda).

sn: वाराहेणैव रूपेण भगवॉल्लोकभावनः। कालानल इवाभाति पृथिवीतलमुद्धरम्॥
en: After having raised the earth, the Supreme Being, the creator of the world, blazes forth in the form of a boar like consuming fire at the universal dissolution,

sn: एतस्योरसि सुव्यक्तं श्रीवत्समभिराजते। पश्यध्वं विबुधाः सर्वे भूतमेतदनामयम्॥
en: On his breast is to be seen (the gem) Srivatsa. Behold all of you that being who does not know deterioration.

sn: लोमश उवाच ततो दृष्ट्वा महात्मानं श्रुत्वा चामन्त्र्य चामराः। पितामहं पुरस्कृत्य जग्मुर्देवा यथागतम्॥
en: Lomasha said: The immortals, with the Grandsire at their head, after having seen that great soul and heard his praise, went back to the place whence they came.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच श्रुत्वा तु तां कथां सर्वे पाण्डवा जनमेजय। लोमशादेशितेनाशु पथा जग्मुः प्रहृष्टवत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : O Janamejya, having heard this story, all the Pandavas with great alacrity proceeded by the way pointed out by Lomasha.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ते शूरास्ततधन्वानस्तूणवन्तः समार्गणाः। बद्धगोधाङ्गलित्राणाः खड्गवन्तोऽमितौजसः॥ परिगृह्य द्विजश्रेष्ठाज्येष्ठाः सर्वधनुष्मताम्। पाञ्चालीसहिता राजन् प्रययुर्गन्धमादनम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : O king, then those foremost of bow men, those immeasurably effulgent heroes, equipped with quivers and arrows and armed with swords and holding bows stringed at full and wearing finger protector made of guana-skin, went towards the Gandhamadana, with the Panchal princess and the best of Brahmanas.

sn: सरांसि सरितश्चैव पर्वतांश्च वनानि च। वृक्षांश्च बहुलच्छायान् ददृशुगिरिमूर्धनि॥
en: On their way they saw many lakes, rivers, mountains, forests with trees of wide spreading shades standing on the summit of the mountains,

sn: नित्यपुष्पफलान् देशान् देवर्षिगणसेवितान्। आत्मन्यात्मानमाधाय वीरा मूलफलाशिनः॥
en: Places with trees bearing flowers and fruits in all seasons and regions frequented by the as were celestials Rishis. Subduing their souls within their souls and living on fruits and roots,

sn: चेरुरुच्चावचाकारान् देशान् विषमसंकटान्। पश्यन्तो मृगजातानि बहूनि विविधानि च॥
en: They passed through rugged, craggy and difficult pigeons seeing (on their way) various kinds of animals.

sn: ऋषिसिद्धामरयुतं गन्धर्वाप्सरसां प्रियम्। विविशुस्ते महात्मानः किन्नराचरितं गिरिम्॥
en: Those high-souled heroes then entered the mountain inhabited by the Rishis, the Siddhas and the immortals and frequented by the Kinnaras which is the favourite pigeon of the Gandharvas and the Apsaras.

sn: प्रविशत्स्वथ वीरेषु पर्वतं गन्धमादनम्। चण्डवातं महद् वर्ष प्रादुरासीत् विशाम्पते।॥
en: O king, they entering Gandhamadana mountain, a violent wind arose accompanied with heavy shower of rain.

sn: ततो रेणुः समुद्भूतः सपत्रबहुलो महान्। पृथिवीं चान्तरिक्षं च द्यां चैव सहसाऽऽवृणोत्॥
en: Thereupon clouds of dust with innumerable dry leaves rose and suddenly covered the earth, the atmosphere and the sky,

sn: न स्म प्रज्ञायते किंचिदावृते व्योम्नि रेणुना। न चापि शेकुस्तत् कर्तुमन्योन्यस्याभिभाषणम्॥
en: The sky being covered with dust, nothing could be seen. They (the Pandavas) could not even express their mental feelings to one another by word.

sn: न चापश्यंस्ततोऽन्योन्यं तमसावृतचक्षुषः। आकृष्यमाणा वातेन साश्मचूर्णेन भारत॥
en: With eyes enveloped in darkness and pushed by the wind full of particles of rocks, they could not see one another.

sn: दुमाणां वातभग्नानां पततां भूतलेऽनिशम्। अन्येषां च महीजानां शब्दः समभवन्महान्॥
en: There arose great sounds proceeding from the trees and also from those trees that continually broke down blown up by the wind and also from those trees that fell down on the ground.

sn: द्यौः स्वित् पतति किं भूमिर्दीर्यते पर्वतो नु किम्। इति ते मेनिरे सर्वे पवनेनापि मोहिताः॥
en: distracted by the wind, they thought in their mind, “Is the heaven coming down or is the earth or the mountain being rent asunder?”

sn: ते पथानन्तरान् वृक्षान् वल्मीकान् विषमाणि च। पाणिभिः परिमार्गन्तो भीता वायोर्निलिल्यिरे॥
en: Being pushed by the wind and being alarmed, they felt their way by their hands and they took shelter under the way-side trees, anthills and caverns.

sn: ततः कार्मुकमादाय भीमसेनो महाबलः। कृष्णामादाय संगम्य तस्थावाश्रित्य पादपम्॥
en: Then taking hold of his bow and taking also Draupadi (by the hand), the greatly powerful Bhimasena stood underneath a tree.

sn: धर्मराजश्चधौम्यश्च निलिल्याते महावने। अग्निहोत्राण्युपादाय सहदेवस्तु पर्वते॥
en: Dharmaraja (Yudhishthira) and Dhaumya crept into a deep wood. Taking the sacred fire, Sahadeva took shelter under a rock.

sn: नकुलो ब्राह्मणाश्चान्ये लोमशश्च महातपाः। वृक्षानासाद्य संत्रस्तास्तत्र तत्र निलिल्यिरे॥
en: Nakula with Lomasha and other greatly ascetic Brahinanas stood alarmed, each underneath a tree.

sn: मन्दीभूते तु पवने तस्मिन् रजसि शाम्यति। महद्भिर्जलधारौघैर्वर्षमभ्याजगाम ह॥
en: When the wind had abated and the dust had subsided, there came down a heavy shower of rain in great torrents.

sn: भृशं चटचटाशब्दो वज्राणां क्षिप्यतामिव। ततस्ताश्चञ्चलाभासश्चेरुरभ्रेषु विद्युतः॥
en: There arose a great noise (of the rains falling on the mountain-side) like that of the roaring of the thunder. The swift flashing lightning began to play gracefully on the clouds.

sn: ततोऽश्मसहिताधाराः संवृण्वन्त्यः समन्ततः। प्रपेतुरनिशं तत्र शीघ्रवातसमीरिताः॥
en: Being helped by the swift wind, showers of rain incessantly poured and filled all sides round.

sn: तत्र सागरागा ह्यापः कीर्यमाणाः समन्ततः। प्रादुरासन् सकलुषाः फेनवत्यो विशाम्पते।॥
en: O king, all around flowed many stream-lets covered with froth and mud.

sn: वहन्त्यो वारि बहुलं फेनोडुपपरिप्लुतम्। परिसस्रुर्महाशब्दाः प्रकर्षन्त्यो महीरुहान्॥
en: Carrying volumes of water and covered with large quantity of froth, they rushed down with tremendous roars uprooting many trees.

sn: तस्मिन्नुपरते शब्दे वाते च समतां गते। गते ह्यम्भसि निम्नानि प्रादुर्भूते दिवाकरे॥
en: When the noise had ceased and the wind had abated and the water had subsided and the sun had arisen,

sn: निर्जग्मुस्ते शनैः सर्वे समाजग्मुश्च भारत। प्रतस्थिरे पुनर्वीराः पर्वतं गन्धमादनम्॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, they cautiously came out and met together. Those heroes then again proceeded towards the Gandhamadana mountain.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच क्रोशमानं प्रयातेषु पाण्डवेषु महात्मसु। पद्भ्यामनुचिता गन्तुं द्रौपदी समुपाविशत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said: When the illustrious Pandavas had gone only two miles, Draupadi unaccustomed to walk, sat down.

sn: श्रान्ता दुःखपरीता च वातवर्षेण तेन च। सौकुमार्याच्च पाञ्चाली सम्मुमोह तपस्विनी॥
en: Fatigued and miserable as she was, the Panchala princess became faint on account of the storin and rain.

sn: सा कम्पमाना मोहेन बाहुभ्यामसितेक्षणा। वृत्ताभ्यामनुरूपाभ्यामूरू समवलम्बत॥
en: Trembling with faintness, the black-eyed lady supported her with her thighs and with her plump and becoming arms.

sn: आलम्बमाना सहितावूरू गजकरोपमौ। पपात सहसा भूमौ वेपन्ती कदली यथा॥
en: Thus trying to support herself with her thighs which were like the trunk of an elephant, she suddenly fell down on the ground, trembling like a plantain tree stirred (by wind).

sn: तां पतन्तीं वरारोहां भज्यमानां लतामिव। नकुलः समभिद्रुत्य परिजग्राह वीर्यवान्॥
en: Seeing that foremost of women falling down like a twisted creeper, the greatly strong Nakula ran forward and supported her.

sn: नकुल उवाच राजन् पञ्चालराजस्य सुतेयमसितेक्षणा। श्रान्ता निपतिता भूमौ तामवेक्षस्व भारत॥
en: Nakula said: O king, O descendant of Bharata, behold, the daughter of the Panchala king, this blackeyed lady has fallen on the ground out of fatigue.

sn: अदुःखार्हा परं दुःखं प्राप्तेयं मृदुगामिनी। आश्वासय महाराज तामिमां श्रमकर्शिताम्॥
en: O great king, this lady of slow gait, though she does not deserve misery, suffers great afflictions. She is worn out with fatigue. Therefore comfort her.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच राजा तु वचनात् तस्य भृशं दुःखसमन्वितः। भीमश्च सहदेवश्च सहसा समुपाद्रवन्॥
en: Vaishampayana said: Having heard his these words, the king, Bhima and Sahadeva became greatly afflicted and they soon ran towards her.

sn: तामवेक्ष्य तु कौन्तेयो विवर्णवदनां कृशाम्। अङ्कमानीयधर्मात्मा पर्यदेवयदातुरः॥
en: Seeing her weak and also seeing her pale face, the high-souled son of Kunti, taking her up on his lap, began to lament (in grief).

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच कथं वेश्मसु गुप्तेषु स्वास्तीर्णशयनोचिता। भूमौ निपतिता शेते सुखार्दा वरवर्णिनी॥
en: Yudhishthira said: How can, this beautiful lady accustomed to a life of case (and accustomed) to live in the private rooms and on beds spread over with sheets, sleep on the ground?

sn: सुकुमारौ कथं पादौ मुखं च कमलप्रभम्। मत्कृतेऽद्य वरार्हायाः श्यामतां समुपागतम्॥
en: The delicate hands and the lotus-like feet of this lady who deserve all excellent things have become dark blue in colour on my account.

sn: किमिदं द्यूतकामेन मया कृतमबुद्धिना। आदाय कृष्णां चरता वने मृगगणायुते॥
en: Having been addicted to dice what have I done foolishly. I am with Krishna (Draupadi) wandering in the forest full of wild animals!

sn: सुखं प्राप्स्यसि कल्याणि पाण्डवान् प्राप्य वै पतीन्। इति दुपदराजेन पित्रा दत्ताऽऽयतेक्षणा॥
en: This large-eyed lady was bestowed on us by her father, the king of Drupada, in the hope that this blessed damsel would be happy by obtaining the Pandavas as her husbands.

sn: तत् सर्वमनवाप्येयं श्रमशोकाध्वकर्शिता। शेते निपतिता भूमौ पापस्य मम कर्मभिः॥
en: Afflicted with hardship, sorrow and travel, it is on account of my wretched act, she (now) lies prostrate on the ground without having obtained any thing hoped for.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तथा लालप्यमाने तुधर्मराजे युधिष्ठिरे। धौम्यप्रभृतयः सर्वे तत्राजग्मुर्द्विजोत्तमाः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : When Dharmaraja Yudhishthira was thus lamenting, Dhaumya and other foremost of Brahmanas all came there.

sn: ते समाश्वासयामासुराशीर्भिश्चाप्यपूजयन्। रक्षोघ्नांश्च तथा मन्त्राओपुश्चक्रुश्च ते क्रियाः॥
en: They comforted and consoled him and they honoured him with blessings. They uttered mantras capable of destroying Rakshasas and they also performed (some) religious rites.

sn: पठ्यमानेषु मन्त्रेषु शान्त्यर्थं परमर्षिभिः। स्पृश्यमाना करैः शीतैः पाण्डवैश्च मुहुर्मुहुः॥
en: On the Mantras being recited by the great Rishis in order to restore her and on the repeated touch of the cool hands of the Pandavas.

sn: सेव्यमाना च शीतेन जलमिश्रेण वायुना। पाञ्चाली सुखमासाद्य लेभे चेतः शनैः शनैः॥
en: And also on being fanned by the cool breeze surcharged with water, the Panchala princess felt ease and slowly regained her consciousness.

sn: परिगृह्य च तां दीनां कृष्णामजितनसंस्तरे। पार्था विश्रामयामासुर्लब्धसंज्ञां तपस्विनीम्॥
en: Placing the poor exhausted lady who had then regained her consciousness on a deer-skin, the sons of Pritha made her take rest.

sn: तस्या यमौ रक्ततलौ पादौ पूजितलक्षणौ। कराभ्यां किणजाताभ्यां शनकैः संववाहतुः॥
en: The twins, taking up her red-soled feet with auspicious marks, began to press them gently with their hands which were scared by the bow-strings.

sn: पर्याश्वासयदप्येनांधर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः। उवाच च कुरश्रेष्ठो भीमसेनमिदं वचः॥
en: Dharmaraja Yudhishthira also comforted her. That foremost of the Kurus thus spoke to Bhimasena.

sn: बहवः पर्वता भीम विषमः हिमदुर्गमाः। तेषु कृष्णा महाबाहो कथं नु विचंरिष्यति॥
en: Yudhishthira said: "O Bhima, many rugged and snowy bound mountains are (before us); O mighty-armed hero, how will Krishna (Draupadi) be able to pass them?

sn: भीमसेन उवाच त्वां राजन् राजपुत्रीं च यमौ च पुरुषर्षभ। स्वयं नेष्यामि राजेन्द्र मा विषादे मनः कृथाः॥
en: Bhima said: O king, I myself will carry the princess and also these two foremost of men, the twins and yourself; therefore O king of kings, do not allow anxiety to come to your mind.

sn: हैडिम्बाश्च महावीर्यो विहगो मद्बलोपमः। वहेदनघ सर्वान्नो वचनात् ते घटोत्कचः॥
en: O sinless one, at your command, the son of Hidimba, Ghatotkacha, who can range the skies and who is as strong as myself will carry us all.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच अनुज्ञातोधर्मराज्ञा पुत्रं सस्मार राक्षसम्। घटोत्कचस्तुधर्मात्मा स्मृतमात्रः पितुस्तदा॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having been ordered by Dharmaraja (Yudhishthira) he remembered his Rakshasa son. As soon as remembered the high-souled Ghatotkacha appeared before his father.

sn: कृताञ्जलिरुपातिष्ठदभिवाद्याथ पाण्डवान्। ब्राह्मणांश्च महाबाहुः स च तैरभिनन्दितः॥
en: The mighty armed hero, after saluting the Pandavas and the Brahmanas, stood before them with joined hands. They too welcomed him in return.

sn: उवाच भीमसेनं स पितरं भीमविक्रमम्। स्मृतोऽस्मि भवता शीघ्रं शुश्रूषुरहमागतः॥
en: He then thus spoke to his greatly powerful father Bhimasena, "Having been remembered by you. I have speedily come here to serve you.

sn: आज्ञापय महाबाहो सर्वं कर्तास्म्यसंशयम्। तच्छ्रुत्वा भीमसेनस्तु राक्षसं परिषस्वजे॥
en: O mighty-armed hero, command me. I shall certainly be able to perform whatever you will order me to do.” Having heard this, Bhimasena embraced the Rakshasa.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच धर्मज्ञों बलवाञ्शूरः सत्यो राक्षसपुङ्गवः। भक्तोऽस्मानौरसः पुत्रो भीम गृहणातु मा चिरम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said : O Bhima, let this powerful and heroic Rakshasha chief, your own begotten son, ever devoted to us and always truthful, carry (his) mother (Draupadi) without any delay.

sn: तव भीम सुतेनाहमतिभीमपराक्रम। अक्षतः सह पाञ्चाल्या गच्छेयं गन्धमादनम्॥
en: O greatly powerful hero, by your strength of arins I shall go with the Panchala princess to Gandhamadana.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच भ्रातुर्वचनमाज्ञाय भीमसेनो घटोत्कचम्। आदिदेश नरव्याघ्रस्तनयं शत्रुकर्शनम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having heard the words of his brother, that foremost of men Bhimasena spoke thus to that chastiser of foes, Ghatotkacha.

sn: भीमसेन उवाच हैडिम्बेय परिश्रान्ता तव मातापराजित। त्वं च कामगमस्तात बलवान् वह तां खग॥
en: Bhima said: O invincible hero, O son of Hidimba, O child, O ranger of skies, you are capable of going everywhere at will. Your mother is worn out with fatigue; therefore, O strong hero, carry her.

sn: स्कन्धमारोप्य भद्रं ते मध्येऽस्माकं विहायसा। गच्छ नीचिकया गत्या यथा चैनां न पीडयेः॥
en: On your shoulder and go with us adopting a course not far overhead, so that you may not make her feel uneasy. Let blessings be on you.

sn: घटोत्कच उवाच धर्मराजं चधौम्यं च कृष्णां च यमजौ तथा। एकोऽप्यहमलं वोढुं किमुताद्य सहायवान्।॥
en: Ghatotkacha said : I can myself alone carry Dharmaraja (Yudhishthira), Dhaumya, Krishna (Draupadi) and the twins (Nakula and Sahadeva), what wonder is then there that I shall today carry them when I have others to help me!

sn: अन्ये च शतशः शूरा विहङ्गाः कामरूपिणः। सर्वान् वो ब्राह्मणैः सार्धं वक्ष्यन्ति सहितानघ॥
en: O sinless one, hundreds of other heroes (Rakshasas), capable of ranging in the skies and of assuming any form at will, will carry you with all the Brahmanas.

sn: एवमुक्त्वा ततः कृष्णामुवाह स घटोत्कचः। पाण्डूनां मध्यगो वीरः पाण्डवानपि चापरे॥
en: Vaishampayana said: Having said this, Ghatotkacha carried Krishna (Draupadi) in the midst of the Pandavas. The other (Rakshasas) carried the Pandavas.

sn: लोमशः सिद्धमार्गेण जगामानुपमद्युतिः। स्वेनैव स प्रभावेण द्वितीय इव भास्करः॥
en: Lomasha of matchless effulgence proceeded in the path of the Siddhas by virtue of his own (ascetic) prowess, like a second sun.

sn: ब्राह्मणांश्चापि तान् सर्वान् समुपादाय राक्षसाः। नियोगाद् राक्षसेन्द्रस्य जग्मुर्भीमपराक्रमाः॥
en: Being ordered by the Rakshasas chief, other greatly powerful Rakshasas took up all the Brahmanas (on their shoulders) and proceeded along.

sn: एवं सुरमणीयानि वनान्युपवनानि च। आलोकयन्तस्ते जग्मुर्विशालां बदरी प्रति॥
en: Blazing up many highly charming forests and woods, they went towards the great Badari tree.

sn: ते त्वाशुगतिभिर्वीरा राक्षसैस्तैर्महाजवैः। उह्यमाना ययुः शीघ्रं दीर्घमध्वानमल्पवत्॥
en: Being carried by the greatly swift and heroic Rakshasas, who were capable of going great distance within the shortest time, they passed over a long way as if it were but a short one.

sn: देशान् म्लेच्छजनाकीर्णान् नानारत्नाकरायुतान्। ददृशुर्गिरि पादांश्च नानाधातुसमाचितान्॥
en: They saw (on their way) many regions crowded with Mlechas, many mines of gems, many hillocks full of various minerals,

sn: विद्याधरसमाकीर्णान् युतान् वानरकिन्नरैः। तथा किंपुरुषैश्चैव गन्धर्वैश्च समन्ततः॥
en: Thronged with Vidyadharas, abounding on all sides in the monkeys and the Kinnaras, the Kimpurushas and the Gandharvas,

sn: मयूरैश्चमरैश्चैव वानरै रुरुभिस्तथा। वराहैर्गवयैश्चैव महिषैश्च समावृतान्॥
en: Full of peacocks, Chamaru cows, apes, Rurus, bears, Gavayas and buffaloes,

sn: नदीजालसमाकीर्णान् नानापक्षियुतान् बहून्। नानाविधमृगैर्जुष्टान् वानरैश्चोपशोभितान्॥
en: Intersected by many rivulets and abounding in a large number of birds of various kinds and also in various sorts of beasts, beautified by elephants.

sn: समदैश्चापि विहगैः पादपैरन्वितास्तथा। तेऽवतीर्य बहून् देशानुत्तमच्छिसमन्वितान्॥
en: Adorned with various trees and enraptured birds. Having passed many such regions and also the country of Uttara-Kurus.

sn: ददृशुर्विविधाश्चर्यं कैलास पर्वतोत्तमम्। तस्याभ्याशे तु ददृशुर्नरनारायणाश्रमम्॥
en: They then saw that best of mountains, the Kailasa, full of wonderful sights. They then saw the hermitage of Nara and Narayana.

sn: उपेतं पापैर्दिव्यैः सदापुष्पफलोपगैः। ददृशुस्तां च बदरी वृत्तस्कन्धां मनोरमाम्॥
en: Adorned with celestials trees bearing fruits and flowers in all seasons of the year. They then saw that charming Badari of large trunk.

sn: स्निग्धामविरलच्छायां श्रिया परमया युताम्। पत्रैः स्निग्धैरविरलैरुपेतां मृदुभिः शुभाम्॥
en: It was full of freshness, of deep shade, of excellent beauty and of thick, soft and green foliage; it was blessed and healthful,

sn: विशालशाखा विस्तीर्णामतिद्युतिसमन्विताम्। फलैरुपचितैर्दिव्यैराचितां स्वादुभि शम्॥
en: With gigantic and wide spreading boughs of matchless lustre, it bore full grown, tasteful and holy fruits.

sn: मधुस्रवैः सदा दिव्यां महर्षिगणसेविताम्। मदप्रमुदितैर्नित्यं नानाद्विजगणैर्युताम्॥
en: All dropping excellent honey. It was frequented by the great Rishis and it was always inhabited by various birds maddened with animal spirits.

sn: अदंशमशके देशे बहुमूलफलोदके। नीलशाद्वलसंच्छन्ने देवगन्धर्वसेविते॥
en: It grew in a place where there were no mosquitoes and gad flies and it abounded in fruits, roots and water, it was covered with green grass, inhabited by the celestials and the Gandharvas.

sn: सुसमीकृतभूभागे स्वभावविहिते शुभे। जातां हिममृदुस्पर्शे देशेऽपहतकण्टके॥
en: It stood on a smooth surface of land which was naturally blessed and healthful it was thronless, beauteous and cool and pleasant in touch.

sn: तामुपेत्य महात्मानः सह तैर्ब्राह्मणर्षभैः। अवतेरुस्ततः सर्वे राक्षसस्कन्धतः शनैः॥
en: Having reached the place with those foremost of Brahmanas, the illustrious (Pandavas) all slowly alighted from the shoulders of the Rakshasas.

sn: ततस्तमाश्रमं रम्यं नरनारायणाश्रितम्। ददृशुः पाण्डवा राजन् सहिता द्विजपुङ्गवैः॥
en: O king, the Pandavas, accompanied by those best of Brahmanas, saw the charming hermitage of Nara and Narayana.

sn: तमसा रहितं पुण्यमनामृष्टं रवेः करैः। क्षुत्तृट्शीतोष्णदोषैश्च वर्जितं शोकनाशनम्॥
en: It was free from darkness, it was holy, it was untouched by the solar rays, it was free from all the miseries, namely hunger and thirst, heat and cold; it destroyed all sorrows.

sn: महर्षिगणसम्बाधं ब्राह्म या लक्ष्या समन्वितम्। दुष्प्रवेशं महाराज नरैर्धर्मबहिष्कृतैः॥
en: It was crowded by the great Rishis and adorned with the grace of the Vedas. It was inaccessible to those men who were beyond the pale of religion.

sn: बलिहोमार्चितं दिव्यं सुसम्मृष्टानुलेपनम्। दिव्यपुष्योपहारैश्च सर्वतोऽभिविराजितम्॥
en: It was adorned with offerings and havyas, it was holy, well swept and daubed with fragrance. It shone beautiful with the offerings of celestials blossoms all around.

sn: विशालैरग्निशरणैः उम्भाण्डैराचितं शुभैः। महद्भिस्तोयकलशैः कठिनैश्चोपशोभितम्॥
en: It was covered over with sacrificial altars, sacred ladles and posts and graced with large water jars and baskets.

sn: शरण्यं सर्वभूतानां ब्रह्मघोषनिनादितम्। दिव्यमाश्रयणीयं तमाश्रमं श्रमनाशनम्॥
en: It was the refuge of all creatures, it echoed with the recitations of the Vedas. It was heavenly and a fit place for a holy hermitage; it destroyed all fatigue.

sn: श्रिया युतमनिर्देश्यं देवचर्योपशोभितम्। फलमूलाशनैर्दान्तैश्चारुकृष्णाजिनाम्बरैः॥ सूर्यवैश्वानरसमैस्तपसा भावितात्मभिः। महर्षिभिर्मोक्षपरैर्यतिभिर्नियतेन्द्रियैः॥ ब्रह्मभूतैर्महाभागैरुपेतं ब्रह्मवादिभिः। सोऽभ्यगच्छन्महातेजास्तानृषीन् प्रयतः शुचिः॥ भ्रातृभिः सहितोधीमान्धर्मपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः। दिव्यज्ञानोपपन्नास्ते दृष्ट्वा प्राप्तं युधिष्ठिरम्॥
en: It was full of splendour, it produced matchless merits, it was majestic with divine qualities. It was inhabited by many great Rishis living on fruits and roots, having their passions controlled, wearing black deer skins, looking as effulgent as the sun and Agni, possessing souls magnified by asceticism and mind intent on emancipation, leading the Vanaprastha life, identifying themselves with the Supreme Soul and reciting the Vedas. That greatly effulgent of Dharma, Yudhishthira, with his brothers, restraining his senses and purifying himself, went to those Rishis, who, having seen by their supernatural knowledge the arrival of Yudhishthira,

sn: अभ्यगच्छन्त सुप्रीताः सर्व एव महर्षयः। आशीर्वादान् प्रयुञ्जानाः स्वाध्यायनिरता भृशम्॥
en: Received him with joy. Those Rishis, engaged in the recitation of the Vedas conferred blessings on him.

sn: प्रीतास्ते तस्य सत्कारं विधिना पावकोपमाः। उपाजहुश्च सलिलं पुष्पमूलफलं शुचि॥
en: Those fire-like ones gladly gave him a fitting, teçeption in due form. They gave him pure water, fruits, flowers and roots,

sn: स तैः प्रीत्याथ सत्कारमुपनीतं महर्षिभिः। प्रयतः प्रतिगृह्याथधर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Dharmaraja Yudhishthira gladly received with subdued soul the offerings offered by the great Rishis for his reception. son

sn: तं शक्रसदनप्रख्यं दिव्यगन्धं मनोरमम्। प्रीतः स्वर्गापमं पुण्यं पाण्डवः सह कृष्णया॥ विवेश शोभया युक्तं भ्रातृभिश्च सहानघ। ब्राह्मणैर्वेदवेदाङ्गपारगैश्च सहस्रशः॥
en: O sinless one, the Pandava (Yudhishthira) with Krishna (Draupadi) and his brothers and with also thousands of Brahmanas, learned in the Vedas and the Vedangas, entered that sacred hermitage which was like the abode of Indra, resembling heaven itself, beautiful and full of celestials fragrance.

sn: तत्रापश्यतधर्मात्मा देवदेवर्षिपूजितम्।। नरनारायणस्थानं भागीरथ्योपशोभितम्॥
en: Then the virtuous-minded (Yudhishthira) saw the hermitage of Nara and Narayana, adored by the celestials and the celestials Rishis and beautified by the Bhagirathi.

sn: पश्यन्तस्ते नरव्याघ्रा रेमिरे तत्र पाण्डवाः। मधुस्रवफलं दिव्यं ब्रह्मर्षिगणसेवितम्॥
en: Seeing it frequented by the Brahmana Rishis and abounding in fruits dropping excellent honey, those foremost of men, the Pandavas, were filled with great delight.

sn: तदुपेत्य महात्मानस्तेऽवसन् ब्राह्मणैः सह। मुदा युक्ता महात्मानो रेमिरे तत्र ते तदा॥
en: Having arrived there those high-souled ones lived at that place with the cheerfully sported there.

sn: आलोकयन्तो मैनाकं नानाद्विजगणायुतम्। हिरण्यशिखरं चैव तच्च बिन्दुसरः शिवम्॥
en: Seeing the Mainaka mountain with golden peaks and also the auspicious Binda lake abounding in various sorts of birds.

sn: तस्मिन् विहरमाणाश्च पाण्डवाः सह कृष्णया। मनोज्ञे काननवरे सर्वर्तुकुसुमोज्ज्वले॥
en: The Pandavas with Krishna (Draupadi) derived great pleasure in roaming in those excellent and charming woods blossomed with flowers of all seasons.

sn: पादपैः पुष्पविकचैः फलभारावनामिभिः। शोभिते सर्वतो रम्यैः पुंस्कोकिलगणायुतैः॥
en: They were beautiful on all sides with trees bearing brown blossoms, bending down with the weight of their fruits, frequented by numerous male Kokilas,

sn: स्निग्धपत्रैरविरलैः शीतच्छायैर्मनोरमैः। सरांसि च विचित्राणि प्रसन्नसलिलानि च॥
en: With glossy and beautiful foliage, with cool shade and with beautiful loveliness, with various lakes of crystal waters,

sn: कमलैः सोत्पलैश्चैव भ्राजमानानि सर्वशः। पश्यन्तश्चारुरूपाणि रेमिरे तत्र पाण्डवाः॥
en: Adorned all around with lotuses and lilies. Seeing this charming scene, the Pandavas derived great delight.

sn: पुण्यगन्धःसुखस्पर्शो ववौ तत्र समीरणः। ह्लादयन् पाण्डवान् सर्वान् द्रौपद्या सहितान् प्रभो॥
en: O lord, a balmy breeze with holy fragrance always blew there, delighting all the Pandavas with Krishna (Draupadi).

sn: भागीरथी सुतीर्थां च शीतां विमलपङ्कजाम्। मणिप्रवालप्रस्तारां पादपैरुपशोभिताम्॥ दिव्यपुष्पसमाकीर्णां मनःप्रीतिविवर्धिनीम्। वीक्षमाणा महात्मानो विशाला बदरीमनु॥
en: The high-souled ones saw near the great Badari tree, the Bhagirathi of easy descent and cool water, adorned with beautiful lotuses, with stairs made of rubies and corals, beautified with trees and scattered over with celestials flowers and giving great pleasure to the mind.

sn: तस्मिन् देवर्षिचरिते देशे परमदुर्गमे। भागीरथीपुण्यजले तर्पयांचक्रिरे तदा॥ देवानृषींश्च कौन्तेयाः परमं शौचमास्थिताः। तत्र ते तर्पयन्तश्च जपन्तश्च कुरूद्वहाः॥
en: Those sons of Kunti, after having purified themselves, offered oblations to the Pitris, the celestials, the Rishis, in the sacred waters of the Bhagirathi in that extremely inaccessible place, frequented by the celestials Rishis. Those perpetuators of the Kuru race thus offered oblations and passed their time in reciting holy writs.

sn: ब्राह्मणैः सहिता वीरा ह्यवसन् पुरुषर्षभाः। कृष्णायास्तत्र पश्यन्तः क्रीडितान्यमरप्रभाः। विचित्राणि नरव्याघ्रा रेमिरे तत्र पाण्डवाः॥
en: Those foremost of men, those heroes then lived there with the Brahmanas. Those best of men, the celestials-like Pandavas, seeing the various scenes with Krishna (Draupadi) derived great pleasure.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तत्र ते पुरुषव्याघ्राः परमं शौचमास्थिताः। षड्रात्रमवसन् वीराधनंजयदिदृक्षवः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : There lived those foremost of men, those heroes, for six nights, leading a highly pure life with the expectation of seeing Dhananjaya (Arjuna).

sn: ततः पूर्वोत्तरे वायुः प्लवमानो यदृच्छया। सहस्रपत्रमर्काभं दिव्यं पद्ममुपाहरत्॥
en: Then there blew a wind from the north-east at pleasure and it brought a celestials and sunlike lotus with one thousand petals.

sn: तदवैक्षत पाञ्चाली दिव्यगन्धं मनोरमम्। अनिलेनाहृतं भूमौ पतितं जलजं शुचि॥
en: The Panchala princess saw that pure and charming lotus of celestials fragrance lying on the ground being brought by the wind.

sn: तच्छुभा शुभमासाद्य सौगन्धिकमनुत्तमम्। अतीव मुदिता राजन् भीमसेनमथाब्रवीत्॥
en: O king, having obtained that excellent, fragrant and blessed lotus, that blessed lady became very much delighted and she thus spoke to Bhimasena.

sn: पश्य दिव्यं सुरुचिरं भीम पुष्पमनुत्तमम्। गन्धसंस्थानसम्पन्नं मनसो मम नन्दनम्॥
en: Draupadi said: "O Bhima, behold this beautiful and excellent celestials flower, it has gladdened my heart by its sweet fragrance.

sn: इदं चधर्मराजाय प्रदास्यामि परंतप। हरेदं मम कामाय काम्यके पुनराश्रमे॥
en: O chastiser of foes, I shall give it to Dharmaraja (Yudhishthira). Procure others (like it) for my satisfaction, so that I may take them to our hermitage in the Kamayaka.

sn: यदि तेऽहं प्रिया पार्थ बहूनीमान्युपाहर। तान्यहं नेतुमिच्छामि काम्यकं पुनराश्रमम्॥
en: O son of Pritha, if I am your beloved, then procure others (like it) in large numbers, for I desire to take them to our hermitage in the Kamyaka (forest).”

sn: एवमुक्त्वा शुभापाङ्गी भीमसेननिन्दिता। जगाम पुष्यमादायधर्मराजाय तत् तदा॥
en: Having said this to Bhimasena, that faultless lady of beautiful eyes took the flower and went to Dharmaraja (Yudhishthira).

sn: अभिप्रायं तु विज्ञाय महिष्याः पुरुषर्षभः। प्रियायाः प्रियकामः स प्रायाद् भीमो महाबलः॥
en: Knowing the desire of their queen (Draupadi), that foremost of men, the greatly strong Bhima, set out, so that he might gratify the desire of the beloved one.

sn: वातं तमेवाभिमुखो यतस्तत् पुष्पमागतम्। आजिहीर्षुर्जगामाशु स पुष्पाण्यपराण्यपि॥
en: Eager to fetch the flowers, he proceeded at a very rapid pace facing the wind, in the direction from which the lotus had come.

sn: रुक्मपृष्ठंधनुर्गृह्य शरांश्चाशीविषोपमान्। मृगराडिव संक्रुद्धः प्रभिन्न इव कुञ्जरः॥
en: Taking the bow in laid with gold and also arrows resembling poisonous snakes, he proceeded like a lion in rage or an elephant in rut.

sn: ददृशुः सर्वभूतानि महाबाणधनुर्धरम्। न ग्लानि च वैकलव्यं न भयं न च सम्भ्रमः॥
en: All creatures stared at that wielder of the great bow and arrows. Neither exhaustion, nor languor, nor fear, nor confusion.

sn: कदाचिज्जुषते पार्थमात्मजं मातरिश्वनः। द्रौपद्याः प्रियमन्विच्छन् स बाहुबलमाश्रितः॥
en: Ever took possession of that son of Pritha and of Vayu (wind). Desiring to please Draupadi, that hero of great strength of arms,

sn: व्यपेतभयसम्मोहः शैलमभ्यपतद् बली। स ते द्रुमलतागुल्मच्छन्नं नीलशिलातलम्॥ गिरि चचारारिहरः किन्नराचरितं शुभम्। नानावर्णधरैश्चित्रंधातुदुममृगाण्डजैः॥
en: That mighty one, free from fear or exhaustion, began to ascend the mountain. That slayer of foes roamed over that beautiful place adorned with trees, creepers and shrubs and paved with black stone and frequented by the Kinnaras. With various minerals, plants, beasts and birds and many colours,

sn: सर्वभूषणसम्पूर्ण भूमेर्भुजमिवोच्छ्रितम्। सर्वत्र रमणीयेषु गन्धमादनसानुषु॥ सक्तचक्षुरभिप्रायान् हृदयेनानुचिन्तयन्। पुस्कोकिलनिनादेषु षट्पदाचरितेषु च।॥ बद्धश्रोत्रमनश्चक्षुर्जगामामितविक्रमः। आजिघ्रन् स महातेजाः सर्वर्तुकुसुमोद्भवम्॥ गन्धमुद्धतमुद्दामो वने मत्त इव द्विपः। वीज्यमानः सुपुण्येन नानाकुसुमगन्धिना॥ पितुः संस्पर्शशीतेन गन्धमादनवायुना। ह्रियमाणश्रमः पित्रा सम्प्रहृष्टतनूरुहः॥
en: It appeared like an upraised arm of the earth adorned with all ornaments. That hero of matchless prowess, fixing his look at the slopes of the Gandhamadana, adorned with the flowers of every season and revolving various thoughts in his mind and with his ears, eyes and mind riveted to the spots resounding with the notes of male Kokilas and ringing with the hum of black bees, like an elephant in rut roving mad in the forest, smelt the excellent fragrance proceeding from the flowers of all seasons. He was fanned by the fresh breeze of the Gandhamadana, full of fragrance of various flowers and as cooling as a feather touch. On his fatigue being removed, the down on his body stood on end.

sn: स यक्षगन्धर्वसुरब्रह्मर्षिगणसेवितम्। विलोकयामास तदा पुष्पहेतोररिदमः॥
en: That chastiser of foes sought for the flowers all over the mountain, frequented by the Yakshas, the Gandharvas, the celestials and the Brahmanas Rishis.

sn: विषमच्छदैरचितैरनुलिप्त इवाङ्गुलैः। वलिभिर्धातुविच्छेदैः काञ्चनाञ्जनराजतैः। सपक्षमिव नृत्यन्तं पार्श्वलग्नैः पयोधरैः॥
en: Being brushed by Saptachada tree and besmeared in red, black and white minerals, he looked decorated with the lines of holy unguents drawn by fingers. The mountain with clouds stretching at its sides looked as if it was dancing with outspread wings.

sn: मुक्ताहारैरिव चितं च्युतैः प्रस्रवणोदकैः। अभिरामदरीकुञ्जनिर्झरोदककन्दरम्॥
en: On account of the trickling of the waters of the springs, it appeared to be adorned with necklaces of pearls. It contained romantic caverns, groves, cascades and caves.

sn: अप्सरोनूपुररवैः प्रनृत्तवरबर्हिणम्। दिग्वारणविषाणग्रैर्घष्टोपलशिलातलम्॥
en: There were innumerable beautiful peacocks dancing to the tinkling of the bangles on the arms of Apsaras. The rocky surface of the mountains had been worn away by (the continual brushing of) the tusks of great elephants.

sn: स्रस्तांशुकमिवाक्षोभ्यैर्निम्नगानिः सृतैर्जलैः। सशष्पकवलैः स्वस्थैदूरपरिवर्तिभिः॥ भयानभिज्ञैर्हरिणैः कौतूहलनिरीक्षितः। चालयन्नुरुवेगेन लताजालान्यनेकशः॥ आक्रीडमानो हृष्टात्मा श्रीमान् वायुसुतो ययौ। प्रियामनोरथं कर्तुमुद्यतश्चारुलोचनः॥
en: With the waters of the streamlets falling down, the mountain looked as if its clothes were getting loosened. That handsome son of Vayu (wind) playfully and cheerfully went on, pushing away innumerable entwining creepers. The stags stared at him in curiosity with grass in their mouth; and as they never knew what fear was, they were not frightened and they did not run away. Eager to fulfill the desire of his beloved, that hero of beautiful eyes,

sn: प्रांशु कनकवर्णाभः सिंहसंहननो युवा। मत्तवारणविक्रान्तो मत्तवारणवेगवान्॥
en: That youth, of the splendour like the color of the gold, having a body as strong as that of the lion, treading like a mad elephant and possessing the prowess of a mad elephant.

sn: मत्तवारणताम्राक्षो मत्तवारणवारणः। प्रियपार्थोपविष्टाभिर्व्यावृत्ताभिर्विचेष्टितैः॥ यक्षगन्धर्वयोषाभिरदृश्याभिर्निरीक्षितः। नवावतारो रूपस्य विक्रीडनिव पाण्डवः॥ चचार रमणीयेषु गन्धमादनसानुषु। संस्मरन् विविधान् क्लेशान् दुर्योधनकृतान् बहून्।।
en: Having coppery eyes like those of a mad elephant and possessing the prowess of checking a mad elephant, began to roam on the romantic sides of the Gandhamadana with two beautiful eyes uplifted and thus displaying a novel beauty. The wives of the Yakshas and the Gandharvas, sitting invisible by the side of their husbands, stared at him turning their faces and making various motions. He (then) remembered the various woes caused by Duryodhana.

sn: द्रौपद्या वनवासिन्याः प्रियं कर्तुं समुद्यतः। सोऽचिन्तयद् गते स्वर्गमर्जुने मयि चागते॥
en: Eager to do the favourite work of Draupadi exiled in the forest, he thought, "Now that Arjuna had gone to heaven and I have come away

sn: पुष्पहेतोः कथं त्वार्यः करिष्यति युधिष्ठिरः। स्नेहान्नरवरो नूनमविश्वासाद् बलस्य च॥ नकुलं सहदेवं च न मोक्ष्यति युधिष्ठिरः। कथं तु कुसुमावाप्तिः स्याच्छीघ्रमिति चिन्तयन्।।३४।
en: In search of the flowers, what will Yudhishthira now do from affection; and doubting their prowess, that foremost of men Yudhishthira will not allow Nakula and Sahadeva to come in search of us. How can I obtain the flowers soon?" He thought thus.

sn: प्रतस्थे नरशार्दूलः पक्षिराडिव वेगितः। सज्जमानमनोदृष्टिः फुल्लेषु गिरिसानुषु॥
en: And that foremost of men proceeded with the speed of the king of birds (Garuda), with his mind and sight fixed on the delightful sides of the mountain.

sn: द्रौपदीवाक्यपाथेयो भीमः शीघ्रतरं ययौ। कम्पयन् मेदिनी पद्भ्यां निर्घात इव पर्वसु॥
en: Having the words of Draupadi as his provisions for the journey, Bhima went with greater speed, shaking the earth with his tread as does a hurricane.

sn: त्रासयन् गजयूथानि वातरंहा वृकोदरः। सिंहव्याघ्रमृगांश्चैव मर्दयानो महाबलः॥ उन्मूलयन् महावृक्षान् पोथयंस्तरसा बली। लतावल्लीश्च वेगेन विकर्षन् पाण्डुनन्दनः। उपर्युपरि शैलाग्रमारुरुक्षुरिव द्विपः॥
en: Frightening the herds of elephants, the lions, tigers and deer, uprooting and crushing large trees, forcibly tearing plants and creepers like an elephant ascending higher and higher the summit of a mountain.

sn: विनर्दमानोऽतिभृशं सविधुदिव तोयदः। तेन शब्देन महता भीमस्य प्रतिबोधिता:॥
en: He roared fearfully as does the clouds surcharged with lightning. Awakened by the loud roaring of Bhima,

sn: गुहां संतत्यजुर्व्याघ्रो निलिल्युर्वनवासिनः। समुत्पेतुः खगास्त्रस्ता मृगयूथानि दुद्रुवुः॥
en: Tigers came out of their dens while other wild animals hid themselves in their own. The birds flew away in alarm and herds of deer ran (in all directions).

sn: ऋक्षाश्चोत्ससृजुर्वृक्षांस्तत्यजुर्हरयो गुहाम्। व्यजृम्भन्त महासिंहा महिषाश्चावलोकयन्॥
en: Birds left the trees, tigers forsook their dens, the mighty lions were roused from their slumber and the buffaloes stared,

sn: तेन वित्रासिता नागाः करेणुपरिवारिताः। तद् वनं स परित्यज्य जग्मुरन्यन्महावनम्॥
en: The elephants in great alarm surrounded by the female elephants felt that forest and ran to more extensive ones.

sn: वराहमृगसंघाश्च महिषाश्च वनेचराः। व्याघ्रगोमायुसंघाश्च प्रणेदुर्गवयैः सह।॥
en: The boars, the deer, the lions, the buffaloes, the tigers, the jackals and the Gavyas and all other wild animals in herds began to cry.

sn: रथाङ्गसाह्वदात्यूहा हंसकारण्डवप्लवा:। शुकाः पुंस्कोकिला: क्रौञ्चा विसंज्ञा भेजिरे दिशः॥
en: The ruddy goose, the Yallendulas, the ducks, the kapandavas, the plavas, the parrots, the male kokilas and the herons all flew in confusion in all directions.

sn: तथान्ये दर्पिता नागा: करेणुशरपीडिताः। सिंहव्याघ्राश्च संक्रुद्धा भीमसेनमथाद्रवन्॥
en: Some proud elephants, urged by female elephants and also some lions and tigers in great anger rushed at Bhimasena.

sn: शकृन्मूत्रं च मुञ्चानां भयविभ्रान्तमानसाः। व्यादितास्या महारौद्रा व्यनदन् भीषणान् रवान्॥
en: As they were bewildered with fear, these fearful animals discharge urine and dung and set up loud yells with gaping mouths.

sn: ततो वायुसुतः क्रोधात् स्वबाहुबलमाश्रितः। गजेनान्यान् गजाञ्छ्रीमान् सिंहं सिंहेन वा विभुः।।४७। तलप्रहारैरन्यांश्च व्यहनत् पाण्डवो बली। ते वध्यमाना भीमेन सिंहव्याघ्रतरक्षवः॥
en: Thereupon the illustrious and the handsome son of Vayu, the mighty Pandava, depending on his own strength of arms, began to kill in anger one elephant with another elephant and one lion with another lion. He killed others (smaller animals) with slaps. Being thus killed by Bhima, the lions, the tigers, the leopards,

sn: भयाद् विससृजुर्भीमं शकृन्मूत्रं च सुनुवुः। प्रविवेश ततः क्षिप्रं तानपास्य महाबलः॥ वनं पाण्डुसुतः श्रीमाञ्छब्देनापूरयन् दिशः। अथापश्यन्महाबाहुर्गन्धमादनसानुषु॥
en: Loudly cried and discharged urine and dung in great fear. The handsome son of Pandu, the mighty armed hero, entered into that forest resounding all sides with his shouts. The mighty armed hero then saw on the slopes of the Gandhamadana.

sn: सुरम्यं कदलीषण्ड बहुयोजनविस्तृतम्। तमभ्यगच्छद् वेगेन क्षोभयिष्यन् महाबलः॥
en: A charming forest of plantain trees extending to many yojanas. The greatly powerful hero, agitating (the forest), went with great speed towards it.

sn: महागज इवास्रावी प्रभञ्जन् विविधान् दुमान्। उत्पाट्य कदलीस्तम्भान् बहुतालसमुच्छ्यान्॥
en: Like a large elephant breaking many trees and uprooting innumerable plantain trees as high as many palm trees put one upon the other.

sn: चिक्षेप तरसा भीमः समन्ताद् बलिनां वरः। विनदन् सुमहातेजा नृसिंह इव दर्पितः॥
en: That foremost of all strong men Bhima threw them on all sides; that greatly powerful hero, as proud as a lion, sent up loud shouts.

sn: ततः सत्त्वान्युपाक्रामद् बहूनि सुमहान्ति च। रुरुवानर सिंहांश्च महिषांश्च जलाशयान्।॥
en: Then he met with innumerable huge animals, deer, monkeys, lions, buffaloes and also aquatic animals.

sn: तेन शब्देन चैवाथ भीमसेनरवेण च। वनान्तरगताश्चापि वित्रेसुगपक्षिणः॥
en: With the roarings of these (animals), as well as with the shouts of Bhima, the wild animals living in distant forests were also alarmed.

sn: तं शब्द सहसा श्रुत्वा मृगपक्षिसमीरितम्। जलार्द्रपक्षा विहगाः समुत्पेतुः सहस्रशः॥ तानौदकान् पक्षिगणान् निरीक्ष्य भरतर्षभः। तानेवानुसरन् रम्यं ददर्श सुमहत् सरः॥
en: Having heard this noise of the beasts and birds, thousands of aquatic fowls suddenly rose into air. That foremost of the Bharata race (Bhima), then went in that direction. He then saw a vast and romantic lake.

sn: काञ्चनैः कदलीषण्डैर्मन्दमारुतकम्पितैः। वीज्यमानमिवाक्षोभ्यं तीरात् तीरविसर्पिभिः॥
en: That fathomless lake was being fanned by the golden plantain trees on its banks, which were slowly shaken by the soft breeze.

sn: तत् सरोऽथावतीर्याशु प्रभूतनलिनोत्पलम्। महागज इवोद्दामश्चिक्रीड बलवद् बली॥
en: Going down to the waters of that lake adorned with innumerable lotuses and lilies, that greatly powerful hero sported merrily there like a mighty elephant in rut.

sn: विक्रीड्य तस्मिन् सुचिरमुत्ततारामितद्युतिः। ततोऽध्यगन्तुं वेगेन तद् वनं बहुपादपम्॥
en: Having sported there for a long while, that immeasurably effulgent hero got up in order to enter quickly into the forest abounding in trees.

sn: दध्मौ च शङ्ख स्वनवत् सर्वप्राणेन पाण्डवः आस्फोटयच्च बलवान् भीमः संनादयन् दिशः॥
en: Then the Pandava (Bhima) sounded with all his might his loud-blowing conch. Striking his arms with his arms, the mighty Bhima made all the points of heaven resound.

sn: तस्य शङ्खस्य शब्देन भीमसेनरवेण च। बाहुशब्देन चोग्रेण नदन्तीव गिरेगुहाः॥
en: Filled with the sounds of the conch and with the shouts of Bhimasena and also with the sounds made by the striking of his arms, the caves of the mountains seemed roaring.

sn: तं वज्रनिष्पेषसममास्फोटितमहारवम्। श्रुत्वा शैलगुहासुप्तैः सिंहैर्मुक्तो महास्वनः॥
en: Hearing those loud striking of his arms resembling the roaring of thunder, the lions sleeping in their caves (awoke and) uttered great howls.

sn: सिंहनादभयत्रस्तैः कुञ्जरैरपि भारत। मुक्तो विरावः सुमहान् पर्वतो येन पूरितः॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, being frightened by the yelling of the lions, the elephants also sent forth tremendous roars which filled the mountain.

sn: तं तु नादं ततः श्रुत्वा मुक्तं वारणपुङ्गवैः। भ्रातरं भीमसेनं तु विज्ञाय हनुमान् कपिः॥
en: Having heard these loud sounds and known that Bhimasena was his brother, the monkeychief, Hanuman, the ape.

sn: दिवंगमं रुरोधाथ मार्ग भीमस्य कारणात्। अनेन हि पथा मा वै गच्छेदिति विचार्य सः॥ आस्त एकायने मार्गे कदलीषण्डमण्डिते। भ्रातुर्भोमस्य रक्षार्थं तं मार्गमवरुध्य वै॥
en: With the desire to do good to Bhima and to secure his safety, obstructed the path to heaven. Thinking thus, he lay across the narrow path adorned with plantain trees.

sn: मात्र प्राप्स्यति शापं वाधर्षणां वेति पाण्डवः। कदलीषण्डमध्यस्थो ह्येवं संचिन्त्य वानरः॥ प्राजृम्भत महाकायो हनूमान् नाम वानरः। कदलीषण्डमध्यस्थो निद्रावशगतस्तदा॥
en: With the object that the Pandava (Bhima) inight not meet with any curse or defeat by entering the plantain forest, the huge Hanuman lay down there as if overcome by drowsiness.

sn: जृम्भमाणः सुविपुलं शक्रध्वजमिवोच्छ्रितम्। आस्फोटयच्च लाडूलमिन्द्राशनिसमस्वनम्॥
en: He began to yawn, lashing his long tail, which resembled a (sacrificial) pole consecrated to Indra and he roared like thunder.

sn: तस्य लाडूलनिनदं पर्वतः सुगुहामुखैः। उद्गारमिव गौर्नर्दनुत्ससर्ज समन्ततः॥
en: On all sides round, the mountain echoed through the mouths of its caves. Those sounds were like the lowings of a cow.

sn: लाङ्कलास्फोटशब्दाच्च चलितः स महागिरिः। विघूर्णमानशिखरः समन्तात् पर्यशीर्यत॥
en: Shaken by the sounds produced by the lashing of his tail, the mountain, with its summits, tottered and crumbled down on all sides.

sn: स लाडूलरवस्तस्य मत्तवारणनि:स्वनम्। अन्तर्धाय विचित्रेषु चचार गिरिसानुषु॥
en: Rising above the roaring of mad elephants, the sounds of the lashing of his tail spread over all the slopes of the mountain.

sn: स भीमसेनस्तच्छ्रुत्त्वा सम्प्रहृष्टतनूरुहः। शब्दप्रभवमन्विच्छंश्चचार कदलीवनम्॥
en: Having heard this noise, the down of Bhima's body stood on end. He began to roam over that plantain tree in search of the source of these sounds.

sn: कदलीवनमध्यस्थमथ पीने शिलातले। ददर्श सुमहाबाहुर्वानराधिपति तदा॥
en: The mighty-armed hero saw the monkeychief in the plantain forest, lying on an elevated rocky base. was

sn: विद्युत्सम्पातदुष्प्रेक्षं विद्युत्सम्पातपिङ्गलम्। विद्युत्सम्पातनिनदं विद्युत्सम्पातचञ्चलम्॥
en: He was difficult to be looked at as a flash of lightning is; he was of coppery colour; he was as quick-moving as lightning.

sn: बाहुस्वस्तिकविन्यस्तपीनह्रस्वशिरोधरम्। स्कन्धभूयिष्ठकायत्वात् तनुमध्यकटीतटम्॥
en: He had a short fleshy neck supported on his shoulders; his waist slender in consequence of the fullness of his shoulders.

sn: किंचिच्चाभुग्नशीर्षेण दीर्घरोमाञ्चितेन च। लाडूलेनोर्ध्वगतिनाध्वजेनेव विराजितम्॥
en: His tail, covered with long hair and bent a little at the end, was raised up like a banner.

sn: ह्रस्वौष्ठं ताम्रजिह्वास्यं रक्तकणं चलद्धृवम्। विवृत्तदंष्ट्रादशनं शुक्लतीक्ष्णाग्रशोभितम्॥ अपश्यद् वदनं तस्य रश्मिवन्तमिवोडुपम्। वदनाभ्यन्तरगतैः शुक्लैर्दन्तैरलंकृतम्॥
en: He (Bhima) saw Hanumana's head furnished with small lips, coppery face, long tongue, red ears, brisk eyes and bare white teeth sharpened at the edge.

sn: केसरोत्करसम्मिश्रमशोकानामिवोत्करम्। हिरण्मयीनां मध्यस्थं कदलीनां महाद्युतिम्॥
en: His head was like the shining moon with hair scattered over, resembling a heap of Ashoka flowers. That greatly effulgent one was lying amidst the golden palm trees.

sn: दीप्यमानेन वपुषा स्वर्चिष्मन्तमिवानलम्। निरीक्षन्तममित्रघ्नं लोचनैर्मधुपिङ्गलैः॥
en: Looking like a blazing fire with his effulgent body. That chastiser of foes was casting glances with his eyes reddened with intoxication.

sn: तं वानरवरंधीमानतिकायं महाबलम्। स्वर्गपन्थानमावृत्य हिमवन्तमिव स्थितम्॥ दृष्ट्वा चैनं महाबाहुरेकं तस्मिन् महावने। अथोपसृज्य तरसा विभीर्भीमस्ततो बली॥ सिंहनादं चकारोग्रं वज्राशनिसमं बली। तेन शब्देन भीमस्य वित्रेसुमंगपक्षिणः॥
en: The intelligent Bhima saw that mighty and huge monkey-chief lying like a second Himalayas obstructing the path of heaven. Seeing him alone in that great forest the undaunted, the mighty-armed and the greatly strong Bhima, quickly came to him and uttered a loud lion-like roar. At his that loud roar, beasts and birds were terrified.

sn: हनूमांश्च महासत्त्व ईषदुन्मील्य लोचने। दृष्ट्वा तमथ सावज्ञं लोचनैमधुपिङ्गलैः। स्मितेन चैनमासाद्य हनूमानिदमब्रवीत्॥
en: The greatly powerful Hanuman opened his eyes but partially and looked at him with thorough disregard with eyes reddened with intoxication. Then smilingly addressing him, he thus spoke to him.

sn: हनूमानुवाच किमर्थं सरुजस्तेऽहं सुखसुप्तः प्रबोधितः। ननु नाम त्वया कार्या दया भूतेषु जानता॥
en: Hanuman said: Why have you awakened me, ill as I am? I was comfortably asleep. As you have reason, you should certainly show kindness to all creatures.

sn: वयंधर्मं न जानीमस्तिर्यग्योनिमुपाश्रिताः। नरास्तु बुद्धिसम्पन्ना दया कुर्वन्ति जन्तुषु॥
en: Being born in the animal kingdom we do not know what Dharma is. But men having reason show kindness to all animals.

sn: रेषु कर्मसु कथं देहवाक्चित्तदूषिषु। धर्मघातिषु सज्जन्ते बुद्धिमन्तो भवद्विधाः॥
en: Why do then men like your august self commit acts that are harmful alike to body, speech and heart and which are also destructive of virtue.

sn: न त्वंधर्म विजानासि बुधा नोपासितास्त्वया। अल्पबुद्धितया बाल्यादुत्सादयसि यन्मृगान्॥
en: You know not what virtue is. You have not taken advice from the wise men. You have but little sense and therefore from childishness you destroy lower animals.

sn: ब्रूहि कस्त्वं किमर्थं वा किमिदं वनमागतः। वर्जितं मानुषैर्भावैस्तथैव पुरुषैरपि॥
en: Tell me who you are. Why have you come to the forest devoid of humanity and human beings?

sn: क्व च त्वयाद्य गन्तव्यं प्रब्रूहि पुरुषर्षभ। अतः परमगम्योऽयं पर्वत: सुदुरारुहः॥
en: O foremost of men, tell me also where you intend to go today. It is impossible to go any further; the yonder mountain is inaccessible.

sn: विना सिद्धगति वीर गतिरत्र न विद्यते। देवलोकस्य मार्गोऽयमगम्यो मानुषैः सदा॥
en: O hero, except success in asceticism there is no other means to go to that place. This is the way to the celestials regions. It is always impassable by men.

sn: कारुण्यात् त्वामहं वीर वारयामि निबोध मे। नातः परं त्वया शक्यं गन्तुमाश्वसिहि प्रभो॥
en: O hero, O lord, out of kindness I ask you, to desist. Listen to my words. Further up from this place you are not able to go. Therefore desist.

sn: स्वागतं सर्वथैवेह तवाद्य मनुजर्षभ। इमान्यमृतकल्पानि मूलानि च फलानि च॥ भक्षयित्वा निवर्तस्व मा वृथा प्राप्स्यसे वधम्। ग्राह्यं यदि वचो मह्यं हितं मनुजपुङ्गव॥
en: O foremost of men, you are welcome here to day in every way. If you at all accept my words, then rest here partaking of fruits and roots as sweet as ambrosia. Do not for nothing be killed.

description: The colloquy between Bhima and Hanuman
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एतच्छ्रुत्वा वचस्तस्य वानरेन्द्रस्यधीमतः। भीमसेनस्तदा वीरः प्रोवाचामित्रकर्षणः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : O chastiser foes, having heard these words of the intelligent monkey chief, the heroic Bhima thus spoke to him.

description: The colloquy between Bhima and Hanuman
sn: भीम उवाच को भवान् किं निमित्तं वा वानरं वपुरास्थितः। ब्राह्मणानन्तरो वर्णः क्षत्रियस्त्वां तु पृच्छति॥
en: Bhima said: Who are your august self? For what reason you are in the shape of a monkey? It is a Kshatriya, an order next to the Brahmanas who asks you.

description: The colloquy between Bhima and Hanuman
sn: कौरवः सोमवंशीयः कुन्त्या गर्भेणधारितः। पाण्डवो वायुतनयो भीमसेन इति श्रुतः॥
en: I am a descendant of Kuru, born in the Lunar dynasty, born by Kunti in her womb, a son of Pandu, begotten by Vayu, known by the name of Bhimasena.

description: The colloquy between Bhima and Hanuman
sn: स वाक्यं कुरुवीरस्य स्मितेन प्रतिगृह्य तत्। हनूमान् वायुतनयो वायुपुत्रमभाषत।॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Hearing the words of that Kuru hero, Hanuman smiled and that son of Vayu thus spoke to the son of Vayu (Bhima).

description: The colloquy between Bhima and Hanuman
sn: हनूमानुवाच वानरोऽहं न ते मार्ग प्रदास्यामि यथेप्सितम्। साधु गच्छ निवर्तस्व मा त्वं प्राप्स्यसि वैशसम्॥
en: Hanuman said : I am a monkey; I shall not grant you the passage you desire. Desist like an honest man and go back. Do not meet with destruction.

description: The colloquy between Bhima and Hanuman
sn: भीमसेन उवाच वैशसं वास्तु यद्वान्यन्न त्वां पृच्छामि वानर। प्रयच्छ मार्गमुत्तिष्ठ मा मत्तः प्राप्स्यसे व्यथाम्॥
en: Bhima said: O monkey, I do not ask you about destruction or anything else. Give me way. Arise, do not meet with grief at my hand.

description: The colloquy between Bhima and Hanuman
sn: हनूमानुवाच नास्ति शक्तिर्ममोत्थातुं व्याधिना क्लेशितो ह्यहम्। यद्यवश्यं प्रयातव्यं लवयित्वा प्रयाहि माम्॥
en: Hanuman said : I am suffering from illness, therefore I have no strength to rise. If you are resolved to go, then go overleaping me.

description: The colloquy between Bhima and Hanuman
sn: भीम उवाच निर्गुणः परमात्मा तु देहं व्याप्यावतिष्ठते। तमहं ज्ञानविज्ञेयं नावमन्ये न लवये॥
en: Bhima said: The attributes Supreme Soul pervades all bodies. I cannot disregard him who is knowable by only knowledge. Therefore I cannot overleap you.

description: The colloquy between Bhima and Hanuman
sn: यद्यागमैर्न विद्यां च तमहं भूतभावनम्। क्रमेयं त्वां गिरि चैव हनूमानिव सागरम्॥
en: Had I not known him from whom all creatures have become manifest, I would have overleaped you, also this mountain, even as Hanuman did the ocean.

description: The colloquy between Bhima and Hanuman
sn: हनूमानुवाच कएष हनुमान् नाम सागरो येन लवित्तः। पृच्छामि त्वां नरश्रेष्ठ कथ्यतां यदि शक्यते॥
en: Hanuman said: Who is he of the name of Hanuman who leaped over the ocean. O foremost of men I ask you, relate it if you can.

description: The colloquy between Bhima and Hanuman
sn: भीम उवाच भ्राता मम गुणश्लाघ्यो बुद्धिसत्त्वबलान्वितः। रामायणेऽतिविख्यातः श्रीमान् वानरपुङ्गवः॥
en: Bhima said: He was my brother, excellent in all accomplishments and endued with with both intelligence and strength. That handsome and foremost of monkeys is celebrated in the Ramayana.

description: The colloquy between Bhima and Hanuman
sn: रामपत्नीकृते येन शतयोजनविस्तृतः। सागर: प्लवगेन्द्रेण क्रमेणैकेन लवित्तः॥
en: The ocean extending over one hundred yojanas was leaped over by that monkey for Rama's wife.

description: The colloquy between Bhima and Hanuman
sn: स मे भ्राता महावीर्यस्तुल्योऽहं तस्य तेजसा। बले पराक्रमे युद्धे शक्तोऽहं तव निग्रहे॥
en: That greatly powerful hero was my brother; I am equal to him in might, strength and prowess. I am able also to chastise you.

description: The colloquy between Bhima and Hanuman
sn: उत्तिष्ठ देहि मे मार्ग पश्य चाद्य पौरुषम्। मच्छासनमकुर्वाणं त्वां वा नेष्ये यमक्षयम्॥
en: Arise therefore, give me way or witness my prowess today. If you fail to do what I say, I send you to the abode of Yama.

description: The colloquy between Bhima and Hanuman
sn: मे वैशम्पायन उवाच विज्ञाय तं बलोन्मत्तं बाहुवीर्येण दर्पितम्। हृदयेनावहस्यैनं हनूमान् वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said: Knowing him to be intoxicated and proud of his strength of arms. Hanuman slighted him (very much) in his mind and he thus spoke to him.

description: The colloquy between Bhima and Hanuman
sn: हनूमानुवाच प्रसीद नास्ति मे शक्तिरुत्थातुं जरयानघ। ममानुकम्पया त्वेतत् पुच्छमुत्सार्य गम्यताम्॥
en: Hanuman said: O sinless one, be kind towards me. I have no strength to rise in consequence of old age. From pity for me go by moving aside my tail.

description: The colloquy between Bhima and Hanuman
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्ते हनुमता हीनवीर्यपराक्रमम्। मनसाचिन्तयद् भीमः स्वबाहुबलदर्पितः॥
