en: Vaishampayana said : Having been thus addressed by Hanuman, Bhima, proud of his own strength, thought in his mind that one (Hanuman) to be destitute of energy and prowess.

description: The colloquy between Bhima and Hanuman
sn: पुच्छे प्रगृह्य तरसा हीनवीर्यपराक्रमम्। सालोश्यमन्तकस्यैनं नयाम्यद्येह वानरम्॥
en: He thought, “Taking fast hold of his tale I will send this monkey destitute of energy and prowess to the abode of Yama."

description: The colloquy between Bhima and Hanuman
sn: सावज्ञमथ वामेन स्मयञ्जग्राह पाणिना। न चाशकच्चालयितुं भीमः पुच्छं महाकपेः॥
en: Therefore with a smile, Bhima carelessly took hold of the tail with his left hand, but he could not move that tail of the mighty monkey.

description: The colloquy between Bhima and Hanuman
sn: उच्चिक्षेप पुनर्दोवा॑मिन्द्रायुधमिवोच्छ्रितम्। नोद्धर्तुमशकद् भीमो दोर्ध्यामपि महाबलः॥
en: Then with both arms he pulled the tail resembling the sacrificial) pole raised up in honour of Indra. But the mighty Bhima failed to raise the tail with both his arms.

description: The colloquy between Bhima and Hanuman
sn: उत्क्षिप्तभूर्विवृत्ताक्षः संहतभृकुटीमुखः। स्विन्नगात्रोऽभवद् भीमो न चोद्धर्तुं शशाक तम्॥
en: His eyes were contracted up and his eye falls rolled, his face was contracted into wrinkles and his body was covered with sweat but still he failed to raise it.

description: The colloquy between Bhima and Hanuman
sn: यत्नवानपि तु श्रीमॉल्लाङ्कलोद्धरणोद्धरः। कयेः पार्श्वगतो भीमस्तस्थौ व्रीडानताननः॥
en: When he failed to raise it after many attempts, the illustrious Bhima came to the side of the monkey and stood before him in great shame.

description: The colloquy between Bhima and Hanuman
sn: प्रणिपत्य च कौन्तेयः प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यमब्रवीत्। प्रसीद कपिशार्दूल दुरुक्तं क्षम्यतां मम॥
en: That son of Kunti bowing down his head and joining his two hands, thus spoke to him, "O foremost of monkeys, be kind towards me. Forgive my harsh words.

description: The colloquy between Bhima and Hanuman
sn: सिद्धो वा यदि वा देवो गन्धर्वो वाथ गुह्यकः। पृष्टः सन् काम्यया ब्रूहि कस्त्वं वानररूपधृक्॥
en: Are you a Siddha, a celestials, a Gandharva or a Guhaka, I ask you in curiosity. Who are you in the shape of a monkey?

description: The colloquy between Bhima and Hanuman
sn: न चेद् गुह्यं महाबाहो श्रोतव्यं चेद् भवेन्मम्। शिष्यवत् त्वां तु पृच्छामि उपपन्नोऽस्मि तेऽनघ॥
en: O mighty armed hero (tell me) if it is not a secret and if I deserve to hear it. O sinless one, I seek your refuge and ask you as a disciple.

description: The colloquy between Bhima and Hanuman
sn: हनूमानुवाच यत् ते मम परिज्ञाने कौतूहलमरिदम। तत् सर्वमखिलेन त्वं शृणु पाण्डवनन्दन॥
en: Hanuman said: O chastiser of foes, as you are curious to know all about me, I shall narrate to you all. O son of Pandu, listen to it.

description: The colloquy between Bhima and Hanuman
sn: अहं केसरिणः क्षेत्रे वायुना जगदायुषा। जातः कमलपत्राक्ष हनूमान् नाम वानरः॥
en: O lotus eyed hero, I am born in the womb of Kesari, begotten by Vayu who is the life of the universe. I am the monkey, named Hanuman.

description: The colloquy between Bhima and Hanuman
sn: सूर्यपुत्रं च सुग्रीवं शक्रपुत्रं च वालिनम्। सर्वे वानरराजानस्तथा वानरयूथपाः॥ उपतस्थुर्महावीर्या मम चामित्रकर्षण। सुग्रीवेणाभवत् प्रीतिरनिलस्याग्निना यथा॥
en: O chastiser of foes, all the mighty monkey chiefs waited upon that son of the sun, Sugriva and that son of Indra, Bali, Friendship between Sugriva and myself was like that between the wind and the fire.

description: The colloquy between Bhima and Hanuman
sn: निकृत: स ततो भ्रात्रा कस्मिश्चित् कारणान्तरे। ऋष्यमूके मया सार्धं सुग्रीवो न्यवसच्चिरम्॥
en: For some cause Sugriva was driven out by his brother and lived for a long time with me at the Hrishvamukha.

description: The colloquy between Bhima and Hanuman
sn: अथ दाशरथिर्वीरो रामो नाम महाबलः। विष्णुर्मानुषरूपेण चचार वसुधातमल्॥
en: Once upon a time, the greatly powerful son of Dasharatha by name Rama who was Vishnu in human form wandered over the earth.

description: The colloquy between Bhima and Hanuman
sn: स पितुः प्रियमन्विच्छन् सहभार्यः सहानुजः। सधनुर्धन्विनां श्रेष्ठो दण्डकारण्यमाश्रितः॥
en: In order to please his father, he with his wife and brother, armed with the best of bows, resided in the Dandaka forest.

description: The colloquy between Bhima and Hanuman
sn: तस्या भार्या जनस्थानाच्छलेनापाहृता बलात्। राक्षसेन्द्रेण बलिना रावणेन दुरात्मना।॥ सुवर्णरत्नचित्रेण मृगरूपेण रक्षसा। वञ्चयित्वा नरव्याघ्रं मारीचेन तदानघ॥
en: O sinless one, his wife was carried away by force and by stratagem from Janasthana by the mighty lord of the Rakshasas, the wicked minded Ravana deceiving that foremost of men through the Rakshasa Maricha who assumed the forn of a deer marked with gems and golden spots.

description: The Colloquy between Bhima and Hanuman
sn: हनूमानुवाच हृतदारः सह भ्रात्रा पत्नी मार्गन् स राघवः। दृष्टवाशैलशिखरे सुग्रीवं वानरर्षभम्॥
en: Hanuman said: Having thus lost his wife while that descendant of Raghu was searching his wife with his brother, he met with the monkey chief Sugriva on the summit of the mountain.

description: The Colloquy between Bhima and Hanuman
sn: तेन तस्याभवत् सख्यं राघवस्य महात्मनः। स हत्वा वालिनं राज्ये सुग्रीवमभिषिक्तवान्॥
en: Then a friendship was contracted between that high-souled descendant of Raghu and Sugriva. Killing Bali, he gave him (Sugriva) the kingdom.

description: The Colloquy between Bhima and Hanuman
sn: स राज्यं प्राप्य सुग्रीवं सीतायाः परिमार्गणे। वानरान् प्रेषयामास शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः॥
en: Having obtained the kingdom, Sugriva sent away hundreds and thousands of monkeys to search out Sita.

description: The Colloquy between Bhima and Hanuman
sn: ततो वानरकोटीभिः सहितोऽहं नरर्षभ। सीतां मार्गन्महाबाहो प्रयातो दक्षिणां दिशम्॥
en: O foremost of men, O mighty armed hero, I also with numerous other monkeys set out towards the south in search of Sita.

description: The Colloquy between Bhima and Hanuman
sn: ततः प्रवृत्तिः सीताया गृध्रेण सुमहात्मना। सम्पातिना समाख्याता रावणस्य निवेशने॥
en: Thereupon I learned the tidings of Sita from a mighty vulture named Sampati that she was in the abode of Ravana.

description: The Colloquy between Bhima and Hanuman
sn: ततोऽहं कार्यसिद्ध्यर्थं रामस्याक्लिष्टकर्मणः। शतयोजनविस्तीर्णमर्णवं सहसाऽऽप्लुतः॥
en: Thereupon to accomplish the work of Rama of stainless deeds, I suddenly leaped over the ocean extending one hundred yojanas.

description: The Colloquy between Bhima and Hanuman
sn: अहं स्ववीर्यादुत्तीर्य सागरं मकरालयम्। सुत जनकराजस्य सीतां सुरसुतोपमाम्॥ दृष्टवान् भरतश्रेष्ठ रावणस्य निवेशने। समेत्य तामहं देवीं वैदेहीं राघवप्रियाम्॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, having crossed by my own prowess the ocean, the abode of sharks and crocodiles, I saw the daughter of king Janaka, celestials like Sita in the abode Ravana. Having interviewed with that lady, the Veda princess, the beloved of Rama.

description: The Colloquy between Bhima and Hanuman
sn: दग्ध्वा लङ्कामशेषेण साट्टप्राकारतोरणाम्। प्रत्यागतश्चास्य पुनर्नाम तत्र प्रकाश्य वै॥
en: And burnt the whole of Lanka with its towers, ramparts and gates and proclaimed my name there, I returned.

description: The Colloquy between Bhima and Hanuman
sn: मद्वाक्यं चावधार्याशु रामो राजीवलोचनः। स बुद्धिपूर्वं सैन्यस्य बद्ध्वा सेतुं महोदधौ।॥
en: Having heard everything from ine, the lotuseyed Rama fixed upon the course of his action and made with the help of his soldiers a bridge over the great ocean.

description: The Colloquy between Bhima and Hanuman
sn: वृतो वानरकोटीभिः समुत्तीर्णो महार्णवम्। ततो रामेण वीरेण हत्वा तान् सर्वराक्षसान्॥
en: He crossed the great ocean followed by million of monkeys. Thereupon all the Rakshasas were killed by Rama's prowess,

description: The Colloquy between Bhima and Hanuman
sn: रणे तु राक्षसगणं रावणं लोकरावणम्। निशाचरेन्द्रं हत्वा तु सभ्रातृसुतबान्धवम्॥
en: And also Ravana, that oppressor of the world, the king of the Rakshasas with all his Rakshasa relatives, brothers, sons and kindred.

description: The Colloquy between Bhima and Hanuman
sn: राज्येऽभिषिच्य लङ्कायां राक्षसेन्द्रं विभीषणम्। धार्मिकं भक्तिमन्तं च भक्तानुगतवत्सलम्॥
en: Rama installed on the throne of Lanka, the Rakshasa chief Vibhishana who was virtuous, reverent and kind to devoted followers.

description: The Colloquy between Bhima and Hanuman
sn: ततः प्रत्याहृता भार्या नष्टा वेदश्रुतिर्यथा। तयैव सहितः साध्व्या पल्या रामो महायशाः॥ गत्वा ततोऽतित्वरितः स्वां पुरी रघुनन्दनः। अध्यावसत् ततोऽयोध्यामयोध्यां द्विषतां प्रभुः॥
en: Then Rama recovered his wife like the lost Vedic lore. Then the greatly illustrious Rama, the descendant of Raghu, with his devoted wife went speedily to his own city of Ayodhya, inaccessible to enemies. That lord then dwelt there.

description: The Colloquy between Bhima and Hanuman
sn: ततः प्रतिष्ठितो राज्ये रामो नृपतिसत्तमः। वरं मया याचितोऽसौ रामो राजीवलोचनः॥
en: When that foremost of kings was established in his kingdom, I asked a boon from the lotus eyed Rama.

description: The Colloquy between Bhima and Hanuman
sn: यावद् राम कथेयं ते भवेल्लोकेषु शत्रुहन्। तावज्जीवेयमित्येवं तथास्त्विति च सोऽब्रवीत्॥
en: I said, "O chastiser of foes, O Rama, let me live as long as the history of your deeds remains extant on earth. Thereupon he said, “So be it."

description: The Colloquy between Bhima and Hanuman
sn: सीताप्रसादाच्च सदा मामिहस्थमरिदम। उपतिष्ठन्ति दिव्या हि भोगा भीम यथेप्सिताः॥
en: O chastiser of foes, O Bhima, through the grace of Sita, all excellent objects of enjoyments are supplied to me who always live in this place.

description: The Colloquy between Bhima and Hanuman
sn: दशवर्षसहस्राणि दशवर्षशतानि च। राज्यं कारितवान् रामस्ततः स्वभवनं गतः॥
en: Rama reigned ten thousand ten hundred years. Then he ascended his own abode.

description: The Colloquy between Bhima and Hanuman
sn: तदिहाप्सरसस्तात गन्धर्वाश्च सदानघ। तस्य वीरस्य चरितं गायन्तो रमयन्ति माम्॥
en: O child, O sinless one, since then Apsaras and the Gandharvas delight me by singing the great deeds of that great hero,

description: The Colloquy between Bhima and Hanuman
sn: अयं च मार्गो मर्त्यानामगम्य: कुरुनन्दन। ततोऽहं रुद्धवान् मार्गं तवेमं देवसेवितम्॥ धर्षयेद् वा शपेद् वापि मा कश्चिदिति भारत। दिव्यो देवपथो ह्येष नात्र गच्छन्ति मानुषाः। यदर्थमागतश्चासि अत एव सरश्च तत्॥
en: O descendant of Kuru, this passage is impassable to mortals; for this reason and as also with the view that none may defeat or curse you, I have obstructed your passage trodden by the celestials. This is one of the paths to heaven. Mortals cannot pass this way. But the lake in search of which you have come lies in that direction.

description: The colloquy between Hanuman and Bhimasena in Kadali forest
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्तो महाबाहुर्भीमसेनः प्रतापवान्। प्रणिपत्य ततः प्रीत्या भ्रातरं हृष्टमानसः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having been thus addressed, the mighty armed and greatly powerful Bhimasena cheerfully bowed down his head to his brother Hanuman.

description: The colloquy between Hanuman and Bhimasena in Kadali forest
sn: उवाच श्लक्ष्णया वाचा हनूमन्तं कपीश्वरम्। मयाधन्यतरो नास्ति यदार्यं हृष्टवानहम्॥
en: He spoke in mild words to the monkey chief, Hanuman, "None is more fortunate than I am for I have been able to see my brother.

description: The colloquy between Hanuman and Bhimasena in Kadali forest
sn: अनुग्रहो मे सुमहांस्तृप्तिश्च तव दर्शनात्। एकं तु कृतमिच्छामि त्वयाद्य प्रियमात्मनः॥
en: It is a great favour shown to me. I have been greatly pleased with you. Now I desire that you will today fulfill my wish.

description: The colloquy between Hanuman and Bhimasena in Kadali forest
sn: यत् ते तदाऽऽसीत् प्लवतः सागरं मकरालयम्। रूपमप्रतिमं वीर तदिच्छामि निरीक्षितुम्॥
en: O hero, I desire to see your that matchless form which you had at the time when you jumped across the ocean, that abode of crocodiles and sharks.

description: The colloquy between Hanuman and Bhimasena in Kadali forest
sn: एवं तुष्टो भविष्यामि श्रद्धास्यामि च ते वचः। एवमुक्तः स तेजस्वी प्रहस्य हरिरब्रवीत्॥
en: I shall be then satisfied and I shall have faith in your words.” Having been thus addressed, that greatly powerful one smilingly thus replied,

description: The colloquy between Hanuman and Bhimasena in Kadali forest
sn: न तच्छक्यं त्वया द्रष्टुं रूपं नान्येन केनचित्। कालावस्था तदा ह्यन्या वर्तते सा न साम्प्रतम्॥
en: "My that form neither you nor any one else can see. The state of things was different at that age. It does not exist now.

description: The colloquy between Hanuman and Bhimasena in Kadali forest
sn: अन्यः कृतयुगे कालस्त्रेतायां द्वापरे परः। अयं प्रध्वंसन: कालो नाद्य तद् रूपमस्ति मे॥
en: In the Krita Yuga, the state of things was one, in the Treta another and in the Dvapara another. Diminution (of everything) is taking place in this age. I have (therefore) not that form today.

description: The colloquy between Hanuman and Bhimasena in Kadali forest
sn: भूमिर्नद्यो नगाः शैलाः सिद्धा देवा महर्षयः। कालं समनुवर्तन्ते यथा भावा युगे युगे।॥
en: The ground, the rivers, the plants, the rocks, the Siddhas, the celestials, the great Rishis, all conform to Time, as it comes to be in the different Yugas.

description: The colloquy between Hanuman and Bhimasena in Kadali forest
sn: बलवर्णप्रभावा हि प्रहीयन्त्युद्भवन्ति च। तदलं वत तद् रूपं द्रष्टुं कुरुकुलोद्वह। युगं समनुवामि कालो हि दुरतिक्रमः॥
en: O perpetuator of the Kuru race, therefore do not desire to see my former form. I am following the tendency of this (present) age. Time is irresistible.

description: The colloquy between Hanuman and Bhimasena in Kadali forest
sn: भीम उवाच युगसंख्यां समाचक्ष्व आचारं च युगे युगे। धर्मकामार्थभावांश्च कर्मवीर्ये भवाभवौ॥
en: Tell me what is the duration of different Yugas and what are the different manners and customs, virtue, pleasure and profit, acts, prowess, life and death in those different ages.

description: The colloquy between Hanuman and Bhimasena in Kadali forest
sn: हनूमानुवाच कृतं नाम युगं तात यत्रधर्मः सनातनः। कृतमेव न कर्तव्यं तस्मिन् काले युगोत्तमे॥
en: O child, that Yuga was called Krita when only one true eternal religion was extant. In that best of Yugas everyone had religious perfection. There was no need for performing (any) religious act.

description: The colloquy between Hanuman and Bhimasena in Kadali forest
sn: न तत्रधर्माः सीदन्ति क्षीयन्ते न च वै प्रजाः। ततः कृतयुगं नाम कालेन गुणतां गतम्॥
en: Virtue then knew no decrease. It was for this reason that Yuga was called Krita (perfect). In course of time it lost all its attributes.

description: The colloquy between Hanuman and Bhimasena in Kadali forest
sn: देवदानवगन्धर्वयक्षराक्षसपन्नगाः। नासन् कृतयुगे तात तदा न क्रयविक्रयः॥
en: O child, in the Krita Yuga there were no celestials, no Danavas, no Gandharvas, no Yakshas, no Rakshasas and no Nagas. There was neither buying nor selling.

description: The colloquy between Hanuman and Bhimasena in Kadali forest
sn: न सामऋग्यजुर्वर्णाः क्रिया नासीच्च मानवी। अभिध्याय फलं तत्रधर्मः संन्यास एव च॥
en: The Sama, the Rick, the Vayu (Vedas) did not exist. There was no manual labour. The necessaries of life were procured only by thinking for them. The only Dharma was then renunciation.

description: The colloquy between Hanuman and Bhimasena in Kadali forest
sn: न तस्मिन् युगसंसर्गे व्याधयो नेन्द्रियक्षयः। नासूया नापि रुदितं न दो नापि वैकृतम्॥ न विग्रहः कुतस्तन्द्री न द्वेषो न च पैशुनम्। न भयं नापि संतापो न चेा न च मत्सरः॥
en: In that Yuga there was neither disease nor the decay of the senses. There was neither Imalice, nor pride, nor hypocrisy nor discord, nor ill-will nor cunningness, nor fear, nor misery, nor envy, nor covetousness.

description: The colloquy between Hanuman and Bhimasena in Kadali forest
sn: ततः परमकं ब्रह्म सा गतियोगिनां परा। आत्मा च सर्वभूतानां शुक्लो नारायणस्तदा॥
en: For this reason, even that chief refuge of all Yugas, the Supreme Brahma was attainable to all. The white cloth-wearing Narayana (also was the soul of all creatures,

description: The colloquy between Hanuman and Bhimasena in Kadali forest
sn: ब्राह्मणाः क्षत्रिया वैश्याः शूद्राश्च कृतलक्षणाः। कृते युगे समभवन् स्वकर्मनिरताः प्रजाः॥
en: In the Krita Yuga, the distinctive characteristics of the Brahmanas, the Kshatriyas, the Vaishyas and the Sudras were the same and all men were engaged in their own respective duties.

description: The colloquy between Hanuman and Bhimasena in Kadali forest
sn: समाश्रयं समाचारं समज्ञानं च केवलम्। तदा हि समकर्माणो वर्णाधर्मानवाप्नुवन्॥
en: Brahma was then the sole refuge (of all men), there manners and customs were adopted to the attainments of Brahma, the object of their knowledge was Brahina; all their acts also had reference to Brahma. Thus men of all orders obtained equal merit.

description: The colloquy between Hanuman and Bhimasena in Kadali forest
sn: एकदेवसदायुक्ता एकमन्त्रविधिक्रियाः। पृथग्धर्मास्त्वेकवेदाधर्ममेकमनुव्रताः॥
en: One uniform Soul was the object of their meditation, there was but one religion and one ordinance. Though Though they had different characteristics, they followed one Veda and they had one religion.

description: The colloquy between Hanuman and Bhimasena in Kadali forest
sn: चातुराश्रम्ययुक्तेन कर्मणा कालयोगिना। अकामफलसंयोगात् प्राप्नुवन्ति परां गतिम्॥
en: According to the divisions of time, they led the four modes of life without aiming at any object. Thus they obtained (final) emancipation.

description: The colloquy between Hanuman and Bhimasena in Kadali forest
sn: आत्मयोगसमायुक्तोधर्मोऽयं कृतलक्षणः। कृते युगे चतुष्पादश्चातुर्वण्यस्य शाश्वतः॥
en: The sign of Krita Yuga was that the religion thian consisted of the identification of self with Brahma. In the Krita age the four orders had eternal fourfold measure.

description: The colloquy between Hanuman and Bhimasena in Kadali forest
sn: एतत् कृतयुगं नाम त्रैगुण्यपरिवर्जितम्। त्रेतामपि निबोध त्वं यस्मिन् खत्रं प्रवर्तते।॥
en: Such was Krita Yuga devoid of the these qualities. Now hear from me all about the Treta Yuga in which sacrifices were introduced (in the word).

description: The colloquy between Hanuman and Bhimasena in Kadali forest
sn: पादेन हसतेधर्मो रक्ततां याति चाच्युतः। सत्यप्रवृत्ताश्च नराः क्रियाधर्मपरायणाः॥
en: (In this age) virtue decreased by a quarter and Narayana assumed a red colour. Men practised truth and devoted themselves to religion and religious rites.

description: The colloquy between Hanuman and Bhimasena in Kadali forest
sn: ततो यज्ञाः प्रवर्तन्तेधर्माश्च विविधाः क्रियाः। त्रेतायां भावसंकल्पाः क्रियादानफलोपगाः॥
en: Thus sacrifices were introduced and many religious rites came to be performed. In the Treta Yuga men began to devise to attain an object and they attained to it by performing (religious) acts and (giving away) gifts.

description: The colloquy between Hanuman and Bhimasena in Kadali forest
sn: प्रचलन्ति न वैधर्मात् तपोदानपरायणाः। स्वधर्मस्थाः क्रियावन्तो नरास्त्रेतायुगेऽभवन्॥
en: Men never deviated from virtue and they were always engaged in asceticism and the bestowal of gifts. The four orders were devoted to their respective duties and they performed (religious) rites. Such were the men in the Treta Yuga.

description: The colloquy between Hanuman and Bhimasena in Kadali forest
sn: द्वापरे च युगेधर्मो द्विभागोनः प्रवर्तते। विष्णुर्वै पीततां याति चतुर्धा वेद एव च॥
en: In the Dvapara Yuga virtue decreased by half; Vishnu assumed a yellow colour; and the Vedas became divided into four parts.

description: The colloquy between Hanuman and Bhimasena in Kadali forest
sn: ततोऽन्ये च चतुर्वेदास्त्रिवेदाश्च तथापरे। द्विवेदाश्चैकवेदाश्चाप्यनृचश्च तथापरे॥
en: Then some learnt all the four Vedas; some again only three, some two and some did not know even the Rich.

description: The colloquy between Hanuman and Bhimasena in Kadali forest
sn: एवं शास्त्रेषु भिन्नेषु बहुधा नीयते क्रिया। तपोदानप्रवृत्ता च राजसी भवति प्रजा॥
en: The Shastras having been thus divided, (religious) acts also (naturally) multiplied. Mostly influenced by passion, men engaged in asceticism and gifts.

description: The colloquy between Hanuman and Bhimasena in Kadali forest
sn: एकवेदस्य चाज्ञानाद् वेदास्ते बहवः कृताः। सत्त्वस्य चेह विभ्रंशात् सत्ये कश्चिदवस्थितः॥
en: As men had no capacity to study the entire Veda, it came to be divided into several parts. And as the intellect (of men) deteriorated, few were devoted to truth.

description: The colloquy between Hanuman and Bhimasena in Kadali forest
sn: सत्यात् प्रच्यवमानानां व्याधयो बहवोऽभवन्। कामाचोपद्रवाश्चैव तदा वै दैवकारिताः॥
en: When men fall off from truth, they become subject to various diseases, lust overtakes men and natural calamities fall on them.

description: The colloquy between Hanuman and Bhimasena in Kadali forest
sn: यैरर्यमानाः सुभृशं तपस्तष्यन्ति मानवाः। कामकामाः स्वर्गकामा यज्ञांस्तन्वन्ति चापरे॥
en: Being affected by these, some then betake to asceticism. Others perform sacrifices with the desire of enjoying worldly luxuries or of obtaining heaven (and its pleasures).

description: The colloquy between Hanuman and Bhimasena in Kadali forest
sn: एवं द्वापरमासाद्य प्रजाः क्षीयन्त्यधर्मतः। पादेनैकेन कौन्तेयधर्मः कलियुगे स्थितः॥
en: O son of Kunti, thus in the Dvapara age men became degenerated on account of their impiety. In the Kali Yuga, only one quarter of virtue remains.

description: The colloquy between Hanuman and Bhimasena in Kadali forest
sn: तामसं युगमासाद्य कृष्णो भवति केशवः। वेदाचाराः प्रशाम्यन्तिधर्मयज्ञक्रियास्तथा॥
en: When this age appears, Keshava (Vishnu) assumes a black colour. The Vedas, the Institutes, the virtue, the sacrifices and religious observances all fall into disuse.

description: The colloquy between Hanuman and Bhimasena in Kadali forest
sn: ईतयो व्याधयस्तन्द्री दोषाः क्रोधादयस्तथा। उपद्रवाः प्रवर्तन्ते आधयः क्षुद्भयं तथा॥
en: Then Ati (excessive rain), draught, rats, locusts, birds and king, diseases, lassitude, anger, deformities, natural calamities, anguish and fear of famine take possession of the world.

description: The colloquy between Hanuman and Bhimasena in Kadali forest
sn: युगेष्वावर्तमानेषुधर्मो व्यावर्तते पुनः। धर्मे व्यावर्तमाने तु लोको व्यावर्तते पुनः॥ लोके क्षीणे क्षयं यान्ति भावा लोकप्रवर्तकाः। युगक्षयकृताधर्माः प्रार्थनानि विकुर्वते॥ एतत् कलियुगं नाम अचिराद् यत् प्रवर्तते। युगानुवर्तनं त्वेतत् कुर्वन्ति चिरजीविनः॥
en: As this Yuga passes on, virtue becomes daily weaker. As virtue becomes weak, all creatures degenerate. And as creatures degenerate. their nature also undergoes deterioration. The religious acts performed at this waning of the Yuga produce contrary effects. Even those who live for several Yugas must conform to their changes.

description: The colloquy between Hanuman and Bhimasena in Kadali forest
sn: यच्च ते मत्परिज्ञाने कौतूहलमरिंदम। अनर्थकेषु को भावः पुरुषस्य विजानतः॥
en: O chastiser of foes, as regards your curiosity to know me, I tell you this, why should a wise man be eager to learn a superfluous thing?

description: The colloquy between Hanuman and Bhimasena in Kadali forest
sn: एतत् ते सर्वमाख्यातं यन्मां त्वं परिपृच्छसि। युगसंख्यां महाबाहो स्वस्ति प्राप्नुहि गम्यताम्॥
en: O mighty-armed hero, I have thus told you all that you asked me about the different Yugas. May good come to you. Now return.

description: The colloquy of Bhima and Hanuman
sn: भीमसेन उवाच पूर्वरूपमदृष्ट्वा ते न यास्यामि कथंचन। यदि तेऽहमनुग्राह्यो दर्शयात्मानमात्मना॥
en: Bhima said: I shall never go without seeing your former form. If you are pleased with me, show me your own form.

description: The colloquy of Bhima and Hanuman
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्तस्तु भीमेन स्मितं कृत्व प्लवगंमः। तद् रूपं दर्शयामास यद् वै सागरलङ्घने।॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having been thus addressed by Bhima, the monkey chief showed him the forin in which he jumped across the sea.

description: The colloquy of Bhima and Hanuman
sn: भ्रातुः प्रियमभीप्सन् वै चकार सुमहद् वपुः। देहस्तस्य ततोऽतीव वर्धत्यायामविस्तरैः॥
en: Desiring to gratify his brother, he (Hanuman) assumed a gigantic body which both in length and breadth grew exceedingly huge.

description: The colloquy of Bhima and Hanuman
sn: सदुमं कदलीषण्डं छादयन्नमितद्युतिः। गिरेश्वोच्छ्रयमाक्रम्य तस्थौ तत्र च वानरः॥
en: That greatly effulgent monkey stood there covering the whole of the plantain forest, full of trees and rising to the height, reached by the Vindhya (mountain).

description: The colloquy of Bhima and Hanuman
sn: समुच्छ्रितमहाकायो द्वितीय इव पर्वतः। ताम्रक्षणस्तीक्ष्णंष्ट्रो भृकुटीकुटिलाननः॥ दीर्घलाङ्गलमाविध्य दिशो व्याप्य स्थितः कपिः। तद् रूपं महदालक्ष्य भ्रातुः कौरवनन्दनः॥
en: Having attained to a lofty and gigantic body which looked like another mountain, (a body) furnished with coppery eyes and sharp teeth and a face marked by frowns, he lay covering all sides, lashing his long tail. That descendant of Kuru (Bhima), seeing his brother's that gigantic form.

description: The colloquy of Bhima and Hanuman
sn: विसिष्मिये तदा भीमो जहषे च पुनः पुनः। तमर्कमिव तेजोभिः सौवर्णमिव पर्वतम्॥ प्रदीप्तमिव चाकाशं दृष्ट्वा भीमो न्यमीलयत्। आवभाषे च हनुमान् भीमसेनं स्मयन्निव॥
en: Was greatly astonished and the down of his body again and again stood on end. Seeing him as blazing as the sun or the golden mountain or the blazing sky, Bhima closed his eyes. Then Hanuman smilingly thus spoke to Bhima.

description: The colloquy of Bhima and Hanuman
sn: एतावदिह शक्तस्त्वं द्रष्टुं रूपं ममानघ। वर्धेऽहं चाप्यतो भूयो यावन्मे मनसि स्थितम्। भीमशत्रुषु चात्यर्थं वर्धते मूर्तिरोजसा॥
en: "O Bhima, O sinless one, you are capable of seeing my form up to this extent. I can go on swelling my body as long as I wish. Amidst foes, my size increases exceedingly by its own energy.

description: The colloquy of Bhima and Hanuman
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तदद्भुतं महारौद्रं विन्ध्यपर्वतसंनिभम्। दृष्ट्वा हनूमतो वर्म सम्भ्रान्तः पवनात्मजः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Seeing that dreadful and wonderful body of Hanuman like the Vindhya mountain, the son of Pavana (Bhima) grew bewildered.

description: The colloquy of Bhima and Hanuman
sn: प्रत्युवाच ततो भीम: सम्प्रहृष्टतनूरुहः। कृताञ्जलिरदीनात्मा हनूमन्तमवस्थितम्॥
en: His down standing on end, the high-souled Bhima with joined hands spoke thus to Hanuman who was standing (in that form).

description: The colloquy of Bhima and Hanuman
sn: दृष्टं प्रमाणं विपुलं शरीरस्यास्य ते विभो। संहरस्व महावीर्य स्वयमात्मानमात्मना॥
en: "O lord, O greatly mighty one. I have seen the vast dimensions of your body. Now decrease it with your own prowess.

description: The colloquy of Bhima and Hanuman
sn: न हि शक्नोमि त्वां द्रष्टुं दिवाकरमिवोदितम्। अप्रमेयमनाघृष्यं मैनाकमिव पर्वतम्॥
en: I am unable to look at you who look like the rising sun, who is immeasurable and irrepressible and who resemble the Mainaka mountain.

description: The colloquy of Bhima and Hanuman
sn: विस्मयश्चैव मे वीर सुमहान् मनसोऽद्य वै। यद् रामस्त्वयि पार्श्वस्थे स्वयं रावणमभ्यगात्॥
en: O hero, this is my great wonder to day that when you were at the side of Rama, he had to fight personally with Ravana.

description: The colloquy of Bhima and Hanuman
sn: त्वमेव शक्तस्तां लङ्कां सयोधां सहवाहनाम्। स्वबाहुबलमाश्रित्य विनाशयितुमञ्जसा॥
en: Depending on your own strength of arms, you were capable of instantly destroying Lanka, with its warriors, heroes, elephants and chariots.

description: The colloquy of Bhima and Hanuman
sn: न हि ते किंचिदप्राप्यं मारुतात्मज विद्यते। तव नैकस्य पर्याप्तो रावणः सगणो युधि॥
en: O son of Vayu, there is nothing that is incapable of being achieved by you. Ravana together with his followers was no match for you in battle, though he fought you single handed.

description: The colloquy of Bhima and Hanuman
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्तस्तु भीमेन हनूमान् प्लवगोत्तमः। प्रत्युवाच ततो वाक्यं स्निग्धगम्भीरया गिरा॥
en: Vaishampayana said: Having been thus addressed by Bhima, that chief of monkeys, Hanuman replied in affectionate words and in solemn accents.

description: The colloquy of Bhima and Hanuman
sn: हनूमानुवाच एवमेतन्महाबाहो यथा वदसि भारत। भीमसेन न पर्याप्तो ममासौ राक्षसाधमः॥
en: Hanuman said: O mighty armed descendant of Bharata. O Bhimasena, it is as you say. That wretch of a Rakshasa (Ravana) was no match for me.

description: The colloquy of Bhima and Hanuman
sn: मया तु निहते तस्मिन् रावणे लोककण्टके। कीर्तिनश्येद् राघवस्य तत एतदुपेक्षितम्॥
en: But if I had killed Ravana, that thorn of the worlds, the glory of Raghu's son (Rama) would have been obscured, for this I left him alone.

description: The colloquy of Bhima and Hanuman
sn: तेन वीरेण तं हत्वा सगणं राक्षसाधमम्। आनीता स्वपुरं सीता कीर्तिश्चाख्यापिता नृषु॥
en: By killing that lord of the Rakashasas together with his followers and bringing back Sita to his own city, that hero established his fame among men.

description: The colloquy of Bhima and Hanuman
sn: तद् गच्छ विपुलप्रज्ञ भ्रातुः प्रियहिते रतः। अरिष्टं क्षेममध्वानं वायुना परिरक्षितः॥
en: O greatly wise one being intent on the welfare of your brothers and being protected by Vayu, go along a fortunate and blessed way.

description: The colloquy of Bhima and Hanuman
sn: एष पन्थाः कुरुश्रेष्ठ सौगन्धिकवनाय ते। द्रक्ष्यसेधनदोद्यानं रक्षितं यक्षराक्षसैः॥
en: O foremost of Kurus, this way will lead you to Saugandhika (forest). You will see the gardens of Kubera, guarded by the Yakshasas and Rakshasas.

description: The colloquy of Bhima and Hanuman
sn: न च ते तरसा कार्यः कुसुमावचयः स्वयम्। दैवतानि हि मान्यानि पुरुषेण विशेषतः॥
en: Do not pluck there any flowers by the force of your personal might, for the celestials deserve respect and regard from mortals,

description: The colloquy of Bhima and Hanuman
sn: बलिहोमनमस्कारैर्मन्त्रैश्च भरतर्षभ। दैवतानि प्रसादं हि भक्त्या दुर्वन्ति भारत।॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, O descendant of Bharata, men gratify the celestials by offerings, homas, sacrifices, reverential salutations, recitations of Mantras and veneration.

description: The colloquy of Bhima and Hanuman
sn: मा तात साहसं कार्षीः स्वधर्म परिपालय। स्वधर्मस्थः परंधर्मं बुध्यस्व गमयस्व च॥
en: O child, therefore do not act rashly, do not deviate from the duties of your order. Adhering to your own Dharma, know and follow the highest morality.

description: The colloquy of Bhima and Hanuman
sn: न हिधमविज्ञाय वृद्धाननुपसेव्य च। धर्मार्थो वेदितुं शक्यौ बृहस्पतिसमैरपि॥
en: Without knowing one's own duties and without waiting upon the old, even men who are like Brihaspati can never understand what Dharma and Artha (really are).

description: The colloquy of Bhima and Hanuman
sn: अधर्मो यत्रधर्माख्योधर्मश्चाधर्मसंज्ञितः। स विज्ञेयो विभागेन यत्र मुह्यन्त्यबुद्धयः॥
en: One should ascertain with discrimination those cases in which vice goes under the name of virtue and in which men, having no intelligence, become perplexed.

description: The colloquy of Bhima and Hanuman
sn: आचारसम्भवोधर्मोधर्मे वेदाः प्रतिष्ठिताः। वेदैर्यज्ञाः समुत्पन्ना यज्ञैर्देवाः प्रतिष्ठिताः॥
en: Four religious observances proceed from virtue, the Vedas are established in virtue and from the Vedas sacrifices came into existence. By sacrifices the celestials are established.

description: The colloquy of Bhima and Hanuman
sn: वेदाचारविधानोक्तैर्यज्ञैर्धार्यन्ति देवताः। बृहस्पत्युशन: प्रोक्तैर्नयैर्धार्यन्ति मानवाः॥
en: The celestials are maintained by the sacrifices prescribed by the Vedas and the ordinances. But men maintain themselves by following ordinances of ordinances of Brihaspati and Ushanas,

description: The colloquy of Bhima and Hanuman
sn: पण्याकरवणिज्याभिः कृष्यागोजाविपोषणैः। विद्ययाधार्यते सर्वधरतौर्द्विजातिभिः॥ त्रयी वार्ता दण्डनीतिस्तिस्रो विद्या विजानताम्। ताभिः सम्यक् प्रयुक्ताभिर्लोकयात्रा विधीयते॥ सा चेद्धर्मकृता न स्यात् त्रयीधर्ममृते भुवि। दण्डनीतिमृते चापि निर्मर्यादमिदं भवेत्॥ वार्ताधर्मे ह्यवर्तिन्यो विनश्येयुरिमाः प्रजाः। सुप्रवृत्तैस्त्रिभिद्येतैर्धर्मं सूयन्ति वै प्रजाः॥
en: And also by those avocations by which the world is maintained, such as serving for wages, receiving taxes, merchandise, agriculture and tending of cattle and sheep. The (study of the) three Vedas, agriculture, trade and government constitute, as it is ordained by the wise, the professions of the twice-born ones; each order maintains itself by following the professions prescribed for it. When these callings are properly pursued, the world is maintained with ease. If however men do not righteously lead their lives, the world becomes lawless for want of Vedic merit and government. And if people do not follow their respective vocations, they perish. But by regularly following their professions, they acquire virtue.

description: The colloquy of Bhima and Hanuman
sn: द्विजातीनामृतंधर्मो ह्येश्चैवैकलक्षणः। यज्ञाध्ययनदानानि त्रयः साधारणाः स्मृताः॥
en: The religion of the twice-born consists of the knowledge of the soul. The colour of that order is universally the The performances of sacrifices, study and the bestowal of gifts, these are the three wellknown general duties.

description: The colloquy of Bhima and Hanuman
sn: याजनाध्यापनं विप्रेधर्मश्चैव प्रतिग्रहः। पालनं क्षत्रियाणां वै वैश्यधर्मश्च पोषणम्॥
en: Performing sacrifices (on behalf of others), teaching and acceptance of gifts are the (three) duties of the Brahmana. The duty of the Kshatriya is to rule and that of Vaishya is to tend (cattle).

description: The colloquy of Bhima and Hanuman
sn: शुश्रूषा च द्विजातीनां शूद्राणां धर्म उच्यते। भैक्ष्यहोमव्रतैींनास्तथैव गुरुवासिताः॥
en: It is said that the duty of the Shudra is to serve the twice-born ones. The (Shudra) cannot beg alms, perform Homas and observe vows. They are to live in their master's house. same..

description: The colloquy of Bhima and Hanuman
sn: क्षत्रधर्मोऽत्र कौन्तेय तवधर्मोऽत्र रक्षणम्। स्वधर्म प्रतिपद्यस्व विनीतो नियतेन्द्रियः॥
en: O son of Kunti, your duty is that of a Kshatriya, namely to protect (men). Therefore controlling your passions, perform your own duties in an humble spirit.

description: The colloquy of Bhima and Hanuman
sn: वृद्धैः सम्मन्त्र्य सद्धिश्च बुद्धिमद्भिः श्रुतान्वितैः। आस्थितः शास्ति दण्डेन व्यसनी परिभूयते॥ निग्रहानुग्रहैः सम्यग् यदा राजा प्रवर्तते। तदा भवन्ति लोकस्य मर्यादा: सुव्यवस्थिताः॥
en: That king only is fit to govern who takes counsel of wise men, who is helped by honest, intelligent and learned ministers. But a sinful king always meets with defeat. When the king duly prescribes and properly confers favours, then only the order of the world is preserved.

description: The colloquy of Bhima and Hanuman
sn: तस्माद् देशे च दुर्गे च शत्रुमित्रबलेषु च। नित्यं चारेण बोद्धव्यं स्थानं वृद्धिः क्षयस्तथा॥
en: Therefore the nature of the hostile country, its fortified places, the allies of the enemy, their prosperity and adversity, must be ascertained by spies.

description: The colloquy of Bhima and Hanuman
sn: राज्ञामुपायश्चाश्च बुद्धिमत्रपराक्रमाः। निग्रहप्रग्रहौ चैव दाक्ष्यं वै कार्यसाधकम्॥ साम्ना दानेन भेदेन दण्डेनोपक्षणेन च। साधनीयानि कर्माणि समासव्यासयोगतः॥
en: Spies are the most important helps to a king; tact, diplomacy, prowess, chastisement, favour and cleverness lead to success. Success should also be attained through the following, either in their combination or in separation, namely conciliation, gifts, sowing dissension's, chastisement and slight.

description: The colloquy of Bhima and Hanuman
sn: मन्त्रमूला नया: भरतर्षभ। सुमन्त्रितेन या सिद्धिस्तां द्विजैः सह मन्त्रयेत्॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, politics has for its roots diplomacy. Diplomacy again is the main qualification of a spy. Well judged policy brings in success; therefore in the political matters, counsels of Brahmanas should be taken.

description: The colloquy of Bhima and Hanuman
sn: स्त्रिया मूढेन बालेन लुब्धेन लघुनापि वा। सर्वे चाराश्च न मन्त्रयीत गुह्यानि येषु चोन्मादलक्षणम्॥
en: In matters of secrecy, a woman, a fool, a boy, a covetous man, a mean-minded person and he in whom signs of insanity are marked must not be consulted.

description: The colloquy of Bhima and Hanuman
sn: मन्त्रयेत् सह विद्वद्भिः शक्तैः कर्माणि कारयेत्। स्निग्धैश्च नीतिविन्यासान् मूर्खान् सर्वत्र वर्जयेत्॥
en: Wise men should only be consulted and affairs should be transacted only through able officer. Diplomacy must be carried on through friendly persons. Fools must always be avoided.

description: The colloquy of Bhima and Hanuman
sn: धार्मिकान्धर्मकार्येषु अर्थकार्येषु पण्डितान्। स्त्रीषु क्लीबान् नियुञ्जीत क्रूरान् क्रूरेषु कर्ममु॥
en: In religious matters pious men, in the matters of gain learned men, in guarding woman eunuchs and in all crooked affairs crooked men should be employed.

description: The colloquy of Bhima and Hanuman
sn: स्वेभ्यश्चैव परेभ्यश्च कार्याकार्यसमुद्भवा। बुद्धिः कर्मसु विज्ञेया रिपूणां च बलाबलम्॥ बुद्ध्या स्वप्रतिपन्नेषु कुर्यात् साधुष्वनुग्रहम्। निग्रहं चाप्यशिष्टेषु निर्मर्यादेषु कारयेत्॥
en: Propriety and impropriety of the resolution of the enemy, as also their strength and weakness should be ascertain through one's own spies as well as the spies of the enemies. Favour should be shown to honest persons that have prudently sought protection. But lawless and disobedient persons should always be punished.

description: The colloquy of Bhima and Hanuman
sn: निग्रहे प्रग्रहे सम्यग् यदा राजा प्रवर्तते। तदा भवति लोकस्य मर्यादा सुव्यवस्थिता॥
en: When a king justly punishes and shows favour, dignity of the law is then well maintained and all people live in good order.

description: The colloquy of Bhima and Hanuman
sn: एष तेऽभिहितः पार्थ घोरोधर्मो दुरन्वयः। तं स्वधर्मविभागेन विनयस्थोऽनुपालय॥
en: O son of Pritha, I have thus explained to you all the kingly duties so difficult to comprehend. Perform with equanimity the duty as prescribed for your order.

description: The colloquy of Bhima and Hanuman
sn: तपोधर्मदमेज्याभिर्विप्रा यान्ति यथा दिवम्। दानातिथ्यक्रियाधमैर्यान्ति वैश्याच सद्गतिम्॥ क्षत्रं याति तथा स्वर्गं भुवि निग्रहपालनैः।
en: The Brahmanas go to heaven by ascetic merits, by controlling their senses and by performing sacrifices. The Vaishyas obtain the blessed state by gifts, hospitality and religious acts. The Kshatriyas go to heaven by protecting and punishing men.

description: The colloquy of Bhima and Hanuman
sn: सम्यक् प्रणीतदण्डा हि कामद्वेषविवर्जिताः। अलुब्धा विगतक्रोधाः सतां यान्ति सलोकताम्॥
en: Being not influenced by lust, malice, avarice and anger, if kings justly and properly punish (their subjects), they then go to the place where virtuous men go.

description: The colloquy of Bhima and Hanuman
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततः संहत्य विपुलं तद् वपुः कामतः कृतम्। भीमसेनं पुनर्दोर्ध्या पर्यष्वजत वानरः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Thereupon contracting his that huge body which he assumed at his pleasure, the monkey again embraced Bhimasena with both his arms.

description: The colloquy of Bhima and Hanuman
sn: परिष्वक्तस्य तस्याशु भ्रात्रा भीमस्य भारत। श्रमो नाशमुपागच्छत् सर्वं चासीत् प्रदक्षिणम्॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, having been thus embraced by his brother, Bhima's fatigue was gone and all his strength was restored.

description: The colloquy of Bhima and Hanuman
sn: बलं चातिबलो मेने न मेऽस्ति सदृशो महान्। ततः पुनरथोवाच पर्यश्रुनयनो हरिः॥ भीममाभाष्य सौहार्दाद् वाष्पगद्गदया गिरा। गच्छ वीर स्वमावासं स्मर्तव्योऽस्मि कथान्तरे॥
en: Having gained great strength, he thought that there was one equal to him in physical power. With tears in his eyes, the monkey again from affection towards Bhima thus spoke to him a choked voice, "O hero, go back to your own abode. Let me be incidentally remembered in your talk.

description: The colloquy of Bhima and Hanuman
sn: इहस्थश्च कुरुश्रेष्ठ न निवेद्योऽस्मि कर्हिचित्। धनदस्यालयाच्चापि विसृष्टानां महाबल॥ देशकाल इहायातुं देवगन्धर्वयोषिताम्। ममापि सफलं चक्षुः स्मारितश्चास्मि राघवम्॥ रामाभिधानं विष्णुं हि जगद्धृदयनन्दनम्। सीतावक्त्रारविन्दाङ दशास्यध्वान्तभास्करम्॥ मानुषं गात्रसंस्पर्शं गत्वा भीम त्वया सह। तदस्मद्दर्शनं वीर कौन्तेयामोघमस्तु ते॥
en: O foremost of the Kurus, do not tell anyone that I live here. O greatly powerful one, the most excellent wives of celestials and the Gandharvas frequent this place. The time of their coming is near. My eyes are blessed (by seeing you). O Bhima, having come in contact (again) with a human being (yourself). I have mentally felt (the presence of) that son of Raghu, who was Vishnu himself in the name of Rama, who was the delight of the whole world and who was the blazing sun to that lotus Sita and to that darkness, Ravana. Therefore, O hero, O son of Kunti, let not your interview with me be futile.

description: The colloquy of Bhima and Hanuman
sn: भ्रातृत्वं त्वं पुरस्कृत्य वरं वरय भारता यदि तावन्मया क्षुद्रा गत्वा वारणसाह्वयम्॥ धार्तराष्ट्रा निहन्तव्या यावदेतत् करोम्यहम्। शिलया नगरं वापि मर्दितव्यं मया यदि॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, with fraternal feeling ask from me a boon. If you desire that I shall go to Hastinapur and kill the insignificant sons of Dhritarashtra, I shall even do this (for your sake) or that I shall grind that city with stone.

description: The colloquy of Bhima and Hanuman
sn: बद्ध्वा दुर्योधनं चाद्य आनयामि तवान्तिकम्। यावदेतत् करोम्यद्य कामं तव महावल॥
en: Or that I shall bind Duryodhana and bring him here. O greatly powerful hero, even this I shall do today.

description: The colloquy of Bhima and Hanuman
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच भीमसेनस्तु तद् वाक्यं श्रुत्वा तस्य महात्मनः। प्रत्युवाच हनूमन्तं प्रहृष्टेनान्तरात्मना॥
en: Having heard the words of that high-souled one, Bhimasena with a delighted heart thus spoke to Hanuman.

description: The colloquy of Bhima and Hanuman
sn: कृतमेव त्वया सर्वं मम वानरपुङ्गवा स्वस्ति तेऽस्तु महाबाहो कामये त्वां प्रसीद मे॥
en: "O foremost of monkeys, O mighty-armed hero, I consider all this already performed by you. Good come to you. I ask you to be pleased with ine.

description: The colloquy of Bhima and Hanuman
sn: सनाथाः पाण्डवाः सर्वे त्वया नाथेन वीर्यवन्। तवैव तेजसा सर्वान् विजेष्यामो वयं परान्॥
en: O mighty-armed hero, when you have become our protector, the Pandavas have (already) secured their lord. With your effulgence we shall conquer all our enemies."

description: The colloquy of Bhima and Hanuman
sn: एवमुक्तस्तु हनुमान् भीमसेनमभाषत। भ्रातृत्वात् सौहृदाच्चैव करिष्यामि प्रियं तव॥
en: Having been thus addressed, Hanuman then spoke to Bhimasena, "From fraternal affection and friendship, I shall do you good.”

description: The colloquy of Bhima and Hanuman
sn: चमू विगाह्य शत्रूणां शरशक्तिसमाकुलाम्। यदा सिंहरवं वीर करिष्यसि महाबला॥
en: By rushing into the enemy's force armed with numerous arrows and javelins when you shall give forth lion-like roars, O hero, O greatly powerful one,

description: The colloquy of Bhima and Hanuman
sn: तदाहं बृहयिष्यामि स्वरवेण रवं तव। विजयस्यध्वजस्थश्च नादान् मोक्ष्यामि दारुणान्॥
en: I shall then with my own (shouts) add to your shouts. Remaining on Vijaya's (Arjuna) flag-staff, I shall send forth fearful shouts.

description: The colloquy of Bhima and Hanuman
sn: शत्रूणां ये प्राणहराः सुखं येन हनिष्यथ। एवमाभाष्य हनुमांस्तदा पाण्डवनन्दनम्॥ मार्गमाख्याय भीमाय तत्रैवान्तरधीयत॥
en: Which will damp the courage of your enemies. You will then be able to destroy them with ease.” Having thus spoken to the son of Pandu, Hanuman first pointed out to him the way and disappeared.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच गते तस्मिन् हरिवरे भीमोऽपि बलिनां वरः। तेन मार्गेण विपुलं व्यचरद् गन्धमादनम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said: When that best of monkeys had gone away, that foremost of powerful men Bhima, went by that way over the extensive Gandhamadana.

sn: अनुस्मरन् वपुस्तस्य श्रियं चाप्रतिमां भुवि। माहात्म्यमनुभावं च स्मरन् दाशरथेर्ययौ॥
en: He went on, reflecting on Hanumana's body and effulgence which were matchless on earth and also the greatness and dignity of Dasharatha's son.

sn: स तानि रमणीयानि वान्युपवनानि च। विलोकयामास तदा सौगन्धिकवनेप्सया॥ फुल्लद्रुमविचित्राणि सरांसि सरितस्तथा। नानाकुसुमचित्राणि पुष्पितानि वनानि च॥
en: Going in search of the place where grew the lotuses (in question), Bhima saw romantic forests, groves, rivers, lakes, trees adorned with blossoms and sylvan wood-lands beautified by various flowers.

sn: मत्तवारणयूथानि पङ्कक्लिन्नानि भारत। वर्षतामिव मेघानां वृन्दानि ददृशे तदा॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, he saw herds of mad elephants besmeared with mud. They looked like masses of clouds pouring rains.

sn: हरिणैश्चपलापाङ्गैर्हरिणीसहितैर्वनम्। सशष्पकवलैः श्रीमान् पथि दृष्ट्वा द्रुतं ययौ॥
en: When proceeding quickly, that handsome hero saw in the forest, deer of quick glances with grass in their mouth standing along with their mates.

sn: महिषैश्च वराहैश्च शार्दूलैश्च निषेवितम्। व्यपेतभीर्गिरि शौर्याद् भीमसेनो व्यगाहत॥ कुसुमानन्तगन्धैश्च ताम्रपल्लवकोमलैः।। याच्यमान इवारण्ये दुमैर्मारुतकम्पितैः॥ कृतपद्माञ्जलिपुटा मत्तषट् पदसेविताः। प्रियतीर्थवना मार्गे पद्मिनी: समतिक्रम॥
en: Bhimasena, fearless from his great prowess, went into that hilly region inhabited by the buffaloes, bears and leopards, as if he had been invited by the forest-trees, shaken by the breeze, ever fragrant with flowers and bearing beautiful copper-coloured twigs. He passed by lakes, each having romantic descents and woods, adorned with lotuses and lilies, which were swarıned with maddened black bees. On account of the presence of the lotus-buds, they appeared as if they had joined hands (before Bhima).

sn: मज्ज्मानमनोदृष्टिः फुल्लेषु गिरिसानुषु। द्रौपदीवाक्यपाथेयो भीमः शीघ्रतरं ययौ॥
en: Having for his provisions, on the way, the words of Draupadi, Bhima proceeded on with great speed, keeping his mind and eyes fixed on the charming slopes of the mountain.

sn: परिवृत्तेऽहनि ततः प्रकीर्णहरिणे वने। काञ्चनैर्विमलैः पौर्ददर्श विपुलां नदीम्॥
en: When the time of noon had passed away, he saw the forest scattered over by deer and also by a great river full of fresh golden lotuses.

sn: हंसकारण्डवयुतां चक्रवाकोपशोभिताम्। रचितामिव तस्याद्रेर्मालां विमलापङ्कजाम्॥
en: Swarmed with swans and Karandavas and adorned with Chakravakas, it (the river) appeared like a garland of pure lotuses worn by the mountain.

sn: तस्यां नद्यां महासत्त्वः सौगन्धिकवनं महत्। अपश्यत् प्रीतिजननं बालार्कसदृशद्युति॥
en: That greatly powerful hero saw, there, the great Sugandhika forest, delightful and effulgent as the sun.

sn: तद् दृष्ट्वा लब्धकामः स मनसा पाण्डुनन्दनः। वनवासपरिक्लिष्टां जगाम मनसा प्रियाम्॥
en: Seeing it, the son of Pandu (Bhima) thought in his mind that his object had been fulfilled. He also mentally presented himself before his beloved (Draupadi) worn out by exile.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच स गत्वा नलिनी रम्यां राक्षसैरभिरक्षिताम्। कैलासशिखराभ्याशे ददर्श शुभकाननाम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Going there, he (Bhima) saw, near the Kailasha peak, that charming lake adorned with lotuses and surrounded by blessed woods and guarded by the Rakshasas.

sn: कुबेरभवनाभ्याशे जातां पर्वतनिर्झरैः। सुरम्यां विपुलच्छायां नानादुमलताकुलाम्॥
en: It was made by the waters of) the springs of the mountains near the abode of Kubera. It was charming, it had wide spreading shade, it was adorned with various trees and creepers.

sn: हरिताम्बुजसंच्छन्नां दिव्यां कनकपुष्कराम्। नानापक्षिजनाकीर्णां सूपतीर्थामकर्दमाम्॥
en: It was covered with green lilies, it was filled with golden lotuses, it swarmed with various birds, its banks were beautiful and free from mud.

sn: अतीवरम्यां सुजला जातां पर्वतसानुषु। विचित्रभूतां लोकस्य शुभामद्भुतदर्शनाम्॥
en: Situated on the mountain, this charming sheet of water was the wonder of the world; it was beautiful and delightful to behold.

sn: तत्रामृतरसं शीतं लघु कुन्तीसुतः शुभम्। ददर्श विमलं तोयं पिबंश्च बहु पाण्डवः॥
en: The son of Kunti saw that ambrosial lake; its water was cool, light, clear and fresh. The Pandava (Bhima) drank much of its water.

sn: तां तु पुष्करिणी रम्यां दिव्यसौगन्धिकावृताम्। जातरूपमयैः पद्मश्छन्नां परमगन्धिभिः॥ वैदूर्यवरनालैश्च बहुचित्रैमनोरमैः। हंसकारण्डवोद्भूतैः सृजद्भिरमलं रजः॥
en: That celestials lake was covered with heavenly Sugandhika lotuses. It was also filled with beautiful, variegated, charming and fragrant golden lotuses with beautiful stalks made of Vaidurya gems. Being disturbed by the and Karandavas, they were scattering fresh and pure farina.

sn: आक्रीडं राजराजस्य कुबेरस्य महात्मनः। गन्धर्वैरप्सरोभिश्च देवैश्च परमार्चिताम्॥
en: It was the play-ground of the king of the kings, the high-souled Kubera. It was adorned swans by the Gandharvas, the Apsaras and the celestials.

sn: सेवितामृषिभिर्दिव्यैर्यक्षैः किम्पुरुषैस्तथा। राक्षसैः किन्नरैश्चापि गुप्तां वैश्रवणेन च॥
en: It was frequented by the celestials Rishis, the Yakshas, the Kimpurushas, the Rakshasas and the Kinniras. It was well-protected by Vaishravana (Kubera).

sn: तां च दृष्टवैव कौन्तेयो भीमसेनो महाबलः। बभूव परमप्रीतो दिव्यं सम्प्रेक्ष्य तत् सरः॥
en: When the greatly powerful son of Kunti, Bhimasena saw that celestials lake, he became greatly delighted.

sn: तच्च क्रोधवशा नाम राक्षसा राजशासनात्। रक्षन्ति शतसाहस्रश्चित्रायुधपरिच्छदाः॥
en: At the command of their king hundreds and thousands of Rakshasas, called Krodhavasas, clad in uniforms and armed with various weapons, were guarding it.

sn: ते तु दृष्ट्वैव कौन्तेयमजिनैः प्रतिवासितम्। रुक्माङ्गदधरं वीरं भीमं भीमपराक्रमम्॥ सायुधं बद्धनिस्त्रिंशमशङ्कितमरिदमम्। पुष्करेप्सुमुपायान्तमन्योन्यमभिचक्रुशुः॥
en: As that chastiser of foes, that son of Kunti, Bhima of fearful prowess clad in deer skins, wearing golden armlets and girding on his sword, fearlessly proceeded with the desire of gathering those lotuses, the Rakshasas saw him; and they immediately shouted out addressing one another.

sn: अयं पुरुषशार्दूल: सायुधोऽजिनसंवृतः। यच्चिकीर्षुरिह प्राप्तस्तत् सम्प्रष्टुमिहार्हथ॥
en: “You should enquire why this foremost of mien, clad in deer skins and armed with weapons, has come here."

sn: ततः सर्वे महाबाहु समासाद्य वृकोदरम्। तेजोयुक्तमपृच्छन्त कस्त्वमाख्यातुमर्हसि॥
en: Thereupon they all came to the mightyarmed and effulgent Vrikodara (Bhima) and asked, "Who are you? you should answer our question.

sn: मुनिवेषधरश्चैव सायुधश्चैव लक्ष्यसे। यदर्थमभिसम्प्राप्तस्तदाचक्ष्व महामते॥
en: We see, you are in the garb of an ascetic, but yet you are armed with weapons. O highminded one, tell us why you have come (here).”

sn: भीम उवाच पाण्डवो भीमसेनोऽहंधर्मराजादनन्तरः। विशाला बदरीं प्राप्तो भ्रातृभिः सह राक्षसाः॥
en: Bhima said: I am Bhimasena, the son of Pandu. I am next in birth to Dharmaraja (Yudhishthira). O Rakshasas, I had come with my brother to the great Badari.

sn: अपश्यत् तत्र पाञ्चाली सौगन्धिकमनुत्तमम्। अनिलोढमितो नूनं सा बहूनि परीप्सति॥
en: There did the Panchala princess see an excellent Sugandhika (lotus), which was certainly carried there by wind from this place. She desired to possess more of that kind lotus.

sn: तस्या मामनवद्याझ्याधर्मपल्याः प्रिये स्थितम्। पुष्पाहारमिह प्राप्तं निबोधत निशाचराः॥
en: O rangers in night, know, that being ever engaged in fulfilling the desire of my wedded wife of faultless feature, I have come here to get the flowers.

sn: राक्षसा ऊचुः आक्रीडोऽयं कुबेरस्य दयितः पुरुषर्षभ। नेह शक्यं मनुष्येण विहर्तुं मर्त्यधर्मणा॥
en: The Rakshasas said : O foremost of men, this place is the favourite play-ground of Kubera. Men subject to the laws of earth cannot sport here.

sn: देवर्षयस्तथा यक्षा देवाश्चात्र वृकोदर। आमन्त्र्य यक्षप्रवरं पिबन्ति रमयन्ति च। गन्धर्वाप्सरसश्चैव विहरन्त्यत्र पाण्डव॥
en: O Vrikodara, the celestials Rishis, the Yakshas and the celestials, after taking permission of the Yaksha chief, drink the water of this lake and sport here. O Pandava, the Gandharvas and the Apsaras (also) sport here.

sn: अन्यायेनेह यः कश्चिदवमान्यधनेश्वरम्। विहर्तुमिच्छेद् दुर्वृत्तः स विनश्येन्न संशयः॥
en: That wicked person, who without heeding the lord of wealth (Kubera), unlawfully tries to sport here, certainly meets with destruction.

sn: तमनादृत्य पद्मानि जिहीर्षसि बलादृतः। धर्मराजस्य चात्मानं ब्रवीषि भ्रातरं कथम्॥
en: Without heeding him (Kubera), you intend to take away the lotuses from this place by main force, why then do you say that you are the brother of Dharmaraja?

sn: आमन्त्र्य यक्षराजं वै ततः पिब हरस्व च। नातोऽन्यथा त्वया शक्यं किंचित् पुष्करमीक्षितुम्।।८।
en: First take the permission of the king of the Yakshas and then drink (the water of this lake) and take away (the lotuses) If you do not act thus, you will not be able even to look at these flowers.

sn: भीमसेन उवाच राक्षसास्तं न पश्यामिधनेश्वरमिहान्तिके। दृष्ट्वापि च महाराजं नाहं याचितुमुत्सहे॥
en: Bhimasena said: Rakshasas, I do not see the lord of wealth here. Even if I see that great king, I shall not pray (for the flowers) to him,

sn: न हि याचन्ति राजान एषधर्मः सनातनः। न चाहं हातुमिच्छामि क्षात्रधर्मं कथंचन॥
en: The Kshatriyas never beg; this is the eternal Dharma. I never wish to forsake the duties of a Kshatriya.

sn: इयं च नलिनी रम्या जाता पर्वतानिर्झरे। नेयं भवनमासाद्य कुबेरस्य महात्मनः॥
en: The lotus-lake has sprung up on the mountain breast. It has not been made in the abode of the illustrious Kubera.

sn: तुल्या हि सर्वभूतानामियं वैश्रवणस्य च। एवं गतेषु द्रव्येषु कः कं याचितुमर्हति॥
en: (Therefore) it belongs to every body equally with Vaisravana (Kubera). In such things, who should beg to others?

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच इत्युक्त्वा राक्षसान् सर्वान् भीमसेनो ह्यमर्षणः। व्यगाहत महाबाहुर्नलिनी तां महाबलः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having said this to all the Rakshasas, the mighty-armed and exceedingly unforbearing and greatly strong Bhimasena plunged into the lake.

sn: ततः स राक्षसैर्वाचा प्रतिषिद्धः प्रतापवान्। मा मैवमिति सक्रोधैर्भर्त्सयद्भिः समन्ततः॥
en: Thereupon that powerful hero was forbidden by the Rakshasas, saying “Don't do it” and from all sides they began to abuse him in anger.

sn: कद कृत्य तु स तान् राक्षसान् भीमविक्रमः। व्यगाहत महातेजास्ते तं सर्वे न्यवारयन्॥
en: Not heeding them at all, that greatly powerful one plunged (into the lake). But they (the Rakshasas) prepared themselves to oppose him.

sn: गृहणीत बध्नीत विकर्ततेमं पचाम खादाम च भीमसेनम्। क्रुद्धा ब्रुवन्तोऽभिययुटुंतं ते शस्त्राणि चोद्यम्य विवृत्तनेत्राः॥
en: With rolling eyes, they upraised their arms and rushed in anger at Bhimasena, crying "Seize him" "Bind him," "Cut him down" "Look to Bhima and eat him up."

sn: ततः स गुर्वी यमदण्डकल्पां महागदां काञ्चनपट्टनद्धाम्। प्रगृह्य तानभ्यपतत् तरस्वी ततोऽब्रवीत् तिष्ठत तिष्ठतेति॥
en: Thereupon that greatly powerful hero, taking up his huge and mighty mace inlaid with gold which resembled the mace of Yama himself, turned towards those (Rakshasas) and exclaimed, "Stay," "Stay".

sn: ते तं तदा तोमरपट्टिशाद्यैर्व्याविद्धशस्त्रैः सहसा निपेतुः। जिघांसवः क्रोधवशाः सुभीमा भीमं समन्तात परिवव्र रुग्राः॥
en: Thereupon they rushed upon him with great force upraising their lances, axes and other weapons. Desiring to kill Bhima, those dreadful and fearful Krodhavasas surrounded hiin on all sides.

sn: वातेन कुन्त्यां बलवान् सुजात: शूरस्तरस्वी द्विषतां निहन्ता। सत्ये चधर्मे च रतः सदैव पराक्रमे शत्रुभिरप्रधृष्यः॥
en: But that mighty hero was begotten by Vayu in the womb of Kunti. He was heroic and courageous; that slayer of foes was ever devoted to virtue and truth. He was incapable of being vanquished by any enemy through prowess.

sn: तेषां स मार्गान् विविधान् महात्मा विहत्य शस्त्राणि च शात्रवाणाम्। यथा प्रवीरान् निजघान भीमः। परं शतं पुष्करिणीसमीपे॥
en: Therefore on the banks of that lake he defeated the foes and broke their arms. He kiiled more than one hundred, beginning from the foremost.

sn: ते तस्य वीर्यं च बलं च दृष्ट्वा विद्याबलं बाहुबलं तथैव। अशक्नुवन्तः सहितं समन्ताद् दुतं प्रवीराः सहसा निवृत्ताः॥
en: Seeing his prowess, strength and also the might of his arms, those foremost of heroes, being unable to withstand (his attack), began suddenly to fly in all directions.

sn: माकाशमास्थाय विमूढसंज्ञाः। कैलासशृङ्गाण्यभिदुद्रुवुस्ते भीमार्दिताः क्रोधवशा: प्रभग्नाः॥
en: Beaten and pierced by Bhimasena, those Krodhavasas left the field of battle and confusedly and hurriedly fled towards Kailasha mountain through the sky.

sn: स शक्रवद् दानवदैत्यसङ्घान् विक्रम्य जित्वा च रणेऽरिसङ्घान्। विगाह्य तां पुष्करिणी जितारिः कामाय जग्राह ततोऽम्बुजानि॥
en: Having thus vanquished those Rakshasas by his prowess, as Indra did the armies of the Daityas and the Danavas, he again plunged into the lake and began to gather the lotuses with the object of accomplishing his purpose.

sn: ततः स पीत्वामृतकल्पमम्भो भूयो बभूवोत्तमवीर्यतेजसाः। उत्पाट्य जग्राह च सोऽम्बुजानि सौगन्धिकान्युत्तमगन्धवन्ति॥
en: When he drank the water (of the lake) which was like ambrosia, his energy and strength were again fully restored; he then plucked and gathered the golden lotuses of excellent fragrance.

sn: ततस्तु ते क्रोधवशाः समेत्य धनेश्वरं भीमबलप्रणुनाः। भीमस्य वीर्यं च बलं च संख्ये यथावदाचख्युरतीव भीताः॥
en: (In the mean while) the Krodhavasas, being driven by the prowess of Bhima and greatly terrified, went to the lord of wealth (Kubera) and informed him of Bhima's prowess and strength.

sn: तेषां वचस्तत् तु निशम्य देवः प्रहस्य रक्षांसि ततोऽभ्युवाच। गृहणातु भीमो जलजानि कामात् कृष्णानिमित्तं विदितं ममैतत्॥
en: Having heard their words, the deity (Kubera) smiled and then said, 'Let Bhima take for Krishna (Draupadi) as many lotuses as he likes. This is already known to me."

sn: ततोऽभ्यनुज्ञाप्यधनेश्वरं ते जग्मुः कुरूणां प्रवरं विरोधाः। भीमं च तस्यां ददृशुर्नलिन्यां यथोपजोषं विहरन्तमेकम्॥
en: Thereupon taking the permission of the lord of wealth (Kubera) and giving up their anger, those (Rakshasas) went (back) to that foremost of the Kurus (Bhima); and they saw Bhima alone sporting in delight in that lotus-lake.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततस्तानि महार्हाणि दिव्यानि भरतर्षभ। बहूनि बहुरूपाणि विरजांसि समादद॥
en: Vaishampayana said: O best of the Bharata race, Bhima then began to gather those rare, celestials, variegated and fresh flowers in profusion.

sn: ततो वायुर्महाशीघ्रो नीचैः शर्करकर्षणः। प्रादुरासीद् खरस्पर्शः संग्राममभिचोदयन्॥
en: Then rose suddenly a high and violent wind, piercing to the touch and blowing gravels and stones.

sn: पपात महती चोल्का सनिर्घाता महाभया। निष्प्रभश्चाभवत् सूर्यश्छन्नरश्मिस्तमोवृतः॥
en: Fearful meteors began to fall with thundering roars. Being enveloped by darkness, the sun became pale and his rays were obscured.

sn: निर्घातश्चाभवद् भीमो भीमे विक्रममास्थिते। चचाल पृथिवी चापि पांसुवर्षं पपात च॥
en: As Bhima displayed his prowess dreadful sounds of explosions rang through the sky; the earth began to tremble and dust fell in showers.

sn: सलोहिता दिशश्चासन् खरवाचो मृगद्विजाः। तमोवृतमभूत् सर्वं न प्राज्ञायत किंचन॥
en: Beasts and birds cried in shrilled voices; everything was enveloped in darkness and nothing could be seen.

sn: अन्ये च बहवो भीमा उत्पातास्तत्र जज्ञिरे। तदद्भुतमभिप्रेक्ष्यधर्मपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Other evil omens also appeared. Saying this strange phenomenon, the son of Dharma, Yudhishthira,

sn: उवाच वदतां श्रेष्ठः कोऽस्मानभिभविष्यति। सज्जीभवत भद्रं वः पाण्डवा युद्धदुर्मदाः॥ यथारूपाणि पश्यामि स्वभ्यग्रो नः पराक्रमः। एवमुक्त्वा ततो राजा वीक्षांश्चक्रे समन्ततः॥
en: That foremost of speakers, thus spoke, “Who will overcome us? OPandavas, who are always invincible in battle, be blessed. Arm yourself. From what I see I am of opinion that time has come near, when we are to display our prowess." Having said this, the king looked around.

sn: अपश्यमानो भीमं तुधर्मपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः। ततः कृष्णां यमौ चापि समीपस्थावरिंदमः॥ पप्रच्छ भ्रातरं भीमं भीमकर्माणमाहवे। कच्चित् क्व भीमः पाञ्चालि किंचित् कृत्यं चिकीर्षति।।
en: Having not seen Bhima, Dharmaraja Yudhishthira, that chastiser of foes, asked Krishna (Draupadi) and the twins who were near by, about his brother Bhima of fearful deeds, “O Panchala princess, is Bhima intent upon performing some great act?

sn: कृतवानपि वा वीरः साहसं साहसप्रियः। इमे ह्यकस्मादुत्पाता महासमरदर्शनाः॥ दर्शयन्तो भयं तीव्र प्रादुर्भूताः समन्ततः। तं तथावादिनं कृष्णा प्रत्युवाच मनस्विनी। प्रिया प्रियं चिकीर्षन्ती महिषी चारुहासिनी॥
en: Or has that hero who delights in daring deeds already achieved some great feat? These omens appear on all sides, indicating a great battle and portending some fearful danger.” When he said this, the intelligent Krishna, (Draupadi) of sweet smiles, his beloved wife, thus spoke to him to remove his anxiety.

sn: द्रौपद्युवाच यत् तत् सौगन्धिकं राजन्नाहृतं मातरिश्वना। तन्मया भीमसेनस्य प्रीतयाद्योपपादितम्॥
en: "O king, the golden lotus that was brought here by the wind, I showed to Bhimasena out of love. I also told that hero "If you can find.

sn: अपि चोक्तो मया वीरो यदि पश्येर्बहून्यपि। तानि सर्वाण्युपादाय शीघ्रमागम्यतामिति॥
en: More of these flowers, get all of them (for me); and soon come back." O son of Pandu, that mighty armed hero with the desire of gratifying my wish,

sn: स तु नूनं महाबाहुः प्रियार्थं मम पाण्डवः। प्रागुदीची दिशं राजंस्तान्याहर्तुमितो गतः॥
en: Has perhaps, O king, gone towards the north-east to get them.” Having been thus addressed by her, the king thus spoke to the twins,

sn: उक्तस्त्वेवं तया राजा यमाविदमथाब्रवीत्। गच्छाम सहितास्तूर्णं येन यातो वृकोदरः॥
en: “We must all soon go along the path Vrikodara (Bhima) has gone. Let the Rakshasas carry all those Brahmanas who are fatigued and who are weak.

sn: वहन्तु राक्षसा विप्रान् यथाश्रान्तान् यथाकृशान्। त्वयध्यमरसंकाश वह कृष्णां घटोत्कच॥
en: O Ghatotkacha, you are like a celestials; carry Krishna (Draupadi). In my opinion and it is quite evident, Bhima has entered (the forest).

sn: व्यक्तं दूरमितो भीमः प्रविष्ट इति मे मतिः। चिरं च तस्य कालोऽयं स च वायुसमो जवे॥
en: It is long since he has gone away; he resembles the wind in speed. In leaping over the grounds, he is like the son of Vinata (Garuda),

sn: तरस्वी वैनतेयस्य सदृशो भुवि लङ्घने। उत्पतेदपि चाकाशं निपतेच्च यथेच्छकम्॥
en: He will even leap into the sky and come down at will. O night-rangers, we shall follow him through your prowess.

sn: तमन्वियाम भवतां प्रभावाद् रजनीचराः। पुरा स नापरानोति सिद्धानां ब्रह्मवादिनाम्॥ तथेत्युक्त्वा तु ते सर्वे हैडिम्बप्रमुखास्तदा। उद्देशज्ञाः कुबेरस्य नलिन्या भरतर्षभ॥ आदाय पाण्डवांश्चैव तांश्च विप्राननेकशः। लोमशेनैव सहिताः प्रययुः प्रीतमानसाः॥
en: He will never first offend the Siddhas, learned in the Vedas." O best of the Bharata race, saying "Be it so," the son of Hidimba (Ghatotkacha) and the other Rakshasas, who knew the place where the lotus-lake of Kuber was situated, cheerfully started with Lomasha, carrying the Pandavas and many of the Brahmanas. Going with great speed, they saw the blessed forest,

sn: ते सर्वे त्वरिता गत्वा ददृशुः शुभकाननाम्। पद्मसौगन्धिकवती नलिनी सुमनोरमाम्॥
en: Adorned with golden lotuses and other lilies and surrounded by beautiful woods. On its shores they saw the high-souled and energetic Bhima.

sn: तं च भीमं महात्मानं तस्यास्तीरे मनस्विनम्। ददृशुनिहतांश्चैव यक्षांश्च विपुलेक्षणान्॥
en: And (they saw) also the slain Yakshas of large eyes, with their bodies, eyes, arms and thighs smashed and their heads crushed.

sn: भिन्नकायाक्षिबाहूरून् संचूर्णितशिरोधरान्। तं च भीमं महात्मानं तस्यास्तीरे व्यवस्थितम्॥ सक्रोधं स्तब्धनयनं संदष्टशनच्छदम्। उद्यम्य च गदां दो• नदीतीरेष्ववस्थितम्॥
en: On seeing the high-souled Bhima standing on the shore of that lake in angry mood and with steadfast eyes and biting lips, with his mace upraised by his two hands, like Yama with his mace at the universal dissolution.

sn: प्रजासंक्षेपसमये दण्डहस्तमिवान्तकम्। तं दृष्ट्वाधर्मराजस्तु परिष्वज्य पुनः पुनः॥
en: (Having him) Dharmaraja (Yudhishthira) again and again embraced him and thus spoke to him in these sweet words "O son of Kunti, what have you done?

sn: उवाच श्लक्ष्णया वाचा कौन्तेय किमिदं कृतम्। साहसं बत भद्रं ते देवानामथ चाप्रियम्॥
en: Be blessed; if you wish to do good to me, you should never again commit such rash acts, nor offend the celestials."

sn: पुनरेवं न कर्तव्यं मम चेदिच्छसि प्रियम्। अनुशिष्य तु कौन्तेयं पद्मानि परिगृह्य च॥
en: Having thus addressed that son of Kunti (Bhiima) and taken those flowers, those celestials-like heroes sported in that lake.

sn: तस्यामेव नलिन्यां तु विजह्वरमरोपमाः। एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु प्रगृहीतशिलायुधाः॥
en: seen (When they were thus sporting) the hugebodied guards of that garden, armed with rocks as their weapons came to that place.

sn: प्रादुरासन् महाकायास्तस्योद्यानस्य रक्षिणः। ते दृष्ट्वाधर्मराजानं महर्षि चापि लोमशम्॥ विनयेन नताः सर्वे प्रणिपत्य च भारत॥ सान्त्विताधर्मराजेन प्रसेदुः क्षणदाचराः। विदिताश्च कुबेरस्य तत्र ते कुरुपुङ्गवाः॥
en: Seeing Dharmaraja (Yudhishthira) and the great Rishi Lomasha and Nakula and Sahadeva and also the other foremost of Brahmanas, They all, O descendent of Bharata, bowed down their heads to them in humility. Being pacified by Dharmaraja (Yudhishthira) the Rakshasas were gratified.

sn: ऊषु तिचिरं कालं रममाणाः कुरूद्वहाः। प्रतीक्षमाणा बीभत्सुं गन्धमादनसानुषु॥
en: With the permission of Kubera, those foremost of the Kurus pleasantly lived for sometime, at that spot on the slopes of the Gandhamadana (mountain) awaiting for Vivatsa (Arjuna). were

description: Arrival at the Nara Narayana hermitage
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तस्मिन् निवसमानोऽथधर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः। कृष्णया सहितान् भ्रातृनित्युवाच सहद्विजान्॥
en: Vaishampayana Said When they all living there, Yudhishthira thus spoke to Krishna (Draupadi), his brothers and the Brahmanas.

description: Arrival at the Nara Narayana hermitage
sn: दृष्टानि तीर्थान्यस्माभिः पुण्यानि च शिवानि च। मनसो ह्लादनीयानि वनानि च पृथक् पृथक्॥
en: "We have alternately soon one after another many sacred and auspicious Tirthas and wood all delightful to look at.

description: Arrival at the Nara Narayana hermitage
sn: देवैः पूर्वं विचीर्णानि मुनिभिश्च महात्मभिः। यथाक्रमविशेषेण द्विजैः सम्पूजितानि च॥
en: They had been before visited by the celestials and the high-souled Rishis. They had been worshipped by the Brahmanas.

description: Arrival at the Nara Narayana hermitage
sn: ऋषीणां पूर्वचरितं तथा कर्म विचेष्टितम्। राजर्षीणां च चरितं कथाश्च विविधाः शुभाः॥ शृण्वानास्तत्र तत्र स्म आश्रमेषु शिवेषु च। अभिषेकं द्विजैः सार्धं कृतवन्तो विशेषतः॥
en: We have in various sacred hermitages performed ablutions with the Brahmanas; we have also heard from them the accounts of the) lives and acts of many Rishis and also of many royal sages of yore and also other pleasant stories.

description: Arrival at the Nara Narayana hermitage
sn: अर्चिताः सततं देवाः पुष्पैरद्भिः सदा च वः। यथालब्धैर्मूलफलैः पितरचापि तर्पिताः॥
en: We have worshipped the celestials with flowers and water, we have offered oblations to the Pitris with fruits and roots as were available there.

description: Arrival at the Nara Narayana hermitage
sn: पर्वतेषु च रम्येषु सर्वेषु च सरस्सु च। उदधौ च महापुण्ये सूपस्पृष्टं महात्मभिः॥
en: We have with the high-souled Rishis performed our ablutions in all the sacred and beautiful mountains and lakes and also in the highly holy sea.

description: Arrival at the Nara Narayana hermitage
sn: इला सरस्वती सिन्धुर्यमुना नर्मदा तथा। नानातीर्थेषु रम्येषु सूपस्पृष्टं सह द्विजैः॥
en: We have with the Brahmanas bathed in the Ila, in the Sarasvati, in the Sindhu, in the Yamuna, in the Narmada and in various other charming Tirthas.

description: Arrival at the Nara Narayana hermitage
sn: गङ्गाद्वारमतिक्रम्य बहवः पर्वताः शुभाः। हिमवान् पर्वतश्चैव नानाद्विजगणायुतः॥
en: Having passed the source of the Ganges, we have seen many charming mountains and also the Himalayas, inhabited by various kinds of birds;

description: Arrival at the Nara Narayana hermitage
sn: विशाला बदरी दृष्टा नरनारायणाश्रमः। दिव्या पुष्करिणी दृष्टा सिद्धदेवर्षिपूजिता॥
en: And also the great Badari, where there is the herinitage of Nara and Narayana. We have seen the celestials lake adored by the Siddhas and he celestials Rishis.

description: Arrival at the Nara Narayana hermitage
sn: यथाक्रमविशेषेण सर्वाण्यायतनानि च। दर्शितानि द्विजश्रेष्ठा लोमशेन महात्मना॥
en: O foremost of Brahmanas, we have one after the other seen all the celebrated and sacred places with the high souled Lomasha.

description: Arrival at the Nara Narayana hermitage
sn: इमं वैश्रवणावासं पुण्यं सिद्धनिषेवितम्। कथं भीम गमिष्यामो गतिरन्तरधीयताम्।१२।।
en: O Bhima, now we shall go to the yonder abode of Vaisravana (Kubera) frequented by the Siddhas. Think of the means of entering it."

description: Arrival at the Nara Narayana hermitage
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवं ब्रुवति राजेन्द्रे वागुवाचाशरीरिणी। न शक्यो दुर्गमो गन्तुमितो वैश्रवणाश्रमात्॥
en: When that king of kings had said this, an invisible voice spoke thus, “You will not be able to go to the inaccessible abode of Vaisravana.

description: Arrival at the Nara Narayana hermitage
sn: अनेनैव पथा राजन् प्रतिगच्छ यथागतम्। नरनारायणस्थानं बदरीत्यभिविश्रुतम्॥
en: By this way, O king, go back from this place to the place whence you have come, to the hermitage of Nara Narayana which is called Badari.

description: Arrival at the Nara Narayana hermitage
sn: तस्माद् यास्यसि कौन्तेय सिद्धचारणसेवितम्। बहुपुष्पफलं रम्यमाश्रमं वृषपर्वणः॥
en: O son of Kunti, from that place you will go to the hermitage of Vrishaparva abounding in flowers and fruits and frequented by the Siddhas and the Charanas,

description: Arrival at the Nara Narayana hermitage
sn: अतिक्रम्य च तं पार्थ त्वाष्टिषेणाश्रमे वसेः। ततो द्रक्ष्यसि कौन्तेय निवेशंधनदस्य च॥
en: O son of Pritha, having passed it, you will go to the hermitage of Arshnisena and O son of Kunti, from that place you will see the abode of Kubera."

description: Arrival at the Nara Narayana hermitage
sn: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे वायुर्दिव्यगन्धवहः शुचिः। सुखप्रह्लादनः शीत: पुष्पवर्षं ववर्ष च॥
en: Just as that moment the breeze became fresh, charming, cool and full of celestials fragrance and it showered flowers.

description: Arrival at the Nara Narayana hermitage
sn: श्रुत्वा तु दिव्यामाकाशाद् वाचं सर्वे विसिस्मियुः। ऋषीणां ब्राह्मणानां च पार्थिवानां विशेषतः॥
en: On hearing the celestials voice in the sky they were all surprised, more specially the Rishis and Brahmanas (who were with the Pandavas).

description: Arrival at the Nara Narayana hermitage
sn: श्रुत्वा तन्महदाश्चर्यं द्विजोधौम्योऽब्रवीत् तदा। न शक्यमुत्तरं वक्तुमेवं भवतु भारत॥
en: On hearing this great wonder, the Brahmana Dhaumya said, "O descendant of Bharata, this should not be gain said. Let this be so."

description: Arrival at the Nara Narayana hermitage
sn: ततो युधिष्ठिरो राजा प्रतिजग्राह तद् वचः। प्रत्यागम्य पुनस्तं तु नरनारायणाश्रमम्॥
en: Thereupon the king Yudhishthira accepted his words. Having returned to the hermitage of Nara and Narayana,

description: Arrival at the Nara Narayana hermitage
sn: भीमसेनादिभिः सर्वैर्धातृभिः परिवारितः। पाञ्चाल्या ब्राह्मणाश्चैव न्यवसन्त सुखं तदा॥
en: He happily lived there surrounded by Bhimasena and his other brothers and also by the Panchala princess and the Brahmanas.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततस्तान् परिविश्वस्तान् वसतस्तत्र पाण्डवान्। पर्वतेन्द्रे द्विजैः सार्धं पार्थागमनकाझ्या॥
en: Vaishampayana said : When the Pandavas had grown confident of living on that king of mountains, with the Brahmanas in expectation of the return of Partha (Arjuna).

sn: गतेषु तेषु रक्षःसु भीमसेनात्मजेऽपि च। रहितान् भीमसेनेन कदाचित् तान् यदृच्छया।॥
en: And when those Rakshasas had all gone away as well as the son of Bhimasena (Ghatotkacha) and when Bhima had gone away to rove (on the mountain) at pleasure,

sn: जहारधर्मराजानं यमौ कृष्णां च राक्षसः। ब्राह्मणो मन्त्रकुशलः सर्वशास्त्रविदुत्तमः॥
en: A certain Rakshasa carried away Dharmaraja (Yudhishthira), the twins and also Krishna (Draupadi).

sn: इति ब्रुवन् पाण्डवेयान् पर्युपास्ते स्म नित्यदा। परीप्समानः पार्थानां कलापानिधनूंषि च॥ अन्तर सम्परिप्रेप्सुयॊपद्या हरणं प्रति। दुष्टात्मा पापबुद्धिः स नाम्ना ख्यातो जटासुरः॥
en: Alleging that he was a Brahmana wellskilled in counsel and learned in all the Shastras, he always lived with the Pandavas with the intention of possessing their bows, quivers and other weapons. He had been watching an opportunity to steal away Draupadi. That wicked and sinful wretch was known by the name of Jatasura.

sn: पोषणं तस्य राजेन्द्र चक्रे पाण्डवनन्दनः। बुबुधे न च तं पापं भस्मच्छन्नमिवानलम्॥
en: O king of kings, the son of Pandu (Yudhishthira) was supporting him; he could not recognise that wretch who was like the fire covered with ashes.

sn: स भीमसेने निष्क्रान्ते मृगयार्थमरिन्दम। घटोत्कचं सानुचरं दृष्ट्वा विप्रद्रुतं दिशः॥
en: When that chastiser of foes, Bhimasena, went out hunting and when he (Jatasura) saw that Ghatotkacha and his followers were scattered in all directions,

sn: लोमशप्रभृतींस्तांस्तु महर्षीच समाहितान्। स्नातुं विनिर्गतान् दृष्ट्वा पुष्पार्थं च तपोधनान्॥
en: And when he saw that the self-controlled great Rishis and ascetics, Lomasha and others, had gone to bathe or to collect flowers,

sn: रूपमन्यत् समास्थाय विकृतं भैरवं महत्। गृहीत्वा सर्वशस्त्राणि द्रौपदी परिगृह्य च॥
en: He (Jatasura) assumed a different form, monstrous, fearful and huge. Having secured all the weapons and taken up Draupadi,

sn: प्रातिष्ठत स दुष्टात्मा त्रीन् गृहीत्वा च पाण्डवान्। सहदेवस्तु यत्नेन ततोऽपक्रम्य पाण्डवः॥
en: And also having taken the Pandavas that wicked-minded wretch fled away. The Pandava Sahadeva extricated himself (from the grasp of the Rakshasa) with great efforts.

sn: विक्रम्य कौशिकं खङ्गं मोक्षयित्वा ग्रहं रिपोः। आक्रन्दद् भीमसेनं वै येन यातो महाबलः॥
en: He snatched by force the sword named Kaushika from the hand of the enemy and loudly calling Bhimasena went in the direction that mighty Rakshasa had gone.

sn: तमब्रवीद्धर्मराजो ह्रियमाणो युधिष्ठिरः। धर्मस्ते हीयते मूढ न तत्त्वं समवेक्षसे॥
en: Having been thus stolen (by the Rakshasa), Dharmaraja Yudhishthira thus spoke to him, "O fool virtue decreases in you; you do not look to it.

sn: येऽन्ये क्वचिन्मनुष्येषु तिर्यग्योनिगताश्च ये। धर्मं ते समवेक्षन्ते रक्षांसि च विशेषतः॥
en: Whether belonging to the human race or to the lower order of creatures, all pay regard to virtue, more specially the Rakshasa.

sn: धर्मस्य राक्षसा मूलंधर्मं ते विदुरुत्तमम्। एतत् परीक्ष्य सर्वं त्वं समीपे स्थातुमर्हसि॥
en: Rakshasas are the root of all virtues. In the beginning they knew virtue better than others. Having considered all this, you should have adhered to virtue.

sn: देवाश्च ऋषयः सिद्धाः पितरश्चापि राक्षस। गन्धर्वोरगरक्षांसि वयांसि पशवस्तथा॥ तिर्यग्योनिगताचैव अपि कीटपिपीलिकाः। मनुष्यानुपजीवन्ति ततस्त्वमपि जीवसि॥
en: O Rakshasa, the celestials, the Pitris, the Siddhas, the Rishis, the Gandharvas, the animals, even worms and ants, depend on men for their lives; you too also live (depending on men).

sn: समृद्ध्या ह्यस्य लोकस्य लोको युष्माकमध्यति। इमं च लोकं शोचन्तमनुशोचन्ति देवताः॥
en: If prosperity attends the human race, your (Rakshasa) race will also be prosperous. If calamity falls on men, even the celestials thereby suffer grief.

sn: पूज्यमानाश्च वर्धन्ते हव्यकव्यैर्यथाविधि। वयं राष्ट्रस्य गोप्तारो रक्षितारश्च राक्षस॥
en: Being gratified by offerings (offered by men) the celestials prosper. O Rakshasa, we are the guardians, governors and protectors of kingdoms.

sn: राष्ट्रस्यारक्ष्यमाणस्य कुतो भूतिः कुतः सुखम्। न च राजावमन्तव्यो राक्षसा जात्वनागसि॥
en: If kingdoms become unprotected, how can prosperity and happiness be produced? unless an offence is given, no Rakshasa should commit any oppression on a king.

sn: अणुरप्यपचारश्च नास्त्यस्माकं नराशन। विघसाशान् यथाशक्त्या कुर्महे देवतादिषु॥
en: O cannibal, we have never committed the least wrong. Living on Vegasha we serve the celestials and other to the best of our power.

sn: गुरूंश्च ब्राह्मणांश्चैव प्रणामप्रवणा: सदा। द्रोग्धव्यं न च मित्रेषु न विश्वस्तेषु कर्हिचित्॥ येषां चान्नानि भुञ्जीत यत्र च स्यात् प्रतिश्रयः। स त्वं प्रतिश्रयेऽस्माकं पूज्यमानः सुखोषितः॥
en: We are ever intent on bowing down to our superiors and the Brahmanas. A friend, a confiding man, he whose food has been partaken and he who has given shelter should never be injured; you have happily lived in our place and you were duly honoured by us.

sn: भुक्त्वा चान्नानि दुष्प्रज्ञ कथमस्मान् जिहीर्षसि। एवमेव वृथाचारो वृथावृद्धो वृथामतिः॥
en: O wicked wretch, having partaken of our food how can you steal us away? As your acts are improper, as you have in vain become old and as your propensities are bad,

sn: वृथामरणमर्हश्च वृथाद्य न भविष्यसि। अथ चेद् दुष्टबुद्धिस्त्वं सर्वैर्धर्विवर्जितः॥
en: So do you deserve to die for nothing; and for nothing will your (surely) die today. If you are really evil-disposed and devoid of all virtue,

sn: प्रदाय शस्त्राण्यस्माकं युद्धेन द्रौपदी हर। अथ चेत् त्वमविज्ञानादिदं कर्म करिष्यसि॥ अधर्मं चाप्यकीर्ति च लोके प्राप्स्यसि केवलम्। एतामद्य परामृश्य स्त्रियं राक्षस मानुषीम्॥ विषमेतत् समालोड्य कुम्भेन प्राशितं त्वया। ततो युधिष्ठिरस्तस्य गुरुकः समपद्यत॥
en: Give us back our weapons, carry away Draupadi after a fight. But if through your folly you must do this, then you will get only demerit and infamy in the world. O Rakshasa, by doing violence to this lady of the human race, you have as if drunk poison after having shaken the vessel.” Thereupon Yudhishthira grew heavy to the Rakshasa.

sn: स तु भाराभिभूतात्मा न तथा शीघ्रगोऽभवत्। अथाब्रवीद् द्रौपदी च नकुलं च युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Being thus oppressed with the weight, he (the Rakshasa) could not go fast as before. Then Yudhishthira thus spoke to Draupadi and Nakula.

sn: मा भैष्ट राक्षसान्मूढाद् गतिरस्य मया हृता। नातिदूरे महाबाहुर्भविता पवनात्मजः॥
en: "Don't be afraid of this wicked Rakshasa; I have checked his speed. The mighty-armed son of Vayu (Bhima) is not far away.

sn: अस्मिन् मुहूर्ते सम्प्राप्ते न भविष्यति राक्षसः। सहदेवस्तु तं दृष्ट्वा राक्षसं मूढचेतनम्॥
en: On Bhima coming up at the next moment, the Rakshasa will not live." Seeing the Rakshasa deprived of all (good) sense, Sahadeva,

sn: उवाच वचनं राजन् कुन्तीपुत्रं युधिष्ठिरम्। राजन् किंनाम सत्कृत्यं क्षत्रियस्यास्त्यतोऽधिकम्॥
en: O king, spoke thus to the son of Kunti, Yudhishthira, "What can be more meritorious for a Kshatriya.

sn: यद् युद्धेऽभिमुखः प्राणांस्त्यजेच्छठे जयेत वा। एष चास्मान् वयं चैनं युद्ध्यमानाः परंतप॥
en: Than to fall in the field of battle or to defeat a foe. O chastiser of foes, we shall fight; and either he will kill us or we will kill him.

sn: सूदयेम महाबाहो देशकालो ह्ययं नृप। क्षत्रधर्मस्य सम्प्राप्तः कालः सत्यपराक्रमः॥
en: O mighty-armed king, O hero of great prowess, this is the (proper) time and place which has come to display our Kshatriya prowess.

sn: जयन्तो हन्यमाना वा प्राप्तुमर्हाम सद्गतिम्। राक्षसे जीवमानेऽद्य रविरस्तमियाद् यदि॥
en: We should gain the blessed state, either by defeating the foe or by being killed by him. If the sun sets today and the Rakshasa remains alive.

sn: नाहं ब्रूयां पुनर्जातु क्षत्रियोऽस्मीति भारत। भो भो राक्षस तिष्ठस्व सहदेवोऽस्मि पाण्डवः॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, I will not then any more say that I am a Kshatriya. Ho, Ho, Rakshasa, stay, I am the son of Pandu, Sahadeva.

sn: हत्वा वा मां नयस्वैनां हतो वाद्येह स्वप्स्यसि। तदा ब्रुवति माद्रेये भीमसेनो यदृच्छया।॥
en: Either after having killed me today, carry this lady away or being killed by me, lie senseless here. When the son of Madri (Sahadeva) was thus speaking, Bhimasena, roaring at pleasure,

sn: प्रत्यदृश्यद् गदाहस्तः सवज्र इव वासवः। सोऽपश्यद् भ्रातरौ तत्र द्रौपदी च यशस्विनीम्॥
en: Came there with the mace in his hand like a secord Vasava (Indra) wielding the thunderbolt. He saw there his brothers and the illustrious Draupadi.

sn: क्षितिस्थं सहदेवं च क्षिपन्तं राक्षसं तदा। मार्गाच्च राक्षसं मूढं कालोपहतचेतसम्॥
en: And also Sahadeva who was rebuking the Rakshasa and also that foolish Rakshasa who, being deprived of his (good) sense by Fate,

sn: भ्रमन्तं तत्र तत्रैव देवेन विनिवारितम्। भ्रातृस्तान् ह्रियतो दृष्ट्वा द्रौपदी च महाबलः॥
en: Was going round in different directions through bewilderment caused by Destiny. Seeing his brothers and Draupadi thus being carried off, the greatly powerful (Bhima).

sn: क्रोधमाहारयद् भीमो राक्षसं चेदमब्रवीत्। विज्ञातोऽसि मया पूर्वं पाप शस्त्रपरीक्षणे॥
en: Was inflamed with anger and he thus spoke to the Rakshasa, "O sinful wretch, I found you out long ago by (observing) your scrutiny of our weapons.

sn: आस्था तु त्वयि मे नास्ति यतोऽसि न हतस्तदा। ब्रह्मरूपप्रतिच्छन्नो न नो वदसि चाप्रियम्॥
en: But as I had no apprehension from you, I did not kill you. You are in the disguise of a Brahmana and you did not speak towards us any harsh words.

sn: प्रियेषु रममाणं त्वां न चैवाप्रियकारिणम्। अतिथिं ब्रह्मरूपं च कथं हन्यामनागसम्॥
en: You took delight in pleasing us, you did not do us any harm and again you were our guest, how could I therefore kill you who were in the garb of a Brahmana and who were innocent?

sn: राक्षसं जानमानोऽपि यो हन्यानरकं व्रजेत्। अपक्वस्य च कालेन वधस्तव न विद्यते॥
