en: He who kills such a one even knowing him to be a Rakshasa goes to hell. Besides you cannot be killed before the (fixed) time (for your death) comes.

sn: नूनमद्यासि सम्पक्वो यथा ते मतिरीदृशी। दत्ता कृष्णापहरणे कालेनाद्भुतकर्मणा॥
en: Today that time has surely come, in as much as your mind has been led away by the wonder-performing fate to carry off Krishna (Draupadi).

sn: बडिशोऽयं त्वया ग्रस्तः कालसूत्रेण लम्बितः। मत्स्योऽम्भसीव स्यूतास्यः कथमद्यभविष्यसि॥
en: (By thus allowing you to commit this act), you have swallowed the hook fastened to the line of Fate. Like the fish (hooked) you will meet with your destruction today.

sn: यं चासि प्रस्थितो देशं मनः पूर्वं गतं च ते। न तं गन्तासि गन्तासि मार्ग बकहिडिम्बयोः। :॥
en: You shall not have to go where you intend to go or where you have already mentally gone. You shall go (today) to the place where Hidimba and Baka have gone.”

sn: एवमुक्तस्तु भीमेन राक्षसः कालचोदितः। भीत उत्सृज्य तान् सर्वान् युद्धाय समुपस्थितः॥
en: Having been thus addressed by Bhima, the Rakshasa became alarmed. He put them down and being forced by Fate came to fright.

sn: अब्रवीच्च पुनर्भीमं रोषात् प्रस्फुरिताधरः। न मे मूढा दिशः पाप त्वदर्थं मे विलम्बितम्॥
en: With his lips trembling in anger, he thus spoke to Bhima,“ sinful wretch, I am not bewildered; I am waiting for you.

sn: श्रुता मे राक्षसा ये ये त्वया विनिहता रणे। तेषामद्य करिष्यामि तवास्रेणोदकक्रियाम्॥
en: I have heard about those Rakshasas whom you have killed in battle. I will today offer oblations of your blood to them."

sn: एवमुक्तस्ततो भीमः सृक्किणी परिसंलिहन्। स्मयमान इव क्रोधात् साक्षात् कालान्तकोपमः।॥ बाहुसंरम्भमेवैक्षन्नभिदुद्राव राक्षसम्। राक्षसोऽपि तदा भीमं युद्धार्थिनमवस्थितम्॥ मुहुर्मुहुाददानः सृक्किणी परिसंलिहन्। अभिदुद्राव संरब्धो बलिर्वज्रधरं यथा॥
en: Having been thus addressed, Bhima, as if bursting with rage, like Yama himself at the time of universal dissolution, rushed towards the Rakshasa, licking the corners of his mouth and staring at him as he struck his own arms with his hands. Seeing Bhima waiting in expectation of fight, the Rakshasa rushed towards him in anger like Bali towards the wielder of thunder (Indra), gaping again and again and licking the corners of his mouth.

sn: वर्तमाने तदा ताभ्यां बाहुयुद्धे सुदारुणे। माद्रीपुत्रावतिक्रुद्धावुभावप्यभ्यधावताम्॥
en: When they were fighting a fearful wrestling match, the sons of Madri (Nakula and Sahadeva), becoming exceedingly angry, rushed forward.

sn: न्यवारयत् तौ प्रहसन् कुन्तीपुत्रो वृकोदरः। शक्तोऽहं राक्षसस्येति प्रेक्षध्वमिति चाब्रवीत्॥
en: The son of Kunti, Vrikodara (Bhima), smiled and asked them to stop. He spoke to them, “Behold, I am more than a match for this (Rakshasa).

sn: आत्मना भ्रातृभिश्चैवधर्मेण सुकृतेन च। इष्टेन च शपे राजन् सूदयिष्यामि राक्षसम्॥
en: O king, by my own self, by my brothers, by my merit, by my good deeds and by my sacrifices, I swear that I shall kill this Rakshasa."

sn: इत्येवमुक्त्वा तौ वीरौ स्पर्धमानौ परस्परम्। बाहुभ्यां समसज्जेतामुभौ रक्षोवृकोदरौ॥
en: Having said this, those two heroes, the Rakshasa and Vrikodara, challenged each other and caught each other by the arms.

sn: तयोरासीत् सम्प्रहारः क्रुद्धयोर्भीमरक्षसोः। अमृष्यमाणयोः सङ्घये देवदानवयोरिव॥
en: They did not forgive each other; the angry Bhima and the Rakshasa fought a terrible battle like that between a celestials and a demon.

sn: आरुज्यारुज्य तौ वृक्ष्यानन्योन्यमभिजघ्नतुः। जीमूताविव गर्जन्तौ निनदन्तौ महाबलौ॥
en: Uprooting the trees, those two greatly strong heroes again and again struck each other, roaring and shouting like masses of clouds.

sn: बभञ्जतुर्महावृक्षानूरुभिर्बलिनां वरौ। अन्योन्येनाभिसंरब्धौ परस्परवधैषिणौ॥
en: Those two foremost of strong men, each wishing to kill the other and each rushing at the other with great force, broke down many gigantic trees by (the press of) their thighs.

sn: तद् वृक्षयुद्धमभवन्महीरुहविनाशनम्। वालिसुग्रीवयोर्धात्रोः पुरा स्त्रीकाक्षिणोर्यथा॥
en: Thus went on that battle with trees, destructive of plants like that between the two brothers Bali and Sugriva, both desirous of possessing the woman.

sn: आविध्याविध्य तौ वृक्षान् मुहूर्तमितरेतरम्। ताडयामासतुरुभौ विनदन्तौ मुहुर्मुहुः॥ तस्मिन् देशे यदा वृक्षाः सर्व एव निपातिताः। पुञ्जीकृताश्च शतशः परस्परवधेप्सया॥
en: Brandishing trees, they struck each other continually shouting. And when all the trees of that spot were pulled down and crushed into hundred parts by their attempt to kill each other,

sn: तत: शिलाः समादाय मुहूर्तमिव भारत। महाभैरिव शैलेन्द्रौ युयुधाते महाबलौ॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, they instantly took up rocks; and those two greatly strong heroes fought like a mountain and a great mass of clouds.

sn: शिलाभिरुग्ररूपाभिवृहतीभिः परस्परम्। वचैरिव महावेगैराजघ्नतुरमर्षणौ॥
en: Not allowing a moment's rest to each other, they struck each other with hard and (large pieces of) rocks each resembling a thunderbolt.

sn: अभिद्रुत्य च भूयस्तावन्योन्यं बलदर्पितौ। भुजाभ्यां परिगृह्याथ चकर्षाते गजाविव॥
en: Defying each other from their great strength, they again rushed at each other and grasping each other by their arms they wrestled like two elephants.

sn: मुष्टिभिश्च महाघोरैरन्योन्यमभिजघ्नतुः। ततः कटकटाशब्दो बभूव सुमहात्मनोः॥
en: They administered each other terrible blows; and those two greatly powerful heroes made chattering sounds by knashing their teeth.

sn: ततः संहृत्य मुष्टिं तु पञ्चशीर्षमिवोरगम्। वेगेनाभ्यहनद् भीमो राक्षसस्य शिरोधराम्॥
en: At last Bhima, clenching his fist like a five headed snake, dealt with great force a blow on the neck of the Rakshasa.

sn: ततः श्रान्तं तु तद् रक्षो भीमसेनभुजाहतम्। सुपरिश्रान्तमालक्ष्य भीमसेनोऽभ्यवर्तत॥
en: Thereupon, struck by the fist of Bhima the Rakshasa fainted away and Bhima seeing this, too, holding that exhausted one.

sn: तत एनं महाबाहुर्बाहुभ्याममरोपमः। समुत्क्षिप्य बलाद् भीमो विनिष्पिष्य महीतले॥
en: Then the celestials-like and mighty-armed Bhima lifted him up with his two arms; and dashing him with force on the ground.

sn: तस्य गात्राणि सर्वाणि चूर्णयामास पाण्डवः। अरनिना चाभिहत्य शिरः कायादपाहरत्॥ संदष्टौष्ठं विवृत्ताक्षं फलं वृक्षादिव च्युतम्। जटासुरस्य तु शिरो भीमसेनबलाद्धतम्॥
en: That son of Pandu pounded (into atoms) all his limbs; and striking him with his elbow, he severed from his body the head with bitten lips and rolling eyes like a fruit from its stem. The head of Jatasura, being severed by the strength of Bhimasena.

sn: पपात रुधिरादिग्धं संदष्टदशनच्छदम्। तं निहत्य महेष्वासो युधिष्ठिरमुपागमत्। स्तूयमानो द्विजावयैस्तु मरुद्भिरिव वासवः॥
en: Fell besmeared with blood and with bitten lips. Having killed him, that great warrior came to Yudhishthira; and the foremost of Brahmanas (all) began to praise him as Marutas do Vasava (Indra).

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच निहते राक्षसे तस्मिन् पुनर्नारायणाश्रमम्। अभ्येत्य राजा कौन्तेयो निवासमकरोत् प्रभुः॥
en: Vaishampayana said: That Rakshasa being killed, the lord king Yudhishthira, the royal son of Kunti, returning to the hermitage of Narayana, began to dwell there.

sn: स समानीय तान् सर्वान् भ्रातृनित्यब्रवीद् वचः। द्रौपद्या सहितान् काले संस्मरन् भ्रातरं जयम्॥
en: He, (Yudhishthira) once upon a time, (during his stay in the hermitage) remembering Jaya (Arjuna) and summoning all his brothers together with Draupadi 1O his presence, addressed them thus:

sn: समाश्चतस्रोऽभिगताः शिवेन चरतां वने। कृतोद्देशः स बीभत्सु पञ्चमीमभितः समाम्॥
en: We have peacefully ranged in the forests these four years. It was arranged by Vivatsu that in the fifth year,

sn: प्राप्य पर्वतराजानं श्वेतं शिखरिणां वरम्। पुष्पितैर्दुमषण्डैश्च मत्तकोकिलषट्पदैः॥
en: He would get to that prince of mountains Shveta (Kailasha), the best of all peaks, enlivened with continuous festivities, celebrated by blossoming floral plants, Kokilas and black bees brimful of joy,

sn: मयूरैश्चातकैश्चापि नित्योत्सवविभूषितम्। व्याप्रैर्वराहैर्महिषैर्गवयैर्हरिणैस्तथा॥
en: And by peacocks and Chatakas, inhabited by tigers, boars, buffaloes, Gabayas and deer,

sn: श्वापदैर्व्यालरूपैश्च रुरुभिश्च निषेवितम्। फुल्लैः सहस्रपत्रैश्च शतपत्रैस्तथोत्पलैः॥
en: And by all sorts of ferocious animals and Rurus; decked with full-blown lotuses of a thousand and hundred petals,

sn: प्रफुल्लैः कमलैश्चैव तथा नीलोत्पलैरपि। महापुण्यं पवित्रं च सुरासुरनिषेवितम्॥
en: And (bright) with blooming lilies and blue lilies; sacred, pure and frequented by the Suras (gods) and the Asuras (demons).

sn: तत्रापि च कृतोद्देशः समागमदिदृक्षुभिः। कृतश्च समयस्तेन पार्थेनामिततेजसा॥
en: And we too, with an ardent desire to meet him, had engaged to repair thither. It had been appointed by Partha of matchless prowess,

sn: पञ्चवर्षाणि वत्स्यामि विद्यार्थीति पुरा मयि। अत्र गाण्डीवधन्वानमवाप्तास्त्रमरिन्दमम्॥ देवलोकादिमं लोकं द्रक्ष्यामः पुनरागतम्। इत्युक्त्वा ब्राह्मणान् सर्वानामन्त्रयत पाण्डवः॥
en: That he should remain in the region of the gods for five years in order to learn all the tactics of warfare. We shall behold in that place (in the mountain Shveta) the wielder of the Gandiva, the terror of his foes returning to our world from the abode of the gods (enriched) with weapons (obtained from them). The Pandava Yudhishthira, having expressed himself thus, greeted the assembled Brahmanas.

sn: कारणं चैव तत् तेषामाचचक्षे तपस्विनाम्। तानुग्रतपसः प्रीतान् कृत्वा पार्थाः प्रदक्षिणाम्॥
en: And having gone round and thereby pleased the sages of fervid devotion he related to them the matter mentioned above.

sn: ब्राह्मणास्तेऽन्वमोदन्त शिवेन कुशलेन च। सुखोदकमिमं क्लेशमचिराद् भरतर्षभ।॥
en: The Brahmanas then approved of the proposal in terms bespeaking happiness and prosperity, saying, "O the most exalted of all the Bharatas, these troubles shall soon end in prosperity.

sn: क्षत्रधर्मेणधर्मज्ञ तीर्खा गां पालयिष्यसि। तत् तु राजा वचस्तेषां प्रतिगृह्य तपस्विनाम्॥
en: O virtuous one, getting over all these difficulties you will govern the earth by the code of laws practised by the Kshatriyas.” Then the Raja Yudhishthira, having bowed to these words of the ascetics,

sn: प्रतस्थे सह विप्रैस्तैर्धातृभिश्च परन्तपः। राक्षसैरनुयातो वै लोमशेनाभिरक्षितः॥
en: Set out with his brothers and those Brahmanas (for the Shveta) followed by the Rakshasas and protected by Lomasha.

sn: क्वचित् पद्भ्यां ततोऽगच्छद् राक्षसैरुह्यते क्वचित्। तत्र तत्र महातेजा भ्रातृभिः सह सुव्रतः॥
en: And that one (Yudhishthira) of unrivalled energy and pious vows at some places walked on foot with his brothers and at others was carried by the Rakshasa.

sn: ततो युधिष्ठिरो राजा बहून् क्लेशान् विचिन्तयन्। सिंहव्याघ्रगजाकीर्णामुदीची प्रययौ दिशम्॥
en: Then King Yudhishthira, apprehending a good many troubles, proceeded towards the north teeming with lions, tigers and elephants.

sn: अवेक्षमाणः कैलासं मैनाकं चैव पर्वतम्। गन्धमादनपादांश्च श्वेतं चापि शिलोच्चयम्॥
en: Beholding the mountain Kailasha and Mainaka, the base of the mountain Gandhamadana and the rocky chiff Shveta,

sn: उपर्युपरि शैलस्य बह्वीश्च सरितः शिवाः। पृष्ठं हिमवतः पुण्यं ययौ सप्तदशेऽहनि॥
en: And many a sacred stream one above the other issuing from the mountain, he ascended the sacred plateau of the Himalayas on the seventeenth day.

sn: ददृशुः पाण्डवा राजन् गन्धमादनमन्तिकात्। पृष्ठे हिमवतः पुण्ये नानाद्रुमलतावृते॥ सलिलावर्तसंजातैः पुष्पितैश्च महीरुहैः। समावृतं पुण्यतममाश्रमं वृषपर्वणः॥
en: Then, O king in the neighbourhood of the mountain Gandhamadana and on the sacred plateau of the Himalayas, decked with various sort of trees and creepers, the Pandavas beheld the most sacred hermitage of Vrishaparva encircled by blossoming trees growing near the water courses.

sn: तमुपागम्य राजर्षिधर्मात्मानमरिन्दमाः। पाण्डवा वृषपर्वाणमवन्दन्त गतक्लमाः॥
en: The Pandavas, the tormentors of foes, on recovering from fatigue, approached the royal sage Vrishaparva and saluted him.

sn: अभ्यनन्दत् स राजर्षिः पुत्रवद् भरतर्षभान्। पूजिताश्चावसंस्तत्र सप्तरात्रमरिन्दमाः॥
en: The royal sage too welcomed those most exalted of the Bharatas as if they were his own children. Thus received, the tormentors of foes remained there for seven nights.

sn: अष्टमेऽहनि सम्प्राप्ते तमृषि लोकविश्रुतम्। आमन्त्र्य वृषपर्वाणं प्रस्थानं प्रत्यरोचयन्॥
en: On the eighth day, greeting the royal sage of world wide renown, they expressed their desire to start on their journey.

sn: एकैकशश्च तान् विप्रान् निवेद्य वृषपर्वणि। न्यासभूतान् यथाकालं बन्धूनिव सुसत्कृतान्॥
en: And at the proper time having introduced to Vrishaparva the Brahmana, whom he only honoured and who had remained in his charge as friends,

sn: पारिबर्ह च तं शेषं परिदाय महात्मने। ततस्ते यज्ञपात्राणि रत्नान्याभरणानि च।॥ न्यदधुः पाण्डवा राजन्नाश्रमे वृषपर्वणः। अतीतानागते विद्वान् कुशलः सर्वधर्मवित्॥
en: And having also committed to his charge their remaining clothes, O king, the sons of Pandu left their sacred ornaments and sacrificial vessels in the hermitage of Vrishaparva. That (sage) well learned, versed in all religions, having a knowledge of the past and the future,

sn: अन्वशासत् सधर्मज्ञः पुत्रवद्भरतर्षभान्। तेऽनुज्ञाता महात्मानः प्रययुर्दिशमुत्तराम्॥
en: And pious gave instructions to the most exalted of the Bharatas as to his own sons. Thus instructed, the high-souled ones proceeded towards the north.

sn: तान् प्रस्थितानभ्यगच्छद् वृषपर्वा महीपतिः। उपन्यस्य महातेजा विप्रेभ्यः पाण्डवांस्तदा॥ अनुसंसार्य कौन्तेयानाशीर्भिरभिनन्द्य च। वृषपर्वा निववृते पन्थानमुपदिश्य च॥
en: The high-souled Vrishaparva accompanied them to a certain distance. And then committing those Pandavas of indomitable spirit of the care of the Brahma's and instructing and blessing those sons of Kunti, Vrishaparva retraced his steps after giving them directions as to the path they were to follow.

sn: नानामृगगणैर्जुष्टं कौन्तेयः सत्यविक्रमः। पदातिर्धातृभिः सार्धं प्रातिष्ठत युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Then Yudhishthira, the son of Kunti possessed of true prowess, began to proceed on foot along the mountain path inhabited by various kinds of beasts.

sn: नानाद्रुमनिरोधेषु वसन्तः शैलसानुषु। पर्वतं विविशुः श्वेतं चतुर्थेऽहनि पाण्डवाः॥
en: And at times having dwelt on the level grounds above the mountains thickly overgrown with many trees, the Pandavas on the fourth day got to the mountain Shveta.

sn: महाभ्रघनसंकाशं सलिलोपहितं शुभम्। मणिकाञ्चनरूप्यस्य शिलानां च समुच्चयम्॥
en: Looking like a mighty mass of clouds, abounding in sacred waters and consisting of a mass of gems, gold, silver and marble.

sn: ते समासाद्य पन्थानं यथोक्तं वृषपर्वणा। अनुससुर्यथोद्देशं पश्यन्तो विविधान्नगान्॥
en: Following the route directed by Vrishaparva they proceeded on their journey beholding various mountains on (their way).

sn: उपर्युपरिः शैलस्य गुहाः परमदुर्गमाः। सुदुर्गमांस्ते सुबहून् सुखेनैवाभिचक्रमुः॥
en: There were many inaccessible caves higher and higher up the mountains which also were equally inaccessible; but they passed them with pleasure all these difficulties notwithstanding.

sn: धौम्यः कृष्णा च पार्थाश्च लोमशश्च महानृषिः। अगच्छन् सहितास्तत्र न कश्चिदवहीयते॥
en: Dhaumya, Krishna, Parthas and the great sage Lomasha all walked together (none lagging behind) without experiencing any fatigue.

sn: ते मृगद्विजसंघुष्टं नानादुमलतायुतम्। शाखामृगगणैश्चैव सेवितं सुमनोरमम्॥ पुण्यं पद्मसरोयुक्तं सपल्वलमहावनम्। उपतस्थुर्महाभागा माल्यवन्तं महागिरिम्॥
en: Those highly fortunate ones then reached that sacred and highly beautiful and mighty mountain Malayavana, resounding with the voices of birds and beasts, abounding in many trees and creepers, inhabited by monkeys and containing lotus lakes, marshes and great forests.

sn: ततः किम्पुरुषावासं सिद्धचारणसेवितम्। ददृशुर्हष्टरोमाणः पर्वतं गन्धमादनम्॥
en: Then with their hair standing on the end, they beheld with great pleasure the mount Gandhamadana, the abode of the Kimpurušas, frequented by the Siddhas and the Charanas,

sn: विद्याधरानुचरितं किन्नरीभिस्तथैव च। गजसङ्घसमावासं सिंहव्याघ्रगणायुतम्॥
en: Visited by the Vidyadharas and the Kinnars, the abode of herds of elephants, full of lions and tigers,

sn: शरभोन्नादसंघुष्टं नानामृगनिषेवितम्। ते गन्धमादनवनं तन्नन्दनवनोपमम्॥ मुदिताः पाण्डुतनया मनोहृदयनन्दनम्। विविशुः क्रमशो वीराः शरण्यं शुभकाननम्॥ द्रौपदीसहिता वीरास्तैश्च विप्रैर्महात्मभिः। शृण्वन्तः प्रीतिजननान् वल्गून् मदकलाञ्छुभान्॥
en: Resounding with the roar of Saravas and inhabited by various other animals. Then with great delight, the heroic Pandavas gradually entered the forest of the Gandhamadana resembling the Nandana gardens, pleasant to the mind and heart, auspicious and capable of affording protection,

sn: श्रोत्ररम्यान् सुमधुराज्छब्दान् खगमुखरितान्। सर्वर्तुफलभाराढ्यान् सर्वर्तुकुसुमोज्ज्वलान्॥ पश्यन्तः पादपांश्चापि फलभारावनामितान्। आम्रनाम्रातकान् भव्यान् नारिकेलान् सतिन्दुकान्॥
en: And as those heroes together with Draupadi and the noble-minded Brahmanas entered the forest of the Gandhamadana they began to hear inarticulate notes causing delight, sweet, auspicious, pleasant to the ear, sweetly melodious and issuing out of the mouth of birds. And they beheld various trees bending down under the weight of fruits and radiant with flowers of all seasons-such as mango Amarataka, Bhabya, Coconut, Tinduka,

sn: मुञ्जातकांस्तथाञ्जीरान् दाडिमान् बीजपूरकान्। पनसॉल्लकुचान् मोचान् खजूरानम्लवेतसान्॥
en: Munjataka, Jiva, Pomegranate, Beejpuran, Panasha, Lakucha, plantains, Kharjara, Amlabatasha,

sn: पारावतांस्तथा क्षौद्रान् नीपांश्चापि मनोरमान्। बिल्वान् कपित्थाञ्जम्बूंश्च काश्मरीबंदरीस्तथा॥
en: Parvata, Champaka and lovely Kadamba, Vilva, Kapitha, Jamboos, Kansmari, Badari,

sn: प्लक्षानुदुम्बरबटानश्वत्थान् क्षीरिकांस्तथा। भल्लातकानामलकीहरीतकबिभीतकान्॥
en: Plaksha, Udumbaras, Vata, Asvattha, Khirika, Bhallataka, Amalaki, Haritaki, Bhibhitaki,

sn: इङ्गुदान् करमर्दाश्च तिन्दुकांश्च महाफलान्। एतानन्यांश्च विविधान् गन्धमादनसानुषु॥
en: Inguda, Karamarda, Tinduka and Mahaphalas, these any many other trees on the plateau of the Gandhamadana,

sn: फलैरमृतकल्पैस्तानाचितान् स्वादुभिस्तरून्। तथैव चम्पकाशोकान् केतकान् बकुलांस्तथा॥
en: Clustered with delicious fruits of ambrosial taste. And (besides these) they beheld Champakas, Ashokas, Aetakas, Aakulas,

sn: पुन्नागान् सप्तपर्णाश्च कर्णिकारान् सकेतकान्। पाटलान् कुटजान् रम्यान् मन्दारेन्दीवरांस्तथा॥
en: Punnagas, Saptaparnas, Karnikaras, Patalas, Kutajas and beautiful Mandaras and lotuses,

sn: पारिजातान् कोविदारान् देवदारुदुमांस्तथा। शालांस्तालास्तमालांच पिप्पलान् हिङ्गुकांस्तथा॥
en: Parijatas, Kovidaras, Devadarus, Salas, Talas, Tamala, Pippalas, Hingukas,

sn: शाल्मली: किंशुकाशोकाञ्छिशपाः सरलांस्तथा। चकोरैः शतपत्रैश्च भृङ्गराजैस्तथा शुकैः॥
en: Salmalis, Kinshukas, Ashokas, Singshapas and Saralas. And these trees were inhabited by Chakoras, Satapatras, Bhringarajas, Shukas,

sn: कोकिलैः कलविहेच हारितैर्जीवजीविकैः। प्रियकैश्चातकैश्चैव तथान्यैर्विविधै खगैः॥ ओत्ररम्यं सुमधुरं कूजद्भिश्चात्यधिष्ठितान्। सरांसि च मनोज्ञानि समन्ताज्जलचारिभिः॥
en: Kokilas, Kalabinkas, Haritas, Jibojibakas, Priakas, Chatakas and various other birds warbling forth sweet notes pleasant to the ear. And they beheld also lakes all around looking beautiful with water birds filled.

sn: कुमुदैः पुण्डरीकैश्च तथा कोकनदोत्पलैः। कलारैः कमलैश्चैव आचितानि समन्ततः॥
en: And interspersed with Kumudas, lotuses, Kakonadas and Utpalas, Kalharas and Kamalas,

sn: कादम्बैश्चक्रवाकैश्च कुररैर्जलकुक्कुटैः। कारण्डवैः प्लवैहसैर्बकैर्महगुभिरेव च॥
en: And teeming with Kadambas, Chakrabakas, Kuraras, waterfowls, Karandavas, Palavas, swans, cranes, Madgus,

sn: एतैश्चान्यैश्च कीर्णानि समन्ताज्जलचारिभिः। हृष्टैस्तथा तामरसरसासवमदालसैः॥ पद्मोदरच्युतरजः किंजल्कारुणरञ्जितैः। मञ्जुस्वरैर्मधुकरैर्विरुतान् कमलाकरान्॥
en: And other aquatic birds of all description. And those most exalted of men beheld on the plateau of the Gandhamadana lakes decorated all over with arrays of lotuses and ringing with the sweet hum of gladdened black-bees drowsy with drinking the intoxicating juice of red lotuses and reddened with pollens falling from the lotus-cups.

sn: अपश्यंस्ते नरव्याघ्रा गन्धमादनसानुषु। तथैव पद्मपण्डैश्च मण्डितांश्च समन्ततः॥ शिखण्डिनीभिः सहिताँल्लतामण्डलकेषु च। मेघतूर्यरवोद्दाममदनाकुलितान् भृशम्॥ कृत्वैव केकामधुरं संगीतं मधुरस्वरम्। चित्रान् कलापान् विस्तीर्य सविलासान् मदालसान्।। मयूरान् ददृशुर्हष्टान् नृत्यतो वनलालसान्। कांश्चित् प्रियाभिः सहितान् रममाणान् कलापिनः॥६२। वल्लीलतासंकटेषु कुटजेषु स्थितांस्तथा। कांश्चिच्च कुटजानां तु विटपेषूत्कटानिव्र॥ कलापरुचिराटोपनिचितान् मुकुटानिव। विवरेषु तरूणां च रुचिरान् ददृशुश्च ते॥
en: And in the groves of creepers they beheld those joyful-wood-loving peacocks with their mates, maddened with an excess of animal propensity caused by the sound of the clouds resembling the trumpet-notes, sportive and drowsy with lust, dancing with their gorgeous tails out spread and warbling forth sweet and melodious notes. Some of the peacocks, seated on the Kutaja trees densely carpeted with creepers, were sporting with their sweet hearts; some, seated on the boughs of the Kutaja trees and proud of their splendid tails spread out looked like so many crowns worn by the trees; and some seated in the holes of trees looked exceedingly beautiful.

sn: सिन्धुवारांस्तथोदारान् मन्मथस्येव तोमरान्। सुवर्णवर्णकुसुमान् गिरीणां शिखरेषु च॥ कर्णिकारान् विकसितान् कर्णपूरानिवोत्तमान्। तथापश्यन् कुरबकान् वनराजिषु पुष्पितान्॥ कामवश्यौत्सुक्यकरान् कामस्येव शरोत्करान्। तथैव वनराजीनामुदारान् रचितानिव॥ विराजमानांस्तेऽपश्यस्तिलकांस्तिलकानिव। तथानङ्गशराकारान् सहकारान् मनोरमान्॥ अपश्यन् भ्रमरारावान् मञ्जरीभिर्विराजितान्। हिरण्यसदृशैः पुष्पैर्दावाग्निसदृशैरपि॥ लोहितैरञ्जनाभैश्च वैदूर्यसदृशैरपि। अतीव वृक्षा राजन्ते पुष्पिता: शैलसानुषु॥
en: On the summits of the mountains they saw the graceful Sindoofar trees looking like the arrows of Cupid and the blossoming and gold coloured Karnikaras appearing like ear-rings of excellent workmanship. And in the woods of the Gandhamadana they beheld the blossoming Kurubakas appearing like the shafts of Cupid and making the lustful persons more and more amorous. They beheld also the Tilaka trees appearing like beauty-spots painted on the forehead of the forest. They beheld further the beautiful Shahakaras (mango trees) have the efficacy of Cupid's darts, graced with blossoms and hummed over by black bees. There grew several trees on the plateau of the mountains; some of which bearing flowers of a golden hue, some, of the colour resembling forest conflagration, some red, some green and some sable, looked supremely beautiful.

sn: तथा शालांस्तमालांश्च पाटलान् बकुलानपि। माला इव समासक्ताः शैलानां शिखरेषु च॥
en: Then again there were rows of Sala, Tamalas Patalas and Bakulas encircling the summing of the mountains like so many garlands.

sn: विमलस्फाटिकाभानि पाण्डुरच्छदनैर्द्विजैः। कलहंसैरुपेतानि सारसाभिरुतानि च॥ सरांसि बहुशः पार्थाः पश्यन्तः शैलासनुषु। पद्मोत्पलविमिश्राणि सुखशीतजलानि च।॥ एवं क्रमेण ते वीरा वीक्षमाणाः समन्ततः। गन्धवन्त्यथ माल्यानि रसवन्ति फलानि च॥ सरांसि च मनोज्ञानि वृक्षांश्चातिमनोरमान्। विविशुः पाण्डवाः सर्वे विस्मयोत्फुल्ललोचनाः॥
en: Thus, gradually beholding on the plateau of the Gandhamadana, many lakes as transparent as crystal, full of swans of white plumage, ringing with the cries of Sarasas, decked with lotuses and lilies and containing water of pleasurable feel and also beholding fragrant flowers and luscious fruits, beautiful lakes and highly beautiful trees, the heroic Parthas with eyes expanded with wonder penetrated into the forest (of Gandhamadana).

sn: कमलोत्पलकह्लारपुण्डरीकसुगन्धिना। सेव्यमाना वने तस्मिन् सुखस्पर्शेन वायुना॥
en: And as they walked on they were fanned by the breeze of balmy feel perfumed by Kamalas, Utapalas, Kalparas and Pandarikas.

sn: ततो युधिष्ठिरो भीममाहेदं प्रीतिमद् वचः। अहो श्रीमदिदं भीम गन्धमादनकाननम्॥
en: Then Yudhishthira said to Bhima in affectionate terms "O Bhima, beautiful indeed is this forest of the Gandhamadana!

sn: वने ह्यस्मिन् मनोरम्ये दिव्याः काननजा द्रुमाः। लताश्च विविधाकाराः पत्रपुष्पफलोपगा:॥
en: In this pleasant forest there are various excellent wild trees and creepers covered with foliage, flowers and fruits.

sn: भान्त्येते पुष्पविकचाः पुंस्कोकिलकुलाकुलाः। नात्र कण्टकिनः केचिन्न च विद्यन्त्यपुष्पिताः॥
en: This forest is beautified with handsome flowers and maddened male Kokilas, nor there are in it any thorny trees and trees that do not flower.

sn: स्निग्धपत्रफला वृक्षा गन्धमादनसानुषु। भ्रमरारावमधुरा नलिनी: फुल्लपङ्कजाः॥ विलोड्यमानाः पश्येमाः करिभिः सकरेणुभिः। पश्येमां नलिनी चान्यां कमलोत्पलमालिनीम्॥ स्रग्धरां विग्रहवती साक्षाच्छ्रियमिवापराम्। नानाकुसुमगन्धाढ्यास्तस्येमाः काननोत्तमे॥ उपगीयमाना भ्रमरै राजन्ते वनराजयः। पश्य भीम शुभान् देशान् देवाक्रीडान् समन्ततः॥८३।
en: On the plateau of the Gandhamadana all the trees are furnished with glossy foliage and fruits. Look! how these lotus-lakes decked with full blown lotuses and sweet with the hum of black fees are being agitated by elephants with their mates! look at another lotus lake decked with an array of lotuses and looking like a second Sree in very flesh and blood with a garland encircling her neck. In this excellent forest, there are ranges of woods rich with the fragrance of various flowers and ringing with the hum of the black fees. O Bhima, behold on all sides the auspicious sporting grounds of the gods!

sn: अमानुषगति प्राप्ताः संसिद्धाः स्म वृकोदर। लताभिः पुष्पिताग्राभिः पुष्पिताः पादपोत्तमाः॥ संश्लिष्टाः पार्थ शोभन्ते गन्धमादनसानुषु। शिखण्डिनीभिश्चरतां सहितानां शिखण्डिनाम्॥ नदतां शृणु निर्घोषं भीम पर्वतसानुषु। चकोराः शतपत्राश्च मत्तकोकिलसारिकाः॥
en: O Vrikodara, by our arrival here we have attained to a state transcending the human and our desire has been fulfilled. O Partha, on these plateaus of the Gandhamadana, you excellent blossoming trees, embraced by flower creepers, look supremely handsome. O Bhima, listen to the warbles of the peacocks wandering with their sweet-hearts on the slopes of the mountain, of the Chataka, Satapatra and maddened Kokila and Sarikas.

sn: पत्रिणः पुष्पितानेतान् संपतन्नि महाद्दुमान्। रक्तपीतारुणाः पार्थ पादपाग्रगताः खगाः॥ परस्परमुदीक्षन्ते बहवो जीवजीवकाः। हरितारुणवर्णानां शाद्वलानां समीपतः॥
en: Birds alighting these great blossoming trees. O Partha, seated on the boughs these myriad of Yivajevaka birds of scarlet, yellow and red colour are looking at one another. And near the green and red grass plots,

sn: सारसाः प्रतिदृश्यन्ते शैलप्रस्रवणेष्वपि। वदन्ति मधुरा वाचः सर्वभूतमनोरमाः॥ भृङ्गराजोपचक्राश्च लोहपृष्ठाः पतत्त्रिणः। चतुर्विषाणाः पद्माभाः कुञ्जराः सकरेणवः॥ एते वैदूर्यवर्णाभं क्षोभयन्ति महत् सरः। बहुतालसमुत्सेधाः शैलशृङ्गपरिच्युताः॥
en: And also near the mountain spring. The cranes are seen and the Bhringaraja, Chakoas and herons are sending forth melodious notes causing delight to all creatures. Elephants, furnished with four tusks and of the colour of lotuses, accompanied by their mates,

sn: नानाप्रस्रवणेभ्यश्च वारिधाराः पतन्ति च। भास्कराभाः प्रभाभिश्च शारदाभ्रधनोपमाः॥ शोभयन्ति महाशैलं नानारजतधातवः। क्वचिदञ्जनवर्णाभाः क्वचित् काञ्चनसंनिभाः॥ धातवो हरितालस्य क्वचिद्धिमुलकस्य च। मनः शिलागुहाश्चैव सन्ध्याभ्रनिकरोपमाः॥ शशलोहितवर्णाभाः क्वचिनैरिकधातवः। सितासिताभ्रप्रतिमा बालसूर्यसमप्रभाः॥ एते बहुविधाः शैलं शोभयन्ति महाप्रभाः। गन्धर्वाः सह कान्ताभिर्यथोक्तं वृषपर्वणा॥
en: Are agitating that great lake of the colour of lapses. And torrents gushing down from the summits of the mountains are spouting forth as high as several palm trees from the springs. And many silvery minerals of sun-like splendour and looking like a dense mass of autumnal clouds are beautifying this mighty mountain. In some places minerals of the hue of the collyrium, in some of golden hue and in some yellow orpiment, in some vermilion and in some caves of red arsenic resembling the evening clouds, in some red chalk of the hue of the rabbit and in some minerals resembling white and sable clouds and of the rays of the rising sun-these and many other minerals of mighty splendour, are adding largely to the beauty of the mountain. As was told by Vrishparvana, Gandharvas with their sweethearts,

sn: दृश्यन्ते शैलशृङ्गेषु पार्थ किम्पुरुषैः सह। गीतानां समतालानां तथा साम्नां च निःस्वनः॥
en: And accompanied by the Kimpurushas, O Partha, are seen on the summits of the mountain. Songs exactly keeping time and also the chanting of the Samaveda,

sn: श्रूयते बहुधा भीम सर्वभूतमनोहरः। महागङ्गामुदीक्षस्व पुण्यां देवनदी शुभाम्॥
en: Delightful to all creatures are being repeatedly heard. Behold the auspicious and sacred celestials river Mahaganga

sn: कलहंसगणैर्जुष्टामृषिकिन्नरसेविताम् धातुभिश्च सरिदिश्च किन्नरैर्मृगपक्षिभिः॥ गन्धर्वैप्सरोभिश्च काननैश्च मनोरमैः। व्यालैश्च विविधाकारैः शतशीषैः समन्ततः॥ उपेतं पश्य कौन्तेय शैलराजमरिन्दम।
en: Adorned with swans and worshipped by the sages and the Kinnaras. O tormentor of foes, O son of Kunti, behold this prince of mountains containing minerals and rivulets, Kinnaras, deer and birds, Gandharvas and Apsaras and pleasant gardens and snakes of many shapes and of hundred heads.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ते प्रीतमनसः शूराः प्राप्ता गमिमनुत्तमाम्॥ नातृप्यन् पर्वतेन्द्रस्य दर्शनेन परन्तपाः। उपेतमथ माल्यैश्च फलवद्भिश्च पादपैः॥ आष्टिषेणस्य राजर्षेराश्रमं ददृशुस्तदा। ततस्ते तिग्मतपसं कृशंधमनिसंततम्। पारगं सर्वधर्माणामार्टिषेणमुपागमन्॥
en: Vaishampayana said: Those tormentors of foes, those heroes accompanied by Draupadi and the high-souled Brahmanas having attained to an excellent state were highly glad at heart and were not satiated by beholding (over and over again) that prince of mountains. They then viewed the hermitage of the royal sage Arstisena adorned with flowers and trees bearing fruits. And they approached that royal sage of fervid devotion, versed in all religious lores and having muscles bare.

description: The colloquy between Arstisena and Yudhishthira
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच युधिष्ठिरस्तमासाद्य तपसा दग्धकिल्बिषम्। अभ्यवादयत प्रीतः शिरसा नाम कीर्तयन्॥
en: Having approached him (Arstisena) whose sins were consumed by austerities and having announced his name, Yudhishthira with great pleasure bowed down to him by bending his head.

description: The colloquy between Arstisena and Yudhishthira
sn: ततः कृष्णा च भीमश्च यमौ च सुतपस्विनौ। शिरोभिः प्राप्य राजर्षि परिवार्योपतस्थिरे॥
en: Then Krishna and Bhima and the twins of good devotion, having bowed down to that royal sage with their heads, stood surrounding him.

description: The colloquy between Arstisena and Yudhishthira
sn: तथैवधौम्योधर्मज्ञः पाण्डवानां पुरोहितः। यथान्यायमुपाक्रान्तस्तमृषि संशितव्रतम्॥ कच्चित् ते
en: And then the virtuous Dhaumya the priest of the Pandavas, duly approached the vowobserving sage.

description: The colloquy between Arstisena and Yudhishthira
sn: अन्वजानात् सधर्मज्ञो मुनिर्दिव्येन चक्षुषा। पाण्डोः पुत्रान् कुरुश्रेष्ठानास्यतामिति चाब्रवीत्॥
en: Knowing these Pandavas, the best of the Kurus-by his spiritual eye, that virtuous one said to them “be seated".

description: The colloquy between Arstisena and Yudhishthira
sn: कुरूणामृषभं पार्थं पूजयित्वा महातपाः। सह भ्रातृभिरासीनं पर्यपृच्छदनामयम्॥
en: Then that one of great devotion having welcomed Partha, the best of the Kurus, who had taken his seat with his brothers, inquired after his welfare saying,

description: The colloquy between Arstisena and Yudhishthira
sn: नानृते कुरुषे भावं कच्चिद्धर्मे प्रवर्तसे। मातापित्रोश्च ते वृत्तिः कच्चित् पार्थ न सीदति॥
en: “Do you not turn your mind towards untruth? Are you inclined towards virtue? Are not your respect and duties towards your parents falling off?

description: The colloquy between Arstisena and Yudhishthira
sn: गुरवः सर्वे वृद्धा वैद्याश्च पूजिताः। कच्चिन्न कुरुषे भावं पार्थ पापेषु कर्मसु॥
en: Are all your superiors and elders and those versed in the Vedas honoured by you? Do you not incline your mind towards sinful acts?

description: The colloquy between Arstisena and Yudhishthira
sn: सुकृतं प्रतिकर्तुं च कच्चिद्धातुं च दुष्कृतम्। यथान्यायं कुरुश्रेष्ठ जानासि न विकत्यसे॥
en: Ó best of the Kurus, do you properly know how to perform praiseworthy acts and how to avoid wicked ones? Are you not selfconceited?

description: The colloquy between Arstisena and Yudhishthira
sn: यथार्ह मानिताः कच्चित् त्वया नन्दन्ति साधवः। वनेष्वपि वसन् कच्चिद्धर्ममेवानुवर्तसे॥
en: Do the virtuous rejoice in being honoured by you? Do you follow virtue though dwelling in the forests?

description: The colloquy between Arstisena and Yudhishthira
sn: कच्चिद्धौम्यस्त्वदाचारैर्न पार्थ परितप्यते। दानधर्मतप:शौचैरार्जवेन तितिक्षया॥ पितृपैतामहं वृत्तं कच्चित् पार्थानुवर्तसे। कच्चिद् राजर्षियातेन पथा गच्छसि पाण्डव॥
en: O Partha, are not Dhaumya pained by your treatment of him? Do you follow in the footsteps of your forefathers by practicing charity, religious observances, devotion, purity, candour and forgiveness? Do you follow the example of the royal sages?

description: The colloquy between Arstisena and Yudhishthira
sn: स्वे स्वे किल कुले जाते पुत्रे नप्तरि वा पुनः। पितरः पितृलोकस्था: शोचन्ति च हसन्ति च॥
en: On a son or a grandson being born in their (respective) families, our ancestors in the Pitris region, either grieve or rejoice, thinking,

description: The colloquy between Arstisena and Yudhishthira
sn: किं तस्य दुष्कृतेऽस्माभिः सम्प्राप्तव्यं भविष्यति। किं चास्य सुकृतेऽस्माभिः प्राप्तव्यमिति शोभनम्॥
en: That they will be either harmed by his sinful acts or be benefited by his meritorious deeds,

description: The colloquy between Arstisena and Yudhishthira
sn: पिता माता तथैवाग्निर्गुरुरात्मा च पञ्चमः। यस्यैते पूजिताः पार्थ तस्या लोकावुभौ जितौ॥
en: He who honours his father and mother and religious guide and Agni and fifthly his soul, conquers both the worlds."

description: The colloquy between Arstisena and Yudhishthira
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच भगवन्नार्थ माहैतद् यथावद्धर्मनिश्चयम्। यथाशक्ति यथान्यायं क्रियते विधिवन्मया॥
en: Yudhishthira said: O adorable one, the duties just mentioned by you are indeed excellent and I perform them properly to the best of my ability.

description: The colloquy between Arstisena and Yudhishthira
sn: आष्टिषेण उवाच अभक्षा वायुभक्षाश्च प्लवमाना विहायसा। जुषन्ते पर्वतश्रेष्ठमृषयः पर्वसंधिषु॥
en: Arstisena said: During the Parvas, sages living on air and water visit this prince of mountains, ranging through the skies.

description: The colloquy between Arstisena and Yudhishthira
sn: कामिनः सह कान्ताभिः परस्परमनुव्रताः। दृश्यन्ते शैलशृङ्गस्था यथा किम्पुरुषा नृप॥
en: O King, amorous persons with their sweet hearts mutually enamoured of one another and Kimpurushas are seen on the summits of this mountain.

description: The colloquy between Arstisena and Yudhishthira
sn: अरजांसि च वासांसि वसानाः कौशिकानि च। दृश्यन्ते बहवः पार्थ गन्धर्वाप्सरसां गणाः॥
en: O Partha, numerous Apsaras and Gandharvas attired in white silk garments are also to be found here,

description: The colloquy between Arstisena and Yudhishthira
sn: विद्याधरगणाश्चैव स्रग्विणः प्रियदर्शनाः। महोरगगणाश्चैव सुपर्णाश्चोरगादयः॥
en: Together with good looking Vidyadharas adorned with garlands and also mighty Uragas, Suparnas and other Uragas.

description: The colloquy between Arstisena and Yudhishthira
sn: अस्य चोपरि शैलस्य श्रूयते पर्वसंधिषु। भेरीपणपवशङ्खानां मृदङ्गानां च निःस्वनः॥
en: And during the Parvas sounds of kettledrums, tabors and shells are heard on the summits of the mountain.

description: The colloquy between Arstisena and Yudhishthira
sn: इहस्थैरेव तत् सर्वं श्रोतव्यं भरतर्षभाः। न कार्या वः कथंचित् स्यात् तत्राभिगमने मतिः॥
en: O most exalted of the Bharatas all these are heard even from this place. Do you by no means, have a mind to go thither.

description: The colloquy between Arstisena and Yudhishthira
sn: न चाप्यतः परं शक्यं गन्तुं भरतसत्तमाः। विहारो ह्यत्र देवानाममानुषगतिस्तु सा॥
en: O most excellent of the Bharatas, it is impossible to proceed beyond this. That place being the sporting-ground of the celestials, men can have no access there.

description: The colloquy between Arstisena and Yudhishthira
sn: ईषच्चपलकर्माणं मनुष्यमिह भारत। द्विषन्ति सर्वभूतानि ताडयन्ति च राक्षसाः॥
en: At this place, O Bharata all creatures are hostile to and the Rakshasas chastise that man who may have even the very slightest presumption.

description: The colloquy between Arstisena and Yudhishthira
sn: अस्यातिक्रम्य शिखरं कैलासस्य युधिष्ठिर। गतिः परमसिद्धानां देवर्षीणां प्रकाशते॥
en: O Yudhishthira, beyond the summit of the Kailasa the path of the divine sages all whose desire have been fulfilled, is visible.

description: The colloquy between Arstisena and Yudhishthira
sn: चापलादिह गच्छन्तं पार्थ यानमितः परम्। अयः शूलादिभिर्जन्ति राक्षसाः शत्रुसूदन॥
en: O destroyer of foes, if any one impudently goes beyond this, the Rakshasas kill him with iron darts and other weapons,

description: The colloquy between Arstisena and Yudhishthira
sn: अप्सरोभिः परिवृतः समृद्ध्या नरवाहनः। इह वैश्रवणस्तात पर्वसंधिषु दृश्यते॥
en: Here too, O affectionate one, during the Parvas is seen Vaisravana (Kubera), carried on the shoulders of men, possessed of vast wealth and surrounded by Apsaras.

description: The colloquy between Arstisena and Yudhishthira
sn: शिखरस्थं समासीनमधिपं यक्षरक्षसाम्। प्रेक्षन्ते सर्वभूतानि भानुमन्तमिवोदितम्॥
en: All the creatures then behold the King of the Rakshasas seated on the summit and looking like the sun just risen

description: The colloquy between Arstisena and Yudhishthira
sn: देवदानवसिद्धानां तथा वैश्रवणस्य च। गिरेः शिखरमुद्यानमिदं भरतसत्तम।॥
en: O best of the Bharatas, that summit of the mountain is the sporting garden of all the Devas (gods) Danavas (demons) Siddhas and of Vaishrvana alike.

description: The colloquy between Arstisena and Yudhishthira
sn: उपासीनस्यधनदं तुम्बुरोः पर्वसंधिषु। गीतसामस्वनस्तात श्रूयते गन्धमादने॥
en: O affectionate one, during the Parvas, when Tambura worships the Lord of wealth, his chanting of the verses of the Samaveda is heard all over the mountain Gandhamadana.

description: The colloquy between Arstisena and Yudhishthira
sn: एतदेवंविधं चित्रमिह तात युधिष्ठिर। प्रेक्षन्ते सर्वभूतानि बहुशः पर्वसंधिषु॥
en: O affectionate one, O Yudhishthira, all souls in the Gandhamadana, observe these and similar wonders several times during the Parvas.

description: The colloquy between Arstisena and Yudhishthira
sn: भुञ्जाना मुनिभोज्यानि रसवन्ति फलानि च। वसध्वं पाण्डवश्रेष्ठा यावदर्जुनदर्शनात्॥
en: O best of the Pandavas, remain here living on luscious fruits eaten by the sages, until you meet with Arjuna.

description: The colloquy between Arstisena and Yudhishthira
sn: न तात चफ्लैर्भाव्यमिह प्राप्तैः कथंचन। उषित्वेह यथाकामं यथाश्रद्धं विहृत्य च। ततः शस्त्रजितां तात पृथिवीं पालयिष्यसि॥
en: O affectionate one, do not betray any restless spirit while remaining here. Dwelling here quite at ease and amusing yourself as you choose, you shall, in the long run, crushing your foes, by the prowess of your weapons, govern the earth. ones

sn: जनमेजय उवाच आर्टिषेणाश्रमे तस्मिन् मम पूर्वपितामहाः। पाण्डोः पुत्रा महात्मानः सर्वे दिव्यपराक्रमाः॥ कियन्तं कालमवसन् पर्वते गन्धमादने। किं च चक्रुर्महावीर्याः सर्वेऽतिबलपौरुषाः॥
en: Janamejaya said : How long did my grandsire, the high-souled sons of Pandu, all of whom were endued with unrivalled prowess, dwell in the hermitage of Arstisena, situated in the mountain Gandhamadana? And (during their stay there) what these exceedingly powerful endowed wit manliness and prowess do?

sn: कानि चाभ्यवहार्याणि तत्र तेषां महात्मनाम्। वसतां लोकवीराणामासंस्तद् ब्रूहि सत्तम॥
en: Tell me, O excellent one, what these highsouled ones those heroes of the worlds subsist upon, while dwelling there?

sn: विस्तरेण च मे शंस भीमसेनपराक्रमम्। यद् यच्चक्रे महाबाहुस्तस्मिन् हैमवते गिरौ॥
en: Narrate to me also in detail of the prowess of Bhimasena and what that mighty armed one did in the mountain Himalaya.

sn: न खल्वासीत् पुनयुद्धं तस्य यक्षैर्द्विजोत्तम। कच्चित् समागमस्तेषामासीद् वैश्रवणस्य च॥
en: O, the most excellent of the Brahmanas, was there no other fight with the Yakshas? Did they meet with Vaisravana?

sn: तत्र ह्यायातिधनद आर्टिषेणो यथाब्रवीत्। एतदिच्छाम्यहं श्रोतुं विस्तरेण तपोधन॥
en: Surely, as Arstisena said, the Lord of wealth, visits that place. O you, whose only wealth is devotion, I am desirous of hearing of all this in detail. I am not yet satisfied with hearing of all their movements.

sn: न हि मे शृण्वतस्तृप्तिरस्ति तेषां विचेष्टितम्। वैशम्पायन उवाच एतदात्महितं श्रुत्वा तस्याप्रतिमतेजसः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : The most exalted on the Bharatas, having heard the instructions of that one of incomparable energy (Arstisena), began always to abide by them accordingly.

sn: शासनं सततं चक्रुस्तथैव भरतर्षभाः। भुञ्जाना मुनिभोज्यानि रसवन्ति फलानि च॥
en: Living on the food eaten by the sages and luscious fruits and the flesh of the deer killed by unpoisoned arrows.

sn: मेध्यानि हिमवत्पृष्ठे मधूनि विविधानि च। एवं ते न्यवसंस्तत्र पाण्डवा भरतर्षभाः॥
en: And various kinds of pure honey, the Pandavas-the most exalted of the Bharatasdwelt in the Himalayas.

sn: तथा निवसतां तेषां पञ्चमं वर्षमभ्यगात्। शृण्वतां लोमशोक्तानि वाक्यानि विविधान्युत॥
en: Living in this way, they passed the fifth year listening to the various stories told by Lomasha

sn: कृत्यकाल उपस्थास्य इति चोक्त्वा घटोत्कचः। राक्षसैः सह सर्वैश्च पूर्वमेव गतः प्रभो॥
en: O Lord, Ghatotkacha together with all the Rakshasas had before this departed saying “I shall appear when occasion arises."

sn: आर्टिषेणाश्रमे तेषां वसतां वै महात्मनाम्। अगच्छन् बहवो मासाः पश्यतां महदद्भुतम्॥
en: Thus, witnessing many wonders, these highsouled ones (Pandavas) spent several months in the hermitage of Arstisena.

sn: तैस्तत्र विहरद्भिश्च रममाणैश्च पाण्डवैः। प्रीतिमन्तो महाभागा मुनय.श्चारणास्तथा॥
en: And when the Pandavas were sporting and playing there at ease, several contented and highly fortunate sages and Charanas,

sn: आजग्मुः पाण्डवान् द्रष्टुं शुद्धात्मानो यतव्रताः। ते तैः सह कथां चक्रुर्दिव्यां भरतसत्तमाः॥
en: Of pure souls and observant of vows came there to see them. And those most exalted to the Bharatas talked with them on divine matters.

sn: ततः कतिपयाहस्य महाह्रदनिवासिनम्। ऋद्धिमन्तं महानागं सुपर्णः सहसाऽऽहरत्॥
en: When a few days had thus passed away, it so happened that Suparna carried off a mighty Nag (serpent) of great prosperity who lived in the great lake.

sn: प्राकम्पत महाशैलः प्रामृद्यन्त महाद्रुमाः। ददृशुः सर्वभूतानि पाण्डवाश्च तदद्भुतम्॥
en: (In consequence of which) the mighty mountain began to tremble and many huge trees were crushed. And the Pandavas together with all creatures witnessed that marvellous scene.

sn: ततः शैलोत्तमस्याचात् पाण्डवान् प्रति मारुतः। अवहत् सर्वमाल्यानि गन्धवन्ति शुभानि च॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Then from the top of that excellent mountain several kinds of auspicious and fragrant flowers were carried along by the wind towards the Pandavas.

sn: तत्र पुष्पाणि दिव्यानि सुहृद्भिः सह पाण्डवाः। ददृशुः पञ्चवर्णानि द्रौपदी च यशस्विनी॥
en: And the Pandavas together with their friends and the renowned Draupadi beheld (those) heavenly flowers of five colours.

sn: भीमसेनं ततः कृष्णा काले वचनमब्रवीत्। विविक्ते पर्वतोद्देशे सुखासीनं महाभुजम्॥
en: And when Bhimasena of mighty arms was comfortably seated on a lonely spot on the

sn: सुपर्णानिलवेगेन श्वसनेन महाचलात्। पञ्चवर्णानि पात्यन्ते पुष्पाणि भरतर्षभ।॥ प्रत्यक्षं सर्वभूतानां नदीमश्वरथां प्रति। खाण्डवे सत्यसंधेन भ्रात्रा तव महात्मना॥ गन्धर्वोरगरक्षांसि वासवश्च निवारितः। हता मायाविनश्चोचाधनुः प्राप्तं च गाण्डिवम्॥
en: "O the best of the Bharatas, it is witnessed by all the creatures that these flowers of five colours, driven by the force of the wind raised by Suparna, are falling (with a crushing force) towards the river Ashvaratha. (In the forest of) Khandava your high-souled brother (Arjuna), true to his promise baffled (the attempts) of the Gandharvas, the Uragyas, the Rakshasas and even of Vasava (Indra) and slew the furious Mayavis (who can assume any shape they choose) and also obtained the bow Gandiva."

sn: तवापि सुमहत् तेजो महद् बाहुबलं च ते। अविषह्यमनाधृष्यं शक्रतुल्यपराक्रम॥
en: You too, are possessed of as indomitable spirit and mighty arms as the powerful Sakra himself.

sn: त्वद्वाहुबलवेगेन त्रासिताः सर्वराक्षसाः। हित्वा शैलं प्रपद्यन्तां भीमसेन दिशो दश।॥
en: (Therefore) O Bhimasena, let all the Rakshasas, terrified with the force of your mighty arms, fly towards the ten cardinal points, leaving this mountain.

sn: ततः शैलोत्तमस्याचं चित्रमाल्यधरं शिवम्। व्यपेतभयसम्मोहाः पश्यन्तु सुहृदस्तव॥
en: Then let your friends devoid of all fear and affliction behold the auspicious top of this excellent mountain decorated with variegated flowers.

sn: एवं प्रणिहितं भीम चिरात् प्रभृति मे मनः। द्रष्टुमिच्छामि शैलाचं त्वद्वाहुबलपालिता।॥
en: O Bhima, I have cherished this thought in my mind for a long time, and I have a mind to behold the summit of this mountain protected by the force of your arms.

sn: ततः क्षिप्तमिवात्मानं द्रौपद्या स परंतपः। नामृष्यत महाबाहुः प्रहारमिव सद्भवः॥
en: Thereupon, the tormentor of his foes, Bhimasena of mighty arms, considering himself as conjured by Draupadi, looked like an wounded bull of excellent breed and could not brook (her remarks).

sn: सिंहर्षभगतिः श्रीमानुदारः कनकप्रभः। मनस्वी बलवान् दृप्तो मानी शूरश्च पाण्डवः॥ लोहिताक्षः पृथुव्यंसो मत्तवारणविक्रमः। सिंहदंष्ट्रो बृहत्स्कन्धः शालपोत इवोद्गतः॥ महात्मा चारुसर्वाङ्गः कम्बुग्रीवो महाभुजः। रुक्मपृष्ठंधनुः खङ्गं तूणांश्चाप परामृशत्॥
en: Then that mighty Pandava having the gait of a lion or a bull, graceful, having the splendour of gold, high-minded, powerful, proud, sensitive, heroic, heaving red eyes, broadshouldered, possessed of the strength of mad elephants, endowed with lionine teeth and a broad neck, tall as a young Sala tree, generous hearted, of symmetrical proportions, of shelllike neck and of mighty arms, took up his bow plaited at the back with gold and also his sword and arrow case.

sn: स केसरीव चोत्सिक्तः प्रभिन्न इव वारणः। व्यपेतभयसम्मोहः शैलमभ्यपतद् बली॥
en: And that mighty one proud as a lion and looking like a mad elephant, rushed towards that cliff tree from all fear and affliction.

sn: तं मृगेन्द्रमिवायान्तं प्रभिन्नमिव वारणम्। ददृशुः सर्वभूतानि बाणकार्मुकधारिणम्॥
en: And all the creatures beheld him appearing like a lion or a maddened bull furnished with bows and arrows.

sn: द्रौपद्या वर्धयन् हर्षं गदामादाय पाण्डवः। व्यपेतभयसम्मोहः शैलराजं समाश्रितः॥
en: And the Pandava devoid of all fear and affliction, proceeded to the mountain furnished with his club to the great delight of Draupadi.

sn: न ग्लानि च कातर्यं न वैक्लव्यं न मत्सरः। कदाचिज्जुषते पार्थमात्मजं मातरिश्वनः॥
en: Neither fatigue, nor fear, nor lassitude nor the malice (of others) took possession of that son of Pritha and god of the wind.

sn: तदेकायनमासाद्य विषमं भीमदर्शनम्। बहुतालोच्छ्रयं शृङ्गमारुरोह महाबलः॥
en: Getting to a pass affording passage to a single individual only, that one of great prowess, ascended that ragged and terriblelooking summit, high as several palm trees.

sn: सकिन्नरमहानागमुनिगन्धर्वराक्षसान्। हर्षयन् पर्वतस्याचमारुह्य स महाबलः॥
en: Causing the delight of the Kinnaras, Mahanagas, sages and the Rakshasas, the best of the Bharatas, endowed with gigantic strength, ascended the summit of the movntain,

sn: ततो वैश्रवणावासं ददर्श भरतर्षभः। काञ्चनैः स्फाटिकैश्चैव वेश्मभिः समलंकृतम्॥
en: And beheld therefrom the abode of Vaisravana adorned with golden and crystal buildings,

sn: प्राकारेण परिक्षिप्तं सौवर्णेन समन्ततः। सर्वरत्नद्युतिमता सर्वोद्यानवता तथा॥
en: Encircled on all sides by golden walls, having the lustre of all gems, containing gardens of all sorts,

sn: शैलादभ्युच्छ्यवता चयाट्टालकशोभिना। द्वारतोरणनिर्वृहध्वजसंवाहशोभिना॥
en: Higher than a mountain peak, adorned with ramparts and towers, graced with doorways, gates and rows of flags,

sn: विलासिनीभिरत्यर्थं नृत्यन्तीभिः समन्ततः। वायुनाधूयमानाभिः पताकाभिरलंकृतम्॥
en: And beautiful with coquettish damsels dancing around and ornamented with flags fluttered by the wind.

sn: धनुष्कोटिमवष्टभ्य वक्रभावेन बाहुना। पश्यमानः स खेदेन द्रविणाधिपतेः पुरम्॥
en: Leaning against the end of his bow with banded arm, he stood beholding the city of Kubera with great sorrow caused by the remembrance of his own fortune).

sn: मोदयन् सर्वभूतानि गन्धमादनसम्भवः। सर्वगन्धवहस्तत्र मारुतः सुसुखो ववौ॥
en: A pleasurable breeze was blowing there, having its origin in the Gandhamadana, gladdening all creatures and carrying sweet odours of all kinds.

sn: चित्रा.विविधवर्णाभाश्चित्रमञ्जरिधारिणः। अचिन्त्या विविधास्तत्र दुमाः परमशोभिनः॥
en: There were many superbly beautiful trees beyond all thought, decorated with variegated colour and bearing graceful blossoms.

sn: रत्नजालपरिक्षिप्तं चित्रमाल्यविभूषितम्। राक्षसाधिपतेः स्थानं ददृशे भरतर्षभः॥
en: That best of the Bharatas then beheld the palace of Kubera covered on all sides with heaps of gems and decorated with variegated garlands.

sn: गदाखड्गधनुष्पाणिः समभित्यक्तजीवितः। भीमसेनो महाबाहुस्तस्थौ गिरिरिवाचलः॥
en: There stood Bhimasena of mighty-arms devoid of all thoughts of life, firm as a rock, with club, sword and bow in his hand.

sn: ततः शङ्खमुपाध्मासीद द्विषतां लोमहर्षणम्। ज्याघोषतलशब्दं च कृत्वा भूतान्यमोहयत्॥
en: Then blowing his conch which made the hair of his adversaries stand on the end and twangling his bow, striking his arms with his palms, he struck terror into the hearts of all the creatures.

sn: ततः प्रहृष्टरोमाणस्तं शब्दमभिदुद्रुवुः। यक्षराक्षसगन्धर्वाः पाण्डवस्य समीपतः॥
en: (Infuriated) at this, the Yakshas, the Rakshasas and the Gandharvas with their hair standing erect, rushed towards the Pandava, following the direction of these sounds.

sn: गदापरिघनिस्त्रिंशशूलशक्तिपरश्वधाः। प्रगृहीता व्यरोचन्त यक्षराक्षसबाहुभिः॥
en: Then the maces, clubs, swords, spears, axes and the javelins carried in their arms by the Rakshasas, began to blaze.

sn: ततः प्रववृते युद्धं तेषां तस्य च भारत। : प्रयुक्तान् महामायैः शूलशक्तिपरश्वधान्॥ भल्लैर्भीमः प्रचिच्छेद भीमवेगतरैस्ततः। अन्तरिक्षगतानां च भूमिष्ठानां च गर्जताम्॥ शरैविव्याध गात्राणि राक्षसानां महाबलः। सा लोहितमहावृष्टिरभ्यवर्षन्महाबलम्॥ गदापरिघपाणीनां रक्षसां कायसम्भवाः। कायेभ्यः प्रच्युताधारा राक्षसानां समन्ततः॥
en: And, O Bharata, when the fight took place between them, Bhima cut off the darts, javelins and axes hurled by those possessing great powers of illusion, with his arrows of tremendous force. And that most powerful one, pierced with his arrows the bodies of those roaring Rakshasas who were on the ground and of those that were in the sky. And that one of great prowess was drenched in that great deluge of blood gushing and flowing on all sides from the bodies of the Rakshasas with maces and clubs in their hands,

sn: तैः भीमबाहुबलोत्सृष्टैरायुधैर्यक्षरक्षसाम्। विनिकृत्तानि दृश्यन्ते शरीराणि शिरांसि च॥
en: And the heads and the bodies of the Rakshasas were seen cut off and mangled by the weapons hurled by the force of Bhima's arms.

sn: प्रच्छाद्यमानं रक्षोभिः पाण्डवं प्रियदर्शनम्। ददृशुः सर्वभूतानि सूर्यमभ्रगणैरिव॥
en: All the creatures, then, saw the good-looking Pandava hemmed in by the Rakshasas and appearing like the sun enveloped with clouds.

sn: स रश्मिभिरिवादित्यः शरैररिनिधातिभिः। सर्वानार्छन्महाबाहुर्बलवान् सत्यविक्रमः॥
en: And that mighty-armed and powerul one (Bhima) of true prowess covered all (the Rakshasas) with his arrows fatal to his enemies, as the sun shrouds all the creatures with his rays.

sn: अभितर्जयमानाश्च रुवन्तश्च महारवान्। न मोहं भीमसेनस्य ददृशुः सर्वराक्षसाः॥
en: Although uttering both loud yells and cries of victory, the Rakshasas did not see Bhima deprived of senses.

sn: यक्षा विकृतसर्वाङ्गा भीमसेनभयार्दिताः। भीममार्तस्वरं चक्रुर्विप्रकीर्णमहायुधाः॥
en: And the Yakshas, with their bodies mangled all over, terrified by the fear of Bhimasena, began to utter frightful cries of distress leaving aside their weapons.

sn: उत्सृज्य ते गदाशूलानसिशक्तिपरश्वधान्। दक्षिणां दिशमाजग्मुस्त्रासिता दृढधन्वना॥
en: And then owing to the fear of that wielder of a strong bow, Bhimaseria, they fled southwards, forsaking their maces, spears, swords, clubs and axes.

sn: तत्र शूलगदापाणियूंढोरस्को महाभुजः। सखा वैश्रवणस्यासीन्मणिमात्राम राक्षसः॥
en: On that side, stood the mighty-armed and broad-chested Rakshasa, Maniman, the friend of Kubera, armed with darts and maces.

sn: अदर्शयदधीकारं पौरुषं च महाबलः। स तान् दृष्ट्वा परावृत्तान् स्मयमान इवाब्रवीत्॥
en: Displaying his masterdom and manliness, he, of gigantic strength, seeing them taking to heels, addressed them smilingly thus-

sn: एकेन बहवः सङ्खये मानुषेण पराजिताः। प्राप्य वैश्रवणावासं किं वक्ष्यथधनेश्वरम्॥
en: "Going to the abode of Vaisravana, how would you tell the lord of wealth that vast numbers (of Yakshas) have been slain by a single man."

sn: एवमाभाष्य तान् सर्वानभ्यवर्तत राक्षसः। शक्तिशूलगदापाणिरभ्यधावत् स पाण्डवम्॥
en: Having addressed them thus, that Rakshasa, holding in the hands, clubs, javelins and maces, rushed against the Pandava.

sn: तमापतन्तं वेगेन प्रभिन्नमिव वारणम्। वत्सदन्तैस्त्रिभिः पार्श्वे भीमसेनः समार्दयत्॥
en: Beholding him approach with the fury of a maddened elephant, Bhimasena pierced his sides with three choice arrows.

sn: मणिमानपि संक्रुद्धः प्रगृह्य महतीं गदाम्। प्राहिणोद् भीमसेनाय परिगृह्य महाबलः॥
en: The mighty Maniman too, in wrath, taking and brandishing a tremendous mace, hurled it at him.

sn: विद्युदूपां महाघोरामाकाशे महतीं गदाम्। शरैबर्हभिरभ्या द् भीमसेनः शिलाशितैः॥
en: Bhimasena too, on his part, beset, with many arrows, sharpened on stones, that tremendous and dreadful mace in the sky resembling a lightning flash.

sn: प्रत्यहन्यन्त ते सर्वे गदामासाद्य सायकाः। न वेगंधारयामासुर्गदावेगस्य वेगिताः॥
en: But all these arrows though discharged with force, on reaching the mace fell back and could not check its onward career.

sn: गदायुद्धसमाचारं बुद्ध्यमानः स वीर्यवान्। व्यंसयामास तं तस्य प्रहारं भीमविक्रमः॥
en: And that spirited one of dreadful prowess (at last) baffled the attack (of the Rakshasa) by resorting to his skill in mace-fighting.

sn: ततः शक्तिं महाधोरां रुक्मदण्डामयस्मयीम्। तस्मिन्नेवान्तरेधीमान् प्रजहाराथ राक्षसः॥
en: At this interval, that intelligent Rakshasa assailed (Bhima) with a dreadful iron club furnished with a golden handle.

sn: सा भुर्ज भीमनिर्हादा भित्त्वा भीमस्य दक्षिणम्। साग्निज्वाला महारौद्रा पपात सहसा भुवि॥
en: And that tremendous (club) emitting flames and sending forth dreadful roars pierced suddenly the right arm of Bhima and then fell to the ground.

sn: सोऽतिविद्धो महेष्वासः शक्त्यामितपराक्रमः। गदां जचाह कौन्तेयः क्रोधपर्याकुलेक्षणः॥
en: (Thus) severely wounded, that great bowman, the exceedingly powerful son of Kunti, with eyes rolling in wrath, took up his mace.

sn: रक्मपट्टपिनद्धां तां शत्रूणां भयवर्धिनीम्। प्रगृह्याथ नदन भीमः शैक्यां सर्वायसीं गदाम्॥
en: And then taking up his iron mace termed Shaika, in-laid with plates of gold and increasing the fear of his enemies, Bhiina, uttering yells,

sn: तरसा चाभिदुद्राव मणिमन्तं महाबलम्। दीप्यमानं महाशूलं प्रगृह्य मणिमानपि॥
en: Rushed with all speed against the exceedingly powerful Maniman, who too, taking a mighty and blazing dart,

sn: प्राहिणोद् भीमसेनाय वेगेन महता नदन्। भक्त्वा शूलं गदाचेण गदायुद्धविशारदः॥
en: Hurled it with force at Bhimasena with tremendous roars; and that adept at macefighting, breaking that dart with the end of his mace.

sn: अभिदुद्राव तं हन्तुं गरुत्मानिव पन्नगम्। सोऽन्तरिक्षमवप्लुत्य विधूय सहसा गदाम्॥ प्रविक्षेप महाबाहुर्विनद्य रणमूर्धनि। सेन्द्राशनिरिवेन्द्रेण विसृष्टा वातरंहसा॥
en: Rushed to kill Maniman, as Garuda (does) to kill the serpent. And then he (Bhima) of mighty arms advancing ahead in the field, suddenly jumped in the air and whirling his mace, hurled (at Maniman) uttering yells. And like the thunderbolt hurled by Indra, that (mace) like a pest, with the speed of the wind,

sn: हत्वा रक्षः क्षितिं प्राप्य कृत्येव निपपात ह। तं राक्षसं भीमबलं भीमसेनेन पातितम्॥ ददृशुः सर्वभूतानि सिंहेनेव गवां पतिम्। तं प्रेक्ष्य निहतं भूमौ हतशेषा निशाचराः। भीममार्तस्वरं कृत्वा जग्मुः प्राची दिशं प्रति॥
en: Killing the Rakshasa reached ground. And all the creatures beheld that exceedingly powerful Rakshasa slain by Bhima as a bull is slain by a lion. Seeing him slain on the ground the surviving Rakshasa, uttering loud cries of distress, went towards the East.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच श्रुत्वा बहुविधैः शब्दैर्नाद्यमानां गिरेर्गुहाम्। अजातशत्रुः कौन्तेयो माद्रीपुत्रावुभावपि॥ धौम्यः कृष्णा च विप्राश्च सर्वे च सुहृदस्तथा। भीमसेनमपश्यन्तः सर्वे विमनसोऽभवन्॥
en: Hearing the caves of the mountains resound with various sounds and not seeing Bhimasena, Ajatshatru (Yudhishthira), the son of Kunti and both the sons of Madri and Dhaumya and Krishna together with all the friends (of the Pandavas) became sick at heart.

sn: द्रौपदीमार्षिणाय सम्प्रधार्य महारथाः। सहिताः सायुधाः शूराः शैलमारुरुहुस्तदा।॥
en: Thereupon leaving Draupadi under the care of Arstisena and furnished with weapons, those heroes and mighty car-warriors ascended the mountain.

sn: ततः सम्प्राप्य शैलाचं वीक्षमाणा महारथाः। ददृशुस्ते महेष्वासा भीमसेनमरिंदमाः॥
en: Then those mighty car-warriors and great bowmen and tormentors of foes having reached the summit of the mountain and casting their looks around saw Bhimasena.

sn: स्फुरतश्च महाकायान् गतसत्त्वांश्च राक्षसान्। महाबलान् महासत्त्वान् भीमसेनेन पातितान्॥
en: And those huge Rakshasas of vast strength and courage slaughtered by Bhimasena, many of whom were (still) moving and many lay dead.

sn: शुशुभे स महाबाहुर्गदाखड्गधनुधरः। निहत्य समरे सर्वान् दानवान् मघवानिव॥
en: And he (Bhima) of mighty arms, armed with mace, sword and bow looked like Maghavana (Indra) having slain all the Danavas in battle.

sn: ततस्ते भ्रातरं दृष्ट्वा परिष्वज्य महारथाः। तत्रोपविविशुः पार्थाः प्राप्ता गतिमनुत्तमाम्॥
en: Then having seen their brother and having embraced him and having attained to excellent state, those mighty car-warriors the Parthas-sat down (there).

sn: तैश्चतुर्भिर्महेष्वासैर्गिरिशृङ्गमशोभता लोकपालैर्महाभागैर्दिवं देववरैरिव॥
en: That summit with those four great bowmen (seated on it) appeared as grandly beautiful as the heaven (itself) with those foremost of the celestials, the highly fortunate Lokapalas.

sn: कुबेरसदनं दृष्ट्वा राक्षसांश्च निपातितान्। भ्राता भ्रातरमासीनमब्रवीत् पृथिवीपतिः॥
en: (And) the lord of the Earth, (Yudhishthira), having beheld the abode of Kubera and those Rakshasas killed (by Bhima), addressed his brother (Bhima) who was seated, thus

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच साहसाद् यदि वा मोहाद् भीम पापमिदं कृतम्। नैतत् ते सदृशं वीर मुनेरिव मृषा वधः॥
en: "O Bhima, whether you have committed this sinful act through rashness or ignorance, it is as unworthy of you as falsehood of the ascetics.

sn: राजद्विष्टं न कर्तव्यमितिधर्मविदो विदुः। त्रिदशानामिदं द्विष्टं भीमसेन त्वया कृतम्॥
en: Righteous men affirm that acts giving offence to the king ought not to be done; but, O Bhimasena, you have committed an act which will offend even the gods.

sn: अर्थधर्मावनादृत्य यः पापे कुरुते मनः। कर्मणां पार्थ पापानां स फलं विन्दतेधुवम्। पुनरेवं न कर्तव्यं मम चेदिच्छसि प्रियम्॥
en: O Partha, he, who despising profit and virtue gives himself up to vice, is sure to pay the penalty of his sinful acts. If you look to my welfare, do not commit such (sinful) acts again."

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्त्वा सधर्मात्मा भ्राता भ्रातरमच्युतम्। अर्थतत्त्वविभागज्ञः कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः॥ विरराम महातेजास्तमेवार्थं विचिन्तयन्। ततस्ते हतशिष्टा ये भीमसेनेन राक्षसाः॥
en: Yudhishthira the virtuous highly energetic and firm-minded son of Kunti, versed in the particulars of the science of profit having addressed his brother (Bhima) thus, kept quiet and began to ponder upon the matter. On the other hand the survivors of the Rakshasas slain by Bhimasena,

sn: सहिताः प्रत्यपद्यन्त कुबेरसदनं प्रति। ते जवेन महावेगाः प्राप्य वैश्रवणालयम्॥
en: Proceeded together towards the abode of Kubera. And they of great fleetness having hastily reached the abode of Kubera,

sn: भीममार्तस्वरं चक्रुर्भीमसेनभयार्दिताः। न्यस्तशस्त्रायुधाः क्लान्तः शोणिताक्ततनुच्छदाः॥
en: Began to utter loud wails of distress afflicted with the fear of Bhimasena. Casting off their weapons and wearied with their armour besmeared with blood,

sn: प्रकीर्णमूर्धजा राजन् यक्षाधिपतिमब्रुवन्। गदापरिघनिस्त्रिंशतोमरप्रासयोधिनः॥ राक्षसा निहताः सर्वे तव देव पुरःसराः। प्रमृद्य तरसा शैलं मानुषेणधनेश्वर।॥ एकेन सहिताः सङ्घये रणे क्रोधवशा गणाः।। प्रवरा राक्षसेन्द्राणां यक्षाणां च नराधिप॥ शेरते निहता देव गतसत्त्वाः परासवः। लब्धशेषा वयं मुक्ता मणिमांस्ते सखा हतः॥
en: And with dishevelled hair, O king, (they) addressed the lord of the Yakshas thus, "O lord, all your foremost Rakshasas who fought with maces, swords, clubs, glances and barbed darts, have all been slaughtered. O lord of wealth, a single man crushing the mountain with great velocity have alone killed in battle all the Rakshasas of the Krodhavara clan and also the best of the Rakshasas and the Yakshas (who) lie senseless with life extinct; we only have been spared; your friend Maniman too has been killed.

sn: मानुषेण कृतं कर्म विधत्स्व यदनन्तरम्। स तच्छ्रुत्वा तु संक्रुद्धः सर्वयक्षगणाधिपः॥
en: All this has been done by one man. Do what you think proper now." Hearing all this, the king of all the Yakshas in great anger,

sn: कोपसंरक्तनयनः कथमित्यब्रवीद् वचः। द्वितीयमपराध्यन्तं भीमं श्रुत्वाधनेश्वरः॥
en: And with eyes reddened with ire, exclaimed "what.” And the Lord of wealth hearing of Bhima's second offence,

sn: चुक्रोध यक्षाधिपतिर्युज्यतामिति चाब्रवीत्। अथाभ्रघनसंकाशं गिरिशृङ्गमिवोच्छ्रितम्॥ रथं संयोजयामासुर्गन्धर्हममालिभिः। तस्य सर्वगुणोपेता विमलाक्षा हयोत्तमाः॥
en: Waxed wrath and then the king of the Yakshas said, "Yoke (the horses to the car)." Thereupon, (the attendants of Kubera) yoked to the car horses, wearing golden garlands, having the colour of dark clouds and high as a mountain summit. And those excellent horses of his, with clear eyes and endued with every noble quality.

sn: तेजोबलगुणोपेता नानारत्नविभूषिताः। शोभमाना रथे युक्तास्तरिष्यन्त इवाशुगाः॥
en: And possessed of energy and strength and decorated with various gems and having grand appearance, being yoked to the car, looked as if desirous of speeding like the wind,

sn: द्वेषयामासुरन्योन्यं हृषितैर्विजयावहैः। स तामस्थाय भगवान् राजराजो महारथम्॥ प्रययौ देवगन्धर्वैः स्तूयमानो महाद्युतिः। तं प्रयान्तं महात्मानं सर्वे यक्षाधनाधिपम्॥ रक्ताक्षा हेमसंकाशा महाकाया महाबलाः। सायुधा बद्धनिस्त्रिंशा यक्षा दशशतावराः॥
en: And began to send forth neighs at each other indicative of victory. (And) that resplendent and divine king of kings, ascending the mighty car and being eulogised by the celestials and the Gandharvas, set out. A thousand principal Yakshas, of reddened eyes, golden lustre and huge structure, possessed of vast strength and equipped with weapons and girding on their swords, followed the noble-minded lord of wealth and king of all the Yakshas.

sn: ते जवेन महावेगाः प्लवमाना विहायसा। गन्धमादनमाजग्मुः प्रकर्षन्त इवाम्बरम्॥
en: (And) they (the horses) of great swiftness ranging through the firmament with great speed reached the Gandhamadanas as if drawing forward the sky.

sn: तत् केसरिमहाजालंधनाधिपतिपालितम्। कुबेरं च महात्मानं यक्षरक्षोगणावृतम्॥ ददृशुर्हष्टरोमाणः पाण्डवाः प्रियदर्शनम्। कुबेरस्तु महासत्त्वान् पाण्डोः पुत्रान् महारथान्॥ आत्तकार्मुकनिस्त्रिंशान् दृष्ट्वा प्रीतोऽभवत् तदा। देवकार्यं चिकीर्षन् स हृदयेन तुतोष ह॥
en: The Pandavas then, with their hair standing on the end and with delight beheld that mighty array of horses maintained by the lord of wealth and also the noble-minded and graceful Kubera himself surrounded by the Yakshas and the Rakshasas. Kubera too, seeing those mighty car-warriors, the sons of Pandu, gifted with great strength and equipped with bows and swords, became pleased; and desirous of performing the task of the celestials was glad at heart.

sn: ते पक्षिण इवापेतुर्गिरिशृङ्ग महाजवाः। तस्थुस्तेषां समभ्याशेधनेश्वरपुरःसराः॥
en: They (the followers of Kubera) (then) alighted like birds on the summit of the mountain with great swiftness and with the lord of wealth at their head remained before them (the Pandavas).

sn: ततस्तं हृष्टमनसं पाण्डवान् प्रति भारत। समीक्ष्य यक्षगन्धर्वा निर्विकारमवस्थिताः॥
en: Then, O Bharata, the Yakshas and Rakshasas seeing that he (Kubera) was well pleased with the Pandavas stood there with indifferent.

sn: पाण्डवाश्च महात्मानः प्रणम्यधनदं प्रभुम्। नकुलः सहदेवश्चधर्मपुत्रश्चधर्मवित्॥ अपराद्धमिवात्मानं मन्यमाना महारथाः। तस्थुः प्राञ्जलयः सर्वे परिवार्यधनेश्वरम्॥
en: Then those mighty car-warriors, the highsouled Pandavas-Nakula, Sahadeva and the virtuous son of Dharma-having saluted that lord, the giver of wealth and having considered themselves as guilty, stood surrounding the lord of the wealth with joined hands.

sn: स ह्यासनवरं श्रीमत् पुष्पकं विश्वकर्मणा। विहितं चित्रपर्यन्तमातिष्ठतधनाधिपः॥
en: That illustrious one (Kubera) was seated on that excellent seat the Pushpaka painted with various colours.

sn: तमासीनं महाकायाः शङ्कुकर्णा महाजवाः। उपोपविविशुर्यक्षा राक्षसाश्च सहस्रशः॥ शतशश्चापि गन्धर्वास्तथैवाप्सरसां गणाः। परिवार्योपतिष्ठन्त यथा देवाः शतक्रतुम्॥
en: Thousands of Rakshasas and Yakshas of great fleetness and huge structure and having ears resembling javelins and hundreds of Gandharvas and Apsaras sat surrounding that one who seated the gods (sit surrounding the performer of hundred sacrifices (Indra).

sn: काञ्चनीं शिरसा बिभ्रद् भीमसेनः स्रजं शुभाम्। पाशखड्गधनुष्पाणिरुदैक्षतधनाधिपम्॥
en: Wearing an auspicious golden garland round his head and holding in his hands noose, sword and bow, Bhimasena began to look at the lord of wealth.

sn: भीमसेनस्य न ग्लानिर्विक्षतस्यापि राक्षसैः। आसीत् तस्यामवस्थायां कुबेरमपि पश्यतः॥
en: Bhimasena did not experience any depression of mind (either) on account of his being wounded by the Rakshasas (or) seeing Kubera in that state.

sn: आददानं शितान् बाणान् यो काममवस्थितम्। दृष्ट्वा भीमंधर्मसुतमब्रवीन्नरवाहनः॥
en: was as He that is carried on the shoulders of men seeing Bhima in a warlike attitudes and armed with sharpened arrows, addressed the son of Dharma thus,

sn: विदुस्त्वां सर्वभूतानि पार्थ भूतहिते रतम्। निर्भयश्चापि शैलाचे वस त्वं भ्रातृभिः सह॥
en: O Partha, all the creatures are aware that you are actively intent on the welfare of the whole creation. (Therefore) dwell on the summit of this mountain without fear.

sn: न च मन्युस्त्वया कार्यो भीमसेनस्य पाण्डव। कालेनैते हताः पूर्वं निमित्तमनुजस्त्व।॥
en: Nor, O Pandava, you ought to be angry with Bhimasena. They (the Rakshasas and Yakshas) were killed before by Destiny, your younger brother being merely the instrument.

sn: व्रीडा चात्र न कर्तव्या साहसं यदिदं कृतम्। दृष्टश्चापि सुरैः पूर्वं विनाशो यक्षरक्षसाम्॥
en: Nor you ought to be ashamed at his act of rashness. The destruction of the Yakshas and the Rakshasas had been fore ordained by the celestials.

sn: न भीमसेने कोपो मे प्रीतोऽस्मि भरतरर्षभ। कर्मणः भीमसेनस्य मम तुष्टिरभूत् पुरा॥
en: O the most exalted of the Bharatas, I am rather pleased than angry with Bhimasena-nay this act of Bhimasena has made me supremely happy.

sn: वैशम्पयान उवाच एवमुक्त्वा तु राजानं भीमसेनमभाषत। नैतन्मनसि मे तात वर्तते कुरुसत्तम॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having said to the king thus, (Kubera) spoke to Bhimasena, “O child, O the best of the Kurus, I do not (at all) mind it.

sn: यदिदं साहसं भीम कृष्णार्थे कृतवानसि। मामनादृत्य देवांश्च विनाशं यक्षरक्षसाम्॥ स्वबाहुबलमाश्रित्य तेनाहं प्रीतिमांस्त्वयि। शापादद्य विनिर्मुक्तो घोरदस्मि वृकोदर॥
en: O Bhima, if disregarding the gods and relying on your own strength of arms you have committed this act of rashness-the destruction of the Yakshas and the Rakshasas-for the sake of Draupadi, I am the more pleased with you for that. O Vrikodara, I have been this day delivered from a terrible curse.

sn: अहं पूर्वमगस्त्येन कुद्धेन परमर्षिणा। शप्तोऽपराधे कस्मिंश्चित् तस्यैषा निष्कृतिः कृता॥
en: Formerly I was cursed by the great sage Agastya in anger for some offence. You have freed me from it by this act (of yours).

sn: दृष्टो हि मम संक्लेशः पुरा पाण्डवनन्दन। न तवात्रापराधोऽस्ति कथंचिदपि पाण्डव॥
en: O son of Pandava, my disgrace was foreordained. O Pandava, no blame, therefore, in any way, can be attributed to you,

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच कथं शप्तोऽसि भगवन्नगस्त्येन महात्मना। श्रोतुमिच्छाम्यहं देव तवैतच्छापकारणम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said : O lord, what were you cursed by the nobleminded Agastya for? O God, I am desirous of hearing the cause of that imprecation.

sn: इदं चाश्चर्यभूतं मे यत् क्रोधात् तस्यधीमतः। तदैव त्वं न निर्दग्धः सबल: सपदानुगः॥
en: It seems wonder to me that you were not at that very moment consumed by the anger of that wise Agastya together with all your forces and attendants.

sn: धनेश्वर उवाच देवतानामभू-मन्त्रः कुशवत्यां नरेश्वर। वृतस्तत्राहमगमं महापद्मशतैस्त्रिभिः॥ यक्षाणां घोररूपाणां विविधायुधधारिणाम्। अध्वन्यहमथापश्यमगस्त्यमृषिसत्तमम्॥ उग्रं तपस्तप्यमानं यमुनातीरमाश्रितम्। नानापक्षिगणाकीर्णं पुष्पितद्रुमशोभितम्॥
en: The Lord of wealth said : O lord of men, once I was proceeding to Kushavati, where a Synod of the gods was being held, surrounded by three hundred Mahapadma terrible-looking Yakshas carrying various weapons. On my way, I beheld the most exalted of the sages Agastya practising rigid austerities on the banks of the Yamuna teeming with various birds and adorned with blossoming plants.

sn: तमूर्ध्वबाहुं दृष्टैव सूर्यस्याभिमुखे स्थितम्। तेजोराशिं दीप्यमानं हुताशनमिवैधितम्॥ राक्षसाधिपतिः श्रीमान् मणिमानाम मे सखा। मौदज्ञानभावाच्च दर्पान्मोहाच्च पार्थिव॥
en: Beholding that mass of lustre, blazing and bright as fire, with upraised arms facing the sun, my illustrious friend Maniman, the lord of the Rakshasas, who was ranging through the firmament, O lord of the earth, through stupidity, foolishness arrogance and ignorance.

sn: न्यष्ठीवदाकाशगतो महर्षेस्तस्य मूर्धनि। स कोपान्मामुवाचेदं दिशः सर्वा दहन्निव॥
en: Spat on the head of that great sage. He (Agastya) as if burning all the cardinal points with his anger,

sn: मामवज्ञाय दुष्टात्मा यस्मादेव सखा तव। धर्षणां कृतवानेतां पश्यतस्तेधनेश्वर॥
en: Said this 'O Lord of wealth, since your friend, this evil-minded one, despising me, has insulted me in your very presence,

sn: तस्मात् सहैभिः सैन्यैस्ते वधं प्राप्स्यति मानुषात्। त्वं चाप्येभिर्हतैः सैन्यैः क्लेशं प्राप्येह दुर्मतिः। तमेव मानुषं दृष्ट्वा किल्बिषाद् विप्रमोक्ष्यसे॥
en: He will, on that account, meet with his end together with his forces at the hands of a man. O evil-minded one, you too shall be sorely grieved at the death of your forces and shall be absolved from your sin on seeing that man.

sn: सैन्यानां तु तवैतेषां पुत्रपौत्रबलान्वितम्। न शापं प्राप्यते घोरं तत् तवाज्ञां करिष्यति॥
en: (But) this terrible curse shall not touch those powerful sons and grandsons of your forces, that will remain obedient to your commands.

sn: एष शापो मय प्राप्तः प्राक् तस्मादृषिसत्तमात्। स भीमेन महाराज भ्रात्रा तव विमोक्षितः॥
en: O king, I, who formerly received this imprecation from that most exalted of the Rishis, have been absolved from it by your brother Bhima.

sn: धनद उवाच युधिष्ठिरधृतिर्दाक्ष्यं देशकालपराक्रमाः। लोकतन्त्रविधानानामेष पञ्चविधो विधिः॥
en: The giver of wealth said : O Yudhishthira, steadiness, ability place and time-these four are the causes of success in human affairs,

sn: धृतिमन्तश्च दक्षाश्च स्वे स्वे कर्मणि भारत। पराक्रमविधानज्ञा नरा कृतयुगेऽभवन्॥
en: O Bharata, men of the Kriti Yuga (golden age) were steady and skilled in their own respective affairs and were well versed in the rules of prowess.

sn: धृतिमान् देशकालज्ञः सर्वधर्मविधानवित्। क्षत्रियः क्षत्रियश्रेष्ठ प्रशास्ति पृथिवी चिरम्॥
en: O the best of the Kshatriyas, a Kshatriya who has patience, who is well versed in (the rules of) time and place and who is well acquainted with the laws of all duties, can govern the world for a long time.

sn: य एवं वर्तते पार्थ पुरुषः सर्वकर्मसु। स लोके लभते वीर यशः प्रेत्य च सद्गतिम्॥
en: O Partha, the person who acts thus in all transaction obtains fame in this world and O hero, attains to an excellent state in the next.

sn: देशकालान्तरप्रेप्सुः कृत्वा शक्रः पराक्रमम्। सम्प्राप्तस्त्रिदिवे राज्यं वृत्रहा वसुभिः सह॥
en: Sakra, the slayer of Vitra, with the Vasus desirous of availing himself of the opportunity, of right time and place, obtained the kingdom of heaven by displaying his prowess.

sn: यस्तु केवलसंरम्भात् प्रपातं न निरीक्षते। पापात्मा पापबुद्धिर्यः पापमेवानुवर्तते॥
en: He who does not foresee his fall through anger and he who through wicked-mindedness and vicious tendency is addicted to sin,

sn: कर्मणामविभागज्ञः प्रेत्य चेह विनश्यति। अकालज्ञः सुदुर्मेधाः कार्याणामविशेषवित्॥ वृथाऽचारसमारम्भः प्रेत्य चेह विनश्यति। साहसे वर्तमानानां निकृतीनां दुरात्मनाम्॥ सर्वसामर्थ्यलिप्सूनां पापो भवति निश्चयः। अधर्मज्ञोऽवलिप्तश्च बालबुद्धिरमर्षणः॥ निर्भयो भीमसेनोऽयं तं शाधि पुरुषर्षभ। आर्टिषेणस्य राजर्षेः प्राप्य भूयस्त्वमाश्रमम्॥
en: And he who is not versed in the propriety relative to acts meet with destruction in this world and in the next. The efforts of that stupid person become futile who is not versed in the rules of time and acts and he meets with destruction in this world and in the next. Rash, deceitful and wicked-minded people who aim at masterdom of every kind, commit sin. This Bhimasena is unrighteous, arrogant, senseless as a child and fearless; therefore, O the best of the Bharatas, chastise him. Getting again to the hermitage of the royal sage Arstisena,

sn: तामिस्रं प्रथमं पक्षं वीतशोकभयो वस। अलकाः सह गन्धर्वैर्यक्षाश्च सह किन्नरैः॥
en: Dwell there without fear or anxiety during the first dark fortnight. The Gandharvas together with the inhabitants of the Alaka and the Kinnaras together with the Yakshas,

sn: मन्नियुक्ता मनुष्येन्द्र सर्वे च गिरिवासिनः। रक्षिष्यन्ति महाबाहो सहितं द्विजसत्तमैः॥
en: And all the dwellers of the mountain, O the best of men and mighty-armed one, being appointed by me will protect you as well as these best of the Brahmanas.

sn: साहसादनुसम्प्राप्तः प्रतिबुध्य वृकोदरः। वार्यतां साध्वयं राजंस्त्वयाधर्मभृतां वर॥
en: O king, O the best of the virtuous, O pure one, considering that Bhima has come here through rashness, do you check him. O king, henceforth creatures inhabiting this forest will always visit you, wait on you and protect you all.

sn: अतः परं च वो राजन् द्रक्ष्यन्ति वनगोचराः। उपस्थास्यन्ति वो राजन् रक्षिष्यन्ते च वः सदा॥ तथैव चान्नपानानि स्वादूनि च बहूनि च। आहरिष्यन्ति मत्प्रेष्याः सदा वः पुरुषर्षभाः॥
en: O the best of men, my attendants will always procure for you various eatables and drinkable. sweet to the taste.

sn: यथा जिष्णुर्महेन्द्रस्य यथा वायोवृकोदरः। धर्मस्य त्वं यथा तात योगोत्पन्नो निजः सुतः॥ आत्मजावात्मसम्पन्नौ यमौ चोभौ यथाश्विनोः। रक्ष्यास्तद्वन्ममापीह यूयं सर्वे युधिष्ठिर॥
en: As Vishnu (Arjuna) has a claim to the protection of Mahendra, Vrikodara of the wind god, you of Dharma and the powerful twins of the Ashvins, in virtue of being their respective offsprings, so, O Yudhishthira, you all have a claim to my protection.

sn: अर्थतत्त्वविधानज्ञः सर्वधर्मविधानवित्। भीमसेनादवरजः फाल्गुनः कुशली दिवि॥
en: Falguni the next by birth to Bhimasena, versed in the science of profit and acquainted with the principles of all duties, is all right in heaven.

sn: याः काश्चन मता लोके स्वाः परमसम्पदः। जन्मप्रभृति ताः सर्वाः स्थितास्तातधनंजये।॥
en: O child, those virtues which are considered in the world as leading to heaven, reside in Dhananjaya even from his very birth.

sn: दमो दानं बलं बुद्धिींकृतिस्तेज उत्तमम्। एतान्यपि महासत्त्वे स्थितान्यमिततेजसि॥
en: In that high-souled being of unrivalled energy reside all these (qualities) of selfcontrol, charity, strength, intelligence, modesty, patience and excellent energy.

sn: न मोहात् कुरुते जिष्णुः कर्म पाण्डव गर्हितम्। न पार्थस्य मृषोक्तानि कथयन्ति नरा नृषु॥
en: O Pandavas, Vishnu never commits any disgraceful act (even) through ignorance. And men never speak to their fellows of his ever having uttered lies.

sn: स देवपितृगन्धर्वैः कुरूणां कीर्तिवर्धनः। मानितः कुरुतेऽस्त्राणि शक्रसद्मनि भारत।॥
en: That augmenter of the glory of the Kurus, honoured by the Devas, Pitris and the Gandharvas, is learning the science of weapons in the abode of Sakra.

sn: योऽसौ सर्वान् महीपालान् धर्मेण वशमानयत्। स शान्तनुर्महातेजाः पितुस्तव पितामहः॥ प्रीयते पार्थ पार्थेन दिवि गाण्डीवधन्वना। सम्यक् चासौ महावीर्यः कुलधुर्येण पार्थिवः॥
en: O king, O Partha, he that reduced to subjection all the rulers of the earth with justice-that highly energetic and highly powerful Shantanu himself, the grandsire of your father-is in heaven fully pleased with Partha, the wielder of the Gandiva and the foremost of his race.

sn: पितॄन् देवानृषीन् विप्रान् पूजयित्वा महातपाः। सप्त मुख्यान् महामेधानाहरद् यमुनां प्रति॥
en: That one of fervid devotion, who having worshipped the Pitris, the Devas, the Rishi and the Brahmanas on the banks of the Yamuna, performed seven horse sacrifices,

sn: अधिराजः स राजंस्त्वां शान्तनुः प्रपितामहः। स्वर्गजिच्छक्रलोकस्थः कुशलं परिपृच्छति॥
en: Even that great emperor Shantanu, your great grandsire, who has conquered (i.e., got access to heaven is inquiring about your welfare, residing in the region of Sakra.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एतच्छ्रुत्वा तु वचनंधनदेन प्रभाषितम्। पाण्डवाश्च ततस्तेन बभूवुः सम्प्रहर्षिताः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : The Pandavas, having listened to these words spoken by the giver of wealth, were much pleased with them.

sn: ततः शक्तिं गदां खड्धनुश्च भरतर्षभः। प्राध्वं कृत्वा नमश्चक्रे कुबेराय वृकोदरः॥
en: Then Vrikodara-the most exalted of the Bharatas-lowering his club, mace sword and bow, saluted Kubera.

sn: ततोऽब्रवीद्धनाध्यक्षः शरण्यः शरणागतम्। मानहा भव शत्रूणां सुहृदां नन्दिवर्धनः॥
en: Thereupon seeing him crave his protection, the lord of wealth, capable of affording protection, said "be you the destroyer of the pride of (your) enemies and enhancer of the joy of (your) friends.

sn: स्वेषु वेश्मसु रम्येषु वसतामित्रतापनाः। काभान्न परिहास्यन्ति यक्षा वो भरतर्षभाः।॥
en: O the tormentors of foes, do you dwell in your own pleasant abode. O the most exalted of the Bharatas, the Yakshas will procure for you the articles desired by you.

sn: शीघ्रमेव गुडाकेशः कृतास्त्रः पुनरेष्यति। साक्षान्मघवता सृष्टः सम्प्राप्स्यतिधनंजयः॥
en: Having mastered the science of weapons Gudakesha will return soon, Dhananjaya, on being bidden farewell to by Maghavana himself, will meet with you.

sn: एवमुत्तमकर्माणमनुशिष्य युधिष्ठिरम्। श्वेतं गिरिवरश्रेष्ठं प्रययौ गुह्यकाधिपः॥
en: The lord of the Guhyakas having thus instructed Yudhishthira, disposed to good deeds, vanished from that excellent of mountains.

sn: तं परिस्तोमसंकीर्णैर्नानारत्नविभूषितैः। यानैरनुययुर्यक्षा राक्षसाश्च सहस्रशः॥
en: Thousands of Yakshas and Rakshasas followed him in conveyances covered with painted cushions and adorned with many gems.

sn: पक्षिणामिव निर्घोषः कुबेरसदनं प्रति। बभूव परमाश्वानामैरावतपथे यथा॥
en: As the excellent horses (swift) as birds proceeded towards the abode of Kubera a noise arose in the region of Indra.

sn: ते जग्मुस्तूर्णमाकाशंधनाधिपतिवाजिनः। प्रकर्षन्त इवाभ्राणि पिबन्त इव मारुतम्॥
en: The steeds of the lord of wealth careered along the firmament as if drawing forwards the sky and drinking the atmosphere.

sn: ततस्तानि शरीराणि गतसत्त्वानि रक्षसाम्। अपाकृष्यन्त शैलाचाद्धनाधिपतिशासनात्॥
en: Then the dead bodies of the Rakshasas were removed from the summit of the mountain by order of the lord of wealth.

sn: तेषां हि शापकालः स कृतोऽगस्त्येनधीमता। समरे निहतास्तस्माच्छापस्यान्तोऽभवत् तदा॥
en: As this period, was appointed by the intelligent Agastya as the limit of their curse, therefore they were absolved from (this) imprecation in being slain in battle.

sn: पाण्डवाश्च महात्मानस्तेषु वेश्मसु तां क्षपाम्। सुखमूषुर्गतोद्वेगा: पूजिताः सर्वराक्षसैः॥
en: The noble-minded Pandavas dwelt happily for several sights in those mansions without anxiety and honoured by all the Rakshasas,

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततः सूर्योदयेधौम्यः कृत्वाऽऽछिकमरिंदम्। आर्टिषेणेन सहितः पाण्डवानभ्यवर्तत॥
en: Then, O tormentor of foes, when the sun rose, Dhaumya, on performing his devotions, visited the Pandavas, with Arstisena.

sn: तेऽभिवाद्याष्टिषेणस्य पादौधौम्यस्य चैव ह। ततः प्राञ्जलयः सर्वे ब्राह्मणांस्तानपूजयन्॥
en: Having bowed down to the feet of Dhaumya and Arstisena, they then worshipped all the Brahmanas with joined hands.

sn: ततो युधिष्ठिरंधौम्यो गृहीत्वा दक्षिणे करे। प्राची दिशमभिप्रेक्ष्य महर्षिरिदमब्रवीत्॥
en: Then the great sage Dhaumya, taking Yudhishthira by the right hand and looking towards the East, said this:

sn: असौ सागरपर्यन्तां भूमिमावृत्य तिष्ठति। शैलराजो महाराज मन्दरोऽति विराजते॥
en: O Great king, covering the earth up to the sea reigns this Mandara, the prince of mountains.

sn: इन्द्रवैश्रवणावेतां दिशं पाण्डव रक्षतः। पर्वतैश्च वनान्तैश्च काननैश्चैव शोभिताम्॥
