en: O Pandava, this point, adorned with mountains, woods and forest, is protected by Indra and Vaisravana.

sn: एतदाहुर्महेन्द्रस्य राज्ञो वैश्रवणस्य च। ऋषयः सर्वधर्मज्ञाः सद्म तात मनीषिणः॥
en: O child, it is said by the intelligent sages, acquainted with all duties, that this (region) is the abode of Mahendra and of king Vaisravana.

sn: अतश्चोद्यन्तमादित्यमुपतिष्ठन्ति वै प्रजाः। ऋषयश्चापिधर्मज्ञाः सिद्धाः साध्याश्च देवताः॥
en: The twice-born ones and the righteous sages and the Siddhas and the Sadhyas and the celestials, worship the sun who rises from this point.

sn: यमस्तु राजाधर्मज्ञः सर्वप्राणभृतां प्रभुः। प्रेतसत्त्वगतिं ह्येनां दक्षिणामाश्रितो दिशम्॥
en: And that righteous king Yama, the lord of all living creatures, presides over yonder southern point, the path of the spirits of the departed.

sn: एतत् संयमनं पुण्यमतीवाद्भुतदर्शनम्। प्रेतराजस्य भवनमृद्ध्या परमया युतम्॥
en: This is Sanyamana, the abode of the lord of the departed souls, sacred, highly wonderful to look at and full of crowning bliss.

sn: यं प्राप्य सविता राजन् सत्येन प्रतितिष्ठति। अस्तं पर्वताराजानमेतमाहुर्मनीषिणः॥
en: The intelligent ones denominate that prince of mountains Ashta, getting to which Savita ever observed the truth.

sn: एतं पर्वतराजानं समुद्रं च महोदधिम्। आवसन् वरुणो राजा भूतानि परिरक्षति॥
en: Similarly, dwelling in this prince of mountains and the mighty sea, king Varuna protects all creatures.

sn: उदीची दीपयन्नेष दिशं तिष्ठति वीर्यवान्। महामेरुर्महाभाग शिवो ब्रह्मविदां गतिः॥
en: O highly fortunate one, illuminating the northern point, there stretches the powerful and auspicious (Mountains) Mahameru-the refuge to those holding communion with Brahma.

sn: यस्मिन् ब्रह्मसदश्चैव भूतात्मा चावतिष्ठते। प्रजापतिः सृजन् सर्वं यत् किञ्चिज्जङ्गमागमम्॥
en: There the court of Brahma is (held) and remaining where the universal soul Prajapati created all that is mobile and immobile.

sn: यानाहुर्ब्रह्मणः पुत्रान् मानसान् दक्षसप्तमान्। तेषामपि महामेरुः शिवं स्थानमनामयम्॥
en: (This) Mahameru is the auspicious and blissful abode of Daksha and six others who are known as the mind-born sons of Brahma.

sn: अत्रैव प्रतितिष्ठन्ति पुनरेवोदयन्ति च। सप्त देवर्षयस्तात वसिष्ठप्रमुखाः सदा॥
en: O child, here too the seven divine sages with Vasishtha at their head sit and rise again.

sn: देशं विरजसं पश्य मेरोः शिखरमुत्तमम्। यत्रात्मतृप्तरध्यास्ते देवैः सह पितामहः॥
en: Behold that excellent summit of the Meru that bright region when the grandsire (Brahma) sits with the gods, happy in self-knowledge.

sn: यमाहुः सर्वभूतानां प्रकृतेः प्रकृतिंध्रुवम्। अनादिनिधनं देवं प्रभुं नारायणं परम्॥ ब्रह्मणः सदनात् तस्य परं स्थान प्रकाशते। देवा अपि न पश्यन्ति सर्वतेजोमयं शुभम्॥
en: (And) next to the abode of Brahma appears the region of that original lord, the god Narayana who has neither beginning nor end and who is said to be the really first cause of the origin of the whole creation. Even the gods cannot behold that auspicious (place)) composed of all energies.

sn: अत्यर्कानलदीप्तं तत् स्थानं विष्णोर्महात्मनः। स्वयैव प्रभया राजन् दुष्प्रेक्ष्यं देवदानवैः॥
en: (And) by reason of its own splendour surpassing the sun or fire in lustre, the place of the high-souled Vishnu is not visible to the gods and the Danavas.

sn: प्राच्यां नारायणस्थानं मेरावतिविराजते। यत्र भूतेश्वरस्तात सर्वप्रकृतिरात्मभूः॥
en: The abode of Narayana lies resplendent to the East of the Meru where the lord of all creatures, the self-existent cause of the universe.

sn: भासयन् सर्वभूतानि सुश्रियाभिविराजते। नात्र ब्रह्मर्षयस्तात कुत एव महर्षयः॥ प्राप्नुवन्ति गतिं ह्येतां यतीनां भावितात्मनाम्। न तं ज्योतींषि सर्वाणि प्राप्य भासन्ति पाण्डव॥
en: Displaying all creatures, appears grand with excellent gracefulness. Even the Brahmarshis cannot have and admittance there; how can the Maharshis? O excellent of the Kurus, only Yatis can have access to it. Nor, O Pandava, can all the luminaries shine (by him).

sn: परेण तपसा युक्ता स्वयं प्रभुरचिन्त्यात्मा तत्र ह्यतिविराजते। यतयस्तत्र गच्छन्ति भक्त्या नारायणं हरिम्॥ भाविताः कर्मभिः शुभैः। योगसिद्धा महात्मानस्तमोमोहविवर्जिताः॥
en: Here the lord of incomprehensible soul reigns supreme. Here, on account of their souls being purified by pious deeds and devotion, the Yatis of rigid asceticism, approach Narayana (Hari). Those high-souled (beings) attaining to perfection by yoga and free from ignorance and pride,

sn: तत्र गत्वा पुनर्नेमं लोकमायान्ति भारत। स्वयम्भुवं महात्मानं देवदेवं सनातनम्॥
en: Repairing thither and attaining to the selfexistent, high-souled and eternal god of gods. O Bharata, do not come back to this world.

sn: स्थानमेतन्महाभागध्रुवमक्षयमव्ययम्। ईश्वरस्य सदा ह्येतत् प्रणमात्र युधिष्ठिर॥
en: O highly fortunate Yudhishthira, this place is eternal, without deterioration or end; because it is always the very life of that god.

sn: एनं त्वहरहर्मेसं सूर्याचन्द्रमसौध्रुवम्। प्रदक्षिणमुपावृत्य कुरुतः कुरुनन्दन।॥
en: O descendant of Kuru, the sun and the moon, through eternity, make their tour around this Meru every day.

sn: ज्योतींषि चाप्यशेषेण सर्वाण्यनघ सर्वतः। परियान्ति महाराज गिरिराजं प्रदक्षिणम्॥
en: O pure one, O great king, all the luminaries too turn round this prince of mountains in the self-same way.

sn: एतं ज्योतींषि सर्वाणि प्रकर्षन् भगवानपि। कुरुते वितमस्कर्मा आदित्योऽभिप्रदक्षिणम्॥
en: The god Aditya too, the dispeller of darkness, attracting all the luminaries, goes round this (Meru).

sn: अस्तं प्राप्य ततः संध्यामतिक्रम्य दिवाकरः। उदीची भजते काष्ठां दिशमेष विभावसुः॥
en: That author of the day, Vibhavasu, having gone down and then having passed the evening, takes the excellent northern point.

sn: पर्वसंधिषु। स मेरुमनुवृत्तः सन् पुनर्गच्छति पाण्डव। प्राङ्मुखः सविता देवः सर्वभूतहिते रतः॥
en: O Pandava, that god Savita, bent on the welfare of all creatures, then coming near the Meru, again goes on his course facing the East.

sn: स मासान् विभजन् काले बहुधा तथैव भगवान् सोमो नक्षत्रैः सह गच्छति॥
en: Similarly, the divine moon moves with the stars (round this mountain) dividing the mouth into many sections when he arrives at the Parvas.

sn: एवमेतं त्वतिक्रम्य महामेरुमतन्द्रितः। भावयन् सर्वभूतानि पुनर्गच्छति मन्दरम्॥
en: Thus crossing the Mahameru unerringly and nourishing all the creatures (the moon) goes back to the Mandara.

sn: तथा तमिस्रहा देवो मयूखैर्भावयञ्जगत्। मार्गमेतदसम्बाधमादित्यः परिवर्तते॥
en: In a similar way, the god Aditya, the dispeller of darkness displaying the universe by his rays, moves round this unobstructed path.

sn: सिसृक्षुः शिशिराण्येव दक्षिणां भजते दिशम्। ततः सर्वाणि भूतानि कालोऽभ्यर्च्छति शैशिरः॥
en: When he takes the southern direction with a view to cause dew, then the cold weather comes upon all the creatures.

sn: स्थावराणां च भूतानां जगमानां च तेजसा। तेजांसि समुपादत्ते निवृत्तः स विभावसुः॥
en: (Then) turning back, he, by his own energy, withdraws the energy from all beings both mobile and immobile.

sn: ततः स्वेदक्लमौ तन्द्री ग्लानिश्च भजते नरान्। प्राणिभिः सततं स्वपो ह्यभीक्ष्णं च निषेव्यते॥
en: In consequence of this perspiration, fatigue, drowsiness and lethargy comes upon men and all living beings always feel inclined to sleep.

sn: एवमेतदनिर्देश्यं मार्गमावृत्य भानुमान्। पुनः सृजति वर्षाणि भगवान् भावयन् प्रजाः॥
en: Then the god Bhanumana coursing that unknown path (i.e. the firmament) gives birth to rains reviving (all) creatures.

sn: वृष्टिमारुतसंतापैः सुखैः स्थावरजङ्गमान्। वर्धयन् सुमहातेजाः पुनः प्रतिनिवर्तते॥
en: And having nourished all (creatures) both mobile and immobile by the comfort caused by rain, wind and warmth, that one of mighty splendour resumes his (former) course.

sn: एवमेष चरन् पार्थ कालचक्रमतन्द्रितः। प्रकर्षन् सर्वभूतानि सविता परिवर्तते॥
en: Thus increasingly turning on the wheel of time and influencing all creatures, O Partha, Savita goes on his course.

sn: संतता गतिरेतस्य नैष तिष्ठति पाण्डव। आदायैव तु भूतानां तेजो विसृजते पुनः॥
en: O Pandava his course is unremitting and he never rests. And withdrawing the energy of (all) creatures, he gives it back.

sn: विभजन् सर्वभूतानामायुः कर्म च भारत। अहोरात्रं कलाः काष्ठाः सृजत्येष सदा विभुः॥
en: O Bharata, the lord (sun), always imparting life and motion to all living creatures, creates day and night, Kala and Kashtha.

description: Return of Arjuna in the Yaksha Yuddha
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तस्मिन् नगेन्द्रे वसतां तु तेषां महात्मनां सद्बतमास्थितानाम्। रतिः प्रमोदश्च बभूव तेषामाकाङ्क्षतां दर्शनमर्जुनस्य॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Those noble-minded (Pandavas), the observers of pious vows, desirous of beholding Arjuna dwelling in that best of mountains, became passionately attached (to it) and got themselves amused.

description: Return of Arjuna in the Yaksha Yuddha
sn: स्तेजस्विनः सत्यधृतिप्रधानान्। र्गन्धर्वसङ्घाश्च महर्षयश्च॥
en: Numerous Gandharvas and Maharshis gladly came to those powerful and energetic ones of chaste desires-(princes), the foremost of those gifted with truth and fortitude.

description: Return of Arjuna in the Yaksha Yuddha
sn: तं पादपैः पुष्पधरैरुपेतं नगोत्तमं प्राप्य महारथानाम्। मनःप्रसादः परमो बभूव यथा दिवं प्राप्य मरुद्गणानाम्॥
en: Getting to that excellent mountain, adorned with blossoming trees, those mighty carwarriors were supremely glad at heart as the Maruts on reaching the heavenly regions.

description: Return of Arjuna in the Yaksha Yuddha
sn: मयूरहंसस्वननादितानि पुष्पोपकीर्णानि महाचलस्य। शृङ्गाणि सानूनि च पश्यमाना गिरेः परं हर्षमवाप्य तस्थुः॥
en: Beholding the summit and the table-land of that mighty mountain, covered with flowers and ringing with the cries of peacocks and cranes, they remained there feeling great joy.

description: Return of Arjuna in the Yaksha Yuddha
sn: साक्षात् कुबेरेण कृताश्च तस्मिन् नगोत्तमे संवृतकूलरोधसः। कादम्बकारण्डवहंसजुष्टाः पद्माकुलाः पुष्करिणीरपश्यन्॥
en: On that excellent mountain they beheld tanks, excavated by Kubera himself, full of lotuses and frequented by Kadamvas, Karandavas and swans and with their banks covered with (trees).

description: Return of Arjuna in the Yaksha Yuddha
sn: क्रीडाप्रदेशांश्च समृद्धरूपान् सुचित्रमाल्यावृतजातशोभान्। मणिप्रकीर्णाश्च मनोरमांश्च यथा भवेयुर्धनदस्य राज्ञः॥
en: (They beheld also) magnificent sporting grounds, pleasant to the mind and covered with arrays of beautiful and variegated garlands and studded with gems and suited to the taste of the king (Kubera), the giver of wealth.

description: Return of Arjuna in the Yaksha Yuddha
sn: अनेकवर्णश्च सुगन्धिभिश्च महाद्रुमैः संततमभ्रजालैः। तपःप्रधानाः सततं चरन्तः शृङ्गं गिरेश्चिन्तयितुं न शेकुः॥
en: The best of ascetics, always wandering (there) could not (sufficiently) comprehended (the sublimity) of that mountain summit furnished as it was with various many-coloured trees and covered with masses of clouds.

description: Return of Arjuna in the Yaksha Yuddha
sn: स्वतेजसा तस्य नगोत्तमस्य महौषधीनां च तथा प्रभावात्। दहोनिशानां पुरुषप्रवी॥
en: O great hero, by reason of the splendour of this excellent mountain itself and of the brilliancy of the annual herbs there was no difference between day and night.

description: Return of Arjuna in the Yaksha Yuddha
sn: यमास्थितः स्थावरजङ्गमानि विभावसुर्भावयतेऽमितौजाः। स्तत्र स्थितास्ते ददृशुर्नृसिंहाः॥
en: Those best of men saw the rising and setting of Vibhavasu of unrivalled splendour, while, dwelling in that mountain, remaining where he (the sun) nourishes all the mobile and the immobile (creatures).

description: Return of Arjuna in the Yaksha Yuddha
sn: रवेस्तमिस्रागमनिर्गमांस्ते तथोदयं चास्तमनं च वीराः। समावृताः प्रेक्ष्य तमोनुदस्य गभस्तिजालैः प्रदिशो दिशश्च॥
en: Having witnessed the setting in and exit of darkness, the rising and the setting of the sun and all the cardinal points covered with his (sun's rays), those heroes,

description: Return of Arjuna in the Yaksha Yuddha
sn: स्वाध्यायवन्तः सततक्रियाश्च धर्मप्रधानाश्च शुचिव्रताश्च। सत्ये स्थितास्तस्य महारथस्य सत्यव्रतस्यागमनप्रतीक्षाः॥
en: Awaiting the arrival of that mighty carwarrior, firm in truth and of true vows, were engaged in reciting the Vedas, constantly practising rituals, chiefly discharging the religious duties and observing pure vows.

description: Return of Arjuna in the Yaksha Yuddha
sn: इहैव हर्षोऽस्तु समागतानां क्षिप्रं कृतास्त्रेणधनंजयेन। इति ब्रुवन्तः परमाशिषस्ते पार्थास्तपोयोगपरा बभूवुः॥
en: Saying "let all those assembled experience joy by meeting speedily here with Arjuna skilled in arms," those highly blessed Parthas became absorbed in Yoga.

description: Return of Arjuna in the Yaksha Yuddha
sn: दृष्ट्वा विचित्राणि गिरौ वनानि किरीटिनं चिन्तयतामभीक्ष्णम्। बभूव रात्रिदिवसश्च तेषां संवत्सरेणैव समानरूपः॥
en: Inspite of beholding many romantic forests on the mountain, as they could not help constantly thinking of Arjuna, every day and night appeared to them (long) as a year.

description: Return of Arjuna in the Yaksha Yuddha
sn: यदैवधौम्यानुमते महात्मा कृत्वा जटां प्रव्रजित: स जिष्णुः। तदैव तेषां न बभूव हर्षः कुतो रतिस्तद्गतमानसानाम्॥
en: From that very moment when the nobleminded Vishnu, with Dhaumya's leave, matting his hair, went abroad, they (Pandavas) did not experience joy. How could they, lost in his thought, experience any happiness there (on that mountain however romantic it might be)?

description: Return of Arjuna in the Yaksha Yuddha
sn: भ्रातुर्नियोगात् तु युधिष्ठिरस्य वनादसौ वारणमत्तगामी। स्तदैव ते शोकहता बभूवुः॥
en: Since the very moment when in accordance with the command of his brother Yudhishthira, Vishnu, endowed with the gait of an elephant (with exuberance of spirits), left the forest Kamyaka they became buried in deep sorrow.

description: Return of Arjuna in the Yaksha Yuddha
sn: मस्त्रार्थिनं वासवमभ्युपेतम्।। स्तस्मिन् नगे भारत भारतानाम्॥
en: O Bharata, in this way the Bharatas passed a month with great difficulty on that mountain thinking of Sitasvha Arjuna, who had gone to Vasava, desirous of learning the (science of) arims.

description: Return of Arjuna in the Yaksha Yuddha
sn: उषित्वा पञ्च वर्षाणि सहस्राक्षनिवेशने। अवाप्य दिव्यान्यस्त्राणि सर्वाणि विबुधेश्वरात्॥
en: (On the other hand) dwelling five years in the abode of the thousand-cyed (Indra) and from that lord of the celestials obtaining all the heavenly weapons,

description: Return of Arjuna in the Yaksha Yuddha
sn: आग्नेयं वारुणं सौम्यं वायव्यपथ वैष्णवम्। ऐन्द्रं पाशुपतं ब्राह्मं पारमेष्ठ्यं प्रजापतेः॥
en: (Namely) those of Agni, Varuna, Soma, Bhrigu, Vishnu, Indra, Pashupati, Brahma, Parameshthi, Prajapati,

description: Return of Arjuna in the Yaksha Yuddha
sn: यमस्यधातुः सवितुस्त्वष्टुर्वैश्रवणस्य च। तानि प्राप्य सहस्राक्षादभिवाद्य शतक्रतुम्॥
en: Yama, Dhata, Savita, Tashta and Vaisravana and getting these weapons, paying homage to the performer of hundred sacrifices.

description: Return of Arjuna in the Yaksha Yuddha
sn: अनुज्ञातस्तदा तेन कृत्वा चापि प्रदक्षिणम्। आगच्छदर्जुनः प्रीतः प्रहृष्टो गन्धमादनम्॥
en: And going round him, Arjuna with his permission, returned Gandhamadana delighted and fully pleased.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततः कदाचिद्धरिसम्प्रयुक्तं महेन्द्रवाहं सहसोपयातम्। विद्युत्प्रभं प्रेक्ष्य महारथानां हर्षोऽर्जुनं चिन्तयतां बभूव॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Once upon a time, when those mighty carwarriors were thinking of Arjuna they were delighted at beholding the car of Mahendra, yoked with horses and bright as lightning ¡ approaching all on a sudden.

sn: स दीप्यमानः सहसान्तरिक्षं प्रकाशयन् मातलिसंगृहीतः। बभौ महोल्केव घनान्तरस्था शिखेव चाग्नेर्खलिता विधूमा॥
en: That flaming car, driven by Matali, suddenly illuminating the firmament, appeared like a mighty meteor hidden in clouds or like the smokeless and blazing tongues of fire.

sn: तमास्थित: संददृशे किरीटी स्रग्वीनवान्याभरणानि बिभ्रत्। धनंजयो वज्रधरप्रभावः श्रिया ज्वलन् पर्वतमाजगाम॥
en: Placed in that car, appeared Kirita wearing garlands and fresh ornaments (Then) Dhananjaya, powerful as the wielder of the thunderbolt and blazing of beauty, alighted on (that) mountain,

sn: स शैलमासाद्य किरीटमाली महेन्द्रवाहादवरुह्य तस्मात्। नजातशत्रोस्तदनन्तरं च॥
en: Arriving at the mountain and descending from the car of Mahendra, that intelligent, one wearing a coronet and garlands, saluted the feet of Dhaumya first and then those of Ajatshatru Yudhishthira.

sn: वृकोदरस्यापि च वन्द्यपादौ माद्रीसुताभ्यामभिवादितश्च। समेत्य कृष्णां परिसान्त्व्य चैनां प्रह्वोऽभवद् भ्रातुरुपह्वरे सः॥
en: He (Arjuna) also bowed down to the feet of Vrikodara and was himself saluted by the (twin) sons of Madri. (And then) going to Krishna and consoling her, he stood before his brother (Yudhishthira) with humility.

sn: बभूव तेषां स्तेनाप्रमेयेण समागतानाम्। स चापि तान् प्रेक्ष्य किरीटमाली ननन्द राजानमभिप्रशंसन्॥
en: Those present (there) were highly delighted at being joined with that peerless man (Arjuna). (And) beholding them he (Arjuna) too, who wore a coronet and garlands, was delighted and began to eulogise the king.

sn: यमास्थितः सप्त जघान पूगान् दितेः सुतानां नमुचेनिहन्ता। तमिन्द्रवाहं समुपेत्य पार्था: प्रदक्षिणं चक्रुरदीनसत्त्वाः॥
en: Beholding that car of Indra, placed in which the slayer of Namuchi had destroyed seven battalions of Diti's sons, those Parthas with rich spirits, went round it.

sn: ते मातलेश्चक्रुरतीव हृष्टाः सत्कारमवयं सुरराजतुल्यम्। सर्वान् यथावच्च दिवौकसस्ते पप्रच्छुरेनं कुरुराजपुत्राः॥
en: Those descendants of the king Kuru, being exceedingly delighted, paid excellent adoration to Matali, worthy of the lord of the celestials himself; and then duly inquired of him about the welfare of all the gods,

sn: तानप्यसौ मातलिरभ्यनन्दत् पितेव पुत्राननुशिष्य पार्थान्। ययौ रथेनाप्रतिमप्रभेण पुनः सकाशं त्रिदिवेश्वरस्य॥
en: Matali too then greeted them and having instructed the Parthas as a father does his (own) sons, (he) returned to the lord of heaven, ascending that car of unrivalled splendour.

sn: गते तु तस्मिन् नरदेववर्यः शक्रात्मजः शक्ररिपुप्रमाथी। शक्रेण दत्तानि ददौ महात्मा महाधनान्युत्तमरूपवन्ति॥ दिवाकराभाणि विभूषणानि प्रियः प्रियायै सुतसोममात्रे। ततः स तेषां कुरुपुङ्गवानां तेषां च सूर्याग्निसमप्रभाणाम्॥ विप्रर्षभाणामुपविश्य मध्ये सर्वं यथावत् कथयांबभूवा एवं मयास्त्राण्युपशिक्षितानि शक्राच्च वाताच्च शिवाच्च साक्षात्॥
en: He (Matali) having departed; that foremost of the royal race-the slayer of all the foes-the noble-minded son of Sakra, made over to his sweet-heart-the mother of Sutashoma-those beautiful and precious gems and ornaments of sun-like splendour presented by Sakra. Then sitting amidst those best of the Kurus and those Brahmanas having the lustre of the sun or fire, he (Arjuna), narrated (to them) faithfully all that happened (to him in heaven). "In this way, I have learnt the (science of) arms from Sakra, Vayu and Shiva himself;

sn: तथैव शीलेन समाधिनाथ प्रीताः सुरा मे सहिताः सहेन्द्राः। संक्षेपतो वै स विशुद्धकर्मा तेभ्यः समाख्याय दिवि प्रवासम्॥ माद्रीसुताभ्यां सहितः किरीटी सुष्वाप तामावसतिं प्रतीतः॥
en: And have pleased all the gods together with Indra by humility and concentration." Having in short related to them to his stay in heaven, Kirita of pure deeds slept pleasantly that night with the sons of Madri."

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततो रजन्यां वयुष्टायांधर्मराज युधिष्ठिरम्। भ्रातृभिः सहितः सर्वैरवन्दतधनंजयः॥
en: Vaishampayana said: Then when the night came to a close Dhananjaya, with all his brothers, saluted Dharmaraja Yudhishthira.

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: एतस्मिन्नेव काले सर्ववादित्रनिःस्वनः। बभूव तुमुल: शब्दस्त्वन्तरिक्षे दिवौकसाम्॥
en: At this time there arose in the firmament tremendous and dreadful sounds of all the musical instruments of the gods;

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: रथनेमिस्वनश्चैव घण्टाशब्दश्च भारत। पृथग् व्यालमृगाणां च पक्षिणामिव सर्वशः॥
en: Such and O Bharata, as the rattling sounds of the car-wheels and thc ringing of bells. (In consequence of which) all the beasts of prey, fo the deer and the birds gave forth their own peculiar cries.

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: ते समन्तादनुययुर्गन्धर्वाप्सरसां गणाः। विमानैः सूर्यसंकाशैर्देवराजमरिंदमम्॥
en: Ascending cars of sun-like splendour, multitudes of Gandharvas and Apsaras followed from all directions the king of the gods, the tormentor of foes.

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: ततः स हरिभिर्युक्तं जाम्बूनदपरिष्कृतम्। मेघनादिनमारुह्य श्रिया परमया ज्वलन्॥ पार्थानभ्याजगामाथ देवराजः पुरंदरः। आगत्य च सहस्राक्षो स्थादवरुरोह वै॥
en: Then Purandara, the king of the gods, blazing in transcendental beauty and ascending a car, yoked with horses, varnished with gold and roaring like clouds, set out (to meet) the Parthas. Arriving (there) he of hundred eyes got down from the car.

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: तं दृष्ट्वैव महात्मानंधर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः। भ्रातृभिः सहितः श्रीमान् देवराजमुपागमत्॥
en: No sooner had Dharmaraja Yudhishthira beheld that high-souled one, than he approached the prosperous lord of the gods together with his brothers.

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: पूजयामास चैवाथ विधिवद् भूरिदक्षिणः। यथार्हममितात्मानं विधिदृष्टेन कर्मणा॥
en: And that generous one (Yudhishthira) duly worshipped (Indra) of immeasurable soul as befitting his dignity having strict regard to proper forin.

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: धनंजयश्च तेजस्वी प्रणिपत्य पुरंदरम्। भृत्यवत् प्रणतस्तस्थौ देवराजसमीपतः॥
en: (And) the energetic Dhananjaya having saluted Purandara, stood before the king of the gods, like a servant with humility.

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: आप्यायत महातेजाः कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः। धनंजयमभिप्रेक्ष्य विनीत स्थितमन्तिके॥ जटिलं देवराजस्य तपोयुक्तमकल्मषम्। हर्षेण महताऽऽविष्टः फाल्गुनस्याथ दर्शनात्॥ बभूव परमप्रीतो देवराजं च पूजयन्। तं तथादीनमनसं राजानं हर्षसम्लुतम्॥ सर्वाणि मत्तः उवाच वचनंधीमान् देवराजः पुरंदरः। त्वमिमां पृथिवीं राजन् प्रशासिष्यसि पाण्डव। स्वस्ति प्राप्नुहि कौन्तेय काम्यकं पुनराश्रमम्॥
en: Yudhishthira, the highly energetic son of Kunti seeing, that sinless and devotional Dhananjaya, bearing clotted hair, stand before the king of the gods in humility and smelling (his head), was lost in great joy, at the sight of Falguni and was exceedingly glad at worshipping the lord of the celestials. Then the intelligent king of the gods, Purandara addressed the noble-minded and exceedingly joyful king (Yudhishthira) thus, saying, “O king, O Pandava, you shall govern the earth. Let prosperity attend three, O son of Kunti, Do you return to Kamyaka.

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: अस्त्राणि लब्धानि च पाण्डवेन प्रयतेन राजन्। कृतप्रियश्चास्मिधनंजयेन जेतुं न शक्यस्त्रिभिरेष लोकैः॥
en: O king, Pandava Dhananjaya has obtained all the weapons from me and has also performed deeds pleasing to me; (therefore) no one in the three worlds is capable of subduing him."

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: एवमुक्त्वा सहस्राक्षः कुन्तीपुत्रं युधिष्ठिरम्। जगाम त्रिदिवं हृष्टः स्तूयमानो महर्षिभिः॥
en: Addressing Yudhishthira, the son of Kunti, thus and being worshipped by the Maharshis, the hundred eyed (Indra) left for heaven with delight.

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: धनेश्वरगृहस्थानां पाण्डवानां समागमम्। शक्रेण य इदं विद्वानधीयीत् समाहितः॥ संवत्सरं ब्रह्मचारी नियतः संशितव्रतः। स जीवेद्धि निराबाधः स सुखी शरदां शतम्॥
en: That learned being, who, for a year observing Brahmacharya and checking his passions and observing vows, peruses with close attention the meeting of the Pandava, residing in the abode of the lord of wealth with Sakra, lives a hundred years free from all disturbances and in great bliss.

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच यथागतं गते शक्रे भ्रातृभिः सह सङ्गतः। कृष्णया चैव बीभत्सुर्धर्मपुत्रमपूजयत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Sakra having left for his own abode. Vivatsu together with (his) brothers and Krishna paid homage to the son of Dharma.

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: अभिवादयमानं तं मूर्युपाघ्राय पाण्डवम्। हर्षगद्गदया वाचा प्रहृष्टोऽर्जुनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Having smelt the head of the Pandava Arjuna who was bowing down to him, (the son of Dharma), highly glad, addressed (him) in words, broken on account of joy, thus

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: कथमर्जुन कालोऽयं स्वर्गे व्यतिगतस्तव। कथं चास्त्राण्यवाप्तानि देवराजश्च तोषितः॥
en: "O Arjuna, how have you spent this period in heaven? And how have you obtained the weapons and pleased the king of the gods?

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: सम्यग् वा ते गृहीतानि कच्चिदस्त्राणि पाण्डव। कच्चित् सुराधिपः प्रीतो रुद्रो वास्त्राण्यदाद् तव॥
en: O Pandava, have you thoroughly secured the weapons? Have the king of the gods and Rudra cheerfully given you the weapons?

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: यथा दृष्टश्च ते शक्रो भगवान् वा पिनाकधृक्। यथैवास्त्राण्यवाप्तानि यथैवाराधितश्च ते॥
en: How did you see the divine Sakra and the wielder of the Pinaka (Shiva) and how did you obtain the weapons and how did you worship (them),

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: यथोक्तवांस्त्वां भगवान् शतक्रतुररिंदम। कृतप्रियस्त्वयास्मीति तस्य ते किं प्रियं कृतम्॥
en: And what good service you rendered to that tormentor of foes the worshipful performer of hundred sacrifices that he said "I have been pleased with you,”

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: एतदिच्छाम्यहं श्रोतुं विस्तरेण महाद्युते। यथा तुष्टो महादेवो देवराजस्तथानघ॥
en: All this, O you of brilliant lustre, I am desirous of hearing in detail. O pure one, how Mahadeva and the king of the gods were pleased (with you).

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: यच्चापि वज्रपाणेस्तु प्रियं कृतमरिंदम। एतदाख्याहि मे सर्वमखिलेनधनंजय॥
en: What good (service) you rendered to the wielder of the thunderbolt-the tormentor of foes, O Dhananjaya, relate to me (all) this fully"

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: अर्जुन उवाच शृणु हन्त महाराज विधिना येन दृष्टवान्। शतक्रतुमहं देवं भगवन्तं च शङ्करम्॥
en: Arjuna rcplied Listen, O great king, in what manner I beheld the divine performer of hundred sacrifices and worshipful Shankara.

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: विद्यामधीत्य तां राजस्त्वयोक्तामरिमर्दन। भवता च समादिष्टस्तपसे प्रस्थितो वनम्॥
en: O destroyer of foes, having studied that (branch of) learning as directed by you, I repaired to the forest at your command for practicing asceticism.

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: भृगुतुङ्गमथो गत्वा काम्यकादास्थितस्तपः। एकरात्रोषितः कञ्चिदपश्यं ब्राह्मणं पथि॥
en: Having repaired from Kamyaktua Brigutunga and having spent there one night in practicing asceticism I met a Brahmana on the way.

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: स मामपृच्छत् कौन्तेय क्वासि गन्ता ब्रवीहि मे। तस्मा अवितथं सर्वमब्रुवं कुरुनन्दन॥
en: He asked me 'O son of Kunti, tell me where you will go' O son of Kuru, thereupon, I related to him everything faithfully.

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: स तथ्यं मम तच्छ्रुत्वा ब्राह्मणो राजसत्तम। अपूजयत मां राजन् प्रीतिमांश्चाभवन्मयि॥
en: O best of kings, hearing me narrate faithfully (everything) that Brahmana became well disposed towards me and, O king, greeted me.

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: ततो मामब्रवीत् प्रीतस्तप आतिष्ठ भारत। तपस्वी नचिरेण त्वं द्रक्ष्यसे विबुधाधिपम्॥
en: And being pleased, he said to me "practice asceticism. By asceticism you will soon behold the lord of the gods.'

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: ततोऽहं वचनात् तस्य गिरिमारुह्य शैशिरम्। तपोऽतप्यं महाराज मासं मूलफलाशनः॥
en: Then, following his instructions I ascended the mountain Saisira (Himalayas) and began to practice asceticism, living on fruits and roots in the (first) month.

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: द्वितीयश्चापि मे मासो जलं भक्षयतो गतः। निराहारस्तृतीयेऽथ मासे पाण्डवनन्दन॥
en: (And), O son of Pandu, I spent the second month living on water only and in the third I ate nothing at all.

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: अर्श्वबाहुश्चतुर्थं तु मासमस्मि स्थितस्तदा। न च मे हीयते प्राणस्तदद्भुतमिवाभवत्॥
en: In the fourth month I remained with upraised arms; and it is a wonder that my strength did not diminish.

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: पञ्चमे त्वथ सम्प्राप्ते प्रथमे दिवसे गते। वराहसंस्थितं भूतं मत्समीपं समागमत्॥
en: And when the first day of the fifth month had passed away, there appeared before me a being having the appearance of a boar,

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: निघ्नन् प्रोथेन पृथिवीं विलिखंचरणैरपि। सम्मार्जञ्जठरेणोर्वी विवर्तश्च मुहुर्मुहुः॥
en: Ploughing the earth with his mouth, striking (it) with his feet, rubbing the ground with his belly and roving constantly to and fro in a frightful manner.

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: अनु तस्यापरं भूतं महत् कैरातसंस्थितम्। धनुर्बाणासिमत् प्राप्तं स्त्रीगणानुगतं तदा॥
en: He was followed by another great being, in the shape of a hunter, armed with bow, arrows and sword and accompanied by females.

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: ततोऽहंधनुरादाय तथाक्षय्ये महेषुधी। अताडयं शरेणाथ तद् भूतं लोमहर्षणम्॥
en: Then, taking up my bow and two inexhaustible quivers, I pierced that creature, causing the hair stand on the end, with an arrow.

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: युगपत् तं किरातस्तु विकृष्य बलवद्धनुः। अभ्याजने दृढतरं कम्पयत्रिव मे मनः॥
en: The hunter too, drawing his strong bow simultaneously (with me), wounded him more efficiently, as if making my mind tremble.

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: स तु मामब्रवीद् राजन् मम पूर्वपरिग्रहः। मृगयाधर्ममुत्सृज्य किमर्थं ताडितस्त्वया॥
en: And he said to me, O King, "why have you, disregarding the rules of hunting aimed at the animal first struck by me?

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: एष ते निशितैर्बाणैर्दप॑ हन्मि स्थिरो भव। सधनुष्मान् महाकायस्ततो मामभ्यभाषत॥
en: Stay (awhile), I will destroy your pride with these sharpened arrows." Then that hugebodied being taking up his bow rushed against me.

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: ततो गिरिमिवात्यर्थमावृणोन्मां महाशरैः। तं चाहं शरवर्षेण महता समवाकिरम्॥
en: He then cnveloped me entirely with mighty arrows (just) as a mountain (is covered with a mighty shower). I too, surrounded him with a mighty shower of shafts.

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: ततः शरैर्दीप्तमुखैर्यन्त्रितैरनुमन्त्रितैः। प्रत्यविध्यमहं तं तु वजैरिव शिलोच्चयम्॥
en: Then I pierced him with steady arrows of blazing points and inspired with mantras (just) as a mountain is pierced by a thunderbolt.

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: तस्य तच्छतधा रूपमभवच्च सहस्रधा। तानि चास्य शरीराणि शरैरहमताडयम्॥
en: Thereupon his body became multiplied a hundred and a thousand times. (But) I pierced all his bodies with arrows.

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: पुनस्तानि शरीराणि एकीभूतानि भारत। अदृश्यन्त महाराज तान्यहं व्यधमं पुनः॥
en: Again, O Bharata, O great king, seeing that all his bodies became merged into one, 1 struck at it a second time.

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: अणुवृहच्छिरा भूत्वा बृहच्चाणुशिराः पुनः। एकीभूतस्तदा राजन् सोऽभ्यवर्तत मां युधि॥
en: He now assumed a diminutive body with large head and then a large body with a small head. And again assuming his former shape, he came before me to fight.

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: यदाभिभवितुं बाणैर्न च शक्नोमि तं रणे। ततो महास्त्रमातिष्ठं वायव्यं भरतर्षभ॥
en: When, O most exalted of the Bharatas, I could not crush him with arrows in the combat, I aimed (at him) the mighty weapon presided over by the wind god.

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: न चैनमशकं हन्तुं तदद्भुतमिवाभवत्। तस्मिन् प्रतिहते चास्त्रे विस्मयो मे महानभूत्॥
en: (But) it was a wonder (to me) that I could not hurt him (even with that). And when that weapon produced no effect I was lost in great wonder.

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: भूय एव महाराज सविशेषमहं ततः। अस्त्रपूगेन महता रणे भूतमवाकिरम्॥
en: Again O king, with a vigorous effort I covered him, in that encounter, with numerous mighty weapons.

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: स्थूणाकर्णभयो जालं शरवर्षमथोल्बणम्। शलभास्त्रमश्मवर्ष समास्थायाहमभ्ययाम्॥
en: I then discharged at him. Sthunakarna, Varuna, Saravarsa, Ulvana, Salava and Asmavarsa weapons.

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: जग्रास प्रसभं तानि सर्वाण्यस्त्राणि मे नृप। तेषु सर्वेषु जग्धेषु ब्रह्मास्त्रं महदादिशम्॥
en: But, O king, he instantly devoured all those weapons discharged by me. And when all those had been swallowed up, I aimed (at him) the weapon presided over by Brahma.

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: ततः प्रज्वलितैर्बाणैः सर्वतः सोपचीयते। उपचीयमानश्च मया महास्त्रेण व्यवर्धत।॥
en: He was then completely covered with flaming arrows (issuing from that weapon) and when thus covered with that mighty weapon his body began to expand.

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: तत: संतापिता लोका मत्प्रसूतेन तेजसा। क्षणेन हि दिशः खं च सर्वतो हि विदीपितम्॥
en: Then on account of the energy of that weapon discharged by me, all the world became oppressed and all the points and the firmament became suddenly illuminated.

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: तदप्यस्त्रं महातेजाः क्षणेनैव व्यशातयत्। ब्रह्मास्त्रे तु हते राजन् भयं मां महदाविशत्॥
en: (But) that highly-energetic being instantly baffled even that weapon. And, O king, that weapon presided over by Brahma being destroyed, I was seized with a terrible fear.

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: ततोऽहंधनुरादाय तथाक्षय्ये महेषुधी। सहसाभ्यहनं भूतं तान्यप्यस्त्राण्यभक्षयत्॥
en: Thereupon instantly taking up my bow and the inexhaustible quivers, I aimed at him, (but) that being devoured those weapons also.

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: हतेष्वस्त्रेषु सर्वेषु भक्षितेष्वायुधेषु च। मम तस्य च भूतस्य बाहुयुद्धमवर्तत॥
en: All the weapons being (thus) baffled and devoured, that being and myself became engaged in a wrestling.

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: व्यायाम मुष्टिभिः कृत्वा तलैरपि समागतैः। अपारयंश्च तद् भूतं निश्चेष्टमगमं महीम्॥
en: At first we dealt blows and then gave slaps; but unable to crush him, I (at last) fell down on the ground deprived of sensation.

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: ततः प्रहस्य तद् भूतं तत्रैवान्तरधीयत। सह स्त्रीभिर्महाराज पश्यतो मेऽद्धृतोपमम्॥
en: Then, O great king, that being, giving forth a laugh, vanished with the women even at that very spot. And this struck me with wonder.

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: एवं कृत्वा स भगवांस्ततोऽन्यद् रूपमास्थितः। दिव्यमेव महाराज वसानोऽद्भुतमम्बरम्॥
en: That divine being, having done this great king, appeared in another divine form, wearing a wonderful garment.

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: हित्वा किरातरूपं च भगवांस्त्रिदशेश्वरः। स्वरूपं दिव्यमास्थाय तस्थौ तत्र महेश्वरः॥
en: (Then) that divine lord of the gods, Maheshvara, giving up the from of hunter, ance.

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: अदृश्यत ततः साक्षाद् भगवान् गोवृषध्वजः। उमासहायो व्यालधृग् बहुरूपः पिनाकधूक्॥
en: (Then) that very divine being, the wielder of the Pinaka, capable of assuming many shapes, having the bull for his emblem and bearing serpents, appeared before me with Uma.

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: स मामभ्येत्य समरे तथैवाभिमुखं स्थितम्। शूलपाणिरथोवाच तुष्टोऽस्मीति परंतप॥
en: He with the trident in his hand, coming up to me and seeing me ready for fight, O tormentor of foes, said "I am pleased (with you)."

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: ततस्तद्धनुरादाय तूणौ चाक्षय्यसायको। प्रादान्ममैव भगवान्धारयस्वेति चाव्रवीत्॥
en: Then, holding (my) bow and the two arrowcase furnished with inexhaustible shafts, that divine one returned them to me saying "crave some boon.

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: तुष्टोऽस्मि तव कौन्तेय ब्रूहि किं करवाणि ते। यत् ते मनोगतं वीर तद् ब्रूहि वितराम्यहम्॥
en: O son of Kunti, I am pleased (with you). Say what I shall do for you. Tell me, O hero, what is your wish. I will fulfill it.

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: अमरत्वमपाहाय ब्रूहि यत् ते मनोगतम्। ततः प्राञ्जलिरेदाहमस्त्रेषु गतमानसः॥
en: Tell me what it is that you cherish in your mind if it be not immortality." Thereupon with joined hands and with my mind bent on obtaining weapons,

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: प्रणम्य मनसा शर्वं ततो वचनमाददे। भगवान् मे प्रसन्नश्चेदीप्सितोऽयं वरो मम॥
en: And adòring him inwardly, I said these words “O god, if you are pleased with me, I crave this boon, (viz.).

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: अस्त्राणीच्छाम्यहं ज्ञातुं यानि देवेषु कानिचित्। ददानीत्येव भगवानब्रवीत् त्र्यम्बकश्च माम्॥
en: I am to have a knowledge of all the weapons presided over by the gods.” Then the god, Traymbaka, said to me" I will give (them).

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: रौद्रमस्त्रं मदीयं त्वामुपस्थास्यति पाण्डव। प्रददौ च मम प्रीत: सोऽस्त्रं पाशुपतं महत्॥
en: O Pandava, my own weapon, Rudra, shall ever be present to you.” (And) being satisfied (with me) he granted that mighty weapon, Pashupatha.

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: उवाच च महादेवो दत्त्वा मेऽस्त्रं सनातनम्। न प्रयोज्यं भवेदेतन्मानुषेषु कथञ्चन॥
en: Having bestowed upon me that eternal weapon, Mahadeva said “this (weapon) shall by no means be discharged against men.

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: जगद् विनिर्दहेदेवमल्पतेजसि पातितम्। पीड्यमानेन बलवत् प्रयोज्यं स्याद्धनंजय॥
en: If hurled at a being of small energy it will burn up the universe. This powerful weapon can be discharged only when you will be hard pressed.

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: अस्त्राणां प्रतिघाते च सर्वथैव प्रयोजयेत्। तदप्रतिहतं दिव्यं सर्वास्त्रप्रतिषेधनम्॥
en: This celestials weapon, as baffling all the weapons, can at all times be discharged in order to ward off other weapons.

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: मूर्तिमन्मे स्थितं पार्श्वे प्रसन्ने गोवृषध्वजे। उत्सादनममित्राणां परसेनानिकर्तनम्॥
en: The god Vrishadhvaja (one having the bull for his emblem) being thus pleased, there remained manifest by my side that (weapon) capable of annihilating enemies and destroying the hostile forces,

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: दुरासदं दुष्प्रसह सुरदानवराक्षसैः। अनुज्ञातस्त्वहं तेन तत्रैव समुपाविशम्॥
en: Unrivalled and difficult to be endured by the gods, the Danavas and the Rakshasas. Commanded by him, I then sat down there,

description: The colloquy between Arjuna and Yudhishthira
sn: प्रेक्षतश्चैव मे देवस्तत्रैवान्तरधीयत॥
en: (And) in my very sight he disappeared at that very spot.

sn: अर्जुन उवाच ततस्तामवसं प्रीतो रजनीं तत्र भारत। प्रसादाद् देवदेवस्य त्र्यम्बकस्य महात्मनः॥
en: Arjuna said : Then, O Bharata, by the favour of that highsouled god of gods-Tryambaka-I pleasantly passed that night there.

sn: व्युषितो रजनीं चाहं कृत्वा पौर्वाहिणकीः क्रियाः। अपश्यं तं द्विजश्रेष्ठं दृष्टवानस्मि यं पुरा॥
en: Having performed my morning devotions when the night drew to a close, I beheld that best of the Brahmanas whom I had previously seen. see

sn: तस्मै चाहं यथावृत्तं सर्वमेव न्यवेदयम्। भगवन्तं महादेवं समेतोऽस्मीति भारत॥
en: I related to him faithfully all that occurred, namely, O Bharata, my interview with the divine Mahadev.

sn: स मामुवाच राजेन्द्र प्रीयमाणो द्विजोत्तमः। दृष्टस्त्वया महादेवो यथा नान्येन केनचित्॥
en: O king of kings, that best of the Brahmanas said to me pleased "none else can Mahadeva as you have seen.

sn: समेत्य लोकपालैस्तु सर्वैर्वैवस्वतादिभिः। द्रष्टास्यनघ देवेन्द्रं स च तेऽस्त्राणि दास्यति॥
en: O sinless being, you will behold the lord of the celestials, together with Vaivasvata and all the Lokapalas, who (the lord of the celestials) will grant you weapons.

sn: एवमुक्त्वा स मां राजन्नाश्लिष्य च पुनः पुनः अगच्छत् स यथाकामं ब्राह्मण: सूर्यसंनिभः॥
en: O king, saying this and embracing me again and again, that sun-like Brahmana went away whither he liked.

sn: अथापराह्ने तस्याह्नः प्रावात् पुण्यः समीरणः। पुनर्नवमिमं लोकं कुर्वन्निव सपत्नहन्।॥
en: Then, O destroyer of foes, in the afternoon of that day, it pure brceze began to blow, as if making this world anew.

sn: दिव्यानि चैव माल्यानि सुगन्धीनि नवानि च। शैशिरस्य गिरेः पादे प्रादुरासन् समीपतः॥
en: (And) at the foot of the mountain Himalayas, fragrant, fresh and fair flowers began to blossomi near and around me.

sn: वादित्राणि च दिव्यानि सुघोराणि समन्ततः। स्तुतयश्चेन्द्रसंयुक्ता अश्रूयन्त मनोहराः॥
en: (And) there was heard from all sides, celestials and sweet symphony together with charming eulogy to Indra.

sn: गणाश्चाप्सरसां तत्र गन्धर्वाणां तथैव च। पुरस्ताद् देवदेवस्य जगुर्गीतानि सर्वशः॥
en: Multitudes of Gandharvas and Apsaras chanted various songs before the god of gods.

sn: मरुतां च गणास्तत्र देवयानैरुपागमन्। महेन्द्रानुचरा ये च ये च सद्मनिवासिनः॥
en: And the whole body of the Marutas, the followers of Mahendra and all the inhabitants of the heavenly regions appeared there on celestials cars.

sn: ततो मरुत्वान् हरिभिर्युक्तैर्वाहैः स्वलङ्कतैः। शची सहायस्तत्रायात् सह सर्वैस्तदामरैः॥
en: Then Marutvana, accompanied by Sachi and all the immortals, appeared there in ornamental cars drawn by horses.

sn: एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु कुबेरो नरवाहनः। दर्शयामास मां राजॅल्लक्ष्म्या परमया युतः॥
en: And, at the very moment, O king, Kubera, of transcendental beauty who is carried on the shoulders of men, came to my presence.

sn: दक्षिणस्यां दिशि यमं प्रत्यपश्यं व्यवस्थितम्। वरुणं देवराजं च यथास्थानमवस्थितम्॥
en: (And) I beheld Yama seated towards the southern point and the king of the gods and Varuna in their respective places.

sn: ते मामूचुर्महाराज सान्त्वयित्वा नरर्षभ। सव्यसाचिन् निरीक्षास्मॉल्लोकपालानवस्थितान्॥
en: Having cheered me up, O great king, O best of mortals, they said to me, “O Savyasachi, behold us the Lokapalas seated (here).

sn: सुरकार्यार्थसिद्ध्यर्थं दृष्टवानसि शङ्करम्। अस्मत्तोऽपि गृहाण त्वमस्त्राणीति समन्ततः॥
en: You have beheld Mahadeva in order to perform the task in behalf of the celestials. Now, receive the weapons from us seated around.

sn: ततोऽहं प्रयतो भूत्वा प्रणिपत्य सुरर्षभान्। प्रत्यगृहणं तदास्त्राणि महान्ति विधिवद् विभो॥
en: Thereupon, O lord bowing down to those best of the celestials and with a pure heart I duly accepted those powerful weapons.

sn: गृहीतास्त्रस्ततो देवैरनुज्ञातोऽस्मि भारत। अथ देवा ययुः सर्वे यथागतमरिदम॥
en: O Bharata, having accepted the weapons I was recognized by the gods (as one of them). And then, O tormentor of foes, all the gods returned to their respective places.

sn: मघवानपि देवेशो रथमारुह्य सुप्रभम। उवाच भगवान् स्वर्गं गन्तव्यं फाल्गुन त्वया॥
en: And the lord king of the gods-Maghavana too, having ascended his splendid car, said "O Falguni, you will have to visit the celestials regions.

sn: पुरैवागमनादस्माद् वेदाहं त्वांधनंजय। अतः परं त्वहं वै त्वां दर्शये भरतर्षभ॥
en: O Dhananjaya, even before my arrival here I had known you (would come). After this, O best of the Bharatas, I will reveal myself to you (in heaven).

sn: त्वया हि तीर्थेषु पुरा समाप्लावः कृतोऽसकृत्। तपश्चेदं महत् तप्तं स्वर्ग गन्तासि पाण्डव॥
en: O Pandava, as you formerly performed ablutions in various Tirthas (i.e. sacred places resorted to by pilgrims) and were absorbed in rigid asceticism, you will be able to go to heaven.

sn: भूयश्चैव च तप्तव्यं तपश्चरणमुत्तमम्। स्वर्गं त्ववश्यं गन्तव्यं त्वया शत्रुनिषूदन॥
en: O destroyer of foes, you will have to practise severe austerities again, for O Pandava, you will surely have to stay in heaven (now in this mortal frame).

sn: मातलिमन्नियोगात् त्वां त्रिदिवं प्रापयिष्यति। विदितस्त्वं हि देवानां मुनीनां च महात्मनाम्।२३॥
en: At my command Matali will take you to heaven, You are already known to the celestials and the high-souled sages.'

sn: इहस्थः पाण्डवश्रेष्ठ तपः कुर्वन् सुदुष्करम्। ततोऽहमब्रुवं शक्रं प्रसीद भगवन् मम। आचार्यं वरयेयं त्वामस्त्रार्थं त्रिदशेश्वर।॥
en: Thereupon I said to Sakra, “be favourably disposed towards me. In order to learn (the science of) weapons, O lord of heaven, I make you my preceptor."

sn: इन्द्र उवाच क्रूरकर्मास्त्रवित् तात भविष्यसि परंतप। यदर्थमस्त्राणीप्सुस्त्वं तं काम पाण्डवाप्नुहि॥
en: Indra said: O tormentor of foes, O child, you will achieve terrible feats (of arms). And that desire of yours which makes you eager to obtain weapons shall be fulfilled.

sn: ततोऽहमब्रुवं नाहं दिव्यान्यस्त्राणि शत्रुहन्। मानुषेषु प्रयोक्ष्यामि विनास्त्रप्रतिघातनात्॥
en: Thereupon I replied, "O destroyer of foes, I will never hurt these celestials weapons at mortals except to ward off their weapons.

sn: तानि दिव्यानि मेऽस्त्राणि प्रयच्छ विबुधाधिप। लोकांश्चास्त्रजितान् पश्चाल्लभेयं सुरपुड़व॥
en: Therefore, O lord of the gods, O best of the celestials, grant me those celestials weapons. Then I shall afterwards attain to the region of the warriors."

sn: इन्द्र उवाच परीक्षार्थं मयैतत् ते वाक्यमुक्तंधनंजय। ममात्मजस्य वचनं सूपपन्नमिदं तव॥
en: Indra said : "O Dhananjaya, in order to test you I have said these words. You being my son, this speech is worthy of you.

sn: शिक्ष मे भवनं गत्वा सर्वाण्यस्त्राणि भारत। वायोरग्नेर्वसुभ्योऽपि वरुणात् समरुद्गणात्॥
en: Repairing to my abode, O Bharata, learn all the weapons of Vayu, of Agni, of the Vasus, of Varuna of the Marutas,

sn: साध्यं पैतामहं चैव गन्धर्वोरंगरक्षसाम्। वैष्णवानि च सर्वाणि नैर्ऋतानि तथैव च॥
en: Of the Sadhyas, of Pitamaha, of the Gandharvas, of the Uragas, of the Rakshasas, of Vishnu and of the Nairitas;

sn: मद्गतानि च जानीहि सर्वास्त्राणि कुरूद्वह। एवमुक्त्वा तु मां शक्रस्तत्रैवान्तरधीयत॥
en: And, Operpetuator of the Kuru race, all those weapons are presided over by me." Addressing me thus, Sakra vanished at that very spot.

sn: अथापश्यं हरियुतं रथमैन्द्रमुपस्थितम्। दिव्यं मायामयं पुण्यं यत्तं मातलिना नृप।॥
en: Then, O king, I saw that sacred, celestials and wonderful and car of Indra, yoked with horses and driven by Matali arrive (there).

sn: लोकपालेषु यातेषु मामुवाचाथ मातलिः। द्रष्टुमिच्छति शक्रस्त्वां देवराजो महायुते॥
en: The Lokapalas having gone away, Matali said to me “O you of unrivalled splendour, the lord of the celestials, Sakra, wishes to see you.

sn: संसिद्ध्यस्व महाबाहो कुरु कार्यमनन्तरम्। पश्य पुण्यकृताँल्लोकान् सशरीरो दिवं व्रज॥
en: O creation of powerful arms, acquire perfection first and then perform your task. Behold the regions of the virtuous and repair to heaven even in the (mortal) frame.

sn: देवराजः सहस्राक्षस्त्वां दिदृक्षति भारत। इत्युक्तोऽहं मातलिना गिरिममामन्त्र्य शैशिरम्॥
en: O Bharata, the thousand-eyed king of the gods is desirous of seeing you.” Thus addressed by Matali and greeting the mountain Himalaya,

sn: प्रदक्षिणमुपावृत्य समारोहं रथोत्तमम्। चोदयामास स हयान् मनोमारुतहंसः॥ मातलिहयतत्त्वज्ञो यथावद् भूरिदक्षिण: अवैक्षत च मे वर्क स्थितस्याथ स सारथिः॥ तथा भ्रान्ते रथे राजन् विस्मितश्चेदमब्रवीत्। अत्यद्भुतमिदं त्वद्य विचित्रं प्रतिभाति मे॥
en: And going round it, I ascended that excellent car. And the exceedingly generous Matali, expert in horse-flesh, properly drove the horses fleet as the mind or the wind. (And)o king that charioteer, seeing that I was steadily seated in the car in motion, looked at my face and being lost in wonder said, “Today it appears to me highly wonderful and unprecedented,

sn: यदास्थितो रथं दिव्यं पदान चलितः पदम्। देवराजोऽपि हि मया नित्यमत्रोपलक्षितः॥ विचलन् प्रथमोत्पाते हयानां भरतर्षभ। त्वं पुनः स्थित एवात्र रथे भ्रान्ते कुरूद्वह॥
en: That placed in this celestials car you are not jerked even a step from your seat. O best of the Bharatas, I have often noticed that (even) the king of the gods is unable to keep up his balance at the first pull by the horses. O perpetuator of the Kuru race, your sitting (steadily) in the car while in motion,

sn: अतिशक्रमिदं सर्वं तवेति प्रतिभाति मे। इत्युक्त्वाऽऽकाशमाविश्य मातलिर्विबुधालयान्॥ दर्शयामास मे राजन् विमानानि च भारत। स रथो हरिभिर्युक्तो अ॒र्ध्वमाचक्रमे ततः॥
en: Appears to me that this power of yours has surpassed even that of Sakra himself." O king, O Bharata, saying this and soaring up to the celestials regions, Matali showed to me the abodes and palaces of the celestials. Then that car yoked with horses soared upwards.

sn: ऋषयो देवताश्चैव पूजयन्ति नरोत्तम। ततः कामगमॉल्लोकानपश्यं वै सुरर्षिणाम्॥ गन्धर्वाप्सरसां चैव प्रभावममितौजसाम्। नन्दनादीनि देवानां वनान्युपवनानि च॥ दर्शयामास मे शीघ्रं मातलिः शक्रसारथिः। ततः शक्रस्य भवनमपश्यममरावतीम्॥
en: (And) O the best of mortals, the sages and the gods began to pay their adorations to it. Then I beheld the regions moving at will and the splendour of the highly energetic divine sages, of the Gandharvas and of the Apsaras. (And) the charioteer of Indra, Matali, soon showed to me the garden of Nandana and other gardens and bowers of the celestials. Then I beheld the palace of Indra, Amravati,

sn: दिव्यैः कामफलैर्वृक्ष रत्नैश्च समलङ्कृताम्। न तत्र सूर्यस्तपति न शीतोष्णे न च क्लमः॥ न बाधते तत्र रजस्तत्रास्ति न जरा नृप। न तत्र शोको दैन्यं वा दौर्बल्यं चोपलक्ष्यते॥ दिवौकसां महाराज न ग्लानिररिमर्दन। न क्रोधलोभौ तत्रास्तां सुरादीनां विशाम्पते॥
en: Gracefully adorned with jewels and celestials trees yielding all sorts of fruits that are desired. There the sun does not shed heat, nor is there any one oppressed with cold, heat or fatigue. And O king there is no senility. O great king, O grinder of foes, nor are the celestials seen there (to be affected with) grief, poverty of spirit, weakness or lassitude. Nor, O lord of the world, there the celestials and others have anger or covetousness.

sn: नित्यतुष्टाश्च ते राजन् प्राणिनः सुरवेश्मनि। नित्यपुष्पफलास्तत्र पादपा हरितच्छदाः॥
en: O king, in the abodes of the celestials all beings are always cheerful. There the trees are always covered with green leaves and fruits and flowers,

sn: पुष्करिण्यश्च विविधाः पद्मसौगन्धिकायुताः। शीतस्तत्र ववौ वायुः सुगन्धी जीवनः शुचिः॥
en: And the lakes are adorned with fragrant lotuses. The breeze is there cool, pleasant, fragrant, pure and invigorating.

sn: सर्वरत्नविचित्रा च भूमिः पुष्पबिभूषिता। मृगद्विजाश्च बहवो रुचिरा मधुरस्वरा:॥
en: (There) the ground is variegated with all sorts of gems and decked with flowers. Various beautiful beasts, birds of sweet voice,

sn: विमानगामिनश्चात्र दृश्यन्ते बहवोऽम्बरे। ततोऽपश्यं वसून् रुद्रान् साध्यांश्च समरुद्गणान्॥
en: And numerous rangers of the sky are to be seen in the air. I then, beheld the Vasus, the Rudras, the Saddhyas, the Marutas,

sn: आदित्यानश्चिनौ चैव तान् सर्वान् प्रत्यपूजयम्। ते मां वीर्येण यशसा तेजसा च बलेन च॥ अस्त्रैश्चाप्यन्वजानन्त संग्रामे विजयेन च। प्रविश्य तां पुरीं दिव्यां देवगन्धर्वपूजिताम्॥
en: The Adityas Adityas and the Ashvins and worshipped them all. They uttered benedictions for my strength, renown, energy prowess, (skill in) aims and victory in battle. Entering that delightful city, adored by the gods and the Gandharvas,

sn: देवराजं सहस्राक्षमुपातिष्ठं कृताञ्जलिः। ददावर्धासनं प्रीतः शक्रो मे ददतां वरः॥
en: I stood before the hundred-eyed king of the gods with joined hands. And Sakra, the best of the liberal-handed, gladly offered to me half his seat.

sn: बहुमानाच्च गात्राणि पस्पर्श मम वासवः। तत्राहं देवगन्धर्वैः सहितो भूरिदक्षिण॥
en: Honouring me greatly Vasava ached my body. There with the generous-hearted gods and the Gandharvas.

sn: अस्त्रार्थमवसं स्वर्गे शिक्षाणोऽस्त्राणि भारत। विश्वावसोश्च वै पुत्रश्चित्रसेनोऽभवत् सखा॥
en: I began, O Bharata, to dwell in heaven desirous of obtaining arms and engaged in the study of the science of weapons. (And) Chitrasena, the son of Visvavasu, became my friend.

sn: स च गान्धर्वमखिलं ग्राहयामास मां नृप। तत्राहमवसं राजन् गृहीतास्त्रः सुपूजितः॥ सुखं शक्रस्य भवने सर्वकामसमन्वितः। शृण्वन् वै गीतशब्दं च तूर्यशब्दं च पुष्कलम्। पश्यंश्चाप्सरसः श्रेष्ठा नृत्यन्तीर्भरतर्षभ॥
en: It was he who taught me that entire science (of arms) known to the Gandharvas, Othe best of the Bharatas, there in the abode of Sakra I began to live happily, duly honoured, acquiring weapons, with my desires gratified, hearing songs and the clear sounds of musical instruments and witnessing the dance of the best of the Apsaras.

sn: तत् सर्वमनवज्ञाय तथ्यं विज्ञाय भारत। अत्यर्थं प्रतिगृह्याहमस्त्रेष्वेव व्यवस्थितः॥
en: O Bharata, without despising those fine arts which I learnt properly, I specially devoted my attention to the acquisition of arms.

sn: ततोऽतुष्यत् सजस्राक्षस्तेन कामेन मे विभुः। एवं मे वसतो राजन्नेष कालोऽत्यगाद् दिवि॥
en: Thereupon, that thousand-eyed lord was pleased with that desire of mine. O king, thus dwelling in heaven I have passed this period.

sn: कृतास्त्रमतिविश्वस्तमथ मां हरिवाहनः। संस्पृश्य मूर्ध्नि पाणिभ्यामिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: When I was skilled in weapons and gained his confidence, that one, who is borne by horses, touching my head with his hands, said these words:

sn: न त्वमद्य युधा जेतुं शक्यः सुरगणैरपि। किं पुनर्मानुषे लोके मानुषैरकृतात्मभिः॥
en: "Not to speak of men of imperfect minds dwelling on earth, even the gods are not now capable of conquering you.

sn: अप्रमेयोऽप्रधृष्यश्च युद्धेष्वप्रतिमस्तथा। अजेयस्त्वं हि संग्रामे सर्वैरपि सुरासुरैः। अथाब्रवीत् पुनर्देवः सम्प्रहृष्टतनूरुहः॥
en: You are incomprehensible in strength, irrepressible and also incomparable in fight.” Then with the hair of his body standing erect he said again,

sn: अस्त्रयुद्धे समो वीर न ते कश्चिद् भविष्यति। अप्रमत्तः सदा दक्षः सत्यवादी जितेन्द्रियः॥
en: "No one shall be equal to you in fighting with weapons who are always vigilant, dexterous, truthful, self-controlled,

sn: ब्रह्मण्यश्चास्त्रविच्चासि शूरश्चासि कुरूद्वह। अस्त्राणि समवाप्तानि त्वया दश च पञ्च च॥
en: Protector of the Brahmana, skilled in arms and brave, O perpetuator of the Kurus. You have obtained five and ten weapons,

sn: पञ्चभिर्विधिभिः पार्थ विद्यते न त्वया समः। प्रयोगमुपसंहारमावृत्तिं चधनंजय॥
en: Together with the five methods of using (them). O Partha, (Therefore) you have no equal, O Dhananjaya; you have also learnt the methods of their discharge, withdrawal, frequent re-discharge and re-withdrawal,

sn: प्रायश्चित्तं च वेत्थ त्वं प्रतीघातं च सर्वशः। ततो गुर्वर्थकालोऽयं समुत्पन्नः परंतप॥
en: And the revival of harmless beings burnt by the fire of weapons and the revival of the weapons (themselves) when baffled by those of the enemies. Now, O tormentor of foes the time has arrived for paying your preceptor's fees.

sn: प्रतिजानीष्व तं कर्तुं ततो वेत्स्याम्यहं परम्। ततोऽहमब्रुवं राजन् देवराजमिदं वचः॥
en: Promise to pay it and then I shall tell you what you will have to do.” Thereupon, O king I said to the king of the gods these words:

sn: विषह्यं यन्मया कर्तुं कृतमेव निबोध तत्। ततो मामब्रवीद् राजन् प्रहसन् बलवृत्रहा॥
en: “If it be in my power to perform the task then consider it as already performed.” Then, O king, the slayer of Vitra said to me smiling:

sn: नाविषह्यं तवाद्यास्ति त्रिषु लोकेषु किंचन। निवातकवचा नाम दानवा मम शत्रवः॥
en: "There is nothing in these three worlds that cannot be achieved by you. My enemies, the Danavas styled Nivatakavachas,

sn: समुद्रकुक्षिमाश्रित्य दुर्गे प्रतिवसन्त्युत। तिस्रः कोट्य: समाख्यातास्तुल्यरूपबलप्रभाः॥
en: Taking refugee in the womb of the ocean, dwell in forts. They are thirty millions in number and are all equal in structure, prowess and splendour.

sn: तांस्तत्र जहि कौन्तेय गुर्वर्थस्ते भविष्यति। ततो मातलिसंयुक्तं मयूरसमरोमभिः॥ हयैरुपेतं प्रादान्मे रथं दिव्यं महाप्रभम्। बबन्ध चैव मे मूर्ध्नि किरीटमिदमुत्तमम्॥
en: O son of Kunti, destroy them there (and) that will be your preceptor's fee.” Then he gave me that splendid celestials car driven by Matali and yoked with horse furnished with hair beautiful as the feather of peacocks. (And) he set upon my head this excellent coronet.

sn: स्वरूपसदृशं चैव प्रादादङ्गविभूषणम्। अभेद्यं कवचं चेदं स्पर्शरूपवदुत्तमम्॥
en: Gave me ornaments for my person worthy of his own body and this impenetrable excellent armour of pleasurable feel,

sn: अजरां ज्यामिमां चापि गाण्डीवे समयोजयत्। ततः प्रायामहं तेन स्यन्दनेन विराजता॥
en: And strung the Gandiva with this strong chord. I then set out ascending that splendid car,

sn: येनाजयद् देवपतिर्बलिं वैरोचनि पुरा। ततो देवाः सर्व एव तेन घोषेण बोधिताः॥
en: Riding which, in days of yore the king of the gods conquered Bali, the son of Virochana. Then all the gods, being aroused by the sound of that car,

sn: मेऽनघाः। मन्वाना देवराजं मां समाजग्मुर्विशाम्पते। दृष्ट्वा च मामपृच्छन्त किं करिष्यसि फाल्गुन॥
en: And mistaking me for the king of the gods, O lord of the earth, approached me. (But) having beheld me they asked “O Falguni, what will you do?"

sn: तानब्रुवं यथाभूतमिदं कर्तास्मि संयुगे। निवातकवचानां तु प्रस्थितं मां वधैषिणम्॥ निबोधत महाभागाः शिवं चाशास्त ततो वाग्भिः प्रशस्ताभिस्त्रिदशाः पृथिवीपते। तुष्टुवुर्मी प्रसन्नास्ते यथा देवं पुरंदरम्॥
en: I related to them exactly what had passed and said "I will do this in battle, O sinless ones, O highly fortunate beings; know I have set out with the desire of slaying the Nivalakavachas and bless me for my success.” (And) being pleased, they paid their adoration to me as to the god, Purandara.

sn: रथेनानेन मघवा जितवान् शम्बरं युधि। नमुचिं बलवृत्रौ च प्रह्लादनरकावपि॥
en: (And said): “ascending this car, Maghavana had conquered in battle, Samvara, Namuchi, Vritra, Bala, Prahrada and Naraka.

sn: बहूनि च सहस्राणि प्रयुतान्यर्बुदान्यपि। रथेनानेन दैत्यानां जितवान् मघवा युधि॥
en: And riding on this car also Maghavana had conquered in battle several thousands and millions and hundreds of millions of Daityas.

sn: त्वमप्यनेन कौन्तेय निवातकवचान् रणे। विजेता युधि विक्रम्य पुरेव मघवा वशी॥
en: You too, O son of Kunti, mounted on this (car) shall, displaying your prowess, obtain victory over the Nivatakavachas in fight as of yore the self-contained Maghavana did.

sn: अयं च शङ्खप्रवरो येन जेतासि दानवान्। अनेन विजिता लोकाः शक्रेणापि महात्मना।1८४॥
en: Here is that excellent conch by which you will conquer the Danavas. By (the help of) it, the high-souled Sakra conquered the worlds.

sn: प्रदीयमानं देवैस्तं देवदत्तं जलोद्भवम्। प्रत्यगृहणं जयायैनं स्तूयमानस्तदामरैः॥
en: And then the gods presented to me this shell, Devadatta, having its origin in the sea. I too accepted it for victory. Then the immortals began to eulogise me.

sn: स शडी कवची बाणी प्रगृहीतशरासनः। दानवालयमत्युग्रं प्रयातोऽस्मि युयुत्सया॥
en: Desirous of fighting, I then set out for the terrible abode of the Danavas equipped with conch, armour and bow."

description: The commencement of the fight with the Nivatakavachas
sn: अर्जुन उवाच ततोऽहं स्तूयमानस्तु तत्र तत्र महर्षिभिः। अपश्यमुदधिं भीममपां पतिमथाव्ययम्॥
en: Arjuna said ; Then praised by the great sages here and there, I (at length) beheld the dreadful oceanthe inexhaustible lord of waters.

description: The commencement of the fight with the Nivatakavachas
sn: फेनवत्यः प्रकीर्णाश्च संहताश्च समुत्थिताः। ऊर्मयश्चात्र दृश्यन्ते वल्गन्त इव पर्वताः॥
en: (And) on it were visible, foamy and swelling waves scattered all over, dashing against each other and looking like moving rocks.

description: The commencement of the fight with the Nivatakavachas
sn: नावः सहस्रशस्तत्र रत्नपूर्णाः समन्ततः। नभसीव विमानानि विचरन्त्यो विरेजिरे। तिमिङ्गिलाः कच्छपाश्च तथा तिमितिमिड्गिलाः॥
en: Ships full of gems were seen on it all around. Timingilas, tortoises, Timitimingilas,

description: The commencement of the fight with the Nivatakavachas
sn: मकराश्चात्र दृश्यन्ते जले मग्ना इवाद्रयः। शङ्खानां च सहस्राणि मग्नान्यप्सु समन्ततः॥
en: And Makaras were seen here like submarine reefs. Thousands of submerged shells lying all around.

description: The commencement of the fight with the Nivatakavachas
sn: दृश्यन्ते स्म यथा रात्रौ तारास्तन्वभ्रसंवृताः। तथा सहस्रशस्तत्र रत्नसङ्घाः प्लवन्त्युत॥
en: Looked like stars on a night covered with light clouds. Thousands of gems were floating in heaps.

description: The commencement of the fight with the Nivatakavachas
sn: वायुश्च घूर्णते भीमस्तदद्भुतमिवाभवत्। तमुदीक्ष्य महावेगं सर्वाम्भोनिधिमुत्तमम्॥ अपश्यं दानवाकीर्णं तद् दैत्यपुरमन्तिकात्। तत्रैव मातलिस्तूर्णं निपत्य पृथिवीतले।॥
en: And a dreadful wind was sweeping over it in whirls, which appeared wonderful to me. Behoiding that excellent lord of all waters with strong tides I saw very near, the city of the Daiytas full of the Danavas. There soon entering into the nether world, Matali,

description: The commencement of the fight with the Nivatakavachas
sn: रथं तं तु समाश्लिष्य प्राद्रवद् रथयोगवित्। त्रासयन् रथघोषेण तत् पुरं समुपाद्रवत्॥
en: Expert in driving the car and sitting steadily on it, drove it with force. And he drove onward making that city resound with the rattling sound of the car.

description: The commencement of the fight with the Nivatakavachas
sn: रथघोषं तु तं श्रुत्वा स्तनयित्लोरिवाम्बरे। मन्वाना देवराजं मामाविग्ना दानवाभवन्॥
en: Hearing that rattling noise of the car as the roar of the clouds in the sky and taking me for the king of the gods, the Danavas became agitated.

description: The commencement of the fight with the Nivatakavachas
sn: सर्वे सम्भ्रान्तमनसः शरचापधराः स्थिताः। तथासिशूलपरशुगदामुसलपाणयः॥
en: (And) with their minds trembling with fear, they stood, holding in their hands arrows, bows, swords, javelins, axes, maces and clubs.

description: The commencement of the fight with the Nivatakavachas
sn: ततो द्वाराणि पिदधुर्दानवास्त्रस्तचेतसः। संविधाय पुरे रक्षां न स्म कश्चन दृश्यते॥
en: Then having made arrangements for the defence of their city, the Danavas. with hearts troubled with fear, closed the gates so that nothing could be seen.

description: The commencement of the fight with the Nivatakavachas
sn: ततः शङ्खमुपादाय देवदत्तं महास्वनम्। परमां मुदमाश्रित्य प्राधमं तं शनैरहम्॥
en: Then taking my conch, Devadatta, emitting tremendous roars, I repeatedly blew it with great joy.

description: The commencement of the fight with the Nivatakavachas
sn: स तु शब्दो दिवं स्तम्वा प्रतिशब्दमजीजनत्। वित्रेसुश्च निलिल्युश्च भूतानि सुमहान्त्यपि॥
en: That sound, ringing through the heavens, sent forth echoes. Upon which, mighty creatures, greatly terrified, hid themselves.

description: The commencement of the fight with the Nivatakavachas
sn: ततो निवातकवचा: सर्व एव स्वलंकृताः। दंशिता विविधैस्त्राणैर्विचित्रायुधपाणयः॥ आयसैश्च महाशूलैर्गदाभिर्मुसलैरपि। पट्टिशैः करवालैश्च रथचक्रैश्च भारत॥ शतघ्नीभिर्भुशुण्डीभिः खङ्गैश्चित्रैः स्वलंकृतैः। प्रगृहीतैर्दितेः पुत्राः प्रादुरासन् सहस्रशः॥
en: Thereupon, O Bharata, all those sons of Ditithe Nivatakavachas-poured in thousands, adorned with ornaments, clad in various kinds of mails and holding in their hands various weapons, (such as) javelins, mighty maces, clubs, hatchets, Pattishas, Sabres, car-wheels, Shataghnis, Bhushundis and variegated and ornamented swords.

description: The commencement of the fight with the Nivatakavachas
sn: ततो विचार्य बहुशो रथमार्गेषु तान् हयान्। प्राचोदयत् समे देशे मातलिर्भरतर्षभ॥
en: Then O best of the Bharatas, deliberately judging of the course the car should take, Matali began to drive the steeds on level grounds,

description: The commencement of the fight with the Nivatakavachas
sn: तेन तेषां प्रणुन्नानामाशुत्वाच्छीघ्रगामिनाम्। नान्वपश्यं तदा किंचित् तन्मेऽद्भुतमिवाभवत्॥
en: Then, on account of the rapid career of the horses, fleet as the wind and guided by him (Matali) I could perceive nothing-and this appeared wonderful to me.

description: The commencement of the fight with the Nivatakavachas
sn: ततस्ते दानवास्तत्र वादित्राणि सहस्रशः। विकृतस्वररूपाणि भृशं सर्वाण्यनादयन्॥
en: Thereupon the Danavas vehemently began to sound thousands of musical instruments, discordant and of awkward shapes.

description: The commencement of the fight with the Nivatakavachas
sn: तेन शब्देन सहसा समुद्रे पर्वतोपमाः। आप्लवन्त गतैः सत्त्वैर्मत्स्याः शतसहस्रशः॥
en: Stupefied at those sounds, hundreds and thousands of fishes (huge) as mountains began suddenly to fly away from the sea.

description: The commencement of the fight with the Nivatakavachas
sn: ततो वेगेन महता दानवा मामुपाद्रवन् विमुञ्चन्तः शितान् बाणान् शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः॥
en: Then the Danavas rushed at me with tremendous force discharging hundreds and thousands of sharpened arrows.

description: The commencement of the fight with the Nivatakavachas
sn: स सम्प्रहारस्तुमुलस्तेषां च मम भारत। अवर्तत महाघोरो निवातकवचान्तकः॥
en: (And), O Bharata, there took place between them and me a terrible fight destructive of the Nivatakavachas.

description: The commencement of the fight with the Nivatakavachas
sn: ततो देवर्षयश्चैव तथान्ये च महर्षयः। ब्रह्मर्षयश्च सिद्धाश्च समाजग्मुर्महामृधे॥
en: The Devarshis, the Danavarshis, the Brahinarshis and the Siddhas came there to witness that terrible encounter.

description: The commencement of the fight with the Nivatakavachas
sn: ते वै मामनुरूपाभिर्मधुराभिर्जयैषिणः। अस्तुवन् मुनयो वाग्भिर्यथेन्द्रं तारकामये।॥
en: (And) those Munis, eager for my victory, began to eulogise me with sweet speeches as they did Indra, at the war which took place on account of Tara (the wife of Brihaspati).

sn: अर्जुन उवाच ततो निवातकवचाः सर्वे वेगेन भारत। अभ्यद्रवन् मां सहिताः प्रगृहीतायुधा रणे।॥
en: Arjuna said: Then, O Bharata, furnished with arms, all the Nivatakavacha flew in a body towards me furiously in battle,

sn: आच्छाद्य स्थपन्थानमुत्क्रोशन्तो महारथाः। आवृत्य सर्वतस्ते मां शरवर्षैरवाकिरन्।॥
en: Those mighty car-warriors obstructing the course of the car and uttering loud yells and surrounding me on all sides, enveloped me with downpours of arrows.

sn: ततोऽपरे महावीर्याः शूलपट्टिशपाणयः। शूलानि च भुशुण्डीश्च मुमुचुर्दानवा मयि॥
en: Then other demons, of great strength armed with spears and Pattishas, hurled at me spears and Bhushundis.

sn: तच्छूलवर्ष सुमहद् गदाशक्तिसमाकुलम्। अनिशं सृज्यमानं तैरपतन्मद्रथोपरि॥
en: That continuous discharge of spears together with maces and clubs fell upon my car.

sn: अन्ये मामभ्यधावन्त निवातकवचा युधि। शितशस्त्रायुधा रौद्राः कालरूपाः प्रहारिणः॥
en: Other dreadful and terrible-looking Nivatakavachas, dexterous in hurling (weapons) and armed with sharpened weapons and bows, rushed at me in fight.

sn: तानहं विविधैर्बाणैर्वेगवद्भिरजिह्मगैः। गाण्डीवमुक्तैरभ्यनमेकैकं दशभिर्मधे॥
en: I (on my part) in the encounter, discharging several fleet arrows coursing straight, from the Gandiva, pierced each of them with ten (shafts).

sn: ते कृता विमुखाः सर्वे मत्प्रयुक्तैः शिलाशितैः। ततो मातलिना तूर्णं हयास्ते सम्प्रचोदिताः॥
en: (And) I drove them back by those arrows of mine sharpened on stones. Then those horses being swiftly driven by Matali,

sn: मार्गान् बहुविधांस्तत्र विचेरुर्वातरंहसः। सुसंयता मातलिना प्रामनन्त दितेः सुतान्॥
en: Careered through several courses with the spread of the wind and being dexterously guided by Matali, trampled upon the sons of Diti.

sn: शतं शतास्ते हरयस्तस्मिन् युक्ता महारथे। शान्ता मातलिना यत्ता व्यचरन्नल्पका इव॥
en: (And) Though that mighty car was yoked with hundreds of horses, yet being skillfully driven by Matali, as they began to move, it seemed as if they were a few only.

sn: तेषां चरणपातेन स्थनेमिस्वनेन च। मम बाणनिपातैश्च हतास्ते शतशोऽसुराः॥
en: By the press of their hoofs and by the thundering noise of the car-wheels and by the discharge of my arrows hundreds of demons fell dead.

sn: गतासवस्तथैवान्ये प्रगृहीतशरासनाः। हतसारथयस्तत्र व्यकृष्यन्त तुरंगमैः॥
en: Others, holding their bows in their hands, even when deprived of life and their charioteers being slain, were carried (hither and thither) by the horses.

sn: ते दिशो विदिशः सर्वे प्रतिरुध्य प्रहारिणः। अभ्यघ्नन् विविधैः शस्त्रैस्ततो मे व्यथितं मनः॥
en: (And) all those dexterous in striking, obstructing all sides and directions, became engaged in the fight with various weapons, at which my mind was distressed.

sn: ततोऽहं मातलेौर्यमपश्यं परमाद्भुतम्। अश्वांस्तथा वेगवतो यदयत्नादधारयत्॥
en: Then the prowess of Matali appeared highly wonderful to me in that he guided the swift steeds with ease.

sn: ततोऽहं लघुभिश्चित्रैरस्त्रैस्तानसुरान् रणे। चिच्छेद सायुधान् राजन् शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः॥
en: O king, then, in the fight, I cut off the Danavas by hundreds and thousands who were furnished with arms, by various swift weapons.

sn: एवं मे चरतस्तत्र सर्वयत्नेन शत्रुहन्। प्रीतिमानभवद् वीरो मातलिः शक्रसारथिः॥
en: O destroyer of foes, the heroic charioteer of Shakra, Matali, seeing me thus course there (on the field of battle) exerting my utmost, became well pleased (with me).

sn: वध्यमानास्ततस्तैस्तु हयैस्तेन रथेन च। अगमन् प्रक्षयं केचित्र्यवर्तन्त तथा परे॥ स्पर्धमाना इवास्माभिर्निवातकवचा रणे। शरवर्षेः शरार्तं मां महद्भिः प्रत्यवारयन्॥
en: Then, some (of the Danavas) crushed by the horses and the car, met with destruction and some gave up fighting; while others, in the encounter, challenged by us and afflicted with arrows, opposed me by heavy downpour of shafts.

sn: ततोऽहं लघुभिश्चित्रैर्ब्रह्मास्त्रपरिमन्त्रितैः। व्यधर्म सायकैराशु शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः॥
en: Thereupon, I began to consume them with hundreds and thousands of ornamented swift arrows inspired with Mantras relating to the weapon of Brahma.

sn: ततः सम्पीडयमानास्ते क्रोधाविष्टा महारथाः। अपीडयन् मां सहिताः शरशूलासिवृष्टिभिः॥
en: Then those mighty demons sore pressed by me and fired with anger, afflicted me with simultaneous discharge of clubs, darts and swords.

sn: ततोऽहमस्त्रमातिष्ठं परमं तिग्मतैजसम्। दयितं देवराजस्य माधवं नाम भारत॥
en: O Bharata, I then, took up that favourite weapon of the lord of the gods, named, Madhava, possessed of exceedingly fiery energy.

sn: ततः खङ्गास्त्रिशूलांश्च तोमरांश्च सहस्रशः। अस्त्रवीर्येण शतधा तैर्मुक्तानहमच्छिदम्॥
en: Then by the power of that weapon, I cut, to a hundred pieces, the swords, tridents and thousands of Tomaras hurled by them.

sn: छित्त्वा प्रहरणान्येषां ततस्तानपि सर्वशः। प्रत्यविध्यमहं रोषाद् दशभिर्दशभिः शरैः॥
en: Having destroyed their weapons, wrathfully pierced each of them with ten arrows.

sn: गाण्डीवाद्धि तदा संख्ये यथा भ्रमरपक्तयः। निष्पतन्ति महाबाणास्तन्मातलिरपूजयत्॥
en: And the fact that on the battle field mighty arrows like (thick flights of black bees), were discharged from the Gandiva, was admired by Matali.

sn: तेषामपि तु बाणास्ते तन्मातलिरपूजयत्। अवाकिरन् मां बलवत् तानहं व्यधमं शरैः॥
en: And the skillfulness with which displaying prowess, I cut off, with my shafts, their arrows which completely surrounded me, drew admiration from Matali.

sn: वध्यमानास्ततस्ते तु निवातकवचाः पुनः। शरवर्षैर्महद्भिर्मां समन्तात् पर्यवारयन्॥
en: Being struck, those Nivatakavachas again completely surrounded me with a mighty discharge of arrows.

sn: शरवेगानिहत्याहमस्त्रैरस्त्रैविघातिभिः। ज्वलद्भिः परमैः शी।स्तानविध्यं सहस्रशः॥
en: Having arrested the career of their shafts by excellent, fleet and blazing weapons inspired with mantras, capable of destroying (other) weapons, I pierced them by thousands.

sn: तेषां छिन्नानि गात्राणि विसृजन्ति स्म शोणितम्। प्रावृषीवाभिवृष्टानि शृङ्गाण्यथधराभृताम्॥
en: Like waters running down from the summit of mountains, in the rainy season, blood began to flow from their mangled bodies.

sn: इन्द्राशनिसमस्पर्शर्वेगवद्भिरजिह्मगैः। मद्बाणैर्वध्यमानास्ते समुद्विग्नाः स्म दानवाः॥
en: Smitten by mighty, fleet and straightcoursing arrows having the touch of the thunderbolt hurled by Indra, those Danavas became greatly agitated.

sn: शतधा भिन्नदेहास्ते क्षीणप्रहरणौजसः। ततो निवातकवचा मामयुध्यन्त मायया॥
en: Their bodies were cut to a hundred pieces and their weapons lost their energy. Then those Nivatakavachas began fighting with me by the help of illusion.

sn: अर्जुन उवाच ततोऽश्मवर्षं सुमहत् प्रादुरासीत् समन्ततः। नगमात्रैः शिलाखण्डैस्तन्मां दृढमपीडयत्॥
en: Arjuna said: Then commenced a mighty shower of stones from all sides; (and) those stones, big as rocks, sore oppressed me.

sn: तदहं वज्रसंकाशैर्महेन्द्रास्त्रप्रचोदितैः। अचूर्णयं वेगवद्भिः शरजालैर्महाहवे॥
en: Thereupon, at that terrible encounter, I crushed (those crags) with showers of fleet arrows, resembling the thunderbolt, discharged from Mahendra's weapon.

sn: चूर्ण्यमानेऽश्मवर्षे तु पावकः समजायत। तत्राश्मचूर्णान्यपतन् पावकप्रकरा इव॥
en: Those crags being reduced to pieces, there ensued fire and those fragments of stones fell like sparks of flame.

sn: ततोऽश्मवर्षे विहते जलवर्षं महत्तरम्। धाराभिरक्षमात्राभिः प्रादुरासीन्ममान्तिके॥
en: Then, those showers of stones having been destroyed, there fell near me a mighty downpour of water having torrents of the size of an axle.

sn: नभसः प्रच्युताधारास्तिग्मवीर्याः सहस्रशः। आवृण्वन् सर्वतो व्योम दिशश्चोपदिशस्तथा॥
en: Thousand of mighty torrents (of water), falling from the sky, enveloped the entire firmament and (all) the directions and the (ten) cardinal points.

sn: धाराणां च निपातेन वायोर्विस्फूर्जितेन च। गर्जितेन च दैत्यानां न प्राज्ञायत किंचन॥
en: (And) I was quite bewildered on account of that (heavy) downpour, blowing of the wind and the yell of the Daityas.

sn: धारा दिवि च सम्बद्धा वसुधायां च सर्वशः। व्यामोहयन्त मां तत्र निपतन्त्योऽनिशं भुवि॥
en: Those showers, covering (the entire space) between the heaven and the earth and incessantly falling upon the ground, (quite) confounded me.

sn: तत्रोपदिष्टमिन्द्रेण दिव्यमस्त्रं विशोषणम्। दीप्तं प्राहिणवं घोरमशुष्यत् तेन तज्जलम्॥
en: Thereupon, I discharged that terrible, flaming and celestials weapon, Vishoshana, learnt from Indra, which dried the water up.

sn: हतेऽश्मवर्षे च मया जलवर्षे च शोषिते। मुमुचुर्दानवा मायामग्निं वायुं च भारत॥
en: The showers of stones being destroyed and the watery shower dried up by me, O Bharata, the Danavas created illusions of fire and wind.

sn: ततोऽहमग्निं व्यधमं सलिलास्त्रेण सर्वशः। शैलेन च महास्त्रेण वायोर्वेगमधारयम्॥
en: Then I totally destroyed the fire by Salila (watery) weapon; and arrested the fury of the wind by the mighty Shaila (rock) weapon.

sn: तस्यां प्रतिहतायां च दानवा युद्धदुर्मदाः। प्राकुर्वन् विविधां मायां योगपद्येन भारत॥
en: (And), O Bharata, on the destruction of these (illusions), the Danavas, irrepressible in battle, produced (simultaneously) several other) illusions.

sn: ततो वर्ष प्रादुरभूत् सुमहल्लोमहर्षणम्। अस्त्राणां घोररूपाणामग्नेर्वायोस्तथाश्मनाम्॥
en: Then commenced a terrible shower of rocks and of the dreadful weapons of fire and wind, making the hair stand on the end (with terror).

sn: सा तु मायामयी वृष्टिः पीडयामास मां युधि। अथ घोरं तमस्तीव्र प्रादुरासीत् समन्ततः॥
en: And that downpour (of rocks and weapons) oppressed me in battle. Then there spread on all sides a dismal darkness.

sn: तमसा संवृते लोके घोरेण परुषेण च। हरयो विमुखाश्चासन् प्रास्खलच्चापि मातलिः॥
en: When the world was enveloped in that terrible and dense darkness, the horses drew back, Matali stumbled,

sn: हस्ताद्धि रश्मयश्चास्य प्रतोदः प्रापतद् भुवि। असकृच्चाह मां भीत: क्वासीति भरतर्षभा॥
en: And the golden whip fell on the ground from his hand. O best of the Bharata, getting terrified, he repeatedly cried out "Where are you?"

sn: मां च भीराविशत् तीव्रा तस्मिन् विगतचेतसि। स च मां विगतज्ञानः संत्रस्तमिदमब्रवीत्॥
en: (And), when he lost his senses, I also was seized with a terrible fear. And (thus stupefied) he said to me in a hurry,

sn: सुराणामसुराणां च संग्रामः सुमहानभूत्। अमृतार्थं पुरा पार्थ स च दृष्टो मयानघ॥
en: "O Sinless being, in days of yore a terrible battle was fought between the gods and the demons for the sake of nectar, which I witnessed.

sn: शम्बरस्य वधे घोरः संग्रामः सुमहानभूत्। सारथ्यं देवराजस्य तत्रापि कृतवानहम्॥
en: (And) in that mighty and terrible encounter, which took place for the destruction of the (Asura) Shambara, I acted as the charioteer of the lord of the gods.

sn: तथैव वृत्रस्य वधे संगृहीता हया मया। वैरोचनेर्महायुद्धं दृष्टं चापि सुदारुणम्॥
en: Again, I drove the horses on the occasion of Vritra's destruction and also witnessed that awful and terrible encounter with the son of Virochana.

sn: एते मया महाघोराः संग्रामाः पर्युपासिताः। न चापि विगतज्ञानोऽभूतपूर्वोऽस्मि पाण्डव॥
en: O Pandava, I witnessed all those terrible encounters. But never before (this) did I lose Imy senses.

sn: पितामहेन संहारः प्रजानां विहितोध्रुवम्। न हि युद्धमिदं युक्तमन्यत्र जगतः क्षयात्॥
en: Verily, it has been ordained by Pitamaha (Brahma) that the creation will be destroyed (at this encounter). For I find no other reason for this battle, If it be not for the destruction of the whole universe."

sn: तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा संस्तभ्यात्मानमात्मना। मोहयिष्यन् दानवानामहं मायाबलं महत्॥
en: Hearing these words (of Matali) and pacifying my mind with my own efforts and deliberating (within myself) how to battle this mighty illusion created by the Danavas,

sn: अब्रुवं मातलिं भीतं पश्य मे भुजयोर्बलम्। अस्त्राणां च प्रभावं वैधनुषो गाण्डिवस्य च॥
en: I spoke to terrified Matali, “behold the prowess of my arms and the power of my weapons and that of my bow Gandiva.

sn: अद्यास्त्रमाययैतेषां मायामेतां सुदारुणाम्। विनिहन्मि तमश्चोग्रं मा भैः सूत स्थिरो भव॥
en: O charioteer do not be afraid, calm yourself. I will, this day, destroy the terrible illusion created by them and also this dense darkness, by illusion-creating weapon."

sn: एवमुक्त्वाहमसृजमस्त्रमायां नराधिप। मोहनी सर्वभूतानां हिताय त्रिदिवौकसाम्॥
en: O lord of men, having said this, I produced an illusion by the means of weapons capable of stupefying the whole creating, for the welfare of the celestials.

sn: पाड्यमानासु मायासु तासु तास्वसुरोत्तमाः। पुनर्बहुविधा मायाः प्राकुर्वन्नमितौजसः॥
en: That illusion being dispelled, some of the foremost amongst the Asuras, possessed of unrivalled prowess, again created various sorts of illusions,

sn: पुनः प्रकाशमभवत् तमसा ग्रस्यते पुनः। भवत्यदर्शनो लोकः पुनरप्सु निमज्जति॥
en: (In consequence of which) now the world displayed itself, now it was enveloped in darkness, now it disappeared (from view) and, now again, it was submerged into water.

sn: सुसंगृहीतैर्हरिभिः प्रकाशे सति मातलिः। व्यचरत् स्यन्दनायेण संग्रामे लोमहर्षणे॥
en: And when it displayed itself again to view, Matali with the well-conducted steeds, began to course in battle field which made the hair stand erect (with fear).

sn: ततः पर्यपतन्नुग्रा निवातकवचा मयि। तानहं विवरं दृष्ट्वा प्राहिण्वं यमसादनम्॥
en: Then the furious Nivatakavachas flew towards me. Seizing this opportunity, I began to send them to the abode of Yama.

sn: वर्तमाने तथा युद्धे निवातकवचान्तके। नापश्यं सहसा सर्वान् दानवान् माययाऽवृतान्॥
en: In that encounter, fatal to the Danavas, which was still regaining, all on a sudden, I could not behold those demons who concealed themselves under the cover of illusion.

sn: अर्जुन उवाच अदृश्यमानास्ते दैत्या योधयन्ति स्म मायया। अदृश्येनास्त्रवीर्येण तानप्यहमयोधयम्॥
en: Arjuna said: The demons, concealed from view, began fighting by the help of illusion. I also by the power of invisible weapons (i.e. weapons operating on unseen objects) fought with them,

sn: गाण्डीवमुक्ता विशिखाः सम्यगस्त्रप्रचोदिताः। अच्छिन्दत्रुत्तमाङ्गानि यत्र यत्र स्म तेऽभवन्॥
en: And by means of arrows duly shot from the Gandiva, I cut off their heads wherever they were stationed.

sn: ततो निवातकवचा वध्यमाना मया युधि। संहृत्य मायां सहसा प्राविशन् पुरमात्मनः॥
en: Thereupon, the Nivatakavachas, thus struck dead by me, all on a sudden, forsook their illusion and entered into their own city.

sn: व्यपयातेषु दैत्येषु प्रादुर्भूते च दर्शने। अपश्यं दानवांस्तत्र हतान् शतसहस्रशः॥
en: The Daityas having fled and everything being disclosed to view, I beheld there hundreds and thousands of the Danavas (lying) slain.

sn: विनिष्पिष्टानि तत्रैषां शस्त्राण्याभरणानि च। शतशः स्म प्रदृश्यन्ते गात्राणि कवचानि च॥
en: (And) I saw by hundred their crushed weapons ornaments, limbs and mails.

sn: हयानां नान्तरं ह्यासीत् पदाद् विचलितुं पदम्। उत्पत्य सहसा तस्थुरन्तरिक्षगमास्ततः॥
