en: In consequence of the battlefield being strewn all over with dead bodies, the steeds had no room to move from one step to another, Thereupon with a sudden spring they took their station in the air.

sn: ततो निवातकवचा व्योम संछाद्य केवलम्। अदृश्या ह्यत्यवर्तन्त विसृन्तः शिलोच्चयान्॥
en: Then concealed from view, the Nivatakavachas, covering the entire firmament, rained down crags.

sn: अन्तर्भूमिगताश्चान्ये हयानां चरणान्यथ। व्यगृहणन् दानवा घोरा रथचक्रे च भारता॥
en: Other dreadful Danavas entering into the entrails of the earth, O Bharata, caught hold of the legs of the horses and the car-wheels.

sn: विनिगृह्य हरीनश्वान् रथं च मम युध्यतः। सर्वतो मामविध्यन्त सरथंधरणीधरैः॥
en: were When engaged in fighting, (they) seizing the horses and the car, covered me on the car, on all sides with rocks.

sn: पर्वतैरुपचीयद्भिः पतमानैस्तथापरैः। स देशो यत्र वर्ताम गुहेव समपद्यत॥
en: On account of the rocks with which we were covered and of the others which were falling (around us), the place where we stationed, looked like a cave.

sn: पर्वतैश्छाद्यमानोऽहं निगृहीतैश्च वाजिभिः। अगच्छं परमामार्तं मातलिस्तदलक्षयत्॥
en: That I was sore afflicted on account of being surrounded by rocks and the steeds being hard pressed, was perceived by Matali.

sn: लक्षयित्वा च मां भीतमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्। अर्जुनार्जुन मा भैस्त्वं वज्रमस्त्रमुदीरय॥
en: Seeing me terrified he spoke these words, "O Arjuna, O Arjuna, don't be afraid; discharge the weapon, Vajra (thunderbolt)."

sn: ततोऽहं तस्य तद् वाक्यं श्रुत्वा वज्रमुदीरयम्। देवराजस्य दयितं भीममस्त्रं नराधिप॥
en: Then, O lord of men, hearing these words of his, I let go that favourite weapon of the king of the celestials, the terrible Vajra (thunderbolt).

sn: अचलं स्थानमासाद्य गाण्डीवमनुमन्त्र्य च। अमुञ्चं वज्रसंस्पर्शानायसान् निशितान् शरान्॥
en: Inspiring the Gandiva with mantras and aiming at the locality of the rocks, I discharged sharpened iron darts having the touch of the thunderbolt.

sn: ततो मायाश्च ताः सर्वा निवातकवचांश्च तान्! ते वज्रचोदिता बाणा वज्रभूताः समाविशन्॥
en: And those arrows, turned into thunderbolt (on account of their) being shot from the Vajra, penetrated through the illusion and all the Nivatakavachas.

sn: ते वज्रवेगविहता दानवाः पर्वतोपमाः। इतरेतरमाश्लिष्य न्यपतन् पृथिवीतले॥
en: Then those Danavas, big as rocks smitten by the force of the thunder, fell on the ground clashing against one another,

sn: अन्तर्भूमौ च येऽगृहणन् दानवा रथवाजिनः। अनुप्रविश्य तान् बाणाः प्राहिण्वन् यमसादनम्॥
en: And the shafts, penetrating those Danavas, who entering into the bowels of the earth had seized the horses and the car, sent them to the abode of Yama.

sn: हतैर्निवातकवचैर्निरस्तैः पर्वतोपमैः। समाच्छाद्यत देशः स विकीर्णैरिव पर्वतैः॥
en: That place was completely filled with those Nivatakavachas looking like mountains, who were (either) killed or wounded and lying scattered like (so many) rocks.

sn: न हयानां क्षति: काचिन्न रथस्य न मातलेः। मम चादृश्यत तदा तदद्भुतमिवाभवत्॥
en: And the fact, that neither did the horses, nor Matali, nor myself, suffer the least (by that event), appeared strange.

sn: ततो मां प्रहसन् राजन् मातलि: प्रत्यभाषत। नैतदर्जुन देवेषु त्वयि वीर्यं यदीक्ष्यते॥
en: Then, O king, Matali addressed me with a smile "the prowess displayed by you cannot be seen even among the gods.”

sn: हतेष्वसुरसंघेषु दारास्तेषां तु सर्वशः। प्राक्रोशन नगरे तस्मिन् यथा शरदि सारसाः॥
en: On the Danava hosts being slain all their wives in that city began to bewail like cranes in autumn.

sn: ततो मातलिना सार्धमहं तत् पुरमभ्ययाम्। त्रासयन् स्थघोषेण निवातकवचस्त्रियः॥
en: Then accompanied by Matali, I entered that city, terrifying the females of the Nivatakavachas by the rattling noise of the car.

sn: तान् दृष्ट्वा दशसाहस्रान् मयूरसदृशान् हयान्। रथं च रविसंकाशं प्राद्रवन् गणशः स्त्रियः॥
en: Beholding those ten thousands of steeds resembling peacocks and that car of the splendour of the sun, the females began to flee in large numbers.

sn: ताभिराभरणैः शब्दस्वासिताभिः समीरितः। शिलानामिव शैलेषु पतन्तीनामभूत् तदा॥
en: Thereupon, there arose a sound of the falling of the ornaments (from the persons) of those terrified ladies like the sound of hail falling upon a mountain.

sn: वित्रस्ता दैत्यनार्यस्ताः स्वानि वेश्मान्यथाविशन्। बहुरलविचित्राणि शातकुम्भमयानि च॥
en: At last the affrighted ladies of the Daityas entered into their respective golden palaces decked with innumerable gems.

sn: तदद्भुताकारमहं दृष्ट्वा नगरमुत्तमम्। विशिष्टं देवनगरादपृच्छं मातलिं ततः॥
en: Then beholding that wonderful and excellent city, superior to that of the gods, I asked Matali,

sn: इदमेवंविधं कस्माद् देवा नावासयन्त्युत। पुरंदरपुराद्धीदं विशिष्टमिति लक्षये॥
en: “This city appears superior to that of Purandara. How is it that the Gods do not reside in such a place?"

sn: मातलिरुवाच आसीदिदं पुरा पार्थ देवराजस्य नः पुरम्। ततो निवातकवचैरितः प्रच्याविताः सुराः॥
en: Matali answered O Partha, formerly it was the city of our lord of the gods. (But) afterwards the gods were expciled from here by the Nivatakavachas.

sn: तपस्तप्त्वा महत् तीव्र प्रसाद्य च पितामहम्। इदं वृतं निवासाय देवेभ्यश्चाभयं युधि॥
en: Having pleased Brahma by the performance of rigid asceticism, they asked (of him) the boons, (namely), to dwell here and to be free from all fears of the gods in wars.

sn: ततः शक्रेण भगवान् स्वयंभूरिति चोदितः। विधत्तां भगवानन्तमात्मनो हितकाम्यया॥
en: Then the self-existent lord (Shiva) was thus addressed by Shakra. "O lord, keeping our welfare in view, do what you think proper."

sn: तत उक्तो भगवता दिष्टमत्रेति भारत। भवितान्तस्त्वमप्येषां देहेनान्येन शत्रुहन्॥
en: Thereupon, O Bharata, the lord (Shiva) thus commanded Indra saying "O destroyer of foes, assuming another body you will kill these (demons).”

sn: तत एषां वधार्थाय शक्रोऽस्त्राणि ददौ तव। न हि शक्याः सुरैर्हन्तुं य एते निहतास्त्वया॥
en: Therefore, Shakra gave you the weapons for the destruction of these (demons). Even the gods had been unable to slay these that have been killed by you.

sn: कालस्य परिणामेन ततस्त्वमिह भारत। एषामन्तकरः प्राप्तस्तत् त्वया च कृतं तथा॥
en: O Bharata, as you have come hither just at the appointed time, you have been able to kill them.

sn: दानवानां विनाशाय अस्त्राणां परमं बलम्। चाहितस्त्वं महेन्द्रेण पुरुषेन्द्र तदुत्तमम्॥
en: O best of mortals, in order to destroy these Danavas, Mahendra conferred on you the energy (that belongs to the possessor) of those excellent weapons.

sn: अर्जुन उवाच ततः प्रशाम्य नगरं दानवांश्च निहत्य तान्। पुनर्मातलिना सार्धमगच्छं देवसद्म तत्॥
en: Arjuna said : Having killed the Danavas and subdued (their) city, I returned to the abode of the celestials accompanied by Matali.

description: Conitnued The destruction of the Daityas of Hiranyapur
sn: अर्जुन उवाच निवर्तमानेन मया महद् दृष्टं ततोऽपरम्। कामचरं दिव्यं पावकार्कसमप्रभम्॥
en: Arjuna said: Then, while returning (to the abode of Indra), I beheld on my way a great celestials city, moving at will, endued with the splendour of the fire or the sun,

description: Conitnued The destruction of the Daityas of Hiranyapur
sn: रत्नदुममयश्चित्रैः सुस्वरैश्च पतत्रिभिः। पौलोमैः कालकजैश्च नित्यहृष्टैरधिष्ठितम्॥
en: Containing trees made of jewels, teeming with many-coloured birds of sweet voice, inhabited by the Paulomas and the Kalakanja ever merry,

description: Conitnued The destruction of the Daityas of Hiranyapur
sn: गोपुराट्टालकोपेतं चतुरं दुरासदम्। सर्वरत्नमयं दिव्यमद्भुतोपमदर्शनम्॥
en: Adorned with gate-ways, towers and four gates, impregnable, made of all sorts of jewels celestials wonderful to look at,

description: Conitnued The destruction of the Daityas of Hiranyapur
sn: दुमैः पुष्यफलोपेतैः सर्वरत्नमयैर्वृतम्। तथा पतत्रिभिर्दिव्यैरुपेतं सुमनोहरैः॥
en: Containing trees made of all sorts of jewels and bearing fruits and flowers, inhabited by beautiful and celestials feathery creatures,

description: Conitnued The destruction of the Daityas of Hiranyapur
sn: असुरैनित्यमुदितैः शूलटिमुसलायुधैः। चापमुद्गरहस्तैश्च स्रग्विभिः सर्वतो वृतम्॥
en: Surrounded on all sides by the Asuras, always cheerful, adorned with garlands and holding in their hands maces, swords, darts, bows and clubs.

description: Conitnued The destruction of the Daityas of Hiranyapur
sn: तदहं प्रेक्ष्य दैत्यानां पुरमद्भुतदर्शनम्। अपृच्छं मातलिं राजन् किमिदं वर्ततेऽद्भुतम्॥
en: Beholding that city of the Daitya, wonderful to look at, O king, I asked Matali "What is it that looks so marvellous?"

description: Conitnued The destruction of the Daityas of Hiranyapur
sn: मातलिरुवाच पुलोमा नाम दैतेयी कालका च महासुरी। दिव्यं वर्षसहस्रं ते चेरतुः परमं तपः॥
en: Matali said : (Formerly) a Daitya-female, named Puloma and another great giantess, Kalaka (by name), practised severe austerities for a thousand celestials years.

description: Conitnued The destruction of the Daityas of Hiranyapur
sn: तपसोऽन्ते ततस्ताभ्यां स्वयम्भूरदद् वरम्। अगृहणीतां वरं ते तु सुतानामल्पदुःखताम्॥ अवध्यतां च राजेन्द्र सुरराक्षसपन्नगैः। पुरं सुरमणीयं च खचरं सुमहाप्रभम्॥
en: When they had finished their austerities, the self-existent (god) Svayambhu granted them boons. (And), O king of kings, they obtained the boons-viz., that their children might never suffer distress; that (they) might obtain a highly beautiful and an exceedingly splendid aerial city,

description: Conitnued The destruction of the Daityas of Hiranyapur
sn: सर्वरत्नैः समुदितं दुर्धर्षममरैरपि। महर्षियक्षगन्धर्वपन्नगासुरराक्षसैः॥
en: Full of all sorts of gems, unassailable even by immortals, the Maharshis, the Yakshas, the Gandharvas, the Pannagas, the Asuras and the Rakshasas,

description: Conitnued The destruction of the Daityas of Hiranyapur
sn: सर्वकामगुणोपेतं वीतशोकमनामयम्। ब्रह्मणा भरतश्रेष्ठ कालकेयकृते कृतम्॥
en: Containing all the desirable objects and devoid of grief and desire. O best of the Bharatas, created by Brahma for the Kalakeyas,

description: Conitnued The destruction of the Daityas of Hiranyapur
sn: तदेतत् खपुरं दिव्यं चरत्यमरवर्जितम्। पौलोमाध्युषितं वीर कालकझैश्च दानवैः॥
en: This is that celestials city, devoid of gods, which is moving about. O hero, it is inhabited by the Pauloma and he Kalakeya Danavas.

description: Conitnued The destruction of the Daityas of Hiranyapur
sn: हिरण्यपुरमित्येवं ख्यायते नगरं महत्। रक्षितं कालकेयैश्च पौलोमैश्च महासुरैः॥
en: This mighty city is called Hiranyapura and is guarded by the powerful Asuras, the Kalakeyas and the Paulomas.

description: Conitnued The destruction of the Daityas of Hiranyapur
sn: त एते मुदिता राजन्नवध्याः सर्वदैवतैः। निवसन्त्यत्र राजेन्द्र गतोद्वेगा निरुत्सुकाः॥
en: O king of kings, there they dwell happily, indestructible by the gods, free from anxiety and having all their desires fulfilled.

description: Conitnued The destruction of the Daityas of Hiranyapur
sn: मानुषान्मृत्युरेतेषां निर्दिष्टो ब्रह्मणा पुरा। एतानपि रणे पार्थ कालकञ्जान् दुरासदान्। वज्रास्त्रेण नयस्वाशु विनाशं सुमहाबलान्॥
en: Formerly it was destined by Brahma that they should be killed by mortals. O Partha, (therefore) destroy speedily these invincible and exceedingly powerful Kalakanjas in battle by the weapon Vajra (thunderbolt).

description: Conitnued The destruction of the Daityas of Hiranyapur
sn: अर्जुन उवाच सुरासुरैरवध्यं तदहं ज्ञात्वा विशाम्पते। अब्रुवं मातलिं हृष्टो याह्येतत् पुरमञ्जसा॥
en: Arjuna said: O lord of earth, learning that they were indestructible by the gods and Asuras. I gladly said to Matali "do you go to this city speedily.

description: Conitnued The destruction of the Daityas of Hiranyapur
sn: त्रिदशेशद्विषो यावत् क्षयमस्त्रैर्नयाम्यहम्। न कथञ्चिद्धि मे पापा न वध्या ये सुरद्विषः॥
en: I will bring about the destruction of all these enemies of the celestials with weapons. There exist no wicked enemies of the gods whom I do not consider my victims."

description: Conitnued The destruction of the Daityas of Hiranyapur
sn: उवाह मां ततः शीघ्रं हिरण्यपुरमन्तिकात्। रथेन तेन दिव्येन हरियुक्तेन मातलिः॥
en: Thereupon, Matali had me speedily conveyed by that celestials car, yoked with steeds, towards the-neighbourhood of Hiranyapura.

description: Conitnued The destruction of the Daityas of Hiranyapur
sn: ते मामालक्ष्य दैतेया विचित्राभरणाम्बराः। समुत्पेतुर्महावेगा रथानास्थाय दंशिताः॥
en: On beholding me, those sons of Diti, wearing various sorts of garments and mounted on chariots, rushed at me with great violence.

description: Conitnued The destruction of the Daityas of Hiranyapur
sn: ततो नालीकनाराचैर्भल्लैः शक्त्यष्टितोमरैः। प्रत्यघ्नन् दानवेन्द्रा मां क्रुद्धास्तीव्रपराक्रमाः॥
en: Then those foremost of the Danavas (possessed) of fiery prowess, angrily assailed me with Nalikas, Narachas, Bhallas, Maces, swords and Tomaras.

description: Conitnued The destruction of the Daityas of Hiranyapur
sn: तदहं शरवर्षेण महता प्रत्यवारयम्। शस्त्रवर्षं महद् राजन् विद्याबलमुपाश्रितः॥
en: Thereupon, O king, availing myself of the strength of my knowledge (in arms), I warded off that shower of weapons by mighty discharges of arrows;

description: Conitnued The destruction of the Daityas of Hiranyapur
sn: व्यामोहयं च तान् सर्वान् रथमार्गश्चरन् रणे। तेऽन्योन्यमभिसम्मूढाः पातयन्ति स्म दानवान्।॥
en: And coursing through the field of battle on the car, bewildered them. Thus confounded, the Danavas began to fell down one another.

description: Conitnued The destruction of the Daityas of Hiranyapur
sn: तेषामेवं विमूढानामन्योन्यमभिधावताम्। शिरांसि विशिस्त्रैर्दीप्तै→हनं शतसङ्घशः॥
en: (And) with blazing arrows I cut off, by hundreds, the heads of those who, getting confounded, were rushing at one another.

description: Conitnued The destruction of the Daityas of Hiranyapur
sn: ते वध्यमाना दैतेयाः पुरमास्थाय तत् पुनः खमुत्पेतुः सनगरा मायामास्थाय दानवीम्॥
en: Thus smitten (by me) those sons of Diti, taking refuge in that city, again rose up in the air with it, by the help of illusion peculiar to the Danavas.

description: Conitnued The destruction of the Daityas of Hiranyapur
sn: ततोऽहं शरवर्षेण महता कुरुनन्दन। मार्गमावृत्य दैत्यानां गतिं चैषामवारयम्॥
en: Thereupon, O descendant of the Kurus, covering the passage of the Daityas by heavy shower of arrows, I obstructed their movement.

description: Conitnued The destruction of the Daityas of Hiranyapur
sn: तत् पुरं खचरं दिव्यं कामगं सूर्यसप्रभम्। दैतेयैर्वरदानेनधार्यते स्म यथासुखम्॥
en: (But) the sons of Diti, on the strength of their boon, easily supported themselves on that celestials and aerial city of sun-like splendour and moving at will.

description: Conitnued The destruction of the Daityas of Hiranyapur
sn: अन्तर्भूमौ निपतति पुनरूज़ प्रतिष्ठते। पुनस्तिर्यक् प्रयात्याशु पुनरप्सु निमज्जति॥
en: At one time it plunged into the earth and then rose up in the air again, now it took a curved direction and then again submerged under water.

description: Conitnued The destruction of the Daityas of Hiranyapur
sn: अमरावतिसंकाशं तत् पुरं कामगं महत्। अहमस्त्रैर्वहुविधैः प्रत्यगृहं परंतप॥
en: (Then), O tormentor of foes, I surrounded with various weapons that mighty moving about at will.

description: Conitnued The destruction of the Daityas of Hiranyapur
sn: ततोऽहं शरजालेन दिव्यास्त्रनुदितेन च। व्यगृहणं सह दैतेयैस्तत् पुरं पुरुषर्षभ॥
en: And, O best of the Bharatas, I assailed that city together with the Daityas by showers of arrows, shot from celestials weapons.

description: Conitnued The destruction of the Daityas of Hiranyapur
sn: विक्षतं चायसैर्बाणैर्मत्प्रयुक्तैरजिह्मगैः। महीमभ्यपतद् राजन् प्रभग्नं पुरमासुरम्॥
en: (And), O king, that city of the Asuras, riven and broken by straight-coursing steels darts shot by me, fell to the ground.

description: Conitnued The destruction of the Daityas of Hiranyapur
sn: ते वध्यमाना मद्वाणैर्वज्रवेगैरयस्मयैः। यथोर्मयः। पर्यध्रमन्त वै राजन्नसुराः कालचोदिताः॥
en: Those Asuras too, O king, wounded by my iron shafts, fleet as the thunder and propelled by Fate, began to rove about.

description: Conitnued The destruction of the Daityas of Hiranyapur
sn: ततो मातलिरारुह्य पुरस्तानिपतन्निव। महीमवातरत् क्षिप्रं रथेनादित्यवर्चसा॥
en: Then, Matali, soaring to the heavens, as if taking a leap in front, speedily came down to the earth on that chariot effulgent as the sun.

description: Conitnued The destruction of the Daityas of Hiranyapur
sn: ततो रथसहस्राणि षष्टिस्तेषाममर्षिणाम्। युयुत्सूनां मया सार्धं पर्यवर्तन्त भारत। तान्यहं निशितैर्बाणैर्व्यधमं गार्धराजितैः॥
en: O Bharata, then, desirous of fighting with me, they furiously hemmed me in with sixty thousand cars. (But) I destroyed those (cars) by sharpened arrows adorned with vulture feathers.

description: Conitnued The destruction of the Daityas of Hiranyapur
sn: ते युद्धे सन्यवर्तन्त समुद्रस्य नेमे शक्या मानुषेण युद्धेनेति प्रचिन्त्य तत्॥
en: They were, then, engaged in the fight, like billows on the sea. Thereupon, considering that they would not be destroyed by the manner of fighting peculiar to mortals,

description: Conitnued The destruction of the Daityas of Hiranyapur
sn: ततोऽहमानुपूर्येण दिव्यान्यस्त्राण्ययोजयम्। ततस्तानि सहस्राणि रथिनां चित्रयोधिनाम्॥ अस्त्राणि मम दिव्यानि प्रत्यघ्नन् शनकैरिव। रथमार्गान् विचित्रांस्ते विचरन्तो महाबलाः॥ प्रत्यदृश्यन्त संचामे शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः। विचित्रमुकुटापीडा विचित्रकवचध्वजाः॥
en: I took to discharging duly the celestials weapons. But the thousands of weapons, discharged by those car-warriors, the wonderful fighters, gradually repelled my celestials weapons, and I beheld hundreds and thousands of exceedingly powerful (Danavas) ranging on their cars, in battle, displaying various tactics. Adorned with variegated helmets ornamented mails, furnished with beautiful flags.

description: Conitnued The destruction of the Daityas of Hiranyapur
sn: विचित्राभरणाश्चैव नन्दयन्तीव मे मनः। अहं तु शरवर्षैस्तानस्त्रप्रचुदितै रणे।॥
en: And decked with various ornaments (they) attracted my mind. I, in that encounter, by showers of arrows shot from weapons,

description: Conitnued The destruction of the Daityas of Hiranyapur
sn: नाशक्नुवं पीडयितुं ते तु मां प्रत्यपीडयन्। तैः पीड्यमानो बहुभिः कृतास्त्रैः कुशलैयुधि॥
en: Could not oppress them; but they sorely afflicted me. (Thus) hard pressed by numerous (Asuras), furnished with weapons and skilled in battle,

description: Conitnued The destruction of the Daityas of Hiranyapur
sn: व्यथितोऽस्मि महायुद्धे भयं चागान्महन्मम। ततोऽहं देवदेवाय रुद्राय प्रयतो रणे॥
en: I was afflicted in that terrible encounter and was seized with a dreadful terror. Thereupon, mustering up (courage), I (bowed down) to the god of gods, Rudra,

description: Conitnued The destruction of the Daityas of Hiranyapur
sn: स्वस्ति भूतेभ्य इत्युक्त्वा महास्त्रं समचोदयम्। यत् तद् रौद्रमिति ख्यातं सर्वामित्रविनाशनम्॥
en: Saying "may all beings remain in place," and sent that mighty weapon which is named Rudra and is destructive of all enemies.

description: Conitnued The destruction of the Daityas of Hiranyapur
sn: ततोऽपश्यं त्रिशिरसं पुरुषं नवलोचनम्। त्रिमुखं षड्भुजं दीप्तमर्कज्वलनमूर्धजम्॥
en: Then I beheld a person with three heads, nine eyes, three faces, six arms and with hair blazing as the sun or the fire.

description: Conitnued The destruction of the Daityas of Hiranyapur
sn: लेलिहानैर्महानागैः कृतचीरममित्रहन्। विभीस्ततस्तदस्त्रं तु घोरं रौद्रं सनातनम्॥
en: (And) O destroyer of foes, as for his clothing he wore huge serpents issuing out their tongues.

description: Conitnued The destruction of the Daityas of Hiranyapur
sn: दृष्ट्वा गाण्डीवसंयोगमानीय भरतर्षभ। नमस्कृत्वा त्रिनेत्राय शर्वायामिततेजसे॥
en: Then, O best of the Bharatas, beholding that terrible and eternal Rudra and shaking off my fear, I fixed it on the Gandiva. (And) bowing down to the three eyed Sarva of unrivalled energy,

description: Conitnued The destruction of the Daityas of Hiranyapur
sn: मुक्तवान् दानवेन्द्राणां पराभावाय भारत। मुक्तमात्रे ततस्तस्मिन् रूपाण्यासन् सहस्रशः॥
en: O Bharata, I discharged (it) for the destruction of those foremost of the Danavas. No sooner had I hurled it, than it at once assumed a thousand shapes;

description: Conitnued The destruction of the Daityas of Hiranyapur
sn: मृगाणामथ सिंहानां व्याघ्राणां च विशाम्पते। ऋक्षाणां महिषाणां च पन्नगानां तथा गवाम्॥
en: (Such as), O lord of the earth, those of deer, of lions, of tigers, of bears, of buffaloes, of serpents, of cows.

description: Conitnued The destruction of the Daityas of Hiranyapur
sn: शरभाणां गजानां च वानराणां च सङ्घशः। ऋषभाणां वराहाणां मार्जाराणां तथैव च॥
en: O Sharabhas, of elephants, of monkeys in vast numbers, of bulls, of boars, of cats,

description: Conitnued The destruction of the Daityas of Hiranyapur
sn: शालावृकाणां प्रेतानां भुरुण्डानां च सर्वशः। गृध्राणां गरुडानां च चमराणां तथैव च॥
en: Of dogs, of ghosts, of all the Bhurundas, of vultures, of Garudas of Chamaras,

description: Conitnued The destruction of the Daityas of Hiranyapur
sn: देवानां च ऋषीणां च गन्धर्वाणां च सर्वशः। पिशाचानां सयक्षाणां तथैव च सुरद्विषाम्॥
en: Of the celestials, of the Rishis, of all the Gandharva, of the Pishachas, of the Yakshas, of the enemies of the gods,

description: Conitnued The destruction of the Daityas of Hiranyapur
sn: गुह्यकानां च संचामे नैर्ऋतानां तथैव च। झषाणां गजवक्त्राणामुलूकानां तथैव च।॥
en: Of the Guhyakas in battle, of the Nirritas, of elephant-mouthed sharks, of owls,

description: Conitnued The destruction of the Daityas of Hiranyapur
sn: मीनवाजिसरूपाणां नानाशस्त्रासिपाणिनाम्। तथैव यातुधानानां गदामुद्गरधारिणाम्॥
en: Of the creatures having the shapes of fishes and horses, of beings armed with various weapons and swords and of the Rakshasas, armed with maces and clubs.

description: Conitnued The destruction of the Daityas of Hiranyapur
sn: एतैश्चान्यैश्च बहुभिर्नानारूपधरैस्तथा। सर्वमासीज्जगद् व्याप्त तस्मिन्नस्त्रे विसर्मिते॥
en: These and numerous other (beings), wearing various shapes, filled the universe when the weapon was discharged.

description: Conitnued The destruction of the Daityas of Hiranyapur
sn: त्रिशिरोभिश्चतुर्दष्ट्रेश्चतुरास्यैश्चतुर्भुजैः। अनेकरूपसंयुक्तैर्मीसमेदोवसास्थिभिः॥ अभीक्ष्णं वध्यमानास्ते दानवा नाशमागताः। अर्कज्वलनतेजोभिर्वज्राशनिसमप्रभैः॥ अद्रिसारमयैश्चान्यैर्बाणैरपि निबर्हणैः। न्यहनं दानवान् सर्वान् मुहूर्तेनैव भारत॥
en: (And) repeatedly smitten by creatures of many shapes covered with flesh, fat, bones and marrow, having three heads, four tusks, four mouths and four arms, the Danavas met with destruction. O Bharata, then, with numerous other shafts, blazing like the sun or fire, glaring like the fire of thunderbolt and made of the essence of rocks, I killed all the Danavas in a moment.

description: Conitnued The destruction of the Daityas of Hiranyapur
sn: गाण्डीवास्त्रप्रणुन्नांस्तान् गतासून् नभसश्च्युतान्। दृष्ट्वाहं प्राणमं भूयस्त्रिपुरघ्नाय वेधसे॥
en: (And) seeing them cut to pieces by the Gandiva weapon, deprived of life and thrown down from the sky. I again bowed down to that god, the slayer of the (Asura), Tripura,

description: Conitnued The destruction of the Daityas of Hiranyapur
sn: तथा रौद्रास्त्रनिष्पिष्टान् दिव्याभरणभूषितान्। निशम्य परमं हर्षमगमद् देवसारथिः॥
en: The charioteer of the gods (Matali), beholding them, that were decked with celestials ornaments, crushed by the Rudra weapon was highly pleased.

description: Conitnued The destruction of the Daityas of Hiranyapur
sn: तदसां कृतं कर्म देवैरपि दुरासदम्। दृष्ट्वा मां पूजयामास मातलिः शक्रसारथिः॥
en: Seeing that I performed this unbearable feat (of arms), unachievable even by the celestials, Matali, the charioteer of Shakra, eulogised me;

description: Conitnued The destruction of the Daityas of Hiranyapur
sn: उवाच वचनं चेदं प्रीयमाणः कृताञ्जलिः। सुरासुरैरसह्यं हि कर्म यत् साधितं त्वया॥
en: And with great delight, said these words with joined-hands-the feat, that you have achieved, is incapable of being borne (even) by the gods and the Asuras.

description: Conitnued The destruction of the Daityas of Hiranyapur
sn: न ह्येतत् संयुगे कर्तुमपि शक्तः सुरेश्वरः। सुरासुरैरवध्यं हि पुरमेतत् खगं महत्॥
en: Even the lord of the gods cannot perform such a fcat in battle. This great aerial city, indestructible by the gods and the Asuras,

description: Conitnued The destruction of the Daityas of Hiranyapur
sn: त्वया विमथितं वीर स्ववीर्यतपसो बलात्। विध्वस्ते स्वपुरे तस्मिन् दानवेषु हतेषु च॥
en: Has been destroyed by you, O hero, by your prowess and strength of asceticism. That city being destroyed and the Danavas being killed,

description: Conitnued The destruction of the Daityas of Hiranyapur
sn: विनदन्त्यः स्त्रियः सर्वा निष्येतुर्नगराद् बहिः। प्रकीर्णकेश्यो व्यथिताः कुरर्य इव दुःखिताः॥
en: All their sorrowing wives smitten with grief and with hair dishevelled, issued out of their city lamenting like Kuraris.

description: Conitnued The destruction of the Daityas of Hiranyapur
sn: पेतुः पुत्रान् पितॄन् भ्रातृन् शोचमाना महीतले। रुदत्यो दीनकण्ठ्यस्तु निनदन्त्यो हतेश्वराः॥ उरांसि परिनिघ्नन्त्यो विस्रस्तस्रग्विभूषणाः। तच्छोकयुक्तमश्रीकं दुःखदैन्यसमाहतम्॥ न बभौ दानवपुरं हतत्विट्कं हतेश्वरम्। गन्धर्वनगराकारं हतनागमिव हृदम्॥ शुष्कवृक्षमिवारण्यमदृश्यमभवत् पुरम्। भां तु संहष्टमनसं क्षिप्रं मातलिरानयत्॥
en: Mourning for their sons, fathers and brothers, uttering piteous cries of distress for the loss of their lords and beating their breasts, (they) fell down upon the ground, their ornaments falling off from their bodies. That city of the Danavas, resembling the city of the Gandharvas, filled with lamentation, afflicted with sorrow and distress, devoid of beauty and deprived of its lords, looked like a lake devoid of elephants or like a forest with all its trees dead, (and then) vanished (from sight). (And) Matali speedily brought me, well-pleased,

description: Conitnued The destruction of the Daityas of Hiranyapur
sn: देवराजस्य भवनं कृतकर्माणमाहवात्। हिरण्यपुरमुत्सृज्य निहत्य च महासुरान्॥
en: And successful in my mission, to the abode of the king of the gods. Having destroyed Hiranyapur and killed those mighty Asuras,

description: Conitnued The destruction of the Daityas of Hiranyapur
sn: निवातकवचांश्चैव ततोऽहं शक्रमागमम्। मम कर्म च देवेन्द्रं मातलिविस्तरेण तत्॥ सर्वं विश्रावयामास यथाभूतं महाद्युते। हिरण्यपुरघातं च मायानां च निवारणम्॥ निवातकवचानां च वधं संख्ये महौजसाम्। तच्छ्रुत्वा भगवान् प्रीतः सहस्राक्षः पुरंदरः॥ मरुद्भिः सहितः श्रीमान् साधु साध्वित्यथाब्रवीत्। ततो मां देवराजो वै समाश्वास्य पुनः पुनः॥ अब्रवीद् विबुधैः सार्धमिदं स मधुरं वचः। अतिदेवासुरं कर्म कृतमेव त्वया रणे॥
en: The Nivatakavachas, I returned to Shakra. And, O highly effulgent (king), Matali narrated in detail to the lord of the gods, my entire feat (of arms) as it had happened. The prosperous hundred-eyed lord Purandara, together with the Vasus, hearing the fall of Hiranyapur, the dispersion of the illusion and the destruction of the exceedingly powerful Nivatakavachas in battle, became pleased and exclaimed “bravo! bravo!" Then the lord of the gods together with the celestials, repeatedly cheering me, spoke these highly delightful words: “The feat that you have displayed in battle, surpasses that of the gods and of the Asuras.

description: Conitnued The destruction of the Daityas of Hiranyapur
sn: गुर्वर्थश्च कृतः पार्थ महाशत्रून् घनता मम। एवमेव सदा भाव्यं स्थिरेणाजौधनंजय॥
en: O Partha, you have (now) paid your preceptor's fees by slaying my powerful enemies. O Dhananjaya, you will, thus, ever remain cool-headed in battle,

description: Conitnued The destruction of the Daityas of Hiranyapur
sn: असम्मूढेन चास्त्राणां कर्तव्यं प्रतिपादनम्। अविषह्यो रणे हि त्वं देवदानवराक्षसैः॥ सयक्षासुरगन्धर्वैः सपक्षिगणपन्नगैः। वसुधां चापि कौन्तेय त्वद्वाहुबलनिर्जिताम्। पालयिष्यतिधर्मात्मा कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: And be able to discharge your weapons unerringly. Neither the celestials, nor the Danavas, nor the Rakshasas, nor the Yakshas, nor the Asuras, nor the Gandharvas, nor the birds, nor the serpents shall be to stand you in fight. (And)O Kuru's son, O virtuous son of Kunti, Yudhishthira, having conquered the earth by the strength of your arms, will govern it.

sn: अर्जुन उवाच ततो मामतिविश्वस्तं संरूढशरविक्षतम्। देवराजो विगृह्येदं काले वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Arjuna said : Then the lord of the gods, seeing me, highly faithful and wounded with a arrows and acknowledging me as his own, duly spoke these words. me

sn: दिव्यान्यस्त्राणि सर्वाणि त्वयि तिष्ठन्ति भारत। न त्वाभिभवितुं शक्तो मानुषो भुवि कश्चन॥
en: "O Bharata, all the celestials weapons are with you; (therefore) no mortal on earth shall by any means be capable of conquering you.

sn: भीष्मो द्रोणः कृपः कर्णः शकुनिः सह राजभिः। संग्रामस्थस्य ते पुत्र कलां नार्हन्ति षोडशीम्॥
en: O son, when you will be engaged in battle, Bhishma, Drona, Kripa, Karma, Shakuni, together with (other) kings, shall not approach (in strength) a sixteenth part of yours."

sn: इदं च मे तनुत्राणं प्रायच्छन्मघवान् प्रभुः। अभेद्यं कवचं दिव्यं स्रजं चैव हिरण्मयीम्॥
en: The lord Maghavan gave this impenetrable celestials armour capable of protecting the body, this golden garland,

sn: देवदत्तं च मे शङ्ख पुनः प्रादान्महारवम्। दिव्यं चेदं किरीटं मे स्वयमिन्द्रो युयोज ह॥
en: And also this conch, Devadatta, emitting forth loud roars. (And) Indra himself fixed this coronet (on my head).

sn: ततो दिव्यानि वस्त्राणि दिव्यान्याभरणानि च। प्रादाच्छक्रो ममैतानि रुचिराणि बृहन्ति च॥
en: Shakra then granted me these precious and beautiful celestials garments and these hcavenly ornaments.

sn: एवं सम्पूजितस्तत्र सुखमसम्युषितो नृप। इन्द्रस्य भवने पुण्ये गन्धर्वशिशुभिः सह॥
en: Thus, O king, duly honoured, I dwelt cheerfully in the abode of Indra with the children of the Gandharvas.

sn: ततो मामब्रवीच्छक्रः प्रीतिमानमरैः सह। समयोऽर्जुन गन्तुं ते भ्रातरो हि स्मरन्ति ते॥
en: Then Shakra, well pleased, unanimously with the immortals spoke to me: “O Arjuna, the time for your departure has (now) arrived, your brothers are thinking of you.”

sn: एवमिन्द्रस्य भवने पञ्च वर्षाणि भारत। उषितानि मया राजन् स्मरता द्यूतजं कलिम्॥
en: Thus, O monarch, remembering the troubles brought on (us) by gambling I passed (these) five years in the abode of Indra.

sn: ततो भवन्तमद्राक्षं भ्रातृभिः परिवारितम्। गन्धमादनपादस्य पर्वतस्यास्य मूर्धनि।॥
en: Then did I behold you surrounded by (my other) brothers on the summit of the lower range of the mountain Gandhamadana.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच दिष्ट्याधनंजयास्त्राणि त्वया प्राप्तानि भारत। दिष्ट्या चाराधितो राजा देवानामीश्वरः प्रभुः॥
en: Yudhishthira said: O Dhananjaya, fortunately you have obtained these celestials weapons and it is by good luck too, that you have worshipped the lord king of the celestials.

sn: दिष्ट्या च भगवान् स्थाणुर्देव्या सह परंतप। साक्षाद् दृष्टः स्वयुद्धेन तोषितश्च त्वयानघ॥
en: And luckily, O tormentor of foes, O sinless being, you have beheld that very god, Sthanu himself, together with the goddess and pleased them by fighting

sn: दिष्ट्या च लोकपालैस्त्वं समेतो भरतर्षभ। दिष्ट्या वर्धामहे पार्थ दिष्ट्यासि पुनरागतः॥
en: And O the best of the Bharatas, luckily it is that you have obtained an interview with the Lokapalas. It is because you are fortunate that we have prospered and fortunately you have come back.

sn: अद्य कृत्स्नां महीं देवीं विजितां पुरमालिनीम्। मन्ये च धृतराष्ट्रस्य पुत्रानपि वशीकृतान्॥
en: Today do I consider the entire earth, adorned with cities, as conquered and the sons of Dhritarashtra as subdued.

sn: इच्छामि तानि चास्त्राणि द्रष्टुं दिव्यानि भारत। यैस्तथा वीर्यवन्तस्ते निवातकवचा हताः॥
en: O Bharata, (now) I wish to see those celestials weapons by means of which you destroyed the powerful Nivatakavachas.

sn: अर्जुन उवाच श्वः प्रभाते भवान् द्रष्टा दिव्यान्यस्त्राणि सर्वशः। निवातकवचा घोरा यैर्मया विनिपातिताः॥
en: Arjuna said : You will behold tomorrow morning all those celestials weapons whereby the Nivatakavachas were slain.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमागमनं तत्र कथयित्वाधनंजयः। भ्रातृभिः सहितः सर्वै रजनी तामुवास ह॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having thus related the events in connection with his arrival there, Dhananjaya passed that night there together with all his brothers.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तस्यां रात्र्यां व्यतीतायांधर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः। उत्थायावश्यकार्याणि कृतवान् भ्रातृभिः सह॥
en: Vaishampayana said : The night being spent, Yudhishthira, the foremost of the virtuous awoke and performed the necessary duties together with his brothers.

sn: ततः संचोदयामास सोऽर्जुनं भ्रातृनन्दनम्। दर्शयास्त्राणि कौन्तेय यैर्जिता दानवास्त्वया॥
en: Then he (Yudhishthira) said to Arjuna, the joy of his mother, “O son of Kunti, show me the weapons whereby you destroyed the Danavas."

sn: ततोधनंजयो राजन् देवैर्दत्तानि पाण्डवः। अस्त्राणि तानि दिव्यानि दर्शयामास भारत॥
en: Thereupon, O king, O Bharata, the Pandava, Arjuna showed those celestials weapons granted (to him) by the god,

sn: यथान्यायं महातेजा; शौचं परममास्थितः। गिरिकूबरपादाक्षं शुभवेणु त्रिवेणुमत्॥ पार्थिवं रथमास्थाय शोभमानोधनंजयः। दिव्येन संवृतस्तेन कवचेन सुवर्चसा॥
en: (And) duly observing the purificatory rites, the highly-energetic Dhananjaya, seated on the earth as (his) car, having the mountain for its pole, the base of the mountain for its axle and the cluster of beautiful bamboo trees for its socket pole and clad in that celestials mail of great splendour, looked (highly) beautiful.

sn: धनुरादाय गाण्डीवं देवदत्तं स वारिजम्। शोशुभ्यमान: कौन्तेय आनुपूर्व्यान्महाभुजः॥ अस्त्राणि तानि दिव्यानि दर्शनायोपचक्रमे। अथ प्रयोक्ष्यमाणेषु दिव्येष्वस्त्रेषु तेषु वै॥
en: (And)o son of Kunti, the handsome (Dhananjaya) of mighty arms, holding (in his hand) the bow Gandiva, together with the conch presented to him by the celestials, was about to exhibit in due order those celestials weapons. (But) As he commenced to display those heavenly weapons,

sn: समाक्रान्ता मही पद्भ्यां समकम्पत सदुमा। क्षुभिताः सरितश्चैव तथैव च महोदधिः॥
en: The earth, being oppressed by the weight of his feet, began to tremble together with all its trees and the rivers and the mighty ocean became troubled.

sn: शैलाथापि व्यदीर्यन्त न ववौ च समीरणः। न बभासे सहस्रांशुर्न जज्वाल च पावकः॥
en: The mountain were rent, the wind ceased to blow, the sun ceased to shine, the fire did not burn,

sn: न वेदाः प्रतिभान्ति स्म द्विजातीनां कथंचन। अन्तर्भूमिगता ये च प्राणिनो जनमेजय॥
en: And the twice-born (Brahmanas) could by no means recite the Vedas. And O Janamejaya, the creatures inhabiting the entrails of the earth,

sn: पीड्यमानाः समुत्थाय पाण्डवं पर्यवारयन्। वेपमानाः प्राञ्जलयस्ते सर्वे विकृताननाः॥
en: Being (sore) oppressed, rose up and with distorted countenances and joined hands and trembling (with fear), surrounded the Pandava (Arjuna).

sn: दह्यमानास्तदास्त्रैस्ते याचन्ति स्मधनंजयम्। ततो ब्रह्मर्षयश्चैव सिद्धा ये च महर्षयः॥
en: And scorched by those (celestials) weapons they prayed to Dhananjaya (to spare their lives). Then the Brahmarshis, the Siddhas, the Maharshis,

sn: जङ्गमानि च भूतानि सर्वाण्येवावतस्थिरे। देवर्षयश्च प्रवरास्तथैव च दिवौकसः॥
en: And the mobile beings-all these creatures arrived there. The most exalted Devarshis, the celestials,

sn: यक्षराक्षसगन्धर्वास्तथैव च पतत्रिणः। खेचराणि च भूतानि सर्वाण्येवावतस्थिरे॥
en: The Yakshas, the Rakshasas, the Gandharvas, the feathery creatures, the skyranging creatures-all these beings appeared (on the scene).

sn: ततः पितामहश्चैव लोकपालाश्च सर्वशः। भगवांश्च महादेवः सगणोऽभ्याययौ तदा॥
en: Then Pitamaha (Brahma), all the Lokapalas (the guardians of the ten cardinal points), the divine Mahadeva, together with all their followers, made their appearance (at that spot).

sn: ततो वायुमहाराज दिव्यैर्माल्यैः सुगन्धिभिः। अभितः पाण्डवं चित्ररवचक्रे समन्ततः॥
en: (And) then, O mighty monarch, Vayu (the wind-god) bearing bearing variegated celestials flowers, began to strew them all around the Pandava (Arjuna).

sn: जगुश्च गाथा विविधा गन्धर्वाः सुरचोदिताः। ननृतुः सङ्घशश्चैव राजन्नप्सरसां गणाः॥
en: O king, commissioned by the gods, the Gandharvas sang various melodies and multitudes of Apsaras danced there.

sn: तस्मिंश्च तादृशे काले नारदचोदितः सुरैः। आगम्याह वचः पार्थं श्रवणीयमिदं नृप॥
en: (And)O king, at that very time, Narada, sent by the celestials, arrived (there) and spoke to Partha these words grateful to the ear:

sn: अर्जुनार्जुन मा युक्ष्व दिव्यान्यस्त्राणि भारत। नैतानि निरधिष्ठाने प्रयुज्यन्ते कथंचन॥
en: "O Arjuna, O Bharata, forebear discharging these celestials weapons. These (weapons) ought, by no means, to be hurled where there is no object to hit at.

sn: अधिष्ठाने न वानातः प्रयुञ्जीत कदाचन। प्रयोगेषु महान् दोषो ह्यस्त्राणां कुरुनन्दन॥
en: And unless sore afflicted, one should not discharge these even if there is an object (present). O descendant of the Kurus, it will result in a terrible disaster, if these weapons are (causclessly) discharged.

sn: एतानि रक्ष्यमाणानिधनंजय यथागमम्। बलवन्ति सुखार्हाणि भविष्यन्ति न संशयः॥
en: O Dhananjaya, if these powerful weapons are duly kept, they will no doubt, lead to your happiness.

sn: अरक्ष्यमाणान्येतानि त्रैलोक्यस्यापि पाण्डव। भवन्ति स्म विनाशाय मैवं भूयः कृथाः क्वचित्।।२२।
en: (But), O Pandava, if they are not (carefully) preserved, they will lead to the destruction of the three worlds. Therefore, do not attempt such a (rash) act again.

sn: अजातशत्रो त्वं चैव द्रक्ष्यसे तानि संयुगे। योज्यमानानि पार्थेन द्विषतामवमर्दने॥
en: O Ajatashatru (Yudhishthira), you will behold them when Partha will make use of them for the destruction of your enemies in battle."

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच निवार्याथ ततः पार्थं सर्वे देवा यथागतम्। जग्मुरन्ये च ये तत्र समाजग्मुर्नरर्षभ॥
en: O the most exalted of mortals, having prevented Arjuna (from hurling these weapons), all the celestials and all other beings who had come there went to their respective abodes.

sn: तेषु सर्वेषु कौरव्य प्रतियातेषु पाण्डवाः। तस्मिन्नेव वने हृष्टास्त अषुः सह कृष्णया।॥
en: O descendant of the Kurus, when all those had taken their departure, the Pandavas, together with Krishna, began to dwell cheerfully in that forest.

sn: जनमेजय उवाच तस्मिन् कृतास्त्रे रथिनां प्रवीरे प्रत्यागते भवनाद् वृत्रहन्तुः। अतः परं किमकुर्वन्त पार्थाः समेत्य शूरेणधनंजयेन॥
en: Janamejaya said : On the return of that best of the car-warriors from the abode of the slayer of Vitra (Indra) being skilled in arms, what did the Parthas do in company with the heroic Dhananjaya.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच वनेषु तेष्वेव तु ते नरेन्द्राः सहार्जुनेनेन्द्रसमेन वीराः। तस्मिंश्च शैलप्रवरे सुरम्ये धनेश्वराक्रीडगता विजह्वः
en: Vaishampayana said : Those foremost of men, brave as Indra, together with Arjuna, sported in the pleasuregardens of the lord of wealth (situated) in those forests on that excellent and beautiful mountain.

sn: वेश्मानि तान्यप्रतिमानि पश्यन् क्रीडाश्च नानादुमसंनिबद्धाः। चचारधन्वी बहुधा नरेन्द्रः सोऽस्त्रेषु यत्तः सततं किरीटी॥
en: Beholding those peerless abodes and pleasure-gardens interspersed with trees, Kiriti, the foremost of men, with a relish for arms and bow in hand, ranged at large (among) those (woods).

sn: अवाप्य वासं नरदेवपुत्राः प्रसादजं वैश्रवणस्य राज्ञः। न प्राणिनां ते स्पृहयन्ति राजन् शिवश्च कालः स बभूव तेषाम्॥
en: O monarch, those sons of a king, having obtained a residence through the favour of king Vaisravana, did not long for the prosperity of earthly creatures, (in as much as) that period (of their lives) was (quite) a blessing (to them).

sn: समेत्य पार्थेन यथैकरात्र मूषुः समास्तत्र तदा चतस्रः। पूर्वाश्च षट् ता दश पाण्डवानां शिवा बभूवुर्वसतां वनेषु॥
en: In company with Partha they lived there for four years which appeared to them (short) as a single night. The former six years and these four together numbering ten of their forest life glided smoothly away.

sn: ततोऽब्रवीद् वायुसुतस्तरस्वी जिष्णुश्च राजानमुपोपविश्य। यमौ च वीरौ सुरराजकल्पावेकान्तमास्थाय हितं प्रियं च॥
en: Then (once upon a time) seated before the king (Yudhishthira), the intrepid son of Vayu (the wind-god), together with Vishnu and the heroic twins, resembling the king of the celestials, spoke in private these sweet and beneficial words.

sn: तव प्रतिज्ञां कुरुराज सत्यां चिकीर्षमाणास्तदनु प्रियं च। ततो न गच्छाम वनान्यपास्य सुयोधनं सानुचरं निहन्तुम्॥
en: "O king of the Kurus, in order to make your promise bear fruit and to further your interests, we are not going to slay Suyodhana together with (all) his followers.

sn: एकादशं वर्षमिदं वसाम: सुयोधनेनात्तसुखाः सुखार्हाः। मज्ञातवासं सुखमाप्नुयाम॥ तवाज्ञया पार्थिव निर्विशङ्का विहाय मानं विचरन् वनानि। समीपवासेन विलोभितास्ते ज्ञास्यन्ति नास्मानपकृष्टदेशान्॥
en: In spite of our being deprived by Suyodhana of the happiness we deserve, we have been (hitherto happily) dwelling (in the woods) these eleven years. And hereafter too, O monarch, at your command, wandering in the forests regardless of our position, we shall easily spend the period of our incognits life, deluding that being of wicked mind and character. And (Suyodhana) being tempted by our residence in the neighbourhood will not be inclined to believe that we have removed to a distant country.

sn: संवत्सरं तत्र विहृत्य गूढं नराधमं तं सुखमुद्धरेम। निर्यात्य वैरं सफलं सपुष्पं तस्मै नरेन्द्राधमपूरुषाय॥ सुयोधनायानुचरैर्वृताय ततो महीमावसधर्मराज। स्वर्गोपमं देशमिमं चरद्भिः शक्यो विहन्तुं नरदेव शोकः॥
en: There O king, remaining in concealment for one year and (then) wrecking our vengeance on that worst of mortals, Suyodhana as well as his followers, we shall root out that vilest being (like a thorn) and regain our kingdom after the overthrow of our enemies. Therefore, O foremost of the virtuous, come down on earth. O king of mortals, if we continue to dwell in this country resembling heaven itself, we shall be able to forget our grief's.

sn: कीर्तिस्तु ते भारत पुण्यगन्धा नश्येद्धि लोकेषु चराचरेषु। तत् प्राप्य राज्यं कुरुपुङ्गवानां शक्यं महत् प्राप्तुमथ क्रियाश्च॥
en: But then, O Bharata, the sacred fragrance of your fame will disappear from (both) the mobile and the immobile worlds; (for) regaining the kingdom of the most exalted of the Kurus, you will be able to perform glorious deeds.

sn: इदं तु शक्यं सततं नरेन्द्र प्राप्तुं त्वया यल्लभसे कुबेरात्। कुरुष्व बुद्धिं द्विषतां वधाय कृतागसां भारत निग्रहे च॥
en: In that case, O monarch, you will always have what we already obtained from Kubera. (Therefore), O Bharata, direct your thoughts towards the punishment and destruction of your guilty enemies.

sn: तेजस्तवोग्रं न सहेत राजन् समेत्य साक्षादपि वज्रपाणिः। न हि व्यथं जातु करिष्यतस्तौ समेत्य देवैरपिधर्मराज॥ तवार्थसिद्ध्यर्थमपि प्रवृत्ती सुपर्णकेतुश्च शिनेश्च नप्ता। तथैव कृष्णोऽप्रतिमो बलेन तथैव चाहं नरदेववर्य॥
en: (For), O king, even the wielder of the thunderbolt himself cannot bear the burnt of your fiery prowess. And O foremost of the virtuous, he, having Suparna for his mark, Krishna and the grandson of Shini Satyaki, both bent on your welfare, will not feel any pain even when fighting the gods themselves. As Arjuna is unrivalled in prowess, so am I, O monarch.

sn: तवार्थसिद्ध्यर्थमभिप्रपन्नो यथैव कृष्णः सह यादवैस्तैः। तथैव चाहं नरदेववर्य यमौ च वीरौ कृतिनौ प्रयोगे॥
en: And, O king, as Krishna together with the Yadavas is eager for your welfare so am I. The twins also are brave and skilled in arms, (And) we, whose chief object consists in the advancement of your wealth and prosperity, encountering your enemies in battle, will kill them."

sn: त्वदर्थयोगप्रभवप्रधानाः शमं करिष्याम परान् समेत्य।। वैशम्पायन उवाच ततस्तदाज्ञाय मतं महात्मा तेषां चधर्मस्य सुतो वरिष्ठः॥ प्रदक्षिणं वैश्रवणाधिवासं चकारधर्मार्थविदुत्तमौजाः। आमन्त्र्य वेश्मनिः नदी: सरांसि सर्वाणि रक्षांसि चधर्मराजः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Then, knowing the intention of their (his brothers) the high-souled and excellent son of Dharma, versed in (the science of) religion and profit and possessed of great energy, went round the abode of Vaisravana. And Dharmaraja, greeting the places, rivers lakes and all the Rakshasas,

sn: यथागतं मार्गमवेक्षमाणः। पुनर्गिरि चैव निरीक्षमाणः। ततो महात्मा स विशुद्धबुद्धिः सम्प्रार्थयामास नगेन्द्रवर्यम्॥
en: Looked at the route which he had taken before. Then that high-souled and pure-minded being, looking at the mountain prayed to that prince of mountains, saying,

sn: र्जित्वा सपत्नान् प्रतिलभ्य राज्यम्। शैलेन्द्र भूयस्तपसे जितात्मा द्रष्टा तवास्मीति मतिं चकार॥
en: “Having performed my task, conquered my enemies and recovered my kingdom, may I, O lord of mountains, together with my friends, behold you again, for performing asceticism with subdued mind."

sn: वृतश्च सर्वैरनुजैर्द्विजैश्च तेनैव मार्गेण पतिः कुरूणाम्। उवाह चैतान् गणशस्तथैव घटोत्कचः पर्वतनिर्झरेषु॥
en: (And) when surrounded by all his brothers and the Brahmanas, the lord of the Kurus proceeded along the former path, he was carried across the mountain waterfalls by Ghatotkacha with his followers.

sn: तान् प्रस्थितान् प्रीतमना महर्षिः पितेव पुत्राननुशिष्य सर्वान्। स लोमशः प्रीतमना जगाम दिवौकसां पुण्यतमं निवासम्॥
en: (And) when they were about to start (on their journey) the great sage, Lomasha, gave them instructions as a father gives to his own sons and then went to the most sacred region of the celestials.

sn: स्तीर्थानि रम्याणि तपोवनानि। महान्ति चान्यानि सरांसि पार्थाः सम्पश्यमानाः प्रययुनरावयाः॥
en: Similarly advised by Arshtishena those foremost of men, the Parthas, proceeded along, beholding (on the way) various great and beautiful Tirthas (sacred places resorted to by pilgrims).

description: The return of the region of Dvaitavana
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच नगोत्तमं प्रस्रवणैरुपेतं दिशां गजैः किन्नरपक्षिभिश्च। सुखं निवासं जहतां हि तेषां न प्रीतिरासीद् भरतर्षभाणाम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Those foremost of the Bharatas, on leaving their delightful abode on that excellent mountain with waterfalls, the elephants of eight quarters, the Kinnaras and birds, were not happy at heart.

description: The return of the region of Dvaitavana
sn: ततस्तु तेषां पुनरेव हर्षः कैलासमालोक्य महान् बभूव। कुबेरकान्तं भरतर्षभाणां महीधरं वारिधरप्रकाशम्॥
en: But those best of the Bharatas again experienced a great delight on beholding the favourite mountain of Kubera, the Kailasa looking (white as the clouds).

description: The return of the region of Dvaitavana
sn: समुच्छ्रयान् पर्वतसंनिरोधरान् गोष्ठान् हरीणां गिरिसेतुमालाः। बहून् प्रपातांश्च समीक्ष्य वीराः स्थलानि निम्नानि च तत्र तत्र॥ तथैव चान्यानि महावनानि मृगद्विजानेकपसेवितानि। स्तेधन्विनः खड्गधरा नरावयाः॥
en: And those heroes, the excellent of mortals, armed with bows and swords, felt a great delight, beholding (on their way) elevations and defiles, dens of lions, rows of craggy causeways, numerous waterfalls, low lands here and there and various other great forests inhabited by numerous deer, birds and elephants.

description: The return of the region of Dvaitavana
sn: वनानि रम्याणि नद्यो सरांसि गुहा गिरीणां गिरिगह्वराणि। दिवानिशं प्राप्य नरर्षभाणाम्॥
en: (And as they journeyed on), romantic forests, rivers, lakes, caves of mountain, mighty mountain, caverns-all these always, by day and night became the dwelling places of those most excellent men.

description: The return of the region of Dvaitavana
sn: ते दुर्गवासं बहुधा निरुष्य व्यतीत्य कैलासमचिन्त्यरूपम्। आसेदुरत्यर्थमनोरमं ते तमाश्रमाचयं वृषपर्वणस्तु॥
en: (Thus) resting in many inaccessible places and crossing the mountain Kailasa of incomprehensible grandeur, they at length reached the exceedingly beautiful hermitage of Vrishaparva.

description: The return of the region of Dvaitavana
sn: समेत्य राज्ञा वृषपर्वणा ते प्रत्यर्चितास्तेन च वीतमोहाः। शशंसिरे विस्तरशः प्रवासं गिरौ यथावद् वृषपर्वणस्ते॥
en: Meeting with the king, Vrishaparva and being welcomed by him they recovered from fatigue and then they related to him) faithfully and fully the story of their stay in the mountains.

description: The return of the region of Dvaitavana
sn: सुखोषितास्तस्य त एकरात्रं पुण्याश्रमे देवमहर्षिजुष्टे। अभ्याययुस्ते बदरौं विशाला सुखेन वीराः पुनरेव वासम्॥
en: And having happily spent a night in that sacred hermitage frequented by the celestials and the Maharshis, those warriors gladly repaired to the great Jujube tree for a sojourn again.

description: The return of the region of Dvaitavana
sn: ऊषुस्ततस्तत्र महानुभावा नारायणस्थानगताः समग्रा:। कुबेरकान्तां नलिनी विशोकाः सम्पश्यमानाः सुरसिद्धजुष्टाम्॥
en: Then arriving at the place of Narayana, all those high-souled men, devoid of sorrow, began to dwell there, beholding the beloved lake of Kubera, frequented by the celestials and he Siddhas.

description: The return of the region of Dvaitavana
sn: तां चाथ दृष्टवा नलिनी विशोकाः पाण्डोः सुताः सर्वनरप्रधानाः। ते रेमिरे नन्दनवासमेत्य द्विजर्षयो वीतमला यथैव॥
en: (And) seeing that lake, those sons of Pandu, the best of all men, devoid of sorrow, began to sport there, (just) as the sinless Brahmana sages do on getting a habitation in the garden of Nandana.

description: The return of the region of Dvaitavana
sn: ततः क्रमेणोपययुर्दैवीरा यथागतेनैव पथा समग्राः। विहत्य मासं सुखिनो बदाँ किरातराज्ञो विषयं सुबाहोः॥
en: Then having spent a month happily at Badari, all those heroes gradually proceeded towards the country of Subahu, the king of the Kiratas, along the same route by which they had come (before).

description: The return of the region of Dvaitavana
sn: पीनांस्तुषारान् दरदांश्च सर्वान् देशान् कुलिन्दस्य च भूमिरलान्। अतीत्य दुर्गं हिमवत्प्रदेशं पुरं सुबाहोर्ददृशुर्नृवीराः॥
en: Journeying through China, Turaska, Darada and all the provinces of Kulinda, rich in heaps of jewels and crossing the inaccessible Himalayan regions, those warriors (at length) beheld the capital of Subahu.

description: The return of the region of Dvaitavana
sn: श्रुत्वा च तान् पार्थिवपुत्रपौत्रान्। प्राप्तान् सुबाहुर्विषये समग्रान्। प्रत्युद्ययौ प्रीतियुतः स राजा तं चाभ्यनन्दन वृषभाः कुरूणाम्॥
en: Hearing of the arrival of those sons and grandsons of kings in his capital, King Subahu, full of joy, advanced to welcome them. And thosc best of the Kurus also greeted him.

description: The return of the region of Dvaitavana
sn: समेत्य राज्ञा तु सुबाहुना सूतैर्विशोकप्रमुखैश्च सर्वे। सहेन्द्रसेनैः परिचारिकैश्च पौरोगवैर्ये च महानसस्था:॥ ते
en: Meeting with King Subahu and joined by their charioteers with Vishoka at their head, by all their attendants together with Indrasena, by the porters and by the servants of the kitchen,

description: The return of the region of Dvaitavana
sn: सुखोषितास्तत्र त एकरात्रं सूतान् समादाय रथांश्च सर्वान्। घटोत्कचं सानुचरं विसृज्य ततोऽभ्ययुर्यामुनमदिराजम्॥
en: They spent a night there happily. Dismissing Ghatotkacha together with all his attendants and retaining all the charioteers and he cars, they then proceeded towards the prince of mountains in the neighbourhood of Yamuna.

description: The return of the region of Dvaitavana
sn: हिमोत्तरीयारुणपाण्डुसानौ। स्तदा निवासं पुरुषप्रवीराः॥ वराहनानामृगपक्षिजुष्टं महावनं चैत्ररथप्रकाशम्। शिवेन पार्था मृगयाप्रधानाः संवत्सरं तत्र वने विजहुः॥
en: And having found in that mountainabounding in water falls-whose orange and grey coloured plateau is covered with a sheet of snow, the great forest (named) Vishakhayupa, inhabited by boars and birds and resembling the forest of Chitraratha, those heroic men began to dwell there. And those foremost of hunters, the Parthas lived peacefully in that forest for a year.

description: The return of the region of Dvaitavana
sn: तत्राससादातिबलं भुजङ्गं क्षुधादितं मृत्युमिवोग्ररूपम्। वृकोदरः पर्वतकन्दरायां विषादमोहव्यथितान्तरात्मा॥
en: There, in a mountain cave, Vrikodara coming across a very powerful serpent distressed with hunger and terrible like death itself, became afflicted at heart with sorrow and distraction.

description: The return of the region of Dvaitavana
sn: द्वीपोऽभवद् यत्र वृकोदरस्य युधिष्ठिरोधर्मभृतां वरिष्ठः। अमोक्षयद् यस्तमनन्ततेजा ग्राहेण संवेष्टितसर्वगात्रम्॥
en: (But) Yudhishthira, of immeasurable prowess, became the liberator of Vrikodara and extricated him from the gripe of the snake which coiled round his whole body.

description: The return of the region of Dvaitavana
sn: ते द्वादशं वर्षमुपोपयातं वने विहर्तुं कुरवः प्रतीताः। तस्माद् वनाच्चैत्ररथप्रकाशात श्रिया ज्वलन्तस्तपसा च युक्ताः॥ ततश्च यात्वा मरुधन्वपार्श्व सदाधनुर्वेदरतिप्रधानाः। सरस्वतीमेत्य निवासकामाः सरस्ततो द्वैतवनं प्रतीयुः॥
en: And when the twelfth of their forest life had arrived, those descendants of the Kurus, blazing in splendour, engaged in asceticism and given principally to the practice of archery, leaving that forest looking like that of Chitraratha, repaired gladly towards the confines of the desert. Thence they arrived at the banks of the river Sarasvati and therefrom desirous of dwelling there repaired to the Lake Dvaitavana.

description: The return of the region of Dvaitavana
sn: समीक्ष्य तान् द्वैतवने निविष्टान् निवासिनस्तत्र ततोऽभिजग्मुः। स्तृणोदपात्रावरणाश्मकुट्टाः॥
en: And seeing them enter Dvaitavana, the inhabitants of that place engaged in asceticism, restraining their passions, practising purity and fervid devotion and living on (foods) crushed with stone, approached them with grass mats and water vessels (in their hands for their reception).

description: The return of the region of Dvaitavana
sn: प्लक्षाक्षरैहीतकवेतसाच तथा बदर्यः खदिराः शिरीषाः। बिल्वेड्दा: पीलुशमीकरीराः सरस्वतीतीररुहा बभूवुः॥
en: The banks of the river Sarasvati were adorned with the holy fig, the Rudraksha, the cane, the Jujube, the Catechu, the Sirisa, the Bel, the Inguda, the Pilu, the Shami and the Karira tree.

description: The return of the region of Dvaitavana
sn: मागारभूतामिव देवतानाम्। सरस्वतीं प्रीतियुताश्चरन्तः सुखं विजहुर्नरदेवपुत्राः॥
en: Wandering joyfully by the Sarasvati, beloved by the Yakshas, the Gandharvas and the Maharshis and looking like the abode of the celestials, those sons of king lived there happily.

description: The seizure of Bhimasena by the serpent
sn: जनमेजय उवाच कथं नागायुतप्राणो भीमो भीमपराक्रमः। भयमाहारयत् तीव्र तस्मादजगरान्मुने॥
en: Janamejaya said : O sage, why did the terribly powerful Bhima endued with the strength of ten thousand elephants entertain such a dreadful fear of that snake!

description: The seizure of Bhimasena by the serpent
sn: पौलस्त्यंधनदं युद्धे च आह्वयति दर्पितः। नलिन्यां कदनं कृत्वा निहन्ता यक्षरक्षसाम्॥ तं शंससि भयाविष्टमापन्नमरिसूदनम्। एतदिच्छाम्यहं श्रोतुं परं कौतूहलं हि मे॥ वैशम्पायन उवाच बह्वाश्चर्ये वने तेषां वसतामुग्धन्विनाम्। प्राप्तानामाश्रमाद् राजन् राजर्षवृषपर्वणः॥
en: That tormentor of foes, who in a defiant spirit challenged even the son of Pulastya, the dispenser of wealth, to a single combat and who encountering the Yakshas and the Rakshasas at the lotus lake (of Kubera) destroyed them (wholesale) has been described by you as seized with fear and dismay. All this I am desirous of hearing; great indeed is my curiosity.

description: The seizure of Bhimasena by the serpent
sn: यदृच्छयाधनुष्पाणिर्बद्धखङ्गो वृकोदरः। ददर्श तद् वनं रम्यं देवगन्धर्वसेवितम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Vrikodara wandering at pleasure armed with (his) bow and sword, beheld that delightful forest frequented by the celestials and the Gandharvas.

description: The seizure of Bhimasena by the serpent
sn: स ददर्श शुभान् देशान् गिरेहिमवतस्तदा। देवर्षिसिद्धचरितानप्सरोगणसेवितान्॥
en: He then viewed those auspicious regions on the Himalaya mountains-frequented by the Devarshis and the Siddhas, inhabited by the Apsaras,

description: The seizure of Bhimasena by the serpent
sn: चकोरैरुपचक्रैश्च पक्षिभिर्जीवजीवकैः। कोकिलै ङ्गराजैश्च तत्र तत्र निनादितान्॥
en: Ringing here and there with the rejoicing of the Chakora, Upachakra, Jivajivaka, Kokila (cuckoo) and Bhringaraja birds,

description: The seizure of Bhimasena by the serpent
sn: नित्यपुष्पफलैर्वृक्षैर्हिमसंस्पर्शकोमलैः। उपेतान् बहुलच्छायैर्मनोनयननन्दनैः॥
en: And abounding in numerous shady trees, always bearing fruits and flowers, soft owing to contact with snow and grateful to the mind and eye.

description: The seizure of Bhimasena by the serpent
sn: स सम्पश्यन् गिरिनदीर्वैदूर्यमणिसंनिभैः। सलिलैर्हिमसंकाशैहँसकारण्डवायुतैः॥
en: He viewed also mountain streamlets containing waters (white and cold) like snow, (sparkling and transparent) like the gem Vaidurya (lapis lazuli) and swarmed with ducks and Karandavas.

description: The seizure of Bhimasena by the serpent
sn: वनानि देवदारूणां मेघानामिव वागुराः। हरिचन्दनमिश्राणि तुङ्गकालीयकान्यपि॥
en: He also saw forests of Devadaru (pine) trees looking like a net for the clouds and also Tunga and Kaliyaka forests interspersed with yellow sandal trees.

description: The seizure of Bhimasena by the serpent
sn: मृगयां परिधावन् स समेषु मस्धन्वसु। विध्यन् मृगान् शरैः शुद्धैश्चचार स महाबलः॥
en: And that exceedingly powerful (Pandava), wandering in the level and dry tracts of the mountain in pursuit of the game, pierced them with unvenomed darts.

description: The seizure of Bhimasena by the serpent
sn: भीमसेनस्तु विख्यातो महान्तं दंष्ट्रिणं बलात्। निघ्नन् नागशतप्राणो वने तस्मिन् महाबलः॥
en: In that forest, the renowned Bhimasena of great prowess and endued with the strength of a hundred elephants, killed (man) dreadful wild boars simply by brute force.

description: The seizure of Bhimasena by the serpent
sn: मृगाणां स वराहाणां महिषाणां महाभुजः। विनिघ्नंस्तत्र तत्रैव भीमो भीमपराक्रमः॥ स मातङ्गशतप्राणो मनुष्यशतवारणः। सिंहशार्दूलविक्रान्तो वने तस्मिन् महाबलः॥
en: And the terribly-powerful Bhima of mighty arms, possessed of the strength of one hundred elephants and capable of encountering an equal number of men and of mighty prowess and strong as the lion or the tiger, killed in that forest many deer, boars and buffaloes.

description: The seizure of Bhimasena by the serpent
sn: वृक्षानुत्पाटयामास तरसा वै बभञ्ज च। पृथिव्याश्च प्रदेशान् ववै नादयंस्तु वनानि च॥
en: (And he) uprooted and broke the trees with great violence, making the earth, the forests and the neighbouring places resound.

description: The seizure of Bhimasena by the serpent
sn: पर्वताग्राणि वै मृद्गन् नादयानश्च विज्वरः। प्रक्षिपन् पादपांश्चापि नादेनापूरयन् महीम्॥ वेगेन न्यपतद् भीमो निर्भयश्च पुनः पुनः। आस्फोटयन् क्ष्वेडयंश्च तलतालांश्च वादयन्॥ चिरसम्बद्धदर्पस्तु भीमसेनो वने तदा। गजेन्द्राश्च महासत्त्वा मृगेन्द्राश्च महाबलाः॥
en: (And) the ever-proud and fearless Bhimasena not subject to decrepitude, crushing the summits of mountains, shouting, felling down the trees, filling the earth with his vociferation's, striking his arms, uttering loud shouts and clapping his hands roamed about in the woods with great violence again and again. Mighty elephants and powerful lions.

description: The seizure of Bhimasena by the serpent
sn: भीमसेनस्य नादेन व्यमुञ्चन्त गुहा भयात्। क्वचित् प्रधावंस्तिष्ठंश्च क्वचिच्चोपविशंस्तथा॥
en: Terrified by the yells of Bhimasena, left their lairs through fear. At some places running, some sitting and at others resting.

description: The seizure of Bhimasena by the serpent
sn: मृगप्रेप्सुर्महारौद्रे वने चरति निर्भयः। स तत्र मनुजव्याघ्रो वने वनचरोपमः॥ पद्भ्यामभिसमापेदे भीमसेनो महाबलः। स प्रविष्टो महारण्ये नादान् नदति चाद्भुतान्॥ त्रासयन् सर्वभूतानि महासत्त्वपराक्रमः। ततो भीमस्य शब्देन भीताः सर्पा गुहाशया:॥
en: (He), desirous of bagging games, wandered about fearlessly in that awfully terrible forest. And in that forest, the exceedingly powerful Bhimasena, valiant and strong as the tiger, roamed on foot like the dweller of woods. And the highly energetic and exceedingly powerful (Bhimasena), entering into that great forest, sent forth strange yells terrifying all the creatures. Then serpents, frightened at the shouts of Bhimasena, hid themselves in the caves.

description: The seizure of Bhimasena by the serpent
sn: अतिक्रान्तास्तु वेगेन जगामानुसृतः शनैः। ततोऽमरवरप्रख्यो भीमसेनो महाबलः॥
en: (But he) overtaken them with speed, leisurely pursued them. Then the highly powerful Bhimasena, resembling the lord of the gods,

description: The seizure of Bhimasena by the serpent
sn: स ददर्श महाकायं भुजङ्गं लोमहर्षणम्। गिरिदुर्गे समापन्नं कायेनावृत्य कन्दरम्॥
en: Saw a terrible-looking serpent of huge shape lie in a mountain fastness, covering the entire cave with its body.

description: The seizure of Bhimasena by the serpent
sn: पर्वताभोगवर्माणमतिकायं महाबलम्। चित्राङ्गमङ्गजैचित्रैर्हरिद्रासदृशच्छविम्॥
en: Its gigantic frame was stretched out like a mountain; and it was possessed of enormous strength. Its skin was speckled with many spots and its colour was yellow.

description: The seizure of Bhimasena by the serpent
sn: गुहाकारेण वक्त्रेण चतुर्दष्ट्रेण राजता। दीप्ताक्षणातिताप्रेण लिहानं सृक्किणी मुहुः॥
en: It had a mouth wide as a cave and furnished with four teeth; its eyes were copper-coloured and glaring and it constantly licked the corners of its mouth.

description: The seizure of Bhimasena by the serpent
sn: त्रासनं सर्वभूतानां कालान्तकयमोपमम्। निःश्वासक्ष्वेडनादेन भत्सर्यन्तमिव स्थितम्॥
en: It was a terror to all creatures and it looked like the (grim) destroyer; and by the hissing noise of its breath it seemed to reprimand (the intruder).

description: The seizure of Bhimasena by the serpent
sn: स भीमं सहसाभ्येत्य पृदाकुः कुपितो भृशम्। जग्राहाजगरो ग्राहो भुजयोरुभयोर्बलात्॥
en: Seeing that, Bhima got so near to him, that goat-devouring serpent suddenly seized him forcibly into the gripe of its two arms.

description: The seizure of Bhimasena by the serpent
sn: तेन संस्पृष्टगात्रस्य भीमसेनस्य वै तदा। संज्ञा मुमोह सहसा वरदानेन तस्य हि॥
en: And in consequence of the boon which the serpent had received, as soon as Bhimasena's body came in contact with that of the serpent, he lost his senses.

description: The seizure of Bhimasena by the serpent
sn: दशनागसहगाणिधारयन्ति हि यद् बलम्। तद् बलं भीमसेनस्य भुजयोरसमं परैः॥
en: The strength of Bhimasena's arms, which by far the most exceeded that of others, was equal to the might of ten thousand elephants.

description: The seizure of Bhimasena by the serpent
sn: स तेजस्वी तथा तेन भुजगेन वशीकृतः। विस्फुरन् शनकैर्भीमो न शशाक विचेष्टितुम्॥
en: Thus subdued by the snake, even that energetic man trembled slowly and was unable to make any effort (to extricate himself).

description: The seizure of Bhimasena by the serpent
sn: नागायुतसमप्राणः सिंहस्कन्धो महाभुजः। गृहीतो व्यजहात् सत्त्वं वरदानविमोहितः॥
en: And seized in the gripe (of the serpent) and charmed by the boon it had received, the leonine-shouldered and mighty armed (Bhima) lost his strength.

description: The seizure of Bhimasena by the serpent
sn: स हि प्रयत्नमकरोत् तीव्रमात्मविमोक्षणे। न चैनमशकद् वीरः कथंचित् प्रतिबाधितुम्॥
en: That hero tried his very best to extricate himself, but in way succeeded in overpowering it. no VYTAUS ".

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच स भीमसेनस्तेजस्वी तथा सर्पवशं गतः। चिन्तयामास सर्पस्य वीर्यमत्यद्भुतं महत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : . The energetic Bhimasena being thus overpowered by the serpent began to ponder on the mighty and wonderful strength of the snake.

sn: उवाच च महासधैं कामया ब्रूहि पन्नग। कस्त्वं भो भुजगश्रेष्ठ किं मया च करिष्यसि॥
en: And he said to that mighty snake “O best of serpents, O snake, kindly tell me who you are and what you will do with me.

sn: पाण्डवो भीमसेनोऽहंधर्मराजादनन्तरः। नागायुतसमप्राणस्त्वया नीतः कथं वशम्॥
en: I am the Pandava, Bhimasena and the younger brother to Dharmaraja. How is it that I, who am possessed of the strength of ten thousand elephants, have been brought under your power?

sn: सिंहाः केसरिणो व्याघ्रा महिषा वारणास्तथा। समागताश्च शतशो निहताश्च मया युधि॥
en: I have in battle slain countless lions, lions having manes, tigers, buffaloes and elephants all assembled together,

sn: राक्षसाश्च पिशाचाश्च पन्नगाश्च महाबलाः। भुजवेगमशक्ता मे सोढुं पन्नगसत्तम॥
en: O excellent of serpents, the exceedingly powerful Rakshasas, Pishachas and Pannagas cannot endure the force of my even arms.

sn: नु किं विद्याबलं किं नु वरदानमथो तव। उद्योगमपि कुर्वाणो वशगोऽस्मि कृतस्त्वया॥
en: Is it my virtue of any science or by that of any boon conferred on you that you have been able to overpower me inspite of my exertions?

sn: असत्यो विक्रमो नृणामिति मेधीयते मतिः। यथेदं मे त्वया नाग बलं प्रतिहतं महत्॥
en: Now it appears to my mind that the strength of men is fruitless, since, O serpent, you have overmastered my great strength."

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच इत्येवंवादिनं वीरं भीममक्लिष्टकारिणम्। भोगेन महता गृह्य समन्तात् पर्यवेष्टयत्॥
en: When the heroic Bhima of great achievements was saying all this, the serpent seized him and coiled him all round with its gigantic body.

sn: निगृह्येनं महाबाहुं ततः स भुजगस्तदा। विमुच्यास्य भुजौ पीनाविदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Having thus overpowered that one of mighty arms and then liberated his plump hands the serpent said these words.

sn: दिष्टस्त्वं क्षुधितस्याद्य देवैर्भक्षो महाभुज। दिष्ट्या कालस्य महतः प्रियाः प्राणा हि देहिनाम्।।
en: O mighty armed being, I have been hungry for a long time. It is to my good fortune, therefore, that you have been today, destined by the god for my food; for life is dear to all corporeal beings.

sn: यथा त्विदं मया प्राप्तं सर्वरूपमरिंदम। तथावश्यं मया ख्याप्यं तवाद्य शृणु सत्तम॥
en: O tormentor of foes, it should be surely narrated by me today how have I worn this snake-shape. Listen, O virtuous being.

sn: इमामवस्थां सम्प्राप्तो ह्यहं कोपान्मनीषिणाम्। शापस्यान्तं परिप्रेप्सुः सर्वं तत् कथयामि ते॥
en: I have been brought down to this state on account of the anger of the Maharshis, now desirous of expiating the curse I shall relate to you all about it.

sn: नहुषो नाम राजर्षिर्व्यक्तं ते श्रोत्रमागतः तवैव पूर्वः पूर्वेषामायोर्वंशधरः सुतः॥
en: It is known (to everybody) that there was a royal sage, named Nahusha and you too, no doubt have heard of him. He was the ancestor of your forefathers, the son of Ayu and the perpetuator of his race.

sn: सोऽहं शापादगस्त्यस्य ब्राह्मणानवमन्य च। इमामवस्थामापन्नः पश्य दैवमिदं मम॥
en: I am he. Owing to my disregard for the Brahmanas I have fallen into this plight by the curse of Agastya. Now behold my fated wretchedness.

sn: त्वां चेदवध्यं दायादमतीव प्रियदर्शनम्। अहमद्योपयोक्ष्यामि विधानं पश्य यादृशम्॥
en: Though you are my descendant, exceedingly handsome and therefore should not be killed by me, yet I will eat you up today.

sn: न हि मे मुच्यते कश्चित् कथंचित् प्रग्रहं गतः। गजो वा महिषो वापि षष्ठे काले नरोत्तम॥
en: O the best of mortals, whether it be a cow or a buffalo, whatever comes within my reach during the sixth part of the day, cannot escape (from me).

sn: नासि केवलसर्पण तिर्यग्योनिषु वर्तता। गृहीतः कौरवश्रेष्ठ वरदानमिदं मम॥
en: O the best of the Kurus, you have been overpowered not by the strength of an animal of a lower order, but by virtue of the boon that it received.

sn: पतता हि विमानायान्मया शक्रासनाद् द्रुतम्। कुरु शापान्तमित्युक्तो भगवान् मुनिसत्तमः॥
en: When I was rapidly falling (down on earth) from the throne of Shakra, placed in front of the palace, I besought the divine and excellent sage (Agastya) to free me from the curse.

sn: स मामुवाच तेजस्वी कृपयाभिपरिप्लुतः। मोक्षस्ते भविता राजन् कस्माच्चित् कालपर्ययात्॥
en: (At which) that energetic sage, filled with pity, replied to me "you will get rid of it after the expiration some time."

sn: ततोऽस्मि पतितो भूमौ न च मामजहात् स्मृतिः। स्मार्तमस्ति पुराणं मे यथैवाधिगतं तथा।॥
en: I then fell down to the earth, but my memory did not fail me. Therefore do I still remember the past, however ancient it might be.

sn: यस्तु ते व्याहतान् प्रश्नान् प्रतिब्रूयाद् विभागवित्। स त्वां मोक्षयिता शापादिति मामब्रवीदृषिः॥
en: That sage (Agastya) told me also however conversant with the relation subsisting between the soul and the Supreme being shall be able to answer your questions shall free you, from the curse.

sn: गृहीतस्य त्वया राजन् प्राणिनोऽपि बलीयसः। सत्त्वभ्रंशोऽधिकस्यापि सर्वस्याशु भविष्यति॥
en: And, O king, beings stronger than yourself if seized by you, shall instantly lose their strength.”

sn: इति चाप्यहमश्रौषं वचस्तेषां दयावताम्। मयि संजातहार्दनामथ तेऽन्तर्हिता द्विजाः॥
en: I heard all these words of those kind-hearted sages who conceived an attachment towards ones me. (And) those twice-born then vanished.

sn: सोऽहं परमदुष्कर्मा वसामि निरयेऽशुचौ। सर्पयोनिमिमां प्राप्य कालकाक्षी महाद्युते॥
en: (Thenceforth) I, who had committed numerous reprehensible acts, having become a serpent, O highly resplendent being, have been dwelling in filthy hell (anxiously) awaiting (the time of the expiration of my curse).

sn: तमुवाच महाबाहुर्भीमसेनो भुजङ्गमम्। न च कुप्ये महासर्प न चात्मानं विगर्हये।।२५।
en: Then the mighty-armed Bhimasena said ic the snake "O highly-energetic creature, I am neither angry nor do I blame myself,

sn: यस्मादभावी भावी वा मनुष्यः सुखदुःखयोः। आगमे यदि वापाये न तत्र ग्लपयेन्मनः॥
en: Because man has sometimes the power of and sometimes becomes powerless in bringing or destroying happiness or sorrow. None should on that account, distress his mind.

sn: दैवं पुरुषकारेण को वञ्चयितुमर्हति। दैवमेव परं मन्ये पुरुषार्थो निरर्थकः॥
en: Who can rise superior to Destiny by selfexertion? I think Destiny is supreme and selfexertion fruitless.

sn: पश्य दैवोपघाताद्धि भुजवीर्यव्यपाश्रयम्। इमामवस्थां सम्प्राप्तमनिमित्तमिहाद्य माम्॥
en: For, behold, struck by (the perversity of) Destiny I have today lost the strength of my arms and been reduced to this condition for no evident cause.

sn: किंतु नाद्यानुशोचामि तथाऽऽत्मानं विनाशितम्। यथा तु विपिने न्यस्तान् भ्रातृन् राज्यपरिच्युतान्।।२९।
en: But this day I do not so much grieve for my death as for my brothers, who have been driven from their kingdom into exile in the forest.

sn: हिमवांश्च सुदुर्गोऽयं यक्षराक्षससंकुलः। मां समुद्रीक्षमाणास्ते प्रपतिष्यन्ति विह्वलाः॥
en: This Himalayan (mountain) is inaccessible and full of the Yakshas and the Rakshasas. Here looking about for me they will be dejected and crest fallen.

sn: विनष्टमथ मां श्रुत्वा भविष्यन्ति निरुद्यमाः। धर्मशीला मया ते हि बाध्यन्ते राज्यगृद्धिना॥
en: Hearing of my death they will give up all exertions (for the recovery of their kingdom). (For), it was I, who, eager for the recovery of our kingdom, incited those pious ones, by harsh words (to make exertions to regain it),

sn: अथवा नार्जुनोधीमान् विषादमुपयास्यति। सर्वास्त्रविदनाधृष्यो देवगन्धर्वराक्षसैः॥
en: Or, (it may be) that Arjuna (alone) will not grieve (for me); because he is intelligent, versed in the science of) all weapons and unconquerable by the gods, the Gandharvas and the Rakshasas,

sn: समर्थः स महाबाहुरेकोऽपि सुमहाबलः। देवराजमपि स्थानात् प्रच्यावयितुपञ्जसा॥ किं पुनधृतराष्ट्रस्य पुत्रं दुर्दूतदेविनम्। विद्विष्टं सर्वलोकस्य दम्भमोहपरायणम्॥
en: Not to speak of the son of Dhritarashtra, that deceitful gambler, despised by all men and full of arrogance and ignorance, he (Arjuna) of mighty arms and endued with exceeding prowess is alone no doubt, capable of tearing the lord of the celestials from his throne.

sn: मातरं चैव शोचामि कृपणां पुत्रगृद्धिनीम्। यास्माकं नित्यमाशास्ते महत्त्वमधिकं परैः॥
en: And I mourn for my poor mother fond of her children, who is always desirous of our greatness superior to that ever attained by our enemies.

sn: तस्याः कथं त्वनाथाया मद्विनाशाद् भुजङ्गमा सफलास्ते भविष्यन्ति मयि सर्वे मनोरथाः॥
en: And, O serpent, will all the hopes and desires that helpless woman has in me prove fruitless on account of my death?

sn: नकुलः सहदेवश्च यमौ च गुरुवर्तिनौ। मद्बाहुबलसंगुप्तौ नित्यं पुरुषमानिनौ।॥
en: And the twins, Nakula and Sahadeva, ever proud of (my) manliness and always protected by the prowess of my arms and who ever follow (me) their lord,

sn: भविष्यतो निरुत्साहौ भ्रष्टवीर्यपराक्रमौ। मद्विनाशात् परिघुनाविति मे वर्तते मतिः॥
en: Will, at my death, be dispirited, deprived of strength and energy and smitten with sorrow. This is what I think of now."

sn: एवंविधं बहु तदा विललाप वृकोदरः। भुजङ्गभोगसंरुद्धो नाशकच्च विचेष्टितुम्॥
en: In this strain Vrikodara gave vent to his grief profusely. But being coiled by the body of the snake. could not make any exertions (to extricate himself from its folds).

sn: युधिष्ठिरस्तु कौन्तेयो बभूवास्वस्थचेतनः। अनिष्टदर्शनान् घोरानुत्पातान् परिचिन्तयन्॥
en: On the other hand, Yudhishthira, the son of Kunti, beholding and thinking of terrible ill omens became uneasy.

sn: दारुणं ह्यशिवं नादं शिवा दक्षिणतः स्थिता। दीप्तायां दिशि वित्रस्ता रौति तस्याश्रमस्य ह॥
en: Alarmed at beholding the points all ablaze, Jackals, stationing themselves in the right of that hermitage, began to send forth dreadful and inauspicious howls.

sn: एकपक्षाक्षिचरणा वर्तिका घोरदर्शना। रक्तं वमन्ती ददृशे प्रत्यादित्यमभासुरा॥
en: And facing the sun, the ugly and dreadfullooking Vartika, having only one leg, one eye and one wing, was seen to vomit blood.

sn: प्रववौ चानिलो रूक्षश्चण्डः शर्करकर्षणः। अपसव्यानि सर्वाणि मृगपक्षिरुतानि च॥
en: And drawing in (volumes of) grifts the wind began to blow dryly and furiously. In the right all the birds and beasts began to bewail.

sn: पृष्ठतो वायसः कृष्णो याहि याहीति शंसति। मुहुर्मुहुः स्फुरति च दक्षिणोऽस्य भुज-तथा॥
en: And at the back the black-crows cried "go, go." And his (Yudhishthira's) right hand began to tremble constantly;

sn: हृदयं चरणश्चापि वामोऽस्य परितप्यति। सव्यस्याक्ष्णो विकारश्चाप्यनिष्टः समपद्यत॥
en: And his heart and left leg began to twitch and his left eye auguring evils, began to contract. to

sn: धर्मराजोऽपि मेधावी मन्यमानो महद् भयम्। द्रौपदी परिपप्रच्छ क्व भीम इति भारत॥
en: And, O Bharata, the intelligent Dharmaraja apprehending some imminent danger asked Draupadi "where is Bhima”?

sn: शशंस तस्मै पाञ्चाली चिरयातं वृकोदरम्। स प्रतस्थे महाबाहुधौम्येन सहितो नृपः॥
en: The daughter of Panchala answered "Vrikodara has been long out.” Then he of mighty arms, accompanied by Dhaumya left (the place),

sn: द्रौपद्या रक्षणं कार्यमित्युवाचधनंजयम्। नकुलं सहदेवं च व्यादिदेश द्विजान् प्रति॥
en: After having given instructions Dhananjaya for the protection of Draupadi and having directed Nakula and Sahadeva to take care of the Brahmanas.

sn: स तस्य पदमुन्नीय तस्मादेवाश्रमात् प्रभुः। मृगयामास कौन्तेयो भीमसेनं महावने॥
en: Then the royal son of Kunti left that hermitage and tracing his (Bhima's) foot prints began to search about for Bhimasena in that mighty forest.

sn: स प्राची दिशमास्थाय महतो गजयूथपान्। ददर्श पृथिवीं चिट्ठीमस्य परिचिछिताम्॥
en: In the west he found many powerful leaders of elephant (killed) and saw the ground impressed with Bhima's (foot) prints.

sn: ततो मृगसहराणि मृगेन्द्राणां शतानि च। पतितानि वने दृष्ट्वा मार्ग तस्याविशनृपः॥
en: Then beholding many thousands of deer and hundreds of lions lying (dead) in that forest, the king became aware of his (Bhima's) route.

sn: धावतस्तस्य वीरस्य मृगार्थं वातरंहसः। ऊरुवातविनिर्भग्ना द्रुमा व्यावर्जिताः पथि॥
en: And he behold numerous trees broken by the wind, caused by Bhima's thighs, lying scattered on the way as that hero of fleet as the wind pursued the game.

sn: स गत्वा तैस्तदा चिद्वैर्ददर्श गिरिगह्वरे। रूक्षमारुतभूयिष्ठे निष्पत्रदुमसंकुले।॥ ईरिणे निर्जले देशे कण्टकिदुमसंकुले। अश्मस्थाणुक्षुपाकीर्णे सुदुर्गे विषमोत्कटे। गृहीतं भुजगेन्द्रेण निश्चेष्टमनुजं तदा॥
en: And following those marks he arrived at a brackish inaccessible, rough and dangerous place full of dry winds and leafless trees, covered with thorny plants and abounding in gravels, stumps and bushes: and there in a mountain cave he discovered his younger brother (lying) stupefied in the folds of that best of snakes.

description: The colloquy between Yudhishthira and the Snake
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच युधिष्ठिरस्तमासाद्य सर्पभोगेन वेष्टितम्। दयितं भ्रातरधीमानिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : The intellectual Yudhishthira, beholding his dear brother coiled by the body of the snake addressed him thus.

description: The colloquy between Yudhishthira and the Snake
sn: कुन्तीमातः कथमिमापापदं त्वमवाप्तवान्। कश्शायं पर्वताभोगप्रतिमः पन्नगोत्तमः॥
en: “O son of Kunti, how have you met with this disaster? And who is this best of serpents endued with a body (huge) as a mountain.

description: The colloquy between Yudhishthira and the Snake
sn: सधर्मराजमालक्ष्य भ्राता भ्रातरमग्रजम्। कथयामास तत् सर्वं ग्रहणादि विचेष्टितम्॥
en: beholding his elder brother Dharmaraja, he narrated to him fully as to how he came into the clutches of the serpent.

description: The colloquy between Yudhishthira and the Snake
sn: भीम उवाच अयमार्य महासत्त्वो भक्षार्थं मां गृहीतवान्। नहुषो नाम राजर्षिः प्राणवानिव संस्थितः॥
en: Bhimasena said: O worshipful brother, this powerful (serpent) has caught me for his food. He is the royal sage Nahusha living in the seipent-shape.

description: The colloquy between Yudhishthira and the Snake
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच मुच्यतामयमायुष्मन् भ्राता मेऽमितविक्रमः। वयमाहारमन्यं ते दास्यामः क्षुनिवारणम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said: O long-lived serpent, (kindly) liberate my exceedingly powerful brother. We will give you some other food to satisfy your hunger.

description: The colloquy between Yudhishthira and the Snake
sn: सर्प उवाच आहारो राजपुत्रोऽयं मया प्राप्तो मुखागतः। गम्यतां नेह स्थातव्यं श्वो भवानपि मे भवेत्॥
en: The snake replied Having come to my mouth, I have got this son of a king for my food. Do leave this place. You ought not to remain here. For, (if do) I will eat you tomorrow.

description: The colloquy between Yudhishthira and the Snake
sn: व्रतमेतन्महाबाहो विषयं मम यो व्रजेत्। स मे भक्षो भवेत् तात त्वं चापि विषये मम॥
en: O mighty-armed child, it is (so) ordained that he who will step into my jurisdiction, shall become my food. You are also in my jurisdiction.

description: The colloquy between Yudhishthira and the Snake
sn: चिरेणाद्य मयाऽऽहारः प्राप्तोऽयमनुजस्तव। नाहमेनं विमोक्ष्यामि न चान्यमभिकाझये।॥
en: After a long period (of abstinence) I have got this your younger brother for my food. I will not (therefore) release him. Nor do I want any other meal.

description: The colloquy between Yudhishthira and the Snake
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच देवो वा यदि वा दैत्य उरगो वा भवान् यदि। सत्यं सर्प वचो ब्रूहि पृच्छति त्वां युधिष्ठिरः। किमर्थं च त्वया चस्तो भीमसेनो भुजङ्गम॥
en: Yudhishthira said: O serpent, Yudhishthira asks you to tell (him) truly whether you are a god or a demon or a uraga. What have you seized Bhimasena for?

description: The colloquy between Yudhishthira and the Snake
sn: किमाहृत्य विदित्वा वा प्रीतिस्ते स्याद् भुजङ्गम्। किमाहारं प्रयच्छामि कथं मुञ्चेद् भवानिमम्॥
en: O snake, by obtaining or knowing what will you be satisfied? What food shall I provide for you? Under what conditions will you let him off?

description: The colloquy between Yudhishthira and the Snake
sn: सर्प उवाच नहुषो नाम राजाहमासं पूर्वस्तवानघ। प्रथितः पञ्चमः सोमादायोः पुत्रो नराधिप।॥
en: The snake replied O sinless being, O monarch, I was your ancestor, the son of Ayu and fifth in descent from Soma and was known by the name of king Nahusha.

description: The colloquy between Yudhishthira and the Snake
sn: क्रतुभिस्तपसा चैव स्वाध्यायेन दमेन च। त्रैलोक्यैश्चर्यमव्यचं प्राप्तोऽहं विक्रमेण च॥
en: By sacrifices, asceticism, study of the Vedas, self-control and prowess I easily gained mastery over the three worlds.

description: The colloquy between Yudhishthira and the Snake
sn: तदैश्वर्यं समासाद्य दो मामगमत् तदा। सह्रां हि द्विजातीनामुवाह शिबिकां मम॥
en: Having attained to such an eminence I was elated with pride. Thousands of Brahmanas carried my palanquin.

description: The colloquy between Yudhishthira and the Snake
sn: ऐश्वर्यमदमत्तोऽहमवमन्य ततो द्विजान्। इमामगस्त्येन दशामानीतः पृथिवीपते॥
en: Intoxicated with the drink of prosperity I then insulted the twice-born ones; and was, (therefore), O monarch, brought to this (miserable) plight by Agastya,

description: The colloquy between Yudhishthira and the Snake
sn: न तु मामजहात् प्रज्ञा यावदद्येति पाण्डव। तस्यैवानुग्रहाद् राजन्नगस्त्यस्य महात्मनः॥
en: But, O Pandava, even till now I have not lost my memory. And it is by the grace of the highsouled Agastya,

description: The colloquy between Yudhishthira and the Snake
sn: षष्ठे काले मयाऽऽहारः प्राप्तोऽयमनुजस्तव। नाहमेनं विमोक्ष्यामि न चान्यदपि कामये।॥
en: That I have got your younger brother in the sixth portion of the day, for my meal. I will neither release him nor do I want any other (food).

description: The colloquy between Yudhishthira and the Snake
sn: प्रश्नानुच्चारितानद्य व्याहरिष्यसि चेन्मम। अथ पश्चाद् विमोक्ष्यामि भ्रातरं ते वृकोदरम्॥
en: But if today you answer the questions put by me, I will then liberate your brother Vrikodara.

description: The colloquy between Yudhishthira and the Snake
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच ब्रूहि सर्प यथाकामं प्रतिवक्ष्यामि ते वचः। अपि चेच्छक्नुयां प्रीतिमाहर्तुं ते भुजङ्गम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said: Ask (me), O serpent whatever you like. In order to cause your satisfaction I shall, if I can, answer your questions.

description: The colloquy between Yudhishthira and the Snake
sn: वेद्यं च ब्राह्मणेनेह तद् भवान् वेत्ति केवलम्। सर्पराज ततः श्रुत्वा प्रतिवक्ष्यामि ते वचः॥
