en: You are no doubt aware what ought to be known by the Brahmanas. Therefore, O king of snakes, on hearing your words I shall answer them.

description: The colloquy between Yudhishthira and the Snake
sn: सर्प उवाच ब्राह्मणः को भवेद् राजन् वेद्यं किं च युधिष्ठिर। ब्रवीह्यतिमतिं त्वां हि वाक्यैरनुमिमीमहे॥
en: The snake said : O king, whom can we call a Brahmana and O Yudhishthira, what is it that ought to be known? From what you have said I deem you to be endowed with very high intelligence.

description: The colloquy between Yudhishthira and the Snake
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच सत्यं दानं क्षमा शीलमानृशंस्यं तपो घृणा। दृश्यन्ते यत्र नागेन्द्र स ब्राह्मण इति स्मृतः॥
en: Yudhishthira said : O monarch of snakes, it is said that he is a Brahmana in whom are found (the qualities of) truthfulness, charity, forgiveness, good conduct, benevolence, asceticism and mercy.

description: The colloquy between Yudhishthira and the Snake
sn: वेद्यं सर्प परं ब्रह्म निर्दुःखमसुखं च यत्। यत्र गत्वा न शोचन्ति भवतः किं विवक्षितम्॥
en: And, O serpent, that which ought to be . known is the Supreme Brahma (universal soul) devoid of the feelings of) pleasure and pain and attaining access to which creatures are past all misery.

description: The colloquy between Yudhishthira and the Snake
sn: सर्प उवाच चातुर्वण्र्यं प्रमाणं च सत्यं च ब्रह्म चैव हि। शूद्रेष्वपि च सत्यं च दानमक्रोध एव च। आनृशंस्यमहिंसा च घृणा चैव युधिष्ठिर॥
en: The serpent said : O Yudhishthira, even in the Shudras are found truthfulness, charity, forgiveness, benevolence, mercy, kindness and knowledge of the Veda which promotes the welfare of the four orders, which is true and which is the guide in religious matters.

description: The colloquy between Yudhishthira and the Snake
sn: वेद्यं यच्चात्र निर्दुःखमसुखं च नराधिप। ताभ्यां हीनं पदं चान्यन्न तदस्तीति लक्षये॥
en: And, O king of men, that which is to be known is asserted by you as devoid of pleasure and pain; but I do not find any such thing in which these feelings are absent,

description: The colloquy between Yudhishthira and the Snake
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच शूद्रे तु यद् भवेल्लम द्विजे तच्च न विद्यते। न वै शूद्रो भवेच्छूद्रो ब्राह्मणो न च ब्राह्मणः॥
en: Yudhishthira said : Thc Shudra in whom these characteristics are present is no Shudra (i.e.) something higher, a Brahma and the Brahmana in whom these are wanting is no Brahmana at all (i.e.) a Shudra.

description: The colloquy between Yudhishthira and the Snake
sn: यत्रैतल्लक्ष्यते सर्प वृत्तं स ब्राह्मणः स्मृतः। यत्रैतन्न भवेत् सर्प तं शूद्रमिति निर्दिशेत्॥
en: And, O serpent, it is asserted that he who is distinguished by these qualities is a Brahmana and he who does not posses them is a Shudra.

description: The colloquy between Yudhishthira and the Snake
sn: यत् पुनर्भवता प्रोक्तं न वेद्यं विद्यतीति च। ताभ्यां हीनमतोऽन्यत्र पदमस्तीति चेदपि॥
en: Again, as regards your remark that the object to be known does not exist, for, nothing that is devoid of these (feelings) of pleasure and pain can have any existence.

description: The colloquy between Yudhishthira and the Snake
sn: एवमेतन्मतं सर्प ताभ्यां हीनं न विद्यते। यथा शीतोष्णयोर्मध्ये भवेन्नोष्णं न शीतता॥
en: It seems (at indeed first sight) that existence is impossible without these (feelings). But as cold is characterised by an absence of heat and heat cold,

description: The colloquy between Yudhishthira and the Snake
sn: एवं वै सुखदुःखाभ्यां हीनमस्ति पदं क्वचित्। एषा मम मतिः सर्प यथा वा मन्यते भवान्॥
en: So cannot there exist an object characterised by the absence of both these feelings (of pleasure and pain). O Serpent, this is my opinion, what do you say?

description: The colloquy between Yudhishthira and the Snake
sn: सर्प उवाच यदि ते वृत्ततो राजन् ब्राह्मणः प्रसमीक्षितः। वृथा जातिस्तदाऽऽयुष्मन् कृतिर्यावन्न विद्यते॥
en: The serpent said : If, O monarch, as you assert, a Brahmana is recognised by certain virtues, then, O longlived one, the distinction of castes is to no purpose so long as he does not posses these qualities.

description: The colloquy between Yudhishthira and the Snake
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच जातिरत्र महासर्प मनुष्यत्वे महामते। संकरात् सर्ववर्णानां दुष्परीक्ष्येति मे मतिः॥
en: Yudhishthira said : O highly intelligent and mighty snake, I think, here in this world it is very difficult to ascertain one's caste on account of promiscuous intercourse of all the orders.

description: The colloquy between Yudhishthira and the Snake
sn: सर्वे सर्वास्वपत्यानि जनयन्ति सदा नराः। वाङ्मथुनमथो जन्म मरणं च समं नृणाम्॥
en: Men of all the four orders are without restriction constantly begetting children on women of all the castes. And speech, cohabitation, birth and death of men of all the orders are similar in all respects.

description: The colloquy between Yudhishthira and the Snake
sn: इदमाएं प्रमाणं च ये यजामह इत्यपि। तस्माच्छीलं प्रधानेष्टं विदुर्ये तत्त्वदर्शिनः॥
en: The proof of this, i.e. the difficulty of ascertaining one's caste is found in such expressions, made use of by the Rishis, as *whatever caste may belong to, we celebrate the sacrifice." It is, on this account, that the wise have asserted that the character is the chief and needful thing.

description: The colloquy between Yudhishthira and the Snake
sn: प्राङ् नाभिवर्धनात् पुंसो जातकर्म विधीयते। तत्रास्य माता सावित्री पिता त्वाचार्य उच्यते॥
en: The natal ceremony of a male person is performed even before the severance of the navel chord. On that occasion his mother is designated Savitri and his father Acharya (priest).

description: The colloquy between Yudhishthira and the Snake
sn: तावच्छूद्रसमो ह्येष यावद् वेदे न जायते। तस्मिन्नेवं मतिद्वैधे मनुः स्वायम्भुवोऽब्रवीत्॥
en: Before initiation into the Vedas every man is regarded as a Shudra. There being a difference of opinion on the point Svyambhuva Manu has laid down;

description: The colloquy between Yudhishthira and the Snake
sn: कृतकृत्याः पुनर्वर्णा यदि वृत्तं न विद्यते। संकरस्त्वत्र नागेन्द्र बलवान् प्रसमीक्षितः॥
en: That if having gone through the purificatory rites (as laid down in the Vedas) the first three orders do not regulate their conduct, according to thein, in that case, O mightiest of serpents, the mixed castes should be considered as superior to them

description: The colloquy between Yudhishthira and the Snake
sn: यत्रेदानीं महासर्प संस्कृतं वृत्तमिष्यते। तं ब्राह्मणमहं पूर्वमुक्तवान् भुजगोत्तम॥
en: O great Snake, O excellent Serpent, I have ere now designated him as a Brahmana who observes the principles of good behaviour.

description: The colloquy between Yudhishthira and the Snake
sn: सर्प उवाच श्रुतं विदितवेद्यस्य तव वाक्यं युधिष्ठिर। भक्षयेयमहं कस्माद् भ्रातरं ते वृकोदरम्॥
en: The snake said: O Yudhishthira, I have listened to your words. You are acquainted with what ought to be known. (Therefore) how can I (now) devour your brother Vrikodara?

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच भवानेतादृशो लोके वेदवेदाङ्गपारगः। ब्रूहि किं कुर्वतः कर्म भवेद् गतिरनुत्तमा॥
en: Yudhishthira said: (O Serpent), in this world, you are so superiority versed in the Vedas and the Vedangas, that I should like you will iell me, by what (sorts of) acts men can obtain heaven.

sn: सर्प उवाच पात्रे दत्त्वा प्रियाण्युक्त्वा सत्यमुक्त्वा च भारत। अहिंसानिरतः स्वर्ग गच्छेदिति मतिर्मम॥
en: The Serpent said : In my opinion, O Bharata, by bestowal of alims on deserving objects, endearing words, truthfulness and unenviousness one can have access to heaven.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच दानाद् वा सर्प सत्याद् वा किमतो गुरु दृश्यते। अहिंसाप्रिययोश्चैव गुरुलाघवमुच्यताम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said: Snake, between benevolence and truthfulness, which is more praiseworthy? And tell me as regards unenviousness and good behaviour which is the more and which is the less important.

sn: सर्प उवाच दानं च सत्यं तत्त्वं वा अहिंसा प्रियमेव च। एषां कार्यगरीयस्त्वाद् दृश्यते गुरुलाघवम्॥
en: The Snake replied The superiority or inferiority among charity, truthfulness, forbearance from malice and sweet speech is estimated at by the benefit which each of these tends to produce.

sn: कस्माच्चिद् दानयोगाद्धि सत्यमेव विशिष्यते। सत्यवाक्याच्च राजेन्द्र किंचिद् दानं विशिष्यते॥
en: Sometimes truthfulness is considered superior to some charitable acts. And, O king of kings, sometimes charity is deemed more praiseworthy than true speech.

sn: एवमेव महेष्वास प्रियवाक्यान्महीपते। अहिंसा दृश्यते गुर्वी ततश्च प्रियमिष्यते॥
en: And similarly, O lord of the earth, O mighty monarch, abstenance from malice is (sometimes) deemed superior to sweet speech and vice versa.

sn: एवमेतद् भवेद् राजन् कार्यापेक्षमनन्तरम्। यदभिप्रेतमन्यत् ते ब्रूहि यावद् ब्रवीम्यहम्॥
en: Thus, O monarch, (their superiority or inferiority) depends on their utility. Now if you have anything more to ask, speak out and I shall solve your doubts.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच कथं स्वर्गे गति: सर्प कर्मणां च फलंध्रुवम्। अशरीरस्य दृश्येत प्रब्रूहि विषयांश्च मे॥
en: (Kindly) tell me O Serpent, how the access of a disembodied being to heaven, how his enjoyment of the rewards and endurance of the punishment consequent on its acts and how its perception through the senses, be conceived. can

sn: सर्प उवाच तिगे वै गतयो राजन् परिदृष्टाः स्वकर्मभिः। मानुषं स्वर्गवासश्च तिर्यग्योनिश्च तत् त्रिधा॥
en: The Snake replied O king, on account of their own (meritorious or evil) acts men are seen to attain one of the three conditions of rebirth as men, heavenly existence or birth among the lower animals.

sn: तत्र वै मानुषाल्लोकाद् दानादिभिरतन्द्रितः। अहिंसार्थसमायुक्तैः कारणैः स्वर्गमश्नुते॥
en: By charity, unenviousness, absence of slothfulness and by self-exertion one goes to heaven from this state of men.

sn: विपरीतैश्च राजेन्द्र कारणैर्मानुषो भवेत्। तिर्यग्योनिस्तथा तात विशेषश्चात्र वक्ष्यते॥
en: (But) by contrary acts, O king of kings, one is either reborn among men or among lower animals. (Therefore)O child, it is particularly laid in this subject,

sn: कामक्रोधसमायुक्तो हिंसालोभसमन्वितः। मनुष्यत्वात् परिभ्रष्टस्तिर्यग्योनौ प्रसूयते॥
en: That he who is subject to lust, anger malice and temptations, being degraded from the human state again takes his birth among the lower animals,

sn: तिर्यग्योन्याः पृथग्भावो मनुष्यार्थे विधीयते। गवादिभ्यस्तथाश्वेभ्यो देवत्वमपि दृश्यते॥
en: And as is laid down in the Vedas, gets rid of the existence among the lower animals in order to attain the human state again. And cows, cattle and horses and other animals are (even sometimes) seen to attain to divine life.

sn: सोऽयमेता गतीस्तात जन्तुश्चरति कार्यवान्। नित्ये महति चात्मानमवस्थापयते द्विजः॥
en: O child, such is the transmigration of a creature according to his (good or evil) actions. But he that is wise reposes his soul in the everlasting Spirit.

sn: जातो जातश्च बलवद् भुङ्क्ते चात्मा स देहवान्। फलार्थस्तात निष्पृक्तः प्रजापालनभावनः॥
en: The embodied spirit enchained by Fate and enjoying the pleasure or suffering the pain consequent on its acts, takes birth repeatedly. But he that has lost touch of his action is conscious of the destiny of all born creatures.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच शब्दे स्पर्श च रूपे च तथैव रसगन्धयोः। तस्याधिष्ठानमव्यचो ब्रूहि सर्प यथातथम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said : Tell me, O Serpent, truly and without hurry how the spirit (parted from the corporeal frame) becomes cognisant of sound, touch, form, smell and taste.

sn: किं न गृहणाति विषयान् युगपच्च महामते। एतावदुच्यतां चोक्तं सर्वं पन्नगसत्तम।॥
en: And, O high-minded being, do you not simultaneously feel the sensations of touch, taste, etc., by means of the senses? O best of Snakes, (kindly) answer all these questions of mine.

sn: सर्प उवाच यदात्मद्रव्यमायुष्मन् देहसंश्रयणान्वितम्। करणाधिष्ठितं भोगानुपभुङ्क्ते यथाविधि॥
en: The Snake replied O long-lived being, the thing termed Atman taking refuge in a physical frame and manifesting itself through the organs of sense, enjoys properly the perceptible objects.

sn: ज्ञानं चैवात्र बुद्धिश्च मनश्च भरतर्षभ। तस्य भोगाधिकरणे करणानि निबोध मे॥
en: O the best of the Bharatas, know that the senses, the mind and the intellect assisting the soul in its enjoyment of the perceptible objects are called Karanas.

sn: मनसा तात पर्येति क्रमशो विषयानिमान्। विषयायतनस्थो हि भूतात्मा क्षेत्रमास्थितः॥
en: O my child, the soul moving out of its proper place and assisted by the mind acting through the organs of sense-the recipients of all sensations-gradually perceives all the sensible objects.

sn: तत्र चापि नरव्याघ्र मनो जन्तोर्विधीयते। तस्माद् युगपदत्रास्य ग्रहणं नोपपद्यते॥
en: O the most exalted of men the mind of creatures is the cause of all perceptions; and therefore it cannot at one and the same time perceive a plurality of objects,

sn: स आत्मा पुरुषव्याघ्र भ्रुवोरन्तरमाश्रितः। बुद्धिं द्रव्येषु सृजति विविधेषु परावराम्॥
en: The Soul, O the most valiant of mortals stationing itself between the eye brows, sends the high and the low intellect to different objects (of sense).

sn: वुद्धेश्त्तरकाला च वेदना दृश्यते बुधैः। एष वै राजशार्दूल विधिः क्षेत्रज्ञभावनः॥
en: O best of kings, knowledge which the yogis drive from the operation of intelligence, manifests the action of the Soul.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच मनसश्चापि बुद्धेश्च ब्रूहि मे लक्षणं परम्। एतदध्यात्मविदुषां परं कार्यं विधीयते॥
en: Yudhishthira said : Tell me the (kindly) the prominent characteristics of the mind and the intellect (respectively); (because) the knowledge (of their functions) is said to be the principal requirements of those conversant with the Supreme being

sn: सर्प उवाच बुद्धिरात्मानुगा तात उत्पातेन विधीयते। तदाश्रिता हि संज्ञैषा बुद्धिस्तस्यैषिणी भवेत्॥
en: The Snake answered Through cloudiness of understanding the soul becomes subject to intellect. For this reason, though it (intellect) is known to be subordinate to the son, it guides the latter.

sn: बुद्धिरुत्पद्यते कार्यान्मनस्तूत्पन्नमेव हि। बुद्धेर्गुणविधानेन मनस्तहगुणवद् भवेत्॥
en: The intellect is called into existence by acts of perception; (but) the mind exists of itself; and the mind and not the intellect, has the power of causing the sensations of pleasure and pain.

sn: एतद् विशेषणं तात मनोबुद्ध्योर्यदन्तरम्। त्वमप्यत्राभिसम्बुद्धः कथं वा मन्यते भवान्॥
en: O my child, these are the points of distinction between the mind and the intellect you are also conversant with this subject. What do you say?

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच अहो बुद्धिमतां श्रेष्ठ शुभा बुद्धिरियं तव। विदितं वेदितव्यं ते कस्मात् समनुपृच्छसि॥
en: Yudhishthira said: O the best of those endowed with intelligence, you have a superb intellect. Why (then) do you ask me this question, when you are well acquainted with all that should be known.

sn: सर्वज्ञं त्वां कथं मोह आविशत् स्वर्गवासिनम्। एवमद्भुतकर्माणमिति मे संशयो महान्॥
en: I am at a great loss to understand how you became subject to illusion who performed excellent deeds and obtained an abode in heaven.

sn: सर्प उवाच सुप्रज्ञमपि चेच्छूरमृद्धिर्मोहयते नरम्। वर्तमानः सुखे सर्वो मुह्यतीति मतिर्मम॥
en: The Serpent said : Even a highly intellectual and wise man is inflated with prosperity. And in my opinion those that are given to luxury lose their sense.

sn: सोऽहमैश्वर्यमोहेन मदाविष्टो युधिष्ठिर। पतितः प्रतिसम्बुद्धस्त्वां तु सम्बोधयाम्यहम्॥
en: So, O Yudhishthira, I too, intoxicated with the drink of prosperity, have fallen into this degraded state and then having recovered my reason am addressed you thus.

sn: कृतं कार्य महाराज त्वया मम परंतप। क्षीण: शापः सुकृच्छ्रो मे त्वया सम्भाष्य साधुना।।
en: O tormentor of foes, O mighty monarch, you have rendered me a good service. And by conversing with your pious self I have been freed from this dreadful curse.

sn: अहं हि दिवि दिव्येन विमानेन चरन् पुरा। अभिमानेन मत्तः सन् कंचिन्नान्यमचिन्तयम्॥
en: In days of yore when mounted on a celestials chariot I used to range through the heavens, elated with pride, I thought of nothing else.

sn: ब्रह्मर्षिदेवगन्धर्वयक्षराक्षसपन्नगाः। करान् मम प्रयच्छन्ति सर्वे त्रैलोक्यवासिनः॥
en: The Brahmarshis, the celestials, the Gandharvas, the Yakshas, the Rakshasas, the Pannagas and all the inhabitants of the three worlds had to pay me taxes.

sn: चक्षुषा यं प्रपश्यामि प्राणिनं पृथिवीपते। तस्य तेजो हराम्याशु तद्धि दृष्टेर्बलं मम॥
en: Such, O king, was the mysmeric power of my eyes, that all whatever creature I cast my looks, I instantly withdrew all his energy.

sn: ब्रह्मर्षीणां सतरं हि उवाह शिबिकां मम। स मामपनयो राजन् भ्रंशयामास वै श्रियः॥
en: Thousands of Brahmarshis were engaged in drawing my palanquin. And O king, this sin on my part brought about my fall from my exalted position.

sn: तत्र ह्यगस्त्यः पादेन वहन् स्पृष्टो मया मुनिः। अगस्तयेन ततोऽस्म्युक्तः सर्पस्त्वं च भवेति ह॥
en: One day when the sage Agastya was drawing my palanquin my feet touched his body. Thereupon Agastya cursed me in anger saying "ruin overtake you; do you turn into a snake."

sn: ततस्तस्माद् विमानावयात् प्रच्युतश्च्युतलक्षणः। प्रपतन् बुबुधेऽऽत्मानं व्यालीभूतमधोमुखम्। अन्याचं तमहं विप्रं शापस्यान्तो भवेदिति॥
en: Thus deprived of my prosperity I fell down from that conveyance. And in the course of my fall I found myself turned into a snake with my head downwards. (Then) I besought that Brahmana “Kindly free me from this curse.

sn: सर्प उवाच प्रमादात् सम्प्रमूढस्य भगवन् क्षन्तुमर्हसि। ततः स मामुवाचेदं प्रपतन्तं कृपान्वितः॥
en: O divine sage, graciously pardon me (because) I have been mad through pride. Thereupon, he, moved with pity addressed me while I was falling down, thus

sn: युधिष्ठिरोधर्मराजः शापात् त्वां मोक्षयिष्यति। अभिमानस्य घोरस्य पापस्य च नराधिप॥
en: Yudhishthira, the best of the virtuous will liberate you from this curse. And O Monarch, when this horrible sin of pride (in you).

sn: फले क्षीणे महाराज फलं पुण्यमवाप्स्यसि। ततो मे विस्मयो जातस्तद् दृष्ट्वा तपसो बलम्॥
en: Will come to an end, you will enjoy the fruits of your virtue." I was then lost in wonder on beholding the strength of his asceticism.

sn: ब्रह्म च ब्राह्मणत्वं च येन त्वाहमचूचुदम्। सत्यं दमस्तपो दानाहिंसाधर्मनित्यता।॥
en: And it is for that reason that I have put to you these questions relating to Brahma and the Brahmanas. Truthfulness, self-control, asceticism, benevolence, unenviousness and adherence to virtue,

sn: साधकानि सदा पुंसां न जातिर्न कुलं नृप। अरिष्ट एष भ्राता भीमसेनो महाबलः। स्वस्ति तेऽस्तु महाराज गमिष्यामि दिवं पुनः॥
en: O king and not race nor (illustrious) family, are the means by which persons must attain salvation. May your younger brother Bhimasena be all hail; and O mighty monarch, may you be happy. I shall now go to heaven again.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच इत्युक्त्वाऽऽजगरं देहं मुक्त्वा स नहुषो नृपः। दिव्यं वपुः समास्थाय गतस्त्रिदिवमेव ह॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having said this, the king Nahusha giving up his snake shape and assuming his celestials body returned to heaven.

sn: युधिष्ठिरोऽपिधर्मात्मा भ्रात्रा भीमेन संगतः। धौम्येन सहितः श्रीमानाश्रमं पुनरागमत्॥
en: And the virtuous and prosperous Yudhishthira too, accompanied by Bhima and Dhaumya came back to his hermitage.

sn: ते ततो द्विजेभ्यः सर्वेभ्यः समेतेभ्यो यथातथम्। कथयामास तत् सर्वधर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Then Yudhishthira, the best of the virtuous, related, in detail, all that had happened, to the assembled Brahmanas.

sn: तच्छ्रुत्वा ते द्विजाः सर्वे भ्रातश्चास्य ते त्रयः। आसन् सुव्रीडिता राजन् द्रौपदी च यशस्विनी॥
en: Hearing all that, O king, all the Brahmanas, his three brothers and the renowned Draupadi were greatly amazed.

sn: ते तु सर्वे द्विजश्रेष्ठाः पाण्डवानां हितेप्सया। मैवमित्यब्रुवन् भीमं गर्हयन्तोऽस्य साहसम्॥
en: And those best of the Brahmanas desirous of the welfare of the Pandavas, condemning the rashness of Bhima, told him not to do such an act again.

sn: पाण्डवास्तु भयान्मुक्तं प्रेक्ष्य भीमं महाबलम्। हर्षमाहारयांचक्रुर्विजह्वश्च मुदा युताः॥
en: The Pandavas too were greatly delighted at seeing the highly powerful Bhima out of danger and continued to dwell there happily.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच निदाघान्तकरः कालः सर्वभूतसुखावहः। तत्रैव वसतां तेषां प्रावृट् समभिपद्यत॥
en: Vaishampayana said: While they (the Pandavas) were living there, the rainy season, which puts an end to summer and is agreeable to all creatures, made its appearance.

sn: छादयन्तो महाघोषाः खं दिशश्च बलाहकाः। प्रववर्षुर्दिवारात्रमसिताः सततं तदा॥ तापत्ययनिकेताश्च शतशोऽथ सहाशः। अपेतार्कप्रभाजालाः सविद्युद्विमलप्रभाः॥
en: Then, hundreds and thousands of sable clouds covering the entire) firmament and the cardinal points, emitting thundering roars and looking like (so many) awnings in the rainy season, incessantly poured down showers night and day. The effulgence of the sun disappeared from the earth; and its place was filled by the stainless splendour of lightning.

sn: विरूढशष्याधरणी मत्तदंशसरीसृपा। बभूव पयसा सिक्ता शान्ता सर्वमनोरमा॥
en: And the earth, over grown with grass teeming with gnats and reptiles, maddened with joy and saturated with water, looked serene and became delightful to all.

sn: न स्म प्रज्ञायते किंचिदम्भसा समवस्तृते। समं वा विषमं वापि नद्यो वा स्थावराणि च॥
en: When the (surface of the earth was flooded with water it could not be discerned whether the ground was even or uneven or whether there were rivers, ground.

sn: क्षुब्धतोया महावेगाः श्वसमाना इवाशुगाः। सिन्धवः शोभयांचक्रुः काननानि तपात्यये॥
en: At the close of summer, the streams full of agitated waters and careering violently with a hissing noise like (flight of) arrows, lent a grace to the woods.

sn: नदतां काननान्तेषु श्रूयन्ते विविधाः स्वनाः। वृष्टिभिश्च्छाद्यमानानां वराहमृगपक्षिणाम्॥
en: The boars, the stage and the birds, drenched in water began to utter various sounds that could be heard in the forests.

sn: स्तोकका: शिखिनश्चैव पुंस्कोकिलगणैः सह। मत्ताः परिपतन्ति स्म दर्दुराश्चैव दर्पिताः॥
en: The Chatakas, .the peacocks, the male kokilas and the excited frogs all intoxicated (with joy) began to frolic about.

sn: तथा बहुविधाकारा प्रावृण्मेघानुनादिता। अभ्यतीता शिवा तेषां चरतां मरुधन्वसु॥
en: Thus, while the Pandavas were wandering about in dry sandy tracts at the neighbourhood of mountains the delightful rainy season so various in aspect and resounding with (the roar of) the clouds passed away.

sn: क्रौञ्चहंससमाकीर्णा शरत् प्रमुदिताभवत्। रूढकक्षवनप्रस्था प्रसन्नजलनिम्नगा।॥
en: Then came autumn, crowded with ganders and cranes, when the forest tracts were over grown with verdure and the streams became clear.

sn: विमलाकाशनक्षत्रा शरत् तेषां शिवाभवत्। मृगद्विजसमाकीर्णा पाण्डवानां महात्मनाम्॥
en: The sky and the stars shone with a stainless lustre and the country was swarmed with beasts and birds. This season of autumn became auspicious to the high-souled sons of Pandu.

sn: दृश्यन्ते शान्तरजसः क्षपा जलदशीतलाः। ग्रहनक्षत्रसङ्घश्च सोमेन च विराजिताः॥
en: (Then) the nights free from dust and cool with clouds were adorned with numerous stars, planets and the moon.

sn: कुमुदैः पुण्डरीकैश्च शीतवारिधराः शिवाः। नदीः पुष्करिणीश्चैव ददृशुः समलंकृताः॥
en: And (the Pandavas) beheld the rivers and the tanks, full of cool water and beautified with lilies and lotuses and pleasant (to the eye)

sn: आकाशनीकाशतटां तीरवानीरसंकुलाम्। बभूव चरतां हर्षः पुण्यतीर्थां सरस्वतीम्॥
en: And they experienced a great delight in wandering along the sacred Sarasvati whose banks resemble the firmament and are covered with canes.

sn: ते वै मुमुदिरे वीराः प्रसन्नसलिलां शिवाम्। पश्यन्तो दृढधन्वानः परिपूर्णां सरस्वतीम्॥
en: And those wielders of strong bows were highly glad at seeing the auspicious Sarasvati full of limpid water.

sn: तेषां पुण्यतमा रात्रिः पर्वसंधौ स्म शारदी। तत्रैव वसतामासीत् कार्तिकी जनमेजय॥
en: O Janamejaya, while dwelling there they passed the most sacred night of the full moon in the month of Kartika.

sn: पुण्यकृद्भिर्महासत्त्वैस्तापसैः सह पाण्डवाः। तत् सर्वे भरतश्रेष्ठाः समूहुर्योगमुत्तमम्॥
en: And in company with the righteous and high-souled ascetics, the Pandavas, the best of the Bharatas, spent that juncture in excellent devotion.

sn: तमिगाभ्युदये तस्मिन्धौम्येन सह पाण्डवाः। सूतैः पौरोगवैश्चैव काम्यकं प्रययुर्वनम्॥
en: And when the dark fort-night set in immediately after, the sons of Pandu together with Dharma and their charioteers and cooks proceeded to the forest of Kamyaka.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच काम्यकं प्राप्य कौरव्य युधिष्ठिरपुरोगमाः। कृतातिथ्या मुनिगणैनिषेदुः सह कृष्णया॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Arriving at (the forest of) Kamyaka and being hospitably received by the saints, Yudhishthira and the other Pandavas began to dwell there with Krishna.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: ततस्तान् परिविश्वस्तान् वसतः पाण्डुनन्दनान्। ब्राह्मणा बहवस्तत्र समन्तात् पर्यवारयन्॥
en: While those sons of Pandu were securely dwelling at that place they were surrounded by multitudes of Brahmanas.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: अथाब्रवीद् द्विजः कश्चिदर्जुनस्य प्रियः सखा। स एष्यति महाबाहुर्वशी शौरिरुदारधीः॥
en: And a certain Brahmana said "Shauri, the dear friend of Arjuna, of mighty arms, possessed of self-restraint and endued with high intellect, will come (here).

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: विदिता हि हरे यमिहायाताः कुरूद्वहाः। सदा हि दर्शनाकाक्षी श्रेयोऽन्वेषी च वो हरिः॥
en: Because it is known to Hari that you the perpetuators of the Kuru race have arrived here; and he is always desirous of seeing you and secks your welfare.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: बहुवत्सरजीवि च मार्कण्डेयो महातपाः। स्वाध्यायतपसा युक्तःक्षिप्रं युष्मान् समेष्यति॥
en: and Markandeya, who has lived for ages, has performed severe austerities, has studied the Vedas and who is given to devotion, will very soon come and join you.”

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: तथैव ब्रुवतस्तस्य प्रत्यदृश्यत केशवः। शैब्यसुग्रीवयुक्तेन रथेन रथिनां वरः॥ मघवानिव पौलोम्या सहितः सत्यभामया। उपायाद् देवकीपुत्रो दिदृक्षुः कुरुसत्तमान्॥
en: And at the very moment when the Brahmana was saying these he saw Keshava coming thither. And that foremost of car-warriors, the son of Devaki, desirous of seeing those most exalted of the Kurus, arrived on a chariot yoked with the horses named Saivya and Sugriva and accompanied by Satyabhama as Indra by the daughter of Puloma (Sachi).

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: अवतीर्य रथात् कृष्णोधर्मराजं यथाविधि। ववन्दे मुदितोधीमान् भीमं च बलिनां वरम्॥
en: Getting down from the car, Krishna following the usual custom, greeted with great delight, the intellectual Dharmaraja and the highly powerful Bhima.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: पूजयामासधौम्यं च यमाभ्यामभिवादितः। परिष्वज्य गुडाकेशं द्रौपदी पर्यसान्त्वयत्॥
en: He then paid his adoration to Dhaumya and (in his turn) was greeted by the twins. Then embracing Gudakesha (Arjuna of the curly hair) he spoke soothing words to Draupadi.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: स दृष्ट्वा फाल्गुनं वीरं चिरस्य प्रियमागतम्। पर्यष्वजत दाशार्हः पुनः पुनररिंदमः॥
en: And that tormentor of foes, the descendant of the Dasharhas, having met with his beloved and heroic Arjuna after a long time, embraced him again and again.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: तथैव सत्यभामापि द्रौपदी परिषस्वजे। पाण्डवानां प्रियां भार्यां कृष्णस्य महिषी प्रिया॥
en: And similarly Satyabhama, the beloved queen of Krishna, embraced Draupadi, the dear wife of the Pandavas.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: ततस्ते पाण्डवाः सर्वे सभार्याः सपुरोहिताः। आनर्चुः पुण्डरीकाक्षं परिवत्रुश्च सर्वशः॥
en: Then the Pandavas together with their wife and priest paid then respects to the lotus-eyed (Krishna) and surrounded him on all sides.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: कृष्णस्तु पार्थेन समेत्य विद्वान् धनंजयेनासुरतर्जनेन। बभौ यथा भूतपतिर्महात्मा समेत्य साक्षाद् भगवान् गुहेन॥
en: And the learned Krishna being joined with the Partha, Dhananjaya (winner of riches), the slayer of demons looked as, beautiful as that high-souled divine lord of all created beings (Shiva) when united with Kartikeya (his son).

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: ततः समस्तानि किरीटमाली वनेषु वृत्तानि गदाचजाय। उक्त्वा यथावत् पुनरन्वपृच्छत् कथं सुभद्रां च स चाभिमन्युः॥
en: Then he who wore a coronet on his head (Arjuna) having related in detail to the elder brother of Gada (Krishna) all the incidents in connection with their forest life asked how are Subhadra and Abhimanyu?

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: स पूजयित्वा मधुहा यथावत् पार्थं च कृष्णां च पुरोहितं चा उवाच राजानमभिप्रशंसन् युधिष्ठिरं तत्र सहोपविश्य॥
en: And the destroyer of (the demon) Madhu, having, in the usual manner greeted Arjuna, Draupadi and the priest (Dhaumya) and having eulogised the king Yudhishthira took his seat with them and spoke these words.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: धर्मः परः पाण्डव राज्यलाभात् तस्यार्थमाहुस्तप एव राजन्। सत्यार्जवाभ्यां चरता स्वधर्म जितस्त्वयायं च परश्च लोकः॥
en: "It is asserted (by the wise), O Pandava, that righteousness is superior to winning kingdoms and, O king, in order to foster it (virtue), asceticism is necessary. And you, who have performed your duties in strict obedience to truth and candour have conquered both this world and the next.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: अधीतमग्रे चरता व्रतानि सम्यग्धनुर्वेदमवाप्य कृत्स्नम्। क्षात्रेणधर्मेण वसूनि लब्ध्वा सर्वे ह्यवाप्ताः क्रतव; पुराणाः॥
en: You first studied (the Vedas) by observing the proper rites; you have next acquired mastery over the whole science of weapons; and then having obtained wealth by pursuing the methods followed by the Kshatriyas you have performed all the ancient sacrificial rites.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: न चाम्यधर्मेषु रतिस्तवास्ति कामान किंचित् कुरुषे नरेन्द्र। न चार्थलोभात् प्रजहासिधर्म तस्मात् प्रभावादसिधर्मराजः॥
en: You are are neither addicted to sensual pleasures, nor, O king of kings, do you perform anything froin motives of self-interest nor do you subserve your duties to greed of wealth. It is (for these reasons) that you have been styled the virtuous King.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: दानं च सत्यं च तपश्च राजन् श्रद्धा च बुद्धिश्च क्षमाधृतिश्च। नेपा परा पार्थ सदा रतिस्ते॥
en: O King, although you have won kingdoms, wealth and are surrounded by all sorts of luxury, you are ever bent on charity, truthfulness, asceticism, faith, meditation, forgiveness and patience.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: यदा जनौघः कुरुजाङ्गलानां कृष्णां सभायामवशामपश्यत्। अपेतधर्मव्यवहारवृत्तं सहेत तत् पाण्डव कस्त्वदन्यः॥
en: When the inhabitants of Kuru Jangala beheld (the modesty of) Krishna outraged in the assembly hall, O Pandu who but yourself could brook that (beastly) conduct (on the part of the Kurus) so very odious to virtue and custom?

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: असंशयं सर्वसमृद्धकामः क्षिप्रं प्रजाः पालयितासि सम्यक्। इमे वयं निग्रहणे कुरूणां यदि प्रतिज्ञा भवतः समाप्ता॥
en: It admits of no doubt that with all your desires gratified you will soon creditably govern your subjects. And when your promise (to spend twelve years in exile) will be fulfilled, we will try our utmost to chastise the Kurus."

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: धौम्यं च भीमं च युधिष्ठिरं च यमौ च कृष्णां च दशार्हसिंहः। उवाच दिष्ट्या भवतां शिवेन प्राप्तः किरीटी मुदितः कृतास्त्रः॥
en: Then, the chief of the Dasharhas said to Dhaumya, Bhima, Yudhishthira, the twins (Nakula and Sahadeva) and Draupadi “it is by your good fortune that Kiriti (Arjuna who wears a coronet on his head) has returned with a merry mind after having been well-versed in the science of weapons."

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: प्रोवाच कृष्णामपि याज्ञसेनी दशाहभर्ता सहितः सुहृद्भिः। दिष्ट्या समग्रासिधनंजयेन समागतेत्येवमुवाच कृष्णः॥
en: And the lord of the Dasharhas (Krishna) together with friends said to Yajnaseni the daughter of Yagnasena (Krishna) "fortunate it is that you have been again united with Dhananjaya (the winner of wealth) all hale and hearty.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: स्तवात्मजास्ते शिशव: सुशीलाः। श्चरन्ति पुत्रास्तव याज्ञसेनि॥
en: O Krishna, O Yajnaseni, these young sons of yours chiefly given to the acquisition of the science of arms are all of good behaviour and always follow in the footsteps of their worthy friends.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: राज्येन राष्ट्रैश्च निमन्त्र्यमाणाः पित्रा च कृष्णे तव सोदरैश्च। य यज्ञसेनस्य न मातुलाना गृहेषु बाला रतिमाप्नुवन्ति॥
en: And, O Krishna, although your father and your brothers try to tempt them with a kingdom and territories, the boys find no pleasure in the abodes of Yajnasena or of their maternal uncles.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: आनर्तमेवाभिमुखाः शिवेन गत्वाधनुर्वेदरतिप्रधानाः। तवात्मजा वृष्णिपुरं प्रविश्य न दैवतेभ्यः स्पृहयन्ति कृष्णे॥
en: And, O Krishna, safely proceeding towards the country of the Anartas when your sons, chiefly bent on the acquisition of arms, enter the city of the Vrishnis, they do not even long for celestials happiness.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: यथा त्वमेवार्हसि तेषु वृत्तं प्रयोक्तुमार्या च तथैव कुन्ती। तेष्वप्रमादेन तथा करोति तथैव भूयश्च तथा सुभद्रा॥
en: And Subhadra always instructs them carefully to observe good manners as you yourself or the venerable Kunti would do.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: र्यथा सुनीथस्य यथैव भानोः। तथा विनेता च गतिश्च कृष्णे तरात्मजानामपि रौक्मिणेयः॥
en: O Krishna, as the son of Rukmani (Pradyumna) is the tutor and guide to Aniruddha, Abhimanyu Sunitha and Bhanu, so he is to your sons also.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: नस्त्रेषु शिक्षासु रथाश्वयाने। स्तांश्चाभिमन्युः सततं कुमारः॥
en: And Prince Abhimanyu, an able teacher always gives instructions to them brave and active as they are, in the arts of wielding maces, swords, buckles and other weapons and of driving cars and riding horses.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: स चापि सम्यक् प्रणिधाय शिक्षा शस्त्राणि चैषां विधिवत् प्रदाय। तवात्मजानां च तथाभिमन्यो: पराक्रमैस्तुष्यति रौक्मिणेयः॥
en: And the son of Rukmani, having thoroughly instructed and having duly conferred weapons upon them, takes much delight in witnessing the valour of your sons and of Abhimanyu.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: यदा विहारं प्रसमीक्षमाणाः प्रयान्ति पुत्रास्तव याज्ञसेनि। एकैकमेषामनुयान्ति तत्र रथाश्च यानानि च दन्तिनश्च॥
en: And O daughter of Yajnasena, when your sons go out for field sports, each of them is followed by cars, horses, vehicles and elephants."

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: अथाब्रवीद्धर्मराजं तु कृष्णो दशाहयोधाः कुकुरान्धकाश्चा स्तिष्ठन्तु यत्रेच्छसि तत्र राजन्॥
en: Krishna, then addressing the Dharmaraja, said “O king, let the Dasharha warrior, the Kukuras and the Andhakas, obeying your orders remain wherever you wish.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: आवर्ततां कार्मुकवेगवाता हलायुधप्रग्रहणा मधूनाम्। सेना तवार्थेषु नरेन्द्र यत्ता ससादिपत्त्यश्वरथा सनागा॥
en: O monarch, let the army of the Madhus, the strength of whose bows is as impetuous as the wind and led by Halayudha (the wielder of the plough) and consisting of cavalry, infantry, horses, chariots and elephants, prepare to carry out your commands.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: प्रस्थाप्यतां पाण्डवधार्तराष्ट्र: सुयोधनः पापकृतां वरिष्ठः। स सानुबन्धः ससुद्गणश्च भौमस्य सौभाधिपतेश्च मार्गम्॥
en: O Pandava, send Suyodhana, the son of Dhritarashtra, the vilest of sinners together with his friends and followers to the path of the lord of Subha (Soila) the son of the earth.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: कामं तथा तिष्ठ नरेन्द्र तस्मिन् यथा कृतस्ते समयः सभायाम्। दाशार्हयोधैस्तु हतारियोधं प्रतीक्षतां नागपुरं भवन्तम्॥
en: Dwell where you please, O monarch, during the period appointed by you in the assembly hall; but at the end of which let the city Nagpur (Hastina) await your arrival therein when the Dasharha warriors have cut down the forces of your enemies.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: व्यपेतमन्युर्व्यपनीतपाप्मा विहृत्य यत्रेच्छसि तत्र कामम्। ततः प्रसिद्धं प्रथमं विशोकः प्रपत्स्यसे नागपुरं सुराष्ट्रम्॥
en: (During the appointed period) abandoning your sorrow and getting rid of your sin, wander at pleasure wherever you like; and then with a merry heart you will enter the renowned city of Hastina and also your principality.”

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: ततस्तदाज्ञाय मतं महात्मा यथावदुक्तं पुरुषोत्तमेन। प्रशस्य विप्रेक्ष्य चधर्मराजः कृताञ्जलि: केशवमित्युवाचः॥
en: Then the high-souled Dharmaraja, being informed of the views thus clearly expressed by that best of men and praising the same and looking at Krishna spoke these words with joined hands to him.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: असंशयं केशव पाण्डवानां भवान् गतिस्त्वच्छरणा हि पार्थाः। कालोदये तच्च ततश्च भूयः कर्ता भवान् कर्म न संशयोऽस्ति।॥
en: "O Keshava, it admits of no doubt that you are the refuge of the Pandavas; and the Parthas are under your protection. When the time for action will arrive, you will undoubtedly do all that you have just said.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: यथाप्रतिज्ञं विहतश्च कालः सर्वाः समा द्वादश निर्जनेषु। अज्ञातचर्यां विधिवत् समाप्य भवद्गताः केशव पाण्डवेयाः॥
en: We will spend the period of twelve years, as we have promised, in lonely forests. And then having duly completed the period of our are incognito life, O Keshava, the sons of Pandu will place themselves under your protection.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: एषैव बुद्धिर्जुषतां सदा त्वां सत्ये स्थिताः केशव पाण्डवेयाः। सदानधर्माः सजनाः सदारा: सबान्धवास्त्वच्छरणा हि पार्थाः॥
en: May this intention of yours, always remain in you. For O Keshava, the Parthas, the sons of Pandu, firmn in truth and devoted to charity and duty, together with their friends, relations and their wives (always) under your protection."

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तथा वदति वार्ष्णेयेधर्मराजे च भारता अथ पश्चात् तपोवृद्धो बहुवर्षसहाधृक्॥ प्रत्यदृश्यतधर्मात्मा मार्कण्डेयो महातपाः। अजरश्चामरश्चैव रूपौदार्यगुणान्वितः॥
en: Vaishampayana said: O Bharata, when the descendant of the Vrishnis and the Dharmaraja were thus conversing, the high-souled Markandeya, of great devotion, grown wise by austerities, who had lived many thousands of years, was seen to approach (there). Being immortal and without signs of senility, endued with beauty and magnanimity.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: व्यदृश्यत तथा युक्तो यथा स्यात् पञ्चविंशकः। तमागतमृषि वृद्ध बहुवर्षसहरिणम्॥
en: He looked like a youth of twenty five years old. When that wise saint who had seen many thousands of years made his appearance,

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: आनर्ब्राह्मणाः सर्वे कृष्णश्च सह पाण्डवैः। तमर्चितं सुविश्वस्तमासीनमृषिसत्तमम्। ब्राह्मणानां मतेनाह पाण्डवानां च केशवः॥
en: All the Brahmanas and the Pandavas together with Krishna paid their adoration to him. And when that most exalted of saints, thus honoured, was peacefully seated, Keshava giving expression to the views of the Brahmanas and the Pandavas thus addressed him.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: कृष्ण उवाच शुश्रूषवः पाण्डवास्ते ब्राह्मणाश्च समागताः। द्रौपदी सत्यभामा च तथाहं परमं वचः॥
en: Krishna said : The Pandavas, the assembled Brahmanas, Draupadi, Satyablama as well as myself are all desirous of hearing your most excellent words.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: पुरावृत्ताः कथाः पुण्याः सदाचारान् सनातनान्। राज्ञा स्त्रीणामृपीणां च मार्कण्डेय विचक्ष्व नः॥
en: (Graciously) narrate to us (therefore) the sacred events of ancient ages and the eternal rules of righteous conduct by which kings, women and saints should be guided.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तेषु तत्रोपविष्टेषु देवर्षिरपि नारदः। आजगाम विशुद्धात्मा पाण्डवानवलोककः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : When they were all seated the divine saint Narada too, of pure soul, came there to see the Pandavas.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: तमप्यथ महात्मानं सर्वे ते पुरुषर्षभाः। पाद्यार्थ्याभ्यां यथान्यायमुपतस्थुर्मनीषिणः॥
en: Then, all those highly intellectual and most exalted of mortals, honoured that magnanimous saint by offering him, according to the usual custom, water to wash his feet and the oblation called Arghya.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: नारदस्त्वथ देवर्षित्वा तांस्तु कृतक्षणान्। मार्कण्डेयस्य वदतस्तां कथामन्वमोदत॥
en: Learning that they were about to hear the words of Markandeya, the divine saint Narada signified his assent to the proposal.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: उवाच चैनं कालज्ञः स्मयन्निव सनातनः। ब्रह्मर्षे कथ्यतां यत् ते पाण्डवेषु विवक्षितम्॥
en: Then the eternal Krishna, who knows well what is the convenient moment, spoke to Markandeya, with a smile "O Brahmarshi, kindly relate to the Pandavas whatever you wish to say"

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: एवमुक्तः प्रत्युवाच मार्कण्डेयो महातपाः। क्षणं कुरुध्वं विपुलमाख्यातव्यं भविष्यति॥
en: Thus addressed, Markandeya, of great austerities replied “wait a moment. I will relate lots of events."

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: एवमुक्ताः क्षणं चक्रुः पाण्डवाः सह तैर्द्विजैः। मध्यन्दिने यथाऽऽदित्यं प्रेक्षन्तस्ते महामुनिम्॥
en: Thus spoken to, the Pandavas together with the Brahmanas waited a little looking at that great saint glorious as the noon-day sun.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तं विवक्षन्तमालक्ष्य कुरुराजो महामुनिम्। कथासंजननार्थाय चोदयामास पाण्डवः॥
en: Vaishampayana said: (Then) the son of Pandu, the king of the Kurus, seeing that the great sage was desirous of speaking, asked him, with the intention of suggesting topics for narration.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: भवान् दैवतदैत्यानामृषीणां च महात्मनाम्। राजर्षीणां च सर्वेषां चरितज्ञः पुरातनः॥
en: “You are ancient in age and are therefore conversant with the events relating to all the gods, the demons, the high-souled sages and the royal saints.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: सेव्यश्चोपासितव्यश्च मतो नः काक्षितश्चिरम्। अयं च देवकीपुत्रः प्राप्तोऽस्मानवलोककः॥
en: We consider you deserve all honour and adoration; and we have, for a long time, been desirous of seeing you. This son of Devaki too has come here to pay us a visit.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: भवत्येव हि मे बुद्धिर्दृष्ट्वाऽऽत्मानं सुखाच्च्युतम्। धार्तराष्ट्रांश्च दुर्वृत्तानृध्यतः प्रेक्ष्य सर्वशः॥ कर्मणः पुरुषः कर्ता शुभस्याप्यशुभस्य वा। स फलं तदुपाश्नाति कथं कर्ता स्विदीश्वरः॥
en: When I consider that I have been deprived of happiness for no fault of mine and when I see the wicked sons of Dhritarashtra prospering in every respect it strikes me that man is the agent of his meritorious or wicked acts and that he reaps the fruits of his own deeds. How can then God be the agent?

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: कुतो वा सुखदुःखेषु नृणां ब्रह्मविदां वर। इह वा कृतमन्वेति परदेहेऽथ वा पुनः॥
en: And O the best of those conversant with the Supreme Being, why does man become subject to pleasure or pain? Is it in this world or in another existence that he reaps the fruits of his acts?

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: देही च देहं संत्यज्य मृग्यमाणः शुभाशुभैः। कधं संयुज्यते प्रेत्य इह वा द्विजसत्तम॥
en: O best of Brahmanas, how is it that the consequences of the good or evil acts of an embodied being follow him in this world or after his death in the next?

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: ऐहलौकिकमेवेह उताहो पारलौकिकम्। क्व च कर्माणि तिष्ठन्ति जन्तोः प्रेतस्य भार्गव॥
en: Do we reap the fruits of our acts in this life or in another existence? And O descendant of Bhrigu, where do the results of the acts of an animated creature rest after his death?”

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच त्वयुक्तोऽयमनुप्रश्नो यथावद् वदतां वर। विदितं वेदितव्यं ते स्थित्यर्थं त्वं तु पृच्छसि॥
en: Markandeya said : "O the best of speakers, this question is worthy of you and is just what you should ask. You are well informed of whatever is fit to be known But it is for the sake of form that you are asking the question.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: अत्र ते कथयिष्यामि तदिहैकमनाः शृणु। यथेहामुत्र च नरः सुखदुःखमुपाश्नुते॥
en: I will now narrate to you how men experience pleasure and pain in this world and in the next. Listen to me with an undivided attention.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: निर्मलानि शरीराणि विशुद्धानि शरीरिणाम्। ससर्जधर्मतन्त्राणि पूर्वोत्पन्नः प्रजापतिः॥
en: Prajapati (the lord of all created beings) who first sprang into existence, created for the corporeal beings, bodies, stainless, pure and given to virtue.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: अमोघफलसंकल्पा: सुव्रताः सत्यवादिनः । ब्रह्मभूता नराः पुण्याः पुराणाः कुरुसत्तम॥
en: O the most exalted of the Kurus, the primary men had all their desires gratified, were given to virtuous deeds and were truthful, godly and pure.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: सर्वे देवैः समायान्ति स्वच्छन्देन नभस्तलम्। ततश्च पुनरायान्ति सर्वे स्वच्छन्दचारिणः॥
en: They were all as good as the gods themselves, could soar to the heavens, come down again and range at pleasure wherever they liked.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: स्वच्छन्दमरणाश्चासन् नरा: स्वच्छन्दचारिणः। अल्पबाधा निरातङ्काः सिद्धार्था निरुपद्रवाः॥
en: They had control over their life and death, had few difficulties and no fear had all their desires gratified, were free from troubles.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: द्रष्टारो देवसङ्घानामृषीणां च महात्मनाम्। प्रत्यक्षाः सर्वधर्माणां दान्ता विगतमत्सराः॥
en: Could visit the high-souled gods and the saints; were well-versed in all the religious ordinances; had self-control and were devoid of envy.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: आसन् वर्षसहरीयास्तथा पुत्रसहहिरणः। तत: कालान्तरेऽन्यस्मिन् पृथिवीतलचारिणः॥
en: They lived for a thousand years and had as many sons. But in process of time their powers, were limited to walking solely on the earth's surface.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: कामक्रोधाभिभूतास्ते मायाव्याजोपजीविनः। लोभमोहाभिभूताश्च त्यक्ता देहैस्ततो नराः॥
en: And they became subject to lust and anger, practised falsehood and duplicity for subsistence and were overpowered by greed and ignorance. And when these (wicked) men died,

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: अशुभैः कर्मभिः पापास्तिर्यनिरयगामिनः। संसारेषु विचित्रेषु पच्यमानाः पुनः पुनः॥
en: They were born among lower animals or driven to hell and again and again had to suffer the pain of rebirth in this wonderful world on account of their vicious deeds.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: मोघेष्टा मोसंकल्पा मोघज्ञाना विचेतसः। सर्वाभिशङ्किनश्चैव संवृत्ताः क्लेशदायिनः॥
en: Then their desires, their aims, their knowledge and their rituals bore up fruit; They were afraid of everything their reason was clouded and they were oppressed with sorrow.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: अशुभैः कर्मभिश्चापि प्रायशः परिचिछिताः। दौष्कुल्या व्याधिबहुला दुरात्मानोऽप्रतापिनः॥
en: And they were generally marked by their wicked deeds, born in low family, afflicted with various diseases and became evil-minded and the terror of others.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: 'भवन्त्यल्पायुषः पापा रौद्रकर्मफलोदयाः। नाथन्तः सर्वकामानां नास्तिका भिन्नचेतसः॥
en: Their life became short and wicked and they paid the penalty of their terrible deeds; were covetous of everything, became atheists and indifferent in mind.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: जन्तोः प्रेतस्य कौन्तेय गतिः स्वैरिह कर्मभिः। प्राज्ञस्य हीनबुद्धेश्च कर्मकोशः क्व तिष्ठति॥
en: O son of Kunti, the fate of a creature after death depends upon his acts in this world. As regards your question as to where the treasure of the acts of the wise and the ignorant remains,

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: क्वस्थस्तत् समुपाश्नाति सुकृतं यदि वेतरत्। इति ते दर्शनं यच्च तत्राप्यनुनयं शृणु॥
en: And where they reap the fruits of their own meritorious or vicious deeds, hear the decisions on the subject.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: अयमादिशरीरेण देवसृष्टेन मानवः। शुभानामशुभानां च कुरुते संचयं महत्॥
en: Man by his original subtle frame, made by the creator, accumulates a great store of good and evil deeds.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: आयुषोऽन्ते प्रहायेदं क्षीणप्रायं कलेवरम्। सम्भवत्येव युगपद् योनौ नास्त्यन्तराभवः॥
en: When his days are numbered he leaves this frail body and is immediately born among another order of creation, and he never remains disembodied even for a single moment.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: तत्रास्य स्वकृतं कर्म छायेवानुगतं सदा। फलत्यथ सुखा) वा दुःखार्हो वाथ जायते॥
en: In that new existence his (good and evil) acts always follow him like his shadow and the consequences thereof make his existence either pleasurable or painful.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: कृतान्तविधिसंयुक्तः स जन्तुर्लक्षणैः शुभैः। अशुभैर्वा निरादानो लक्ष्यते ज्ञानदृष्टिभिः॥
en: The wise only by means of spiritual insight know that every creature is chained to an unchangeable fate by the destroyer (Yama) for his virtue or vice and that he is unable to get rid of the consequences of his acts in good or evil fortune.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: एषा तावदबुद्धीनां गतिरुक्ता युधिष्ठिर। अतः परं ज्ञानवतां निबोध गतिमुत्तमाम्॥
en: O Yudhishthira, I have related (to you) the fate of those whose intelligence has been clouded with ignorance. Now hear of the excellent state attained to by the wise.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: मनुष्यास्तप्ततपसः सर्वागमपरायणाः। स्थिरव्रताः सत्यपरा गुरुशुश्रूषणे रताः॥
en: These men are of great ascetic merits, learned in all the religious books (i.e. the Vedas and the Tantras), firm in duty, devoted to truth, engaged in ministering to the comforts of their elders;

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: सुशीलाः शुक्लजातीयाः क्षान्ता दान्ताः सुतेजसः। शुचियोन्यन्तरगताः प्रायशः शुभलक्षणाः॥
en: Are well behaved, given to the practice of yoga, of forgiving spirit, self-controlled, energetic, well-born and are endowed with the signs of greatness.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: जितेन्द्रियत्वाद् वशिनः शुक्लत्वान्मन्दरोगिणः। अल्पाबाधपरित्रासाद् भवन्ति निरुपद्रवाः॥
en: Owing to their control over their passions they are well-governed in mind; by practising Yoga they are devoid of disease and by the absence of sorrow and fear they are free from (mental troubles).

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: च्यवन्तं जायमानं च गर्भस्थं चैव सर्वशः। स्वमात्मानं परं चैव बुध्यन्ते ज्ञानचक्षुषा॥
en: In course of birth whether timely or premature or while confined in the womb, (in short) in every state, they know the relation subsisting between their own souls and the eternal spirit, by spiritual insight.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: ऋषयस्ते महात्मानः प्रत्यक्षागमबुद्धयः। कर्मभूमिमिमां प्राप्य पुनर्यान्ति सुरालयम्॥
en: The high-souled saints gifted with positive and intuitive knowledge being born in this world of actions attain to the celestials regions again.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: किंचिद् दैवाद्धद्दात् किंचित् किंचिदेव स्वकर्मभिः। प्राप्नुवन्ति नरा राजन् मा तेऽस्त्वन्या विचारणा॥
en: O monarch, by practising Yoga or by Destiny or by their own acts, men attain to (happiness or misery). Do not thing otherwise.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: इमामत्रोपमां चापि निबोध वदतां वर। मनुष्यलोके यच्छ्रेयः परं मन्ये युधिष्ठिर॥
en: O the best of speakers, O Yudhishthira, hear an instance of what I deem to be the highest good in this world.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: इह वैकस्य नामुत्र अमुत्रैकस्य नो इह। इह वामुत्र चैकस्य नामुत्रैकस्य नो इह॥
en: Some men enjoy happiness in this world but not in the next; some attain it in the next world but not in this; while others neither in this world nor in that to come.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: धनानि येषां विपुलानि सन्ति नित्यं रमन्ते सुविभूषिताङ्गाः। तेषामयं शत्रुवरघ्न लोको नासौ सदा देहसुखे रतानाम्॥
en: They, that possess vast wealth, sport themselves every day richly adorning their persons (with ornaments and dresses). Such men, O destroyer of powerful enemies being addicted to physical enjoyment, attain to happiness in this world but not in the next.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: ते योगयुक्तास्तपसि प्रसक्ताः स्वाध्यायशीला जरयन्ति देहान्। स्तेषामसौ नायमरिन लोकः॥
en: O slayer of foes, those who are absorbed in spiritual thoughts, devoted to asceticism, engaged in the study of the Vedas and who mortify their bodies, have a control over their passions and abstain from killing animals, enjoy happiness in the next world but not in this.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: येधर्ममेव प्रथमं चरन्ति धर्मेण लब्वा चधनानि काले। न चापि दारानवाप्य क्रतुभिर्यजन्ते तेषामयं चैव परश्च लोकः॥
en: Those that first lead a virtuous life and honestly acquire wealth in due time and then marry and perform sacrificial rites, attain happiness both in this world and in that to come.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: ये नैव विद्यां न तपो न दानं मूढाः प्रजने यतन्ति। स्तेषामयं नैव परच लोकः॥
en: And those stupid persons who have neither learning nor asceticism, nor charity and who do not multiply their kind and are not given to worldly joys attain to happiness neither in this world nor in the next.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: सर्वे भवन्तस्त्वतिवीर्यसत्त्वा दिव्यौजसः संहननोपपन्नाः। लोकादमुष्मादवनि प्रपन्नाः स्वधीतविद्याः सुरकार्यहेतोः॥
en: You are highly powerful, vigorous, endued with celestials energy, well read and in order to serve the purpose of the gods have come down (from the heavens) and been born in this world for the extirpation (of the wicked people).

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: स्तपोदमाचारविहारशीलाः। देवानृषीन् प्रेतगणांश्च सर्वान् संतर्पयित्वा विधिना परेण॥
en: Having achieved glorious deeds and having gratified all the gods, the saints and the Pitris, you, who are so heroic, devoted to spiritual meditation, self-controlled, given to purity and engaged in self-extertion will at length in due course.

description: The narration by Markandeya (of the events of by gone times)
sn: स्वर्गं परं पुण्यकृतो निवासं क्रमेण सम्प्राप्स्यथ कर्मभिः स्वैः। मा भूद् विशङ्का तव कौरवेन्द्र दृष्ट्वाऽऽत्मनः क्लेशमिमं सुखार्हम्॥
en: Gradually attain to that excellent heavenly region, the abode of the virtuous, by means of your own (meritorious) deeds. O the lord of the Kurus, let no doubt, trouble your mind on account of your misfortune, for this affliction will lead to your (ultimate) happiness.

description: The story of the greatness of the Brahmanas
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच मार्कण्डेयं महात्मानमूचुः पाण्डुसुतास्तदा। माहात्म्यं द्विजमुख्यानां श्रोतुमिच्छाम कथ्यताम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Then the sons of Pandu said to the magnanimous Markandeya “(kindly) narrate to us of the greatness of the Brahmanas which we are very desirous of hearing."

description: The story of the greatness of the Brahmanas
sn: एवमुक्तः स भगवान् मार्कण्डेयो महातपाः। उवाच सुमहातेजाः सर्वशास्त्रविशारदः॥
en: Thus addressed, the highly energetic and divine Markandeya of great austerities and well versed in all the departments of religious writs replied (to them).

description: The story of the greatness of the Brahmanas
sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच हैहयानां कुलकरो राजा परपुरंजयः। कुमारो रूपसम्पन्नो मृगयां व्यचरद् बली॥
en: Markandeya said : Once upon a time a handsome and vigorous young prince of the Haihaya race, conqueror of enemies' cities, went out to hunt.

description: The story of the greatness of the Brahmanas
sn: चरमाणस्तु सोऽरण्ये तृणवीरुत्समावृते। कृष्णाजिनोत्तरासङ्गं ददर्श मुनिमन्तिके॥
en: While he was wandering in the forest covered with grass and creepers he saw near (him) a Muni wrapped up in an antelope's skin which served as an upper garment.

description: The story of the greatness of the Brahmanas
sn: स तेन निहतोऽरण्ये मन्यमानेन वै मृगम्। व्यथितः कर्म तत् कृत्वा शोकोपहतचेतनः॥
en: And mistaking him for a deer he killed (the Muni). Afflicted at heart and smitten with grief for what he had done,

description: The story of the greatness of the Brahmanas
sn: जगाम हैहयानां वै सकाशं प्रथितात्मनाम्। राज्ञां राजीवनेत्रोऽसौ कुमारः पृथिवीपतिः। तेषां च तद् यथावृत्तं कथयामास वै तदा॥
en: The lotus-eyed prince went to the distinguished Haihaya Chiefs and informed them of the matter,

description: The story of the greatness of the Brahmanas
sn: तं चापि हिसितं तात मुनि मूलफलाशिनम्। श्रुत्वा दृष्ट्वा च ते तत्र बभूवुर्दीनमानसाः॥
en: O child, on hearing of it and seeing the (dead body) of the Muni who lived on fruits and roots they became sick at heart.

description: The story of the greatness of the Brahmanas
sn: कस्यायमिति ते सर्वे मार्गमाणास्ततस्ततः। जग्मुश्चारिष्टनेम्नोऽथ तार्श्वस्वाश्रममञ्जसा॥
en: Then all those (kings) making enquiries here and there as to whose son the Muni was, soon arrived at the hermitage of Arishtanemi, the son of Kashyapa.

description: The story of the greatness of the Brahmanas
sn: तेऽभिवाद्य महात्मानं तं मुनि नियतव्रतम्। तस्थुः सर्वे स तु मुनिस्तेषां पूजामथाहरत्॥
en: And bowing down to that high-souled sage constantly engaged in austerities they remained standing there and the Muni 10O busied himself to welcome them.

description: The story of the greatness of the Brahmanas
sn: ते तमूचुर्महात्मानं न वयं सत्क्रियां मुने। त्वत्तोऽर्हाः कर्मदोषेण ब्राह्मणो हिसितो हि नः॥
en: They then said to that magnanimous sage, "we are no longer worthy of your reception in as much as we have unfortunately killed a Brahmana."

description: The story of the greatness of the Brahmanas
sn: तानब्रवीत् स विप्रर्षिः कथं वो ब्राह्मणो हतः। क्व चासौ ब्रूत सहिताः पश्यध्वं मे तपोबलम्॥
en: And that Brahmanical sage said to them "how have you killed a Brahmana? Say where he is; and you all behold the power of my devotional exercise."

description: The story of the greatness of the Brahmanas
sn: ते तु तत् सर्वमखिलमाख्यायास्मै यथातथम्। नापश्यंस्तमृषिं तत्र गतासुं ते समागताः॥
en: The chiefs, then having truly related to him all that had taken place and having returned to the place (where the corpse of the Rishi was) did not find it there.

description: The story of the greatness of the Brahmanas
sn: अन्वेषमाणाः सव्रीडाः स्वप्नवद्गतचेतनाः। तानब्रवीत् तत्र मुनिस्तार्क्ष्यः परपुरंजय॥
en: And searching about for it they returned covered with shame and devoid of consciousness like one in a dream. Then, O the conqueror of your enemy's cities, that sage, the son of Kashyapa, said to them.

description: The story of the greatness of the Brahmanas
sn: स्यादयं ब्राह्मणः सोऽथ युष्माभिर्यो विनाशितः। पुत्रो ह्ययं मम नृपास्तपोबलसमन्वितः॥
en: "O kings, is this the Brahmana who was killed by you? He is indeed my son devoted to great austerities."

description: The story of the greatness of the Brahmanas
sn: ते च दृष्ट्वैव तमृर्षि विसमयं परमं गताः। महदाश्चर्यमिति वै ते ब्रुवाणा महीपते॥
en: And O king, beholding that Rishi they were highly amazed and they all exclaimed “it is indeed highly wonderful.

description: The story of the greatness of the Brahmanas
sn: मृतो ह्ययमुपानीतः कथं जीवितमाप्तवान्। किमेतत् तपसो वीर्यं येनायं जीवितः पुनः॥
en: How has the dead been restored to life? Is it by the strength of asceticism that he has been brought to life again?

description: The story of the greatness of the Brahmanas
sn: श्रोतुमिच्छामहे विप्र यदि श्रोतव्यमित्युत। स तानुवाच नास्माकं मृत्युः प्रभवते नृपाः॥
en: O Brahmana, we are (very) curious to hear it, if indeed it can be heard.” (Thereupon) he replied “O kings, death cannot display its power before us.

description: The story of the greatness of the Brahmanas
sn: कारणं वः प्रवक्ष्यामि हेतुयोगसमासतः। सत्यमेवाभिजानीमो नानृते कुर्महे मनः। स्वधर्ममनुतिष्ठामस्तस्मान्मृत्युभयं न नः॥
en: I will relate to you the reason here of briefly and argumentatively. As we strictly adhere to our own duties, we are not afraid of death.

description: The story of the greatness of the Brahmanas
sn: यद् ब्राह्मणानां कुशलं तदेषां कथयामहे। नैषां दुश्चरितं ब्रूमस्तस्मान्मृत्युभयं न नः॥
en: We speak well of the Brahmanas and never vilify them; therefore we do not fear death.

description: The story of the greatness of the Brahmanas
sn: अतिथीनन्नपानेन भृत्यानत्यशेनन च। सम्भोज्य शेषमनीमस्तस्मान्मृत्युभयं न नः॥
en: As we entertain our guests with food and drink and regale our dependents with plenty of food and then eat what is left; so we have no fear of death.

description: The story of the greatness of the Brahmanas
sn: शान्ता दान्ताः क्षमाशीलास्तीर्थदानपरायणाः। पुण्यदेशनिवासाच्च तस्मान्मृत्युभयं न नः। तेजस्विदेशवासाच्च तस्मान्मृत्युभयं न नः॥
en: We are peaceful, charitable of forgiving disposition, fond of visiting sacred shrines, benevolent and we dwell in holy places; therefore we entertain no fear of death. And as we associate with men of devotional spirit, death has no fear for us.

description: The story of the greatness of the Brahmanas
sn: एतद् वै लेशमात्रं वः समाख्यातं विमत्सराः। गच्छतध्वं सहिताः सर्वे न पापाद् भयमस्ति वः॥
en: I have told you a bit only (of our devotional power). Now devoid of pride and vanity you all return together (to your homes).

description: The story of the greatness of the Brahmanas
sn: एवमस्त्विति ते सर्वे प्रतिपूज्य महामुनिम्। स्वदेशमगमन् हृष्टा राजानो भरतर्षभ॥
en: O best of the Bharatas, (then) those kings, saying "be it so" and bowing down to that great sage returned cheerfully to their country.

description: The story of the greatness of the Brahmana
sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच भूय एव महाभाग्यं ब्राह्मणानां निबोध मे। वैन्यो नामेह राजर्षिरश्वमेधाय दीक्षितः॥ तमत्रिर्गन्तुमारेभे वित्तार्थमिति नः श्रुतम्। भूयोऽर्थं नानुरुध्यत् सधर्मव्यक्तिनिदर्शनात्॥
en: Markandeya said : Hear from me again of the great glory of the Brahmanas. We have heard that a royal sage Vainya by name was engaged in celebrating the horse-sacrifice and that Atri was prepared to go to him for alms. But at last actuated by religious motives he abandoned his desire for riches.

description: The story of the greatness of the Brahmana
sn: स विचिन्त्य महातेजा वनमेवान्वरोचयत्। धर्मपत्नी समाहूय पुत्रांश्चेदमुवाच ह॥
en: After much deliberation (as to what he should do) that highly energetic (sage) became desirous of living in the forests and calling his wedded wife and sons together spoke to them thus

description: The story of the greatness of the Brahmana
sn: प्राप्स्यामः फलमत्यन्तं बहुलं निरुपद्रवम्। अरण्यगमनं क्षिप्रं रोचतां वो गुणाधिकम्॥
en: May it be your inclination to go to the forests soon; because (by repairing there) we shall attain the highly blissful and tranquil fulfillment (of our desires).

description: The story of the greatness of the Brahmana
sn: तं भार्या प्रत्युवाचाथधर्ममेवानुतन्वती। वैन्यं गत्वा महात्मानमर्थयस्वधनं बहु॥
en: To this his wife, actuated by virtuous motives, also replied “go to the high-souled Vainya and beg of him immense wealth.

description: The story of the greatness of the Brahmana
sn: स ते दास्यति राजर्षियजमानोऽर्थितोधनम्। तत आदाय विप्रर्षे प्रतिगृह्यधनं बहु॥
en: That royal sage engaged in horse sacrifice will give you the wealth begged by you. Then, O Brahmanic sage, having received from him vast wealth,

description: The story of the greatness of the Brahmana
sn: भृत्यान् सुतान् संविभज्य ततो व्रज यथेप्सितम्। एष वै परमोधर्मोधर्मविद्भिदाहृतः॥
en: And having distributed it among the sons and the attendants, you may go whither you like. This is the highest virtue as instanced by men versed in religion.

description: The story of the greatness of the Brahmana
sn: अत्रिरुवाच कथितो मे महाभागे गौतमेन महात्मना। वैन्योधर्मार्थसंयुक्तः सत्यव्रतसमन्वितः॥
en: Atri said: O highly fortunate (wife), I have been told by the noble-minded Gautama that Vainya is religious, conversant with (the principles of the science of) profit and devoted to truth.

description: The story of the greatness of the Brahmana
sn: द्वेष्टारः किंतु नः सन्ति वसन्तस्तत्र वै द्विजाः। यथा मे गौतमः प्राह ततो न व्यवसाम्यहम्॥
en: But he is surrounded by Brahmanas who are very envious of me. As Gautama has informed me of this I dare not go there.

description: The story of the greatness of the Brahmana
sn: तत्र स्म वाचं कल्याणीधर्मकामार्थसंहिताम्। मयोक्तामन्यथा ब्रूयुस्ततस्ते वै निरर्थिकाम्॥
en: For even if I speak these (highly) beneficial and religious words calculated to bring about the fulfillment of one's desires they will oppose me with speeches productive of no good.

description: The story of the greatness of the Brahmana
sn: गमिष्यामि महाप्राज्ञे रोचते मे वचस्तव। गाश्च मे दास्यते वैन्यः प्रभूतं चार्थसंचयम्॥
en: But, O highly wise (wife), I relish your proposal and will (therefore) go there. Vainya will bestow on me cows and immense wealth.

description: The story of the greatness of the Brahmana
sn: एवमुक्त्वा जगामाशु वैन्ययज्ञं महातपाः। गत्वा च यज्ञायतनमत्रिस्तुष्टाव तं नृपम्॥ वाक्यैर्मङ्गलसंयुक्तैः पूजयानोऽब्रवीद् वचः।
en: Markandeya continued Saying this, that sage of great devotion, soon repaired to Vainya's sacrifice. And reaching the sacrificial altar he eulogised the king. With noble speeches and then said these words.

description: The story of the greatness of the Brahmana
sn: अत्रिरुवाच राजन् धन्यस्तवमीशश्च भुवि त्वं प्रथमो नृपः॥
en: Atri said : O king, you are indeed blessed, you are the lord of all beings and are the greatest sovereign on earth.

description: The story of the greatness of the Brahmana
sn: स्तुवन्ति त्वां मुनिगणास्त्वदन्यो नास्तिधर्मवित्। तमब्रवीदृषिः क्रुद्धो वचनं वै महातपाः॥
en: The sages pay their adorations to you. And there is none conversant with religion besides you.” Thereupon that sage of great austerities (Gautama) said to him in anger.

description: The story of the greatness of the Brahmana
sn: गौतम उवाच ते मैवमत्रे पुन या न प्रज्ञा समाहिता। अत्र नः प्रथमं स्थाता महेन्द्रो वै प्रजापतिः॥
en: Gautama said: O Atri, do you not repeat such (foolish words) again. Your understanding is not yet matured. In this world, Mahendra, the lord of all creatures, is the greatest monarch.

description: The story of the greatness of the Brahmana
sn: अथात्रिरपि राजेन्द्र गौतमं प्रत्यभाषत। अयमेव विधाता हि यथैवेन्द्रः प्रजापतिः। त्वमेव मुह्यसे मोहान्न प्रज्ञानं तवास्ति ह॥
en: O king of kings, thereupon, Atri replied to Gautama “this king is as much the dispenser of our destiny as Indra, the lord of all creatures. Your intellect is clouded with ignorance and you have no sense at (all)."

description: The story of the greatness of the Brahmana
sn: गौतम उवाच जानामि नाहं मुह्यामि त्वमेवात्र विमुह्यते। स्तौषि त्वं दर्शनप्रेप्सू राजानं जनसंसदि॥
en: Gautama said: I am sure, it is not I but you who are labouring under a misconception in this matter. Desirous of obtaining his favour you are flattering the king before this assembly of men.

description: The story of the greatness of the Brahmana
sn: न वेत्थ परमंधर्मं न चावैषि प्रयोजनम्। बालस्त्वमसि मूढश्च वृद्धः केनापि हेतुना॥
en: You are not conversant with what is the highest duty nor do feel any need for it. You are ignorant as a child; why then have you grown so old in years?

description: The story of the greatness of the Brahmana
sn: विवदन्तौ तथा तौ तु मुनीनां दर्शने स्थितौ। ये तस्य यज्ञे संवृत्तास्तेऽपृच्छन्त कथं त्विमौ॥
en: Markandeya continued When they were thus quarreling before the Munis who were engaged in the sacrifice, the latter enquired "What is the matter with these two men?

description: The story of the greatness of the Brahmana
sn: प्रवेशः केन दत्तोऽयमुभयोर्वैन्यसंसदि। उच्चैः समभिभाषन्तौ केन कार्येण धिष्ठितौ॥
en: Who did admit them to the court of Vainya? What is it that they are clamouring for?”

description: The story of the greatness of the Brahmana
sn: ततः परमधर्मात्मा काश्यपः सर्वधर्मवित्। विवादिनावनुप्राप्तौ तावुभौ प्रेत्यवेदयत्॥
en: Then the highly righteous Kashyapa versed in all duties stepping between the disputants inquired of them the cause of their quarrel.

description: The story of the greatness of the Brahmana
sn: अथाब्रवीत् सदस्यांस्तु गौतमो मुनिसत्तमान्। आवयोर्व्याहृतं प्रश्नं शृणुत द्विजसत्तमाः॥
en: Thereupon, Gautama addressing that assembly of the most exalted sages said. "O the best of Brahmanas, hear the cause of our dispute.

description: The story of the greatness of the Brahmana
sn: वैन्यं विधातेत्याहात्रिरत्र नौ संशयो महान्। श्रुत्वैव तु महात्मानो मुनयोऽभ्यद्रवन् दुतम्॥
en: Atri says that Vainya rules over our destiny. But we entertain a grave doubt on the point. Markandeya said : Hearing this, those high-souled sages soon repaired to

description: The story of the greatness of the Brahmana
sn: सनत्कुमारंधर्मज्ञं संशयच्छेदनाय वै। स च तेषां वचः श्रुत्वा यथातत्त्वं महातपाः। प्रत्युवाचाथ तानेवंधर्मार्थसहितं वचः॥
en: The righteous Sanatkumara in order to solve their doubt. And he (Sanatkumara) of great devotional spirit, hearing their their words, addressed them with these words of true religious import..

description: The story of the greatness of the Brahmana
sn: सनत्कुमार उवाच ब्रह्म क्षत्रेण सहितं क्षत्रं च ब्रह्मणा सह! संयुक्तौ दहतः शत्रून् वनानीवाग्निमारुतौ॥
en: Sanatkumara said: As (when) fire united with the wind burns down forests, so (when) a Brahmana's energy is united with that of a Kshatriya and vice versa it consumes all enemies.

description: The story of the greatness of the Brahmana
sn: राजा वै प्रथितोधर्मः प्रजानां पतिरेव च। स एव शक्रः शुक्रश्च सधाता च बृहस्पतिः॥
en: The king is noted for establishing religion and he is the protector of his subjects. He is (like) Indra (a protector of all beings) like Shukra (a propounder of morals) like Brihaspati (an adviser) and (therefore) he is (justly) styled the ruler of our destiny.

description: The story of the greatness of the Brahmana
sn: प्रजापतिविराट् सम्राट् क्षत्रियो भूपतिर्नृपः। य एभिः स्तूयते शब्दैः कस्तं नार्चितुमर्हति॥
en: Is there (therefore) anybody who considers himself above worshipping the individual to whom such appellations as 'Prajapati' (the lord of all creatures), 'Virata', 'Emperor', 'Kshatriya' (one who preserves from pain), 'lord of earth,' and 'Monarch', are applied in praise?

description: The story of the greatness of the Brahmana
sn: पुरायोनियुधाजिच्च अभिया मुदितो भवः। स्वर्णेता सहजिद् बभुरिति राजाभिधीयते॥
en: The monarch is further styled 'the prime cause,' (of social order), 'the conqueror of battles,' (and therefore) the preserver of the (peace), 'the watchman', 'the contented', 'the lord', 'guide to heaven,' 'the easily victorious', 'Vishnu like.'

description: The story of the greatness of the Brahmana
sn: सत्ययोनिः पुराविच्च सत्यधर्मप्रवर्तकः। अधर्मादृषयो भीता बलं क्षत्रे समादधन्॥
en: 'Of effective wrath,' 'the victorious in wars' and 'the introducer of true religion.' The Rishis afraid of committing sins made over the (temporal) powers to the Kshatriyas.

description: The story of the greatness of the Brahmana
sn: आदित्यो दिवि देवेषु तमो नुदति तेजसा। तथैव नृपतिर्भूमाबधर्मान्नुदते भृशम्॥
en: Like the sun among the gods in heaven who destroys darkness by his rays the king among men eradicates sin from the earth.

description: The story of the greatness of the Brahmana
sn: ततो राज्ञः प्रधानत्वं शास्त्रप्रामाण्यदर्शनात्। उत्तरः सिद्ध्यते पक्षो येन राजेति भाषितम्॥
en: Therefore by the authority of the Shastras the greatness of the king is established. And I declare for him who has spoken in favour of the king.

description: The story of the greatness of the Brahmana
sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच ततः स राजा संहृष्टः सिद्धे पक्षे महामनाः। तमत्रिमब्रवीत् प्रीतः पूर्वं येनाभिसंस्तुतः॥
en: Markandeya said : Then the high minded king, greatly satisfied with the victorious party who first spoke in high terms of him, gladly addressed him with these words.

description: The story of the greatness of the Brahmana
sn: यस्मात् पूर्वं मनुष्येषु ज्यायांसं मामिहाब्रवीः। सर्वदेवैश्च विप्रर्षे सम्मितं श्रेष्ठमेव च।॥
en: 'O Brahmanic sage, as you have styled me the greatest and best of men, here and have compared me with the gods,

description: The story of the greatness of the Brahmana
sn: तस्मात् तेऽहं प्रदास्यामि विविधं वसु भूरि च। दासीसहरं श्यामानां सुवस्त्राणामलंकृतम्॥
en: I will therefore confer on you immense and dressed and well-adorned Shyama maids.

description: The story of the greatness of the Brahmana
sn: दशकोटीर्हिरण्यस्य रुक्मभारांस्तथा दश। एतद् ददामि विप्रर्षे सर्वज्ञस्त्वं मतो हि मे॥
en: I bestow on you one hundred millions of coins and ten Bharas (each bhara is equal to 32 maunds) of gold. According to my belief you are conversant with everything.

description: The story of the greatness of the Brahmana
sn: तदत्रिया॑यतः सर्वं प्रतिगृह्याभिसत्कृतः। प्रत्युज्जगाम तेजस्वी गृहानेव महातपाः॥
en: And the energetic Atri, thus honored by the king and having rightfully accepted all the wealth returned home.

description: The story of the greatness of the Brahmana
sn: प्रदाय चधनं प्रीतः पुत्रेभ्यः प्रयतात्मवान्। पः समभिसंधाय वनमेवान्वपद्यत॥
en: And having distributed that wealth among his sons, that self-contained sage gladly went to the forests with the view of performing asceticism.

sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच अत्रैव च सरस्वत्या गीतं परपुरंजय। पृष्टया मुनिना वीर शृणु तायेणधीमता॥
en: Markandeya said : O conqueror of hostile cities, O hero in this connection, Sarasvati, when asked by that intelligent Rishi Tarkshya, said (the following). Hear it.

sn: तार्क्ष्य उवाच किं नु श्रेयः पुरुषस्येह भद्रे कथं कुर्वन् न च्यवते स्वधर्मात्। आचक्ष्व मे चारुसर्वाङ्गि कुर्यां त्वया शिष्टो न च्यवेयं स्वधर्मात्॥
en: Tarkshya said: O blessed lady, what is the best thing for a man to do here on earth) and how he must act so that he may not deviate from (the path of) virtue. O beautiful lady, tell me all, so that being instructed by you I may not deviate from the path of my own duty (Dharma).

sn: कथं वाग्निं जुहुयां पूजये वा कस्मिन् काले केनधर्मो न नश्येत्। एतत् सर्वं सुभगे प्रब्रवीहि यथा लोकान् विरजाः संचरेयम्॥
en: When and how must one offer oblations to the fire and when must he worship, so that his virtue may not be destroyed? O blessed lady, tell me all, so that I may live in this world without any passion, craving or desire.

sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच एवं पृष्टा प्रीतियुक्तेन तेन शुश्रूषुमीक्ष्योत्तमबुद्धियुक्तम्। तालुं विप्रंधर्मयुक्तं हितं च सरस्वती वाक्यमिदं बभाषे॥
en: Markandeya said : Thus questioned by that cheerful Rishi and having seen him eager to learn and at the same time possessed of great intelligence, Sarasvati spoke these virtuous and beneficial words to the Brahmana Tarkshya.

sn: सरस्वत्युवाच यो ब्रह्म जानाति यथाप्रदेश स्वाध्यायनित्यः शुचिरप्रमत्तः। सवै पारं देवलोकस्य गन्ता सहामरैः प्राप्नुयात् प्रीतियोगम्॥
en: Sarasvati said : He who knows Brahma, he who perceives the Supreme with purity and equanimity goes to the celestials region and obtains the supreme bliss with the immortals.

sn: तत्र स्म रम्या विपुला विशोकाः सुपुष्पिताः पुष्करिण्यः सुपुण्याः। अकर्दमा मीनवत्यः सुतीर्था हिरण्मयैरावृताः पुण्डरीकैः॥
en: Many large, beautiful and sacred lakes are there, abounding in fishes, flowers and golden lotuses. They are like holy shrines and their very sight drives away all grief.

sn: तासां तीरेष्वासते पुण्यभाजो महीयमानाः पृथगप्सरोभिः। हिरण्यवर्णाभिरतीव हृष्टाः॥
en: Pious men, specially adored by the Apsaras, who are viriuous, well-adorned and goldencomplexioned, live in contentment on the banks of these lakes,

sn: परं लोकं गोप्रदास्त्वाप्नुवन्ति दत्त्वानड्वाहं सूर्यलोकं व्रजन्ति। वासो दत्त्वा चान्द्रमसं तु लोकं दत्त्वा हिरण्यममरत्वमेति॥
en: He who gives away cows (to the Brahmanas here) goes to the highest region. By giving bullocks he goes to the solar region, by giving ciothes he goes to the lunar region and by giving gold he goes to the region of the immortals.

sn: धेनुं दत्त्वा सुप्रभां सुप्रदोहां कल्याणवत्सामपलायिनीं च। स्तावद् वर्षाण्यासते देवलोके॥
en: He who gives away a beautiful cow with a fine calf, a cow which is easily milked and which does not run away lives in the celestials region as many years as there are hairs on the body of that cow.

sn: अनड्वाहं सुव्रतं यो ददाति हलस्य वोढारमनन्तवीर्यम्। धुरन्धरं बलवन्तं युवानं प्राप्नोति लोकान् दशधेनुदस्य॥
en: He who gives a fine, strong, powerful and young bullock which is capable of drawing the plough and of carrying burdens goes to the region obtained by men who give away ten kine.

sn: ददाति यो वै कपिलां सचैलां कांस्योपदोहां द्रविणैरुत्तरीयैः। तैस्तैर्गुणैः कामदुहाथ भूत्वा नरं प्रदातारमुपैति सा गौः॥
en: When a man gives away a well-caparisoned Kapila cow with money and with a bronze milk pot, he finds that cow, becoming a giver of boons, has come to his side by her own distinguished qualities,

sn: स्तावत् फलं भवति गोप्रदाने। मासप्तमं तारयते परत्र॥
en: He who gives away cows obtains so many merits as are the number of hair on the body of those cows. He also saves (from hell) his sons, grandsons and ancestors up to the seventh generation (upwards and downwards).

sn: सदक्षिणां काञ्चनचारुशृङ्गी कांस्योपदोहां द्रविणैरुत्तरीयैः। धेनुं तिलानां ददतो द्विजाय लोका वसूनां सुलभा भवन्ति।॥
en: He, who presents to a Brahmana sesame made up in the form of a cow having horns made of gold with money and a brazen milk pail, goes easily to the region of the Vasus.

sn: स्वकर्मभिर्दानसंनिरुद्ध तीव्रान्धकारे नरके सम्पतन्तम्। महार्णवे नौरिव वातयुक्ता दानं गवां तारयते परत्र॥
en: A man by his own acts falls into the dark depth of the lower region infested by evil spirits, as a ship (goes down) tossed by the tempest on the high sea. But gift of kine saves him in the next world.
