sn: यो ब्राह्मदेयां तु ददाति कन्यां भूमिप्रदानं च करोति विप्रे। ददाति दानं विधिना च यश्च स लोकमाप्नोति पुरंदरस्य॥
en: He who gives his daughter in marriage in the Brahma form, who gives away land to the Brahmanas and duly makes other presents goes to the region of Purandara.

sn: यः सप्त वर्षाणि जुहोति तार्क्ष्य हव्यं त्वग्नौ नियतः साधुशीलः। सप्तावरान् सप्त पूर्वान् पुनाति पितामहानात्मना कर्मभिः स्वैः॥
en: O Tarkshya, the virtuous man who continually offers oblations to the sacred fire for seven years sanctifies by his this action his seven generations upwards and downwards,

sn: तार्क्ष्य उवाच माचक्ष्व मे पृच्छतश्चानुरूपे। त्वयानुशिष्टोऽहमिहाद्य विद्यां यदग्निहोत्रस्य व्रतं पुराणम्॥
en: Tarkshya said: O beautiful lady, tell me who ask you the rules of the Agnihotra as explained in the Vedas. I shall learn from you the timehonoured rules for perpetually keeping the sacred fire.

sn: सरस्वत्युवाच ब्रह्मविज्जुहुयानाविपश्चित्। बुभुत्सवः शुचिकामा हि देवा नाश्रद्दधानाद्धि हविर्जुषन्ति॥
en: Goddess Sarasvati explained that "O Sage! the person impure physically and mentally both viz who has unwashed hands, denied of conscious on Vedas and inexperienced to dealing with the essence of Vedas is unentitled to offer the oblation in the fire. The Gods are always interested to know the deposition of others, they prefer sanctity and this is the reason they do not accept the oblations offered by a man without obeisance.

sn: नाश्रोत्रियं देवहव्ये नियुञ्ज्यान्मोघं पुरा सिञ्चति तादृशो हि। अपूर्वमश्रोत्रियमाह ता न तादृग् जुहुयादग्निहोत्रम्॥
en: A man having no expertise in Vedic hymns should not be appointed in the work of offering the oblations to gods, because it proves merely a futile exercise. O tearkshya! such a mari nor properly known to Veda is considered as alien to the offering projects. Hence, he is liot entitled to join with Agnihotra.

sn: कृशाश्च ये जुह्वति श्रद्दधानाः सत्यव्रता हुतशिष्टाशिनश्च। वै गवां लोकं प्राप्य ते पुण्यगन्धं पश्यन्ति देवं परमं चापि सत्यम्॥
en: The people sacrosanct in heart by virtues of observing the austerity, who execute offering in their day to day exercise, accept only residual to the offering ; Access to the abode of cows field with pleasing fragrance and their eyes see a supreme soul, the truth.

sn: तार्क्ष्य उवाच क्षेत्रज्ञभूतां परलोकभावे कर्मोदये बुद्धिमतिप्रविष्टाम्। प्रज्ञां च देवीं सुभगे विमृश्य पृच्छामि त्वां का ह्यसि चारुरूपे॥
en: Tarkshya said: O Goddess! having attracting complexion you are in the form of soul and the supreme wisdom inserted in metaphysics and the topics related to the consequence of action. You too are a goddess of conscience Assuming you in this both forms I ask the real identity of yours.

sn: सरस्वत्युवाच अग्निहोत्रादहमभ्यागतास्मि विप्रर्षभाणां संशयच्छेदनाय। त्वत्संयोगादहमेतब्रुवं भावे स्थिता तथ्यमर्थं यथावत्॥
en: Sarasvati said : O sage! I am Sarasvati in the form of learning, came duly summon by the offering made by Brahmanas with a purpose of alleviating your lurking doubts. You are devotee, hence I have explained the above said topics solemnly because I exist in the internal disposition of devotees.

sn: तार्थ्य उवाच न हि त्वया सदृशी काचिदस्ति विभ्राजसे ह्यतिमात्रं यथा श्रीः। रूपं च ते दिव्यमनन्तकान्ति प्रज्ञां च देवीं सुभगे बिभर्षि॥
en: Tar enquired again O nice goddess! nobody here is worth comparison with you. You are perceived luminating like goddess Lakshmi. Your complexion with this supreme radiance is a divine one. You also hold the divine conscience concomitant to it. (I am curious to know its reason).

sn: सरस्वत्युवाच श्रेष्ठानि यानि द्विपदां वरिष्ठ यज्ञेषु विद्वन्नुपपादयन्ति। तैरेव चाहं सम्प्रवृद्धा भवामि चाप्यायिता रूपवती च विप्र॥
en: Sarasvati replied: O scholar! you really are great man. O great Bhramin! my divine complexion is due to noble deeds of performed by the persons engrossed with offering or accumulating the best thing to their account which automatically satiates and gives radiance to me.

sn: यच्चापि द्रव्यमुपयुज्यते ह वानस्पत्यमायसं पार्थिवं वा। दिव्येन रूपेण च प्रज्ञया च तेनैव सिद्धिरिति विद्धि विद्वन्॥
en: scholar! put it properly in your understanding that the offerings made by Brahmins are consisting of the wooden products like Shruva, fuel, the glittering items like gold etc. and physical items like Brihi etc. These all items as a gross effect provide me with divine complexion and conscience both.

sn: तार्क्ष्य उवाच इदं श्रेयः परमं मन्यमाना व्यायच्छन्ते मुनयः सम्प्रतीताः। आचक्ष्व मे तं परमं विशोकं मोक्षं परं यं प्रविशन्तिधीराः। सांख्या योगा परमं यं विदन्ति परं पुराणं तमहं न वेद्मि॥
en: O Goddess! kindly describe that supreme position of emancipation where is left no place for agony for which sake the great sages imposed due checks on their sensories and the people of high degree patience inter into. This is because that supreme position as perceived to the yogis having expertise in Samkhya and Karma. I am absolutely alien to that element of emancipation.

sn: सरस्वत्युवाच तं वै परं वेदविदः प्रपन्नाः परं परेभ्यः प्रथितं पुराणम्। स्तपोधना वीतशोका विमुक्ताः॥
en: Sarasvati replied : Position of Brahman all immortal is for which the yogis observed regular perseverance and consider austerity as only wealth and ultimately get-read of the net work of agony as a result of taking over that supreme position. The experts in Vedas shelter to that very supreme position.

sn: तस्याथ मध्ये वेतसः पुण्यगन्धः सहाशाखो विपुलो विभाति। तस्य मूलात् सरितः प्ररवन्ति मधूदकप्रावणा: सुपुण्याः॥
en: A huge tree of cane in the form of cosmos within that supreme Brahman is existed. Its branches are unending and represent the luxuries and the words etc. are the fragrant giving the material pleasures added with this tree. The root to that cosmos formed tree is Avidya (ignorance). A number of reverse flowing continuously are in the form of temptation and luxuries. These rivers are emanated from the root of that ignorance. These rivers appear attractive having pure water with fragrance extraneously and float the satiating matters like water and as sweet as honey.

sn: शाखां शाखां महानद्यः संयान्ति सिकताशयाः। धानापूपा मांसशाकाः सदा पायसकर्दमाः॥
en: However, these all are incapable to give any fruitful result like fried barley, field with a number of pores like sweet bread, impure as the flesh, void like dry vegetable and generate malice to the heart and mind not lesser than marsh inspite of appearing like sweet dish, These are distinct to each other like sand particles and these flow inside the branches of that cane tree (Calamus).

sn: यस्मिन्नग्निमुखा देवाः सेन्द्राः सहमरुद्गणाः। ईजिरे क्रतुभिः श्रेष्ठैस्तत् पदं परमं मम॥
en: O sage! the supreme position belongs to me which is duly worshipped by Indra, Agni and Vayu and other gods including Maruts through arranging several offerings in order to attain that supreme position known as Brahman.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततः स पाण्डवो विप्रं मार्कण्डेयमुवाच ह। कथयस्वेति चरितं मनोवैवस्वतस्य च॥शा
en: Vaishampayana said: Then that son of Pandu (Yudhishthira) spoke thus to the Brahmana Markandeya, “narrate (to me) the history of Vaivasvata Manu.”

sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच विवस्वतः सुतो राजन् महर्षिः सुप्रतापवान्। बभूव नरशार्दूल प्रजापतिसमद्युतिः॥
en: Markandeya said : O king, O foremost of men, there was a mighty great Rishi; he was the son of Vivasvata and he was as effulgent as Prajapati.

sn: ओजसा तेजसा लक्ष्या तपसा च विशेषतः। अतिचक्राम पितरं मनुः स्वं च पितामहम्॥
en: He far excelled his father and grand-father in prowess, in strength, in fortune and also in religious penances.

sn: अर्श्वबाहुर्विशालायां बदर्यां स नराधिप। एकपादस्थितस्तीव्र चकार सुमहत् तपः॥
en: Standing on one leg and with uplifted arms, that chief of men performed severe asceticism in the extensive Badari.

sn: अवाक्शिरास्तथा चापि नेत्रैरनिमिषैर्दढम्। सोऽतप्यत तपो घोरं वर्षाणामयुतं तदा॥
en: With head downwards and with steadfast eyes he performed these severe austerities for ten thousand years.

sn: तं कदाचित् तपस्यन्तमार्द्रचीरजटाधरम्। चीरिणीतीरमागम्य मत्स्यो वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Once upon a time when he, with wet clothes on and with matted looks on his head, was performing such austerities, there came a fish on the banks of the Chirini and spoke to him thus.

sn: भगवन् क्षुद्रमत्स्योऽस्मि बलवद्भ्यो भयं मम। मत्स्येभ्यो हि ततो मां त्वं त्रातुमर्हसि सुव्रत॥
en: "O exalted one, I am a helpless little fish; I am afraid of the large ones; a vow-observing Rishi, you should extend your protection to me,

sn: दुर्बलं बलवन्तो हि मत्स्या मत्स्य विशेषतः। आस्वदन्ति सदा वृत्तिर्विहिता नः सनातनी॥ तस्माद् भयौघान्महतो मज्जन्तं मां विशेषतः। त्रातुमर्हसि कर्तास्मि कृते प्रतिकृतं तव॥
en: Especially when this is the fixed custom amongst us that the big fishes prey upon the smaller ones. Therefore be pleased to save me from being drowned in the sea of terrors. I shall requite you for your help to me."

sn: स मत्स्यवचनं श्रुत्वा कृपयाभिपरिप्लुतः। मनुर्वैवस्वतोऽगृहणात् तं मत्स्य पाणिना स्वयम्।।१०।
en: Having heard these words of the fish, the Vaivasvata Manu was filled with pity and took out the fish from the water with his own hands.

sn: उदकान्तमुपानीय मत्स्यं वैवस्वतो मनुः। अलिञ्जरे प्राक्षिपत् तं चन्द्रांशुसदृशप्रभम्॥
en: The fish which had a body as bright as the rays of the moon, after being taken out of the water, was again put back in an earthen water vessel.

sn: स तत्र ववृधे राजन् मत्स्यः परमसत्कृतः। पुत्रवत् स्वीकरोत् तस्मै मनुर्भावं विशेषतः॥
en: O king, thus being reared, that fish grew in size and Manu carefully tended it as if were a child of his.

sn: अथ कालेन महता स मत्स्यः सुमहानभूत्। अलिञ्जरे यथा चैव नासौ समभवत् किल॥
en: After a long period of time that fish grew to be so large that there was no room for it in that vessel.

sn: अथ मत्स्यो मनुं दृष्ट्वा पुनरेवाभ्यभाषत। भगवन् साधु मेऽद्यान्यत् स्थानं सम्प्रतिपादय॥
en: Manu saw that the fish again spoke to him thus, “O exalted one, appoint a better habitation for me."

sn: उद्धृत्यालिञ्जरात् तस्मात् ततः स भगवान् मनुः। तं मत्स्यमनयद् वापी महतीं स मनुस्तदा॥
en: Then the exalted Manu, that conqueror of hostile cities, took it out of that vessel and carried it to a large tank and put it into its water).

sn: तत्र तं प्राक्षिपच्चापि मनुः परपुरंजय। अथावर्धत मत्स्यः स पुनर्वर्षगणान् बहून्॥ द्वियोजनायता वापी विस्तृता चापि योजनम्। तस्यां नासौ समभवन्मत्स्यो राजीवलोचन॥ विचेष्टितुं च कौन्तेय मत्स्यो वाप्यां विशाम्पते। मनु मत्स्यस्ततो दृष्ट्वा पुनरेवाभ्यभाषत॥
en: The fish began to grow even there for a long period of time, till at last though the tank was (wo yojanas in length and one yojana in breadth. O lotus eyed son of Kunti, O ruler of men, he had no room (even) there to play about. Manu saw that the fish again spoke to him thus,

sn: नयं मा भगवन् साधो समुद्रमहिषीं प्रियाम्। गङ्गां तत्र निवत्स्यामि यथा वा तात मन्यसे॥
en: "O exalted one, O pious one, O sire, take me to the Ganga, the favourite wife of the Ocean or do what you think proper.

sn: निदेशे हि मया तुभ्यं स्थातव्यमनसूयता। वृद्धिर्हि मया प्राप्ता त्वत्कृते हि मयानघ॥
en: O sinless one, as I have grown to this size through your favour, I shall cheerfully do what you command me."

sn: एवमुक्तो मनुर्मत्स्यमनयद् भगवान् वशी। नदीं गङ्गां तत्र चैनं स्वयं प्राक्षिपदच्युतः॥
en: Having been thus addressed, the up-right, continent and the adorable Manu took the fish to the river Ganga and put it into its water with his own hands.

sn: स तत्र ववृधे मत्स्यः किंचित्कालमरिदम। ततः पुनर्मनुं दृष्ट्वा मत्स्यो वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: O chastiser of foes, the fish there also began to grow for some time and then seeing Manu it spoke to him thus,

sn: गङ्गायां हि न शक्नोमि बृहत्वाच्चेष्टितुं प्रभो। समुद्रं नय मामाशु प्रसीद भगवन्निति॥
en: "O lord, I am unable to move about in the Ganga on account of my huge body. Therefore, O exalted one, take me soon to the sea.”

sn: उद्धृत्य गङ्गासलिलात् ततो मत्स्यं मनुः स्वयम्। समुद्रमनयत् पार्थ तत्र चैनमवासृजत्॥
en: O son of Pritha, Manu took it out of the Ganga and carried it to the sea and put it there.

sn: सुमहानपि मत्स्यस्तु स मनोनयतस्तदा। आसीद् यथेष्टहार्यश्च स्पर्शगन्धसुखस्य वै॥
en: Notwithstanding its huge size Manu easily carried it and its touch and smell were also pleasant to him.

sn: यदा समुद्रे प्रक्षिप्तः स मत्स्यो मनुना तदा। तत एनमिदं वाक्यं स्पयमान इवाब्रवीत्।॥
en: When that fish was thrown into the sea by Manu, it smilingly spoke these words to Manu,

sn: भगवन् हि कृता रक्षा त्वया सर्वा विशेषतः। प्राप्तकालं तु यत् कार्यं त्वया तच्छूयतां मम॥
en: “O exalted one, you have protected me with special care; hear what you should do in the fullness of time.

sn: अचिराद् भगवन् भौममिदं स्थावरजङ्गमम्। सर्वमेव महाभाग प्रलयं वै गमिष्यति॥
en: O exalted one, O greatly blessed one; the dissolution of all this mobile and immobile world is now near at hand.

sn: सम्प्रक्षालनकालोऽयं लोकानां समुपस्थितः। तस्मात् त्वां बोधयाम्यद्य यत् ते हितमनुत्तमम्॥
en: The proper time for purging off this earth is almost come; therefore I tell you what will be good for you.

sn: त्रसानां स्थावराणां च यच्चेङ्गं यच्च नेङ्गति। तस्य सर्वस्य सम्प्राप्तः कालः परमदारुणः॥
en: The terrible doom has now come to the mobile and the immobile things of the creation, those that have locomotion and those that have not.

sn: नौश्च कारयितव्या ते दृढा युक्तवटारका। तत्र सप्तर्षिभिः सार्धमारुहेथा महामुने॥
en: You should (at once) build a strong and huge ark and furnish it with a long rope. O great Rishis, get into it with the seven Rishis.

sn: बीजानि चैव सर्वाणि यथोक्तानि द्विजैः पुरा। तस्यामारोहयेर्नावि सुसंगुप्तानि भागशः॥
en: Take with you all the different seeds which were enumerated in the days of yore by the twice-born Brahmanas; and you must separately and carefully preserve them.

sn: नौस्थश्च मां प्रतीक्षेथास्ततो मुनिजनप्रिय। आगमिष्याम्यहं शृङ्गी विज्ञेयस्तेन तापस॥
en: O beloved of the Rishis, while remaining in that ark wait for me, and I shall appear to you in the shape of a homed animal. O ascetic, recognise me then.

sn: एवमेतत् त्वया कार्यमापृष्टोऽसि व्रजाम्यहम्। ता न शक्या महत्यो वै आपस्ततु मया विना॥
en: I now depart, you should act according to my instructions, for without my help, you cannot save yourself from the fearful flood.”

sn: नाभिशक्यमिदं चापि वचनं मे त्वया विभो। एवं करिष्य इति तं स मत्स्यं प्रत्यभाषत॥
en: He (Manu) then thus replied to that fish, "O lord, I do not doubt all that you have said. I shall do all this."

sn: जग्मतुश्च यथाकाममनुज्ञाप्य परस्परम्। ततो मनुर्महाराज यथोक्तं मत्स्यकेन ह॥
en: Giving instructions to each other, they both went away as they pleased. O great king, then Manu as told by the fish,

sn: बीजान्यादाय सर्वाणि सागरं पुप्लुवे तदा। नौकया शुभया वीर महोर्मिणमरिंदम॥
en: O chastiser of foes, O hero, procured all the different seeds and set sail in an excellent vessel on the surging sea.

sn: चिन्तयामास च मनुस्तं पृथिवीपते। स च तच्चिन्तितं ज्ञात्वा मत्स्यः परपुरंजय॥
en: O ruler of earth, O conqueror of hostile cities, he thought of that fish and that fish also, knowing his thought,

sn: शृङ्गी तत्राजगामाशु तदा भरतसत्तम। तं दृष्ट्वा मनुजव्याघ्र मनुर्मत्स्यं जलार्णवे॥ शृङ्गिणं तं यथोक्तेन रूपेणादिमिवोच्छ्रितम्। वटारकमयं पाशमथ मत्स्यस्य मूर्धनि॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, appeared there with horns in its head. O foremost of men, seeing in the ocean that fish with the horn emerging like a rock (as he was told before, he (Manu) threw the noose (made by the rope) on the head of that fish,

sn: मनुर्मनुजशार्दूल तस्मिन् शृङ्गे न्यवेशयत्। संयतस्तेन पाशेन मत्स्यः परपुरंजय॥ वेगेन महता नावं प्राकर्षल्लवणाम्भसि। स च तांस्तारयन् नावा समुद्रं मनुजेश्वर॥ नृत्यमानमिवोर्मीभिर्गर्जमानमिवाम्भसा। क्षोभ्यमाणा महाबातैः सा नौस्तस्मिन् महोदधौ॥ घूर्णते चपलेव स्त्री मत्ता परपुरंजय। नैव भूमिर्न च दिशः प्रदिशो वा चकाशिरे॥
en: O foremost of men, O conqueror of hostile cities, fattened by the noose, the fish towed the ark with great force over the salt water. O best of men, it dragged him in that vessel in the roaring and bellowing sea. Tossed by the tempest on the great ocean, the vessel reeled about like a drunken harlot. O conqueror of hostile cities, neither land nor the four cardinal points of the horizon could be then distinguished.

sn: सर्वमाम्भसमेवासीत् खं द्योश्च नरपुङ्गव। एवंभूते तदा लोके संकुले भरतर्षभ॥
en: O foremost of men, there was water everywhere; the water covered the heaven and the sky. O best of the Bharata race, when the world was thus flooded,

sn: अदृश्यन्तर्षयः सप्त मनुर्मत्स्यस्तथैव च। एवं बहून् वर्षगणांस्तां नावं सोऽथ मत्स्यकः॥ चकर्षातन्द्रितो राजंस्तस्मिन् सलिलसंचये। ततो हिमवतः शृङ्ग यत् परं भरतर्षभ।॥ तत्राकर्षत् ततो नावं स मत्स्यः कुरुनन्दन। अथाब्रवीत् तदा मत्स्यस्तानृषीन् प्रहसन् शनैः॥
en: None but Manu, the seven Rishis and the fish could be seen. O king, for many years it diligently dragged the boat on the flood. Then, O descendant of Kuru, O best of the Bharata race, it then dragged the ark to the peak of the Himalayas. Then that fish smilingly spoke thus to those Rishis.

sn: अस्मिन् हिमवतः शृङ्गे नावं बध्नीत मा चिरम्। सा बद्धा तत्र तैस्तूर्णमृषिभिर्भरतर्षभ॥
en: "Without delay bind the ark to peak of the Himalayas." O best of the Bharata race, they soon tied the vessel there.

sn: नौमत्स्यस्य वचः श्रुत्वा शृङ्गे हिमवतस्तदा। तच्च नौबन्धनं नाम शृङ्गं हिमवतः परम्॥
en: On the Himalayan peakon hearing the words of the fish. Since that day that great Himalayan peak is called Naukabandhana.

sn: ख्यातमद्यापि कौन्तेय तद् विद्धि भरतर्षभ। अथाब्रवीदनिमिषस्तानृषीन् सहितस्तदा॥
en: And is celebrated as such up to date. O son of Kunti, know this. Then that fish thus spoke to those Rishis assembled together,

sn: अहं प्रजापतिर्ब्रह्मा मत्परं नाधिगम्यते। मत्स्यरूपेण यूयं च मयास्मान्मोक्षिता भयात्॥
en: “I am the Lord of creatures, Brahma; none is greater than myself. In ihe form of a fish I have saved you from this fear.

sn: मनुना च प्रजाः सर्वाः सदेवासुरमानुषाः। इष्टव्याः सर्वलोकाश्च यच्चेङ्गं यच्च नेङ्गति॥
en: Manu will create all beings, gods Asuras and men and all those who have power of locomotion and who have not.

sn: तपया चापि तीव्रण प्रतिभास्य भविष्यति। मत्प्रसादात् प्रजासर्गे न च मोहं गमिष्यति॥
en: By practising severe asceticism, he will acquire this power. With my blessings, illusion will have no power over him."

sn: इत्युक्त्वा वचनं मत्स्यः क्षणेनादर्शनं गतः। इष्टुकामः प्रजाश्चापि मनुर्वैवस्वतः स्वयम्॥
en: Having said this, the fish disappeared in a moment. Vaivasvata Manu also became esirous of creating the creatures.

sn: प्रमूढोऽभूत् प्रजासर्गे तपस्तेपे महत् ततः। तपसा महता युक्तः सोऽथ उरष्टुं प्रचक्रमे॥ सर्वाः प्रजा मनुः साक्षाद् यथावद् भरतर्षभ। इत्येतन्मात्स्यकं नाम पुराणं परिकीर्तितम्॥
en: In this work of creation, illusion overtook him: he therefore performed great asceticism, Having obtained ascetic success, O best of the Bharata race, Manu again took up the work of creation in proper and exact order. I have thus narrated to you the old story called the Legend of the Fish.

sn: आख्यानमिदमाख्यातं सर्वपापहरं मया। य इदं शृणुयान्नित्यं मनोश्चरितमादितः। स सुखी सर्वपूर्णार्थः सर्वलोकमियान्नरः॥
en: He who every day hears this old history of Manu obtains all happiness and all other objects of desires and goes to heaven.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततः स पुनरेवाथ मार्कण्डेयं यशस्विनम्। पप्रच्छ विनयोपेतोधर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Then Dharmaraja Yudhishthira again asked the illustrious Markandeya in all humility.

sn: नैके युगसलान्तास्त्वया दृष्टा महामुने। न चापीह समः कश्चिदायुष्मान् दृश्यते तव॥
en: "O great Rishi, you have seen many thousands of ages pass away. In this world there is none who is seen to be so long lived as you.

sn: वर्जयित्वा महात्मानं ब्रह्माणं परमेष्ठिनम्। न तेऽस्ति सदृशः कश्चिदायुषा ब्रह्मवित्तम॥
en: O foremost of Brahmanas, there is none equal to you in years except the high-souled Brahma Parameshthi.

sn: अनन्तरिक्षे लोकेऽस्मिन् देवदानववर्जिते। त्वमेव प्रलये विप्र ब्रह्माणमुपतिष्ठसे॥
en: O Brahmana, you worship Brahma at the time of the great dissolution of the universe when this world becomes devoid of sky, the celestials and the Danavas.

sn: प्रलये चापि निर्वृत्ते प्रबुद्धे च पितामहे। त्वमेकः सृज्यमानानि भूतानीह प्रपश्यसि॥ चतुर्विधानि विप्रर्षे यथावत् परमेष्ठिना। वायुभूता दिशः कृत्वा विक्षिप्यापस्ततस्ततः॥
en: When that dissolution ceases and the grandsire awakes, you alone, O great Rishi, see the Parameshti (Brahma) duly recreate the four orders of beings after having filled the cardinal points with air and placed the waters in their proper places.

sn: त्वया लोकगुरुः साक्षात् सर्वलोकपितामहः। आराधितो द्विजश्रेष्ठ तत्परेण समाधिना॥
en: O foremost of Brahmanas, you have worshipped in his own presence the great Lord and the grandsire of all creatures with your soul in great Samadhi.

sn: स्वप्रमाणमथो विप्र त्वया कृतमनेकशः। घोरेणाविश्य तपसा वेधसो निर्जितास्त्वया॥
en: O Brahmana, you have many times seen with your eyes, the primeval acts of creation. Being deeply engaged in severe asceticism, you have also excelled the celestials themselves.

sn: नारायणाङ्कप्रख्यस्त्वं साम्परायेऽतिपठ्यसे। भगवाननेकशः कृत्वा त्वया विष्णोश्च विश्वकृत्॥ कर्णिकोद्धरणं दिव्यं ब्रह्मणः कामरूपिणः। रत्नालंकारयोगाभ्यां दृग्भयां दृष्टस्त्वया पुरा॥
en: You are considered to be one who is near Narayana in the next world. In the days of yore you had many times seen the supreme creator of the world with spiritual eyes and with renunciation which first opened your pure and lotuslike heart, the only place where the multiform Vishnu of universal knowledge might be seen.

sn: तस्मात् तवान्तको मृत्युर्जरा वा देहनाशिनी। न त्वां विशति विप्रर्षे प्रसादात् परमेष्ठिनः॥
en: Hence through the favour of Parameshti, O Brahmana Rishi, neither death nor old age that causes the destruction of the body has any power over you.

sn: यदा नैवं रविर्नाग्निर्न वायुर्न च चन्द्रमाः। नैवान्तरिक्षं नैवोर्वी शेषं भवति किंचन॥
en: When neither the sun nor the moon nor fire, nor earth, nor air, nor sky, remains,

sn: तस्मिन्नेकार्णवे लोके नष्टे स्थावरजङ्गमे। नष्टे देवासुरगणे समुत्सन्नमहोरगे॥
en: When the world with its mobile and immobile creation being destroyed looks like an ocean, when the celestials, the Asuras and the great Nagas are destroyed,

sn: शयानममितात्मानं पद्मोत्पलनिकेतनम्। त्वमेकः सर्वभूतेशं ब्रह्माणमुपतिष्ठसि।॥
en: When (at such a period) the lord of creatures takes his seat on a lotus and sleeps there then you alone remain to worship him.

sn: एतत् प्रत्यक्षतः सर्वं पूर्वं वृत्तं द्विजोत्तम। तस्मादिच्छाम्यहं श्रोतुं सर्वहेत्वात्मिकां कथाम्॥ अनुभूतं हि बहुशस्त्वयैकेन द्विजोत्तमा न तेऽस्त्यविदितं किंचित् सर्वलोकेषु नित्यदा॥
en: O foremost of Brahmanas, you have seen with your own eyes all that happened before. You alone have seen many things by your senses. There is nothing in all the world that is not known to you. Therefore, I eagerly desire to hear all about things.

sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच हन्त ते वर्णयिष्यामि नमस्कृत्वा स्वयम्भुवे। पुरुषाय पुराणाय शाश्वतायाव्ययाय च॥ अव्यक्ताय सुसूक्ष्माय निर्गुणाय गुणात्मने। स एष पुरुषव्याघ्र पीतवासा जनार्दनः॥
en: Markandeya said : Bowing down to that self-existent, primordial Being, who is eternal, undeteriorating and inconceivable who is both endued and devoid of attributes, I shall explain to you all. O foremost of men, Janardana clad in yellow garb,

sn: एष कर्ता विकर्ता च भूतात्मा भूतकृत् प्रभुः। अचिन्त्यं महदाश्चर्यं पवित्रमिति चोच्यते॥
en: Is the great mover and creator of all; he is the soul and the framer of all things. He is the lord of all; he is called great, incomprehensible, wonderful and immaculate,

sn: अनादिनिधनं भूतं विश्वमव्ययमक्षयम्। एष कर्ता न क्रियते कारणं चापि पौरुषे॥२०
en: He is without beginning and without end, he pervades all the world, he is unchangeable and undeteriorating. He is the creator of all. But himself is increate, the cause of all power.

sn: यद्येष पुरुषो वेद वेदा अपि न तं विदुः। सर्वमाश्चर्यमेवैतन्निर्वृत्तं राजसत्तम॥
en: His knowledge is greater than that of all the celestials. O foremost of kings, of kings, alter dissolution, all this wonderful creation,

sn: आदितो मनुजव्याघ्रकृत्स्नस्य जगत: क्षये। चत्वार्याहुः सहाणि वर्षाणां तत् कृतं युगम्॥ तस्य तावच्छती संध्या संध्यांशश्च तथाविधः। त्रीणि वर्षसलराणि त्रेतायुगमिहोच्यते॥
en: O best of men, again comes to life. It is said Krita Yuga constitutes four thousand years, including its morning and evening which comprise four hundred years. Treta Yuga is said to comprise three thousand years.

sn: तस्य तावच्छती संध्या संध्यांशश्च ततः परम्। तथा वर्षसहहरे द्वे द्वापरं परिमाणतः॥
en: Its morning and evening comprise three hundred years. The Yuga that follows is called Dvapara and it is said to comprise two thousand years.

sn: तस्यापि द्विशती संध्या संध्यांशश्च तथाविधः। सहरमेकं वर्षाणां ततः कलियुगं स्मृतम्॥
en: Its morning and evening comprise two hundred years. It is said that Kali Yuga constitutes one thousand years,

sn: तस्य वर्षशतं संधिः संध्यांशश्च ततः परम्। संधिसंध्यांशयोस्तुल्यं प्रमाणमुपधारय॥
en: Its morning and evening comprise one hundred years. Know that the duration of the morning and evening (of a Yuga) is the same.

sn: क्षीणे कलियुगे चैव प्रवर्तेत कृतं युगम्। एषा द्वादशसाही युगाख्या परिकीर्तिता॥
en: After Kali Yuga is over, Treta Yuga comes again; and thus it is said that all the Yugas comprise a cycle of twelve thousand years.

sn: एतत् सहरपर्यन्तमहो ब्राह्ममुदाहृतम्। विश्वं हि ब्रह्मभवने सर्वतः परिवर्तते॥ लोकानां मनुजव्याघ्र प्रलयं तं विदुर्बुधाः। अल्पावशिष्टे तु तदा युगान्ते भरतर्षभ॥ सहगन्ते नराः सर्वे प्रायशोऽनृतवादिनः। यज्ञप्रतिनिधिः पार्थ दानप्रतिनिधिस्तथा॥
en: One full thousand of such cycles would constitute a day of Brahma. O foremost of men, when this universe is withdrawn and taken back within its (original) home, (namely) Brahma himself, that disappearance of all things is called by the learned "the universal dissolution." O best of the Bharata race, at the end of the last mentioned one thousand years, men become addicted to falsehood. O son of Pritha, they then perform sacrifices and gifts by representatives.

sn: व्रतप्रतिनिधिश्चैव तस्मिन् काले प्रवर्तते। ब्राह्मणाः शूद्रकर्माणस्तथा शूद्राधनार्जकाः॥
en: Vows observed by representatives are also introduced. The Brahmanas perform acts that should be performed by the Shudras and the Shudras take to earn wealth.

sn: क्षत्रधर्मेण वाप्यत्र वर्तयन्ति गते युगे। निवृत्तयज्ञस्वाध्याया दण्डाजिनविवर्जिताः॥ ब्राह्मणाः सर्वभक्षाश्च भविष्यन्ति कलौ युगे। अजपा ब्राह्मणास्तात शूद्रा जपपरायणाः॥
en: The Kshatriyas also adopt the practices of the Brahmanas. In the Kali Yuga the Brahmanas will abstain from sacrifices and the study of the Vedas. They will give up their staff and deer skin and they will eat everything. O child, the Brahmanas will give up prayer and the Shudras will betake themselves to these.

sn: विपरीते तदा लोके पूर्वरूपं क्षयस्य तत्। बहवो म्लेच्छराजानः पृथिव्यां मनुजाधिप॥
en: O ruler of men, the course of the world then looks subverted, there are the signs of the universal dissolution. Then will rule over the earth many Mlechchha kings.

sn: मृषानुशासिनः पापा मृषावादपरायणाः। आन्ध्राः शकाः पुलिन्दाश्च यवनाश्च नराधिपाः॥
en: These sinful kings addicted to falsehood will govern their subjects on principles that are false. The Andhras, the Shakas, the Pulandas, the Yavana kings,

sn: काम्बोजा बाह्निकाः शूरास्तथाऽऽभीरा नरोत्तम। न तदा ब्राह्मणः कश्चित् स्वधर्ममुपजीवति॥
en: The Kambojas, the Balhikas and the Abhiras will then foremost of men, be endued with courage and they will possess the sovereignty of the earth. O descendant of Bharata, at the end of the Kali Yuga such becomes the state of the world. Not a single Brahmana then adheres to the duties of his order.

sn: क्षत्रियाश्चापि वैश्याश्च विकर्मस्था नराधिपा। अल्पायुषः स्वल्पबलाः स्वल्पवीर्यपराक्रमाः॥
en: O king, the Kshatriyas and the Vaishyas also follow practices contrary to those of their own orders. Men become short-lived, weak in strength, energy and prowess.

sn: अल्पसाराल्पदेहाश्च तथा सत्याल्पभाषिणः। बहुशून्या जनपदा मृगव्यालावृता दिशः॥
en: They possess little strength and diminutive bodies; and they hardly become truthful. The country becomes deserts and all directions are filled with beasts and wild animals.

sn: युगान्ते समनुप्राप्ते वृथा च ब्रह्मवादिनः। भोवादिनस्तथा शूद्रा ब्राह्मणाश्चार्यवादिनः॥
en: When the end of the Yuga comes, the uttering of the Vedas become futile. The Shudras address (others) saying “Bho;" while the Brahinanas address (others) saying "Noble Sir."

sn: युगान्ते मनुजव्याघ्र भवन्ति बहुजन्तवः। न तथा घ्राणयुक्ताश्च सर्वगन्धा विशाम्पते॥
en: O foremost of men, at the end of the Yuga animals enormously increase. O rulers of men, perfumes even do not become agreeable to our sense of smell.

sn: रसाश्च मनुजव्याघ्र न तथा स्वादुयोगिनः। बहुप्रजा ह्रस्वदेहाः शीलाचारविवर्जिताः। मुखे भगाः स्त्रियो राजन् भविष्यन्ति युगक्षये॥
en: O foremost of men, the tastes of things do not become so agreeable to our sense of taste as at other times. Women give birth to numerous children who become of diminutive body, destitute of good conduct and good manners. O king at the end of the Yuga women's mouth serves the purpose of intercourse.

sn: अट्टशूला जनपदाः शिवशूलाश्चतुष्पथाः। केशशूलाः स्त्रियो राजन् भविष्यन्ति युगक्षये॥
en: O king, at the end of the Yuga, famine ravages the habitations of men and the highways are infested by women of ill fame. O king, all women become hostile to their husbands and destitute of all modesty.

sn: अल्पक्षीरास्तथा गावो भविष्यन्ति जनाधिप। अल्पपुष्पफलाचापि पादपा बहुवायसाः॥
en: O ruler of men, cows yield little milk; trees are crowded with swarms of crows; they do not produce any fruits and flowers.

sn: ब्रह्मवध्यानुलिप्तानां तथा मिथ्याभिशंसिनाम्। नृपाणां पृथिवीपाल प्रतिगृहणन्ति वै द्विजाः॥
en: O ruler of earth, the Brahmanas, polluted with the sin of killing the twice-born, accept gifts from kings who are addicted to falsehood.

sn: लोभमोहपरीताच मिथ्याधर्मध्वजावृताः। भिक्षार्थं पृथिवीपाल चयूर्यन्ते द्विजैर्दिशः॥
en: Filled with covetousness and ignorance; and bearing the outward symbols of religion, the Brahınanas afflicting the people of the earth rove about for alms.

sn: करभारभयाद् भीता गृहस्थाः परिमोषकाः। मुनिच्छद्माकृतिच्छन्ना वाणिज्यमुपजीविनः॥ मिथ्या च नखरोमाणिधारयन्ति तदा द्विजाः। अर्थलोभान्नरव्याघ्र तथा च ब्रह्मचारिणः॥
en: Men, leading domestic life, being afraid of the weight of taxation, become deceivers; while Brahmanas assuming the disguise of ascetics earn wealth by trade. O foremost of men, many Brahmanas become from their avarice of wealth religious mendicants of the Brahmacharya order.

sn: आश्रमेषु वृथाचाराः पानपा गुरुतल्पगाः। इह लौकिकमीहन्ते मांसशोणितवर्धनम्॥
en: O king, men at such a time behave contrary to the mode of life to which they belong; they become addicted to intoxicating drinks, they become capable of violating even the bed of their preceptors. They are deluded with the desires of this world and they pursue things that only give pleasure ministering to flesh and blood.

sn: बहुपाषण्डसंकीर्णाः परान्नगुणवादिनः। आश्रमा मनुजव्याघ्र भविष्यन्ति युगक्षये॥
en: O foremost of men, at the end of the Yuga the hermitage of ascetics becomes crowded with sinful and insolent wretches who always praise the life of dependence.

sn: यथर्तुवर्षी भगवान् न तथा पाकशासनः। न चापि सर्वबीजानि सम्यग् रोहन्ति भारत॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, the illustrious chastiser of Paka (Indra) never showers rain according to the season. The seeds that are scattered on earth never spring forth.

sn: हिंसाभिरामश्च जनस्तथा सम्पद्यतेऽशुचिः। अधर्मफलमत्यर्थं तदा भवति चानघा॥
en: Unholy both in thought and deed, men take pleasure in envy and malice. O sinless one, the earth becomes full of sin and immorality.

sn: तदा च पृथिवीपाल यो भवेद्धर्मसंयुतः। अल्पायुः स हि मन्तव्यो न हिधर्मोऽस्ति कश्चन।।५२।
en: O ruler of earth, he who becomes virtuous in such periods does not at all live long. The earth becomes devoid of virtue in every shape.

sn: भूयिष्ठं कूटमानैश्च पण्यं विक्रीणते जनाः। वणिजश्च नरव्याघ्र बहुमाया भवन्त्युत॥
en: O foremost of men, traders, becoming full of deceit, sell their goods with false weights and measures.

sn: धर्मिष्ठाः परिहीयन्ते पापीयान् वर्धते जनः। धर्मस्य बलहानिः स्यादधर्मश्च बली तथा॥
en: The virtuous men do not prosper, only the sinful men then exceedingly prosper. Virtue then loses her strength and sin becomes all powerful.

sn: अल्पायुषो दरिद्राश्चधर्मिष्ठा मानवास्तथा। दीर्घायुषः समृद्धाश्च विधर्माणो युगक्षये॥
en: Those that are devoted to virtue then become poor and short-lived. At the end of the Yuga those that are sinful become wealthy and longlived.

sn: नागराणां विहारेषु विधर्माणो युगक्षये। अधर्मिष्ठरुपायैश्च प्रजा व्यवहरन्त्युत॥
en: At the end of the Yuga people behave sinfully even in places of public entertainment, in cities and towns. Men then always seek the accomplishment of their ends by means that are sinful.

sn: संचयेन तथाल्पेन भवन्त्याढ्यमदान्विताः। धनं विश्वासतो न्यस्तं मिथो भूयिष्ठशो नराः॥ हर्तु व्यवसिता राजन् पापाचारसमन्विताः। नैतदस्तीति मनुजा वर्तन्ते निरपत्रपाः॥
en: Having earned fortunes that are really small, men become intoxicated with the pride of wealth. O king, many men at the end of Yuga try to rob the wealth that has been secretly deposited with them by others out of trust. Full of sinful practices, they shamelessly declare, "they have nothing in deposit.”

sn: पुरुषादानि सत्त्वानि पक्षिणोऽथ मृगास्तथा। नगराणां विहारेषु चैत्येष्वपि च शेरते॥
en: Beast of prey and other animals and birds are seen to lie down in places of public entertainments, in cities and towns, as well as in sacred temples.

sn: सप्तवर्षाष्टवर्षाश्च स्त्रियो गर्भधरा नृप। दशद्वादशवर्षाणां पुंसां पुत्रः प्रजायते॥
en: O king, girls of seven and eight years of age, give birth to children and boys of ten or twelve years beget offspring.

sn: भवन्ति षोडशे वर्षे नराः पलितिनस्तथा। आयुःक्षयो मनुष्याणां क्षिप्रमेव प्रपद्यते॥
en: In their sixteenth year men are over-taken by decripitude. And a man's life is soon run out.

sn: क्षीणायुषो महाराज तरुणो वृद्धशीलिनः। तरुणानां च यच्छील तद् वृद्धेषु प्रजायते॥
en: O great king, when men become so shortlived, mere youths act like old men, while all that is seen in the youths is seen in old men.

sn: विपरीतास्तदा नार्यो वञ्चयित्वार्हतः पतीन्। व्युच्चरन्त्यपि दुःशीला दासैः पशुभिरेव च॥
en: Women, prone to impropriety of conduct and distinguished by bad manners, deceive even the best of husbands and forget themselves with servants and slaves, even with animals,

sn: वीरपल्यस्तथा नार्यः संश्रयन्ति नरान् नृप। भर्तारमपि जीवन्तमन्यान् व्यभिचरन्त्युत॥
en: O king, even women who are the wives of good men forget themselves with others even at the life time of their husbands.

sn: तस्मिन् युगसलरान्ते सम्प्राप्ते चायुषः क्षये। अनावृष्टिर्महाराज जायते बहुवार्षिकी॥
en: O king, at the end of those thousands of years and when men become so short-lived, a draught takes place which extends for many years.

sn: ततस्तान्यल्पसारणि सत्त्वानि क्षुधितानि वै। प्रलयं यान्ति भूयिष्ठं पृथिव्यां पृथिवीपते॥
en: O lord of earth, then men and (other) creatures, possessing but little strength and vitality, die of starvation by thousands.

sn: ततो दिनकरैर्दीप्तैः सप्तभिर्मनुजाधिप। पीयते सलिलं सर्वं समुद्रेषु सरित्सु च॥
en: O ruler of men, seven blazing suns then appear in the sky and drink up all the waters of the earth that are in the rivers and in the scas.

sn: यच्च काष्ठं तृणं चापि शुष्कं चार्दै च भारत। सर्वं तद् भस्मसाद् भूतं दृश्यते भरतर्षभ॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, O best of the Bharata race, then everything of the nature of wood and grass, whether dry or wet, is burnt down and reduced to ashes.

sn: ततः संवर्तको वह्निर्वायुना सह भारत। लोकमाविशते पूर्वमादित्यैरुपशोषितम्॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, then the fire (called) Samvartaka helped by the wind appears on earth which has been already burnt (to ashes) by the seven suns.

sn: ततः स पृथिवीं भित्त्वा प्रविश्य च रसातलम्। देवदानवयक्षाणां भयं जनयते महत्॥
en: Thereupon it (fire), penetrating the earth and reaching the nether region, creates great terror to the celestials, the Danavas and the Rakshasas.

sn: निर्दहन् नागलोकं च यच्च किञ्चित् क्षिताविह। अधस्तात् पृथिवीपाल सर्वं नाशयते क्षणात्॥
en: O ruler of earth, burning down the nether region and also everything on this earth, that fire then destroys all things in a moment.

sn: ततो योजनविंशानां साणि शतानि च। निर्दहत्यशिवो वायुः स च संवर्तकोऽनलः॥
en: That Samvartaka fire, helped by that inauspicious wind, consume this world which extends for hundreds of thousands of yojanas.

sn: सदेवासुरगन्धर्वं सयक्षोरगराक्षसम्। ततो दहति दीप्तः स सर्वमेव जगद् विभुः॥
en: That lord of all things, that fire, blazing forth in great effulgence, burns down this universe with the celestials, the Asuras, the Gandharvas, the Yakshas, the Nagas and the Rakshasas.

sn: ततो गजकुलप्रख्यास्तडिन्मालाविभूषिताः। उत्तिष्ठन्ति महामेधा नभस्यद्भुतदर्शनाः॥
en: Then there rise in the sky great masses of clouds resembling herds of elephants all adorned with garlands of lightning beautiful to look at.

sn: केचिन्नीलोत्पलश्यामाः केचित् कुमुदसंनिभाः। केचित् किञ्जल्कसंकाशाः केचित् पीताः पयोधराः॥७५
en: Some of them are of the colour of blue lotus, some like lilies, some like the colour of the filaments of the lotus and some are red.

sn: केचिद्धारिद्रसंकाशा: कारण्डवनिभास्तथा। केचित् कमलपत्राभाः केचिद्धिगुलसप्रभा:॥
en: Some are yellow as turmeric, some are of the colour of a crow's egg, some are like that of the lotus leaves and some red as Vermilion.

sn: केचित् पुरवराकाराः केचिद् गजकुलोपमाः। केचिदञ्जनसंकाशाः केचिन्मकरसंनिभाः॥
en: Some in shape are like palatial cities, some resemble herds of elephants, some are in the form of lizards and some of crocodiles and sharks.

sn: विद्युन्मालापिनद्धाङ्गाः समुत्तिष्ठन्ति वै घनाः। घोररूपा महाराज घोरस्वननिनादिताः। ततो जलधराः सर्वे व्याप्नुवन्ति नभस्तलम्॥
en: O great king, the clouds adorned with garlands of lightning that gather in the sky on that occasion, are terrible to behold and they fearfully roar. Those masses of clouds charged with rain soon cover the whole of the firmament.

sn: तैरियं पृथिवीं सर्वा सपर्वतवनाकरा। आपूर्यते महाराज सलिलौघपरिप्लुता॥
en: O great king, those masses of clouds then flood with water the whole earth with her mountains, forests and mines.

sn: ततस्ते जलदा घोरा राविणः पुरुषर्षभ। सर्वत: प्लावयन्त्याशु चोदिताः परमेष्ठिना॥
en: O foremost of men, then commanded by Parameshthi (Brahma) those clouds roaring fearfully soon flood all places.

sn: वर्षमाणा महत् तोयं पूरयन्तो वसुंधराम्। सुघोरमशिवं रौद्रं नाशयन्ति च पावकम्॥
en: Pouring a great quantity of water and filling the whole earth (with it), they extinguish that fearful, terrible and in auspicious fire.

sn: ततो द्वादशवर्षाणि पयोदास्त उपप्लवे। धाराभिः पूरयन्तो वै चोद्यमाना महात्मना।1८२॥
en: Commanded by the supreme lord, they shower continually for twelve years and fill the earth with their downpour.

sn: ततः समुद्रः स्वां वेलामतिक्रामति भारत। पर्वताश्च विदीर्यन्ते मही चाप्सु निमज्जति॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, the ocean then over-floods it bounds; the mountains fall down in fragments and the earth sinks under the increasing flood.

sn: सर्वतः सहसा भ्रान्तास्ते पयोदा नभस्तलम्। संवेष्टयित्वा नश्यन्ति वायुवेगपराहताः॥
en: Then suddenly moved by the wind, those cloud go over the entire expanse of the sky and then disappear from the view.

sn: ततस्तं मारुतं घोरं स्वयम्भूर्मनुजाधिप। आदिः पद्मालयो देवः पीत्वा स्वपिति भारत॥
en: O ruler of men, O descendant of Bharata, the Self Create, lord, the first cause, the deity who so abode is the lotus (Lakshmi) drinks up these fearful winds and goes then to sleep.

sn: तस्मिन्नेकार्णवे घोरे नष्टे स्थावरजङ्गमे। नष्टे देवासुरगणे यक्षराक्षसवर्जिते॥
en: Then when earth becomes one great ocean, when all mobile and immobile creatures have been destroyed, when the celestials and the Asuras are annihilated, when the Yakshas and the Rakshasas are no more,

sn: निर्मनुष्ये महीपाल निःश्वापदमहीरुहे। अनन्तरिक्षे लोकेऽस्मिन् भ्रमाम्येकोऽहमाहतः॥
en: O ruler of earth, when there is no human being, when trees and wild animals have disappeared, when the firmament itself has ceased to exist, I alone in affliction rove about.

sn: एकार्णवे जले घोरे विचरन् पार्थिवोत्तम। अपश्यन् सर्वभूतानि वैक्लव्यमगमं ततः॥
en: O foremost of kings, once thus roving over that one great ocean, my heart was filled with great affliction on not seeing any creature.

sn: ततः सुदीर्घ गत्वाहं प्लवमानो नराधिप। श्रान्तः क्वचिन शरणं लभाम्यहमतन्द्रितः॥
en: O ruler of men, then thus roving about for a long time, I became fatigued; but I did not get any resting place.

sn: ततः कदाचित् पश्यामि तस्मिन् सलिलसंचये। न्यग्रोधं सुमहान्तं वै विशालं पृथिवीपते॥
en: O ruler of earth, thereupon one day I saw in that great expanse of water a great and wide extending banian tree.

sn: शाखायां तस्य वृक्षस्य विस्तीर्णायां नराधिप। पर्यङ्के पृथिवीपाल दिव्यास्तरणसंस्तुते॥
en: O great king, O descendant of Bharata, I then saw seated on a cot overlaid with a celestials bed and attached to one of the farextending boughs of that banian trce.

sn: उपविष्टं महाराज पद्मेन्दुसदृशाननम्। फुल्लपद्मविशालाक्षं बालं पश्यामि भारत॥
en: A boy with a face as beautiful as the lotus or the moon, O ruler of men, with eyes as large as the petals of full blown lotuses.

sn: ततो मे पृथिवीपाल विस्मयः सुमहानभूत्। कथं त्वयं शिशुः शेते लोके नाशमुपागते॥
en: O ruler of earth, thereupon I was filled with great astonishment and (I asked myself) "how can this child alone lie here when all the world is destroyed.”

sn: तपसा चिन्तयंश्चापि तं शिशुं नोपलक्षये। भूतं भव्यं भविष्यं च जानन्नपि नराधिप॥
en: O ruler of men, though I knew the Present, the Past and the Future and though I took the help of ascetic meditation, I could not learn anything about the boy.

sn: अतसीपुष्पवर्णाभः श्रीवत्सकृतभूषणः। साक्षाल्लक्ष्म्या इवावासः स तदा प्रतिभाति मे॥
en: Possessing the lustre of the Atasi flower and adorned with the mark of Srivatsa, he appeared to me as if he were the abode of Lakshmi.

sn: ततो मामब्रवीद् बालः स पद्यनिभलोचनः। श्रीवत्सधारी द्युतिमान् वाक्यं श्रुतिसुखावहम्॥
en: That lotus-eyed and greatly effulgent boy with the mark of Srivatsa then thus spoke to me in words highly pleasant to the ear.

sn: जानामि त्वां परिश्रान्तं ततो विश्रामकाक्षिणम्। मार्कण्डेय इहास्स्व त्वं यावदिच्छसि भार्गव॥
en: "O child, I know you are fatigued and you are eager for rest. O descendant of Bhrigu, O Markandeya, rest here as long as you like.

sn: अभ्यन्तरं शरीरे मे प्रविश्य मुनिसत्तम। आस्स्व भो विहितो वासः प्रसादस्ते कृतो मया॥
en: foremost of Rishis, enter into my body and rest there. That is the place assigned to you by me. I am gratified with you."

sn: ततो बालेन तेनैवमुक्तस्यासीत् तदा मम। निर्वेदो जीविते दीर्घ मनुष्यत्वे च भारत॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, thus addressed by that boy, a sense of total disregard possessed me in respect both of my long life and state of manhood.

sn: ततो बालेन तेनास्यं सहसा विवृतं कृतम्। तस्याहमवशो वक्त्रे दैवयोगात् प्रवेशितः॥
en: Then suddenly that boy opened his mouth and as fate would have it, I having lost all power of locomotion, entered his mouth.

sn: ततः प्रविष्टस्तत्कुक्षिं सहसा मनुजाधिप। सराष्ट्रनगराकीर्णां कृत्स्नां पश्यामि मेदिनीम्॥
en: O ruler of men, thus suddenly entering his stomach, I beheld the whole earth (there within it) with all its cities and kingdoms.

sn: गङ्गां शतदुं सीतां च यमुनामथ कौशिकाम्। चर्मण्वती वेत्रवती चन्द्रभागां सरस्वतीम्॥ सिन्धुं चैव विपाशां च नदी गोदावरीमपि। वस्वोकसारां नलिनी नर्मदां चैव भारत॥ नदी तानां च वेणां च पुण्यतोयां शुभावहाम्। सुवेणां कृष्णवेणां च इरामां च महानदीम्॥ वितस्तां च महाराज कावेरी च महानदीम्। शोणं च पुरुषव्याघ्र विशल्यां किम्पुनामपि॥ एताश्चान्याश्च नद्योऽहं पृथिव्यां या नरोत्तम। परिक्रामन् प्रपश्यामि तस्य कुक्षौ महात्मनः॥
en: O foremost of men when wandering about in his stomach, I saw within it, the Ganga, the Satadru, the Sita, the Yamuna, the Kausaku, the Charmanvati, the Vetravati, the Chandrabhaga, the Sarasvati, the Sindhu, the Vipasa, the Godavari, the Vasvokasara, the Nalini, the Narmada, the Tamra, the Vena of fearful currents and sacred waters, the Suvena, the Krishnavena, the Irama, the Mahanadi, the Vitasta, that large river Kaveri, the Vishalya, the Kimpuna and many others.

sn: ततः समुद्रं पश्यामि यादोगणनिषेवितम्। रत्नाकरममित्रघ्न पयसो निधिमुत्तमम्॥
en: O chastiser of foes, I saw there also the ocean inhabited by alligators and sharks, that mine of gems, that excellent abode of waters.

sn: तत्र पश्यामि गगनं चन्द्रसूर्यविराजितम्। जाज्वल्यमानं तेजोभिः पावकार्कसमप्रभम्॥
en: I saw there also the sky adorned with the sun and the moon, blazing in great effulgence and possessing the lustre of the sun.

sn: पश्यामि च महीं राजन् काननैरुपशोभिताम्। यजन्ते हि तदा राजन् ब्राह्मणा बहुभिर्मखैः। :॥
en: O king, I saw there also the earth beautiful with the forests and woods. O king, (I also saw) many Brahmanas engaged in many sacrifices,

sn: क्षत्रियाश्च प्रवर्तन्ते सर्ववर्णानुरंजनैः। वैश्याः कृषि यथान्यायं कारयन्ति नराधिप॥ शुश्रूषायां च निरता द्विजानां वृषलास्तदा। ततः परिपतन् राजंस्तस्य कुक्षौ महात्मनः॥
en: Many Kshatriyas engaged in doing good to all the other orders, many Vaishyas engaged in the pursuits of agriculture and many Shudras engaged in serving the Brahmanas. Then wandering in the stomach of that high-souled being,

sn: हिमवन्तं च पश्यामि हेमकूटं च पर्वतम्। निषधं चापि पश्यामि श्वेतं च रजतान्वितम्॥
en: I saw the mountains of Himavat and Hemakuta. I also saw the Nishada and Shveta abounding in silver.

sn: पश्यामि च महीपाल पर्वतं गन्धमादनम्। मन्दर मनुजव्याघ्र नीलं चापि महागिरिम्॥
en: O ruler of earth, I saw also the mountain Gandhamadana and foremost of men, I also saw Mandara and the great mountain Nila.

sn: पश्यामि च महाराज मेरुं कनकपर्वतम्। महेन्द्रं चैव पश्यामि विन्ध्यं च गिरिमुत्तमम्॥
en: O great king, I saw also the golden mountain Meru, also Mahendra and also that excellent mountain Vindhya.

sn: मलयं चापि पश्यामि पारियात्रं च पर्वतम्। एते चान्ये च बहवो यावन्तः पृथिवीधराः॥
en: I also saw there the mountains of Malaya and Paripatra. These and many mountains.

sn: तस्योदरे मया दृष्टाः सर्वे रत्नविभूषिताः। सिंहान् व्याघ्रान् वराहांश्च पश्यामि मनुजाधिप॥
en: Were seen by me in his stomach. They were all decked with gems and jewels. O ruler of men, I saw also there the lions, the tigers and the bears.

sn: पृथिव्यां यानि चान्यानि सत्त्वानि जगतीपते। तानि सर्वाण्यहं तत्र पश्यन् पर्यचरं तदा॥
en: O ruler of the earth, all the other creatures that are on earth were all seen by me in his stomach as I was wandering about there.

sn: कुक्षौ तस्य नरव्याघ्र प्रविष्टः संचरन् दिशः। शक्रादींश्चापि पश्यामि कृत्स्नान् देवगणानहम्॥
en: O foremost of men, having entered his stomach, as I wandered about, I saw the whole race of the celestials, Indra and others,

sn: साध्यान् रुद्रांस्तथाऽऽदित्यान् गुह्यकान् पितरस्तदा। सर्पान् नागान् सुपर्णाश्च वसूनप्यश्विनावपि॥
en: The Saddhya, the Rudra, the Adityas, the Guhyakas, the Pitris, the Nagas, the birds, the Vasus, the Asmas,

sn: गन्धर्वाप्सरसो यक्षानृषींश्चैव महीपते। दैत्यदानवसङ्घांश्च नागांश्च मनुजाधिप॥
en: The Gandharvas, the Rishis, the Daityas, the Danavas, the Nagas,

sn: सिंहिकातनयांश्चापि ये चान्ये सुरशत्रवः। यच्च किंचिन्मया लोके दृष्टं स्थावरजङ्गमम्॥
en: The son of Singhikas and all other enemies of the celestials. Whatever mobile and immobile things I saw on earth.

sn: सर्वं पश्याम्यहं राजस्तस्य कुक्षौ महात्मनः। चरमाणः फलाहारः कृत्स्नं जगदिदं विभो॥ अन्तःशरीरे तस्याहं वर्षाणामधिकं शतम्। न च पश्यामि तस्याहं देहस्यान्तं कदाचन॥
en: O king, I saw them all in the stomach of that high-souled one. O lord, living on fruits, wandering over the entire universe which was there, I lived within his body for many hundred years. But I did not see the end of his body.

sn: सततधावमानश्च चिन्तयानो विशाम्पते। आसदयामि नैवान्तं तस्य राजन् महात्मनः॥
en: O king, though I continuously roved about within his body in great anxiety, I could not find the limit of the body of that high-souled one.

sn: ततस्तमेव शरणं गतोऽस्मि विधिवत् तदा। वरेण्यं वरदं देवं मनसा कर्मणैव च॥
en: Then in both thought and deed I sought the protection of that boon-giving and preeminently great deity and duly acknowledged his superiority.

sn: ततोऽहं सहसा राजन् वायुवेगेन निःसृतः। महात्मनो मुखात् तस्य विवृतात् पुरुषोत्तम॥
en: O king, O foremost of men, then I suddenly came out of the open mouth of that high-souled one by means of a great gust of wind.

sn: ततस्तस्यैव शाखायां न्यग्रोधस्य विशाम्पते। आस्ते मनुजशार्दूल कृत्स्नमादाय वै जगत्॥
en: O king, foremost of men, I then saw seated on the branch of the banian tree that immeasurably effulgent being in the form of a boy, with the mark of Srivatsa, who had swallowed up the universe.

sn: तेनैव बालवेषेण श्रीवत्सकृतलक्षणम्। आसीनं तं नरव्याघ्र पश्याम्यमिततेजसम्॥
en: O foremost of men, that greatly effulgent boy with the mark of Srivatsa and with yellow robes on, being gratified with me smilingly spoke to me,

sn: ततो मामब्रवीद् बाल: स प्रीतः प्रहसन्निव। श्रीवत्सधारी द्युतिमान् पीतवासा महाद्युतिः॥ अपीदानीं शरीरेऽस्मिन् मामके मुनिसत्तम। उषितस्त्वं सुविश्रान्तो मार्कण्डेय ब्रवीहिमे॥
en: "O foremost of Rishis, O Markandeya, you were living for sometime within my body, I shall however speak to you."

sn: मुहूर्तादथ मे दृष्टिः प्रादुर्भूता पुनर्नवा। यया निर्मुक्तमात्मानमपश्यं लब्धचेतसम्॥
en: As he said to me, within that very moment, I acquired as if new sight; in consequence of which I saw myself possessed of true knowledge and freed from the illusions of the world.

sn: तस्य ताम्रतलौ तात चरणौ सुप्रतिष्ठितौ। सुजातौ मृदुरक्ताभिरङ्गुलीभिर्विराजितौ॥ प्रयत्लेन मया मूर्धा गृहीत्वा ह्यभिवन्दितौ। दृष्ट्वा परिमितं तस्य प्रभावममितौजसः॥ विनयेनाञ्जलिं कृत्वा प्रयत्नेनोपगम्य ह। दृष्टो मया स भूतात्मा देवः कमललोचनः॥ तमहं प्राञ्जलिर्भूत्वा नमस्कृत्येदमब्रुवम्। ज्ञातुमिच्छामि देव त्वां मायां चैतां तवोत्तमाम्॥
en: O child, having seen the inexhaustible prowess of that immeasurably effulgent being, I worshipped his revered and well-shaped feet with soles as bright as the burnished copper and with toes of mild red colour. Having placed them reverentially on my head and joined my hands in humility and having gone to him with all reverence. I saw that Divine Being who is the soul of all things and whose cyes are like the petals vf loius. Ilaving thus bowed to him with joined hands I spoke to him thus, "O God, I desire to know you and also your this wonderful illusion.

sn: आस्येनानुप्रविष्टोऽहं शरीरे भगवंस्तव। दृष्टवानखिलान् सर्वान् समस्तान् जठरे हि ते॥
en: O excellent one, having entered into your body through your mouth, I have seen the entire universe in your stomach.

sn: तव देव शरीरस्था देवदानवराक्षसाः। यक्षगन्धर्वनागाश्च जगत् स्थावरजङ्गमम्॥
en: O god, the celestials, the Danavas, the Rakshasas, the Yakshsas, the Gandharvas, the Nagas, may the whole universe mobile immobile are all within your body.

sn: त्वत्प्रसादाच्च मे देव स्मृतिर्न परिहीयते। दुतमन्तःशरीरे ते सततं परिवर्तिनः॥
en: Though I continuously ran over your body, yet through your grace, O god, my memory did not fail.

sn: निर्गतोऽहमकामस्तु इच्छया ते महाप्रभो। इच्छामि पुण्डरीकाक्ष ज्ञातुं त्वाहमनिन्दितम्॥
en: O great lord, I have come out through your desire and not mine. O lotus-eyed one, I desire to know you who are faultless.

sn: इह भूत्वा शिशुः साक्षात् किं भवानवतिष्ठते। पीत्वा जगदिदं सर्वमेतदाख्यातुमर्हसि॥
en: Why do you stay here becoming a boy and swallowing up the universe? You should explain to me all this.

sn: किमर्थं च जगत् सर्वं शरीरस्थं तवानघ। कियन्तं च त्वया कालमिह स्थेयमरिदम॥
en: O sinless one, O chastiser of foes, why does the universe is within your body? How long will you stay here?

sn: त्वत्तः एतदिच्छामि देवेश श्रोतुं ब्राह्मणकाम्यया। कमलपत्राक्ष विस्तरेण यथातथम्॥
en: O lord of celestials, I desire to hear all this in detail and as they all happened. O lotus-eyed one, it is not improper for a Brahmana to desire to know it.

sn: महद्ध्येतदचिन्त्यं च यदहं दृष्टवान् प्रभो। इत्युक्तः स मया श्रीमान् देवदेवो महाद्युतिः। सान्त्वयन् मामिदं वाक्यमुवाच वदतां वरः॥
en: lord, what I have seen is wonderful and inconceivable.” Having been thus addressed by me, that highly effulgent and blessed god of gods, that foremost of all speakers, duly consoling me, thus spoke to me.

sn: देव उवाच कामं देवा अपि न मां विप्र जानन्ति तत्त्वतः। त्वत्प्रीत्या तु प्रवक्ष्यामि यथेदं विसृजाम्यहम्॥
en: The Deity said: O Brahmana, even the celestials do not know me truly. But as I am pleased with you, I shall tell you how I created the universe.

sn: पितृभक्तोऽसि विप्रर्षे मां चैव शरणं गतः। ततो दृष्टोऽस्मि ते साक्षाद् ब्रह्मचर्यं च ते महत्॥
en: O Brahmana Rishi, you have filial piety and you have also sought my protection; you have also seen me with your eyes and your Brahmacharya is also great.

sn: अपां नारा इति पुरा संज्ञाकर्म कृतं मया। तेन नारायणोऽप्युक्तो मम तत् त्वयनं सदा॥
en: In days of yore, I called the waters by the name of Nara and because the waters have ever been my Ayana (abode), I am called Narayana.

sn: अहं नारायणो नाम प्रभवः शाश्वतोऽव्ययः। विधाता सर्वभूतानां संहर्ता च द्विजोत्तम॥
en: O foremost of Brahmana, I am Narayana, the source of all things, the eternal, the unchangeable; I am the creator of all things and also the destroyer of all.

sn: अहं विष्णोरहं ब्रह्मा शक्रश्चाहं सुराधिपः। अहं वैश्रवणो राज यमः प्रेताधिपस्तथा॥
en: I am Vishnu, I am Brahma, I am Indra, the lord of the celestials. I am king Vaisravana (Kubera), I am Yama, the king of the deceased spirits.

sn: अहं शिवश्च सोमश्च कश्यपोऽथ प्रजापतिः। अहंधाता विधाता च यज्ञश्चाहं द्विजोत्तम॥
en: O foremost of Brahmanas, I am Shiva, I am Soma, I am Kashyapa, I am the lord of all treated things; I am Dhata, Vidhata, I am the sacrifice embodied.

sn: अग्निरास्यं क्षितिः पादौ चन्द्रादित्यौ च लोचने। द्यौर्मूर्धा खं दिशः श्रोत्रे तथाऽप: स्वेदसम्भवाः॥
en: Fire is my mouth, the earth my feet, the sun and the moon are my eyes, the heaven is my head, the sky and the directions are my ears. And the waters are my sweats (of the body).

sn: सदिशं च नभः कायो वायुमनसि मे स्थितः। मया क्रतुशतैरिष्टं बहुभिः स्वाप्तदक्षिणैः॥
en: Space with the cardinal points are my body and the air is my mind. I have performed many hundreds of sacrifices in which Dakshina were in abundance.

sn: यजन्ते वेदविदुषो मां देवयजने स्थितम्। पृथिव्यां क्षत्रियेन्द्राश्च पार्थिवाः स्वर्गकाक्षिणः॥
en: I am ever present in the sacrifices of the celestials; those that know the Vedas offer sacrifices to On earth those chief Kshatriyas, those kings who desire to obtain heaven.

sn: यजन्ते मां तथा वैश्याः स्वर्गलोकजिगीषया। चतु:समुद्रपर्यन्तां मेरुमन्दरभूषणाम्॥ शेषो भूत्वाहमेवैतांधारयामि वसुन्धराम। वाराहं रूपमास्थाय मयेयं जगती पुरा॥ मज्जामाना जले विप्र वीर्येणासीत् समुद्धृता। अग्निश्च वडवावक्त्रो भूत्वाहं द्विजसत्तम॥
en: And those Vaishyas who also desire to attain to those blessed region, all worship me. Becoming Shesha it is I who support (on my head) this earth bounded by the four seas and decked by Meru and Mandara. Assuming the me. form of the boar in the days of yore I raised up this universe sunk in water. foremost of Brahmans, becoming the fire that issues forth from the Equine mouth.

sn: पिबाम्यपः सदा विद्वंस्ताश्चैवं विसृजाम्यहम्। ब्रह्म वक्त्रं भुजौ क्षत्रमूरू मे संस्थिता विशः॥
en: It is I who drink up the water and create them again. From my month Brahmanas, from my arms the Kshatriyas, from my thighs the Vaishyas,

sn: पादौ शूद्रा भवन्तीमे विक्रमेण क्रमेण च। ऋग्वेदः सामवेदश्च यजुर्वेदोऽप्यथर्वणः॥
en: From my feet the Shudras, one after the other, sprang up through my great energy. The Rig, the Sama, the Yaju and the Atharva Vedas,

sn: मत्तः प्रादुर्भवन्त्येते मामेव प्रविशन्ति च। यतयः शान्तिपरमा यतात्मानो बुभुत्सवः॥ कामक्रोधद्वेषमुक्ता नि:संगा वीतकल्मघाः। सत्त्वस्था निरहङ्कारा नित्यमध्यात्मकोविदाः॥ मामेव सततं विप्राश्चिन्तयन्त उपासते। अहं संवर्तको वह्निरहं संवर्तकोऽनलः॥
en: Issued forth from me and disappear also in me. The Brahmanas, devoted to asceticism, those that value peace as the highest attribute, those that have their souls under complete control, those that are desirous of knowledge, those that are freed from lust and wrath and envy, those that are unweded to earthly things, those that have their sins completely destroyed, those that possess gentleness and virtue, those that are free from pride, those that have a full knowledge of the soul-all these worship me with profound meditation. I am the fire called Samvartaka, I am the wind called Samvartaka.

sn: अहं संवर्तकः सूर्यस्त्वहं संवर्तकोऽनिलः। तारारूपाणि दृश्यन्ते यान्येतानि नभस्तले॥
en: I am the Samvartaka sun, I am the Samvartaka fire. Those that are seen in the skies in the shape of stars,

sn: मम वै रोमकूपाणि विद्धि त्वं द्विजसत्तम। रत्नाकरा: समुद्राश्च सर्व एव चतुर्दिशम्॥
en: O foremost of Brahmanas, know them to be the pores of my skin. The oceans, those mines of gems and the four directions.

sn: वसनं शयनं चैव विलयं चैव विद्धि मे। मयैव सुविभक्तास्ते देवकार्यार्थसिद्धये॥
en: Know, they are my robes, my bed, my abode. They have been spread by me to accomplish the purposes of the celestials.

sn: काम क्रोधं च हर्षं च भयं मोहं तथैव च। ममैव विद्धि रोमाणि सर्वाण्येतानि सत्तम॥
en: O excellent man, know that desire, anger, joy, fear and ignorance are all different forms of myself.

sn: प्राप्नुवन्ति नरा विप्र यत् कृत्वा कर्म शोभनम्। सत्यं दानं तपश्चोग्रमहिंसा चैव जन्तुषु॥ मद्विधानेन विहिता मम देहविहारिणः। मयाऽऽविर्भूतविज्ञाना विचेष्टन्ते न कामतः॥
en: O Brahmana, whatever is obtained by men by the practice of truth, charity, asceticism, peace, harmlessness towards all creatures and other such good deeds is obtained through my arrangements. Led by my laws, men rove about within my body, their senses being always overwhelmed by me. They do not move according to their will, they are moved by me,

sn: सम्यग् वेदमधीयाना यजन्ते विविधैर्मखैः। शान्तात्मानो जितक्रोधाः प्राप्नुवन्ति द्विजातयः॥ प्राप्तुं न शक्यो यो विद्वन् नरैर्दुष्कृतकर्मभिः। लोभाभिभूतैः कृपणेनार्यैरकृतात्मभिः॥ तं मां महाफलं विद्धि नराणां भावितात्मनाम्। सुदुष्प्रापं विमूढानां मार्ग योगैर्निषेवितम्॥
en: The Brahmanas, that have thoroughly studied the Vedas, that have obtained tranquility in their souls and that have subdued their anger, obtain a high reward by performing many sacrifices. But such reward is not obtained by men who are wicked in their acts, who are overwhelmed with covetousness, who are mean and disputable, who have their souls unblessed and impure. Therefore, O Brahmana, know that this reward which is obtained by only self-controlled men and not obtained by ignorant and foolish men-this which is attainable by asceticism alone, produces high merits.

sn: यदा यदा चधर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति सत्तम। अभ्युत्थानमधर्मस्य तदाऽऽत्मानं सृजाम्यहम्॥
en: O excellent man, at those times when virtue and morality decrease in the world) and sin and immorality increase, I create myself.

sn: दैत्या हिंसानुरक्ताश्च अवध्याः सुरसत्तमैः। राक्षसाश्चापि लोकेऽस्मिन् यदोत्पत्स्यन्ति दारुणाः॥ तदाहं सम्प्रसूयामि गृहेषु शुभकर्मणाम्। प्रविष्टो मानुषं देहं सर्वं प्रशमयाम्यहम्॥
en: When fearful and vicious-minded Daityas and Rakshasas, that are incapable of being killed by even the foremost of the celestials, are born on earth, I then take my birth in the families of virtuous men. And assuming a human form, 1 restore peace by destroying all evils.

sn: सृष्ट्वा देवमनुष्यांस्तु गन्धर्वोरगराक्षसान्। स्थावराणि च भूतानि संहराम्यात्ममायया॥
en: By my own Maya I create the celestials, the men, the Gandharvas, the Rakshasas and all the mobile and immobile things. And I again destroy them all (when the time comes).

sn: कर्मकाले पुनर्देहमविचिन्त्यं सृजाम्यहम्। आविश्य मानुषं देहं मर्यादाबन्धकारणात्॥
en: For the preservation of virtue and morality I assume a human form and when the times come I assumes form that are inconceivable.

sn: श्वेतः कृतयुगे वर्णः पीतस्त्रेतायुगे मम। रक्तो द्वापमासाद्य कृष्णः कलियुगे तथा॥
en: In the Satya Yuga I become white, in the Treta Yuga I become yellow, in the Dvapara I become red and in the Kali Yuga I become black.

sn: त्रयो भागा ह्यधर्मस्य तस्मिन् काले भवन्ति च। अकाले च समाप्ते कालो भूत्वातिदारुणः॥ त्रैलोक्यं नाशयाम्येकः कृत्स्नं स्थावरजङ्गमम्। अहं त्रिवा विश्वात्मा सर्वलोकसुखावहः॥
en: In that Kali Yuga, the virtue remains only three fourths. When the end of Kali Yuga comes, I assume the fearful form of death and destroy all the three worlds with all their mobile and immobile creatures. I then cover the universe with three steps. I am the soul of the world, I am the source of all happiness.

sn: आविर्भूः सर्वगोऽनन्तो हृषीकेश उरुक्रमः। कालचक्रं नयाम्येको ब्रह्मन्नहमरूपकम्॥
en: I am the humbler of all pride, I am omnipresent, I am infinite. I am the lord of the senses, I am great in power. O Brahmana, I alone set the wheel of the Time in motion. I am formless.

sn: शमनं सर्वभूतानां सर्वलोककृतोद्यमम्। एवं प्रणिहितः सम्यङ् ममात्मा मुनिसत्तम। सर्वभूतेषु विप्रेन्द्र न च मां वेत्ति कश्चन॥
en: O foremost of Rishis, I am the destroyer of all creatures and I am also the cause of all efforts of all creatures. My soul completely pervades all creatures. O chief of Brahmanas, none knows me.

sn: सर्वलोके च मां भक्ताः पूजयन्ति च सर्वशः। यच्च किंचित्त्वया प्राप्तं मयि क्लेशात्मकं द्विज॥
en: It is I whom the pious and the devoted worship in all the worlds. O Brahmana, whatever pains you have felt within my stomach.

sn: सुखोदयाय तत् सर्वं श्रेयसे च तवानघ। यच्च किंचित् त्वया लोके दृष्टं स्थावरजङ्गमम्॥
en: O sinless one, know all that was for your happiness and good fortune. Whatever worlds with their mobile and immobile beings you have seen (within my stomach).

sn: विहितः सर्वथैवासौ ममात्मा भूतभावनः। अर्धं मम शरीरस्य सर्वलोक पितामहः॥
en: Everything has been ordained by my soul which is the source of all existence. The Grandsire of all the worlds is half of my body.

sn: अहं नारायणो नाम शङ्खचक्रगदाधरः। यावद्युगानां विप्रचे सहपरिवर्तनात्॥
en: I am named Narayana, wielding the conch, the discus and the mace. O Brahmana Rishi, for a period of thousand times of the four। Yugas,

sn: तावत् स्वपिमि विश्वात्मा सर्वभूतानि मोहयन्। एवं सर्वमहं कालमिहास्से मुनिसत्तम॥
en: I, who am the soul of the universe sleep, overwhelming all creatures in unconsciousness, O foremost of Rishis, then do I stay here for everlasting time,

sn: अशिशुः शिशुरूपेण यावद्ब्रह्मा न बुध्यते। मया च दत्तो विप्रावय वरस्ते ब्रह्मरूपिणा॥
en: O foremost of Brahmanas, in the form of a boy, though I am old, stay here until Brahmana wakes up. I who am Brahma have given you boons.

sn: असकृत् परितुष्टेन विप्रर्षिगणपूजिता सर्वमेकार्णवं दृष्ट्वा नष्टं स्थावरजङ्गमम्॥
en: I am gratified with you, O the adored of the Brahmana Rishis. Seeing one vast expanse of water and seeing that all mobile and immobile creatures are destroyed.

sn: विक्लवोऽसि मया ज्ञातस्ततस्ते दर्शितं जगत्। अभ्यन्तरं शरीरस्य प्रविष्टोऽसि यदा मम॥
en: You were afflicted with arrow. I knew this and it is for this reason I showed the universe when you entered within my body.

sn: दृष्ट्वा लोकं समस्तं च विस्मितो नावबुध्यसे। ततोऽसि वक्त्राद् विप्रर्षे द्रुतं निःसारितो मया॥
en: You became astonished and bewildered by seeing the entire universe (with in my stomach). O Brahmana Rishi, therefore you were soon brought out by me. I have spoken to you about that Soul which is inconceivable even to the celestials and the Asuras. As long as that great ascetic, the holy Brahma, does not awake,

sn: आख्यातस्ते मया चात्मा दुर्जेयो हि सुरासुरैः॥ यावत् स भगवान् ब्रह्मा न बुध्येत महातपाः। तावत् त्वमिह विप्रर्षे विश्रब्धश्चर वै सुखम्॥
en: O Brahmana Rishi, till then, live here happily and trustfully.

sn: ततो विबुद्धे तस्मिंस्तु सर्वलोकपितामहे। एकीभूतो हि हरक्ष्यामि शरीराणि द्विजोत्तम॥ आकाशं पृथिवीं ज्योतिर्वायु सलिलमेव च। लोके यच्च भवेच्छेषमिह स्थावरजङ्गमम्॥
en: O foremost of Brahmanas, when that Grandsire of all creatures will awake. I shall alone create all creatures having bodies, also the firmament, the earth, the light, the atmosphere, the water and also all mobile and immobile creatures on earth.

sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच इत्युक्तवान्तर्हितस्तात स देवः परमाद्भुतः। प्रजाश्चेमाः प्रपश्यामि विचित्रा विविधाः कृताः॥
en: Markandeya said : O child, having said this that greatly wonderful deity disappeared. I then saw this varied and wonderful creation start into life.

sn: एवं दृष्टं मया राजंस्तस्मिन् प्राप्ते युगक्षये। आश्चर्यं भरतश्रेष्ठ सर्वधर्मभृतां वर॥
en: O king, O best of the Bharata race, O foremost of all virtuous men, I saw all this wonderful sight at the end of the Yuga.

sn: यः य देवो मया दृष्टः पुरा पद्मायतेक्षणः। स एष पुरुषव्याघ्र सम्बन्धी ते जनार्दनः॥
en: The lotus-eyed deity whom I saw in days of yore, that foremost of beings is Janardana (Krishna) who has now become your relative.

sn: अस्यैव वरदानाद्धिस्मृतिर्न प्रजहाति माम्। दीर्घमायुश्च कौन्तेय स्वच्छन्दमरणं मम॥
en: O son of Kunti, in consequence of the boon bestowed upon me by that deity O my child, memory does not fail, that the period of my life is long and that death itself is under my control.

sn: स एष कृष्णो वार्ष्णेयः पुराणपुरुषो विभुः। आस्ते हरिरचिन्त्यात्मा क्रीडन्निव महाभुजः॥
en: That deity is Krishna, the descendant of Vrishni, the ancient supreme lord, the inconceivable Hari, the mighty-armed hero, who seems to sport (in the world).

sn: एषधाता विधाता च संहर्ता चैव शाश्वतः। श्रीवत्सवक्षा गोविन्दः प्रजापतिपतिः प्रभुः॥
en: He is Dhata, Vidhata, the destroyer of all, the Eternal, the hearer of Srivatsa mark on his breast, he is Govinda, the lord of all creatures, the highest of the high.

sn: दृष्ट्वेमं वृष्णिप्रवरं स्मृतिर्मामियामागता। आदिदेवमयं जिष्णुं पुरुषं पीतवाससम्॥
en: Seeing the chief of the Vrishnis, this Primeval Deity, this victorious God, wearing the yellow robe, my recollections come back to me.

sn: सर्वेषामेव भूतानां पिता माता च माधवः। गच्छध्वमेनं शरणं शरण्यं कौरवर्षभाः॥
en: This descendant of Madhu (Krishna) is the father and mother of all creatures, O foremost of the Kurus, take refuge in this great protector.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्ताश्च ते पार्था यमौ च पुरुषर्षभौ। द्रौपद्या सहिताः सर्वे नभश्चक्रुर्जनार्दनम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said: Having been thus addressed, the sons of Pritha and those two foremost of men, the twins, with Draupadi, all bowed down to Janardana (Krishna).

sn: स चैतान् पुरुषव्याघ्र साम्ना परमवल्गुना। सान्त्वयामास मानार्हो मन्यमानो यथाविधि॥
en: That foremost of men (Krishna), deserving of all honour, being thus revered by them, comforted them with sweet words.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच युधिष्ठिरस्तु कौन्तेयो मार्कण्डेयं महामुनिम्। पुन: पप्रच्छ साम्राज्ये भविष्यां जगतो गतिम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : The son of Kunti, Yudhishthira again asked the great Rishi Markandeya about the future government of the earth,

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच आश्चर्यभूतं १ प्रतः श्रुतं नो वदतां वर। मुने भार्गव यद् वृत्तं युगादौ प्रभवात्ययम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said: O Rishi, O descendant of Bhrigu, O foremost of speakers, the account of the destruction and recreation of things at the end of Yuga which we have heard from you is highly wonderful.

sn: अस्मिन् कलियुगे त्वस्ति पुनः कौतूहलं मम। समाकुलेषुधर्मेषु किं नु शेषं भविष्यति॥
en: I am very curious to know what will happen in the Kali Yuga and when virtue will be destroyed, what would remain.

sn: किंवीर्या मानवास्तत्र किमाहारविहारिणः। किमायुषः किंवसना भविष्यन्ति युगक्षये॥ कां च काष्ठांसमासाद्य पुनः सम्पत्स्यते कृतम्। विस्तरेण मुने ब्रूहि विचित्राणीह भाषसे॥
en: What will be the power of men then and what will be their food and what their amusements; what will be the length of their life, what their dress and what also will be the limit of time, after attaining which the Krita (age) will again begin. O Rishi, tell me all this. All that you narrate is varied and delightful.

sn: इत्युक्तः स मुनिश्रेष्ठः पुनरेवाभ्यभाषत। रमयन् वृष्णिशार्दूलं पाण्डवांश्च महानृषिः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having been thus addressed, that great Rishi again began to narrate, delighting that foremost of the Vrishni race (Krishna) and the Pandavas.

sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच शृणु राजन् मया दृष्टं यत् पुरा श्रुतमेव च। अनुभूतं च राजेन्द्र देवदेवप्रसादजम्॥
en: Markandeya said : O king, hear all that has been and heard by me and all that has been known to me by intuition through the grace of the god of gods.

sn: भविष्यं सर्वलोकस्य वृत्तान्तं भरतर्षभ। कलुषं कालमासाद्य कथ्यमानं निबोध मे॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, hear as I narrate the account of the world when the sinful time would come.

sn: कृते चतुष्पात् सकलो निर्व्याजोपाधिवर्जितः। वृषः प्रतिष्ठितोधर्मो मनुष्ये भरतर्षभ॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, in the Krita age, everything was free from deceit and guile, avarice and covetousness. Virtue like a bull was among men with four legs complete.

sn: अधर्मपादविद्धस्तु त्रिभिरंशैः प्रतिष्ठितः। त्रेतायां द्वापरेऽर्धेन व्यामिश्रोधर्म उच्यते॥
en: In the Treta sin took away one of its legs; and virtue had then (only) three legs. In the Dvapara, sin and virtue are mixed half and half.

sn: त्रिभिरंशैरधर्मस्तु लोकानाक्रम्य तिष्ठति। तामसं युगमासाद्य तदा भरतसत्तम॥ चतुर्थांशेनधर्मस्तु मनुष्यानुपतिष्ठति। आयुर्वीर्यमथो बुद्धिर्बलं तेजश्च पाण्डव॥ मनुष्याणामनुयुगं ह्रसतीति निबोध मे। राजानो ब्राह्मणा वैश्याः शूद्राश्चैव युधिष्ठिर॥ व्याजैर्धर्म चरिष्यन्तिधर्मवैतंसिका नराः। सत्यं संक्षेप्स्यते लोके नरैः पण्डितमानिभिः॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, in the dark age (Kali) virtue being mixed with three parts of sin lives by the side of men. Accordingly virtue is said to wait upon men with only fourth part remaining. O Yudhishthira, know that the period of life, the energy, the intellect and the physical strength of men (gradually) decrease in every Yuga. O Yudhishthira, the Brahmanas, the Kshatriyas, the Vaishyas and Shudras will practise morality and virtue with deceit and men in general will deceive their fellow men by spreading the (false) net of virtue. Men with false pride of learning by their acts will make truth concealed.

sn: सत्यहान्या ततस्तेषामायुरल्पं भविष्यति। आयुषः प्रक्षयाद् विद्यां नांशक्ष्यन्त्युपजीवितुम्॥
en: In consequence of the loss of truth the lives of men will be short and in consequence of the shortness of life they will not be able to acquire much knowledge.

sn: विद्याहीनानविज्ञानाल्लोभोऽप्यभिभविष्यति। लोभक्रोधपरा मूढाः कामासक्ताश्च मानवाः॥
en: In consequence of the littleness of knowledge, they will have no wisdom. And for this, covetousness and avarice will overwhelm them all. Men being wedded to avarice, anger, ignorance and desire,

sn: वैरबद्धा भविष्यन्ति परस्परवधैषिणः। ब्राह्मणाः क्षत्रिया वैश्याः संकीर्यन्तः परस्परम्॥ शूद्रतुल्या भविष्यन्ति तप:सत्यविवर्जिताः। अन्त्या मध्या भविष्यन्ति मध्याशान्त्या न संशयः।।
en: Will display enmity towards one another and will desire to take one another's life. Thus virtue diminished and their asceticism and truth gone Vaishyas. Brahmanas and Kshatriyas will all be equal to the Shudras. The lowest (orders of men) will rise to the middle (orders of men) and the middle will certainly descend to the lowest.

sn: ईदृशो भविता लोको युगान्ते पर्युपस्थिते। वस्त्राणां प्रवरा शाणीधान्यानां कोरदूषकाः॥
en: At the end of Yuga such will be the state of the world. The robes made of flax will be considered the best and Koradushaka grain will be considered to be the best.

sn: भार्यामित्राश्च पुरुषा भविष्यन्ति युगक्षये। मत्स्यामिषेण जीवन्तो दुहन्तश्चाप्यजैडकम्॥ गोषु नष्टासु पुरुषा येऽपि नित्यंधृतव्रताः। तेऽपि लोभसमायुक्ता भविष्यन्ति युगक्षये॥
en: At the end of Yuga men will consider their wives as only friends; they will live on fish and milk of goats and sheep's, for cows will then be extinct. At this time even those that always observe vows will become covetous.

sn: अन्योन्यं परिमुष्णान्तो हिंसयन्तश्च मानवाः। अजपा नास्तिका: स्तेना भविष्यन्ति युगक्षये॥
en: At the end of Yuga men will be opposed to one another and seek one another's life. They will be atheists and thieves.

sn: सरित्तीरेषु कुद्दालैर्वापयिष्यन्ति चौषधीः। ताश्चाप्यल्पफलास्तेषां भविष्यन्ति युगक्षये॥
en: They will dig even the banks of streams with their spades and sow grains there. But even these places will prove barren to them at this period of time.

sn: श्राद्धे दैवे च पुरुषा येऽपि नित्यंधृतव्रताः। तेऽपि लोभसमायुक्ता भोक्ष्यन्तीह परस्परम्॥
en: Those men who are devoted to the rites in honour of the deceased and of the celestials will be covetous and will also appropriate and enjoy what belongs to others.

sn: पिता पुत्रस्य भोक्ता च पितुः पुत्रस्तथैव च। अतिक्रान्तानि भोज्यानि भविष्यन्ति युगक्षये॥
en: The father will enjoy what belongs to the son and the son what belongs to the father. At such time things forbidden by the Shastras will be enjoyed by men.

sn: न व्रतानि चरिष्यन्ति ब्राह्मणा वेदनिन्दकाः। न यक्ष्यन्ति न होष्यन्ति हेतुवादविमोहिताः। निम्नेष्वीहां करिष्यन्ति हेतुवादविमोहिताः॥
en: The Brahmanas will speak ill of the Vedas and they will not observe any vows. Their understanding being clouded by the science of controversy, they will neither perform sacrifices nor Homas. Deluded by the sciences of controversy, their heart will be led away to things mean and low.

sn: निम्ने कृषि करिष्यन्ति योक्ष्यन्तिधुरिधेनुकाः। एकहायनवत्सांश्च योजयिष्यन्ति मानवाः॥
en: Men will till low-lands and employ cows and calves that are but one year old in drawing the plough and carrying the burdens.

sn: पुत्रः पितृवधं कृत्वा पिता पुत्रवधं तथा। निसद्वेगो बृहद्वादी न निन्दामुपलप्स्यते॥
en: Sons having killed their fathers and fathers having killed their sons will incur no opprobrium by doing it; and they ever will take glory in them.

sn: म्लेच्छभूतं जगत् सर्वं निष्क्रियं यज्ञवर्जितम्। भविष्यति निरानन्दमनुत्सवमथो तथा॥
en: The whole world will be filled with Mlechchha conduct and Mlechchha notions, All (religious) rites and sacrifices will cease; there will be joy no where and general festivities will disappear.

sn: प्रायशः कृपणानां हि तथाबन्धुमतामपि। विधवानां च वित्तानि हरिष्यन्तीह मानवाः॥
en: Men will rob the possessions of helpless persons, of those that are friendless and of those that are widows.

sn: स्वल्पवीर्यबलाः स्तब्धा लोभमोहपरायणाः। तत्कथादानसंतुष्टा दुष्टानामपि मानवाः॥ परिग्रहं करिष्यन्ति मायाचारपरिग्रहाः। समाह्वयन्तः कौन्तेय राजानः पापबुद्धयः॥ परस्परवधोयुक्ता मूर्खाः पण्डितमानिनः। भविष्यन्ति युगस्यान्ते क्षत्रिया लोककण्टकाः॥
en: Possessing little energy and strength and no knowledge and being addicted to avarice, ignorance and sinful practices, men will accept with joy the gifts made by the wicked-minded people with contemptuous words. O son of Kunti, the kings with their hearts wedded to sin, having no knowledge and always being proud of their wisdom will fight with one another with the intention of taking one another's lives. The Kshatriyas will be at the end of the Yuga the thorns of the earth.

sn: अरक्षितारो लुब्धाच मानाहङ्कारदर्पिताः। केवलं दण्डरुचयो भविष्यन्ति युगक्षये॥
en: Full of avarice, swelling with pride and vanity, unable and unwilling to protect (their subjects) they will take pleasure in punishing (their subjects).

sn: आक्रम्याक्रम्य साधूनां दारांश्चापिधनानि च। भोक्ष्यन्ते निरनुक्रोशा रुदतामपि भारत॥
en: Again and again attacking the good and the honest and feeling no pity for them even when they will cry in grief, the Kshatriyas will, O descendant of Bharata, rob them of their wives and wealth.

sn: न कन्यां याचते कश्चिात्रापि कन्या प्रदीयते। स्वयंग्राहा भविष्यन्ति युगान्ते समुपस्थित्ते॥
en: When this Yuga will come, no one will ask for a girl (for marriage) and no one also will give away a girl. The girls will themselves chocse their own husbands.

sn: राजानश्चाप्यसंतुष्टाः परार्थान् मूढचेतसः। सर्वोपायैर्हरिष्यन्ति युगान्ते पर्युपस्थिते॥
en: The kings with their mind darkened by ignorance and discontented with what they have, will at such a time rob their subjects by every means in their power.

sn: म्लेच्छीभूतं जगत् सर्वं भविष्यति न संशयः। हस्तो हस्तं परिमुषेद् युगान्ते समुपस्थिते॥
en: There is no doubt the world will be then Mlechchhafield. When this Yuga would come, the right hand will deceive the left and the left the right.

sn: सत्यं संक्षिप्यते लोके नरैः पण्डितमानिभिः। स्थविरा बालमतयो बालाः स्थविरबुद्धयः॥
en: Men with false pride of learning will diminish truth. The old will display the folly of the young and the young will show in them the dotage of the old.

sn: भीरुस्तथा शूरमानी शूरा भीरुविषादिनः। न विश्वसन्ति चान्योन्यं युगान्ते पर्युपस्थिते॥
en: The cowards will have the reputation of bravery and the brave will be as melancholy (fools) as the cowards. At this age men will not trust one another.

sn: एकाहार्यं युगं सर्वं लोभमोहव्यवस्थितम्। अधर्मो वर्द्धते तत्र न तुधर्मः प्रवर्तते॥
en: Full of avarice and ignorance all the world will have but one sort of food, sin will increase and virtue will fade away.

sn: ब्राह्मणाः क्षत्रिया वैश्या न शिष्यन्ति जनाधिप। एकवर्णस्तदा लोको भविष्यति युगक्षये॥
en: O ruler of men, the Brahmanas, the Kshatriyas and the Vaishyas will disappear, leaving no trace of their orders. At this time all men will be of one order.

sn: न क्षस्यति पिता पुत्रं पुत्रश्च पितरं तथा। भार्याश्च पतिशुश्रूषां न करिष्यन्ति संक्षय॥
en: Fathers will not forgive their sons and the sons will not forgive their fathers; at this time wives will not serve their husbands.

sn: ये यवान्ना जनपदा गोधूमान्नास्तथैव च। तान् देशान् संश्रयिष्यन्ति युगान्ते पर्युपस्थिते॥
en: When this age will come men will seek those countries where men's staple food is wheat and barley.

sn: स्वैराचाराश्च पुरुषा योषितश्च विशाम्पते। अन्योन्यं न सहिष्यन्ति युगान्ते पर्युपस्थिते॥
en: O king, men and women will become perfectly free in their conduct. When this age will come, they will not tolerate one another's acts.

sn: म्लेच्छभूतं जगत् सर्वं भविष्यति युधिष्ठिर। न श्राद्धैस्तर्पयिष्यन्ति दैवतानीह मानवाः॥
en: O Yudhishthira, the whole world will be then Mlechchhafied; men will no more gratify the celestials performing the Shraddha ceremony.

sn: न कश्चित्कस्यचिच्छ्रोता न कश्चित्कस्यचिद् गुरुः। तमोग्रस्तस्तदा लोको भविष्यति जनाधिप।॥
en: O ruler of men, no one will listen to the words of others and none will be considered as another's preceptor. The whole world will be enveloped by fearful (intellectual) darkness.

sn: परमायुश्च भविता तदा वर्षाणि षोडश। ततः प्राणान् विमोक्ष्यन्ति युगान्ते समुपस्थिते॥
en: Then the length of men's life will be sixteen years. When this age would come men will die at this age.

sn: पञ्चमे वाथ षष्ठे वा वर्षे कन्या प्रसूयते। सप्तपवर्षाष्टवर्षाश्च प्रजास्यन्ति नरास्तदा॥
en: Girls of five and six years will give birth to children and boys of seven or eight years of age will be fathers.

sn: पत्यौ स्त्री तु तदा राजन् पुरुषो वा स्त्रियं प्रति। युगान्ते राजशार्दूल न तोषमुपयास्यति॥
en: O king, O foremost of monarchs, when this age would come the wife will not remain content with her husband and the husband also will not remain content with his wife.

sn: अल्पद्रव्या वृथालिङ्गा हिंसा च प्रभविष्यति। न कश्चित् कस्यचिद् दाता भविष्यति युगक्षये॥
en: When this age would come, the possession of men will be small and they will falsely bear the marks of religion. The world will be filled with avarice and jealousy. No one will be a giver to the other.

sn: अट्टशूला जनपदाः शिवशूलाश्चतुष्पथाः। केशशूलाः स्त्रियश्चापि भविष्यन्ति युगक्षये॥
en: The country will be afflicted with dearth and famine. The roads will be filled with lustful men and unchaste women. Women will also hate their husbands.

sn: म्लेच्छाचाराः सर्वभक्षा दारुणाः सर्वकर्मसु। भाविनः पश्चिमे काले मुनष्या नात्र संशयः॥
en: When this age will come, men will certainly adopt the Mlechchha conduct; they will eat all things; they will be free in all their all acts.

sn: क्रयविक्रयकाले च सर्वः सर्वस्य वञ्चनम्। युगान्ते भरतश्रेष्ठ वित्तलोभात् करिष्यति॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, led by avarice, men will deceive one another when they will buy and sell.

sn: ज्ञानानि चाप्यविज्ञाय करिष्यन्ति क्रियास्तथा। आत्मच्छन्देन वर्तन्ते युगान्ते समुपस्थिते॥
en: When this age would come, men will perform the ceremonies and rites without knowing the ordinances; they will behave as they would like.

sn: स्वभावात् क्रूरकर्माणश्चान्योन्यमभिशंसिनः। भवितारो जनाः सर्वे सम्प्राप्ते तु युगक्षये॥
en: When this age would come, led by their nature, men will act with cruelty and will speak ill of one another.

sn: आरामांश्चैव वृक्षांश्च नाशयिष्यन्ति निर्व्यथाः। भविता संशये लोके जीवितस्य हि देहिनाम्॥
en: People will pitilessly destroy trees and gardens. Men will be filled with anxiety for their livelihood.

sn: तथा लोभाभिभूताश्च भविष्यन्ति नरा नृप। ब्राह्मणांश्च हनिष्यन्ति ब्राह्मणस्वोपभोगिनः॥
en: O king, led away by covetousness, men will kill the Brahmanas and appropriate and enjoy their wealth.

sn: हाहाकृता द्विजाश्चैव भयार्ता वृषलार्दिताः। त्रातारमलभन्तो वै भ्रमिष्यन्ति महीमिमाम्॥
