Then with joined hands he said, "Why don't I know this king? He placed sacrificial stakes one thousand time when kindling the sacrificial fire.

sn: सरचेदमस्य दक्षिणाभिर्दत्ताभिगोभिरतिक्रममाणाभिः कृतम्। अत्र चाहं प्रतिवसामीति॥
en: This lake was made by the feet of the king given away by this king to the Brahmanas as Dakshinas when the sacrifice was completed. I have lived here ever since.

sn: अथैतत् सकलं कच्छपेनोदाहृतं श्रुत्वा तदनन्तरं देवलोकाद् देवरथः प्रादुरासीद् वाचश्चाश्रूयन्तेन्द्रद्युम्नं प्रति प्रस्तुतस्ते स्वर्गो स्वर्गो यथोचितं स्थानं प्रतिपद्यस्व कीर्तिमानस्यव्यग्रो याहीति॥
en: When we were hearing all this from the tortoise, a celestials car came there from the celestials region and an invisible voice was heard which said, "Come and go to the place, you desire to obtain in heaven. Your achievements are great. Therefore cheerfully come to the place (set apart) for you.”

sn: भवन्ति चात्र श्लोकाःदिवं स्पृशति भूमिं च शब्दः पुण्यस्य कर्मणः। यावत् स शब्दो भवति तावत् पुरुष उच्यते॥
en: Here occur these Slokas, “The report of virtuous acts spreads all over the carth and it reaches heaven. As long as the report lasts so long it is said that he lives in heaven.

sn: अकीर्तिः कीर्त्यते लोके यस्य भूतस्य कस्यचित्। स पतत्यधमाँल्लोकान् यावच्छब्दः प्रकीर्त्यते॥
en: The man, the report of whose evil deeds is talked about, is said to fall down; and he lives in the lower region as long as that evil report lasts. me

sn: दनन्ताय नरः सदा। विहाय चित्तं पापिष्ठं धर्ममेव समाश्रयेत्॥
en: Therefore a man should be virtuous if he desires to obtain heaven. Abandoning a sinful mind, he should seek refuge in virtue.”

sn: इत्येतच्छ्रुत्वा स राजाब्रवीत् तिष्ठ तावद् यावदिमौ वृद्धौ यथास्थानं प्रतिपादयामीति॥
en: Having heard this, the king said, “Let the car stay here so long I do not take back the old persons from the places whence I brought them."

sn: स मां प्रावारकर्णं चोलूकं यथोचिते स्थाने प्रतिपाद्य तेनैव यानेन संस्थितो यथोचितं स्थानं प्रतिपेदे। तन्मयानुभूतं चिरजीविनेदृशमिति पाण्डवानुवाच मार्कण्डेयः॥
en: Having brought and the owl Pravarakarna to our respective places, he went away in that car to the place which was a fit region for him. Long-lived as I am saw all this. Vaishampayana said: Thus Markandeya told ail this to the Pandavas.

sn: पाण्डवाश्चोचुः साधु शोभनं भवता कृतं राजानमिन्द्रद्युम्नं स्वर्गलोकाच्च्युतं स्वे स्थाने प्रतिपादयतेत्यथैतानब्रवीदसौ ननु देवकीपुत्रेणापि कृष्णेन कृष्णेन नरके मज्जामानो राजर्षिर्तृगस्तस्मात् कृच्छ्रात् पुनः समुद्धृत्य स्वर्ग प्रापित इति॥
en: The Pandavas said : O blessed one, you acted properly in causing king Indradhyumna who had fallen from heaven to regain it. He (Markandeya) said, “The son of Devaki Krishna also had thus rescued the royal sage Nriga who had fallen into hell. He caused him to regain heaven.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच श्रुत्वा स राजा राजर्षेरिन्द्रद्युम्नस्य तत् तदा। मार्कण्डेयान्महाभागात् स्वर्गस्य प्रतिपादनम्॥ युधिष्ठिरो महाराज पुनः पप्रच्छ तं मुनिम्।
en: Vaishampayana said : Having heard from the highly exalted Markandeya the story of the royal sage Indradyumna's regaining heaven, the king Yudhishthira, the great monarch, again asked the Rishi,

sn: कीदृशीषु ह्यवस्थासु दत्त्वा दानं महामुने॥ इन्द्रलोकं त्वनुभवेत् पुरुषस्तद् द्रवीहि मे।
en: “O great Rishi, tell me how a man should practice charity to go to the regions of Indra.

sn: गार्हस्थ्येऽप्यथवा बाल्ये यौवने स्थविरेऽपि वा। यथा फलं समश्याति तथा त्वं कथयस्व मे॥
en: Is it by practicing charity when leading the domestic life or in boyhood or in youth or in the old age (that one goes to Indra's abode)? Tell me the respective merits of charity in different stages of life.

sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच वृथा जन्मानि चत्वारि वृथा दानानि षोडश। वृथा जन्म ह्यपुत्रस्य ये च धर्मबहिष्कृताः॥ परपाकेषु येऽश्नन्ति आत्मार्थं च पचेत् तु यः। पर्यश्नन्ति वृथा ये च तदसत्यं प्रकीर्त्यते।५॥
en: Markandeya said : The life, that is useless, is of four kinds and the charity which is useless is of sixteen kinds. That life is useless in which there is no son born, in which one has no virtue. In which one lives on food given by another and in which one cook (food) for himself only, without giving to the Pitris, the celestials and the guests and one who eats before all these.

sn: आरूढपतिते दत्तमन्यायोपहृतं च यत्। व्यर्थंतु पतिते दानं ब्राह्मणे तस्करे तथा॥
en: The gift to one who has fallen away from the path of virtue and the gift of wealth which has been earned wrongly and dishonestly are both useless. The gifts to a fallen Brahmana, to a thief to a false preceptor, are also useless.

sn: गुरौ चानृतिके पापे कृतघ्ने ग्रामयाजके। वेदविक्रयिणे दत्तं तथा वृषलयाजके॥ ब्रह्मबन्धुषु यद् दत्तं यद् दत्तं वृषलीपतौ। स्त्रीजनेषु च यद् दत्तं व्यालग्राहे तथैव च॥ परिचारकेषु यद् दत्तं वृथा दानानि षोडश।
en: The gift to an untruthful man, to one who officiates at sacrifices performed by all classes of people residing in a village, to one that sells the Vedas to a Brahmana who cooks for a Shudra, to one who is by birth a Brahmana, but who does not perform the duties of his order, is all in vain. The gift to one who has married a girl already in her puberty, to a woman, to one who sports with a snake and to one who is engaged in minimal services, is also in vain. These are the sixteen useless charities.

sn: तमोवृतस्तु यो दद्याद् भयात् क्रोधात् तथैव च।॥ भुङ्क्ते च दानं तत् सर्वं गर्भस्थस्तु नरः सदा। ददद् दानं द्विजातिभ्यो वृद्धभावेन मानवः॥
en: He who gives away wealth out of fear or anger. Enjoys the fruits of that charity when he remains in the womb of his mother. The man who gives away (wealth) to the Brahmanas, enjoys its fruits while he is in old age.

sn: तस्मात् सर्वास्ववस्थासु सर्वदानानि पार्थिव दातव्यानि द्विजातिभ्यः स्वर्गमार्गजिगीषया॥
en: O king, therefore, the man who desires to get to the path of heaven should under all conditions give away (wealth) to the Brahmanas.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच चातुर्वर्ण्यस्य सर्वस्य वर्तमानाः प्रतिग्रहे। केन विप्रा विशेषेण तारयन्ति तरन्ति च॥
en: Yudhishthira said : By what means do the Brahmanas, who receive gifts from all the four orders, save others as well as themselves?

sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच जपैर्मन्त्रैश्च होमैश्च स्वाध्यायाध्ययनेन च। नावं वेदमयीं कृत्वा तारयन्ति तरन्ति च॥
en: Markandeya said: By Japa, by Mantras by Homa and by the study of the Vedas, they (Brahmanas) build a Veda boat and with it they save others as well as themselves.

sn: ब्राह्मणांस्तोषयेद् यस्तु तुष्यन्ते तस्य देवताः। वचनाच्चापि विप्राणां स्वर्गलोकमवाप्नुयात्॥
en: The celestials themselves are gratified with that man who gratifies the Brahmanas. At the command of a Brahmana a man obtains heaven.

sn: पितृदैवतपूजाभिर्ब्राह्मणाभ्यर्चनेन च। अनन्तं पुण्यलोकं तु गन्तासि त्वं न संशयः॥
en: O king, you will certainly go to heaven for your worshipping the Pitris and the celestials and for your showing great reverence to the Brahmanas,

sn: श्लेष्मादिभिर्व्याप्ततनुम्रियमाणो विचेतनः। ब्राह्मणा एव सम्पूज्याः पुण्यं स्वर्गमभीप्सता।१६।।
en: Even if your body be dull and weak and full of phlegm. He who desires to obtain virtue and heaven should worship the Brahmanas.

sn: श्राद्धकाले तु यत्नेन भोक्तव्या ह्यजुगुप्सिताः। दुर्वर्णः कुनखी कुष्ठी मायावी कुण्डगोलकौ॥ वर्जनीयाः प्रयलेन काण्डपृष्ठाश्च देहिनः। जुगुप्सितं हि यच्छ्राद्धं दहत्यग्निरिवेन्धनम्॥
en: One should with great care feed them at the time of Shraddha ceremonies, but those among them (Brahmana) that are cursed or fallen, that are either exceeding handsome or excessively black, that have diseased nails, that are lepers, that are deceitful, that are bastards, born of widows or of women with their husbands in exile and that support themselves by the profession of arms, all these should be excluded. A censurable Shraddha consumes the performer as fire consumes the wood.

sn: ये ये श्राद्धे न युज्यन्ते मूकान्धबधिरादयः। तेऽपि सर्वे नियोक्तव्या मिश्रिता वेदपारगैः॥
en: If those that are to be employed in a Shraddha happen to be dumb, blind or deaf, care should be taken to employ them with the Brahmanas who are learned in the Vedas.

sn: प्रतिग्रहश्च वै देयः शृणु यस्य युधिष्ठिर। प्रदातारं तथाऽऽत्मानं यस्तारयति शक्तिमान्॥ तस्मिन् देयं द्विजे दानं सर्वागमविजानता। प्रदातारं यथाऽऽत्मानं तारयेद् यः स शक्तिमान्॥
en: O Yudhishthira, hear now what you should give away. He who knows the Vedas should give away to only those Brahmanas who are able to save both the giver and himself, for he only is to be considered a competent (Brahmana) who can save the giver and himself.

sn: न तथा हविषो होमैन पुष्पैर्नानुलेपनैः। अग्नयः पार्थ तुष्यन्ति यथा ह्यतिथिभोजने॥
en: O son of Pritha, the sacred fire does not become so much gratified in receiving the libations of Ghee, the offering of flowers and sandal paste and other perfumes as by the entertainment of guests.

sn: तस्मात् त्वं सर्वयत्नेन यतस्वातिथिभोजने। पादोदकं पादघृतं दीपमन्नं प्रतिश्रयम्॥ प्रयच्छन्ति तु ये राजन् नोपसर्पन्ति ते यमम्।
en: Therefore with all care entertain guests. O king, those that give to his guests water to wash his feet, butter to rub over his tired legs, light in darkness and food and shelter, do not (at all) go before Yama.

sn: देवमाल्यापनयनं द्विजोच्छिष्टावमार्जनम्॥ आकल्प: परिचर्या च गात्रसंवाहनानि च। अत्रैकैकं नृपश्रेष्ठ गोदानाद्ध्यतिरिच्यते॥
en: The removal of garlands of flowers offered to the gods, the removal of the remnant of a Brahmana's food, serving with prepared pastes, the shampooing of a Brahmana's legs, O foremost of kings, each of these gives better fruits than the giving away of kine.

sn: कपिलायाः प्रदानात् तु मुच्यते नात्र संशयः। तस्मादलंकृतां दद्यात् कपिलां तु द्विजातये॥
en: A man certainly rescues himself (from hell) by giving away Kapila cow, therefore a Kapila cow, decked with ornaments, should be given to a Brahmana.

sn: श्रोत्रियाय दरिद्राय गृहस्थायाग्निहोत्रिणे। पुत्रदाराभिभूताय तथा ह्यनुपकारिणे॥
en: One should make gifts to a person nobly born, one who is learned in the Vedas, one that is fair, one who leads a domestic life, but who is burdened with wife and children, one who duly worships the sacred fire and one who has done you no service.

sn: एवंविधेषु दातव्या न समृद्धेषु भारत। को गुणो भरतश्रेष्ठ समृद्धेष्वभिवर्जितम्॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, O descendant of Bharata, you should always give away to such men and not to those who are wealthy. What merit is there to give (wealth) to one who is wealthy?

sn: एकस्यैका प्रदातव्या न बहूनां कदाचन। सा गौर्विक्रयमापन्ना हन्यात् त्रिपुरुषं कुलम्॥ न तारयति दातारं ब्राह्मणं नैव नैव तु।
en: One cow must be given to one Brahmana. One single cow must not be given to many Brahmanas. If that cow is sold, three generations of the giver's family would be lost. Such a gift will neither rescue the giver nor the Brahmana who takes it.

sn: सुवर्णस्य विशुद्धस्य सुवर्णं यः प्रयच्छति॥ सुवर्णानां शतं तेन दत्तं भवति शाश्वतम्।
en: He who gives away eighty Ratis of pure gold, obtains the everlasting fruit of giving away one hundred pieces of gold.

sn: अनड्वाहं तु यो दद्याद् बलवन्तं धुरंधरम्॥ स लिस्तरति दुर्गाणि स्वर्गलोकं च गच्छति।
en: He who gives away a strong bull capable of drawing the plough, does not certainly meet with any calamity; he finally goes to heaven.

sn: वसुन्धरां तु यो दद्याद् द्विजाय विदुरात्मने।॥ दातारं ह्यनुगच्छन्ति सर्वे कामाभिवाञ्छिताः।
en: He who gives away land to a learned Brahmana, has all his desires fulfilled.

sn: पृच्छन्ति चात्र दातारं वदन्ति पुरुषा भुवि॥ अध्वनि क्षीणगात्राश्च पांसुपादावगुण्ठिताः। तेषामेव श्रमार्तानां यो ह्यन्नं कथयेद् बुधः॥ अन्नदातृसमः सोऽपि कीयंते नात्र संशयः।
en: The tired traveller, with weakened limbs and with feet besmeared with dust, asks for the name of him who gives him food. There are men who answer him by telling him the name. That wise man who informs the toil-worn travellers the name of the persons who give them food is certainly considered equal in virtue as the giver of food himself.

sn: तस्मात् त्वं सर्वदानानि हित्वान्नं सम्प्रयच्छ हा॥ न हीदृशं पुण्यफलं विचित्रमिह विद्यते। यथाशक्ति च यो दद्यादन्नं विप्रेषु संस्कृतम्॥ स तेन कर्मणाऽऽमोति प्रजापतिसलोकताम्।
en: O Yudhishthira, Therefore (even) abstaining from other kinds of gifts, give away food. There is no virtue so great as that of giving well-cooked and pure food to the Brahmanas according to one's ability. That man by his this act obtains the companionship of Prajapati.

sn: अन्नमेव विशिष्टं हि तस्मात् परतरं न च॥ अन्नं प्रजापतिश्चोक्तः स च संवत्सरो मतः। संवत्सरस्तु यज्ञोऽसौ सर्वं यज्ञे प्रतिष्ठितम्॥
en: There is no gift superior to that of food. The food is the foremost and the first of all things. It is said that food is Prajapati. Prajapati (again) is considered as year and the year is sacrifice.

sn: तस्मात् सर्वाणि भूतानि स्थावराणि चराणि च। तस्मादन्नं विशिष्टं हि सर्वेभ्य इति विश्रुतम्॥
en: From sacrifice all mobile and immobile creatures take their birth. For this reason it has been heard by us that food is the foremost of all things.

sn: येषां तटाकानि महोदकानि वाप्यश्च कूपाश्च प्रतिश्रयाश्च। अन्नस्य दानं मधुरा च वाणी यमस्य ते निर्वचना भवन्ति॥
en: Those, that give away lakes and large tanks, wells and ponds, shelter and food with sweet words, have not to bear the up-braiding of Yama.

sn: धान्यं श्रमेणार्जितवित्तसंचितं विप्रे सुशीले च प्रयच्छते यः। वसुन्धरा तस्य भवेत् सुतुष्टा धारां वसूनां प्रतिमुञ्चतीव॥
en: Earth is always satisfied with that man who gives rice and wealth earned by his own labour to the Brahmanas whose behaviour is good. She pours upon such a man showers of wealth.

sn: अन्नदाः प्रथमं यान्ति सत्यवाक् तदनन्तरम्। अयाचितप्रदाता च समं यान्ति त्रयो जनाः॥
en: The giver of food walks first, then follows the speaker of truth; and then the man who gives away to a person who does not ask. But all these three go to the same place.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच कौतूहलसमुत्पन्नः पर्यपृच्छद् युधिष्ठिरः। मार्कण्डेयं महात्मानं पुनरेव सहानुजः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Being filled with curiosity, Yudhishthira, with his brothers, again asked the illustrious Markandeya.

sn: यमलोकस्य चाध्वानमन्तरं मानुषस्य च। कीदृशं किम्प्रमाणं वा कथं वा तन्महामुने। तरन्ति पुरुषाश्चैव केनोपायेन शंस मे॥
en: Yudhishthira said: O great Rishi, what is the distance of the region of Yama from that of men? What is its measurement? How does a man pass over it and by what meant? Tell me all this.

sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच सर्वगुह्यतमं प्रश्न पवित्रमृषिसंस्तुतम्। कथयिष्यामि ते राजन् धर्म्य धर्मभृतां वर॥
en: Markandeya said : O king, O foremost of all virtuous men, your this question relates to a great mystery. It is sacred and it is much praised by the Rishis. I shall speak to you about this Dharma.

sn: षडशीतिसहस्राणि योजनानां नराधिप। यमलोकस्य चाध्वानमन्तरं मानुषस्य च॥
en: O ruler of men, the distance of the region of Yama from the abode of men is eighty-six thousand yojanas.

sn: आकाशं तदपानीयं घोरं कान्तारदर्शनम्। न तत्र वृक्षच्छाया वा पानीयं केतनानि च॥ विश्रमेद् यत्र वै श्रान्तः पुरुषोऽध्वनि कर्शितः।
en: The way is over space. There is no water there and it is terrible to look at. There is nowhere in that region any shade of any tree, any water and any resting place, in which the traveller when fatigued, may take rest for some time.

sn: नीयते यमदूतैस्तु यमस्याज्ञाकरैर्बलात्॥ नराः स्त्रियस्तथैवान्ये पृथिव्यां जीवसंज्ञिताः।
en: Along this path are forcibly taken by messenger of Yama, obedient to his command, all men and women and all creatures that have life.

sn: ब्राह्मणेभ्यः प्रदानानि नानारूपाणि पार्थिव॥ हयादीनां प्रकृष्टानि तेऽध्वानं यान्ति वै नराः। संनिवार्यातपं यान्ति छत्रेणैव हि छत्रदाः॥
en: O ruler of earth, O king, those that have given horses and other good conveyances to the Brahmanas, go along (this path) on those animals and conveyances. Those that have given. umbrellas thus (to the Brahmanas) go along this path with umbrellas, warding off the sun's rays.

sn: तृप्ताश्चैवान्नदातारो ह्यतृप्ताश्चाप्यनन्नदाः। वस्त्रिणो वस्त्रदा यान्ति अवस्त्रा यान्त्यवस्त्रदाः॥
en: Those that have given food go along without any hunger and those that have not given food go along afflicted with (great) hunger. Those that have given cloths go along attired in cloths and those that have not given cloths go along naked,

sn: हिरण्यदाः सुखं यान्ति पुरुषास्त्वभ्यलंकृताः। भूमिदास्तु सुखं यान्ति सर्वैः कामैः सुतर्पिताः॥
en: Those that have given gold go along in happiness, well adorned in ornaments. And those that have given land go along with their every desire completely gratified.

sn: यान्ति चैवापरिक्लिष्टा नराः सस्यप्रदायकाः। नराः सुखतरं यान्ति विमानेषु गृहप्रदाः॥
en: Those that have given grains go along without being afflicted with any want; and those that have given houses go along on cars.

sn: पानीयदा ह्यतृषिताः प्रहृष्टमनसो नराः। पन्थानं द्योतयन्तश्च यान्ति दीपप्रदाः सुखम्॥
en: Those that have given king go along with cheerful hearts without ever being afflicted by thirst. Those that have given lights go along in great happiness lighting the way before them.

sn: गोप्रदास्तु सुखं यान्ति निर्मुक्ताः सर्वपातकैः। विमानैर्हससंयुक्तैर्यान्ति मासोपवासिनः॥
en: Those that have given kine go along in happiness, their sins being all destroyed. Those that have fasted for a month, go along on cars drawn by swans.

sn: तथा बर्हिप्रयुक्तैश्च षष्ठरात्रोपवासिनः। त्रिरात्रं क्षपते यस्तु एकभक्तेन पाण्डव॥ अन्तरा चैव नाश्नाति तस्य लोका ह्यनामयाः। पानीयस्य गुणा दिव्याः प्रेतलोकसुखावहाः॥
en: O son of Pandu, those that have fasted for six nights, go on cars drawn by peacocks. O son of Pandu, he who fasts for three nights taking only one meal without a second goes to a region free from disease and anxiety. The water has this excellent property that it produces happiness in the region of the dead.

sn: तत्र पुष्पोदका नाम नदी तेषां विधीयते। शीतलं सलिलं तत्र पिबन्ति ह्यमृतोपमम्॥
en: There they see a river named Pushpodaka. They there drink cool water which is like the very ambrosia.

sn: ये च दुष्कृतकर्माणः पूयं तेषां विधीयते। एवं नदी महाराज सर्वकामप्रदा हि सा॥
en: He who is of evil deed drinks there puss which is the thing that has been ordained for him. O great king, that river fulfills one's all desires.

sn: तस्मात् त्वमपि राजेन्द्र पूजयनान् यथाविधि। अध्वनि क्षीणगात्रश्च पथि पांसुसमन्वितः॥ पृच्छते ह्यन्नदातारं गृहमायाति चाशया। तं पूजयाथ यत्नेन सोऽतिथिर्ब्राह्मणश्च सः॥
en: O king of kings, worship there these (Brahmanas) in all due form. Weakened with travelling and besmeared with the dust on this way, the traveller asks for the name of him who gives food and comes in hope to his house to worship him with all care, for he is a great Brahmana.

sn: तं यान्तमनुगच्छन्ति देवाः सर्वे सवासवाः। तस्मिन् सम्पूजिते प्रीता निराशा यान्त्यपूजिते॥
en: As he proceeds all the celestials with Vasava (Indra) follow him. If he is worshipped, they are gratified; and if he is not worshipped they become cheerless.

sn: तस्मात् त्वमपि राजेन्द्र पूजयैनं यथाविधि। एतत् ते शतशः प्रोक्तं किं भूयः श्रोतुमिच्छसि॥
en: O king of kings, therefore duly worship these (Brahmanas). I have thus spoken to you on one hundred subjects. What do you desire to hear from me more?

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच पुनः पुनरहं श्रोतुं कथां धर्मसमाश्रयाम्। पुण्यामिच्छामि धर्मज्ञ कथ्यमानां त्वया विभो॥
en: Yudhishthira said : O lord, O virtuous man, I desire to hear you again and again on sacred subjects relating to virtue and morals.

sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच धर्मान्तरं प्रति कथां कथ्यमानां मया नृप। सर्वपापहरां नित्यं शृणुष्वावहितो मम॥
en: Markandeya said: O king, I shall now speak on another sacred subject relating to eternity which destroys all sins. Listen to me with all others.

sn: कपिलायां तु दत्तायां यत् फलं ज्येष्ठपुष्करे। तत् फलं भरतश्रेष्ठ विप्राणां पादधावने॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, the merit equal to that of giving away a Kapila cow in Pushkara (Tirtha) is obtained by washing the feet of the Brahmanas.

sn: द्विजपादोदकक्लिन्ना यावत् तिष्ठति मेदिनी। तावत् पुष्करपर्णेन पिबन्ति पितरो जलम्॥
en: As long as the earth remains moist with the water touched by the feet of a Brahmana, so long do the Pitris drink water from the lotus leaves.

sn: स्वागतेनाग्नयस्तृप्ता आसनेन शतक्रतुः। पितरः पादशौचेन अन्नाद्येन प्रजापतिः॥
en: If a guest is welcomed, Agni is gratified. If he is offered a seat, Indra is gratified. If his feet are washed, it is the Pitris who are delighted. If he is fed, it is Prajapati (Brahma) himself who is gratified.

sn: यावद् वत्सस्य वै पादौ शिरश्चैव प्रदृश्यते। तस्मिन् काले प्रदातव्या प्रयत्नेनान्तरात्मना॥ अन्तरिक्षगतो वत्सो यावद् योन्यां प्रदृश्यते। तावद् गौ पृथिवी ज्ञेया यावद् गर्भं न मुञ्चति॥
en: One should with subdued soul give away a cow when the feet and the head of her calf are visible. Before her delivery is complete, a cow with her calf in the air in the course of falling from the uterus to the earth is to be considered as equal to the earth herself.

sn: यावन्ति तस्या रोमाणि वत्सस्य च युधिष्ठिर। तावद् युगसहस्राणि स्वर्गलोके महीयते॥
en: O Yudhishthira, he is adored in the celestials region as many thousand Yugas as there are hairs on the bodies of that cow and the calf.

sn: सुवर्णनासां यः कृत्वा सुखुरां कृष्णधेनुकाम्। तिलैः प्रच्छादितां दद्यात् सर्वरत्नैरलंकृताम्॥
en: The person who donets a black cow duly ornamented with jwels including nose-ring made of gold and the hoof made of silver.

sn: प्रतिग्रहं गृहीत्वा यः पुनर्ददति साधवे। फलानां फलमश्नाति तदा दत्त्वा च भारत॥ ससमुद्रगुहा तेन सशैलवनकानना। चतुरन्ता भवेद् दत्त पृथिवी नात्र संशयः॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, he who, having accepted a gift, gives it away immediately to a person who is virtuous and honest, obtains great merit. He certainly obtains the fruit of giving away the whole earth to her utmost limits with her oceans, seas and caves, her mountains and forests and woods.

sn: अन्तर्जानुशयो यस्तु भुङ्क्ते संसक्तभाजनः। यो द्विजः शब्दरहितं स क्षमस्तारणाय वै॥
en: The Brahmana, who eats in silence from a plate, keeping his hands between his knees, succeeds in saving others.

sn: अपानपा न गदितास्तथान्ये ये द्विजातयः। जपन्ति संहितां सम्यक् ते नित्यं तारणक्षमाः॥
en: Those Brahmanas who abstain from drink and who are never spoken by others as having any fault and who daily read the Samhitas are capable of saving others,

sn: हव्यं कव्यं च यत् किंचित् सर्वं तच्छ्रोत्रियोऽर्हति। दत्तं हि श्रोत्रिये साधौ ज्वलितेऽग्नौ यथा हुतम्॥
en: Havya (libation of ghee) and Kavya (edible offerings) should all be presented to a Brahmana who is learned in the Vedas. As an offering of ghee to Agnis is never in vain, so a gift to the Brahmanas learned in the Vedas is never in vain.

sn: मन्युप्रहरणा विप्रा न विप्राः शस्त्रयोधिनः। निहन्युर्मन्युना विप्रा वज्रपाणिरिवासुरान्॥
en: The Brahinanas have anger as their weapon; they never fight with weapons made of iron or steel. The Brahmanas kill their enemies with anger, as the wielder of thunder killed the Asuras.

sn: धर्माश्रितेयं त कथा कथितेयं तवानघ। यां श्रुत्वा मुनयः प्रीता नैमिषारण्यवासिनः॥
en: O sinless one, the theme relating to virtue and morality is now over. Having heard them, the Rishis, in the Naimisha forest, greatly delighted.

sn: वीतशोकभयक्रोधा विपाप्मानस्तथैव च। श्रुत्वेमां तु कथां राजन् न भवन्तीह मानवाः॥
en: O king, (hearing them) they were freed from grief, fear and anger and they were cleansed of their sins. Those men who hear them are freed from the bondage of rebirth.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच किं तच्छौचं भवेद् येन विप्रः शुद्धः सदा भवेत्। तदिच्छामि महाप्राज्ञ श्रोतुं धर्मभृतां वर॥
en: Yudhishthira said : O greatly wise one, O foremost of virtuous men, what purification is there by which a Brahmana might always be pure. I desire to hear it.

sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच वाक् शौचं कर्मशौचं च यच्च शौचं जलात्मकम्। त्रिभिः शौचैरुपेतो यः स स्वर्गी नात्र संशयः॥
en: Markandeya continued There are three kinds of purity, namely purity in speech, purity in deed and purity by water. He who takes to these certainly obtains heaven.

sn: सायं प्रातश्च संध्यां यो ब्राह्मणोऽभ्युपसेवते। प्रजपन् पावनी देवीं गायत्री वेदमातरम्॥ स तया पावितो देव्या ब्राह्मणो नष्टकिल्बिषः। न सीदेत् प्रतिगृहणनो महीमपि ससागराम्॥
en: That Brahmana who adores (the goddess) Sandhya in the morning and in the evening and who recites the sacred Gayatri, who is the mother of the Vedas, is cleansed from all his sins after being sanctified by the latter. Even if he accepts in gift the entire earth with her oceans, he does not suffer the least unhappiness.

sn: ये चास्य दारुणाः केचिद् ग्रहाः सूर्यादयो दिवि। ते चास्य सौम्या जायन्ते शिवाः शिवतराः सदा॥
en: Those planets in the sky including the sun that may be inauspicious and hostile towards him soon become favourable and auspicious towards him for his these acts. And those that are auspicious and favourable become more auspicious and favourable.

sn: चैनं दारुणाः पिशिताशनाः। घोररूपा महाकाया धर्षयन्ति द्विजोत्तमम्॥
en: The terrible Rakshasas who feed on animal food and who have gigantic and fearful appearances, all become incapable of doing any injury to a Brahmana who practises these purifications.

sn: नाध्यापनाद् याजनाद् वा अन्यस्माद् वा प्रतिग्रहात्। दोषो भवति विप्राणां ज्वलिताग्निसमा द्विजाः॥
en: They incur no fault in consequence of teaching, of officiating at sacrifice and of accepting gifts from others. The Brahmanas are like the blazing fire.

sn: सर्वे नानुगतं दुर्वेदा वा सुवेदा वा प्राकृताः संस्कृतास्तथा। ब्राह्मणा नावमन्तव्या भस्मच्छन्ना इवाग्नयः॥
en: Whether learned in the Vedas or not, whether pure or impure, they should never be insulted, for Brahmanas are like fires, 'covered with ashes.

sn: यथा श्मशाने दीप्तौजाः पावको नैव दुष्यति। एवं विद्वानविद्वान् वा ब्राह्मणो दैवतं महत्॥
en: A fire that blazes forth in a place of cremation is never impure, so is a Brahmana either learned or ignorant is always pure. He is superior to a celestials.

sn: प्राकारैश्च पुरद्वारैः प्रासादैश्च पृथग्विधैः। नगराणि न शोभन्ते हीनानि ब्राह्मणोत्तमैः॥
en: Cities adorned with walls and gates and palaces lose their beauty if they are not inhabited by Brahmanas.

sn: वेदाढ्या वृत्तसम्पन्ना ज्ञानवन्तस्तपस्विनः। यत्र तिष्ठति वै विप्रास्तन्नाम नगरं नृप॥
en: O king, that is really a city in which live Brahmanas learned in the Vedas, who duly observe the duties of their order and who possess learning and ascetic merit.

sn: व्रजे वाप्यथवारण्ये यत्र सन्ति बहुश्रुताः। तत् तन्नगरमित्याहुः पार्थ तीर्थं च तद् भवेत्॥
en: O son of Pritha, whether it be a forest or a pasture ground where learned Brahmanas live is called a city. It is also a Tirtha.

sn: रक्षितारं च राजानं ब्राह्मणं च तपस्विनम्। अभिगम्याभिपूज्याथ सद्यः पापात् प्रमुच्यते॥
en: By going to a king who protects (his subjects) and to a Brahmana who possesses ascetic merits and also by worshipping them both, one may be immediately cleansed off all his sins.

sn: पुण्यतीर्थाभिषेकं च पवित्राणां च कीर्तनम्। सद्भिः सम्भाषणं चैव प्रशस्तं कीर्त्यते बुधैः॥
en: The learned men have said that ablutions in the sacred Tirthas, recitations of the names of holy ones and conversations with the good and the virtuous are all praiseworthy acts.

sn: साधुसङ्गमपूतेन वाक्सुभाषितवारिणा। पवित्रीकृतमात्मानं सन्तो मन्यन्ति नित्यशः॥
en: Those that are virtuous and honest always consider themselves sanctified by the holy companionship of persons like themselves and also by the water of pure and sacred conversation.

sn: त्रिदण्डधारणं मौनं जटाभारोऽथ मुण्डनम्। वल्कलाजिन संवेष्टं व्रतचर्याभिषेचनम्॥ अग्निहोत्रं वने वासः शरीरपरिशोषणम्। सर्वाण्येतानि मिथ्या स्युर्यदि भावो न निर्मलः॥
en: Carrying of the three stays, the vow of silence, matted locks (on head), shaving of the head, wearing barks and deer skins, observing vows, practicing ablutions, worshipping of fire and living in the forest emaciating the body, all these are useless to one if his heart be not pure.

sn: न दुष्करमनाशित्वं सुकर ह्यशनं विना। विशुद्धिं चक्षुरादीनां षण्णामिन्द्रियगामिनाम्॥
en: O king of kings, the indulgence of the six senses is (very) easy if purity be not its aim. Abstinence is itself difficult to acquire and it is more so if purity be not its aim. Among all the senses mind is the most dangerous.

sn: विकारि तेषां राजेन्द्र सुदुष्करकरं मनः। ये पापानि न कुर्वन्ति मनोवाक्कर्मबुद्धिभिः। ते तपन्ति महात्मानो न शरीरस्य शोषणम्॥
en: These high-souled, men who do not commit sin in word, in deed, in heart or in soul, are said (really) to perform asceticism; but not those who make their bodies emaciated by fasts and penances.

sn: न ज्ञातिभ्यो दया यस्य शुक्लदेहोऽविकल्मषः। हिंसा सा तपसस्तस्य नानाशित्वं तपः स्मृतम्॥
en: He who has no feeling of kindness for his relatives even if his body be pure cannot be free from sin. That hard-heartedness of his mind is his great enemy to asceticism.

sn: तिष्ठन् गृहे चैव मुनिर्नित्यं शुचिरलंकृतः। यावज्जीवं दयावांश्च सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते॥
en: He who is always pure, who is endued with virtue and who practice virtue all his life, even if he leads a domestic life, is a (real) Rishi. He is freed from all sins.

sn: न हि पापानि कर्माणि शुद्ध्यन्त्यनशनादिभिः। सीदत्यनशनादेव मांसशोणितलेपनः॥
en: Fasts and other penances, however they may weaken and dry up the body which is made of flesh and blood, cannot destroy sins.

sn: अज्ञातं कर्म कृत्वा च क्लेशो नान्यत् प्रहीयते। नाग्निर्दहति कर्माणि भावशून्यस्य देहिनः॥
en: The man whose heart is without holiness suffers torture by undergoing penances only being ignorant of their meaning. He is never freed from sins of such acts. The fire he worships does not consume his sins.

sn: पुण्यादेव प्रव्रजन्ति शुद्ध्यन्त्यनशनानि च। न मूलफलभक्षित्वान्न मौनान्नानिलाशनात्॥ शिरसो मुण्डनाद् वापि न स्थानकुटिकासनात्। न जटाधारणाद् वापि न तु स्थण्डिलशय्यया॥ नित्यं ह्यनशनाद् वापि नाग्निशुश्रूषणादपि। न चोदकप्रवेशेन न च क्षमाशयनादपि॥
en: Through holiness and virtue alone men can go to the regions of bliss and their vows and fasts can become efficacious. Living on fruits and roots, observing the vow of silence, living on air, shaving one's head, abandoning a fixed home, having matted locks on head, lying under the sky, observing daily fasts, worshipping the fire, bathing in water and lying on the ground, these alone cannot lead one to heaven.

sn: ज्ञानेन कर्मणा वापि जरामरणमेव च। व्याधयश्च प्रहीयन्ते प्राप्यते चोत्तमं पदम्॥
en: Those only that are endued with holiness succeed by knowledge and by (virtuous) deeds to conquer disease, decrepitude and death and they alone obtain a very high state.

sn: बीजानि ह्यग्निदग्धानि न रोहन्ति पुनर्यथा। ज्ञानदग्धैस्तथा क्लेशैर्नात्मा संयुज्यते पुनः॥
en: As seeds that have been scorched by fire do not produce the plant, so the pains that have been burnt by knowledge cannot affect the soul.

sn: आत्मना विप्रहीणानि काष्ठकुड्योपमानि च। विनश्यन्ति न संदेहः फेनानीव महार्णवे॥
en: The inert body, which is like a block of wood when destitute of soul, is certainly very short-lived like the forth in the ocean.

sn: आत्मानं विन्दते येन सर्वभूतगुहाशयम्। श्लोकेन यदि वार्धेन क्षीणं तस्य प्रयोजनम्॥
en: He who obtains a view of his soul that dwells within every one's body by the help of one or the half of a rhythmic line (of the Vedas) has no need for anything else.

sn: व्यक्षरादभिसंधाय केचिच्छ्लोकपदाङ्कितैः। शतैरन्यैः सहस्रश्च प्रत्ययो मोक्षलक्षणम्॥
en: Some, by obtaining a knowledge of the identity of the supreme soul from but two letters (of the Vedas) and some, from hundreds and thousands of slokas, acquire salvation; for the knowledge of one's identity with the supreme soul is the sure sign of salvation.

sn: नायं लोकोऽस्ति न परो न सुखं संशयात्मनः। ऊचुर्ज्ञानविदो वृद्धाः प्रत्ययो मोक्षलक्षणम्॥
en: The learned old men have said that neither this world, nor that hereafter, nor bliss can come to one who is full of doubts. Faith is the certain sign of salvation.

sn: विदितार्थस्तु वेदानां परिवेद प्रयोजनम्। उद्विजेत् स तु वेदेभ्यो दावाग्नेरिव मानवः॥
en: He who knows the true meaning of the Vedas also understands their true use. He is frightened at the Vedic rites as man at a conflagration.

sn: शुष्कं तर्कं परित्यज्य आश्रयस्व श्रुतिं स्मृतिम्। एकाक्षराभिसम्बद्धं तत्त्वं हेतुभिरिच्छसि। बुद्धिर्न तस्य सिद्ध्येत साधनस्य विपर्ययात्॥
en: Abandoning dry discussion, take to Smriti and Shruti. Seek with the help of your reason the knowledge of the undying one who is without a second. One's search (for a thing) becomes in vain from the defect of means.

sn: वेदपूर्वं वेदितव्यं प्रयत्नात् तद् वै वेदस्तस्य वेदः शरीरम्। वेदस्तत्त्वं तत्समासोपलब्धौ क्लीबस्त्वात्मा तत् स वेद्यस्य वेद्यम्॥
en: Therefore one should carefully try to obtain knowledge by means of the Vedas. The Vedas are the supreme soul, they are his body, they are the truth. The soul, that is bound by the animal organism belonging to a man in whom all the Vedas are manifest, can (only) know Him.

sn: वेदोक्तमायुर्देवानामाशिषश्चैव कर्मणाम्। फलत्यनुयुगं लोके प्रभावश्च शरीरिणाम्॥
en: The existence of the celestials as stated in the Vedas, the efficacy of (religious) acts and the capacity for action of beings furnished with bodies are noticeable in every Yuga.

sn: इन्द्रियाणां प्रसादेन तदेतत् परिवर्जयेत्। तस्मादनशनं दिव्यं निरुद्धेन्द्रियगोचरम्॥
en: Independence from and the annihilation of these are to be sought by means of the purity of the senses. Therefore the suspension of the function of the senses is the true fasting.

sn: तपसा स्वर्गगमनं भोगो दानेन जायते। ज्ञानेन मोक्षो विज्ञेयस्तीर्थस्नानादधक्षयः॥
en: One may obtain heaven by asceticism, one may obtain objects of enjoyments by the practice of charity, one may have his sins all destroyed by bathing in Tirthas, but complete emancipation cannot be obtained without knowledge.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्तस्तु राजेन्द्र प्रत्युवाच महायशाः। भगवन् श्रोतुमिच्छामि प्रधानविधिमुत्तमम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : O king of kings, having been thus addressed, the greatly illustrious (Yudhishthira) replied, "O exalted one, I desire to hear about the rules of charity which is (really) meritorious.

sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच यत् त्वमिच्छसि राजेन्द्र दानधर्मं युधिष्ठिर। इष्टं चेदं सदा मह्यं राजन् गौरवतस्तथा॥
en: Markandeya said : O king of kings, O Yudhishthira, O monarch, the rules of charity which you desire to hear from me are highly valued by him.

sn: शृणु दानरहस्यानि श्रुतिस्मृत्युदितानि च। छायायां करिणः श्राद्धं तत् कर्णपरिवीजिते। दश कल्पायुतानीह न क्षीयेत युधिष्ठिर॥
en: Hear about the mysteries of charity as they have been expounded in the Shrutis and Smritis. O Yudhishthira, he who performs a Shraddha in the conjunction of Gajachhaya at a place fanned by the leaves of an Ashvattha tree enjoys its fruits one hundred thousand Kalpas.

sn: जीवनाय समाक्लिन्नं वसु दत्त्वा महीयते। वैश्यं तु वासयेद् यस्तु सर्वयज्ञैः स इष्टवान्॥
en: O ruler of earth, he who gives food to one who is dying of hunger and he who founds a home of charity with a person to look after it both acquire the fruits of (performing) all sacrifices.

sn: प्रतिस्रोतश्चित्रवाहाः पर्जन्योऽन्नानुसंचरन्। महाधुरि यथा नावा महापापैः प्रमुच्यते॥
en: He who gives away a horse at a Tirtha where the current of the water runs in an opposite direction obtains merits that are inexhaustible. A guest who comes for food is Indra himself. If he is entertained with food, Indra confers on the feeder merits that are inexhaustible. As men cross rivers and seas by boats, so is he saved from all his sins (by giving board to guests).

sn: विप्लवे विप्रदत्तानि दधिमस्त्वक्षयाणि च। पर्वसु द्विगुणं दानमृतौ दशगुणं भवेत्॥
en: Therefore what is given to the Brahmanas produces, like the gift of curds, inexhaustible merits. A gift on a particular festive day produces twice the merit and on a particular season produces ten times the merit.

sn: अयने विषुवे चैव षडशीतिमुखेषु च। चन्द्रसूर्योपरागे च दत्तमक्षयमुच्यते॥
en: And in a particular year produces one hundred times the merit (than gifts made at any other time). A gift made on the last day of the month produces inexhaustible merit. A gift made when the sun is on the solicit points, a gift made on the last day of the sun's path through Ubra, Asris, Gemini, Vrigo and Pisces and a gift made during the eclipses of the sun and the moon produce merits that are inexhaustible.

sn: ऋतुषु दशगुणं वदन्ति दत्तं शतगुणमृत्वयनादिषु ध्रुवम्। र्विषुवति चाक्षयमश्नुते फलम्॥
en: The learned men say that gifts made during the seasons produce merit that is ten times, those made during the change of seasons one hundred times and those made during the day when Rahu is visible one thousand times greater than what is produced at other times. A gift made on the last day of the sun's course though Libra and Aria produces merit that is everlasting.

sn: नाभूमिदो भूमिमश्नाति राजन् नायानदो यानमारुह्य याति। यान् यान् कामान् ब्राह्मणेभ्यो ददाति तांस्तान् कामान् जायमानः स भुङ्क्ते॥
en: O king, no one can enjoy landed property who does not give away lands; no one can drive on cars and conveyances who does not give them away. With whatever, desire one gives away to the Brahmanas, one enjoys the fruition of that gift in the next birth.

sn: अग्नेरपत्यं प्रथमं सुवर्ण भूवैष्णवी सूर्यसुताश्च गावः। लोकास्त्रयस्तेन भवन्ति दत्ता यः काञ्चनं गाश्च महीं च दद्यात्॥
en: Gold has been produced from fire, the earth from Vishnu and the kine from the sun. Therefore he who gives away gold, land and kine obtains all the regions of Agni, Vishnu and the Sun.

sn: परं हि दानान्न बभूव शाश्वत्तं भव्यं त्रिलोके भवते कुतः पुनः। तस्मात् प्रधानं परमं हि दानं वदन्ति लोकेषु विशिष्टबुद्धयः॥
en: There is nothing so everlasting as a gift. Is there any thing in the three worlds that is more auspicious? It is therefore that they who are greatly intelligent say that there is nothing higher in the three worlds than making gifts.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच श्रुत्वा तु राजा राजर्षेरिन्द्रद्युम्नस्य तत् तथा। मार्कण्डेयान्महाभागात् स्वर्गस्य प्रतिपादनम्॥ युधिष्ठिरो महाराज पप्रच्छ भरतर्षभ। मार्कण्डेयं तपोवृद्धं दीर्घायुषमकल्मषम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : O great king, having heard from the highsouled Markandeya the account of the attainment of heaven by the royal sage Indradhyumna, that foremost of the Bharatas, Yudhishthira, again thus asked that sinless great ascetic and long-lived Markandeya.

sn: विदितास्तव धर्मज्ञ देवदानवराक्षसाः। राजवंशाश्च विविधा ऋषिवंशाश्च शाश्वतः॥
en: Yudhishthira said : O virtuous one, you know all the celestials and the Danavas, the Rakshasas, also various royal dynasties and many everlasting dynasties of the Rishis.

sn: न तेऽस्त्यविदितं किञ्चिदस्मॅिल्लोके द्विजोत्तम् कथां वेत्सि मुने दिव्यां मनुष्योरगरक्षसाम्॥ देवगन्धर्वयक्षाणां किन्नराप्सरसां तथा।
en: O foremost of Brahmanas, there is nothing in this world which you do not know. O Rishis, you know also excellent stories of men, of the Nagas, of the Rakshasas, of the celestials, the Gandharvas, the Yakshas, the Kinnaras and the Apsaras.

sn: इदमिच्छाम्यहं श्रोतुं तत्त्वेन द्विजसत्तम॥ कुवलाश्व इति ख्यात इक्ष्वाकुरपराजितः। कथं नामविपर्यासाद् धुन्धुमारत्वमागतः॥
en: O foremost of Brahmanas, I desire to hear from you all these accounts. Why did that invincible descendant of Ikshvaku, known by the name of Kuvalashva change and assume another, namely Dhundhumara?

sn: एतदिच्छामि तत्त्वेन ज्ञातुं भार्गवसत्तम। विपर्यस्तं यथा नाम कुवलाश्वस्य धीमतः॥
en: O best of the Bhrigu race, I desire to know in detail why the name of the highly intelligent Kuvalashva underwent a change.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच युधिष्ठिरेणैवमुक्तो मार्कण्डेयो महामुनिः। धौन्धुमारमुपाख्यानं कथयामास भारत॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, having been thus addressed by Yudhishthira, the great Rishi Markandeya narrated the story of Dhundhumara.

sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच हन्त ते कथयिष्यामि शृणु राजन् युधिष्ठिर। धर्मिष्ठमिदमाख्यानं धुन्धुमारस्य तच्छृणु॥
en: Markandeya said : O king Yudhishthira, I shall tell you all. Listen to me. The story of Dhundhumara is a moral story, hear it.

sn: यथा स राजा इक्ष्वाकुः कुवलाश्वो महीपतिः। धुन्धुमारत्वमगमत् तच्छृणुष्व महीपते॥
en: O ruler of earth, hear why the royal sage Kuvalashva of the race of Ikshvaku came to be known as Dhundhumara.

sn: महर्षिर्विश्रुतस्तात उत्तङ्क इति भारत। मरुधन्वसु रम्येषु आश्रमस्तस्य कौरव॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, O child, there was a celebrated great Rishi named Uttanka. He had his hermitage in a charming forest.

sn: उत्तङ्कस्तु महाराज तपोऽतप्यत् सुदुश्चरम्। आरिराधयिषुर्विष्णुं बहून् वर्षगणान् विभुः॥
en: O great king, Uttanka performed serverest asceticism. In order to secure the grace of Vishnu that lord (Uttanka) performed that severest penance for many hundreds of years.

sn: तस्य प्रीतः स भगवान् साक्षाद् दर्शनमेयिवान्। दृष्ट्वैव चर्षिः प्रह्वस्तं तुष्टाव विविधैः स्तवैः॥
en: Being gratified with him that exalted deity (Vishnu) appeared before him in his embodied form. As soon as the Rishi saw him, he gratified him in all humility and with many hymns.

sn: उत्तङ्कं उवाच त्वया देवा प्रजाः सर्वाः ससुरासुरमानवाः। स्थावराणि च भूतानि जङ्गमानि तथैव च।॥
en: Uttanka said: O god, all mobile and immobile creatures with the celestial, the Asuras and the humanbeings have been all created by you.

sn: ब्रह्म वेदाश्च वेद्यं च त्वया सृष्टं महाद्युते। शिरस्ते गगनं देव नेत्रे शशिदिवाकरौ॥
en: O greatly effulgent one, Brahma himself, the Vedas and all things that are capable of being known, have been all created by you. O lord, the sky is your head and the sun and the moon are your eyes.

sn: निःश्वासः पवनश्चापि तेजोऽग्निश्च तवाच्युत। बाहवस्ते दिशः सर्वाः कुक्षिश्चापि महार्णवः॥
en: O undeteriorating one, the winds are your breaths, the fire is your splendour, the directions are your arms and the great ocean is your stomach.

sn: ऊरू ते पर्वता देव खं नाभिर्मधुसूदन। पादौ ते पृथिवी देवी रोमाण्योषधयस्तथा॥
en: O god, O slayer of Madhu, the hills and the mountains are your thighs, the atmosphere is your hips, the goddess earth is your feet and the plants are the down of your body.

sn: इन्द्रसोमाग्निवरुणा देवासुरमहोरगाः। प्रह्वास्त्वामुपतिष्ठन्ति स्तुवन्तो विविधैः स्तवैः॥
en: Indra, Soma, Agni and Varuna, the celestial, the Asuras and the great Nagas, all wait upon you and adore you with various hymns.

sn: त्वया व्याप्तानि सर्वाणि भूतानि भुवनेश्वर। योगिनः सुमहावीर्याः स्तुवन्ति त्वां महर्षयः॥
en: O lord of earth all created things are pervaded by you. The great Rishis and the greatly effulgent Yogis all adore you with hymns.

sn: त्वयि तुष्टे जगत् स्वास्थ्यं त्वयि क्रुद्ध महद् भयम्। भयानामपनेतासि त्वमेकः पुरुषोत्तम।॥
en: O foremost of men, when you are pleased the universe enjoys peace; when you are angry, a great fear pervades all. You are the only great dispeller of all fears; you are the supreme one.

sn: देवानां मानुषाणां च सर्वभूतसुखावहः। त्रिभिर्विक्रमणैर्देव त्रयो लोकास्त्वया हृताः॥
en: O god, you are the cause of happiness of both the celestials and the human beings. By your three steps you covered all the three worlds.

sn: असुराणां समृद्धानां विनाशश्च त्वया कृतः। तव विक्रमणैर्देवा निर्वाणमगमन् परम्॥
en: It was you who destroyed the Asuras when they were in their great affluence. Through your prowess the celestials obtained peace and happiness.

sn: पराभूताश्च दैत्येन्द्रास्त्वयि क्रुद्धे महाद्युते। त्वं हि कर्ता विकर्ता च भूतानामिह सर्वशः॥ आराधयित्वा त्वां देवाः सुखमेधन्ति सर्वशः।
en: O greatly effulgent one, it was your anger that vanquished the great Daitya chiefs. You are the creator, you are the destroyer of all the creatures of this world. Adoring you, the celestials have obtained happiness and bliss.”

sn: एवं स्तुतो हृषीकेश उत्तङ्केन महात्मना॥ उत्तङ्कमब्रवीद् विष्णुः प्रीतस्तेऽहं वरं वृणु।
en: There was Hrishikesha (Vishnu) praised by the high-souled Uttanka. Vishnu then thus spoke to Uttanka, “I am gratified, Ask for a boon."

sn: उत्तङ्क उवाच पर्याप्तो मे वरो ह्येष यदहं दृष्टवान् हरिम्॥ पुरुषं शाश्वतं दिव्यं स्रष्टारं जगतः प्रभुम्।
en: (Uttanka said), “It is (already) a great boon to me that you have become visible to me, you who are Hari, the eternal being, the celestials creator, the lord of the universe."

sn: विष्णुरुवाच प्रीतस्तेऽहमलौल्येन भक्त्या तव च सत्तम॥ अवश्यं हि त्वया ब्रह्मन् मत्तो चाह्यो वरो द्विज।
en: Vishnu said, "O excellent one. I am pleased with your this littleness of desire and great devotion. O Brahmana, O twice-born one, you should certainly accept some boon from me."

sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच एवं स छन्द्यमानस्तु वरेण हरिणा तदा॥ उत्तङ्कः प्राञ्जलिर्ववे वरं भरतसत्तम।
en: Thus requested by Hari to ask for a boon, O best of the Bharata race, Uttanka with joined hands asked for a boon.

sn: यदि मे भगवन् प्रीतः पुण्डरीकनिभेक्षण॥ धर्मे सत्ये दमे चैव बुद्धिर्भवतु मे सदा। अभ्यासश्च भवेद् भक्त्या त्वयि नित्यं ममेश्वर॥
en: "O lotus-eyed deity, if your exalted self is pleased with me, O lord, then let my heart be always devoted to virtue, truth and contentment. Let my mind be always devoted to you."

sn: श्रीभगवानुवाच सर्वमेतद्धि भविता मत्प्रसादात् तव द्विज। प्रतिभास्यति योगश्च येन युक्तो दिवौकसाम्॥ त्रयाणामपि लोकानां महत् कार्यं करिष्यसि।
en: (The deity replied), “O Brahmana, all this will happen to you through my favour. A Yoga will be manifest in you. Through its power you will perform a great act for the dwellers of heaven as also for the three worlds.

sn: उत्सादनार्थं लोकानां धुन्धुर्नाम महासुरः॥ तपस्यति तपो घोरं शृणु यस्तं हनिष्यति।
en: A great Asura, named Dhundhu, is now undergoing severe austerities in order to destroy the world. Hear who will kill him.

sn: राजा हि वीर्यवांस्तात इक्ष्वाकुरपराजितः॥ बृहदश्व इति ख्यातो भविष्यति महीपतिः। तस्य पुत्रः शुचिर्दान्तः कुवलाश्व इति श्रुतः॥
en: O child, a mighty and invincible king of the race of Ikshvaku, known by the name of Brihadashva, will be the ruler over earth. His son will be very illustrious, self-controlled and holy; he will be known by the name of Kuvalashva.

sn: स योगबलमास्थाय मामकं पार्थिवोत्तमः। शासनात् तव विप्रर्षे धुन्धुमारो भविष्यति। एवमुक्त्वा तु तं विप्रं विष्णुरन्तरधीयत॥
en: O foremost of Brahmanas, that best of kings will be endued with Yoga power derived from me. Commanded by you he will be the slayer of Dhundhu.” Having said this to that Brahmana Vishnu disappeared.

sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच इक्ष्वाको संस्थिते राजन् शशादः पृथिवीमिमाम्। प्राप्तः परमधर्मात्मा सोऽयोध्यायां नृपोऽभवत्॥
en: Markandeya said : O king, when Ikshvaku died, the greatly virtuous Shashada, becoming the king of Ayodhya began to rule over this earth.

sn: शशादस्य तु दायादः ककुत्स्थो नाम वीर्यवान्। अनेनाश्चापि काकुत्स्थः पृथुश्चानेनसः सुतः॥
en: Shashada had a powerful son, named Kakutstha. Kakutstha had a son named Anenas. Anenas had a son named Prithu.

sn: विष्वगश्वः पृथोः पुत्रस्तस्मादद्रिश्च जज्ञिवान्। अद्रेश्च युवनाश्वस्तु श्रावस्तस्यात्मजोऽभवत्॥
en: Prithu had a son named Vishvagashva and Vishvagashva begot a son, named Adri. Adri had a son called Yuvanashva and Yuvanashva begot Shravasta.

sn: तस्य श्रावस्तको ज्ञेयः श्रावस्ती येन निर्मिता। श्रावस्तकस्य दायादो बृहदश्वो महाबलः॥
en: From this Shravasta, the city called Shravasti was founded. The son of Shravasta was the greatly powerful Brihadashva.

sn: बृहदश्वस्य दायादः कुवलाश्व इति स्मृतः। कुवलाश्वस्य पुत्राणां सहस्राण्येकविंशतिः॥
en: The son of Brihadashva was known by the name Kuvalashva; Kuvalashva had twenty one thousand sons.

sn: सर्वे विद्यासु निष्णाता बलवन्तो दुरासदाः। कुवलाश्वश्च पितृतो गुणैरभ्यधिकोऽभवत्॥
en: All these sons were powerful and fierce, but they were learned. Kuvalashva became superior to his father in all qualifications.

sn: समये तं पिता राज्ये बृहदश्वोऽभ्यषेचयत्। कुवलाश्वं महाराज शूरमुत्तमधार्मिकम्॥
en: O great king, in due time his father Brihadashva installed that foremost of heroes and virtuous men, Kuvalashva, on the throne.

sn: पुत्रसंक्रामितश्रीस्तु बृहदश्वो महीपतिः। जगाम तपसे धीमांस्तपोवनममित्रहा॥
en: Having thus made over the royal dignity to his son, that ruler of earth, that chastiser of foes and the greatly intelligent Brihadashva retired into a forest to perform asceticism.

sn: अथ शुश्राव राजर्षि तमुत्तको नराधिप। वनं सम्प्रस्थितं राजन् बृहदश्वं द्विजोत्तमः॥
en: O rulers of men, O king, when the royal sage Brihadashva was about to go away into the forest, that best of Brahmanas, Uttanka, heard of it.

sn: तमुत्तको महातेजाः सर्वास्त्रविदुषां वरम्। न्यवारयदमेयात्मा समासाद्य नरोत्तमम्॥
en: The greatly effulgent and the high-souled Uttanka came to that foremost of all wielder of arms, that best of men, (Brihadashva) and asked him not to do it.

sn: उत्तङ्क उवाच भवता रक्षणं कार्यं तत् तावत् कर्तुमर्हसि। निरुद्विग्ना वयं राजंस्त्वत्प्रसादाद् भवेमहि॥
en: Uttanka said: O king, your duty is to protect men. You should perform your that duty. Let us be freed from all anxieties through your favour.

sn: त्वया हि पृथिवी राजन् रक्ष्यमाणा महात्मना। भविष्यति निरुद्विग्ना नारण्यं गन्तुमर्हसि॥
en: O king, the earth, being protected by your august self, will be freed from all anxieties. Therefore you should not retire into the forest.

sn: पालने हि महान् धर्मः प्रजानामिह दृश्यते। न तथा दृश्यतेऽरण्ये माभूत् ते बुद्धिरीदृशी॥
en: Great merit is the fruit of protecting men in this world. Such merit can never be acquired in a forest. Therefore, let not your heart have such an inclination

sn: ईदृशो न हि राजेन्द्र धर्मः क्वचन दृश्यते। प्रजानां पालने यो वै पुरा राजर्षिभिः कृतः॥
en: O king of kings, such a (great) merit is not seen in anything else as it is seen in the protection of men as done by the royal sages in the days of yore.

sn: रक्षितव्याः प्रजा राज्ञा तास्त्वं रक्षितुमर्हसि। निरुद्विग्नस्तपश्चर्तुं न हि शक्नोमि पार्थिव॥
en: O ruler of earth, the subjects should (always) be protected by the kings; you should therefore protect your people. I shall not be able to perform asceticism in peace.

sn: ममाश्रमसमीपे वै समेषु मरुधन्वसु। समुद्रो बालुकापूर्ण उज्जालक इति स्मृतः॥
en: Near my hermitage there is a large desert, a sea of sand, known by the name of Ujjalaka. It occupies a level country and it has no water.

sn: बहुयोजनविस्तीर्णो बहुयोजनमायतः। तत्र रौद्रो दानवेन्द्रो महावीर्यपराक्रमः॥ मधुकैटभयोः पुत्रो धुन्धुर्नाम सुदारुणः। अन्तर्भूमिगतो राजन् वसत्यमितविक्रमः॥
en: It extends many yojanas in length and breadth. There lives a fearful and greatly powerful Danava chief. He is the fearful son of Madhukaitabha and his name is Dhundhu. O king, this immeasurably powerful one lives underneath the ground.

sn: तं निहत्य महाराज वनं त्वं गन्तुमर्हसि। शेते लोकविनाशाय तप आस्थाय दारुणम्॥ त्रिदशानां विनाशाय लोकानां चापि पार्थिव।
en: O great king, kill him and then retire into the forest. He is now engaged in the severe penances with the intention of destroying the world and as well as the celestials.

sn: अवध्यो दैवतानां हि दैत्यानामथ रक्षसाम्॥ नागानामथ यक्षाणां गन्धर्वाणां च सर्वशः। अवाप्य स वरं राजन् सर्वलोकपितामहात्॥
en: O king, he has become incapable of being killed by the celestials, the Daityas, the Rakshasas, the Nagas, the Yakshas and the Gandharvas for his obtaining. O king, a boon from the Grandsire of all creatures.

sn: तं विनाशय भद्रं ते मा ते बुद्धिरतोऽन्यथा। प्राप्स्यसे महतीं कीर्ति शाश्वतीमव्ययां ध्रुवाम्॥
en: Kill him and be blessed. Let not your heart be led away to any other course. By killing him you will certainly achieve a great thing and also eternal and undying fame.

sn: क्रूरस्य तस्य स्वपतो बालुकान्तर्हितस्य च। संवत्सरस्य पर्यन्ते निःश्वासः सम्प्रवर्तते।॥ यदा तदा भूश्चलति सशैलवनकानना। तस्य निःश्वासवातेन रज उद्भूयते महत्॥ आदित्यपथमाश्रित्य सप्ताहं भूमिकम्पनम्। सविस्फुलिङ्गं सज्वालं धूममिश्रं सुदारुणम्॥ तेन राजन् न शक्नोमि तस्मिन् स्थातुं स्व आश्रमे तं विनाशय राजेन्द्र लोकानां हितकाम्यया॥
en: O king, when at the end of every year that wicked Asura, lying covered with sands, wakes up and begins to breathe, then the whole earth with her mountains, forests and woods begins to tremble. His breath raises up clouds of sands and covers the very sun. For seven days continually the earth trembles and sparks and flames of fire mixed with smoke spread all over the ground. For all this, O king, I cannot enjoy peace in my hermitage. O king of kings, kill him therefore for the good of the world.

sn: लोकाः स्वस्था भविष्यन्ति तस्मिन् विनिहतेऽसुरे त्वं हि तस्य विनाशाय पर्याप्त इति मे मतिः॥
en: When this Asura will be killed, the three worlds will be in peace and happiness. My opinion is that you are quite competent to kill him.

sn: तेजसा तव तेजश्च विष्णुराप्याययिष्यति। विष्णुना च वरो दत्तः पूर्वं मम महीपते॥ यस्तं महासुरं रौद्रं वधिष्यति महीपतिः। तेजस्तं वैष्णवमिति प्रवेक्ष्यति दुरासदम्॥
en: Your energy will be increased by that of Vishnu, the ruler of earth. A boon was granted by Vishnu in the days of yore. Namely that he who will kill this fearful and great Asura would be pervaded by the matchless energy of Vishnu himself.

sn: तत् तेजस्त्वं समाधाय राजेन्द्र भुवि दुःसहम्। तं निषूदय राजेन्द्र दैत्यं रौद्रपराक्रमम्॥
en: O king of kings, bearing that (Vishnu) energy which is hardly to be borne by any other on earth, kill this Daitya of fearful power.

sn: न हि धुन्धुर्महातेजास्तेजसाल्पेन शक्यते। निर्दग्धुं पृथिवीपाल स हि वर्षशतैरपि॥
en: The greatly powerful Dhundhu, O ruler of earth, is incapable of being killed by any other man, even if that man tries for one hundred years to kill him.

sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच स एवमुक्तो राजर्षिरुत्तङ्केनापराजितः। उत्तवं कौरवश्रेष्ठ कृताञ्जलिरथाब्रवीत्॥
en: Markandeya said : Having been thus addressed by Uttanka, O foremost of the Kurus, that invincible royal sage spoke thus to Uttanka with joined hands.

sn: न तेऽभिगमनं ब्रह्मन् मोघमेतद् भविष्यति। पुत्रो ममायं भगवन् कुवलाश्व इति स्मृतः॥ धृतिमान् क्षिप्रकारी च वीर्येणाप्रतिमो भुवि।
en: "O Brahmana, your this visit will not be in vain. O holy one, my this son, known by the name of Kuvalashva, is both active and steady; and he is also matchless in prowess on earth.

sn: प्रियं च ते सर्वमेतत् करिष्यति न संशयः॥ पुत्रैः परिवृतः सर्वैः शूरैः परिघबाहुभिः। विसर्जयस्व मां ब्रह्मन् न्यस्तशस्त्रोऽस्मि साम्प्रतम्॥
en: He will certainly accomplish that which is pleasing to you. Surrounding by his brave sons all of whom possess arms like maces. O Brahmana, give me leave to depart, for I have now abandoned all weapons."

sn: तथास्त्विति च तेनोक्तो मुनिनामिततेजसा। स तमादिश्य तनयमुत्तङ्काय महात्मने॥ क्रियतामिति राजर्षिर्जगाम वनमुत्तमम्।
en: Having been thus addressed by him, that immeasurably, effulgent Rishi said, "So be it." And the royal sage, after ordering his son to obey the command of the high-souled Uttanka, retired into an excellent forest.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच क एष भगवन् दैत्यो महावीर्यस्तपोधन॥ कस्य पुत्रोऽथ नप्ता वा एतदिच्छामि वेदितुम्।
en: Yudhishthira said: O exalted one, O great ascetic, who was this greatly powerful Daitya? Whose son and whose grandson was he? I desire to know all this.

sn: एवं महाबलो दैत्यो न श्रुतो मे तपोधन॥ एतदिच्छामि भगवन् याथातथ्येन वेदितुम्। सर्वमेव महाप्राज्ञ विस्तरेण तपोधन॥
en: O great ascetic, I never heard of this greatly powerful Daitya. O exalted Rishi, O greatly wise one, O great ascetic, I desire to know all this in detail with all its true particulars.

sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच शृणु राजन्निदं सर्वं यथावृत्तं नराधिप। कथ्यमानं महाप्राज्ञ विस्तरेण यथातथम्॥
en: Markandeya said : O king, O ruler of men, O greatly wise one, hear all this as I narrate it in detail with all its true particulars.

sn: एकार्णवे तदा लोके नष्टे स्थावरजङ्गमे। प्रणष्टेषु च भूतेषु सर्वेषु भरतर्षभ॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, when the world became one great ocean and all mobile and immobile creatures were killed,

sn: प्रभवं लोककर्तारं विष्णुं शाश्वतमव्ययम्। यमाहुर्मुनयः सिद्धाः सर्वलोकमहेश्वरम्॥ सुष्वाप भगवान् विष्णुरप्सु योगत एव सः। नागस्य भोगे महति शेषस्यामिततेजसः॥
en: He who is the source and creator of the universe, the eternal and undeteriorating Vishnu, whom the Rishis endued with ascetic success call the lord of all the worlds, that being of great sanctity, then lay in Yoga sleep on the wide hood of the snake Shesha of immeasurably energy.

sn: लोककर्ता महाभाग भगवानच्युतो हरिः। नागभोगेन महता परिरभ्य महीमिमाम्॥
en: The creator of the universe, the greatly blessed one, the exalted and undeteriorating Hari, lay on the hood of the snake encircling the whole world.

sn: स्वपतस्तस्य देवस्य पद्मं सूर्यसमप्रभम्। नाभ्यां विनिःसृतं दिव्यं तत्रोत्पन्नः पितामहः॥ साक्षाल्लोकगुरुर्ब्रह्मा पद्मे सूर्यसमप्रभः।
en: When he (thus) lay asleep, a lotus as beautiful and effulgent as the sun sprang from his navel. From the sun-like effulgent lotus sprang the Grandsire.

sn: चतुर्वेदश्चतुर्मूर्तिस्तथैव च चतुर्मुखः॥ स्वप्रभावाद् दुराधर्षो महाबलपराक्रमः।
en: That lord of the worlds, Brahma, who is the four Vedas, who has four forms and four faces and who possesses great strength and prowess.

sn: कस्यचित् त्वथ कालस्य दानवौ वीर्यवत्तमौ॥ मधुश्च कैटभश्चैव दृष्टवन्तौ हरिं प्रभुम्। शयानं शयने दिव्ये नागभोगे महाद्युतिम्॥ बहुयोजनविस्तीर्णे बहुयोजनमायते। किरीटकौस्तुभधरं पीतकौशेयवाससम्॥ दीप्यमानं श्रिया राजंस्तेजसा वपुषा तथा। सहस्रसूर्यप्रतिममद्भुतोपमदर्शनम्॥
en: Once upon a time the two greatly powerful Danavas, Madhu and Kaitabha saw the lord Hari of great effulgence adorned with a crown and the Kaustubha gem and clad in purple silk robe, lying stretched for many yojanas on that excellent celestials bed furnished by the hood of the snake which itself lay extended far and wide blazing in its own beauty and lustre which resembled like one thousand suns concentrated in one mass.

sn: विस्मयः सुमहानासीन्मधुकैटभयोस्तथा। दृष्ट्वा पितामहं चापि पद्म पद्मनिभेक्षणम्॥ वित्रासयेतामथ तौ ब्रह्माणममितौजसम्। वित्रस्यमानो बहुशो ब्रह्मा ताभ्यां महायशाः॥ अकम्पयत् पद्मनालं ततोऽबुध्यत केशवः। अथापश्यत गोविन्दो दानवौ वीर्यवत्तरौ॥
en: Madhu and Kaitabha became greatly astonished on seeing the lotus-eyed Grandsire sitting on the lotus. They then began to terrify Brahma of immeasurable prowess. The illustrious Brahma, frightened by them, began to tremble on his seat. At his trembling, the stalk of the lotus began to tremble and thus Keshava awoke and he saw those two greatly effulgent Danavas.

sn: दृष्ट्वा तावब्रवीद् देवः स्वागतं वां महाबलौ। ददामि वां वरं श्रेष्ठं प्रीतिमर्हि मम जायते॥
en: Seeing them the deity said to them, "O mighty heroes, be welcome. I am gratified with you. I shall therefore give you some excellent boons."

sn: तौ प्रहस्य हृषीकेशं महादौ महाबलौ। प्रत्यबूतां महाराज सहितौ मधुसूदनम्॥
en: O great king, those two greatly proud and powerful Danavas then laughingly replied to Hrishikesha, that slayer of Madhu,

sn: आवां वरय देव त्वं वरदौ स्वः सुरोत्तम। दातारौ स्वो वरं तुभ्यं तद् ब्रवीह्यविचारयन्॥
en: "O deity, O foremost of the celestials, ask some boons from us. We are inclined to grant you some boons that you think proper.

sn: श्रीभगवानुवाच प्रतिगृहणे वरं वीरावीप्सितश्च वरो मम। युवां हि वीर्यसम्पन्नौ न वामस्ति समः पुमान्॥ वध्यत्वमुपगच्छेतां मम सत्यपराक्रमौ। एतदिच्छाम्यहं कामं प्राप्तुं लोकहिताय वै॥
en: The Deity said: I shall accept a boon from you. There is a boon which I desire (to have from you). Both of you are indeed endued with very great prowess. There is none equal to you (on earth). O heroes of matchless prowess, allow yourselves to be killed by me. This is what I desire to do for the good of the world.

sn: मधुकैटभावूचतुः अनृतं नोक्तपूर्वं नौ स्वैरेष्वपि कुतोऽन्यथा। सत्ये धर्मे च निरतौ विद्ध्यावां पुरुषोत्तम॥
en: Madhu Kaitabha said: foremost of Purushas, we have never before spoken an untruth, not even in joke, what to speak of the other occasions? Know that we are always firm in truth and morality.

sn: बले रूपे च शौर्ये च न शमे च समोऽस्ति नौ। धर्मे तपसि दाने च शीलसत्त्वदमेषु च॥
en: There is none equal to us in strength, in appearance, in beauty, in virtue, in asceticism, in charity, in conduct, in goodness and in selfcontrol.

sn: उपप्लवो महानस्मानुपावर्तत केशव। उक्तं प्रतिकुरुष्व त्वं कालो हि दुरतिक्रमः॥
en: O Keshava, a great danger has overtaken us. Therefore do what you say. None can prevail over Time.

sn: आवामिच्छावहे देव कृतमेकं त्वया विभो। अनावृतेऽस्मिन्नाकाशे वधं सुरवरोत्तम॥
en: O deity, O lord, O foremost of all the celestials, there is one thing, however, which we want to be done by you. You must kill us at a place which is absolutely uncovered.

sn: पुत्रत्वमधिगच्छाव तव चापि सुलोचन। वर एष वृतो देव तद् विद्धि सुरसत्तम॥ अनृतं मा भवेद् देव यद्धि नौ संश्रुतं तदा।
en: O exalted one, O deity, O divine being, we desire to become your sons. Know this is the boon that we desire to get from you. Let not that which you spoke first be false.

sn: श्रीभगवानुवाच बाढमेवं करिष्यामि सर्वमेतद् भविष्यति॥
en: The Deity said : Be it so. I shall do as you desire. Every thing will happen as you wish.

sn: स विचिन्त्याथ गोविन्दो नापश्यद् यदनावृतम्। अवकाशं पृथिव्यां वा दिवि वा मधुसूदनः॥ स्वकावनावृतावूरू दृष्ट्वा देववरस्तदा। मधुकैटभयो राजन् शिरसी मधुसूदनः। चक्रेण शितधारेण न्यकृन्तत महायशाः॥
en: Then Govinda (Vishnu) reflected; but he could not find any uncovered place. When the slayer of Madhu could not find such a place, either in heaven or on carth, that foremost of the celestials then saw. his thighs absolutely uncovered. And there, ( king, the slayer of Madhu, cut off the heads of Madhu and Kaitabha with his sharp discus.

sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच धुन्धुर्नाम महाराज तयोः पुत्रो महाद्युतिः। स तपोऽतप्यत महन्महावीर्यपराक्रमः॥
en: Markandeya said : great monarch, they (Madhu and Kaitabha) had a son, Dhundhu by name, who was most illustrious and possessed of immense power and energy; and who also observed severe asceticism.

sn: अतिष्ठदेकपादेन कृशो धमनिसंततः। तस्मै ब्रह्मा ददौ प्रीतो वरं वव्रे स च प्रभुम्॥
en: He remained for a time, standing on one leg; and became lean as the skeleton. Much pleased Brahmana granted him a boon, which he asked of the Lord in the following way:

sn: देवदानवयक्षाणां सर्पगन्धर्वरक्षसाम्। अवध्योऽहं भवेयं च वर एष वृतो मया।॥
en: "Such a boon is asked by me, as will render me incapable of being killed by either the celestials, the Danavas the Yakshas or by the snakes, Gandharvas or Rakshasas.'

sn: एवं भवतु गच्छेति तमुवाच पितामहः। स एवमुक्तस्तत्पादौ मूर्धा स्पृश्य जगाम ह॥
en: The grandsire answered him, saying, "So be it and do you go away". Having been thus addressed, he touched his feet by his head and went away.

sn: स तु धुन्धुर्वरं लब्वा महावीर्यपराक्रमः। अनुस्मरन् पितृवधं दुतं विष्णुमुपागमत्॥
en: The most courageous and energetic Dhundhu, too, speedily advanced to Vishnu, after gaining this boon and also recollecting the murder of his father (by that god). at

sn: स तु देवान् सगन्धर्वान् जित्वा धुन्धुरमर्षणः। बबाध सर्वानसकृद् विष्णुं देवांश्च वै भृशम्॥
en: The unconquerable Dhundhu first defeated all the celestials as well as the Gandharvas; and then he began to cruelly oppress the other celestials with Vishnu at their head.

sn: समुद्रे बालुकापूर्णे उज्जालक इति स्मृते। आगम्य च स दुष्टात्मा तं देशं भरतर्षभ।॥ बाधते स्म परं शक्त्या तमुत्तकाश्रमं विभो। अन्तर्भूमिगतस्तत्र बालुकान्तर्हितस्तथा॥
en: O foremost of the Bharata race, that wickedminded one came to a country where there was an ocean of sands, known by the name of Ujjalaka. O illustrious one, he, lying in an under-ground cave excavated in the bed of sands, greatly harassed the asylum of Uttanka.

sn: मधुकैटभयोः पुत्रो धुन्धुर्भीमपराक्रमः। शेते लोकविनाशाय तपोबलमुपाश्रितः॥
en: The fearfully powerful son of Madhu and Kaitabha, Dhundhu, laid himself there (in that cave), performing severe religious austerities, with a view to destroy the three worlds.

sn: उत्तङ्कस्याश्रमाभ्याशे निःश्वसन् पावकार्चिषः। एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु राजा सबलवाहनः॥ उत्तङ्कविप्रसहितः : कुवलाश्वो महीपतिः। पुत्रैः सह महीपालः प्रययौ भरतर्षभ॥
en: While, at this time, he was taking his breath, resting very close to the asylum of the Uttanka, who was like the fire in effulgence, then O ruler of the earth, O foremost of the Bharata race, the great king Kuvalashva departed to that country with the Brahmanas, Uttanka and all his sons.

sn: सहस्ररेकविंशत्या पुत्राणामरिमर्दनः। कुवलाश्वो नरपतिरन्वितो बलशालिनाम्॥
en: The repressor of enemies, the ruler of men, Kuvalashva was accompanied by the most powerful sons, who were twenty-one thousand in number.

sn: तमाविशत् ततो विष्णुर्भगवांस्तेजसा प्रभुः। उत्तङ्कस्य नियोगेन लोकानां हितकाम्यया।॥
en: Thereupon at the injunction of Uttanka, the omnipotent Lord Vishnu, imparted to him his own energy, with the object of doing good to the three worlds.

sn: तस्मिन् प्रयाते दुर्धर्षे दिवि शब्दो महानभूत्। एष श्रीमानवध्योऽद्य धुन्धुमारो भविष्यति॥
en: When the haughty one was gone away, a loud noise was heard in the heaven, uttering the words-'this invincible hero will this day be the slayer of Dhundhu.'

sn: दिव्यैश्च पुष्पैस्तं देवाः समन्तात् पर्यवारयन्। देवदुन्दुभयश्चापि नेदुः स्वयमनीरिताः॥
en: The celestials showered heaven-grown flowers upon him from the sky; as also the divine kettle-drums played spontaneously without cessation.

sn: शीतश्च वायुः प्रववौ प्रयाणे तस्य धीमतः। विपांसुलां महीं कुर्वन् ववर्ष च सुरेश्वरः॥
en: While that intelligent one was proceeding onwards, cool breezes began to blow and showers were poured forth by the chief of the gods, making the earth free from dusts.

sn: अन्तरिक्षे विमानादि देवतानां युधिष्ठिर। तत्रैव समदृश्यन्त धुन्धुर्यत्र महासुरः॥
en: O Yudhishthira, the cars of the gods were seen on the sky just when the great Asura, Dhundhu, was below the heaven.

sn: कुवलाश्वस्य धुन्धोश्च युद्धकौतूहलान्विताः। देवगन्धर्वसहिताः समवैक्षन् महर्षयः॥
en: Propelled by curiosity the celestials with the Gandharvas, as well as the great sages, beheld from heaven the combat between Kuvalashva and Dhundhu.

sn: नारायणेन कौरव्य तेजसाऽऽप्यायितस्तदा। स गतो नृपतिः क्षिप्रं पुत्रैस्तैः सर्वतो दिशम्॥ अर्णवं खानयामास कुवलाश्वो महीपतिः।
en: O son of the Kuru race, thereupon that ruler of men, supplied with the energy of Narayana went speedily in all directions with all of his sons. Kuvalashva, excavated that sea of sands.

sn: कुवलाश्वस्य पुत्रैश्च तस्मिन् वै बालुकार्णवे॥ सप्तभिर्दिवसैः खात्वा दृष्टो धुन्धुर्महाबलः।
en: While the sons of Kuvalashva were digging that sea, they found out, after seven days, the greatly powerful Dhundhu.

sn: आसीद् घोरं वपुस्तस्य बालुकान्तर्हितं महत्॥ दीप्यमानं यथा सूर्यस्तेजसा भरतर्षभ।
en: O foremost of the Bharata race, the monstrous body of that hero lay in the interior of those sands and shone as the sun in splendour.

sn: ततो धुन्धुर्महाराज दिशमावृत्य पश्चिमाम्॥ सुप्तोऽभूद् राजशार्दूल कालानलसमद्युतिः।
en: Thereupon O great monarch, Dhundhu lay asleep, occupying the whole of the western point of the horizon; and he looked effulgent like the all-destroying fire.

sn: कुवलाश्वस्य पुत्रैस्तु सर्वतः परिवारितः॥ अभिद्रुतः शरैस्तीक्ष्णैर्गदाभिर्मुसलैरपि। पट्टिशैः परियैः प्रासैः खङ्गैच विमलैः शितैः॥ स वध्यमानः संक्रुद्धः समुत्तस्थौ महाबलः। क्रुद्धश्चाभक्षयत् तेषां शस्त्राणि विविधानि च।॥
en: Then the ruler of the earth, and entirely surrounded as he was by all the sons of Kuvalashva. He was also assaulted with the sharp arrows, the maces and clubs, as well as with the axes, iron spikes, shafts and sharp and bright swords. Having been thus wounded, the greatly powerful one rose up in anger; and swallowed up all the various sorts of weapons in great excitement.

sn: आस्याद् वमन् पावकं स संवर्तकसम तदा। तान् सर्वान् नृपतेः पुत्रानदहत् स्वेन तेजसा॥
en: Thereupon he vomited from his mouth the fire, that was like the Samvartaka (appearing at the end of the Yoga); and he burnt the sons of the king by these his own flames.

sn: मुखजेनाग्निना क्रुद्धो लोकानुद्वर्तयन्निव। क्षणेन राजशार्दूल पुरेव कपिलः प्रभुः॥ सगरस्यात्मजान् क्रुद्धस्तदद्भुतमिवाभवत्।
en: Surrounding the three worlds with the fire emitted from his mouth, the wrathful one seemed in a moment to be a miracle like Lord Kapila of old, who consumed the sons of Sagara (by the fire of his wrath).

sn: तेषु क्रोधाग्निदग्धेषु तदा भरतसत्तम॥ तं प्रबुद्धं महात्मानं कुम्भकर्णमिवापरम्। आससाद महातेजाः कुवलाश्वो महीपतिः॥
en: O foremost of the Bharata race, after the sons were thus consumed by the fire of wrath, the ruler of earth, Kuvalashva, endued with great energy, approached that high-souled one (Asura) who, now awake, was like a second Kumbhakarna.

sn: तस्य वारि महाराज सुस्राव बहु देहतः। तदापीय ततस्तेजो राजा वारिमयं नृप॥ योगी योगेन वछि च शमयामास वारिणा।
en: O great king, a current of water flowed copiously from the body of the monarch, who now extinguished those flames, O king, by that stream of water endued with the Yuga prowess, he extinguished the fire by the stream of water flowing from his body.

sn: ब्रह्मास्त्रेण च राजेन्द्र दैत्यं क्रूरपराक्रमम्॥ ददाह भरतश्रेष्ठ सर्वलोकभवाय वै। सोऽस्त्रेण दग्ध्वा राजर्षिः कुवलाश्वो महासुरम्॥ सुरशत्रुममित्रघ्नं त्रैलोक्येश इवापरः।
en: O best of kings he then repressed the evilspirited Daitya by the weapon, called Brahma, with the object of benefiting the three words. O best of the Bharata race, thus having been repressed by that weapon the great Asura, who was the enemy of the gods, as well as the chastiser of all foes, the sage-like king, Kuvalashva became a second chief of the three worlds.

sn: धुन्धोर्वधात् तदा राजा कुवलाश्वो महामनाः॥ धुन्धुमार इति ख्यातो नाम्नाप्रतिरथोऽभवत्।
en: And from that day the lofty-minded king Kuvalashva became known by the name of Dhundhumara and was thought to be unconquerable on account of his slaying Dhundhu.

sn: प्रीतैश्च त्रिदशैः सर्वैमहर्षिसहितैस्तदा॥ वरं वृणीष्वेत्युक्तः स प्राञ्जलिः प्रणतस्तदा। अतीव मुदितो राजन्निदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Thereupon all the celestials as well as the great sages became highly gratified with him. Having been solicited by them to take a boon from them, he folded his hands and bowed down to them; and, O king, being highly delighted, he addressed them, saying,

sn: दद्यां वित्तं द्विजावयेभ्यः शत्रूणां चापि दुर्जयः। सख्यं च विष्णुना मे स्याद् भूतेष्वद्रोह एव च॥
en: 'Grant me the boon that I may give wealth to the best of the Brahmanas and that I may be unconquerable in respect to all enemies; and I may have friendship with Vishnu; and that I may not entertain any animosity against any body.

sn: धर्मे रतिश्च सततं स्वर्गे वासस्तथाक्षयः। तथास्त्विति ततो देवैः प्रीतैरुक्तः स पार्थिवः॥ ऋषिभिश्च सगन्धर्वैरुक्तङ्केन च धीमता। सम्भाष्य चैनं विविधैराशीर्वादैस्ततो नृप॥
en: That I may have heart always turned towards virtue; and also that I may have an everlasting abode in heaven.' Thereupon the celestials, with the sages and Gandharvas, as also with the intelligent 'Uttanka, highly gratified, said to the king "So be it," O monarch, then they also saluted him with various other blessings.

sn: देवा महर्षयश्चापि स्वानि स्थानानि भेजिरे। तस्य पुत्रास्त्रयः शिष्टा युधिष्ठिर तदाभवन्॥
en: The celestials as well as the great sages departed to their respective residences. O Yudhishthira, then the king (Kuvalashva) had still three son left.

sn: दृढाश्वः कपिलाश्वश्च चन्द्राश्वश्चैव भारत। तेभ्यः परम्परा राजनिक्ष्वाकूणां महात्मनाम्॥ वंशस्य सुमहाभाग राज्ञाममिततेजसाम्।
en: O descendant of the Bharata race, they (the sons) were called Dridhashva, Kapilashva and Chandrashva, from whom, O king, has sprung the line of greatly powerful kings belonging to that most illustrious race of Ikshyaku.

sn: एवं स निहतस्तेन कुवलाश्वेन सत्तम॥ धुन्धुर्नाम महादैत्यो मधुकैटभयोः सुतः। कुवलाश्वश्च नृपतिधुन्धुमार इति स्मृतः॥
en: O blessed one, O the most excellent, thus was slain by Kuvalashva. The great Daitya, Dhundhu, the son of Madhu and Kaitabha. The king Kuvalashva, too, came to be known by the name of Dhundhumara.

sn: नाम्ना च गुणसंयुक्तस्तदाप्रभृति सोऽभवत्। एतत् ते सर्वमाख्यातं यन्मां त्वं परिपृच्छसि॥ धौन्धुमारमुपाख्यानं प्रथितं यस्य कर्मणा।
en: By his assuming this appellation, he really became, from that time forward, one of innumerable virtues. Now I have related to you the whole account, which you asked me. By this act of his (Kuvalashva's) the story of Dhundhu's death has become famous.

sn: इदं तु पुण्यमाख्यानं विष्णो:समनुकीर्तनम्॥ शृणुयाद् यः स धर्मात्मा पुत्रवांश्च भवेन्नरः। आयुष्मान् भूतिमांश्चैव श्रुत्वा भवति पर्वसु। न च व्याधिभयं किंचित् प्राप्नोति विगतज्वरः॥
en: For it has been associated with the glory of Vishnu. The person, who listens to this history becomes virtuous; and also father of children; and listening to it on the holy days, he becomes blessed with longevity and good fortune. Becoming delivered from all diseases, he even gets no fear of indisposition.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततो युधिष्ठिरो राजा मार्कण्डेयं महाद्युतिम्। पप्रच्छ भरतश्रेष्ठ धर्मप्रश्नं सुदुर्विदम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : O best of the Bharata race, thereupon king Yudhishthira asked the most enlightened Markandeya a question that is too difficult to be understood.

sn: श्रोतुमिच्छामि भगवन् स्त्रीणां माहात्म्यमुत्तमम्। कथ्यमानं त्वया विप्र सूक्ष्मं धर्म्यं च तत्त्वतः॥
en: O you that are possessed of great energy, I desire to listen to the best account of a woman's greatness, O Brahmanas, you relate to me in detail the principles of pure morality.

sn: प्रत्यक्षमिह विप्रर्षे देवा दृश्यन्ति सत्तम। सूर्याचन्द्रमसौ वायुः पृथिवी वह्निरेव च॥
en: O Brahmanical sages, O foremost of men, the sun, the moon, the earth and the fire look like the deities in their embodied forms.

sn: पिता माता च भगवन् गुरुरेव च सत्तम्। यच्चान्यद् देवविहितं तच्चापि भृगुनन्दन॥
en: O holy one, O excellent one, O descendant of the Bhrigu race, the father, the mother and the preceptor-these and others, as ordained by the celestials, also appear as deities.

sn: मान्या हि गुरवः सर्वे एकपत्न्यस्तथा स्त्रियः। पतिव्रतानां शुश्रूषा दुष्करा प्रतिभाति मे॥
en: All venerable persons are to be respected, as also the women who are devoted to one husband. The service, that chaste women offer to their husbands, seems to me to be very difficult.

sn: पतिव्रतानां माहात्म्यं वक्तुमर्हसि नः प्रभो। निरुद्ध्य चेन्द्रियग्रामं मनः संरुध्य चानघ॥ पतिं दैवतवच्चापि चिन्तयन्त्यः स्थिता हि याः। भगवन् दुष्करं त्वेतत् प्रतिभाति मम प्रभो॥ मातापित्रोश्च शुश्रूषा स्त्रीणां भर्तरि च द्विजा स्त्रीणां धर्मात् सुघोराद्धि नान्यं पश्यामि दुष्करम्॥
en: O lord, it behoves you to relate to us the excellency of chaste women, who, O blameless one, putting a check upon all their senses and even restraining their minds, always think their husbands as gods. O holy one, O lord, O Brahmana, the worship that sons offer to their fathers and mothers and also what wives render to their husbands, appears to me be fraught with difficulty. In fact, I do not find anything more difficult than the duties of chaste women (to their husbands).

sn: साध्वाचाराः स्त्रियो ब्रह्मन् यत् कुर्वन्ति सदाऽऽदृताः। दुष्करं खलु कुर्वन्ति पितरं मातरं च वै॥
en: O Brahmanas, what the wives of good behaviours perform carefully ſin respect to their husbands) and also what the sons do to their father and mother, are indeed, highly difficult.

sn: एकपल्यश्च या नार्यो याश्च सत्यं वदन्त्युत। कुक्षिणा दश मासांश्च गर्भं संधारयन्ति याः॥
en: To those women who are attached to one lord; and those who speak the truth; and those who conceive in their womb a child for full ten months;

sn: नार्यः कालेन सम्भूय किमद्भुततरं ततः। संशयं परमं प्राप्य वेदनामतुलामपि॥
en: And to those women also who in due time are subject to great troubles and suffer extraordinary pains, what is more wonderful than these?

sn: प्रजायन्ते सुतान् नार्यो दुःखेन महता विभो। पुष्णन्ति चापि महता स्नेहेन द्विजपुङ्गव॥
en: O worshipful one, women give birth to their children with great pain to themselves; and, O foremost of the Brahmanas they bring them up with great affection.

sn: याश्च क्रूरेषु सत्त्वेषु वर्तमाना जुगुप्सिताः। स्वकर्म कुर्वन्ति सदा दुष्करं तच्च मे मतम्॥
en: That the persons, who are desirous of doing evils to others and who are always engaged in cruel deeds, discharge their duties, is, in my opinion, highly difficult.

sn: क्षत्रधर्मसमाचारतत्त्वं व्याख्याहि मे द्विज। धर्मः सुदुर्लभो विप्र नृशंसेन महात्मनाम्॥
en: O twice-born one, relate to me the detailed account of the virtue of the Kshatriya race. O Brahmana, the acquisition of virtue becomes very difficult for the lofty-minded ones, for they have to perform certain cruel deeds (in obedience to their racial duties).

sn: एतदिच्छामि भगवन् प्रश्नं प्रश्नविदां वर। श्रोतुं भृगुकुलश्रेष्ठ शुश्रूषे तव सुव्रत॥
en: O worshipful one, O you that do know answer to all questions, I desire to listen to the answers that you will relate; for, O foremost of the Bhrigu race, O you of excellent vows, I always worship you.

sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच हन्त तेऽहं समाख्यास्ये प्रश्नमेतं सुदुर्वचम्। तत्त्वेन भरतश्रेष्ठ गदतस्तन्निबोध मे॥
en: Markandeya said : O the best of the Bharata race, I will relate to you in detail the whole history of your question, although it is too difficult to state; you listen to me, as I tell you.

sn: मातृस्तु गौरवादन्ये पितृनन्ये तु मेनिरे। दुष्करं कुरुते माता विवर्धयति या प्रजाः॥
en: Some consider the mother to be superior and some again consider the father as such. The mother, however, performs the most difficult thing; for she propagates the species.

sn: तपसा देवतेज्याभिवन्दनेन तितिक्षया। सुप्रशस्तैरुपायैश्चापीहन्ते पितरः सुतान्॥
en: The fathers, too, by observing severe asceticism, by the adorations of the celestials and by chanting their praises, by undergoing the rigour of heat and cold, by repeating incantations and also by other expedients desire to possess children.

sn: एवं कृच्छ्रेण महता पुत्र प्राप्य सुदुर्लभम्। चिन्तयन्ति सदा वीर कीदृशोऽयं भविष्यति॥
en: O hero, thus having obtained a child after having recourse to these painful expedients, a child which is difficult of attainment, they always think what the child would do in the future.

sn: आशंसते हि पुत्रेषु पिता माता च भारत। यशः कीर्तिमथैश्वर्यं प्रजा धर्मं तथैव च॥
en: O descendant of the Bharata race, both the father and the mother aspire that the son is possessed of fame and celebration, wealth and subjects, as also virtue.

sn: तयोराशां तु सफलां यः करोति स धर्मवित्। पिता माता च राजेन्द्र तुष्यतो यस्य नित्यशः॥ इह प्रेत्य च तस्याथ कीर्तिर्धर्मश्च शाश्वतः।
en: O best of kings, the son who satisfies these aspirations of the parents, is considered to be virtuous. The son, whose father and mother are always satisfied with him, establishes everlasting reputation and virtue both in this world and the next.

sn: नैव यज्ञक्रियाः काश्चिन्न श्राद्धं नोपवासकम्॥ या तु भर्तरि शुश्रूषा तया सवर्गं जयत्युता।
en: She needs no sacrifices, nor she is required to perform Shraddha or to observe abstinence. When the wife offers all her services to her husband. In fact, thereby he alone obtains heaven.

sn: एतत् प्रकरणं राजन्नधिकृत्य युधिष्ठिर॥ पतिव्रतानां नियतं धर्मं चावहितः शृणु॥
en: O king, O Yudhishthira, remembering this fact, listen to the virtue of chaste women with as much attention as possible.

description: The history of a chaste woman
sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच कश्चिद् द्विजातिप्रवरो वेदाध्यायी तपोधनः। तपस्वी धर्मशीलश्च कौशिको नाम भारत॥
en: Markandeya said : O descendant of the Bharata race, there was a high class Brahmana, known by the name of Kaushika, who was a student of the Vedas and was rich with the wealth of devotion, himself a great devotee and possessed of virtuous behaviour.

description: The history of a chaste woman
sn: साङ्गोपनिषदो वेदानधीते द्विजसत्तमः। स वृक्षमूले कस्मिंश्चिद् वेदानुच्चारयन् स्थितः॥
en: That foremost of the Brahmanas had finished the study of the Vedas with the Angas and the Upanishadas. On a certain day, he was reciting the Vedas, seated on the root of a tree.

description: The history of a chaste woman
sn: उपरिष्टाच्च वृक्षस्य बलाका संन्यलीयत। तया पुरीषमुत्सृष्टं ब्राह्मणस्य तदोप॥ि३॥
en: On that occasion there sat on the top of the tree a female crane, which at the time voided excrement on the body of the Brahmana.

description: The history of a chaste woman
sn: तामवेक्ष्य ततः क्रुद्धः समपध्यायत द्विजः। भृशं क्रोधाभिभूतेन बलाका सा निरीक्षिता॥
en: Thereupon the twice-born one, who was greatly chraged, beholding the female crane, intended to do her an injury. The crane was looked by him, when he became insensible with great rage.

description: The history of a chaste woman
sn: अपध्याता च विप्रेण न्यपतद् धरणीतले। बलाकां पतितां दृष्ट्वा गतसत्त्वामचेतनाम्॥
en: Having been injured by the Brahmana, the crane fell down upon the ground; and as she fell, the Brahmana, seeing her insensible and lifeless,

description: The history of a chaste woman
sn: कारुण्यादभिसंतप्तः पर्यशोचत तां द्विजः। अकार्यं कृतवानस्मि रोषरागबलात्कृतः॥
en: Became oppressed with compassion and lamented for her, saying, 'I have committed a crime forced by passion and anger.'

description: The history of a chaste woman
sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच इत्युक्त्वा बहुशो विद्वान् चामं भक्ष्याय संश्रितः। चामे शुचीनि प्रचरन् कुलानि भरतर्षभ॥
en: Markandeya said : Having uttered these words several times, the educated Brahmana entered a village for alms and foremost of the Bharata race, after having gone round the sacred families in the village.

description: The history of a chaste woman
sn: प्रविष्टस्तत् कुलं यत्र पूर्वं चरितवांस्तु सः। देहीति याचमानोऽसौ तिष्ठेत्युक्तः स्त्रिया ततः॥
