en: He, at last entered a house where he used to come before. There he asked by saying-'Give'. Thereupon he was answered by a female, saying, 'wait'.

description: The history of a chaste woman
sn: शौचं तु यावत् कुरुते भाजनस्य कुटुम्बिनी। एतस्मिन्नन्तरे राजन् क्षुधासम्पीडितो भृशम्॥
en: While the matron was cleansing the vessel for giving the alms, then, her husband entered the house all of a sudden. O foremost of the Bharata race, oppressed with great hunger.

description: The history of a chaste woman
sn: भर्ता प्रविष्टः सहसा तस्या भरतसत्तम। सा तु दृष्ट्वा पतिं साध्वी ब्राह्मणं व्यवहाय तम्॥ पाद्यमाचमनीयं वै ददौ भर्तुस्तथाऽऽसनम्। प्रह्वा पर्यचरच्चापि भर्तारमसितेक्षणा॥
en: Her husband, O foreinost of the Bharat race, entered the house all on a sudden. The chaste house-wife, seeing her husband and neglecting that Brahmana, gave to her husband water for rinsing the feet and mouth, as also a seat.

description: The history of a chaste woman
sn: आहारेणाथ भक्ष्यैश्च भोज्यैः सुमधुरैस्तथा। उच्छिष्टं भाविता भर्तुर्भुङ्क्ते नित्यं युधिष्ठिर॥
en: Then the black-eyed matron served her husband with sweet food and drink and stood by his side, as if to attend to all what he would want. O Yudhishthira, that lady, devoted to her husband, daily ate the remnants of her husband's dish.

description: The history of a chaste woman
sn: दैवतं च पति मेने भर्तुश्चित्तानुसारिणी। कर्मणा मनसा वाचा नान्यचित्ताभ्यगात् पतिम्॥
en: That lady, always pursuing the thoughts of her husband, regarded the husband, as a celestial; and either in action, thought or speech, she never considered her husband otherwise.

description: The history of a chaste woman
sn: तं सर्वभावोपगता पतिशुश्रूषणे रता। साध्वाचारा सुचिर्दक्षा कुटुम्बस्य हितैषिणी॥
en: Her thoughts all turned towards her husband; and she was always engaged in serving her lord. She was virtuous and was skillful in good behaviours; and also was ever beneficent to her relatives.

description: The history of a chaste woman
sn: भर्तुश्चापि हितं यत् तत् सततं सानुवर्तते। देवतातिथिभृत्यानां श्वश्रूश्वशुरयोस्तथा॥ शुश्रूषणपरा नित्यं सततं संयतेन्द्रिया।
en: She was always attentive to what was beneficial to her husband and with her controlled passions she daily attended to the service of the gods, the guests, the mother-inlaw, the father-in-law and the servants.

description: The history of a chaste woman
sn: सा ब्राह्मणं तदा दृष्ट्वा संस्थितं भैक्ष्यकाक्षिणम्। कुर्वती पतिशुश्रूषां सस्माराथ शुभेक्षणा॥
en: While thus engaged in the service of her husband, she of beautiful eyes saw the Brahmana, who was still waiting for alms.

description: The history of a chaste woman
sn: वीडिता साभवत् साध्वी तदा भरतसत्तम। भिक्षामादाय विप्राय निर्जगाम यशस्विनी॥
en: Remembering this she was ashamed. Then, O foremost of the Bharata race, that chaste and famous lady went away to give alms to the Brahmanas.

description: The history of a chaste woman
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच किमिदं भवति त्वं मां तिष्ठेत्युक्त्वा वराङ्गने। उपरोधं कृतवती न विसर्जितवत्यसि॥
en: The Brahmana said : O the most excellent of women, what was this, that you requested me to wait and that you have not dismissed me?

description: The history of a chaste woman
sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच ब्राह्मणं क्रोधसंतप्तं ज्वलन्तमिव तेजसा। दृष्ट्वा साध्वी मनुष्येन्द्र सान्त्वपूर्वं वचोऽब्रवीत्॥
en: Markandeya said : O foremost of individuals, seeing that Brahmana greatly enraged and effulgent in energy, the chaste lady addressed him in friendly expressions.

description: The history of a chaste woman
sn: स्त्र्युवाच क्षन्तुमर्हसि मे विद्वन् भर्ता मे दैवतं महत्। स चाप क्षुधितः श्रान्तः प्राप्तः शुश्रूषितो मया॥
en: The Woman said : O learned one, it behoves you to grant me forgiveness. My husband is my chief god. He was very hunger and fatigued. Finding him thus, I served him.

description: The history of a chaste woman
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच ब्राह्मणा न गरीयांसो गरीयांस्ते पतिः कृतः। गृहस्थधर्मे वर्तन्ती ब्राह्मणानवमन्यसे॥
en: Brahmana said: The Brahmanas are not regarded by you to be superior, rather you supposed your lord to be superior to all. Living a domestic life you disrespect the Brahmanas.

description: The history of a chaste woman
sn: इन्द्रोऽप्येषां प्रणमते किं पुनर्मानवो भुवि। अवलिप्ते न जानीषे वृद्धानां न श्रुतं त्वया॥ ब्राह्मणा ह्यग्निसदृशा दहेयुः पृथिवीमपि।
en: Not to mention the men on earth, even Indra bows down to them. O proud one, do you not know or have you not heard from old men that really the Brahmanas are like fire and even can burn the wheel earth.

description: The history of a chaste woman
sn: स्त्र्युवाच नाहं बलाका विप्रर्षे त्यज क्रोधं तपोधन॥ अनया क्रुद्धया दृष्ट्या क्रुद्धः किं मां करिष्यसि। नावजानाम्यहं विप्रान् देवैस्तुल्यान् मनस्विनः॥
en: The Woman said: O sage-like Brahmana, O you who are possessed of the wealth of asceticism, do not consider that I am the female crane. Wrathful as you are, what will you do to me by this your wrathful look? Really I never disrespect the Brahmanas, who are like the celestials themselves, possessed of great energy.

description: The history of a chaste woman
sn: अपराधमिमं विप्र क्षन्तुमर्हसि मेऽनघ। जानामि तेजो विप्राणां महाभाग्यं च धीमताम्॥
en: O Brahmanas, O sinless one, you should forgive this fault of mine. I know the energy of the Brahmanas, as also the superior position of those who are possessed of great intelligence.

description: The history of a chaste woman
sn: अपेयः सागरः क्रोधात् कृतो हि लवणोदकः। तथैव दीप्ततपसां मुनीनां भावितात्मनाम्॥ येषां क्रोधाग्निरद्यापि दण्डके नोपशाम्यति।
en: By their wrath the ocean was made brackish and undrinkable. (I know also the energy of) the sages, blazing with asceticism. and who are possessed of restrained souls. The fire of their wrath has not been appeased us yet in the woods Dandaka.

description: The history of a chaste woman
sn: ब्राह्मणानां परिभवाद् वातापिः सुदुरात्मवान्॥ अगस्त्यमृषिमासाद्य जीर्णः क्रूरो महासुरः।
en: Owing to his disregard of the Brahmanas, the evil-minded Vatapi, the crooked, but great Asura, having advanced to the sage, Agastya, was digested by him.

description: The history of a chaste woman
sn: बहुप्रभावाः श्रूयन्ते ब्राह्मणानां महात्मनाम्॥ क्रोधः सुविपुलो ब्रह्मन् प्रसादश्च महात्मनाम्। अस्मिंस्त्वतिक्रमे ब्रह्मन् क्षन्तुमर्हसि मेऽनघ॥
en: Thus the superior energy of the high-souled Brahmanas has been heard. O Brahmana, the high-souled ones possess immense wrath, as also a good deal of forgiveness. O Brahmana, O sinless one, it behoves you to grant me forgiveness in this matter of my transgression.

description: The history of a chaste woman
sn: पतिशुश्रूषया धर्मो य: स मे रोचते द्विज। दैवतेष्वपि सर्वेषु भर्ता मे दैवतं परम्॥
en: O regenerate one, the merit, that is derived from the worship of my husband, is liked by me. Of all the gods, my husband is my highest deity.

description: The history of a chaste woman
sn: अविशेषेण तस्याहं कुर्यां धर्मं द्विजोत्तम्। शुश्रूषायाः फलं पश्य यत्युाह्मण यादृशम्॥
en: the most excellent of the Brahmanas, I cultivate that special virtue viz., the serving of my husband as the highest god. O Brahmana, you observe what results from the worship of one's husband.

description: The history of a chaste woman
sn: बलाका हि त्वया दग्धा रोषात् तद् विदितं मया क्रोधः शत्रुः शरीरस्थो मनुष्याणां द्विजोत्तम॥
en: It is known to me that the female crane was consumed by you with your wrath. But, O best of the Brahmanas, the wrath of persons, that resides in their body, is their mortal enemy.

description: The history of a chaste woman
sn: यः क्रोधमोहौ त्यजति तं देवा ब्राह्मणं विदुः। यो वदेदिह सत्यानि गुरुं संतोषयेत च॥ हिंसितश्च न हिंसेत तं देवा ब्राह्मणं विदुः।
en: The gods know him to be a Brahmana, who forsakes his wrath and spiritual ignorance; and who also speaks the truth here and comforts the preceptor, who having himself injured, never injures others.

description: The history of a chaste woman
sn: जितेन्द्रियो धर्मपरः स्वाध्यायनिरतः शुचिः॥ कामक्रोधौ वशौ यस्य तं देवा ब्राह्मणं विदुः।
en: Who again, possesses passions all controlled; and who is holy, virtuous and ever devoted to the studies of the Vedas and who has a control over the wrath and desires. The gods know him to be a Brahmana,

description: The history of a chaste woman
sn: यस्य चात्मसमो लोको धर्मज्ञस्य मनस्विनः॥ सर्वधर्मेषु च रतस्तं देवा ब्राह्मणं विदुः।
en: Who again, acquainted with virtue and possessed of energy, consider man to be equal to him. Who is conversant with all systems of a religion. The gods know him to be Brahmana.

description: The history of a chaste woman
sn: योऽध्यापयेदधीयीत यजेद् वा याजयीत वा॥ दद्याद् वापि यथाशक्ति तं देवा ब्राह्मणं विदुः।
en: Who himself studies and teaches others; and who, again, performs sacrifices himself and presides at the sacrifices performed by others, who gives away according to his means. The gods know him to be a Brahmana.

description: The history of a chaste woman
sn: ब्रह्मचारी वदान्यो योऽधीयीत् द्विजपुङ्गवः॥ स्वाध्यायवानमत्तो वै तं देवा ब्राह्मणं विदुः।
en: Who that foremost of the Brahmanas, is a Brahmachari, possessed of liberality and always attends to the studies, who carefully studies (the Vedas). The gods know him to be a Brahmana.

description: The history of a chaste woman
sn: यद् ब्राह्मणानां कुशलं तदेषां परिकीर्तयेत्॥ सत्यं तथा व्याहरतां नानृते रमते मनः।
en: What is agreeable to the Brahmanas repeats before them. The mind of those, who always walk in the path of truth, never takes pleasure in untruth.

description: The history of a chaste woman
sn: धर्म तु ब्राह्मणस्याहुः स्वाध्यायं दममार्जवम्॥ इन्द्रियाणां निग्रहं च शाश्वतं द्विजसत्तम।
en: The virtue of the Brahmana is said to consist in the study of the Vedas, in the repression of all passions and in the simplicity of manners.

description: The history of a chaste woman
sn: सत्यार्जवे धर्ममाहुः परं धर्मविदो जनाः॥ दुर्जेयः शाश्वतो धर्मः स च सत्ये प्रतिष्ठितः। श्रुतिप्रमाणो धर्मः स्यादिति वृद्धानुशासनम्॥
en: O best of the Brahmanas, the persons, who are versed in morality, consider the subduing of the senses, truth and simplicity of behaviours to be the eternal and highest virtue. Virtue is eternal and difficult of attainment. It is established upon truth. Virtue, again, rests entirely upon Shruti, which is the saying of old men.

description: The history of a chaste woman
sn: बहुधा दृश्यते धर्मः सूक्ष्म एव द्विजोत्तम। भवानपि च धर्मज्ञः स्वाध्यायनिरतः शुचिः॥
en: O foremost of the Brahmanas, virtue seems to be varied and fine. You, too, are holy, virtuous and devoted to the study of the Vedas.

description: The history of a chaste woman
sn: न तु तत्त्वेन भगवन् धर्मं वेत्सीति मे मतिः। यदि विप्र न जानीघे धर्मं परमकं द्विज॥ धर्मव्याधं ततः पृच्छ गत्वा तु मिथिलां पुरीम्।
en: O all-powerful one, in my opinion, you do not know the real essence of virtue. O Brahmana, O regenerate one, if you do not know that highest virtue, go to the city of Mithila and there you ask the virtuous Fowler.

description: The history of a chaste woman
sn: मातापितृभ्यां शुश्रूषुः सत्यवादी जितेन्द्रियः॥ मिथिलायां वसेद् व्याधः स ते धर्मान् प्रवक्ष्यति। तत्र गच्छस्व भद्रं ते यथाकामं द्विजोत्तम॥
en: That fowler lives in Mithila, who is ever ready to serve his father and mother, who is truthful and who has a control over his passions. O foremost of the twice-born ones, He will explain to you the different systems of religion. If you like, you, O blessed one, may go there.

description: The history of a chaste woman
sn: अत्युक्तमपि मे सर्वं क्षन्तुमर्हस्यानिन्दित। स्त्रियो ह्यवध्याः सर्वेषां ये च धर्मविदो जनाः॥
en: Whatever. I tell you, tell you, is merely merely an exaggeration; and, therefore, O sinless one, you should excuse me. For to them, who really learns virtue, the women are incapable of being injured.

description: The history of a chaste woman
sn: ब्राह्मणं उवाच प्रीतोऽस्मि तव भद्रं ते गतः क्रोधश्च शोभने। उपालम्भस्त्वयात्युक्तो मम निःश्रेयसं परम्। स्वस्ति तेऽस्तु गमिष्यामि साधयिष्यामि शोभने।॥
en: The Brahmana said: O beauteous lady, be happy. I am much satisfied with you. My wrath has been appeased. The chiding's uttered by you will prove most beneficial to me. O beautiful one, be happy. I shall go there and perform what is advantageous to me.

description: The history of a chaste woman
sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच तया विसृष्टो निर्गम्य स्वमेव भवनं ययौ। विनिन्दन् स स्वमात्मानं कौशिको द्विजसत्तमः॥
en: Markandeya said : Thus dismissed by her, Kaushika, the foremost of the twice-born ones, came out; and, chiding himself, returned to his own house.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच चिन्तयित्वा तदाश्चर्यं स्त्रिया प्रोक्तमशेषतः। विनिन्दन् स स्वमात्मानमागस्कृत इवाबभौ॥
en: Markandeya said : Continuously meditating upon that wonder, which the woman had told and reproaching himself very often, he appeared as if he was a criminal.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: चिन्तयानः स्वधर्मस्य सूक्ष्मां गतिमथाब्रवीत्। श्रद्दधानेन वै भाव्यं गच्छामि मिथिलामहम्॥
en: Thus meditating upon the fine way of virtue, he said, I should, indeed, respectfully agree to her speech; and, therefore, go at once to Mithila.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: कृतात्मा धर्मवित् तस्यां व्याधो निवसते किला तं गच्छाम्यहमद्यैव धर्मं प्रष्टुं तपोधनम्॥
en: Surely there lives in that city a fowler, who possess a soul under complete control and who also is thoroughly versed in the principles of morality. This day I will go to him, who possesses wealth of asceticism in order to ask him about the principles of morality.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: इति संचित्य मनसा श्रद्दधानः स्त्रिया वचः। बलाकाप्रत्ययेनासौ धयश्च वचनैः शुभैः॥ सम्प्रतस्थे स मिथिलां कौतूहलसमन्वितः।
en: Thus meditating in his mind and relying upon the statement of the woman, which was ensured by her knowledge of the death of the female crane, as also by her happy discourse bearing upon the principles of virtue, he (Kaushika), being filled with curiosity.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: अतिक्रामनरण्यानि ग्रामांश्च नगराणि चा॥ ततो जगाम मिथिलां जनकेन सुरक्षिताम्। धर्मसेतुसमाकीर्णां यज्ञोत्सववती शुभाम्॥
en: (He) departed to Mithila and crossed over forests, villages and cities. Then at last he came to Mithila, which was governed by king Janaka. The city was decorated with the flags hoisted by men of various creeds. It was echoed with the sound of sacrifices and festive celebrations. Also the city looked most beautiful.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: गोपुराट्टालकवती हर्म्यप्राकारशोभनाम्। प्रविश्य नगरी रम्यां विमानैर्बहुभिर्युताम्॥
en: Having entered that beautiful city, he saw that it was adorned with magnificent porches, buildings and splendid palaces, and protected on all sides by lofty walls and also filled with numberless cars.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: पण्यैश्च बहुभिर्युक्तां सुविभक्तमहापथाम्। अश्वै रथैस्तथा नागैर्योधैश्च बहुभिर्युताम्॥
en: The city was traversed by several broad roads, lined with innumerable shops. It was also covered over with innumerable horses, cars, elephants and warriors.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: हृष्टपुष्टजनाकीर्णां नित्योत्सवसमाकुलाम्। सोऽपश्यद् बहुवृत्तान्तां ब्राह्मण: समतिक्रमन्॥
en: The Brahmana saw the town full of men, who were enjoying health and cheer and were always engaged in the celebration of festivities; as also he saw there various other things.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: धर्मव्याधमपृच्छच्च स चास्य कथितो द्विजैः। अपश्यत् तत्र गत्वा तं सूनामध्ये व्यवस्थितम्॥
en: Having entered the city, he searched after the virtuous Fowler. Some regenerate persons pointed out to him the place, where he repaired and saw the Fowler seated in the midst of a butcher's yard.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: मार्गमाहिषमांसानि विक्रीणन्तं तपस्विनम्। आकुलत्वाच्च क्रेतृणामेकान्ते संस्थितो द्विजः॥
en: The twice-born person stood at a distant corner; for the fowler, devoted to asceticism, was then selling venison and the flesh of the buffalo; and a large number of buyers gathered round him in right earnest.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: स तु ज्ञात्वा द्विजं प्राप्तं सहसा सम्भ्रमोत्थितः। आजगाम यतो विप्रः स्थित एकान्तदर्शने॥
en: Understanding that the twice-born one had come to him, he (fowler) suddenly got up from his seat and went to the place, where the Brahmana was standing in seclusion.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: व्याध उवाच अभिवादये त्वां भगवन् स्वागतं ते द्विजोत्तम्। अहं व्याधो हि भद्रं ते किं करोमि प्रशाधि माम्॥
en: The Fowler said: O virtuous one, O foremost of the regenerate ones, I salute you. You are welcome! I am the fowler. Indeed, be you happy! Command me what I will do for you.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: एकपल्या यदुक्तोऽसि गच्छ त्वं मिथिलामिति। जानाम्येतदहं सर्वं यदर्थं त्वमिहागतः॥
en: The words, that a woman told to you, viz., you go to Mithila, are all known to me. I know also with what object you have come here.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: श्रुत्वा च तस्य तद् वाक्यं स विप्रो भृशविस्मितः द्वितीयमिदमाश्चर्यमित्यचिन्तयत द्विजः॥
en: Hearing these words of his, the Brahmana became greatly astonished. The regenerate person went on meditating-Oh! this is the second marvel!

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: अदेशस्थं हि ते स्थानमिति व्याधोऽब्रवीदिदम्। गृहं गच्छाव भगवन् यदि ते रोचतेऽनघ॥
en: The fowler then addressed the Brahmana, saying-Indeed, you are now staying at a place, that is not at all proper for you. O holy one, O faultless one, should you like, let us go to my own abode.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच बाढमित्येव तं विप्रो हृष्टो वनचमब्रवीत्। अचतस्तु द्विजं कृत्वा स जगाम गृहं प्रति॥
en: Markandeya said : The Brahmana, highly gratified, addressed him, saying, "So be it". Making the Brahmana proceed before him, he (fowler) departed towards his own abode.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: प्रविश्य च गृहं रम्यमासनेनाभिपूजितः। अर्येण च स वै तेन व्याधेन द्विजसत्तमः॥
en: Having entered his beautiful abode, he honoured him with a seat. Accepting the water that was given to him for washing the feet and face, the foremost of the regenerate ones.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: ततः सुखोपविष्टस्तं व्याधं वचनमब्रवीत्। कर्मैतद् वै न सदृशं भवतः प्रतिभाति मे। अनुतप्ये भृशं तात तव घोरेण कर्मणा॥
en: Seated himself at his ease. Thereupon he addressed the fowler, saying, "It appears to me that this business is not really suitable to you. O father, I greatly regret that you should adopt such a dishonourable profession",

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: व्याध उवाच कुलोचितमिदं कर्म पितृपैतामहं परम्। वर्तमानस्य मे धर्मे स्वे मन्युं मा कृथा द्विज॥
en: The Fowler said: This profession belongs to my race; and it has descended to me from my father and grandfather. O twice-born one, do not be sorry for the reason of my adopting the profession that belongs to my own family.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: विधात्रा विहित पूर्वं कर्म स्वमनुपालयन्। प्रयत्नाच्च गुरू वृद्धौ शुश्रूषेऽहं द्विजोत्तम॥
en: Fulfilling the duties of my own trade, to which I am already destined by the creator, I carefully devote myself, O best of the regenerate ones, to the service of my superiors as well as the old men.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: सत्यं वदे नाभ्यसूये यथाशक्ति ददामि च। देवतातिथिभृत्यानामवशिष्टेन वर्तये॥
en: I always speak the truth; and I never envy other persons. As also I give away to the best of my power; and live upon what is left after the service of the gods, the guests and my own dependents.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: न कुत्सयाम्यहं किंचिन्न गर्हे बलवत्तरम्। कृतमन्वेति कर्तारं पुरा कर्म द्विजोत्तम॥
en: I never speak evil of anything; neither I hate anything, however great. O best of the twiceborn persons, the actions done in the past existence always follow the doer.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: कृषिगोरक्ष्यवाणिज्यमिह लोकस्य जीवनम्। दण्डनीतिस्त्रयी विद्या तेन लोको भवत्युत॥
en: In this world the chief professions of men are agriculture, the rearing of cows and trade. But in the next world, the acquaintance in ethics and the three special branches of knowledge (the three Vedas) prove most conducive.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: कर्म शूद्रे कृषिर्वैश्ये संग्रामः क्षत्रिये स्मृतः। ब्रह्मचर्यं तपो मन्त्राः सत्यं च ब्राह्मणे सदा॥
en: Service of other three classes has been the fixed duty of the Shudra. Agriculture has been fixed for the Vaishyas; and fighting has been ordained for the Kshatriyas. The vow of Brahmacharya, devotion, repetition of the mantras and truthfulness are always to be observed by the Brahmanas.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: राजा प्रशास्ति धर्मेण स्वकर्मनिरताः प्रजाः। विकर्माणश्च ये केचित् तान् युनक्ति स्वकर्मसु॥
en: The king should govern, in accordance with the dictates of virtue, the subjects, who always stick to their fixed profession. He should also appoint men to their own profession, who have really fallen from it.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: भेतव्यं हि सदा राज्ञः प्रजानामधिपा हि ते। वारयन्ति विकर्मस्थं नृपा मृगमिवेषुभिः॥
en: The king should always be feared by his subjects; because he is their lord. The kings, again, should check their subject, who has gone away from his fixed profession, even as they restrain the deer by the arrows.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: जनकस्येह विप्रर्षे विकर्मस्थो न विद्यते। स्वकर्मनिरता वर्णाश्चत्वारोऽपि द्विजोत्तम॥
en: O twice-born sage, O best of the Brahmanas, there is none here in the kingdom of king Janaka, who has fallen from his ordained duties. In fact, all the four classes strictly follow their respective duties.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: स एष जनको राजा दुर्वृत्तमपि चेत् सुतम्। दण्ड्यं दण्डे निक्षिपति तथा न ग्लाति धार्मिकम्।२९॥
en: Janaka is such a king that, even if his son be a cruel and a criminal one, he puts him under punishment. But he never inflicts penalty upon the virtuous.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: सुयुक्तचारो नृपतिः सर्वं धर्मेण पश्यति। श्रीश्च राज्यं च दण्डश्च क्षत्रियाणां द्विजोत्तम॥
en: With the assistance of the spies appointed by him, he casts a virtuous look upon all things. O best of the regenerate ones, prosperity, kingdom and the power of inflicting punishment rest with the Kshatriyas.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: राजानो हि स्वधर्मेण श्रियमिच्छन्ति भूयसीम्। सर्वेषामेव वर्णानां त्राता राजा भवत्युत॥
en: Indeed, the kings, practising their own special virtues, crave for immense prosperity. In fact, the king is the preserver of all the four classes.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: परेण हि हतान् ब्रह्मन् वराहमहिषानहम्। न स्वयं हन्मि विप्रर्षे विक्रीणामि सदात्वहम्॥
en: O regenerate one, I never slay the hogs and buffaloes myself. They are slain by others. O twice-born sage, only I always sell their flesh afterwards.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: न भक्षयामि मांसानि ऋतुगामी तथा ह्यहम्। सदोपवासी च तथा नक्तभोजी सदा द्विज॥
en: I never eat flesh myself. Really I have an intercourse with my wife during her season. O twice-born one, I always fast during the day and eat only during the night.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: अशीलश्चापि पुरुषो भूत्वा भवति शीलवान्। प्राणिहिंसारतश्चापि भवते धार्मिकः पुनः॥
en: A person, being born bad, may be of good character. Again, he may turn out virtuous, even if he be a slayer of animals by birth or profession.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: व्यभिचारानरेन्द्राणां धर्मः संकीर्यते महान्। अधर्मो वर्धते चापि संकीर्यन्ते ततः प्रजाः॥
en: Virtue diminishes in strength on account of the misconduct of the kings, and sin becomes predominant. Thereon the subjects grow less.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: भेरुण्डा वामनाः कुब्जाः स्थूलशीर्षास्तथैव च। क्लीबाश्चान्धाश्च बधिरा जायन्तेऽत्युच्चलोचनाः॥
en: Then also the formidable monsters, dwarfs and those, who have crooked backs and wide heads and those, who have lost the power of procreation, the dead and blind persons as also those, who have their eye-sight paralysed, begin to take birth.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: पार्थिवानामधर्मत्वात् प्रजानामभवः सदा। स एष राजा जनकः प्रजा धर्मेण पश्यति॥
en: In consequence of the criminality of the rulers of the earth, the subjects undergo continuous harms. But Janaka is such a monarch, that he looks upon his subjects with virtuous eyes.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: अनुगृहणन् प्रजाः सर्वा स्वधर्मनिरताः सदा। ये चैव मां प्रशंसन्ति ये च निन्दन्ति मानवाः॥ सर्वान् सुपरिणीतेन कर्मणा तोषयाम्यहम्।
en: He is ever kind to all his subjects, who perform their fixed duties. As for myself, those who praise me or those men who blame me, all of them I satisfy with deeds well done.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: ये जीवन्ति स्वधर्मेण संयुञ्जन्ति च पार्थिवाः॥ न किंचिदुपजीवन्ति दान्ता उत्थानशीलिनः।
en: But those kings, who lead their lives in the strict observance of their duties and are ever busy (in the performance of honest deeds) and who can bear austerity and possess smartness and promptitude, never depend upon anything for their support.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: शक्त्यानदानं सततं तितिक्षा धर्मनित्यता॥ यथार्ह प्रति पूजा च सर्वभूतेषु वै सदा। त्यागान्नान्यत्र मर्त्यानां गुणास्तिष्ठन्ति पूरुषे॥
en: Giving away food incessantly to the best of one's power, patience and firm belief in virtue, necessary regard for all creatures always, these virtues are present only in that person, who has wholly abandoned the world (the worldly pleasures); but in none else.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: मृषा वादं परिहरेत् कुर्यात् प्रियमयाचितः। न च कामान्न संरम्भान्न द्वेषाद् धर्ममुत्सृजेत्॥
en: One should do away with falsehood. He should render good to all without being asked. He should never forsake virtue out of lust or anger or malice.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: प्रिये नातिभृशं हृष्येदप्रिये न च संज्वरेत्। न मुह्येदर्थकृच्छ्रेषु न च धर्मं परित्यजेत्॥
en: One should not express unnatural joy at good fortune or succumb under calamities. He should not grow dispirited, when overpowered by poverty or forsake his virtue when so overpowered.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: कर्म चेत्किंचिदन्यत् स्यादितरन्न तदाचरेत्। यत् कल्याणमभिध्यायेत् तत्रात्मानं नियोजयेत्॥
en: If on a certain occasion one commits a wrong, he should not commit it again. One should direct his soul to what contributes to the happiness of others.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: न पापे प्रतिपाप: स्यात् साधुरेव सदा भवेत्। आत्मनैव हतः पापो यः पापं कर्तुमिच्छति॥
en: There should be no wrong over wrong; rather one should deal honestly. The sinful person, who desires to commit a crime, is slain by himself.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: कर्म चैतदसाधूनां वृजिनानामसाधुवत्। न धर्मोऽस्तीति मन्वानाः शुचीनवहसन्ति ये॥ अश्रद्दधाना धर्मस्य ते नश्यन्ति न संशयः। महादृतिरिवाघ्मातः पापो भवति नित्यदा॥
en: By committing a crime one becomes wicked and dishonest. Those who consider that there is no virtue or those, who laugh at the pure and good, these vicious men undoubtedly find decay in the long run. The wicked person daily grows flatulent, even as the leather bag inflated with wind.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: मूढानामवलिप्तानामसारं भावितं भवेत्। दर्शयत्यन्तरात्मा तं दिवा रूपमिवांशुमान्॥
en: The ideas of those, who are destitute of all sensibilities and who also are most worldly, are worthless. The inner soul points him out (as a fool), even as the sun discovers all features during the day.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: न लोके राजते मूर्खः केवलात्मप्रशंसया। अपि चेह श्रिया हीनः कृतविद्यः प्रकाशते॥
en: The fool cannot shine in this world only by praising himself. Rather the learned man, even if he be dirty and anointed, shines gloriously in this world.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: अब्रुवन् कस्यचिनिन्दामात्मपूजामवर्णयन्। न कश्चिद् गुणसम्पन्नः प्रकाशो भुवि दृश्यते॥
en: He never speaks ill of any one; nor does he utter his own praise. No person is found on earth, who shines with all the excellent qualities.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: विकर्मणा तप्यमानः पापाद् विपरिमुच्यते। न तत् कुर्यां पुनरिति द्वितीयात् परिमुच्यते॥
en: The person, who repents for his sins, is freed from them. If one declares that he would not commit the sin again, he is delivered from committing a second one.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: कर्मणा येन तेनेह पापाद् द्विजवरोत्तमा एवं श्रुतिरियं ब्रह्मन् धर्मेषु प्रतिदृश्यते॥
en: O best and foremost of the Brahmanas, he may also be saved from sin by the performance of any one of the ordained acts. O Brahmana, this is Shruti, which may be referred to as one this relating to virtue.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: पापान्यबुद्धवेह पुरा कृतानि प्राग् धर्मशीलोऽपि विहन्ति पश्चात्। धर्मो राजन् नुदते पूरुषाणां यत् कुर्वते पापमिह प्रमादात्॥
en: A person, who was formerly virtuous, having committed sins out of ignorance, can destroy those sins afterwards. O monarch, the virtue of persons shines again (drives off all sins), if sins are committed out of mistake.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: पापं कृत्वा हि मन्येत नाहमस्मीति पूरुषः। तं तु देवाः प्रपश्यन्ति स्वस्यैवान्तर पूरुषः॥
en: After having committed a sin, one should consider that he is no longer a man. The gods behold his sin, as also the monitor that is within him.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: चिकीर्षेदेव कल्याणं श्रद्दधानोऽनसूयकः। वसनस्येव छिद्राणि साधूनां विवृणोति यः॥
en: The person, who with piety and without detestation, hides the faults of the honest, like holes in his own garment surely desires to provide for the means of salvation.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: पापं चेत् पुरुषः कृत्वा कल्याणमभिपद्यते। मुच्यते सर्वपापेभ्यो महाभ्रेणेव चन्द्रमाः॥
en: After having committed the sin, if a person really seeks salvation, he is delivered from all his sins, even as the moon looks bright after it has come out of the clouds.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: यथाऽऽदित्यः समुद्यन् वै तमः पूर्वं व्यपोहति। एवं कल्याणमातिष्ठन् सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते॥
en: Thus seeking salvation, a man is freed from all his sins, even as the sun, upon rising, displays its lustre after it has driven off all darkness.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: पापानां विद्ध्यधिष्ठान् लोभमेव द्विजोत्तम। लुब्धाः पापं व्यवस्यन्ति नरा नातिबहुश्रुताः॥
en: O best of the twice-born ones, do you know that temptation forms the ground-work of all sins. Men, that are destitute of enough of knowledge, having been given to temptation, commit sins.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: अधर्मा धर्मरूपेण तृणैः कूपा इवावृताः। तेषां दमः पवित्राणि प्रलापा धर्मसंश्रिताः। सर्वं हि विद्यते तेषु शिष्टाचारः सुदुर्लभः॥
en: Sinful persons hide themselves under the guise of virtue, even as the wells remain undiscovered on account of the grasses growing over and covering them. The selfcontrol, which they seem to possess, their holiness, their speeches regarding virtue, all these are witnessed in them. But good behaviours are hardly found in them.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच स तु विप्रो महाप्राज्ञो धर्मव्याधमपृच्छत। शिष्टाचारं कथमहं विद्यामिति नरोत्तम॥
en: Markandeya said : Indeed, that greatly wise Brahmana asked the virtuous flower, saying, "O foremost of men, how shall I know the the virtuous behaviours?"

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: एतदिच्छामि भद्रं ते श्रोतुं धर्मभृतां वर। त्वत्तो महामते व्याध तद् ब्रवीहि यथातथम्॥
en: O best of virtuous persons, you are blessed! I desire to hear this from you. O lofty-minded one, O Fowler, tell me the details of it truly.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: व्याध उवाच यज्ञो दानं तपो वेदाः सत्यं च द्विजसत्तम। पञ्चैतानि पवित्राणि शिष्टाचारेषु सर्वदा॥
en: The Fowler said : O foremost of the regenerate ones, sacrifice, gift, austerity, the study of the Vedas and truthfulness, these five holy things are always noticed. in . virtuous conduct. over

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: कामक्रोधौ वशे कृत्वा दम्भं लोभमनार्जवम्। धर्ममित्येव संतुष्टास्ते शिष्टाः शिष्टसम्मताः॥
en: Having control desires, anger, haughtiness, avarice and wickedness, those who take pleasure in virtue because it is virtue, are, in the opinion of the honest and wise, really reckoned to be virtuous.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: न तेषां विद्यतेऽवृत्तं यज्ञस्वाध्यायशीलिनाम्। आचारपालनं चैव द्वितीयं शिष्टलक्षणम्॥
en: Those persons who perform sacrifices and are ever devoted to the study of Vedas, have no behaviours other than what are practised by the virtuous. Indeed good behaviours form the second attribute of the pious.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: गुरुशुश्रूषणां सत्यमक्रोधो दानमेव च। एतच्चतुष्टयं ब्रह्मन् शिष्टाचारेषु नित्यदा॥
en: O Brahmana, rendering services to the superiors, truthfulness, worthlessness and gift, these four are ever present in those, who are really virtuous.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: शिष्टाचारे मनः कृत्वा प्रतिष्ठाप्य च सर्वशः। यामयं लभते वृत्तिं सा न शक्या हतोऽन्यथा॥
en: Once can wholly obtain credit by directing the heart towards virtuous behaviours. This he gains only be practising the above four; Otherwise to gain this becomes impossible.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: वेदस्योपनिषत् सत्यं सत्यस्योपनिषद् दमः। दमस्योपनिषत् त्यागः शिष्टाचारेषु नित्यदा॥
en: Truth constitutes the essence of the Vedas. Control over passions constitutes the essence of truth. And self-denial (refraining from the worldly enjoyments) forms the essence of selfcontrol. These attributes are always present in a virtuous conduct.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: ये तु धर्मानसूयन्ते बुद्धिमोहान्विता नराः। अपथा गच्छतां तेषामनुयाता च पीड्यते॥
en: Those persons, who, being intelligent and full of delusions, hate these virtues, surely tread in the sinful path. The men who follow them fall in the abyss of decay.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: ये तु शिष्टाः सुनियताः श्रुतित्यागपरायणाः। धर्मपन्थानमारूढाः सत्यधर्मपरायणाः॥
en: They, who are virtuous and are devoted to the observance of the vows, to the Shrutis and to self-denial; and they who have ascended the paths of virtue and are engaged in speaking truth and observing virtues;

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: नियच्छन्ति परां बुद्धिं शिष्टाचारान्विता जनाः। उपाध्यायमते युक्ताः स्थित्या धर्मार्थदर्शिनः॥
en: They, who are endued with the virtuous behaviours; they, who follow the orders of the preceptors; and they, who minutely observe the import of the scriptures, obtain the highest intelligence.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: नास्तिकान् भिन्नमर्यादान् क्रूरान् पापमतौ स्थितान्। त्यज तान् ज्ञानमाश्रित्य धार्मिकानुपसेव्य च॥
en: Forsake the atheists, who are notorious, wicked and always entertain cruel ideas. Take shelter under knowledge and always worship those, that are virtuous.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: कामलोभग्रहाकी) पञ्चेन्द्रियजला नदीम्। नावं धृतिमयीं कृत्वा जन्मदुर्गाणि संत॥
en: By means of the boat of endurance you cross over that river, which is replete with such creatures as the desires and temptations. Its waters are the fine senses and the shoals found therein are the successive births.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: क्रमेण संचितो धर्मो बुद्धियोगमयो महान्। शिष्टाचारे भवेत् साधू रागः शुक्लेव वाससि।॥
en: As great is virtue or as it consists in the practice of intelligence and yoga, it looks very beautiful, when acquired and added to a virtuous behaviour, like the dye on a white garment.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: अहिंसा सत्यवचनं सर्वभूतिहतं परम्। अहिंसा परमो धर्मः स च सत्ये प्रतिष्ठितः। सत्ये कृत्वा प्रतिष्ठां तु प्रवर्तन्ते प्रवृत्तयः॥
en: Absence of malice and truthfulness are most beneficial to all creatures. Absence of malice constitutes the chief virtue, which, again, is founded upon truth. Indeed, all our desirabilities find their scope, when they are all based upon truth.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: सत्यमेव गरीयस्तु शिष्टाचारनिषेवितम्। आचारश्च सतां धर्मः संतश्चाचारलक्षणाः॥
en: Truth is the supreme virtue, which is specially adopted by the the pious. Good behaviour forms the peculiar virtue of the honest and the wise. Those, that are holy, possess good conduct.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: यो यथाप्रकृतिर्जन्तुः स स्वां प्रकृतिमश्नुते। पापात्मा क्रोधकामादीन् दोषानापनोत्यनात्मवान्॥
en: Every creature frames principles of his own according to his inherent tendency. The vicious man, who can not restrain his own self, becomes subject to these vices, viz., desires, wrath and others.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: आरम्भो न्याययुक्तो यः स हि धर्म इति स्मृतः। अनाचारस्त्वधर्मेति एतच्छिष्टानुशासनम्॥
en: It is an immortal maxim that justice constitutes virtue. The virtuous say that evil behaviours constitute sin.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: अक्रुद्ध्यन्तोऽनसूयन्तो निरहकारमत्सराः। ऋजवः शमसम्पन्नाः शिष्टाचारा भवन्ति ते॥
en: Those men are reckoned to be virtuous, who never show wrath, pride or haughtiness and malice or whose conduct is ever marked by simplicity and quiet due.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: विद्यवृद्धाः शुतयो वृत्तवन्तो मनस्विनः। गुरुशुश्रूषवो दान्ताः शिष्टाचारा भवन्त्युत॥
en: Those again, are said to possess virtuous conduct, who carefully follow the rites laid down in the three Vedas; who are holy; who possess piety and sacred character; who serve the superiors; and who also have the power of restraining the self.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: तेषामहीनसत्त्वानां दुष्कराचारकर्मणाम्। स्वैः कर्मभिः सत्कृतानां घोरत्वं सम्प्रणश्यति॥
en: The actions and behaviours of those great men are difficult of acquisition. The sins of those men, who are made pure by means of their own actions, die out of themselves.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: तं सदाचारमाश्चर्यं पुराणं शाश्वतं ध्रुवम्। धर्मं धर्मेण पश्यन्तः स्वर्ग यान्ति मनीषिणः॥
en: This pious behaviour is most wonderful, ancient, inchangeable and eternal. The wise men's who with sanctity lead a virtuous life secure heaven.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: आस्तिका मानहीनाश्च द्विजातिजनपूजकाः। श्रुतवृत्तोपसम्पन्नाः सन्तः स्वर्गनिवासिनः॥
en: The holy men, who are atheists, as also who are unaustentatious and who are respectful towards the degenerate persons and who, again, are familiar with the holy rites, are deserved to live in heaven.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: वेदोक्तः परमो धर्मो धर्मशास्त्रेषु चापरः। शिष्टाचारश्च शिष्टानां त्रिविधं धर्मलक्षणम्।
en: The explanation of virtue is threefold. The first is called the supreme virtue, which is inculcated in the Vedas. The second is what is laid down in Dharmashastras. The third is called the honest behaviour, which is observed by the pious.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: धारणं चापि विद्यानां तीर्थानामवगाहनम्॥ क्षमा सत्यार्जवं शौचं सतामाचारदर्शनम्।
en: Crossing over (the ocean of) knowledge, the performance of ablutions in the places of pilgrimage, forgiveness, truthfulness, simplicity, sacredness are the characteristics of virtuous conduct.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: सर्वभूतदयावन्तो अहिंसानिरताः सदा॥ परुषं च न भाषन्ते सदा सन्तो द्विजप्रियाः।
en: Those who, are king to all creatures and who are never malignant and who never speak ill of anybody, are always dear to the twice-born ones.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: शुभानामशुभानां च कर्मणां फलसंचये॥ विपाकमभिजानन्ति ते शिष्टाः शिष्टसम्मताः। न्यायोपेता गुणोपेताः सर्वलोकहितैषिणः॥ सन्तः स्वर्गजितः शुक्लाः संनिविष्टाश्च सत्पथे।
en: Who are familiar with the results of good or evil actions, are reckoned by the wise to be virtuous. Again, those who are just and virtuous and well disposed towards all and who are honest and have obtained heaven, who possess sacred characters and constantly tread in the path of virtue.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: दातारः संविभक्तारो दीनानुग्रहकारिणः॥ सर्वपूज्याः श्रुतधनास्तथैव च तपस्विनः। सर्वभूतदयावन्तस्ते शिष्टाः शिष्टसम्मताः॥
en: Who are liberal in gifts and unselfish, who show favour to the distressed and who are revered by all, who possess the wealth of knowledge, who are devotees and who are kind to all creatures, are virtuous according to the honest and wise.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: दानशिष्टाः सुखाँल्लोकानाप्नुवन्तीह च श्रियम्। पीडया च कलत्रस्य भृत्यानां च समाहिताः॥ अतिशक्त्या प्रयच्छन्ति सन्त: सद्भिः समागताः। लोकयात्रां च पश्यन्तो धर्ममात्महितानि च॥
en: The persons, who are charitable, secure prosperity in this world and abodes of happiness, in the next. The virtuous men, if approached and solicited by the honest and wise, give away alms to them with the best of his power, even at the denial of the comforts of his wife and dependents. Looking to their own interest and having an eye upon virtue and the ways of the world.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: एवं सन्तो वर्तमानास्त्वेधन्ते शाश्वतीः समाः। अहिंसा सत्यवचनमानृशंस्यमथार्जवम्॥ अद्रोहो नाभिमानश्च ह्रीस्तितिक्षा दमः शमः। धीमन्तो धृतिमन्तश्च भूतानामनुकम्पकाः॥ अकामद्वेषसंयुक्तास्ते सन्तो लोकसाक्षिणः।
en: The men, who thus practise virtue, obtain the greatest amount of virtue through eternal ages. Persons, who possess the attributes of truthfulness, abstention from injuring others, modestly and simplicity and who are not malicious and proud, who are mild and selfsacrificing, who have self-control and forbearance, intelligence and patience, who are kind towards all creatures and who are free from desires and malice, are said to be the witnesses of the world.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: त्रीण्येव तु पदान्याहुः सतां व्रतमनुत्तमम्॥ न चैव दुह्येद् दद्याच्च सत्यं चैव सदा वदेत्।
en: These three are reckoned to constitute the highest way of the pious, viz., a man must not offend anybody. He must be charitable. Also he must speak the truth always. Those great men of highest virtue.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: सर्वत्र च दयावन्तः सन्तः करुणवेदिनः॥ गच्छन्तीह सुसंतुष्टा धर्मपन्थानमुत्तमम्। शिष्टाचाराः महात्मानो येषां धर्मः सुनिश्चितः॥
en: Who are kind on all occasions and who are filled with compassion, obtain the greatest contentment and ascend the superior path of virtue; and whose acquisition of virtue is most certain.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: अनसूया क्षमा शान्तिः संतोष: प्रियवादिता। कामक्रोधपरित्याग: शिष्टाचारनिषेवणम्॥ कर्म च श्रुतसम्पन्नं सतां मार्गमनुत्तमम्।
en: Harmlessness, forgiveness, peacefulness, contentment, agreeable speech, giving away passions and excitements, the service of the virtuous characters and actions performed in accordance with the dictates of the Shastra constitute the superior path of the honest and the wise.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: शिष्टाचार निषेवन्ते नित्यं धर्ममनुव्रताः॥ प्रज्ञाप्रासादमारुह्य मुच्यन्ते महतो भयात्। प्रेक्षन्तो लोकवृत्तानि विविधानि द्विजोत्तम॥ अतिपुण्यानि पापानि तानि द्विजवरोत्तम।
en: Those who constantly follow the path of virtue and daily worship the virtuous, can ascend the palace of knowledge. It is they only who are freed from that greatest terror (rebirth). O best of Brahmanas, it is they only who have the power of observing the several aspects of human nature.

description: The colloquy between the Brahmana and the Fowler
sn: एतत् ते सर्वमाख्यातं यथाप्रज्ञं यथाश्रुतम्। शिष्टाचारगुणं ब्रह्मन् पुरस्कृत्य द्विजर्षभ॥
en: O foremost of Brahmanas I have thus related to you all about the virtuous as well as the vicious, behaviours according to my own knowledge or as I have heard on the matter. O Brahmana, O foremost of the twice-born ones, I have done justice to the subject of virtuous conduct, which I had introduced.

sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच स तु विप्रमथोवाच धर्मव्याधो युधिष्ठिर। यदहमाचरे कर्म घोरमेतदसंशयम्॥
en: Markandeya said : O Yudhishthira, that virtuous fowler then said to that Brahmana, “The acts that I perform are certainly cruel, there is no doubt.

sn: विधिस्तु बलवान् ब्रह्मन् दुस्तरं हि पुरा कृतम्। पुरा कृतस्य पापस्य कर्मदोषो भवत्ययम्॥
en: O Brahmana, Destiny in all powerful; it is difficuit to overcome the consequences of our past actions. This is the Karma, evil arising from sins committed in a former life.

sn: दोषस्यैतस्य वै ब्रह्मन् विघाते यत्नवानहम्। विधिना हि हते पूर्वं निमित्तं घातको भवेत्॥
en: O Brahmana, I am always assiduous in eradicating this evil. The Destiny has already killed one when he is killed by another, the executioner is but an instrument.

sn: निमित्तभूता हि वयं कर्मणोऽस्य द्विजोत्तम। येषां हतानां मांसानि विक्रीणामीह वै द्विज॥ तेषामपि भवेद् धर्म उपयोगे न भक्षणे। देवतातिथिभृत्यानां पितृणां चापि पूजनम्॥
en: O foremost of Brahmanas, we are but such agents in consequence of our Karma, O twiceborn one, those animals that are killed and the most of which are sold, also acquire Karma, for the celestials the guests and servants are entertained and Pitris are gratified with this dainty food.

sn: ओषध्यो वीस्थश्चैव पशवो मृगपक्षिणः। अनादिभूता भूतानामित्यपि श्रूयते श्रुतिः॥
en: It is mentioned in the Shruti that herbs, vegetables, deer, birds and the wild animals are the ordained food for all creatures.

sn: आत्ममांसप्रसादेन शिबिरौशीनरो नृपः। स्वर्ग सुदुर्गमं प्राप्तः क्षमावान् द्विजसत्तम॥
en: O foremost of Brahmanas, the son of Ushinara, Shibi of great forbearance, obtained heaven which is very difficult to obtain, by giving away his own flesh.

sn: स्वधर्म इति कृत्वा तु न त्यजामि द्विजोत्तम। पुरा कृतमिति ज्ञात्वा जीवाम्येतेन कर्मणा॥
en: O foremost of Brahmanas, knowing this to be the duty of my order, I do not give it up. Knowing this to be the result of my own acts, I earn my livelihood by doing it.

sn: स्वकर्म त्यजतो ब्रह्मन्नधर्म इह दृश्यते। स्वकर्मनिरतो यस्तु धर्मः स इति निश्चयः॥
en: O Brahmana, to abandon one's own duty is considered to be sin. To stick to one's own duty is certainly a meritorious act.

sn: पूर्वं हि विहितं कर्म देहिनं न विमुञ्चति। धात्रा विधिरयं दृष्टो बहुधा कर्मनिर्णये॥
en: The acts done before (in one's own former birth) never leave any creature. In determining the various effects of Karma, the Creator did see it.

sn: द्रष्टव्या तु भवेत् प्रज्ञा क्रूरे कर्मणि वर्तता। कथं कर्म शुभं कुर्यां कथं मुच्ये पराभवात्॥
en: A man, being under the influence of evil Karma, must always consider 'how he can done for his Karma and how he can extricate himself from an evil doom.'

sn: कर्मणस्तस्य घोरस्य बहुधा निर्णयो भवेत्। दाने च सत्यवाक्ये च गुरुशुश्रूषणे तथा॥ द्विजातिपूजने चाहं धर्मे च निरतः सदा। अभिमानातिवादाभ्यां निवृत्तोऽस्मि द्विजोत्तम॥
en: There are various ways in which evil Karma might be expiated, such as, by making gifts, by speaking truth and by serving the preceptor, by worshipping the order of the twice-born, by becoming devoted to virtue, free from pride and idle talk. O foremost of Brahmanas, I do these things.

sn: कृषि साध्विति मन्यन्ते तत्र हिंसा परा स्मृता। कर्षन्तो लाइलैः पुंसोध्नन्ति भूमिशयान् बहून्। जीवानन्यांश्च बहुशस्तत्र किं प्रतिभाति ते॥
en: Agriculture is considered to be a praiseworthy occupation, but it is well-known that even in it great harm is done to animal life. In ploughing the ground, various creatures and animal lives are destroyed. What is your opinion on this matter?

sn: धान्यबीजानि यान्याहुज्ह्यादीनि द्विजोत्तम। सर्वाण्येतानि जीवानि तत्र किं प्रतिभाति ते॥
en: O foremost of Brahmanas, Vrihi and other so called seeds of rice are all living organisms, what is your opinion on this matter?

sn: अध्याक्रम्य पशूश्चापि नन्ति वै भक्षयन्ति च। वृक्षांस्तथौषधीश्चापि छिन्दन्ति पुरुषा द्विज॥ जीवा हि बहवो ब्रह्मन् वृक्षेषु च फलेषु च। उदके बहवश्चापि तत्र किं प्रतिभाति ते॥
en: O Brahmana, Men hunt wild animals and kill them to eat their meat; they also cut up trees and plants. O Brahmana, there are innumerable animal organisms in trees and fruits and also in water, do you not think so?

sn: सर्वं व्याप्तमिदं ब्रह्मन् प्राणिभिः प्राणिजीवनैः। मत्स्यान् चसन्ते मत्स्याश्च तत्र किं प्रतिभाति ते॥ सत्त्वैः सत्त्वानि जीवन्ति बहुधा द्विजसत्तम। प्राणिनोऽन्योन्यभक्षाश्च तत्र किं प्रतिभाति ते॥
en: O Brahmana, the whole universe is full of animals and animal organisms. Do you not see that fish preys upon fish and various other species of animals prey on various other animals and there are also some who prey upon one another.

sn: चक्रम्यमाणा जीवांश्च धरणीसंश्रितान् बहून्। पद्भ्यां नन्ति नरा विप्र तत्र किं प्रतिभाति ते॥
en: O Brahmana, a man kills innumerable animals that live in the ground by trampling them by their feet. What have you to say to this?

sn: उपविष्टाः शयानाश्च मन्ति जीवाननेकशः। ज्ञानविज्ञानवन्तश्च तत्र किं प्रतिभाति ते॥
en: Even wise and learned men kill many animals in various ways when sleeping or resting. What have you to say to this?

sn: जीदैर्चस्तमिदं सर्वमाकाशं पृथिवी तथा। अविज्ञानाच्च हिंसन्ति तत्र किं प्रतिभाति ते॥
en: The earth and the sky are all full of animal organisms. Which are unconsciously killed by men from ignorance, what have you to say to this?

sn: अहिंसेति यदुक्तं हि पुरुषैर्विस्मितैः पुरा। के न हिंसन्ति जीवान् वैलोकेऽस्मिन् द्विजसत्तम बहु संचित्य इति वै नास्ति कश्चिदहिंसकः॥
en: O foremost of men, who is there on earth who does not do harm to any creature? After full consideration, this is the conclusion (that I have come to that there is none who has not killed an animal.

sn: अहिंसायां तु निरता यतयो द्विजसत्तम। कुर्वन्त्येव हि हिंसां ते यत्नादल्पतरा भवेत्॥
en: O foremost of Brahmanas, even the Rishis whose vows are not to destroy animals, (do destroy animals). Only on account of their very great care, they commit less destruction (of animals).

sn: आलक्ष्याश्चैव पुरुषाः कुले जाता महागुणाः। महाघोराणि कर्माणि कृत्वा लज्जन्ति वै द्विज॥
en: Men of noble birth and great accomplishment perpetrate wicked acts in defiance of all and they are not ashamed of it.

sn: सुहृदः सुहृदोऽन्यांश्च दुर्हदश्चापि दुहृदः। सम्यक प्रवृत्तान् पुरुषान् न सम्यगनुपश्यतः॥
en: Good men acting in an exemplary way are not praised by other good men, nor bad men acting in a contrary way are praised by other wicked men.

sn: समृद्धैश्च न नन्दन्ति बान्धवा बान्धवैरपि। गुरूंश्चैव विनिन्दन्ति मूढाः पण्डितमानिनः॥
en: Friends are not agreeable to friends, however accomplished they might be. Foolish pedantic men (ever) find fault with the virtue of their preceptors.

sn: बहु लोके विपर्यस्तं दृश्यते द्विजसत्तम। धर्मयुक्तमधर्मं च तत्र किं प्रतिभाति ते॥
en: Such reverses of the natural orders of things, O foremost of Brahmanas, are always seen (in this world). What is your opinion as to the virtuousness or otherwise of this state of things?

sn: वक्तुं बहुविधं शक्यं धर्माधर्मेषु कर्मसु। स्वकर्मनिरतो यो ह स यशः प्राप्नुयान्महत्॥
en: There can be said many things as regards the goodness or the badness of our actions. But he who sticks to the Dharma of his own order acquires great fame.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच धर्मव्याधस्तु निपुणं पुनरेव युधिष्ठिर। विप्रर्षभमुवाचेदं सर्वधर्मभृतां वर॥
en: Markandeya said : O Yudhishthira, that foremost of all virtuous men, that pious fowler, then skillfully thus again spoke to that best of Brahmanas.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: व्याध उवाच श्रुतिप्रमाणो धर्मोऽयमिति वृद्धानुशासनम्। सूक्ष्मा गतिर्हि धर्मस्य बहुशाखा ह्यनन्तिका॥
en: The Fowler said: It is ordained by the old as found in the Shruti that the ways of virtue are subtle, diverse and infinite.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: प्राणान्तिके विवाहे च वक्तव्यमनृतं भवेत्। अनृतेन भवेत् सत्यं सत्येनैवानृतं भवेत्॥
en: In life being at risk and in marriage, it is proper to speak an untruth. Sometimes by untruth, truth is maintained and by truth untruth is maintained.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: यद् भूतहितमत्यन्तं तत् सत्यमिति धारणा। विपर्ययकृतोऽधर्मः पश्य धर्मस्य सूक्ष्मताम्॥
en: Whatever conduces to the greatest good of all creatures is considered to be the truth. Virtue is thus perverted. Do you mark its subtle ways?

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: यत् करोत्यशुभं कर्म शुभं वा यदि सत्तम। अवश्यं तत् समाप्नोति पुरुषो नात्र संशयः॥ विषमां च दशां प्राप्तो देवान् गर्हति वै भृशम्। आत्मनः कर्मदोषाणि न विजानात्यपण्डितः॥
en: O excellent one, man's actions are either good or bad and he undoubtedly reaps their fruits. The ignorant man, having attained to an object state, grossly abuses the gods, not knowing that it is the result of his own evil Karma.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: मूढो नैकृतिकश्चापि चपलश्च द्विजोत्तम। सुखदुःखविपर्यासान् सदा समुपपद्यते॥
en: O foremost of Brahmanas, the foolish men, designing men and the fickle men attain the very reverse of happiness or misery.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: नैनं प्रज्ञा सुनीतं वा त्रायते नैव पौरुषम्। योऽयमिच्छेद् यथा कामं तं तं कामं स आप्नुयात्।८॥ यदि स्यादपराधीनं पौरुषस्य क्रियाफलम्। संयताश्चापि दक्षाश्च मतिमन्तश्च मानवाः॥
en: Neither learning nor good morals, nor personal exertion can save them. If the fruits of one's exertions were not dependent on any thing else, men would have obtained the object of their desire by their own exertions. Able, intelligent and diligent men.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: दृश्यन्ते निष्फलाः सन्तः प्रहीणाः सर्वकर्मभिः। भूतानामयरः कश्चिद्धिंसायां सततोत्थितः॥ वञ्चनायां च लोकस्य स सुखी जीवते सदा। अचेष्टमपि चासीनं श्री: कंचिदुपतिष्ठति॥
en: Are seen to have been baffled in their efforts; and they attain the fruits of their actions. Persons who are always active in injuring others and in practising deception lead a happy life in this world. There are many who obtain prosperity without any exertion.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: कश्चित् कर्माणि कुर्वन् हि न प्राप्यमधिगच्छति। देवानिष्ट्वा तपस्तप्त्वा कृपणैः पुत्रगृद्धिभिः॥
en: There are other again who with the greatest exertion are unable to obtain what is their own dues. The miserly persons with the object of having sons worship the celestials and perform asceticism.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: दशमासधृता गर्भे जायन्ते कुलपांसनाः। अपरे धनधान्यैश्च भोगैश्च पितृसंचितैः॥
en: These sons, remaining for ten months in the womb, (when born) become the stains of their family. Other enjoy luxury, wealth and coins amassed by their ancestors.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: विपुलैरभिजायन्ते लब्धास्तैरेव मङ्गलैः। कर्मजा हि मनुष्याणां रोगा नास्त्यत्र संशयः॥ आधिभिश्चैव बाध्यन्ते व्याधैः क्षुद्रमृगा इव। ते चापि कुशलैवैद्यैर्निपुणैः सम्भृतौषधैः॥ व्याधयो विनिवार्यन्ते मृगा व्याधैरिव द्विज। येषामस्ति च भोक्तव्यं ग्रहणीदोषपीडिताः॥
en: The diseases froin which men suffers are certainly the result of their own Karma. They then behave like small deer in the hands of the hunters. They are afflicted with mental troubles. O Brahmana, as deer are stopped by the hunters, so these diseases are checked by able and skillful physician with their many drugs. Those that have objects of enjoyments suffer from severe bowl complaints.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: न शक्नुवन्ति ते भोक्तुं पश्य धर्मभृतां वर। अपरे बाहुबलिन: क्लिश्यन्ते बहवो जनाः॥
en: Behold, O foremost of all virtuous men, he cannot enjoy. O those who possess great strength of arms suffer from misery.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: दुःखेन चाधिगच्छन्ति भोजनं द्विजसत्तम। इति लोकमनाक्रन्दं मोहशोकपरिप्लुतम्॥
en: O foremost of Brahmanas, they are enabled to eain their livelihood with (only) good deal of difficulty. Thus men are helpless, afflicted with grief and illusion and

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: स्रोतसासकृदाक्षिप्तं ह्रियमाणं बलीयसा। न प्रियेयुर्न जीर्येयुः सर्वे स्युः सार्वकामिकाः॥ नाप्रियं प्रतिपश्येयुर्वशित्वं यदि वै भवेत्। उपर्युपरि लोकस्य सर्वो गन्तुं समीहते। यतते च यथाशक्ति न च तद् वर्तते तथा॥
en: Again and again tossed and overpowered by the powerful current of his own actions. If there were absolute freedom of action, then no creature would die and none would be subject to decay or await his evil doom. Every body would then attain the object of his desire. All persons try to excel their neighbours; they try to do it with the utmost of their power, but the result becomes the reverse.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: बहवः सम्प्रदृश्यन्ते तुल्यनक्षत्रमङ्गलाः। महच्च फलवैषम्यं दृश्यते कर्मसंधिषु॥
en: Many persons are born under the influence of the same star and the same auspicious good luck, but a great diversity is observed in all their actions.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: न केचिदीशते ब्रह्मन् स्वयंचाह्यस्य सत्तम। कर्मणां प्राक् कृतानां वै इह सिद्धिः प्रदृश्यते॥
en: O Brahmana, O excellent one, none can be the dispenser of his own destiny. The actions done in a former life is seen to produce fruits in this life.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: यथाश्रुतिरियं ब्रह्मन् जीवः किल सनातनः। शरीरमध्रुवं लोके सर्वेषां प्राणिनामिह॥
en: O Brahmana, it is said in the everlasting Shruti that the soul is eternal and everlasting, but the bodies of all creatures are liable to be destroyed here (in this world).

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: वध्यमाने शरीरे तु देहनाशो भवत्युत। जीवः सङ्क्रमतेऽन्यत्र कर्मबन्धनिबन्धनः॥
en: Thereupon when death occurs, only the body is destroyed, but the spirit bound in the bonds of actions goes elsewhere.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच कथं धर्मविदां श्रेष्ठ जीवो भवति शाश्वतः। एतदिच्छाम्यहं ज्ञातुं तत्त्वेन वदतां वर॥
en: The Brahmana said: O excellent one, learned in the mystery of Karma, O foremost of speakers, how does the spirit become eternal? I desire to hear this in detail.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: व्याध उवाच न जीवनाशोऽस्ति हि देहभेदे मिथ्यैतदाहुर्मियते किलेति। जीवस्तु देहान्तरितः प्रयाति दशार्धतैवास्य शरीरभेदः॥
en: The Fowler said : The spirit does not die, in death it simply has a change of abode. They are mistaken who foolishly say that all creatures are to die. The are never soul only goes to another body and its this change of abode is called the Death.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: अन्यो हि नाश्नाति कृतं हि कर्म मनुष्यलोके मनुजस्य कश्चित्। यत् तेन किंचिद्धि कृतं हि कर्म तदश्नुते नास्ति कृतस्य नाशः॥
en: In the world of men none reaps the fruits of another man's Karma. Whatever one does, he is sure to reap the fruits of his own actions, for the consequences of Karma destroyed.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: सुपुण्यशीला हि भवन्ति पुण्या नराधमाः पापकृतो भवन्ति। स्ततः समुत्पद्यति भावितस्तैः॥
en: The virtuous become endued with great virtue and the sinful become the perpetrators of wicked deeds. Men's actions follow them and influenced by these (fruits of his actions) they are born again.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच कथं सम्भवते योनौ कथं वा पुण्यपापयोः। जातीः पुण्यास्त्वपुण्याश्च कथं गच्छति सत्तम॥
en: The Brahmana said: Why does the soul take its birth and how does it become sinful or virtuous? O excellent one, how does it come to belong to a sinful or virtuous man?

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: व्याध उवाच गर्भाधानसमायुक्तं कर्मेदं सम्प्रदृश्यते। समासेन तु ते क्षिप्रं प्रवक्ष्यामि द्विजोत्तम॥ यथा सम्भृतसम्भारः पुनरेव प्रजायते। शुभकृच्छुभयोनीषु पापकृत् पापयोनिषु॥
en: The Fowler said: This mystery belongs to the subject of procreation, but I shall briefly describe it to you. O foremost of Brahmanas, the soul is again born with its accumulated load of Karina, the virtuous ones in the virtuous and the sinful ones in the sinful.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: शुभैः प्रयोगैर्देवत्वं व्यामिश्रर्मानुषो भवेत्। मोहनीयैर्वियोनीषु त्वधोगामी च किल्बिषी॥
en: By performing (only) virtuous actions, it attains to the state of the celestials. By a combination of good and bad (actions), it acquires the state of human beings. By indulging in sensuality and similar vicious propensities, it is born as lower animals and by sinful acts it goes to hell.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: जातिमृत्युजरादुःखैः सततं समभिद्रुतः। संसारे पच्यमानश्च दोषैरात्मकृतैर्नरः॥
en: Afflicted with the miseries of birth, death and dotage, man is destined to rot here (on earth) from the evil effects of his own actions (in a previous birth).

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: तिर्यग्योनिसहस्राणि गत्वा नरकमेव च। जीवाः सम्परिवर्तन्ते कर्मबन्धनिबन्धनाः॥
en: Passing through hell and also through thousands of various births, our souls bound by the bonds of their own Karma travel (for everlasting time).

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: जन्तुस्तुकर्मभिस्तैस्तैः स्वकृतैः प्रेत्य दुःखितः। तदुःखप्रतिघातार्थमपुण्यां योनिमाप्नुते॥
en: Animate creatures become miserable in the next world from their own actions and as the result of those miseries they are (again) born as lower animals.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: ततः कर्म समादत्ते पुनरन्यं नवं बहु। पच्यते तु पुनस्तेन भुक्त्वापथ्यमिवातुरः॥
en: Then they again accumulate a new store of actions and consequently they suffer misery over again, as does a discased man who eats unwholesome food.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: अजस्रमेव दुःखार्तोऽदुःखितः सुखसंज्ञितः। ततोऽनिवृत्तबन्धत्वात् कर्मणामुदयादपि॥
en: Although they are thus afflicted with misery, they consider themselves to be (very) happy and comfortable; and consequently their bonds (of Karma) are not loosened and new Karma thus again arises.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: परिक्रामति संसारे चक्रवद् बहुवेदनः। स वृत्तबन्धस्तु विशुद्धश्चापि कर्मभिः॥
en: Suffering from various miseries, they turn in this world like a wheel. If they cast off their bonds (of actions) and if they purify themselves by their actions,

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: तपोयोगसमारम्भं कुरुते द्विजसत्तम। कर्मभिर्बहुभिश्चापि लोकानश्नाति मानवः॥
en: If they perform asceticism and practise religious meditation, then, O foremost of Brahmanas, men by their these acts can attain to the region of bliss.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: स चेन्निवृत्तबन्धस्तु विशुद्धश्चापि कर्मभिः। प्राप्नोति सुकृताँल्लोकान् यत्र गत्वा न शोचति॥
en: By casting off their bonds (of Karma) and by purifying Karma, men attain those regions of bliss where misery is unknown.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: पापं कुर्वन् पापवृत्तः पापस्यान्तं न गच्छति। तस्मात् पुण्यं यतेत् कर्तुं वर्जयीत च पापकम्॥
en: The sinful man who is addicted to vices never comes to the end of his course of inequities. Therefore we must do what is virtuous and forbear from doing what is sinful.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: अनसूयुः कृतज्ञश्च कल्याणानि च सेवते। सुखानि धर्ममर्थं च स्वर्गं च लभते नरः॥
en: Whoever with a heart full of gratitude and free from malice try to do what is good, obtain wealth, virtue, happiness and heaven.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: संस्कृतस्य च दान्तस्य नियतस्य यतात्मनः। प्राज्ञस्यानन्तरा वृत्तिरिह लोके परत्र च॥
en: Those who are freed from sin, those who are wise, forbearing, righteous and self-controlled enjoy continuous bliss in this world and in the world next.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: सतां धर्मेण वर्तेत क्रियां शिष्टवदाचरेत्। असंक्लेशेन लोकस्य वृत्तिं लिप्सेत वै द्विज॥ सन्ति ह्यागमविज्ञानाः शिष्टाः शास्त्रे विचक्षणाः। स्वधर्मेण क्रिया लोके कर्मणः सोऽप्यसंकरः॥
en: O Brahmana, man must follow the standard of virtue of the good; and in his acts he must imitate the example of the virtuous. There are virtuous men learned in the holy Shastras and conversant in all moralities. Man's proper duty consists in his following his own proper avocations such being the case, these avocations never become confused and mixed up.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: प्राज्ञो धर्मेण रमते धर्मं चैवोपजीवति। तस्माद् धर्मादवाप्तेन घनेन द्विजसत्तम॥ तस्यैव सिञ्चते मूलं गुणान् पश्यति तत्र वै। धर्मात्मा भवति ह्येवं चित्तं चास्य प्रसीदति॥
en: The wise man delights in virtue and he lives by virtue. O foremost of Brahmanas, such a man with the wealth of virtue which he thus acquires waters the root of the plant (particular righteousness) in which he finds most virtue. The virtuous man thus acts and his mind becomes thus calin.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: स मित्रजनसंतुष्ट इह प्रेत्य च नन्दति। शब्दं स्पर्श तथा रूपं गन्धानिष्टांश्च सत्तम॥ प्रभुत्वं लभते चापि धर्मस्यैतत् फलं विदुः। धर्मस्य च फलं लख्वा न तृप्यति महाद्विज॥
en: He is pleased with his friend, in this world and he also enjoys happiness in the world next. O excellent one, know, virtuous men acquire sovereignty over all and obtain (the pleasure) of beauty, flavour, sound and touch according to their desire. O Brahmana, (an enlightened) man is not satisfied with the fruits of virtue.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: अतृप्यमाणो निर्वेदमापेदे ज्ञानचक्षुषा। प्रज्ञानक्षुर्नर इह दोषं नैवानुरुध्यते॥ विरज्यति यथाकामं न च धर्मं विमुञ्चति। सर्वत्यागे च यतते दृष्ट्वा लोकं क्षयात्मकम्॥ ततो मोक्षे प्रयतते नानुपायादुपायतः। एवं निर्वेदमादत्ते पापं कर्म जहाति च॥
en: Not satisfied with it, he with the light of spiritualism becomes indifferent to pain and pleasure; the worldly vices cannot influence him. Of his own free will, he becomes indifferent to all worldly pursuits, but he does not forsake virtue. Observing everything worldly as transcient, he tries to renounce everything and not calculating on mere chance, he devises means for the attainments of salvation. Thus does he renounce all worldly pursuits and shuns all sins.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: धार्मिक्श्चापि भवति मोक्षं च लभते परम्। तपो निःश्रेयसं जन्तोस्तस्य मूलं शमो दमः॥
en: He thus becomes virtucus and he thus finally attains salvation. Tara (meditation) is the chief requisite for obtaining salvation, resignation and forbearance are its roots.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: तेन सर्वानवाप्नोति कामान् यान् मनसेच्छति। इन्द्रियाणां निरोधेन सत्येन च दमेन च। ब्रह्मणः पदमाप्नोति यत् परं द्विजसत्तम।॥
en: By this means he obtains all the objects of his desire. By subduing his senses and by means of truthfulness and forbearness, O foremost of Brahmanas, he obtains the supreme state of Brahma.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच इन्द्रियाणि तु यान्याहुः कानि तानि यतव्रत। निग्रहश्च कथं कार्यो निग्रहस्य च किं फलम्॥ कथं च फलमाप्नोति तेषां धर्मभृतां वर। एतदिच्छामि तत्त्वेन धर्मं ज्ञातुं निबोध मे॥
en: The Brahmana said: O foremost of all virtuous and vowobserving men, you talk of the senses; what are they? How might they be subdued? What is the good of subduing them? How does a creature obtain the fruits of doing it? I eagerly desire to kuow all about these matters.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच एवमुक्तस्तु विप्रेण धमव्याधो युधिष्ठिर। प्रत्युवाच यथा विप्रं तच्छृणुष्व नराधिप॥
en: Markandeya said : O Yudhishthira, O ruler of men, hear what the virtuous fowler said to that Brahmana when he was thus asked by him.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: व्याध उवाच विज्ञानार्थं मनुष्याणां मनः पूर्वं प्रवर्तते। तत् प्राप्य कामं भजते क्रोधं च द्विजसत्तम॥
en: The Fowler said : O foremost of Brahmanas, men's minds are first bent towards acquiring knowledge. When that is acquired, they indulge in their desires and anger.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: ततस्तदर्थं यतते कर्म चारभते महत्। इष्टानां रूपगन्धानामभ्यासं च निषेवते॥
en: For that end, they labour and perform great works and indulge in their much desired pleasures of beauty, of flavour.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: ततो रागः प्रभवति द्वेषश्च तदनन्तरम्। ततो लोभः प्रभवति मोहश्च तदनन्तरम्॥
en: Then follows attachment, then follows envy, then avarice and then illusion (extinction of all spiritual light).

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: ततो लोभाभिभूतस्य रागद्वेषहतस्य च। न धर्मे जायते बुद्धिर्व्याजाद् धर्मं करोति च॥
en: When men are thus influenced by avarice, envy and attachment, their understanding does not lean towards virtue; and they then practise the very mockery of virtue.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: व्याजेन चरते धर्ममर्थ व्याजेन रोचते। व्याजेन सिध्यमानेषु धनेषु द्विजसत्तम॥ तत्रैव रमते बुद्धिस्तत: पापं चिकीर्षति। सुहद्भिर्वार्यमाणश्च पण्डितैश्च द्विजोत्तम॥
en: O foremost of Brahmanas, practising virtue with hypocracy, they remain satisfied in acquiring wealth by dishonourable means. And with the wealth thus acquired, their intelligence becomes attached to the evil ways; they were then filled with the desire to commit sins. O foremost of Brahmanas, when their friends and the learned men remonstrate.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: उत्तरं श्रुतिसम्बद्धं ब्रवीत्यश्रुतियोजितम्। अधर्मस्त्रिविधस्तस्य वर्तते रागदोषजः॥
en: They are ready with various answers which are neither sound nor convincing. From their attachment for evil ways, they are guilty of threefold sins.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: पापं चिन्तयते चैव ब्रवीति च करोति च। तस्याधर्मप्रवृत्तस्य गुणा नश्यन्ति साधवः॥
en: They commit sin in thought, in word and also in action. Addicted to evil ways, all their good qualities are destroyed.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: एकशीलैश्च मित्रत्वं भजन्ते पापकर्मिणः। स तेन दुःखमाप्नोति परत्र च विपद्यते॥
en: These men of evil deeds form friendship with men of similar character and therefore as its result, they suffer misery in this world as well as in the next.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: पापात्मा भवति ह्येवं धर्मलाभं तु मे तु में शृणु। यस्त्वेतान् प्रज्ञया दोषान् पूर्वमेवानुपश्यति॥ कुशलः सुखदुःखेषु साधूंश्चाप्युपसेवते। तस्य साधुसमारम्भाद् बुद्धिर्धर्मेषु राजते॥
en: All sinful men are of this nature. Now hear about the virtuous man. He discerns evils by means of his spiritual sight. He is able to discriminate between happiness and misery. He is full of respectful attention to men of virtue; and by practising virtues, his mind becomes inclined to virtue.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच ब्रवीषि सूनृतं धर्म्य यस्य वक्ता न विद्यते। दिव्यप्रभावः सुमहानृषिरेव मतोऽसि मे॥
en: The Brahmana said : You have given a true exposition of virtue which none else is able to do. Your spiritual power is great and you appear to me to be a great Rishi.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: व्याध उवाच ब्राह्मणा वै महाभागाः पितरोऽचभुजः सदा। तेषां सर्वात्मना कार्यं प्रियं लोके मनीषिणा॥
en: The Fowler said: are The greatly powerful Brahmanas worshipped with the same honours as our ancestors. They are before others always propitiated with offerings of food. Wisemen in this world do what is pleasing to them with all their heart.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: यत् तेषां च प्रियं तत् ते वक्ष्यामि द्विजसत्तम। नमस्कृत्वा ब्राह्मणेभ्यो ब्राह्मी विद्यां निबोध मे॥
en: O foremost of Brahmanas, after having bowed down to Brahmanas as a class I shall now tell you what is pleasing to them. Learn now the Brahma Philosophy,

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: जगत् सर्वमजय्यं चापि सर्वशः। महाभूतात्मकं ब्रह्म नातः परतरं भवेत्॥ इदं विश्वं
en: This whole universe, which is unconquerable and which abounds in great elements, is Brahma (himself). There is nothing high than this.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: महाभूतानि खं वायुरग्निरापस्तथा च भूः। शब्दः स्पर्शश्च रूपं च रसो गन्धश्च तहगुणाः॥
en: Earth, air, water and sky are the great elements. Form, flavour, sound, touch and taste are their characteristic properties.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: तेषामपि गुणाः सर्वे गुणवृत्तिः परस्परम्। पूर्वपूर्वगुणाः सर्वे क्रमशो गुणिषु त्रिषु॥
en: These latter also have their (own peculiar) properties correlated to each other. Of the three qualities they are characterised by each in order of priority.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: षष्ठस्तु चेतना नाम मन इत्यभिधीयते। सप्तमी तु भवेद् बुद्धिरहंकारस्ततः परम्॥
en: The sixth property is consciousness which is called mind. The seventh is intelligence and then follows Egoism,

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: इन्द्रियाणि च पञ्चात्मा रजः सत्त्वं तमस्तथा। इत्येष सप्तदशको राशिरव्यक्तसंज्ञकः॥ सर्वैरिहेन्द्रियार्थैस्तु व्यक्ताव्यक्तैः सुसंवृतः। चतुर्विंशक इत्येष व्यक्ताव्यक्तमयो गुणः। एतत् ते सर्वमाख्यातं किं भूयः श्रोतुमिच्छसि॥
en: Then are the five senses, then the soul, then the moral qualities, called, Sattva, Raja and Tama. These seventeen are said to be the unknown or incomprehensible qualities. I have told you all this, what else do you wish to know?

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच एवमुक्तः स विप्रस्तु धर्मव्याधेन भारत। कथामकथयद् भूयो मनसः प्रीतिवधनीम्॥
en: Markandeya said : O descendant of Bharata, having been thus addressed by that Brahmana, the virtuous fowler again began to speak (on things) so pleasing to the mind.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच महाभूतानि यान्याहुः पञ्च धर्मभृतां वर। एकैकस्य गुणान् सम्यक् पञ्चानामपि मे वद॥
en: The Brahmana said : O foremost of all virtuous men, it is said that there are five great elements. Will you describe to me in detail the properties of those five (elements)?

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: व्याध उवाच भूमिरापस्तथा ज्योतिर्वायुराकाशमेव च। गुणोत्तराणि सर्वाणि तेषां वक्ष्यामि ते गुणान्॥
en: The Fowler said: The earth, water, fire, air and sky, all have properties enter-lapping each other. I shall describe them to you.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: भूमिः पञ्चगुणा ब्रह्मन्नुदकं च चतुर्गुणम्। गुणास्त्रयस्तेजसि च त्रयश्चाकाशवातयोः॥
en: O Brahmana, the earth has five qualities, water four, fire three and the air and the sky together three.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: शब्दः स्पर्शश्च रूपं च रसो गन्धश्च पञ्चमः। एते गुणाः पञ्च भूमेः सर्वेभ्यो गुणवत्तरा॥
en: Sound, touch, form, flavour and taste, these five qualities belong to earth.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: शब्दः स्पर्शश्च रूपं च रसश्चापि द्विजोत्तम। अपामेते गुणा ब्रह्मन् कीर्तितास्तव सुव्रत॥
en: O foremost of Brahmanas, O twice-borm one, O vow-observing Rishi, sound, touch, form and taste have been described to you as the properties of water.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: शब्दः स्पर्शश्च रूपं च तेजसोऽथ गुणास्त्रयः। शब्दः स्पर्शश्च वायौ तु शब्दश्चाकाश एव तु॥
en: Sound, touch and form are the three properties of fire; sound and touch are the two properties of the air; and sound is the property of the sky.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: एते पञ्चदश ब्रह्मन् गुणा भूतेषु पञ्चसु। वर्तन्ते सर्वभूतेषु येषु लोकाः प्रतिष्ठिताः॥
en: O Brahmana, these fifteen fifteen properties inherent in five elements, exist in all substances of which this universe is composed.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: अन्योन्यं नातिवर्तन्ते सम्यक् च भवति द्विजा यदा तु विषमं भावमाचरन्ति चराचराः॥ तदा देही देहमन्यं व्यतिरोहति कालतः। आनुपूर्व्या विनश्यन्ति जायन्ते चानुपूर्वशः॥
en: O Brahmana, they are not opposed to one another; they exist in proper combination. When this universe is thrown into a state of chaos then every corporeal being in proper time assumes another body. It perishes also in due order.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: तत्र तत्र हि दृश्यन्ते धातवः पाञ्चभौतिकाः। यैरावृतमिदं सर्वं जगत् स्थावरजङ्गमम्॥ इन्द्रियैः सृज्यते यद् यत् तत् तद् व्यक्तमिति स्मृतम्। तदव्यक्तमिति ज्ञेयं लिङ्गचाह्यमतीन्द्रियम्॥
en: There (everlastingly) exist the five elementary substances of which all the mobile and immobile world is composed. Whatever is perceptible by the senses is called Vyakta (manifest) and whatever is not perceptible by the senses is called Avyakta (not manifest).

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: यथास्वं चाहकाण्येषां शब्दादीनामिमानि तु। इन्द्रियाणि यदा देही धारयन्निव तप्यते॥ लोके विततमात्मानं लोकं चात्मनि पश्यति। परावरज्ञो यः शक्तः स तु भूतानि पश्यति॥
en: When a person engages in Tapa after having duly subdued his senses which have their own proper objective play in the external conditions of sound, form, then he sees that his own spirit pervades the whole universe and the universe is also reflected in him.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: पश्यतः सर्वभूतानि सर्वावस्थासु सर्वदा। ब्रह्मभूतस्य संयोगो नाशुभेनोपपद्यते॥ अज्ञानमूलं तं क्लेशमतिवृत्तस्य पौरुषम्। लोकवृत्तिप्रकाशेन ज्ञानमार्गेण गम्यते॥ अनादिनिधनं जन्तुमात्मयोनिं सदाव्ययम्। अनौपम्यममूर्तं च भगवानाह बुद्धिमान्॥
en: He who is bound to the bonds of his previous Karma, although learned in the highest spiritual wisdom, is cognizant only of his own soul's objective existence, but the person whose soul is never affected by the objective conditions around is never subject to ills, owing to its absorption in the primal spirit of Brahma. When a person has overcome illusion, his manly virtues consisting the essence of spiritual wisdom turn to spiritual enlightenment which illuminates the intelligence of all beings.
