Such a being is called by the omnipotent, the intelligent one who is without beginning and without end, selfexistence, immutable, incorporeal and incomparable.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: तपोमूलमिदं सर्वं यन्मां विप्रानुपृच्छसि। इन्द्रियाण्येव संयम्य तपो भवति नान्यथा॥
en: O Brahmana, what you have enquired of me is the result of self-discipline. This selfdiscipline can only be acquired by subduing the senses. It can not be acquired by any other means.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: इन्द्रियाण्येव तत् सर्वं यत् स्वर्गनरकावुभौ। निगृहीतविसृष्टानि स्वर्गाय नरकाय च॥
en: Heaven and hell both are dependent on our senses. When subdued, they lead us to heaven and when indulged in, they lead us to hell.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: एष योगविधिः कृत्स्नो यावदिन्द्रियधारणम्। एतन्मूलं हि तपसः कृत्स्नस्य नरकस्य च।॥
en: This subjugation of the senses is the highest means of attaining spiritual advancement; it is also at the root of all our spiritual degradation.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: इन्द्रियाणां प्रसङ्केन दोषमार्छन्त्यसंशयम। संनियम्य तु तान्येव ततः सिद्धिं समाप्नुयात्॥
en: By indulging in them, a person contracts vices and by bringing them under control, he attains salvation.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: घण्णामात्मनि नित्यानामैश्वर्यं योऽधिगच्छति। न स पापैः कुतोऽनर्थैर्युज्यते विजितेन्द्रियः॥
en: The self-controlled man who acquires over his six senses is never tainted with win; and consequently evil has no power over him.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: मात्मा नियन्तेन्द्रियाण्याहुरश्वान्। र्दान्तः सुखं याति रथीव धीरः॥
en: Man's body has been compared with a chariot, his soul with a charioteer and his senses with the horses. A skillful man drives about without confusion, like an able charioteer with well-broken horses.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: षण्णामात्मनि युक्तानामिन्द्रियाणां प्रमाथिनाम्। यो धीरो धारयेद् रश्मीन् स स्यात् परमसारथिः॥
en: That man is an excellent driver who knows how to patiently wield the reins of these and horses, namely the six senses inherent in our nature.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: इन्द्रियाणां प्रसृष्टानां हयानामिव वर्त्मसु। धृतिं कुर्वीत सारथ्ये धृत्या तानि जयेद् ध्रुवम्॥
en: When our senses become ungovernable like horses on the road, we must patiently rein them in, for with patience we are sure to get the better of them.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: इन्द्रियाणां विचरतां यन्मनोऽनु विधीयते। तदस्य हरते बुद्धिं नावं वायुरिवाम्भसि॥
en: When man's mind is overpowered by any one of these senses running wild, he loses his reason and becomes like a ship tossed by the tempest in the sea.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: येषु विप्रतिपद्यन्ते षट्सु मोहात् फलागमम्। तेष्वध्यवसिताध्यायी विन्दते ध्यानजं फलम्॥
en: Men are deceived by illusion in hoping to reap the fruit of those six things the effects of which are studied by persons of spiritual insight who thereby reap the fruits of their clear perception.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच एवं तु सूक्ष्मे कथिते धर्मव्याधेन भारत। ब्राह्मणः स पुनः सूक्ष्मं पप्रच्छ सुसमाहितः॥
en: Markandeya said : O descendant of Bharata, when the fowler expounded these abstruse points, the Brahmana with great attention asked about other subtle points.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच सत्त्वस्य रजसश्चैव तमसश्च यथातथम्। गुणांस्तत्त्वेन मे ब्रूहि यथावदिह पृच्छतः॥
en: The Brahmana said: Truly describe to me who duly now ask you tne respective virtues of the three qualities, namely Sattva, Raja and Tama.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: व्याध उवाच हन्त ते कथयिष्यामि यन्मां त्वं परिपृच्छसि। एषां गुणान् पृथक्त्वेन निबोध गदतो मम॥
en: I shall tell you what you ask me. I shall separately describe to you their respective virtues. Listen to them.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: मोहात्मकं तमस्तेषां रज एषां प्रवर्तकम्। प्रकाशबहुलत्वाच्च सत्त्वं ज्याय इहोच्यते॥
en: Tama is characterised by illusion, Raja incites men to action, Sattva is of great splendour and therefore it is called the greatest of them all.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: अविद्याबहुलो मूढः स्वप्नशीलो विचेतनः। दुर्हषीकस्तमोध्वस्तः सक्रोधस्तामसोऽलसः॥
en: He who is greatly under the influence of spiritual ignorance, who is foolish, senseless and given to (day) dreaming, who is idle, unenergetic, full of anger and haughtiness, is said to be under the influence of Tama.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: प्रवृत्तवाक्यो मन्त्री च यो नरावयोऽनसूयकः। विधित्समानो विप्रर्षे स्तब्धो मानी स राजसः॥
en: O Brahmana Rishi, that excellent man who is agreeable in speech, thoughtful, free from envy, industrious in action from an eager desire to reap its fruits and of warm temperament, is said to be under the influence of Raja.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: प्रकाशबहुलो धीरो निर्विधित्सोऽनसूयकः। अक्रोधनो नरो धीमान् दान्तश्चैव स सात्त्विकः॥
en: He who is resolute, patient, not subject to anger, free from malice and is not skillful in action from want of a selfish desire to reap its fruits and who is wise and forbearing, is said to be under the influence of Sattva.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: सात्त्विकस्त्वथ सम्बुद्धो लोकवृत्तेन क्लिश्यते। यदा बुध्यति बोद्धव्यं लोकवृत्तं जुगुप्सते॥ वैराग्यस्य च रूपं तु पूर्वमेव प्रवर्तते। मृदुर्भवत्यहङ्कारः प्रसीदत्यार्जवं च यत्॥ ततोऽस्य सर्वद्वन्द्वानि प्रशाम्यन्ति परस्परम्। न चास्य संशयो नाम क्वचिद् भवति कश्चन॥
en: When a man endued with Sattva quality is influenced by worldliness he suffers misery but he hates worldliness when he realises its full significance. Then a feeling of indifference to worldly affairs begins to influence him. And then his pride decreases and uprightness becomes more prominent. His conflicting moral sentiments are reconciled and then selfrestraint in any matter (for him) becomes unnecessary.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: शूद्रयोनौ हि जातस्य सहगुणानुपतिष्ठतः। वैश्यत्वं लभते ब्रह्मन् क्षत्रियत्वं तथैव च॥ आर्जवे वर्तमानस्य ब्राह्मण्यमभिजायते। गुणास्ते कीर्तिताः सर्वे किं भूयः श्रोतुमिच्छसि॥
en: O Brahmana, a man may be born as a Shudra but if he is endued with good qualities, he may attain to the state of a Vaishya. Similarly that of a Kshatriya and if he is steadfast in rectitude he may even become a Brahmana. I have described to you all these virtues, what else do you wish to learn.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच पार्थिव धातुमासाद्य शारीरोऽग्निः कथं भवेत्। अवकाशविशेषेण कथं वर्तयतेऽनिलः।।।।
en: The Brahmana said: How is it that the (vital) fire in combination with the earthly elements (matter) becomes the corporeal (living creatures)? And how does the (vital) air (the breath) according to the nature of its seat excites to action (the corporeal living creatures)?

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच प्रश्नमेतं समुद्दिष्टं ब्राह्मणेन युधिष्ठिर। व्याधस्तु कथयामास ब्राह्मणाय महात्मने।॥
en: Markandeya said : O Yudhishthira, this question being put to the fowler by the Brahmana, the fowler thus replied to that high-souled Brahmana.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: व्याध उवाच मूर्धानमाश्रितो वह्निः शरीरं परिपालयन्। प्राणो मूर्धनि चाग्नौ च वर्तमानो विचेष्टते॥
en: The Fowler said: The vital spirit manifesting itself it seat the consciousness causes the action of the corporeal frame. The soul being present in both of these acts.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: भूतं भव्यं भविष्यं च सर्वं प्राणे प्रतिष्ठितम्। श्रेष्ठं तदेव भूतानां ब्रह्मयोनिमुपास्महे॥
en: The past, the present and the future are inseparably associated with the soul. It is the highest of the possessions of all creatures. It is the essence of Supreme Spirit and we adore it.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: स जन्तुः सर्वभूतात्मा पुरुषः स सनातनः। महान् बुद्धिरहङ्कारो भूतानां विषयश्च सः॥
en: It is the animating principle of all creatures, it is the eternal Purusha. It is great, it is the intelligence and it is the Ego, it is the seat of all elements.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: एवं त्विह स सर्वत्र प्राणेन परिपाल्यते। पृष्ठतस्तु समानेन स्वां स्वां गतिमुपाश्रितः॥
en: Thus while seated here (in the corporeal form), it is sustained in all its external or internal relations by the subtle eternal air called Prana and afterwards each creature goes its own way by the action of another subtle air called Samana.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: बस्तिमूलं गुदं चैव पावकं समुपाश्रितः। वहन् मूत्रं पूरीषं वाप्यपान: परिवर्तते॥
en: This (Samana) transforming itself to Apana air and supported by the head of the stomach carries the refuge matter of the body, such as urine to the kidneys and intestines.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: प्रयत्ने कर्मणि बले स एष त्रिषु वर्तते। उदानमिति तं प्राहुरध्यात्मविदुषो जनाः॥
en: It is present in the three elements of actions, exertion and power and then in that state is called Udana by men learned in the physical science.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: संधौ संधौ संनिविष्टः सर्वेष्वपि तथानिलः। शरीरेषु मनुष्याणां व्यान इत्युपदिश्यते॥
en: When it manifests itself by its presence at all the junction points of the system, it is known by the name of Vyana.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: धातुष्वग्निस्तु विततः स तु वायुसमीरितः। रसान् धातूंश्च दोषांश्च वर्तयन् परिधावति॥
en: The internal heat is diffused over all the tissues of our system and supported by these kinds of air, it transforms our food and the tissues and the humours of our system.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: प्राणानां संनिपातात् तु संनिपातः प्रजायते। ऊष्मा चाग्निरिति ज्ञेयो योऽन्नं पचति देहिनाम्॥
en: By the coalition of Prana and other airs, a reaction ensues and the heat generated thereby is known as the internal heat of the human system which causes digestion of food.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: समानोदानयोर्मध्ये प्राणापानौ समाहितौ। समर्थितस्त्वधिष्ठानं सम्यक् पचति पावकः॥
en: The Prana and the Apana airs are interposed within the Samana and the Udana airs. The heat generated by their coalition causes the growth of the body.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: अस्यापि पायुपयन्तस्तथा स्याद् गुदसंज्ञितः। स्रोतांसि तस्माज्जायन्ते सर्वप्राणेषु देहिनाम्॥ अग्निवेगवहः प्राणो गुदान्ते प्रतिहन्यते। स ऊर्ध्वमागम्य पुनः समुत्क्षिपति पावकम्॥ पक्काशयस्त्वधो नाभ्यामूर्ध्वमामाशयः स्थितः। नाभिमध्ये शरीरस्य प्राणाः सर्वे प्रतिष्ठिताः॥
en: That portion of its seat extending to as far as the rectum, is called Apana and from that, arteries arise in the five airs Prana. Prana acted on by the heat, strikes against the extremity of Apana region and then recoiling, it reacts on the heat. Above the navel is the region of undigest food and below it, the region of digestion. Prana and all other airs of the system are seated in the navel.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: प्रवृत्ता हृदयात् सर्वे तिर्यगूर्ध्वमधस्तथा। वहन्त्यन्नरसान् नाड्यो दशप्राणप्रचोदिताः॥
en: The arteries issuing from the heart run upwards and downwards and also in oblique directions, they carry the best essence of our food and are acted upon by the ten Prana airs.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: योगिनामेष मार्गस्तु येन गच्छन्ति तत् परम्। जितक्लमाः समा धीरा मूर्धन्यात्मानमादधुः। एवं सर्वेषु विततौ प्राणापानौ हि देहिषु॥
en: This is the way, by which go to the highest state, the Yogis who have overcome all difficulties who are patient and self-controlled and who have their souls seated in their brains. The Prana and Apana are thus present in all creatures.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: एकादशविकारात्मा कलासम्भारसम्भृतः। मूर्तिमन्तं हि तं विद्धि नित्यं योगजितात्मकम्॥ तस्मिन् यः संस्थितो ह्यग्निर्नित्यं स्थाल्यामिवाहितः। आत्मानं तं विजानीहि नित्यं योगजितात्मकम्॥ देवो यः संस्थितस्तस्मिन्नबिन्दुरिव पुष्करे। क्षेत्रज्ञं तं विजानीहि नित्यं योगजितात्मकम्॥ जीवात्मकानि जानीहि रजः सत्त्वं तमस्तथा। जीवमात्मगुणं विद्धि तथाऽऽत्मानं परात्मकम्॥
en: Know that the soul is embodied in the corporeal disguise, in the eleven alloteopus conditions (of the animal system) and that though eternal, its normal state is apparently modified by its accompaniments even like the fire purified in its pan, eternal yet with its course altered by its surroundings; and that the divine thing which is kindred with the body is related to the latter in the same way as a drop of water to sleek surface of a lotus leaf on which it rolls; know that Sattva Raja and Tama are the attributes of all life. Life is the attribute of spirit and spirit again is the attribute of the Supreme Soul.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: अचेतनं जीवगुणं वदन्ति स चेष्टते चेष्टयते च सर्वम्। ततः परं क्षेत्रविदो वदन्ति प्राक्लपयद् यो भुवनानि सप्त॥
en: Inert and insensible matter is the seat of the living principle which is active in itself and induces activity in others. That by which the seven worlds are incited to action is called the most high by men of high spiritual insight.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: एवं सर्वेषु भूतेषु भूतात्मा सम्प्रकाशते। दृश्यते त्वङ्घयया बुद्ध्या सूक्ष्मया ज्ञानवेदिभिः॥
en: Thus in all these elements the eternal spirit does not show itself, but is perceived by the learned in spiritual science by reason of their high and keen perception.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: चित्तस्य हि प्रसादेन हन्ति कर्म शुभाशुभम्। प्रसन्नात्माऽऽत्मनि स्थित्वा सुखमानन्त्यमश्नुते॥
en: A pure-minded man, by purifying his heart, is able to destroy the good and evil effects of his actions and obtains eternal bliss by the enlightenment of his inner spirit.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: लक्षणं तु प्रसादस्य यथा तृप्तः सुखं स्वपेत्। निवाते वा यथा दीपो दीप्येत् कुशलदीपितः॥
en: This state of peace and purification of heart is likened to the state of a person who, in a cheerful state of mind, sleeps soundly or to the brilliance of a lamp trimmed by a skillful hand.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: पूर्वरात्रे परे चैव युञ्जानः सततं मनः। लध्वाहारो विशुद्धात्मा पश्यन्नात्मानमात्मनि॥ प्रदीप्तेनेव दीपेन मनोदीपेन पश्यति। दृष्ट्वाऽऽत्मानं निरात्मानं स तदा विप्रमुच्यते॥
en: Such a pure-minded man living on frugal diet perceives the supreme spirit reflected in his own mind and by practising concentration of mind in the evening and early in the morning sees the Supreme Spirit which has no attributes, in the light of his heart, shining like a dazzling lamp and thus he obtains salvation.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: सर्वोपायैस्तु लोभस्य क्रोधस्य च विनिग्रहः एतत् पवित्रं लोकानां तपो वै संक्रमो मतः॥
en: Avarice and anger must be subdued by all means, for this constitutes the most sacred virtue that people can practice. It is considered to be the means by which men cross over to the other side of this sea of misery and pair.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: नित्यं क्रोधात् तपो रक्षेद् धर्म रक्षेच्च मत्सरात्। विद्यां मानापमानाभ्यामात्मानं तु प्रमादतः॥
en: A man must preserve his virtue, being overcome by anger, his righteousness by pride, his learning by vanity and his soul by illusion.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: आनृशंस्यं परो धर्मः क्षमा च परम बलम्। आत्मज्ञानं परं ज्ञानं सत्यं व्रतपरं व्रतम्॥
en: Leniency is the best of virtues and forbearance is the best of the powers; the knowledge of the spirit is the best of all knowledge and truthfulness is the best of religious vows.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: सत्यस्य वचनं श्रेयः सत्यं ज्ञानं हितं भवेत्। यद् भूतहितमत्यन्तं तद् वै सत्यं परं मतम्॥
en: To tell the truth is good and the knowledge of truth also is good, but what conduces to the greatest good of all creatures is known as the highest truth.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: यस्य सर्वे समारम्भा निराशीर्बन्धनाः सदा। त्यागे यस्य हुतं सर्वं स त्यागी स च बुद्धिमान्॥
en: He whose actions are performed not with the object of securing any reward or blessing, who has sacrificed all to the requirements of his renunciation is a real Sanyasi and is really wise.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: यतो न गुरुरप्येनं श्रावयेदुपपादयेत्। तं विद्याद् ब्रह्मणो योगं वियोग योगसंज्ञितम्॥
en: Communion with Brahma cannot be taught to us even by our spiritual preceptor; he can only give us a clue to the mystery; renunciation of things of the material world is called Yoga.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: न हिंस्यात् सर्वभूतानि मैत्रायगणतश्चरेत्। नेदं जीवितमासाद्य वैरं कुर्वीत केनचित्॥
en: We must not do harm to any creature and must live in amity with all. In this our present existence we must not avenge ourselves on any creature.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: आकिञ्चन्यं सुसंतोषो निराशित्वमचापलम्। एतदेव परं ज्ञानं सदात्मज्ञानमुत्तमम्॥
en: Self-abnegation, peace of mind, renunciation of hope and equanimity, these are the ways by which spiritual enlightenment can always be secured. The knowledge of self is the best of all knowledge.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: परिग्रहं परित्यज्य भवेद् बुद्ध्या यतव्रतः। अशोकं स्थानमाश्रित्य निश्चलं प्रेत्य चेह च॥
en: It this world as well as in the next, renouncing all worldly desires and assuming a stolid indifference, in which all suffering is at rest, people should fulfill their religious duties with the aid of their intelligence.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: तपोनित्येन दान्तेन मुनिना संयतात्मना। अजितं जेतुकामेन भाव्यं सङ्गेष्वसङ्गिना॥
en: The Rishi who desires to obtain salvation which is very difficult to obtain, must always perform austerities, must be forbearing, selfcontrolled and must give up that longing fondness which binds him to the things of the earth.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: गुणागुणमनासङ्गमेककार्यमनन्तरम्। एतत् तद् ब्रह्मणो वृत्तमाहुरेकपदं सुखम्॥ परित्यजति यो दुःखं सुखं चाप्युभयं नरः। ब्रह्म प्राप्नोति सोऽत्यन्तमसङ्गेन च गच्छति॥
en: The attributes that are perceptible in us become non-attributes in Him. He is not bound by anything. He is perceptible only by the expansion and development of our spiritual vision. As soon as the illusion of ignorance is dispelled, this supreme and unalloyed bliss is obtained. By foregoing the objects of both pleasure and pain and by renouncing the feeling which binds him to the things of the earth, one attains to Brahma.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: यथाश्रुतमिदं सर्वं समासेन द्विजोत्तम। एतत् ते सर्वमाख्यातं किं भूयः श्रोतुमिच्छसि॥
en: O excellent Brahmana, I have told you in brief all that I have heard. What else do you desire to hear.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच एवं संकथिते कृत्स्ने मोक्षधर्मे युधिष्ठिर। दृढप्रीतमना विप्रो धर्मव्याधमुवाच ह॥
en: Markandeya said : O Yudhishthira, when all this about the mystery of salvation was told to the Brahmana, he was highly pleased. He then thus spoke to the virtuous Fowler.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: न्याययुक्तमिदं सर्वं भवता परिकीर्तितम्। न तेऽस्त्यविदितं किंचिद् धर्मेष्विह हि दृश्यते॥
en: The Brahmanas said: All this that you have told me is rational. It appears that there is nothing in connection with the mysteries of religion which you do not know.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: व्याध उवाच प्रत्यक्षं मम यो धर्मस्तं च पश्य द्विजोत्तम। येन सिद्धिरियं प्राप्ता मया ब्राह्मणपुङ्गव॥
en: The Fowler said: O foremost of Brahmanas, chief of the twice-born, behold with your own eyes all the virtues that I possess and by reason of which I have attained to this success (blissful state).

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: उत्तिष्ठ भगवन् क्षिप्रं प्रविश्याभ्यन्तरं गृहम्। द्रष्टुमर्हसि धर्मज्ञ मातरं पितरं च मे॥
en: O exalted one, arise, soon enter this inner apartment. O virtuous one, you should see (first) my father and my mother.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच इत्युक्तः स प्रविश्याथ ददर्श परमार्चितम्। सौधं हृद्यं चतुःशालमतीव च मनोरमम्॥ देवतागृहसंकाशं दैवतैश्च सुपूजितम्। शयनासनसम्बाधं गन्धैश्च परमैयुतम्॥
en: Markandeya said : Having been thus addressed, he went in and saw a magnificent and charming house, divided in suits of rooms, resembling the abode of the celestials adorned by the gods. It was furnished with seats and beds and filled with excellent perfumes.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: तत्र शुक्लाम्बरधरौ पितरावस्य पूजितौ। कृताहारौ तु संतुष्टावुपविष्टौ वरासने। धर्मव्याधस्तु तौ दृष्ट्वा पादेषु शिरसापतत्॥
en: His adorable parents, after their meal, were comfortably seated there on excellent seats, with white robes on. Seeing them the Fowler prostrated himself before them with his head at their feet.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: वृद्धावूचतुः उत्तिष्ठोत्तिष्ठ धर्मज्ञ धर्मस्त्वामभिरक्षतु। प्रीतौ स्वस्तव शौचेन दीर्घमायुरवाप्नुहि॥
en: The Aged ones said: O virtuous one, arise, arise, may virtue protect you. We are much pleased with your virtue. Be blessed with a long life,

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: गतिमिष्टां तपो ज्ञानं मेधां च परमां गतः। सत्पुत्रेण त्वया पुत्र नित्यं काले सुपूजितौ॥
en: And with knowledge, high intelligence and fulfillment of your desires. O son, you are good and dutiful son, we are always taken care by you.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: न तेऽन्यद् दैवतं किंचिद् दैवतेष्वपि वर्तते। प्रयतत्वाद् द्विजातीनां दमेनासि समन्वितः॥
en: There is not even among the celestials such a one as to deserve worship from you. By always subduing your senses you have acquired the self-control of the twice born.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: पितुः पितामहा ये च तथैव प्रपितामहाः। प्रीतास्ते सततं पुत्र दमेनावां च पूजया॥
en: Your father, grand-father and great grandfathers are, O son, always pleased with you, for your (great) self-control and for your reverence for us.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: मनसा कर्मणा वाचा शुश्रूषा नैव हीयते। न चान्या हि तथा बुद्धिदृश्यते साम्प्रतं तव॥
en: In thought, in word or in action, your attention to us never flags and it appears, even at present, that you have no other thought in your mind.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: जामदग्न्येन रामेण यथा वृद्धौ सुपूजितौ। तथा त्वया कृतं सर्वं तद्विशिष्टं च पुत्रक॥
en: O son, as the son of Jamadagni, Rama tried to serve his old parents, so have you done to please us, nay you have done more.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: ततस्तं ब्राह्मणं ताभ्यां धर्मव्याधो न्यवेदयत्। तौ स्वागतेन तं विप्रमर्चयामासतुस्तदा॥
en: Then the virtuous Fowler introduced the Brahmana to his parents; they received him with the usual salutation of welcome.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: प्रतिपूज्य च तां पूजां द्विजः पप्रच्छ तावुभौ। सुपुत्राभ्यां सभृत्याभ्यां कच्चिद् वां कुशलं गृहे॥ अनामयं च वां कच्चित् सदैवेह शरीरयोः।
en: The Brahmana accepting their welcome, enquired if they with their children and servants were well and if they were always enjoying good health.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: वृद्धावूचतुः कुशलं नौ गृहे विप्र भृत्यवर्गे च सर्वशः। कच्चित् त्वमप्यविघ्नेन सम्प्राप्तो भगवन्निति॥
en: The aged ones said : O Brahmana, we are all well in our home with all our servants. O exalted, one, have you come here without any difficulty?

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच बाढमित्येव तौ विप्रः प्रत्युवाच मुदान्वितः। धर्मव्याधो निरीक्ष्याथ ततस्तं वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
en: Markandeya said : The Brahmana replied in gladness by saying, “Yes, I am not face any difficulty". Then the virtuous Fowler thus spoke to the Brahmana.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: व्याध उवाच पिता माता च भगवन्नेतौ मदैवतं परम्। यद् दैवतेभ्यः कर्तव्यं तदेताभ्यां करोम्यहम्॥
en: The Fowler said: O exalted one, these my father and mother are the idols I worship with whatever adoration due to the gods.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: त्रयस्त्रिंशद् यथा देवाः सर्वे शक्रपुरोगमाः। सम्पूज्याः सर्वलोकस्य तथा वृद्धाविमौ मम॥
en: Thirty three million gods with Indra at their head, are worshipped by all men, so are these aged parents of mine worshipped by me.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: उपाहारनाहरन्तो देवतानां यथा द्विजाः। कुर्वन्ति तद्वदेताभ्यां करोम्यहमतन्द्रितः॥
en: As the Brahmanas try to procure offerings for their gods, so do I, with diligence for these two (my aged parents).

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: एतौ मे परमं ब्रह्मन् पिता माता च दैवतम्। एतौ पुष्पैः फलै रस्स्तोषयामि सदा द्विज॥
en: O Brahmana, these my father and mother are my supreme gods. O twice-born one, I always try to gratify them with the offering of fruits, flowers and gems.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: एतावेवाग्नयो मह्यं यान् वदन्ति मनीषिणः। यज्ञा वेदाच चत्वारः सर्वमेतौ मम द्विज॥
en: To me they are like the three sacred fires mentioned by the learned. O Brahmana, they are to me as the sacrifices in the four Vedas.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: एतदर्थं मम प्राणा भार्या पुत्रः सुहृज्जनः। सपुत्रदारः सुश्रूषां नित्यमेव करोम्यहम्॥
en: My five vital airs, my wife, children and friends are all for them. With my wife and my children, I always serve them.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: स्वयं च स्नापयाम्येतौ तथा पादौ प्रधावये। आहारं च प्रयच्छामि स्वयं च द्विजसत्तम॥
en: O foremost of Brahmanas, with my own hands I assist them in bathing; I also wash their feet, I give them food.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: अनुकूलं तथा वच्मि विप्रियं परिवर्जये। अधर्मेणापि संयुक्तं प्रियमाभ्यां करोम्यहम्॥
en: I speak to them only what is agreeable, avoiding all that is unpleasant and disagreeable. I even do that which is not virtuous, to please them.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: धर्ममेव गुरुं ज्ञात्वा करोमि द्विजसत्तम। अतन्द्रितः सदा विप्र शुश्रूषां वै करोम्यहम्॥ पञ्चैव गुरवो ब्रह्मन् पुरुषस्य बुभूषतः। पिता माताग्निरात्मा च गुस्च द्विजसत्तम॥ एतेषु यस्तु वर्तेत सम्यगेव द्विजोत्तम। भवेयुरग्नयस्तस्य परिचीर्णास्तु नित्यशः। गार्हस्थ्ये वर्तमानस्य एष धर्मः सनातनः॥
en: O foremost of the twice-born, O Brahmanas, I am always diligent in always waiting upon them. The parents, the sacred, fire, the soul, the preceptor, these five. O foremost of Brahmanas deserve the highest worship from a person who seeks prosperity. By properly serving them, one acquires the merit of perpetually keeping up the sacred fires. It is the eternal and invariable duty of all who lead domestic life.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच गुरुं निवेद्य विप्राय तौ मातापितरावुभौ। पुनरेव स धर्मात्मा व्याधो ब्राह्मणमब्रवीत्॥
en: Markandeya said : Having introduced both of his parents to that Brahmanas as his highest Gurus that virtuousminded fowler again thus spoke to the Brahmana.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: प्रवृत्तचक्षुर्जातोऽस्मि सम्पश्य तपसो बलम्। यदर्थमुक्तोऽसि तया गच्छ त्वं मिथिलामिति॥ पतिशुश्रूषपरया दान्तया सत्यशीलया। मिथिलायां वसेद् व्याधः स ते धर्मान् प्रवक्ष्यति॥
en: The Fowler said: Behold the power of my this virtue by which iny spiritual vision has extended. For this reason you were told by that self-controlled and truthful and chaste lady, 'Go to Mithila, there lives a Fowler who will explain to you the mysteries of religion.'

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच पतिव्रतायाः सत्यायाः शीलाढ्याया यतव्रता संस्मृत्य वाक्यं धर्मज्ञ गुणवानसि मे मतः॥
en: The Brahmana said: O virtuous and vow-observing man, thinking of what that truthful, well-behaved and chaste lady told me, I am of opinion, that you really possess very high qualities.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: व्याध उवाच यत् तदा त्वं द्विजश्रेष्ठ तयोक्तो मां प्रति प्रभो। दृष्टमेव तया सम्यगेकपल्या न संशयः॥
en: The Fowler said: O foremost of Brahmanas, O Lord, what that chaste lady told you about me, was certainly said with full knowledge of the facts.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: त्वदनुग्रहबुद्ध्या तु विप्रेतद् दर्शितं मया। वाक्यं च शृणु मे तात यत् ते वक्ष्ये हितं द्विज॥
en: O sire, I have explained to you all this as a matter of favour. O Brahmana, hear what will be good for you.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: त्वया विनिकृता माता पिता च द्विजसत्तम। अनिसृष्टोऽसि निष्क्रान्तो गृहात् ताभ्यामनिन्दित॥
en: O foremost of Brahmanas, O faultless one, you have wronged your father and mother, for you have left home for learning the Vedas without their permission.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: वेदोच्चारणकार्यार्थमयुक्तं तत् त्वया कृतम्। तव शोकेन वृद्धौ तावन्धीभूतौ तपस्विनौ॥
en: You have not properly acted in this matter, for your ascetic and aged parents have become completely blind from grief at your loss.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: तौ प्रसादयितुं गच्छ मा त्वां धर्मोऽत्यगादयम्। तपस्वी त्वं महात्मा च धर्मे च निरतः सदा॥
en: Go back to please them. May this virtue never forsake you. You are an ascetic, you are high-souled; you are always devoted to your religion,

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: सर्वमेतदपार्थं ते क्षिप्रं तौ सम्प्रसादय। श्रद्दधस्व मम ब्रह्मन् नान्यथा कर्तुमर्हसि। गम्यतामद्य विप्रर्षे श्रेयस्ते कथयाम्यहम्॥
en: But all has become in vain, therefore soon go back to console your parents. Have regard for my words and do not act in any other way. I tell you what is good for you, O Brahmana return even today.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच यदेतदुक्तं भवथा सर्वं सत्यमसंशयम्। प्रीतोऽस्मि तव भद्रं ते धर्माचारगुणान्वित॥
en: The Brahmana said: man of virtuous practices, what you have said is certainly true. Be blessed, I am much pleased with you.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: व्याध उवाच दैवतप्रतिमो हि त्वं यस्त्वं धर्ममनुव्रतः। पुराणं शाश्वतं दिव्यं दुष्प्राप्यमकृतात्मभिः॥ मातापित्रोः सकाशं हि गत्वा त्वं द्विजसत्तम। अतन्द्रितः कुरु क्षिप्रं मातापित्रोर्हि पूजनम्। अतः परमहं धर्मं नान्यं पश्यामि कंचन॥
en: The Fowler said: O foremost of Brahmanas, as you assiduously practise these divine, ancient and eternal virtues which are so difficult to be acquired even by pure-minded men, you seem to be a divine being. Return soon to the side of your parents and be quick and diligent in honouring your father and mother, for I do not know, if there is any virtue higher than this.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच इहाहमागतो दिष्ट्या दिष्ट्या मे सङ्गतं त्वया। ईदृशा दुर्लभा लोके नरा धर्मप्रदर्शकाः॥
en: The Brahmana said: By good luck, I have come here and by good luck I have met with you. Such expounders of religion are difficult to get in this world.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: एको नरसहस्रेषु धर्मविद् विद्यते न वा। प्रीतोऽस्मि तव सत्येन भद्रं ते पुरुषर्षभ॥
en: There is hardly one man amongst one thousand, who is leaned in the mysteries of religion. O foremost of men, I am highly pleased with you. Let prosperity and good fortune be yours.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: पतमानोऽद्य नरके भवतास्मि समुद्धृतः। भवितव्यमथैवं च यद् दृष्टोऽसि मयानघ।॥
en: O sinless one, I was at the point of falling into hell, but I have been saved by you. It was ordained and therefore I did meet you.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: राजा ययातिौहित्रैः पतितस्तारितो यथा। सद्भिः पुरुषशार्दूल तथाहं भवता द्विजः॥
en: O foremost of men, as the fallen king Yayati was saved by his virtuous grandson, so have I now been saved by you.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: मातापितृभ्यां शुश्रूषां करिष्ये वचनात् तव। नाकृतात्मा वेदयति धर्माधर्मविनिश्चयम्॥
en: I shall serve my father and mother at your command. No vicious-minded man can ever expound the mysteries of virtue and vice.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: दुर्जेयः शाश्वतो धर्मः शूद्रयोनौ हि वर्तते। न त्वां शूद्रमहं मन्ये भवितव्यं हि कारणम्॥
en: As it is very difficult for a Shudra to learn the mysteries of eternal religion. I do not consider you to be a Shudra. There must be some reason for all this.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: येन कर्मविशेषेण प्राप्तेयं शूद्रता त्वया। एतदिच्छामि विज्ञातुं तत्त्वेन हि महामते। कामया ब्रूहि मे सर्वं सत्येन प्रयतात्मना॥
en: You must have been born as a Shudra as a result of your past Karma (in a previous birth). O high-souled one, I eagerly desire to learn truth of this matter. Tell this to me with attention and according to your inclination.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: व्याध उवाच अनतिक्रमणीया वै ब्राह्मणा मे द्विजोत्तम। शृणु सर्वमिदं वृत्तं पूर्वदेहे ममानघ॥
en: The Fowler said: O foremost of the Brahmanas, O sinless one, Brahmanas are worthy of all respect from me, hear about the story of my previous existence.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: अहं हि ब्राह्मणः पूर्वमासं द्विजवरात्मजः। वेदाध्यायी सुकुशलो वेदाङ्गानां च पारगः॥
en: O son of the best of Brahmanas, I was a Brahmana previously (in my another birth); I was well-read in the Vedas and earned in the Vedangas.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: आत्मदोषकृतैर्ब्रहान्नवस्थामाप्तवानिमाम्। कश्चिद् राजा मम सखा धनुर्वेदपरायणः॥
en: Through my own fault I have been degraded to my present state. A certain king learned in the science of arms was my friend.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: संसर्गाद् धनुषि श्रेष्ठस्ततोऽहमभवं द्विज) एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु मृगयां निर्गतो नृपः॥
en: O Brahmana, from his companionship, I too became proficient in archery. Once upon a time the king went out hunting,

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: सहितो योधमुख्यैश्च मन्त्रिभिश्च सुसंवृतः। ततोऽभ्यहन् मृगांस्तत्र सुबहूनाश्रमं प्रति॥
en: Surrounded by his ministers and followed by his best warriors. He killed many deer near a hermitage.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: अथ क्षिप्तः शरो घोरो मयापि द्विजसत्तम। ताडितश्च ऋषिस्तेन शरेणानतपर्वणा॥
en: O foremost of Brahmanas, I too shot a swift and fearful arrow. A Rishi was wounded by that arrow with head bent.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: भूमौ निपतितो ब्रह्मन्नुवाच प्रतिनादयन्। नापराध्याम्यहं किंचित् केन पापमिदं कृतम्॥
en: The Brahmana fell down on the ground and screaming aloud said "I have done no wrong, what wretch has done this?

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: मन्वानस्तं मृगं चाहं सम्प्राप्तः सहसा प्रभो। अपश्यं तमृषि विद्धं शरेणानतपर्वणा॥
en: O lord, taking him for a deer I soon went near him and saw that Rishi pierced by my that arrow with head bent.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: अकार्यकरणाच्चापि भृशं मे व्यथितं मनः। तमुचतपसं विप्रं निष्टनन्तं महीतले॥ अजानता कृतमिदं मयेत्यहमथाब्रुवम्। क्षन्तुमर्हसि मे सर्वमिति चोक्तो मया मुनिः॥
en: For my wicked deed I was very much aggrieved in my mind. I said to that Rishi of severe austerities who was loudly crying lying on the ground, “I have unconsciously done this." I again said to that Rishi “you should pardon ine for this sinful act.”

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: ततः प्रत्यब्रवीद् वाक्यमृषिर्मा क्रोधमूर्छितः। व्याधस्त्वं भविता क्रूर शूद्रयोनाविति द्विज॥
en: But the Brahmana, becoming exceedingly angry said, “You shall be born as a cruel fowler in the Shudra order."

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: व्याध उवाच एवं शप्तोऽहमृषिणा तदा द्विजवरोत्तम। अभिप्रसादयमृषि गिरा त्राहीति मां तदा॥ अजानता मयाकार्यमिदमद्य कृतं मुने। क्षन्तुमर्हसि तत् सर्वं प्रसीद भगवन्निति॥
en: The Fowler said: O foremost of the best of Brahmanas, having been thus cursed by the Rishi, I said "Pardon me, O Rishi, I have unconsciously done this wicked act. You should pardon all (my fault). Oexalted Rishi, be graceful (to me).

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: ऋषिरुवाच नान्यथा भविता शाप एवमेतदसंशयम्। आनृशंस्यात् त्वहं किञ्चित् कर्तानुग्रहमद्य ते॥
en: The Rishi said : The curse that I have pronounced can never be falsified. This is certain. But for kindness I shall do you a favour.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: शूद्रयोन्यां वर्तमानो धर्मज्ञो हि भविष्यसि। मातापित्रोश्च शुश्रूषां करिष्यसि न संशयः॥
en: Even taking your birth as a Shudra, you will be virtuous, you shall certainly serve and wait upon your parents.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: तया शुश्रूषया सिद्धिं महत्त्वं समवाप्स्यसि। जातिस्मरश्च भविता स्वर्गं चैव गमिष्यसि॥
en: By (thus) serving them, you will acquire great success. You shall also remember the events of your past life and shall go to heaven.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: शापक्षये तु निर्वृत्ते भवितासि पुनर्द्विजः। एवं शप्तः पुरा तेन ऋषिणास्य्युचतेजसा॥
en: On the expiration of this curse, you shall again become a Brahmana. I was thus in the days of yore cursed by that greatly effulgent Rishi.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: प्रसादश्च कृतस्तेन ममैव द्विपदां वर। शरं चोद्धृतवानस्मि तस्य वै द्विजसत्तम॥
en: O foremost of men, thus was he propitiated by me. O best of men, I extricated the arrow from his body.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: आश्रमं च मया नीतो न च प्राणैर्व्ययुज्यत। एतत् ते सर्वमाख्यातं यथा मम पुराभवत्॥ अभितश्चापि गन्तव्यं मया स्वर्गं द्विजोत्तम॥
en: I took him to the hermitage, but he was not deprived of his life, (he recovered from the । wound). I have thus narrated to you all that happened to me before. O foremost of men and also now I can go to heaven hereafter.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच एवमेतानि पुरुषा दुःखानि च सुखानि च। आप्नुवन्ति महाबुद्धे नोत्कण्ठां कर्तुमर्हसि॥
en: The Brahmana said: O greatly intelligent one, all men are thus subject to happiness or misery. You should not therefore grieve for it.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: दुष्करं हि कृतं कर्म जानता जातिमात्मनः। लोकवृत्तान्ततत्त्वज्ञ नित्यं धर्मपरायण॥
en: O virtuous man, O man learned in the ways of the world, in obedience to the customs of your present caste (Fowler), you have pursued these wicked ways.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: कर्मदोषश्च वै विद्वन्नात्मजातिकृतेन ते। कञ्चित् कालमुष्यतां वै ततोऽसि भविता द्विजः॥
en: These being the duties of your profession, the stain of evil Karma will not attach to you. After living here for sometime you shall again become a Brahmana.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: साम्प्रतं च मतो मेऽसि ब्राह्मणो नात्र संशयः। ब्राह्मणः पतनीयेषु वर्तमानो विकर्मसु॥ दाम्भिको दुष्कृतः प्रायः शूद्रेण सदृशो भवेत्।
en: There is no doubt that even now I consider you to be a Brahmana, for the Brahmana who is vain and haughty who is sinful and evilminded and who is fond of degraded practices, is no better than a Shudra.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: यस्तु शूद्रो दमे सत्ये धर्मे च सततोत्थितः॥ तं ब्राह्मणमहं मन्ये वृत्तेन हि भवेद् द्विजः।
en: The Shudra who is, endued with righteousness, self-control and truthfulness, is considered by me as a Brahmana. A man becomes a Brahmana by his own good act.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: कर्मदोषेण विषमां गतिमाप्नोति दारुणाम्॥ क्षीणदोषमहं मन्ये चाभितस्त्वां नरोत्तम।
en: By his own evil Karma a man meets with an evil and terrible doom. O foremost of men, 1 believe that all your sin is destroyed.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: कर्तुमर्हसि नोत्कण्ठां त्वद्विधा ह्यविषादिनः। लोकवृत्तानुवृत्तज्ञा नित्यं धर्मपरायणाः॥
en: You must not grieve for it, for men like you, who are so virtuous and learned in the ways and niysteries of the world, can have no cause of grief.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: व्याध उवाच प्रज्ञया मानसं दुःखं हन्याच्छारीरमौषधैः। एतद् विज्ञानसामर्थ्य न बालैः समतामियात्॥
en: The Fowler said: The bodily disease should be cured with medicines and the mental ones by spiritual wisdom. This is the power of knowledge. Knowing this, the wise should not behave like boys.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: अनिष्टसम्प्रयोगाच्च विप्रयोगात् प्रियस्य च। मनुष्या मानसैर्दुःखैर्युज्यन्ते चाल्पबुद्धयः॥ गुणैर्भूतानि युज्यन्ते वियुज्यन्ते तथैव च। सर्वाणि नैतदेकस्य शोकस्थानं हि विद्यते॥ अनिष्टं चान्वितं पश्यंस्तथा क्षिप्रं विरज्यते। ततश्च प्रतिकुर्वन्ति यदि पश्यन्त्युपक्रमात्॥
en: Men of low intelligence are overpowered with grief at the occurrence of something which is not agreeable to them or nonoccurrence of something which is good or much desired. Every creature is subject to this (law). It is not merely a single creature or a class, that is subject to misery. Congnisant of this evil people quickly mend their ways, if they perceive it at the very out-set, they succeed in curing it altogether.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: शोचतो न भवेत् किंचित् केवलं परितप्यते। परित्यजन्ति ये दुःखं सुखं वाप्युभयं नराः॥ त एव सुखमेधन्ते ज्ञानतृप्ता मनीषिणः। असंतोषपरा मूढाः संतोषं यान्ति पण्डिताः॥
en: Whoever grieves for it, only makes himself miserable. Those wise men whose knowledge has made them happy and contented and who are indifferent to happiness and misery, are really happy. The wise are always contented and the foolish are always discontented.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: असंतोषस्य नास्त्यन्तस्तुष्टिस्तु परमं सुखम्। न शोचन्ति गताध्वानः पश्यन्तः परमां गतिम्॥ न विषादे मनः कार्यं विषादो विषमुत्तमम्। मारयत्यकृतप्रज्ञं बालं क्रुद्ध इवोरगः॥
en: There is not end to to discontent and contentment is the highest happiness. The man who has attained the highest state does not grieve. They are always conscious of the final destruction of all creatures. One must not give way to discontent, for it is like a virulently poisonous snake. It kills persons of undeveloped intelligence just as a child is killed by an enraged snake.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: यं विषादोऽभिभवति विक्रमे समुपस्थिते। तेजसा तस्य हीनस्य पुरुषार्थो न विद्यते॥
en: That man has no manliness whose energies do abandon him and who is overpowered with perplexity, when an occasion for displaying vigour presents itself.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: अवश्यं क्रियमाणस्य कर्मणो दृश्यते फलम्। न हि निर्वेदमागम्य किंचित् प्राप्नोति शोभनम्॥
en: Our actions are with certainty followed by their effects. Whoever merely gives himself up to passive indifference (to worldly affairs) accomplishes no good.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: अथाप्युपायं पश्येत दुःखस्य परिमोक्षणे। अशोचन्नारभेतैवं मुक्तश्चाव्यसनी भवेत्॥
en: Instead of gruinbling, one must try to find out the means by which he can be freed from all misery.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: भूतेष्वभावं संचिन्त्य ये तु बुद्धेः परं गताः। न शोचन्ति कृतप्रज्ञाः पश्यन्तः परमां गतिम्॥
en: He who has attained the highest state, being conscious of the great deficiency of all matter and seeing before him the final doom, never grieves.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: न शोचामि च वै विद्वन् कालाकाक्षी स्थितो ह्यहम् एतैर्निदर्शनैर्ब्रह्मन् नावसीदामि सत्तम॥
en: O excellent man, O learned one, I too do not grieve. I wait abiding my time. For this reason I am not confined (in any way).

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच कृतप्रज्ञोऽसि मेधावी बुद्धिर्हि विपुला तव। नाहं भवन्तं शोचामि ज्ञानतृप्तोऽसि धर्मवित्॥
en: The Brahmana said: You are wise great in knowledge and vast in your intelligence; O virtuous one, you are content with your wisdom. I have nothing to complain in you.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: आपृच्छे त्वां स्वस्ति तेऽस्तु धर्मस्त्वां परिरक्षतु। अप्रमादस्तु कर्तव्यो धर्मे धर्मभृतां वर॥
en: O foremost of all virtuous men, (now) farewell. May prosperity come to you, may virtue protect you and may you be ever steady in the practice of virtuc.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: पार्कण्डेय उवाच बाढमित्येव तं व्याधः कृताञ्जलिरुवाच ह। प्रदक्षिणमथो कृत्वा प्रस्थितो द्विजसत्तमः॥
en: Markandeya said : The Fowler with joined hands said to him, "So be it.” That foremost of Brahmanas then walked round him and went away.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: स तु गत्वा द्विजः सर्वां शुश्रूषां कृतवांस्तदा। मातापितृभ्यां वृद्धाभ्यां यथान्यायं सुशंसितः॥
en: When the Brahmana returned home he assiduously and duly began to serve his old father and mother.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: एतत् ते सर्वमाख्यातं निखिलेन युधिष्ठिर। पृष्टवानसि यं तात धर्मं धर्मभृतां वर॥
en: O Yudhishthira, O child, O foremost of virtuous men, I have thus told you in detail all that you asked me:

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: पतिव्रताया माहात्म्यं ब्राह्मणस्य च सत्तम। मातापित्रोश्च शुश्रूषा धर्मव्याधेन कीर्तिता॥
en: The virtue of women's devotion to their husbands and the filial piety as described to the Brahmana by the virtuous fowler.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच अत्यद्भुतमिदं ब्रह्मन् धर्माख्यानमनुत्तमम्। सर्वधर्मविदां श्रेष्ठ कथितं मुनिसत्तम॥
en: Yudhishthira said: O foremost of all virtuous men, O best of Rishis, O Brahmana, wonderful is this excellent moral story.

description: The colloquy between the Fowler and the Brahmana
sn: सुखश्रव्यतया विद्वन् मुहूर्त इव मे गतः। न हि तृप्तोऽस्मि भगवन् शृण्वानो धर्ममुत्तमम्॥
en: Listening to you, O learned man, O exalted one, my time has passed away as if it were but a (fleeting) moment. But I am not as yet satiated with hearing about Dharma.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच श्रुत्वेमां धर्मसंयुक्तां धर्मराजः कथां शुभाम्। पुनः पप्रच्छ तमृषि मार्कण्डेयमिदं तदा॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having heard this excellent discourse on religion, Dharmaraja (Yudhishthira) again

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच कथमग्निर्वनं यातः कथं चाप्यङ्गिराः पुरा। नष्टेऽग्नौ हव्यमवहदग्निर्भूत्वा महाद्युतिः॥
en: Yudhishthira said: Why did in the days of yore, Agni hide himself in water and why did the greatly effulgent Angirasa convey the oblations by becoming Agni, when Agni had disappeared?

sn: अग्निर्यदा त्वेक एव बहुत्वं चास्य कर्मसु। दृश्यते भगवन् सर्वमेतदिच्छामि वेदितुम्॥
en: O exalted one, there is but one fire, but it is seen, according to the nature of its actions as many. I desire to hear all this.

sn: कुमारश्च यथोत्पन्नो यथा चाग्नेः सुतोऽभवत्। यथा रुद्राच्च सम्भूतो गङ्गायां कृत्तिकासु च॥
en: How Kumara (Kartikeya) was born, how he came to be known as the son of Agni and how he was begotten by Rudra (Shiva) on Ganga and Krittika?

sn: एतदिच्छाम्यहं त्वत्तः श्रोतुं भार्गवसत्तम। कौतूहलसमाविष्टो याथातथ्यं महामुने॥
en: O best of the Bhrigu race, O great Rishi, I desire to hear all this in detail. I am filled with great curiosity.

sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। यथा क्रुद्धो हुतवहस्तपस्तप्तुं वनं गतः॥
en: Markandeya said : This is the old history cited as an instance, in which (is related) why Agni in wrath went to the forest to perform asceticismi.

sn: यथा च भगवानग्निः स्वयमेवाङ्गिराऽभवत्। संतापयंश्च प्रभया नाशयस्तिमिराणि च॥
en: And why the exalted, Angirasa, transforming himself into Agni, destroyed all the darkness and distress (the world) by his splendour.

sn: पुराङ्गिरा महाबाहो चचार तप उत्तमम्। आश्रमस्थो महाभागो हव्यवाहं विशेषयन्। तथा स भूत्वा तु तदा जगत् सर्वं व्यकाशयत्॥
en: O mighty-armed hero, in the days of yore Angiras performed severe asceticism in his herinitage. That highly exalted one even excelled Agni. Becoming such he illuminated the whole universe.

sn: तपश्चरंस्तु हुतभुक् संतप्तस्तस्य तेजसा। भृशं ग्लानश्च तेजस्वी न च किंचित् प्रजज्ञिवान्॥
en: Agni was then performing asceticism and he became greatly aggrieved with that effulgence. That greatly powerful deity was greatly sorry, but he did not know what to do.

sn: अथ संचिन्तयामास भगवान् हव्यवाहनः। अन्योऽग्निरिह लोकानां ब्रह्मणा सम्प्रकल्पितः॥
en: The exalted one thus reflected, “Another Agni was created by Brahma.

sn: अग्नित्वं विप्रणष्टं हि तप्यमानस्य मे तपः। कथमग्निः पुनरहं भवेयमिति चिन्त्य सः॥
en: As I am practising asceticism my services as Agni have been dispensed with.” He then considered how he could again become the deity of fire.

sn: अपश्यदग्निवल्लोकांस्तापयन्तं महामुनिम्। सोपासर्पच्छनैतिस्तमुवाच तदाङ्गिराः॥
en: Seeing the great Rishi giving heat to the entire universe, he came to him with fear; thereupon Angiras said,

sn: शीघ्रमेव भवस्वाग्निस्त्वं पुनर्लोकभावनः। विज्ञातश्चासि लोकेषु त्रिषु संस्थानचारिषु॥
en: "Soon become Agni, the protector of the world, you are celebrated over the three stable worlds.

sn: त्वमग्निः प्रथमं सृष्टो ब्रह्मणा तिमिरापहः। स्वस्थानं प्रतिपद्यस्व शीघ्रमेव तमोनुद॥
en: You Agni was first created by Brahma to dispel darkness. O destroyer of darkness, do you quickly occupy your own place."

sn: अग्निरुवाच नष्टकीर्तिरहं लोके भवान् जातो हुताशनः। भवन्तमेव ज्ञास्यन्ति पावकं न तु मां जनाः॥
en: Agni said : My reputation has been destroyed in this world, you have become the fire, people will know you as Agni and not me.

sn: निक्षिपाम्यहमग्नित्वं त्वमग्निः प्रथमो भव। भविष्यामि द्वितीयोऽहं प्राजापत्यक एव च॥
en: I have relinquished my god-hood of fire, do you become primeval fire. I shall act as the second Prajapatya fire.

sn: अङ्गिरा उवाच कुरु पुण्यं पुरजास्वयं भवाग्निस्तिमिरापहः। मां च देव कुरुष्वाग्ने प्रथम पुत्रमञ्जसा॥
en: Angiras said: O deity of fire, do you become the fire-god and the destroyer of darkness. Do you attend to your sacred duty of clearing people's way to heaven. O god, make me your first child.

sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच तच्छ्रुत्वाङ्गिरसो वाक्यं जातवेदास्तथाकरोत्। राजन् बृहस्पति भ तस्याप्यङ्गिरसः सुतः॥
en: Markandeya said : O king, having heard the words of Angiras, Agni did as desired; Angiras had a son, named Brihaspati.

sn: ज्ञात्वा प्रथमजं तं तु वढेराङ्गिरसं सुतम्। उपेत्य देवाः पप्रच्छुः कारणं तत्र भारत॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, knowing him to be the first son of Angiras by Agni, the celestials came and enquired about the mystery.

sn: स तु पृष्टस्तदा देवैस्तत: कारणमब्रवीत्। प्रत्यगृह्णस्तु देवाश्च तद् वचोऽङ्गिरसस्तदा॥
en: Having been thus addressed by the celestials, he told them the reason; and the celestials accepted the explanation of Angiras.

sn: तत्र नानाविधानग्नीन् प्रवक्ष्यामि महाप्रभान्। कर्मभिर्बहुभिः ख्यातान् नानार्थान् ब्राह्मणेष्विह॥
en: I shall (now) describe to you various sorts of fire of great effulgence which are known to the Brahmanas by their respective names.

sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच ब्रह्मणो यस्तृतीयस्तु पुत्रः कुरुकुलोद्वह। तस्याभवत् सुभा भार्या प्रजास्तस्यां च मे शृणु॥
en: Markandeya said : O perpetuator of the Kuru race, he who was the third son of Brahma had a wife named Subha. Hear about her sons.

sn: बृहत्कीर्तिवृहज्ज्योतिर्वृहद्ब्रह्मा बृहन्मनाः। बृहन्मन्त्रो बृहद्भासस्तथा राजन् बृहस्पतिः॥
en: O King, his son Brihaspati was very famous, high-souled and vigorous. His genius and learning were very great. He was highly renowned as a counsellor.

sn: प्रजासु तासु सर्वासु रूपेणाप्रतिमाभवत्। देवी भानुमती नाम प्रथमाङ्गिरसः सुता॥
en: Bhanumati was the name of his eldest daughter; she was the most beautiful of all his children.

sn: भूतानामेव सर्वेषां यस्यां रागस्तदाभवत्। रागाद्रागेति यामाहुर्द्वितीयाङ्गिरसः सुता॥
en: Angira's second daughter was called Raga, she was so named because she was the source of all creatures' love.

sn: यां कपर्दिसुतामाहुद्देश्यादृश्येति देहिनः। तनुत्वात्सा सिनीवाली तृतीयाङ्गिरसः सुता॥
en: Sinivali was the third daughter of Angiras. Her body was of such slender make, that she was visible at one time and invisible at another and therefore she was likened to the daughter of Rudra.

sn: पश्यत्यर्चिष्मती भाभिर्हविभिश्च हविष्मती। षष्ठीमङ्गिरसः कन्यां पुण्यामाहुर्महिष्मतीम्॥
en: Archishmati was his fourth daughter, she was so named because of her great effulgence; the fifth was Havishmati, so named from her accepting Havish (oblations); the sixth daughter of Angiras was named Mahishmati, whe was very pious.

sn: महामखेष्वाङ्गिरसी दीप्तिमत्सु महामते। महामतीति विख्याता सप्तमी कथ्यते सुता।॥ यां तु दृष्ट्वा भगवतीं जनः कुहुकुहायते। एकानशेति तामाहुः कुहूमङ्गिरसः सुताम्॥
en: O high-minded one, his seventh daughter was named Mahamati; she was always present at sacrifices of great splendour and that adorable daughter of Angiras whom they called matchless and about whom me cried kuhu, kuhu, in wonder was called Kuhu.

sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच बृहस्पतेश्चान्द्रमसी भार्याऽऽसीद् या यशस्विनी। अग्नीन् साजनयत् पुण्यान् षडेकां चापि पुत्रिकाम्॥
en: Markandeya said : Brihaspati had a celebrated wife belonging to the lunar world. He begot on her six sons, all of them by different fires and one daughter.

sn: आहुतिष्वेव यस्याग्नेहविषाद्यं विधीयते। सोऽग्निद्र्हस्पतेः पुत्रः शंयुर्नाम महाव्रतः॥
en: The fire in which oblations of ghee are offered at the Paurnamashya and at other sacrifices was a son of Brihaspati and that high-souled one is called Shanyu.

sn: चातुर्मास्येषु यस्येष्टमश्वमेधेऽचजः प्रभुः। दीप्तो ज्वालैरनेकाभैरग्निरेकोऽथ वीर्यवान्॥
en: At the Chaturmasya and the Ashvamedha sacrifices, animals are first offered in his honour; this powerful fire is indicated by numerous flames.

sn: शंयोरप्रतिमा भार्या सत्या सत्याथ धर्मजा। अग्निस्तस्य सुतो दीप्तस्तिस्रः कन्याश्च सुव्रताः॥
en: Shanyu's wife was called Satya; she was of matchless beauty; she sprang from Dharma for the sake of truth, the blazing fire was his son and he had three daughters of great religious merit.

sn: प्रथमेनाज्यभागेन पूज्यते योऽग्निरध्वरे। अग्निस्तस्य भरद्वाजः प्रथमः पुत्र उच्यते॥ पौर्णमासेषु सर्वेषु हविषाऽऽज्यं स्रुवोद्यतम्। भरतो नामतः सोऽग्निर्द्वितीयः शंयुतः सुतः॥
en: The fire which is honoured with the first oblations at sacrifices is his first son called Bharadvaja, the second son of Shanyu is called Bharata in whose honour oblations of Ghee are offered with the sacrificial laddle at all the Paurnamasya sacrifices.

sn: तिस्रः कन्या भवन्त्यन्या यासां स भरतः पतिः। भरतस्तु सुतस्तस्य भरत्येका च पुत्रिका॥
en: Besides these, there were then other sons, of whom Bharata was the eldest. He had a son named Bharata and a daughter called Bharati.

sn: भरतो भरतस्याग्नेः पावकस्तु प्रजापतेः। महानत्यर्थमहितस्तथा भरतसप्तम॥
en: The Bharata Agni was the son of Prajapati Bharata Agni. O best of the Bharata race, because he was greatly honoured, therefore he was called “great".

sn: भरद्वाजस्य भार्या तु वीरा वीरस्य पिण्डदा। प्राहुराज्येन तस्येज्यां सोमस्येव द्विजाः शनैः॥
en: Vira was the wife of Bharadvaja, she gave birth to Vira. It is said by the Brahmanas that he is worshipped like Soma with offering of Ghee.

sn: हविषा यो द्वितीयेन सोमेन सह युज्यते। रथप्रभू रथध्वानः कुम्भरेताः स उच्यते॥
en: He is joined with Soma in the secondary oblations of Ghee and is called Rathaprabhu and Rathadhvana and Kumbhareta.

sn: सरय्वां जनयत् सिद्धिं भानु भाभिः समावृणोत्। आग्नेयमानयन् नित्यमाह्वाने ह्येष सूयते॥
en: He begot a son on his wife Sarayu named Siddhi and covered the Sun with his splendour. As he is the presiding genius of fire, he is always mentioned in all fire hymn.

sn: यस्तु न च्यवते नित्यं यशसा वर्चसा श्रिया। अग्निनिश्च्यवनो नाम पृथिवीं स्तौति केवलम्॥
en: The fire Nischyavana only praises the earth; he never suffers in reputation, splendour and prosperity.

sn: विपाप्मा कलुषैर्मुक्तो विशुद्धश्चार्चिषा ज्वलन्। विपापोऽग्निः सुतस्तस्य सत्यः समयधर्मकृत्॥
en: The sinless fire Satya blazing with pure flame was his son. He is free from all stain, he is not defiled by sin, he is the regulator of time.

sn: आक्रोशतां हि भूतानां यः करोति हि निष्कृतिम्। अग्निः स निष्कृति म शोभयत्यभिसेविते॥
en: That fire has another name called Nishkriti, because he accomplishes the Nishkriti of all creatures, when properly worshipped, he gives good fortune.

sn: अनुकूजन्ति येनेह वेदनार्ताः स्वयं जनाः। तस्य पुत्रः स्वनो नाम पावकः स रुजस्करः॥ यस्तु विश्वस्य जगतो बुद्धिमाक्रम्य तिष्ठति। तं प्राहुरध्यात्मविदो विश्वजिन्नाम पावकम्॥
en: Son of Satya is called Svana who is the generator of all diseases, he inflicts severe sufferings on men for which they loudly cry. He moves in the intelligence of all creatures; the other fire is called Vishvajit by mean of spiritual wisdom.

sn: अन्तराग्निः स्मृतो यस्तु भुक्तं पचति देहिनाम्। स जज्ञे विश्वभुड्नाम सर्वलोकेषु भारत॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, the fire, which is known as the internal heat by which all foods are digested, is called Sarvabhuk and was begotten by him.

sn: ब्रह्मचारी यतात्मा च सततं विपुलव्रतः। ब्राह्मणाः पूजयन्त्येनं पाकयज्ञेषु पावकम्॥
en: He is self-controlled, he is of great religious merit, he is a Brahmachari and he is worshipped by the Brahmanas at the Paka sacrifice.

sn: पवित्रा गोमती नाम नदी यस्याभवत् प्रिया। तस्मिन् कर्माणि सर्वाणि क्रियन्ते धर्मकर्तृभिः॥
en: The sacred river Gomati was his wife and by him all religious-minded men perform their sacrifices.

sn: वडवाग्निः पिबत्यम्भो योऽसौ परमदारुणः। ऊर्श्वभागूर्ध्वभाङ्नाम कविः प्राणाश्रितस्तु यः॥
en: That terrible water-drinking sea fire called Vadava has the tendency to go upwards and hence it is called Urdhvabhaga, It stands in the Prana.

sn: उदग्द्वारं हविर्यस्य गृहे नित्यं प्रदीयते। ततः स्विष्टं भवेदाज्यं स्विष्टकृत् परमः स्मृतः॥
en: The sixth son is called the Svishtakrit, for him oblations became Shveta; Udagdvara oblations are always made in his honour.

sn: यः प्रशान्तेषु भूतेषु मन्युर्भवति पावकः। क्रुद्धस्य तु रसो जज्ञे मन्युतीव्रा च पुत्रिका। स्वाहेति दारुणा क्रूरा सर्वभूतेषु तिष्ठति॥
en: When all creatures are calmed the fire named Brihaspati becomes full of fury. This inexorable, fearful and highly wrathful fire is the daughter of Brihaspati. He is known by the name of Svaha and is present in everything.

sn: त्रिदिवे यस्य सदृशो नास्ति रूपेण कश्चन। अतुलत्वात् कृतो देवैर्नाम्ना कामस्तु पावकः॥
en: He had a son like whom there was none in heaven in personal beauty. And therefore he was called by the celestials “Kama Agni”.

sn: संहर्षाद् धारयन् क्रोधं धन्वी स्रग्वी रथे स्थितः। समरे नाशयेच्छनमोघो नाम पावकः॥ उक्थो नाम महाभाग त्रिभिरुक्थैरभिष्टुतः। महावाचं त्वजनयत् समाश्वासं हि यं विदुः॥
en: He had another son, called Amogha, who was the destroyer of all his enemies in battle. Assured of success he controls his wrath. He is armed with a bird, he is seated on a chariot and is adorned with garlands of flowers; she had another son named Uktha, praised by the three Uktha. He is the originator of the great words (the Vedas) and he is therefore called Samasvasa.

sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच काश्यपो ाथ वासिष्ठः प्राणश्च प्राणपुत्रकः। अग्निराङ्गिरसश्चैव च्यवनस्त्रिषु वर्चकः॥ अचरन्त तपस्तीव्र पुत्रार्थे बहुवार्षिकम्। पुत्रं लभेम धर्मिष्ठं यशसा ब्रह्मणा समम्॥ महाव्यातिभिातः पञ्चभिस्तैस्तदा त्वथ। जज्ञे तेजो महार्चिष्मान् पञ्चवर्णः प्रभावनः॥
en: Markandeya said : He performed severe asceticism lasting for many hundred years with the desire of getting a virtuous son equal to a Brahmana, in reputation when invocation was made with Vyahriti hymns and with the aid of the five sacred fires, namely Kashyapa, Vasishtha, Pranaka, the son of Prana, the son of Angira, Chyavana and Trivarcha, there was a bright fire full of the animating principle and of five different colours.

sn: समिद्धोऽग्निः शिरस्तस्य बाहू सूर्यनिभौ तथा। त्वड्नेत्रे च सुवर्णाभे कृष्णे जङ्ग्रे च भारत॥
en: Its head was brilliant as the flaming fire, its arms were as bright as the sun; its skin and eyes were gold coloured and its feet, O descendant of Bharata, were black.

sn: पञ्चवर्णः स तपसा कृतस्तै पञ्चभिर्जनैः। पाञ्चजन्यः श्रुतो देवः पञ्चवंशकरस्तु सः॥
en: Its five colours were given to it by these five men, by reason of their great penance. This celestials being is therefore described as appertaining to five men and he is the progenitor of the five tribes.

sn: दशवर्षसहस्राणि तपस्तप्त्वा महातपाः। जनयत् पावकं घोरं पितॄणां स प्रजाः सृजन्॥
en: Having performed asceticism for ten thousand years, that being of great merit, produced the terrible fire appertaining to the Pitris in order to begin the work of creation and from his head and mouth respectively. was son

sn: बृहद् स्थन्तरं मूों वक्त्राद् वा तरसाहरौ। शिवं नाभ्यां बलादिन्द्रं वाय्वग्नी प्राणतोऽसृजत्॥
en: He created Brihat and Rathantara, who quickly steal life away. He created Shiva from his naval, Indra from his prowess and wind and fire from his soul.

sn: बाहुभ्यामनुदात्तौ च विश्वे भूतानि चैव ह। एतान् सष्ट्वा ततः पञ्च पितृणामसृजत् सुतान्॥
en: And from his two arms and hymns Udatta and Anudatta. He also created the mind and the five senses and other creatures. Having created these he produced the five sons of the Pitris,

sn: बृहद्रथस्य प्रणिधिः काश्यपस्य महत्तरः। भानुरङ्गिरसो धीरः पुत्रो वर्चस्य सौभरः॥
en: Of these Pranidhi was the son of Brihadratha, Mahattara the son of Kashyapa, Bhanu was the grand son of Chyavana and Saubhara, the son of Varcha.

sn: प्राणस्य चानुदात्तस्तु व्याख्याताः पञ्चविंशतिः। देवान् यज्ञमुषश्चान्यान् सृजत् पञ्चदशोत्तरान्॥ सुभीममतिभीमं च भीमं भीमबलाबलम्। एतान् यज्ञमुषः पञ्च देवानां ह्यसृजत् तपः॥ सुमित्रं मित्रवन्तं च मित्रज्ञं मित्रवर्धनम्। मित्रधर्माणमित्येतान् देवानभ्यसृजत् तपः॥ सुरप्रवीरं वीरं च सुरेशं च सुवर्चसम्। सुराणामपि हन्तारं पञ्चैतानसृजत् तपः॥
en: Anudatta the son of Prana. These twenty five beings were created by him. Tapa also created fifteen other gods who obstruct sacrifices. (They are) Subhima, Bhima, Atibhima, Bhimabala and Abala, Sumitra, Mitravan, Mitrajna, Mitravardhana, Mitradharman, Surapravira Vira, Suresha, Suvarchas and Surahanta.

sn: त्रिविधं संस्थिता होते पञ्च पञ्च पृथक् पृथक्। मुष्णन्त्यत्र स्थिता ह्येते स्वर्गतो यज्ञयाजिनः॥
en: These deities were divided into three classes of five each. Placed here in this world, they destroy the sacrifices in heaven.

sn: तेषामिष्टं हरन्त्येते निघ्नन्ति च महद्धविः। स्पर्धया हव्यवाहानां निघ्नन्त्येते हरन्ति च॥
en: They frustrate their objects and spoil their oblations of Ghee; they do this only to spite the sacred fires carrying oblations to the celestials.

sn: बहिर्वेद्यां तदादानं कुशलैः सम्प्रवर्तितम्। तदेते नोपसर्पन्ति यत्र चाग्निः स्थितो भवेत्॥
en: If the priests are careful, they place the oblation in their honour outside the sacrificial altar; to that particular place where the sacred fire may be placed, they cannot go.

sn: चितोऽग्निरुद्वहन् यज्ञं पक्षाभ्यां तान् प्रबाधते। मन्त्रैः प्रशमिता ह्येते नेष्टं मुष्णन्ति यज्ञियम्॥
en: They carry the oblations offered by the votaries by means of wings. When appeased by hymns they do not frustrate the sacrificial rites.

sn: बृहदुक्थस्तपस्यैव पुत्रो भूमिमुपाश्रितः। अग्निहोत्रे हूयमाने पृथिव्यां सद्रिरिज्यते॥
en: Brihaduktha, another son of Tapa belongs to the earth. He is worshipped in the world by virtuous who perform Agnihotra sacrifices.

sn: रथन्तरश्च तपसः पुत्रोऽग्निः परिपठ्यते। मित्रविन्दाय वै तस्य हविरध्वर्यवो विदुः॥ मुमुदे परमप्रीत: सह पुत्रैर्महायशाः॥
en: Of the son of Tapa, who is known as Rathantara, it is said by the priests that oblation offered in his honour is offered to Mitravinda. The celebrated Tapa was thus very happy with his sons. men J

sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच गुरुभिर्नियमैर्युक्तो भरतो नाम पावकः। अग्निः पुष्टिमतिर्नाम तुष्टः पुष्टिं प्रयच्छति। भरत्येष प्रजाः सर्वास्ततो भरत उच्यते॥
en: Markandeya said : The fire named Bharata was bound by severe rules of asceticism; Pushtimati is his another name; when he is satisfied he grants pushti (development) to all creatures and therefore he is called Bharata.

sn: अग्नियश्च शिवो नाम शक्तिपूजापरश्च सः। दुःखार्तानां च सर्वेषां शिवकृत् सततं शिवः॥
en: The fire named Shiva is ever engaged in worshipping the force (of nature). As he always relieves the sufferings of creatures, he is called Shiva.

sn: तपसस्तु फलं दृष्ट्वा सम्प्रवृद्धं तपो महत्। उद्धर्तुकामो मतिमान् पुत्रो जज्ञे पुरंदरः॥
en: When Tapa acquired great ascetic merit, an intelligent son, named Purandara was born to him to inherit all these ascetic merits.

sn: ऊष्मा चैवोष्मणो जज्ञे सोऽग्निधूतस्य लक्ष्यते। अग्निश्चापि मनु म प्राजापत्यमकारयत्॥
en: Another son was also born to him, named Ushma. This fire is seen in all vapours. Another son named Manu was also born; he officiated as Prajapatya.

sn: शम्भुमग्निमथ प्राहुर्ब्राह्मणा वेदपारगाः। आवसथ्यं द्विजाः प्राहुर्दीप्तमग्नि महाप्रभम्॥
en: The Brahmanas learned in the Vedas then speak of the deeds of the fire named Shambhu. Then the Brahmanas speak of the greatly effulgent fire (called) Avasathya.

sn: ऊर्जस्करान् हव्यवाहान् सुवर्णसदृशप्रभान्। ततस्तपो ह्यजनयत् पञ्च यज्ञसुतानिह॥
en: Tapa thus created the five Urjaskara fires, they were as brilliant as gold. They all partake of the Soma in sacrifices.

sn: प्रशान्तेऽग्निर्महाभाग परिश्रान्तो गवां पतिः। असुरान् जनयन् घोरान् मांश्चैव पृथग्विधान्॥
en: The greatly exalted sun, when fatigued is known as the Prashanta (fire). He created the fearful Asura and various other creatures of the earth.

sn: तपसश्च मनुं पुत्रं भानु चाप्यङ्गिराः सृजत्। बृहद्भानुं तु तं प्राहुर्ब्राह्मणा वेदपारगाः॥
en: Angira also created the Prajapati Bhanu, the son of Tapa. He is also called Brihadbhanu by Brahmanas learned in the Vedas.

sn: भानोर्भार्या सुप्रजा तु बृहद्भासा तु सूर्यजा। असृजेतां तु षट् पुत्रान् शृणु तासां प्रजाविधिम्॥
en: Bhanu's wife was Supraja and Brihadbhanu, the daughter of Supraja; they gave birth to six sons, hear about their progeny.

sn: दुर्बलानां तु भूतानामसून् यः सम्प्रयच्छति। तमग्नि बलदं प्राहुः प्रथमं भानुतः सुतम्॥
en: The fire who gives strength to the weak is called Balada. He is the first son of Bhanu.

sn: यः प्रशान्तेषु भूतेषु मन्युर्भवति दारुणः। अग्निः स मन्युमानाम द्वितीयो भानुतः सुतः॥
en: The fire, who appears as terrible when all the elements are in tranquility, is called the Manyuman fire; he is the second son of Bhanu.

sn: दर्श च पौर्णमासे च यस्येह हविरुच्यते। विष्णुर्नामेह योऽग्निस्तु धृतिमान्नाम सोऽङ्गिराः॥
en: The fire in whose honour oblations of Ghee are poured in the Darsha and Paurnamasya sacrifices is known as Vishnu in this world. He is called Dhritiman or Angira.

sn: इन्द्रेण सहितं यस्य हविराचयणं स्मृतम्। अग्निराचयणो नाम भानोरेवान्वयस्तु सः॥
en: The fire to whom with Indra, the Agrayana oblation is made is called Agrayana fire. He is the (fourth) son of Bhanu.

sn: चातुर्मास्येषु नित्यानां हविषा योनिरग्रहः। चतुर्भिः सहितः पुत्रैर्भानोरेवान्वयः स्तुभः॥ निशा त्वजनयत् कन्यामग्नीषोमावुभौ तथा। मनोरेवाभवद् भार्या सुषुवे पञ्च पावकान्॥ पूज्यते हविषाग्येण चातुर्मास्येषु पावकः। पर्जन्यसहितः श्रीमानग्निर्वैश्वानरस्तु सः॥
en: The fifth son of Bhanu, is Agraha who is the source of the oblations which are daily made for the performance of the Chaturmasya rites. Stubha is the sixth son of Bhanu, Nisha was the name of another wife of that Manu who was known under the name of Bhanu. She gave birth to one daughter, the two Agni-somas and also five other fire deities. The effulgent fire, who is honoured with the first oblations with the deity of clouds, is called Vaishvanara.

sn: अस्य लोकस्य सर्वस्य यः प्रभुः परिपठ्यते। सोऽग्निविश्वपति म द्वितीयो वै मनोः सुतः॥
en: The fire who is called the lord of all the worlds is named Vishvapati, the second son of Manu.

sn: तत: स्विष्टं भवेदाज्यं स्विष्टकृत् परमस्तु सः। कन्या सा रोहिणी नाम हिरण्यकशिपोः सुता॥
en: The daughter of Manu is called Svistakrit, for by offering oblations to her, one acquires great merit. That damsel named Rohini was the 'aughter of Hiranyakashipu;

sn: कर्मणासौ बभौ भार्या स वह्निः स प्रजापतिः। प्राणानाश्रित्य यो देहं प्रवर्तयति देहिनाम्। तस्य संनिहितो नाम शब्दरूपस्य साधनः॥
en: But on account of her evil deeds, she became his wife. That fire was however a Prajapati. The other fire which sits on the vital airs of all creatures is called Sannihita. It is the cause of our perception of sound and form.

sn: शुक्लकृष्णगतिर्देवो यो बिभर्ति हुताशनम्। अकल्मषः कल्मषाणां कर्ता क्रोधाश्रितस्तु सः॥ कपिलं परमर्षि च यं प्राहुर्यतयः सदा। अग्निः स कपिलो नाम सांख्ययोगप्रवर्तकः॥
en: The divine spirit whose course is marked by black and white stains, who is the supporter of the fire, who though free from sin is the accomplisher of tainted Karma, whom the wise man consider to be a great Rishi, is the fire named Kapila, the propounder of that system of (Yoga) called Sankhya.

sn: अचं यच्छन्ति भूतानां येन भूतानि नित्यदा। कर्मस्विह विचित्रेषु सोऽचणीर्वह्निरुच्यते॥
en: The fire, through whom the elementary spirits always receive the offering called Agra made by other creatures at the performance of all the peculiar rites in the world, is called Agrani.

sn: इमानन्यान् समसृजत् पावकान् प्रथितान् भुवि। अग्निहोत्रस्य दुष्टस्य प्रायश्चित्तार्थमुल्बणान्॥ संस्पृशेयुर्यदान्योन्यं कथञ्चिद् वायुनाग्नयः। इष्टिरष्टाकपालेन कार्या वै शुचयेऽग्नये॥
en: Those other effulgent fires, celebrated all over the world, were created for rectification of the Agnihotra rites when marked by any defect. If the fires inter-lap each other by the action of the wind, then the rectification must be made with the Ashtakapala rites in honour of the fire named Suchi.

sn: दक्षिणाग्निर्यदा द्वाभ्यां संसृजेत तदा किला इष्टिरष्टाकपालेन कार्या वै वीतयेऽग्नये॥
en: If the southern fire comes in contact with the two other fires, then rectification must be made by the performance of the Ashtakapala rites in honour of the fire named Viti.

sn: यद्यग्नयो हि स्पृश्येयुनिवेशस्था दवाग्निना। इष्टिरष्टाकपालेन कार्या तु शुचयेऽग्नये॥
en: If the fire named Nivasa comes in contact with the fire called Davagni, then Ashtakapala rites must be performed in honour of the fire called Suchi.

sn: अग्नि रजस्वला वै स्त्री संस्पृशेदग्निहोत्रिकम्। इष्टिरष्टाकपालेन कार्या वसुमतेऽग्नये।॥
en: If the perpetual fire is touched by a woman in her monthly course, then for rectification the Ashtakapala rites must be performed in honour of the fire named Vasumana.

sn: मृतः श्रूयेत यो जीवः परेयुः पशवो यदा। इष्टिरष्टाकपालेन कार्या सुरभिमतेऽग्नये॥
en: If at the time of the Agnihotra sacrifice, the death of any creature is spoken of or any animal dies, then rectification must be made with the performance of the Ashtakapala rites in the honour of the fire Surabhiman.

sn: आर्तो न जुहुयादग्नि त्रिरात्रं यस्तु ब्राह्मणः। इष्टिरष्टाकपालेन कार्या स्यादुत्तराग्नये॥
en: The Brahmana who is unable to offer oblations to the sacred fire for three nights, on account of illness must make Prayaschitya by performing Ashtakapala rites in honour of the southern fire.

sn: दर्श च पौर्णमासं च यस्य तिष्ठेत् प्रतिष्ठितम्। इष्टिरष्टाकपालेन कार्या पथिकृतेऽग्नये।॥
en: He who has performed the Darsha and the Paurnamasya rites, must make the rectification by performing Ashtakapala rites in honour of the northern fire named Pathikrit.

sn: सूतिकाग्निर्यदा चाग्नि संस्पृशेदग्निहोत्रिकम्। इष्टिरष्टाकपालेन कार्या चाग्निमतेऽग्नये॥
en: If the fire of a lying-in-room comes in contact with the eternal sacred fire, then rectification must be made with the performance of Ashtakapala in honour of the fire named Agniman.

sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच आपस्य मुदिता भार्या सहस्य परमा प्रिया। भूपतिर्भुवभर्ता च जनयत् पावकं परम्॥ भूतानां चापि सर्वेषां यं प्राहुः पावकं पतिम्। आत्मा भुवनभर्तेति सान्वयेषु द्विजातिषु॥
en: Markandeya said : Mudita, the favourite wife of the fire named Svaha, live in water. Svaha who was the lord of the sky, begot on his that wife a greatly sacred fire named Adbhuta. There is a tradition among the Brahmanas, namely that this fire is the ruler and the inner soul of all creatures.

sn: महतां चैव भूतानां सर्वेषामिह यः पतिः। भगवान् स महातेजा नित्यं चरति पावकः॥ अग्निहपति म नित्यं यज्ञेषु पूज्यते। हुतं वहति यो हव्यमस्य लोकस्य पावकः॥
en: That fire is adorable and effulgent, he is the lord of all the Bhutas here. And that fire under the name of Grihapati is always worshipped at all sacrifices and conveys all the oblations that are made in this world.

sn: अपां गर्भो महाभागः सत्त्वभुग् यो महाद्भुतः। भूपतिर्भुवभर्ता च महतः पतिरुच्यते॥
en: That great son of Svaha, the great Adbhuta fire, is the soul of the waters and the prince and the regent of the sky and the lord of everything great.

sn: दहन् मृतानि भूतानी तस्याग्निर्भरतोऽभवत्। अग्निष्टोमे च नियतः क्रतुश्रेष्ठो भरस्य तु॥
en: His son, the Bharata fire, consumes the dead bodies of all creatures. His first Kratu is known as Niyata at the performance of Agnishtoma.

sn: स वह्निः प्रथमो नित्यं देवैरन्विष्यते प्रभुः। आयान्तं नियतं दृष्ट्वा प्रविवेशार्णवं भयात्॥
en: That mighty chief fire (Svaha) is always missed by the celestials, for when he sees Niyata coming towards him, he hides himself in the sea for fear.

sn: देवास्तत्रापि गच्छन्ति मार्गमाणा यथादिशम्। दृष्ट्वा त्वग्निरथर्वाणं ततो वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Seeing him in every direction, the celestials could not find him out and seeing Atharvan, the fire thus spoke to him.

sn: देवानां वह हव्यं त्वमहं वीर सुदुर्बलः। अथ त्वं गच्छ मध्वक्षं प्रियमेतत् कुरुष्व मे॥
en: "O hero, carry the oblations for the celestials. I am unable to do it for the want of strength. Becoming the red-eyed fire, be good enough to do me this favour."

sn: प्रेष्य चाग्निरथर्वाणमन्यं देशं ततोऽगमत्। मत्स्यास्तस्य समाचख्युः क्रुद्धस्तानग्निरब्रवीत्। भक्ष्या वै विविधैर्भावैर्भविष्यथ शरीरिणाम्॥
en: Having thus spoken to Atharvan, the fire went away to some other place. But his place of concealment was divulged by the fish, Upon them he passed this course in anger.

sn: अथर्वाणं तथा चापि हव्यवाहोऽब्रवीद् वचः।११।।
en: You shall be the food of all creatures in various ways." Then the fire spoke to Atharvan (again as he did before).

sn: अनुनीयमानो हि भृशं देववाक्याद्धि तेन सः। नैच्छद् वोढुं हविः सोढुं शरीरं चापि सोऽत्यजत्॥
en: Though entreated by the celestials, he did not agree to continue to carry the oblations. He then became insensible and abandoned his body.

sn: स तच्छरीरं संत्यज्य प्रविवेश धरां तदा। भूमिं स्पृष्टासृजद् धातून पृथक् पृथगतीव हि॥ पूयात् स गन्धं तेजश्च अस्थिभ्यो देवदारु च। श्लेष्मणः स्फाटिकं तस्य पित्तान्मारकतं तथा॥ यकृत् कृष्णायसं तस्य त्रिभिरेव वभुः प्रजाः। नखास्तस्याभ्रपटलं शिराजलानि विदुमम्॥
en: Leaving his material body, he entered into the nether world. Coming in contact with the earth, he created different force and perfume arose from his puss, the Deodar tree from his bones, grass from this phlegm, the Marakata jewel from his bile and the black iron from his liver. All the worlds have been established with these three substances. The clouds were made from his nails and corals from his arteries,

sn: शरीराद् विविधाश्चान्ये धातवोऽस्याभवन् नृप। एवं त्यक्त्वा शरीरं च परमे तपसि स्थितः॥
en: O King, various other metals were produced from his body. Thus leaving his material body, he lay absorbed in meditation.

sn: भृग्वङ्गिरादिभिर्भूयस्तपसोत्थापितस्तदा। भृशं जज्वाल तेजस्वी तपसाऽऽप्यायित: शिखी।॥
en: He was roused by the penance of Bhrigu and Angirasa. The mighty Agni, thus gratified by their penance, blazed forth in great effulgence.

sn: दृष्ट्वा ऋषि भयाच्चापि प्रविवेश महार्णवम्। तस्मिन् नष्टे जगद् भीतमथर्वाणमथाश्रितम्। अर्चयामासुरेवैनमथर्वाणं सुरादयः॥
en: But seeing the Rishi, he in fear again entered the great ocean. When he thus disappeared, all the worlds were filled with fear and came to Atharvan for protection. The celestials and others then began to adore Atharvan.

sn: अथर्वा त्वसृजल्लोकानात्मनाऽऽलोक्य पावकम्। मिषतां सर्वभूतानामुन्ममाथ महार्णवम्॥ एवमग्निर्भगवता नष्टः पूर्वमथर्वणा। आहूतः सर्वभूतानां हव्यं वहति सर्वदा॥
en: Atharvan overhauled the whole sea and (at last) finding Agni, he himself (then) began the creation. Thus the fire was destroyed and rescued from the sea. thus was he revived by the exalted Atharvan; and thus from that time he always carries the oblations of all creatures.

sn: एवं त्वजनयद् धिष्ण्यान् वेदोक्तान् विबुधान् बहून्। विचरन् विविधान् देशान् भ्रममाणस्तु तत्र वै॥
en: Living in the sea and travelling in various countries, he produced the various fires mentioned in the Shastras.

sn: सिन्धुनदं पञ्चनदं देविकाथ सरस्वती। गङ्गा च शतकुम्भा च सरयूर्गण्डसाह्वया॥ चर्मग्वती मही चैव मेध्या मेधातिथिस्तदा। ताम्रवती वेत्रवती नद्यस्तिस्रोऽथ कौशिकी॥ तमसा नर्मदा चैव नदी गोदावरी तथा। वेणोपवेणा भीमा च वडवा चैव भारत॥ भारती सुप्रयोगा च कावेरी मुर्मुरा तथा। तुड़वेणा कृष्णवेणा कपिला शोण एव च॥ एता नद्यस्तु धिष्ण्यानां मातरो याः प्रकीर्तिताः।
en: The river Sindhu, the five rivers, the Devika, the Sarasvati, the Ganga, the Shatakumbha, the Sarayu, the Gandaki, the Charmnavati, the Mahi, the Medhya, the Medhatithi, the three rivers Tamravati, the Vetravati, the Kaushiki, the Tamasa, the Narmada, the Godavari, the Vena, the Upavena, the Bhima, the Vadava, the Bharati, the Suprayoga, the Kaveri, the Murmura, the Tungavena, the Krishnavena, the Kapila and the Sonabhadra, these rivers are said to be the mothers of the fires.

sn: अद्भुतस्य प्रिया भार्या तस्य पुत्रो विभूरसिः॥ यावन्तः पावकाः प्रोक्ताः सोमास्तावन्त एव तु। अत्रेचाप्यन्वये जाता ब्रह्मणो मानसाः प्रजाः॥
en: Adbhuta had a wife named Priya and Vibhurasi was his eldest son. There are as many kinds of Soma sacrifices as the number of fires mentioned. All these fires were first born from the spirit of Brahma, but they also sprung from the race of Atri.

sn: अत्रिः पुत्रान् स्रष्टुकामस्तानेवात्मन्यधारयत्।२८॥ तस्य तद्ब्रह्मणः कार्यान्निर्हरन्ति हुताशनाः।
en: He in his own mind conceived these sons in order to extend the creation. These fires all sprung from his Brahmic body.

sn: एवमेते महात्मानः कीर्तितास्तेऽग्नयो मया।॥ अप्रमेया यथोत्पन्नाः श्रीमन्तस्तिमिरापहाः।
en: I have thus narrated to you the history of the origin of the (different) fires. They are great, effulgent and matchless in prowess; and they are the destroyer of darkness.

sn: अद्भुतस्य तु माहात्म्यं यथा वेदेषु कीर्तितम्॥ तादृशं विद्धि सर्वेषामेको ह्येषु हुताशनः।
en: Know that the prowess of all fires is the same as that of the Adbhuta fire as described in the Vedas. All these fires are one and the same.

sn: एक एवैष भगवान् विज्ञेयः प्रथमोऽङ्गिराः॥ बहुधा निःसृतः कायाज्ज्योतिष्टोमः क्रतुर्यथा।
en: This adorable and exalted being, the firstborn fire, must be considered as all the fires, for like the Jyotishtoma sacrifice, he came out of Angira's body in various forms.

sn: इत्येष वंशः सुमहानग्नीनां कीर्तितो मया। योऽर्चितो विविधैर्मन्त्रैर्हव्यं वहति देहिनाम्॥
en: I have thus told you the history of the great Agni race. When duly worshipped with hymns they carry the oblations of all creatures to the celestials.
