sn: त्रासितं विविधैर्बाणैः कृतं चैव पराङ्मुखम्। अथोत्क्रुष्टं तदा हृष्टैः सर्वैर्देवैरुदायुधैः॥ संहतनि च तूर्याणि प्रावाद्यन्त ह्यनेकशः। एवमन्योन्यसंयुक्तं युद्धमासीत् सुदारुणम्॥
en: Were struck with panic and they wavered at that shower of various arrows. Then the celestials loudly gave vent to their joy with uplifted weapons. The celestials musicians began to play various airs. Thus took place that great battle, so fearful to both sides.

sn: देवानां दानवानां च मांसशोणितकर्दमम्। अनयो देवलोकस्य सहसैवाभ्यदृश्यत॥ तथा हि दानवा घोरा विनिघ्नन्ति दिवौकसः। ततस्तूर्यप्रणादाश्च भेरीणां च महास्वनः॥ बभूवुर्दानवेन्द्राणां सिहनादाश्च दारुणाः। अथ दैत्यवलाद् घोरान्निष्पपात महाबलः॥ दानवो महिषो नाम प्रगृह्य विपुलं गिरिम्।
en: The battle field was covered with blood and strewn with the bodies of both the Devas and the Danavas. The celestials however, were soon worsted and the fearful Danavas again made a great havoc of the celestials army. The Asura drums were sounded and their shrill bugles were loudly blown. The Danava chiefs sent forth terrific lion-like roars. Then came forward from the fearful Danava army a greatly powerful Danava, named Mahisha with a large mass of rocks in his hands.

sn: ते तं घरिवादित्यं दृष्ट्वा सम्परिवारितम्॥ तमुद्यतगिरिं राजन् व्यद्रवन्त दिवौकसः।
en: He looked like the sun peeping from amongst a mass of dark clouds. O king, seeing that uplifted mass of rocks about to be hurled on them, the dwellers of heaven fled in confusion.

sn: अथाभिदुत्य महिषो देवांश्चिक्षेप तं गिरिम्॥ पतता तेन गिरिणा देवसैन्यस्य पार्थिव। भीमरूपेण निहतमयुतं प्रापतद् भुवि॥
en: But they were pursued by Mahisha who hurled on them the rock. O ruler of earth, by the falling of that rock, ten thousand warriors of the celestials army were killed by being crushed to the ground.

sn: अथ तैर्दानवैः सार्धं महिषस्त्रासयन् सुरान्। अभ्यद्रवद् रणे तूर्णं सिंहः क्षुद्रमृगानिव॥
en: This act of Mahisha struck terror into the hearts of the celestials. With other Danavas, he again attacked them as a lion attacks a herd of small deer.

sn: तमापतन्तं महिषं दृष्ट्वा सेन्द्रा दिवौकसः। व्यद्रवन्त रणे भीता विकीर्णायुधकेतनाः॥
en: When Indra and the other dwellers of heaven saw that Mahisha was advancing to attack them, they fled leaving behind their arms and colours.

sn: ततः स महिषः क्रुद्धस्तूर्णं रुद्ररथं ययौ। अभिद्रुत्य च जग्राह रुद्रस्य रथकूबरम्॥
en: Thereupon Mahisha was greatly enraged and the quickly advanced towards the chariot of Rudra. Reaching near, he seized its pole with his hands.

sn: यदा रुद्ररथं क्रुद्धो महिषः सहसा गतः। रेसतू रोदसी गाढं मुमुहुश्च महर्षयः॥
en: When Mahisha in great wrath thus seized the pole of Rudra's chariot, the earth began to groan and the great Rishis fainted away.

sn: अनदंश्च महाकाया दैत्या जलधरोपमाः। आसीच्च निश्चितं तेषां जितमस्माभिरित्युत॥
en: Huge and cloud-like Daityas made great noise in joy, thinking that they had already won the victory.

sn: तथाभूते तु भगवान् नावधीन्महिषं रणे। सस्मार च तदा स्कन्दं मृत्यु तस्य दुरात्मनः॥
en: Though the exalted Rudra was in this plight, he did not kill Mahisha, for he knew that the wicked wretch would be killed by Skanda.

sn: महिषोऽपि रथं दृष्ट्वा रौद्रोरुद्रस्य चानदत्। देवान संत्रासयंश्चापि दैत्यांश्चापि प्रहर्षयन्॥
en: The fiery Mahisha, gloating over the prize he had secured, sent up in great joy loud roars to the great alarm of the celestials and to the great joy of the Danavas.

sn: ततस्तस्मिन् भये घोरे देवानां समुपस्थिते। आजगाम महासेनः क्रोधात् सूर्य इव ज्वलन्॥
en: When the celestials were in that great danger, Mahasena burning like a (second) sun came forward in great wrath.

sn: लोहिताम्बरसंवीतो लोहितस्त्रग्विभूषणः। लोहिताश्वो महाबाहुर्हिरण्यकवचः प्रभुः॥
en: That mighty armed lord was clad in red , clothes, adorned with garlands of red flowers and incased in golden armour.

sn: रथमादित्यसंकाशमास्थितः कनकप्रभम्। तं दृष्ट्वा दैत्यसेना सा व्यद्रवत् सहसा रणे॥
en: He rode on a golden chariot as bright as the sun, drawn by chest-nut horses. Seeing him the Daitya forces suddenly lost heart in the field of battle.

sn: स चापि तां प्रज्वलितां महिषस्य विदारिणीम्। मुमोच शक्ति राजेन्द्र महासेनो महाबलः॥ सा मुक्ताभ्यहरत् तस्य महिषस्य शिरो महत्। पपात भिन्ने शिरसि महिषस्त्यक्तजीवितः॥
en: O king of kings, the greatly powerful Mahasena hurled a blazing Shakti (weapon) for the destruction of Mahisha. That weapon cut off his head and he fell on the ground dead.

sn: पतता शिरसा तेन द्वारं षोडशयोजनम्। पर्वताभेन पिहितं तदागम्यं ततोऽभवत्॥ उत्तराः कुरवस्तेन गच्छन्त्यद्य यथासुखम्। क्षिप्ताक्षिप्ता तु सा शक्तिहत्वा शत्रून् सहस्रशः॥ स्कन्दहस्तमनुप्राप्ता दृश्यते देवदानवैः। प्रायः शरैर्विनिहता महासेनेन धीमता॥ शेषा दैत्यगणा घोरा भीतास्त्रस्ता दुरासदैः। स्कन्दपारिषदैर्हत्वा भक्षिताश्च सहस्रशः॥ दानवान् भक्षयन्तस्ते प्रपिबन्तश्च शोणितम्। क्षणान्निनवं सर्वमकार्षु शहर्षिताः॥
en: His head, as massive as a hill, extending in length sixteen yojanas, falling on the ground barred the entrance to the country of the northern Kurus, though now the people of that country easily pass by that gate. It was seen by the Devas and the Danavas that Skanda hurled his Shakti again and again on the field of battle. It returned to his hands again and again killing thousands of the enemies. The fearful Danavas were killed in large numbers by the arrows of the greatly intelligent Mahasena. Then they were exceedingly alarmed and the followers of Skanda began to kill and cut them down and drink their blood. They in great joy exterminated the Danavas in no time.

sn: तमांसीव यथा सूर्यो वृक्षानग्निर्घनान् खगः। तथा स्कन्दोऽजयच्छत्रून् स्वेन वीर्येण कीर्तिमान्।१०२॥
en: As the sun destroys darkness or as fire destroys a forest or as the wind drives away clouds. In this manner, the illustrious Skanda defeated all his enemies.

sn: सम्पूज्यमानस्त्रिदशैरभिवाद्य महेश्वरम्। शुशुभे कृत्तिकापुत्रः प्रकीर्णांशुरिवांशुमान॥
en: The celestials came to congratulate him and he in his turn worshipped Maheshvara (Shiva). The son of Kritika looked as grand as the sun in all his glorious effulgence.

sn: नष्टशत्रुर्यदा स्कन्दः प्रयातस्तु महेश्वरम्। तदाब्रवीन्महासेनं परिष्वज्य पुरंदरः॥
en: When the enemies (of the celestials) were completely destroyed by Skanda and when Maheshvara went away, then Purandara embraced him and thus spoke to him,

sn: ब्रह्मदत्तवरः स्कन्द त्वयायं महिषो हतः। देवास्तृणसमा यस्य बभूवुर्जयतां वर॥
en: "O Skanda, O foremost of all warriors, this Mahisha who was made invincible by Brahma is (now) killed by you. The celestials were like grass to him.

sn: सोऽयं त्वया महाबाहो शमितो देवकण्टकः। शतं महिषतुल्यानां दानवानां त्वया रणे॥ निहतं देवशत्रूणां यैर्वयं पूर्वतापिताः। तावकैर्भक्षिताश्चान्ये दानवाः शतसङ्घशः॥
en: O mighty armed hero, you have removed a thorn from the side of the celestials; you have killed in battle hundreds of Danavas, as brave as Mahisha, those enemies of the celestials who used to harass us always. Your followers have eaten up hundreds of Danavas,

sn: अजेयस्त्वं रणेऽरीणामुमापतिरिव प्रभुः। एतत् ते प्रथमं देव ख्यातं कर्म भविष्यति॥
en: O god, you are as invincible in battle as the husband of Uma (Shiva). This victory will be celebrated as your first great achievement.

sn: त्रिषु लोकेषु कीर्तिश्च तवाक्षय्या भविष्यति। वशगाश्च भविष्यन्ति सुरास्तव महाभुज॥
en: Your fame will be everlasting all over the three worlds. O mighty armed hero, all the celestials will pay allegiance to you."

sn: एवमुक्त्वा महासेनं निवृत्तः सह दैवतैः। अनुज्ञातो भगवता त्र्यम्बकेण शचीपतिः॥
en: Having said this to Mahasena, the husband of Sachi with the permission of the three eyed deity (Shiva) left the place accompanied by the celestials.

sn: गतो भद्रवट रुद्रो निवृत्ताश्च दिवौकसः। उक्ताश्च देवा रुद्रेण स्कन्दं पश्यत मामिव॥
en: Rudra returned to Bhadravata and the celestials returned to their respective abodes. The celestials were thus addressed by Rudra, “Look at Skanda as you do me.

sn: स हत्वा दानवगणान् पूज्यमानो महर्षिभिः। एकाद्वैवाजयत् सर्वं त्रैलोक्यं वह्निनन्दनः॥ स्कन्दस्य य इदं विप्रः पठेज्जन्म समाहितः। स पुष्टिमिह सम्प्राप्य स्कन्दसालोक्यमाप्नुयात्॥
en: That son of Agni, having killed the Danavas, have conquered the three worlds in one day. He has been worshipped by the great Rishis. The Brahmanas who attentively read this story of the birth of Skanda obtain prosperity in this world and the association with Skanda in the next world."

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच भगवन् श्रोतुमिच्छामि नामान्यस्य महात्मनः। त्रिषु लोकेषु यान्यस्य विख्यातानि द्विजोत्तम॥
en: Yudhishthira said : O high-souled and the exalted Brahmana, I desire to know the names of that great deity by which he is celebrated all over the three worlds.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच इत्युक्तः पाण्डवेयेन महात्मा ऋषिसंनिधौ। उवाच भगवांस्तत्र मार्कण्डेयो महातपाः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having been thus addressed by the illustrious Pandava in the midst of the Rishis, the exalted and the greatly ascetic Markandeya said-

sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच आग्नेयश्चैव स्कन्दश्च दीप्तकीर्तिरनामयः। मयूरकेतुर्धर्मात्मा भूतेशो महिषार्दनः॥ कामजित् कामदः कान्तः सत्यवाग् भुवेनश्वरः। शिशुः शीघ्रः शुचिश्चण्डो दीप्तवर्णः शुभाननः॥ अमोघस्त्वनधो रौद्रः प्रियश्चन्द्राननस्तथा। दीप्तशक्तिः प्रशान्तात्मा भद्रकृत् कूटमोहनः॥ षष्ठीप्रियश्च धर्मात्मा पवित्रो मातृवत्सलः। कन्याभर्ता विभक्तश्च स्वाहेयो रेवतीसुतः॥ प्रभुर्नेता विशाखश्च नैगमेयः सुदुश्चरः। सुव्रतो ललितश्चैव बालक्रीडनकप्रियः॥ खचारी ब्रह्मचारी च शूरः शरवणोद्भवः। विश्वामित्रप्रियश्चैव देवसेनाप्रियस्तथा।॥ वासुदेवप्रियश्चैव प्रिय: प्रियकृदेव तु। नामान्येतानि दिव्यानि कार्तिकेयस्य यः पठेत्। स्वर्ग कीर्तिं धनं चैव स लभेन्नात्र संशयः॥
en: Markandeya said : (They are) Agneya, Skanda, Diptakirti, Anameya, Mayuraketu, Dharmatma, Bhutesha, Mahishmardana, Kamajit, Kamada, Kanta, Satyavak, Bhuvaneshvara, Shishu, Shighra, Suchi, Chanda, Dipatvarna, Shubhanana, Amogha, Anagha, Raudra, Priya, Chandranana, Diptashakti, Prashantatman, Bhadrakrit, Kutamohana, Shashtipriya, Pavitra, Matrivatsala, Kanyabharta, Vibhakta, Svaheya, Revatisuta, Prabhu, Neta, Vishakha, Naigameya, Suduschara, Suduschara, Suvrata, Lalita, Balakridanakapriya, Akashachari, Brahmachari, Shura, Shakhanodbhava, Vishvamitrapriya, Devasenapriya, Vasudevapriya, Priya and Priyakrit. These are the divine names of Kartikeya. Whoever repeats them there is no doubt he secures fame, wealth and salvation.

sn: स्तोष्यामि देवैर्ऋषिभिश्च जुष्टं शक्त्या गुहं नामभिरप्रमेयम्। षडाननं शक्तिधरं सुवीरं निबोध चैतानि कुरुप्रवी॥
en: O foremost of the Kurus, I shall now with devotion pray to that matchless, powerful, six faced and brave Guha who is worshipped by the celestials and the Rishis. Listen to them.

sn: ब्रह्मण्यो वै ब्रह्मजो ब्रह्मविच्च ब्रह्मेशयो ब्रह्मवतां वरिष्ठः। ब्रह्मप्रियो ब्राह्मणसव्रती त्वं ब्रह्मज्ञो वै ब्राह्मणानां च नेता॥
en: O Skanda, you are devoted to Brahma you are begotten by Brahma, you are versed in the mysteries of Brahma, you are Brahmeshya, you are the foremost of those who possess Brahma, you are fond of Brahma, you are as austere as the Brahmanas, you are learned in the great mystery of Brahma and you are the leader of the Brahmanas.

sn: स्वाहा स्वधा त्वं परमं पवित्रं मन्त्रस्तुतस्त्वं प्रथितः षडर्चिः। संवत्सरस्त्वमृतवश्च घड् वै मासार्धमासावयनं दिशश्च॥
en: You are Guha, you are Svadha, you are the holiest of the holy. You are invoked by Mantras and you are celebrated as the six flamed fire, you are the year, you are the six seasons, you are the months, the fortnights, the solar declination and the cardinal points of firmament.

sn: त्वं पुष्कराक्षस्त्वरविन्दवक्त्रः सहस्रवक्त्रोऽसि सहस्रबाहुः। त्वं लोकपालः परमं हविश्व त्वं भावनः सर्वसुरासुराणाम्॥
en: You are lotus-eyed, you possess a lotus-like face, you have one thousand faces and one thousand arms. You are the ruler of the universe and you are the great oblations, you are the animating spirit of all the celestials and the Asuras.

sn: त्वमेव सेनाधिपतिः प्रचण्डः प्रभुर्विभुश्चाप्यथ शत्रुजेता। सहस्रभूस्त्वं धरणी त्वमेव सहस्रतुष्टिश्च सहस्रभुक् च॥
en: You are the generallissimo of armies, you are fury, you are the lord, you are the great master, you are the conqueror of your enemies, you Sahasrbhu, Sahasratushti and Sahasrbhuk.

sn: सहस्रशीर्षस्त्वमनन्तरूपः सहस्रपात् त्वं गुह शक्तिधारी। गङ्गासुतस्त्वं स्वमतेन देव स्वाहामहीकृत्तिकानां तथैव॥
en: You are the Sahasrapat, you are the earth herself, you possess innumerable forms and thousands of heads, you are endued with great strength. O god, you have with your own desire are appeared as the son of Ganga, Svaha and Mahikritika.

sn: त्वं क्रीडसे षण्मुख कुक्कुटेन यथेष्टनानाविधकामरूपी। दीक्षासि सोमो मरुतः सदैव धर्मोऽसि वायुरचलेन्द्र इन्द्रः॥
en: O six-faced god, you play with the cock, you assume various forms according to your own will, you are Daksha, Soma, Marutas, Dharma, Vayu and the king of mountains.

sn: सनातनानामपि शाश्वतस्त्वं प्रभुः प्रभूणामपि चोचधन्वा। ऋतस्य कर्ता दितिजान्तकस्त्वं जेता रिपूणां प्रवरः सुराणाम्॥
en: For everlasting time you are mighty, you are the most eternal of all eternal things and you are the lord of lords, you are the origin of Truth, you are the destroyer of the children of Diti, you are the great conqueror of the enemies of the celestials.

sn: सूक्ष्मं तपस्तत् परमं त्वमेव परावरज्ञोऽसि परावरस्त्वम्। धर्मस्य कामस्य परस्य चैव त्वत्तेजसा कृत्स्त्रमिदं महात्मन्॥
en: You are the personation of virtue. Being yourself both vast and minute, you are acquainted with the highest and the lowest points of virtuous acts, you are the mysteries of Brahma.

sn: व्याप्तं जगत् सर्वसुरप्रवीर शक्त्या मया संस्तुत लोकनाथ। नमोऽस्तु ते द्वादशनेत्रबाहो अतः परं वेद्मि गतिं न तेऽहम्॥
en: O foremost of the celestials, O lord of the universe, this whole creation is pervaded by your spirit. I have thus prayed to you according to the best of my power. I bow to you who possess twelve eyes and twelve hands. Your remaining attributes are beyond my conception.

sn: स्कन्दस्य य इदं विप्रः पठेज्जन्म समाहितः। श्रावयेद् ब्राह्मणेभ्यो यः शृणुयाद् वा द्विजेरितम्॥ धनमायुर्यशो दीप्तं पुत्राञ्छत्रुजयं तथा। स पुष्टितुष्टी सम्प्राप्य स्कन्दसालोम्यमाप्नुयात्॥
en: The Brahmana who attentively reads this story of the birth of Skanda or narrates it to Brahmanas or hears it narrated by Brahmanas obtains wealth, long-life, fame, children, victory, prosperity, contentment and association with Skanda.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच उपासीनेषु विप्रेषु पाण्डवेषु महात्मसु। द्रौपदी सत्यभामा च विविशाते तदा समम्॥
en: Vaishampayana sajd : When the high-souled Pandavas and the Brahmanas had taken their seats. Draupadi and Satyabhama entered the hermitage.

sn: जाहस्यमाने सुप्रीते सुखं तत्र निषीदतुः। चिरस्य दृष्ट्वा राजेन्द्र तेऽन्योन्यस्य प्रियंवदे॥ कथयामासतुश्चित्राः कथा: कुरुयत्थिताः। अथाब्रवीत् सत्यभामा कृष्णस्य महिषी प्रिया।॥ सात्राजिती याज्ञसेनी रहसीदं सुमध्यमा। केन द्रौपदि वृत्तेन पाण्डवानधितिष्ठसि॥
en: O king of kings, with hearts full of joy, they laughed merrily and they seated themselves at their ease. Those ladies who always spoke sweetly to each other, having met after a long time, began to talk upon various delightful topics arising out of the accounts of the Kurus and the Yadus. The slender waited Satyabhama, the favourite wife of Krishna and the daughter of Satrajit then asked (Draupadi) in private saying, "How, O Draupadi, can you rule the sons of Pandu.

sn: लोकपालोपमान् वीरान् पुन: परमसंहतान्। कथं च वशगास्तुभ्यं न कुप्यन्ति च ते शुभे॥
en: Those heroes who are endued with great strength and beauty and who are like the Lokapalas themselves. O beautiful lady, how is it that they are so obedient to you and that they are never angry with you?

sn: तव वश्या हि सततं पाण्डवाः प्रियदर्शने। मुखप्रेक्षाश्च ते सर्वे तत्त्वमेतद् ब्रवीहि मे॥
en: O lady of lovely feature, the Pandavas are always obedient to you. They are all watchful to do your bidding. Tell me its reason.

sn: व्रतचर्या तपो वापि स्नानमन्त्रौषधानि वा। विद्यावीर्यं मूलवीर्यं जपहोमागदास्तथा॥
en: It is vows or asceticism or incantations or drug in your season or the efficacy of science or the influence of youthful appearance or the recitation of particular formulae or homa or collyrium and other medicament?

sn: ममाद्याचक्ष्व पाञ्चालि यशस्यं भगदैवतम्। येन कृष्णे भवेन्नित्यं मम कृष्णो वशानुगः॥
en: Tell me, O Panchala princess, of that blessed and auspicious thing by which, O Krishna, (Draupadi) my husband (Krishna) may be ever obedient to me.”

sn: एवमुक्त्वा सत्यभामा विरराम यशस्विनी। पतिव्रता महाभागा द्रौपदी प्रत्युवाच ताम्॥
en: Having said this, the illustrious Satyabhama stopped. The greatly blessed and chaste Draupadi thus replied to her,

sn: असत्स्त्रीणां समाचारं सत्ये मामनुपृच्छसि। असदाचरिते मार्गे कथं स्यादनुकीर्तनम्॥
en: “O Satyabhama, you ask me of the practices of wicked women. How can I speak of practices adopted by wicked women?

sn: अनुप्रश्नः संशयो वा नैतत् त्वय्युपपद्यते। तथा छुपेता बुद्ध्या त्वं कृष्णस्य महिषी प्रिया॥
en: It does not become you to put further questions to me or to doubt me. You are intelligent, you are the favourite wife of Krishna.

sn: यदैव भर्ता जानीयान्मन्त्रमूलपरां स्त्रियम्। उद्विजेत तदैवास्याः सर्पाद् वेश्मगतादिव।॥
en: When the husband learns that his wife is addicted to incantations and drugs, from that day he begins to dread her as if a poisonous snake has entered into his sleeping chamber.

sn: उद्विग्नस्य कुतः शान्तिरशान्तस्य कुतः सुखम्। न जातु वशगो भर्ता स्त्रियाः स्यान्मन्त्रकर्मणा॥
en: Can a man afflicted with fear have peace? How can one who has no peace have happiness? A husband can never be made obedient by a wife with the help of mantras.

sn: अमित्रप्रहितांश्चापि गदान् परमदारुणान्। मूलप्रचारैर्हि विषं प्रयच्छन्ति जिघांसवः॥ जिह्वया यानि पुरुषस्त्वचा वाप्युपसेवते। तत्र चूर्णानि दत्तानि हन्युः क्षिप्रमसंशयम्॥
en: We hear of painful diseases transmitted by enemies. Those that desire to kill others send poison in the shape of gifts, so that the man that takes the powders so sent by tongues or skin is certainly deprived of his life as soon as possible.

sn: जलोदरसमायुक्ताः श्चित्रिणः पलितास्तथा। अपुमांसः कृताः स्त्रीभिर्जडान्धबधिरास्तथा॥
en: Women have sometimes caused dropsy and leprosy, decrepitude, impotency and idiocy, blindness and deafness in men (by administering drugs to enchant them).

sn: पापानुगास्तु पापास्ताः पतीनुपसृजन्त्युत। न जातु विप्रियं भर्तुः स्त्रिया कार्यं कथंचन॥
en: These wicked women, ever treading in the path of sin, do some times injure their husbands. But the wife should never do injury to her husband.

sn: वर्ताम्यहं तु यां वृत्तिं पाण्डवेषु महात्मसु। तां सर्वां शृणु मे सत्यां सत्यभामे यशस्विनि॥
en: O illustrious Satyabhama, hear now of my conduct towards the high-souled Pandavas.

sn: अहंकारं विहायाहं कामक्रोधौ च सर्वदा। सदारान् पाण्डवान् नित्यं प्रयतोपचराम्यहम्॥
en: Abandoning vanity and subduing desire and wrath, I always serve with devotion the Pandavas with all their wives.

sn: प्रणयं प्रतिसंहृत्य निधायात्मानमात्मनि। शुश्रुषुनिरहंमाना पतीनां चित्तरक्षिणी॥
en: Restraining jealously with devotion of heart and without any feeling of degradation at the service I perform, I always serve my husbands.

sn: दुर्व्याहताच्छङ्कमाना दुःस्थिताद् दुरवेक्षितात्। दुरासिताद् दुर्वजितादिङ्गिताध्यासितादपि॥ सूर्यवैश्वानरसमान् सोमकल्पान् महारथान्। सेवे चक्षुर्हणः पार्थानुचवीर्यप्रतापिनः॥
en: Ever fearing to utter what is evil and false or to look or sit or walk with impropriety or to cast glances indicative of the feelings of the heart, I serve the sons of Pritha, those mighty warriors as blazing as the sun or fire and as handsome as the moon, those heroes who are endued with fearful energy and prowess and who are capable of killing their enemies by a glance of their eyes.

sn: देवो मनुष्यो गन्धर्वो युवा चापि स्वलंकृतः। द्रव्यवानभिरूपो वा न मेऽन्यः पुरुषो मतः॥
en: Celestials or men or Gandharvas, young or handsome, wealthy and adorned with ornaments, my heart is never attracted to any other.

sn: नाभुक्तवति नास्नाते नासंविष्टे च भर्तरि। न संविशामि नाश्नामि सदा कर्मकरेष्वपि॥
en: I never bathe or eat or sleep till he that is my husband has bathed or eaten or slept, till all our servants and followers have bathed, eaten and slept.

sn: क्षेत्राद् वनाद् वा ग्रामाद् वा भर्तारं गृहमागतम्। अभ्युत्थायाभिनन्दामि आसनेनोदकेन च॥
en: Whether returning from the field, the forest or the town or hastily rising up I always salute my husband with water and seat.

sn: प्रमृष्टभाण्डा मृष्टान्ना काले भोजनदायिनी। संयता गुप्तधान्या च सुसम्मृष्टनिवेशना॥
en: I always keep the house and all the household articles and the food that is to be taken well-ordered and clean. I carefully keep the rice and serve them the food at the proper time.

sn: अतिरस्कृतसम्भाषा दुःस्त्रियो नानुसेवती। अनुकूलवती नित्यं भवाम्यनलसा सदा॥
en: I am never angry, I never speak harsh words, I never imitate women that are wicked. Avoiding idleness, I always do what is agreeable.

sn: अनर्म चापि हसितं द्वारि स्थानमभीक्षणशः। अवस्करे चिरस्थानं निष्कुटेषु च वर्जये॥
en: I never laugh except at a jest, I never stay for a long time at the gate of the house, I never stay long in places of nature's call or in pleasure gardens of the house.

sn: अतिहासातिरोषौ च क्रोधस्थानं च वर्जये। निरताहं सदा सत्ये भर्तृणामुपसेवने।॥
en: I always refrain from laughing loudly or indulging in high passion and from everything that may give offence. O Satyabhama, I am always engaged in serving my husbands.

sn: सर्वथा भर्तृरहितं न ममेष्ट कथंचन। यदा प्रवसते भर्ता कुटुम्बार्थेन केनिचत्॥
en: A separation from my husband is never agreeable to me. When my husbands leave home to go to my relatives,

sn: सुमनोवर्णकापेता भवामि व्रतचारिणी। यच्च भर्ता न पिवति यच्च भर्ता न सेवते॥
en: I give up flowers and fragrant paste of every kind and I undergo penances. Whatever my husband does not drink, whatever he does not eat.

sn: यच्च नाश्नाति मे भर्ता सर्वं तद् वर्जयाम्यहम्। यथोपदेशं नियता वर्तमाना वराङ्गने॥ स्वलंकृता सुप्रयता भर्तुः प्रियहिते रता। ये च धर्माः कुटुम्बेषु श्वश्र्वा मे कथिताः पुरा॥
en: Whatever my husband does not enjoy, I always renounce. O beautiful lady, adorned with ornaments and ever self-controlled by the instructions received by me, I always devotedly seek the welfare of my husbands. I always perform those duties that my mother-in-law formerly told me in respect of relatives.

sn: भिक्षाबलिश्राद्धमिति स्थालीपाकाच पर्वसु। मान्यानां मानसत्कारा ये चान्ये विदिता मम॥ तान् सर्वाननुवर्तेऽहं दिवारात्रमतन्द्रिता। विनयान् नियमांश्चैव सदा सर्वात्मना श्रिता॥ मृदून् सतः सत्यशीलान् सत्यधर्मानुपालिनः। आशीविषानिव क्रुद्धान् पतीन् परिचराम्यहम्॥
en: As also in respect of alms-giving, of offering worship to the celestials, of offering oblations to the Pitris or boiling food on auspicious days in order to offer it to the Pitris and the guests, of reverence and of service to those that deserve our respect and of all else that are known to me. I always perform my duty night and day without the least idleness. Having my heart firmly fixed in humility and fixed in approved rules, I serve my gentle, truthful and virtuous husbands, considering them always as so many poisonous snakes capable of being enraged at trifle.

sn: पत्याश्रयो हि मे धर्मो मतः स्त्रीणां सनातनः। स देवः सा गतिर्नान्या तस्य का विप्रियं चरेत्॥
en: My opinion is that to depend on one's husband is the eternal virtue of women. The husband is wife's god, he is her (sole) refuge. There is no other refuge for her. How can then a wife act what is disagreeable to her husband?

sn: अहं पतीन् नातिशये नात्यश्ने नातिभूषये। नापि श्वश्रू परिवदे सर्वदा परियन्त्रिता॥
en: I never either in sleeping or in eating or in adorning my person act against the wishes of my husbands. I am always guided by my husbands. I never speak ill of my mother-inlaw.

sn: अवधानेन सुभगे नित्योत्थिततयैव च। भर्तारो वशगा मह्यं गुरुशुश्रूषयैव च॥
en: O blessed lady, my husband has become obedient to me for my diligence, my alacrity and for the humility with which I serve my Gurus.

sn: नित्यमार्यामहं कुन्तीं वीरसूं सत्यवादिनीम्। स्वयं परिचराम्येतां पानाच्छादनभोजनैः॥
en: Every day I personally wait with food and drink and clothes upon the revered and truthful Kunti, the mother of those heroes.

sn: नैतामतिशये जातु वस्त्रभूषणभोजनैः। नापि परिवदे चाहं तां पृथां पृथिवीरामाम्॥
en: I never show any preference for myself over her in matters of food and attire and ornaments. I never reprove in words Pritha (Kuni) who is equal to the earth herself in forgiveness.

sn: अष्टावचे ब्राह्मणानां सहस्राणि स्म नित्यदा। भुञ्जते रुक्मपात्रीषु युधिष्ठिरनिवेशने॥
en: Eight thousand Brahmanas were formerly fed every day in the palace of Yudhishthira from plates of gold.

sn: अष्टाशीतिसहस्राणि स्नातका गृहमेधिनः। त्रिंशद्दासीक एकैको यान् बिभर्ति युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Eighty thousand Snataka Brahmanas, all leading domestic lives, were entertained by Yudhishthira with thirty maid-servants assigned to each.

sn: दशाऱ्यानि सहस्राणि येषामन्नं सुसंस्कृतम्। ह्रियते रुक्मपात्रीभिर्यतीनामूवरेतसाम्॥
en: Besides these, ten thousand Yatis with their desire under complete control had their pure and well-cooked food carried to them in golden plates.

sn: तान् सर्वानग्रहारेण ब्राह्मणान् वेदवादिनः। यथार्ह पूजयामि स्म पानाच्छादनभोजनैः॥
en: All those Brahmanas that were the utterers of the Vedas, I used always to worship duty with food, drink and clothes taken from stores, when a portion of them had been dedicated to Vishvadeva.

sn: शतं दासीसहस्राणि कौन्तेयस्य महात्मनः। कम्बुकेयूरधारिण्यो निष्ककण्ठ्यः स्वलकृताः॥ महार्हमाल्याभरणाः सुवर्णाश्चन्दनोक्षिताः। मणीन् हेम च बिभ्रत्यो नृत्यगीतविशारदाः॥
en: The illustrious son of Kunti, had one hundred thousand well-dressed maid-servants with bracelets of their arms and golden ornaments on their necks; they were adorned with costly garlands and gold in profusion and they were sprinkled with sandal paste. Adorned with gems and gold, they were all well-skilled in dancing and singing.

sn: तासां नाम च रूपं च भोजनाच्छादनानि च। सर्वासामेव वेदाहं कर्म चैव कर्म चैव कृताकृतम्॥
en: I knew the names and features of every one of those girls and also what they used to eat and what they used to wear and what they used not to do.

sn: शतं दासीसहस्राणि कुन्तीपुत्रस्य धीमतः। पात्रीहस्ता दिवारात्रमतिथीन् भोजयन्त्युत॥
en: The greatly intelligent son of Kunti had also one hundred thousand maid-servants who duly used to feed the guests with plates of gold in their hands.

sn: शतमश्वसहस्राणि दशनागायुतानि च। युधिष्ठिरस्यानुयात्रमिन्द्रप्रस्थनिवासिनः॥
en: When Yudhishthira lived in Indraprastha, one lakh horses and one lakh elephants used to follow him.

sn: एतदासीत् तदा राज्ञो यन्महीं पर्यपालयत्। येषां संख्याविधिं चैव प्रदिशामि शृणोमि च॥ अन्तःपुराणां सर्वेषां भृत्यानां चैव सर्वशः। आगोपालाविपालेभ्यः सर्वं वेद कृताकृतम्॥ सर्वं राज्ञः समुदयमायं च व्ययमेव च। एकाहं वेधि कल्याणि पाण्डवानां यशस्विनि॥
en: Such was the procession of Yudhishthira when he ruled over earth. It was I who regulated their number and formed the rules to be observed in respect to them. It was I who had to listen to all their complaints. I knew everything about the maid-servants of the palace and other servants, nay even of the cowherds and shepherds of the royal household. O blessed and illustrious lady, it was I alone among the Pandavas who knew the (real) income and expenditure of the king and what (really) their (Pandavas') whole income was.

sn: मयि सर्वं समासज्य कुटुम्ब भरतर्षभाः। उपासनरताः सर्वे घटयन्ति वरानने॥
en: O beautiful lady, those foremost of Bharatas, throwing upon me the (whole) burden of looking after all those that were to be fed by them, would .iways pay their court to me.

sn: तमहं भारमासक्तमनाधृष्यं दुरात्मभिः। सुखं सर्वं परित्यज्य राज्यहानि घटामि वै॥
en: This load, so heavy and incapable of being borne by persons of evil heart, 1 sacrificing my ease used to bear day and night, all the while being affectionately devoted to them.

sn: अधृष्यं वरुणस्येव निधिपूर्णमिवोदधिम्। एकाहं वेद्मि कोशं वै पतीनां धर्मचारिणाम्॥
en: While my husbands were engaged in virtuous pursuits, I supervised their treasury as inexhaustible as the ever full abode of Varuna (ocean).

sn: अनिशायां निशायां च सहा या क्षुत्पिपासयोः। आराधयन्त्याः कौरव्यांस्तुल्या रात्रिरहश्च मे॥
en: Day and night bearing hunger and thirst, I used to wait upon the Kuru princes, so that my nights and days were equal to me.

sn: प्रथमं प्रतिबुध्यामि चरमं संविशामि च। नित्यकालमहं सत्ये एतत् संवननं मम॥
en: I used to rise up from my bed first and to go to my bed last. O Satyabhama, this has ever been my custom.

sn: एतज्जानाम्यहं कर्तुं भर्तृसंवननं महत्। असत्स्त्रीणां समाचार नाहं कुर्यां न कामये॥
en: This is the great charm ever known to me for making my husbands obedient to me. I have never used any charms of wicked women and I never wish to use them."

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तच्छ्रुत्वा धर्मसहितं व्याहृतं कृष्णया तदा। उवाच सत्या सत्कृत्य पाञ्चालीं धर्मचारिणीम्॥ अभिपन्नास्मि पाञ्चालि याज्ञसेनि क्षमस्व मे। कामकारः सखीनां हि सोपहासं प्रभाषितम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having heard these virtuous words of Krishna (Draupadi), Satyabhama expressed her greatest reverence for the Panchala princess and she thus spoke to her, "O Panchala princess, O Yajnaseni, I am in fault, forgive me. Among friends conversations in jest naturally and without premeditation arise."

sn: द्रौपद्युवाच इमं तु ते मार्गमपेतमोहं वक्ष्यामि चित्तग्रहणाय भर्तुः। अस्मिन् यथावत् सखि वर्तमाना भर्तारमाच्छेत्स्यसि कामिनीभ्यः॥
en: Draupadi said: I shall now point out to you a way for attracting the hearts of your husband which is free from deceit. O friend, by duly adopting it, you will be able to withdraw your husband from other women.

sn: नैतादृशं दैवतमस्ति सत्ये सर्वेषु लोकेषु सदेवकेषु। यथा पतिस्तस्य त सर्वकाम लभ्याः प्रसादात् कुपितश्च हन्यात्॥
en: O Satyabhama, in all the worlds including that of the celestials, there is no god equal to the husband. When gratified with you, you may get (from your husband) ever object of desire, but when angry, all of them may be lost.

sn: तस्मादपत्यं विविधाश्च भोगाः शय्यासनान्युत्तमदर्शनानि। वस्त्राणि माल्यानि तथैव गन्धाः स्वर्गश्च लोको विपुला च कीर्तिः॥
en: It is from her husband that the wife obtains offspring and various articles of enjoyments. From your husband you may have handsome beds and seats, robes and garlands, perfumes and great fame and heaven itself hereafter.

sn: सुखं सुखेनेह न जातु लभ्यं दुःखेन साध्वी लभते सुखानि। सा कृष्णमाराधय सौहदेन प्रेम्णा च नित्यं प्रतिकर्मणा च॥
en: One cannot obtain happiness here by means that are easy. The woman that is chaste obtains happiness with great misery. Therefore always adore Krishna with friendship, love and sufferings.

sn: र्दाक्षिण्ययोगैर्विविधैश्च गन्धैः। अस्याः प्रियोऽस्मीति यथा विदित्वा त्वामेव संश्लिष्यति तद् विधस्त्व॥
en: Act in such a way by offering handsome seats and excellent garlands and various perfumes and prompt service that he may be devoted to you, thinking, "I am truly loved by her."

sn: श्रुत्वा स्वरं द्वारगतस्य भर्तुः प्रत्युत्थिता तिष्ठ गृहस्य मध्ये। दृष्ट्वा प्रविष्टं त्वरिताऽऽसनेन पायेन चैनं प्रतिपूजयस्व॥
en: Hearing the voice of your husband at the gate, rise from your seat and stay in readiness within the room. As soon as you see him enter your room, worship him by offering him a seat and water to wash his feet.

sn: मुत्थाय सर्वं स्वयमेव कार्यम्। जानातु कृष्णस्तव भावमेतं सर्वात्मना मां भजतीति सत्ये॥
en: O Satyabhama, when he orders a maidservant to do any thing, soon get up and do it yourself. Let Krishna know that you adore him with all your heart.

sn: त्वत्संनिधौ यत् कथयेत् पतिस्ते यद्यप्यगुह्यं परिरक्षितव्यम्। काचित् सपत्नी तव वासुदेवं प्रत्यादिशेत् तेन भवेद् विरागः॥
en: Whatever your husband speaks before you, do not speak it out to every body, though it does not deserve to be concealed, for if any of your co-wives is to speak of it Vasudeva (Krishna), he might be irritated with you.

sn: स्तान् भोजयेथा विविधैरुपायैः। द्वेष्यैरुपेक्ष्यैरहितैश्च तस्य भिद्यस्व नित्यं कुहकोद्यतैश्च॥
en: Always seek the good of your husband and feed by every means in your power those that are dear and devoted to him. You should always keep yourself aloof from those that are hostile to your husband or those who seek to do him injury and those that are deceitful.

sn: मदं प्रमादं पुरुषेषु हित्वा संयच्छ भावं प्रतिगृह्य मौनम्। प्रद्युम्नसाम्बावपि ते कुमारी नोपासितव्यौ रहिते कदाचित्॥
en: Avoiding all excitement and carelessness in the presence of men, conceal your mind by observing silence. You should not stay or talk long even with your sons Pradyumna and Samba.

sn: महाकुलीनाभिरपापिकाभिः स्त्रीभिः सतीभिस्तव सख्यमस्तु। चण्डाश्च शौण्डाश्च महाशनाश्च चौराश्च दुष्टाश्चपलाश्च वाः॥
en: You should make friendship with only those ladies who are highly born, who are sinless and devoted to their husbands; you should always shun women who are wrathful, addicted to drinks, gluttonous, thievish, wicked and fickle.

sn: एतद् यशस्यं भगदैवतं च स्वार्थं तथा शत्रुनिबर्हणं च। महार्हमाल्याभरणाङ्गरागा भर्तारमाराधय पुण्यगन्धा॥
en: Such conduct is always praiseworthy and it always produces prosperity. While it neutralizes hostility, it also leads one to heaven. Therefore worship your husband, adorning yourself with costly garments and ornaments and besmearing yourself with unguents and perfumes.

description: The colloquy between Draupadi and Satyabhama
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच मार्कण्डेयादिभिर्विप्रैः पाण्डवैश्च महात्मभिः। कथाभिरनुकूलाभिः सह स्थित्वा जनार्दनः॥ ततस्तैः संविदं कृत्वा यथावन्मधुसूदनः। आरुरुक्षू रथं सत्यामाह्वयामास केशवः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : The slayer of Madhusudana Keshava Janardana (Krishna), having talked on various agreeable topics with the illustrious Pandavas and with the Brahmanas headed by Markandeya and then having bade them all farewell, ascended his chariot and called for Satyabhama.

description: The colloquy between Draupadi and Satyabhama
sn: सत्यभामा ततस्तत्र स्वजित्वा दुपदात्मजाम्। उवाच वचनं हृद्यं यथाभावं समाहितम्॥
en: Satyabhama then embracing Draupadi spoke these cordial words to her expressive of her feelings towards her.

description: The colloquy between Draupadi and Satyabhama
sn: कृष्णे मा भूत् तवोत्कण्ठा मा व्यथा मा प्रजागरः। भर्तृभिर्देवसंकाशैर्जितां प्राप्स्यसि मेदिनीम्॥
en: "O Krishna, (Draupadi) let there be no anxiety and no grief for you. You have no cause to pass your nights in sleeplessness, for you will surely obtain back the earth subjugated by your husbands who are all equal to the celestials.

description: The colloquy between Draupadi and Satyabhama
sn: न ह्येवं शीलसम्पन्ना नैवं पूजितलक्षणाः। प्राप्नुवन्ति चिरं क्लेशं यथा त्वमसितेक्षणे॥
en: O black and beauty, women having such disposition and possessing such auspicious marks (as you have) can suffer misfortune for a long time.

description: The colloquy between Draupadi and Satyabhama
sn: अवश्यं च त्वया भूमिरियं निहतकण्टका। भर्तृभिः सह भोक्तव्या निर्द्वन्द्वेति श्रुतं मया।॥
en: It has been heard by me that you will with your husbands enjoy without any doubt this earth in peace and free from all thorns. never

description: The colloquy between Draupadi and Satyabhama
sn: धार्तराष्ट्रवधं कृत्वा वैराणि प्रतियात्य च। युधिष्ठिरस्थां पृथिवीं द्रक्ष्यसि दुपदात्मजे॥
en: O daughter of Draupada, when the sons of Dhritarashtra have been all destroyed and severe vengeance has been taken for their hostility, you will certainly see the earth ruled by Yudhishthira.

description: The colloquy between Draupadi and Satyabhama
sn: यास्ताः प्रव्रजमानां त्वां प्राहसन् दर्पमोहिताः। ता: क्षिप्रं हतसंकल्पा द्रक्ष्यसि त्वं कुरुस्त्रियः॥
en: You will soon see those wives of the Kurus, who, deprived of sense by pride, laughed at you when you were coming away in exile, themselves placed in a state of hopelessness and despair.

description: The colloquy between Draupadi and Satyabhama
sn: तव दुःखोपपन्नाया यैराचरितमप्रियम्। विद्धि सम्प्रस्थितान् सर्वांस्तान् कृष्णे यमसादनम्॥
en: O Krishna, know that those who do you any injury when you are in distress are already gone to the abode of Yama,

description: The colloquy between Draupadi and Satyabhama
sn: पुत्रस्ते प्रतिविन्ध्यश्च सुतसोमस्तथाविधः। श्रुतकर्मार्जुनिश्चैव शतानीकश्च नाकुलिः॥
en: Your brave son Prativindhya, Sutasoma and Shrutakarman by Arjuna and Shatanika by Nakula and Shrutasena by Sahadeva are all skillful heroes and experts in weapons.

description: The colloquy between Draupadi and Satyabhama
sn: सहदेवाच्च यो जातः श्रुतसेनस्तवात्मजः। सर्वे कुशलिनो वीराः कृतास्त्राश्च सुतास्तव॥ अभिमन्युरिव प्रीता द्वारवत्यां रता भृशम्। त्वमिवैषां सुभद्रा च प्रीत्या सर्वात्मना स्थिता।॥ प्रीयते तव निर्द्वन्द्वा तेभ्यश्च विगतज्वरा। दुःखिता तेन दुःखेन सुखेन सुखिता तथा॥
en: With Abhimanyu they are all living in Dvarka, much delighted with the place. Subhadra cheerfully and with her whole heart looks after them as you yourself used to do. Like you she takes great delight in them and derives much happiness from them. She grieves in their grief's and joys in their joys.

description: The colloquy between Draupadi and Satyabhama
sn: भजेत् सर्वात्मना चैव प्रद्युम्नजननी तथा। भानुप्रभृतिभिश्चैनान् विशिनष्टि च केशवः॥
en: The mother of Pradyumna also loves them with all their heart. Keshava (Krishna) with his sons Bhanu and others watches over them with special affection.

description: The colloquy between Draupadi and Satyabhama
sn: भोजनाच्छादने चैषां नित्यं मे श्वशुराः स्थितः। रामप्रभृतयः सर्वे भजन्त्यन्धकवृष्णयः॥
en: My mother-in-law is ever attentive in feeding and clothing them. All the Anddhakas and Vrishnis with Rama and others love them very much.

description: The colloquy between Draupadi and Satyabhama
sn: तुल्यो हि प्रणयस्तेषां प्रद्युम्नस्य च भाविनि। एवमादि प्रियं सत्यं हृद्यमुक्त्वा मनोऽनुगम्॥ गमनाय मनश्चक्रे वासुदेवरथं प्रति। तां कृष्णां कृष्णमहिषी चकाराभिप्रदक्षिणम्॥
en: O beautiful lady, their affection for your sons is equal to what they feel for Pradyumna." Having said these agreeable, truthful and delighting and cordial words, Satyabhama desired to go to the chariot of Vasudeva (Krishna). The wife of Krishna then walked round Krishna (Draupadi).

description: The colloquy between Draupadi and Satyabhama
sn: आरुरोह रथं शौरेः सत्यभामाथ भाविनी। स्मयित्वा तु यदुश्रेष्ठो द्रौपदी परिसान्त्व्य च। उपावर्त्य ततः शीघैर्हयैः : प्रायात् पुरं स्वकम्॥
en: The beautiful Satyabhama then ascended the chariot of Krishna. The chief of the Yudus (Krishna) comforted Draupadi with a smile; and then asking the Pandavas to return to their house), he started for his own city with swift horses.

sn: जनमेजय उवाच एवं वने वर्तमाना नराम्याः शीतोष्णवातातपकर्शिताङ्गाः। सरस्तदासाद्य वनं च पुण्यं ततः परं किमकुर्वन्त पार्थाः॥
en: Janamejaya said : O Brahmana, when those foremost of men, the sons of Pritha, were passing their days in the forest exposed to the inclemencies of the winter and the summer, of the wind and the sun, what did they do after they had reached the lake and the forest named Dvaita?

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच सरस्तदासाद्य तु पाण्डुपुत्रा जनं समुत्सृज्य विधाय वेशम्। वनानि रम्याण्यथ पर्वतांश्च नदीप्रदेशांश्च तदा विचेरुः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : When the Pandavas reached the lake, they chose a place to live in far from the habitations of men. They roamed through charming forests and delightful mountains and beautiful valleys through which ran many rivers and stream-lets.

sn: तथा वने तान् वसतः प्रवीरान् स्वाध्यायवन्तश्च तपोधनाचा स्तान् पूजयामासुरथो नरायाः॥
en: When they began to live there, many venerable ascetics, learned in the Vedas, often came to see them. Those foremost of men always received those Veda-knowing Rishis with great respect.

sn: ततः कदाचित् कुशल: कथासु विप्रोऽभ्यगच्छद् भुवि कौरवेयान्। स तैः समेत्याथ यदृच्छयैव वैचित्रवीर्यं नृपमभ्यगच्छत्॥
en: Thereupon one day there came to the Kuru princes a certain Brahmana who was celebrated on carth for his powers of speech. Having talked with them for some time, he went away to the king, the of Vichitravirya (Dhritarashtra).

sn: अथोपविष्टः प्रतिसत्कृतश्च वृद्धेन राज्ञा कुरुसत्तमेन। प्रचोदित: संकथयाम्बभूव धर्मानिलेन्द्रप्रभवान् यमौ च॥
en: Having been received with all respect by that foremost of the Kurus, that old king (Dhritarashtra) the Brahmanas took his seat; and then asked by the king, he talked about the son of Dharma, Pavana, Indra and the twins (Asvinis). son

sn: कृशांश्च वातातपकर्शिताङ्गान् दुःखस्य चोचस्य मुखे प्रपन्नान्। तां चाप्यनाथामिव वीरनाथां कृष्णां परिक्लेशगुणेन युक्ताम्॥
en: All of whom having fallen into great misery had become emaciated and reduced owing to exposure to the wind and the sun. He also talked of Krishna (Draupadi) who had been overwhelmed with sufferings and who had become protectorless though she had heroes for her lords.

sn: ततः कथास्तस्य निशभ्य राजा वैचित्रवीर्यः कृपयाभितप्तः। वने तथा पार्थिवपुत्रपौत्रान् श्रुत्वा तथा दुःखनदी प्रपन्नान्॥
en: On hearing his words, the king Vichitravirya's son became afflicted with grief, thinking that the royal princess (Draupadi) had been drowned in a river of sorrow.

sn: प्रोवाच दैन्याभिहतान्तरात्मा निःश्वासवातोपहतस्तदानीम्। वाचं कथंचित् स्थिरतामुपेत्य तत् सर्वमात्मप्रभवं विचिन्त्या८॥
en: His inmost soul was afflicted with sorrow. Trembling all over with sighs, he quieted himself with great effort, thinking that his folly was the cause of everything. He said,

sn: कथं नु सत्यः शुचिरार्यवृत्तो ज्येष्ठः सुतानां मम धर्मराजः। अजातशत्रुः पृथिवीतले स्म शेते पुरा राङ्कवकूटशायी॥
en: "Alas, how is it that Dharmaraja Yudhishthira who is the eldest of my sons, who is truthful and pious and virtuous in his behaviour, who has not a single enemy (on earth) and who formerly used to sleep on beds made of soft Ranku-skins, sleeps now on the bare ground!

sn: नित्यं स्तुवद्भिः स्वयमिन्द्रकल्पः। पतत्त्रिसझै स जघन्यरात्रे प्रबोध्यते नूनमिडातलस्थः॥
en: He used to be awakened by the Sutas and Magdhas and other singers with his praises melodiously chanted every morning. That Indra-like Kuru prince is now awakened from the bare ground early in the morning by innumerable birds.

sn: कथं नु वातातपकर्शिताङ्गो वृकोदरः कोपपरिप्लुताङ्गः। शेते पृथिव्यामतथोचिताङ्गः कृष्णासमक्षं वसुधातलस्थः॥
en: How does Vrikodara, reduced by exposure to wind and sun and filled with wrath, sleep on the bare ground in the presence of the Panchala princess unfit as he is to suffer such misery?

sn: तथार्जुनः सुकुमारो मनस्वी वशे स्थितो धर्मसुतस्य राज्ञः। धुवं न शेते वसतीरमर्षात्॥
en: Perhaps the intelligent Arjuna who is incapable of bearing pain and who though ever obedient to Yudhishthira yet feels himself pierced by the remembrance of his wrongs, does not at all sleep in the night.

sn: यमौ च कृष्णां च युधिष्ठिरं च भीमं च दृष्ट्वा सुखविप्रयुक्तम्। विनिःश्वसन् सर्प इवोचतेजा ध्रुवं न शेते वसतीरमर्षात्॥
en: Seeing the twins (Nakula and Sahadeva) and Krishna (Draupadi) and Yudhishthira and Bhima in the greatest possible misery, Arjuna certainly sighs like a fearful serpent and from wrath does not sleep in the night.

sn: तथा यमौ चाप्यसुखौ सुखार्हो समृद्धरूपावमरौ दिवीव। प्रजागरस्थौ ध्रुवमप्रशान्तौ धर्मेण सत्येन च वार्यमाणौ॥
en: The twins also, who are even like a couple of blessed celestials in heaven, sunk in misery though deserving of happiness and comfort, certainly pass their nights without sleep, only restrained from taking revenge by virtue and truth.

sn: समीरणेनाथ समो बलेन समीरणस्यैव सुतो बलीयान्। स धर्मपाशेन सितोऽचजेन ध्रुवं विनिःश्वस्य सहत्यमर्षम्॥
en: The mighty son of Vayu (Bhima) who is equal to Vayu himself in strength certainly sighs and restrains his wrath tied through his eldest brother (Yudhishthira) to the bond of truth.

sn: स चापि भूमौ परिवर्तमानो वधं सुतानां मम काक्षमाणः। सत्येन धर्मेण च वार्यमाणः कालं प्रतीक्षत्यधिको रणेऽन्यैः॥
en: Superior in battle to all warriors, he now quietly lies on the ground. Being restrained by virtue and truth but burning to kill my sons, he simply passes his time.

sn: अजातशत्रौ तु जिते निकृत्या दुःशासनो यत् परुषाण्यवोचत्। तानि प्रविष्टानि वृकोदराङ्गं दहन्ति कक्षाग्निरिवेन्धनानि॥
en: The cruel words that Duhshasana spoke after Ajatshatru (Yudhishthira) had been deceitfully defeated at dice have reached the inner most depth of Vrikodara's heart. They are consuming him as a blazing bundle of straw consumes a faggot of dry wood.

sn: न पापकं ध्यास्यति धर्मपुत्रो धनंजयश्चाप्यनुवय॑ते तम्। अरण्यवासेन विवर्धते तु भीमस्य कोपोऽग्निरिवानिलेन॥
en: The son of Dharma (Yudhishthira) never sinfully acts. Dhananjaya (Arjuna) also always obeys him, but the anger of Bhima is daily increasing like a fire helped by the wind in consequence of a life of exile.

sn: स तेन कोपेन विदह्यमानः करं करेणाभिनिपीड्य वीरः। विनिःश्वसत्युष्णमतीव घोरं दहन्निवेमान् मम पुत्रपौत्रान्॥
en: That hero, burning in wrath, squeezes his hands and breathes hot and fearful sighs, as if he wants to consume by them all my sons and grandsons.

sn: गाण्डीवधन्वा च वृकोदरश्च संरम्भिणावन्तककालकल्पौ। न शेषयेतां युधि शत्रुसेनां शरान् किरन्तावशनिप्रकाशान्॥
en: The wielder of Gandiva (Arjuna) and Bhima when angry are like Yama and Kala themselves. Hurling their arrows which are like so many thunderbolts, they exterminate their enemies in battle.

sn: दुर्योधनः शकुनिः सूतपुत्रो दुःशासनश्चापि सुमन्दचेताः। मधु प्रपश्यन्ति न तु प्रपातं यद् द्यूतमालम्ब्य हरन्ति राज्यम्॥
en: Alas, Duryodhana and Shakuni and Suta's son (Karna) and the wicked minded Duhshasana in robbing the Pandavas of their kingdom by means of dice saw only honey (on the tree) without thinking the terrible fall from it!

sn: शुभाशुभं कर्म नरो हि कृत्वा प्रतीक्षते तस्य फलं स्म कर्ता। स तेन मुह्यत्यवशः फलेन मोक्षः कथं स्यात् पुरुषस्य तस्मात्॥
en: A man having acted rightly or wrongly expects to get the fruit of his acts. But fruits however (often) confounds and paralyses him. How can a man thus obtain salvation!

sn: क्षेत्रे सुकृष्टे ह्यपिते च बीजे देवे च वर्षत्यूतुकालयुक्तम्। रन्यत्र दैवादिति चिन्तयामि॥ कृतं मताक्षेण यथा न साधु साधुप्रवृत्तेन च पाण्डवेन। मया च दुष्पुत्रवशानुगेन तथा कुरूणामयमन्तकालः॥
en: If land is properly cultivated and the seed sown and if the god (Indra) seasonably showers rain, still the crop might not grow. This is what we often hear. How could this be true as I think unless everything here in this world) is ruled by Destiny. The gambler Shakuni has behaved deceitfully towards the son of Pandu (Yudhishthira) who always acts honestly and virtuously. From the love and fondness that I bear of my wicked sons I also have similarly acted. Alas, it is for this the time, for the destruction of the Kurus has come.

sn: गर्भिणी या। ध्रुवं प्रवास्यत्यसमीरितोऽपि ध्रुवं प्रजास्यत्युत स्तथा क्षपादौ च दिनप्रणाशः॥
en: Or perhaps what is inevitable must come to pass. The wind, whether impelled or not, must move. The woman who conceives must give birth to a child. Darkness must pass away in the morning and the day in the evening.

sn: वित्तं न दद्युः पुरुषाः कथंचित्। प्राप्यार्थकालं च भवेदनर्थ: कथं न तत् स्यादिति तत् कुतः स्यात्॥ कथं न भिद्येत न च स्रवेत न च प्रसिच्येदिति रक्षितव्यम्। अरक्ष्यमाणं शतधा प्रकीर्येद् ध्रुवं न नाशोऽस्ति कृतस्य लोके॥
en: Whatever may be earned by us and others, whether people spend it or not, it would bring us misery when the time would come. Why then people become so anxious to earn wealth? If what is acquired is the result of Fate, then it should be protected, so that is may not be divided nor protected, so that it may not be divided nor lost little by little nor permitted to flow out at once, for if unprotected it may break into one one hundred fragments. But whatever the character of our possession may be, our acts in this world are never lost.

sn: गतो हरण्यादपि शक्रलोकं धनंजयः पश्यत वीर्यमस्य। अस्त्राणि दिव्यानि चतुर्विधानि ज्ञात्वा पुनर्लोकमिमं प्रपन्नः॥
en: Behold what great is the prowess of Arjuna who went to the abode of Indra from the forest. Having secured the four kinds of celestials weapons, he has returned to earth.

sn: स्वर्गं हि गत्वा सशरीर एव को मानुषः पुनरागन्तुमिच्छेत्। अन्यत्र कालोपहताननेकान् समीक्षमाणस्तु कुरून् मुमूर्षुन्॥
en: What man is there who having gone to heaven in his own human body ever wishes to come back? Because he sees the Kurus at the point of death by Time, he has returned.

sn: धनुर्चाहश्चार्जुनः सव्यसाची धनुश्च तद् गाण्डिवं भीमवेगम्। अस्त्राणि दिव्यानि च तानि तस्य त्रयस्य तेजः प्रसहेत कोऽत्र॥
en: The wielder of the bow is Arjuna Savyasachi, the bow is the Gandiva of fearful energy, the weapons are also all celestials, who is there who would be able to withstand the (combination of these) three."

sn: निशम्य तद् वचनं पार्थिवस्य दुर्योधनं रहिते सौबलोऽथ। अबोधयत् कर्णमुपेत्य सर्वं स चाप्यहृष्टोऽभवदल्पचेताः॥
en: Having heard those words of the king, the son of Subala Shakuni went to Duryodhana who was then with Karna and told them everything in private. The foolish Duryodhana was filled with grief at what he heard.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच धृतराष्ट्रस्य तद् वाक्यं निशम्य शकुनिस्तदा। दुर्योधनमिदं काले कर्णेन सहितोऽब्रवीत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having heard those words of Dhritarashtra, Shakuni, when he got an opportunity through Karna, spoke thus to Duryodhana.

sn: प्रव्राज्य पाण्डवान् वीरान् स्वेन वीर्येण भारत। भुक्ष्येमां पृथिवीमेको दिवि शम्बरहा यथा॥
en: Shakuni said: Having exiled the heroic Pandavas through your own prowess, O descendant of Bharata, you now rule this earth without a rival, as the slayer of Shambara rules the heaven.

sn: प्राच्याश्च दाक्षिणात्याश्च प्रतीच्योदीच्यवासिनः। कृताः करप्रदाः सर्वे राजानस्ते नराधिप।॥
en: O ruler of men, O king, the kings of the east, west, north and south all pay tribute to you.

sn: या हि सा दीप्यमानेव पाण्डवानभजत् पुरा। साद्य लक्ष्मीस्त्वया राजन्नवाप्ता भ्रातृभिः सह॥
en: O king, the blazing goddess of prosperity, that once used to pay court to the Pandavas, has now been secured by you with your brothers.

sn: इन्द्रप्रस्थगते यां तां दीप्यमानां युधिष्ठिरे। अपश्याम श्रियं राजन् दृश्यते सा तवाद्य वै॥
en: O king, the blazing prosperity that we formerly saw in Yudhishthira at Indraprastha is now seen by us in you.

sn: शत्रवस्तव राजेन्द्र न चिरं शोककर्शिताः। सा तु बुद्धिबलेनेयं राज्ञस्तस्माद् युधिष्ठिरात्॥
en: O king of kings, that which you saw not long ago with so much grief has been now snatched by you from the king Yudhishthira by the force of intellect alone.

sn: त्वयाऽऽक्षिप्ता महाबाहो दीप्यमानेव दृश्यते। तथैव तव राजेन्द्र राजानः परवीरहन्॥ शासनेऽधिष्ठिताः सर्वे किं कुर्म इति वादिनः। तवेयं पृथिवी राजन् निखिला सागराम्बरा॥ सपर्वतवना देवी सग्रामनगराकरा। नानावनोद्देशवती पर्वतैरुपशोभिता।॥ वन्द्यमानो द्विजै राजन् पूज्यमानश्च राजभिः। पौरुषाद् दिवि देवेषु भ्राजसे रश्मिवानिव॥
en: O mighty armed hero, O chastiser of foes, all the kings of the world are now under your subjection. They now await your commands as they used to do before those of Yudhishthira. O king, the goddess earth bounded with the seas with her mountains and forests towns and cities and mines, with her woodlands and hills is now yours. Adored by the Brahmanas and worshipped by the kings, O monarch, you (now) blaze forth in your prowess like the sun among the celestials in heaven.

sn: सबैरिव यमो राजा मरुद्भिरिव वासवः। कुरुभिस्त्वं वृतो राजन् भासि नक्षत्रराडिव॥
en: Surrounded by the Kurus, O king, as Yama is surrounded by the Rudras and Vasava by the Marutas, you shine like the moon among the stars.

sn: यैः स्म ते नाद्रियेताज्ञा न च ये शासने स्थिताः। पश्यामस्तान् श्रिया हीनान् पाण्डवान् वनवासिनः॥
en: Let us go and see the Pandavas who are now divested of their prosperity, who are now living in the forest, who never obeyed commands and who never owed you subjection.

sn: श्रूयते हि महाराज सरो द्वैतवनं प्रति। वसन्तः पाण्डवाः सार्धं ब्राह्मणैर्वनवासिभिः॥
en: O great king, we have heard that they are now living on the banks of the lake situated in the forest named Dvaitavana with many Brahmanas, the dwellers of the wood.

sn: स प्रयाहि महाराज श्रिया परमया युतः। तापयन् पाण्डुपुत्रांस्त्वं रश्मिवानिव तेजसा॥
en: O king, go there with all your prosperity and thus scorch the Pandavas with a sight of your glory, as the sun scorches every thing with his hot rays.

sn: स्थितो राज्ये च्युतान् राज्याच्छ्यिा हीनाञ्छ्यिा वृतः। असमृद्धान् समृद्धार्थः पश्य पाण्डुसुतान् नृप॥
en: You a (great) sovereign and they deprived of their sovereignty, you in prosperity and they deprived of it, you are in affluence and they are in poverty. O king, go and (now) see the Pandavas.

sn: महाभिजनसम्पन्नं भद्रे महति संस्थितम्। पाण्डवास्त्वाभिवीक्षन्तां ययातिमिव नाहुषम्॥
en: Let the Pandavas see you like Yayati, the son of Nahusha accompanied by a large number of followers and in the enjoyment of great bliss.

sn: यां श्रियं सुहृदश्चैव दुर्हदश्च विशाम्पते। पश्यन्ति पुरुषे दीप्तां सा समर्था भवत्युत॥
en: O king, that blazing prosperity which is seen by one's both friend and foe is considered to be the real prosperity.

sn: समस्थो विषमस्थान् हि दुर्हदो योऽभिवीक्षते। जगतीस्थानिवाद्रिस्थः किमतः परमं सुखम्॥
en: What happiness could be more complete than what one enjoys by being himself in great prosperity and his enemy being in adversity just like the man on the top of a hill looking down upon another who crawls on the earth.

sn: न पुत्रधनलाभेन न राज्येनापि विन्दति। प्रीतिं नृपतिशार्दूल याममित्राघदर्शनात्॥
en: O foremost of kings, the happiness that one drives from seeing his enemies in grief is greater than what one drives on getting a son or wealth or kingdom.

sn: किं नु तस्य सुखं न स्यादाश्रमे यो धनंजयम्। अभिवीक्षेत सिद्धार्थो वल्कलाजिनवाससम्॥
en: What happiness will not be his who himself being in affluence sees Dhananjaya (Arjuna) in barks and skins.

sn: सुवाससो हि ते भार्या वल्कलाजिनसंवृताम्। पश्यन्तु दुःखितां कृष्णां सा च निर्विद्यतां पुनः॥
en: Let your wife clad in costly robes look at the afflicted Krishna (Draupadi) now in barks and skins and thus increase her misery.

sn: विनिन्दतां तथाऽऽत्मानं जीवितं च धनच्युतम्। न तथा हि सभामध्ये तस्या भवितुमर्हति। वैमनस्यं यथा दृष्ट्वा तव भार्याः स्वलंकृताः॥
en: Let the daughter of Drupada reproach herself and her life deprived as she is of wealth, for the sorrow that she will feel on seeing your wife adorned with ornaments will be far greater than what she had felt in the Sava.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्त्वा तु राजानं कर्णः शकुनिना सह। तूष्णीम्बभूवतुरुभौ वाक्यान्ते जनमेजय॥
en: Vaishampayana said: O Janamejaya, having thus spoken to the king, Shakuni and Karna when their speech was over both became silent.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच कर्णस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा राजा दुर्योधनस्ततः। हृष्टो भूत्वा पुनर्दीन इदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having heard the words of Karna, the king Duryodhana became greatly delighted. But soon again the became melancholy and he then thus spoke.

sn: ब्रवीषि यदिदं कर्ण सर्वं मनसि मे स्थितम्। न त्वभ्यनुज्ञा लप्स्यामि गमने यत्र पाण्डवाः॥
en: Duryodhana said : O Karna, what you tell me is always in my mind. But I shall not get permission to go where the Pandavas are.

sn: परिदेवति तान् वीरान् धृतराष्ट्रो महीपतिः। मन्यतेऽभ्यधिकांश्चापि तपोयोगेन पाण्डवान्॥
en: King Dhritarashtra is always grieving for those heroes. The king considers them (now) more powerful (than before) by their asceticism.

sn: अथवाप्यनुबुध्येत नृपोऽस्माकं चिकीर्षितम्। एवमप्यायतिं रक्षन् नाभ्यनुज्ञातुमर्हति॥ न हि द्वैतवने किंचिद् विद्यतेऽन्यत् प्रयोजनम्। उत्सादनमृते तेषां वनस्थानां महाद्युते॥
en: O greatly effulgent one, if the king understands our motives, he will never grant us permission, for we can have no other business in Dvaitavana than to exterminate the Pandavas in their exile.

sn: जानासि हि यथा क्षत्ता द्यूतकाल उपस्थिते। अब्रवीद् यच्च मां त्वां च सौबलं वचनं तदा॥
en: You know what Khatva (Vidura) said to me, to yourself and to the son of Subala (Shakuni) at the time of the play.

sn: तानि सर्वाणि वाक्यानि यच्चान्यत् परिदेवितम्। विचिन्त्य नाधिगच्छामि गमनायेतराय वा॥
en: Reflecting on those words and also on (their) lamentations, I cannot make up my mind as to whether I should or should not go.

sn: ममापि हि महान् हर्षो यदहं भीमफाल्गुनौ। क्लिष्टावरण्ये पश्येयं कृष्णया सहिताविति।॥
en: I shall certainly feel great delight if I see Bhima and Falguna (Arjuna) passing their days with Krishna (Draupadi) in great misery in the forest.

sn: न तथा ह्याप्नुयां प्रीतिमवाप्य वसुधामिमाम्। दृष्ट्वा यथा पाण्डुसुतान् वल्कलाजिनवाससः॥
en: The joy that I may feel by obtaining the entire sovereignty over the earth is nothing in comparison to what I shall obtain on seeing the Pandavas clad in barks and skins.

sn: किं नु स्यादधिकं तस्माद् यदहं दुपदात्मजाम्। द्रौपदी कर्ण पश्येयं काषायवसनां वने।॥
en: O Karna, what joy could be greater than what I shall drive on seeing Draupadi, the daughter of Draupada, clad in rags in the forest?

sn: यदि मां धर्मराजश्च भीमसेनश्च पाण्डवः। युक्तं परमया लक्ष्या पश्येतां जीवितं भवेत्॥
en: If king Dharmaraja (Yudhishthira), Bhima and the son of Pandu (Arjuna) see me graced with great prosperity, then only shall I attain to the great end of my life.

sn: उपायं न तु पश्यामि येन गच्छेम तद् वनम्। यथा चाभ्यनुजानीयाद् गच्छन्तं मां महीपतिः॥
en: But I do not see the means through which I can go to that forest and by which I may get the permission of the king Dhritarashtra.

sn: स सौबलेन सहितस्तथा दुःशासनेन च। उपायं पश्य निपुणं येन गच्छेम तद् वनम्॥
en: Therefore find out some skillful plan with the help of Subala's son (Shakuni) and Duhshasana, by which we may go to the forest (where the Pandavas) are.

sn: अहमष्यद्य निश्चित्य गमनायेतराय च। कल्यमेव गमिष्यामि समीपं पार्थिवस्य ह॥
en: I shall also today make up my mind whether I should go or not and then I shall see the king (my father) tomorrow.

sn: मयि तत्रोपविष्टे तु भीष्मे च कुरुसत्तमे। उपायो यो भवेद् दृष्टस्तं ब्रूयाः सहसौबलः॥
en: When I shall remain seated (tomorrow) with that foremost of the Kurus, you will then with Subala's son propose the pretext you may have fixed upon.

sn: वचो भीष्मस्य राज्ञश्च निशम्य गमनं प्रति। व्यवसायं करिष्येऽहमनुनीय पितामहम्॥
en: Hearing then the words of Bhishma and of the king (my father) on the subject of this journey, I shall settle everything, beseeching (the permission of) our grand father (Bhishma).

sn: तथेत्युक्त्वा तु ते सर्वे जग्मुरावसथान् प्रति। व्युषितायां रजन्यां तु कर्णो राजानमभ्ययात्॥
en: Vaishampayana said: Having said “So be it.” They then all went away to their respective houses. As soon as the night passed, Karna came to the king.

sn: ततो दुर्योधनं कर्णः प्रहसन्निदमब्रवीत्। उपायः परिदृष्टोऽयं तं निबोध जनेश्वर।॥
en: Thereupon Karna thus smilingly spoke to Duryodhana, “O ruler of men, a plan has been fixed upon by me. Hear it.

sn: घोषा द्वैतवने सर्वे त्वत्प्रतीक्षा नराधिप। घोषयात्रापदेशेन गमिष्यामो न संशयः॥
en: O ruler, of men, our herds of cattle are now in Dvaitavana all waiting for you. There is no doubt we can go on the pretext of seeing our cattle.

sn: उचितं हि सदा गन्तुं घोषयात्रां विशाम्पते। एवं च त्वां पिता राजन् समनुज्ञातुमर्हति॥
en: O king, O ruler of earth, it is always proper to go and see the cattle; if you say this to your father, you will get his permission."

sn: तथा कथयमानौ तौ घोषयात्राविनिश्चयम्। गान्धारराजः शकुनिः प्रत्युवाच हसन्निव॥
en: When they were thus talking about the cattle, the Gandhara king Shakuni thus smilingly spoke,

sn: उपायोऽयं मया दृष्टो गमनाय निरामयः। अनुज्ञास्यति नो राजा बोधयिष्यति चाप्युत॥ घोषा द्वैतवने सर्वे त्वत्प्रतीक्षा नराधिप। घोषयात्रापदेशेन गमिष्यामो न संशयः॥
en: “O ruler of men, this plan which has no difficulty to be carried out was what I also saw for the purpose of going (to Dvaitavana). The king will certainly grant us permission or even he may send us there of his own accord. Our herds of cattle are now all waiting in the forest of Dvaitavana. We may certainly go there under the pretext of seeing our cattle."

sn: ततः प्रहसिताः सर्वे तेऽन्योन्यस्य तलान् ददुः। तदेव च विनिश्चित्य ददृशुः कुरुसत्तमम्॥
en: They then all three laughed together and gave their hands to one another. Having arrived at this conclusion, they then went to see the chief of the Kurus (Dhritarashtra).

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच धृतराष्ट्र ततः सर्वे ददृशुर्जनमेजय। पृष्ट्वा सुखमथो राज्ञः पृष्टा राज्ञा च भारत॥
en: Vaishampayana said : O Janamejaya, O descendant of Bharata, then they all saw Dhritarashtra and asked his welfare; they were also asked their welfare in reiurn,

sn: ततस्तैर्विहितः पूर्वं समङ्गो नाम बल्लवः। समीपस्थास्तदा गावो धृतराष्ट्र न्यवेदयत्॥
en: Then a cowherd named Samanga who had been instructed before-hand come to the king Dhritarashtra and spoke about the cattle.

sn: अनन्तरं च राधेयः शकुनिश्च विशाम्पते। आहतुः पार्थिवश्रेष्ठं धृतराष्ट्र जनाधिपम्॥
en: O king, the son of Radha (Karna) and Shakuni thus spoke to that foremost of kings, the ruler of earth, Dhritarashtra,

sn: रमणीयेषु देशेषु घोषाः सम्प्रति कौरव। स्मारणे समयः प्राप्तो वत्पानामपि चाङ्कनम्॥
en: "O descendant of Kuru, our cattle are now stationed in a charming place. The time for marking the calves has also come.

sn: मृगया चोचिता राजन्नस्मिन् काले सुतस्य ते। दुर्योधनस्य गमनं समनुज्ञातुमर्हसि॥
en: O king, this is also an excellent season for your son Duryodhana to go to a hunting expedition. Therefore you should grant him permission to go there.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच मृगया शोभना तात गवां हि समवेक्षणम्। विश्रम्भस्तु न गन्तव्यो वल्लवानामिति स्मरे॥
en: Dhritarashtra said: O child, hunting and seeing the cattle are both very proper acts. I think the herdsman should not be (completely) trusted.

sn: ते तु तत्र नरव्याघ्राः समीप इति नः श्रुतम्। अतो नाभ्यनुजानामि गमनं तत्र वः स्वयम्॥
en: But I have heard that those foremost of men (the Pandavas) are living some where near that place; therefore I think you should not yourselves go there.

sn: छद्मना निर्जितास्ते तु कर्शिताश्च महावने। तपोनित्याश्च राधेय समर्थाश्च महारथाः॥
en: Defeated by deceitful means, they are now living in the deep forest in great misery. O son of Radha, those greatly powerful car-warriors are now engaged in asceticism.

sn: धर्मराजो न संक्रुद्ध्येद् भीमसेनस्त्वमर्षणः। यज्ञसेनस्य दुहिता तेज एव तु केवलम्॥
en: Dharmaraja (Yudhishthira) will never be angry, but Bhimasena is naturally wrathful; the daughter of Yajnasena (Draupadi) also is effulgence herself.

sn: यूयं चाप्यपराध्येयुर्दर्पमोहसमन्विताः। ततो विनिर्दहेयुस्ते तपसा हि समन्विताः॥
en: Full of pride and folly as you are you are certain to give her offence. Endued with ascetic merit as she is (now), she will certainly consume you.

sn: अथवा सायुधा वीरा मन्युनाभिपरिप्लुताः। सहिता बद्धनिस्त्रिंशा दहेयुः शस्त्रतेजसा॥ वै
en: Or perhaps, those heroes, armed with swords and other weapons and filled with wrath, may consume you with the fire of their weapons.

sn: अथ यूयं बहुत्वात् तानभियात कथंचन। अनार्यं परमं तत् स्यादशक्यं तच्च मतम्॥
en: Or if from the force of numbers you seek to injure them in any way, even that will be a highly improper act, though I know you will never succeed.

sn: उषितो हि महाबाहुरिन्द्रलोके धनंजयः। दिव्यान्यस्त्राण्यवाप्याथ ततः प्रत्यागतो वनम्॥
en: The mighty armed Dhananjaya (Arjuna) had lived in the abode of Indra. Having obtained the celestials weapons, he has returned to the forest.

sn: अकृतास्त्रेण पृथिवी जिता बीभत्सुना पुरा। किं पुनः स कृतास्त्रोऽद्य न हन्याद् वो महारथः॥
en: While unaccomplished in arms, Bibhatsu (Arjuna) conquered the whole earth. He is now a great car-warrior and highly accomplished in arms, why will he not be able (now) to kill you all?

sn: अथवा मद्वचः श्रुत्वा तत्र यत्ता भविष्यथा उद्विग्नवासो विश्रम्भाद् दुःखं तत्र भविष्यति॥
en: Or if you in obedience to my words on going there, behave carefully you will then never be able to live happily, as you will always be in a state of trustlessness.

sn: अथवा सैनिकाः केचिदपकुर्युर्युधिष्ठिरम्। तदबुद्धिकृतं कर्म दोषमुत्पादयेच्च वः॥ तस्माद् गच्छन्तु पुरुषाः स्मारणायाप्तकारिणः। न स्वयं तत्र गमनं रोचये तव भारत॥
en: Or some soldiers of yours may do some injury to Yudhishthira and that unpremeditated act may be ascribed to you. O descendant of Bharata, therefore let some faithful men go there to count the cattle and mark the calves. I do not think it is proper for your to go in person.

sn: शकुनिरुवाच धर्मज्ञः पाण्डवो ज्येष्ठः प्रतिज्ञातं च संसदि। तेन द्वादश वर्षाणि वस्तव्यानीति भारत।॥
en: Shakuni said: O descendant of Bharata, the eldest Pandava is virtuous; he has taken the pledge in the assembly that he will live twelve years in the forest.

sn: अनुवृत्ताश्च ते सर्वे पाण्डवा धर्मचारिणः। युधिष्ठिरस्तु कौन्तेयो न नः कोपं करिष्यति॥
en: The other Pandavas are virtuous and obedient to him. The son of Kunti, Yudhishthira will never be angry with us.

sn: मृगयां चैव नो गन्तुमिच्छा संवर्तते भृशम्। स्मारणं तु चिकीर्षामो न तु पाण्डवदर्शनम्॥
en: We desire very much to go to a hunting expedition; we shall also take that opportunity to count the cattle. We have no wish to see the Pandavas.

sn: न चानार्यसमाचारः कश्चित् तत्र भविष्यति। न च तत्र गमिष्यामो यत्र तेषां प्रतिश्रयः॥
en: We shall not go to that place where the Pandavas are living. Therefore no misconduct on our part can possibly arise.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्तः शकुनिना धृतराष्ट्रो जनेश्वरः। दुर्योधनं महामात्यमनुजज्ञे न कामतः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having been thus addressed by Shakuni, the ruler of earth, Dhritarashtra, unwillingly gave permission to Duryodhana and his counsellors togo.

sn: अनुज्ञातस्तु गान्धारिः कर्णेन सहितस्तदा। निर्ययौ भरतश्रेष्ठो बलेन महता वृतः॥
en: Having received permission, the son of Gandhari, that foremost of the Bharata race (Duryodhana) with Karna and with a large host started.

sn: दुःशासनेन च तथा सौबलेन च धीमता। संवृतो भ्रातृभिश्चान्यैः स्त्रीभिश्चापि सहस्रशः॥
en: He has accompanied by Dushasana the intclligent son of Subala (Shakuni) and by many others of his brothers and also thousands of women.

sn: तं निर्यान्तं महाबाहुं द्रष्टुं द्वैतवनं सरः। पौराश्चानुययुः सर्वे सहदारा वनं च तत्॥
en: When he started to see that lake in the Dvaitavana, the citizens also with their wives proceeded towards that forest.

sn: अष्टौ रथसहस्राणि त्रीणि नागायुतानि च। पत्तयो बहुसाहस्रा हयाश्च नवतिः शताः॥
en: Eight thousand cars, thirty thousand elephants, nine thousand horses and many thousands of foot soldiers,

sn: शकटापणवेशाश्च वणिजो वन्दिनस्तथा। नराश्च मृगयाशीलाः शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः॥
en: Carriages, shops, pavilions, traders, bards and men, trained in hunting, by hundred and thousands, followed the king.

sn: ततः प्रयाणे नृपतेः सुमहानभवत् स्वनः। प्रावृषीव महावायोरुद्धतस्य विशाम्पते॥
en: O monarch, as the king started, followed by many thousands of men, the uproar caused by the march resembled the deep roar of winds in the rains.

sn: गव्यूतिमात्रे न्यवसद् राजा दुर्योधनस्तदा। प्रयातो वाहनैः सर्वैस्ततो द्वैतवनं सरः॥
en: Arriving at the lake of Dvaitavana with his followers and conveyances, king Duryodhana encamped at the distance of four miles from the lake.

description: The colloquy between Duryodhana's soldiers and the Gandharvas
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच अथ दुर्योधनो राजा तत्र वने वसन्। जगाम घोषानभितस्तत्र चक्रे निवेशनम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Then the king Duryodhana, living in various parts of that forest, at last came to the cattle stations and encamped there.

description: The colloquy between Duryodhana's soldiers and the Gandharvas
sn: रमणीये समाज्ञाते सोदके समहीरहे। देशे सर्वगुणोपेते चक्रुरावसथान् पराः॥
en: Selecting a well known charming place which had a plentiful supply of water and which abounded in trees and possessed every convenience, his attendants built a house for him.

description: The colloquy between Duryodhana's soldiers and the Gandharvas
sn: तथैव तत्समीपस्थान् पृथगावसथान् बहून्। कर्णस्य शकुनेश्चैव भ्रातृणां चैव सर्वशः॥
en: Near the royal residence, they also erected separate houses for Karna, Shakuni and other brothers of the king.

description: The colloquy between Duryodhana's soldiers and the Gandharvas
sn: ददर्श स तदा गावः शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः। अङ्कुर्लक्षैश्च ताः सर्वा लक्षयामास पार्थिवः॥
en: The king saw his cattle by hundreds and thousands. Examining their limbs and marks, he supervised their counting.

description: The colloquy between Duryodhana's soldiers and the Gandharvas
sn: अङ्कयामास वत्सांश्च जज्ञे चोपसृतांस्त्वपि। बालवत्साश्च या गावः कालयामास ता अपि॥
en: He caused the calves to be marked and took notes of those that required to be tamed. He also counted all those cows of which calves had not yet been yeaned.

description: The colloquy between Duryodhana's soldiers and the Gandharvas
sn: अथ स स्मारणं कृत्वा लक्षयित्वा त्रिहायनान्। वृतो गोपालकैः प्रीतो व्यहरत् कुरुनन्दनः॥
en: Completing the task of counting and marking every calf which was three years old, the Kuru prince, surrounded by the cow-herds, began cheerfully to sport and wander about (in that forest).

description: The colloquy between Duryodhana's soldiers and the Gandharvas
sn: स च पौरजनः सर्वः सैनिकाच सहस्रशः। यथोपजोषं चिक्रीडुर्वने तस्मिन् यथामराः॥
en: The citizens and the soldiers by thousands sported in that forest as best pleased them like the celestials.

description: The colloquy between Duryodhana's soldiers and the Gandharvas
sn: ततो गोपाः प्रगातारः कुशला नृत्यवादने। धार्तराष्ट्रमुपातिष्ठन् कन्याश्चैव स्वलंकृताः॥
en: The herdsman, well-skilled in singing and dancing and playing on musical instruments and maidens adorned with ornaments ministered to the pleasures of Dhritarashtra's son.

description: The colloquy between Duryodhana's soldiers and the Gandharvas
sn: स स्त्रीगणावृतो राजा प्रहृष्टः प्रददौ वसु। तेभ्यो यथार्हमन्नानि पानानि विविधानि च॥
en: The king surrounded by the ladies of the royal household began cheerfully to distribute according to the merit of each, wealth, food and drinks of various kinds among those that sought to please him.

description: The colloquy between Duryodhana's soldiers and the Gandharvas
sn: ततस्ते सहिताः सर्वे तरखून् महिषान् मृगान्। गवयर्डवराहांश्च समन्तात् पर्यकालयन्॥ स ताञ्छरैर्विनिर्भिद्य गजांश्च सुबहून् वने। रमणीयेषु देशेषु ग्राहयामास वै मृगान्॥
en: Attended by all his followers, the king killed many bison's, buffaloes, deer gavayas, bear and boars. Pierced by his arrows animals by thousands died in that deep forest. He caused the deer to be caught in the most delightful parts of the forest.

description: The colloquy between Duryodhana's soldiers and the Gandharvas
sn: गोरसानुपयुञ्जान उपभोगांश्च भारत। पश्यन् स रणमीयानि वनान्युपवनानि च।॥ मत्तभ्रमरजुष्टानि बर्हिणाभिरुतानि च। अगच्छदानुपूर्येण पुण्यं द्वैतवनं सरः॥
en: Drinking milk and enjoying various other delicious articles, O descendant of Bharata and also seeing as he proceeded many delightful forests and woods swarming with bees intoxicated with the honey of flowers and resounding with the sweet notes of peacock, the king at last reached the sacred lake of Dvaitavana.

description: The colloquy between Duryodhana's soldiers and the Gandharvas
sn: मत्तभ्रमरसंजुष्टं नीलकण्ठरवाकुलम्। सप्तच्छदसमाकीर्णं पुन्नागबकुलैर्युतम्॥
en: The place was swarmed with bees intoxicated with the honey of the flowers; it echoed with the sweet notes of blue throated jay (bird); it was shaded by Saptachadas and Punnyagas and Bakulas.

description: The colloquy between Duryodhana's soldiers and the Gandharvas
sn: ऋद्ध्या परमया युक्तो महेन्द्र इव वलाभृत्। यदृच्छया च तत्रस्थो धर्मपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः॥ ईजे राजर्षियज्ञेन साद्यस्केन विशाम्पते। दिव्येन विधिना चैव वन्येन कुरुसत्तम॥ कृत्वा निवेशमभितः सरसस्तस्य कौरव। द्रौपद्या सहिता धीमान् धर्मपल्या नराधिपः॥
en: The king (Duryodhana) graced with great prosperity went there like the wielder of thunder, the lord of the celestials (Indra). O foremost of the Kuru race, the greatly intelligent Dharmaraja Yudhishthira was then, O king, living near that lake and was performing with his wife Draupadi the sacrifice called Rajarshi according to the ordinance sanctioned for the celestials and persons living in the forest.

description: The colloquy between Duryodhana's soldiers and the Gandharvas
sn: ततो दुर्योधनः प्रेष्यानादिदेश सहस्रशः। आक्रीडावसथा: क्षिप्नं क्रियन्तामिति भारत॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, Duryodhana, having arrived at that place, commanded thousands of his men to build there pleasure houses with the least delay.

description: The colloquy between Duryodhana's soldiers and the Gandharvas
sn: ते तथेत्येव कौरव्यमुक्त्वा वचनकारिणः। चिकीर्षन्तस्तदाऽऽक्रीडाञ्जग्मुद्वैतवनं सरः॥
en: Saying "So be it", they at the command of the king went towards the banks of the lake to build the pleasure houses.

description: The colloquy between Duryodhana's soldiers and the Gandharvas
sn: प्रविशन्तं वनद्वारि गन्धर्वाः समवारयन्। सेनाच्यं धार्तराष्ट्रस्य प्राप्तं द्वैतवनं सरः॥
en: As the best of the soldiers of Dhritarashtra's son, having reached the lake, were about to enter the woods, many Gandharvas came forward and commanded them not to enter.

description: The colloquy between Duryodhana's soldiers and the Gandharvas
sn: तत्र गन्धर्वराजो वै पूर्वमेव विशाम्पते। कुबेरभवनाद् राजन्नाजगाम गणावृतः॥
en: O monarch, the king of the Gandharvas with his followers had already arrived there from the abode of Kubera.

description: The colloquy between Duryodhana's soldiers and the Gandharvas
sn: गणैरप्सरसां चैव त्रिदशानां तथाऽऽत्मजैः। विहारशीलः क्रीडार्थं तेन तत् संवृतं सरः॥
en: He had come surrounded by various Apsaras and also by many sons of the celestials. Having come to that lake to sport, he had closed the place to all comers.

description: The colloquy between Duryodhana's soldiers and the Gandharvas
sn: तेन तत् संवृतं दृष्ट्वा ते राजपरिचारकाः। प्रतिजग्मुस्ततो राजन् यत्र दुर्योधनो नृपः॥
en: O king, finding the lake closed by the Gandharva king, the royal attendants (of Duryodhana) went back to the place where their king was.

description: The colloquy between Duryodhana's soldiers and the Gandharvas
sn: स तु तेषां वचः श्रुत्वा सैनिकान् युद्धदुर्मदान्। प्रेषयामास कौरव्य उत्सारयत तानिति॥
en: O descendant of Kuru, hearing their words, he (Duryodhana) sent a number of his soldiers, to all difficult to be vanquished in battle, commanding them drive away the Gandharvas.

description: The colloquy between Duryodhana's soldiers and the Gandharvas
sn: तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा राज्ञः सेनाचयायिनः। सरो द्वैतवनं गत्वा गन्धर्वानिदमब्रुवन्॥
en: Those warriors, who forned the vanguard of the Kuru army, having heard those words of the king, went back to the lake of the Dvaitavana and thus spoke to the Gandharvas.

description: The colloquy between Duryodhana's soldiers and the Gandharvas
sn: राजा दुर्योधनो नाम धृतराष्ट्रसुतो बली। विजिहीर्षुरिहायाति तदर्थमपसर्पत॥
en: “The powerful king named Duryodhana, the son of Dhritarashtra, has come here for sport. Therefore leave this place at once.”

description: The colloquy between Duryodhana's soldiers and the Gandharvas
sn: एवमुक्तास्तु गन्धर्वाः प्रहसन्तो विशाम्पते। प्रत्यब्रुवंस्तान् पुरुषानिदं हि परुषं वचः॥
en: Having been thus addressed. O king, the Gandharvas laughed aloud. They thus replied to them in harsh words,

description: The colloquy between Duryodhana's soldiers and the Gandharvas
sn: न चेतयति वो राजा मन्दबुद्धिः सुयोधनः। योऽस्मानाज्ञापयत्येवं वैश्यानिव दिवौकसः॥
en: “Your wicked-minded Duryodhana has but little sense. Or else how could he thus command us who are dwellers of heaven as if we are his servants.

description: The colloquy between Duryodhana's soldiers and the Gandharvas
sn: यूयं मुमूर्षवश्चापि मन्दप्रज्ञा न संशयः। ये तस्य वचनादेवमस्मान् ब्रूत विचेतसः॥
en: You are certainly fools to rush thus to the point of death. You are senseless idiots to bring such massage to us.

description: The colloquy between Duryodhana's soldiers and the Gandharvas
sn: गच्छध्वं त्वरिताः सर्वे यत्र राजा स कौरवः। न चेदद्यैव गच्छध्वं धर्मराजनिवेशनम्॥
en: Go back soon where that Kuru king is or else you will today go to the abode of Dharmaraja (Yama)."

description: The colloquy between Duryodhana's soldiers and the Gandharvas
sn: एवमुक्तास्तु गन्धर्वै राज्ञः सेनाचयायिनः। सम्प्राद्रवन् यतो राजा धृतराष्ट्रसुतोऽभवत्॥
en: Having been thus addressed by the Gandharvas, those vanguards (of the Kuru army) ran back to the place where the king (Duryodhana), the son of Dhritarashtra was.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततस्ते सहिताः सर्वे दुर्योधनमुपागमन्। अब्रुवंश्च महाराज यदूचुः कौरवं प्रति॥शा
en: Vaishampayana said : O great king, they then all came to Duryodhana and spoke to that Kuru prince all that they (the Gandharvas) had spoken to them.

sn: गन्धर्वैर्वारिते सैन्ये धार्तराष्ट्रः प्रतापवान्। अमर्षपूर्णः सैन्यानि प्रत्यभाषत भारत॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, finding that his soldiers had been opposed by the Gandharvas, the mighty son of Dhritarashtra was filled with great anger and thus spoke to the soldiers,

sn: शासतैनानधर्मज्ञान् मम विप्रियकारिणः। यदि प्रक्रीडते सर्वैर्देवैः सह शतक्रतुः॥
en: "Chastise these wicked witches who want to do what is not agreeable to me, even if he be Shatakratu (Indra) who is sporting here with all the celestials."

sn: दुर्योधनव चः श्रुत्वा धार्तराष्ट्रा महाबलाः। सर्व एवाभिसंनद्धा योधाश्चापि सहस्रशः॥ ततः प्रमथ्य सर्वांस्तांस्तद् वनं विविशुर्बलात्। सिंहनादेन महता पूरयन्तो दिशो दश॥
en: Having heard the words of Duryodhana, the greatly powerful sons of Dhritarashtra, thousands of warriors armed themselves for battle. Filling ten directions with loud leonine roars and crushing all they entered by force that forest.

sn: ततोऽपरैरवार्यन्त गन्धर्वैः कुरुसैनिकाः। ते वार्यमाणा गन्धर्वैः साम्नैव वसुधाधिप॥ ताननादृत्य गन्धर्वांस्तद् वनं विविशुर्महत्। यदा वाचा न तिष्ठन्ति धार्तराष्ट्राः सराजकाः॥ ततस्ते खेचराः सर्वे चित्रसेने न्यवेदयन्।
en: O ruler of earth, the Gandharvas, again forbade the Kuru soldiers to advance. Though gently forbidden by the Gandharvas, disregarding all those Gandharvas, they entered that great forest. When the son of Dhritarashtra did not stop his soldiers, then those rangers of the sky went and spoke to Chitrasena.

sn: गन्धर्वराजस्तान् सर्वानब्रवीत् कौरवान् प्रति॥ अनार्याञ्छासतेत्येतांश्चित्रसेनोऽत्यमर्षणः।
en: The Gandharva king, when he heard it, was filled with anger and he thus commanded his followers "Punish and chastise these wicked wretches."

sn: अनुज्ञाताश्च गन्धर्वाश्चित्रसेनेन भारत॥ प्रगृहीतायुधाः सर्वे धार्तराष्ट्रानभिद्रवन्।
en: O descendant of Bharata, thus commanded by Chitrasena, the Gandharvas, rushed towards ihe Dhritarashtra people with weapons in hand.

sn: तान् दृष्ट्वा पततः शीघ्रान् गन्धर्वानुद्यतायुधान्॥ प्राद्रवंस्ते दिशः सर्वे धार्तराष्ट्रस्य पश्यतः।
en: Seeing the Gandharvas rushing towards them with great force and with uplifted weapons, the Dhritarashtra warriors fled in all directions.

sn: तान् दृष्ट्वा द्रवतः सर्वान् धार्तराष्ट्रान् पराङ्मुखान्।११।। राधेयस्तु तदा वीरो नासीत् तत्र पराङ्मुखः।
en: Seeing that all the Dhritarashtra people were flying before the enemy. The heroic son of Radha (Karna) alone did not fiy.

sn: आपतन्ती तु सम्प्रेक्ष्य गन्धर्वाणां महाचमूम्॥ महता शरवर्षेण राधेयः प्रत्यवारयत्।
en: Seeing that the the great army army of the Gandharvas was rushing towards him, the son of Radha stopped them with a very large shower of arrows.

sn: क्षुरप्रैर्विशिखैभल्लैर्वत्सदन्तैस्तथाऽऽयसैः॥ गन्धर्वाञ्छतशोऽभ्य ल्लघुत्वात् सूतनन्दनः।
en: That son of Suta by his great lightness of hands struck hundreds of Gandharvas with Khurupas and arrows and Bhallas and various other weapons made of bones and steel.

sn: पातयन्नुत्तमाङ्गानि गन्धर्वाणां महारथः॥ क्षणेन व्यधमत् सर्वां चित्रसेनस्य वाहिनीम्।
en: That great car-warrior cut off within a moment the heads of many Gandharvas and thus they made the army of Chitrasena yell in pain.

sn: ते वध्यमाना गन्धर्वाः सूतपुत्रेण धीमता॥ भूय एवाभ्यवर्तन्त शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः। गन्धर्वभूता पृथिवी क्षणेन समपद्यत॥ आपतद्भिर्महावेगैश्चित्रसेनस्य सैनिकैः।
en: Although the Gandharvas were killed by the greatly intelligent son of Suta (Karna). They returned to the charge by hundreds and thousands; and in consequence of the hoards of Gandharvas rushing to battle, earth became covered over by the Gandharva army.

sn: अथ दुर्योधनो राजा शकुनिश्चापि सौबलः॥ दुःशासनो विकर्णश्च ये चान्ये धृतराष्ट्रजाः। न्यहनस्तत् तदा सैन्यं स्थैर्गरुडनिःस्वनैः॥
en: Then king Duryodhana and also the son of Subala (Shakuni), Duhshasana and Vikarna and the sons of Dhritarashtra, riding on cars, the clatter of the wheels of which resembled the roars of Garuda, followed the lead of Karna and returned to the charge and began to kill the (Gandharva) army.

sn: भूयश्च योधयामासुः कृत्वा कर्णमथाचतः। महता रथसङ्ग्रेन रथचारेण चाप्युत॥ वैकर्तनं परीप्सन्तो गन्धर्वान् समवाकिरन्।
en: With the desire of supporting Karna, the (Kuru) princes attacked the Gandharva army. With a very large number of cars and horses, the whole of the Gandharva army began to fight.

sn: ततः संन्यपतन् सर्वे गन्धर्वाः कौरवैः सह॥ तदा सुतुमुलं युद्धमभवल्लोमहर्षणम्। ततस्ते मृदवोऽभूवन् गन्धर्वाः शरपीडिताः॥ उच्चुक्रुशुश्च कौरव्या गन्धर्वान् प्रेक्ष्य पीडितान्।
