en: The battle that took place was fearful and hair-stirring. Then the Gandharvas, afflicted with thc arrows of the Kurus army, seemed to be exhausted. Having seen the Gandharvas afflicted, the Kurus sent up a loud roar.

sn: गन्धर्वास्त्रासितान् दृष्ट्वा चित्रसेनो ह्यमर्षणः॥ उत्पपातासनात् क्रुद्धो वधे तेषां समाहितः।
en: Seeing the Gandharva army afflicted with fear, Chitrasena jumped up in great anger from his seat and resolved to exterminate the Kuru army.

sn: ततो मायास्त्रमास्थाय युयुधे चित्रमार्गवित्। तयामुह्यन्त कौरव्याचित्रसेनस्य मायया।॥
en: That hero, learned in the various modes of warfare, fought with his weapons of illusion. The Kuru heroes were all deprived of their senses by the illusion of Chitrasena.

sn: एकैको हि तदा योधो धार्तराष्ट्रस्य भारत। पर्यवर्तत गन्धर्वैर्दशभिर्दशभिः सह।॥
en: Then, O descendant of Bharata, it appeared that every Kuru warrior was attacked and surrounded by the Gandharvas.

sn: ततः सम्पीड्यमानास्ते बलेन महता तदा। प्राद्रवन्त रणे भीता ये च राजञ्जिगीषवः॥
en: Being thus attacked with great force the Kuru army was afflicted and it was with panic, O king, those that desired to live fled from the field (of battle).

sn: भज्यमानेष्वनीकेषु धार्तराष्ट्रेषु सर्वशः। कर्णो वैकर्तनो राजंस्तस्थौ गिरिरिवाचलः॥
en: O king, when the whole of the Kuru army broke and fled, the son of Surya (Karna) alone stood there as immoveable as a hill.

sn: दुर्योधनश्च कर्णश्च शकुनिश्चापि सौबलः। गन्धर्वान् योधयामासुः समरे भृशविक्षताः॥
en: Duryodhana, Karna and Shakuni, the son of Subala, all fought with the Gandharvas though they were all severely wounded.

sn: सर्व एव तु गन्धर्वाः शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः। जिघांसमानाः सहिताः कर्णमभ्यद्रवन् रणे॥
en: All the Gandharvas then with the desire of killing Karna rushed upon him in battle in hundreds and thousands.

sn: असिभिः पट्टिशैः शूलैर्गदाभिश्च महाबलाः। सूतपुत्रं जिघांसन्तः समन्तात् पर्यवाकिरन्।॥
en: Those greatly powerful heroes, with the desire of killing that Suta's son, surrounded him on all sides with swords, battle axes and spears.

sn: अन्येऽस्य युगमच्छिन्दन् ध्वजमन्ये न्यपातयन्। ईषामन्ये हयानन्ये सूतमन्ये न्यपातयन्॥
en: Some cut down the yoke of his car, some its flag-staff, some its shafts, some its horses and some its charioteer.

sn: अन्ये छत्रं वरूथं च बन्धुरं च तथापरे। गन्धर्वा बहुसाहस्रास्तिलशो व्यधमन् रथम्॥ ततो रथादवप्लुत्य सूतपुत्रोऽसिचर्मभृत्। विकर्णरथमास्थाय मोक्षायाश्वानचोदयत्॥
en: Some cut down his umbrella, some the wooden fender round his car and some its joints. It was thus many thousands of Gandharvas attacked his car and broke it into many pieces. When his car was thus attacked, Karna leaped from it with sword and shield in his hands. He then jumped upon the car of Vikarna and whipped the horses (to leave the field and) save himself.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच गन्धर्वैस्तु महाराज भग्ने कर्णे महारथे। सम्प्राद्रवच्चमूः सर्वा धार्तराष्ट्रस्य पश्यतः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : O great king, when the great car-warrior Karna was routed by the Gandharvas, the great army of Dhritarashtra's son fled away in his very sight.

sn: तान् दृष्ट्वा द्रवतः सर्वान् धार्तराष्ट्रान् पराङ्मुखान्। दुर्योधनो महाराजो नासीत् तत्र पराङ्मुखः॥
en: Seeing all the Kuru soldiers flying from the enemy, the great king Duryodhana refused to run away.

sn: तामापतन्ती सम्प्रेक्ष्य गन्धर्वाणां महाचमूम्। महता शरवर्षेण सोऽभ्यवर्षदरिंदमः॥
en: Seeing the greatly powerful Gandharva army rushing towards him, that chastiser of foes hurled on them a thick shower of arrows.

sn: अचिन्त्य शरवर्षं तु गन्धर्वास्तस्य तं रथम्। दुर्योधनं जिघांसन्तः समन्तात् पर्यवारयन्॥
en: Without minding that shower of arrows the Gandharvas, with the desire of killing Duryodhana, surrounded his car.

sn: युगमीषां वरूथं च तथैव ध्वजसारथी। अश्वांस्त्रिवेणुं तल्पं च तिलशो व्यधमञ्छरैः॥ दुर्योधनं चित्रसेनो विरथं पतितं भुवि। अभिद्रुत्य महाबाहुर्जीवग्राहमथाग्रहीत्॥
en: With their arrows, they cut off into pieces its yoke, shafts, fenders, the flag-staff, threefold bamboo poles and the chief turret. They also cut off his charioteer and horses. When Duryodhana thus deprived to his car fell on the ground, the mighty-armed Chitrasena rushed upon him and seized him with such force that it seemed as if his life itself was taken.

sn: तस्मिन् गृहीते राजेन्द्र स्थितं दुःशासनं रथे। पर्यगृह्णन्त गन्धर्वाः परिवार्य समन्ततः॥
en: O king of kings, when he was thus taken prisoner, the Gandharvas surrounded the car on which Duhshasana was seated; and they took him also as a prisoner.

sn: विविंशतिं चित्रसेनमादायान्ये विदुद्रुवुः। विन्दानुविन्दावपरे राजदारांश्च सर्वशः॥
en: Some seized Vivenshati and Chitrasena and some Vinda and Anuvinda and some again seized all the ladies of the royal household.

sn: सैन्यं तद् धार्तराष्ट्रस्य गन्धर्वैः समभिद्रुतम्। पूर्वं प्रभग्नाः सहिताः पाण्डवानभ्ययुस्तदा॥
en: The soldiers of the son of Dhritarashtra who were routed by the Gandharvas then came to the Pandavas.

sn: शकटापणवेशाश्च यानयुग्यं च सर्वशः। शरणं पाण्डवाञ्जग्मुह्रियमाणे महीपतौ।॥
en: When the king (Duryodhana) was taken prisoner, the vehicles, the shops, the pavilions, the conveyances and the beasts of burden were all made over to the Pandavas for protection. some

sn: सैनिका ऊचुः प्रियदर्शी महाबाहुर्धार्तराष्ट्रो महाबलः। गन्धर्वैह्रियते राजा पार्थास्तमनुधावत॥
en: The soldiers said: The handsome, the mighty-armed and the greatly powerful son of Dhritarashtra (Duryodhana) is taken away by the Gandharvas as prisoner. O sons of Pritha, follow them.

sn: दुःशासनो दुर्विषहो दुर्मुखो दुर्जयस्तथा। बद्ध्वा ह्रियन्ते गन्धर्वै राजदाराश्च सर्वशः॥
en: Duhshasana, Durvisha, Durmukha and Durjaya are all being led away as prisoners bound in chains and also the ladies of the royal household.

sn: इति दुर्योधनामात्याः क्रोशन्तो राजगृद्धिनः। आर्ता दीनाप्ततः सर्वे युधिष्ठिरमुपागमन्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Thus crying, the followers of Duryodhana, afflicted with grief and sorrow, came to Yudhishthira desiring to effect the rescue of their king.

sn: तांस्तथा व्यथितान् दीनान् भिक्षमाणान् युधिष्ठिरम्। वृद्धान् दुर्योधनामात्यान् भीमसेनोऽभ्यभाषत॥
en: Then to those old counsellors of Duryodhana who came, in grief and being melancholy, ask protection from Yudhishthira, Bhimsena said,

sn: महता हि प्रयत्नेन संना गजवाजिभिः। अस्माभिर्यदनुष्ठेयं गन्धर्वैस्तदनुष्ठितम्॥
en: "That, we ought to have done with great efforts arriving ourselves in the line of battle, supported by horses and elephants has indeed been done (today) by the Gandharvas.

sn: अन्यथा वर्तमानानामर्थो जातोऽयमन्यथा। दुर्मन्त्रितमिदं तावद् राज्ञो दुर्दूतदेविनः॥
en: They that came here with other purposes have been overtaken by consequences which they have not foreseen. This is the result of the c'il counsus of a king who is fond of gambling.

sn: द्वेष्टारमन्ये क्लीबस्य पातयन्तीति नः श्रुतम्। इदं कृतं नः प्रत्यक्षं गन्धर्वैरतिमानुषम्॥
en: It has been heard by us that even the enemy of a inan who is powerful is overthrown by to others. the Gandharvas have done this extraordinary feat before our very eyes.

sn: दिष्ट्या लोके पुमानस्ति कश्चिदस्मत्प्रिये स्थितः। येनास्माकं हृतो भार आसीनानां सुखावहः॥
en: There is in the world still fortunately (for us) some who is desirous of doing us good and who has taken upon his shoulder our pleasant load.

sn: शीतवातातपसहांस्तपसा चैव कर्शितान्। समस्थो विषमस्थान् हि द्रष्टुमिच्छति दुर्मतिः॥
en: The wicked-minded wretch had come here to us, himself being in prosperity, while we are now sunk in misery, being emaciated by severe austerities and exposed to wind, cold and heat.

sn: अधर्मचारिणस्तस्य कौरव्यस्य दुरात्मनः। ये शीलमनुवर्तन्ते ते पश्यन्ति पराभवम्॥
en: Those that imitate the conduct of that sinful and wicked Kuru (Duryodhana) are now seeing his own disgrace.

sn: अधर्मो हि कृतस्तेन येनैतदुपशिक्षितम्। अनृशंसास्तु कौन्तेयास्तत् प्रत्यक्षं ब्रवीमि वः॥
en: He who instructed Duryodhana to do this had certainly acted sinfully. I tell you, the sons of Kunti are not wicked and sinful."

sn: एवं ब्रुवाणं कौन्तेयं भीमसेनमपस्वरम्। न काल: परुषस्यायमिति राजाभ्यभाषत॥
en: When the son of Kunti Bhimasena was thus talking in a voice of sarcasm, the king (Yudhishthira) said, “This is not the time for using cruel words.”

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच अस्मानभिातांस्तात भयार्ताञ्छरणैषिणः। कौरवान् विषमप्राप्तान् कथं ब्रूयास्त्वमीदृशम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said : O child, why do you speak these cruel words to these frightened Kurus who are now in adversity and who have come to us for protection?

sn: यदा तु भवन्ति भेदा ज्ञातीनां कलहाश्च वृकोदर। प्रसक्तानि च वैराणि कुलधर्मो न नश्यति॥
en: O Vrikodara, dissensions and disputes often take place among those that are connected in blood. Such hostilities always exist, but for it family honour is never suffered to be destroyed.

sn: कश्चिज्ज्ञातीनां बाह्यः पोथयते कुलम्। न मर्षयन्ति तत् सन्तो बाह्येनाभिप्रधर्षणम्॥
en: If any stranger seeks to destroy the honour of a family, they that are good never tolerate such insult to be offered by the stranger.

sn: जानात्येष हि दुर्बुद्धिरस्मानिह चिरोषितान्। स एवं परिभूयास्मानकादिदमप्रियम्॥
en: The wretched minded one (Gandharva king) knows that we are living here for some time. (Even knowing this), he has disregarded us and has done this which is disagreeable to us.

sn: दुर्योधनस्य ग्रहणाद् गन्धर्वेण बलात् प्रभो। स्त्रीणां बाह्याभिमर्शाच्च हतं भवति नः कुलम्॥
en: O exalted one, from this forcible seizure of Duryodhana and from this insult offered to the ladies of our family by a stranger, our family honour is destroyed,

sn: शरणं च प्रपन्नानां त्राणार्थं च कुलस्य च। उत्तिष्ठत नरव्याघ्राः सज्जीभवत मा चिरम्॥
en: O foremost of men, arise and arm yourselves without the least delay to rescue those that have sought protection and also to save the honour of our family.

sn: अर्जुनश्च यमौ चैव त्वं च वीरापराजितः। मोक्षयध्वं नरव्याघ्रा ह्रियमाणं सुयोधनम्॥
en: Let Arjuna and the twins (Nakula and Sahadeva) and yourself and also those that are brave and invincible (at once go and) rescue Duryodhana who is even now being taken away as a prisoner.

sn: एते रथा नरव्याघ्राः सर्वशस्त्रसमन्विताः। धृतराष्ट्रस्य पुत्राणां विमलाः काञ्चनध्वजाः॥ सस्वनानधिरोहध्वं नित्यसज्जानिमान् रथान्। इन्द्रसेनादिभिः सूतैः कृतशस्त्रैरधिष्ठितान्॥ एतानास्थाय वै यत्ता गन्धर्वान् यो माहवे। सुयोधनस्य मोक्षाय प्रयतध्वमतन्द्रिताः॥ य एव कश्चिद् राजन्यः शरणार्थमिहागतम्। परं शक्त्याभिरक्षेत किं पुनस्त्वं वृकोदर॥
en: These blazing cars with golden flag-staffs belonging to the son of Dhritarashtra are now all ready (before you). With Indrasena and other charioteers who are all skilled in arms, ride all of you these ever furnished cars with deep rattling noise. Ride on them and fight to your utmost power with the Gandharvas to rescue Duryodhana. Even an ordinary Kshatriya would try his best to protect one who has come to him for protection. What then, O Vrikodara, shall I speak to you?

sn: क इहार्यो भवेत् त्राणमभिधावेति नोदितः। प्राञ्जलिं शरणापन्नं दृष्ट्वा शत्रुमपि ध्रुवम्॥ वरप्रदानं राज्यं च पुत्रजन्म च पाण्डवाः। शत्रोच मोक्षणं क्लेशात् त्रीणि चैकं च तत्समम्॥
en: Entreated for assistance in such words as these, “O hasten to my help,” who is there that is so mean as not to help even his enemy when he see him to crave for protection with joined hands? The bestowal of a boon, a sovereignty and the birth of a son are sources of great happiness. But to rescue an enemy from distress is equal to all three.

sn: किं चाप्यधिकमेतस्माद् यदापन्नः सुयोधनः। त्वद्वाहुबलमाश्रित्य जीवितं परिमार्गते॥
en: What could be greater joy to you than that Duryodhana now in distress seeks his very life which now depends on the strength of your arms?

sn: स्वयमेव प्रधावेयं यदि न स्याद् वृकोदर। विततो मे क्रतुर्वीर न हि मेऽत्र विचारणा॥
en: O Vrikodara, O hero, if the vow which I am engaged in observing were over, I would have certainly myself run to his assistance.

sn: साम्नैव तु यथा भीम मोक्षयेथाः सुयोधनम्। तथा सर्वैरुपायैस्त्वं यतेथाः कुरुनन्दन॥ न साम्ना प्रतिपद्येत यदि गन्धर्वराडसौ। पराक्रमेण मृदुना मोक्षयेथाः सुयोधनम्॥
en: Try by all means, O Bhima, O Kuru prince, to rescue Duryodhana (first) by the act of conciliation. If however the Gandharva king cannot be managed by the act of conciliation, then you must try to rescue Duryodhana by light fighting.

sn: अथासौ मृदुयुद्धेन न मुञ्चेद् भीम कौरवान्। सर्वोपायैविमोच्यास्ते निगृह्य परिपन्थिनः॥
en: If the Gandharvas do not let off the Kurus, even then, O Bhima, you must then rescue them by crushing the enemy by all means.

sn: एतावद्धि मया शक्यं संदेष्टुं वै वृकोदर। वैताने कर्मणि तते वर्तमाने च भारत॥
en: O Vrikodara, all this I can tell you now, for my vow has begun, but it has not ended as yet."

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच अजातशत्रोर्वचनं तच्छ्रुत्वा तु धनंजयः। प्रतिजज्ञे गुरोर्वाक्यं कौरवाणां विमोक्षणम्॥
en: Having heard these words of Ajatshatru, Dhananjaya (Arjuna) at the command of his Guru, vowed to rescue the Kurus.

sn: अर्जुन उवाच यदि साम्ना न मोक्ष्यन्ति गन्धर्वा धृतराष्ट्रजान्। अद्य गन्धर्वराजस्य भूमि: पास्यति शोणितम्॥ अर्जुनस्य तु तां श्रुत्वा प्रतिज्ञां सत्यवादिनः। कौरवाणां तदा राजन् पुनः प्रत्यागतं मनः॥
en: “If the Gandharvas do not peacefully let off the Dhritarashtra people, the earth shall this day drink the blood of the Gandharvas." Hearing the vow of the truthful Arjuna, O king, the Kurus were fully cheered up.

description: Battle between the Pandavas and the Gandharvas
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच युधिष्ठिरवचः श्रुत्वा भीमसेनपुरोगमाः। प्रहृष्टवदनाः सर्वे समुत्तस्थुर्नरर्षभाः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having heard the words of Yudhishthira, those foremost of men headed by Bhimasena rose up in great delight.

description: Battle between the Pandavas and the Gandharvas
sn: अभेद्यानि ततः सर्वे समनह्यन्त भारत। जाम्बूनदविचित्राणि कवचानि महारथाः॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, those great carwarriors then put on impenetrable armours that were a decked with gold.

description: Battle between the Pandavas and the Gandharvas
sn: आयुधानि च दिव्यानि विविधानि समादधुः। ते दंशिता रथैः सर्वे ध्वजिनः सशरासनाः॥ पाण्डवाः प्रत्यदृश्यन्त ज्वलिता इव पावकाः।
en: They armed themselves with celestials weapons of various kinds. Thus armed, they ascended the cars furnished with flag-staffs with bows and arrows in their hands. The Pandavas looked like so many blazing fires.

description: Battle between the Pandavas and the Gandharvas
sn: तान् रथान् साधुसम्पन्नान् संयुक्ताञ्जवनैर्हयैः॥ आस्थाय रथशार्दूलाः शीघ्रमेव ययुस्ततः।
en: Those foremost of car-warriors, riding on those well-furnished cars drawn by fleet horses, went to the place where the Gandharvas were) without the least delay.

description: Battle between the Pandavas and the Gandharvas
sn: ततः कौरवसैन्यानां प्रादुरासीन्महास्वनः॥ प्रयातान् सहितान् दृष्ट्वा पाण्डुपुत्रान् महारथान् जितकाशिनश्च खचरास्त्वरिताश्च महारथाः॥ क्षणेनैव वने तस्मिन् समाजग्मुरभीतवत्। न्यवर्तन्त ततः सर्वे गन्धर्वा जितकाशिनः॥
en: Thereupon, the Kuru soldiers sent up a very loud shout. O seeing the great car-warriors the sons of Pandu going to fight with the Gandharvas). Those rangers of the sky (Gandharvas), the great car-warriors, were flushed with victory. Those warriors, the Pandavas, fearlessly encountered one other in the forest.

description: Battle between the Pandavas and the Gandharvas
sn: दृष्ट्वा रथागतान् वीरान् पाण्डवांश्चतुरो रणे। तांस्तु विभाजितान् दृष्ट्वा लोकपालानिवोद्यताम्॥ व्यूढानीका व्यतिष्ठन्त गन्धमादनवासिनः।
en: The Gandharvas, seeing the four sons of Pandu coming to battle on their cars, all turned son back towards the advancing combatants. Seeing the Pandavas looking like the blazing Lokapalas, those dwellers of Gandhamadana (Gandharva) were inflamed with anger and they stood in battle array.

description: Battle between the Pandavas and the Gandharvas
sn: राज्ञस्तु वचनं स्मृत्वा धर्मपुत्रस्य धीमतः॥ क्रमेण मृदुना युद्धमुपक्रान्तं च भारत।
en: In accordance with the command of the greatly intelligent of Dharma, Yudhishthira, O descendant of Bharata, the battle that took place was but a skirmish.

description: Battle between the Pandavas and the Gandharvas
sn: न त गन्धर्वराजस्य सैनिका मन्दचेतसः॥ शक्यन्ते मृदुना श्रेयः प्रति श्रेयः प्रतिपादयितुं तदा। ततस्तान् युधि दुर्धर्षान् सव्यसाची परंतपः॥ सान्त्वपूर्वमिदं वाक्यमुवाच खचरान् रणे। विसर्जयत राजानं भ्रातरं मे सुयोधनम्॥
en: But the foolish minded soldiers of the Gandharva chief were seen by that chastiser of foes Savyasachi (Arjuna) that they could not be by means of a light skirmish made to understand what was good for them. He thus spoke to those rangers of the sky in these conciliatory words, “Let off my brother, the king Duryodhana.”

description: Battle between the Pandavas and the Gandharvas
sn: त एवमुक्ता गन्धर्वाः पाण्डवेन यशस्विना। उत्स्मयन्तस्तदा पार्थमिदं वचनमब्रुवन्॥
en: Having been thus addressed by that illustrious Pandava, the Gandharvas laughed aloud. They thus replied to Partha,

description: Battle between the Pandavas and the Gandharvas
sn: एकस्यैव वयं तात कुर्याम वचनं भुवि। यस्य शासनमाज्ञाय चरामो विगतज्वराः॥ तेनैकेन यथाऽऽदिष्टं तथा वर्ताम भारत। न शास्ता विद्यतेऽस्माकमन्यस्तस्मात् सुरेश्वरात्॥
en: "O child, there is that one whose command we obey and living under whose rule we pass our days being free from all miseries. O descendant of Bharata, we always act as that person commands us.”

description: Battle between the Pandavas and the Gandharvas
sn: एवमुक्तः स गन्धर्वैः कुन्तीपुत्रो धनंजयः। गन्धर्वान् पुनरेवेदं वचनं प्रत्यभाषत॥
en: Having been thus addressed by the Gandharvas in these words, the son of Kunti, Dhananjaya, thus replied to the Gandharvas in these words,

description: Battle between the Pandavas and the Gandharvas
sn: न तद् गन्धर्वराजस्य युक्तं कर्म जुगुप्सितम्। परदाराभिमर्शश्च मानुषैश्च समागमः॥
en: "This contact with other females and this fight with men are not proper for the Gandharva king.

description: Battle between the Pandavas and the Gandharvas
sn: उत्सृज्यध्वं महावीर्यान् धृतराष्ट्रसुतानिमान्। दारांश्चैषां विमुञ्चध्वं धर्मराजस्य शासनात्॥
en: Therefore let off all these mighty sons of Dhritarashtra. Let off also these ladies at the command of Dharmaraja (Yudhishthira).

description: Battle between the Pandavas and the Gandharvas
sn: यदा साम्ना न मुञ्चध्वं गन्धर्वा धृतराष्ट्रजान्। मोक्षयिष्यामि विक्रम्य स्वयमेव सुयोधनम्॥
en: O Gandharva, if you do not set the sons of Dhritarashtra free in peace, I shall certainly rescue Duryodhana by my prowess.

description: Battle between the Pandavas and the Gandharvas
sn: एवमुक्त्वा ततः पार्थः सव्यसाची धनंजयः। ससर्जनिशितान् बाणान् खचरान् खचरान् प्रति॥
en: Having said this, the son of Pritha Savyasachi Dhananjaya (Arjuna) hurled a shower of sky-ranging and sharp arrows on those sky-rangers.

description: Battle between the Pandavas and the Gandharvas
sn: तथैव शरवर्षेण गन्धर्वास्ते बलोत्कटाः। पाण्डवानभ्यवर्तन्त पाण्डवाश्च दिवौकसः॥ ततः सुतुमुलं युद्धं गन्धर्वाणां तरस्विनाम्। बभूव भीमवेगानां पाण्डवानां च भारत॥
en: Thus attacked, those greatly powerful Gandharvas then rushed on the Pandavas and showered on them innumerable arrows. The Pandavas also in their turn attacked those dwellers of heaven. O descendant of Bharata, then a very fearful battle was fought between the active and energetic Gandharvas and the impetuous Pandavas.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततो दिव्यास्त्रसम्पन्ना गन्धर्वा हेममालिनः। विसृजन्तः शरान् दीप्तान् समन्तात् पर्यकारयन्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Thereupon the Gandharvas armed with celestials weapons and adorned with golden garlands, showering showering innumerable blazing arrows, surrounded them on all sides.

sn: चत्वारः पाण्डवा वीरा गन्धर्वाश्च सहस्रशः। रणे संन्यपतन् राजंस्तदद्भुतमिवाभवत्॥
en: There were but four Pandavas heroes; on the other hand there were thousands of Gandharvas. Therefore, O king, the battle that was fought was extraordinary.

sn: यथा कर्णस्य च रथो धार्तराष्ट्रस्य चोभयोः। गन्धर्वैः शतशश्छिन्नौ तथा तेषां प्रचक्रिरे॥
en: As the Gandharvas cut off the chariot of Karna and of the sons of Dhritarashtra, so they tried to do the same with respect to their (Pandava's) chariots.

sn: तान् समापततो राजन् गन्धर्वाञ्छतशो रणे। प्रत्यगृह्णन् नरव्याघ्राः शरवर्षैरनेकशः॥
en: O king, those foremost of men attacked with showers of arrows thousands and thousands of Gandharvas who were rushing towards them.

sn: ते कीर्यमाणाः खगमाः शरवर्षेः समन्ततः। न शेकुः पाण्डुपुत्राणां समीपे परिवर्तितुम्॥
en: Those mighty rangers of the sky, thus checked on all sides by that shower of arrows, did not succeed to come even near the Pandavas.

sn: अभिक्रुद्धानभिक्रुद्धो गन्धर्वानर्जुनस्तदा। लक्षयित्वाथ दिव्यानि महास्त्राण्युपचक्रमे॥
en: Arjuna who was greatly enraged after carefully aiming at them hurled against the angry Gandharvas his celestials weapons.

sn: सहस्राणां सहस्राणि प्राहिणोद् यमसादनम्। आग्नेयेनार्जुनः संख्ये गन्धर्वाणां बलोत्कटः॥
en: In that battle the greatly powerful Arjuna with his Agneya weapon sent ten lakhs of Gandharvas to the abode of Yama.

sn: तथा भीमो महेष्वासः संयुगे बलिनां वरः। गन्धर्वाञ्छतशो राजञ्जघान निशितैः शरैः॥
en: That great bowman, Bhima, that foremost of all strong men, killed in that battle thousands of Gandharvas with his sharp arrows.

sn: ते शकुन्ता इव पञ्जरे। माद्रीपुत्रावपि तथा युध्यमानौ बलोत्कटौ। परिगृह्याचतो राजञ्जघ्नतुः शतशः परान्॥
en: O king, the greatly powerful sons of Madri, fighting with great prowess, attacked hundreds of Gandharvas and killed them all,

sn: ते वध्यमाना गन्धर्वा दिव्यैरस्त्रैर्महारथैः। उत्पेतुः खमुपादाय धृतराष्ट्रसुतांस्ततः॥
en: When the Gandharvas were thus killed by the nighty heroes with the celestials weapons, they ascended the skies and took with them the son of Dhritarashtra.

sn: स तानुत्पतितान् दृष्ट्वा कुन्तीपुत्रो धनंजयः। महता शरजालेन समन्तात् पर्यवारयत्॥
en: But the son of Kunti, Dhananjaya (Arjuna), seeing them rise to the sky, surrounded them on all sides by a net of arrows.

sn: बद्धाः शरजालेन ववर्षुरर्जुनं क्रोधाद् गदाशक्त्यष्टिवृष्टिभिः॥
en: Having been confined within that net of arrows of birds are confined in a cage, they angrily hurled upon Arjuna maces, darts and swords.

sn: गदाशक्त्यृष्टिवृष्टीस्ता निहत्य परमास्त्रवित्। गात्राणि चाहनद् भल्लैर्गन्धर्वाणां धनंजयः॥
en: But Dhananjaya, learned in weapons, soon stopped that shower of maces, darts and swords. He then mangled the limbs of the enemies by his crescent-shaped arrows.

sn: शिरोभिः प्रपतद्भिश्च चरणैर्बाहुभिस्तथा। अश्मवृष्टिरिवाभाति परेषामभवद् भयम्॥
en: Heads, legs and arms (of the Gandharvas) began to drop down from above like a shower of stones; thereupon the enemy was struck with terror.

sn: ते वध्यमाना गन्धर्वाः पाण्डवेन महात्मना। भूमिष्ठमन्तरिक्षस्थाः शरवर्षैरवाकिरन्॥
en: As the Gandharvas were killed by the illustrious Pandava, they hurled a heavy shower of weapons on Arjuna who was on earth.

sn: तेषां तु शरवर्षाणि सव्यसाची परंतपः। अस्त्रैः संवार्य तेजस्वी गन्धर्वान् प्रत्यविध्यत।॥
en: But that chastiser of foes, that greatly powerful Savyasachi (Arjuna), stopped that shower of weapons with his own weapons and began to wound them.

sn: स्थूणाकर्णेन्द्रचालं च सौरं चापि तथार्जुनः। आग्नेयं चापि सौम्यं च ससर्ज कुरुनन्दनः॥
en: That descendant of Kuru, Arjuna, shot his well-known weapons, named Sthunakarna, Indrajala, Saura, Agneya and Saumya.

sn: ते दह्यमाना गन्धर्वाः कुन्तीपुत्रस्य सायकैः। दैतेया इव शक्रेण विषादमगमन् परम्॥
en: The Gandharvas, consumed by the arrows of the son of Kunti, became greatly afflicted, as the Daityas were by Shakra.

sn: ऊर्ध्वमाक्रममाणाश्च शरजालेन वारिताः। विसर्पमाणा भल्लैश्च वार्यन्ते सव्यसाचिना॥
en: When they attacked Savyasachi (Arjuna) from above, they were stopped by his net of arrows. While they attacked him from all sides on earth, they were stopped by his Bhala (weapon).

sn: गन्धर्वांस्त्रासितान् दृष्ट्वा कुन्तीपुत्रेण भारत। चित्रसेनो गदां गृह्य सव्यसाचिनमाद्रवत्॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, seeing the Gandharvas routed by the son of Kunti, Chitrasena took up a mace and rushed upon Savyasachi.

sn: तस्याभिपततस्तूर्णं गदाहस्तस्य संयुगे। गदां सर्वायसी पार्थः शरैश्चिच्छेद सप्तधा॥
en: As he was rushing with his mace in his hand, Partha (Arjuna) cut off that iron mace into seven pieces.

sn: स गदा बहुधा दृष्ट्वा कृत्तां बाणैस्तरस्विना। संवृत्य विद्ययाऽऽत्मानं योधयामास पाण्डवम्॥
en: Seeing his mace cut into piece by that very active hero, (Arjuna), with his arrows, he with his own science (of illusion) began to fight with the Pandava.

sn: अस्त्राणि तस्य दिव्यानि सम्प्रयुक्तानि सर्वशः। दिव्यैरस्स्तदा वीरः पर्यवारयदर्जुनः॥
en: The heroic Arjuna, however, stopped with his celestials weapons all the celestials weapons that were aimed at him by the Gandharva king.

sn: स वार्यमाणस्तैरस्त्रैरर्जुनेन महात्मना। गन्धर्वराजो बलवान् माययान्तर्हितस्तदा॥
en: When the mighty Gandharva king saw that he was checked by the high-souled Arjuna with his weapons, he disappeared from view by the help of illusion.

sn: अन्तर्हितं तमालक्ष्य प्रहरन्तमथार्जुनः। ताडयामास खचरैर्दिव्यास्त्रप्रतिमन्त्रितैः॥
en: Seeing that the ranger of sky was striking at him concealed from sight, Arjuna attacked him with his celestials weapons with proper mantras.

sn: अन्तर्धानवधं चास्य चक्रे क्रुद्धोऽर्जुनस्तदा। शब्दवेधं समाश्रित्य बहुरूपो धनंजयः॥
en: Dhananjaya, becoming greatly enraged, prevented the disappearance of his enemy with his weapon called Shabdavedha.

sn: स वध्यमानस्तैरस्त्रैरर्जुनेन महात्मना। ततोऽस्यदर्शयामास तदाऽऽत्मानं प्रियः सखा।॥
en: Attacked by those weapons by the illustrious Arjuna, his dear friend the Gandharva king appeared before him.

sn: चित्रसेनस्तथोवाच सखायं युधि विद्धि माम्। चित्रसेनमथालक्ष्य सखायं युधि दुर्बलम्॥ संजहारास्त्रमथ तत् प्रसृष्टं पाण्डवर्षभः। दृष्ट्वा तु पाण्डवाः सर्वे संहतास्त्रं धनंजयम्॥ संजह्वः प्रदुतानश्वाञ्छरवेगान् धनूंषि च।
en: Chitrasena thus spoke to him, “Behold, your friend is fighting with you." Seeing his friend weak in battle, that foremost of Pandavas withdrew his weapons. The Pandavas, seeing Arjuna withdraw his weapons, checked their flying horses and stopped their weapons and withdrew their bows.

sn: चित्रसेनश्च भीमश्च सव्यसाची यमावपि। पृष्ट्वा कौशलमन्योन्यं रथेष्वेवारतस्थिरे॥
en: Chitrasena, Bhima and Arjuna and the twins then enquired after one another's welfare and sat down on their respective chariots.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततोऽर्जुनश्चित्रसेनं प्रहसन्निदमब्रवीत्। मध्ये गन्धर्वसैन्यानां महेष्वासो महाद्युतिः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : The greatly effulgent great bowman Arjuna then smilingly thus spoke to Chitrasena in the midst of the Gandharvas soldiers.

sn: किं ते व्यवसितं वीर कौरवाणां विनिग्रहे। किमर्थं च सदारोऽयं निगृहीत: सुयोधनः॥
en: "O hero, what purpose do you serve by punishing the Kurus? Why do you persecute Duryodhana with his wives."

sn: चित्रसेन उवाच विदितोऽयमभिप्रायस्तत्रस्थेन दुरात्मनः। दुर्योधनस्य पापस्य कर्णस्य च धनंजय॥
en: Chitrasena said : O Dhananjaya, I knew long before the (real) purpose of the wicked Duryodhana and the wretched Karna in coming here.

sn: वनस्थान् भवतो ज्ञात्वा क्लिश्यमानाननाथवत्। समस्थो विषमस्थांस्तान् द्रक्ष्यामीत्यनवस्थितान्॥
en: That purpose is this, knowing that you are exiled in the forest and suffering great afflictions, as if you had no one to take care of you, himself in prosperity, this wretch desired to see you in adversity and misfortune.

sn: इमेऽवहसितुं प्राप्ता द्रौपदी च यशस्विनीम्। ज्ञात्वा चिकीर्षितं चैषां मामुवाच सुरेश्वरः॥
en: They came here to mock you and the illustrious Draupadi. Knowing their purpose the lord of the celestials thus spoke to me,

sn: गच्छ दुर्योधनं बद्ध्वा सहामात्यमिहानय। धनंजयश्च ते रक्ष्यः सह भ्रातृभिराहवे।॥ स च प्रियः सखा तुभ्यं शिष्यश्च तव पाण्डवः।
en: "Go and bring Duryodhana in chains with all his counsellors. Protect Dhananjaya with all his brothers in battle; he is my dear friend and that Pandava is also my disciple.”

sn: वचनाद् देवराजस्य ततोऽस्मीहागतो द्रुतम्॥ अयं दुरात्मा बद्धश्च गमिष्यामि सुरालयम्। नेष्याम्येनं दुरात्मानं पाकशासनशासनात्॥
en: At these words of the lord of the celestials, I speedily came here. The wicked wretch is now in chains, I shall go to the abode of the celestials. I shall now take this wicked-minded one at the command of the slayer of Paka.

sn: अर्जुन उवाच उत्सृज्यतां चित्रसेन भ्रातास्माकं सुयोधनः। धर्मराजस्य संदेशान्मम चेदिच्छसि प्रियम्॥
en: Arjuna said : O Chitrasena, if you wish to do what is agreeable to me, then set Duryodhana free at the command of Dharmaraja, he is our brother.

sn: चित्रसेन उवाच पापोऽयं नित्यसंतुष्टो न विमोक्षणमर्हति। प्रलब्धा धर्मराजस्य कृष्णायाश्च धनंजय॥ नेदं चिकीर्षितं तस्य कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः। जानाति धर्मराजो हि श्रुत्वा कुरु यथेच्छसि॥
en: Chitrasena said : This sinful wretch is always full of vanity. He deserves not to be let off. O Dhananjaya, he has deceived and wronged both Dharmaraja and Krishna (Draupadi). The son of Kunti Yudhishthira knows not the purpose in which this wretch came here. Let the king therefore do what he likes after knowing everything.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ते सर्व एव राजानमभिजग्मुर्युधिष्ठिरम्। अभिगम्य च तत् सर्वं शशंसुस्तस्य चेष्टितम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said: Thereupon all of them went to king Yudhishthira. Going to him they told all that had happened.

sn: अजातशत्रुस्तच्छ्रुत्वा गन्धर्वस्य वचस्तदा। मोक्षयामास तान् सर्वान् गन्धर्वान् प्रशशंस च॥
en: Ajatshatru (Yudhishthira), having heard the words of the Gandharva, asked to set them all free and he also praised the Gandharva.

sn: दिष्ट्या भवद्भिर्बलिभिः शक्तैः सर्वैर्न हिंसितः। दुर्वृत्तो धार्तराष्ट्रोऽयं सामात्यज्ञातिबान्धवः॥
en: (He said), “It is fortunate for us that though you possess great prowess, you did not kill the wicked sons of Dhritarashtra (Duryodhana) with all his counsellors and relatives.

sn: उपकारो महांस्तात कृतोऽयं मम खेचरैः। कुलं न परिभूतं मे मोक्षणेऽस्य दुरात्मनः॥
en: O sir, this is a great kindness that has been shown to me by the Gandharvas. The honour of my family is also saved by liberating the wicked wretch.

sn: आज्ञापयध्वनिमिष्टानि प्रीयामो दर्शनेन वः। प्राप्य सर्वानभिप्रायांस्ततो व्रजत मा चिरम्॥
en: I am pleased to see you all. Command me what I can do for you. Having received all that you desire to have, go back to the place whence you came."

sn: अनुज्ञातास्तु गन्धर्वाः पाण्डुपुत्रेण धीमता। सहाप्सरोभिः संहृष्टाश्चित्रसेनमुखा ययुः॥
en: Thus requested by the greatly intelligent Pandava, the Gandharvas became greatly delighted. They went away with the Apsaras with Chitrasena at their head.

sn: देवराडपि गन्धर्वान् मृतांस्तान् समजीवयत्। दिव्येनामृतवर्षेण ये हताः कौरवैर्युधि॥
en: The lord of the celestials then came there and vivified with the celestials Ambrosia all those Gandharvas that were killed in the battle with the Kurus.

sn: ज्ञातींस्तानवमुच्याथ राजदारांश्च सर्वशः। कृत्वा च दुष्करं कर्म प्रीतियुक्ताश्च पाण्डवाः॥
en: The Pandavas also, having rescued their relatives with the ladies of the royal household and having achieved that great feat, became exceedingly delighted.

sn: सस्त्रीकुमारैः कुरुभिः पूज्यमाना महारथाः। बभ्राजिरे महात्मानः क्रतुमध्ये यथाग्नयः॥
en: Those illustrious car-warriors, worshipped by the Kurus with their sons and wives, blazed forth in splendour, as a fire blazes in a sacrifice.

sn: ततो दुर्योधनं मुक्तं भ्रातृभिः सहितस्तदा। युधिष्ठिरस्तु प्रणयादिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Then Yudhishthira thus spoke out of affection to the liberated Duryodhana in the midst of his brothers.

sn: मा स्म तात पुनः कार्षीरीदृशं साहसं क्वचित्। न हि साहसकर्तारः सुखमेधन्ति भारत॥
en: "O child, O descendant of Bharata never again commit such a rash act. A rash man never becomes happy.

sn: स्वस्तिमान् सहितः सर्वैर्धातृभिः कुरुनन्दन। गृहान् व्रज यथाकामं वैमनस्यं च मा कृथाः॥
en: Kuru prince, be blessed with all your brothers. Go back home as pleases you without any despondency or cheerlessness."

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच पाण्डवेनाभ्यनुज्ञातो राजा दुर्योधनस्तदा। प्रणम्य धर्मपुत्रं तु गतेन्द्रिय इवातुरः॥ विदीर्यमाणो व्रीडावाञ्जगाम नगरं प्रति।
en: Having been thus dismissed by the Pandavas, Duryodhana saluted the son of Dharma (Yudhishthira). Overwhelmed with shame, his heart appeared as if rent in two. He mechanically started for his city as destitute of life.

sn: तस्मिन् गते कौरवेये कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः॥ भ्रातृभिः सहितो वीरः पूज्यमानो द्विजातिभिः। तपोधनैश्च तैः सर्वैर्वृतः शक्र इवामरैः॥ तथा द्वैतवने तस्मिन् विजहार मुदा युतः॥
en: When that Kuru (Duryodhana), had gone away, the son of Kunti Yudhishthira with his brothers was worshipped by the Brahmanas. Surrounded by these great ascetics, as Indra by the celestials, he lived in great happiness in that forest of Dvaitavana. one

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: जनमेजय उवाच शत्रुभिर्जितबद्धस्य पाण्डवैश्च महात्मभिः। मोक्षितस्य युधा पश्चान्मानिनः सुदुरात्मनः॥ कत्थनस्यावलिप्तस्य गर्वितस्य च नित्यशः। सदा च पौरुषौदार्यैः पाण्डवानवमन्यतः॥ दुर्योधनस्य पापस्य नित्याहंकारवादिनः। प्रवेश हास्तिनपुरे दुष्करः प्रतिभाति मे॥ तस्य लज्जान्वितस्यैव शोकव्याकुलचेतसः। प्रवेशं विस्तरेण त्वं वैशम्पायन कीर्तय॥
en: Janamejaya said : After his defeat and capture by the enemy and his subsequent liberation by the highsouled sons of Pandu by their prowess of arms, it seems to me that the entry of the proud, wicked, boastful, vicious insolent and wretched Duryodhana, ever engaged in insulting the Pandavas and boastful of his own superiority into Hastinapur must have been exceedingly difficult. O Vaishampayana, describe to me in detail the entry into the capital of that prince, overwhelmed as he was then with shame and grief.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच धर्मराजनिसृष्टस्तु धार्तराष्ट्रः सुयोधनः। लज्जयाधोमुखः सीदन्नुपपासर्पत् सुदुःखितः॥
en: Vaishampayana said: Having been dismissed by king Dharmaraja (Yudhishthira), the son of Dhritarashtra, Duryodhana, bending his head down in shame and greatly afflicted with grief and sorrow, slowly went away.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: स्वपुरं प्रययौ राजा चतुरङ्गबलानुगः। शोकोपहतया बुद्ध्या चिन्तयानः पराभवम्॥
en: The king (Duryodhana), accompanied by his four kinds of forces went towards his city, his heart rent in grief and his mind filled with thoughts of his defeat.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: विमुच्य पथि यानानि देशे सुयवसोदके। सनिविष्टः शुभे रम्ये भूमिभागे यथेप्सितम्॥
en: Leaving his chariots in the way in a place which abounded in grass and water, the king encamped on a delightful and good place as pleased him best.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: हस्त्यश्वरथपादातं यथास्थानं न्यवेशयत्। अथोपविष्टं राजानं पर्यङ्के ज्वलनप्रभे॥
en: With his elephants, cars, cavalry and infantry stationed all around (the camp), he was seated on an elevated bed-stead as bright as fire.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: उपप्लुतं यथा सोमं राहुणा रात्रिसंक्षये। उपागम्याब्रवीत् कर्णो दुर्योधनमिदं तदा।॥
en: Himself looking like the moon under eclipse. At the end of the night, Karna came to Duryodhana and thus spoke to him,

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: दिष्ट्या जीवसि गान्धारे दिष्ट्या नः सङ्गमः पुनः। दिष्ट्या त्वया जिताश्चैव गन्धर्वाः कामरूपिणः॥
en: "O son of Gandhari, fortunate it is that you are alive. Fortunate it is that we have again met. By good luck you have defeated the Gandharvas who are capable of assuming any form at will.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: दिष्ट्या समग्रान् पश्यामि भ्रातूंस्ते कुरुनन्दन। विजिगीषन् रणे युक्तान् निर्जितारीन् महारथान्॥
en: O descendant of Kuru, by good luck alone that I am enabled to see your brothers, who are all mighty car-warriors, come off victorious from that battle.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: अहं त्वभिद्रुतः सर्वैर्गन्धर्वैः पश्यतस्तव। नाशक्नुवं स्थापयितुं दीर्यमाणां च वाहिनीम्॥ शरक्षताङ्गश्च भृशं व्यपयातोऽभिपीडतः। इदं त्वत्यद्भुतं मन्ये यद् युष्मानिह भारत॥ अरिष्टानक्षतांश्चापि सदारबलवाहनान्। विमुक्तान् सम्प्रपश्यामि युद्धात् तस्मादमानुषात्॥
en: As for myself, being attacked by the Gandharvas and being unable to rally our hosts I fled before your eyes. Attacked by the enemy with all the prowess and my body mangled with their arrows, I sought safety in flight. This, however, O descendant of Bharata, seemed to me to be a great wonder that I see you all come back safe with your wives, troops and vehicles out of that super-human battle.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: नैतस्य कर्ता लोकेऽस्मिन् पुमान् भारत विद्यते। यत् कृतं ते महाराज सह भ्रातृभिराहवे।॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, O great king, that is no other man in this world who can achieve what you have achieved in battle today with your brothers.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्तस्तु कर्णेन राजा दुर्योधनस्तदा। उवाच चाङ्गराजानं वाष्पगद्गदया गिरा॥
en: Vaiskampayana said : Having been thus addressed by Karna, king Duryodhana thus spoke in reply to the Anga king (Karna) in a voice choked with tears.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: दुर्योधन उवाच अजानतस्ते राधेय नाभ्यसूयाम्यहं वचः। जानासि त्वं जिताञ्छत्रून् गन्धर्वांस्तेजसा मया॥
en: Duryodhana said : O son of Radha, you do not know what had happened; therefore I am not angry at your word. You think that the hostile Gandharvas had been defeated by my own prowess.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: आयोधितास्तु गन्धर्वाः सुचिरं सोदरैर्मम। मया सह महाबाहो कृतश्चोभयतः क्षयः॥
en: O mighty-armed hero, for a long time my brothers standing by me fought with the Gandharvas. But the slaughter on both the sides was very great.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: मायाधिकास्त्वयुध्यन्त यदा शूरा वियद्गताः। तदा नो न समं युद्धमभवत् खेचरैः सह॥
en: When those heroes (the Gandharvas) fought with the illusion, then our battle with those rangers of skies became an unequal one.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: पराजयं च प्राप्ताः स्मो रणे बन्धनमेव च। सभृत्यामात्यपुत्राश्च सदारबलवाहनाः॥
en: We then met with defeat and we were then all made prisoners along with our attendants, counsellors, children, wives, troops and cars.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: उच्चैराकाशमार्गेण हता:स्मस्तैः सुदुःखिताः। अथ नः सैनिकाः केचिदमात्याश्च महारथाः॥
en: We were overwhelmed with sorrow and we were being taken by them ihrough high skies. Our Thereupon some of soldiers and counsellers and great car-warriors.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: उपगम्याब्रुवन् दीनाः पाण्डवाञ्छरणप्रदान्। एष दुर्योधनो राजा धार्तराष्ट्रः सहानुजः॥
en: Went in grief to the Pandavas who never refuse help to those that ask for it; they thus spoke to them, “Here is king Duryodhana, the son of Dhritarashtra with his brothers.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: सामात्यदारो ह्रियते गन्धर्वैर्दिवमाश्रितैः। तं मोक्षयत भद्रं वः सहदारं नराधिपम्॥
en: And also with his counsellors and wives. He is being carried away a prisoner by the Gandharvas who are in the sky. Be blessed. Rescue the king with his wives.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: पराभवो मा भविष्यत् कुरुदारेषु सर्वशः। एवमुक्ते तु धर्मात्मा ज्येष्ठः पाण्डुसुतस्तदा॥
en: Do not allow great insult to be offered to all the Kuru ladies." Having been thus addressed, the eldest Pandava, who is ever virtuous.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: प्रसाद्य पाण्डवान् सर्वानाज्ञापयत मोक्षणे। अथागम्य तमुद्देशं पाण्डवाः पुरुषर्षभाः॥ सान्त्वपूर्वमयाचन्त शक्ताः सन्तो महारथाः। यदा चास्मान् न मुमुचुर्गन्धर्वाः सान्त्विता अपि॥
en: Conciliating all the Pandavas ordered them to rescue us. Thereupon those foremost of men, the Pandavas, overtaking them (the Gandharvas), asked them in sweet words to release us, although they were able to rescue us by force. But when they refused to release us in sweet words.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: ततोऽरर्जुनश्च भीमश्च यमजौ न बलोत्कटौ। मुमुचुः शरवर्षाणि गन्धर्वान् प्रत्यनेकशः॥
en: Then the greatly powerful Bhima, Arjuna and the twins (Nakula and Sahadeva) hurled on the Gandharvas a great shower of arrows.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: अथ सर्वे रणं मुक्त्वा प्रयाताः खेचरा दिवम्। अस्मानेवाभिकर्षन्तो दीनान् मुदितमानसाः॥
en: Thereupon those rangers of skies, abandoning the fight fled through the sky and dragged our poor-selves after them in great joy.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: ततः समन्तात् पश्यामः शरजालेन वेष्टितम्। अमानुषाणि चास्त्राणि प्रमुञ्चन्तं धनंजयम्॥
en: Then we saw a net-work of arrows all around us spread out by Dharmaraja who was shooting extraordinary weapons on the enemy.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: समावृता दिशो दृष्ट्वा पाण्डवेन शितैः शरैः। धनंजयसखाऽऽत्मानं दर्शयामास वै तदा॥
en: Seeing all directions covered with a net work of sharp arrows shot by the Pandavas, that friend of Dhananjaya (the Gandharva king) appeared before him,

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: चित्रसेनः पाण्डवेन समाश्लिष्य परस्परम्। कुशलं परिपप्रच्छ तैः पृष्टश्चाप्यनामयम्॥ ते समेत्य तथान्योन्यं सन्नाहान् विप्रमुच्य च। एकीभूतास्ततो वीरा गन्धर्वाः सह पाण्डवैः। अपूजयेतामन्योन्यं चित्रसेनधनंजयौ॥
en: Then Chitrasena and the Pandava (Arjuna) embraced each other and enquired after each other's health. The other Pandavas were also embraced by him in return. They also enquired about one another's welfare. The heroic Gandharvas then casting aside their armours and weapons mixed freely with the Pandavas. Then Chitrasena and Dharmaraja worshipped each other with great respect and regard.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: दुर्योधन उवाच चित्रसेनं समागम्य प्रहसनर्जुनस्तदा। इदं वचनकक्लीबमब्रवीत् परवीरहा॥
en: Duryodhana said : That slayer of hostile army, Arjuna, then came to Chitrasena and he smilingly spoke these manly words.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: भ्रातृनर्हसि मे वीर मोक्तुं गन्धर्वसत्तम। अनर्हधर्षणा हीमे जीवमानेषु पाण्डुषु॥
en: "O hero, O foremost of the Gandharvas, you should release my brothers. They are not to be insulted so long the Pandavas are alive."

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: एवमुक्तस्तु गन्धर्वः पाण्डेवन महात्मना। उवाच यत् कर्ण वयः मन्त्रयन्तो विनिर्गताः॥ द्रष्टारः स्म सुखाद्धीनान् सदारान् पाण्डवानिति।
en: Having been thus addressed by the illustrious son of Pandu, O Karna, the Gandharva told him of the (secret) counsel with which we came, namely we had gone there for seeing the Pandavas, with their wife in the greatest misery.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: तस्मिन्नुच्चार्यमाणे तु गन्धर्वेण वचस्तथा॥ भूमेर्विवरमन्वैच्छं प्रवेष्टुं व्रीडयान्वितः।
en: When these counsels of ours were disclosed by the Gandharva, I desired then in great shame to enter the earth.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: युधिष्ठिरमथागम्य गन्धर्वाः सह पाण्डवैः॥ अस्महुर्मन्त्रितं तस्मै बद्धांश्चास्मान् न्यवेदयन्।
en: The Gandharva then accompanied by the Pandavas went to Yudhishthira describing to him our (secret) counsels, bound as we were, he made us over to him.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: स्त्रीसमक्षमहं दीनो बद्धः शत्रुवशं गतः॥ युधिष्ठिरस्योपहृतः किं नु दुःखमतः परम्।
en: Alas, what greater sorrow could be mine than that I should thus be offered as tribute to Yudhishthira in the very sight of our women, myself in chains and in great misery and also under the complete control of our enemies!

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: ये मे निराकृता नित्यं रिपुर्येषामहं सदा॥ तैर्मोक्षितोऽहं दुर्बुद्धिर्दत्तं तैरेव जीवितम्।
en: Alas, they that were ever persecuted by me, they that were my everlasting enemies, released me from captivity! Wretch that I am, I am indebted to them for my life!

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: प्राप्त: स्यां यद्यहं वीर वधं तस्मिन् महारणे॥ श्रेयस्तद् भविता मह्यं नैवंभूतस्य जीवितम्।
en: O hero, if I had met with my death in that great battle that would have been far better than that I have obtained my life in this way.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: भवेद् यशः पृथिव्यां मे ख्यातं गन्धर्वतो वधात्॥ प्राप्ताश्च पुण्यलोकाः स्युर्महेन्द्रसदनेऽक्षयाः।
en: If I would have been killed by the Gandharvas, my fame would have spread over the earth. I would have then obtained holy regions of everlasting happiness in the abode of Indra.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: यत् त्वद्य मे व्यवसितं तच्छृणुध्वं नरर्षभाः॥ इह प्रायमुपासिष्ये यूयं व्रजत वै गृहान्।
en: O foremost of men, listen to me now as to what I intend to do. I shall stay here fasting, all of you go back home.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: भ्रातरश्चैव मे सर्वे यान्त्वद्य स्वपुरं प्रति॥ कर्णप्रभृतयश्चैव सुहृदो बान्धवाश्च ये। दुःशासनं पुरस्कृत्य प्रयान्वद्य पुरं प्रति॥
en: Let all my brothers also go to their own city (Hastinapur). Let all our relatives and friends headed by Dushasana go back to the city.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: न ह्यहं सम्प्रयास्यामि पुरं शत्रुनिराकृतः। शत्रुमानापहो भूत्वा सुहृदां मानकृत् तथा॥
en: Insulted as I am by the enemy I shall never again return to that city; I was ever respected and feared by my enemy, I who ever enhanced the respect of my friends and relatives,

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: स सुहृच्छोकदो जातः शत्रूणां हर्षवर्धनः। वारणाह्वयमासाद्य किं वक्ष्यामि जनाधिपम्॥
en: Have now become a source of sorrow to my friends and joy to my enemies. Having gone to Hastinapura, what shall I say to the king (Dhritarashtra)?

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: भीष्मद्रोणौ कृपद्रौणी विदुरः संजयस्तथा। बाह्रीकः सौमदत्तिश्च ये चान्ये वृद्धसम्मताः॥ ब्राह्मणाः श्रेणिमुख्याश्च तथोदासीनवृत्तयः। किं मां वक्ष्यन्ति किं चापि प्रतिवक्ष्यामि तानहम्॥
en: What will Bhishma, Drona, Kripa, the son of Drona (Ashvathama), Vidura, Sanjaya, the son of Balhika (king), the son of Somadatta and the other revered chiefs and also the chief men of independent professions say to me and what shall I say to them in return?

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: रिपूणां शिरसि स्थित्वा तथा विक्रम्य चोरसि। आत्मदोषात् परिभ्रष्टः कथं वक्ष्यामि तानहम्॥
en: Having hitherto stayed over the heads of my enemies, having hitherto trod upon their breasts, I have been now degraded from my position. What shall I say to them (now)?

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: दुर्विनीता: श्रियं प्राप्य विद्यामैश्वर्यमेव च। तिष्ठन्ति न चिरं भद्रे यथाहं मदगर्वितः॥
en: Like me who was puffed up with vanity, insolent men, even obtaining prosperity, knowledge and affluence, are never blessed for any length of time.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: अहो नाहमिदं कर्म कष्टं दुश्चरितं कृतम्। स्वयं दुर्बुद्धिना मोहाद् येन प्राप्तोऽस्मि संशयम्॥
en: Alas, led by folly I have done a highly improper and wicked act, for which, fool that I am, I have now fallen into such distress.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: तस्मात् प्रायमुपासिष्ये हि शक्ष्यामि जीवितुम्। चेतयानो हि को जीवेत् कृच्छ्राच्छत्रुभिरुद्धतः॥
en: I shall therefore die of starvation; I shall not be able to live. Rescued by one's own enemy, what man of manliness could dragon (a miserable) existence?

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: शत्रुभिश्चावहसितो मानी पौरुषवर्जितः। याण्डवैविक्रमाढ्यैश्च सावमानमवेक्षितः॥
en: Proud as I am, the enemy has laughed at me when they found me deprived of all manliness. The Pandavas, who possessed great prowess (joyously) looked at me who was then in the greatest possible misery."

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवं चिन्तापरिगतो दुःशासनमथाब्रवीत्। दुःशासन निबोधेदं वचनं मम भारत॥
en: Vaishampayana said : When he was thus bewailing, he thus spoke to Dushasana, "O Dushasana, O descendant of Bharata, hear my words.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: प्रतीच्छ त्वं मया दत्तमभिषेकं नृपो भव। प्रशाधि पृथिवीं स्फीतां कर्णसौबलपालिताम्॥
en: Accepting this installation offered by me, becorne king. Rule over the earth protected by Karna and the son of Subala.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: भ्रातृन् पालय विस्रब्धं मरुतो वृत्रहा यथा। बान्धवाश्चोपजीवन्तु देवा इव शतक्रतुम्॥
en: As the slayer of Vritra (Indra) cherishes the arutas, so cherish our brothers in such a way as they may trust you. Let your friends and relatives depend on you as the celestials depend on you as the celestials depend on Shatakratu (Indra).

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: ब्राह्मणेषु सदा वृत्तिं कुर्वीथाश्चाप्रमादतः। बन्धूनां सुहृदां चैव भवेथस्त्वं गतिः सदा॥
en: Always bestow pensions on Brahmanas; be always the refuge of your friends and relatives.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: ज्ञातींश्चाप्यनुपश्येथा विष्णुर्देवगणान् यथा। गुरवः पालनीयास्ते गच्छ पालय मेदिनीम्॥ नन्दयन् सुहृदः सर्वान् शात्रवांश्चावभर्सयन्। कण्ठे चैनं परिष्वज्य गम्यतामित्युवाच ह॥
en: As Vishnu looks after the celestials, you should also look after all your poor and helpless relatives. Always cherish your Gurus. Go, rule the earth, gladdening all your friends and chastising all your enemies." Clasping his neck he said, “Go."

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा दीनो दुःशासनोऽब्रवीत्। अश्रुकण्ठः सुदुःखार्तः प्राञ्जलिः प्रणिपत्य च॥ सगद्गदमिदं वाक्यं भ्रातरं ज्येष्ठमात्मनः। प्रसीदेत्यपतद् भूमौ दूयमानेन चेतसा॥ दुःखितः पादयोस्तस्य नेत्रजं जलमुत्सृजन्। उक्तवांश्च नरव्याघ्रो नैतदेवं भविष्यति॥
en: Having heard his words, Dushasana in great misery and grief said to his eldest brother with joined hands, with bent down head and with voice choked in tears, “Relent.” Saying this, he fell down on the earth in the greatest possible misery. In sorrow and grief that foremost of men shed tears on the feet of his brother and thus spoke to him, “This can never be done.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: विदीर्येत् सकला भूमियोश्चापि शकलीभवेत्। रविरात्मप्रभा जह्यात् सोमः शीतांशुतां त्येजत्॥ वायुः शैयमथो जह्याद्धिमवांश्च परिव्रजेत्। शुष्येत् तोयं समुद्रेषु वह्निरप्युष्णतां त्येजत्॥ न चाहं त्वदृते राजन् प्रशासेयं वसुन्धराम्। पुनः पुनः प्रसीदेति वाक्यं चेदमुवाच ह॥
en: The earth may split, the heavens may fall down in pieces, the sun may lose his rays, the moon may abandon her coolness, the wind may forsake its speed, the Himalayas may be moved from its site, the waters of the ocean may dry up and fire may lose its heat; But, ( king, I cannot rule the earth without you.” He again and again said, “Relent," "Relent".

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: त्वमेव नः कुले राजा भविष्यसि शतं समाः। एवमुक्त्वा स राजानं सुस्वरं प्ररुरोद ह॥
en: “You alone shall be king in our race, for one hundred years.” Having said this, he loudly wept before the king.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: पादौ संस्पृश्य मानार्हो भ्रातुर्येष्ठस्य भारत। तथा तौ दुःखितौ दृष्ट्वा दुःशासनसुयोधनौ।॥ अधिगम्य व्यधाविष्टः कर्णस्तौ प्रत्यभाषत। विषीदथः किं कौरव्यौ बालिश्यात् प्राकृताविव॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, catching, the feet of his eldest brother who deserved worship from him. Having seen Dushasana in great grief and Duryodhana in greatest possible misery, Karna came to them and said, “O Kuru princes, why do you childishly weep like ordinary people?

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: न शोकः शोचमानस्य विनिवर्तेत कर्हिचित्। यदा च शोचतः शोको व्यसनं नापकर्षति॥
en: Men can never by weeping drive away their grief. Weeping can never remove one's own grief.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: सामर्थ्य किं ततः शोके शोचमानौ प्रपश्यथः। धृतिं गृहणीतमा शत्रून् शोचन्तौ नन्दयिष्यथः॥
en: What do you gain by thus giving way to sorrow? Summon patience. Do not grieve and thus give joy to your enemies.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: कर्तव्यं हि कृतं राजन् पाण्डवैस्तव मोक्षणम्। नित्यमेव प्रियं कार्यं राज्ञो विषयवासिभिः॥
en: O king, the Pandavas did only their duty in rescuing you. Those that reside in the dominions of the king should always do what is agreeable to the king.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: पाल्यमानास्त्वया ते हि निवसन्ति गतज्वराः। नार्हस्येवंगते मन्युं कर्तुं प्राकृतवद् यथा॥
en: Under your protection, the Pandavas are residing in your dominion in great happiness. You should not indulge in sorrow like ordinary people.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: विषण्णास्त्व सोदर्यास्त्वयि प्रायं समास्थिते। उत्तिष्ठ व्रज भद्रं ते समाश्वासय सोदरान्॥
en: 'Behold, your brothers are all sad and miserable on seeing you resolved to die by starvation. Be blessed. Rise up and come to your city and console your brothers.'

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: कर्ण उवाच राजन्नाधावगच्छामि तवेह लघुसत्त्वताम्। किमत्र चित्रं यद् वीर मोक्षितः पाण्डवैरसि॥
en: Karna said.: O king, your today's conduct is childish. O hero, what is to be wondered at in all this, that you were rescued by the Pandavas.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: सद्यो वशं समापन्नः शत्रूणां शत्रुकर्शन। सेनाजीवैश्च कौरव्य तथा विषयवासिभिः॥
en: When you were defeated by the foe. O chastiser of foes, O descendant of Kuru, those that reside in the dominion of the king, specially the warriors.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: अज्ञातैर्यदि वा ज्ञातैः कर्तव्यं नृपतेः प्रियम्। प्राय: प्रधानाः पुरुषाः क्षोभयन्त्यरिवाहिनीम्॥ निगृह्यन्ते च युद्धेषु मोक्ष्यन्ते चैव सैनिकैः। सेनाजीवाश्च ये राज्ञां विषये सन्ति मानवाः॥ तैः सङ्गम्य नृपार्थाय यतितव्यं यथातथम्। यद्येवं पाण्डवै राजन् भवद्विषयवासिभिः॥ यदृच्छया मोक्षितोऽसि तत्र का परिदेवना। न चैतत् साधु यद् राजन् पाण्डवास्त्वां नृपोत्तमम्॥
en: Should always do what is agreeable to the king, whether they happen to be known to the king or unknown to him. Often happens that even the foremost of men who are capable of crushing the enemy are often defeated by them; under such circumstances they are often rescued by their troops. The warriors living in a king's dominion should always combine and try their utmost for their king. If, therefore, O king, the Pandavas who live in your dominion have rescued you, what is there to be sorry for? O foremost of kings, O monarch, it was not proper for the Pandavas.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: स्वसेनया सम्प्रयान्तं नानुयान्ति स्म पृष्ठतः। शूराश्च बलवन्तश्च संयुगेष्वपलायिनः॥ भवतस्ते सहाया वै प्रेष्यतां पूर्वमागताः। पाण्डवेयानि रत्नानि त्वमद्याप्युपभुञ्जसे॥ सत्त्वस्थान् पाण्डवान् पश्य न ते प्रायमुपाविशन् उत्तिष्ठ राजन् भद्रं ते न चिरं कर्तुमर्हसि॥
en: That they did not follow you when you marched to battle at the head of your troops. They have long before come under your power by becoming your slaves. Endued as they are with courage and prowess and incapable as they are to turn back from the field of battle they are bound to help you. You are now enjoying all the rich possessions of the Pandavas; O king, see, the Pandavas are yet active. They have not resolved to die by fasting. Rise, () king, be blessed; you should not grieve.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: अवश्यमेव नृपते राज्ञो विषयवासिभिः। प्रियाण्याचरितव्यानि तत्र का परिदेवना॥
en: O lord of men, it is the certain duty of those who live in a king's dominion to do which is agreeable to that king, what is there then to be Sorry for?

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: मद्वाक्यमेतद् राजेन्द्र यद्येवं न करिष्यसि। स्थास्यामीह भवत्पादौ शुश्रूषन्नरिमर्दन॥
en: O king of kings, O chastiser of foes, if you do not act as I say, I shall then stay here and serve at your feet with all respect.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: नोत्सहे जीवितुमहं त्वविहीनो नरर्षभ। प्रायोपविष्टस्तु नृप राज्ञां हास्यो भविष्यसि॥
en: O forernost of men, O king, I do not desire to live without you. If you resolve to die by fasting, you will simply be the laughing-stock of all other kings.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Duryodhana
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्तस्तु कर्णेन राजा दुर्योधनस्तदा। नैवोत्यातुं मनश्चक्रे स्वर्गाय कृतनिश्चयः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having been thus addressed by Karna, king Duryodhana, being firmly resolved to die, determined not to rise from the place where he sat.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच प्रायोपविष्टं राजानं दुर्योधनममर्षणम्। उवाच सान्त्वयन् राजञ्छकुनिः सौबलस्तदा॥
en: Vaishampayana said : O king, seeing Duryodhana who is always incapable of putting up with an insult, seated with the determination of dying by starvation, the son of Subala, Shakuni, spoke thus.

sn: शकुनिरुवाच सम्यगुक्तं हि कर्णेन तच्छ्रुतं कौरव त्वया। मया हृतां श्रियं स्फीतां तां मोहादपहाय किम्॥ त्वमल्पबुद्ध्या नृपते प्राणानुत्स्रष्टुमर्हसि। अथवाप्यवगच्छामि न वृद्धाः सेवितास्त्वया।॥
en: Shakuni said: O descendant of Kuru, you have heard that Karna has said. His words are indeed full of wisdom. O king, why should you foolishly throw away the great prosperity that I won for you by abandoning your life today through mere silliness? It appears to me today that you never waited upon (wise) old men.

sn: यः समुत्पतितं हर्ष दैन्यं वा न नियच्छति। स नश्यति श्रियं प्राप्य पात्रमाममिवाम्भसि॥
en: Like an unburnt earthen vessel in water, he, who is incapable of controlling sudden occasions of joy or grief, is lost even if he obtains prosperity.

sn: अतिभीरुमतिक्लीबं दीर्घसूत्रं प्रमादिनम्। व्यसनाद् विषयाक्रान्तं न भजन्ति नृपं प्रजाः॥
en: The king who is entirely destitute of courage, no has no spark of manliness, who is the slave of procrastination and who is addicted to sensual pleasures is never respected by his subjects.

sn: सत्कृतस्य हि ते शोको विपरीते कथं भवेत्। मा कृत शोभनं पाथैः शोकमालम्ब्य नाशया।६।।
en: Befitted as you have been, whence is this unseasonable grief of yours? Do not undo this graceful act done by the sons of Pritha by indulging in grief.

sn: यत्र हर्षस्त्वया कार्यः सत्कर्तव्याश्च पाण्डवाः। तत्र शोचसि राजेन्द्र विपरीतमिदं तव।॥
en: O king of kings, when you should express your joy and reward the Pandavas, you are grieving. Your this behaviour is very inconsistent.

sn: प्रसीद मा त्यजात्मानं तुष्टश्च सुकृतं स्मर। प्रयच्छ राज्यं पार्थानां यशो धर्ममवाप्नुहि॥
en: Be cheerful; do not abandon your life. But with a very pleased heart think of the good work they have done to you. Give back to the sons of Pritha their kingdom and win both virtue and renown by your this act.

sn: क्रियामेतां समाज्ञाय कृतज्ञस्त्वं भविष्यसि। सौभ्रानं पाण्डवैः कृत्वा समवस्थाप्य चैव तान्॥ पित्र्यं राज्यं प्रयच्छैषां ततः सुखमवाप्स्यसि।
en: Establishing brotherly relations with the Pandavas, become their friends and make them your friends, give them back their paternal kingdom, for you will then be happy.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच शकुनेस्तु वचः श्रुत्वा दुःशासनमवेक्ष्य च।॥ पादयोः पतितं वीरं विकृतं भ्रातृसौहृदम्। बाहुभ्यां साधुजाताभ्यां दुःशासनमरिंदमम्॥ उत्थाप्य सम्परिष्वज्य प्रीत्याजिघ्नत मूर्धनि।
en: Vaishampayana said : Having heard the words of Shakuni and having seen Dushashana lying at the feet of the king (Duryodhana) unmanned by fraternal affection, the king raised Dushashana and clasping him in his well formed arms he smelt his head.

sn: कर्णसौबलयोश्चापि संश्रुत्य वचनान्यसौ॥ निर्वेदं परमं गत्वा राजा दुर्योधनस्तदा। व्रीडयाभिपरीतात्मा नैराश्यमगमत् परम्॥
en: Having heard the words of Karna and Subala's son (Shakuni), the king Duryodhana was overwhelmed with shame. He lost heart more than ever and utter despair overtook his soul.

sn: तच्छ्रुत्वा सुहृदश्चैव समन्युरिदमब्रवीत्। न धर्मधनसौख्येन नैश्चर्येण न चाज्ञया॥ नैव भोगैश्च मे कार्यं मा वहन्यत गच्छत। निश्चितेयं मम मतिः स्थिता प्रायोपवेशने॥ गच्छध्वं नगरं सर्वे पूज्याश्च गुरवो मम।
en: Having heard all that his friends said, he thus again spoke in sorrow, "I have nothing more to do with virtue, wealth, friendship, affluence, sovereignty and enjoyments. Do not oppose me; leave me all of you. I am firmly resolved to abandon my life by fasting. Go back to the city and worship all my Gurus with respect."

sn: त एवमुक्ताः प्रत्यूचू राजानमरिमर्दनम्॥ या गतिस्तव राजेन्द्र सास्माकमपि भारत। कथं वा सम्प्रवेक्ष्यामस्त्वविहीनाः पुरं वयम्॥
en: Having been thus addressed by him, they thus replied to that royal chastiser of foes, “O king of kings, O descendant of Bharata, the course that is yours is also ours. How can we enter the city without you?”

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच स सुहृद्भिरमात्यैश्च भ्रातृभिः स्वजनेन च। बहुप्रकारमप्युक्तो निश्चयान्न विचाल्यते॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Though addressed in all manner of ways by his friends and counsellors and brothers and relatives, the king waved not from his firm resolve.

sn: दर्भास्तरणमास्तीर्य निश्चयाद् धृतराष्ट्रजः। संस्पृश्यापः शुचिर्भूत्वा भूतले समुपस्थितः॥ कुशचीराम्बरधरः परं नियममास्थितः। वाग्यतो राजशार्दूलः स स्वर्गगतिकाम्यया॥ मनसोपचितिं कृत्वा निरस्य च बहिः क्रियाः।
en: In accordance with his resolve, he spread Kusha grass on the ground and purifying himself by touching water, he sat down on it. Clad in rags and Kusha grass, he engaged in observing the greatest vow. That foremost of kings, with the desire of going to heaven, stopped all speech. He began to pray and worship internally and he suspended all external intercourse.

sn: अथ तं निश्चयं तस्य बुद्ध्वा दैतेयदानवाः॥ पातालवासिनो रौद्राः पूर्वं देवैर्विनिर्जिताः। ते स्वपक्षक्षयं तं तु ज्ञात्वा दुर्योधनस्य वै॥ आह्वानाय तदा चक्रुः कर्म वैतानसम्भवम्। बृहस्पतत्युशनोक्तैश्च मन्त्रैर्मन्त्रविशारदाः॥ अथर्ववेदप्रोक्तैश्च याश्योपनिषदि क्रिया:। मन्त्रजप्यसमायुक्तास्तास्तदा समवर्तयन्॥
en: On learning his resolve, the sons of Diti and the Danavas, who live in the nether region and who were once defeated by the celestials, fearing that their party would be destroyed without Duryodhana, began a sacrifice with fire to summon him before them. Mantraknowing men then commenced with the formulae of Brihaspati and Ushana. Those rites that are indicated in the Atharvaveda and the Upanishadas and which are capable of being achieved by mantras and prayers.

sn: जुह्वत्यग्नौ हविः क्षीरं मन्त्रवत् सुसमाहिताः। ब्राह्मणा वेदवेदाङ्गपारगाः सुदृढव्रताः॥ कर्मसिद्धौ तदा तत्र जृम्भमाणा महाद्भुता। कृत्या समुत्थिता राजन् किं करोमीति चाब्रवीत्॥
en: Brahmanas of rigid vows well-versed in the Vedas and their branches began with great and deep meditation to pour libations of ghee and milk into the fire with mantras. After those rites were completed, a strange goddess, O king, rose up saying, "What shall I do?"

sn: आहुदैत्याश्च तां तत्र सुप्रीतेनान्तरात्मना। प्रायोपविष्टं राजानं धार्तराष्ट्रमिहानय॥
en: With well-pleased hearts the Daityas commanded her by saying, “Bring here the king, the son of Dhritarashtra, who is now engaged in a vow of fasting."

sn: तथेति च प्रतिश्रुत्य सा कृत्या प्रययौ तदा। निमेषादगमच्चापि यत्र राजा सुयोधनः॥
en: Thus commanded, she went away saying, "So be it.” In a moment she came to the place where the king, Duryodhana, was.

sn: समादाय च राजानं प्रविवेश रसातलम्। दानवानां मुहूर्ताच्च तमानीतं न्यवेदयत्। तमानीतं नृपं दृष्ट्वा रात्रौ संगत्य दानवाः॥ प्रहृष्टमनसः सर्वे किंचिदुत्फुल्ललोचनाः। साभिमानमिदं वाक्यं दुर्योधनमथाब्रुवन्॥
en: Taking up the king, she brought him to the nether world and within a moment she came back to the Danavas and told them (that she had brought the king). Seeing the king brought before them in their assembly in the night, the Danavas. With well-pleased hearts and with expanded eyes in delight, thus spoke these flattering words to Duryodhana.

sn: दानवा ऊचुः भोः सुयोधन राजेन्द्र भरतानां कुलोद्वह। शूरैः परिवृतो नित्यं तथैव च महात्मभिः॥
en: The Danavas said: O king of kings, O perpetuator of the Bharata race, O Duryodhana, you are always surrounded by heroes and illustrious men.

sn: अकार्षीः साहसमिदं कस्मात् प्रायोपवेशनम्। आत्मत्यागी ह्यधो याति वाच्यतां चायशस्करीम्॥
en: Why have you then taken this rash step such as this vow of starvation? Suicide always leads (a man) to hell. It becomes the subject of calumnious speech.

sn: न हि कार्यविरुद्धेषु बहुपापेषु कर्मसु। मूलघातिषु सज्जन्ते बुद्धिमन्तो भवद्विधाः॥
en: Intelligent men like you never engage in acts that are sinful and opposed to their best interests and which strike at the very root of their purposes.

sn: नियच्छैनां म.। राजन् धर्मार्थसुखनाशिनीम्। यशः प्रतापवीर्यघ्नीं शत्रूणां हर्षवर्धनीम्॥
en: O king, therefore restrain your this resolve. It is destructive of morality, profit and happiness and of fame, prowess and energy. It enhances the joy of one's enemies.

sn: श्रूयतां तु प्रभो तत्त्वं दिव्यतां चात्मनो नृप। निर्माणं च शरीरस्य ततो धैर्यमवाप्नुहि॥
en: O king, of lord, know the truth, the celestials origin of your birth and the make up of your body; and then assume patience.

sn: पुरा त्वं तपसास्माभिर्लब्धो राजन् महेश्वरात्। पूर्वकायश्च पूर्वस्ते निर्मितो वलासंचयैः॥
en: O king, in the days of yore, we obtained you from Maheshvara by ascetic austerities. The upper part of your body is wholly made of Vajra (thunder).

sn: अस्त्रैरभेद्यः शस्त्रैश्चाप्यधः कायश्च तेऽनघ। कृतः पुष्पमयो देव्या रूपतः स्त्रीमनोहरः॥
en: On sinless one, therefore it is invincible to weapons of every description. The lower part of your body, capable of captivating the female heart by its comeliness, was made of flowers by the goddess herself.

sn: एवमोश्वरसंयुक्तस्तव देहो नृपोत्तम। देव्या च राजशार्दूल दिव्यस्त्वं हि न मानुषः॥
en: O foremost of kings, thus your body was created by Ishvara himself and the goddess. Therefore, O best of kings, your origin is celestials and not human.

sn: क्षत्रियाच महावीर्या भगदत्तपुरोगमाः। दिव्यास्त्रविदुषः शूराः क्षपयिष्यन्ति ते रिपून्।॥
en: Other greatly powerful Kshatriyas headed by Bhagadatta, all learned in the celestials weapons, will kill your enemies.

sn: तदलं ते विषादेन भयं तव न विद्यते। साहाय्यार्थं च ते वीराः सम्भूता भुवि दानवाः॥
en: Therefore there is not need for you grief. You have no cause for fear. In order to help you, many heroic Danavas have been born on earth.

sn: भीष्मद्रोणकृपादींश्च प्रवेक्ष्यन्त्यपरेऽसुराः। यैराविष्टा घृणां त्यक्त्वा योत्स्यन्ते तव वैरिभिः॥
en: Other Asura will possess Bhishma, Drona and Karna and others. Possessed by the Asuras, those heroes will cast away their kindness and fight with your enemies.

sn: नैव पुत्रान् न च भ्रातृन् न पितॄन् न च बान्धवान्। नैव शिष्यान् न च ज्ञातीन् न बालान् स्थविरान् न च।। युधि सम्प्रहरिष्यन्तो मोक्ष्यन्ति कुरुसत्तम। नि:स्नेहा दानवाविष्टाः समाक्रान्तेऽन्तरात्मनि॥
en: When the Danavas will enter their heart and completely possess them flinging all affection to a distance and becoming hard-hearted, those heroes will then strike every one opposed to them without sparing sons, brothers, fathers, friends, disciples, relatives, even children and old men.

sn: प्रहरिष्यन्ति विवशा: स्नेहमुत्सृज्य दूरतः। हृष्टाः पुरुषशार्दूला: कलुषीकृतमानसाः। अविज्ञानविमूढाश्च दैवाच्च विधिनिर्मितात्॥ व्याभाषमाणाश्यान्योन्यं न मे जीवन् विमोक्ष्यसे सर्वे शस्त्रास्त्रमोक्षेण पौरुषे समवस्थिताः॥ श्लाघमानाः कुरुश्रेष्ठ करिष्यन्ति जनक्षयम्। तेऽपि पञ्च महात्मानः प्रतियोत्स्यन्ति पाण्डवाः॥
en: Blinded by ignorance and wrath and impelled by destiny which has been ordained by the creator, those foremost of men with hearts steeped in sin will. O foremost of the Kurus, depopulate the earth by hurling all kinds of weapons with great manliness and strength and always boastfully addressing one another with words such as these, “You will not escape from me today with life.” The five illustrious sons of Pandu will fight with these (heroes).

sn: वधं चैषां करिष्यन्ति दैवयुक्ता महाबलाः। दैत्यरक्षोगणाश्चैव सम्भूताः क्षत्रयोनिषु॥ योत्स्यन्ति युधि विक्रम्य शत्रुभिस्त्व पार्थिव। गदाभिर्मुसलैः शूलैः शस्त्रैरुच्चावचैस्तथा॥
en: Possessing great strength and favoured by the fate, they would bring about the destruction of all. Many Daityas and Yakshas, that have been born in the Kshatriya order, will fight with great prowess in battle with your enemies using maces, clubs, lances and various weapons.

sn: यच्च तेऽन्तर्गतं वीर भयमर्जुनसम्भवम्। तत्रापि विहितोऽस्माभिर्वधोपायोऽर्जुनस्य वै॥
en: O hero, as for the fear of Arjuna in your heart, we have already settled the means of killing Arjuna.

sn: हतस्य नरकस्यात्मा कर्णमूर्तिमुपाश्रितः। तद् वैरं संस्मरन् वीर योत्स्यते केशवार्जुनौ॥
en: The soul of the killed Naraka has assumed the form of Karna. Recollecting. O hero, his former enmity, he will kill both Keshava (Krishna) and Arjuna.

sn: स ते विक्रमशौटीरो रणे पार्थं विजेष्यति। कर्णः प्रहरतां श्रेष्ठः सर्वांश्चारीन् महारथः॥
en: That great car-warrior, that foremost of all wielders of weapons, proud of his prowess, will vanquish Arjuna in battle, as also all your enemies.

sn: ज्ञात्वैतच्छद्मना वली रक्षार्थं सव्यसाचिनः। कुण्डले कवचं चैव कर्णस्यापहरिष्यति॥
en: The wielder of thunder (Indra), knowing all this and desirous of saving Savyasachi (Arjuna), will in disguise take away from Karna his ear-rings and armour.

sn: तस्मादस्माभिरप्यत्र दैत्याः शतसहस्रशः। नियुक्ता राक्षसाश्चैव ये ते संशप्तका इति॥
en: We have therefore appointed hundreds upon hundreds and thousands upon thousand of Daityas and Rakshasas; they are known by the name of Samshaptakas.

sn: प्रख्यातास्तेऽर्जुनं वीरं हनिष्यन्ति च मा शुचः। असपत्ना त्वया हीयं भोक्तव्या वसुधा नृप॥
en: These illustrious warriors will kill the heroic Arjuna. Do not therefore grieve. O king, you will rule the whole earth without a rival.

sn: मा विषादं गमस्तस्मान्नैतत्त्वय्युपपद्यते। विनष्टे त्वयि चास्माकं पक्षो हीयेत कौरव॥
en: Do not give way to despondency. O descendant of Kuru, this conduct does not suit you. If you die, our party will become weak.

sn: गच्छ वीर न ते बुद्धिरन्या कार्या कथञ्चन। त्वमस्माकं गतिर्नित्यं देवतानां च पाण्डवाः॥
en: O hero, go, you should never direct your mind in any other course. You are our refuge.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्त्वा परिष्वज्य दैत्यास्तं राजकुञ्जरम्। समाश्वास्य च दुर्धर्षं पुत्रवद् दानवर्षभाः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having thus addressed him, the Daityas embraced that foremost of kings; and those best of the Danavas then cheered that irrepressible hero like a son.

sn: स्थिरां कृत्वा बुद्धिमस्य प्रियाण्युक्त्वा च भारत। गम्यतामित्यनुज्ञाय जयमाप्नुहि चेत्यथ॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, cheering his mind by soft speeches, they permitted him to depart saying, “Go and attain victory."

sn: तैर्विसृष्टं महाबाहुं कृत्या सैवानयत् पुनः। तमेव देशं यत्रासौ तदा प्रायमुपाविशत्॥
en: When they had given leave to the mighty armed one, (to-depart), that very goddess carried him back to the spot where he had sat down intent upon putting an end to his life.

sn: प्रतिनिक्षिप्य त वीरं कृत्या समभिपूज्य च। अनुज्ञाता च राज्ञा सा तथैवान्तरधीयत॥
en: Having set that hero down and paid him homage, the goddess vanished with the king's permission.

sn: गतायामथ तस्यां तु राजा दुर्योधनस्तदा। स्वप्नभूतमिदं सर्वमचिन्तयत भारत॥ विजेष्यामि रणे पाण्डूनिति चास्याभवन्मतिः।
en: O descendant of Bharata, when she disappeared, the king considered all this to be a dream. (He thought), “I shall defeat the Pandavas in battle."

sn: कर्ण संशप्तकांश्चैव पार्थस्यामित्रघातिनः॥ अमन्यत वधे युक्तान् समर्थांश्च सुयोधनः।
en: Duryodhana considered that Karna and the Samshaptaka army were both able to kill that chastiser of foes Partha (Arjuna).

sn: एवमाशा दृढा तस्य धार्तराष्ट्रस्य दुर्मतेः॥ विनिजये पाण्डवानामभवद् भरतर्षभ।
en: Thus was strengthened the hope of the wicked-minded son of Dhritarashtra, to conquer the Pandavas.

sn: कर्णोऽप्याविष्टचित्तात्मा नरकस्यान्तरात्मना॥ अर्जुनस्य वधे क्रूरां करोति स्म तदा मतिम्।
en: O foremost of Bharatas, Karna also, his soul and mind possessed by Naraka and influenced by the qualities of emotion and darkness, became cagerly desirous of killing Falguni (Arjuna).

sn: संशप्तकाच ते वीरा राक्षसाविष्टचेतसः॥ रजस्तमोभ्यामाक्रान्ता: फाल्गुनस्य वधैषिणः।
en: Thus those Shanshaptaka various being surrounded by monsters came under sheer infuence of Rajas and Tamas property and intedned to kill Arjuna.

sn: भीष्मद्रोणकृपाद्याश्च दानवाक्रान्तचेतसः॥ न तथा पाण्डुपुत्राणां स्नेहवन्तो विशाम्पते। न चाचचक्षे कस्मैचिदेतद् राजा सुयोधनः॥
en: Bhishma, Drona, Kripa and others, their mind possessed by the Danavas. O king, were not so affectionate towards the Pandavas as they were before. The king Suyodhana did not tell this to any one.

sn: दुर्योधनं निशान्ते च कर्णो वैकर्तनोऽब्रवीत्। स्मयन्निवाञ्जलिं कृत्वा पार्थिवं हेतुमद् वचः॥
en: At the end of the night, the son of the sun, Karna, thus smilingly spoke to Duryodhana with joined hands.

sn: न मृतो जयते शत्रूञ्जीवन् भद्राणि पश्यति। मृतस्य भद्राणि कुतः कौरवेय कुतो जयः॥
en: “No dead man can conquer his foes, it is when he is alive that he can see his good. Where is the good of the dead person and O descendant of Kuru, where is his victory?

sn: न कालोऽद्य विषादस्य भयस्य मरणस्य वा। परिष्वज्याब्रवीच्चैनं भुजाभ्यां स महाभुजः॥
en: Therefore this is no time for grief or fear or death.” Having with his arms embraced that mighty armed hero,

sn: उत्तिष्ठ राजन् किं शेषे कस्माच्छोचसि शत्रुइन्। शत्रुन् प्रताप्य वीर्येण स कथं मृत्युमिच्छसि॥
en: He further said, "O king, rise up. Why do you lie down? O slayer of foes, why do you wish to die?

sn: अथवा ते भयं जातं दृष्ट्वार्जुनपराक्रमम्। सत्यं ते प्रतिजानामि वधिष्यामि रणेऽर्जुनम्॥
en: Fear has possessed you at the sight of Arjuna. I truly promise to you that I will kill Arjuna in battle.

sn: गते त्रयोदशे वर्षे सत्येनायुधमालभे। आनयिष्याम्यहं पार्थान् वशं तव जनाधिप॥
en: O ruler of men, I swear by my weapons that when thirteen years have passed away, I will bring the sons of Pritha under your subjection."

sn: एवमुक्तस्तु कर्णेन दैत्यानां वचनात् तथा। प्रणिपातेन चाप्येषामुदतिष्ठत् सुयोधनः॥
en: Having been thus addressed by Karna and having (also) remembered the words of the Daityas and the supplications made by (his brothers), Duryodhana rose up.

sn: दैत्यानां तद् वचः श्रुत्वा हदि कृत्वा स्थिरां मतिम्। ततो मनुजशार्दूलो योजयामास वाहिनीम्॥ रथनागाश्वकलिला पदातिजनसंकुलाम्। गगौघप्रतिमा राजन् सा प्रयाता महाचमूः॥
en: Having heard the words of the Daityas, that foremost of men with a firm resolve in his heart arrayed his army full of horses, elephants, chariots and foot soldiers. O king, as it moved on like the waters of the Ganga.

sn: श्वेतच्छत्रैः पताकाभिश्चामरैश्च सुपाण्डुरैः। स्थैर्नागैः पदातैश्च शुशुभेऽतीव संकुला॥ व्यपेताभ्रघने काले द्यौरिवाव्यक्तशारदी।
en: With numerous white umbrellas and pennons and white Chamaras and chariots and elephants and foot soldiers that great army, as is moved on like the waters of the Ganga looked as beautiful as the sky at a season when the clouds have been dispersed and the signs of autumn have been but partially developed.

sn: जयाशीभिर्द्विजेन्द्रैः स स्तूयमानोऽधिराजवत्॥ गृहणन्नञ्जलिमालाश्च धार्तराष्ट्रो जनाधिपः। सुयोधनो ययावचे श्रिया परमया ज्वलन्।॥
en: O king of kings, eulogised as a monarch by the foremost of Brahmanas who all prayed for his victory, that king, Suyodhana, the son of Dhritarashtra, received honours paid to him by innumerable men) with joined hands.

sn: कर्णेन सार्धं राजेन्द्र सौबलेन च देविना। दुःशासनादयश्चास्य भ्रातरः सर्व एव ते॥ भूरिश्रवाः सोमदत्तो महाराजश्च बाह्निकः। स्थैर्नानाविधाकारैर्हयैर्गजधरैस्तथा॥ प्रयान्तं नृपसिंहं तमनुजग्मुः कुरूद्वहाः। कालेनाल्पेन राजेन्द्र स्वपुरं विविशुस्तदा॥
en: Blazing in great splendour he went in front (of the army) accompanied by Karna, Subala's son, the gambler (Shakuni), Dushashana and all his other brothers, Bhurishrava, Somadatta, the great king Bahlika followed that foremost of kings with various sorts of chariots, horses and excellent elephants. O foremost of kings, within a short time all those perpetuators of the Kuru race entered their own city.

sn: जनमेजय उवाच वसमानेषु पार्थेषु वने तस्मिन् महात्मसु। धार्तराष्ट्रा महेष्वासाः किमकुर्वत सत्तमाः॥
en: Janamejaya said : When the illustrious sons of Pritha were living in the forest, what did those foremost of men and mighty bow-men, the the sons of Dhritarashtra do?

sn: कर्णो वैकर्तनश्चैव शकुनिश्च महाबलः। भीष्मद्रोणकृपाश्चैव तन्मे शंसितुमर्हसि॥
en: What did the son of the sun, Karna and the powerful Shakuni and Bhishma, Drona and Kripa do. You should narrate all this to me.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवं गतेषु पार्थेषु विसृष्टे च सुयोधने। आगते हास्तिनपुरं मोक्षिते पाण्डुनन्दनैः॥ भीष्मोऽब्रवीन्महाराज धार्तराष्ट्रमिदं वचः।
en: Vaishampayana said : O great king, when in this manner the Pandavas had gone away leaving Duryodhana and when having been rescued by the Pandavas, he had gone to Hastinapur, Bhishma spoke thus to the son of Dhritarashtra (Duryodhana),

sn: उक्तं तात यथा पूर्वं गच्छतस्ते तपोवनम्॥ गमनं मे न रुचितं तव तत्र कृतं च ते।
en: "O child, I told you before when you intended to go to the forest of the ascetics. That I did not like your journey. But you did go notwithstanding

sn: तत: प्राप्तं त्वया वीर ग्रहणं शत्रुभिर्बलात्॥ मोक्षितश्चासि धर्मज्ञैः पाण्डवैर्न च लज्जसे।
en: O hero, you were forcibly taken captive by the enemy; you were rescued by the virtuous Pandavas, but still you were not ashamed.

sn: प्रत्यक्षं तव गान्धारे ससैन्यस्य विशाम्पते॥ सूतपुत्रोऽपयाद् भीतो गन्धर्वाणां तदा रणात्।
en: O king, O son of Gandhari, even in your presence and also in the presence of your army did the Suta's (Karna) son, struck with panic, fly away from the battle of the Gandharvas.

sn: क्रोशतस्तव राजेन्द्र ससैन्यस्य नृपात्मज॥ दृष्टस्ते विक्रमश्चैव पाण्डवानां महात्मनाम्।
en: O king of kings, O son of a king, while you with your army were crying in great distress, you saw, O mighty armed hero, the prowess of the high-souled Pandavas

sn: कर्णस्य च महाबाहो सूतपुत्रस्य दुर्मतेः॥ न चापि पादभाक् कर्णः पाण्डवानां नृपोत्तम। धनुर्वेद च शौर्ये च धर्मे वा धर्मवत्सल॥
en: And also that of the wicked-minded son of the Suta, Karna. O foremost of kings, O lover of virtue, whether in the science of arms or heroisrm or morality, Karna is not (even) the fourth part of the Pandavas.

sn: तस्मादहं क्षमं मन्ये पाण्डवैस्तैर्महात्मभिः। संधिं संधिविदां श्रेष्ठ कुलस्यास्य विवृद्धये॥
en: Therefore for the welfare of this race, peace is I think most desirable with the sons of Pandu.”

sn: एवमुक्तश्च भीष्मेण धार्तराष्ट्रो जनेश्वरः। प्रहस्य सहसा राजन् विप्रतस्थे ससौबलः॥
en: Having been thus addressed by Bhishma, that lord of men, the son of Dhritarashtra (Duryodhana) laughed aloud and he suddenly went away with the son of Subala (Shakuni).

sn: तं तु प्रस्थितमाज्ञाय कर्णदुःशासनादयः। अनुजग्मुर्महेष्वासा धार्तराष्ट्र महाबलम्॥
en: Then knowing that he was gone, those mighty bowmen with Karna and Dushasana at their head followed that mighty bowman and greatly powerful son of Dhritarashtra.

sn: तांस्तु सम्प्रस्थितान् दृष्ट्वा भीष्मः कुरुपितामहः। लज्जया वीडितो राजञ्जगाम स्वं निवेशनम्॥
en: Having seen them gone, Bhishma, the grandfather of the Kurus, bent down his head in shame. O king, he too then went away to his house,

sn: गते भीष्मे महाराज धार्तराष्ट्रो जनेश्वरः। पुनरागम्य तं देशममन्त्रयत मन्त्रिभिः॥
en: O great king, when Bhishma had gone away, that lord of men, the son of Dhritarashtra (Duryodhana) again came there and consulted with his counsellors.

sn: किमस्माकं भवेच्छ्रेयः किं कार्यमवशिष्यते। कथं च सुकृतं तत् स्यान्मन्त्रयामोऽद्य यद्धितम्॥
en: Duryodhana said : “What is good for me? What remains to be done? How can we most effectually bring about the good that we shall fix upon today?”

sn: कर्ण उवाच दुर्योधन निबोधेदं यत् त्वां वक्ष्यामि कौरव। भीष्मोऽस्मान् निन्दति सदा पाण्डवांश्च प्रशंसति॥
en: Karna said: Odescendant of Kuru, O Duryodhana, lay to your heart the words I say. Bhishma always blames us and praises the Pandavas.

sn: त्वद् द्वेषाच्च महाबाहो ममापि द्वेष्टुमर्हति। विगर्हते च मां नित्यं त्वत्समीपे नरेश्वर॥
en: O mighty-armed hero, from the illness he bears towards you, he insults me; O lord of men, in your presence he always abuses me.

sn: सोऽहं भीष्मवचस्तद् वै न मृष्यामीह भारत! त्वत्समक्षं यदुक्तं च भीष्मेणामित्रकर्षण॥ पाण्डवानां यशो राजंस्तव निन्दां च भारता अनुजानीहि मां राजन् सभृत्यबलवाहनम्॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, O chastiser of focs, I shall never bear the words that Bhishma has said as regards this matter by praising the Pandavas and censuring you. O king, join with me with your attendants, troops and chariots.

sn: जेष्यामि पृथिवीं राजन् सशैलवनकाननाम्। जिता च पाण्डवैर्भूमिश्चतुर्भिर्बलशालिभिः॥ तामहं ते विजेष्यामि एक एव न संशयः। सम्पश्यतु सुदुर्बुद्धिर्भीष्मः कुरुकुलाधमः॥
