en: O king, I shall then conquer the earth adorned with mountains, woods and forests. The earth has been conquered by the four mighty Pandavas. I shall certainly conquer it for you single-handed. Let that wretch of the Kuru race, the exceedingly wicked minded Bhishma see it.

sn: अनिन्धं निन्दते यो हि अप्रशंस्यं प्रशंसति। स पश्यतु बलं मेऽद्य आत्मानं तु विगर्हतु॥
en: He abuses those that do not deserve it and praises those that should not be praised. Let hiin today see my prowess and blame himself.

sn: अनुजानीहि मां राजन् ध्रुवो हि विजयस्तव। प्रतिजानामि ते सत्यं राजन्नायुधमालभे॥
en: O king, command me. Victory shall surely be yours. O king, I swear by my weapon.

sn: तच्छ्रुत्वा तु वचो राजन् कर्णस्य भरतर्षभ। प्रीत्या परमया युक्तः कर्णमाह नराधिपः॥
en: Vaishampayana said: O king, O foremost of the Bharata race, having heard these words of Karna, that lord of men became exceedingly delighted and he thus spoke to Karna.

sn: धन्योऽस्म्यनुगृहीतोऽस्मि यस्य मे त्वं महाबलः हितेषु वर्तसे नित्यं सफलं जन्म चाद्य मे॥
en: "I am blessed, for I have been favoured by you. When you who possess the greatest prowess are eager to look after my welfare, my life has borne fruit today.

sn: यदा च मन्यसे वीर सर्वशत्रुनिबर्हणम्। तदा निर्गच्छ भद्रं ते ह्यनुशाधि च मामिति॥
en: O hero, you desire to vanquish all my foes. Go. May good come to you. Command me what I am to do."

sn: एवमुक्तस्तदा कर्णो धार्तराष्ट्रेण धीमता। सर्वमाज्ञापयामास प्रायात्रिकमरिंदम॥
en: O chastiser of foes, having been thus addressed by the intelligent son of Dhritarashtra, Karna ordered (to be ready) all the necessaries for expedition.

sn: प्रययौ च महेष्वासो नक्षत्रे शुभदैवते। शुभे तिथौ मुहूर्ते च पूज्यमानो द्विजातिभिः॥ मङ्गलैश्च शुभैः स्नातो वाग्भिश्चापि प्रपूजितः। नादयन् रथघोषेण त्रैलोक्यं सचराचरम्॥
en: On an auspicious lunar day and at an auspicious moment and under the influence of a star presided over by an auspicious deity, that mighty bowman, having been honoured by the Brahmanas and bathed with auspicious and holy substances and also worshipped by all, started, filling with the rattle of his car the three worlds with all mobile and immobile objects.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततः कर्णो महेष्वासो बलेन महता वृतः। द्रुपदस्य पुरं रम्यं रुरोध भरतर्षभ।।।।
en: Vaishampayana said : O foremost of the Bharatas, then the great bowman Kama, surrounded by a large army, attacked the beautiful city of Drupada.

sn: युद्धेन महता चैनं चक्रे वीरं वशानुगम्। सुवर्ण रजतं चापि रत्नानि विविधानि च॥ करं च दापयामास दुपदं नृपसत्तम। तं विनिर्जित्य राजेन्द्र राजानस्तस्य येऽनुगाः॥ तान् सर्वान् वशगांश्चक्रे करं चैनानदापयत्।
en: After a great battle, he brought that hero under subjection and foremost of kings, he made Drupada pay tribute and give silver, gold and gems. O king of kings, after subduing him, he brought under his subjection all those kings to that were under him. He made them pay tribute.

sn: अथोत्तरां दिशं गत्वा वशे चक्रे नराधिपान्॥ भगदत्तं च निर्जित्य राधेयो गिरिमारुहत्। हिमवन्तं महाशैलं युध्यमानश्च शत्रुभिः॥ प्रययौ च दिशः सर्वान् नृपतीन् वशमानयत्। स हैमवतिकाञ्जित्वा करं सर्वानदापयत्॥
en: He then brought under subjection all the kings the northern country. Having vanquished Bhagadatta, the son of Rudra (Karna) ascended the great mountain Himalayas fighting all along with many foes. Going on all sides, he conquered and brought under subjection all the kings inhabiting the Himalayas and he made them pay tribute.

sn: नेपालविषये ये च राजानस्तानवाजयत्। अवतीर्य ततः शैलात् पूर्वां दिशमभिद्रुतः॥ अङ्गान् वङ्गान् कलिंगांश्च शुण्डिकान् मिथिलानथ मागधान् कर्कखण्डांश्च निवेश्य विषयेऽऽत्मनः॥ आवशीरांश्च योध्यांश्च अहिक्षत्रं च निर्जयत्। पूर्वां दिशं विनिर्जित्य वत्सभूमिं तथागमत्॥
en: Then coming down from the mountain and going towards the east, he vanquished the Angas and the Vargas and the Kalingas and the Shundika and the Mithilas and the Magadhas and the Karkakhandas and also the Avashiras, the Yodhyas and the Ahikshatras. Having conquered the eastern country, he went to Vatsabhumi.

sn: वत्सभूमिं विनिर्जित्य केवलां मृत्तिकावतीम्। मोहं पत्तनं चैव त्रिपुरी कोसलां तथा॥ एतान् सर्वान् विनिर्जित्य करमादाय सर्वशः।
en: Having then conquered Vatsabhumi, he subjugated Kevala, Mrittikavati, Mohana and Pattana, Tripuri and Kosala. He made them all pay tributes.

sn: दक्षिणां दिशमास्थाय कर्णो जित्वा महारथान्॥ रुक्मिणं दाक्षिणात्येषु योधयामास सूतजः। स युद्धं तुमुलं कृत्वा रुक्मी प्रोवाच सूतजम्॥
en: Then going towards the south, Karna vanquished many great car-warriors. In the southern country the Suta's son (Karna) fought a great battle with Rukmi. Having fought a great battle, he thus spoke to the Suta's son,

sn: प्रीतोऽस्मि तव राजेन्द्र विक्रमेण बलेन च। न ते विघ्नं करिष्यामि प्रतिज्ञां समपालयम्॥
en: "O foremost of kings, I have been pleased with your strength and prowess. I shall not do you any wrong. I have fulfilled the (Kshatriya) vow.

sn: प्रीत्या चाहं प्रयच्छामि हिरण्यं यावदिच्छसि। समेत्य रुक्मिणा कर्णः पाण्ड्यं शैलं च सोऽगमत्।।१४।
en: I shall gladly give you as many gold coins as you desire." Having met with Rukmi, Karna went to Pandya and the mountain.

sn: स केरलं रणे चैव नीलं चापि महीपतिम्। वेणुदारिसुतं चैव ये चान्ये नृपसत्तमाः॥ दक्षिणस्यां दिशि नृपान् करान् सर्वानदापयत्।
en: He then vanquished Kerala and then king Nila, the son of Venudari and other foremost of the kings living in the southern country. He made them all pay tributes.

sn: शैशुपालिं ततो गत्वा विजिग्ये सूतनन्दनः॥ पार्श्वस्थांश्चापि नृपतीन् वशे चक्रे महाबलः।
en: Then going to the son of Shishupala, the Suta's son defeated him and that greatly powerful hero then brought under subjection all the neighbouring chiefs.

sn: आवन्त्यांश्च वशे कृत्वा साम्ना च भरतर्षभ। वृष्णिभिः सह संगम्य पश्चिमामपि निर्जयत्॥
en: O foremost of Bharata race, having subjugated the Avantis and concluded peace with them and having fought with the Vrishnis, he conquered the west.

sn: वारुणी दिशमागम्य यवनान् बर्बरांस्तथा। नृपान् पश्चिमभूमिस्थान् दापयामास वैकरान्॥
en: Having then gone to the abode of Varuna, he made all the Yavana and Barbara kings pay tributes.

sn: विजित्य पृथिवीं सर्वां स पूर्वापरदक्षिणाम्। सम्लेच्छाटविकान् वीरः सपर्वतनिवासिनः॥ भद्रान् रोहितकांश्चैव आचेयान् मालवानपि। गणान् सर्वान् विनिर्जित्य नीतिकृत् प्रहसन्निव॥ शशकान् यवनांश्चैव विजिग्ये सूतनन्दनः। नग्नजित्प्रमुखांश्चैव गणाञ्जित्वा महारथान्॥ एवं स पृथिवीं सर्वां वशे कृत्वा महारथः। विजित्य पुरुषव्याघ्रो नागसाह्वयमागमत्॥
en: Having conquered the entire earth, east west, south and north, that hero single-handed conquered all the Mleccha nations, the mountaineers, the Bhadras, the Rohitakas, the Agreyas and the Malavas. Having conquered the great car-warriors headed by Nagnajita, the Suta's son brought the Shashakas and the Yavanas under his sway. Having thus conquered and subjugated the whole world, the great car-warrior, that foremost of men (Karna) came back to Hastinapur.

sn: तमागतं महेष्वासं धार्तराष्ट्रो जनाधिपः। प्रत्युद्गम्य महाराज सभ्रातृपितृबान्धवः॥ अर्चयामास विधिना कर्णमाहवशोभिनम्। आश्रावयच्च तत् कर्म प्रीयमाणो जनेश्वरः॥
en: That foremost of men, the son of Dhritarashtra, accompanied by his father and brothers came to that great bowman and duly honoured him. The king (Duryodhana) proclaimed his feat.

sn: यन्न भीष्मान्न च द्रोणान्न कृपान्न च बाह्निकात्। प्राप्तवानस्मि भद्रं ते त्वत्त: प्राप्तं मया हि तत्॥
en: Then he said to Karna, “What I have not received from Bhishma, Drona, Kripa or Balhika, I have (today) received from you. Be blessed.

sn: बहुना च किमुक्तेन शृणु कर्म वचो मम। सनाथोऽस्मि महाबाहो त्वया नाथेन सत्तम॥
en: What need is there to speak in length. O Karna, listen to my words. O mighty-armed hero, in you I have got my protector.

sn: न हि ते पाण्डवाः सर्वे कलामर्हन्ति षोडशीम्। अन्ये वा पुरुषव्याघ्र राजानोऽभ्युदितोदिताः॥
en: O foremost of men, all the Pandavas and other kings who are crowned with success cannot come to sixteenth part of you.

sn: स भवान् धृतराष्ट्रं तं गान्धारी च यशस्विनीम्। पश्य कर्ण महेष्वास अदितिं वलाभृद् यथा।॥
en: O great bowman, O Karna, look at Dhritarashtra and the illustrious Gandhari as the wielder of thunder (Indra) saw Aditi."

sn: ततो हलहलाशब्दः प्रादुरासीद् विशाम्पते। हाहाकाराश्च बहवो नगरे नागसाह्वये॥
en: O king, then rose in the city of Hastinapur a great uproar and also cries of "Oh" and "Alas".

sn: केचिदेनं प्रशंसन्ति निन्दन्ति स्म तथापरे। तूष्णीमासंस्तथा चान्ये नृपास्तत्र जनाधिप॥
en: O ruler of men, some of the people praised him, While others again remained silent.

sn: एवं विजित्य राजेन्द्र कर्णः शस्त्रभृतां वरः। सपर्वतवनाकाशां ससमुद्रां सनिष्कुटाम्॥ देशैरुच्चावचैः पूर्णा पत्तनैर्नगरैरपि। द्वीपैश्चानूपसम्पूर्णैः पृथिवीं पृथिवीपते॥ कालेन नातिदीर्पण वशे कृत्वा तु पार्थिवान्। अक्षयं धनमादाय सूतजो नृपमभ्ययात्॥
en: O foremost of kings, having thus in a very short time conquered this earth furnished with mountains and forests and skies and with ocean and fields, with high and low tracts and cities and with innumerable islands and thus having obtained inexhaustible wealth, Suta's son presented himself before the king.

sn: प्रविश्य च गृहं राजन्नभ्यन्तरमरिंदम। गान्धारीसहितं वीरो धृतराष्ट्रं ददर्श सः॥ पुत्रवच्च नरव्याघ्र पादौ जग्राह धर्मवित्। धृतराष्ट्रेण चाश्लिष्य प्रेम्णा चापि विसर्जितः॥
en: O chastiser of foes, then entering the palace, that hero saw Dhritarashtra and Gandhari. O foremost of men, that virtuous one then took hold of their feet as one of their sons. He was first embraced affectionately by Dhritarashtra and was then dismissed.

sn: तदा प्रभृति राजा च शकुनिश्चापि सौबलः। जानते निर्जितान् पार्थान् कर्णेन युधि भारत॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, from that day king Duryodhana and Shakuni, the son of Subala, thought that the sons of Pritha (the Pandavas) had already been defeated by Karna.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच जित्वा तु पृथिवीं राजन् सूतपुत्रो जनाधिप। अब्रवीत् परवीरघ्नो दुर्योधनमिदं वचः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : O king, O lord of men, that slayer of hostile heroes, the Suta's son (Karna) then spoke these words to Duryodhana.

sn: कर्ण उवाच दुर्योधन निबोधेदं यत् त्वां वक्ष्यामि कौरव। श्रुत्वा वाचं तथा सर्वं कर्तुमर्हस्यरिंदम॥ तवाद्य पृथिवी वीर नि:सपत्ना नृपोत्तम। तां पालय यथा शक्रो हतशत्रुर्महामनाः॥
en: "O descendant of Kuru, O Duryodhana, lay into your heart the words that I shall tell you. O chastiser of foes, after having heard my words, you should act accordingly. O foremost of kings, O hero, the earth has been now got rid of all our enemies. Now rule over the earth like the illustrious Indra."

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्तस्तु कर्णेन कर्णं राजाब्रवीत् पुनः। न किंचिद् दुर्लभं तस्य यस्य त्वं पुरुषर्षभ॥ सहायश्चानुरक्तश्च मदर्थं च समुद्यतः। अभिप्रायस्तु मे कश्चित् तं वै शृणु यथातथम्॥
en: Having been thus addressed by Karna, the king again thus spoke to him, “O foremost of men, nothing is unattainable to him who has you as a protector and to whom you are attached and on whose welfare you are entirely intent. Now I shall speak to you something which you should listen to.

sn: राजसूयं पाण्डवस्य दृष्ट्वा क्रतुवरं महत्। मम स्पृहा समुत्पन्ना तां सम्पादय सूतज॥
en: O Suta's son, seeing the great sacrifice Rajasuya of the Pandavas, I desire to perform the same. Fulfill my this desire."

sn: एवमुक्तस्ततः कर्णो राजानमिदमब्रवीत्। तवाद्य पृथिवीपाला वश्याः सर्वे नृपोत्तम॥ आहूयन्तां द्विजवराः सम्भाराश्च यथाविधि। सम्भ्रियन्तां कुरुश्रेष्ठ यज्ञोपकरणानि च॥
en: Having been thus addressed, Karna thus spoke to the king, “Now as all the chief monarchs of the earth have been brought under your subjection, you summon the Brahmanas, O foremost of Kurus and then duly procure the articles required for the sacrifice.

sn: ऋत्विजश्च समाहूता यथोक्ता वेदपारगाः। क्रियां कुर्वन्तु ते राजन् यथाशास्त्रमरिंदम॥
en: O king, O chastiser of foes, let Ritvijas, learned in the Vedas, celebrate your rites according to the ordinance.

sn: बन्नपानसंयुक्तः सुसमृद्धगुणान्वितः। प्रवर्ततां महायज्ञस्तवापि भरतर्षभ॥
en: O foremost of the Bharata race, let your great sacrifice also abound in meats and drink and be grand in every thing."

sn: एवमुक्तस्तु कर्णेन धार्तराष्ट्रो विशाम्पते। पुरोहितं समानाय्य वचनं चेदमब्रवीत्॥ राजसूयं क्रतुश्रेष्ठं समाप्तवरदक्षिणम्। आहर त्वं मम कृते यथान्यायं यथाक्रमम्॥
en: O king, having been thus addressed by Karna, Dhritarashtra's son summoned the priest and spoke to him him these words, “Celebrate duly and in proper order the foremost of all sacrifices the Rajasuya abounding in large Dakshinas."

sn: स एवमुक्तो नृपतिमुवाच द्विजसत्तमः। न स शक्यः क्रतुश्रेष्ठो जीवमाने युधिष्ठिरे॥ आहर्तुं कौरवश्रेष्ठ कुले तव नृपोत्तमा दीर्घायुर्जीवति च ते धृतराष्ट्र: पिता नृप।॥ अतश्चापि विरुद्धस्ते क्रतुरेष नृपोत्तम।
en: Having been thus addressed that foremost of Brahmanas spoke thus to the king, “You cannot perform that great sacrifice, so long Yudhishthira is alive. O best of the Kurus, O feremost of kings, your long-lived father Dhritarashtra is still alive. For this reason also you cannot perform it. There is.

sn: अस्ति त्वन्यन्महत् सत्रं राजसूयसमं प्रभो॥
en: O lord, another great sacrifice resembling the Rajasuya.

sn: तेन त्वं यज राजेन्द्र शृणु चेदं वचो मम। य इमे पृथिवीपालाः करदास्तव पार्थिव॥ ते करान् सम्प्रयच्छन्तु सुवर्णं च कृताकृतम्। तेन ते क्रियतामद्य लागलं नृपसत्तम॥
en: O foremost of kings, perform this sacrifice. Listen to me. All those rulers of earth, O king, who have come to your subjection will pay you tribute in pure and impure gold. O best of kings, with that gold make a (sacrificial) plough.

sn: यज्ञवाटस्य ते भूमिः कृष्यतां तेन भारत। तत्र यज्ञो नृपश्रेष्ठ प्रभूतान्नः सुसंस्कृतः॥ प्रवर्ततां यथान्यायं सर्वतो ह्यनिवारितः।
en: O descendant of Bharata, with it plough the sacrificial ground. At that spot let there commence, O foremost of kings, with due rites and without any disturbance, the sacrifice sanctified with Mantra and abounding in eatables.

sn: एष ते वैष्णवो नाम यज्ञः सत्पुरुषोचितः॥ एतेन नेष्टवान् कश्चिदृते विष्णुं पुरातनम्। राजसूयं क्रतुश्रेष्ठं स्पर्धत्येष महाक्रतुः॥
en: This sacrifice worthy to be performed by virtuous men is called Vaishnava. No person except the ancient Vishnu has ever performed it. This great sacrifice vies with that foremost of sacrifices, the Rajasuya.

sn: अस्माकं रोचते चैव श्रेयश्च तव भारत। निर्विघ्नश्च भवत्येष सफला स्यात् स्पृहा तव॥
en: It is desired by us and it is also for your good It is capable of being performed without any disturbance. Your desire also will be fulfilled.”

sn: एवमुक्तस्तु तैविप्रैर्धारिष्ट्रो महीपतिः। कर्णं च सौबलं चैव भ्रातूंश्चैवेदमब्रवीत्॥
en: Having been thus addressed by those Brahmanas, the son of Dhritarashtra, the king (Duryodhana), thus spoke to Karna, his brothers and the son of Subala (Shakuni).

sn: रोचते मे वचः कृत्स्नं ब्राह्मणानां न संशयः। रोचते यदि युष्माकं तस्मात् प्रब्रूत मा चिरम्॥
en: "The words of the Brahmanas are certainly very much liked by me. If they are liked by you, express it without delay."

sn: एवमुक्तास्तु ते सर्वे तथेत्यूचुर्नराधिपम्। संदिदेश ततो राजा व्यापारस्थान् यथाक्रमम्॥ हलस्य करणे चापि व्यादिष्टाः सर्वशिल्पिनः। यथोक्तं च नृपश्रेष्ठ कृतं सर्वं यथाक्रमम्॥
en: Having been thus addressed, they all said to the king, "So be it.” Then the king one by one appointed persons to the respective posts in the sacrifice). He desired the artizans to construct the plough. O foremost of kings, all that was commanded by the king was gradually executed.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततस्तु शिल्पिनः सर्वे अमात्यप्रवराश्च ये। विदुरश्च महाप्राज्ञो धार्तराष्ट्र न्यवेदयन्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Thereupon all the artizans, the principal counsellors and the highly wise Vidura thus spoke to Dhritarashtra's son.

sn: सज्ज क्रतुवरं राजन् प्राप्तकालं च भारत। सौवर्णं च कृतं सर्वं लागलं च महाधनम्॥
en: “O king, all the preparations for the excellent sacrifice have been made. O descendant of Bharata, the (proper) time (to perform it) has also come. The greatly valuable golden plough has also been made."

sn: एतच्छ्रुत्वा नृपश्रेष्ठो धार्तराष्ट्रो विशाम्पते। आज्ञापयामास नृपः क्रतुराजप्रवर्तनम्॥ ततः प्रववृते यज्ञः प्रभूतार्थः सुसंस्कृतः। दीक्षितश्चापि गान्धारिर्यथाशास्त्रं यथाक्रमम्॥
en: O king, having heard this, that foremost of kings, Dhritarashtra's son commanded that foremost of sacrifices to be commenced. Then commenced that sacrifice sanctified by mantras and abounding in food. The son of Gandhari was duly installed according to the ordinance.

sn: प्रहृष्टो धृतराष्ट्रश्च विदुरश्च महायशाः। भीष्मो द्रोणः कृपः कर्णो गान्धारी च यशस्विनी॥
en: Dhritarashtra, the high-souled Vidura, Bhishma, Drona, Kripa and Karna and the illustrious Gandhari all were filled with great delight.

sn: निमन्त्रणार्थं दूतांश्च प्रेषयामास शीघ्रगान्। पार्थिवानां च राजेन्द्र ब्राह्मणानां तथैव च॥
en: O king of kings, swift messengers were sent to invite the kings and the Brahmanas.

sn: ते प्रयाता यथोद्दिष्टा दूतास्त्वरितवाहनाः। तत्र कंचित् प्रयातं तु दूतं दुःशासनोऽब्रवीत्॥
en: Ascending swift cars, they went to the directions assigned to them. Then to one messenger at the point of starting thus spoke Dushashana.

sn: गच्छ द्वैतवनं शीघ्रं पाण्डवान् पापपूरुषान्। निमन्त्रय यथान्यायं विप्रांस्तस्मिन् वने तदा॥
en: "Go soon to the forest of Dvaitavana and in that forest duly invite the Brahmanas and those wicked men, the Pandavas.

sn: स गत्वा पाण्डवान् सर्वानुवाचाभिप्रणम्य च। दुर्योधनो महाराज यजते नृपसत्तमः॥ स्ववीयर्जितमर्थौघमवाप्य कुरुसत्तमः। तत्र गच्छन्ति राजानो ब्राह्मणाश्च ततस्ततः॥
en: Thereupon he went there and bowing down his head to all the Pandavas said "O great king, the foremost of kings that Veda of the Kurus, Duryodhana is performing a sacrifice after having acquired immense wealth by his own prowess. Brahmanas from all quarters are going to it.

sn: अहं तु प्रेषितो राजन् कौरवेण महात्मना। आमन्त्रयति वो राजा धार्तराष्ट्रो जनेश्वरः॥ मनोऽभिलषितं राज्ञस्तं क्रतुं द्रष्टुमर्हथ।
en: "O king, I have been sent here by that illustrious Kuru king, the lord of men Dhritarashtra's son to invite you. You should therefore see that charming sacrifice of that king."

sn: ततो युधिष्ठिरो राजा तच्छ्रुत्वा दूतभाषितम्॥ अब्रवीनृपशार्दूलो दिष्ट्या राजा सुयोधनः। यजते क्रतुमुख्येन पूर्वेषां कीर्तिवर्धनः॥
en: Having heard the words of the messenger that foremost of monarchs king Yudhishthira, thus spoke to him, “By good fortune, king Duryodhana, that enhancer of his forefather's glory, is performing this foremost of sacrifices.

sn: वयमप्युपयास्यामो न त्विदानी कथंचन। समयः परिपाल्यो नो यावद् वर्षं त्रयोदशम्॥
en: We shall certainly go there, but we cannot do now. We shall have to live in the forest for thirteen years according to our pledge.”

sn: श्रुत्वैतद् धर्मराजस्य भीमो वचनमब्रवीत्। तदा तु नृपतिर्गन्ता धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः॥ अस्त्रशस्त्रप्रदीप्तेऽग्नौ यदा तं पातयिष्यति। वर्षात् त्रयोदशादूर्ध्वं रणसत्रे नराधिपः॥ यदा क्रोधहविर्मोक्ता धार्तराष्ट्रेषु पाण्डवः। आगन्ताहं तदास्मीति वाच्यस्ते स सुयोधनः॥
en: Hearing the words of Dharmaraja (Yudhishthira) Bhima thus spoke, "the king Dharmaraja Yudhishthira will then go when he will put him (Duryodhana) into the fire kindled by weapon. Speaks these words to Duryodhana “when at the end of the thirteenth year that lord of men, the Pandavas, will in the sacrifice of battle pour upon the sons of Dhritarashtra, the Ghee of his anger, then will I come.”

sn: शेषास्तु पाण्डवा राजन् नैवोचुः किंचिदप्रियम्। दूतश्चापि यथावृत्तं धार्तराष्ट्र न्यवेदयत्॥
en: O king, the other Pandavas did not say anything unpleasant. The messenger on his return told everything to Dhritarashtra's son.

sn: अथाजग्मुर्नरश्रेष्ठा नानाजनपदेश्वराः। ब्राह्मणाश्च महाभाग धार्तराष्ट्रपुरं प्रति॥
en: Then there came to the city of Dhritarashtra many foremost of men, the rulers of various countries and also many highly virtuous Brahmanas.

sn: ते त्वर्चिता यथाशास्त्रं यथाविधि यथाक्रमम्। मुदा परमया युक्ताः प्रीताश्चापि नरेश्वराः॥
en: Duly received in accordance the ordinance, these lords of men felt much delight and they were all well-pleased. to

sn: धृतराष्ट्रोऽपि राजेन्द्र संवृतः सर्वकौरवैः। हर्षेण महता युक्तो विदुरं प्रत्यभाषत॥
en: O king of kings that foremost of kings, Dhritarashtra, surrounded by all the Kurus felt the greatest joy and he thus spoke to Vidura.,

sn: यथा सुखी जनः सर्व: क्षत्तः स्यादन्नसंयुतः। तुष्येत् तु यज्ञसदने तथा क्षिप्रं विधीयताम्॥
en: "O Khatva, soon act thus that all men present in this sacrifice may with food served to them be refreshed and satisfied.

sn: विदुरस्तु तदाज्ञाय सर्ववर्णानरिंदम। यथा प्रमाणतो विद्वान् पूजयामास धर्मवित्॥ भक्ष्यपेयान्नपानेन माल्यैश्चापि सुगन्धिभिः। वासोभिर्विविधैश्चैव योजयामास हृष्टवत्॥
en: Then the learned and the virtuous Vidura cheerfully entertained all the orders of men with foods and drinks and also with fragrant garland and various kinds of dresses.

sn: कृत्वा ह्यावसथान् वीरो यथाशास्त्रं यथाक्रमम्। सान्त्वयित्वा च राजेन्द्रो दत्त्वा च विविधं वसु।॥ विसर्जयामास नृपान् ब्राह्मणांश्च सहस्रशः। विसृज्य च नृपान् सर्वान् भ्रातृभिः परिवारितः॥ विवेश हास्तिनपुरं सहितः कर्णसौबलैः॥
en: Having built many pavilions that hero and the foremost of kings, duly entertained the monarchs and the Brahmanas by thousands. He bestowed upon them wealth of various kinds and then bade them farewell. having dismissed all the kings, surrounded by his brothers. He (Duryodhana) entered Hastinapur in company with Karna and Subala's son (Shakuni).

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच प्रविशन्तं महाराज सूतास्तुष्टुवुरच्युतम्। जनाश्चापि महेष्वासं तुष्टुवू राजसत्तम॥
en: Vaishampayana said: O great king, when he (Duryodhana) was entering (the city) the bards and penegyrists eulogised that undeteriorating one. Other people also eulogised that great bow man, that foreinost of kings.

sn: लाजैश्चन्दनचूर्णैश्च विकीर्य च जनास्ततः। ऊचुर्दिष्ट्या नृपाविघ्नः समाप्तोऽयं क्रतुस्तव॥
en: Sprinkling over him fried paddy and sandal paste; the people said “By good luck, O king, your sacrifice has been completed without obstruction.

sn: अपरे त्वब्रुवंस्तत्र वातिकास्तं महीपतिम्। युधिष्ठिरस्य यज्ञेन न समो ह्येष ते क्रतुः॥
en: Some who were present and who were not very careful in their speech said to that lord of earth, “Surely this sacrifice cannot be compared with that of Yudhishthira.

sn: नैव तस्य क्रतोरेष कलामर्हति षोडशीम्। एवं तत्रानुवन् केचिद् वातिकास्तं जनेश्वरम्॥
en: It does not come to the sixteenth part of that (sacrifice); thus spoke to that king some that were reckless in their speech.

sn: सुहृदस्त्वब्रुवंस्तत्र अति सर्वानयं क्रतुः। ययातिनहुषश्चापि मान्धाता भरतस्तथा॥ क्रतुमेनं समाहत्य पूताः सर्वे दिवं गताः।
en: His friends said, “your this sacrifice has surpassed all others. Yayati, Nahusa, Mandhata and Bharata having been sanctified by performing such a sacrifice have all gone to heaven”.

sn: एता वाचः शुभाः शृण्वन् सुहृदां भरतर्षभ॥ प्रविवेश पुरं हृष्टः स्ववेश्म च नराधिपः।
en: O foremost of the Bharatas, hearing such pleasing words from the friends, that ruler of men (Duryodhana) cheerfully entered the city and his iron palace.

sn: अभिवाद्य ततः पादौ मातापित्रोविशाम्पते।॥ भीष्मद्रोणकृपादीनां विदुरस्य च धीमतः। अभिवादितः कनीयोभिर्धातृभिर्धातनन्दनः॥
en: O king, then worshipping the feet of his father and mother and others headed by Bhishma, Drona and the wise Vidura and being worshipped also by his younger brothers.

sn: निषसादासने मुख्य भ्रातृभिः परिवारितः। तमुत्थाय पहाराजं सूतपुत्रोऽब्रवीद् वचः॥
en: He sat on an excellent seat surrounded by all his brothers. Then O great king, Suta's son (Karna) rose and thus spoke to him.

sn: दिष्ट्या ते भरतश्रेष्ठ समाप्तोऽयं महाक्रतुः। हतेषु युधि पार्थेषु राजसूये तथा त्वया॥ आहतेऽहं नरश्रेष्ठ त्वां सभाजयिता पुनः।
en: “O foremost of the Bharata race, by good luck you have completed the great sacrifice. When the Pandavas will be killed in battle and when you will thus complete Rajasuya sacrifice, then at that time again I shall thus honour you."

sn: तमब्रवीन्महाराजो धार्तराष्ट्रो महायशाः॥ सत्यमेतत् त्वयोक्तं हि पाण्डवेषु दुरात्मसु। निहतेषु नरश्रेष्ठ प्राप्ते चापि महाक्रतौ॥ राजसूये पुनर्वीर त्वमेवं वर्धयिष्यसि।
en: The greatly illustrious son of Dhritarashtra, that great king (Duryodhana) thus spoke to him, "Truly has this been said by you. When, O foremost of men, the wicked-minded Pandavas have been killed and when the great Rajasuya has been performed by me, then O hero, you shall again thus honour me."

sn: एवमुक्त्वा महाराज कर्णमाश्लिष्य भारत।॥ राजसूयं क्रतुश्रेष्ठं चिन्तयामास कौरवः।
en: O great king, O descendant of Bharata, having said this, he embraced Karna. That Kuru prince then began to think of that foremost of sacrifices Rajasuya.

sn: सोऽब्रवीत् कौरवांश्चापि पार्श्वस्थान् नृपसत्तमः॥ कदा तु तं क्रतुवरं राजसूयं महाधनम्। निहत्य पाण्डवान् सर्वानाहरिष्यामि कौरवाः॥
en: That best of kings then thus spoke to the Kurus who were near him. O Kurus, when shall I celebrate that costly and foremost of sacrifices Rajasuya after having killed all the Pandavas?

sn: तमब्रवीत् तदा कर्णः शृणु मे राजकुञ्जर। पादौ न धावये तावद् यावन्न निहतोऽर्जुनः॥ कीलालजं न खादेयं करिष्ये चासुरव्रतम्। नास्तीति नैव वक्ष्यामि याचितो येन केनचित्॥
en: Thereupon Karna said to the king, "O foremost of kings, hear what I say? As long I sons do not kill Arjuna, so long I shall not wash my feet. Nor shall I taste meat. I shall observe the Asura vow. Whoever will ask from me any thing, I shall never say “I have it not.”

sn: अथोत्क्रुष्टं महेष्वासैर्धार्तराष्ट्रैर्महारथैः। प्रतिज्ञाते फाल्गुनस्य वधे कर्णेन संयुगे॥
en: When Karna had thus vowed to kill Arjuna in battle those mighty car-warriors and bowmen, the sons of Dhritarashtra, sent up a loud shout.

sn: विजितांश्चाप्यमन्यन्त पाण्डवान् धृतराष्ट्रजाः। दुर्योधनोऽपि राजेन्द्र विसृज्य नरपुङ्गवान्॥ प्रविवेश गृहं श्रीमान् यथा चैत्ररथं प्रभुः। तेऽपि सर्वे महेष्वासा जग्मुर्वेश्मानि भारत॥
en: Dhritarashtra's thought that the Pandavas were already killed. O king of kings, Duryodhana, then leaving those foremost of men, that handsome one entered his house as Kubera the lord' enters the garden of Chitraratha. O descendant of Bharata, those great bow-men also went to their own houses.

sn: पाण्डवाश्च महेष्वासा दूतवाक्यप्रचोदिताः। चिन्तयन्तस्तमेवार्थं नालभन्त सुखं क्वचित्॥
en: (Meanwhile) those great bowmen, the Pandavas, moved by the words of the messenger, became anxious and they did not experience the least happiness.

sn: भूयश्च चारै राजेन्द्र प्रवृत्तिरुपपादिता। प्रतिज्ञा सूतपुत्रस्य विजयस्य वधं प्रति॥
en: O king of kings, the news had been brought to him by spies that the Suta's son (Karna) had aken the vow to kill Vijaya (Arjuna).

sn: एतच्छ्रुत्वा धर्मसुतः समुद्विग्नो नराधिप। अभेद्यकवचं मत्वा कर्णमद्भुतविक्रमम्॥ अनुस्मरंश्च संक्लेशान् न शान्तिमुपयाति सः।
en: O ruler of men, having heard this the son of Dharma (Yudhishthira) became filled with great anxiety; thinking of the impenetrable armour of the greatly powerful Karna. Remembering all their misery, he felt no peace of mind.

sn: तस्य चिन्तापरीतस्य बुद्धिर्जज्ञे महात्मनः॥ बहुव्यालमृगाकीर्णं त्यक्तुं द्वैतवनं वनम्।
en: That high-souled hero, filled with anxiety, made up his mind to abandon the forest of Dvaitavana abounding in wild animals.

sn: धार्तराष्ट्रोऽपि नृपतिः प्रशशास वसुन्धराम्॥ भ्रातृभिः सहितो वीरैर्भीष्मद्रोणकृपैस्तथा। सङ्गम्य सूतपुत्रेण कर्णेनाहवशोभिना॥
en: The king, the son of Dhritarashtra, meanwhile began to rule the earth, along with his heroic brothers as also with Bhishma, Drona and Kripa. With the assistance of the Suta's son crowned with martial glory.

sn: दुर्योधन: प्रिये नित्यं वर्तमानो महीभृताम्। पूजयामास विप्रेन्द्रान् क्रतुभिर्भूरिदक्षिणैः॥
en: Duryodhana remained ever intent on the welfare of the ruler of earth. He worshipped the foremost of Brahmanas by celebrating sacrifices with large Dakshinas.

sn: भ्रातृणां च प्रियं राजन् स चकार परंतपः। निश्चित्य मनसा वीरो दत्तभुक्तफलं धनम्॥
en: O king, that hero, that chastiser of foes was engaged in doing good to his brothers, concluding in his mind that giving and enjoying are the only (proper) uses of the wealth.

sn: जनमेजय उवाच दुर्योधनं मोक्षयित्वा पाण्डुपुत्रा महाबलाः। किमकार्षुर्वने तस्मिंस्तन्ममाख्यातुमर्हसि॥
en: Janamejaya said : After having rescued Duryodhana, what did the mighty Pandavas do in that forest? You should tell me all this.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततः शयानं कौन्तेयं रात्रौ द्वैतवने मृगाः। स्वप्नान्ते दर्शयामासुर्वाष्पकण्ठा युधिष्ठिरम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : One day, when Yudhishthira was sleeping at night in the Dvaitavana, some deer with accents choked in tears appeared before him in his dreams.

sn: भवतो भ्रातरः शूराः तानब्रवीत् स राजेन्द्रो वेपमानान् कृताञ्जलीन्। ब्रूत यद् वक्तु कामाः स्थ के भवन्तः किमिष्यते॥
en: To them standing with joined hands, their bodies trembling all over, that foremost of kings said, “Tell me what you wish to say. Who are you and what do you desire."

sn: एवमुक्ताः पाण्डवेन कौन्तेयेन यशस्विना। प्रत्यब्रुवन् मृगास्तत्र हतशेषा युधिष्ठिरम्॥
en: Having been thus addressed by the son of Kunti, the illustrious Pandava (Yudhishthira), those deer, the remaining ones of the herd that had been slaughtered, thus spoke to him,

sn: वयं मृगा द्वैतवने हतशिष्टास्तु भारत। नोत्सीदेम महाराज क्रियतां वासपर्ययः॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, we are deer of Dvaitvana, those that are alive after the rest has been slaughtered. We shall completely be exterminated. Therefore change your abode (from this forest to some other).

sn: सर्व एवास्त्रकोविदाः। कुलान्यल्पावशिष्टानि कृतवन्तो वनौकसाम्॥
en: Your brothers are all heroes, learned in weapons. They have thinned the dwellers of the forest (animals).

sn: बीजभूता वयं केचिदविशष्टा महामते। विवर्धेमहि राजेन्द्र प्रसादात् ते युधिष्ठिर।॥
en: O high-minded one, O Yudhishthira, we few only remain as seed. O king of kings, through your favour let us multiply.

sn: तान् वेपमानान् वित्रस्तान् बीजमात्रावशेषितान्। मृगान् दृष्ट्वा सुदुःखार्तो धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Seeing those deer which remained like seed after the rest had been destroyed, trembling and afflicted with fear, Dharamaraja (Yudhishthira) was greatly affected with grief.

sn: तांस्तथेत्यब्रवीद् राजा सर्वभूतहिते रतः। यथा भवन्तो ब्रुवते करिष्यामि च तत् तथा॥
en: The king, ever intent on the welfare of all creatures, said to them "So be it”. I shall act as you say.

sn: इत्येवं प्रतिबुद्धः स रात्र्यन्ते राजसत्तमः। अब्रवीत् सहितान् भ्रातॄन् दयापन्नो मृगान् प्रति॥ ते उक्तो रात्रौ मृगैरस्मि स्वप्नान्ते हतशेषितैः। तन्तुभूताः स्म भद्रं ते दया नः क्रियतामिति॥
en: Awakening after the dream that foremost of kings, moved by pity towards the deer, thus spoke to his brothers assembled there. "Those deer that are still alive after the rest have been slaughtered all appeared before me last night and said "we remain as the seed of our species. Be blessed. Have compassion on us."

sn: सत्यमाहुः कर्तव्या दयास्माभिर्वनौकसाम्। साष्टमासं हि नो वर्षं यदेतदुपयुक्ष्महे॥
en: They spoke truly. We ought to have compassion for the dwellers of the forest (animals). We have been feeding on them for one year and eight months.

sn: पुनर्बहुमृगं रम्यं काम्यकं काननोत्तमम्। मरुभूमेः शिरःस्थानं तृणबिन्दुसरः प्रति॥ तत्रेमां वसतिं शिष्टां विहरन्तो रमेमहि।
en: Therefore let us again go to the charming forest of Kamyaka, that foremost of forests abounding in wild animals, situated at the head of the desert near the lake Trinabindu. Let us there pleasantly pass the rest of our time."

sn: ततस्ते पाण्डवाः शीघ्रं प्रययुर्धर्मकोविदाः॥ ब्राह्मणैः सहिता राजन् ये च तत्र सहोषिताः। इन्द्रसेनादिभिश्चैव प्रेष्यैरनुगतास्तदा।॥
en: Then the Pandavas learned in Dharma soon went away (from the Dvaitavana). O king, with the Brahmanas and all those that lived with them. They were followed by Indrasena and other servants.

sn: ते यात्वानुसृतैर्मार्ग: स्वनैः शुचिजलान्वितैः। ददृशुः काम्यकं पुण्यमाश्रमं तापसायुतम्॥
en: Proceeding along the road furnished with excellent corn and clear water they at last saw the sacred hermitage of Kamyaka.

sn: विविशुस्ते स्म कौरव्या वृता विप्रर्षभैस्तदा। तद् वनं भरतश्रेष्ठाः स्वर्ग सुकृतिनो यथा॥
en: As virtuous men enter the celestials regions, those foremost of the Bharata race, those descendants of Kuru, surrounded by the excellent Brahmanas, entered that forest.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच वने निवसतां तेषां पाण्डवानां महात्मनाम्। वर्षाग्येकादशातीयुः कृच्छ्रेण भरतर्षभ॥
en: Vaishampayana said : O best of the Bharata race, thus living in the forest, the high-souled Pandavas spent eleven years in great misery.

sn: फलमूलाशनास्ते हि सुखाहाँ दुःखमुत्तमम्। प्राप्तकालमनुध्यान्तः सेहिरे वरपूरुषाः॥
en: Although deserving of happiness, those best of men, brooding over their miserable plight, passed their days in misery living on fruits and roots.

sn: युधिष्ठिरस्तु राजर्षिरात्मकर्मापराधजम्। चिन्तयन् स महाबाहुर्धातृणां दुःखमुत्तमम्॥ न सुष्वाप सुखं राजा हृदि शल्यैरिवार्पितैः। दौरात्म्यमनुपश्यंस्तत् काले द्यूतोद्भवस्य हि॥
en: That royal sage, the illustrious Yudhishthira, reflecting that the extremity of misery which had befallen his brothers was owing to his own fault and remembering also the sufferings that had arisen from his act of gambling, could not sleep in peace. He felt as if his heart had been pierced with a lance.

sn: संस्मरन् परुषा वाचः सूतपुत्रस्य पाण्डवः। निःश्वासपरमो दीनो बिभ्रत् कोपविषं महत्॥
en: Remembering the harsh words of the Suta's son, the Pandava, repressing the venom of his wrath passed his days in humble guise and he often sighed heavily.

sn: अर्जुनो यमजौ चोभौ द्रौपदी च यशस्विनी। स च भीमो महातेजाः सर्वेषामुत्तमो बली॥ युधिष्ठिरमुदीक्षन्तः सेहुर्दुःखमनुत्तमम्।
en: Arjuna and both the twins and the illustrious Draupadi and the mighty Bhima, he that was strongest of all men, felt the greatest pain in casting their eyes on Yudhishthira.

sn: अवशिष्टमल्पकालं मन्वानाः पुरुषर्षभाः॥ वपुरन्यदिवाकार्षुरुत्साहामर्षचेष्टितैः।
en: Thinking that only a short time remained (of their exile) those foremost of men, influenced by rage and hope and by resorting to various exertions and endeavours made their bodies assume almost different shapes.

sn: कस्यचित् त्वथ कालस्य व्यासः सत्यवतीसुतः॥ आजगाम महायोगी पाण्डवानवलोककः। तमागतमभिप्रेक्ष्य कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः॥ प्रत्युद्गम्य महात्मानं प्रत्यगृह्णाद् यथाविधि।
en: After a while the son of Satyavati, Vyasa, the great Yogi came there to see the Pandavas. Seeing him coming, the son of Kunti, Yudhishthira, went forward and duly received that high-souled one.

sn: तमासीनमुपासीनः शुश्रूषुर्नियतेन्द्रियः॥ तोषयन् प्रणिपातेन व्यासं पाण्डवनन्दनः।
en: Having gratified Vyasa by bowing down to him, the self-controlled Pandava (Yudhishthira), when the Rishi sat down, sat down before him with the desire of listening to him.

sn: तानवेक्ष्य कृशान् पौत्रान् वने वन्येन जीवतः॥ महर्षिरनुकम्पार्थमब्रवीद्वाष्पगद्गदम्।
en: Seeing his grandson lean and living on forest produce, that great Rishi, moved by compassion spoke thus in accents choked with tears.

sn: युधिष्ठिर महाबाहो शृणु धर्मभृतां वर॥ नातप्ततपसो लोके प्राप्नुवन्ति महासुखम्। सुखदुःखे हि पुरुषः पर्यायेणोपसेवते॥
en: "O mighty armed Yudhishthira, O foremost of all virtuous men, lear; those men who do not perform asceticism never obtain great happiness in this world; men experience happiness and misery by turn.

sn: न ह्यनन्तं सुखं कश्चित् प्राप्नोति पुरुषर्षभ। प्रज्ञावांस्त्वेव पुरुषः संयुक्तः परया धिया॥ उदयास्तमनज्ञो हि न हृष्यति न शोचति।
en: O foremost of the Bharatas, no man ever enjoys unmixed happiness. A wise man, possessing high wisdom, knowing that life has its ups and downs, is neither filled with joy nor with grief.

sn: सुखमापतितं सेवेद् दुःखमापतितं वहेत्॥ कालप्राप्तमुपासीत सस्यानामिव कर्षकः।
en: When happiness comes one should enjoy it and when misery comes one should bear it. As a sower of crops must wait for the (proper) season (to gather his crops).

sn: तपसो हि परं नास्ति तपसा विन्दते महत्॥ नासाध्यं तपस: किंचिदिति बुद्ध्यस्व भारत।
en: There is nothing superior to asceticism. Asceticism produces great results. descendant of Bharata, know that there is nothing which asceticism cannot produce.

sn: सत्यमार्जवमक्रोधः संविभागो दमः शमः।।१७। अनसूयाविहिंसा च शौचमिन्द्रियसंयमः। पावनानि महाराज नराणां पुण्यकर्मणाम्॥
en: Truth, sincerity, freedom from anger, justice, self-control, restraint of faculties, immunity from malice, guilelessness, sanctity and mortification of the senses, these, O great king, purify a man of pure acts.

sn: अधर्मरुचयो मूढास्तिर्यग्गतिपरायणाः। कृच्छ्रां योनिमनुप्राप्ता न सुखं विन्दते जनाः॥
en: Foolish persons, addicted to vice and bestial ways, obtain the birth of beasts in after life and they never enjoy happiness.

sn: इह यत् क्रियते कर्म तत् परत्रोपयुज्यते। तस्माच्छरीरं युञ्जीत तपसा नियमेन च॥
en: The fruits of acts done in this world are obtained in the next world. Therefore one restrains his body by asceticism and the observance of vows.

sn: यथाशक्ति प्रयच्छेत सम्पूज्याभिप्रणम्य च। काले प्राप्ते च हृष्टात्मा राजन् विगतमत्सरः॥
en: O king, being free from guile and with a cheerful spirit, one, according to his power, bestows gifts after bowing down to the recipient and paying him homage.

sn: सत्यवादी लभेतायुरनायासमथार्जवम्। अक्रोधनोऽनसूयश्च निर्वृतिं लभते पराम्॥ दान्तः शमपरः शश्वत् परिक्लेशं न विन्दति। न च तप्यति दान्तात्मा दृष्ट्वा परगतां श्रियम्॥
en: A truthful man obtains a life which is free from all trouble. A person, free from anger, attains to sincerity and one free from malice obtains supreme contentments. A man who has subdued his senses and his inner faculties never knows tribulation, nor is a person of subdued senses affected by sorrow at the sight of other's prosperity.

sn: संविभक्ता च दाता च भोगवान् सुखवान् नरः। भवत्यहिंसकश्चैव परमारोग्यमश्नुते॥
en: A man who gives every one his due and he who gives boons obtains happiness and every object of enjoyment, while a man who is free from envy reaps perfect ease.

sn: मान्यमानयिता जन्म कुले महति विन्दति। व्यसनैर्न त संयोगं प्राप्नोति विजितेन्द्रियः॥
en: He who honours those to whom honour is due obtains birth in an illustrious family and he who has subdued his senses never mects with any misfortune.

sn: शुभानुशयबुद्धिर्हि संयुक्तः कालधर्मणा। प्रादुर्भवति तद्योगात् कल्याणमतिरेव सः॥
en: A man whose mind follows good after death is born on that account possessing a virtuous mind.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच भगवन् दानधर्माणां तपसो वा महामुने। किंस्विद् बहुगुणं प्रेत्य किं वा दुष्करमुच्यते॥
en: Yudhishthira said : O great Rishi, O exalted one, of the bestowal of gifts and asceticism which is of greater efficacy in the next world and which is more difficult to be practised.

sn: व्यास उवाच दानान्न दुष्करं तात पृथिव्यामस्ति किंचन। अर्थ च महती तृष्णा स च दुःखेन लभ्यते॥
en: Vyasa said : O child, there is nothing in this world more difficult to practise than charity. Men thirst for wealth and obtain it with great difficulty.

sn: परित्यज्य प्रियान् प्राणान् धनार्थं हि महामते। प्रविशन्ति नरा वीराः समुद्रमटवीं तथा॥
en: O high-minded one, even abandoning (the hope of) dear life itself, heroic men enter into the depths of the sea and the forest for wealth.

sn: कृषिगोरक्ष्यमित्येके प्रतिपद्यन्ति मानवाः। पुरुषाः प्रेष्यतामेके निर्गच्छन्ति धनार्थिनः॥
en: For wealth some take to agriculture, some to the tending of the kine and some serve others. Therefore it is extremely difficult to part with wealth which is obtained with such great difficulty.

sn: तस्माद् दुःखार्जितस्यैव परित्यागः सुदुष्करः। न दुष्करतरं दानात् तस्माद् दानं मतं मम॥
en: As there is nothing harder to practise than charity, in my opinion, even bestowal of boons is superior to every thing.

sn: विशेषस्त्वत्र विज्ञेयो न्यायेनोपार्जितं धनम्। पात्रे काले च देशे च साधुभ्यः प्रतिपादयेत्॥
en: Specially this is to be remembered that wellgotten gains should in proper time and place be given away to pious men.

sn: अन्यायात् समुपात्तेन दानधर्मो धनेन यः। क्रियते न स कर्तारं त्रायते महतो भयात्॥
en: But the bestowal of ill-gotten wealth can never rescue the giver from the great fear (of the evil of rebirth).

sn: पात्रे दानं स्वल्पमपि काले दत्तं युधिष्ठिर। मनसा हि विशुद्धेन प्रेत्यानन्तफलं स्मृतम्॥ अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। व्रीहिद्रोणपरित्यागाद् यत् फलं प्राप मुद्गलः॥
en: O Yudhishthira, it has been said that by bestowing in a pure spirit even a slight gift in due time and to a fit recipient a man obtains inexhaustible fruits in the next world. In this connection a story is told about the fruit obtained by Mudgala by giving away only a Drona of corn.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच व्रीहिद्रोणः परित्यक्तः कथं तेन महात्मना। कस्मै दत्तश्च भगवन् विधिना केन चास्थ मे॥
en: Yudhisthira said: O exalted one, why did that highsouled one give away a Drona of corn? To whom and in what prescribed way he gave it. Tell me this.

sn: प्रत्यक्षधर्मा भगवान् यस्य तुष्टो हि कर्मभिः। सफलं तस्य जन्माहं मन्ये सद्धर्मचारिणः॥
en: O exalted one, I consider the life of that virtuous man as having borne fruits with whose acts the supreme one himself is well-pleased.

sn: व्यास उवाच शिलोच्छवृत्तिर्धर्मात्मा मुद्गलः संयतेन्द्रियः। आसीद् राजन् कुरुक्षेत्रे सत्यवागनसूयकः॥
en: Vyasa said : O king, there lived in Kurukshetra a virtuous man, named Mudgala. He was truthful and free from malice. He was self-controlled. He led the Sila and Uncha modes of life.

sn: अतिथिव्रती क्रियावांश्च कापोती वृत्तिमास्थितः। सत्रमिष्टीकृतं नाम समुपास्ते महातपाः॥ सपुत्रदारो हि मुनिः पक्षाहारो बभूव ह। कपोतवृत्त्या पक्षण व्रीहिद्रोणमुपार्जयत्॥
en: Although leading his life like a pigeon that great ascetic entertained his guests, celebrated the sacrefice called Ishtikhita and performed other rites. That Rishi, with his wife and son, ate for a fortnight and during the other fortnight he led the life of a pigeon collecting (but) a drona of corn.

sn: दर्श च पौर्णमासं च कुर्वन् विगतमत्सरः। देवतातिथिशेषेण कुरुते देहयापनम्॥
en: Celebrating the Darsa and Paurnamashya sacrifices that guileless Rishi used to pass his days by taking the food that remained after the deities and the guests had eaten.

sn: तस्येन्द्रः सहितो देवैः साक्षात् त्रिभुवनेश्वरः। प्रत्यगृह्णान्महाराज भागं पर्वणि पर्वणि॥
en: In (all) auspicious lunar days, the lord of the three worlds, Indra accompained by the celestials, O great king, used to partake the food offered at his sacrifice.

sn: स पर्वकालं कृत्वा तु मुनिवृत्त्या समन्वितः। अतिथिभ्यो ददावनं प्रहृष्टेनान्तरात्मना॥
en: On such (auspicious) days that Rishi leading the life of a Muni cheerfully entertained his guests also with food.

sn: व्रीहिद्रोणस्य तद्ध्यस्य ददतोऽन्नं महात्मनः। शिष्टं मात्सर्यहीनस्य वर्धतेऽतिथिदर्शनात्॥
en: As that high-souled one distributed his food with great speed, the reaminder of the Drona of corn increased as soon as (fresh) guests appeared.

sn: तच्छतान्यपि भुञ्जन्ति ब्राह्मणानां मनीषिणाम्। मुनेस्त्यागविशुद्ध्या तु तदन्नं वृद्धिमृच्छति॥
en: By virtue of the pure spirit in which the Rishi gave away (food), it increased so much that hundreds upon hundreds of leanred Brahmanas were fed with it.

sn: तं तु शुश्राव धर्मिष्ठं मुद्गलं संशितव्रतम्। दुर्वासा नृप दिग्वासास्तमथाभ्याजगाम ह॥ बिभ्रच्चानियतं वेषमुन्मत्त इव पाण्डव। विकचः परुषा वाचो व्याहरन् विविधा मुनिः॥
en: O king (once upon a time) having heard of the virtuous and bow-observing Mudgala, the naked Rishi Durvasa, with his dress like that of a maniac and his head bare of hair, came there, O Pandava, uttering various insulting words.

sn: अभिगम्याथ तं विप्रमुवाच मुनिसत्तमः। अन्नार्थिनमनुप्राप्तं विद्धि मां द्विजसत्तम॥
en: Having arrived there, that foremost of Rishis spoke thus to that Brahimana, “O best of Brahmanas, know that I have come here for food.

sn: स्वागतं तेऽस्त्विति मुनि मुद्गलः प्रत्यभाषत। पाद्यमाचमनीयं च प्रतिपाद्यार्थ्यमुत्तमम्॥ प्रादात् स तापसायान्नं क्षुधितायातिथिव्रती। उन्मत्ताय परां श्रद्धामास्थाय स धृतव्रतः॥ ततस्तदन्नं रसवत् स एव क्षुधयान्वितः। बुभुजे कृत्स्नमुन्मत्तः प्रादात् तस्मै च मुद्गलः॥
en: The Rishi Mudgala replied by saying “Welcome.” Offered to that hungry, mad ascetic, water to wash his feet and mouth; that Rishi, ever observant of the vow of feeding guests, then placed before him excellent food. Affected by hunger, the mad Rishi ate up all the food given to him. Then Mudgala gave him more food.

sn: भुक्त्वा चान्नं ततः सर्वमुच्छिष्टेनात्मनस्ततः। अथाङ्गं लिलिपेऽनेन यथागतमगाच्च सः॥
en: Having eaten up all that food, he besmeared his body with the uncleaned remainder and went away as he had come.

sn: एवं द्वितीये सम्प्राप्ते यथाकाले मनीषिणाः। आगम्य बुभुजे सर्वमन्नमुच्छोपजीविनः॥
en: In this manner during the next sea-son, he came again and ate up all the food given to him by that wise Rishi leading the Unccha mode of life.

sn: निराहारस्तु स मुनिरुञ्छमार्जयते पुनः। न चैनं विक्रियां नेतुमशकन्मुद्गलं क्षुधा।॥
en: Thereupon without eating any food himself, the Rishi Mudgala again became engaged in collecting corn, following the Unccha mode. Hunger could not disturb his equanimity,

sn: न क्रोधो न च मात्सर्यं नावमानो न सम्भ्रमः। सपुत्रदारमुञ्छन्तमाविवेश द्विजोत्तमम्॥
en: Nor could anger or guile or sense of degradation or agitationenter into the heart of that best of Brahmanas leading the Unccha mode of life along with his son and his wife.

sn: तथा तमुच्छधर्माणं दुर्वासा मुनिसत्तमम्। उपतस्थे यथाकालं षट्कृत्वः कृतनिश्चयः॥ न चास्य मनसा कंचिद् विकारं ददृशे मुनिः। शुद्ध सत्त्वस्य शुद्धं स ददृशे निर्मलं मनः॥
en: In ths way Durvasa during successive seasons came for several times before that best of sages living according to the Unccha mode of life. But that rishi could not perceive any senses agitation in the heart of Mudgala. He found the heart of that virtuous-minded Rishi always pure.

sn: तमुवाच ततः प्रीतः स मुनिर्मुद्गलं ततः। त्वत्समो नास्ति लोकेऽस्मिन् दाता मात्सर्यवर्जितः॥२३।
en: Thereupon becoming very much pleased he thus spoke to the Rishi Mudgala, There is no other simpleand charitable being like you on earth.

sn: क्षुद् धर्मसंज्ञा प्रणुदत्यादत्ते धैर्यमेव च। रसानुसारिणी जिह्वा कर्षत्येव रसान् प्रति॥
en: The pangs of hunger drive away all sense of virtue and deprive people of patience. The gongues, that always love, delicacies, attract men towards them.

sn: आहारप्रभवाः प्राणा मनो दुर्निग्रहं चलम्। मनसश्चेन्द्रियाणां चाप्यैकाग्यं निश्चितं तपः॥
en: Life is sustained by food. The mind is however fickle and it is hard to keep it in subjection. The concentration of mind and the control of the constitute (true) asceticism.

sn: श्रमेणोपार्जितं त्यक्तुं दुःखं शुद्धेन चेतसा। तत् सर्वं भवता साधो यथावदुपपादितम्॥
en: It is very hard to abandon in a pure spirit a thing earned by pain. O virtuous one, but all this has been duly achieved by you.

sn: प्रीताः स्मोऽनुगृहीताश्च समेत्य भवता सह। इन्द्रियाभिजयो धैर्यं संविभागो दमः शमः॥ दरा सत्यं च धर्मश्च त्वयि सर्वं प्रतिष्ठितम्। जितास्ते कर्मभिर्लोकाः प्राप्तोऽसि परमां गतिम्॥
en: In your company we feel obliged and gratified. Self-restraint, Self-restraint, fortitude, justice, control of the senses and of the faculties, mercy and virtue are all established in you. You have conquered all the worlds by your deeds, you have obtained the highest state.

sn: अहो दानं विधुष्टं ते सुमहत् स्वर्गवासिभिः। सशरीरो भवान् गन्ता स्वर्ग सुचरितव्रत॥
en: Even the dwellers of heaven are proclaiming your great deeds of charity. O vow-observing Rishi, you shall go to heaven in your own body.

sn: इत्येवं वदतस्तस्य तदा दुर्वाससो मुनेः। देवदूतो विमानेन मुद्गलं प्रत्युपस्थितः॥ हंससारसयुक्तेन किङ्किणीजालमालिना। कामगेन विचित्रेण दिव्यगन्धवता तथा॥
en: When the Rishi Durvasa was thus speaking, celestial messenger appeared before Mudgala in a car yoked with swans and cranes, adorned with numerous bells, scented with divine fragrance, picturesquely painted and possessing the power of going everywhere at will.

sn: उवाच चैनं विप्रर्षि विमानं कर्मभिर्जितम्। समुपारोह संसिद्धि प्राप्तोऽसि परमां मुने॥
en: He spoke thus to the Brahmanas. Ascend this car. O Rishis, the result of your acts, you have obtained the fruit of your asceticism.

sn: तमेवंवादिनमृषिदेवदूतमुवाच हा इच्छामि भवता प्रोक्तान् गुणान् स्वर्गनिवासिनाम्॥ के गुणास्तत्र वसतां किं तपः कश्च निश्चयः। स्वर्गे तत्र सुखं किं च दोषो वा देवदूतक॥
en: When the celestial messenger was thus talking, the Rishi told him, O celestial messenger, I desire that you should describe to methe attributes of those that live there. What is their asceticism and what is their purpose? What is the happiness in heaven and what are its defects?

sn: सतां साप्तपदं मैत्रमाहुः सन्तः कुलोचिताः। मित्रतां च पुरस्कृत्य पृच्छामि त्वामहं विभो॥ यदत्र तथ्यं पथ्यं च तद् ब्रवीह्यविचारयन्। श्रुत्वा तथा करिष्यामि व्यवसायं गिरा तव।॥
en: O lord, it has been declared by nobly born virtuous men that friendship with five men is formed by only walking with them seven faces. In the name of friendship, I ask you, tell me the truth and that which is good for me to know. Hearing you, I shall according to your words fix the course I ought to follow.

description: The colloquy between Mudgada and the celestial messenger
sn: देवदूत उवाच महर्षे आर्यबुद्धिस्त्वं यः स्वर्गसुखमुत्तमम्। सम्प्राप्तं बहु मन्तव्यं विमृशस्यबुधो यथा॥
en: The celestial messenger said: O great Rishi, you are very simple, for having obtained that celestial bliss which brings great honour, you are still delebrating like an unwise person.

description: The colloquy between Mudgada and the celestial messenger
sn: उपरिष्टादसौ लोको योऽयं स्वरिति संज्ञितः। ऊर्ध्वगः सत्पथः शश्वद् देवयानचरो मुने॥
en: O Rishi, that which is known in the world by the name of heaven exists above us. It is high, it is furnished with excellent paths and is always frequented by celestial cars.

description: The colloquy between Mudgada and the celestial messenger
sn: नातप्ततपसः पुंसो नामहायज्ञयाजिनः। नानृता नास्तिकाश्चैव तत्र गच्छन्ति मुद्गल॥
en: O sage, atheists and untruthful persons, those that have not performed asceticism and those that have not performed great sacrifices, cannot go there.

description: The colloquy between Mudgada and the celestial messenger
sn: धर्मात्मानो जितात्मानः शान्ता दान्ता विमत्सराः। दानधर्मरता मर्त्याः शूराश्चाहवलक्षणाः॥ तत्र गच्छन्ति धर्माग्र्यं कृत्वा शमदमात्मकम्। लोकान् पुण्यकृतां ब्रह्मन् सद्भिराचरितान् नृभिः॥
en: Only virtuous souls and those of subdued minds and those that have their faculties under control and those that have controlled their senses and those that are free from malice and persons intent on the practice of charity and heroes and men bearing marks of battle, after having subdued senses and faculties and performed the most meritorious rites, attain to those regions, O Brahmana, capable of beings obtained only by virtuous acts and inhabitatedd by pious men.

description: The colloquy between Mudgada and the celestial messenger
sn: देवाः साध्यास्तथा विश्वे तथैव च महर्षयः। यामा धामाश्च मौद्गल्य गन्धर्वाप्सरसस्तथा।॥ एषां देवनिकायानां पृथक् पृथगनेकशः। भास्वन्त: कामसम्पन्ना लोकास्तेजोमयाः शुभाः॥
en: O Mudgala, there are established separately myriads of beautiful, shinning and respendent worlds bestowing every object of desire owned by those celestial beings, the gods, the Sadhyas, the Vishvadevas, the great sages, the Yamas, the Dhamas and the Gandharvas and the Apsaras.

description: The colloquy between Mudgada and the celestial messenger
sn: त्रयस्त्रिंशत्सहस्राणि योजनानि हिरण्मयः। मेरुः पर्वतराट् यत्र देवोद्यानानि मुद्गल॥ नन्दनादीनि पुण्यानि विहाराः पुण्यकर्मणाम्। न क्षुत्पिपासे न ग्लानिर्न शीतोष्णे भयं तथा॥
en: There is that foremost of mountains, the golden Meru extending thirty-three thousand Yojanas. O Mudgala, there are also the celestial gardens. With Nandan at their head here sport the persons of meritorious acts. Neither hunger nor thirst nor heat or cold nor fear.

description: The colloquy between Mudgada and the celestial messenger
sn: बीभत्समशुभं वापि तत्र किंचिन्न विद्यते। मनोज्ञाः सर्वतो गन्धाः सुखस्पर्शाश्च सर्वशः॥ शब्दाः श्रुतिमनोचाह्याः सर्वतस्तत्र वै मुने। न शोको न जरा तत्र नायासपरिदेवने।॥
en: Nor anything that is disgusting and inauspicious is there. Delightful fragrance is everywhere and breezes are delicious and sounds are captivating both to the ear and mind; there is no grief, no old age; nor labour nor repentance is there.

description: The colloquy between Mudgada and the celestial messenger
sn: ईदृशः स मुने लोकः स्वकर्मफलहेतुकः। सुकृतैस्तत्र पुरुषाः सम्भवन्त्यात्मकर्मभिः॥
en: O Rishi, the world obtained as the fruit of one's (good) acts is like this. Men go there by virtue of their meritorious acts.

description: The colloquy between Mudgada and the celestial messenger
sn: तैजसानि शरीराणि भवन्त्यत्रोपपद्यताम्। कर्मजान्येव मौद्गल्य न मातृपितृजान्युत॥
en: Men that live there look resplendant and O Mudgala, solely by virtue of their own acts and not through the me its of fathers or mothers.

description: The colloquy between Mudgada and the celestial messenger
sn: न संस्वेदो न दौर्गन्ध्यं पुरीषं मूत्रमेव च। तेषां न च रजो वस्त्रं बाधते तत्र वै मुने॥
en: O Rishi, there is neither sweat nor stench, nor exeretion nor urine. There dust does not soil one's clothes.

description: The colloquy between Mudgada and the celestial messenger
sn: न म्लायन्ति स्रजस्तेषां दिव्यगन्धा मनोरमाः। संयुज्यन्ते विमानैश्च ब्रह्मन्नेवंविधैश्च ते॥
en: There excellent garments full of celestial fragrance never fade. O Brahmana, there are such cars as this (one I have brought).

description: The colloquy between Mudgada and the celestial messenger
sn: ईर्ष्याशोकक्लमापेता मोहमात्सर्यवर्जिताः। सुखं स्वर्गजितस्तत्र वर्तयन्ते महामुने॥
en: O great Rishi, being free from envy and grief and fatigue and ignorance and malice, men, who have gone to heaven, live in that region in great happiness.

description: The colloquy between Mudgada and the celestial messenger
sn: तेषां तथाविधानां तु लोकानां मुनिपुङ्गवा उपर्युपरि लोकस्य लोका दिव्या गुणान्विताः॥
en: O foremost of Rishis, higher and higher over such regions, there are others possessing higher celestial virtues.

description: The colloquy between Mudgada and the celestial messenger
sn: पुरस्ताद् ब्राह्मणास्तत्र लोकास्तेजोमयाः शुभाः। यत्र यान्त्यषयो ब्रह्मन् पूताः स्वैः कर्मभिः शुभैः॥
en: Of these, the charming and effulgent region of Brahma is the highest. O Brahmana, there go the Rishis that have been purified by their meritorious acts.

description: The colloquy between Mudgada and the celestial messenger
sn: ऋभवो नाम तत्रान्ये देवानामपि देवताः। तेषां लोकात् परतरे यान् यजन्तीह देवताः॥
en: There live certain beings called Ribhus, they are the gods of the gods. Their region is highly blessed and they are adored even by the celestials.

description: The colloquy between Mudgada and the celestial messenger
sn: स्वयंप्रभास्ते भास्वन्तो लोका: कामदुधाः परे। न तेषां स्त्रीकृतस्तापो न लोकैश्वर्यमत्सरः॥
en: They shine in their own effulgence and they bestow every object of desire. They suffer no pangs arising from women. They do not possess worldly wealth and they are free from ill.

description: The colloquy between Mudgada and the celestial messenger
sn: न वर्तयन्त्याहुतिभिस्ते नाष्यमृतभोजनाः। तथा दिव्यशरीरास्ते न च विग्रहमूर्तयः॥
en: They do not live on oblations or on ambrosia. They possess such celestial forms that they cannot be perceived by the senses.

description: The colloquy between Mudgada and the celestial messenger
sn: न सुखे सुखकामास्ते देवदेवाः सनातनाः। न कल्पपरिवर्तेषु परिवर्तन्ति ते तथा॥
en: Those everlasting gods of the gods do not desire happiness for happiness sake, nor do they undergo any change at the change of a Kalpa.

description: The colloquy between Mudgada and the celestial messenger
sn: जरा मृत्युः कुतस्तेषां हर्षः प्रीतिः सुखं न च। न दुःखं न सुखं चापि रागद्वेषौ कुतो मुने॥
en: Old, age, death they have none; for them there is neither ecstacy, nor joy nor happiness. They have neither happiness nor misery, O Rishi, anger and aversion they have none.

description: The colloquy between Mudgada and the celestial messenger
sn: देवानामपि मौद्गल्य काक्षिता सा गतिः परा। दुष्प्रापा परमा सिद्धिरगम्या कामगोचरैः॥
en: O Mudgala, their supreme state is coveted even by the celestial. The great emancipation, which is very difficult to attain, can never be acquired by people subject to desire.

description: The colloquy between Mudgada and the celestial messenger
sn: त्रयस्त्रिंशदिमे देवा येषां लोका मनीषिभिः। गम्यन्ते नियमैः श्रेष्ठैर्दानैर्वा विधिपूर्वकैः॥
en: The number of these gods is thirty-three. To their region go wise men after having observed excellent vows or bestowed gifts according to the ordiance.

description: The colloquy between Mudgada and the celestial messenger
sn: सेयं दानकृता व्युष्टिरनुप्राप्ता सुखं त्वया। तां भुक्ष्व सुकृतैर्लब्धां तपसा द्योतितप्रभः॥ एतत् स्वर्गसुखं विप्र लोका नानाविधास्तथा। गुणाः स्वर्गस्य प्रोक्तास्ते दोषानपि निबोध मे॥
en: You have easily acquired that success by your charities, your effulgence is displayed by virtue of your asceticism. (Now) enjoy that condition which is obtained by your meritorious acts. Such, O Brahmana, is bliss of heaven containing many worlds. Thus have I described to you the blessing of the celestial, region. Now hear some of its disadvantages.

description: The colloquy between Mudgada and the celestial messenger
sn: कृतस्य कर्मणस्तत्र भुज्यते यत् फलं दिवि। न चान्यत् क्रियते कर्म मूलच्छेदेन भुज्यते॥ सोऽत्र दोषो मम मतस्तस्यान्ते पतनं च यत्। सुखव्याप्तमनस्कानां पतनं यच्च मुद्गल॥
en: O Mudgala, in the celestial region a person, while enjoying the fruits of acts he had already performed, cannot perform any other new acts. He must enjoy the fruits of the former life till they are completely exhausted and besides he is liable to fall after he has entirely exhausted his merit, these are in my opinion the disadvantages of heaven. The fall of persons whose minds have been once steeped in happiness must be called a great draw back (of heaven).

description: The colloquy between Mudgada and the celestial messenger
sn: असंतोषः परीतापो दृष्ट्वा दीप्ततराः श्रियः। यद् भवत्यवरे स्थाने स्थितानां तत् सुदुष्करम्॥
en: The discontent and regret that must follow ones stay in an inferior place after he has enjoyed more auspicious and effulgent regions must be very difficult to bear.

description: The colloquy between Mudgada and the celestial messenger
sn: संज्ञामोहश्च पततां रजसा च प्रधर्षणम्। प्रम्लानेषु च माल्येषु ततः पिपतिषोर्भयम्॥
en: The consciousness of those about to fall is stupified and it is also agitated by emotions. As the garlands of those about to fall fade away, fear possesses their hearts.

description: The colloquy between Mudgada and the celestial messenger
sn: आब्रह्मभवनादेते दोषा मौद्गल्य दारुणाः। नाकलोके सुकृतिनां गुणास्त्वयुतशो नृणाम्॥
en: O Mudgala, these are the great draw backs that exist even in the region of Brahma. In the celestial region the virtues, of men who have performed righteous acts, are countless.

description: The colloquy between Mudgada and the celestial messenger
sn: अयं त्वन्यो गुणः श्रेष्ठश्च्युतानां स्वर्गतो मुने। शुभानुशययोगेन मनुष्येषूपजायते॥
en: O Rishi, this is another of the attributes of the fallen that by reason of their merits, they take birth amongst men.

description: The colloquy between Mudgada and the celestial messenger
sn: तत्रापि स महाभागः सुखभागभिजायते। न चेत् सम्बुध्यते तत्र गच्छत्यधमतां ततः॥ इह यत् क्रियते कर्म तत् परत्रोपभुज्यते। कर्मभूमिरियं ब्रह्मन् फलभूमिरसौ मता॥
en: O Rishi, then they obtain high fortune and happiness. If one however cannot acquire knowledge, he takes an inferior birth. The fruits of acts performed in this world are reaped in the next. O Brahmana, this worid has been declared to be one of acts.

description: The colloquy between Mudgada and the celestial messenger
sn: मुद्गल उवाच महान्तस्तु अमी दोषास्त्वया स्वर्गस्य कीर्तिताः। निर्दोष एव यस्त्वन्यो लोकं तं प्रवदस्व मे॥
en: O Mudgala, thus have I, as asked by you, described all to you. Now, O virtuous Rishi, with your favour, we shall easily go with speed.

description: The colloquy between Mudgada and the celestial messenger
sn: देवदूत उवाच ब्रह्मणः सदनादूर्ध्वं तद् विष्णोः परमं पदम्। शुद्धं सनातनं ज्योतिः परं ब्रह्मेति यद् विदुः॥
en: Vyasa said : Having heard those words, Mudgala reflected in his mind. Having reflected that foremost of Rishis thus spoke to the celestial Messenger.

description: The colloquy between Mudgada and the celestial messenger
sn: न तत्र विप्र गच्छन्ति पुरुषा विषयात्मकाः। दम्भलोभमहाक्रोधमोहद्रोहैरभिद्रुताः॥
en: O celestial messenger, I bow to you. O sir, go back in peace. I have nothing to do with either happiness or heaven with such drawbacks.

description: The colloquy between Mudgada and the celestial messenger
sn: निर्ममा निरहङ्कारा निर्द्वन्द्वाः संयतेन्द्रियाः। ध्यानयोगपराश्चैव तत्र गच्छन्ति मानवाः॥
en: Men who enjoy heaven suffer great misery and extreme regret in this world. Therefore I do not desire (to go to) heaven.

description: The colloquy between Mudgada and the celestial messenger
sn: एतत् ते सर्वमाख्यातं यन्मां पृच्छसि मुद्गल। तवानुकम्पया साधो साधु गच्छाम मा चिरम्॥
en: I seek that unfailing region, going where people have not to lament or to be pained or to be agitated.

description: The colloquy between Mudgada and the celestial messenger
sn: व्यास उवाच एतच्छ्रुत्वा मौद्गल्यो वाक्यं विममृशे धिया। विमृश्य च मुनिश्रेष्ठो देवदूतमुवाच ह॥
en: You have described to me the great draw backs of the celestial region. Now describe to me a region which is free from fault.

description: The colloquy between Mudgada and the celestial messenger
sn: देवदूत नमस्तेऽस्तु गच्छ तात यथासुखम्। महादेषेण मे कार्यं न स्वर्गेण सुखेन वा॥
en: The Celestial Messenger said: Above the abode of Brahma there is the supreme seat of Vishnu which is pure, eternal and effulgent. It is known by the name of Parabrahma. senses are

description: The colloquy between Mudgada and the celestial messenger
sn: पतनान्ते महद् दुःखं परितापः सुदारुणः। स्वर्गभाजश्चरन्तीह तस्मात् स्वर्गं न कामये॥
en: O Brahmana, persons who are addicted to sensual objects or those who are subject to arrogance, coveteousness, ignorance, anger and envy, cannot go to that place.

description: The colloquy between Mudgada and the celestial messenger
sn: यत्र गत्वा न शोचन्ति न व्यथन्ति चलन्ति वा। तदहं स्थानमत्यन्तं मार्गयिष्यामि केवलम्॥
en: Those men who are free from conflicting emotions and those that have restrained their and those that given to contemplation and Yoga can go there.

description: The colloquy between Mudgada and the celestial messenger
sn: इत्युक्त्वा स मुनिर्वाक्यं देवदूतं विसृज्य तम्। शिलोच्छवृत्तिर्धर्मात्मा शममातिष्ठदुत्तमम्॥
en: O Mudgala, thus have I told you all that you asked me. O pious one, now without any further delay kindly come with me. Hearing those words that virtuous Rishi, leading unccha mode of life, assumed perfect contentment.

description: The colloquy between Mudgada and the celestial messenger
sn: तुल्यनिन्दास्तुतिर्भूत्वा समलोष्टाश्मकाञ्चनः। ज्ञानयोगेन शुद्धेन ध्याननित्यो बभूव ह॥
en: Then praise and blame became equal to him. A brick,a stone and a piece of gold all became the same to him. By pure Jnana Yoga, he always became engaged in meditation.

description: The colloquy between Mudgada and the celestial messenger
sn: ध्यानयोगाद् बलं लब्ध्वा प्राप्य बुद्धिमनुत्तमाम्। जगाम शाश्वती सिद्धिं परां निर्वाणलक्षणाम्॥
en: Having acquired power by means of knowledge. He acquired excellent understanding and obtained that supreme state of emancipation which is eternal.

description: The colloquy between Mudgada and the celestial messenger
sn: तस्मात् त्वमपि कौन्तेय न शोकं कर्तुमर्हसि। राज्यात् स्फीतात् परिभ्रष्टस्तपसा तदवाप्स्यसि॥
en: Therefore, O son of Kunti, you ought not to grieve. You have been deprived of a great kingdom, but you will region it by your asceticism.

description: The colloquy between Mudgada and the celestial messenger
sn: सुखस्यानन्तरं दुःखं दुःखस्यानन्तरं सुखम्। पर्यायेणोपसर्पन्ते नरं नेमिमरा इव॥
en: Misery after happiness and happiness after misery revolve by turns round a man like a wheel round its axile.

description: The colloquy between Mudgada and the celestial messenger
sn: पितृपैतामहं राज्यं प्राप्स्यस्यमितविक्रम। वर्षात् त्रयोदशादूर्ध्वं व्येतु ते मानसो ज्वरः॥
en: O undeterioratingly powerful one, after the thirteenth year has passed away, you will get back the kingdom of your father and grandfather.

description: The colloquy between Mudgada and the celestial messenger
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच स एवमुक्त्वा भगवान् व्यासः पाण्डवनन्दनम्। जगाम तपसे धीमान् पुनरेवाश्रमं प्रति॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having said thus to the Pandava, the severed Vyasa went back to his hermitage for performing asceticism.

sn: जनमेजय उवाच वसत्स्वेवं वने तेषु पाण्डवेषु महात्मसु। रममाणेषु चित्राभिः कथाभिर्मुनिभिः सह॥ सूर्यदत्ताक्षयान्नेन कृष्णाया भोजनावधि। ब्राह्मणांस्तर्पमाणेषु ये चान्नार्थमुपागताः॥ धार्तराष्ट्रा दुरात्मानः सर्वे दुर्योधनादयः। कथं तेष्वन्ववर्तन्त पापाचारा महामुने॥ दुःशासनस्य कर्णस्य शकुनेश्च मते स्थिताः। एतदाचक्ष्व भगवन् वैशम्पायन पृच्छतः॥
en: Janamejaya said : While the high-souled Pandavas were living in the forest, delighted with the pleasant conversation they held with the Rishis and engaged in distributing the food, they obtained from the sun, with various kinds of venison to Brahmanas and others that came to them for fool till the hour of Krishna's meal, how O great Rishi, did Duryodhana and the other wicked and sinful sons of Dhritarashtra, guided by the counsels of Dushasana, Karna and Sakuni, deal with them? I ask you, O reverend one, O Vaishampayana, tell me all this.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच श्रुत्वा तेषां तथा वृत्तिं नगरे वसतामिव। दुर्योधनो महाराज तेषु पापमरोचयत्॥ तथा तैनिकृतिप्रज्ञैः कर्णदुःशासनादिभिः। नानोपायैरघं तेषु चिन्तयत्सु दुरात्मसु॥ अभ्यागच्छत् स धर्मात्मा तपस्वी सुमहायशाः। शिष्यायुतसमोपेतो दुर्वासा नाम कामतः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Hearing that they (the Pandavas) are living in the forest as in a city, the great king Duryodhana with Karna, Dushashana and others longed to do them harm. When those wicked men were concerting various evil designs, the virtuous and the celebrated ascetic Durvasa, wandering about at will, came to the city of the Kurus with ten thousand disciples.

sn: तमागतमभिप्रेक्ष्य मुनि परमकोपनम्। दुर्योधनो विनीतात्मा प्रश्रयेण दमेन च॥ सहितो भ्रातृभिः श्रीमानातिथ्येन न्यमन्त्रयत्।
en: Seeing the greatly wrathful Rishi arrived. The handsome Duryodhana and his brother welcomed him with great humility, self-abuse and gentleness.

sn: विधिवत् पूजयामास स्वयं किङ्करवत् स्थितः॥ अहानि कतिचित् तत्र तस्थौ स मुनिसत्तमः।
en: Himself he waited upon the Rishi as a menial. The illustrious Rishi remained there for a few days.

sn: तं च पर्यचरद् राजा दिवारानमतन्द्रितः॥ दुर्योधनो महाराज शापात् तस्य विशङ्कितः।
en: Janamejaya, king Duryodhana, fearing his curse, served him diligently day and right.

sn: क्षुधितोऽस्मि ददस्वान्नं शीघ्रं मम नराधिप॥ इत्युक्त्वा गच्छति स्नातुं प्रत्यागच्छति वै चिरात्। न भोक्ष्याम्यद्य मे नास्ति क्षुधेत्युक्त्वैत्यदर्शनम्॥
en: Sometime saying “O ruler of men I am hungry, give me food without delay," he would go to bathe but would return after along time and say, “I shall not eat anything today, I have no appetite." So saying he would disappear.

sn: अकस्मादेत्य च ब्रूते भोजयास्मांस्त्वरान्वितः। कदाचिच्च निशीथे स उत्थाय निकृतौ स्थितः॥ पूर्ववत् कारयित्वान्नं न भुङ्क्ते गर्हयन् स्म सः।
en: Sometimes suddenly coming, he would say "feed us soon.” At other times, being bent on mischief, he would awake at midnight and having ordered his food to be prepared, he would not eat it at all.

sn: वर्तमाने तथा तस्मिन् यदा दुर्योधनो नृपः॥ विकृति नैति न क्रोधं तदा तुष्टोऽभवन्मुनिः। आह चैनं दुराधर्षो वरदोऽस्मीति भारत।॥
en: When the Rishi found that king Duryodhana was not enraged or annoyed, he became gracious towards him. O descendant of Bharata, then the wrothful Durvasa thus spoke to him, “I am capable of giving boons."

sn: दुर्वासा उवाच वरं वरय भद्रं ते यत् मनसि वर्तते। मयि प्रीते तु यद् धर्म्य नालभ्यं विद्यते तव॥
en: Durvasa said: You may ask from me whatever you desire to possess. Be blessed. I am pleased with you, you may obtain from me anything that is not opposed to religion.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एतच्छ्रुत्वा वचस्तस्य महर्षर्भावितात्मनः। अमन्यत पुनर्जातमात्मानं स सुयोधनः॥
en: Vaishampayana said: Having heard those words of the high-souled ascetic, Duryodhana became inspired with a new life.

sn: प्रागेव मन्त्रितं चासीत् कर्णदुःशासनादिभिः। याचनीयं मुनेस्तुष्टादिति निश्चित्य दुर्मतिः॥ अतिहर्षान्वितो राजन् वरमेनमयाचत। शिष्यैः सह मम ब्रह्मन् यथा जातोऽतिथिर्भवान्॥ अस्मत्कुले महाराजो ज्येष्ठः श्रेष्ठो युधिष्ठिरः। वने वसति धर्मात्मा भ्रातृभिः परिवारितः॥ गुणवान् शीलसम्पन्नस्तस्य त्वमतिथिर्भव।
en: It had been settled between that wicked wretch and Karna and Duhshasana as to the boon he would ask, if the Rishi be so pleased as to agree to bestow one. With great joy the king (Duryodhana) asked for the following boon, O Brahman, as you have been my guest for sometime. So you become the guest of Yudhisthira who is accomplished and who is well-behaved; he is the great king, the best and the eldest of our family, that viruous-minded one is now living in the forest surrounded by his brothers.

sn: यदा च राजपुत्री सा सुकुमारी यशस्विनी॥ भोजयित्वा द्विजान् सर्वान् पतींश्च वरवर्णिनी। विश्रान्ता च स्वयं भुक्त्वा सुखासीना भवेद् यदा।।२२। तदा त्वं तत्र गच्छेथा यद्यनुचाह्यता मयि।
en: Then at that time you should once go there as you have favoured me (by coming here), when that illustrious princess, that delicate lady, that excellent lady (Draupadi) after having fed the Brahmanas and regaled her husbands and also eating herself, will be comfortably seated for rest.

sn: तथा करिष्ये त्वत्प्रीत्येत्येवमुक्त्वा सुयोधनम्॥ दुर्वासा अपि विप्रेन्द्रो यथागतमगात् ततः। कृतार्थमपि चात्मानं तदा मेने सुयोधनः॥
en: He (Rishi) replied to the Duryodhana “I shall do it for your satisfaction.” Having said this, that great Brahmana went in the way he came. Duryodhana then considered that all his desires had been fulfilled.

sn: करेण च करं गृह्य कर्णस्य मुदितो भृशम्। कर्णोऽपि भ्रातृसहितमित्युवाच नृपं मुदा॥
en: Holding Karna by the hand he expressed his great delight. Karna also with great joy thus spoke to the king (Duryodhana).

sn: कर्ण उवाच दिष्ट्या कामः सुसंवृत्तो दिष्ट्या कौरव वर्धसे। दिष्ट्या ते शत्रवो मग्ना दुस्तरे व्यसनार्णवे॥ दुर्वासः क्रोधजे वह्नौ पतिताः पाण्डुनन्दनाः। स्वैरेव ते महापापैर्गता वै दुस्तरं तमः॥
en: Karna said: By singular good luck, you have fared well and attained to the fulfilment of your desire. By good luck your enemies have been plunged into the sea of misery which is difficult to cross. The Pandavas are now exposed to the fire of Durvasa's anger. Through their own fault they have fallen into an abyss of darkness.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच इत्यं ते निकृतिप्रज्ञा राजन् दुर्योधनादयः। हसन्तः प्रीतमनसो जग्मुः स्वं स्वं निकेतनम्॥
en: O king, thus expressing their great delight, Duryodhana and others, ever bent on mischief, cheerfully went to their respective house.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततः कदाचिद् दुर्वासाः सुखासीनांस्तु पाण्डवान्। भुक्त्वा चावस्थितां कृष्णां ज्ञात्वा तस्मिन् वने मुनिः।१ अभ्यागच्छत् परिवृतः शिप्यैरयुतसम्मितैः।
en: Vaishampayana said : Thereupon one day, knowing that the Pandavas had been comfortably seated and Krishna was taking her rest after meal the ascetic entered the forest surrounded by ten thousand disciples.

sn: दृष्ट्वाऽऽयान्तं तमतिथिं स च राजा युधिष्ठिरः॥ जगामाभिमुखः श्रीमान् सह भ्रातृभिरच्युतः। तस्मै बद्धवाञ्जलिं सम्यगुपवेश्य वरासने॥ विधिवत् पूजयित्वा तमातिथ्येन न्यमन्त्रयत्। आह्निकं भगवन् कृत्वा शीघ्रमेहीति चाब्रवीत्॥
en: Beholding that guest arrive there the king Yudhishthira graceful and honest, proceeded with his brothers. Joining his hands and making him sit on an excellent seat. And adoring him duly he treated him with hospitalicy. He said, “Come back soon, O venerably sir, after performing your ablutions and reciting your prayers."

sn: जगाम च मुनिः सोऽपि स्नातुं शिष्यैः सहानघः। भोजयेत् सहशिष्यं मां कथमित्यविचिन्तयन्॥ न्यमज्जत् सलिले चापि मुनिसङ्घः समाहितः।
en: That innocent ascetic went to bathe along with his disciples, thinking "how will he feed me and my disciples.” Those ascetics of controlled minds went into the water.

sn: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे राजन् द्रौपदी योषितां वरा॥ चिन्तामवाप परमामन्नहेतोः पतिव्रता।
en: In the interval, O king, Draupadi, the best of women ever devoted to her husband, began to think how she could provide food.

sn: सा चिन्तयन्ती च यदा नान्नहेतुमविन्दत॥ मनसा चिन्तयामास कृष्णं कंसनिषूदनम्।
en: While she was thus thinking she could not find any means. She then thought in mind of Krishna, the slayer at Kansa.

sn: कृष्ण कृष्ण महाबाहो देवकीनन्दनाव्यया॥ वासुदेव जगन्नाथ प्रणतातिविनाशन। विश्वात्मन् विश्वजनक विश्वहर्तः प्रभोऽव्यय॥ प्रपन्नपाल गोपाल प्रजापाल परात्पर। आकृतीनां च चित्तीनां प्रवर्तक नतास्मि ते॥
en: (She said) O Krishna, O Krishna of mighty arms, O eternal, O son of Devaki.O Vasudeva, O lord of the universe, O you the killer of the difficulties of those that bow to you, O soul of the universe, O creator of the universe, O destroyer, O lord O inexhaustible. Oh the protector of the afflicted, O the saviour of kine and subjects, O the highest of the high, O the source of the mental perceptions such as faculties of knowledge and moral sense, I bow to you.

sn: वरेण्य वरदानन्त अगतीनां गतिर्भव। पुराणपुरुष प्राणमनोवृत्त्याद्यगोचर॥ सर्वाध्यक्ष पराध्यक्ष त्वामहं शरणं गता। पाहि मां कृपया देव शरणागतवत्सल॥
en: O worshipful one, O endless giver of boons, you are the refuge of the helpless; You are the ancient Purusha, the vital breath, beyond the perception of mental faculties. Oh lord of all, the most excellent lord, I seek your refuge; O lord, O you fond of your votaries, kindly protect me.

sn: नीलोत्पलदलश्याम पद्मगर्भारुणेक्षण। पीताम्बरपरीधान लसत्कौस्तुभभूषण॥ त्वमादिरन्तो भूतानां त्वमेव च परायणम्। परात्परतरं ज्योतिर्विश्वात्मा सर्वतोमुखः॥
en: O you having complexion dark as the leaves of the blue lotus having eyes red as the corola of the lilly, O you clad in yellow raiment, O you adorned with the brilliant Kaustava. You are the beginning and the end of creation; the great refuge of all, you are the supreme light and essence of the universe with your face directed towards all directions.

sn: त्वामेवाहुः परं बीजं निधानं सर्वसम्पदाम। त्वया नाथेन देवेश सर्वापद्भ्यो भयं न हि॥
en: They call you the supreme germ and the depository of all wealth; O king of gods, being protected by you all will lose their terrors.

sn: दुःशासनादहं पूर्व सभायां मोचिता यथा। तथैव संकटादस्मान्मामुद्धर्तुमिहार्हसि॥
en: You did save me before from Dushasana in the assembly; it behoves you now to save me from this difficutly.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवं स्तुतस्तदा देवः कृष्णया भक्तवत्सलः। द्रौपद्याः संकटं ज्ञात्वा देवदेवो जगत्पतिः॥ पार्श्वस्थां शयने त्यक्त्वा रुक्मिणी केशवः प्रभुः। तत्राजगाम त्वरितो ह्यचिन्त्यगतिरीश्वरः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Then thus eulogised by Krishna the lord, fond of his votaries, the god of gods, the lord of the universe, Kesava of mysterious movements, percieving Draupadi's difficulty and leaving Rukmani on the bed him, came there quickly.

sn: ततस्तं द्रौपदी दृष्ट्वा प्रणम्य परया मुदा। अब्रवीद् वासुदेवाय मुनेरागमनादिकम्॥
en: Thereupon beholding him arrived there Draupadi, in great delight, bowed to him and communicated to Vasudeva the coming of the ascetic and every other thing,

sn: ततस्तामब्रवीत् कृष्णः क्षुधितोऽस्मि भृशातुरः। शीघ्रं भोजय मां कृष्णे पश्चात् सर्वं करिष्यसि॥ निशम्य तद्वचः कृष्णा लज्जिता वाक्यमब्रवीत्। स्थाल्यां भास्करदत्तायामन्नं मद्भोजनावधि॥ भुक्तवत्यस्म्यहं देव तस्मादन्नं न विद्यते।
en: “Thereupon Krishna said to her, I am greatly stricken with hunger; soon feed me, O Krishna and afterwards I shall do all.” Hearing his words Krishna, ashamed, said, The vessel given by the sun remains full till I take my meals. O lord, I have taken my meals and there is no food.

sn: ततः प्रोवाच भगवान् कृष्णां कमललोचनः॥ कृष्णे न नर्मकालोऽयं क्षुच्छ्रमेणातुरे मयि। शीघ्रं गच्छ मम स्थालीमानीय त्वं प्रदर्शय॥ इति निर्बन्धतः स्थालीमानाय्य स यदूद्वहः। स्थाल्याः कण्ठेऽथ संलग्नं शाकानं वीक्ष्य केशवः॥ उपयुज्याब्रवीदेनामनेन हरिरीश्वरः। विश्वात्मा प्रीयतां देवस्तुष्टश्चास्त्विति यज्ञभुक्॥
en: Thereupon the lotus-eyed god said to Krishna. This is not the time for joke, O Krishna; I am assailed with hunger and fatigue; soon go, fetch the vessel and show me. Having thus got persistently the vessel brought, the ornament of the Yadu race, Keshava, saw a particle of rice and vegetable sticking at a corner. Eating it up he said to her "May the lord Hari, the soul of the universe, be pleased with it and may the God who partakes at sacrifices be satiated with it."

sn: आकारय मुनीन् शीघ्रं भोजनायेति चाब्रवीत्। सहदेवं महाबाहुः कृष्णः कलेशविनाशनः॥
en: Then the long-armed Krishna, the destroyer of miseries said to Sahadeva, “soon bring the ascetics here and feed them."

sn: ततो जगाम त्वरितः सहदेवो महायशाः। आकारितुं तु तान् सर्वान् भोजनार्थं नृपोत्तम॥ स्नातुं गतान् देवनद्यां दुर्वासः प्रभृतीन् मुनीन्। ते चावतीर्णाः सलिले कृतवन्तोऽघमर्षणम्॥ दृष्ट्वोद्गारान् सान्नरसांस्तृप्त्या परमया युताः। उत्तीर्य सलिलात् तस्माद् दृष्टवन्तः परस्परम्॥ दुर्वाससमभिप्रेक्ष्य ते सर्वे मुनयोऽब्रुवन्। राज्ञा हि करायित्वान्नं वयं स्नातुं समागताः॥ आकण्ठतृप्ता विप्रर्षे किंस्विद् भुञ्जामहे वयम्। वृथा पाकः कृतोऽस्माभिस्तत्र किं करवामहे॥
en: O foremost of kings, thereupon the mighty illustrious Sahaveda soon went to invite them to repast. The ascetic Durvasa and others, who had gone to the nearest river to cool and transparent water to bath, all having plunged into the river, were rubbing their persons. And they were all feeling their stomachs to be full. Coming out of the water they began to eye each other. Then turning their faces towards Durvasa they all said, "Having asked the king to get our meals ready we have come here to bathe. Our stomachs have been filled to the throat; how can we eat anything now, O Brahmana Rishi? The food has been uselessly prepared for us, what shall we do now?"

sn: दुर्वासा उवाच वृथा पाकेन राजर्षेरपराधः कृतो महान्। मास्मानधाक्षुर्दृष्ट्वैव पाण्डवाः क्रूरचक्षुषा॥ स्मृत्वानुभावं राजर्षेरम्बरीषस्य धीमतः। बिभेमि सुतरां विप्रा हरिपादाश्रयाज्जनात्॥ पाण्डवाश्च महात्मानः सर्वे धर्मपरायणाः। शूराश्च कृतविद्याश्च वतिनस्तपसि स्थिताः॥ सदाचाररता नित्यं वासुदेवपरायणाः। क्रुद्धास्ते निर्दहेयुर्वै तूलराशिमिवानलः। तत एतानपृष्ट्वैव शिष्याः शीघ्रं पलायत॥
en: Durvasa said : By uselessly making him prepare our food we have done a great wrong to that royal sage. Will not the Pandavas distroy us by looking down upon us with angry eyes? I know, the royal sage is endued with great ascetic power; O Brahmana, I am afraid of those man who are devoted to Hari's feet. All those Pandavas are high-souled, pious, heroic, learned, observant of vows and of devout panances. They always observe the rules of good conduct and are devoted to Vasudeva; if angry, they can consume us with their anger as fire does a bale of cotton. So O disciples, you all run away quickly without seeing them.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच इत्युक्तास्ते द्विजाः सर्वे मुनिना गुरुणा तदा। पाण्डवेभ्यो भृशं भीता दुद्रुवुस्ते दिशो दश॥
en: Vaishampnyana said : Being thus addressed by their ascetic preceptor, all those Bramhanas, greatly afraid of the Pandavas, fled away in all directions.

sn: सहदेवो देवनद्यामपश्यन् मुनिसत्तमान्। तीर्थेष्वितस्ततस्तस्या विचचार गवेषयन्॥
en: Not beholding those best ascetics in the celestial river. Sahadeva searched them here, there and at all the landing places.

sn: तत्रस्थेभ्यस्तापसेभ्यः श्रुत्वा तांश्चैव विद्रुतान्। युधिष्ठिरमथाभ्येत्य तं वृत्तान्तं न्यवेदयत्॥
en: Then learning from the other ascetics there that they had all fled away he came and communicated the news to Yudhishthira.

sn: ततस्ते पाण्डवाः सर्वे प्रत्यागमनकाक्षिणः। प्रतीक्षन्तः कियत्कालं जितात्मानोऽवतस्थिरे॥
en: Thereupon all the self-controlled Pandavas, awaiting their arrival, remained in expectation for some time.

sn: निशीथेऽभ्येत्य चाकस्मादस्मान् स छलयिष्यति कथं च निस्तरेमास्मात् कृच्छ्राद् दैवोपसादितात्॥
en: Yudhisthira said: Coming in the dead of night the ascetics will impose on us; Oh, how can we escape from this difficulty created by destiny.

sn: इति चिन्तापरान् दृष्ट्वा निःश्वसन्तो मुहुर्मुहुः। उवाच वचनं श्रीमान् कृष्णः प्रत्यक्षतां गतः॥
en: Seeing them thus stricken with anxiety and breathing long deep sighs frequently the graceful Krishna suddenly appeared before them and said,

sn: श्रीकृष्ण उवाच भवतामापदं ज्ञात्वा ऋषेः परमकोपनात्। द्रौपद्या चिन्तितः पार्था अहं सत्वरमागतः॥
en: Krishna said: O son of Pritha, knowing your difficulty from the highly wrathful Rishi implored by Draupadi I soon came here.

sn: न भयं विद्यते तस्मादृषेर्दुर्वाससोऽल्पकम्। तेजसा भवतां भीतः पूर्वमेव पलायितः॥
en: Now you have not the least fear from the ascetic Durvasa; afraid of your ascetic powers, he has already fled away.

sn: धर्मनित्यास्तु ये केचिन्न ते सीदन्ति कहिचित्। आपृच्छे वो गमिष्यामि नियतं भद्रमस्तु वः॥
