en: Those who always abide by virtue never suffer. I now ask your permission to return home; may good always betide you.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच श्रुत्वेरितं केशवस्य बभूवुः स्वस्थमानसाः। द्रौपद्या सहिताः पार्थास्तमूचुर्विगतज्वराः॥ त्वया नाथेन गोविन्द दुस्तरामापदं विभो। तीर्णाः प्लवमिवासाद्य मज्जमाना महार्णवे॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Hearing Kashava's words the sons of Pritha along with Draupadi became easy in mind and relieved from anxiety they said, O lord, O Govinda, as persons drowning in the vast deep, reach shore by means of a boat, so have we, by your protection, overcome this great difficulty.

sn: स्वस्ति साधय भद्रं ते इत्याज्ञातो ययौ पुरीम्। पाण्डवाश्च महाभाग द्रौपद्या सहिताः प्रभो॥
en: Now go in peace; may good betide you. Thus commanded he repaired to his own city and the Pandavas too, O great king, O lord, long with Draupadi.

sn: ऊषुः प्रहष्टमनसो विहरन्तो वनाद् वनम्। इति तेऽभिहितं राजन् यत् पृष्टोऽहमिह त्वया॥
en: Delightedly spent their days wandering from forest to forest. O king, I have thus, as asked by you, recounted the story.

sn: एवंविधान्यलीकानि धार्तराष्ट्रैर्दुरात्मभिः। पाण्डवेषु वनस्थेषु प्रयुक्तानि वृथाभवन्॥
en: It was in this way the evil desires of the wicked sons of Dhritarastra about the Pandavas in the forest, were baffled.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तस्मिन् बहुमृगेऽरण्ये अटमाना महारथाः। काम्यके भरतश्रेष्ठा विजहस्ते यथामराः॥
en: Viashampayana said : Those mighty car-warriors, the foremost of the Bharata race, wandering like immortals in the forest of Kamyaka abounding in many deer, were pleased.

sn: प्रेक्षमाणा बहुविधान् वनोद्देशान् समन्ततः। यथर्तुकालरम्याश्च वनराजीः सुपुष्पिताः॥
en: Beholding various wild tracts of country on all sides, the woodland decorated with the beautiful, blossming season flowers.

sn: पाण्डवा मृगयाशीलाश्चरन्तस्तन्महद् वनम्। विजहुरिन्द्रप्रतिमाः कञ्चित् कालमरिंदम॥
en: Those Indra-like Pandavas, fond of hunting and subdues of their enemies, lived there for some time wandering in that huge forest.

sn: ततस्ते यौगपद्येन ययुः सर्वे चतुर्दिशम्। मृगयां पुरुषव्याघ्रा ब्राह्मणार्थे परंतपाः॥ द्रौपदीमाश्रमे न्यस्य तृणबिन्दोरनुज्ञया। महर्षेर्दीप्ततपसो धौम्यस्य च पुरोधसः॥
en: One day those men, those repressors of their enemies, wandered about on all sides, in search of game for feeding the Brahmanas who were with them, leaving Draupadi alone in the hermitage with the permission of Trinabindu the great ascetic of burning asceticism and their priest Dhaumya.

sn: ततस्तु राजा सिन्धूनां वार्द्धक्षत्रिर्महायशाः। विवाहकामः शाल्वेयान् प्रयात: सोऽभवत् तदा॥
en: At that time the illustrious king of Sindhu, the son of Vriddhakshatra was, for marriage, going to the territory of Shalva,

sn: महता परिबहेण राजयोग्येन संवृतः। राजभिर्बहुभिः सार्धमुपायात् काम्यक च सः॥
en: Dressed in his best royal robe and accompanied by many princes he halted at the forest of Kamayaka.

sn: वपुषा बिभ्रती तां तत्रापश्यत् प्रियां भार्यां पाण्डवानां यशस्विनीम्। तिष्ठन्तीमाश्रमद्वारि द्रौपदी निर्जने वने।॥
en: In that solitary place he found the handsome Draupadi, the beloved and the illustrious wife of the Pandavas, standing at the threshold of the hermitage.

sn: विभ्राजमानां रूपमुत्तमम्। भ्राजयन्तीं वनोद्देशं नीलाभ्रमिव विद्युतम्॥
en: She appeared in her form having the most excellent beauty, shedding lustre on woodland like lightning illuminating masses of dark clouds.

sn: अप्सरा देवकन्या वा माया वा देवनिर्मिता। इति कृत्वाञ्जलिं सर्वे ददृशुस्तामनिन्दिताम्॥
en: (Thinking): “Is she an Apsara or the daughter of a god or a celestials phantom,” they all with joined hands, stood gazing on the perfect and faultless beauty of her person.

sn: ततः स राजा सिन्धूनां वार्द्धक्षत्रिर्जयद्रथः। विस्मितस्त्वनवद्यागीं दृष्ट्वा दुष्टमानसः॥
en: Seeing that lady of faultless feature, Jayadratha, the king of Sindhu, the son of Vriddhakshatra, possessed by evil intention.

sn: स कोटिकास्यं राजानमब्रवीत् काममोहितः। कस्य त्वेषानवद्याङ्गी यदि वापि न मानुषी॥
en: Possessed by desire he said to the prince named Kotikasya, “Who is this lady of faultless feature? Is she a human being?

sn: विवाहार्थो न मे कश्चिदिमां प्राप्यातिसुन्दरीम्। एतामेवाहमादाय गमिष्यामि स्वमालयम्॥
en: I do not desire to marry if I can secure this exquisitely beautiful lady. Taking her with me I shall go back to my house.

sn: गच्छ जानीहि सौम्येमां कस्य वात्र कुतोऽपि वा। किमर्थमागता सुभूरिदं कण्टकितं वनम्॥
en: O gentle sir, go and enquire who she is and whence she has come and why she, of fine eyebrows, has come to this forest full of thorns.

sn: अपि नाम वरारोहा मामेषा लोकसुन्दरी। भजेदद्यायतापाङ्गी सुदती तनुमध्यमा॥
en: was Will this most excellent beauty of the world, this slender-waisted lady, having beautiful teeth and large eyes, accept me as her lord?

sn: अप्यहं कृतकामः स्यामिमां प्राप्य वरस्त्रियम्। गच्छ जानीहि को न्वस्या नाथ इत्येव कोटिक॥ स कोटिकास्यस्तच्छ्रुत्वा रथात् प्रस्कन्द्य कुण्डली। उपेत्य पप्रच्छ तदा क्रोष्टा व्याघ्रवधूमिव॥
en: I shall certainly consider myself successful if I can obtain this best of females. Go Kotika and learn who her husband is.” Hearing this Kotikasya, wearing a Kundala, jumped out of the car and approached her as a jackal comes near a tigress and spoke to her.

sn: कोटिक उवाच मेकाऽऽश्रमे तिष्ठसि शोभमाना। देदीप्यमानाग्निशिखेव नक्तं व्याधूयमाना पवनेन सुभूः॥
en: Kotikasya said : O fair one, who are you that stand alone leaning on a branch of the Kadamba tree at this hermitage and looking majestic like flame of fire burning at night and fanned by the wind?

sn: अतीव रूपेण समन्विता त्वं न चाप्यरण्येषु बिभेषि किं नु। देवी नु यक्षी यदि दानवी वा वराप्सरा दैत्यवराङ्गना वा॥
en: You are endued with great beauty; do you not feel any fear in this forest? Are you a goddess or a Yakshi or a Danavi or the beautiful wife of a Daitya?

sn: वपुष्मती वोरगराजकन्या वनेचरी वा क्षणदाचरस्त्री। यद्येव राज्ञो वरुणस्य पत्नी यमस्य सोमस्य धनेश्वरस्य॥
en: Or a daughter of the king of serpents or the wife of a night ranger or the wife of Varuna or of Yama or of Soma or of Kubera who assuming a human form are wandering in this forest?

sn: धातुर्विधातुः सवितुर्विभोर्वा शक्रस्य वा त्वं सदनात् प्रपन्ना। न ह्येव नः पृच्छसि ये वयं स्म न चापि जानीम् तवेह नाथम्॥
en: Or have you come from the palace of Dhata or Vidhata or of Savita or of Vibhu or of Shakra? You do not ask us who we are, nor do we know who is your lord.

sn: वयं हि मानं तव वर्धयन्तः पृच्छाम भद्रे प्रभवं प्रभुं च। आचक्ष्व बन्धूंश्च पतिं कुलं च तत्त्वेन यच्चेह करोषि कार्यम्॥
en: Increasing your respect we do ask you. O gentle lady, who is your heroic father. Tell us the names of your husband, relatives, your race and what you do here.

sn: अहं तु राज्ञः सुरथस्य पुत्रो कोटिकास्येति विदुर्मनुष्याः। असौ तु यस्तिष्ठति काञ्चनाङ्गे रथे हुतोऽग्निश्चयने यथैव॥ त्रिगर्तराजः कमलायताक्षि क्षेमङ्करो नाम स एष वीरः।
en: I am the son of the king Suratha, whom the people know as Kotikasya. That man who sits on the golden car, like sacrificial fire on the altar, is the king of Trigarta having eyes like lotus petals; that hero is known by the name of Kshemankara;

sn: अस्मात् परस्त्वेष महाधनुष्मान्। पुत्रः कुलिन्दाधिपतेर्वरिष्ठः॥ निरीक्षते त्वां विपुलायताक्षः सुपुष्पितः पर्वतवासनित्यः।
en: Behind him is the great bowman that one of arge eyes, adorned with blazing garlands gazing on you, the famous son of the king of Kulinda. Who always lives on mountain.

sn: असौ तु यः पुष्करिणीसमीपे श्यामो युवा तिष्ठति दर्शनीयः॥ इक्ष्वाकुराज्ञः सुबलस्य पुत्रः स एव हन्ता द्विषतां सुगात्रि।
en: O beautiful lady, that dark and handsome young man who is standing at the brink of the tank. Is the son of the Ikshvaku king Subala; he is the slayer of his elements.

sn: यस्यानुचक्रं ध्वजिनः प्रयान्ति सौवीरका द्वादश राजपुत्राः॥ शोणाश्वयुक्तेषु रथेषु सर्वे मखेषु दीप्ता इव हव्यवाहाः। अङ्गारकः कुञ्जरो गुप्तकश्च शत्रुञ्जयः संजयसुप्रवृद्धौ॥ भयंकरोऽथ भ्रमरो रविश्व शूरः प्रतापः कुहनश्च नामा यं घट सहस्रा रथिनोऽनुयान्ति नागा हयाश्चैव पदातिनश्च॥ जयद्रथो नाम यदि श्रुतस्ते सौवीरराजः सुभगे स एषः।
en: If you have ever heard of the name Jayadratha, the king of Sauviras, he is there at the head of six thousand cars, with horses and elephants and followed by twelve Sauvira princes carrying his peanons, namely Angaraka, Kunjara Guptaka, Shatrunjaya, Sanjaya, Supravriddha, Bhayankara, Bhramara, Ravi, Shura, Pratapa and Kuhana, all riding on cars drawn by chestnut steeds and looking like the fire on the sacrificial altar.

sn: तस्यापरे भ्रातरोऽदीनसत्त्वा बलाहकानीकविदिारणाद्याः॥
en: The brothers of the king namely the mighty Balahaka, Anika, Vidarana and others also constitute his following.

sn: सौवीरवीराः प्रवरा युवानो राजानमेते बलिनोऽनुयान्ति। एतैः सहायैरुपयाति राजा मरुद्गणैरिन्द्र इवाभिगुप्तः॥
en: These mighty, youthful and leading heroes of Sauvira race are following the king. He is journeying in the company of these friends of his, like Indra surrounded by Maruts.

sn: अजानतां ख्यापय नः सुकेशि कस्यासि भार्या दुहिता च कस्य॥
en: O you having fine hair, tell us, who do not know whose wife and whose daughter you are.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच अथाब्रवीद् द्रौपदी राजपुत्री पृष्टा शिबीनां प्रवरेण तेन। अवेक्ष्य मन्दं प्रविमुच्य शाखां संगृह्णती कौशिकमुत्तरीयम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Being thus accosted that foremost of Shibi's race, the princess Draupadi, looking gently, leaving of the Kadamba branch and arranging her silken raiment, said,

sn: बुद्ध्याभिजानामि नरेन्द्रपुत्र न मादृशी त्वामभिभाष्टुमर्हति। मन्यो नरो वाप्यथवपि नारी॥
en: I know it, O prince, that it is not proper for me to address you thus, there is no other man or woman who can speak with you.

sn: एका ह्यहं सम्प्रति तेन वाचं ददामि वै भद्र निबोध चेदम्। अहं शरण्ये कथमेकमेका त्वामालपेयं निरता स्वधर्मे॥
en: I am alone here just now so I should speak, know, O gentle sir, being alone in this forest, I should not speak to you, remembering the practices of our sex.

sn: जानामि च त्वां सुरथस्य पुत्रं यं कोटिकास्येति विदुर्मनुष्याः। माख्यामि बन्धून् प्रथितं कुलं च॥
en: I have learnt you to be the son of Suratha whom people know as Kotikasya; so O Shaivya, I shall tell you of my relations and illustrious race.

sn: अपत्यमस्मि द्रुपदस्य राज्ञः कृष्णेति मां शैब्य विदुर्मनुष्याः। साहं वृणे पञ्च जनान् पतित्वे ये खाण्डवप्रस्थगताः श्रुतास्ते॥
en: I am the daughter of the king Drupada, O Shaivya, people know me as Krishna; I have elected five men as my husbands of whom you may have heard while they were living in Khandavaprastha.

sn: युधिष्ठिरो भीमसेनार्जुनौ च माझ्याश्च पुत्रौ पुरुषप्रवीरौ। ते मां निवेश्येह दिशश्चतस्रो विभज्य पार्था मृगयां प्रयाताः॥
en: Those foremost of men, Yudhishthira, Bhimasena, Arjuna and the two sons of Madri, leaving me hear and having assigned four quarters, have gone out on hunting.

sn: प्राची राजा दक्षिणां भीमसेनो जयः प्रतीची यमजावुदीचीम्। मन्ये त तेषां रथसत्तमानां कालोऽभितः प्राप्त इहोपयातुम्॥
en: The king has gone to the east, Bhimasena towards the south, Arjuna to the west and the twin brothers towards the north. Me-thinks, the time of the arrival of those leading carwarriors, has come.

sn: सम्मानिता यास्यथ तैर्यथेष्टं विमुच्य वाहानवरोहयध्वम्। प्रियातिथिर्धर्मसुतो महात्मा प्रोतो भविष्यत्यभिवीक्ष्य युष्मान्॥
en: Do you get down and dismiss your carriage so that yet may go after receiving a befitting welcome from them. The high-souled son of Dharma is fond of guests and will, in sooth, be glad to see you.

sn: एतावदुक्त्वा दुपदात्मजा सा शैव्यात्मजं चन्द्रमुखी प्रतीता। विवेश तां पर्णशालां प्रशस्तां संचिन्त्य तेषामतिथित्वमर्थे॥
en: Having thus addressed Shaivya's son, the daughter of Draupadi, with a face beautiful as the moon, remembering well the hospitable tendency of her husband, entered her spacious cottage.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Jayadratha
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तथाऽऽसीनेषु सर्वेषु तेषु राजसु भारत। यदुक्तं कृष्णया सार्धं तत् सर्वं प्रत्यवेदयत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said: O descendant of Bharata, when all those princes were seated at rest, he related to them the conversation that he had with Krishna.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Jayadratha
sn: कोटिकास्यवचः श्रुत्वा शैब्यं सौवीरकोऽब्रवीत्। यदा वाचं व्याहरन्त्यामस्यां मे रमते मनः॥ सीमन्तिनीनां मुख्यायां विनिवृत्तः कथं भवान्। एतां दृष्ट्वा स्त्रियो मेऽन्या यथा शाखामृगस्त्रियः॥ प्रतिभान्ति महाबाहो सत्यमेतद् ब्रवीमि ते। दर्शनादेव हि मनस्तया मेऽपहृतं भृशम्॥ तां समाचक्ष्व कल्याणी यदि स्याच्छैव्य मानुषी।
en: Hearing the words of Kotikasya, the Sauvira hero said to Shaivya, "Hearing her words my mind has been inclined towards her. Why have you come unsuccessful from that best of females; having once seen this lady other women appear to me as so many monkeys. O mighty-armed heroes, I tell you the truth. From the very moment I saw her my mind has been entirely captivated by her. Tell me, O Shaivya, if that excellent lady is a human being."

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Jayadratha
sn: कोटिक उवाच एषा वै दो दी कृष्णा राजपुत्री यशस्विनी॥ पञ्चानां पाण्डुपुत्राणां महिषी सम्मता भृशम्। सर्वेषां चैव पार्थानां प्रिया बहुमता सती॥ तया समेत्य सौवीर सौवीराभिमुखो व्रजा
en: Kotika said : She is the illustrious princes, Krishna Draupadi. She is recognised queen of the five sons of Pandu and chaste damsel is highly regarded and loved by all the Parthas. Taking her with you, O Sauvira, proceed towards Sauvira.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Jayadratha
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्तः प्रत्युवाच पश्यामि द्रौपदीमिति॥ पति: सौवीरसिन्धूनां दुष्टभावो जयद्रथः।
en: Vaishampayana said: Being thus addressed the evil-minded Jayadratha, the king of Sindhu, Sauvira and other countries said: "I wish to see Draupadi.”

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Jayadratha
sn: स प्रविश्याश्रमं पुण्यं सिंहगोष्ठं वृको यथा।॥ आत्मना सप्तमः कृष्णामिदं वचनमब्रवीत्। कुशलं ते वरारोहे भर्तारस्तेऽप्यनामयाः॥ येषां कुशलकामासि तेऽपि कच्चिदनामयाः।
en: Like a wolf entering the den of lion, he with six followers entered the holy hermitage and said to Krishna: "Are you well, O excellent lady? Are your husbands well? Are they all well whose prosperity you seek?"

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Jayadratha
sn: द्रौपद्युवाच अपि ते कुशलं राजन् राष्ट्र कोशे बले तथा॥ कच्चिदेकः शिबीनाढ्यान् सौवीरान् सह सिन्धुभिः। अनुतिष्ठसि धर्मेण ये चान्ये विजितास्त्वया॥
en: Draupadi said : It is all well with your kingdom, countries, treasury and army? Are you, as sole ruler, governing justly the prosperous countries of Sauvira, Shibi, Sindhu and others, that you have brought under your sway?

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Jayadratha
sn: कौरव्यः कुशली राजा कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः। अहं च भ्रातरश्चास्य यांश्चान्यान् परिपृच्छसि॥ पाद्यं प्रतिगृहाणेदमासनं च नृपात्मज।
en: Kunti's son Yudhishthira, of the Kuru race, his brother, myself and all of whom you have enquired are well? O prince, accept this water to wash your feet and seat. I offer you fifty animals for the breakfast of your followers.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Jayadratha
sn: जयद्रथ उवाच एहि मे रथमारोह सुखमाप्नुहि केवलम्॥ गतश्रीकांश्च्युतान् राज्यात् कृपणान् गतचेतसः। अरण्यवासिनः पार्थान् नानुरोढुं त्वमर्हसि॥ नैव प्राज्ञा गतश्रीकं भर्तारमुपयुञ्जते। युञ्जानमनुयुञ्जीत न श्रियः संक्षये वसेत्॥
en: Jayadratha said: "All well with me; by offering us breakfast you have already done it. Come ride my chariot and be completely happy. It does not behoove you to regard the wretched sons of Pritha who are living in the forest, whose prowess has been spoiled, whose kingdom has been taken away and whose prosperity is gone. A woman of your good sense does not devote herself to a poor husband. She should follow her husband in prosperity and relinquish him when he is in adversity.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Jayadratha
sn: श्रिया विहीना राष्ट्राच्च विनष्टाः शाश्वतीः समाः। अलं ते पाण्डुपुत्राणां भक्त्या क्लेशमुपासितुम्॥
en: The sons of Pandu have forever fallen from their high dignity and have lost their kingdom? You should not therefore, out of regard, participate in their miseries.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Jayadratha
sn: भार्या मे भव सुश्रोणि त्यजैनान् सुखमाप्नुहि। अखिलान् सिन्धुसौवीरानाप्नुहि त्वं मया सह॥
en: O you of beautiful hips, renouncing them, be happy by becoming my wife and share with me the kingdoms of Sindhu and Sauvira."

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Jayadratha
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच इत्युक्ता सिन्धुराजेन वाक्यं हृदयकम्पनम्। कृष्णा तस्मादपाक्रामद् देशात् सभृकुटीमुखी॥
en: Being thus addressed by the king of Sindhu with those heart-rending words, Krishna went away from that place with a frowning face.

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Jayadratha
sn: अवमत्यास्य तद् वाक्यमाक्षिप्य च सुमध्यमा। मैवमित्यब्रवीत् कृष्णा लज्जस्वेति च सैन्धव॥
en: Disregarding his words and remonstrating with him that youthful Krishna said to the king of Saindhava, “Do not speak this again. Are you not ashamed?”

description: The conversation between Draupadi and Jayadratha
sn: सा काक्षमाणा भर्तृणामुपयातमनिन्दिता। विलोभयामास परं वाक्यैर्वाक्यानि युञ्जती॥
en: Then expecting the return of her husbands that lady of irreproachable character, began to beguile him completely with intricate words.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच सरोषरागोपहतेन वल्गुना सरागनेत्रेण नतोन्नतभ्रुवा। मुखेन विस्फूर्य सुवीरराष्ट्रपं ततोऽब्रवीत् तं दुपदात्मजा पुनः॥
en: Vaishampayana said: Having her naturally handsome face suffused with crimson arising from ire, with eyes inflamed and eye brows bent in anger the daughter of Drupada remonstrated with the king of Sauviras and again said,

sn: नभिब्रुवन् मूढ न लज्जसे कथम्। महेन्द्रकल्पान् निरतान् स्वकर्मसु स्थितान् समूहेष्वपि यक्षरक्षसाम्॥
en: O fool, are you not ashamed to use such insulting words to those illustrious and dreadful heroes, each like Indra himself, who all abide by their duties and never wave in fight even with hosts of Yakshas and Rakshasas.

sn: न किंचिदीड्यं प्रवदन्ति पापं वनेचरं वा गृहमेधिनं वा। तपस्विनं सम्परिपूर्णविद्यं भषन्ति हैवं श्वनराः सुवीरा॥
en: O Sauvira, (the wise) never speak ill of learned persons carrying on devout penances, no matter whether they live in forest or houses; it is only the mean like dogs who speak so.

sn: देतादृशे क्षत्रियसंनिवेशे। यस्त्वाद्य पातालमुखे पतन्तं पाणौ गृहीत्वा प्रतिसंहरेत्॥
en: Me-thinks, there is none in this assemblage of Kshatriyas who can hold you by hand to save from falling into the pit you have dug under your feet.

sn: मुपत्यकां हैमवती चरन्तम्। दण्डीव यूथादपसेधसि त्वं यो जेतुमाशंससि धर्मराजम्॥
en: Expecting to defeat the pious Yudhishthira, you really hope to separate, with a stick in hand, the leader of elephants, huge as a mountain peak, with temporal juice trickling down from its rent temple, from a herd ranging in the Himalayan valleys.

sn: बाल्यात् प्रसुप्तस्य महाबलस्य सिंहस्य पक्ष्माणि मुखाल्लुनासि। पदा समाहत्य पलायमानः क्रुद्धं यदा द्रक्ष्यसि भीमसेनम्॥
en: Out of childishness, you are arousing a sleeping lion to pluck the hair from off his face. You shall however have to run away when you shall sec the enraged Bhimasena.

sn: महाबलं घोरतरं प्रवृद्धं जातं हरिं पर्वतकन्दरेषु। प्रसुप्तमुचं प्रपदेन हंसि यः क्रुद्धमायोत्स्यसि जिष्णुमुचम्॥
en: Your attempt at an encounter with the dreadful Jishnu is like arousing a powerful, dreadful, full grown and furious lion asleep in a mountain cave.

sn: कृष्णोरगौ तीक्ष्णमुखौ द्विजिह्वौ मत्तः पदाऽऽक्रामसि पुच्छदेशे। यः पाण्डवाभ्यां पुरुषोत्तमाभ्यां जघन्यजाभ्यां प्रयुयुत्ससे त्वम्॥
en: The combat that you wish to have with those two youthful younger Pandavas is like the act of a fool of wantonly trampling on the tails to two venomous black cobras with bifurcated tongues.

sn: यथा च वेणुः कदली नलो वा फलन्त्यभावाय भूतयेऽऽत्मनः। मादास्यसे कर्कटकीव गर्भम्॥
en: As the bamboo, the reed and the plantain bear fruit only to die and not to grow in size, as a crab conceives only to perish so you will by laying your hands on me who am protected by these powerful heroes.

sn: जयद्रथ उवाच जानामि कृष्णे विदितं ममैतद् यथाविधास्ते नरदेवपुत्राः न त्वेवमेतेन विभीषणेन शक्या वयं त्रासयितुं त्वयाद्य॥
en: Jayadratha said : I know all this, O Krishna, as also how those princes are. You shall not be able to frighten me now with these threats.

sn: वयं पुनः सप्तदशेषु कृष्णे कुलेषु सर्वेऽनवमेषु जाताः। घड्भ्योगुणेभ्योऽभ्यधिका विहीनान् मन्यामहे द्रौपदि पाण्डुपुत्रान्॥
en: We too, O Krishna, are born in the seventeen races and are endowed with six royal qualities. We consider, O Draupadi, Pandavas as inferior men.

sn: सा क्षिप्रमातिष्ठ गजं रथं वा न वाक्यमात्रेण वयं हि शक्याः। आशंस वा त्वं कृपणं वदन्ती सौवीरराजस्य पुनः प्रसादम्॥
en: Therefore soon ride this elephant or car for you cannot dissuade us with mere words; speaking less boastfully better seek the mercy of the king of Sauviras.

sn: द्रौपद्युवाच महाबला किंत्विह दुर्बलेव सौवीरराजस्य मताहमस्मि। नाहं प्रमाथादिह सम्प्रतीता सौवीरराजं कृपणं वदेयम्॥
en: Draupadi said : Although so powerful, why I am taken by the king of Sauvira to be so powerless? I cannot for fear of violence do mean act myself before that king.

sn: यस्या हि कृष्णौ पदवी चरेतां समास्थितावेकरथे समेतौ। न्मनुष्यमात्रः कृपणः कुतोऽन्यः॥
en: Even Indra himself cannot abduct her for whose protection Krishna and Arjuna, riding in the saine chariot, would follow; what to speak of any other weak human beings?

sn: यदा किरीटी परवीरघाती निघ्नन् रथस्थो द्विषतां मनांसि। मदन्तरे त्वद्ध्वजिनीं प्रवेष्टा कक्षं दहनग्निरिवोष्णगेषु॥
en: When Arjuna, the slayer of hostile heroes, riding on his car, on my behalf, shall enter your ranks, striking terror into every heart, he will destroy everything on all sides like fire consuming a pack of dry grass in summer.

sn: जनार्दनः सान्धकवृष्णिवीरो महेष्वासाः केकयाश्चापि सर्वे। एते हि सर्वे मम राजपुत्राः प्रहृष्टरूपाः पदवी चरेयुः॥
en: Janardana, with heroes of Andhaka and Vrishni race, the mighty bowmen of the Kaikeya tribe, all these princes will follow me arduously.

sn: मौर्वीविसृष्टाः स्तनयित्नुघोषा गाण्डीवमुक्तास्त्वतिवेगवन्तः। हस्तं समाहत्य धनंजयस्य भीमाः शब्दं घोरतरं नदन्ति॥
en: The dreadful shafts of Dhananjaya shot from the string of Gandiva and propelled by his arms shoot through the air with grcat force and create a dreadful sound.

sn: गाण्डीवमुक्तांश्च महाशरौघान् पतंगसङ्घानिव शीघ्रवेगान्। यदा द्रष्टास्यर्जुनं वीर्यशालिनं तदा स्वबुद्धिं प्रतिनिन्दितासि॥
en: When you shall see the collection of dreadful shafts discharged by Arjuna from Gandiva, quick-coursing and like locusts you shall repent for your own folly.

sn: सशङ्खघोषः सतलत्रघोषो गाण्डीवधन्वा मुहुरुद्वहंश्च। यदा शरानर्पयिता तवोरसि तदा मनस्ते किमिवाभविष्यत्॥
en: Think yourself what will then happen when that heroes, armed with Gandiva and with gloves reverberating with the strokes of his bow string, will repeatedly pierce your breast with arrows.

sn: गदाहस्तं भीममभिद्रवन्तं माद्रीपुत्रौ सम्पतन्तौ दिशश्च। अमर्षजं क्रोधविषं वमन्तौ दृष्ट्वा चिरं तापमुपैष्यसेऽधम॥
en: Beholding Bhima advance towards you with mace in his hands and the two sons of Madri range in all quarters vomiting forth the venom of their ire, you shall meet with everlasting repentance.

sn: यथा वाहं नातिचरे कथंचित् पतीन् महार्हान् मनसापि जातु। तेनाद्य सत्येन वशीकृतं त्वां द्रष्टास्मि पाथैः परिकृष्यमाणम्॥
en: As I have never proved false even in my mind to my worthy husbands, so by that merit I shall see you today vanquished and dragged by the sons of Pritha.

sn: न सम्भ्रमं गन्तुमहं हि शक्ष्ये त्वया नृशंसेन विकृष्यमाणा। समागताहं हि कुरुप्रवीरैः पुनर्वनं काम्यकमागतास्मि॥
en: Ruthless as you are, you cannot terrify me by seizing me violently; for as soon as those Kuru heroes will see me they will bring me back to the Kamyaka forest.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच सा ताननुप्रेक्ष्य विशालनेत्रा जिघृक्षमाणानवभर्ल्सयन्ती। प्रोवाच मा मा स्पृशतेति भीता धौम्यं प्रचुक्रोश पुरोहितं सा॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Thereupon seeing them ready to seize her violently that of expansive eyes reinonstrated with him and said, "Do not one pollute me by your touch." Then terrified she called for her spiritual guide Dhaumya.

sn: जग्राह तामुत्तरवस्त्रदेशे जयद्रथस्तं समवाक्षिपत् सा। तया समाक्षिप्ततनुः स पाप: पपात शाखीव निकृत्तमूलः॥
en: Jayadratha caught hold of her by her upper garment but she pushed him with great force; pushed by her, that sinful wretch fell down on earth like an uprooted tree.

sn: प्रगृह्यमाणा तु महाजवेन मुहुविनिःश्वस्य च राजपुत्री। सा कृष्यमाणा रथमारोह धौम्यस्य पादावभिवाद्य कृष्णा॥
en: But being seized by him again with great force the princess sighed again and again; then dragged by him Krishna, worshipping the feet of Dhaumya, ascended the car.

sn: धौम्य उवाच नेयं शक्या त्वया नेतुमविजित्य महारथान्। धर्मं क्षत्रस्य पौराणमवेक्षस्व जयद्रथ॥
en: Dhaumya said : Without defeating the mighty car-warriors she should not be taken away by you; O Jayadratha, you should observe this ancient custom of the Kshatriyas.

sn: क्षुद्रं कृत्वा फलं पापं त्वं प्राप्स्यसि न संशयः। आसाद्य पाण्डवान् वीरान् धर्मराजपुरोगमान्॥
en: Forsooth you shall reap the fruit of your this mean action when you shall meet the heroic Pandavas with the pious Yudhishthira at their head.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच इत्युक्त्वा ह्रियमाणां तां राजपुत्रीं यशस्विनीम्। अन्वगच्छत् तदा धौम्यः पदातिगणमध्यगः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having said this and entered into his rank of infantry he followed that princes, who was being carried away.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततो दिशः सम्प्रविहृत्य पार्था मृगान् वराहान् महिषांश्च हत्वा। धनुर्धराः श्रेष्ठतमाः पृथिव्यां पृथक् चरन्तः सहिता बभूवुः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having ranged in all directions and wandered on earth separately, those Parthas, the foremost of bowmen killing many deers, bear and buffaloes met together.

sn: ततो मृगज्यालगणानुकीर्ण महावनं तद् विहगोपघुष्टम्। भ्रातूंश्च तानभ्यवदद् युधिष्ठिरः श्रुत्वा गिरो व्याहरतां मृगाणाम्॥
en: Seeing that huge forest abounding in many deer and wild animals, resonant with the shrill cries of birds and hearing the yells of the wild animals, Yudhishthira said to his brothers,

sn: आदित्यदीप्तां दिशमभ्युपेत्य मृगा द्विजाः क्रूरमिमे वदन्ति। आयासमुचं प्रतिवेदयन्तो महावनं शत्रुभिर्बाध्यमानम्॥
en: “Those birds and wild animals flying to the direction lighted up by the sun are emitting discordant cries and displaying excitement. This shows that this mighty forest has been invaded by the enemies.

sn: मनो हि मे दूयति दह्यते च। रुद्धूयते प्राणपतिः शरीरे॥
en: Let us without delay desist; no more with game; my heart aches and seems to burn; clouding the intellect, the soul, in my body, seems to fly away.

sn: सरः सुपर्णेन हृतोरगं यथा राष्ट्रं यथाराजकमात्तलक्ष्मि। एवंविधं मे प्रतिभाति काम्यकं शौण्डैर्यथा पीतरसश्च कुम्भः॥
en: Like a tank freed from serpents by Garuda, a pot drained of its contents by thirsty men, a kingdom shorn of its king and its prosperity this forest of Kamyaka appears to me.'

sn: महाजवैर्वाजिभिरुह्यमानाः। स्तदाऽऽश्रमायाभिमुखा बभूवुः॥
en: Thereupon those heroes drove towards their hermitage on mighty and beautifully made cars, drawn by exceedingly fleet horses of Saindhava breed and possessed of the speed of hurricane.

sn: तेषां तु गोमायुरनल्पघोषो निवर्ततां वाममुपेत्य पार्श्वम्। प्रव्याहरत् तत् प्रविमृश्य राजा प्रोवाच भीमं च धनंजयं च॥
en: On their left side they espied a jackal yelling hideously. Marking it attentively the king (Yudhishthira), said to Bhima and Dhananjaya.

sn: यथा वदत्येष विहीनयोनिः शालावृको वाममुपेत्य पार्श्वम्। सुव्यक्तमस्मानवमन्य पापैः कृतोऽभिमर्दः कुरुभिः प्रसह्य॥
en: “This jackal of inferior breed, sneaking to our left side, is speaking a language, that clearly shows that violent oppression has been commenced by the sinful Kurus disregarding us.

sn: इत्येव ते तद् वनमाविशन्तो महत्यरण्ये मृगयां चरित्वा। बालामपश्यन्त तदा रुदन्ती धात्रेयिकां प्रेष्यवधू प्रियायाः॥
en: Having given up the chase they in that great forest entered the grove containing their hermitage and there they saw their beloved one's maid, the girl Dhatreyika weeping and sobbing.

sn: तामिन्द्रसेनस्त्वरितोऽभिसृत्य रथादवप्लुत्य ततोऽभ्यधावत्। प्रोवाच चैनां वचनं नरेन्द्र धात्रेयिकामन्तितरस्तदानीम्॥
en: Then descending from the car and quickly approaching Dhatreyika, who was then greatly stricken with grief, Indrasena, O king, asked her (saying).

sn: किं रोदिषि त्वं पतिता धरण्यां किं ते मुखं शुष्यति दीनवर्णम्। कच्चिन्न पापैः सुनृशंसकृद्भिः प्रमाथिता द्रौपदी राजपुत्री॥
en: "Why do you weep lying down on earth and why is your mouth dried and pale? I hope the princess Draupadi has not been injured by any cruel wretch.

sn: अचिन्त्यरूपा सुविशालनेत्रा शरीरतुल्या कुरुपुङ्गवानाम्। यद्येव देवी पृथिवीं प्रविष्टा दिवं प्पपन्नाप्यश्चवा समुद्रम्॥ तस्या गमिष्यन्ति पदे हि पार्था यथा हि संतप्यति धर्मपुत्रः।
en: She is possessed of incomparable beauty, large eyes and is the second self of every one of those foremost of Kuru race. Dharma's son has grown so anxious that if the princess has entered into the earth or soared into heavens or has gone to the bottom of the deep, he and his brothers will go there in search of her.

sn: को हीदृशानामरिमर्दनानां क्लेशक्षमानामपराजितानाम्॥ दनुत्तमं रत्नमिव प्रमूढः।
en: Who could that fool be who could carry away the priceless jewel belonging to the powerful and ever victorious sons of Pandu, those repressors of foes, which is dear to them like the very life.

sn: न बुध्यते नाथवतौमिहाद्य बहिश्चरं हृदयं पाण्डवानाम्॥ कस्याद्य कायं प्रतिभिद्य घोरा महीं प्रवेक्ष्यन्ति शिताः शराग्र्याः।
en: I cannot perceive (any one who could carry her) having (such powerful heroes) as her husband and who is like the walking embodiment of the sons of Pandu. Piercing whose body today, the dreadful and sharpened ends of shafts shall enter the earth?

sn: मा त्वं शुचस्तां प्रति भीरु विद्धि यथाद्य कृष्णा पुनरेष्यतीति॥ निहत्य सर्वान् द्विषतः समग्रान् पार्थाः समेष्यन्त्यथा याज्ञसेन्या।
en: Do not weep for her, O timid girl; know that Krishna shall come back even this very day. Having slain all their enemies the sons of Pritha shall be united with Yajnaseni."

sn: अथाब्रवीच्चारु मुखं प्रमृज्य धात्रेयिका सारथिमिन्द्रसेनम्॥ जयद्रथेनापहृता प्रमथ्य पञ्चेन्द्रकल्पान् परिभूय कृष्णा। तिष्ठन्ति वानि नवान्यमूनि वृक्षाश्च न म्लान्ति तथैव भग्नाः॥
en: Then rubbing her beautiful face Dhatreyika said to the charioteer Indrasena. “Disregarding the five Indra like princess Jayadratha has carried away Krishna by force. The way pursued by him still exists for the broken branches of the trees have not yet disappeared.

sn: आवर्तयध्वं ह्यनुयात शीघ्रं न दूरयातैव हि राजपुत्री। संनह्यध्वं सर्व एवेन्द्रकल्पा महान्ति चारूणि च दंशनानि॥
en: Therefore turn your cars and follow her speedily for the princess has not gone far by this time. Taking your handsomely made precious bows and quivers.

sn: गृणीत चापानि महाधनानि शरांश्च शीघ्रं पदवीं चरध्वम्। पुरा हि निर्भर्त्सनदण्डमोहिता प्रमोहचित्ता वदनेन शुष्यता॥ ददाति कस्मैचिदनर्हते तनुं वराज्यपूर्णामिव भस्मनि स्रुचम्। पुरा तुषाग्नाविव हूयते हविः पुरा श्मशाने स्रगिवापविद्ध्यते॥ पुरा च सोमोऽध्वरगोऽवलिाते शुना यथा विप्रजने प्रमोहिते। महत्यरण्ये मृगयां चरित्वा पुरा शृगालो नलिनी विगाहते॥
en: O warriors gifted with the strength of Indra and highly precious shafts, quickly proceed in quest of her, lest overpowered by ineanness and violence and being beside herself and with a dried mouth, she may give up her person to an unworthy person as the sanctified oblation is thrown into a mass of ashes. Let not the clarified butter be poured into an unigniting fire of paddy chaff and a garland of flowers be thrown into a cremation ground. Let not the Soma juice of a sacrifice be licked up by a dog through the carelessness of the officiating priest. Let not the lily be ruthlessly torn by a jackal walking for its prey in the deep forest.

sn: मा वः प्रियायाः सुनसं सुलोचनं चन्द्रप्रभाच्छं वदनं प्रसन्नम्। स्पृश्याच्छुभं कश्चिदकृत्यकारी श्वा वै पुरोडाशमिवाध्वरस्थम्। एतानि वान्यनुयात शीनं मा वः कालः क्षिप्रमिहात्यगाद् वै॥
en: Let no mean man touch with his lips the brilliant and charming face of your wife, delightful as the rays of the moon, having high nose and beautiful eyes like a dog licking ghee kept in a sacrificial pot. Go speedily by this way and let not time go before you."

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच भद्रे प्रतिक्राम नियच्छ वाचं मास्मत्सकाशे परुषाण्यवोचः। राजानो वा यदि वा राजपुत्रा बलेन मत्ता वञ्चनां प्राप्नुवन्ति॥
en: Yudhishthira said: Go away, O gentle woman and govern your tongue; kings or princes who are inflated with the possession of power, are sure to come to grief.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एतावदुक्त्वा प्रययुर्हि शीघ्रं तान्येच वान्यनुवर्तमानाः। मुहुर्महालवदुच्छ्वसन्तो ज्यां विक्षिपन्तश्च महाधनुर्यः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Saying this, they speedily went, wending the way pointed out to them, sighing hot and hard like snakes and twanging their large bows,

sn: मुद्भूतं वै वाजिखुरप्रणुन्नम्। पदातीनां मध्यगतं च धौम्यं विक्रोशन्तं भीममभिद्रवेति॥
en: Then they saw dust raised by the hoops of the steeds belonging to his (Jayadratha's) soldiers; they saw also Dhaumya in the midst of (his) infantry bewailing and asking Bhima to go quickly.

sn: ते सान्त्व्य धौम्यं परिदीनसत्त्वाः सुखं भवानेत्विति राजपुत्राः। श्येना यथैवामिषसम्प्रयुक्ता जवेन तत् सैन्यमथाभ्यधावन्।॥
en: Then with hearts not depressed the princes, consoling Dhaumya said, "Go back cheerfully', then they rushed furiously towards that army like hawks swooping down on their prey.

sn: तेषां महेन्द्रोपमविक्रमाणां संरब्धानां धर्षणाद् याज्ञसेन्याः। क्रोधः प्रजज्वाल जयद्रथं च दृष्ट्वा प्रियां तस्य रथे स्थितां च॥
en: Endued with the strength of Indra, they had grown furious at the insult offered to Draupadi; but their anger was inflamed (the more) seeing Jayadratha and their sweet heart-seated in his car.

sn: प्रचुकुशुश्चाप्यथ सिन्धुराज वृकोदरश्चैव धनंजयश्च। स्ततो दिशः सम्मुमुहुः परेषाम्॥
en: Vrikodara, Dhananjaya, the twins and the king, those mighty bowmen called out to the king of Sindhu to stop; (at which) the enemies lost all knowledge of directions.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततो घोरतरः शब्दो वन समभवत् तदा। भीमसेनार्जुनौ दृष्ट्वा क्षत्रियाणाममर्षिणाम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said: Thereupon on beholding Bhimasena and Arjuna, the Kshatriyas, inflated, sent up a terrible shout in that forest.

sn: तेषां ध्वजाचाण्यभिवीक्ष्य राजा स्वयं दुरात्मा नरपुङ्गवानाम्। जयद्रथो याज्ञसेनीमुवाच रथे स्थितां भानुमती हतौजाः॥
en: Beholding the standards of those foremost of Kurus the wicked-minded king Jayadratha, losing all heart, said to Yajnaseni, who was seated on the car and was shining in her effulgence.

sn: आयान्तीमे पञ्च रथा महान्तो मन्ये च कृष्णे पतयस्तवैते। सा जानती ख्यापय नः सुकेशि परं परं पाण्डवानां रथस्थम्॥
en: "Five great heroes are coming, O Krishna, me-thinks they are your husbands; as you know them well, O you of fair hairs, point out which of them rides which car?

sn: द्रौपद्युवाच रनायुष्यं कर्म कृत्वातिघोरम्। एते वीराः पतयो मे समेता न वः शेषः कश्चिदिहास्ति युद्धे॥
en: Draupadi said : "Having committed such an henious deed that will shorter your life, of what use, O fool, it will be now to know the names of those great heroes; as my heroic husbands have come, none of you shall be left alive in battle.

sn: आख्यातव्यं त्वेव सर्वं मुमूर्षोर्मया तुभ्यं पृष्टया धर्म एषः। न मे व्यथा विद्यते त्वद्भयं वा सम्पश्यन्त्याः सानुजं धर्मराजम्॥
en: Still, as you, being on the point of death, have asked me, I shall relate it for such is the duty; seeing Dharmaraja with his younger brothers I have not the slightest anxiety or fear from you.

sn: यस्य ध्वजाचे नदतो मृदङ्गो नन्दोपनन्दौ मधुरौ युक्तरूपौ। एतं स्वधर्मार्थविनिश्चयज्ञं सदा जनाः कृत्यवन्तोऽनुयान्ति॥
en: (He) at whose flag-staff, two beautiful and sonorous tabors, Nanda and Upananda are always played upon, knows very well the propriety of his own acts. Successful men always follow him.

sn: य एष जाम्बूनदशुद्धगौरः प्रचण्डघोणस्तनुरायताक्षः। एतं कुरुश्रेष्ठतमं वदन्ति युधिष्ठिरं धर्मसुतं पति मे॥
en: He has a complexion like the colour of pure gold, high nose, large eyes and is of a thin make; people call my husband Yudhishthira, the son of Dharına and the foremost of Kurus.

sn: अप्येष शत्रोः शरणागतस्य दद्यात् प्राणान् धर्मचारी नृवीरः। परेह्येनं मूढ जवेन भूतये त्वमात्मनः प्राञ्जलिन्यस्तशस्त्रः॥
en: That pious, heroic man gives life even to his enemy who seeks his shelter; therefore, O fool, leaving off your weapons and with folded hands, run quickly to him for your own safety.

sn: अथाप्येनं पश्यसि यं रथस्थं महाभुजं शालमिव प्रवृद्धम्। संदष्टौष्ठं भृकुटीसंहतभ्रवं वृकोदरो नाम पतिर्ममैषः॥
en: The one, whom you see seated on the car, with long arms and tall as the Shala tree biting his lips, contracting his forehead so as to bring his two eye-brows close together, is my husband by name Vrikodara.

sn: आजानेया बलिनः साधु दान्ता महाबलाः शूरमुदावहन्ति। एतस्य कर्माण्यतिमानुषाणि भीमेति शब्दोऽस्य गतः पृथिव्याम्॥
en: Plump, strong, well-trained and powerful horses of best breed draw that heroe's chariot; his actions are super-human; he is known on earth by the name of Bhima.

sn: नास्यापराद्धाः शेषमवाप्नुवन्ति नायं वैरं विस्मरते कदाचित्। वैरस्यान्तं संविधायोपयाति पश्चाच्छान्तिं न च गच्छत्यतीव॥
en: Those who offend him are never allowed to live; he never forgets his enemy; on come pretext or other he takes revenge; and even after that he is not pacified.

sn: धनुर्धरात्र्यो धृतिमान् यशस्वी जितेन्द्रियो वृद्धसेवी नृवीरः। भ्राता च शिष्यश्च युधिष्ठिरस्य धनंजयो नाम पतिर्ममैषः॥
en: That foremost of bow-men, intelligent, illustrious, self-controlled and reverencing the old and heroic among men, is the brother and disciple of Yudhishthira. He is my husband by name Dhananjaya.

sn: यो वै न कामान्न भयान्न लोभात् त्यजेद् धर्मं न नृशंसं च कुर्यात्। स एष वैश्वानरतुल्यतेजाः कुन्तीसुतः शत्रुसहः प्रमाथी॥
en: He never relinquishes virtue out of fear, lust or anger; he never commits a cruel decd; that son of Kunti has the energy of fire, can withstand every enemy and represses his foes.

sn: यः सर्वधर्मार्थविनिश्चयज्ञो भयार्तानां भयहर्ता मनीषी। यस्योत्तमं रूपमाहुः पृथिव्यां यं पाण्डवाः परिरक्षन्ति सर्वे॥ प्राणैर्गरीयांसमनुव्रतं वै स एष वीरो नकुलः पतिर्म।
en: The other youth, proficient in Dharma and Artha, who always removes the fear of the afraid, who is gifted with high wisdom, who is protected by all the sons of Pandu, who is dearer to them even than their life, for his unflinching devotion, is my husband, the heroic Nakula.

sn: यः खड्गयोधी लघुचित्रहस्तो महांश्च धीमान् सहदेवोऽद्वितीयः॥ यस्याद्य कर्म द्रक्ष्यसे मूढसत्त्व शतक्रतोर्वा दैत्यसेनासु संख्ये। शूरः कृतास्त्रो मतिमान् मनस्वी प्रियङ्करो धर्मसुतस्य राज्ञः॥
en: That intelligent and great one, having Sahadeva for the second, is light-handed and an expert in the use of swords. O stupid man, you shall see to day his exploits in battle like those of Indra in the army of Daityas. Heroic, well-skilled in weapon, intelligent, wise, ever satisfying the king, the son of Dharma,

sn: य एष चन्द्रार्कसमानतेजा जघन्यजः पाण्डवानां प्रियश्च। बुद्ध्या समो यस्य नरो न विद्यते वक्ता तथा सत्सु विनिश्चयज्ञः॥
en: Effulgent like the rays of the moon, the favourite and the youngest born of the Pandavas, equal to whom in intelligence no man exists or in eloquence in the midst of the assembly of the wise.

sn: स एष शूरो नित्यममर्षणपश्च धीमान् प्राज्ञः सहदेवः पतिर्म। त्यजेत् प्राणान् प्रविशेद्धव्यवाह न त्वेवैष व्याहरेद् धर्मबाह्यम्॥ सदा मनस्वी क्षत्रधर्मे रतश्च कुन्त्याः प्राणैरिष्टतमो नृवीरः।
en: Heroic, ever wrathful, intelligent and wise, Sahadeva is my husband. He would rather rush into fire or give up his life than say anything against religion and morals. That high-minded one always abides by the duties of the Kshatriyas, is dearer than her life to Kunti and heroic among men.

sn: विशीर्यन्तीं नावमिवार्णवान्ते रत्नाभिपूर्णां मकरस्य पृष्ठे॥ सेनां तवेमां हतसर्वयोधां विक्षोभितां द्रक्ष्यसि पाण्डुपुत्रैः।
en: When the sons of Pandu will kill your heroes in battle you will see your army in the wretched condition of a ship on the sea wrecked with its freight of jewels on the back of a whale.

sn: इत्येते वै कथिताः पाण्डुपुत्रा यांस्त्वं मोहादवमन्य प्रवृत्तः। यद्येतेभ्यो मुच्यसेऽरिष्टदेहः पुनर्जन्म प्राप्स्यसे जीव एव॥
en: I have thus described to you the prowess of the Pandavas, foolishly disregarding whom you have acted so. If you can escape unhurt from them you will then obtain a new lease of life.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच स्त्यक्त्वा त्रस्तान् प्राञ्जलींस्तान् पदातीन्। रथानीकं शरवर्षान्धकारं चक्रुः क्रुद्धाः सर्वतः संनिगृह्य॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Then those five sons of Pritha, cach like Indra himself, growing angry and leaving the terrified foot-soldiers only who were begging for mercy, attacked furiously on all sides the charioteers darkening the very air with a thick shower of shafts they discharged.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच संतिष्ठत प्रहरत तूर्णं विपरिधावत। इति स्म सैन्धवो राजा चोदयामास तान् नृपान्॥
en: Vaishampayana said: In the interval, the king of Sindhu was commanding the princes saying, “Halt, strike, march quick."

sn: ततो घोरतमः शब्दो रणे समभवत् तदा। भीमार्जुनयमान् दृष्ट्वा सैन्यानां सयुधिष्ठिरान्॥
en: Then there arose a dreadful noise in the encounter when the soldiers saw, Bhima, Arjuna and the twin brothers with Yudhishthira.

sn: शिबिसौवीरसिन्धूनां विषादश्चाप्यजायत। तान् दृष्ट्वा पुरुषव्याघ्रान् व्याघ्रानिव बलोत्कटान्॥
en: Seeing those powerful heroes like dreadful tigers the heroes of Shibi, Sauvira and Sindhu tribes lost heart.

sn: हेमचित्रसमुत्सेधां सर्वशैक्यायसीं गदाम्। प्रगृह्याभ्यद्रवद् भीम: सैन्धवं कालचोदितम्॥
en: Then armed with a mace made entirely of Shaikya iron and coated with gold, Bhimasena rushed towards the Saindhava king doomed to death.

sn: तदन्तरमथावृत्य कोटिकास्योऽभ्यहारयत्। महता रथवंशेन परिवार्य वृकोदरम्॥
en: Thereupon quickly encircling Vrikodara with mighty charioteers Kotikasya interposed between and separated the combatants.

sn: शक्तितोमरनाराचैर्वीरबाहुप्रचोदितैः। कीर्यमाणोऽपि बहुभिर्न स्म भीमोऽभ्यकम्पत॥
en: And although assailed by many clubs and iron shafts hurled at him by the mighty arms of hostile heroes, Bhima did not waver for a moment.

sn: गजं तु सगजारोहं पदातींश्च चतुर्दश। जघान गदया भीमः सैन्धवध्वजिनीमुखे॥
en: But he slew, with mace, an elephant with its driver and fourteen foot-soldiers fighting in front of a Jayadratha's chariot.

sn: पार्थः पञ्च शतान् शूरान् पर्वतीयान् महारथान्। परीप्समानः सौवीरं जघान ध्वजिनीमुखे॥
en: Wishing to seize the Sauvira king, Partha too killed five hundred brave mountaineers fighting in the van of the Sindhu army.

sn: राजा स्वयं सुवीराणां प्रवराणां प्रहारिणाम्। निमेषमात्रेण शतं जघान समरे तदा॥
en: In the twinkling of an eye the king himself destroyed, in that encounter, the flowers of the Sauviras.

sn: ददृशे नकुलस्तत्र स्थात् प्रस्कन्ध खड्गधृक्। शिरांसि पादरक्षाणां बीजवत् प्रवपन् मुहुः॥
en: And Nakula was seen there coming down from the chariot, with a sword in hand and scattering in no time the heads of the battalions fighting on the rear like a cultivator sowing seeds.

sn: सहदेवस्तु संयाय रथेन गजयोधिनः। पातयामास नाराचैर्दुमेभ्य इव बर्हिणः॥
en: From his chariot, Sahadeva began to cut down with his iron arrows, many heroes fighting on elephants like birds dropped from the branches of a tree.

sn: ततस्त्रिगर्तः सधनुरवतीर्य महारथात्। गदया चतुरो वाहान् राज्ञस्तस्य तदावधीत्॥
en: Thereupon descending from his huge car Trigarta, with bow in hand, slew the four horses of the king with his mace.

sn: तमभ्याशगतं राजा पदाति कुन्तिनन्दनः। अर्धचन्द्रेण बाणेन विव्याधोरसि धर्मराट्॥
en: Seeing the enemy approach so near and fighting on foot the pious king Yudhishthira, the son of Kunti, pierced his breast with a crescent-shaped shaft.

sn: स भिन्नहृदयो वीरो वक्त्राच्छोणितमुद्वमन्। पपाताभिमुखः पार्थं छिन्नमूल इव दुमः॥
en: Thus struck on the breast that hero began to vomit blood and fell down on earth like an uprooted tree by the side of Pritha's son.

sn: इन्द्रसेनद्वितीयस्तु रथात् प्रस्कन्ध धर्मराट्। हताश्वः सहदेवस्य प्रतिपेदे महारथम्॥
en: Having his horse thus slain the pious king, with Indrasena, descended from his chariot and got upon the huge car of Sahadeva.

sn: नकुलं त्वभिसंधाय क्षेमङ्करमहामुखौ। उभावुभयतस्तीक्ष्णैः शरवर्षैरवर्षताम्॥
en: Then singling out Nakula, the two heroes Kshemankara and Mahamukha began to hurl at him from both sides with keen-edged arrows.

sn: तोमरैरभिवर्षन्तौ जीमूताविव वार्षिको। एकैकेन विपाठेन जघ्ने माद्रवतीसुतः॥
en: With two arrows however the son of Madri succeeded in killing those two heroes who had been pouring on him a shower of arrows like clouds in rains.

sn: त्रिगर्तराजः सुरथस्तस्याथ रथधूर्गतः। रथमाक्षेपयामास गजेन गजयानवित्॥
en: Going to the front of Nakula's chariot, Suratha, the king of Trigarta, expert in driving elephants, caused it to be dragged by the elephant of which he mounted.

sn: नकुलस्त्वपभीस्तस्माद् रथाच्चर्मासिपाणिमान्। उद्भ्रान्तं स्थानमास्थाय तस्थौ गिरिरिवाचलः॥
en: Little afraid at this, Nakula jumped out of his car and securing an advantageous position, stood, shield and sword in hand immoveable as a hill.

sn: सुरथस्तं गजवरं वधाय नकुलस्य तु। प्रेषयामास सक्रोधमत्युच्छ्रितकरं ततः॥
en: Thereupon desiring to kill Nakula at once Suratha goaded his huge and infuriated elephant with its trunk upraised (to rush towards him).

sn: नकुलस्तस्य नागस्य समीपपरिवर्तिनः। सविषाणं भुजं मूले खड्न निरकृन्तत॥
en: But he with his sword cut off from his head both trunk and tusks when the elephant came near him.

sn: स विनद्य महानादं गजः किङ्किणभूषणः। पतन्नवाक्शिरा भूमौ हस्त्यारोहमपोथयत्॥
en: Then emitting a loud noise that elephant, clad with mail, fell headlong upon the ground crushing its riders by its fall.

sn: स तत् कर्म महत् कृत्वा शूरो माद्रवतीसुतः। भीमसेनरथं प्राप्य शर्म लेभे महारथः॥
en: Performing that great exploit the heroic and mighty car-warrior, son of the Madri, ascending Bhimasen's car, got some rest.

sn: भीमस्त्वापततो राज्ञः कोटिकास्यस्य सङ्गरे। सूतस्य नुदतो वाहान् क्षुरेणापाहरच्छिरः॥
en: Beholding the prince Kotikasya rush to the battle, Bhima, with a horse shoe shaft, sundered the head of his charioteer.

sn: न बुबोध हतं सूतं स राजा बाहुशालिना। तस्याश्वा व्यद्रवन् संख्ये हतसूतास्ततस्ततः॥
en: The king could not perceive that his charioteer had been slain by the mighty-armed (enemy). The horses, no longer restrained by the driver, ran about hither and thither in the battle field.

sn: विमुखं हतसूतं तं भीमः प्रहरतां वरः। जघान तलयुक्तेन प्रासेनाभ्येत्य पाण्डवः॥
en: The Pandava Bhima, the foremost of heroes, slew, with a bearded arrow, that prince who had lost his chariot and was flying from the battle-field.

sn: द्वादशानां तु सर्वेषां सौवीराणां धनंजयः। चकर्त निशितैर्भल्लैर्धनूंषि च शिरांसि च॥
en: With his sharp crescent-shaped shafts Dhananjaya also cut off the heads and bows of all the twelve Sauvira heroes.

sn: शिबीनिक्ष्वाकुमुख्यांश्च त्रिगर्तान् सैन्धवानपि। जघानातिरथः संख्ये बाणगोचरमागतान्॥
en: That great warrior slew with shafts in battle, the leader of the Ikshvakus, the army of the Shibis, Trigarta and Saindhava.

sn: सादिताः प्रत्यदृश्यन्त बहवः सव्यसाचिना। सपताकाच मातङ्गाः सध्वजाश्च महारथाः॥
en: Many elephants with flags and great cars with standards were to have been destroyed by Savyasachi. seen

sn: प्रच्छाद्य पृथिवीं तस्थुः सर्वमायोधनं प्रति। शरीराण्यशिरस्कानि विदेहानि शिरांसि च॥
en: There lay covering the entire field of battle heads without trunks and trunks without heads.

sn: श्वगृध्रकङ्ककाकोलभासगोमायुवायसाः। अतृप्यंस्तत्र वीराणां हतानां मांसशोणितैः॥
en: Dogs, heroes, ravens, crows, falcons, jackals and vultures feasted on the flesh and blood of the heroes killed in the battle-field.

sn: हतेषु तेषु वीरेषु सिन्धुराजो जयद्रथः। विमुच्य कृष्णां संत्रस्त: पलायनपरोऽभवत्॥
en: Beholding his warriors slain, Jayadratha, the king of Sindhu became terrified and anxious to run away leaving Krishna behind.

sn: स तस्मिन् संकुले सैन्ये द्रौपदीमवतार्य ताम्। प्राणप्रेप्सुरुपाधावद् वनं येन नराधमः॥
en: Getting Draupadi down, the wretch, in the confusion, fled away for life following the same forest path by which he had come.

sn: द्रौपदी धर्मराजस्तु दृष्ट्वा धौम्यपुरस्कृताम्। माद्रीपुत्रेण वीरेण रथमारोपयत् तदा॥
en: Beholding Draupadi with Dhaumya walking before, the pious king Yudhishthira made her taken up on the car by the heroic Sahadeva, the son of Madri.

sn: ततस्तद् विद्रुतं सैन्यमपयाते जयद्रथे। आदिश्यादिश्य नाराचैराजघान वृकोदरः॥
en: After Jayadratha had fled away Vrikodara, with Narachas, slew all those soldiers who were running away, marking (each one of them).

sn: सव्यसाची तु तं दृष्ट्वा पलायन्तं जयद्रथम्। वारयामास निघ्नन्तं भीमं सैन्धवसैनिकान्॥
en: Beholding Jayadratha fled, Savyasachi asked Bhima to desist from killing the remnant of the Saindhava army.

sn: अर्जुन उवाच यस्यापचारात् प्राप्तोऽयमस्मान् क्लेशो दुरासदः तमस्मिन् समरोद्देशे न पश्यामि जयद्रथम्॥
en: Arjuna said: I do not see Jayadratha in the battle-field through whose folly we have met with this misfortune.

sn: तमेवान्विष भद्रं ते किं ते योधैर्निपातितः। अनामिषमिदं कर्म कथं वा मन्यते भवान्॥
en: Seek him out; may good betide you. What is the use of killing these soldiers? Why are you bent upon this useless business?

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच इत्युक्तो भीमसेनस्तु गुडाकेशेन धीमता। युधिष्ठिरमभिप्रेक्ष्य वाग्मी वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Being thus accosted by the intelligent Gudakesha, Bhimasena, skilled in speech, turning to Yudhishthira, said,

sn: हतप्रवीरा रिपवो भूयिष्ठं विदुता दिशः। गृहीत्वा द्रौपदी राजन् निवर्ततु भवानितः॥
en: "Many of the enemy's heroes have been slain; others have fled away to various directions; taking Draupadi with you, O king, return home.

sn: यमाभ्यां सह राजेन्द्र धौम्येन च महात्मना। प्राप्याश्रमपदं राजन् द्रौपदी परिसान्त्वय॥
en: O king of kings, O king, reaching hermitage with the twins and the high-souled Dhaumya console Draupadi.

sn: न हि मे मोक्ष्यते जीवन मूढः सैन्धवको नृपः। पातालतलसंस्थोऽपि यदि शक्रोऽस्य सारथिः॥
en: I shall not let along the stupid king of Sindhu even if he finds shelter in the nether world or is supported by Indra himself.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच न हन्तव्यो महाबाहो दुरात्मापि स सैन्धवः। दुःशलामभिसंस्मृत्य गान्धारीं च यशस्विनीम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said: O you of mighty arms, remembering our sister Dushala and the illustrious Gandhari, the wicked-minded Saindhava should not be slain by you.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तच्छ्रुत्वा द्रौपदी भीममुवाच व्याकुलेन्द्रिया। कुपिता ह्रीमती प्राज्ञा पती भीमार्जुनावुभौ॥
en: Vaishampayana said: Hearing those words Draupadi was excited; that bashful, angry and intelligent (lady) said to her husbands Bhima and Arjuna.

sn: कर्तव्यं चेत् प्रियं मह्यं वध्यः स पुरुषाधमः। सैन्धवापसदः पापो दुर्मतिः कुलपांसनः॥
en: “If you wish to encompass my pleasure, that vile, wretch of a man, the wicked-minded, infamous and despicable king of the Saindhava race should be killed by you.

sn: भार्याभिहर्ता वैरी यो यश्च राज्यहरो रिपुः। याचमानोऽपि संग्रामे न मोक्तव्यः कथंचन॥
en: The enemy who carries away one's wife or wrests his kingdom, should by no means be forgiven in battle even if he craves for mercy.”

sn: इत्युक्तौ तौ नरव्याघ्रौ ययतुर्यत्र सैन्धवः। राजा निववृते कृष्णामादाय सपुरोहितः॥
en: Having been thus addressed those two foremost of men went where Saindhava was; taking Draupadi with him, the king alone with his priest returned.

sn: स प्रविश्याश्रमपदमपविद्धबृसीमठम्। मार्कण्डेयादिभिर्विप्रैरनुकीर्णं ददर्श ह॥
en: Entering the hermitage he saw it covered with the seats for the ascetics, filled with their disciples and graced with the presence of Markandeya and other Brahmanas.

sn: द्रौपदीमनुशोचद्भिाह्मणैस्तैः समाहितैः। समिमाय महाप्राज्ञः सभार्यो भ्रातृमध्यगः॥
en: While those self-controlled Brahmanas where lamenting for Draupadi, the greatly wise (king) with his wife and brothers joined them.

sn: ते स्म तं मुदिता दृष्ट्वा पुन: प्रत्यागतं नृपम्। जित्वा तान् सिन्धु सौवीरान् द्रौपदीं चाहतां पुनः॥
en: Beholding the king then return, having vanquished the Sindhu and Sauvira princes and taken Draupadi, they were delighted.

sn: स तैः परिवृतो राजा तत्रैवोपविवेश ह। प्रविवेशाश्रमं कृष्णा यमाभ्यां सह भाविनी॥
en: Encircled by them the king sat there and the good Krishna, alone with the twins, entered the hermitage.

sn: भीमसेनार्जुनौ चापि श्रुत्वा क्रोशगतं रिपुम्। स्वयमश्वांस्तुदन्तौ तौ जवेनैवाभ्यधावताम्॥
en: Hearing that the enemy has gone only two miles Bhima and Arjuna spurred their horses to greatest speed in pursuit of him.

sn: इदमत्यद्भुतं चात्र चकार पुरुषोऽर्जुनः। कोशमात्रगतानश्वान् सैन्धवस्य जघान यत्॥
en: The heroic Arjuna performed a wonderful fcat by killing the horses of Saindhava, which were at a distance of two miles.

sn: स हि दिव्यास्त्रसम्पन्नः कृच्छ्रकालेऽप्यसम्भ्रमः। अकरोद् दुष्करं कर्म शरैरस्त्रानुमन्त्रितैः॥
en: Armed with celestials weapons and undaunted by difficulties he performed this difficult work with weapons inspired with Mantras.

sn: ततोऽभ्यधावतां वीरावुभौ भीमधनंजयौ। हताश्वं सैन्धवं भीतमेकं व्याकुलचेतसम्॥
en: Then the two heroes Bhima and Arjuna rushed towards the terror-stricken king of Sindhu whose horses had been killed and who was perplexed in mind.

sn: सैन्धवस्तु हतान् दृष्ट्वा तथाश्वान् स्वान् सुदुःखितः। अतिविक्रमकर्माणि कुर्वाणं च धनंजयम्॥
en: Beholding his own horses slain and Dhananjaya perform such a greatly powerful exploits Saindhava was greatly sorry.

sn: पलायनकृतोत्साहः प्राद्रवद् येन वै वनम्। सैन्धवं त्वभिसम्प्रेक्ष्य पराक्रान्तं पलायने॥
en: Determined on flying away he followed the same forest path by which he had come. Beholding Saindhava thus engaged in flying away.

sn: अनुयाय महाबाहुः फाल्गुनो वाक्यमब्रवीत्। अनेन वीर्येण कथं स्त्रियं प्रार्थयसे बलात्॥
en: The mighty-armed Falguna, following him, said "with such prowess how could you desire to take away a female by force?

sn: राजपुत्र निवर्तस्व न ते युक्तं पलायनम्। कथं ह्यनुचरान् हित्वा शत्रुमध्ये पलायसे॥
en: Desist, O princes it does not behoove you, leaving your followers in the midst of enemies, to take to your heels?

sn: इत्युच्यमानः पार्थेन सैन्धवो न न्यवर्तत। तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति तं भीमः सहसाभ्यद्रवद् बली। मा वधीरिति पार्थस्तं दयावान् प्रत्यभाषत॥
en: (Although) addressed by Partha thus Saindhava did not return. Saying "Wait, wait! the mighty Bhima all on a sudden overtook him. But the merciful Partha said, "Don't kill him."

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच जयद्रथस्तु सम्प्रेक्ष्य भ्रातरावुद्यतावुभौ। प्राधावत् तूर्णमव्यचो जीवितेऽप्सुः सुदुःखिताः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Beholding the two brothers with upraised weapons, Jayadratha, desirous of living, stricken sorely with grief, ran away speedily and coolly.

sn: तं भीमसेनो धावन्तमवतीर्य रथाद् बली। अभिदुत्य निजग्राह केशपक्षे ह्यमर्षणः॥
en: But getting down from his chariot the powerful Bhimasena pursued him speedily, who had thus taken to his heels and seized him by the hair of his head.

sn: समुद्यम्य च तं भीमो निष्पिपेष महीतले। शिरो गृहीत्वा राजानं ताडयामास चैव ह॥
en: Holding him up Bhima again crushed him on earth; then taking the king by the head, he knocked him about.

sn: पुनः संजीवमानस्य तस्योत्पतितुमिच्छतः। पदा मूर्ध्नि महाबाहुः प्राहरद् विलपिष्यतः॥
en: When regaining his consciousness he expressed his desire of getting up the mightyarmcu herces kicked him on the head.

sn: तस्य जानू ददौ भीमो जघ्ने चैनमरलिना। स मोहमगमद् राजा प्रहारवरपीडितः॥
en: Bhima struck him on the breast with his knees and fists, and thus assailed the king soon lost his consciousness.

sn: सरोषं भीमसेनं तु वारयामास फाल्गुनः। दुःशलायाः कृते राजा यत् तदाहेति कौरव॥
en: Falguna prevented the wrathful Bhimasena by reminding him of what the Kaurava king had said on behalf of Duhshala.

sn: भीमसेन उवाच नायं पापसमाचारो मत्तो जीवितुमर्हति। कृष्णायास्तदनस्याः परिक्लेष्टा नराधमः॥
en: Bhima said: “This vilest and foolish man has done a great injury to Krishna who does not deserve it; so he does not deserve to live.

sn: किं नु शक्यं मया कर्तुं यद् राजा सततं घृणी। त्वं च बालिशया बुद्ध्या सदैवास्मान् प्रबाधसे॥
en: But what can I do? The king is always merciful and you too, out of childishness, are always preventing me.”

sn: एवमुक्त्वा सटास्तस्य पञ्च चक्रे वृकोदरः। अर्धचन्द्रेण बाणेन किंचिदब्रुवतस्तदा॥
en: Having said this Vrikodara, with his crescent-shaped arrow, shaved the hair of the king's head keeping five tufts at five places. But (Jayadratha) did not utter a word.

sn: विकत्थयित्वा राजानं ततः प्राह वृकोदरः। जीवितुं चेच्छसे मूढ हेतुं मे गदतः शृणु॥
en: Thereupon Vrikodara said to the king, “O fool, if you wish to live, listen, I shall tell you the means.

sn: दासोऽस्मीति तथा वाच्यं संसत्सु च सभासु च) एवं ते जीवितं दद्यामेष युद्धजितो विधिः॥
en: In public meetings and open courts you should always say that you are our slave; (if you can make this condition) I can give you your life. This is the custom of the victorious."

sn: एवमस्त्विति तं राजा कृष्यमाणो जयद्रथः। प्रोवाच पुरुषव्याघ्र भीममहावशोभिनम्॥
en: Being thus treated the king Jayadratha said to that best of men, Bhima, who beautifies the battle-field "So be it."

sn: तत एनं विचेष्टन्तं बद्ध्वा पार्थो वृकोदरः। रथमारोपयामास विसंज्ञं पांसुगुण्ठितम्॥
en: Thereupon taking him who was unconscious and besmeared with dust Partha and Vrikodara placed him on the chariot.

sn: ततस्तं रथमास्थाय भीमः पार्थानुगस्तदा। अभ्येत्याश्रममध्यस्थमभ्यगच्छद् युधिष्ठिरम्॥
en: Thereupon placing him on the car, Bhima, followed by Partha, reached the hermitage and approached Yudhishthira who sat in the middle.

sn: दर्शयामास भीमस्तु तदवस्थं जयद्रथम्। तं राजा प्राहसद् दृष्ट्वा मुच्यतामिति चाब्रवीत्॥
en: Bhima showed him Jayadratha who was in that plight. Seeing him, the king smilingly said "set him at liberty,"

sn: राजानं चाब्रवीद् भीमो द्रौपद्याः कथ्यतामिति। दासभावगतो ह्येष पाण्डूनां पापचेतनः॥
en: Bhima said to the king, “Tell Draupadi, that this vile man has become the slave of the Pandavas."

sn: तमुवाच ततो ज्येष्ठो भ्राता सप्रणयं वचः। मुञ्चैनमधमाचारं प्रमाणा यदि ते वयम्॥
en: Thereupon his eldest brother said to him a affectionate terms. "If you have any regard for me let him be free."

sn: द्रौपदी चाब्रवीद् भीममभिप्रेक्ष्य युधिष्ठिरम्। दासोऽयं मुच्यतां राज्ञस्त्वया पञ्चसटः कृतः॥
en: Beholding Yudhishthira Draupadi also said to Bhima, "Release him who is the slave of the king and whom you have disfigured by leaving five tufts on his head."

sn: स मुक्तोऽभ्येत्य राजानमभिवाद्य युधिष्ठिरम्। ववन्दे विह्वलो राजस्तांश्च दृष्ट्वा मुनींस्तदा॥
en: Being released he approached and bowed to the king Yudhishthira; and seeing the ascetics there, he, beside himself, saluted them all.

sn: तमुवाच घृणी राजा धर्मपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः। तथा जयद्रथं दृष्ट्वा गृहीतं सव्यसाचिना॥
en: Beholding Jayadratha supported by Savyasachi, the kind king Yudhishthira, Dharma's son, said to him,

sn: अदासो गच्छ मुक्तोऽसि मैवं कार्षीः पुनः क्वचित्। स्त्रीकामं वा धिगस्तु त्वां क्षुद्रः क्षुद्रसहायवान्॥
en: "You are a free man, go, I release you; but do not commit any such thing again. Fie on you! You wanted to take away a female by force, although you are so weak and powerless.

sn: एवंविधं हि कः कुर्यात् त्वदन्यः पुरुषाधमः। गतसत्त्वमिव ज्ञात्वा कर्तारमशुभस्य तम्॥ सम्प्रेक्ष्य भरतश्रेष्ठः :: कृपां चक्रे नराधिपः। धर्मे ते वर्धतां बुद्धिर्मा चाधर्मे मनः कृथाः॥
en: What other vile man, except you, would think of doing this again?” Knowing that he had lost heart and looking at that perpetrator of evil deed, the foremost of Bharatas and king of men showed mercy (saying), "May your heart grow in virtue, never think of doing any such impious deed.

sn: साश्वः सरथपादातः स्वस्ति गच्छ जयद्रथ। एवमुक्तस्तु सव्रीडं तूष्णीं किंचिदवाड्मुखः॥
en: O Jayadratha, go now in peace with your charioteers, cavalry and infantry." Being this accosted he was filled with shame; then bending low his head,

sn: जगाम राजन् दुःखार्तो गङ्गाद्वाराय भारत। स देवं शरणं गत्वा विरूपाक्षमुमापितम्॥
en: And stricken with sorrow the king, O Bharata, went to the gate of the Ganges. Then sceking the shelter of the deity Virupaksha, the lord of Uma.

sn: तपश्चचार विपुलं तस्य प्रीतो वृषध्वजः। बलिं स्वयं प्रत्यगृह्णात् प्रीयणाणस्त्रिलोचनः॥
en: He engaged in great austerity and Shiva was pleased with him. Being pleased the three-eyed deity himself brought his offerings.

sn: वरं चास्मै ददौ देवः स जग्राह च तच्छृणु। समस्तान् सरथान् पञ्च जयेयं युधि पाण्डवान्॥
en: The Deity conferred upon him a boon and hear, how he took it, “May I be able to vanquish in battle all the five sons of Pandu on their chariots."

sn: इति राजाब्रवीद् देवं नेति देवस्तमब्रवीत्। अजय्यांश्चाप्यवध्यांश्च वारयिष्यसि तान् युधि॥ ऋतेऽर्जुनं महाबाहुं नरं नाम सुरेश्वरम्। बदाँ तप्ततपसं नारायणसहायकम्॥
en: This the king said to the god but he said "this cannot be." You shall once check them in battle who are unconquerable and are not capable of being slain, except the mightyarmed Arjuna who is the lord of the celestials incarnate named Nara. He carried on devout penances in Badari and is backed by Narayana.

sn: अजितं सर्वलोकानां देवैरपि दुरासदम्। मया दत्तं पाशुपतं दिव्यमप्रतिमं शरम्। अवाप लोकपालेभ्यो वलादीन् स महाशरान्॥
en: He is unconquerable by all men even by the celestials; I myself have given him the celestial shaft Pashupata. He obtained from the Lokapalas thunderbolt and other mighty shafts.

sn: देवदेवो ह्यनन्तात्मा विष्णुः सुरगुरुः प्रभुः। प्रधानपुरुषोऽव्यक्तो विश्वात्मा विश्वमूर्तिमान्॥
en: The great god Vishnu, the Infinite Spirit, the Lord preceptor of the celestials, is the unmanifest, Pradhana Purusha, the soul of the universe and has His manifestation in the universe.

sn: युगान्तकाले सम्प्राप्ते कालाग्निर्दहते जगत्। सपर्वतार्णवद्वीपं सशैलवनकाननम्॥
en: At the end of the Yuga, assuming the form of the all consuming fire he burnt down the universe, with mountains, seas, islands, hills, woods and forest.

sn: निर्दहन् नागलोकांश्च पातालतलचारिणः। अथान्तरिक्षे सुमहन्नानावर्णाः पयोधराः॥
en: After he had consumed the region of the Nagas who range in the region underneath the earth, huge clouds of many colours were seen in the sky.

sn: घोरस्वरा विनदिनस्तडिन्मालावलम्बिनः। समुत्तिष्ठन् दिशः सर्वा विवर्षन्तः समन्ततः॥
en: Loud sounding accompanied by lighting and sr reading all over the sky.

sn: ततोऽग्नि नाशयामासुः संवर्ताग्निनियामकाः। अक्षमात्रैश्च धाराभिस्तिष्ठन्त्यापूर्य सर्वशः॥
en: Then filling all quarters with showers thick as axles of cars they extinguished that allconsuming fire.

sn: एकार्णवे तदा तस्मिन्नुपशान्तचराचरे। नष्टचन्द्रार्कपवने ग्रहनक्षत्रवर्जिते॥ चतुर्युगसहस्रान्ते सलिलेनाप्लुता मही। ततो नारायणाख्यस्तु सहस्राक्षः सहस्रपात्॥ सहस्रशीर्षाः पुरुषः स्वप्तुकामस्त्वतीन्द्रियः। फटासहस्रविकटं शेषं पर्यङ्कभाजनम्॥ सहस्रमिव तिग्मांशुसंघातममितद्युतिम्। कुन्देन्दुहारगोक्षीरमृणालकुमुदप्रभम्॥ तत्रासौ भगवान् देवः स्वपञ्जलनिधौ तदा। नैशेन तमसा व्याप्तां स्वां रात्रिं कुरुते विभुः॥
en: When at the end of the four thousand Yugas the earth was over flooded with water like one vast ocean and all mobile and immobile creatures were silenced to death, the sun, moon and the winds were all destroyed and the universe was shorn of planets and stars, the supreme being, Narayana, who is beyond the perception of senses and is adorned with a thousand heads eyes and ears, longed for rest. The dreadful serpent Shesha, having thousand heads and the lustre of ten thousand suns and white as the Kunda flower or the moon or a string of pearls or the white lotus or milk, of fibres of lotus, became His conch. There the Divine Lord slept on the bosom of the deep enveloping all quarters with nocturnal darkness.

sn: सत्त्वोद्रेकात् प्रबुद्धस्तु शून्यं लोकमपश्यत। इमं चोदाहरन्त्यत्र श्लोकं नारायणं प्रति॥
en: When His creative faculty was excited he awoke and saw the universe void of everything. In this connection there is a Sloka recited (throwing light on the word) Narayana.

sn: आपो नारास्तत्तनव इत्यपां नाम शुश्रुम। अयनं तेन चैवास्ते तेन नारायणः स्मृतः॥
en: The water was the body of the (Rishi) Nara and we hear it called Nara; and because it formed his resting place he is called Narayana.

sn: प्रध्यानसमकालं तु प्रजाहेतोः सनातनः। ध्यातमात्रे तु भगवन्नाभ्यां पद्मः समुत्थितः॥
en: As soon as the Eternal deity engaged in thought for the creation of progeny a lotus sprang up from the navel of the Divine Lord.

sn: ततश्चतुर्मुखो ब्रह्मा नाभिपद्माद् विनिःसृतः। तत्रोपविष्टः सहसा पद्मे लोकपितामहः॥
en: Thereupon arose from the lotus navel the four-headed deity Brahma; there on the lotus sat all on a sudden the Grandfather of the creatures.

sn: शून्यं दृष्ट्वा जगत् कृत्स्नं मानसानात्मनः समान् ततो मरीचिप्रमुखान् महर्षीनसृजन्नव॥
en: Seeing the universe entirely blank he created after him and from his mind the nine great ascetics Marichi and others.

sn: तेऽसृजन् सर्वभूतानि त्रसानि स्थावराणि च। यक्षराक्षसभूतानि पिशाचोरगमानुषान्॥
en: They also seeing the same thing created Yakshas, Rakshasas, Pishachas, reptiles, men and all mobile and immobile creatures.

sn: सृज्यते ब्रह्ममूर्तिस्तु रक्षते पौरुषी तनुः। रौद्रीभावेन शमयेत् तिस्रोऽवस्थाः प्रजापतेः॥
en: There are three states of the supreme being; in the form of Brahma, he is the creator, in the form of Vishnu, he is the preserver and in the form of Rudra he is the destroyer.

sn: न श्रुतं ते सिन्धुपते विष्णोरद्भुतकर्मणः। कथ्यमानानि मुनिभिर्ब्राह्मणैर्वेदपारगैः॥
en: O king of Sindhu, have you not heard of the marvellous exploits of Vishnu recounted to you by the ascetics and Brahmanas well-versed in the Vedas?

sn: जलेन समनुप्राप्ते सर्वतः पृथिवीतले। तदा चैकार्णवे तस्मिन्नेकाकाशे प्रभुश्चरन्।॥ निशायामिव खद्योतः प्रावृट् काले समन्ततः। प्रतिष्ठानाय पृथिवीं मार्गमाणस्तदाभवत्॥
en: While the entire surface of the earth was converted into a vast expanse of water, with only one sky above it, the lord, like a fire-fly at night during the rainy season, moved about here and there in search of a permanent footing for re-establishing the earth.

sn: जले निमग्नां गां दृष्ट्वा चोद्धर्तुं मनसेच्छति। किं नु रूपमहं कृत्वा सलिलादुद्धरे महीम्॥
en: Beholding the earth submerged in water he made up his mind to rescue it (He thought) "Assuming what form shall I rescue the earth from water?"

sn: एवं संचिन्त्य मनसा दृष्ट्वा दिव्येन चक्षुषा। जलक्रीडाभिरुचितं वाराह रूपमस्मरत्॥
en: Thus thinking in his mind and seeing with his divine eyes he thought of the shape of a boar fond of sporting in water.

sn: कृत्वा वराहवपुषं वाङ्मयं वेदसम्मितम्। दशयोजनविस्तीर्णमायतं शतयोजनम्॥ महापर्वतवभिं तीक्ष्णदंष्ट्र प्रदीप्तिमत्। महामेघौघनिर्घोषं नीलजीमूतसंनिभम्॥ भूत्वा यज्ञवराहो वै अपः सम्प्राविशत् प्रभुः। दंष्ट्रेणैकेन चोद्धृत्य स्वे स्थाने न्यविशन्महीम्॥
en: Assuming the form of a sacrificial boar, effulgent and instinct with the Vedas, ten yojanas in length, with pointed tusks, having the hue of dark clouds, a body huge as a mountain and roaring like the muttering of clouds, the Lord went into the water, raised up the Earth with one of its tusks and replaced it in its proper place.

sn: पुनरेव माहाबहुरपर्वां तनुमाश्रितः। नरस्य कृत्वार्धतर्नु सिंहस्यार्धतर्नु प्रभुः॥ दैत्येन्द्रस्य सभां गत्वा पाणिं संस्पृश्य पाणिना। दैत्यानामादिपुरुषः सुरारिदितिनन्दनः॥ दृष्ट्वा चापूर्वपुरुषं क्रोधात् संरक्तलोचनः।
en: Again assuming a wonderful form, half-lion, half-man, the mighty armed Lord, squeezing his hand, went to the court of the king of Daityas. The first man of the Daitya race, the enemy of the celestials, the son of Diti, beholding this wonderful form, became worked up with anger and his eyes became red.

sn: शूलोद्यतकरः स्रग्वी हिरण्यकशिपुस्तदा॥ मेघस्तनितनि?षो नीलाभ्रचयसंनिभः। देवारिदितिजो वीरो नृसिंहं समुपाद्रवत्॥
en: Hiranyakashipu, the heroic son of Diti and the enemy of the celestials adorned with garlands and looking like a mass of dark clouds, rushed on that Being half lion, half . man, with an uplifted mace in his inand.

sn: समुपेत्य ततस्तीक्ष्णैर्मृगेन्द्रेण बलीयसा। नारसिंहेन वपुषा दारित: करजैर्भृशम्॥
en: Then approaching him, that king of beasts, half lion, half man, immediately rent him with his sharp claws.

sn: एवं निहत्य भगवान् दैत्येन्द्रं रिपुघातिनम्। भूयोऽन्यः पुण्डरीकाक्षः प्रभुलॊकहिताय च॥ कश्यपस्यात्मजः श्रीमानदित्या गर्भधारितः। पूर्णे वर्षसहस्रे तु प्रसूता गर्भमुत्तमम्॥
en: Having thus slain the king of Daityas, the killer of his enemies, for the behalf of creatures, the lotus-eyed, effulgent lord, again took his birth as Kashyapa's son in the womb of Aditi. At the expiration of full one thousand years she was delivered of that excellent conception.

sn: दुर्दिनाम्भोदसदृशो दीप्ताक्षो वामनाकृतिः। दण्डी कमण्डलुधरः श्रीवत्सोरसि भूषितः॥६३।
en: He became of dwarfish stature, with bright eyes and of the complexion of the rain-charged clouds. He had the ascetic staff and Kamandalu (water pot) in his hand and was adorned with the mystic mark of Srivatsa on his breast.

sn: जटी यज्ञोपवीती च भगवान् बालरूपधृक्। यज्ञवाटं गतः श्रीमान् दानवेन्द्रस्य वै तदा॥
en: The Lord wore matted locks, the sacrificial thread and was stout, beautiful and effulgent.

sn: बृहस्पतिसहायोऽसौ प्रविष्टो बलिनो मखे। तं दृष्ट्वा वामनतनुं प्रहष्टो बलिरब्रवीत्॥
en: With the help of Brihaspati he entered into the sacrificial ground of Bali. Beholding his dwarfish stature Bali laughed and said,

sn: प्रीतोऽस्मि दर्शने विप्र ब्रूहि त्वं किं ददानि ते। एवमुक्तस्तु बलिना वामनः प्रत्युवाच ह॥ स्वस्तीत्युक्त्वा बलिं देवः स्मयमानोऽभ्यभाषत। मेदिनी दानवपते देहि मे विक्रमत्रयम्॥
en: “I am pleased on seeing you, O Vipra, tell me what can I give you." Being thus accosted by Bali the dwarf replied. Saying "may good betide you" the Deity smilingly said to Bali, “O king of Danavas, give me land to cover my three footsteps."

sn: बलिर्ददौ प्रसन्नात्मा विप्रायामिततेजसे। ततो दिव्याद्भुततमं रूपं विक्रमतो हरेः॥
en: Delightedly Bali gave what that highly powerful Vipra wanted. Thereupon while measuring the space Hari assumed a highly wonderful form.

sn: विक्रमैस्त्रिभिरक्षोभ्यो जहाराशु स मेदिनीम्। ददौ शक्राय च महीं विष्णुर्देवः सनातनः॥
en: With his three foot-steps he immediately covered the entire earth then the eternal deity Vishnu gave the earth to Shakra.

sn: एष ते वामनो नाम प्रादुर्भावः प्रकीर्तितः। तेन देवाः प्रादुरासन् वैष्णवं चोच्यते जगत्॥
en: This history which I have just related is known as the incarnation of the dwarf; from him all the celestials came into being and the universe is called Vaishnava (or pervaded by Vishnu).

sn: असतां निग्रहार्थाय धर्मसंरक्षणाय च। अवतीर्णो मनुष्याणामजायत यदुक्षये॥
en: For the suppression of the impious and the protection of virtue he has taken his birth among men in the race of the Yadus.

sn: स एवं भगवान् विष्णुः कृष्णेति परिकीर्त्यते। अनाद्यन्तमजं देवं प्रभुं लोकनमस्कृतम्॥
en: That Divine Vishnu is now called Krishna. That unborn Deity, without beginning or end, is adored by the world.

sn: यं देवं विदुषो गान्ति तस्य कर्माणि सैन्धव। यामाहुरजितं कृष्णं शङ्खचक्रगदाधरम्॥
en: These are his achievement, O Saindhava, whom the wise thus describe. They call him the unconquerable Krishna, with conch, discus and club in his hands.

sn: श्रीवत्सधारिणं देवं पीतकौशेयवाससम्। प्रधानः सोऽस्त्रविदुषां तेन कृष्णेन रक्ष्यते॥
en: The Deity has the mystic mark of Srivatsa, is clad in yellow silken raiment and is the best of those versed in the use of weapons. (Arjuna) is protected by such Krishna.

sn: सहायः पुण्डरीकाक्षः श्रीमानतुलविक्रमः। समानस्यन्दने पार्थमास्थाय परवीरहा॥
en: The graceful, lotus-eyed deity of incomparable prowess, the slayer of hostile heroes in his help and he rides with Partha in the same chariot.

sn: न शक्यते तेन जेतुं त्रिदशैरपि दुःसहः। कः पुनर्मानुषो भावो रणे पार्थं विजेष्यति॥
en: Even the celestials with great difficulty cannot defeat him; how can again a man vanquish Partha in battle?

sn: तमेकं वर्जयित्वा तु सर्वं यौधिष्ठरं बलम्। चतुरः पाण्डवान् राजन् दिनैकं जेष्यसे रिपून्॥
en: Leaving him alone you shall for one day defeat the army of Yudhishthira, O king, with your four enemies.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच इत्येवमुक्त्वा नृपतिं सर्वपापहरो हरः। उमापतिः पशुपतिर्यज्ञहा त्रिपुरार्दनः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having said this to the king, Hara, the destroyer of all sins, Uma's lord, Pashupati, the destroyer of (Daksha's) sacrifice, the slayer of Tripura.

sn: वामनैर्विकटैः कुब्जैरुच श्रवणदर्शनैः। वृतः पारिषदैर्पोरैर्नानाप्रहरणोद्यतैः॥ त्र्यम्बको राजशार्दूलो भगनेत्रनिपातनः। उमासहायो भगवांस्तत्रैवान्तरधीयत॥
en: He, who had taken out the eyes of Bhaga encircled by his dwarfish haunch-backed and dreadful followers, with fearful eyes and ears and uplifted weapons, Traymbaka, having Uma as his help, disappeared.

sn: जयद्रथोऽपि मन्दात्मा स्वमेव भवनं ययौ। पाण्डवाश्च वने तस्मिन् न्यवसन् काम्यके तथा॥
en: The vicious-minded Jayadratha too repaired to his own house, the Pandavas too lived in the forest of Kamyaka.

sn: जनमेजय उवाच एवं हृतायां कृष्णायां प्राप्य क्लेशमनुत्तमम्। अत ऊर्ध्वं नरव्याघ्राः किमकुर्वत पाण्डवाः॥
en: Janamejaya said : Having suffered such misery consequent upon Draupadi's being carried away what did those Pandavas, the foremost of men, do?

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवं कृष्णां मोक्षयित्वा विनिर्जित्य जयद्रथम्। आसांचक्रे मुनिगणैर्धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having thus released Krishna and vanquished Jayadratha, the pious king Yudhishthira took his seat by the side of the ascetics.

sn: तेषां मध्ये महर्षीणां शृण्वतामनुशोचताम्। मार्कण्डेयमिदं वाक्यमब्रवीत् पाण्डुनन्दनः॥
en: Amongst those great ascetics who were expressing their sorrow on hearing of the incident) the descendant of Pandu, addressing Markandeya, gave vent to the following.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच भगवन् देवर्षीणां त्वं ख्यातो भूतभविष्यवित्। संशयं परिपृच्छामि छिन्धि मे हृदि संस्थितम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said : O venerable sir, amongst the ascetics and the celestials, you are reputed to have the fullest knowledge of both the past and future. I have a doubt in my mind, I shall ask you, (kindly) solve it.

sn: दुपदस्य सुता ह्येषा वेदिमध्यात् समुत्थिता। अयोनिजा महाभागा स्नुषा पाण्डोर्महात्मनः॥
en: This lady is the daughter of Drupada and has sprung from the sacrificial altar. She is not begotten of flesh; she is the mighty and illustrious daughter-in-law of the high-souled Pandu.

sn: मन्ये कालश्च भगवान् दैवं च विधिनिर्मितम्। भवितव्यं च भूतानां यस्य नास्ति व्यतिक्रमः॥
en: Me-thinks, Time and Destiny, instituted by the Deity, are inevitable io creatures and cannot be warded off.

sn: इमां हि पत्नीमस्माकं धर्मज्ञां धर्मचारिणीम्। संस्पृशेदीदृशो भावः शुचिं स्तैन्यमिवानृतम्॥
en: How could (such a misfortune) overcome such a pious, chaste wife of ours, abiding by virtue, like a false accusation of theft against an honest man?

sn: न हि पापं कृतं किंचित् कर्म वा निन्दितं क्वचित् द्रौपद्या ब्राह्मणेष्वेव धर्मः सुचरितो महान्॥
en: Draupadi has not committed any iniquity or heinous deed; she has always practised highest virtues towards the Brahmanas.

sn: तां जहार बलाद् राजा मूढबुद्धिर्जयद्रथः। तस्याः संहरणात् पापः शिरसः केशपातनम्॥ पराजयं च संग्रामे ससहायः समाप्तवान्। प्रत्याहृता तथास्माभिर्हत्वा तत् सैन्धवं बलम्॥
en: The foolish king Jayadratha took her away by force; on account of this violence on her that sinful man has got his hair shaved off and has met with defeat in battle along with his soldiers. True it is, that we have rescued her after slaying the army of Saindhava.

sn: तद् दारहरणं प्राप्तमस्माभिरवितर्कितम्। ज्ञातिभिर्विप्रवासश्च मिथ्याव्यवसितैरियम्॥
en: Forsooth this disgrace, of our wife, being carried away during a moment of carelessness, has sullied us. This forest life is full of miseries; we live on chase. Though we live in forest we (always) injure the dwellers thereof. This banishment of ours is owing to our deceitful relatives.

sn: अस्ति नूनं मया कश्चिदल्पभाग्यतरो नरः। भवता दृष्टपूर्वो वा श्रुतपूर्वोऽपि वा भवेत्॥
en: Is there any one indeed who is more unfortunate than I am. Have you heard or seen of any such man before.

description: The story of the birth of Rama and Ravana
sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच प्राप्तमप्रतिमं दुःखं रामेण भरतर्षभ। रक्षसा जानकी तस्य हृता भार्या बलीयसा॥
en: Markandeya said : O foremost of the Bharatas, an incomparable calamity was met with by Rama. His wife Janaki was carried away by force by the Rakshasas.

description: The story of the birth of Rama and Ravana
sn: आश्रमाद् राक्षसेन्द्रेण रावणेन दुरात्मना। मायामास्थाय तरसा हत्वा गृधं जटायुषम्॥
en: Resorting to Maya and having slain the vulture Jatayu, the vicious-souled Ravana, the king of Rakshasas (carried her away) from the hermitage.

description: The story of the birth of Rama and Ravana
sn: प्रत्याजहार तां रामः सुग्रीवबलमाश्रितः। बद्ध्वा सेतुं समुद्रस्य दग्ध्वा लङ्कां शितैः शरैः॥
en: Constructing a bridge over the ocean and burn in down Lanka with sharp shafts, by the help of Sugriva, Rama brought her back.

description: The story of the birth of Rama and Ravana
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच कस्मिन् रामः कुले जातः किंवीर्यः किम्पराक्रमः। रावणः कस्य पुत्रो वा किं वैरं तस्य तेन ह॥
en: Yudhishthira said: In what family was be born? How was his mighty and prowess? Whose son was Rama? What enmity had he with him?

description: The story of the birth of Rama and Ravana
sn: सर्वं सम्यगाख्यातुमर्हसि। श्रोतुमिच्छामि चरितं रामस्याक्लिष्टकर्मणः॥
en: Oh Sir, relate ail this to me. I wish to hear the story of Rama of unwearied actions.

description: The story of the birth of Rama and Ravana
sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच अजो नामाभवद् राजा महानिक्ष्वाकुवंशजः। तस्य पुत्रो दशरथः शश्वतस्वाध्यायवाञ्छुचिः॥
en: Markandeya said : There was a great king in the family of Ikshvakus by name Aja. His son was Dasharatha, who was pure and ever devoted to the study of the Vedas.

description: The story of the birth of Rama and Ravana
sn: एतन्मे भगवन् अभवंस्तस्य चत्वारः पुत्रा धर्मार्थकोविदाः। रामलक्ष्मणशत्रुघ्ना भरतश्च महाबलः॥
en: He had four sons well-versed in Dharma and Artha namely Rama, Lakshmana, Shatrughna and the mighty Bharata.

description: The story of the birth of Rama and Ravana
sn: रामस्य माता कौसल्य कैकेयी भरतस्य तु। सुतौ लक्ष्मणशत्रुघ्नौ सुमित्रायाः परंतपौ॥
en: Rama's mother was Kausalaya, Bharata's mother was Kaikeyi and Sumitra was the mother of Lakshmana and Shatrughana, the repressors of enemies.

description: The story of the birth of Rama and Ravana
sn: विदेहराजो जनकः सीता तस्यात्मजा विभो। यां चकार स्वयं त्वष्टा रामस्य महिषीं प्रियाम्॥
en: O lord, Janaka was the king of Videha and his daughter was Sita. Tvashtri himself created her wishing to make her the beloved queen of Rama.

description: The story of the birth of Rama and Ravana
sn: एतद् रामस्य ते जन्म सीतायाश्च प्रकीर्तितम्। रावणस्यापि ते जन्म व्याख्यास्यामि जनेश्वर।॥
en: I have thus recounted to you the birth of Rama and Sita; O lord of men, I shall now describe the birth of Ravana.

description: The story of the birth of Rama and Ravana
sn: पितामहो रावणस्य साक्षाद् देवः प्रजापतिः। स्वयम्भूः सर्वलोकानां प्रभुः स्रष्टा महातपाः॥
en: Prajapati himself, the self-create, the creator, the Lord of creatures, of great exertions, is the grand-father of Ravana.

description: The story of the birth of Rama and Ravana
sn: पुलस्त्यो नाम तस्यासीन्मानसो दयितः सुतः। तस्य वैश्रवणो नाम गवि पुत्रोऽभवत् प्रभुः॥
en: Prajapati had a favourite son born of his mind by name Pulastya; and he had a powerful son begotten of cow by name Vaishravana.

description: The story of the birth of Rama and Ravana
sn: पितरं स समुत्सृज्य पितामहमुपस्थितः। तस्य कोपात् पिता राजन् ससर्जात्मानमात्मा॥
en: Leaving his father he went to his grandfather. Accordingly worked up with anger, O king, he created a second self of himself.

description: The story of the birth of Rama and Ravana
sn: स जज्ञे विश्रवा नाम तस्यात्मार्धेन वै द्विजः। प्रतीकाराय सक्रोधस्ततो वैश्रवणस्य वै॥
en: Thereupon for wrecking vengeance on Vaishravana in great anger that regenerate one, with half of his own self, created Vaishravana.

description: The story of the birth of Rama and Ravana
sn: पितामहस्तु प्रीतात्मा ददौ वैश्रवणस्य ह। अमरत्वं धनेशत्वं लोकपालत्वमेव च॥
en: (However) pleased, the grand-father conferred on Vaishravana immortality, the sovereignty of all wealth and guardianship of one of the quarters.

description: The story of the birth of Rama and Ravana
sn: ईशानेन तथा सख्यं पुत्रं च नलकूबरम्। राजधानीनिवेशं च लङ्कां रक्षोगणान्विताम्॥
en: The friendship with Ishana and a son named Nalakubera. He created Lanka as his capital protected by Rakshasas.

description: The story of the birth of Rama and Ravana
sn: विमानं पुष्पकं नाम कामगं च ददौ प्रभुः। यक्षाणामाधिपत्यं च राजराजत्वमेव च॥
en: The Lord gave him a chariot coursing at will by name Pushpaka, the sovereignty over he Yakshas and the supremacy over kings.

description: The story of the birth of Rama and Ravana
sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच पुलस्त्यस्य तु यः क्रोधादर्धदेहोऽभवन्मुनिः। विश्रवा नाम सक्रोधः स वैश्रवणमैक्षत॥
en: Markandeya said : The ascetic Vishrava, who was begotten of the half body of Pulastya, with great anger began to look upon Vaishravana.

description: The story of the birth of Rama and Ravana
