sn: बुबुधे तं तु सक्रोधं पितरं राक्षसेश्वरः। कुबेरस्तत्प्रसादार्थं यतते स्म सदा नृप॥
en: Knowing that his sire was angry with him, Kubera, the lord of Rakshasas, always tried to please him, O king.

description: The story of the birth of Rama and Ravana
sn: स राजराजो लङ्कायां न्यवसन्नरवाहनः। राक्षसीः प्रददौ तिस्रः पितुर्वै परिचारिकाः॥
en: Living in Lanka that king of kings, borne on the shoulders of men, sent three Rakshasis to wait upon his father.

description: The story of the birth of Rama and Ravana
sn: ताः सदा तं महात्मानं संतोषयितुमुद्यताः। ऋषि भरतशार्दूल नृत्यगीतविशारदाः॥
en: O foremost of the Bharata, they, well-versed in the art of singing and dancing, always engaged in encompassing the pleasure of the high-souled Rishi.

description: The story of the birth of Rama and Ravana
sn: पुष्पोत्कटा च राका च मालिनी च विशाम्पते। अन्योन्यस्पर्धया राजन् श्रेयस्कामाः सुमध्यमाः॥
en: O lord of the world, O king, Pushpotkata and Raka and Malini, slender waisted, vied with one another in pleasing him.

description: The story of the birth of Rama and Ravana
sn: स तासां भगवांस्तुष्टो महात्मा प्रददौ वरान्। लोकपालोपमान् पुत्रानेकैकस्या यथेप्सितान्॥
en: Being pleased with them, the high-souled sage conferred boons on them-and on each of them sons like Lokapalas according to their desire.

description: The story of the birth of Rama and Ravana
sn: पुष्पोत्कटायां जज्ञाते द्वौ पुत्रौ राक्षसेश्वरौ। कुम्भकर्णदशग्रीवौ बलेनाप्रतिमौ भुवि॥
en: He begot on Pushpotkata two sons, the lords of the Rakshasas, Kumbhakarna and the tenheaded (Ravana) both unequalled in prowess on earth.

description: The story of the birth of Rama and Ravana
sn: मालिनी जनयामास पुत्रमेकं विभीषणम्। राकायां मिथुनं जज्ञे खरः शूर्पणखा तथा॥
en: On Malini he begot one son named Vibhishana; on Raka he begot one son and one daughter named Khara and Shurpanakha.

description: The story of the birth of Rama and Ravana
sn: विभीषणस्तु रूपेण सर्वेभ्योऽभ्यधिकोऽभवत्। स बभूव महाभागो धर्मगोप्ता क्रियारतिः॥
en: In beauty Vibhishana surpassed them all; he grew very pious and used to perform rites.

description: The story of the birth of Rama and Ravana
sn: दशग्रीवस्तु सर्वेषां श्रेष्ठो राक्षसपुङ्गवः। महोत्साहो महावीर्यो महासत्त्वपराक्रमः॥
en: That foremost of Rakshasas, the ten-headed (Ravana) became the greatest of them all; highly energetic, powerful and gifted with great strength and prowess.

description: The story of the birth of Rama and Ravana
sn: कुम्भकर्णो बलेनासीत् सर्वेभ्योऽभ्यधिको युधि। मायावी रणशौण्डश्च रौद्रश्च रजनीचरः॥
en: The Rakshasa Kumbhakarna was the most powerful in battle; he was fierce, terrible and a perfect master of the arts of illustration.

description: The story of the birth of Rama and Ravana
sn: खरो धनुषि विक्रान्तो ब्रह्मविट् पिशिताशनः। सिद्धविघ्नकरी चापि रौद्री शूर्पणाखा तथा॥
en: Khara was proficient in archery, inimical towards Brahmanas and used to eat flesh; Shurpanakha used always to put impediments in the performance of ascetic observances.

description: The story of the birth of Rama and Ravana
sn: सर्वे वेदविदः शूराः सर्वे सुचरितव्रताः। ऊषुः पित्रा सह रता गन्धमादनपर्वते॥
en: All those heroes, well-versed in the Vedas and intent on the performance of religious rites, lived with their father in the Gandhamadana mountain.

description: The story of the birth of Rama and Ravana
sn: ततो वैश्रवणं तत्र ददृशुर्नरवाहनम्। पित्रा सार्धं समासीनमृद्ध्या परमया युतम्॥
en: There they saw Vaishravana seated with their father possessed of wealth and carried by men.

description: The story of the birth of Rama and Ravana
sn: जातामर्षास्ततस्ते तु तपसे धृतनिश्चयाः। ब्रह्माणं तोषयामासुघरिण तपसा तदा॥
en: Possessed by jealousy they made up their mind to perform devout penances; and they pleased Brahma with severest ascetic penances.

description: The story of the birth of Rama and Ravana
sn: अतिष्ठदेकपादेन सहस्रं परिवत्सरान्। वायुभक्षो दशग्रीवः पञ्चाग्निः सुसमाहितः॥
en: Subsisting on air only surrounded by five sacred fires and engaged in meditation the tenheaded Ravana remained standing on one leg for a thousand years.

description: The story of the birth of Rama and Ravana
sn: अध:शायी कुम्भकर्णो यताहारो यतव्रतः। विभीषणः शीर्णपर्णमेकमभ्यवहारयन्॥ उपवासरतिर्धीमान् सदा जप्यपरायणः। तमेव कालमातिष्ठत् तीव्र तप उदारधीः॥
en: Lying down on earth and with restricted diet Kumbhakarna was engaged in penances; the wise and noble Vibhishana, fasting and living on dry leaves, engaged in meditation and practised devout penances for as long a period.

description: The story of the birth of Rama and Ravana
sn: खरः शूर्पणखा चैव तेषां वै तप्यतां तपः। परिचर्यां च रक्षां च चक्रतुर्हष्टमानसौ॥
en: Khara and Shurpanakha with delighted hearts waited upon and protected them who were thus engaged in devout penances.

description: The story of the birth of Rama and Ravana
sn: पूर्णे वर्षसहस्रे तु शिरश्छित्त्वा दशाननः। जुहोत्यग्नौ दुराधर्षस्तेनातुष्यज्जगत्प्रभुः॥
en: After the completion of a thousand years the invincible ten-headed, cutting off his ten heads, made them an offering to the sacred fire. The Lord of the universe was pleased with this act.

description: The story of the birth of Rama and Ravana
sn: ततो ब्रह्मा स्वयं गत्वा तपसस्तान् न्यवारयत्। प्रलोभ्य वरदानेन सर्वानेव पृथक् पृथक्॥
en: Thereupon Brahma, going there himself, made them desist from ascetic observances by promising to confer upon each one of them boons separately.

description: The story of the birth of Rama and Ravana
sn: ब्रह्मोवाच प्रीतोऽस्मि वो निवर्तध्वं वरान् वृणुत पुत्रकाः। यद् यदिष्टमृते त्वेकममरत्वं तथास्तु तत्॥
en: Brahma said: I am pleased with you, desist, O sons and pray for boons; all your desires, with the exception of immortality only, will be fulfilled.

description: The story of the birth of Rama and Ravana
sn: यद् यदग्नौ हुतं सर्वं शिरस्ते महदीप्सया। तथैव तानि ते देहे भविष्यन्ति यथेप्सया॥
en: As you have given your heads to fire from great ambition, they will again adorn your body as before, according to your desire.

description: The story of the birth of Rama and Ravana
sn: वैरूप्यं च न ते देहे कामरूपधरस्तथा। भविष्यसि रणेऽरीणां विजेता न च संशयः॥
en: There will be no disfigurement in your person; you shall be able to assume any person according to your desire, you shall always vanquish your enemies in battle.

description: The story of the birth of Rama and Ravana
sn: रावण उवाच गन्धर्वदेवासुरतो यक्षराक्षसतस्तथा। सर्पकिन्नरभूतेभ्यो न मे भूयात् पराभवः॥
en: Ravana said: May I never meet with defeat at the hands of Gandharvas, celestials, Kinnaras Asuras, Yakshas, Rakshasas, Nagas and all other creatures.

description: The story of the birth of Rama and Ravana
sn: ब्रह्मोवाच य एते कीर्तिताः सर्वे न तेभ्योऽस्ति भयं तव। ऋते मनुष्याद् भद्रं ते तथा तद् विहितं मया।॥
en: Brahma said: You shall have no fear from those of whom you have mentioned except from men; may good betide you, this has been ordained by me.

description: The story of the birth of Rama and Ravana
sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच एवमुक्तो दशग्रीवस्तुष्टः समभवत् तदा। अवमेने हि दुर्बुद्धिर्मनुष्यान् पुरुषादकः॥
en: Markandeya said : Thus accosted the ten headed Ravana was greatly delighted; on account of his perverted understanding, the man-eating (demon) disregarded human beings.

description: The story of the birth of Rama and Ravana
sn: कुम्भकर्णमथोवाच तथैव प्रपितामहः। स वढे महतीं निद्रां तमसा चस्तचेतनः॥
en: In the same way the grandfather addressed Kumbhakarna also; his reason being clouded by darkness he prayed for long lasting sleep.

description: The story of the birth of Rama and Ravana
sn: तथा भविष्यतीत्युक्त्वा विभीषणमुवाच ह। वरं वृष्णीष्व पुत्र त्वं प्रीतोऽस्मीति पुनः पुनः॥
en: Saying "So it shall be" he said to Vibhishana, “pray for a boon, O my son, I have been repeatedly pleased with you."

description: The story of the birth of Rama and Ravana
sn: विभीषण उवाच परमापद्गतस्यापि नाधर्मे मे मतिर्भवेत्। अशिक्षितं च भगवन् ब्रह्मास्त्रं प्रतिभातु मे॥
en: Vibhishana said: Even in great calamity may I have no inclination for impiety; ignorant, as I am, O lord, may the light of divine knowledge appear before me.

description: The story of the birth of Rama and Ravana
sn: ब्रह्मोवाच यस्माद् राक्षसयोनौ ते जातस्यामित्रकर्शन्। नाधर्मे धीयते बुद्धिरमरत्वं ददानि ते॥
en: Brahma said : O repressor of your enemies, as your mind is not inclined to impiety, although you are born as a Rakshasas, I grant you immortality.

description: The story of the birth of Rama and Ravana
sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच राक्षसस्तु वरं लब्ध्वा दशग्रीवो विशाम्पते। लङ्कायाश्च्यावयामास युधि जित्वा धनेश्वरम्॥
en: Markandeya said : Having obtained this boon, the ten-headed Ravana defeated Kubera in battle and wrested from him the sovereignty of Lanka.

description: The story of the birth of Rama and Ravana
sn: हित्वा स भगवाँल्लङ्कामाविशद् गन्धमादनम्। गन्धर्वयक्षानुगतो रक्षःकिम्पुरुषैः सह॥
en: That Divine one leaving Lanka and followed by Gandharva, Yakshas, Rakshasas and Kinnaras went to live on the mor atain Gandhamadana.

description: The story of the birth of Rama and Ravana
sn: विमानं पुष्पकं तस्य जहाराक्रम्य रावणः। शशाप तं वैश्रवणो न त्वामेतद् वहिष्यति॥
en: By force Ravana took from him the chariot Pushpaka. Vaishravana then cursed him, “This will not carry you;

description: The story of the birth of Rama and Ravana
sn: यस्तु त्वां समरे हन्ता तमेवैतद् वहिष्यति। अवमन्य गुरुं मां च क्षिप्रं त्वं न भविष्यसि॥
en: It will carry him who will kill you in battle; as you have insulted me who am your adorable, you shall soon die.”

description: The story of the birth of Rama and Ravana
sn: विभीषणस्तु धर्मात्मा सतां मार्गमनुस्मरन्। अन्वगच्छन्महाराज श्रिया परमया युतः॥
en: Always wending the way of the pious, those virtuous-souled Vibhishana, endued with great glory, followed him, O great king.

description: The story of the birth of Rama and Ravana
sn: तस्मै स भगवांस्तुष्टो भ्राता भ्रात्रे धनेश्वरः। सैनापत्यं ददौ धीमान् यक्षराक्षससेनयोः॥
en: Then pleased with his younger brother, the Divine king of wealth, conferred upon him the command of the Yaksha and Rakshasa hosts.

description: The story of the birth of Rama and Ravana
sn: राक्षसाः पुरुषादाश्च पिशाचाश्च महाबलाः। सर्वे समेत्य राजानमभ्यषिञ्चन् दशाननम्॥
en: The man-eating and highly powerful Rakshasas and Pishachas, having assembled together, installed the ten-headed Ravana as their king.

description: The story of the birth of Rama and Ravana
sn: दशग्रीवश्च दैत्यानां देवानां च बलोत्कटः। आक्रम्य रत्नान्यहरत् कामरूपी विहङ्गमः॥
en: The terribly powerful, ten-headed (Ravana) assuming form at will and capable of going through the sky, attacked the gods and demons and took away by force from them their valuable property.

description: The story of the birth of Rama and Ravana
sn: रावयामास लोकान् यत् तस्माद्रावण उच्यते। दशग्रीवः कामबलो देवानां भयमादधत्॥
en: Because he had terrified all creatures he was called Ravana. And the ten-headed demon, capable of having any might at will, struck terror even to the very gods.

sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच ततो ब्रह्मर्षयः सर्वे सिद्धा देवर्षयस्तथा। हव्यवाहं पुरस्कृत्य ब्रह्माणं शरणं गताः॥
en: Markandeya said : Thereupon the Brahmarshis, the Siddhas, the celestials, saints, with Havyavaha as their spokesman, sought the protection of Brahma.

sn: अग्निरुवाच योऽसौ विश्रवसः पुत्रो दशग्रीवो महाबलः। अवध्यो वरदानेन कृतो भगवता पुरा॥
en: The highly powerful, ten-headed son of Vishrava cannot be slain for the boon, that was given him before by you.

sn: स बाधते प्रजाः सर्वा विप्रकारैर्महाबलः। ततो नस्त्रातु भगवन् नान्यस्त्राता हि विद्यते॥
en: The mighty powerful one is oppressing the creatures in every possible way; therefore save us, O lord; there is none else except you to save us.

sn: ब्रह्मोवाच न स देवासुरैः शक्यो युद्धे जेतुं विभावसो। विहितं तत्र यत् कार्यमभितस्तस्य निग्रहः॥
en: Brahma said: O Vibhavasu, he cannot slain in battle either by the celestials or the Asuras I have already ordained what is necessary for this purpose. But his death is near.

sn: तदर्थमवतीर्णोऽसौ मन्नियोगाच्चतुर्भुजः। विष्णुः प्रहरतां श्रेष्ठः स तत् कर्म करिष्यति।॥
en: For this purpose and at my command the four-headed god has already been incarnated; Vishnu, the foremost of repressors, shall accomplish this.

sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच पितामहस्ततस्तेषां संनिधौ शक्रमब्रवीत्। सर्वैर्दवगणैः सार्धं सम्भव त्वं महीतले॥
en: In their presence then the Grandfather said to Shakra, “You also take your birth on earth, with all these celestials.

sn: विष्णोः सहायानृक्षीषु वानरीषु च सर्वशः। जनयध्वं सुतान् वीरान् कामरूपबलान्वितान्॥
en: You all beget on monkeys and bears heroic and powerful sons capable of assuring forms at will to help Vishnu."

sn: ततो भागानुभागेन देवगन्धर्वपन्नगाः। अवतर्तुं महीं सर्वे मन्त्रयामासुरञ्जसा॥
en: At this, the celestial, the Gandharvas and the Danavas quickly assembled to consult as to how they should he born on earth according to their respective parts.

sn: तेषां समक्षं गन्धर्वी दुन्दुभी नाम नामतः। शशास वरदो देवो गच्छ कार्यार्थसिद्धये॥
en: In their presence the Deity, conferring boons commanded a Gandharvi named Dundubhi saying, “Go there for accomplishing this object.”

sn: पितामहवचः श्रुत्वा गन्धर्वी दुन्दुभी ततः। मन्थरा मानुषे लोके कुब्जा समभवत् तदा॥
en: Hearing the words of Grandfather, Dundubhi became born on earth as the haunchbacked Manthara.

sn: शक्रप्रभृतयश्चैव सर्वे ते सुरसत्तमाः। वानरक्षवरस्त्रीषु जनयामासुरात्मजान्॥
en: And all the leading celestial, Shakra and others begot offspring on the wives of the foremost of monkeys and bears.

sn: तेऽन्ववर्तन् पितृन् सर्वे यशसा च बलेन च। भेत्तारो गिरिशृङ्गाणां शालतालशिलायुधाः॥
en: They all took after their fathers, in strength and fame; they were capable of breaking down mountain summits and their weapons were trees of Shala and Tala.

sn: वलासंहननाः सर्वे सर्वे चौघबलास्तथा। कामवीर्यबलाश्चैव सर्वे युद्धविशारदाः॥ वनौकसः॥
en: Their bodies were as hard as adamant and they were all endued with very great strength; they were all skilled in the art of warfare and could summon any amount of strength at their will.

sn: नागायुतसमप्राणा वायुवेगसमा जवे। यत्रेच्छकनिवासाश्च केचिदत्र
en: They were gifted with the strength of an Ayuta elephants and were like the wind in speed; some of them lived wherever they liked; others lived in woods.

sn: एवं विधाय तत् सर्वं भगवाँल्लोकभावनः। मन्थरां बोधयामास यद् यत् कार्यं यथा यथा॥
en: Having ordained all this the worshipful creator instructed Manthara as to what she should do.

sn: सा तद्वचः समाज्ञाय तथा चक्रे मनोजवा। इतश्चेतश्च गच्छन्ती वैरसन्धुक्षणे रता॥
en: Understanding his words she, quick as thought, did accordingly. She moved about here and there fanning quarrels.

description: The exile of Rama into the forest
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच उक्तं भगवता जन्म रामादीनां पृथक् पृथक्। प्रस्थानकारणं ब्रह्मच्छ्रोतुमिच्छामि कथ्यताम्॥ कथं दाशरथी वीरौ भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ। सम्प्रस्थितौ वने ब्रह्मन् मैथिली च यशस्विनी॥
en: Yudhishthira said : Your worshipful self has related (to me) separately of the birth of Rama and others, O Brahmana, I am (now) desirous of hearing of the cause of their exile. Tell me, O Brahmana, why the heroic sons of Dasharatha, the brothers Rama and Lakshmana, departed to the forest, together with the renowned Maithili (Sita, daughter of the king of Mithila).

description: The exile of Rama into the forest
sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच जातपुत्रो दशरथः प्रीतिमानभवनृप। क्रियारतिधर्मरतः सततं वृद्धसेविता॥
en: Markandeya said: O King, Dasharatha, always devoted to religion and given to the performance of) religious ceremonies and engaged in ministering to the comforts of his elders, was (very) glad at the birth of his sons.

description: The exile of Rama into the forest
sn: क्रमेण चास्य ते पुत्रा व्यवर्धन्त महौजसः। वेदेषु सरहस्येषु धनुर्वेदेषु पारगाः॥
en: Those sons of his, gradually grew up in strength, obtained mastery over the Vedas together with all their mysteries and became skilled in the science of weapons.

description: The exile of Rama into the forest
sn: चरितब्रह्मचर्यास्ते कृतदाराश्च पार्थिव। यदा तदा दशरथः प्रीतिमानभवत् सुखी॥
en: When after having observed the Brahmacharya vows, they got they got married. Dasharatha, O king, became (very) pleased and happy.

description: The exile of Rama into the forest
sn: ज्येष्ठो रामोऽभवत् तेषां रमयामास हि प्रजाः। मनोहरतया धीमान् पितुर्हदयनन्दनः॥
en: (And) among them his intelligent eldest son, who gladdened the heart of his father and delighted his subjects, was named Rama on account of his sweet disposition.

description: The exile of Rama into the forest
sn: ततः स राजा मतिमान् मत्वाऽऽत्मानं वयोऽधिकम्। मन्त्रयामास सचिवैधर्मज्ञैश्च पुरोहितैः॥ अभिषेकाय रामस्य यौवराज्येन भारत।
en: O Bharata, then that wise monarch considering himself far too advanced in age (to look after worldly affairs), for the installation of Rama as the prince regent; consulted with his righteous ministers and priests.

description: The exile of Rama into the forest
sn: प्राप्तकालं च ते सर्वे मेनिरे मन्त्रिसत्तमाः॥ लोहिताक्षं महाबाहुं मत्तमातङ्गगामिनम्। कम्बुग्रीवं महोरस्कं नीलकुञ्चितमूर्धजम्॥ दीप्यमानं श्रिया वीरं शक्रादनवरं रणे। पारगं सर्वधर्माणां बृहस्पतिसमं मतौ॥ सर्वानुरक्तप्रकृति सर्वविद्याविशारदम्। जितेन्द्रियममित्राणामपि दृष्टिमनोहरम्॥ नियन्तारमसाधूनां गोप्तारं धर्मचारिणाम्। धृतिमन्तनाधृष्यं जेतारमपराजितम्॥ पुत्रं राजा दशरथः कौसल्यानन्दवर्धनम्। संदृश्य परमां प्रीतिमगच्छत् कुरुनन्दन॥
en: And all those best of advisers thought that it was the proper time (for the purpose). O descendant of the Kurus, king Dasharatha was greatly pleased on beholding his son (Rama) of red eyes and mighty arms, endued with the gait of an elephant mad (with exuberance of spirits), of long arms and broad chest, having blue and curly hair, blazing with beauty, brave as Shakra in battle, versed in all the religious duties, wise as Brihaspati, an object of adoration with all his subjects, proficient in every science and art, of subdued passions, pleasant to the eye of even his enemies, the chastiser of the wicked, the protector of the virtuous, endued with high intellect, invincible, ever victorious and never vanquished and the enhancer of the joy of (his mother) Kausalya.

description: The exile of Rama into the forest
sn: चिन्तयंश्च महातेजा गुणान् रामस्य वीर्यवान्। अभ्यभाषत भद्रं ते प्रीयमाणः पुरोहितम्॥ अद्य पुष्यो निशि ब्रह्मन् पुण्यं योगमुपैष्यति। सम्भाराः सम्भियन्तां मे रामश्चोपनिमन्त्र्यताम्॥
en: That highly energetic and powerful one (Dasharatha) thinking of the qualifications of Rama, was well-pleased and (thus) addressed his priest, "O Brahmana, this night the constellation Paushya being in the ascendant, will be a highly auspicious time. Let therefore my attendants collect materials (for the inauguration) and let Rama also be invited.”

description: The exile of Rama into the forest
sn: इति तद् राजवचनं प्रतिश्रुत्याथ मन्थरा। कैकेयीमभिगम्येदं काले वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Hearing these words of the king, Manthara (the maid of Kaikeyi) went to Kaikeyi and addressed her these words suited to the occasion.

description: The exile of Rama into the forest
sn: अद्य कैकेयि दौर्भाग्यं राज्ञा ते ख्यापितं महत्। आशीविषस्त्वां संक्रुद्धश्चण्डो दशतु दुर्भगे॥
en: O Kaikeyi, your great ill-luck has today been proclaimed by the king. O unfortunate one, may a fierce and angry venomous snake bite you.

description: The exile of Rama into the forest
sn: सुभगा खलु कौसल्या यस्याः पुत्रोऽभिषेक्ष्यते। कुतो हि तव सौभाग्यं यस्याः पुत्रो न राज्यभाक्।।१८।
en: It is indeed Kausalya who is fortunate in as much as her son will be installed. Where is your good fortune since your son will not obtain the kingdom?

description: The exile of Rama into the forest
sn: सा तद्वचनमाज्ञाय सर्वाभरणभूषिता। देवी विलग्नमध्येव बिभ्रती रूपमुत्तमम्॥ विविक्ते पतिमासाद्य हसन्तीव शुचिस्मिता। प्रणयं व्यञ्जयन्तीव मधुरं वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
en: O hearing these words of (Manthara), Kaikeyi with her waist resembling the middle of a Dambura, decked with all sorts of ornaments and wearing a highly beautiful appearance, sought her lord in a secluded place and making a show of love, smilingly spoke these sweet words.

description: The exile of Rama into the forest
sn: सत्यप्रतिज्ञ यन्मे त्वं काममेकं निसृष्टवान्। उपाकुरुष्व तद् राजस्तस्मान्मुच्यस्व संकटात्॥
en: "O king, you are (always) firm in your promise. Formerly you promised me a boon. Do you grant it now and thereby save yourself the sin of an unredeemed promise."

description: The exile of Rama into the forest
sn: राजोवाच वरं ददानि ते हन्त तद् गृहाण यदिच्छसि। अबध्यो बध्यतां कोऽद्य बध्यः कोऽद्यविमुच्यताम्॥
en: The King said: "I am ready to grant you any boon you like. Is there anybody to be slain that does not deserve death or is there any one to be set at liberty who is imprisoned?

description: The exile of Rama into the forest
sn: धनं ददानि कस्याद्य ह्रियतां कस्य वा पुनः। ब्राह्मणस्वादिहान्यत्र यत् किंचिद् वित्तमस्ति मे॥
en: Whom shall I heap riches upon and whom shall I deprive of his wealth? Everything on earth belongs to me except what is possessed by the Brahmanas.

description: The exile of Rama into the forest
sn: पृथिव्यां राजराजोऽस्मि चातुर्वर्ण्यस्य रक्षिता। यस्तेऽभिलषित: कामो ब्रूहि कल्याणि मा चिरम्॥
en: I am, in this world, the king of all kings and the guardian of the four orders, O fortunate one, express your desire without delay".

description: The exile of Rama into the forest
sn: सा तद्वचनमाज्ञाय परिगृहा नराधिपम्। आत्मनो बलमाज्ञाय तत एनमुवाच ह॥
en: Listening to these words of the king and binding him to his promise, she, well aware of her influence over him, spoke these words,

description: The exile of Rama into the forest
sn: आभिषेचनिकं यत् ते रामार्थमुपकल्पिपतम्। भरतस्तदवाप्नोतु वनं गच्छतु राघवः॥
en: “Let Bharata be installed with the materials brought for Rama and let Raghava depart to the forests."

description: The exile of Rama into the forest
sn: स तद् राजा वचः श्रुत्वा विप्रियं दारुणोदयम्। दुःखार्तो भरतश्रेष्ठ न किंचिद् व्याजहार ह॥
en: O the best of the Bharata, on hearing this disagreeable speech of terrible significance, the king weighed down with grief, could not speak anything.

description: The exile of Rama into the forest
sn: ततस्तथोक्तं पितरं रामो विज्ञाय वीर्यवान्। वनं प्रतस्थे धर्मात्मा राजा सत्यो भवत्विति॥
en: Learning that his father has been thus promise-bound and considering that the king's truth ought to remain inviolable, the virtuous and powerful Rama went into the forests.

description: The exile of Rama into the forest
sn: तमन्वगच्छल्लक्ष्मीवान् धनुष्मॉल्लक्ष्मणस्तदा। सीता च भार्या भद्रं ते वैदेही जनकात्मजा॥
en: And, may you be blessed, he (Rama) was followed by the prosperous Lakshmana, the foremost of bowmen and his wife Sita, the princess of Videha and daughter of Janaka.

description: The exile of Rama into the forest
sn: ततो वनं गते रामे राजा दशरथस्तदा। समयुज्यत देहस्य कालपर्यायधर्मणा॥
en: Then Rama having departed to the forest, Dasharatha, following the eternal law of time, gave up the ghost.

description: The exile of Rama into the forest
sn: रामं तु गतमाज्ञाय राजानं च तथागतम्। आनाय्य भरतं देवी कैकेयी वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
en: And seeing that Rama had left for the forest and that the king had breathed his last, Kaikeyi causing Bharata to be brought, addressed to him these words.

description: The exile of Rama into the forest
sn: गतो दशरथः स्वर्ग वनस्थौ रामलक्ष्मणौ। गृहाण राज्यं विपुलं क्षेमं निहतकण्टकम्॥
en: “Now that the king has gone to heaven and Rama and Lakshmana have left for the forest, accept this auspicious and extensive kingdom with all its thorns weeded out."

description: The exile of Rama into the forest
sn: तामुवाच स धर्मात्मा नृशंसं वत ते कृतम्। पतिं हत्वा कुलं चेदमुत्साद्य धनलुब्धया।॥ अयशः पातयित्वा मे मूर्ध्नि त्वं कुलपांसने। सकामा भव मे मातरित्युक्त्वा प्ररुरोद ह॥
en: (Thereupon), the virtuous (Bharata) said to her “You have committed a very cruel deed by killing your husband and exterminating the family actuated by greed of wealth alone. O accursed (woman) of (our) family, hurling disgrace upon my head, fulfill your desire now.” Saying this to her mother, he gave free vent to his tears.

description: The exile of Rama into the forest
sn: स चारित्रं विशोध्याथ सर्वप्रकृतिसंनिधौ। अन्वयाद् भ्रातरं रामं विनिवर्तनलालसः॥
en: And vindicating his character before all the subjects, he set out, desirous of bringing back his brother Rama.

description: The exile of Rama into the forest
sn: कौसल्यां च सुमित्रां च कैकेयीं च सुदुःखितः। अचे प्रस्थाप्य यानैः स शत्रुघ्नसहितो ययौ॥
en: Placing, Kausalya, Sumitra and Kaikeyi in vehicle at the van (of his train), he set out with a sorrowful heart, accompanied by Shatrughna.

description: The exile of Rama into the forest
sn: वसिष्ठवामदेवाभ्यां विप्रैश्चान्यैः सहस्रशः। पौरजानपदैः सार्धं रामानयनकाझया।॥
en: Vasishtha, Vamadeva, thousands of other Brahmanas and the people of the cities and the provinces, with an eager desire to bring Rama back.

description: The exile of Rama into the forest
sn: ददर्श चित्रकूटस्थं स रामं सहलक्ष्मणम्। तापसानामलंकारं धारयन्तं धनुर्धरम्॥
en: (And he) found Rama together with Lakshmana in the mountain) Chitrakuta bow in hand and wearing the garb of ascetics.

description: The exile of Rama into the forest
sn: विसर्जित: स रामेण पितुर्वचनकारिणा। नन्दिग्रामेऽकरोद् राज्यं पुरस्कृत्यास्य पादुके॥
en: (But), being dismissed by Rama who was bent on obeying his fathers; words, he (Bharata) began to reign at Nandigram placing his brother's shoes before him.

description: The exile of Rama into the forest
sn: रामस्तु पुनराशङ्कय पौरजानपदागमम्। प्रविवेश महारण्यं शरभङ्गाश्रमं प्रति॥
en: And Rama too, afraid of the return of the people of the cities and provinces entered into the mighty forest of Dandaka near the hermitage of Sharabhanga.

description: The exile of Rama into the forest
sn: सत्कृत्य शरभङ्गं स दण्डकारण्यमाश्रितः। नदी गोदावरी रम्यामाश्रित्य न्यवसत् तदा॥
en: Paying his adorations to Sharabhanga and taking refuge in the Dandaka, forest he began to dwell on the banks of the beautiful river Godavari.

description: The exile of Rama into the forest
sn: वसतस्तस्य रामस्य ततः शूर्पणखाकृतम्। खरेणासीन्महद् वैरं जनस्थाननिवासिना॥
en: While dwelling there, Rama had great enmity with Khara who had his abode in the Janasthana, on account of Shurpanakha.

description: The exile of Rama into the forest
sn: रक्षार्थं तापसानां तु राघवो धर्मवत्सलः। चतुर्दश सहस्राणि जघान भुवि रक्षसाम्॥ दूषणं च खरं चैव निहत्य सुमहाबलौ। चक्रे क्षेमं पुनर्धीमान् धर्मारण्यं स राघवः॥
en: The descendant of Raghu, devoted to virtue, slew fourteen thousands of Rakshasas on earth for the protection of the ascetics and the intelligent Raghava having slain the highlypowerful Khara and Dushana resorted peace to that sacred forest.

description: The exile of Rama into the forest
sn: हतेषु तेषु रक्षःसु ततः शूर्पणखा पुनः। ययौ निकृत्तनासोष्ठी लङ्का भ्रातुर्निवेशनम्॥
en: Those Rakshasas being slain, Shurpanakha with her nose and lips cut off returned to Lanka, the abode of her brother (Ravana).

description: The exile of Rama into the forest
sn: ततो रावणमभ्येत्य राक्षसी दुःखमूर्च्छिता। पपात पादयोर्धातुः संशुष्करुधिरानना॥
en: Then that Rakshasas-woman senseless with grief and with marks of dry blood on her face, approaching Ravana, fell down at his feet.

description: The exile of Rama into the forest
sn: तां तथा विकृतां दृष्ट्वा रावणः क्रोधमूर्च्छितः। उत्पपातासनात् क्रुद्धो दन्तैर्दन्तानुपस्पृशन्॥
en: Seeing her thus multilated Ravana became senseless with rage and fired with anger and gnashing his teeth, rose up from his throne.

description: The exile of Rama into the forest
sn: स्वानमात्यान् विसृज्याथ विविक्ते तामुवाच सः। केनास्येवं कृता भद्रे मामचिन्त्यावमन्य च॥
en: And dismissing his ministers he asked her in private "O gentle sister, who has made you so by despising and disregarding me?

description: The exile of Rama into the forest
sn: कः शूलं तीक्ष्णमासाद्य सर्वगात्रैनिषेवते। कः शिरसस्यग्निमाघाय विश्वस्तः स्वपते सुखम्॥
en: Who is he that having got a sharp spear has rubbed it all over his body? Who is he that is sleeping in peace and security, keeping a fire near his head?

description: The exile of Rama into the forest
sn: आशीविषं घोरतरं पादेन स्पृशतीह कः। सिंह केसरिणं कश्च दंष्ट्रायां स्पृश्य तिष्ठति॥
en: Who is he that has trodden over a terrible snake? Who is he that has thrust his hand into the jaws of a mained lion?"

description: The exile of Rama into the forest
sn: इत्येवं ब्रुवतस्तस्य स्रोतोभ्यस्तेजसोऽचिषः। निश्चेरुर्दह्यतो रात्रौ वृक्षस्येव स्वरन्ध्रतः॥
en: While he was saying thus, sparks of flame issued out from his organs of senses like those that are emitted from the hollows of a tree on fire at night.

description: The exile of Rama into the forest
sn: तस्य तत् सर्वमाचख्यौ भगिनी रामविक्रमम्। खरदूषणसंयुक्तं राक्षसानां पराभवम्॥
en: Then his sister informed him of the prowess of Rama causing the defeat of the Rakshasas led by Khara and Dushana.

description: The exile of Rama into the forest
sn: स निश्चित्य ततः कृत्यं स्वसारमुपसान्त्व्य च। ऊर्ध्वमाचक्रमे राजा विधाय नगरे विधिम्॥
en: Then king (Ravana) settling as to what course to adopt and making arrangements for the protection of his capital and consoling his sister, rose up in the air.

description: The exile of Rama into the forest
sn: त्रिकूटं समतिक्रम्य कालपर्वतमेव च। ददर्श मकरावासं गम्भीरोदं महोदधिम्॥
en: Crossing the mountains Trikuta and Kala he beheld the mighty ocean of deep waters, the abode of the Makaras (alligators).

description: The exile of Rama into the forest
sn: तमतीत्याथ गोकर्णमभ्यगच्छद् दशाननः। दयितं स्थानमव्यचं शूलपाणेर्महात्मनः॥
en: Then Dashanana (Ravana, who had ten mouths) crossing it (the ocean) reached Gokarna the beloved place of the high-souled wielder of the trident (Shiva).

description: The exile of Rama into the forest
sn: तत्राभ्यगच्छन्मारीचं पूर्वामात्यं दशाननः। पुरा समभयादेव तापस्यं समुपाश्रितम्॥
en: Then the ten-headed one went to his exminister Maricha who had long before at that very place adopted the mode of life led by the ascetics, through fear of Rama.

sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच मारीचस्त्वथ सम्भ्रान्तो दृष्ट्वा रावणमागतम्। पूजयामास सत्कारैः फलमूलादिभिस्ततः॥
en: Markandeya said : Seeing Ravana come, Maricha accorded to him a respectful welcome by offering fruits and roots.

sn: विश्रान्तं चैनमासीनमन्वासीनः स राक्षसः। उवाच प्रश्रितं वाक्यं वाक्यज्ञो वाक्यकोविदम्॥
en: When he (Ravana) had been seated and rested awhile, that Rakshasa (Maricha), well aware of the proper made of speech, sat beside Ravana, who was himself an eloquent speaker and humbly addressed himn thus.

sn: न ते प्रकृतिमान् वर्ण: कच्चित् क्षेमं पुरे तव। कच्चित् प्रकृतयः सर्वा भजन्ते त्वां यथा पुरा॥
en: “Your complexion is not in its natural state. Is it all right with your Kingdom? Do your subjects render obedience to you (now) as they did before?

sn: किमिहागमने चापि कार्यं ते राक्षसेश्वर। कृतमित्येव तद् विद्धि यद्यपि स्यात् सुदुष्करम्॥
en: O lord of the Rakshasas, what business has brought you here? Know it to be already performed even if it be very difficult of fulfillment."

sn: शशंस रावणस्तस्मै तत् सर्वं रामचेष्टितम्। समासेनैव कार्याणि क्रोधामर्षसमन्वितः॥
en: Ravana, whose heart was distracted with grief and anger, briefly told him of the acts of Rama and the steps that were to be taken.

sn: मारीचस्त्वब्रवीच्छ्रुत्वा समासनैव रावणम्। अलं ते राममासाद्य वीर्यज्ञो ह्यस्मि तस्य वै॥
en: On hearing Ravana, Maricha shortly told him “You must not provoke Rama, for I am well aware of his prowess.

sn: बाणवेगं हि कस्तस्य शक्तः सोढुं महात्मनः। प्रव्रज्यायां हि मे हेतुः स एव पुरुषर्षभः॥ विनाशमुखमेतत् वे केनाख्यातं दुरात्मना।
en: Is there any body who can stand the fury of the arrows of that high-souled one? That most heroic mortal is the cause of my leading this ascetic life. What wicked-minded creature has given you this advice which will lead you to the very mouth of destruction?”

sn: तमुवाचाथ सक्रोधो रावणः परिभर्स्यन्॥ अकुर्वतोऽस्मद्वचनं स्यान्मृत्युरपि ते ध्रुवम्।
en: (On hearing Maricha) Ravana reproachfully replied to him in anger. "If you do not comply with my be hests, you shall surely meet with death."

sn: मारीचश्चिन्तयामास विशिष्टान्मरणं वरम्॥ अवश्यं मरणे प्राप्ते करिष्याम्यस्य यन्मतम्।
en: Maricha then considered (within himself) "since death is certain then it is preferable at the hands of a superior being. I shall do what he (Ravana) desires."

sn: ततस्तं प्रत्युवाचाथ मारीचो रक्षसां वरम्॥ किं ते साह्यं मया कार्यं करिष्याम्यवशोऽपि तत्।
en: Then Maricha replied to the king of the Rakshasas. “What service shall I have to render to you? I shall (surely) do it even if I am not equal to it."

sn: तमब्रवीद् दशग्रीवो गच्छ सीतां प्रलोभय॥ रत्नशृङ्गो मृगो भूत्वा रत्नचित्रतनूरूहः। ध्रुवं सीता समालक्ष्य त्वां रामं चोदयिष्यति॥
en: (There at) the ten-headed one replied to him "go and tempt Sita wearing the form of a deer with golden horns and a golden skin. It is certain that on beholding you she will send Rama after you".

sn: अपक्रान्ते च काकुत्स्थे सीता वश्या भविष्यति। तामादायापनेष्यामि ततः स न भविष्यति॥ भार्यावियोगाद् दुर्बुद्धिरेतत् साह्यं कुरुष्व मे।
en: When the descendant of Kakustha (Rama) will go away (after you) Sita will be under my control. I will then forcibly take her away. (And then) that wicked-minded being (Rama) will die in consequence of the loss of his wife, Render to me this help."

sn: इत्येवमुक्तो मारीचः कृत्वोदकमथात्मनः॥ रावणं पुरतो यान्तमन्वगच्छत् सुदुःखितः।
en: Thus spoken to Maricha having performed his last rites (in anticipation of sure death) and with a heavy heart, followed Ravana who was going before him.

sn: ततस्तस्याश्रमं गत्वा रामस्थाक्लिष्टकर्मणः॥ चक्रतुस्तद् तथा सर्वमुभौ यत् पूर्वमन्त्रितम्।
en: Then having got to the hermitage of Rama of untiring action, they both did as was arranged previously.

sn: रावणस्तु यतिर्भूत्वा मुण्डः कुण्डी त्रिदण्डधृक्॥ मृगश्च भूत्वा मारीचस्तं देशमुपजग्मतुः। दर्शयामास मारीचो वैदेहीं मृगरूपधृक॥
en: Ravana, assuming the shape of an ascetic with his head shaven and holding (in his hands) a triheaded staff and Maricha in the guise of a deer appeared on the scene. And Maricha showed himself to the princess of Videha in the form of a deer.

sn: चोदयामास तस्यार्थे सा रामं विधिचोदिता। रामस्तस्याः प्रियं कुर्वन् धनुरादाय सत्वरः॥ रक्षार्थे लक्ष्मणं न्यस्य प्रययौ मृगलिप्सया।
en: Driven by destiny, Sita sent Rama in pursuit of him. And Rana (too) with a view to please her, soon taking up his bow and instructing Lakshmana to protect her, went in pursuit of that deer.

sn: स धन्वी बद्धतूणीरः खङ्गगोधाङ्गुलित्रवान्॥ अन्वधावन्मृगं रामो रुद्रस्तारामृगं यथा।
en: Equipped with his bow, quiver and sword and with his fingers encased in the skin of Godha, Rama ran after that deer as Rudra followed the stellar deer (i.e. Prajapati, who in the guise of a deer followed his daughter, but Shiva cut off his head which became the constellation called Mrigashira i.e. the deerhead).

sn: सोऽन्तर्हितः पुनस्तस्य दर्शनं राक्षसो व्रजन्॥ चकर्ष महदध्वानं रामस्तं बुबुधे ततः। निशाचरं विदित्वा तं राघवः प्रतिभानवान्॥ अमोघं शरमादाय जघान मृगरूपिणम्।
en: And that Rakshasa now appearing before him and then disappearing from his view. Allured Rama to a great distance. Rama, then, knew what that deer really was. The intelligent Raghava knowing him to be a Rakshasa, took up an arrow of infallible energy and killed him who wore the shape of a deer.

sn: स रामबाणाभिहतः कृत्वा रामस्वरं तदा।॥ हा सीते लक्ष्मणेत्येवं चुक्रोशार्तस्वरेण ह।
en: Struck by Rama's arrow, he, imitating the voice of Rama, began to cry piteously calling upon Sita and Lakshmana.

sn: शुश्राव तस्य वैदेही ततस्तां करुणां गिरम्॥ सा प्राद्रवद् यतः शब्दस्तामुवाचाथ लक्ष्मणः। अलं ते शङ्कया भीरु को रामं प्रहरिष्यति॥ मुहूर्ताद् द्रक्ष्यसे रामं भर्तारं त्वं शुचिस्मिते।
en: And (when) the princess of Videha heard those piteous cries, she was about to run towards the direction from which the sound came. Then Lakshmana spoke to her, "O timid lady, there is no reason for your fear. Who is able to strike Rama? O lady of sweet smiles, you will in a moment see your lord Rama."

sn: इत्युक्ता सा प्ररुदती पर्यशङ्कत लक्ष्मणम्॥ हता वै स्त्रीस्वभावेन शुक्लचारित्रभूषणा। सा तं परुषमारब्धा वक्तुं साध्वी पतिव्रता॥
en: Thus addressed, she, who was weeping aloud, from the weakness natural to her sex, began to suspect Lakshmana adorned with a spotless character. And that chaste woman, devoted to her husband, began to level against Lakshmana these harsh words,

sn: नैघ कामो भवेन्मूढ यं त्वं प्रार्थयसे हृदा। अप्यहं शस्त्रमादाय हन्यामात्मानमात्मना॥ पतेयं गिरिशृङ्गाद वा विशेयं वा हुताशनम्। रामं भर्तारमुत्सृज्य न त्वहं त्वां कथंचन॥ निहीनमुपतिष्ठेयं शार्दूली क्रोष्टुकं यथा।
en: "O fool, the desire which you cherish in your heart shall never be gratified. I will rather kill myself with a weapon or throw myself from the summit of a mountain or enter into fire, than forsaking my husband Rama live with such a mean wretch as you, like a tigress under the protection of jackal.

sn: एतादृशं वचः श्रुत्वा लक्ष्मणः प्रियराघवः॥ पिधाय को सद्वत्तः प्रस्थितो येन राघवः। स रामस्य पदं गृह्य प्रससार धनुर्धरः॥ अवीक्षमाणो बिम्बोष्ठी प्रययौ लक्ष्मणस्तदा।
en: Thus addressed by her, Lakshmana who was devotedly attached to Rama and who possessed a noble character, shutting up his ears (with his hands) and armed with bow went out following the foot-prints of Rama. And without casting a single look upon her whose lips resembled a (ripe) Bimba fruit, (he) set out (in search of Rama).

sn: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे रक्षो रावणः प्रत्यदृश्यत॥ अभव्यो भव्यरूपेण भस्मच्छन्न इवानलः। यतिवेषप्रतिच्छन्नो जिहीर्षुस्तामनिन्दिताम्॥
en: In the meantime, the Rakshasa Ravana appeared (before Sita). Assuming a gentele appearance though inwardly very wicked and like a fire hidden under ashes. Disguised as an ascetic he (showed himself there) in order to carry off that lady of blameless character.

sn: सा तमालक्ष्य सम्प्राप्तं धर्मज्ञा जनकात्मजा। निमन्त्रयामास तदा फलमूलाशनादिभिः॥
en: On perceiving him, the virtuous daughter of Janaka welcomed him by offering fruits roots and a seat.

sn: अवमन्य ततः सर्वं स्वरूपं प्रत्यपद्यत। सान्त्वयामास वैदेहीमिति राक्षसपुङ्गवः॥
en: But that foremost of the Rakshasas disregarding all those things and assuming his natural shape began to cheer up the Princess of Videha saying,

sn: सीते राक्षसराजोऽहं रावणो नाम विश्रुतः। मम लङ्का पुरी नाम्ना रम्या पारे महोदधेः॥
en: "O Sita, I am the lord of the Rakshasas and celebrated under the name of Ravana. My beautiful city is named Lanka and is situate on the other side of the ocean.

sn: तत्र त्वं नरनारीषु शोभिष्यसि मया सह। भार्या मे भव सुश्रोणि तापसं त्यज राघवम्॥
en: There amongst beautiful damsels you will shine with me. O lady of beautiful lips, do become my consort and abandon the ascetic Raghava".

sn: एवमादीनि वाक्यानि श्रुत्वा तस्याथ जानकी। पिधाय की सुश्रोणी मैवमित्यब्रवीद् वचः॥
en: Addressed in this strain, the daughter of Janaka, endued with beautiful lips, shut up her ears (with hands) and said "Do not say such words again.

sn: प्रपतेद् द्यौः सनक्षत्रा पृथिवी शकलीभवेत्। शैत्यमग्निरियानाहं त्यजेयं रघुनन्दनम्॥
en: Even if the firmament with all its stars fall down, even if the earth be reduced to atoms and even if the fire be deprived of heat and turn cold, I will not forsake the descendant of Raghu.

sn: कथं हि भिन्नकरटं पद्मिनं वनगोचरम्। उपस्थाय महानागं करेणुः सूकरं स्पृशेत्॥
en: Is it possible for a she-elephant who has enjoyed the company of the mighty ranger of forest with rent temples, to live with a (miserable) hog?

sn: कथं हि पीत्वा माध्वीकं पीत्वा च मधुमाधवीम्। लोभं सौवीरके कुर्यान्नारी काचिदिति स्मरेत्॥
en: How can a lady who has tasted of the sweet wire prepare . out of honey or flowers, be tempted to drink the (wretched) wine prepared from peutrid rice”!

sn: इति सा तं समाभाष्य प्रविवेशाश्रमं ततः। क्रोधात् प्रस्फुरमाणौष्ठी विधुन्वाना करौ मुहुः॥
en: Having spoken thus, she with her lips trembling in ire and repeatedly shaking her hands entered the hermitage.

sn: तामभिद्रुत्य सुश्रोणी रावणः प्रत्यषेधयत्। भर्त्सयित्वा तु रूक्षेण स्वरेण गतचेतनाम्॥
en: (But) Ravana, pursuing that lady of beautiful lips, cut off her retreat. And harshly scolded by Ravana she fell into a soon.

sn: मूर्धजेषु निजग्राह ऊर्ध्वमाचक्रमे ततः। तां ददर्श ततो गृध्रो जटायुर्गिरिगोचरः। रुदतीं राम रामेति ह्रियमाणां तपस्विनीम्॥
en: But (he) seizing her by the hair (of her head) rose up in the air. Then a vulture, Jatayu, living in a mountain, saw that helpless lady crying in distress uttering the name of Rama while being carried off (by Ravana).

description: The destruction of the headless monster
sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच सखा दशरथस्यासीज्जटायुरुणात्मजः। गृध्रराजो महावीरः सम्पातिर्यस्य सोदरः॥
en: Markandeya said : The highly-powerful lord of the vultures, Jatayu, the son of Aruna and the brother of Sampati was a friend of Dasharatha's.

description: The destruction of the headless monster
sn: स ददर्श तदा सीतां रावणाङ्कगतां स्नुषाम्। सक्रोधोऽभ्यद्रवत् पक्षी रावणं राक्षसेश्वरम्॥
en: (When) that bird saw his daughter-in-law in the arms of Ravana he furiously rushed against the lord of the Rakshasas.

description: The destruction of the headless monster
sn: अथैनमब्रवीद् गृध्रो मुञ्च मुञ्चेति मैथिलीम्। ध्रियमाणे मयि कथं हरिष्यसि निशाचर॥
en: The vulture then said to him "let go the princess of Mithila; leave her. O night-ranger, how can you carry her off when I am alive?

description: The destruction of the headless monster
sn: न हि मे मोक्ष्यसे जीवन् यदि नोत्सृजसे वधूम्। उक्त्वैवं राक्षसेन्द्रं तं चकर्त नखरै शम्॥
en: If you do not release my daughter-in-law you must not escape with your life.” Saying thus, he began to pierce the lord to the Rakshasas with his claws.

description: The destruction of the headless monster
sn: पक्षतुण्डप्रहारैश्च शतशो जर्जरीकृतम्। चक्षार रुधिरं भूरि गिरिः प्रस्रवणैरिव॥
en: By striking him with wings and beak several times, he (frightfully) lacerated (Ravana). And blood began to gush (out of his body) as copiously as waters from a mountain-spring.

description: The destruction of the headless monster
sn: स वध्यमानो गृध्रेण रामप्रियहितैषिणा। खङ्गमादाय चिच्छेद भुजौ तस्य पतत्रिणः॥
en: Thus struck by the vulture, the well-wisher of Rama, he (Ravana) taking up his sword cut off the wings of that feathery creature.

description: The destruction of the headless monster
sn: निहत्य गृध्रराजं स भिन्नाभ्रशिखरोपमम्। ऊर्ध्वमाचक्रमे सीतां गृहीत्वाङ्केन राक्षसः॥
en: Having killed that king of the vultures resembling a mountain peak penetrating through the clouds, the Rakshasa with Sita on his lap rose up (in the air).

description: The destruction of the headless monster
sn: यत्र यत्र तु वैदेही पश्यत्याश्रममण्डलम्। सरो वा सरितो वापि तत्र मुञ्चति भूषणम्॥
en: Wherever the Princess of Vaidehi beheld a hermitage, a lake or a river, she threw down there an ornament.

description: The destruction of the headless monster
sn: सा ददर्श गिरिप्रस्थे पञ्च वानरपुङ्गवान्। तत्र वासो महद्दिव्यमुत्ससर्ज मनस्विनी॥
en: That intelligent lady saw on a mountainpeak five foremost of monkeys and there she threw down a highly beautiful piece of cloth.

description: The destruction of the headless monster
sn: तत् तेषां वानरेन्द्राणां पपात पवनोद्धतम्। मध्ये सुपीतं पञ्चानां विद्युन्मेघान्तरे यथा॥
en: And like lightning (playing) among the (dark) clouds that beautiful and yellow (cloth) fluttering through the air fell down among those five (dark-coloured monkeys).

description: The destruction of the headless monster
sn: अचिरेणातिचक्राम खेचरः खे चरनिव। ददर्शाथ पुरीं रम्यां बहुद्वारा मनोरमाम्॥
en: Ranging through the air like a bird he (Ravana) soon cleared a great distance and beheld his beautiful and lovely city adorned with many gates,

description: The destruction of the headless monster
sn: प्राकारवप्रसम्बाधां निर्मितां विश्वकर्मणा। प्रविवेश पुरी लङ्कां ससीतो राक्षसेश्वरः॥
en: Surrounded by high ramparts and built by Vishvakarma. And then the lord of the Rakshasas entered his city, Lanka, with Sita.

description: The destruction of the headless monster
sn: एवं हृतायां वैदेह्यां रामो हत्वा महामृगम्। निवृत्तो ददृशे धीमान् भ्रातरं लक्ष्मणं तथा॥
en: The princess of Videha being thus carried off, the intelligent Rama having slain the great deer on his way back met his brother Lakshmana.

description: The destruction of the headless monster
sn: कथमुत्सृज्य वैदेहीं वने राक्षससेविते। इति तं भ्रातरं दृष्ट्वा प्राप्तोऽसीति व्यगर्हयत्।१४॥
en: Beholding his brother, (Rama) said to him with a rebuke "How could you leave alone the princess of Videha in the forest frequented by the Rakshasas"?

description: The destruction of the headless monster
sn: मृगरूपधेरणाथ रक्षसा सोऽपकर्षणम्। भ्रातुरागमनं चैव चिन्तयन् पर्यतप्यत॥
en: And he was greatly afflicted with grief thinking of his being allured to a great distance by the Rakshasa assuming the form of a deer and of the arrival of his brother (leaving Sita alone).

description: The destruction of the headless monster
sn: गर्हयन्नेव रामस्तु त्वरितस्तं समासदत्। अपि जीवति वैदेही नेति पश्यामि लक्ष्मणा॥
en: Having quickly come upto Lakshmana whom he was still reproving, he said “O Lakshmana, is the princess of Videha still alive? I am afraid I shall see her no more."

description: The destruction of the headless monster
sn: तस्य तत् सर्वमाचख्यौ सीताया लक्ष्मणो वचः। यदुक्तवत्यसदृशं वैदेही पश्चिमं वचः॥
en: Lakshmana then informed Rama of everything that Sita had said to him, especially the harsh words with which she subsequently rebuked him.

description: The destruction of the headless monster
sn: दह्यमानेन तु हृदा रामोऽभ्यपतदाश्रमम्। स ददर्श तदा गृधं निहतं पर्वतोपमम्॥
en: Rama then with a burning heart quickly proceeded forwards the hermitage and (on the way) he beheld the vulture, huge as mountain, in his last moments.

description: The destruction of the headless monster
sn: राक्षसं शङ्कमानस्तं विकृष्य बलवद् धनुः। अभ्यधावत काकुत्स्थस्ततस्तं सहलक्ष्मणः॥
en: Suspecting him to be a Rakshasa, the descendant of Kakustha drawing his bow powerfully, rushed at him with Lakshmana.

description: The destruction of the headless monster
sn: स तावुवाच तेजस्वी सहितौ रामलक्ष्मणौ। गृध्रराजोऽस्मि भद्रं वां सखा दशरथस्य वै॥
en: The spirited (vulture) then said to Rama and Lakshmana. “All hail to you, I am the king of the vultures and a friend of Dasharatha's."

description: The destruction of the headless monster
sn: तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा संगृह्य धनुषी शुभे। कोऽयं पितरमस्माकं नाम्नाऽऽहेत्यूचतुश्च तौ॥
en: Thus addressed by him, they put their auspicious bows aside and said "who is this one that is mentioning the name of our father?”

description: The destruction of the headless monster
sn: ततो ददृशतुस्तौ तं छिन्नपक्षद्वयं खगम्। तयोः शशंस गृध्रस्तु सीतार्थे रावणाद् वधम्॥
en: Then they both beheld the bird with its wings cut off; and the vulture related to him as to how he came by death while attempting to rescue Sita.

description: The destruction of the headless monster
sn: अपृच्छद् राघवो गृधं रावण: कां दिशं गतः। तस्य गृध्रः शिरः कम्पैराचचक्षे ममार च॥
en: Rama then asked the vultures as to the way taken by Ravana. But the vulture indicated it by a nod of the head and then passed away.

description: The destruction of the headless monster
sn: दक्षिणामिति काकुत्स्थो विदित्वास्य तदिङ्गितम्। संस्कारं लम्भयामास सखायं पूजयन् पितुः॥
en: Knowing from the sign made by the vulture that it was the south (towards which Ravana had gone) the descendant of Kakustha, out of regard for his father's friend, caused his last rites to be performed.

description: The destruction of the headless monster
sn: ततो दृष्ट्वाऽऽश्रमपदं व्यपविद्धबृसीमठम्। विध्वस्तकलशं शून्यं गोमायुशतसंकुलम्॥
en: Then beholding (on their way) many hermitages, scattered all over with seats of Kusha grass and umbrellas of leaves, broken jars of water, devoid of inmates and abounding with hundreds of Jackals,

description: The destruction of the headless monster
sn: दुःखशोकमाविष्टौ वैदेहीहरणार्दितौ। जग्मतुर्दण्डकारण्यं दक्षिणेन परंतपौ॥
en: Those tormentors of foes afflicted with distraction and grief at the abduction of Sita a proceeded towards the south of the forest Dandaka.

description: The destruction of the headless monster
sn: वने महति तस्मिंस्तु रामः सौमित्रिणा सह। ददर्श मृगयूथानि द्रवमाणानि सर्वशः॥
en: In that great forest Rama together with the son of Sumitra (Lakshmana) saw many herds of deer flying in all directions.

description: The destruction of the headless monster
sn: शब्दं च घोरं सत्त्वानां दावाग्नेरिव वर्धतः। अपश्येतां मुहूर्ताच्च कबधं घोरदर्शनम्॥
en: And they heard a terrible uproar of various creatures like that which is heard during a forest-fire spreading far and wide. In a moment they saw headless trunk of terrible appearance,

description: The destruction of the headless monster
sn: मेघपर्वतसंकाशं शालस्कन्धं महाभुजम्। उरोगतविशालाक्षं महोदरमहामुखम्॥
en: Dark as clouds and huge as a rock, with shoulders broad as a Shala tree, of gigantic arms, having large eyes on his breast and a large mouth situated on his capacious belly.

description: The destruction of the headless monster
sn: यदृच्छयाथ तद् रक्षः करे जग्राह लक्ष्मणम्। विषादमगमत् सद्यः सौमित्रिरथ भारत॥
en: And that Rakshasa with great ease seized Lakshmana by the hand. (Thus overpowered), O Bharata, Lakshmana was instantaneously seized with dismay.

description: The destruction of the headless monster
sn: स राममभिसम्प्रेक्ष्य कृष्यते येन तन्मुखम्। विषण्णश्चाब्रवीद् रामं पश्यावस्थामिमां मम॥
en: He, (the monster), then turning his eyes towards Rama, began to draw Lakshmana (forcibly) towards that portion of his body where his mouth was situated. And Lakshmana afflicted with grief said to Rama “look at my (sad) plight.

description: The destruction of the headless monster
sn: हरणं चैव वैदेह्या मम चायमुपप्लवः। राज्यभ्रंशश्च भवतस्तातस्य मरणं तथा॥
en: Your exile from the kingdom, the death of our father, the loss of the princess of Videha and (lastly) this my dangerous condition have quite overpowered me.

description: The destruction of the headless monster
sn: नाहं त्वां सह वैदेह्या समेतं कोसलागतम्। द्रक्ष्यामि पृथिवीराज्ये पितृपैतामहे स्थितम्॥
en: Alas, I shall never behold your return to Kausala with Vaidehi and your installation in the kingdom of our sire and grandsire as the ruler of the entire earth.

description: The destruction of the headless monster
sn: द्रक्ष्यन्त्यार्यस्य धन्या ये कुशलाजशमीदलैः। अभिषिक्तस्य वदनं सोमं शान्तघनं यथा।॥
en: Blessed indeed are they who will behold your face, resplendent as the moon emerged from the clouds and bathed in the coronation water sanctified with Kusha, fried paddy and black pease."

description: The destruction of the headless monster
sn: एवं बहुविधं धीमान् विललाप स लक्ष्मणः। तमुवाचाथ काकुत्स्थः सम्भ्रमेष्वप्यसम्भ्रमः॥
en: In this strain the intelligent Lakshmana gave vent to his lamentations profusely. Then, the descendant of Kakustha, dauntless even in the very face of danger, thus spoke to him.

description: The destruction of the headless monster
sn: मा विषीद नरव्याघ्र नैष कश्चिन्मयि स्थिते। छिन्थ्यस्य दक्षिणं बाहुं छिन्नः सव्यो मया भुजः॥
en: "O bravest of men, do not give way to sorrow. This (monster) can do you nothing when I am present. Cut off his right hand with sword and I shall hack his left."

description: The destruction of the headless monster
sn: इत्येवं वदता तस्य भुजो रामेण पातितः खड्नेन भृशतीक्ष्णेन निकृत्तस्तिलकाण्डवत्॥
en: While thus speaking Rama cut off his (left) hand with a sharp sword (as easily) as if it were a stalk of tila corn.

description: The destruction of the headless monster
sn: ततोऽस्य दक्षिणं बाहुं खङ्गेनाजनिवान् बली। सौमित्रिरपि सम्प्रेक्ष्य भ्रातरं राघवं स्थितम्॥
en: The heroic son of Sumitra, seeing Raghava stand by him, hacked his right hand with his sword.

description: The destruction of the headless monster
sn: पुनर्जघान पार्श्वे वै तद् रक्षो लक्ष्मणो भृशम्। गतासुरपतद् भूमौ कबन्धः सुमहांस्ततः॥
en: Then Lakshmana again and again smote him in his sides and the huge headless monster fell dead on the ground.

description: The destruction of the headless monster
sn: तस्य देहाद् विनिःसृत्य पुरुषो दिव्यदर्शनः। ददृशे दिवमास्थाय दिवि सूर्य इव ज्वलन्॥
en: Then a being of celestials appearance issued out of his body and stationing himself in the air appeared as resplendent as the sun in the heavens.

description: The destruction of the headless monster
sn: पप्रच्छ रामस्तं वाग्मी कस्त्वं प्रब्रूहि पृच्छतः। कामया किमिदं चित्रमाश्चर्यं प्रतिभाति मे॥
en: Then the eloquent Rama asked him "tell me who you are. How did such a thing come about? All this appears to me highly marvellous.”

description: The destruction of the headless monster
sn: तस्याचचक्षे गन्धर्वो विश्वावसुरहं नृप। प्राप्तो ब्राह्मणशापेन योनि राक्षससेविताम्॥
en: To him that being replied “O king I am the Gandharva Vishvavasu. I had to assume the shape of a Rakshasa owing to an imprecation of a Brahmana.

description: The destruction of the headless monster
sn: रावणेन हृता सीता राज्ञा लङ्काधिवासिना। सुग्रीवमभिगच्छस्व स ते साह्यं करिष्यति॥
en: Sita has been abducted by Ravana who lives in Lanka. Go to Sugriva who will help you (to recover her).

description: The destruction of the headless monster
sn: एषा पम्पा शिवजला हंसकारण्डवायुता। ऋष्यमूकस्य शैलस्य संनिकर्षे तटाकिनी॥
en: In the vicinity of the (mountain) Rishyamukha there is a lake named Pampa of auspicious waters, teeming with swans and crames.

description: The destruction of the headless monster
sn: वसते तत्र सुग्रीवश्चतुर्भिः सचिवैः सह। भ्राता वानरराजस्य वालिनो हेममालिनः॥
en: There, adorned with a golden garland dwells Sugriva, the brother of Bali, the king of monkeys, with four counsellors.

description: The destruction of the headless monster
sn: तेन त्वं सह संगम्य दुःखमूलं निवेदय। समानशीलो भवतः साहाय्यं स करिष्यति॥
en: Do you go to him and inform him of the cause of your sorrow. Being in the same predicament as you are, he will help you.

description: The destruction of the headless monster
sn: एतावच्छक्यमस्माभिर्वक्तुं द्रष्टासि जानकीम्। ध्रुवं वानरराजस्य विदितो रावणालयः॥
en: Thus far I am able to say that you the daughter of Janaka again. It is certain that the abode of Ravana is known to the monkeyking.

description: The destruction of the headless monster
sn: इत्युक्त्वान्तर्हितो दिव्यः पुरुषः सह महाप्रभः। विस्मयं जग्मतुश्चोभौ प्रवीरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ॥
en: will see Saying this that highly resplendent celestials being vanished and the highly-powerful Rama and Lakshmana both were struck with wonder.

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच ततोऽविदूरे नलिनी प्रभूतकमलोत्पलाम्। सीताहरणदुःखार्तः पम्पां रामः समासदत्॥
en: Markandeya said : Then, Rama, distracted with grief at the abduction of Sita, got to the Lake Pampa situated at a short distance and full of several kinds of lotuses.

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: मारुतेन सुशीतेन सुखेनामृतगन्धिना। सेव्यमानो वने तस्मिञ्जगाम मनसा प्रियाम्॥
en: In that forest fanned by cool and pleasant breezes charged with the ordour of ambrosia, the thoughts of his dear wife crept into the mind of Rama.

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: विललाप स राजेन्द्रस्तत्र कान्तामनुस्मरन्। कामबाणाभिसंतप्तः सौमित्रिस्तमथाब्रवीत्॥
en: O king of kings, smitten with Cupid's arrows by thinking of his beloved spouse he lamented (profusely). Then the son of Sumitra thus spoke to him.

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: न त्वामेवंविधो भावः स्प्रष्टुमर्हति मानद। आत्मवन्तमिव व्याधिः पुरुषं वृद्धशीलिनम्॥
en: “O respector of those that deserve honour, this state of your mind is as unworthy of you, as diseases in a self-contained old man of regular habits.

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: प्रवृत्तिरुपलब्धा ते वैदेह्या रावणस्य च। तां त्वं पुरुषकारेण बुद्ध्या चैवोपपादय॥
en: You have received intelligence concerning Ravana and the princess of Videha. (Now try to) liberate her by exertion and wisdom.

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: अभिगच्छाव सुग्रीवं शैलस्थं हरिपुङ्गवम्। मयि शिष्ये च भृत्ये च सहाये च समाश्वस॥
en: Let us go to Sugriva, the foremost of monkeys who dwells in (yonder) mountain. Cheer yourself up since I, your disciple servant and assistant, am near."

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: एवं बहुविधैर्वाक्यैर्लक्ष्मणेन स राघवः। उक्तः प्रकृतिमापेदे कार्ये चानन्तरोऽभवत्॥
en: By these and various other words of the same significance spoken by Lakshmana, the descendant of Raghu recovered his natural calmness and became mindful of his business.

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: निषेव्य वारि पम्पायास्तर्पयित्वा पितृनपि। प्रतस्थतुरुभौ वीरौ भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ॥
en: And both those heroic brothers Rama and Lakshmana bathing in the waters of the Pampa and offering oblations to their ancestors left (for Rishyamukha).

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: तावृष्यमूकमभ्येत्य बहुमूलफलद्रुमम्। गिर्यचे वानरान् पञ्च वीरौ ददृशतुस्तदा॥
en: Then, having reached the (mountain) Rishyamukha full of various roots, fruits and trees, those heroes saw at the summit of the mountain five monkeys.

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: सुग्रीवः प्रेषयामास सचिवं वानरं तयोः। बुद्धिमन्तं हनूमन्तं हिमवन्तमिव स्थितम्॥
en: Sugriva, (then), sent, his minister, the intelligent monkey Hanuman huge as mountain, to (receive them).

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: तेन सम्भाध्य पूर्वं तौ सुग्रीवमभिजग्मतुः। सख्यं वानरराजेन चक्रे रामस्तदा नृप॥
en: Having first conversed with him, they both came to Sugriva. O king, Rama then contracted a friendship with the monkey-king.

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: तद् वासो दर्शयामासुस्तस्य कार्ये निवेदिते। वानराणां तु यत् सीता ह्रियमाणा व्यपासृजत्॥
en: When Rama had unfolded his intentions to him, he (Sugriva) showed to him the piece of cloth dropped among the monkeys by Şita while being carried off (by Ravana).

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: तत् प्रत्ययकरं लस्वा सुग्रीवं प्लवगाधिपम्। पृथिव्यां वानरैश्वर्ये स्वयं रामोऽभ्यषेचयत्॥
en: Having obtained this token, Rama installed Sugriva the monkey-king, in sovereignty over all the monkeys on earth. a

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: प्रतिजज्ञे च काकुत्स्थः समरे वालिनो वधम्। सुग्रीवश्चापि वैदेह्याः पुनरानयनं नृप॥
en: (And) the descendant of Kakustha promised to kill Bali in battle; and O king, Sugriva also pledged himself to liberate Sita.

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: इत्युक्त्वा समयं कृत्वा विश्वास्य च परस्परम्। अभ्येत्य सर्वे किष्किन्धा तस्थुर्युद्धाभिकाक्षिणः।।१५।
en: Having come to this (mutual) understanding, reposing confidence in each other, they all arrived at Kishkindha and desirous of battle remained prepared (for counter with Bali).

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: सुग्रीवः प्राप्य किष्किन्धां ननादौघनिभस्वनः। नास्य तन्ममृषे वाली तारा तं प्रत्यषेधयत्॥
en: Having reached Kishkindha, Sugriva sent forth a yell like the roar of a torrent. Bali could not brook that; but Tara (his wife) stood in his way, saying

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: यथा नदति सुग्रीवो बलवानेष वानरः। मन्ये चाश्रयवान् प्राप्तो न त्वं निष्क्रान्तुमर्हसि॥
en: "From the manner in which this powerful monkey Sugriva is roaring, I think he has received assistance. (Therefore) do not go out."

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: हेममाली ततो वाली तारां ताराधिपाननाम्। प्रोवाच वचनं वाग्मी तां वानरपतिः पतिः॥
en: Thereupon, (her) husband, the eloquent Bali, the monkey-king who wore a golden garland replied to Tara endued with a face resplendent as the moon, the lord of the stars.

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: सर्वभूतरुतज्ञा त्वं पश्य बुद्ध्या समन्विता। केन चाश्रयवान् प्राप्तो ममैष भ्रातृगन्धिकः॥
en: “You are acquainted with the voice of all creatures; (therefore) by the exercise of your intelligence ascertain, whose assistance, this being who bears the relation of brother to me, has obtained.

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: चिन्तयित्वा मुहूर्तं तु तारा ताराधिप्रभा। पतिमित्यब्रवीत् प्राज्ञा शृणु सर्वं कपीश्वर।॥
en: The wise Tara, resplendent as the lord of the stars, reflecting a moment thus replied to her husband. “O lord of the monkeys, listen to all this.

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: हृतदारो महासत्त्वो रामो दशरथात्मजः। तुल्यारिमित्रतां प्राप्तः सुग्रीवेण धनुर्धरः॥
en: That bowman, Rama, the highly energetic son of Dasharatha, whose wife has been carried off (by Ravana) has formed an offensive and a defensive alliance with Sugriva.

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: भ्राता चास्य महाबाहुः सौमित्रिरपराजितः। लक्ष्मणो नाम मेधावी स्थितः कार्यार्थसिद्धये॥
en: His brother, the intellectual Lakshmana of mighty arms, the ever-victorious son of Sumitra, stands by him for the furtherance of Sugriva's aims.

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: मैन्दा द्विविदश्चापि हनूमांश्चानिलात्मजः। जाम्बवानृक्षराजश्च सुग्रीवसचिवाः स्थिताः॥
en: (Moreover), Mainda, Dvivida, Hanuman, the son of the wind god and Jambuvana, the king of the bears, all these counsellors of Sugriva stand up for him.

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: सर्व एते महात्मानो बुद्धिमन्तो महाबलाः। अलं तव विनाशाय रामवीर्यबलाश्रयात्॥
en: All these are endued with magnanimity, intellect and great strength; and being backed up by the strength of Rama are surely able to kill you."

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: तस्यास्तदाक्षिप्य वचो हितमुक्तं कपीश्वरः। पर्यशङ्कत तामीर्षुः सुग्रीवगतमानसाम्॥
en: (But) the lord of the monkeys, discarding her beneficial words, was filled with jealousy and suspected that her heart was inclined towards Sugriva.

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: तारां परुषमुक्त्वा तु निर्जगाम गुहामुखात्। स्थितं माल्यवतोऽभ्याशे सुग्रीवं सोऽभ्यभाषत॥
en: Having spoken harshly to Tara he (Bali) issued out of his cave and coming up to Sugriva who the Malyavan (mountain) addressed him thus,

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: असकृत् त्वं मया पूर्वं निर्जितो जीवितप्रियः। मुक्तो ज्ञातिरिति ज्ञात्वा का त्वरा मरणे पुनः॥
en: "You who are (very) fond of life, were equently defeated by me before; (but) considering the relationship you bear to me, I allowed you to escape (without taking your life).Then, why are you rushing into death so soon?" was near

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: इत्युक्तः प्राह सुग्रीवो भ्रातरं हेतुमद् वचः। प्राप्तकालममित्रघ्नो रामं सम्बोधयन्निव॥
en: Thus addressed (by Bali), Sugriva, the slayer of his foes, as if addressing Rama himself, spoke to his brother these significant words, (well) suited to the occasion.

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: हतराज्यस्य में राजन् हृतदारस्य च त्वया। किं मे जीवितसामर्थ्यमिति विद्धि समागतम्॥
en: "O monarch, deprived of my wife as well as of my kingdom by you, what need is there for my life? Know that it is for this (i.e. death) that I have sought you."

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: एवमुक्त्वा बहुविधं ततस्तौ संनिपेततुः। समरे वालिसुग्रीवौ शालतालशिलायुधौ।॥
en: Addressing each other in these and various other words in the same strain, both Bali and Sugriva were engaged in battle with Shalas, Talas and stones, which served the purpose of arrows.

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: उभौ जघ्नतुरन्योन्यमुभौ भूमौ निपेततुः। उभौ ववल्गतुश्चित्रं मुष्टिभिश्च निजघ्नतुः॥
en: Both smote each other and both struck down each other on the ground; both moved about with wonderful (dexterity) and both dealt blows (at each other).

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: उभौ रुधिरसंसिक्तौ नखदन्तपरिक्षतौ। शुशुभाते तदा वीरौ पुष्पिताविव किंशुकौ॥
en: Both those warriors torn with each others) nails and teeth were besmeared with blood and shone like two blooming Kinshuka flowers.

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: न विशेषस्तयोर्युद्धे यदा कश्चन् दृश्यते। सुग्रीवस्य तदा मालां हनुमान् कण्ठ आसजत्॥
en: (On account of their similarity appearance) no difference (in aspect) could be discovered between those fighters. Hanuman then placed a garland round the neck of Sugriva.

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: स मालया तदा वीरः शुशुभे कण्ठसक्तया। श्रीमानिव महाशैलो मलयो मेघमालया॥
en: Thereupon that hero adorned with that garland on his neck shone like the beautiful and mighty Malaya mountain encircled with the clouds. in

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: कृतचिह्नं तु सुग्रीवं रामो दृष्ट्वा महाधनुः। विचकर्ष धनुः श्रेष्ठं वालिमुद्दिश्य लक्ष्यवत्॥
en: Recognizing Sugriva by that mark, the mighty bowman Rama drew his excellent bow aiming at Bali as his mark.

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: विस्फारस्तस्य धनुषो यन्त्रस्येव तदा बभौ। वितत्रास तदा वाली शरेणाभिहतोरसि॥
en: The twang of his bow was like (the roar of) an engine. And pierced through the heart by the arrow Bali became alarmed.

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: स भिन्नहदयो वाली वक्राच्छोणितमुद्वमन्। ददर्शावस्थितं रामं ततः सौमित्रिणा सह॥
en: With his heart riven (by Rama's arrow) Bali began to vomit blood through his mouth and then he saw Rama standing (before him) together with the son of Sumitra.

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: गर्हयित्वा स काकुत्स्थं पपात भुवि मुर्छितः। तारा ददर्श तं भूमौ तारापतिसमौजसम्॥
en: Rebuking the descendant of Kakustha, (for taking his life without cause) he fell down senseless on the ground. Tara then beheld him (Bali) of moon-like splendour, lying (slain) on the earth.

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: हते वालिनि सुग्रीवः किष्किन्धा प्रत्यपद्यता तां च तारापतिमुखीं तारां निपतितेश्वराम्॥
en: Bali being thus slain, Sugriva obtained possession of Kishkindha and (the hand of) the widowed Tara also endued with a face lovely as the lord of the stars.

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: रामस्तु चतुरो मासान् पृष्ठे माल्यवत: शुभे। निवासमकरोद् धीमान् सुग्रीवेणाभ्युपस्थितः॥
en: And the intelligent Rama too, worshipped by Sugriva, in every way, lived on the auspicious plateau of the mountain Malyavan for four months.

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: रावणोऽपि पुरीं गत्वा लङ्कां कामबलात्कृतः। सीतां निवेशयामास भवने नन्दनोपमे॥
en: (On the other hand) the lustful Ravana too, having repaired to his capital Lanka, placed Sita in a retreat (beautiful) like the Nandana (gardens).

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: अशोकवनिकाभ्याशे तापसाश्रमसंनिभे। भर्तृस्मरणतन्वङ्गी तापसीवेषधारिणी॥
en: Situate within the Ashoka garden, resembling an asylum of ascetics. (And there) with her body reduced to a skeleton thinking of her husband and wearing the garb of ascetics.

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: उपवासतप:शीला तत्रास पृथुलेक्षणा। उवास दुःखवसतिं फलमूलकृताशना॥
en: And engaged in austerities and observing fasts, that large-eyed lady began to dwell sorrowfully subsisting on fruits and roots.

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: दिदेश राक्षसीस्तत्र रक्षणे राक्षसाधिपः। सासिलशूलपरशुमुद्गरालातधारिणीः॥
en: In order to guard her, the lord of the Rakshasas appointed Rakshasa women holding (in their hands) barbed darts, swords, maces, axes, clubs and flaming brands.

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: व्यक्षीं त्र्यक्षीं ललाटाक्षीं दीर्घजिह्वामजिबिकाम्। त्रिस्तनीमेकपादां च त्रिजटामेकलोचनाम्॥
en: And some (of them) had two and some three eyes, (some) had their eyes on the forehead, (some) were possessed of long tongues and some none, (some) had three breasts (some) one leg, (some) three braids of matted hair and (some) only one eye.

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: एताश्चान्याश्च दीप्ताक्ष्यः करभोत्कटमूर्द्धजाः। परिवार्यासते सीतां दिवारानमतन्द्रिताः॥
en: These and other (Rakshasas) females with flaming eyes and hair stiff as that of a camel, surrounded Sita very watchfully day and night.

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: तास्तु तामायतापाङ्गी पिशाच्यो दारुणस्वराः। तर्जयन्ति सदा रौद्राः परुषव्यञ्जनस्वराः॥
en: And those terrible-looking Pishachi women of dreadful voice always spoke that large-eyed lady in harsh words (such as),

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: खादाम पाटयामैनां तिलश: प्रविभज्य ताम्। येयं भर्तारमस्माकमवमन्येह जीवति॥
en: "Let us devour her; mangle her and tear her to pieces, who is living here despising our lord."

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: इत्येवं परिभर्त्सन्तीस्त्रास्यमाना पुनः पुनः। भर्तृशोकसमाविष्टा निःश्वस्येदमुवाच ताः॥
en: Thus repeatedly threatened and censured, Sita, afflicted with grief for her husband, replied to them with a deep sigh.

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: आर्याः खादत मां शीघ्रं न मे लोभोऽस्ति जीविते। विना तं पुण्डरीकाक्षं नीलकुञ्चितमूर्धजम्॥
en: "Worshipful ladies, eat me up soon. I have no need of life without the lotus-eyed (Rama) of curly and blue hair.

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: अप्येवाहं निराहारा जीवितप्रियवर्जिता। शोषयिष्यामि गात्राणि व्याली तालगता यथा॥
en: Separated from my beloved, so dear to my life I will rather live without food and waste away my frame like a she-serpent living near a Tala tree.

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: न त्वन्यमभिगच्छेयं पुमांसं राघवादृते। इति जानीत सत्यं मे क्रियतां यदनन्तरम्॥
en: Than live with any other person except the descendant of Raghu. Know this to be my firm resolve; and now do, whatever you like, with me.”

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: तस्यास्तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा राक्षस्यस्ताः खरस्वनाः। आख्यातुं राक्षसेन्द्राय जग्मुस्तत् सर्वमादृताः॥
en: The Rakshasa women, of harsh voice, hearing those words of hers, went to the king of the Rakshasas in order to tell him all that were spoken by her (Sita).

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: गतासु तासु सर्वासु त्रिजटा नाम राक्षसी। सान्त्वयामास वैदेहीं धर्मज्ञा प्रियवादिनी॥
en: They all having gone (to Ravana), a pious Rakshasa woman Trijata by name, who spoke sweet words, (thus) consoled the princess of Videha.

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: सीते वक्ष्यामि ते किंचिद् विश्वासं कुरु मे सखि। भयं त्वं त्यज वामोरु शृणु चेदं वचो मम॥
en: “Sita, I shall tell you something. O friend, believe me. O lady of fair hips, drive away your fears and hear these my words.

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: अविन्ध्यो नाम मेधावी वृद्धो राक्षसपुङ्गवः। स रामस्य हितान्वेषी त्वदर्थे हि स मावदत्॥
en: There is an old and intelligent Rakshasas chief named Avindhya. He seeks Rama's welfare and for your sake has told me (these words).

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: सीता मद्वचनाद् वाच्या समाश्वास्य प्रसाद्य च। भर्ता ते कुशली रामो लक्ष्मणानुगतो बली॥
en: "Having reassured and consoled Sita, address her in these my words (that I tell you now), saying, your husband, the heroic Rama, followed by Lakshmana, is all right.

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: सख्यं वानरराजेन शक्रप्रतिमतेजसा। कृतवान् राघवः श्रीमांस्त्वदर्थे च समुद्यतः॥
en: The illustrious descendant of Raghu has contracted friendship with the king of the monkeys, as powerful as Shakra himself and is ready for your deliverance.

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: मा च तेऽस्तु भयं भीरु रावणाल्लोकगहितात्। नलकूबरशापेन रक्षिता ह्यसि नन्दिनि॥
en: O timid lady, you have no fear from Ravana who is cursed by all the world, (because) O daughter, you are protected by Nalakubera's imprecation.

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: शप्तो ह्येष पुरा पापो वधू रम्भां परामृशन्। न शक्नोत्यवशां नारीमुपैतुमजितेन्द्रियः॥
en: Formerly this sinful wretch was cursed for having committed rape on his (own) daughterin-law, Rambha. (Therefore) this lustful being is not capable of forcibly violating any woman.

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: क्षिप्रमेष्यति ते भर्ता सुग्रीवेणाभिरक्षितः। सौमित्रिसहितो धीमांस्त्वां चेतो मोक्षयिष्यति॥
en: Your intelligent husband accompanied by the son of Sumitra and protected by Sugriva will soon arrive (here) and deliver you hence.

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: स्वप्ना हि सुमहाघोरा दृष्टा मेऽनिष्टदर्शनाः। विनाशायास्य दुर्बुद्धेः पौलस्त्यकुलघातिनः॥
en: I have dreamed an awfully-terrible dream of evil omen, indicative of the destruction of this evil-minded destroyer of the race of Pulastya.

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: दारुणो ह्येष दुष्टात्मा क्षुद्रकर्मा निशाचरः। स्वभावाच्छीलदोषेण सर्वेषां भयवर्धनः॥
en: This night-ranger is terribly wicked-minded and is prone to mean deeds and on account of his innate bad nature he terrifies all (creatures).

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: स्पर्धते सर्वदेवैर्यः कालोपहतचेतनः। मया विनाशलिङ्गानि स्वप्ने दृष्टानि तस्य वै॥
en: He challenges all the gods having lost his sense through Fate. I have in my dream seen all the indications of his destruction.

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: तैलाभिषिक्तो विकचो मज्जन् पङ्के दशाननः। असकृत् खरयुक्ते तु रथे नृत्यन्निव स्थितः॥
en: (I have in my dream seen) the ten-headed monster dancing repeatedly in a car drawn by assess with his head shaven and his body saturated with oil and besmeared with mud.

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: कुम्भकर्णादयश्चेमे नग्नाः पतितमूर्धजाः। गच्छन्ति दक्षिणामाशां रक्तमाल्यानुलेपनाः॥
en: (I have also seen) Kumbhakarna and others stark naked, besmeared with blood and with their heads shaven, taking to the southern direction.

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: श्वेतातपत्रः सोष्णीषः शुक्लमाल्यानुलेपनः। श्वेतपर्वतमारूढ एक एव विभीषणः॥
en: I have beheld only Vibhishana with a white umbrella (over his head) and a turban and graced with white garlands and unguents ascending the mountain Shveta.

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: सचिवाश्चास्य चत्वारः शुक्लमाल्यानुलेपनाः। श्वेतपर्वतमारूढा मोक्ष्यन्तेऽस्मान्महाभयात्॥
en: And I saw his four counsellors adorned with white garlands and unguents on the mountain Shveta. These only will be saved from this terrible calamity.

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: रामस्यास्त्रेण पृथिवी परिक्षिप्ता ससागरा। यशसा पृथिवीं कृत्स्ना पूरयिष्यति ते पतिः॥
en: The earth with all its oceans will be covered with Rama's weapons, and your husband will fill the whole world with his renown.

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: अस्थिसंचयमारूढो भुञ्जानो मधुपायसम्। लक्ष्मणश्च मया दृष्टो दिधक्षुः सर्वतो दिशम्॥
en: I have (in my dream) beheld Lakshmana burning all the points (with his arrows) and eating rice mixed with honey and boiled with milk mounted on a heap of bones.

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: रुदती रुधिरार्द्राङ्गी व्याघ्रण परिरक्षिता। असकृत् त्वं मया दृष्टा गच्छन्ती दिशमुत्तराम्॥
en: And I have seen you also lamenting, covered all over with blood and protected by a tiger, repeatedly run towards the southern direction.

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: हर्षमेष्यसि वैदेहि क्षिप्रं भ; समन्विता। राघवेण सह भ्रात्रा सीते त्वमचिरादिव॥
en: O princess of Videha, O Sita, being reunited with your husband, the descendant of Raghu, followed by Lakshmana, you will soon experience happiness.”

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: इत्येतन्मृगशावाक्षी तच्छ्रुत्वा त्रिजटावचः। बभूवाशावती बाला पुनर्भर्तृसमागमे॥
en: And that damsel gifted with eyes beautiful as those of a fawn, hearing these words of Trijata became hopeful of her reunion with her husband.

description: The consolation offered to Sita by Trijata
sn: यावदभ्यागता रौद्राः पिशाच्यस्ताः सुदारुणाः। ददृशुस्तां त्रिजटया सहासीनां यथा पुरा॥
en: And when those terrible-looking and cruel Pishacha women returned, they saw Sita seated with Trijata as before.

description: The colloquy between Sita and Ravana
sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच ततस्तां भर्तृशोकार्ता दीनां मलिनवाससम्। मणिशेषाभ्यलङ्कारां रुदतीं च पतिव्रताम्॥ राक्षसीभिरुपास्यन्ती समासीनां शिलातले। रावणः कामबाणातॊ ददर्शोपससर्प च॥ देवदानवगन्धर्वयक्षकिम्पुरुषैर्युधि। अजितोऽशोकवनिकां ययौ कन्दर्पपीडितः॥
en: Markandeya said : Then, Ravana, smarting under the shafts of Cupid, saw Sita-afflicted with sorrow for her husband, melancholy, wearing an unclean garb, having a jewel only for her ornament, lamenting (profusely), devoted to her husband, waited upon by the Rakshasa females and seated on a stone and approached her and he, whom the gods, the demons, the Gandharvas, the Yakshas and the Kimpurushas could never conquer in battle, inflamed with lust, repaired to the Ashoka gardens.

description: The colloquy between Sita and Ravana
sn: दिव्याम्बरधरः श्रीमान् सुमृष्टमणिकुण्डलः। विचित्रमाल्यमुकुटो वसन्त इव मूर्तिमान्॥
en: Attired in a celestials garment, wearing a handsome appearance, adorned with jewelled ear-rings, decked with a beautiful garland and a crown and looking as (handsome as) the very embodiment of Spring.

description: The colloquy between Sita and Ravana
sn: न कल्पवृक्षसदृशो यत्नादपि विभूषितः। श्मशानचैत्यगुमवद् भूषितोऽपि भयंकरः॥
en: Being dressed carefully he looked as (beautiful as) the Kalpa tree. But with all his rich dress he appeared as terrible as a banian tree in the midst of a cremation ground.

description: The colloquy between Sita and Ravana
sn: स तस्यास्तनुमध्यायाः समीपे रजनीचरः। ददृशे रोहिणीमेत्य शनैश्चर इव ग्रहः॥
en: That night-ranger, approaching the slenderwaisted lady, looked like (the grim) planet Saturn before (the beautiful) Rohini.

description: The colloquy between Sita and Ravana
sn: स तामामन्त्र्य सुश्रोणी पुष्पकेतुशराहतः। इदमित्यब्रवीद् वाक्यं त्रस्तां रोहीमिवाबलाम्॥
en: Having greeted that lady of beautiful hips, terrified like a helpless doe, he (Ravana) smarting under the shafts of that god having the flower for his emblem, addressed her thus,

description: The colloquy between Sita and Ravana
sn: सीते पर्याप्तमेतावत् कृतो भर्तुरनुग्रहः। प्रसादं कुरु तन्वङ्गि क्रियतां परिकर्म ते॥
en: "Sita, you have favoured too much your husband up to this time. O lady of slender form, be now favourably disposed towards me. Let your person be well-dressed.

description: The colloquy between Sita and Ravana
sn: भजस्व मां वरारोहे महार्हाभरणाम्बरा। भव मे सर्वनारीणामुत्तमा वरवर्णिनी॥
en: O excellent lady, live under my protection and O fair, complexioned damsel, adorned with rich ornaments and dresses be the first lady among all the females (of my harem).

description: The colloquy between Sita and Ravana
sn: सन्ति मे देवकन्याश्च गन्धर्वाणां च योषितः। सन्ति दानवकन्याश्च दैत्यानां चापि योषितः॥
en: Many daughters of the celestials and the Gandharvas are in my household and I possess several daughters of the Danavas and the Daityas.

description: The colloquy between Sita and Ravana
sn: चतुर्दश पिशाचानां कोट्यो मे वचने स्थिताः। द्विस्तावत् पुरुषादानां रक्षसां भीमकर्मणाम्॥
en: as One hundred and forty millions Pishachas, twice many man-eating Rakshasas of terrible deed execute my commands.

description: The colloquy between Sita and Ravana
sn: ततो मे त्रिगुणा यक्षा ये मद्वचनकारिणः। केचिदेव धनाध्यक्षं भ्रातरं मे समाश्रिताः॥
en: And thrice as many Yakshas carry out my orders. Some only are under the sway of my brother (Kubera) the lord of wealth.

description: The colloquy between Sita and Ravana
sn: गन्धर्वाप्सरसो भद्रे मामापानगतं सदा। उपतिष्ठन्ति वामोरु यथैव भ्रातरं मम॥
en: O gentle lady gifted with fair thighs, the Gandharvas and the Apsaras attend upon me in my drinking hall as they do my brother.

description: The colloquy between Sita and Ravana
sn: पुत्रोऽहमपि विप्रर्षेः साक्षाद् विश्रवसो मुनेः। पञ्चमो लोकपालानामिति मे प्रथितं यशः॥
en: (Again) I am the son to that Brahmanic sage, the Muni Vishrava and am celebrated under the name of the fifth Lokapala (regent of the universe).

description: The colloquy between Sita and Ravana
sn: दिव्यानि भक्ष्यभोज्यानि पानानि विविधानि च। यथैव त्रिदशेशस्य तथैव मम भाविनि॥
