en: O lady, I have as plenty of eatables, foods and drinks as the lord of the celestials himself.

description: The colloquy between Sita and Ravana
sn: क्षीयतां दुष्कृतं कर्म वनवासकृतं तव। भार्या मे भव सुश्रोणि यथा मन्दोदरी तथा॥
en: Let all your troubles of a forest life be over. O fair-hipped damsel, be my consort as Mandodari herself.

description: The colloquy between Sita and Ravana
sn: इत्युक्ता तेन वैदेही परिवृत्य शुभानना। तृणमन्तरतः कृत्वा तमुवाच निशाचरम्॥
en: Thus spoken to, the princes of Videha endued with a beautiful face, turning away (from Ravana) and considering him as something more insignificant than a straw thus replied to him.

description: The colloquy between Sita and Ravana
sn: अशिवेनातिवामोरूरजलं नेत्रवारिणा। स्तनावपतितौ बाला संहतावभिवर्षती॥ उवाच वाक्यं तं क्षुद्रं वैदेही पतिदेवता। असकृद् वदतो वाक्यमीदृशं राक्षसेश्वर॥ विषादयुक्तमेतत् ते मया श्रुतमभाग्यया। तद् भद्रसुख भद्रं ते मानसं विनिवर्त्यताम्॥
en: And that fair-hipped lady, the princess of Videha to whom her husband was as her god, drenching her solid breasts with copious flow of inauspicious tears which she incessantly shed, spoke these words to that mean wretch. “O lord of the Rakshasas, unfortunate as I am, I have been compelled to listen to such painful words repeatedly uttered by you. May you be blessed, you who take so much delight in sensual pleasure. Withdraw your mind (from me).

description: The colloquy between Sita and Ravana
sn: परदारासयलभ्या च सततं च पतिव्रता। न चैवोपयिकी भार्या मानुषी कृपणा तव॥
en: Being the wife of another and always attached to my husband I am not to be won over (by you). And this helpless woman cannot be a suitable wife to you.

description: The colloquy between Sita and Ravana
sn: विवशां धर्षयित्वा च कां त्वं प्रीतिमवाप्स्यसि। प्रजापतिसमो विप्रो ब्रह्मयोनिः पिता तव॥
en: What pleasure will you derive from violating an unwilling woman? Your father is equal to the lord of (all) creatures, a Brahmana and begotten of Brahma.

description: The colloquy between Sita and Ravana
sn: न च पालयसे धर्मं लोकपालसमः कथम्। भ्रातरं राजराजानं महेश्वरसखं प्रभुम्॥ धनेश्वरं व्यपदिशन् कथं त्विह न लज्जसे।
en: Being equal to a Lokapala why have you no regard for virtue! Dishonouring that king, your adorable brother, the lord of wealth and friend of Maheshvara how it is that you do not feel shame"?

description: The colloquy between Sita and Ravana
sn: इत्युक्त्वा प्रारुदत् सीता कम्पयन्ती पयोधरौ॥ शिरोधरां च तन्वङ्गी मुखं प्रच्छाद्य वाससा।
en: Saying (all) this, that lady of delicate limbs Sita, with her breasts and neck trembling (in emotion) and covering her face with her clothes, began to weep profusely.

description: The colloquy between Sita and Ravana
sn: तस्या रुदत्या भाविन्या दीर्धा वेणी सुसंयता॥ ददृशे स्वसिता स्रिग्धा काली व्यालीव मूर्धनि।
en: And while that fair lady was weeping, her long, well-woven, black and glossy, braid hanging down from her head looked like a black snake.

description: The colloquy between Sita and Ravana
sn: श्रुत्वा तद् रावणो वाक्यं सीतयोक्तं सुनिष्ठुरम्॥ प्रत्याख्यातोऽपि दुर्मेधाः पुनरेवाब्रवीद् वचः। काममङ्गानि मे सीते दुनोतु मकरध्वजः॥ न त्वामकामां सुश्रोणी समेष्ये चारुहासिनीम्।
en: Hearing those cruel words spoken by Sita, Ravana, of malicious intelligence, although thus rejected (by Sita) spoke to her these words again. "O Sita, let that god having the Makara for his emblem consume me. But O fair-hipped lady of sweet smiles, I will, by no means enjoy you against your will.

description: The colloquy between Sita and Ravana
sn: किं नु शक्यं मया कर्तुं यत् त्वमद्यापि मानुषम्॥ आहारभूतमस्माकं राममेवानुरुध्यसे॥
en: What am I able to do since you even to this day cherish Rama, who is but a man (and therefore) our food"

description: The colloquy between Sita and Ravana
sn: इत्युक्त्वा तामनिन्द्यागी स राक्षसमहेश्वरः। तत्रैवान्तर्हितो भूत्वा जगामाभिमतां दिशम्॥
en: Thus addressing that lady of faultless proportions, the lord of the Rakshasas vanished at that very spot and went whether he liked.

description: The colloquy between Sita and Ravana
sn: राक्षसीभिः परिवृता वैदेही शोककर्शिता। सेव्यमाना त्रिजटया तत्रैव न्यवसत् तदा।॥
en: And the princess of Videha weighed down with grief continued to dwell there, surrounded by Rakshasa women and kindly treated by Trijata.

sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच राघवः सहसौमित्रिः सुग्रीवेणाभिपालितः। वसन् माल्यवतः पृष्ठे ददृशे विमलं नभः॥
en: Markandeya said: (On the other hand) while the descendant of Raghu together with Lakshmana, properly served by Sugriva, was dwelling on the plateau of the Malyavana mountain, he cast his eyes (one night) on the azure firmament.

sn: स दृष्ट्वा विमले व्योम्नि निर्मलं शशलक्षणम्। ग्रहनक्षत्रताराभिरनुयातममित्रहा॥ कुमुदोत्पलपद्मानां गन्धमादाय वायुना। महीधरस्थः शीतेन सहसा प्रतिबोधित: ॥
en: From that mountain beholding on the clear cloudless heavens, the resplendent moon surrounded by planets, stars and constellations and (fanned) by a cool breeze laden with the fragrance of lilies, lotuses and other flowers of the same kind, that destroyer of foes was suddenly awakened (to a recollection of Sita).

sn: प्रभाते लक्ष्मणं वीरमभ्यभाषत दुर्मनाः। सीतां संस्मृत्य धर्मात्मा रुद्धां राक्षसवेश्मनि॥
en: Afflicted at the thoughts of Sita confined in the abode of the Rakshasha (Ravana), the virtuous (Rama) thus addressed the war-like Lakshmana in the (next) morning.

sn: गच्छ लक्ष्मण जानीहि किष्किन्धायां कपीश्वरम्। प्रमत्तं चाम्यधर्मेषु कृतघ्नं स्वार्थपण्डितम्॥
en: "O Lakshmana, do you repair to Kishkindha and there seek out the ungrateful, self-seeking and licentious lord of the monkeys.

sn: योऽसौ कुलाधमो मूढो मया राज्येऽभिषेचितः। सर्ववानरगोपुच्छा यमृक्षाश्च भजन्ति वै॥
en: That stupid wretch of his race whom I have installed on the throne (of Kishkindha) and to whom all the monkeys, apes and bears pay their homage,

sn: यदर्थं निहतो वाली मया रघुकुलोद्वह। त्वया सह महाबाहो किष्किन्धोपवने तदा॥
en: And for whose sake, O mighty-armed perpetuator of Raghu's race, I have, with your assistance slain Bali in the pleasure-gardens of Kishkindha.

sn: कृतघ्नं तमहं मन्ये वानरापसदं भुवि। यो मामेवंगतो मूढो न जानीतेऽद्य लक्ष्मण॥
en: I deem that worst of monkeys to be highly ungrateful on earth, because, O Lakshmana, that wretch has now forgotten me reduced to such a plight!

sn: असौ मन्ये न जानीते समयप्रतिपालनम्। कृतोपकारं मा नूनमवमन्याल्पया धिया।॥
en: I consider that, through scantiness of intellect, he does not care to fulfill his promise, disregarding me who have done him (such) a good turn.

sn: यदि तावदनुयुक्तः शेते कामसुखात्मकः। नेतव्यो वालिमार्गेण सर्वभूतगति त्वया।॥
en: If he indulges in sensual pleasures without making any exertions (for the discovery of Sita), you are to send him to the path of Bali, the common goal of all creatures.

sn: अथापि घटतेऽस्माकमर्थे वानरपुङ्गवः। तमादायैव काकुत्स्थ त्वरावान् भव मा चिरम्॥
en: But if that foremost of monkeys be devoted to our cause, then O descendant of Kakustha, bring him hither. Go soon and make no delay.”

sn: इत्युक्तो लक्ष्मणो भ्रात्रा गुरुवाक्यहिते रतः। प्रतस्थे रुचिरं गृह्य समार्गणगुणं धनुः॥
en: Lakshmana (ever) obedient to the behests and devoted to the welfare of his superiors, thus addressed by his brother, took his beautiful bow together with string and arrows and (soon) set out (for Kishkindha).

sn: किष्किन्धाद्वारमासाद्य प्रविवेशानिवारितः। सक्रोध इति तं मत्वा राजा प्रत्युद्ययौ हरिः॥
en: And reaching the gate of Kishkindha he entered (the city) unopposed. The monkey-king deeming him to be angry advanced (to meet him).

sn: तं सदारो विनीतात्मा सुग्रीवः प्लवगाधिपः। पूजया प्रतिजग्राह प्रीयमाणस्तदर्हया॥ तमब्रवीद् रामवचः सौमित्रिरकुतोभयः।
en: And with a humble mind, the monkey-king accompanied by his consort, welcomed him joyously and respectfully. (Then) the dauntless son of Sumitra made him acquainted with the words told by Rama.

sn: सर्वमशेषेण श्रुत्वा प्रह्वः कृताञ्जलिः॥ सभृत्यदारो राजेन्द्र सुग्रीवो वानराधिपः। इदमाह वचः प्रीतो लक्ष्मणं नरकुञ्जरम्॥
en: O king of kings, hearing all this in detail, Sugriva, the lord of the monkeys together with his consort and attendants joined his palms with humility and joyfully told Lakshmana, the most valiant of men, these words.

sn: स तत् नास्मि लक्ष्मण दुर्मेधा नाकृतज्ञो न निघृणः। श्रूयतां यः प्रयत्नो मे सीतापर्येषणे कृतः॥
en: "O Lakshmana, I am neither evil-minded nor ungrateful nor cruel. Listen, what pains I have taken in the direction of the discovery of Sita.

sn: दिशः प्रस्थापिताः सर्वे विनीता हरयो मया। सर्वेषां च कृतः कालो मासेनागमनं पुनः॥
en: I have sent (many) intelligent monkeys in all the directions and have appointed a month for the return of them all.

sn: वैरियं सवना साद्रिः सपुरा सागराम्बरा। विचेतव्या मही वीर सचमनगराकरा॥
en: O mighty hero, the entire earth with its forests, mountains, cities, seas, villages, towns and mines will be ransacked by them.

sn: स मासः पञ्चरात्रेण पूर्णो भवितुमर्हति। ततः श्रोष्यसि रामेण सहितः सुमहत् प्रियम्॥
en: That month will be complete in another five nights. And then you will, together with Rama, hear that great and joyful news about the discovery of Sita)."

sn: इत्युक्तो लक्ष्मणस्तेन वानरेन्द्रेण धीमता। त्यक्त्वा रोषमदीनात्मा सुग्रीवं प्रत्यपूजयत्॥
en: Thus addressed by the intelligent monkeyking, the magnanimous Lakshmana, giving up his anger, adored Sugriva.

sn: स रामं सहसुग्रीवो माल्यवत्पृष्ठमास्थितम्। अभिगम्योदयं तस्य कार्यस्य प्रत्यवेदयत्॥
en: Accompanied by Sugriva he then returned to Rama who was dwelling on the plateau of the mountain Malyavana and approaching him related the success of his mission,

sn: इत्येवं वानरेन्द्रास्ते समाजग्मुः सहस्रशः। दिशस्तिस्रो विचित्याथ न तु ये दक्षिणां गताः॥
en: Thousands of monkeys 3oon began to return after searching, the three quarters, excepting those who were sent towards the south.

sn: आचख्युस्तत्र रामाय महीं सागरमेखलाम्। विचितां न तु वैदेह्या दर्शनं रावणस्य वा॥
en: And they told Rama “Although we have searched the (entire) sea-girt earth, we have not found either the princess of Videha or Ravana.

sn: गतास्तु दक्षिणामाशां ये वै वानरपुङ्गवाः। आशावांस्तेषु काकुत्स्थः प्राणानार्तोऽभ्यधारयत्॥
en: And though sorely grieved (at this unpleasant news) the descendant of Kakustha dragged his existence hopeful of the success of those great monkeys who were despatched towards the south.

sn: द्विमासोपरमे काले व्यतीते प्लवगास्ततः। सुग्रीवमभिगम्येदं त्वरिता वाक्यमब्रुवन्॥
en: When two months had passed away, (some) monkeys hastily approaching Sugriva told him these words.

sn: रक्षितं वालिना यत् तत् स्फीतं मधुबनं महत्। त्वया च प्लवगश्रेष्ठ तद् भुङ्क्ते पवनात्मजः॥
en: "O chief of the monkeys, the great and extensive orchard, Madhuvana which was (so) carefully preserved by Bali and is well-guarded by you also, is being pillaged by the son of Pavana,

sn: वालिपुत्रोऽङ्गदश्चैव ये चान्ये प्लवगर्षभाः। विचेतुं दक्षिणामाशां राजन् प्रस्थापितास्त्वया॥
en: Angada, the son of Bali and other foremost of monkeys who, O monarch, were despatched by you to search the southern direction."

sn: तेषामपनयं श्रुत्वा मेने स कृतकृत्यताम्। कृतार्थानां हि भृत्यानामेतद् भवति चेष्टितम्॥
en: Hearing of this act of indulgence on their part, he (Sugriva) thought they successful, for such behaviour could be possible for those servants whose efforts were crowned with success.

sn: स तद् रामाय मेधावी शशंस प्लवगर्षभः। रामश्चाप्यनुमानेन मेने दृष्टां तु मैथिलीम्॥
en: Then that intellectual and foremost of monkeys informed Rama of this. And Rama too inferred (from the statement of Sugriva) that Sita must have been seen (by the monkeys).

sn: हनुमत्प्रमुखाश्चापि विश्रान्तास्ते प्लवङ्गमाः। अभिजग्मुर्हरीन्द्रं तं रामलक्ष्मणसंनिधौ॥
en: (Meanwhile) those monkeys with Hanuman at their head, having rested themselves, were approached the monkey-king who was with Rama and Lakshmana.

sn: गतिं च मुखवर्णं च दृष्ट्वा रामो हनूमतः। अगमत् प्रत्यय भूयो दृष्टा सीतेति भारत।॥
en: O Bharata, observing the gestures of Hanuman and the colour of his face, Rama became thoroughly convinced of the discovery of Sita.

sn: हनुमत्प्रमुखास्ते तु वानराः पूर्णमानसाः। प्रणेतुर्विधिवद् रामं सुग्रीवं लक्ष्मणं तथा॥
en: The monkeys, headed by Hanuman and successful in their mission, duly bowed down to Rama, Lakshmana and Sugriva.

sn: तानुवाचानतान् रामः प्रगृह्य सशरं धनुः। अपि मां जीवयिष्यध्वमपि वः कृतकृत्यता॥
en: (Then) Rama, holding (in his hand) his bow together with arrows, addressed those assembled (monkeys) thus, “Will you make me bear life? Have you been successful?

sn: अपि राज्यमयोध्यायां कारयिष्याम्यहं पुनः। निहत्य समरे शत्रूनाहत्य जनकात्मजाम्॥
en: Having killed my enemy in battle and delivered the daughter of Janaka, will you enable me to reign at Ayodhya?

sn: अमोक्षयित्वा वैदेहीमहत्वा च रणे रिपून्। हृतदारोऽवधूतश्च नाहं जीवितुमुत्सहे॥
en: Deprived of my wife and honour, I do not wish to live so long as the princess of Videha is not rescued and my enemies are not slain."

sn: इत्युक्तवचनं रामं प्रत्युवाचानिलात्मजः। प्रियमाख्यामि ते राम दृष्टा सा जानकी मया॥
en: Rama having said this, Hanuman the son of the wind-god thus replied to him. “O Rama, I am giving you good news. The daughter of Janaka has been seen by me.

sn: विचित्य दक्षिणामाशां सपर्वतवनाकराम्। श्रान्ताः काले व्यतीते स्म दृष्टवन्तो महागुहाम्॥
en: Searching the southern direction with all its mountains, forests and mines, we got fatigued and then after the expiration of the appointed time we saw a great cave.

sn: प्रविशामो वयं तां तु बहुयोजनमायताम्। सान्धकारां सुविपिनां गहनां कीटसेविताम्॥
en: We then entered it (the cave) extending over many a yojana, dark, woody, deep and infested by insects.

sn: गत्वा सुमहदध्वानमादित्यस्य प्रभां ततः। दृष्टवन्तः स्म तत्रैव भवनं दिव्यमन्तरा॥
en: Having traversed a great way through it, we saw the splendour of the sun and a beautiful palace within it.

sn: मयस्य किल दैत्यस्य तदासीद् वेश्म राघव। तत्र प्रभावती नाम तपोऽतप्यत तापसी॥
en: O scion of Raghu's race, that palace belonged to the Daitya Maya. There a female ascetic Prabhavati by name, was engaged in austerities.

sn: तया दत्तानि भोज्यानि पानानि विविधानि च। भुक्त्वा लब्धबलाः सन्तस्तयोक्तेन पथा ततः॥
en: She gave us many sorts of eatables and drinkable. Regaining our strength after partaking of food, we proceeded along the route indicated by her.

sn: निर्याय तस्मादुद्देशात् पश्यामो लवणाम्भसः। समीपे सह्यमलयौ दर्दुरं च महागिरिम्॥
en: And issuing out of the cave (we) beheld near the briny ocean the Sahya, the Malaya and the mighty Dardura mountains.

sn: ततो मलयमारुह्य पश्यन्तो वरुणालयम्। विषण्णा व्यथिताः खिन्ना निराशा निराशा जीविते भृशम्॥
en: Then ascending the Malaya mountain (when) we beheld the abode of Varuna (i.e. the ocean-god), we became sorely grieved, afflicted and dejected and gave up all hopes of life.

sn: अनेकशतविस्तीर्णं योजनानां महोदधिम्। निमिनक्रझपा ।सं चिन्तयन्तः सुदुःखिताः॥
en: Considering that this mighty ocean was many hundred yojanas in width and the abode of whales, alligators and fishes, we became sorely grieved.

sn: तत्रानशनसंकल्पं कृत्वाऽऽसीना वयं तदा। ततः कथान्ते गृध्रस्य जटायोरभवत् कथा॥
en: Then we sat down resolving to die of starvation. Then in the course of our conversation, we happened to talk of the vulture Jatayu.

sn: ततः पर्वतशृङ्गाभं घोररूपं भयावहम्। पक्षिणं दृष्टवन्तः स्म वैनतेयमिवापरम्॥
en: Then we beheld an awe-inspiring and a terrible-looking bird huge as mountain-peak and looking like another son of Vinata (Garuda).

sn: सोऽस्मानतळयद् भोक्तुमथाभ्येत्य वचोऽब्रवीत्। भोः क एष मम भ्रातुर्जटायोः कुरुते कथाम्॥
en: And desirous of devouring us, he approached us and spoke these words “who is it that is speaking of my brother Jatayu?

sn: सम्पातिर्नाम तस्याहं ज्येष्ठो भ्राता खगाधिपः। अन्योन्यस्पर्धयारूढावावामादित्यसत्पदम्॥
en: I am his elder brother Sampati by name and the lord of birds. Once desirous of competing with each other we soared toward the sun.

sn: ततो दग्धाविमौ पक्षौ न दग्धौ तु जटायुषः। तदा मे चिरदृष्टः स भ्राता गृध्रपतिः प्रियः॥ निर्दग्धपक्षः पतितो ह्यहमस्मिन् महागिरौ।
en: In consequence of which my wings were burnt but those of Jatayu were not. That was the last time when I saw my dear brother, the king of the vultures. My wings being burnt I fell down and have been since lying on this mighty mountain."

sn: तस्यैवं वदतोऽस्माभिर्हतो भ्राता निवेदितः॥ व्यसनं भवतश्चेदं संक्षेपाद् वै निवेदितम्।
en: He, having said this, we told him of the death of his brother. And we informed him briefly of your calamity.

sn: स सम्पातिस्तदा राजञ्छ्रुत्वा सुमहदप्रियम्॥ विषण्णचेताः पप्रच्छ पुनरस्मानरिंदम। कः स रामः कथं सीता जटायुश्च कथं हतः॥ इच्छामि सर्वमेवैतच्छ्रोतुं प्लवगसत्तमाः।
en: Hearing this very disagreeable news, O king, Sampati, became dejected at heart and O tormentor of foes again asked “who is this Rama? Why was Sita abducted? And how was Jatayu slain? O best of monkeys, I am desirous of hearing all this."

sn: तस्याहं सर्वमेवैतद् भवतो व्यसनागमम्॥ प्रायोपवेशने चैव हेतुं विस्तरशोऽब्रुवम्।
en: I then fully informed him of the calamity that has befallen your worshipful self and of the cause of our resolve to die of starvation.

sn: सोऽस्मानुत्थापयामास वाक्येनानेन पक्षिराट्॥ रावणो विदितो मह्यं लङ्का चास्य महापुरी। दृष्टा पारे समुद्रस्य त्रिकूटगिरिकन्दरे॥ भवित्री तत्र वैदेही न मेऽस्त्यत्र विचारणा।
en: But that monarch of birds stirred us up with these words. Ravana is indeed known to me. His mighty capital, Lanka, can be seen across the sea (situate) in a valley of the Trikuta mountains. The princess of Videha must be there. I have no doubt on this point.

sn: इति तस्य वचः श्रुत्वा वयमुत्थाय सत्वराः॥ सागरक्रमणे मन्त्रं मन्त्रयामः परंतप।
en: Hearing him thus speak, we got up soon and O tormentor of foes, held a consultation together as to how to cross the sea;

sn: नाध्यवास्यद् यदा कश्चित् सागरस्य विलङ्घनम्॥ ततः पितरमाविश्य पुप्लवेऽहं महार्णवम्। शतयोजनविस्तीर्णं निहत्य जलराक्षसीम्॥
en: But none had courage enough to attempt it. Then inspired with the energy of my father, whom I invoked, I crossed the vast ocean, a thousand yojanas wide, after having killed a Rakshasa woman (on my way) who lived in the waters.

sn: तत्र सीता मया दृष्टा रावणान्तःपुरे सती। उपवासतप:शीला भर्तृदर्शनलालसा॥
en: I (then) discovered the chaste Sita in the । Ravana's household observing austerities and fasts, eager to behold her husband,

sn: जटिला मलदिग्धाङ्गी कृशा दीना तपस्विनी। निमित्तैस्तामहं सीतामुपलभ्य पृथग्विधैः॥
en: With clotted hair, covered with dirt, melancholy, lean and lank and devoted to asceticism. Knowing her to be Sita by these unusual signs,

sn: उपसृत्याब्रुवं चार्यामभिगम्य रहोगताम्। सीते रामस्य दूतोऽहं वानरो मारुतात्मजः॥
en: I approached her and bowing down to that worshipful lady who was alone, said “Sita, I am Ram's messenger, a monkey and the son of Pavana (the wind-god).

sn: त्वदर्शनमभिप्रेप्सुरिह प्राप्तो विहायसा। राजपुत्रौ कुशलिनौ भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ॥
en: Desirous of seeing you, I have come here ranging through the firmament. Those princes, the brothers Rama and Lakshmana are all right,

sn: सर्वशाखामृगेन्द्रेण सुग्रीवेणाभिपालितौ। कुशलं त्वाब्रवीद् रामः सीते सौमित्रिणा सह॥
en: Being well cared for by Sugriva and the monkeys. O Sita, both Rama and the son of Sumitra have enquired of your welfare.

sn: सखिभावाच्च सुग्रीवः कुशलं त्वानुपृच्छति। क्षिप्रमेष्यति ते भर्ता सर्वशाखामृगैः सह॥ प्रत्ययं कुरु मे देवि वानरोऽस्मि न राक्षसः।
en: And Sugriva too being a friend (of them) has enquired of your welfare. Your husband will soon arrive (here) accompanied by all the monkeys. O divine lady, believe in me. I am a monkey and not a Rakshasa.

sn: मुहूर्तमिव च ध्यात्वा सीता मां प्रत्युवाच ह॥ अवैमि त्वां हनूमन्तमविन्ध्यवचनादहम्। अविन्ध्यो हि महाबाहो राक्षसो वृद्धसम्मतः॥
en: Reflecting a moment on what I said, Sita replied to me, “From what has been said by Avindhya I know you to be Hanuman. O (monkey) of mighty arms, Avindhya is an old and a revered Rakshasa.

sn: कथितस्तेन सुग्रीवस्त्वद्विधैः सचिवैर्वृतः। गम्यतामिति चोक्त्वा मां सीता प्रादादिमं मणिम्॥ धारिता येन वैदेही कालमेतमनिन्दिता। प्रत्ययार्थं कथां चेमां कथयामास जानकी॥
en: He told me “Sugriva is surrounded by such advisers as you" Then asking me to go away Sita gave me this jewel (as a token), which enabled the faultless princess of Videha to bear life so long. And the daughter of Janaka further told me these words as a credential.

sn: क्षिप्तामिषीका काकाय चित्रकूटे महागिरौ। भवता पुरुषव्याघ्र प्रत्यभिज्ञानकारणात्॥
en: (Namely) that while dwelling in the mighty mountain Chitrakuta, O most valiant of meen, you shot a straw at a crow.

sn: ग्राहयित्वाहमात्मानं ततो दग्ध्वा च तां पुरीम्। सम्प्राप्त इति तं रामः प्रियवादिनमार्चयत्॥
en: Then suffering myself to be seized (by the guards) and setting fire to that city (Lanka) I have come back" (Hearing these words) Rama adored that being who spoke agreeable words.

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The construction of the bridge (across the sea
sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच ततस्तत्रैव रामस्य समासीनस्य तैः सह। समाजग्मुः कपिश्रेष्ठाः सुग्रीववचनात् तदा।॥
en: Markandeya said : Then while Rama was seated at that very place with them (the monkeys), the monkeychiefs, at the command of Sugriva, began to assemble there.

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The construction of the bridge (across the sea
sn: वृतः कोटिसहस्रेण वानराणां तरस्विनाम्। श्वशुरो वालिनः श्रीमान् सुषेणो राममभ्ययात्॥
en: Surrounded by ten billions of powerful monkeys the illustrious father-in-law of Bali, Sushena, came to Rama.

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The construction of the bridge (across the sea
sn: कोटीशतवृतो वापि गजो गवय एव च। वानरेन्द्रौ महावी? पृथक् पृथगदृश्यताम्॥
en: Those two foremost of monkeys, the highlypowerful Gaja and Gavaya, each surrounded by billion (monkeys) made their appearance.

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The construction of the bridge (across the sea
sn: षष्टिकोटिसहरू णि प्रकर्षन् प्रत्यदृश्यत। गोलाङ्गलो महाराज गवाक्षो भीमदर्शनः॥
en: O mighty monarch, the terrible-looking Gavakshya having the tail of a cow, came thither, after having collected six hundred billions (of monkeys). one

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The construction of the bridge (across the sea
sn: गन्धमादनवासी तु प्रथितो गन्धमादनः। कोटीशतसहस्राणि हरीणां समकर्षत॥
en: The celebrated Gandhamadana, the dweller of the mountain Gandhamadana, gathered a hundred thousand crores of monkeys.

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The construction of the bridge (across the sea
sn: पनसो नाम मेधावी वानरः सुमहाबलः। कोटीर्दश द्वादश च त्रिंशत् पञ्च प्रकर्षति॥
en: The intelligent monkey, Panasa by name and endued with a vast strength collected together fifty two hundreds of millions (of monkeys).

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The construction of the bridge (across the sea
sn: श्रीमान् दधिमुखोनाम हरिवृद्धोऽतिवीर्यवान्। प्रचकर्ष महासैन्यं हरीणां भीमतेजसाम्॥
en: The highly-powerful and illustrious old monkey, Dadhimukha by name, gathered a great army of monkeys endued with terrible prowess.

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The construction of the bridge (across the sea
sn: कृष्णानां मुखपुण्ड्राणामृक्षाणां भीमकर्मणाम्। कोटीशतसहस्रेण जाम्बवान् प्रत्यदृष्यत॥
en: Jambuvana, accompanied by a hundred thousand crores of black bears of terrible deeds with the Tilaka mark on their faces, made his appearance there.

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The construction of the bridge (across the sea
sn: एते चान्ये च बहवो हरियूथपयूथपाः। असंख्येया महाराज समीयू रामकारणात्॥
en: O great king, these and countless other monkey-chiefs arrived thither for the sake of Rama.

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The construction of the bridge (across the sea
sn: गिरिकूटनिभाङ्गानां सिंहानामिव गर्जताम्। श्रूयते तुमुलः शब्दस्तत्र तत्र प्रधावताम्॥
en: A great tumultuous uproar was heard there caused by those monkeys running hither and thither, having bodies huge as mountain-peaks and roaring like lions.

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The construction of the bridge (across the sea
sn: गिरिकूटनिभाः केचित् केचिन्महिषसंनिभाः। शरदभ्रप्रतीकाशा: केचिद्धिङ्गलकाननाः॥
en: Some resembled mountain-peaks and some buffaloes, some looked like autumnal clouds and some had faces red as vermillion.

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The construction of the bridge (across the sea
sn: उत्पतन्तः पतन्तश्च प्लवमानाश्च वानराः। उद्धन्वन्तोऽपरे रेणून् समाजग्मुः समन्ततः॥
en: And as the monkeys flocked in from all sides, some fell down, some leaped about and some scattered the dust.

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The construction of the bridge (across the sea
sn: स वानरमहासैन्यः पूर्णसागरसंनिभः। निवेशमकरोत् तत्र सुग्रीवानुमते तदा॥
en: Then the mighty monkey-army, looking like a sea full of the brim, took up their quarters there at the command of Sugriva.

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The construction of the bridge (across the sea
sn: ततस्तेषु हरीन्द्रेषु समावृत्तेषु सर्वशः। तिथौ प्रशस्ते नक्षत्रे मुहूर्ते चाभिपूजिते॥ तेन व्यूढेन सैन्येन लोकानुद्वर्तयन्निव। प्रययौ राघवः श्रीमान् सुग्रीवसहितस्तदा॥
en: All the monkey-chiefs having assembled together from all directions, the illustrious descendant of Raghu's together with Sugriva and the (monkey) army drawn up in the battle array began his march (towards Lanka) at an auspicious moment of fair day and under a lucky constellation, as if desirous of destroying all the worlds.

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The construction of the bridge (across the sea
sn: मुखमासीत् तु सैन्यस्य हनूमान् मारुतात्मजः। जघनं पालयामास सौमित्रितरकुतोभयः॥
en: Hanuman, the son of Pavana marched in the van of the army while its rear was protected by the dauntless son of Sumitra.

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The construction of the bridge (across the sea
sn: बद्धगोधाङ्गुलित्राणौ राघवौ तत्र जग्मतुः। वृतौ हरिमहामात्रैश्चन्द्रसूर्यौ ग्रहैरिव॥
en: As they proceeded on, the two descendants of Raghu with their fingers encased in gloves of Godha's skin and surrounded by the monkey-chiefs shone like the sun or the moon (surrounded by) the planets.

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The construction of the bridge (across the sea
sn: प्रबभौ हरिसैन्यं तत् सालतालशिलायुधम्। सुमहच्छालिभवनं यता सूर्योदयं प्रति॥
en: That (vast) monkey-army holding (in their hands) Sala and Tala trees which served the purpose of arrows, looked like an extensive corn-field under the morning son.

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The construction of the bridge (across the sea
sn: नलनीलाङ्गदक्राथमैन्दद्विविदपालिता। ययौ सुमहती सेना राघवस्यार्थसिद्धये।॥
en: Protected by Nala, Nila, Angada, Kratha and Mainda that mighty host moved on for accomplishing the object of Rama.

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The construction of the bridge (across the sea
sn: विविधेषु प्रशस्तेषु बहुमूलफलेषु च। प्रभूतमधुमूलेषु वारिमत्सु शिवेषु च॥ निवसन्ती निराबाधा तथैव गिरिसानुषु। उपायाद्धरिसेना सा क्षारोदमथ सागरम्॥
en: And encamping unopposed on many extensive and auspicious tracts and valleys abounding with fruits, roots, water, honey and meat, that monkey-army at last came near the briny Sea.

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The construction of the bridge (across the sea
sn: द्वितीयसागरनिभं तद् बलं बहुलध्वजम्। वेलावनं समासाद्य निवासमकरोत् तदा॥
en: And that (vast) army which looked like a second ocean furnished with innumerable standards reached the shores of the sea) and encamped there.

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The construction of the bridge (across the sea
sn: ततो दाशरथिः श्रीमान् सुग्रीवं प्रत्यभाषत। मध्ये वानरमुख्यानां प्राप्तकालमिदं वचः॥
en: Then the renowned son of Dasharatha addressed Sugriva who was surrounded by monkey-chiefs these words appropriate to the occasion.

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The construction of the bridge (across the sea
sn: उपायः को नु भवतां मतः सागरलडने। इयं हि महती सेना सागरचातिदुस्तरः॥
en: “This army is vast and the ocean too is very difficult to cross. What steps, therefore, in your opinion, should be taken in order to cross it?

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The construction of the bridge (across the sea
sn: तत्रान्ये व्याहरन्ति स्म वानरा बहुमानिनः। समर्था लङ्घने सिन्धोर्न तु तत् कृत्स्नकारकम्॥
en: There at, very many self-conceited monkeys said "we are capable of crossing the sea.” But this could not serve the purpose fully (as all the monkeys were not able to cross the sea).

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The construction of the bridge (across the sea
sn: केचिन्नौभिर्व्यवस्यन्ति केचिच्च विविधैः प्लवैः। नेति रामस्तु तान् सर्वान् सान्त्वयन् प्रत्यभाषत॥
en: Some proposed to cross by boats and some by various kinds of rafters. But Rama, having consoled them all, said "This will not do.

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The construction of the bridge (across the sea
sn: शतयोजनविस्तारं न शक्ताः सर्ववानराः। क्रान्तुं तोयनिधिं वीरा नैषा वो नैष्ठिकी मतिः॥
en: O heroes, all the monkeys will not be able to cross the sea which is a hundred yojanas in width. Therefore, your proposal cannot be agreeable to reason.

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The construction of the bridge (across the sea
sn: नावो न सन्ति सेनाया बयस्तारयितुं तथा। वणिजामुपघातं च कथमस्मद्विधश्चरेत्॥
en: (Moreover), there are not plenty of boats of land our troops. Again (the interests of) trade should not suffer at the hands of men like us.

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The construction of the bridge (across the sea
sn: विस्तीर्णं चैव नः सैन्यं हन्याच्छिद्रेण वै परः। प्लवोडुपप्रतारश्च नैवात्र मम रोचते॥
en: Our army is vast. The enemy will the able to destroy it, if it can detect a (single) weak point in it. (Therefore) in my opinion it is not desirable to cross the sea by rafters and boats.

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The construction of the bridge (across the sea
sn: अहं त्विमं जलनिधि समारप्स्याम्युपायतः। प्रतिशेष्याम्युपवसन् दर्षयिष्यति मां ततः॥
en: I will, however, pray to this Lord of waters (to show me) a means (to cross the sea) and by observing fasts will lie down on the shores. He will then surely show me (a means).

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The construction of the bridge (across the sea
sn: न चेद् दर्शयिता मार्ग धक्ष्याम्येनमहं ततः। महास्त्रैरप्रतिहतैरत्यग्निपवनोज्ज्वलैः॥
en: If, however, he does not show me a way (to cross the ocean), I will burn him up with irresistible and mighty weapons surpassing fire itself in fury.”

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The construction of the bridge (across the sea
sn: इत्यक्तुवा सह सौमित्रिरुपस्पृश्याथ राघवः। प्रतिशिश्ये जलनिधिं विधिवत् कुशसंस्तरे॥
en: Saying this, the descendant of Raghu together with the son of Sumitra performed achamana (i.e. touched water thrice as a purifactory ceremony) and duly laid themselves down on a bed of Kusha grass on the sea-shore.

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The construction of the bridge (across the sea
sn: सागरस्तु ततः स्वप्ने दर्शयामास राघवम्। देवो नदनदीभर्ता श्रीमान् यादोगणैर्वृतः॥
en: Then that Lord of all the rivers, the ocean, surrounded by aquatic animals showed himself to the descendant of Raghu in a dream.

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The construction of the bridge (across the sea
sn: कौसल्यामातरित्येवमाभाष्य मधुरं वचः। इदमित्याह रत्नानामाकरैः शतशो वृतः॥
en: And addressing him in such sweet words as "O son of Kausalya," (the Ocean) surrounded by hundreds of mines of gems thus spoke to Rama).

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The construction of the bridge (across the sea
sn: ब्रूहि किं ते करोम्यत्र साहाय्यं पुरुषर्षभ। ऐक्ष्वाको ह्यस्मि ते ज्ञातिरिति रामस्तमब्रवीत्॥
en: "O most valiant of men, tell me what assistance I shall render to you. I belong to the race of Ikshvaku and can therefore claim kinship with you." Rama (then) replied to him.

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The construction of the bridge (across the sea
sn: मार्गमिच्छामि सैन्यस्य दत्तं नदनदीपते। येन गत्वा दशग्रीवं हन्यां पौलस्त्यपांसनम्॥
en: "O lord of all the rivers, I desire that you will grant, for my army, a way, marching through which I may kill the ten-headed wretch of Paulastya's race.

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The construction of the bridge (across the sea
sn: यद्येवं याचतो मार्ग न प्रदास्यति मे भवान्। शरैस्त्वां शोषयिष्यामि दिव्यास्त्रप्रतिमन्त्रितैः॥
en: If you do not grant the passage prayed for, I will dry you up with arrows inspired with mantras and shot from celestials weapons."

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The construction of the bridge (across the sea
sn: इत्येवं ब्रुवतः श्रुत्वा रामस्य वरुणालयः। उवाच व्यथितो वाक्यमिति बद्धाञ्जलिः स्थितः॥
en: Hearing Rama say so, the abode of Varuna (i.e. the Ocean) sorely grieved said these words with joined palms.

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The construction of the bridge (across the sea
sn: नेच्छामि प्रतिघातं ते नास्मि विघ्नकरस्तव। शृणु चेदं वचो राम श्रुत्वा कर्तव्यमाचर॥
en: "I am neither desirous of throwing any obstacles in your way nor am I inclined to your mischief. O Rama, hear these words and then do what is fit.

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The construction of the bridge (across the sea
sn: यदि दास्यामि ते मार्गं सैन्यस्य व्रजतोऽऽज्ञया। अन्ये व्याज्ञापयिष्यन्ति मामेवं धनुषो बलात्॥
en: If, at your command I grant you a passage for the transport of your troops, then others too, from the strength of their bows, will command me to do so.

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The construction of the bridge (across the sea
sn: अस्ति त्वत्र नलो नाम वानरः शिल्पिसम्मतः। त्वष्टुर्देवस्य तनयो बलवान् विश्वकर्मणः॥
en: There is a powerful monkey (in your army) Nala by name, who is a skillful mechanic and the son of the god Tvashtri, the architect of the universe.

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The construction of the bridge (across the sea
sn: स यत् काष्ठं तृणं वापि शिलां वा क्षेप्स्यते मयि। सर्वं तद् धारयिष्याभि स ते सेतुर्भविष्यति॥
en: And whatsoever he may throw into my waters, whether it be a piece of wood or a straw or a stone, I will support them all and which will be bridge to you."

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The construction of the bridge (across the sea
sn: इत्युक्त्वान्तहिते तस्मिन् रामो नलमुवाच ह। कुरु सेतुं समुद्रे त्वं शक्तो ह्यसि मतो मम॥
en: Saying this the Ocean vanished. And then Rama said to Nala "build a bridge across the sea. For, in my opinion, you are able to do it."

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The construction of the bridge (across the sea
sn: तेनोपायेन काकुत्स्थः सेतुबन्धमकारयत्। दशयोजनविस्तारमायतं शतयोजनम्॥
en: The descendant of Kakustha by this means caused a bridge ten yojanas broad and a hundred yojanas long to be erected (over the sea).

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The construction of the bridge (across the sea
sn: नलसेतुरिति ख्यातो योऽद्यापि प्रथितो भुवि। रामस्याज्ञां पुरस्कृत्य निर्यातो गिरिसंनिभः॥
en: And having constructed the bridge which to this day is known on earth by the name of Nala's bridge, Nala (endued with a body) huge a rock came out at the command of Rama.

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The construction of the bridge (across the sea
sn: तत्रस्थं स तु धर्मात्मा सभागच्छद् विभीषणः। भ्राता वै राक्षसेन्द्रस्य चतुर्भिः सचिवैः सह॥
en: While Rama there the virtuous Vibhishana, the (youngest) brother of the Rakshasa king accompanied by four advisers came to him.

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The construction of the bridge (across the sea
sn: प्रतिजग्राह रामस्तं स्वागतेन महामनाः। सुग्रीवस्य तु शङ्काभूत् प्रणिधिः स्यादिति स्म ह॥
en: And the magnanimous Rama welcomed him with due honours. But Sugriva had his misgivings, considering that he might be a spy.

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The construction of the bridge (across the sea
sn: राघवः सत्यचेष्टाभिः सम्यक् च चरितेङ्गितैः। यदा तत्त्वेन तुष्टोऽभूत् तत एनमपूजयत्॥
en: The descendant of of Raghu, however, observing the sincerity of his exertions and many signs of good conduct (in him) was perfectly satisfied (that he was not a spy) and adored him.

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The construction of the bridge (across the sea
sn: सर्वराक्षसराज्ये चाप्यभ्यषिञ्चद् विभीषणम्। चक्रे च मन्त्रसचिवं सुहृदं लक्ष्मणस्य च॥
en: And he installed him in sovereignty over all the Rakshasas and made him his junior adviser and a friend of Lakshmana's. was

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The construction of the bridge (across the sea
sn: विभीषणमते चैव सोऽत्यकामन्महार्णवम्। ससैन्यः सेतुना तेन मासेनैव नराधिप॥
en: O king of men, in accordance with the instructions of Vibhishana, he crossed the sea with his troops by means of the bridge within a month.

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The construction of the bridge (across the sea
sn: ततो गत्वा समासाद्य लङ्कोद्यानान्यनेकशः। भेदयामास कपिभिर्महान्ति च बहूनि च॥
en: Then, having reached Lanka, he caused its numerous and extensive gardens to be ravaged by the monkeys.

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The construction of the bridge (across the sea
sn: ततस्तौ रावणामात्यौ मन्त्रिणौ शुकसारणौ। चरौ वानररूपेण तौ जग्राह विभीषणः॥
en: And Vibhishana arrested two of Ravana's ministers, Shuka and Sarana, who, disguised as monkeys, came there as spies.

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The construction of the bridge (across the sea
sn: प्रतिपन्नौ यदा रूपं राक्षसं तौ निशाचरौ। दर्शयित्वा ततः सैन्यं रामः पश्चादवासृजत्॥
en: And when those two night-rangers, assumed their real Rakshasa shape, Rama showed them his troops and then dismissed them.

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The construction of the bridge (across the sea
sn: निवेश्योपवने सैन्यं तत् पुरः प्राज्ञवानरम्। प्रेषयामास दौत्येन रावणस्य ततोऽङ्गदम्॥
en: Having placed his army in the pleasuregardens of that city, Rama sent that wise monkey, Angada, as his envoy to Ravana.

description: The entry of Rama into Lanka
sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच प्रभूतान्नोदके तस्मिन् बहुमूलफले वने। सेनां निवेश्य काकुत्स्थो विधिवत् पर्यरक्षत॥
en: Markandeya said : The descendant of Kakustha having encamped his troops in those woods and abounding with plenty of food and drink and various (sorts of) fruits and roots, began to watch over them carefully.

description: The entry of Rama into Lanka
sn: रावणः संविधं चक्रे लङ्कायां शास्त्रनिर्मिताम्। प्रकृत्यैव दुराधर्षा दृढप्राकारतोरणा॥ अगाधतोयाः परिखा मीननक्रसमाकुलाः। बभूवुः सप्त दुर्धर्षाः खादिरैः शङ्कुभिश्चिताः॥
en: (On the other hand) Ravana set up, in Lanka, engines constructed in accordance with (the rules of the science on war). And the seven moats, (which encircled the city), protected by strong walls and gates, full of deep waters and abounding with fishes and alligators, though naturally unassailable, were rendered more so by being surrounded with pointed stakes of Khadira wood.

description: The entry of Rama into Lanka
sn: कपाटयन्त्रदुर्धर्षा बभूवुः सहुडोपलाः। साशीविषघटायोधाः ससर्जरसपांसवः॥
en: And the ramparts furnished with rounded stones and iron clubs were made unassailable by means of ballistas. The warriors (who mounted guard on the gates) had with them earthen jars full of poisonous snakes, resinous powders.

description: The entry of Rama into Lanka
sn: मुसलालातनाराचतोमरासिपरश्वधैः। अन्विताश्च शतघ्नीभिः समधूच्छिष्टमुद्गराः॥
en: And were armed with maces, fire-brands, Narichas, Tomaras, swords, axes, Shataghnis and clubs saturated with wax.

description: The entry of Rama into Lanka
sn: पुरद्वारेषु सर्वेषु गुल्म: स्थावरजङ्गमाः। बभूवुः पत्तिबहुलाः प्रभूतगजवाजिनः॥
en: And all the city gates were guarded by permanent and temporary encampments containing large numbers of infantry and by innumerable elephants and horses.

description: The entry of Rama into Lanka
sn: अगदस्त्वथ लङ्काया द्वारदेशमुपागतः। विदितो राक्षसेन्द्रस्य प्रविवेश गतव्यथः॥
en: Angada having reached one of the gates of Lanka and being made known to the Rakshasa king entered (the city) fearlessly.

description: The entry of Rama into Lanka
sn: मध्ये राक्षसकोटीनां बह्वीनां सुमहाबलः। शुशुभे मेघमालाभिरादित्य इव संवृतः॥
en: And that highly-powerful one surrounded by innumerable crores of Rakshasas shone like the sun in the midst of masses of clouds.

description: The entry of Rama into Lanka
sn: स समासाद्य पौलस्त्यममात्यैरभिसंवृतम्। रामसंदेशमामन्त्र्य वाग्मी वक्तुं प्रचक्रमे॥
en: And that eloquent (monkey) having approached and saluted the descendant of Pulastya who was surrounded by (his) ministers, began to deliver Rama's message (in the following words).

description: The entry of Rama into Lanka
sn: आह त्वां राघवो राजन् कोसलेन्द्रो महायशाः। प्राप्तकालमिदं वाक्यं तदादत्स्व कुरुष्व च॥
en: "O king, the highly-renowned lord of Kosala, the descendant of Raghu says to you (through me) these words appropriate to the occasion. Accept that (message) and act in obedience to it.

description: The entry of Rama into Lanka
sn: अकृतात्मानमासाद्य राजानमनये रतम्। विनश्यन्त्यनयाविष्टा देशाश्च नगराणि च॥
en: (Those) countries and cities whose kings are addicted to immoral acts and are incapable of controlling their minds, are themselves covered with sin and destroyed.

description: The entry of Rama into Lanka
sn: त्वयैकेनापराद्धं मे सीतामाहरता बलात्। वधायानपराद्धानामन्येषां तद् भविष्यति॥
en: You alone are guilty of forcibly carrying off Sita; but your guilt will lead many innocent persons to death.

description: The entry of Rama into Lanka
sn: ये त्वया बलदर्पाभ्यामाविष्टेन वनेचराः। ऋषयो हिंसिताः पूर्वं देवाश्चाप्यवमानिताः॥ राजर्षयश्च निहता रुदत्यश्च हृताः स्त्रियः। तदिदं समनुप्राप्तं फलं तस्यानयस्य ते॥
en: Elated with power and pride, you who formerly killed many Rishis living in the forests, insulted the gods, slew many royal sages and carried off weeping damsels, are about to be visited with retributive justice for your those vicious deeds.

description: The entry of Rama into Lanka
sn: हन्तास्मि त्वां सहामात्यैर्युध्यस्व पुरुषो भव। पश्य मे धनुषो वीर्यं मानुषस्य निशाचर॥
en: I will kill you together with your advisers. Give battle and play the hero. O night-ranger, behold the strength of my bow though I ar only a mortal.

description: The entry of Rama into Lanka
sn: मुच्यतां जानकी सीता न मे मोक्ष्यसि कर्हिचित्। अराक्षसमिमं लोकं कर्तास्मि निशितैः शरैः॥
en: Liberate Sita, the daughter of Janaka. But if you persist in not releasing her I will make this earth bare of all the Rakshasas with sharpened arrows."

description: The entry of Rama into Lanka
sn: इति तस्य ब्रुवाणस्य दूतस्य परुषं वचः। श्रुत्वा न ममृषे राजा रावणः क्रोधमूर्छितः॥
en: Hearing these harsh words of the messenger, king Ravana could not brook them and became senseless with rage.

description: The entry of Rama into Lanka
sn: इशितज्ञास्ततो भर्तुश्चत्वारो रजनीचराः। चतुर्भुङ्गेषु जगृहुः शार्दूलमिव पक्षिणः॥
en: Thereupon four night-wanderers who understood (well) the signs of their lord seized Angada by his four limbs like birds seizing a tiger.

description: The entry of Rama into Lanka
sn: तांस्तथाङ्गेषु संसक्तानङ्गदो रजनीचरान्। आदायैव खमुत्पत्य प्रासादतलमाविशत्॥
en: And along with those wanderers of the night who held him fast by his limbs Angada took a leap upwards and alighted on the roof of the palace.

description: The entry of Rama into Lanka
sn: वेगेनोत्पततस्तस्य पेतुस्ते रजनीचराः। भुवि सम्भिन्नहृदयाः प्रहारवरपीडिताः॥
en: Those Rakshasa raised up with great force fell down on the ground with their ribs shattered and sorely afflicted by the violence of the fall.

description: The entry of Rama into Lanka
sn: संसक्तो हर्म्यशिखरात् तस्मात् पुनरवापतत्। लवयित्वा पुरीं लङ्कां सुवेलस्य समीपतः॥
en: And he again took a leap from the roof of the palace whereon he descended and clearing the city of Lanka, come down to his comrades.

description: The entry of Rama into Lanka
sn: कोसलेन्द्रमथागम्य सर्वमावेद्य वानरः। विशश्राम स तेजस्वी राघवेणाभिनन्दितः॥
en: Then that monkey, approaching the lord of Kosala told him everything; and being highly praised by the descendant of Raghu, the energetic monkey went away to take rest.

description: The entry of Rama into Lanka
sn: ततः सर्वाभिसारेण हरीणां वातरंहसाम्। भेदयामास लङ्कायाः प्राकारं रघुनन्दनः॥
en: Then the descendant of Raghu by the simultaneous exertions of all monkeys, fleet as the wind, caused the walls of Lanka to be broken down.

description: The entry of Rama into Lanka
sn: विभीषणाधिपती पुरस्कृत्याथ लक्ष्मणः। दक्षिणं नगरद्वारमवामृद्गाद् दुरासदम्॥
en: Then Lakshmana with Vibhishana and the lord of the bears (Jambuvana) marching ahead, demolished the impregnable southern gate of the city.

description: The entry of Rama into Lanka
sn: करभारुणपाण्डूनां हरीणां युद्धशालिनाम्। कोटीशतसहस्रेण लङ्कामभ्यपपत् तदा॥
en: Rama then invaded Lanka with a hundred thousand crores of monkeys skilled in battle and resembling young camels in the reddish complexion which they had.

description: The entry of Rama into Lanka
sn: प्रलम्बबाहूरुकरजवान्तरविलम्बिनाम्। ऋक्षाणां धूम्रवर्णानां तिस्रः कोट्यो व्यवस्थिताः॥
en: Thirty millions of grey-coloured bears having long arms and thighs, broad paws and supporting themselves on their broad haunches prepared themselves (for battle).

description: The entry of Rama into Lanka
sn: उत्पतद्भिः पतद्भिश्च नियतद्भिश्च वानरैः। नादृश्यत तदा सूर्यो रजसा नाशितप्रभः॥
en: And the sun, with his rays shadowed by the dust raised by the monkeys leaping up an down and crosswise, could not be seen.

description: The entry of Rama into Lanka
sn: शालिप्रसूनसदृशैः शिरीषकुसुमप्रभैः। तरुणादित्यसदृशैः शणगौरैश्च वानरैः॥ प्राकारं ददृशुस्ते तु समन्तात् कपिलीकृतम्। राक्षसा विस्मिता राजन् सस्त्रीवृद्धाः समन्ततः॥
en: And the walls (of Lanka) covered all over with monkeys endued with complexions (yellow) as the ears of paddy, (grey) as shirisha flowers (crimson) as the morning sun and white as flax, assumed a tawny hue. And O king, the Rakshasas together with their wives and elders were wonder-struck (at this unusual sight).

description: The entry of Rama into Lanka
sn: बिभिदुस्ते मणिस्तम्भान् कर्णाट्टशिखराणि च। भग्नोन्मथितशृङ्गाणि यन्त्राणि च विचिक्षिपुः॥
en: And they (the monkeys and the bears) broke down pillars made of gems and the terraces of spires of the palaces. Pulling down and breaking to pieces the engines and their propellers they threw them away.

description: The entry of Rama into Lanka
sn: परिगृह्य शतघ्नीश्च सचक्राः सहुडोपलाः। चिक्षिपुर्भुजवेगेन लङ्कामध्ये महास्वनाः॥
en: And seizing the Shataghnis together with discs, clubs and stones, they threw them violently into Lanka uttering load yells.

description: The entry of Rama into Lanka
sn: प्राकारस्थाश्च ये केचिनिशाचरगणास्तथा। प्रदुद्रुवुस्ते शतशः कपिभिः समभिद्रुताः॥
en: The night-wanderers that were stationed on the walls, attacked by the monkeys fled hurriedly by hundreds.

description: The entry of Rama into Lanka
sn: ततस्तु राजवचनाद् राक्षसाः कामरूपिणः। निर्ययुर्विकृताकाराः सहस्रशतसङ्घशः॥
en: Then, at the command of the king, hundreds and thousands of Rakshasas of unnatural shapes and who could assume any form they liked, issued out (of the city to meet the enemy).

description: The entry of Rama into Lanka
sn: शस्त्रवर्षाणि वर्षन्तो द्रावयित्वा वनौकसः। प्राकारं शोभयन्तस्ते परं विक्रममास्थिताः॥
en: Discharging a (perfect) deluge of arrows and displaying great prowess, they graced the walls on driving away the dwellers of forests.

description: The entry of Rama into Lanka
sn: स माषराशिसदृशैर्बभूव क्षणदाचरैः। कृतो निर्वानरो भूयः प्राकारो भीमदर्शनैः॥
en: And those terrible-looking night-rangers resembling heaps of flesh made the walls clear of monkeys.

description: The entry of Rama into Lanka
sn: पेतुः शूलविभिन्नाङ्गा बहवो वानरर्षभाः। स्तम्भतोरणभग्नाश्च पेतुस्तत्र निशाचरा:॥
en: And there with their bodies pierced by lances many foremost of monkeys fell (dead) and several night-rangers also crushed by pillars broken in the course of battle breathed their last.

description: The entry of Rama into Lanka
sn: केशाकेश्यभवद् युद्धं रक्षसां वानरैः सह। नखैर्दन्तैश्च वीराणां खादतां वै परस्परम्॥
en: And the battle raged on between the heroic Rakshasas who fell to devouring (the monkeys) and the monkeys both parties dragging one another by the hair of the head and mangling one another with nails and teeth.

description: The entry of Rama into Lanka
sn: निष्टनन्तो [भयतस्तत्र वानरराक्षसाः। हता निपतिता भूमौ न मुञ्चन्ति परस्परम्॥
en: The Rakshasas and the monkeys with terrific yells and roars killed and struck down one another on the ground but (still) they did not give up the fight.

description: The entry of Rama into Lanka
sn: रामस्तु शरजालानि ववर्ष जलदो यथा। तानि लङ्कां समासाद्य जघ्नुस्तान् रजनीचरान्॥
en: Rama too, then, poured down showers of arrows like the very clouds. And those arrows reaching Lanka killed many night-rangers.

description: The entry of Rama into Lanka
sn: सौमित्रिरपि नाराजैर्दृढधन्वा जितक्लमः। आदिश्यादिश्य दुर्गस्थान् पातयामास राक्षसान्॥
en: And that mighty bowman, the indefatiguable son of Sumitra also, naming (particular) Rakshasas who were stationed in the forts killed them with Narachas.

description: The entry of Rama into Lanka
sn: ततः प्रत्यवहारोऽभूत् सैन्यानां राघवाज्ञया। कृते विमर्दे लङ्कायां लब्धलक्ष्यो जयोत्तरः॥
en: Then by order of Rama the forces retired (from the battle field) after having achieved success (in battle) and demolished (the defences of) Lanka and thereby making all the objects (of the city) easy of being aimed at.

description: The single combat between Rama and Ravana
sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच ततो निविशमानांस्तान् सैनिकान् रावणानुगाः। अभिजग्मुर्गणानेके पिशाचक्षुद्ररक्षसाम्॥ पर्वणः पतनो जम्भः खरः क्रोधवशो हरिः। प्ररुजश्चारुजश्चैव प्रघसश्चैवमादयः॥
en: Markandeya said : Then, when those troops were in their quarters, Parvana Patana, Jambha, Khara, Krodhavasha, Hari, Praruja, Aruja, Praghasa and many other minor Rakshasas and Pishachas under the sway of Ravana entered amongst them.

description: The single combat between Rama and Ravana
sn: ते ततोऽभिपततां तेषामदृश्यानां दुरात्मनाम्। अन्तर्धानवधं तज्ज्ञश्चकार स विभीषणः॥
en: And remaining invisible, as those wickedsouled creatures were thus stealthily entering, Vibhishana, knew all this and did away with their power of invisibility.

description: The single combat between Rama and Ravana
sn: दृश्यमाना हरिभिर्बलिभिर्दूरपातिभिः। निहताः सर्वशो राजन् महीं जग्मुर्गतासवः॥
en: O king, when disclosed to view, all of them being slain by the powerful and long-leaping monkeys fell dead on the ground.

description: The single combat between Rama and Ravana
sn: अमृष्यमाण: सबलो रावणो निर्ययावथ। राक्षसानां बलैघरिः पिशाचानां च संवृतः।५।। युद्धशास्त्रविधानज्ञ उशना इव चापरः। व्यह्य चौशनसं व्यूहं हरीनभ्यवहारयत्॥
en: Unable to brook this, the mighty Ravana, skilled in the art of war like a second Ushana (Shukracharya), marched out, surrounded by his dreadful Rakshasa and Pishacha troops, and drawing up his army in that array known by the name of Ushana attacked all the monkeys.

description: The single combat between Rama and Ravana
sn: राघवस्तु विनिर्यान्तं व्यढानीकं दशाननम्। बार्हस्पत्यं विधिं कृत्वा प्रत्यव्यूहनिशाचरम्॥
en: And the descendant of Raghu also, seeing the ten-headed advance, opposed the nightranger by drawing up his army after the manner recommended by Brihaspati.

description: The single combat between Rama and Ravana
sn: समेत्य युयुधे तत्र ततो रामेण रावणः। युयुधे लक्ष्मणश्चापि तथैवेन्द्रजिता सह॥
en: Then Ravana, coming up to Rama, began fighting with him. And Lakshmana fought with Indrajita.

description: The single combat between Rama and Ravana
sn: विरूपाक्षेण सुग्रीवस्तारेण च निखर्वटः। तुण्डेन च नलस्तत्र पटुश: पनसेन च।॥
en: Sugriva with Virupaksha, Nikharvata with Tara, Nala with Tunda and Patusha with Panasa.

description: The single combat between Rama and Ravana
sn: विषह्यं यं हि यो मेने स स तेन समेयिवान्। युयुधे युद्धवेलायां स्वबाहुबलमाश्रितः॥
en: On that field of battle, he who considered another a match for him, advanced against and began fighting with him depending on his own prowess of arms.

description: The single combat between Rama and Ravana
sn: स सम्प्रहारो ववृधे भीरूणां भयवर्धनः। लोमसंहर्षणो घोरः पुरा देवासुरे यथा।॥
en: And that battle so frightful to cowards and which makes one's hair stand erect, was as furious as that fought between the gods and the demons in days of yore.

description: The single combat between Rama and Ravana
sn: रावणो राममानर्छच्छक्तिशूलासिवृष्टिभिः। निशितैरायसैस्तीक्ष्णै रावणं चापि राघवः॥
en: Ravana afflicted Rama with a downpour of darts, lances and swords and the descendant of Raghu too oppressed Ravana with sharpened iron darts having keen points.

description: The single combat between Rama and Ravana
sn: तथैवेन्द्रजितं यत्तं लक्ष्मणो मर्मभेदिभिः। इन्द्रजिच्चापि सौमित्रिं बिभेद बहुभिः शरैः॥
en: Similarly, Lakshmana wounded the exerting Indrajita and Indrajita Lakshmana, by various darts capable of piercing the vital parts.

description: The single combat between Rama and Ravana
sn: विभीषणः प्रहस्तं च प्रहस्तश्च विभीषणम्। खगपत्रैः शरैस्तीक्ष्णैरभ्यवर्षद् गतव्यथः॥
en: And Vibhishana discharged at Prahasta and Prahasta at Vibhishana, showers of sharpened arrows furnished with plumes of birds.

description: The single combat between Rama and Ravana
sn: तेषां बलवतामासीन्महास्त्राणां समागमः। विव्यथुः सकला येन त्रयो लोकाश्चराचराः॥
en: (And thus) there ensued an encounter among those powerful warriors skilled in wielding mighty weapons, which (encounter) sorely afflicted the three worlds with their mobile and immobile creatures.

description: The march of Kumbhakarna to battle
sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच ततः प्रहस्तः सहसा समभ्येत्य विभीषणम्। गतया ताडयामास विनद्य रणकर्कशः॥
en: Markandeya said : Then Prahasta, harsh in battle, rushing against Vibhishana all on a sudden and sending forth a terrible yell, smote him with his mace.

description: The march of Kumbhakarna to battle
sn: स तयाभिहतो धीमान् गदया भीमवेगया। नाकम्पत महाबाहुर्हिमवानिव सुस्थिरः॥
en: (But) the intellectual Vibhishana of mighty arms, although struck with that mace (hurled) with a terrible force, did not tremble in the least and stood firm as the Himavana mountains.

description: The march of Kumbhakarna to battle
sn: ततः प्रगृह्य विपुलां शतघण्टां विभीषणः। अनुमन्त्र्य महाशक्तिं चिक्षेपास्य शिरः प्रति॥
en: Then Vibhishana, taking up a huge and mighty Javelin studded with a hundred bells and inspiring it with the mantras hurled it at the head of Prahasta.

description: The march of Kumbhakarna to battle
sn: पतन्त्या स तया वेगाद् राक्षसोऽशनिवेगया। हृतोत्तमाङ्गो ददृशे वातरुग्ण इव दुमः॥
en: (And that Javelin) falling with a (great) force like that of the thunderbolt cut off the head of Prahasta, who thereupon looked like a tree broken by the wind.

description: The march of Kumbhakarna to battle
sn: तं दृष्ट्वा निहतं संख्ये प्रहस्तं क्षणदाचरम्। अभिदुद्राव धूम्राक्षो वेगेन महता कपीन्॥
en: Seeing that night-ranger (Prahasta) thus slain in the encounter, Dhumraksha rushed furiously against the monkeys.

description: The march of Kumbhakarna to battle
sn: तस्य मेघोपमं सैन्यमापतद् भीमदर्शनम्। दृष्ट्वैव सहसा दीर्णा रणे वानरपुङ्गवाः॥
en: The monkey-chiefs, on beholding that his terrible-looking soldiers, resembling the clouds, were rushing against them, fled from (the field of) battle.

description: The march of Kumbhakarna to battle
sn: ततस्तान् सहसा दीर्णान् दृष्ट्वा वानरपुङ्गवान्। निर्ययौ कपिशार्दूलो हनूमान् मारुतात्मजः॥
en: Seeing those foremost of monkeys run away all on a sudden, Hanuman, the brave of monkeys rallied them and stood ready (for battle).

description: The march of Kumbhakarna to battle
sn: तं दृष्ट्वावस्थितं संख्ये हरयः पवनात्मजम्। महत्या त्वरया राजन् संन्यवर्तन्त सर्वशः॥
en: (And), O king, beholding the son of Pavana remaining on the battlefield, all the monkeys rallied with great haste.

description: The march of Kumbhakarna to battle
sn: ततः शब्दो महानासीत् तुमुलो लोमहर्षणः। रामरावणसैन्यानामन्योन्यमभिधावताम्॥
en: Then there arose a great and tumultuous uproar, causing the hair stand on end, as the soldiers of Rama and Ravana rushed against one another.

description: The march of Kumbhakarna to battle
sn: तस्मिन् प्रवृत्ते संग्रामे घोरे रुधिरकर्दमे। धूम्राक्षः कपिसैन्यं तद् द्रावयामास पत्रिभः॥
en: (And) in that battle which raged hot and furious, making the field muddy with blood, Dhumraksha began to oppress the monkeyarmy with (showers of) arrows.

description: The march of Kumbhakarna to battle
sn: तं स रक्षोमहामात्रमापतन्तं सपत्निजत्। प्रतिजग्राह हनुमांस्तरसा पवनात्मजः॥
en: Then the son of Pavana, Hanuman, the vanquisher of his foes, quickly seized that leader of the Rakshasas who was advancing (against the monkey host).

description: The march of Kumbhakarna to battle
sn: तयोर्युद्धमभूद् घोरं हरिराक्षसवीरयोः। जिगीषतोयुधान्योन्यमिन्द्रप्रह्लादयोरिव॥
en: And there took place, between the Rakshasa and the monkey warrior, each desirous of vanquishing the other, as dreadful a battle as that (fought) between Indra and Pralhada (in olden days).

description: The march of Kumbhakarna to battle
sn: गदाभिः परिघेश्चैव राक्षसो जनिवान् कपिम्। कपिञ्च जनिवान् रक्षः सस्कन्धविटपैर्दुमैः॥
en: The Rakshasa smote the monkey with clubs and pikes and the monkey struck the Rakshasas with trees furnished with branches and trunks.

description: The march of Kumbhakarna to battle
sn: ततस्तमतिकोपेन साश्चं सरथसारथिम्। धूम्राक्षमवधीत् क्रुद्धो हनूमान् मारुतात्मजः॥
en: Then the angry Hanuman the son of Pavana fired with a mighty rage, destroyed Dhumraksha together with his horses charioteer and car.

description: The march of Kumbhakarna to battle
sn: ततस्तं निहतं दृष्ट्वा धूम्राक्षं राक्षसोत्तमम्। हरयो जातविस्रम्भा जघ्नुरन्ये च सैनिकान्॥
en: And seeing that foremost of Rakshasas, Dhumraksha, (thus) killed, the monkeys giving up their fear, slew many other soldiers.

description: The march of Kumbhakarna to battle
sn: ते वध्यमाना हरिभिर्बलिभिर्जितकाशिभिः। राक्षसा भग्नसंकल्पा लङ्कामभ्यपतन् भयात्॥
en: Thus slain by the powerful and victorious monkeys the Rakshasas lost their hearts and fled to Lanka in (great) fear.

description: The march of Kumbhakarna to battle
sn: तेऽभिपत्य परुं भग्ना हतशेषा निशाचराः। सर्वं राज्ञे यथावृत्तं रावणाय न्यवेदयन्॥
en: And the surviving might-wanderers, who fled (from the battle-field), reaching the city, informed king Ravana of all that had happened.

description: The march of Kumbhakarna to battle
sn: श्रुत्वा तु रावणस्तेभ्यः प्रहस्तं निहतं युधि। धूम्राक्षं च महेष्वासं ससैन्यं वानरर्षभैः॥ सुदीर्घमिव निःश्वस्य समुत्पत्य वरासनात्। उवाच कुम्भकर्णस्य कर्मकालोऽयमागतः॥
en: Hearing from them that the valiant monkeys, had in battle, killed Prahasta and the mighty bowman Dhumraksha together with (all) their forces, Ravana drawing a heavy sigh and rising from his excellent throne said, "The time for Kumbhakarna to act, is come."

description: The march of Kumbhakarna to battle
sn: इत्येवमुक्त्वा विविधैर्वादित्रैः सुमहास्वनैः। शयानमतिनिद्रालुं कुम्भकर्णमबोधयत्॥
en: Saying this, he awakened Kumbhakarna by means of various instruments emitting loud sounds, from his deep and prolonged sleep.

description: The march of Kumbhakarna to battle
sn: प्रबोध्य महता चैनं यत्नेनागतसाध्वसः। स्वस्थमासीनमव्यचं विनिद्रं राक्षसाधिपः॥ ततोऽब्रवीद् दशग्रीवः कुम्भकर्णं महाबलम्। धन्योऽसि यस्य ते निद्रा कुम्भकर्णेयमीदृशी॥
en: And when Kumbhakarna, who was aroused by great exertions, was comfortably seated, recovered consciousness and self-possession, the terrified lord of the Rakshasas, the tenheaded (Ravana) addressed Kumbhakarna endued with a giant strength thus, "O Kumbhakarna, you are indeed happy who enjoy such a (prolonged) sleep.

description: The march of Kumbhakarna to battle
sn: य इदं दारुणाकारं न जानीषे महाभयम्। एष तीर्वार्णवं रामः सेतुना हरिभिः सह॥ अवमन्येह नः सर्वान् करोति कदनं महत्। मया त्वपहृता भार्या सीता नामास्य जानकी॥
en: Unaware of this dreadful calamity (we have been visited with). This Rama together with the monkeys having crossed the sea by means of a bridge and disregarding us all is waging a terrible war. I have stealthily abducted his wife, named Sita, the daughter of Janaka.

description: The march of Kumbhakarna to battle
sn: तां नेतुं स इहायातो बद्ध्वा सेतुं महार्णवे। तेन चैव प्रहस्तादिमहान् नः स्वजनो हतः॥
en: And in order to recover her, he has come here having constructed a bridge over the vast ocean. He has killed Prahasta and many other kinsmen of ours.

description: The march of Kumbhakarna to battle
sn: तस्य नान्यो निहन्तास्ति त्वामृते शत्रुकर्शन। स दंशितोऽमिनिर्याय त्वमद्य बलिनां वरा॥ रामादीन् समरे सर्वाञ्जहि शत्रूनरिंदमा
en: O scourage of your enemies, there is no other person capable of slaying him than you. O bravest of the brave, do you (therefore) march out this day donning your mail and O tormentor of foes, slay in battle all your enemies, Rama and others.

description: The march of Kumbhakarna to battle
sn: दूषणावरजौ चैव वलावेगप्रमाथिनौ॥ तौ त्वां बलेन महता सहितावनुयास्यतः।
en: The two younger brothers of Dushana, Vajravega and Pramathin, accompanied by a mighty army will follow you."

description: The march of Kumbhakarna to battle
sn: इत्युक्त्वा राक्षसपति: कुम्भकर्णं तरस्विनम्। संदिदेशेतिकर्तव्यं वलावेगप्रमाथिनौ॥
en: Thus addressing the mighty Kumbhakarna, the lord of the Rakshasas pointed out to Vajravega and Pramathin what they should do.

description: The march of Kumbhakarna to battle
sn: तथेत्युक्त्वा तु तौ वीरौ रावणं दूषणानुजौ। कुम्भकर्णं पुरस्कृत्य तूर्णं निर्ययतुः पुरात्॥
en: And those two heroes, the younger brothers of Dushana saying to Ravana “It shall be so" (i.e. you orders shall be carried out) soon marched out of the city with Kumbhakarna at their head.

sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच ततो निर्याय स्वपुरात् कुम्भकर्णः सहानुगः। अपश्यत् कपिसैन्यं तज्जितकाश्यचतः स्थितम्॥
en: Markandeya said : Then having marched out of the city with his followers, Kumbhakarna beheld the victorious monkey-army lying before him.

sn: स वीक्षमाणस्तत् सैन्यं रामदर्शनकाक्षया अपश्यच्चापि सौमित्रिं धनुष्पाणिं व्यवस्थितम्॥
en: Having observed (carefully) the monkey host with the desire of finding out Rama (among it) he saw Lakshmana stand (ready for fight), bow in hand.

sn: तमभ्येत्याशु हरयः परिवः समन्ततः। अभ्यघ्नंश्च महाकायैर्बहुभिर्जगतीरुहै:॥
en: The monkeys, (then), coming up to him completely surrounded him and began to smite him with numerous huge trees.

sn: करजैरतुदंश्चान्ये विहाय भयमुत्तमम्। बहुधा युध्यमानास्ते युद्धमार्गः प्लवङ्गमाः॥ नानाप्रहरणैर्भीमै राक्षसेन्द्रमताडयन्।
en: (And) giving up their fear some began to tear him with nails and several monkeys fought him by resorting to various ways (of battle). And they hurled at that foremost of Rakshasas various terrible weapons.

sn: स ताड्यमानः प्रहसन् भक्षयामास वानरान्॥ बलं चण्डबलाख्यं च वल्लाबाहुं च वानरम्।
en: Thus struck, he only laughed (at them) and fell to eating up the monkeys, named Bala, Chandabala and Vajrabahu.

sn: तद् दृष्ट्वा व्यथनं कर्म कुम्भकर्णस्य रक्षसः॥ उदक्रोशन् परित्रस्तास्तारप्रभृतयस्तदा।
en: Seeing that terrible act of the Rakshasa Kumbhakarna, Tara and others were greatly alarıned and sent forth a loud wai).

sn: तानुच्चैः क्रोशतः सैन्याञ्छ्रुत्वा स हरियूथपान्॥ अभिदुद्राव सुग्रीवः कुम्भकर्णमपेतभीः।
en: Hearing the loud cry of the monkey chiefs, Sugriva fearlessly rushed at Kumbhakarna.

sn: ततो निपत्य वेगेन कुम्भकर्णं महामनाः॥ शालेन जनिवान् मूर्ध्नि बलेन कपिकुञ्जरः।
en: Then that high-minded king of the monkeys, coming up to Kumbhakarna with great speed struck him furiously on the head with a Sala tree.

sn: स महात्मा महावेगः कुम्भकर्णस्य मूर्धनि॥ बिभेद शालं सुग्रीवो न चैवाव्यथयत् कपिः।
en: And though that large-hearted monkey, Sugriva endued with a great speed, broke that Sala tree on the head of Kumbhakarna, yet he could not afflict him (in the least).

sn: ततो विनय सहसा शालस्पर्शविबोधितः॥ दोर्ध्यामादाय सुग्रीवं कुम्भकर्णोऽहरद् बलात्।
en: Then suddenly awakening at the touch of the Sala tree, Kumbhakarna, with a terrible yell, stretching forth his arms, seized Sugriva by main force.

sn: ह्रियमाणं तु सुग्रीवं कुम्भकर्णेन रक्षसा॥ अवेक्ष्याभ्यद्रवद् वीरः सौमित्रर्मित्रनन्दनः।
en: Seeing Sugriva (thus) seized by the Rakshasa Kumbhakarna, the war-like son of Sumitra, the delighter of his friends, rushed (to his rescue).

sn: सोऽभिपत्य महावेगं रुक्मपुङ्ख महाशरम्॥ प्राहिणोत् कुम्भकर्णाय लक्ष्मणः परवीरहा।
en: And coming up, that slayer of hostile warriors, Lakshmana, sent after him an impetuous and mighty dart furnished with golden wings.

sn: स तस्य देहावरणं भित्त्वा देहं च सायकः॥ जगाम दारयन् भूमि रुधिरेण समुक्षितः।
en: That arrow piercing through his armour and his body and covered with blood, penetrated into the earth.

sn: तथा स भिन्नहृदयः समुत्सृज्य कपीश्वरम्॥ कुम्भकर्णो महेष्वासः प्रगृहीतशिलायुधः। अभिदुद्राव सौमित्रिमुद्यम्य महतीं शिलाम्॥
en: His heart being (thus) riven, he let go the monkey king. (And then) that mighty bowman, Kumbhakarna, taking a stone as his arrow, rushed at the son of Sumitra, aiming that huge stone at him.

sn: तस्याभिपततस्तूर्णं क्षुराभ्यामुच्छ्रितौ करौ। चिच्छेद निशिताचाभ्यां स बभूव चतुर्भुजः॥
en: When he was (thus) advancing, (Lakshmana) quickly cut off his upraised arms with a pair keen-edged razors. He then became four-handed.

sn: तानप्यस्य भुजान् सर्वान् प्रगृहीतशिलायुधान्। क्षुचिच्छेद लघ्वस्त्रं सौमित्रिः प्रतिदर्शयन्॥
en: (But) the son of Sumitra, displaying his skill in arms cut off all those arms, holding stones as arrows, by razors.

sn: स बभूवातिकायश्च बहुपादशिरोभुजः। तं ब्रह्मास्त्रेण सौमित्रिर्ददाराद्रिचयोपमम्॥
en: His body then assumed formidable proportions and his head and arms began to multiply in large numbers. The son of Sumitra, then, pierced Kumbhakarna, looking like heaps of rocks, by that weapon presided over by Brahma.

sn: स पपात महावीर्यो दिव्यास्त्राभिहतो रणे। महाशनिविनिर्दग्धः पादपोऽङ्कुरवानिव॥
en: And he, endued with a vast strength, struck by that celestials weapon, fell dead on the battle (field) like a gigantic tree having its spreading branches burnt up by the fire of) the thunderbolt.

sn: तं दृष्ट्वा वृत्रसंकाशं कुम्भकर्णं तरस्विनम्। गतासुं पतितं भूमौ राक्षसाः प्राद्रवन् भयात्॥
en: Seeing the mighty Kumbhakarna (powerful) as (the Asura) Vritra, lying dead on the ground, the Rakshasas ran away in (great) terror.

sn: तथा तान् द्रवतो योधान् दृष्ट्वा तौ दूषणानुजौ। अवस्थाप्याथ सौमित्रिं संक्रुद्धावभ्यधावताम्॥
en: Then, the two younger brothers of Dushana, seeing those warriors fly away, rallied them and rushed furiously against the son of Sumitra.

sn: तावाद्रवन्तौ संक्रुद्धौ वलावेगप्रमाथिनौ। अभिजग्राह सौमित्रिर्विनियोभौ पतत्रिभिः॥
en: Seeing Vajravega and Pramathin advance against him in great wrath, the son of Sumitra with a loud shout assailed them both with shafts.

sn: ततः सुतुमुलं युद्धमभवल्लोमहर्षणम्। दूषणानुजयोः पार्थ लक्ष्मणस्य च धीमतः॥
en: Then, O Partha, there ensued an awfullyterrible encounter, making the hair stand erect, between the younger brothers of Dushana and the intelligent Lakshmana.

sn: महता शरवर्षेण राक्षसौ सोऽभ्यवर्षत। तौ चापि वीरौ संक्रुद्धावुभौ तं समवर्षताम्॥
en: And he (Lakshmana) covered the Rakshasas with a heavy downpour of arrows and those two (Rakshasa) heroes also in great wrath overwhelmed Lakshmana with showers (of arrows).

sn: मुहूर्तमेवमभवद् वलावेगप्रमाथिनोः। सौमित्रेश्च महाबाहोः सम्प्रहारः सुदारुणः॥
en: That furious battle between Vajravega and Pramathin (on one hand) and the mighty-armed son of Sumitra (on the other) lasted for a moment only.

sn: अथाद्रिशृङ्गमादाय हनुमान् मारुतात्मजः। अभिद्रुत्याददे प्राणान् वलावेगस्य रक्षसः॥
en: Then Hanuman, the son of Pavana, taking up a mountain-peak rushed at and took the life of, the Rakshasa Vajravega.

sn: नीलश्च महता चाव्णा दूषणावरजं प्रमाथिनमभिद्रुत्य प्रममाथ महाबलः॥
en: (And) the monkey Nila, endued with a vast strength, rushing towards Pramathin, the younger brother of Dushana crushed him with a huge rock.

sn: ततः प्रावर्तत पुनः संग्रामः कटुकोदयः। रामरावणसैन्यानामन्योन्यमभिधावताम्॥
en: Then there again raged a terrible encounter between the forces of Rama and Ravana, smiting one another.

sn: शतशो नैर्ऋतान् वन्या जनुर्वन्यांश्च नैर्ऋताः। नैर्ऋतास्तत्र वध्यन्ते प्रायेण न तु वानराः॥
en: The monkeys slew hundreds and Rakshasas and the Rakshasas too killed many dwellers of forest. But the number of Rakshasas killed was greater than that of the monkeys.

sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच ततः श्रुत्वा हतं संख्ये कुम्भकर्णं सहानुगम्। प्रहस्तं च महेष्वासं धूम्राक्षं चातितेजसम्॥ पुत्रमिन्द्रजितं वीरं रावणः प्रत्यभाषत। जहि रामममित्रघ्न सुग्रीवं च सलक्ष्मणम्॥
en: Markandeya said : Then, hearing that the mighty bowman Prahasta, the highly-energetic Dhumraksha and Kumbhakarna together with his followers had been killed in battle, Ravana spoke to his heroic son Indrajita (thus), “O destroyer of foes, slay Rama together with Sugriva and Lakshmana.

sn: त्वया हि मम सत्पुत्र यशो दीप्तमुपार्जितम्। जित्वा वलाधरं संख्ये सहस्राक्षं शचीपतिम्॥
en: O my dutiful son, by conquering the thousand-eyed wielder of the Vajra (thunderbolt), the husband of Sachi, in battle, you have acquired a blazing renown for me.

sn: अन्तर्हितः प्रकाशो वा दिव्यैर्दत्तवरैः शरैः। जहि शत्रूनमित्रघ्न मम शस्त्रभृतां वर॥
en: Remaining (either) invisible or visible, O slayer of foes, the best of those that wield weapon, kill my enemies by celestials weapons granted to you as boons.

sn: रामलक्ष्मणसुग्रीवाः शरस्पर्श न तेऽनघ। समर्थाः प्रतिसोढुं च कुतस्तदनुयायिनः॥
en: O sinless one, not to speak of their followers, even Rama, Lakshmana and Sugriva cannot endure the touch of your weapons.

sn: अकृता या प्रहस्तेन कुम्भकर्णेन चानघ। खरस्यापचिति: संख्ये तां गच्छ त्वं महाभुज॥
en: O sinless and mighty-armed one, bring to a (successful) termination the hostilities which even Prahasta and Kumbhakarna could not effect in battle.

sn: त्वमद्य निशितैर्बाणैर्हत्वा शत्रून् ससैनिकान्। प्रतिनन्दन मां पुत्र पुरा जित्वेव वासवम्॥
en: My son, destroying, today, my enemies together with their followers, increase my delight as you did before by conquering Vasava."

sn: इत्युक्तः स तथेत्युक्त्वा रथमास्थाय दंशितः। प्रययाविन्द्रजिद् राजस्तूर्ममायोधनं प्रति॥
en: O king, thus addressed (by his father), Indrajita replied “it shall be so" and donning his armour and riding on his car, he soon marched towards the battle-field.

sn: ततो विश्राव्य विस्पष्टं नाम राक्षसपुङ्गवः। आह्वयामास समरे लक्ष्मणं शुभलक्षणम्॥
en: Then that foremost of Rakshasas distinctly announcing his name, challenged Lakshmana bearing auspicious signs, to battle.

sn: तं लक्ष्मणोऽभ्यधावच्च प्रगृह्य सशरं धनुः। त्रासयंस्तलघोषेण सिंहः क्षुद्रमृगान् यथा॥
en: (And) like a lion (pursuing) a fawn, Lakshmana taking up his bow together with arrows and terrifying his adversary by striking his arm with his palms, rushed towards him.

sn: तयोः समभवद् युद्धं सुमहज्जयगृद्धिनोः। दिव्यास्त्रविदुषोस्तीव्रमन्योन्यस्पर्धिनोस्तदा॥
en: Then, there ensued a terrible and mighty encounter between those two (warriors), desirous of overcoming each other, both skilled in celestials weapons and setting at defiance the prowess of each other.

sn: रावणिस्तु यदा नैनं विशेषयति सायकैः। ततो गुरुतरं यत्नमातिष्ठद् बलिनां वरः॥
en: When the son of Ravana, the strongest of the strong, could not get the better of his adversary by his arrows, he began to make vigorous exertions.

sn: तत एनं महावेगैरर्दयामास तोमरैः। तानागतान् स चिच्छेद सौमित्रिर्निशतैः शरैः॥
en: Then he (Indrajita) began to hurl violently at Lakshmana, many javelins. But the son of Sumitra severed them to pieces as they were coming up to him, with sharpened arrows.

sn: ते निकृत्ताः शरैस्तीक्ष्णैर्यपतन् धरणीतले। तमङ्गदो वालिसुतः श्रीमानुद्यम्य पादपम्॥ अभिद्रुत्य महावेगस्ताडयामास मूर्धनि। तस्येन्द्रजिदसम्भ्रान्तः प्रासेनोरसि वीर्यवान्॥ प्रहर्तुमैच्छत् तं चास्य प्रासं चिच्छेद लक्ष्मणः।
en: (Thus) cut down by sharpened darts they fell down on earth. Then the renowned Angada, the son to Bali, uprooting a tree and coming up with great speed, struck him (Indrajita) on the head. (But) the mighty Indrajita 'nothing daunted at this, took up a lance (and) wished to hurl it at him. (But) Lakshmana severed that lance.

sn: तमभ्याशगतं वीरमगदं रावणात्मजः॥ गदयाताडयत् सव्ये पार्श्वे वानरपुङ्गवम्।
en: (Then) the son of Ravana, (seeing) the heroic Angada stand close to him, struck on the left side of the foremost of monkeys with a mace.

sn: तमचिन्त्य प्रहारं स बलवान् वालिनः सुतः॥ ससर्जेन्द्रजित: क्रोधाच्छालस्कन्धं तथाङ्गदः।
en: Disregarding that stroke, the mighty son of Bali, Angada, wrathfully hurled a Sala stem at Indrajita.

sn: सोऽङ्गदेन रुषोत्सृष्टो वधायेन्द्रजितस्तरुः॥ जघानेन्द्रजितः पार्थ रथं साश्वं ससारथिम्।
en: And that tree, hurled wrathfully by Angada for killing Indrajita, O Partha, destroyed his car together with the charioteer and horses.

sn: ततो हताश्वात् प्रस्कन्ध रथात् स हतसारथिः॥ तत्रैवान्तर्दधे राजन् मायया रावणात्मजः।
en: His horses and driver being slain, he jumped down from the car; and O king, resorting to his power of illusion, the son of Ravana vanished at that very spot.

sn: अन्तर्हितं विदित्वा तं बहुमायं च राक्षसम्॥ रामस्तं देशमागम्य तत् सैन्यं पर्यरक्षत।
en: Knowing that the Rakshasa capable of spreading various illusions, had disappeared, Rama coming up to that place (where the battle was raging) began to carefully protect his army.

sn: स राममुद्दिश्य शरैस्ततो दत्तवरैस्तदा॥ 'विव्याध सर्वगात्रेषु लक्ष्मणं च महाबलम्।
en: He (Indrajita), then, aiming at Rama and the highly-powerful Lakshmana began to pierce them, with arrows obtained as boons, all over their bodies.

sn: तमदृश्यं शरैः शूरौ माययान्तर्हितं तदा॥ योधयामासतुरुभौ रावणिं रामलक्ष्मणौ।
en: Then both the heroic Rama and Lakshmana, began to fight the son of Ravana, who remained invisible by his powers of illusion, by means of arrows.

sn: स रुषा सर्वगात्रेषु तयोः पुरुषसिंहयोः॥ व्यसृजत् सायकान् भूयः शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः।
en: But Indrajita discharged at the bodies of those lions among men, incessant showers of arrows by hundreds and thousands.

sn: तमदृश्यं विचिन्वन्तः सृजन्तमनिशं शरान्॥ हरयो विविशुफ्रेम प्रगृह्य महती: शिलाः।
en: Seeing that he (Indrajita) remaining invisible, poured down showers of arrows, the monkeys taking up huge stones entered into (every part of the) firmament.

sn: तांश्च तौ चाप्यदृश्यः स शरैर्विव्याधराक्षसः॥ स भृशं ताडयामास रावणिर्माययाऽऽवृतः।
en: But the Rakshasa being invisible, pierced them and the two (brothers Rama and Lakshmana), with arrows hidden by illusion, the son of Ravana sorely afflicted them (the monkeys).

sn: तौ शरैराचितौ वीरौ भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ। पेततुर्गगनाद् भूमिं सूर्याचन्द्रमसाविव॥
en: And the two brothers, the heroic Rama and Lakshmana, wounded all over with shafts fell down on earth, as if the sun and the moon had fallen from the firmament.

sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच तावुभौ पतितौ दृष्ट्वा भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ। बबन्ध रावणिर्भूयः शरैर्दत्तवरैस्तदा॥
en: Markandeya said : Seeing those two brothers, Rama and Lakshmana drop down on earth, the son of Ravana tied them in a net-work of arrows, granted to him as boons.

sn: तौ वीरौ शरबन्धेन बद्धाविन्द्रजिता रणे। रेजतुः पुरुषव्याघ्रौ शकुन्ताविव पञ्जरे॥
en: Those heroes, those valiant of men, thus covered by that net-work of arrows on the field of battle looked like a couple of birds confined in a cage.

sn: तौ दृष्ट्वा पतितौ भूमौ शतशः सायकैश्चितौ। सुग्रीवः कपिभिः सार्धं परिवार्य ततः स्थितः॥ सुषेणमैन्दद्विविदैः कुमुदेनाङ्गदेन च। हनुमन्नीलतारैश्च नलेन च कपीश्वरः॥
en: Seeing those two (brothers) lying stretched on the ground, pierced with hundreds of arrows, Sugriva, the king of the monkeys together with Sushena, Mainda, Dvivida, Kumuda, Angada, Hanuman, Nila, Tara, Nala and (other) monkeys stood surrounding them.

sn: ततस्तं देशमागम्य कृतकर्मा विभीषणः। बोधयामास तौ वीरौ प्रज्ञास्त्रेण प्रबोधितौ॥
en: Then, the successful Vibhishana arriving at that place and restoring those two heroes to consciousness by means of the weapon (named) Prajna brought them back to senses.

sn: विशल्यौ चापि सुग्रीवः क्षणेनैतौ चकार ह। विशल्यया महौषध्या दिव्यमन्त्रप्रयुक्तया॥
en: Then Sugriva soon drew out the arrows (from their bodies). And by that highly-potent medicine, Vishalya, applied with the celestials mantras,

sn: तौ लब्धसंज्ञौ नृवरौ विसल्यावुदतिष्ठताम्। गततन्द्रीक्लमौ चापि क्षणैनैतौ महारथौ॥
en: Those two foremost of men recovered their senses. (And) the arrows being extracted from their bodies, those mighty car-warriors sat up and became, in a moment free from pain and fatigue.

sn: ततो विभीषणः पार्थ राममिक्ष्वाकुनन्दनम्। उवाच विज्वरं दृष्ट्वा कृताञ्जलिरिदं वचः॥
en: O Partha, seeing Rama, the descendant of Ikshvaku perfectly free from pain. Vibhishana, with joined hands said these words,

sn: इदमम्भो गृहीत्वा तु राजराजस्य शासनात्। गुह्यकोऽभ्यागतः श्वेतात् त्वत्सकाशमरिन्दम॥
en: "O tormentor of foes, at the command of the king of kings, a Guhyaka has come (to you) from the Shveta mountains, with this water.

sn: इदमम्भः कुबेरस्ते महाराजः प्रयच्छति। अन्तर्हितानां भूतानां दर्शनार्थं परंतप॥
en: O chastiser of foes, Kubera, the king of kings has sent you this water in order that you may behold all invisible beings.

sn: अनेन मृष्टनयनो भूतान्यन्तर्हितान्युत। भवान् द्रक्ष्यति यस्मै च प्रदास्यति नरः स तु॥
en: If you wash your eyes with this you and any man whom you may give this will be able to see all invisible creatures."

sn: तथेति रामस्तद् वाारि प्रतिगृह्याभिसंस्कृतम्। चकार नेत्रयोः शौचं लक्ष्मणश्च महामनाः॥ सुग्रीवजाम्बवन्तौ च हनुमानङ्गदस्तथा। मैन्दद्विविदनीलाश्च प्रायः प्लवगसत्तमाः॥
en: Saying “be it so" Rama took that water and minded Lakshmana, Sugriva, Jambuvana, Hanuman, Angada, Mainda, Dvivida, Nila and almost all the foremost of monkeys did the same.

sn: तथा समभवच्चापि यदुवाच विभीषणः। क्षणेनातीन्द्रियाण्येषां चढूंष्यासन् युधिष्ठिर॥
en: (Thereupon) what Vibhishana had said, (exactly) came about. And, O Yudhishthira, soon their eyes became capable of perceiving objects beyond the reach of the senses.

sn: इन्द्रजित् कृतकर्मा च पित्रे कर्म तदाऽऽत्मनः। निवेद्य पुनरागच्छत् त्वरयाऽऽजिशिरः प्रति॥
en: On the other hand, the successful Indrajita, having informed his father of what he had done, soon returned to the field of battle.

sn: तमापतन्तं संक्रुद्धं पुनरेव युयुत्सया। अभिदुद्राव सौमित्रिविभीषणमते स्थितः॥
en: (And) as he (Indrajita) desirous of battle, was advancing wrathfully, the son of Sumitra, at the advice of Vibhishana rushed at him.

sn: अकृताह्निकमेवैनं जिघांसुर्जितकाशिनम्। शरैर्जघान संक्रुद्धः कृतसंज्ञोऽथ लक्ष्मणः।१७।।
en: And desirous of slaying Indrajita, who was elated with success and who had not yet completed his daily sacrifice, Lakshmana, at a hint (from Vibhishana) assailed him wrathfully with arrows.

sn: तयोः समभवद् युद्धं तदान्योन्यं जिगीषतोः। अतीव चित्रमाश्चर्यं शक्रप्रह्लादयोरिव॥
en: Then between those (warriors) each desirous of vanquishing the other, there took place an exceedingly wonderful battle like that (which had taken place) between Shakra and Pralhada.

sn: अविध्यदिन्द्रजित् तीक्ष्णैः सौमित्रिं मर्मभेदिभिः। सौमित्रिश्चानलस्पर्शेरविध्यद् रावणि शरैः॥
en: Then Indrajita pierced the son of Sumitra by sharpened arrows capable of penetrating into the vital parts. And the son of Sumitra too wounded the son of Ravana with arrows having the touch of fire.

sn: सौमित्रिशरसंस्पर्शाद् रावणिः क्रोधमूर्च्छितः। असृजल्लक्ष्मणायाष्टौ शरानाशीविषोपमान्॥
en: Pierced by the arrows of the son of Sumitra, Indrajita, being senseless with rage, discharged at him eight darts (fierce) as poisonous snakes.

sn: तस्यासून् पावकस्पर्शः सौमित्रिः पत्रिभिस्त्रिभिः। यथा निरहरद् वीरस्तन्मे निगदतः शृणुः॥
en: Listen, attentively as I tell you, how the heroic son of Sumitra killed (Indrajita) by means of three arrow of fiery energy.

sn: एकेनास्य धनुष्मन्तं बाहुं देहादपातयत्। द्वितीयेन सनाराचं भुजं भूमौ न्यपातयत्॥ तृतीयेन तु बाणेन पृथुधारेण भास्वता। जहार सुनसं चापि शिरो भ्राजिष्णुकुण्डलम्॥
en: By one of these (arrows), he severed from his body that arm which wielded the bow; by the second, he cut down to the ground that arm which wielded the arrows and by the third arrow of keen edge and bright lustre he cut off his head having a beautiful nose and decked with earrings.

sn: विनिकृत्तभुजस्कन्धं कबन्धं भीमदर्शनम्। तं हत्वा सूतमप्यस्त्रैर्जघान बलिनां वरः॥
en: Deprived of head and arms, the trunk looked terrible. Having slain him (Indrajita), the strongest of the strong, (Lakshmana) killed his charioteer with weapons.

sn: लङ्कां प्रवेशयामासुस्तं रथं वाजिनस्तदा। ददर्श रावणस्तं च रथं पुत्रविनाकृतम्॥ स पुत्रं निहतं ज्ञात्वा त्रासात् सम्भ्रान्तमानसः। रावणः शोकमोहा” वैदेहीं हन्तुमुद्यतः॥
en: Then the horses dragged away the car into Lanka and Ravana then saw that his son was not on the car. Knowing (from this) that his son was killed, Ravana, his mind being agitated with fear and afflicted with grief and sorrow was actuated with the desire of killing the daughter of the king of Mithila.

sn: अशोकवनिकास्थां तां रामदर्शनलालसाम्। खङ्गमादाय दुष्टात्मा जवेनाभिपपात ह॥
