en: And that evil-minded one, taking his sword, furiously rushed at Sita, who was living in the Ashoka gardens longing for the sight of Rama.

sn: तं दृष्ट्वा तस्य दुर्बुद्धेरविन्ध्यः पापनिश्चयम्। शमयामास संक्रुद्धं श्रूयतां येन हेतुना॥
en: Now hear how Avindhya, seeing the evilminded one bent on this reprehensible act, softened down his wrath by showing these reasons.

sn: महाराज्ये स्थितो दीप्ते न स्त्रियं हन्तुमर्हसि। हतैवैषा यदा स्त्री च बन्धनस्था च ते वशे॥
en: (He said) "Placed as you are on the throne of this renowned and mighty empire, you should not kill a woman. This woman (to all intents and purposes) is already slain in as much as she is a prisoner in your power.

sn: न चैषा देहभेदेन हता स्यादिति मे मतिः। जहि भर्तारमेवास्याहते तस्मिन् हता भवेत्॥
en: In my opinion, she would not be killed if her body were destroyed. Kill her husband and then she will be killed too.

sn: न हि ते विक्रमे तुल्यः साक्षादपि शतक्रतुः। असकृद्धि त्वया सेन्द्रास्त्रासितास्त्रिदशा युधि॥
en: Even the very lord of a hundred sacrifices is no match for you in prowess. You have several times struck terror into the hearts of Indra together with the celestials in battle."

sn: एवं बहुविधैर्वाक्यैरविन्थ्यो रावणं तदा। क्रुद्धं संशमयामास जगृहे च स तद्वचः॥
en: With these and similar other words, Avindhya pacified the wrath of Ravana who accepted his advice.

sn: निर्याणे स मतिं कृत्वा निधायासिं क्षपाचरः। आज्ञापयामास तदा रथो मे कल्प्यतामिति॥
en: Then resolving to set out (for the field of battle himself) that night-ranger put his sword into sheath and ordered his attendants) to prepare his car.

sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच ततः क्रुद्धो दशग्रीवः प्रिये पुढे निपातिते। निर्ययौ रथमास्थाय हेमरत्नविभूषितम्॥
en: Markandeya said : Then, angry at the death of his dear son, the ten-necked, ascending his car, studded with gems and gold set out (for the field of battle).

sn: स वृतो राक्षसैोरैर्विविधायुधपाणिभिः। अभिदुद्राव रामं स योधयन् हरियूथपान्॥
en: Surrounded by dreadful Rakshasas holding in their hands various weapons, he fighting with the monkey-chiefs rushed upon Rama.

sn: तमाद्रवन्तं संक्रुद्धं मैन्दनीलनलाङ्गदाः। हनूमाञ्जाम्बवांश्चैव ससैन्याः पर्यवारयन्॥
en: As he (Ravana) was furiously advancing, Mainda, Nala, Nila, Angada, Hanuman and Jambavan together with their forces surrounded him.

sn: ते दशग्रीवसैन्यं तदृक्षावनरपुङ्गवाः। दुमैविध्वंसयांचक्रुर्दशग्रीवस्य पश्यतः॥
en: Those foremost of bears and monkeys destroyed, with trees, the forces of the tennecked in his (very) presence.

sn: ततः स सैन्यमालोक्य वध्यमानमरातिभिः। मायावी चासृजन्मायां रावणो राक्षसाधिपः॥
en: Then, seeing that his troops were being destroyed by the enemy, Ravana, the king of the Rakshasas began to create illusions with which he was gifted.

sn: तस्य देहविनिष्क्रान्ताः शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः। राक्षसाः प्रत्यदृश्यन्त शरशक्त्वृष्टिपाणयः॥
en: (Thereupon) hundreds and thousands of Rakshasas, armed with arrows, lances and double-edged swords, issuing out of his body appeared (on the scene).

sn: तान् रामो जघ्निवान् सर्वान् दिव्येनास्त्रेण राक्षसान्। अथ भूयोऽपि मायां स व्यदधाद् राक्षसाधिपः॥
en: (But) Rama destroyed all those Rakshasas with celestials weapons. There at the lord of the Rakshasas created (new) illusions again.

sn: कृत्वा रामस्य रूपाणि लक्ष्मणस्य च भारत। अभिदुद्राव रामं च लक्ष्मणं च दशाननः॥
en: (And) O Bharata, the ten-headed creating several Rakshasas wearing the shape of Rama and Lakshmana, rushed upon them.

sn: ततस्ते राममार्छन्तो लक्ष्मणं च क्षपाचराः। अभिपेतुस्तदा रामं प्रगृहीतशरासनाः॥
en: Then those night-rangers adverse to Rama and Lakshmana, armed with bows rushed against Rama.

sn: तां दृष्ट्वा राक्षसेन्द्रस्य मायाभिक्ष्वाकुनन्दनः। उवाच रामं सौमित्रिरसम्भ्रान्तो बृहद् वचः॥
en: (Then) the dauntless son of Sumitra, the descendant of Ikshvaku said to Rama these heroic words.

sn: जहीमान् राक्षसान् पापानात्मनः प्रतिरूपकान्। जधान रामस्तांश्चान्यानात्मनः प्रतिरूपकान्॥
en: "Kill those wicked-souled Rakshasas wearing your shape.” (Thereupon) Rama destroyed those Rakshasas resembling him in shape and (various) others also.

sn: ततो हर्यश्वयुक्तेन रथेनादित्यवर्चसा। उपतस्थे रणे रामं मातलिः शक्रसारथिः॥
en: Then, Matali, the charioteer of Shakra, came to Rama with a car, of sun-like splendour and yoked with tawny-coloured horses.

sn: मातलिरुवाच अयं हर्यश्वयुग जैत्रो मघोनः स्पन्दनोत्तमः। अनेन शक्रः काकुत्स्थ समरे दैत्यदानवान्॥ शतशः पुरुषव्याघ्र रथोदारेण जजिवान्। तदनेन नरव्याघ्र मया यत्तेन संयुगे।॥ स्पन्दनेन जहि क्षिप्रं रावणं मा चिरं कृथाः।
en: Matali said: "This excellent and victorious car yoked with this team of tawny horses belongs to Maghavana (Indra). O descendant of Kakustha, O foremost of men, riding on this splendid car Shakra slew in battle numerous Daityas and Danavas. Therefore, O most valiant of men, ascending this car guided by me, do you soon kill Ravana in battle. Do not make any delay."

sn: इत्युक्तो राघवस्तथ्यं वचोऽशङ्कत मातलेः॥ मायैषा राक्षसस्येति तमुवाच विभीषणः। नेयं माया नरव्याघ्र रावणस्य दुरात्मनः॥
en: Thus addressed, the descendant of Raghu, suspecting that this might be another illusion produced by the Rakshasas, doubted the truthful words of Matali. Vibhishana then said to him “O foremost of men, this is no illusion of the wicked-souled Ravana.

sn: तदातिष्ठ रथं शीघ्रमिममैन्द्रं महायुते। ततः प्रहृष्टः काकुत्स्थस्तथेत्युक्त्वा विभीषणम्॥
en: O highly-resplendent one, therefore do you soon ascend this car of Indra." Thereupon the descendant of Kakustha gladly saying to Vibhishana “be it so,"

sn: रथेनाभिपपाताथ दशग्रीवं रुषान्वितः। हाहाकृतानि भूतानि रावणे समभिद्रुते॥
en: And riding on that car rushed in great wrath against the ten-necked. (And) when Ravana flew (towards Rama) all the creatures began to wail loudly.

sn: सिंहनादाः सपटहा दिवि दिव्यास्तथानदन्। दशकन्धरराजसून्वोस्तथा युद्धमभून्महत्॥
en: And in the heavens the celestials sent forth roars like lions and sounded large drums. Then there took place a terrible encounter between the ten-necked and the prince (Rama).

sn: अलब्धोपममन्यत्र तयोरेव तथाभवत्। स रामाय महाघोरं विससर्ज निशाचरः॥
en: And that (fight) between them is without its parallel elsewhere. The night-ranger hurled at Rama an awfully-terrible.

sn: शूलमिन्द्राशनिप्रख्यं ब्रह्मदण्डभिवोद्यतम्। तच्छूलं सत्वरं रामश्चिच्छेद निशितैः शरैः॥
en: Javelin like the thunder-bolt of Indra and resembling the upraised Brahmdanda. (But) Rama quickly cut off that javelin with sharpened darts.

sn: तद् दृष्ट्वा दुष्करं कर्म रावणं भयमाविशत्। ततः क्रुद्धः ससर्जाशु दशग्रीवः शिताञ्छरान्॥ सहस्रायुतशो रामे शस्त्राणि विविधानि च। ततो भुशुण्डीः शूलानि मुसलानि परश्वधान्॥ शक्तीश्च विविधाकाराः शतमीश्च शितान् क्षुरान्।
en: Seeing that terrible feat Ravana was seized with dismay. (But) the ten-necked (soon) became wrathful and discharged at Rama thousands and tens of thousands of sharp arrows and numerous other weapons, (such as) maces, battle-axes, various kinds of darts, Shataghnis and sharp arrows.

sn: तां मायां विकृतां दृष्ट्वा दशग्रीवस्य रक्षसः॥ भयात् प्रदुदुवः सर्वे वानराः सर्वतोदिशम्।
en: Seeing the terrible illusions spread by the ten-necked Rakshasa, the monkeys got alarmed and ran away in all directions.

sn: ततः सुपत्रं सुमुखं हेमपुल शरोत्तमम्॥ तूणादादाय काकुत्स्थो ब्रह्मास्त्रेण युयोज ह। तं बाणवर्यं रामेण ब्रह्मास्त्रेणानुमन्त्रितम्॥ जहषुर्देवगन्धर्वा दृष्ट्वा शक्रपुरोगमाः। अल्पावशेषमायुश्च ततोऽमन्यन्त रक्षसः॥ ब्रह्मास्त्रोदीरणाच्छनोर्देवदानवकिन्नराः।
en: Thereupon, the descendant. of Kakustha, taking from his quiver an excellent arrow arrow adorned with beautiful feathers, golden wings and a beautiful face adjusted it to the Brahma weapon. When Rama inspired that arrow with the Mantras peculiar to the weapon of Brahma. All the celestials and the Gandharvas with Indra at their head were highly delighted. The gods, the Danavas and the Kinnaras, seeing the display of that Brahma weapon began to consider that a little only of their Rakshasa enemy's life was left to him.

sn: ततः ससर्ज तं रामः शरमप्रतिमौजसम्॥ रावणान्तकरं घोरं ब्रह्मदण्डमिवोद्यतम्।
en: Rama then discharged that of unrivalled splendour, dreadful, resembling the upraised Brahmadanda and destined to slay Ravana.

sn: मुक्तमात्रेण रामेण दूराकृष्टेन भारत॥ स तेन राक्षसश्रेष्ठः सरथः साश्चसारथिः। प्रजज्वाल महाज्वालेनाग्निनाभिपरिप्लुतः॥
en: And O Bharata, soon as Rama discharged it by drawing to a great length (his bowstring), the lord of the Rakshasas together with his horses and charioteer, enveloped in a great and blazing fire was burnt up.

sn: ततः प्रहृष्टास्त्रिदशाः सहगन्धर्वचारणाः। निहतं रावणं दृष्ट्वा रामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा॥
en: Then the celestials accompanied by the Gandharvas and the Charanas, beholding Ravana slain by Rama. of untiring exertions were highly delighted.

sn: तत्यजुस्तं महाभागं पञ्च भूतानि रावणम्। भ्रंशितः सर्वलोकेभ्यः स हि ब्रह्मास्त्रतेजसा॥
en: Then the five elements (i.e., earth water, air, fire and space) forsook Ravana; and he was deprived all of the worlds by the energy of the Brahma weapon.

sn: शरीरधातवो ह्यस्य मांसं रुधिरमेव च। नेशुर्ब्रह्मास्त्रनिर्दग्धा न च भस्माप्यदृश्यत॥
en: The ingredients of his body together with his flesh and blood were all so totally consumed by the Brahma weapon that the ashes even could not be seen.

sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच स हत्वा रावणं क्षुद्रं राक्षसेन्द्रं सुरद्विषम्। बभूव हृष्टः ससुहृद् रामः सौमित्रिणा सह॥
en: Markandeya said : Having killed the mean-minded Ravana, the lord of the Rakshasas and the enemy of the gods, great indeed was the joy of Rama and the son of Sumitra.

sn: ततो हते दशग्रीवे देवाः सर्षिपुरोगमाः। आशीर्भिर्जययुक्ताभिरानचुस्तं महाभुजम्॥
en: The ten-necked being slain, the celestials with the Rishis at their head eulogised the mighty-armed one by uttering blessings indicative of victory,

sn: रामं कमलपत्राक्षं तुष्टुवुः सर्वदेवताः। गन्धर्वाः पुष्पवर्षेच वाग्भिश्च त्रिदशालयाः॥
en: All the gods together with the Gandharvas and the inhabitants of the celestials regions delighted Rama gifted with eyes resembling lotus-petals by (chanting) hymns (in his praise) and showering flowers (over his head).

sn: पूजयित्वा यथा रामं प्रतिजग्मुर्यथागतम्। तन्महोत्सवसंकाशमासीदाकाशमच्युत॥
en: Having thus worshipped Rama, they returned to their respective abodes. And O being of everlasting fame, it then appeared as if a great carnival was being held in the firmament.

sn: ततो हत्वा दशग्रीवं लङ्कां रामो महायशाः। विभीषणाय प्रददौ प्रभुः परपुरञ्जयः॥
en: Then the highly-renowned lord Rama, the destroyer of his enemy's cities, having slain Ravana, gave Lanka to Vibhishana.

sn: ततः सीतां पुरस्कृत्य विभीषणपुरस्कृताम्। अविध्यो नाम सुप्रज्ञो वृद्धामात्यो विनिर्ययौ॥
en: Then Avindhya, the wise and old adviser of Ravana, preceded by Sita who was herself preceded by Vibhishana, set out from Lanka.

sn: उवाच च महात्मानं काकुत्स्थं दैन्यमास्थितः। प्रतीच्छ देवीं सद्वृत्तां महात्मञ्जानकीमिति॥
en: And he (Avindhya) with great humility said to the high-souled descendant of Kakustha, “O high-souled one, accept this divine lady, the daughter of Janaka, of spotless character."

sn: एतच्छ्रुत्वा वचस्तस्मादवतीर्य रथोत्तमात्। बाष्पेणापिहितां सीतां ददशेक्ष्वाकुनन्दनः॥
en: Hearing these words, Rama, the descendant of Kakustha got down from that excellent car and saw Sita weeping profusely.

sn: तां दृष्ट्वा चारुसर्वाङ्गी यानस्थां शोककर्शिताम् मलोपचितसर्वाङ्गी जटिलां कृष्णवाससम्॥
en: And beholding her of faultless proportions, seated in the vehicle weighed down with grief, covered all over with dirt, having matted locks and wearing a dirty cloth.

sn: उवाच रामो वैदेही परामर्शविशङ्कितः। गच्छ वैदेहि मुक्ता त्वं यत् कार्यं तन्मया कृतम्॥
en: Rama, suspecting the loss of her virtue, addressed the daughter of the king of Mithila thus, "O Princess of Videha, go (wheresoever you like)! You are now liberated (from your captivity). I have done my duty.

sn: मामासाद्य पतिं भद्रे न त्वं राक्षसवेश्मनि। जरां व्रजेथा इति मे निहतोऽसौ निशाचरः॥
en: O gentle creatures, I have killed that nightranger thinking that myself being your husband you should not grow old in the abode of the Rakshasa.

sn: कथं ह्यस्मद्विधो जातु जानन् धर्मविनिश्चयम्। परहस्तगतां नारी मुहूर्तमपि धारयेत्॥
en: How can men like us, well acquainted with moral duty, accept for even a moment, a woman carried off by another?

sn: सुवृत्तामसुवृत्तां वाप्यहं त्वामद्य मैथिलि। नोत्सहे परिभोगाय श्वावलीढं हविर्यथा॥
en: O daughter of the king of Mithila, whether you are of pure or impure character, I dare not enjoy you, who are now like sanctified butter lapped by a dog?"

sn: ततः सा सहसा बाला तच्छ्रुत्वा दारुणं वचः। पपात देवी व्यथिता निकृत्ता कदली यथा॥
en: That divine lady, hearing these cruel words (of Rama) was sorely afflicted with grief and suddenly fell down (to the ground) like a plantain tree torn up by the roots.

sn: योऽप्यस्या हर्षसम्भूतो मुखरागस्तदाभवत्। क्षणेन स पुनर्नष्टो निःश्वास इव दर्पणे॥
en: And the lively colour of her face sprung from her delight (at seeing Rama) as quickly disappeared as breath on a mirror.

sn: ततस्ते हरयः सर्वे तच्छ्रुत्वा रामभाषितम्। गतासुकल्पा निश्चेष्टा बभूवुः सहलक्ष्मणाः॥
en: Then, hearing these words of Rama all the monk ys together with Lakshmana became motionless as death itself.

sn: ततो देवो विशुद्धात्मा विमानेन चतुर्मुखः। पायोनिर्जगत्स्रष्टा दर्शयामास राघवम्॥
en: Then the pure-souled and the four-faced god (Brahma) the creator of the universe, who sprang from a lotus (on the nave of Vishnu), appeared before the descendant of Raghu on a chariot.

sn: शक्रश्चाग्निश्च वायुश्च यमो वरुण एव च। यक्षाधिपश्च भगवांस्तथा सप्तर्षयोऽमलाः॥
en: (Then) Shakra, Agni, Vayu, Yama, Varuna, the divine lord of the Yakshas, the seven holy sages (whom Brahma created first of all).

sn: राजा दशरथश्चैव दिव्यभास्वरमूर्तिमान्। विमानेन महाहेण हंसयुक्तेन भास्वता॥
en: And king Dasharatha also in his celestials appearance and robes and mounted on a highly-resplendent and bright car (appeared on the scene).

sn: ततोऽन्तरिक्षं तत् सर्वं देवगन्धर्वसंकुलम्। शुशुभे तारकाचित्रं शरदीव नभस्तलम्॥
en: Then the firmament crowded with the gods and the Gandharvas shone like the autumnal sky studded with stars.

sn: तत उत्थाय वैदेही तेषां मध्ये यशस्विनी। उवाच वाक्यं कल्याणी रामं पृथुलवक्षसम्॥
en: Then rising in the midst of them, the blessed and renowned princess of Videha spoke these words to the broad-chested Rama.

sn: राजपुत्र न ते दोषं करोमि विदिता हि ते। गतिः स्त्रीणां नराणां च शृणु चेदं वचो मम॥
en: "O prince, I do not blame you; (for) you are conversant with the ways of men and women. (Yet) listen to these my words.

sn: अन्तश्चरति भूतानां मातरिश्वा सदागतिः। स मे विमुञ्चतु प्राणान् यदि पापं चराम्यहम्॥
en: The air which is always in motion, moves within (the hearts of) all the creatures. If I have sinned, let it forsake my life.

sn: अग्निरापस्तथाऽऽकाशं पृथिवी वायुरेव च। विमुञ्चन्तु मम प्राणान् यदि पापं चराम्यहम्॥
en: And not only let air, but let fire, water, space and earth forsake my life if I have erred.

sn: यथाहं त्वदृते वीर नान्यं स्वप्नेऽप्यचिन्तयम्। तथा मे देवनिर्दिष्टस्त्वमेव हि पतिर्भव॥
en: As, O hero, I have thought of no other person than you even in my dreams, so you only be my husband as ordained by the gods."

sn: ततोऽन्तरिक्षे वागासीत् सुभगा लोकसाक्षिणी। पुण्या संहर्षणी तेषां वानराणां महात्मनाम्॥
en: Then a sacred and auspicious voice, joyful to the high-souled monkeys, was heard in the firmament which made the whole universe bear testimony to it.

sn: वायुरुवाच भो भो राघव सत्यं वै वायुरस्मि सदागतिः। अपापा मैथिली राजन् संगच्छ सह भार्यया॥
en: Vayu said: O descendant of Raghu, (what Sita has said) is true. I am the wind (god) and ever in motion. O king, the princess of Mithila is pure. Be united with your wife.

sn: अग्निरुवाच अहमन्तःशरीरस्थो भूतानां रघुनन्दन। सुसूक्ष्ममपि काकुत्स्थ मैथिली नापराध्यति॥
en: Agni said: O scion of Raghu's race, I am in the body of every creature. O descendant of Kakustha, the princess of Videha is thoroughly guiltless.

sn: वरुण उवाच रसा वै मतप्रसूता हि भूतदेहेषु राघव। अहं वै त्रां प्रब्रवीमि मैथिली प्रतिगृह्यताम्॥
en: Varuna said: O descendant of Raghu, the humours in animal bodies owe their existence to me. (Therefore) I ask you to accept the princess of Mithila.

sn: ब्रह्मोवाच पुत्र नैतदिहाश्चर्यं त्वयि राजर्षिधर्मणि। साधो सद्वृत्त काकुत्स्थ शृणु चेदं वचो मम॥
en: Brahma said: O descendant of Kakustha, O son of good character, this (behaviour) is not surprising on your part, (because) you are honest and know the duties of the royal sages: (Now) hear these my words.

sn: शत्रुरेष त्वया वीर देवगन्धर्वभोगिनाम्। यक्षाणां दानवानां च महर्षीणां च पातितः॥३.।।
en: O hero, this enemy of the gods, the Gandharvas, the Uragas, the Yakshas, the Danavas and the Maharshis has been destroyed by yol.

sn: अवध्यः सर्वभूतानां मत्प्रसादात् पुराभवत्। कस्माच्चित् कारणात् पापः कञ्चित् कालमुपेक्षितः॥
en: Formerly, he was made, through my favour, indestructible of all the creatures. And for some reason I spared that sinful wretch for sometime.

sn: वधार्थमात्मनस्तेन हृता सीता दुरात्मना। नलकूबरशापेन रक्षा चास्याः कृता मया॥
en: It was for his own destruction that Sita was carried off by that wicked-souled (wretch). (But) I protected her (from being violated) through Nalakubera's curse.

sn: यदि ह्यकामा सेवेत स्त्रियमन्यामपि ध्रुवम्। शतधास्य फलेन्मूर्धा इत्युक्तः सोऽभवत् पुरा॥
en: For, he (Ravana) was formerly cursed by that person (Nalakubera) to the effect that if he would enjoy any woman against her will, his head should surely be split into a hundred fragments.

sn: नात्र शङ्का त्वया कार्या प्रतीच्छेमां महाद्युते। कृतं त्वया महत् कार्यं देवानाममरप्रभ॥
en: O highly-resplendent one, O creature of divine effulgence, you need not entertain any doubt on this point. You have, (indeed) done a great service to the gods (by slaying Ravana).

sn: दशरथ उवाच प्रीतोऽस्मि वत्स भद्रं ते पिता दशरथोऽस्मिते। अनुजानामि राज्यं च प्रशाधि पुरुषोत्तम॥
en: Dasharatha said: My son, I am pleased with you. May you be blessed. I am your father Dasharatha. O foremost of men, I command you to govern your kingdom.

sn: राम उवाच अभिवादये त्वां राजेन्द्र यदि त्वं जनको मम। गमिष्यामि पुरीं रम्यामयोध्यां शासनात् तव॥
en: Rama said : O king of kings, if you are my father I bow down to you. I will repair to the beautiful city of Ayodhya at your command.

sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच तमुवाच पिता गच्छायोध्यां प्रशाधीति रामं रक्तान्तलोचनम्॥ सम्पूर्णानीह वर्षाणि चतुर्दश महाद्युते।
en: Markandeya said : O best of the Bharatas, well pleased with Rama, the corners of whose eyes were red, his father again said to him "O highly resplendent one, now that the fourteen years (of your exile) are complete, repair to Ayodhya and reign there."

sn: ततो देवान् नमस्कृत्य सुहृद्भिरभिनन्दितः॥ महेन्द्र इव पौलोम्या भार्यया स समेयिवान्।
en: Then, bowing down to the gods and congratulated by his friends, he was united with his wife like Mahendra with the daughter Pauloma.

sn: ततो वरं ददौ तस्मै ह्यविध्याय परंतपः॥ त्रिजटां चार्थमानाभ्यां योजयामास राक्षसीम्। भूयः प्रहृष्टो भरतर्षभ।
en: That tormentor of foes then conferred a boon on Avindhya. He then honoured and gave riches to the Rakshasa woman Trijata.

sn: तमुवाच ततो ब्रह्मा देवैः शक्रपुरोगमैः॥ कौसल्यामातरिष्टांस्ते वरानद्य ददानि कान्।
en: Then Brahma together with (all) the celestials headed by Shakra said to him, “O son of Kausalya, what desirable boons shall we bestow on you today"?

sn: वने रामः स्थितिं धर्मे शत्रुभिश्चापराजयम्॥ राक्षसैनिहतानां च वानराणां समुद्भवम्।
en: (Thereupon) Rama asked for these boons viz., devotion to virtue, victory over his enemies and the revival of those monkeys killed by the Rakshasas.

sn: ततस्ते ब्रह्मणा प्रोक्ते तथेति वचने तदा॥ समुत्तस्थुर्महाराज वानरा लब्धचेतसः।
en: And when Brahma had said "be it so," O mighty monarch, the monkeys brought back to life, rose up.

sn: सीता चापि महाभागा वरं हनुमते ददौ॥ रामकीर्त्या समं पुत्र जीवितं ते भविष्यति।
en: And the highly fortunate Sita also, conferred on Hanuman this boon, saying “My son, you will live as long as Rama's achievements.

sn: दिव्यास्त्वामुपभोगाश्च मत्प्रसादकृताः सदा॥ उपस्थास्यन्ति हनुमन्निति स्म हरिलोचन।
en: And through my favour, O yellow-eyed Hanuman, celestials dishes and drinks will over be within your reach.

sn: ततस्ते प्रेक्षमाणानां तेषामक्लिष्टकर्मणाम्॥ अन्तर्धानं ययुर्देवाः सर्वे शक्रपुरोगमाः।
en: Then in the very sight of those heroes of untiring achievements, all the gods with Shakra at their head vanished away.

sn: दृष्ट्वा रामं तु जानक्या संगतं शक्रसारथिः॥ उवाच परमप्रीतः सुहृन्मध्य इदं वचः। वगन्धर्वयक्षाणां मानुषासुरभोगिनाम्॥ अपनीतं त्वया दुःखमिदं सत्यपराक्रम।
en: Then the charioteer of Shakra seeing Rama united with the daughter of Janaka was well pleased and addressed him, in the midst of friends, these words. “O truly-powerful one, as you have done away with this distress of the gods, the Gandharvas, the Yakshas, the mortals, the Asuras and the serpents.

sn: सदेवासुरगन्धर्वा यक्षराक्षसपन्नगाः॥ कथयिष्यन्ति लोकास्त्वां यावद् भूमिर्धरिष्यति।
en: Therefore always the Asuras, Gandharvas, Yakshas, Rakshasas and the Punagas and all the world will speak (well) of you so long as the world will exist.

sn: इत्येवमुक्त्वानुज्ञाप्य रामं शस्त्रभृतां वरम्॥ सम्पूज्यापाक्रमत् तेन रथेनादित्यवर्चसा।
en: Saying these words to Rama, the foremost of the wielders of weapons and taking leave of and paying his respects to him (matali) set out (for the celestials regions) on that car of sunlike splendour.

sn: ततः सीतां पुरस्कृत्य रामः सौमित्रिणा सह॥ सुग्रीवप्रमुखैश्चैव सहितः सर्ववानरैः। विधाय रक्षां लङ्कायां विभीषणपुरस्कृतः॥ संततार पुनस्तेन सेतुना मकरालयम्। पुष्पकेण विमानेन खेचरेण विराजता॥ कामगेन यथामुख्यैरमात्यैः संवृतो वशी।
en: Then Rama with Sita in this front and accompanied by the son of Sumitra and by all the monkeys with Sugriva at their head and preceded by Vibhishana and taking steps for the protection of Lanka and one that selfcontained (Rama) surrounded by his chief advisers in order of precedence rode on that sky-ranging car Pushpaka, moving anywhere at will re-crossed the abode of the Makaras (i.e. the ocean) by means of the same bridge.

sn: ततस्तीरे समुद्रस्य यत्र शिश्ये स पार्थिवः॥ तत्रैवोवास धर्मात्मा सहितः सर्ववानरैः।
en: Then that virtuous lord of the earth together with all the monkeys took up his (temporary) quarter son that portion of the sea-shore where had lain down before (on a bed of Kusha grass to invoke the aid of the ocean).

sn: अथैनान् राघवः काले समानीयाभिपूजय च।॥ विसर्जयामास तदा रत्नैः संतोष्य सर्वशः।
en: Then the descendant of Raghu bringing all those (monkeys) together at the due time worshipped them all. He then dismissed them all after having satisfied them with gifts of gems.

sn: गतेषु वानरेन्द्रेषु गोपुच्छर्केषु तेषु च।॥ सुग्रीवसहितो रामः किष्किन्धां पुनरागमत्।
en: Those foremost of monkeys, the apes with tails like cows and the bears having departed, Rama reentered Kishkindha with Sugriva.

sn: विभीषणेनानुगतः सुग्रीवसहितस्तदा॥ पुष्पकेण विमानेन वैदेह्या दर्शयन् वनम्। किष्किन्धांत समासाद्य रामः प्रहरतां ववः॥ अङ्गदं कृतकर्माणं यौवराज्येऽभ्यषेचयत्।
en: (And on his way from the sea-shore to Kishkindha) Rama in company with Vibhishana and Sugriva, riding on the car Pushpaka showed the princess of Videha all the woods. Having reached Kishkindha, Rama, the most efficient of all smiters, made the successful Angada prince-regent.

sn: ततस्तैरेव सहितो रामः सौमित्रिणा सह॥ यथागतेन मार्गेण प्रययौ स्वपुरं प्रति।
en: (He) then, together with all these and accompanied by the son of Sumitra, set out for his capital by the same route by which he had come.

sn: अयोध्यां स समासाद्य पुरीं राष्ट्रपतिस्ततः॥ भरताय हनूमन्तं दूतं प्रास्थापयत् तदा।
en: Having reached Ayodhya the king sent Hanuman as his messenger to Bharata.

sn: लक्षयित्वेङ्गितं सर्वं प्रियं तस्मै निवेद्य वै॥ वायुपुत्रे पुनः प्राप्ते नन्दिग्राममुपागमत्।
en: (Hanuman) then communicated to him the happy news on having observed his external signs and (gestures). And the son of the windgod having come back, (Rama himself) went to Nandigrama.

sn: स तत्र मलदिग्धाङ्गं भरतं चीरवाससम्॥ अचतः पादुके कृत्वा ददर्शासीनमासने।
en: He there saw Bharata covered with dirt, attired in barks of trees and seated on the throne with (Rama's) shoes before him.

sn: संगतो भरतेनाथ शत्रुघ्नेन च वीर्यवान्॥ राघवः सहसौमित्रिर्मुमुदे भरतर्षभ।
en: Then, O best of the Bharatas, the mighty descendant of Raghu together with the son of Sumitra experienced a great delight on being joined with Bharata and Shatrughna.

sn: ततो भरतशत्रुघ्नौ समेतौ गुरुणा तदा॥ वैदेह्या दर्शनेनोभौ प्रहर्षं समवापतुः।
en: And Bharata and Shatrughna too being united with their eldest brother and beholding the princess of Mithila rejoiced exceedingly.

sn: तस्मै तद् भरतो राज्यमागतायातिसत्कृतम्। न्यासं निर्यातयामास युक्तः परमया मुदा॥
en: Having paid his respects to Rama who had returned (from exile) Bharata with great pleasure made over the kingdom, to him, which he governed as a trustee (for Rama).

sn: ततस्तं वैष्णवे शूरं नक्षत्रेऽभिमतेऽहनि। वसिष्ठो वामदेवश्च सहितावभ्यषिञ्चताम्॥
en: Then Vasishtha together with Vamadeva installed that hero, at the eighth muhurta (a muhurta is equal to two dandas that is 4 minutes), of day under the constellation Shravana.

sn: सोऽभिषिक्तः कपिश्रेष्ठं सुग्रीवं ससुहृज्जनम्। विभीषणं च पौलस्त्यमन्वजानाद् गृहान् प्रति॥
en: Being installed (on the throne) Rama gave his permission to that foremost of monkeys, Sugriva together with his friends and also to Vibhishana, the son of Pulastya to return to their homes.

sn: अभ्यर्च्य विविधैर्भोगैः प्रीतियुक्तौ मुदा युतौ। समाधायेतिकर्तव्यं दुःखेन विससर्ज ह॥
en: Having entertained those two (friends) Sugriva and Vibhishana who were well pleased and exceedingly glad, with various sorts of foods and drinks and having done his duty suitable to the occasion he dismissed them with a heavy heart.

sn: पुष्पकं च विमानं तत् पूजयित्वा स राघवः। प्रादाद् वैश्रवणायैव प्रीत्या स रघुनन्दनः॥
en: And having worshipped the car Pushpaka, the descendant of Raghu, gladly gave it back to Kubera.

sn: ततो देवर्षिसहितः सरितं गोमतीमनु। दशाश्वमेधानाजढे जारूथ्यान् स निरर्गलान्॥
en: Then assisted by that divine sage (Vasishtha) he safely celebrated ten horse sacrifices on the banks of the (river) Gomati by offering to the Brahmanas presents thrice (as much as usual).

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The consolation of Yudhishthira (by Markandeya
sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच एवमेतन्महाबाहो रामेणामिततेजसा। प्राप्तं व्यसनमत्युचं वनवासकृतं पुरा॥
en: Markandeya said: O mighty-armed one, thus, in days of old Rama of unrivalled energy had experienced such a terrible disaster owing to his being exiled in the forests.

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The consolation of Yudhishthira (by Markandeya
sn: मा शुचः पुरुषव्याघ्र क्षत्रियोऽसि परंतप। बाहुवीर्याश्रिते मार्गे वर्तसे दीप्तनिर्णये॥
en: O most valiant of men, do not (therefore) lament (over your misfortune); for, O tormentor of foes, you are a Kshatriya. You are journeying along the path which calls forth the prowess of arms and which is calculated to lead to sure success.

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The consolation of Yudhishthira (by Markandeya
sn: न हि ते वृजिनं किंचिद् वर्तते परमण्वपि। अस्मिन् मार्गे निषीदेयुः सेन्द्रा अपि सुरासुराः॥
en: (By following this path) you have not incurred even an atom of sin. The gods together with Indra and the Asuras have (sometimes) to adopt this path.

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The consolation of Yudhishthira (by Markandeya
sn: संहत्य निहतो वृत्रो मरुद्भिर्वलापाणिना। नमुचिश्चैव दुर्धर्षो दीर्घजिह्वा च राक्षसी॥
en: (It was by adopting this path) that the wielder of the thunderbolt (Indra) together with the Marutas slew Vritra, the invincible Namuchi and the Rakshasa female Dirghajivha.

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The consolation of Yudhishthira (by Markandeya
sn: सहायवति सर्वार्थाः संतिष्ठन्तीह सर्वशः। किं नु तस्याजितं संख्ये यस्य भ्राता धनंजयः॥
en: In this world, he, that is backed up, has all his desires gratified. What is there that cannot be overcome by him in battle whose brother is Dhananjaya?

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The consolation of Yudhishthira (by Markandeya
sn: अयं च बलिनां श्रेष्ठो भीमो भीमपराक्रमः। युवानौ च महेष्वासौ वीरौ माद्रवतीसुतौ॥
en: This Bhima of terrible prowess is the strongest of the strong; and the two youthful and heroic sons of Madravati are mighty bowmen.

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The consolation of Yudhishthira (by Markandeya
sn: एभिः सहायैः कस्मात् त्वं विषीदसि परंतप। य इमे वलिाणः सेनां जयेयुः समरुद्गणाम्॥
en: Why, then, O tormentor of foes, do you grieve, since you have such supporters, as are capable of vanquishing the forces of the wielder of the thunderbolt together with the Marutas?

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The consolation of Yudhishthira (by Markandeya
sn: त्वमप्येभिर्महेष्वासैः सहायैर्देवरूपिभिः। विजेष्यसे रणे सर्वानमित्रान् भरतर्षभ॥
en: O best of the Bharatas, with these mighty bowmen of celestials appearance you will surely conquer in battle all your enemies.

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The consolation of Yudhishthira (by Markandeya
sn: इतश्च त्वमिमां पश्य सैन्धवेन बलिना वीर्यमत्तेन हृतामेभिर्महात्मभिः॥ आनीतां द्रौपदी कृष्णां कृत्वा कर्म सुदुष्करम्। जयद्रथं च राजानं विजितं वशमागतम्॥
en: Just see, these high-minded (brothers of yours) after achieving terrible feats (of arms) have rescued this daughter of Drupada carried off by the evil-minded Saindhava puffed up with pride and power. (And they) have also vanquished and reduced to subjection king Jayadratha.

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The consolation of Yudhishthira (by Markandeya
sn: असहायेन रामेण वैदेही पुनराहता। हत्वा संख्ये दशग्रीवं राक्षसं भीमविक्रमम्॥
en: Again, the princess of Videha was rescued by Rama with almost no allies after having slain in battle the terribly-powerful ten-necked.

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The consolation of Yudhishthira (by Markandeya
sn: दुरात्मना। यस्य शाखामृगा मित्राण्यक्षाः कालमुखास्तथा। जात्यन्तरगता राजन्नेतद् बुद्ध्यानुचिन्तय॥
en: Consider this, O king, by (the exercise of your) intelligence, that his (Rama's) only allies were the bears and the monkeys born in other orders of creation.

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The consolation of Yudhishthira (by Markandeya
sn: तस्मात् स त्वं कुरुश्रेष्ठ मा शुचो भरतर्षभ। त्वद्विधा हि महात्मानो न शोचन्ति परंतप॥
en: Therefore, O best of the Kurus, O most exalted of the Bharata, do not grieve over all this. O tormentor of foes, high-minded men like you never give way to sorrow.

parva: RAMOPAKHYANA PARVA)-Continued The consolation of Yudhishthira (by Markandeya
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमाश्वासितो राजा मार्कण्डेयेन धीमता। त्यक्त्वा दुःखमदीनात्मा पुनरप्येनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Thus consoled by the intelligent Markandeya, the large-hearted king giving up his sorrow again spoke to Markandeya.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच नात्मानमनुशोचामि नेमान् भ्रातृन् महामुने। हरणं चापि राज्यस्य यथेमां दुपदात्मजाम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said : O great sage, I do not grieve so much for myself or for these my brothers or for the loss of my kingdom as (I do) for this daughter of Drupada.

sn: द्यूते दुरात्मभिः क्लिष्टा: कृष्णया तारिता वयम्। जयद्रथेन च पुनर्वनाच्चापि हृता बलात्॥
en: When the wicked-souled (sons of Dhritarashtra) gave us pain at the game of dice we were delivered by Krishna. (But) Jayadratha forcibly carried her off even from the forest.

sn: अस्ति सीमन्तिनी काचिद् दृष्टपूर्वापि वा श्रुता। पतिव्रता महाभागा यथेयं दुपदात्मजा॥
en: Have you ever seen or heard of a lady as highly fortunate and as devoted to her husband as the daughter of Dripada?

sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच शृणु राजन् कुलस्त्रीणां महाभाग्यं युधिष्ठिर। सर्वमेतद् यथा प्राप्तं सावित्र्या राजकन्यया।॥
en: Markandeya said : Hear, O king Yudhishthira, how the princess Savitri attained to all the high virtues of chaste ladies.

sn: आसीन्मनेषु धर्मात्मा राजा परमधार्मिकः। ब्रह्मण्यश्च महात्मा च सत्यसंधो जितेन्द्रियः॥
en: Among the Madra there was a pious, exceedingly virtuous and a high-souled king devoted to the ministrations of the Brahmanas, firm in promise and of subdued passions.

sn: यज्वा दानपतिर्दक्षः पौरजानपदप्रियः। पार्थिवोऽश्वपति म सर्वभूतहिते रतः॥
en: This king, who was called Ashvapati was ever engaged in sacrifices, the foremost of the benevolent able loved by the people of the cities and provinces and was devoted to the welfare of all creatures.

sn: क्षमावाननपत्यश्च सत्यवान् विजितेन्द्रियः। अतिक्रान्तेन वयसा संतापमुपजग्मिवान्॥
en: But that truthful and self-controlled monarch having no offspring, was much pained when he was far advanced in years.

sn: अपत्योत्पादनार्थं च तीव्र नियममास्थितः। काले परिमिताहारो ब्रह्मचारी जितेन्द्रियः॥
en: And in order to be blessed with children, he observed rigid vows, partook of moderate food at the proper time, led the Brahmacharya (mode of) life and subdued his passions.

sn: हुत्वा शतसहस्रं स सावित्र्या राजसत्तमः। षष्ठे षष्ठे तदा काले बभूव मितभोजनः॥
en: That most exalted of kings (daily) offered ten thousand oblations to Savitri and partook of a moderate food at the sixth portion of the day.

sn: एतेन नियमेनासीद् वर्षाण्यष्टादशैव तु। पूर्णे त्वष्टादशे वर्षे सावित्री तुष्टिमभ्यगात्॥
en: He observed (all) these vows for eighteen years and when the eighteenth year was complete, Savitri was pleased with him.

sn: रूपिणी तु तदा राजन् दर्शयामास तं नृपम्। अग्निहोत्रात् समुत्थाय हर्षेण महतान्विता। उवाच चैनं वरदा वचनं पार्थिवं तदा॥
en: And O monarch, rising from the sacrificial fire with great delight, she appeared before the king and desirous of conferring boons addressed the monarch thus,

sn: सावित्र्युवाच ब्रह्मचर्येण शुद्धेन दमेन नियमेन च। सर्वात्मना च भक्त्या च तुष्टास्मि तव पार्थिव॥
en: Savitri said: "O king, I have been pleased with your Brahmacharya life, purity, self-control, observance of vows and all your endeavours and devotion.

sn: वरं वृणीष्वाश्वपते मद्रराज यदीप्सितम्। न प्रमादश्च धर्मेषु कर्तव्यस्ते कथञ्चन॥
en: O Ashvapati, O king of Madra, ask for whatever boon you desire. You should, however by no means disrespect virtue.

sn: अश्वपतिरुवाच अपत्यार्थः समारम्भः कृतो धर्मेप्सया मया। पुत्रा मे बहवो देवि भवेयुः कुलभावनाः॥
en: Ashvapati said : Desirous of attaining virtue, I have observed all these vows so that I may have children. O goddess, many numerous sons, woryour of my race, be born to me.

sn: तुष्टासि यदि मे देवि वरमेतं वृणोम्यहम्। संतानं परमो धर्म इत्याहुर्मां द्विजातयः॥
en: O goddess, if you are pleased with me, then I pray for this boon. The Brahmanas have told me that one attains to the crowning merit by having children.

sn: सावित्र्युवाच पूर्वमेव मया राजन्नभिप्रायमिमं तव। ज्ञात्वा पुत्रार्थमुक्तो वै भगवांस्ते पितामहः॥
en: Savitri said : Aware of your intentions before hand, I spoke about your sons to the divine Grandsire (Brahma).

sn: प्रसादाच्चैव तस्मात् ते स्वयम्भुविहिताद् भुवि। कन्या तेजस्विनी सौम्य क्षिप्रमेव भविष्यति॥
en: O virtuous one, you will, through the grace of that self-existent lord, have soon a highlyenergetic daughter on earth.

sn: उत्तरं च न ते किंचिद् व्याहर्तव्यं कथञ्चन। पितामहनिसर्गेण तुष्टा ह्येतद् ब्रवीमि ते॥
en: I gladly tell you all this at the command of the Grandsire; you need not, therefore, make any reply.

sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच स तथेति प्रतिज्ञाय सावित्र्या वचनं नृपः। प्रसादयामास पुनः क्षिप्रमेतद् भविष्यति॥
en: Markandeya said : The king then bowing assent to the words of Savitri and saying "be it so," pleased her again and said "may this soon happen."

sn: अन्तर्हितायां सावित्र्यां जगाम स्वपुरं नृपः। स्वराज्ये चावसद् वीरः प्रजा धर्मेण पालयन्॥
en: When Savitri had disappeared the king entered his own city. And that hero began to dwell in his kingdom and govern his subjects righteously.

sn: कस्मिंश्चित् तु गते काले स राजा नियतव्रतः। ज्येष्ठायां धर्मचारिण्यां महिष्यां गर्भमादधे॥
en: Some time having elapsed that king observant of vows, begot offspring in the womb of his eldest queen devoted to religion.

sn: राजपुत्र्यास्तु गर्भः स मालव्या भरतर्षभ। व्यवर्धत तदा शुक्ले तारापतिरिवाम्बरे॥
en: O best of the Bharata, the embryo in the womb of the princess Malavi began to increase like the lord of the stars in heaven, during the lighted fortnight.

sn: प्राप्ते काले तु सुषुवे कन्यां राजीवलोचनाम्। क्रियाश्च तस्या मुदितश्चक्रे च नृपसत्तमः॥
en: And at the proper time she gave birth to a daughter with eyes resembling lotus. And that best of kings gladly performed her natal rites.

sn: सावित्र्या प्रीतया दत्ता सावित्र्या हुत्या ह्यपि। सावित्रीत्येव नामास्याश्चक्रुर्विप्रास्तथा पिता॥
en: And as Savitri gladly gave (him) that daughter on account of the king (daily) offering her oblations, both her father and the Brahmanas named her Savitri.

sn: सा विग्रहवतीव श्रीळवर्धत नृपात्मजा। कालेन चापि सा कन्या यौवनस्था बभूव ह॥
en: The king's daughter (gradually) grew up like the very embodiment of Sri (Lakshmi). And that damsel, in time stepped into youth.

sn: तां सुमध्यां पृथुश्रोणी प्रतिमां काञ्चनीमिव। प्राप्तेयं देवकन्येति दृष्ट्वा सम्मेनिरे जनाः॥
en: Seeing that slender-waisted damsel of robust hips and looking like a golden image, people thought "we have got a goddess."

sn: तां तु पद्मपलाशाक्षीं ज्वलन्तीमिव तेजसा। न कश्चिद् वरयामास तेजसा प्रतिवारितः॥
en: And oppressed by her, energy none could marry that girl of lotus-like eyes who seemed as if blazing in splendour.

sn: अथोपोष्य शिर:स्नाता देवतामभिगम्य सा। हुत्वाग्नि विधिवद् विप्रान् वाचयामास पर्वणि॥
en: Then on a Parva day, Savitri, observing fasts, bathing her head and approaching the family deity caused the Brahmanas to offer oblations to the sacrificial fire in accordance with due rites.

sn: ततः सुमनसः शेषाः प्रतिगृह्य महात्मनः। पितुः समीपमगमद् देवी श्रीरिव रूपिणी॥
en: Then taking the flowers and garlands with which she worshipped the deity, Savitri looking like the very embodiment of Sri, repaired to her high-souled sire.

sn: साभिवाद्य पितुः पादौ शेषाः पूर्वं निवेद्य च। कृताञ्जलिर्वरारोहा नृपतेः पार्श्वमास्थिता।॥
en: And bowing down to the feet of her father and offering him those flowers and garlands, that highly beautiful damsel with joined-hands stood beside the king.

sn: यौवनस्थां तां दृष्ट्वा स्वां सुतां देवरूपिणीम्। अयाच्यमानां च वरैर्नृपतिर्दुःखितोऽभवत्॥
en: Seeing that his daughter (beautiful), as a goddess, attained her puberty and was not courted by suitors, the king became sorry.

sn: तु राजोवाच पुत्रि प्रदानकालस्ते न च कश्चिद् वृणोति माम्। स्वयमन्विच्छ भर्तारं गुणैः सदृशमात्मनः॥
en: The king said: Daughter, the time for giving you away is arrived. (But) none asks me (for your hand). Do you, (therefore) seek for a husband as qualified as you.

sn: प्रार्थितः पुरुषो यश्च स निवेद्यस्त्वया मम। विमृश्याहं प्रदास्यामि वरय त्वं यथेप्सितम्॥
en: Speak of that person, to me, whom you desire (for your husband). Choose, whom you like, for your husband. I will (afterwards) on (due) deliberation give you away (to him).

sn: श्रुतं हि धर्मशास्त्रेषु पठ्यमानं द्विजातिभिः। तथा त्वमपि कल्याणि गदतो मे वचः शृणु॥
en: Hear, O auspicious girl, as I tell you the words, which I have heard the twice-born ones to recite from the sacred books.

sn: अप्रदाता पिता वाच्यो वाच्यश्चानुपयन् पतिः। मृते भर्तरि पुत्रश्च वाच्यो मातुररक्षिता॥
en: That father who does not give away his daughter in marriage, is blamed. That husband who does not enjoy his wife during her courses is also blamed. And that son, who does not maintain his mother in her widowhood, meets with disgrace.

sn: इदं मे वचनं श्रुत्वा भर्तुरन्वेषणो त्वर। देवतानां यथा वाच्यो न भवेयं तथा कुरु॥
en: Hearing these my words do you speedily go in search of a husband. Act in such a way that we may not be blamed by the gods.

sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच एवमुक्त्वा दुहितरं तथा वृद्धांश्च मन्त्रिणः। व्यादिदेशानुयात्रं च गम्यतां चेत्यचोदयत्॥
en: Markandeya said : Addressing thus his daughter and his old ministers, (the king) gave orders to make preparations (for their departure) and said "go".

sn: साभिवाद्य पितुः पादौ वीडितेव मनस्विनी। पितुर्वचनमाज्ञाय निर्जगामाविचारितम्॥
en: (Thereupon), she, (gentle and meek) as a fernale ascetic, bashfully bowing down to the feet of her father, set out without hesitation, in obedience to the commands of her sire.

sn: सा हैमं रथमास्थाय स्थविरैः सचिवैर्वृता। तपोवनानि रम्याणि राजर्षीणां जगाम ह॥
en: Seated on a car of gold and surrounded by the ministers, she visited the delightful hermitage of the royal sages.

sn: मान्यानां तत्र वृद्धानां कृत्वा पादाभिवादनम्। वनानि क्रमशस्तात सर्वाण्येवाभ्यगच्छत॥
en: O son, there bowing down to the feet of the elders and the revered, she visited all the forests one after the other.

sn: एवं तीर्थेषु सर्वेषु धनोत्सर्गं नृपात्मजा। कुर्वती द्विजमुख्यानां तं तं देशं जगाम ह॥
en: Thus giving away riches in all the Tirthas, the king's daughter travelled over all those places inhabited by the foremost of the twiceborn ones.

sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच अथ मद्राधिपो राजा नारदेन समागतः। उपविष्टः सभामध्ये कथायोगेन भारत॥
en: Markandeya said : OBharata, (one day) when that monarch, the king of the Madra, joined by Narada and seated in the midst of his court, was conversing with him.

sn: ततोऽभिगम्य तीर्थानि सर्वाण्येवाश्रमांस्तथा। आजगाम पितुर्वेश्म सावित्री सह मन्त्रिभिः॥
en: Savitri, after visiting all the Tirthas and the hermitages, came to the abode of her father together with the ministers.

sn: नारदेन सहासीनं सा दृष्ट्वा पितरं शुभा। उभयोरेव शिरसा चक्रे पादाभिवादनम्॥
en: That auspicious one, seeing her father seated with Narada, bowed down to the feet of both with her head.

sn: नारद उवाच क्व गदाभूत् सुतेयं ते कुतश्चैवागता नृप। किमर्थं युवती भत्रे न चैनां सम्प्रयच्छसि॥
en: Narada said: O king, where did this your daughter go to and where does she come from? Why do you not bestow this youthful (damsel) on a husband?

sn: अश्वपतिरुवाच कार्येण खल्वनेनैव प्रेषितायैव चागता। एतस्याः शृणु देवर्षे भर्तारं योऽनया वृतः॥
en: Ashyapati said : She was sent on that very business and she is just now come. Hear, O divine sage, from her, whom she has chosen for her husband.

sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच सा ब्रूहि विस्तरेणेति पित्रा संचोदिता शुभा। तदैव तस्य वचनं प्रतिगृह्येदमब्रवीत्॥
en: Markandeya said : That auspicious one, at the command of her father to relate everything in detail, regarded his words like those of a god and said thus,

sn: सावित्र्युवाच आसीच्छाल्वेषु धर्मात्मा क्षत्रियः पृथिवीपतिः। धुमत्सेन इति ख्यातः पश्चाच्चान्धो बभूव ह॥
en: Savitri said : There was, in Shalya, a pious Kshatriya king, Dyumatsena by name, who lost his eyes in course of time.

sn: विनष्टचक्षुषस्तस्य बालपुत्रस्य धीमतः। सामीप्येन हृतं राज्यं छिद्रेऽस्मिन् पूर्ववैरिणा॥
en: That intellectual (monarch) who had an only infant son, having lost his eyes, a neighbouring enemy who bore him an old grudge, taking advantage of his blindness, seized his kingdom.

sn: स बालवत्सया साधु भार्यया प्रस्थितो वनम्। महारण्यं गतश्चापि तपस्तेपे महाव्रतः॥
en: (Deprived of his kingdom), he (Dyumatsena) accompanied by his wife with the infant at her breast, retired to the woods. And having gone to a great forest, he, observant of rigid vows, began to practise asceticism.

sn: तस्य पुत्र पुरे जातः संवृद्धश्च तपोवने। सत्यवाननुरूपो मे भर्तेति मनसा वृतः॥
en: His son, Satyavana (by name), born in the city and brought up in the hermitage, is my fit husband and I have wedded him in my mind.

sn: नारद उवाच अहो बत महत् पापं सावित्र्या नृपते कृतम्। अजानन्त्या यदनया गुणवान् सत्यवान् वृतः॥
en: Narada said: Alas, O king, Savitri has done a very foolish act in as much as she, has through ignorance, chosen for her husband, Satyavana endued with (high) qualities.

sn: सत्यं वदत्यस्य पिता सत्यं माता प्रभाषते। तथास्य ब्राह्मणाश्चक्रुर्नामैतत् सत्यवानिति॥
en: It is because his father is (ever) truthful and his mother speaks the truth, that the Brahmanas have named him Satyavana (i.e. truthful).

sn: बालस्याश्वाः प्रियाश्चास्य करोत्यश्वांश्च मृन्मयान्। चित्रेऽपि विलिखत्यश्वांश्चित्राश्व इति चोच्यते॥
en: In his boyhood he was very fond of horses, made horses of clay and painted them. Therefore he is (sometimes) called Chitrashva (i.e. one who paints horses)

sn: राजोवाच अपीदानी स तेजस्वी बुद्धिमान् वा नृपात्मजः। क्षमावानपि वा शूरः सत्यवान् पितृवत्सलः॥
en: The King said: Is now the prince Satyavana, who is attached to his father, energetic, intelligent, forgiving and brave?

sn: नारद उवाच विवस्वानिव तेजस्वी बृहस्पतिसमो मतौ। महेन्द्र इव वीस्थ वसुधेव समन्वितः॥
en: Narada said: He is energetic as Vibhavasu (the sun), wise as Brihaspati, heroic as Mahendra and forgiving as the earth.

sn: अश्वपतिरुवाच अपि राजात्मजो दाता ब्रह्मण्यश्चापि सत्यवान्। रूपवानप्युदारो वाप्यथवा प्रियदर्शनः॥
en: Ashvapati said : Is the king's son, Satyavana, charitable, devoted to the Brahmanas, handsome, largehearted and of amiable appearance?

sn: नारद उवाच सांकृते रन्तिदेवस्य स्वशक्त्या दानतः समः। ब्रह्मण्यः सत्यवादी न शिबिरौशीनरो यथा॥
en: Narada said : With regard to charity commensurate with his means, he is equal to Rantideva, the son of Sankriti and he is as devoted to the Brahmanas and as truthful as Shibi, the son of Ushinara.

sn: ययातिरिव चोदारः सोमवत् प्रियदर्शनः। रूपेणान्यतमोऽश्विभ्यां धुमत्सेनसुतो बली॥
en: The heroic Satyavana is equal to Yayati in magnanimity, is as lovely to look at as the moon and is as beautiful as either of the twin Ashvinis.

sn: स दान्तः स मृदुः शूरः स सत्यः संयतेन्द्रियः। स मैत्रः सोऽनसूयश्च स ह्रीमान् द्युतिमांश्च सः॥
en: He is (moreover) possessed of self-restraint, is meek, heroic, truthful, of subdued senses, faithful to his friends, free from malice, modest and patient.

sn: नित्यशश्चार्जवं तस्मिन् स्थितिस्तस्यैव च ध्रुवा। संक्षेपतस्तपोवृद्धैः शीलवृद्धश्च कथ्यते॥
en: To be brief, men of great asceticism and of high character say that he (Satyavana) is ever plain and firm in honour.

sn: अश्वपतिरुवाच गुणैरुपेतं सर्वैस्तं भगवन् प्रब्रवीषि मे। दोषानष्यस्य मे ब्रूहि यदि सन्तीह केचन॥
en: Ashvapati said: O adorable one, you have described him as possessed of all noble qualities. Now tell me of his defects, if there be any.

sn: नारद उवाच एक एवास्य दोषो हि गुणानाक्रम्य तिष्ठति। स च दोषः प्रयत्नेन न शक्यमतिवर्तितुम्॥
en: Narada said: He has only one defect which has eclipsed all his qualities and which even by the most vigorous exertions cannot be rooted out.

sn: एको दोषोऽस्ति नान्योऽस्य सोऽद्यप्रभृति सत्यवान्। संवत्सरेण क्षीणायुहन्यासं करिष्यति॥
en: He has only one defect and no other. Satyavana who has a little of life in store for him, will, within a year from this day, breathe his last.

sn: राजोवाच एहि सावित्रि गच्छस्व अन्यं वरय शोभने। तस्य दोषो महानेको गुणानाक्रम्य च स्थितः॥
en: The King said: O beautiful Savitri, go and seek another for your husband. He has a great defect which lies surpassing all his merits.

sn: यथा मे भगवानाह नारदो देवस्तकृतः। संवत्सरेण सोऽल्पायुहन्यासं करिष्यति॥
en: The divine Narada, who is honoured by the celestials, tells me that within a year, he, of short life, will give up the ghost.

sn: सावित्र्युवाच सकृदंशो निपतति सकृत् कन्या प्रदीयते। सकृदाह ददानीति त्रीण्येतानि सकृत् सकृत्॥
en: Savitri said: The die falls but once and the daughter can once be bestowed. The words "I bestow" are uttered but once and once only these three things occur.

sn: दीर्घायुरथवाल्पायुः सगुणो निर्गुणोऽपि वा। सकृद् वृतो मया भर्ता न द्वितीयं वृणोम्यहम्॥
en: Whether his life be long or short, whether he be gifted with (noble) qualities or destitute of them, I have for once, chosen him for my husband and will not select any other a second time.

sn: मनसा निश्चयं कृत्वा ततो वाचाभिधीयते। क्रियते कर्मणा पश्चात् प्रमाणं मे मनस्ततः॥
en: Having (first) settled a thing in mind, it is then expressed in words and is ultimately given effect to by (external) acts. My (own) mind is a proof of this.

sn: नारद उवाच स्थिरा बुद्धिर्नरश्रेष्ठ सावित्र्या दुहितुस्तव। नैष वारयितुं शक्या धर्मादस्मात् कथंचन॥
en: Narada said: O best of men, your daughter is firm in her resolve. It is impossible to wean her away from virtue.

sn: नान्यस्मिन् पुरुषे सन्ति ये सत्यवति वै गुणाः। प्रदानमेव तस्मान्मे रोचते दुहितुस्तव॥
en: The qualities that are present in Satyavana are wanting in any other person. Therefore I command the bestowal of your daughter (on Satyavana).

sn: राजोवाच अविचाल्यं तदुक्तं यत् तथ्यं भगवता वचः। करिष्याम्येतदेवं च गुरुर्हि भगवान् मम॥
en: The King said: The words of your respectable self are true and should never be dishonoured. Since O adorable one, you are my preceptor I will do as directed by you.

sn: नारद उवाच अविघ्नमस्तु सावित्र्याः प्रदाने दुहितुस्तव। साधयिष्याम्यहं तावत् सर्वेषां भद्रमस्तु वः॥
en: Narada said: May your daughter Savitri, be given away without any obstruction. I shall now go away. May you be all happy.

sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच एवमुक्त्वा समुत्पत्य नारदस्त्रिदिवं गतः। राजापि दुहितुः सज्जं वैवाहिकमकारयत्॥
en: Markandeya said : Saying this, Narada, soaring upwards, returned to heaven. And the king too began to ..jake preparations for the marriage of his daughter.

sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच अथ कन्याप्रदाने स तमेवार्थं विचिन्तयन्। समानिन्ये च तत् सर्वं भाण्डं वैवाहिकं नृपः॥
en: Markandeya said : The monarch, reflecting on the words (of Narada) with regard to his daughter's marriage, began to make preparations for the wedding.

sn: ततो वृद्धान् द्विजान् सर्वानृत्विजः सपुरोहितान्। समाहूय दिने पुण्ये प्रययौ सह कन्यया॥
en: Then, inviting all the old Brahmanas and the Ritvijas together with the priests, the king accompanied by his daughter set out on an auspicious day.

sn: मेध्यारण्यं स गत्वा च धुमत्सेनाश्रमं नृपः। पद्भ्यामेव द्विजैः सार्धं राजर्षि तमुपागमत्॥
en: Having reached the hermitage of Dyumatsena (situate) in the sacred forest, the king (Ashvapati) accompanied by the Brahmanas advanced on foot to meet that royal sage.

sn: तत्रापश्यन्महाभाग शालवृक्षमुपाश्रितम्। कौश्यां बृस्यां समासीनं चक्षुर्हीनं नृपं तदा॥
en: And there (in the hermitage) he saw that highly wise and old king seated on a mat of Kusha grass under a Sala tree.

sn: स राजा तस्य राजर्षेः कृत्वा पूजां यथार्हतः। वाचा सुनियतो भूत्वा चकारात्मनिवेदनम्॥ तस्यार्थ्यमासनं चैव गां चावेद्य स धर्मवित्। किमागमनमित्येवं राजा राजानमब्रवीत्॥
en: The King (Ashvapati) having in conformity with usage, paid his respects to that royal sage, introduced himself (to him) by an appropriate speech and the king (Dyumatsena) versed in religion, having offered to the monarch (Ashvapati) a seat, (the oblation called) Arghya and a cow asked him what brought him there,

sn: तस्य सर्वमभिप्रायमितिकर्तव्यतां च ताम्। सत्यवन्तं समुद्दिश्य सर्वमेव न्यवेदयत्॥
en: He (Ashvapati) then expressed all his intentions and purposes in detail with regard to Satyavana.

sn: अश्वपतिरुवाच सावित्री नाम राजर्षे कन्येयं मम शोभना। तां स्वधर्मेण धर्मज्ञ स्नुषार्थे त्वं गृहाण मे॥
en: Ashvapati said : O royal sage, this fair damsel, named Savitri, is my daughter. O virtuous one, do you accept her for your daughter-in-law in conformity with the usage of your order.

sn: धुमत्सेन उवाच श्वराम धर्म नियतास्तपस्विनः। कथं त्वनीं वनवासमाश्रमे निवत्स्यते क्लेशमिमं सुता तव॥
en: Dyumatsena said : Exiled from my kingdom we have taken refuge in the woods and have been, like ascetics, practising virtue with subdued passions. How will (therefore), your daughter, unworyour of a forest life, put up with (its) hardships living in the forest?

sn: अश्वपतिरुवाच सुखं च दुःखं च भवाभवात्मकं यदा विजानाति सुताहमेव च। न मद्विधे युज्यति राक्यमीदृशं विनिश्चयेनाभिगतोऽस्मि ते नृप॥
en: Ashvapati said : Neither happiness nor misery has any permanence. My daughter and myself are aware of this. Therefore, O king, you should not use such words towards me. Having (previously) made up my mind. I have come here.

sn: आशां नार्हसि मे हन्तुं सौहृदात् प्रणतस्य च। अभितश्चागतं प्रेम्णा प्रत्याख्यातुं न मार्हसि॥
en: You should not dishearten me since I have saluted you through friendship. As I have come here actuated by love, you ought not to refuse me.

sn: अनुरूपो हि युक्तश्च त्वं ममाहं तवापि च। स्नुषां प्रतीच्छ मे कन्यां भार्यां सत्यवतः सतः॥
en: You are my and I am your equal; and we are suitable to each other. Be pleased, (therefore) to accept my daughter as your daughter-in-law and wife of good Satyavana.

sn: धुमत्सेन उवाच पूर्वमेवाभिलषितः सम्बन्धो मे त्वया सह। भ्रष्टराज्यस्त्वहमिति तत एतद् विचारितम्॥
en: Dyumatsena said: Formerly, I cherished a desire of forming an alliance with you. (But) deprived of my kingdom (afterwards) I hesitated (to do it).

sn: अभिप्रायस्त्वयं यो मे पूर्वमेवाभिकाक्षितः। स निर्वर्ततु मेऽद्यैव काक्षितो ह्यसि मेऽतिथिः॥
en: Let, what I desired before, be accomplished this very day. You are a welcome guest to me.

sn: ततः सर्वान् समानाय्य द्विजानाश्रमवासिनः। यथाविधि समुद्वाहं कारयामासतुनृपौ॥
en: Then, those two monarchs, inviting all the Brahmanas dwelling in the hermitages, caused the wedding to be celebrated agreeably to the usage.

sn: दत्त्वा सोऽश्वपतिः कन्यां यथार्ह सपिरच्छदम्। ययौ स्वमेव भवनं युक्तः परमया मुदा॥
en: Having given away his daughter with suitable robes, Ashvapati with a merry heart left for his own abode.

sn: सत्यवानपि तां भार्यां लब्ध्वा सर्वगुणान्विताम्। मुमुदे सा च तं लब्ध्वा भर्तारं मनसेप्सितम्॥
en: Satyavana having obtained a wife graced with all the (noble) qualities and she (Savitri) too having got a husband after her own heart, rejoiced exceedingly.

sn: गते पितरि सर्वाणि संन्यस्याभरणानि सा। जगृहे वल्कलान्येव वस्त्रं काषायमेव च॥
en: Her father having departed, she cast off all her ornaments and put on barks of trees and cloths dyed red.

sn: परिचारैर्गुणैश्चैव प्रश्रयेण दमेन च। सर्वकामक्रियाभिश्च सर्वेषां तुष्टिमादधे॥
en: By her ministrations, good qualities, affections, self-control and good services to all, she pleased every one.

sn: शुश्रू शरीरसत्कारैः सर्वैराच्छादनादिभिः। श्वशुरं देवसत्कारैर्वाचः संयमनेन च॥
en: By ministering to her physical comforts and by (covering her with) all sorts of robes, she delighted her mother-in-law. And she pleased her father-in-law by worshipping him as a god and by controlling her words.

sn: तथैव प्रियवादेन नैपुणेन शमेन च। रहाचैवोपचारेण भर्तारं पर्यतोषयत्॥
en: Similarly, by agreeable words, by skillfulness, by sweet disposition and by ministering to him in private she delighted her husband.

sn: एवं तत्राश्रमे तेषां तदा निवसतां सताम्। कालस्तपस्यतां कश्चिदपाक्रामत भारत॥
en: Thus, O Bharata, these good people engaged in asceticism continued to dwell for some time in that hermitage.

sn: सावित्र्या ग्लायमानायास्तिष्ठन्त्यास्तु दिवानिशम्। नारदेन यदुक्तं तद् वाक्यं मनसि वर्तते॥
en: And Savitri too, whether asleep or awake, could not forget the words of Narada which were present in her mind day and night.

sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच ततः काले बहुतिथे व्यतिक्रान्ते कदाचन। प्राप्तः स कालो मर्तव्यं यत्र स्तयवता नृप॥
en: Markandeya aid : After the lapse of a long while, O king, the time for Satyavana's death at last arrived.

sn: गणयन्त्याश्च सावित्र्या दिवसे दिवसे गते। यद् वाक्यं नारदेनोक्तं वर्तते हृदि नित्यशः॥
en: Savitri counted each days it passed away, (for) the words of Narada were always present in her mind.

sn: चतुर्थेऽहनि मर्तव्यमिति संचिन्त्य भाविनी। व्रतः त्रिरात्रमुद्दिश्य दिवारानं स्थिताभवत्॥
en: Having ascertained (by calculation) that her husband's death would take place on the fourth day (thence), that observant of the Triratra vow, fasted day and night.

sn: तं श्रुत्वा नियमं तस्या भृशं दुःखान्वितो नृपः। उत्थाय वाक्यं सावित्रीमब्रवीत् परिसान्त्वयन्॥
en: Aware of her vow, the king (Dyumatsena) became very sorry and rising up consoled Savitri with these words.

sn: द्युमत्सेन उवाच अतितीव्रोऽयमारम्भस्त्वयाऽऽरब्धो नृपात्मजे। तिसृणां वससीतनां हि स्थानं परमदुश्चरम्॥
en: Dyumatsena said : Princess, the vow you have taken is very difficult to observe, for, it is extremely hard to fast continuously for three nights.

sn: सावित्र्युवाच न कार्यस्तात संताप: पारयिष्याम्यहं व्रतम्। व्यवसायकृतं हीदं व्यवसायश्च कारणम्॥
en: Savitri said: O sire, you need not be sorry. I will be able to complete the vow. I have undertaken this vow with a firm resolve; and determination is the (sole) cause of success (in every undertaking).

sn: धुमत्सेन उवाच व्रतं भिन्धीति वक्तुं त्वां नास्मि शक्तः कथञ्चन। पारयस्येति वचनं युक्तमस्मद्विधो वदेत्॥
en: Dyumatsena said : I can, by no means tell you to give up your vow. Men like us should rather encourage you to complete it.

sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच एवमुक्त्वा धुमत्सेनो विरराम महामनाः। तिष्ठन्ती चैव सावित्री काष्ठभूतेव लक्ष्यते॥
en: Markandeya said : Saying this, the high-minded Dyumatsena ceased; and Savitri thus remaining (without food) looked like a wooden doll.

sn: श्वोभूते भर्तृमरणे सावित्र्या भरतर्षभ। दुःखान्वितायास्तिष्ठन्त्याः सा रात्रिर्व्यत्यवर्तत॥
en: O best of the Bharatas, thinking that her husband would die tomorrow, Savitri, stricken with grief and observing fasts, passed the night in great sorrow.

sn: अद्य तद् दिवसं चेति हुत्वा दीप्तं हुताशनम्। युगमात्रोदिते सूर्ये कृत्वा पौर्वाहिणकी: क्रियाः॥
en: Then, when the sun rose a couple of hands (on the horizon), Savitri performed her morning devotions and offered oblation to the blazing fire.

sn: ततः सर्वान् द्विजान् वृद्धान् श्व श्वशुरमेव च। अभिवाद्यानुपूर्येण प्राञ्जलिर्नियता स्थिता॥
en: She then bowed down to all the aged Brahmanas, her father-in-law and mother-inlaw, one after the other and stood humbly before them with joined hands.

sn: अवैधव्याशिषस्ते तु सावित्र्यर्थं हिताः शुभाः। ऊचुस्तपस्विनः सर्वे तपोवननिवासिनः॥
en: And all the ascetics living in the hermitage pronounced, for the welfare of Savitri, the benediction that she might never be a widow.

sn: एवमस्त्विति सावित्री ध्यानयोगपरायणा। मनसा ता गिरः सर्वा प्रत्यगृह्णात् तपस्विनाम्॥
en: Savitri, who was buried in contemplation, saying in her mind “be it so" bowed down to the words of the ascetics,

sn: तं कालं तं मुहूर्तं च प्रतीक्षन्ती नृपात्मजा। यथोक्तं नारदवचश्चिन्तयन्ती सुदुःखिता॥
en: And with a heavy heart, the princess, pondering on the words of Narada (anxiously) awaited the hour and the moment of her husband's death).

sn: ततस्तु श्वश्रूश्वशुरावूचतुस्तां नृपात्मजाम्। एकान्तमास्थितां वाक्यं प्रीत्या भरतसत्तम॥
en: Then, O best of the Bharatas, her father-in-law and mother-in-law gladly told the king's daughter who was seated alone, these words.

sn: श्वशुरावूचतुः व्रतं यथोपदिष्टं तु तथा तत् पारितं त्वया। आहारकालः सम्प्राप्तः क्रियतां यदनन्तरम्॥
en: The Father-in-law said : You have performed the vow as directed. It is now the time to eat. Do what you think proper.

sn: सावित्र्युवाच अस्तं गते मयाऽऽदित्ये भोक्तव्यं कृतकामया। एष मे हृदि संकल्प: समयश्च कृतो मया॥
en: Savitri said : Having observed the desired vow I appointed the time when the sun would go down for my meals. (Even now) this is the determination of my heart.

sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच एवं सम्भाषणाणायाः सावित्र्या भोजनं प्रति। स्कन्धे परशुमादाय सत्यवान् प्रस्थितो वनम्॥
en: Markandeya said : When Savitri was saying this about her meals. Satyavana, taking his hatchet on his shoulders, left for the woods.

sn: सावित्री त्वाह भर्तारं नैकस्त्वं गन्तुमर्हसि। सह त्वया गमिष्यामि न हि त्वां हातुमुत्सहे॥
en: (Thereupon) Savitri said to her husband "you should not go alone. I will go with you. I do not feel inclined to be separated from you.

sn: सत्यावानुवाच वनं न गतपूर्वं ते दुःखः पन्थाश्च भाविनि। व्रोतपवासक्षामा च कथं पद्भ्यां गमिष्यसि॥
en: Satyavana said: Dearest, you have never visited the woods before. The path is very rugged (Moreover), lean and weak as you have been by the observance of fasts and vow how will you be able to walk?

sn: सावित्र्युवाच उपवासान्न मे ग्लानिर्नास्ति चापि परिश्रमः। गमने च कृतोत्साहां प्रतिषेढुं न मार्हसि।॥
en: Savitri said : Neither do I feel exhaustion nor lassitude on account of the fast. (Moreover) I am very eager to go. Do not (therefore) prevent me.

sn: सत्यवानुवाच यदि ते गमनोत्साहः करिष्यामि तव प्रियम्। मम त्वामन्त्रय गुरून् न मां दोषः स्पृशेदयम्॥
en: Satyavana said: Since you are so eager to go, I will fulfill your desire. (But) take leave of my parents (first) so that no blame can be attached to me.

sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच साभिवाद्याब्रवीच्छ्वधू श्वशुरं च महाव्रता। अयं गच्छति मे भर्ता फलाहारो महावनम्॥
en: Markandeya said : (Then) bowing down to her mother-in-law and father-in-law, she of great vows said (to them) "my husband is going to the great forest for gathering fruits.

sn: इच्छेयमभ्यनुज्ञाता आर्यया श्वशुरेण ह। अनेन सह निर्गन्तुं न मेऽद्य विरहः क्षमः॥
en: It is my desire that your worshipful self and my father-in-law will (kindly) permit me to accompany him. I cannot bear to be separated (from him) this day.

sn: गुर्वग्निहोत्रार्थकृते प्रस्थितश्च सुतस्तव। न निवार्यो निवार्यः स्यादन्यथा प्रस्थितो वनम्॥
en: As your son is going to the forest for the sacrificial fire and for his superiors, you ought not to prevent him. Had it been for any other (business) he should have been prevented.

sn: संवत्सरः किंचिदूनो न निष्क्रान्ताहमाश्रमात्। वनं कुसुमितं द्रष्टुं परं कौतूहलं हि मे॥
en: I have not walked out for a little less than a year. Great indeed is my desire to witness the woods.

sn: द्युमत्सेन उवाच यतः प्रभृति सावित्री पित्रा दत्ता स्नुषा मम। नानयाभ्यर्थनायुक्तमुक्तपूर्वं स्मराम्यहम्॥
en: Dyumatsena said : From the very time that Savitri was made my daughter-in-law by her father, I do not remember her to have ever made any request to me.

sn: तदेषा लभतां कामं यथाभिलषितं वधूः। अप्रमादश्च कर्तव्यः पुत्रि सत्यवतः पथि॥
en: So, let what my daughter-in-law desires be fulfilled. Daughter, act in such a manner that Satyavana does not neglect his business on the way.

sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच उभाब्यामभ्यनुज्ञाता सा जगाम यशस्विनी। सह भ; हसन्तीव हृदयेन विदूयता॥
en: Thus permitted by both, the renowned (Savitri) with a smiling (countenance) though with a sorrowful heart accompanied her husband (to the woods).

sn: सा वनानि विचित्राणि रमणीयानि सर्वशः। मयूरगणजुष्टानि ददर्श विपुलेक्षणा॥३
en: And that large-eyed lady beheld, on all sides romantic and charming forests frequented by swarms of peacocks.

sn: नदीः पुण्यवहाश्चैव पुष्पितांश्च नगोत्तमान्। सत्यवानाह पश्येति सावित्री मधुरं वचः॥
en: And Satyavana said these sweet words to Savitri "behold these streams of sacred waters and these excellent blossoming trees.”

sn: निरीक्षमाणा भर्तारं स्रवावस्थमनिन्दिता। मृतमेव हि भर्तारं काले मुनिवचः स्मरन्॥
en: That blameless girl, however, began to watch all the movements of her husband; but remembering what the sage (Narada) had said, she considered him as already dead.

sn: अनुव्रजन्ती भर्तारं जगाम मृदुगामिनी। द्विधेष हृदयं कृत्वा तं च कालमवेक्षती॥
en: With her heart divided into two parts, she (with one of these) replying to her husband and (with the other) awaiting the (fatal) hour, followed him slowly.

sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच अथ भार्यासहायः स फलान्यादाय वीर्यवान्। कठिनं पूरयामास ततः काष्ठान्यपाटयत्॥
en: Markandeya said : Accompanied by his wife the powerful Satyavana (first) gathered fruits and filled his bag; he then began to cut down the trees.

sn: तस्य पाटयतः काष्ठं स्वेदो वै समजायत। व्यायामेन च तेनास्य जज्ञे शिरसि वेदना॥ सोऽभिगम्य प्रियां भार्यामुवाच श्रमपिडितः।
en: As he was felling the branches he began to sweat and had an headache in consequence of the labour. Oppressed with toil, he came to his dear wife and said to her thus.

sn: सत्यावानुवाच व्यायामेन ममानेन जाता शिरसि वेदना॥ अङ्गानि चैव सावित्रि हृदयं दूयतीव च। अस्वस्थमिव चात्मानं लक्षये मितभाषिणी॥ शूलैरिव शिरो विद्धमिदं संलक्षयाम्यहम्। तत् खप्तुमिच्छे कल्याणि न स्थातुं शक्तिरस्ति मे॥
en: Satyavana said : I have a headache on account of this exercise. And, O Savitri, my limbs and heart are aching. O lady of restrained speech, I feel unwell. It seems (to me) that my head is being pierced by arrows. Therefore, O blessed lady, I feel inclined to sleep; for I am quite unable to stand.

sn: सा समासाद्य सावित्री भर्तारमुपगम्य च। उत्सङ्गेऽस्य शिरः कृत्वा निषसाद महीतले॥
en: (Thereupon), Savitri coming up to her husband, sat down on the ground with his head on her lap.

sn: ततः सा नारदवचो विमृशन्ती तपस्विनी। तं मुहूर्त क्षणं बेला दिवसं च युयोज ह॥
en: Then that devout lady, remembering the words of Narada, began to calculate the moment, the hour, the time and the day.

sn: मुहूर्तादेव चापश्यत् पुरुषं रक्तवाससम्। बद्धमौलिं वपुष्मन्तमादित्यसमतेजसम्॥ श्यामावदातं रक्ताक्षं पाशहस्तं भयावहम्। स्थितं सत्यवतः पार्श्वे निरीक्षन्तं तमेव च॥
en: And in a moment she saw a person attired in red garments, wearing a diadem, of an enormous structure, having the splendour of the sun of a dark and yellow complexion, endued with red eyes, with a noose in his hands, dreadful to look at, standing beside Satyavana and gazing at him.

sn: तं दृष्ट्वा सहसोत्थाय भर्तुर्यस्य शनैः शिरः। कृताञ्जलिरुवाचार्ता हृदयेन प्रवेपती॥
en: Beholding him she gently placed her husband's head on the ground. Then rising suddenly she, with a trembling heart and joined palms, said these words in a great sorrow.

sn: सावित्र्युवाच दैवतं त्वाभिजानामि वपुरेतद्ध्यमानुषम्। कामया ब्रूहि देवेश कस्त्वं किं च चिकीर्षसि॥
en: Savitri said: From your superhuman appearance I know you to be a god. Kindly tell me, O god of gods, who you are and what is your desire.

sn: यम उवाच पतिव्रततासि सावित्रि तथैव च तपोऽन्विता। अतस्त्वामबिबाषामि विद्धि मां त्वं शुभे यमम्॥
en: Yama said: O Savitri, you are devotedly attached to your husband and are of ascetic virtue. And it for this reason that I address you. Know me, O auspicious girl, to be Yana.

sn: अयं ते सत्यवान भर्ता क्षीणायुः पार्थिवात्मजः। नेष्यामि तमहं बद्ध्वा विद्ध्यतन्मे चिकीर्षितम्॥
en: The years of this prince, your husband, being numbered, I will bind (him with this noose) and take him hence. Know this to be my। intention.

sn: सावित्र्युवाच श्रूयते भगवन् दूतास्तवागच्छन्ति मानवान्। नेतुं किल भवान् कस्मादागतोऽसि स्वयं प्रभो॥
en: Savitri said: We hear, O god, that your emissaries come to take away men. How is it that your worshipful self has come in person?

sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच इत्युक्तः पितृराजस्तां भगवान् स्वचिकीर्षितम्। यथावत् सर्वमाख्यातुं तत्प्रियार्थं प्रचक्रमे॥
en: Markandeya said : Thus addressed by her, the divine lord of the Pitris, in order to please her, began faithfully to relate everything about his intentions.

sn: अयं च धर्मसंयुक्तो रूपवान् गुणसागरः। ना) मत्पुरुषैर्नेतुमतोऽस्मि स्वयमागतः॥
en: And he said, I have come here personally considering that my emissaries are not fit to bring such a devotional and handsome person, endued with qualities, vast as a sea."

sn: ततः सत्यवतः कायात् पाशबद्धं वशं गतम्। अङ्गुष्ठमात्रं पुरुषं निश्चकर्ष यमो बलात्॥
en: Then Yama powerfully drew out of the body of Satyavana a person of the measure of the thumb, bound him with the noose and brought him under control.

sn: ततः समुद्धृतप्राणं गतश्वासं हतप्रभम्। निर्विचेष्टं शरीरं तद् बभूवाप्रियददर्शनम्॥
en: The life being taken out, the body deprived of breath, destitute of lustre and devoid of motion, became disagreeable to the eye.

sn: यमस्तु तं ततो बद्ध्वा प्रयातो दक्षिणामुखः। सावित्री चैव दुःखार्ता यममेवान्वगच्छत। नियमव्रतसंसिद्धा महाभागा पतिव्रता॥
en: Binding it thus, Yama proceeded towards the south; and weighed down with grief, the exalted Savitri also, devotedly attached to her husband and successful in her vow, followed him.

sn: यम उवाच निवर्त गच्छ सावित्री कुरुष्वास्यौर्ध्वदेहिकम्। कृतं भर्तुस्त्वयाऽऽनृण्यं यावद् गम्यं गतं त्वया॥
en: Yama said: Go back, O Savitri and perform the last rites of your husband. Your debt to your husband is discharged. You have come as far as is possible (for you) to do.

sn: सावित्र्युवाच यत्र मे नीयते भर्ता स्वयं वा यत्र गच्छति। मया च तत्र गन्तव्यमेष धर्मः सनातनः॥
en: Savitri said: I ought to follow my husband thither where he is being carried to or whither he goes of his own accord. (Because) this is the eternal duty.

sn: तपसा गुरुभक्त्या च भर्तुः स्नेहाद् व्रतेन च। तव चैव प्रसादेन न मे प्रतिहता गतिः॥
en: There shall be no obstacle to my course on account of my asceticism, my devotion to superiors, my affection for my husband, my observance of vows and your grace.

sn: प्राहुः साप्तपदं मैत्रं बुधास्तत्त्वार्थदर्शिनः। मित्रतां च पुरस्कृत्य किञ्चिद् वक्ष्यामि तच्छृणु॥
en: It is asserted by the wise, versed in true knowledge, that one contracts a friendship with another by going only seven paces with him. I will tell you something keeping this friendship in view. Pray listen to it.

sn: नानात्मवन्तस्तु वने चरन्ति धर्मं च वासं च परिश्रमं च। विज्ञानतो धर्ममुदाहरन्ति तस्मात् सन्तो धर्ममाहुः प्रधानम्॥
en: Men, wanting in self-control do not observe (the proper rites and sacrifices) even in the forest. Nor do they go through and discharge the necessary duties of these three modes of life, namely conjugal or domestic life, life of celebacy and study in the house of the preceptor and thirdly a life of the total renunciation of the world. Conjugal life or domesticity leads to true religious merit. It is for this reason that the wise assert that domestic (which leads to righteousness) is the best of all (other modes of life).

sn: एकस्य धर्मेण सतां मतेन सर्वे स्म तं मार्गमनुप्रपन्नाः। मा वै द्वितीयं मा तृतीयं च वाञ्छेत् तस्मात् सन्तो धर्ममाहुः प्रधानम्॥
en: By discharging faithfully the necessary duties of this one mode of life (i.e. conjugal life) we have all attained to the path (of righteousness) and therefore we do not covet the second and the third modes of life (i.e. celebacy and renunciation of the world). It is therefore that domesticity with its necessary duties is considered by the wise as the foremost of all (other lives).

sn: यम उवाच निवर्त तुष्टोऽस्मि तवानया गिरा स्वराक्षरव्यञ्जनहेतुयुक्तया। वरं वृणीष्वेह विनास्य जीवितं ददानि ते सर्वमनिन्दिते वरम्॥
en: Yama said: Do go back. I have been delighted with your words couched in (proper) letters and accents and resting on reason. Do you ask for a boon with the exception of your husband's life. O lady of faultless proportions, I will give any boon (you desire).

sn: सावित्र्युवाच च्युतः स्वराज्याद् वनवासमाश्रितो विनष्टचक्षुः श्वशुरो ममाश्रमे। स्तव प्रसादाज्ज्दलनार्क संनिभः॥
en: Savitri said: My father-in-law has been driven away from this kingdom and has lost his eyes. He now leads a forest life in our hermitage. Let that king, through your grace, be restored to his sight and be as powerful as the sun or fire.

sn: यम उवाच ददानि तेऽहं तमनिन्दिते वरं यथा त्वयोक्तं भविता च तत् तथा। तवाध्वना ग्लानिमिवोपलक्षये निवर्त गच्छस्व न ते श्रमो भवेत्॥ सुरेश भूयश्च
en: Yama said: O blameless girl, I give you this boon, that, what you have asked of me, will take place. I see you are wearied with your journey. Do not proceed further. Go back. Do not take any more trouble.

sn: सावित्र्युवाच श्रमः कुतो भर्तृसमीपतो हि मे यतो हि भर्ता मम सा गतिधुवा। यतः पति नेष्यसि तत्र मे गतिः वचो निबोध मे॥
en: Savitri said : I do not feel fatigue as I am with my husband. I will surely follow the same path as my husband does. I will surely go thither where you are taking my lord to. O best of the celestials, listen again to what I say.

sn: सतां सकृत्संगतमीप्सितं परं ततः परं मित्रमिति प्रचक्षते। न चाफलं सत्पुरुषेण सङ्गतं ततः सतां सन्निवसेत् सपागमे॥
en: (It is asserted by the wise) that even a single interview with the virtuous is highly desirable. Friendship with them is much more so. Communion with the righteous is never without fruit. So one should always associate with the virtuous.

sn: यम उवाच मनोऽनुकूलं बुधबुद्धिवर्धनं त्वया यदुक्तं वचनं हिताश्रयम्। विना पुनः सत्यवतोऽस्य जीवितं वरं द्वितीयं वरयस्व भामिनि॥
en: Yama said: The words spoken by you are pregnant with great import. They augment the wisdom of even the learned and are delightful to the mind. Therefore, O damsel, with the exception of Satyavana's life to you ask for a second boon.

sn: सावित्र्युवाच हृतं पुरा मे स्वशुरस्य धीमतः स्वमेव राज्यं लभतां स पार्थिवः। जह्यात् स्वधर्मं न च मे गुरुर्यथा द्वितीयमेतद् वरयामि ते वरम्॥
en: Savitri said: Let that king, my intellectual father-in-law, regain his kingdom that he lost before. And may that worshipful one never fail to properly discharge his duties. This is the second boon that I pray for.

sn: यम उवाच न च स्वधर्मात् परिहास्यते नृपः। कृतेन कामेन मया नृपात्मजे निवर्तगच्छस्व न ते श्रमो भवेत्॥
en: Yama said: That monarch will be soon restored to his kingdom and be ever firm in his duties Princess, I have now gratified your wish. Do not proceed further; go back; do not allow yourself to be any more weary.

sn: सावित्र्युवाच पतास्त्वयैता नियमेन संयता नियम्य चैता नयसे निकामया। ततो यमत्वं तव देव विश्रुतं निबोध चेमां गिरमीरितां मया॥
en: Savitri said: You have controlled all the creatures by your ordinances and you carry them away not according to your caprice but those regulations. Therefore, O god, you are styled Yama (i.e. one who governs by ordinances). Hear (again) these my words.

sn: अद्रोहः सर्वभूतेषु कर्मणा मनसा गिरा। अनुग्रहश्च दानं च सतां धर्मः सनातनः॥
en: The eternal duty of the righteous is mercy and charity, benevolence and favour towards all creation in thought, word and deed.

sn: एवंप्रायश्च लोकोऽयं मनुष्याः शक्तिपेशलाः। सन्तस्त्वेवाप्यमित्रेषु दयां प्राप्तेषु कुर्वते॥
en: In this world, it is generally the case that men here are destitute of energy and skill. (But) the righteous show mercy even to their enemies when the latter throw themselves into the protection.

sn: यम उवाच स्तथा त्वया वाक्यमिदं समीरितम्। विना पुनः सत्यवतोऽस्य जीवितं वरं वृणीष्वेह शुभे यदिच्छसि॥
en: Yama said: The words uttered by you appear (to me) as delicious as water to a thirsty person. (Therefore), O auspicious girl, do you ask again for any other boon that you like than the life of Satyavana.

sn: सावित्र्युवाच ममानपत्यः पृथिवीपतिः पिता भवेत् पितुः पुत्रशतं तथौरसम्। कुलस्य सन्तानकरं च यद् भवेत् तृतीयमेतद् वरयामि ते वरम्॥
en: Savitri said: My royal father is childless. Let him have one hundred sons, begotten by him, who will perpetuate his family. This is the third boon that I ask of you.

sn: यम उवाच कुलस्य सन्तानकरं सुवर्चसं शतं सुतानां पितुरस्तु ते शुभे! कृतेन कामेन नराधिपात्मजे निवर्त दूरं हि पथस्त्वमागता॥
en: Yama said: O auspicious girl, your father shall have one hundred highly-energetic sons, the perpetuators of his race. Princess, your desire is now gratified. Do retrace your steps. You have come too far.

sn: सावित्र्युवाच न दूरमेतन्मम भर्तृसंनिधौ मनो हि मे दूरतरं प्रधावति। अथ व्रजन्नेव गिरं समुद्यतां मयोच्यमानां शृणु भूय एव च॥
en: Savitri said : It appears no distance to me since I am beside my husband. My mind travels a greater distance. (Now) listen, as you proceed on, to the words that I will presently utter.

sn: स्ततो हि वैवस्वत उच्यसे बुधैः। स्ततस्तवेहेश्वर धर्मराजता॥
en: You are the powerful son of Vivasavata and are therefore called by the wise Vaivasvata. You judge all the creatures impartially and rightfully and for this reason, O lord, you are styled the lord of justice.

sn: आत्मन्यपि न विश्वासस्तथा भवति सत्सु यः। तस्मात् सत्सु विशेषेण सर्वः प्रणयमिच्छति॥
en: People do not place so inuch reliance on their own selves as on the virtuous. Therefore everybody wishes particularly to cultivate intimacy with the righteous.

sn: सौहृदात् सर्वभूतानां विश्वासो नाम जायते। तस्मात् सत्सु विशेषेण विश्वासं कुरुते जनः॥
en: And friendship alone generates the confidence among all creatures. It is therefore that people repose confidence specially in the virtuous.

sn: यम उवाच उदाहृतं ते वचनं यदङ्गने शुभे न तादृक् त्वदृते श्रुतं मया। अनेन तुष्टोऽस्मि विनास्य जीवितं वरं चतुर्थं वरयस्व गच्छ च॥
en: Yama said: O auspicious and fair damsel. I never before heard such words as you have (just now) spoken from any other person than you. I am pleased with these. Do you ask for a fourth boon with the exception of Satyavana's life and then retrace your steps.

sn: सावित्र्युवाच ममात्मजं सत्यवतस्तथौरसं भवेदुभाभ्यामिह यत् कुलोद्वहम्। मिदं चतुर्थं वरयामि ते वरम्॥
en: Savitri said : Let me have one hundred strong and powerful sons, born of Satyavana's loins and begotten of both of us, who will perpetuate our line. This is the fourth boon I pray for.

sn: यम उवाच शतं सुतानां बलवीर्यशालिनां भविष्यति प्रीतिकरं तवाबले। परिश्रमस्ते न भवेनृपात्मजे निवर्त दूरं हि पथस्त्वमागता॥
en: Yama said : Lady, you shall have one hundred strong and powerful sons who will cause your delight. Princess, do not take any further trouble; go back; indeed you have come a great way.

sn: सावित्र्युवाच सतां सदा शाश्वतधर्मवृत्तिः सन्तो न सीदन्ति न च व्यथन्ति। सतां सद्धि फलंः सङ्गमोऽस्ति सद्भयो भयं नानुवर्तन्ति सन्तः॥
en: Savitri said : The pious are ever unceasingly devoted to religion. They do neither fecl lassitude nor affliction. The intercourse of the pious with the virtuous is (ever) productive of good. And the righteous apprehend no fear from the virtuous.

sn: सन्तो हि सत्येन नयन्ति सूर्यं सन्तो भूमिं तपसा धारयन्ति। सन्तो गतिर्भूतभव्यस्य राजन् सतां मध्ये नावसीदन्ति सन्तः॥
en: Indeed, the righteous by their truthfulness make the sun move and it is the pious who by asceticism support the earth. O king, it is the righteous that are the cause of the past and the future. And the pious remaining in the midst of the righteous do never feel languor.

sn: आर्यजुष्टमिदं वृत्तमिति विज्ञाय शाश्वतम्। सन्तः परार्थं कुर्वाणा नावेक्षन्ति परस्परम्॥
en: Knowing that this is the eternal custom of the good and the virtuous, pious people devote themselves to acts of self-sacrifice for others without expecting any return.

sn: न च प्रसादः सत्पुरुषेषु मोघो न चाप्यर्थो नश्यति नापि मानः। यस्मादेतन्नियतं सत्सु नित्यं तस्मात् सन्तो रक्षितारो भवन्ति॥
en: Good acts done to the virtuous are never fruitless. Such acts never destroy our honour or interest. Since the righteous are characterised by such (noble) conduct they become protectors (of all creatures).

sn: यम उवाच यथा यथा भाषसि धर्मसंहितं मनोऽनुकूलं सुपदं महार्थवत्। तथा तथा मे त्वयि भक्तिरुत्तमा वरं वृणीष्वाप्रतिमं पतिव्रते॥
en: Yama said: The more you address me in words pregnant with religious meaning, delightful to the mind, full of sweet phrases and of grave import, the more I am inclined to respect you. O lady, devotedly attached to your husband, crave an incomparable boon.

sn: सावित्र्युवाच स्तथा यथान्येषु वरेषु मानद। वरं वृणे जीवतु सत्यवानयं यथा मृता ह्येवमहं पतिं विना॥
en: Savitri said : The boon that you have (just) given me cannot bear fruit (without my union with my husband). Therefore, O bestower of honour, among other boons (that you have already granted me) I crave this boon that Satyavana may be brought back to life. I am as good as dead without my husband.

sn: न कामये भर्तृविनाकृता सुखं न कामये भर्तृविनाकृता दिवम्। न कामये भर्तृविनाकृता श्रियं न भर्तृहीना व्यवसामि जीवितुम्॥
en: I do not want happiness bereft of my husband. Without my lord I do not crave heaven itself. Deprived of my husband I do not long for prosperity. And bereft of my husband I am unable to bear life.

sn: वरातिसर्ग: शतपुत्रता मम त्वयैव दत्तो ह्रियते च मे पतिः। वरं वृणे जीवतु सत्यवानयं तवैव सत्यं वचनं भविष्यति॥
en: You have granted me the boon that I shall have one hundred sons and yet you are carrying away my husband. Now I pray for this boon that Satyavana may be alive again and then your words will prove true.

sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच तथेत्युक्त्वा तु तं पाशं मुक्त्वा वैवस्वतो यमः। धर्मराजः प्रहृष्टात्मा सावित्रीमिदमब्रवीत्॥
en: Markandeya said : Thereupon, Yama, the son of Vivasvata and the lord of justice saying "be it so" and unloosing his noose, cheerfully spoke to Savitri thus,

sn: एष भद्रे मया मुक्तो भर्ता ते कुलनन्दिनि। अरोगस्तव नेयश्च सिदार्थः स भविष्यति॥
en: "O chaste and gentle lady, I release your husband. You will be able to take him back. He will be free from disease and (ever) successful (in his undertakings).

sn: चतुर्वर्षशतायुश्च त्वया सार्धमवाप्स्यति। इष्ट्वा यज्ञैश्च धर्मेण ख्यातिं लोके गमिष्यति॥
en: He as well as you will live four hundred years. By his devoutness and by celebrating many sacrifices he will win a great renown in the world.

sn: त्वयि पुत्रशतं चैव सत्यवाञ्जनयिष्यति। ते चापि सर्वे राजानः क्षत्रियाः पुत्रपौत्रिणः॥
en: And Satyavana will beget on you one hundred sons. And those Kshatriya sons (of you) together with their sons and grandsons will be kings;

sn: ख्यातास्त्वन्नामधेयाश्च भविष्यन्तीह शाश्वताः। पितुश्च ते पुत्रशतं भविता तव मातरि॥ मालव्यां मालवा नाम शाश्वताः पुत्रपौत्रिणः। भ्रातरस्ते भविष्यन्ति क्षत्रियास्त्रिदशोपमाः॥
en: And bearing your name will ever be renowned. Your father also will beget a hundred sons on your mother Malavi and those Kshatriya brothers of you resembling the celestials, together with their sons and grandsons will be celebrated under the name of the Malavas."

sn: एवं तस्यै वरं दत्त्वा धर्मराजः प्रतापवान्। निवर्तयित्वा सावित्रीं स्वमेव भवनं ययौ॥
en: Having conferred these boons on her and having thus made her retrace her steps, the lord of justice (Yama) returned to his own abode.
