sn: सावित्र्यपि यमे याते भर्तारं प्रतिलभ्य च। जगाम तत्र यत्रास्या भर्तुः शावं कलेवरम्॥
en: Then Savitri having regained her husband, returned to the place where her husband's ashy pale corpse lay.

sn: सा भूमौ प्रेक्ष्य भर्तारमुपसृत्योपगृह्य च। उत्सङ्गे शिर आरोप्य भूमावुपविवेश ह॥
en: Beholding her husband on the ground she approached and took hold of him. She then sat down placing his head on her lap.

sn: संज्ञां च स पुनर्लब्ध्वा सावित्रीमभ्यभाषत। प्रोष्यागत इव प्रेम्णा पुनः पुनरुदीक्ष्य वै॥
en: Having regained his consciousness, he looked at her again and again like one returned from a distant clime (after a long time) and (then) endearingly addressed her thus.

sn: सत्यवानुवाच सुचिरं बत सुप्तोऽस्मि किमर्थं नावबोधितः। क्व चासौ पुरुष: श्यामो योऽसौ मां संचकर्ष ह।।६५।
en: Satyavana said : Oh, I have slept for a long time. Why did you not awaken me? Where is that darkcomplexioned person who was dragging me away?

sn: सावित्र्युवाच सुचिरं त्वं प्रसुप्तोऽसि ममाङ्के पुरुषर्षभ। गतः स भगवान् देवः प्रजायसंयमनो यमः॥
en: Savitri said: O best of men, you have (indeed) slept long on my lap. That god, the divine Yama, who governs all creatures, has departed.

sn: विश्रान्तोऽसि महाभाग विनिद्रश्च नृपात्मज! यदि शक्यं समुत्तिष्ठ विगाढां पश्य शर्वरीम्॥
en: O blessed one, you are (now) soothed and O prince, you have awakened from sleep. If you are able, rise up. Look, the night is far advanced.

sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच उपलभ्य ततः संज्ञां सुखसुप्त इवोत्थितः। दिशः सर्वा वनान्तांश्च निरीक्ष्योवाच सत्यवान्॥
en: Markandeya said : Having regained his consciousness, Satyavana got up like one who had enjoyed an undisturbed sleep; and seeing all the sides covered with woods he said:

sn: फलाहारोऽस्मि निष्क्रान्तस्त्वया सह सुमध्यमे। ततः पाटयत: काष्ठं शिरसो मे रुजाभवत्॥
en: "O slender-waisted damsel, I set out with you for gathering fruits. And when I was hewing down the woods my headached.

sn: शिरोऽभितापसंतप्तः स्थातुं चिरमशक्नुवन्। तवोत्सङ्गे प्रसुप्तोऽस्मि इति सर्वं स्मरे शुभे॥
en: Sorely distressed with headache I could not stand up long and (therefore) lay down on your lap. O auspicious girl, I remember all this.

sn: त्वयोपगूढस्य च मे निद्रयापहृतं मनः। ततोऽपश्यं तमो घोरं पुरुषं च महौजसम्॥७११
en: Embraced by you, sleep gently came upon me. I then saw it was intensenly dark and also a highly effulgent person.

sn: तद् यदि त्वं विजानासि किं तद् ब्रूहि सुमध्यमे। स्वप्नो मे यदि वा दृष्टो यदि वा सत्यमेव तत्॥
en: O slender-waisted lady, tell me, if you are aware of all that happened whether what I saw was a dream or a reality."

sn: तमुवाचाथ सावित्री रजनी व्यवगाहते। वस्ते सर्वं यथावृत्तमाख्यास्यामि नृपात्मज॥
en: Thereupon Savitri replied to him "prince, the night is deepening tomorrow, I will disciose to you faithfully all that occurred.

sn: उत्तिष्ठोत्तिष्ठ भद्रं ते पितरौ पश्य सुव्रत। विगाढा रजनी चेयं निवृत्तश्च दिवाकरः॥
en: Get up, get up, may you be all hale, O you of good devotion, come and see your parents. The sun has long gone down and the night is deepening.

sn: नक्तंचराचरन्त्येते हृष्टाः क्रूराभिभाषिणः। श्रूयन्ते पर्णशब्दाश्च मृगाणां चरतां वने॥
en: The night-wandering creatures of harsh voices are joyfully roving about. And the rustling of leaves consequent on the footsteps of beasts are heard.

sn: एता घोरं शिवा नादान दिशं दक्षिणपश्चिमाम्। आस्थाय विरुवन्त्युचाः कम्पयन्त्यो मनो मम॥
en: Jackals of frightful appearance stationed in the south and east have set up terrible howls which make my heart tremble.

sn: सत्यवानुवाच वनं प्रतिभयाकारं घनेन तमसाऽऽवृतम्। न विज्ञास्यसि पन्थानं गन्तुं चैव न शक्ष्यसि॥
en: Satyavana said : The forest, enveloped with a dense darkness, has worn a dreadful appearance. You will therefore neither be able to discern the paths nor to go.

sn: सावित्र्युवाच अस्मिन्नद्य वने दग्धे शुष्कवृक्षः स्थितो ज्वलन्। वायुना धम्यमानोऽत्र दृश्यतेऽग्निः क्वचित् क्वचित्।।७८
en: Savitri said: There is a withered tree in a burning state in this forest which caught fire today. And the flames stirred up by the wind are seen now and then.

sn: ततोऽग्निमानयित्वेह ज्वालयिष्यामि सर्वतः। काष्ठानीमानि सन्तीह जहि सन्तापमात्मनः॥
en: Fetching some fire (from that tree) I will kindle a fire all around. There are plenty of logs here. (So) give up your uneasiness.

sn: यदि नोत्सहसे गन्तुं सरुजं त्वां हि लक्षये। न च ज्ञास्यसि पन्थानं तमसा संवृते वने॥
en: If you do not venture to go. (I will do all this). I see you are unwell. You will not be able to discern the paths as a dense darkness is hanging over these woods.

sn: श्वः प्रभाते वने दृश्ये यास्यावोऽनुमते तव। वसावेह क्षपामेकां रुचितं यदि तेऽनघ॥
en: We shall, with your leave, go tomorrow when the forest will be visible. O sinless one, we shall remain here for the night if you wish.

sn: सत्यवानुवाच शिरोरुजा निवृत्ता मे स्वस्थान्यङ्गानि लक्षये। मातापितृभ्यामिच्छामि संगमं त्वत्प्रसादजम्॥
en: Satyavana said : I have recovered from the headache and my limbs are in a sound condition. I am therefore, through your favour, desirous of seeing my parents.

sn: न कदाजिद् विकालं हि गतपूर्वो मयाऽऽश्रमः। अनागतायां सन्ध्यायां माता मे प्ररुणद्धि माम्॥
en: Never before did I return to the hermitage after the lapse of the proper time. My mother is used to shut me up in the asylum even before the evening sets in.

sn: दिवापि मयि निष्क्रान्ते संतष्येते गुरू मम। विचिनोति हि मां तातः सहैवाश्रमवासिभिः॥
en: Even if I go out during the day my parents are filled with anxiety. And my father together with all the inhabitants of the hermitages searches for me.

sn: मात्रा पित्रा च सुभृशं दुःखिताभ्यामहं पुरा। उपालब्धश्च बहुशश्चिरेणागच्छसीति ह॥
en: Several times before this my parents afflicted with grief rebuked me saying “you have been long out."

sn: का त्ववस्था तयोरद्य मदर्थमिति चिन्तये। तयोरदृश्ये मयि च महद् दुःखं भविष्यति॥
en: I am now reflecting as to what a state they will be reduced for my sake. Surely, they will be sorely afflicted on account of my absence.

sn: पुरा मामूचतुश्चैव रात्रावस्रायमाणको। भृशं सुदुःखितौ वृद्धौ बहुशः प्रीतिसंयुतौ॥
en: Sometimes ago, one night, the cheerful old couple, being greatly distressed and weeping profusely said to me repeatedly,

sn: त्वया हीनौ न जीवाव मुहूर्तमपि पुत्रका यावद् धरिष्यसे पुत्र तावन्नौ जीवितं ध्रुवम्॥
en: “Dear son, bereft of you, we cannot endure life for a single moment. Surely we must not survive you.

sn: वृद्धयोरन्धयोदृष्टिस्त्वयि वंशः प्रतिष्ठितः। त्वयि पिण्डश्च कीर्तिश्च संतानं चावयोरिति॥
en: You are the only support of these blind ones. The perpetuity of our line, our funeral oblations, our fame, our descendants, (all) depend on you."

sn: माता वृद्धा पिता वृद्धस्तयोर्यष्टिरहं किल। तौ रात्रौ मामपश्यन्तौ कामवस्थां गमिष्यतः॥
en: My father is, old and so also is my mother; and surely I am their only stay. To what a state will they be reduced if they miss me during the night?

sn: निद्रायाश्चाभ्यसूयामि यस्या हेतोः पिता मम। माता च संशयं प्राप्ता मत्कृतेऽनपकारिणी॥
en: I blame that sleep in consequence of which my harmless parents are in agonising suspense for my sake.

sn: अहं च संशयं प्राप्तः कृच्छ्रामापदमास्थितः। मातापितृभ्यां हि विना नाहं जीवितुमुत्सहे॥
en: And (on account of which) I also placed in this critical position am filled with anxiety. Without my parents I do not care to bear life.

sn: व्यक्तमाकुलया बुद्ध्या प्रज्ञाचक्षुः पिता मम। एकैकमस्यां वेलायां पृच्छत्याश्रमवासिनम्॥
en: I am sure, that by this time my blind father with his mind torn with grief is inquiring of the dwellers of the hermitages about me.

sn: नात्मानमनुशोचामि यथाहं पितरं शुभे। भर्तारं चाप्यनुगतां मातरं परिदुर्बलाम्॥
en: I do not, O auspicious girl, grieve so much for myself as for my father and my weak mother (ever) devoted to her husband.

sn: मत्कृतेन हि तावद्य सन्तापं परमेध्यतः। जीवन्तावनुजीवामि भर्तव्यौ तौ मयेति ह॥ तयोः प्रियं मे कर्तव्यमिति जानामि चाप्यहम्।
en: Surely, they will experience a deep sorrow for my sake. I know that my life will last so long as theirs, that I should support them and do only such acts as are agreeable to them.

sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच एवमुक्त्वा स धर्मात्मा गुरुभक्तो गुरुप्रियः॥ उच्छ्रित्य बाहू दुःखार्तः सुस्वरं प्ररुरोद ह।
en: Markandeya said : Saying this, that virtuous one devoted to and fond of his parents, raising his arms began to bewail loudly in great sorrow.

sn: ततोऽब्रवीत् तथा दृष्ट्वा भर्तारं शोककर्शितम्॥ प्रमृज्याश्रूणि नेत्राभ्यां सावित्री धर्मचारिणी। यदि मेऽस्ति तपस्तप्तं यदि दत्तं हुतं यदि॥ शुश्रूश्वशुरभर्तृणां मम पुण्यास्तु शर्वरी।
en: Seeing that her husband was oppressed with such a deep sorrow, the virtuous Savitri wiping the tears from his eyes spoke to him thus, “If I have practised asceticism, if I have done charitable acts, if I have offered oblations (to the fire), then, may this night be conducive to the welfare of my father-in-law, mother-in-law and my husband.

sn: न स्मराम्युक्तपूर्वं वै स्वैरेष्वप्यनृतां गिरम्॥ तेन सत्येन तावद्य ध्रियेतां श्वशुरौ ममा
en: I do not remember to have offered a falsehood even in jest. By virtue of that truth may my father-in-law and mother-in-law remain alive this day.

sn: सत्यवानुवाच कामये दर्शनं पित्रोर्याहि सावित्रि मा चिरम्॥
en: Satyavana said: impatient to my parents. (Therefore), O Savitri, let us start immediately.

sn: पुरा मातुः पितुर्वापि यदि पश्यामि विप्रियम्। न जीविष्ये वरारोहे सत्येनात्मानमालभे॥
en: If I find my parents overtaken by any calamity, then, O fair girl, I swear by my own self I shall not bear life. I am see

sn: यदि धर्मे च ते बुद्धिर्मा चेज्जीवन्तमिच्छसि। मम प्रियं वा कर्तव्यं गच्छावाश्रममन्तिकात्॥
en: If you are devoted to virtue, if you wish to see me alive, if it is your duty to do what is agreeable to me, (then) let us return to the hermitage (at once).

sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच सावित्री तत उत्थाय केशान् संयम्य भाविनी। पतिमुत्थापयामास बाहुभ्यां परिगृह्य वै॥
en: Thereupon, the fair Savitri rose up and adjusted her hair. She (next) taking her husband by his arms made him arise.

sn: उत्थाय सत्यवांश्चापि प्रमृज्याङ्गानि पाणिना। सर्वा दिशः समालोक्य कठिने दृष्टिमादधे॥
en: Satyavana too having risen, rubbed his limbs with his hand. Then looking around all sides, he cast his eyes on the fruit bag.

sn: तमुवाचाथ सावित्री श्वः फलानि हरिष्यसि। योगक्षेमार्थमेतं ते नेष्यामि परशुं त्वहम्॥
en: And Savitri said to him “gather fruit tomorrow. I shall carry your hatchet which is conducive to your devotion and welfare."

sn: कृत्वा कठिनभारं सा वृक्षशाखावलम्बिनम्। गृहीत्वा परशुं भर्तुः सकाशे पुनरागमत्॥
en: (Having said this), she hanging the bag on the branch of a tree and taking the hatchet, returned to her husband.

sn: वामे स्कन्धे तु वामोरूर्भर्तुर्बाहुं निवेश्य च। दक्षिणेन परिष्वज्य जगाम गजगामिनी॥
en: Then that lady of fair thighs, placing her husband's left hand on her left shoulder and embracing him by her right hand proceeded slowly like an elephant.

sn: सत्यवानुवाच अभ्यासगमनाद् भीरु पन्थानो विदिता मम। वृक्षान्तरालोकितया ज्योत्स्नया चापि लक्षये॥
en: Satyavana said : Timid girl, the paths are well known to me as I go by them often. Further, by the moonlight falling between the trees I can discern them.

sn: आगतौ स्वः पथा येन पलान्यवचितानि च। यथागतं शुभे गच्छ पन्थानं मा विचारय॥
en: We have now reached the path we came by for gathering fruits. O auspicious girl, go along the way we took (in the morning) without hesitation.

sn: पलाशखण्डे चैतस्मिन् पन्था व्यावर्तते द्विधा। तस्योत्तरेण यः पन्थास्तेन गच्छ त्वरस्व च॥ स्वस्थोऽस्मि बलवानस्मि दिदृक्षुः पितरावुभौ।
en: Near yonder Palasa tree the road has branched off into two. Follow the path that lies to the north of it; be quick. I am now all right, have regained my strength and am very desirous of seeing my parents.

sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच ब्रुवन्नेवं त्वरायुक्तः सम्प्रायादाश्रमं प्रति॥
en: Saying this, he quickly proceeded towards the hermitage.

sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु धुमत्सेनो महाबलः। लब्धचक्षुः प्रसन्नायां दृष्ट्यां सर्वं ददर्श ह॥
en: Markandeya said : In the meantime, the highly-powerful Dyumatsena, being restored to his sight, could behold everything with a clear vision.

sn: स सर्वानाश्रमान् गत्वा शैब्यया सह भार्यया। पुत्रहेतोः परामाति जगाम भरतर्षभ॥
en: O most exalted of the Bharatas, accompanied by his wife Shaivya he visited all the hermitages in search of his son) and was greatly afflicted for his sake.

sn: तावाश्रमान् नदीश्चैव वनानि च सरांसि च। तस्यां निशि विचिन्वन्तौ दम्पती परिजग्मतुः॥
en: The (old) couple, at that night walked about searching (for their son) in all the hermitages, rivers, woods and lakes.

sn: श्रुत्वा शब्दं तु यं कञ्चिदुन्मुखौ सुतशङ्कया। सावित्रीसहितोऽभ्येति सत्यवानित्यभाषताम्॥
en: And as soon as they heard any sound, considering that it was (caused by the footsteps of) their son they raised up their heads and said “there comes Satyavana accompanied by Savitri."

sn: भिन्नैश्च परुषैः पादैः सव्रणैः शोणितोक्षितैः। कुशकण्टकविद्धाङ्गावुन्मत्ताविव धावतः॥
en: And with their feet torn, cracked, wounded and bleeding and pierced by thorns and Kusha blades they ran about like mad men.

sn: ततोऽभिसृत्य तैर्विप्रैः सर्वैराश्रमवासिभिः। परिवार्य समाश्वास्य तावानीतौ स्वमाश्रमम्॥
en: Then all the twice-born ones, dwelling in the (neighbouring) hermitages approached and surrounded them. And soothing the old couple they brought them back to their own hermitage.

sn: तत्र भार्यासहायः स वृतो वृद्धैस्तपोधनैः। आश्वासितोऽपि चित्रार्थैः पूर्वराज्ञां कथाश्रयैः॥
en: There the aged ascetics surrounding the old man together with his wife began to console him with stories of wonderful import about the kings of by gone ages.

sn: ततस्तौ पुनराश्वस्तौ वृद्धौ पुत्रदिदृक्षया। बाल्यवृत्तानि पुत्रस्य स्मरन्तौ भृशदुःखितौ॥
en: Although the old couple, eager to behold their son, thus comforted, the remembrance of the youthful days of their son again awakened deep sorrow in them.

sn: पुनरुक्त्वा च करुणां वाचं तौ शोककर्शितौ। हा पुत्र हा साध्वि वधूः क्वासि क्वासीत्यरोदताम्। ब्राह्मणः सत्यवाक् तेषामुवाचेदं तयोर्वचः॥
en: And weighed down with affliction, they again began to give vent to their grief in mournful accents saying "Alas, O son, O chaste daughter-in-law, where are you?" Then a truthful Brahmana told them these words.

sn: सुवर्चा उवाच ययास्य भार्या सावित्री तपसा च दमेन च। आचारेण च संयुक्ता तथा जीवति सत्यवान्॥
en: Suvarcha said: was "Satyavana is surely alive, because his wife Savitri is devoted to asceticism, is selfcontrolled and is well behaved."

sn: गौतम उवाच वेदाः साङ्गा मयाधीतास्तपो मे संचितं महत्। कौमारब्रह्मचर्यं च गुरवोऽग्निश्च तोषिताः॥
en: Gautama said: "I have read the Vedas together with all their branches and have laid up a great store of asceticism. I have led a life of celebacy, have gone through the Brahmacharya mode of life and have appeased the fire and my superiors.

sn: समाहितेन चीर्णानि सर्वाण्येव व्रतानि मे। वायुभक्षोपवासश्च कृतो मे विधिवत् पुरा॥
en: I have observed all the vows with a devout spirit; and agreeably to the ordinances I have very often subsisted on air alone and observed fasts.

sn: अनेन तपसा वेद्मि सर्वं परचिकीर्षितम्। सत्यमेतन्निबोधध्वं ध्रियते सत्यवानिति॥
en: By virtue of this asceticism I am aware of the doings of other people. Know this to be certain that Satyavana is alive.

sn: शिष्य उवाच उपाध्यायस्य मे वक्त्राद् यथा वाक्यं विनिःसृतम् नैव जातु भवेन्मिथ्या तथा जीवति सत्यवान्॥
en: The disciple of Gautama said : The words that have come out of the mouth of my preceptor can never be false. Therefore, Satyavana is (surely) alive.

sn: ऋषय ऊचुः यथास्य भार्या सावित्री सर्वैरेव सुलक्षणैः। अवैधव्यकरैर्युक्ता तथा जीवति सत्यवान्॥
en: The Rishis said : As his wife Savitri bears all the auspicious signs indicative of her exemption from widowhood, it is certain that Satyavana lives.

sn: भारद्वाज उवाच यथास्य भार्या सावित्री तपसा च दमेन च। आचारेण च संयुक्ता तथा जीवति सत्यवान्॥
en: Bharadvaja said : As his wife Savitri is possessed of devotion, self control and good behaviour, it admits of no doubt that Satyavana is alive.

sn: दाल्भ्य उवाच यथा दृष्टिः प्रवृत्ता ते सावित्र्याश्च यथा व्रतम्। गताऽऽहारमकृत्वा च तथा जीवति सत्यवान्॥
en: Dalbhya said: Considering that you have regained your sight and that Savitri has gone out without meals after the performance of her vow, it is certain that Satyavana is alive.

sn: आपस्तम्ब उवाच यथा वदन्ति शान्तायां दिशि वै मृगपक्षिणः। पार्थिवी च प्रवृत्तिस्ते तथा जीवति सत्यवान्॥
en: Mandyavya said: From the manner in which birds and beasts are sending forth their voices in the still atmosphere and since you have regained your sight making you useful for worldly purposes, it is sure that Satyavana lives.

sn: धौम्य उवाच सर्वैर्गुणैरुपेतस्ते यथा पुत्रो जनप्रियः। दीर्घायुर्लक्षणोपेतस्तथा जीवति सत्यवान्॥
en: Dhaumya said : Your son Satyavana is surely alive in as much as he is endued with all the noble qualities, beloved by all and bears signs indicative of a long life.

sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच एवमाश्वासितस्तैस्तु सत्यवाग्भिस्तपस्विभिः। तांस्तान् विगणयन् सर्वांस्ततः स्थिर इवाभवत्॥
en: Markandeya said : Thus consoled by those truthful sages and reflecting on the words they said, Dyumatsena became a little pacified.

sn: ततो मुहूर्तात् सावित्री भ; सत्यवता सह। आजगामाश्रमं रात्रौ प्रहृष्टा प्रविवेश ह॥
en: A moment after, Savitri accompanied by her husband Satyavana arrived at the asylum during the night and entered it cheerfully.

sn: ब्राह्मणा ऊचुः पुत्रेण संगतं त्वां तु चक्षुष्मन्तं निरीक्ष्य च। सर्वे वयं वै पृच्छामो वृद्धिं वै पृथिवीपते।॥
en: The Brahmanas said : O lord of the earth, we all congratulate you heartily on your union with your son and your recovery of eye sight.

sn: समागमेन पुत्रस्य सावित्र्या दर्शनेन च। चक्षुषश्चात्मनो लाभात् त्रिभिर्दिष्ट्या विवर्धसे॥
en: Your meeting with your son, your sight of Savitri and your restoration to sight, these three blessing will make you prosper.

sn: सर्वैरस्माभिरुक्तं यत् तथा तन्नात्र संशयः। भूयोभूयः समृद्धिस्ते क्षिप्रमेव भविष्यति॥
en: What we have said,, shall undoubtedly come to pass. You will soon rapidly grow in prosperity.

sn: ततोऽग्नि तत्र संज्वाल्य द्विजास्ते सर्व एव हि। उपासांचक्रिरे पार्थ धुमत्सेनं महीपतिम्॥
en: Markandeya said : Then, O Partha, all those twice born ones kindled a fire and took their seats before the king Dyumatsena.

sn: शैब्या च सत्यवांश्चैव सावित्री चैकतः स्थिताः। सर्वैस्तैरभ्यनुज्ञाता विशोकाः समुपाविशन्।॥
en: Shaivya, Satyavana and Savitri who all stood on one side, gladly sat down with the permission of them all.

sn: ततो राज्ञा सहासीनाः सर्वे ते वनवासिनः। जातकौतूहलाः पार्थं पप्रच्छुर्नृपतेः सुतम्॥
en: Then O Partha all those inhabitants of forest, who were seated with the king, actuated by curiosity asked the kings son.

sn: ऋषय ऊचुः प्रागेव नागतं कस्मात् सभार्येण त्वया विभो। विरात्रे चागतं कस्मात् कोऽनुबन्धस्तवाभवत्॥
en: The Rishis said : O renowned prince, why did you not make your appearance with your wife earlier? Why did you come so late at night? What obstacle stood in your way?

sn: संतापित: पिता माता वयं चैव नृपात्मज! कस्मादिति न जानीमस्तत् सर्वं वक्तुमर्हसि॥
en: O Prince, we can not make out why you have given so much pain to your father, mother and ourselves also. You ought to relate all this.

sn: सत्यवानुवाच पित्राहमभ्यनुज्ञातः सावित्री सहितो गतः। अथ मेऽभूच्छिरोदुःखं वने काष्ठानि भिन्दतः॥
en: Satyavana said: Taking leave of my father I went out with Savitri. While cutting down the woods in the forest my head began to ache.

sn: सुप्तश्चाहं वेदनया चिरमित्युपलक्षये। तावत् कालं न च मया सुप्तपूर्वं कदाचन॥
en: Afflicted with the pain I slept a long while. Thus far only do I remember. Never before did I sleep for so long a time.

sn: सर्वेषामेव भवतां संतापो मा भवेदिति। अतो विरात्रागमनं नान्यदस्तीह कारणम्॥
en: Considering that you all should not be troubled on my account, I came so late at night. There is no other reason (for my late arrival).

sn: गौतम उवाच अकस्माच्चक्षुषः प्राप्तिर्युमत्सेनस्य ते पितुः। नास्य त्वं कारणं वेत्सि सावित्री वक्तुमर्हति॥
en: Gautama said: You, then, do not know how your father Dyumatsena has suddenly recovered his eyes. Let, therefore, Savitri relate it.

sn: श्रोतुमिच्छामि सावित्रि त्वं हि वेत्थ परावरम्। त्वां हि जानामि सावित्रि सावित्रीमिव तेजसा॥
en: We are desirous of learning all this from you who are surely acquainted with the mysteries of good and evil. For, O Savitri, we know you are as resplendent as Savitri herself (the wife of Brahma).

sn: त्वमत्र हेतुं जानीषे तस्मात् सत्यं निरुच्यताम्। रहस्यं यदि ते नास्ति किंचिदत्र वदस्व नः॥
en: You are (undoubtedly) aware of the cause of this. Therefore speak truly. If you have nothing to conceal, then relate it to us.

sn: सावित्र्युवाच एवमेतद् यथा वेत्थ संकल्पो नान्यथा हि वः। न हि किंचिद् रहस्यं मे श्रूयतां तथ्यमेव यत्॥
en: Savitri said: It is as you know it to be. Your desire can never prove fruitless. I have nothing to conceal from you. Now hear the true cause of this.

sn: मृत्युर्मे पत्युराख्यातो नारदेन महात्मना। स चाद्य दिवसः प्राप्तस्ततो नैनं जहाम्यहम्॥
en: The high-souled Narada had fore told the death of my husband. Today being the appointed time, I did not leave his company.

sn: सुप्तं चैनं यमः साक्षादुपागच्छत् सकिङ्करः। स एनमनयद् बद्ध्वा दिशं पितृनिषेविताम्॥
en: When he fell asleep Yama in person together with his attendants approached him and tying him (with the noose) proceeded towards the region inhabited by the Pitris.

sn: अस्तौषं तमहं देवं सत्येन वचसा विभुम्। पञ्च वै तेन मे दत्ता वराः शृणुत तान् मम॥
en: I then began to eulogise that lord god, with truthful words, who conferred on me five boons. Hear of these (boons) from me.

sn: चक्षुषी च स्वराज्यं च द्वौ वरौ श्वशुरस्य मे। लब्धं पितुः पुत्रशतं पुत्राणां चात्मनः शतम्॥
en: I have obtained two boons for my father-inlaw viz. recovery of his sight and kingdom. I have (further), obtained for my father a hundred sons and an equal number of sons for myself.

sn: चतुर्वर्षशतायुर्मे भर्ता लब्धश्च सत्यवान्। भर्तुर्हि जीवितार्थं तु मया चीर्णं त्विदं व्रतम्॥
en: (Again) my husband Satyavana has been blessed with a life of four hundred years. I observed the vow for the sake of my husband's life.

sn: एतत् सर्वं मयाऽऽख्यातं कारणं विस्तरेण वः। यथावृत्तं सुखोदर्कमिदं दुःखं महन्मम॥
en: I have now faithfully described to you in detail the cause which ultimately turned my great sorrow into a crowing bliss.

sn: ऋषय ऊचुः निमज्जमानं व्यसनैरभिद्रुतं कुलं नरेन्द्रस्य तमोमये ह्रदे। त्वया सुशीलव्रतपुण्यया कुलं समुद्भूतं साध्वि पुनः कुलीनया॥
en: The Rishis said: O chaste girl, you are of gentle disposition, observant of vows, possessed of virtue and have sprung from a noble line. And it is by you that the line of this best of kings, overwhelmed with calamities and drowned in a deep gulf (of obscurity) has, (at last), been rescued.

sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच तथा प्रशस्य ह्यभिपूज्य चैव वरस्त्रियं तामृषयः समागताः। नरेन्द्रमामन्त्र्य सपुत्रमञ्जसा शिवेन जग्मुर्मुदिताः स्वमालयम्॥
en: Markandeya said : The assembled sages, then, having eulogised and paid their adorations to that most exalted lady and having taken leave of that most excellent of kings together with his son, soon left for their respective asylums in peace and with merry hearts.

sn: मार्कण्डेय उवाच तस्यां रात्र्यां व्यतीतायामुदिते सूर्यमण्डले। कृतपौर्वाणिकाः सर्वं समेयुस्ते तपोधनाः॥
en: Markandeya said : The night having come to a close, when the sun's disc had appeared (on the horizon), all th 'se ascetius, whose only wealth devotion, having performed their mations, congregated (at the asylum of Dyumatsena).

sn: तदेव सर्वं सावित्र्या महाभाग्यं महर्षयः। धुमत्सेनाय नातृप्यन् कथयन्तः पुनः पुनः॥
en: was Those great sages were never satisfied in relating again and again of the high fortune of Savitri, to Dyumatsena.

sn: ततः प्रकृतयः सर्वाः शाल्वेभ्योऽभ्यागता नृप। आचख्युनिहतं चैव स्वेनामात्येन तं द्विषम्॥
en: Then, O king, it so chanced that all the subjects came from Shalva and informed Dyumatsena of the death of his enemy at the hands of his own minister.

sn: तं मन्त्रिणा हतं श्रुत्वा ससहायं सबान्धवम्। न्यवेदयन् यथावृत्तं विद्रुतं च द्विषद्बलम्॥ ऐकमत्यं च सर्वस्य जनस्याथ नृपं प्रति। सचक्षुर्वाप्यचक्षुर्वा स नो राजा भवत्विति॥
en: And they related to him all that had taken place saying "hearing the death of the usurper together with his friends and allies at the hands of his own minister and of the dispersion of his troops, all the subjects have in one voice declared for you, their legitimate king and they have also said whether you are blind or not you shall be (their) king.

sn: अनेन निश्चयेनेह वयं प्रस्थापिता नृप। प्राप्तानीमानि यानानि चतुरङ्गं च ते बलम्॥
en: O king, we have been dispatched to you on the strength of this determination (on the part of your subjects to install you king). These cars and these four kinds of troops have arrived for you.

sn: प्रयाहि राजन् भद्रं ते घुष्टस्ते नगरे जयः। अध्यास्स्व चिररात्राय पितृपैतामहं पदम्॥
en: (Therefore), O monarch, do set out. May you prosper. Your restoration has been proclaimed in the city. May you for ever occupy the portion filled by your sire and grandsire."

sn: चक्षुष्मन्तं च तं दृष्ट्वा राजानं वपुषान्वितम्। मूर्धा निपतिताः सर्वे विस्मयोत्फुल्ललोचनाः॥
en: And seeing the king restored to sight and healthy, they with their eyes expanded in wonder, bowed down their heads to him.

sn: ततोऽभिवाद्य तान् वृद्धान् द्विजानाश्रमवासिनः। तैश्चाभिपूजितः सर्वैः प्रययौ नगरं प्रति॥
en: Then the king having greeted all the aged Brahmanas inhabiting the hermitage and in his turn being greeted by them, set out for his capital.

sn: शैब्या च सह सावित्र्या स्वास्तीर्णेन सुवर्चसा। नरयुक्तेन यानेन प्रययौ सेनया वृता॥
en: And Shaivya together with Savitri surrounded by troops, went in a palanquin, adorned with splendid sheets and carried by men.

sn: ततोऽभिषिषिचुः प्रीत्या धुमत्सेनं पुरोहिताः। पुत्रं चास्य महात्मानं यौवराज्येऽभ्यषेचयन्॥
en: Then the priests joyfully installed Dyumatsena as king and his high-souled son as prince regent.

sn: ततः कालेन महता सावित्र्याः कीर्तिवर्धनम्। तद् वै पुत्रशतं जज्ञे शूराणामनिवर्तिनाम्॥
en: After a long time Savitri was deliver of a hundred heroic and illustrious sons who never retreated from battle.

sn: भ्रातृणां सौदराणां च तथैवास्याभवच्छतम्। मद्राधिपस्याश्वपतेर्मालब्यां सुमहद् बलम्॥
en: She had also one hundred highly powerful uterine brothers begotten by Ashvapati, the king of Madra, on Malavi.

sn: एवमात्मा पिता माता श्वश्रूः श्वशुर एव च। भर्तुः कुलं च सावित्र्या सर्वं कृच्छ्रात् समुद्भुतम्॥
en: Thus Savitri rescued from misfortune, her own self, her father, mother-in law, father-inlaw and her husband's line.

sn: तथैवैषा हि कल्याणी द्रौपदी शीलसम्मता। तारयिष्यति वः सर्वान् सावित्रीव कुलाङ्गना॥
en: Similarly, the auspicious Draupadi of excellent character, will deliver you all from your misfortune as the virtuous Savitri did.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवं स पाण्डवस्तेन अनुनीतो महात्मना। विशोको विज्वरो राजन् काम्यके न्यवसत् तदा॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Thus, O monarch, instructed by that highsouled one ((Markandeya), the Pandava (Yudhishthira) devoid of grief and affliction continued to dwell in Kamyaka.

sn: यश्चेदं शृणुयाद् भक्त्या सावित्र्याख्यानमुत्तमम्। स सुखी सर्वसिद्धार्थो न दुःखं प्राप्नुयानरः॥
en: The man who listens with a devout spirit, to the excellent history of Savitri ever meets with happiness and success and never experiences sorrow.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: जनमेजय उवाच यत् तत् तदा महद् ब्रह्मल्लँलोमशो वाक्यमब्रवीत्। इन्द्रस्य वचनादेव पाण्डुपुत्रं युधिष्ठिरम्॥ यच्चापि ते भयं तीव्र न च कीर्तयसे क्वचित्। तच्चाप्यपहरिष्यामि धनंजय इतो गते॥ किं न तज्जपतां श्रेष्ठ कर्णं प्रति महद् भयम्। आसीन्न च स धर्मात्मा कथयामास कस्यचित्।।३।
en: Janamejaya said : O Brahmana, (you say) at that time, Lomasha conveyed to Yudhishthira, the son Pandu, a message from Indra in these words of grave consequence, “I will remove that great terror which you do not reveal to any one when Dhananjaya departs from this place," now tell me, O best of devotees, what this great fear was which Yudhishthira entertained in respect of Karna and why he did not reveal it to any one.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच अहं ते राजशार्दूल कथयामि कथामिमाम्। पृच्छतो भरतश्रेष्ठ शुश्रूषस्व गिरं मम॥
en: Vaishampayana said : O best of kings, I will relate that history to you, as asked by you. O best of the Bharatas, listen to my words.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: द्वादशे समतिक्रान्ते वर्षे प्राप्ते त्रयोदशे। पाण्डूनां हितकृच्छक्र: कर्ण भिक्षितुमुद्यतः॥
en: On the expiration of the twelfth year of their forest life when the thirteenth had set in, Shakra, the well-wisher of the Pandavas, resolved to ask Karna for his ear-rings.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: अभिप्रायमथो ज्ञात्वा महेन्द्रस्य विभावसुः। कुण्डलार्थे महाराज सूर्यः कर्णमुपागतः॥
en: But Vibhavasu (the sun) aware of the intentions of Mahendra about the ear-rings, O mighty Monarch, appeared before Karna.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: महार्हे शयने वीरं स्पास्तरणसंवृते। शयानमतिविश्वस्तं ब्रह्मण्यं सत्यवादिनम्॥
en: And when that truthful hero, devoted to the Brahmanas, was comfortably lying down on a costly bed furnished with a rich sheet.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: स्वप्नान्ते निशि राजेन्द्र दर्शयामास रश्मिवान्। कृपया परयाऽऽविष्टः पुत्रस्नेहाच्च भारत॥
en: The resplendent god, the sun, O king of kings, moved with great kindness consequent on paternal affection, showed himself, at night, in a dream, O Bharata.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: ब्राह्मणो वेदविद् भूत्वा सूर्यो योगर्द्धिरूपवान्। हितार्थमब्रवीत् कर्णं सान्त्वपूर्वमिदं वचः॥
en: And by his devotional power, wearing the shape of a handsome Brahmana, well read in the Vedas, the Sun addressed Karna for his welfare, these sweet words.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: कर्ण मद्वचनं तात शृणु सत्यभृतां वर। ब्रुवतोऽद्य महाबाहो सौहृदात् परमं हितम्॥
en: "O son, O Karna, O foremost of the truthful, O mighty-armed one, listen to these highly beneficial words of mine that I tell you today out of affection for you.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: उपायास्यति शक्रस्त्वां पाण्डवानां हितेप्सया। ब्राह्मणच्छद्मना कर्ण कुण्डलापजिहीर्षया॥
en: O Karna, Shakra with the desire of doing good to the Pandavas will come to you in the disguise of a Brahmana in order to have your ear-rings.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: विदितं तेन शीलं ते सर्वस्य जगतस्तथा। यथा त्वं भिक्षितः सद्भिर्ददास्येव न याचसे॥
en: This noble conduct on your part that when asked by the pious you give away to them whatsoever they ask but never beg, is known to Shakra himself and the world at large.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: तु वै त्वं हि तात ददास्येव ब्राह्मणेभ्यः प्रयाचितम्। वित्तं यच्चान्यदप्याहुन प्रत्याख्यासि कस्यचित्॥
en: O son, you bestow on the Brahmanas wealth or any other thing asked by them and never refuses anything to any one.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: त्वां चैवंविधं ज्ञात्वा स्वयं पाकशासनः। आगन्ता कुण्डलार्थाय कवचं चैव भिक्षितुम्॥
en: The vanquisher (of the Asura) Paka, who is well aware of this, will come to you in person, in order to beg your ear-rings and armour.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: तस्मै प्रयाचमानाय न देये कुण्डले त्वया। अनुनेयः परं शक्त्या श्रेय एतद्धि ते परम्॥
en: When he will ask for the ear-rings, you must not part with them but entreat him to the best of your power to make him desist; because that will tend to your greatest good.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: कुण्डलार्थे ब्रुवंस्तात कारणैर्बहुभिस्त्वया। अन्यैर्बहुविधैर्वित्तैः सन्निवार्यः पुनः पुनः॥
en: O son, when he will tell you about the earrings, you will, by showing various reasons, refuse him over and over again and offer him various other sorts of riches.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: रत्नैः स्त्रीभिस्तथा गोभिर्धनैर्बहुविधैरपि। निदर्शनैश्च बहुभिः कुण्डलेप्सुः पुरन्दरः॥
en: And you will try to appease Purandara, desirous of getting the ear-rings, by offering gems, women, cows, various sorts of riches and by citing precedents.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: यदि दास्यसि कर्ण त्वं सहजे कुण्डले शुभे। आयुषः प्रक्षयं गत्वा मृत्योर्वशमुपैष्यसि॥
en: If, O Karna, you part with those auspicious ear-rings with which you were born, your life will be shortened and you will be subject to death.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: कवचेन समायुक्तः कुण्डलाभ्यां च मानद। अवध्यस्त्वं रणेऽरीणामिति विद्धि वचो मम॥
en: O bestower of honours, arrayed in your armour and ear-rings you will be unslayable by your enemies in battle. Know these my words to be certain.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: अमृतादुत्थितं ह्येतदुभयं रत्नसम्भवम्। तस्माद् रक्ष्यं त्वया कर्ण जीवितं चेत् प्रियं तव॥
en: These two jewelled ear-rings have derived their origin from ambrosia. Therefore, they should be carefully preserved by you, if you have any love for your life.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: कर्ण उवाच को मामेवं भवान् प्राह दर्शयन् सौहृदं परम्। कामया भगवन् ब्रूहि को भवान् द्विजवेषधृक्॥
en: Karna said: Who are you, that, showing so great an affection for me, are addressing me thus? Tell me, O god, if you desire, who you are in the shape of a Brahmana.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच अहं तात सहस्रांशुः सौहृदात् त्वां निदर्शये। कुरुष्वैतद् वचो मे त्वमेतच्छ्रेयः परं हि ते॥
en: The Brahmana said : O child, I am the god of hundred rays (sun). Out of affection I give you this advice. Act in obedience to my advice as it is highly beneficial to you.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: कर्ण उवाच श्रेय एव ममात्यन्तं यस्य मे गोपतिः : प्रभुः। प्रवक्ताद्य हितान्वेषी शृणु चेदं वचो मम॥
en: Karna said : It is (no doubt) highly fortunate for me that the lord god of splendour, desirous of my welfare, speaks to me today. Listen to my words.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: प्रसादये त्वां वरदं प्रणयाच्च ब्रवीम्यहम्। न निवार्यो व्रतास्मादहं यद्यस्मि ते प्रियः॥
en: I am adoring you, who are the giver of boons and out of love am saying to you this. If I am at all dear to you, I should not be prevented (by you) from observing this vow.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: व्रतं वै मम लोकोऽयं वेत्ति कृत्स्नं विभावसो। यथाहं द्विजमुख्येभ्यो दद्यां प्राणानपि ध्रुवम्॥
en: O Vibhavasu, all the world is aware of this vow on my part that I am surely ever ready to give my very life to the best of Brahmanas.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: यद्यागच्छति मां शक्रो ब्राह्मणच्छद्यना वृतः। हितार्थं पाण्डुपुत्राणां खेचरोत्तम भिक्षितुम्॥ दास्यामि विबुधश्रेष्ठ कुण्डले वर्म चोत्तमम्। न मे कीर्तिः प्रणश्येत त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुता।॥
en: If, O best of sky-rangers, Shakra disguised as a Brahmana comes to me to beg (the earrings) for the good of the sons of Pandu, then, O best of the celestials, I will give the car-rings and the excellent armour. In that case my renown which has spread over the three worlds, will not be at a discount.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: मद्विधस्य यशस्यं हि न युक्तं प्राणरक्षणम्। युक्तं हि यशसा युक्तं मरणं लोकसम्मतम्॥
en: It is not at all proper for men like us to save life by a degrading act. Death coupled with honour and meeting with the approbation of the world is preferable.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: सोऽहमिन्द्राय दास्यामि कुण्डले सह वर्मणा। यदि मां बलवृत्रघ्नो भिक्षार्थमुपयास्यति॥
en: Therefore I will give the ear-rings together with the armour to Indra. If the slayer of Bala and Vritra comes to me to beg.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: हितार्थं पाण्डुपुत्राणां कुण्डले मे प्रयाचितुम्। तन्मे कीर्तिकरं लोके तस्याकीर्तिर्भविष्यति॥
en: The ear-rings for the good of the sons of Pandu, then the whole world will be redolent of my fame and will proclaim his infamy.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: वृणोमि कीर्ति लोके हि जीवितेनापि भानुमन्। कीर्तिमानश्नुते स्वर्ग हीनकीर्तिस्तु नश्यति॥
en: O Brahmana, I long for renown in this world even at the sacrifice of my life. Men having renown attain to heaven while those having none are lost.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: कीर्तिर्हि पुरुषं लोके संजीवयति मातृवत्। अकीर्तिर्जीवितं हन्ति जीवतोऽपि शरीरिणः॥
en: Even like a mother fame keeps people alive; but a man given to in famy is as good as dead even though his frame be not destroyed.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: अयं पुराणः श्लोको हि स्वयं गीतो विभावसो। धात्रा लोकेश्वर यथा कीर्तिरायुर्नरस्य ह॥
en: O Vibhavasu, O lord of the worlds, that fame is the very life of man is evident from the (following) ancient sloka (verse) sung by the creator himself.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: पुरुषस्य परे लोके कीतिरेव परायणम्। इह लोके विशुद्धा च कीर्तिरायुर्विवर्द्धनी॥
en: "In the next world fame leads men to supreme bliss while in this pure fame prolongs life."

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: सोऽहं शरीरजे दत्त्वा कीर्ति प्राप्स्यामि शाश्वतीम् दत्त्वा च विधिवद् दानं ब्राह्मणेभ्यो यथाविधि।॥ हुत्वा शरीरं संग्रामे कृत्वा कर्म सुदुष्करम्। विजित्य च परानाजौ यशः प्राप्स्यामि केवलम्॥
en: So, I will win an everlasting renown by giving (my car-rings) born with my body. By duly bestowing on the Brahmanas (gifts) sanctioned by ordinances, by sacrificing my life in battle on performing unachievable feats and by conquering my enemies I will win nothing but fame.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: भीतानामभयं दत्त्वा संग्रामे जीवितार्थिनाम्। वृद्धान् बालान् द्विजातींश्च मोक्षयित्वा महाभयात्॥ प्राप्स्यामि परमं लोके यशः स्वर्ग्यमनुत्तमम्। जीवितेनापि मे रक्ष्या कीर्तिस्तद् विद्धि मे व्रतम्॥
en: By sparing the affrighted in battle who crave their lives and delivering old men, children and the twicc-born ones, from great danger, I will win a great renown in this world and have access to the highest heaven (in the next).

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: सोऽहं दत्त्वा मघवते भिक्षामेतामनुत्तमाम्। ब्राह्मणच्छदिने देव लोके गन्ता परां गतिम्॥
en: Know this to be my solemn determination that I will preserve my fame even at the sacrifice of my very life.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: सूर्य उवाच माहितं कर्ण कार्षीस्त्वमात्मनः सुहृदां तथा। पुत्राणामथ भार्याणामथो मातुरथो पितुः॥
en: Surya said : O Karna, never do such acts as will lead to the injury of your own self, your friends, your sons, your wives, your mother and your father.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: शरीरस्याविरोधेन प्राणिनां प्राणभृद्वर। इष्यते यशसः प्राप्तिः कीर्तिश्च त्रिदिवे स्थिरा॥
en: O best of those that bear life, creatures do not wish to sacrifice their bodies for renown in this world and everlasting fame in heaven.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: यस्त्वं प्राणविरोधेन कीर्तिमिच्छसि शाश्वतीम्। सा ते प्राणान् गमिष्यति न संशयः॥
en: There is no doubt that the everlasting renown which you long for at the cost of your life, will deprive you of it.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: जीवतां कुरुते कार्यं पिता माता सुतास्तथा। ये चान्ये बान्धवाः केचिल्लोकेऽस्मिन् पुरुषर्षभ।॥
en: O most exalted of men, so long as a person is alive, his father, mother, son and other relations in this world are useful to him.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: राजानश्च नरव्याघ्र पौरुषेण निबोध तत्। कीर्तिश्च जीवतः साध्वी पुरुषस्य महाद्युते॥
en: The kings also, O best of men, can avail themselves of their prowess, so long as they are alive. Do understand it. O highly-resplendent being, fame is serviceable to living beings only.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: मृतस्य कीर्त्या किं कार्यं भस्मीभूतस्य देहिनः। मृतः कीर्ति न जानीते जीवन कीर्तिं समश्नुते॥
en: As regards a dead person whose frame has been reduced to ashes, what necessity is there for fame? It is not the dead but living persons that can enjoy fame.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: मृतस्या कीर्तिमर्त्यस्य यथा माला गतायुषः। अहं तु त्वां ब्रवीम्येतद् भक्तोऽसीति हितेप्सया॥
en: The fame of a dead person is like a garland (round the neck) of a man whose life is extinct. For the reason that you are a worshipper of mine I am telling you all this for your good,

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: भक्तिमन्तो हि मे रक्ष्या इत्येतेनापि हेतुना। भक्तोऽयं परया भक्त्या मामित्येव महाभुजा ममापि भक्तिरुत्पन्ना स त्वं कुरु वचो मम॥
en: And for this further reason that all my devotees should be protected protected by me. Considering, O mighty-amed one, that this person is a great devotee to me, I have been inclined to revere you. Therefore accept my advice.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: अस्ति चात्र परं किञ्चिदध्यात्मं देवनिर्मितम्। अतश्च त्वां ब्रवीम्येतत् क्रियतामविशङ्कया॥
en: A deep mystery ordained by fate, underlies all this. It is on this account that I am addressing you thus. Act (according to my words) and let no doubts cross your mind.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: देवगुह्यं त्वया ज्ञातुं न शक्यं पुरुषर्षभ। तस्मान्नाख्यामि ते गुह्यं काले वेत्स्यति तद् भवान्॥
en: O best of men, you are not fit to learn this which even the gods do not know. It is why I do not reveal it to you. You will, however know it in time.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: पुनरुक्तं च वक्ष्यामि त्वं राधेय निबोध तत्। मास्मै ते कुण्डले दद्या भिक्षिते वलापाणिना॥
en: O Radha's son, I am telling you again what I have already said. Pay attention to it. You will by no means give the ear-rings to the wielder of the thunderbolt when he will beg them (of you).

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: शोभसे कुण्डलाभ्यां च रुचिराभ्यां महाद्युते। विशाखयोर्मध्यगतः शशीव विमले दिवि॥
en: Adorned with your beautiful ear-rings you shine like the moon in the azure sky between the Vishakha constellations, O highly effulgent creature.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: कीर्तिश्च जीवतः साध्वी पुरुषस्येति विद्धि तत्। प्रत्याख्येयस्त्वया तात कुण्डलार्थे सुरेश्वरः॥
en: Know that fame is useful to a person so long as he is alive. Therefore, O son, you must refuse the lord of the celestials when he will beg the ear-rings.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: शक्या बहुविधैर्वाक्यैः कुण्डलेप्सा त्वयानघ। विहन्तुं देवराजस्य हेतुयुक्तैः पुनः पुनः॥
en: O sinless one, you will be able to do away with the eager desire of the lord of the gods for the ear-rings by repeatedly addressing him in various words coupled with reason.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: हेतुमदुपपन्नार्थैर्माधुर्यकृतभूषणैः। पुरन्दरस्य कर्ण त्वं बुद्धिमेतामपानुद॥
en: O Karna, remove the desire of Purandara by sweet and reasonable words consequence. of great

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: त्वं हि नित्यं नरव्याघ्र स्पर्धसे सव्यसाचिना। सव्यसाची त्वया चेह युधि शूरः समेष्यति॥
en: O most valiant of men, you always challenge Savyasachi (i.e. Arjuna who can draw the bow with his left hand) and the warlike Savyasachi too, will no doubt, encounter you in battle.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: न तु त्वामर्जुनः शक्तः कुण्डलाभ्यां समन्वितम्। विजेतुं युधि यद्यस्य स्वयमिन्द्रः सखा भवेत्॥
en: But arrayed in your ear-rings Arjuna, even with the assistance of Indra himself shall not be able to defeat you in battle.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: तस्मान्न देये शक्राय त्वयैते कुण्डले शुभे। संग्रामे यदि निर्जेतुं कर्ण कामयसेऽर्जुनम्॥
en: Therefore, O Karna, if you are at all desirous of defeating. Arjuna in battle, do not give your auspicious ear-rings to Shakra.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: कर्ण उवाच भगवन्तमहं भक्तो यथा मां वेत्थ गोपते। तथा परमतिग्मांशो नास्त्यदेयं कथंचन॥
en: Karna said: O god, O lord of splendour and scorching rays, you are as much aware of my being a worshipper of yours, (as of the fact) that there is nothing which I can not part with.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: न मे दारा न मे पुत्रा न चात्मा सुहृदो न च। तथेष्टा वै सदा भक्त्या यथा त्वं गोपते मम॥
en: By virtue of the reverence that I always feel for you, you are. O lord of splendour, dearer (to me) then my wife, my sons, my own self and my friends.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: इष्टानां च महात्मानो भक्तानां च न संशयः। कुर्वन्ति भक्तिमिष्टां च जानीषे त्वं च भास्कर।॥
en: O author of light, you are no doubt aware that high-souled persons cherish a high regard for their devoted worshipper.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: इष्टो भक्तश्च मे कर्णो न चान्यद् दैवतं दिवि। जानीत इति वै कृत्वा भगवानाह मद्धितम्॥
en: Considering that Karna is your devoted worshipper and that he known no other god in heavens, you have given me these instructions.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: भूयश्च शिरसा याचे प्रसाद्य च पुनः पुनः। इति ब्रवीमि तिग्मांशो त्वं तु मे क्षन्तुमर्हसि॥
en: Again with bended head and repeated prayers do I implore you and tell you this. O lord of searching rays, that you will (graciously) pardon me.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: विभेमि न तथा मृत्योर्यथा बिभ्येऽनृतादहम्। विशेषेण द्विजातीनां सर्वेषां सर्वदा सताम्॥ प्रदाने जीवितस्यापि न मेऽत्रास्ति विचारणा।
en: I do not fear death so much as falsehood. Especially for the sake of all the righteous twice-born ones ever, I am ready to sacrifice my life without (the least) hesitation.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: यच्च मामात्थ देव त्वं पाण्डवं फाल्गुनं प्रति॥ व्येतु संतापजं दुःखं तव भास्कर मानसम्। अर्जुनप्रतिमं चैव विजेष्यामि रणेऽर्जुनम्॥
en: As to what you have said to me about the Pandava Falguna. O author light, (I ask you) to dispel your caused by mental uneasiness regarding Arjuna and myself. (Because) I will surely defeat Arjuna in battle.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: तवापि विदितं देव ममाप्यस्त्रबलं महत्। जामदग्न्यादुपात्तं यत् तथा द्रोणान्महात्मनः॥
en: O god, you are no doubt aware of the great strength of my weapons which I have obtained from the son of Jamadagni (i.e. Parashuram) and from the high-souled Drona.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: इदं त्वमनुजानीहि सुरश्रेष्ठ व्रतं मम। भिक्षते वलिाणे दद्यामपि जीवितमात्मनः॥
en: O best of the gods, permit me now to observe the vow on my part that I may bestow my very life upon the begging wielder of the thunderbolt.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: सूर्य उवाच यदि तात ददास्येते वलिाणे कुण्डले शुभे। त्वमप्येनमथो ब्रूया विजयार्थं महाबलम्॥ नियमेन प्रदद्यां ते कुण्डले वै शतक्रतो।
en: Surya said: O highly-powerful son, if you bestow your beautiful car-rings to the wielder of the sorrow thunderbolt, you should, in order to secure victory, say to him, “O lord of hundred sacrifices, I can only part with my ear-rings under a condition."

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: अवध्यो ह्यसि भूतानां कुण्डलाभ्यां समन्वितः।१२॥ अर्जुनेन विनाशं हि तव दानवसूदनः। प्रार्थयानो रणे वत्स कुण्डले ते जिहीर्षति॥
en: As you cannot surely be slain by any creature when furnished with your earrings, so the destroyer of the Danavas, O son, wishing your death at the hands of Arjuna in battle, wants to rob you of your ear-rings.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: स त्वमप्येनमाराध्य सूनृताभिः पुनः पुनः। अभ्यर्थयेथा देवेशममोघार्थं पुरन्दरम्॥
en: Worshipping again and again with agreeable and truthful speeches the lord of the celestials, Purandara, the possessor of infallible weapons.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: अमोघां देहि मे शक्तिममित्रविनिबर्हिणीम्। दास्यामि ते सहस्राक्ष कुण्डले वर्म चोत्तमम्॥
en: You will say to him, “O thousand-eyed lord, I will give you the two ear-rings and the excellent armour, if you will bestow on me an infallible dart destructive of enemies."

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: इत्येव नियमेन त्वं दद्याः शक्राय कुण्डले। तया त्वं कर्ण संग्रामे हनिष्यसि रणे रिपून्।॥
en: It is under this condition only, O Karna, that you will give your ear-rings to Shakra. Then you will be able to destroy your enemies in battle.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: नाहत्वा हि महाबाहो शत्रूनेति करं पुनः। सा शक्तिर्देवराजस्य शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः॥
en: O mighty-armed one, that arrow of the lord of the gods does not return to the hand of the person who discharges it, without destroying hundreds and thousands of enemies.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्त्वा सहस्रांशुः सहसान्तरधीयत। ततः सूर्याय जप्यान्ते कर्णः स्वप्नं न्यवेदयत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Saying this, the lord of thousand rays suddenly became invisible. (The next day) Karna after having performed his devotions told the sun of the dreara.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: यथादृष्टं यथातत्त्वं यथोक्तमुभयोर्निशि। तत् सर्वमानुपूर्वेण शशंसास्मै वृषस्तदा॥
en: And Vrisha (Karna) faithfully related to him everything in detail, viz. his meeting with the sun and the conversation that took place between them during the nighi.

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: तच्छ्रुत्वा भगवान् देवो भानुः स्वर्भानुसूदनः। उवाच तं तथेत्येव कर्णं सूर्यः स्मयन्निव॥
en: Hearing all this, the divine lord Bhanu, the subduer of Svarbhanu (Rahu) spoke to Karna with a smile, "it is all true.”

description: The colloquy between Karna and Surya
sn: ततस्ततत्वमिति ज्ञात्वा राधेयः परवीरहा। शक्तिमेवाभिकाङ्क्षन् वै वासवं प्रत्यपालयत्॥
en: Then the son of Radha, the slayer of enemies, knowing all this to be true, awaited (the arrival of) Vasava, with the desire of obtaining the dart.

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA)-Continued The instructions (given) to Pritha (by her father
sn: जनमेजय उवाच किं तद् गुह्यं न चाख्यातं कर्णायेहोष्णरश्मिना। कीदृशे कुण्डले ते च कवचं चैव कीदृशम्॥१ कुतश्च कवचं तस्य कुण्डले चैव सत्तम। एतदिच्छाम्यहं श्रोतुं तन्मे ब्रूहि तपोधन॥
en: Janamejaya said : What was that secret which the god of hot rays did not give out to Karna? Of what nature were that coat of mail and those two ear-rings? Orighteous one, where did that armour and those two ear-rings of his spring from? O being whose wealth is devotion, I am curious to learn all this. Therefore relate to me all this.

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA)-Continued The instructions (given) to Pritha (by her father
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच अयं राजन् ब्रवीम्येतत् तस्य गुह्यं विभावसोः। यादृशे कुण्डले ते च कवचं चैव यादृशम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : O king, I am now relating to you the secret of the god having his rays for wealth and also of what sort the armour and the pair of earrings were.

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA)-Continued The instructions (given) to Pritha (by her father
sn: कुन्तिभोज पुरा राजन् ब्राह्मणः पर्युपस्थितः। तिग्मतेजा महाप्रांशुः श्मश्रुदण्डजटाधरः॥
en: Formerly, O monarch, there came a highlyenergetic Brahmana to Kuntibhoja. He was tall in stature, wore beard and matted locks, carried a staff in his hand.

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA)-Continued The instructions (given) to Pritha (by her father
sn: दर्शनीयोऽनवद्याङ्गस्तेजसा प्रज्वलनिव। मधुपिङ्गो मधुरवाक् तप:स्वाध्यायभूषणः॥
en: Was agreeable to look at and of faultless proportions and seemed as if burning in splendour. His complexion was yellow and he spoke sweet words. He was possessed of devotion and he studied the Vedas.

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA)-Continued The instructions (given) to Pritha (by her father
sn: स राजानं कुन्तिभोजमब्रवीत् सुमहातपाः। भिक्षामिच्छामि वै भोक्तुं तव गेहे विमत्सर॥
en: That Brahmana of great and excellent devotion said to king Kuntibhoja "O being that is free from pride, I am desirous of eating at your house (the food) obtained as alms.

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA)-Continued The instructions (given) to Pritha (by her father
sn: न मे व्यलीकं कर्तव्यं त्वया वा तव चानुगैः। एवं वत्स्यामि ते गेहे यदि ते रोचतेऽनघ॥
en: I can, if you like it, dwell at your house under the condition that neither you nor your attendants will cross me in any way.

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA)-Continued The instructions (given) to Pritha (by her father
sn: यथाकामं च गच्छेयमागच्छेयं तथैव च। शय्यासने च मे राजन् नापराध्येत कश्चन॥
en: I will go out and come in at my pleasure. And O king, with regard to my food or bed no body shall disturb me."

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA)-Continued The instructions (given) to Pritha (by her father
sn: तमब्रवीत् कुन्तिभोजः प्रीतियुक्तमिदं वचः। एवमस्तु परं चेति पुनश्चैनमथाब्रवीत्॥
en: (Then) Kuntibhoja gladly said these words "be it so and even more than this.” And he told him again thus.

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA)-Continued The instructions (given) to Pritha (by her father
sn: मम कन्या महाप्राज्ञ पृथा नाम यशस्विनी। शीलवृत्तान्विता साध्वी नियता चैव भाविनी॥
en: "O highly wise one, I have a renowned daughter, Pritha by name. That damsel is endowed with good manners, is observant of vows, chaste and self-controlled.

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA)-Continued The instructions (given) to Pritha (by her father
sn: उपस्थास्यति सा त्वां वै पूजयानवमन्य च। तस्याश्च शीलवृत्तेन तुष्टिं समुपयास्यसि॥
en: She, without despising you, will wait on you and minister to your comforts. And you also will be pleased with her (graceful) manners.”

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA)-Continued The instructions (given) to Pritha (by her father
sn: एवमुक्त्वा तु तं विप्रमभिपूज्य यथाविधि। उवाच कन्यामभ्येत्य पृथां पृथुललोचनाम्॥
en: Saying this and duly worshipping that Brahmana, he (the king) went to his daughter Pritha, endued with large eyes and said to her thus,

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA)-Continued The instructions (given) to Pritha (by her father
sn: अयं वत्से महाभागो ब्राह्मणो वस्तुमिच्छति। मम गेहे मया चास्य तथेत्येवं प्रतिश्रुतम्॥
en: "This highly fortunate Brahmana, O child, wishes to dwell in my house. I have promised hiin this saying “be it so."

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA)-Continued The instructions (given) to Pritha (by her father
sn: त्वयि वत्से पराश्वस्य ब्राह्मणस्याभिराधनम्। तन्मे वाक्यममिथ्या त्वं कर्तुमर्हसि कर्हिचित्॥
en: O child, you will minister to this Brahimana with great skill. And you will act in such a way as not to belie my words.

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA)-Continued The instructions (given) to Pritha (by her father
sn: अयं तपस्वी भगवान् स्वाध्यायनियतो द्विजः। यद् यद् ब्रूयान्महातेजास्तत्तद् देयममत्सरात्॥
en: What this highly-energetic, reverend and ascetic twice-born one devoted to the study of the Vedas, asks for, will be given him without and pride.

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA)-Continued The instructions (given) to Pritha (by her father
sn: ब्राह्मणो हि परं तेजो ब्राह्मणो हि परं तपः। ब्राह्मणानां नमस्कारैः सूर्यो दिवि विराजते॥
en: A Brahmana represents the highest energy and the highest devotion, and it is in virtue of the devoutness of the Brahmanas that the sun shines in the heavens.

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA)-Continued The instructions (given) to Pritha (by her father
sn: अमानयन् हि मानार्हान् वातापिश्च महासुरः। निहतो ब्रह्मदण्डेन तालजङ्घस्तथैव च।॥
en: Disregarding those that deserve honour, the great Asura, Vatapi, as well Talajangha, met with destruction by virtue of the curse of the Brahmanas.

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA)-Continued The instructions (given) to Pritha (by her father
sn: सोऽयं वत्से महाभार आहितस्त्वयि साम्प्रतम्। त्वं सदा नियता कुर्या ब्राह्मणस्याभिराधनम्॥
en: O child, now this highly fortunate one is entrusted to your care. You should be particularly careful in ministering to him.

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA)-Continued The instructions (given) to Pritha (by her father
sn: जानामि प्रणिधानं ते बाल्यात् प्रभृति नन्दिनि। ब्राह्मणेष्विह सर्वेषु गुरुबन्धुषु चैव ह॥ तथा प्रेष्येषु सर्वेषु मित्रसम्बन्धिमातृषु। मयि चैव यथावत् त्वं सर्वमावृत्य वर्तसे॥
en: O daughter, I am aware, that since your very infancy you have been ever attentive to the Brahmanas, all your superiors, all the servants, friends, relations, your mothers and myself. You have a proper regard for every one.

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA)-Continued The instructions (given) to Pritha (by her father
sn: न हतुष्टो जनोऽस्तीह पुरे चान्तःपुरे च ते। सम्यग्वृत्त्यानवद्याङ्गि तव भृत्यजनेष्वपि॥
en: O girl of faultless proportions, on account of your good dealings no one in the city or in the palace, even none of your servants, is displeased with you.

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA)-Continued The instructions (given) to Pritha (by her father
sn: संदेष्टव्यां तु मन्ये त्वां द्विजाति कोफ्नं प्रति। पृथे बालेति कृत्वा वै सुता चासि ममेति च॥
en: I have, therefore, thought you fit for the ministration of the Brahmanas, who as a rule, are of irritable temper. O Pritha, you are a girl (yet) and my daughter by adoption.

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA)-Continued The instructions (given) to Pritha (by her father
sn: वृष्णीनां च कुले जाता शूरस्य दयिता सुता। दत्ता प्रीतिमता मह्यं पित्रा बाला पुरा स्वयम्॥
en: You have sprung from the race of the Vrishnis and are the beloved daughter of Shura. Formerly, your father himself gladly mmade you over to me.

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA)-Continued The instructions (given) to Pritha (by her father
sn: वसुदेवस्य भगिनी सुतानां प्रवरा मम। अग्र्यमग्रे प्रतिज्ञाय तेनासि दुहिता मम॥
en: You are the sister of Vasudeva and the foremost of my daughter. You are my daughter in virtue of the promises made by your father that he should give his first born to me.

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA)-Continued The instructions (given) to Pritha (by her father
sn: तादृशे हि कुले जाता कुले चैव विवर्धिता। सुखात् सुखमनुप्राप्ता ह्रदाद्धदमिवागता।॥
en: Born in such a line and brought up in this race, you have like a lotus, transferred from one lake to another, attained to one blissful state from another.

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA)-Continued The instructions (given) to Pritha (by her father
sn: दौष्कुलेया विशेषेण कथंचित् प्रग्रहं गताः। बालभावाद् विकुर्वन्ति प्रायशः प्रमदाः शुभे॥
en: O beautiful girl, women, especially those that are born in low families, although they are with great difficulty kept under restraint, are generally of deformed character on account of their unripe age.

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA)-Continued The instructions (given) to Pritha (by her father
sn: पृथे राजकुले जन्म रूपं चापि तवाद्भुतम्। तेन तेनासि सम्पन्ना समुपेता च भाविनी॥
en: O Pritha, you have been born in a kingly line and you are gifted with a wonderful beauty. And O girl, you are graced with every accomplishment.

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA)-Continued The instructions (given) to Pritha (by her father
sn: सा त्वं दर्पं परित्यज्य दम्भं मानं च भाविनि। आराध्य वरदं विप्रं श्रेयसा योक्ष्यसे पृथे॥
en: So, O damsel, O Pritha, giving up your pride, haughtiness and the sense of your high position, you will minister to this Brahmana capable of bestowing boons. In that case you will surely be blessed.

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA)-Continued The instructions (given) to Pritha (by her father
sn: एवं प्राप्स्यसि कल्याणि कल्याणमनघे ध्रुवम्। कोपिते च द्विजश्रेष्ठे कृत्स्नं दह्येत मे कुलम्॥
en: By acting in such a way, O auspicious and sinless girl, you will certainly attain to blissfulness. But if you stir up the wrath of this foremost of the twice born ones, he will consume my entire race."

description: Ministrations by Pritha to the twice born one
sn: कुन्त्युवाच ब्राह्मणं यन्त्रिता राजन्नुपस्थास्यामि पूजया। यथाप्रतिज्ञं राजेन्द्र न च मिथ्या ब्रवीम्यहम्॥
en: Kunti said: "O king of kings, agreeably to your promise, I will, by restraining my senses, wait upon and minister to that Brahmana. I am speaking no falsehood (in this respect).

description: Ministrations by Pritha to the twice born one
sn: एष चैव स्वभावो मे पूजयेयं द्विजानिति। तव चैव प्रियं कार्यं श्रेयश्च परमं मम॥
en: To worship the Brahmanas is my habit. And as this is agreeable to you, it will lead to my highest good.

description: Ministrations by Pritha to the twice born one
sn: यद्येवैष्यति सायाह्ने यदि प्रातरथो निशि। यद्यर्धरात्रे भगवान् न मे कोपं करिष्यति॥
en: He will never have any cause to be angry with me whether the worshipful one comes in the morning or in the evening or during the night or at midnight.

description: Ministrations by Pritha to the twice born one
sn: लाभो ममैष राजेन्द्र यद् वै पूजयती द्विजान्। आदेशे तव तिष्ठन्ती हितं कुर्यां नरोत्तम॥
en: O king of kings, O best of men, it is highly beneficial to me to worship the twice-born ones, to carry out your commands and to do good to you.

description: Ministrations by Pritha to the twice born one
sn: विस्रब्धो भव राजेन्द्र न व्यलीकं द्विजोत्तमः। वसन् प्राप्स्यति ते गेहे सत्यमेतद् ब्रवीमि ते॥
en: O foremost of kings, rest assured of it. I am telling you truly that the best of Brahmanas dwelling in your house will not in any way be dissatisfied..

description: Ministrations by Pritha to the twice born one
sn: यत् प्रियं च द्विजस्यास्य हितं चैव तवानघ। यतिष्यामि तथा राजन् व्येतु ते मानसो ज्वरः॥
en: I will pay (particular) attention to what is agreeable to this Brahmana and to what is beneficial to you. Therefore O king, give up your mental anxiety.

description: Ministrations by Pritha to the twice born one
sn: ब्राह्मणा हि महाभागाः पूजिताः पृथिवीपते। तारणाय समर्थाः स्युर्विपरीते वधाय च॥
en: The Brahmanas, O lord of the earth, are highly fortunate and when pleased are capable of bestowing salvation. But if displeased, they become (instruments) for destruction.

description: Ministrations by Pritha to the twice born one
sn: साहमेतद् विजानन्ती तोषयिष्ये द्विजोत्तमम्। न मत्कृते व्यथां राजन् प्राप्स्यसि द्विजसत्तमात्॥
en: I, who am well aware of this, will propitiate this foremost of Brahmanas, And O king, you will never, for any act of mine, experience any trouble from that most exalted of Brahmanas.

description: Ministrations by Pritha to the twice born one
sn: अपराधेऽपि राजेन्द्र राज्ञामश्रेयसे द्विजाः। भवन्ति च्यवनो यद्वत् सुकन्यायाः कृते पुरा॥
en: O foremost of kings, owing to the faults of the kings, the twice-born ones become the instruments of their misfortune as formerly Chyavana had become on account of the acts of Sukanya.

description: Ministrations by Pritha to the twice born one
sn: नियमेन परेणाहमुपस्थाये द्विजोत्तमम्। यथा त्वया नरेन्द्रेदं भाषितं ब्राह्मणं प्रति॥
en: Agreeably to your instructions with regard to this Brahmana, I will serve him with great regularity, O king of kings."

description: Ministrations by Pritha to the twice born one
sn: एवं ब्रुवन्तीं बहुशः परिष्वज्य समर्थ्य च। इति चेति च कर्तव्यं राजा सर्वमथादिश॥
en: And when she said thus repeatedly, the king encouraged and embraced her and then instructed her minutely as to what she ought to do.

description: Ministrations by Pritha to the twice born one
sn: एवमेतत् त्वया भद्रे कर्तव्यमविशङ्कया। मद्धितार्थं तथाऽऽत्मार्थं कुलार्थं चाप्यनिन्दिते॥
en: “O gentle and blameless girl, you will act in this way, without any fear, for my welfare, for your good and for the welfare of the race."

description: Ministrations by Pritha to the twice born one
sn: राजोवाच एवमुक्त्वा तु तां कन्यां कुन्तिभोजो महायशाः। पृथां परिददौ तस्मै द्विजाय द्विजवत्सलः॥
en: The King said : Saying this, the highly-renowned Kuntibhoja, devoted to the Brahmanas, made over his daughter Pritha to that twice-born one.

description: Ministrations by Pritha to the twice born one
sn: इयं ब्रह्मन् मम सुता बाला सुखविवर्धिता। अपराध्येत यत् किंचिन्न कार्यं हृदि तत् त्वया॥
en: (Saying), “O Brahmana, this is my daughter (Pritha) of tender years and reared in luxury. If she commits any fault, do not mind it.

description: Ministrations by Pritha to the twice born one
sn: द्विजातयो महाभागा वृद्धबालतपस्विषु। भवन्त्यक्रोधनाः प्रायो ह्यपराद्धेषु नित्यदा।॥
en: The highly renowned Brahmanas do not get angry with old men, ascetics and children, even if they repeatedly offend them.

description: Ministrations by Pritha to the twice born one
sn: सुमहत्यपराधेऽपि क्षान्ति: कार्या द्विजातिभिः। यथाशक्ति यथोत्साहं पूजा चाह्या द्विजोत्तम॥
en: The twice-born ones again ought to pardon even a very serious offence; and the best of Brahmanas should accept that worship which is offered to the best of one's ability and exertion.

description: Ministrations by Pritha to the twice born one
sn: तथेति ब्राह्मणेनोक्तं स राजा प्रीतमानसः। हंसचन्द्रांशुसंकाशं गृहमस्मै न्यवेदयत्॥
en: And that Brahmana having said “be it so," the king with a merry mind placed at his disposal a suite of apartments white as the swan or the ray of the moon.

description: Ministrations by Pritha to the twice born one
sn: तत्राग्निशरणे क्लृप्तमासनं तस्य भानुमत्। आहारादि च सर्वं तत् तथैव प्रत्यवेदयत्॥
en: And in the fire-room the king placed a resplendent seat especially made for him and also all sorts of food and other articles of the same good quality.

description: Ministrations by Pritha to the twice born one
sn: निक्षिप्य राजपुत्री तु तन्द्रीं मानं तथैव च। आतस्थे परमं यत्नं ब्राह्मणस्याभिराधने॥
en: And driving away her idleness and pride, the princess began to exert herself with the utmost care for the service of the Brahmana.

description: Ministrations by Pritha to the twice born one
sn: तत्र सा ब्राह्मणं गत्वा पृथा शौचपरा सती। विधिवत् परिचारार्ह देववत् पर्यतोषयत्॥
en: And going to the Brahmana there in the fire-room) the chaste Pritha, observant of purity, duly ministering to him as if he were a god, pleased him highly.

description: The initiation of Pritha into the Mantras
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच सा तु कन्या महाराज ब्राह्मणं संशितव्रतम्। तोषयामास शुद्धेन मनसा संशितव्रता॥
en: Vaishampayana said : O great monarch, that damsel observant of vows, began with a pure heart, to propitiate that vow observing Brahmana.

description: The initiation of Pritha into the Mantras
sn: प्रातरेष्याम्यथेत्युक्त्वा कदाचिद् द्विजसत्तमः। तत आयाति राजेन्द्र सायं रात्रावथो पुनः॥
en: O king of kings, that foremost of Brahmanas sometimes saying “I will come in the morning" made his appearance in the evening or at night.

description: The initiation of Pritha into the Mantras
sn: तं च सर्वासु वेलासु भक्ष्यभोज्यप्रतिश्रयैः। पूजयामास सा कन्या वर्धमानैस्तु सर्वदा॥
en: (But) that damsel at all hours entertained him with excellent food, drink and bed.

description: The initiation of Pritha into the Mantras
sn: अन्नादिसमुदाचाराः शय्यासनकृतस्तथा। दिवसे दिवसे तस्य वर्धते न तु हीयते॥
en: And her hospitality towards him as regards his food, seat and bed increased rather than decreased day by day.

description: The initiation of Pritha into the Mantras
sn: निर्भर्त्सनापवादैश्च ततैवाप्रियया गिरा। ब्राह्मणस्य पृथा राजन् न चकाराप्रियं तदा॥
en: Even if the Brahmana reproved, found fault with and spoke harsh words, to her, Pritha did not do anything disagreeable to him.

description: The initiation of Pritha into the Mantras
sn: व्यस्ते काले पुनश्चैति न चैति बहुशो द्विजः। सुदुर्लभमपि ह्यन्नं दीयतामिति सोऽब्रवीत्॥
en: At several times the Brahmana came after the appointed time or did never come at all and (on many occasions) asked for food when it could only be procured with utmost difficulty.

description: The initiation of Pritha into the Mantras
sn: कृतमेव च तत् सर्वं यथा तस्मै न्यवेदयत्। शिष्यवत् पुत्रवच्चैव स्वसृवच्च सुसंयता॥
en: (But at all these times) Pritha said "everything is ready," and placed the meal before him. And like a disciple, like a daughter or like a sister, with a pure heart.

description: The initiation of Pritha into the Mantras
sn: यथोपजोषं राजेन्द्र द्विजातिप्रवरस्य सा। प्रीतिमुत्पादयामास कन्यारत्नमनिन्दिता।॥
en: That faultless jewel of a damsel, O king of kings, caused the satisfaction of that foremost of the Brahmanas as he liked.

description: The initiation of Pritha into the Mantras
sn: तस्यास्तु शीलवृत्तेन तुतोष द्विजसत्तमः। अवधानेन भूयोऽस्याः परं यत्नमथाकरोत्॥
en: That most exalted of the twice-born ones was highly pleased with her manners and character and on account of her ministrations tried his very best for her welfare.

description: The initiation of Pritha into the Mantras
sn: तां प्रभाते च सायं च पिता पप्रच्छ भारत। अपि तुष्यति ते पुत्रि ब्राह्मणः परिचर्यया॥
en: And O Bharata, her father asked her every morning "O daughter, is the Brahmana satisfied with your ministrations?”

description: The initiation of Pritha into the Mantras
sn: तं सा परममित्येव प्रत्युवाच यशस्विनी। तत: प्रीतिमवापायां कुन्तिभोजो महामनाः॥
en: And that renowned damsel replied “yes very much". Thereupon, the high-minded Kuntibhoja felt a great joy.

description: The initiation of Pritha into the Mantras
sn: ततः संवत्सरे पूर्णे यदासौ जपतां वरः। नापश्यद् दुष्कृतं किंचित् पृथायाः सौहृदे रतः॥
en: When on the expiration of a whole year, that best of devotees could not find any cause to be dissatisfied with Pritha, devoted to his service.

description: The initiation of Pritha into the Mantras
sn: तः प्रीतमना भूत्वा स एनां ब्राह्मणोऽब्रवीत्। प्रीतोऽस्मि परमं भद्रे परिचारेण ते शुभे॥
en: That Brahmana, then, with a joyful heart said to her “O gentle and graceful maid, I have been highly pleased with your ministrations.

description: The initiation of Pritha into the Mantras
sn: वरान् वृणीष्व कल्याणि दुरापान् मानुषैरिह। यैस्त्वं सीमन्तिनी: सर्वा यशसाभिभविष्यसि॥
en: O auspicious girl, ask for (such) a boon as is very difficult for men to receive in this word, by virtue of which you will be able to ecclipse all the ladies in fame.

description: The initiation of Pritha into the Mantras
sn: कुन्त्युवाच कृतानि मम सर्वाणि यस्या मे वेदवित्तम। त्वं प्रसन्नः पिता चैव कृतं विप्र वरैर्मम॥
en: Kunti said: O best of those versed in the Vedas, all my desires have been gratified in as much as you as well as my father are pleased with me. So, O Brahmana, I think I have already received boons.

description: The initiation of Pritha into the Mantras
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच यदि नेच्छसि मत्तस्त्वं वरं भद्रे शुचिस्मिते। इमं मन्त्रं गृहाण त्वमाह्वानाय दिवौकसाम्॥
en: The Brahmana said: O gentle girl of sweet smiles, if you do not desire for boons from me, then take this Mantra for invoking the gods.

description: The initiation of Pritha into the Mantras
sn: यं यं देवं त्वमेतेन मन्त्रेणावाहयिष्यसि। तेन तेन वशे भद्रे स्थातव्यं ते भविष्यति॥
en: Whatever god you may invoke by (uttering) this Mantra, he will be, O gentle girl, quite under your control.

description: The initiation of Pritha into the Mantras
sn: अकामो वा सकामो वा स समेष्यति ते वशे। विबुधो मत्रसंशान्तो भवेद् भृत्य इवानतः॥
en: Whether he desires or not, that god, (whom you may invoke) by virtue of the mantra (will come to you) in a gentle guise and like a slave will be subject to you.

description: The initiation of Pritha into the Mantras
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच न शशाक द्वितीयं सा प्रत्याख्यातुमनिन्दिता। तं वै द्विजातिप्रवरं तदा शापभयानृप॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Then O king, afraid of being cursed by that foremost of the twice-born ones, that faultless girl could not refuse him a second time.

description: The initiation of Pritha into the Mantras
sn: ततस्तामनवद्याङ्गीं चाहयामास स द्विजः। मन्त्रग्राम तदा राजन्नथर्वशिरसि श्रुतम्॥
en: Then, O monarch, that Brahmana initiated that girl of faultless proportions into the Mantras, placed in the beginning of the Atharvaveda.

description: The initiation of Pritha into the Mantras
sn: तं प्रदाय तु राजेन्द्र कुन्तिभोजमुवाच ह। उषितोऽस्मि सुखं राजन् कन्यया परितोषितः॥ तव गेहेषु विहितः सदा सुप्रतिपूजितः। साधयिष्यामहे तावदित्युक्त्वान्तरधीयत।२२।।
en: O lord of kings, having thus initiated her (into the mantras), he said to Kuntibhoja, “O Monarch, being always duly worshipped and gratified by your daughter I have lived happily in your house. I will now depart". Saying this he vanished away.

description: The initiation of Pritha into the Mantras
sn: स तु राजा द्विजं दृष्ट्वा तत्रैवान्तर्हितं तदा। बभूव विस्मयाविष्टः पृथां च समपूजयत्॥
en: The king was wonder-struck at beholding him vanish at that very spot. He then properly adored Pritha.

description: The invoking of Surya by Kunti
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच गते तस्मिन् द्विजश्रेष्ठे कस्मिंश्चित् कारणान्तरे। चिन्तयामास सा कन्या मन्त्रग्रामबलाबलम्॥
en: That best of the twice-born ones having gone away on some other business, the maiden began to think of the efficacy or otherwise of the Mantras.

description: The invoking of Surya by Kunti
sn: अयं वै कीदृशस्तेन मम दत्तो महात्मना। मन्त्रचामो बलं तस्य ज्ञास्ये नातिचिरादिति॥
en: "Of what manner are these Mantras imparted to me by that high-souled one? I shall soon test their efficacy."

description: The invoking of Surya by Kunti
sn: एवं संचिन्तयन्ती सा ददर्शर्तुं यदृच्छया। वीडिता साभवद् बाला कन्याभावे रजस्वला॥
en: While thus musing (within herself) she suddenly perceived that she attained puberty. Having attained maturity during her maidenhood, the girl was covered with shame.

description: The invoking of Surya by Kunti
sn: ततो हर्म्यतलस्था सा महार्हशयनोचिता। प्राच्यां दिशि समुद्यन्तं ददर्शादित्यमण्डलम्॥
en: And as she was seated on a costly bed in her room she beheld the sun's disc rising in the east.

description: The invoking of Surya by Kunti
sn: तत्र बद्धमनोदृष्टिरभवत् सा सुमध्यमा। न चातप्यत रूपेण भानोः संध्यागतस्य सा॥
en: And both the mind and the eye of that slender-waisted girl were steadfastly fixed on the solar orb. She did not feel satiety at beholding the beauty of the morning sun.

description: The invoking of Surya by Kunti
sn: तस्या दृष्टिरभूद् दिव्या सापश्यद् दिव्यदर्शनम्। आमुक्तकवचं देवं कुण्डलाभ्यां विभूषितम्॥
en: She was, then, all on a sudden gifted with celestials sight. And she perceived the deity of divine form clad in armour and decked with ear-rings.

description: The invoking of Surya by Kunti
sn: तस्याः कौतूहलं त्वासीन्मन्त्रं प्रति नराधिप। आह्वानमकरोत् साथ तस्य देवस्य भाविनी॥
en: O lord of men, her curiosity was then excited to test the efficacy of the Mantras; and the maiden made up her mind to invoke that god.

description: The invoking of Surya by Kunti
sn: प्राणानुपस्पृश्य तदा ह्याजुहाव दिवाकरम्। आजगाम ततो राजंस्त्वरमाणो दिवाकरः॥
en: Having gone through Pranayam, she invoked the author of the day. And, O king, the sun too speedily appeared before her.

description: The invoking of Surya by Kunti
sn: मधुपिङ्गो महाबाहुः कम्बुग्रीवो हसन्निव। अङ्गदी बद्धमुकुटो दिशः प्रज्वालयन्निव॥
en: His complexion was yellow like honey, he had mighty arms and his neck resembled a conch. And wearing bracelets and a diadem he came as if setting ablaze all the directions.

description: The invoking of Surya by Kunti
sn: योगात् कृत्वा द्विधाऽऽत्मानमाजगाम तताप च। आबभाषे ततः कुन्ती साम्ना परमवल्गुना॥
en: Having recourse to Yoga he divided himself in twain, one of which began to impart heat and the other appeared (before Kunti). He then addressed Kunti in very sweet words thus,

description: The invoking of Surya by Kunti
sn: आगतोऽस्मि वशं भद्रे तव मन्त्रबलात्कृतः। किं करोमि वशो राज्ञि ब्रूहि कर्ता तदस्मि ते॥
en: Gentle lady, drawn by the power of your Mntras, I have come under your power. Now that I have been subject to your power, tell me, Queen, what I shall do. I shall do whatever you may command me.

description: The invoking of Surya by Kunti
sn: कुन्त्युवाच गम्यतां भगवंस्तत्र यत एवागतो ह्यसि। कौतूहलात् समाहूतः प्रसीद भगवन्निति॥
en: Kunti said: O god, go to that place from which you have come. It is through curiosity that you have been invoked. O worshipful one, pardon me (for my folly).

description: The invoking of Surya by Kunti
sn: सूर्य उवाच गमिष्येऽहं यथा मां त्वं ब्रवीषि तनुमध्यमे। न तु देवं समाहूय न्याय्यं प्रेषयितुं वृथा॥
en: Surya said : O slender-waisted damsel, I will go away as you tell me. (But) it is not proper to send away a deity in vain after having invoked him.

description: The invoking of Surya by Kunti
sn: तवाभिसंधिः सुभगे सूर्यात् पुत्रो भवेदिति। वीर्येणाप्रतिमो लोके कवची कुण्डलीति च॥
en: O fortunate damsel, your desire is to have from Surya a son, of unrivalled prowess in the world and furnished with a coat-of-mail and ear-rings.

description: The invoking of Surya by Kunti
sn: सा त्वमात्मप्रदानं वै कुरुष्व गजगामिनि। उत्पत्स्यति हि पुत्रस्ते यथासंकल्पमङ्गने॥
en: O maid, endued with the gait of an elephant, surrender yourself to me. O damsel, you will then, have a son as you desire.

description: The invoking of Surya by Kunti
sn: अथ गच्छाम्यहं भद्रे त्वया संगम्य सुस्मिते। यदि त्वं वचनं नाद्य करिष्यसि मम प्रियम्॥ शपिष्ये त्वामहं क्रुद्धो ब्राह्मणं पितरं च ते। त्वत्कृते तान् प्रधक्ष्यामि सर्वानपि न संशयः॥
en: O damsel of sweet siniles, I will go away after having enjoyed you. If you today do not comply with my words and gratify my desire, I will angrily curse you, that Brahmana and your father also. And I will undoubtedly consume them all for your fault.

description: The invoking of Surya by Kunti
sn: पितरं चैव ते मूढं यो न वेत्ति तवानयम्। तस्य च ब्राह्मणस्याद्य योऽसौ मन्त्रमदात् तव॥
en: I will severely chastise both your stupid father who is unaware of this offence on your part and that Brahmana who, without knowing your character and manners has imparted the mantras to you. All the gods in heaven with Purandara at their head.

description: The invoking of Surya by Kunti
sn: शीलवृत्तमविज्ञाय धास्यामि विनयं परम्। एते हि विबुधाः सर्वे पुरन्दरमुखा दिवि॥ त्वया प्रलब्धं पश्यन्ति स्पयन्त इव भाविनि। पश्य चैनान् सुरगणान् दिव्यं चक्षुरिदं हि ते। पूर्वमेव मया दत्तं दृष्टवत्यसि येन माम्॥
en: O lady, seeing me deceived by you are laughing at me. Behold those celestials with your divine sight, which I bestowed on you before, in virtue of which you were able to see me.

description: The invoking of Surya by Kunti
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततोऽपश्यत् त्रिदशान् राजपुत्री सर्वानेव स्वेषु धिष्ण्येषु खस्थान्। प्रभावन्तं भानुमन्तं महान्तं यथाऽऽदित्यं रोचमानांस्तथैव॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Then the king's daughter, saw in the heavens those celestials stationed in their respective places, as she had seen before Aditya endued with rays and great effulgence.

description: The invoking of Surya by Kunti
sn: सा तान् दृष्ट्वा वीडमानेव बाला सूर्यं देवी वचनं प्राह भीता। गच्छ त्वं वै गोपते स्वं विमानं कन्याभावाद् दुःख एवापचारः॥
en: Beholding them, the maiden was covered with shame. And being alarmed, the damsel spoke these words to Surya “O lord of rays, go to your own place. This outrage on your part is greatly distressing to me as I am a maiden.

description: The invoking of Surya by Kunti
sn: पिता माता गुरवश्चैव येऽन्ये देहस्यास्य प्रभवन्ति प्रदाने। नाहं धर्म लोपयिष्यामि लोके स्त्रीणां वृत्तं पूज्यते देहरक्षा॥
en: Father, mother and other superiors only are competent to bestow my person. I will not surrender my virtue. In this world keeping their bodies (pure) is considered to be the highest duty on the part of women.

description: The invoking of Surya by Kunti
sn: मया मन्त्रबलं ज्ञातुमाहूतस्त्वं विभावसो। बाल्याद् बालेति तत् कृत्वा क्षन्तुमर्हसि मे विभो।।२४।
en: O deity possessed of the wealth of effulgence, in order to test the potency of the Mantras, I have, through mere childish curiosity, invoked you. O god, you should pardon me, considering that it has been done by a mere girl."

description: The invoking of Surya by Kunti
sn: सूर्य उवाच बालेति कृत्वानुनयं तवाह ददानि नान्यानुनयं लभेत। आत्मप्रदानं कुरु कुन्तिकन्ये शान्तिस्तवैवं हि भवेच्च भीरु॥
en: Surya said: It is on the consideration that you are a mere girl, that I am entreating you (thus). But others can not expect this from me. O damsel, O Kunti, surrender your person to me. O timid girl, you wil, then surely attain to peacefulness.

description: The invoking of Surya by Kunti
sn: न चापि गन्तुं युक्तं हि मया मिथ्याकृतेन वै। असमेत्य त्वया भीरु मन्त्राहूतेन भाविनि॥
en: O timid girl, when you have invoked me by the help of the mantras, I should not go away in vain without enjoying you.

description: The invoking of Surya by Kunti
sn: गमिष्याम्यनवद्याङ्गि लोके समवहास्यताम्। सर्वेषां विबुधानां च वक्तव्यः स्यां तथा शुभे॥
en: If, O damsel of faultless proportions, I go away (thus), I shall be the laughing stock of the whole world and an object of ridicule with the celestials.

description: The invoking of Surya by Kunti
sn: सा त्वं मया समागच्छ लप्स्यसे मादृशं सुतम्। विशिष्टा सर्वलोकेषु भविष्यसि न संशयः॥
en: Therefore, surrender yourself to me. You will then have a son like myself and will undoubtedly be extolled in all the worlds.

description: The enjoyment of Pritha by Surya
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच सा तु कन्या बहुविदं ब्रुवन्ती मधुरं वचः। अनुनेतुं सहस्रांशुं न शशाक मनस्विनी॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Though that high-minded damsel spoke very many sweet words (to Surya) she could by no means soften him of a thousand rays.
