description: The enjoyment of Pritha by Surya
sn: न शशाक यदा बाला प्रत्याख्यातुं तमोनुदम्। भीता शापात् ततो राजन् दध्यौ दीर्घमथान्तरम्॥
en: And when all the entreaties of that maiden to the dispeller of darkness were unavailing, afraid of her curse she long meditated thus

description: The enjoyment of Pritha by Surya
sn: अनागसः पितुः शापो ब्राह्मणस्य तथैव च। मनिमित्तः कथं न स्यात् क्रुद्धादस्माद् विभावसोः॥
en: “How may my unoffending father and that Brahmana be saved from the curse of the wrathful Vibhavasu on my account?

description: The enjoyment of Pritha by Surya
sn: बालेनापि सता मोहाद् भृशं पापकृतान्यपि। नाभ्यासादयितव्यानि तेजांसि च तपांसि च॥
en: Although energy and asceticism destructive of sins, yet even honest persons of tender years, through foolishness ought not to draw them near.

description: The enjoyment of Pritha by Surya
sn: साहमद्य भृशं भीता गृहीता च करे भृशम। कथं त्वकार्यं कुर्यां वै प्रदानं ह्यात्मनः स्वयम्॥
en: are (By acting foolishly) I have been today seriously alarmed and have been placed entirely in the power (of Surya). How can I myself (without the consent of my guardians) do this sinful act, the surrender of my person (to him)"?

description: The enjoyment of Pritha by Surya
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच सा वै शापपरित्रस्ता बहु चिन्तयती हृदा। मोहेनाभिपरीताङ्गी स्मयमाना पुनः पुनः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Afraid of (his) curse she reflected much in her mind. Her limbs were quite paralysed and she was repeatedly at a loss as to how to act.

description: The enjoyment of Pritha by Surya
sn: तं देवमब्रवीद् भीता बन्धूनां राजसत्तम। व्रीडाविह्वलया वाचा शापत्रस्ता विशाम्पते॥
en: Oforemost of kings, O lord of the world, afraid of the censure of her friends and afflicted with the fear of curse, she spoke to that deity these words tremulous with bashfulness.

description: The enjoyment of Pritha by Surya
sn: कुन्त्युवाच पिता मे ध्रियते देव माता चान्ये च बान्धवाः। न तेषु ध्रियमाणेषु विधिलोपो भवेदयम्॥
en: Kunti said: O god, my father is alive and so also my mother and friends. And since they are (still) living, this violation of duty (on my part) is not allowable.

description: The enjoyment of Pritha by Surya
sn: त्वया तु संगमो देव यदि स्याद् विधिवर्जितः। मन्निमित्तं कुलस्यास्य लोके कीर्तिनशेत् ततः॥
en: If, O god, I hold this unlawful intercourse with you, then the reputation of this race will be destroyed for my sake.

description: The enjoyment of Pritha by Surya
sn: अथवा धर्ममेतं त्वं मन्यसे तपतां वर। ऋते प्रदानाद् बन्धुभ्यस्तव कामं करोम्यहम्॥
en: Or if you consider it a virtue, I will then, O best of those that shed heat, gratify your desire even without being given away to you by my friends.

description: The enjoyment of Pritha by Surya
sn: आत्मप्रदानं दुधर्ष तव कृत्वा सती त्वहम्। त्वयि धर्मो यशश्चैव कीर्तिरायुश्च देहिनाम्॥
en: As O irrepressible one, the virtue, the reputation, the renown and the life of all embodied beings are established in you, may I remain chaste after having yielded my person to you.

description: The enjoyment of Pritha by Surya
sn: सूर्य उवाच न ते पिता न ते माता गुरवो वा शुचिस्मिते। प्रभवन्ति वरारोहे भद्रं ते शृणु मे वचः॥
en: Surya said: O beautiful damsel of sweet smiles, neither your father, nor your mother nor your superiors are competent to bestow you. May you be happy. Hear what I say.

description: The enjoyment of Pritha by Surya
sn: सर्वान् कामयते यस्मात् कमेर्धातोश्च भाविनि। तस्मात् कन्येह सुश्रोणि स्वतन्त्रा वरवर्णिनि॥
en: O damsel, the term Kanya, derived from the root Kama (to desire) is applied to a maiden, because she desires (in have intercourse with) every body. Therefore, fair-hipped girl of excellent complexion, she is free (to act as she chooses) in this world.

description: The enjoyment of Pritha by Surya
sn: नाधर्मश्चरितः कश्चित् त्वया भवति भाविनि। अधर्मं कुत एवाहं वरेयं लोककाम्यया॥
en: You will, O beauteous girl, on no account fall away from virtue (by satisfying my desire). How can I, who seek the welfare of everybody commit an act of sin?

description: The enjoyment of Pritha by Surya
sn: अनावृताः स्त्रियः सर्वा नराश्च वरवर्णिनि। स्वभाव एष लोकानां विकारोऽन्य इति स्मृतः॥
en: O fair complexioned girl, it is the human nature that all men and women should be without restraint. And it is asserted that the contrary (condition) is (its) perversion.

description: The enjoyment of Pritha by Surya
sn: सा मया सह संगम्य पुनः कन्या भविष्यसि। पुत्रश्च ते महाबाहुर्भविष्यति महायशाः॥
en: You will also remain a virgin even after having held intercourse with me and your son will be of mighty arms and high renown.

description: The enjoyment of Pritha by Surya
sn: कुन्त्युवाच यदि पुत्रो मम भवेत् त्वत्तः सर्वतमोनुद। कुण्डली कवची शूरो महाबाहुर्महाबलः॥
en: Kunti said : O dispeller of all darkness, if I have a son by powerful and furnished with a coat-of-mail and ear-rings.

description: The enjoyment of Pritha by Surya
sn: सूर्य उवाच भविष्यति महाबाहुः कुण्डली दिव्यवर्मभृत्। उभयं चामृतमयं तस्य भद्रे भविष्यति॥
en: Surya said : Gentle maiden, your (son) will be mightyarmed, furnished with ear-rings and an impenetrable and celestials armour made of Amrita.

description: The enjoyment of Pritha by Surya
sn: कुन्त्युवाच यद्येतदमृतादस्ति कुण्डले वर्म चोत्तमम्। मम पुत्रस्य यं वै त्वं मत्त उत्पादयिष्यसि॥ अस्तु मे सङ्गमो देव यथोक्तं भगवंस्त्वया। त्वद्वीर्यरूपसत्त्वौजा धर्मयुक्तो भवेत् स च॥
en: Kunti said: If both the ear-rings and the armour of the son you will beget on me, be made of Amrita, then, O god, you may enjoy me, as your worshipful self has said. And may he (the son) be powerful, beautiful, strong energetic and virtuous like you.

description: The enjoyment of Pritha by Surya
sn: सूर्य उवाच अदित्या कुण्डले राज्ञि दत्ते मे मत्तकाशिनि। तेऽस्य दास्यामि वै भीरु वर्म चैवेदमुत्तमम्॥
en: Surya said: O queen, O beauteous and timid damsel, I will bestow on him these ear-rings which were given to me by Aditi and also this excellent armour.

description: The enjoyment of Pritha by Surya
sn: कुन्त्युवाच परमं भगवन्नेवं संगमिष्ये त्वया सह। यदि पुत्रो भवेदेवं यथा वदसि गोपते॥
en: Kunti said: O adorable one, it is very well. O lord of rays, if I have such a son as you say, then I snall giatify your desire.

description: The enjoyment of Pritha by Surya
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तथेत्युक्त्वा तु तां कुन्तीमाविवेश विहङ्गमः। स्वर्भानुशत्रुर्योगात्मा नाभ्यां पस्पर्श चैव ताम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having said to her "be it so” that ranger of sky, the enemy of Svarbhanu, with his soul absorbed in yoga entered into Kunti and touched her on the naval.

description: The enjoyment of Pritha by Surya
sn: ततः सा विह्वलेवासीत् कन्या सूर्यस्य तेजसा। पपात चाथ सा देवी शयने मूढचेतना॥
en: Thereupon, that damsel became stupefied by the energy of the sun and fell down on her bed insensible.

description: The enjoyment of Pritha by Surya
sn: सूर्य उवाच साधयिष्यामि सुश्रोणि पुत्रं वै जनयिष्यसि। सर्वशस्त्रभृतां श्रेष्ठं कन्या चैव भविष्यसि॥
en: Surya said : O fair-hipped maiden, I shall now disappear. You will give birth to a son who will be the foremost of all wielders of arms.

description: The enjoyment of Pritha by Surya
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततः सा वीडिता बाला तदा सूर्यमथाब्रवीत्। एवमस्त्विति राजेन्द्र प्रस्थितं भूरिवर्चसम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Then, O king of kings, that maiden said bashfully to the highly resplendent Surya who was about to go away “may it be so."

description: The enjoyment of Pritha by Surya
sn: इति स्मोक्ता कुन्तिराजात्मजा सा विवस्वन्तं याचमाना सलज्जा। तस्मिन् पुण्ये शयनीये पपात मोहाविष्टा भज्यमाना लतेव॥
en: Thus the daughter of Kuntiraja, having bashfully asked for a son from Vivasvata fell down unconscious on her auspicious bed like a broken creeper.

description: The enjoyment of Pritha by Surya
sn: तिग्मांशुस्तां तेजसा मोहयित्वा योगेनाविश्यात्मसंस्थां चकार। न चैवैनां दूषयामास भानुः संज्ञां लेभे भूय एवाथ बाला॥
en: And that deity of hot rays making her insensible by his energy placed himself within her by his yoga power. But Bhanu did not corrupt her. The girl, then (i.e. when the sun had departed) recovered her senses.

description: The desertion of Karna by his mother
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततो गर्भः समभवत् पृथायाः पृथिवीपते। शुक्ले दशोत्तरे पक्षे तारापतिरिवाम्बरे॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Then, O lord of the earth, like the lord of the stars in the heavens, Pritha conceived a son on the first day of the lighted fortnight during the tenth month.

description: The desertion of Karna by his mother
sn: सा बान्धवभयाद् बाला गर्भं तं विनिगूहती। धारयामास सुश्रोणी न चैनां बुबुधे जनः॥
en: That fair-hipped damsel afraid of the censure of her friends concealed her pregnancy, so that no body was aware of her real state.

description: The desertion of Karna by his mother
sn: न हि तां वेद नार्यन्या काचिद् धात्रेयिकामृते। कन्यापुरगतां बालां निपुणां परिरक्षणे॥
en: And as that girl lived in the apartments of maidens, no other women knew her condition except her nurse's daughter who was wellskilled in ministrations.

description: The desertion of Karna by his mother
sn: ततः कालेन सा गर्भं सुषुवे वरवर्णिनी। कन्यैव तस्य देवस्य प्रसादादमरप्रभम्॥
en: (And) in time that damsel of excellent complexion by the favour of that god, Surya, was delivered of a son beautiful as a celestials.

description: The desertion of Karna by his mother
sn: तथैवाबद्धकवचं काकोज्ज्वलकुण्डलम्। हर्यक्षं वृषभस्कन्धं यथास्य पितरं तथा॥
en: And like his father he was clad in armour, adorned with brilliant golden ear-rings, endued with leonine eyes and bovine shoulders.

description: The desertion of Karna by his mother
sn: जातमात्रं च तं गर्भ धान्या सम्मन्य भाविनी। मञ्जूषायां समाधाय स्वास्तीर्णायां समन्ततः॥ मधूच्छिष्टस्थितायां सा सुखायां रुदती तथा। श्लक्ष्णायां सुपिधानायामश्वनद्यामवासृजत्॥
en: And as soon as her delivery took place that girl, in consultation with her nurse, placed her child in a water-proof basket, covered all over with sheets, made of wicker work, smooth, comfortable and furnished with a beautiful pillow. And with tearful eyes she consigned it to the (waters of) the river Ashva.

description: The desertion of Karna by his mother
sn: जानती चाप्यकर्तव्यं कन्याया गर्भधारणम्। पुत्रस्नेहेन सा राजन् करुणं पर्यदेवयत्॥
en: O king of kings, though she knew that it was not proper for a maiden to be big with child, yet from her affection towards the child she wept bitterly.

description: The desertion of Karna by his mother
sn: समुत्सृजन्ती मञ्जूषामश्वनद्यां तदा जले। उवाच रुदती कुन्ती यौनि वाक्यानि तच्छृणु॥
en: And hear the words which Kunti uttered while she, weeping bitterly, consigned the basket to the waters of the river Ashva.

description: The desertion of Karna by his mother
sn: स्वस्ति ते चान्तरिक्षेभ्यः पार्थिवेभ्यश्च पुत्रका दिव्येभ्यश्चैव भूतेभ्यस्तथा तोयचराश्च ये॥
en: "O son, may all the creatures inhabiting the firmament, the earth, the celestials regions and the water contribute to your welfare.

description: The desertion of Karna by his mother
sn: शिवास्ते सन्तु पन्थानो मा च ते परिपन्थिनः। आगताच तथा पुत्र भवन्त्वद्रोहचेतसः॥
en: May all your ways be auspicious and unobstructed. And, O son, may the minds of those that may meet with you, be not inclined to enmity towards you.

description: The desertion of Karna by his mother
sn: पातु त्वां वरुणो राजा सलिले सलिलेश्वरः। अन्तरिक्षेऽन्तरिक्षस्थः पवनः सर्वगस्तथा॥
en: On the waters may king Varuna, the lord of waters, protect you. And similarly may Pavana (the wind-god) who ranges in the sky and wanders everywhere protect you in the sky.

description: The desertion of Karna by his mother
sn: पिता त्वां पातु सर्वत्र तपनस्तपतां वरः। येन दत्तोऽसि मे पुत्र दिव्येन विधिना किल॥
en: O son, may your father, the foremost of those that shed heat and by whom you have been begotten on me by the ordinance of Destiny preserve you everywhere.

description: The desertion of Karna by his mother
sn: आदित्या वसवो रुद्राः साध्या विश्वे च देवताः। मरुतश्च सहेन्द्रेण दिशश्च दसिगीश्वराः॥
en: And may you be protected by the Adityas, the Vasus, the Rudras, the Sadhyas the Vishvadevas, the Marutas and the cardinal points together with their guardians and Indra.

description: The desertion of Karna by his mother
sn: रक्षन्तु त्वां सुराः सर्वे समेषु विषमेषु च। वेत्स्यामि त्वां विदेशेऽपि कवचेनाभिसूचितम्॥
en: And may all the gods protect you in every state whether favourable or adverse. Even in foreign countries I shall be able to recognise you on account of your coat-of-mail.

description: The desertion of Karna by his mother
sn: धन्यस्ते पुत्र जनको देवो भानुर्विभावसुः। यस्त्वां द्रक्ष्यति दिव्येन चक्षुषा वाहिनीगतम्॥
en: Blessed is indeed your divine father, Bhanu, having effulgence for his wealth, who by means of his celestials sight, beholds you going down the stream.

description: The desertion of Karna by his mother
sn: धन्या सा प्रमदा या त्वां पुत्रत्वे कल्पयिष्यति। यस्यास्त्वं तृषितः पुत्र स्तनं पास्यसि देवज॥
en: And O son of a deity, that lady is also blessed who will adopt you as her son and feed you from her breast when you are thirsty.

description: The desertion of Karna by his mother
sn: को नु स्वप्नस्तया दृष्टो या त्वामादित्यवर्चसम्। दिव्यवर्मसमायुक्तं दिव्यकुण्डलभूषितम्॥ पद्मायतविशालाक्षं पद्मताम्रदलोज्वलम्। सुललाटं सुकेशान्तं पुत्रत्वे कल्पयिष्यति॥
en: What a dream she has dreamed who will adopt for her son you who are resplendent as the sun, clad in a celestials armour, adorned with celestials ear-rings, endued with broad and expansive eyes like lotuses, possessed of a complexion bright as the copper-coloured lotus-leaves, graced with a beautiful forehead and beautiful hair.

description: The desertion of Karna by his mother
sn: धन्या द्रक्ष्यन्ति पुत्र त्वां भूमौ संसर्पमाणकम्। अव्यक्तकलवाक्यानि वदन्तं रेणुगुण्ठितम्॥
en: They are also blessed, O son, who will behold you crawl on the ground covered with dust and who will hear your sweet inarticulate speech.

description: The desertion of Karna by his mother
sn: धन्या द्रक्ष्यन्ति पुत्र त्वां पुनर्योवनगोचरम्। हिमवद्वनसम्भूतं सिंहं केसरिणं यथा॥
en: Blessed are they too, who will see you arrive at manhood like a mained lion of the Himalayan forests.

description: The desertion of Karna by his mother
sn: एवं बहुविधं राजन् विलप्य करुणं पृथा। अवासृजत मञ्जूषामश्वनद्यास्तदा जले॥
en: Having, O king, thus wept long and bitterly, Pritha then consigned the basket to the waters of the river Ashva.

description: The desertion of Karna by his mother
sn: रुदती पुत्रशोकार्ता निशीथे कमलेक्षणा। धात्र्या सह पृथा राजन् पुत्रदर्शनलालसा॥
en: And, O monarch, accompanied by her nurse the lotus-eyed Pritha desirous of beholding her son again and again and overpowered with grief for her son and weeping piteously, at night.

description: The desertion of Karna by his mother
sn: विसर्जयित्वा मञ्जूषां सम्बोधनभयात् पितुः। विवेश राजभवनं पुनः शोकातुरा ततः॥
en: Laid the basket (on the waters of the Ashva) and entered into the palace with a heavy heart lest her father might know (the secret).

description: The desertion of Karna by his mother
sn: मञ्जूषा त्वश्वनद्याः सा ययौ चर्मण्वती नदीम्। चर्मण्वत्याश्च यमुनां ततो गङ्गां जगाम ह॥
en: (On the other hand) the basket came from the Ashva to the river Charmavati, from the Charınavati to the Yamuna and thence to the Ganga.

description: The desertion of Karna by his mother
sn: गङ्गायाः सूतविषयं चप्पामनुययौ पुरीम्। स मञ्जूषागतो गर्भस्तरङ्गरुह्यमानकः॥
en: And that basket containing the child, borne along the waves of the Ganga arrived at the city of Champa in the Suta territory.

description: The desertion of Karna by his mother
sn: अमृतादुत्थितं दिव्यं तनुवर्म सकुण्डलम्। धारयामास तं गर्भं दैवं च विधिनिर्मितम्॥
en: And that child was kept alive on account of the celestials mail and ear-rings both made of Amrita and also on account of the ordinance of Destiny.

description: The obtaining of Karna by Radha
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु धृतराष्ट्रस्य वै सखा। सूतोऽधिरथ इत्येव सदारो जाह्नवीं ययौ॥
en: Vaishampayana said : At this time one Adhiratha of the Suta tribe and a friend of Dhritarashthra's accompanied by his wife came to the Jahnavi (Ganga).

description: The obtaining of Karna by Radha
sn: तस्य भार्याभवद् राजन् रूपेणासदृशी भुवि। राधा नाम महाभागा न सा पुत्रमविन्दत॥
en: O monarch, his wife named Radha was peerless in beauty on earth. That highly fortunate lady had no son.

description: The obtaining of Karna by Radha
sn: अपत्यार्थे परं यत्नमकरोच्च विशेषतः। सा ददर्शाथ मञ्जूषामुह्यमानां यदृच्छया॥
en: Although, she made the very best endeavours to obtain one. She, then, beheld drifting along the stream, a basket.

description: The obtaining of Karna by Radha
sn: दत्तरक्षाप्रतिसरामन्वालम्भनशोभनाम्। ऊर्मीतरङ्गैर्जाह्नव्याः समानीतामुपह्वरम्॥
en: Containing things preventive of dangers and dyed with saffron. And (that basket) was carried before her by the waves of the Janhavi.

description: The obtaining of Karna by Radha
sn: सा तु कौतूहलात् प्राप्तां ग्राहयामास भाविनी। ततो निवेदयामास सूतस्याधिरथस्य वै॥
en: And that lady, impelled by curiosity had it seized. She then told all to Adhiratha of the Suta caste.

description: The obtaining of Karna by Radha
sn: स तामुद्धृत्य मञ्जूषामुत्सार्य जलमन्तिकात्। यन्त्रैरुद्धाटयामास सोऽपश्यत् तत्र बालकम्॥
en: He (Adhiratha) then carried the basket from the water-side and had it opened by instruments. And therein he teheld a boy.

description: The obtaining of Karna by Radha
sn: तरुणादित्यसंकाशं हेमवर्मधरं तथा। मृष्टकुण्डलयुक्तेन वदनेन विराजता॥
en: (Beautiful) as the morning sun, clad in a golden armour and with a beautiful face adorned with brilliant ear-rings.

description: The obtaining of Karna by Radha
sn: स सूतो भार्यया सार्धं विस्मयोत्फुल्ललोचनः। अङ्कमारोप्य तं बालं भार्यां वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: That Suta together with his wife with eyes expanded in wonder, took the infant on his lap and spoke these words to her.

description: The obtaining of Karna by Radha
sn: इदमत्यद्भुतं भीरु यतो जातोऽस्मि भाविनी। दृष्टवान् देवगर्भोऽयं मन्येऽस्मान् समुपागतः॥
en: "O timid lady, since my very birth I have never witnessed such a marvel. I think, this boy that has come to us, is begotten by a celestials,

description: The obtaining of Karna by Radha
sn: अनपत्यस्य पुत्रोऽयं देवैर्दत्तो ध्रुवं मम। इत्युक्त्वा तं ददौ पुत्रं राधायै स महीपते॥
en: Surely, considering that I have no son, the gods have sent this child to me.” O lord of the earth, saying this, he made over the child to Radha.

description: The obtaining of Karna by Radha
sn: प्रतिजग्राह तं राधा विधिवद् दिव्यरूपिणम्। पुत्रं कमलगर्भामं देवगर्भं श्रिया वृतम्॥
en: Thereupon, Radha duly adopted that body of celestials appearance and birth, endued with the splendour of the filaments of lotuses and possessed of excellent grace.

description: The obtaining of Karna by Radha
sn: पुपोष चैनं विधिवद् ववृधे स च वीर्यवान्। ततः प्रभृति चाप्यन्ये प्रभावन्नौरसाः सुताः॥
en: She brought him properly up and that mighty boy too began to grow up. Since that time he (Adhiratha) had other sons begotten by him.

description: The obtaining of Karna by Radha
sn: वसुवर्मधरं दृष्ट्वा तं बालं हेमकुण्डलम्। नामास्य वसुषेणेति ततश्चक्रुर्द्विजातयः॥
en: The twice-born ones seeing the boy ciad in a golden armour and adorned with golden earrings called him Vasusena.

description: The obtaining of Karna by Radha
sn: एवं स सूतपुत्रत्वं जगामामितविक्रमः। वसुषेण इति ख्यातो वृष इत्येव च प्रभुः॥
en: Thus did the boy of immeasurable strength and splendour come to be known as the son of a charioteer and was styled Vasusena and Vrisha.

description: The obtaining of Karna by Radha
sn: सूतस्य ववृधेऽङ्गेषु श्रेष्ठः पुत्रः स वीर्यवान्। चारेण विदितश्चासीत् पृथया दिव्यवर्मभृत्॥
en: That the powerful child, clad in celestials armour (known as) the eldest son of the charioteer (Adhiratha) was growing up in the country of the Angas, was known to Pritha through her spies.

description: The obtaining of Karna by Radha
sn: सूतस्त्वधिरथः पुत्रं विवृद्धं समयेन तम्। दृष्ट्वा प्रस्थापयामास पुरं वारणसाह्वयम्॥
en: When the charioteer saw that his son in course of time had grown up, he sent him to the city of Hastina.

description: The obtaining of Karna by Radha
sn: तत्रोपसदनं चक्रे द्रोणस्येष्वस्त्रकर्णमि। सख्यं दुर्योधनेनैवमगमत् स च वीर्यवान्॥
en: There the powerful youth lived with Drona in order to learn weapons and made friends with Duryodhana.

description: The obtaining of Karna by Radha
sn: द्रोणात् कृपाच्च रामाच्च सोऽस्त्रग्रामं चतुर्विधम् लब्ध्वा लोकेऽभवत् ख्यातः परमेष्वासतां गतः॥
en: Having obtained from Drona, Kripa and Rama (i.e. Parashurama), all the four kinds of weapons, he (Karna) became celebrated in the world as a great bowman.

description: The obtaining of Karna by Radha
sn: संधाय धार्तराष्ट्रेण पार्थानां विप्रिये रतः। योद्धमाशंसते नित्यं फाल्गुनेन महात्मना॥
en: Having contracted a friendship with the son of Dhritarashtra, he became hostile to the Parthas and was always desirous of fighting with the high-souled Falguna.

description: The obtaining of Karna by Radha
sn: सदा हि तस्य स्पर्धाऽऽसीदर्जुनेन विशाम्पते। अर्जुनस्य च कर्णेन यतो दृष्टो बभूव सः॥
en: And O lord of the earth, since they first saw each other, he (Karna) challenged Arjuna and Arjuna too challenged him.

description: The obtaining of Karna by Radha
sn: एतद् गुह्यं महाराज सूर्यस्यासीन्न संशयः। यः सूर्यसम्भवः कर्णः कुन्त्यां सूतकुले तथा॥
en: And O great king, that Karna begotten by him on Kunti was growing up in the race of the Sutas, was, no doubt known to Surya.

description: The obtaining of Karna by Radha
sn: तं तु कुण्डलिनं दृष्ट्वा वर्मणा च समन्वितम्। अवध्यं समरे मत्वा पर्यतप्यद् युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Seeing that he was furnished with armour and ear-rings, Yudhishthira was much pained thinking that he was unslayable in battle.

description: The obtaining of Karna by Radha
sn: यदा च कर्णो राजेन्द्र भानुमन्तं दिवाकरम्। स्तौति मध्यन्दिने प्राप्ते प्राञ्जलिः सलिले स्थितः॥ तत्रैनमुपतिष्ठन्ति ब्राह्मणा धनहेतुना। नादेयं तस्य तत्काले किञ्चिदस्ति द्विजातिषु॥
en: O king of kings, when at noon Karna rose from the water and worshipped the author of the day possessed of rays with joined palms, the Brahmanas prayed to him for riches. And at that time there was nothing that he would not bestow on the twice-born ones.

description: The obtaining of Karna by Radha
sn: तमिन्द्रो ब्राह्मणो भूत्वा भिक्षां देहीत्युपस्थितः। स्वागतं चेति राधेयस्तमथ प्रत्यभाषत॥
en: (For this reason) disguised as a Brahmana Indra came to him and said "give me alms." And the son of Radha replied to him "you are welcome."

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA) Continued The bestowal of his mail and ear-rings by Karna (on Indra
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच देवराजमनुप्राप्तं ब्राह्मणच्छद्मना वृतम्। दृष्ट्वा स्वागतमित्याह न बुबोधास्य मानसम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Beholding the king of the celestials disguised as a Brahmana come (to him), (Karna) said "you are right welcome.” But he could not divine his intentions.

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA) Continued The bestowal of his mail and ear-rings by Karna (on Indra
sn: हिरण्यकण्ठी: प्रमदा ग्रामान् वा बहुगोकुलान्। किं ददानीति तं विप्रमुवाचाधिरथिस्ततः॥
en: Then the (adopted) son of Adhiratha said to that Brahmana "Between beautiful damsels adorned with golden necklaces and villages full of cows which shall I give you?”

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA) Continued The bestowal of his mail and ear-rings by Karna (on Indra
sn: ब्राह्मण उवाच हिरण्यकण्ठ्यः प्रमदा यच्चान्यत् प्रीतिवर्धनम्। नाहं दत्तमिहेच्छामि तदर्थभ्यः प्रदीयताम्॥
en: The Brahmana said : I do not wish to have beauteous damsels with gold necklaces or other agreeable things. Give these (things) to those that beg them.

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA) Continued The bestowal of his mail and ear-rings by Karna (on Indra
sn: यदेतत् सहजं वर्म कुण्डले च तवानघ। एतदुत्कृत्य मे देहि यदि सत्यव्रतो भवान्।॥
en: O sinless one, if you truly observe your vow then cut off (from your body) this armour and these ear-rings born with you and bestow them on me.

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA) Continued The bestowal of his mail and ear-rings by Karna (on Indra
sn: एतदिच्छाम्यहं क्षिप्रं त्वया दत्तं परंतप। एष मे सर्वलाभानां लाभः परमको मतः॥
en: O tormentor of foes, I wish you will very soon give them to me, as I consider this one gain to be the best of all others.

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA) Continued The bestowal of his mail and ear-rings by Karna (on Indra
sn: कर्ण उवाच अवनि प्रमदा गाश्च निवापं बहुवार्षिकम्। तते ते विप्र प्रदास्यामि न तु वर्म सकुण्डलम्॥
en: Karna said: O Brahmana, I will bestow on you homestead lands, beauteous women, cows and (sufficient) plots of land which will enable you to maintain yourself as long as you live.

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA) Continued The bestowal of his mail and ear-rings by Karna (on Indra
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवं बहुविधैर्वाक्यैर्याच्यमानः स तु द्विजः। कर्णेन भरतश्रेष्ठ नान्यं वरमयाचत॥
en: Vaishampayana said: O best of the Bharatas, though Karna thus entreated that twice-born one with various words, yet he (the Brahmana) did not crave any other boon.

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA) Continued The bestowal of his mail and ear-rings by Karna (on Indra
sn: सान्वितश्च यथाशक्ति पूजितश्च यथाविधि। न चान्यं स द्विजश्रेष्ठः कामयामास वै वरम्॥
en: Though he tried his very best to propitiate him and though he worshipped him duly, yet that best of the twice-born ones did not beg any other boon.

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA) Continued The bestowal of his mail and ear-rings by Karna (on Indra
sn: यदा नान्यं प्रवृणुते वरं वै द्विजसत्तमः। तदैनमब्रवीद् भूयो राधेयः प्रहसन्निव॥
en: When that most exalted of the twice-born ones did not ask for any other boon, the son of Radha then addressed him again with a smile,

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA) Continued The bestowal of his mail and ear-rings by Karna (on Indra
sn: सहजं वर्म मे विप्र कुण्डले चामृतोद्भवे। तेनावध्योऽस्मि लोकेषु ततो नैतज्जहाम्यहम्॥
en: “O Brahmana, by virtue of my coat-of-mail, which I have been born with and of the two ear-rings which have sprung from Amrita, I am indestructible by (all) the worlds. I will not, therefore, part with them.

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA) Continued The bestowal of his mail and ear-rings by Karna (on Indra
sn: विशालं पृथिवीराज्यं क्षेमं निहतकण्टकम्। प्रतिगृहणीष्व मत्तस्त्वं साधु ब्राह्मणपुङ्गव॥
en: O most exalted of the Brahmanas, may you be in peace. Accept from me the extensive and peaceful empire of the world with its thorns (enemies) weeded out.

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA) Continued The bestowal of his mail and ear-rings by Karna (on Indra
sn: कुण्डलाभ्यां विमुक्तोऽहं वर्मणा सहजेन च। गमनीयो भविष्यामि शत्रूणां द्विजसत्तम॥
en: Divested of my ear-rings and the armour with which I was born, Obest of the Brahmanas, I shall be liable to be killed by my enemies.

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA) Continued The bestowal of his mail and ear-rings by Karna (on Indra
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच यदान्यं न वरं ववे भगवान् पाकशासनः। ततः प्रहस्य कर्णस्तं पुनरित्यब्रवीद् वचः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : When the exalted chastiser of the (Asura) Paka did not ask for any other boon, then Karna smilingly said to him again these words.

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA) Continued The bestowal of his mail and ear-rings by Karna (on Indra
sn: विदितो देवदेवेश प्रागेवासि मम प्रभो। न तु न्याय्यं मया दातुं तव शक्र वृथा वरम्॥
en: "O lord, O god of gods, I knew before that you (would come). O Shakra, it is not proper for me to bestow on you a boon uselessly.

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA) Continued The bestowal of his mail and ear-rings by Karna (on Indra
sn: त्वं हि देवेश्वरः साक्षात् त्वया देयो वरो मम। अन्येषां चैव भूतानामिश्वरो ह्यसि भूतकृत्॥
en: (Because) you are the very lord of the celestials. It is for you to confer boons on me as you are the creator and lord of all other creators.

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA) Continued The bestowal of his mail and ear-rings by Karna (on Indra
sn: यदि दास्यामि ते देव कुण्डले कवचं तथा। वध्यतामुपयास्यामि त्वं च शक्रावहास्यताम्॥
en: If, O god, I give you my ear-rings and armour, I shall be liable to be killed and you, too will be an object of ridicule.

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA) Continued The bestowal of his mail and ear-rings by Karna (on Indra
sn: तस्माद् विनिमयं कृत्वा कुण्डले वर्म चोत्तमम्। हरस्व शक्र कामं मे न दद्यामहमन्यथा॥
en: Therefore, O Shakra, take my ear-rings and excellent armour in exchange (for boons to be conferred on me by you). Else I will in no way, give (them to you).

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA) Continued The bestowal of his mail and ear-rings by Karna (on Indra
sn: शक्र उवाच विदितोऽहं रवेः पूर्वमायानेव तवान्तिकम्। तेन ते सर्वमाख्यातमेवमेतन्न संशयः॥
en: Shakra said: Before I came to you, Ravi (the sun) was aware of my intentions. There is no doubt that he has told you all.

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA) Continued The bestowal of his mail and ear-rings by Karna (on Indra
sn: काममस्तु तथा तात तव कर्ण यथेच्छसि। वर्जयित्वा तु मे वलां प्रवृणीष्व यथेच्छसि॥
en: O son, O Karna, let it be what you desire, With the exception of my Vajra (thunderbolt) tell me what you desire.

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA) Continued The bestowal of his mail and ear-rings by Karna (on Indra
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततः कर्णः प्रहृष्टस्तु उपसंगम्य वासवम्। अमोघां शक्तिमभ्येत्य वव्रे सम्पूर्णमानसः॥
en: Vaishampayana said: Thereupon, Karna gladly approached Vasava. And desirous of obtaining an infallible dart, he, with his purposes (nearly) gratified spoke.

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA) Continued The bestowal of his mail and ear-rings by Karna (on Indra
sn: कर्ण उवाच वर्मणा कुण्डलाभ्यां च शक्तिं मे देहि वासव। अमोघां शत्रुसंघानां घातिनी पृतनामुखे॥
en: Karna said: In exchange for my armour and ear-rings, O Vasava, bestow on me an infallible dart, destructive of hostile forces when drawn up in battle-array.

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA) Continued The bestowal of his mail and ear-rings by Karna (on Indra
sn: ततः संचिन्त्य मनसा मुहूर्तमिव वासवः। शक्त्यर्थं पृथिवीपाल कर्णं वाक्यमथाब्रवीत्॥
en: Thereupon, O lord of the earth, Vasava reflecting a moment with in his mind for the dart, spoke to Karna these words.

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA) Continued The bestowal of his mail and ear-rings by Karna (on Indra
sn: कुण्डले मे प्रयच्छस्व वर्म चैव शरीरजम्। गृहाण कर्ण शक्तिं त्वमनेन समयेन च॥
en: Bestow on me your ear-rings and the armour born with your body and (then) O Karna, take the dart under the (following) condition.

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA) Continued The bestowal of his mail and ear-rings by Karna (on Indra
sn: अमोघा हन्ति शतशः शत्रून् मम करच्युता। पुनश्च पाणितमभ्येति मम दैत्यान् विनिघ्नतः॥
en: This infallible dart, when I am engaged in slaughtering the Daityas, hurled by my hand kills hundreds of enemies and then returns to my hand.

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA) Continued The bestowal of his mail and ear-rings by Karna (on Indra
sn: सेयं तव करप्राप्ता हत्वैकं रिपुमूर्जितम्। गर्जन्तं प्रतपन्तं च मामेवैष्यति सूतज॥
en: But, O charioteer's son, hurled by your hand, it shall kill one powerful enemy (of yours), roaring and hot as fire and shall then return to me.

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA) Continued The bestowal of his mail and ear-rings by Karna (on Indra
sn: कर्ण उवाच एकमेवाहमिच्छामि रिपुं हन्तुं महाहवे। गर्जन्तं प्रतपन्तं च यतो मम भयं भवेत्॥
en: Karna said: I am desirous of killing in mighty encounter (only) one enemy, roaring and furious, who may strike terror into me.

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA) Continued The bestowal of his mail and ear-rings by Karna (on Indra
sn: इन्द्र उवाच एकं हनिष्यसि रिपुं गर्जन्तं बलिनं रणे। त्वं तु यं प्रार्थयस्येकं रक्ष्यते स महात्मना॥
en: Indra said: You will kill one powerful and roaring enemy in battle. But he whom you seek (to kill) is protected by a high-souled being.

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA) Continued The bestowal of his mail and ear-rings by Karna (on Indra
sn: यमाहुर्वेदविद्वांसो वरार्हमपराजितम्। नारायणमचिन्त्यं च तेन कृष्णेन रक्ष्यते॥
en: He is protected by Krishna who is styled by those learned in the Vedas, the unvanquished Boar and the inconceivable Narayana.

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA) Continued The bestowal of his mail and ear-rings by Karna (on Indra
sn: कर्ण उवाच एवमप्यस्तु भगवन्नेकवीरवधे मम। अमोघां देहि मे शक्तिं यथा हन्यां प्रतापिनम्॥
en: Karna said: Notwithstanding it is so, O adorable one, give me an infallible dart, destructive of a heroic person, wherewith I can kill a mighty (foe).

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA) Continued The bestowal of his mail and ear-rings by Karna (on Indra
sn: उत्कृत्य तु प्रदास्यामि कुण्डले कवचं च ते। निकृत्तेषु तु गात्रेषु न मे बीभत्सता भवेत्॥
en: Cutting the ear-rings and the mail from my body, I will give them to you. But let not my limbs, thus wounded, look ugly.

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA) Continued The bestowal of his mail and ear-rings by Karna (on Indra
sn: इन्द्र उवाच न ते बीभत्सता कर्ण भविष्यति कथञ्चन। व्रपाश्चैव न गात्रेषु यस्त्वं नानृतमिच्छसि॥
en: Indra said: O Karna, since you are are desirous of observing the truth, you will not look ugly nor will there be any scars on your body.

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA) Continued The bestowal of his mail and ear-rings by Karna (on Indra
sn: यादृशस्ते पितुर्वर्णस्तेजश्च वदतां वर। तादृशेनैव वर्णेन त्वं कर्ण भविता पुनः॥
en: O best of speakers, O Karna, you will be again endued with the complexion and energy of your father.

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA) Continued The bestowal of his mail and ear-rings by Karna (on Indra
sn: विद्यमानेषु शस्त्रेषु यद्यमोघामसंशये। प्रमत्तो मोक्ष्यसे चापि त्वय्येवैषा पतिष्यति॥
en: If you hurl this infallible dart maddened with rage when your life is not in danger and when you have other weapons with you, then it shall fall upon yourself.

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA) Continued The bestowal of his mail and ear-rings by Karna (on Indra
sn: कर्ण उवाच संशयं परमं प्राप्य विमोक्ष्ये वासवीमिमाम्। यथा मामात्थ शक्र त्वं सत्यमेतद् ब्रवीमि ते॥
en: Karna said : I tell you truly, O Shakra, that according to your directions I will hurl this Vasavi weapon only when my life is in great jeopardy.

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA) Continued The bestowal of his mail and ear-rings by Karna (on Indra
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततः शक्तिं प्रज्वलितां प्रतिगृह्य विशाम्पते। शस्त्रं गृहीत्वा निशितं सर्वगात्राण्यकृन्तत॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Then, O lord of the earth, accepting that blazing dart, Karna began to cut off his body with sharp weapons.

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA) Continued The bestowal of his mail and ear-rings by Karna (on Indra
sn: ततो देवा मानवा दानवाश्च निकृन्तन्तं कर्णमात्मानमेवम्। न ह्यस्यासीन्मुखजो वै विकारः॥
en: The gods, the mortals and the Danavas, seeing Karna cut off his own body, began to roar like lions, because no signs of contortions were visible on his face.

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA) Continued The bestowal of his mail and ear-rings by Karna (on Indra
sn: ततो दिव्या दुन्दुभयः प्रणेदुः पपातोच्चैः पुष्पवर्षं च दिव्यम्। दृष्ट्वा कर्णं शस्त्रसंकृत्तगात्रं मुहुश्चापि स्मयमानं नृवीरम्॥
en: Seeing that hero among men, Karna, smile again and again even while cutting off his body, the celestials drums began to sound and celestials flowers were showered (upon his head).

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA) Continued The bestowal of his mail and ear-rings by Karna (on Indra
sn: ततश्छित्त्वा कवचं दिव्यमङ्गात् तथैवार्दै प्रददौ वासवाय। तथोत्कृत्य प्रददौ कुण्डले ते कर्णात् तस्मात् कर्मणा तेन कर्णः॥
en: Then Karna cutting off his excellent mail from his body, when it was still wet, gave it to Vasava, And he also cut off his ear-rings from his ear and give them to him. It is on this account that he was styled Karna.

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA) Continued The bestowal of his mail and ear-rings by Karna (on Indra
sn: ततः शक्रः प्रहसन् वञ्चयित्वा कर्णं लोके यशसा योजयित्वा। कृतं कार्यं पाण्डवानां हि मेने ततः पश्चाद् दिवमेवोत्पपात॥
en: Thus deceiving Karna but making him famous in the world, Shakra smilingly considered that he had accomplished the purpose of the Pandavas. He then soared to the heavens.

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA) Continued The bestowal of his mail and ear-rings by Karna (on Indra
sn: श्रुत्वा कर्णं मुषितं धार्तराष्ट्रा दीनाः सर्वे भग्नदर्पा इवासन्। तां चावस्थां गमितं सूतपुत्रं श्रुत्वा पार्था जहषुः काननस्थाः॥
en: Hearing that Karna was thus deceived, all the sons of Dhritarashtra were dejected and became (as dispirited) as if their pride was wounded. The Parthas, (on the other hand) hearing that the son of Suta was reduced to such a state rejoiced (greatly).

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA) Continued The bestowal of his mail and ear-rings by Karna (on Indra
sn: जनमेजय उवाच क्वस्था वीराः पाण्डवास्ते बभूवुः। कुतश्चैते श्रुतवन्तः प्रियं तत्। किं वाकार्पर्द्वादशेऽब्दे व्यतीते तन्मे सर्वं भगवान् व्याकरोतु॥
en: Janamejaya said : Where did the heroic Pandavas dwell (at that time) and from whom did they receive this joyful news and what did they do after the twelve years of their exile? O adorable one, relate all this to me.

parva: KUNDALAHARANA PARVA) Continued The bestowal of his mail and ear-rings by Karna (on Indra
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच लम्वा कृष्णां सैन्धवं द्रावयित्वा विप्रैः सार्धं काम्यकादाश्रमात् ते। मार्कण्डेयाच्छृतवन्तः पुराणं देवर्षीणां चरितं विस्तरेण॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Those heroic men having rescued Krishna, chastised the chief of the Sindhus, heard from Markandeya the old storied about the celestials and the Rishis and passed the entire period of their painful forest life, returned from their hermitage in Kamyaka to the sacred Dvaiytavana together with the Brahmanas, their cars, followers, charioteers, the citizens (who had followed them to the forest) and their COWS.

description: The searching about for the deer
sn: जनमेजय उवाच एवं हृतायां भार्यायां प्राप्य क्लेशमनुत्तमम्। प्रतिपद्य ततः कृष्णां किमकुर्वत पाण्डवाः॥
en: Janamejaya said : Krishna being thus abducted the Pandavas experienced very great sorrow. What did they next do after having rescued her?

description: The searching about for the deer
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवं हृतायां कृष्णायां प्राप्य क्लेशमनुत्तमम्। विहाय काम्यकं राजा सह भ्रातृभिरच्युतः॥ पुनद्वैतवनं रम्यमाजगाम युधिष्ठिरः। स्वादुमूलफलं रम्यं विचित्रबहुपादपम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having felt great distress for the abduction of Krishna, the undeteriorating king Yudhishthira together with his brothers leaving Kamayaka returned to the charming and delightful Dvaiytvana, full of fruits and roots of delicious taste and abounding in various picturesque trees.

description: The searching about for the deer
sn: अनुभुक्तफलाहाराः सर्व एव मिताशनाः। न्यवसन् पाण्डवास्तत्र कृष्णया सह भार्यया॥
en: And all the Pandavas together with their wife Krishna began to dwell there observant of vows, living on fruits and partaking of frugal fares.

description: The searching about for the deer
sn: वसन् द्वैतवने राजा कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः। भीमसेनोऽर्जुनश्चैव माद्रीपुत्रौ च पाण्डवौ॥ ब्राह्मणार्थे पराक्रान्ता धर्मात्मानो यतव्रताः। क्लेशमार्छन्त विपुलं सुखोदक परंतपाः॥
en: And while king Yudhishthira, the son of Kunti, Bhimasena, Arjuna and the other two Pandavas, the sons of Madri, were dwelling in Dvaiytvana, those powerful and virtuous observers of vows, those tormentors of foes, experienced, for the sake of a Brahmana a great trouble which resulted in their (ultimate) happiness.

description: The searching about for the deer
sn: तस्मिन् प्रतिवसन्तस्ते यत् प्रापुः कुरुसत्तमाः। वने क्लेशं सुखोदकं तत् प्रवक्ष्यामि ते शृणु॥
en: I will now tell you of the trouble, which those most exalted of the Kurus went through and which led to their ultimate happiness. Listen to it.

description: The searching about for the deer
sn: अरणीसहितं मन्थं ब्राह्मणस्य तपस्विनः। घर्षमाणस्य विषाणे विषाणे समसज्जतः॥
en: Once, the two sticks for making fire together with a churning rod of an ascetic Brahmana stuck fast to the horns of a deer as it was butting about.

description: The searching about for the deer
sn: तदादाय गतो राजंस्त्वरमाणो महामृगः। आश्रमान्तरितः शीघ्रं प्लवमानो महाजवः॥
en: And O monarch, taking those (articles) away that great deer of exceeding fleetness, with great leaps very soon distanced itself (a great way) from the hermitage.

description: The searching about for the deer
sn: ह्रियमाणं तु तं दृष्ट्वा स विप्रः कुरुसत्तम। त्वरितोऽभ्यागमत् तत्र अग्निहोत्रपरीप्सया॥
en: O best of the Kurus, beholding those (articles) carried away, that Brahmana desirous of preserving his Agnihotra speedily came there,

description: The searching about for the deer
sn: मृगस्य घर्षमाणस्य अजातशत्रुमासीनं भ्रातृभिः सहितं वने। आगम्य ब्राह्मणस्तूर्णं संतप्तश्चेदमब्रवीत्॥
en: Where Ajatashatru together with his brothers was seated in the forest. And the Brahmana quickly approaching spoke (thus) sorrowfully.

description: The searching about for the deer
sn: अरणीसहितं मन्यं समासक्तं वनस्पतौ। मृगस्य घर्षमाणस्य विषाणे समसज्जत॥
en: "My fire-sticks together with the churning rod placed against a large tree were stuck to the horns of a deer as it was butting about.

description: The searching about for the deer
sn: तमादाय गतो राजंस्त्वरमाणो महामृगः। आश्रमात् त्वरितः शीघ्रं प्लवमानो महाजवः॥
en: And, O king, that great deer endued with great speed, soon distanced itself (a great way) from the hermitage with long leaps.

description: The searching about for the deer
sn: तस्य गत्वा पदं राजन्नासाद्य च महामृगम्। अग्निहोत्रं न लुप्येत तदानयत पाण्डवाः॥
en: And following the foot-prints of that great deer, O king, O Pandavas, bring those (articles) to me so that my Agnihotra may not be stopped.”

description: The searching about for the deer
sn: ब्राह्मणस्य वचः श्रुत्वा संतप्तोऽथ युधिष्ठिरः। धनुरादाय कौन्तेयः प्राद्रवद् भ्रातृभिः सह॥
en: Hearing the words of the Brahmana, Yudhishthira, the son of Kunti, became very sorry and taking his bow sallied out together with his brothers.

description: The searching about for the deer
sn: सन्नद्धा धन्विनः सर्वे प्राद्रवन् नरपुङ्गवाः। ब्राह्मणार्थे यतन्तस्ते शीघ्रमन्वगमन् मृगम्॥
en: Taking great care for the sake of the Brahmana, all those foremost of men, taking up their bows and doing their corslets speedily went out in pursuit of the deer.

description: The searching about for the deer
sn: कर्णिनालीकनाराचानुत्सृजन्तो महारथाः। नाविध्यन् पाण्डवास्तत्र पश्यन्तो मृगमन्तिकात्॥
en: Beholding that deer at a short distance, those mighty car-warriors the Pandavas hurled barbed darts, javelins and arrows (at it) but they could not pierce it.

description: The searching about for the deer
sn: तेषां प्रयतमानानां नादृश्यत महामृगः। अपश्यन्तो मृगं शान्ता दुःखं प्राप्ता मनस्विनः॥
en: When they were thus exerting (their utmost to slay it) that great deer went out of sight. That deer disappearing (from sight) those highsouled ones became fatigued and disappointed.

description: The searching about for the deer
sn: शीतलच्छायमागम्य न्यचोधं गहने वने। क्षुत्पिपासापरीताङ्गाः पाण्डवाः समुपाविशन्॥
en: And afflicted with hunger and thirst, the Pandavas coming to a banian tree in that forest sat down in its cool shade.

description: The searching about for the deer
sn: तेषां समुपविष्टानां नकुलो दुःखितस्तदा। अब्रवीद् भ्रातरं श्रेष्ठममर्षात् कुरुनन्दनम्॥
en: When they were seated, Nakula with a heavy heart and through impatience addressed his (eldest) brother, the best of the sons of the Kuru race, (thus)

description: The searching about for the deer
sn: नास्मिन् कुले जातु ममज्ज धर्मो न चालस्यादर्थलोपो बभूव। अनुत्तराः सर्वभूतेषु भूयः सम्प्राप्ताः स्मः संशयं किं नु राजन्॥
en: "In our race virtue has never been sacrificed nor there has been any loss of wealth through idleness. Again, we have never refused anything to any creature. How is it, then, O king, that this disaster has befallen us?"

description: The death of Nakula and others
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच नापदामस्ति मर्यादा न निमित्तं न कारणम्। धर्मस्तु विभजत्यर्थमुभयोः पुण्यपापयोः॥
en: Yudhishthira said : There is no limit to misfortunes and neither their effects nor their causes can be ascertained. It is Dharma who distributes the fruits of both virtue and sin.

description: The death of Nakula and others
sn: भीम उवाच प्रातिकाम्यनयत् कृष्णां सभायां प्रेष्यवत् तदा। न मया निहतस्तत्र तेन प्राप्ताः स्म संशयम्॥
en: Bhima said: We have met with this disaster, because I did not slay Pratikami when he dragge Krishna into the assembly hall like a slave.

description: The death of Nakula and others
sn: अर्जुन उवाच वाचस्तीक्ष्णास्थिभेदिन्यः सूतपुत्रेण भाषिताः। अतितीव्रा मया क्षान्तास्तेन प्राप्ताः स्म संशयम्॥
en: Arjuna said: As I did not present those very sharp and biting words, piercing the very bones, uttered by the son of Suta, so we have met with this calamity.

description: The death of Nakula and others
sn: सहदेव उवाच शकुनिस्त्वां यदाजैषीदक्षद्यूतेन भारत। स मया न हतस्तत्र तेन प्राप्ताः स्म संशयम्॥
en: Sahadeva said : This calamity, O Bharata, has overtaken us because I did not kill Shakuni when he defeated you at the game of dice.

description: The death of Nakula and others
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततो युधिष्ठिरो राजा नकुलं वाक्यमब्रवीत्। आरुह्य वृक्षं माद्रेय निरीक्षस्व दिशो दश॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Then, king Yudhishthira said to Nakula "O son of Madri, climbing this tree look around the ten points.

description: The death of Nakula and others
sn: पानीयमन्तिके पश्य वृक्षांश्चाप्युदकाश्रितान्। एते हि भ्रातरः श्रान्तास्तव तात पिपासिताः॥
en: O affectionate one, as these your brothers are fatigued and thirsty, so see whether any water or trees growing by water-side, are near.”

description: The death of Nakula and others
sn: नकुलस्तु तथेत्युक्त्वा शीघ्रमारुह्य पादपम्। अब्रवीद् भ्रातरं ज्येष्ठमभिवीक्ष्य समन्ततः॥
en: Nakula too saying “be it so" soon ascended a tree. And casting his looks around said to his eldest brother thus,

description: The death of Nakula and others
sn: पश्यामि बहुलान् राजन् वृक्षानुदकसंश्रयान्। सारसानां च निदिमत्रोदकमसंशयम्॥
en: "O king, I see numerous trees growing near water and also hear the cries of the Sarasas. Therefore, surely water must be somewhere here."

description: The death of Nakula and others
sn: ततोऽब्रवीत् सत्यधृतिः कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः। गच्छ सौम्य ततः शीघ्रं तूणैः पानीयमानय॥
en: Thereupon, Yudhishthira, the son of Kunti, firm in truth, said "O beautiful one, do go (there) and soon bring water in the quivers."

description: The death of Nakula and others
sn: नकुलस्तु तथेत्युक्त्वा भ्रातुर्येष्ठस्य शासनात्। प्राद्रवद् यत्र पानीयं शीघ्रं चैवान्वपद्यत॥
en: Saying “be it so" Nakula, at the command of his eldest brother, quickly, proceeded towards the spot where the water was and soon reached it.

description: The death of Nakula and others
sn: स दृष्ट्वा विमलं तोयं सारसैः परिवारितम्। पातुकामस्ततो वाचमन्तरिक्षात् स शुश्रुवे॥
en: And seeing the transparent water surrounded by cranes, as he was desirous of drinking of it, he heard these words from the firmament.

description: The death of Nakula and others
sn: यक्ष उवाच मा तात साहसं कार्मिम पूर्वपरिग्रहः। प्रश्नानुक्त्वा तु माद्रेय ततः पिब हरस्व च॥
en: The Yaksha said: O child, do not venture to do this. I have got possession of it before. O son of Madri, first answer my questions and then drink of it and carry it away.

description: The death of Nakula and others
sn: अनादृत्य तु तद् वाक्यं नकुलः सुपिपासितः। अपिबच्छीतलं तोयं पीत्वा च निपपात ह॥
en: Nakula, (however), who was very thirsty, disregarding these words, drank the cool water. But as (soon) as he drank it he fell dead.

description: The death of Nakula and others
sn: चिरायमाणे नकुले कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः। अब्रवीद् भ्रातरं वीरं सहदेवमरिंदमम्॥
en: Seeing Nakula's delay, Yudhishthira the son of Kunti, said to his heroic brother Sahadeva, the tormentor of his foes,

description: The death of Nakula and others
sn: भ्राता हि चिरयातो नः सहदेव तवाचजः। तथैवानय सोदर्यं पानीयं च त्वमानय॥
en: “O Sahadeva, our brother (Nakula) who was born (just) before you, has been long out. Go and bring him and also water.

description: The death of Nakula and others
sn: सहदेवस्तथेत्युक्त्वा तां दिशं प्रत्यपद्यत। ददर्श च हतं भूमौ भ्रातरं नकुलं तदा॥
en: Saying “be it so,” Sahadeva proceeded towards that direction and he then beheld his brother Nakula lying dead on the ground.

description: The death of Nakula and others
sn: भ्रातृशोकाभिसंतप्तस्तृषया च प्रपीडितः। अभिदुद्राव पानीयं ततो वागभ्यभाषत॥
en: Sorely afflicted at the death of his brother and oppressed with thirst, as he made for the water he heard these words.

description: The death of Nakula and others
sn: मा तात साहसं कार्मिम पूर्वपरिग्रहः। प्रश्नानुक्त्वा यथाकामं पिवस्व च हरस्व च॥
en: "O child, do not venture this. It has been before obtained possession by me. First answer my questions and then drink water and carry it away.”

description: The death of Nakula and others
sn: अनाहृत्य तु तद् वाक्यं सहदेवः पिपासितः। अपिबच्छीतलं तोयं पीत्वा च निपपात ह॥
en: Sahadeva, as he was thirsty, despising those words drank the cool water and as he drank he fell dead.

description: The death of Nakula and others
sn: अथाब्रवीत् स विजयं कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः। भ्रातरौ ते चिरगतौ बीभत्सो शत्रुकर्शन॥
en: Then Yudhishthira, the son of Kunti, said to Vijaya (Arjuna) “O Vivatsu, O tormentor of foes, your brothers (Nakula and Sahadeva) have been long out.

description: The death of Nakula and others
sn: तौ चैवानय भद्रं ते पानीयं च त्वमानय। त्वं हि नस्तात सर्वेषां दुःखितानामपाश्रयः॥
en: May you be in peace. Go and bring them and also water. O affectionate one, you are the refuge of all of us when in distress."

description: The death of Nakula and others
sn: एवमुक्तो गुडाकेशः प्रगृह्य सशरं धनुः। आमुक्तखङ्गो मेधावी तत् सरः प्रत्यपद्यत॥
en: Thus spoken to, the intellectual Gudakesha taking up his bow together with arrows and his naked sword soon proceeded towards that lake.

description: The death of Nakula and others
sn: ततः पुरुषशार्दूलो पानीयहरणे गतौ। तौ ददर्श हतौ तत्र भ्रातरौ श्वेतवाहनः॥
en: (Having arrived at that lake), Shvetavahana beheld his two brothers, those most valiant of men, who came to fetch water, lying dead.

description: The death of Nakula and others
sn: प्रसुप्ताविव तौ दृष्ट्वा नरसिंहः सुदुःखितः। धनुरुद्यम्य कौन्तेयो व्यलोकयत् तद् वनम्॥
en: And that lion amongst men, beholding them as if buried in slumber, became very afflicted, And then the son of Kunti upraising his bow looked around that forest.

description: The death of Nakula and others
sn: नापश्यत् तत्र किञ्चित् स भूतमस्मिन् महावने। सव्यसाची ततः श्रान्तः पानीयं सोऽभ्यधावत॥
en: But he beheld no creature in that great forest. And oppressed with fatigue, Savyasachi made for the water.

description: The death of Nakula and others
sn: अभिधावंस्ततो वाक्यमन्तरिक्षात् स शुश्रुवे। किमासीदसि पानीयं तच्छक्यं बलात् त्वया।॥
en: And as he rushed (towards the water) he heard these words from the firmament “Why are you coming towards the water You will not। be able to drink of it forcibly.

description: The death of Nakula and others
sn: कौन्तेय यदि प्रश्नांस्तान् मयोक्तान् प्रतिपत्स्यसे। ततः पास्यसि पानीयं हरिष्यसि च भारत॥
en: O son of Kunti, O Bharata, if you can answer the questions put by me, then you may drink of the water and take it away.”

description: The death of Nakula and others
sn: वारितस्त्वब्रवीत् पार्थो दृश्यमानो निवारय। यावद् बाणैर्विनिर्भिन्नः पुन:वं वदिष्यसि॥
en: Thus forbidden, Partha said "come to my presence and then prevent me. You will not speak again in this strain when I will rive you with darts."

description: The death of Nakula and others
sn: एवमुक्त्वा ततः पार्थः शरैरस्त्रानुमन्त्रितैः। प्रववर्ष दिशः कृत्स्ना: शब्दवेधं च दर्शयन्॥
en: Saying this, Partha displaying his skill in hitting at an invisible object by sound alone, entirely covered all the sides by discharges of arrows inspired with the mantras,

description: The death of Nakula and others
sn: कर्णिनालीकनाराचानुत्सृजन् भरतर्षभ। स त्वमोघानिषून मुक्त्वा तृष्णायाभिप्रपीडितः॥
en: O best of the Bharatas, oppressed with thirst, he began to hurl barbed darts, javelins, Narachas and numerous infallible arrows.

description: The death of Nakula and others
sn: अनेकैरिषुसङ्घातैरन्तरिक्षे ववर्ष ह।
en: And he discharged at the firmament innumerable darts.

description: The death of Nakula and others
sn: यक्ष उवाच किं विघातेन ते पार्थ प्रश्नानुक्त्वा ततः पिब॥
en: The Yaksha said: Partha, your exertions are to no purpose, (First) answer my questions and then drink

description: The death of Nakula and others
sn: अनुक्त्वा च पिबन् प्रश्नान् पीत्वैव न भविष्यसि। एवमुक्तस्ततः पार्थः सव्यसाची धनंजयः॥ अवज्ञायैव तां वाचं पीत्वैव निपपात ह।
en: If however you drink before answering my questions, you will die as soon as you will drink. Thus addressed, the son of Pritha, Dhananjaya who could draw his bow by his left hand. Disregarding those words, as he drank, fell dead.

description: The death of Nakula and others
sn: अथाब्रवीद् भीमसेनं कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिः॥ नकुलः सहदेवश्च बीभत्सुश्च परंतप! चिरं गतास्तोयहेतोर्न चागच्छन्ति भारत॥ तांश्चैवानय भद्रं ते पानीयं च त्वमानय।
en: Then, Yudhishthira, the son of Kunti spoke to Bhimsena, “O tormentor of foes, O Bhimasena Nakula, Sahadeva and Vivatsu have been long out to fetch water and they have not come as yet. You are to bring them as well as water.

description: The death of Nakula and others
sn: भीमसेनस्तथेत्युक्त्वा तं देशं प्रत्यपद्यत॥ यत्र ते पुरुषव्याघ्रा भ्रातरोऽस्य निपातिताः। तान् दृष्ट्वा दुःखितो भीमस्तृषया च प्रपीडितः॥
en: May you be blessed.” Saying “be it so" Bhimasena proceeded towards that place, where his brothers, those most valiant of men, lay dead. Afflicted at seeing them (dead) and oppressed with thirst.

description: The death of Nakula and others
sn: अमन्यत महाबाहुः कर्म तद् यक्षरक्षसाम्। स चिन्तयामास तदा योद्धव्यं ध्रुवमद्य वै॥
en: That mighty-armed one considered (within himself). “This act must have been done by some Yaksha or Rakshasa." And he thought (further) “I will have surely to fight today.

description: The death of Nakula and others
sn: पास्यामि तावत् पानीयमिति पार्थो वृकोदरः। ततोऽभ्यधावत् पानीयं पिपासुः पुरुषर्षभः॥
en: Let me therefore, (first) drink water.” Then, Vrikodara, the son of Pritha and the best of the Bharatas, desirous of drinking, rushed towards the water.

description: The death of Nakula and others
sn: यक्ष उवाच मा तात साहसं कार्मिम पूर्वपरिग्रहः। प्रश्नानुक्त्वा तु कौन्तेय ततः पिब हरस्व च॥
en: The Yaksha said: O child, do not attempt it. It has already been in my possession, (first) answer my questions and then drink water and carry it away (for your brother).

description: The death of Nakula and others
sn: एवमुक्तस्तदा भीमो यक्षेणामिततेजसा। अनुक्त्वैव तु तान् प्रश्नान् पीत्वैव निपपात ह॥
en: Thus addressed by that Yaksha of unrivalled energy, soon as Bhima without answering his questions, drank of it, he fell down dead.

description: The death of Nakula and others
sn: ततः कुन्तीसुतो राजा प्रचिन्त्य पुरुषर्षभः। समुत्थाय महाबाहुर्दह्यमानेन चेतमा॥ व्यपेतजननिर्घोषं प्रविवेश महावनम्। रुरुभिश्च वराहैश्च पक्षिभिश्च निषेवितम्॥
en: Then that best of men, the royal son of Kunti of mighty arms, whose heart was burning in grief, after much deliberation rose up and entered that mighty forest where no sound of human voice could be heard. It was inhabited by rurus, boars and birds.

description: The death of Nakula and others
sn: नीलभास्वरवर्णश्च पादैपरुपशोभितम्। भ्रमरैरुपगीतं च पक्षिभिश्च महायशाः॥
en: Adorned with trees of blue and bright colours and ringing with the hum of bees and warbling of birds. And that highly renowned.

description: The death of Nakula and others
sn: स गच्छन् कानने तस्मिन् हेमजालपरिष्कृतम्। ददर्श तत् सरः श्रीमान् विश्वकर्मकृतं यथा॥
en: And illustrious one, entering into the forest saw that lake beautified with gold-coloured filaments, looking as if it had been made by the Architect of the universe.

description: The death of Nakula and others
sn: उपेतं नलिनीजालैः सिन्धुवारैः सवेतसैः। केतकैः करवीरैश्च पिप्पलैश्चैव संवृतम्। श्रमार्तस्तदुपागम्य सरो दृष्ट्वाथ विस्मितः॥
en: Adorned with rows of lotuses, Sindhuvara flowers together with cane trees and covered all over with Ketakas, Karaviras and Pippalas. Oppressed with fatigue, he approached that lake and was wonder-struck at what he saw.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच स ददर्श हतान् भ्रातृन् लोकपालानिव च्युतान्। युगान्ते समनुप्राप्ते शक्रप्रतिमगौरवान्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : He (Yudhishthira) then beheld his brothers, glorious as Shakra himself, lying dead like the Lokapalas dropped down form their regions at the end of a Yuga.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: विनिकीर्णधनुर्बाणं दृष्ट्वा निहतमर्जुनम्। भीमसेनं यमौ चैव निर्विचेष्टान् गतायुषः॥ स दीर्घमुष्णं नि:श्वस्य शोकवाष्पपरिप्लुतः। तान् दृष्ट्वा पतितान् भ्रातृन् सर्वांश्चिन्तासमन्वितः॥ धर्मपुत्रो महाबाहुर्विललाप सुविस्तरम्।
en: Seeing Arjuna dead with his bow and arrow lying scattered and also Bhimasena and the twins lying motionless with life extinct, Yudhishthira breathing out a long and hot sigh was bathed in tears caused by grief. Afflicted with anxiety at beholding all his brothers lying dead. The mighty-armed son of Dharma gave bent to a great profusion of grief

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: ननु त्वया महाबाहो प्रतिज्ञातं वृकोदरा॥ सुयोधनस्य भेत्स्यामि गदया सक्थिनी रणे। व्यर्थं तदद्य मे सर्वं त्वयि वीर निपातिते॥ महात्मनि महाबाहो कुरूणां कीर्तिवर्धने।
en: He said, "O mighty-armed Vrikodara, you swore, I will break the thighs of Duryodhana with mace in battle.' O Bhima, since you are dead all that has become to no purpose to me.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: मनुष्यसम्भवा वाचो विधर्मिण्य: प्रतिश्रुताः॥ भवतां दिव्यवाचस्तु ता भवन्तु कथं मृषा।
en: O high-minded and mighty-armed enhancer of the glory of the Kurus, human promises may not be fulfilled, but how is it that celestials words with regard to you have proved untrue?

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: देवाश्चापि यदावाचन सूतके त्वां धनंजय॥ सहस्राक्षादनवरः कुन्ति पुत्रस्तवेति वै। उत्तरे पारियात्रे च जगुर्भूतानि सर्वशः॥ विप्रणष्टां श्रियं चैषामाहर्ता पुनरञ्जसा। नास्य जेता रणे कश्चिदजेता नैष कस्यचित्॥
en: O Dhananjaya, when you were born, the very gods themselves said, “O Kunti, this son of yours shall in no way be inferior to the thousand-eyed deity.” And in the northern r'aripatra mountain all the beings sang, “The prosperity these have been deprived of, by enemies, shall surely be recovered by this one. There shall be no vanquisher of him in battle and there shall be none whom he will not be able to conquer."

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: सोऽयं मृत्युवंश यातः कथं जिष्णुमहाबलः। अयं ममाशां संहत्य शेते भूमौ धनंजयः॥ आश्रित्य यं वयं नाथं दुःखान्येतानि सेहिम।
en: How is it, then, that this highly powerful Jishnu has been subject to death? Why does that Dhananjaya lie dead on the ground destroying all my hopes, depending on whom we have gone through all these miseries?

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: रणे प्रमत्तौ वीरौ च सदा शत्रुनिबर्हणौ॥ कथं रिपुवशं यातौ कुन्तीपुत्रौ महाबलौ। यौ सर्वास्त्राप्रतिहतौ भीमसेनधनंजयौ॥
en: Why have these two highly powerful and heroic sons of Kunti, Bhimasena and Dhananjaya, furious in battle, who always destroyed their enemies and whom no weapons could resist, been subjugated by the enemy?

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: अश्मसारमयं नूनं हृदयं ममम दुहृदः। यमौ यदेतौ दृष्ट्वाद्य पतितौ नावदीर्यते॥
en: Surely this vile heart of me is made of the essence of marble, since seeing these twins lying dead today it is not riven.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: शास्त्रज्ञा देशकालज्ञास्तपोयुक्ताः क्रियान्विताः। अकृत्वा सदृशं कर्म किं शेध्वं पुरुषर्षभाः॥
en: Why do you, O most exalted of men, versed in the Shastras, acquainted with the rules of proper time and place, performers of religious rites, lie dead without performing acts 'worthy of you?

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: अविक्षतशरीराश्चाप्यप्रमृष्टशरासनाः। असंज्ञा भुवि संगम्य किं शेध्वमपराजिताः॥
en: O unvanquished ones, with your bodies unwounded and bows untouched, why do you lie insensible embracing the earth”?

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: सानूनिवारेः संसुप्तान् दृष्ट्वा भ्रातृन् महामतिः। सुखं प्रसुप्तान् प्रस्विनः खिन्नः कष्टां दशां गतः॥
en: And that large hearted one, beholding his brothers sweetly asleep as (they slept peacefully) on the plateaus of mountains perspired profusely, became sorely afflicted and was reduced to a piteous plight,

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: एवमेवेदमित्युक्त्वा धर्मात्मा स नरेश्वरः। शोकसागरमध्यस्थो दध्यौ कारणमाकुलः॥
en: That virtuous souled lord of men, saying "it is so," and drowned in the sea of sorrow and with an agitated heart, began to think of the cause of his brothers' death.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: इतिकर्तव्यतां चेति देशकालविभागवित्। नाभिपेदे महाबाहुश्चिन्तयानो महामतिः॥
en: And though that high-minded one of mighty arms, acquainted with the divisions of time and place, pondered much, he could not settle what he should do.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: अथ संस्तभ्य धर्मात्मा तदाऽऽत्मानं तपोयुतः। एवं विलप्य बहुधा धर्मपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Thus lamenting profusely, the virtuous minded son of Tapa or Dharma, Yudhishthira, pacified his soul.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: बुद्ध्या विचिन्तयामास वीराः केन निपातिताः॥
en: And began, by the exercise of his intelligence, to ponder thus “by whom these warriors have been slain?

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: नैषां शस्त्रप्रहारोऽस्ति पदं नेहास्ति कस्यचित्। भूतं महदिदं मन्ये भ्रातरो येन मे हताः॥
en: There are no strokes of weapons on their bodies nor are there any foot prints of any body. I consider he is a mighty being who has slain my brothers.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: एकाचं चिन्तयिष्यामि पीत्वा वेत्स्यामि वा जलम्। स्यात् तु दुर्योधनेनेदमुपांशुविहितं कृतम्॥ गान्धारराजरचितं सततं जिह्मबुद्धिना। यस्य कार्यमकार्यं वा सममेव भवत्युत॥ कस्तस्य विश्वसेद् वीरो दुष्कृतेकृतात्मनः। अथवा पुरुषैर्गुढैः प्रयोगोऽयं दुरात्मनः॥
en: I will reflect on this with concentration or I will try to know of it after drinking water. Perhaps the crooked-minded Duryodhana with whom good and evil are alike has got it (the tark) destruc.ive of life, made by the king of Gandhara. What cool-headed person can trust that wicked minded man ever bent on evil deeds? Or perhaps that wicked souled one has caused it to be made by some secret messengers of his."

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: भवेदिति महाबुद्धिर्बहुधा तदचिन्तयत्। तस्यासीन्न विषेणेदमुदकं दूषितं यथा॥
en: Thus that highly intellectual one gave way to many thoughts. But he could, in no way, persuade himself that the water was prisoned,

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: मृतानामपि चैतेषां विकृतं नैव जायते। मुखवर्णाः प्रसन्ना मे भ्रातृणामित्यचिन्तयत्॥
en: For, though dead, their features had undergone no change. And he thought "the colour on the face of my brothers is still lively.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: एकैकशश्चौघबलानिमान् पुरुषसत्तमान्। कोऽन्यः प्रतिसमासेत कालान्तकयमादृते॥
en: Each of these foremost of men is possessed of the force of a water fall. Who else, therefore, can vanquish them except that being who carries away every thing in proper time."

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: एतेन व्यवसायेन तत् तोयं व्यवगाढवान्। गाहमानश्च तत् तोयमन्तरिक्षात् स शुश्रुवे॥
en: Thinking it to be certain, he plunged into that water. And as he got into it he heard these words from the firmament.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: यक्ष उवाच अहं बकः शैवलमत्स्यभक्षो नीता मया प्रेतवशं तवानुजाः। त्वं पञ्चमो भविता राजपुत्र न चेत् प्रश्नान् पृच्छतो व्याकरोषि॥
en: The Yaksha said: I am a crane living on moss and fish. Your younger brothers have been, by me, brought under the control of death. If, O king's son, you do not answer the questions put by me, you shall be the fifth victim.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: मा तात साहसं कार्षीर्मम पूर्वपरिग्रहः। प्रश्नानुक्त्वा तु कौन्तेय ततः पिब हरस्व च॥
en: O child, do not attempt this. It has been possessed by me before. First! answer my questions and then drink water kind take it away.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच रुद्राणां वा वसूनां वा मरुतां वा प्रधानभाक्। पृच्छामि को भवान् देवो नैतच्छकुनिना कृतम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said : Are you the foremost of the Rudras or the Vasus or the Marutas? I ask you what god you are. It is not possible for a bird to have done this.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: हिमवान् पारियात्रश्च विन्ध्यो मलय एव च। चत्वारः पर्वताः केन पातिता भूरितेजसः॥
en: Who has felled these four mountains of great energy viz. Himavat, Pariyatra, Vindhya and Malaya?

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: अतीव ते महत् कर्म कृतं च बलिनां वर। यान् न देवा न गन्धर्वा नासुराश्च न राक्षसाः॥
en: O strongest of those endued with strength, you have (indeed) achieved a very great feat in as much as neither the celestials, nor the Gandharvas nor the Asuras, nor the Rakshasas.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: विषहेरन् महायुद्धे कृतं ते तन्महाद्भुतम्। न ते जानामि यत् कार्यं नाभिजानामि काक्षितम्॥
en: Could stand them in mighty conflict. (Therefore) what you have done is highly marvellous. Neither am I aware of what is your business nor do I know of your intentions.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: कौतूहलं महज्जातं साध्वसं चागतं मम। येनास्म्युद्विग्नहदयः समुत्पन्नशिरोज्वरः॥ पृच्छामि भगवंस्तस्मात् को भवानिह तिष्ठति।
en: I am very curious (to learn all this) and am terrified also. For which my heart is troubled and my head is racked. Therefore, O adorable one, I ask you who you are that are staying here.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: यक्ष उवाच यक्षोऽहमस्मि भद्रं ते नास्मि पक्षी जलेचरः॥ मयैते निहताः सर्वे भ्रातरस्ते महौजसः।
en: The Yaksha said : I am a Yaksha and not an aquatic bird. All hail to you. It is I who have slain your greatly energetic brothers.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततस्तामशिवां श्रुत्वा वाचं स परुषाक्षराम्॥ यक्षस्य ब्रुवतो राजन्नुपक्रम्य तदा स्थितः। विरूपाक्षं महाकायं यक्षं तालसमुच्छ्रयम्॥ ज्वलनार्कप्रतीकाशमधृष्यं पर्वतोपमम्। वृक्षमाश्रित्य तिष्ठन्तं ददर्श भरतर्षभः॥ मेघगम्भीरनादेन तर्जयन्तं महास्वनम्।
en: Vaishampayana said : Thereupon, hearing those inauspicious words couched in harsh letters, which the Yaksha was speaking, he (Yudhishthira), O king, approaching him stood there. And that best of the Bharatas saw that huge-bodied Yaksha endued with unnatural eyes, tall as a palm tree, blazing like the sun or the fire, irresistible, huge as a rock, staying on a tree and uttering deep loud roars like the rumbling of the clouds.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: यक्ष उवाच इमे ते भ्रातरो राजन् वार्यमाणा मयासकृत्॥ बलात् तोयं जिहीर्षन्तस्ततो वै मृदिता मया। न पेयमुदकं राजन् प्राणानिह परीप्सता॥ पार्थ मा साहसं कार्मिम पूर्वपरिग्रहः। प्रश्नानुक्त्वा तु कौन्तेय ततः पिब हरस्व च।॥
en: The Yaksha said: These brothers of you, O king, though again and again forbidden by me. Wanted to take away water by force. I have therefore killed them. He that has a love for his life ought not, O king, to drink this water. O Partha, do not attempt it. This (pond) has been taken possession of by me before. O son of Kunti, answering my questions, you may drink and take away water.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच न चाहं कामये यक्ष तव पूर्वपरिग्रहम्। कामं नैतत् प्रशंसन्ति सन्तो हि पुरुषाः सदा॥ यदात्मना स्वमात्मानं प्रशंसे पुरुषर्षभ। यथाप्रज्ञं तु ते प्रश्नान् प्रतिवक्ष्यामि पृच्छ माम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said : O Yaksha, I do not want what you have already taken possession of. Virtuous persons never like, that one should extol his own self, O most exalted of creatures. I shall answer your questions according to my knowledge. Ask me.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: यक्ष उवाच किं स्विदादित्यमुन्नयति के च तस्याभितश्चराः। कश्नमस्तं नयति कस्मिश्च प्रतितिष्ठति॥
en: The Yaksha said: What is that which makes Aditya, (the sun) rise? Who remain near him? Who does make him set? (And) in what is he established?

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच ब्रह्मादित्यमुन्नयति देवास्तस्याभितश्चराः। धर्मश्चास्तं नयति च सत्ये च प्रतितिष्ठति॥
en: Yudhishthira said: It is Brahma that makes the sun rise. The celestials remain near him. Dharma makes him set. And he is established in truth.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: यक्ष उवाच केनस्विच्छ्रोत्रियो भवति केनस्विद् विन्दते महत्। केनस्विद् द्वितीयवान् भवति राजन् केन च बुद्धिमान्।४७
en: The Yaksha said : What makes one Shrotriya (learned) By what does one attain to what is very exalted? what makes one have a second And, by what, O king, one becomes wise?

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच श्रुतेन श्रोत्रियो भवति तपसा विन्दते महत्। धृत्या द्वितीयवान् भवति बुद्धिमान् वृद्धसेवया॥
en: Yudhishthira said : By the Shruti (i.e. the study of the Vedas) one becomes learned. By asceticism one attains to what is very exalted. Intelligence makes one have a second. Ministration to the old makes one wise.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: यक्ष उवाच किं ब्राह्मणानां देवत्वं कश्च धर्मः सतामिव। कश्चैषां मानुषो भावः किमेषामसतामिव॥
en: The Yaksha said : What is the divine attribute of the Brahmanas? What virtuous practices of theirs resemble those of the pious? What is their human attribute? And what (practices) of theirs resemble those of the impious?

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच स्वाध्याय एषां देवत्वं तप एषां सतामिव। मरणं मानुषो भावः परिवादोऽसतामिव॥
en: Yudhishthira said : The study of the Vedas is their divine attribute. Their asceticism is like the virtuous practices of the pious. Death is their human attribute. And slander (by them) is like the behaviour of the impious.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: यक्ष उवाच किं क्षत्रियाणां देवत्वं कश्च धर्मः सतामिव। कश्चैषां मानुषो भावः किमेषामसतामिव।॥
en: The Yaksha said: What is the divine quality of the Kshatriyas? What practice of theirs resembles the behaviour of the pious? What is their human attribute? And what (practice) on their part resembles that of the impious?

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच इष्वस्त्रमेषां देवत्वं यज्ञ एषां सतामिव। भयं वै मानुषो भावः परित्यागोऽसतामिव॥
en: Yudhishthira said : It is the arrows ard weapons that constitute their divinity. Sacrifices (on their part) resemble the virtuous practices of the pious. Fear is their human attribute. And their abandoning (the distraced) is like the practice of the impious.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: यक्ष उवाच किमेकं यज्ञियं साम किमेकं यज्ञियं यजुः। का चैषां वृणुते यज्ञं कां यज्ञो नातिवर्तते॥
en: The Yaksha said: What is that one thing) which is the sacrificial Soma? What is that which constitutes the sacrificial Yaju? What is that which sacrifice can not do without?

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच प्राणो वै यज्ञियं साम मनो वै यज्ञियं यजुः। ऋगेका वृणुते यज्ञं तां यज्ञो नातिवर्तते॥
en: Yudhishthira said: Life is the sacrificial Soma; mind is the sacrificial Yaju; it is Rich which accompanies sacrifice and without which sacrifice can not do.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: यक्ष उवाच किंस्विदावपतां श्रेष्ठं किंस्विन्निवपतां वरम्। किंस्वित् प्रतिष्ठमानानां किंस्वित् प्रसवतां वरम्॥
en: The Yaksha said : What thing is the best with regard to the cultivators? What is of the greatest value to those that seek prosperity? And what is of the highest value to those that bring forth?

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच वर्षमावपतां श्रेष्ठं बीजं निवपतां वरम्। गाव: प्रतिष्ठमानानां पुत्रः प्रसवतां वरः॥
en: Yudhishthira said: Rain is the best thing to the cultivators; seed is of the great value to the sowers; cow is the best thing to those that seek prosperity and son is of the greatest value to those that bring forth.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: यक्ष उवाच इन्द्रियार्थाननुभवन् बुद्धिमॉल्लोकपूजितः। सम्मतः सर्वभूतानामुच्छ्वसन् को न जीवति॥
en: The Yaksha said : Is there any person, endowed with intelligence, worshipped by the world, respected by all the creatures, who, though enjoying the objects of senses and breathing, is not alive?

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच देवतातिथिभृत्यानां पितृणामात्मनश्च यः। न निर्वपति पञ्चानामुच्छ्वसन् न स जीवति॥
en: Yudhishthira said : That person, who does not satisfy the gods, the guests, the servants, the Pitris and his own self, though breathing, is not alive.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: यक्ष उवाच किंस्विद् गुरुतरं भूमेः किस्विदुच्चतरं च खात्। किंस्विच्छीघ्रतरं वायोः किंस्विद् बहुतरं तृणात्॥
en: The Yaksha said : What thing is weightier than the earth? What is it that is higher than the sky? What is fleeter than the wind? And what is more numerous than the grass?

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच माता गुरुतरा भूमेः खात् पितोच्चतरस्तथा। मनः शीघ्रतरं वाताच्चिन्ता बहुतरी तृणात्॥
en: Yudhishthira said: The mother is weightier than the earth; the father is higher than the sky; the mind is fleeter than the wind; and the thoughts are more numerous than the grass.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: यक्ष उवाच किंस्वित् सुप्तं न निमिषति किंस्विज्जातं न चोपति। कस्यस्विद्धदयं नास्ति किंस्विद् वेगेन वर्धते॥
en: The Yaksha said: What is that which does not close the eyes while sleeping? What is it that has no heart? And what is it that swells with its own force?

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच मत्स्यः सुप्तो न निमिषत्यण्डं जातं न चोपति। अश्मनो हृदयं नास्ति नदी वेगेन वर्धते॥
en: Yudhishthira replied Fishes do not close their eyes while sleeping. Eggs do not move after birth. A stone has no heart. And a stream swells with its own force.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: यक्ष उवाच किंस्वित् प्रवसतो मित्रं किंस्विन्मित्रं गृहे सतः। आतुरस्य च किं मित्रं किंस्विन्मित्रं मरिष्यतः॥
en: The Yaksha asked Who is the friend of an exile? Who is the friend of a householder? Who is the friend of a sick person and who of a dying one?

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच सार्थः प्रवसतो मित्रं भार्या मित्रं गृहे सतः। आतुरस्य भिषमित्रं दानं मित्रं मरिष्यतः॥
en: Yudhishthira replied The friend of an exile is his companion; that of a householder is his wife; that of a sick person is his physician and that of a dying one is charity.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: यक्ष उवाच कोऽतिथिः सर्वभूतानां किंस्विद् धर्मं सनातनम्। अमृतं किंस्विद् राजेन्द्र किंस्वित् सर्वमिदं जगत्॥
en: The Yaksha said: Who is the guest of all the creatures? What is the eternal religion? O king of kings, what is Amrita? And what is this entire universe?

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच अतिथिः सर्वभूतानामग्निः सोमो गवामृतम्। सनातनोऽमृतो धर्मो वायुः सर्वमिदं जगत्॥
en: Yudhishthira replied Agni is the guest of all creatures; the milk of the cows is Amrita; Homa with Amrita is the eternal religion; and air is this entire universe.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: यक्ष उवाच किंस्विदेको विचरते जातः को जायते पुनः। किंस्विद्धिमस्य भैषज्यं किंस्विदावपनं महत्॥
en: The Yaksha said : What is it what wanders alone? What is it that is born again after its birth? What is the antidote to cold? And what is the largest field?

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच सूर्य एको विचरते चन्द्रमा जायते पुनः। अग्निहिमस्य भैषज्यं भूमिरावपनं महत्॥
en: Yudhishthira said: It is the sun that wanders alone. The moon is reborn (after her birth). Agni (fire) is the antidote to cold and the earth is the largest field.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: यक्ष उवाच किंस्विदेकपदं धर्म्य किंस्विदेकपदं यशः। किंस्विदेकपदं स्वर्णं किंस्विदेकपदं सुखम्॥
en: The Yaksha asked What is the crowning refuge of religion? What of renown? What is the highest refuge of heaven and what of happiness?

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच दाक्ष्यमेकपदं धर्म्य दानमेकपदं यशः। सत्यमेकपदं स्वयं शीलमेकपदं सुखम्॥
en: Yudhishthira replied The crowning refuge of religion is liberality, that of renown is charity, that of heaven is truth and that of happiness is good conduct.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: यक्ष उवाच किंस्विदात्मा मनुष्यस्य किंस्विद् दैवकृतः सखा। उपजीवनं किंस्विदस्य किंस्विदस्य परायणम्॥
en: The Yaksha asked What is the soul of a man? Who is that friend given to him by Destiny? What is his chief support and what is his best refuge?

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच पुत्र आत्मा मनुष्यस्य भार्या दैवकृतः सखा। उपजीवनं च पर्जन्यो दानमस्य परायणम्॥
en: Yudhishthira replied The soul of a man is his son. The wife is his friend given by Destiny. The clouds are his principal support and charity is his best refuge.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: यक्ष उवाच धन्यानामुत्तमं किंस्विद् धनानां स्यात् किमुत्तमम्। लाभानामुत्तमं किं स्यात् सुखानां स्यात् किमुत्तमम्।७३।
en: The Yaksha asked What is the best of all praise-worthy objects? What is the best of all sorts of wealth? What is the most important of all gains? And what is the best of all kinds of happiness?

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच धन्यानामुत्तमं दाक्ष्यं धनानामुत्तमं श्रुतम्। लाभानां श्रेय आरोग्यं सुखानां तुष्टिरुत्तमा॥
en: Yudhishthira replied Skillfulness is the best of all praise-worthy objects. Knowledge (of the (Vedas) is the best of all (sorts of) wealth. Of all gain health is the most important one. And of all (sorts of) happiness contentment is the best.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: यक्ष उवाच कश्च धर्मः परो लोके कश्च धर्मः सदाफलः। किं नयम्य न शोचन्ति कैश्च संधिर्न जीर्यते॥
en: The Yaksha said: What is the greatest virtue in the world? What religion always bears fruits? What is that controlling which (men) never experience misery? With whom does friendship never break:

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच आनृशंस्यं परो धर्मस्त्रयोधर्मः सदाफलः। मनो यम्य न शोचन्ति संधिः सद्भिर्न जीर्यते॥
en: Yudhishthira said: Absence of cruelty is the highest virtue. The religion of the three (Vedas) always bears fruit. The mind, if subdued, does not lead to misery and friendship with the righteous never breaks.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
