sn: यक्ष उवाच किं नु हित्वा प्रियो भवति किं नु हित्वा न शोचति। । किं नु हित्वार्थवान् भवति किं नु हित्वा सुखी भवेत्॥
en: The Yaksha asked What is it, the renunciation of which makes one dear? What is that which if given up, does not lead to misery? What is that renouncing which one become wealthy? And what is it the renunciation of which makes one happy?

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच मानं हित्वा प्रियो भवति क्रोधं हित्वा न शोचति। कामं हित्वार्थवान् भवति लोभं हित्वा सुखी भवेत्।।७८।
en: Yudhishthira replied It is the sense of pride which, if given up, makes one dear. Abandonment of anger never leads to misery. Desire, if it is renounced, makes one wealthy. Abandonment of avarice makes one happy.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: यक्ष उवाच किमर्थं ब्राह्मणे दानं किमर्थं नटनर्तके। किमर्थं चैव भृत्येषु किमर्थं चैव राजसु॥
en: The Yaksha said: For what purpose does one give away to the Brahmanas? For what to the Natas and the dancers? For what, to the servants? And for what purpose to the kings?

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच धर्मार्थं ब्राह्मणे दानं यशोऽर्थं नटनर्तके। भृत्येषु भरणार्थं वै भयार्थं चैव राजसु॥
en: Yudhishthira said: It is for religious purposes that one gives away to the Brahmanas. It is for renown, to the Natas and the dancers. It is for their support, to the servants. And it is to be saved from fear, to the kings.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: यक्ष उवाच केनस्विदावृतो लोकः केनस्विन्न प्रकाशते। केन त्यजति मित्राणि केन स्वर्गं न गच्छति॥
en: The Yaksha said : What is the thing with which the world is enveloped? Is it for what that a thing cannot discover itself? For what are friends forsaken? What is it for which one can not go to heaven?

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच अज्ञानेनावृतो लोकस्तमसा न प्रकाशते। लोभात् त्यजति मित्राणि संगात् स्वर्ग न गच्छति॥
en: Yudhishthira replied The world is enveloped with ignorance's. It is for spiritual darkness that a thing can not discover itself. It is through avarice that one forsakes his friend. And it is for connection with the world that one cannot go to heaven.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: यक्ष उवाच मृतः कथं स्यात् पुरुषः कथं राष्ट्रं मृतं भवेत्। श्राद्धं मृतं कथं वा स्यात् कथं यज्ञो मृतो भवेत्।।८३।
en: The Yaksha said : Why is a person regarded as dead? Is it for what that a kingdom becomes dead? And for what does a sacrifice become dead?

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच मृतो दरिद्रः पुरुषो मृतं राष्ट्रमराजकम्। मृतमश्रोत्रियं श्राद्धं मृतो यज्ञस्त्वदक्षिणः॥
en: Yudhishthira replied A poor person (though alive) is (considered as) dead. A kingdom without the king becomes dead. A Shraddha celebrated by an ignorant priest becomes dead. And a sacrifice in which nothing is given away is (as good as) dead.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: यक्ष उवाच का दिक् किमुदकं प्रोक्तं किमन्नं किं च वै विषम्। श्राद्धस्य कालमाख्याहि ततः पिब हरस्व च॥
en: The Yaksha said: What is the direction (i.e. the path one should follow)? What is spoken of as water, what, as food and what, as poison? Relate what is the (proper) time of a Shraddha and then drink and carry away water,

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच सन्तो दिग् जलमाकाशं गौरनं प्रार्थना विषम्। श्राद्धस्य ब्राह्मणः कालः कथं वा यक्ष मन्यसे॥
en: Yudhishthira said : It is the righteous that are the direction (i.e. one should follow in the foot steps of the virtuous). The firmament is spoken of as water, the cow as food and request as poison. A Brahmana is the (proper) time for a Shraddha as (i.e. there is no special time for a Shraddha. It may be celebrated whenever an able priest can be secured). O Yaksha, what is your opinion?

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: यक्ष उवाच तपः किंलक्षणं प्रोक्तं को दमश्च प्रकीर्तितः। क्षमा च का परा प्रोक्ता का च ह्रीः परिकीर्तिता॥
en: The Yaksha said: What has been spoken of the characteristic of asceticism? What of self control? What are the prominent features of forgiveness and what of shame?

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच तपः स्वधर्मवर्तित्वं मनसो दमनं दमः। क्षमा द्वन्द्वसहिष्णुत्वं ह्रीरकार्यनिवर्तनम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said: (The characteristic of) asceticism is staying in one's own religion, (that of) self-restraint is control over the mind, (that of) forgiveness is the endurance of enmity and (that of) shame is refraining from all vile acts.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: यक्ष उवाच किं ज्ञानं प्रोच्यते राजन् कः शमश्च प्रकीर्तितः। दया च क परा प्रोक्ता किं चार्जवमुदाहृतम्॥
en: 'The Yaksha asked O king, what is spoken of as knowledge? What is said to be tranquility? What is spoken of as the greatest kindness? And what is instanced as simplicity?

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच ज्ञानं तत्त्वार्थसम्बोधः शमश्चित्तप्रशान्तता। दया सर्वसुखैषित्वमार्जवं समचित्तता॥
en: Yudhishthira replied A thorough grasp of divinity is true knowledge, peacefulness of the mind is tranquility, kindness consists in a desire to do good to all. And equanimity of the mind is (true) simplicity.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: यक्ष उवाच कः शत्रुर्दुर्जयः पुंसां कश्च व्याधिरनन्तकः। कीदृशश्च स्मृतः साधुरसाधुः कीदृशः स्मृतः॥
en: The Yaksha asked What is the invincible enemy of men? What is (their) permanent disease? What sort of men is regarded as honest? And what kind of men is spoken of as dishonest?

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच क्रोधः सुदुर्जयः शत्रुर्लोभो व्याधिरनन्तकः। सर्वभूतहितः साधुरसाधुर्निर्दयः स्मृतः॥
en: Yudhishthira replied Anger is the most invincible enemy. Covetousness is the incurable disease. He who is friendly to all creatures is honest. And he that is cruel is spoken of as dishonest.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: यक्ष उवाच को मोहः प्रोच्यते राजन् कश्च मानः प्रकीर्तितः। किमालस्यं च विज्ञेयं कश्च शोकः प्रकीर्तितः॥
en: The Yaksha said: O king, what is it that is called ignorance? What is spoken of as pride? What is understood by idleness? And what is it that is called grief?

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच मोहो हि धर्ममूढत्वं मानस्त्वात्माभिमानिता। धर्मनिष्क्रियताऽऽलस्यं शोकस्त्वज्ञानमुच्यते॥
en: Yudhishthira said: Absence of religious knowledge is called ignorance. What is called pride is an over weaning opinion of one's ownself. Inaciivity with regard to religion is idleness. And ignorance is grief.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: यक्ष उवाच किं स्थैर्यगृषिभिः प्रोक्तं किं च धैर्यमुदाहृतम्। स्नानं च किं परं प्रोक्तं दानं च किमिहोच्यते॥
en: The Yaksha said : What is it that is spoken of as steadiness by the Rishis? What is it that is instanced as patience? What is said to be the highest ablution? And what is spoken of as charity?

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच स्वधर्मे स्थिरता स्थैर्य धैर्यमिन्द्रियनिग्रहः। स्नानं मनोमलत्यागो दानं वै भूतरक्षणम्॥
en: Yudhishthira replied Steadiness consists in remaining firmly in one's own religion. Control over passions is called patience. True ablution consists in the purification of the mind. Preservation of all creatures is true charity.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: यक्ष उवाच कः पण्डितः पुमाज्ञेयो नास्तिकः कश्च उच्यते। को मूर्खः कश्च कामः स्यात् को मत्सर इति स्मृतः॥
en: The Yaksha said : What person is considered as learned? Who is called an atheist? Who is ignorant? What is it that is spoken of as desire and what, envy?

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच धर्मज्ञः पण्डितो ज्ञेयो नास्तिको मूर्ख उच्यते। कामः संसारहेतुश्च हृत्तापो मत्सरः स्मृतः॥
en: Yudhishthira said : He that is versed in religion is considered as learned. He that is ignorant is called an atheist. Desire consists in a longing for the worldly objects. And what is spoken of as envy is grief is grief of the heart.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: यक्ष उवाच कोऽहङ्कार इति प्रोक्तः कश्च दम्भः प्रकीर्तितः। किं तद् दैवं परं प्रोक्तं किं तत् पैशुन्यमुच्यते॥
en: The Yaksha said : What is spoken of as pride? What is it that is called hypocrisy? What is said to be the grace of the gods? And what is called wickedness?

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच महाज्ञानमहङ्कारो दम्भो धर्मो ध्वजोच्छ्रयः। दैवं दानफलं प्रोक्तं पैशुन्यं परदूषणम्॥१००।
en: Yudhishthira said : Pride consists in stolid ignorance. What is called hypocrisy is the setting up (false show) of the banner of religion. The fruit of charity is divine gift. And wickedness consists in slandering others.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: यक्ष उवाच धर्मश्चार्थश्च कामश्च परस्परविरोधिनः। एषां नित्यविरुद्धानां कथमेकत्र संगमः॥
en: The Yaksha asked Virtue, profit and desire clash against one another. How can, (therefore) these things ever opposed to one another can be united together?

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच यदा धर्मश्च भार्या च परस्परवशानुगौ। तदा धर्मार्थकामानां त्रयाणामपि संगमः॥
en: Yudhishthira replied When virtue and a wife are in harmony with each other (i.e. when the celebration of Agnihotri rites etc. is nor like a Brahmacharya mode of life opposed to a wife and when a wife too does not prove a hindrance to religious duties by opposing acts of charity &c), then these three things virtue, profit and desire can exist together.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: यक्ष उवाच अक्षयो नरकः केन प्राप्यते भरतर्षभ। एतन्मे पृच्छतः प्रश्नं तच्छीघ्रं वक्तुमर्हसि॥
en: The Yaksha asked O best of the Bharatas, who is doomed to eternal damnation? Speedily answer this question asked by me.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच ब्राह्मणं स्वयमाहूय याचमानमकिञ्चनम्। पश्चाननास्तीति यो ब्रूयात् सोऽक्षयं नरकं व्रजेत्।।१०४।
en: Yudhishthira replied He that himself having summoned a poor Brahmana asking (for alms), says that he has nothing, is doomed to eternal hell.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: वेदेषु धर्मशास्त्रेषु मिथ्या यो वै द्विजातिषु। देवेषु पितृधर्मेषु सोऽक्षयं नरकं व्रजेत्॥
en: He, (also), who imputes falsehood to the Vedas, the religious books, the twice-born ones, the gods and the religion of his fore fathers goes to eternal hell.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: विद्यमाने धने लोभाद् दानभोगविवर्जितः। पश्चान्नास्तीति यो ब्रूयात् सोऽक्षयं नरकं व्रजेत्॥
en: He also who has wealth, but who never enjoys it nor gives it away through avarice and says he has none, is doomed to eternal damnation.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: यक्ष उवाच राजन् कुलेन वृत्तेन स्वाध्यायेन श्रुतेन वा। ब्राह्मण्यं केन भवति प्रब्रूह्येतत् सुनिश्चितम्॥
en: The Yaksha said: O king, relate with certainty whether by birth, good character, study of the Vedas or learning or by what a person becomes a Brahmana.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच शृणु यक्ष कुलं तात न स्वाध्यायो न च श्रुतम्। कारणं हि द्विजत्वे च वृत्तमेव न संशयः॥
en: Yudhishthira replied Hear, O Yaksha, O adorable one, Neither birth nor learning (makes one a Brahmana). It admits of no doubt that good character only is the cause of Brahmanhood.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: वृत्तं यत्नेन संरक्ष्यं ब्राह्मणेन विशेषतः। अक्षीणवृत्तो न क्षीणो वृत्ततस्तु हतो हतः॥
en: One, especially a Brahmana, should very carefully maintain his character. One whose character is not weak is never weakened. But he that has lost his character is himself lost.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: पठकाः पाठकाश्चैव ये चान्ये शास्त्रचिन्तकाः। सर्वे व्यसनिनो मूर्खा यः क्रियावान् स पण्डितः॥११०
en: Teachers and students and others who study the Scriptures, if inclined to wicked deeds are to be considered as ignorant. He only that performs meritorious acts is learned.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: चतुर्वेदोऽपि दुर्वृत्तः स शूद्रादतिरिच्यते। योऽग्निहोत्रपरो दान्तः स ब्राह्मण इति स्मृतः॥
en: Even he who has studied the four Vedas but whose conduct is wicked cannot be distinguished from Shudra. He who celebrates the Agnihotra and of subdued passions is called a Brahmana.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: यक्ष उवाच प्रियवचनवादी किं लभते विमृशितकार्यकरः किं लभते। बहुमित्रकरः किं लभते धर्मरत किं लभते कथय॥
en: The Yaksha said: What does a person of agreeable speech gain? What does he gain that acts deliberately? a What does he, who has many friends, gain? And what does he gain who is given to virtue?

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच प्रियवचनवादी प्रियो भवति विमृशितकार्यकरोऽधिकं जयति। बहुमित्रकरः सुखं वसते यश्च धर्मरतः स गतिं लभते॥
en: Yudhishthira said: A person of agreeable speech becomes dear (to all). He that acts deliberately obtains much. He that has many friends lives happily. And he that is given to virtue attains to (an excellent) state.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: यक्ष उवाच को मोदते किमाश्चर्यं कः पन्थाः का च वार्तिका। ममैतांश्चतुरः प्रश्नान् कथयित्वा जलं पिब॥
en: The Yaksha said: Who is happy? What is wonderful? What is the path? And what is the news? Answer these four questions put by me and then let your four dead kinsinen be restored to life.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच पञ्चमेऽहनि षष्ठे वा शाकं पचति स्वे गृहे। अनृणी चाप्रवासी च स वारिचर मोदते॥
en: Yudhishthira said: O aquatic creatures, that one is truly happy who cooks in his own house scanty vegetables in the fifth or sixth portion of the day, but who is neither in debt nor exiled from home.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: अहन्यहनि भूतानि गच्छन्तीह यमालयम्। शेषाः स्थावरमिच्छन्ति किमाश्चर्यमतः परम्॥
en: In this world day by day (innumerable) creatures are going to the abode of Yama. Yet they that remain desire immortality. What can be more marvelous than this?

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: तर्कोऽप्रतिष्ठः श्रुतयो विभिन्ना नैको ऋषिर्यस्य मतं प्रमाणम्। धर्मस्य तत्त्वं निहितं गुहायां महाजनो येन गतः स पन्थाः॥
en: Discussions do not lead to no definite conclusions. The Shrutis are divided (in opinion). And there is not a single Rishi whose opinions can be accepted as conclusive. Truth about religious matters is hidden in caves. (Therefore, that is the proper path which has been followed by great men.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: अस्मिन् महामोहमये कटाहे सूर्याग्निना रात्रिदिवेन्धनेन। मासर्तुदर्वीपरिघट्टटेन भूतानि कालः पचतीति वार्ता।।११८।
en: In this cauldron of the word, which is full of great ignorance, with the sun as its fire, the days and nights as its fuel and the months and the seasons as its wooden ladle, Time is cocking (all) creatures. This is the news.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: यक्ष उवाच व्याख्याता मे त्वया प्रश्ना याथातथ्यं परंतप। पुरुषं त्विदानी व्याख्याहि यश्च सर्वधनी नरः॥
en: The Yaksha said: O tormentor of foes, you have rightly answered all my questions. Now relate to me who can be called a man and what man is enriched with all sorts of wealth.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच दिवं स्पृशति भूमिं च शब्दः पुण्येन कर्मणा। यावत् स शब्दो भवति तावत् पुरुष उच्यते॥
en: Yudhishthira said : The report of a man's meritorious deeds reaches both heaven and earth. And so long as that report continues, he is called a man.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: तुल्ये प्रियाप्रिये यस्य सुखदुःखे तथैव च। अतीतानागते चोभे स वै सर्वधनी नरः॥
en: The man to whom the agreeable and the disagreeable, happiness and misery the past and the future are all alike, is enriched with all sorts of wealth.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: यक्ष उवाच व्याख्यातः पुरुषो राजन् यश्च सर्वधनी नरः। तस्मात् त्वमेकं भ्रातृणां यमिच्छसि स जीवतु॥
en: The Yaksha said: O king, you have (truly) related as to what erson is possessed of all sorts of wealth. Therefore, one of your brothers whomever you wish, be restored to life.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच श्यामो य एष रक्ताक्षो बृहच्छाल इवोत्थितः। व्यूढोरस्को महाबाहुर्नकुलो यक्ष जीवतु॥
en: Yudhishthira said : O Yaksha, let this Nakula, having dark complexion, red eyes, towering as a sala tree, endued with broad chest and long arms, be brought back to life.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: यक्ष उवाच प्रियस्ते भीमसेनोऽयमर्जुनो वः परायणम्। स कस्मान्नकुलं राजन् सापलं जीवमिच्छसि॥
en: The Yaksha said : This Bhimasena is (very) dear to you and this Arjuna is your chief support. Why then, O king, do you desire for the life of Nakula, who is only a step brother of yours?

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: यस्य नागसहस्रेण दशसंख्येन वै बलम्। तुल्यं तं भीममुत्सृज्य नकुलं जीवमिच्छसि॥
en: Why do you, leaving out of consideration Bhima, endued with the strength of ten thousand elephants, desire Nakula to be restored to life?

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: तथैनं मनुजाः प्राहुर्भीमसेनं प्रियं तव। अथ केनानुभावेन सापत्नं जीवमिच्छसि॥
en: They say that Bhimasena is very dear to you. On what consideration, then do you desire for the life of a step brother?

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: यस्य बाहुबलं सर्वे पाण्डवाः समुपासते अर्जुनं तमयाहाय नकुलं जीवमिच्छसि॥
en: Why do you, forsaking Arjuna the strength of whose arms is worshipped by all the Pandavas, wish Nakula to revive?

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच धर्म एव हतो हन्ति धर्मो रक्षति रक्षितः। तस्माद् धर्मं न त्यजामि मा नो धर्मो हतोऽवधीत्॥
en: Yudhishthira said: He who sacrifices virtue is himself destroyed. And he that preserves it is himself preserved. I therefore, do not sacrifice virtue, considering that if destroyed it will destroy us.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: आनृशंस्यं परो धर्मः परमार्थाच्च मे मतम्। आनृशंस्यं चिकीर्षामि नकुलो यक्ष जीवतु॥
en: Refraining from cruelty is the greater virtue and in my opinion greater than the greatest desirable object. I prefer that virtue, viz., refraining from cruelty. Let, O Yaksha, therefore, Nakula be alive.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: धर्मशीलंः सदा राजा इति मां मानवा विदुः। स्वधर्मान्न चलिष्यामि नकुलो यक्ष जीवतु॥
en: People know that, king (Yudhishthira) is always given to virtue. I will never swerve from my duty. Therefore, O Yaksha, let Nakula revive.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: कुन्ती चैव तु माद्री च द्वे भार्ये तु पितुर्मम। उभे सपुत्रे स्यातां वै इति मे धीयते मति॥
en: It is my intention that both the wives of my father, Kunti and Madri have sons.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: यथा कुन्ती तथा माद्री विशेषो नास्ति मे तयोः। मातृभ्यां सममिच्छामि नकुलो यक्ष जीवतु॥
en: As Kunti is to me, so also is Madri. I do not make any distinction between them. I desire to behave equally towards my two mothers, Therefore, O Yaksha, let Nakula be brought back to life.

parva: ARANEYA PARVA)-Continued The questions put by Yaksha (to Yudhishthira
sn: यक्ष उवाच तस्य तेऽर्थाच्च कामाच्च आनृशंस्यं परं मतम्। तस्मात् ते भ्रातरः सर्वे जीवन्तु भरतर्षभ।१३३॥
en: The Yaksha said: O best of the Bharatas, since abstention from cruelty is, in your opinion, superior to both profit and desire, let, therefore all your brothers be restored to life.

description: The revival of Nakula and others
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततस्ते यक्षवचनादुदतिष्ठन्त पाण्डवाः। क्षुत्पिपासे च सर्वेषां क्षणेन व्यपगच्छताम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Then, at the words of the Yaksha the Pandavas rose up and their hunger and thirst forsook them in a short time.

description: The revival of Nakula and others
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच सरस्येकेन पादेन तिष्ठन्तमपराजितम्। पृच्छामि को भवान् देवो न मे यक्षो मतो भवान्॥
en: Yudhishthira said: I ask you, who stand on one leg in the lake and who are unconquerable, what god you are. I can not believe that you are a Yaksha.

description: The revival of Nakula and others
sn: वसूनां वा भवानेको रुद्राणामथवा भवान्। अथवा मरुतां श्रेष्ठो वलशी वा त्रिदशेश्वरः॥
en: Are you the best of the Marutas or the Rudras or the lord of the celestials, the wielder of the thunderbolt.

description: The revival of Nakula and others
sn: मम हि भ्रातर इमे सहस्रशतयोधिनः। तं योधं न प्रपश्यामि येन सर्वे निपातिताः॥
en: Each of these my brothers is able to fight a thousand warriors and I do not find any warrior capable of destroying them all.

description: The revival of Nakula and others
sn: सुखं प्रतिप्रबुद्धानामिन्द्रियाण्युपलक्षये। स भवान् सुहृदोऽस्माकमथवा न: पिता भवान्॥
en: Their organs of sense indicate as if they have awakened from an agreeable slumber. Are you a friend of ours or are you our father himself?

description: The revival of Nakula and others
sn: यक्ष उवाच अहं ते जनकस्तात् धर्मोऽमृदुपराक्रम। त्वां दिदृक्षुरनुप्राप्तो विद्धि मां भरतर्षभ॥
en: The Yaksha said: O child, I am your father Dharma of great strength. Know, O best of the Bharatas, that I have come with the intention on seeing you.

description: The revival of Nakula and others
sn: यशः सत्यं दमः शौचमार्जवं ह्रीरचापलम्। दानं तपो ब्रह्मचर्यमित्येतास्तनवो मम॥
en: Fame, truth, self-control, purity, simplicity, modesty steadiness, charity, asceticism and Brahmacharya are my limbs.

description: The revival of Nakula and others
sn: अहिंसा समता शान्तिरानृशंस्यममत्सरः। द्वाराण्येतानि मे विद्धि प्रियो ह्यसि सदा मम॥
en: Know that absence of cruelty, impartiality, peacefulness, asceticism, purity and want of pride are the (so many) avenues (of attaining to me). You are always (very) dear to me.

description: The revival of Nakula and others
sn: दिष्ट्या पञ्चसुरक्तोऽसि दिष्ट्या तेषट्पदी जिता। द्वे पूर्वे मध्यमे द्वे च द्वे चान्ते साम्परायिके॥
en: It is by good fortune that you are given to the (practice of the) five (virtues namely, equanimity of the mind, self-control, abstenance from sensual indulgence, forgiveness and Yoga). You have by good luck conquered the six (i.e. hunger and thirst, sorrow, delusion, decrepitude and death). (Of these six the first) two show themselves in the first stage of life; the second two in the middle stage and the third two in the last part in order to make creatures go to the next world.

description: The revival of Nakula and others
sn: धर्मोऽहमिति भद्रं ते जिज्ञासुस्त्वामिहागतः। आनृशंस्येन तुष्टोऽस्मि वरं दास्यामि तेऽनघ॥
en: I am Dharma, May you be in bliss. I came here to test you and have been pleased with your spirit of mercy. O sinless one, I will give you boons.

description: The revival of Nakula and others
sn: वरं वृणीष्व राजेन्द्र दाता ह्यस्मि तवानघ। ये हि मे पुरुषा भक्ता न तेषामस्ति दुर्गतिः॥
en: O foremost of kings, crave boons, O sinless one, I will bestow them on you. Those persons that are devoted to me never experience misfortune.

description: The revival of Nakula and others
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच अरणीसहितं यस्य मृगो ह्यादाय गच्छति। तस्याग्नयो न लुप्येरन् प्रथमोऽस्तु वरो मम॥
en: Yudhishthira said: May the Agni of the Brahmana whose firesticks are being carried away by that deer, be not destroyed. This the first boon that I crave.

description: The revival of Nakula and others
sn: यक्ष उवाच अरणीसहितं ह्यस्य ब्राह्मणस्य हृतं मया। मृगवेषेण कौन्तेय जिज्ञासार्थं तव प्रभो॥
en: The Yaksha said: O effulgent son of Kunti, it was in order to test you that I, in the shape of a deer, carried off the fire sticks of that Brahmana.

description: The revival of Nakula and others
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ददानीत्येव भगवानुत्तरं प्रत्यपद्यत। अन्यं वरय भद्रं ते वरं त्वममरोपम॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Thereupon, that exalted one replied “ I give (you this boon). Be blessed. Do you who are like an immortal ask for another boon.

description: The revival of Nakula and others
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच वर्षाणि द्वादशारण्ये त्रयोदशमुपस्थितम्। तत्र नो नाभिजानीयुर्वसतो मनुजाः क्वचित्॥
en: Yudhishthira said: The twelve years O our forest life have passed away and the thirteenth is come. May no man recognise us in the course of this year wherever we may live.

description: The revival of Nakula and others
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ददानीत्येव भगवानुत्तरं प्रत्यपद्यत। भूयश्चाश्वासयामास कौन्तेयं सत्यविक्रमम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said : That god then replied “I give you (this boon also)” He then consoled the son of Kunti endued with the strength of truth (in these words),

description: The revival of Nakula and others
sn: यद्यपि स्वेन रूपेण चरिष्यथ महीमिमाम्। न वो विज्ञास्यते कश्चित् त्रिषु लोकेषु भारत॥
en: "O Bharata, even if you wander in the world in your own proper shapes, no one in the three worlds shall be able to recognize you.

description: The revival of Nakula and others
sn: वर्षं त्रयोदशमिदं मत्प्रसादात् कुरूद्वहाः। विराटनगरे गूढा अविज्ञाताश्चरिष्यथ॥
en: Through my favour, O perpetuator of the Kuru race, you will lead a secret and incognito life in the city of Virata during this thirteenth year.

description: The revival of Nakula and others
sn: यद् वः संकल्पितं रूपं मनसा यस्य यादृशम्। तादृशं तादृशं सर्वे छन्दतो धारयिष्यथ॥
en: And whatever shape every one of you desires in his mind to assume, he will be able to wear (that form) at will.

description: The revival of Nakula and others
sn: अरणीसहितं चेदं ब्राह्मणाय प्रयच्छत। जिज्ञासार्थं मया ह्येतदाहृतं मृगरूपिणा॥
en: Now give to that Brahmana these fire-sticks which I carried away in the shape of a deer in order to test you.

description: The revival of Nakula and others
sn: प्रवृणीष्वापरं सौम्य वरमिष्टं ददानि ते। न तृष्यामि नरश्रेष्ठ प्रयच्छन् वै वरांस्तथा।॥
en: O amiable one, crave another boon that you desire. I will give it. O best of men, I am not satisfied with conferring boons on you.

description: The revival of Nakula and others
sn: तृतीयं गृह्यतां पुत्र वरमप्रतिमं महत्। त्वं हि मत्प्रभवो राजन् विदुरश्च ममांशजः॥
en: O son, accept a third great and unparalleled boon. O king, you have been begotten by me and Vidura is born of a portion of mine.

description: The revival of Nakula and others
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच देवदेवो मया दृष्टो भवान् साक्षात् सनातनः। यं ददासि वरं तुष्टस्तं ग्रहीष्याम्यहं पितः॥
en: Yudhishthira said : You are the god of gods. It is enough that I have seen you in our own shape. I will, O father, accept whatsoever boon you may be pleased to grant me.

description: The revival of Nakula and others
sn: जयेयं लोभमोहौ च क्रोधं चाहं सदा विभो। दाने तपसि सत्ये च मनो मे सततं भवेत्॥
en: O adorable one, may I always get the better of avarice, folly and anger and may my mind be always inclined towards charity, asceticism and truth.

description: The revival of Nakula and others
sn: धर्म उवाच उपपन्नो गुणैरेतैः स्वभावेनासि पाण्डव। भवान् धर्मः पुनश्चैव यथोक्तं ते भविष्यति॥
en: Dharma said: You are by nature gifted with all those virtues, O Pandava. You are (the very embodiment of) Virtue (itself) However, may you again have what you desire.

description: The revival of Nakula and others
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच इत्युक्त्वान्तर्दधे धर्मो भगवाँल्लोकभावनः। समेताः पाण्डवाश्चैव सुखसुप्ता मनस्विनः॥
en: Vaishampayana said: Saying this, the adorable Dharma, whom all the worlds pay homage to, disappeared. And the magnanimous sons of Pandu were joined together after they had enjoyed and agreeable sleep.

description: The revival of Nakula and others
sn: उपेत्य चाश्रमं वीराः सर्व एव गतक्लमाः। आरणेयं ददुस्तस्मै ब्राह्मणाय तपस्विने॥
en: All those heroes, free from fatigue, arriving. at the hermitage gave to that ascetic Brahmana his fire-sticks.

description: The revival of Nakula and others
sn: इदं समुत्थानसमागतं महत्। पितुश्च पुत्रस्य च कीर्तिवर्धनम्। पठन् नरः स्याद् विजितेन्द्रियो वशी सपुत्रपौत्रः शतवर्षभाग् भवेत्॥
en: The man who reads this great and fameenhancing story of the restoration to life (of the Pandavas) and the meeting of the father and the son (i.e. Dharma and Yudhishthira) becomes self controlled, obtains masters over the passions, is blessed with sons and grandsons and lives to a hundred years.

description: The revival of Nakula and others
sn: न चाप्यधर्मे न सुहृद्विभेदने परस्वहारे परदारमर्शने। कदर्यभावे न रमेन्मनः सदा नृणां सदाख्यानमिदं विजानताम्॥
en: Those men that thoroughly apprehend this story are never inclined towards unrighteousness, breaking friendships, misappropriating other peoples property or violating other peoples wives and they never indulge in vile thoughts.

description: The revival of Nakula and others
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच धर्मेण तेऽभ्यनुज्ञाताः पाण्डवाः सत्यविक्रमाः। अज्ञातवासं वत्स्यन्तश्च्छन्ना वर्ष त्रयोदशम्॥ उपोपविष्टा विद्वांसः सहिताः संशितव्रताः। ये तद्भक्ता वसन्ति स्म वनवासे तपस्विनः॥ तानब्रुवन् महात्मानः स्थिताः प्राञ्जलयस्तदा। अभ्यनुज्ञापयिष्यन्तस्तं निवासं धृतव्रताः॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Agrecably to the command to Dharma to pass the thirteenth year (of their exile) incognito, the Pandavas endued with the strength of truth and observant of vows, sat near those learned ascetics who were out of love (for them) dwelling with them in the forest. And with the view of obtaining the permission of these high-souled and vowobserving ones to spend (the afore said thirteenth year) incognito, they (i.e. the Pandavas) spoke to them with joined palms,

description: The revival of Nakula and others
sn: विदितं भवतां सर्वं धार्तराष्ट्रर्यथा वयम्। छाना हृतराज्याश्चानयाश्च बहुशः कृताः॥
en: “You are (no doubt) aware that the sons of Dhritarashtra have robbed us of our kingdom and have inflicted many other injuries on us.

description: The revival of Nakula and others
sn: उषिताश्च वने कृच्छ्रे वयं द्वादश वत्सरान्। अज्ञातवाससमयं शेषं वर्षं त्रयोदशम्॥
en: We have in great misery dwelt in the woods (these) twelve years. The thirteenth year, which we are to spend incognito yet remains, (Therefore) permit us to spend this year unrecognized.

description: The revival of Nakula and others
sn: तद् वसामो वयं छन्नास्तदनुज्ञातुमर्हथ। सुयोधनश्च दुष्टात्मा कर्णश्च सहसौबलः॥ जानन्तो विषमं कुर्युरस्मास्वत्यन्तवैरिणः। युक्तचाराश्च युक्ताश्च पौरस्य स्वजनस्य च॥
en: Now we want to make abode in concealment and you are able to permit us for that. Those rancorous enemies of ours. Suyodhana, the wicked-minded Karna and the son of Subala should they discover us would do great wrong to the citizens and our friends.

description: The revival of Nakula and others
sn: अपि नस्तद् भरेद् भूयो यद् वयं ब्राह्मणैः सह। समस्ताः स्वेषु राष्ट्रेषु स्वराज्यस्था भवेमहि ॥ वैशम्पायन उवाच इत्युक्त्वा दुःखशोकार्तः शुचिर्धर्मसुतस्तदा। सम्मूर्छितोऽभवद् राजा साश्रुकण्ठो युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Shall we all with the Brahmanas be again established in our own kingdom? Having said these words that holy, overwhelmed with deep sorrow and accents choked tears, the son of Dharma king Yudhishthira swooned away.

description: The revival of Nakula and others
sn: तमथाश्वासयन् सर्वे ब्राह्मणा भ्रातृभिः सह। अथ धौम्योऽब्रवीद् वाक्यं महार्थं नृपतिं तदा॥
en: After that the Brahmanas and his brothers began to cheer him up. Then Dhaumya told the King these worlds of fraught and great meaning.

description: The revival of Nakula and others
sn: राजन् विद्वान् भवान् दान्तः सत्यसंधो जितेन्द्रियः। नैवंविधाः प्रमुह्यन्ते नराः कस्याञ्चिदापदि॥
en: O king, you are well leamed, tamed, observant of vows and subdued sense, men of such type are not overwhelmed by any calamity whatever.

description: The revival of Nakula and others
sn: देवैरप्यापदः प्राप्ताश्च्छन्नैश्च बहुशस्तथा। तत्र तत्र सपत्नानां निग्रहार्थं महात्मभिः॥
en: Even the high-souled gods themselves have wandered over various places in concealment, for the purpose of destroying the enemies.

description: The revival of Nakula and others
sn: इन्द्रेण निषधान् प्राप्य गिरिप्रस्थाश्रमे तदा। छन्नेनोष्य कृतं कर्म द्विषतां च विनिग्रहे।॥
en: Indra for the purpose of defeating his enemies, dwelt in disguise in the asylum of Giriprastha in Nishadha and thus attained his end.

description: The revival of Nakula and others
sn: विष्णुनाश्वशिरः प्राप्य तथादित्यां निवत्स्यता। गर्भ वधार्थं दैत्यानामज्ञातेनोषितं चिरम्॥
en: And for the purpose of killing the Danavas Lord Vishnu passed a long time indisguise in the womb of Aditi (mother of gods) before taking his birth simulating the form of the Hayagriva (horse-necked).

description: The revival of Nakula and others
sn: प्राप्य वामनरूपेण प्रच्छन्नं ब्रह्मरूपिणा। बलेर्यथा हृतं राज्यं विक्रमैस्तच्च ते श्रुतम्॥
en: Then how disguising himself in the form of dwarf, he (Vishnu) by his prowess deprived vail of the kingdom of Bali, have been heard by you?

description: The revival of Nakula and others
sn: हुताशनेन यच्चापः प्रविश्यच्छन्नमासता। विबुधानां कृतं कर्म तच्च सर्वं श्रुतं त्वया॥
en: And also Hutashana entering into water and remaining in disguise, obtained the purpose of the gods, have been heard by you?

description: The revival of Nakula and others
sn: प्रच्छन्नं चापि धर्मज्ञ हरिणारिविनिग्रह। वलां प्रविश्य शक्रस्य यत् कृतं तच्च ते श्रुतम्॥
en: How Hari for the purpose of overcoming his enemies, entered into Shakra's thunderbolt lying unrecognized there, O skilled in duly, have you heard this?

description: The revival of Nakula and others
sn: और्वेण वसता छन्नमूरौ ब्रह्मर्षिणा तदा। यत् कृतं तात देवेषु कर्म तत्तेऽनघ श्रुतम्॥
en: O Sinless one, O child you have heard of the office the regenerate Rishi Auarv at one time performed for the gods having disguised in the womb of his mother?

description: The revival of Nakula and others
sn: एवं विवस्वता तात छन्नेनोत्तमतेजसा। निर्दग्धाः शात्रवाः सर्वे वसता भुवि सर्वशः॥
en: And O child, remaining concealed in every part of the earth, Vivasvata, endued with excellent power, at last entirely burnt up all his foes,

description: The revival of Nakula and others
sn: विष्णुना वसता चापि गृहे दशरथस्य वै। दशग्रीवो हतश्छन्नं संयुगे भीमकर्मणा॥
en: And also living disguised in the abode of Dasharatha, the dreadful acted Lord Vishnu killed the ten-necked Ravana in battle.

description: The revival of Nakula and others
sn: एवमेव महात्मानः प्रच्छन्नास्तत्र तत्र ह। अजयञ्छात्रवान् युद्धे तथा त्वमपि जेष्यसि॥
en: Having disguised in many places, high souled persons have conquered their foes in battle, thus you will also win your enemies.

description: The revival of Nakula and others
sn: तथा धौम्येन धर्मज्ञो वाक्यैः सम्परितोषितः। शास्त्रबुद्ध्या स्वबुद्ध्या च न चचाल युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Thus cheered by these words of Dhaumya, the virtuous Yudhishthira, relying on his own wisdom and also that gained from Shastras, regained his patience.

description: The revival of Nakula and others
sn: अथाब्रवीन्महाबाहुर्भीमसेनो महाबलः। राजानं बलिनां श्रेष्ठो गिरा सम्परिहर्षयन्॥
en: Then the exceeding strong and long armed Bhimasena, the foremost of mighty person encouraging the king greatly spoke these words

description: The revival of Nakula and others
sn: अवेक्षया महाराज तव गाण्डीवधन्वना। धर्मानुगतया बुद्ध्या न किञ्चित् साहसं कृतम्॥
en: O King, looking towards your face, the wilder of Gandiva bow acting according to his sense of duty has not shown my rashness.

description: The revival of Nakula and others
sn: सहदेवो मया नित्यं नकुलश्च निवारितौ। शक्तौ विध्वंसने तेषां शत्रूणां भीमविक्रमौ॥
en: Nakula and Sahadeva of dreadful valour were also fully capable to slay those enemies, but they have been prevented by me all the time.

description: The revival of Nakula and others
sn: न वयं तत् प्रहास्यामो यस्मिन् योक्ष्यति नो भवान्। भवान् विधत्तां तत् सर्वं क्षिप्रं जेष्यामहे रिपून्।॥
en: Never shall we town aside from that in which you will engage us? Do you tell us a proper act? We shall overcome to our foes at very soon.

description: The revival of Nakula and others
sn: इत्युक्ते भीमसेनेन ब्राह्मणः परमाशिषा। उक्त्वा चापृच्छ्य भरतान्यथास्वान्स्वान्ययुगुहान्॥
en: Having said these words by Bhimasena, the Brahmanas uttered blessings on the Bharatas and after that receiving their permission, went to their own abodes.

description: The revival of Nakula and others
sn: सर्वे वेदविदो मुख्या यतयो मुनयस्तथा। आसेदुस्ते यथान्यायं पुनर्दर्शनकाझया॥
en: And all those foremost of Yatis and Munis, versed in the Vedas, exceedingly desirous of again beholding the Pandavas went back to their respective homes.

description: The revival of Nakula and others
sn: सह धौम्येन विद्वांसस्तथा पञ्च च पाण्डवाः। उत्थाय प्रययुर्वीराः कृष्णामादाय धन्विनः॥
en: And accompanied by Dhaumya, these heroes, the learned five Pandavas versed in bows get out with lord Krishna.

description: The revival of Nakula and others
sn: क्रोशमात्रमुपागम्य तस्माद् देशान्निमित्ततः। श्वोभूते मनुजव्याघ्राश्छन्नवासार्थमुद्यताः॥ पृथक्छास्त्रविदः सर्वे सर्वे मन्त्रविशारदाः। संधिविग्रहकालज्ञा मन्त्राय समुपाविशन्॥
en: After passing a Kosa from that place they sat down with the view of taking advice of each other, about to enter upon a life of unrecognized. They all were learned in separate science (Shastra) and all proficient in the Mantras. Those tigers among the men were cognizant of time for peace and war.

description: The counsel of Yudhishthira and others
sn: नारायणं नमस्कृत्यं नरं चैव नरोत्तमम्। देवी सरस्वतीं व्यासं ततो जयमुदीरयेत्॥
en: Having saluted Narayana and Nara the best of male beings as also the goddess of learning let us cry success.

description: The counsel of Yudhishthira and others
sn: जनमेजय उवाच कथं विराटनगरे मम पूर्वपितामहाः। अज्ञातवासमुषिता दुर्योधनभयार्दिताः॥
en: Janamejaya said How did my great grand fathers, stricken with the fear of Duryodhana, live incognito in the city of Virata?

description: The counsel of Yudhishthira and others
sn: पतिव्रतः महाभागा सततं ब्रह्मवादिनी। द्रौपदी च कथं ब्रह्मन्नज्ञाता दुःखितावसत्॥
en: O Brahmana, how did the highly lucky Draupadi, devoted to her husbands, afflicted with woe and in the habit of reciting the names of the Supreme being, live undiscovered?

description: The counsel of Yudhishthira and others
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच यथा विराटनगरे तव पूर्वपितामहाः। अज्ञातवासमुषितास्तच्छृणुष्व नराधिप॥
en: Vaishampayana said Listen, O ruler of men, how your great grand-fathers spent their days in the city of Virata without being discovered.

description: The counsel of Yudhishthira and others
sn: तथा स तु वरॉल्लब्ध्वा धर्मो धर्मभृतां वरः। गत्वाऽऽश्रमं ब्राह्मणेभ्य आचख्यौ सर्वमेव तत्॥
en: Having thus received the boon from Dharma (the god of virtue) the best of the virtuous retired to the asylum, and described to the Brahmanas, all that came to pass.

description: The counsel of Yudhishthira and others
sn: कथयित्वा तु तत् सर्वं ब्राह्मणेभ्यो युधिष्ठिरः। अरणीसहितं तस्मै ब्राह्मणाय न्यवेदयत्॥
en: Having described everything to the Brahmanas, Yudhishthira gave over to the Brahmana the fire sticks along with the churning staff which he had lost.

description: The counsel of Yudhishthira and others
sn: ततो युधिष्ठिरो राजा धर्मपुत्रो महामनाः। संनिवर्त्यानुजान् सर्वानिति होवाच भारत॥
en: 0 Bharata, then the high-souled potentate Yudhishthira, the offspring of Dharma, called all his younger brothers together and addressed them thus:

description: The counsel of Yudhishthira and others
sn: द्वादशेमानि वर्षाणि राज्यविप्रोषिता वयम्। त्रयोदशोऽयं सम्प्राप्तः कृच्छ्रात् परमदुर्वसः॥
en: For these twelve years, we have been exiled from our kingdom. This is the thirteenth year very had to pass.

description: The counsel of Yudhishthira and others
sn: स साधु कौन्तेय इतो वासमर्जुन रोचय। संवत्सरमिमं यत्र वसेमाविदिताः परैः॥
en: Therefore, O Arjuna, the son of Kunti, from here make a judicious choice of a place where we may stay one year without being known by our enemies.

description: The counsel of Yudhishthira and others
sn: अर्जुन उवाच तस्यैव वरदानेन धर्मस्य मनुजाधिप। अज्ञाता विचरिष्यामो नराणां नात्र संशयः॥
en: Arjuna said O lord of men, by virtue of Dharma's gift of boon we shall to about without being known to the people. There is no doubt of it.

description: The counsel of Yudhishthira and others
sn: तत्र वासाय राष्ट्राणि कीर्तयिष्यामि कानिचित्। रमणीयानि गुप्तानि तेषां किञ्चित् स्म रोचया॥
en: from among But for purposes of our abode I shall mention some places some places both pleasant and sequestered, please fix upon those.

description: The counsel of Yudhishthira and others
sn: सन्ति रम्या जनपदा बनाः परितः कुरून्। पाञ्चालाचैदिमत्स्याश्च शूरसेनाः पटच्चराः॥ दशार्णा नवराष्ट्राश्च मल्लाः शाल्वा युगन्धराः। कुन्तिराष्ट्रं च विपुलं सुराष्ट्रावन्तयस्तथा॥
en: About the kingdom of Kurus there are many beautiful countries with plenty of corn viz. Panchala, Chedi, Matsya, Shurasena, Patachchara, Dasharna, Navarashtra, Malla, Shalva, Yugandhara and extensive Kuntirashtra, Saurashtra and Avanti.

description: The counsel of Yudhishthira and others
sn: एतेषां कतमो राजन् निवासस्तव रोचते। यत्र वत्स्यामहे राजन् संवत्सरमिमं वयम्॥
en: Which of these, O king, do you select for your abode, where we may live all the year round. On which of these places, Oking, does your choice fall, where we may live all the year round.

description: The counsel of Yudhishthira and others
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच श्रुतमेतन्महाबाहो यथा स भगवान् प्रभुः। अब्रवीत् सर्वभूतेशस्तत् तथा न तदन्यथा॥
en: Yudhishthira said O you of mighty arms, what the worshipful deity (Dharma), the lord of all beings, has said must be so; there can be no other alternative.

description: The counsel of Yudhishthira and others
sn: अवश्यं त्वेव वासार्थं रमणीयं शिवं सुखम्। सम्मन्त्र्य सहितैः सर्वैर्वस्तव्यमकुतोभयैः॥
en: After consulting together we must seek out a pleasant auspicious and agreeable place, where we may live all together without fear.

description: The counsel of Yudhishthira and others
sn: मत्स्यो विराटो बलवानभिरक्तोऽथ पाण्डवान्। धर्मशीलो वदान्यश्च वृद्धश्च सततं प्रियः॥
en: The aged Virata, the king of Matsya, is powerful, charitable, of righteous disposition, ever beloved and also attached to the Pandavas.

description: The counsel of Yudhishthira and others
sn: विराटनगरे तात संवत्सरमिमं वयम्। कुर्वन्तस्तस्य कर्माणि विहरिष्याम भारत॥
en: In the city of Virata, O dear one, we shall, O Bharata, spend the whole of his year, doing his work.

description: The counsel of Yudhishthira and others
sn: तत् कर्म यानि यानि च कर्माणि तस्य वक्ष्यामहे वयम्। आसाद्य मत्स्यं प्रबूत कुरुनन्दनाः॥
en: Tell me, O sons of Kuru, in what capacities we shall have to present ourselves after we shall have gone to the king of the Matsya.

description: The counsel of Yudhishthira and others
sn: अर्जुन उवाच नरदेव कथं तस्य राष्ट्रे कर्म करिष्यसि। विराटनगरे साधो रंस्यसे केन कर्मणा॥
en: Arjuna said O god among men, how will you work in his domain, O virtuous one, in what capacity will you reside in the city of Virata?

description: The counsel of Yudhishthira and others
sn: मृदुर्वदान्यो ह्रीमांश्च धार्मिकः सत्यविक्रमः। राजंस्त्वमापदाऽऽकृष्टः किं करिष्यसि पाण्डव॥
en: O king, you are gentle, charitable, modest, righteous, and true to promise. O Pandava, what will you do, although afflicted with calamity.

description: The counsel of Yudhishthira and others
sn: न दुःखमुचितं किञ्चिद् राजन् वेद यथा जनः। स इमामापदं प्राप्य कथं घोरां तरिष्यसि॥
en: Like an ordinary person a king is not accustomed to hardships; how will you, as a king, thus get over the awful calamity that has overtaken you.

description: The counsel of Yudhishthira and others
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच शृणुध्वं यत् करिष्यामि कर्म वै कुरुनन्दनाः। विराटमनुसम्प्राप्य राजानं पुरुषर्षभाः॥
en: Yudhishthira said O you sons of Kuru, O you best among men, listen what work I shall do after having come before the king Virata.

description: The counsel of Yudhishthira and others
sn: सभास्तारो भविष्यामि तस्य राज्ञो महात्मनः। कङ्को नाम द्विजो भूत्वा मताक्षः प्रियदेवनः॥
en: Appearing as a twice-born one, Kanka by name, expert in dice and fond of game, I shall be a counter of that high-minded king.

description: The counsel of Yudhishthira and others
sn: वैदूर्यान् काञ्चनान् दान्तान् फलैर्योतीरसैः सह। कृष्णाँल्लोहितवर्णाश्च निर्वामि मनोरमान्॥ विराटराजं रमयन् सामात्यं सहबान्धवम्। न च मां वेत्स्यते कश्चित् तोषयिष्ये च तं नृपम्।।२६
en: Moving upon boards nice ivory pawns, blue, yellow, red and white, by means of red and black dice I shall please the king with his friends and ministers. When I shall thus be satisfying the king no body shall be able to find me out.

description: The counsel of Yudhishthira and others
sn: आसं युधिष्ठिरस्याहं पुरा प्राणसमः सखा। इति वक्ष्यामि राजानं यदि मां सोऽनुयोक्ष्यते॥
en: If the king asks me I shall say-"formerly I was the friend of Yudhishthira, as dear as his life.”

description: The counsel of Yudhishthira and others
sn: इत्येतद् वो मयाऽऽख्यातं विहरिष्याम्यहं यथा। वृकोदर विराटे त्वं रंस्यसे केन हेतुना॥
en: I have told you all that-how I would pass my days there. O Vrikodara, in what capacity will you live in the city of Virata?

description: The counsels of Yudhishthira and others
sn: भीमसेन उवाच पौरोगवो ब्रुवाणोऽहं बल्लवो नाम भारत। उपस्थास्यामि राजानं विराटमिति मे मतिः।।।।
en: Bhima said O Bharata, I shall present myself before the king Virata, calling myself a cook, named Ballava. This is my intention.

description: The counsels of Yudhishthira and others
sn: सूपानस्य करिष्यामि कुशलोऽस्मि महानसे। कृतपूर्वाणि यान्यस्य व्यञ्जनानि सुशिक्षितैः॥ तान्यप्यभिभविष्यामि प्रीतिं संजनयन्त्रहम्। आहरिष्यामि दारूणां निचयान् महतोऽपि च॥ यत् प्रेक्ष्य विपुलं कर्म राजा संयोक्ष्यते स माम्। अमानुषाणि कुर्वाणस्तानि कर्माणि भारत॥ राज्ञस्तस्य परे प्रेष्या मंस्यन्ते मां यथा नृपम्। भक्ष्यान्नरसपानानां भविष्यामि तथेश्वरः॥
en: I shall prepare his curries. I am expert in the business of the kitchen. I shall supercede even those experts who used to made curries for him before and I shall carry from biggest loads of wood and thus render every service; and the king, having seen that splendid work, will appoint me. O Bharata, beholding me doing these superhuman deeds the servants of the monarch will regard me as a king. Thus I shall be the lord of all sorts of food and drink.

description: The counsels of Yudhishthira and others
sn: द्विपा वा बलिनो राजन् वृषभा वा महाबलाः। विनिग्राह्या यदि मया निग्रहीष्यामि तानपि॥ ये च केचिन्नियोत्स्यन्ति समाजेषु नियोधकाः। तानहं हि नियोत्स्यामि रतिं तस्य विवर्धयन्॥ न त्वेतान् युद्ध्यमानान् वै हनिष्यामि कथञ्चन। तथैतान् पातयिष्यामि यथा यास्यन्ति न क्षयम्॥
en: O king, if I am commanded to overpower the mighty elephants and powerful bulls I will do that. I will defeat those combatants who will fight against me in the lists in order to satisfy the monarch but I shall not kill those fighting heroes, but bring them down in such a way that they may not perish.

description: The counsels of Yudhishthira and others
sn: आरालिको गोविकर्ता सूपकर्ता नियोधकः। आसं युधिष्ठिरस्याहमिति वक्ष्यामि पृच्छतः॥ आत्मानमात्मना रक्षश्चरिष्यामि विशाम्पते। इत्येतत् प्रतिजानामि विहरिष्याम्यहं यथा॥
en: On being asked, I shall say, “Formerly I was the cook, subduer of animals, maker of curries and wrestler of Yudhishthira. O lord of me, in whatever direction I shall went my way I shall take care of my own person. This much I promise.

description: The counsels of Yudhishthira and others
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच यमग्निर्ब्राह्मणो भूत्वा समागच्छन्नृणां वरम्। दिधक्षुः खाण्डवं दावं दाशार्हसहितं पुरा॥ महाबलं महाबाहुमजितं कुरुनन्दनम्। सोऽयं किं कर्म कौन्तेयः करिष्यति धनंजयः॥
en: Yudhishthira said What work will Dhananjaya, the son of Kunti, perform, who is mighty, long armed, invincible, the foremost of men, and the joy of Kurus, and before whom formerly the fire-god, desirous of consuming the Khandava forest, appeared in the guise of a Brahmana.

description: The counsels of Yudhishthira and others
sn: योऽयमासाद्य तं दावं तर्पयामास पावकम्। विजित्यैकरथेनेन्द्रं हत्वा पन्नगराक्षसान्॥ वासुकेः सर्पराजस्य स्वसारं हृतवांश्च यः। श्रेष्ठो यः प्रतियोधानां सोऽर्जुनः किं करिष्यति॥
en: What work will be performed by the best of dualists Arjuna, who having ascended the single chariot with Krishna, repaired to the forest and gratified the fire god after defeating and destroying the Pannagas and Rakshasas and who carried off the sister of the serpentking named Vasuki.

description: The counsels of Yudhishthira and others
sn: सूर्यः प्रतपतां श्रेष्ठो द्विपदां ब्राह्मणो वरः। आशीविषश्च सर्पाणामग्निस्तेजस्विनां वरः॥ आयुधानां वरं वज्रं ककुद्मी च गवां वरः। ह्रदानामुदधिः श्रेष्ठः पर्जन्यो वर्षतां वरः॥ धृतराष्ट्रश्च नागानां हस्तिष्वैरावणो वरः। पुत्रः प्रियाणामधिको भार्या च सुहृदां वरा॥ यथैतानि विशिष्टानि जात्यां जात्यां वृकोदर। एवं युवा गुडाकेश: श्रेष्ठः सर्वधनुष्मताम्॥
en: The sun is the foremost of all shining bodies, the Brahmana is the foremost of all bipeds, the Ashivisha is the foremost of all serpents, the fire is the foremost of all bright substances, thunder is the foremost of all weapons, the humped bull is the foremost of its kind, the ocean is the foremost of all watery expanses, the Parjanya is the foremost of all rain clouds, Dhritarashtra is the foremost of all Nagas, Airavata is the foremost of all elephants, the son is the foremost of all beloved objects, and the wife is the foremost of all friends. O Vrikodara, as every species has its, best, so is the youthful Gudakesha the best of all archers.

description: The counsels of Yudhishthira and others
sn: सोऽयमिन्द्रादनवरो वासुदेवान्महाद्युतिः। गाण्डीवधन्वा बीभत्सुः श्वेताश्वः किं करिष्यति॥
en: What office will be performed by Bibhatsu of great splendour, whose bow is Gandiva, and whose chariot is drawn by white horses and who is in no way inferior to Indra or Vasudeva himself?

description: The counsels of Yudhishthira and others
sn: उषित्वा पञ्च वर्षाणि सहस्राक्षस्य वेश्मनि। अस्त्रयोगं समासाद्य स्ववीर्यान्मानुषाद्भुतम्। दिव्यान्यस्त्राणि चाप्तानि देवरूपेण भास्वता॥ यं मन्ये द्वादशं रुद्रमादित्यानां त्रयोदशम्। वसूनां नवमं मन्ये ग्रहाणां दशमं तथा॥ यस्य बाहू समौ दी? ज्याघातकठिनत्वचौ। दक्षिणे चैव सव्ये च गवामिव वहः कृतः॥ हिमवानिव शैलानां समुद्रः सरितामिव। त्रिदशानां यथा शक्रो वसूनामिव हव्यवाट्॥ मृगाणामिव शार्दूलो गरुडः पततामिव। वरः संन्यमानानां सोऽर्जुनः किं करिष्यति॥
en: What office will be performed by Arjuna shining in celestial grace, who, having stayed for five years in the abode of the thousandeyed deity, acquired by his superhuman prowess, the art of using arms along with all the celestial weapons, and who is me-seems like the Rudra, thirteenth of the Adityas, ninth of the Vasus and the tenth of the Grahas, whose arms are symmetrical and long, having the skin rendered hard by repeated strokes of the bow string and knobs on which appear like the humps of bulls and who is the foremost of warriors as the Himavata of mountains, the sea of rivers, Shakra of the gods, Havyavahak (fire) of the Vasus, the tiger of the beasts, Garuda of the winged tribes.

description: The counsels of Yudhishthira and others
sn: अर्जुन उवाच प्रतिज्ञा घण्ढकोऽस्मीति करिष्यामि महीपते। ज्याघातौ हि महान्तौ मे संवर्तुं नृप दुष्करौ॥
en: Arjuna said O ruler of the earth, I shall declare myself to be one of the neuter sex, but O king, it is very difficult to conceal the big strokes of the bow-string on my arms.

description: The counsels of Yudhishthira and others
sn: वलयैश्छादयिष्यामि बाहू किणकृताविमौ। कर्णयोः प्रतिमुच्याहं कुण्डले ज्वलनप्रभे॥
en: However, I shall conceal with the bangles the marks of my arm caused by the bow-string.

description: The counsels of Yudhishthira and others
sn: पिनद्धकम्बुः पाणिभ्यां तृतीयां प्रकृतिं गतः। वेणीकृतशिरा राजन् नाम्ना चैव बृहन्नला।॥ पठन्नाख्यायिकाश्चैव स्त्रीभावेन पुनः पुनः। रमयिष्ये महीपालमन्यांश्चान्तःपुरे जनान्॥
en: Having worn rings shining as fire on my ears and conch-bangles on my wrist, and dressing my hair in a bread on my head and taking the name of Brihannala I shall, O king, appear as one of the third sex, and please the king and others in the seraglio by reciting stories often and often as becomes a female.

description: The counsels of Yudhishthira and others
sn: गीतं नृत्यं विचित्रं च वादिनं विविधं तथा। शिक्षयिष्याम्यहं राजन् विराटस्य पुरस्त्रियः॥
en: O king, I shall instruct the ladies of Virata's house in singing, delightful dancing and also in musical performances of sundry sorts.

description: The counsels of Yudhishthira and others
sn: प्रजानां समुदाचारं बहु कर्म कृतं वदन। छादयिष्यामि कौन्तेय माययाऽऽत्मानमात्मना॥
en: And in reciting various good deeds and customs of people, I shall, O son of Kunti, conceal myself in disguise.

description: The counsels of Yudhishthira and others
sn: युधिष्ठिरस्य गेहे वै द्रौपद्याः परिचारिका। उषितास्मीति वक्ष्यामि पृष्टो राज्ञा च पाण्डव॥
en: O Pandava, on being asked by the king I shall say “I lived as a waiting maid of Draupadi in the palace of Yudhishthira.

description: The counsels of Yudhishthira and others
sn: एतेन विधिना छन्नः कृतकेन यथानलः। विहरिष्यामि राजेन्द्र विराटभवने सुखम्॥
en: O great king, hiding myself by this counterfeiting means as fire is concealed by ashes, I shall happily pass my days in the palace of Virata.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच स्तथार्जुनो धर्मभृतां वरिष्ठः। वाक्यं तथासौ विरराम भूयो नृपोऽपरं भ्रातरमाबभाषे॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having spoken thus, Arjuna, the best of men and the foremost of the virtuous, ceased, and the king again asked his another brother.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच किं त्वं नकुल कुर्वाणस्तत्र तात चरिष्यसि। कर्म तत् त्वं समाचक्ष्व राज्ये तस्य महीपतेः। सुकुमारश्च शूरश्च दर्शनीयः सुखोचितः॥
en: Yudhishthira said O Nakula, tender, heroic, graceful and accustomed to pleasurable pursuits as you are, what work will you do in the dominion of Virata, tell me that.

sn: नकुल उवाच अश्वबन्धो भविष्यामि विराटनृपतेरहम्। सर्वथा ज्ञानसम्पन्नः कुशलः परिरक्षणे॥
en: Nakula said I shall be the keeper of the horses of king Virata; I possess thorough knowledge of the business, and am expert in the tending of them,

sn: ग्रन्थिको नाम नाम्नाहं कमैतत् सुप्रियं मम। कुशलोऽस्म्यश्वशिक्षायां तथैवाश्वचिकित्सने।।
en: I shall be designated Granthika. The avocation is congenial to me. I am expert both in training and treating horses.

sn: प्रियाश्च सततं मेऽश्वाः कुरुराज यथा तव॥ ये मामामन्त्रयिष्यन्ति विराटनगरे जनाः। तेभ्य एवं प्रवक्ष्यामि विहरिष्याम्यहं यथा॥ पाण्डवेन पुरा तात अश्वेष्वधिकृतः : पुरा। विराटनगरे छन्नश्चरिष्यामि महीपते॥
en: O king of the Kurus, horses are even dear to me as they are to you. Those who will question me in the city of the Virat will be thus told by me. "Formerly I was placed by Yudhishthira in charge of his horses. O ruler of the earth, I shall thus disguised go about in the city of Virata.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच सहदेव कथं तस्य समीपे विहरिष्यसि। किं वा त्वं कर्म कुर्वाणः प्रच्छन्नो विहरिष्यसि॥
en: Yudhishthira said O Sahadeva, how will you appear before him or what work will you do so that you may walk about undiscovered.

sn: सहदेव उवाच गोसंख्याता भविष्यामि विराटस्य महीपतेः। प्रतिषेद्धा च दोग्धा च संख्याने कुशलो गवाम्॥
en: Sahadeva said I shall be the counter of the cows of the king Virata; I am skilled in taming, milking and counting them.

sn: तन्तिपाल इति ख्यातो नाम्नाहं विदितस्त्वथ। निपुणं च चरिष्यामि व्येतु ते मानसो ज्वरः॥
en: Denominated as Tantipala and by that name I shall clearly do my duty. Let your mental anxiety be dispelled.

sn: अहं हि सततं गोषु भवता प्रहितः पुरा। तत्र मे कौशलं सर्वमवबुद्धं विशाम्पते।॥
en: Very often was I formerly employed by you in looking after your cows. O Lord of the earth, all the arts that the business involves are known to me.

sn: लक्षणं चरितं चापि गवां यच्चापि मङ्गलम्। तत् सर्वं मे सुविदितमन्यच्चापि महीपते॥
en: 0 ruler of the earth, the nature, the characteristics and the favorable marks and other points regarding cows are well known to me.

sn: वृषभानपि जानामि राजन् पूजितलक्षणान्। येषां मूत्रमुपाघ्राय अपि वध्या प्रसूयते॥
en: I also know the bulls bearing favourable marks whose urine on being smelt makes even the barren productive.

sn: सोऽहमेवं चरिष्यामि प्रीतिरत्र हि मे सदा। न च मां वेत्स्यते कश्चित् तोषयिष्ये च पार्थिवम्॥१३
en: Thus shall I pass my days; there is always a delight for me in this work, and no one shall recognize me and moreover I will entertain the monarch.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच इयं हि नः प्रिया भार्या प्राणेभ्योऽपि गरीयसी। मातेव परिपाल्या च पूज्या ज्येष्ठेव च स्वसा॥
en: Yudhishthira said This is our beloved wife dearer even than life. Like a mother she is to be cherished and like an elder sister she is to be respected.

sn: केन स्म द्रौपदी कृष्णा कर्मणा विचरिष्यति। न हि किञ्चिद् विजानाति कर्म कर्तुं यथा स्त्रियः।।१५
en: In what capacity will Krishna the daughter of Drupada, appear; like other women she does not know how to do any work.

sn: सुकुमारी च बाला च राजपुत्री यशस्विनी। पतिव्रता महाभागा कथं नु विचरिष्यति॥
en: Tender and young is the king's daughter, endowed with eminence, devoted to her lords and highly virtuous; how will she pass her days?

sn: माल्यगन्धानलङ्कारान् वस्त्राणि विविधानि च। एतान्येवाभिजानाति यतो जाता हि भामिनी॥
en: Since her very birth the handsome lady has only been accustomed to garlands, perfumes, ornaments and diverse kinds of robes.

sn: द्रौपधुवाच सैरन्ध्रयो रक्षिता लोके भुजिष्याः सन्ति भारत। नैवमन्याः स्त्रियो यान्ति इति लोकस्य निश्चयः।। साहं ब्रुवाणा सैरन्ध्री कुशला केशकर्मणि॥
en: Draupadi said O Bharata, there is a class of maid-servants called Sairandhri employed in the service of others and it is the conviction of people that no (respectable) ladies will enter it.

sn: युधिष्ठिरस्य गेहे वै द्रौपद्याः परिचारिका। उषितास्मीति वक्ष्यामि पृष्टा राज्ञा च भारत॥ आत्मगुप्ता चरिष्यामि यन्मां त्वं परिपृच्छसि।॥
en: I shall call myself Sairandhri skilled in dressing hair; and asked by the king, O Bharata, I shall say “I was a waiting maid to Draupadi in the house of Yudhishthira," and as you ask me (I say) I, shall pass my days concealing myself.

sn: सुदेष्णां प्रत्युपस्थास्ये राजभार्यां यशस्विनीम्। सा रक्षिष्यति मां प्राप्तां मा भूत् ते दुःखमीदृशम्।।२१
en: I shall serve Shudeshna the reputed wife, of the king, and getting me, she will keep me. Let this anxiety of yours be set at rest.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच कल्याणं भाषसे कृष्णे कुले जातासि भामिनि। न पापमभिजानासि साध्वी साधुव्रते स्थिता॥
en: Yudhishthira said O Krishna, you have spoken well, O fair one, you are born in a noble family; chaste as you are and engaged in pursuit of pious vows you are a stranger to sin.

sn: यथा न दुहृदः पापा भवन्ति सुखिनः पुनः। कुर्यास्तत् त्वं हि कल्याणि लक्षयेयुर्न ते तथा॥
en: O blessed one, you should behave yourself in such a way that the wicked and sinful men inay have no chance of deriving pleasure from looking at you.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच कर्माण्युक्तानि युष्माभिर्यानि यानि करिष्यथ। मम चापि यथा बुद्धिरुचिता विधिनिश्चयात्॥
en: Yudhishthira said In consonance with the ordinance, the works which you will perform have been already described by you, and I have also said according to my discretion the office which I shall perform.

sn: पुरोहितोऽयमस्माकमग्निहोत्राणि रक्षतु। सूदपौरोगवैः सार्द्ध दुपदस्य निवेशने॥
en: Let this our priest go back to the house of Drupada with our charioteer and cooks, and preserve our Agnihotra fires.

sn: इन्द्रसेनमुखाश्चेमे रथानादाय केवलान्। यान्तु द्वारवतीं शीघ्रमिति मे वर्तते मतिः॥
en: Let these people with Indrasena as their head repair speedily with empty cars to the city of Amaravati. This is my wish.

sn: इमाश्च नार्यो द्रौपद्याः सर्वाश्च परिचारिकाः। पाञ्चालानेव गच्छन्तु सूदपौरोगवैः सह॥
en: Let all these attending maids of Draupadi go to the Panchalas with our charioteers and cooks.

sn: सर्वैरपि च वक्तव्यं न प्राज्ञायन्त पाण्डवाः। गता ह्यस्मानपाहाय सर्वे द्वैतवनादिति॥
en: All of them also must say this "we do not know the Pandavas, they have all departed from Dvaitavana leaving us alone here."

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवं तेऽन्योन्यमामन्त्र्य कर्माण्युक्त्वा पृथक् पृथक् धौम्यमामन्त्रयामासुः स च तान् मन्त्रमब्रवीत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Thus having consulted one another and mentioned their own respective duties they asked the advice of Dhaumya and he also gave his advice.

sn: धौम्य उवाच विहितं पाण्डवाः सर्वं ब्राह्मणेषु सुहृत्सु च। याने प्रहरणे चैव तथैवाग्निषु भारत॥
en: O Pandavas, you have made arrangements in regard to the Brahmanas, friends, weapons and also in regard to the fires.

sn: त्वया रक्षा विधातव्या कृष्णायाः फाल्गुनेन च। विदितं वो यथा सर्वं लोकवृत्तमिदं तव।॥ विदिते चापि वक्तव्यं सुहृद्भिरनुरागतः। एष धर्मश्च कामश्च अर्थश्चैव सनातनः॥ अतोऽहमपि वक्ष्यामि हेतुमत्र निबोधत।
en: You and Falguna (Arjuna) are to protect। Krishna. O kings, the characters of men are properly known to you all. Inspite of your knowledge, it behoves the friends to describe them out of their regard for you and that is reckoned as the everlasting virtue, pleasure and profit. Therefore I shall say something-you should attend.

sn: हन्तेमां राजवसतिं राजपुत्रा ब्रवीम्यहम्॥ यथा राजकुलं प्राप्य सर्वान् दोषांस्तरिष्यथ। दुर्वसं चैव कौरव्य जानता राजवेश्मनि॥ अमानितैर्मानितैर्वा अज्ञातैः परिवत्सरम्। ततश्चतुर्दशे वर्षे चरिष्यथ यथासुखम्॥
en: Alas! it is woeful to stay with a king, I shall tell you. O princes, how you shall avert the calamities while residing in the royal premises. O Kauravas, whether respected or not, may you pass thus at the royal residence undiscovered by those who know you. Then in the fourteenth year you will act according to your own pleasure.

sn: दृष्टद्वारो लभेद् द्रष्टुं राजस्वेषु न विश्वसेत्। तदेवासनमन्विच्छेद् यत्र नाभिपतेत् परः॥
en: One ought to obtain previous permission should he want to appear before the king. As regards royal secrets one should not give credit when they are mentioned; one should rather court that seat where no one can defeat him.

sn: यो न यानं न पर्यत न पीठं न गजं रथम्। आरोहेत् सम्मतोऽस्मीति स राजवसतिं वसेत्॥
en: He alone can live in a royal residence who does not, with the confidence that he is a favorite, make use of the king's car, vehicle, or bedstead, or seat, or elephant or chariot.

sn: यत्र यत्रैनमासीनं शङ्करन् दुष्टचारिणः। न तत्रोपविशेद् यो वै स राजवसतिं वसेत्॥
en: He alone can live in a royal house who sits on a seat the occupation of which cannot create any suspicion in the minds of the wicked.

sn: न चानुशिष्याद् राजानमपृच्छन्तं कदाचन। तूष्णीं त्वेनमुपासीत काले समभिपूजयेत्॥ असूयन्ति हि राजानो जनाननृतवादिनः। तथैव चावमन्यन्ते मन्त्रिणं वादिनं मृषा॥
en: Unasked no one should even offer a counsel to the king; one should pay respect to never him with reticence and homage in time. Kings wish to have those who babble and hate counsellors who tell lies.

sn: नैषां दारेषु कुर्वीत मैत्री प्राज्ञः कदाचन। अन्तःपुरचरा ये च द्वेष्टि यानहिताश्च ये॥
en: A wise man should contract friendship with the wife of the king nor with the other inmates of his seraglio, nor with those whom the despises and who are hostile to him.

sn: विदिते चास्य कुर्वीत कार्याणि सुलघून्यपि। एवं विचरतो राज्ञि न क्षतिर्जायते क्वचित्॥
en: One about the king should perform the act, however greatly insignificant may be in his presence. There would be no harm to him should he behave himself towards the king in the way.

sn: गच्छन्नपि परां भूमिमपृष्टो ह्यनियोजितः। जात्यन्ध इव मन्येत मर्यादामनुचिन्तयन्॥
en: Holding even the highest office one should, until he is asked or commanded, regard himself as born-blind in consideration of the dignity of his position).

sn: न हि पुत्रं न नप्तारं न भ्रातरमरिंदमाः। समतिक्रान्तमर्यादं पूजयन्ति नराधिपाः॥
en: Because the kings show no consideration even to their sons, grandsons and brothers when they are found to disregarded their dignity.

sn: यत्नाच्चोपचरेदेनमग्निवद् देववत् त्विह। अनृतेनोपचीर्णो हि हन्यादेव न संशयः॥
en: In this world a king should be carefully served like the fire-god or any other deity; one that plays false to the king is killed by him; this admits of no doubt.

sn: यद् यद् भर्तानुयुट्टीत तत् तदेवानुवर्तयेत्। प्रमादमवलेपं च कोप च परिवर्जयते॥
en: One should follow what the master directs, and renounce carelessness, pride and anger.

sn: समर्थनासु सर्वासु हितं च प्रियमेव च। संवर्णयेत् तदेवास्य प्रियादपि हितं भवेत्॥
en: After carefully pondering over all things one should relate to the king what is both agreeable and profitable; but one must say what is beneficial in preference to what is merely agreeable.

sn: अनुकूलो भवेच्चास्य सर्वार्थेषु कथासु च। अप्रियं चाहितं यत् स्यात् तदस्मै नानुवर्णयेत्॥
en: In all matters and works one ought to be well-disposed towards the king and should never relate to him what is disagreeable and unprofitable.

sn: नाहमस्य प्रियोऽस्मीति मत्वा सेवेत पण्डितः। अप्रमत्तश्च सततं हितं कुर्यात् प्रियं च यत्॥
en: Thinking that one is not his favourite, one should serve the king, always do him what is good and pleasant without neglect.

sn: नास्यानिष्टानि सेवेत नाहितैः सह संवदेत्। स्वस्थानान्न विकम्पेत स राजवसतिं वसेत्॥
en: He alone can live in a royal house who does not swerve from his place, nor does him any injury, nor associates with those who are unfriendly to him (the king).

sn: दक्षिणं वाथ वामं वा पार्श्वमासीत् पण्डितः। रक्षिणां ह्यात्तशस्त्राणां स्थानं पश्चाद् विधीयते॥ नित्यं हि प्रतिषिद्धं तु पुरस्तादासनं महत्। न च संदर्शने किञ्चित् प्रवृत्तमपि संजयेत्॥
en: Learned men should sit either on the right or the left side of the king, because the place behind him is reverend, for the guards furnished with arms and seats in his front are always forbidden.

sn: अपि ह्येतद् दरिद्राणां व्यलीकस्थानमुत्तमम्। न मृषाभिहितं राज्ञां मनुष्येषु प्रकाशयेत्॥
en: No one should give publicity to what transpires in the very presence of the king because even for those who are very favourite it is looked upon as the height of impertinence.

sn: असूयन्ति हि राजानो नराननृतवादिनः। तथैव चावमन्यन्ते नरान् पण्डितमानिनः॥
en: One should not reveal to others any lie, that has been told by the king for he is annoyed with those who report his lies and also despise those who regard themselves as learned.

sn: शूरोऽस्मीति न दृप्तः स्याद् बुद्धिमानिति वा पुनः। प्रियमेवाचरन् राज्ञः प्रियो भवति भोगवान्॥
en: A person that does not take pride in thinking "I am heroic and intelligent," and conducts himself agreeably to the wishes of the king is worthy of royal favour and amenities of life.

sn: ऐश्वर्यं प्राप्य दुष्प्रापं प्रियं प्राप्य च राजतः। अप्रमत्तो भवेद् राज्ञः प्रियेषु च हितेषु च॥
en: A person, obtaining from the king wealth and other agreeable things hard to acquire, must employ himself assiduously in doing for him what is both pleasant and profitable.

sn: यस्य कोपो महाबाधः प्रसादश्च महाफलः। कस्तस्य मनसापीच्छेदनर्थं प्राज्ञसम्मतः॥
en: What person, that is agreeable to the wise, can even contemplate a wrong to him, whose wrath is a great trouble and whose propitiation is productive of great fruits?

sn: न चोष्ठौ न भुजौ जानू न च वाक्यं समाक्षिपेत्। सदा वातं च वाचं च ष्ठीवनं चाचरेच्छनैः॥
en: In the presence of the king no one should move his lips, anus and thighs and one should speak gently, spit slowly and break wind softly.

sn: हास्यवस्तुषु चान्यस्य वर्तमानेषु केषुचित्। नातिगाढं प्रहृष्येत न चाप्युन्मत्तवद्धसेत्॥
en: In the presence of the king if any laughable matter is mooted, a person should not enjoy it with the utmost reserve, nor should he laugh like a maniac.

sn: न चातिधैर्येण चरेद् गुरुतां हि व्रजेत् ततः। स्मितं तु मृदुपूर्वेण दर्शयेत प्रसादजम्॥ लाभे न हर्षयेद् यस्तु न व्यथेद् योऽवमानितः। असम्मूढश्च यो नित्यं स राजवसतिं वसेत्॥
en: No person should restrain himself to the reserve, for in that case he should lead him to an unnecessary gravity. But he should smile with modesty and without betraying any mistaken interest as regards real cause of the mirth. He that is always on his guard, and is neither exalted by reward nor feels wronged by disgrace, is alone worthy of residing in a royal palace.

sn: राजानं राजपुत्रं वा संवर्णयति यः सदा। अमात्यः पण्डितो भूत्वा स चिरं तिष्ठते प्रियः॥
en: The learned courtier who always describes the king and princes in suitable terms can stay long as a favorite in a royal residence.

sn: प्रगृहीतश्च योऽमात्यो निगृहीतस्त्वकारणैः। न निर्वदति राजानं लभते सम्पदं पुनः॥
en: The favored counsel or who refrains from speaking ill of the king, if ever deprived of royal grace for some causes, regains his prosperity.

sn: प्रत्यक्षं च परोक्षं च गुणवादी विचक्षणः। उपजीवी भवेद् राज्ञो विषये योऽपि वा भवेत्॥
en: The person, who earns his livelihood through the favour of the king or lives in his dominion, if prudent, must eulogize him both in his presence and behind him.

sn: अमात्यो हि बलाद् भोत्तुंक्क राजानं प्रार्थयेत यः। न स तिष्ठेच्चिरं स्थानं गच्छेच्च प्राणसंशयम्॥
en: The courtier, who desires to gain his end by using force on the king, does not hold his place long and incurs the danger of losing his life.

sn: श्रेयः दृष्ट्वा परं राज्ञा न संवदेत्। विशेषयेच्च राजानं योग्यभूमिषु सर्वदा॥
en: No person should, for the sake of his own interest, hold communion with the king's enemies, nor should one always come forward to instruct the king on all occasions, however suitable they may be.

sn: अम्लानो बलवाञ्छूरश्छायेवानुगतः सदा। सत्यवादी मृदुर्दान्तः स राजवसतिं वसेत्॥
en: He, who is cheerful mighty, brave, truthful, gentle and of subdued passions, and who always follows the king like a shadow, is alone capable of living in a royal palace.

sn: अन्यस्मिन् प्रेष्यमाणे तु पुरस्ताद् यः समुत्पतेत्। अहं किं करवाणीति स राजवसतिं वसेत्॥ सदाऽऽत्मनो
en: He who steps forward saying "pray, I will do it," when another is entrusted with a work, is alone worthy of living in a royal residence.

sn: आन्तरे चैव बाह्ये च राज्ञा यश्चाथ सर्वदा। आदिष्टो नैव कम्पेत स राजवसतिं वसेत्॥
en: He who never fears when commanded by the king to do work, wither in or out of his dominion, is alone fit for living in the royal premises.

sn: यो वै गृहेभ्यः प्रवसन् प्रियाणां नानुसंस्मरेत्। दुःखेन सुखमन्विच्छेत् स राजवसतिं वसेत्॥
en: He alone, can live in a royal palace, who, although staying away from home, never remembers his beloved ones and suffers misery in the expectation of future happiness.

sn: समवेषं न कुर्वीत नोच्चैः संनिहितो वसेत्। न मन्त्रं बहुधा कुर्यादेवं राज्ञः प्रियो भवेत्॥
en: One should not dress like the king, should not burst out into a loud laughter in the presence of the king, nor should one divulge royal counsels; behaving in this way one may become favourite of the king.

sn: न कर्मणि नियुक्तः सन् धनं किञ्चिदपि स्पृशेत्। प्राप्नोति हि हरन् द्रव्यं बन्धनं यदि वा वधम्॥
en: Appointed to a work one should not lay hands on money; if one does it he runs the risk of being imprisoned or put to death.

sn: यानं वस्त्रमलङ्कारं यच्चान्यत् सम्प्रयच्छति। तदेव धारयेन्नित्यमेवं प्रियतरो भवेत्॥
en: One should always use the cars, the robes, the ornaments and other things which the king bestows; and by doing this one should win the royal favour.

sn: एवं संयम्य चित्तानि यत्नतः पाण्डुनन्दनाः। संवत्सरमिमं तात तथाशीला बुभूषत। अथ स्वविषयं प्राप्य यथाकामं करिष्यथ॥
en: O sons of Pandu, thus controlling your minds with great efforts, spend, O children, this year, adorned with good manners. Then regaining your kingdom you may act according to your own pleasure.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच अनुशिष्टाः स्म भद्रं ते नैतद् वक्तास्ति कश्चन्। कुन्तीमृते मातरं नो विदुरं वा महामतिम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said By you we have been instructed; let good betide you. There is no one else who could say so except our mother Kunti and the highininded Vidura,

sn: यदेवानन्तरं कार्य तद् भवान् कर्तुमर्हति। तारणायास्य दुःखस्य प्रस्थानाय जयाय च॥
en: Now it behoves you to do all that is necessary for our departure, for the removal of our woes and for the achievement of victory over foe.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्तस्ततो राज्ञा धौम्योऽथ द्विजसत्तमः। अकरोद् विधिवत् सर्वं प्रस्थाने यद् विधीयते॥
en: Vaishampayana said Thus addressed by the king, Dhaumya, the best of the twice-born, arranged all that was necessary for their departure.

sn: तेषां समिध्य तानग्नीन् मन्त्रवच्च जुहाव सः। समृद्धिवृद्धिलाभाय पृथिवीविजयाय च॥
en: Lighting up fires, he offered with Mantras the oblations on them that they might gain prosperity and success and spread their conquest all over the earth.

sn: अग्नीन् प्रदक्षिणीकृत्य ब्राह्मणांश्च तपोधनान्। याज्ञसेनी पुरस्कृत्य षडेवाथ प्रवव्रजुः॥
en: Then the six, having circumbulated the fire and the Brahmanas whose only treasure is austerity, departed with Yajnseni ahead of them.

sn: गतेषु तेषु वीरेषु धौम्योऽथ जपतां वरः। अग्निहोत्राण्युपादाय पाञ्चालानभ्यगच्छत॥
en: These heroes having departed, Dhaumya, the great among ascetics, took their Agnihotra fires and started for Panchalas.

sn: इन्द्रसेनाद्रयश्चैव यथोक्ताः प्राप्य यादवान्। रथानश्वांश्च रक्षन्तः सुखमूषुः सुसंवृताः॥
en: Indrasena and others as mentioned before, after having gone to the Yadavas spent their days happily and privately in looking after the horses and cars of the Pandavas.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ते वीरा बद्धनिस्त्रिंशास्तथा बद्धकलापिनः। बद्धगोधाङ्गुलित्राणा: कालिन्दीमभितो ययुः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Those heroes equipped with swords and finger-protectors made of Iguna leather and furnished with weapons and quivers proceeded in the direction of the river Kalindi.

sn: ततस्ते दक्षिणं तीरमन्वगच्छन् पदातयः। निवृत्तवनवासा हि स्वराष्ट्र प्रेप्सवस्तदा। वसन्तो गिरिदुर्गेषु वनदुर्गेषु धन्विनः॥
en: Then they desirous of regaining their own kingdom put an end to their forest-life and walked on foot to the southern bank of the river (Kalindi).

sn: विध्यन्तो मृगजातानि महेष्वासा महाबलाः। उत्तरेण दशार्णांस्ते पञ्चालान् दक्षिणेन च॥ अन्तरेण यकृल्लोमान् शूरसेनांश्च पाण्डवाः। लुब्धा ब्रुवाणा मत्स्यस्य विषयं प्राविशन् वनात्॥ धन्विनो बद्धनिस्त्रिंशा विवर्णाः श्मश्रुधारिणः। ततो जनपदं प्राप्य कृष्णा राजानमब्रवीत्॥
en: Having put an end to their forest life, those sons of Pandu, wielders of great bows, endued with great strength, equipped with swords, wearing beards and looking wan proceeded through Yakrilloma and and Shurasena, and leaving the country of Panchalas on the south and that of Dasharna on the north, dwelling (sometimes) in hill-forts and forest fastness and killing the deer (in their journey) entered Matsya's dominions giving out themselves as hunters.

sn: पश्यैकपद्यो दृश्यन्ते क्षेत्राणि विविधानि च। व्यक्तं दूरे विराटस्य राजधानी भविष्यति। वसामेहापरां रात्रिं बलरान् मे परिश्रमः॥
en: Having arrived at the country Krishna said to the king-“Look here, there are seen many foot-paths and these indicate the existence of Virata's metropolis in the distance. Spend the remaining part of the night here for great is my fatigue."

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच धनंजय समुद्यम्य पाञ्चालीं वह भारत। राजधान्यां निवत्स्यामो विमुक्ताश्च वनादितः॥
en: Yudhishthira said 0 Dhananjaya, o Bharata, take up Panchali and carry her. As we are come out of this forest we shall settle ourselves in the capital.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तामादायार्जनुस्तूर्णं द्रौपदीं गजराडिव। सम्प्राप्य नगराभ्याशमवतारयदर्जुनः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Arjuna, like the leader of elephants, quickly took up Draupadi (Drupada's daughter) and on reaching the skirts of the forest let her down.

sn: स राजधानी सम्प्राप्य कौन्तेयोऽर्जुनमब्रवीत्। क्वायुधानि समासज्ज्य प्रवेक्ष्यामः पुरं वयम्॥
en: After having arrived at the capital the son of Kunti, asked Arjuna-where shall we keep our weapons before we enter the city?

sn: सायुधाश्च प्रवेक्ष्यामो वयं तात पुरं यदि। समुद्वेगं जनस्यास्य करिष्यामो न संशयः॥ गाण्डीवं च महद् गाढं लोके च विदितं नृणाम्। तच्चेदायुधमादाय गच्छामो नगरं वयम्। क्षिप्रमस्मान् विजानीयुर्मनुष्या नात्र संशयः॥
en: If we enter the city with our weapons we shall undoubtedly cause terror to the citizens. Moreover your gigantic bow, the Gandiva, is known to the people of the world, therefore, if we enter the city with that weapon, the people will undoubtedly cognizant us very soon.

sn: ततो द्वादश वर्षाणि प्रवेष्टव्यं वने पुनः। एकस्मिन्नपि विज्ञाते प्रतिज्ञातं हि नस्तथा॥
en: And if any one of us be discovered we hall have to enter the forest again for another twelve years, for that has truly been our promise.

sn: अर्जुन उवाच इयं कूटे मनुष्येन्द्र गहना महती शमी। भीमशास्त्रा दुरारोहा श्मशानस्य समीपतः॥
en: Arjuna said O lord of men, close by the cremation ground there stands, on the mountain peak, a large Shami tree, gigantic in size, hard to climb upon and with tremendous boughs.

sn: न चापि विद्यते कश्चन्मनुष्य इति मे मतिः। योऽस्मान् निदधतो द्रष्टा भवेच्छस्त्राणि पाण्डवाः।।१४।
en: Nor is their any human being I believe who can observe us, O Pandava, depositing our weapons.

sn: उत्पथे हि वने जाता गृगव्यालनिषेविते। समीपे च श्मशानस्य गहनस्य विशेषतः॥
en: Remote from the road there grows the tree in the forest inhabited by beasts and snakes and it stands beside a dismal cremation ground,

sn: समाधायायुधं शम्यां गच्छामो नगरं प्रति। एवमत्र यथायोगं विहरिष्याम भारत॥
en: Having thus deposited our weapons on the Shami tree we shall, O Bharata, go to the city and pass our days there in style befitting us.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्त्वा स राजानं धर्मराज युधिष्ठिरम्। प्रचक्रमे निधानाय शस्त्राणां भरतर्षभ॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having spoken thus the king Yudhishthira, the virtuous Arjuna, O best of the Bharata race, prepared for putting aside the weapons on that tree. W to

sn: येन देवान् मनुष्यांश्च सर्वांश्चैकरथोऽजयत्। स्फीताञ्जानपदांश्चान्यानजयत् कुरुपुङ्गवः॥ तदुदारं महाघोषं सम्पन्नबलसूदनम्। अपज्यमकरोत् पार्थो गाण्डीवं सुभयङ्करम्॥
en: Pritha's son, the best of the Kurus, loosened the string of the large and tremendous Gandiva, capable of producing a deeply terrific twang, of destroying the mighty hosts of enemies and by which he, on a single car, had conquered all the gods and men and many opulent countries.

sn: येन वीरः करुक्षेत्रमभ्यरक्षत् परंतपः। अमुञ्चद् धनुषस्तस्य ज्यामक्षय्यां युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: The warlike Yudhishthira, the chastiser of enemies, loosened the undecaying string of bow with which he had protected the field of the Kurus (Kurukshetra).

sn: पाञ्चालान् येन संग्रामे भीमसेनोऽजयत् प्रभुः। प्रत्यषेधद् बहूनेकः सपत्नांश्चैव दिग्जये॥ निशम्य यस्य विस्फारं व्यद्रवन्त रणात् परे। पर्वतस्येव दीर्णस्य विस्फोटमशनेरिव॥ सैन्धवं येन राजानं पर्यामृषितवानथ। ज्यापाशं धनुषस्तस्य भीमसेनोऽवतारयत्॥
en: The mighty Bhimasena unfastened the string of the bow with which the sinless one had conquered the Panchalas in fight, defeated the lord of Sindhu, opposed many of his foes alone at the time of spreading his conquest in all directions and hearing whose twang like the splitting of a mountain, or like the roar of the thunder, the enemies had fled from the field.

sn: अजयत् पश्चिमामाशां धनुषा येन पाण्डवः। माद्रीपुत्रो महाबाहुस्ताम्रास्यो मितभाषिता॥ तस्य मौर्वीमपाकर्षच्छूरः संक्रन्दनो युधि। कुले नास्ति समो रूपे यस्येति नकुलः स्मृतः।।२५।
en: The heroic son of Pandu by Madri, having large arms, copper complexion, frugal speech and immense prowess in the field of battle, known by the name Nakula by virtue of his matchless beauty in the family, took away the string of his bow with which he had conquered all the regions of the west.

sn: दक्षिणां दक्षिणाचारो दिशं येनाजयत् प्रभुः। अपज्यमकरोद् वीरः सहदेवस्तदायुधम्॥
en: The heroic Sahadeva of noble conduct rendered his bow stringless with which he made conquests in the southern regions.

sn: खगांश्च दीप्तान् दीर्घाश्च कलापांश्च महाधनान्। विपाठान् क्षुरधारांश्च धनुर्भिनिदधुः सह॥
