en: Along with their bows they deposited their long and shining swords, quivers of great value, and arrows with edges as sharp as those of razors.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच अथान्वशासन्नकुलं कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः। आरुह्येमां शमी वीर धनूंष्येतानि निक्षिप॥
en: Vaishampayana said: Then Yudhishthira, the son of Kunti, commanded Nakula-"O heroic one ascend this Shami tree and deposit those bows thereon.”

sn: तामुपारुह्य नकुलो धनूंषि निदधे स्वयम्। यानि तस्यावकाशानि दिव्यरूपाण्यमन्यत॥ यत्र चापश्यत स वै तिरोवर्षाणि वर्षति। तत्र तानि दृढैः पाशैः सुगाढं पर्यबन्धत॥
en: Having ascended the Shami tree Nakula himself placed these bows. He tied them with strong ropes with those parts of the tree which he thought to be well-formed and where the rain in an oblique lines.

sn: शरीरं च मृतस्यैकं समबनन्त पाण्डवाः। विवर्जयिष्यन्ति नरा दूरादेव शमीमिमाम्॥
en: There also the Pandavas fastened a corpse so that the people getting the bad smell and saying-"there is a corpse fastened, will shun this Shami from a distance."

sn: आबद्धं शवमत्रेति गन्धमाघ्राय पूतिकम्। अशीतिशतवर्षेयं माता न इति वादिनः॥ कुलधर्मोऽयमस्माकं पूर्वैराजरितोऽपि वा। समासज्ज्याथ वृक्षेऽस्मिन्निति वै व्याहरन्ति ते॥
en: After having finished the fastening they gave out-"This is our mother, one hundred and eight years old. This is our ancestral custom, observed by our forefathers."

sn: आगोयालाविपालेभ्य आचक्षाणाः परंतपाः। आजग्मुर्नगराभ्याशं पार्थाः शत्रुनिबर्हणाः॥
en: Having said this to the cow-herds and shipherds Pritha's sons, the subduers of enemies, approached the capital.

sn: जयो जयन्तो विजयो जयत्सेनो जयद्बलः। इति गुह्यानि नामानि चक्रे तेषां युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: (In order to live incognito) Yudhishthira selected for himself and his brothers these false names-Jaya, Jayanta, Vijaya, Jayatsena and Jayadbala.

sn: ततो यथाप्रतिज्ञाभिः प्राविशान् नगरं महत्। अज्ञातचर्यां वत्स्यन्तो राष्ट्र वर्षं त्रयोदशम्॥
en: For the purpose of passing the thirteenth year undiscovered in that kingdom they entered the great city in conformity to their promise (to Duryodhana).

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच विराटनगरं रम्यं गच्छमानो युधिष्ठिरः। अस्तुवन्मनसा देवी दुर्गा त्रिभुवनेश्वरीम्॥ यशोदागर्भसम्भूतां नारायणवरप्रियाम्। नन्दगोपकुले जातां मङ्गल्यां कुलवर्धिनीम्॥ कंसविद्रावणकरीमसुराणां क्षयंकरीम्। शिलातटविनिक्षिप्तामाकाशं प्रति गामिनीम्॥ वासुदेवस्य भगिनी दिव्यमाल्यविभूषिताम्। दिव्याम्बरधरां देवी खड्गखेटकधारिणीम्॥ भारावतरणे पुण्ये ये स्मरन्ति सदाशिवाम्। तान् वै तारयसे पापात् पङ्के गामिव दुर्बलाम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said While Yudhishthira was about to enter the beautiful city of Virata, he mentally hymned the divine Durga, the goddess of the three worlds, born of the womb of Yashoda, very dear to Narayana, born in the family of Nandagopa, bestower of prosperity capable of enhancing a family, the terror of Kansa, slayer of Asuras, the goddess who ascended the welkin when dashed on a stone slate. Vasudeva's sister, adorned with celestial garlands, attired in celestial apparel and holding sword and scimitar capable of rescuing worshippers, like a cow in the mire, who for the purpose of getting themselves released of the burden, invoke the aid of that giver of eternal blessing.

sn: स्तोतुं प्रचक्रमे भूयो विविधैः स्तोत्रसम्भवैः। आमन्त्र्य दर्शनाकाक्षी राजा देवीं सहानुजः॥
en: The king, with his brothers, desirous of obtaining a sight of the goddess, invoked her and began to sing praises by various hymns.

sn: नमोऽस्तु वरदे कृष्णे कुमारि ब्रह्मचारिणि। बालार्कसदृशाकारे पूर्णचन्द्रनिभानने।॥
en: I salute you, O bestower of boons, O you that are the same as Krishna, O maiden ( your Chaya, O your that have a form bright as the newly risen sun, and a face as beautiful as the full moon itself.

sn: चतुर्भुजे चतुर्वक्त्रे पीनश्रोणिपयोधरे। मयूरपिच्छवलये केयूराङ्गदधारिणि।
en: I salute you, O you of four hands and four faces, O you that have large hips and a very high-boom, O you that wears bangles and bears arınlets.

sn: भासि देवि यथा पद्मा नारायणपरिग्रहः॥ स्वरूपं ब्रह्मचर्यं च विशदं गगनेश्वरी। कृष्णच्छविसमा कृष्णा संकर्षणसमानना॥
en: O goddess you appear like Padma the consort of Narayana, O you ranger in the sky, your Brahmacharya and the real forms are both without a spot.

sn: बिभ्रती विपुलौ बाहू शक्रध्वजसमुच्छ्यौ। पात्री च परूजी घण्टी स्त्रीविशुद्धा च या भुवि॥ पाशं धनुर्महाचक्रं विविधान्यायुधानि च। कुण्डलाभ्यां सुपूर्णाभ्यां कर्णाभ्यां च विभूषिता॥ चन्द्रविस्पर्द्धिना देवि मुखेन त्वं विराजसे। मुकुटने विचित्रेण केशबन्धेन शोभिना॥
en: O goddess, you appear with a countenance that vies with the moon, vith a pair of well shaped ears decorated with excellent rings, having a pair of large arms like Indra's pole; you are the only female in the world endowed with the attributes of piety, purity-you are the one holding a vessel a lotus, a bell, a noose, a bow and a large discus and various other weapons.

sn: भुजङ्गाभोगवासेन श्रोणिसूत्रेण राजता। विभ्राजसे चाबद्धेन भोगेनेवेह मन्दरः॥ ध्वजेन शिखिपिच्छानामुच्छ्रितेन विराजसे।
en: With a beautiful crown and graceful tresses, with dresses made of the hoods of serpents and an ornament fascinating your hip, you appear to be like the mount Mandara girded with serpents; also you shine with peacock-plumes standing high on your crest.

sn: कौमारं व्रतमास्थाय त्रिदिवं पावितं त्वया।॥ तेन त्वं स्तूयसे देवि त्रिदशैः पूज्यसेऽपि च।
en: Having accepted the vow of maiden hood you have sanctified the heaven; therefore, O goddess, you are praised and adorned by the gods.

sn: त्रैलोक्यरक्षणार्थाय महिषासुरनाशिनि। प्रसन्ना मे सुरश्रेष्ठे दयां कुरु शिवा भव॥
en: For the protection of the three worlds, you have slain the demon Mahisha (buffalo); O foremost of deities, be propitious to me; give me your grace and be the cause of my wellbeing.

sn: जया त्वं विजया चैव संग्रामे च जयप्रदा। ममापि विजयं देहि वरदा त्वं च साम्प्रतम्॥
en: You are Jaya and Vijaya and capable of giving victory in battle, as you are also capable of granting boons, now be pleased to grant me victory.

sn: विन्ध्ये चैव नगरश्रेष्ठे तव स्थानं हि शाश्वतम्। कालि कालि महाकालि खड्गखट्वाङ्गधारिणि॥
en: O Kali, Kali, O Mahakali, fond of wine, meat and animal-sacrifice your eternal abode is on the Vindhya, the chief of the mountains

sn: कृतानुयात्रा भूतैस्त्वं वरदा कामचारिणि। भारावतारे ये च त्वां संस्मरिष्यन्ति मानवाः॥ प्रणमन्ति च ये त्वां हि प्रभाते तु नरा भुवि। न तेषां दुर्लभं किंचित् पुत्रतो धनतोऽपि वा।॥ दुर्गात् तारयसे दुर्गे तत् त्वं दुर्गा स्मृता जनैः।
en: O giver of boon, capable of ranging every where at will, you are followed by celestials beings (in your journey). Persons who, for the purpose of shaking off their burdens, bow down to, or call upon, you in the morning on earth, attain all either in respect of children or riches. O Durga, as you rescue people from danger, you are called by them Durga.

sn: कान्तारेष्ववसन्नानां मग्नानां च महार्णवे॥ दस्युभिर्वा निरुद्धानां त्वं गतिः परमा नृणाम्।
en: You are the greatest refuge of people who are groping in the wilderness, getting drowned in the great ocean, and are taken captives by high-way-men.

sn: जलप्रतरणे चैव कान्तारेष्वटवीषु च॥ ये स्मरन्ति महादेवि न च सीदन्ति ते नराः।
en: 0 great goddess, the persons who remember you in the crossing of waters and in the forest and wilderness are never afflicted with calamity.

sn: त्वं कीर्तिः श्रीतिः सिद्धिीविद्या संततिर्मतिः॥ संध्या रात्रिः प्रभा निद्रा ज्योत्स्ना कान्तिः क्षमा दया।
en: O great fame, and prosperity, you are fortitude and success, you are modesty and knowledge, you are offspring and intellect, you are evening and night, you are light and sleep, you are lunar beam and beauty, and you are forgiveness and mercy.

sn: नृणां च बन्धनं मोहं पुत्रनाशं धनक्षयम्॥ व्याधिं मृत्यु भयं चैव पूजिता नाशयिष्यसि।
en: When worshipped, you remove men's fetters ignorance, loss of sons, loss of wealth and disease, death and dread.

sn: सोऽहं राज्यात् परिभ्रष्टः शरणं त्वां प्रपन्नवान्॥ प्रणतश्च यथा मूर्धा तव देवि सुरेश्वरि।
en: I have been deprived of my kingdom and seek your refuge. O supreme goddess, I make obeisance to you with bended head.

sn: त्राहि मां पद्मपत्राक्षि सत्ये सत्या भवस्व नः॥ शरणं भव मे दुर्गे शरण्ये भक्तवत्सले।
en: O possessor of eyes like the petals of lotuses, be truth to us who are seeking after truth. O Durga, O refuge of all, O affectionate to devotees, be pleased to grant me protection.

sn: एवं स्तुता हि सा देवी दर्शयामास पाण्डवम्॥ उपगम्य तु राजानमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्।
en: Thus praised the goddess showed herself to the Pandavas and having addressed him thus said.

sn: देव्युवाच शृणु राजन् महाबाहो मदीयं वचनं प्रभो॥ भविष्यत्यचिरादेव संग्रामे विजयस्तव।
en: O Lord endowed with massive arms, listen to my words; shortly you shall get victory in battle.

sn: मम प्रसादानिर्जित्य हत्वा कौरवाहिनीम्॥ राज्यं निष्कण्टकं कृत्वा भोक्ष्यसे मेदिनीं पुनः।
en: Having defeated and slaughtered the Kaurava forces through my benediction and rendered the kingdom destitute of thorns you shall enjoy the earth again.

sn: भ्रातृभिः सहितो राजन् प्रीतिं प्राप्स्यसि पुष्कलाम्।। मत्प्रसादाच्च ते सौख्यमारोग्यं च भविष्यति।
en: O king, you shall with your brothers again enjoy an abundance through my grace, health and happiness.

sn: ये च संकीर्तयिष्यन्ति लोके विगतकल्मषाः॥ तेषां तुष्टा प्रदास्यामि राज्यमायुर्वपुः सुतम्।
en: I propitiated, will confer, kingdom longevity, goodly form and offspring on those stainless persons who will chant my attributes aloud to the world,

sn: प्रवासे नगरे चापि संग्रामे शत्रुसंकटे॥ अटव्यां दुर्गकान्तारे सागरे गहने गिरौ। ये स्मरिष्यन्ति मां राजन् यथाहं भवता स्मृता॥ न तेषां दुर्लभं किंचिदस्मिस्मल्लोके भविष्यति।
en: To persons who will remember me, as you have done, in exile, in the town in battle, in danger by foes, in forest, in unapproachable deserts, in seas or in mountains, there will be nothing unattainable in this world.

sn: इदं स्तोत्रवरं भक्त्या शृणुयाद् वा पठेत वा॥ तस्य सर्वाणि कार्याणि सिद्धिं यास्यन्ति पाण्डवाः।
en: O sons of Pandu, he who will listen to, or recite with faith this excellent hymn, shall attain success in all his undertakings.

sn: मत्प्रसादाच्च वः सर्वान् विराटनगरे स्थितान्॥ न प्रज्ञास्यन्ति कुरवो नरा वा तन्निवासिनः।
en: Through my grace neither the Kurus nor the people inhabiting the city of Virata, will be able to recognize you all during your stay in that city.

sn: इत्युक्त्वा वरदा देवी युधिष्ठिरमरिंदमम्। रक्षां कृत्वा च पाण्डूनां तत्रैवान्तरधीयत॥
en: Having said this to Yudhishthira the repressor of foes and bestowed protection on the sons of Pandu the Goddess disappeared.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततो विराटं प्रथमं युधिष्ठिरो राजा सभायामुपविष्टमाव्रजत्। नक्षान् स कक्षे परिगृह्य वाससा॥ नराधिपो राष्ट्रपति यशस्विनं महायशाः कौरववंशवर्धनः। महानुभावो नरराजसत्कृतो दुरासदस्तीक्ष्णविषो यथोरगः॥ नपूर्वरूपेण यथामरस्तथा। र्यथानलो भस्मवृतश्च वीर्यवान्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Then having tied up in his cloth dice made of gold set with sapphires and placed them under his arm-pit, the king Yudhishthira, the lord of men, of great glory, founder of the Kuru family, of great soul, respected by kings, hard to be approached like a serpent of virulent venom. The best of men, great in might and beauty, resembling a deity in form, appearing like the sun enveloped with thick clouds, and like the mighty fire covered with ashes, first presented himself before the illustrious king Virata while he was seated in the court.

sn: तमापतन्तं प्रसमीक्ष्य पाण्डवं विराटराडिन्दुमिवाभ्रसंवृतम्। समागतं पूर्णशशिप्रभाननं महानुभावं न चिरेण दृष्टवान्॥
en: The king Virata first saw the Pandava coming like the moon covered with clouds and then in a moment found him arrived at the court, with a countenance like the full moon and possessed of a great splendour.

sn: मन्त्रिद्विजान् सूतमुखान् विशस्तथा ये चापि केचित् परितः समासते। पप्रच्छ कोऽयं प्रथम समेयिवान् नृपोपमोऽयं समवेक्षते सभाम्॥
en: The king Virata asked his counsellors, the Brahmanas, the charioteers, the Vaishyas and all others who took their seats about him, "who might be the man that has come first, and just like a king appears in my court.

sn: न तु द्विजोऽयं भविता नरोत्तमः पतिः पृथिव्या इति मे मनोगतम्। न चास्य दासो न रथो न कुढारः समीपतो भ्राजति चायमिन्द्रवत्॥
en: This best of men can not be a Brahmin; me-thinks he is a lord of earth, though he has neither a slave, nor a car, nor an elephant with him, yet he shines just like Indra.

sn: शरीरलिङ्गैरूपसूचितो ह्ययं मूर्द्धाभिषिक्त इति मे मनोगतम्। समीपमायाति च मे गतव्यथो यथा गजस्तामरसी मदोत्कटः॥
en: By the marks on his person it is indicated that he is no other than one whose head has gone through the ceremony of coronal baths, and that is my belief. He approaches me as fearless as an elephant in a ruttish frenzy approaches a lotus.”

sn: वितर्कयन्तं तु नरर्षभस्तथा युधिष्ठिरोऽभ्येत्य विराटमब्रवीत्। सम्राड्विजानात्विह जीवनार्थिनं विनष्टसर्वस्वमुपागतं द्विजम्॥
en: Yudhishthira, the best of men, having come near the king Virata while he was thus indulging in thoughts, addressed him saying "O great king, know me to be a Brahmin, who having lost all, have come to you, solicitous for his livelihood.

sn: इहाहमिच्छामि तवानघान्तिके वस्तुं यथा कामचरस्तथा विभो। तमब्रवीत् स्वागतमित्यनन्तरं राजा प्रहृष्टः प्रतिसंगृहाण च॥
en: O sinless one, I wish to reside with you just like one obeying the voice of his master 0 Lord!" After having accorded him a due welcome the king well pleased said “accept the post you seek for."

sn: तं राजसिंहं प्रतिगृह्य राजा प्रीत्याऽऽत्मना चैनमिदं बभाषे। कामेन ताताभिवदाम्यहं त्वां कस्यासि राज्ञो विषयादिहागतः॥ गोत्रं च नामापि च शंस तत्त्वतः। किं चापि शिल्पं तव विद्यते कृतम्॥
en: Having appointed him the best of kings, O king, glad at heart addressed him saying “O worshipful one I bow down to you" from the dominions of what king you are come here? Please tell me truly what your name is and what family you belong to and whether you have knowledge of any art.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच युधिष्ठिरस्यासमहं पुरा सखा वैयाघ्रपद्यः पुनरस्मि विप्रः। अक्षान् प्रयोक्तुं कुशलोऽस्मि देविनां कङ्केति नाम्नास्मि विराट विश्रुतः॥
en: Yudhishthira said I was formerly a friend of Yudhishthira, I am a Brahmin belonging to the family named Vaiayghara, I am expert in casting dice. O Virata, I am known by the name of Kanka.

sn: विराट उवाच ददामि ते हन्त वरं यमिच्छसि प्रशाधि मत्स्यान् वशगो ह्यहं तव। प्रियाश्च धूर्ता मम देविनः सदा भवांश्च देवोपम राज्यमर्हति॥
en: Virata said I grant you the boon which you may desire. Rule over the Matsyas. Know me to be your obedient. Even the cunning gamblers are always beloved of me, you, like a king, deserve a kingdom.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच प्राप्तो विवादः प्रथमं विशाम्पते न विद्यते कं च न मत्स्य हीनतः। न मे जितः कश्चन धारयेद् धनं वरो ममैषोऽस्तु तव प्रसादजः॥
en: Yudhishthira said O Matsya, O lord of people, I shall never pick a quarrel, from the play at dice, with low people, nor shall any person be defeated by me. Let this boon be granted to me through your grace.

sn: विराट उवाच हन्यामवश्यं यदि तेऽप्रियं चरेत् प्रव्राजयेयं विषयाद् द्विजांस्तथा। शृण्वन्तु में जानपदा: समागताः कङ्को यथाहं विषये प्रभुस्तथा॥
en: Virata said Surely shall I kill him who may do wrong to you. Should he be a Brahmin I shall banish him from my kingdom. Let my assembled subjects hear, Kanka, is as much lord of this my dominion as I myself.

sn: समानयानो भवितासि मे सखा प्रभूतवस्त्रो बहुपानभोजनः। पश्येस्त्वमन्तश्च बहिश्च सर्वदा कृतं च ते द्वारमपावृतं मया॥
en: You (Kanka) shall be my friend, your vehicle shall be the same as mine, you shall have plenty of clothes and sundry sorts of drinks and dishes. You shall look into both ins and outs of my affair, I shall always keep my doors open for you.

sn: ये त्वानुवादेऽयुरवृत्तिकर्शिता ब्रूयाश्च तेषां वचनेन मां सदा। दास्यामि सर्वं तदहं न संशयो न ते भयं विद्यति संनिधौ मम॥
en: When the people pressed by the want of employment, will apply to you, you shall at all hours tell me all their words. I shall undoubtedly give them all that they will ask for, before iny presence there will be no fear to you.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवं स लब्वा तु वरं समागम विराटराजेन नरर्षभस्तदा। उवास धीरः परमार्चितः सुखी न चापि कश्चिच्चरितं बुबोध तत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having thus obtained the boon from the king Virata he too the best of men began to live there happily, highly respected by all. Nor could any one discover him.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच त्रुपाययौ सिंहविलासविक्रमः। नसिं च कालाङ्गमकोशमव्रणम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Then there came another of dreadful strength and of shining beauty, with a gait as pleasant as that of a lion; holding in hand a cooking laddle and a spoon and an unsheathed sword of azure body and without a spot on the blade.

sn: स सूदरूपः परमेण वर्चसा रविर्यथा लोकमिमं प्रकाशयन्। स्तं मत्स्यराजं समुपेत्य तस्थिवान्॥
en: Although in the guise of a cook he endued with the strength of the lord of mountains, and attired in dark garments, reached the king of the Matsya's and stood before him illuming, with his great splendour, all around him like the sun revealing the world.

sn: तं प्रेक्ष्य राजा रमयन्नुपागतं ततोऽब्रवीज्जानपदान् समागतान्। सिंहोन्नतांसोऽयमतीव रूपवान् प्रदृश्यते को नु नरर्षभो युवा॥
en: Beholding hiin like a king present before him Virata asked the people assembled there "who is this young man seen, the best of men, exceedingly beautiful, and having shoulders as high as those of a lion.

sn: अदृष्टपूर्वः पुरुषो रविर्यथा वितर्कयन् नास्य लभामि निश्चयम्। तथास्य चित्तं ह्यपि संवितर्कयन् नरर्षभस्यास्य न यामि तत्त्वतः॥
en: This man, not seen before, is like one seen; thinking and thinking over I cannot come to a definite conclusion (who he may be); nor do I, with a serious deliberation, understand the intention of that best of men.

sn: दृष्ट्वैव चैनं तु विचारयाम्यह गन्धर्वराजो यदि वा पुरंदरः। जानीत कोऽयं मम दर्शने स्थितो यदीप्सितं तल्लभतां च मा चिरम्॥
en: Beholding him I do not deem it worth while to discuss whether he is the king of the Gandharvas or Purandara himself; ascertain who it is standing before my eyes, let him have in no time what he desires.

sn: विराटवाक्येन च तेन चोदिता नरा विराटस्य सुशीघ्रगामिनः। उपेत्य कौन्तेयमथाब्रुवंस्तदा यथा स राजावदताच्युतानुजम्॥
en: Thus commissioned by the words of Virata, his quick-paced messengers went to the son of Kunti and told that younger brother of Yudhishthira all that the king had said.

sn: स्त्वदीनरूपं वचनं महामनाः। उवाच सूदोऽस्मि नरेन्द्र बल्लवो भजस्व मां व्यढानकारमुत्तमम्॥
en: Then the high-souled son of Pandu approaching the king Virata spoke in words not poorly on the occasion "O king, I am a cook named Ballava; appoint me, pray, an expert in culinary arts."

sn: विराट उवाच न सूदतां बल्लव श्रद्दधामि ते सहस्रनेत्रप्रतिमो विराजसे। श्रिया च रूपेण च विक्रमेण च प्रभाससे त्वं नृवरो नरेष्विव॥
en: Virata said I do not believe that cooking is your business, you shine like a thousand-eyed deity amongst men; you seem to be the best in grace, beauty and prowess.

sn: भीम उवाच नरेन्द्र परिचारकोऽस्मि ते जानामि सूपान् प्रथमं च केवलान्। आस्वादिता ये नृपते पुराभवन् युधिष्ठिरेणापि नृपेण सर्वशः॥ सूदः
en: Bhima said O king, I am your cook and servant; it is not so that I have only the knowledge of curries, although O king, they were always tasted, in days gone by, by the king Yudhishthira.

sn: बलेन तुल्यश्च न विद्यते मया नियुद्धशीलश्च सदैव पार्थिवा गजैश्च सिंहैश्च समेयिवानहं सदा करिष्यामि तवानघ प्रियम्॥
en: O ruler of the earth, I am also a wrestler, there is no equal to me in strength. O sinless one, I shall always entertain you by fighting with elephants and lions.

sn: विराट उवाच ददामि ते हन्त वरान् महानसे तथा च कुर्याः कुशलं प्रभाषसे। न चैव मन्ये तव कर्म यत् समं समुद्रनेमि पृथिवीं त्वमर्हसि॥
en: Virata said I grant you the boons; you will take possession of the kitchen in which you say you are skilled. I do not think this office is worthy of you. You deserve the whole earth having seas for its walls, (girt by the seas).

sn: तथा हि कामो भवतस्तथा कृतं महानसे त्वं भव मे पुरस्कृतः। नराश्च ये तत्र समाहिताः पुरा भवांश्च तेषामधिपो मया कृतः॥
en: I have done what you desire, you are appointed in my kitchen. I place you at the head of those who have been appointed there before by me.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तथा स भीमो विहितो महानसे विराटराज्ञो दयितोऽभवद् दृढम्। उवास राज्ये न च तं पृथग् जनो बुबोध तत्रानुचराश्च केचन॥
en: Thus appointed in the kitchen Bhima became a great favorite of the king Virata. O king, he began to live there, but neither the servants of Virata nor other people recognized him.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततः केशान् समुत्क्षिप्य वेल्लिताग्राननिन्दितान्। कृष्णान्सूक्ष्मान्मृदुन्दीर्घान् समुद्ग्रथ्य शुचिस्मिता॥ जुगूहे दक्षिणे पार्श्वे मृदूनसितलोचना।
en: Vaishampayana said Then Draupadi, of pleasant smile and of dark eyes, bending her black; glossy, soft, long and fine tresses of crispy ends into a twisted braid, threw it on her right side and kept it concealed (under her cloth).

sn: वासश्च परिधायैकं कृष्णा सुमलिनं महत्॥ कृत्वा वेषं च सैरन्ध्रयास्ततो व्यचरदार्तवत्। तां नराः परिघावन्ती स्त्रियश्च समुपाद्रवन्॥
en: Having put on a very big dirty piece of cloth and dressed herself as a Sairandhri, Krishna began to ramble hither and thither like one in a miserable plight. All males and females came running to her wandering about.

sn: अपृच्छंश्चैव तां दृष्ट्वा का त्वं किं च चिकीर्षसि। सा तानुवाच राजेन्द्र सैरर्थ्यहमिहागता॥ कर्म चेच्छामि वै कर्तुं तस्य यो मां युयुक्षति।
en: Beholding her they asked "who are you and what you want to do”? O king, she said to them "I am a Sairandhri; here have I come to do his work who will maintain me."

sn: तस्या रूपेण वेषेण श्लक्ष्णया च तथा गिरा। न श्रद्दधत तां दासीमन्नहेतोरूपस्थिताम्॥
en: The people, seeing her beauty and dress, hearing her voice so sweet, could not believe her to be in a position of a maid servant come in quest of livelihood.

sn: विराटस्य तु कैकेयी भार्या परमसम्मता। आलोकयन्ती ददृशे प्रासादाद् द्रुपदात्मजाम्॥
en: While going abroad from the root of the palace Virata's beloved wife, the daughter of Kaikeyi, beheld the daughter of Drupada.

sn: सा समीक्ष्य तथारूपमनाथामेकवाससम्। समाहूयाब्रवीद् भद्रे का त्वं किं च चिकीर्षसि॥
en: Beholding her thus plighted, unprotected and clad in a single piece of cloth, she (Virata's wife) addressed her saying “O gentle one, who are you and what you desire to do.”

sn: सा तामुवाच राजेन्द्र सैरन्ध्यहमुपागता। कर्म चेच्छाम्यहं कर्तुं तस्य यो मां युयुक्षति॥
en: O king, she said to her “I am a Sairandhri, I desire to do his work who will maintain me.'

sn: सुदेष्णोवाच नैवंरूपा भवन्त्येव यथा वदसि भामिनि। प्रेषयन्तीव वै दासीर्दासांश्च विविधान् बहून्॥
en: Sudeshna said It cannot be so as you say, O beautiful one, (but on the contrary) it seems you can appoint numerous servants both male and female.

sn: नोच्चगुल्फा संहतोरुस्त्रिगम्भीरा षडुन्नता। रक्ता पञ्चसु रक्तेषु हंसगद्गदभाषिणी॥
en: You are such a one as your heels are not high, thighs touch each other, deep are your intelligence, voice and navel, highly developed are your soles, palms, tongue, upper and neither lips and your voice is as sweet as that of a swan.

sn: सुकेशी सुस्तनी श्यामा पीनश्रोणिपयोधरा। तेन तेनैव सम्पन्ना काश्मीरीव तुरङ्गमी॥
en: You are one of beautiful tresses, good breasts and possessed of high graces; and plump are your buttock and breasts. Being furnished with all these beautiful signs, you appear like a Kashmirean woman.

sn: अरालपक्ष्मनयना बिम्बोष्ठी तनुमध्यमा। कम्बुग्रीवा गूढशिरा पूर्णचन्द्रनिभानना॥
en: You are one with eyes having its line of hairs gracefully bent, lips scarlet as Bimba, waist slender, neck having the lines like those on the conch, veins scarcely visible and countenance like the full moon.

sn: शारदोत्पलपत्राक्ष्या शारदोत्पलगन्धया। शारदोत्पलसेविन्या रूपेण सदृशी श्रिया॥
en: In beauty you are Sri (goddess of beauty) herself with eyes resembling the petals of the autumnal lotus, with a person fragrant as the autumnal lotus chief, and seated on the autumnal lotus.

sn: का त्वं ब्रूहि यथा भद्रे नासि दासी कथंचना यक्षी वा यदि वा देवी गन्धर्वी यदि वाप्सराः॥ देवकन्या भुजङ्गी वा नगरस्याथ देवता। विद्याधरी किन्नरी वा यदि वा रोहिणी स्वयम्॥ अलम्बुषा मिश्रकेशी पुण्डरीकाथ मालिनी। इन्द्राणि वारुणी वा त्वं त्वष्टुर्धातुः प्रजापतेः। देव्यो देवेषु विख्यातास्तासां त्वं कतमा शुभे॥
en: O gentle one, tell me who you are; you cannot be a maid-servant; are you a Yakshi or a goddess, a Gandharvi or an Apsara (nymph)? are you the daughter of a celestials or female Naga? is a presiding deity of the city? Are you a Vidyadhari or a Kinnari or Rohini herself? Are you Alambusha or Mishrakeshi Pundarika or Malini or the queen of Indra or Varuna, or are you the wife of Vishvakarma or of the Prajapati himself? These goddesses are renowned in the regions of celestials; of these who are you, O beautiful one?

sn: द्रौपद्युवाच नास्मि देवी न गन्धर्वी नासुरी न च राक्षसी। सैरन्ध्री तु भुजिष्यास्मि सत्यमेतद् ब्रवीमि ते॥
en: or Draupadi said I am neither a goddess nor a Gandharvi nor an Asuri nor a Rakshasi; I am a maid-servant of the Sairandhiri class; I tell you this truth.

sn: केशाञ्जानाम्यहं कर्तुं पिंधे साधु विलेपनम्। मल्लिकोत्पलपद्मानां चम्पकानां तथा शुभे॥ ग्रथयिष्ये विचित्राश्च स्रजः परमशोभनाः। आराधयं सत्यभामां कृष्णस्य महिषीं प्रियाम्॥ कृष्णां च भार्यां पाण्डूनां कुरूणामेकसुन्दरीम्। तत्र तत्र चराम्येवं लभमाना सुभोजनम्॥ वासांसि यावन्ति लभे तावत् तावद् रमे तथा।
en: I know how to dress the hair, pound (fragrant staff) to make unguents. O auspicious lady, I know also how to make beautiful and variegated garlands of Jasamines, lotuses, lilies and Champakas. Formerly served Satyabhama, the beloved queen of Krishna, and also Krishna the wife of the Pandavas, and the only beauty of the Kuru race. I serve in those places where I may get good food and clothes; as long as I get them I continue to serve.

sn: मालिनीत्येव मे नाम स्वयं देवी चकार सा। साहमद्यागता देवि सुदेष्णे त्वन्निवेशनम्॥
en: Draupadi herself called me by name Malini, O lady Sudeshna, I, her serving maid, have come to your house today.

sn: सुदेष्णोवाच मूर्ध्नि त्वां वासयेयं वै संशयो मे न विद्यते। न चेदिच्छति राजा त्वां गच्छेत् सर्वेण चेतसा॥
en: Sudeshna said I can place you on my head, and there is no doubt in that, provided that the king does not desire you and be not captivated with his whole heart.

sn: स्त्रियो राजकुले याश्च याश्चेमा मम वेश्मनि। प्रसक्तास्त्वां निरीक्षन्ते पुमांसं कं न मोहयेः॥
en: Charmed by your beauty even the females of the royal house hold and as well as those in my own seraglio are gazing at you. What male person is there whom you will not captivate?

sn: वृक्षांश्चावस्थितान् पश्य य इमे मम वेश्मनि। तेऽपि त्वां संनमन्तीव पुमांसं कं न मोहयेः॥
en: Look again, even the very trees that stand in my palace seem to bend low as if by way of paying homage to you, what male person is there that will not be attracted by you?

sn: राजा विराटः सुश्रोणि दृष्ट्वा वपुरमानुषम्। विहाय मां वरारोहे गच्छेत् सर्वेण चेतसा॥
en: O you of well-shaped hips; o you girl of surpassing beauty, beholding your superhuman form, king Virata, will surely forsake me and will turn to you with his whole heart.

sn: यं हि त्वमनवद्याङ्गि तरलायतलोचने। प्रसक्तमभिवीक्षेथाः स कामवशगो भवेत्॥
en: O you of expanded eyes, of nimble glances, the person, on whom you endued with faultless limbs, will cast a look with desire, will surely fall a victim to the God of Love.

sn: यश्च त्वां सततं पश्येत् पुरुषश्चारुहासिनि। एवं सर्वानवद्याङ्गि स चानङ्गवशो भवेत्॥
en: 0 you of sweet smiles, O you of perfectly faultless form, the man who will behold you often and often will surely be subject to that formless deity.

sn: अध्यारोहेद् यथा वृक्षान् वधायैवात्मनो नरः। राजवेश्मनि ते सुभ्रु गृहे तु स्यात् तथा मम॥
en: As a person climbs up a tree for his own destruction, so, O you of graceful eyebrows, your stay in this royal house-hold will bring out the same result to me.

sn: यथा च कर्कटी गर्भमाधत्ते मृत्युमात्मनः :1 तथाविधमहं मन्ये वासं तव शुचिस्मिते॥
en: As a crab conceives for her own death so. O you of pleasant smiles, my desire for your stay here will surely be ruinous to me.

sn: द्रौपद्युवाच नास्मि लभ्या विराटेन न चान्येन कदाचन। गन्धर्वाः पतयो मह्यं युवानः पञ्च भामिनि॥
en: Draupadi said Neither by Virata nor by any other man I am to be won, O fair lady, for I have five youthful husbands who are all Gandharvas.

sn: पुत्रा गन्धर्वराजस्य महासत्त्वस्य कस्यचित्। रक्षन्ति ते च मां नित्यं दुःखाचारा तथा ह्यहम्॥
en: They are the sons of certain Gandharva king of extra-ordinary strength; they always protect me. Also my mode of living is very hard.

sn: यो मे न दद्यादृच्छिष्टं न च पादौ प्रधावयेत्। प्रीणेरंस्तेन वासेन गन्धर्वाः पतयो मम॥
en: My Gandharva husbands wish me to serve only such person as will not give me to eat food already partaken of by another or ask me to wash their feet.

sn: यो हि मां पुरुषो गृद्ध्येद् यथान्याः प्राकृताः स्त्रियः। तामेव निवसेद् रात्रिं प्रविश्य च परां तनुम्॥
en: The person who will desire me like any other woman, will surely encounter destruction that very night.

sn: न चाप्यहं चालयितुं शक्या केनचिदङ्गने। दुःखशीला हि गन्धर्वास्ते च मे बलिनः प्रियाः॥
en: O lady of sweet smiles, no one is able to decay me from the paths of rectitude; those beloved Gandharvas of exceeding prowess always protect me secretly.

sn: सुदेष्णोवाच प्रच्छन्नाश्चापि रक्षन्ति ते मां नित्यं शुचिस्मिते। एवं त्वां वासयिष्यामि यथा त्वं नन्दिनीच्छसि॥ न च पादौ न चोच्छिष्टं स्प्रक्ष्यसि त्वं कथंचन।
en: Sudeshna said O charming one, it being so, I will allow you a residence in my palace) according to your desire. You will never have to touch food partaken of by another nor even to wash another's feet.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवं कृष्णा विराटस्य भार्यया परिसान्त्विता॥ उवास नगरे तस्मिन् पतिधर्मवती सती। न चैनां वेद तत्रान्यस्तत्त्वेन जनमेजय॥
en: Vaishampayana said Thus assured by the wife of Virata the chaste Krishna, devoted to her lords, began to live in that city. O Janamejaya, no one of that place could know who she really was.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच सहदेवोऽपि गोपानां कृत्वा वेषमनुत्तमम्। भाषां चैषां समास्थाय विराटमुपयादथ॥
en: Vaishampayana said Wearing an excellent dress of a cowherd and learning the dialect of the same, Saladeva also arrived at the city of the king Virata.

sn: गोष्टमासाद्य तिष्ठन्तं भवनस्य समीपतः। राजाथ दृष्ट्वा पुरुषान् प्राहिणोज्जातविस्मयः॥
en: Then the king, seeing him standing in the cow pasture in the vicinity of the royal palace, became amazed and sent for him.

sn: तमायान्तमभिप्रेक्ष्य भ्राजमानं नरर्षभम्। समुपस्थाय वै राजा पप्रच्छ कुरुनन्दनम्॥
en: The king, seeing that best of men shining in splendour, coming, asked the son of Kuru.

sn: कस्य वा त्वं कुतो वा त्वं किंवा त्वं तु चिकीर्षसि। न हि मे दृष्टपूर्वस्त्वं तत्त्वं ब्रूहि नरर्षभ॥
en: To whom do you belong? Whence are you come and what do you seek? You were not seen by me before, tell me in sooth all about you, O best of men.

sn: सम्प्राप्य राजानममित्रतापनं ततोऽब्रवीन्मेघमहौघनिःस्वनः। गोसंख्य आसं कुरुपुङ्गवानाम्॥
en: Having come to the king, the repressor of foes Sahadeva said with a voice deep as the roar of the clouds, "I am a Vaishya known by the name Arishtanemi, I served as an enumerator of the cows of those best of the Kuru race.

sn: वस्तुं त्वयीच्छामि विशां वरिष्ठ तान् राजसिंहान् न हि वेद्मि पार्थान्। न शक्यते जीवितुमप्यकर्मणा न च त्वदन्यो मम रोचते नृपः॥
en: O foremost of men, I do no know where the sons, of Pritha the foremost among men, are; I want to live with you. I can not keep myself without service. I do not like to serve any other king except you.

sn: विराट उवाच त्वं ब्राह्मणो यदि वा क्षत्रियोऽसि समुद्रनेमीश्वररूपवानसि। आचक्ष्व मे तत्त्वममित्रकर्शन न वैश्यकर्म त्वयि विद्यते क्षमम्॥
en: Virata said You must either be a Brahmana or a Kshatriya, you are as graceful as the lord of the entire earth girt by the sea. Tell me truly, O afflicter of enemies, the offlice of a Vaishya does not become you.

sn: कस्यासि राज्ञो विषयादिहागतः किं वापि शिल्पं तव विद्यते कृतम्। कथं त्वमस्मासु निवत्स्यसे सदा वदस्व किं चापि तवेह वेतनम्॥
en: Tell me from the dominion, of what king you are come here, what knowledge of art you are versed with, in what capacity you will remain with us and what your pay will be.

sn: सहदेव उवाच पञ्चानां पाण्डुपुत्राणां ज्येष्ठो भ्राता युधिष्ठिरः। तस्याष्टशतसाहस्रा गवां वर्गाः शतं शतम्॥ अपरे शतसाहस्रा विस्तावन्तस्तथा परे। तेषां गोसंख्य आसं वै तन्तिपालेति मां विदुः॥
en: Sahadeva said Of the five sons of Pandu Yudhishthira is the eldest. He had one division of kine the number where of amounts to eight hundred and ten thousand and another ten thousand, and another twenty thousand and so forth. I was employed as an enumerator of cows under them; people used to call me Tantipala.

sn: भूतं भव्यं भविष्यं च यच्च संख्यागतं गवाम्। न मेऽस्त्यविदितं किंचित् समन्ताद् दशयोजनम्॥
en: Nothing is unknown to me about the cows that live within ten Yojanas and whose tale has been taken in reference to their present past and future.

sn: गुणाः सुविदिता ह्यासन् मम तस्य महात्मनः। असकृत् स मया तुष्टः कुरुराजो युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: My merits were known to that high-souled one, and the Kuru king Yudhishthira was pleased with me.

sn: क्षिप्रं च गावो बहुला भवन्ति न तासु रोगो भवतीह कश्चना देतानि शिल्पानि मयि स्थितानि॥
en: I am perfectly aware of the arts by means of which the kine may increase in number within a short time and no disease may come upon them.

sn: ऋषभाँश्चापि जानामि राजन् पूजितलक्षणान्। येषां मूत्रमुपाघ्राय अपि वन्ध्या प्रसूयते॥
en: O king, I also know the bulls having marks for which they are adored by people and by smelling whose urine even the barren may be fruitful.

sn: विराट उवाच शतं सहस्राणि समाहितानि सवर्णवर्णस्य विमिश्रितान् गुणैः। पशून् सपालान् भवते ददाम्यहं त्वदाश्रया मे पशवो भवन्त्विह॥
en: Virata said I have a hundred thousand kine of various classes the merits of which have not yet been brought to light. I give you the charge of these beasts with their keepers. Let my beasts be henceforth in your keep.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच रुवास तत्रैव सुखं नरोत्तमः। न चैनमन्येऽपि विदुः कथंचन प्रादाच्च तस्मै भरणं यथेप्सितम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said The best of men began to live there happily without being recognized by the king, the lord of men, nor did any one else know him; the king also allowed him a stipend as much as he desired. A

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच अथापरोऽदृश्यत रूपसम्पदा स्त्रीमाणलङ्कारधरो बृहत्पुमान्। प्राकारवप्रे प्रतिमुच्य कुण्डले दीर्घ च कम्बूपरि हाटके शुभे॥
en: Vaishampayana said Then there was seen at the gate of the ramparts another person of colossal form, rich in the wealth of beauty, adorned with the ornaments of woman, and putting on large earrings and fine conch bracelets set with gold.

sn: बाहू च दीर्घान् प्रविकीर्य मूर्धजान् महाभुजो वारणतुल्यविक्रमः। गतेन भूमि प्रतिकम्पयंस्तदा विराटमासाद्य सभासमीपतः॥
en: That long armed one, having the gait like that of an elephant, with long and abundant tissues hanging about, came to Virata shaking the earth with his tread and stood in his court.

sn: तं प्रेक्ष्य राजोपगतं सभातले व्याजात् प्रतिच्छन्नमरिप्रमाथिनम्। विराजमानं परमेण वर्चसा सुतं महेन्द्रस्य गजेन्द्र विक्रमम्॥ सर्वानपृच्छच्च सभानुचारिणः कुतोऽयमायाति पुरा न मे श्रुतः। न चैनमूचुर्विदितं तदा नराः सविस्मयं वाक्यमिदं नृपोऽब्रवीत्॥
en: Beholding him, the son of the great Indra, resembling an elephant in gait, him capable of crushing foes, having his real form hidden in disguise, entering the court chamber and stepping forward to the king, he (Virata) asked all his courtiers "whence does this man come; I have never heard of him before.” The people thereof said of the person as one unknown to them. Thereupon the king said wonderingly.

sn: सत्त्वोपपन्नः पुरुषोऽमरोपमः श्यामो युवा वारणयूथपोपमः। आमुच्य कम्बूपरि हाटके शुभे विमुच्य वेणीमपिना कुण्डले॥ स्रग्वी सुकेशः परिधाय चान्यथा शुशोभ धन्वी कवची शरीयथा। आरुह्य यानं परिधावतां भवान् सुतैः समो मे भव वा मया समः॥
en: Endowed with might you appear like a celestials; you are are young and of dark complexion and resemble the leader of a herd of elephants. Although you have worn fine conch-bracelets beset with gold ear-rings and loosened your braid, yet you shine as one decked with garlands and fine hairs and equipped with bow, bow, mail and arrows; ascending the car you wander at your pleasure. Be you like my son or like myself.

sn: वृद्धो ह्यहं वै परिहारकामः सर्वान् मत्स्यांस्तरसा पालयस्व। नैवंविधाः क्लीपरूपा भवन्ति कथंचनेति प्रतिभाति मे मनः॥
en: I am decrepit, and desirous of cast-off my burden. Rule you cheerfully the whole of the Matsya territory, I cannot believe that such persons may even be of the neuter sex.”

sn: अर्जुन उवाच गायामि नृत्याम्यथ वादयामि भद्रोऽस्मि नृत्ये कुशलोऽस्मि गीते। त्वमुत्तरायै प्रदिशस्व मां स्वयं भवामि देव्या नरदेव नर्तकः॥
en: Arjuna said I sing, dance and play on instruments. I am skilled in dancing and expert in singing. O god among men, assign me to Uttara. I shall be the dancing-master to the princess.

sn: इदं तु रूपं मम येन किं तव प्रकीर्तयित्वा भृशशोकवर्धनम्। बृहन्नलां मां नरदेव विद्धि सुतं सुतां वा पितृमातृवर्जिताम्॥
en: It will be of no avail to describe how I have come by this form. It will merely augment my pain, O lord of men; know me to be Brihannala, a son or daughter without parents.

sn: विराट उवाच ददामि ते हन्त वरं बृहन्नले सुतां च मे नर्तय याश्च तादृशीः। इदं तु ते कर्म समं न मे मतं समुद्रनेमि पृथिवीं त्वमर्हसि॥
en: Virata said O Brihannala, I grant you the boon you seek for; instruct my daughter and those like her in dancing; me-seems this office is not worthy of you, you deserve the whole earth surrounded by seas.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच बृहन्नलां तामभिवीक्ष्य मत्स्यराट कलासु नृत्येषु तथैव वादिते। सम्मन्त्र्य राजा विविधैः स्वमन्त्रिभिः परीक्ष्य चैनं प्रमदाभिराशु वै॥ अपुस्त्वमप्यस्य निशम्य च स्थिरं ततः कुमारीपुरमुत्ससर्ज तम्। स शिक्षयामास च गीतवादितं सुतां विराटस्य धनंजयः प्रभुः॥ सखींश्च तस्याः परिचारिकास्तथा प्रियश्च तासां स बभूव पाण्डवः॥
en: Vaishampayana said The king of the Matsya's, having tested Brihannala in dancing, in playing on instruments also in other fine arts, sent him to the quarters of the maidens, after consulting with his different ministers having him examined by women and being assured of his impotency of a permanent type. There the mighty Dhananjaya began to teach singing and playing on instruments to the daughter of Virata, and her friends and serving maids. The Pandava soon became their favorite.

sn: तथा स सत्रेण धनंजयो वसन् प्रियाणि कुर्वन् सह ताभिरात्मवान्। तथा च तं तत्र न जज्ञिरे जना बहिश्चरा वाप्यथ चान्तरेचराः॥
en: There the self-subdued Dhananjaya began to live in disguise behaving amiably with them. The people within or without the palace could not recognize him.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच विराटराजं तरसा समेयिवान्। तमापतन्तं ददृशे पृथग्जनो विमुक्तमभ्रादिव सूर्यमण्डलम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Then there was seen another mighty son of Pandu approaching king Virata in haste; the common people thereof saw him coming like solar orb freed from the clouds.

sn: स वै हयानैक्षत तांस्ततस्ततः समीक्षमाणं स ददर्श मत्स्यराट्। ततोऽब्रवीत् ताननुगान् नरेश्वरः कुतोऽयमायाति नरोऽमरोपमः॥
en: He began to observe the horses around; the king of the Matsya's, the lord of people, seeing him observing his horses minutely asked his followers "whence is this man lustrous like a celestials, coming"?

sn: स्वयं हयानीक्षति मामकान् दृढं ध्रुवं हयज्ञो भविता विचक्षणः। प्रवेश्यतामेष समीपामाशु मे विभाति वीरो हि यथामरस्तथा॥
en: This person looks closely at my horses. Must he be proficient in horse-lore. Let him quickly enter into my presence. This heroic one seems to me as much as a celestials.

sn: ज्जयोऽस्तु ते पार्थिव भद्रमस्तु वः। हयेषु युक्तो नृप सम्मतः सदा तराश्वसूतो निपुणो भवाम्यहम्॥
en: That slaughterer of enemies, having approached the king addressed him thus "O king, let victory be to you and good betide you all. I am always esteemed by kings for my ability as a horse-painter. I will be an expert keeper of your horses.

sn: विराट उवाच ददामि यानानि धनं निवेशनं ममाश्वसूतो भवितुं त्वमर्हसि। कुतोऽसि कस्यासि कथं त्वमागतः प्रब्रूहि शिल्पं तव विद्यते च यत्॥
en: Virata said I give you vehicles, wealth and quarters; you deserve to be the keeper of my horses. But tell me whence you are come, whose you are, and how you came here, also tell me of the arts you are versed with.

sn: नकुल उवाच पञ्चानां पाण्डुपुत्राणां ज्येष्ठो भ्राता युधिष्ठिरः। तेनाहमश्वेषु पुरा नियुक्तः शत्रुकर्शन॥
en: Nakula said O repressor of foes, of the five sons of Pandu, Yudhishthira is the eldest brother, by him I was formerly employed as a keeper of his horses.

sn: अश्वानां प्रकृति वेद्मि विनयं चापि सर्वशः। दुष्टानां प्रतिपत्तिं च कृत्स्नं चैव चिकित्सितम्॥
en: I know the temper of horses, and the art of breaking them completely. I know how to correct the wicked steeds and the treatment of all kinds.

sn: न कातरं स्यान्मम जातु वाहनं न मेऽस्ति दुष्टा वडवा कुतो हयाः। जनस्तु मामाह स चापि पाण्डवो युधिष्ठिरो ग्रन्थिकमेव नामतः॥
en: Under my care hardly does any animal fall ill. What to speak of horses even mares in my hands are not to be found wicked. People called me by name, Granthika so also Yudhishthira the son of Pandu.

sn: विराट उवाच यदस्ति किंचिन्मम वाजिवाहनं तदस्तु सर्वं त्वदधीनमद्य वै। स्त्वदाश्रयाः सारथयश्च सन्तु मे॥
en: Virata said Let all my horses that belong to me be entrusted to your care from today. Let all my charioteers and those to yoke my horses, be henceforth subordinate to you.

sn: इदं तवेष्टं यदि वै सुरोपम ब्रवीहि यत् ते प्रसमीक्षितं वसु। न तेऽनुरूपं हयकर्म विद्यते प्रभासि राजेव हि सम्मतो मम॥
en: If this be your desire, O god-like one, tell me what remuneration is sought by you. This office of horse-training does not become you, because you look like a king and you are agreeable to me.

sn: युधिष्ठिरस्येव हि दर्शनेन मे समं तवेदं प्रियमत्र दर्शनम्। कथं तु भृत्यैः स विनाकृतो वने वसत्यनिन्द्यो रमते च पाण्डवः॥
en: Here, the very sight of you is as much pleasing to me as that of Yudhishthira himself. Oh how does that faultless son of Pandu, dwell and divert himself in the forest without his servants.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तथा स गन्धर्ववरोपमो युवा विराटराज्ञा मुदितेन पूजितः। न चैनमन्येऽपि विदुः कथंचन प्रियाभिरामं विचरन्तमन्तरा॥
en: Vaishampayana said That youthful one resembling the chief of the Gandharvas was thus honoured by the delighted king of Virata, and no one recognized him conducting himself agreeably in the city.

sn: एवं हि मत्स्ये न्यवसन्त पाण्डवा यथाप्रतिज्ञाभिरमोघदर्शनाः। अज्ञातचर्यां व्यचरन् समाहिताः समुद्रनेमीपतयोऽतिदुःखिताः॥
en: Thus the son of Pandu, whose very sight never proved abortive, began to live in the kingdom of Matsya; and in conformity with their pledge, the lords of the earth surrounded by seas although stricken with woe began to pass their days of non-discovery with composure.

sn: जनमेजय उवाच । एवं ते मत्स्यनगरे प्रच्छन्नाः कुरुनन्दनाः। अत ऊर्ध्वं महावीर्याः किमकुर्वत वै द्विजः॥
en: Janamejaya said O twice-born one, living thus disguised in the city of the Matsyas what did the Kuru's sons of exceeding might do.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवं मत्स्यस्य नगरे प्रच्छन्नाः कुरुनन्दनाः। आराधयन्तो राजानं यदकुर्वत तच्छृणु॥
en: Vaishampayana said Hear, what the descendants of Kuru did living thus disguised in the city of the Matsyas and serving the king thereof.

sn: तृणबिन्दुप्रसादाच्च धर्मस्य च महात्मनः। अज्ञातवासमेवं तु विराटनगरेऽवसन्॥
en: By the grace of the ascetic Trinabindu and of the high-souled Dharma they began to live incognito in the city of Virata.

sn: युधिष्ठिरः सभास्तारो मत्स्यानामभवत् प्रियः। तथैव च विराटस्य सपुत्रस्य विशाम्पते॥
en: Yudhishthira as a courtier made himself a favorite to Virata and his son, as well as to all the Matsyas, O lord of people.

sn: स ह्यक्षहृदयज्ञस्तान् क्रीडयामास पाण्डवः। अक्षवत्यां यथाकामं सूत्रबद्धानिव द्विजान्॥
en: Well versed in the mysteries of the dice he caused him to play at dice in the dice-hall in accordance with his pleasure like the birds bound by the string.

sn: अज्ञातं च विराटस्य विजित्य वसु धर्मराट्। भ्रातृभ्यः पुरुषव्याघ्रो यथार्ह सम्प्रयच्छति॥
en: That best of men, the king of justice (Yudhishthira) having won the wealth of Virata duly distributed it without the knowledge of the monarch among his brothers.

sn: भीमसेनोऽपि मांसानि भक्ष्याणि विविधानि च। अतिसृष्टानि मत्स्येन विक्रीणीते युधिष्ठिरे॥
en: Bhimsena also sold to Yudhishthira, the meat and the viands of various sorts which were given by the king of the Matsyas.

sn: वासांसि परिजीर्णानि लब्धान्यन्तःपुरेऽर्जुनः। विक्रीणानस्च सर्वेभ्यः पाण्डवेभ्यः प्रयच्छति॥
en: Arjuna parted with the worn out clothes by sale, which he obtained from women's quarters, to the other sons of Pandu.

sn: सहदेवोऽपि गोपानां वेषमास्थाय पाण्डवः। दधि क्षीरं घृतं चैव पाण्डवेभ्यः प्रयच्छति॥
en: Sahadeva also, who had assumed the dress of a cow-herd, distributed to them curds, milk and clarified butter.

sn: नकुलोऽपि धनं लब्ध्वा कृते कर्मणि वाजिनाम्। तुष्टे तस्मिन् नरपतौ पाण्डवेभ्यः प्रयच्छति॥
en: Nakula also gave the wealth to his brothers which he acquired from the king who was satisfied with him for his tending the horses.

sn: कृष्णा तु सर्वान् भर्तृस्तान् निरीक्षन्ती तपस्विनी। यथा पुनरविज्ञाता तथा चरति भामिनी॥
en: In the form of ascetic and very charmful draupadi served their husband, so nobody can identify their reality.

sn: एवं सम्पादयन्तस्ते तदान्योन्यं महारथाः। विराटनगरे चेरुः पुनर्गर्भधृता इव॥
en: They, the mighty warriors, then looking after the interest of one another, lived in the city of Virata in such a manner, as if they were once more in the house of their mother.

sn: साशङ्का धार्तराष्ट्रस्य भयात् पाण्डुसुतास्तदा। प्रेक्षमाणास्तदा कृष्णामूषुश्छन्ना नराधिप॥
en: Then the sons of Pandu, the lords of men, appending evil from the sons of Dhritarashtra, continued to live there in disguise keeping vigilant eyes upon their wife Krishna.

sn: अथ मासे चतुर्थे तु ब्रह्मणः सुमहोत्सवः। आसीत् समृद्धो मत्स्येषु पुरुषाणां सुसम्मतः॥
en: Then in the fourth month there happened a great festival, in honor of the divine Brahma, slender in form and highly valued by people, in the city of the Matsya's.

sn: तत्र मल्लाः समापेतुर्दिग्भ्यो राजन् सहस्रशः। समाजे ब्रह्मणो राजन् यथा पशुपतेरिव॥
en: 0 king, there came, by thousands, wrestlers from all quarters in that field of festivity in honour of the divine Brahma, as also on the occasion of a festival held in honor of Shiva.

sn: महाकाया महावीर्याः कालखजा इवासुराः। वीर्योन्मत्ता बलोदग्रा राज्ञा समभिपूजिताः॥
en: They were of colossal forms and of exceeding might, like the demons named Kalakhanjas; they were maddened with their latent power; furious with their prowess and highly honored by the king.

sn: सिंहस्कन्धकटिग्रीवाः स्वावदाता मनस्विनः। असकृल्लब्धलक्षास्ते रङ्गे पार्थिवसंनिधौ॥
en: Their shoulders, waists and necks were like those of lions, their bodies were free from dirt, and their hearts were large. Many times before they achieved success in the lists in the very august presence of the king.

sn: तेषामेको महानासीत् सर्वमल्लानथाह्वयत्। आवल्गमानं तं रङ्गे नोपतिष्ठति कश्चन॥
en: Amongst them there was one who was the greatest of all and challenged all other combatants to a wrestle; there was none that ventured to encounter him as he strided over in the arena.

sn: यदा सर्वे विमनसस्ते मल्ला हतचेतसः। अथ सूदेन तं मल्लं योधयामास मत्स्यराट्।॥
en: When all the wrestlers stood stupefied and dejected in spirit then the king of the Matsyas made him fight with his cook.

sn: नोद्यमानस्तदा भीमो दुःखेनैवाकरोन्मतिम्। न हि शक्नोति विवृते प्रत्याख्यातुं नराधिपम्॥
en: Impelled by the king, Bhima made up his mind with reluctance, for it was not in his power to openly disobey the royal mandate.

sn: ततः स पुरुषव्याघ्रः शार्दूलशिथिलश्चरन्। प्रविवेश महारङ्गं विराटमभिपूजयन्॥
en: Then that the best of men, having worshipped the king Virata, entered the spacious arena with listless steps like those of a lion.

sn: बबन्ध कक्षां कौन्तेयस्ततः संहर्षयञ्जनम्। ततस्तु वृत्रसंकाशं भीमो मल्लं समाह्वयत्॥
en: Then Bhima, the son of Kunti, girded up his lions and caused the delight of the spectators. There he summoned the wrestler of distinguished prowess named Jimuta resembling Vritra himself. were

sn: जीमूतं नाम तं तत्र मल्लं प्रख्यातविक्रमम्। तावुभौ सुमहोत्साहावुभौ भीमपराक्रमौ॥ मत्ताविव महाकायौ वारणौ षष्टिहायनौ। ततस्तौ नरशार्दूलो बाहुयुद्धं समीयतुः॥
en: Both of them were of exceeding energy and of terrible prowess, and they both were like a couple of infuriated elephants of gigantic form each being sixty years old. Then those two best of men became engaged in hand-tohand fight.

sn: वीरौ परमसंहृष्टावन्योन्यजयकाक्षिणौ। आसीत् सुभीमः सम्पातो वज्रपर्वतयोरिव॥
en: Those two heroic combatants exceedingly cheerful, each being desirous of gaining victory over the other; exceedingly terrible was the encounter between them, just like the clash of the thunderbolt against the mountain.

sn: उभौ परमसंहृष्टौ बलेनातिबलावुभौ। अन्योन्यस्यान्तरं प्रेप्सू परस्परजयैषिणौ॥
en: Both of them were exceedingly powerful and were highly pleased with each other's strength; each of them was desirous of winning the victory over the other and was vigilant to take advantage of his rival's lapse.

sn: उभौ परमसंहष्टौ मत्ताविव महागजौ। कृतप्रतिकृतैश्चित्रैर्बाहुभिश्च सुसरूटैः।
en: Both of them were exceedingly delighted and resembled a couple of infuriated elephants of huge forms; and various were the manners of their attack and defence shown by means of their clenched fists.

sn: संनिपातावधूतैश्च प्रमौथोन्मथनैस्तथा॥ क्षेपणैर्मुष्टिभिश्चैव वराहोद्भूतनि:स्वनैः।
en: They fought in a manner that each dashed against the other, threw his rival far off his stand, each crushed the other down, and pressed him hard on the ground, each showing the other off exchanged blows, and each whirled the other round with his head downward and threw him away with a loud noise.

sn: तलैर्वज्रनिपातैश्च प्रसृष्टाभिस्तथैव च॥ शलाकानसखपातैश्च पादोद्भूतैश्च दारुणैः।
en: With their palms each gave a good slap to the other, striking as hard as the thunder bolt and with outstretched fingers they slapped each other. They thrust spear like nails into each other's person; each gave violent kicks to the other.

sn: जानुभिश्चाश्मनिर्घोषैः शिरोभिश्चावघदनैः॥ तद् युद्धमभवद् घोरमशस्त्रं बाहुतेजसा।
en: They struck knee against knee, dashed head against head, producing the crash of one stone against another. That was the furious combat without weapons, sustained chiefly by the might of their arms.

sn: बलप्राणेन शूराणां समाजोत्सवसंनिधौ॥ अरज्यत जन: सर्वः सोत्क्रुष्टनिनदोत्थितः।
en: By both physical and mental energy of the two heroic combatants, as represented in the presence of people assembled in the arena on the occasion of the festivity, all the spectators were extremely delighted, and their delight was manifested by joyous shouts given out at intervals.

sn: बलिनोः संयुगे राजन् वृत्रवासवयोरिव॥ प्रकर्षणाकर्षणयोरभ्याकर्षविकर्षणैः। आकर्षतुरधान्योन्यं जानुभिश्चापि जघतुः॥ महता भर्त्सयन्तौ परस्परम्।
en: O king, in the wrestling of the two mighty persons, resembling Vitra and Vasava respectively, they pulled, pressed, whirled and hurried down each other and struck each other with their knees and expressed their hatred for each other in loud voices.

sn: व्यूढोरस्कौ दीर्घभुजौ नियुद्धकुशलावुभौ। बाहुभिः समसज्जेतामायसैः परिधैरिव॥
en: Then they both of expansive chest, and long arms, and expert in wrestling began to fight with their arms resembling huge bolts of iron.

sn: चकर्ष दोर्ध्यामुत्पात्य भीमो मल्लममित्रहा। निनदन्तमभिक्रोशन् शार्दूल इव वारणम्॥ ततः शब्देन
en: Bhima, the slayer of enemies, seized, with a big seized, his vociferous rival wrestler by the arms and drew him near even as the lion seizes the elephant.

sn: समुद्यम्य महाबाहूर्धामयामास वीर्यवान्। ततो मल्लाच मत्स्याश्चं विस्मयं चक्रिरे परम्॥
en: Then the mighty-armed Bhima of great prowess raised him up and began to whirl him round; then all the athlete and the people of the Matsya's, who had assembled on the occasion, were greatly astonished.

sn: भ्रामयित्वा शतगुणं गतसत्त्वमचेतनम्। प्रत्यपिंषन्महाबाहुर्मल्लं भुवि वृकोदरः॥
en: Then having whirled him round and round a hundred times, the mighty armed Vrikodara inade him utterly insensible and threw him down lifeless on the ground.

sn: तस्मिन् विनिहते वीरे जीमूते लोकविश्रूते। विराटः परमं हर्षमगच्छद् बान्धवैः सह॥
en: That distinguished athlete Jimuta being slain, Virata and his friends were exceedingly delighted.

sn: प्रहर्षात् प्रददौ वित्तं बहु राजा महामनाः। बल्लवाय महारङ्गे यथा वैश्रवणस्तथा॥
en: In his great joy the high-minded king gave away to Ballava plenty of riches in the shape of a reward on the very field of combat with as much liberality as that of Kubera.

sn: एवं स सुबहून् मल्लान् पुरुषांश्च महाबलान्। विनिघ्नन् मत्स्यराजस्य प्रीतिमाहरदुत्तमाम्॥
en: Having thus slain numerous athletes and many other persons of great strength he received the great favour of the king of the Matsya's.

sn: यदास्य तुल्यः पुरुषो न कश्चित् तत्र विद्यते। ततो व्याप्रैश्च सिंहैश्च द्विरदैश्चाप्ययोधयत्॥
en: When there was found no one such as to stand equal to him the king made him fight with tigers and lions and elephants.

sn: पुनरन्तःपुरगतः स्त्राणां मध्ये वृकोदरः। योध्यते स विराटेन सिंहैर्मत्तैर्महाबलैः॥
en: Again the king made Vrikodara fight with furious lions of exceeding strength in the assembly of the ladies of the harem.

sn: बीभत्सुरपि गीतेन स्वनृत्येन च पाण्डवः। विराटं तोषयामास सर्वाश्चान्तःपुरस्त्रियः॥
en: Bibhatsu, the son of Pandu, pleased Virata and all the ladies of the harem by singing and dancing.

sn: अश्वैर्विनीतैर्जवनस्तत्र तत्र समागतः। तोषयामास राजानं नकुलो नृपसत्तमम्॥ तस्मै प्रदेयं प्रायच्छत् प्रीतो राजा धनं बहु।
en: Nakula pleased the king, the best of kings by showing him the fast-going and well-trained horses and the king, pleased gave him a plenty of money as a reward.

sn: विनीतान् वृषभान् दृष्ट्वा सहदेवस्य चाभितः। धनं ददौ बहुविधं विराटः पुरुषर्षभः॥
en: Beholding a herd of well-trained bullocks around Sahadeva, Virata the best of men, gave him wealth of various kinds.

sn: द्रौपदी प्रेक्ष्य तान् सर्वान् क्लिश्यमानान् महारथान्। नातिप्रीतमना राजन् निःश्वासपरमाभवत्॥
en: O king, beholding all these mighty warriors suffer pain, Draupadi felt herself dejected in mind and had recourse to constant sighs.

sn: एवं ते न्यवसंस्तत्र प्रच्छन्नाः पुरुषर्षभाः। कर्माणि तस्य कुर्वाणा विराटनृपतेस्तदा॥
en: Those best among men began to live there in disguise rendering services to the king Virata.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच वसमानेषु पार्थेषु मत्स्यस्य नगरे तदा। महारतेषु छन्नेषु मासा दश समाययुः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Those mighty warriors, the sons of Pritha, spent ten months living thus in disguise in Matsya's city.

sn: याज्ञसेनी सुदेष्णां तु श्रुश्रूषन्ती विशाम्पते। आवसत् परिचारार्हा सुदुःखं जनमेजय॥
en: O lord of people, Yajnaseni, although herself worthy of being served by others, began to live, O Janamejaya, in great misery by waiting upon Sudeshna.

sn: तथा चरन्ती पाञ्चाली सुदेष्णाया निवेशने। तां देवीं तोषयामास तथा चान्त:पुरस्त्रियः॥
en: Conducting herself in this way in Sudeshna's apartments the daughter of Panchala pleased that lady as well as the other women of the harem.

sn: तस्मिन् वर्षे गतप्राये कीचकस्तु महाबलः। सेनापतिविराटस्य ददर्श दुपदात्मजाम्॥
en: That year being nearly expired the mighty Kichaka the commander of Virata's forces happened to see the daughter of Drupada.

sn: तां दृष्ट्वा देवगर्भाभां चरन्ती देवतामिव। कीचकः कामयामास कामबाणप्रपीडितः॥
en: Beholding her having effulgence like that of a divine girl and waiting on the earth like a goddess, Kichaka, struck hard with the shafts of Cupid, desired to obtain her.

sn: स तु कामाग्निसंतप्तः सुदेष्णामभिगम्य वै। प्रहसन्निव सेनानीरिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Burning with the flame of lust, the leader of Virata's forces went to Sudeshna (his sister) and smilingly spoke to her in the following words.

sn: नेयं मया जातु पुरेह दृष्टा राज्ञो विराटस्य निवेशने शुभा। रूपेण चोन्मादयतीव मां भृश गन्धेन जाता मदिरेव भामिनी॥
en: This damsel was never seen by me before in Virata palace. This beautiful lady maddenis me very much with her beauty as wine does with its odour.

sn: का देवरूपा हृदयङ्गमा शुभे ह्याचक्ष्व मे कस्य कुतोऽत्र शोभने। चित्तं हि निर्मध्य करोति मां वशे न चान्यदत्रौषधमस्ति मे मतम्॥
en: Tell me, O lady, who is this be-witching girl of fine beauty, endued with the grace of a goddess and whose she is and where she comes from. She has brought me to subjection by grinding my heart. I think there is no other medicine to heal me (except her).

sn: अहो तवेयं परिचारिका शुभा प्रत्यग्ररूपा प्रतिभाति मामियम्। अयुक्तरूपं हि करोति कर्म ते प्रशास्तु मां यच्च ममास्ति किंचन॥
en: This fine and maid of yours appears to me as one possessed of the blooming beauty of a goddess. The service which she renders to you is quite unsuitable to her.

sn: प्रभूतनागाश्वरथं महाजनं समृद्धियुक्तं बहुपानभोजनम्। मनोहरं काञ्चचित्रभूषणं गृहं महच्छोभयतामियं मम॥
en: Let her grace my splendid and beautiful residence adorned with various ornaments of gold, furnished with viands and drinks in plenty, decked with excellent plates and containing everything signifying prosperity, besides elephants and cars in lots.

sn: स्ततः समभ्येत्य नराधिपात्मजाम्। उवाच कृष्णामभिसान्त्वयंस्तदा मृगेन्द्रकन्यामिव जम्बुको वने॥
en: Having thus consulted Sudeshna Kichaka approached the daughter of the king (Draupadi) and addressed her in words of amity just as a jackal accosts a lioness in the forest.

sn: का त्वं कस्यासि कल्याणि कुतो वा त्वं वरानने। प्राप्ता विराटनगरं तत् त्वमाचक्ष्व शोभने।॥
en: Who and whose are you, O graceful one? Whence are you come to this city of Virata, O you of beautiful countenance. Tell me truly, O fair one.

sn: रूपमङ्गयं तथा कान्तिः सौकुमार्यमनुत्तमम्। कान्त्या विभाति वक्त्रं ते शशाङ्क इव निर्मलम्।।१३।
en: Your beauty is rankled as the foremost of its order, so also is your gracefulness. Excellent is your tenderness; in respect of loveliness your countenance shines as clearly as the moon.

sn: नेत्रे सुविपुले सुभ्र पद्मपत्रनिभे शुभे। वाक्यं ते चारुसर्वाङ्गि परपुष्टरुतोपमम्॥
en: O one of lovely eye-brows, your eyes are large resembling the petals of lotuses. O you of graceful limbs, your voice is like the notes of the cuckoo.

sn: एवंरूपा मया नारी काचिदन्या महीतले। न दृष्टपूर्वा सुश्रोणि यादृशी त्वमनिन्दिते॥
en: O you of fair hips, never before have I beheld in the world a woman endued with such beauty as you are, O blameless one.

sn: लक्ष्मी: पद्मालया का त्वमथ भूतिः सुमध्यमे। ह्रीः श्रीः कीर्तिरथो कान्तिरासां का त्वं वरानने।।१६।
en: Are you Lakshmi herself having lotuses for abode, or O slender-waisted one, are you Bhuti herself? Which of these-Hri, Sri, Kiriti and Kanti, are you the impersonation, O you of excellent features?

sn: अतीवरूपिणी किं त्वमनङ्गाङ्गविहारिणी। अतीव भ्राजसे सुभ्र प्रभेवेन्दोरनुत्तमा॥
en: Are you the one endued with the beauty of Rati, enjoying dalliance in the embrace of the god of love? O you of fair eye-brows, exceedingly do you shine like the excellent light of the moon.

sn: अपिचेक्षणपक्ष्माणां स्मितं ज्योत्स्नोपमं शुभम्। दिव्यांशुरश्मिभिर्वृत्तं दिव्यकान्तिमनोरमम्॥ निरीक्ष्य वक्त्रचन्द्रं ते लक्ष्यानुपमया युतम्। कृत्स्ने जगति को नेह कामस्य वशगो भवेत्॥
en: Who is there in the whole world that will not yield to the influence of Cupid beholding your face endued with matchless grace-your face endued with the halo of celestials light, are pleasant in consequence of the heavenly bcauty, resembles the moon in full having smile for its rays and eye-lashes for its spots.

sn: हारालंकारयोग्यौ तु स्तनौ चोभौ सुशोभनौ। सुजातौ सहितौ लक्ष्म्या पीनौ वृत्तौ निर गै॥
en: Both your breasts exceedingly graceful, well-shaped, endued with beauty, well rounded and without a space between, and are worthy of being decked with garlands.

sn: कुड्मलाम्बुरुहाकारौ तव सुभ्रु पयोधरौ। कामप्रतोदाविव मां तुदतश्चारुहासिनि॥
en: Your breasts, O you of fair eye-brows, resemble lotus-buds in shape; like the whips of Kama they are afflicting me, O you of pleasant smiles.

sn: वलीविभङ्गचतुरं स्तनभारविनामितम्। कराग्रसम्मितं मध्यं तवेदं तनुमध्यमे॥ दृष्ट्वैव चारु जघनं सरित्पुलिनसंनिभम्। कामव्याधिरसाध्यो मामप्याक्रामति भामिनि॥
en: O slender-waisted lady, beholding this your waist marked with four waivy wrinkles, stooping forward with the veight of your breasts and measuring only a span, and also looking on your beautiful hips resembling the banks of the river the incurable disease of lust afflicts me greatly, O beautiful one.

sn: जज्वाल चाग्निमदनो दावाग्निरिव निर्दयः। त्वत्सङ्गमाभिसंकल्पविवृद्धो मां दहत्ययम्॥
en: The flame of lust like forest conflagration augmented by the hope of union with you burns me without mercy.

sn: आत्मप्रदानवर्षेण संगमाम्भोधरेण च। शमयस्व वरारोहे ज्वलन्त मन्मथानलम्॥
en: O fair one of excellent hip, pray quench the flaming fire kindled by the god of love, by self-surrender resembling a shower, the cloud thereof being union with you.

sn: मच्चित्तोन्मादनकरा मन्मथस्य शरोत्कराः। त्वत्संगमाशानिशितास्तीवाः शशिनिभानने। मां विदार्य हृदयमिदं निर्दयवेगिताः॥ प्रविष्टा ह्यसितापाङ्गि प्रचण्डाश्चण्डदारुणाः। अत्युन्मादसमारम्भाः प्रीत्युन्मादकरा मम। आत्मप्रदानसम्भोगैर्मामुद्धर्तुमिहार्हसि॥
en: O you of a countenance resembling the moon, the dreadful, violent and cruel shafts of Cupid, capable of causing my mind quite out of sorts, sharpened by the desire of dalliance with you, piercing my heart with a rapid course, have penetrated into its core, O black eyed one. The maddening gestures and movements of yours are really transporting my joy into madness. It behoves you to save me from this plight by surrendering your person to me and allowing me to enjoy your company.

sn: चित्रमाल्याम्बरधरा सर्वाभरणभूषिता। कामं प्रकामं सेव त्वं मया सह विलासिनि॥
en: Wearing beautiful garlands and clothes and adorned with all kinds of ornaments enjoy with ine. O sweet one, all the objects of your desire to your fill.

sn: । नार्हसीहासुखं वस्तुं सुखार्हा सुखवर्जिता। प्राप्नुह्यनुत्तमं सौख्यं मत्तस्त्वं मत्तगामिनि॥ स्वादून्यमृतकल्पानि पेयानि विविधानि च। पिबमाना मनोज्ञानि रममाणा यथासुखम्॥ भोगोपचारान् विविधान् सौभाग्यं चाप्यनुत्तमम्। पानं पिब महाभागे भोगैश्चानुत्तमैः शुभैः॥
en: you endued with the gait of an elephant in ruttish state, as you are accustomed to happiness, though deprived of it now, it behoves you not to live here in misery; pray receive from me all kinds of excellent things contributing to your happiness. Eating delightful and dainty viands of various kinds with taste almost equal to ambrosia, and sporting at your sweet will, attain fortune and all the enjoyable articles of superior and excellent kind and drink and wine, O blessed one.

sn: इदं हि रूपं प्रथमं तवान निरर्थकं केवलमद्य भामिनि। अधार्यमाणा स्रगिवोत्तमा शुभा न शोभसे सुन्दरि शोभना सती॥ दारान् मम ये
en: This beauty and prime of your youth, O beauteous lady, is now totally useless. O beautiful and chaste lady, lovely as you are, do you not shine like fine garlands unused?

sn: त्यजामि पुरातना भवन्तु दास्यस्तव चारुहासिनि। अहं च ते सुन्दरि दासवत् स्थितः सदा भविष्ये वशगो वरानने॥
en: I will renounce all my old wives. Let them be your serving hands, O one of sweet smile. O beautiful one, I will stay as a slave to you and be ever obedient to you, O you of fair face.

sn: द्रौपद्युवाच अप्रार्थनीयामिह मां सूतपुत्राभिमन्यसे। निहीनवर्णां सैरन्ध्रीं बीभत्सां केशकारिणीम्॥
en: Draupadi said I am Sairandhri of low caste holding the hateful office of dressing hair; O Suta's son, in desiring me you desire one who is not worthy of such honour.

sn: परदारास्मि भद्रं ते न युक्तं तव साम्प्रतम्। दयिता: प्राणिनां दारा धर्मं समनुचिन्तय॥
en: I am the wife of others; good be to you. This conduct does not become your position. The wives of others are dear to them, think of this axiomatic precept.

sn: परदारे न ते बुद्धिर्जातु कार्या कथंचन। विवर्जनं ह्यकार्याणामेतत् सुपुरुषव्रतम्॥
en: Let your heart never be inclined to adultery, because the complete abandonment of all improper acts is ever the duty of those that are good.

sn: मिथ्याभिगृनो हि नरः पापात्मा मोहमास्थितः। अयशः प्राप्नुयाद् घोरं महद् वा प्राप्नुयाद् भयम्॥३७
en: The person who hankers after the worldly desire leads a sinful life, and under the influence of deceptive knowledge, comes by either dire disgrace or grim calamity.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्तस्तु सैरन्ध्या कीचकः काममोहितः। जानन्नपि सुदुर्बुद्धिः परदाराभिमर्शने।॥ दोषान् बहून् प्राणहरान् सर्वलोकविगर्हितान्। प्रोवाचेदं सुदुर्बुद्धिद्रौपदीमजितेन्द्रियः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Thus addressed by Sairandhri the wickedminded Kichaka, with senses unsubdued and overcome by lust, in spite of the knowledge of numerous evils of adultery the evils denounced by every body and sometimes ending fatally, spoke the following to Draupadi.

sn: नार्हस्येवं वरारोहे प्रत्याख्यातुं वरानने। मां मन्मथसमाविष्टं त्वत्कृते चारुहासिनि॥
en: O fair faced damsel of excellent hips, it is not seemly on your part thus to disregarded me who am quite under the influence of Cupid on your account, O you of sweet smiles.

sn: प्रत्याख्याय च मां भीरु वशगं प्रियवादिनम्। नूनं त्वमसितापाङ्गि पश्चात्तापं करिष्यसि॥
en: O timid one, having disregarded me speaking so sweet to you and totally under your influence, surely, O black eyed one, you will have to true afterwards.

sn: अहं हि सुभ्र राज्यस्य कृत्स्नस्यास्य सुमध्यमे। प्रभुर्वासयिता चैव वीर्ये चाप्रतिमः क्षितौ॥
en: O you of fair eye-brows, I am the lord of the whole of this realm, 0 slender-waisted lady, the people of this kingdom owe to me their safe living here. In heroisin I have to rival on earth.

sn: पृथिव्यां मत्समो नास्ति कश्चिदन्यः पुमानिह। रूपयौवनसौभाग्यैर्भोगैश्चानुत्तमैः शुभैः॥
en: In personal beauty, youth, prosperity as well as in the possession of all the excellent objects of luxury, there is no other man on earth that can stand equal to me.

sn: सर्वकामसमृद्धेषु भोगेष्वनुपमेष्विह। भोक्तव्येषु च कल्याणि कस्माद् दास्ये रता ह्यसि॥
en: Having everything of luxury, comfort and enjoyment of no parallel at your command, why do you, O auspicious lady, prefer to remain enchained in servitude?

sn: मया दत्तमिदं राज्यं स्वामिन्यसि शुभानने। भजस्व मां वरारोहे भुक्ष्व भोगाननुत्तमान्॥
en: O fair-faced one, I confer on you the whole of the kingdom; accept me O you of large ips and enjoy all the excellent objects of desire.

sn: एवमुक्ता तु सा साध्वी कीचकेनाशुभं वचः। कीचकं प्रत्युवाचेदं गर्हयन्त्यस्य तद् वचः॥
en: Thus addressed by Kichaka in these foul words the chaste Draupadi set his word at naught and addressed him thus.

sn: सैरभ्युवाच मा सूतपुत्र मुह्यस्व माद्य त्यक्ष्यस्व जीवितम्। जानीहि पञ्चभि।रैर्नित्यं मामभिरक्षिताम्॥
en: Sairandhri said O son of a Suta, do not play the fool and do not throw away your life this very day; know me always protected by five heroes.

sn: न चाप्यहं त्वया लभ्या गन्धर्वाः पतयो मम। ते त्वां निहन्युः कुपिता: साध्वलं मा व्यनीनशः॥४८
en: I am not to be won by you; I have Gandharvas for my husband, they, if enraged, shall slay you. It is good for you not to bring destruction upon yourself.

sn: अशक्यरूपं पुरुषैरध्वानं गन्तुमिच्छसि। यथा निश्चेतनो बालः कूलस्थ: कूलमुत्तरम्। तर्तुमिच्छति मन्दात्मा तथा त्वं कर्तुमिच्छसि॥
en: You wish to go by the way which was never passed by men, O wicked one; you intend to act just like a foolish boy who standing on one bank of the ocean desires to go to the other side of it.

sn: अन्तर्महीं वा यदि वोर्ध्वमुत्पतेः समुद्रपारं यदि वा प्रधावसि। तथापि तेषां न विमोक्षमर्हसि प्रमाथिनो देवसुता हि खेचराः।॥
en: If you enter the subterreneous pit of the earth or soar up the sky or go to the other shore of the ocean, still you will have no escape from their hands, for it is in the nature of these skyranging offspring of gods to crush enemies.

sn: त्वं कालरात्रीमिव कश्चिदातुरः किं मां दृढं प्रार्थयसेऽद्य कीचक। श्चन्द्र जिघृक्षुरिव मन्यसे हि माम्॥
en: Why do you, O Kichaka, desire me today so firmly, just like a sick man who wishes for the night that will put an end to his existence. Why do you solicit me just like a child who lies on its mother's lap wishes to obtain the moon.

sn: तेषां प्रियां प्रार्थयतो न ते भुवि गत्वा दिवं वा शरणं भविष्यति। न वर्तते कीचक ते दृशा शुभं या तेन संजीवनमर्थयेत् सा॥
en: There will be nowhere any refuge for you soliciting their beloved wife whether you go to the earth or to the heaven. O Kichaka, you have no eyes that may win for you any good or safety of your life.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच प्रत्याख्यातो राजपुत्र्या सुदेष्णां कीचकोऽब्रवीत्। अमर्यादेन कामेन घोरेणाभिपरिप्लुतः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Rejected thus by the princess Kichaka, over-pressed with fearful lust capable of making one forgetful of all sense of propriety, said to Sudeshna.

sn: यथा कैकेयि सैरन्ध्री समेयात् तद् विधीयताम्। येनोपायेन सैरन्ध्री भजेन्मां गजगामिनी। तं सुदेष्णे परीप्सस्व प्राणान् मोहात् प्रहासिषम्॥
en: O Kaikeyi, do that by which Sairandhri may be united with me. O Sudeshna, device a plan by which that Sairandhri of elephant-gait may accept me. Otherwise I intend putting end to my life.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तस्य सा बहुशः श्रुत्वा वाचं विलपतस्तदा। विराटमहिषी देवी कृपां चक्रे मनस्विनी॥
en: Hearing the words of his thus lamenting in manifold terms the intelligent lady, Virata's queen, took pity on him.

sn: स्वमन्त्रमभिसंधाय तस्यार्थमनुचिन्त्य च। उद्योगं चैव कृष्णायाः सुदेष्णा सूतमब्रवीत्॥
en: Holding counsel with her own self and pondering over his desire and over the perturbation of Krishna, Sudeshna said to Suta's son (Kichaka).

sn: पर्वणि त्वं समुद्दिश्य सुरामन्नं च कारय। तत्रैनां प्रेषयिष्यामि सुराहारी तवान्तिकम्॥
en: Taking the advantage of some festival, better have wines and viands prepared. I shall then send her to you to bring some wine.

sn: तत्र सम्प्रेषितामेनां विजने निरवग्रह। सान्त्वयेथा यथाकामं सान्त्व्यमाना रमेद् यदि॥
en: Thus sent thereto you should, in uninterrupted solitude, humour her according to your will. Thus cajoled most likely she may be attached to you.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच इत्युक्तः स विनिष्क्रम्य भगिन्या वचनात् तदा। सुरामाहारयामास राजाहाँ सुपरिष्कृताम्॥
en: Thus addressed he, in pursuance of his sister's words, came out and procured very fine wines worthy of a king.

sn: भक्ष्यांश्च विविधाकारान् बहूंचोच्चावचांस्तदा। कारयामास कुशलैरन्नं पानं सुशोभनम्॥
en: Then he had various kinds of food, diverse sorts of meat of excellent degree and delicious drinks, and dishes prepared by the cooks skilled in the business.

sn: तस्मिन् कृते तदा देवी कीचकेनोपमन्त्रिता। सुदेष्णा प्रेषयामास सैरन्ध्रीं कीचकालयम्॥
en: This being done Sudeshna as previously intimated by Kichaka sent her Sairandhri to the abode of Kichaka, saying.

sn: सुदेष्णोवाच उत्तिष्ठ गच्छ सैरन्ध्र कीचकस्य निवेशनम्। पानमानय कल्याणि पिपासा मां प्रबाधते॥
en: Sudeshna said O Sairandhri, get up and repair to the abode of Kichaka. O gentle one, bring wine for ime, for thirst afflicts me.

sn: सैरन्ध्युवाच न गच्छेयमहं तस्य राजपुत्रि निवेशनम्। त्वमेव राज्ञि जानासि यथा स निरपत्रपः॥
en: Draupadi said O princess, I shall not go to his house; O queen, you know yourself how shameless he is.

sn: न चाहमनवद्याङ्गि तव वेश्मनि भामिनि। कामवृत्ता भविष्यामि पतीनां व्यभिचारिणी॥
en: O beautiful lady of excellent limbs, in your house, I shall never prove myself faithless to my husband and lead a life of chastity.

sn: त्वं चैव देवि जानासि यथा स समयः कृतः। प्रविशन्त्या मया पूर्वं तव वेश्मनि भामिनि॥
en: O beautiful lady, you know full well the condition I made before I had entered your palace.

sn: कीचकस्तु सुकेशान्ते मूढो मदनदर्पितः। सोऽवमंस्यति मां दृष्ट्वा न यास्ये तत्र शोभने॥
en: O you of beautiful hairs having good curls at the end, on seeing me that wicked Kichaka, rendered insolent by the god of desire, will dishonour me. O beautiful one, I shall not repair thither.

sn: सन्ति बयस्तव प्रेष्या राजपुत्रि वशानुगाः। अन्यां प्रेषय भद्रं ते स हि मामवमंस्यते॥
en: O princess, you have good many obedient maids, pray send one of them. Let good betide you, for surely he will insult me.

sn: सुदेष्णोवाच नव त्वां जातु हिंस्यात् स इतः सम्प्रेषितां मया। इत्युक्त्वा प्रददौ पात्रं सपिधानं हिरण्मयम्॥
en: Sudeshna said "Dispatched by me from my palace he will hardly do any harm to you"; saying this she handed out to her a golden pot with a cover.

sn: सा शङ्कमाना रुदती दैवं शरणमीयुषी। प्रातिष्ठत सुराहारी कीचकस्य निवेशनम्॥
en: Filled with fear and shedding tears she asked for the divine protection, an then departed for Kichaka's house for fetching wine.

sn: सैरभ्युवाच यथाहमन्यं भर्तृभ्यो नाभिजानामि कंचन। तेन सत्येन मां प्राप्तां मा कुर्यात् कीचको वशे।।१८।
en: Draupadi said As I do not know any other save and except my husband, let not Kichaka, by strength of that virtue, be able to bring me into his power.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच उपातिष्ठत सा सूर्यं मुहूर्तमबला ततः। स तस्यास्तनुमध्यायाः सर्वं सूर्योऽवबुद्धवान्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Then that helpless one worshipped the sungod for a moment and the deity understood all the prayers of her of slender waist.

sn: अन्तर्हितं ततस्तस्या रक्षो रक्षार्थमादिशत्। तच्चैनां नाजहात् तत्र सर्वावस्थास्वनिन्दिताम्॥
en: Then he ordered a Rakshasa to protect her invisibly and from that time that Rakshasas also never left that blameless lady alone under any circumstances whatever.

sn: तां मृगीमिव संत्रस्तां दृष्ट्वा कृष्णां समीपगाम्। उदतिष्ठन्मुदा सूतो नावं लब्वेव पारगः॥
en: Beholding Krishna come to his presence like a terrified doe, the Suta rose up just like a person wishing to go to the other end of a river when he obtains a boat.

sn: कीचक उवाच स्वागतं ते सुकेशान्ते सुव्युष्टा रजनी मम। स्वामिनी त्वमनुप्राप्ता प्रकुरुष्व मम प्रियम्॥
en: Kichaka said O fair one of beautiful tresses with curls at the end, you are welcome; very luckily for me the night has passed. I have got you as the mistress of my house, pray do what is good to me,

sn: सुवर्णमालाः कम्बूश्च कुण्डले परिहाटके। नानापत्तनजे शुभ्रे मणिरत्नं च शोभनम्॥
en: Let golden chains, couches, brilliant golden ear-rings of different countries, beautiful gems and jewels, silken garments and dcer skins be gathered for you.

sn: आहरन्तु च वस्त्राणि कौशिकान्यजिनानि च। अस्ति मे शयनं दिव्यं त्वदर्थमुपक्लिपतम्। एहि तत्र मया सार्द्धं पिबस्व मधुमाधवीम्॥
en: I have a very fine bed prepared only for you; pray come there and drink with me the honeyed wine.

sn: द्रौपद्युवाच अप्रैषीद् राजपुत्री मां सुराहारी तवान्तिकम्। पानमाहर मे क्षिप्रं पिपासा मेऽति चाब्रवीत्॥
en: Draupadi said The princess has sent me to you for taking away wine; give it to me quickly, she said to ine she has a great thirst.

sn: कीचक उवाच अन्या भद्रे नयिष्यन्ति राजपुत्र्याः प्रतिश्रुतम्। इत्येतां दक्षिणे पाणौ सूतपुत्रः परामृशत्॥
en: Kichaka said O gentle one, others will take the wine that has been wromised to the princess, Saying this the Suta's son seized her by the right arm.

sn: द्रौपद्युवाच यथैवाहं नाभिचरे कदाचित् पतीन् मदाद् वै मनसापि जातु। तेनैव सत्येन वशीकृतं त्वां द्रष्टास्मि पापं परिकृष्यमाणम्॥
en: Draupadi said As I have never acted faithlessly towards my husbands, even at heart through infatuation; by virtue of that truth, O sinful one, I shall behold you overpowered and completely hurled down on the ground.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच स तामभिप्रेक्ष्य विशालनेत्रां जिघृक्षमाणः परिभर्सयन्तीम्। जग्राह तामुत्तरवस्त्रदेशे स कीचकस्तां सहसाऽऽक्षिपन्तीम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Wishing thus to take hold of her Kichaka, seeing that large-eyed lady reproaching him in this wise, seized her by the end of her upper garment while she was about to run away.

sn: प्रगृह्यमाणा तु महाजवेन मुहुर्विनिःश्वस्य च राजपुत्री। तया समाक्षिप्ततनुः स पापः पपात शाखीव निकृत्तमूलः॥
en: But seized with great force the princess of excellent limbs began to pant and unable to put up with it, she, with a frame trembling in wrath, hurled him hard on the ground. Being thus thrown down by her that sinful one fell to the ground like a tree whose root has been cut.

sn: सा गृहीता विधुन्वाना भूमावाक्षिप्य कीचकम्। सभां शरणमागच्छद् यत्र राजा युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Having thus thrown Kichaka down on the ground while seized by him she ran trembling to the court, where the king Yudhishthira was, to seek protection.

sn: तां कीचकः प्रधावन्ती केशपाशे परामृशत्। अथैनां पश्यतो राज्ञः पातयित्वा पदावधीत्॥
en: Kichaka seized her by the locks while she was running with speed and struck her down by a kick in the very presence of the king.

sn: तस्य योऽसौ तदार्केण राक्षसः संनियोजितः। स कीचकमपोवाह वातवेगेन भारत॥
en: 0 Bharata, the Rakshasa that was appointed by the sun-god for her protection, gave a push to Kichaka with as much force as that of the wind.

sn: स पपात तदा भूमौ रक्षोबलसमाहतः। विघूर्णमानो निश्चेष्टश्छिन्नमूल इव दुमः॥
en: Then he, completely overpowered by the Rakshasa might, fell down on the ground, reeling and motionless like a tree whose root has been cut.

sn: तां चासीनौ ददृशतुर्भीमसेनयुधिष्ठिरौ। अमृष्यमाणौ कृष्णायाः कीचकेन पराभवन्॥
en: Both Bhimasena and Yudhishthira, who were seated there, beheld with unforgiving attitude, that outrage on Krishna committed by Kichaka.

sn: तस्य भीमो वधं प्रेप्सुः कीचकस्य दुरात्मनः। दन्तैर्दन्तांस्तदा रोषान्निष्पिपेष महामनाः॥
en: Desiring the death of that wicked Kichaka the high-minded Bhima began to knash his teeth in wrath.

sn: धूमच्छाया ह्यभजतां नेत्रे चोच्छ्रित श्मणी। सस्वेदा भृकुटी चोग्रा ललाटे समवर्तत॥
en: His eyes with their lashes upraised, assumed the aspect of smoky dark, and terrible wrinkles covered with sweat appeared on his forehead.

sn: हस्तेन ममृजे चैव ललाटं परवीरहा। भूयश्च त्वरितः क्रुद्धः सहसोत्थातुमैच्छत॥
en: That slayer of hostile heroes rubbed his forehead with his hand and incensed with ire desired many times to rise up in haste.

sn: अथावमृद्गादङ्गुष्ठमङ्गुष्ठेन युधिष्ठिरः। प्रबोधनभयाद् राजा भीमं तं प्रत्यषेधयत्॥
en: The king Yudhishthira, apprehending discovery, pressed his thumb with his own and commanded Bhima to desist.

sn: तं मत्तमिव मातङ्गं वीक्षमाणं वनस्पतिम्। स तमावारयामास भीमसेनं युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Yudhishthira forbade Bhimasena who looked like an infuriated elephant beholding a large tree.

sn: आलोकयसि किं वृक्षं सूद दारुकृतेन वै। यदि ते दारुभिः कृत्यं बहिर्वक्षान्निगृह्यताम्॥
en: O cook, do you behold trees for fuel? If you are in need of faggots better gather them up from the trees abroad.

sn: सा सभाद्वारमासाद्य रुदती मत्स्यमब्रवीत्। अवेक्षमाणा सुश्रोणी पतीस्तान् दीनचेतसः॥ आकारमभिरक्षन्ती प्रतिज्ञाधर्मसंहिता। दह्यमानेव रौद्रेण चक्षुषा दुपदात्मजा॥
en: The weeping daughter of Draupadi, endowed with excellent hips, approaching the entrance of the court and beholding her lords of melancholy mood, tenacious in keeping up the disguise observing the pledge they had already sworn, burning with flashing eyes, spoke to the king of the Matsya's.

sn: येषां वैरी न स्वपिति षष्ठेऽपि विषये वसन्। तेषां मां मानिनीं भार्यां सूतपुत्रः पदावधीत्॥
en: The son of a Suta has kicked me the honored spouse of those whose enemies can never sleep even if they reside in regions of anchorites (what to speak of their living in a country of their own).

sn: ये दधुर्न च याचेयुर्ब्रह्मण्याः सत्यवादिनः। तेषां मां मानिनी भार्यां सूतपुत्रः पदावधीत्॥
en: The son of a Suta has kicked me, the respected consort of those who are truthful, devoted to Brahmans and used to give away without asking any thing in gift.

sn: येषां दुन्दुभिनिर्घोषो ज्याघोषः श्रूयतेऽनिशम्। तेषां मां मानिनीं भार्यां सूतपुत्रः पदावधीत्॥
en: The son of a Suta has kicked me the beloved wife of those, the sounds of whose drums and twangs of whose bow are constantly heard.

sn: ये च तेजस्विनी दान्ता बलवन्तोऽतिमानिनः। तेषां मां मानिनीं भार्यां सूतपुत्रः पदावधीत्॥
en: The son of a Suta has kicked me the respected wife of those who are endowed with energy, and power of self-control, and who are exceedingly mighty and highly dignified.

sn: सर्वलोकमिमं हन्युर्धर्मपाशसितास्तु ये। तेषां मां मानिनीं भार्यां सूतपुत्रः पदावधीत्॥
en: The son of a Suta has kicked me the honored wife of those who, if they had not been tied down by duty, could destroy the whole of this world.

sn: शरणं ये प्रपन्नानां भवन्ति शरणार्थिनाम्। चरन्ति लोके प्रच्छन्नाः क्व नु तेऽद्य महारथाः॥
en: Alas where do those mighty warriors ramble in disguise today who grant refuge to those that come to solicit it.

sn: कथं ते सूतपुत्रेण वध्यमानां प्रियां सतोम्। मर्षयन्ति यथा क्लीबा बलवन्तोऽमितौजसः॥
en: How do these inighty personages of exceeding energy quietly suffer, like eunuchs, their beloved and chaste wife to be thus outraged by the son of a Suta?

sn: क्व नु तेषाममर्षश्च वीर्य तेजश्च वर्तते। न परीप्सन्ति ये भार्यां वध्यमानां दुरात्मना॥
en: Ah, where is their wrath, the prowess and the energy when they cannot protect their wife from being thus insulted by a wretch.

sn: मयात्र शक्यं किं कर्तुं विराटे धर्मदूषके। यः पश्यन् मां मर्षयति वध्यमानामनागसम्॥
en: What can I do in the city of Virata, the defiler of virtue, who coolly allows my innocent self thus to be insulted although he sees it (with his own eyes).

sn: न राजा राजवत् किंचित् समाचरति कीचके। दस्यूनामिव धर्मस्ते न हि संसदि शोभते॥
