en: The king does not act like a king in the slightest degree towards Kichaka. O king, your conduct is like that of a robber and does not become the royal court.

sn: नाहमेतेन युक्तं वै हन्तुं मत्स्य तवान्तिके। सभासदोऽत्र पश्यन्तु कीचकस्य व्यतिक्रमम्॥
en: O Matsya, it is highly unbecoming that I should thus be outraged by this villain in the very presence of yours. Let all the courtiers mark this laxity on the part of Kichaka.

sn: कीचको न च धर्मज्ञो न च मत्स्यः कथंचन। सभासदोऽप्यधर्मज्ञा य एनं पर्युपासते।॥
en: Neither Kichaka is virtuous nor ever is Matsya. The courtiers who wait upon the king are also destitute of virtue.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवंविधैर्वचोभिः सा तदा कृष्णाश्रुलोचना। उपलाभत राजानं मत्स्यानां वरवर्णिनी॥
en: Vaishampayana said With words like these the graceful Krishna, with eyes teeming with tears, rebuked the king of the Matsya.

sn: विराट उवाच परोक्षं नाभिजानामि विग्रहं युवयोरहम्। अर्थतत्त्वमविज्ञाय किं नु स्यात् कौशलं मम॥
en: Virata said I do not know anything of your quarrel that happened out of our light. How can there be any justice on that score unless I go through the true version of the case.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततस्तु सभ्या विज्ञाय कृष्णां भूयोऽभ्यपूजयन्। साधु साध्विति चाप्याहुः कीचकं च व्यगर्हयन्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Then the courtiers, hearing everything, praised Krishna and repeatedly exclaimed “well done well done,” and reproached Kichaka.

sn: सभ्या ऊचुः यस्येयं चारुसर्वाङ्गी भार्या स्यादायतेक्षणा। परो लाभस्तु तस्य स्यान्न च शोचेत् कथंचन॥
en: The Courtiers said Surely the man, who has this lady of expansive eyes and of all-graceful limbs for his wife, possesses every thing that is valuable and shall on.no occasion have to indulge in grief.

sn: न हीदृशी मनुष्येषु सुलभा वरवर्णिनी। नारी सर्वानवद्याङ्गी देवीं मन्यामहे वयम्॥
en: Surely such a lady, of exceeding grace an perfectly faultless limbs, is hardly to be found among men. Indeed she seems in all wise to be a goddess to us.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवं सम्पूजयन्तस्ते कृष्णां प्रेक्ष्य सभासदः। युधिष्ठिरस्य कोपात् तु ललाटे स्वेद आगमत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said While the courtiers, seeing Krishna, were praising her in this way, there came from ire the drops of perspiration on the forehead of Yudhishthira.

sn: अथाब्रवीद् राजपुत्री कौरव्यो महिषीं प्रियाम्। गच्छ सैरन्ध्र मात्र स्थाः सुदेष्णाया निवेशनम्॥
en: Then the chief of the Kurus addressed the princess, his beloved consort, saying "O Sairandhri, do not stay here, go to the apartment of Sudeshna.

sn: भर्तारमनुरुन्धन्त्यः क्लिश्यन्ते वीरपत्नयः। शुश्रूषया क्लिश्यमानाः पतिलोकं जयन्त्युत॥
en: The wives of heroes endure pain for the sake of their husbands; but undergoing trouble in waiting upon their lords they at last go to the regions where their husbands depart.

sn: मन्ये न कालं क्रोधस्य पश्यन्ति पतयस्तव। तेन त्वां नाभिधावन्ति गन्धर्वाः सूर्यवर्चसः॥
en: Me-seems your Gandharva husbands of sun-like effulgence do not consider this as a befitting opportunity of giving vent to their spleen, and therefore do not run on to your succour.

sn: अकालज्ञासि सैरन्ध्र शैलूषीव विरोदिषि। विघ्नं करोषि मत्स्यानां दीव्यतां राजसंसदि॥
en: O Sairandhri, you are ignorant of opportunity and therefore weep like an actress; you are causing annoyance in the court of the Matsya's while they are diverting themselves with gaming.

sn: गच्छ सैरन्ध्र गन्धर्वाः करिष्यन्ति तव प्रियम्। व्यपनेष्यन्ति ते दुःखं येन ते विप्रियं कृतम्॥
en: Retire, O Sairandhri, the Gandharvas will do what is agreeable to you. They will dispel your sorrow and make away with him who has wronged you.

sn: सैरभ्युवाच अतीव तेषां घृणिनामर्थेऽहं धर्मचारिणी। तस्य तस्यैव ते वध्या येषां ज्येष्ठोऽक्षदेविता॥
en: Sairandhri said I practise piety for their sake who are extremely kind. They, of whom the eldest is addicted to dice, are to be oppressed by all.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच इत्युक्त्वा प्राद्रवत् कृष्णा सुदेष्णाया निवेशनम्। केशान् मुक्त्वा च सुश्रोणी संरम्भाल्लोहितेक्षणा।।४६
en: Vaishampayana said Having said this the fair Krishna with loosened hair and eyes reddened with wrath, rushed on towards the apartments of Sudeshna.

sn: शुशुभे वदनं तस्या रुदत्याः सुचिरं तदा। मेघलेखाविनिर्मुक्तं दिवीव शशिमण्डलम्॥
en: On her having wept so long her countenance appeared like the lunar disc in the sky freed from the clouds.

sn: सुदेष्णोवाच कस्त्वावधीद् वरारोहे कस्माद् रोदिषि शोभने। कस्याद्य न सुखं भद्रे केन ते विप्रियं कृतम्॥
en: Sudeshana said O beautiful one of excellent hips, who has slighted you, why do you weep. O gentle one, whose happiness will come to an end this day? Who has done wrong to you?

sn: द्रौपद्युवाच कीचको मावधीत् तत्र सुराहारीं गतां तवा सभायां पश्यतो राज्ञो यथैव विजने वने॥
en: Draupadi said As I went to fetch wine for you Kichaka struck me in the court in the very presence of the king as if in the midst of a lonely forest.

sn: सुदेष्णोवाच घातयामि सुकेशान्ते कीचकं यदि मन्यसे। योऽसौ त्वां कामसम्मत्तो दुर्लभामवमन्यते॥
en: Sudeshana said 50. O you of tresses with curly ends, if it be your will, I shall cause Kichaka to be slain, who maddened with lust, has insulted you utterly incapable of being won by him.

sn: सैन्ध्युवाच अन्ये चैनं वधिष्यन्ति येषामागः करोति सः। मन्ये चैवाद्य सुव्यक्तं यमलोकं गमिष्यति॥
en: Sairandhri said Others whom he has wronged will slay him; I think he will certainly go this very day to the region of Yama (Death).

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच सा हता सूतपुत्रेण राजपत्नी यशस्विनी। वधं कृष्णा परीप्सन्ती सेनावाहस्य भामिनी।।।।
en: Vaishampayana said Thus outraged by the Suta's son that illustrious princess Krishna of exceeding beauty, brooding over the destruction of the leader of Virata's forces, repaired to her own apartments.

sn: जगामावासमेवाथ सा तदा द्रुपदात्मजा। कृत्वा शौचं यथान्यायं कृष्णा सा तनुमध्यमा।॥ गात्राणि वाससी चैव प्रक्षाल्य सलिलेन सा। चिन्तयामास रुदती तस्य दुःखस्य निर्णयम्॥
en: Having duly washed her body and clothes with water the slender-waisted Krishna, the daughter of Drupada, began to ponder weepingly on the means of discarding her grief.

sn: किं करोमि क्व गच्छामि कथं कार्यं भवेन्मम। इत्येवं चिन्तयित्वा सा भीमं वै मनसागमत्॥
en: What shall I do? Whither shall I go? How can my desire be accomplished? while she was thinking thus she thought of Bhima.

sn: नान्यः कर्ता ऋते भीमान्ममाद्य मनसः प्रियम्। तत उत्थाय रात्रौ सा विहाय शयनं स्वकम्॥ प्राद्रवन्नाथमिच्छन्ती कृष्णा नाथवती सती। भवनं भीमसेनस्य क्षिप्रमायतलोचना॥ दुःखेन महता युक्ता मानसेन मनस्विनी।
en: Save and except Bhima there is none else that can do this very day what is agreeable to me. Then afflicted with great woe that largeeyed Krishna of spacious breast and approved chastity, with mighty lords as her protectors, rose up at night, left her own bed and repaired speedily to the abode of Bhimasena, desirous of accosting her lord.

sn: सैरन्ध्युवाच तस्मिञ्जीवति पापिष्ठे सेनावाहे मम द्विषि॥ तत् कर्म कृतवानद्य कथं निद्रां निषेवसे।
en: Sairandhri said How can you enjoy the sweets of sleep while that foe of mine, the wretched commander of Virata's forces, lives still, having perpetrated that foul deed today?

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्त्वाथ तां शालां प्रविवेश मनस्विनी॥ यस्यां भीमस्तथा शेते मृगराज इव श्वसन्।
en: Vaishampayana said Having said this the high-minded Draupadi entered the chamber where Bhima lay asleep snoring like a lion.

sn: तस्या रूपेण सा शाला भीमस्य च महात्मनः॥ सम्मूर्छितेव कौरव्य प्रजज्वाल च तेजसा। सा वै महानसं प्राप्य भीमसेनं शुचिस्मिता॥ सर्वश्वेतेव माहेयी वने जाता त्रिहायणी।
en: O son of Kuru! Bhima's kitchen got grandeur and glamour as it was illumined with the divine touch of Draupadi's complexion and her presence. Draupadi with her innocent smile, accessed to great Bhima with her entrance in kitchen like (she) her on born in water (gradually access to heron, ox and elephant), parthiva cow of three years age and she elephant.

sn: उपातिष्ठत पाञ्चाली वासितेव नरर्षभम्॥ सा लतेव महाशालं फुल्लं गोमतितीरजम्।
en: The daughter of Panchala embraced the second son of Pandu even as a creeper embraces a vigorous and huge Sala tree on the banks of the Gomati.

sn: परिष्वजत पाञ्चाली मध्यमं पाण्डुनन्दनम्॥ बाहुभ्यां परिरभ्यैनं प्राबोधयदनिन्दिता। सिंहं सुप्तं वने दुर्गे मृगराजवधूरिव।॥
en: Having clasped him with her arms that faultless one roused him from his bed just as lioness awakes a sleeping lion in a solitary forest.

sn: भीमसेनमुपाश्लिष्यद्धस्तिनीव महागजम्। वीणेव मधुरालापा गान्धारं साधु मूर्छती। अभ्यभाषत पाञ्चाली भीमसेनमनिन्दिता॥
en: Having embraced Bhimasena as a sheelephant embraces her mighty mate, that faultless daughter of Panchala, possessed of a voice sweet as the sound of a Vina, sounding out clearly the Gandharva tune addressed Bhimasena thus.

sn: उत्तिष्ठोत्तिष्ठ किं शेषे भीमसेन यथा मृतः। नामृतस्य हि पापीयान् भार्यामालभ्य जीवति॥
en: O Bhimasena, rise up, why do you sleep like a dead one? For a sinful wretch cannot live after insulting the wife of one that is not dead.

sn: स सम्प्रहाय शयनं राजपुत्र्या प्रबोधितः। उपातिष्ठत मेधाभः पर्यङ्के सोपसंग्रहे॥
en: Being awakened by the princess he, having complexion like that of the clouds, left his bed and sat on the couch furnished with pillows.

sn: अथाब्रवीद् राजपुत्री कौरव्यो महिषीं प्रियाम्। केनास्यर्थेन सम्प्राप्ता त्वरितेव ममान्तिकम्॥
en: Then the son of Kunti addressed his beloved consort saying "For what purpose have you come hither so speedily to me?

sn: न ते प्रकृतिमान् वर्णः कृशा पाण्डुश्च लक्ष्यसे। आचक्ष्व परिशेषेण सर्वं विद्यामहं यथा॥
en: Your complexion seems to have lost its natural hue; you appear lean and pale, tell me all in detail that I may know every thing.

sn: सुखं वा यदि वा दुःखं द्वेष्यं वा यदि वा प्रियम्। यथावत् सर्वमाचक्ष्व श्रुत्वा ज्ञास्यामि यत् क्षमम्।।१९
en: Tell me everything clearly whether it be pleasurable; having heard all I shall do what lies in my power.

sn: अहमेव हि ते कृष्णा विश्वास्यः सर्वकर्मसु। अहमापत्सु चापि त्वां मोक्षयामि पुनः पुनः॥
en: In all works of yours, O Krishna, I am your confident, for I alone deliver you from danger again and again.

sn: शीघ्रमुक्त्वा यथाकामं यत् ते कार्यं विवक्षितम्। गच्छ वै शयनायैव पुरा नान्येन बुध्यते॥
en: Telling me quickly what is your wish and what you purpose to do, repair to your bed before others are up.

sn: द्रौपद्युवाच अशोच्यत्वं कुतस्तस्य यस्या भर्ता युधिष्ठिरः। जानन् सर्वाणि दुःखानि किं मां त्वं परिपृच्छसि॥
en: Draupadi said Whence can there be a freedom of grief to her who has Yudhishthira for her husband? Knowing all my griefs do you ask me?

sn: यन्मां दासीप्रवादेन प्रातिकामी तदानयत्। सभापरिषदो मध्ये तन्मां दहति भारत।।२
en: The grief, when Pratikami dragged me in the court in the midst of the courtiers calling me a slave, burns me still, C Bharata,

sn: पार्थिवस्य सुता नाम का नु जीवति मादृशी। अनुभूयेदृशं दुःखमन्यत्र द्रौपदी प्रभो॥
en: What other princess like me, would live enduring such a hard misery?

sn: वनवासगतायाश्च सैन्धवेन दुरात्मना। परामर्शो द्वितीयो वै सोढुमुत्सहते तु का॥
en: Who else except me has so much energy as to suffer the insult offered by the wicked prince of Sindhu during our stay in the forest?

sn: मत्स्यराजसमक्षं तु तस्य धूर्तस्य पश्यतः। कीचकेन परामृष्टा का नु जीवति मादृशी॥
en: Who else like me, can live having been kicked by Kichaka in the very presence of the wicked king of the Matsya's?

sn: एवं बहुविधैः क्लेशैः क्लिश्यमानां च भारत। न मां जानासि कौन्तेय किं फलं जीवितेन मे॥
en: O Bharata, of what use is the life to me, when you, O son of Kunti, do not think of me, who have been afflicted with various woes like these?

sn: योऽयं राज्ञो विराटस्य कीचको नाम भारत। सेनानी: पुरुषव्याघ्रः श्यालः परमदुर्मतिः॥ स मां सैरन्ध्रवेषेण वसन्ती राजवेश्मनि। नित्यमेवाह दुष्टात्मा भार्या मम भवेति वै॥
en: O Bharata, the most wicked-minded one of vile nature, known by the name Kichaka, who is the leader of his forces, addresses we, everyday, O best men, while living in the royal palace in the guise of a Sairandhri, saying "do you become my wife."

sn: तेनोपमन्त्र्यमाणाया वधाहेण सपत्नहन्। कालेनेव फलं पक्वं हृदयं मे विदीर्यते॥
en: O slayer of foes, thus addressed by him deserving destruction, my heart is bursting like a fruit ripened in due time.

sn: भ्रातरं च विगर्हस्व ज्येष्ठं दुर्दूतदेविनम्। यस्यास्मि कर्मणा प्राप्ता दुःखमेतदनन्तकम्॥
en: You should pass censure on your eldest brother who is sorely addicted to the despicable game of dice, through whose act alone I have received this endless woe.

sn: को हि राज्यं परित्यज्य सर्वस्वं चात्मना सह। प्रव्रज्यायैव दीव्येत विना दुर्दूतदेविनम्॥
en: Who else, except him, addicted sore to gambling, would play, renouncing kingdom and every thing including his self, in order to lead a life in the forest?

sn: यदि निष्कसहस्रेण यच्चान्यत् सारवद् धनम्। सायम्प्रातरदेविष्यदपि संवत्सरान् बहून्॥ रुक्मं हिरण्यं वासांसि यानं युग्यमजाविकम्। अश्वाश्वतरसङ्घांश्च न जातु क्षयमावहेत्॥
en: If he had played morning and evening for many years together pawning Nishkas by thousands and other treasures of value, still his silver and gold robes and cars, teams and goats, and sheep and horses and mules would have hardly suffered any diminution.

sn: सोऽयं द्यूतप्रवादेन श्रियः प्रत्यवरोपितः। तूष्णीमास्ते यथा मूढः स्वानि कर्माणि चिन्तयन्।।१४।
en: But deprived of fortune by rivalry of dice he now holds silence like a fool meditating over his own misdeeds.

sn: दश नागसहस्राणि हयानां हेममालिनाम्। यं यान्तमनुयान्तीह सोऽयं द्यूतेन जीवति॥
en: It is he, who while going out, was followed by ten thousand elephants, adorned with golden garlands, and he now supports himself by gambling at dice.

sn: रथाः शतसहस्राणि नृपाणाममितौजसाम्। उपासन्त महाराजमिन्द्रप्रस्थे युधिष्ठिरम्॥ शतं दासीसहस्राणां यस्य नित्यं महानसे। पात्रीहस्तं दिवारात्रमतिथीन् भोजयन्त्युत॥ एष निकसहस्राणि प्रदाय ददतां वरः। द्यूतजेन ह्यनर्थेन महता समुपाश्रितः॥
en: That great king, Yudhishthira, the best of the charitable, whom the kings by hundreds of thousands endowed with unparalleled power worshipped at the city of Indraprastha, at whose kitchen a hundred thousand maids, with plate in hand used to feed every day, day and night, numbers of guests, and who used to give away in charity a thousand nishkas, is also overpowered by great calamity caused by gambling.

sn: एवं हि स्वरसम्पन्ना बहवः सूतमागधाः। सायम्प्रातरुपातिष्ठन् सुमृष्टमणिकुण्डलः॥
en: Many bards and eulogists gifted with musical voice, and decked with bright ear-rings beset with gems, worshipped him morning and evening.

sn: सहस्रमृषयो यस्य नित्यमासन् सभासदः। तपःश्रुतोपसम्पन्नाः सर्वकामैरुपस्थिताः॥ अष्टाशीतिसहस्राणि स्नातका गृहमेधिनः। त्रिंशद्दासीक एकैको यान् बिभर्ति युधिष्ठिरः॥ अप्रतिग्राहिणां चैव यतीनामूर्ध्वरेतसाम्। दश चापि सहस्राणि सोऽयमास्ते नरेश्वरः॥
en: That Yudhishthira, who had a number of sages versed in the Vedas, gifted with ascetic merit, and having all their wishes complied with, as his daily courtiers, and who maintained eighty-eight thousands of wedded snatakas, to each of whom there were assigned maids thirty in number, as well as ten thousand yatis abstaining from accepting any thing in shape of gift and having their vital seed totally drawn up, that lord of men lives in such a plight.

sn: आनृशंस्यमनुक्रोशं संविभागस्तथैव च। यस्मिन्नेतानि सर्वाणि सोऽयमास्ते नरेश्वरः॥
en: That lord of men, who is free from cruelty, full of compassion and used to give every one his legitimate due, is, inspite of all these excellent attributes, destined to live in such a guise.

sn: अन्धान् वृद्धांस्तथानाथान् बालान् राष्ट्रेषु दुर्गतान्। बिभर्ति विविधान् राजा धृतिमान् सत्यविक्रमः। संविभागमना नित्यमानृशंस्याद् युधिष्ठिरः॥ स एष निरयं प्राप्तो मत्स्यस्य परिचारकः। सभायां देविता राज्ञः कङ्को ब्रूते युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: That very monarch Yudhishthira, who is forbearing, of unfailing prowess, and having a mind bent on giving every one his legitimate due, and in consequence of his not indulging in to a harmful feeling, maintained daily, in his kingdom, the blind, the old, the helpless, the orphans of various kinds and many others in such distress. That Yudhishthira, NOW becoming a servant of the king of the Matsya's, and a gambler in his court, and calling himself by the name Kanka, has surely attained the misery of hell.

sn: इन्द्रप्रस्थे निवसतः समये यस्य पार्थिवाः। आसन् बलिभृतः सर्वे सोऽद्यान्यै तिमिच्छति॥
en: Alas! even he begs for his subsistence at another's hands whom residing at Indraprastha, all the kings of earth used to pay tributes.

sn: पार्थिवाः पृथिवीपाला यस्यासन् वशवर्तिनः। स वशे विवशो राजा परेषामद्य वर्तते॥
en: Alas! even that king, who had all the kings of earth in subjection, has lost his liberty and lives in subjection to others.

sn: प्रताप्य पृथिवीं सर्वां रश्मिमानिव तेजसा। सोऽयं राज्ञो विराटस्य सभास्तारो युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Having dazzled, like the sun, the whole of this earth with his power, even that king Yudhishthira remains as a courtier of king Virata.

sn: यमुपासन्त राजानः सभायामृषिभिः सह। तमुपासीनमद्यान्यं पश्य पाण्डव पाण्डवम्॥
en: O Pritha's son, behold that Pandava today waiting upon another, who was waited upon in court by the kings with sages.

sn: सदस्यं यमुपासीनं परस्य प्रियवादिनम्। दृष्ट्वा युधिष्ठिरं कोपो वर्धते मामसंशयम्॥
en: Beholding Yudhishthira as a courtier sitting beside another and uttering eulogistic speeches, who is there that is not positively afflicted with grief.

sn: अतदर्ह महाप्राज्ञं जीवितार्थेऽभिसंस्थितम्। दृष्ट्वा कस्य न दुःखं स्याद् धर्मात्मानं युधिष्ठिरम्॥
en: Beholding that virtuous Yudhishthira of great wisdom, undeserving of such a plight and serving another for maintenance who is there that is not overtaken by grief.

sn: उपास्ते स्म सभायां यं कृत्स्ना वीर वसुन्धरा। तमुपासीनमप्यन्यं पश्य भारत भारतम्॥
en: 0 Bharata, behold that Bharata, who was worshipped by all the heroes of earth in court, even he is now serving another for subsistence.

sn: एवं बहुविधैर्दुःखैः पीड्यमानामनाथवत्। शोकसागरमध्यस्थां किं मां भीम न पश्यसि॥
en: O Bhima, why do you not look at me who am stationed in the midst of the sea of sorrow and afflicted like a helpless one, with various woes.

sn: द्रौपयुवाच इदं तु ते महद् दुःखं यत् प्रवक्ष्यामि भारत। न मेऽभ्यसूया कर्तव्या दुःखादेतद् ब्रवीम्यहम्॥
en: Draupadi said O Bharata, what I am going to tell you now is another great grief of mine; you should not get angry with me, as I tell you this out of a sheer sadness of heart.

sn: सूदकर्मणि हीने त्वमसमे भरतर्षभ। ब्रुवन् बल्लवजातीयः कस्य शोकं न वर्धयेः॥
en: Who is there whose grief is not enhanced seeing you employed in the abominable service of a cook, entirely unbecoming of you, and calling yourself as belonging to the sect of Ballava.

sn: सूपकारं विराटस्य बल्लवं त्वां विदुर्जनाः। प्रेष्यत्वं समनुप्राप्त ततो दुःखतरं नु किम्॥ यदा महानसे सिद्धे विराटमुपतिष्ठसि। ब्रुवाणो बल्लव: सूदस्तदा सीदति मे मनः॥
en: What can be more distressful than this that people should know you as Virata's cook Ballava by name and fallen into servitude. When you wait on the king Virata calling yourself as Ballava the cook after getting through the work of the kitchen, then my very niind sinks into despair.

sn: यदा प्रहृष्टः सम्राट् त्वां संयोधयति कुवारैः। हसन्त्यन्तःपुरे नार्यो मम तूद्विजते मनः॥
en: When the monarch in joy makes you fight with elephants and the women of his seraglio laugh my mind totally sinks in sorrow.

sn: शार्दूलैर्महिषैः सिंहैरागारे योध्यसे यदा। कैकेय्याः प्रेक्षमाणायास्तदा मे कश्मलं भवेत्॥
en: When you fought with lions, tigers and buffaloes in the inner apartment of the palace in the occular presence of Kaikayi then the faint came over me.

sn: तत उत्थाय कैकेयी सर्वास्ताः प्रत्यभाषत। प्रेष्याः समुत्थिताश्चापि कैकेयीं ताः स्त्रियोऽब्रुवन्॥ प्रेक्ष्य मामनवद्यागी कश्मलोपहतामिव। स्नेहात् संवासजाद् धर्मात् सूदमेषा शुचिस्मिता॥ योद्ध्यमानं महावीर्यमियं समनुशोचति। कल्याणरूपा सैरन्ध्री बल्लवश्चापि सुन्दरः॥ स्त्रीणां चित्तं च दुर्जेयं युक्तरूपौ च मे मतौ। सैरन्ध्री प्रियसंवासान्नित्यं करुणवादिनी॥ अस्मिन् राजकुले चेमौ तुल्यकालनिवासिनौ। इति ब्रुवाणा वाक्यानि सा मां नित्यमतर्जयत्॥
en: Then rising from her seat along with her maids who also rose up with her, Kaikayi beholding me with limbs uninjured and only overtaken by swoon, addressed them saying "surely it is from the affection originated by living together that this lady of beautiful smile grieves for the cook, seeing him fighting with beasts of exceeding strength. Sairandhri is one of exceeding beauty and Ballava is handsome too, the heart of woman is so hard to know; and me-thinks they both are deserving of each other. Sairandhri is seen constantly lamenting for the connection with her lover and they both have entered this royal family at the same time.” Speaking such words she always scolds me.

sn: क्रुध्यन्तीं मां च सम्प्रेक्ष्य समशङ्कत मां त्वयि। तस्यां तथा ब्रुवत्यां तु दुःखं मां महदाविशत्॥
en: Beholding me getting enraged she suspects me to be attached to you which she speaks; thus I am overtaken by great grief.

sn: त्वय्येवं निरयं प्राप्ते भीमे भीमपराक्रमे। शोके यौधिष्ठिरे मग्ना नाहं जीवितुमुत्सहे॥
en: Beholding you, O Bhima of terrible prowess, suffering from being fallen into such a dire calamity and sunk in grief for Yudhishthira I do not intend to live.

sn: यः सदेवान् मनुष्यांश्च सर्वांश्चैकरथोऽजयत्। सोऽयं राज्ञो विराटस्य कन्यानां नर्तको युवा॥
en: Alas! that youthful one, who on a single car defeated all celestials and men, is now the dancing master of the daughters of the king Virata.

sn: योऽतर्पयदमेयात्मा खाण्डवे जातवेदसम्। सोऽन्तःपुरगतः पार्थ कूपेऽग्निरिव संवृतः॥
en: That Pritha's son, who with his immeasurable energy gratified the fire-god in the Khandava forest, is now stationed in the seraglio like fire concealed in a well.

sn: यस्माद् भयममित्राणां सदैव पुरुषर्षभात्। स लोकपरिभूतेन वेषेणास्ते धनंजयः॥
en: That Dhananjaya, from whom, the best of men, enemies had constant dread, is now living in a guise hated by all.

sn: यस्य ज्याक्षेपकठिनौ बाहू परिघसंनिभौ। स शङ्खपरिपूर्णाभ्यां शोचन्नास्ते धनंजयः॥
en: That Dhananjaya, whose arms are likes inaces of iron and are marked by the strokes of the bow-string, is living in grief with his wrists covered with conch-bracelets.

sn: यस्य ज्यातलनिर्घोषात् समकम्पन्त शत्रवः। स्त्रियो गीतस्वनं तस्य मुदिताः पर्युपासते॥
en: The singing sound of that one, the sound of whose bow-string caused tremble to his enemies, is now courted by only delightful women.

sn: किरीटं सूर्यसंकाशं यस्य मूर्धन्यशोभत। वेणीविकृतकेशान्तः सोऽयमद्य धनंजयः॥
en: That Dhananjaya, whose head was decked with a diadem of solar effulgence, is now appearing with braids ending in ugly curls.

sn: तं वेणीकृतकेशान्तं भीमधन्वानमर्जुनम्। कन्यापरिवृतं दृष्ट्वा भीम सीदति मे मनः॥
en: O Bhima, seeing that mighty wielder of bow, Arjuna, with braids ending in ugly curls and surrounded by damsels, my heart is stricken with distress.

sn: यस्मिन्नस्त्राणि दिव्यानि समस्तानि महात्मनि। आधारः सर्वविद्यानां स धारयति कुण्डले॥
en: That high-souled one, to whom all the celestials weapons are known, and who is the repository of all the sciences, is now wearing a pair of ear-rings.

sn: स्प्रष्टुं राजसहस्राणि तेजसाप्रतिमानि वै। समरे नाभ्यवर्तन्त वेलामिव महार्णवः॥ सोऽयं राज्ञो विराटस्य कन्यानां नर्तको युवा। आस्ते वेषप्रतिच्छन्नः कन्यानां परिचारकः॥
en: That youthful one, whom myriads of kings of matchless prowess could not overcome in fight, even as the great ocean cannot overleap its banks, is now the dancing master of the daughters of king Virata and passes his days in disguise as one in the capacity of a servant to them.

sn: यस्य स्म रथघोषेण समकम्पत मेदिनी। सपर्वतवना भीम सहस्थावरजङ्गमा।॥ यस्मिट्ठाते महाभागे कुन्त्याः शोको व्यनश्यता स शोचयति मामद्य भीमसेन तवानुजः॥
en: O Bhima, that exalted younger brother of yours, the rattling sound of whose car-wheels made the entire earth with all her mountains and forests and with all things mobile and immobile, tremble, and O Bhimasena, who being born, all the grief's of Kunti vanished, now causes me to lament for him.

sn: भूषितं तमलंकारैः कुण्डलैः परिहाटकैः। कम्बुपाणिनमायान्तं दृष्ट्वा सीदति मे मनः॥
en: Beholding him approaching me adorned with golden ear-rings and other ornaments and with wrists with bracelets of conches, my heart sinks into sorrow.

sn: यस्य नास्ति समो वीर्ये कश्चिदुर्व्या धनुर्धरः। सोऽद्य कन्यापरिवृतो गायन्नास्ते धनंजयः॥
en: That Dhananjaya, to whom there is no bowman on the entire earth, equal in prowess, is now passing his days in singing surrounded by women.

sn: धर्मे शौर्ये च सत्ये च जीवलोकस्य सम्मतम्। स्त्रीवेषविकृतं पार्थं दृष्ट्वा सीदति मे मनः॥
en: Beholding that son of Pritha honored to the world for virtue, prowess and truthfulness, now living in the hated guise of a woman, my heart sinks into sorrow.

sn: यदा ह्येनं परिवृतं कन्याभिर्देवरूपिणम्। प्रभिन्नमिव मातङ्गं परिकीर्णं करेणुभिः॥ मत्स्यमर्थपतिं पार्थं विराटं समुपस्थितम्। पश्यामि तूर्यमध्यस्थं दिशो नश्यन्ति मे तदा॥
en: When I look upon that good-like Partha surrounded by females in this music hall like an elephant of rent temples encircled by sheelephant before Virata, the king of the Matsyas, then all the cardinal points seem to me to have lost their existence.

sn: नूनमार्या न जानाति कृच्छ्रे प्राप्तं धनंजयम्। अजातशत्रु कौरव्यं मग्नं दुर्दूतदेविनम्॥
en: Surely my mother-in-law does not know Dhananjaya sorely distressed with sorrow; nor does she know the descendant of Kuru, Ajatashatru, addicted to vicious gambling thus sunk in misery.

sn: तथा दृष्ट्वा यवीयांसं सहदेवं गवां पतिम्। गोषु गोवेषमायान्तं पाण्डुभूतास्मि भारत॥
en: 0 Bharata, beholding Sahadeva, the youngest of you all, in the capacity of a protector of kine and in the guise of a cowherd, I grow pale.

sn: सहदेवस्य वृत्तानि चिन्तयन्ती पुनः पुनः। न निद्रामभिगच्छामि भीमसेन कुतो रतिम्॥
en: Thinking over and over of Sahadeva's office I cannot obtain sleep what to speak of rest?

sn: न विन्दामि महाबाहो सहदेवस्य दुष्कृतम्। यस्मिन्नेववंविधं दुःखं प्राप्नुयात् सत्यविक्रमः॥
en: 0 mighty-armed one, I know not of Sahadeva's sin for which that one of unfailing prowess suffers thus.

sn: दूयामि भरतश्रेष्ठ दृष्ट्वा ते भ्रातरं प्रियम्। गोषु गोवृषसंकाशं मत्स्येनाभिनिवेशितम्॥
en: O foremost of the Bharata's beholding the beloved brother of yours, the foremost of men, appointed by the king of the Matsyas in looking after his kine, I feel grieved.

sn: संरब्धं रक्तनेपथ्यं गोपालानां पुरोगमम्। विराटमभिनन्दन्तमथ मे भवति ज्वरः॥
en: Beholding that hero clad in red garments, busy in gratifying Virata and posing himself at the head of the cowherds, fever comes on me.

sn: सहदेवं हि मे वीर नित्यमार्या प्रशंसति। महाभिजनसम्पन्नः शीलवान् वृत्तवानिति॥
en: My mother-in-law always speaks of that heroic Sahadeva as one possessed of high reputation, good character and excellent conduct.

sn: ह्रीनिषेवो मधुरवाकधार्मिकश्च प्रियश्च मे। स तेऽरण्येषु वोढव्यो याज्ञसेनि क्षपास्वपि॥ सुकुमारश्च शूरच राजानं चाप्यनुव्रतः। ज्येष्ठापचायिनं वीरं स्वयं पाज्ञालि भोजये:।३९॥ इत्युवाच हि मां कुन्ती रुदती पुत्रगृद्धिनी। प्रव्रजन्तं महारण्यं तं परिष्वज्य तिष्ठती॥
en: Kunti, greatly attached to her sons, stood weeping with Sahadeva in her arms, while he was starting (with us) for the great forest and addressed me thus-"Sahadeva is bashful, sweet-voiced, virtuous, and very dear to me, therefore, Yajnaseni cheer him up while he feels dejected and tend him in the forest, day and night. He is tender and brave, devoted to the king, heroic and always respectful to his elder brother; O Panchali, feed him yourself."

sn: तं दृष्ट्वा व्यापृतं गोषु वत्सचर्मक्षपाशयम्। सहदेवं युधां श्रेष्ठं किं नु जीवामि पाण्डव।॥
en: Beholding that Sahadeva, the best of warriors, engaged in tending kine and lying on calf skins at night, O Pandava, how can I live?

sn: यस्त्रिभिनित्यसम्पन्नो रूपेणास्त्रेण मेधया। सोऽश्वबन्धो विराटस्य पश्य कालस्य पर्ययम्॥
en: Again that one, who is gifted with the three attributes of beauty, arms and intellect, is now tending the steed of Virata. Lo! how times change!

sn: अभ्यकीर्यन्त वृन्दानि दामग्रन्थिमुदीक्ष्य तम्। विनयन्तं जवेनाश्वान् महाराजस्य पश्यतः॥
en: Granthika, at whose presence hostile forces ran away from the field of battle, is now engaged in training horses before the king driving them with speed.

sn: अपश्यमेनं श्रीमन्तं मत्स्यं भ्राजिष्णुमुत्तमम्। विराटमुपतिष्ठन्तं दर्शयन्तं च वाजिनः॥
en: I now see that graceful one wait upon the richly dressed and excellent Virata, the king of the Matsya's and make a show of his horses before the king.

sn: किं नु मां मन्यसे पार्थ सुखिनीति परंतप। एवं दुःखशताविष्टा युधिष्ठिरनिमित्ततः॥
en: O Pritha's son, afflicted with hundreds of sorrows on account of Yudhishthira, do you deem me happy, O repressor of foes.

sn: अतः प्रतिविशिष्टानि दुःखान्यन्यानि भारत। वर्तन्ते मयि कौन्तेय वक्ष्यामि शृणु तान्यपि॥
en: O Bharata, there are various other woes greater than these which I am afflicted with; listen, O son of Kunti, I shall relate tell them all to you.

sn: युष्मासु ध्रियमाणेषु दुःखानि विविधान्युत। शोषयन्ति शरीरं मे किं नु दुःखमतः परम्॥
en: Alas, you being all alive these various woes (render my person emaciated) undermine my system; what can be sadder than this?

sn: द्रौपद्युवाच अहं सैरन्ध्रवेषेण चरन्ती राजवेश्मनि। शौचदास्मि सुदेष्णाया अक्षधूर्तस्य कारणात्॥
en: Draupadi said Alas, on account of that one skilled in gambling I am under Sudeshna's command, dwelling in the palace in the guise of a Sairandhri.

sn: विक्रियां पश्य मे तीव्रां राजपुत्र्याः परंतप। आत्मकालमुदीक्षन्ती सर्वं दुःखं किलान्तवत्।।२।
en: O repressor of foes, princess as I am, see what pitiful change has come upon me I am living in expectation of a hopeful future, but my misery has reached its extremity.

sn: अनित्या किल मानामर्थसिद्धिर्जयाजयौ। इति कृत्वा प्रतीक्षामि भर्तृणामुदयं पुनः॥
en: Accomplishment of purposes and victory and defeat with regard to mortals are of short duration. Thinking this, I am expecting the return of prosperity to my husbands.

sn: चक्रवत्परिवर्तन्ते ह्याश्च व्यसनानि च। इति कृत्वा प्रतीक्षामि भर्तृणामुदयं पुनः॥
en: Like a wheel prosperity and adversity revolve. Thinking this, I am expecting the return of prosperity to my husbands.

sn: य एव हेतुर्भवति पुरुषस्य जयावहः। पराजये च हेतुश्च स इति प्रतिपालये। किं मां न प्रतिजानीषे भीमसेन मृतामिव॥
en: That which becomes a cause of a man's victory may become the cause of his defeat as well. I live in that hope.

sn: दत्त्वा याचन्ति पुरुषा हत्वा वध्यन्ति चापरे। पातयित्वा च पात्यन्ते परैरिति च मे श्रुतम्॥ न दैवस्यातिभारोऽस्ति न चैवास्यातिवर्तनम्। इति चाप्यागमं भूयो दैवस्य प्रतिपालये॥
en: O Bhimasena, why do you not consider me as dead? I am told that persons that give may beg, persons that slaughter may be slaughtered by others, and that persons that ever throw others may be over-thrown by enemies. There is nothing difficult for destiny nor can any one over-rule destiny.

sn: स्थितं पूर्वं जलं यत्र पुनस्तत्रैव गच्छति। इति पर्यायमिच्छन्ती प्रतीक्षे उदयं पुनः॥
en: It is with this hope, I am expecting the return of favorable fortune; once before where there was water, there comes it back again. Hoping for this change, I am awaiting the return of prosperity.

sn: दैवेन किल यस्यार्थ: सुनीतोऽपि विपद्यते। दैवस्य चागमे यत्नस्तेन कार्यो विजानता॥
en: When a man's business, although brought into a stage of completion, is seen to be endangered then a wise man should strive hard for the getting of good fortune.

sn: यत् तु मे वचनस्यास्य कथितस्य प्रयोजनम्। पृच्छ मां दु:खितां तत्त्वं पृष्टा चात्र ब्रवीमि ते॥
en: Immersed as I am in grief, whether you ask me or not I shall tell you in detail, the purpose of these words now spoken by me.

sn: महिषी पाण्डुपुत्राणां दुहिता दुपदस्य च। इमामवस्थां सम्प्राप्ता मदन्या का जिजीविषेत्॥
en: Queen of the sons of Pandu, and daughter of Drupada, who else but me wishes to live, having been reduced to such a plight?

sn: कुरून् परिभवेत् सर्वान् पञ्चालानपि भारत। पाण्डवेयांश्च सम्प्राप्तो मम क्लेशो ह्यरिंदम॥
en: () repressor of foes, this my misery surely brings humiliation, O Bharata, on all the Kurus, the Panchalas and the Pandavas.

sn: भ्रातृभिः श्वशुरैः पुत्रैर्बहुभिः परिवारिता। एवं समुदिता नारी का त्वन्या दुःखिता भवेत्॥
en: Being surrounded by numerous brothers, father-in-law and sons and thus having ample cause for rejoicing what other woman but myself has become so miserable?

sn: नूनं हि बालया धातुर्मया वै विप्रियं कृतम्। यस्य प्रसादाद् दुर्नीतं प्राप्तास्मि भरतर्षभ॥
en: O foremost of the Bharata race, certainly in my childhood I did some wrongful act to Dhata and through his displeasure I have fallen into such a woeful plight.

sn: वर्णावकाशमपि मे पश्य पाण्डव यादृशम्। तादृशो मे न तत्रासीद् दुःखे परमके तदा॥
en: Behold, O son of Pandu, the paleness of my complexion which even in the extremely miserable life in the forest could not come over me.

sn: त्वमेव भीम जानीषे यन्मे पार्थ सुखं पुरा। साहं दासीत्वमापन्ना न शान्तिमवशा लभे॥
en: O Pritha's son, it is you alone that know what happiness had I in my former days, O Bhima; even I, who was thus circumstance, have now sunk in slavery: paralysed in grief I cannot obtain rest.

sn: नादैविकमहं मन्ये यत्र पार्थो धनंजयः। भीमधन्वा महाबाहुरास्ते छन्न इवानलः॥
en: As the mighty-armed and terrible bowman Dhananjaya, the son of Pritha, lives here, like a fire covered over by ashes, then must I think that all these actions are due to Destiny.

sn: अशक्या वेदितुं पार्थ प्राणिनां वै गतिर्नरैः। विनिपातमिमं मन्ये युष्माकं ह्यविचिन्तिततम्॥
en: O son of Pritha, it is not possible for people to understand the destiny of creatures. Therefore this your downfall, I think, could not have been thwarted by fore-thought.

sn: यस्या मम मुखप्रेक्षा यूयमिन्द्रसमाः सदा। सा प्रेक्षे मुखमन्यासामवराणां वरा सती॥
en: Alas, she who has you all resembling Indra always to look after her comforts, even that one, who is so chaste and bears so lofty a station in life, is ministering to the comforts of others who are far below in rank to her.

sn: पश्य पाण्डव मेऽवस्थां यथा नार्हामि वै तथा। युष्मासु ध्रियमाणेषु पश्य कालस्य पर्ययम्॥
en: Though all of you are alive, behold O Pandava, my plight. It is such as is quite undeserving of me. Lo! how times change.

sn: यस्याः सागरपर्यन्ता पृथिवी वशवर्तिनी। आसीत् साद्य सुदेष्णाया भीताहं वशवर्तिनी॥
en: Alas! she, who had the entire earth as far as the verge of the sea under her command, is now living in fear of Sudeshna and in subjugation to her. a

sn: यस्याः पुरःसरा आसन् पृष्ठतश्चानुगामिनः। साहमद्य सुदेष्णायाः पुरः पश्चाच्च गामिनी॥ इदं तु दुःखं कौन्तेय ममासा निबोध तत्।
en: Even she, who had number of dependents to walk both in van and rear, is now walking before and behind Sudeshna. O Kunti's son, listen to another grief of mine; it is unbearable to me.

sn: या न जातु स्वयं पिंपे गात्रोद्वर्तनमात्मनः। अन्यत्र कुन्त्या भद्रं ते सा पिनष्यद्य चन्दनम्॥
en: Even she, who had never pounded unguents for herself except for Kunti, has been now pounding the sandal (for others) O! let good betide you.

sn: पश्य कौन्तेय पाणी मे नैवाभूतां हि यौ पुरा। इत्यस्य दर्शयामास किणवन्तौ करावुभौ॥
en: O Kunti's son, behold these hands of mine, they were not so before.” Saying this she showed both of her hands marked with corns.

sn: विभेमि कुन्त्या या नाहं युष्माकं वा कदाचन। साद्याग्रतो विराटस्य भीता तिष्ठामि किङ्करी॥
en: Even that one, who had never feared Kunti nor any of you, now stays a slave in fear before Virata,

sn: किं नु वक्ष्यति सम्राण्मां वर्णकः सुकृतो न वा। नान्यपिष्टं हि मत्स्यस्य चन्दनं किल रोचते॥
en: (Always do I remain in fear thinking) what the king of kings will say to me as about the unguents if they are not well pounded; because the king of the Matsya's does not like the sandal pounded by others.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच सा कीर्तयन्ती दुःखानि भीमसेनस्य भामिनी। सरोद् शनकैः कृष्णा भीमसेनमुदीक्षती॥
en: Vaishampayana said Narrating her woes to Bhimasena, O Bharata, the lady Krishna wept silently with her glance fixed on Bhimasena.

sn: सा वाष्पकलया वाचा निःश्वसन्ती पुनः पुनः। हृदयं भीमसेनस्य घयन्तीदमब्रवीत्॥
en: She, with words tremulous with tears, and sighing repeatedly addressed Bhimasena thus powerfully moving his heart.

sn: नाल्पं कृतं मया भीम देवानां किल्बिषं पुरा। अभाग्या यत्र जीवामि कर्तव्ये सति पाण्डव॥
en: O Bhima, surely had I committed many sinful acts to gods in my former days. Unfortunate as I am, I am still alive, my death is preferable to me, O Pandava.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततस्तस्याः करौ सूक्ष्मौ किणबद्धौ वृकोदरः। मुखमानीय वै पल्या रुरोद परवीरहा॥
en: Then Vrikodara the slayer of hostile heroes, covering his face with the delicate hands of his wife, marked with scars, began to weep.

sn: तौ गृहीत्वा च कौन्तेयो बाष्पमुत्सृज्य वीर्यवान्। ततः परमदुःखार्त इदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: The powerful son of Kunti, having held both of her hands in his own, began to shed tears, and stricken with great woe spoke the following.

description: The conversation between Bhima and Draupadi
sn: भीमसेन उवाच धिगस्तु मे बाहुबलं गाण्डीवं फाल्गुनस्य च। यत् ते रक्तौ पुरा भूत्वा पाणी कृतकिणाविमौ॥
en: Bhima said Fie to the strength of my arms and fie to the Gandiva of Phalguni, since these your hands red before have now become marked with scars.

description: The conversation between Bhima and Draupadi
sn: सभायां तु विराटस्य करोमि कदनं महत्। तत्र मे कारणं भाति कौन्तेयो यत् प्रतीक्षते॥
en: I would have caused a great havoc in the court of Virata but the son of Kunti looked at me (by way of forbidding); that was the reason of my forbearance.

description: The conversation between Bhima and Draupadi
sn: अथवा कीचकस्याहं पोथयामि पदा शिरः। ऐश्वर्यमदमत्तस्य क्रीडन्निव महाद्विपः॥
en: Or like a mighty elephant I would have easily crushed with a single kick the head of Kichaka intoxicated with the pride of wealth.

description: The conversation between Bhima and Draupadi
sn: अपश्यं त्वां यदा कृष्णे कीचकेन पदा हताम्। तदैवाहं चिकीर्षामि मत्स्यानां कदनं महत्॥
en: O Krishna, when I saw you kicked by Kichaka, I intended the very moment to bring about a great devastation of the whole of the Matsya's.

description: The conversation between Bhima and Draupadi
sn: तत्र मां धर्मराजस्तु कटाक्षेण न्यवारयत्। तदहं तस्य विज्ञाय स्थित एवास्मि भामिनि॥
en: But the lord of justice forbade me by a glance, O beautiful one; knowing his intention I desisted from the purpose and kept quiet.

description: The conversation between Bhima and Draupadi
sn: यच्च राष्ट्रात् प्रच्यवनं कुरूणामवधश्च यः। सुयोधनस्य कर्णस्य शकुनेः सौबलस्य च॥ दुःशासनस्य पापस्य यन्मया नाहृतं शिरः। तन्मे दहति गात्राणि हृदि शल्यमिवार्पितम्। मा धर्मं जहि सुश्रोणि क्रोधं जहि महामते॥
en: That we have been expelled from our kingdom, that I have not yet killed the Kurus, and that I have not yet taken the heads of Suyodhana, Karna, Shakuni the son of Subala the sinful Duryodhana, have been scorching every limb of mine and causing pain to my heart as if a peg is thrust into it.

description: The conversation between Bhima and Draupadi
sn: इमं तु समुपालम्भं त्वत्तो राजा युधिष्ठिरः। शृणुयाद्वापि कल्याणि कृत्स्नं जह्यात्स जीवितम्॥
en: O you beautiful, do not give up virtue; O noble minded lady, renounce your wrath. O auspicious one, if king Yudhishthira hears from you such rebukes, he is sure to give up his life.

description: The conversation between Bhima and Draupadi
sn: धनंजयो वा सुश्रोणि यमौ वा तनुमध्यमे। लोकान्तरगतेष्वेषु नाहं शक्ष्यामि जीवितुम्॥
en: O slender-waisted lady of beautiful hips, if Dhananjaya or the twins hear you speak thus, they will surely put an end to their lives; and they having given up life I shall not be able to keep up my own.

description: The conversation between Bhima and Draupadi
sn: पुरा सुकन्या भार्या च भार्गवं च्यवनं वने। वल्मीकभूतं शाम्यन्तमन्वपद्यत भामिनी॥
en: In days of yore, the body of sage Chyavana had turned into a termite like feature due to incessant and long term penance. It seemed that the camp of his life will shortly cease illumine, yet his wife Sukanya did not show any way negligence towards him and kept on serving

description: The conversation between Bhima and Draupadi
sn: नारायणी चेन्द्रसेना रूपेण यदि ते श्रुता। पतिमन्वचरद् वृद्धं पुरा वर्षसहस्रिणम्॥
en: In olden days, perhaps you may have heard that Indrasena, who resembled Narayani in beauty, followed her old husband or a thousand years of age.

description: The conversation between Bhima and Draupadi
sn: दुहिता जनकस्यापि वैदेही यदि ते श्रुता। पतिमन्वचरत् सीता महारण्यनिवासिनम्॥
en: You may have heard that Janaka's daughter Sita, the princess of Videha, went in the wake of her lord while he was dwelling in a great dreary forest.

description: The conversation between Bhima and Draupadi
sn: रक्षसा निग्रहं प्राप्य रामस्य महिषी प्रिया। क्लिश्यमानापि सुश्रोणि राममेवान्वपद्यत॥
en: That lady of beautiful hips, the beloved queen of Rama, although she received a great calamity at the hands of the Rakshasas and was afflicted with woe, was at length reunited with Rama.

description: The conversation between Bhima and Draupadi
sn: लोपामुद्रा तथा भीरु वयोरूपसमन्विता। अगस्तिमन्वयाद्धित्वा कामान् सर्वानमानुषान्॥
en: O excellent one, Lopamudra also, endued with youth and beauty, followed her lord Agastya, renouncing all objects of enjoyments hardly to be attained by men.

description: The conversation between Bhima and Draupadi
sn: धुमत्सेनसुतं वीरं सत्यवन्तमनिन्दिता। सावित्र्यनुचचारैका यमलोकं मनस्विनी॥
en: The noble-minded lady of spotless beauty, Savitri, followed the heroic Satyavana, the son of Dyumatsena, alone into the reign of death.

description: The conversation between Bhima and Draupadi
sn: यथैताः कीर्तिता नार्यो रूपवत्यः पतिव्रताः। तथा त्वमपि कल्याणि सर्वैः समुदिता गुणैः॥
en: As these beautiful and chaste ladies are described by me, so also, by you, O auspicious one, appear endued with every virtue.

description: The conversation between Bhima and Draupadi
sn: मादीर्घ क्षम कालं त्वं मासधर्मं च सम्मितम्। पूर्णे त्रयोदशे वर्षे राज्ञां राज्ञी भविष्यसि॥
en: Wait a short whole more that is measured by a half month, when the thirteenth year is full and you shall become the empress.

description: The conversation between Bhima and Draupadi
sn: द्रौपद्युवाच आर्तयैतन्मया भीम कृतं बाष्पप्रमोचनम्। अपारयन्त्या दुःखानि न राजानमुपालभे॥
en: Draupadi said O Bhima, I am unable to endure my griefs; it is out of sheer grief, I have shed these tears, I do not rebuke the king (Yudhishthira).

description: The conversation between Bhima and Draupadi
sn: किमुक्तेन व्यतीतेन भीमसेन महाबल। प्रत्युपस्थितकालस्य कार्यस्यानन्तरो भव॥
en: O Bhimsena, what is the use of dwelling on what is passed. Be ready for the present.

description: The conversation between Bhima and Draupadi
sn: ममेह भीम कैकेयी रूपाभिभवशङ्कया। नित्यमुद्विजते राजा कथं नेयादिमामिति॥
en: O Bhima, Kaikeyi, fearing that the king might take a fancy for me for my beauty, tries how to send me away from this place.

description: The conversation between Bhima and Draupadi
sn: तस्या विदित्वा तं भावं स्वयं चानृतदर्शनः। कीचकोऽयं सुदुष्टात्मा सदा प्रार्थयते हि माम्॥
en: Understanding her intention, that wickedsouled Kichaka of sinful conduct, always solicits me himself.

description: The conversation between Bhima and Draupadi
sn: तमहं कुपिता भीम पुनः कोपं नियम्य च। अब्रुवं कामसम्मूढमात्मानं रक्ष कीचक॥ गन्धर्वाणमहं भार्या पञ्चानां महिषी प्रिया। ते त्वां निहन्युः कुपिताः शूराः साहसकारिणः॥
en: O Bhima, getting enraged with him and then again suppressing my anger I said to Kichaka, rendered senseless by lust in the following words)-0Kichaka save yourself; I am the dear queen and wife of five Gandharvas; those heroes if enraged will kill you who are going to act so rashly.”

description: The conversation between Bhima and Draupadi
sn: एवमुक्तः सुदुष्टात्मा कीचकः प्रत्युवाच ह। नाहं बिभेमि सैरन्ध्र गन्धर्वाणां शुचिस्मिते॥
en: Thus addressed, the wicked-souled Kichaka answered, saying “O Sairandhri of beautiful smile, I am never afraid of the Gandharvas.

description: The conversation between Bhima and Draupadi
sn: शतं शतसहस्राणि गन्धर्वाणामहं रणे। समागतं हनिष्यामि त्वं भीरु कुरु मे क्षणम्॥
en: I will do away with a hundred thousand Gandharvas in battle, O timid one, give me your consent."

description: The conversation between Bhima and Draupadi
sn: इत्युक्ते चाब्रुवं मत्तं कामातुरमहं पुनः। न त्वं प्रतिबलश्चैषां गन्धर्वाणां यशस्विनाम्॥
en: Thus replied to, I addressed again that lust stricken Suta saying, "you are no rival to those illustrious Gandharvas.

description: The conversation between Bhima and Draupadi
sn: धर्मे स्थितास्मि सततं कुलशीलसमन्विता। नेच्छामि कंचिद् वध्यन्तं तेन जीवसि कीचक॥
en: Born of a noble family and endued with good disposition, do I even regard virtue as my stay and never wish for the death of any one. O Kichaka, therefore you live still.

description: The conversation between Bhima and Draupadi
sn: एवमुक्तः स दुष्टात्मा प्राहसत् स्वनवत् तदा। अथ मां तत्र कैकेयी प्रेषयत् प्रणयेन तु॥ तेनैव देशिता पूर्वं भ्रातृप्रियचीकीर्पया। सुरामानय कल्याणि कीचकस्य निवेशनात्॥
en: Thus addressed, that wicked-souled Kichaka burst out into a loud laughter. Then Kaikeyi, out of affection for her brother, and previously urged by him and having a mind to do good to him, sent me to Kichaka saying, “O auspicious one, bring wine from Kichaka's house."

description: The conversation between Bhima and Draupadi
sn: सूतपुत्रस्तु मां दृष्ट्वा महत् सान्त्वमवर्तयत्। सान्त्वे प्रतिहते क्रुद्धः परामर्शमनाभवत्।॥
en: Beholding me, the Suta's son began to court me in sweet words; when his court failed, he became enraged and attempted to use violence on me.

description: The conversation between Bhima and Draupadi
sn: विदित्वा तस्य संकल्पं कीचकस्य दुरात्मनः। तथाहं राजशरणं जवेनैव प्रधाविता॥
en: Having understood the intention of that wicked-souled Kichaka, I ran with speed to the royal protection.

description: The conversation between Bhima and Draupadi
sn: संदर्शने तु मां राज्ञः सूतपुत्रः परामृशत्। पातयित्वा तु दुष्टात्मा पदाहं तेन ताडिता॥
en: In the presence of the king, I was thrown down on the ground and kicked by the Suta's son of wicked soul.

description: The conversation between Bhima and Draupadi
sn: प्रेक्षते स्म विराटस्तु कङ्कस्तु बहवो जनाः। रथिनः पीठमर्दाश्च हस्त्यारोहाच नैगमाः॥ उपालब्धो मया राजा कङ्कश्चापि पुनः पुनः। ततो न वारितो राज्ञा न तस्याविनयः कृतः॥
en: This scene was witnessed by Virata, Kanka and many others, namely the charioteers, royal favorites, elephant riders, and merchants. Then he was neither prevented nor any punishment was inflicted on him by the king.

description: The conversation between Bhima and Draupadi
sn: योऽयं राज्ञो विराटस्य कीचको नाम सारथिः। त्यक्तधर्मा नृशंसश्च नरस्त्रीसम्मतः प्रियः॥
en: This very Kichaka is the principal ruler of the king Virata. He is devoid of virtue, cruel, favoured by the king and liked by women at large.

description: The conversation between Bhima and Draupadi
sn: शूरोऽभिमानी पापात्मा सर्वार्थेषु च मुग्धवान्। दारामर्शी महाभाग लभतेऽर्थान् बहूनपि॥
en: That wicked-souled Kichaka is war-like, proud, outrager of female modesty and engrossed in all objects of pleasure; O blessed one, he acquires plenty of money (from the king).

description: The conversation between Bhima and Draupadi
sn: आहरेदपि वित्तानि परेषां क्रोशतामपि। न तिष्ठति स्म सन्मार्गे न च धर्मं बुभूषति॥
en: He extorts money from others, even if they cry in woe; he never stays in paths of rectitude nor does he even feel inclined to virtue.

description: The conversation between Bhima and Draupadi
sn: पापात्मा पापभावश्च कामबाणवशानुगः। अविनीतश्च दुष्टात्मा प्रत्याख्यातः पुनः पुनः॥ दर्शने दर्शने हन्याद् यदि जह्यां च जीवितम्। तद् धर्मे यतमानानां महान् धर्मो नशिष्यति॥
en: He is wicked-souled, of sinful disposition, impudent, villaneous and afflicted by Cupid's shaft. Although I have repeatedly rejected him, he will, I am sure, outrage me, whenever he happens to see me, and then I shall surely give up my life; although you are striving to acquire that virtue but on my death, surely you will lose that great one.

description: The conversation between Bhima and Draupadi
sn: समयं रक्षमाणानां भार्या वो न भविष्यति। भार्यायां रक्ष्यमाणायां प्रजा भवति रक्षिता॥
en: You, who are trying to keep your pledge, will lose your wife; wife being protected, one's offspring will be protected.

description: The conversation between Bhima and Draupadi
sn: प्रजायां रक्ष्यमाणायामात्मा भवति रक्षितः। आत्मा हि जायते तस्यां तेन जायां विदुर्बुधाः॥
en: Offspring being protected, soul is saved. In a wife one's own self is begotten and it is therefore the wife is called Jaya by the wise.

description: The conversation between Bhima and Draupadi
sn: भर्ता तु भार्यया रक्ष्यः कथं जायान्ममोदरे। वदतां वर्णधर्माश्च ब्राह्मणानामिति श्रुतः॥
en: The wife should also protect the husband, thinking "How then can he take his birth in my womb?" I have heard it from Brahmanas, who are expert in expounding the duties of all orders.

description: The conversation between Bhima and Draupadi
sn: क्षत्रियस्य सदा धर्मो नान्यः शत्रुनिबर्हणात्। पश्यतो धर्मराजस्य कीचको मां पदावधीत्॥
en: There is no other duty of Kshatriyas but the repressing of their foes. Taking no notice of the presence of Dharmaraja, as well as of yours, O mighty Bhimasena, Kichaka kicked me.

description: The conversation between Bhima and Draupadi
sn: तव चैव समक्षे वै भीमसेन महाबल। त्वया ह्यहं परित्राता तस्माद् घोराज्जटासुरात्॥ जयद्रथं तथैव त्वमजैषीर्धातृभिः सह। जहीममपि पापिष्ठं योऽयं मामवमन्यते॥
en: It was you that rescued me from that terrible Jatasura, it was you only, who also with the help of your brothers, defeated Jayadratha. I entreat you to kill this wretch who has insulted me.

description: The conversation between Bhima and Draupadi
sn: कीचको राजवाल्लभ्याच्छोककृन्मम भारत। तमेवं कामसम्मत्तं भिन्धि कुम्भमिवाश्मनि॥
en: O Bharata, Kichaka, out of confidence that he is a favourite of the king, causes woe to me. I solicit you to crush this beloved one maddened with lust, even as an earthen pot dashed against a stone.

description: The conversation between Bhima and Draupadi
sn: यो निमित्तमनर्थानां बहूनां मम भारत। तं चेज्जीवन्तमादित्यः प्रातरभ्युदयिष्यति॥ विषमालोड्य पास्यामि मा कीचकवशं गमम्। श्रेयो हि मरणं मह्यं भीमसेन तवाग्रतः॥
en: If, O Bharata, the men make him rise up again in the morning living, who is the root of all these griefs of mine, I shall mix poison with some drink and swallow it up, but never shall I yield myself to the power of Kichaka. O Bhimasena, certainly death is preferable to me in the very sight of you.

description: The conversation between Bhima and Draupadi
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच इत्युक्त्वा प्रारुदत् कृष्णा भीमस्योर:समाश्रिता। भीमश्च तां परिष्वज्य महत् सान्त्वं प्रयुज्य च॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having said this, Krishna, lying on the breast of Bhima, began to weep. Having clasped her, Bhima also afforded her a great consolation.

description: The conversation between Bhima and Draupadi
sn: आश्वासयित्वा बहुशो भृशमा सुमध्यमाम्। हेतुतत्त्वार्थसंयुक्तैर्वचोभिर्दुपदात्मजाम्॥ प्रमृज्य वदनं तस्याः पाणिनाश्रुसमाकुलम्। कीचकं मनसागच्छत् सृक्किणी परिसंलिहन्। उवाच चैनां दुःखार्ती भीमः क्रोधसमन्वितः॥
en: Having consoled that greatly afflicted lady of slender waist in various ways, and having wiped with his hands her face flooded with tears, Bhima filled with ire, began to think of Kichaka in his mind, licking repeatedly the corners of his mouth with his tongue; and he addressed the daughter of Drupada afflicted with woe with words replete with reason.

sn: भीमसेन उवाच तथा भद्रे करिष्यामि यथा त्वं भीरु भाषसे। अद्य तं सूदयिष्यामि कीचकं सहबान्धवम्॥
en: Bhima said O gentle one, I will do that which you say. O timid one, I will kill Kichaka today with all his friends.

sn: अस्याः प्रदोषे शर्वर्याः कुरुष्वानेन संगतम्। दुःखं शोकं च निर्धूय याज्ञसेनि शुचिस्मिते॥
en: O Yagaseni of beautiful smile, having given up your sorrow and grief do so as will bring him on good terms with you on tomorrow's evening.

sn: यैषा नर्तनशालेह मत्स्यराजेन कारिता। दिवात्र कन्या नृत्यन्ति रात्रौ यान्ति यथागृहम्॥
en: There is the dancing house which the king of the Matsya's has caused to be built; there the girls dance during the day and retire to their respective homes at night.

sn: तत्रास्ति शयनं दिव्यं दृढाङ्गं सुप्रतिष्ठितम्। तत्रास्य दर्शयिष्यामि पूर्वप्रेतान् पितामहान्॥
en: In that hall there is a bedstead fixed firm and conveniently placed; there I will make him see the spirits of his deceased manes.

sn: यथा च त्वां न पश्येयुः कुर्वाणां तेन संविदम्। कुर्यास्तथा त्वं कल्याणि यथा संनिहितो भवेत्॥
en: In course of holding conversation with him, do such as others might not see you. O auspicious one, also manage in such a way as he might come near you.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तथा तौ कथयित्वा तु वाष्पमुत्सृज्य दुःखितौ। रात्रिशेषं तमत्युग्रं धारयामासतुर्हदि॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having thus held their mutual conversation, and shedding tears in grief, they both awaited the dawn of that night with an anxious heart.

sn: तस्यां रात्र्यां व्यतीतायां प्रातरुत्थाय कीचकः। गत्वा राजकुलायैव द्रौपदीमिदमब्रवीत्॥
en: That night being passed, Kichaka rose up in the morning, and having gone to the royal house, addressed Draupadi in the following terms.

sn: सभायां पश्यतो राज्ञः पातयित्वा पदाहनम्। न चैवालभसे त्राणमभिपन्ना बलीयसा॥
en: I hurled you down in the court and kicked you in the very presence of the king. Having fallen under the grasp of my mighty self you could not obtain deliverance.

sn: प्रवादेनेह मत्स्यानां राजा नाम्नायमुच्यते। अहमेव हि मत्स्यानां राजा वै वाहिनीपतिः॥
en: Virata is said to be the king of the Matsya's, but that is only in name; lord of the forces, it is I alone who am verily the king of the Matsya's.

sn: मां सुखं प्रतिपद्यस्व दासो भीरु भवामि ते। अह्नाय तव सुश्रोणि शतं निष्कान् ददाम्यहम्॥ दासीशतं च ते दद्यां दासानामपि चापरम्। रथं चाश्वतरीयुक्तमस्तु नौ भीरु संगमः॥
en: O timid one, accept me happily; I shall become your slave. O you of beautiful hips, I shall give you anon a hundred Nishkas and a hundred male and a hundred female servants. I shall also bestow on you cars yoked with mules; ( beautiful one, let us be united.

sn: द्रौपद्युवाच एवं मे समयं त्वद्य प्रतिपद्यस्व कीचका न त्वां सखा वा भ्राता वा जानीयात् संगतं मया।।१२। अनुप्रवादाद् भीतास्मि गन्धर्वाणां यशस्विनाम्। एवं मे प्रतिजानीहि ततोऽहं वशगा तव॥
en: Draupadi said O Kichaka, (I agree to this now, this is my condition, that you should accede to (do so); neither your friends nor your brothers may know that we are united. I am really afraid of the detection by those renowned Gandharvas. If you promise me this, I shall certainly be yours.

sn: कीचक उवाच एवमेतत् करिष्यामि यथा सुश्रोणि भाषसे। एको भद्रे गमिष्यामि शून्यमावसथं तव॥ समागमार्थ रम्भोरु त्वया मदनमोहितः। यथा त्वां नैव पस्येयुर्ग-धर्वा: सूर्यवर्चसः॥
en: Kichaka said O you of beautiful hips, I will do what you say; overcome by the god of love O gentle one, I shall go alone to your lonely abode for the purpose of being united with you, so that, O you of elegant thighs, the Gandharvas, as brilliant as the sun, might not be able to see you.

sn: द्रौपद्युवाच यदेतनर्तनागारं मत्स्यराजेन कारितम्। दिवात्र कन्या नृत्यन्ति रात्रौ यान्ति यथागृहम्॥
en: Draupadi said Behold there is the dancing hall erected by the king of the Matsya's. Here the girls dance during the day and retire to their respective homes at night.

sn: तमिस्र तत्र गच्छेथा गन्धर्वास्तन्न जानते। तत्र दोषः परिहतो भविष्यति न संशयः॥
en: Everywhere there surrounds darkness so, come to see me there. The Gandharvas do not know that place. No doubt, the vice too shall be removed by reason of meeting there,

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तमर्थमपि जल्पन्त्याः कृष्णायाः कीचकेन ह। दिवसाधु समभवन्मासेनैव समं नृप॥
en: Vaishampayana said O king, thinking of the conversation she had with Kichaka, that half day appeared to Krishna as long as a whole month.

sn: कीचकोऽथ गृहं गत्वा भृशं हर्षपरिप्लुतः। सैरन्ध्रीरूपिणं मूढो मृत्युं तं नावबुद्धवान्॥
en: Thereupon she again informed Bhimasena of his conduct; Kichaka too, going to his house, was filled with joy.

sn: गन्धाभरणमाल्येषु व्यासक्तः सविशेषतः। अलंचक्रे तदाऽऽत्मानं सत्वरः काममोहितः॥
en: That stupid could not understand that his death was in the shape of Sairandhri and he became especially busy with perfumeries, ornaments and garlands.

sn: तस्य तत् कुर्वतः कर्म कालो दीर्घ इवाभवत्। अनुचिन्तयतश्चापि तामेवायतलोचनाम्॥ आसीदभ्यधिका चापि श्रीः श्रियं प्रमुमुक्षतः। निर्वाणकाले दीपस्य वर्तीमिव दिधक्षतः॥
en: He, then possessed by lust adorned himself speedily. While he was doing this and thinking of the female with large eyes, the time appeared to him to be long; and the beauty which was about to forsake him, appeared to him to be increased,

sn: कृतसम्प्रत्ययस्तस्याः कीचकः काममोहितः। नाजानाद् दिवसं यान्तं चिन्तयानः समागमम्॥
en: Like the wick of a burning lamp at the time of its expiration. Placing perfect confidence in her, Kichaka, possessed by lust,

sn: ततस्तु द्रौपदी गत्वा तदा भीमं महानसे। उपातिष्ठत कल्याणी कौरव्यं पतिमन्तिकम्॥
en: Thinking of the meeting could not perceive that the day had passed away. Thereupon going to Bhima in the kitchen Draupadi.

sn: तमुवाच सुकेशान्ता कीचकस्य मया कृतः। संगमो नर्तनागारे यथावोचः परंतप॥ शून्यं स नर्तनागारमागमिष्यति कीचकः। एको निशि महाबाहो कीचकं तं निषूदय॥
en: Of auspiciousness, sat by his husband, the descendant of Kuru; that lady of beautiful hair said to him: “O slayer of foes, as directed by you, I have given Kichaka to understand that our meeting shall take place in the theatre hall. Kichaka shall come to that empty dancing-hall.

sn: तं सूतपुत्रं कौन्तेय कीचकं मददर्पितम्। गत्वा त्वं नर्तनागारं निर्जीवं कुरु पाण्डव।॥
en: Alone at night, O son of Kunti, slay him, that son of a Suta inflated with pride.

sn: दोश्च सूतपुत्रोऽसौ गन्धर्वानवमन्यते। तं त्वं प्रहरतां श्रेष्ठ ह्रदानागमिवोद्धर॥
en: O Pandava, going to that dancing hall, take his life. From pride only, that son of a Suta slights the Gandharvas.

sn: अश्रु दुःखाभिभूताया मम माजस्व भारत। आत्मनश्चैव भद्रं ते कुरु मानं कुलस्य च॥
en: O you the best of repressors, lift him up like (Krishna) lifting up the serpent from the lake. O Pandava, wipe my tears who am stricken with grief; may good betide you; save your own honor and that of your family.

sn: भीमसेन उवाच स्वागतं ते वरारोहे यन्मां वेदयसे प्रियम्। न ह्यन्यं कञ्चिदिच्छामि सहायं वरवर्णिनी॥
en: Bhimasena said O fair and timid lady, I shall do what you say, welcome, O fair damsel, you, who have communicated this pleasant news to me.

sn: या मे प्रीतिस्त्वयाऽऽख्याता कीचकस्य समागमे। हत्वा हिडिम्बं सा प्रीतिर्ममासीद् वरवर्णिनी॥ सत्यं भ्रातूंश्च धर्मं च पुरस्कृत्य ब्रवीमि ते। कीचकं निहनिष्यामि वृत्रं देवपतिर्यथा।॥
en: O beautiful lady, I do not wish to have any other help from you. My joy on hearing from you of my coming encounter with Kichaka is equal to what I felt when I slew Hidimba. I swear this by truth, morality and my brothers.

sn: तं गहरे प्रकाशे वा पोथयिष्यामि कीचकम्। अथ चेदपि योत्स्यन्ति हिंसे मत्स्यानपि ध्रुवम्॥
en: I shall slay Kichaka as did the king of the celestials Vritra; secretly or openly, I shall crush Kichaka.

sn: ततो दुर्योधनं हत्वा प्रतिपत्स्ये वसुन्धराम्। कामं मत्स्यमुपास्तां हि कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: If the Matsya's side with him, I shall kill them too; and then slaying Duryodhana, I shall regain the earth; let Kunti's son Yudhishthira continue to pay his homage to the king of the Matsya's.

sn: द्रौपद्युवाच यथा न संत्यजेथास्त्वं सत्यं वै मत्कृते विभो। निगूढस्त्वं तथा पार्थ कीचकं तं निषूदय॥
en: Draupadi said O lord, if you do not wish to transgress the pledge you have taken to me, you should, of Partha, slay Kichaka in secret.

sn: भीमसेन उवाच एवमेतत् करिष्यामि यथा त्वं भीरु भाषसे। अद्य तं सूदयिष्यामि कीचकं सह बान्धवैः॥
en: Bhimasena said O timid lady, I shall do what you say; I shall slay today Kichaka with his friends.

sn: अदृश्यमानस्तस्याथ तमस्विन्यामनिन्दिते। नागो बिल्वमिवाक्रम्य पोथयिष्याम्यहं शिरः। अलभ्यामिच्छतस्तस्य कीचकस्य दुरात्मनः॥
en: O you of faultless feature, hidden from the view of others in darkness, I shall crush, as an elephant crushes a Bel fruit, the head of the wicked Kichaka, who desires for a thing that cannot be acquired by him.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच भीमोऽथ प्रथमं गत्वा रात्रौ छन्न उपाविशत्। मृगं हरिरिवादृश्यः प्रत्याकाङ्क्षत कीचकम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Thereupon going there hidden at night, Bhima sat expecting Kichaka like a lion for deer.

sn: कीचकश्चाप्यलंकृत्य यथाकाममुपागमत्। तां वेलां नर्तनागारं पाञ्चालीसंगमाशया॥
en: Having adorned himself to his liking, Kichaka arrived at the dancing hall at the appointed hour with a view to meet Panchali.

sn: मन्यमानः स संकेतमागारं प्राविशच्च तत्। प्रविश्य च स तद् वेश्म तसमा संवृतं महत्॥ पूर्वागतं ततस्तत्र भीममप्रतिमौजसम्। एकान्तावस्थितं चैनमाससाद स दुर्मतिः॥
en: Considering this as sign, he entered there. Entering the hall enshrouded in darkness, that highly wicked one, came up to Bhima of unequalled prowess, who had gone there before and was waiting in a corner.

sn: शयानं शयने तत्र सूतपुत्रः परामृशत्। जाज्वल्यमानं कोपेन कृष्णाधर्षणजेन ह॥
en: Suta's son approached him who was lying on a bed, burning in anger begotten of the insult (offered to Krishna).

sn: उपसंगम्य चैवैनं कीचकः काममोहितः। हर्षोन्मथितचित्तात्मा स्मयमानोऽभ्यभाषत॥
en: Approaching him, Kichaka possessed by lust, having his heart filled with delight, smilingly said.

sn: प्रापितं ते मया वित्तं बहुरूपमनन्तकम्। यत् कृतं धनरत्नाढ्यं दासीशतपरिच्छदम्॥ रूपलावण्ययुक्ताभिर्युवतीभिरलंकृतम्। गृहं चान्तःपुरं सुभ्र क्रीडारतिविराजितम्। तत् सर्वं त्वां समुद्दिश्य सहसाहमुपागतः॥ अकस्मान्मां प्रशंसन्ति सदा गृहगताः स्त्रियः। सुवासा दर्शनीयश्च नान्योऽस्ति त्वादृशः पुमान्॥
en: I have already given to you immense and various wealth and for you a hundred maid servants, with riches and jems and finest robes; O you of air eye-brows, also a palace with inner apartment filled with beautiful, lovely and youthful maid servants and adorned with various sorts of sports and amusements. Having arranged all this, I have all on a sudden come here; the women of my house have begun to praise me, saying: 'There is none like you amongst all the people so well-dressed and beautiful.

sn: भीमसेन उवाच दिष्ट्या त्वं दर्शनीयोऽथ दिष्ट्याऽऽत्मानं प्रशंससि। ईदृशस्तु त्वया स्पर्शः स्पृष्टपूर्वो न कर्हिचित्॥
en: Bhimasena said By my good fortune, you are handsome and you are praising yourself; I think you had not before any such pleasurable touch.

sn: स्पर्श वेत्सि विदग्धस्त्वं कामधर्मविचक्षणः। स्त्रीणां प्रीतिकरो नान्यस्त्वत्समः पुरुषस्त्विह॥
en: I consider your touch as burning and you are an expert at gallantry. I do not see any other man like you favourite to women.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच इत्युक्त्वा तं महाबाहुर्भीमो भीमपराक्रमः। सहसोत्पत्य कौन्तेयः प्रहस्येदमुवाच ह॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having said this to him, and jumping up all on a sudden, the mighty-armed Bhima, the son of Kunti, endued with dreadful prowess, smilingly said.

sn: अद्य त्वां भगिनी पापं कृष्यमाणं मया भुवि। द्रक्ष्यतेऽद्रिप्रतीकाशं सिंहेनेव महागजम्॥
en: Your sister shall behold you, vile as you are, today drawn by me on earth, like a mighty elephant huge as a mountain dragged by another to the ground.

sn: निराबाधा त्वयि हते सैरन्ध्री विचरिष्यति। सुखमेव चरिष्यन्ति सैरन्ध्याः पतयः सदा॥
en: You being slain, Sairandhri shall wander unobstructed and we, her husbands, shall live happily.

sn: ततो जग्राह केशेषु माल्यवत्सु महाबलः। स केशेषु परामृष्टो बलेन बलिनां वरः॥ आक्षिप्य केशान् वेगेन बाह्वोर्जग्राह पाण्डवम्। बाहुयुद्धं तयोरासीत् क्रुद्धयोर्नरसिंहयोः॥
en: The highly powerful Bhima seized him by the hair which were adorned with garlands. Thus caught with force by the hair, that foremost of the powerful, speedily freed his hair and grasped the arms of Bhima. Then there arose a hand to hand fight between those who foremost of men worked up with anger.

sn: वसन्ते वासिताहेतोर्बलवद्गजयोरिव। कीचकानां तु मुख्यस्य नराणामुत्तमस्य च॥
en: The fight of Kichaka and the foremost of men was like that between two powerful elephants for one she-elephants in the season of spring,

sn: वालिसुग्रीवयोर्धात्रोः पुरेव कपिसिंहयोः। अन्योन्यमपि संरब्धौ परस्परजयैषिणौ॥
en: Or like what took place in the days of yore between the two leading monkeys the brothers Bali and Sugriva. Both equally enraged and desirous of victory,

sn: ततः समुद्यम्य भुजौ पञ्चशीर्षाविवोरगौ। नखदंष्ट्राभिरन्योन्यं घतः क्रोधविषोद्धतौ॥
en: They raised up their arms like two snakes having five hoods; and worked up with the poison of anger, they attacked each other with nails and teeth.

sn: वेगेनाभिहतो भीमः कीचकेन बलीयसा। स्थिरप्रतिज्ञः स रणे पदान्न चलितः पदम्॥
en: Being struck with great force by the powerful Kichaka, the resolute (Bhima) did not waver a step in the encounter.

sn: तावन्योन्यं समाश्लिष्य प्रकर्षन्तौ परस्परम्। उभावपि प्रकाशेते प्रवृद्धौ वृषभाविव॥
en: Then embracing and dragging each other, they appeared there like two powerful bulls.

sn: तयोासीत् सुतुमुलः सम्प्रहारः सुदारुणः। नखदन्तायुधवतोाघ्योरिव दृप्तयोः॥
en: They having nails and teeth for their weapon, there arose a fierce and great encounter between them like that between two maddened tigers.

sn: अभिपत्याथ बाहुभ्यां प्रत्यगृह्णादमर्षितः। मातङ्ग इव मातङ्गं प्रभिन्नकरटामुखम्॥
en: Throwing each other down with their arms and then again seizing in great anger, they fought like two elephants with rent temples.

sn: स चाप्येनं तदा भीमः प्रतिजग्राह वीर्यवान्। तमाक्षिपत् कीचकोऽथ बलेन बलिनां वरः॥
en: Then the powerful Bhima seized Kichaka, and Kichaka too, the foremost of the strong, again threw him down with force.

sn: तयोर्भुजविनिष्पेषादुभयोर्बलिनोस्तदा। शब्दः समभवद् घोरो वेणुस्फोटसमो युधि॥
en: Those two powerful (heroes) thus fighting, the crush of their arms engendered a sound resembling the clatter of splitting bamboo's.

sn: अथैनमाक्षिप्य बलाद् गृहमध्ये वृकोदरः। धूनयामास वेगेन वायुश्चण्ड इव दुमम्॥
en: Then throwing Kichaka down with great force in the room, Vrikodara tossed him about with velocity, as a hurricane tosses a tree.

sn: भीमेन च परामृष्टो दुर्बलो बलिना रणे। प्रास्पन्दत यथाप्राणं विचकर्ष च पाण्डवम्॥
en: Being thus assailed by the powerful Bhima in the encounter, he grew weak, trembled and tugged at the Pandava to his very best.

sn: ईषदाकलितं चापि क्रोधाद् दुतपदं स्थितम्। कीचको बलवान् भीमं जानुभ्यामाक्षिपद् भुवि॥
en: Making him waver a little, the powerful Kichaka speedily stuck Bhima on the breast with his knees and felled him on the ground.

sn: पातितो भुवि भीमस्तु कीचकेन बलीयसा। उत्पपाताथ वेगेन दण्डपाणिरिवान्तकः॥
en: Being thrown on the ground by the powerful Kichaka, Bhima rose up again with force, like Yama with mace in his hands.

sn: स्पर्धया च बलोन्मत्तौ तावुभौ सूतपाण्डवौ। निशीथे पर्यकर्षेतां बलिनौ निर्जने स्थले॥
en: Then both Suta and Pandava, maddened with their strength, challenged and grappled with each other at night in that secluded hall.

sn: ततस्तद् भवनं श्रेष्ठं प्राकम्पत मुहुर्मुहुः। बलवच्चापि संक्रुद्धावन्योन्यं प्रति गर्जतः॥
en: While enraged they were thus roaring at each other, that best of houses shook at every moment.

sn: तलाभ्यां स तु भीमेन वक्ष्स्यभिहतो बली। कीचको रोषसंतप्तः पदान्न चलितः पदम्॥
en: Slapped on the breast by the powerful Bhima, Kichaka worked up with anger, did not move for a single step.

sn: मुहूर्तं तु स तं वेगं सहित्वा भुवि दुःसहम्। बलादहीयत तदा सूतो भीमबलादितः॥
en: Bearing for a moment the force which is incapable of being borm on earth, Suta, belaboured by Bhima, grew enfeebled.

sn: तं हीयमानं विज्ञाय भीमसेनो महाबलः। वक्षस्थानीय वेगेन ममर्दैनं विचेतसम्॥
en: And seeing that he was growing weak, the highly powerful Bhimasena drawing him forcibly to his breast began to press him who was senseless.

sn: क्रोधाविष्टो विनिःश्वस्य पुनश्चैनं वृकोदरः। जग्राह जयतां श्रेष्ठः केशेष्वेव तदा भृशम्॥
en: Breathing hard again and again in anger, Vrikodara the foremost of the victorious held him up always by the hair.

sn: गृहीत्वा कीचकं भीमो विरराज महाबलः। शार्दूलः पिशिताकाक्षी गृहीत्वेव महामृगम्॥
en: Seizing Kichaka, the powerful Bhima began to roar like a hunger tiger that has slain a large animal.

sn: तत एनं परिश्रान्तमुपलभ्य वृकोदरः। योक्त्रयामास बाहुभ्यां पशुं रशनया यथा॥
en: Thereupon on serving him greatly exhausted, Vrikodara bound him fast with his arms like one binding a beast with a rope.

sn: नदन्तं च महानादं भिन्नभेरीसमस्वनम्। भ्रामयामास सुचिरं विस्फुरन्तमचेतसम्॥
en: Then Bhima began to whirl him who was senseless, for a considerable time, and he roared terribly like a discordant bugle.

sn: प्रगृह्य तरसा दोर्भ्यां कण्ठं तस्य वृकोदरः। अपीडयत कृष्णायास्तदा कोपोपशान्तये॥
en: Then to console Krishna, Vrikodara got hold of Kichaka's throat with his arms and began to squeeze it.

sn: अथ तं भग्नसर्वाङ्गं व्याविद्धनयनाम्बरम्। आक्रम्य च कटीदेशे जानुना कीचकाधमम्। अपीडयत बाहुभ्यां पशुमारममारयत्॥ तं विषीदन्तमाज्ञाय कीचकं पाण्डुनन्दनः। भूतले भ्रामयामास वाक्यं चेदमुवाच ह॥
en: Then striking with his knees the waist of that wretch of Kichaka, all whose limbs had been broken into pieces and whose eye-lids were closed, that descendant of Pandu killed him like one killing a beast. Then beholding Kichaka senseless,

sn: अद्याहमनृणो भूत्वा भ्रातुर्भार्यापहारिणम्। शान्तिं लब्धास्मि परमां हत्वा सैरन्ध्रकण्टकम्॥
en: He rolled him on earth and said: “Killing this wretch who has wished to ravish our wife, this thorn of Sairandhri, I am freed from the debt I owed to my brother and am in peace."

sn: स्तं कीचकं क्रोधसरागनेत्रः। मुद्धान्तनेत्रं व्यसुमुत्ससर्ज॥
en: Saying this, that foremost of men, with eyes reddened with ire, left off Kichaka, whose dress and ornaments had been thrown off his body, whose eyes were rolling and who was even then trembling.

sn: निष्पिष्य पाणिना पाणिं संदष्टौष्ठपुटं बली। समाक्रम्य च संक्रुद्धो बलेन बलिनां वरः॥ तस्य पादौ च पाणी च शिरो ग्रीवां च सर्वशः। काये प्रवेशयामास पशोरिव पिनाकधृक्॥
en: Squeezing his own hand and biting his lips in anger, that foremost of the powerful, attacked him with great force and thrust his arms, legs, neck and head into his body, as did the holder of Pinaka the beast.

sn: तं सम्मथितसर्वाङ्गं मांसपिण्डोपमं कृतम्। कृष्णाया दर्शयामास भीमसेनो महाबलः॥
en: The highly-powerful Bhimasena then showed him to Krishna; all his limbs were crushed and he was reduced into a ball of flesh.

sn: उवाच च महातेजा द्रौपदी योषितां वराम्। पश्यैनमेहि पाञ्चालि कामुकोऽयं यथा कृतः॥
en: Gifted with great energy (as he was) he said to Draupadi, that best of women “Behold, O Panchali, what I have done of this hurtful wretch."

sn: एवमुक्त्वा महाराज भीमो भीमपराक्रमः। पादेन पीडयामास तस्य कायं दुरात्मनः॥
en: Saying this, O king, Bhima, endued with dreadful prowess, struck with his foot the body of that vicious-souled one.

sn: ततोऽग्नि तत्र प्रज्वाल्य दर्शयित्वा तु कीचकम्। पाञ्चालीं स तदा वीर इदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Then lighting a lamp there and showing her Kichaka, that hero addressed the following to Panchali.

sn: प्रार्थयन्ति सुकेशान्ते ये त्वां शीलगुणान्विताम्। एवं ते भीरु वध्यन्ते कीचकः शोभते यथा॥
en: "O you of fair hair, O timid damsel, all those who seek you who are gifted with a good character and accomplishments, will be slain by me like this Kichaka."

sn: तत् कृत्वा दुष्करं कर्म कृष्णायाः प्रियमुत्तमम्। तथा स कीचकं हत्वा गत्वा रोषस्य वै शमम्॥
en: Performing that difficult work, highly pleasing to Krishna, and slaying Kichaka, his anger was pacified.

sn: आमन्त्र्य द्रौपदी कृष्णां क्षिप्रमायान्महानसम्। कीचकं घातयित्वा तु द्रौपदी योषितां वरा। प्रहृष्टा गतसंतापा सभापालानुवाच ह॥
en: Bidding farewell to Draupadi, he speedily went to the kitchen. Having brought about the destruction of Kichaka, Draupadi too, the foremost of females.

sn: कीचकोऽयं हतः शेते गन्धर्वैः पतिभिर्ममा परस्त्रीकामसम्मत्तस्तत्रागच्छत पश्यत॥
en: Delighted and having her grief removed, said to the guards of the assembly-hall; 'This Kichaka has been slain by my Gandharva husbands.

sn: तच्छ्रुत्वा भाषितं तस्या नर्तनागाररक्षिणः। सहसैव समाजग्मुरादायोल्काः सहस्रशः॥
en: He who desired for another's wife; come and see.” Hearing her words the guards of the assembly-hall.

sn: ततो गत्वाथ तद् वेश्म कीचकं विनिपातितम्। गतासुं ददृशुर्भूमौ रुधिरेण समुक्षितम्॥ पाणिपादविहीनं तु दृष्ट्वा च व्यथिताऽभवन्। निरीक्षन्ति ततः सर्वे परं विस्मयमागताः॥
en: Came there by thousands, with torches in their hands. And going to that room they saw Kichaka fallen on the ground lifeless, bathing in a pool of blood. Beholding him without arms and legs they were pained.

sn: अमानुषं कृतं कर्म तं दृष्ट्वा विनिपातितम्। क्वास्य ग्रीवा क्व चरणौ क्व पाणी क्व शिरस्तथा इति स्म तं परीक्षन्ते गन्धर्वेण हतं तदा॥
en: When they saw him they were struck with wonder. Seeing that super-human work of his destruction. (They said) : “Where is his neck, where are his feet, arms and where is his head.” They then concluded that he had been slain by the Gandharvas.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तस्मिन् काले समागम्य सर्वे तत्रास्य बान्धवाः। रुरुदुः कीचकं दृष्ट्वा परिवार्य समन्ततः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Coming there at that time and beholding Kichaka and surrounding him all sides his friends began to lament.

sn: सर्वे संहृष्टरोमाणः संत्रस्ताः प्रेक्ष्य कीचकम्। तथा सम्भिन्नसर्वाङ्गं कूर्म स्थल इवोद्भुतम्॥
en: Then beholding Kichaka with all his limbs mangled like a tortoise brought to the land, the hairs of their bodies siood erect and they were filled with fear.

sn: पोथितं भीमसेनेन तमिन्द्रेणेव दानवम्। संस्कारयितुमिच्छन्तो बहिर्नेतुं प्रचक्रमुः॥
en: Then seeing him crushed by Bhimasena like a Danava by Indra they tried to take him out side for performing his obsequial ceremonies.

sn: ददृशुस्ते ततः कृष्णां सूतपुत्राः समागताः। अदूराच्चानवद्याङ्गी स्तम्भमालिङ्गय तिष्ठतीम्॥
en: Then the assembled sons of Suta beheld Krishna of faultless features standing hard by reclining on a pillar.

sn: समवेतेषु सर्वेषु तामूचुरुपकीचकाः। हन्यतां शीघ्रमसती यत्कृते कीचको हतः॥
en: Amongst those assembled, some wicked Kichaka's exclaimed: "soon kill this unchaste woman for whom Kichaka has been slain.

sn: अथवा नैव हन्तव्या दह्यतां कामिना सह। मृतस्यापि प्रियं कार्यं सूतपुत्रस्य सर्वथा।॥
en: Or without slaying her, let us burn her, with him who desired to have her; for we should do by all means what was liked by the deceased son of a Suta."

sn: ततो विराटमूचुस्ते कीचकोऽस्याः कृते हतः। सहानेनाद्य दह्येम तदनुज्ञातुमर्हसि॥
en: Then they said to Virata: "For her, Kichaka has been slain; we shall burn her with him; it behoves you to give permission.”

sn: पराक्रमं तु सूतानां मत्वा राजान्वमोदत। सैरन्याः सूतपुत्रेण सह दाहं विशाम्पतिः॥
en: 0 King, knowing well the prowess of Sutas, he gave them permission to burn down Sairandhri with Suta's son.

sn: तां समासाद्य वित्रस्तां कृष्णां कमललोचनाम्। पोमुह्यमानां ते तत्र जगृहुः कीचका भृशम्॥
en: Then approaching terrified Krishna, stricken with stupor and having lotus eyes the Kichaka's caught hold of her violently.

sn: ततस्तु तां समारोप्य निबध्य च सुमध्यमाम्। जग्मुरुद्यम्य ते सर्वे श्मशानाभिमुखास्तदा॥
en: Then binding that youthful damsel and placing her upon the bier they started with great joy towards the cremation ground.

sn: ह्रियमाणा तु सा राजन् सूतपुत्रैरनिन्दिता। प्राक्रोशन्नाथमिच्छन्ती कृष्णा नाथवती सती॥
en: Being thus carried away by the sons of Suta, O king, the faultless fertured and chaste Krishna, having lord, bewailed for the help of her husbands.

sn: द्रौपद्युवाच जयो जयन्तो विजयो जयत्सेनो जयद्वलः। ते मे वाचं विजानन्तु सूतपुत्रा नयन्ति माम्॥
en: Draupadi said Let Jaya, Jayanta, Vijaya, Jayatsena and Jayadbala hear my words. The Sutas are taking me away.

sn: येषां ज्यातलनिर्घोषो विस्फूर्जितमिवाशनेः। व्यश्रूयत महायुद्धे भीमघोषस्तरस्विनाम्॥ स्थघोषश्च बलवान् गन्धर्वाणां तरस्विनाम्। ते मे वाचं विजानन्तु सूतपुत्रा नयन्ति माम्॥
en: Let those powerful and quick-coursing Gandharvas, the clatter of whose cars is very great and the twang of whose bows in a great encounter is heard like the roar of thunder, understand that the Sutas are taking me away.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तस्यास्ताः कृपणा वाचः कृष्णायाः परिदेवितम्। श्रुत्वैवाभ्यापतद् भीमः शयनादविचारयन्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Hearing those sorrowful words and bewailing of Krishna, Bhima, without reflecting the least, got up from his bed.

sn: भीमसेन उवाच अहं शृणोमि ते वाचं त्वया सैरन्ध्र भाषिताम्। तस्मात् ते सूतपुत्रेभ्यो भयं भीरु न विद्यते॥
en: Bhimasena said: I have heard those which O Sairandhri, you have said; you have no fear any more, O timid lady, from the Sutas.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच इत्युक्त्वा स महाबाहुर्विजजृम्भे जिघांसया। ततः स व्यायतं कृत्वा वेषं विपरिवर्त्य च॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having said this, the mighty-armed; Bhima, to slay them, began to swell his body and then carefully changing his dress.

sn: अद्वारेणाभ्यवस्कन्ध निर्जगाम बहिस्तदा। स भीमसेनः प्राकारादारुह्य तरसा दुमम्॥
en: He went out of the palace by a wrong way. Then speedily scaling the walls, Bhimasena.

sn: श्मशानाभिमुखः प्रायाद् यत्र ते कीचका गताः। स लवयित्वा प्राकारं नि:सृत्य च पुरोत्तमात्।
en: Went to the cremation ground where the Kichaka's had-gone. Then scaling the walls and issuing out of the excellent city.

sn: जवेन पतितो भीमः सूतानामग्रतस्तदा॥ चितासमीपे गत्वा स तत्रापश्यद् वनस्पतिम्।
en: Bhima furiously rushed before the Sutas. And going near the funeral pyre he saw there a tree.

sn: तालमात्रं महास्कन्धं मूर्धशुष्कं विशाम्पते।॥ तं नागवदुपक्रम्य बाहुभ्यां परिरभ्य च।
en: Tall as a palmyra, with huge branches and with red top; then holding it like an elephant with his arms, he uprooted it.

sn: स्कन्धमारोपयामास दशव्यामं परंतपः॥ स तं वृक्षं दशव्यामं सस्कन्धविटपं बली। प्रगृह्याभ्यद्रवत् सूतान् दण्डपाणिरिवान्तकः॥ ऊरुवेगेन तस्याथ न्यग्रोधाश्वत्यकिंशुकाः। भूमौ निपतिता वृक्षाः सङ्घशस्तत्र शेरते॥ तं सिंहमिव संक्रुद्ध दृष्ट्वा गन्धर्वमागतम्। वित्रेसुः सर्वशः सूता विषादभयकम्पिताः॥
en: Measuring ten Vyamas and placed it on his shoulders. Then taking that tree up with its trunk and branches, measuring ten Vyamas that slayer of foes rushed towards the Sutas like Yama with mace in his hand. By the velocity of his movement, the banian, Nyagrodha, Kinshukh and other trees fell down on earth an lay in a heap. Beholding that Gandharva approach enraged like a lion, all those Sutas were afraid and trembled in sorrow and fear, Then beholding the Gandharva approach like death, the Kichaka's cremated their cldest brother and spoke amongst themselves trembling in fear and sorrow.

sn: गन्धर्वो बलवानेति क्रुद्ध उद्यम्य पादपम्। सैरन्ध्री मुच्यतां शीघ्रं यतो नो भयमागतम्॥
en: “Here comes the powerful Gandharva enraged uprooting a tree. Soon release Sairandhri from whom this fear has come."

sn: ते तु दृष्ट्वा तदाऽऽविद्धं भीमसेनेन पादपम्। विमुच्य द्रौपदी तत्र प्राद्रवन्नगरं प्रति॥
en: Then seeing the tree that had been uprooted by Bhimaseni they set Draupadi free and ran towards the city.

sn: द्रवतस्तांस्तु सम्प्रेक्ष्य स वज्री दानवानिव। शतं पञ्चाधिकं भीमः प्राहिणोद् यमसादनम्॥ वृक्षेणैतेन राजेन्द्र प्रभवानसुतो बली। तत आश्वासयत् कृष्णां स विमुच्य विशाम्पते।॥
en: Beholding them thus taking to their heels, the powerful Bhima, the son of the Wind-god, dispatched with that tree, O king, hundred and five of them to the abode of death, like the wielder of thunder-bolt, the Danavas. Then releasing Krishna he comforted her.

sn: उवाच च महाबाहुः पाञ्चालीं तत्र द्रौपदीम्। अश्रुपूर्णमुखीं दीनां दुर्धर्षः स वृकोदरः॥
en: Then the irrepressible mighty-armed Vrikodara Bhima said to the poor Panchali, Draupadi, with tearful eyes.

sn: एवं ते भीरु वध्यन्ते ये त्वां क्लिश्यन्त्यनागसम्। प्रैहि त्वं नगरं कृष्णे न भयं विद्यते तव॥ अन्येनाहं गमिष्यामि विराटस्य महानसम्॥
en: Then, O timid lady, all those from whom proceeded you misery, have been killed. Return O Krishna, to the city, you have no fear. I shall go to Virata's kitchen by another way.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच पञ्चाधिकं शतं तच्च निहतं तेन भारत। महावनमिवच्छिन्नं शिश्ये विगलितगुमम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said O descendant of Bharata, thus there were slain hundred and five of them (as if) a huge forest over-spread with uprooted trees.

sn: एवं ते निहता राजञ्छतं पञ्च च कीचकाः। स च सेनापतिः पूर्वमित्येतत् सूतषट्शतम्॥
en: Thus, Oking, one hundred and five Kichaka's killed. Including the commander-in-chief who was slain before, they were one hundred and six.

sn: तद् दृष्ट्वा महदाश्चर्यं नरा नार्यश्च संगताः। विस्मयं परमं गत्वा नोचुः किञ्चन भारत॥
en: Beholding that wonderful deed men and women assembled; O descendant of Bharata, they were filled with surprise and could not speak any thing.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ते दृष्ट्वा निहतान् सूतान् राज्ञे गत्वा न्यवेदयन्। गन्धर्वैनिहता राजन् सूतपुत्रा महाबलाः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Beholding the Suta's slain, people went and communicated to the king: "O king, the highly powerful sons of Suta have been slain by the Gandharvas.

sn: यथा वज्रेण वै दीर्ण पर्वतस्य महच्छिरः। व्यतिकीर्णाः प्रदृश्यन्ते तथा सूता महीतले॥
en: The Suta's are to be seen scattered on the surface of the earth like huge mountain summits clapped by thunder-bolt.

sn: सैरन्ध्री च विमुक्तासौ पुनरायाति ते गृहम्। सर्वं संशयितं राचन् नगरं ते भविष्यति॥
