en: And released Sairandhri comes back to your city; your (whole) city, o king, indeed shall be in danger.

sn: यथारूपा च सैरन्ध्री गन्धर्वाश्च महाबलाः। पुंसामिष्टश्च विषयो मैथुनाय न संशयः॥
en: Sairandhri is highly beautiful and the Gandharvas are greatly powerful and forsooth, men are undoubtedly lustful.

sn: यथा सैरन्ध्रदोषेण न ते राजनिदं पुरम्। विनाशमेति वै क्षिप्रं तथा नीतिविधीयताम्॥
en: Soon find out some means O king, by which your kingdom may not be ruined on account of the injuries done to Sairandhri.'

sn: तेषां तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा विराटो वाहिनीपतिः। अब्रवीत् क्रियतामेषां सूतानां परमक्रिया॥
en: Hearing their words, Virata, the king of armies, said : “Perform the obsequial rites of the Sutas."

sn: एकस्मिन्नेव ते सर्वे सुसमिद्धे हुताशने। दह्यन्तां कीचकाः शीघ्रं रत्नैर्गन्धैश्च सर्वशः॥
en: Let all the Kichaka's be burnt down on one burning, funeral pyre with profuse jems and perfumes.

sn: सुदेष्णामब्रवीद् राजा महिषीं जातसाध्वसः। सैरन्ध्रीमागतां ब्रूया ममैव वचनादिदम्॥
en: Then filled with fear, the king said to his queen Sudeshna: 'When Sairandhri comes, tell her these words of mine.

sn: गच्छ सैरन्ध्र भद्रं ते यथाकामं वरानने। बिभेति राजा सुश्रोणि गन्धर्वेभ्यः पराभवात्॥
en: Go Sairandhri, wherever you like; may good betide you, O fair one, O you having beautiful eye-brows, the king is afraid of defeat from the Gandharvas.

sn: न हि त्वामुत्सहे वक्तुं स्वयं गन्धर्वरक्षिताम्। स्त्रियास्त्वदोषस्तां वक्तुमतस्त्वां प्रब्रवीम्यहम्॥
en: I dare not speak all this to you in person, protected as you are by the Gandharvas. A woman cannot offend (any body) so I speak this through her.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच अथ मुक्ता भयात् कृष्णा सूतपुत्रान् निरस्य च। मोक्षिता भीमसेनेन जगाम नगरं प्रति॥ त्रासितेव मृगी बाला शार्दूलेन मनस्विनी। गात्राणि वाससी चैव प्रक्षाल्य सलिलेन सा॥
en: Vaishampayana said Thus released by Bhimasena after the destruction of Sutas, the intelligent Krishna freed from fear, washed her body and raiment in water and went towards the city like a doe put to fright by a tiger,

sn: तां दृष्ट्वा पुरुषा राजन् प्राद्रवन्त दिशो दश। गन्धर्वाणां भयत्रस्ताः केचिद् दृष्ट्वा न्यमीलयन्।।१३।
en: Beholding her, O king, people fled away in all directions in fear of the Gandharvas and some even shut up their eyes.

sn: ततो महानसद्वारि भीमसेनमवस्थितम्। ददर्श राजन् पाञ्चाली यथा मत्तं महाद्विपम्॥
en: Then, o king, Panchali saw Bhimsena, waiting at the kitchen door like a huge infuriated elephant.

sn: तं विस्मयन्ती शनकैः संज्ञाभिरिदमब्रवीत्। गन्धर्वराजाय नमो येनास्मि परिमोचिता॥
en: She wonderingly said to him in words intelligible to them: “Salutation to that king of Gandharvas by whom I have been released.

sn: भीमसेन उवाच ये पुरा विचरन्तीह पुरुषा वशवर्तिनः। तस्यास्ते वचनं श्रुत्वा ह्यनृणा विहरन्त्वतः॥
en: Bhima said Hearing these words of hers under which those persons were till then living in that city, they will now live there freed from debt.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततः सा नर्तनागारे धनंजयमपश्यता राज्ञः कन्या विराटस्य नर्तयानं महाभुजम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said She there the mighty-armed Dhananjaya in the dancing hall giving instructions in dancing to the daughter of the king Virata.

sn: ततस्ता नर्तनागाराद् विनिष्क्रम्य सहार्जुनाः। कन्या ददृशुरायान्तीं क्लिष्टां कृष्णामनागसम्॥
en: Then coming out with Arjuna from the dancing hall, those daughters saw the innocent saw Krishna (though) sorely persecuted coming. Beholding her arrive there they all delightedly said.

sn: कन्या ऊचुः दिष्ट्या सैरन्ध्र मुक्तासि दिष्ट्यासि पुनरागता। दिष्ट्या विनिहताः सूता ये त्वां क्लिश्यन्त्यनागसम्॥
en: The Daughters said By good luck, O Sairandhri, you have been released and by good-luck you have returned. And by good luck the Sutas have been slain from whom this your misery came.

sn: बृहन्नलोवाच कथं सैरन्ध्रि मुक्तासि कथं पापाश्च ते हताः। इच्छामि वै तव श्रोतुं सर्वमेव यथातथम्॥
en: Brihannala said Have you been released, O Sairandhri, and have those wicked men been slain? I wish to hear all this exactly as it happened.

sn: सैरन्ध्युवाच बृहन्नले किं नु तव सैरन्ध्या कार्यमद्य वै। या त्वं वससि कल्याणि सदा कन्यापुरे सुखम्॥
en: Sairandhri said O blessed Brihnnala, you always live happily in the apartment of the girls, what have you to do with Sairandhri?

sn: न हि दुःखं समाप्नोषि सैरन्ध्री यदुपाश्नुते। तेन मां दुःखितामेवं पृच्छसे प्रहसन्निव॥
en: You shall not meet with grief when Sairandhri does it. You are asking me thus in jest who am stricken with sorrow.

sn: बृहन्नलोवाच बृहन्नलापि कल्याणि दुःखमाप्नोत्यनुत्तमम्। तिर्यग्योनिगता बाले न चैनामवबुध्यसे॥
en: Brihannala said O blessed lady, Brihannala also has sorrow of her own without any comparison; she has been born in the species of brutes, you do not understand this, O girl.

sn: त्वया सहोषिता चास्मि त्वं च सर्वैः सहोषिता। क्लिश्यन्त्यां त्वयि सुश्रोणि को नु दुःखं न चिन्तयेत्।।२४
en: I have lived with you and you also have lived with us; why should not one, O you of beautiful hips, feel sorrow for you who are afflicted with sorrow.

sn: न तु केनचिदत्यन्तं कस्यचिद्धृदयं क्वचित्। वेदितुं शक्यते नूनं तेन मां नावबुध्यसे॥
en: No one can definitely read another's heart; therefore O fair one, you cannot understand me.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततः सहैव कन्याभिद्रौपदी राजवेश्म तत्। प्रविवेश सुदेष्णायाः समीपमुपगामिनी॥
en: Then accompanied by those girls Draupadi entered the palace with a view to appear before Sudeshna.

sn: तामब्रवीद् राजपुत्री विराटवचनादिदम्। सैरन्ध्र गम्यतां शीघ्रं यत्र कामयसे गतिम्॥
en: Then the queen communicated to her Virata's words: 'Sairandhri, soon go wherever you wish.

sn: राजा बिभेति ते भद्रे गन्धर्वेभ्यः पराभवात्। त्वं चापि तरुणी सुभ्र रूपेणाप्रतिमा भुवि। पुंसामिष्टश्च विषयो गन्धर्वाश्चातिकोपनाः॥
en: O fair one, the king is afraid of the defeat from the Gandharvas. O you of beautiful eyebrows, you are youthful and in beauty, unparalleled on earth. You are an object of desire to men and the Gandharvas are wrathful.

sn: सैरभ्युवाच त्रयोदशाहमात्रं मे राजा क्षाम्यतु भामिनि। कृतकृत्या भविष्यन्ति गन्धर्वास्ते न संशयः॥
en: Sairandhri said O fair queen, let the king permit me to live here for thirteen days more. Undoubtedly the Gandharvas shall be highly obliged for this.

sn: ततो मामुपनेष्यन्ति करिष्यन्ति च ते प्रियम्। ध्रुवं च श्रेयसा राजा योक्ष्यते सह बान्धवैः॥
en: They will then take me away from here and will do what is agreeable to you. Forsooth the king with his friends shall meet with wellbeing.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच कीचकस्य तु घातेन अत्याहितं चिन्तयित्वा व्यस्मयन्त पृथग् जनाः॥ सानुजस्य विशाम्पते।
en: Vaishampayana said O king, at the destruction of Kichaka and his brothers and thinking of this calamity, people were filled with surprise.

sn: तस्मिन् पुरे जनपदे संजल्पोऽभूच्च सङ्घशः। शौर्याद्धि वल्लभो राज्ञो महासत्त्वः स कीचकः॥
en: All over the city and provinces, it was widely known that the kings Vallabha and Kichaka were both brave and powerful heroes.

sn: आसीत् प्रहर्ता सैन्यानां दारामर्शी च दुर्मतिः। स हतः खलु पापात्मा गन्धर्वैर्दुष्टपूरुषः॥
en: The wicked-minded Kichaka was the oppressor of men and the ravisher of soldier's wives; that vicious, wicked man has been slain by the Gandharvas.

sn: इत्यजल्पन् महाराज परानीकविनाशनम्। देशे देशे मनुष्याश्च कीचकं दुष्प्रधर्षणम्॥
en: It is in this way, O great king, that people of various countries spoke about the irrepressible Kichaka, the slayer of hostile armies.

sn: अथ वै धार्तराष्ट्रेण प्रयुक्ता ये बहिश्चराः। मृगयित्वा बहून् ग्रामान् राष्ट्राणि नगराणि च॥
en: In the meantime spies, engaged by Dhritarashtra's son, searching many villages, provinces and cities.

sn: संविधाय यथादृष्टं यथादेशप्रदर्शनम्। कृतकृत्या न्यवर्तन्त ते चरा नगरं प्रति॥
en: Accomplishing all they had been commanded and seeing all countries, returned to the city; being successful (in one thing).

sn: तत्र दृष्ट्वा तु राजानं कौरव्यं धृतराष्ट्रजम्। द्रोणकर्णकृपैः साधु भीष्मेण च महात्मना॥ संगतं भ्रातृभिश्चापि त्रिगर्तेश्च महारथैः। दुर्योधनं सभामध्ये आसीनमिदमब्रुवन्॥
en: Then beholding Dhritarashtra's son, king Duryodhana of the Kuru race, seated in his court, with Drona, Karna, Kripa, the noble Bhishma, his brothers and the great heroes, the Trigarthas, they said to him.

sn: चरा ऊचुः कृतोऽस्माभिः परो यत्नस्तेषामन्वेषणे सदा। पाण्डवानां मनुष्येन्द्र तस्मिन् महति कानने॥
en: The spies said O king of men, we have with great care searched the sons of Pandu in that huge forest.

sn: निर्जने मृगसंकीर्णे नानादुमलताकुले। लताप्रतानबहुले नानागुल्मसमावृते॥
en: Solitary, abounding in wild animals, filled with various trees, creepers, entwining creepers and various groves.

sn: न च विद्मो गता येन पार्थाः सुदृढविक्रमाः। मार्गमाणाः पदन्यासं तेषु तेषु तथा तथा॥
en: 1But we haven failed to find out the way (stamped) with their footsteps, by which the highly powerful sons of Pritha might have gone.

sn: गिरिकूटेषु तुङ्गेषु नानाजनपदेषु च। जनाकीर्णेषु देशेषु खवटेषु पुरेषु च।॥
en: On mountain summits, in fastness, in various countries, in provinces filled with men, in encampments and cities.

sn: नरेन्द्र बहुशोऽन्विष्टा नैव विद्यश्च पाण्डवान्। अत्यन्तं वा विनष्टास्ते भद्रं तुभ्यं नरर्षभ॥
en: We have made many inquires, O king, but we have not found out the Pandavas; may good betide you. O king; it seems they have perished.

sn: वर्मन्यन्वेष्यमाणा वै रथिनां रथिसत्तम। न हि विद्मो गतिं तेषां वासं हि नरसत्तम॥
en: O foremost of car-warriors, we pursued (also) the track of those car-warriors, but O foremost of men, we have not found out their whereabouts and movements.

sn: किंचित्काले मनुष्येन्द्र सूतानामनुगा वयम्। मृगयित्वा यथान्यायं वेदितार्थाः स्म तत्त्वतः॥
en: O king of men, for sometime we pursued their charioteers; and making due enquiries we have got at the truth.

sn: प्राप्ता द्वारवती सूता विना पार्थः परंतप। न तत्र कृष्णा राजेन्द्र पाण्डवाश्च महाव्रताः॥
en: O slayer of enemies, the charioteers reached, Dvaravati without the son of Pritha. O king, there is neither Krishna nor are the Pandavas of great vows.

sn: सर्वथा विप्रणष्टास्ते नमस्ते भरतर्षभ। न हि विद्मो मतिं तेषां वासं वापि महात्मनाम्॥
en: They have all perished. We bow to you. O foremost of Bharata. We do no know the movements and whereabouts of those highsouled ones.

sn: पाण्डवानां प्रवृत्तिं च विद्मः कर्मापि वा कृतम्। स नः शाधि मनुष्येन्द्र अत ऊर्ध्वं विशाम्पते॥
en: We know of the inclination of ht Pandavas and some of their deeds. After this, give us instructions, O king, O lord of men.

sn: अन्वेषणे पाण्डवानां भूयः किं करवामहे। इमां च नः प्रियां वीर वाचं भद्रवतीं शृणु॥
en: As to what we should again do in our search after the Pandavas. O heroes, listen to these pleasing words tending to your wellbeing.

sn: येन त्रिगर्ता निहता बलेन महता नृप। सूतेन राज्ञो मत्स्यस्य कीचकेन बलीयसा॥
en: Oking, the Trigarthas were repeatedly vanquished by the great prowess of Kichaka, the charioteer of the king of Matsya.

sn: स हतः पतितः शेते गन्धर्वैर्निशि भारत। अदृश्यमानैर्दुष्टात्मा भ्रातृभिः सह सोदरैः॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, that vicioussouled one lies slain on earth with his brother by some invisible Gandharvas at night.

sn: प्रियमेतदुपश्रुत्य शत्रूणां च पराभवम्। कृतकृत्यश्च कौरव्य विधत्स्व यदनन्तरम्॥
en: Hearing this pleasant news of the defeat of our enemy, do you decide, O Kauravya, as to what you should do hereafter.

description: The words of Karna and Dushasana
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततो दुर्योधनो राजा ज्ञात्वा तेषां वचस्तदा। चिरमन्तर्मना भूत्वा प्रत्युवाच सभासदः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Thereupon hearing their words, the king Duryodhana thought in his mind and then said to his courtiers.

description: The words of Karna and Dushasana
sn: सुदुःखा खलु कार्याणां गतिर्विज्ञातुमन्ततः। तस्मात् सर्वे निरीक्षध्वं क्व नु ते पाण्डवा गताः।।२।
en: It is very difficult to ascertain definitely the tide of affairs. Do you all ascertain where the Pandavas have gone.

description: The words of Karna and Dushasana
sn: अल्पावशिष्टं कालस्य गतभूयिष्ठमन्ततः। तेषामज्ञातचर्यायामस्मिन् वर्षे त्रयोदशे॥
en: Of these thirteen years which they have to pass hidden from us all, the greater portion has well-high elapsed and only a little remains.

description: The words of Karna and Dushasana
sn: अस्य वर्षस्य शेषं चेद् व्यतीयुरिह पाण्डवाः। निवृत्तसमयास्ते हि सत्यव्रतपरायणाः॥
en: And if they can truly pass the remaining portion of this year hidden from our view in pursuance of their vow they will then have fulfilled their pledge.

description: The words of Karna and Dushasana
sn: क्षरन्त इव नागेन्द्राः सर्वे ह्याशीविषोपमाः। दुःखा भवेयुः संरब्धाः कौरवान् प्रति ते ध्रुवम्॥
en: Forsooth, they, worked up with anger, will torment the Kauravas like the elephants in rut or virulent snakes.

description: The words of Karna and Dushasana
sn: सर्वे कालस्य वेत्तारः कृच्छ्ररूपधराः स्थिताः। प्रविशेयुर्जितक्रोधास्तावदेव पुनर्वनम्॥
en: Let them, with anger controlled, acquainted with all seasons, living in painful disguise, enter the woods again.

description: The words of Karna and Dushasana
sn: तस्मात् क्षिप्रं बुभूषध्वं यथा तेऽत्यन्तमव्ययम्। राज्यं निर्द्वन्द्वमव्यग्रं निःसपत्नं चिरं भवेत्॥
en: Do you all concert measures speedily for this, so that our kingdom may remain without enemies, rivals and diminution.

description: The words of Karna and Dushasana
sn: अथाब्रवीत् ततः कर्णः क्षिप्रं गच्छन्तु भारत। अन्ये धूर्ता नरा दक्षा निभृताः साधुकारिणः॥
en: Thereupon Karna said : “O descendant of Bharata, let other spies, more, cunning, capable and better fitted for this work, proceed in disguise.

description: The words of Karna and Dushasana
sn: चरन्तु देशान् संवीताः स्फीताञ्जानपदाकुलान्। तत्र गोष्ठीषु रम्यासु सिद्धप्रव्रजितेषु च।॥
en: Let them range all over the country, various provinces over-flowing with population, assemblies of learned men and charming retreats of ascetics.

description: The words of Karna and Dushasana
sn: परिचारेषु तीर्थेषु विविधेष्वाकरेषु च। विज्ञातव्या मनुष्यैस्तैस्तर्कया सुविनीतया॥
en: In inner apartments, places of pilgrimage, mines and various other places (they should be searched after) with vigilance and humility.

description: The words of Karna and Dushasana
sn: विविधैस्तत्परैः सम्यक् तज्जैनिपुणसंवृतैः। अन्वेष्टव्याः सुनिपुणैः पाण्डवाश्छन्नवासिनः॥
en: The Pandavas, living in disguise, should be searched after by a number of expert spies, devoted to this work, themselves disguised and well acquainted with the object of search.

description: The words of Karna and Dushasana
sn: नदीकुट्ठोषु तीर्थेषु ग्रामेषु नगरेषु च। आश्रमेषु च रम्येषु पर्वतेषु गुहासु च॥
en: On the banks of the rivers, in sacred shrines, villages, cities, hermitages, charming mountains and caves.

description: The words of Karna and Dushasana
sn: अथाग्रजानन्तरजः पापभावानुरागवान्। ज्येष्ठं दुःशासनस्तत्र भ्राता भ्रातरमब्रवीत्॥
en: Thereupon his younger brother Dushasana, taking delight in sins, said before his elder brother.

description: The words of Karna and Dushasana
sn: येषु नः प्रत्ययो राजंश्चारेषु मनुजाधिप। ते यान्तु दत्तदेया वै भूयस्तान् परिमार्गितुम्॥
en: O king, O lord of men, let those spies, in whom we have confidence, receive their remuneration in advance and proceed in search of them.

description: The words of Karna and Dushasana
sn: एतच्च कर्णो यत् प्राह सर्वमीहामहे तथा। यथोद्दिष्टं चराः सर्वे मृगयन्तु यतस्ततः॥
en: This and what Karna has said have my full approbation. As directed let all those spies search at all those places.

description: The words of Karna and Dushasana
sn: एते चान्ये च भूयांसो देशाद् देशं यथाविधि। न तु तेषां गतिर्वासः प्रवृत्तिश्चोपलभ्यते॥
en: Let those and others make a due search in various countries. My belief is that their movements and whereabouts are not to be known.

description: The words of Karna and Dushasana
sn: अत्यन्तं वा निगूढास्ते पारं चोर्मिमतो गताः। व्यालैश्चापि महारण्ये भक्षिताः शूरमानिनः॥
en: They are living in very great secrecy; or perhaps they have gone to the other side of the ocean. Those respecters of heroes might have been devoured by wild animals in that huge forest.

description: The words of Karna and Dushasana
sn: अथवा विषमं प्राप्य विनष्टाः शाश्वतीः समाः। तस्मान्मानसमव्यग्रं कृत्वा त्वं कुरुनन्दन। कुरु कार्यं महोत्साहं मन्यसे यन्नराधिप॥
en: Or overtaken by some dreadful calamity, they have perished for ever. Therefore, O Kuru chief, removing all anxiety from your heart, acquire what you may, working with your energy, O king.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच अथाब्रवीन्महावीर्यो द्रोणस्तत्त्वार्थदर्शिवान्। न तादृशा विनश्यन्ति न प्रयान्ति पराभवम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Thereupon the highly energetic and greatly wise Drona said : "Persons like them can never meet with destruction of discomfiture."

sn: शूराश्च कृतविद्याश्च बुद्धिमन्तो जितेन्द्रियाः। धर्मज्ञाश्च कृतज्ञाश्च धर्मराजमनुव्रताः॥ नीतिधर्मार्थतत्त्वज्ञं पितृवच्च समाहितम्। धर्मे स्थितं सत्यधृति ज्येष्ठं ज्येष्ठानुयायिनः॥ अनुव्रता महात्मानं भ्रातरो भ्रातरं नृप। अजातशत्रु श्रीमन्तं सर्वभ्रातृननुव्रतम्॥
en: Heroic, well educated, intelligent, selfcontrolled, pious, grateful, observant of vows, ever following their eldest brother, the pious Yudhishthira like a father, stationed in morality and truthful-all these brothers, O king, are obedient to this high-souled brother, graceful and having no enemy and himself (also) obeying his brothers.

sn: तेषां तथा विधेयानां निभृतानां महात्मनाम्। किमर्थं नीतिमान् पार्थः श्रेयो नैषां करिष्यति॥
en: Why not Partha conversant with policy should look to the well being of such highsouled brothers obedient to him?

sn: तस्माद् यत्नात् प्रतीक्षन्ते कालस्योदयमागतम्। न हि ते नाशमृच्छेयुरिति पश्याम्यहं धिया॥
en: It is for this they are carefully waiting for the opportune hour. Such persons never die; this is what I perceive by my good sense.

sn: साम्प्रतं चैव यत् कार्यं तच्च क्षिप्रमकालिकम्। क्रियतां साधु संचिन्त्य वासश्चैषां प्रचिन्त्यताम्॥ यथावत् पाण्डुपुत्राणां सर्वार्थेषु धृतात्मनाम्। दुर्जेयाः खलु शूरास्ते दुरापास्तपसा वृताः॥
en: Do you immediately without any loss of time and after proper thought what should be done. Also appoint duly the habitation of those sons of Pandu, who are self-controlled in all things. Those heroic, sinless and devout Pandavas are hard to be discovered.

sn: शुद्धात्मा गुणवान् पार्थः सत्यवान् नीतिमाशुचिः। तेजोराशिरसंख्येयो गृह्णीयादपि चक्षुषा॥
en: The pure-souled, accomplished, truthful, honest son of Pritha, conversant with policy, and a very collection of effulgence, is capable of consuming by his very look.

sn: विज्ञाय क्रियतां तस्माद् भूयश्च मृगयामहे। ब्राह्मणैश्चारकैः सिद्धर्ये चान्ये तद्विदो जनाः॥
en: Knowing this, do (what you should); we shall again search them through Brahmana spies, Siddhas and others who know them.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततः शान्तनवो भीष्मो भरतानां पितामहः। श्रुतवान् देखकालज्ञस्तत्त्वज्ञः सर्वधर्मवित्॥ आचार्यवाक्योपरमे तद्वाक्यमभिसंदधत्। हितार्थं समुवाचैनां भारती भारतान् प्रति॥
en: Vaishampayana said Thereupon the grand-father, of Bharatas, Shantanu's son, Bhishma, well-read in the Vedas, and informed of the truth of the place and time and endued with a knowledge of his own duties, after the speech of the preceptor Drona, applauded it and said the following words to the descendants of Bharata for their interest.

sn: युधिष्ठिरे समासक्तां धर्मज्ञे धर्मसंवृताम्। असत्सु दुर्लभां नित्यं सतां चाभिमतां सदा॥
en: Bespeaking his attachment to the pious Yudhishthira, words that are rarely given vent to by the dishonest men and always liked by the honest.

sn: भीष्मः समवदत् तत्र गिरं साधुभिरर्चिताम्। यश्चैष ब्राह्मणः प्राह द्रोणः सर्वार्थतत्त्ववित्॥
en: Bhishma gave bent to impartial words always liked by the wise: “I have nothing to say on and fully approve of the words, which the Brahmana Drona, acquainted with the truth of all things, has said.

sn: सर्वलक्षणसम्पन्नाः साधुव्रतसमन्विताः। श्रुतवर्तोपपन्नाश्च नानाश्रुतिसमन्विताः॥ वृद्धानुशासने युक्ताः सत्यव्रतपरायणाः। समयं समयज्ञास्ते पालयन्तः शुचिव्रताः॥ क्षत्रधर्मरता नित्यं केशवानुगता: सदा। प्रवीरपुरुषास्ते वै महात्मानो महाबलाः। नावसीदितुमर्हन्ति उद्वहन्तः सतां धुरम्॥
en: Gifted with all auspicious marks, observant of religious vows, well-read in the Vedas and intent upon the performance of various religious observances, (always) engaged in carrying out the orders of elderly men, of truthful vows, acquainted with the use of time, always satisfying their condition, pure, always performing the duties of the Kshatriya order, always following Keshava, those high-souled and highly powerful heroes.

sn: धर्मतश्चैव गुप्तास्ते सुवीर्येण च पाण्डवाः। न नाशमधिगच्छेयुरिति मे धीयते मतिः॥ तत्र बुद्धिं प्रवक्ष्यामि पाण्डवान् प्रति भारत। न तु नीतिः सुनीतस्य शक्यतेऽन्वेषितुं परैः॥
en: Carrying the burden of the wise do not seem to wither away. Protected, by their own great energy, the Pandavas ever treading virtue shall not die. This is what I surmise. O descendant of Bharata, I tell you what I think we should do towards the Pandavas,

sn: यत् तु शक्यमिहास्माभिस्तान् वै संचिन्त्य पाण्डवान्। बुद्ध्या प्रयुक्तं न द्रोहात् प्रवक्ष्यामि निबोध तत्।।१०।
en: To search them through mean spies would not be the policy of a (really wise man.) Consulting with others we should decide what we should do towards the Pandavas.

sn: न त्वियं मादृशेर्नीतिस्तस्य वाच्या कथंचन) सा त्वियं साधु वक्तव्या न त्वनीतिः कथंचन॥
en: Know that I say nothing out of ill will towards you. I shall never give such counsels to him who is dishonest.

sn: वृद्धानुशासने तात तिष्ठता सत्यशीलिना। अवश्यं त्विह धीरेण सतां मध्ये विवक्षता॥
en: Good counsels should be given and never evil. O child, one following the words of the aged and truthful.

sn: यथाहमिह वक्तव्यं सर्वथा धर्मलिप्सया। तत्र नाहं तथा मन्ये यतायमितरो जनः॥
en: And calm, while speaking in the midst of an assembly, should always speak the truth if he wishes to acquire virtue.

sn: निवासं धर्मराजस्य वर्षेऽस्मिन् वै त्रयोदश। तत्र तात न तेषां हि राज्ञां भाव्यमसाम्प्रतम्॥ पुरे जनपदे चापि यत्र राजा युधिष्ठिरः।
en: I think differently from all these ordinary people here regarding the whereabouts of the pious Yudhishthira in this thirteenth year of his exile.

sn: दानशीलो वदान्यश्च निभृतो ह्रीनिषेवकः। जनो जनपदे भाव्यो यत्र राजा युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Wherever the king Yudhishthira lives o my child, the rulers, either of cities or of provinces there never meet with calamity. The people, of the country where the king Yudhishthira lives, become charitable, liberal, humble and modest.

sn: प्रियवादी सदा दान्तो भव्यः सत्यपरो जनः। हृष्टः पुष्टः शुचिर्दक्षो यत्र राजा युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Where the king Yudhishthira lives the people become sweet-speeched, selfcontrolled, observant of truth, cheerful, healthy, pure in conduct and expert in works.

sn: नासूयको न चापीर्नाभिमानी न मत्सरी। भविष्यति जनस्तत्र स्वयं धर्ममनुव्रतः॥
en: The people of the place where Yudhishthira lives envious, malicious, vain or proud but they always perform their respective duties.

sn: ब्रह्मघोषाश्च भूयांसः पूर्णाहुत्यस्तथैव च। क्रतवश्च भविष्यन्ति भूयांसो भूरिदक्षिणाः॥
en: There the Vedic hymns are chanted all over, sacrifices are performed, the last full libations are offered to clarified butter and the gifts to Brahmanas are always abundant.

sn: सदा व तत्र पर्जन्यः सम्यग्वर्षी न संशयः। सम्पन्नसस्या च मही निरातङ्का भविष्यति॥
en: are never There undoubtedly the clouds always pour heavy showers; the earth, filled with crops, shall be freed from fear.

sn: गुणवन्ति च धान्यानि रसवन्ति फलानि च। गन्धवन्ति च माल्यानि शुभशब्दा च भारती॥
en: There the paddy is full of grain and the fruits are juicy-the garlands are fragrant and the conversation is full of auspicious words.

sn: वायुश्च सुखसंस्पर्शो निष्प्रतीपं च दर्शनम्। न भयं त्वाविशेत् तत्र यत्र राजा युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Where the king Yudhishthira lives the breezes are sweet, the meetings of men are friendly and there exists no cause of fear.

sn: गावश्च बहुलास्तत्र न कृशा न च दुर्बलाः। पयांसि दधिसपीषि रसवन्ति हितानि च॥
en: The kine there are plentiful, none of them being weak or lean and milk, curd and butter are all savoury and nutritious.

sn: गुणवन्ति च पेयानि भोज्यानि रसवन्ति च। तत्र देशे भविष्यन्ति यत्र राजा युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Where the king Yudhishthira lives the drinks and edibles are sweet and wholesome.

sn: रसाः स्पर्शाश्च गन्धाश्च शब्दाश्चापि गुणान्विताः। दृश्यानि च प्रसन्नानि यत्र राजा युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Where the king Yudhishthira lives the objects of taste, touch, smell and hearing are all of excellent quality and the views are all delightful.

sn: धर्माश्च तत्र सर्वैस्तु सेविताश्च द्विजातिभिः। स्वैः स्वैर्गुणैश्च संयुक्ता अस्मिन् वर्षे त्रयोदश॥
en: In those places, religious duties are observed by twice-born ones endued with all their respective qualities in this thirteenth year.

sn: देशे तस्मिन् भविष्यन्ति तात पाण्डवसंयुते। सम्प्रीतिमाढानस्तत्र संतुष्टः शुचिरव्ययः॥
en: O my child, in countries where the Pandavas will live, people will all be contented, cheerful, pure and of eternal virtue.

sn: देवतातिथिपूजासु सर्वभावानुरागवान्। इष्टदानो महोत्साहः स्वस्वधर्मपरायणः॥
en: Whole-mindedly devoted to the worship of guests and deities they, with great energy, perform charities and shall be devoted to eternal virtue.

sn: अशुभाद्धि शुभप्रेप्सुरिष्टयज्ञः शुभव्रतः। भविष्यति जनस्तत्र यत्र राजा युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Where the king Yudhishthira lives people, discarding all that is evil, acquire what is good only, they always perform sacrifices and observe pure vows.

sn: त्यक्तवाक्यानृतस्तात शुभकल्याणमङ्गलः। शुभार्थेप्सुः शुभमतिर्यत्र राजा युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Where the king Yudhishthira is, people, renouncing untruth, shall acquire what is good, auspicious and beneficial and thus good mind shall be inclined towards the good.

sn: भविष्यति जनस्तत्र नित्यं चेष्टप्रियव्रतः। धर्मात्मा शक्यते ज्ञातुं नापि तात द्विजातिभिः॥ किं पुनः प्राकृतैस्तात पार्थो विज्ञायते क्वचित्। यस्मिन् सत्यं धृतिर्दानं परा शान्तिधूवा क्षमा॥ ह्रीः श्रीः कीर्तिः परं तेज आनृशंस्यमथार्जवम्। तस्मात् तत्र निवासं तु छन्नं यत्नेन धीमतः। गतिं च परमां तत्र नोत्सहे वत्तुक्कमन्यथा॥
en: People there shall daily perform sacrifices and observe holy vows. O child, the pious son of Pritha, in whom exist, truth fortitude, intelligence, excellent forgiveness, highest tranquility, modest, prosperity, fame, great energy, simplicity and love for all creatures, cannot with be known by Brahmanas, what to speak of ordinary people.

sn: एवमेतत् तु संचिन्त्य यत्कृते मन्यसे हितम्। तत् क्षिप्रं कुरु कौरव्य यद्येवं श्रद्दधासि मे॥
en: I have with great care described the secret habitation of that intelligent one; about his excellent mode of life I do not dare speak anything more. Thinking well of this do you without any loss of time what you think proper, foremost of Kurus, if you have any faith in my words. eveni care

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तत: शारद्वतो वाक्यमित्युवाच कृपस्तदा। युक्तं प्राप्तं च वृद्धेन पाण्डवान् प्रति भाषितम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Thereupon Sharadvata's son Kripa said the following words: “What the aged Bhishma has said about the Pandavas is reasonable and suited to the occasion.

sn: धर्मार्थसहितं श्लक्ष्णं तत्त्वतश्च सहेतुकम्। तत्रानुरूपं भीष्मेण ममाप्यत्र गिरं शृणु।॥
en: Consistent with Dharma and Artha, praise worthy, reasonable, truthful and is worthy of him. Hear my words on this.

sn: तेषां चैव गतिस्तीर्थैर्वासश्चैषां प्रचिन्त्यताम्। नीतिर्विधीयतां चापि साम्प्रतं या हिता भवेत्॥
en: It is proper for you to find out the way they have followed and their whereabouts through spies and adopt what may conduce to your well-being.

sn: नावज्ञेयो रिपुस्तात प्राकृतोऽपि बुभूषता। किं पुनः पाण्डवास्तात सर्वास्त्रकुशला रणे॥
en: O my child, one seeking his welfare should not disregard an enemy, even if he be an ordinary man, what to speak of the Pandavas, well-versed in forms of warfare.

sn: तस्मात् सत्रं प्रविष्टेषु पाण्डवेषु महात्मसु। गूढभावेषु छन्नेषु काले चोदयमागते॥ स्वराष्ट्र परराष्ट्रे च ज्ञातव्यं बलमात्मनः। उदयः पाण्डवानां च प्राप्ते काले न संशयः॥
en: When the time for the return of the highsoul Pandavas comes, who are now passing their days in close disguise in woods you should gauge your own strength in your own kingdom and in those of other kings. Forsooth, the time of the return of the Pandavas is near at hand.

sn: निवृत्तसमयाः पार्था महात्मानो महाबलाः। महोत्साहा भविष्यन्ति पाण्डवा ह्यमितौजसः॥
en: When the time of their exile shall be over, the high-minded and the greatly powerful son of Pritha, of incomparable prowess, shall be brimful with energy.

sn: तस्माद् बलं च कोषश्च नीतिश्चापि विधीयताम्। यथा कालोदये प्राप्ते सम्यक् तैः संदधामहे॥
en: Therefore (replenish) your treasury and (increase) your forces; and take recourse to a sound policy to conclude an advantageous treaty with them, when the proper time of their return comes.

sn: तात बुद्ध्यापि तत् सर्वं बुध्यस्व बलमात्मनः। नियतं सर्वमित्रेषु बलवत्स्वबलेषु च॥
en: Knowing all this, determine your own strength, O my child, with respect to your allies, weak and powerful.

sn: उच्चावचं बलं ज्ञात्वा मध्यस्थं चापि भारत। प्रहृष्टमप्रहृष्टं च संदधाम तथा परैः॥
en: Determining the efficiency, weakness or indifference of your forces, as well as who amongst them are satisfied and dissatisfied we should enter into fight with our enemies or form a treaty.

sn: साम्ना दानेन भेदेन दण्डेन बलिकर्मणा। न्यायेनाक्रम्य च परान् बलाच्चानभ्य दुर्बलान्॥ सान्त्वयित्वा तु मित्राणि बलं चाभाष्यतां सुखम्। सुकोषबलसंवृद्धः सम्यक् सिद्धिमवाप्स्यसि॥
en: Resorting to the expedients of conciliation, disunion, chastisement, bribery, presents and fair conduct attack your-enemies and vanquish the weak by strength and reconcile the allies and soldiers by sweet speeches. When you shall be able to reinforce your army and replenish your treasury success shall be yours.

sn: योत्स्यसे चापि बलिभिररिभिः प्रत्युपस्थितैः। अन्यस्त्वं पाण्डवैर्वापि हीनैः स्वबलवाहनैः
en: You shall then be able to fight with the powerful enemies who will come-what of Pandavas, weak in soldiers and animals.

sn: एवं सर्वं विनिश्चित्य व्यवसायं स्वधर्मतः। यथाकालं मनुष्येन्द्र चिरं सुखमवाप्स्यसि॥
en: Having determined all these expedients according to the practice of your order, you shall, O king of men, acquire lasting happiness in due time.

description: The going of Susharma and others to Matsya country
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच अथ राजा त्रिगर्तानां सुशर्मा रथयूथपः। प्राप्तकालमिदं वाक्यमुवाच त्वरितो बली॥ असकृनिकृताः पूर्वं मत्स्यशाल्वेयकैः प्रभो। सूतेनैव च मत्स्यस्य कीचकेन पुनः पुनः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Vanquished repeatedly by the Matsya king's charioteer, Kichaka, backed by other Matsya's, the powerful king of Trigartas, Susharma, owning many cars, gave vent to the following words at the opportune moment.

description: The going of Susharma and others to Matsya country
sn: बाधितो बन्धुभिः सार्धं बलाद् बलवता विभो। स कर्णमभ्युदीक्ष्याथ दुर्योधनमभाषत॥
en: O King of the powerful, being forcibly defeated along with his relatives, he, looking askance at Karna, said to Duryodhana.

description: The going of Susharma and others to Matsya country
sn: असकृन्मत्स्यराज्ञा मे राष्ट्र बाधितमोजसा। प्रणेता कीचकस्तस्य बलवानभवत् पुरा॥
en: My kingdom has been again and again forcibly invaded by the king of Matsya's. Formerly the mighty Kichaka was his general.

description: The going of Susharma and others to Matsya country
sn: क्रूरोऽमर्षी स दुष्टात्मा भुवि प्रख्यातविक्रमः। निहतः स तु गन्धर्वैः पापकर्मा नृशंसवान्॥
en: Crooked, wrathful, wicked-minded, having his powers kuown all over the world, that crucl and vicious one has been slain by the Gandharvas.

description: The going of Susharma and others to Matsya country
sn: तस्मिन् विनिहते राजा हतदर्पो निराश्रयः। भविष्यति निरुत्साहो विराट इति मे पतिः॥
en: He being slain, the king Virata, me-thinks, shorn of pride an refugc, will lose energy.

description: The going of Susharma and others to Matsya country
sn: तत्र यात्रा मम मता यदि ते रोचतेऽनघ। कौरवाणां च सर्वेषां कर्णस्य च महात्मनः॥
en: I think, O sinless one, we should go there, if it pleases you as well as all the Kauravas and the high-souled Karna.

description: The going of Susharma and others to Matsya country
sn: एतत् प्राप्तमहं मन्ये कार्यमात्ययिकं हि नः। राष्ट्रं तस्याभियास्यामो बहुधान्यसमाकुलम्॥
en: I consider, this accident, which has occurred, as favorable to us. Let us all go to his kingdom abounding in corn.

description: The going of Susharma and others to Matsya country
sn: आददामोऽस्य रत्नानि विविधानि वसूनि च। ग्रामान राष्ट्राणि वा तस्य हरिष्यामो विभागशः॥
en: We will all take his various jewels and wealth and divide amongst ourselves his villages and provinces.

description: The going of Susharma and others to Matsya country
sn: अथवा गोसहस्राणि शुभानि च बहूनि च। विविधानि हरिष्यामः प्रतिपीड्य पुरं बलात्॥
en: Invading his city by force we shall carry away his thousands of excellent kine of varicus kinds.

description: The going of Susharma and others to Matsya country
sn: कौरवैः सह संगत्य त्रिगर्तेश्च विशाम्पते। गास्तस्यापहरामोऽद्य सर्वेश्चैव सुसंहताः॥
en: O emperor, uniting the Kaurava army with Trigarta, we will today carry away his collections of kine with all.

description: The going of Susharma and others to Matsya country
sn: निबनीमोऽस्य पौरुषम्। हत्वा चास्य चमूं कृत्स्नां वशमेवानयामहे॥
en: Arranging our army we shall destroy his manliness; or completely destroying his army we shall bring him under our subjection.

description: The going of Susharma and others to Matsya country
sn: तं वशे न्यायतः कृत्वा सुखं वत्स्यामहे वयम्। भवतां बलवृद्धिश्च भविष्यति न संशयः॥
en: Having brought him under our control by lawful means we shall live happily in our kingdom and undoubtedly your power shall increase.

description: The going of Susharma and others to Matsya country
sn: तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं तस्य कर्णो राजानमब्रवीत्। सूक्तं सुशर्मणा वाक्यं प्राप्तकालं हितं च नः॥ संविभागेन कृत्वा तु
en: Hearing those words Karna said to the king Susharman has spoken well; it is a good opportunity and is likely to be beneficial to us.

description: The going of Susharma and others to Matsya country
sn: तस्मात् क्षिप्रं विनिर्यामो योजयित्वा वरूथिनीम्। विभज्य चाप्यनीकानि यथा वा मन्यसेऽनघ॥
en: If you like, O sinless one, we shall speedily issue out by collecting our forces and arranging them in divisions.

description: The going of Susharma and others to Matsya country
sn: प्राज्ञो वा कुरुवृद्धोऽयं सर्वेषां नः पितामहः। आचार्यश्च यथा द्रोणः कृपः शारद्वतस्तथा। मन्यन्ते ते यथा सर्वे तथा यात्रा विधीयताम्॥
en: Or so arrange the expedition, as is liked by Sharadvata's son Kripa, the preceptor Drona and the wise and the aged grand-father of the Kurus; O king of the earth, consulting with each other we shall speedily start to gainour end.

description: The going of Susharma and others to Matsya country
sn: सम्मन्त्र्य चाशु गच्छामः साधनार्थं महीपतेः। किं च नः पाण्डवैः कार्यं हीनार्थबलपौरुषैः॥
en: What business have we with the Pandavas who have been shorn of wealth, army and manliness. They have either gone away for good or repaired to the abode of Yama.

description: The going of Susharma and others to Matsya country
sn: अत्यन्तं वा प्रणष्टास्ते प्राप्ता वापि यमक्षयम्। यामो राजन् निरुद्विग्ना विराटनगरं वयम्। आदास्यामो हि गास्तस्य विविधानि वसूनि च॥
en: Shorn of anxiety, O king, we will repair to the city of Virata and bring his kine and diverse wealth.

description: The going of Susharma and others to Matsya country
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततो दुर्योधनो राजा वाक्यमादाय तस्य तत्। वैकर्तनस्य कर्णस्य क्षिप्रमाज्ञापयत् स्वयम्॥ शासने नित्यसंयुक्तं दुःशासनमनन्तरम्। सह वृद्धस्तु सम्मन्त्र्य क्षिप्रं योजय वाहिनीम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Thereupon accepting the words of Karna, the son of Vikartana, the king Duryodhana, himself speedily commanded Dushasana, born immediately after him, and always obeying his behest: “Consulting with our elders, arrange our army without any delay."

description: The going of Susharma and others to Matsya country
sn: ते यथोद्देशं च गच्छामः सहितास्तत्र कौरवैः। सुशर्मा च यथोद्दिष्टं देशं यातु महारथः।
en: We, with all the Kauravas will go to the place, appointed. Let the mighty car-warrior Susharma also go as commanded.

description: The going of Susharma and others to Matsya country
sn: त्रिगर्तेः सहितो राजा समग्रबलवानहः॥ प्रागेव हि सुसंवीतो मत्स्यस्य विषयं प्रति।
en: Accompanied by Trigartas and the entire army and conveyances to the kingdom of Matsya concealing his intention.

description: The going of Susharma and others to Matsya country
sn: जघन्यतो वयं तत्र यास्यामो दिवसान्तरे! विषयं मत्स्यराजस्य सुसमृद्धं सुसंहताः॥
en: Following them, we will start the next day, well-prepared, for the prosperous territory of the king of Matsya's.

description: The going of Susharma and others to Matsya country
sn: यान्तु सहितास्तत्र विराटनगरं प्रति। क्षिप्रं गोपान् समासाद्य गृह्णन्तु विपुलं धनम्॥
en: Let them with (Trigarta) go to the city of Virata and securing speedily his kine, let them take his immense wealth.

description: The going of Susharma and others to Matsya country
sn: गवां शतसहस्राणि श्रीमन्ति गुणवन्ति च। वयमप्यनुगृहीमो द्विधा कृत्वा वरूथिनीम्॥
en: Going there in two detachments we will also take his thousand excellent kine endued with all qualities.

description: The going of Susharma and others to Matsya country
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ते स्म गत्वा यथोद्दिष्टां दिशं वह्वेर्महीपते। संनद्धा रथिनः सर्वे सपदाता बलोत्कटाः॥ प्रति वैरं चिकीर्षन्तो गोषु गृद्धा महाबलाः। आदातुं गा: सुशर्माथ कृष्णपक्षस्य सप्तमीम्॥ अपरे दिवसे सर्वे राजन् सम्भूय कौरवाः। अष्टम्यां ते न्यगृह्णन्त गोकुलानि सहस्रशः॥
en: king, those heroes, Trigartas, accompanied by their terribly powerful infantry, proceeded towards the south east। wishing to fight with Virata in order to take possession of his kine. Susharma also started on the dark half of the month. Then on the day following the Kauravas, accompanied by their army, began to seize kine by thousands.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततस्तेषां महाराज तत्रैवामिततेजसाम्। छद्मलिङ्गप्रविष्टानां पाण्डवानां महात्मनाम्॥ व्यतीतः समयः सम्यग् वसतां वै पुरोत्तमे। कुर्वतां तस्य कर्माणि विराटस्य महीपतेः। :॥
en: Vaishampayana said O great king, entering the service of the king Virata and living in that excellent city, the high-souled Pandavas of immeasurable prowess, passed the promised period in disguise, without being detected.

sn: कीचके तु हते राजा विराटः परवीरहा। परां सम्भावनां चक्रे कुन्तीपुत्रे युधिष्ठिरे॥
en: After the death of Kichaka, the powerful king Virata, the slayer of hostile heroes, began to form great expectations of the sons of Kunti.

sn: ततस्त्रयोदशस्यान्ते तस्य वर्षस्य भारत। सुशर्मणा गृहीतं तद् गोधनं तरसा बहु॥
en: Thereupon, O descendant of Bharata, after the expiration of the thirteenth year, Susharma by force seized many of his kine.

sn: ततो जवेन महता गोपः पुरमथाव्रजत्। स दृष्ट्वा मत्स्यराजं च रथात् प्रस्कन्ध कुण्डली॥५। शूरैः परिवृतं योधैः कुण्डलाङ्गदधारिभिः। संवृतं मन्त्रिभिः सार्धं पाण्डवैस्च महात्मभिः॥
en: Then a herdsman came with great speed to the city; coming down from the car and seeing the king of Matsya with ear-rings, consulting with his counsellors, the high-souled Pandavas and surrounded by heroes and warriors, adorned with ear-rings and bracelets,

sn: तं सभायां महाराजमासीनं राष्ट्रवर्धनम्। सोऽब्रवीदुपसंगम्य विराटं प्रणतस्तदा॥
en: And approaching the great king Virata, the enhancer of kingdom, seated in the court, he, with humility, said.

sn: अस्मान् युधि विनिर्जित्य परिभूय सबान्धवान्। गवां शतसहस्राणि त्रिगर्ताः कालयन्ति ते॥
en: Vanquishing and humiliating us with our relatives in battle, the Trigartas are taking away thousands of your kine.'

sn: तान् परीप्सस्व राजेन्द्र मा नेशुः पशवस्तव। तच्छ्रुत्वा नृपतिः सेनां मत्स्यानां समयोजयत्।।९।
en: O king of kings, "rescue them speedily so that they may not be lost.” Hearing his words the king collected his Matsya, army.

sn: रथनागाश्वकलिलां पत्तिध्वजसमाकुलाम्। राजानो राजपुत्राश्च तनुत्राण्यथ भेजिरे॥
en: Consisting of cars, elephants, horses, infantry and pennons. The kings and princes put on their respective armours.

sn: भानुमन्ति विचित्राणि शूरसेव्यानि भागशः। सवज्रायसग तु कवचं तत्र काञ्चनम्॥ विराटस्य प्रियो भ्राता शतानीकोऽभ्यहारयत्। सर्वपारसवं वर्म कल्याणपटलं दृढम्॥ शतानीकादवरजो मदिराक्षोऽभ्यहारयत्। शतसूर्यं शतावर्ती शतबिन्दु शताक्षिमत्॥ अभेद्यकल्पं मत्स्यानां राजा कवचमाहरत्। उत्सेधे यस्य पद्मानि शतं सौगन्धिकानि च॥ सुवर्णपृष्ठं सूर्याभं सूर्यदत्तोऽभ्यहारयत्। दृढमायसगर्भं च श्वेतं वर्म शताक्षिमत्॥ विराटस्य सुतो ज्येष्ठो वीरः शङ्खोऽभ्यहारयत्। शतशश्च तनुत्राणि यथास्वं ते महारथाः॥ योत्स्यमाना अनह्यन्त देवरूपाः प्रहारिणः। सूपस्करेषु शुभ्रेषु महत्सु च महारथाः॥
en: Brilliant, variegated and worthy of being worn by heroes according to their respective divisions. Virata's beloved brother Shatanika put on an armour made of adamant and adorned with gold. Madiraksha, next born to Shatanika, put on a strong armour plaited with gold and capable of withstanding every weapon. The armour, which the king of Matsya's himself wore, invincible, adorned with a hundred suns, a hundred was circles, a hundred spots, and a hundred eyes. The armour, that Suryadatta put on, was radiant like the sun, plaited with gold and broad like a hundred fragrant lotuses. The one, that Virata's eldest son Sankasha put on, was invulnerable, inade of burnished steel and adorned with a hundred golden eyes. In this way hundreds of god-like and powerful heroes, mighty carwarriors, adorned with weapons, put on their coats of mail.

sn: पृथक् काञ्चनसंनाहान् रथेष्वश्वानयोजयन्। सूर्यचन्द्रप्रतीकाशे रथे दिव्ये हिरण्मये॥ महानुभावो मत्स्यस्य ध्वज उच्छिश्रिये तदा। अथान्यान् विविधाकारान् ध्वजान् हेमपरिष्कृतान्।।१९ यथास्वं क्षत्रियाः शूरा रथेषु समयोजयन्। अथ मत्स्योऽब्रवीद् राजा शतानीकं जघन्यजम्॥
en: Then they yoked to their excellent white cars, horses, equipped in mail. Matsya's glorious standard was hoisted on his beautiful car decked with gold and resembling the sun or moon in lustre. Other Kshatriya heroes too hoisted on their own cars golden flags of various forms and contrivances. Then the king of Matsya said to his younger brother Shatanika.

sn: कङ्कबल्लवगोपाला जामग्रन्थिश्च वीर्यवान्। युद्ध्येयुरिति मे बुद्धिवर्तते नात्र संशयः॥
en: There is no doubt Kanka, Ballava, Tantipala and the greatly energetic Damagranthi will fight.

sn: एतेषामपि दीयन्तां रथा ध्वजपताकनः। कवचानि च चित्राणि दृढानि च मृदूनि च॥
en: Give them cars adorned with flags and pennons, and variegated armours, invulnerable, and easy to wear.

sn: प्रतिमुढान्तु गात्रेषु दीयन्तामायुधानि च। वीराङ्गरूपाः पुरुषा नागराजकरोपमाः॥
en: Let them put on these on their persons; give them also weapons. That persons thus assuming heroic forms and resembling arms of elephant chiefs,

sn: नेमे जातु न युध्येरन्निति मे धीयते मतिः। एतच्छ्रुत्वा तु नृपतेर्वाक्यं त्वरितमानसः।
en: Cannot fight, I can not lead myself to believe.” Hearing those words of the king, who was anxiously hurrying on,

sn: शतानीकस्तु पार्थेभ्यो स्थान् राजन् समादिशत्॥ सहदेवाय राज्ञे च भीमाय नकुलाय च।
en: O king, Shatanika, ordered chariots for the sons of Pritha-Sahadeva, the king Bhima and Nakula.

sn: तान् प्रहृष्टांस्तत: सूता राजभक्तिपुरस्कृताः॥ निर्दिष्टा नरदेवेन रथाञ्छीघ्रमयोजयन्।
en: Then those charioteers, delightedly having the devotion to the king always before them, speedily got the cars ready as commanded by the king.

sn: कवचानि विचित्राणि मृदूनि च दृढानि च।॥ विराटः प्रादिशद् यानि तेषामक्लिष्टकर्मणाम्। तान्यामुच्य शरीरेषु दंशितास्ते परंतपाः॥ रथान् हयैः सुसम्पन्नानास्थाय च नरोत्तमाः।
en: Those slayers of foes then put on their persons those strong, easy and variegated armours which the king Virata had ordered for (those heroes) of unwearied actions. Then ascending cars drawn by good horses, those best of men,

sn: निर्ययुर्मुदिताः पार्थाः शत्रुसंघावमर्दिनः॥ तरस्विनश्छन्नरूपाः सर्वे युद्धविशारदाः। रथान् हेमपरिच्छन्नानास्थाय च महारथाः॥ विराटमन्वयुः पार्थाः सहिताः कुरुपुङ्गवाः। चत्वारो भ्रातरः शूराः पाण्डवाः सत्यविक्रमाः॥ भीमाश्च मत्तमातङ्गा प्रभिन्नकरटामुखाः। क्षरन्तश्चैव नागेन्द्राः सुदन्ताः षष्टिहायनाः॥ स्वारूढा युद्धकुशलैः शिक्षिता हस्तिसादिभिः। राजानमन्वयुः पश्चाच्चलन्त इव पर्वताः॥ विशारदानां मुख्यानां हृष्टानां चारुजीविनाम्। अष्टौ रथसहस्राणि दश नागशतानि च॥ षष्टिश्चाश्वसहस्राणि मत्स्यानामभिनिर्ययुः।
en: The repressors of hostile army, the sons of Pritha, delightedly issued out. Those mighty car-warriors, the four heroic brothers, the Pandavas, of unfailing prowess, living in disguise, endue with celerity of movements and all well-skilled in the art of war, the sons of Pritha, ascending golden cars, those foi most of Kurus, followed Virata. Dreadful and infuriated elephants, sixty years old with beautiful tusks and rent temples and temporal juice trickling down, appearing like clouds pouring rain, driven by trained and skilled heroes, followed the king like so many moving hills. The leading heroes of Matsya who delightedly followed the king had eight thousand cars, a thousand elephants and sixty thousand horses.

sn: तदनीकं विराटस्य शुशुभे भरतर्षभ॥ सम्प्रयातं तदा राजन् निरीक्षन्तं गवां पदम्।
en: O foremost of the Bharatas, that army of Virata, issuing out marking the foot-prints of the kine, looked beautiful.

sn: तद् बलाग्यं विराटस्य सम्प्रस्थितमशोभत। दृढायुधजनाकीर्णं गजाश्वरथसंकुलम्॥
en: While marching, that best of armies, belonging to Virata, filled with soldiers armed with strong weapons, abounding in elephants, horses and cars, looked really splendid.

description: The encounter between Susharma and Virata
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच निर्याय नगराच्छूरा व्यूढानीकाः प्रहारिणः। त्रिगर्तानस्पृशन् मत्स्याः सूर्ये परिणते सति॥
en: Vaishampayana said Issuing out from the city, those heroic repressors, the Matsya's, arranged in battle array, met the Trigartas when the sun had passed the meridian.

description: The encounter between Susharma and Virata
sn: ते त्रिगर्ताश्च मत्स्याश्च संरब्धा युद्धदुर्मदाः। अन्योन्यमभिगर्जन्तो गोषु गृद्धा महाबलाः॥
en: The mighty and powerful Trigartas and Matsya's, both worked up with ire and irrepressible in battle, desirous of possessing kine, sent up a loud war-cry.

description: The encounter between Susharma and Virata
sn: भीमाश्च मत्तमातङ्गास्तोमराङ्कुशनोदिताः। ग्रामणीयैः समारूढाः कुशलैर्हस्तिसादिभिः॥
en: Terrible and infuriated elephants, mounted by skillful heroes of both sides, were urged on with spikes and hooks.

description: The encounter between Susharma and Virata
sn: तेषां समागमो घोरस्तुमुलो लोहमर्षणः। घ्नतां परस्परं राजन् यमराष्ट्रविवर्धनः॥ देवासुरसमो राजन्नासीत् सूर्येऽवलम्बति। पदातिरथनागेन्द्रहयारोहबलौघवान्॥
en: The combat that took place, O king, when the sun was declining, between the infantry and cavalry, chariots and elephants of both sides, resembling that which took place in the days of yore between the gods and demons, was dreadful, fierce, hair-stirring and calculated to increase the dominion of Yama.

description: The encounter between Susharma and Virata
sn: अन्योन्यमभ्यापततां निघ्नतां चेतरेतरम्। उदतिष्ठद् रजो भौम प्राज्ञायत किंचन॥
en: As the combatants rushed on slaying each other there arose a thick cloud of dust in which nothing could be seen.

description: The encounter between Susharma and Virata
sn: पक्षिणश्चापतन् भूमौ सैन्येन रजसाऽऽवृताः। इषुभिर्व्यतिसर्पद्भिरादित्योऽन्तरधीयत॥
en: Covered with dust raised by the soldiers the birds began to drop down on earth and the sun himself disappeared behind the thick cloud of arrows.

description: The encounter between Susharma and Virata
sn: खद्योतैरिव संयुक्तमन्तरिक्षं व्यराजत। रुक्मपृष्ठानि चापानि व्यतिषिक्तानि धन्विनाम्॥ पततां लोकवीराणां सव्यदक्षिणमस्यताम्। रथा रथैः समाजग्मुः पादातैश्च पदातयः॥
en: The sky shone resplendent as if with (a number of) fire-flies. Changing their bows feathered in gold from one hand to another, the heroes began to smite each other discharging their shafts right and left. The charioteers fought with charioteers, the infantry fought with infantry.

description: The encounter between Susharma and Virata
sn: सादिनः सादिभिश्चैव गजैश्चापि महागजाः। असिभिः पदृिशैः प्रासैः शक्तिभिस्तोमरैरपि॥
en: The cavalry with cavalry and elephants with mighty elephants. With sword axes, Prasas, Shaktis, and Tomaras,

description: The encounter between Susharma and Virata
sn: संरब्धाः समरे राजन् निजघ्नुरितरेतरम्। निघ्नन्तः समरेऽन्योन्यं शूराः परिघबाहवः॥
en: They, enraged, O king, struck each other in the encounter. Although these mighty armed heroes struck each other,

description: The encounter between Susharma and Virata
sn: न शेकुरभिसंरब्धाः शूरान् कर्तुं पराङ्मुखान्। कृत्तोत्तरोष्ठं सुनसं कृत्तकेशमलंकृतम्॥ अदृश्यत शिरश्छिन्नं रजोध्वस्तं सकुण्डलम्। अदृश्यंस्तत्र गात्राणि शरैश्छिन्नानि भागशः॥ शालस्कन्धनिकाशानि क्षत्रियाणां महामृधे। नागभोगनिकाशैश्च बाहुभिश्चन्दनोक्षितैः॥ आस्तीर्णा वसुधा भाति शिरोभिश्च सकुण्डलैः। रथिनां रथिभिश्चात्र सम्प्रहारोऽभ्यवर्तत॥
en: None of them succeeded in weakening the other. And severed heads, some with beautiful noses, some with upper lips wounded, some adorned with ear-rings, some cut into twain about the well-arranged hair, were seen rolling in the field covered with dust. And in that battle field were seen the limbs of Kshatriya heroes cut off by shafts and lying like trunks of Sala trees. And spread over with heads adorned with car-rings and arms smeared with sandal looking like the bodies of snakes the battlefield appeared in beauty. The charioteers approached the charioteers striking each other.

description: The encounter between Susharma and Virata
sn: सादिभिः सादिनां चापि पदातीनां पदातिभिः। उपाशाम्यद् रजो भौमं रुधिरेण प्रसर्पता॥
en: The cavalry (encountered) the cavalry and the infantry the infantry and the dreadful dust was drenched by the over-spreading blood.

description: The encounter between Susharma and Virata
sn: कश्मलं चाविशद् घोरं निर्मर्यादमवर्तत। उपाविशन् गरुत्मन्तः शरैर्गाढं प्रवेजिताः। अन्तरिक्षे गतिर्येषां दर्शनं चाप्यरुध्यत॥ ते जन्तः समरेऽन्योन्यं शूराः परिघबाहवः। न शेकुरभिसंरब्धाः शूरान् कर्तुं पराङ्मुखान्॥ शतानीकः शतं हत्वा विशालक्षश्चतुःशतम्। प्रविष्टौ महतीं सेनां त्रिगर्तानां महारथौ॥
en: There arose a dreadful combat shorn of all considerations. And having their course and vision obstructed by the shower of arrows the vultures began to come down. Although these mighty-armed heroes struck cach other in the battle none of them could overpower his antagonist. Shatanika slaying a hundred, and Vishalaksha a four hundred,

description: The encounter between Susharma and Virata
sn: तौ प्रविष्टौ महासेनां बलवन्तौ मनस्विनौ। आर्छतां बहुसंरब्धौ केशाकेशि रथारथिः॥
en: These two mighty car-warriors entered into the huge army of Trigartas. And having entered into the great army those two intelligent and powerful.

description: The encounter between Susharma and Virata
sn: लक्षयित्वा त्रिगर्तानां तौ प्रविष्टौ रथव्रजम्। अग्रतः सूर्यदत्तश्च मदिराक्षश्च पृष्ठतः॥
en: (Heroes) (began an encounter) hand-tohand, hair to hair and car to car. And marking they entered into the collection of cars belonging to the Trigartas.

description: The encounter between Susharma and Virata
sn: विराटस्तत्र संग्रामे हत्वा पञ्चशतान् रथान्। हयानां च शतान्यष्टौ हत्वा पञ्च महारथान्॥
en: Destroying five hundred cars in that encounter with Suryadatta before and Madiraksha after him,

description: The encounter between Susharma and Virata
sn: चरन् स विविधान् मार्गान् रथेन रथसत्तमः। त्रिगर्तानां सुशर्माणमार्च्छद् रुक्मरथं रणे॥
en: And slaying eight hundred horses, five mighty car-warriors, that foremost of charioteers began to display many manuvaeres in that field of battle.

description: The encounter between Susharma and Virata
sn: तौ व्यवाहरतां तत्र महात्मानौ महाबलौ। अन्योन्यमभिगर्जन्तौ गोष्ठेषु वृषभाविव॥
en: He then came upon Susharma, the king of Trigartas mounted on a golden chariot; there those two high-souled and highly powerful (heroes) struck (each other)

description: The encounter between Susharma and Virata
sn: ततो राजा त्रिगर्तानां सुशर्मा युद्धदुर्मदः। मत्स्य समायाद् राजानं द्वैरथेन नरर्षभः॥
en: Roaring like two bulls in a pasture. Thereupon the king of Trigartas, Susharman, irrepressible in battle,

description: The encounter between Susharma and Virata
sn: ततो स्थाभ्यां रथिनौ व्यतीयतुरमर्षणौ। शरान् व्यसृजतां शीघ्रं तोयधारा घना इव॥
en: That foremost of men invited the king of Matsya to a single combat on the chariot. Thereupon those two car-warriors, worked up with fury, rushed upon each other in their cars.

description: The encounter between Susharma and Virata
sn: अन्योन्यं चापि संरब्धौ विचेस्तुरमर्षणौ। कृतास्त्रौ निशितैर्बाणैरसिशक्तिगदाभृतौ॥
en: They discharged arrows quickly like clouds pouring torrents of rain. Enraged with each other the (two) wrathful (heroes) moved about,

description: The encounter between Susharma and Virata
sn: ततो राजा सुशर्माणं विव्याध दशभिः शरैः। पञ्चभिः पञ्चभिश्चास्य विव्याध चतुरो हयान्॥
en: Skilled in weapons, and armed with sharpened arrows, swords, shaktis and maces. Then the king pierced Susharman with ten arrows,

description: The encounter between Susharma and Virata
sn: तथैव मत्स्यराजानं सुशर्मा युद्धदुर्मदः। पञ्चाशता शितैर्बाणैर्विव्याध परमास्त्रवित्॥ ततः सैन्यं महाराज मत्स्यराजसुशर्मणोः। नाभ्यजानात् तदान्योन्यं सैन्येन रजसाऽऽवृतम्॥३
en: Each of his four horses also with five arrows. Susharma too, irrepressible in battle and acquainted with the use of fatal weapons, pierced, the king of Matsya with fifty sharpened arrows. Then, Ogreat king, on account of the dust in the field of battle, the soldiers of both Susharma and the king of Matsya could not recognise each other.

description: The discomfiture of Susharma in Goharana
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तमसाभिप्लुते लोके रजसा चैव भारत। अतिष्ठन् वै मुहूर्तं तु व्यूढानीका: प्रहारिणः॥
en: Vaishampayana said O descendant of Bharata, the whole world being enshrouded in dust and natural darkness, the soldiers of both sides, without breaking the battle array, stopped for some time.

description: The discomfiture of Susharma in Goharana
sn: ततोऽन्धकारं प्रणुदन्नुदतिष्ठत चन्द्रमाः। कुर्वाणो विमलां रात्रि नन्दयन् क्षत्रियान् युधि॥
en: Then dispelling the darkness the moon rose, making the night clear and gladdening the Kshatriyas in the battle field.

description: The discomfiture of Susharma in Goharana
sn: ततः प्रकाशमासाद्य पुनर्युद्धमवर्तत। घोररूपं ततस्ते स्म नावैक्षन्त परस्परम्॥
en: When every thing came in view, the battle began again; and it became so dreadful that they could not see each other.

description: The discomfiture of Susharma in Goharana
sn: ततः सुशर्मा त्रैगर्तः सह भ्रात्रा यवीयसा। अभ्यद्रवन्मत्स्यराजं रथवातेन सर्वशः॥
en: Then Susharma, the king of Trigartas, with his younger brother and surrounded by his cars, encountered the king of Matsya.

description: The discomfiture of Susharma in Goharana
sn: ततो रथाभ्यां प्रस्कन्ध भ्रातरौ क्षत्रियर्षभौ। गदापाणी सुसंरब्धौ समभ्यद्रवतां रथान्॥
en: Then descending from their chariots, those two brothers, the foremost of Kshatriyas, worked up with anger, with mace in hands, rushed towards (the enemy's) cars.

description: The discomfiture of Susharma in Goharana
sn: तथैव तेषां तु बलानि तानि क्रुद्धान्यथान्योन्यमभिद्रवन्ति। गदासिख श्च परश्वधैश्च प्रासैश्च तीक्ष्णाग्रसुपीतधारैः॥
en: The hostile armies fiercely assailed each other with maces, swords, scimitars, axes, nooses, and with sharpened points.

description: The discomfiture of Susharma in Goharana
sn: बलं तु मत्स्यस्य बलेन राजा सर्वं त्रिगर्ताधिपतिः सुशर्मा। प्रमथ्य जित्वा च प्रसह्य मत्स्यं विराटमोजस्विनमभ्यधावत्।॥
en: Having assailed and vanquished with energy the entire army of the king of Matsya's, Susharman, the king of Trigartas, rushed furiously at the highly energetic Virata.

description: The discomfiture of Susharma in Goharana
sn: तौ निहत्य पृथग् धुर्यावुभौ तौ पार्ष्णसारथी। विरथं मत्स्यराजानं जीवग्राहमगृह्णताम्॥
en: Having slain severally his two horses, his charioteer as also the soldiers who protected him in the rear they took the king of Matsya captive, even alive, deprivation of his car.

description: The discomfiture of Susharma in Goharana
sn: तमुन्मथ्य सुशर्माथ युवतीमिव कामुकः। स्यन्दनं स्वं समारोप्य प्रययौ शीघ्रवाहनः॥
en: Then assailing him fiercely like a lustful person (oppressing) a female, they placed him on the car and speedily went out.

description: The discomfiture of Susharma in Goharana
sn: तस्मिन् गृहीते विरथे विराटे बलवत्तरे। प्राद्रवन्त भयान्मत्स्यास्त्रिगर्तेरर्दिता भृशम्॥
en: After the powerful Virata, deprived of his car, had been taken captive, the Matsya's, greatly assailed by Trigartas, fled away to different directions in fear.

description: The discomfiture of Susharma in Goharana
sn: तेषु संत्रस्यमानेषु कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः। प्रत्यभाषन्महाबाहुं भीमसेनमरिंदमम्॥
en: Beholding them thus terrified Yudhishthira, the son of Kunti, said to the mighty-armed Bhimasena, the slayer of enemies.

description: The discomfiture of Susharma in Goharana
sn: मत्स्यराजः परामृष्टस्त्रिगर्तेन सुशर्मणा। तं मोचय महाबाहो न गच्छेद् द्विषतां वशम्॥
en: The king of Matsya has been captivated by Susharman, the king of Trigartas; O you of mighty arms, release him so that he may not be subject to the enemies.

description: The discomfiture of Susharma in Goharana
sn: उषिताः स्म सुखं सर्वे सर्वकामैः सुपूजिताः। भीमसेन त्वया कार्या तस्य वासस्य निष्कृतिः॥
en: We have lived happily in his house with our desire satisfied O Bhimasena, you should satisfy that debt.

description: The discomfiture of Susharma in Goharana
sn: भीमसेन उवाच अहमेनं परित्रास्ये शासनात् तव पार्थिवा पश्य युध्यतः सह शत्रुभिः॥
en: Bhimasena said By your command, O king, I shall set him free: behold my great feat of fighting with the enemies.

description: The discomfiture of Susharma in Goharana
sn: मे सुमहत् कर्म स्वबाहुबलमाश्रित्य तिष्ठ त्वं भ्रातृभिः सह। एकान्तमाश्रितो राजन् पश्य मेऽद्य पराक्रमम्॥
en: Stay aside with brothers at a corner depending on the strength of your arms and behold my prowess today.

description: The discomfiture of Susharma in Goharana
sn: सुस्कन्धोऽयं महावृक्षो गदारूप इव स्थितः। अहमेनमपारुज्य द्रावयिष्यामि शात्रवान्॥
en: uprooting this huge tree with a trunk looking like a mace I shall assail the enemies.

description: The discomfiture of Susharma in Goharana
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तं मत्तमिव मातङ्गं वीक्षमाणं वनस्पतिम्। अब्रवीद् भ्रातरं वीरं धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Seeing Bhima look at that tree like an infuriated elephant the heroic and pious king Yudhishthira said to his brother.

description: The discomfiture of Susharma in Goharana
sn: मा भीम साहसं कार्षीस्तिष्ठत्वेष वनस्पतिः। मा त्वां वृक्षण कर्माणि कुर्वाणमतिमानुषम्॥
en: "Do not commit such a rash act, О Bhima, let the tree stand there." You should not with a tree perform superhuman deeds.

description: The discomfiture of Susharma in Goharana
sn: जनाः समवबुध्येरन् भीमोऽयमिति भारत। अन्यदेवायुधं किंचित् प्रतिपद्यस्व मानुषम्॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, people will then recognize you and say “This is Bhima". Take you therefore, some other human weapon,

description: The discomfiture of Susharma in Goharana
sn: चापं वा यदि वा शक्तिं निस्त्रिंशं वा परश्वधम्। यदेव मानुषं भीम भवेदन्यैरलक्षितम्॥ तदेवायुधमादाय मोक्षयाशु महीपतिम्। यमौ च चक्ररक्षौ ते भवितारौ महाबलौ॥ सहिताः समरे तत्र मत्स्यराज परीप्सत।
en: A bow, or a dart, sword or battle-axe. Taking a weapon that is human, release the king, O Bhima, speedily, so that people may not recognize you. The highly powerful twins will be the protectors of your wheels. Being united together in battle, release the king of Matsya.

description: The discomfiture of Susharma in Goharana
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्तस्तु वेगेन भीमसेनो महाबलः॥ गृहीत्वा तु धनुः श्रेष्ठं जवेन सुमहाजवः।
en: Thus accosted the highly powerful Bhimasena, gifted with great speed, took up with great force his best of bows,

description: The discomfiture of Susharma in Goharana
sn: व्यमुञ्चच्छरवर्षाणि सतोय इव तोयदः॥ तं भीमो भीमकर्माणं सुशर्माणमथाद्रवत्।
en: And discharged from it a shower of shafts like a cloud surcharged with water. Bhima then fell upon Susharma of dreadful deeds.

description: The discomfiture of Susharma in Goharana
sn: विराटं समवीक्ष्यैनं तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति चावदत्॥ सुशर्मा चिन्तयामास कालान्तकयमोपमम्।
en: Casting his looks on Virata he said to (Susharma) “stay stay.” Susharma thought him to be Yama-the very regent of death.

description: The discomfiture of Susharma in Goharana
sn: तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति भाषन्तं पृष्ठतो रथपुङ्गवः। पश्यतां सुमहत् कर्म महद् युद्धमुपस्थितम्॥
en: That foremost of charioteers saw him at his back exclaiming "stay, stay, behold a highly great feat-a mighty encounter is at hand."

description: The discomfiture of Susharma in Goharana
sn: परावृत्तो धनुर्गृह्य सुशर्मा भ्रातृभिः सह। निमेषान्तरमात्रेण भीमसेनेन ते रथाः॥
en: Taking up his bow, Susharma with his brothers turned back and within the twinkling of an eye those cars (were destroyed by) Bhimasena.

description: The discomfiture of Susharma in Goharana
sn: रथानां च गजानां च वाजिनां च ससादिनाम्। सहस्रशतसङ्घाता शूराणामुग्रधन्विनाम्॥
en: And hundreds of thousand of chariots, elephants, horses, horsemen and brave and powerful bowmen were over thrown by him before the very presence of Virata.

description: The discomfiture of Susharma in Goharana
sn: पातिता भीमसेनेन विराटस्य समीपतः। पत्तयो निहतास्तेषां गदां गृह्य महात्मना॥
en: Their infantry was slain by the high-souled (Bhima with mace in hand): Beholding such a fight Susharma, irrepressible in battle,

description: The discomfiture of Susharma in Goharana
sn: तद् दृष्ट्वा तादृशं युद्धं सुशर्मा युद्धदुर्मदः। चिन्तयामास मनसा किं शेषं हि बलस्य मे। अपरो दृश्यते सैन्ये पुरा मग्नो महाबले॥
en: Thought within his mind: "Is this the end of my army. I see my brother drowned in the midst of his powerful army.”

description: The discomfiture of Susharma in Goharana
sn: आकर्मपूर्णेन तदा धनुषा प्रत्यदृश्यत। सुशर्मा सायकांस्तीक्ष्णान् क्षिपते च पुनः पुनः॥
en: Stretching his bow to his ear Susharma began to retreat and discharge repeatedly sharpened shafts.

description: The discomfiture of Susharma in Goharana
sn: ततः समस्तास्ते सर्वे तुरगानभ्यचोदयन्। दिव्यमस्त्रं विकुर्वाणास्त्रिगर्तान् प्रत्यमर्षणाः॥ तान् निवृत्तरथान् दृष्ट्वा पाण्डवान् सा महाचमूः। वैराटिः परमक्रुद्धो युयुधे परमाल्लुतम्॥
en: Beholding the Pandavas return to their cars the entire huge army urged on their horses and began to assail the Trigartas with excellent weapons. Virata's son, greatly enraged, began to display highly wonderful feats in battle.

description: The discomfiture of Susharma in Goharana
sn: सहस्रमवधीत् तत्र कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः। भीमः सप्त सहस्राणि यमलोकमदर्शयत्॥
en: Kunti's son Yudhishthira killed one thousand and Bhima dispatched seven thousand.

description: The discomfiture of Susharma in Goharana
sn: नकुलश्चापि सप्तैव शतानि प्राठिोच्छरैः। शतानि त्रीणि शूराणां सहदेवः प्रतापवान्॥ युधिष्ठिरसमादिष्टो निजघ्ने पुरुषर्षभः। ततोऽभ्यपतदत्युग्रः सुशर्माणमुदायुधः॥ हत्वा तां महती सेनां त्रिगर्तानां महारथः। ततो युधिष्ठिरो राजा त्वरमाणो महारथः॥
en: Nakula killed with arrows seven hundred and powerful Sahadeva the foremost of men, commanded by Yudhishthira, slew three hundreds of heroes. Slaying that huge army of Trigartas, the mighty car-warrior, Yudhishthira, with uplifted weapon, attacked him sorely with shafts.

description: The discomfiture of Susharma in Goharana
sn: अभिपत्य सुशर्माणं शरैरभ्याहन भृशम्। सुशर्मापि सुसंरब्धस्त्वरमाणो युधिष्ठिरम्॥ अविध्यन्नवभिर्बाणैश्चतुर्भिश्चतुरो हयान्। ततो राजन्नाशुकारी कुन्तीपुत्रो वृकोदरः॥ समासाद्य सुशर्माणमश्वानस्य व्यपोथयत्। पृष्ठगोपांश्च तस्याथ हत्वा परमसायकैः॥ अथास्य सारथिं क्रुद्धो रथोपस्थादपातयत्। चक्ररक्षश्च शूरो वै मदिराक्षोऽतिविश्रुतः॥
en: Susharma, too greatly enraged, with impetuosity pierced Yudhishthira with nine shafts and his four horses with four. Then 0 king, the quick-coursing son of Kunti, Vrikodara, nearing Susharma, assailed his horses. Having slain the soldiers that were in the rear with huge shafts, he, in anger, brought down his (Susharmas') charioteer from his car. The heroic protector of the wheels celebrated as Madiraksha,

description: The discomfiture of Susharma in Goharana
sn: समायाद् विरथं दृष्ट्वा त्रिगर्तं प्राहरत् तदा। ततो विराटः प्रस्कन्ध रथादथ सुशर्मणः॥
en: Seeing Trigarta deprived of his car, came there. Then coming down from Susharma's car Virata.

description: The discomfiture of Susharma in Goharana
sn: गदां तस्य परामृश्य तमेवाभ्यद्रवद् बली। स चचार गदापाणिर्वृद्धोऽपि तरुणो यथा।॥
en: Heroic (as he was) took up his Susharma's mace and rushed upon him, And he, with mace in hand moved about like a young man, although an old man.

description: The discomfiture of Susharma in Goharana
sn: पलायमानं त्रैगर्त दृष्ट्वा भीमोऽभ्यभाषत। राजपुत्र निवर्तस्व न ते युक्तं पलायनम्॥
en: Beholding the king of Trigarta taking to his heels, Bhima said :"Desist, O prince, it does not behove you to fly away.

description: The discomfiture of Susharma in Goharana
sn: अनेन वीर्येण कथं गास्त्वं प्रार्थयसे बलात्। कथं चानुचरांस्त्यक्त्वा शत्रुमध्ये विषीदसि॥
en: With such powers how could you think of taking away the kine? Why forsaking your followers do you droop in the midst of your enemies?

description: The discomfiture of Susharma in Goharana
sn: इत्युक्तः स तु पार्थेन सुशर्मा रथयूथपः। तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति भीमं स सहसाऽभ्यद्रवद् बली॥
en: Being thus addressed by Partha, the powerful Susharma, owner of cars, all on a sudden rushed upon Bhima (saying "stay! stay!!').

description: The discomfiture of Susharma in Goharana
sn: भीमस्तु भीमसंकाशो रथात् प्रस्कन्ध पाण्डवः। प्राद्रवत् तूर्णमव्यग्रो जीवितेप्सुः सुशर्मणः॥४६
en: Getting down from the car the dreadful Bhimasena, the son of Pandu, rushed towards him with coolness, desirous of taking Susharma's life.

description: The discomfiture of Susharma in Goharana
sn: तं भीमसेनो धावन्तमभ्यधावत वीर्यवान्। त्रिगर्तराजमादातुं सिंहः क्षुद्रमृगं यथा॥
en: With a view to get hold of the king of Trigarta approaching towards him the energetic Bhimasena rushed upon him like a lion upon a small deer.

description: The discomfiture of Susharma in Goharana
sn: अभिद्रुत्य सुशर्माणं केशपक्षे परामृशत्। समुद्यम्य तु रोषात् तं निष्पिपेष महीतले॥
en: Rushing upon Susharma he held him by the hair; and lifting him up in anger he dashed him against the earth.

description: The discomfiture of Susharma in Goharana
sn: पदा मूर्ध्नि महाबाहुः प्राहरद् विलपिष्यतः। तस्य जानुं ददौ भीमो जने चैनमरलिना।
en: The mighty-armed (Bhima) struck him on the head, who was weeping, with his foot and placing his keen on his breast dealt him severe blows.

description: The discomfiture of Susharma in Goharana
sn: स मोहमगमद् राजा प्रहारवरपीडितः॥ तस्मिन् गृहीते विरथे त्रिगर्तानां महारथे।
en: Assailed by the stroke the king lost consciousness. The mighty car-warrior, the king of Trigartas, deprived of car, being scized,

description: The discomfiture of Susharma in Goharana
sn: अभज्यत बलं सर्वं त्रैगर्तं तद् भयातुरम्॥ निवर्त्य गास्ततः सर्वा: पाण्डुपुत्रा महारथाः।
en: The entire army, of Trigarta afflicted with fear, were dispersed. Thereupon preventing the kine from being taken away, all the mighty carwarriors, the sons of Pandu,

description: The discomfiture of Susharma in Goharana
sn: अवजित्य सुशर्माणं धनं चादाय सर्वशः॥ स्वबाहुबलसम्पन्ना ह्रीनिषेवा यतव्रताः।
en: Discomfitting Susharma and taking all his wealth-they, endued with the strength of their own arms, humble and observant of vows,

description: The discomfiture of Susharma in Goharana
sn: विराटस्य महात्मानः परिक्लेशविनाशनाः॥ स्थिताः समक्षं ते सर्वे त्वथ भीमोऽभ्यभाषत॥
en: The destroyers of the affliction of the highsouled Virata, all stationed themselves before him. Then Bhima said:

description: The discomfiture of Susharma in Goharana
sn: नायं पापसमाचारो मत्तो जीवितुमर्हति। किं तु शक्यं मया कर्तुं यद् राजा सततं घृणी॥५४।
en: This perpetrator of impious deeds does not deserve living at my hands. But what can I do, the king is always merciful.

description: The discomfiture of Susharma in Goharana
sn: गले गृहीत्वा राजानमानीय विवशं वशम्। तत एनं विचेष्टन्तं बद्धवा पार्थो वृकोदरः॥
en: Then holding the king (Susharma) by the neck who was unconscious, bringing him and binding him who could make no exertion, Vrikodara, the son of Pritha,

description: The discomfiture of Susharma in Goharana
sn: रथमारोपयामास विसंज्ञं पांसुगुण्ठितम्। अभ्येत्य रणमध्यस्थमभ्यगच्छद् युधिष्ठिरम्॥
en: Placed him on the chariot who was insensible and covered with dust. Then approaching Yudhishthira who was in the midst of the battle field,

description: The discomfiture of Susharma in Goharana
sn: दर्शयामास भीमस्तु सुशर्माणं नराधिपम्। प्रोवाच पुरुषव्याघ्रो भीममाहवशोभिनम्॥
en: Bhima showed to him the king Susharma. The foremost of men then said to Bhima. beautifying the battle field.

description: The discomfiture of Susharma in Goharana
sn: तं राजा प्राहसद् दृष्ट्वा मुच्यतां वै नराधमः। एवमुक्तोऽब्रवीद् भीमः सुशर्माणं महाबलम्॥
en: Then seeing him the king smilingly said: “Release this wretch." Thus addressed Bhima said to the highly powerful Susharma.

description: The discomfiture of Susharma in Goharana
sn: भीम उवाच जीवितुं चेच्छसे मूढ हेतुं मे गदतः शृणु। दासोऽस्मीति त्वया वाच्यं संसत्सु च सभासु च।।५९
en: “If you wish to live, O wretch, hear my words. You should say in courts and assemblies that you are our slave.

description: The discomfiture of Susharma in Goharana
sn: एवं ते जीवितं दद्यामेष युद्धजितो विधिः। तमुवाच ततो ज्येष्ठो भ्राता सप्रणयं वचः॥
en: Under this condition I can grant you your life: such is the custom of the victorious." Then his eldest brother addressed to him affectionate words.

description: The discomfiture of Susharma in Goharana
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच मुञ्च मुञ्चाधमाचारं प्रमाणं यदि ते वयम्। दासभावं गतो ह्येष विराटस्य महीपतेः। अदासो गच्छ मुक्तोऽसि मैवं कार्षीः कदाचन॥
en: "If you regard me, release this wicked wretch. He has already become the slave of the great king Virata. (Then he said to Susharma): “You are free, go and never do such a thing."

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्ते तु सव्रीडः सुशर्माऽऽसीदधोमुखः। स मुक्तोऽभ्येत्य राजानमभिवाद्य प्रतस्थिवान्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Thus addressed Susharma was filled with shame and bent down his head. And liberated and bowing to the king he went away.

sn: विसृज्य तु सुशर्माणं पाण्डवास्ते हतद्विषः। स्वबाहुबलसम्पन्ना ह्रीनिषेवा यतव्रताः॥ संग्रामशिरसो मध्ये तां रात्रिं सुखिनोऽवसन्। ततो विराटः कौन्तेयानतिमानुषविक्रमान्। अर्चयामास वित्तेन मानेन च महारथान्॥
en: Having released Susharma, the Pandavas, then enemies slain, endowed with the strength of arms, observant of vows, and modest, passed that night happily in the midst of the battle-field. Then Virata honoured, with wealth and respect, those mighty car-warriors, the of Kunti, who were gifted with superhuman prowess.

sn: विराट उवाच यथैव मम रत्नानि युष्माकं तानि वै तथा। कार्यं कुरुत वै सर्वे यथाकामं यथासुखम्॥
en: sons Virata said All these my jewels are as much mine as yours; do you all work as you like and as may conduce to your happiness.

sn: ददाम्यलंकृताः कन्या वसूनि विविधानि च। मनसश्चाप्यभिप्रेतं युद्धे शत्रुनिबर्हणाः॥
en: O repressors of foes in battle, I shall center upon you women adorned with ornaments, plentiful riches and other things that you may like.

sn: युष्माकं विक्रमादद्य मुक्तोऽहं स्वस्तिमानिह। तस्माद् भवन्तो मत्स्यानामीश्वराः सर्व एव हि॥
en: By your prowess today I have been saved from peril. I am now crowned with victory. Do you all become the kings of Matsya's.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तथेतिवादिनं मत्स्यं कौरवेयाः पृथक् पृथक्। ऊचुः प्राढालयः सर्वे युधिष्ठिरपुरोगमाः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Those Kauravas, headed by Yudhishthira, with folded heads, said each severally to the king of the Matsya who had addressed them thus.

sn: प्रतिनन्दाम ते वाक्यं सर्वं चैव विशाम्पते। एतेनैव प्रतीताः स्म यत् त्वं मुक्तोऽद्य शत्रुभिः॥
en: O king, we have been perfectly pleased with what you have said. It is a matter of gratification to us that you have been released from the enemies.

sn: ततोऽब्रवीत् प्रीतमना मत्स्यराजो युधिष्ठिरम्। पुनरेव महाबाहुर्विराटो राजसत्तमः॥
en: Then the mighty armed, Virata, the king of Matsya's, the foremost of monarchs, again delightedly said to Yudhishthira.

sn: एहि त्वामभिषेक्ष्यामि मत्स्यराजस्तु नो भवान्॥ मनसश्चाप्यभिप्रेतं यथेष्टं भुवि दुर्लभम्।
en: Come, I shall install you and be the king of us, the Matsya's. Whatever you desire in mind, any thing, even though rare on earth,

sn: तत् तेऽहं सम्प्रदास्यामि सर्वमर्हति नो भवान्॥ रत्नानि गाः सुवर्णं च मणिमुक्तमथापि च।
en: I shall confer upon you all-jewels, kine, gold, pearls, jems and all; you deserve every thing.

sn: वैयाघ्रपद्य विप्रेन्द्र सर्वथैव नमोऽस्तु ते॥ त्वत्कृते ह्यद्य पश्यामि राज्यं संतानमेव च।
en: I bow to you, it is for you that once more today I see my kingdom and children.

sn: यतश्च जातसंरम्भो न च शत्रुवशं गतः॥ ततो युधिष्ठिरो मत्स्यं पुनरेवाभ्यभाषत।
en: Through you, afflicted with fear I did not pass into the hands of the enemies." Yudhishthira then again said to the king of Matsya's.

sn: प्रतिनन्दामि ते वाक्यं मनोज्ञं मत्स्य भाषसे॥ आनृशंस्यपरो नित्यं सुसुखी सततं भव।
en: O king of Matsya, we highly relish the delightful words you have given vent to. Being humane towards all do you live happily ever and anon.

sn: गच्छन्तु दूतास्त्वरितं नगरं तव पार्थिव।॥ सुहृदां प्रियमाख्यातुं घोषयन्तु च ते जयम्।
en: O king, let emissaries speedily go to your city, to communicate this pleasant tidings to your friends and announce your victory.

sn: ततस्तद्वचनान्मत्स्यो दूतान् राजा समादिशत्।।१६ आचक्षध्वं पुरं गत्वा संग्रामविजयं मम।
en: At his words the king of Matsya's dispatched his emissaries, saying: “Going to my city do you announce my victory.

sn: कुमार्यः समलंकृत्य पर्यागच्छन्तु मे पुरात्॥ वादित्राणि च सर्वाणि गणिकाश्च स्वलंकृताः।
en: Let damsels and courtezans, adorned with ornaments, come out of the city with various musical instruments.

sn: एतां चाज्ञां ततः श्रुत्वा राज्ञा मत्स्येन नोदिताः। तामाज्ञां शिरसा कृत्वा प्रस्थिता हृष्टमानसाः॥
en: Hearing this his command and being thus addressed by the Matsya king, they, placing his command on their heads, delightedly went away.

sn: ते गत्वा तत्र तां रात्रिमथ सूर्योदयं प्रति। विराटस्य पुराभ्याशे दूता जयमघोषयन्॥
en: Going to the city that very night they announced, at the hour of sun-rise, the victory of the king.

description: The praise of Uttara in Goharana
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच याते त्रिगर्तान् मत्स्ये तु पशूस्तान् वै परीप्सति। दुर्योधनः सामात्यो विराटमुपयादथ॥
en: Vaishampayana said After the king of Matsya's had gone out in pursuit of Trigartas for recovering his kine, Duryodhana, with his courtiers, attacked his kingdom.

description: The praise of Uttara in Goharana
sn: भीष्मो द्रोणश्च कर्णश्च कृपश्च परमास्त्रवित्। द्रौणिश्च सौबलश्चैव तथा दुःशासन प्रभो॥ विविंशतिर्विकर्णश्च चित्रसेनश्च वीर्यवान्। दुर्मुखो दुःशलश्चैव ये चैवान्ये महारथाः॥ एते मत्स्यानुपागम्य विराटस्य महीपतेः। घोषान् विद्राव्य तरा गोधनं जहरोजसा॥
en: Bhishma, Drona, Karna, Kripa, versed in the use of the best of weapons, Ashvathama, Subala's son, Dushasana, O king, Vivinshati, Vikarana, the greatly energetic Chitrasena, Durmukha, Dushasana and many other highly powerful heroes, overtaking Matsya, speedily drove away his cow-herds and got possession of the king by force.

description: The praise of Uttara in Goharana
sn: षष्टिं गवां सहस्राणि कुरवः कालयन्ति च। महता रथवंशेन परिवार्य समन्ततः॥
en: Encircling all sides with a huge array of cars, the Kauravas seized the sixty thousand kine.

description: The praise of Uttara in Goharana
sn: गोपालानां तु घोषस्य हन्यतां तैर्महारथैः। आरावः सुमहानासीत् सम्प्रहारे भयंकरे॥
en: A great cry was set up in that dreadful combat by the cow-herds struck by those inighty car-warriors.

description: The praise of Uttara in Goharana
sn: गोपध्याक्षो भयत्रस्तो रथमास्थाय सत्वरः। जगाम नगरायैव परिक्रोशंस्तदाऽऽर्तवत्॥
en: Greatly stricken with grief the chief, of the cow-herds, quickly got upon a chariot and started for the city bewailing in affliction.

description: The praise of Uttara in Goharana
sn: स प्रविश्य पुरं राज्ञो नृपवेश्माभ्ययात् ततः। अवतीर्य रथात् तूर्णमाख्यातुं प्रविवेश ह॥
en: Entering the city of the king, he went to the palace and getting down from the car proceeded to relate (what took place).

description: The praise of Uttara in Goharana
sn: दृष्ट्वा भूमिजयं नाम पुत्रं मत्स्यस्य मानिनम्। तस्मै तत् सर्वमाचष्ट राष्ट्रस्य पशुकर्षणम्॥
en: Seeing the haughty son of Matsya Bhuminjaya, he described to him everything about the royal kine being taken away.

description: The praise of Uttara in Goharana
sn: षष्टिं गवां सहस्राणि कुरवः कालयन्ति ते। तद् विजेतुं समुत्तिष्ठ गोधनं राष्ट्रवर्धन॥
en: The Kauravas are taking away your sixty thousand kine; rise up, o increaser of territories, to bring them back.

description: The praise of Uttara in Goharana
sn: राजपुत्र हितप्रेप्सुः क्षिप्रं निर्याहि च स्वयम्। त्वां हि मत्स्यो महीपाल: शून्यपालमिहाकरोत्॥
en: If you wish your well-being, speedily go out yourself, O prince. The emperor Matsya left you alone in the city.

description: The praise of Uttara in Goharana
sn: त्वया परिषदो मध्ये श्लाघते स नराधिपः। पुत्रो ममानुरूपश्च शूरश्चेति कुलोद्वहः॥
en: The king speaks highly of you in the court: My son, after me, is heroic and the supporter (of the prestige) of the race.

description: The praise of Uttara in Goharana
sn: इष्वस्त्रे निपुणो योधः सदा वीरश्च मे सुतः। तस्य तत् सत्यमेवास्तु मनुष्येन्द्रस्य भाषितम्॥
en: My son is a heroic warrior, and an expert in the use of shafts. Make good these words of the Emperor.

description: The praise of Uttara in Goharana
sn: आवर्तय कुरूढिात्वा पशून् पशुमतां वर। निर्दहैषामनीकानि भीमेन शरतेजसा॥
en: O you the foremost of those who own cattle, having discomfited the Kurus, do you bring back the animals, consume their soldiers with the dreadful prowess of your shafts,

description: The praise of Uttara in Goharana
sn: धनुश्च्युतै रुक्मपुङ्खैः शरैः संनतपर्वभिः। द्विषतां भिन्ध्यनीकानि गजानामिव युथपः॥
en: Crush down the enemics' life, with straight shafts feathered in gold discharged off your bow like an elephant chief rushing at a herd.

description: The praise of Uttara in Goharana
sn: पाशोपधानां ज्यातन्त्री चापदण्डां महास्वनाम्। शरवर्णां धनुर्वीणां शत्रुमध्ये प्रवादय॥
en: Your bow is like a Vina, the two ends being like ivory pillows; the string is the main chord, the staff is the finger board and the arrows represent the time. Strike this Vina of a bow in the midst of the enemies.

description: The praise of Uttara in Goharana
sn: श्वेता रजतसंकाशा रथे युज्यन्तु ते हयाः। ध्वजं च सिंहं सौवर्णमुच्छ्रयन्तु तव प्रभो॥
en: Let your horses, white as silver, be yoked to the cars and let your flag, having the emblem of a golden lion, he hoisted up, O lord.

description: The praise of Uttara in Goharana
sn: रुक्मपुङ्खाः प्रसन्नाया मुक्ता हस्तवता त्वया। छादयन्तु शराः सूर्यं राज्ञां मार्गनिरोधकाः॥
en: Let your sharp arrows, feathered in gold, discharged by your powerful arms, stand in the way of these kings and overshadow the sun.

description: The praise of Uttara in Goharana
sn: रणे जित्वा कुरून् सर्वान् वज्रपाणिरिवासुरान्। यशो महदवाप्य त्वं प्रविशेदं पुरं पुनः॥
en: Defeating all the Kurus in battle like the holder of Vajra the Asuras and acquiring great fame, return to your city.

description: The praise of Uttara in Goharana
sn: त्वं हि राष्ट्रस्य परमा गतिर्मत्स्यपतेः सुतः। यथा हि पाण्डुपुत्राणामर्जुनो जयतां वरः॥
en: You are the greatest support of the kingdom, the son of Matsya king, like Arjuna, the foremost of the victors amongst the sons of Pandu.

description: The praise of Uttara in Goharana
sn: एवमेव गतिर्नूनं भवान् विषयवासिनाम्। गतिमन्तो वयं त्वद्य सर्वे विषयवासिनः॥
en: Even like him you are forsooth the refuge of those who live in this country; we all look upon you as our protector.

description: The praise of Uttara in Goharana
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच स्त्रीमध्य उक्तस्तेनासौ तद् वाक्यमभयंकरम्। अन्त:पुरे श्लाघमान इदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Being thus addressed by him in the midst of females with fearless words in the inner apartment he gave went to the following praiseworthy words.

sn: उत्तर उवाच अद्याहमनुगच्छेयं दृढधन्वा गवां पदम्। यदि मे सारथिः कश्चिद् भवेदश्वेषु कोविदः॥
en: Uttara said An expert in the use of bow as I am, I shall today go out in pursuit of kine, if some body, skilled in the management of horses, becomes my charioteer.

sn: तं त्वहं नावगच्छामि यो मे यन्ता भवेन्नरः। पश्यध्वं सारथिं क्षिप्रं मम युक्तं प्रयास्यतः॥
en: I do not know of a man who may be iny charioteer; find out out therefore quickly a charioteer who may suit me who am going out.

sn: अष्टाविंशतिरात्रं वा मासं वा नूनमन्ततः। यत् तदासीन्महद् युद्धं तत्र मे सारथिर्हतः॥
en: My charioteer was killed in the great encounter that lasted for a month or at least twenty nights certain.

sn: स लभेयं यदा त्वन्यं हययानविदं नरम्। त्वरावानद्य यात्वाहं समुच्छितमहाध्वजम्॥
en: As soon as I shall get a man experienced in the management of horses I shall immediately start hoisting the huge standard.
