en: Drona, Kripacharya, Vivimshati and Dushasana too turned towards Arjuna immediately. All of them had come hurriedly and began defending Duryodhana from Arjuna's attack at front side or east. Their bows were duly stretched to release arrows.

description: The return of Uttara to his city in the Goharana
sn: न्यालोक्य पूर्णौधनिभानि पार्थः। हंसो यथा मेघमिवापतन्तं धनंजयः प्रत्यतपत् तरस्वी॥
en: As the sun heats up severely the cluster of clouds, Dhananjaya, the son of Kunti began attacking fiercely that Kauravas army return then like a unsurprising flood.

description: The return of Uttara to his city in the Goharana
sn: मस्त्राणि दिव्यानि समाददानाः। न्मेघा यथा भूधरमम्बुवर्गः॥
en: Those warriors holding divine arms and weapons, covered Arjuna from four sides and began shooting arrow at him like the cloud start raining from all sides after a stumble at the mountain.

description: The return of Uttara to his city in the Goharana
sn: ततोऽस्त्रमस्त्रेण निवार्य तेषां गाण्डीवधन्वा कुरुपुङ्गवानाम्। सम्मोहनं शत्रुसहोऽन्यदस्त्रं प्रादुश्चकारैन्द्रिरपारणीयम्॥
en: Arjuna, the holder of Gandiva and capable to face the attacks of enemy, splitted all their arms in pieces by using his own arms and immediately got another arm Sammohana, an specific arm impossible to destroy by other.

description: The return of Uttara to his city in the Goharana
sn: ततो दिशश्चानुदिशो विवृत्य शरैः सुधारैर्निशितैः सुपत्रैः। गाण्डीवघोषेण मनांसि तेषां महाबलः प्रव्यथयाञ्चकार॥
en: That great chivalrous had then covered all directions and sub-directions with a volley of arrows having attractive wings and acute edge. The continuous sound made by his Gandiva bow with arrow shots, frightened the Kauravas' warriors.

description: The return of Uttara to his city in the Goharana
sn: ततः पुनर्भीमरवं प्रगृह्य दो महाशङ्खमुदारघोषम्। व्यनादयत् स प्रदिशो दिशः खं भुवं च पार्थो द्विषतां निहन्ता॥
en: The son of Kunti, the killer of enemy had then caught with both hands his conch (Mahashankha) known for its disastrous sound covering a distant area under its echo and started blowing. The echo of that conch gripped all directions, sub-directions, sky and the earth also.

description: The return of Uttara to his city in the Goharana
sn: ते शङ्खनादेन कुरुप्रवीराः सम्मोहिताः पार्थसमीरितेन। उत्सृज्य चापानि दुरासदानि सर्वे तदा शान्तिपरा बभूवुः॥
en: The sound was so loud that it fainted all warriors fighting for Kauravas and they stunned in unconscious state so deep as the arms/weapons in their hands were dropped down when the conch was blown by Arjuna.

description: The return of Uttara to his city in the Goharana
sn: तथा विसंज्ञेषु च तेषु पार्थः स्मृत्वा च वाक्यानि तथोत्तरायाः। मुवाच यावत् कुरवो विसंज्ञाः॥ आचार्यशारद्वतयोः सुशुक्ले कर्णस्य पीतं रुचिरं च वस्त्रम्। द्रौणेश्च राज्ञश्च तथैव नीले वस्त्रे समादत्स्व नरप्रवीर॥
en: Just when those warriors were fainted, the facts told by Uttara came to Arjuna's mind and he instructed Uttara, the son of Matsya king to slip carefully out from that place before they could regain conscious. He further said that Uttara should take-off white clothes from the body of preceptor Drona and Kripacharya, the yellow garment from Karnas body and blue garments from the body of Ashvatthama and king Duryodhana.

description: The return of Uttara to his city in the Goharana
sn: भीष्मस्य संज्ञां तु तथैव मन्ये जानाति सोऽस्त्रप्रतिघातमेषः। मेवं हि यातव्यममूढसंज्ञैः॥
en: (Arjuna again instructed) I understand, Bhishma, our grand-father knows the method to take Sammohana off and he would still in conscious. As the method to walk through vicinity of warriors not lost of conscious envisages, you should leave (cross) his horses at the left.

description: The return of Uttara to his city in the Goharana
sn: रश्मीन् समुत्सृज्य ततो महात्मा रथादवप्लुत्य विराटपुत्रः। वस्त्राण्युपादाय महारथानां तूर्णं पुन: स्वं रथमारुरोह॥
en: The son of Virata immediately left the rein of his horses and jumped down from chariot. He collected the clothes of those warriors and again rod on his chariot.

description: The return of Uttara to his city in the Goharana
sn: ततोऽन्वशासच्चतुरः सदश्वान् पुत्रो विराटस्य हिरण्यकक्षान्। ते तद् व्यतीयुर्ध्वजिनामनीकं श्वेता वहन्तोऽर्जुनमाजिमध्यात्॥
en: The son of Virata then drove those four attractive horses duly decorated with gold trimmings and yoked with his chariot. Those white horses passed through the middle part of battle-field with Arjuna on chariot crossed soon the circle of army of chariot riders with flags fixed on them.

description: The return of Uttara to his city in the Goharana
sn: तथानुयान्तं पुरुषप्रवीरं भीष्मः शरैरभ्यहनत् तरस्वी। स चापि भीष्मस्य हयान् निहत्य विव्याध पार्थो दशभिः पृषत्कैः॥
en: Bhishma shot an arrow at Arjuna and injured him when he saw him leaving that place so hideously. Arjuna on his part killed his horses and injured him by shooting ten arrows.

description: The return of Uttara to his city in the Goharana
sn: ततोऽर्जुनो भीष्ममपास्य युद्धे विद्ध्वास्य यन्तारमरिष्टधन्वा। न्मेधं विदार्येव सहस्ररश्मिः॥
en: Arjuna with his mighty bow left Bhishma on battle-field, shot hard his charioteer with acute arrows and thus, came out safely from the circle of chariots. He graced like sun god shining after the clouds shattered.

description: The return of Uttara to his city in the Goharana
sn: लम्वा हि संज्ञां तु कुरुप्रवीराः पार्थं निरीक्ष्याथ सुरेन्द्रकल्पम्। रणे विमुक्तं स्थितमेकमाजौ स धार्तराष्ट्रस्त्वरितं बभाषे॥
en: The warriors fighting for Kauravas got conscious soon and saw Arjuna standing lonely outside the circle of chariots. He seemed valorous like Indra, the king of gods. Having seen him alone, Duryodhana, the son of Dhritarashtra enquired immediately.

description: The return of Uttara to his city in the Goharana
sn: स्तथा प्रमनीत यथा न मुच्येत्। तमब्रवीच्छान्तनवः प्रहस्य क्व ते गता बुद्धिरभूत् क्व वीर्यम्॥ रुत्सृज्य बाणांश्च धनुर्विचित्रम्॥
en: "O Grandfather! How had he escaped from your hands? Churn him so badly as he could not escape." Bhishma, the son of Shantanu toughed and replied Duryodhana "O king! Where had your wit gone when you fell down unconscious here and your bow and arrows left aside? Tell me that where was your valour at that time?

description: The return of Uttara to his city in the Goharana
sn: त्वेष बीभत्सुरलं नृशंसं कर्तुं न पापेऽस्य मनो विशिष्टिम्॥ त्रैलोक्यहेतोर्न जहेत् स्वधर्म सर्वे न तस्मानिहता रणेऽस्मिन्। क्षिप्रं कुरून् याहि कुरुप्रवीर विजित्य गाश्च प्रतियातु पार्थः। मा ते स्वकोऽर्थो निपतेत मोहात् तत् संविदातव्यमरिष्टबन्धम्॥
en: Arjuna cannot behave cruelly as his mind never entangles in coming vice. He cannot abandon his religion even if enticed for ruling on trio-worlds. This is the reason, he did not killed us at that unconscious state. O one of pioneer warriors in Kuru race, go back to Kuru state immediately. Let Arjuna return to his destination with cows. Keep in mind your own interest and don't become cause for defeat of your own purpose. All of us should do whatever may ensure our welfare.

description: The return of Uttara to his city in the Goharana
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच दुर्योधनस्तस्य तु तन्निशम्य पितामहस्यात्महितं वचोऽथ। अतीतकामो युधि सोऽत्यमर्षी राजा विनिःश्वस्य बभूव तूष्णीम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said-O Janamejaya! King Duryodhana gave up an idea to continue fight any more following the advice of grand-father in his interest. He kept mum in the matter sobbing deep with in heart for the humiliation suffered.

description: The return of Uttara to his city in the Goharana
sn: तद् भीष्मवाक्यं हितमीक्ष्य सर्वे धनंजयाग्निं च विवर्धमानम्। दुर्योधनं ते परिरक्षमाणाः॥
en: All other warriors affirmed the advice of Bhishma as they guessed of eruption of fire more and more in the form of Arjuna. Finally, they arrived at a conclusion to go back at their state with duly defending Duryodhana.

description: The return of Uttara to his city in the Goharana
sn: तान् प्रस्थितान् प्रीतमनाः स पार्थो धनंजयः प्रेक्ष्य कुरुप्रवीरान्। अभाषमाणोऽनुनयं मुहूर्त वचोब्रवीत् सम्परिहत्य भूयः॥
en: Dhananjaya, the son of Kunti filled with joy within heart when he saw Kaurava's army moving from there. He kept mum for more than half an hour without saying anything in request and submission.

description: The return of Uttara to his city in the Goharana
sn: पितामहं शान्तनवं च वृद्धं द्रोणं गुरुं च प्रणिपत्य मू । ज्छरैर्विचित्रैरभिवाद्य चैव॥ दुर्योधनस्योत्तमरत्नचित्रं चिच्छेद पार्थो मुकुटं शरेण।
en: He then saluted with his head bowed on the feet of grand-father Bhishma and preceptor Drona and talked on certain matters for a while. He then saluted through application of arrows varied ways to Ashvatthama, Kripacharya and other respected Kauravas (Banahika, Somadatta etc.) and cut the excellent gem-studded crown off from Duryodhana's head through an arrow.

description: The return of Uttara to his city in the Goharana
sn: आमन्त्र्य वीरांश्च तथैव मान्यान्। गाण्डीवघोषेण विनाद्य लोकान्॥ स देवदत्तं सहसा विनाद्य विदार्य वीरो द्विषतां मनांसि।
en: He similarly, bid farewell with other respected warriors, spreaded echo on stretch to his bow through out the world and threatened the enemies when he blew his conch Devadatta.

description: The return of Uttara to his city in the Goharana
sn: ध्वजेन सर्वानभिभूय शत्रून् सहेममालेन विराजमानः॥ दृष्ट्वा प्रयातांस्तु कुरून् किरीटी हृष्टोऽब्रवीत् तत्र स मत्स्यपुत्रम्। आवर्तयाश्वान् पशवो जितास्ते याताः परे याहि पुरं प्रहृष्टः॥
en: Thus Arjuna attained special grace with ecstacy of victory on all enemies. The flag trimmed with garland of gold duly erected on his chariot seemed as if humiliating his all enemies. Arjuna with a crown on head; exhilarated observing return of Kauravas from there. He said Uttara, the son of Matsya's king-"O Prince! Turn your horses back now. Your cows are won and enemies have departed. Hence, move now towards city with pleasure.

description: The return of Uttara to his city in the Goharana
sn: देवास्तु दृष्ट्वा महदद्भुतं तद् युद्धं कुरूणां सह फाल्गुनेन। जग्मुर्यथास्वं भवनं प्रतीताः पार्थस्य कर्माणि विचिन्तयन्तः॥
en: The gods enjoyed with ecstacy the fight between Arjuna and Kaurava and returned to their respective palaces with Arjuna's valour on their lips.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततो विजित्य संग्रामे कुरून् स वृषभेक्षणः। समानयामास तदा विराटस्य धनं महत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having defeated the Kurus, that one (Arjuna), having the eyes of a bull, brought back the immense wealth of Virata.

sn: गतेषु च प्रभग्नेषु धार्तराष्ट्रेषु सर्वतः। वनान्निष्क्रम्य गहनाद् बहवः कुरुसैनिकाः॥ भयात् संत्रस्तमनसः समाजग्मुस्ततस्ततः। मुक्तकेशास्त्वदृश्यन्त स्थिताः प्राहालयस्तदा॥
en: While the sons of Dhritarashtra, after being defeated, were going away, a large number of Kuru soldiers, coming out of the deep forest, appeared slowly before Partha, their hearts filled with fear. They stood before him with joined hands and disheveled hair.

sn: क्षुत्पिपासापरिश्रान्ता विदेशस्था विचेतसः। ऊचुः प्रणम्य सम्भ्रान्ताः पार्थ किं करवाम ते॥
en: Exhausted with hunger and thrust, come in a foreign country, beside themselves with fear, and bewildered, they bowed down to the son of Pritha and said "We are your slaves." (At which Arjuna said):

sn: स्वस्ति व्रजत वो भद्रं न भेतव्यं कथंचन। नाहमार्ताब्दिाघांसामि भृशमाश्वासयामि वः॥
en: “Welcome! May you are well. Go away. You have nothing to fear. I assure you, I will not kill them who are stricken with fear."

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तस्य तामभयां वाचं श्रुत्वा योधाः समागताः। आयुः कीर्तियशोदाभिस्तमाशीर्भिरनन्दयन्॥
en: Hearing these words of assurance, the warriors blessed him by praising his illustrious deeds and wishing him a long life.

sn: मुत्सृज्य शत्रून् विनिवर्तमानम्। विराटराष्ट्राभिमुखं प्रयान्तं नाशक्नुवंस्तं कुरवोऽभियातुम्॥
en: The Kauravas could not withstand Arjuna, when, after dispersing the enemies, he proceeded towards Virata's city, like an elephant with rent temples.

sn: ततः स तन्मेपमिवापतन्तं विद्राव्य पार्थः कुरुसैन्यवृन्दम्। मत्स्यस्य पुत्रं द्विषतां निहन्ता वचोऽब्रवीत् सम्परिरभ्य भूयः॥
en: Having dispersed the Kuru army, like a violent wind scattering the clouds, that destroyer of foes, Partha, respectfully said to the Matsya Prince.

sn: पितुः सकाशे तव तात सर्वे वसन्ति पार्था विदितं तवैव। तान् मा प्रशंसेनगरं प्रविश्य भीतः प्रणश्यद्धि स मत्स्यराजः॥
en: "It is known to you alone that the sons of Pritha are living with your father. Do not applaud them after going to the city, for then, the king of Matsya's will die in fear.

sn: मया जिता सा ध्वजिनी कुरूणां मया च गावो विजिता द्विषद्भ्यः। पितुः सकाशं नगरं प्रविश्य त्वमात्मनः कर्म कृतं ब्रवीहि॥
en: Rather entering the city, do you announce this as your own work before your father, saying “The army of the Kurus has been defeated by me, and the kine have been rescued by me from the enemies."

sn: उत्तर उवाच यत् ते कृतं कर्म न पारणीयं तत् ते कर्म कर्तुं मम नास्ति शक्तिः। न त्वां प्रवक्ष्यामि पितुः सकाशे यावन्न मां वक्ष्यसि सव्यसाचिन्॥
en: Uttara said “I have not the power to accomplish the deed you have done. I shall not, however, O Savyasachin, disclose you before my father till you do not ask me to do it."

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच राच्छिद्य सर्वं च धनं कुरुभ्यः। मभ्येत्य तस्थौ शरविक्षताङ्गः॥
en: Having defeated the enemy and rescued the kine from the Kurus, Vishnu, again came back to the cremation ground; and coming to the Shami tree, he stood there, with his body wounded with arrows.

sn: ततः स वह्निप्रतिमो महाकपिः सहैव भूतैर्दिवमुत्पपात। तथैव माया विहिता बभूव ध्वजं च सैंह युयुजे रथे पुनः॥
en: Then that huge monkey, resembling the fire, got up into the sky with other creatures. In the same way the illusion died away, and he twisted his banner, having the emblem of a lion again on his car.

sn: विधाय तच्चायुधमाजिवर्धनं कुरूत्तमानामिषुधीः शरांस्तथा। प्रायात् स मत्स्यो नगरं प्रहृष्टः किरीटिना सारथिना महात्मना॥
en: Then, having kept, as before, the arrows and quivers of those great Pandu princes and also the other weapon (Gandiva) which makes the battle dreadful, the Matsya Prince, having Kiritin for his charioteer, gladly started for his city.

sn: पार्थस्तु कृत्वा परमार्यकर्म निहत्य शत्रून् द्विषतां निहन्ता। चकार वेणी च तथैव भूयो जग्राह रश्मीन् पुनरुत्तरस्य। विवेश हृष्टो नगरं महामना बृहन्नलारूपमुपेत्य सारथिः॥
en: Having performed a highly wonderful deed and slain the foe, Partha, too, finding his hair into a band, as before, took the reins from Uttara's hands. That high-souled one (Partha), again assuming the form of Brihannala, gladly entered the city as the charioteer.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततो निवृत्ताः कुरवः प्रभग्ना वशमास्थिनाः। हस्तिनापुरमुद्दिश्य सर्वे दीना ययुस्तदा॥
en: Then, all the Kurus, routed and defeated started for Hastinapur with a dejected mind.

sn: पन्थानमुपसङ्गम्य फाल्गुनो वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥ राजपुत्र प्रत्यवेक्ष समानीतानि सर्वशः। गोकुलानि महाबाहो वीर गोपालकैः सह॥ ततोऽपराठे यास्यामो विराटनगरं प्रति। आश्वास्य पाययित्वा च परिप्लाव्य च वाजिनः॥ गच्छन्तु त्वरिताश्चेमे गोपालाः प्रेषितास्त्वया। नगरे प्रियमाख्यातुं घोषयन्तु च ते जयम्॥
en: Phalguni, on his way back, addressed Uttara, saying "O Prince, O mighty-armed hero, the kine have been escorted in advance by the cow-herds. Having refreshed the horses with drink and bath, we shall enter the city in the afternoon. Let the cow-herd, sent by you, go in advance to the city with the good news and announce your victory."

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच नाज्ञापयद् वचनात् फाल्गुनस्य। आचक्षध्वं विजयं पार्थिवस्य भग्नाः परे विजिताश्चापि गावः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Thereupon, at the words of Phalguni, Uttara speedily dispatched messengers to announce the king's victory with the messages “The enemies have been defeated and the kine rescued."

sn: इत्येवं तौ भारतमत्स्यवीरौ सम्मन्त्र्य सङ्गम्य ततः शमी ताम्। वुत्सृष्टमारोपयतां स्वभाण्डम्॥ माच्छिद्य सर्वं च धनं कुरुभ्यः। वैराटिरायानगरं प्रतीतोथ बृहन्नलासारथिना प्रवीरः॥
en: No translation

description: The colloquy between Uttara and Virata
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच धनं चापि विजित्याशु विराटो वाहिनीपतिः। विवेश नगरं हृष्टश्चतुर्भिः पाण्डवैः सह॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having recovered speedily his wealth, Virata, the master of the army entered delightedly the city with the four Pandavas.

description: The colloquy between Uttara and Virata
sn: जित्वा त्रिगर्तान् संग्रामे गाश्चैवादाय सर्वशः। अशोभत महाराज सहपार्थः श्रिया वृतः॥
en: Having defeated the Trigartas in battle and rescued the kine, the king shone there, in the inidst of the Partha's.

description: The colloquy between Uttara and Virata
sn: तमासनगतं वीरं सुहृदां हर्षवर्धनम्। उपासाञ्चक्रिरे सर्वे सह पाथैः परंतपाः॥
en: All the heroes, with the sons of Pritha, worshipped the heroic (Virata) the increaser of friend's joy, who was seated on his throne.

description: The colloquy between Uttara and Virata
sn: उपतस्थुः प्रकृतयः समस्ता ब्राह्मणैः सह। सभाजित: ससैन्यस्तु प्रतिनन्द्याथ मत्स्यराट्॥ विसर्जयामास तदा द्विजांश्च प्रकृतीस्तथा। तथा स राजा मत्स्यानां विराटो वाहिनीपतिः॥ उत्तरं परिपप्रच्छ क्व यात इति चाब्रवीत्। आचख्युस्तस्य तत्सर्वं स्त्रियः कन्याश्च वेश्मनि॥ अन्तःपुरचराश्चैव कुरुभिर्गोधनं हृतम्। विजेतुमभिसंरब्ध एक एवातिसाहसात्। बृहन्नलासहायश्च निर्गतः पृथिवीठ्ठायः॥ उपयातानतिरथान् भीष्मं शान्तवनं कृपम्। कर्णं दुर्योधनं द्रोणं द्रोणपुत्रं च षड् रथान्॥
en: All his subjects, along with the Brahmanas and the soldiers, came and adored him. Welcoming them, the king of Matsya sent away the Brahmanas and the subjects. Then the king of Matsya's, Virata, the commander of armies, enquired of Uttara and said “Where has he gone?” Then all the females and girls of the inner apartments said “The kine were taken away by the Kurus. Out o excessive bravery, the conqueror of the earth alone, with Brihannala as his help, went out to vanquish them-the six powerful car-warriors Bhishma the son of Shantanu, Kripa, Karna, Duryodhana, Drona and Drona's son, who all have come.”

description: The colloquy between Uttara and Virata
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच राजा विराटोऽथ भृशाभितप्तः श्रुत्वा सुतं त्वेकरथेन यातम्। बृहन्नलासारथिमाजिवर्धनं प्रोवाच सर्वानथ मन्त्रिमुख्यान्॥
en: Hearing that his brave son had gone out with only one car and Brihannala as his charioteer, the king Virata was filled with sorrow and said to his leading ministers:

description: The colloquy between Uttara and Virata
sn: सर्वथा कुरवस्ते हि ये चान्ये वसुधाधिपाः। त्रिगर्तान् निःसृताञ्छ्रुत्वा न स्थास्यन्ति कदाचन।।१०।
en: “Hearing of the discomfiture of the Trigartas, all the Kurus and other kings will not surely wait there.

description: The colloquy between Uttara and Virata
sn: तस्माद् गच्छन्तु मे योधा बलेन महता वृताः। उत्तरस्य परीप्सार्थं ये त्रिगतैरविक्षताः॥
en: Let those of my warriors, who have not been wounded by Trigartas, go out with a highly powerful army to rescue Uttara."

description: The colloquy between Uttara and Virata
sn: हयांश्च नागांश्च रथांस्च शीघ्रं पदातिसङ्घांश्च ततः प्रवीरान्। प्रस्थापयामास सुतस्य हेतोविचित्रशस्त्राभरणोपपन्नान्॥
en: Saying this, the king Virata soon dispatched for his son, horses, elephants, cars, and a large number of infantry, decked with various dresses and ornaments.

description: The colloquy between Uttara and Virata
sn: एवं स राजा मत्स्यानां विराटो वाहिनीपतिः। व्यादिदेशाथ तां क्षिप्रं वाहिनी चतुरङ्गिणीम्॥
en: Virata, the king of Matsya's and commander of armies, ordered out speedily an army consisting of four divisions.

description: The colloquy between Uttara and Virata
sn: कुमारमाशु जानीत यदि जीवति वा न वा। यस्य यन्ता गतः षण्ढो मन्येऽहं स न जीवति॥
en: He said: “Learn without delay, if the prince is still alive or not. Methinks, he, who has got an useless person for his charioteer, is not yet alive.

description: The colloquy between Uttara and Virata
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तमब्रवीद् धर्मराजो विहस्य विराटराजं तु भृशाभितप्तम्। बृहन्नला सारथिश्चेन्नरेन्द्र परे न नेष्यन्ति तवाद्य गास्ताः॥
en: Then the king Yudhishthira smilingly said to the king Virata, who was greatly stricken with sorrow. If Brihannala has been his charioteer, the enemies will not be able to take away the kine.

description: The colloquy between Uttara and Virata
sn: सर्वान् महीपान् सहितान् कुरुश्च तथैव देवासुरसिद्धयक्षान्। अलं विजेतुं समरे सुतस्ते स्वनुष्ठितः सारथिना हि तेन॥
en: Well guarded by that charioteer, your son will be able to defeat all the kings allied with the Kurus, as well as all the celestials, Asuras and Yakshas.

description: The colloquy between Uttara and Virata
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच अथोत्तरेण प्रहिता दूतास्ते शीघ्रगामिनः। विराटनगरं प्राप्य विजयं समवेदयन्॥
en: In the meantime, the swiftly coursing emissaries, dispatched by Uttara, reached the city and announced the victory.

description: The colloquy between Uttara and Virata
sn: राज्ञस्तत् सर्वमाचख्यौ मन्त्री विजयमुत्तमम्। पराजयं कुरूणां चाप्युपायान्तं तथोत्तरम्॥ सर्वा विनिर्जिता गावः कुरवश्च पराजिताः। उत्तरः सह सूतेन कुशली च परंतपः॥
en: The messenger then described to the king everything-the excellent victory, the defeat of the Kurus, and the expected arrival of Uttara. He said: "All the kine have been rescued, the Kurus have been vanquished, and Uttara, the slayer of enemies, fares well with his charioteer.”

description: The colloquy between Uttara and Virata
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच दिष्ट्या विनिर्जिता गावः कुरवश्च पलायिताः। नाद्भुतं त्वेव मन्येऽहं यत् ते पुत्रोऽजयत् कुरून्।।२०। ध्रुव एव जयस्तस्य यस्य यन्ता बृहन्नला।
en: Yudhishthira said "By good luck it is, that the kine have been rescued and the Kurus have fled away. I do not consider it strange, that your son defeated the Kurus. Victory is secure to him who has got Brihannala as his charioteer.”

description: The colloquy between Uttara and Virata
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततो विराटो नृपतिः सम्प्रहृष्टतनूरुहः॥ श्रुत्वा स विजयं तस्य कुमारस्यामितौजसः।
en: Hearing of the victory of his son of immeasurable energy, the king Virata was greatly delighted, and the hairs of his body stood up.

description: The colloquy between Uttara and Virata
sn: आच्छादयित्वा दूतांस्तान्मन्त्रिणं सोऽभ्यचोदयत्।।२२ राजमार्गाः क्रियन्तां मे पताकाभिरलंकृताः।
en: Then having covered the messengers with presents, he said to the ministers "Let my highway be decorated with flags."

description: The colloquy between Uttara and Virata
sn: पुष्पोपहारैरय॑न्तां देवताश्चापि सर्वशः॥ कुमारा योधमुख्याश्च गणिकाश्च स्वलंकृताः।
en: "Let all the gods be adored with presents of flowers. Let the princes, leading warriors, harlots adorned with ornaments."

description: The colloquy between Uttara and Virata
sn: वादित्राणि च सर्वाणि प्रत्युद्यान्तु सुतं मम॥ घण्टावान मानवः शीघ्रं मत्तमारुह्य वारणम्।
en: And all the musicians go out to receive iny son. Let the man who rings the bell, riding an infuriated elephant.

description: The colloquy between Uttara and Virata
sn: शृङ्गाटकेषु सर्वेषु आख्यातुं विजयं मम॥ उत्तरा च कुमारीभिर्बह्वीभिः परिवारिता। शृङ्गारवेषाभरणा प्रत्युद्यातुं सुतं मम॥
en: Announce my victory at the meeting of the four roads. Let Uttara, too, encircled by many princesses, dressed and adorned in a charming style, go out to receive my son.

description: The colloquy between Uttara and Virata
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच श्रुत्वा चेदं वचनं पार्थिवस्य सर्वं पुरं स्वस्तिकपाणिभूतम्। भेर्यश्च तूर्याणि च वारिजाश्च वेषैः पराध्यैः प्रमदाः शुभाश्च॥ तथैव सूतैः सह मागधैश्च नान्दीवाधाः पणवास्तूर्यवाद्याः। अक्षानाहर सैरन्ध्रि पुराद् विराटस्य महाबलस्य प्रत्युद्ययुः पुत्रमनन्तवीर्यम्॥
en: Hearing the words of the king, all the citizens, with auspicious things in their hands, with cymbals, trumpets and conchs, and gorgeously attired handsome ladies, reciters of hymns, and many other musicians, went out to welcome the highly powerful son of Virata.

description: The colloquy between Uttara and Virata
sn: प्रस्थाप्य सेनां कन्याश्च गणिकाश्च स्वलकृताः। मत्स्यराजो महाप्राज्ञः प्रहृष्ट इदमब्रवीत्॥
en: Having ordered out soldiers, maidens and well-adorned harlots, the wise king delightedly said these words.

description: The colloquy between Uttara and Virata
sn: कङ्क द्यूतं प्रवर्तताम्। तं तथावादिनं दृष्ट्वा पाण्डवः प्रत्यभाषत।॥ न देवितव्यं हृष्टेन कितवेनेति नः श्रुतम्। तं त्वामद्य मुदा युक्तं नाहं देवितुमुत्सहे। प्रियं त ते चिकीर्षामि वर्ततां यदि मन्यसे॥
en: “Bring the dice, O Sairandhri, and let us play, O Kanka.” To him then speaking, We have heard that one, in an ecstasy of joy, should not gamble . I do not wish to play with you today who are filled with joy. I always wish to do you good. If you (still wish), begin.

description: The colloquy between Uttara and Virata
sn: विराट उवाच स्त्रियो गावो हिरण्यं च यच्चान्यद् वसु किञ्चन। न मे किञ्चित् त्वया रक्ष्यमन्तरेणापि देवितुम्॥
en: Virata said Females, kine, gold and other riches whatever I have, nothing you will be able to keep today even if I do not gamble.

description: The colloquy between Uttara and Virata
sn: कङ्क उवाच किं ते द्यूतेन राजेन्द्र बहुदोषेण मानद। देवने बहवो दोषास्तस्मात् तत् परिवर्जयेत्॥
en: Kanka said "O king, O giver of honours, what have you to do with gambling which is attended with so many evils. There are many evils in gambling, and so you should avoid it.

description: The colloquy between Uttara and Virata
sn: श्रुतस्ते यदि वा दृष्टः पाण्डवेयो युधिष्ठिरः। स राष्ट्रं सुमहत् स्फीतं भ्रातृ॑श्च त्रिदशोपमान्॥ राज्यं हारितवान् सर्वं तस्माद् द्यूतं न रोचये। अथवा मन्यसे राजन् दीव्याम यदि रोचते॥
en: You might have heard, if not seen, that the king Yudhishthira lost his vast and prosperous kingdom, his god-like brothers, and everything at a game of dice. I, therefore, do not like this game. If you, however, like, O king, I shall begin.”

description: The colloquy between Uttara and Virata
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच प्रवर्तमाने द्यूते तु मत्स्यः पाण्डवमब्रवीत्। पस्य पुत्रेण मे युद्धे तादृशाः कुरवो जिताः॥ ततोऽब्रवीन्महात्मा स एनं राजा युधिष्ठिरः। बृहन्नला यस्य यन्ता कथं स न जयेद् युधि॥
en: While the play was going on, the Matsya king said to Yudhishthira "Even so very fearful Kauravas have been defeated in battle by my son." Whereto Yudhishthira replied “Why should he not conquer who has got Brihannala as his charioteer?"

description: The colloquy between Uttara and Virata
sn: इत्युक्तः कुपितो राजा मत्स्यः पाण्डवमब्रवीत्। समं पुत्रेण मे षण्ढं ब्रह्मबन्धो प्रशंससि॥
en: At this, being enraged, the king of Matsya's said to the son of Pandu: “O wretch of a Brahman, you speak highly of an eunuch as compared with my son.

description: The colloquy between Uttara and Virata
sn: वाच्यावाच्यं न जानीघे नूनं मामवमन्यसे। भीष्मद्रोणमुखान् सर्वान् कस्मान्न स विजेष्यति॥
en: Have you not an idea of what is proper and what is not proper? Forsooth, you insult me. Why should he not defcat all the heroes headed by Bhishma and Drona?

description: The colloquy between Uttara and Virata
sn: वयस्यत्वात् तु ते ब्रह्मन्नपराधमिमं क्षमे। नेदृशं तु पुनर्वाच्यं यदि जीवितुमिच्छसि॥
en: For the sake of friendship, O Brahmana, I forgive you for this offence. You must not speak so again, if you wish to live."

description: The colloquy between Uttara and Virata
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच यत्र द्रोणस्तथा भीष्मो द्रौणिर्वैकर्तनः कृपः। दुर्योधनश्च राजेन्द्रस्तथान्ये च महारथाः॥ मरुद्गणैः परिवृतः साक्षादपि मरुत्पतिः। कोऽन्यो वृहन्नलायास्तान् प्रतियुध्येत सङ्गतान्॥
en: Yudhishthira said There, where Drona, Bhishma Drona's son, Vikartanas son, Kripa, the king Duryodhana, and other kings and car-warriors are, and where Indra himself is surrounded by Maruts, who else, save Brihannala, can fight with them, all collectively.

description: The colloquy between Uttara and Virata
sn: यस्य बाहुबले तुल्यो न भूतो न भविष्यति। अतीव समरं दृष्ट्वा हर्षो यस्योपजायते॥ योऽजयत् सङ्गत्तान् सर्वान् ससुरासुरमानवान्। तादृशेन सहायेन कस्मात् स न विजेष्यते॥
en: None has been and none will be his equal in strength of arms. It is he only who takes delight on seeing a mighty encounter. Why should he not come off victorious, being aided by him who defeated all the celestials, the Asuras and the human beings, assembled together?

description: The colloquy between Uttara and Virata
sn: विराट उवाच बहुशः प्रतिषिद्धोऽसि न च वाचं नियच्छसि। नियन्ता चेन्न विद्येत न कश्चिद् धर्ममाचरेत्॥
en: Virata said “Although prevented by me repeatedly, you do not control your speech. If there is none to govern, who will practise virtues?"

description: The colloquy between Uttara and Virata
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततः प्रकुपितो राजा तमक्षेणानहद् भृशम्। मुखे युधिष्ठिरं कोपान्नैवमित्येव भर्सयन्॥ बलवत् प्रतिविद्धस्य नस्तः शोणितमावहत्। तद्प्राप्तं महीं पार्थः पाणिभ्यां प्रत्यगृह्णत॥
en: Vaishampayana said Saying this, the king, worked up with anger, siruck Yudhishthira on the face with a dice, and remonstrated with him in anger. Having been struck with great force, blood began to glow from his nose. But Partha held it in his hands so that it mighty not fall on the ground.

description: The colloquy between Uttara and Virata
sn: अवैक्षत स धर्मात्मा द्रौपदी पार्श्वत: स्थिताम्। सा ज्ञात्वा तमभिप्रायं भर्तुश्चित्तवशानुगा॥ पात्रं गृहीत्वा सौवर्णं जलपूर्णमनिन्दिता। तच्छोणितं प्रत्यगृह्णाद् यत् प्रसुस्राव नस्ततः॥
en: The pious Yudhishthira then looked at Draupadi who was standing by his side. Understanding his intention, that faultless one, ever obedient to her husband, brought a golden vessel filled with water, and held the blood that flowed from his nose.

description: The colloquy between Uttara and Virata
sn: अथोत्तरः शुभैर्गन्धैर्माल्यैश्च विविधैस्तथा। अवकीर्यमाण: संहृष्टो नगरं स्वैरमागतः॥
en: In the meantime, Uttara, covered with various perfumes and garlands, slowly entered the city with delight.

description: The colloquy between Uttara and Virata
sn: सभाज्यमानः पौरेश्च स्त्रीभिर्जानपदैस्तथा। आसाद्य भवनद्वारं पित्रे सम्प्रत्यवेदयत्॥ ततो द्वाः स्थः प्रविश्यैव विराटमिदमब्रवीत्। बृहन्नलासहायश्च पुत्रो द्वार्युत्तरः स्थितः॥
en: He was welcomed by the citizens, females and villagers. Arrived at the gate, he sent news to his father. The waiter, approaching the king Virata said: “Your son waits at the gate with Brihannala as his help.”

description: The colloquy between Uttara and Virata
sn: ततो हृष्टो मत्स्यराजः क्षत्तारमिदमब्रवीत्। प्रवेश्यतामुभौ तूर्णं दर्शनेप्सुरहं तयोः॥ क्षत्तारं कुरुराजस्तु शनैः कर्ण उपाजपत्। उत्तरः प्रविशत्वेको न प्रवेश्या बृहन्नला॥
en: The king of Matsya then said with delight to the porter. “Bring them here-I am anxious to see them.” Then Yudhishthira whispered to the porter. “Let Uttara alone come, and not Brihannala.

description: The colloquy between Uttara and Virata
sn: एतस्य हि महाबाहो व्रतमेतत् समाहितम्। यो ममाङ्गे व्रणं कुर्याच्छोणितं वापि दर्शयेत्। अन्यत्र संग्रामगान स जीवेत् कथञ्चन॥ न मृष्याद् भृशसंक्रुद्धो मां दृष्ट्वा तु सशोणितम्। विराटमिह सामात्यं हन्यात् सबलवाहनम्॥
en: That mighty-armed hero has taken this vow that whoever shall wound my body or shed my blood except in battle, shall never live. Greatly angered, he will never see me bleeding but will kill Virata with his counsellors, horses and soldiers."

description: The colloquy between Uttara and Virata
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततो राज्ञः सुतो ज्येष्ठः प्राविशत् पृथिवीट्टायः। सोऽभिवाद्य पितुः पादौ ककं चाप्युपतिष्ठत॥ ततो रुधिरसंयुक्तमनेकाग्रमनागसम्। भूमावासीनमेकान्ते सैरभ्या प्रत्युपस्थितम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Then the eldest son of the king, Bhuminjaya, entered there. Having saluted the feet of his father, he approached Kanka. He saw him there, bathed in blood, sitting on the ground, at one end of the court, attended upon by Sairandhri.

description: The colloquy between Uttara and Virata
sn: तत: पप्रच्छ पितरं त्वरमाण इवोत्तरः। केनायं ताडितो राजन् केन पापमिदं कृतम्॥
en: Uttara, then, in a hurry, asked his father “Who has struck him, Oking? Who has committed this iniquity?"

description: The colloquy between Uttara and Virata
sn: विराट उवाच मयायं ताडितो जिह्मो न चाप्येतावदर्हति। प्रशस्यमाने यच्छूरे त्वयि षण्ढं प्रशंसति॥
en: Virata said : “This wily Brahmana has been struck by me. He deserves even more than this. When I was speaking highly of you, heroic as you are, he praised a eunuch.”

description: The colloquy between Uttara and Virata
sn: उत्तर उवाच अकार्यं ते कृतं राजन् क्षिप्रमेव प्रसाद्यताम्। मा त्वां ब्रह्मविषं घोरं समूलमिह निर्दहेत्॥
en: Uttara said: "You have committed a great sin. Please him soon so that the deadly venom of Brahmana's curse may not consume you to the very roots.

description: The colloquy between Uttara and Virata
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच स पुत्रस्य वचः श्रुत्वा विराटो राष्ट्रवर्धनः। क्षमयामास कौन्तेयं भस्मच्छन्नमिवानलम्॥
en: Hearing the words of his son Virata, enhancer of the state begged pardon with the son of Kunti, radiant like fire within ashes,

description: The colloquy between Uttara and Virata
sn: क्षमयन्तं तु राजानं पाण्डवः प्रत्यभाषत। चिरं क्षान्तमिदं राजन् न मन्युर्विद्यते मम॥
en: Seeking forgiveness him, the son of Pandu said the king that I have taken the vow of pardon, so I have no anger in my mind.

description: The colloquy between Uttara and Virata
sn: यदि ह्येतत् पतेद् भूमौ रुधिरं मम नस्ततः सराष्ट्रस्त्वं महाराज विनश्येथा न संशयः॥
en: Forsooth, If the blood comes out from my nose, and falls on the ground, O king, you with your kingdom would have been destroyed.

description: The colloquy between Uttara and Virata
sn: न दूषयामि ते राजन् यद् वै हन्याददूषकम्। बलवन्तं प्रभुं राजन् क्षिप्रं दारुणमाप्नुयात्॥
en: O king! Do not censure anybody and killing of others is a sinful act, but sometimes mighty king as you is bound to take this cruel step.

description: The colloquy between Uttara and Virata
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच शोणिते तु व्यतिक्रान्ते प्रविवेश बृहन्नला। अभिवाद्य विराटं तु ककं चाप्युपतिष्ठत॥
en: Vaishampayana sajd When the bleeding had stopped, Brihannala entered the room and having saluted Virata and Kanka, stood silent.

description: The colloquy between Uttara and Virata
sn: क्षामयित्वा तु कौरव्यं रणादुत्तरमागतम्। प्रशशंस ततो मत्स्यः शृण्वत: सव्यसाचिनः॥ त्वया दायादवानस्मि कैकेयीनन्दिवर्धन। त्वया मे सदृशः पुत्रो न भूतो न भविष्यति॥
en: Having pacified Yudhishthira, the king began to praise Uttara in the hearing of Arjuna. "O descendant of Kaikeya, in you I have truly got a son. Like you I never had nor shall have a son."

description: The colloquy between Uttara and Virata
sn: पदं पदसहस्रेण यश्चरन् नापरानुयात्। तेन कर्णेन ते तात कथमासीत् समागमः॥ मनुष्यलोके सकले यस्य तुल्यो न विद्यते। तेन भीष्मेण ते तात कथमासीत् समागमः॥
en: O son! How did you fight with that Karna who on his one target releases arrows for thousand targets unfailingly. And how did you meet in battle with who is unequal to any person in this world.

description: The colloquy between Uttara and Virata
sn: आचार्यो वृष्णिवीराणां कौरवाणां च यो द्विजः। सर्वक्षत्रस्य चाचार्यः सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वरः। तेन द्रोणेन ते तात कथमासीत् समागमः॥
en: O son! How did you fight with that twiceborn Drona, who is preceptor of the Vishni heroes and sons of Kurus, preceptor of all the Kshatriyas and the foremost among the armed soldiers.

description: The colloquy between Uttara and Virata
sn: आचार्यपुत्रो यः शूरः सर्वशस्त्रभृतामपि। अश्वत्थामेति विख्यातस्तेनासीत् संगरः कथम्॥
en: How is the battle was that of Ashvatthama with you, the son of your preceptor who was the best among the warriors and armed heroes.

description: The colloquy between Uttara and Virata
sn: रणे यं प्रेक्ष्य सीदन्ति हतस्वा वणिजो यथा। कृपेण तेन ते तात कथमासीत् समागमः॥
en: As a Vaishya becomes much distressed on destruction of his wealth, the warriors seeing Kripa become f}accid. How did you fight with them.

description: The colloquy between Uttara and Virata
sn: पर्वतं योऽभिविध्येत राजपुत्रो महेषुभिः। दुर्योधनेन ते तात कथमासीत् समागमः॥
en: O son, how was that your encounter with prince Duryodhana, who had broken the hills by his great arrows.

description: The colloquy between Uttara and Virata
sn: अवगाढा द्विषन्तो मे सुखो वातोऽभिवाति माम्। यस्त्वं धनमथाजैषीः कुरुभिम्रस्तमाहवे॥
en: O son! The Kuru sons had been kidnapped the kine wealth, you regain it. I feel great pleasure, wind also delighted me.

description: The colloquy between Uttara and Virata
sn: तेषां भयाभिपन्नानां सर्वेषां बलशालिनाम्। नूनं प्रकाल्य तान् सर्वांस्त्वया युधि नरर्षभ। आच्छिन्नं गोधनं सर्वं शार्दूलेनामिषं यथा॥
en: Forsooth, o foremost of men, having routed the enemy of having great streinght but afraid, you have snatched away from them by precious kine like a tiger his prey.

description: Uttara's account of the battle in the Goharana
sn: उत्तर उवाच न मया निर्जिता गावो न मया निर्जिताः परे। कृतं तत् सकलं तेन देवपुत्रेण केनचित्॥
en: Uttara said The kine have not been rescued by me nor have the enemy been defeated by me. All that has been done by the son of a celestials.

description: Uttara's account of the battle in the Goharana
sn: स हि भीतं द्रवन्तं मां देवपुत्रो न्यवर्तयत्। स चातिष्ठद् रथोपस्थे वज्रसंहननो युवा॥
en: Seeing me running away in fear, a youth of celestials birth, capable of wielding thunderbolt, stopped me, and got on my chariot.

description: Uttara's account of the battle in the Goharana
sn: तेन ता निर्जिता गावः कुरुवश्च पराजिताः। तस्य तत् कर्म वीरस्य न मया तात तत् कृतम्॥
en: By him the kine have been rescued and the Kauravas defeated. This is the work of that hero and not mine.

description: Uttara's account of the battle in the Goharana
sn: स हि शारद्वतं द्रोणं द्रोणपुत्रं च घड् रथान्। सूतपुत्रं च भीष्मं च चकार विमुखाञ्छरैः॥
en: It was he who repulse with arrows the six warriors namely Kripa, Drona, Ashvathama, Karna, Bhishma and Vikarana.

description: Uttara's account of the battle in the Goharana
sn: दुर्योधनं विकर्णं च सनागमिव यूथपम्। प्रभग्नमब्रवीद् भीतं राजपुत्रं महाबलः॥
en: That highly powerful one said to the prince, Duryodhana, terrified and broken like a leader of elephant-herds.

description: Uttara's account of the battle in the Goharana
sn: न हास्तिनपुरे त्राणं तव पश्यामि किंचन। व्यायामेन परीप्सस्व जीवितं कौरवात्मज॥
en: O Kuru prince, I do not see that by any means you are safe even at Hastinapur. Protect your life by displaying your energy.

description: Uttara's account of the battle in the Goharana
sn: न मोक्ष्यसे पलायंस्त्वं राजन् युद्धे मनः कुरु। पृथिवीं भोक्ष्यसे जित्वा हतो वा स्वर्गमाप्स्यसि॥
en: You will not be free by escaping. Therefore make up your mind, O king, for fight. By conquering you will enjoy the earth, and by being slain you will attain to heaven.

description: Uttara's account of the battle in the Goharana
sn: स निवृत्तो नरव्याघ्रो मुञ्चन् वज्रनिभाञ्छरान्। सचिवैः संवृतो राजा रथे नाग इव श्वसन्॥
en: Thus addressed, the king Duryodhana, the foremost of men, sighing on his car like a snake, turned, surrounded by his ministers, and discharging thunder-like arrows.

description: Uttara's account of the battle in the Goharana
sn: तं दृष्ट्वा रोमहर्षोऽभूदूरुकम्बश्च मारिष। स तत्र सिंहसंकाशमनीकं व्यधमच्छरैः॥
en: Beholding it, my hairs stood erect and the thighs to treinble. But he struck with his arrows that army of lions.

description: Uttara's account of the battle in the Goharana
sn: तत् प्रणुद्य रथानीकं सिंहसंहननो युवा। कुरूंस्तान् प्रहसन् राजन् संस्थितान् हृतवाससः॥१०।
en: Having assailed those mighty car-warriors the Kurus. O king, the youth, powerful as a lion, laughed and stripped them off their robes.

description: Uttara's account of the battle in the Goharana
sn: एकेन तेन वीरेण षड् रथा: परिनिर्जिताः। शार्दूलेनेव मत्तेन यथा वनचरा मृगाः॥
en: Those six great Kuru car-warriors were defeated by that hero alone, as animals, ranging in the forest, are killed by a single angry tiger."

description: Uttara's account of the battle in the Goharana
sn: विराट उवाच क्व स वीरो महाबाहुर्देवपुत्रो महायशाः। यो मे धनमथाजैषीत् कुरुभिर्मस्तमाहवे॥ इच्छामि तमहं द्रष्टुमचितुं च महाबलम्। येन मे त्वं च गावश्च रक्षिता देवसूनुना॥
en: Virata said-Dear son! Tell me where that illustrious and chivalrous angel who has won my cows once taken in possession by Kauravas in battle? I want to see and honour that angel for his valour who have defended you including all cows.

description: Uttara's account of the battle in the Goharana
sn: उत्तर उवाच अन्तर्धानं गतस्तत्र देवपुत्रो महाबलः। स तु श्वो वा परश्वो वा मन्ये प्रादुर्भविष्यति।॥
en: Uttara replied-"Dear father! That mighty angel had vanished there but I am sure enough that he will again appear here either tomorrow or the day after tomorrow.

description: Uttara's account of the battle in the Goharana
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमाख्यायमानं तु छन्नं सत्रेण पाण्डवम्। वसन्तं तत्र नाज्ञासीद् विराटो वाहिनीपतिः॥
en: Vaishampayana says-O Janamejaya! In spite of told impliedly, the king Virata could not recognise Arjuna, the son of Pandu living those hideously as an eunuch.

description: Uttara's account of the battle in the Goharana
sn: ततः पार्थोऽभ्यनुज्ञातो विराटेन महात्मना। प्रददौ तानि वासांसि विराटदुहितुः स्वयम्॥
en: Arjuna, in disguise of Brihannala then gave all garments took-off from the bodies of great commanders (rathis) to Uttara, daughter of Virata in compliance with the king's order.

description: Uttara's account of the battle in the Goharana
sn: उत्तरा तु महार्हाणि विविधानि नवानि च। प्रतिगृह्याभवत् प्रीता तानि वासांसि भामिनी॥ मन्त्रयित्वा तु कौन्तेय उत्तरेण महात्मना। इतिकर्तव्यतां सर्वां राजन् पार्थे युधिष्ठिरे॥ ततस्तथा तद् व्यदधाद् यथावत् पुरुषर्षभ। सह पुत्रेण मत्स्यस्य प्रहृष्टा भरतर्षभाः॥
en: Uttara was exhilarated while receiving those various new and precious garments. O Janamejaya! Arjuna, the son of Kunti consulted the prince Uttara regarding revealing actual identity of Yudhishthira and decided duly all other affairs which were to be executed. O king! He then in a systematic manner, executed all affairs. Pandava, the greatest jewel to Bharata dynasty, exhilarated when all that arrangement was made in company of Uttara.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततस्तृतीये दिवसे भ्रातरः पञ्च पाण्डवाः। स्नाता: शुक्लाम्बरधराः समये चरितव्रताः॥ युधिष्ठिरं पुरस्कृत्य सर्वाभरणभूषिताः। द्वारि मत्ता यथा नागा भ्राजमाना महारथाः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Thereupon, on the third day, being bathed and wearing white clothes and adorned with all ornaments, the five brothers, having observed their vows in due time and placed Yudhishthira before them, appeared at the gate like five infuriated elephants.

sn: विराटस्य सभां गत्वा भूमिपालासनेष्वथ। निषेदुः पावकप्रख्याः सर्वे धिष्ण्येष्विवागनयः॥
en: Having entered the assembly hall of the king Virata, they sat on thrones reserved for kings and shone there like fire on the sacrificial altar.

sn: तेषु तत्रोपविष्टेषु विराटः पृथिवीपतिः। आजगाम सभां कर्तुं राजकार्याणि सर्वशः॥
en: They, having taken their seats, the Emperor Virata came there to perform his manifold royal duties.

sn: श्रीमतः पाण्डवान् दृष्ट्वा ज्वलतः पावकानिव। मुहूर्तमिव च ध्यात्वा सरोषः पृथिवीपतिः॥
en: Beholding the beautiful Pandavas, who shone there like burning fire, the king thought for a moment and was worked up with anger.

sn: अथ मत्स्योऽब्रवीत् कवं देवरूपमिव स्थितम्। मरुद्गणैरुपासीनं त्रिदशानामिवेश्वरम्॥
en: Then the king of Matsya's said to Kanka, who was seated there like the king of gods attended by the Maruts.

sn: स किलाक्षातिवापस्त्वं सभास्तारो मया वृतः। अथ राजासने कस्मादुपविष्टस्त्वलंकृतः॥
en: You were a player at dice and were appointed by me as a courtier. Why do you, adorned with ornaments, sit on a royal throne?”

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच परिहासेप्सया वाक्यं विराटस्य निशम्य तत्। स्मयमानोऽर्जुनो राजन्निदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Hearing the words of Virata, Arjuna, as if smiling, said the following words to the king:

sn: अर्जुन उवाच इन्द्रस्यार्धासनं राजन्नयमारोढुमर्हति। ब्रह्मण्यः श्रुतवांस्त्यगी यज्ञशीलो दृढव्रतः॥
en: This man, o king, is worthy of even sharing a seat with Indra. Respectful toward Brahmanas, well read in Shrutis, even engaged in the performance of sacrifices, selfsacrificing, of firm vows,

sn: एष विग्रहवान् धर्म एष वीर्यवतां वरः। एष बुद्ध्याधिको लोके तपसां च परायणम्॥
en: He is in fact the embodiment of Virtue and the foremost of the powerful. He is of superior intelligence in this world and intent on the performance of ascetic rites.

sn: एषोऽस्त्रं विविधं वेत्ति त्रैलोक्ये सचराचरे। न चैवान्यः पुमान् वेत्ति न वेत्स्यति कदाचन॥
en: He knows the use of various weapons. No creature in the three worlds, either amongst the mobile or immobile, knows this like him, nor will know it.

sn: न देवा नासुराः केचिन्न मनुष्या न राक्षसाः। गन्धर्वयक्षप्रवराः सकिन्नरमहोरगाः॥
en: Neither the celestials, Asuras, human beings. Rakshasas, Gandharvas, the leading Yakshas, Kinnaras, or serpents (are like him).

sn: दीर्घदर्शी महातेजाः पौरजानपदप्रियः। पाण्डवानामतिरथो यज्ञधर्मपरो वशी॥
en: He is far-sighted, highly energetic, beloved of the citizens and villagers, the foremost of car-warriors among the sons of Pandu, the performer of sacrifices, pious, and selfcontrolled.

sn: महर्षिकल्पो राजर्षिः सर्वलोकेषु विश्रुतः। बलवान् धृतिमान् दक्षः सत्यवादी जितेन्द्रियः। धनैश्च सञ्चयैश्चैव शक्रवैश्रवणोपमः॥
en: A royal saint like a great Rishi as he is, he is celebrated all over the world. He is powerful, intelligent, capable, truthful and selfcontrolled. In wealth he is equal to Indra and in amassed wealth to Kubera,

sn: यथा मनुर्महातेजा लोकानां परिरक्षिता। एवमेष महातेजाः प्रजानुग्रहकारकः॥
en: He is the preserver of the world like the highly powerful Manu himself. Highly powerful and kind to his subjects.

sn: अयं कुरूणामृषभो धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः। अस्य कीर्तिः स्थिता लोके सूर्यस्येवोद्यतः प्रभा।।१६।
en: He is the best in Kuru dynasty and known as Dharmaraja Yudhishthira. As the pleasant and cool radiance of the rising sun, his pleasure pouring fame has been spreaded throughout the world.

sn: संसरन्ति दिशः सर्वा यशसोऽस्य इवांशवः। उदितस्येव सूर्यस्य तेजसोऽनु गभस्तयः॥
en: As the sun rays spread in all directions on sun rise due to radiation, his fame with its nectar pouring white rays is spreading in all directions.

sn: एनं दशसहस्राणि कुञ्जराणां तरस्विनाम्। अन्वयुः पृष्ठतो राजन् यावदध्यावसत् कुरून्॥
en: O king, during his dwelling in Kuru country, as much as ten thousand mighty elephants used to follow him.

sn: त्रिंशदेनं सहस्राणि रथाः काञ्चनमालिनः। सदश्वरूपसम्पन्नाः पृष्ठतोऽनुययुस्तदा।॥
en: Similarly, thirty thousand chariots trimmed with garments made of gold and best quality horses used to follow him while in Kuru country.

sn: एनमष्टशताः सूताः सुमृष्टमणिकुण्डलाः। अब्रुवन् मागधैः सार्धं पुरा शक्रमिवर्षयः॥
en: As all sages chant pray lord Indra, he was carlier prayed by eight hundred soothsayers and Magadha (clown) bearing gem-studded car-rings.

sn: एनं नित्यमुपासन्त कुरवः किंकरा यथा। सर्वे च राजन् राजानो धनेश्वरमिवामराः॥
en: O king! As the gods pray Kubera, the treasurer, all kings and Kauravas used to follow his orders daily like servants.

sn: एष सर्वान् महीपालान् करदान् समकारयत्। वैश्यानिव महाभागो विवशान् स्ववशानपि॥
en: This great man had made all kings tax payers like Vaishyas (by subjugation) and by directing them varied ways (viz. all kings used to pay him taxes imposed).

sn: अष्टाशीतिसहस्राणि स्नातकानां महात्मनाम्। उपजीवन्ति राजानमेनं सुचरितव्रतम्॥
en: This great resolute had employed as much as eighty eight thousand learned graduates (Snatakas) and he used to consult with them daily.

sn: एष वृद्धाननाथांश्च पङ्गुनन्धांश्च मानवान्। पुत्रवत् पालयामास प्रजा धर्मेण वै विभुः॥
en: He used to provide senior people, orphans, handicapped and blind people of state with proper maintenance. This king used to defend his subjects like son with all legitimate means and resources.

sn: एष धर्मे दमे चैव क्रोधे चापि जितव्रतः। महाप्रसादो ब्रह्मण्यः सत्यवादी च पार्थिवः॥
en: This king has resolved to control the sensory organs, always prepared to execute all what is legitimate and has ail extreme control on anger. He is kind hearted, devotee to Brahmins and truthful.

sn: शीघ्रं तापेन चैतस्य तप्यते स सुयोधनः। सगणः सह कर्णेन सौबलेनापि वा विभुः॥
en: By virtue of his valour, Duryodhana in spite of being so mighty shortly punished for his evil tricks with Karna, Shakuni and all other attendants.

sn: न शक्यन्ते ह्यस्य गुणाः प्रसंख्यातुं नरेश्वर। एष धर्मपरो नित्यमानृशंसश्च पाण्डवः॥ एवं युक्तो महाराजः पाण्डव: पार्थिवर्षभः। कथं नार्हति राजार्हमासनं पृथिवीपते।॥
en: O king! His great virtues cannot be counted. He, the son of Pandu is generous and always religion abiding. Oking! Why is Yudhishthira, the son of Pandu not entitled to the position of a king in spite of the best virtues resting in his personality?

description: The proposal of the marriage of Uttara
sn: विराट उवाच यद्येष राजा कौरव्यः कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः। कतमोऽस्यार्जुनो भ्राता भीमश्च कतमो बली॥
en: Virata said If this be the king of Kurus, Yudhishthira, the son of Kunti, who, amongst those is his brother Arjuna and who the powerful Bhima?

description: The proposal of the marriage of Uttara
sn: नकुलः सहदेवो वा द्रौपदी वा यशस्विनी। यदा द्यूतजिताः पार्था न प्राज्ञायन्त ते क्वचित्॥
en: Which of them is Nakula, who Sahadeva and where is the illustrious Draupadi? From the time of their defeat at dice, the sons of Pritha have not been known by any.

description: The proposal of the marriage of Uttara
sn: अर्जुन उवाच य एष बल्लवो ब्रूते सूदस्तव नराधिप। एष भीमो महाराज भीमवेगपराक्रमः॥
en: Arjuna said This one, O king, your cook, known as Ballava, is Bhima of dreadful prowess and energy.

description: The proposal of the marriage of Uttara
sn: एष क्रोधवशान् हत्वा पर्वते गन्धमादने। सौगन्धिकानि दिव्यानि कृष्णार्थे समुपाहरत्॥
en: It was he who, having killed the angry Rakshasas on the Gandhamadana mountain, secured for Draupadi fragrant celestials flowers.

description: The proposal of the marriage of Uttara
sn: गन्धर्व एष वै हन्ता कीचकानां दुरात्मनाम्। । व्याघ्रानृक्षान् वराहांश्च हतवान् स्त्रीपुरे तव॥
en: He is the Gandharva who killed the wicked-souled Kichaka's, and it was he who slew the tigers, bears, and boars in your inner apartment.

description: The proposal of the marriage of Uttara
sn: यश्चासीदश्वबन्धस्ते नकुलोऽयं परंतपः। गोसङ्ख्यः सहदेवश्च माद्रीपुत्रौ महारथौ॥
en: He, who is the keeper of your horses is Nakula, the slayer of horses. The one, in charge of your kine, is Sahadeva. Both the sons of Madri are great car-warriors.

description: The proposal of the marriage of Uttara
sn: शृङ्गारवेषाभरणौ रूपवन्तौ यशस्विनौ। महारथसहस्राणां समर्थो भरतर्षभौ॥
en: Adorned with beautiful ornaments and robes, and illustrious, these two foremost of Bharatas are capable of withstanding a thousand car-warrior.

description: The proposal of the marriage of Uttara
sn: एषा पद्मपलाशाक्षी सुमध्या चारुहासिनी। सैरन्ध्री द्रौपदी राजन् यस्यार्थे कीचका हताः॥
en: This lotus-eyed, beautiful, waited Sairandhri, of sweet smiles, is Draupadi, O king, for whom the Kichakas were slain.

description: The proposal of the marriage of Uttara
sn: अर्जुनोऽहं महाराज व्यक्तं ते श्रोत्रमागतः। भीमादवरजः पार्थो यमाभ्यां चापि पूर्वजः॥
en: I am Arjuna, Oking. You might have heard that I am the son of Pritha, the younger brother of Bhima and the elder brother of the twins.

description: The proposal of the marriage of Uttara
sn: उषिताः स्मो महाराज सुखं तव निवेशने। अज्ञातवासमुषिता गर्भवास इव प्रजाः॥
en: We have spend happily the period of our exile, undiscovered, in your house, like creatures living in the womb.

description: The proposal of the marriage of Uttara
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच यदार्जुनेन ते वीराः कथिताः पञ्च पाण्डवाः। तदार्जुनस्य वैराटिः कथयामास विक्रमम्॥ पुनरेव च तान् पार्थान् दर्शयामास चोत्तरः॥
en: Vaishampayana said After Arjuna had spoken of the five heroic sons of Pandu, the son of Virata then described his prowess. Uttara, too, again identified the sons of Pritha. (He said):

description: The proposal of the marriage of Uttara
sn: उत्तर उवाच तनुर्महान् सिंह इव प्रवृद्धः। स्ताम्रायताक्षः कुरुराज एषः॥
en: The one, whose complexion is like pure gold, who is of developed proportions like a huge lion, whose eyes are expansive and coppery, whose nose is high, is the king of the Kurus.

description: The proposal of the marriage of Uttara
sn: अयं पुनर्मत्तगजेन्द्रगामी प्रतप्तचामीकरशुद्धगौरः। वृकोदरः पश्यत पश्यतैनम्॥
en: He, who courses like an infuriated elephant, whose complexion is bright like burning gold, whose shoulders are expansive, whose arms are long and heavy, is Vrikodara.

description: The proposal of the marriage of Uttara
sn: यस्त्वेव पार्श्वेऽस्य महाधनुष्मान् श्यामो युवा वारणयूथपोपमः। सिंहोन्नतांसो गजराजगामी पद्मायताक्षोऽर्जुन एष ऽर्जुन एष वीरः॥
en: And that youthful hero, of dark blue colour, O great bowman, who stands by him, who is like an elephant-chief, who is high like a lion and courses like an elephant, and has lotus-eyes, is Arjuna.

description: The proposal of the marriage of Uttara
sn: राज्ञः समीपे पुरुषत्तमौ तु यमाविमौ विष्णुमहेन्द्रकल्पौ। मनुष्यलोके सकले समोऽस्ति ययोर्न रूपे न बले न शीले।॥
en: Those two foremost of men, who are near the king, are the twins. They are equal to Vishnu and Mahendra. In this world, there is none equal to them in beauty, strength and accomplishments.

description: The proposal of the marriage of Uttara
sn: आभ्यां तु पार्श्वे कनकोत्तमाङ्गी यैषा प्रभा मूर्तिमतीव गौरी। नीलोत्पला भा सुरदेवतेव कृष्णा स्थिता मूर्तिमतीव लक्ष्मीः॥
en: Near them is Draupadi, having the hue of gold. Her complexion is an embodiment of brightness, her eyes are like dark-blue lotuses, and she is like the very goddess of prosperity (Lakshmi).

description: The proposal of the marriage of Uttara
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवं निवेद्य तान् पार्थान् पाण्डवान् पञ्च भूपतेः। ततोऽर्जुनस्य वैराटिः कथयामास विक्रमम्॥
en: Having thus pointed out those five sons of Pandu and Pritha to the king, the son of Virata, then began to describe the prowess of Arjuna.

description: The proposal of the marriage of Uttara
sn: उत्तर उवाच अयं स द्विषतां हन्ता मृगाणामिव केसरी। अचरद् रथवृन्देषु निघ्नंस्तांस्तान् वरान् रथान्॥
en: It was he who slew the enemies, like a lion killing the deer. He moved about on the cars, killing the car-warriors.

description: The proposal of the marriage of Uttara
sn: अनेन विद्धो मातङ्गो महानेकेषुणा हतः। सुवर्णकक्षः संग्रामे दन्ताभ्यामगमन्महीम्॥
en: A huge elephant was pierced with a shaft and killed by him. That one of huge tusks, and bedecked with gold, fell down on earth.

description: The proposal of the marriage of Uttara
sn: अनेन विजिता गावो जिताश्च कुरवो युधि। अन्य शङ्खप्रणादेन की मे बधिरीकृतौ॥
en: By him the kine have been rescued, the Kurus vanquished; and, by the sound of his conch, my ears were deafened.

description: The proposal of the marriage of Uttara
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा मत्स्यराजः प्रतापवान्। उत्तरं प्रत्युवाचेदमभिपनो युधिष्ठिरे॥
en: Hearing the words of Uttara, the powerful king of of Matsya's, who had insulted Yudhishthira, said to him.

description: The proposal of the marriage of Uttara
sn: प्रसादनं पाण्डवस्य प्राप्तकालं हि रोचते। उत्तरां च प्रयच्छामि पार्थाय यदि मन्यसे॥
en: Methinks, the time has come to propitiate the Pandavas. If you like I shall confer Uttara (my daughter) upon Arjuna.

description: The proposal of the marriage of Uttara
sn: उत्तर उवाच आर्याः पूज्याश्च मान्याश्च प्राप्तकालं च मे मतम्। पूज्यन्तां पूजनाश्चि महाभागाश्च पाण्डवाः॥
en: Uttara said Methinks, the time has come for honoring the illustrious sons of Pandu, who are worthy of honour, respect and adoration.”

description: The proposal of the marriage of Uttara
sn: विराट उवाच अहं खल्वपि संग्रामे शत्रूणां वशमागतः। मोक्षितो भीमसेनेन गावश्चापि जितास्तथा॥
en: Virata said When I passed into the hands of the enemies in battle, it was Bhimasena who saved me and rescued the kine.

description: The proposal of the marriage of Uttara
sn: एतेषां बाहुवीर्येण अस्माकं विजयो मृधे। एवं सर्वे सहामात्याः कुन्तीपुत्रं युधिष्ठिरम्। प्रसादयामो भद्रं ते सानुजं पाण्डवर्षभम्॥ यदस्माभिरजानद्धिः किंचिदुक्तो नराधिपः। क्षन्तुमर्हति तत् सर्वं धर्मात्मा ह्येष पाण्डवः॥
en: By their prowess, we have won victory in battle. Along with our ministers, we shall propitiate the son of Kunti, Yudhishthira, the foremost of Pandavas, together with his younger brothers. (He then said to him): "May good betide you. O king, If I we have unwittingly given you any offence, you should forgive me for all that. The son of Pandu is virtuous-souled.

description: The proposal of the marriage of Uttara
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततो विराट: परमाभितुष्टः समेत्य राजा समयं चकार। राज्यं च सर्वं विससर्ज तस्मै सदण्डकोश सपुरं महात्मा॥
en: Vaishampayana said Then noble Virata, made an alliance wit the king and offered him the entire kingdom together with his scepter, treasury and city.

description: The proposal of the marriage of Uttara
sn: पाण्डवांश्च ततः सर्वान् मत्स्यराजः प्रतापवान्। धनंजयं पुरस्कृत्य दिष्ट्या दिष्ट्येति चाब्रवीत्॥
en: Then addressing all the Pandavas and particularly Dhananjaya, the king of Matsya's, again and again, said "Oh good fortune."

description: The proposal of the marriage of Uttara
sn: समुपाघ्राय मूर्धानं संश्लिष्य च पुनः पुनः। युधिष्ठिरं च भीमं च माद्रीपुत्रो च पाण्डवौ॥
en: Then, having repeatedly embraced and smelt the heads of Yudhishthira, Bhima and the two sons of Madri,

description: The proposal of the marriage of Uttara
sn: नातृप्यद् दर्शने तेषां विराटो वाहिनीपतिः। स प्रीयमाणो राजानं युधिष्ठिरमथाब्रवीत्॥
en: Virata, the lord of armies, was not satiated with seeing them. He, then delightedly, said to the king Yudhishthira.

description: The proposal of the marriage of Uttara
sn: दिष्ट्या भवन्तः सम्प्राप्ताः सर्वे कुशलिनो वनात्। दिष्ट्या सम्पालितं कृच्छ्रमज्ञातं वै दुरात्मभिः॥
en: "By good luck, I have got you, all safe from the forest. And by good luck, it is that you spent the period of exile, undiscovered by these wicked ones.

description: The proposal of the marriage of Uttara
sn: इदं च राज्यं पार्थाय यच्चान्यदपि किञ्चन। प्रतिगृह्णन्तु तत् सर्वं पाण्डवा अविशङ्कया।॥
en: I make a gift of this my kingdom and what else I have, to the sons of Pritha. May they accept it without any hesitation.

description: The proposal of the marriage of Uttara
sn: उत्तरां प्रतिगृह्णातु सव्यसाची धनंजयः। अयं ह्यौपयिको भर्ता तस्याः पुरुषसत्तमः॥
en: Let Savyasachin, Dhananjaya, accept Uttara (my daughter). That foremost of men is her becoming husband."

description: The proposal of the marriage of Uttara
sn: एवमुक्तो धर्मराजः पार्थमैक्षद् धनंजयम्। ईक्षितश्चार्जुनो भ्रात्रा मत्स्यं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Thus addressed, the pious king Yudhishthira looked towards Dhananjaya. And looked at by his brother, Arjuna said to the king of Matsya's.

description: The proposal of the marriage of Uttara
sn: प्रतिगृह्णाम्यहं राजन् स्नुषां दुहितरं तव। युक्तश्चावां हि सम्बन्धो मत्स्यभारतयोरपि॥
en: Oking, I shall accept your daughter as my daughter-in-law. Such an alliance between the Matsya's and Bharatas is indeed proper..

sn: विराट उवाच किमर्थं पाण्डवश्रेष्ठ भार्यां दुहितरं मम। प्रतिग्रहीतुं नेमां त्वं मया दत्तामिहेच्छसि॥
en: Virata said O foremost of Pandavas, why do you not wish to accept, as your wife, my daughter whom I wish to confer upon you?

sn: अर्जुन उवाच अन्तःपुरेऽहमुषितः सदा पश्यन् सुतां तव। रहस्यं च प्रकाशं च विश्वस्ता पितृवन्मयि॥
en: Arjuna said Living in your inner apartment, I always saw your daughter. Alone or before all, she always used to confide in me as her father.

sn: प्रियो बहुतमश्चासं नर्तको गीतकोविदः। आचार्यवच्च मां नित्यं मन्यते दुहिता तव॥
en: Well-versed in dancing and singing, I was always loved and much liked by her. Your daughter always regards me as her preceptor.

sn: वयःस्थया तया राजन् सह संवत्सरोषितः। अतिशङ्का भवेत् स्थाने तव लोकस्य वा विभो॥
en: O king, I lived for one year with her who is youthful. O lord, you or your men may therefore suspect me.

sn: तस्मान्निमन्त्रयेऽहं ते दुहितां मनुजाधिप। शुद्धो जितेन्द्रियो दान्तस्तस्याः शुद्धिः कृता मया।॥
en: O king, I, therefore, wish to have your daughter as my daughter-in-law-pure, selfcontrolled, I am. I thus prove her purity.

sn: स्नुषायां दुहितुर्वापि पुत्रे चात्मनि वा पुनः। अत्र शङ्कां न पश्यामि तेन शुद्धिर्भविष्यति॥
en: There is no difference between a daughter and a daughter-in-law as that between one's ownself and a son. I do not find any fear in it-for by it purity will be proved.

sn: अभिशापादहं भीतो मिथ्यावादात् परंतप। स्नुषार्थमुत्तरां राजन् प्रतिगृह्णामि ते सुताम्॥
en: O king, I am afraid of curses and false accusation. O king, I shall therefore accept your daughter Uttara as my daughter-in-law.

sn: स्वस्रीयो वासुदेवस्य साक्षाद् देवशिशुर्यथा। दयितश्चक्रहस्तस्य सर्वास्त्रेषु च कोविदः॥
en: A nephew of Vasudeva, like a very celestials boy-my son, who has mastered all weapons, is the favourite of the holder of discus.

sn: अभिमन्युर्महाबाहुः पुत्रो मम विशाम्पते। जामाता तव युक्तो वै भर्ता च दुहितुस्तव॥
en: O king, my son is the mighty-armed Abhimanyu. He is a proper son-in-law for you and husband for you daughter.

sn: विराट उवाच उपपन्नं कुरुश्रेष्ठे कुन्तीपुत्र धनंजये। य एवं धर्मनित्यश्च जातज्ञानश्च पाण्डवः॥
en: Virata said It is indeed proper for the foremost of Kurus, Dhananjaya, the son of Kunti, always virtuous and wise, to say this.

sn: यत् कृत्यं मन्यसे पार्थ क्रियतां तदनन्तरम्। सर्वे कामाः समृद्धा मे सम्बन्धी यस्य मेऽर्जुनः॥
en: O Partha, do what you think proper after this. He, who has a relationship with Arjuna, has all his desires fulfilled.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवं ब्रुवति राजेन्द्रे कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः। अन्वशासत् स संयोगं समये मत्स्यपार्थयोः॥
en: Vaishampayana said After the king had said this, Yudhishthira, the son of Kunti, gave his assent to the alliance between Matsya and Partha.

sn: ततो मित्रेषु सर्वेषु वासुदेवं च भारत। प्रेषयामास कौन्तेयो विराटश्च महीपतिः॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, then the son of Kunti sent invitations to all his friends and Vasudeva, and so did the king Virata.

sn: ततस्त्रयोदशे वर्षे निवृत्ते पञ्च पाण्डवाः। उपप्लव्यं विराटस्य समपद्यन्त सर्वशः॥
en: Thus after the expiration of the thirteenth year, the five Pandavas took up their quarters in Virata's town called Upaplavya.

sn: अभिमन्युं च बीभत्सुरानिनाय जनार्दनम्। आनर्तेभ्योऽपि दाशार्हानानयामास पाण्डवः॥
en: Bibhatsu then brought over Abhimanyu, Janardana and many members of the Dasharha family from the Anarta country.

sn: काशिराजश्च शैब्यश्च प्रीयमाणौ युधिष्ठिरे। अक्षौहिणीभ्यां सहितावागतौ पृथिवीपती॥
en: The king of Kashi and Shaivya, who were great friends of Yudhishthira, came there, each accompanied by an Akshauhini of soldiers.

sn: अक्षौहिण्या च सहितो यज्ञसेनो महाबलः। द्रौपद्याश्च सुता वीराः शिखण्डी चापराजितः॥
en: There came as also the mighty powerful Yajnasena with an Akshauhini of soldiers, the heroic sons of Draupadi and the invincible Shikhandi.

sn: धृष्टद्युम्नश्च दुर्धर्षः सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वरः। समस्ताक्षौहिणीपाला यज्वानो भूरिदक्षिणाः। वेदावभृथसम्पन्नाः सर्वे शूरास्तनुत्यजः॥
en: Chivalrous Dhrishtadyumna, the best weaponer and expert in war-craft were also with them. Apart from these, numerous other kings commanding one Akshauhini army each, observer of offering, generous in the matter of Dakshina for offerings arranged and ready to die for the cause of Pandavas.

sn: तानागतानभिप्रेक्ष्य मत्स्यो धर्मभृतां वरः। पूजयामास विधिवत् सभृत्यबलवाहनान्॥ प्रीतोऽभवद् दुहितरं दत्त्वा तामभिमन्यवे।
en: The king, the foremost of the virtuous, duly worshipped them all along with their servants and troops. And having given away his daughter, he was pleased.

sn: ततः प्रत्युपयातेषु पार्थिवेषु ततस्ततः॥ तत्रागमद् वासुदेवो वनमाली हलायुधः। कृतवर्मा च हार्दिक्यो युयुधानश्च सात्यकिः॥ अनाधृष्टिस्तथाक्रूरः साम्बो निश एव च। अभिमन्युमुपादाय सह मात्रा परंतपाः॥ इन्द्रसेनादयश्चैव रथैस्तैः सुसमाहितैः। आययुः सहिताः सर्वे परिसंवत्सरोषिताः॥ दशनागसहस्राणि हयानां द्विगुणं तथा। रथानामयुतं पूर्णं नियुतं च पदातिनाम्॥ वृष्ण्यन्धकाश्च बहवो भोजाश्च परमौजसः। अन्वयुर्वृष्णिशार्दूलं वासुदेवं महाद्युतिम्॥
en: There came Vasudeva, decked with garlands, Halayudha, Kritavarman, Hridika, Yuyudhana, the son of Satyaki, Anadhrishti, Akrura, Samba, Nishath-all these repressors of foes came there with Abhimanyu and his mother. Indrasena and others came with their cars-having lived there for one whole year. There came also ten thousand elephants and ten millions of horses, ten billions of cars and one Nikharva of infantry and many other highly energetic Vrishni, Andhaka and Bhoja heroes-following the highly effulgent Vasudeva-the foremost of Vrishnis.

sn: पारिबर्ह ददौ कृष्णः पाण्डवानां महात्मनाम्। स्त्रियो रत्नानि वासांसि पृथक् पृथगनेकशः॥ ततो विवाहो विधिवद् ववृधे मत्स्यपार्थयोः।
en: Lord Srikrishna made a gift of several maids, various type gems and a pile of garments separately in the form of dowry or invitation to great Pandavas. Then there took place duly the nuptial tie between the Matsya and the Pandu families.

sn: ततः शङ्खाश्च भेर्यश्च गोमुखा डम्बरास्तथा॥ पार्थैः संयुज्यमानस्य नेदुर्मत्स्यस्य वेश्मनि। भक्ष्यान्नभोज्यपानानि प्रभूतान्यभ्यहारयन्॥ गायनाख्यानशीलाच नटवैतालिकास्तथा।
en: Then conchs, cymbals, drums, trumpets and various other musical instruments were played in the palace of Virata. Various deer and animals were slain. Wines and various celestials drinks were procured and there came also many songsters, panegyrists and actors.

sn: स्तुवन्तस्तानुपातिष्ठान् सूताश्च सह मागधैः॥ सुदेष्णां च पुरस्कृत्य मत्स्यानां च वरस्त्रियः।
en: The singers, the fabulists, acrobats and the magic-mongers began chanting pray and psalms for Pandavas in company of soothsayers and Magadhas (clowns) there.

sn: आजग्मुश्चारुसर्वाङ्गयः सुमृष्टमणिकुण्डलाः॥ वर्णोपपन्नास्ता नार्यो रूपवत्यः स्वलंकृताः। सर्वाश्चाभ्यभवन् कृष्णा रूपेण यशसा श्रिया॥ परिवार्योत्तरां तास्तु राजपुत्रीमलंकृताम्। सुतामिव महेन्द्रस्य पुरस्कृत्योपतस्थिरे॥ तां प्रत्यगृह्णात् कौन्तेयः सुतस्यार्थे धनंजयः। सौभद्रस्यानवद्याङ्गी विराटतनयां तदा॥ तत्रातिष्ठन्महाराजो रूपमिन्द्रस्य धारयन्। स्नुषां तां प्रतिजग्राह कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Many dainsel, beautiful and adorned, with jeweled ear-rings, of whom Draupadi was the foremost, came there leading the princess Uttara adorned with many ornaments and resembling the accepted that all-beautiful daughter of Virata for his son Abhimanyu, begotten on Subhadra. There stood the great king, in beauty-like Indra. Yudhishthira, the son of Kunti, accepted her for his daughter-inlaw.

sn: प्रतिगृह्य च तां पार्थः पुरस्कृत्य जनार्दनम्। विवाहं कारयामास सौभद्रस्य महात्मनः॥
en: Thus, Partha accepted Uttara for his son Abhimanyu in the presence of lord Krishna and their marriage was solemnised.

sn: तस्मै सप्त सहस्राणि हयानां वातरंहसाम्। द्वे च नागशते मुख्ये प्रादाद् बहुधनं तदा॥ हुत्वा सम्यक् समिद्धाग्निमर्चयित्वा द्विजन्मनः। राज्यं बलं च कोशं च सर्वमात्मानमेव च॥
en: The king Virata made a gift of seven thousand horses as speedy as the air, two hundred mighty elephants and considerable money in the form of dowry to bridegroom party when he duly honoured Brahmins and made offering in fire in course of solemnising the marriage of his daughter. He assigned with them the throne, army and everything including treasury as also surrendered himself for their service.

sn: कृते विवाहे तु तदा धर्मपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः। ब्राह्मणेभ्यो ददौ वित्तं यदुपाहरदच्युतः॥
en: On completion of the conjugal ceremony, Yudhishthira, an incarnate to Dharma, made a gift of the major part of money received from lord Krishna to Brahmanas.

sn: गोसहस्राणि रत्नानि वस्त्राणि विविधानि च। भूषणानि च मुख्यानि यानानि शयनानि च॥ भोजनानि च हृद्यानि पानानि विविधानि च। तन्महोत्सवसंकाशं हृष्टपुष्टजनायुतम्। नगरं मत्स्यराजस्य शुशुभे भरतर्षभ।॥
en: He offered several thousand cows, gems, various type of garments, ornaments, cardinal vehicles, bed, eatables and several type of drinks also. O Janamejaya! The city of Matsyaraja crowded with thousands of lakhs hale and hearty people was being seen as a great festivity in live feature. Thus ends the seventy-second chapter, the marriage of Abhimanyu in the Vaivahika of the Virata Parva.

sn: नारायणं नमस्कृत्य नरं चैव नरोत्तमम्। देवी सरस्वतीं व्यासं ततो जयमुदीरयेत्।।
en: Having saluted the Supreme Deity (Narayana) and the highest of all male beings (Nara) and also the Goddess of Learning (Sarasvati), let us cry success!

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच स्तदाभिमन्योर्मुदिताः स्वपक्षाः। विश्रम्य रात्रावुषसि प्रतीताः सभां विराटस्य ततोऽभिजग्मुः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Then the heroic sons of Kuru belonging to the party of Abhimanyu pleased at having celebrated his (Abhimanyu's) nuptials and having rested during the night, awoke at break of day and went to the court of Virata.

sn: सभा तु सा मत्स्यपतेः समृद्धा मणिप्रवेकोत्तमरत्नचित्रा। न्यस्तासना माल्यवती सुगन्धा तामभ्ययुस्ते नरराजवृद्धाः॥
en: The court of the Lord of the Matsyas was richly decorated and adorned with a collection of precious stones and choice gems, with seats arranged in it, having garlands and filled with fragrance. Those aged kings among men came there.

sn: दुभौ विराटदुपदौ नरेन्द्रौ। वृद्धौ च मान्यौ पृथिवीपतीनां पित्रा समं रामजनार्दनौ च॥
en: On the front seats sat the two kings Virata and Drupada, aged and revered among the rulers of the earth and Rama and Janardana also along with their father.

sn: पाञ्चालराजस्य समीपतस्तु शिनिप्रवीरः सहरौहिणेयः। मत्स्यस्य राज्ञस्तु सुसंनिकृष्टो जनार्दनश्चैव युधिष्ठिरश्च॥
en: Near the king of Panchala sat the brave ruler of Shini along with the son of Rohini and next to the king of Matsya (sat) Janardana and Yudhishthira.

sn: सुताश्च सर्वे दुपदस्य राज्ञो भीमार्जुनौ माद्रवतीसुतौ च। प्रद्युम्नसाम्बौ च युधि प्रवीरौ विराटपुत्रैश्च सहाभिमन्युः॥
en: (There sat) also all the sons of king Drupada, Bhima and Arjuna, the two sons of Madri, Pradyumna and Samba, who were valiant in battle and Abhimanyu in company with the son of Virata.

sn: सर्वे च शूराः पितृभिः समाना वीर्येण रूपेण बलेन चैव। उपाविशन् द्रौपदेयाः कुमारा: सुवर्णचित्रेषु वरासनेषुः॥
en: And on the best seats wrought in gold sat the heroic sons of Draupadi who were equal to their fathers in valour, beauty and strength.

sn: तथोपविष्टेषु महारथेषु विराजमानाभरणाम्बरेषु। रराज सा राजवती समृद्धा ग्रहैरिव द्यौर्विमलैरुपेता॥
en: Those mighty heroes, shining in ornaments and clothes, being seated, that assemblage of kings shone like the firmament studded with beautiful stars.

sn: तत: कथास्ते समवाययुक्ताः कृत्वा विचित्राः पुरुषप्रवीराः। तस्थुर्मुहूर्तं परिचिन्तयन्तः कृष्णं नृपास्ते समुदीक्षमाणाः॥
en: Then those kings, heroes among men, having engaged in conversation with one another on various topics, remained for a moment gazing pensively on Krishna.

sn: कथान्तमासाद्य च माधवेन संघट्टिताः पाण्डवकार्यहेतोः। ते राजसिंहाः सहिता ह्यशृण्वन् वाक्यं महार्थं सुमहोदयं च॥
en: Those lions among kings, having reached the end of their talk and their attention having been called by Madhava to the affairs of the Pandavas, listened to his lofty speech which conveyed deep meaning. Krishna said

sn: श्रीकृष्ण उवाच सर्वैर्भवद्भिर्विदितं यथायं युधिष्ठिरः सौबलेनाक्षवत्याम्। जितो निकृत्यापहृतं च राज्यं वनप्रवासे समयः कृतश्च।॥
en: It is known to you all how this Yudhishthira was defeated by a trick at a game of dice by the son of Subala, how he was robbed of his kingdom and how he made a stipulation regarding his exile in the forest.

sn: शक्तैविजेतुं तरसा महीं च सत्ये स्थितैः सत्यरथैर्यथावत्। पाण्डोः सुतैस्तग्र व्रतमग्ररूपं वर्षाणि षट् सप्त च चीर्णमग्र्यैः॥
en: The sons of Pandu, who are capable of subjugating the word by sheer force of arms, whose chariots go unrestrained to the celestial or the terrestrial regions and who are true of their words, have fulfilled that austere vow for thirteen years.

sn: मज्ञायमानैर्भवतां समीपे। महात्मभिश्चापि वने निविष्टम्॥
en: The thirteenth year in the forest has been very hard, but this these great men have passed, unknown to you and suffering various sorts of unbearable hardships.

sn: एतैः परप्रेष्यनियोगयुक्त रिच्छद्भिराप्तं स्वकुलेन राज्यम्। एवंगते धर्मसुतस्य राज्ञो दुर्योधनस्यापि च यद्धितं स्यात्॥
en: Even they who have been engaged in the menial service of others seek their family and their kingdom; such being the case, consider what is best for the son of Dharma (Yudhishthira) and for king Duryodhana.

sn: तच्चिन्तयध्वं कुरुपुङ्गवानां धर्म्यं च युक्तं च यशस्करं च। अधर्मयुक्तं न च कामयेत राज्यं सुराणामपि धर्मराजः॥
en: (Consider) also what is right, suitable and calculated to redound to the glory of the illustrious Kauravas. The virtuous king Yudhishthira does not want even the kingdom of the gods wrongfully.

sn: धर्मार्थयुक्तं तु महीपतित्वं ग्रामेऽपि कस्मिंश्चिदयं बुभूषेत्। पित्र्यं हि राज्यं विदितं नृपाणां यथापकृष्टं धृतराष्ट्रपुत्रैः॥ मिथ्योपचारेण यथा ह्यनेन कृच्छ्रे महत् प्राप्तमसह्यरूपम्। न चापि पार्थो विजितो रणे तैः स्वतेजसा धृतराष्ट्रस्य पुत्रैः॥
en: He would rather prefer the rightful lordship of some single village. It is known to all the kings (assembled here) how he has been robbed of his ancestral kingdom with the help of a mean trick by the sons of Dhritarashtra by whom the son of Pritha has not been vanquished through prowess borne by him.

sn: रभीप्सतेऽनामयमेव तेषाम्। यत् तु स्वयं पाण्डुसुतैर्विजित्य समाहृतं भूमिपतीन् प्रपीड्य॥ तत् प्रार्थयन्ते पुरुषप्रवीराः कुन्तीसुता माद्रवतीसुतौ च। बालास्त्विमे तैर्विविधैरुपायैः सम्प्रार्थिता हन्तुममित्रसंघैः॥ राज्यं जिहीर्षद्भिरसद्भित्रैः सर्वं च तद् वो विदितं यथावत्। तेषां च लोभं प्रसमीक्ष्य वृद्धं धर्मज्ञतां चापि युधिष्ठिरस्य॥
en: Still the king Yudhishthira with his friends wishes them prosperity. The sons of Kunti, heroes among men and the two sons of Madri, seek only what has been earned by the sons of Pandu by overthrowing the king and winning victory over him. It is also well know to you how, when they were mere boys, their enemies who were cruel, dishonest and who sought to get the kingdom, attempted by several means to kill them. Consider their greediness and also the extreme piety of Yudhishthira.

sn: सम्बन्धितां चापि समीक्ष्य तेषां मर्ति कुरुध्वं सहिताः पृथक् च। इमे च सत्येऽभिरताः सदैव तं पालयित्वा समयं यथावत्॥
en: Consider also the relationship between them; consult together and also think each of you yourself. They have always been attached to truth and have always fulfilled their promises.

sn: अतोऽन्यथा तैरुपचर्यमाणा हन्युःसमेतान् धृतराष्ट्रपुत्रान्। तैर्विप्रकारं च निशम्य कार्ये सुहृज्जनास्तान् परिवारयेयुः॥
en: If they are now wrongfully treated let them slay all the sons of Dhritarashtra or let their friends who see the unworthy treatment they get in this matter make them (the sons of Dhritarashtra) desist.

sn: युद्धेन बाधेयुरिमांस्तथैव तैर्बाध्यमाना युधि तांश्च हन्युः। स्तेषां जयोयेति भवेन्मतं वः॥ स्तेषां विनाशाय यतेयुरेव। न ज्ञायते किं न करिष्यतीति॥
en: If they (the sons of Dhritarashtra) oppose them (the Pandavas) in battle the letter thus opposed will kill them; and if you are of opinion that the Pandavas, owing to insufficiency of numbers, will not be able to win victory over them let them combine with all their friends and try to overthrow them. The intentions of Duryodhana are not known nor what he is going to do.

sn: अज्ञायमाने च मते परस्य किं स्यात् समारभ्यतमं मतं वः। तस्मादितो गच्छतु धर्मशील: शुचिः कुलीनः पुरुषोऽप्रमत्तः॥ दूतः समर्थः प्रशमाय तेषां राज्यार्धदानाय युधिष्ठिरस्य।
en: The intentions of the other side not being known, how can you determine on what to do yourself. Therefore let a man virtuous, holy, of good parentage and wifeless go from here-a capable ambassador who will be able to pursuable them into surrendering half of Yudhishthira's kingdom.

sn: निशम्य वाक्यं तु जनार्दनस्य धर्मार्थयुक्तं मधुरं समं च॥ समाददे वाक्यमथाग्रजोऽस्य सम्पूज्य वाक्यं तदतीव राजन्॥
en: Hearing this speech of Janardana which was pregnant with meaning and virtue, interesting and impartial, his elder brother accepted the suggestions and after praising the speech addressed him O king, thus.

sn: बलदेव उवाच श्रुतं भवद्भिर्गदपूर्वजस्य वाक्यं यथा धर्मवदर्थवच्च। अजातशत्रोश्च हितं हितं च दुर्योधनस्यापि तथैव राज्ञः।।
en: Baladeva said The speech of the elder brother of Gada which is at once marked by a sense of virtue and prudence and which has aimed at the good of both Yudhishthira (one who has created no enemies) and king Duryodhana, has been listened to by you.

sn: अर्धं हि राज्यस्य विसृज्य वीराः कुन्तीसुतास्तस्य कृते यतन्ते। प्रदाय चार्घं धृतराष्ट्रपुत्रः सुखी सहास्माभिरतीव मोदेत्॥
en: The heroic sons of Kunti, being willing to forego half of their kingdom, are trying to get the other half, the son of Dhritarashtra too should give up half and pass his days very happily with us.

sn: लब्ध्वा हि राज्यं पुरुषप्रवीराः सम्यक्प्रवृत्तेषु परेषु चैवा स्तेषां प्रशान्तिश्च हितं प्रजानाम्॥
en: These heroes among men, having obtained half of the kingdom, will take to a quiet life, if the other party dose the same for their quietness means the good of their subjects.

sn: दुर्योधनस्यापि मतं च वेत्तुं वक्तुं च वाक्यानि युधिष्ठिरस्य। प्रियं च मे स्याद् यदि तत्र कश्चिद् व्रजेच्छमार्थं कुरुपाण्डवानाम्॥
en: I should be glad if some body were to go there to bring about good feelings among the Kauravas and the Pandavas, to know the intentions of Duryodhana and to tell them the views of Yudhishthira.

sn: स भीष्मामन्त्र्य कुरुप्रवीरं वैचित्रवीर्यं च महानुभावम्। द्रोणं सपुत्रं विदुरं कृपं च गान्धारराजं च ससूतपुत्रम्।।
en: Let him invite Bhishma, the heroic son of Kuru and the noble minded of Vichitravirya, Drona, with his son, Vidura and Kripa and the king of Gandhara with the son of Suta. son

sn: सर्वे च येऽन्ये धृतराष्ट्रपुत्रा बलप्रधाना निगमप्रदधानाः। स्थिताश्च धर्मेषु तथा स्वकेषु लोकप्रवीराः श्रुतकालवृद्धाः॥
en: And (with) also all the other sons of Dhritarashtra who have under their command the best army and a thorough knowledge of politics, who adhere to virtue, who are heroes among men and who know the meaning of the Vedas and the signs of the times.

sn: एतेषु सर्वेषु समागतेषु पौरेषु वृद्धेषु च संगतेषु। ब्रवीतु वाक्यं प्रणिपातयुक्तं कुन्तीसुतस्यार्थकरं यथा स्यात्॥
en: Let him all these men and also the citizens and aged men, assembled together what the son of Kunti has said with all deference and which is fraught with meaning.

sn: सर्वास्ववस्थासु च ते न कोप्या प्रस्तो हि सोऽर्थो बलमाश्रितैस्तैः। प्रियाभ्युपेतस्य युधिष्ठिरस्य द्यते प्रसक्तस्य हृतं च राज्यम्॥
en: Though they have taken possession of Yudhishthira's kingdom by force when he was addicted to gambling, still they ought not to be provoked under all situations.

sn: निवार्यमाणश्च कुरुप्रवीरः सर्वैः सुहृद्भियमप्यतज्ज्ञः। स दीव्यमानः प्रतिदीव्य चैनं गान्धारराजस्य सुतं मताक्षम्॥
en: This brave son of Kuru, unskillful at the game of dice, though dissuaded by all his friends, challenged this son of Gandhari, an expert in the game, to a match.

sn: हित्वा हि कर्णं च सुयोधनं च समाह्वयद् देवितुमाजमीढः। दुरोदरास्तत्र सहक्रस्रशोऽन्ये युधिष्ठिरो यान् विषहेत जेतुम्॥ उत्सृज्य तान् सौबलमेव चायं समाह्वयत् तेन जितोऽक्षवत्याम्। स दीव्यमानः प्रतिदेवनेन अक्षेषु नित्यं तु पराङ्मुखेषु॥
en: Although there were then at the place a thousand other people whom Yudhishthira could defeat at a game of dice, he took no notice of these and none of Karna and Suyodhana but challenged Subala's son and was defeated by him in the game. He lost at every step.

sn: संरम्भमाणो विजितः प्रसा तत्रापराधः शकुनेर्न कश्चित्। तस्मात् प्रणम्यैव वचो ब्रवीतु वैचित्रवीर्यं बहुसामयुक्तम्॥
en: Having once commenced, he lost through anger and no blame can for this attach to the son of Shakuni; therefore it behooves him (the messenger) to speak with due deference to the son of Vichitravirya and assume a conciliatory tone.

sn: तथा हि शक्यो धृतराष्ट्रपुत्रः स्वार्थं नियोक्तुं पुरुषेण तेन। अयुद्धमाकाक्षत कौरवाणां साम्नैव दुर्योधनमाह्वयध्वम्॥
en: By this means can the son of Dhritarashtra be persuaded, to enlist himself in our service, by the messenger. Let him address Duryodhana in a conciliatory tone and with the desire of the reverse of war.

sn: साम्ना जितोऽर्थोऽर्थकरो भवेत युद्धेऽनयो भविता नेह सोऽर्थः॥
en: A point gained by peaceful means is really beneficial, that gained by war is not a gain at all-it is only injurious.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवं ब्रुवत्येव मधुप्रवीरे शिनिप्रवीरः सहसोत्पपात। तच्चापि वाक्यं परिनिन्द्य तस्य समाददे वाक्यमिदं समन्युः॥
en: Vaishampayana said While that valiant son of Madhu was yet speaking, all on a sudden rose the brave descendant of Shini and condemning his speech addressed these words to him.

sn: सात्यकिरुवाच यादृशः पुरुषस्यात्मा तादृशं सम्प्रभाषते। यथारूपोऽन्तरात्मा ते तथारूपं प्रभाषसे।।।।
en: Satyaki said As the inner nature of a man is, so he speaks. As your inner nature is, so do you speak.

sn: सन्ति वै पुरुषाः शूराः सन्ति कापुरुषास्तथा। उभावेतौ दृढौ पक्षौ दृश्यते पुरुषान् प्रति॥
en: There are brave men and there are cowards. Both these well defined divisions are seen among human beings.

sn: एकस्मिन्नेव जायेते कुले क्लीबमहाबलौ। फलाफलवती शाखे यथैकस्मिन् वनस्पतौ॥
en: In the same family are born very powerful men and powerless ones, as the same forest contains trees that bear fruits and those that do not.

sn: नाभ्यसूयामि ते वाक्यं ब्रुवतो लाङ्गलध्वज। ये तु शृण्वन्ति ते वाक्यं तानसूयामि माधव॥
