en: O you who have the sign of a slough on your standard, I am not finding fault with your speech; I am, O son of Madhu, only blaming these who are listening to it.

sn: कथं हि धर्मराजस्य दोषमल्पमपि ब्रुवन्। लभते परिषन्मध्ये व्याहर्तुमकुतोभयः॥
en: How can one, who even in the slightest degree speaks ill of the virtuous king, dare continue in that stain without being checked, in this assembly.

sn: समाहूय महात्मानं जितवन्तोऽक्षकोविदाः। अनक्षज्ञं यथाश्रद्धं तेषु धर्मजयः कुतः॥
en: People, experts at the game of dice, challenged the noble minded one who was unskillful in the game and defeated him; how can this be a defeat in the proper sense?

sn: एवमप्ययमत्यन्तं यदि कुन्तीसुतं गेहे क्रीडन्तं भ्रातृभिः सह। अभिगम्य जयेयुस्ते तत् तेषां धर्मतो भवेत्। समाहूय तु राजानं क्षत्रधर्मरतं सदा॥ निकृत्या जितवन्तस्ते किं नु तेषां परं शुभम्। कथं प्रणिपतेच्चायमिह कृत्वा पणं परम्॥
en: If the son of Kunti had been playing with his brothers at home and those people coming there, defeated him, then that would have been a proper defeat. But they challenged the king who was ever attached to the observance of the rites of a Kshatriya. They won by a mean trick; how can prosperity attend such men? And why should those man here, after fulfilling his vow, approach them in a humiliating spirit.

sn: वनवासाद् विमुक्तस्तु प्राप्तः पैतामहं पदम्। यद्ययं पापवित्तानि कामयेत युधिष्ठिरः॥ परान् नार्हति याचितुम्। कथं च धर्मयुक्तास्ते न च राज्यं जिहीर्षवः॥
en: Freed now from his cxile in the forest he has now attained to the position of his grandfather. Even if this Yudhishthira is secking property wrongfully, it is not proper that he should beg other people's property though it would be righteous on their part not to surrender the kingdom.

sn: निवृत्तवासान् कौन्तेयान् य आहुर्विदिता इति। अनुनीता हि भीष्मेण द्रोणेन विदुरेण च॥
en: Through Bhishina, Drona and Vidura have passed the prescribed period unknown in exile, yet have they said that they have been recognized.

sn: न व्यवस्यन्ति पाण्डूनां प्रदातुं पैतृकं वसु। अहं तु ताञ्छितैर्बाणैरनुनीय रणे बलात्॥
en: They would not now consent to give back the ancestral territories of the Pandavas. And I shall persuade them by means of cold arrows in the field of battle.

sn: पादयोः पातयिष्यामि कौन्तेयस्य महात्मनः। अथ ते न व्यवस्यन्ति प्रणिपाताय धीमतः॥
en: And make them fall at the fect of the noble son of Kunti. If they refuse to fall at the feet of the wise (Yudhishthira).

sn: न हि ते गमिष्यन्ति सहामात्या यमस्य सदनं प्रति। युयुधानस्य संरब्धस्य युयुत्सतः॥
en: Then must they with their ministers go to the kingdom of death (Yama); they cannot surely withstand Yuyudhana (myself) determined to fight.

sn: वेगं समर्थाः संसोढुं वज्रस्येव महीधराः। को हि गाण्डीवधन्वानं कश्च चक्रायुधं युधि।१५।।
en: Can the mountains bears the force of the thunderbolt? Who can bear the force of him who uses the Gandiva as his bow (Arjuna) and of him who has the wheel in his hand (Bhimasena)?

sn: मां चापि विषहेत् क्रुद्धं कश्च भीमं दुरासदम्। यमौ च दृढधन्वानौ यमकालोपमद्युती। विराटद्रुपदौ वीरौ यमकालोपमद्युती॥
en: (Who can bear force of) myself when in wrath or of the Bhima who is hard to approach or of the twin brothers who firmly grasp the bow and whose effulgence is like that of Yama (who carries away life) and Kala (who cuts the thread of life) and the heroes Virates and Drupada who have the same quality?

sn: को जिजीविषुरासादेद् धृष्टद्युम्नं च पार्षतम्। पञ्चैतान् पाण्डवेयांस्तु द्रौपद्याः कीर्तिवर्धनान्॥
en: What man valuing his life can approach the descendant of Prishata Dhrishtadyumna also the five sons of the Pandavas who have added to Draupadi's glory.

sn: समप्रमाणान् पाण्डूनां समवीर्यान् मदोत्कटान्। सौभद्रं च महेष्वासममरैरपि दुःसहम्॥
en: And who are the equals of the Pandavas in valour and in every other respect and having the true pride of a soldier or (who can approach) the son of Subhadra, whose impetus is hard to be borne even by the gods.

sn: गदप्रद्युम्नसाम्बांश्च कालसूर्यानलोपमान्। ते वयं धृतराष्ट्रस्य पुत्रं शकुनिना सह॥ कर्णं चैव निहत्याजावभिषेक्ष्याम पाण्डवम्। नाधर्मो विद्यते कश्चिच्छत्रून् हत्वाऽऽततायिनः॥
en: And (who can approach) Gada, Pradyumna and Samba resembling Kala, the son of the fire. We shall after killing the son of Dhritarashtra, with Shakuni and also Karna in battle appoint (as king) the Pandava. It is no sin to destroy an enemy who would have slain ourselves.

sn: अधर्म्यमयशस्यं च शात्रवाणां प्रयाचनम्। हृद्गतस्तस्य य: कामस्तं कुरुध्वमतन्द्रिताः॥
en: It is both impious and shameful to beg from enemies; do speedily, therefore that which is his (Yudhishthira's) heart-felt desire.

sn: निसृष्टं धृतराष्ट्रेण राज्यं प्राप्नोतु पाण्डवः। अद्य पाण्डुसुतो राज्यं लभतां वा युधिष्ठिरः॥ निहता वा रणे सर्वे स्वप्स्यन्ति वसुधातले॥
en: Let the Pandava get the kingdom surrendered by Dhritarashtra. This day cither shall Yudhishthira, the son of Pandu get the kingdom or all our enemies fall on the ground stain in battle.

sn: दुपद उवाच एवमेतन्महाबाहो भविष्यति न संशयः। न हि दुर्योधनो राज्यं मधुरेण प्रदास्यति॥
en: Drupada said O you with long arms, it will doubtless turn out as you have said. Duryodhana will not give back the kingdom by peaceful means.

sn: अनुवय॑ति तं चापि धृतराष्ट्रः सुतप्रियः। भीष्मद्रोणौ च कार्पण्यान्माद् राधेयसौबलौ॥
en: And Dhritarashtra, fond of his son, will follow him. So will Bhima and Drona out of a false regard for the kingdom and the two sons of Subala out of folly.

sn: बलदेवस्य वाक्यं तु मम ज्ञाने न युज्यते। एतद्धि पुरुषेणारे कार्यं सुनयमिच्छता॥
en: In my opinion the suggestion of Baladeva is not appropriate; it can certainly be acted on by a man who is desirous of an amicable settlement.

sn: न तु वाच्यो मृदुवचो धार्तराष्ट्रः कथंचन। न हि मार्दवसाध्योऽसौ पापबुद्धिर्मतो मम॥
en: The son of Dhritarashtra ought by no means to be addressed to in a conciliatory tone; I think that it is impossible to bring the illmatured Duryodhana to reason by peaceful means.

sn: गर्दभे मार्दवं कुर्याद् गोषु तीक्ष्णं समाचरेत्। मृदु दुर्योधने वाक्यं यो ब्रूयात् पापचेतसि॥ मृदुं वै मन्यते पापो भाषमाणमशक्तिकम्। जितम) विजानीयादबुधो मार्दवे सति॥
en: Peaceful means should be adopted for asses; but severe measures should be resorted to for kines. He who uses mild words to the illhearted Duryodhana would be set down as an incapable man by that vicious one and if a mild course is adopted the fool will think himself to have won.

sn: एतच्चैव करिष्यामो यत्नश्च क्रियतामिह। प्रस्थापयाम मित्रेभ्यो बलान्युद्योजयन्तु नः॥
en: We shall do this; let us make preparations here and send word to our friends to collect armies for us.

sn: शल्यस्य धृष्टकेतोश्च जयत्सेनस्य वा विभो। केकयानां च सर्वेषां दूता गच्छन्तु शीघ्रगाः॥
en: Let swift going messengers go to Shalya. Dhrishtakctu, Jayatsena and the ruler of the Kaikeyas.

sn: स च दुर्योधनो नूनं प्रेषयिष्यति सर्वशः। पूर्वाभिपन्नाः सन्तश्च भजन्ते पूर्वचोदनम्॥
en: Duryodhana, too will certainly send his messenger to all places and good men attend to those who send word first and who ask for help first.

sn: तत् त्वरध्वं नरेन्द्राणां पूर्वमेव प्रचोदने। महद्धि कार्यं वोढव्यमिति मे वर्तते मतिः॥
en: Make haste, therefore, in first sending words to this kings among men. I think that some great event is about to come.

sn: शल्यस्य प्रेष्यतां शीघ्रं ये च तस्यानुगा नृपाः। भगदत्ताय राज्ञे च पूर्वसागरवासिने॥
en: Send quickly to Shalya and to those kings who are under his suzerainty and the king Bhagadatta and the inhabitants of the Eastern seas,

sn: अमितौजसे तथोग्राय हार्दिक्यायान्धकाय च। दीर्घप्रज्ञाय शूराय रोचमानाय वा विभो॥
en: And to Hardikya of unequaled prowess and to the haughty Andhaka and Rochamana, the hero of good understanding.

sn: आनीयतां बृहन्तश्च सेनाबिन्दुश्च पार्थिवः। सेनजित् प्रतिविन्ध्यश्च चित्रवर्मा सुवास्तुकः॥
en: Invite Brihanta, the king Senabindu and Senajit, Prativindhya, Chitravarma and Suvastuka.

sn: बाह्रीको मुञ्जकेशश्च चैद्याधिपतिरेव च। सुपार्श्वश्च सुबाहुश्च पौरवश्च महारथः॥
en: Also Bahlika, Munjakesha and the lord of the Chedis, Suparshva, Subahu and the mighty Paurava.

sn: शकानां पह्लवानां च दरदानां च ये नृपाः। सुरारिश्च नदीजश्च कर्णवेष्टश्च पार्थिवः॥
en: Also those who rule over the Shakas the Pahlavas and the Daradas and Surari Nadija and the king Karnaveshta.

sn: नीलश्च वीरधर्मा च भूमिपालश्च वीर्यवान्। दुर्जयो दन्तवक्त्रश्च रुक्मी च जनमेजयः॥ आषाढो वायुवेगश्च पूर्वपाली च पार्थिवः। भूरितेजा देवकश्च एकलव्यः सहात्मजैः॥
en: And Nila, Viradharma and the heroic Bhumipala, Dantavaktra hard to vanquish, Rukmi and Janamejaya, Ashadha, Vayuvega and king Purvapali, Devaka of unusual prowess and Ekalavya with his son.

sn: कारूषकाच राजानः क्षेमधूर्तिश्च वीर्यवान्। काम्बोजा ऋषिका ये च पश्चिमानूपकाश्च ये॥
en: And the kings of the Karusha and the heroic Kshemadhurti and the rulers Kamboja and the Rishika tribes and the races inhabiting the west.

sn: जयत्सेनश्च काश्यश्च तथा पञ्चनदा नृपाः। क्राथपुत्रश्च दुर्धर्षः पार्वतीयाश्च ये नृपाः॥
en: And Jayatsena and the rulers of Kashi and of the land of the five rivers and the invulnerable son of Kratha and the rulers of the hilly districts.

sn: जानकिश्च सुशर्मा च मणिमान् योतिमत्सकः। पांशुराष्ट्राधिपश्चैव धृष्टकेतुश्च वीर्यवान्।॥
en: And Janaki, Susharma and Maniman and Yotimatsaka and the king Panshurashtra and the heroic Dhrishtaketu.

sn: तुण्डश्च दण्डधारश्च बृहत्सेनश्च वीर्यवान्। अपराजितो निषादस्व श्रेणिमान् वसुमानपि॥
en: And Tunda and Dandadhara and the valiant Brihatsena and the unconquered Nishada and Shreniman and Vasuman.

sn: बृहद्बलो महौजाश्च बाहुः परपुरञ्जयः। समुद्रसेनो राजा च सह पुत्रेण वीर्यवान्।॥
en: And Bahu of great strength and prowess and Parapuranjaya and Samudrasena with his brave son.

sn: उद्भवः क्षेमकश्चैव वाटधानश्च पार्थिवः। श्रुतायुश्च दृढायुश्च शाल्वपुत्रश्च वीर्यवान्॥
en: And Udbhava and Kshemaka and the king Vatadhana and Shrutayu and Dridhayu the valiant son of Shalva.

sn: कुमारश्च कलिङ्गानामीश्वरो युद्धदुर्मदः। एतेषां प्रेष्यतां शीघ्रमेतद्धि मम रोचते।॥
en: And Kumara and the Prince of the Kalingas haughty in battle. I think that you should send (messengers) quickly warinvitation to him.

sn: अयं च ब्राह्मणो विद्वान् मम राजन् पुरोहितः। प्रेष्यतां धृतराष्ट्राय वाक्यमस्मै प्रदीयताम्॥
en: This Brahmin, O king, who is my priest, is a wise man, send him to Dhritarashtra and tell him what he is to say.

sn: यथा दुर्योधनो वाच्यो यथा शान्तनवो नृपः। धृतराष्ट्रो यथा वाच्यो द्रोणश्च रथिनां वरः॥
en: How Duryodhana is to be addressed, how the king Shantanva, how Dhritarashtra and how Drona, the best among the charioteers, tell him what he is to say.

sn: वासुदेव उवाच उपपन्नमिदं वाक्यं सोमकानां धुरंधरे। अर्थसिद्धिकरं राज्ञः पाण्डवस्यामितौजसः॥
en: Vasudeva said These words befit the chief of the king of the Pandu race, who is unequaled in prowess.

sn: एतच्च पूर्वं कार्यं नः सुनीतमभिकाङ्क्षताम्। अन्यथा ह्याचरन् कर्म पुरुषः स्यात् सुबालिशः॥
en: It ought to be done first of all by us, who desire to act on the principles of politics and the man who acts otherwise is a fool.

sn: किं तु संभन्धकं तुल्यमस्माकं कुरुपाण्डुषु। यथेष्टं वर्तमानेषु पाण्डवेषु च तेषु च॥
en: But our relations, are the same with the sons of Kuru and Pandu, whatever at this present moment might be those amongst themselves.

sn: ते विवाहार्थमानीता वयं सर्वे तथा भवान्। कृते विवाहे मुदिता गमिष्यामो गृहान् प्रति॥
en: We all have been invited here and you as well for the wedding and the ceremony being over we shall go well pleased homeward bound.

sn: भवान् वृद्धतमो राज्ञां वयसा च श्रुतेन च। शिष्यवत् ते वयं सर्वे भवामेह न संशयः॥
en: You are the oldest among kings both in age and in learning and we doubtless are like your pupils.

sn: भवन्तं धृतराष्ट्रश्च सततं बहु मन्यते। आचार्ययोः : सखा चासि द्रोणस्य च कृपस्य च॥
en: Dhritarashtra too always reveres you much and are the friend of the preceptors Drona and Kripa.

sn: स भवान् प्रेषयत्वद्य पाण्डवार्थकरं वचः। सर्वेषां निश्चितं तन्नः प्रेषयिष्यति यद् भवान्॥
en: This day, therefore, tutor us in what is to the interests of the Pandavas. None of us shall question what you say.

sn: यदि तावच्छमं कुर्यान्यायेन कुरुपुङ्गवः। न भवेत् कुरुपाण्डूनां सौभ्रात्रेण महान् क्षयः॥
en: If the chief among the Kurus seek peace on equal terms, there will be no injury done to the brotherly feeling between the Kauravas and the Pandavas.

sn: अथ दर्यान्वितो मोहान्न कुर्याद् धृतराष्ट्रजः। अन्येषां प्रेषयित्वा च पश्चादस्मान् समाह्वये॥
en: If the son of Dhritarashtra dose not thus seek peace owing to the ignorance mixed with vanity, summon us after sending word to others.

sn: ततो दुर्योधनो मन्दः सहामात्यः सबान्धवः। निष्ठामापत्स्यते मूढः क्रुद्धे गाण्डीवधन्वनि॥
en: Then the bad man Duryodhana along with his ministers and friends will meet his fate at the hands of him who uses the Gandiva as his bow and who will be fired with wrath.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततः सत्कृत्य वार्ष्णेयं विराटः पृथिवीपतिः। गृहान् प्रस्थापयामास सगणं सहबान्धवम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Then the lord of the earth Virata, having treated the descendant of Vrishni with due honours, sent him home along with his men and his friends.

sn: द्वारकां तु गते कृष्णे युधिष्ठिरपुरोगमाः। चक्रुः सांग्रामिकं सर्वं विराटश्च महीपतिः॥
en: Krishna having gone to Dwarka the followers of Yudhishthira and also the king Virata made all preparations for the war.

sn: ततः सम्प्रेषयामास विराट: सह बान्धवैः। सर्वेषां भूमिपालानां द्रुपदश्च महीपतिः॥
en: Then did Virata and his friends and also the king Drupada send word to all the rulers.

sn: वचनात् कुरुसिंहानां मत्स्यपाञ्चालयोश्च ते। समाजग्मुर्महीपालाः सम्प्रहृष्टा महाबलाः॥
en: At the request of those lions among the Kauravas of the rulers of the Matsya and Panchala, came there cheerfully kings with large arinies.

sn: तच्छ्रुत्वा पाण्डुपुत्राणां समागच्छन्महबलम्। धृतराष्ट्रसुताश्चापि समानिन्युर्महीपतीन्॥
en: Having heard that a large army was being collected for the sons of Pandu, Dhritarashtra's too brought together many rulers.

sn: समाकुला मही राजन् कुरुपाण्डवकारणात्। तदा समभवत् कृत्स्ना सम्प्रयाणे महीक्षिताम्॥
en: At that time, o king the earth became crowded with the throng of kings who had come either for the Kauravas or for the Pandavas.

sn: संकुला च तदा भूमिश्चतुरङ्गबलान्विता। बलानि तेषां वीराणामागच्छन्ति ततस्ततः॥
en: And the earth at time became thronged with the four elements of the army. The armies of those heroes began to pour from all quarters.

sn: चालयन्तीव गां देवीं सपर्वतवनामिमाम्। ततः प्रज्ञावयोवृद्ध पाञ्चाल्यः स्वपुरोहितम्। कुरुभ्यः प्रेषयामास युधिष्ठिरमते स्थितः॥
en: And the goddess earth, with her mountains and forest seemed as if trembling. And the king of the Panchałas, who was of the same opinion with; Yudhishthira, sent to the Kauravas his own priest who was old both in wisdom and in age.

sn: दुपद उवाच भूतानां प्राणिनः श्रेष्ठाः प्राणिनां बुद्धिजीविनः। बुद्धिमत्सु नराः श्रेष्ठा नरेष्वपि द्विजातयः॥
en: Drupada said Of all beings, those that have life are superior. Of those that have life, those that live with the help of their intelligence are superior, those that have intelligence man is superior and among men, those that are twice-born are superior.

sn: द्विजेषु वैद्याः श्रेयांसो वैद्येषु कृतबुद्धयः। कृतबुद्धिषु कर्तारः कर्तृषु ब्रह्मवादिनः॥
en: Among the twice-born, those that know the Vedas are superior and among the Vedaknowing people whose understanding is cultured are superior and among people with cultured understanding those living practical lives are superior and among practical people those that know Brahma are superior.

sn: स भवान् कृतबुद्धीनां प्रधान इति मे मतिः। कुलेन च विशिष्टोऽसि वयसा च श्रुतेन च॥
en: I am of opinion that you are the chief among those who have cultured understanding, you come of a respectable family and you are aged both in years and in learning.

sn: प्रज्ञया सदृशश्चासि शुक्रेणाङ्गिरसेन च। विदितं चापि ते सर्वं यथावृत्तः स कौरवः॥
en: Your wisdom is equal to that of Shukra or the son of Angirasa and it is known to you what sort of a man the Kaurava is.

sn: पाण्डवश्च यथावृत्तः कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः। धृतराष्ट्रस्य विदिते वञ्चिताः पाण्डवाः परैः॥
en: Also what sort of a man Yudhishthira and the son of Kunti the descendant of Pandu is. The sons Pandu were dispossessed (of their kingdom) with the help of the knowledge of Dhritarashtra.

sn: विदुरेणानुनीतोऽपि पुत्रमेवानुवर्तते। शकुनिर्बुद्धिपूर्वं हि कुन्तीपुत्रं समाह्वयत्॥
en: Though he is advised by Vidura, he follows the instructions of his son and it was at the instigation of Shakuni that he challenged the son of Kunti.

sn: अनक्षज्ञं मताक्षः सन् क्षत्रवृत्ते स्थितं शुचिम्। ते तथा वञ्चयित्वा तु धर्मराज युधिष्ठिरम्॥
en: Adepts at the play, they robbed the virtuous king Yudhishthira who was holy, attached to the rules of the Kshatriya class and unskillful at the game of dice.

sn: न कस्याञ्चिदवस्थायां राज्यं दास्यन्ति वै स्वयम्। भवांस्तु धर्मसंयुक्तं धृतराष्ट्र ब्रुवन् वचः॥
en: On no account whatever will they give back the kingdom voluntarily. You, too who will speak words of virtue to Dhritarashtra.

sn: मनांसि तस्य योधानां ध्रुवमावर्तयिष्यति। विदुरश्चापि तद् वाक्यं साधयिष्यति तावकम्॥ भीष्मद्रोणकृपादीनां भेदं संजनयिष्यति। अमात्येषु च भिन्नेषु योधेषु विमुखेषु च॥
en: Will certainly gain the hearts of his soldiers. And Vidura also by men of your words will try to create disaffection in minds the minds of Bhishma, Drona Kripa and others. With difference opinion among the ministers and disaffection in the soldiers.

sn: पुनरेकत्रकरणं तेषां कर्म भविष्यति। एतस्मिन्नन्तरे पार्थाः सुखमेकाग्रबुद्धयः॥ सेनाकर्म करिष्यन्ति द्रव्याणां चैव संचयम्। विद्यमानेषु च स्वेषु लम्बमाने तथा त्वयि॥
en: It will be their duty to make them agree and join one another; and in the meantime the very wise sons of Pritha will easily make preparations for the war and collect stores.

sn: न तथा ते करिष्यन्ति सेनाकर्म न संशयः। एतत् प्रयोजनं चात्र प्राधान्येनोपलभ्यते॥
en: While you are still there and their men are delaying, they no doubt will not be able to make preparations. This is necessary and here it seems imperative.

sn: संगत्या धृतराष्ट्रश्च कुर्याद् धर्म्यं वचस्तव। स भवान् धर्मयुक्तश्च धन॑ तेषु समाचरन्॥
en: Yourself, being virtuous, should behave virtuously with them and Dhritarashtra, on your meeting him, may act in conformity with your virtuous words.

sn: कृपालुषु परिक्लेशान् पाण्डवीयान् प्रकीर्तयन्। वृद्धेषु कुलधर्मं च ब्रुवन् पूर्वैरनुष्ठितम्॥
en: By detailing those that are kind the hardships of the Pandavas and telling before old people the virtuous acts in the family done by their ancestors,

sn: विभेत्स्यति मनांस्येषामिति मे नात्र संशयः। न च तेभ्यो भयं तेऽस्ति ब्राह्मणो ह्यसि वेदवित्॥
en: I have no doubt you will estrange the minds of the men and you need not have any fear for them for you are a Veda knowing Brahmin,

sn: दूतकर्मणि युक्तश्च स्थविरश्च विशेषतः। स भवान् पुष्ययोगेन मुहूर्तेन जयेन च। कौरवेयान् प्रयात्वाशु कौन्तेयस्यार्थसिद्धये॥
en: And engaged in the post of an ambassador especially as you are aged. You therefore set out quick for the accomplishment of the interests of the son of Kunti the moment called Jaya and at the position of the planets named Pushya.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तथानुशिष्टः प्रययौ दुपदेन महात्मना। पुरोधा वृत्तसम्पन्नो नगरं नागसाह्वयम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Being instructed in this way by the noblehearted Drupada the priest went to the city called after the elephant.

sn: शिष्यैः परिवृतो विद्वान् नीतिशास्त्रार्थकोविदः। पाण्डवानां हितार्थाय कौरवान् प्रति जग्मिवान्॥
en: The priest, who was learned in scriptures of ethics and economy went to the city of Kauravas with his disciples.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच पुरोहितं ते प्रस्थाप्य नगरं नागसाह्वयम्। दूतान् प्रस्थापयामासुः पार्थिवेभ्यस्ततस्ततः॥
en: Vaishampayana said His (Drupada's) priest, having gone towards the city called after the elephant, the Pandavas sent in messengers to the rulers in the several parts.

sn: प्रस्थाप्य दूतानन्यत्र द्वारकां पुरुषर्षभः। स्वयं जगाम कौरव्यः कुन्तीपुत्रो धनंजयः॥
en: Having sent messengers elsewhere, the best among men, Dhananjaya, the son of Kunti, of race Kuru himself, went to Dwraka.

sn: गते द्वारवती कृष्णे बलदेवे च माधवे। सह वृष्ण्यन्धकैः सर्वैर्भोजैश्च शतशस्तदा।॥
en: sons The of Madhu, Krishna and Balarama, in company with the Vrishni race and Andhaka and Bhoja by hundreds, having gone to Dvaravati.

sn: सर्वमागमयामास पाण्डवानां विचेष्टितम्। धृतराष्ट्रात्मजो राजा गूढैः प्रणिहितैश्चरैः॥
en: The son of Dhritarashtra, himself a king, by sending scouts, privately, came to know all that had been done by the Pandavas.

sn: स श्रुत्वा माधवं यान्त सदश्वैरनिलोपमैः। बलेन नातिमहता द्वारकामभ्ययात् पुरीम्॥
en: Having heard that Madhava was on his way he set out for the city of Dwraka, with a retinue not large and good horses which could be compared to the wind.

sn: तमेव दिवसं चापि कौन्तेयः पाण्डुनन्दनः। आनर्तनगरी रम्या जगामाशु धनंजयः॥
en: That very day had Dhananjaya, the son of Kunti, of the race of Pandu, arrived at the beautiful city of the Anartas.

sn: तौ यात्वा पुरुषव्याघ्रौ द्वारकां कुरुनन्दनौ। सुप्तं ददृशतुः कृष्णं शयानं चाभिजग्मतुः॥
en: The two sons of Kuru, foremost among men, having reached Dwraka, saw Krishna asleep and went near him as he lay.

sn: ततः शयाने गोविन्दे प्रविवेश सुयोधनः। उच्छीर्षतश्च कृष्णस्य निषसाद वरासने॥
en: And as Govinda lay, Suyodhana entered and sat him down on the floor which he used as a seat near the head of Krishna.

sn: ततः किरीटी तस्यानुप्रविवेश महामनाः। पश्चाच्चैव स कृष्णस्य प्रह्वोऽतिष्ठत् कृताञ्जलिः॥
en: Then did enter the large-minded one, wearing a crown and stood with the hands clasped near the foot of Krishna.

sn: प्रतिबुद्धः स वार्ष्णेयो ददर्शाग्रे किरीटिनम्। स तयोः स्वागतं कृत्वा यथावत् प्रतिपूज्य तौ॥
en: The son of Vrishni, having awakened, first saw the one wearing a crown and welcomed them and did them due honours.

sn: तदागमनजं हेतुं पप्रच्छ मधुसूदनः। ततो दुर्योधनः कृष्णमुवाच प्रहसन्निव॥
en: The son of Madhu asked the cause of their coming and Duryodhana said as if in jest-

sn: विग्रहेऽस्मिन् भवान् साह्यं मम दातुमिहार्हति। समं हि भवतः सख्यं मम चैवार्जुनेऽपि च॥
en: "It is befitting that you should lend me your help in this war, for your friendship with myself and that with Arjuna are equal.

sn: तथा सम्बन्धकं तुल्यमस्माकं त्वयि माधव। अहं चाभिगतः पूर्वं त्वामद्य मधुसूदन॥
en: And, O slayer of Madhu our relations with you are the same and this day I have come first to you.

sn: पूर्वं चाभिगतं सन्तो भजन्ते पूर्वसारिणः। त्वं च श्रेष्ठतमो लोके सतामद्य जनार्दन। सततं सम्मतश्चैव सद्वृत्तमनुपालय॥
en: From the time of our ancestors, good men have befriended him who has been the first to come; and you, O Janardana, are the best person in this world; therefore act after this good example which has always been followed."

sn: कृष्ण उवाच भवानभिगतः पूर्वमत्र मे नास्ति संशयः। दृष्टस्तु प्रथमं राजन् मया पार्थो धनंजयः॥
en: Srikrishna said I have not the slightest doubt that you came here first, but Dhananjaya, the son of Pritha has been, O king, first seen by me.

sn: तव पूर्वाभिगमनात् पूर्वं चाप्यस्य दर्शनात्। साहाय्यमुभयोरेव करिष्यामि सुयोधन॥
en: O Suyodhana, yourself having come first and he having been seen by me first, I shall help both of you.

sn: प्रवारणं तु बालानां पूर्वं कार्यमिति श्रुतिः। तस्मात् प्रवारणं पूर्वमर्हः पार्थो धनंजयः॥
en: But the holy books lay down that the younger persons should be aided first, therefore I should first assist Dhananjaya, the son of Pritha.

sn: मत्संहननतुल्यानां गोपानामर्बुद महत्। नारायणा इति ख्याताः सर्वे संग्रामयोधिनः॥
en: There is that large army of a hundred million of gopas who fight in battle, each of whom is capable of slaying me and who are known as the Narayanas.

sn: ते वा युधि दुराधर्षा भवन्त्वेकस्य सैनिकाः। अयुध्यमानः संग्रामे न्यस्तशस्त्रोऽहमेकतः॥
en: Let them, who are hard to vanquish in battle, be the army of one party of you and let myself who shall not fight, having put off my weapons, take the side of the other.

sn: आभ्यामन्यतरं पार्थ यत् ते हृद्यतरं मतम्। तद वृणीतां भवानग्रे प्रवार्यस्त्वं हि धर्मतः॥
en: Of these two, O son of Pritha, choose any one after your liking, for have the right of choosing first.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्तस्तु कृष्णेन कुन्तीपुत्रो धनंजयः। अयुध्यमानं संग्रामे वरयामास केशवम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Dhananjaya the son of Kunti being thus spoken to by Krishna chose Keshava, who was not to fight in the battle.

sn: नारायणममित्रघ्नं कामाज्जातमजं नृषु। सर्वक्षत्रस्य पुरतो देवदानवयोरपि॥
en: (Who was) Narayana himself, the destroyer of those who were not his friends, who had volunteered a birth among men and who was superior to all the Kshatriyas, the gods and the Danavas.

sn: दुर्योधनस्तु तत् सैन्यं सर्वमावरयत् तदा। सहस्राणां सहस्रं तु योधानां प्राप्य भारत॥ कृष्णं चापहृतं ज्ञात्वा सम्प्राय परमां मुदम्। दुर्योधनस्तु तत् सैन्यं सर्वमादाय पार्थिवः॥ ततोऽभ्ययाद् भीमबलो रौहिणेयं महाबलम्। सर्वं चागमने हेतुं स तस्मै संन्यवेदयत्। प्रत्युवाच ततः शौरिर्द्धार्तराष्ट्रमिदं वचः॥
en: And Duryodhana then chose the whole of that army. And O son of Bharata, having got thousands upon thousands of warriors and knowing (even) that Krishna was lost to him, he became mighty pleased; And O king, Duryodhana having taken that whole army of fearful strength came to the son of Rohini who was of great strength. He submitted to him the whole cause of his coming, upon which the son of Sura said in reply to the son of Dhritarashtra.

sn: बलदेव उवाच विदितं ते नरव्याघ्र सर्वं भवितुमर्हति। यन्मयोक्तं विराटस्य पुरा वैवाहिके तदा॥
en: O you best among men, it is fitting that what was said by me at the time of the marriage, should be known to you.

sn: निगृह्योक्तो हृषीकेशस्त्वदर्थं कुरुनन्दन। मया सम्बन्धकं तुल्यमिति राजन् पुनः पुनः॥
en: O you son of Kuru, for your sake did I speak contradicting what Hrishikesha had said. O king! again and again did I point out that our relations with both of you were equal.

sn: न च तद् वाक्यमुक्तं वै केशवं प्रत्यपद्यत। न चाहमुत्सहे कृष्णं विना स्थातुमपि क्षणम्॥
en: And what I said, Keshava did not accept. I cannot for a moment exist separated from Krishna.

sn: नाहं सहायः पार्थस्य नापि दुर्योधनस्य वै। इति मे निश्चिता बुद्धिर्वासुदेवमवेक्ष्य ह॥
en: I am no helper of either the son of Pritha or that of Duryodhana; such is the unalterable resolution I have come to after the opinion formed by Krishna.

sn: जातोऽसि भारते वंशे सर्वपार्थिवपूजिते। गच्छ युद्धस्व धर्मेण क्षात्रेण पुरुषर्षभा॥
en: You are born in the race of Bharata, honored by all rulers of the earth; O you best among men, go and fight in strict accordance with the rules of honour and those of the military class."

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच इत्येवमुक्तस्तु तदा परिष्वज्य हलायुधम्। कृष्णं चापहतं ज्ञात्वा युद्धान्मने जितं जयम्॥
en: Being thus addressed he embraced him who used the plough as a weapon and knowing that Krishna had gone over to the other side he regarded as through a victory had already been achieved in battle.

sn: सोऽभ्ययात् कृतवर्माणं धृतराष्ट्रसुतो नृपः। कृतवर्मा ददौ तस्य सेनामक्षौहिणी तदा॥
en: The son of Dhritarashtra, himself a king, then went to Kritavarma and Kritavarma gave him an army counting an Akshauhini.

sn: स तेन सर्वसैन्येन भीमेन कुरुनन्दनः। वृतः परिययौ हृष्टः सुहृदः सम्प्रहर्षयन्॥
en: The son of Kuru, surrounded by all those troops, which were terrible looking, went forward with a light heart causing delight to his friends.

sn: ततः पीताम्बरधरो जगत्स्रष्टा जनार्दनः। गते दुर्योधने कृष्णः किरीटिनमथाब्रवीत्। अयुध्यमानः कां बुद्धिमास्थायाहं वृतस्त्वया॥
en: Duryodhana having departed, the creator of the world, Janardana, with yellow robes on, said to the wearer of the crown-"Knowing that I shall not take any part in the battle, why have you chosen me?"

sn: अर्जुन उवाच भवान् समर्थस्तानं सर्वान् निहन्तु नात्र संशयः। निहन्तुमहमष्येकः समर्थः पुरुषर्षभ॥
en: Arjuna said "There is no doubt that you can slay all of them. O foremost among men, I too, alone, am able to slay them all.

sn: भवांस्तु कीर्तिमाँल्लोके तद् यशस्त्वां गमिष्यति। यशसां चाहमप्यर्थी तस्मादसि मया वृतः॥
en: In this world you are an illustrious man and I shall attain to eminence similar to yours by killing them single-handed. I too am a seeker after fame and so will you be surrounded by me.

sn: सारथ्यं तु त्वया कार्यमिति मे मानसं सदा। चिररात्रेप्सितं कामं तद् भवान् कर्तुमर्हति॥
en: It has been my desire to have the office of the charioteer filled by you and it is fitting that you should fulfill this desire which has been felt by me for a long time.

sn: वासुदेव उवाच उपपत्रमिदं पार्थ यत् स्पर्धसि मया सह। सारथ्यं ते करिष्यामि कामः सम्पद्यतां तव॥
en: Vasudeva said It is fitting, O son of Pritha, that you measure yourself with me. I shall act as your charioteer, let your desire be fulfilled.

sn: वैशम्पयान उवाच एवं प्रमुदितः पार्थः कृष्णेन सहितस्तदा। वृतो दशाहप्रवरैः पुनरायाद् युधिष्ठिरम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Being thus rendered glad, the son of Pritha, in company with Krishna and surrounded by the chiefs of the Dasharha race, came back to Yudhishthira.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच शल्यः श्रुत्वा तु दूतानां सैन्येन महता वृतः। अभ्ययात् पाण्डवान् राजन् सह पुत्रैर्महारथैः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Shalya, having heard the news of hostility between the two parties, went to help the Pandavas, O king, surrounded by a large army and by his friends who were mighty in battle.

sn: तस्य सेनानिवेशोऽभूदध्यर्धमिव योजनम्। तथा हि विपुलां सेनां बिभर्ति स नरर्षभः॥
en: The encampment of his army occupied one half of a yojana. That foremost among men was the lord of such a large army.

sn: अक्षौहिणीपती राजन् महावीर्यपराक्रमः। विचित्रकवचाः शूरा विचित्रध्वजकार्मुकाः॥ विचित्राभरणाः सर्वे विचित्ररथवाहनाः। विचित्रस्रग्धराः सर्वे विचित्राम्बरभूषणाः॥ स्वदेशवेषाभरणा वीराः शतसहस्रशः। तस्य सेनाप्रणेतारो बभूवुः क्षत्रियर्षभाः॥
en: That man of great prowess and strength was, O king, the lord of an Akshauhini and heroes-best among the Kshatriyas with diverse armours, diverse omaments and all riding cars diverse and animals, with diverse garlands, all putting on diverse dresses the dresses and ornaments of their respective lands, counted by hundreds and thousands ecame the leaders of his army.

sn: व्यथयन्निव भूतानि कम्पयन्निव मेदिनीम्। शनैर्विश्रामयन् सेनां स ययौ येन पाण्डवः॥
en: He went by show marches to the place where the Pandavas were encamped, affording rest to his army and as if causing pain to the beings and shaking the earth.

sn: ततो दुर्योधनः श्रुत्वा महात्मानं महारथम्। उपायान्तमभिद्रुत्य स्वयमानर्च भारत॥
en: Duryodhana, having, O son of Bharata, heard that the great-minded one, mighty in battle, was coming hastened towards him and welcomed him in person.

sn: कारयामास पूजार्थं तस्य दुर्योधनः सभाः। रमणीयेषु देशेषु रत्नचित्राः स्वलंकृताः॥
en: And for his accommodation and honour, Duryodhana had palaces erected in charming spots ornamented with gems and well decorated.

sn: शिल्पिभिर्विविधैश्चैव क्रीडास्तत्र प्रयोजिताः। तत्र माल्यानि मांसानि भक्ष्यं पेयं च सत्कृतम्॥
en: And sent there various artists for the amusement (of Shalya and his men) and provided there all sorts of eatables, drinks, meats and garlands.

sn: कूपाश्च विविधाकारा मनोहर्षविवर्धनाः। वाष्यश्च विविधाकारा औदकानि गृहाणि च॥
en: And he (provided) wells of various shapes calculated to increase the cheerfulness of the heart and several sorts of streams, fountains and buildings.

sn: स ताः सभाः समासाद्य पूज्यमानो यथाऽमरः। दुर्योधनस्य सचिवैर्देशे देशे समन्ततः॥
en: Being welcomed and honoured by the agents of Duryodhana, as he arrived at these palaces in different countries, with the worship due to the gods.

sn: आजगाम सभामन्यां देवावसथवर्चसम्। स तत्र विषयैर्युक्तः कल्याणैरतिमानुषैः॥
en: He came to a palace, which would have been suitable even as the resting place for the gods; and being provided with all sorts of things and greeted with honours due to beings superior to man.

sn: मेनेऽभ्यधिकमात्मानमवमेने पुरंदरम्। पप्रच्छ स ततः प्रेष्यान् प्रहृष्टः क्षत्रियर्षभः॥
en: He thought too highly of himself and too little even of Purandara (Indra) and that, best among the Kshatriyas being pleased, asked the servants, sayingयुधिष्ठिरस्य पुरुषाः केऽत्र चक्रुः सभा इमाः।

sn: आनीयन्तां सभाकाराः प्रदेयारे हि मे मताः॥
en: Where are the men of Yudhishthira who erected these palaces here? Bring them. In my opinion it is proper for those builders of palaces to be rewarded by me.

sn: प्रसादमेषां दास्यामि कुन्तीपुत्रोऽनुमन्यताम्। दुर्योधनाय तत् सर्वं कथयन्ति स्म विस्मिताः॥
en: "I shall reward them, may it so please the son of Kunti.” They all then, surprised, informed Duryodhana of all this,

sn: सम्प्रहृष्टो यदा शल्यो दिदित्सुरपि जीवितम्। गूढो दुर्योधनस्तत्र दर्शयामास मातुलम्॥
en: And when Shalya was very highly pleased and did not mind giving away even his life, Duryodhana, who had concealed himself there, appeared before his maternal uncle.

sn: तं दृष्ट्वा मद्रराजश्च ज्ञात्वा यत्नं च तस्य तम्। परिष्वज्याब्रवीत् प्रीत इष्टोऽर्थो गृह्यतामिति॥
en: Seeing the king of Madra, he knew that all these attentions came from him and embracing Duryodhana said, accept what you desire.

sn: दुर्योधन उवाच सत्यवान् भव कल्याण वरो वै मम दीयताम्। सर्वसेनाप्रणेता वै भवान् भवितुमर्हति॥
en: Duryodhana said May your word be true. Grant me an auspicious boon. It is fitting that you should be the leader of my army.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच कृतमित्यब्रवीच्छल्यः किमन्यत् क्रियतामिति। कृतमित्येव गान्धारिः प्रत्युवाच पुनः पुनः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Said Shalya “It is done. What else do you desire of me?" and the son of Gandhari kept on repeating, “It is done."

sn: शल्य उवाच गच्छ दुर्योधन पुरं स्वकमेव नरर्षभ। अहं गमिष्ये द्रष्टुं वै युधिष्ठिरमरिंदमम्॥
en: Shalya said O Duryodhana, O you best among men, go to your own capital, I shall go to see that subduer of his enemies, Yudhishthira.

sn: दृष्ट्वा युधिष्ठिरं राजन् क्षिप्रमेध्ये नराधिप। अवश्यं चापि द्रष्टव्यः पाण्डवः पुरुषर्षभः॥
en: Having seen Yudhishthira, I shall come soon, O king. That best among men the son of Pandu, must be seen by me.

sn: दुर्योधन उवाच क्षिप्रमागम्यतां राजन् पाण्डवं वीक्ष्य पार्थिव। त्वय्यधीनः स्म राजेन्द्र वरदानं स्मरस्व नः॥
en: Duryodhana said O king, O Ruler of the earth, come soon after seeing the son of Pandu. I depend on you. O best among kings, remember the boon you have granted me.

sn: शल्य उवाच क्षिप्रमेष्यामि भद्रं ते गच्छस्व स्वपुरं नृप। परिष्वज्य तथाऽन्योन्यं शल्यदुर्योधनावुभौ॥
en: Shalya said "Soon shall I return. (In the mean time) I wish you well; O king, go to your own capital.” Then the two, Shalya and Duryodhana, embraced each other.

sn: स तथा शल्यमामन्त्र्य पुनरायात् स्वकं पुरम्। शल्यो जगाम कौन्तेयानाख्यातुं कर्म तस्य तत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said And having thus done honour to Shalya, he came back to his own capital while Shalya went to the sons of Kunti to tell them of that act of Duryodhana's.

sn: उपप्लव्यं स गत्वा तु स्कन्धावारं प्रविश्य च। पाण्डवानथ तान् सर्वान् शल्यस्तत्र ददर्श ह॥
en: Having come to Upaplavya and entered the camp, Shalya saw all the sons of Pandu there.

sn: समेत्य च महाबाहुः शल्यः पाण्डुसेतैस्तदा। पाद्यमयं च गां चैव प्रत्यगृह्णाद् यथाविधि॥
en: And having come there, he, the long armed one accepted the customary water for washing his feet and other gifts including a cow.

sn: ततः कुशलपूर्वं हि मद्रराजोऽरिसूदनः। प्रीत्या परमया युक्तः समाश्लिष्यद् युधिष्ठिरम्॥
en: And then that slayer of his enemies, the king of the Madras, having asked them about their health, embraced Yudhishthira, with great cheerfulness.

sn: तथा भीमार्जुनौ कृष्णौ स्वस्रीयौ च यमावुभौ। आसने चोपविष्टस्तु शल्यः पार्थमुवाच ह॥
en: And having done the same to Bhima and Arjuna and both the twin brothers, the sons of his sister, Shalya, who had seated himself, said to the son of Pritha:

sn: कुशलं राजशार्दूलं कच्चित् ते कुरुनन्दन। अरण्यवासाद् दिष्ट्यासि विमुक्तो जयतां वर॥
en: O best among kings, O son of Kuru, is it all right with you? O you victorious one! you have now passed the prescribed period of residence in the forest.

sn: सुदुष्करं कृतं राजन् निर्जने वसता त्वया। भ्रातृभिः सह राजेन्द्र कृष्णया चानया सह।॥
en: 0 king, great difficulties have been overcome by yourself residing in the forest, in the company, O chief of kings, of your brothers and this lady.

sn: अज्ञातवासं घोरं च वसता दुष्करं कृतम्। दुःखमेव कुतः सौख्यं भ्रष्टराज्यस्य भारत॥
en: Residence unknown and unrecognised was another great difficulty overcome by you. O son of Bharata, naught but misery attends him who has lost a kingdom. Where is happiness for him?

sn: दुःखस्यैतस्य महतौ धार्तराष्ट्रकृतस्य वै। अवाप्स्यसि सुखं राजन् हत्वा शत्रून् परंतप॥
en: After all this great trouble and misery brought on by the son of Dhritarashtra, O king, you will get happiness after having slain your enemies, O great devotee.

sn: विदितं ते महाराज लोकतन्त्रं नराधिप। तस्माल्लोभकृतं किञ्चित् तव तात न विद्यते॥
en: The ways and habits of men are known to you, O great king, O lord of men and therefore, O son, never has the slightest avarice been present in you.

sn: राजर्षीणां पुराणानां मार्गमन्विच्छ भारत। दाने तपसि सत्ये च भव तात युधिष्ठिर॥
en: O son of Bharata, follow in the path of the great Rishi, king of old and O my son Yudhishthira, be their equal in liberality, devotion and truth,

sn: क्षमा दमश्च सत्यं च अहिंसा च युधिष्ठिर। अद्भुतश्च पुनर्लोकस्त्वयि राजन् प्रतिष्ठितः॥
en: O Yudhishthira, forgiveness, power of self-control, truth, absence of desire for harm to anybody and all other virtues, that are rare in this world, are present in you, O king.

sn: मृदुर्वदान्यो ब्रह्मण्यो दाता धर्मपरायणः। धर्मास्ते विदिता राजन् बहवो लोकसाक्षिकाः॥
en: You are mild, generous, religions, liberal and attached to virtue. O king, all the virtues known among men are also known to you.

sn: सर्वं जगदिदं तात विदितं ते परंतप। दिष्ट्या कृच्छ्रमिदं राजन् पारितं भरतर्षभ॥
en: O son, everything connected with this world is known to you. O king, O you best among the race of Bharata, it is fortunate that this trouble is past.

sn: दिष्ट्या पश्यामि राजेन्द्र धर्मात्मानं सहानुगम्। निस्तीर्णं दुष्करं राजंस्त्वा धर्मनिचयं प्रभो॥
en: It is fortunate that I see, O king O chief among the kings, O Lord, yourself, the treasury of virtues and large-minded, come out of your difficulties.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततोऽस्याकथयद् राजा दुर्योधनसमागमम्। तच्च शुश्रूषितं सर्वं वरदानं च भारत॥
en: Vaishampayana said Then, O descendant of Bharata, did the king (Shalya) tell (the Pandavas) all about his meeting with Duryodhana, his promise and his boon.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच सुकृतं ते कृतं राजन् प्रहृष्टेनान्तरात्मना। दुर्योधनस्य यद् वीर त्वया वाचा प्रतिश्रुतम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said "O king, a good act has been done by you in that you have fulfilled a promise made when you were well pleased in the recesses of your heart.

sn: एकं त्विच्छामि भद्रं ते क्रियमाणं महीपते। राजन्नकर्तव्यमपि कर्तुमर्हसि सत्तम॥
en: But, O lord of earth, I wish you well. I want you to do one thing for me. O king, O you most honest one, though it is improper still must you do it.

sn: ममत्ववेक्षया वीर शृणु विज्ञापयामि ते। भवानिह च सारथ्ये वासुदेवसमो युधि॥
en: O hero, listen to what I tell you, you are a great king equal to the son of Vasudeva in battle.

sn: कर्णार्जुनाभ्यां सम्प्राप्ते द्वैरथे राजसत्तम। कर्णस्य भवता कार्यं सारथ्यं नात्र संशयः॥
en: O you best among kings, when the two, Karna and Arjuna meet in two chariots (in battle) I have no doubt that the office of charioteer of Karna will be filled by you.

sn: तत्र पाल्योऽर्जुनो राजन् यदि मत्प्रियमिच्छसि। तेजोवधश्च ते कार्य: सौतेरस्मज्जयावहः॥ अकर्तव्यमपि ह्येतत् कर्तुमर्हसि मातुल।
en: O king, if you wish well to me, Arjuna must be protected by you and you should do what kills the energy of the son of Suta and what is calculated to bring him defeat. Though this is improper, yet must you do it, maternal uncle of mine.

sn: शल्य उवाच शृणु पाण्डव ते भद्रं यद् ब्रवीषि महात्मनः। तेजोवधनिमित्तं मां सूतपुत्रस्य सङ्गमे॥
en: Shalya said Hear me, O son of Pandu, I wish you well O noble-minded one, what you are telling me is to kill the energy of the son of Suta, when I am with him.

sn: अहं तस्य भविष्यामि संग्रामे सारथिध्रुवम्। वासुदेवेन हि समं नित्यं मां स हि मन्यते॥
en: I shall most certainly be his charioteer in the battle. He has always regarded me as the equal of the son of Vasudeva.

sn: तस्याहं कुरुशार्दूल प्रतीपमहितं वचः। ध्रुवं संकथयिष्यामि योद्धुकामस्य संयुगे॥
en: O you best among the race of Kuru, I shall most certainly, when with him who is desirous of battle, speak what will do him harm and go against him.

sn: यथा स हतदर्पश्च हृततेजाश्च पाण्डव। भविष्यति सुखं हन्तु सत्यमेतद् ब्रवीमि ते॥
en: (I shall do this) so that his energy will be killed and his pride gone, O son of Pandu and then it will be easy to kill him. I speak with all sincerity.

sn: एवमेतत् करिष्यामि यथा तात त्वमात्थ माम्। यच्चान्यदपिशक्ष्यामि तत् करिष्यामि ते प्रियम्॥
en: O son, I shall do what you have told me and I shall do any thing more can I which is for your good.

sn: यच्च दुःखं त्वया प्राप्तं द्यूते वै कृष्णया सह। परुषाणि च वाक्यानि सूतपुत्रकृतानि वै॥ जटासुरात् परिक्लेश: कीचकाच्च महाद्युते। द्रौपद्याधिगतं सर्वं दमयन्त्या यथाऽशुभम्॥ सर्वं दुःखमिदं वीर सुखोदकं भविष्यति। नात्र मन्युस्त्वया कार्यो विधिर्हि बलवत्तरः॥
en: All the troubles you have encountered with Draupadi after the game of dice and the harsh words you have had, to listen to, through the son of Suta and all the miseries endured, o illustrious one, through the Asura named Jata and Kichaka-all these unhappiness endured by Draupadi as (unhappiness was endured) by Damayanti-all this trouble, O hero, will give rise to happiness. Do not think that all this is through you, this is done by the fate which has greater control over matters.

sn: दुःखानि हि महात्मानः प्राप्नुवन्ति युधिष्ठिर। देवैरपि हि दुःखानि प्राप्तानि जगतीपते॥
en: 0 Yudhishthira, great minded persons, meet with difficulties. O Lord of the world, difficulties have been met with by the gods too.

sn: इन्द्रेण श्रूयते राजन् सभार्येण महात्मना। अनुभूतं महद् दुःखं देवराजेन भारत॥
en: We are told O king, O son of Bharata that the large minded Indra, the chief among the gods, had to endure great misery with his queen.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच कथमिन्द्रेण राजेन्द्र सभार्येण महात्मना। दुःखं प्राप्तं परं घोरमेतदिच्छामि वेदितुम्।।।।
en: Yudhishthira said I want to hear how is was, O chief among, kings, that the large minded Indra, with his queen met with grave difficulties.

sn: शल्य उवाच शृणु राजन् पुरावृत्तमितिहासं पुरातनम्। सभार्येण यथा प्राप्तं दुःखमिन्द्रेण भारत॥
en: Shalya said O king, listen to this old story as related in ancient history, of how Indra with his queen met with difficulties, O son of Bharata.

sn: त्वष्टा प्रजापति सीद् देवश्रेष्ठो महातपाः। स पुत्रं वै त्रिशिरसमिन्द्रद्रोहात् किलासृजत्॥
en: There was a great devotee named Tvashtri who was the lord of all beings and the chief among gods. Out of pure wrath towards Indra, he created a son with three heads.

sn: ऐन्द्रं स प्रार्थयत् स्थान् विश्वरूपो महाद्युतिः। तैस्त्रिभिर्वदनै।रैः सूर्येन्दुज्वलनोपमैः॥
en: The place, occupied by Indra, was desired by this mysterious personage, who was as it were the image of the universe and had three awful faces comparable to the sun, the moon and fire.

sn: वेदानेकेन सोऽधीते सुरामेकेन चापिबत्। एकेन च दिशः सर्वाः पिबन्निव निरीक्षते॥
en: With one mouth be read the Veda, with the second he drank wine and with the other he looked as if he would absorb the cardinal points.

sn: स तपस्वी मृदुर्दान्तो धर्मं तपसि चोद्यतः। तपस्तस्य महत् तीव्र सुदुश्चरमरिन्दम॥
en: He was a devotee, mild, having powers of self-control and engaged in religious worship and devotion. And O subduer of foes, the austerities practised by him could not be practised by others, for they were very hard and very difficult to be practised.

sn: तस्य दृष्ट्वा तपोवीर्यं सत्यं चामिततेजसः। विषादमगमच्छक इन्द्रोऽयं मा भवेदिति॥
en: Shakra was depressed in spirits, at seeing the strength in devotion and truthfulness of the one with unrivaled power, for fear lest he be the chief among gods.

sn: कथं सज्जेच्च भोगेषु न च तप्येन्महत् तपः। विवर्धमानस्त्रिशिराः सर्वं हि भुवनं ग्रसेत्॥ इति संचिन्त्य बहुधा बुद्धिमान् भरतर्षभ। आज्ञापयत् सोऽप्सरसस्त्वट्टपुत्रप्रलोभने।॥
en: O best among the race of Bharata, the skillful Indra through of many ways by which the one with three heads, whose strength was ever increasing and who threatened to absorb the entire universe, could be made to engage himself in the enjoyment of sensual pleasures and not in that hard devotion.

sn: यथा स सज्जेत् त्रिशिराः कामभोगेषु वै भृशम्। क्षिप्रं कुरुत गच्छध्वं प्रलोभयत् मा चिरम्॥
en: He ordered fairies (to engage themselves) in decoying the son of Tvashtri, so that the three-headed one might, for certain, engage himself in the enjoyment of sensual pleasure saying them

sn: शृङ्गारवेषाः सुश्रोण्यो हारैर्युक्ता मनोहरैः। हावभावसमायुक्ताः सर्वाः सौन्दर्यशोभिताः॥ प्रलोभयत् भद्रं वः शमयध्वं भयं मम। अस्वस्थं ह्यात्मनाऽऽत्मानं लक्ष्यामि वराङ्गनाः। भयं तन्मे महाघोरं क्षिप्रं नाशयताबलाः॥
en: Be quick, go and delay not in decoying him, (yourself) having beautiful hips, deck yourself in necklaces and beautiful pearls in such a way that his desires may be excited. I wish you well, decoy him with all the gestures of lust marked with every sort of fascination and thus allay my fear. O beautiful damsels, I feel restless in my heart. O ladies, destroy quickly this great fear of mine.

sn: अप्सरस ऊचुः तथा यत्नं करिष्यामः शक्र तस्य प्रलोभने। यथा नावाप्स्यसि भयं तस्माद् बलनिषूदन॥
en: The Nymphs said O Shakra, we shall try to decoy him so that, O you slayer of Bala, you may not experience any dread from him

sn: निर्दहन्निव चक्षुर्त्यां योऽसावास्ते तपोनिधिः। तं प्रलोभयितुं देव गच्छामः सहिता वयम्॥ यतिष्यामो वशे कर्तुं व्यपनेतुं च ते भयम्।
en: The great devotee who now sits, as if scorching with his eyes, O lord and whom we are going together to decoy. We shall try to get him under our control and thus destroy your fears.

sn: शल्य उवाच इन्द्रेण तास्त्वनुज्ञाता जग्मुस्त्रिशिरसोऽन्तिकम्। तत्र ता विविधैर्भावैलॊभयन्त्यो वराङ्गनाः॥
en: Shalya said Being commanded by Indra they went to the three-headed one and the lovely damsels tempted him there with various gestures of lust.

sn: नित्यं संदर्शयामासुस्तथैवाङ्गेषु सौष्ठवम्। नाभ्यगच्छत् प्रहर्षं ताः स पश्यन् सुमहातपाः॥
en: They displayed too the beauties of their person but the great devotee, though looking at them, did not at all enjoy the satisfaction (of looking at them).

sn: इन्द्रियाणि वशे कृत्वा पूर्वसागरसंनिभः। तास्तु यत्नं परं कृत्वा पुनः शक्रमुपस्थिताः॥
en: Having brought his senses under his control, he was in point of gravity as the full ocean. The damsels too, having tried their best, came back of Shakra.

sn: कृताञ्जलिपुटाः सर्वा देवराजमथाब्रुवन्। न स शक्यः सुदुर्धर्षो धैर्याच्चालयितुं प्रभो॥
en: Then, with the palms their hands elapsed they all said to the chief among the gods. O Lord, he, whom it is very difficult to subdue, cannot be influenced away from his purpose.

sn: यत् ते कार्यं महाभाग क्रियतां तदनन्तरम्। सम्पूज्याप्सरसः शक्रो विसृज्य च महामतिः॥
en: O you with great parts, do what you should after this. The great-minded Shakra, having greeted the nymphs with due honours, sent them away

sn: चिन्तयामास तस्यैव वधोपायं युधिष्ठिर। स तूष्र्णी चिन्तयन् वीरो देवराजः प्रतापवान्।॥ विनिश्चितमतिर्धीमान् वधे त्रिशिरसोऽभवत्।
en: O Yudhishthira, he thought of some means to slay him. And the chief among the gods who was valiant, famous as a gifted being of unfailing judgment and intelligent, fixed on a plan for slaying the three-headed one.

sn: वज्रमस्य क्षिपाम्यद्य स क्षिप्रं न भविष्यति॥ शत्रुः प्रवृद्धो नोपेक्ष्यो दुर्बलोऽपि बलीयसा।
en: (Thought he) I shall this soon cease to exist. A foe who has already grown up must not be made light of by even the powerful, a weak foe though he might be.

sn: शास्त्रबुद्धया विनिश्चित्य कृत्वा बुद्धिं वधे दृढाम्॥ अथ वैश्वानरनिभं घोररूपं भयावहम्। मुमोच वज्रं संक्रुद्धः शक्रस्त्रिशिरसं प्रति॥ स पपात हतस्तेन वज्रेण दृढमाहतः। पर्वतस्येव शिखरं प्रणुन्नं मेदिनीतले॥
en: Deciding on this course of action laid down in the books, he firmly resolved on slaying him. Shakra, wrathful, flung his fearful and dress-inspiring thunderbolt, which could be compared to the fire, on the head of the three-headed one. Being severely struck by the thunderbolt he fell down to the earth, like the loosened summit of a mountain.

sn: तं तु वज्रहतं दृष्ट्वा शयानमचलोपमम्। न शर्म लेभे देवेन्द्रो दीपितस्तस्य तेजसा॥
en: Seeing him struck by the thunderbolt and lying like a mountain, the chief among the gods got no peace of mind, owing to his luster which still retained its effulgence.

sn: हतोऽपि दीप्ततेजाः स जीवन्निव हि दृश्यते। घातितस्य शिरांस्याजौ जीवन्तीवाद्धतानि वै॥
en: Though killed, his luster was effulgent and he seemed as if he were alive. It was strange that the heads of the slain one looked as if alive.

sn: ततोऽतिभीतगात्रस्तु शक्र आस्ते विचारयन्। अथाजगाम परशुं स्कन्धेनादाय वर्धकिः॥
en: For that reason fearful to behold. Shakra remained kept in thought. Then there came a wood cutter with an axe on his shoulder to that forest.

sn: तदरण्यं महाराज यत्रास्तेऽसौ निपातितः। स भीतस्तत्र तक्षाणं घटमानं शचीपतिः॥ अपश्यदब्रवीच्चैनं सत्वरं पाकशासनः। क्षिप्रं छिन्धि शिरांस्यस्य कुरुष्व वचनं मम॥
en: O great king, where he was lying felled down. The Lord of Sachi, who still had fears, saw that wood cutter coming there by chance and the subduer of Paka soon said to him "quickly cut down the heads of this being; do what I tell you."

sn: तक्षोवाच महास्कन्धो भृशं ह्येष परशुर्न भविष्यति। कर्तुं चाहं न शक्ष्यामि कर्म सद्भिर्विगर्हितम्॥
en: The wood cutter said This man has large shoulders; the axe cannot cut down the heads) nor shall I be able to do the deed which is regarded to be wrong by honest people.

sn: इन्द्र उवाच मा भेस्त्वं शीघ्रमेतद् वै कुरुष्व वचनं मम। मत्प्रसादाद्धि ते शस्त्रं वज्रकल्पं भविष्यति॥
en: Shakra said You need not have any fears, do quickly what I tell you; through my favour shall your weapon be equal to the thunderbolt.

sn: तक्षोवाच कं भवन्तमहं विद्यां घोरकर्माणमद्य वै। एतदिच्छाम्यहं श्रोतुं तत्त्वेन कथयस्व मे॥
en: The wood cutter said I must know who you are and I want to hear why you have done this cruel deed today. Tell me the truth.

sn: इन्द्र उवाच अहमिन्द्रो देवराजस्तक्षन् विदितमस्तु ते। कुरुष्वैतदद् यथोक्तं मे तक्षन् माऽत्र विचारय॥
en: Indra said I am Indra, the chief among the gods, let it be known to you O wood cutter. Do as I have told you. O wood cutter, do not ponder.

sn: तक्षोवाच क्रूरेण नापत्रपसे कथं शक्रेह कर्मणा। ऋषिपुत्रमिमं हत्वा ब्रह्महत्याभयं न ते॥
en: The wood cutter said O Shakra, how is it that you are not ashamed at this cruel deed? Having killed this son of a Rishi, have you no fear of the sin of killing a Brahmana?

sn: शक्र उवाच पश्चाद् धर्मं चरिष्यामि पावनार्थं सुदुश्चरम्। शत्रुरेष महावीर्यो वज्रेण निहतो मया।॥
en: Shakra said For the purification of my soul I shall thereafter precise some severe penance. He was my enemy, possessed of great strength and has been killed by my thunderbolt.

sn: अद्यापि चाहमुद्विग्नस्तक्षन्नस्माद् बिभेमि वै। क्षिप्रं छिन्धि शिरांसि त्वं करिष्येऽनुग्रहं तव॥
en: To this day, O wood cutter, am I anxious and dread this. Quickly cut off his heads. I shall bestow a favour on you.

sn: शिरः पशोस्ते दास्यस्ति भागं यज्ञेषु मानवाः। एष तेऽनुग्रहस्तक्षन् क्षिप्रं कुरु मम प्रियम्॥
en: In sacrificial rites, men will give the heads of the beasts. This is the favour I great you. Quickly do what I desire.

sn: शल्य उवाच एतच्छ्रुत्वा तु तक्षा स महेन्द्रवचनात् तदा। शिरांस्यथ त्रिशिरसः कुठारेणाच्छिनत् तदा॥
en: Shalya said Having heard this, the wood cutter, after the speech of Indra, cut down the heads of the three-headed one with his axe.

sn: निकृत्तेषु ततस्तेषु निष्क्रामन्नण्डजास्त्वथा कपिञ्जलास्तित्तिराश्च कलविङ्काश्च सर्वशः।॥
en: The heads, being cut off, came out from them a good many birds of the Kapinjala, (doves) Titara (sparrows) and Kalavinka (parrots) species.

sn: येन वेदानधीते स्म पिबते सोममेव च। तस्माद् वक्त्राद् विनिश्चेरुः क्षिप्रं तस्य कपिञ्जलाः॥४०
en: From the mouth by which he used to read the Veda and drink Soma juice, came forth quickly birds of the Kapinjala species,

sn: येन सर्वा दिशो राजन् पिबन्निव निरीक्षते। तस्माद् वक्त्राद् विनिश्चेरुस्तित्तिरास्तस्य पाण्डव॥
en: From the one by which, o king, he looked as if he would absorb (the cardinal points) came forth, O son of Pandu, birds of the Titara species.

sn: यत् सुरापं तस्यासीद् वक्त्रं त्रिशिरसस्तदा। कलविङ्काः समुत्पेतुः श्येनाश्च भरतर्षभ।॥
en: And from the mouth of the three-headed one which used to drink wine, came out birds of the Kalavinka species and birds of prey, O best among the race of Bharata.

sn: ततस्तेषु निकृत्तेषु विज्वरो मघवानथ। जगाम त्रिदिवं हृष्टस्तक्षऽपि स्वगृहान् ययौ॥
en: They having come out, Indra became tranquilized and went to heaven and the wood cutter too, well pleased, went home.

sn: मेने कृतार्थमात्मानं हत्वा शत्रु सुरारिहा। त्वष्टा प्रजापतिः श्रुत्वा शक्रेणाथं हतं सुतम्॥ क्रोधसंरक्तनयन इदं वचनमब्रवीत्।
en: This chief among the gods, having killed his enemy, thought himself gratified. Tvashtri, the lord of all beings, having heard of the slaying of his son by Shakra, said these words with eyes red with wrath.

sn: त्वष्टोवाच तष्यमानं तपो नित्यं क्षान्तं दान्तं जितेन्द्रियम्। विनाऽपराधेन यतः पुत्रं हिंसितवान् मम॥
en: Tvashtri said due to my My son who was ever devoted to devotion, of a forgiving nature, endowed with selfcontrol and who had brought his passions under his control, has been killed by you without any fault.

sn: तस्माच्छकविनाशाय वृत्रमुत्पादयाम्यहम्। लोकाः पश्यन्तु मे वीर्यं तपसश्च बलं महत्॥
en: For this reason shall I create Vritra with a view to destroy Shakra. Let the worlds see my influence and power as also the great strength devotion.

sn: स च पश्यतु देवेन्द्रो दुरात्मा पापचेतनः। उपस्पृश्य ततः क्रुद्धस्तपस्वी सुमहायशाः॥
en: Let the chief of the gods also see it who is vile and of a vicious nature. Then the wrathful devotee of very great fame having performed his ablutions.

sn: अग्नौ हुत्वा समुत्पाद्य घोरं वृत्रमुवाच ह। इन्द्रशत्रो विवर्धस्व प्रभावात् तपसो मम॥
en: And having made his offerings to fire and having created the hero Vritra said-"O you foe of Indra, grow up through the strength due to my devotions."

sn: सोऽवर्धत दिवं स्तब्वा सूर्यवैश्वानरोपमः। किं करोमीति चोवाच कालसूर्य इवोदितः॥
en: He grew up and the height of his figure reached beyond the sky and could be compared with the sun or fire. Like the sun that rises at the time of the annihilation of the universe, he said-"What shall I do?"

sn: शक्रं जहीति चाप्युक्तो जगाम त्रिदिवं ततः। ततो युद्धं समभवद् वृत्रवासवयोर्महत्॥
en: And the powerful one, being told to slay Shakara, went to the third heaven. And then there was a fierce battle between Vritra and Vasava.

sn: संक्रुद्धयोर्महाघोरं प्रसक्तं कुरुसत्तम। ततो जग्राह देवेन्द्रं वृत्रो वीरः शतक्रतुम्॥
en: O you the best among the race of Kuru! There was a hot contest between the two, both of whom were fired with wrath and then the hero Vritra caught hold of the chief among the gods who had performed a hundred sacrifices.

sn: अपावृत्याक्षिपद् वक्त्रे शक्रं कोपसमन्वितः। ग्रस्ते वृत्रेण शक्रे तु सम्भ्रान्तास्त्रिदिवेश्वराः॥
en: And opening his mouth the wrathful one threw him into his mouth. And Shakra being swallowed up by Vritra, the lords of the third heaven became very much terrified.

sn: असृजस्ते महासत्त्वा जृम्भिकां वृत्रनाशिनीम्। विजृम्भमाणस्य ततो वृत्रस्यास्यादपावृतात्॥ स्वान्यङ्गान्यभिसंक्षिप्य निष्क्रान्तो बलनाशनः। ततः प्रभृति लोकस्य जृम्भिका प्राणसंश्रिता॥
en: They highly powerful then created the Yawn which was to destroy Vritra and then the slayer of Bala contracted his limbs and came out of the open mouth of the yawning Vritra. Since that day has the yawn remained in the breath of men.

sn: जहषुश्च सुराः सर्वे शक्रं दृष्ट्वा विनिःसृतम्। ततः प्रववृते युद्धं वृत्रवासवयोः पुनः॥
en: And seeing Shakra come out the gods all became joyful and then Vritra and Vasava again engaged themselves is fight.

sn: संरब्धयोस्तदा घोरं सुचिरं भरतर्षभ। यदा व्यवर्धत रणे वृत्रो बलसमन्वितः॥ त्वष्टस्तेजोबलाविद्धस्तदा शक्रो न्यवर्तत। निवृत्ते च तदा देवा विषादमगमन् परम्॥
en: 0 best among the race of Bharata, the fierce contest between the two, fired with ire, lasted for a long time, when in battle Vritra, possessed of power, got the victory through the strength due to the inner spirit of Tvashtri. Shakra turned his back and he turning his back the gods were very much depressed.

sn: समेत्य सह शक्रेण त्वष्टस्तेजोविमोहिताः। अमन्त्रयन्त ते सर्वे मुनिभिः सह भारत॥
en: Being pierced with the spirit of Tvashtri they untied with Shakra and all held a consultation with the Rishis, O son of Bharata.

sn: किं कार्यमिति वै राजन् विचिन्त्य भयमोहिताः। जग्मुः सर्वे महात्मानं मनोभिर्विष्णुमव्ययम्। उपविष्टा मन्दराग्नेये सर्वे वृत्रवधेप्सवः॥
en: Filled with dread they thought, O king, on what could best be done. Seated at the summit of Mandara, they all desirous of the destruction of Vritra, went in imagination of Vishnu, who was never to be destroyed.

sn: इन्द्र उवाच सर्वं व्याप्तमिदं देवा वृत्रेण जगदव्ययम्। न ह्यस्य सदृशं किंचित् प्रतिघाताय यद् भवेत्॥
en: Shakra said The whole of this indestructible universe has been pervaded, O gods, by Vritra. There is nothing equal to opposing him.

sn: समर्थो ह्यभवं पूर्वमसमर्थोऽस्मि साम्प्रतम्। कथं नु कार्यं भद्रं वो दुर्धर्षः स हि मे मतः॥
en: I was before this capable of (doing this) but at present I am incapable. I wish you well. What can I do? I think he is hard to vanquish.

sn: तेजस्वी च महात्मा च युद्धे चामितविक्रमः। ग्रसेत् त्रिभुवन् सर्वं सदेवासुरमानुषम्॥
en: He is spirited large minded and of unparalleled prowess in battle and he will absorb all the three worlds with all their gods, Asuras and men.

sn: तस्माद् विनिश्चयमिमं शृणुध्वं त्रिदिवौकसः। विष्णोः क्षयमुपागम्य समेत्य च महात्मना। तेन सम्मन्त्र्य वेत्स्यामो वधोपायं दुरात्मनः॥
en: Therefore O you denizens of the heaven, this is certain that by going to the abode of Vishnu and joining with that large-minded one and consulting with him we shall know the means of slaying the vicious one.

sn: शल्य उवाच एवमुक्ते मघवता देवाः सर्षिगणास्तदा। शरण्यं शरणं देवं जग्मुर्विष्णुं महाबलम्॥
en: Shalya said The gods being thus spoken to by Maghavan the group of Rishis placed themselves under the protection of the god Vishnu of great influence and competent to be a protector.

sn: ऊचुश्च सर्वे देवेशं विष्णुं वृत्रभयार्दिताः। त्रयो लोकास्त्वया क्रान्तास्त्रिभिर्विक्रमणैः पुरा॥
en: And they, distressed with the fear of Vritra, spoke thus to Vishnu the lord of all gods-In days of yore did you cover the three worlds with three steps.

sn: अमृतं चाहृतं विष्णो दैत्याच निहता रणे। बलिं बद्ध्वा महादैत्यं शक्रो देवाधिपः कृतः॥
en: And O Vishnu, robbed it of nectar and killed in battle all the Daityas and after slaying Vali the great Daityas appointed Shakra, as the lord of the gods.

sn: त्वं प्रभुः सर्वदेवानां त्वया सर्वमिदं ततम्। त्वं हि देवो महादेव सर्वलोकनमस्कृतः॥
en: You are the Supreme Lord of all the gods and the whole (of this world) is pervaded by you; you, O Lord, are the supreme Lord revered by all the worlds.

sn: गतिर्भव त्वं देवानां सेन्द्राणाममरोत्तम। जगद् व्याप्तमिदं सर्वं वृत्रेणासुरसूदन॥
en: O you best among the immortals, be the means of salvation of the gods including Indra. O you slayer of Asuras, the entire world is pervaded by Vritra.

sn: विष्णुरुवाच अवश्यं करणीयं मे भवतां हितमुत्तमम्। तस्मादुपायं वक्ष्यामि यथाऽसौ न भविष्यति॥
en: Vishnu said Doing your good is my imperative duty; therefore am I speaking of the means by which he shall cease to exist.

sn: गच्छध्वं सर्षिगन्धर्वा यत्रासौ विश्वरूपधृक्। साम तस्य प्रयुञ्जध्वं तत एनं विजेष्यथ॥
en: In company with the Rishis and the Gandharvas you go to the place where that holder of the universal from is staying; make use of conciliatory policy towards him; then shall you win victory over him.

sn: भविष्यति जयो देवाः शक्रस्य मम तेजसा। अदृश्यश्च प्रवेक्ष्यामि वज्रे ह्यस्यायुधोत्तमे॥
en: O gods, through my influence, victory will be on the side of Shakra. Being invisible shall I enter the thunder bolt-that excellent weapons of his.

sn: गच्छध्वमृषिभिः सार्धं गन्धर्वैश्च सुरोत्तमाः। वृत्रस्य सह शक्रेण सन्धिं कुरुत मा चिरम्॥
en: O you best among the gods, go in company with the Rishis and the Gandharvas. Effect a truce without delay between Shakra and Vritra.

sn: शल्य उवाच एवमुक्ते तु देवेन ऋषयस्त्रिदशास्तथा। ययुः समेत्य सहिताः शक्रं कृत्वा पुरःसरम्॥
en: Shalya said The Rishis and the dwellers, of the third heaven being thus spoken to by that god, went together, with Shakra at their head.

sn: समीपमेत्य च यदा सर्व एव महौजसः। तं तेजसा प्रज्वलितं प्रतपन्तं दिशो दश॥
en: Then all those mighty ones came near him, through whose influence the ten cardinal points were on fire and being scorched.

sn: ग्रसन्तमिव लोकांस्त्रीन् सूर्याचन्द्रमसौ यथा। ददृशुस्ते ततो वृत्रं शक्रेण सह देवताः॥
en: Those gods, with Indra, then saw Vritra who seemed as if swallowing the three worlds and looking as the sun or the moon.

sn: ऋषयोऽथ ततोऽभ्येत्य वृत्रमूचुः प्रियं वचः। व्याप्तं जगदिदं सर्वं तेजसा तव दुर्जय॥
en: Then the Rishis came there and said these conciliatory words of Vritra. O you hard to conquer, this world is pervaded by your energy.

sn: अ च शक्नोषि निर्जेतुं वासवं बलिनां वर। युध्यतोश्चापि वां कालो व्यतीतः सुमहानिह॥
en: O you best of powerful beings, you will not be able to conquer Vasava and a very long period has elapsed since you commenced fighting.

sn: पीड्यन्ते च प्रजाः सर्वाः सदेवासुरमानुषाः। सख्यं भवतु ते वृत्र शक्रेण सह नित्यदा॥
en: All beings including the gods, the Asuras and the human beings, are enduring misery. Let there always exit, O Vritra, friendship between you and Shakra.

sn: अवाप्स्यसि सुखं त्वं च शक्रलोकांश्च शाश्वतान्। ऋषिवाक्यं निशम्याथ वृत्रः स तु महाबलः॥
en: You will gain happiness and ever dwell in the regions of Shakra. Hearing these words of the Rishis, Vritra of great strength.

sn: उवाच तानृषीन् सर्वान् प्रणम्य शिरसाऽसुरः। सर्वे यूयं महाभागा गन्धर्वाश्चैव सर्वशः॥ यद् बूथ तच्छतं सर्वं ममापि शृणुतानघाः। संधिः कथं वै भविता मम शक्रस्य चोभयोः। तेजसोहि द्वयोर्देवाः सख्यं वै भविता कथम्॥
en: The Asura bowed unto all those Rishis with his head and said to them-O you endowed with good qualities and you Gandharvas, what you all have said, I have listened to. O you stainless beings, hear now what I say. How can there be peace between us two-myself and Shakra? How can there be friendship between two gods who are both powerful?

sn: ऋषय ऊचुः सकृत् सतां संगतं लिप्सितव्यं ततः परं भविता भव्यमेव। नातिकामेत् सत्पुरुषेण संगतं तस्मात् सतां संगत् लिप्सितव्यम्॥
en: The Rishis said The company of virtuous ones is desirable (even for a time); thereafter what is fated will come to pass. The opportunity of friendship with virtuous men should not be lost; therefore is the company of virtuous men desirable.

sn: दृढं सतां संगतं चापि नित्यं ब्रूयाच्चा) ह्यर्थकृच्छ्रेषु धीरः। महार्थवत् सत्पुरुषेण संगतं तस्मात् सन्तं न जिघांसेत धीरः॥
en: Wise men ever speak of firm friendship with virtuous men as wealth is times of pecuniary difficulties. The company of virtuous men is vast wealth indeed; therefore wise men should not injure virtuous ones.

sn: इन्द्रः सतां सम्मतश्च निवासश्च महात्मनाम्। सत्यवादी ह्यनिन्द्यश्च धर्मवित् सूक्ष्मनिश्चयः॥
en: Indra is honoured by virtuous men and the refuse of the large-minded. He is also truth speaking, blameless, understands virtue and has refined judgment.

sn: तेन ते सह शक्रेण संधिर्भवतु नित्यदा। एवं विश्वासमागच्छ मा तेऽभूद् बुद्धिरन्यथा।॥
en: Let there be peace, to eternity, with Indra; come to entertain faith in him; let not your opinion be otherwise.

sn: शल्य उवाच महर्षिवचनं श्रुत्वा तानुवाच महाद्युतिः। अवश्यं भगवन्तो मे माननीयास्तपस्विनः॥
en: Shalya said The being with great luster, having heard the speech of the great Rishis, said to them! O devotees, O lord, you are, of course, to be honoured by me.

sn: ब्रवीमि यदहं देवास्तत् सर्वं क्रियते यदि। ततः सर्वं करिष्यामि यदूचुर्मी द्विजर्षभाः॥
en: O gods, if you do all that I am going to say then shall I do all that you have said to me, O foremost among the twice born.

sn: न शुष्केण न चाद्रेण नाश्मना न च दारुणा। न शस्त्रेण न चास्त्रेण न दिवा न तथा निशि॥
en: Not by dry thing nor be a wet one, not by stone, nor by wood, nor by a weapon fit for use from a distance, nor by one fit for hand to hand fight, not during the day time nor during the night,

sn: वध्यो भवेयं विप्रेन्द्राः शक्रस्य सह दैवतैः। एवं मे रोचते सन्धिः शक्रेण सह नित्यदा।॥
en: Shall I be capable of being slain, O chief among the Brahmanas, by Shakra, assisted by the gods. If you ordain this then shall there ever be peace with Shakra.

sn: बाढमित्येव ऋषयस्तमूचुर्भरतर्षभ। एवंवृत्ते तु संधाने वृत्रः प्रमुदितोऽभवत्॥
en: O best among the race of Bharata the Rishis said-"very well" and Vritra too became pleased with having peace under these conditions.

sn: युक्तः सदाभवच्चापि शक्रो हर्षसमन्वितः। वृत्रस्य वधसंयुक्तानुपायानन्वचिन्तयत्॥
en: Shakra too became delighted and became constantly engaged in the thought of finding out some means of killing Vritra.

sn: छिद्रान्वेषी समुद्विग्नः सदा वसति देवराट्। स कदाचित् समुद्रान्ते समपश्यन्महासुरम्॥
en: The chief among the gods always remained anxious land on the look out for some loop-hole. He one day saw the great Asura at the sea coast.

sn: संध्याकालं उपावृत्ते मुहुर्ते चातिदारुणे। ततः संचिन्त्य भगवान् वरदानं महात्मनः॥
en: It was evening and the moment was aweinspiring and the god thus thought of the boons granted by the large minded one (Vishnu).

sn: संध्येयं वर्तते रौद्रा ना रात्रिर्दिवसं न च। वृत्रश्चावश्यवध्योऽयं मम सर्वहरो रिपुः॥
en: This is evening, it is not in the sun; it is neither the night nor the day. And Vritra, the enemy who has robbed me of all must be slain.

sn: यदि वृत्रं न हम्यद्य वञ्चयित्वा महासुरम्। महाबलं महाकायं न मे श्रेयो भविष्यति॥
en: If I do not this day slay the great Asura, Vritra of great strength and of a huge body by an artifice, it will not be well with me.

sn: एवं संचिन्तयन्नेव शक्रो विष्णुमनुस्मरन्। अथ फेनं तदाऽपश्यत् समुद्रे पर्वतोपमम्॥
en: Thus thinking Shakra invoked Vishnu and then saw coming out of the sea, foam high as a mountain.

sn: नायं शुष्को न चाद्रोऽयं न च शस्त्रमिदं तथा। एनं क्षेप्स्यामि वृत्रस्य क्षणादेव नशिष्यति॥
en: This is not wet nor dry nor is this a weapon. I shall fling this which will destroy Vritra is moment.

sn: सवज्रमथ फेनं तं क्षिप्रं वृत्रे निसृष्टवान्। प्रविश्य फेन तं विष्णुरथ वृत्रं व्यनाशयत्॥
en: Quickly did he fling the foam with the thunderbolt at Vritra and Vishnu having entered the foam destroyed Vritra.

sn: निहते तु ततो वृत्रे दिशो वितिमिराऽभवन्। प्रववौ च शिवो वायुः प्रजाश्च जहषुस्तथा॥
en: And Vritra being slain, the cardinal points became divested of darkness and a pleasant wind blew and the beings of the earth rejoiced.

sn: ततो देवाः सगन्धर्वा यक्षरक्षोमहोरगाः। ऋषयश्च महेन्द्रं तमस्तुवन् विविधैः स्तवैः॥
en: And then the gods along with the Gandharvas, Yakshas, Rakshasas and Pannagas and the Rishis propitiated the great Indra with diverse hymns.

sn: नमस्कृतः सर्वभूतैः सर्वभूता सान्त्वयत्। हत्वा शत्रु प्रहृष्टात्मा वासवः सह दैवतैः॥
en: Being bowed down to by all beings, he encouraged all the beings in his turn. Slaying the enemy, the mind of Vasava became delighted with the gods.

sn: विष्णुं त्रिभुवनश्रेष्ठं पूजयामास धर्मवित्। ततो हते महावीर्ये वृत्रे देवभयंकरे॥
en: The one knowing virtue worshipped the foremost in the three worlds, Vishnu, after the great hero and fierce god Vritra was slain.

sn: अनृतेनाभिभूतोऽभूच्छक्रः परमदुर्मनाः। त्रैशीर्षयाभिभूतश्च स पूर्वं ब्रह्महत्यया॥
en: Now, Shakra became overpowered by false-hood and exceedingly depressed in spirits and also overpowered by the sin of slaying the Brahmana (the three headed one).

sn: सोऽन्तमाश्रित्य लोकानां नष्टसंज्ञो विचेतनः। न प्राज्ञायत देवेन्द्रस्त्वभिभूतः स्वकल्मषैः॥
en: Staying at the end of the worlds, he became deprived of his senses and consciousness and the chief of the gods overpowered with the weight of his own sins could not be recognised.

sn: प्रतिच्छन्नोऽवसच्चाप्सु चेष्टमान इवोरगः। ततः प्रनष्टे देवेन्द्रे ब्रह्महत्याभयादिते॥
en: He remained as if in disguise under the water restless as a serpent. And then the lord of the gods, struck with the fear of the sin of killing a Brahmana, was destroyed, so to say.

sn: भूमिः प्रध्वस्तसंकाशा निर्वृक्षा शुष्ककानना। विच्छिन्नस्रोतसो नद्यः सरांस्यनुदकानि च।॥
en: The earth became desolate and went to ruins and became treeless and the forests became dry. And the currents of the rivers became stopped and the lakes lost all their water.

sn: संक्षोभश्चापि सत्त्वानामनावृष्टिकृतोऽभवत्। देवाश्चापि भृशं त्रस्तास्तथा सर्वे महर्षयः॥
en: And there came distress among the beings of the earth, owing to death of rain and the gods and the great Rishis remained struck with intense fear.

sn: अराजकं जगत् सर्वमभिभूतमुपद्रवैः। ततो भीताऽभवन् देवाः को नो राजा भरेदिति॥
en: And the entire world oppressed with anarchy became overpowered with all sorts of disasters and the gods became frightened for no hody would be their king.

sn: दिवि देवर्षयश्चापि देवराजविनाकृताः। न स्म कश्चन देवानां राज्ये वै कुरुते मतिम्॥
en: And the divine saints in heaven also being deprived of the protection of the king of the gods became fearful. No body was inclined to be the king of the gods.

description: The fear of the queen of Indra
sn: शल्य उवाच ऋषयोऽथाब्रुवन् सर्वे देवाश्च त्रिदिवेश्वराः। अयं वै नहुष: श्रीमान् देवराज्येऽभिषिच्यताम्॥
en: Shalya said Then did all the gods and Yakshas with the Kinnaras say 'Anoint this handsome Nahusha in the kingship of the gods.'

description: The fear of the queen of Indra
sn: तेजस्वी च यशस्वी च धार्मिकश्चैव नित्यदा। ते गत्वा त्वब्रुवन् सर्वे राजा नो भव पार्थिव॥
en: He is powerful, enjoys fame and is ever virtuous. Going to him they said-'O ruler of the earth be our king.'

description: The fear of the queen of Indra
sn: स तानुवाच नहुषो देवानृषिगणंस्तथा। पितृभिः सहितान् राजन् परीप्सन हितमात्मनः॥
en: Thus, O king, did Nahusha, who wished their welfare, address the gods and the Rishis who were accompanied by our ancestors.

description: The fear of the queen of Indra
sn: दुर्बलोऽहं न मे शक्तिर्भवतां परिपालने। बलवाञ्जायते राजा बलं शक्रे हि नित्यदा॥
en: I am weak; it is not in my power to protect you. The powerful should make kings, (and) power ever graced Shakra.

description: The fear of the queen of Indra
sn: तमब्रुवन् पुनः सर्वे देवा ऋषिपुरोगमाः। अस्माकं तपसा युक्तः पाहि राज्यं त्रिविष्टपे॥
en: All the gods and the foremost among the Rishis said to him, Endued with the virtue of devotion, protect our kingdom in heaven.

description: The fear of the queen of Indra
sn: परस्परभयं घोरमस्माकं हि न संशयः। अभिषिच्यस्व राजेन्द्र भव राजा त्रिविष्टपे॥
en: All of us doubtless have grave fears; be anointed our king, foremost among monarchs, be the king of heaven.

description: The fear of the queen of Indra
sn: देवदानवयक्षाणामृषीणां रक्षसां तथा। पितृगन्धर्वभूतानां चक्षुर्विषयवर्तिनाम्॥ तेज आदास्यसे पश्यन् बलवांश्च भविष्यसि। धर्म पुरस्कृत्य सदा सर्वलोकाधिपो भव॥
en: You will absorb the power, of the gods, the Danavas, the Yakshas. Rishis the Rakshasas, the Pitris, the Gandharvas and all other beings within the range of your sight as soon as you see them. Setting virtue always above all other considerations be the lord of all worlds.

description: The fear of the queen of Indra
sn: ब्रह्मर्षीश्चापि देवांश्च गोपायस्व त्रिविष्टपे। अभिषिक्तः स राजेन्द्र ततो राजा त्रिविष्टपे॥
en: Protect also the Brahmarshis and the gods in heaven. And that chief among the kings being anointed the king in heaven.

description: The fear of the queen of Indra
sn: धर्मं पुरस्कृत्य तदा सर्वलोकाधिपोऽभवत्। सुदुर्लभं वरं लब्ध्वा प्राप्य राज्यं त्रिविष्टपे॥ धर्मात्मा सततं भूत्वा कामात्मा समपद्यत।
en: And placing virtue above everything else became the protector of the worlds. Being granted a rare boon and obtaining the kingdom in heaven, he gave himself up to gratifying every wish of his, though before this he had ever been a virtuous being.

description: The fear of the queen of Indra
sn: देवोद्यानेषु सर्वेषु नन्दनोपवनेषु च॥ कैलासे हिमवत्पृष्ठे मन्दरे श्वेतपर्वते। सह्ये महेन्द्र मलये समुद्रेषु सरित्सु च॥ अप्सरोभिः परिवृतो देवकन्यासमावृतः। नहुषो देवराजोऽथ क्रीडन् बहुविधं तदा॥ शृण्वन् दिव्या बहुविधाः कथाः श्रुतिमनोहराः। वादित्राणि च सर्वाणि गीतं च मधुरस्वनम्॥
en: In all the gardens of the gods and in the pleasure gardens, on the Kailasa and on the brow of the Himavat, on the Mandara and on the white mountains, on the Shalya, on the Mahendra and on the Malaya in the seas and in the lakes surrounded by fairies and nymphs. Nahusha, the king of the gods, spent his time in many sorts of sports and hearing many sorts of। stories relating to the gods, which were sweet to listen to. (He spent his time also) with all sorts of musical instruments and sweet sounding songs.

description: The fear of the queen of Indra
sn: विश्वावसुर्नारदश्च गन्धर्वाप्सरसां गणाः। ऋतवः षट् च देवेन्द्रं मूर्तिमन्त उपस्थिताः॥
en: Vishvavasu, Narada, Gandharvas and celestial nymphs and the six personified, attended on him. seasons

description: The fear of the queen of Indra
sn: मारुतः सुरभिर्वाति मनोज्ञः सुखशीतलः। एवं च क्रीडतस्तस्य नहुषस्य दुरात्मनः॥ सम्प्राप्ता दर्शनं देवी शक्रस्य महिषी प्रिया।
en: Breezes, fragrant, cooling and charming too blew on him. The goddess, the dearly beloved Queen of Shakra, caught the gaze of the high-minded Nahusha, given thus to sporting.

description: The fear of the queen of Indra
sn: स तां संदृश्य दुष्टात्मा प्राह सर्वान् सभासदः॥ इन्द्रस्य महिषी देवी कस्मान्मां नोपतिष्ठति। अहमिन्द्रोऽस्मि देवानां लोकानां च तथेश्वरः॥ आगच्छतु शची मह्यं क्षिप्रमद्य निवेशनम्।
en: Seeing her the evil minded one thus addressed his courtiers-"Why does not the goddess, the queen of Indra, attend on me. As the lord of the gods and the worlds, I am Indra. Let Sachi come to my palace this day at once."

description: The fear of the queen of Indra
sn: तच्छ्रुत्वा दुर्मना देवी बृहस्पतिमुवाच ह॥ रक्ष मां नहुषाद् ब्रह्मंस्त्वामस्मि शरणं गता। सर्वलक्षणसम्पन्नां ब्रह्मंस्त्वं मां प्रभाषसे॥ देवराजस्य दयितामत्यन्तं सुखभागिनीम्। अवैधव्येन युक्तां चाप्येकपत्नी पतिव्रताम्॥
en: Hearing this speech of the evil minded one the goodness said to Brihaspati-'Protect me from Nahusha O Brahmana. I throw myself entirely under your protection. O Brahmana, do you speak of me as having all the auspicious marks on my person, as the consort of the king of the gods and so exceedingly prosperous. Before this have you spoken of me as being (ever) without widowhood, an only wife and strictly chaste.

description: The fear of the queen of Indra
sn: उक्तवानसि मां पूर्वमृतां तां कुरु वै गिरम्। नोक्तपूर्वं च भगवन् वृथा ते किंचिदीश्वर॥ तस्मादेतद् भवेत् सत्यं त्वयोक्तं द्विजसत्तम।
en: O god, let this speech of your be made true. O lord, what you have said has never before proved false, therefore, O you foremost among the twice-born, let this said by you be true.

description: The fear of the queen of Indra
sn: बृहस्पतिरथोवाच शक्राणी भयमोहिताम्॥ यदुक्ताऽसि मया देवि सत्यं ध्रुवम्। तद् भविता द्रक्ष्यसे देवराजानमिन्द्रं शीघ्रमिहागतम्॥ न भेतव्यं च नहुषात् सत्यमेतद् ब्रवीमि ते। समानयिष्ये शक्रेण न चिराद् भवतीमहम्॥
en: Then did Brihaspati address the panicstricken queen of Indra-"What has been said by me, O goddess, will most certainly prove true. You will soon see the king of the gods, Indra, come here. Nahusha need not be feared by you. I speak this truly. I shall without delay bring Indra near you.

description: The fear of the queen of Indra
sn: अथ शुश्राव नहुषः शक्राणी शरणं गताम्। बृहस्पतेरङ्गिरसचक्रोध स नृपस्तदा॥
en: Nahusha heard that the queen of Indra had placed herself under the protection of Brihaspati the son of Angirasa and the king became very angry.

sn: शल्य उवाच क्रुद्धं तु नहुषं दृष्ट्वा देवा ऋषिपुरोगमाः। अब्रुवन् देवराजानां नहुषं घोरदर्शनम्॥
en: Shalya said The gods and the foremost among the Rishis seeing Nahusha enraged said to the (now) terrible looking king of the gods.

sn: देवराज जहि क्रोधं त्वयि क्रुद्धे जगद् विभो। त्रस्तं सासुरगन्धर्वं सकिन्नरमहोरगम्॥
en: O king of the gods, put aside this anger. At your anger the world, with its Asuras and Gandharyas and Kinnaras and the great serpents, is stricken with panic.

sn: जहि क्रोधमिमं साधो न कुप्यन्ति भवधिधाः। परस्य पत्नी सा देवी प्रसीदस्व सुरेश्वर॥
en: 0 virtuous one, put aside this anger. Beings like you never get angry. That goddess is the wife of another. O lord of the gods, be propitious.

sn: निवर्तय मनः पापात् परदाराभिमर्शनात्। देवराजोऽसि भद्रं ते प्रजा धर्मेण पालय॥
en: Turn back your mind from the wish of ravishing the wife of another. You are the king of the gods, we wish you well, protect your subjects by virtuous means.

sn: एवमुक्तो न जग्राह तद्वचः काममोहितः। अथ देवानुवाचेदमिन्द्रं प्रति सुराधिपः॥
en: Being thus addressed, he, struck with passion, listened not to those words. The protector of the gods then said to the gods regarding Indra.

sn: अहल्या थर्षिता पूर्वमृषिपत्नी यशस्विनी। जीवतो भर्तुरिन्द्रेण स वः किं न निवारितः॥
en: Ahalya, the wife of a Rishi (herself) of good reputation, was ravished by Indra while her husband was alive. Why was he not then prevented by you.

sn: बहूनि च नृशंसानि कृतानीन्द्रेण वै पुरा। वैधाण्युपधाश्चैव स वः किं न निवारितः॥
en: In bygone days, many were the deeds of cruelty done by Indra, as also vicious deeds and deceitful ones. Why was he not prevented by you.

sn: उपतिष्ठतु देवी पामेतदस्या हितं परम्। युष्याकं च सदा देवाः शिवमेवं भविष्यति॥
en: Let the goddess attend on me; this will be of great benefit to her and it will also prove to be your means of safety.

sn: देवा ऊचुः इन्द्राणीमानयिष्यामो यथेच्छसि दिवस्पते। जहि क्रोधमिमं वीर प्रीतो भव सुरेश्वर॥
en: The gods said We shall bring here the wife of Indra as you wish, O lord of the heaven; O hero put aside this anger and be propitious, o lord of the gods.

sn: शल्य उवाच इत्युक्त्वा तं तदा देवा ऋषिभिः सह भारत। जग्मुर्ब्रहस्पतिं वक्तुमिन्द्राणीं चाशुभं वचः॥
en: Shalya said Saying this, the gods accompanied by the Rishis, O on of Bharata, went to tell this unwelcome news to Brihaspati and the wife of Indra.

sn: जानीमः शरण प्राप्तामिन्द्राणीं तव वेश्मनि। दत्ताभयां च विप्रेन्द्र त्वया देवर्षिसत्तम॥
en: And they said we are aware that the queen of Indra has placed herself under your protection at your abode, O chief among the Brahmanas and that she has been accorded (your) protection, 0 chief among the Devarshis.

sn: ते त्वां देवाः सगन्धर्वा ऋषयश्च महाद्युते। प्रसादयन्ति चेन्द्राणी नहुषाय प्रदीयताम्॥
en: They, the gods with the Gandharvas and Rishis, pray you, O you of great luster, to make over the Queen of Indra to Nahusha.

sn: इन्द्रादं विशिष्टो नहुषो देवराजो महाद्युतिः। वृणोत्विमं वरारोहा भर्तृत्वे वरवर्णिनी॥
en: The king of the gods Nahusha of great luster is superior to Indra. Let this lady with slender waist and bright complexion, choose him as her husband.

sn: एवमुक्ते तु सा देवी बाष्पमुत्सृज्य सस्वनम्। उवाच रुदती दीना बृहस्पतिमिदं वचः॥
en: The goddess being thus spoken to, became depressed and sobbed aloud with tears in her eyes and then crying said these words to Brihaspati.

sn: नाहमिच्छामि नहुषं पतिं देवर्षिसत्तम। शरणागतास्मि ते ब्रह्मस्त्रायस्व महतो भयात्॥
en: O you best among the Devarshis, I have no inclination for Nahusha; I have thrown myself under your protection, O Brahmanas, save me from this great calamity.

sn: बृहस्पतिरुवाच शरणागतं न त्यजेयमिद्राणि मम निश्चयः। धर्मज्ञां सत्यशीलां च न त्यजेयमनिन्दिते॥
en: Brihaspati said It is settled that the queen of Indra, who has thrown herself under my protection, will not be turned out by me. I shall not turn out, O you who know what virtue is, the truthful and blameless.

sn: नाकार्यं कर्तुमिच्छामि ब्राह्मणः सन् विशेषतः। श्रुतधर्मा सत्यशीलो जानन् धर्मानुशासनम्॥
en: I do not wish to do a wrong thing, especially as I am a Brahmanas, who have heard what virtue is and know the rules of virtue and am truthful.

sn: नाहमेतत् करिष्यामि गच्छध्वं वै सुरोत्तमाः। अस्मिंश्चार्थं पुरा गीतं ब्रह्मणा श्रुयतामिदम्॥
en: I shall not do this; go, you best among the gods; listen to what has before been sung by Brahma, with regard to this matter, in days of old.

sn: न तस्य बीजं रोहति रोहकाले न तस्य वर्ष वर्षति वर्षकाले। भीतं प्रपन्नं प्रददति शत्रवे न स त्रातारं लभते त्राणमिच्छन्॥
en: He that makes over a man, stricken with fear who has sought refuge with him, to the enemy, does not get protection himself when he desires it. His seed cannot be sown at seed time nor does he get rain at the time for rains.

sn: मोघमन्नं विन्दति चाप्यचेताः स्वर्गाल्लोकाद् भ्रश्यति नष्टचेष्टः। भीतं प्रपन्नं प्रददाति यो वै न तस्य हव्यं प्रगतिगृह्णन्ति देवाः॥
