en: The gods do not favour the undertakings of him who makes over a man stricken with fear, who has sought refuge with him, to his enemy. The offering made by such a weak-hearted person is refused by the gods and he loses the kingdom of heaven, as if shorn of all power.

sn: प्रमीयते चास्य प्रजा ह्यकाले सदाविवासं पितरोऽस्य कुर्वते। भीतं प्रपन्नं प्रददाति शत्रवे सेन्द्रा देवाः प्रहरन्त्यस्य वज्रम्॥
en: The gods with Indra will level his thunderbolt on him who makes over a man stricken with fear, who has sought refuse with him, to his enemy. And his children will die untimely deaths and his fathers ever engage themselves in quarrels.

sn: एतदेवं विजानन् वै न दास्यामि शचीमिमाम्। इन्द्राणी विश्रुतां लोके शक्रस्य महिषीं प्रियाम्॥
en: Knowing it to be so, I shall not give up this Sachi, the queen of Indra, known in this world as the beloved queen of Shakra.

sn: अस्या हितं भवेद् यच्च मम चापि हितं भवेत्। क्रियातां तत् सुरश्रेष्ठा नहि दास्याम्यहं शचीम्॥
en: What will be of benefit to her will also be of benefit to me. Do that then, O chief among the gods. I shall not give up Sachi.

sn: शल्य उवाच अथ देवाः सगन्धर्वा गुरुमाहुरिदं वचः। कथं सुनीतं नु भवेन्मन्त्रयस्व बृहस्पते॥
en: Shalya said Then the gods with the Gandharvas said to their preceptor O Brihaspati, deliberate on what will be good policy.

sn: बृहस्पतिरुवाच नहुषं याचतां देवी किंचित् कालान्तरं शुभा। इन्द्राणी हितमेतद्वि तथाऽस्माकं भविष्यति॥
en: Brihaspati said Let this auspicious goddess ask time of Nahusha; this will be of benefit to herself and the same to us.

sn: बहुविनः सुराः कालः कालः कालं नयिष्यति। गर्वितो बलवांश्चापि नहुषो वरसंश्रयात्॥
en: O God, time is full of impediments. Time will lead time (i.e. we are in the dark as to what will happen hereafter). Nahusha is haughty and powerful alike by virtue of the boon granted him.

sn: शल्य उवाच ततस्तेन तथोक्ते तु प्रीता देवास्तथाऽब्रुवन्। ब्रह्मन् साध्विदमुक्तं ते हितं सर्वदिवौकसाम्॥
en: Shalya said Being thus addressed by Brihaspati the gods became well pleased and said-O Brahmanas, it is well said by you; this will be of benefit to all the denizens of heaven.

sn: एवमेतद् द्विजश्रेष्ठ देवी चेयं प्रसाद्यताम्। ततः समस्ता इन्द्राणी देवाश्चाग्निपुरोगमाः। ऊचुर्वचनमव्यग्रा लोकानां हितकाम्यया॥
en: O chief among the twice born, this is so. Let us propitiate this goddess. Then all the gods headed by Indra addressed these quiet words to the queen of Indra, through a desire to do good to the worlds.

sn: देवा ऊचुः त्वया जगदिदं सर्वं धृतं स्थावजङ्गमम्। एकपल्यसि सत्या च गच्छस्व नहुषं प्रति॥
en: The gods said This entire world, with all its movable and immovable, is held by you, you are an only wife and truthful; go to Nahusha.

sn: क्षिप्रं त्वामभिकामश्च विनशिष्यति पापकृत्। नहुषो देवि शक्रश्च सुरेश्वर्यमवाप्स्यति॥
en: That doer of vicious deeds Nahusha, desirous of you, O goddess, will soon be destroyed and Shakra will regain the lordship of the gods.

sn: एवं विनिश्चयं कृत्वा इन्द्राणी कार्यसिद्धये। अभ्यगच्छत सव्रीडा नहुषं घोरदर्शनम्॥
en: Making herself sure on this point, the queen of Indra went with bashful looks to Nahusha (now) fearful to look at, for the accomplishment of the object.

sn: दृष्ट्वा तां नहुषश्चापि वयोरूपसमन्विताम्। समहष्यत दुष्टात्मा कामोपहतचेतनः॥
en: And Nahusha seeing her, possessed of youth and beauty, became pleased; the consciousness of that vicious soul was stricken with passion.

sn: शल्य उवाच अथ तामब्रवीद् दृष्ट्वा नहुषो देवराट् तदा। त्रयाणामपि लोकानामहमिन्द्रः शुचिस्मिते॥
en: Shalya said Then did Nahusha, the king of the gods, seeing her address her thus-“I am the Indra of the three worlds, O you of sweet smiles." me as

sn: भजस्व मां वरारोहे पतित्वे वरवर्णिनि। एवमुक्ता तु सा देवी नहुषेण पतिव्रता॥
en: o you with slender waist, O you with bright complexion, choose your husband." The chaste goddess being thus spoken to by Nahusha.

sn: प्रावेपत भयोद्विग्ना प्रवाते कदली यथा। प्रणम्य सा हि ब्रह्माणं शिरसा तु कृताञ्जलिः॥
en: Literally trembled with fear as the plantain tree does during a storm and bowing her head to Brahma and clasping her hands together.

sn: देवराजमथोवाच नहुषं घोरदर्शनम्। कालमिच्छाम्यहं लब्धं त्वत्तः कंचित् सुरेश्वर॥
en: Said to the (now) terrific looking king of the gods. “I want time to get information on certain points, O lord of the gods.

sn: न हि विज्ञायते शक्रः किंवा प्राप्तः क्व वा गतः। तत्त्वमेतत् तु विज्ञाय यदि न ज्ञायते प्रभो॥
en: I do not know where Shakra now is, nor where he has gone to. If after trying to get information on these points, I do not get them, Olord.

sn: ततोऽहं त्वामुपस्थास्ये सत्यमेतद् ब्रवीमि ते। एवमुक्तः स इन्द्राण्या नहुषः प्रीतिमानभूत्॥
en: Then shall I attend on you; I speak sincerely." Being thus addressed by the queen of Indra, Nahusha became highly pleased.

sn: नहुष उवाच एवं भवतु सुश्रोणि यथा मामिह भाषसे। ज्ञात्वा जागमनं कार्यं सत्यमेतदनुस्मरेः॥
en: Nahusha said O you with beautiful things, let it be as you tell me here; but remember your plighted word.

sn: नहुषेण विसृष्टा च निश्चक्राम ततः शुभा। बृहस्पतिनिकेतं च सा जगाम यशस्विनी॥
en: Shalya said Then did the beautiful one, thus dismissed by Nahusha, came out and the renowned one went to the abode of Brihaspati.

sn: तस्याः संश्रुत्यं च वचो देवाश्चाग्निपुरोगमाः। चिन्तयामासुरेकाग्राः शनार्थं राजसत्तम॥
en: Having heard her words, the gods with Agni at their head, began to deliberate earnestly on the means of attaining to Shakra's good, O best among kings.

sn: देवदेवेन सङ्गम्य विष्णुना प्रभविष्णुना। ऊचुश्चैनं समुद्विग्ना वाक्यं वाक्यविशारदाः॥
en: Having met the god among the gods, the Lord Vishnu, the anxious ones, who wore adepts at speeches, thus addressed him.

sn: ब्रह्मवध्याभिभूतो वै शक्रः सुरगणेश्वरः। गतिश्च नस्त्वं देवेश पूर्वजो जगतः प्रभुः॥
en: Shakra, the lord of the gods, is overpowered by the crime of slaying a Brahmana. You, O lord, O lord of the gods, are our refuge, O you born before the universe.

sn: रक्षार्थं सर्वभूतानां विष्णुत्वमुपजग्मिवान्। त्वद्वीर्यनिहते वृत्रे वासवो ब्रह्महत्यया।॥ वृतः सुरगणश्रेष्ठ मोक्षं तस्य विनिर्दिशा तेषां तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा देवानां विष्णुरब्रवीत्॥
en: You assumed the form of Vishnu for protecting all the beings. Vritra being slain through (the aid of) your strength, Vasava, the chief among all the gods, is overpowered by the sin of slaying a Brahmana. Indicate to us the means of his salvation. Vishnu, having

sn: मामेव यजतां शक्रः पावयिष्यामि वज्रिणम्। पुण्येन हयमेधेन मामिष्ट्वा पाकशासनः॥
en: "Let Shakra offer sacrifice to me, I shall purity the one with the thunderbolt. Having duly worshipped me, by the holy sacrifice of a horse, shall the chastiser of the Paka.

sn: पुनरेष्यति देवानामिन्द्रत्वमकुतोभयः। स्वकर्मभिश्च नहुषो नाशं यास्यति दुर्मतिः॥
en: Regain the position of the king of the gods without any fear. And the evil-minded Nahusha will meet with destruction, as the effect of his own deeds.

sn: किंचित् कालमिदं देवा मर्षयध्वमतन्द्रिताः। श्रुत्वा विष्णोः शुभां सत्यां वाणी ताममृतोपमाम्॥
en: For some time, O gods, must you be patient and watchful." Hearing these words of Vishnu which were true, auspicious and like nectar.

sn: ततः सर्वे सुरगणाः सोपाध्यायाः सहर्षिभिः। यत्र शक्रो भयोद्विग्नस्तं देशमुपचक्रमुः॥
en: All the gods, with the preceptors and the Rishis, went to the spot where Shakra lay stricken with fear.

sn: तत्राश्वमेधः सुमहान् महेन्द्रस्य महात्मनः। ववृते पावनार्थं वै ब्रह्महत्यापहो नृप॥
en: There did they perform the sacrifice of a horse on a large scale, capable of absolving one from the sin of having slier of Brahmana, for the absolution of the large minded Mahendra.

sn: विभज्य ब्रह्महत्यां तु वृक्षेषु च नदीषु च। पर्वतेषु पृथिव्यां च स्त्रीषु चैव युधिष्ठिर॥
en: Then, O Yudhishthira was the crime of slaying that Brahmana divided among the trees, the rivers and the mountains and the world and the women.

sn: संविभज्य च भूतेषु विसृज्य च सुरेश्वरः। विज्वरो धूतपाप्मा च वासवोऽभवदात्मवान्॥
en: (This sin) being thus divided among all beings having left the lord of the gods, Vasava was cured of his disorder and getting rid of his sins, came to himself.

sn: अकम्पन्नहुषं स्थानादं दृष्ट्वा बलनिषूदनः। तेजोनं सर्वभूतानां वरदानाच्च दुःसहम्॥
en: Form that place the slayer of Bala saw Nahusha, who was not afraid of him and who absorbed the power of all beings and who could not be approached through the boon granted him.

sn: ततः शचीपतिर्देवः पुनरेव व्यनश्यत। अदृश्यः सर्वभूतानां कालाकाक्षी चचार ह॥
en: Then the god, the husband of Sachi again melted himself into the air and invisible by all beings he remained for a fitting opportunity.

sn: प्रनष्टे तु ततः शक्रे शची शोकसमन्विता। हा शक्रेति तदा देवी विललाप सुदुःखिता।॥
en: Shakra having rendered himself invisible, Sachi, being stricken with grief and the goddess, exceedingly sad thus lamented for him, Alas Shakra.

sn: यदि दत्तं यदि हुतं गुरवस्तोषिता यदि। एकभर्तृत्वमेवास्तु सत्यं यद्यस्ति वा मयि॥
en: If ever a gift has been made by me or an offering (made by me) or my superiors satisfied by me and if there is any truth in me, let me be with one husband only.

sn: पुण्यां चेमामहं दिव्या प्रवृत्तामुत्तरायणे। देवीं रात्रिं नमस्यामि सिध्यतां मे मनोरथः॥
en: I bow to this holy, godly goddess night who is now on the northern solstice; let my wish be satisfied.

sn: प्रयता च निशां देवीमुपातिष्ठत तत्र सा! प्रतिव्रतात्वात् सत्येन सोपश्रुतिमथाकरोत्॥
en: Then did she making her body and soul pure, offer due worship to the goddess night and for the sake of her truth and chastity she had recourse to divination.

sn: यत्रास्ते देवराजोऽसौ तं देशं दर्शयस्व मे। इत्याहोपश्रुतिं देवीं सत्यं सत्येन दृश्यताम्॥
en: Show me the spot where stays he the king of gods. Show me truth by means of truth. Thus did she ask of Upashruti.

description: The prayer of the queen of Indra
sn: शल्य उवाच अथैनां रूपिणि साध्वीमुपातिष्ठदुपश्रुतिः। तां वयोरूपसम्पन्नां दृष्ट्वा देवीमुपस्थिताम्॥
en: Shalya said Then did beautiful Upashruti appear before the chaste one. Ard seeing the goddess possessed of youth and beauty appear before her.

description: The prayer of the queen of Indra
sn: इन्द्राणी सम्प्रहृष्टात्मा सम्पूज्यनामथाब्रवीत्। इच्छामि त्वामहं ज्ञातुं का त्वं ब्रूहि वरानने॥
en: The Queen of Indra became well-pleased and having propitiated her, thus spoke-O you of a beautiful face, 'I want to know you, tell me who you are.'

description: The prayer of the queen of Indra
sn: उपश्रुतिरुवाच उपश्रुतिरहं देवि तवान्तिकमुपागता। दर्शनं चैव सम्प्राप्ता तव सत्येन भाविनि॥
en: Upashruti said I am, O goddess, Upashruti, who have come to you. O you of noble mind, I have appeared in your sight through your truthfulness.

description: The prayer of the queen of Indra
sn: पतिव्रता च युक्ता च यमेन नियमेन च। दर्शयिष्यामि ते शक्रं देवं वृत्रनिषूदनम्॥
en: You are chest, you observe all the rules of life and you possess the power self control. I shall show you the god Shakra the slayer of Vritra.

description: The prayer of the queen of Indra
sn: क्षिप्रमन्वेहि भद्रं ते द्रक्ष्यसे सुरसत्तमम्। ततस्तां प्रहितां देवीमिन्द्राणी सा समन्वगात्॥
en: I wish you well, follow me soon, you shall see the best among the gods. Then did the goddess the queen of Indra, follow her w went in advance.

description: The prayer of the queen of Indra
sn: देवारण्यान्यतिक्रम्य पर्वतांश्च बहूंस्ततः। हिमवन्तमतिक्रम्य उत्तरं पार्श्वमागमत्॥
en: Having gone through many forests of the gods and many mountains and having crossed the Himavat, the northern side was reached by them.

description: The prayer of the queen of Indra
sn: समुद्रं च समासाद्य बहुयोजनविस्तृतम्। आससाद महाद्वीपं नानादुमलतावृतम्॥
en: And having crossed the sea which extended over many yojanas they came to a large island which was covered by many trees and creepers.

description: The prayer of the queen of Indra
sn: तत्रापश्यत् सरो दिव्यं नानाशकुनिभिर्वृतम्। शतयोजनविस्तीर्णं तावदेवायतं शुभम्॥
en: They there saw a lake, suitable for the gods frequented by many birds and which extended over a hundred yojanas in length and a similar space in breadth.

description: The prayer of the queen of Indra
sn: तत्र दिव्यानि पद्मानि पञ्चवर्णानि भारत। षट्पदैरुपगीतानि प्रफुल्लानि सहस्रशः॥
en: And saw there, O son of Bharata thousands of beautiful lotuses of five colours full blown and around which the bees hummed.

description: The prayer of the queen of Indra
sn: सरसस्तस्य मध्ये तु पद्मिनी महती शुभा। गौरेणोन्नतनालेन पद्मेन महता वृता॥
en: Having penetrated into a particular lotus and entered into stalk, along with her (Sachi) they there saw the performer of a hundred sacrifices who had entered the stalk.

description: The prayer of the queen of Indra
sn: पद्मस्य भित्त्वा नालं च विवेश सहिता तया। विसतन्तुप्रविष्टं च तत्रापश्यच्छतक्रतुम्॥
en: Seeing her lord staying there in a diminutive form, the goddess too assumed a diminutive form and so did Upashruti.

description: The prayer of the queen of Indra
sn: तं दृष्ट्वा च सुसूक्ष्मेण रूपेणावस्थितं प्रभुम्। सूक्ष्मरूपधरा देवी बभूवोपश्रुतिश्च सा॥
en: Beholding there Indra in a form of very minute, goddesses Upashruti and Indrani also became in the form of minuteness.

description: The prayer of the queen of Indra
sn: इन्द्रं तुष्टाव चेन्द्राणी विश्रुतैः पूर्वकर्मभिः। स्तूयमानस्ततो देवः शचीमाह पुरन्दरः॥
en: And the queen of Indra propitiated Indra by reciting the deeds done by him in olden days and the god Purandara, being thus propitiated, said to Sachi.

description: The prayer of the queen of Indra
sn: किमर्थमसि सम्प्राप्ता विज्ञातश्च कथं त्वहम्। ततः सा कथयामास नहुषस्य विचेष्टितम्॥
en: With what object have you come here and by what means came you to know that I was here. Then did she narrate the attempt of Nahusha.

description: The prayer of the queen of Indra
sn: इन्द्रत्वं त्रिषु लोकेषु प्राप्य वीर्यसमन्वितः। दाविष्टश्च दुष्टात्मा मामुवाच शतक्रतो॥
en: Having obtained the lordship of the three worlds and so being vain of his strength and being haughty the evil minded one asked me to attend on him, Operformer of a hundred sacrifices.

description: The prayer of the queen of Indra
sn: उपतिष्ठेति स. क्रूरः कालं च कृतवान् मम। यदि न त्रास्यसि विभो करिष्यति स मां वशे॥
en: And the evil minded one has granied me time (to do his bidding). If you do not save me, O lord, he will bring me under his sway.

description: The prayer of the queen of Indra
sn: एतेन चाहं सम्प्राप्ता द्रुतं शक्र तवान्तिकम्। जहि रौद्रं महाबाहो नहुषं पापनिश्चयम्॥
en: For this reason have I come to you so soon O Shakra, O you with long arms slay Nahusha of wicked purposes.

description: The prayer of the queen of Indra
sn: प्रकाशयात्मनाऽऽत्मानं दैत्यदानवसूदन। तेजः समाप्नुहि विभो देवराज्यं प्रशाधि च॥
en: O you slayer of Daityas and Danavas, hide no longer your ownself. O lord, assume your own strength and rule the kingdom of the gods.

sn: शल्य उवाच एवमुक्तः स भगवाञ्छच्या तां पुनरब्रवीत्। विक्रमस्य न कालोऽयं नहुषो बलवत्तरः॥
en: Shalya said The god, being thus spoken to, thus addressed Sachi in reply-'This is not the time for (showing) strength, Nahusha is stronger.

sn: विवर्धितश्च ऋषिभिर्हव्यकव्यैश्च भाविनि। नीतिमत्र विधास्यामि देवि तां कर्तुमर्हसि॥
en: He has grown up to his present position by the virtue of the offerings made him by the Rishis. In this instance, I shall prescribe a politic course and it is proper that it should be followed by you.

sn: गुह्यं चैतत् त्वया कार्यं नाख्यातव्यं शुभे क्वचित्। गत्वा नहुषमेकान्ते ब्रवीहि च सुमध्यमे॥
en: It should be done by you with secrecy and on no account should you give it out. O you of slender waist, go to Nahusha and speak thus to him.

sn: ऋषियानेन दिव्येन मामुपैहि जगत्पते। एवं तव वशे प्रीता भविष्यामीति तं वदा॥
en: "O lord of the universe, come near me riding a conveyance suitable for the gods and borne by Rishis. By thus showing yourself attached to me, shall I be pleased with you" speak thus to him.

sn: इत्युक्त्वा देवराजेन पत्नी सा कमलेक्षणा। एवमस्त्वित्यथोक्त्वा तु जगाम नहुषं प्रति॥
en: Being thus spoken to by the king of the gods his queen of lotus-like eyes, replied “Be it so" and went to Nahusha.

sn: नहुषस्तां ततो दृष्ट्वा सस्मितो वाक्यमब्रवीत्। स्वागतं ते वरारोहे किं करोमि शुचिस्मिते॥
en: Nahusha surprised at seeing her, spoke these words-Welcome to you, O you of beautiful hips, what shall I do, O you of lovely smiles?

sn: भक्तं मां भज कल्याणि कमिच्छसि मनस्विनि। तव कल्याणि यत् कार्यं तत् करिष्ये सुमध्यमे॥
en: Accept me devoted to you; O blessed one, what do you wish, O maiden of independent spirit? O blessed one, O you of slender waist.

sn: न च व्रीडा त्वया कार्या सुश्रोणि मयि विश्वसेः। सत्येन वै शपे देवि करिष्ये वचनं तव॥
en: You need not be shy; O you of slender waist, have confidence in me. I swear by truth, O goddess, I shall do your bidding.

sn: इन्द्राण्युवाच यो मे कृतस्त्वया कालस्तमाकाङ्क्षे जगत्पते। ततस्त्वमेव भर्ता मे भविष्यसि सुराधिप॥
en: The queen of Indra said O lord of the world, I only want time-the favour that has already been accorded to me. After that you shall become my husband, O lord of the gods.

sn: कार्यं च हृदि मे यत् तद् देवराजावधारय। वक्ष्यामि यदि मे राजन् प्रियमेतत् करिष्यसि॥ वाक्यं प्रणयसंयुक्तं ततः स्यां वशगा तव।
en: The subject that is in my mind is this listen, O lord of the gods; I shall speak it to you, O king, fulfill my desire. The boon, that I demand of you, has connection with your love.

sn: इन्द्रस्य वाजिनो वाहा हस्तिनोऽथ रथास्तथा॥ इच्छाम्यहमथापूर्वं वाहनं ते सुराधिप। यन्न विष्णोर्न रुद्रस्य नासुराणां न रक्षसाम्॥
en: Indra had for his conveyance, horses, elephants and a car. I wish that you, O lord of the gods should have a conveyance, the like of which was never seen before, which was never owned by Vishnu, nor by Rudra, nor by the Asuras and the Rakshasas.

sn: वहन्तु त्वां महाभागा ऋषयः संगता विभो। सर्वे शिबिकया राजन्नेतद्धि मम रोचते॥
en: O Lord, to see yourself being borne by the Rishis having good attributes, united together in a palankin, is my wish, oking.

sn: नासुरेषु न देवेषु तुल्यो भवितुमर्हसि। सर्वेषा तेज आदत्से स्वेन वीर्येण दर्शनात्। न ते प्रमुखतः स्थातुं कश्चिच्छक्नोति वीर्यवान्॥
en: You should not be (merely) equal to the Asuras or the gods. By your own strength do you absorb that of all beings the moment you set your eyes on them. No one can stand face to face with you, O you powerful being.

sn: शल्य उवाच एवमुक्तस्तु नहुषः प्राहृष्यत् तदा किल। उवाच वचनं चापि सुरेन्द्रस्तामनिन्दिताम्॥
en: Shalya said Nahusha, being thus spoken to became well pleased and the king of the gods said these words to that blameless one.

sn: नहुष उवाच अपूर्वं वाहनमिदं त्वयोक्तं वरवर्णिनि। दृढं मे रुचितं देवि त्वद्वशोऽस्मि वरानने॥
en: Nahusha said 0 you of bright complexion, the conveyance spoken of by you has never before been in existence. I have taken a strong fancy to it O goddess. I am at your disposal, O lovely faced one.

sn: न ह्यल्पवीर्यो भवति यो वाहान् कुरुते मुनीन्। अहं तपस्वी बलवान् भूतभव्यभवत्प्रभुः॥
en: The one who makes the Rishis his bearers cannot be of little strength. I am a devotee, strong and lord of what has been, what is to be and what is.

sn: मयि क्रुद्धे जगन्न स्यान्मयि सर्वं प्रतिष्ठितम्। देवदानवगन्धर्वाः किन्नरोरगराक्षसाः॥ न मे क्रुद्धस्य पर्याप्ताः सर्वे लोकाः शुचिस्मिते। चक्षुषा यं प्रपश्यामि तस्य तेजो हराम्यहम्॥
en: At my being angry the world will be annihilated; everything depends on me. The gods, the Danavas and the Gandharvas, the Kinnaras, the serpents and the Rakashasas, not all of these, not all the world even can stand against me when I am angry. Whoever I see by my eyes, his strength do I absorb.

sn: तस्मात् ते वचनं देवि करिष्यामि न संशयः। सप्तर्षयो मां वक्ष्यन्ति सर्वे ब्रह्मर्षयस्तथा। पश्य महात्म्ययोगं मे ऋद्धिं च वरवर्णिनि॥
en: Therefore O goddess, shall I do your bidding, there is no doubt about it. Seven Rishis shall bear me, Brahmarshis all see, my powers and influence, having thus said to that goddess.

sn: शल्य उवाच एवमुक्त्वा तु तां देवीं विसृज्य च वराननाम्। विमाने योजयित्वा च ऋषीन् नियममास्थितान्॥ अब्रह्मण्यो बलोपेतो मत्तो मदबलेन च। कामवृत्तः स दुष्टात्मा वाहयामास तानृषीन्॥
en: Shalya said O king! O you of bright complexion and having dismissed that lovely face one, he yoked, to car, Rishis who used to observe the rules of their class. The habits of his life being unworthy of a Brahmana, having come to the possession of power, vain of his strength, willful and of a vicious nature, he made the Rishis carry him.

sn: नहुषेण विसृष्टा च बृहस्पतिमथाब्रवीत्। समयोऽल्पावशेषो मे नहुषेणेह यः कृतः॥
en: Being dismissed by Nahusha, she said to Brihaspati-“But little remains to fulfill in its entirety the boon granted by Nahusha.

sn: शक्रं मृगय शीघ्रं त्वं भक्तायाः कुरु मे दयाम्। बाढमित्येव भगवान् बृहस्पतिरुवाच ताम्॥
en: Be quick in hunting out Indra and do me who am devoted to you, a favour and the god Brihaspati said to her-"Be it so."

sn: न भेतव्य त्वया देवि नहुषाद् दुष्टचेतसः। न होष स्थास्यति चिरं गत एष नराधमः॥
en: The evil minded Nahusha need not be feared by you. He will not exist till eternity; indeed he is already gone.

sn: अधर्मज्ञो महर्षीणां वाहनाच्च ततः शुभे। इष्टिं चाहं करिष्यामि विनाशायास्य दुर्मतेः॥ शक्रं चाधिगमिष्यामि मा भैस्त्वं भद्रमस्तु ते।
en: He is regardless of virtue so to say, having employed the great Rishis as his bearer, O lovely lady; and I shall perform sacrifices for the destruction of this evil minded one. I shall approach Shakra. You need not have any fears, I wish you well.

sn: ततः प्रज्वाल्य विधिवज्जुहाव परमं हविः॥ बृहस्तपतिर्महातेजा देवराजोपलब्धये। हुत्वाग्निं सोऽब्रवीद् राजञ्छक्रमन्विष्यतामिति॥
en: Then having lighted up a fire he offered the best offerings in the prescribed form. Brihaspati of great strength, in order to get the gods, having made offerings to Agni (the God of fire) said to him-Oking search out Shakra.

sn: तस्माच्च भगवान् देवः स्वयमेव हुताशनः। स्त्रीवेषमद्भुतं कृत्वा तत्रैवान्तरधीयत॥
en: From that place, the god (of fire) the consumer of offerings having himself assumed the wonderful form of a female vanished from sight.

sn: स दिशः प्रदिशश्चैव पर्वतानि वनानि च। पृथिवीं चान्तरिक्षं च विचिन्त्याथ मनोगतिः। निमेषान्तरमात्रेण बृहस्पतिमुपागमत्॥
en: Having searched in all countries and provinces, mountains and forest, the earth and the sky, with the speed of the mind, he in a moment came back to Brihaspati.

sn: अग्निरुवाच बृहस्पते न पश्यामि देवराजमिह क्वचित्। आपः शेषाः सदा चापः प्रवेष्टुं नोत्सहाम्यहम्॥
en: The god of fire said O Brihaspati, nowhere, in this world do I see the king of the gods. The waters (alone) remain (to be searched). I have never been able to enter the waters.

sn: न मे तत्र गतिर्ब्रह्मन् किमन्यत् करवाणि ते! तमब्रवीद् देवगुरुरपो विश महायुते॥
en: I have no ingress there O Brahmana, what else shall I do for you. The preceptor of the gods said to him-"O you of great luster, enter the waters."

sn: अग्निरुवाच नापः प्रवेष्टुं शक्ष्यामि क्षयो मेऽत्र भविष्यति। शरणं त्वां प्रपन्नोऽस्मि स्वस्ति तेऽस्तु महाद्युते॥
en: The god of fire said I cannot enter the water there I am destroyed. I throw myself under your protection. O you of great luster, I wish you well.

sn: अद्भयोऽग्निर्ब्रह्मतः क्षत्रमश्मनो लोहमुत्थितम्। तेषां सर्वत्रगं तेजः स्वासु योनिषु शाम्यति॥
en: From the waters rose fire, from the Brahmana, the Kshatriya and from stone, the iron. Its strength penetrates everywhere; only in its birth-place is it powerless.

description: Varuna and others' news to Indra
sn: बृहस्पतिरुवाच त्वमग्ने सर्वदेवानां मुखं त्वमसि हव्यवाट्। त्वमन्तः सर्वभूतानां गूढश्चरसि साक्षिवत्॥
en: Brihaspati said O Agni, you are within all beings and concealed there you act like a witness.

description: Varuna and others' news to Indra
sn: त्वामाहुरेकं कवयस्त्वामाहुस्त्रिविधं पुनः। त्वया त्यक्तं जगच्चेदं सद्यो नश्येद्भुताशन॥
en: The poets sang of you as the one and then again as the three. O you consumer of offerings, bereft of you this world is at once annihilated.

description: Varuna and others' news to Indra
sn: कृत्वा तुभ्यं नमो विप्राः स्वकर्मविजितां गतिम्। गच्छन्ति सह पत्नीभिः सुतैरपि च शाश्वतीम्॥
en: The Brahmanas, having bowed down to you, go away along with their wives and sons, to the eternal region, which has been won by the merit of their own deeds.

description: Varuna and others' news to Indra
sn: त्वमेवाग्ने हव्यवाहस्त्वमेव परमं हविः। जयन्ति सत्रैस्त्वामेव यज्ञैश्च परमाध्वरे॥
en: You are, O god of fire, the receiver of offering and you are yourself the best offering. They worship you in a sacrificial ceremony by the best offerings.

description: Varuna and others' news to Indra
sn: सृष्ट्वा लोकांस्त्रीनिमान् हव्यवाह प्राप्ते काले पचसि पुनः समिद्धः। स्त्वमेवाग्ने भवसि पुनः प्रतिष्ठा॥
en: O you receiver of offerings, having created the three worlds in due time you again in due time consume them in an enkindled form; you are, O god of fire, the progenitor of the entire world and you again annihilate it.

description: Varuna and others' news to Indra
sn: त्वामग्ने जलदानाहुर्विद्युतश्च मनीषिणः। दहन्ति सर्वभूतानि त्वत्तो निष्क्रम्य हेतयः॥
en: Wise people called you, O Agni, the giver of water and lightning and flames coming out from you support all beings.

description: Varuna and others' news to Indra
sn: त्वय्यापो निहिताः सर्वास्त्वयि सर्वमिदं जगत्। न तेऽस्त्यविदितं किंचित् त्रिषु लोकेषु पावक॥
en: Water depends on you, everything and this entire world; o you purifying element, there is not the least thing unknown to you in these three worlds.

description: Varuna and others' news to Indra
sn: स्वयोनि भजते सर्वो विशस्वापोऽविशङ्कितः। अहं त्वां वर्धयिष्यामि ब्राझैर्मन्त्रैः सनातनैः॥
en: Everything accepts that which comes from it, enter the waters without any fear. I shall make you strong by reciting eternal hymns relating to Brahma.

description: Varuna and others' news to Indra
sn: एवं स्तुतो हव्यवाट् स भगवान् कविरुत्तमः। बृहस्पतिमथोवाच प्रीतिमान् वाक्यमुत्तमम्। दर्शयिष्यामि ते शक्रं सत्यमेतद् ब्रवीमि ते॥
en: Thus propitiated, the bearer of offerings, the god, the best among poets, said to Brihaspati, these good words indicating satisfaction. “I shall show you Shakra. I speak this truly.

description: Varuna and others' news to Indra
sn: शल्य उवाच प्रविश्यापस्ततो वह्निः ससमुद्राः सपल्वलाः। आससाद सरस्तच्च गूढो यत्र शतक्रतुः॥
en: Shalya said Agni (the god of fire) thus having entered the waters including the seas and the small lakes, came to the lake where Shakra lay in disguise.

description: Varuna and others' news to Indra
sn: अथ तत्रापि पद्मानि विचिन्वन् भरतर्षभ। अपश्यत् स तु देवेन्द्र बिसमध्यगतं स्थितम्॥
en: And there searching among the lotuses, O you foremost in the race of Bharata, he saw at last the king of gods, in one of the stalks.

description: Varuna and others' news to Indra
sn: आगत्य च ततस्तूर्णं तमाचष्ट बृहस्पतेः। अणुमात्रेण वपुषा पद्मतन्त्वाश्रितं प्रभुम्॥
en: And then coming back quickly he gave that information to Brihaspati, namely that the lord having assumed a diminutive form was lying within a lotus.

description: Varuna and others' news to Indra
sn: गत्वा देवर्षिगन्धर्वैः सहितोऽथ बृहस्पतिः। पुराणैः कर्मभिर्देवं तुष्टाव बलसूदनम्॥
en: Brihaspati, then having gone (there) along with the Devarshis and Gandharvas, propitiated the slayer of Bala by reciting his deeds of olden days.

description: Varuna and others' news to Indra
sn: महासुरे हतः शक्र नमुचिर्दारुणस्त्वया। शम्बरच बलश्चैव तथोभौ घोरविक्रमौ॥
en: 0 Shakra, the great Asura, Namuchi of great power has been slain by you; so are Shambara and Bala, both of great prowess.

description: Varuna and others' news to Indra
sn: शथक्रतो विवर्धस्व सर्वाञ्छत्रुन् निषूदय। उत्तिष्ठ शक्र सम्पश्य देवर्षीश्च समागतान्॥
en: O you performer of a hundred sacrifices, gain in strength and slay all enemies; rise up Shakra and see the Devarshis come to you.

description: Varuna and others' news to Indra
sn: महेन्द्र दानवान् हत्वा लोकास्त्रातास्त्वया विभो। अपां फेन समासाद्य विष्णुतेजोऽतिबृंहितम्। त्वया वृत्रो हतः पूर्वं देवराज जगत्पते॥
en: O Great Indra, having slain the Danavas, you have saved the worlds. O Lord, having got the foam of the waters and with the assistance of the strength of Vishnu, you have killed Vritra before this; o you king of the gods, 0 you lord of the universe.

description: Varuna and others' news to Indra
sn: स्त्वया समं विद्यते नेह भूतम्। त्वया धार्यन्ते सर्वभूतानि शक्त त्वं देवानां महिमानं चकर्थ॥
en: You are the saviour of all beings and worthy of beings and worthy of being propitiated by them. There is no being is this world equal to you. All the beings and support by you, O Shakra and you created the greatness of the gods.

description: Varuna and others' news to Indra
sn: पाहि सर्वांश्च लोकांश्च महेन्द्र बलमाप्नुहि। एवं संस्तूयमानश्च सोऽवर्धत शनैः शनैः॥
en: O great Indra, rule over all three worlds and grow in strength. Being thus propitiated he, by slow degrees, increased (in strength).

description: Varuna and others' news to Indra
sn: स्वं चैव वपुरास्थाय बभूव स बलान्वितः। अब्रवीच्च गुरुं देवो बृहस्पतिमवस्थितम्॥
en: Having gained his own form he became endowed with strength and the god thus addressed his preceptor who was standing before him.

description: Varuna and others' news to Indra
sn: किं कार्यमवशिष्टं वो हतस्त्वाष्ट्रो महासुरः। वृत्रश्च सुमहाकायो यो वै लोकाननाशयत्॥
en: What is there still remaining to be done. The great Asura, the son of Tvashtri, has been killed and so has been Vritra of large stature who destroyed the three worlds.

description: Varuna and others' news to Indra
sn: बृहस्पतिरुवाच मानुषो नहुषो राजा देवर्षिगणतेजसा। देवराज्यमनुप्राप्तः सर्वान् नो बाधते भृशम्॥
en: Brihaspati said The human being Nahusha, through the influence of the Devarshis, having gained the kingdom of gods, is very much inflecting us.

description: Varuna and others' news to Indra
sn: कथं च नहुषो राज्यं देवानां प्राप दुर्लभम्। तपसा केन वा युक्तः किंवीर्यो वा बृहस्पते।॥
en: Indra said How did Nahusha obtain the kingdom of the gods, which is hard to gain; with what strength of devotion is he endued, what is his power, O Brihaspati.

description: Varuna and others' news to Indra
sn: बृहस्पतिरुवाच देवा भीताः शक्रमकामयन्त त्वया त्यक्तं महदैन्द्रं पदं तत्। तदा देवाः पितरोऽथर्षयश्च गन्धर्वमुख्याश्च समेत्य सर्वे॥
en: Brihaspati said Yourself having left the celebrated position of Indra, the gods became anxious and wished for a Shakra; and at that time the gods, the Pitris, the Rishis and the chief among the Gandharvas all united together.

description: Varuna and others' news to Indra
sn: गत्वाब्रुवन् नहुषं तत्र शक्र त्वं नो राजा भव भुवनस्य गोप्ता। तानब्रवीनहुषो नास्मि शक्त आप्यायध्वं तपसा तेजसा माम्॥
en: And going, O Shakra, to Nahusha they said-Be you king, the protector of the worldNahusha said to them-I am not capable of being your king); infuse in me, strength with the virtue of devotion.

description: Varuna and others' news to Indra
sn: एवमुक्तैर्वर्धितश्चापि देव राजाभवन्नहुषो घोरवीर्यः। त्रैलोक्ये च प्राप्य राज्य महर्षीन् कृत्वा वाहान् याति लोकान् दुरात्मा॥
en: The gods being thus spoken to, infused strength into Nahusha (now) of great strength and, he became the king; having got the kingdom of the three worlds, he has made the great Rishis his bears and the wicked-minded one is now roaming about the worlds.

description: Varuna and others' news to Indra
sn: तेजोहरं दृष्टिविषं सुधोरं मा त्वं पश्येर्नहुषं वै कदाचित्। देवाश्च सर्वे नहुषं भृशार्ता न पश्यन्ते गूढरूपाश्चरन्तः॥
en: Never do you look at Nahusha who absorbs all energy and whose gaze is as very subtle as poison. The gods too, being very much afraid of Nahusha, do not look at him and roam about in concealment.

description: Varuna and others' news to Indra
sn: शल्य उवाच एवं वदत्यङ्गिरसां वरिष्ठे बृहस्पतौ लोकपालः कुबेरः। वैवस्वतश्चैव यमः पुराणो देवश्च सोमो वरुणचाजगाम॥
en: Shalya said While Brihaspati, that best among the race of Angira, was yet speaking, Kubera, the ruler of the world and Yama, the son of Vivasvata and the aged god Soma and Varuna came there.

description: Varuna and others' news to Indra
sn: दिष्ट्या त्वाष्ट्रो निहतश्चैव वृत्रः। दिष्ट्या च त्वां कुशलिनमक्षतं च पश्यामो वै निहतारिं च शक्र।।२८।'
en: They having come there spoke thus to the great Indra-"it is lucky that the son of Tvashtri has been killed and Vritra; it is lucky that we see you, O Shakra, safe and sound and without any would, with all your enemies slain.

description: Varuna and others' news to Indra
sn: स तान् यथावच्च हि लोकपालान् समेत्य वै प्रीतमना महेन्द्रः। उवाच चैनान प्रतिभाष्य शक्रः संचोदयिष्यन्नहुषस्यान्तरेण॥
en: And he, the great Indra, with a glad heart having greeted the assembled rulers of the world each with suitable words, said to them, with a view to cutwit Nahusha.

description: Varuna and others' news to Indra
sn: स्तत्र साह्यं दीयतां मे भवद्भिः। ते चाब्रुवन् नहुष घोररूपो दृष्टीविषस्तस्य विभीम ईश॥
en: "Nahusha, the king of the gods is of a terrible form; therefore assistance to me must be rendered by you.” They too said-"Nahusha is terrible-looking and we fear, O lord, his poisonous gaze.

description: Varuna and others' news to Indra
sn: स्ततो वयं भागमर्हाम शक्र। र्यमः कुबेरच मयाऽभिषेकम्॥
en: If you overthrow the king Nahusha, then O Shakra, it is only fitting that we too shall be entitled to our share (of the glory).” Indra said-you, O lord of waters and Kubera and Yama be crowed king along with me.

description: Varuna and others' news to Indra
sn: सम्प्राप्नुवन्त्वद्य सहैव दैवतै रिपुं जयाम तं नहुषं घोरदृष्टिम्। ततः शक्रं ज्वलनोऽप्याह भागं प्रयच्छ मह्यं तव साह्यं करिष्ये। तमाह शक्रो भविताग्ने तवापि चेन्द्राग्न्योर्वे भाग एको महाक्रतौ॥
en: Coming together, shall we this day, with the aid of the gods, win victory over our enemy, Nahusha, of terrific gaze. Then the god of fire said to Shakra-"give me a share, I shall render you assistance" and Indra said to him; "O God of fire, you too shall get a share; in large sacrificial ceremonies, there will be but one share for Indra and Agni."

description: Varuna and others' news to Indra
sn: शल्य उवाच एवं संचिन्त्य भगवान् महेन्द्रः पाकशासनः। कुबेरं सर्वयक्षाणां धनानां च प्रभुं तथा॥ वैवस्वतं पितृणां च वरुणं चाप्यपां तथा। आधिपत्यं ददौ शक्रः संचिन्त्य वरदस्तथा॥
en: Shalya said Thus thinking, the god, the great Indra, the chastiser of the Paka, the giver of boons, with due deliberation, gave to Kubera the lordship of all the Yakshas and treasures and to the son of Vivasvata that over the Pitris and to Varuna that over the waters.

sn: शल्य उवाच अथ संचिन्तयानस्य देवराजस्य धीमतः। नहुषस्य वधोपायं लोकपालैः सदैवतैः॥ तपस्वी तत्र भगवानगस्त्यः प्रत्यदृश्यत। सोऽब्रवीदर्घ्य देवेन्द्रं दिष्ट्या वै वर्धते भवान्॥ विश्वरूपविनाशेन वृत्रासुरवधेन च। दिष्ट्याद्य नहुषो भ्रष्टो देवराज्यात् पुरंदर। दिष्ट्या हतारिं पश्यामि भवन्तं बलसूदन॥
en: Shalya said While the wise king of the gods was fixing on means of killing Nahusha, along with the ruler of the worlds and the gods, the ascetic, who had the six attributes of a godly being, Agastya, appeared there and having delay greeted the king of the gods, said-It is fortunate that you are gaining in strength, having already killed the great Aşura who had assumed a universal form; it is fortunate, O Purandara the Nahusha is this day ousted from the kingdom of heaven; it is fortunate, O slayer of Bala, that I see you with all your enemies, killed.

sn: इन्द्र उवाच स्वागतं ते महर्षेऽस्तु प्रीतोऽहं दर्शनात् तव। पाद्यमाचमनीयं च गामर्थ्य च प्रतीच्छ मे॥
en: Indra said Welcome to you, O great Rishi; I am pleased at seeing you; be so good as to accept from me water for washing your feet and your face and also the things suitable for your worship and a cow.

sn: शल्य उवाच पूजितं चोपविष्टं तमासने मुनिसत्तमम्। पर्यपृच्छत देवेशः प्रहृष्टो ब्राह्मणर्षमम्॥
en: Shalya said That best among the Rishis being duly worshipped and seated on a seat, the chief of the gods, well pleased, asked that best among the Brahmanas.

sn: एतदिच्छामि भगवन् कथ्यमानं द्विजोत्तम। परिभ्रष्टः कथं स्वर्गान्नहुषः पापनिश्चयः॥
en: O you best among the twice born, having the six attributes, narrate how Nahusha of vicious purpose came to be ousted from heaven. I want to hear that.

sn: अगस्त्य उवाच शृणु शक्र प्रियं वाक्यं यथा राजा दुरात्मवान्। स्वर्गाद् भ्रष्टो दुराचारो नहुषो बलदर्पितः॥
en: Agastya said Listen, O Shakra, to this story as to how the vicious-souled Nahusha, of bad habits, vain of his strength, has been ousted from heaven.

sn: श्रमाश्चि वहन्तस्तं नहुषं पापकारिणम्। देवर्षयो महाभागास्तथा ब्रह्मर्षयोऽमला:॥ पप्रच्छुर्नहुषं देव संशयं जयतां वर। य इमे ब्रह्मणा प्रोक्ता मन्त्रा वै प्रोक्षणे गवाम्॥ एते प्रमाणं भवत उताहो नेति वासव। नहुषो नेति तानाह तमसा मूढचेतनः॥
en: The Devarshis of great attributes and the Brahmarshis of spotless fame wearied with bearing Nahusha, the doer of vicious deeds, asked him (Nahusha), O best of victors, if the hymns prescribed to be chanted by Brahma, at the time of sprinkling the cows, were authentic. And also if he believed in their authenticity, told them that it was not authentic.

sn: ऋषय ऊचुः अधर्मे सम्प्रवृत्तस्त्वं धर्मं न प्रतिपद्यसे। प्रमाणमेतदस्माकं पूर्वं प्रोक्तं महर्षिभिः॥
en: The Rishis said You are going along the path of vice; you do not act virtuously. “That they are authentic" has before been said by our great Rishis.

sn: अगस्त्य उवाच ततो विवदमानः स मुनिभिः सह वासव। अथ मामस्पृशन्मूर्ध्नि पादेनाधर्मपीडितः॥
en: Agastya said Then, O Vasava, he began quarreling with the Rishis and then the one, ruled by vice, touched my head with his feet.

sn: तेनाभूद्धततेजाश्च नि:श्रीकश्च महीपतिः। ततस्तं तमसाऽऽविग्नमवोचं भृशपीडितम्॥
en: By that act did the king lose his strength and became shorn of prosperity; and then as he was agitated and oppressed with fear and had lost the power of speech, I said-

sn: यस्मात् पूर्वैः कृतं राजन् ब्रह्मर्षिभिरनुष्ठितम्। अदुष्टं दूषयसि मे यच्च मूर्ध्यस्पृशः पदा॥ यच्चापि त्वमृषीन् मूढ ब्रह्मकल्पान् दुरासदान्॥ वाहान् कृत्वा वाहयसि तेन स्वर्गाद्धतप्रभः। ध्वसं पाप परिभ्रष्टः क्षीणपुण्यो महीतले॥
en: Since, O king, you call into question, the hymns authorized by our ancestors and chanted by Brahmarshis and since you have touched me with your feet and since, O fool, you have your conveyance carried by Rishis equal to Brahma and unapproachable, whom you have made your bearers, therefore be shorn of your power. O Vice, be destroyed and turned out of heaven, go you to the earth where there is little virtue.

sn: दशवर्षसहस्राणि सर्परूपधरो महान्। विचरिष्यसि पूर्णेषु पुनः स्वर्गमवाप्स्यसि॥
en: For ten thousand years, assuming the form of a large snake, shall you roam about and at the completion of that period shall you again get into heaven.

sn: एवं भ्रष्टो दुरात्मा स देवराज्यादरिंदम। दिष्ट्या वर्धामहे शक्र हतो ब्राह्मणकण्टकः॥
en: The wicked-souled one was thus turned out of the kingdom of the gods, O you subduer of foes. It is lucky, O Shakra, that we are now on the ascendant and that thorn, of the Brahmanas, has been killed.

sn: त्रिविष्टपं प्रपद्यस्व पाहि लोकाञ्छचीपते। जितेन्द्रियो जितामित्रः स्तयूमानो महर्षिभिः॥
en: O you lord of Sachi, go you to heaven and rule over the world, after conquering your senses and subduing your enemies and being propitiated by the great Rishis.

sn: शल्य उवाच ततो देवा भृशं तुष्टा महर्षिगणसंवृताः। पितरश्चैव यक्षाच भुजगा राक्षसास्तथा॥ गन्धर्वा देवकन्याच सर्वे चाप्सरसां गणाः। सरांसि सरितः शैलाः सागराश्च विशाम्पते॥
en: Shalya said Then the gods were highly pleased, along with the great Rishis and the Pitris and the Yakshas and the Rakshasas and the Gandharvas and the celestial nymphs and all the fairies; and all the tanks and the lakes and the mountains and the rivers rejoiced.

sn: उपागम्याब्रुवन् सर्वे दिष्ट्या वर्धसि शत्रुहन्। हतश्च नहुषः पापो दिष्ट्यागस्त्येन धीमता। दिष्ट्या पापसमाचारः कृतः सर्पो महीतले॥
en: They all coming there said-it is fortunate, Oslayer of enemies, that you are on the ascendant; it is fortunate that the vicious Nahusha has been killed by the wise Agastya; it is fortunate that being of vicious habits has been turned into a snake in the earth.

sn: शल्य उवाच ततः शक्रः स्तूयमानो गन्धर्वप्सरसां गणैः। ऐरावतं समारुह्य द्विपेन्द्रं लक्षणैर्युतम्॥ पावकः सुमहातेजा महर्षिश्च बृहस्पतिः। यमश्च वरुणश्चैव कुबेश्च धनेश्वरः॥ सर्वैर्देवैः परिवृतः शक्रो वृत्रनिषूदनः। गन्धर्वैरप्सरोभिश्च यातस्त्रिभुवनं प्रभुः॥
en: Shalya said Then Shakra being glorified by the Gandharvas and the celestial nymphs, ascended on the Airavata, the chief among elephants, which bore auspicious marks. The god of fire, of very great strength and the great Rishi Brihaspati, Yama, Varuna and Kubera, the god of wealth, surrounded by all these gods and by the Gandharvas and the celestial nymphs Shakra, the slayer of Vritra and the lord of the three worlds, went round.

sn: स समेत्य महेन्द्राण्या देवराजः शतक्रतुः। मुदा परमया युक्तः पालयामास देवराट्॥
en: Being united with his queen the great Indra, the king of the gods, the performer of a hundred sacrifices, highly pleased ruled over the gods.

sn: ततः स भगवांस्तत्र अङ्गिराः समदृश्यता अथर्ववेदमन्त्रैश्च देवेन्द्रं समपूजयत्॥
en: Then the god there Angira propitiating the king of the gods by chanting hymns from the Atharvaveda.

sn: ततस्तु भगवानिन्द्रः संहृष्टः समपद्यत। वरं च प्रददौ तस्मै अथर्वाङ्गिरसे तदा॥
en: saw Then the god Indra became highly pleased and he granted a boon to Angiras who was chanting the Atharvaveda.

sn: अथर्वाङ्गिरसो नाम वेदोऽस्मिन् वै भविष्यति। उदाहरणमेतद्धि यक्षभागं च लप्स्यसे॥
en: To this Veda, there will be given the name of Atharvangirasa; this is an example; and you will also get a share of the offerings in a sacrifice.

sn: एवं सम्पूज्य भगवानथर्वाङ्गिरसं तदा। व्यसर्जयन्महाराज देवराजः शतक्रतुः॥
en: The god having thus greeted Angirasa, the king of the gods, the performer of a hundred sacrifices dismissed him, O great king.

sn: सम्पूज्य सर्वास्त्रिदशानृषीश्चापि तपोधनान्। इन्द्रः प्रमुदितो राजन् धर्मेणापालयत् प्रजाः॥
en: Doing due honours to all, to the thirteen Rishis and those whose wealth consisted in devotion alone and well pleased, Indra ruled over his subjects with virtue, O king.

sn: एवं दुःखमनुप्राप्तमिन्द्रेण सह भार्यया। अज्ञातवासश्च कृतः शत्रूणां वधकाझ्या॥
en: Such was the trouble experienced by Indra in company with his queen; he had also to remain unknown in exile through his wishing for the downfall of his enemies.

sn: नात्र मन्युस्त्वया कार्यो यत् क्लिष्टोऽसि महावने। द्रौपद्या सह राजेन्द्र भ्रातृभिश्च महात्मभिः॥
en: You should not, for this reason, mind the troubles that you experienced in the great forest in company with Draupadi, O chief among kings and your noble minded brothers.

sn: एवं त्वमपि राजेन्द्र राज्यं प्राप्स्यसि भारता वृत्रं हत्वा यथा प्राप्तः शक्रः कौरवनन्दन॥
en: O chief among kings, O son of Bharata, you too will get your kingdom in the same way as Shakra got his by slaying Vritra, O you who cause rejoicing among the race of Kurus.

sn: दुराचारश्च नहुषो ब्रह्मविट् पापचेतनः। अगस्त्यशापाभिहतो विनष्टः शाश्वती: समाः॥
en: Nahusha, of evil habits, the enemy of Brahmanas, of vicious mind, was overthrown through the curse of Agastya and absolutely ruined for a long period.

sn: एवं तव दुरात्मानः शत्रवः शत्रुसूदन्। क्षिप्रं नाशं गमिष्यन्ति कर्णदुर्योधनादयः॥
en: So shall your evil minded foes, Karna, Duryodhana and others, O subduer of enemies, soon meet with ruin.

sn: ततः सागरपर्यन्तां भोक्ष्यसे मेदिनीमिमाम्। भ्रातृभिः सहितो वीर द्रौपद्या च सहानया॥
en: Then will you come into the possess of this world ending with the ocean, in company with your brothers, O hero and this lady Draupadi.

sn: उपाख्यानमिदं शक्रविजयं वेदसम्मितम्। राज्ञा व्यूढेष्वनीकेषु श्रोतव्यं जयमिच्छता॥
en: This story of the victory of Shakra is of the same rank, as the Veda, with regard to its sanctity and it ought to be listened to by a king who is desirous of a victory and who has his army ready for battle.

sn: तस्मात् संश्रावयामि त्वां विजयं जयतां वर। संस्तूयमाना वर्धन्ते महात्मानो युधिष्ठिर॥
en: Therefore do I make it listened to by you so that you may gain a victory, O best of victors. The great minded increase (in strength) by being glorified, O Yudhishthira.

sn: क्षत्रियाणामभावोऽयं युधिष्ठिर महात्मनाम्। दुर्योधनापराधेन भीमार्जुनबलेन च॥
en: O Yudhishthira, the destruction of large minded Kshatriyas, through the crimes of Duryodhana and the strength of Bhima and Arjuna, is approaching.

sn: आख्यानमिन्द्रविजयं य इदं नियतः पठेत्। धूतपाप्मा जितस्वर्गः परत्रेह च मोदते॥
en: He who constantly reads this story of the victory of Indra becomes free from (the effects of) his crimes and goes to heaven and passes his life pleasantly in this world and in another.

sn: न चारिजं भयं तस्य नापुत्रो वा भवेन्नरः। नापदं प्राप्नुयात् कांचिदं दीर्घमायुश्च विन्दति। सर्वत्र जयमाप्नोति न कदाचित् पराजयम्॥
en: He need not have any fear from his enemy and he will never become sonless. He will never meet with any danger and he will live a long life. Everywhere he will get victories and seldom defeat.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमाश्वासितो राजा शल्येन भरतर्षभ। पूजयामास विधिवच्छल्यं धर्मभृतां वरः॥
en: Vaishampayana said The king being thus encouraged by Shalya, O you best of the race of Bharata, that chief among the supporters of virtue did due honours to Shalya.

sn: श्रुत्वा तु शल्यवचनं कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः। प्रत्युवाच महाबाहुर्मद्रराजमिदं वचः॥
en: And Yudhishthira, the son of Kunti, having heard the speech of Shalya, said these words in reply to the king of Madra of long arms.

sn: भवान् कर्णस्य सारथ्यं करिष्यति न संशयः। तत्र तेजोवधः कार्यः कर्णस्यार्जुनसंस्तवः॥
en: The post of charioteer of Karna will be field by you no doubt and from that position shall you destroy the spirit of Karna by chanting the glories of Arjuna.

sn: शल्य उवाच एवमेतत् करिष्यामि यथा मां सम्प्रभाषसे। यच्चान्यदपि शक्ष्यामि तत् करिष्याम्यहं तव।॥
en: Shalya said I shall do this, even as you dictate to me; and whatever else that I am able to do I shall do for you.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततस्त्वामन्त्र्य कौन्तेयाञ्छल्यो मद्राधिपस्तदा। जगाम सबलः श्रीमान् दुर्योधनमरिंदम॥
en: Vaishampayana said The ruler of Madra, Shalya, having bade farewell to the sons of Kunti, that beautiful man went with his army to Duryodhana, O subduer of foes.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच युयुधानस्ततो वीरः सात्वतानां महारथः। महता चतुरङ्गेण बलेनागाद् युधिष्ठिरम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Then did the hero Yuyudhana of the Satvata race, of great prowess, come to Yudhishthira with a large army containing all the four elements.

sn: तस्य योधा महावीर्या नानादेशसमागताः। नानाप्रहरणा वीराः शोभयाञ्चक्रिरे बलम्॥
en: His warriors of great strength, came from many countries and heroes, holding many suits of weapons, beautified the army.

sn: परश्वधैर्भिन्दिपालैः शूलतोमरमुद्गरैः। परिधैर्यष्टिभिः पाशैः करवालैश्च निर्मलैः॥ खगकार्मुकनियूँहैः शरैश्च विविधैरपि। तैलधौतैः प्रकाशद्भिसदाऽशोभत वै बलम्॥
en: That army was ever beautiful for it had in it, battle axes, missiles, spears, lances, mallets, clubs, staves, cords, stainless, swords and daggers and arrows of various kinds all of the best sort.

sn: तस्य मेघप्रकाशस्य सौवर्णैः शोभितस्य च। बभूव रूपं सैन्यस्य मेघस्येव सविद्युतः॥
en: The appearance of that army with those weapons was like the clouds with lightning.

sn: अक्षौहिणी तु सा सेना तदा यौधिष्ठिरं बलम्। प्रविश्यान्तर्दधे राजन् सागरं कुनदी यथा॥
en: And that army, numbering an Akshauhini when it became incorporated with Yudhishthira's army, vanished as it were, O king, as does a small river when it falls into the sea.

sn: तथैवाक्षौहिणी गृह्य चेदीनामृषभो बली। धृष्टकेतुरुपागच्छत् पाण्डवानमितौजसः॥
en: And in the same way did Dhrishtaketu, who was powerful as the best of the Chedis come with an army, an Akshauhini in number, to the Pandavas, of immeasurable strength.

sn: मागधश्च जयत्सेनो जारासन्धिर्महाबलः। अक्षौहिण्यैव सैन्यस्य धर्मराजमुपागमत्॥
en: And Jayatsena of great strength, son of Jarasandh, king of Magadha, came to the virtuous king with an army counting an Akshauhini.

sn: तथैव पाण्ड्यो राजेन्द्र सागरानूपवासिभिः। वृतो बहुविधैर्योधैर्युधिष्ठिरमुपागमत्॥
en: In the same way, Pandya, O chief among kings, came to Yudhishthira surrounded by many warriors who had colonized along the sea.

sn: तस्य सैन्यमतीवासीत् तस्मिन् बलसमागमे। प्रेक्षणीयतरं राजन् सुवेषं बलवत् तदा॥
en: And all his troops being assembled, the army with its fine dress and which was very strong became an object worth seeing, O chief among kings.

sn: दुपदस्याप्यभूत् सेना नानादेशसमागतैः। शोभिता पुरुषैः शूरैः पुत्रैश्चास्य महारथैः॥
en: And the army of the king of Drupada, assembled from several countries, was graced by heroic men and also by his sons of wonderful valour.

sn: तथैव राजा मत्स्यानां विराटो वाहिनीपतिः। पर्वतीयैर्महीपालैः सहितः पाण्डवानियात्॥
en: In the same way did Virata, the king of the Matsya, the leader of an army come to the sons of Pandu, accompanied by a large body of soldiers, inhabiting hilly tracts.

sn: इतश्चेतश्च पाण्डूनां समाजग्मुर्महात्मनाम्। अक्षौहिण्यस्तु सप्तैता विविधध्वजसंकुलाः॥ युयुत्समानाः कुरुभिः पाण्डवान् समहर्षयन्।
en: And from several directions came for the noble minded sons of Pandu seven Akshauhini carrying flags of various sorts. All of them were desirous a fight with the sons of Kuru and so caused the sons of Pandu to rejoice.

sn: तथैव धार्तराष्ट्रस्य हर्षं समभिवर्धयन्॥ भगदत्तो महीपालः सेनामक्षौहिणीं ददौ। तस्य चीनैः किरातैश्च काञ्चनैरिव संवृतम्॥ बभौ बलमनाधृष्यं कर्णिकारवनं यथा।
en: In the same way increasing the delight of the son of Dhritarashtra, the king Bhagadatta gave army numbering an Akshauhini. And the army was filled with Chins and Kiratas as also with gold. The invulnerable army looked beautiful like a forest of Karnikaras.

sn: तथा भूरिश्रवाः शूरः शल्यश्च कुरुनन्दन॥ दुर्योधनमुपायातावक्षौहिण्या पृथक् पृथक्।
en: In the same way, Bhurishravas and the hero Shalya, O son of Kuru, went to Duryodhana, each with an army counting an Akshauhini separately.

sn: कृतवर्मा च हार्दिक्यो भोजान्धकुकुरैः सह॥ अक्षौहिण्यैव सेनाया दुर्योधनमुपागमत्।
en: Kritavarman, the son of Hridika in company with the Bhojas, the Andhak and the Kukuras, went to Duryodhana with an Akshauhini of troops.

sn: तस्य तैः पुरुषव्याप्रैर्वनमालाधरैर्बलम्॥ अशोभत यथा मत्तैर्वनं प्रक्रीडितैर्गजैः।
en: His army, with those foremost among men, graced with garlands of wild flowers, looked charming as a forest run about by wild elephants.

sn: जयद्रथमुखाश्चान्ये सिन्धुसौवीरवासिनः॥ आजग्मुः पृथिवीपालाः कम्पयन्त इवाचलान्।
en: And others, the people of Sindhu Sauvira, under the leadership of Jayadratha and also other rulers of the earth, came as if shaking the mountains.

sn: तेषामक्षौहिणी सेना बहुला विबभौ तदा॥ विधूयमानो वातेन बहुरूप इवाम्बुदः।
en: And their large army looked beautiful at that time like various sorts of clouds shaken by the winds.

sn: सुदक्षिणश्च काम्बोजो यवनैश्च शकैस्तथा॥ उपाजगाम कौरव्यमक्षौहिण्या विशाम्पते। तस्य सेनासमावायः शलभानामिवाबभौ॥ स च सम्प्राप्य कौरव्यं तत्रैवान्तर्दधे तदा।
en: Oking! Sudakshina, the ruler of Kamboja with the Yavanas and the Shakas came to the son of Kuru, with an Akshauhini of troops. His army looked beautiful like locusts. And having entered the Kaurava army it vanished at the time.

sn: तथा माहिष्मतीवासी नीलो नीलायुधैः सह॥ महीपालो महावीर्यैर्दक्षिणापथवासिभिः।
en: So did Nila, the resident of Mahishmati, a king of great strength along with the residents of the southern countries with blue weapons.

sn: आवन्त्यौ च महीपालौ महाबलसुसंवृतौ॥ पृथगक्षौहिणीभ्यां तावभियातौ सुयोधनम्।
en: And so did the two kings of Avanti surrounded by large forces, each with an Akshauhini of troops came to Suyodhana.

sn: केकयाश्च नरव्याघ्राः सोदर्याः पञ्च पार्थिवाः॥ सहर्षयन्तः कौरव्यमक्षौहिण्या समाद्रवन्।
en: The five rulers of the earth, the sons of the same mother, the best among men, the Kaikeya princes, causing delight to the son of Kuru, came there with an Akshauhini.

sn: ततस्ततस्तु सर्वेषां भूमिपानां महात्मनाम्॥ तिस्रोऽन्याः समवर्तन्त वाहिन्यो भरतर्षभ।
en: O you foremost among the race of Bharata, from the large minded kings of other countries, there came three other armies.

sn: एवमेकादशावृत्ताः सेना दुर्योधनस्य ताः॥ युयुत्समानाः कौन्तेयान् नानाध्वजसमाकुलाः।
en: In this way Duryodhana was surrounded by an army eleven Akshauhinis strong. All of them were desirous of a fight with the sons of Kunti and filled with banners of various sorts.

sn: न हास्तिनपुरे राजन्नवकाशोऽभवत् तदा॥ राज्ञां स्वबलमुख्यानां प्राधान्येनापि भारत।
en: Oking, In the city of Hastinapura, there was not space, even for the principal leaders of the king's own army.

sn: ततः पञ्चनदं चैव कृत्स्नं च कुरुजाङ्गलम्॥ तथा रोहितकारण्य मरुभूमिश्च केवला। अहिच्छत्रं कालकूटं गङ्गाकूलं च भारत॥ वारणं वाटधानं च यामुनश्चैव पर्वतः। एष देश: सुविस्तीर्णः प्रभूतधनधान्यवान्॥
en: O son of Bharata, for this reason the country of the five rivers, Krishna, Kurujangala and the forest of Rohitaka and the desert of Kevala and Ahichhatra and Kalakuta and the bank of the Ganges and Varana and Vatadhana and the mountains of Yamuna, all these extensive tracts containing large quantities of corn and wealth became exceedingly crowded with the army of the Kauravas.

sn: बभूव कौरवेयाणां बलेनातीव संवृतः। तत्र सैन्यं तथा युक्तं ददर्श स पुरोहितः॥ यः स पाञ्चालराजेन प्रेषितः कौरवान् प्रति॥
en: There the priest saw the army of this description-the priest who was sent by the king of Panchala to the Kauravas.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच स च कौरव्यमासाद्य द्रुपदस्य पुरोहितः। सत्कृतो धृतराष्ट्रेण भीष्मेण विदुरेण च॥
en: Vaishampayana said The priest of Drupada, having arrived near the son of Kuru, was greeted by Dhritarashtra, Bhishma and Vidura.

sn: सर्वं कौशल्यमुक्त्वाऽऽदौ पृष्ट्वा चैवमनामयम्। सर्वसेनाप्रणेतृणां मध्ये वाक्यमुवाच ह॥
en: Having asked him if everything were well with him and also made enquiries about his health in the midst of all the leaders of his army he said these words.

sn: सर्वैर्भवद्भिर्विदितो राजधर्मः सनातनः। वाक्योपादानहेतोस्तु वक्ष्यामि विदिते सति॥
en: It is known to all, what the duty of a king is as it obtains since a long period back, but through known, yet shall I speak, as a preface to my speech proper.

sn: धृतराष्ट्रश्च पाण्डुश्च सुतावेकस्य विश्रुतौ। तयोः समानं द्रविणं पैतृकं नात्र संशयः॥
en: It is known that Dhritarashtra and Pandu are the sons of one and their paternal kingdom must be shared by them equally-there is no doubt about it.

sn: धृतराष्ट्रस्य ये पुत्राः प्राप्तः तैः पैतृकं वसु। पाण्डुपुत्राः कथं नाम न प्राप्ताः पैतृकं वसु॥
en: Those who are the sons of Dhritarashtra have obtained the position of their father why have not the sons of Pandu obtained the paternal kingdom?

sn: एवंगते पाण्डवेयैर्विदितं वः पुरा यथा। न प्राप्तं पैतृकं द्रव्यं धृतराष्ट्रेण संवृतम्॥
en: It is known to you, how in former days, the sons of Pandu, did not obtain their ancestral wealth which was wrested from them by the son of Dhritarashtra.

sn: प्राणान्तिकैरप्युपायैः प्रयतद्भिरनेकशः। शेषवन्तो न शकिता नेतुं वै यमसादनम्॥
en: They sought (to remove them) by several means, calculated even to bring their lives to an end, but they have not yet reached the termination's of their lives, so they were unable to send them to the palace of the king of Death (Yama).

sn: पुनश्च वर्धितं राज्यं स्वबलेन महात्मभिः। छद्मनापहृतं क्षुदैर्धार्तराष्ट्रैः ससौबलैः॥
en: Then again, the kingdom gained by the noble-minded ones through their own strength was taken away from them by a trick by the mean sons of Dhritarashtra united with the son of Subala.

sn: तदप्यनुमतं कर्म यथायुक्तमनेन वै। वासिताश्च महारण्ये वर्षाणीह त्रयोदश॥
en: Even this act, undesirable as it was, approved of by him and they lived for thirteen years in the great forest.

sn: सभायां क्लेशितैवीरैः सहभायैस्तथा भृशम्। अरण्येविविधा: क्लेशाः सम्प्राप्तास्तैः सुदारुणाः।।१०
en: In the court too serious troubles were experienced by the heroes along with their wife and in the forest diverse troubles of great magnitude were met with by them.

sn: तथा विराटनगरे योन्यन्तरगतैरिव। प्राप्तः परमसंक्लेशो यथा पापैर्महात्मभिः॥
en: And in the same way in the town of Virata, hard troubles were met with by the large minded ones as great pains are endured by wicked souls, when they transmigrate into other beings.

sn: ते सर्वं पृष्ठतः कृत्वा तत् सर्वं पूर्वकिल्बिषम्। सामैव कुरुभिः सार्धमिच्छन्ति कुरुपुङ्गवाः॥
en: Forgetting all these troubles gone through by them in past times those foremost, among the race of Kuru, are desirous of peace with the son of Kuru.

sn: तेषां च वृत्तमाज्ञाय वृत्तं दुर्योधनस्य च। अनुनेतुमिहार्हन्ति धार्तराष्ट्र सुहृज्जनाः॥
en: Knowing their nature and the nature of Duryodhana, the well wishers (of the letter) should, properly speaking on this occasion, lead the son of Dhritarashtra (to an amicable settlement).

sn: न हि ते विग्रहं वीराः कुर्वन्ति कुरुभिः सह। अविनाशेन लोकस्य काइक्षन्ते पाण्डवाः स्वकम्॥१४।
en: These heroes do not (want to) wage war with the son of Kuru. The sons of Pandu do not want (to get back) their own by ruining the world.

sn: यश्चापि धार्तराष्ट्रस्य हेतुः स्याद् विग्रहं प्रति। स च हेतुर्न मन्तव्यो बलीयांसस्तथा हि ते॥
en: The reason, which the son of Dhritarashtra brings forward for war, cannot be regarded as a reason for they are the stronger.

sn: अक्षौहिण्यश्च सप्तैव धर्मपुत्रस्य संगताः। युयुत्समानाः कुरुभिः प्रतीक्षन्तेऽस्य शासनम्॥
en: Seven Akshauhinis have been collected for the son of Dharma (Yudhishthira), they all desirous of fighting with the sons of Kuru, are waiting for his permission.

sn: अपरे पुरुषव्याघ्राः सहस्राक्षौहिणीसमाः। सात्यकिर्भीमसेनश्च यमौ च सुमहाबलौ॥
en: There are others, best among men, who are, each of them equal to thousand Akshauhinis-for instance, the son of Satyaki, Bhimasena and the twin brothers of very great strength.

sn: एकादशैताः पृतना एकतश्च समागताः। एकतश्च महाबाहुर्बहुरूपी धनंजयः॥
en: On one side are united those eleven (Akshauhinis) and on the other, Dhananjaya of great strength and of many forms.

sn: यथा किरीटी सर्वाभ्यः सेनाब्यो व्यतिरिच्यते। एवमेव महाबाहुर्वासुदेवो महाद्युतिः॥
en: An Kiritin suppress the entire army, so does Vasudeva of long arms and of great luster.

sn: बहुलत्वं च सेनानां विक्रमं च किरीटिनः। बुद्धिमत्त्वं च कृष्णस्य बुद्ध्वा युध्येत को नरः॥
en: What man will fight against an army superior in number, the prowess of Kiritin and the wisdom of Krishna.

sn: ते भवन्तो यथाधर्मं यथासमयमेव च। प्रयच्छन्तु प्रदातव्यं मा व: कालोऽत्यगादयम्॥
en: Therefore do you, as dictated by virtue and as agreed to in the stipulation, give back that which should be returned. Don't you let this opportunity.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा प्रज्ञावृद्धो महाद्युतिः। सम्पूज्यैनं यथाकालं भीष्मो वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having heard these words of his, Bhishma, of great luster and old in wisdom, did him due honours and spoke these words to him as suited the occasion.

sn: दिष्ट्या कुशलिन: सर्वे सह दामोदरेण ते। दिष्ट्या सहायवन्तश्चदिष्ट्या धर्मे च ते रताः॥
en: It is lucky that they all along with Damodara are doing well; it is lucky that have secured aid and it is lucky that they are intent on acting virtuously.

sn: दिष्ट्या च संधिकामास्ते भ्रातरः कुरुनन्दनाः। दिष्ट्या न युद्धमनसः पाण्डवाः सह बान्धवैः॥
en: And it is lucky that our cousins, the sons of Kuru, desire peace, it is lucky that the sons of Pandu are not desirous of war with their relations.

sn: भवता सत्यमुक्तं तु सर्वमेतन्न संशयः। अतितीक्ष्णं तु ते वाक्यं ब्राह्मण्यादिति मे मतिः॥
en: Truth has been spoken by you; it is so; no doubt your words are very sharp; in my opinion that is so because you are a Brahmana.

sn: असंशयं क्लेशितास्ते वने चेह च पाण्डवाः। प्राप्ताश्च धर्मतः सर्वं पितुर्धनमसंशयम्॥
en: Kiritin the son of Pritha is strong, well coached in handling weapons and of mighty prowess; who is there to stand against Dhananjaya the son of Pandu?

sn: किरीटी बलवान् पार्थः कृतास्त्रश्च महारथः। को हि पाण्डुसुतं युद्धे विषहेत धनंजयम्॥
en: These sons, of Pandu, have doubtless borne much troubles here and in the forest and rightly speaking they are doubtless entitled to the wealth of their fathers.

sn: अपि वज्रधरः साक्षात् किमुतान्ये धनुर्भृतः। त्रयाणामपि लोकानां समर्थ इति मे मतिः॥
en: Even the holder of the thunderbolt himself (cannot withstand him) how can others bearing the bow? He is capable of standing against the three worlds; this is my opinion.

sn: भीष्मे ब्रुवति तद् वाक्यं धृष्टमाक्षिप्य मन्युना। दुर्योधनं समालोक्य कर्णो वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: While Bhishma was speaking Karna, having interrupted his words in anger and insolence and looking at Duryodhana, said-

sn: न तत्राविदितं ब्रह्माल्लोके भूतेन केनचित्। पुनरुक्तेन किं तेन भाषितेन पुनः पुनः॥
en: Brahmana, what you say is not unknown in this world nor by any being; why do you repeat it again and again?

sn: दुर्योधनार्थं शकुनि ते निर्जितवान् पुरा। समयेन गतोऽरण्यं पाण्डुपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: In days of old, Shakuni on behalf of Duryodhana defeated (Yudhishthira) at a game of dice and it was according to a stipulation that Yudhishthira the son of Pandu went to the forest.

sn: स तं समयमाश्रित्य राज्यं नेच्छति पैतृकम्। बलमाश्रित्य मत्स्यानां पञ्चालानां च मूर्खवत्॥
en: He now, like a fool disregarding that stipulation, wants his paternal wealth depending on the armies supplied him by the Matsyas and by the king of Panchala.

sn: दुर्योधनो भयाद् विद्वन् न दद्यात् पादमन्ततः। धर्मतस्तु महीं कृत्स्नां प्रदद्याच्छत्रवेऽपि च॥
en: O learned one, Duryodhana will not yield even one foot of ground through fear, but responding to the call of virtue he will yield even the entire world to his enemy.

sn: यदि काक्षन्ति ते राज्यं पितृपैतामहं पुनः। यथाप्रतिज्ञं कालं तं चरन्तु वनमाश्रिताः॥
en: If they want back the kingdom of their forefathers let them, as stipulated, reside in the forest to the end of the period (agreed on).

sn: ततो दुर्योधनस्याङ्के वर्तन्तामकुतोभयाः। अधार्मिकी तु मा बुद्धि मौात् कुर्वन्तु केवलात्।।१४।
en: Then may they come to seek refuse with Duryodhana without any fear; let them not through folly adopt an unrighteous course,

sn: अथ ते धर्ममुत्सृज्य युद्धमिच्छन्ति पाण्डवाः। आसाद्येमान् कुरुश्रेष्ठान् स्मरिष्यन्ति वचो मम॥
en: If the sons of Pandu, bidding adieu to a righteous course, desire war, then will they, after coming face to face with these foremost among the race of Kurus, have occasion to remember my words.

sn: भीष्म उवाच किं नु राधेय वाचा ते कर्म तत् स्मर्तुमर्हसि। एक एव यदा पार्थः षड्रस्थाञ्जितवान् युधि॥
en: Bhishma said O son of Radha, why do you talk so much? It is fitting that you should remember his deeds; alone the son of Pritha vanquished in battle six charioteers.

sn: बहुशो जीयमानस्य कर्म दृष्टं तदैव ते। न चेदेवं करिष्यामो यदयं ब्राह्मणोऽब्रवीत्। ध्रुवं यधि हतास्तेन भक्षयिष्याम पांसुकान्॥
en: You have seen the deeds of him who had been victories on many occasions; if we do not do what this Brahmana has said most certainly shall we be killed by him.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच धृतराष्ट्रस्ततो भीष्ममनुमान्य प्रसाद्य च। अवभय॑ च राधेयमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Then Dhritarashtra, having pleased Bhishma by approving of his words and having rebuked the son of Radha, said these words.

sn: अस्मद्धितं वाक्यमिदं भीष्मः शान्तनवोऽब्रवीत्। पाण्डवानां हितं चैव सर्वस्य जगतस्तथा॥
en: What Bhishma, the son of Shantanu, has said is calculated to promote sur interests and those of the entire world.

sn: चिन्तयित्वा तु पार्थेभ्यः प्रेषयिष्यामि संजयम्। स भवान् प्रति यात्वद्य पाण्डवानेव मा चिरम्॥
en: After mature deliberation, shall I send Sanjaya to the sons of Pritha, therefore do you go back at once this day to the sons of Pandu.

sn: स तं सत्कृत्य कौरव्यः प्रेषयामास पाण्डवान्। सभामध्ये समाहूय संजयं वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
en: And the son of Kuru, having done him honours, sent him to the sons of Pandu and having summoned Sanjaya to the council, said these words.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच प्राप्तानाहुः संजय पाण्डपुत्रानुपप्लव्ये तान् विजानीहि गत्वा। अजातशत्रु च समाजयेथा दिष्ट्याऽऽनह्य स्थानमुपस्थितस्त्वम्॥
en: Dhritarashtra said It is said, O Sanjaya, that the sons of Pandu have reached Upaplavya; going out do you find out (if) this (is true), do due honours to the one who has created no enemies (Yudhishthira); it is fortunate that you are present here.

sn: सर्वान् वदेः संजय स्वस्तिमन्तः कृच्छ्रे वासमतदर्हान् निरुष्य। तेषां शान्तिर्विद्यतेऽस्मासु शीघ्रं मिथ्यापेतानामुपकारिणां सताम्॥
en: To all do you, O Sanjaya, communicate our well being. Having resided in the forest and met with troubles, they who are inclined to do good to others without deceit and honest still entertain friendly feeling towards us.

sn: नाहं क्वचित् संजय पाण्डवानां मिथ्यावृत्ति काञ्चन जात्वपश्यम्। सर्वां श्रियं ह्यात्मवीर्येण लब्धां पर्याकार्षुः पाण्डवा मह्यमेव॥
en: Never did I, O Sanjaya, observe any falsehood in the sons of Pandu. Having gained all their wealth through sheer strength of their own, have they made over the same to me.

sn: दोषं ह्येषां नाध्यगच्छं परीच्छन् नित्यं कंचिद् येन ग¥य पार्थान्। धर्मार्थाभ्यां कर्म कुर्वन्ति नित्यं सुखप्रिये नानुरुध्यन्ति कामात्॥
en: Never did I observe any questionable act in them. Though I was always on the look-out, yet never did I find anything done by these sons of Pritha for which we could blame them. They always work for the sake of virtue and their own interests and never request others for : their own well being.

sn: धर्मं शीतं क्षुत्पिपासे तथैव निद्रां तन्द्रीं क्रोधहर्षो प्रमादम्। धृत्या चैव प्रज्ञया चाभिभूय धर्मार्थयोगात् प्रयतन्ति पार्थाः॥
en: Having by their patience and wisdom subjugated heat, cold, hunger, thirst, sleep, laziness anger, pleasure and folly, the sons of Pritha always try for virtue and their own interests.

sn: त्यजन्ति मित्रेषु धनानि काले न संवासाज्जीर्यति तेषु मैत्री। स्तेषां द्वेष्टा नास्त्याजमीढस्य पक्षे॥
en: On suitable occasions, do they give away wealth to their friends and friendship with them does not decrease through long residence together. The sons of Pritha honour others and promote their interest according to their deserts. They have no haters in the side of Ajmida.

sn: दुर्योधनात् क्षुद्रतराच्च कर्णात्। तेषां हीमो हीनसुखप्रियाणां महात्मनां संजनयतो हि तेजः॥
en: Except the great weak-minded fool, Duryodhana and the still meaner Karna. These two alone are increasing the energy of these large-minded souls who do not desire for their own happiness.

sn: उत्थानवीर्यः सुखमेधमानो दुर्योधनः सुकृतं मन्यते तत्। तेषां भागं यच्च मन्येत बाल: शक्यं हर्तुं जीवतां पाण्डवानाम्॥
en: Duryodhana who is strong in the beginning only and who is accustomed to every sort of indulgence thinks that he does well (increasing their energy). The boy thinks too that he is capable of robbing the living son of Pandu, of their share.

sn: यस्यार्जुनः पदवीं केशवश्च वृकोदरः सात्यकोऽजातशत्रोः। माद्रीपुत्रौ सृजयाश्चापि यान्ति पुरा युद्धात् साधु तस्य प्रदानम्॥
en: He who is followed by Arjuna, Keshava, Vrikodara, Satyaki, the two sons of Madri (Nakula and Sahadeva) and Sanjaya; it is best to give up his share before the war.

sn: स ह्येवैकः पृथिवीं सव्यसाची गाण्डीवधन्वा प्रणुदेद् रथस्थः। तथा जिष्णुः केशवोऽप्यप्रधृष्यो लोकत्रयस्याधिपतिर्महात्मा।॥
en: Savyasachin, holding the Gandiva bow is alone capable of subjugating the ear from his chariot and in the same way is the nobleminded Keshava, accustomed to got victories and unapproachable, the ruler of the three worlds.

sn: तिष्ठेत कस्तस्य मर्त्यः पुरस्ताद् यः सर्वलोकेषु वरेण्य एकः। पर्जन्यघोषान् प्रवपञ्छरौघान् पतङ्गसङ्घानिव शीघ्रवेगान्॥
en: In all the worlds, he is the only worthy man. What man could stand against his flight of arrows which roar like the clouds and which fly with the swiftness of locusts.

sn: दिशं धुंदीचीमपि चोत्तरान् कुरून् गाण्डीवधन्वैकरथो जिगाय। धनं चैषामाहरत् सव्यसाची सेनानुगान् द्रविडांश्चैव चक्रे॥
en: Seated on one car, with the help of the Gandiva bow, Savyasachin, having subjugated the Kauravas of the north and the northern country as well, took away their wealth and turned the people of Dravida into his soldier followers.

sn: यश्चैव देवान् खाण्डवे सव्यसाची गाण्डीवधन्वा प्रजिगाय सेन्द्रान्। उपाहरत् पाण्डवो जातवेदसे यशो मानं वर्धयन् पाण्डवानाम्॥
en: Savyasachin, with the help of the Govinda bow, having subjugated the gods with Indra at their head, in the Agni and thus enhanced the honour and redwing of the sons of Pandu.

sn: द्धस्त्यारोहो नास्ति समश्च तस्य। रथेऽर्जुनादाहुरहीनमेनं बाह्वोर्बलेनायुतनागवीर्यम्॥
en: There is none equal to Bhima in wielding the mace, none too equal to him in riding elephants and it is said that as a car-warrior he is not inferior to Arjuna and in strength of arms he has the prowess of ten thousand elephants.

sn: सुशिक्षितः कृतवैरस्तरस्वी दहेत् क्षुद्रांस्तरसा धार्तराष्ट्रान्। सदात्यमर्षी न बलात् स शक्यो युद्धे जेतु वासवेनापि माक्षात्॥
en: Well-trained and strong, being rendered an enemy and inspired with worth he would burn down the sons of Dhritarashtra. Being always very wrathful and strong he is incapable of being defeated even by Vasava (Indra) himself.

sn: सुचेतसौ बलिनौ शीघ्रहस्तौ सुशिक्षितौ भ्रातरौ फाल्गुनेन। श्येनौ यथा पक्षिपूगान् रुजन्तौ माद्रीपुत्रौ शेषयेतां न शत्रून्॥
en: The two brothers, the sons of the king of Madri, of good heart, strong quick-handed and well trained by the sons of Falguna, will leave no vestige of the enemies as a pair of birds of prey destroy a flight of birds.

sn: एतद् बलं पूर्णमस्माकमेवं यत् सत्यं तान् प्राप्य नास्तीति मन्ये। तेषां मध्ये वर्तमानस्तरस्वी धृष्टद्युम्नः पाण्डवानामिहैकः॥
en: I regard this vast army of ours, as being not in existence, when it encounters them. Among them is the powerful Dhrishtadyumna who is regarded as one of the Pandavas.

sn: सहाभात्यः सोमकानां प्रबर्हः संत्यक्तात्मा पाण्डवार्थं श्रुतो मे। अजातशत्रु प्रसहेत कोऽन्यो येषां स स्यादग्रणीवृष्णिसिंहः॥
en: I understand that the foremost, among the Somakas with his ministers, has devoted his soul to the cause of the sons of Pandu; who else can withstand him who has made no enemies (Yudhishthira) whose army is led by that best among the Vrishnis.

sn: सहोषितश्चरितार्थो वयस्थो मात्स्येयानामधिपो वै विराटः। स वै सपुत्रः पाण्डवार्थं च शश्वद् युधिष्ठिरं भक्त इति श्रुतं मे॥
en: Virata, the lord of the people of Matsya, who is of mature age, who has lived with the Pandavas and whose desires have been fulfilled by them, with his sons is there ever increased in the cause of the sons of Pandu and a staunch adherent of Yudhishthira.

sn: अवरुद्धा रथिनः केकयेभ्यो महेष्वासा भ्रातरः पञ्च सन्ति। केकयेभ्यो राज्यमाकाङ्क्षमाणा युद्धार्थनश्चानवसन्ति पार्थान्।।२०
en: And the five brothers, the eminent and mighty princes of Kaikeya, have been deprived of their kingdom (by us) and they follow the sons of Pritha, desirous of the kingdom of the Kaikeyas and waiting for an opportunity of fighting (with us).

sn: सर्वांश्च वीरान् पृथिवीपतीनां समागतान् पाण्डवार्थं निविष्टान्। शूरानहं भक्तिमतः शृणोमि प्रीत्या युक्तान् संश्रितान् धर्मराजम्॥
en: And all the heroes among the lords of the Earth have been brought together and are interested in the cause of the sons of Pandu. I hear that these heroes worthy of respect have become followers of the virtuous king out of love.

sn: गिर्याश्रया दुर्गनिवासिनश्च योधाः पृथिव्यां कुलजातिशुद्धाः। म्लेच्छाश्च नानायुधवीर्यवन्तः समागताः पाण्डवार्थं निविष्टाः॥
en: Heroes who live in the hills and in fortresses, who are of good lineage in the world and aged and many Mlechas who are adepts in handling various weapons have been brought together and made interested in the cause of the sons of Pandu.

sn: पाण्ड्यश्च राजा समितीन्द्रकल्पो योधप्रवीरैर्बहुभिः समेतः। समागतः पाण्डवार्थं महात्मा लोकप्रवीरोऽप्रतिवीर्यतेजाः॥
en: And king Pandya too, in battle an equal of Indra, who is noble-minded, a hero energy, accompanied by many heroes, has come, espousing the cause of the sons of Pandu.

sn: अस्त्रं द्रोणादर्जुनाद् वासुदेवात् कृपाद् भीष्माद् येन वृतं शृणोमि। यं तं कार्ष्णिप्रतिममाहुरेकं स सात्यकिः पाण्डवार्थ निविष्टः॥
en: That Satyaki, who has learnt the use of arms from Drona, Arjuna, Vasudeva, Kripa and Bhima and who is said to be the equal of the son of Krishna, Pradyumna, is enlisted in the cause of the sons of Pandu.

sn: उपाश्रिताश्चेदिकरूपषकाश्च सर्वोद्योगैर्भूमिपालाः समेताः। तेषां मध्ये सूर्यमिवातपन्तं श्रिया वृतं चेदिपतिं ज्वलन्तम्॥
en: Formerly did assemble the kings of the Chedis and the Karushas with all their preparations and among them stood the king of Chedis, with his blazing beauty and scorching (sight) like the sun.

sn: अस्तम्भनीयं युधि मन्यमानो ज्यां कर्षतां श्रेष्ठतमं पृथिव्याम्। सर्वोत्साहं क्षत्रियाणां निहत्य प्रसह्य कृष्णस्तरसा सम्ममर्द॥
en: He was regarded as being incapable of being vanquished in battle and the foremost among all the users of the bow. Krishna at once killed him by force of his own strength and thus destroyed all the hopes of the Kshatriyas.

sn: यशोमानौ वर्धयन् पाण्डवानां पुराऽभिनच्छिशुपालं समीक्ष्य। यस्य सर्वे वर्धयन्ति स्म मानं करूषराजप्रमुखा नरेन्द्राः॥
en: In days of old did Krishna merely by looking at him (Shishupala) who was honoured by the kings, at whose head stood the king of the Karushas thereby increasing the fame and honour of the Pandavas.

sn: तमसा केशवं तत्र मत्वा सुग्रीवयुक्तेन रथेन कृष्णम्। केप्राद्रवंश्चेदिपति विहाय सिंहं दृष्ट्वा क्षुद्रमृगा इवान्ये॥
en: Seeing that Keshava was incapable of being vanquished in his chariot drawn by white horses they fled leaving the ruler of the Chedis as small animals do at the sight of a lion.

sn: दाशंसमानो द्वैरथे वासुदेवम्। तेनेवोन्मथितः कर्णिकारः॥
en: He, who out of impudence, engaged in a fight in chariots with Vasudeva, lies killed by Krishna like a Karnikara tree uprooted by the wind.

sn: पराक्रमं मे यदवेदयन्त तेषामर्थं संजय केशवस्य। र्गावल्गणे नाधिगच्छामि शान्तिम्॥
en: Remembering what has been brought to my notice regarding the might of Keshava and the deeds of Vishnu I got no peace of mind, O son of Gavalgani.

sn: न जातु ताञ्छत्रुरन्यः सहेत येषां स स्यादग्रणीवृष्णिसिंहः। प्रवेपते मे हृदयं भयेन श्रुत्वा कृष्णावेकरथे समेतौ॥
en: No enemy whatever can withstand them whose leader is that best of the Vrishnis. My heart trembles with fear at hearing that the, two Krishna's are united together on one the same chariot.

sn: स्ताभ्यां लभेच्छर्म तदा सुतो मे। मिन्द्राविष्णू दैत्यसेनां यथैव॥
en: If the dull-headed one dose not fight with these two then may my son fare well, otherwise will they burn up the Kurus as Indra and Vishnu did the army of the Daityas.

sn: मतो हि मे शक्रसमो धनंजयः सनातनो वृष्णिवीरच विष्णुः। धर्मारामो ह्रीनिषेवस्तरस्वी कुन्तीपुत्रः पाण्डवोऽजातशत्रुः॥
en: In my opinion is equal to Shakra himself and the hero of the Vrishni race is Vishnu himself. The son of Kunti has refuge in virtue, is brave and avoids shameful deeds and the son of Pandu has created no enemies.

sn: दुर्योधनेन निकृतो मनस्वी नो चेत् क्रुद्धः प्रदहेद् धार्तराष्ट्रान्। नाहं तथा हर्जुनाद् वासुदेवाद् भीमाद् वाहं यमयोर्वा बिभेमि॥
en: He. who has been banished by Duryodhana, is not evil-minded otherwise being wrathful he would have consumed all the sons of Dhritarashtra. I do not fear Arjuna, Vasudeva or even Bhima or the twins so I, in the same measure, fear.

sn: यथा राज्ञः क्रोधदीप्तस्य सूत मन्योरहं भीततरः सदैव। महातपा ब्रह्मचर्येण युक्तः संकल्पोऽयं मानसस्तस्य सिद्ध्येत्॥
en: The wrath of the king, O Suta, when he is angry; having practiced great austerities and Brahmacharya vows his desire will be fulfilled.

sn: तस्य क्रोधं संजयाह समीक्ष्य स्थाने जानन् भृशमस्म्यद्य भीतः। स गच्छ शीघ्रं प्रहितो रथेन पाञ्चालराजस्य चमूनिवेशनम्॥
en: Seeing his wrath and knowing that the cause is just, I am now very much afraid, therefore as an emissary from me do you quickly go to the encampment of the king of Panchala on a swift-going car.

sn: अजातशत्रु कुशलं स्म पृच्छेः पुनः पुनः प्रीतियुक्तं वदेस्त्वम्। जनार्दनं चापि समेत्य तात महामात्रं वीर्यवतामुदारम्॥
en: Repeatedly will you ask him who has created no enemies in affectionate terms about his health; and going, O son, near Janardana also, who is possessed of great qualities, heroic and noble-minded.

sn: धृतराष्ट्रः पाण्डवैः शान्तिमीप्सुः। न तस्य किंचिद् वचनं न कुर्यात् कुन्तीपुत्रो वासुदेवस्य सूत॥
en: Will you ask about his welfare, on my behalf and say that Dhritarashtra is desirous of peace with the sons of Pandu. There is request of that the son of Kunti will not comply with, O Suta.

sn: प्रियश्चैषामात्मसमश्च कृष्णो विद्वांश्चैषां कर्मणि नित्ययुक्तः। समानीतान् पाण्डवान् सृजयांश्च जनार्दनं युयुधानं विराटम्॥
en: Krishna is as dear to them as their own selves and being wise he is ever engaged in their. Also of the assembled sons of Pandu and the Srinjayas and Janardana and Yuyudhana and Virata,

sn: अनामयं मद्वचनेन पृच्छेः सर्वांस्तथा द्रौपदेयांश्च पञ्च। स्त्वं मन्येथा भारतानां हितं च। तद् भाषेथाः संजय राजमध्ये न मूर्च्छयेद् यन्न च युद्धहेतुः॥
en: Will you enquire about their health on my behalf and in the same way of the five sons of Draupadi, And whatever you think fit to be said to the foe, as occasion arises and also whatever you think to be conducive the interests of the race of Bharata must you say, O Sanjaya, among those kings. And do not utter anything which may give cause for hostility.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच राज्ञस्तु वचनं श्रुत्वा धृतराष्ट्रस्य संजयः। उपप्लव्यं ययौ द्रष्टुं पाण्डवानमितौजसः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Sanjaya, having heard the words of king Dhritarashtra, to Upaplavya to see the sons of Pandu of illimitable strength.

sn: स तु राजानमासाद्य कुन्तीपुत्रं युधिष्ठिरम्। अभिवाद्य ततः पूर्वं सूतपुत्रोऽभ्यभाषत॥
en: And having reached the presence of king Yudhishthira the son of Kunti, the son of Suta (caste) first made his obeisance and then said-

sn: रजातशत्रुमवदत् प्रतीतः। दिष्ट्या राजंस्त्वामरोगं प्रपश्ये सहायवन्तं च महेन्द्रकल्पम्॥
en: And Sanjaya the son of Gavalgana and the son of a Suta (caste) cheerfully said to him who had created no enemies. It is fortunate, O king, that I see you without decease, having friends and equal to the great Indra.

sn: अनामयं पृच्छति त्वाऽऽम्बिकेयो वृद्धो राजा धृतराष्ट्रो मनीषी। कच्चिद् भीमः कुशली पाण्डवाग्र्यो धनंजयस्तौ च माद्रीतनूजौ॥
en: The aged and wise king Dhritarashtra the son of Ambika, asks about your health. Is Bhima the foremost among the sons of Pandu well and is Dhananjaya so are these two sons of the king of Madri,

sn: कच्चित् कृष्णा द्रौपदी राजपुत्री सत्यव्रता वीरपत्नी सपुत्रा। मिष्टान् कामान् भारत स्वस्तिकामः॥
en: How is the princess Krishna, the daughter of Drupada, who is truthful, wife of a hero, with her sons, that spirited lady for whose benefit you pray for (the accomplishment of your fondest wishes) O son of Bharata, O you of good desires?

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच गावल्गणे संजय स्वागतं ते प्रीयामहे ते वयं दर्शनेन। अनामयं प्रतिजाने तवाहं सहानुजै:कुशली चास्मि विद्वन्॥
en: Yudhishthira said O son of Gavalgana, O Sanjaya, you are welcome. We are delighted at seeing you. In return to know about your health. I am well with my younger brothers. O you learned man.

sn: चिरादिदं कुशलं भारतस्य श्रुत्वा राज्ञः कुरुवृद्धस्य सूत। मन्ये साक्षाद् दृष्टमहं नरेन्द्र दृष्ट्वैव त्वां संजय प्रीतियोगात्॥
en: Having after a long time, heard the news of the health of the aged king of the Kurus, O Suta and having seen you, O Sanjaya, am I so pleased that regard as having seen the king himself.

sn: पितामहो नः स्थविरो मनस्वी महाप्राज्ञः सर्वधर्मोपपन्नः। स कौरव्यः कुशली तात भीष्मो यथापूर्वं वृत्तिरस्त्यस्य कच्चित्॥
en: Our grandsire is aged, wise, great in wisdom and endued with every virtue. Is this Bhishma, the son of Kunti, in health? Is he of the same habits, as in days of old?

sn: कच्चिद् राजा धृतराष्ट्रः सपुत्रो वैचित्रवीर्यः कुशली महात्मा। महाराजो बाह्निकः प्रातिपेयः कच्चिद् विद्वान् कुशली सूतपुत्र॥
en: Is the large-minded king Dhritarashtra, the son of Vichitravirya, well along with his sons. Is the great king Balhika, the son of Pratipa, O you learned son of Suta (caste).

sn: स सोमदत्तः कुशली तात कच्चिद् भूरिश्रवाः सत्यसंधः शलश्च। द्रोणः सपुत्रश्च कृपश्च विप्रो महेष्वासाः कच्चिदेतेऽप्यरोगाः॥
en: Is Somadatta, well? How are Bhurishrava, Satyasandha, Shalya, Drona and Kripa, the twice born with his sons, all endued with great qualities? How are these? Are they without illness?

sn: सर्वे कुरुभ्यः स्पृहयन्ति संजय धनुर्धरा ये पृथिव्या प्रधानाः। महाप्राज्ञाः सर्वशास्त्रावदाता धनुर्भूता मुख्यतमाः पृथिव्याम्॥
en: All the foremost bowmen in the world have, O Sanjaya, side with the Kurus and so have the foremost of all those who are endued with great wisdom and know all sciences and can wield the bow in the world.

sn: कच्चिन्मानं तात लभन्त एते धनुर्भूतः कच्चिदेतेऽप्यरोगाः। येषां राष्ट्रे निवसति दर्शनीयो महेष्वासः शीलवान् द्रोणपुत्रः॥
en: Do these wielders of the bow get honours? Are they without disease in whose kingdom worth seeing lives the well-behaved son of Drona endued with great qualities?

sn: महाप्राज्ञो राजपुत्रो युयुत्सुः। कर्णोऽमात्यः कुशली तात कच्चित् सुयोधनो यस्य मन्दो विधेयः॥
