en: Is the very wise prince Yuyutsu, the son of (Dhritarashtra by) the Vaishya lady in health? Is the minister Karna in health whose advice the dull-headed Suyodhana follows?

sn: स्त्रियो वृद्धा भारतानां जनन्यो महानस्यो दासभार्याश्च सूत। वध्वः पुत्रा भागिनेया भगिन्यो दौहित्रा वा कच्चिदप्यव्यलीकाः॥
en: Are the aged ladies the mothers of the sons of Bharata and the slave-wives of the great one, O Suta and daughter-in law, sons, sister' sons and daughter' sons in peace?

sn: कच्चिद् राजा ब्राह्मणानां यथावत् प्रवर्तते पूर्ववत् तात वृत्तिम्। कच्चिद् दायान् मामकान् धार्तराष्ट्रो द्विजातीनां संजय नोपहन्ति॥
en: Dose the king grant suitable annuities to the Brahmanas as in former days? Have the sons of Dhritarashtra discontinued the annuities granted by me the twice-born, O Sanjaya?

sn: कच्चिद् राजा धृतराष्ट्रः सपुत्र उपेक्षते ब्राह्मणातिक्रमान् वै। मुपेक्षते तेषु सदैव वृत्तिम्॥
en: Dose the king Dhritarashtra, with his sons, treat with contempt the Brahmanas when they commit breaches of law? Dose he treat with lightness the provision for Brahmanas which is the road to heaven?

sn: एतज्ज्योतिश्चोत्तमं जीवलोके शुक्लं प्रजानां विहितं विधात्रा। ते चेद् दोषं न नियच्छन्ति मन्दा: कृत्स्नोनाशो भविता कौरवाणाम्॥
en: This light has been instituted by Providence for the good of beings in this world. If those dull-headed ones do not treat with forbearance their short-comings will the sons of Kuru meet with ruin.

sn: कच्चिद् राजा धृतराष्ट्रः सपुत्रो बुभूषते वृत्तिममात्यवर्गे। कच्चिन्न भेदेन जिजीविषन्ति सुहृदूपा दुर्हदैश्चैकमत्यात्।।
en: Dose the king Dhritarashtra with his sons make provisions for his group of ministers. Are there no enemies in the disguise of well wishers combined for their ruin?

sn: कच्चिन्न पापं कथयन्ति तात ते पाण्डवानां कुरवः सर्व एव। द्रोणः सपुत्रश्च कृपश्च वीरो नास्मासु पापानि वदन्ति कच्चित्॥
en: Do all those sons of Kuru tall of crimes committed by the sons of Pandu? Do Drona and hero Kripa with his sons speak of our crimes.

sn: कच्चिद् राज्ये धृतराष्ट्र सपुत्रं समेत्याहुः कुरवः : कुरवः सर्व एव। कच्चिद् दृष्ट्वा दस्युसङ्घान् समेतान् स्मरन्ति पार्थस्य युधां प्रणेतु॥
en: Do all the sons of Kuru speak of Dhritarashtra, with his sons as their king? Do they, when they see a band of highway men assembled, remember in battle (Arjuna).

sn: मौर्वीभुजाग्रप्रहितान् स्म तात दोधूयमानेन धनुर्धरेण। नजिह्मगान् कच्चिदनुस्मरन्ति॥
en: Do they remember, the arrows shot from the Gandiva bow by means of the string of the bow and dexterity of the hands, the former shaking often and again and making a noise like the roaring of the clouds and flying swiftly.

sn: न चापश्यं कचिदहं पृथिव्यां योधं समं वाधिकमर्जुनेन। यस्यैकषष्टिनिशितास्तीक्ष्णधाराः सुवाससः सम्मतो हस्तवापः॥
en: I have not seen in this world any warrior who is superior to Arjuna or even equal to him, who with single effort, can send out sixty one whetted arrows with good feathers and with sharp edges.

sn: गदापाणिर्भीमसेनस्तरस्वी प्रवेपयञ्छत्रुसङ्घाननीके। नागः प्रभिन्न इव नड्वलेषु चंक्रम्यते कच्चिदेनं स्मरन्ति॥
en: Bhimasena is strong indeed with the mace in hand and makes a large number of enemies in an army tremble with fear as an elephant does in a place abounding with reeds. Do they remember him?

sn: माद्रीपुत्रः सहदेवः कलिङ्गान् समागतानजयद् दन्तकरे। वामेनास्यन् दक्षिणेनैव यो वै महाबलं कच्चिदेनं स्मरन्ति॥
en: Sahadeva, the son of the king of Madri, conquered the combined Kalingas and Dantakura by (shooting arrows with) his right and left hands; do they remember this strong one?

sn: पुरा जेतुं नकुलः प्रेषितोऽयं शिबींस्त्रिगर्तान् संजय पश्यतस्ते। दिशं प्रतीची वशमानयन्मे माद्रीसुतं कच्चिदेनं स्मरन्ति॥
en: In days of was Nakula sent to conquer the Shibis and the Trigartas. This is within your knowledge. O Sanjaya, they subjugated the western countries. Do they remember these sons of the king of Madri.

sn: पराभवो द्वैतवने य आसीद् दुर्मन्त्रिते घोषयात्रागतानाम्। यत्र मन्दाञ्छत्रुवशं प्रयातानमोचयद् भीमसेनो जयश्च।।
en: The defeat that they met with in the forest named when ill advised they went there and when Bhimasena and Arjuna faced these dull headed ones who were imprisoned by the enemy.

sn: अहं पश्चादर्जुनमभ्यरक्षं माद्रीपुत्रौ भीमसेनोऽप्यरक्षत्। गाण्डीवधन्वा शत्रुसङ्घानुदस्य स्वस्त्यागमत् कच्चिदेनं स्मरन्ति॥
en: Where I protected Arjuna, in the rear and Bhimasena protecting the rear of the two sons of the king of Madri and where the wielder of the Gandiva bow issued out uninjured after rendering the enemy depressed do they remember?

sn: न कर्मणा साधुनैकेन नूनं सुखं शक्यं वै भवतीह संजय। न शक्नुमो धृतराष्ट्रस्य पुत्रम्॥
en: It is not by a single good deed that we can be happy in this world, O Sanjaya, when with all our endeavors are we unable to win over the son of Dhritarashtra.

sn: संजय उवाच यथाऽऽत्य मे पाण्डव तत् तथैव कुरून् कुरुश्रेष्ठ जनं च पृच्छसि। अनामयास्तात मनस्विनस्ते कुरुश्रेष्ठान् पृच्छसि पार्थ यांस्त्वम्॥
en: Sanjaya said It is exactly as you, say O son of Pandu. You enquire, dear sir, about the Kurus and the foremost among them. Those whom you enquire about, O soil of Pritha, viz., the foremost among the race of Kuru, those wise ones are doing well.

sn: सन्त्येव वृद्धाः साधवो धार्तराष्ट्र सन्त्येव पापाः पाण्डव तस्य विद्धि। दद्याद् रिपुभ्योऽपि हि धार्तराष्ट्रः कुतो दायाँल्लोपयेद् ब्राह्मणानाम्॥
en: Know them that the son of Dhritarashtra is surrounded by aged men and true and also by wicked men, O son of Pandu. To the enemy even would the son of Dhritarashtra give away, why then should he discontinue what is due to the Brahmanas?

sn: मगुग्धेषु दुग्धवत् तन्न साधु। मित्रध्रुक स्याद् धृतराष्ट्रः सपुत्रो युष्मान् द्विषन् साधुवृत्तानसाधुः॥
en: The rule that obtains among among you (Kshatriyas) viz., to harm those that do not injure you is rule for butchers. It is not good, if Dhritarashtra, with his sons like a bad man, speaks ill of you who follow good practices, they would be guilty of conspiring against friends.

sn: न चानुजानाति भृशं च तप्यते शोचत्यन्तः स्थविरोऽजातशत्रो। शृणोति हि ब्राह्मणानां समेत्य मित्रद्रोहः पातकेभ्यो गरीयान्॥
en: He dose not approve of it (the injury done to you); he is very sorry for it and the old man on his part repents for it. ( you who have created no enemies, having consulted the Brahmanas he has come to know that conspiring against friends is the worst of all sins.

sn: स्मरन्ति तुभ्यं नरदेव संयुगे युद्धे च जिष्णोश्च युधां प्रणेतुः। समुत्कृष्टे दुन्दुभिशङ्खशब्दे गदापाणिं भीमसेनं स्मरन्ति॥
en: They remember, O god among men, your might in battle and remember also the one who always gets victories and is the leader in battles (Arjuna). They remember Bhimasena with the mace in his hand when there is sound of conch shells and drums.

sn: माद्रीसुतौ चापि रणाजिमध्ये सर्वा दिशः सम्पतन्तौ स्मरन्ति। सेनां वर्षन्तौ शरवरजस्त्रं महारथौ समरे दुष्प्रकम्पौ॥
en: They remember too the two mighty sons of the king of Madri who, in battle, fell (the enemies) in all directions showering on the (hostile) army continuous flight of arrows and whom it is hard to cause to tremble in battle.

sn: ननागतं ज्ञायते यद् भविष्यम्। त्वं चेत् तथा सर्वधर्मोपपन्नः प्राप्तः क्लेशं पाण्डव कृच्छ्ररूपम्। त्वमेवैतत् कृच्छ्रगतश्च भूयः समीकुर्याः प्रज्ञयाऽजातशत्रो॥
en: I think that we cannot know what is yet to befall a man, what futurity has in store for him. For this reason have you, O son of Pandu, though endued with all the virtuous, met with very hard troubles. You will no by means of your wisdom, make up for all these, O you who have created no enemies.

sn: न कामार्थं संत्यजेयुर्हि धर्म पाण्डोः सुताः सर्व एवेन्द्रकल्पाः। त्वमेवैतत् प्रज्ञयाऽजातशत्रो समीकुर्या येन शर्माप्नुयुस्ते॥ धार्तराष्ट्राः पाण्डवा संजयाश्च ये चाप्यन्ये संनिविष्टा नरेन्द्राः।
en: The sons of Pandu all equal to Indra, will not leave virtue for the sake of pleasure. You will, O you who have created no enemies, so make it up with your wisdom so that all will obtain peace-the sons of Dhritarashtra the sons of Pandu, the Srinjayas and all the other king who have assembled here.

sn: मजातशत्रो वचनं पिता ते॥ सहामात्यः सहपुत्रश्च राजन् समेत्य तां वाचमिमां निबोध॥
en: Listen to what Dhritarashtra, who is equal to your father, has said, O you who have created no enemies, in consultation with his ministers and sons. O king attend to these words.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच समागताः पाण्डवाः सुंजयाश्च जनार्दनो युयुधानो विराटः। यत् ते वाक्यं धृतराष्ट्रानुशिष्टं गावल्गणे ब्रूहि तत् सूतपुत्र॥
en: Yudhishthira said Here are assembled the sons of Pandu, the Srinjayas, Yudhishthira, Virata; speak the words, you have been instructed to say by Dhritarashtra, O son of Gavalgana, O son of Suta.

sn: संजय उवाच अजातशत्रु च वृकोदरं च धनंजय माद्रवतीसुतौ च। आमन्त्रये वासुदेवं च शौरिं युयुधान् चेकितान विराटम्॥
en: Sanjaya said I make my obeisance to him who has created no enemies, to Vrikodara, Dhananjaya and the two sons of the king of Madri and also the son of Shura, the son of Vasudeva, Yuyudhana, Chekitana and Virata,

sn: पञ्चालानामधिपं चैव वृद्धं धृष्टद्युम्नं पार्ष याज्ञसेनिम्। सर्वे वाचं शृणुतेमा मदीयां वक्ष्यामि यां भूतिमिच्छन् कुरूणाम्॥
en: And also to the aged lord of the people of Panchala, Dhrishtadyumna the son of Prishata and Yagaseni. All of you listen to these words which I speak, being desirous of the welfare of the Kurus.

sn: नयोजयत् त्वरमाणो रथं मे। स्तद् रोचतां पाण्डवानां शमोऽस्तु॥
en: King Dhritarashtra had my car speedily got ready for he welcomed the chance of peace. Therefore may the king, with his brothers, sons and friends, find these words acceptable to them. Let there be peace.

sn: सर्वैर्धर्मः समुपेतास्तु पार्थाः संस्थानेन मार्दवेनार्जवेन। जाताः कुले ह्यनृशंसा वदान्या ह्रीनिषेवाः कर्मणां निश्चयज्ञाः॥
en: With all virtues are the sons of Pritha endued, with steadiness, with mildness and with frankness. They are born in a good family, the reverse of cruel and generous, they avoid all deeds that one, should be ashamed of and know for certainly the nature of each deed.

sn: न युज्यते कर्म युष्मासु हीनं सत्त्वं हि वस्तादृशं भीमसेनाः। उद्भासते ह्यञ्जनबिन्दवक्त च्छुभ्र वस्त्रे यद् भवेत् किल्बिषं वः॥
en: A mean act does not befit you for you are noble-minded and have a terrible army. If you act mean, it will get undue preponderance as does a black spot on a white cloth.

sn: सर्वक्षयो दृश्यते यत्र कृत्स्नः पापोदयो निरयोऽभावसंस्थः। कस्तत्र् कुर्याज्जातु कर्म प्रजानन् पराजयो यत्र समो जयश्च॥
en: An act which on the very face of it will cause destruction to all and which is sinful and leading to hell, who will do such an act consciously, an act which gives the same result in case of victory and defeat alike.

sn: ते वै धन्या यैः कृतं ज्ञातिकार्य ते वै पुत्राः सुहृदो बान्धवाश्च। र्यतः कुरूणां नियतो वैभव: स्यात्॥
en: Blessed are they who promote the interests of their cousins. They are the sons, friends and well-wishers indeed (of the Kurus) who, in order that prosperity may ever attend the Kurus, would sacrifice their life which is of small value.

sn: ते चेत् कुरूननुशिष्याथ पार्था निर्णीय सर्वान् द्विषतो निगृह्य। समं वस्तज्जीवितं मृत्युना स्याद् यज्जीवध्वं ज्ञातिवधे न साधु॥
en: If after subjugating the Kurus, O you sons of Pritha and defeating all, you destroy those who despise you, then the succeeding portion of your life will be equal to death, since what is life after killing all your all your cousins?

sn: को ह्येव युष्मान् सह केशवेन सचेकितानान् पार्षतबाहुगुप्तान्। ससात्यकीन् विषहेत प्रजेतुं लध्वाऽपि देवान् सचिवान् सहेन्द्रान्॥
en: Who is capable of withstanding you who are assisted by Keshava, Chekitana and Satyaki and protected by the arms of the son of Prishata even after getting Indra and all his divine followers on his side.

sn: नश्वत्थाम्ना शल्यकृपादिभिश्च। रणे विजेतुं विषहेत राजन् राधेयगुप्तान् सह भूमिपालैः॥
en: Who, on the other hand, can withstand with a view to conquer in battle, the Kurus, who are protected by Drona, Bhishma, Ashvathama, Shalya, Kripa and others and also protected by the son of Radha along with other kings.

sn: महद् बलं धार्तराष्ट्रस्य राज्ञः को वै शक्तो हन्तुमक्षीयमाणः। सोऽहं जये चैव पराजये च निःश्रेयसं नाधिगच्छामि किञ्चित्॥
en: Who is capable of staying, without any loss to his own army, the large force of the royal son of Dhritarashtra? Therefore do I see not the slightest good in either victory or defeat.

sn: कथं हि नीचा इव दौष्कुलेया निर्धर्मार्थं कर्म कुर्युश्च पार्थाः। सोऽहं प्रसाद्य प्रणतो वासुदेवं पञ्चालानामधिपं चैव वृद्धम्॥
en: Why should the sons of Pritha do an wicked act like mean people and those born in low families? Therefore having approached you, do I bow to the son of Vasudeva and the aged lord of the people of Panchala.

sn: कृताञ्जलिः शरणं वः प्रपद्ये कथं स्वस्ति स्यात् कुरुसंजयानाम्। न ह्येवमेवं वचनं वासुदेवो धनंजयो वा जातु किंचिन्न कुर्यात्॥
en: With hands clasped, do I throw myself under your protection so that it may go well with the Kurus and the Srinjayas. Why should not the son of Vasudeva and Dhananjaya act in the manner indicated by me?

sn: देतद् विद्वन् साधनार्थं ब्रवीमि। एतद् राज्ञो भीष्मपुरोगमस्य मतं यद् वः शान्तिरिहोत्तमा स्यात्॥
en: If so requested they would give away their lives; why should not they do this which is, I say, O learned man, for the preservation of others.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच कां नु वाचं संजय मे शृणोषि युद्धैषिणी येन युद्धाद् बिभेषि। अयुद्धं वै तात युद्धाद् गरीयः कस्तल्लब्ध्वा जातु युद्ध्येत सूत॥
en: Yudhishthira said What words, of mine, O Sanjaya, have you heard meaning ever, that you fear war. The reverse of war, is better than war. Who having got that (peace) goes to war, O Suta?

sn: अकुर्वतश्चेत् पुरुषस्य संजय सिद्ध्येत् संकल्पो मनसा ये यमिच्छेत्। दन्यत्र युद्धाद् बहु यल्लघीयः॥
en: If what a man desires in his heart is fulfilled, O Sanjaya, without doing anything then he will not do anything even if that be very much easier than war.

sn: कुतो युद्धं जातु नरोऽवगच्छेत् को देवशप्तो हि वृणीत युद्धम्। सुखैषिणः कर्म कुर्वन्ति पार्था धर्मादहीनं यच्च लोकस्य पथ्यम्॥
en: Wherefore should a man go to war; who is there cursed by the gods who would chose war? The sons of Pritha do acts which bring on happiness and at the same time are conducive to the well being of the world and not inferior to virtue (i.e. virtuous acts).

sn: धर्मोदयं सुखमाशंसमानाः कृच्छ्रोपायं तत्त्वतः कर्म दुःखम्। सुखं प्रेप्सुर्विजिघांसुश्च दुःखं य इन्द्रियाणां प्रीतिरसानुगामी॥
en: They are men desirous of only such happiness as has its source in virtue. He, who being desirous of happiness and of destroying misery, follows the pleasant dictates of his senses, adopts a way which leads to misery.

sn: कामाभिध्या स्वशरीरं दुनोति यया प्रमुक्तो न करोति दुःखम्। यथेध्यमानस्य समिद्धतेज़सो भूयो बलं वर्धते पावकस्य॥
en: Seeking pleasure he pains his own body as fuel to a burning flame increases its force; and when a man has freed himself from this longing he does not bring misery on himself.

sn: कामार्थलाभेन तथैव भूयो न तृप्यते सर्पिषेवाग्निरिद्धः। सम्पश्येमं भोगचयं महान्तं सहास्माभिधृतराष्ट्रस्य राज्ञः॥
en: In the same way, by the satisfaction of our sensual desires we are not satiated but are like fire with clarified butter added on to it. Compare this great source of enjoyment of the king Dhritarashtra with ourselves.

sn: नाश्रेयानीश्वरो विग्रहाणां नाश्रेयान् वै गीतशब्दं शृणोति। नाश्रेयान् वै सेवते माल्यगन्धान् न चाप्यश्रेयाननुलेपनानि॥
en: Deserted by the goddess of fortune people never win victory in battle; unfortunate people never hear the sound of music, unfortunate people never enjoy garlands and fragrance and unfortunate people (never enjoy) ungents.

sn: नाश्रेयान् वै प्रावारान् संविवस्ते कथं त्वस्मान् सम्प्रणुदेत् कुरुभ्यः। अत्रैव स्यादबुधस्यैव कामः प्रायः शरीरे हृदयं दुनोति॥
en: Also, unfortunate people never get fine sheets to wear, (we are unfortunate) otherwise why should we have been exiled from the country of the Kurus. It must be so. The desires of an unwise man give trouble to his body as well as to his mind.

sn: स्वयं राजा विषमस्थः परेषु सामर्थ्यमन्विच्छति तन्न साधु। यथाऽऽत्मनः पश्यति वृत्तमेव तथा परेषामपि सोऽभ्युपैति॥
en: The king himself in trouble wants to get strength from others; this is hardly fair. As he sees himself surrounded (by friends) so let him see others surrounded (by friends).

sn: आसन्नमग्नि तु निदाघकाले गम्भीरकक्षे गहने विसृज्य। यथा विवृद्धं वायुवसेन शोचेत् क्षेमं मुमुक्षुः शिशिरव्यपाये॥
en: A man having thrown, burning fire, at midday, at the end of winter, on a thick wood of reeds and which fire spreads with the wind, repents his act when he is desirous of escape.

sn: प्राप्तैश्वर्यो धृतराष्ट्रोऽद्य राजा लालप्यते संजय कस्य हेतोः। प्रगृह्य दुर्बुद्धिमनार्जवे रतं पुत्रं मन्दं मूढममन्त्रिणं तु॥
en: Having got wealth why does the king Dhritarashtra now grieve for his lot O Sanjaya? Simply because he had accepted the secret advice to his dull-headed son of vicious soul and addicted to dishonest ways.

sn: अनाप्तवच्चाप्ततमस्य वाचः सुयोधनो विदुरस्यावमत्या सुतस्य राजा धृतराष्ट्रः प्रियैषी सम्बुध्यमानो विशतेऽधर्ममेव॥
en: Suyodhana treated with contempt the world of Vidura, whom he regarded as his enemy though he was his friend and the king Dhritarashtra, desirous of meeting the wishes of his son, consciously deserted virtue.

sn: मेधाविनं ह्यर्थकामं कुरूणां बहुश्रुतं वाग्मिनं शीलवन्तम्। स तं राजा धृतराष्ट्रः कुरुभ्यो न सस्मार विदुरं पुत्रकाम्यात्॥
en: The king Dhritarashtra, from a desire to please his son, remembered not that Vidura was a wise man among the Kurus and wished for the well-being of the Kurus, of very great learning, adept at speech and well behaved.

sn: माननस्यासौ मानकामस्य चे!ः संरम्भिणश्चार्थधर्मातिगस्य। दुर्भाषिणो मन्युवशानुगस्य कामात्मनो दौ«दैर्भावितस्य॥
en: He (the son) through himself desirous of honour, seeks to deprive others of honour, is jealous, wrathful, goes beyond the limits of virtue for his own interests, haughty in sensual desires and is induced with a bad heart.

sn: मित्रदुहः संजय पापबुद्धेः। सुतस्य राजा धृतराष्ट्रः प्रियैषी प्रपश्यमानः प्राजहाद् धर्मकामौ॥
en: He leads a bad life, is deserted by the Goddess of Fortune, cherishes wrongs for a long time, conspires, against friends and has a vicious mind. For meeting the wishes of such an one did king Dhritarashtra, with his eyes wide open, forsake virtue and pleasure.

sn: न्मतिः कुरूणामागतः स्यादभावः। काव्यां वाचं विदुरो भाषमाणो न विन्दते यद् धार्तराष्ट्रात् प्रशंसाम्॥
en: At that time, O Sanjaya, when I was playing at dice did it occur to me that the destruction of the Kurus was come for Vidura speaking these wise words did not obtain praise from Dhritarashtra.

sn: क्षत्तुर्यदा नान्ववर्तन्त बुद्धि कृच्छ्रे कुरून् सूत तदाभ्याजगाम्। यावत् प्रज्ञामन्ववर्तन्त तस्य तावत् तेषां राष्ट्रवृद्धिर्बभूव॥
en: When they no longer followed the instructions of Vidura, troubles overtook the Kurus, O Suta. So long as they followed his wisdom, did their kingdom prosper.

sn: तदर्थलुब्धस्य निबोध मेऽद्य ये मन्त्रिणो धार्तराष्ट्रस्य सूत। दुःशासनः शकुनिः सूतपुत्रो गावल्गणे पश्य सम्मोहमस्य॥
en: Hear now from me who are the ministers of the son of Dhritarashtra for the promotion of his interest, O Suta. They are Dhritarashtra, Shakuni and the son of Suta (Karna). O son of Gavalgani, look at his folly.

sn: सोऽहं न पश्यामि परीक्षमाणः कथं स्वस्ति स्यात् कुरुसुंजयानाम्। आत्तैश्वर्यो धृतराष्ट्रः परेभ्यः प्रवाजिते विदुरे दीर्घदृष्टो॥
en: Therefore even when I consider, do I not see how it can go well with the Kurus and the Srinjayas, Dhritarashtra having usurped the wealth of others and the far seeing Vidura having been banished to a foreign country.

sn: आशंसते वै धृतराष्ट्रः सपुत्रो महाराज्यमसपत्नं पृथिव्याम्। तस्मिञ्छमः केवलं नोपलभ्यः सर्वं स्वकं मद्गते मन्यतेऽर्थम्॥
en: Dhritarashtra, with his son, hopes for an undisputed suzerainty over this world. Absolute peace therefore is unobtainable. Whatever wealth is under his possession he regards as belonging to himself.

sn: यत् तत् कर्णो मन्यते पारणीयं युद्धे गृहीतायुधमर्जुनं वै। आसंश्च युद्धानि पुरा महान्ति कथं कर्णो नाभवद् द्वीप एषाम्॥
en: Karna considers Arjuna capable of being vanquished when the latter takes up his weapons in battle. In former days there were many great battles. Why were they not benefited by Karna.

sn: कर्णश्च जानाति सुयोधनश्च द्रोणश्च जानाति पितामहश्च। अन्ये च कर कुरवस्तत्र सन्ति यथार्जुनान्नास्त्यपरो धनुर्धरः॥
en: Karna knows, so does Suyodhana, Drona knows so does our grandsire and so do the other Kurus that there is no wielder of the bow superior to Arjuna.

sn: जानन्त्येतत् कुरवः सर्व एव ये चाप्यन्ये भूमिपालाः समेताः। दुर्योधने राज्यमिहाभवद् यथा अरिंदमे फाल्गुने विद्यमाने॥
en: All the Kurus, know and so do all the other kings that are assembled, how this kingdom came under the possession of Duryodhana, during the life-time of Arjuna, the subduer of foes.

sn: तेनानुबन्धं मन्यते धार्तराष्ट्रः शक्यं हर्तुं पाण्डवानां ममत्वम्। किरीटिना तालमात्रायुधेन तद्वेदिना संयुगं तत्र गत्वा॥
en: With that precedent in their mind, the sons of Dhritarashtra think that they are capable of depriving the sons of Pandu of what is their own through they are aware having been present there, of the deportment of Arjuna in a battle when the only weapon he had was a bow.

sn: वशृण्वाना धार्तराष्ट्रा ध्रियन्ते। क्रुद्धं न चेदीक्षते भीमसेनं सुयोधनो मन्यते सिद्धमर्थम्॥
en: Not yet having heard the twang of the Gandiva when fully stretched out, the sons of Dhritarashtra are yet alive. So long as he does not see Bhimasena inspired with wrath, Suyodhana thinks that his object is gained.

sn: इन्द्रोऽप्येतन्नोत्सहेत् तात हर्तु मैश्वर्यं नो जीवति भीमसेने। धनंजये नकुले चैव सूत तथा वीरे सहदेवे सहिष्णौ॥
en: Indra even would not be able to stand against him, for robbing us of our wealth, during the life time of Bhimasena and Dhananjaya, 0 Suta and the patient Nakula and the hero Sahadeva.

sn: स चेदेता प्रतिपद्येत बुद्धि वृद्धो राजा सह पुत्रेण सूत। एवं रणे पाण्डवकोपदग्धा न नश्येयुः संजय धार्तराष्ट्राः॥
en: The old king with his son, O Suta, still entertains the thought that the sons of Dhritarashtra will not be killed in battle consumed by the son of Pandu, O Sanjaya.

sn: जानासि त्वं क्लेशमस्मासु वृत्तं त्वां पूजयन् संजयाहं क्षमेयम्। यच्चास्माकं कौरवैर्भूतपूर्व या नो वृत्तिर्धार्तराष्ट्र तदाऽऽसीत्॥
en: You know what troubles have overtaken us. For my respect for you, I would forgive them, (you know as well) that which has taken place between ourselves and the sons of Kuru and what our treatment towards the son of Dhritarashtra was at the time.

sn: अद्यापि तत् तत्र तथैव वर्ततां शान्तिं गमिष्यामि यथात्वमात्थ। इन्द्रप्रस्थे भवतु ममैव राज्यं सुयोधनो यच्छतु भारताग्रयः॥
en: Even let that treatment be the same, I shall make peace, as you ask me to do. Let Indraprastha be my kingdom. Let the foremost of the race of Bharata, give it back to me.

sn: संजय उवाच धर्मनित्या पाण्डव ते विचेष्टा लोके श्रुता दृश्यते चापि पार्थ। महाश्रावं जीवितं चाप्यनित्यं सम्पश्यत्वं पाण्डव मा व्यनीनशः॥
en: Sanjaya said That you are attached to virtue, O Pandava, is known in this word and I see also that it is so, O son of Pritha. The life that is full of great deeds, also is unstable; considering this, you should not destroy (the Kurus).

sn: न चेद् भागं कुरवोऽन्यत्र युद्धात् प्रयच्छेरंस्तुभ्यमजातशत्रो। भैक्षचर्यामन्धकवृष्णिराज्ये श्रेयो मन्ये न तु युद्धेन राज्यम्॥
en: If the sons of Kuru do not give back to you your share without war, O you who have created no enemies; but I consider that living as a beggar in the kingdoms of Andhaka and Vrishni is better than a kingdom (attained) by means of war.

sn: अल्पकालं जीवितं यन्मनुष्ये महास्रावं नित्यदुःखं चलं च। भूयश्च तद् यशसो नानुरूपं तस्मात् पापं पाण्डव मा कृथास्त्वम्॥
en: Şince a man's life lasts but for a short time and is ever subject to sufferings and is unstable and since again it is not comparable to fame, therefore should you not do, O son of Pandu, a sinful art.

sn: कामा मनुष्यं प्रसजन्त एते धर्मस्य ये विघ्नमूलं नरेन्द्र। पूर्वं नरस्तान् मतिमान् प्रणिघल्लोके प्रशंसां लभतेऽनवद्याम्॥
en: Desires adhere to a man and they are the source of all impediments to virtue, O king of men. A wise man, having killed them beforehand, gained unspeakable praise in the world.

sn: निबन्धनी ह्यर्थतृष्णेह पार्थ तामिच्छता बाध्यते धर्म एव। धर्मं तु यः प्रवृणीते स बुद्धः कामे गृध्नो हीयतेऽर्थानुरोधात्॥
en: Thirst for wealth is a bond in this world, O son of Pritha. Those, who desire it, go against virtue as it were. He who chooses virtue is wise. The man, who desires pleasure, becomes degraded for the sake of pleasure.

sn: धर्म कृत्वा कर्मणां तात मुख्यं महाप्रतापः सवितेव भाति। हीनो हि धर्मेण महीमपीमां लब्ध्वा नरः सीदति पापबुद्धिः॥
en: A man, who makes virtue his prime duty, gains great fame and shines like the sun, and the man, of vicious intellect, devoid of virtue, is ruined even if he obtains the earth.

sn: वेदोऽधीतश्चरितं ब्रह्मचर्य यज्ञैरिष्टं ब्राह्मणेभ्यश्च दत्तम्। परं स्थानं मन्यमानेन भूय आत्मा दत्तो वर्षपूगं सुखेभ्यः॥
en: The Vedas have been read by you; the hard austerities of Brahmacharya have been practised by you and in sacrificial ceremonies the desires of Brahmanas have been fulfilled by you and with the other world before your mind, your soul has been devoted to happiness for a series of years.

sn: सुखप्रिये सेवमानोऽतिवेलं योगाभ्यासे यो न करोति कर्म। वित्तक्षये हीनसुखोऽतिवेलं दुःखं शेते कामवेगप्रणुन्नः॥
en: He, who having having devoted himself excessively to pleasures, does not to any deed leading to religious meditation, becomes extremely devoid of happiness after his wealth is gone and remains liable to be led by the force of his desires.

sn: एवं पुनर्ब्रह्मचर्याप्रसक्तो हित्वा धर्मं यः प्रकरोत्यधर्मम्। अश्रद्दधत् परलोकाय मूढो हित्वा देहं तप्यते प्रेत्य मन्दः॥
en: In the same way, the fool, who despising virtue and without practicing religious meditation, gives himself up to vice, shows no regard (for the Supreme Being). The soul, after leaving the body and reaching the other world, comes to grief.

sn: न कर्मणा विप्रणाशोऽस्त्यमुत्र पुण्यानां वाप्यथवा पापकानाम्। पूर्वं कर्तुर्गच्छति पुण्यपापं पश्चात् त्वेनमनुयात्येव कर्ता॥
en: Here (i.e. in the other world) there is no absolute annihilation for either virtuous or for vicious deeds. The good and evil deeds go before and the agent only follows them.

sn: न्यायोपेतं ब्राह्मणेभ्योऽथ दत्तं श्रद्धापूतं गन्धरसोपपन्नम्। अन्वाहार्येषूत्तमदक्षिणेषु तथारूपं कर्म विख्यायते ते॥
en: Your deeds are famous, as the offerings of savory and delicious victuals, rendered holy with the respect (with which they are offered), made to Brahmanas accompanied by gifts with perfect propriety, on the occasion of religious ceremonies.

sn: इह क्षेत्रे क्रियते पार्थ कार्य न वै किञ्चित् क्रियते प्रेत्य कार्यम्। कृतं त्वया पारलौक्यं च कर्म पुण्यं महत् सद्भिरतिप्रशस्तम्॥
en: During this life deeds are done, O son of Pritha and after death, no act whatever is done. And virtuous deeds that are valuable in the next world and so be-lauded by the great and the honest, have been done by you.

sn: जहाति मृत्युं च जरां भयं च न क्षुत्पिपासे मनसोऽप्रियाणि। दन्यत्र वै चेन्द्रियप्रीणनाद्धि॥
en: Death does away with decrepitude, fear, as also hunger and thirst and all that is disagreeable to the mind. There is no duty there but delighting in one's senses.

sn: एवंरूपं कर्मफलं नरेन्द्र मात्रावहं हृदयस्य प्रियेण। स क्रोधज पाण्डव हर्षजं च लोकावुभौ मा प्रहासीश्चिराय॥
en: Such is the fruit of our deeds, O king of men; therefore do not, in this world, carry the load of doing what is pleasing to the heart, O son of Pandu, do not (by your action) go forever either to the region that is full of causes begetting wrath (hell) or to the one that abounds with causes begetting delight.

sn: अन्तं गत्वा कर्मणां मा प्रजह्याः सत्यं दमं चार्जवमानृशंस्यम्। अश्वमेधं राजसूयं तथज्याः पापस्यान्तं कर्मणो मा पुनर्गाः॥
en: Having got to the end of your deeds, do not however, put truth, self-conduct, candour and humility. You may perform the Ashvamedha and Rajasuya sacrifices, but do not come again near the limits of sinful acts.

sn: तच्चेदेवं द्वेषरूपेण पार्थाः करिष्यध्वं कर्म पापं चिराय। निवसध्वं वर्षपूगान् वनेषु दुःखं वासं पाण्डवा धर्म एव॥
en: If now, actuated by malice, you sons of Pritha, do vicious deeds, you have, in vain, for a series of years, resided in forests undergoing all sorts of troubles like virtue itself.

sn: दात्माधीनं यद् बलं ह्येतदासीत्। नित्यं च वश्याः सचिवास्तवेमे जनार्दनो युयुधानश्च वीरः॥
en: In vain did you also roam about in the forests, parting with this army, which was formerly subject to your control and also (parting with) these followers of yours, namely Janardana and the hero Yuyudhana.

sn: मत्स्यो राजा रुक्मरथः सपुत्रः प्रहारिभिः सह पुत्रैविराटः। राजानश्च ये विजिताः पुरस्तात् त्वामेव ते संश्रयेयुः समस्ताः॥
en: And also (your followers) the king of the Matsya, Virata of the golden car with his son at the head of his shoulders. And the kings who were formerly vanquished by you, all have come over to your side.

sn: महासहायः प्रतपन् बलस्थः पुरस्कृतो वासुदेवार्जुनाभ्याम्। वरान् हनिष्यन् द्विपतो रङ्गमध्ये व्यनेष्यथा धार्तराष्ट्रस्य दर्पम्॥
en: With all these great resources, with great fame (which then attached to your name) and possessing an army at the head of which were the son of Vasudeva and Arjuna, you might after having slain the most valorous among your despisers in the field of battle, have destroyed the pride of the sons of Dhritarashtra.

sn: बलं कस्माद् वर्धयित्वा परस्य निजान् कस्मात् कर्शयित्वा सहायान्। निरुष्य कस्माद् वर्षपूगान् वनेषु युयुत्ससे पाण्डव हीनकालम्॥
en: Why after having increased the strength of your enemy and after weakening your own friends and after having lived in exile in the forest for a series of years, are you now desirous of fighting, O son of Pandu, after the proper time.

sn: ऽधर्मज्ञो वा भूतिमथोऽभ्युपैति। प्रज्ञावान् वा बुध्यमानोऽपि धर्म संस्तम्भाद् वा सोऽपि भूतेरपैति॥
en: An unwise man, O son of Pandu or one that does not know virtue, may obtain prosperity by fighting or a wise man and virtuous, may lose his prosperity by not fighting.

sn: न संरम्भात् कर्म चकर्थ पापम्। आत्थ किं तत् कारणं यस्य हेतोः प्रज्ञाविरुद्ध कर्म चिकीर्षसीदम्॥
en: Your instinct does not urge you to an unrighteous act, O son of Pritha and never did you, out of wrath, do a sinful act. Tell me, therefore, what the reason is which makes you desirous of doing this sinful act, which is against the dictates wisdom.

sn: अव्याधिजं कटुकं शीर्षरोगि यशोमुषं पापफलोदयं वा। सतां पेयं यनन पिबन्त्यसन्तो मन्युं महाराज पिब प्रशाम्य॥
en: Wrath is a bitter remedy for evils, it causes malady in the head, destroys fame and is a source of sinful acts. It ought to be controlled by a good man and those that do not control it are bad men. O great king, control your wrath. Incline to peace.

sn: पापानुबन्धं को नु तं कामयेत क्षमैव ते ज्यासी नोत भोगाः। यत्र भीष्मः शान्तनवो हतः स्याद् यत्र द्रोणः सहपुत्रो हतः स्यात्॥
en: Who would desire wrath which leads to sin. Forbearance is good for you, not enjoyments where Bhishma and the son of Shantanu will be killed and Drona with his son slain.

sn: कृपः शल्यः सौमदत्तिर्विको विविंशतिः कर्णदुर्योधनौ च। एतान् हत्वा कीदृशं तत् सुखं स्याद् यद् विन्देथास्तदनु ब्रूहि पार्थ॥
en: Kripa, Shalya, the son of Somadatta, Vikarana, Vivingshati, Karna and Duryodhana-having killed all these, what sort of happiness is it that you will get after that, tell me, O son of Pritha.

sn: लब्ध्वापीमां पृथिवीं सागरान्तां जरामृत्यू नैव हि त्वं प्रजह्याः। नेवं विद्वान् नैव युद्धं कुरु त्वम्॥
en: Having gained even this earth bounded by the sea, you will not get rid of descripitude or death, desirable results or undesirable, happiness or misery. O king knowing this, do not wage war.

sn: रेवं युक्तं कर्म चिकीर्षसि त्वम्। अपक्रामे: स्वं प्रदायैव तेषां मा गास्त्वं वै देवयानात् पथोऽद्य॥
en: If you are desirous of doing this deed, attended with such results, simply because your advisers wish it, then abdicate everything to them and go away. You should not now forsake the path leading to the region of the gods.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच असंशयं संजय सत्यमेतद् धर्मो वरः कर्णणां यत् त्वमात्थ। ज्ञात्वा तु मां संजय गर्हयेस्त्वं यदि धर्मं यद्यधर्मं चरेयम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said Undoubtedly, O Sanjaya, it is as you say namely that virtuous acts are the best among deeds; and knowing, O Sanjaya, whether it is Qur virtue or vice that I follow should you blame me.

sn: यत्राधर्मो धर्मरूपाणि धत्ते धर्मः कृत्स्नो दृश्यतेऽधर्मरूपः। बिभ्रद् धर्मो धर्मरूपं तथा च विद्वांसस्तं सम्प्रपश्यन्ति बुद्ध्या॥
en: Where vice assumes the appearance of virtue and virtue appears completely as vice and virtue appears in its own form wise men should distinguish it from virtue by their intelligence.

sn: एवं तथैवापदि लिङ्गमेतद् धर्माधर्मी नित्यवृत्ती भजेताम्। मापद्धर्मं संजय तं निबोध॥
en: A man should follow the profession of the order among which he is born, but similarly in tirnes of distress these occupations which are fixed, follow the rule of virtue and vice. Hear now, O Sanjaya, what constitutes profession in times of distress.

sn: लुप्तायां तु प्रकृतौ येन कर्म निष्पादयेत् तत् परीप्सेद् विहीनः। प्रकृतिस्थश्चादि वर्तमान उभौ गौ भवतः संजयैतौ॥
en: With his means of livelihood gone, a destitute man ought to desire for such means as may enable him to perform such duties as are laid down for him. O Sanjaya; both the man whose means of livelihood is not gone and the one who is in distress, are culpable (if they act as if they are not what they are)O Sanjaya,

sn: अविनाशमिच्छतां ब्राह्मणानां प्रायश्चित्तं विहितं यद् विधात्रा। सम्पश्येथाः कर्मसु वर्तमानान् विकर्मस्थान् संजय गर्हयेस्त्वम्॥
en: Since expiation has been prescribed by the creator, for those Brahmanas who without wishing for ruin to themselves (do actions sinful for them to do). With due regard to this fact, O Sanjaya, should you find fault with those whose means of livelihood is gone and those who are not in that position.

sn: सर्वोत्सङ्गं साधु मनीषिणां सत्त्वविच्छेदनाय विधीयते सत्सु वृत्तिः सदैवा अब्राह्मणाः सन्ति तु ये न वैद्याः मन्येत तेभ्यः॥
en: For the acquirement of the knowledge of our inner self and for bringing the mind under control is always prescribed accepting alms from good men. For those that are not Brahmanas and do not want to know about the inner self, the practices prescribed for their respective orders are considered to be the best.

sn: तदध्वानः पितरो ये च पूर्वे पितामहा ये च तेभ्यः परेऽन्ये। र्नान्यं ततो नास्तिकोऽस्मीति मन्ये॥
en: That path has been followed by our fathers and grandfathers and also by others and all those who are wise adopt the same path. For this I do not consider that they were not orthodox.

sn: यत् किंचनेदं वित्तमस्यां पृथिव्यां यद् देवानां त्रिदशानां परं यत्। प्राजापत्यं त्रिदिवं ब्रह्मलोकं नाधर्मतः संजय कामयेयम्॥
en: What little wealth there is in this world, what in the possessions of the gods and what is beyond them or the region of the Prajapatis, the heaven or the region of Brahma. I do not desire even unrighteously, O Sanjaya.

sn: प्युपासिता ब्राह्मणानां मनीषी। नानाविधांश्चैव महाबलांश्च राजन्यभोजाननुशास्ति कृष्णः॥
en: Krishna, is the lord (as it were) of virtue, well versed in every science, politic, wise and has been attended by Brahmanas and by him are instructed many kings of great prowess.

sn: यदि ह्यहं विसृजन् साम गर्यो नियुध्यमानो यदि जह्या स्वधर्मम्। महायशाः केशवस्तद् ब्रवीतु वासुदेवस्तूभयोरर्थकामः॥
en: If I am to blame by not making peace and if I swerve from the duties of my order, let Keshava, the son of Vasudeva, of great fame, who desires the welfare of both parties, say.

sn: शैनेयोऽयं चेदयश्चान्धकाश्च वार्ष्णेयभोजाः कुकुरा: संजयाश्च। उपासीना वासुदेवस्य बुद्धिं निगृह्य शत्रून् सुहृदो नन्दयन्ति॥
en: This Shini and the king of the Chedis and the king of the Andhakas and of the Vrishnis, of the Bhojas, of the Kukuras and of the Srinjayas, all by following the counsels of the son of Vasudeva slay their enemies and thus please their friends.

sn: वृष्ण्यन्धका एग्रसेनादयो वै कृष्णप्रणीताः सर्व एवेन्द्रकल्पाः। मनस्विनः सत्यपरायणाश्च महाबला यादवा भोगवन्तः॥
en: The kings of Vrishni and Andhaka and Ugrasena and others, led by Krishna, are all the equals of Indra and are spirited, attached to truth, of great prowess and happy.

sn: काश्यो बर्भुः श्रियमुत्तमां गतो लब्ध्वा कृष्णं भ्रातरमीशितारम्। यस्मै कामान् वर्षति वासुदेवो चीष्मात्यये मेघ इव प्रजाभ्यः॥
en: The king, of Kashi having obtained Krishna, the giver of boons, as his brother, has attained to great prosperity; on him the son of Vasudeva, showers blessings as the cloud on earthly beings at the close of summer.

sn: ईदृशोऽयं केशवस्तात विद्वान् विद्धि ह्येनं कर्मणां निश्चयज्ञम्। प्रियश्च नः साधुतमश्च कृष्णो नातिक्रामे वचनं केशवस्य॥
en: Such is this learned Keshava. Know him to be aware of the ethics of actions. The good Krishna is moreover our friend and I shall not act against the advice of Keshava.

sn: वासुदेव उवाच मिच्छाम्यहं भूतिमेषां प्रियं च। तथा राज्ञो धृतराष्ट्रस्य सूत समाशंसे बहुपुत्रस्य वृद्धिम्॥
en: Vasudeva said I desire, O Sanjaya, the continuance of the existence of the sons of Pandu-their prosperity and their good and in the same way, O Suta, do I desire the prosperity of king Dhritarashtra who has many sons.

sn: कामो हि मे संजय नित्यमेव नान्यद् व्रयां तान् प्रति शाम्यतेति। राज्ञश्च हि प्रियमेतच्छृणोमि मन्ये चैतत् पाण्डवानां समक्षम्॥
en: It has ever been my desire, O Sanjaya, to say to them, “Be peaceful” nothing else. I hear that this is also the wish of the king (Dhritarashtra) and I consider this to be equally to the good of the sons of Pandu.

sn: सुदुष्करस्तत्र शमो हि नूनं प्रदर्शितः संजय पाण्डवेन। यस्मिन् गृद्धो धृतराष्ट्रः सपुत्रः कस्मादेषां कलहो नावमूछेत्॥
en: Peace, of a rare sort, indeed, has been shown, O Sanjaya, by the son of Pandu, when Dhritarashtra with his sons is avaricious; why should the quarrel between these two parties rise to good proportions.

sn: न त्वं धर्मं विचरं संजयेह मत्तश्चं जानासि युधिष्ठिराच्च। अथो कस्मात् संजय पाण्डवस्य उत्साहिनः पूरयतः स्वकर्म॥ यथाऽऽख्यातमावसतः कुटुम्बे पुरा कस्मात् साधुविलोपमात्या दुच्चावचा मतयो ब्राह्मणानाम्॥
en: or You do know, O Sanjaya, the nature of right wrong better than myself or Yudhishthira; then for what reason, O Sanjaya, do you find fault with the son of Pandu, who is energetic, mindful of his own duties, whose duties towards his relations have been such as have been laid down from the days of yore. Why do you say that their goodness is vanished? With regard to the matter at present under discussion the opinions of the Brahmanas differ.

sn: कर्मणाऽऽहुः सिद्धिमेके परत्र हित्वा कर्म विद्यया सिद्धिमेके। नाभुञ्जानो भक्ष्यभोज्यस्य तृप्येद् विद्वानपीह विहितं ब्राह्मणानाम्॥
en: One school say that it is by work that we obtain salvation and again another school say that it is by putting aside work and through knowledge, that we attain to salvation. It has been so laid down by the superior beings that a man, even knowledge all the properties of good, will not be satisfied without eating.

sn: या वै विद्याः साधयन्तीह कर्म तासां फलं विद्यते नेतरासाम्। तत्रेह वै दृष्टफलं तु कर्म पीत्वोदकं शाम्यति तृष्णयाऽऽतः॥
en: That knowledge alone bears fruit, which does work, not others. In this world the result of action admits of ocular proof; one oppressed by thirst is satisfied by drinking water.

sn: सोऽयं विधिर्विहितः कर्मणैव संवर्तते संजय तत्र कर्मी तत्र योऽन्यत् कर्मणः साधु मन्येन्मोघं तस्यालपितं दुर्बलस्य॥
en: Therefore it has been ordained by the creator that through work results, O Sanjaya, work. Therefore the opinion that anything other than work is good, is nothing but the uttering of a fool and of a weak man.

sn: कर्मणाऽमी भान्ति देवाः परत्र कर्मणैवेह प्लवते मातरिश्वा। अहोरात्रे विदधत् कर्मणैव अतन्द्रितो नित्यमुदेति सूर्यः॥९
en: Elsewhere (i.e. in the other world) the gods are resplendent through work, the wind blows through work. Causing day and night, through work, the sleepless sun rises every day.

sn: नतन्द्रितश्चन्द्रमाश्चाभ्युपैति। अतन्द्रितो दहते जातवेदाः समिद्धयमानः कर्म कुर्वन् प्रजाभ्यः॥
en: The sleepless moon, too, goes through half months and months and certain peculiar positions of the moon (through work) burns, doing good to the creatures of the Earth.

sn: अतन्द्रिता भारमिमं महान्तं बिभर्ति देवी पृथिवी बलेन। अतन्द्रिताः शीघ्रमपो वहन्ति संतर्पयन्त्यः सर्वभूतानि नद्यः॥
en: The goddess Earth, sleepless, carries this great load through her strength and the sleepless rivers carry their waters with speed, satisfying the desire of all beings.

sn: अतन्द्रितो वर्षति भूरितेजाः संनादयन्नन्तरिक्षं दिशश्च। अतन्द्रितो ब्रह्मचर्यं चचार श्रेष्ठत्वमिच्छन् बलभिद् देवतानाम्॥
en: The sleepless one of mighty strength (Indra) showers rain, resounding every corner and the cardinal points; and desiring kingship among the gods he practised the austerities of a Brahmacharya life, being sleepless.

sn: हित्वा सुखं मनसश्च प्रियाणि तेन शक्रः कर्मणा श्रेष्ठ्यमाप। सत्यं धर्मं पालयन्त्रप्रमत्तो दमं तितिक्षां मतां प्रियं च॥
en: Giving up pleasure and the satisfaction of his desires, the position of a chief was obtained by Shakra by means of work. He strictly observed truth, virtue, self-control, forbearance, impartially and amiability.

sn: एतानि सर्वाण्युपसेवमानः स देवराज्यं मघवान् प्राप मुख्यम्। बृहस्पतिर्ब्रह्मचर्यं चचार समाहितः संशितात्मा यथावत्॥
en: Devoting himself to all these, Indra got the high position of the king of the gods. Brihaspati too practised the austerities of a Brahmacharya life, with his mind shut up everything else and controlling his self as usual.

sn: हित्वा सुखं प्रतिध्येन्द्रियाणि तेन देवानामगमद् गौरवं सः। तथा नक्षत्राणि कर्मणामुत्र भान्ति रुद्रादित्या वसवोऽथापि विश्वे॥
en: Giving up pleasure and controlling his senses he obtains glory from the gods and similarly like the planets and Rudra and Aditya and the Vasus in the heaven shines resplendent through works.

sn: यमो राजा वैश्रवणः कुवेरो गन्धर्वयक्षाप्सरसश्च सूत। ब्रह्मविद्या ब्रह्मचर्य क्रिया च निषेवमाणा ऋषयोऽमुत्र भान्ति॥
en: King Yama, the son of Vishravana, Karna, the Gandharvas, the Yakshas and the celestial nymphs, O Suta and the Rishis in the other world shine resplendent practicing the austerities of a Brahmacharya life and seeking the knowledge of self.

sn: जानन्निमं सर्वलोकस्य धर्म विप्रेन्द्राणां क्षत्रियाणां विशां च। स कस्मात् त्वं जानतां ज्ञानवान् सन् व्यायच्छसे संजय कौरवार्थे॥
en: Knowing all these truths regarding this world and knowing the duties of the best among Brahmanas and the Kshatriyas and the Vaishyas, why do you, who are wise, plead on behalf of the sons of Kurus.

sn: आम्नायेषु नित्यसंयोगमस्य तथाश्वमेधे राजसूये च विद्धिा संयुज्यते धनुषा वर्मणा च हस्यश्वाथै रथशस्त्रैश्च भूयः॥
en: Yudhishthira is ever attached to the study of the Vedas and know him also to be attached to Ashvamedha and Rajasuya sacrificial ceremonies and again riding on cars and on horses and elephants; he also acts with the bow and weapons and puts on armour.

sn: मवगच्छेयुरवधेनैव पार्थाः। दार्ये वृत्ते भीमसेनं निगृह्य॥
en: If the son of Pritha can see some means, not involving the slaughter of the sons of Kuru, their virtue would be saved and a virtuous deed would be done by them by forcing Bhimasena to adopt a more honorable course of life.

sn: ते चेत् पित्र्ये कर्मणि वर्तमाना आपोरन् दिष्टवशेन मृत्युम्। यथाशक्त्या पूरयन्तः स्वकर्म तदप्येषां निधनं स्यात् प्रशस्तम्॥
en: And if by the ordination of fate they should meet with death, while engaged in the work which their ancestors did, then too doing all that lies in their power towards the fulfillment of their duty their death would be praiseworthy.

sn: उताहो त्वं मन्यसे शाम्यमेव राज्ञां युद्धे वर्तते धर्मतन्त्रम्। अयुद्धे वा वरतते धर्मतन्त्रं तथैव ते वाचमिमां शृणोमि॥
en: If you approve of peace, I want to hear your answer to this question-Does the duty of kings lie in fighting or does it lie in not fighting.

sn: मवेक्ष्य त्वं संजय स्वं च कर्म। निशम्याथो पाण्डवानां च कर्म प्रशंस वा निन्द वा या मतिस्ते॥
en: Having considered the principle on which the four divisions were originally based and the duties of each, O Sanjaya and having fully ascertained the proposed line of action of the Pandavas, praise or blame it, as you may think fit.

sn: अधीयीत ब्राह्मणो वै यजेत दद्यादीयात् तीर्थमुख्यानि चैवा अध्यापयेद् याजयेच्चापि याज्यान् प्रतिग्रहान् वा विहितान् प्रतीच्छेत्॥
en: A Brahmana should be steady, perform sacrificial ceremonies, give alms and go to the principal places of pilgrimage; he should also teach and officiate as priest in the ceremonies performed by others who need his help and should accept donations from well known persons.

sn: तथा राजन्यो रक्षणं वै प्रजानां कृत्वा धर्मेणाप्रमत्तोऽथ दत्त्वा। यज्ञैरिष्ट्वा सर्ववेदानधीत्य दारान् कृत्वा पुण्यकृदावसेद् गृहान्॥
en: In the same way, having protected his kingdom and his subjects, making donations to persons leading a holy life and performing sacrificial ceremonies and studied all the Vedas and taken a wife (a Kshatriya) should become a house holder continuing to do virtuous deeds.

sn: स धर्मात्मा धर्ममधीत्य पुण्यं यदिच्छया व्रजति ब्रह्मलोकम्। वित्तं चिन्वन् पालयन्नप्रमत्तः॥
en: The virtuous soul, doing virtuous deeds, roams at his will in the region of Brahma. A Vaishya should study and accumulate wealth by agriculture, keeping cattle and commerce. He should observe these duties intently.

sn: प्रियं कुर्वन् ब्राह्मणक्षत्रियाणां धर्मशीलः पुण्यकृदावसेद् गृहान्। परिचर्या वन्दनं ब्राह्मणानां नाधीयीत प्रतिषिद्धोऽस्य यज्ञः। देवं स्मृतः शूद्रधर्म: पुराणः॥
en: And pleasing the Brahmanas and Kshatriyas, of virtuous habits, he should become a house-holder, doing virtuous deeds. He should serve the Brahmanas and worship them; he should not study; sacrifice is forbidden to him; he should ever be wakeful and sleepless in doing good to beings, such are the duties of a Shudra as laid down in the ancient religious books.

sn: एतान् राजा पालयन्त्रप्रमत्तो नियोजयन् सर्ववर्णान् स्वधर्मे। अकामात्मा समवृत्तिः प्रजासु नाधार्मिकाननुरुध्येत कामान्॥
en: The king, protecting all these intently and employing all these orders in their respective spheres should himself be without any service, impartial to all his subjects and should never give himself to the prompting of his unholy desires.

sn: दभिज्ञातः सर्वधर्मोपपन्नः। स तं दुष्टुमनुशिष्यात् प्रजानां न चैतद् बुध्येदिति तस्मिन्नसाधुः॥
en: If there is any body superior to him (the king) and known to be endued with all virtues, he should instruct his subjects to see him. A bad king will not however observe all this.

sn: यदा गृध्येत् परभूतौ नृशंसो विधिप्रकोपाद् बलमाददानः। ततो राज्ञामभवद् युद्धमेतत् तत्र जातं वर्म शस्त्रं धनुश्च॥
en: When he is desirous of obtaining the wealth of others, growing inhuman and gifted with strength and through the wrath of the creator,

sn: इन्द्रेणैतद् दस्युवधाय कर्म उत्पादितं वर्म शस्त्रं धनुश्च॥
en: There comes into being war, for which again was created armour, weapon and bow. For the purpose of slaying robbers were created armour, weapon and bow by Indra.

sn: तत्र पुण्यं दस्युवधेन लभ्यते सोऽयं दोषः कुरुभिस्तीव्ररूपः। अधर्मज्ञैर्धर्ममबुध्यमानैः प्रादुर्भूतः संजय साधु तन्न।॥
en: In such cases a virtuous deed is done by slaying such a robber and this weakness appears in a large measure in the sons of Kuru. They have been overpowered by a too slight knowledge of virtue and by non-observance of law and religion; O Sanjaya, this is not right.

sn: तत्र राजा धृतराष्ट्रः सपुत्रो धन॑ हरेत् पाण्डवानामकस्मात्। नावेक्षन्ते राजधर्मं पुराणं तदन्वयाः कुरवः सर्व एव॥
en: The king Dhritarashtra with his sons all on a sudden robbed the sons of Pandu of their just inheritance and thus has set at naught the duties observed by kings from times immemorial. And all the Kurus follow him.

sn: स्तेनो हरेद् यत्र धनं ह्यदृष्टः प्रसह्य वा यत्र हरेत दृष्टः। उभौ गौं भवतः संजयैतौ किं वै पृथक्त्वं धृतराष्ट्रस्य पुत्रे॥
en: A thief, when he steals wealth unseen and when he steals it by force, in both these, 0 Sanjaya, he is to blame; what difference (redeeming feature) has the son of Dhritarashtra?

sn: सोऽयं लोभान्मन्यते धर्ममेतं यमिच्छति क्रोधवशानुगामी। स्तं नः कस्मादाददीरन् परे वै॥
en: What he is desirous of following through anger is considered as virtuous by him through avarice. Then again the share of the sons of Pandu is fixed, why should that which is ours be taken away by others?

sn: अस्मिन् पदे युध्यतां नो वधोऽपि श्लाध्य: पित्र्यं परराज्याद् विशिष्टम्। नाचक्षीथाः संजय राजमध्ये॥
en: Under these circumstances, to be killed white fighting would be praise-worthy for us. Ancestral wealth is better than the kingdom of another. Lay these ancient principles before the sons of Kurus amidst the assembled chiefs,

sn: एते मदान्मृत्युवशाभिपन्नाः समानीता धार्तराष्ट्रेण मूढाः। इदं पुन: कर्म पापीय एव सभामध्ये पश्य वृत्तं कुरूणाम्॥
en: The chiefs, that is to say, the fools that have been brought together by the sons of Dhritarashtra and are thus very near the kingdom of Death. Then again look at this sinful act, of the Kurus in the council hall.

sn: प्रियां भार्यां द्रौपदी पाण्डवानां यशस्विनी शीलवृत्तोपपन्नाम्। यदुपैक्षन्त कुरवो भीष्ममुख्या: कामानुगेनोपरुद्धां व्रजन्तीम्॥
en: The Kurus with Bhishma at their head stood by without interference while the Draupadi, the dearly beloved wife of the son of Pandu, that lady of fame and endued with good behaviour, stood weeping in the clutches of that slave of lust.

sn: तं चेत् तदा ते सकुमारवृद्धा अवारयिष्यन् कुरवः समेताः। मम प्रियं धृतराष्ट्रोऽकरिष्यत् पुत्राणां च कृतमस्थाभविष्यत्॥
en: If at that time the sons of Kuru, who were assembled there, old and young, had prevented this, Dhritarashtra would have done what would have pleased me and such behaviour would also have been to the benefit of his sons.

sn: दुःशासन: प्रातिलोम्यान्निनाय सभामध्ये श्वशुराणां च कृष्णाम्। सा तत्र नीता करुणं व्यपेक्ष्य नान्यं क्षत्तु थमवाप किंचित्॥
en: Dushasana brought Krishna by force into the council chamber where there were her fathers-in-law at the time. Brought there she expected kind treatment, but she found there no protector save Vidura.

sn: कार्पण्यादेव सहितास्तत्र भूपा नाशक्नुवन् प्रतिवक्तुं सभायाम्। एकः क्षत्ता धर्म्यमर्थं ब्रुवाणो धर्मबुद्ध्या प्रत्युवाचाल्पबुद्धिम्॥
en: The kings, who were assembled there could not say anything against such treatment, in the council hall, through idiocy; and there was only one Kshatriya, who from a sense of righteousness spoke words indicating virtue and calculated to secure the interest of Krishna, to the one of little intelligence. (Duryodhana).

sn: मथेच्छसे पाण्डवस्योपदेष्टुम्। कृष्णा त्वेतत् कर्म चकार शुद्धं सुदुष्करं तत्र सभां समेत्य॥
en: You did not, then in the council hall, speak one word, but now you want to preach sense to the sons of Pandu. Krishna however accomplished something, in that council, which was right and hard to do.

sn: येन कृच्छ्रात् पाण्डवानुज्जहार तथाऽऽत्मानं नौरिव सागरौघात्। यत्राब्रवीत् सूतपुत्रः सभायां कृष्णां स्थितां श्वशुराणां समीपे॥
en: By this (i.e., the deed of Krishna) she took the sons of Pandu out of their difficulty and herself out of hers, as a sailor takes (a ship) out of the sea waves. There, in that council hall, where was standing Krishna in the presence of her father-in-law, the son of Karna thus addressed her.

sn: न ते गतिविद्यते याज्ञसेनि प्रपद्य दासी धार्तराष्ट्रस्य वेश्म। पराजितास्ते पतयो न सन्ति पतिं चान्यं भाविनि त्वं वृणीष्व॥
en: O daughter of Yajnasena, no other course is left open to you; be a slave in the house of son of Dhritarashtra. Your husband vanquished (at a game of dice) no longer are husbands for you and you of a romantic soul, choose some other husbands for yourself.

sn: दस्थिच्छिन्दन् मर्मघाती सुघोरः। कर्णाच्छरो वाङ्मयस्तिग्मतेजाः प्रतिष्ठितो हृदये फाल्गुनस्य॥
en: The (speech) frightful and sharp as it was, went deep into the heart cutting the very bones. This arrow, of words, proceeding from Karna, possessed the power of fire and is buried in the heart of the son of Phulguna.

sn: कृष्णाजिनानि परिधित्समानान् दुःशासनः कटुकान्यभ्यभाषत्। एते सर्वे षण्ढतिला विनष्टाः क्षयं गता नरकं दीर्घकालम्॥
en: Dushasana also spoke these harsh words when they were about to put on garments made of the skin of black deer. "All these eunuchs vanquished and ruined are going to hell for a long period."

sn: गान्धारराजः शकुनिर्निकृत्या यदब्रवीत् द्यूतकाले स पार्थम्। पराजितो नन्दनः किं तवास्ति कृष्णया त्वं दीव्य वै याज्ञसेन्या॥
en: The king of Gandhara, Shakuni, aiso thus spoke by way of jest to the son of Pritha (Yudhishthira) at the time of playing at dice-"Your younger brother being defeated, what else have you but Krishna, the daughter of Yajnasena. Stake her.'

sn: जानासि त्वं संजय सर्वमेतद् द्यूते वाक्यं गहमेवं यथोक्तम्। स्वयं त्वहं प्रार्थये तत्र गन्तुं समाधातुं कार्यमेतद् विपन्नम्॥
en: You know, O Sanjaya, all these objectionable words, that were said, at the game of dice. I want to go there myself to settle this.

sn: अहापयित्वा यदि पाण्डवार्थ शमं कुरूणामपि चेच्छकेयम्। पुण्यं च मे स्याच्चरितं महोदयं मुच्येरंश्च कुरवो मृत्युपाशात्॥
en: If I can bring about peace without injury to the interests of the sons of Pandu a virtuous act shall have been done by me resulting in great good and at the same time I shall have freed the Kurus from the clutches of death.

sn: अपि मे वाचं भाषमाणस्य काव्यां धर्मारामामर्थवतीमहिनाम्। अवेक्षेरन् धार्तराष्ट्राः समक्षं मां च प्राप्तं कुरवः पूजयेयुः॥
en: I hope that the sons of Dhritarashtra will attend to me when I speak to them words of wisdom, based on the principles of virtue and humanity and that the Kurus will treat me when I go there, with respect.

sn: अतोऽन्यथा रथिना फाल्गुनेन भीमेन चैवाहवदंशितेन। परासिक्तान् धार्तराष्ट्रांश्च विद्धि प्रदह्यमानान् कर्मणा स्वेन पापान्॥
en: If it is otherwise, you may be sure, that the sons of Dhritarashtra who are being consumed by their own vicious deeds, will be rendered devoid of all prosperity by Arjuna in his car and Bhima equipped for fight.

sn: पराजितान् पाण्डवेयांस्तु वाचो रौद्रा रूक्षा भाषते धार्तराष्ट्रः। गदाहस्तो भीमसेनोऽप्रमत्तो दुर्योधनं स्मारयिता हि काले॥
en: The son of Dhritarashtra spoke harsh and rude words to the sons of Pandu when they were defeated (at the game of dice). At the proper time Bhima, with the mace in his hand, will remained Duryodhana (of his language).

sn: सुयोधनो मन्युमयो महाद्रुमः स्कन्धः कर्णः शकुनिस्तस्य शाखाः। दुःशासनः पुष्पफले समृद्धे मूलं राजा धृतराष्ट्रोऽमनीषी॥
en: Suyodhana is a big tree, full of malice Karna the trunk and Shakuni the branch. Dushasana presents its numerous fruits and flowers while the wise king Dhritarashtra is the root.

sn: युधिष्ठिरो धर्ममयो महाद्रुमः स्कन्धोऽर्जुनो भीमसेनोऽस्य शाखाः। माद्रीपुत्रौ पुष्पफले समृद्धे मूलं त्वहं ब्रह्म च ब्राह्मणाश्च।।
en: Yudhishthira is a big tree full of virtue, Arjuna the trunk and Bhimasena its branch. The two sons of Madri represent the numerous fruits and flowers while myself and the Supreme Being and the Brahmanas ate the roots.

sn: वनं राजा धृतराष्ट्रः सपुत्रो व्याघ्रास्ते वै संजय पाण्डुपुत्राः॥ मा वनं छिन्धि सव्यानं मा व्याघ्राऽनीनशन्वनात्॥
en: The king Dhritarashtra with his sons in the forest and the sons of Pandu, O Sanjaya, the tigers. The forest with the tigers cannot be cut down ner the tigers in the forest destroyed.

sn: निर्वनो वध्यते व्याघ्रो निर्व्याघ्रं छिद्यते वनम्। तस्माद् व्याघ्रो वनं रक्षेद् वनं व्याघ्रं च पालयेत्॥
en: The tiger without the forest (to protect it) is easily killed and so is the forest without tigers in it (to overawe people) easily cut down. The tiger therefore protects the forest and the forest the tiger.

sn: लताधर्मा धार्तराष्ट्राः शाला: संजय पाण्डवाः। न लता वर्धते जातु महाद्रुममनाश्रिता॥
en: The sons of Dhritarashtra are the creepers of virtue, while, O Sanjaya, the sons of Pandu are Sala trees. The creeper cannot grow without the support of a big tree.

sn: स्थिताः शुश्रूषितुं पार्थाः स्थिता योद्भुमरिंदमाः। यत् कृत्यं धृतराष्ट्रस्य तत् करोतु नराधिपः॥
en: The sons of Pritha are ready to attend on Dhritarashtra; the subduers of foes are ready for fight. Let the king (Yudhishthira) do what Dhritarashtra is going to do.

sn: स्थिताः शमे महात्मानः पाण्डवा धर्मचारिणः। योधाः समर्थास्तद् विद्वन्नाचक्षीथा यथातथम्॥
en: The noble-minded and virtuous sons of Pandu, though ready and in a position to fight, are yet in peace. Tell them, O wise one all these things as they are.

sn: संजय उवाच आमन्त्रये त्वां नरदेवदेव गच्छाम्यहं पाण्डव स्वस्ति तेऽस्तु। दुच्चारितं मे मनसोऽभिषङ्गात्॥
en: Sanjaya said After bidding you adieu, O god among men, shall I go awayo lord, O son of Pandu, may it be well with you. Has any objectionable language been uttered by me, in the heat of the moment.

sn: जनार्दनं भीमसेनार्जुनौ च माद्रीसुतौ सात्यकिं चेकितानम्। आमन्त्र्य गच्छामि शिवं सुखः वः सौम्येन मां पश्यत चक्षुषा नृपाः॥
en: After bidding adieu also to Janardana, Bhimasena, Arjuna, the two sons of Madri, Satyaki and Chekitana, shall I go away. May happiness and prosperity be yours. May the king look upon us with an eye of good will.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच अनुज्ञातः संजय स्वस्ति गच्छ न नः स्मरस्यप्रियं जातु विद्वन्। विद्मश्च त्वां ते च वयं च सर्वे शुद्धात्मानं मध्यगतं सभास्थम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said Perinitted by ourselves, go away 0 Sanjaya, May you fare well. Do not, O learned man, think ill of us. They and ourselves all know you to be a pure-souled man, in the midst of (their) court.

sn: आप्तो दूतः संजय सुप्रियोऽसि कल्याणवाक् शीलवांस्तृप्तिमांश्च। न मुह्येस्त्वं संजय जातु मत्या न च क्रुद्ध्येरुच्यमानो दुरुक्तैः॥
en: As an enjoy sent (by them) O Sanjaya, you have made yourself dear to us and you are of peaceful speech, well behaved and satisfy every body. You are not ill disposed towards us and through spoken to harshly you are never angry.

sn: न मर्मगां जादु वक्तासि रूक्षां नोपश्रुतिं कटुकां नोत मुक्ताम्। मेतां वाचं तव जानीम सूत॥
en: You are not a speaker of cutting and rude words, nor of harsh or false words. We are aware that your words are based on the principles of virtue, pregnant with meaning and humane, O Suta.

sn: त्वमेव नः प्रियतमोऽसि दूत इहागच्छेद् विदुरो वा द्वितीयः। अभीक्ष्णदृष्टोऽसि पुरा हि नस्त्वं धनंजयस्यात्मसमः सखाऽसि॥
en: You are our favorite; Vidura is the only other envoy that can come here. In former days you were often seen by us and you are our friend like Dhananjaya.

sn: इतो गत्वा संजय क्षिप्रमेव उपातिष्ठेथा ब्राह्मणान् ये तदर्हाः। विशुद्धवीर्याश्चरणोपपन्नाः कुले जाताः सर्वधर्मोपपन्नाः॥
en: Departing from here, O Sanjaya, you should speedily wait on these Brahmanas, who are endued with the practice of pure energy, born in high family and endued with all the virtues.

sn: स्वाध्यायिनो ब्राह्मणा भिक्षवश्च तपस्विनो ये च नित्या वनेषु। स्तथेतरेषां कुशलं वदेथाः॥
en: And those Brahmanas who are devoted to study and devotees living on arms and those who always dwell in the forests. Greeting all these on my behalf, you should enquire the health of these old people and of others as well.

sn: स्तथाऽऽचार्यानृत्विजो ये च तस्य। तैश्च त्वं तात सहितैर्यथार्ह संगच्छेथाः कुशलेनैव सूत॥
en: You should also meet the priest of Dhritarashtra and all his preceptors and Ritvijas and ask them about their health O Suta.

sn: अश्रोत्रिया ये च वसन्ति वृद्धा मनस्विनः शीलबलोपपन्नाः। आशंसन्तोऽस्माकमनुस्मरन्तो यथाशक्ति धर्ममात्रां चरन्तः॥
en: And those, who though not of good blood, are aged, spirited, endued with behaviour and strength, who remember and expect us and practise the slightest virtue, according to their means.

sn: श्लाघस्व मां कुशलिनं स्म तेभ्यो ह्यनामयं तात पृच्छेर्जघन्यम्। ये जीवन्ति व्यवहारेण राष्ट्र ये पालयन्तो निवसन्ति राष्ट्रे॥
en: Inform them of my good health and enquire of them about theirs, as also those who live in the kingdom carrying on the traders and those who live in the kingdom maintaining it (by filling offices of the state).

sn: आचार्य इष्टो नयगो विधेयो वेदानभीप्सन् ब्रह्मचर्यं चचार। योऽस्त्रं चतुष्पात् पुनरेव चक्रे द्रोणः प्रसन्नोऽभिवाद्यस्त्वयाऽसौ॥
en: Our preceptor Drona, who is well versed in the code of morality and who practised the Brahmacharya life wishing for a knowledge of the Vedas and who made the four Padas (viz., mantra, upachara, prayoga and sanhara) his weapon, should be pleased by you after being duly greeted.

sn: अधीतविद्यश्चरणोपपन्नो योऽस्त्रं चतुष्पात् पुनरेव चक्रे। गन्धर्वपुत्रप्रतिम तरस्विनं तमश्वत्थामानं कुशलं स्म पृच्छेः॥
en: You should also enquire about the health of Ashvathama who is endued with the practice of studying and who has read the Vedas and also again has made the four Pandas his weapon and who is strong as the son of a Gandharva.

sn: शारद्वतस्यावसथं स्म गत्वा महारथस्यात्मविदां वरस्या त्वं मामभीक्ष्णं परिकीर्तयन् वै कृपस्य पादौ संजय पाणिना स्पृशेः॥
en: Going to the residence of the son of Sharadvata, of mighty prowess and the chief among those who have a knowledge of self, you should again and again greet him on my behalf and touch the feet of Kripa, O Sanjaya, with your hands.

sn: यस्मिशौर्यमानृशंस्य तपश्च प्रज्ञा शीलं श्रुतिसत्त्वे धृतिश्च। पादौ गृहीत्वा कुरुसत्तमस्य भीष्मस्य मां तत्र निवेदयेथाः॥
en: You should also, touching the feet of that chief among the Kurus, Bhishma in whom are centered heroism, humility, devotion, wisdom, good behaviour, great learning, goodness and prowess, submit my proposals to him.

sn: प्रज्ञाचक्षुर्यः प्रणेता कुरूणां बहुश्रुतो वृद्धसेवी मनीषी। तस्मै राज्ञे स्थविरायाभिवाद्य आचक्षीथाः संजय मामरोगम्॥
en: Saluting the aged king too, who sees by the eyes of wisdom, is the leader of the Kurus, of great learning, who waits upon the old and wise, you should tell him that I am without any disease.

sn: ज्येष्ठः पुत्रो धृतराष्ट्रस्य मन्दो मूर्खः शठः संजय पापशीलः। प्रशास्ता वै पृथिवीं येन सर्वां सुयोधनं कुशलं तात पृच्छेः॥
en: You should also enquire, about the health of Suyodhana, the eldest son of Dhritarashtra, who is dull-headed, ignorant wicked and addicted to vice and, by whom, O Sanjaya, all this world is being ruled over.

sn: स्तथाशीलः संजय सोऽपि शश्वत्। महेष्वासः शूरतमः कुरूणां दुःशासनः कुशलं तात वाच्यः॥
en: You should also enquire, about the health of his younger brother Dushasana, who is dullheaded and of the same behavior (as his elder brother) and who is a great bow man and one of the best heroes among the Kurus.

sn: यस्य कामो वर्तते नित्यमेव नान्यः शमाद् भारतानामिति स्म। स बाह्निकानामृषभो मनीषी त्वंयाभिवाद्यः संजय साधुशीलः॥
en: The one who has no other wish except that there should be peace among the Bharata race, the best among the Balhika's, a wise and honest man, should also be saluted by you.

sn: गुणैरनेकैः प्रवरैश्च युक्तो विज्ञानवान् नैव च निष्ठुरो यः। स्नेहादमर्षं सहते सदैव स सोमदत्तः पूजनीयो मतो मे॥
en: In my opinion Somadatta too should be saluted by you who is endued with many good qualities, wise and merciful and who always subdues his anger towards the Kurus out of affection for them.

sn: अर्हत्तमः कुरुषु सौमदत्तिः स नो भ्राता संजय मत्सखा च। महेष्वासो रथिनामुत्तमोऽर्हः सहामात्यः कुशलं तस्य पृच्छेः॥
en: The most venerable among the Kurus is the son of Somadatta; he is our brother, 0 Sanjaya and my friend as well. He is a good bowman a car-warrior as well and with his counselor, worthy of the highest respect. You should enquire about his health.

sn: ये चैवान्ये कुरुमुख्या युवानः पुत्रा: पौत्रा भ्रातरश्चैव ये नः। यं यमेषां मन्यसे येन योग्यं तत् तत् प्रोच्यानामयं सूत वाच्याः॥
en: Those others, who are high among the Kurus and young and those who are as sons, grand-sons and brothers to us, should also be asked, O Suta, regarding their health, in terms which you consider suitable for each.

sn: ये राजानः पाण्डवायोधनाय समानीता धार्तराष्ट्रण केचित्। वशातयः शाल्वकाः केकयाश्च तथाम्बष्ठा ये त्रिगर्ताश्च मुख्याः॥
en: Those kings who have been brought together by the son of Dhritarashtra for fighting with the Pandavas, the Vashati, the Shalvakas, the Kaikeyas, the Ambasthan and the chief among the Trigartas.

sn: स्तथा प्रतीच्याः पर्वतीयाश्च सर्वे। स्तेषां सर्वेषां कुशलं सूत पृच्छेः॥
en: Those that have come from the east and the north, from the south and the west and all those heroes that have come from the hilly districts, you should ask O Suta, regarding their welfare; (and specially) those among them that are human and endued with good behaviour.

sn: हस्त्यारोहा रथिन: सादिनश्च पदातयश्चार्यसङ्घाः महान्तः। मनामयं परिपृच्छेः समग्रान्॥
en: Of those who ride on elephants and chariots and horses and those who fight on foot, of that assemblage of great and honorable men after informing my welfare, you should ask regarding their health collectively.

sn: तथा राज्ञो ह्यर्थयुक्तानमात्यान् दौवारिकान् ये च सेनां नयन्ति। मर्थांश्च ये महतश्चिन्तयन्ति॥
en: In the same way you should enquire about them that are the financial ministers of the king and the door-keepers and those that lead the army and those that calculate the revenue and expenditure and the great men who ever think about the welfare of the kingdom,

sn: वृन्दारकं कुरुमध्येष्वमूढ़ महाप्रज्ञं सर्वधर्मोपपन्नम्। न तस्य युद्धं रोचते वै कदाचिद् वैश्यापुत्रं कुशलं तात पृच्छेः॥
en: You should also enquire about the health of the son of Dhritarashtra by his Vaishya wife, who is the best among the Kurus and one among them, not a fool, of great wisdom and endued with all virtues. By no means is he inclined to fight.

sn: श्छन्नोपधः साधुदेवी मताक्षः। यो दुर्जयो देवस्थेन संख्ये स चित्रसेनः कुशलं तात वाच्यः॥
en: The one who has no rival in the tricks of dice, whose tricks cannot be detected, who plays dice and who can handle the dice cleverly, who is hard to defeat in the game, viz., Chitrasena, should also be asked concerning his health.

sn: गान्धारराजः शकुनिः पर्वतीयो निकर्तने योऽद्वितीयोऽक्षदेवी। मानं कुर्वन् धार्तराष्ट्रस्य सूत मिथ्याबुद्धेः कुशलं तात पृच्छेः॥
en: The, king of Gandhara, Shakuni, who comes from the hills and who too is unrivaled in the tricks of the dice and who contributes to the honour of the son Dhritarashtra, of false intelligence, should, () Suta, be asked concerning his health.

sn: यः पाण्डवानेकरथेन वीरः समुत्सहत्यप्रधृष्यान् विजेतुम्। यो मुह्यतां मोहयिताद्वितीयो वैकर्तनः कुशलं तस्य पृच्छेः॥
en: The heroes, who above from his car, excepts to defeat the sons of Pandu who are hard to vanquish, the one who is without a rival in de-fooling the fools (sons of Dhritarashtra) viz., (Karna) the son of Vaikartana should also be asked concerning his health.

sn: स एव भक्तः स गुरुः स भर्ता स वै पिता स च माता सुहृच्च। अगाधबुद्धिर्विदुरो दीर्घदर्शी स नो मन्त्री कुशलं तं स्म पृच्छेः॥
en: He who is devoted to our interests, who is our preceptor and lord, who is our father, mother and friend, Vidura of immeasurable wisdom and of good foresight, he who is our adviser, should also be asked concerning his health.

sn: वृद्धाः स्त्रियो याश्च गुणोपपन्ना ज्ञायन्ते न: संजय मातरस्ताः। ताभिः सर्वाभिः सहिताभिः समेत्य स्त्रीभिर्वृद्धाभिरभिवादं वदेथाः॥
en: The aged ladies and those among them who being endued with good qualities are regarded by us, O Sanjaya, as our mothers,. should be greeted when they are all together.

sn: कच्चित् पुत्रा जीवपुत्राः सुसम्यम् वर्तन्ते वो वृत्तिमनृशंसरूपाः। दजातशत्रुः कुशली सपुत्रः॥
en: “O you with living sons, do your sons treat you properly" saying this, O Sanjaya, afterwards tell them that he who has created no enemies is doing well with his sons.

sn: या नो भार्याः संजय वेत्थ तत्र तासां सर्वासां कुशलं तात पृच्छेः। सुसंगुप्ताः सुरभयोऽनवद्या: कच्चिद् गृहानावसथाप्रमत्ताः॥
en: Those who are like our wives, O Sanjaya, should all be asked regarding their health and address them thus-"Are your leading careful lives in your houses, well protected and with fragrant fame and unblamable conduct?

sn: कच्चिद् वृत्तिं श्वशुरेषु भद्राः कल्याणी वर्तध्वमनृशंसरूपाम्। स्तथा वृत्तिमात्मनः स्थापयध्वम्॥
en: O gentle ladies, is your treatment towards your fathers-in-law gentle and considerate? You should secure for yourself such behaviour as will make your husbands kind towards you."

sn: या नः स्नुषाः संजय वेत्थ तत्र प्राप्ताः कुलेभ्यश्च गुणोपपन्नाः। प्रजावत्यो ब्रूहि समेत्य ताच युधिष्ठिरो वोऽभ्यवदत् प्रसन्नः॥
en: Going to those who are like our daughtersin-law, endued with good qualities who have been brought there from good families and with issues, tell them that Yudhishthira who is well disposed towards them sends his greetings.

sn: कन्याः स्वजेथाः सदनेषु संजय अनामयं मद्वचनेन पृष्ट्वा। कल्याणाः वः सन्तु पतयोऽनकूला यूयं पतीनां भवतानुकूलाः॥
en: The daughters of your house, O Sanjaya, should be embraced by you and after asking them about their health on my behalf you should thus address them O blessed ones, may your husbands be favorably disposed towards you and may you be favorably disposed towards your husband.

sn: अलंकृता वस्त्रवत्यः सुगन्धा अबीभत्साः सुखिता भोगवत्यः। लघु यासां दर्शनं वाक् च लध्वी वेशस्त्रियः कुशलं तात पृच्छेः॥
en: You should also, enquire about the health of these ladies who wear ornaments and good cloths on their person, use perfumery, live without any fear, are made happy and in the enjoyment of comforts and whose looks are mild and speech is low.

sn: दास्यः स्युर्या ये च दासाः कुरूणां तदाश्रया बहवः कुब्जखञ्जाः। ऽप्यनामयं परिपृच्छेर्जघन्यम्॥
en: The maid-servants and the male servants and the many hunch-backed and lame men who have been sheltered by them too should after being informed of my welfare be asked regarding their health and spoken to in these terms.

sn: कच्चिद् वृत्ति वर्तते वै पुराणी कच्चिद् भोगान् धार्तराष्ट्रो ददाति। अङ्गहीनान् कृपणान् वामनान् वा यानानृशंस्यो धृतराष्ट्रो बिभति॥ अन्धांश्च सर्वान् स्थविरांस्तथैव हस्त्याजीवा बहवो येऽत्र सन्ति। ऽप्यनामयं परिपृच्छेर्जघन्यम्॥
en: Does the son of Dhritarashtra continue the stipend granted you in old and does he allow you comforts. Those persons of defective limbs, idiots and dwarfs whom the humane Dhritarashtra supports and the many blind persons and decrepit ones and those who live by their hands (having no legs) that are there should be first told of my welfare and then asked about theirs.

sn: मा भैष्ट दुःखेन कुजीवितेन नूनं कृतं परलोकेषु पापम्। निगृह्य शत्रून् सुहृदोऽनुगृह्या वासोभिरनेन च वो भरिष्ये॥
en: Do not be sorry for this uncomfortable life; sins must surely have been committed by you in the life before; after destroying my enemies I shall support them with food and clothes and favour my friends.

sn: सन्त्येव मे ब्राह्मणेभ्यः कृतानि भावीन्यथो नो बत वर्तयन्ति। तान् पश्यामि युक्तरूपांस्तथैव तामेव सिद्धिं श्रावयेथा नृपं तम्॥
en: Ask the king (Duryodhana) if the stipends made by me to Brahmanas are the same (as before); I shall see them properly rewarded and attain to their objects.

sn: मात्मन्येव प्रयतन्तेऽथ मूढाः। ह्यस्मद्वाक्यात् कुशलं तात पृच्छेः॥
en: And those weak persons who have no body to protect them and those that are vainly striving to earn bread for themselves and also those that are ignorant and imbecile should also be asked, regarding their health on my behalf.

sn: ये चाप्यन्ते संश्रिता धार्तराष्ट्रान् नानादिग्भ्योऽभ्यागताः सूतपुत्र। दृष्ट्वा तांश्चैवार्हतश्चापि सर्वान् सम्पृच्छेथाः कुशलं चाव्ययं च॥
en: Those also, that have taken refuge with the sons of Dhritarashtra, coming from different directions, should be asked concerning their health.

sn: एवं सर्वानागताभ्यागतांश्च राज्ञो दूतान् सर्वदिग्भ्योऽभ्युपेतान्। पृष्ट्वा सर्वान् कुशलं तांश्च सूत पश्चादहं कुशली तेषु वाच्यः॥
en: In the same way all the ambassadors, of the king (Dhritarashtra) who have come there from all directions, should first be asked about their health and afterwards they should be told that I am doing well.

sn: न हीदृशाः सन्त्यपरे पृथिव्यां ये योधका धार्तराष्ट्रेण लब्धाः। धर्मस्तु नित्यो मम धर्म एव महाबलः शत्रुनिबर्हणाय॥
en: There is not in the world anything equal to the warriors that have been gained by the son of Dhritarashtra on his side. Virtue is even on my side and virtue is my great strength for the destruction of my enemies.

sn: इदं पुनर्वचनं धार्तराष्ट्र सुयोधनं संजय श्रावयेथाः। यस्ते शरीरे हृदयं दुनोति कामः कुरूनसपत्नोऽनुशिष्याम्॥ त्रैवंविधाः स्याम यथा प्रियं ते। ददस्व वा शक्रपुरी ममैव युध्यस्व वा भारतमुख्य वीर॥
en: You should, O Sanjaya, make Suyodhana, the son of Dhritarashtra hear these words "The desire which is tormenting your heart, to rule the Kurus without any rival, has no justification for it. We shall do nothing that will not be agreeable to you. Either give me back the city of Indra or fight, you chief hero among the race of Bharata."

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच उत सन्तमसन्तं वा बालं वृद्धं च संजय। उताबलं बलीयांसं धाता प्रकुरुते वशे॥
en: Yudhishthira said The creator has, under his control, the good and the bad, the young and the old the weak and the strong.

sn: उत बालाय पाण्डित्यं पण्डितायोत बालताम्। ददाति सर्वमीशानः पुरस्ताच्छुक्रमुच्चरन्॥
en: The supreme lord gives wisdom to the child and childishness to the wise, developing the seed in a being.

sn: बलं जिज्ञासमानस्य आचक्षीथा यथातथम्। अथ मन्त्रं मन्त्रयित्वा याथातथ्येन हृष्टवत्॥
en: To him (Dhritarashtra) desirous of knowing our strength should you say how matters really stand, having cheerfully held a consultation with a view to knowing the true information.

sn: गावल्गणे कुरून् गत्वा धृतराष्ट्र महाबलम्। अभिवाद्योपसंगृह्य ततः पृच्छेरनामयम्॥
en: O son of Gavalgani, going to the Kauravas, you should great king Dhritarashtra of great strength hand touching his feet ask him regarding his health.

sn: ब्रूयाश्चैनं त्वमासीनं कुरुभिः परिवारितम्। तवैव राजन् वीर्येण सुखं जीवन्ति पाण्डवाः॥
en: And you shall say to him, who will be seated surrounded by the Kurus-The sons of Pandu are living happily solely through your prowess.

sn: तव प्रसादाद बालास्ते प्राप्ता राज्यमरिंदम्। राज्ये तान् स्थापयित्वाग्रे नोपेक्षस्व विनश्यतः॥
en: It was through your grace, O subduer of enemies, that they thought mere boys obtained a kingdom. First establishing them in the kingdom, do not treat them with carelessness or they would be ruined.

sn: सर्वमप्येतदेकस्य नालं संजय कस्यचित्। तात संहत्य जीवामो द्विषतां मा वशं गमः॥
en: All this kingdom is too much, O Sanjaya, for any body. You should say this speaking on our behalf-Sire, we shall live united; do not go into the clutches of despisers.

sn: तथा भीष्मं शान्तनवं भारतानां पितामहम्। शिरसाभिवदेथास्त्वं मम नाम प्रकीर्तयन्॥
en: In the same way should you bow down your head, on my behalf, to the grandsire of the race of Bharata, Bhishma, the son of Shantanu.

sn: अभिवाद्य च वक्तव्यस्ततोऽस्माकं पितामहः। भवता शन्तनोवंशो निमग्नः पुनरुद्धृतः॥
en: After being greeted, our grandsire should thus be addressed-By you was the race, of Shantanu when about to be involved in ruin, was extricated.

sn: स त्वं कुरु तथा तात स्वमतेन पितामह। यथा जीवन्ति ते पौत्राः प्रीतिमन्तः परस्परम्॥
en: You, who have done this, now do what according to your own opinion, O Grandsire, will enable your grandsons to live in peace and amity with each other.

sn: तथैव विदुरं ब्रूयाः कुरूणां मन्त्रधारिणम्। अयुद्धं सौम्य भाषस्व हितकामो युधिष्ठिरे॥
en: In the same way should you thus speak to Vidura, the adviser of the Kurus, "O you peaceful one, advice peace, O you well wisher of Yudhishthira."

sn: अथ दुर्योधनं ब्रूया राजपुत्रममर्षणम्। मध्ये कुरूणामासीनमनुनीय पुनः पुनः॥
en: And then speak to the wrathful prince Duryodhana seated in the midst of the Kurus entreating him again and again.

sn: अपापां यदुपैक्षस्त्वं कृष्णामेतां सभागताम्। तद् दुःखमतितिक्षाम मा वधीष्म कुरूनिति॥
en: "The insults you have offered to the blameless Krishna who had been brought to this council hall, we will quietly endure so that the Kurus may not be slaughtered.

sn: एवं पूर्वापरान् क्लेशानतितिक्षन्त पाण्डवाः। बलीयांसोऽपि सन्तो यत् तत् सर्वं कुरवो विदुः॥
en: The Pandavas will quietly bear similar insults offered before and after that though they are strong enough. All this the Kauravas know.

sn: यन्नः प्रव्राजयः सौम्य अजिनैः प्रतिवासितान्। तद् दुःखमतितिक्षाम मा वधिष्म कुरूनिति॥
en: O amiable one, you sent us into exile with raiment's made of deer skin on. This hardship shall we quietly bear so that the Kurus may not be slaughtered.

sn: यत् कुन्ती समतिक्रम्य कृष्णां केशेष्वधर्षयत्। दुःशासनस्तेऽनुमते तच्चास्माभिरुपेक्षतम्॥
en: O Dushasana, it was at your bidding that Krishna was dragged here by the hair setting at naught the protest of Kunti. That too is forgiven by us.

sn: अथोचितं स्वकं भागं लभेमहि परंतप। निवर्तय परद्रव्याद् बुद्धिं गृद्धां नरर्षभ॥
en: But o repressor of enemies, we want our due share; O best among men, turn away your avaricious inclination from what belongs to others.

sn: शान्तिरेवं भवेद् राजन् प्रीतिश्चैव परस्परम्। राज्यैकदेशमपि नः प्रयच्छ शममिच्छताम्॥
en: By this means, O king, there shall be peace and good will among each other; give back to us, who are desirous of peace, even one province out of the kingdom.

sn: अविस्थलं वृकस्थलं माकन्दी वारणावतम्। अवसानं भवत्वत्र किंचिदेकं च पञ्चमम्॥
en: Give us Avisthala, Vrikasthala, Makandi and Varanavata, with any other village for a fifth and let there be an end of our quarrel over this matter.

sn: भ्रातृणां देहि पञ्चानां पञ्च ग्रामान् सुयोधन। शान्ति!ऽस्तु महाप्राज्ञ ज्ञातिभिः सह संजया॥
en: O Suyodhana, give but five villages to your five cousins and let there be peace among ourselves and our cousins, O Sanjaya of great wisdom.

sn: भ्राता भ्रातरमन्वेतु पिता पुत्रेण युज्यताम्। स्मयमानाः समायान्तु पाञ्चालाः कुरुभिः सह।॥
en: Let brother follow brother and let father unite with son. Let the Panchala join the Kurus with a smiling face.

sn: अक्षतान् कुरुपाञ्चालान् पश्येयमिति कामये। सर्वे सुमनसस्तात शाम्याम भरतर्षभ॥
en: I desire that I shall see the Kauravas and the Panchalas, without any wounds and we shall all establish peace with cheerful hearts, O you best among the race of Bharata.

sn: अलमेव शमायास्मि तथा युद्धाय संजय। धर्मार्थयोरलं चाहं मृदवे दारुणाय च॥
en: I am surely ready for peace and to war as well, O Sanjaya. For the acquirement of wealth, am I surely prepared to mild measures and harsh ones.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच अनुज्ञातः पाण्डवेन प्रययौ संजयस्तदा। शासनं धृतराष्ट्रस्य सर्वं कृत्वा महात्मनः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Then did Sanjaya, permitted by the son of Pandu, depart, doing all the behest's of the great-souled Dhritarashtra.

sn: सम्प्राप्य हास्तिनपुरं शीघ्रमेव प्रविश्य च। अन्तःपुरं समास्थाय द्वा:स्थं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Having reached Hastinapura, he entered it quickly and standing at the gate (entrance of the) inner apartments of the palace said these words to the gate-keeper.

sn: आचक्ष्व धृतराष्ट्राय द्वाःस्थ मां समुपागतम्। सकाशात् पाण्डुपुत्राणां संजयं मा चिरं कृथाः॥
en: Tell Dhritarashtra, O gate-keeper, that, I, Sanjaya, have returned from the presence of the sons of Pandu, delay not.

sn: जागर्ति चेदभिवदेस्त्वं हि द्वाःस्थ प्रविशेयं विदितो भूमिपस्य। निवेद्यमत्रात्ययिकं हि मेऽस्ति द्वाःस्थोऽथ श्रुत्वा नृपति जगाम्॥
en: If he is awake, tell him this, O gate-keeper and make the ruler of the earth acquainted with (the news of) my entrance (into the city); I have business to submit to him. Hearing this, the gate-keeper went to the king.

sn: द्वा:स्थ उवाच संजयोऽथ भूमिपते नमस्ते दिदृक्षया द्वारमुपागतस्ते। प्राप्तो दूतः पाण्डवानां सकाशात् राजन् किमयं करोतु।॥
en: The gate-keeper said O you lord of the earth, I bow down to you. Sanjaya is come to your door, desirous of an audience. He is arrived here as an envoy from the presence of the sons of Pandu. Command, O king, as to what he should do.

sn: प्रशाधि है धृतराष्ट्र उवाच आचक्ष्व मां कुशलिनं कल्पमस्मै प्रवेश्यतां स्वागतं संजयाय। न चाहमेतस्य भवाम्यकल्पः स मे कस्माद् द्वारि तिष्ठेच्च सक्तः॥
en: Dhritarashtra said Inform him of my well-being. Let him enter. Welcome to Sanjaya. I am never unwilling to receive him, why does he, who can enter at any moment, stand at my door.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततः प्रविश्यानुमते नृपस्य महद् वेश्म प्राज्ञशूरार्यगुप्तम्। सिंहासनस्थं पार्थिवमाससाद वैचित्रवीर्यं प्राञ्जलि: सूतपुत्रः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Then with the king's permission, the son of Suta having entered that large hall with clasped hands, approached the royal so Vichitravirya, seated on the throne and protected by wise men, heroes and honorable men.

sn: संजय उवाच संजयोऽहं भूमिपते नमस्ते प्राप्तोऽस्मि गत्वा नरदेव पाण्डवान्। अभिवाद्य त्वां पाण्डुपुत्रो मनस्वी युधिष्ठिरः कुशलं चान्वपृच्छत्॥
en: Sanjaya said I am Sanjaya, I bow down to the lord of the earth. Setting out from here, I reached the sons of Pandu, O god among men. The spirited Yudhishthira having sent his greetings to you, afterwards asked me about your health.

sn: स ते पुत्रान् पृच्छति प्रीयमाण: कच्चित् पुत्रैः परीयसे नप्तृभिश्च। तथा सुहृद्भिः सचिवैश्च राजन् ये चापि त्वामुपजीवन्ति तैश्च॥
