en: Falls into a deep mire which he cannot cross. A wise man should have an eye on the following six means of secrets being divulged.

sn: मदं स्वप्नमविज्ञानमाकारं चात्मसम्भवम्। दुष्टामात्येषु विश्रम्भं दूताच्चाकुशलादपि॥ द्वाराण्येतानि यो ज्ञात्वा संवृणोति सदा नृप। त्रिवर्गाचरणे युक्तः स शत्रूनधितिष्ठति॥ न वै श्रुतमविज्ञाय वृद्धाननुपसेव्य वा। धर्मार्थों वेदितुं शक्यौ बृहस्पतिसमैरपि।॥
en: He who desires wealth and children should ever keep himself away from these-vanity, dream, knowledge that spies have been set on, one's demeanor which depends on his thoughts, excessive trust on wicked ministers and incompetent ambassadors. He who being fully aware of these six door ( through which secrets ooze out). O king, keeps them always closed and engages in the attainment of the three kinds of objects (virtue, worldly good and desire), triumph over his enemies. Without a knowledge of the holy books and without proper reverence to old people.

sn: नष्टं समुद्रे पतितं नष्टं वाक्यमशृण्वति। अनात्मनि श्रुतं नष्टं नष्ट हुतमनग्निकम्॥
en: Virtue and profit cannot be known even by one equal (intelligent) to Brihaspati; A thing is lost when it falls into the ocean. So an advice is lost when it is not listened.

sn: मत्या परीक्ष्य मेधावी बुद्ध्या सम्पाद्य चासकृत्। श्रुत्वा दृष्ट्वाथ विज्ञाय प्राझैमैत्री समाचरेत्॥
en: The holy books are lost on those who have no souls of their own (have no control over them); and an offering of clarified butter is lost when poured on what is not fire (i.e. when the fire has been extinguished and ashes only remain). Having examined by his intelligence and searched by his understanding.

sn: अकीर्ति विनयो हन्ति हन्त्यनर्थं पराक्रमः। हन्ति नित्यं क्षमा क्रोधमाचारो हन्त्यलक्षणम्॥
en: And having heard the opinions of other men seen and known the life of the men, a wise man forms friendship with wise men. Humility removes bad repute and prowess puts an end to adversity.

sn: परिच्छदेन क्षेत्रेण वेश्मना परिचर्यया। परीक्षेत कुलं राजन् भोजनाच्छादनेन च॥
en: Forgiveness ever destroys anger; good behaviour neutralises the effects of evil omens in the appearance of a man. By means of one's dress, sphere of action, house, behaviour,

sn: उपस्थितस्य कामस्य प्रतिवादो न विद्यते। अपि निर्मुक्तदेहस्य कामरक्तस्य किं पुनः॥
en: Should a man's lineage be jaded about, O king and also by his food and dress. There is no struggling with a desire when it come on.

sn: प्राज्ञोपसेविनं वैद्यं धार्मिकं प्रियदर्शनम्। मित्रवन्तं सुवाक्यं च सुहृदं परिपालयेत्॥
en: Even in men who have attained salvation not to speak of those who are slaves to their desires. One who worships the wise is learned, virtuous and of a mild look.

sn: दुष्कुलीनः कुलीनो वा मर्यादां यो न लङ्घयेत्। धर्मापेक्षी मृदुह्रीमान् स कुलीनशताद् वरः॥
en: And has friends, is one, who of agreeable speech, has good heart, should me protected. He, who whether comes of a high or a low family, dose not transgress the houour due to others.

sn: ययोश्चित्तेन वा चित्तं निभृतं निभृतेन वा। समेति प्रज्ञया प्रज्ञा तयोमैत्री न जीर्यति॥
en: Who leans to virtue, who is graced with humility, who has a sense of modesty, is better than a hundred men coming of high families. When the heart of one agrees with that of another, then the secret pursuits of the former are the same as those of the latter.

sn: दुर्बुद्धिमकृतप्रज्ञं छन्नं कूपं तृणैरिवा विवर्जयीत मेधावी तस्मिन् मैत्री प्रणश्यति॥
en: And the learning of the former is the same as that of the latter, the friendship between the two person never wears out. One who has a wicked soul, one whose understanding has not been cultivated.

sn: अवलिप्तेषु मूर्खेषु रौद्रसाहसिकेषु च। तथैवापेतधर्मेषु न मैत्रीमाचरेद् बुधः॥
en: Should be shunned by an intelligent man like a well covered over with grass growing over it; friendship with them does not last. With those that are proud, ignorant, fierce and rash.

sn: कृतज्ञं धार्मिकं सत्यमक्षुद्रं दृढभक्तिकम्। जितेन्द्रियं स्थितं स्थित्यां मित्रमत्यागि चेष्यते॥
en: Wise men should never contract friendship, nor with them who have fallen from the path of virtue. The man who is grateful, virtuous, the reverse of mean, has firm devotion.

sn: इन्द्रियाणामनुत्सर्गो मृत्युनापि विशिष्यते। अत्यर्थं पुनरुत्सर्गः सादयेद् दैवतान्यपि॥
en: And has his senses under control and attaches himself to what ought to be attached to should be desired for a friend. The renouncement of the objects of the senses is worse than death difficult of practices.

sn: मार्दवं सर्वभूतानामनसूया क्षमा धृतिः। आयुष्याणि बुधाः प्राहुर्मित्राणां चाविमानना॥
en: On the other hand, leaving them to be too much exercised would ruin the gods even; humility, kindness to all creatures, forgiveness and patience.

sn: अपनीतं सुनीतेन योऽर्थं प्रत्यानिनीषते। मतिमास्थाय सुदृढां तदकापुरुषव्रतम्॥
en: Conduce to life, the wise men have said; as also a constant respect for friends. He who desires again to accomplish, by virtuous means, an object that has once been frustrated,

sn: आयत्यां प्रतिकारशस्तदात्वे दृढनिश्चयः। अतीते कार्यशेषज्ञो नरोऽथैर्न प्रहीयते॥
en: And is in his right senses, the determination of that man is firm. The man who knows what remedy ought to be applied in future, who has a firm determination on present matters.

sn: कर्मणा मनसा वाचा यदभीक्ष्णं निषेवते। तदेवापहरत्येनं तस्मात् कल्याणमाचरेत्॥
en: And who knows (in beginning) how acts done in the past would end accomplishes all his objects. That which a man follows in deed, thought or speech.

sn: मङ्गलालम्भनं योगः श्रुतमुत्थानमार्जवम्। भूतिमेतानि कुर्वन्ति सतां चाभीक्ष्णदर्शनम्॥
en: Draws him away to itself; therefore a virtuous policy should be followed. Efforts for the attainment of one's holy objects, knowledge of the holy books, simplemindedness.

sn: अनिर्वेदः श्रियो मूलं लाभस्य च शुभस्य च। महान् भवत्यनिर्विण्णः सुखं चानन्त्यमश्नुते॥
en: These bring on prosperity; so do constant meetings with the good. Perseverance is the root the of prosperity and of gain and of happiness.

sn: नातः श्रीमत्तरं किंचिदन्यत् पथ्यतमं पतम्। प्रभविष्णोर्यथा तात क्षमा सर्वत्र सर्वदा॥
en: That man who pursues his object with perseverance and who is not annoyed at the long time a think takes to accomplish, that man is really great and gets unending happiness. It is my opinion that there is no better means of bringing in prosperity.

sn: क्षमेदशक्तः सर्वस्य शक्तिमान् धर्मकारणात्। अर्थानौ समौ यस्य तस्य नित्यं क्षमा हिता॥
en: Than for really strong man to exercise forgiveness at all times and at all places. The weak should forgive every body and the strong should forgive for the sake of virtue. He to whom the attainment and the non-attainment of an object is the same is ever forgiving.

sn: यत् सुखं सेवमानोऽपि धर्मार्थाभ्यां न हीयते। कामं तदुपसेवेत न मूढव्रतमाचरेत्॥
en: That happiness which when pursued dose not injure the virtue or the worldly profit of a man should be enjoyed one so may desire but he should not act like a fool (by giving himself up entirely to enjoyment).

sn: दुःखार्तेषु प्रमत्तेषु नास्तिकेष्वलसेषु च। न श्रीर्वसत्यदान्तेषु ये चोत्साहविवर्जिताः॥
en: In those that are overpowered by grief, in those that are too much attached to anything, in those that deny the existence of God and in those that are lazy, prosperity dose not reside, nor in those who have no control over their souls and who are devoid of all enthusiasm.

sn: आर्जवेन नरं युक्तमार्जवात् सव्यपत्रपम्। अशक्तं मन्यमानास्तु धर्षयन्ति कुबुद्धयः॥
en: Persons of bad intelligence oppress people endued with humility and modesty by reason of that humility, thinking them to be weak.

sn: अत्यार्यमतिदातारमतिशूरमतिव्रतम्। प्रज्ञाभिमानिनं चैव श्रीयानोपसर्पति॥
en: To those who are honest in the extreme, who give away in large measures, who are too heroic, who are of too firm determination and who are vain of their wisdom, prosperity never comes out of fear.

sn: न चातिगुणवत्स्वेषा नात्यन्तं निर्गुणेषु च। नैषा गुणान् कामयते नैर्गुण्यानानानुरज्यते। उन्मत्ता गौरिवान्धा श्रीः क्वचिदेवावतिष्ठते॥
en: Nor (dose prosperity reside) in persons endued with every virtue nor in those having none; she (prosperity) dose not desire a strong combination of good qualities. Prosperity resides in some one (without any fixed rule) like a mad cow.

sn: अग्निहोत्रफला वेदाः शीलवृत्तफलं श्रुतम्। रतिपुत्रफला नारी दत्तभुत्तफलं धनम्॥
en: The result of (the study of) the Vedas is the performance of the Home; the result of a knowledge of the holy books is good manners and good conduct. The fruits of a woman are the pleasures of co-habitation and offspring; and the consequences of wealth are the pleasure of gift and enjoyment.

sn: अधर्मोपार्जितैरथैर्यः करोत्यौदेहिकम्। न स तस्य फलं प्रेत्य भुङ्क्तेऽर्थस्य दुरागमात्॥
en: He who performs ceremonies for his good in the other world with wealth got by foul means. Dose not get the usual fruits of such ceremonies after death owing to the foul means by which the wealth was got.

sn: कान्तारे वनदुर्गेषु कृच्छ्रास्वापत्सु सम्भ्रमे। उद्येतेषु च शस्त्रेषु नास्ति सत्त्ववता भयम्॥
en: In deserts, foresees, in difficulties and calamities or when weapons are raised (by others to strike him) he who has a strong mind has no fear.

sn: उत्थानं संयमो दाक्ष्यमप्रमादो धृतिः स्मृतिः। समीक्ष्य च समारम्भो विद्धि मूलं भवस्य तु॥
en: Energy, self-control, skillfulness steadiness, patience and the act of beginning a thing after mature thought, know these to be the roots of prosperity.

sn: तपो बलं तापसानां ब्रह्म ब्रह्मविदां बलम्। हिंसा बलमसाधूनां क्षमा गुणवतां बलम्॥
en: Devotion is the strength of asceticism; the Vedas are the strength of those that know what is in them. Injury is the strength of those that are vicious; forgiveness is the strength of those that are endued with good qualities.

sn: अष्टौ तान्यव्रतनानि आपो मूलं फलं पयः। हविर्ब्रह्मणकाम्या च गुरोर्वचनमौषधम्॥
en: These eight do not lead to the nonobservance of a vow-water, roots, fruits, milk, clarified butter, acts done at the desire of a Brahmana or the commands of an elder and medicine.

sn: न तत् परस्य संदध्यात् प्रतिकूलं यदात्मनः। संग्रहेणैष धर्मः स्यात् कामादन्यः प्रवर्तते॥
en: That should not be done to others which is against the interest of one's self. This is virtue, put tersely; there are other sorts of virtue, but it is not compulsory that they (the better) should be acted up to.

sn: अक्रोधेन जयेत् क्रोधमसाधु साधुना जयेत्। जयेत् कदर्यं दानेन जयेत् सत्येन चानृतम्॥
en: Anger should be subjugated by the reverse of anger; and virtuous man should be subjugated by virtue, by gifts should a miser be subjugated, by truth one addicted to untruth should be won.

sn: स्त्रीधूर्तकेऽलसे भीरौ चण्डे पुरुषमानिनि। चौरे कृतघ्ने विश्वासो न कार्यो न च नास्तिके॥
en: A woman, a cunning and deceitful person, one that is lazy, one that is fierce, one that is wrathful, one that is vain of his own power, a thief, one that is ungrateful should never be trusted; nor should atheist.

sn: अभिवादनशीलस्य नित्यं वृद्धोसेविनः। चत्वारि सम्प्रवर्धन्ते कीर्तिरायुर्यशो बलम्॥
en: He who has the habit of doing due honours to his elders and who always attends to the wishes of old persons, gets an increase of these four, viz., good name, life, fame and strength.

sn: अतिक्लेशेन येऽर्थाः स्युर्धर्मस्यातिक्रमेण वा। अरेर्वा प्रणिपातेन मा स्म तेषु मनः कृथाः॥
en: The prosperity which can be attained by excessive toil or by the non-observance of the principles of honesty, or by blowing to an enemy, do not set your heart on these.

sn: अविद्यः पुरुषः शोच्यः शोच्यं मैथुनमप्रजम्। निराहाराः प्रजाः शोच्याः शोच्यं राष्ट्रमराजकम्॥
en: One who is ignorant ought to be pitied; and intercourse that does not produce offspring ought to be pitied. The subjects of a king who go without food are to be pitied; and anarchy in a kingdom ought to be regretted.

sn: अध्वा जरा देहवतां पर्वतानां जलं जरा। असम्भोगो जरा स्त्रीणां वाक्शल्यं मनसो जरा॥
en: The roads are the sources of pain and weakness to those beings who have bodies; and water is the source of pain and weakness to the mountains, non-enjoyment is the source of pain to women; and harshness in speech is the source of pain to the mind.

sn: अनाम्नायमला वेदा ब्राह्मणस्याव्रतं मलम्॥ मलं पृथिव्या बाह्रीकाः पुरुषस्यानृतं मलम्। कौतूहलमला साध्वी विप्रवासमला: स्त्रियः॥
en: Not taking the name even, is the worst thing for the Vedas; not observing religious observances, the worst act of the Brahmanas; the Balhika's (a race of people, morally dead) are the worst inhabitants of the globe. Falsehood is the worst thing in a man. Curiosity is the worst thing in a chaste woman; and exile from home is the worst thing for all women.

sn: सुवर्णस्य मलं रूप्यं रूप्यस्यापि मलं त्रपु। ज्ञेयं त्रपुमलं सीसं सीसस्यापि मलं मलम्॥
en: The worst part of gold is silver; tin is the worst part of silver; lead should be known as the worst part of tin; and dust is the worst part of lead.

sn: न स्वप्नेन जयेन्निद्रां न कामेन जयेत् स्त्रियः। नेन्धनेन जयेदग्नि न पानेन सुरां जयेत्॥
en: The inclination to sleep cannot be got over by lying down; women cannot be won by desire; fire cannot be won by wood and excess drinking cannot be conquered by drinking.

sn: यस्य दानजितं मित्रं शत्रवो युधि निर्जिताः। अन्नपानजिता दाराः सफलं तस्य जीवितम्॥
en: He, whose friends have been won by gifts, whose enemies vanquished in battle, whose wife won over by food and drink, has his life crowned with success.

sn: सहस्रिणोऽपि जीवन्ति जीवन्ति शतिनस्तथा। धृतराष्ट्र विमुञ्चेच्छां न कथञ्चिन्न जीव्यते॥
en: Life is real to those who have thousands (of anything or everything); life is also real to those (in a small measure) who have hundreds. 0 Dhritarashtra, renounce this (excessive) desire; there is none who cannot live by some means or other.

sn: यत् पृथिव्यां व्रीहियवं हिरण्यं पशवः स्त्रियः। नालमेकस्य तत् सर्वमिति पश्यन् न मुह्यति॥
en: All the grains, gold, animals and women that are in this world are not sufficient even for one man. Seeing all this a wise man does not grieve (for possession of everything).

sn: राजन् भूयो ब्रवीमि त्वां पुत्रेषु सममाचर। समता यदि ते राजन् स्वेषु पाण्डुसुतेषु वा॥
en: O king, again do I ask you to behave equally well with all your sons; let there be equality between your own sons and the sons of Pandu.

sn: विदुर उवाच योऽभ्यर्चितः सद्भिरसज्जमानः करोत्यर्थं शक्तिमहापयित्वा। मलं प्रसन्ना हि सुखाय सन्तः॥
en: Vidura said The good man who, respected by the virtuous, is engaged in the attainment of his objects without going beyond his limits, soon gains fame, for good beings when gratified with a good man give him happiness.

sn: महान्तमप्यर्थमधर्मयुक्तं यः संत्यजत्यनपाकृष्ट एव। सुखं सुदुःखान्यवमुच्य शेते जीर्णां त्वचं सर्प इवावमुच्य॥
en: He who forsakes, without any inducement, a grand object which is fraught with unrighteousness, lies in happiness free from misery like a snake casting off the worn out slough.

sn: अनृते च समुत्कर्षो राजगामि च पैशुनम्। गुरोचालीकनिर्बन्धः समानि ब्रह्महत्यया॥
en: A victory gained by untruth, a deceit that reaches (in its injurious effects) a king and the expression of false intentions before an elder na. are

sn: असूयैकपदं मृत्युरतिवादः श्रियो वधः। अशुश्रूषा त्वरा श्लाघा विद्यायाः शत्रवस्त्रयः॥
en: A monopoly of jealously, death and vanity conduce to the destruction of prosperity. The want of proper attention to the elder, haste and boastfulness the three enemies of knowledge.

sn: आलस्यं मदमोहौ च चापलं गोष्ठिरेव च। स्तब्धता चाभिमानित्वं तथात्यागित्वमेव च। एते वै सप्त दोषाः स्युः सदा विद्यार्थिनां मताः॥
en: Laziness, inattention and confusion of the brains, unsteadiness, clubbing together, haughtiness, variety and covetousness.

sn: सुखार्थिनः कुतो विद्या नास्ति विद्यार्थिनः सुखम्। सुखार्थी वा त्येजद् विद्या विद्यार्थी वा त्यजेत् सुखम्।।
en: These seven are ever the defects in those that are striving for knowledge, is my opinion; where is knowledge in those that care for pleasures and there is pleasure for those that care for knowledge. Knowledge should pronounce pleasure.

sn: नाग्निस्तृप्यति काष्ठानां नापगानां महोदधिः। नान्तकः सर्वभूतानां न पुंसां वामलोचना॥
en: One who cares for pleasures should renounce knowledge; and one that cares for knowledge should renounce pleases. Fire is never satiated with fuel; the great ocean, with rivers; death, with all the creatures; and a pretty woman, with men.

sn: आशा धृति हन्ति समृद्धिमन्तकः क्रोधः श्रियं हन्ति कदर्यता। त्रेकः क्रुद्धो ब्राह्मणो हन्ति राष्ट्रम्॥
en: Hope kills patience; death kills development; anger kills prosperity; miserliness kills fame; want of proper tending kills animals; and, O king, one single wrathful Brahmana destroys a kingdom,

sn: अजाश्च कांस्यं रजतं च नित्यं मध्वाकर्षः शुकनिः श्रोत्रियश्च। वृद्धो ज्ञातिरवसन्नः कुलीन एतानि ते सन्तु गृहे सदैव।॥
en: Goats, white metal, silver, honey, that which draws away (poison), birds, Brahmanas having a knowledge of the holy books, old cousins, persons of good birth but poor, let these ever stay in your house.

sn: अजोक्षा चन्दनं वीणा आदर्शो मधुसर्पिषी। विषमौदुम्बरं शङ्खः स्वर्णनाभोऽथ रोचना॥
en: Goat, bull, sandal, flute, mirror, honey, clarified butter, iron, copper utensil, conchshells, pieces of stone (images of Vishnu) with gold within and Rochana (a pigment prepared from the urine and dung of cow).

sn: गृहे स्थापयितव्यानि धन्यानि मनुरब्रवीत्। देवब्राह्मणपूजार्थमतिथीनां च भारत॥
en: Are always to be kept in a blessed houseManu has said-for the proper worship of the gods, the Brahmanas and guests, OBharata.

sn: इदं च त्वां सर्वपरं ब्रवीमि पुण्यं पदं तात महाविशिष्टम्। न जातु कामान भयान्न लोभाद् धर्मं जह्याज्जीवितस्यापि हेतोः॥
en: I now speak of another sacred lesson, O sire, superior in sacredness to all these, fraught with a large meaning. Virtue should not be forsaken out of desire, fear, temptation, nor for the sake of life itself.

sn: नित्यो धर्मः सुखदुःखे त्वनित्ये जीवो नित्यो हेतुरस्य त्वनित्यः। त्यक्त्वानित्यं प्रतितिष्ठस्व नित्ये संतुष्य त्वं तोषपरो हि लाभः॥
en: Virtue is stable; happiness and misery are unstable; life is stable but its ever recurring phases unstable; forsaking the unstable; keep yourself attached to the stable and be satisfied, for satisfaction is superior to all other acquirements.

sn: महाबलान् पश्य महानुभावान् प्रशास्य भूमिं धनधान्यपूर्णाम्। राज्यानि हित्वा विपुलांश्च भोगान् गतान् नरेन्द्रान् वशमन्तकस्य॥
en: Behold rulers of men endued with great strength and great luster. After having ruled the land abouunding in wealth and corn, they have forsaken their kingdoms and great sources of enjoyments and have been subject to the God of death.

sn: मृतं पुत्रं दुःखपुष्टं मनुष्या उत्क्षिप्य राजन् स्वगृहान्निर्हरन्ति। तं मुक्तकेशाः करुणं रुदन्ति चितामध्ये काष्ठमिव क्षिपन्ति॥
en: Men after having taken away a dead son tended with greatest care, O king, set out from their own houses; and with the hair hanging loose they mourn for him piteously and then throw him into the funeral pyre like a piece of wood.

sn: अन्यो धनं प्रेतगतस्य भुङ्क्ते वयांसि चाग्निश्च शरीरधातून्। द्वाभ्यामयं सह गच्छत्यमुत्र पुण्येन पापेन च वेष्ट्यमानः॥
en: The corn and wealth of the dead are enjoyed by others; and the elements of the body are eaten up by fire and birds. Surrounded by these two only, viz., virtue and sin, does a man go to the other world.

sn: उत्सृज्य विनिवर्तन्ते ज्ञातयः सुहृदः सुताः। अपुष्पानफलान् वृक्षान् यथा तात पतत्रिणः॥
en: After leaving behind the body, do the cousins, friends and sons return as birds do trees devoid of blossoms and fruits.

sn: अग्नौ प्रास्तं तु पुरुषं कर्मान्वेति स्वयंकृतम्। तस्मात् तु पुरुषो यत्नाद् धर्मं संचिनुयाच्छनैः॥
en: Deeds done by his own self follow a man thrown into the funeral pyre; therefore should a man carefully and in slow degrees pick up the fruits of virtue.

sn: अस्माल्लोकादूर्ध्वममुष्य चाधो महत् तमस्तिष्ठति ह्यन्धकारम्। तद् वै महामोहनमिन्द्रियाणां बुध्यस्व मा त्वां प्रलभेत राजन्॥
en: Elsewhere, above this world and also below, there is the greatest darkness. In these regions, know, O king, that the senses are totally stupefied; may such places be not yours.

sn: निशम्य सर्वं प्रतिपत्तुमेव। यशः परं प्राप्स्यसि जीवलोके भयं न चामुत्र न चेह तेऽस्ति।॥
en: After listening to these world of mine, if you can follow them in their entirely, you will get great fame in this world of living beings and you will never meet with fear here in this world or elsewhere.

sn: आत्मा नदी भारत पुण्यतीर्था सत्योदका धृतिकूला दयोर्मिः। तस्यां स्नातः पूयते पुम्यकर्मा पुण्यो ह्यात्मा नित्यमलोभ एव॥
en: The soul is as the river, O Bharata, having several holy spots; truth is as its waters; selfcontrol, its banks; and kindness, its waves; the man of virtuous acts purifies himself be a bath therein; the soul is pure and the absence of desire is a virtue.

sn: कामक्रोधग्राहवतीं पञ्चेन्द्रियजला नदीम्। नावं धृतिमयीं कृत्वा जन्मदुर्गाणि संतर॥
en: Making a boat of your self-control in the river (of life which has the five senses for its water and desire and anger its monsters, cross over (i.e. get rid of) the waves of repeated births.

sn: प्रज्ञावृद्धं धर्मवृद्धं स्वबन्धु विद्यावृद्धं वयसा चापि वृद्धम्। कार्याकार्ये पूजयित्वा प्रसाद्य यः सम्पृच्छेन्न स मुह्येत् कदाचित्॥
en: He who after doing due honours to such of his friends as are old in wisdom, old in virtue, old in knowledge and old in age asks them regarding what ought to be done and what ought not to be done is seldom deceived.

sn: धृत्या शिश्नोदरं रक्षेत् पाणिपादं च चक्षुषा। चक्षुःश्रोत्रे च मनसा मनो वाचं च कर्मणा॥
en: By patience should lust and greediness be restrained; by the ages should the hands and feet be controlled, the eyes and ears by the mind; and the mind and speech by one's actions.

sn: नित्योदकी नित्ययज्ञोपवीती नित्यस्वाध्यायी पतितान्नवर्जी। सत्यं ब्रुवन् गुरवे कर्म कुर्वन् न ब्राह्मणश्च्यवते ब्रह्मलोकात्॥
en: The Brahmana, ever attached to the performance of his ablutions, ever having the holy thread on his body, ever studying (the Vedas), who avoids food touched or offered by a person who has lost his caste, who always speaks the truth and fulfills his duties towards his elders, never falls down from the region of Brahma.

sn: निष्ट्वा यज्ञैः पालयित्वा प्रजाश्च। गोब्राह्मणार्थ शस्त्रपूतान्तरात्मा हतः संग्रामे क्षत्रियः स्वर्गमेति॥
en: After having studied the Vedas, poured offerings fire, performed sacrificial ceremonies, protected subjects, made his inner self blessed by drawing his weapons for the protection of cows and Brahmanas and being killed in battle, a Kshatriya goes to heaven.

sn: वैश्योऽधीत्य ब्राह्मणान् क्षत्रियांश्च धनैः काले संविभज्याश्रितांश्च। त्रेतापूतं धूममाघ्राय पुण्यं प्रेत्य स्वर्गे दिव्यसुखानि भुङ्क्ते॥
en: A Shudra, after worshipping in due order Brahmanas, Kshatriyas and Vaishyas; and a Vaishya, having completed his study and on distributed his wealth among Brahmanas and Kshatriyas and among his dependents and after having smelt the sacred smokes purified by the three sorts of fire, enjoy heavenly bliss after death.

sn: ब्रह्म क्षत्रं वैश्यवर्णं च शूद्रः क्रमेणैतान् न्यायतः पूजयानः। स्त्यक्त्वा देहं स्वर्गसुखानि भुङ्क्ते॥
en: These having been satisfied, they become devoid of sins by burning them and casting off their body enjoy heavenly bliss.

sn: चातुर्वर्ण्यस्यैष धर्मस्तवोक्तो हेतुं चानुब्रुवतो मे निबोध। स्तं त्वं राजन् राजधर्मे नियुक्ष्वा॥
en: Such are the duties of the four orders told to you. Listen to the reason of my describing them. The son of Pandu (Yudhishthira) is falling from the duties of a Kshatriya; O king, you place him in a position to discharge the duties of a king.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच एवमेतद् यथा त्वं मामनुशाससि नित्यदा। ममापि च मतिः सौम्य भवत्येवं यथाऽऽत्य माम्॥३०
en: Dhritarashtra said It is even as you have been instructing me constantly; my inclination, too, turns towards peace, of which you speak to me.

sn: सा तु बुद्धिः कृताप्येवं पाण्डवान् प्रति मे सदा। दुर्योधनं समासाद्य पुनर्विपरिवर्तते॥
en: My inclination through made to turn towards the Pandavas constantly turns away in a contrary; direction by coming in contact with Duryodhana.

sn: न दिष्टमभ्यतिक्रान्तुं शक्यं भूतेन केनचित्। दिष्टमेव ध्रुवं मन्ये पौरुषं तु निरर्थकम्॥
en: Destiny cannot be transgressed by any created beings. I consider that destiny alone is certain; human exertion is vain.

description: The parley between Vidura and Dhritarashtra
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच अनुक्तं यदि ते किंचिद् वाचा विदुर विद्यते। तन्मे शुश्रूषतो ब्रूहि विचित्राणि हि भाषसे।॥
en: Dhritarashtra said If there is anything you have left unsaid, O Vidura, speak to me who am listening to you. You are speaking of interesting things.

description: The parley between Vidura and Dhritarashtra
sn: विदुर उवाच धृतराष्ट्र कुमारो वै यः पुराणः सनातनः। सनत्सुजातः प्रोवाच मृत्यु स्तीति भारत॥
en: Vidura said O Dhritarashtra, the ancient and eternal Rishi Sanat-Sujata, who lived a life of perpetual celibacy, said that there was no death, O Bharata.

description: The parley between Vidura and Dhritarashtra
sn: स ते गुह्यान् प्रकाशांश्च सर्वान् हृदयसंश्रयान्। प्रवक्ष्यति महाराज सर्वबुद्धिमतां वरः॥
en: That chief among intelligent beings will speak to you. O great king, on the subjects thought of by you, whether you have made them known or kept them locked up in your heart.

description: The parley between Vidura and Dhritarashtra
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच किं त्वं न वेद तद् भूयो ब्रूयात् सनातनः। त्वमेव विदुर ब्रूहि प्रज्ञाशेषोऽस्ति चेत् तव॥
en: Dhritarashtra said Do you not know what that internal being will say to me? You, O Vidura, speak (about these things) if your mind has that limit of wisdom.

description: The parley between Vidura and Dhritarashtra
sn: विदुर उवाच शूद्रयोनावहं जातो नातोऽन्यद् वक्तुमुत्सहे। कुमारस्य तु या बुद्धिर्वेद तां शाश्वतीमहम्॥
en: Vidura said I am born among the Shudra class; for that reason, I do not dare say anything more (than what I have already said); the knowledge of that celebrate being, however, is considered by me as eternal.

description: The parley between Vidura and Dhritarashtra
sn: ब्राह्मी हि योनिमापन्नः सुगुह्यमपि यो वदेत्। न तेन गह्यो देवानां तस्मादेतद् ब्रवीमि ते॥
en: He, born is the Brahmana class, even when speaking of highly mysterious affairs, will not incur the blame of the gods; therefore I am speaking thus to you.

description: The parley between Vidura and Dhritarashtra
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवा ब्रवीहि विदुर त्वं मे पुराणं तं सनातनम्। कथमेतेन देहेन स्यादिहैव समागमः॥
en: Dhritarashtra said Tell me, O Vidura, how I can with this body of mine meet with that ancient and eternal being in this world.

description: The parley between Vidura and Dhritarashtra
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच चिन्तयामास विदुरस्तमृषि शंसितव्रतम्। स च तच्चिन्तितं ज्ञात्वां दर्शयामास भारत॥
en: Vaishampayana said Then did Vidura think of that Rishi of rigid austerities; he, too, becoming aware of that thought showed himself then, O Bharata.

description: The parley between Vidura and Dhritarashtra
sn: स चैनं प्रतिजग्राह विधिदृष्टेन कर्मणा। सुखोपविष्टं विश्रान्तमथैनं विदुरोऽब्रवीत्॥
en: Vidura, too, received him by the rites prescribed by custom; and Vidura addressed him when he (the latter) was seated at his ease and taking rest.

description: The parley between Vidura and Dhritarashtra
sn: भगवन् संशयः कश्चिद् धृतराष्ट्रस्य मानसः। यो न शक्यो मया वक्तुं त्वमस्मै वक्तुमर्हसि॥
en: O Lord, there is certainly a doubt in the mind of Dhritarashtra, which cannot be removed by me; therefore it is fitting that you should speak to him (and remove the doubt).

description: The parley between Vidura and Dhritarashtra
sn: यं श्रुत्वायं मनुष्येन्द्रः सर्वदुःखातिगो भवेत्। लाभालाभौ प्रियद्वेष्यौ यथैनं न जरान्तकौ॥ विषहेरन् भयामर्षी क्षुत्पिपासे मदोद्भवौ। अरतिश्चैव तन्द्री च कामक्रोधौ क्षयोदयौ॥
en: Hearing which (your speech) this chief among men will be past all misery; so that gain and the reverse of gain, what is agreeable and disagreeable, old age and death, fear and jealously, hunger and thirst, pride and prosperity, disinclination for women, sleep, desire, anger, loss and gain may be borne by him (with ease).

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततो राजा धृतराष्ट्रो मनीषी सम्पूज्य वाक्यं विदुरेरितं तत्। सनत्सुजातं रहिते महात्मा पप्रच्छ बुद्धि परमां बुभूषन्।॥
en: Vaishampayana said Then the high-souled and wise king Dhritarashtra, after having supported the speech made by Vidura, questioned SanatSujata in private, desirous of obtaining the highest knowledge.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच सनत्सुजात यदिदं शृणोमि न मृत्युरस्तीति तव प्रवादम्। देवासुरा ह्याचरन् ब्रह्मचर्यममृत्यवेतत्कतरन्नु सत्यम्।।२।
en: Dhritarashtra said O Sanat-Sujata, I hear that in your opinion, death does not exist. The gods and the Asura however practiced austere asceticism for the sake of immortality, Wish of these is true?

sn: सनत्सुजात उवाच अपृच्छः कर्मणा केचिन्मृत्युर्नास्तीति चापरमु। शृणु मे ब्रुवतो राजन् यथैतन्मा विशङ्किथाः॥
en: Sanat-Sujata said You have asked how death is avoided by certain actions and how it does not exit at all. Listen to me, discoursing on this, and do not be moved by doubts for this (inconsistency).

sn: उभे सत्ये क्षत्रियैतस्य विद्धि मोहान्मृत्युः सम्मतोऽयं कवीनाम्। प्रमादं वै मृत्युमहं ब्रवीमि तथाप्रमादममृतत्वं ब्रवीमि॥
en: Both of these (statements) are true; know what is the great death in the opinion of the wise. Ignorance is death. In the same way, I say that there is no death where there is no ignorance.

sn: प्रमादाद् वै असुराः पराभवनप्रमादाद ब्रह्मभूताः भवन्ति। नैव मृत्युर्व्याघ्र इवात्ति जन्तून् न ह्यस्य रूपमुपलभ्यते हि॥
en: From ignorance do the Asuras become subject (to death); and from the reverse of ignorance do they attain to the conditions of Brahma. Death does not destroy animals like a tiger; its shape cannot be known.

sn: रात्मावसन्नममृतं ब्रह्मचर्यम्। पितृलोके राज्यमनुशास्ति देवः शिवः शिवानामशिवोऽशिवानाम्॥
en: Current opinion is that Yama is one sort of Death; the wearing out of the soul is said to be another sort; the pursuit of Brahman or selfknowledge is immortality. The god (Yama) rules the region of the Pitris, conferring blessings on the honest and curses on the dishonest.

sn: अस्यादेशानिःसरते नराणां क्रोधः प्रमादो लोभरूपश्च मृत्युः। अहंगतेनैव चरन् विमार्गान् न चात्मनो योगमुपैति कश्चित्॥
en: At his command there is death in the form of anger, ignorance and covetousness among men; out of vanity they follow unrighteous paths; and of them attains selfknowledge.

sn: ते मोहितास्तद्वशे वर्तमाना इतः प्रेतास्तत्र पुनः पतन्ति। ततस्तान् देवा अनुविप्लवन्ते अतो मृत्युर्मरणाख्यामुपैति॥
en: They stripped of intellect and being subject to vanity and being dead in this world fall into hell repeatedly and to hell they go accompanied by their senses. This sort of death also is known by the name of "death". none

sn: स्तत्रानु ते यान्ति न तरन्ति मृत्युम्। सदर्थयोगानवगमात् समन्तात् प्रवर्तते भोगयोगेन देही॥
en: Those, however, who have faith in the fruits of actions, when the time for the fruits comes, go to heaven, without meeting with Death (i.e. they simply transfer their souls elsewhere. Creatures having bodies, however), owing to their incapacity to understand Brahman and owing to their being wedded to earthly enjoyments have come to this world again and again, in all directions (i.e. sometimes they are born in the same position as before, at other times they are born higher or lower according to the effects of their work).

sn: तद् वै महामोहनमिन्द्रियाणां मिथ्यार्थयोगस्य गतिहि नित्या। मिथ्यार्थयोगामिहतान्तरात्मा स्मरनुपास्ते विषयान् समन्तात्॥
en: Man has a natural inclination towards objects that are unreal; and this inclination cause the senses to be led into very grave errors. The inner soul, directed towards objects that are unreal and remembering only the objects in which it was employed, worships only the enjoyments, by which it is surrounded.

sn: अभिध्या वै प्रथमं हन्ति लोकान् कामक्रोधावनुगृह्याशु पश्चात्। एते बालान् मृत्यवे प्रापयन्ति धीरास्तु धैर्येण तरन्ति मृत्युम्॥
en: The remembrance of earthy enjoyments is the first cause of death to men; afterwards come desire (to have those enjoyments) and anger (at the failure to have enjoyments from or other). These (i.e. the remembrance of enjoyments, desire and anger) cause death to be met with by boys (men of little sense); but those that have successes in controlling their souls cross over death unharmed by means of their self-restraint.

sn: दनादरेणाप्रतिबुध्यमानः। नैनं मृत्युर्मृत्युरिवात्ति भूत्वा एवं विद्वान् यो विनिहन्ति कामान्॥
en: some cause He who has succeeded in controlling his soul, having an eye on himself kills (keeps away from) his soaring desires regarding them as not worth having by means of his selfknowledge. The (real) Death assuming the form of death (as known to the people in general) cannot destroy that learned man who controls his desires in this way.

sn: कामानुसारी पुरुषः कामाननु विनश्यति। कामान् व्युदस्य धुनुते यत् किंचित् पुरुषो रजः॥
en: A man who follows his desires is destroyed soon after the desires (are destroyed). The man, however, who can control his desires can keep away from woes in whatever form they come.

sn: तमोऽप्रकाशो भूतानां नरकोऽयं प्रदृश्यते। मुह्यन्त इव धावन्ति गच्छन्तः शुभ्रवत् सुखम्॥
en: Desire appears to be ignorance, darkness and hell of all creatures (for when they follow desire, they loose all control over their senses). Persons following desire run on like intoxicated men towards the drains and holes of this life.

sn: अमूढवृत्तेः पुरुषस्येह कुर्यात् किं वै मृत्युस्तार्ण इवास्य व्याघ्रः। नाधीयीत निर्गुदनिवास्य चायुः॥
en: What can death do in this world to a person, whose habits of life are not led by desire. Death is to him like a tiger made of straw. Therefore, for the destruction of the cause of the life (existence) of desire, (which means ignorance) every wish is to be disregarded; and the slightest one is not to be given a place in the mind even.

sn: स क्रोधलोभौ मोहवानन्तरात्मा स वै मृत्युस्त्वच्छरीरे य एषः। एवं मृत्यु जायमानं विदित्वा ज्ञाने तिष्ठन् न बिभेतीह मृत्योः। र्मृत्योर्यथा विषयं प्राप्य मर्त्यः॥
en: That inner soul exists in your body, wedded to wrath and desire as it is like death; and knowing that death is generated in this way, the person who puts his faith in knowledge is not afraid of death. Death itself is destroyed when it comes under the influence of knowledge, even as earthly beings are destroyed when they come under the influence of death.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच यानेवाहुरिज्यया साधुलोकान् द्विजातीनां पुण्यतमान् सनातनान्। तेषां परार्थं कथयन्तीह वेदा एतद् विद्वान् नोपैति कथं नु कर्म॥
en: Dhritarashtra said The blessed regions, highly sacred and eternal, to which, it is said, the twice-born can go by the performance of sacrificial ceremonies, are declared by the Vedas of offer emancipation to mortals. Having got this knowledge why should not learned man engage in acts in this world.

sn: सनत्सुजात उवाच एव ह्यविद्वानुपयाति तत्र तत्रार्थजातं च वदन्ति वेदाः। अनीह आयाति परं परात्मा प्रयाति मार्गेण निहत्य मार्गान्॥
en: Sanat-Sujata said He that is not learned goes there, (to those blessed regions) by this means (performance of sacrificial ceremonies) and the Vedas say that in those regions are to be attained the true objects of life. He that has renounced all desires gains emancipation at once; but he who confuses the material body with the soul, if he can renounce desire, obtains emancipation but if emancipation is sought without the renunciation of desires, then must one proceed step by step along the path, killing it (the path) by itself (i.e. when a particular grade has been attained, the path already crossed over must be killed; or the chances of his retracing the steps being once more degraded must be removed).

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच कोऽसौ नियुङ्क्ते तमजं पुराणं स चेदिदं सर्वमनुक्रमेणा किं वास्य कार्यमथवा सुखं च तन्म विद्वन् ब्रूहि सर्वं यथावत्॥
en: Dhritarashtra said Who is he that induces action into the Ancient Being without birth? If it is He who has pervaded everything, what can be His action or His happiness? O learned Being, speak to me about all this truly.

sn: सनत्सुजात उवाच दोषो महानत्र विभेदयोगे ह्यनादियोगेन भवन्ति नित्याः। दनादियोगेन भवन्ति पुंसः॥
en: Sanat-Sujata said There is great inconsistency in the complete identification of things that are essentially different. Creatures comes into existence by the union of the Supreme Soul with certain conditions of time, place, etc., that have no beginning. The fact of such being the case in no way lessens the importance or supremacy of Him (the unborn and ancient one) in the slightest degree. Men, too, come into existence by the union of Him that has no beginning (with certain conditions of time, place, etc.).

sn: य एतद् वा भगवान् स नित्यो विकारयोगेन तथा च तच्छक्तिरिति स्म मन्यते तथार्थयोगे च भवन्ति वेदाः॥
en: The Supreme Being by his constant transformation creates this universe; the Vedas make it plain that the Supreme Being possesses the power (of constant transformation) and that He is the cause of transformation in this world.

sn: करोति विश्वम्। धृतराष्ट्र उवाच येऽस्मिन्धर्मान् नाचरन्तीह केचित् तथा धर्मान् केचिदिहाचरन्ति। दुताहो धर्मः प्रतिहन्ति पापम्॥
en: Dhritarashtra said Some there are in this world who practice virtue and some that do not practice virtue but renounce all sorts of actions. (Regarding the former I ask) Is virtue destroyed by unrighteousness or does righteousness destroy virtue?

sn: सनत्सुजात उवाच उभयमेव तत्रोपयुज्यते फलं धर्मस्यैवेतरस्य च॥
en: Sanat-Sujata said The fruits of virtue and also those of the other (complete inaction), both of these are of use that respect (for obtaining emancipation).

sn: तस्मिन् स्थितो वाप्युभयं हि नित्यं ज्ञानेन विद्वान् प्रतिहन्ति सिद्धम्। तथान्यथा पुण्यमुपैति देही तथागतं पापमुपैति सिद्धम्॥
en: Both are of use in obtaining emancipation. The wise man, however, is successful (in obtaining it) be means of knowledge. In other case, the man, who ascribes an undue importance to the body, acquires the merit of his actions (and hence also emancipation); but having obtained emancipation falls therefrom.

sn: गत्वोभय कर्मणा युज्यतेऽस्थिरं शुभस्य पापस्य स चापि कर्मणा। धर्मेण पापं प्रणुदतीह विद्वान् धर्मो बलीयानिति तस्य सिद्धिः॥
en: Having acquired both (i.e. the fruits of virtue and vice) which have an end (men of action attains heaven or hell for a limited time only), men of action again come into this world and become attached to actions by reasons of their previous virtue of vice. A wise man neutralizes the effects of his sinful acts by his virtues. Virtue is strong and hence his emancipation.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच यानिहाहुः स्वस्य धर्मस्य लोकान् द्विजातीनां पुण्यकृतां सनातनान्। तेषां क्रमान् कथय ततोऽपि चान्यान् नैतद् विद्वन् वेत्तुमिच्छामि कर्म॥
en: Dhritarashtra said Those ancient and sacred regions of this „rn by their own virtuous acts-speak of them according to their degree (of sacredness). Speak also of other (sinless) regions. O learned one, I do not desire to know (the merit) of actions.

sn: सनत्सुजात उवाच येषां व्रतेऽथ विस्पर्धा बले बलवतामिव। ते ब्राह्मणा इतः प्रेत्य ब्रह्मलोकप्रकाशकाः॥
en: Sanat-Sujata said These Brahmanas, who are proud of their austerities like powerful men of strength, on their exit from the world shine in the eternal regions.

sn: येषां धर्मे च विस्पर्धा तेषां तज्ज्ञानसाधनम्। ते ब्राह्मणा इतो मुक्ताः स्वर्ग यान्ति त्रिविष्टपम्॥
en: Those who are proud of their virtuous acts acquire the merit of having performed sacrificial ceremonies-such blessed persons freed from this world go to heaven, the abode of the gods.

sn: तस्य सम्यक् समाचारमाहुर्वेदविदो जनाः। नैनं मन्येत भूयिष्ठं बाह्यमाभ्यन्तरं जनम्॥
en: Due performance of these (sacrificial ceremonies) again is said to be compulsory by some persons having a knowledge of the Vcdas; but such persons should not be thought very highly of for, through seeking the truth of inner self, they put undue importance to eternal forins.

sn: यत्र मन्येत भूयिष्ठं प्रावृषीव तृणोपलम्। अन्नं पानं ब्राह्मणस्य तज्जीवेन्नानुसंज्वरेत्॥
en: Whenever (in whatever family) food and drink fit for a Brahmana abound like grass and reeds in the spots, there should (a Yogi) go for his living and not pain himself (by hunger and thirst).

sn: यत्राकथयमानस्य प्रयच्छत्यशिवं भयम्। अतिरिक्तमिवाकुर्वन् स श्रेयान् नेतरो जनः॥
en: In a place where there is fear of great danger for not proclamation one's superiority, he who does not do so (speak out his superiority) is worthier than the other (who does).

sn: यो वा कथयमानस्य ह्यात्मान् नानुसंज्वरेत्। ब्रह्मस्वं नोपभुञ्जीत तदन्नं सम्मतं सताम्॥
en: He who is not pained by another proclaiming his (the latter) true worth and who eats his food after offering it to the gods, the food offered by such a man is approved by the righteous.

sn: यथा स्वं वान्तमश्नाति श्वा वै नित्यमभूतये। एवं ते वान्तमश्नन्ति स्ववीर्यस्योपसेवनात्॥
en: As dogs eat up their own vomit to their constant injury, so they who proclaim their own worth eat up their own vomit.

sn: नित्यमज्ञातचर्या मे इति मन्येत ब्राह्मणः। ज्ञातीनां तु वसन् मध्ये तं विदुर्ब्राह्मणं बुधाः॥
en: That man is to be regarded as a Brahmana whose religious practices remain ever unknown even to the members of his family among whom he lives, wise men also know him to be a Brahmana.

sn: को हनन्तरमात्मानं ब्राह्मणो हन्तुमर्हति। निर्लिङ्गमचलं शुद्धं सर्वद्वैतविवर्जितम्॥ तस्माद्धि क्षत्रियस्यापि ब्रह्मावसति पश्यति॥
en: What other Brahmana is worthy to know the supreme soul, that has no form, is without change, is alone and is devoid of all sorts of duality. By the performance of such practices, the supreme soul resides in a Kshatriya too and is seen by him.

sn: योऽन्यथा सन्तमात्मानमन्यथा प्रतिपद्यते। किं तेन न कृतं पापं चौरेणात्मापहारिणा॥
en: He who considers that heaven is attainable by actions alone and so employs himself in action, what sin is not committed by that thief who robs the soul (of its true attributes)?

sn: अश्रान्तः स्यादनादाता सम्मतो निरुपद्रवः। शिष्टो न शिष्टवत् स स्याद् ब्राह्मणो ब्रह्मवित् कविः।।
en: He who never exerts himself, never accepts gifts from others, who is respected quiet, who though well versed (in the holy books) does not seem to be well versed, is a Brahmana-a wise man knowing Brahman or the Supreme soul.

sn: अनाढ्या मानुषे वित्ते आढ्या दैवे तथा क्रतौ। ते दुर्धर्षा दुष्प्रकम्प्यास्तान् विद्याद् ब्रह्मणस्तनुम्॥
en: Those, who are but poor in what is regarded as wealth by ordinary men, are yet rich in heavenly wealth and in devotion and become hard to vanquish and without fear reside and they become equal to Brahma for their learning.

sn: सर्वान् स्विष्टकृतो देवान् विद्याद् इह कश्चन। न समानो ब्राह्मणस्य तस्मिन् प्रयतते स्वयम्॥
en: That man, who in this world having performed all sorts of sacrifices comes to know the gods, cannot be equal to one knowing Brahma; for he (the former) has to exert himself.

sn: यमप्रयतमानं तु मानयन्ति स मानितः। न मान्यमानो मन्येत न मान्यमभिसंज्वरेत्॥
en: He, who is honoured (by the gods) without any action, is honoured (like one knowing the true nature of the inner self). If honoured (by others than gods) a man should not think himself really honoured; and he should not be sorry at others not honouring him.

sn: लोकः स्वभाववृत्तिर्हि निमेषोन्मेषवत् सदा। विद्वांसो मानयन्तीह इति मन्येत मानितः॥
en: People follow their natural inclinations in the same way as they close or open their eyelids; and the man that is respected should consider that it is the learned only in this world that respect others.

sn: अधर्मनिपुणा मूढा लोके मायाविशारदाः। न मान्यं मानयिष्यन्ति मान्यानामवमानिनः॥
en: Those wretches again in this world who are adepts at unrighteousness and at deceit do not respect those that are worthy of respect. On the contrary, they insult those who ought to be respected.

sn: न वै मानं च मौनं च सहितौ वसतः सदा। अयं हि लोको मानस्य असौ मौनस्य तद् विदुः।।४४
en: The esteem of the world and the vow of silence (holy asceticism) can never dwell together. Know that this (world) is for those who want esteem and the other for those that have observed the vow of silence.

sn: श्रीः सुखस्येह संवासः सा चापि परिपन्थिनी। ब्राह्मी सुदुर्लभा श्रीहि प्रज्ञाहीनेन क्षत्रिय॥
en: In this world, respect resides in worldly prosperity, through it is an impediment to virtue. Heavenly prosperity is not attainable by one that is devoid of (true) wisdom, O Kshatriya.

sn: द्वाराणि तस्येह वदन्ति सन्तो बहुप्रकाराणि दुराधराणि। सत्यार्जवे ह्रीर्दमशौचविद्या यथा न मोहप्रतिबोधनानि।।
en: Virtuous men speak of several doors in this world to heavenly prosperity, which are difficult of being properly watched. The doors are truthfulness, kindness, modesty, selfcontrol and knowledge which are antidotes of ignorance.

description: The speech as delivered by Sanat-Sujata
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच कस्यैष मौनः कतरन्नु मौनं प्रब्रूहि विद्वन्निह मौनभावम्। मौनेन विद्वानुत याति मौनं कथं मुने मौनमिहाचरन्ति॥
en: Dhritarashtra said What purpose does the practice of asceticism serve? Which is better, the practice of asceticism or the vow of silence? Speak to me, O learned one, the real nature of asceticism. Can a learned person attain to the state of the Supreme Being by the vow of silence? How in this world O Muni, is asceticism practiced?

description: The speech as delivered by Sanat-Sujata
sn: सनत्सुजात उवाच मनुप्रविशन्ति ततोऽथमौनम्। यत्रोत्थितो वेदशब्दस्तथाऽयं स तन्मयत्वेन विभाति राजन्॥
en: Sanat-Sujata said Since not even a knowledge of the Vedas, applied with all possible concentration of the mind, penetrates into the Supreme Soul; therefore is it (the Supreme Soul) called Mauna (asceticism) from which is derived the Vedas and which, on account of its being pregnant with the knowledge of the Vedas, reigns supreme, O king.

description: The speech as delivered by Sanat-Sujata
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच ऋचो यजूंषि यो वेद सामवेदं च वेद यः। पापानि कुर्वन् पापेन लिप्यते किं न लिप्यते॥
en: Dhritarashtra said He who is conversant with the Rig and Yajurvedas and also with the Samaveda, is such a man, having committed sins, guilty thereof?

description: The speech as delivered by Sanat-Sujata
sn: सनत्सुजात उवाच नैनं सामान्यूचो वापि न यजूंष्यविचक्षणम्। त्रायन्ते कर्मणः पापान ते मिथ्या ब्रवीम्यहम्॥
en: Sanat-Sujata said I speak no falsehood to you when I declare that neither the Sama nor the Yajur nor the Rigvedas do rescue a man, who has no control over his senses, from his sin.

description: The speech as delivered by Sanat-Sujata
sn: नच्छन्दांसि वृजिनात् तारयन्ति मायाविनं मायया वर्तमानम्। श्छन्दांस्येनं प्रजहत्यन्तकाले॥
en: The hymns of the Veda do not rescue from sin the cheat that lives by deception. Like a bird which has got feathers forsaking its nest, the hymns forsake such a man when his end comes.

description: The speech as delivered by Sanat-Sujata
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच न चेद् वेदा विना धर्मं त्रातुं शक्ता विचक्षण। अथ कस्मात् प्रलापोऽयं ब्राह्मणानां सनातनः॥
en: Dhritarashtra said If the Vedas, without the aid of virtue, are not competent to rescue (men from sins), 0 you, who have control over your senses, then whence is this false and old idea of the Brahmanas (that a knowledge of the Vedas rescues a man from sins)?

description: The speech as delivered by Sanat-Sujata
sn: सनत्सुजात उवाच तस्यैव नामादिवेशेषरूपैरिदं जगद् भाति महानुभाव। निर्दिश्य सम्यक् प्रवदन्ति वेदास्तद् विश्वरैरूप्यमुदाहरन्ति॥
en: Sanat-Sujata said This universe shines (has come into existence) from the Supreme Soul and is distinct from the latter in name, form etc. The Vedas, too, pointing this out declare that the universe is distant (from Supreme Soul).

description: The speech as delivered by Sanat-Sujata
sn: ताभ्यामसौ पुण्यमुपैति विद्वान्। पुण्येन पापं विनिहत्य पश्चात् संजायते ज्ञानविदीपितात्मा॥
en: Sacrificial ceremonies and asceticism are prescribed for that object (i.e. for attaining to the Supreme Soul). By means of these two does a man man of leaning acquire virtue? Destroying sins by sins by virtuous deeds, he afterwards has his soul illuminated with knowledge.

description: The speech as delivered by Sanat-Sujata
sn: नथान्यथा वर्गफलानुकाक्षी। ममुत्र भुङ्क्ते पुनरेति मार्गम्॥
en: A learned man by his knowledge, attains to the Supreme Soul; an unwise man desiring the fruits of the fold objects of humanity in general, having taken with him the effects of acts done here, enjoys them in the other world and (when the enjoyment is over) comes back again to bridge along the same path.

description: The speech as delivered by Sanat-Sujata
sn: अस्मॅिल्लोके तपस्तप्तं फलमन्यत्र भुज्यते। ब्राह्मणानामिमे लोका धात्वे तपसि तिष्ठताम्॥
en: The fruits of asceticism in this world are enjoyed in the other (by those who have not brought their souls under their control); but to those blessed persons engaged in austerities these regions yield fruits.

description: The speech as delivered by Sanat-Sujata
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच कथं समृद्धमसमृद्धं तपो भवति केवलम्। सनत्सुजात् तद् ब्रूहि यथा विद्याम तद् वयम्॥
en: Dhritarashtra said How can asceticism which is ever the same be successful now and unsuccessful at another time. O Sanat-Sujata, tell us this that we two may know it.

description: The speech as delivered by Sanat-Sujata
sn: सनत्सुजात उवाच निष्कल्मषं तपस्त्वेतत् केवलं परिचक्षते। एतत् समृद्धमप्युद्धं तपो भवति केवलम्॥
en: Sanat-Sujata said Asceticism unstained by faults (desire, insufficient concentration etc.) alone leads to emancipation; this (asceticism) is successful; other sorts of devotion are unsuccessful.

description: The speech as delivered by Sanat-Sujata
sn: तपोमूलमिदं सर्वं यन्मां पृच्छसि क्षत्रिय। तपसा वेदविद्वांसः परं त्वतमाप्नुयुः॥
en: What you ask me, O Kshatriya, have all their bases on asceticism do learned men know the Supreme Soul and win immortality.

description: The speech as delivered by Sanat-Sujata
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच कल्मषं तपसो ब्रूहि श्रुतं निष्कल्मषं तपः। सनत्सुजात येनेदं विद्यां गुह्यं सनातनम्॥
en: Dhritarashtra said Speak about asceticism stained by fruits; I have heard all about that unstained by faults, by which, O Sanat-Sujata, I have come to know of an ancient mystery.

description: The speech as delivered by Sanat-Sujata
sn: सनत्सुजात उवाच स्तथा नृशंसानि दशत्रि राजन्। धर्मादयो द्वादशैते पितॄणां शास्त्रे गुणा ये विदिता द्विजानाम्॥
en: Sanat-Sujata said Stained asceticism is that which has for its faults the twelve (vices) with anger at the beginning as also the thirteen descriptions of wickedness, O king. The twelve virtues having righteousness at the beginning which are known to the twice-born are also included in the code of the Pitris.

description: The speech as delivered by Sanat-Sujata
sn: क्रोधः कामो लोभमोहौ विधित्सा कृपासूये मानशौको स्पृहा चा ईर्ष्या जुगुप्सा च मनुष्यदोषा वाः सदा द्वादशैते नराणाम्॥
en: Anger, desire, covetousness, ignorance of right and wrong, discontentment, unkindness, jealousy, vanity, grief, love, of pleasure, envy and a tendency to speak ill of others are the faults of men and these twelve ought ever to be avoided by human beings.

description: The speech as delivered by Sanat-Sujata
sn: एकैकः पर्युपास्ते ह मनुष्यान् मनुजर्षभ। लिप्समानोऽन्तरं तेषां मृगाणामिव लुब्धकः॥
en: Each of these by itself by itself can bring about the ruin of mankind, O bull among men; opportunity is awaited by these (vices) like deer by a hunter.

description: The speech as delivered by Sanat-Sujata
sn: विकत्थनः स्पृहयालुर्मनस्वी बिभ्रत् कोपं चपलोऽरक्षणाश्च। एतान् पापाः षण्नराः पापधर्मान् प्रकुर्वते नोत्रसन्तः सुदुर्गे॥
en: Speaking ill of others and well of themselves, adopting every means to enjoy the wives of others, vanity, anger, fickleness and not protecting proper persons-these vices wretches of wicked soul commit and do not fear the gravest dangers in this world and in the other.

description: The speech as delivered by Sanat-Sujata
sn: सम्भोगसंविद् विषमोऽतिमानी दत्तानुतापी कृपणो बलीयान्। वर्गप्रशंसी वनितासु द्वेष्टा एते परे सप्त नृशंसवर्गाः॥
en: He who considers enjoyment to be a grand aim of life, he who repents after making a gift, he who is a miser, he who oppresses others, he who is pleased at the misery of others and he who hates his wife-these seven are extremely wicked.

description: The speech as delivered by Sanat-Sujata
sn: धर्मश्च सत्यं च दमस्तपश्च अमात्सर्यं ह्रीस्तितिक्षानसूया। यज्ञश्च दानं च धृतिः श्रुतं च व्रतानि वै द्वादश ब्राह्मणस्य॥
en: Righteousness, truthfulness, self-control, asceticism, delight at other's happiness, modesty, forgiveness, reverse of malice performance of sacrificial ceremonies, gifts, patience, learning and vows, these twelve are the attributes of a Brahmana.

description: The speech as delivered by Sanat-Sujata
sn: यस्त्वेतेभ्यः प्रभवेद् द्वादशभ्यः सर्वामपीमां पृथिवीं स शिष्यात्। स्तस्य स्वमस्तीति स वेदितव्यः॥
en: He who excels in these twelve is capable over the whole of this earth and he who is graced with these, too or even one of these should be regarded as having gained his object.

description: The speech as delivered by Sanat-Sujata
sn: दमस्त्यागोऽप्रमादश्च एतष्वमृतमाहितम्। तानि सत्यमुखान्याहुर्ब्राह्मणा ये मनीषिणः॥
en: Self-control, renunciation and true knowledge-in these is centered immortality. Those Brahmanas that have great minds are of opinion that truth underlies all these virtues.

description: The speech as delivered by Sanat-Sujata
sn: दमो ह्यष्टादशगुणः प्रतिकूलं कृताकृते। अनृतं चाभ्यसूया च कामार्थौ च तथा स्पृहा।॥ क्रोधः शोकस्तथा तृष्णा लोभः पैशुन्यमेव च। मत्सरच विहिंसा च परितापस्तथाऽरतिः॥ अपस्मारश्चातिवादस्तथा सम्भावनाऽऽत्मनि। एतैर्विमुक्तो दोषैर्यः स दान्तः सद्भिरुच्यते॥
en: Self-control has for its elements eighteen virtues, the non-observance through laziness of acts prescribed in the Vedas, untruthfulness, malice, desire, wealth, love of pleasure, anger, grief, thirst, avarice, deceitfulness, delight at the pain of others, envy, repentance, aversion from virtues and noble acts, forgetfulness, speaking ill of others and well or self-he who is freed from these vices is said to possess selfcontrol by good people.

description: The speech as delivered by Sanat-Sujata
sn: मदोऽष्टादशदोषः स्यात् त्यागो भवति षड् विधः। विपर्ययाः स्मृता एते मददोषा उदाहृताः॥
en: The eighteen vices constitute mada, renouncement is of six kinds, the Smritis call the reverse of these six sorts of renouncement as mada.

description: The speech as delivered by Sanat-Sujata
sn: श्रेयांस्तु षड्विधस्त्यागस्तृतीयो दुष्करो भवेत्। तेन दुःखं तरत्येव भिन्नं तस्मिन् जितं कृते॥
en: The six kinds of renunciation are all good, the third is hard to practice; but by means of that relief is obtained from sorrow, besides that one being achieved, one gets over all difficulties.

description: The speech as delivered by Sanat-Sujata
sn: श्रेयांस्तु षड्विधस्त्यागः श्रियः प्राप्य न हृष्यति। इष्टापूर्ते द्वितीयं स्यान्नित्यवैराग्ययोगतः॥
en: The six kinds of renunciation are all good, (they are) not delighting at the acquirement of prosperity; the second is the performance of sacrificial ceremonies and pious acts (renouncement of the reverse of these).

description: The speech as delivered by Sanat-Sujata
sn: कामत्यागश्च राजेन्द्र स तृतीय इति स्मृतः। अप्यवाच्यं वदन्त्येतं स तृतीयो गुणः स्मृतः॥
en: (Renouncement of desire is known in the Smritis, as the third, O chief among kings. He who has not this third sort of renouncement is not fit to come under the above description, which the Smritis declare.

description: The speech as delivered by Sanat-Sujata
sn: त्यक्तैर्द्रव्यैर्यद् भवति नोपयुक्तैश्च कामतः। न च द्रव्यैस्तद भवति नोपयुक्तैश्च कामतः॥
en: (The third sort is) that which abandons enjoyments without enjoying them and not that which abandons them after enjoying them to heart's content.

description: The speech as delivered by Sanat-Sujata
sn: न च कर्मस्वसिद्धेषु दुःखं तेन च न ग्लपेत्। सर्वैरेव गुणैर्युक्तो द्रव्यवानपि यो भवेत्॥
en: (He who speaks of the fourth sort) one should not be sorry at the failure of an action, nor allow himself to be afflicted by the failure; even he possesses all the virtue and the means (of achieving the act).

description: The speech as delivered by Sanat-Sujata
sn: अप्रिये च समुत्पन्ने व्यथां जातु न गच्छति। इष्टान् पुत्रांश्च दारांश्च न याचेत कदाचन।॥
en: Or on a disagreeable thing taking place, he dose not feel pain. (The fifth sort is now treated of) one should never ask for a son or a wife or any other favour.

description: The speech as delivered by Sanat-Sujata
sn: अर्हते याचमानाय प्रदेयं तच्छुभं भवेत्। अप्रमादी भवेदेतैः स चाप्यष्टगुणो भवेत्॥
en: (Sixth sort) that a gift should be made to one asking for it; by this happiness can always be attained. By these means can one gain a true knowledge of self and the last one is made up of eight qualities.

description: The speech as delivered by Sanat-Sujata
sn: सत्यं ध्यानं समाधानं चोद्यं वैराग्यमेव च। अस्तेयं ब्रह्मचर्यं च तथा संचहमेव च।॥
en: These are truth meditation, a conception of the distinctness of subject and object, capability of arriving at conclusions, renouncement of the world, the habit of never taking what belongs to another, asceticism and non-acceptance of gifts.

description: The speech as delivered by Sanat-Sujata
sn: एवं दोषां मदस्योक्तास्तान् दोषान् परिवर्जयेत्। तथा त्यागोऽप्रमादश्च स चाप्यष्टगुणो मतः॥
en: Such are said to be the vises of man and these vices should always be avoided. The same should be done of the averse of renouncement and ignorance of self. A true knowledge of self, again, has eight virtues.

description: The speech as delivered by Sanat-Sujata
sn: अष्टौ दोषाः प्रमादस्य तान् दोषान् परिवर्जयेत्। इन्द्रियेभ्यश्च पञ्चभ्यो मनसश्चैव भारत। अतीतानागतेभ्यश्च मुक्त्युपेतः सुखी भवेत्॥
en: Ignorance of self has eight vices. These vices should be avoided. He who has attained freedom from the five, senses and from desire, O Bharata and from all concern for the past and future becomes happy.

description: The speech as delivered by Sanat-Sujata
sn: सत्यात्मा भव राजेन्द्र सत्ये लोकाः प्रतिष्ठिताः। तांस्तु सत्यमुखानाहुः सत्ये ह्यमृतमाहितम्॥
en: Let your soul be attached to truth, O chief among kings; on truth is founded the universe. Self-control, true knowledge and renunciation are said to be based on truth; on truth is centered immortality.

description: The speech as delivered by Sanat-Sujata
sn: निवृत्तेनैव दोषेण तपोव्रतभिहाचरेत्। एतद् धातृकृतं वृत्तं सत्यमेव सतां व्रतम्॥
en: Being devoid of all vices, devotion and asceticism should be practiced here. It has been prescribed by God that truth shall constitute the vow of the righteous.

description: The speech as delivered by Sanat-Sujata
sn: दोषैरेतैर्वियुक्तस्तु गुणैरेतैः समन्वितः। एतत् समृद्धमत्यर्थं तपो भवति केवलम्॥
en: Asceticism devoid of these vices and graced with these virtues becomes eminently successful in achieving prosperity.

description: The speech as delivered by Sanat-Sujata
sn: यन्मां पृच्छसि राजेन्द्र संक्षेपात् प्रब्रवीमि ते। एतत् पापहरं पुण्यं जन्ममृत्युजरापहम्॥
en: What you ask me, O chief among king, I have told you in brief-a subject sacred and sindestroying and capable of rescuing people from birth, death and decrepitude.

description: The speech as delivered by Sanat-Sujata
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच आख्यानपञ्चमैर्वेदैर्भूयिष्ठं कथ्यते जनः। तथा चान्ये चतुर्वेदास्त्रिवेदाश्च तथा परे॥
en: Dhritarashtra said By the fifth Veda, called Akhyana, it is declared that the Supreme Soul is identical with the universe; but there are some that recognize only three.

description: The speech as delivered by Sanat-Sujata
sn: द्विवेदाश्चैकवेदाश्चाष्यनृचश्च तथा परे। तेषां तु कतरः स स्याद् यमहं वेद वै द्विजम्॥
en: Some again recognize only two Vedas and others only one; while another class recognize only the Supreme Being. Of these, whom am I to regard as really possessing a knowledge of the Supreme Being.

description: The speech as delivered by Sanat-Sujata
sn: सनत्सुजात उवाच एकस्य वेदस्याज्ञानाद् वेदास्ते बहवः कृताः। सत्यस्यैकस्य राजेन्द्र सत्ये कश्चिदवस्थितः॥
en: Sanat-Sujata said Form ignorance of the one that ought to be known, have several Vedas been conceived. There is but one truth, O chief among kings. Who is there, who has attained to that truth?

description: The speech as delivered by Sanat-Sujata
sn: एवं वेदमविज्ञाय प्राज्ञोऽहमिति मन्यते। दानमध्ययनं यज्ञो लोभादेतत् प्रवर्तते॥
en: Not knowing such a one that ought to be known, a man thinks "I am wise" and from hope of gaining happiness employs himself in gifts, study and the performance of sacrifices.

description: The speech as delivered by Sanat-Sujata
sn: सत्यात् प्रच्यवमानानां संकल्पश्च तथा भवेत्। ततो यज्ञः प्रतायेत सत्यस्यैवावधारणात्॥
en: The purposes of those that have deviated from truth are in accordance with their condition and, so replying on the truth of the Vedas, perform sacrificial ceremonies.

description: The speech as delivered by Sanat-Sujata
sn: मनसान्यस्य भवति वाचान्यस्याथ कर्मणा। संकल्पसिद्धः पुरुषः संकल्पानधितिष्ठति॥
en: Some (perform sacrifices) by (concentration of) the mind, some by speech (recitation of hymns); and some by acts (the real ceremonies); but the man who is destined to attain to the true object, gets a true knowledge of self through the proper means.

description: The speech as delivered by Sanat-Sujata
sn: अनैभृत्येन चैतस्य दीक्षितव्रतमाचरेत्। नामैतद् धातुनिर्वृत्तं सत्यमेव सतां परम्॥
en: When a man's purposes have failed through a defect in his heart, he should not make vows of silence, called the Dikshitavrata. This name comes from a root (Diksh), which signifies the observance of vows. Truth is the only object of the good.

description: The speech as delivered by Sanat-Sujata
sn: ज्ञानं वै नाम प्रत्यक्षं परोक्षं जायते तपः। विद्याद् बहु पठन्तं तु द्विजं वै बहुपाठिनम्॥
en: The fruits of knowledge are immediate that of asceticism remote. A twice-born who has read much should only be known as a wellread man.

description: The speech as delivered by Sanat-Sujata
sn: तस्मात् क्षत्रिय मा मंस्था जल्पितेनैव वै द्विजम्। व एव सत्यान्नापैति स ज्ञेयो ब्राह्मणस्त्वया॥
en: Therefore, O Kshatriya, that one can know the Supreme Soul by mere reading. He, who does not fall away from truth, should be known by you as one who has attained a knowledge of the Supreme Being.

description: The speech as delivered by Sanat-Sujata
sn: छन्दांसि नाम क्षत्रिय तान्यथर्वा पुरा जगौ महर्षिसङ्घ एषः। छन्दोविदस्ते य उत नाधीतवेदा न वेदवेद्यस्य विदुर्हि तत्त्वम्॥
en: "Verses" is the name given, O Kshatriya, to what was recited by Atharvan in ancient days, in company with other great Rishis. Those who have read the Vedas and yet do not know the Being that ought to be known are not to be regarded as conversant with those verses.

description: The speech as delivered by Sanat-Sujata
sn: छन्दांसि नाम द्विपदां वरिष्ठ स्वच्छन्दयोगेन भवन्ति तत्र। छन्दोविदस्तेन च तानधीत्य गता न वेदस्य न वेद्यमार्याः॥
en: The verses, O chief among the best beings, independently become the means of obtaining Truth. They are not conversant with (the spirit of) the verses, who perform sacrifices after study of the Vedas and do not know the Supreme Being.

description: The speech as delivered by Sanat-Sujata
sn: न वेदानां वेदिता कश्चिदस्ति कश्चित् त्वेतान् बुध्यते वाऽपि राजन्। यो वेद वेदान् न स वेद वेद्यं सत्ये स्थितो यस्तु स वेद वेद्यम्॥
en: There are some who do not know the Vedas and some that know them, O king. He, who (merely) knows the Veda, does not know the knowable Being; but he who stands on truth knows knowable Being.

description: The speech as delivered by Sanat-Sujata
sn: न वेदानां वेदितां कश्चिदस्ति वेद्येन वेदं न विदुर्न वेद्यम्। यो वेद वेदं स च वेद वेद्यं यो वेद वेद्यं न स वेद सत्यम्॥
en: Among the faculties of the mind there is none which can help us in obtaining a true knowledge of self. There is none, again, who by means of the mind alone can acquire a knowledge of the knowable Being. He who knows what self is knows what self is not. He who stands on Truth knows the Supreme Soul.

description: The speech as delivered by Sanat-Sujata
sn: यो वेद वेदान् स च वेद वेद्यं न तं विदुर्वेदविदो न वेदाः। तथापि वेदेन विदन्ति वेदं ब्राह्मणा वेदविदो भवन्ति।॥
en: He who knows the proofs knows also that which is sought to be proved; but the true essence and nature thereof neither the Vedas, nor those conversant with the Vedas know. Still those twice-born that are conversant with the Vedas know the knowable Being by means of the Vedas.

description: The speech as delivered by Sanat-Sujata
sn: धामांशभागस्य तथा हि वेदा यथा च शाखा हि महीरुहस्य। संवेदने चैव यथाऽऽमनन्ति तस्मिन् हि सत्ये परमात्मनोऽर्थे॥
en: As a twig obtained from a big tree is used in pointing out the new moon; so are the Vedas used in pointing out the truth and other attributes of the Supreme Soul.

description: The speech as delivered by Sanat-Sujata
sn: अभिजानामि ब्राह्मणं व्याख्यातारं विचक्षणम्। यश्छिन्नविचिकित्स: स व्याचष्टे सर्वसंशयान्॥
en: I consider him to be a Brahmana, who knowing the Supreme Soul can expound (the rules of life) and explain the doubts of all, himself having all doubts removed from his mind.

description: The speech as delivered by Sanat-Sujata
sn: नास्य पर्येषणं गच्छेत् प्राचीनं नीत दक्षिणम्। नार्वाचीनं कुतस्तिर्यङ् नादिशं तु कथञ्चन॥
en: No clue can be found of the soul in the West, nor in the East, nor in the South, nor in the North, nor in the intermediate directions-in fact in no direction.

description: The speech as delivered by Sanat-Sujata
sn: तस्य पर्येषणं गच्छेत् प्रत्यर्थिषु कथञ्चन। अविचिन्वनिमं वेदे तपः पश्यति तं प्रभुम्॥
en: Very rarely can a clue be found of the soul by one who regards the earthly body as identical with the soul. The man of devotion perceives the Lord who is not even conceivable by the Vedas.

description: The speech as delivered by Sanat-Sujata
sn: तूष्णीम्भूत उपासीत न चेष्टेन्मनसाऽपि च। उपावर्तस्व तद् ब्रह्म अन्तरात्मनि विश्रुतम्॥
en: Bringing all your senses under control and without any exertion of your mind in other direction), seek to know that Brahma who, you have heard, resides in your inner soul.

description: The speech as delivered by Sanat-Sujata
sn: मौनान्न स मुनिर्भवति नारण्यवसनान्मुनिः। स्वलक्षणं तु यो वेद स मुनिः श्रेष्ठ उच्यते॥
en: That man is not a devotee who observes the vow of silence, nor he who lives in the woods; but that one is said to be a true devotee who knows his own nature.

description: The speech as delivered by Sanat-Sujata
sn: सर्वार्थानां व्याकरणाद् वैयाकरण उच्यते। तन्मूलतो व्याकरणं व्याकरोतीति तत् तथा॥
en: That man is said to be a grammarian who can trace each word to its root and explain it. Similarly that man is a true grammarian who can trace each object to its root (Brahma or the Supreme Soul).

description: The speech as delivered by Sanat-Sujata
sn: प्रत्यक्षदर्शी लोकानां सर्वदर्शी भवेन्नरः। सत्ये वै ब्राह्मणस्तिष्ठंस्तद् विद्वान् सर्वविद् भवेत्।।६२
en: A man, who sees all the worlds before his eyes, sees everything and that learned Brahmana who is established on truth knows everything.

description: The speech as delivered by Sanat-Sujata
sn: धर्मादिषु स्थितोऽप्येवं क्षत्रिय ब्रह्म पश्यति। वेदानां चानुपूर्येण एतद् बुद्ध्या ब्रवीमि ते॥
en: A Kshatriya, too, who practises such virtues beholds the Supreme Soul and can do the same by performing all the acts prescribed in the Vedas. Knowing this I tell you.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच सनत्सुजात यामिमां परां त्वं ब्राह्मीं वाचं वदसे विश्वरूपाम्। परां हि कामेन सुदुर्लभां कथां प्रब्रूहि मे वाक्यमिदं कुमार॥
en: Dhritarashtra said O Sanat-Sujata, what you have been saying regarding the attainment of emancipation and the origin of the universe is the best (discourse I have heard). Speak to me such words, (treating of subjects) rarely to be attained by men of desire, O you who have observed celibacy!

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: सनत्सुजात उवाच नैतद् ब्रह्म त्वरमाणेन लभ्यं यन्मां पृच्छन्नतिहष्यतीव। बुद्धौ विलीने मनसि प्रचिन्त्या विद्या हि सा ब्रह्मचर्येण लभ्या॥
en: Sanat-Sujata said This supreme soul regarding which you ask me with such exaltation cannot be attained by him who is in a hurry. When the mind (desire) has been lost in the intellect (i.e. when intellect has gained a control over desire), the mind of man becomes indifferent to worldly things and this state is attainable only by asceticism.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच यत् सनातनी अत्यन्तविद्यामिति ब्रवीषि त्वं ब्रह्मचर्येण सिद्धाम्। अनारभ्यां वसतीह कार्यकाले कथं ब्राह्मण्यममृतत्वं लभेत॥
en: Dhritarashtra said The true knowledge, that you are speaking of attainable by hard asceticism, is unborn in the mind and needs not any efforts for its manifestation and is manifested during the seeking of Brahma. How then can that immortality which is connected with a knowledge of the Supreme soul be obtained?

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: सनत्सुजात उवाच अव्यक्तविद्यामभिधास्ये पुराणी बुद्ध्या च तेषां ब्रह्मचर्येण सिद्धाम्। यां प्राप्यैनं मर्त्य लोकं त्यजन्ति या वै विद्या गुरुवृद्धेषु नित्या॥
en: Sanat-Sujata said This true knowledge that is unborn is said to be undeveloped and is developed by asceticism. On obtaining the true knowledge, men leave this world. True knowledge is ever present in the old and eminent preceptors.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच ब्रह्मचर्येण या विद्या शक्या वेदितुमञ्जसा। तत् कथं ब्रह्मचर्यं स्यादेतद् ब्रह्मन् ब्रवीहि मे॥
en: Dhritarashtra said That knowledge is capable of being gained by asceticism without difficulty. What sort of asceticism must be that? O Brahma, speak to me that.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: सनत्सुजात उवाच आचार्ययोनिमिह ये प्रविश्य भूत्वा गर्भ ब्रह्मचर्यं चरन्तिा इहैव ते शास्त्रकारा भवन्ति प्रहाय देहं परमं यान्ति योगम्॥
en: Sanat-Sujata said Those who having entered into the dwelling of a preceptor and residing therein serve them and practice asceticism become Brahma himself, as it were; and casting off their bodies are united with Him.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: अस्मिल्लोके वै जयन्तीह कामान् ब्राही स्थिति ह्यनुतितिक्षमाणाः। न्मुञ्जादिषीकामिव सत्त्वसंस्थाः॥
en: Those who are in this world desirous of obtaining emancipation, subdue their desires. Those virtuous men get their souls separated from their body like a blade of grass from a marshy plot of ground.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: शरीरमेतौ कुरुतः पिता माता च भारत। आचार्यशास्ता या जातिः सा पुण्या साजराऽमरा॥
en: The father and the mother, O Bharata, these two create the body; but the state gained from the instructions of the preceptor is sacred, free from death and without old age.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: नृतं कुर्वनमृतं सम्प्रयच्छन्। तं मन्येत पितरं मातरं च तस्मै न दुह्येत् कृतमस्य जानन्।॥
en: He (the preceptor) who discoursing on the Supreme Soul frees a man from untruth and distributes nectar should be regarded as father and mother. No injury should ever be done to him, knowing what he does.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: गुरुं शिष्यो नित्यमभिवादयीत स्वाध्यायमिच्छेच्छुचिरप्रमत्तः। मेष प्रथमो ब्रह्मचर्यस्य पादः॥
en: A disciple should every day pay due respects to his preceptor and engage himself in study with a pure mind and concentrated attention. He should not be annoyed (at the humble and menial services he is called upon to perform) and not feel wrathful. This is the first step of asceticism.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: शिष्यवृत्तिक्रमेणैव विद्यामाप्नोति यः शुचिः। ब्रह्मचर्यव्रतस्यास्य प्रथमः पाद उच्यते॥
en: He who gains knowledge (of his duties) by observing the duties of other disciples is said to observe the first step of the vow of asceticism.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: आचार्यस्य प्रियं कुर्यात् प्राणैरपि धनैरपि। कर्मणा मनसा वाचा द्वितीयः पाद उच्यते॥
en: What is agreeable to a preceptor should be done at the expense of life and wealth, by the mind, by actions or by speech. Doing this is said to be the second step.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: समा गुरौ यथा वृत्तिर्णरुपल्यां तथाऽऽचरेत्। तत्पुत्रे च तथा कुर्वन् द्वितीयः पाद उच्यते॥
en: A similar behaviour like that towards a preceptor should be adopted towards the preceptor's woke and the same should be done to his son. Doing this is said to be the second step.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: आचार्येणात्मकृतं विजानन् ज्ञात्वा चार्थ भावितोऽस्मीत्यनेन। यन्मन्यते तं प्रति हृष्टबुद्धिः स वै तृतीयो ब्रह्मचर्यस्य पादः॥
en: Fully, appreciating what has been done to one's self by his preceptor and knowing the object thereof, a disciple should with exaltation in his heart think-I have been developed by him. This is the third step of asceticism.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: नाचार्यस्यानपाकृत्य प्रवास प्राज्ञः कुर्वीतं नैतदहं करोमि। इतीव मन्येत न भाषयेत स वै चतुर्थो ब्रह्मचर्यस्य पादः॥
en: A wise man should not remove himself (from the preceptor's abode) without requesting the preceptor; nor should he even speak or think “I do this” (i.e. I make this gift). This is the fourth step of asceticism.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: कालेन पादं लभते तथाऽर्थं ततश्च पादं गुरुयोगतश्च। च्छास्त्रेण पादं च ततोऽभियाति॥
en: A man obtains the object of the first step of asceticism by the aid of time (i.e. in due course), the second step by contact with the preceptor, the third by the energy of his own intellect and the next by discussion with others.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: मन्यानि चाङ्गानि तथा बलं च। ब्रह्मार्थयोगेन च ब्रह्मचर्यम्॥
en: The effects of the practice of asceticism, which is made up of twelve constituent elements including righteousness and the effects of Angas and Balam (particular forms of asceticism) are said to be obtained by contact with the preceptor and by an earnest desire to know the Supreme Soul.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: एवं प्रवृत्तो यदुपालभेत वै धनमाचार्याय तदनुप्रयच्छेत्। सतां वृत्तिं बहुगुणामेवमेति गुरोः पुत्रे भवति च वृत्तिरेषा॥
en: While in the position of a disciple, whatever wealth is earned should be given to the preceptor. It is by this means that he (the preceptor) earns his honest livelihood graced with many virtues. Such should also be the conduct of the preceptor's son.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: एवं वसन् सर्वतो वर्धतीह बहून् पुत्राँल्लभते च प्रतिष्ठाम्। वर्षन्ति चास्मै प्रदिशो दिशश्च वसन्त्यस्मिन् ब्रह्मचर्ये जनाश्च॥
en: With this rule of life one prospers in every way and obtains many sons and fame; to such a man, wealth is poured from all sides and to that place many people come for practicing asceticism.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: एतेन ब्रह्मचर्येण देवा देवत्वमाप्नुवन्। ऋषयश्च महाभागा ब्रह्मलोकं मनीषिणः॥
en: By means of such asceticism, the gods attained their divine character and the wise Rishis of heavenly qualities attained to the regions of Brahma.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: गन्धर्वाणामनेनैव रूपमप्सरसामभूत्। एतेन ब्रह्मचर्येण सूर्योऽप्यह्राय जायते॥
en: By this also did the beauty of the Gandharvas and Apsaras spring up; by such asceticism does the sun rise to make the day.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: आकाक्ष्यार्थस्य संयोगाद् रसभेदार्थिनामिव। एवं ह्येते समाज्ञाय तादृग्भावं गता इमे॥
en: on These (i.e. Gandharvas, etc.) completion of their asceticism by this means attained to the state of the seekers of the Rasabheda (a fabulous gem supposed to grant every desire of the possessor) through the obtainment of the object of their desire.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: य आश्रयेत् पावयेच्चापि राजन् सर्वं शरीरं तपसा तप्यमानः। एतेन वै बाल्यमभ्येति विद्वान् मृत्युं तथा स जयत्यन्तकाले॥
en: He, who attached to austerities has recourse to asceticism and thereby purifies his body, comes to the condition of a child (free from passions, etc., characteristic of the old men) and that learned man in the end conquers death.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: अन्तवतः क्षत्रिय ते जयन्ति लोकान् जनाः कर्मणा निर्मलेन। ब्रह्मैव विद्वांस्तेन चाभ्येति सर्व नान्यः पन्था अयनाय विद्यते॥
en: By pure work men obtain the perishable worlds, O Kshatriya-but that learned man, by means of his knowledge, obtains emancipation. There is no other path to emancipation.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच आभाति शुक्लमिव लोहितमिवाथो कृष्णमथाञ्जनं काद्रवं वा। सद्ब्रह्मणः पश्यति योऽत्र विद्वान् कथं रूपं तदमृतमक्षरं पदम्॥
en: Dhritarashtra said Of what form is the Supreme Soul, which is immortal and omnipresent and which the learned man sees in this world. Does he shine as white, red, black, blue or purple?

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: सनत्सुजात उवाच आभाति शुक्लमिव लोहितमिवाथो कृष्णमायसमर्कवर्णम्। न पृथिव्यां तिष्ठति नान्तरिक्षे नैतत् समुद्रे सलिलं बिभर्ति॥
en: Sanat-Sujata said (The Supreme Soul) may appear as white, red, black, brown or like the sun; but its like is not to be met with in the earth, the sky, nor in the water of the sea.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: न तारकासु न च विद्युदाश्रितं न चाभ्रेषु दृश्यते रूपमस्या न चापि वायौ न च देवतासु नैतच्चन्द्रे दृश्यते नोत सूर्ये॥
en: It cannot be found among the stars, nor is it shut up in the lightning and its form cannot be seen among the clouds, nor in the air, nor among the gods, nor in the moon, nor in the sun,

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: नैवटुं तन्न यजुषु नाप्यथर्वसु न दृश्यते वै विमलेषु सामसु। रथन्तरे बार्हद्रथे वाऽपि राजन् महाव्रते नैव दृश्येद् ध्रुवं तत्॥
en: Nor in the Rich, nor in the Yajush, nor in the Atharva, nor in the sacred Sama (Vedas). It is certain, O king, that it cannot be seen in the Rathantara, nor in the Barhadrath, nor in the great vows.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: अपारणीयं तमसः परस्तात् तदन्तकोऽप्येति विनाशकाले। अणीयो रूपं क्षुरधारया समं महच्च रूपं तद् वै पर्वतेभ्यः॥
en: Incapable of being reached by our ignorance, even the king of Death, at the time of his end, is lost in it. Its form cannot be gazed at; it is like the edge of a razor and its form is like that of a high mountain.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: सा प्रतिष्ठा तदमृतं लोकास्तद् ब्रह्म तद् यशः। भूतानि जज्ञिरे तस्मात् प्रलयं यान्ति तत्र हि॥
en: It is the foundation of everything; it is nectar; it is the universe; it is vast and delightful. From it are born all creatures and there do they come to their end.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: अनामयं तन्महदुद्यत् यशो वाचो विकारं कवयो वदन्ति। यस्मिन् जगत् सर्वमिदं प्रतिष्ठितं ये तद् विदुरमृतास्ते भवन्ति॥
en: Having no duality, it is manifest in the form of the universe. Poets speak of it as having no change but in the language and form used for its description. That on which all this world stands-those who know this become immortal.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: सनत्सुजात उवाच शोकः क्रोधश्च लोभश्च कामो मानः परासुता। ईर्ष्या मोहो विधित्सा च कृपाऽसूया जुगुप्सुता॥ द्वादशैते महादोषा मनुष्यप्राणनाशनाः।
en: Sanat-Sujata said Grief, anger, avarice, desire, vanity, idleness, malice, stupidity, love of gain, affection, jealousy and evil speech these twelve are great evils leading to the destruction of the life of man.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: एकैकमेते राजेन्द्र मनुष्यान् पर्युपासते। यैराविष्टो नरः पापं मूढसंज्ञो व्यवस्यति॥
en: Each of this, O chief among kings, awaits (opportunity for getting into its clutches) mankind. Man affected with them loses his senses and does sinful acts.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: स्पृहयालुरुचः पुरुषो वा वदान्यः क्रोधं बिभ्रन्मनसा वै विकत्थी। नृशंसधर्माः षडिमे जना वै प्राप्याप्यर्थं नोत सभाजयन्ते।॥
en: He who loves pleasure; he who is haughty; he who harsh of speech; he who talks too much; he who nurses and feeds anger in the heart and he who speaks ill of others-these six sorts of men of wicked disposition, having even gained their objects, do not treat others with politeness.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: सम्भोगसंविद् विषमोऽतिमानी दत्त्वा विकत्थी कृपणो दुर्बलश्च। बहुप्रशंसी वन्दितद्विट् सदैव सप्तैवोक्ताः पापशीला नृशंसाः॥
en: He who is too much attached enjoyment, he who boats after giving away, he to who speaks evil, he who is a miser, he who is (mentally) weak, he who praises himself too much and he who hates his wife-these seven are ever spoken of as vicious wrenches.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
