sn: धर्मश्च सत्यं च तपो दमश्च अमात्सर्यं ह्रीस्तितिक्षाऽनसूया। दानं श्रुतं चैव धृतिः क्षमा च महाव्रता द्वादश ब्राह्मणस्य॥
en: Righteousness, truth, asceticism, selfcontrol, contentment, modesty, patience, unselfishness, gifts, acquaintance with the holy books, wisdom, forgiveness, are the twelve great vows of a Brahmanas.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: यो नैतेभ्यः प्रच्यवेद् द्वादशभ्यः सर्वामपीमां पृथिवीं स शिष्यात्। त्रिभिभ्यिामेकतो वाऽर्थितो यो नास्य स्वमस्तीति च वेदितव्यम्॥
en: He, who does not deviate from these twelve, can rule even the whole of this earth. He who is graced with these two or even one, does not regard anything as solely his own.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: दमस्त्यागोऽथाप्रमाद इत्येतेष्वमृतं स्थितम्। एतानि ब्रह्ममुख्यानां ब्राह्मणानां मनीषिणाम्॥
en: Self-control, renunciation and knowledge-on these depends immortality. These are the attributes of those learned Brahmanas, who regard Brahma as the Prime Being.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: सद् वासद् वा परीवादो ब्राह्मणस्य न शस्यते। नरकप्रतिष्ठास्ते वै स्युर्य एव कुर्वते जनाः॥
en: True or false, speaking ill of others, is not proper for a Brahmana. People who do this have hell for their abode.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: मदोऽष्टादशदोषः स स्यात् पुरा योऽप्रकीर्तितः। लोकद्वेष्यं प्रातिकूल्यमभ्यसूया मृषा वचः॥
en: Mada has eighteen vices which have not before been described. (They are) hatred towards men, acting against the interests of others, speaking ill of others who do not deserve it, untruthfulness,

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: कामक्रोधौ पारतन्त्र्यं परिवादोऽथ पैशुनम्। अर्थहानिर्विवादश्च मात्सर्यं प्राणिपीडनम्॥
en: Desire, anger, excessive reliance on others, blaming others, calumny, waste of wealth, true quarrels, imprudence, oppression on living beings.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: ईर्ष्या मोदोऽतिवादश्च संज्ञानाशोऽभ्यसूयिता। तस्मात् प्राज्ञो न माद्येत सदा ह्येतद् विगर्हितम्॥
en: Envy, ignorance, excessive speech, loss of the senses and the desire to harm others. Therefore should a wise man never yield to Mada. It is ever reprehensible.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: सौहृदे वै षड् गुणा वेदितव्याः प्रिये हृष्यन्त्यप्रिये च व्यथन्ते। स्यादात्मनः सुचिरं याचते यो ददात्ययाच्यमपि देयं खलु स्यात्। नभ्यर्थितश्चार्हति शुद्धभावः॥
en: In friendship, it should be known, are six virtues; they (friends) are delighted in (their friend's) prosperity and pained in their adversity; if a man asks for anything that ought not to be asked for, it is at once given.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: त्यक्तद्रव्यः संवसेन्नेह कामाद् भुङ्क्ते कर्म स्वाशिषं बाधते च॥
en: One (a friend) who is pure mind when asked, gives away every blessing that he enjoys his wealth, his son, himself, his wife even. A friend should not reside in the house of him whom he has given away everything but should live on what is earned by himself alone.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: द्रव्यवान् गुणवानेव त्यागी भवति सात्त्विकः। पञ्च भूतानि पञ्चभ्यो निवर्तयति तादृशः॥
en: The godly man of possessions and virtues, who wants to be thus endued with virtue, should turn away his five senses from their five objects.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: एतत् समृद्धमप्यूर्ध्वं तपो भवति केवलम्। सत्त्वात् प्रच्यवमानानां संकल्पेन समाहितम्॥
en: Such acquirement of noble qualities constitutes asceticism. These who practice these with patience attain to emancipation.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: यतो यज्ञाः प्रवर्धन्ते सत्यस्यैवावरोधनात्। मनसान्यस्य भवति वाचान्यस्याथ कर्मणा॥
en: Owing to having understood the nature of truth of which are directed all sacrifices, a certain class of men perform sacrifices by the mind (meditation), another by words (recitation of hymns) and another by actions.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: संकल्पसिद्धं पुरुषमसंकल्पोऽधितिष्ठति। ब्राह्मणस्य विशेषेण किञ्चान्यदपि मे शृणु॥
en: In a man, who knows Brahma through his attributes, resides truth; in one who knows him as himself (i.e. does not regard him as the sum total of certain attributes) it resides more completely. Hear me now on some other subjects.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: अध्यापयेन्महदेतद् यशस्यं वाचो विकाराः कवयो वदन्ति। अस्मिन् योगे सर्वमिदं प्रतिष्ठितं ये तद् विदुरमृतास्ते भवन्ति॥
en: This grand system of philosophy should be taught to those who desire to obtain Brahma; all other systems, are mere tissues of words, which wise men declare. On this philosophy all this universe stands and those who know it become immortal.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: न कर्मणा सुकृतेनैव राजन् सत्यं जयेज्जुहुयाद् वा यजेद् वा। नैतेन बालोऽमृत्युमभ्येति राजन् रति चासौ न लभत्यन्तकाले॥
en: By means of deeds well done, Oking, one cannot obtain Truth; whether he offers libations on the Homa fire or performs sacrificial ceremonies; the man of childlike simplicity does not obtain immortality. O king, nor does he obtain satisfaction in the end.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: तूष्णीमेक उपासीत चेष्टेत मनसाऽपि न। तथा संस्तुतिनिन्दाभ्यां प्रीतिरोषौ विवर्जयेत्॥
en: Bringing all the senses under control and alone one should seek Brahma; he should not work even by the mind and while so employed one should avoid joy and eager at praise and blame.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: अत्रैव तिष्ठन् क्षत्रिय ब्रह्माविशति पश्यति। वेदेषु चानुपूर्येण एतद् विद्वन् ब्रवीमि ते॥
en: Living a life according to this and doing one by one all that is prescribed in the Vedas, OKshatriya, does a man learn and see Brahma, O learned one, I tell you this.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: सनत्सुजात उवाच यत् तच्छूक्रं महज्ज्योतिर्दीप्यमानं महद् यशः। तद् वै देवा उपासते तस्मात् सूर्यो विराजते। योगिनस्तं प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तं सनातनम्॥
en: Sanat-Sujata said That which is the seed (of the universe) blazes with great effulgence and is of great fame. The gods worship him; from him shines the sun; the ascetics perceive that Lord who is Eternal.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: शुक्राद् ब्रह्म प्रभवति ब्रह्म शुक्रेण वर्धते। तच्छु– ज्योतिषां मध्येऽतप्तं तपति तापनम्। योगिनस्तं प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्त सनातनम्॥
en: By reason of the seed is Brahma the Lord; by means of the seed does he develop. That seed communicates heat and light to lightgiving bodies and not getting heat from any other body; yet it is a source of terror to luminous bodies. The ascetics perceive that Lord who is Eternal.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: अपोऽथ अद्भ्यः सलिलस्य मध्ये उमौ देवो शिश्रियातेऽन्तरिक्षे। नुभो बिभर्ति पृथिवीं दिवं च। योगिनस्तं प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तं सनातनम्॥
en: From Brahma spring up the five subtle elements (Mahabhut) which again give birth to the five gross elements which make up the human body; the heart that is in it contains both the gods (the creature-soul and the supreme soul). Ever-wakeful, this sun of the sun upholds both the earth and the sky. Ascetics perceive that Lord who is Eternal.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: उभौ च देवौ पृथिवीं दिवं च दिशः शुक्रो भुवनं बिभर्ति। तस्माद् दिशः सरितश्च स्रवन्ति तस्मात् समुद्रा विहिता महान्ताः। योगिनस्तं प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तं सनातनम्॥
en: car The seed supports the two gods (the creature-soul and the supreme soul), the earth and the heaven, the cardinal points of the earth and the universe. From that spring up the cardinal point and the latter and from that the vast oceans have originated. The ascetics perceive that Lord who is Eternal.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: चक्रे रथस्य तिष्ठन्तोऽध्रुवस्याव्ययकर्मणः। केतुमन्तं वहन्त्यश्वास्त दिव्यमजरं दिवि। योगिनस्तं प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तं सनातनम्॥
en: Attached to the wheels to the (representing the acts of past lives) of human body which is uncertain, but the acts of which are ever present; a man of true knowledge is led by the steeds of the senses towards the regions that have no birth and the Being present there. The ascetics perceive that Lord who is immortal.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: न सादृश्ये तिष्ठति रूपमस्य न चक्षुषा पश्यति कश्चिदेनम्। मनीषयाथो मनसा हृदा च य एनं विदुरमृतास्ते भवन्ति। योगिनस्तं प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तं सनातनम्॥
en: Its form is not similar to that of any other being; no body ever sees it with his eyes; that wise man who knows it by the mind or the heart becomes immortal. The ascetics perceive that Lord who is immortal.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: द्वादशपूगां सरितं पिबन्तो देवरक्षिताम्। मध्वीक्षन्तश्च ते तस्याः संचरन्तीह घोराम्। योगिनस्तं प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तं सनातनम्॥
en: Drinking of the lake (of life) guarded by the gods and bearing fruits and beholding many a dear object in its middle, man disports in the waters, that lake has its origin in the seed. The ascetics perceive that Lord who is immortal.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: तदर्धमासं पिबति संचित्य भ्रमरो मधु। ईशानः सर्वभूतेषु हरिर्भूतमकल्पयत्। योगिनस्तं प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तं सनातनम्॥
en: The being who, like a bee sucking honey only for half the month, enjoys only one-half of the fruits of his actions and has to come back to the world to enjoy the other half and is present in all creatures ordains sacrifices. The ascetics perceive that Lord who is immortal.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: हिरण्यपर्णमश्वत्थमभिपद्य ह्यपक्षकाः। ते तत्र पक्षिणो भूत्वा प्रपतन्ति यथा दिशम्। योगिनस्तं प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तं सनातनम्॥
en: Originally without plumes (i.e. conditions) he comes to possess plumes (becomes vested with conditions) in a large tree of golden foliage, representing a world transitory and ephemeral and flies away in different directions (i.e. reborn among several orders of men). The Sloka simply means that the supreme should when vested with conditions becomes the creature-soul. The ascetics perceive that Lord who is Eternal.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: पूर्णात् पूर्णान्युद्धरन्ति पूर्णात् पूर्णानि चक्रिरे। हरन्ति पूर्णात् पूर्णानि पूर्णमेवावशिष्यते। योगिनस्तं प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तं सनातनम्॥
en: Form that which is complete (Brahma) has the complete universe sprung; and from that which is complete have also the conditions which are complete sprung and when those which are full (conditions) are separated from that which is full (Brahma) the true full remains. The ascetics perceive that Lord who is eternal.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: तस्माद् वै वायुरायातस्तस्मिंश्च प्रयतः सदा। तस्मादग्निश्च सोमश्च तस्मिश्च प्राण आततः॥
en: It is from that the air has come and towards that again it ever goes; it is from that Agni (consumer) and Some (consumed) have originated and on them depends the entire living world.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: सर्वमेव ततो विद्यात् तत् तद् वक्तुं न शक्नुमः। योगिनस्तं प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तं सनातनम्॥
en: It should be known that everything has its origin in that; we cannot describe that; the ascetics that Lord who is Eternal.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: अपानं गिरति प्राणः प्राणं गिरति चन्द्रमाः। आदित्यो गिरते चन्द्रमादित्यं गिरते परः। योगिनस्तं प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तं सनातनम्॥
en: The vital air called Apana is lost in the air called Prana which again is lost in the mind. The last again is lost in the intellect which again is lost in the supreme being. The ascetics perceive that Lord who is Eternal.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: एकं पादं नोत्क्षिपति सलिलाद्धंस उच्चरन्। तं चेत् संततमूर्ध्वाय न मृत्युर्नामृतं भवेत्। योगिनस्तं प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तं सनातनम्॥
en: Like a swan walking out of water the eternal one (as embodied in a man) endued with four legs (respectively called waking dreaming, sleeping and) turiya hides one of the legs (turiya, which can be perceived alone by ascetics, all other men perceiving the other three); he who sees this hidden leg for purpose of grinding the other three, regards and emancipation as the same. The ascetics perceive that Lord who is Eternal.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: अङ्गुष्ठमात्रः पुरुषोऽन्तरात्मा लिङ्गस्य योगेन स याति नित्यम्। तमीशमीड्यमनुकल्पमाद्यं पश्यन्ति मूढा न विराजमानम्। योगिनस्तं प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तं सनातनम्॥
en: The being who is the inner soul is of the size of the thumb, by being joined with the human body ever moves. Fools alone do not perceive Him manifest within everything, who is the Lord, Who is worthy of being worshipped, Who is capable of anything and the Prime Being. The ascetics perceive that Lord who is Eternal.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: असाधना वापि ससाधना वा समानमेतद् दृश्यते मानुषेषु। समानमेतदमृतस्येतरस्य मुक्तास्तत्र मध्व उत्सं समापुः। योगिनस्तं प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तं सनातनम्॥
en: It is seen equally among men who have obtained true knowledge and those that have not. It is present equally in men that have obtained immortality and others (i.e. those who have not) but the emancipated ones obtain honey flowing in a thick stream. The ascetics perceive that Lord who is Eternal.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: उभौ लोकौ विद्यया व्याप्य याति तदा हुतं चाहुतमग्निहोत्रम्। मा ते ब्राह्मी लघुतामादधीत प्रज्ञानं स्यानाम धीरा लभन्ते। योगिनस्तं प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तं सनातनम्॥
en: To a man of true knowledge, both the worlds are accessible and though they may not have performed the Agnihotra ceremony, yet do they obtain the fruits thereof. Do you not proclaim your deficiency in matters spiritual. True knowledge is another name of the inner soul which those who have self-control gain. The ascetics perceive that Lord who is Eternal.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: एवंरूपो महात्मा स पावकं पुरुषो गिरन्। यो वै तं पुरुषं वेद तस्येहार्थो न रिष्यते। योगिनस्तं प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तं सनातनम्॥
en: Of this description is that illustrious Being in whom is lost all living creatures. He who knows that sacred being does not envy the attainment of objects of others in this world, (he himself having attained to emancipation). Ascetics perceive that Lord who is Eternal.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: यः सहस्रं सहस्राणां पक्षान् संतत्य सम्पतेत्। मध्यमे मध्य आगच्छेदपि चेत् स्यान्मनोजवः। योगिनस्तं प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तं सनातनम्॥
en: He that flies away with thousands of thousands of wings outstretched must come back to the central spirit within the body. The ascetics perceive that Lord who is Eternal.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: न दर्शने तिष्ठति रूपमस्य पश्यन्ति चैनं सुविशुद्धसत्त्वाः। हितो मनीषी मनसा न तप्यते ये प्रव्रजेयुरमृतास्ते भवन्ति। योगिनस्तं प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तं सनातनम्॥
en: His from cannot be seen by the eye; those that follow pure lives see them. He who seek the general good of man in his mind, who does not grieve and who can renounce the Lord who is Eternal.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: गृहन्ति सर्पा इव गह्वराणि स्वशिक्षया स्वेन वृत्तेन माः। तेषु प्रमुह्यन्ति जना विमूढा यथाध्वानं मोहयन्ते भयाय। योगिनस्तं प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तं सनातनम्॥
en: Some men conceal their habits which are different from their teachings from others, as serpents conceal themselves in their holes. Men who are ignorant are deceived by them, who following the right Path deceive their victims into ruin. Ascetics perceive that Lord who is immortal.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: चामृत्युरमृतं मे कुतः स्यात्। सत्यानृते सत्यसमानबन्धे सतश्च योनिरसतश्चैक एवा योगिनस्तं प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तं सनातनम्॥
en: I am beyond the reach of earthly evils; whence can the death and life come to me? nor am I desirous of emancipation for truth and untruth, good and evil-all rest in the Supreme Being. (Thus does the emancipated soul think within himself). Ascetics perceive that Lord that Lord who is Eternal.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: न साधुना नोत असाधुना वासमानमेतद् दृश्यते मानुषेषु। देवंयुक्तो मधु तद् वै परीप्सेत्। योगिनस्तं प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तं सनातनम्॥
en: Acts, virtuous or sinful, cannot touch the man who has obtained true knowledge. This inequality is observed only by ordinary men. The man who has seen the Supreme Being is immortal. Being possessed of this knowledge, one should attain to that sweetness (Brahma). The ascetics perceive that Being who is Eternal.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: नास्यातिवादा हृदयं तापयन्ति नानधीतं नाहुतमग्निहोत्रम्। मनो ब्राह्मी लघुतामादधीत प्रज्ञां चास्मै नाम धीरा लभन्ते। योगिनस्तं प्रपश्यन्ति भगवन्तं सनातनम्॥
en: The heart of such a man is not grieved at calumny, nor the want of study of the holy books, nor the non-performance of sacrificial ceremonies; by a knowledge of the supreme Being those who are given to asceticism soon obtain true wisdom. The ascetics perceive that Lord who is Eternal.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: एवं यः सर्वभूतेषु आत्मानमनुपश्यति। अन्यत्रान्यत्र युक्तेषु किं स शोचेत् ततः परम्॥
en: The man who thus perceives soul in all creatures, why should he grieve after this perception? Grief comes to those who are employed occupations.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: यथोदपाने महति सर्वतः सम्प्लुतोदके। एवं सर्वेषु वेदेषु आत्मानमनुजानतः॥
en: As one can do as well with a well as with a large tank, so one who knows the supreme should can do as well with his own knowledge as with the entire Veda.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: अङ्गुष्ठमात्रः पुरुषो महात्मा न दृश्यते सौहृदि संनिविष्टः। अजश्चरो दिवारानमतन्द्रितश्च स तं मत्वा कविरास्ते प्रसन्नः॥
en: Of the measure of the thumb, that illustrious Being, though dwelling in the heart, cannot be seen by the eye. Though without birth, he moves about in full consciousness, day and night. He that knows him becomes wise and full of joy.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: अहमेव स्मृतो माता पिता पुत्रोऽस्म्यहं पुनः। आत्माऽहमपि सर्वस्य यच्च नास्ति यदस्ति च॥
en: According to the Smritis, I am the mother, the father and again I am the son-I am the soul of everything, past and present.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: पितामहोऽस्मि स्थविरः पिता पुत्रश्च भारत। ममैव यूयमात्मस्था न मे यूयं न वो वयम्॥
en: I am the old grandfather, father and son; O Bharata, you depend on my soul; O Bharata, yet you are not mine.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: आत्मैव स्थानं मम जन्म चात्मा ओतप्रोतोऽहमजरप्रतिष्ठः। अजश्चरो दिवारात्रमतन्द्रितोऽहं मां विज्ञाय कविरास्ते प्रसन्नः॥
en: The soul is my place and the soul is my birth, I am both the warp and the woof; I am established on that which is in destructible. Though without birth, I roam about in full consciousness, day and night; knowing me wise men become satisfied.

description: On honest speech, in the Sanat-Sujata
sn: अणोरणीयान् सुमनाः सर्वभूतेषु जाग्रति। पितरं सर्वभूतेषु पुष्करे निहितं विदुः॥
en: The supreme soul is subtler than the subtle, of noble mind and is present in all creatures. He is known as the universal father, dwelling in the heart of every creature,

description: Sanjaya sent in message, in the Yanasandhi
sn: वैसम्पायन उवाच एवं सनत्सुजातेन विदुरेण च धीमता। साधु कथयतो राज्ञः सा व्यतीयाय शर्वरी॥॥
en: Vaishampayana said In this way discoursing with Sanat-Sujata and wise Vidura, the king passed that night.

description: Sanjaya sent in message, in the Yanasandhi
sn: तस्यां रजन्यां व्युष्टायां राजानः सर्व एव ते। सभामाविविशुहृष्टाः सूतस्योपदिदृक्षया॥
en: That night having passed away, all the kings entered the Council Chamber with glad hearts with the desire of seeing the Suta.

description: Sanjaya sent in message, in the Yanasandhi
sn: शुश्रुषमाणाः पार्थानां वाचो धर्मार्थसंहिताः। धृतराष्ट्रमुखाः सर्वे ययू राजसभां शुभाम्॥
en: Desirous of hearing the message of those sons of Pritha, full of virtue and worldly benefit, all with Dhritarashtra at their head went to the blessed Council Chamber.

description: Sanjaya sent in message, in the Yanasandhi
sn: सुधावदातां विस्तीर्णा कनकाजिरभूषिताम्। चन्द्रप्रभां सुरुचिरां सिक्तां चन्दनवारिणा॥
en: Of a bright whit and large area and adorned with a golden floor it was beautiful as the moon and wet with sandal water.

description: Sanjaya sent in message, in the Yanasandhi
sn: रुचिरैरासनैस्तीर्णां काञ्चनैरवैरपि। अश्मसारमयैर्दान्तैः स्वास्तीर्णैः सोत्तरच्छदैः॥
en: It was covered over with handsome seats made of gold and of wood and of marble and of ivory, having excellent covers.

description: Sanjaya sent in message, in the Yanasandhi
sn: भीष्मो द्रोणः कृपः शल्यः कृतवर्मा जयद्रथः। अश्वत्थामा विकर्णश्च सोमदत्तश्च बाह्निकः॥ विदुरच महाप्राज्ञो युयुत्सुश्च महारथः। सर्वे च सहिताः शूराः पार्थिवा भरतर्षभ॥ धृतराष्ट्रं पुरस्कृत्य विविशुस्ता सभां शुभाम्।
en: Bhishma, Drona, Kripa, Shalya, Kritavarman, Jayadratha, Ashvathama, Vikarna, Somadatta, Balhika, Vidura of great wisdom and Yuyutsu of great prowess, all these heroes and rulers of the earth, O bull among the race of Bharata, keeping Dhritarashtra in the front entered that blessed Council Chamber.

description: Sanjaya sent in message, in the Yanasandhi
sn: दुःशासनश्चित्रसेन: शकुनिश्चापि सौबलः॥ दुर्मुखो दुःसहः कर्ण उलूकोऽथ विविंशतिः। कुरुराजं पुरस्कृत्य दुर्योधनममर्षणम्॥ विविशुस्तां सभां राजन् सुराः शक्रसदो यथा।
en: As also did Dushasana, Shakuni and Saubala. Durmukha, Dussaha, Karna, Uluka, Vivingshati having placed Duryodhana, the wrathful king of the Kurus, in the front, entered that Council, O king, like the gods forming the train of Shakra.

description: Sanjaya sent in message, in the Yanasandhi
sn: आविशद्भिस्तदा राजन्शूरैः परिघबाहुभिः॥ शुशुभे सा सभा राजन् सिंहैरिव गिरेर्गुहा।
en: At the time, O king, filled with those heroes, having arms like iron maces, that Council Chamber, O king, appeared like a den filled with lion.

description: Sanjaya sent in message, in the Yanasandhi
sn: ते प्रविश्य महेष्वासाः सभां सर्वे महौजसः॥ आसनानि विचित्राणि भेजिरे सूर्यवर्चसः।
en: All those mighty bowmen of great prowess having entered the hall, those of the effulgence of the sun seated themselves on the variegated seats.

description: Sanjaya sent in message, in the Yanasandhi
sn: आसनस्थेषु सर्वेषु तेषु राजसु भारत॥ द्वा:स्थो निवेदयामास सूतपुत्रमुपस्थितम्। अयं स रथ आयाति योऽयासीत् पाण्डवान् प्रति॥ दूतो नस्तूर्णमायातः सैन्धवैः साधुवाहिभिः।
en: And to all those kings, seated on their seats, O Bharata, the gate-keeper (thus) submitted for their information, the presence of the Suta's son. Here comes he with his car who was sent to the sons of Pandu. Our messenger has returned speedily by the aid of horses of Sindhu species, which are good barriers of loads.

description: Sanjaya sent in message, in the Yanasandhi
sn: उपेयाय स तु क्षिप्रं रथात् प्रस्कन्द्य कुण्डली। प्रविवेश सभां पूर्णां महीपालैर्महात्मभिः॥
en: Coming to that place quickly and dismounting from the chariot the one having earrings entered the Council Chamber full of great-souled rulers of the earth.

description: Sanjaya sent in message, in the Yanasandhi
sn: संजय उवाच प्राप्तोऽस्मि पाण्डवान् गत्वा तं विजानीत कौरवाः। यथावयः कुरून् सर्वान् प्रतिनन्दन्ति पाण्डवाः॥
en: Sanjaya said Having gone to the Pandavas, I am returned; know you this, O sons of Kuru. The Pandus salute all the sons of Kurus, each according to his age.

description: Sanjaya sent in message, in the Yanasandhi
sn: अभिवादयन्ति वृद्धाश्च वयस्यांश्च वयस्यवत्। यूनश्चाभ्यवदन् पार्थाः प्रतिपूज्य यथावयः॥
en: They pay their respects to the old and present suitable greetings to those of their age and also to those their younger. In fact, the sons Pritha present suitable greetings to all according to their respective ages.

description: Sanjaya sent in message, in the Yanasandhi
sn: यथाहं धृतराष्ट्रेण शिष्टः पूर्वमितो गतः। अब्रुवं पाण्डवान् गत्वा तन्निबोधत पार्थिवाः॥
en: What I, instructed by Dhritarashtra before having gone there from hence said to the sons Pandu, listen to that, O rulers.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच पृच्छामि त्वां संजय राजमध्ये किमब्रवीद् वाक्यमदीनसत्त्वः। धनंजयस्तात युधां प्रणेता दुरात्मनां जीवितच्छिन्महात्मा॥
en: Dhritarashtra said I ask you, O Sanjaya, in the midst of these kings, what words the noble minded Dhananjaya of Pure habits, the leader in battles, the destroyer of the lives of men of vicious habits, said.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: सञ्जय उवाच दुर्योधनो वाचमिमां शृणोतु यदब्रवीदर्जुनो योत्स्यमानः। युधिष्ठिरस्यानुमते महात्मा धनंजयः शृण्वतः केशवस्य॥
en: Sanjaya said Let Duryodhana listen to this speech which was made by Arjuna, who was eager to fight, with the permission of Yudhishthira and in the hearing of Keshava.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: अन्वत्रस्तो बाहुवीर्यं विदान उपह्वरे वासुदेवस्य धीरः। अवोचमा योत्स्यमानः किरीटी मध्ये ब्रूया धार्तराष्ट्र कुरूणाम्॥
en: Without the slightest fear and conscious of the strength of his arms, in the presence of Vasudeva, the wise one spoke to me. Kiritin, eager to fight, said to me. “Tell the son of Dhritarashtra in the midst of the Kurus."

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: संशृण्वतस्तस्य दुर्भाषिणो वै दुरात्मनः सूतपुत्रस्य सूता यो योद्धमाशंसति मां सदैव मन्दप्रज्ञः कालपक्वोऽतिमूढः॥
en: And in the hearing of the son of Suta of wicked soul, of disagreeable speech, O Suta, who is ever desirous of a fight with me and who is of stupid intellect and of extreme ignorance and whose time is come.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: ये वै राजानः पाण्डवायोधनाय समानीताः शृण्वतां चापि तेषाम्। यथा समग्रं वचनं मृयोक्तं सहामात्यं श्रावयेथा नृपं तत्॥
en: And also in the hearing of those kings who have been assembled to fight the Pandavas, the entire collection of words used by me; let that king with his ministers hear what I say.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: यथा नूनं देवराजस्य देवाः शुश्रूषन्ते वज्रहस्तस्य सर्वे। तथाशृण्वन् पाण्डवा: संजयाश्च किरीटिना वाचमुक्तां समर्थाम्॥
en: As all the gods hear what is said by the chief of the deities, with the thunderbolt in his hands, so did the Pandavas and the Srinjaya listen to the able speech made by Kiritin.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: इत्यब्रवीदर्जुनो योत्स्यमानो गाण्डीवधन्वा लोहितपद्मनेत्रः। न चेद् राज्यं मुञ्चति धार्तराष्ट्रो युधिष्ठिरस्याजमीढस्य राज्ञः॥
en: Thus spoke Arjuna eager for fight armed with the Gandharva-bow and with his lotus eyes looking red-If the son of Dhritarashtra does not surrender the kingdom of Yudhishthira, the king of Ajmida.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: दनिर्विष्टं पापकं धार्तराष्ट्रः। येषां युद्धं भीमसेनार्जुनाभ्यां तथाश्विभ्यां वासुदेवेन चैव॥
en: Then there are surely some acts done before (by them), the fruits of which have not been obtained by the son of Dhritarashtra of wicked souls for which battle is desired with Bhimasena and Arjuna and the same with the sons of Ashvin and Vamdeva.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: शैनेयेन ध्रुवमात्तायुधेन धृष्टद्युम्नेनाथ शिखण्डिना च। युधिष्ठिरेणेन्द्रकल्पेन चैव योऽपध्यानान्निर्दहेद् गां दिवं च॥
en: And with the son of Shini and with Dhrishtadyumna of sure arms and with Shikhandin and with Yudhishthira who is equal to Indra and who can consume the Earth and the Heaven by the strength of his asceticism.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: तैश्चेद् योद्धं मन्यते धार्तराष्ट्रो निर्वृत्तोऽर्थः सकलः पाण्डवानाम्। रुपैहि युद्धं यदि मन्यसे त्वम्॥
en: If war with them is thought of by the son of Dhritarashtra, then are all the subjects of the Pandavas gained. Therefore do not propose peace for gaining the end of the Pandavas; let there be war if you please.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: यां तां वने दुःखशय्यामवात्सीत् प्रव्राजितः पाण्डवो धर्मचारी। आप्नोतु तां दुःखतरामनर्थामन्त्यां शय्यां धार्तराष्ट्रः परासुः॥
en: The bed of woe which the son of Pandu attached to virtuous habits lay, exiled in woods-let the son of Dhritarashtra when dead in the field obtain a bed of greater endless woe.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: ह्रिया ज्ञानेन तपसा दमेन शौर्येणाथो धर्मगुप्त्या धनेन। नध्यातिष्ठद् धार्तराष्ट्रो दुरात्मा॥
en: The son of Dhritarashtra of wicked soul and of unrighteous conduct could never conquer the son of Kuru and Pandu (at the game of dice) by means of modesty, knowledge, asceticism, self-control, heroism or by strength accompanied with righteousness,

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: मायोपधः प्रणिपातार्जवाभ्यां तपोदमाभ्यां धर्मगुप्त्या बलेना स्तितिक्षमाणः क्लिश्यमानोऽतिवेलम्॥
en: Graced with meekness and benevolence, with asceticism and self-control and with might attended with virtue, speaking the truth, (Yudhishthira), a prey to deception, has borne great sufferings.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: यदा ज्येष्ठः पाण्डवः संशितात्मा क्रोधं यत्तं वर्षपूगान् सुघोरम्। स्तदा युद्धं धार्तराष्ट्रोऽन्वतप्स्यत्॥
en: When the eldest son of Pandu, who has brought his soul under control, will direct his wrath nursed during a series of years towards the Kurus, then will the son of Dhritarashtra repent for the war.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: कृष्णवर्मेव ज्वलितः समिद्धो यथा दहेत् कक्षमग्निर्निदाघे। एवं दग्धा धार्तराष्ट्रस्य सेना युधिष्ठिरः क्रोधदीप्तोऽन्ववेक्ष्य॥
en: As blazing fire, raging in all directions, burns up and withers dry grass during summer, so will the army of the son of Dhritarashtra be withered by the mere glance of Yudhishthira fired by wrath.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: यदा द्रष्टा भीमसेनं रथस्थं गदाहस्तं क्रोधविषं वमन्तम्। अमर्षणं पाण्डवं भीमवेगं तदा युद्धं धार्तराष्ट्रोऽन्वतप्स्यत्॥
en: When the son of Dhritarashtra sees Bhimasena, riding his car with mace in his hand and vomiting the poison of his wrath, that wrathful Pandava of terrible strength, then will he repent for the war.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: सेनानगं दंशितं भीमसेनं स्वालक्षणं वीरहणं परेषाम्। मन्तं चमूमन्तकसंनिकाशं तदा स्मर्ता वचनस्यातिमानी॥
en: When that exceedingly vain one beholds Bhimasena sled in iron, fighting in the front ranks of his army, incapable of being grazed at even by his own men, killing the heroes of other side and sending them to the abode of the God of death, then will these words be remembered by him.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: यदा द्रष्टा भीमसेनेन नागान् निपातितान् गिरिकूटप्रकाशान्। स्तदा युद्धं धार्तराष्ट्रोऽन्वतप्स्यत्॥
en: When the son of Dhritarashtra sees elephants felled to the ground by Bhimasena looking like the summits of mountains with their pierced pot-like heads pouring blood like pots pouring water, then will he repent for the war.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: महासिंहो गा व इव प्रविश्य गदापाणिर्धार्तराष्ट्रानुपेत्य। यदा भीमो भीमरूपो निहन्ता तदा युद्धं धार्तराष्ट्रोऽन्वतप्स्यत्॥
en: When like a huge lion falling upon battle, with a mace in hand, Bhimasena like a slayer of terrible appearance approaches the son of Dhritarashtra, then will that son of Dhritarashtra repent for the war.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: महाभये वीतभयः कृतास्रः समागमे शत्रुबलामर्दी। सकृद् रथेनाप्रतिमान रथौघान् पदातिसंघान् गदयाऽभिनिघ्नन्॥
en: When that one who is without fear even in great dangers and skilled in the use of weapons and the slayer of the enemies armies, riding on his beautiful car works havoc with his mace among the numerous cars and foot-soldiers;

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: शैक्येन नागांस्तरसा विगृह्णन् यदा छेत्ता धार्तराष्ट्रस्य सैन्यम्। स्तदा युद्धं धार्तराष्ट्रोऽन्वतप्स्यत्॥
en: Fastening quickly the elephants by nooses, when he fells down the army of the son of Dhritarashtra like a sturdy man cutting down a forest with an axe, then will the son of Dhritarashtra repent for the war.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: तृणप्रायं ज्वलनेनेव दग्धं ग्रामं यथा धार्तराष्ट्रान् समीक्ष्य। पक्वं सस्यं वैद्युतेनेव दग्धं परासिक्तं विपुलं स्वं बलौघम्॥
en: When like a village containing several huts of straw burnt up by fire, he sees the army of the son of Dhritarashtra consumed or when he sees his vast hosts of armies scattered like ripe corns struck by lightning.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: हतप्रवीरं विमुखं भयात पराङ्मुखं प्रायशोऽधृष्टयोधम्। शस्त्रार्चिषा भीमसेनेन दग्धं तदा युद्धं धार्तराष्ट्रोऽन्वतप्स्यत्॥
en: With their heroic leaders killed and his soldiers struck with fear flying with their backs towards the field and their vast army dispersed, consumed as it were by the fire of the arms of Bhimasena, then will the son of Dhritarashtra repent for the war.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: उपासंगानाचरेद् दक्षिणेन वराङ्गानां नकुलचित्रयोधी। यदा रथाग्यो रथिनः प्रणेता तदा युद्धं धार्तराष्ट्रोऽन्वतप्स्यत्॥
en: When Nakula, the chief among carwarriors, of great skill in the use of weapons skillfully shoots hundreds of arrows and kill the car-warriors of the other side, then will the son of Dhritarashtra repent of the war.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: रथैः शुभैः सुखोचितो दुःखशय्यां वनेषु दीर्घ कालं नकुलो यामशेत। आशीविषः क्रुद्ध इवोद्वमन् विषं तदा युद्धं धार्तराष्ट्रोऽन्वतप्स्यत्॥
en: Accustomed to comforts, Nakula for a long time slept on an uncomfortable bed in the woods; and when like an angry snake he will vomit poison, then will the son of Dhritarashtra repent for the war.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: त्यक्तात्मानः पार्थिवा योधनाय समादिष्टा धर्मराजेन सूत। सैन्यमभिद्रवन्तो दृष्ट्वा पश्चात् तप्स्यते धार्तराष्ट्रः॥
en: Desperate of their lives the rulers of the earth, directed to fight by the king of Dharma (virtue), O Suta, riding on white cars will work havoc among the (enemies') army. Seeing that the son of Dhritarashtra will afterwards repent.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: शिशून् कृतास्त्रानशिशुप्रकाशान् यदा द्रष्टा कौरवः पञ्च शूरान्। स्तदा युद्धं धार्तराष्ट्रोऽन्वतप्स्यत्॥
en: When the sons of Kuru see the five heroes, children in years but old in acts, desperate of their lives, working havoc among the sons of Kuru; then will the sons of Dhritarashtra repent for the war.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: यदा गतोद्वाहमकूजनाक्षं सुवर्णतारं रथमाततायीः। दान्तैर्युक्तं सहदेवोऽधिरूढः शिरांसि राज्ञां क्षेप्स्यते मार्गणौघैः॥
en: When Sahadeva, mounted on a car with well trained horses, proceeding in the wished for direction, having noiseless wheels and adorned with golden stars, will fell down the heads of kings with innumerable arrows.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: महाभये सम्प्रवृत्ते रथस्थं विवर्तमानं समरे कृतास्त्रम्। सर्वा दिशः सम्पतन्तं समीक्ष्य तदा युद्धं धार्तराष्ट्रोऽन्वतप्स्यत्॥
en: Seeing that warrior skilled in the use of weapons, mounted on a car, present in the battlefield on working havoc and filling soldiers in all directions, the son of Dhritarashtra will repent for the war.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: ह्रीनिषेवो निपुणः सत्यवादी महाबलः सर्वधर्मोपपन्नः। गान्धारिमार्छस्तुमुले क्षिप्रकारी क्षेप्ता जनान् सहदेवस्तरस्वी॥
en: When Sahadeva who is modest, skillful in battle truthful, of great strength and graced with all virtues, active, capable of speedily doing things, meets the son of Gandhara in terrible and fells down his men.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: यदा द्रष्टा द्रौपदेयान् महेषून् शूरान् कृतास्त्रान् रथयुद्धकोविदान्। स्तदा युद्धं धार्तराष्ट्रोऽन्वतप्स्यत्॥
en: When he sees the son of Draupadi, the mighty heroes, skillful in the use of weapons and having a knowledge of fighting on cars, darting at the enemies like serpents of quick poison, then will the son of Dhritarashtra repent for the war.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: यदाभिमन्युः परवीरघाती शरैः परान् मेघ इवाभिवर्षन्। स्तदा युद्धं धार्तराष्ट्रोऽन्वतप्स्यत्।॥
en: When Abhimanyu the slayer of heroes on the other side, shoots arrows on the enemies as the clouds pour water-when he, skilled in the weapons like Krishna, overpowers the enemies, then will the son of Dhritarashtra repent for the war.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: यदा द्रष्टा बालमबालवीर्य द्विषच्चामूं मृत्युमिवोत्पतन्तम्। सौभद्रमिन्द्रप्रतिमं कृतास्त्रं तदा युद्धं धार्तराष्ट्रोऽन्वतप्स्यत्॥
en: When he sees the son of Subhadra, who though a child is not a child in heroism is like Indra is skillful in the use of weapons falling on the men of the enemies like death itself; then will the son of Dhritarashtra repent for the war.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: प्रभद्रकाः शीघ्रतरा युवानो विशारदाः सिंहसमानवीर्याः। स्तदा युद्धं धार्तराष्ट्रोऽन्वतप्स्यत्॥
en: When the young Prabhadrakas having great activity, skilled in battle and having the might equal to that of lions, fell down the sons of Dhritarashtra along with their armies; then will the son of Dhritarashtra repent for the war.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: वृद्धौ विराटदुपदौ महारथौ पृथक् चमूभ्यामभिवर्तमानौ। स्तदा युद्धं धार्तराष्ट्रोऽन्वतप्स्यत्॥
en: When he sees those veterans in war, Virata and Drupada, mighty car-warriors, each present in his own post separately attack the sons of Dhritarashtra with their armies; then will the son of Dhritarashtra repent for the war,

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: यदा कृतास्त्रो दुपदः प्रचिन्वन् शिरांसि यूनां समरे रथस्थः। स्तदा युद्धं धार्तराष्ट्रोऽन्वतप्स्यत्॥
en: When Drupada, skilled in the use of weapons, from the car down the heads of young warriors in battle; and when, wrathful, he shoots arrows from his bow; then will the son of Dhritarashtra repent for the war.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: यदा विराटः परवीरघाती रणान्तरे शत्रुचमूं प्रवेष्टा। स्तदा युद्धं धार्तराष्ट्रोऽन्वतप्स्यत्॥
en: When Virata, the slayer of heroes in the other side, penetrates into the ranks of the enemy and works havoc among them with the aid of the Matsyas of cool courage. then will the son of Dhritarashtra repent for the war.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: ज्येष्ठं मात्स्यमनृशंसार्यरूपं विराटपुत्रं रथिनं पुरस्तात्। यदा द्रष्टा दंशितं पाण्डवार्थे तदा युद्धं धार्तराष्ट्रोऽन्वतप्स्यत्॥
en: When he sees the eldest son of Virata, the king of the Matsyas of cool courage, clad in iron, in his chariot in the front ranks of his army on the side of the Pandavas, then will the son of Dhritarashira repent for the war.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: रणे हते कौरवाणां प्रवीरे शिखण्डिना सत्तमे शान्तनूजे। न जातु नः शत्रवो धारयेयुरसंशयं सत्यमेतद् ब्रवीमि।।
en: The virtuous son of Shantanu; that hero among the sons of Kuru, being killed in battle by Shikhandin; then our enemies will undoubtedly perish. I speak this truly.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: यदा शिखण्डी रथिनः प्रचिन्वन् भीष्मं रथेनाभियाता वरूथी। स्तदा युद्धं धार्तराष्ट्रोऽन्वतप्स्यत्॥
en: When cutting down the car-warriors, Shikhandin, on a car well protected goes forth to meet Bhishma leveling to the dust the host of cars by his celestial horses, then will the son of Dhritarashtra repent for the war.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: यदा द्रष्टा संजयानामनीके धृष्टद्युम्नं प्रमुखे रोचमानम्। अस्त्रं यस्मै गुह्यमुवाच धीमान् द्रोणस्तदा तप्स्यति धार्तराष्ट्रः॥
en: When he sees, seated in the front ranks of the Srinjayas, effulgent in his splendour, Dhrishtadyumna, whom the wise Drona initiated in to the mysteries of the use of wcapons; then will the son of Dhritarashtra repent.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: यदा स सेनापतिरप्रमेयः परामृद्नन्निषुभिर्धार्तराष्ट्रान्। द्रोणं रणे शत्रुसहोऽभियाता तदा युद्धं धार्तराष्ट्रोऽन्वतप्स्यत्॥
en: When that leader of armies, of immeasurable strength, working havoc among the armies of the sons of Dhritarashtra by his arrows, goes forth to encounter Drona and the enemy in battle; then will the son of Dhritarashtra repent for the war.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: ह्रीमान् मनीषी बलवान् मनस्वी स लक्ष्मीवान् सोमकानां प्रबर्हः। न जातु तं शत्रवोऽन्ये सहेरन् येषां स स्यादग्रणीर्वृष्णिसिंहः॥
en: No foe can withstand them who have for their leader of the lion of the Vrishni race, that chief of the Somaka tribe, who is modest, wise, powerful, independent, blessed with prosperity.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: इदं च ब्रूया मा वृणीष्वेति लोके युद्धेऽद्वितीयं सचिवं रथस्थम्। शिनेर्नप्तारं प्रवृणीम सात्यकि महाबलं वीतभयं कृतास्त्रम्॥
en: Tell this also (to Duryodhana); Do not desire (the kingdom), we have chosen Satyaki, the guard of Shini for our leader; he is unequaled in battle in this world, a car-warrior of dauntless and powerful might and skilled in the use of weapons,

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: महोरस्को दीर्घबाहुः प्रमाथी युद्धेऽद्वितीयः परमास्त्रवेदी। शिनेर्नप्ता तालमात्रायुधोऽयं महारथो वीतभयः कृतास्त्रः॥
en: Of broad chest and long arms, the slayer of enemies unequaled in battle and acquainted with the best of weapons, the grandson of Shini well versed in the use of weapons, a mighty car-warrior who knows no fear has a bow measuring four cubits.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: यदा शिनीनामधिपो मयोक्तः शरैः परान् मेघ इव प्रवर्षन्। स्तदा युद्धं धार्तराष्ट्रोऽन्वतप्स्यत्॥
en: When the ruler of the Shinis, the slayer of foes directed by me, will shower volleys of arrows on the enemy, as the clouds do (the rain) and completely cover them then will the son of Dhritarashtra repent for the war.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: यदा धृतिं कुरुते योत्स्यमानः स दीर्घबाहुर्दृढधन्वा महात्मा। सिंहस्येव गन्धमाघ्राय गावः संचेष्टन्ते शत्रवोऽस्माद् रणाग्रे॥
en: When that one with long arms and of firm grasp on the bow makes up his mind for fight; then will the foes before the battle act like cattle who have got scent of a lion.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: स दीर्घबाहुर्दृढधन्वा महात्मा भिन्द्याद् गिरीन् संहरेत् सर्वलोकान्। अस्त्रे कृती निपुणः क्षिप्रहस्तो दिवि स्थितः सूर्य इवाभिमाति॥
en: He, of long arms of firm grasp on the bow and of a large fond, can pierce the mountain and destroy the whole world. Acquainted with the use of weapons, skillful and of an agile, hand, he shores like the sun in the sky.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: चित्रः सूक्ष्मः सुकृतो यादवस्य अस्त्रे योगो वृष्णिसिंहस्य भूयान्। यथाविधं योगमाहुः प्रशस्तं सर्वैर्गुणैः सात्यकिस्तैरुपेतः॥
en: The lion of the Vrishni race, that descendant of Yadu of superior training, has many delicate and wonderful weapons. Satyaki has competent knowledge of the use of excellent arms; and he is endued with all the good qualities that are said to be good.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: र्यदा युक्तं स्यन्दनं माघवस्या स्तदा तप्स्यत्यकृतात्मा स मन्दः॥
en: When he sees the golden car of Satyaki, the descendant of Madhu with four white horses; then that foolish son of Dhritarashtra with a soul addicted to vices repent for the war.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: यदा रथं हेममणिप्रकाशं श्वेताश्वयुक्तं वानरकेतुमुचम्। द्रष्टा ममाप्यास्थितं केशवेन तदा तप्स्यत्यकृतात्मा स मन्दः॥
en: When also he sees my terrible car, guided by Keshava, shining with gold and precious stones, with white horses and with a banner having the figure of a monkey; then will that vicious-souled fool repent.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: यदा मौास्तलनिष्पेषमुग्रं महाशब्दं वज्रनिष्पेषतुल्यम्। विधूयमानस्य महारणे मया स गाण्डिवस्य श्रोष्यति मन्दबुद्धिः॥ स्तप्ता युद्धे दुर्मतिर्दुःसहायः। दृष्ट्रा सैन्यं बाणवर्षान्धकारे प्रभज्यन्तं गोकुलवद् रणाचे॥
en: When that fool hears the fierce twanging sound produced by the contact of the leather covering fingers with the string of the bow, resembling the roaring of thunder and the great battle field covered with smoke by my Gandiva bow; then will the foolish son of Dhritarashtra of weak intellect repent on seeing himself helpless, his soldiers destroyed in the darkness produced by the raining of arrows like herds of cows, before the actual fighting commences.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: बलाहकादुच्चरतः सुभीमान् विद्युत्स्फुलिङ्गानिव घोररूपान्। सहस्रघ्नान् द्विषतां सङ्गरेषु अस्थिच्छिदो मर्मभिदः सुपुङ्खान्॥ यदा द्रष्टा ज्यामुखाद् बाणसंघान् गाण्डीवमुक्तानापतत: शिताग्रान्। स्तदा युद्धं धार्तराष्ट्रोऽन्वतप्स्यत्॥
en: When he sees the terrible host of arrows, with sharp edges having beautiful feathers and able to penetrate into the vitals shot from the string of the Gandiva bow, like terrible flashes of lightning proceeding from clouds, killing thousands of the host of enemies and devouring innumerable horses and elephants clad in mail; then will the son of Dhritarashtra repent for the war.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: यदा मन्दः परबाणान् विमुक्तान् ममे षुभिर्जियमाणान् प्रतीपम्। स्तदा युद्धं धार्तराष्ट्रोऽन्वतप्स्यत्॥
en: When the fool sees the arrows shot from the bows of our enemies being struck by my arrows twined back or cut off being pierced obliquely by my shafts; then will the son of Dhritarashtra repent for the war.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: यदा विपाठा मद्भुजविप्रमुक्ता द्विजाः फलानीव महीरुहाग्रात्। प्रचेतार उत्तमाङ्गानि यूनां तदा युद्धं धार्तराष्ट्रोऽन्वतप्स्यत्॥
en: When the arrows shot by me cut off the five figures of young men on the other side as birds pluck off fruits from the top of trees then will the son of Dhritarashtra repent for the war.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: यदा द्रष्टा पततः स्यन्दनेभ्यो महागजेभ्योऽश्वगतान् सुयोधनान्। शरैर्हतान् पातितांश्चैव रङ्गे तदा युद्धं धार्तराष्ट्रोऽन्वतप्स्यत्॥
en: When he sees excellent warriors falling dead from their chariots and huge elephants struck by my arrows in the field then will the son of Dhritarashtra repent for the war.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: असम्प्राप्तानस्त्रपथं परस्य तदा द्रष्टा नश्यतो धार्तराष्ट्रान्। अकुर्वतः कर्म युद्धे समन्तात् तदा युद्धं धार्तराष्ट्रोऽन्वतप्स्यत्॥
en: When he sees the (other) sons of Dhritarashtra before even reaching within the range of the enemies' weapons fall down dead without even doing anything in the field; then will the son of Dhritarashtra repent for the war.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: पदातिसंघान् रथसंघान् समन्ताद् ह्यात्ताननः काल इवाततेषुः। प्रणोत्स्यामि ज्वलितैर्बाणवषैः शत्रूस्तदा तप्स्यति मन्दबुद्धिः॥
en: When I shall fell down by pouring down burning arrows the enemies and their hosts of infantry and car-warriors in all directions like death with his mouth open, then will that man of weak intellect repent for the war.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: सर्वा दिशः सम्पतता रथेन रजोध्वस्तं गाण्डिवेन प्रकृत्तम्। यदा द्रष्टा स्वबलं सम्प्रमूढं तदा पश्चात् तप्स्यति मन्दबुद्धिः॥
en: When he sees his own army covered by the dust of my chariot going in all sides cut down by my Gandiva and rendered senseiess; then will that man of weak intellect repent.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: कान्दिग्भूतं छिन्नगात्रं विसंज्ञं दुर्योधनो द्रक्ष्यति सर्वसैन्यम्। हताश्ववीराग्रयनरेन्द्रनागं पिपासितं श्रान्तपत्रं भयार्तम्॥ आर्तस्वरं हन्यमानं हतं च विकीर्णकेशास्थिकपालसंघम्। प्रजापतेः कर्म यथार्थनिष्ठितं तदा दृष्ट्वा तप्स्यति मन्दबुद्धिः॥
en: When Duryodhana sees all his soldiers overpowered and runring away all sides with their bodies cut open, senseless and his horses, commanders rulers killed, his army thirsty, struck with fear, crying piteously for help, dead and dying, with their animals rendered faint and hair, bones and heads strewn about as if they were really the work of the Lord of creatures; then will that man of weak intellect repent.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: यदा रथे गाण्डिवं वासुदेवं दिव्यं शङ्ख पाञ्चजन्यं हयांश्च। तूणावक्षय्यौ देवदत्तं च मां च द्रष्ट्वा युद्धे धार्तराष्ट्रोऽन्वतप्स्यत्॥
en: When he sees in the chariot, the Gandiva bow, Vasudeva, the heavenly conch Panchajanya, my horses, the two arrow-holders which are never emptied, Devadatta and myself; then will the son of Dhritarashtra repent for the war.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: उद्वर्तयन् दस्युसङ्घान् समेतान् प्रवर्तयन् युगमन्यद् युगान्ते। स्तदा तप्ता धृतराष्ट्रः सपुत्रः॥
en: When I shall burn the sons of Kuru like the god of fire burning at the time of bringing in this world a Yoga, at the end of another a large number of wicked souls, then will Dhritarashtra with his sons repent for the war.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: सभ्राता वै सहसैन्यः सभृत्यो भ्रष्टैश्वर्व्यः क्रोधवशोऽल्पचेताः। दर्पस्यान्ते निहतो वेपमानः पश्चान्मन्दस्तप्स्यति धार्तराष्ट्रः॥
en: The son of Dhritarashtra, wrathful and of wicked heart, having lost his property along with his brothers, his soldiers and his dependents, at the end of the period of pride, trembling will afterwards repent.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: पूर्वाह्ने मां कृतजप्यं कदाचिद् विप्रः प्रोवाचोदकान्ते मनोज्ञम्। कर्तव्यं ते दुष्करं कर्म पार्थ योद्धव्यं ते शत्रुभिः सव्यसाचिन्॥
en: One day before this when I had finished my prayers a certain Brahmana said to me, after my getting up from the water, these pleasing words-A difficult task will have to be performed by you, O son of Pritha, O Savyasachin, you will have to fight with your enemies.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: इन्द्रो वा ते हरिमान् वज्रहस्तः पुरस्ताद् यातु समरेऽरीन् विनिघ्नन्। सुग्रीवयुक्तेन रथेन वा ते पश्चात् कृष्णो रक्षतु वासुदेवः॥
en: Either Indra on his steed, thunderbolt in his hand will go before you in battle, killing your enemies or mounted on a chariot with Sugriva (name of horse) and other steeds Krishna, the son of Vasudeva will protect you from behind.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: दस्मिन् युद्धे वासुदेवं सहायम्। स मे लब्धो दस्युवधाय कृष्णो मन्ये चैतद् विहितं दैवतैर्मे॥
en: In this war, have I preferred the help of Vasudeva to Indra with the thunderbolt in his hand. That Krishna has come over to my side for the purpose of slaying these wicked men. This I consider has been ordained by the gods.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: अयुद्ध्यमानो मनसाऽपि यस्य जयं कृष्णः पुरुषस्याभिनन्देत्। एवं सर्वान् स व्यतीयादमित्रान् सेन्द्रान् देवान् मानुषे नास्ति चिन्ता॥
en: That man whose victory is merely desired by Krishna, even if the latter does not fight, is sure to triumph over all enemies though they be the gods themselves with Indra. If they are men, there is no anxiety.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: न्महोदधिं सलिलस्याप्रमेयम्। तेजस्विनं कृष्णमत्यन्तशूरं युद्धेन यो वासुदेवं जिगीषेत्॥
en: That man is desirous of crossing the ocean of vast expanse and unfathomable waters, with his two arms, who is desirous of vanquishing in fight the exceedingly heroic Krishna, the son of Vasudeva, of great prowess.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: गिरिं य इच्छेत् तु तलेन भेत्तुं शिलोच्चयं श्वेतमतिप्रमाणम्। न चापि किंचित् स गिरेस्तु कुर्यात्॥
en: He, who desires to pierce by the palm of his hand the high white mountain of huge dimensions, has his hand with his nails only wasted away; and absolutely no harm is done to the mountain.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: अग्नि समिद्धं शमयेद् भुजाभ्यां चन्द्रं च सूर्यं च निवारयेत। हरेद् देवानाममृतं प्रसह्य युद्धेन यो वासुदेवं जिगीषेत्॥
en: He who aspires to vanquish the son of Vasudeva after encountering him in battle, would rob the gods of nectar by force and with his two hands would put out a blazing fire and stop the Sun and the Moon in their course.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: नुत्साद्य राज्ञः समरे प्रसह्या उवाह भार्या यशसा ज्वलन्ती यस्यां जज्ञे रौक्मिणेयो महात्मा॥
en: That Krishna, who alone in his chariot having encountered in battle vanquished the army of the king of the Bhojas, married Rukmini of great fame and effulgence; in her was born the high-souled Pradyumna.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: अयं गान्धारांस्तरसा सम्प्रमथ्य जित्वा पुत्रान् नग्नजित: समग्रान्। बद्धं मुमोच विनदन्तं प्रसह्य सुदर्शनं वै देवतानां ललामम्॥
en: This favorite of the gods, who had speedily vanquished the Gandharvas and conquered all the sons of Nagnajita by sheer force, liberated the imprisoned Sudarshana of great power.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: अय कपाटेन जघान पाण्ड्यं तथा कलिङ्गान् दन्तकूरे ममर्द। अनेन दग्धा वर्षपूगान् विनाथा वाराणसी नगरी सम्बभूव॥
en: He by striking his breast slew the king of Pandya and vanquished the Kalingas in battle; burnt by the city of Varanasi for series of years remained without a lord.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: अयं स्म युद्धे मन्यतेऽन्यैरजेयं तमेकलव्यं नाम निषादराजम्। वेगेनैव शैलमभिहत्य जम्भः शेते स कृष्णेन हतः परासुः॥
en: He was challenged by the king of Nishadas, named Ekalavya, who was incapable of being vanquished by others; but he being struck with force by Krishna lay dead smashed on the hillock like Jambha.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: तथोडग्रसेनस्य सुतं सुदुष्टं वृष्ण्यन्धकानां मध्यगतं समास्थम्। अपातयद् बलदेवद्वितीयो हत्वा ददौ चोग्रसेनाय राज्यम्॥
en: Then did he, having Baladeva as his coadjutor, fell down the extremely wicked son of Baladeva who was seated in court amidst the Vrishnis and Andhakas and then bestowed the kingdom on Ugrasena.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: अयं सौभं योधयामास स्वस्थं विभीषणं मायया शाल्वराजम्। सौभद्वारि प्रत्यगृह्णाच्छतघ्नीं दो• क एनं विषहेत मर्त्यः॥
en: He fought with the terrible king Shalva, the lord of Saubha, without being beside himself (through fear) in consequence of his power of producing effect; and near the gate of Saubha caught hold of Shataghni with his hand; what being on this earth can withstand him in fight?

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: प्राग्जोतिषं नाम बभूव दुर्गं पुरं घोरमसुराणामसह्यम्। महाबलो नरकस्तत्र भौमो जहारादित्या मणिकुण्डले शुभे॥
en: There was fastness of the Asuras, terrible and impenetrable, named Pragjyotisha. There Naraka, son of the Earth of great strength stole the beautiful earrings of Aditi bedecked with gems and kept them.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: न तं देवाः सह शक्रेण शेकुः समागता युधि मृत्योरभीताः। दृष्ट्वा च तं विक्रम केशवस्य बलं तथैवास्त्रमवारणीयम्॥
en: The very gods with Indra who gathered together fearless of death for fight could not fight with him; and seeing the prowess and strength and the irresistible weapons of Krishna.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: जानन्तोऽस्य प्रकृति केशवस्य न्ययोजयन् दस्युवधाय कृष्णम्। मैश्वर्यवान् सिद्धिषु वासुदेवः॥
en: And knowing his nature, they employed Krishna far slaying that wicked being. And Vasudeva undertook (endued with all kinds of prosperity), the accomplishment of that difficult task.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: निर्मोचने षट् सहस्राणि हत्वा संच्छिद्य पाशान् सहसा क्षुरान्तान्। मुरं हत्वा विनिहत्यौघरक्षौ निर्मोचनं चापि जगाम वीरः॥
en: Having slain six thousand near the city of Nirmochana and having broken sharp-edged arrows suddenly coming on him, having killed Mura and also having killed crowds of Rakshasas, that hero went into the city of Nirmochana.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: तत्रैव तेनास्य बभूव युद्धं महाबलेनातिबलस्य विष्णोः। तेनेवोन्मथितः कर्णिकारः॥
en: There did take place a battle between him (Naraka) possessed of great strength and this Vishnu also endued with great strength. And he lay killed by Krishna like a Karnikara tree uprooted by a gale.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: आहृत्य कृष्णो मणिकुण्डले ते हत्वा च भौमं नरकं मुरं च। श्रिया वृतो यशसा प्रत्याजगामाप्रतिमप्रभावः॥ चैव विद्वान्
en: Having killed Naraka, the son of the earth and Mura and taking back that pair of earrings bedecked with gems, the learned one endued with prosperity and fame and of unparalled proves came back.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: अस्मै ववाण्यददंस्तत्र देवा दृष्ट्वा भीमं कर्म कृतं रणे तत्। दाकाशे चाप्सु च ते क्रमः स्यात्॥
en: To him the gods seeing the terrible tasks done in that battle granted boons there, saying-“When you are fighting, you will not have fatigue and there shall be no impediment in your way either in the sky or below the waters.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: नित्येव कृष्णश्च ततः कृतार्थः। एवंरूपे वासुदेवेऽप्रमेये महाबले गुणसम्पत् सदैव॥
en: Nor shall arms stick on your body. Krishna, too, at this considered himself gratificd. Such are ever the virtues of the son of Vasudeva of immeasurable fame and the great strength.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: माशंसते धार्तराष्ट्रो विजेतुम्। सदा ह्येनं तर्कयते दुरात्मा तच्चाप्ययं सहतेऽस्मान् समीक्ष्य॥
en: The son of Dhritarashtra aspires to vanquish this Vishnu, who cannot be withstood in fight and who is of endless strength; and that one of wicked soul is ever trying to imprison him. This Krishna however endures even this for our sake.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: पर्यागतं मम कृष्णस्य चैव यो मन्यते कलहं सम्प्रसह्य। शक्यं हर्तुं पाण्डवानां ममत्वं तद् वेदिता संयुगं तत्र गत्वा॥
en: He, however, who desires to get our Krishna on his side after creating disunion between us will know how far he can take away the affection of Krishna for us, aiter going to the field of battle.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: चैव। नमस्कृत्वा शान्तनवाय राज्ञे द्रोणायाथो सहपुत्राय शारद्वतायाप्रतिद्वन्द्विने च योत्स्याम्यहं राज्यमभीप्समानः॥
en: Having paid due respects to the son of Shantanu and also the king Drona with his son and also to the son of Sharadvata and being desirous of getting back the kingdom, shall I oppose them in battle.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: धर्मेणाप्तं निधनं तस्य मन्ये यो योत्स्यते पाण्डवैः पापबुद्धिः। मिथ्या ग्लहे निर्जिता वै नृशंसैः संवत्सरान् वै द्वादश राजपुत्राः॥
en: That man of wicked intelligence fights with the Pandavas. I shall regard this death as being justly got. Conquered by deceit at the game of dice by those inhuman ones, we ourselves, the sons of a king, for twelve long years.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: वास: कृच्छ्रो विहितश्चाप्यरण्ये दीर्घ कालं चैकमज्ञातवर्षम्। ते हि कस्माज्जीवतां पाण्डवानां नन्दिष्यन्ते धार्तराष्ट्राः पदस्थाः॥
en: Had to reside in the forest encountering all sorts of troubles and difficulties and one year in disguise. During the life time of these Pandavas how shall the sons of Dhritarashtra rejoice possessed of a royal status.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: वैर्महेन्द्रप्रमुखैः सहायैः। स्ततो ध्रुवं नास्ति कृतं च साधु॥
en: If they conquer us engaged in fight being aided by the gods, headed by the great Indra, then will the practice of vice be better than that of virtue and there will surely be no use of behaving honestly.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: न चेदिमं पुरुषं कर्मबद्धं न चेदस्मान् मन्यतेऽसौविशिष्टान्। आशंसेऽहं वासुदेवद्वितीयो दुर्योधनं सानुबन्धं निहन्तुम्॥
en: If the effects of a man's actions redound on him; and if we be superior to him, as I think we are, I hope that with the son of Vasudeva as my coadjutor, I shall kill Duryodhana with all his assistants.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: न चेदिदं कर्म नरेन्द्र वध्यं न चेद् भवेत् सुकृतं निष्फलं वा। इदं च तच्चाभिसमीक्ष्य नूनं पराजयो धार्तराष्ट्रस्य साधुः॥
en: This act, O chief of me, (sending us into exile and themselves possessing our kingdom) cannot but be wicked; and all our good deeds cannot be totally devoid of good fruits. Having considered this as well as that (I think that) the defeat of the son of Dhritarashtra is certain.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: प्रत्यक्षं वः कुरवो यद् ब्रवीमि युध्यमाना धार्तराष्ट्रा न सन्ति। न युद्धे वै शेष इहास्ति कश्चित्॥
en: You will yourselves be witnesses, O son of Kuru, to (the events) I prophesy; the sons of Dhritarashtra will cease to exist, if they fight. If they do not fight, then they may live; but in a fight with us, none of them will be alive.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: हत्वा त्वहं धार्तराष्ट्रान् सकर्णान् राज्यं कुरूणामवजेता समग्रम्। यद् वः कार्यं तत् कुरुध्वं यथास्वमिष्ठान् दारानात्मभोगान् भजध्वम्॥
en: Having killed the sons of Dhritarashtra along with Karna, I shall take the whole of the kingdom from the sons of Kúru. (In the mean time) do whatever work you may have and enjoy yourselves and your wives and everything sweet.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: अप्येवं नो ब्राह्मणाः सन्ति वृद्धा बहुश्रुताः शीलवन्तः कुलीनाः। सांवत्सरा ज्योतिषि चाभियुक्ता नक्षत्रयोगेषु च निश्चयज्ञाः॥
en: Even among ourselves there are Brahmanas, old, well versed in the knowledge of the holy books, of good conduct of noble birth, acquainted with the events of the year and certain of their interpretation of the motion of the planets,

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: उच्चावचं दैवयुक्तं रहस्यं दिव्यः प्रश्ना मृगचक्रा मुहूर्ताः। क्षयं महान्तं कुरुसुंजयानां निवेदयन्ते पाण्डवानां जयं च॥
en: Capable of explaining the mysteries of the gods and of answering questions regarding coming events, understanding the signs of the zodiac, prophesying the great overthrow of the Kurus and the Srinjayas and the triumph of the Pandavas.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: यथा हि नो मन्यतेऽजातशत्रुः संसिद्धार्थो द्विषतां निग्रहाय। जनार्दनश्चाप्यपरोक्षविद्यो न संशयं पश्यति वृष्णिसिंहः॥
en: Owing to this he who has created no enemies considers his objects attained by reason of the overthrow of his enemies. Janardana, too, the lion among the race of the Vrishnis, who has a knowledge of what is to came in the future, undoubtedly sees all this.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: अहं तथैवं खलु भाविरूपं पश्यामि बुद्ध्या स्वयमप्रमत्तः। दृष्टिश्च मे न व्यथते पुराणी संयुध्यमाना धार्तराष्ट्रा न सन्ति॥
en: I, too, who have not lost my senses see all these events of the future by my foresight. My power of vision into the future) acquired a long time ago does not pain me. I see clearly that the sons of Dhritarashtra fighting shall cease to exist.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: रनाहता कम्पति मे धनुर्ला। बाणाश्च मे तूणमुखाद् विसृत्य मुहुर्मुहुर्गन्तुमुशन्ति चैव॥
en: Without any touch, my Gandiva bow yawns. Though my bow remains untouched, yet the string shakes. My arrows, too, coming near the mouth of my arrow holder try to fly away every moment.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: खङ्गः कोशान्निःसरति प्रसन्नो हित्वेव जीर्णीमुरगस्त्वचं स्वाम्। ध्वजे वाचो रौद्ररूपा भवन्ति कदा रथो योक्ष्यते ते किरीटिन्॥
en: The polished sword comes out of the scabbard, as a snake does out of its own worn out skin, and near my banners are heard terrific words like these-'O Kiritin, when will your chariot be yoked?'

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: गोमायुसंघाश्च नदन्ति रात्रौ रक्षांस्यथो निष्पतन्त्यन्तरिक्षात्। मृगाः शृगाला: शितिकण्ठाश्च काका गृध्रा बकाश्चैव तरक्षवश्च॥
en: At night crowds of jackals make their rejoicing; and from the sky do Rakshasas come down as also the deer and jackals, peacocks and crows and vultures and cranes and wolves.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: सुवर्णपत्राश्च पतन्ति पश्चाद् दृष्ट्वा रथं श्वेतहयप्रयुक्तम्। अहं ह्येकः पार्थिवान् सर्वयोधान् शरान् वर्षन् मृत्युलोकं नयेयम्॥
en: Also birds, having golden feathers, come down and having seen my chariot with white steeds follow it. I alone unaided can send to the regions of death all the rulers and warriors by showing my arrows.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: समाददानः पृथगस्त्रमार्गान् यथाग्निरिद्धो गहन् निदाघे। स्थूणाकर्णं पाशुपतं महास्त्रं ब्राह्मं चास्त्रं यच्च शक्रोऽप्यदान्मे॥
en: I shall fling the great weapons, called Sthuna, Karna, Pashupata and Brahma all of which Shakra gave me, in different directions; as fire in the hot season burns up a forest.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: वधे धृतो वेगवतः प्रमुञ्चन् नाहं प्रजाः किंचिदिहावशिष्ये। शान्ति लप्स्ये परमो ह्येष भाव: स्थिरो मम ब्रूहि गावल्गणे तान्॥
en: Bringing all my powers and by the aid of my work of destruction, shall I fling these weapons and leave no trace of those that come to the field; and then shall I obtain rest. Such a state of rest is excellent. This is my determination. Tell them this, O son of Gavalgani.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: ये वै जय्याः समरे देवानपीन्द्रप्रमुखान् समेतान्। सूत लब्वा तैर्मन्यते कलहं सम्प्रसह्य स धार्तराष्ट्रः पश्यत मोहमस्य॥
en: Those who are victors in battle even with the entire body of gods headed by Indra, O Suta-the son of Dhritarashtra thinks that in a battle with them, he will be the victor. Look at his folly.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: वृद्धो भीष्मः शान्तनवः कृपश्च द्रोणः सपुत्रो विदुरश्च धीमान्। एते सर्वे यद् वदन्ते तदस्तु आयुष्मन्तः कुरवः सन्तु सर्वे॥
en: The aged Bhishma, the son of Shantanu, Kripa, Drona with his son and the wise Vidura, what all these say, let that be. May all the sons of Kuru attain to old age.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच समवेतेषु सर्वेषु तेषु राजसु भारत। दुर्योधनमिदं वाक्यं भीष्मः शान्तनवोऽब्रवीत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said In the midst of all those kings, O Bharata, Bhima, the son of Shantanu, spoke these words of Duryodhana:

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: बृहस्पतिश्चोशना च ब्रह्माणं पर्युपस्थितौ। मरुतश्च सहेन्द्रेण वसवश्चाग्निना सह॥
en: (Once on a time) Brihaspati along with Shakra went to Brahma, as also did thc Maruta with Indra and the Vasus with Agni.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: आदित्याश्चैव साध्याश्च ये च सप्तर्षयो दिवि। विश्वावसुश्च गन्धर्वः शुभाश्चाप्सरसां गणाः॥
en: The Adityas, the Sadhyas, the seven heavenly Rishis, the Vishvavasu, the Gandharvas and beautiful cluster of the Apsaras.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: नमस्कृत्योपजग्मुस्ते लोकवृद्धं पितामहम्। परिवार्य च विश्वेशं पर्यासत दिवौकसः॥
en: Having saluted to that old grandsire of the universe, approached him and the dwellers of heaven sat round that lord of the universe.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: तेषां मनश्च तेजश्चाप्याददानाविवौजसा। पूर्वदेवौ व्यतिक्रान्तौ नरनारायणावृषी॥
en: As if attracting unto themselves by their own energy the intellects and energies of them all, the two ancient Rishis, Nara and Narayana, departed.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: बृहस्पतिस्तु पप्रच्छ ब्रह्माणं काविमाविति। भवन्तं नोपतिष्ठेते तौ नः शंस पितामहः॥
en: Brihaspati too asked Brahma "who are these two, who, 0 O grandsire, without worshipping you, go away. Tell us that.”

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: ब्रह्मोवाच यावेतौ पृथिवीं द्यां च भासयन्तौ तपस्विनौ। ज्वलन्तौ रोचमानौ च व्याप्यातीतौ महाबलौ॥
en: Brahma said These two ascetics blazing, as it were with beauty and illuminating the earth and heaven and possessed of great energy went away.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: नरनारायणावेतौ लोकाल्लोकं समास्थितौ। ऊर्जितौ स्वेन तपसा महासत्त्वपराक्रमौ॥
en: They are Nara and Narayana who have just come from the earth and are at present staying in these regions. With the fruits of their own asceticism they are resplendent and are possessed of great energy and prowess.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: एतौ हि कर्मणा लोकं नन्दयामासतुवि॒वम्। द्विधाभूतौ महाप्राज्ञौ विद्धि ब्रह्मन् परंतपौ। असुराणां विनाशाय देवगन्धर्वपूजितौ॥
en: These two by their acts ever bring rejoicing to the words; they worshipped by the gods and the Gandharvas live for the destruction of the Asuras.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच जगाम शक्रस्तच्छुत्वा यत्र तौ तेपतुस्तपः। सार्धं देवगणः सर्वैर्वृहस्पतिपुरोगमैः॥
en: Shakra having heard this went to the place where these two were practicing their devotions, in company with all that host of gods with Brihaspati going in front of them.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: तदा देवासुरे युद्धे भये जाते दिवौकसाम्। अयाचत महात्मानौ नरनारायणौ वरम्॥
en: At the time, among the dwellers of the heaven there was a great panic owing to a battle between the gods and the Asuras and they (the gods) asked a boon of the noblesouled Nara and Narayana.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: तावब्रूतां वृणीष्वेति तदा भरतसत्तम। अथैतावब्रवीच्छक्रः साह्यं नः क्रियतामिति॥
en: Those two then said “Choose (the boon)," O best of the race of Bharata. Shakra then said to those two-"make us invincible".

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: ततस्तौ शक्रमब्रूतां करिष्यावो यदिच्छसि। ताभ्यां च सहितः शक्रो विजिग्ये दैत्यदानवान्॥
en: Then did the two tell Shakra, "we shall do what you wish.” Then aided by them Shakra triumphed over the Daityas and the Danavas.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: नर इन्द्रस्य संग्रामे हत्वा शत्रून् परन्तपः। पौलोमान् कालखमांश्च सहस्राणि शतानि च॥
en: That excellent among the ascetics, Nara, having killed the enemies in the battle for Indra, (killed) hundred and thousands of Paulomas and Kalakhanjas.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: एषं भ्रान्ते रथे तिष्ठन् भल्लेनापाहरच्छिरः। जम्भस्य ग्रसमानस्य तदा ह्यर्जुन आहवे॥
en: Seated on a revolving car, this Arjuna, by mcans of a broad-headed arrow, cut down the head of Jambha, who had opened his mouth to swallow him.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: एष पारे समुद्रस्य हिरण्यपुरमारुजत्। जित्वा षष्टिं सहस्राणि निवातकवचान् रणे॥
en: He penetrated into Hiranyapura, on the other side of the sea, after vanquiching in battle sixty thousands of Nivatakvachas.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: एष देवान् सहेन्द्रेण जित्वा परपुरञ्जयः। अतर्पयन्महाबाहुरर्जुनो जातवेदसम्॥
en: This Arjuna, the conqueror of hostile cities, of long arms gratified the god of fire by conquering the gods with Indra.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: नारायणस्तथैवात्र भूयसोऽन्याञ्जघान ह। एवमेतौ महावीर्यौ तौ पश्यत समागतौ॥
en: In the same way Narayana has in this world killed innumerable other (Asuras); such are these two of great prowess that are seen to be united together.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: वासुदेवार्जुनौ वीरौ समवेतौ महारथौ। नरनारायणौ देवौ पूर्वदेवाविति श्रुतिः॥
en: The son of Vamdeva and Arjuna, the two great heroic car-warriors that have now allied together are the two ancient gods, Nara and Narayana. Such is the general belief.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: अजेयौ मानुषे लोके सेन्ट्रैरपि सुरासुरैः। एष नारायणः कृष्णः फाल्गुनश्च नरः स्मृतः। नारायणो नरश्चैव सत्त्वमेकं द्विधा कृतम्॥
en: In capable of being vanquished by men in this world and by the gods and Asuras with Indra, this Krishna is Narayana and this son of Phalguni, Nara, which the holy books declare. Narayana and Nara are of the same essence split up into two.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: एतौ हि कर्मणा लोकानश्नुवातेऽक्षयान् ध्रुवान्। तत्र तत्रैव जायते युद्धकाले पुनः पुनः॥
en: These two by their acts attain to several eternal and inexhaustible regions and are born in those places again and again in times of war.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: तस्मात् कर्मैव कर्तव्यमिति होवाच नारदः। एतद्धि सर्वमाचष्ट वृष्णिचक्रस्य वेदवित्॥
en: Therefore is war their duty. This what Narada conversant with the Vedas has said to the race of the Vrishnis.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: शङ्खचक्रगदाहस्तं यदा द्रक्ष्यसि केशवम्। पर्याददानं चास्त्राणि भीमधन्वानमर्जुनम्॥
en: When you will see Keshava with the conch, the disc and the mace in his hand and Arjuna with that terrific-looking bow taking up weapons.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: सनातनौ महात्मानौ कृष्णावेकरथे स्थितौ। दुर्योधन तदा तात स्मर्ताऽसि वचनं मम॥
en: The two eternal and noble-souled Krishna's seated on the same chariot, O Duryodhana, O dear, then will you remember my words.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: नोचेदयमभाव: स्यात् कुरूणां प्रत्युपस्थितः। अर्थाच्च तात धर्माच्च तव बुद्धिरुपप्लुता॥
en: Otherwise why should the sons of Kuru have come to this state. Your intellect. O dear, has fallen off from both virtue and worldly profit.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: न चेद् ग्रहीष्यसे वाक्यं श्रोतासि सुबहून् हतान्। तवैव हि मतं सर्वे कुरवः पर्युपासते॥
en: If you do not accept my advice; then you will hear of the slaying of numerous men of your army; my advice is listen to by all the sons of Kuru.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: त्रयाणामेव च मतं तत् त्वमेकोऽनुमन्यसे। रामेण चैव शप्तस्य कर्णस्य भरतर्षभ॥
en: The advice of the three persons you alone listen to, O bull among the race of Bharata, viz. Karna, who was cursed by Rama,

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: दुर्जातेः सूतपुत्रस्य शकुनेः सौबलस्य च। तथा क्षुद्रस्य पापस्य भ्रातुर्दुःशासनस्य च॥
en: The son of Suta, a low born fellow, Shakuni, the son of Subala and your little minded vicious brother Dushasana.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: कर्ण उवाच नैवमायुष्मता वाच्यं यन्मामात्थ पितामह। क्षत्रधर्मे स्थितो ह्यस्मि स्वधर्मादनपेयिवान्॥
en: Karna said It is not proper for you, O grandfather, to say to me the words you have spoken. I observe the rules of the Kshatriya caste and am not fallen from my own virtue.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: किं चान्यन्मयि दुर्वृत्तं येन मां परिगर्हसे। न हि मे वृजिनं किंचिद् धार्तराष्ट्रा विदुः क्वचित्।।३०
en: What vice is there in one for which you revile me so; the son of Dhritarashtra knows that there is no sin in me.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: नाचरं वृजिनं किंचिद् धार्तराष्ट्रस्य नित्यशः। अहं हि पाण्डवान् सर्वान् हनिष्यामि रणेस्थितान्॥
en: I have never been without the slightest injury towards the son of Dhritarashtra and I shall kill all the sons of Pandu, engaged in battle.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: प्राग्विरुद्धैः शमं सद्धिः कथं वा क्रियते पुनः। राज्ञो हि धृतराष्ट्रस्य सर्वं कार्यं प्रियं मया। तथा दुर्योधनस्यापि स हि राज्ये समाहितः॥
en: How can these that are honest be reconciled with those that were formerly their enemies. The interest of king Dhritarashtra is ever looked after by me and the same of Duryodhana; he is now established in the kingdom.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच कर्णस्य तु वचः श्रुत्वा भीष्मः शान्तनवः पुनः। धृतराष्ट्रः महाराज सम्भाष्येदं वचोऽब्रवीत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Bhima, the son of Shantanu, having heard the words of Karna, again addressing the great king Dhritarashtra, said these words-

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: यदयं कत्थते नित्यं हन्ताहं पाण्डवानिति। नायं कलापि सम्पूर्णा पाण्डवानां महात्मनाम्॥
en: Though he ever says “I shall be the slayer of the son of Pandu", yet he is not even one sixteenth part of these large-hearted sons of Pandu.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: अनयो योऽयमागन्ता पुत्राणां ते दुरात्मनाम्। तदस्य कर्म जानीहि सूतपुत्रस्य दुर्मतेः॥
en: The great calamity, that is about to come on your sons of wicked souls, know that it is the work of this son of Suta of wicked mind.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: एतमाश्रित्य पुत्रस्ते मन्दबुद्धिः सुयोधनः। अवामन्यत तान् वीरान् देवपुत्रानरिंदमान्॥
en: Your son Suyodhana of weak intellect depending on him for support has insulted those heroic sons of godly men, the subduer of their foes.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: किं चाप्येतेन तत्कर्म कृतपूर्वं सुदुष्करम्। तैर्यथा पाण्डवैः सर्वैरेकैकेन कृतं पुरा॥
en: What difficult task of there that has before been accomplished by him which is equal to what has been done by each of the sons of Pandu in days gone by.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: दृष्ट्वा विराटनगरे भ्रातरं निहतं प्रियम्। धनंजयेन विक्रम्य किमनेन तदा कृतम्॥
en: Having seen in the city of Virata his dear brother killed by Dhananjaya who evinced a great deal of prowess, what did he do at that time.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: सहितान् हि कुरून् सर्वानभियातो धनंजयः। प्रमथ्य चाच्छिनद् वासः किमयं प्रोषितस्तदा॥
en: When Dhananjaya rushing against all the Kurus and smashing them dispossessed them of their clothes, what did he then do.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: गन्धर्वैर्घोषयात्रायां ह्रियते यत् सुतस्तव। क्व तदा सूतपुत्रोऽभूद् य इदानीं वृषायते॥
en: When your son was being taken as a captive towards the Ghoshayatra by the Gandharvas, where was then the son of Suta who is now roaring like a bull.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: ननु तत्रापि भीमेन पार्थेन च महात्मना। यमाभ्यामेव संगम्य गन्धर्वास्ते पराजिताः॥
en: Even in that case it was Bhima and the large minded Partha, who aided by the twins vanquished those Gandharvas.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: एतान्यस्य मृषोक्तानि बहूनि भरतर्षभ। विकत्थनस्य भद्रं ते सदा धर्मार्थलोपिनः॥
en: These are the many unfounded statements that he makes; for he is boastful and regards not either morality or worldly profit. May good betide you.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: भीष्मस्य तु वचः श्रुत्वा भारद्वाजो महामनाः। धृतराष्ट्रमुवाचेदं राजमध्येऽभिपूजयन्॥
en: The son of Bharadvaja of large mind having heard the words of Bhishma spoke thus to Dhritarashtra, among the assembled kings after duly saluting him.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: यदाह भरतश्रेष्ठो भीष्मस्तत् क्रियतां नृप। न काममर्थलिप्सूनां वचनं कर्तुमर्हसि॥
en: What the chief among the race of Bharata, Bhishma, has said-do that, O protector of men. It is not proper that you should do what they that covet desire and wealth tell you to do.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: पुरा युद्धात् साधु मन्ये पाण्डवैः सह संगतम्। यद् वाक्यमर्जुनेनोक्तं संजयेन निवेदितम्॥
en: Before the battle, I think that peace with the Pandavas seems to be the best. What has been prophesied by Arjuna and submitted to us by Sanjaya.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: सर्वं तदपि जानामि करिष्यति च पाण्डवः। न ह्यस्य त्रिषु लोकेषु सदृशोऽन्ति धनुर्धरः॥
en: Will all be done by the son of Pandu, I know. In the three worlds there is no wilder of the bow equal to him.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: अनादृत्य तु तद् वाक्यमर्थवद् द्रोणभीष्मयोः। ततः स संजयं राजा पर्यपृच्छत पाण्डवान्॥
en: Minding not however the speeches of Drona and Bhishma, which were good advice, the king asked Sanjaya about the sons of Pandu.

description: The speech of Arjuna, in the Yanasandhi
sn: तदैव कुरवः सर्वे निराशा जीवितेऽभवन्। भीष्मद्रोणौ यदा राजा न सम्यगनुभाषते॥
en: From that time did all the Kurus despair of their lives, when the king did not give a proper reply to the speeches of Bhishma and Drona.

description: The speech of Sanjaya, in the Yanasandhi
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच किमसौ पाण्डवौ राजा धर्मपुत्रोऽभ्यभाषत। श्रुत्वेह बहुला: सेनाः प्रीत्यर्थं नः समागताः॥
en: Dhritarashtra said What did the son of Dharma, the king of the Pandavas, say after hearing that several armies had collected here for our help.
