description: The speech of Sanjaya, in the Yanasandhi
sn: किमसौ चेष्टते सूत योत्स्यमानो युधिष्ठिरः। के वास्य भ्रातृपुत्राणां पश्यन्त्याज्ञेप्सवो मुखम्॥
en: What preparations are Yudhishthira, who is ready for war, making? Who among his sons and brothers are looking up to his face desirous of receiving his orders?

description: The speech of Sanjaya, in the Yanasandhi
sn: के स्विदेनं वारयन्ति युद्धाच्छाम्येति वा पुनः। निकृत्या कोपितं मन्दैर्धर्मज्ञं धर्मचारिणम्॥
en: Who among them again dissuades him from war, saying-“Be peaceful” him who knows the nature of virtue and who practices virtue and who has been moved to wrath by the wrong done by the wicked ones (my sons).

description: The speech of Sanjaya, in the Yanasandhi
sn: संजय उवाच राज्ञो मुखमुदीक्षन्ते पञ्चालाः पाण्डवै सह। युधिष्ठिरस्य भद्रं ते स सर्वाननुशास्ति च॥
en: Sanjaya said All the the Panchalas, along with the Pandavas, are looking up to the face of the king Yudhishthira and he, good betide you, rules over them all.

description: The speech of Sanjaya, in the Yanasandhi
sn: पृथग्भूताः पाण्डवानां पञ्चालानां रथव्रजाः। आयान्तमभिनन्दन्ति कुन्तीपुत्रं युधिष्ठिरम्॥
en: Hosts of cars belonging to the Panchalas are coming separately and inspire joy into the heart of Yudhishthira, the son of Kunti.

description: The speech of Sanjaya, in the Yanasandhi
sn: नभः सूर्यमिवोद्यन्तं कौन्तेयं दीप्ततेजसम्। पञ्चालाः प्रतिनन्दन्ति तेजोराशिमिवोदितम्॥
en: The Panchalas like a cluster of rays gladden the heart of the son of Kunti, who is of effulgent prowess, like the sun rising making the sky look cheerful.

description: The speech of Sanjaya, in the Yanasandhi
sn: आगोपालाविपालाश्च नन्दमाना युधिष्ठिरम्। पञ्चाला: केकया मत्स्याः प्रतिनन्दन्ति पाण्डवम्॥
en: Down to the very herdsmen who look after cattle and sheep, the tribes of Panchalas, Kaikeya and Matsyas gladden the heart of Yudhishthira, the Pandu king.

description: The speech of Sanjaya, in the Yanasandhi
sn: ब्राह्मण्यो राजपुत्र्यश्च विशां दुहितरश्च याः। क्रीडन्त्योऽभिसमायान्ति पार्थं संनद्धमीक्षितुम्॥
en: The daughters of Brahmanas and of chieftains and of the Vaishyas, while playing, come to Partha to see him clad in a coat of mail.

description: The speech of Sanjaya, in the Yanasandhi
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच संजयाचक्ष्व येनास्मान् पाण्डवा अभ्ययुञ्जत। धृष्टद्युम्नस्य सैन्येन सोमकानां बलेन च॥
en: Dhritarashtra said O Sanjaya, tell us about those with whose aid that Pandu king will high, viz., the army of Dhrishtadyumna and of the Somakas.

description: The speech of Sanjaya, in the Yanasandhi
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच गावल्गणिस्तु तत्पृष्टः सभायां कुरुसंसदि। निःश्वस्य सुभृशं दीर्घ मुहुः संचिन्तयन्निव॥
en: Vaishampayana said The son of Gavalgani, being thus questioned in that council of the assembly of Kurus and having drawn long sighs, again and again became thoughtful for a moment.

description: The speech of Sanjaya, in the Yanasandhi
sn: तत्रानिमित्ततो दैवात् सूतं कश्मलमाविशत्। तदाऽऽचचक्षे विदुरः सभायां राजसंसदि॥ संजयोऽयं महाराज मूर्च्छितः पतितो भुवि। वाचं न सृजते कांचिद्धीनप्रज्ञोऽल्पचेतनः॥
en: Without any reason, as if by the hand of the gods, the Suta suddenly fell down. Then in that assembly of kings, in that council chamber, Vidura said loudly-This Sanjaya, O great king, has fallen down senseless; and he cannot utter one word bereft of his wisdom.

description: The speech of Sanjaya, in the Yanasandhi
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच अपश्यत् संजयो नूनं कुन्तीपुत्रान् महारथान्। तैरस्य पुरुषव्याघे शमुद्वेजितं मनः॥
en: Dhritarashtra said Sanjaya, seeing these mighty car-warriors, the sons of Kunti, has certainly got his mind excited owing to those tigers among men.

description: The speech of Sanjaya, in the Yanasandhi
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच संजयश्चेतनां लब्ध्वा प्रत्याश्वस्येदमब्रवीत्। धृतराष्ट्र महाराज सभायां कुरुसंसदि॥
en: Vaishampayana said Sanjaya having regained consciousness and being comforted addressed these words to the great king, Dhritarashtra, amidst that assemblage of Kurus in that hall.

description: The speech of Sanjaya, in the Yanasandhi
sn: संजय उवाच दृष्टवानस्मि राजेन्द्र कुन्तीपुत्रान् महारथान्। मत्स्यराजगृहावासनिरोधेनावकर्शितान्॥
en: Sanjaya said I have seen, O chief among kings, those mighty car-warriors, the sons of Kunti, grown lean through the restraint in which they lived in the court of the Matsya king.

description: The speech of Sanjaya, in the Yanasandhi
sn: शृणु यैर्हि महाराज पाण्डवा अभ्ययुञ्जत। धृष्टद्युम्नेन वीरेण युद्धे वस्तेऽब्ययुञ्जत॥
en: Hear, O great king, aided by whom the Pandavas will fight. There will he fight between yourselves and them, aided by the hero Dhrishtadyumna.

description: The speech of Sanjaya, in the Yanasandhi
sn: यो नैव रोषान्न भयान्न लोभान्नार्थकारणात्। न हेतुवादाद् धर्मात्मा सत्यं जह्यात् कदाचन॥
en: That man of virtuous soul who, through wealth and fear, avarice or wealth or for the sake of argument never falls from truth.

description: The speech of Sanjaya, in the Yanasandhi
sn: यः प्रमाणं महाराज धर्मं धर्मभृतां वरः। अजातशत्रुणा तेन पाण्डवा अभ्ययुञ्जत॥
en: Who is an authority, O great king, in religious matters and who is the chief among men attached to virtue, who has created no enemies, aided by him the Pandavas will fight with you.

description: The speech of Sanjaya, in the Yanasandhi
sn: यस्य बाहुबले तुल्यः पृथिव्यां नास्ति कश्चन। यो वै सर्वान् महीपालान् वशे चक्रे धनुर्धरः। यः काशीनङ्गमगधान् कलिङ्गाश्च युधाऽजयत्॥
en: Whose equal in strength of arms there is none in those world; that wielder of the bow who subdued all protectors of the earth and who subjugated in battle the people of Kashi, Anga and Magadha and also the Kalingas.

description: The speech of Sanjaya, in the Yanasandhi
sn: तेन वो भीमसेनेन पाण्डवा अभ्ययुञ्जत। यस्य वीर्येण सहसा चत्वारो भुवि पाण्डवाः॥
en: With that Bhimasena the Pandavas will fight with you; and through whose prowess the four Pandavas came down.

description: The speech of Sanjaya, in the Yanasandhi
sn: निःसृत्य जतुगेहाद् वै हिडिम्बात् पुरुषादकात्। यश्चैषामभवद् द्वीपः कुन्तीपुत्रो वृकोदरः॥
en: After issuing from the house of lac, Vrikodara, the son of Kunti, who became the means of their rescue from Hidimba, the man eater.

description: The speech of Sanjaya, in the Yanasandhi
sn: याज्ञसेनीमथो यत्र सिन्धुराजोऽपकृष्टवान्। तत्रैषामभवद् द्वीपः कुन्तीपुत्रो वृकोदरः॥
en: That son of Kunti, Vrikodara, who became the means of rescue at the time when Sindhuraja was gratifying his lust on the daughter of Yajnasena.

description: The speech of Sanjaya, in the Yanasandhi
sn: यश्च तान् संगतान् सर्वान् पाण्डवान् वारणावते। दह्यतो मोचयामास तेन वस्तेऽभ्ययुञ्जत॥
en: Aided by him who liberated all the assembled Pandavas when they were burning at the conflagration of Varanavata they will fight against you.

description: The speech of Sanjaya, in the Yanasandhi
sn: कृष्णायां चरता प्रीतिं येन क्रोधवशा हताः। प्रविश्य विषमं घोरं पर्वतं गन्धमादनम्॥
en: Aided by him whom to gratify Krishna (Draupadi) killed the the Krodhavasas after penetrating into the terrific mountain Gandhamadana.

description: The speech of Sanjaya, in the Yanasandhi
sn: यस्य नागायुतैर्वीर्यं भुजयोः सारमर्पितम्। तेन वो भीमसेनेन पाण्डवा अभ्ययुञ्जत॥
en: By him whose substantial arms the strength of ten thousands has been given by the aid of such Brahmana will the Pandavas fight with you.

description: The speech of Sanjaya, in the Yanasandhi
sn: कृष्णाद्वितीयो विक्रम्य तुष्ट्यर्थं जातवेदसः। अजयद् य: पुरा वीरो युध्यमानं पुरंदरम्॥
en: That hero who, in days of old, for the satisfaction of the god of fire, aided by Krishna, conquered Purandara (Indra) fighting.

description: The speech of Sanjaya, in the Yanasandhi
sn: यः स साक्षान्महादेवं गिरिशं शूलपाणिनम्। तोषयामास युद्धेन देवदेवमुमापतिम्॥
en: He who passed by his fight that god among gods, the lord of Uma-that Mahadeva himself, with the trident in his hand, that lord of the mountains.

description: The speech of Sanjaya, in the Yanasandhi
sn: यश्च सर्वान् वशे चक्रे लोकपालान् धनुर्धरः। तेन वो विजयेनाजौ पाण्डवा अभ्ययुञ्जत।॥
en: That wielder of the bow, who subjugated all the rulers of the earth by the aid of that Vijaya will the Pandavas fight.

description: The speech of Sanjaya, in the Yanasandhi
sn: यः प्रतीची दिशं चक्रे वशे म्लेच्छगणायुताम्। स तत्र नकुलो योद्धा चित्रयोधी व्यवस्थितः॥
en: He, who subjugated the western country inhabited by hordes of Mlecchas, that warrior Nakula of wonderful weapons is present in their camp.

description: The speech of Sanjaya, in the Yanasandhi
sn: तेन वो दर्शनीयेन वीरेणातिधनुर्भूता। माद्रीपुत्रेण कौरव्य पाण्डवा अभ्ययुञ्जत॥ यः काशीनङ्गमगधान् कलिङ्गांश्च युधाजयत्। तेन वः सहदेवेन पाण्डवा अभ्ययुञ्जत॥
en: With that beautiful hero, that excellent wielder of your bow, the son of Madri, O Kurus, will the sons of Pandu fight. With that Sahadeva, who conquired the kings of Kashi, Anga, Magadha and Kalinga in bettle, will the sons of Pandu fight.

description: The speech of Sanjaya, in the Yanasandhi
sn: यस्य वीर्येण सदृशाश्चत्वारो भुवि मानवाः। अश्वत्थामा धृष्टकेतू रुक्मी प्रद्युम्न एव च॥ तेन वः सहदेवेन युद्धं राजन् महात्ययम्। यवीयसा नृवीरेण माद्रीनन्दिकरेण च॥
en: He whose might is equaled by only four men in this world, Ashvathaman, Dhrishtaketu, Rukmi and Pradyumna; with that Sahadeva, with that hero among men and with that joygiver to Madri, O king, will you have a great fight.

description: The speech of Sanjaya, in the Yanasandhi
sn: तपश्चचार या घोरं काशिकन्या पुरा सती। भीष्मस्य वधमिच्छन्ती प्रेत्यापि भरतर्षभ॥ पाञ्चालस्य सुता जज्ञे दैवाच्च स पुनः पुमान्। स्त्रीपुंसोः पुरुषव्याघ्र यः स वेद गुणागुणान्॥
en: The chaste woman, the daughter of the king of Kashi, who practiced austere asceticism, who was desirous of the destruction of Bhishma even after death (i.e. in another birth) O bull of the race of Bharata, was born as the daughter of the king of Panchala and by the hand of the gods she became a male afterwards; that one, O tiger among men, who knows the virtues and vices of female-males.

description: The speech of Sanjaya, in the Yanasandhi
sn: यः कलिङ्गान् समापेदे पाञ्चाल्यो युद्धदुर्मदः। शिखण्डिना वः कुरवः कृतास्त्रेणाभ्ययुञ्जत॥
en: Who fought with the Kalingas, that prince of Panchala; hard to vanquish in battle with that Shikhandin skillful in the use of weapons will they fight with you, the Kurus.

description: The speech of Sanjaya, in the Yanasandhi
sn: यं यक्षः पुरुषं चक्रे भीष्मस्य निधनेच्छया। महेष्वासेन रौद्रेण पाण्डवा अभ्ययुञ्जत॥
en: She who was turned into a male through a desire for the death of Bhishma, with that terrific bowman will the Pandavas fight.

description: The speech of Sanjaya, in the Yanasandhi
sn: महेष्वासा राजपुत्रा भ्रातरः पञ्च केकयाः। आमुक्तकवचाः शूरास्तैश्च वस्तेऽभ्ययुञ्जत॥
en: With those five Kaikeya princes, brothers to one another and mighty bowmen, with these heroes; with the coats of arms on will they fight with you.

description: The speech of Sanjaya, in the Yanasandhi
sn: यो दीर्घबाहुः क्षिप्रास्त्रो धृतिमान् सत्यविक्रमः। तेन वो वृष्णिवीरेण युयुधानेन संगरः॥
en: With that heroe among the race of the Vrishnis, of long arms, of great activity in the use of weapons, possessed of true strength, with that Suyodhana will you have to fight.

description: The speech of Sanjaya, in the Yanasandhi
sn: य आसीच्छरणं काले पाण्डवानां महात्मनाम्। रणे तेन विराटेन भविता वः समागमः॥
en: He who has been the protector of the greatsouled Pandavas for a time, with that Virata will you meet in battle.

description: The speech of Sanjaya, in the Yanasandhi
sn: यः स काशिपती राजा वाराणस्यां महारथः। स तेषामभवद् योद्धा तेन वस्तेऽभ्ययुञ्जत॥
en: He who is the Lord of Kashi, the carwarrior who is the king of Varanasi, has become their warrior, with him they will fight with you.

description: The speech of Sanjaya, in the Yanasandhi
sn: शिशुभिर्दुर्जयैः संख्ये द्रौपदेयैर्महात्मभिः। आशीविषसमस्पर्शः पाण्डवा अभ्ययुञ्जत॥
en: With the children hard to vanquish, the sons of Draupadi of noble souls, who are like snakes, will the Pandavas fight.

description: The speech of Sanjaya, in the Yanasandhi
sn: यः कृष्णसदृशो वीर्ये युधिष्ठिरसमो दमे। तेनाभिमन्युना संख्ये पाण्डवा अभ्ययुञ्जत॥
en: He who is like Krishna in strength and like Yudhishthira in self-control, with that Abhimanyu will the Pandavas fight.

description: The speech of Sanjaya, in the Yanasandhi
sn: यश्चैवाप्रतिमो वीर्ये धृष्टकेतुर्महायशाः। दुःसहः समरे क्रुद्धः शैशुपालिमहारथः॥ तेन वश्चेदिराजन पाण्डवा अभ्ययुञ्जत। अक्षौहिण्या परिवृतः पाण्डवान् योऽभिसंश्रितः॥
en: Dhrishtaketu of great fame, who is of unparalleled strength, who wrathful in battle is hard to vanquish, that son of Shishupala, a great car-warrior, with him, the king of the Chedis who has come and joined the Pandavas with an Akshauhini, will the Pandavas fight.

description: The speech of Sanjaya, in the Yanasandhi
sn: यः संश्रयः पाण्डवानां देवानामिव वासवः। तेन वो वासुदेवेन पाण्डवा अभ्ययुञ्जत॥
en: He who is the refuge of the Pandavas as Vasava is of the gods, with that Vamdeva will the Pandavas fight.

description: The speech of Sanjaya, in the Yanasandhi
sn: तथा चेदिपतेर्धाता शरभो भरतर्षभ। करकर्षेण सहितस्ताभ्यां वस्तेऽभ्ययुञ्जत॥
en: So also will the brother of the king of the Chedis, Sharabha, O bull of the race of Bharata who is accompanied by Karakarsha with these two will the Pandavas fight.

description: The speech of Sanjaya, in the Yanasandhi
sn: जारासंधिः सहदेवो जयत्सेनश्च तावुभौ। युद्धेऽप्रतिस्थौ वीरौ पाण्डवार्थं व्यवस्थितौ॥
en: The son of Jarasandha, Sahadeva and Jayatsena, both of whom are unrivaled heroes in battle, are present in the cause of the Pandavas.

description: The speech of Sanjaya, in the Yanasandhi
sn: द्रुपदश्च महातेजा बलेन महता वृतः। त्यक्तात्मा पाण्डवार्थाय योत्स्यमानो व्यवस्थितः॥
en: Drupada too of great prowess and surrounded by a large force has sacrificed his interests for the Pandava's cause and desirous of fighting is present.

description: The speech of Sanjaya, in the Yanasandhi
sn: एते चान्ये च बहवः प्राच्योदीच्या महीक्षितः। शतशो यानुपाश्रित्य धर्मराजो व्यवस्थितः॥
en: These and many others come from the countries in the east and the north depending on hundreds of them the king Dharma is prepared for battle.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच सर्व एते महोत्साहा ये त्वया परिकीर्तिताः। एकतस्त्वेव ते सर्वे समेता भीम एकतः॥
en: Dhritarashtra said All these who have been enumerated by you are of great energy and courage; but Bhima alone is equal to all of them combined.

sn: भीमसेनाद्धि मे भूयो भयं संजायते महत्। क्रुद्धादमर्षणात् तात व्याघ्रादिव महारुरोः॥
en: From Bhimasena wrathful I have very great fear like that of a large deer from an enraged tiger.

sn: जागर्मि रात्रयः सर्वा दीर्घमुष्णं च निःश्वसन्। भीतो वृकोदरात् तात सिंहात् पशुरिवापरः॥
en: I am awake during entire nights breathing large and hot sighs, being afraid of Vrikodara, O dear, as any other animal fears a lion.

sn: न हि तस्य महाबाहोः शक्रप्रतिमतेजसः। सैन्येऽस्मिन् प्रतिपश्यामि य एनं विषहेद् युधि॥
en: In this entire army do I not see one who can withstand in battle this one of long arms and having strength like that of Shakra.

sn: अमर्षणश्च कौन्तेयो दृढवैरच पाण्डवः। अनर्महासी सोन्मादस्तिर्यकप्रेक्षी महास्वनः॥
en: That son of Kunti and Pandu when wrathful is an implacable enemy; and he smiles not even in jest and is mad with rage, looks at things askance and is of loud voice,

sn: महावेगो महोत्साहो महाबाहुर्महाबलः। मन्दानां मम पुत्राणां युद्धेनान्तं करिष्यति॥
en: Possessed of great force and of great energy, possessed of long arms and of great strength will put an end to the existence of any wicked sons in battle.

sn: ऊरुचाहगृहीतानां गदां बिभ्रद् वृकोदरः। कुरूणामृषभो युद्धो दण्डपाणिरिवान्तकः॥
en: Vrikodara, that bull in the race of Kuru, wielding the mace slay them struck by a heavy calamity in battle like the god of death with his staff in his hand.

sn: अष्टानिमायसी घोरां गदां काञ्चनभूषणाम्। मनसाऽहं प्रपश्यामि ब्रह्मदण्डमिवोद्यतम्॥
en: That terrible steel mace with eight sides and ornamented with gold I now see in my mind like the staff of Brahma uplifted.

sn: यथा मृगाणां यूथेषु सिंहो जातबलश्चरेत्। मामकेषु तथा भीमो बलेषु विचरिष्यति॥
en: As a fully grown up lion roams among a hear of deer, so Bhima roam among my army.

sn: सर्वेषां मम पुत्राणां स एकः क्रूरविक्रमः। बह्वाशी विप्रतीपश्च बाल्येऽपि रभसः सदा॥
en: Towards all my sons he alone (of all his brothers) showed his cruel strength. A voracious eater and endued with great strength, even in his childhood was he inimical (to my sons).

sn: उद्वेपते मे हृदयं ये मे दुर्योधनादयः। बाल्येऽपि तेन युध्यन्तो वारणेनेव मर्दिताः॥
en: My heart quakes that Duryodhana and other sons of mine even when fighting with him in their childhood were smashed as by elephants.

sn: तस्य वीर्येण संक्लिष्टा नित्यमेव सुता मम। स एव हेतुर्भेदस्य भीमो भीमपराक्रमः॥
en: O pressed by his strength my sons have ever been; and that Bhima of terrible prowess is the cause of this rupture.

sn: ग्रसमानमनीकानि नरवारणवाजिनाम्। पश्यामीवाग्रतो भीमं क्रोधमूर्च्छितमाहवे॥
en: Devouring my army composed of men, elephants and horses, do I see Bhima in the front senseless with wrath,

sn: अस्त्रे द्रोणार्जुनसमं वायुवेगसमं जवे। महेश्वरसमं क्रोधे को हन्याद् भीममाहवे॥
en: In arms equal of Drona and Arjuna and in speed having the force of wind, in wrath equal to Maheshvara himself, who will kill Bhima in battle.

sn: संजयाचक्ष्व मे शूरं भीमसेनममर्षणम्। अतिलाभं तु मन्येऽहं यत् तेन रिपुघातिना॥
en: O Sanjaya, that hero, the wrathful Bhimasena; tell me that; it is a great gain I consider, that by that slayer of enemies.

sn: सर्वे येन भीमबला यक्षा राक्षसाश्च पुरा हताः॥
en: My sons were not all killed by that one of independent mind by whom Yakshas of terrible strength and the Rakshasas were killed in days of old.

sn: कथं तस्य रणे वेगं मानुषः प्रसहिष्यति। न स जातु वशे तस्थौ मम बाल्येऽपि संजय॥
en: How can a man withstand the force of him in battle. He was not under my control even in his childhood, O Sanjaya.

sn: किं पुनर्मम दुष्पुत्रैः क्लिष्टः सम्प्रति पाण्डवः। निष्ठुरो रोषणोऽत्यर्थं भज्येतापि न संनमेत्। तदैव न हताः पुत्रा मम मनस्विना। तिर्यक्प्रेक्षी संहतभूः कथं शाम्येद् वृकोदरः॥
en: How can that son of Pandu do so now having been wronged by my wicked sons. Cruel and wrathful, he could not bend even when broken. Looking at things ask once, with his eyebrows contracted how can Vrikodara be peaceful.

sn: शूरस्तथाप्रतिबलो गौरस्ताल इवोन्नतः। प्रमाणतो भीसेनः प्रादेशेनाधिकोऽर्जुनात्॥
en: A hero of exceedingly white complexion and tall like the palm tree, Bhimasena measures a Prasesha (the span of a thumb) more than Arjuna.

sn: जवेन वाजिनोऽत्येति बलेनात्येति कुञ्चरान्। अव्यक्तजपी मध्वक्षो मध्यमः पाण्डवो बली॥
en: Surpassing in speed the horses, in strength the elephants, the second son of Pandu who is of great strength has sweet eyes.

sn: इति बाल्ये श्रुतः पूर्वं मया व्यासमुखात् पुरा। रूपतो वीर्यतश्चैव याथातथ्येन पाण्डवः॥
en: The Pandava in form and power just as I heard from the lips of Vyasa in days gone by.

sn: आयसेन स दण्डेन रथान् नागान् नरान् हयान्। हनिष्यति रणे क्रुद्धो रौद्रः क्रूरपराक्रमः॥
en: Easily by means of his mace, the chariots, the elephants, men and horses he will kill in battle, that terrible being when wrathful, that man of cruel purposes.

sn: अमर्षी नित्यसंरब्धो भीमः प्रहरतां वरः। मया तात प्रतीपानि कुर्वन् पूर्वं विमानितः॥
en: That wrathful Bhima, who is ever furiousthat chief among the smiters has by acting against my wishes, O dear, before been insulted by me.

sn: निष्कर्णामायसी स्थूलां सुपार्छा काञ्चनीं गदाम्। शतघ्नीं शतनिर्हादां कथं शक्ष्यन्ति मे सुताः॥
en: That mace which has no curves, which is made of steel, which is of bulk, of beautiful sides, adorned with gold, which is capable of killing a hundred and when flung producing a terrible sound-how will my sons bears?

sn: अपारमप्लवागाधं समुद्रं शरवेधिनम्। भीमसेनमयं दुर्गं तात मन्दास्तितीर्षवः॥
en: That inaccessible ocean, which has no shore, which is unfathomable and which has currents in the shape of Bhima, those wicked ones are desirous of crossing over.

sn: क्रोशतो मे न शृण्वन्ति बालाः पण्डितमानिनः। विषमं न हि मन्यन्ते प्रपातं मधुदर्शिनः॥
en: Those children thinking themselves to be wise do not listen to my words, even if I cry out. Seeing the honey (formerly collected on mountain tops) they do not care for the heavy fall.

sn: संयुगं ये गमिष्यन्ति नररूपेण मृत्युना। नियतं चोदिता धात्रा सिंहेनेव महामृगाः॥
en: Those who encounter in battle that death in human shape have their dooms settled by the father of the universe, like those of large deer encountering lions,

sn: शैक्यां तात चतुष्किष्कुं षडस्रिममितौजसम्। प्रहितां दुःखसंस्पर्शी कथं शक्ष्यन्ति मे सुताः॥
en: How shall my sons bear, Odear, the mace when flung at them the mace which is four cubits long, having six sides of illimitable powers of destruction and terrible to touch.

sn: कदां भ्रामयतस्तस्य भिन्दतो हस्तिमस्तकान्। सृक्किणी लेलिहानस्य वाष्यमुत्सृजतो मुहुः॥ उद्दिश्य नागान् पततः कुर्वतो भैरवान् रवान्। प्रतीपं पततो मत्तान् कुञ्जरान् प्रतिगर्जतः॥ विगाह्य रथमार्गेषु वरानुद्दिश्य निघ्नतः। अग्नेः प्रज्वलितस्येव अपि मुच्येत मे प्रजा॥
en: Whirling the mace and piercing the heads of elephants, licking the corners of his lips and giving out (terrific) breaths every moment, making terrific noises in return of those of falling elephants and rushing with loud roars against elephants coming against him, having penetrated into the place where the chariots stand, when he kills the heroes after taking aim against them, will one of my soldiers escape from him who is blazing like fire?

sn: वीथीं कुर्वन् महाबाहुर्द्रावयन् मम वाहिनीम्। नृत्यन्निव गदापाणिर्युगान्तं दर्शयिष्यति॥
en: Grinding the four elements of my army and cutting his passage out through it, as if dancing with the mace in his hand, he will show (to people) the scene which takes place at the end of a Yuga (universal destruction).

sn: प्रभिन्न इव मातङ्गः प्रभञ्जन् पुष्पितान् द्रमान्। प्रवेक्ष्यति रणे सेनां पुत्राणां मे वृकोदरः॥
en: Like an elephant mad with rage, breaking trees with flowers, Vrikodara will crush the army of my sons of battle.

sn: कुर्वन् रथान् विपुरुषान् विसारथिहयध्वजान्। आरुजन् पुरुषव्याघ्रो रथिनः सादिनस्तथा॥ गङ्गावेग इवानूपांस्तीरजान् विविधान् दुमान्। प्रभक्षयति रणे सेनां पुत्राणां मम संजय॥
en: Rendering the chariots devoid of men, drivers, horse and banners and giving trouble to the warriors fighting from cars and elephants, the tiger among men, like the force of the currents of the Ganga uprooting various sorts of trees, will vanquish in battle the army of my sons, O Sanjaya.

sn: दिशो नूनं गमिष्यन्ति भीमसेनभयार्दिताः। मम पुत्राञ्च भृत्याश्च राजानश्चैव संजय॥
en: My with their servants and subordinate chiefs, O Sanjaya, troubled with the fear of Bhimasena will certainly fly in different directions.

sn: येन राजा महावीर्यः प्रविश्यान्तःपुरं पुरा। वासुदेवसहायेन जरासंधो निपातितः॥
en: (That Bhimasena) by whom, aided by the son of Vasudeva, the king Jarasandha of great prowess was killed after his inner apartments being entered in the days of old.

sn: कृत्स्नेयं पृथिवी देवी जरासंधेन धीमता। मागधेन्द्रेण बलिना वशे कृत्वा प्रतापिताः॥
en: The goddess Earth was brought under control by the wise Jarasandha and that mighty Lord of Magadha, who subjugated her and oppressed her people.

sn: भीष्मप्रतापात् कुरवो नयेनान्धकवृष्णयः। यन्न तस्य वशे जग्मुः केवलं दैवमेव तत्॥
en: That the Kurus through the prowess of Bhima and the Andhakas and the Vrishnis and sons through their diplomacy, were not brought under subjection by them, which was only due to the gods.

sn: स गत्वा पाण्डुपुत्रेण तरसा बाहुशालिना। अनायुधेन वीरेण निहतः किं ततोऽधिकम्॥
en: The son of Pandu, the heroic of long arms, having approached him without any arms, killed him. What can be more (wonderful) than this?

sn: दीर्घकालसमासक्तं विषमाशीविषो यथा। स मोक्ष्यति रणे तेजः पुत्रेषु मम संजय॥
en: Like venomous snake having accumulated its poison for a long time, he (Bhima) will fling his strength on my sons in the field of battle, O Sanjaya.

sn: महेन्द्र इव वज्रेण दानवान् देवसत्तमः। भीमसेनो गदापाणिः सूदयिष्यति मे सुतान्॥
en: Like that chief among the gods, great Indra with his thunderbolt (killing) the Danavas, Bhimasena with mace in his hand will kill my a sons.

sn: अविषह्यमनावार्य तीव्रवेगपराक्रमम्। पश्यामीवातिताम्राक्षमापतन्तं वृकोदरम्॥
en: I see (in my mind) Vrikodara having eyes of the colour of copper, incapable of being opposed or prevented and having fearful force of strength falling on (my sons).

sn: अगदस्याप्यधनुषो विरथस्य विवर्मणः। बाहुभ्यां युद्ध्यमानस्य कस्तिष्ठेग्रतः पुमान्॥
en: Who can stay in front of that man fighting with his two arms without mace or bow and without being on his car.

sn: भीष्मो द्रोणश्च विप्रोऽयं कृपः शारद्वतस्तथा। जानन्त्येते यथैवाहं वीर्यज्ञस्तस्य धीमतः॥
en: Bhishma, this regenerate Drona, Kripa and also the son of Shardavata-all these know as much as I do the prowess of that wise one.

sn: आर्यव्रतं तु जानन्तः संगरान्तं विधित्सवः। सेनामुखेषु स्थास्यन्ति मामकानां नरर्षभाः॥
en: Conversant with the habits of life of the virtuous and desirous of death in battle, those bulls among men in our party will stand in front of the army.

sn: बलीयः सर्वतो दिष्ठं पुरुषस्य विशेषतः। पश्यन्नपि जयं तेषां न नियच्छामि यत् सुतान्॥
en: Destiny is always powerful specially in a man through I see them (the Pandavas) victorious, yet I do not dissuade my sons.

sn: ते पुराणं महेष्वासा मार्गमैन्द्रं समास्थिताः। त्यक्ष्यन्ति तुमुले प्राणान् रक्षन्तः पार्थिवं यशः॥
en: They (the warriors of our party), desirous of going along the eternal, noble and heavenly path, will part with their lives in fierce battle thus keeping your earthly fame unsullied.

sn: यथैषां मामकास्तात तथैषां पाण्डवा अपि। पौत्रा भीष्मस्य शिष्याश्च द्रोणस्य च कृपस्य च॥
en: As these are, O dear, to my sons, so are they to the Pandavas (in ties of blood and affection). They (the Pandavas) are grandsons of Bhishma and disciples of Drona and Kripa.

sn: यदस्मदाश्रयं किंचिद् दत्तमिष्टं च संजय। तस्यापचितिमार्यत्वात् कर्तारः स्थविरास्त्रयः॥
en: The protection that we have afforded to the three-aged ones, the little we have given them and the little good we have done to them, they will compensate us for that in return owing to their noble nature.

sn: आददानस्य शस्त्रं हि क्षत्रधर्मं परीप्सतः। निधनं क्षत्रियस्याजौ वरमेवाहुरुत्तमम्॥
en: That death of a Kshatriya is said to be a peaceful and commendable one, which is met with in battle when one takes up arms desirous of observing Kshatriya practices.

sn: स वै शोचामि सर्वान् वै ये युयुत्सन्ति पाण्डवैः। विक्रुष्टं विदुरेणादौ तदेतद् भयमागतम्॥
en: I grieve however for all those who will fight with the son of Pandu; the calamity prophesied by Vidura is now come.

sn: न तु मन्ये विघाताय ज्ञानं दुःखस्य संजय। भवत्यतिबलं ह्येतज्ज्ञानस्याप्युपघातकम्॥
en: I consider, O Sanjaya, that knowledge cannot destroy woe; in fact, it is excessive distress that kills knowledge.

sn: ऋषयो ह्यपि निर्मुक्ताः पश्यन्तो लोकसंग्रहान्। सुखैर्भवन्ति सुखिनस्तथा दुःखेन दुःखिताः॥
en: Even the Rishis who are emancipated and who merely look on this crowd of men become happy at prosperity and aggrieved at adversity.

sn: किं पुनर्मोहमासक्तस्तत्र तत्र सहस्रधा। पुत्रेषु राज्यदारेषु पौत्रेष्वपि च बन्धुषु॥
en: Why then should I not be affected by grief. When I ain attached to my sons, my kingdom, my wife, my grandsons, my friends and a thousand other objects.

sn: संशये तु महत्यस्मिन् किं नु मे क्षममुत्तरम्। विनाशं ह्येव पश्यामि कुरूणामनुचिन्यन्॥
en: I have grave doubts that I shall have any prosperity in the future; thinking thus I see (in my mind) the destruction of the Kurus.

sn: द्यूतप्रमुखमाभाति कुरूणां व्यसनं महत्। मन्देनैश्चर्यकामेन लोभात् पापमिदं कृतम्॥
en: The great calamity of the Kurus beginning with the game at dice now stands out in bold relief; this wicked act has been done by that fool desiring for prosperity out of avarice.

sn: मन्ये पर्यायधर्मोऽयं कालस्यात्यन्तगामिनः। चक्रे प्रधिरिवासक्तो नास्य शक्यं पलायितुम्॥
en: I consider this to be the work of Eternal Time. I am not able to fly from it like the iron ring attached to the wheel.

sn: किनुं कुर्यां कथं कुर्यां क्व नु गच्छामि संजय। एते नश्यन्ति कुरवो मन्दाः कालवशं गताः॥
en: What shall I do? how shall I do it and where shall I go, O Sanjaya? These foolish Kurus will be destroyed being subject to the effects of time.

sn: अवशोऽहं तदा तात पुत्राणां निहते शते। श्रोष्यामि निनदं स्त्रीणां कथं मां मरणं स्पृशेत्॥
en: I shall be helpless, O dear, on my hundred sons being killed and shall hear the loud lamentation of women. How shall death touch me?

sn: यथा निदाघे ज्वलनः समिद्धो दहेत् कक्षं वायुना चोद्यमानः। गदाहस्तः पाण्डवो वै तथैव हन्ता मदीयान् सहितोऽर्जुनेन॥
en: As in the hot season a fire ignited and urged by wind burns up dry grass, so will the son of Pandu, having mace in hand along with Arjuna, be the slayer of my party.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच यस्य वै नानृता वाचः कदाचिदनुशुश्रुम। त्रैलोक्यमपि तस्य स्याद् योद्धा यस्य धनंजयः॥
en: Dhritarashtra said He, from whom we have never heard an untruthful word, he who has Dhananjaya to fight for him can possess himself the three worlds.

sn: तस्यैव च न पश्यामि युधि गाण्डीवधन्वनः। अनिशं चिन्तयानोऽपि यः प्रतीयाद् रथेन तम्॥
en: I do not see any one equal in battle to the one who has the Gandiva bow, who seated on a car could oppose him, though I think about it day and night.

sn: अस्यत: कर्णिनालीकान् मार्गणआन् हृदयच्छिदः। प्रत्येता न समः कश्चिद् युधि गाण्डीवधन्वनः॥
en: There is no equal in battle of the wielder of the Gandiva bow shooting winged arrows, Nalikas (muskets) and arrows penetrating into the heart.

sn: द्रोणकर्णी प्रतीयातां यदि वीरौ नरर्षभौ। कृतास्त्रौ बलिनां श्रेष्ठौ समरेष्वपराजितौ॥
en: If the two heroes, these bulls among men, Drona and Karna, skillful in the use of weapons, the chief among those having strength and unconquerable in battle, oppose him?

sn: महान् स्यात् संशयो लोके न त्वस्ति विजयो मम। घृणी कर्णः प्रमादी च आचार्याः स्थविरो गुरुः॥
en: There may be great doubts among other men, but (I am afraid) victory will not be mine. Karna is careless and compassionate and the preceptor is old in age and is beside the preceptor (of the Pandavas).

sn: बलवान् पार्थो समर्थो दृढधन्वा जितक्लमः। भवेत् सुतमुलं युद्धं सर्वशोऽप्यपराजयः॥
en: Partha of firm grasp on the bow however is able, mighty and has conquered fatigue; there will be terrible fight between them, but both sides will remain undefeated.

sn: सर्वे शस्त्रविदः शूराः सर्वे प्राप्ता महद् यशः। अपि सर्वामरैश्वव्यं त्यजेयुर्न पुनर्जयम्॥
en: All of these are heroes knowing the use of weapons and all of them have gained great fame, they may forego even the lordship over all the gods but not victory (in this battle).

sn: वधे नूनं भवेच्छान्तिस्तयोर्वा फाल्गुनस्य च। न तु हन्तार्जुनस्यास्ति जेता चास्य न विद्यते॥
en: The two (Drona and Karna) or the son of Falguna being killed, there will certainly be peace; but there is none who can kill Arjuna, nor one who can conquer him.

sn: मन्युस्तस्य कथं शाम्येन्मन्दान् प्रति य उत्थितः। अन्येऽप्यस्त्राणि जानन्ति जीयन्ते च जयन्ति च॥
en: How can his wrath that has arisen, against those foolish ones be pacified; there are others knowing the use of weapons, who conquer (others) and (sometimes) are conquered (by those).

sn: एकान्तविजयस्त्वेव श्रूयते फाल्गुनस्य ह। त्रयस्त्रिंशत् समाहूय खाण्डवेऽग्निमतर्पयत्॥
en: But the rumour is that Falguna (when fighting) has but one result-victory; thirty three years ago (he) having invited the god of fire gratified him.

sn: जिगाय च सुरान् सर्वान् नास्य विद्मः पराजयम्। यस्य यन्ता हृषीकेशः शीलवृत्तसमो युधि॥
en: Having first vanquished the gods; no man ever heard of his defeat anywhere. He who has for his charioteer in battle Hrishikesha is equal to him in character.

sn: ध्रुवस्तस्य जयस्तात यथेन्द्रस्य जयस्तथा। कृष्णावेकरथे यत्तावधिज्यं गाण्डिवं धनुः॥
en: He has victory certain 0 dear, as the victory of Indra. The two Krishna's on one car and the stringed Gandiva bow.

sn: युगपत् त्रीणि तेजांसि समेतान्यनुशुश्रुभ। नैवास्ति नो धनुस्तादृक् न योद्धा न च सारथिः॥
en: These there forces have come together, I hear; there is no similar bow, nor a warrior of that stamp, nor a charioteer of that character.

sn: तच्च मन्दा न जानन्ति दुर्योधनवशानुगाः। शेषयेदशनिर्दीप्तो विपतन् मूर्ध्नि संजय॥
en: Those fools under the control of Duryodhana do not know this. The thunderbolt falling on the head ablaze leaves some remnants undestroyed, O Sanjaya.

sn: न तु शेषं शरास्तात कुर्युरस्ताः किरीटिना। अपि चास्यन्निवाभाति निघ्नन्निव धनंजयः॥
en: But the shafts shot by Kritin leaves no remnant, O dear. I see now (in my mind) Dhananjaya shining forth by working havoc.

sn: उद्धरन्निव कायेभ्यः शिरांसि शरवृष्टिभिः। अपि बाणमयं तेजः प्रदीप्तमिव सर्वतः॥
en: And by his shower of arrows separating heads from the bodies. (I see) also his strength in the shape of arrows blazing in all directions.

sn: गाण्डीवोत्थं दहेताजौ पुत्राणां मम वाहिनीम्। अपि सारथ्यघोषेण भयार्ता सव्यसाचिनः॥
en: And coming out of the Gandiva bow and burning up the four elements of the army of my sons. (I see) also that struck with fear from the sound of Savyasachin's chariot.

sn: वित्रस्ता बहुधा सेना भारती प्रतिभाति मे। यथा कक्षं महानग्निः प्रदहेत् सर्वतश्चरन्। महार्चिरनिलोद्भूतस्तद्वद् धक्ष्यति मामकान्॥
en: My army consisting of numerous forces are flying away in all directions. As a great fire raging in all directions burns up withered grass urged by the wind, so will the great fire (in the shape of Arjuna's weapons) consume my army.

sn: स्तानाततायी समरे किरीटी। सृष्टोऽन्तकः सर्वहरो विधात्रा यथा भवेत् तद्वदपारणीयः॥
en: When Kiritin, incapable of being withstood, opposing them (iny men) in battle will shoot destructive showers of arrows upon them, it will be like the king of death directed by the all destroying Father.

sn: तदा ह्यभीक्ष्णं सुबहून् प्रकारान् श्रोतास्मि तानावसथे कुरूणाम्। तेषां समन्ताच्च तथा रणाग्रे क्षयः किलायं भरतानुपैति॥
en: When I shall see and hear innumerable kinds of evil omens in the camp of the Kurus and around them and before the battle, then will destruction come to the race of Bharata.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच यथैव पाण्डवाः सर्वे पराक्रान्ता जिगीषवः। तथैवाभिसरास्तेषां त्यक्तात्मानो जये धृताः॥
en: Dhritarashtra said As the sons of Pandu are all powerful and desirous of victory, so are their followers who are self-sacrificing and have set their mind on victory.

sn: त्वमेव हि पराक्रान्तानाचक्षीथाः परान् मम। पञ्चालान् केकयान् मत्स्यान् मागधान् वत्सभूमिपान्॥२
en: You have related to me about those mighty foes of mine-of the kings of the Panchalas, Kaikeyas, Matsyas, Magadhas.

sn: यश्च सेन्द्रानिमाल्लोकानिच्छन् कुर्याद् वशे बली। स स्रष्टा जगतः कृष्णः पाण्डवानां जये धृतः॥
en: Even that mighty one who by his mere wish could bring under control these worlds with Indra, that creator of the world, Krishna, has set his mind on the victory of the Pandavas.

sn: समस्तामर्जुनाद् विद्यां सात्यकिः क्षिप्रमाप्तवान्। शैनेयः समरे स्थाता बीजवत् प्रवपञ्छरान्॥
en: Satyaki very quickly obtained all knowledge (of the use of arms) from Arjuna and the son of Shini will stand on the field of battle and shoot arrows as (men) sow the seeds.

sn: धृष्टद्युम्नश्च पाञ्चाल्यः क्रूरकर्मा महारथः। मामकेषु रणं कर्ता बलेषु परमास्त्रवित्॥
en: Dhrishtadyumna, the king of Panchalas, of cruel deeds and a mighty car-warrior and well acquainted with the use of superior weapons, too, will fight with my army.

sn: युधिष्ठिरस्य च क्रोधादर्जुनस्य च विक्रमात्। यमाभ्यां भीमसेनाच्च भयं मे तात जायते॥
en: From the wrath of Yudhishthira and from the prowess of Arjuna and from the twins and also from Bhimasena, do I derive great fear, O dear.

sn: अमानुषं मनुष्येन्द्रैर्जालं विततमन्तरा। न मे सैन्यास्तरिष्यन्ति ततः क्रोशामि संजय॥
en: On a superhuman net (of arrows) being spread over my army, they will not be able to get out of it; therefore do I weep, O Sanjaya.

sn: दर्शनीयो मनस्वी च लक्ष्मीवान् ब्रह्मवर्चसी। मेधावी सुकृतप्रज्ञो धर्मात्मा पाण्डुनन्दनः॥
en: Beautiful, independent, endued with prosperity and with the force of Brahma, intelligent, of great wisdom and of virtuous soul, is that son of Pandu (Yudhishthira).

sn: मित्रामात्यैः सुसम्पन्नः सम्पन्नो युद्धयोजकैः। भ्रातृभिः श्वशुरैर्वीरैरुपपन्नो महारथैः॥ धृत्या च पुरुषव्याघ्रो नैभृत्येन च पाण्डवः। अनृशंसो वदान्यश्च ह्रीमान् सत्यपराक्रमः॥ बहुश्रुतः कृतात्मा च वृद्धसेवी जितेन्द्रियः। तं सर्वगुणसम्पन्नं समिद्धमिव पावकम्॥
en: With friends and counselors and surrounded by men prepared for battle and also by brothers, fathers-in-law who are all excellent heroes and eminent car-warriors, the son of Pandu, that tiger among men, is also graced with patience, secrecy, humanity, benevolence, modesty, truth and prowess, versed in the knowledge of holy books, having self-control, attending to the old, is that one who has subdued his senses and is possessed of every virtue and he is like a blazing fire.

sn: तपन्तमभि को मन्दः पतिष्यति पतङ्गवत्। पाण्डवाग्निमनावार्यं मुमूर्षुर्नष्टचेतनः॥
en: What fool, about to die and who has lost his consciousness is there who will fall into the inextinguishable fire of the Pandavas ablaze like a moth.

sn: तनुरुद्धः शिखी राजा मिथ्योपचरितो मया। मन्दानां मम पुत्राणां युद्धेनान्तं करिष्यति॥
en: That king resembling a fire of high and long flames has been treated deceitfully by me and he will, in battle, put an end to the existence of all my sons of weak intellect.

sn: तैरयुद्धं साधु मन्ये कुरवस्तन्निबोधत। युद्धे विनाशः कृत्स्नस्य कुलस्य भविता ध्रुवम्॥
en: I consider that it is best not to fight with them; you, Kurus, follow that (my opinion). If you wage war, destruction will surely overtake the race which will be extinct.

sn: एषा मे परमा बुद्धिर्यया शाम्यति मे मनः। यदि त्वयुद्धमिष्टं वो वयं शान्त्यै यतामहे॥
en: This appears to me very clear and by acting in accordance with it my mind will obtain peace. If you consider that peace with them is desirable, then we shall try for peace.

sn: न तु नः क्लिश्यमानानामुपेक्षेत युधिष्ठिरः। जुगुप्सति ह्यधर्मेण मामेवोद्दिश्य कारणम्॥
en: Yudhishthira will never adopt an attitude of indifference towards ourselves, when distressed; he blames me by ascribing unrighteousness, thinking me to be the cause (of the war).

sn: संजय उवाच एवमेतन्महाराज यथा वदसि भारत। युद्धे विनाशः क्षत्रस्य गाण्डीवेन प्रदृश्यते॥
en: Sanjaya said It is, O great king, as you say, O Bharata. The destruction of the Kshatriya by war with the Gandiva bow seems apparent.

sn: इदं तु नाभिजानामि तव धीरस्य नित्यशः। यत् पुत्रवशमागच्छेस्तत्त्वज्ञः सव्यसाचिनः॥
en: I do not know how it is that you, who are ever wise and know about the attributes of Savyasachin, allow yourself to be controlled by your sons.

sn: नैष कालो महाराज तव शश्वत् कृतागसः। त्वया ह्येवादितः पार्था निकृता भरतर्षभ।॥
en: This is not the time, O great king, (to give way to grief); for you have repeatedly wronged them. By you in the beginning were the Parthas cxiled, O bull among the race of Bharata.

sn: पिता श्रेष्ठः सुहृद् यश्च सम्यक् प्रणिहितात्मवान्। आस्थेयं हि हितं तेन न द्रोग्धा गुरुरुच्यते॥
en: A father is the best friend and he should guide well those who are his own selves. Their welfare should be sought after carefully; but he who overlooks this duty, cannot be called a superior.

sn: इदं जितमिदं लब्धमिति श्रुत्वा पराजितान्। द्यूतकाले महाराज स्मयसे स्म कुमारवत्॥
en: Hearing of the defeat (at the game), like a boy you laughed out, O great king, saying-"this is gained, this is won”.

sn: परुषाण्युच्यमानांश्च पुरा पार्थानुपेक्षसे। कृत्स्नं राज्यं जयन्तीति प्रपातं नानुपश्यसि॥
en: Formerly you neglected the Parthas, who were being addressed in hashed words thinking that the kingdom had been acquired (by your sons). You did not then foresee this fall.

sn: पित्र्यं राज्यं महाराज कुरुवस्ते सजाङ्गलाः। अथ वीरैर्जितामुर्वीमखिलां प्रत्यपद्यथाः॥
en: The country of the Kurus, with Jangala, O great king, is your ancestral kingdom; but you have possessed yourself the entire kingdom subjugated by the heroes.

sn: बाहुवीर्यार्जिता भूमिस्तव पार्थेनिवेदिता। मयेदं कृतमित्येव मन्यसे राजसत्तम॥
en: The kingdom acquired by their arms and prowess was made over to you by the Parthas and you think, "it has been acquired by me," O best of kings.

sn: चस्तान् गन्धर्वराजेन मज्जतो ह्यप्लवेऽम्भसि। आनिनाय पुनः पार्थः पुत्रांस्ते राजसत्तम॥
en: Your sons, O best of kings, overpowered by the king of the Gandharvas and thus sinking as it were in a scoreless open, were brought back by Partha.

sn: कुमारवच्च स्मयसे छूते विनिकृतेषु यत्। पाण्डवेषु वने राजन् प्रव्रजत्सु पुनः पुनः॥
en: Like a boy, too, did you repeatedly laugh at the defeat (of the Pandavas) at dice and also when they were wandering about being exiled.

sn: प्रवर्षतः शरवातानर्जुनस्य शितान् बहून्। अप्यर्णवा विशुष्येयुः किं पुनर्मांसयोनयः॥
en: At the shower, by Arjuna, of a great many sharp edged arrows, even the oceans dry up, not to speak of those things, that owe their origin to flesh.

sn: अस्यतां फाल्गुनः श्रेष्ठोगाण्डीवं धनुषां वरम्। केशवः सर्वभूतानामायुधानां सुदर्शनम्॥
en: Among the shooters of arrows, the son of Falguna is the chief, among the bows the Gandiva is the best; Keshava is the chief of all creatures, and the Sudarshana among weapons.

sn: वानरो रोचमानश्च केतुः केतुमतां वरः। एवमेतानि सरयो वहू वेतहयो रणे॥
en: Of all things having banners the one shining with the banner and having the device of an ape (is the foremost). The car, having all these and having many white horses in battle.

sn: क्षपयिष्यति नो राजन् कालचक्रमिवोद्यतम्। तस्याद्य वसुधा राजन् निखिला भरतर्षभ॥
en: Will overthrow us, O king, like the uplifted wheel of death. To-day, the entire earth is his, O king, O bull of the race of Bharata.

sn: यस्य भीमार्जुनौ योधौ स राजा राजसत्तम। तथा भीमहतप्रायां मज्जन्तीं तव वाहिनीम्॥
en: He who has the two warriors, Bhima and Arjuna, on his side, O best of kings is the king seeing your army nearly killed by Bhima.

sn: दुर्योधनमुखा दृष्ट्वा क्षयं यास्यन्ति कौरवाः। न भीमार्जुनयोर्भीता लप्स्यन्ते विजयं विभो॥
en: The Kauravas, headed by Duryodhana, will be destroyed, struck by the terror of Bhima and Arjuna; and victory will not be gained, O Lord,

sn: तव पुत्रा महाराज राजानश्चानुसारिणः। मत्स्यास्त्वामद्य नार्चन्ति पञ्चालाश्च सकेकयाः॥ शाल्वेयाः शूरसेनाश्च सर्वे त्वामवजानते। पार्थं ह्येते गताः सर्वे वीर्यज्ञास्तस्य धीमतः।।१८।
en: By your son, O great king or by the kings who are his followers. The king of the Matsyas does not pay you homage now; nor does the Panchala with the Kaikeyas; nor do the Shalvas and the Shurasenas. All disregard you. All of them have gone over to the side of Partha, well knowing the heroism of that wise one.

sn: भक्त्या ह्यस्य विरुध्यन्ते तव पुत्रैः सदैव ते। अनर्हानेव तु वधे धर्मयुक्तान् विकर्मणा॥ योऽक्लेशयत् पाण्डुपुत्रान् यो विद्वेष्ट्यधुनापि वै। सर्वोपायनियन्तव्यः सानुगः पापपूरुषः॥
en: Out of regard for him, they are ever against your sons. He who troubles the sons of Pandu endued with virtue and undeserving of injury by unworthy actions and he who despises them even now, that evil-minded man, along with his followers, should be checked by all means.

sn: तव पुत्रो महाराज नानुशोचितुमर्हसि। द्यूतकाले मया चोक्तं विदुरेण च धीमता॥
en: It is not proper, O great king, that you should grieve for your sons. At the time of the game at dice, all this was predicted by me, as also by the wise Vidura.

sn: यदिदं ते विलपितं पाण्डवान् प्रति भारत। अनीशेनेव राजेन्द्र सर्वमेतन्निरर्थकम्॥
en: All these lamentations of yours for the sons of Pandu, O Bharata, as if you had no hand in the matter, are all useless, O chief among kings.

sn: दुर्योधन उवाच न भेतव्यं महाराज न शोच्या भवता वयम्। समर्थाः स्म पराञ्जेतुं बलिनः समरे विभो॥
en: Duryodhana said There is nothing to fear, O great king; nor should you grieve for us. We are capable, O king, of winning victory over our battle, O king.

sn: वने प्रवाजितान् पार्थान् यदाऽऽयान्मधुसूदनः। महता बलचक्रेण परराष्ट्रावमर्दिना॥ केकया धृष्टकेतुश्च धृष्टद्युम्नश्च पार्षतः। राजानश्चान्वयुः पार्थान् बहवोऽन्येऽनुयायिनः॥
en: When the slayer of Madhu came to the sons of Pritha wandering in exile in the forest with a large army capable of subjugating the kingdom of the enemies and when Kaikeya, Dhrishtaketu, Dhrishtadyumna of the race of Prishata and many other kings followed them to the sons of Pritha.

sn: इन्द्रप्रस्थस्य चादूरात् समाजग्मुर्महारथाः। व्यगर्हयंश्च संगम्य भवन्तं कुरुभिः सह॥
en: And when not far from Indraprastha there assembled together the car-warriors and having joined together, they blamed you along with the Kurus.

sn: ते युधिष्ठिरमासीनमजिनैः प्रतिवासितम्। कृष्णप्रधानाः संहत्य पर्युपासन्त भारत॥ प्रत्यादानं च राज्यस्य कार्यमूचुर्नराधिपाः। भवतः सानुबन्धस्य समुच्छेदं चिकीर्षवः॥
en: And when they, with Krishna at their head, paid homage to Yudhishthira, who was wearing deer skin, O Bharata, and when the rulers of men spoke of giving back the duties of a king (to Yudhishthira) and they longed to bring about the overthrow of yourself with all your followers.

sn: श्रुत्वा चैवं मयोक्तास्तु भीष्मद्रोणकृपास्तदा। ज्ञातिक्षयभयाद् राजन् भीतेन भरतर्षभ॥ ततः स्थास्यन्ति समये पाण्डवा इति मे मतिः। समुच्छेदं हि नः कृत्स्नं वासुदेवश्चिकीर्षति॥
en: Then were Bhishma, Drona and Kripa thus addressed by me, who heard this, through fear of the ruin of our cousins, Oking, "That the sons of Pandu will abide by the terms agreed to, is my opinion; our destruction does the son of Vasudeva desire.

sn: ऋते च विदुरात् सर्वे यूयं वध्या मता मम। धृतराष्ट्रस्तु धर्मज्ञो न वध्यः कुरुसत्तमः॥
en: That with the exception of Vidura, will you be slain, is my opinion; and Dhritarashtra, who knows the nature of virtue-that best one among the Kurus cannot possibly be slain.

sn: समुच्छेदं च कृत्स्नं नः कृत्वा तात जनार्दनः। एकराज्यं कुरूणां स्म चिकीर्षति युधिष्ठिरे॥
en: O dear, having effected our extinction, Janardana desires to bestow on Yudhishthira the entire kingdom of the Kurus.

sn: तत्र किं प्राप्तकालं नः प्रणिपातः पलायनम्। प्राणान् वा सम्परित्यज्य प्रतियुध्यामहे परान्॥
en: When the time comes, what should we do? Surrender or fly or shall we fight against the enemies and give up (all hopes of) our lives.

sn: प्रतियुद्धे तु नियतः स्यादस्माकं पराजयः। युधिष्ठिरस्य सर्वे हि पार्थिवा वशवर्तिनः॥
en: In a fight against them, defeat shall surely be ours; all the rulers are on the side of Yudhishthira.

sn: विरक्तराष्ट्राश्च वयं मित्राणि कुपितानि नः। धिक्कृताः पार्थिवैः सर्वैः स्वजनेन च सर्वशः॥
en: On their being dispossessed of their kingdom, our friends are angry with us; and we are reviled by all the kings and by all our kinsmen.

sn: प्रणिपाते न दोषोऽस्ति सन्धिनः शाश्वतीः समाः। पितरं त्वेव शोचामि प्रज्ञानेनं जनाधिपम्॥
en: There is no objection to our surrender; for men or our position seek peace from a long time; but I grieve for my father, that lord of men, who has his wisdom only for his eyes.

sn: मत्कृते दुःखमापन्नं क्लेशं प्राप्तमनन्तकम्। कृतं हि तव पुत्रैश्च परेषामवरोधनम्। मत्प्रियार्थं पुरैवैतद् विदितं ते नरोत्तम॥
en: And who may for my doings be beset with troubles and endless woes. The enemies were opposed by your sons simply for our good; which is known to you before, O best among men.

sn: ते राज्ञो धृतराष्ट्रस्य सामात्यस्य महारथाः। वैरं प्रतिकरिष्यन्ति कुलोच्छेदन पाण्डवाः॥
en: The sons of Pandu, these mighty carwarriors, will have their revenge for their wrongs by the extinction of the race of the king Dhritarashtra with that of his ministers.

sn: ततो द्रोणोऽब्रवीद् भीष्मः कृपो द्रौणिश्च भारत। मत्वा मां महतीं चिन्तामास्थितं व्यथितेन्द्रियम्॥
en: Then did Drona and Bhima and Kripa and the son of Drona thus speak, O Bharata, thinking me to be in the midst of great anxiety and with the senses tortured.

sn: अभिदुग्धाः परे चेन्नो न भेतव्यं परंतप। असमर्थाः परे जेतुमस्मान् युधि समास्थितान्॥
en: The enemies ready to fight need not be feared, 0 subduer of foes; for the foes when in the battle field are incapable of conquering us.

sn: एकैकशः समर्थाः स्मो विजेतुं सर्वपार्थिवान्। आगच्छन्तु विनेष्यामो दर्पमेषां शितैः शरैः॥
en: Each one of us by himself can conquer all the rulers of the earth. Let them come; we shall curb their pride by sharp arrows.

sn: पुरैकेन हि भीष्मेण विजिताः सर्वपार्थिवाः। मृते पितर्यतिक्रुद्धो रथेनैकेन भारत॥
en: In days of old, all the rulers of the earth were conquered by the single Bhima seated on the single car, extremely wrathful on the death of his father.

sn: जघान सुबहूंस्तेषां संरब्धः कुरुसत्तमः। ततस्ते शरणं जग्मुर्देवव्रतमिमं भयात्॥
en: That best one among the race of the Kurus, wrathful, killed many among them (enemies); them they out of fear sought the protection of this Devavrata.

sn: स भीष्मः सुसमर्थोऽयमस्माभिः सहितो रणे। परान् विजेतुं तस्मात् ते व्येतु भीर्भरतर्षभ॥
en: That Bhishma is well capable to fight along with us and to conquer to enemies; therefore, O bull among the race of Bharata, let your fears be dispelled.

sn: इत्येषां निश्चयो ह्यासीत् तत्कालेऽमिततेजसाम्। पुरा परेषां पृथिवी कृतस्नाऽऽसीद् वशवर्तिनी॥
en: Such was the determination, at that time, of these ones of immeasurable prowess. In days of old the earth was under the possession of the enemies.

sn: अस्मान् पुनरमी नाद्य समर्था जेतुमाहवे। छिन्नपक्षाः परे ह्यद्य वीर्यहीनाश्च पाण्डवाः॥
en: Now they are not capable of again conquering us; the Pandavas are now shorn of their wings and devoid of strength.

sn: अस्मत्संस्था च पृथिवी वर्तते भरतर्षभ। एकार्थाः सुखदुःखेषु समानीताश्च पार्थिवाः॥
en: The earth, too, O bull among the race of Bharata, is now under our subjection and the rulers of the earth assembled are of the same mind with me in happiness or misery.

sn: अप्यग्नि प्रविशेयुस्ते समुद्रं वा परंतप। मदर्थं पार्थिवाः सर्वे तद् विद्धि कुरुसत्तम॥
en: O subduer of foes, for my sake, the rulers of the earth, can enter into fireor even the ocean; know this, O you best among the race of Kurus.

sn: उन्मत्तमिव चापि त्वां प्रहसन्तीह दुःखितम्। विलपन्तं बहुविधं भीतं परविकत्थने॥
en: In this case they laugh at you, who are grieved and like one insane and giving vent to many sorts of lamentations, struck with fear by the descriptions of the enemies.

sn: एषां ह्येकैकशो राज्ञां समर्थः पाण्डवान् प्रति। आत्मानं मन्यते सर्वो व्येतु ते भयमागतम्॥
en: Each of these kings by himself are capable of opposing the Pandavas. Every one considers himself all in all. Let the fear which has come on you be dispelled,

sn: जेतुं समग्रां सेनां मे वासवोऽपि न शक्नुयात्। हन्तुमक्षय्यरूपेयं ब्रह्मणोऽपि स्वयम्भुवः॥
en: To conquer my entire army, which is endless, cannot be annihilated even by Brahma, who is born of himself.

sn: युधिष्ठिरः पुरं हित्वा पञ्च ग्रामान् स याचति। भीतो हि मामकात् सैन्यात् प्रभावाच्चैव मे विभो।।३०
en: That Yudhishthira foregoing his claims to the entire kingdom begs only five villages; he is afraid of my army and my prowess, O Lord.

sn: समर्थं मन्यसे यच्च कुन्तीपुत्रं वृकोदरम्। तन्मिथ्या न हि मे कृत्स्नं प्रभावं वेत्सि भारत॥
en: The impression you have of the might of Vrikodara, the son of Kunti, has no foundation; you do not know my prowess, O Bharata.

sn: मत्समो हि गदायुद्धे पृथिव्यां नास्ति कश्चन। नासीत् कश्चिदतिक्रान्तो भवति न च कश्चन॥
en: My equal in a fight with the mace, there is none in the world; there has been none my equal, nor will there be any.

sn: युक्तो दुःखोषितश्चाहं विद्यापारगतस्तथा। तस्मान्न भीमान्नान्येभ्यो भयं मे विद्यते क्वचित्॥
en: Suffering a lot of troubles and employing myself earnestly to my task, have I lived at the abode of my preceptor and learnt my lessons; therefore have I not the slightest fear from Bhima, nor from any other.

sn: दुर्योधनसमो नास्ति गदायामिति निश्चयः। संकर्षणस्य भद्रं ते यत् तदैनमुपावसम्॥
en: In a fight with the mace there is none equal to Duryodhana-this is sure; for he used to live with Sankarshana (his preceptor), good betide you.

sn: युद्धे संकर्षणसमो बलेनाभ्यधिको भुवि। गदाप्रहारं भीमो मे न जातु विषहेद् युधि।॥
en: In a fight I am Sankarshana's equal and in strength there is none my equal in the world; Bhima will not be able to bear the blows of my mace in battle.

sn: एकं प्रहारं यं दद्यां भीमाय रुषितो नृप। स एवैनं नयेद् घोरः क्षिप्रं वैवस्वतक्षयम्॥
en: Being enraged, the one blow that I shall deal Bhima, o king, will strike him severely and speedily send him to the palace of death.

sn: इच्छेयं च गदाहस्तं राजन् दुष्टुं वृकोदरम्। सुचिरं प्रार्थितो ह्येष मम नित्य मनोरथः॥
en: I am desirous, O king, to see Vrikodara with the mace in his hand; this has been prayed for by me for a long time, this has ever been the desire of my heart.

sn: गदया निहतो ह्याजौ मया पार्थो वृकोदरः। विशीर्णगात्रः पृथिवीं परासुः प्रपतिष्यति॥
en: Struck by me with the mace, Vrikodara, the son of Pritha, will fall lifeless on the ground with his body smashed.

sn: गदाप्रहाराभिहतो हिमवानपि पर्वतः। सकृन्मया विदीर्येत गिरिः शतसहस्रधा॥
en: Struck by a blow from my mace, even the Himavat mountain can be split up into a hundred thousand pieces.

sn: स चाप्येतद् विजानाति वासुदेवार्जुनौ तथा। दुर्योधनसमो नास्ति गदायामिति निश्चयः॥
en: It is very well known to both Vasudeva and Arjuna that it is certain that in a fight with the mace there is none equal to Duryodhana.

sn: तत् ते वृकोदरमयं भयं व्येतु महाहवे। व्यपनेष्याम्यहं ह्येनं मा राजन् विमना भव॥
en: There let your fear proceeding from Vrikodara be dispelled; for I shall kill this one. Do not, O king, yield to grief.

sn: तस्मिन् मया हते क्षिप्रमर्जुनं बहवो रथाः। तुल्यरूपा विशिष्टाश्च क्षेप्स्यन्ति भरतर्षम॥
en: He being slain by me, many car-warriors, educed with similar qualities, speedily throw down Arjuna, o bull among the race of Bharata.

sn: भीष्मो द्रोणः कृपो द्रौणिः कर्णो भूरिश्रवास्तथा। प्राग्ज्योतिषाधिपः शल्यः सिन्धुराजो जयद्रथः॥
en: Bhishma, Drona, Kripa, Drona's son and Bhurishrava, Shalya, the king of the Pragjyotish and Jayadratha, the king of the Sindhus,

sn: एकैक एषां शक्तस्तु हन्तुं भारत पाण्डवान्। समेतास्तु क्षणैनैतान् नेष्यन्ति यमसादनम्। समग्रा पार्थिवो सेना पार्थमेकं धनंजयम्॥
en: Each one of these by himself is competent to kill the Pandavas, O Bharata, Acting together they will in an instant bring them to the abode of death.

sn: कस्मादशक्ता निर्जेतुमिति हेतुर्न विद्यते। शरवातैस्तु भीष्मेण शतशो निचितोऽवशः॥
en: There is no reason why the entire army of the kings on one side is incapable of conquering the single Dhananjaya. Covered by arrows shot by Bhishma a hundred times.

sn: द्रोणद्रौणिकृपैश्चैव गन्ता पार्थो यमक्षयम्। पितामहोऽपि गाङ्गेयः शान्तनोरधि भारत॥
en: And by Drona, his son and Kripa, this son of Pritha will go to the region of the dead. Born of Ganga, our grandfather, too, is superior to the son of Shantanu, O Bharata.

sn: ब्रह्मर्षिसदृशो जज्ञे देवैरपि सुदुःसहः। न हन्ता विद्यते चापि राजन् भीष्मस्य कश्चन॥
en: Like a Brahmarshi ( a devotee of the first rank and order) he was born among men and is hard to be vanquished even by the gods. There is no slayer of Bhishma, Oking.

sn: पित्रा ह्युक्तः प्रसन्नेन नाकामस्त्वं मरिष्यसि। ब्रह्मर्षेच भरद्वाजाद् द्रोणो द्रोण्यामजायत॥
en: This boon was granted by his father who was gratified-'You will not die without your own desire. Drona was born of the Brahmarshi Bharadvaja in a water pot.

sn: द्रोणाज्जज्ञे महाराज द्रौणिश्च परमास्त्रवित्। कृपश्चाचार्यमुख्योऽयं महर्षे!तमादपि॥
en: From Drona was born his son, well acquainted with the use of arins. This Kripa, too, is the foremost among the preceptors and was born of the great Rishi Gautama.

sn: शरस्तम्बोद्भवः श्रीमानवध्य इति मे मतिः। अयोनिजास्त्रयो होते पिता माता च मातुलः॥
en: This one, endued with prosperity and born in a clump of heath, is incapable of being killed, such is my impression. Then, too, the father, mother and maternal uncle of Ashvathaman did not take their birth in a woman's womb.

sn: अश्वत्थाम्नो महाराज स च शूरः स्थितो मम। सर्व एते महाराज देवकल्पा महारथाः॥
en: That hero, too, is on my side. All these, o great king, are car-warriors equal to the gods themselves.

sn: शक्रस्यापि व्यथां कुर्युः संयुगे भरतर्षभ। नैतेषामर्जुनः शक्त एकैकं प्रति वीक्षितुम्॥
en: They are capable even of giving trouble to Shakra himself in battle. Arjuna is not capable even of gazing at any of them by himself.

sn: सहितास्तु नरव्याघ्रा हनिष्यन्ति धनंजयम्। भीष्मद्रोणकृपाणां च तुल्यः कर्णो मतो मम॥
en: And these tigers among men united together will kill Dhananjaya. Bhishma, Drona and Kripa together are equal to Karna, such is my opinion.

sn: अनुज्ञातश्च रामेण मत्समोऽसीति भारत। कुण्डले रुचिरे चास्तां कर्णस्य सहजे शुभे॥
en: He has been told by Rama-you are equal to me, O Bharata. Two beautiful and blessed ear-rings Karna had from his very birth.

sn: ते शच्यर्थं महेन्द्रेण याचितः स परंतपः। अमोघया महाराज शक्त्या परमभीमया॥
en: These two were asked by the great Indra himself for the sake of Sachi, O subduer of foes, in exchange, O great king of greatly terrific strength and infallible.

sn: तस्य शक्त्योपगूढस्य कस्माज्जीवेद् धनंजयः। विजयो मे ध्रुवं राजन् फलं पाणाविवाहितम्॥
en: How can Dhananjaya escape (after a struggle with) from him who is thus protected; therefore is my victory certain, O king, as a fruit comes within the grasp of my two hands.

sn: अभिव्यक्तः परेषां च कृत्स्नो भुवि पराजयः। अह्ना टेकेन भीष्मोऽयं प्रयुतं हन्ति भारत॥
en: Our defeat and the success of enemies, too, are proclaimed in the world. In one day this Bhishma kills ten thousand (enemies), 0 Bharata.

sn: तत्समाश्च महेष्वासा द्रोणद्रौणिकृपा अपि। संशप्तकानां वृन्दानि क्षत्रियाणां परंतप॥ अर्जुनं वयमस्मान् वा निहन्यात् कपिकेतनः। तं चालमिति मन्यन्ते सव्यसाचिवधे धृताः॥
en: The mighty bowmen, Drona, his son and Kripa, are equal to him (in this respect). Then, too, the ranks of the Sanshaptaka Kshatriya, O subduer of foes, these determined on the destruction of Savyasachin have made this resolution in their mind-Either we shall kill Arjuna or that one having the figure of a monkey on his flag will kill us.

sn: पार्थिवाः स भवांस्तेभ्यो हकस्माद् व्यथते कथम्। भीमसेने च निहते कोऽन्यो युध्येत भारत॥
en: Such are the kings (on my side); why do you all on a sudden express fear for the enemies. Bhimasena being slain, what other warriors will fight, O Bharata.

sn: परेषां तन्ममाचक्ष्व यदि वेत्थ परंतप। पञ्च ते भ्रातरः सर्वे धृष्टद्युम्नोऽथ सात्यकिः॥ परेषां सप्त ये राजन् योधाः सारं बलं मतम्। अस्माकं तु विशिष्टा ये भीष्मद्रोणकृपादयः॥
en: If you know any among the enemies (who will) thus tell me of him, O subduer of enemies. The five brothers along with Dhrishtadyumna and Satyaki these seven warriors whom you consider to be the best among the enemies and the accomplished warriors on our side are Bhishma, Drona, Kripa and others.

sn: द्रौणिर्विकर्तनः कर्णः सोमदत्तोऽथ बाह्निकः। प्राग्ज्योतिषाधिपः शल्य आवन्त्यौ च जयद्रथः॥ दुःशासनो दुर्मुखश्च दुःसहश्च विशाम्पते। श्रुतायुश्चित्रसेनश्च पुरुमित्रो विविंशतिः॥ शलो भूरिश्रवाश्चैव विकर्णश्च तवात्मजः। अक्षौहिण्यो हि मे राजन् दशैका च समाहृताः। न्यूनाः परेषां सप्तैव कस्मान्मे स्यात् पराजयः॥
en: The son of Drona, Karna, Somadatta, Balhika, Shalya the king of the Pragjyotish, the two kings of Avanti and Jayadratha and Dushasana, Durmukha, Dussaha, O Lord of the world, Shrutayu, Shrutayu, Chitrasena, Purumitra, Vivanshati, Shala, Bhurishravas and Vikarna, your sons. These two can never be equal. Ten and one Akshauhinis have been brought together by me, Oking.

sn: बलं त्रिगुणतो हीनं योध्यं प्राह बृहस्पतिः। परेभ्यस्त्रिगुणा चेयं मम राजन्ननीकिनी॥
en: That of the enemies is less, it is only seven; why thus should defeat be mine; an army less by a third should be fought with, said Brihaspati. My army, o king, exceeds that of the enemy by a third.

sn: गुणहीनं परेषां च बहु पश्यामि भारत। गुणोदयं बहुगुणमात्मनश्च विशाम्पते॥
en: Then again do I see the enemy without any accomplishment, O Bharata; while ours, many accomplishments.

sn: एतत् सर्वं समाज्ञाय बलाग्यं मम भारत। न्यूनतां पाण्डवानां च न मोहं गन्तुमर्हसि॥
en: O lord, knowing well all this the superiority of my army, O Bharata; and the inferior number of the Pandavas, it is not proper that you should lose your senses.

sn: इत्युक्त्वा संजयं भूयः पर्यपृच्छत भारत। विवित्सुः प्राप्तकालानि ज्ञात्वा परपुरंजयः॥
en: Having thus addressed, he asked again of Sanjaya, O Bharata, desirous of knowing more of the enemies thinking that the proper time has come.

sn: दुर्योधन उवाच अक्षौहिणी: सप्त लब्ध्वा राजभिः सह संजय। किंस्विदिच्छति कौन्तेयो युद्धप्रेप्सुर्युधिष्ठिरः।।शा
en: Duryodhana said Having obtained an army of seven Akshauhinis, what does Yudhishthira, the son of Kunti, desirous of war, do along with the other kings.

sn: संजय उवाच अतीव मुदितो राजन् युद्धप्रेप्सुर्युधिष्ठिरः। भीमसेनार्जुनौ चोभौ यमावपि न बिभ्यतः॥
en: Sanjaya said Yudhishthira, desirous of war, is extremely cheerful; and the two, Bhimasena and Arjuna, are not otherwise. The twins too, are not afraid.

sn: रथं तु दिव्यं कौन्तेयः सर्वा विभ्राजयन् दिशः। मन्त्रं जिज्ञासमानः सन् बीभत्सुः समयोजयत्॥
en: The son of Kunti, roamed about in his heavenly car in all directions. Vibhatsu, yoked the horses to it to test the efficacy of the Mantras (obtained by him).

sn: तमपश्याम संनद्धं मेघं विद्युद्युतं यथा। समन्तात् समभिध्याय हृष्यमाणोऽभ्यभाषत॥
en: I beheld him, with his coat of mail on, like clouds with lightning. After thinking for a short time he addressed me thus with a light heart.

sn: पूर्वरूपमिदं पश्य वयं जेष्याम संजय। बीभत्सुर्मा यथोवाच तथावैम्यहमप्युत॥
en: See these signs of prophecy; we will conquer, O Sanjaya, what Vibhatsu told me. I also saw the truth of this.

sn: दुर्योधन उवाच प्रशंसस्यभिनन्दस्तान् पार्थानक्षपराजितान्। अर्जुनस्य रथे ब्रूहि कथमश्वाः कथं ध्वजाः॥
en: Duryodhana said You are pleased at praising those sons of Pritha, who were defeated at the game at dice. Tell me now what sort of horses are attached to the car of Arjuna and what sort of banners.

sn: संजय उवाच भौमनः सह शक्रेण बहुचित्रं विशाम्पते। रूपाणि कल्पयामास त्वष्टा धाता सदा विभो॥
en: Sanjaya said Tvashtri or Bhaumana and Dhatri, aided by Shakra thought out, o lord of the world, diverse forms%3B

sn: ध्वजे हि तस्मिन् रूपाणि चक्रुस्ते देवमायया। महाधनानि दिव्यानि महान्ति च लघूनि च॥
en: And those forms they included in the banner by the help of divine illusion-these forms, large and small, of heavenly origin and of great value.

sn: भीमसेनानुरोधाय हनूमान् मारुतात्मजः। आत्मप्रतिकृति तस्मिन् ध्वज आरोपयिष्यति॥
en: At the request of Bhimasena, Hanumat, the son of the god of wind, will place his own figure on that banner.

sn: सर्वा दिशो योजनमात्रमन्तरं स तिर्यगूज़ च रुरोध वै ध्वजः। न सज्जत्यऽसौ तरुभिः संवृतोऽपि तथा हि माया विहता भौमनेन॥
en: Such is the illusion produced by Bhimasena, that the banner occupies the space one yojana in all directions, both perpendicularly and obliquely; and through surrounded by trees its progress cannot be obstructed.

sn: यथाऽऽकाशे शक्रधनुः प्रकाशते न चैकवर्णं न च वेद्मि किं नु तत्। तथा ध्वजो विहितो भौमनेन बह्वाकारं दृश्यते रूपमस्य॥
en: The banner designed by Bhaumana and its form appear as of diverse sorts like the diverse colours of Shakra's bow, which appears in the sky; but nobody knows what it is made of.

sn: यथाग्निधूमो दिवमेति रुद्ध्वा वर्णान् बिभ्रत् तैजसाचित्ररूपान्। तथा ध्वजो विहितो भौमनेन न चेद् भारो भविता नोत रोधः॥
en: As smoke mixed with fire mounts the sky appearing beautiful and holding its many colours, so the flag manufactured by Brahmana has no weight and knows no impediment.

sn: श्वेतास्तस्मिन् वातवेगाः सदश्वा दिव्या युक्ताश्चित्ररथेन दत्ताः। भुव्यन्तरिक्षे दिवि वा नरेन्द्र येषां गतिहीयते नात्र सर्वा। शतं यत् तत् पूर्यते नित्यकालं हतं हतं दत्तवरं पुरस्तात्॥१३।
en: And to that (car) are yoked many excellent celestial horses, white in colour, presented by Chitraratha and with the speed of wind. There is nothing in the world or in this world. Their number of hundred would ever remain constant however often they may be slain. Such was the effect of a boon granted in ancient days.

sn: तथा राज्ञो दन्तवर्णा बृहन्तो रथे युक्ता भान्ति तद्वीर्यतुल्याः। ऋक्षप्रख्या भीमसेनस्य वाहा रथे वायोस्तुल्यवेगा बभूवुः॥
en: In the same way, in the car of the king (Yudhishthira) are yoked large horses of the colour of ivory and of a strength similar to the king, The horses attached to Bhimasena's car are of the speed of wind, having the splendor of Rishis.

sn: कल्माषाङ्गास्तित्तिरिचित्रपृष्ठा भ्रात्रा दत्ताः प्रीयता फाल्गुनेन। भ्रातुर्वीरस्य स्वैस्तुरङ्गैर्विशिष्टा मुदा युक्ताः सहदेवं वहन्ति॥
en: Horses of black bodies, with backs of variegated colour, like the Tittara bird, presented by his brother Falguna out of dearness and possessed of better limbs than those of his heroic brother (Falguna), bear Sahadeva cheerfully.

sn: माद्रीपुत्रं नकुलं त्वाजमीढ महेन्द्रदत्ता हरयो वाजिमुख्याः। समा वायोर्बलवन्तस्तरस्विनो वहन्ति वीरं वृत्रशत्रु यथेन्द्रम्॥
en: Horses superior of their race presented by the great Indra and equal in speed to the wind, strong and speedy, bear the hero Nakula, the son of Madri, of Ajmida's race; even as they bear Indra himself the enemy of Vritra.

sn: तुल्य चैभिर्वयसा विक्रमेण महाजवाश्चित्ररूपाः सदश्वाः। सौभद्रादीन् द्रौपदेयान् कुमारान् वहन्त्यश्वा देवदत्ता बृहन्तः॥
en: Excellent horses of large size, of the same age as these and of equal strength, of many colours and great activity, presented by the gods, bear the princes, the sons of Subhadra and Draupadi.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच कांस्तत्र संजयापश्यः प्रीत्यर्थेन समागतान्। ये योत्स्यन्ते पाण्डवार्थं पुत्रस्य मम वाहिनीम्॥
en: Dhritarashtra said Whom have you, O Sanjaya, seen there coming out of love and who will fight with the army of my sons on behalf of the sons of Pandu?

sn: संजय उवाच मुख्यमन्धकवृष्णीनामपश्यं कृष्णमागतम्। चेकितान् च तत्रैव युयुधानं च सात्यकिम्॥
en: Sanjaya said The chief of the Andhakas and Vrishnis, Krishna have I seen come there; as also Chekitana, Yuyudhana and Satyaki.

sn: पृथगक्षौहिणीभ्यां तु पाण्डवानभिसंश्रितौ। महारथौ समाख्यातावुभौ पुरुषमानिनौ॥
en: The two famous and great car-warriors, proud among men, each with a separate Akshauhini of soldiers, have gone to the side of the Pandavas.

sn: अक्षौहिण्याथ पाञ्चाल्यो दशभिस्तनयैर्वृतः। सत्यजित्प्रमुखैवीरैधृष्टद्युम्नपुरोगमैः॥
en: And the king of the Panchalas Drupada, surrounded by his ten heroic sons, headed by Dhrishtadyumna, with an Akshauhini.

sn: दुपदो वर्धयन् मानं शिखण्डिपरिपालितः। उपायात् सर्वसैन्यानां प्रतिच्छाद्य तदा वपुः॥
en: And protected by Shikhandin has joined them after well protecting the limbs of his soldiers, enhancing the honour of the Pandavas.

sn: विराटः सह पुत्राभ्यां शङ्खनैवोत्तरेण च। सूर्यदत्तादिभिर्वीरैर्मदिराक्षपुरोगमैः॥ सहितः पृथिवीपालो भ्रातृभिस्तनयैस्तथा। अक्षौहिण्यैव सैन्यानां वृतः पार्थं समाश्रितः॥
en: Virata, too, with his two sons Shankha and Uttara and with the heroes Suryadatta and others headed by Madiraksha and with his brother and sons, surrounded by an Akshauhini of troops, has joined the son of Pritha.

sn: जारासंधिर्मागधश्च धृष्टकेतुश्च चेदिराट्। पृथक् पृथगनुप्राप्तौ पृथगक्षौहिणीवृतौ॥
en: The king of Magadha, the of Jarasandha, too and Dhrishtaketu, the king of the Chedis-these two have come separately each surrounded by an Akshauhini.

sn: केकया भ्रातरः पञ्च सर्वे लोहितकध्वजाः। अक्षौहिणीपरिवृताः पाण्डवानभिसंश्रिताः॥
en: The five brothers of Kaikeya, all having red flags, surrounded by an Akshauhini, have joined the sons of Pandu.

sn: एतानेतावतस्तत्र तानपश्यं समागतान्। ये पाण्डवार्थं योत्स्यन्ति धार्तराष्ट्रस्य वाहिनीम्॥
en: These parties and of their respective numbers have I seen come there, who will fight with the army of Dhritarashtra, on behalf of the sons of Pandu. son

sn: यो वेद मानुषं व्यूहं दैवं गान्धर्वमासुरम्। स तत्र सेनाप्रमुखे धृष्टद्युम्नो महारथः॥
en: He, who is acquainted with the human system of fight, is celestial and is followed by the Gandharvas and by the Asuras that great car-warrior, Dhrishtadyumna, is at the head of that army.

sn: भीष्मः शान्तनवो राजन् भागः क्लृप्तः शिखण्डिनः। तं विराटोऽनुसंयाता सार्धं मत्स्यैः प्रहारिभिः॥
en: Bhishma, the son of Shantanu, O king, has been reserved as the share of Shikhandin. Virata will help him (the latter) along with the soldiers from Matsya.

sn: ज्येष्ठस्य पाण्डुपुत्रस्य भागो मद्राधिपो बली। तौ तु तत्राब्रुवन् केचिद् विषमौ नो मताविति॥
en: The ruler of the Madras, endued with strength, has been reserved as the share of the eldest son of Pandu, through somebody in their party said that he was of opinion that the two did match very well.

sn: दुर्योधनः सहसुतः सार्धं भ्रातृशतेन च। प्राच्याश्च दाक्षिणात्याश्च भीमसेनस्य भागतः॥
en: Duryodhana with his son and his hundred brothers and the soldiers coming from the castern and southern countries have fallen to the share of Bhimasena.

sn: अर्जुनस्य तु भागेन कर्णो वैकर्तनो मतः। अश्वत्थामा विकर्णश्च सैन्धवश्च जयद्रथः॥
en: Arjuna has for his share Karna the son of Vikartana, Ashvathaman, Vikarna and the king of Sindhu Jayadratha.

sn: अशक्याश्चैव ये केचिद् पृथिव्यां शूरमानिनः। सर्वांस्तानर्जुनः पार्थः कल्पयामास भागतः॥
en: Whoever there is in this world who boasts that he is invincible. Arjuna, the son Pritha, has accepted all of them also as his share.

sn: महेष्वासा राजपुत्रा भ्रातरः पञ्च केकयाः। केकयानेव भागेन कृत्वा योत्स्यन्ति संयुगे॥
en: The great bowmen, the five Kaikeya princes, brothers to one another, taking the Kaikeya warriors (on the Kurus side) for his share, will fight in the battle. same sons

sn: तेषामेव कृतो भागो मालवाः शाल्वकास्तथा। त्रिगर्तानां चैव मुख्यौ यौ तौ संशप्तकाविति॥
en: In their share have also fallen the Malavas, the Shalvakas and the two foremost of the Trigartas, who have resolved to win or to die.

sn: दुर्योधनसुताः सर्वे तथा दुःशासनस्य च। सौभद्रेण कृतो भागो राजा चैव बृहद्बलः॥
en: In the way all the sons of Duryodhana and Dushasana have been accepted by the son of Subhadra as his share, as also the king Brihadbala.

sn: द्रौपदेया महेष्वासाः सुवर्णविकृतध्वजाः। धृष्टद्युम्नमुखा द्रोणमभियास्यन्ति भारत।॥
en: The mighty bowmen, the of Draupadi, having their flag ornamented with gold, with Dhrishtadyumna at their head, will fight with Drona, O Bharata.

sn: चेकितान: सोमदत्तं द्वैरथे योद्धमिच्छति। भोजं तु कृतवर्माणं युयुधानो युयुत्सति॥
en: Chekitana desires to fight with Somadatta in single combat, each seated on his own car; and Yuyudhana is desirous of fighting against Kritavarma of the Bhoja tribe.

sn: सहदेवस्तु माद्रेयः शूरः संक्रन्दनो युधि। स्वमंशं कल्पयामास श्यालं ते सुबलात्मजम्॥
en: The son of Madri, the hero Sahadeva, who makes loud roars in battle, has accepted as his own share your brother the son of Subala.

sn: उलूकं चैव कैतव्यं ये च सारस्वता गणाः। नकुलः कल्पयामास भागं माद्रवतीसुतः॥
en: Uluka, the deceitful one and hordes of Sarasvata tribes have been accepted by Nakula, the son of Madravati; as his own share.

sn: ये चान्ये पार्थिवा राजन् प्रत्युद्यास्यन्ति सङ्गरे। समाह्वानेन तांश्चापि पाण्डुपुत्रा अकल्पयन्॥
en: The other rulers, too, Oking, who will fight in the battle, have been assigned to the share of some one on their side by the sons of Pandu.

sn: एवमेषामनीकानि प्रविभक्तानि भागशः। यते ते कार्य सपुत्रस्य क्रियतां तदकालिकम्॥
en: In this way has this army been divided into batches. Do whatever is to be done by you, along with your son, speedily.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच न सन्ति सर्वे पुत्रा मे मूढा दु तदेविनः। येषां युद्धं बलवता भीमेन रणमूर्धनि॥
en: Dhritarashtra said All my foolish sons, those addicted to the wicked dice who have taken it in their hand to fight with the powerful Bhima, have ceased to exist already.

sn: राजानः पार्थिवाः सर्वे प्रोक्षिताः कालधर्मणा। गाण्डीवाग्नि प्रवेक्ष्यन्ति पतङ्गा इव पावकम्॥
en: The kings and the rulers, too, all consecrated by the king of death himself shall enter the Gandiva bow as moths fall on fire.

sn: विद्रुतां वाहिनीं मन्ये कृतवैरैर्महात्मभिः। तां रणे केऽनुयास्यन्ति प्रभग्नां पाण्डवैर्युधि॥
en: I see in my mind my army already routed by these large minded ones, whom I converted into enemies, who will follow them to battle, who have been routed by the Pandavas in fight.

sn: सर्वे ह्यतिरथाः शूराः कीर्तिमन्तः प्रतापिनः। सूर्यपावकयोस्तुल्यास्तेजसा समितिञ्जयाः॥
en: All of them are extremely good carwarriors, heroes, famous and powerful having might like that of the sun or fire and victorious in battle.

sn: येषां युधिष्ठिरो नेता गोप्ता च मधुसूदनः। योधौ च पाण्डवौ वीरौ सव्यसाचिवृकोदरौ॥ नकुलः सहदेवश्च धृष्टद्युम्नश्च पार्षतः। सात्यकिर्दुपदश्चैव धृष्टकेतुश्च सानुजः॥ उत्तमौजाश्च पाञ्चाल्यो युधामन्युश्च दुर्जयः। शिखण्डी क्षत्रदेवश्च तथा वैराटिरुत्तरः॥ काशयश्चेदयश्चैव मत्स्याः सर्वे च सुंजयाः। विराटपुत्रो बभ्रुश्च पञ्चालाश्च प्रभद्रकाः॥ येषामिन्द्रोऽप्यकामानां न हरेत् पृथिवीमिमाम्। वीराणां रणधीराणां ये भिन्द्युः पर्वतानपि॥ तान् सर्वगुणसम्पन्नानमनुष्यप्रतापिनः। क्रोशतो मम दुष्पुत्रो योद्भुमिच्छति संजय॥
en: son Those whose leader is Yudhishthira and whose protector is the slayer of Madhu and whose warriors are the heroic sons of Pandu, Savyasachin and Vrikodara and Nakula, Sahadeva, Dhrishtadyumna, the of Prishata, Satyki, Drupada, with his brother and the king of the Panchalas, endued with excellent prowess and the invincible Yudhamanyu and Shikhandin and Kshatradeva and Uttra and the son Virata and the Kashis, the Chedis, the Matsyas and all the Srinjayas, the son of Virata, Babhru, the Panchalas and the Prabhadrakas. From these even Indra himself cannot wrest this Earth, if they are not so willing-the heroes, who are cool and composed in battle and who are capable even of breaking the mountains, my wicked son desires to fight, O Sanjaya-these endued with all the virtues and endued with superhuman strength, disregard me me who am loudly protesting.

sn: दुर्योधन उवाच उभौ स्व एकजातीयौ तथोभौ भूमिगोचरौ। अथ कस्मात् पाण्डवानामेकतो मन्यसे जयम्॥
en: Duryodhana said Both the parties are of the same race and both roam about on the earth; why then do you regard victory as coming solely to the Pandavas.

sn: पितामहं च द्रोणं च कृपं कर्णं च दुर्जयम्। जयद्रथं सोमदत्तमश्वत्थामानमेव च।॥ सुतेजसो महेष्वासानिन्द्रोऽपि सहितोऽमरैः। अशक्तः समरे जेतुं किं पुनस्तात पाण्डवाः॥
en: Our grandfather Bhishma, Drona, Kripa and Karna hard to be vanquished, Jayadratha, Somadatta and Ashvathama, Indra even, united with the gods, is incapable of defeating these great bowmen endued with great energy in battle. How can the Pandavas do it, O sire.

sn: सर्वे च पृथिवीपाला मदर्थं तात पाण्डवान्। आर्याः शस्त्रभृतः शूराः समर्थाः प्रतिबाधितुम्॥
en: All the rulers of the earth, too, leading honourable lives, the heroes capable of wielding weapons can for my sake, O sire, oppose the Pandavas.

sn: न मामकान् पाण्डवास्ते समर्थाः प्रतिवीक्षितुम्। पराक्रान्तो ह्यहं पाण्डून् सपुत्रान् योद्धमोहवे॥
en: These Pandavas are not even able to gaze on my soldiers. I am sufficiently powerful to challenge the Pandus with their sons to fight.

sn: मप्रियं पार्थिवाः सर्वे ये चिकीर्षन्ति भारत। ते तानावारयिष्यन्ति ऐणेयानिव तन्तुना॥
en: Those rulers of the earth, who wish me well, O Bharata, will get hold of them, as deer are caught by means of a trap.

sn: महता रथवंशेन शरजालैश्च मामकैः। अभिद्रुता भविष्यन्ति पाञ्चालाः पाण्डवैः सह॥
en: By means of our large number of cars and our net of arrows, the Panchalas along with the Pandavas will be vanquished.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच उन्मत्त इव मे पुत्रो विलपत्येष संजय। न हि शक्तो रणे जेतुं धर्मराज युधिष्ठिरम्॥
en: Dhritarashtra said My son raves like a maniac, O Sanjaya; he is not capable of defeating in battle Yudhishthira the king of Dharma.

sn: जानाति हि यथा भीष्मः पाण्डवानां यशस्विनाम्। बलवत्तां सपुत्राणां धर्मज्ञानां महात्मनाम्॥
en: Bhishma knows the truth of the sons of Pandu and their sons of great fame and prowess, conversant with the code of morality and having large minds.

sn: यतो नारोचयदयं विग्रहं तैर्महात्मभिः। किं तु संजय मे ब्रूहि पुनस्तेषां विचेष्टितम्॥
en: Since he does not desire fight with those ones of great soul; but, O Sanjaya, tell me again of their doings.

sn: कस्तांस्तरस्विनो भूयः संदीपयति पाण्डवान्। अर्चिष्मतो महेष्वासान् हविषा पावकानिव॥
en: Who among them are endued with activity and who are inciting the Pandavas. These great bowinen are like those pouring clarified butter on fire.

sn: संजय उवाच धृष्टद्युम्नः सदैवैतान् संदीपयति भारत। युद्ध्यध्वमिति मा भैष्ट युद्धाद् भरतसत्तमाः॥
en: Sanjaya said Dhritarashtra is ever inciting them, O Bharata, saying, “Fight and do not fear a fight, you best among the race of Bharata.

sn: ये केचित् पार्थिवास्तत्र धार्तराष्ट्रेण संवृताः। युद्धे समागमिष्यन्ति तुमुले शस्त्रसंकुले॥
en: The few rulers of the earth, who are surrounded by the sons of Dhritarashtra, will engage in fierce fight with marks of numberless weapons on their bodies.

sn: तान् सर्वानाहवे क्रुद्धान् सानुबन्धान् समागतान्। अहमेकः समादास्ये तिमिर्मत्स्यानिवौदकात्॥
en: All these wrathful kings who have assembled on the other side, with their friends and followers, I alone will capture like a big fish, seizing small ones from the water.

sn: भीष्मं द्रोणं कृपं कर्णं द्रौणि शल्यं सुयोधनम्। एतांश्चापि निरोत्स्यामि वेलेव मकरालयम्॥
en: Bhishma, Drona, Kripa, Karna, the son of Drona, Shalya and Suyodhana-these I will opposed like the shore, resisting the flow of the swelling waters.

sn: तथा ब्रुवन्तं धर्मात्मा प्राह राजा युधिष्ठिरः। तव धैर्यं च वीर्यं पाञ्चालाः पाण्डवैः सह॥
en: King Yudhishthira of a virtuous soul said to him who was thus speaking-'The Panchalas along with the Pandavas all depend on your wisdom and prowess.

sn: सर्वे समधिरूढाः स्म संग्रामानः समुद्धर। जानामि त्वां महाबाहो क्षत्रधर्मे व्यवस्थितम्॥
en: Rescue us from this fight; I am aware that you, O you with long arms, are established on the virtue of a Kshatriya.

sn: समर्थमेकं पर्याप्तं कौरवाणां विनिग्रहे। पुरस्तादुपयातानां कौरवाणां युयुत्सताम्॥
en: Alone you are quite capable of effecting the overthrow of the Kauravas. To meet the Kauravas, desirous of war and standing in front of us.

sn: स त्वं भवता यद् विधातव्यं तन्नः श्रेयः परंतप। संग्रामादपयातानां भग्नानां शरणैषिणाम्॥
en: What ever will be decided on by you will conduce to our good, O subduer of foes, why those fly from the field of battle out of the original army and are at our mercy.

sn: पौरुषं दर्शयशूरो यस्तिष्ठेदग्रतः पुमान्। क्रीणीयात् तं सहस्रेण इति नीतिमतां मतम्॥
en: The hero, who after showing forth his strength himself helps such men (those flying, referred to in the last Sloka), is worth purchasing for a thousand. Such is the opinion of those who are conversant with the code of morality.

sn: शूरच वीरश्च विक्रान्तश्च नरर्षभ। भयार्तानां परित्राता संयुगेषु न संशयः॥
en: O you bull among men, you are just such a hero, brave and powerful. There is no doubt that in battle you are the rescuer of those struck with fear.

sn: एवं ब्रुवति कौन्तेये धर्मात्मनि युधिष्ठिरे। धृष्टद्युम्न उवाचेदं मां वचो गतसाध्वसम्। सर्वाञ्जनपदान् सूत योधा दुर्योधनस्य ये॥ सबाह्निकान् कुरून् ब्रूयाः प्रातिपेयाशरद्वतः। सूतपुत्रं तथा द्रोणं सहपुत्रं जयद्रथम्॥ दुःशासनं विकर्णं च तथा दुर्योधनं नृपम्। भीष्मं च ब्रूहि त्वमाशु गच्छ च मा चिरम्॥
en: The son of Kunti, Yudhishthira, of virtuous soul having said this Dhrishtadyumna without the least fear said these words to me-O Suta, all the men that have come to fight for Duryodhana, tell them and the Kurus who have descended from the Pratipas with the Bahlika's, son of Sharadvata and Drona with his son, as also Jayadratha with his son and Dushasana and Vikarna and also the king Duryodhana and Bhima-go to them and tell them go just now, without delay.

sn: युधिष्ठिरः साधुनैवाभ्युपेयो मा वो वधीदर्जुनो देवगुप्तः। राज्यं दद्ध्वं धर्मराजस्य तूर्णं याचध्वं वै पाण्डवं लोकवीरम्॥
en: Yudhishthira should be approached by an honourable man, let not Arjuna, protected by the gods, kill you and the king of virtue the son of Pandu-that hero among men should be forthwith asked to accept the kingdom surrender to him.

sn: नैतादृशो हि योधोऽस्ति पृथिव्यामिह कश्चन। यथाविधः सव्यसाची पाण्डवः सत्यविक्रमः॥
en: There is no warrior in this world as the son of Pandu, Savyasachin of true strength.

sn: देवैर्हि सम्भृतो दिव्यो रथो गाण्डीवधन्वनः। न स जेयो मनुष्येण मा स्म कृदूध्वं मनो युधि॥
en: By the gobs themselves in the heavenly car of the wielder of the Gandiva bow protected; he cannot be defeated by men; do not think in mind even of a fight with him.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच क्षत्रतेजा ब्रह्मचारी कौमारादपि पाण्डवः। तेन संयुगमेष्यन्ति मन्दा विलपतो मम॥
en: Dhritarashtra said The son of Pandu, from his youth, has the prowess of a Kshatriya and leads the life of a Brahmachari. Those fools desire to fight with him, thought I am lamenting.

sn: दुर्योधन निवर्तस्व युद्धाद् भरतसत्तम। न हि युद्धं प्रशंसन्ति सर्वावस्थमरिंदम॥
en: O Duryodhana, O you best among the race of Bharata, turn your mind away from fight; war is not desirable under all conditions, O you subduer of enemies.

sn: अलमर्धं पृथिव्यास्ते सहामात्यस्य जीवितुम्। प्रयच्छ पाण्डुपुत्राणां यथोचितमरिंदम॥
