en: One half of the earth is sufficient for the livelihood of yourself and your ministers. Give back to the sons of Pandu their dues, O you subduer of enemies.

sn: एतद्धि कुरवः सर्वे मन्यन्ते धर्मसंहितम्। यत् त्वं प्रशान्ति मन्येथाः पाण्डुपुत्रैर्महात्मभिः॥
en: All the Kurus think this to be in accordance with virtue that you should conclude peace with the high-souled sons of Pandu.

sn: अङ्गेमां समवेक्षस्व पुत्र स्वामेव वाहिनीम्। जात एष तवाभावस्त्वं तु मोहान बुध्यसे॥
en: Think well, O son, of the elements of your own army; it has been collected for your own death; you do not accept this out of folly.

sn: न त्वहं युद्धमिच्छामि नैतदिच्छति बाह्निकः। न च भीष्मो न च द्रोणो नाश्वत्थामा न संजयः॥ न सोमदत्तो न शलो न कृपो युद्धमिच्छति। सत्यव्रतः पुरुमित्रो जयो भूरिश्रवास्तथा॥
en: I do not wish war; nor is Balhika desirous of it; nor is Bhishma; nor is Drona, nor is Ashvathama; nor is Sanjaya nor Somadatta, nor Shala, nor Kripa desire war; nor does Satyavrata, nor Purumitra, nor Jaya, nor Bhurishravas.

sn: येषु सम्प्रतितिष्ठेयुः कुरवः पीडिताः परैः। ते युद्धं नाभिनन्दन्ति तत् तुभ्यं तातरोचताम्॥
en: Those on whom depend the Kurus, when troubled by the enemy not rejoice at the prospect of war; O dear, may you accept that.

sn: न त्वं करोषि कामेन कर्णः कारयिता तव। दुःशासनश्च पापात्मा शकुनिश्चापि सौबलः॥
en: You do not act in this way of your own will; but Karna leads you to it and Dushasana and the wicked-souled Shakuni and the son of Subala (lead you).

sn: दुर्योधन उवाच नाह भवति न द्रोणे नाश्वत्थाम्नि न संजये। न भीष्मे न च काम्बोजे न कृपे न च बाह्निके॥ सत्यव्रते पुरुमित्रे भूरिश्रवसि वा पुनः। अन्येषु वा तावकेषु भारं कृत्वा समाह्वयम्॥
en: Duryodhana said I do not depend on Drona or Ashvathama or Sanjaya or Bhishma or Kamboja or Kripa or Balhika or Satyavrata or Purumitra or on Bhurishravas, nor do I challenge them to fight, depending on others.

sn: अहं च तात कर्णश्च रणयज्ञं वितत्य वै। युधिष्ठिरं पशुं कृत्वा दीक्षितौ भरतर्षभ॥
en: O Sire, I and Karna will perform the sacrifice of war after preparing ourselves, making Yudhishthira the beast for sacrifice.

sn: रथो वेदी स्रुवः खङ्गो गदा सुकू कवचं सदः। चातुर्होत्रं च धुर्या मे शरा दर्भा हविर्यशः॥
en: In the ceremony my car will be the substitute for the platform; my scimitar, the ladle; my mace, the large ladle; and my coat of mail, the witnesses; my horses will answer the purpose of the four priests; my rafts will stand for the Kusha grass; and my fame, for the clarified butter.

sn: आत्मयज्ञेन नृपते इष्ट्वा वैवस्वतं रणे। विजित्य च समेष्यावो हतामित्रौ श्रिया वृतौ॥
en: Having performed, O king, this sacrifice in the field of battle, in honour of the God of death, by ourselves and having won a victory and slain our enemies, we shall come back surrounded by a halo of glory.

sn: अहं च तात कर्णश्च भ्राता दुःशासनश्च मे। एते वयं हनिष्यामः पाण्डवान् समरे त्रयः॥
en: Myself, O Sire, Karna and my brother Dushasana, these three of us will kill the sons of Pandu in battle.

sn: अहं हि पाण्डवान् हत्वा प्रशास्ता पृथिवीमिमाम्। मां वा हत्वा पाण्डुपुत्रा भोक्तारः पृथिवीमिमाम्॥
en: Either I shall rule this earth, having slain the sons of Pandu; or the sons of Pandu will enjoy sovereignty over this earth after having slain me.

sn: त्यक्तं मे जीवितं राज्यं धनं सर्वं च पार्थिव। न जातु पाण्डवैः सार्धं वसेयमहमच्युत॥
en: I can sacrifice my life, my kingdom, my wealth, my everything, O king; but I cannot live in peace with the sons of Pandu, O you of unfading renown.

sn: यावद्धि सूच्यास्तीक्ष्णाया विध्येदग्रेण मारिष। तावदप्यपरित्याज्यं भूमेनः पाण्डवान् प्रति॥
en: That extent of land which is pierced by the extremity of a sharp needle, O venerable Sire, I shall not surrender to the sons of Pandu.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच सर्वान् वस्तात शोचामि त्यक्तो दुर्योधनो मया। ये मन्दमनुयास्यध्वं यान्तं वैवस्वतक्षयम्॥
en: Dhritarashtra said I grieve for you all, O rulers, who are following that fool to the abode of the king of death; but Duryodhana is cast off by me forever.

sn: रुरूणामिव यूथेषु व्याघ्राः प्रहरतां वराः। वरान् वरान् हनिष्यन्ति समेता युधि पाण्डवाः॥
en: Like tigers in a herd of deer these foremost of strikers, those Pandavas assembled together will kill the principal warriors in battle.

sn: प्रतीपमिव मे भाति युयुधानेन भारती। व्यस्ता सीमन्तिनी ग्रस्ता प्रमृष्टा दीर्घबाहुना॥
en: The army of the Bharatas appears to me as already fallen down like a woman troubled and afflicted and struck by one of the long arms.

sn: सम्पूर्णं पूरयन् भूयो धनं पार्थस्य माधवः। शैनेयः समरे स्थाता बीजवत् प्रवपशरान्॥
en: Increasing in strength, what was already full, viz., Yudhishthira's army the son of Shini will stand on the field shooting arrows as one sows the seeds.

sn: सेनामुखे प्रयुद्धानां भीमसेनो भविष्यति। तं सर्वे संश्रयिष्यन्ति प्राकारमकुतोभयम्॥
en: In front of the fighting soldiers Bhimasena will stand and all will be shatered behind him as behind a strong wall, fearlessly.

sn: यदा द्रक्ष्यसि भीमेन कुञ्जरान् विनिपातितान्। विशीर्णदन्तान् गिर्याभान् भिन्नकुम्भान् सशोणितान्।।
en: When you will see your elephants, big as mountains, felled down by Bhima with their tusks broken and with blood flowing resembling a broken pot (with water flowing).

sn: तानभिप्रेक्ष्य संग्रामे विशीर्णानिव पर्वतान्। भीतो भीमस्य संस्पर्शात् स्मर्ताऽसि वचनस्य मे॥
en: Beholding them in the field of battle like mountains separated and struck with fear by coming in contract with Bhima, then will you remember my words.

sn: निर्दग्धं भीमसेनेन सैन्यं रथहयद्विपम्। गतिमग्नेरिव प्रेक्ष्य स्मर्ताऽसि वचनस्य मे॥
en: Beholding your army composed of chariot, horses and elephants burnt up as it were by Bhimasena like the path followed by a fire, will you remember my words.

sn: महद् वो भयमागामि न चेच्छाम्यथ पाण्डवैः। गदया भीमसेनेन हताः शममुपैष्यथ॥
en: A heavy calamity will you meet, if you do not conclude peace with the Pandavas. Killed by Bhimasena with his mace, will you ever remain in peace.

sn: महावनमिवच्छिन्नं यदा द्रक्ष्यसि पातितम्। बलं कुरूणां भीमेन तदा स्मर्ताऽसि मे वचः॥
en: When you will see the army of the Kurus, felled down by Bhima like a large forest torn off, then will you remember my words.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एतावदुक्त्वा राजा तु सर्वांस्तान् पृथिवीपतीन्। अनुभाष्य महाराज पुनः पप्रच्छ संजयम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having said this to all those rulers of the earth, the king, O great king, addressing Sanjaya asked him.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच यदबूतां महात्मानौ वासुदेवधनंजयौ। तन्मे ब्रूहि महाप्राज्ञ शुश्रूषे वचनं तव॥
en: Dhritarashtra said What the two great-souled ones, the son of Vasudeva and Dhananjaya, said? Tell me that, O exceedingly wise one. I shall hear your words.

sn: संजय उवाच शृणु राजन् यथा दृष्टौ मया कृष्णधनंजयौ। ऊचतुश्चापि यद् वीरौ तत् ते वक्ष्यामि भारत॥
en: Sanjaya said Listen, O king, how the two, Krishna and Dhananjaya, were seen by me and what the two heroes said. I shall tell you, O Bharata.

sn: पादाङ्गुलीरभिप्रेक्षन् प्रयतोऽहं कृताञ्जलिः। शुद्धान्तं प्राविशं राजन्नाख्यातुं नरदेवयोः॥
en: Looking towards my toes and with my hands clasped together and thinking of holy things in my mind, did I enter the inner apartments to meet with those gods among men.

sn: नैवाभिमन्युर्न यमौ तं देशमभियान्ति वै। यत्र कृष्णौ च कृष्णा च सत्यभामा च भामिनी॥
en: Neither Abhimanyu nor the twins can go to the place where the two Krishna and Krishna (Draupadi) and the lady Satyabhama reside.

sn: उभौ मध्वासवक्षीबावुभौ चन्दनरूषितौ। स्रग्विणौ वरवस्त्रौ तौ दिव्याभरणभूषितौ॥
en: The two were there, cheerful with a drink of the Madri wine; and both had their bodies smeared with sandal; and both also were dressed in excellent attires and wore beautiful ornaments.

sn: नैकरत्नविचित्रं तु काञ्चनं महदासनम्। विविधास्तरणाकीर्णं यत्रासातामरिंदमौ॥
en: The two subduer of enemies were seated there on a spacious seat of gold covered with many sorts of carpets.

sn: अर्जुनोत्सङ्गगौ पादौ केशवस्योपलक्षये। अर्जुनस्य च कृष्णायां सत्यायां च महात्मनः॥
en: On the lap of Arjuna were the feet of Keshava and those of the noble-minded Arjuna rested on Krishna and Satyabhama.

sn: काञ्चनं पादपीठं तु पार्थो मे प्रादिशत् तदा। तदहं पाणिना स्पृष्ट्वा ततो भूमावुपाविशम्॥
en: A seat made of gold did the son of Pritha point out to me; after touching which with my hands, I took my seat on the ground.

sn: ऊर्ध्वरेखातलौ पादौ पार्थस्य शुभलक्षणौ। पादपीठादपहतौ तत्रापश्यमहं शुभौ॥
en: Two longitudinal lines on the soles of the son of Pritha, the auspicious marks, did I see on his taking away his feet from the seat.

sn: श्यामौ बृहन्तौ तरुणौ शालस्कन्धाविवोद्गतौ। एकासनगतौ दृष्ट्वा भयं मां महदाविशत्॥
en: Having seen the two young men of black complexion and large stature rising like the trunks of Shala trees, seated on the same seat, a great fear seized me.

sn: इन्द्रविष्णुसमावेतौ मन्दात्मा नावबुद्ध्यते। संश्रयाद् द्रोणभीष्माभ्यां कर्णस्य च विकत्थनात्॥
en: They were like Indra and Vishnu seated together. That one of foolish intellect does not understand that owing to his belief in the power of Drona and Bhishma.

sn: निदेशस्थाविमौ यस्य मानसस्तस्य सेत्स्यते। संकल्पो धर्मराजस्य निश्चयो मे तदाभवत्॥
en: The wishes of him who had under his command these two, the desires of the king of virtue were bound to bear fruit such was my belief at the time.

sn: सत्कृतश्चान्नपानाभ्यामासीनो लब्धसक्रियः। अञ्जलिं मूर्ध्नि संधाय तौ संदेशमचोदयम्॥
en: Entertained with food and drink and having my wishes (of beholding the two) gratified, I placed my clasped hands on my head and conveyed to them your message.

sn: धनुर्गुणकिणाङ्केन पाणिना शुभलक्षणम्। पादमानमयन् पार्थः केशवं समचोदयत्॥
en: With his hands, having auspicious signs and marks made by friction with the bow and string, the son of Pritha removing the feet of Keshava asked him to give a suitable reply.

sn: इन्द्रकेतुरिवोत्थाय सर्वाभरणभूषितः। इन्द्रवीर्योपमः कृष्णः संविष्टो माभ्यभाषत॥ वाचं स वदतां श्रेष्ठो ह्लादिनीं वचनक्षमाम्। त्रासिनीं धार्तराष्ट्राणां मृदुपूर्वां सुदारुणाम्॥
en: Then did Krishna of prowess similar to Indra's and adorned with all sorts of ornaments and rising like the banner of Indra speak addressing me, the words of that foremost of the speakers were mild, charming and conciliatory but were awful and calculated to cause fear in the sons of Dhritarashtra.

sn: वाचं तां वचनार्हस्य शिक्षाक्षरसमन्विताम्। अश्रौषमहमिष्टार्था पश्चाद्धृदयहारिणीम्॥
en: I then heard the words of that one who is fit to speak, which were rhythmical and calculated to lead to the good of all, though heart-rending in the end.

sn: वासुदेव उवाच संजयेदं वचो ब्रूया धृतराष्ट्र मनीषिणम्। कुरुमुख्यस्य भीष्मस्य द्रोणस्यापि च शृण्वतः॥
en: The son of Vasudeva said O Sanjaya, speak these words to the intelligent Dhritarashtra in the hearing of the foremost of Kurus, Bhishma and Drona.

sn: आवयोर्वचनात् सूत ज्येष्ठानप्यभिवादयन्। यवीयसश्च कुशलं पश्चात् पृष्ट्वैवमुत्तरम्॥
en: Before repeating our answer, O Suta, convey our respects to our elders in age and then asking about the health of our younger,

sn: यजध्वं विविधैर्यज्ञैविप्रेभ्यो दत्त दक्षिणाः। पुत्रैर्दारैश्च मोदध्वं महद् वो भयमागतम्॥
en: Perform many sorts of sacrificial ceremonies and make many presents to the Brahmanas and make merry with your sons and wives; for a heavy calamity is come on you.

sn: अर्थांस्त्यजत पात्रेभ्युः सुतान् प्राप्नुत कामजान्। प्रियं प्रियेभ्यश्चरत राजा हि त्वरते जये॥
en: Distribute wealth among proper recipients; get desirable sons and serve those that are dear to you by doing them good; for the king is anxious for victory.

sn: ऋणमेतत् प्रवृद्धं मे हृदयानापसर्पति। यद् गोविन्देति चुक्रोश कृष्णा मां दूरवासिनम्॥
en: That old debt has not yet been wiped off from my mind (for I have not paid it), that is the invocation of me living at a distance by Krishna saying "Govinda".

sn: तेजोमयं दुराधर्षं गाण्डीवं यस्य कार्मुकम्। मद्वितीयेन तेनेह वैरं वः सव्यसाचिना॥
en: Him whose weapon is the invisible Gandiva bow, full of energy and him who has me for his second-of such Savyasachin have you made enemy.

sn: मद्वितीयं पुनः पार्थं कः प्रार्थयितुमिच्छति। यो न कालपरीतो वाप्यपि साक्षात् पुरंदरः॥
en: Who would like to challenge the son of Pritha, having me for his second, unless his time were come, even if he were Purandara himself?

sn: बाहुभ्यामुद्वहेद् भूमि दहेत् क्रुद्ध इमाः प्रजाः। पातयेत् त्रिदिवाद् देवान् योऽर्जुनं समरे जयेत्॥
en: He who defeats Arjuna in battle bears the earth in his two arms; and when wrathful, he could burn up all creatures and could make the gods fall off from heaven.

sn: देवासुरमनुष्येषु यक्षगन्धर्वभोगिषु। न तं पश्याम्यहं युद्धे पाण्डवं योऽभ्ययाद् रणे॥
en: Among the gods, the Asuras and the human beings and among Yakshas, Gandharvas and Bhogis do I not see him, who could stand against (Arjuna), the son of Pandu, in battle.

sn: यत् तद् विराटनगरे श्रुयते महदद्भुतम्। एकस्य च बहूनां च पर्याप्तं तन्निदर्शनम्॥
en: The greatly wonderful event, which is heard to have taken place in the city of Virata of a fight of one against many, is a sufficient proof of this.

sn: एकेन पाण्डुपुत्रेण विराटनगरे यदा। भग्नाः पलायत दिशः पर्याप्तं तन्निदर्शनम्॥
en: When in the city of Virata you fled in all directions, dispersed by the son of Pandu alone that is sufficient proof of this.

sn: बलं वीर्यं च तेजश्च शीघ्रता लघुहस्तता। अविषादश्च धैर्यं च पार्थान्नान्यत्र विद्यते॥
en: Strength, heroism, prowess, agility, lightness of hand, untiring energy and patience are centered in the son of Pritha and are not present anywhere else.

sn: इत्यब्रवीद्धृषीकेशः पार्थमुद्धर्षयन् गिरा। गर्जन् समयवर्षीव गगने पाकशासनः॥
en: Thus spoke Hrishikesha cheering the spirits of the son of Pritha by his voice and roaring like the instrument which chastised Paka (thunder) in the sky during the rainy season.

sn: केशवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा किरीटी श्वेतवाहनः। अर्जुनस्तन्महद् वाक्यमब्रवीद् रोमहर्षणम्॥
en: Having heard the words of Keshava, Kiritin of white steeds, Arjuna spoke significant words calculated to make the hairs erect.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच संजयस्य वचः श्रुत्वा प्रज्ञाचक्षुर्जनेश्वरः। ततः संख्यातुमारेभे तद्वचो गुणदोषतः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Hearing the words of Sanjaya, then that lord of men having eyes of wisdom then commenced to count the merits and defects of that speech.

sn: प्रसंख्याय च सौक्ष्म्येण गुणदोषान् विचक्षणः। यथावन्मतितत्त्वेन जयकामः सुतान् प्रति॥ बलाबलं विनिश्चित्य याथातथ्येन बुद्धिमान्। शक्ति संख्यातुमारेभे तदा वै मनुजाधिपः॥
en: Having skillfully counted the merits and defeats as far as in his power that wise and intelligent king of men, desirous of victory for his sons and having ascertained the strength and weakness of both parties by suitable means, commanded counting the army of each.

sn: देवमानुषयोः शक्त्या तेजसा चैव पाण्डवान्। कुरून् शक्त्याल्पतरया दुर्योधनमथाब्रवीत्॥
en: And having concluded that the Pandavas had strength and prowess, both human and divine on, their side and that the Kurus were weaker in strength, he said to Duryodhana!

sn: दुर्योधनेयं चिन्ता मे शश्वन्न व्युपशाम्यति। सत्यं ह्येतदहं मन्ये प्रत्यक्षं नानुमानतः॥
en: O Duryodhana, this thought never leaves my mind; it is very true that I see with my own eyes and do not infer it from my imagination.

sn: आत्मजेषु पुरं स्नेहं सर्वभूतानि कुर्वते। प्रियाणि चैषां कुर्वन्ति यथाशक्ति हितानि च॥
en: All creatures have excessive affection for their offsprings; and they also do what is agreeable to the latter to the best of their power and also what leads to their good.

sn: एवमेवोपकर्तृणां प्रायशो लक्षयामहे। इच्छान्ति बहुलं सन्तः प्रतिकर्तुं महत् प्रियम्॥
en: The same is also seen in benefactors generally. Good men always have a great inclination to repay the great good done them and to do what is highly agreeable to their benefactors.

sn: अग्निः साचिव्यकर्ता स्यात् खाण्डवे तत्कृतं स्मरन्। अर्जुनस्यापि भीमेऽस्मिनं कुरुपाण्डुसमागमे॥
en: Agni, recollecting the doings of Arjuna at Khandava, will help him and Bhima in this vas.

sn: जातिगृद्ध्याभिपन्नाश्च पाण्डवानामनेकशः। धर्मादयः समेष्यन्ति समाहूता दिवौकसः॥
en: Out of affection for those born of them Dharma and many other dwellers of the heaven will, when invoked, come on the side of the Pandavas.

sn: भीष्मद्रोणकृपादीनां भयादशनिसंनिभम्। रिरक्षिषन्तः संरम्भं गमिष्यन्तीति मे मतिः॥
en: Desirous of protecting them from the fear of Bhishma, Drona, Kripa and others they will be filled with wrath equal to the thunderbolt (in its effects).

sn: ते देवैः सहिताः पार्था न शक्याः प्रतिवीक्षितुम्। मानुषेण नरव्याघ्रा वीर्यवन्तोऽस्त्रपारगाः॥
en: The sons of Pritha, those heroic tigers among men, capable of using the weapons, united with the gods, will be incapable of being even gazed at by a human being.

sn: दुरासदं यस्य दिव्यं गाण्डीवं धनुरुत्तमम्। वारुणौ चाक्षयौ दिव्यौ शरपूर्णी महेषुधी॥ वानस्श्च ध्वजो दिव्यो निःसङ्गो धूमवद्गतिः। रथश्च चतुरन्तायां यस्य नास्ति समः क्षितौ।॥ महामेघनिभश्चापि निर्घोषः श्रूयते जनैः। महाशनिसमः शब्दः शात्रवाणां भयंकरः॥ यं चातिमानुषं वीर्ये कृत्स्नो लोको व्यवस्यति। देवानामपि जेतारं यं विदुः पार्थिवा रणे॥ शतानि पञ्च चैवेषून् यो गृह्णन् नैव दृश्यते। निमेषान्तरमात्रेण मुञ्चन् दूरं च पातयन्॥ यमाह भीष्मो द्रोणश्च कृपो द्रौणिस्तथैव च। मद्रराजस्तथा शल्यो मध्यस्था ये च मानवाः॥ युद्धायावस्थितं पार्थं पार्थिवैरतिमानुषैः। अशक्यं नरशार्दूलं पराजेतुमरिंदमम्॥ क्षिपत्येकेन वेगेन पञ्च बाणशतानि यः। सदृशं बाहुवीर्येण कार्तवीर्यस्य पाण्डवम्॥ तमर्जुनं महेष्वासं महेन्द्रोपेन्द्रविक्रमम्। निघ्नन्तमिव पश्यामि विमर्देऽस्मिन् महाहवे॥
en: He who has the excellent and invincible Gandiva bow and two inexhaustible arrow holders of heavenly make and always filled with shafts, he who has the figure of a monkey on his heavenly banner which can proceed as smoothly as a column of smoke and whose car has no equal in the earth, bounded by the four seas and the sound of which is heard by men, similar to the roaring of a large mass of clouds and which, like death itself, frightens the enemy. He who is known in this world as of superhuman strength and he who is known by the rulers of the earth as the victor over the gods even in battle, he, who unnoticed by others takes up five hundred arrows and but in a moment shoots them and makes them fall at a distance, he, who is said by Bhishma, Drona, Kripa and the son of Drona and by Shalya the king of Madras and by all disinterested persons, to be invisible by superhuman rulers of the earth when standing on the field of battle, as a tiger arnong car-warriors and a subduer of enemies, he at one effort shoots five hundred arrows and in strength of arms is equal to Kartavirya. In this great battle do I see that great bowmen Arjuna equal in might to Indra united with Upendra working havoc.

sn: इत्येवं चिन्तयत् कृत्स्नमहोरात्राणि भारत। अनिद्रो निःसुखश्चास्मि कुरूणां शमचिन्तया॥
en: Thinking this day and night, O Bharata, am I sleepless and unhappy through anxiety for the good of the Kurus.

sn: क्षयोदयोऽयं सुमहान् कुरूणां प्रत्युपस्थितः। अस्त चेत् कलहस्यान्तः शमादन्यो न विद्यते॥ शमो मे रोचते नित्यं पार्थस्तात न विग्रहः। कुरुभ्यो हि सदा मन्ये पाण्डवान् शक्तिमत्तरान्॥
en: A great cause of the destruction of the Kurus is now come. If there is no other means of an end to this quarrel, than peace, peace seems desirable to me and not war with the sons of Pritha. I have ever been of opinion that the Pandavas are possessed of greater strength than the Kurus.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच पितुरेतद् वचः श्रुत्वा धार्तराष्ट्रोऽत्यमर्षणः। आधाय विपुलं क्रोधं पुनरेवेदमब्रवीत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having heard these words of his father, the extremely passionate son of Dhritarashtra became highly enraged and again said this-

sn: अशक्यादेवसचिवाः पार्थाः स्युरिति यद् भवान्। मन्यते तद् भयं व्येतु भवतो राजसत्तम॥
en: You think that the sons of Pritha having the gods for their assistants are incapable of being withstood; let this fear of yours be dispelled, O you best among kings.

sn: अकामद्वेषसंयोगलोभाद्रोहाच भारत। उपेक्षया च भावानां देवा देवत्वमाप्नुवन्॥
en: From an absence of desire and of hatred and of avarice and of anxiety and for their indifference to worldly property, did the gods obtain their god-ships.

sn: इति द्वैपायनो व्यासो नारदश्च महातपाः। जामदग्न्यश्च रामो नः कथामकथयत् पुरा॥
en: Such was the tale told to us in days of yore by the great devotees Dvaipayana, Vyasa, Narayana and Rama the son of Jamadagna.

sn: नैव मानुषवद् देवा: प्रवर्तन्ते कदाचन। कामात् क्रोधात् तथा लोभावेषाच्च भरतर्षभ॥
en: Never like men do the gods engage themselves in the work out of desire, wrath, avarice, hatred, O bull among the race of Bharata.

sn: यदा ह्यग्निश्च वायुश्च धर्म इन्द्रोऽश्विनावपि। कामयोगात् प्रवर्तेरन् न पार्था दुःखमाप्नुयुः॥
en: If Agni (god of fire) or Vayu (god of wind) or Dharma (god of Virtue) or Indra or Ashvina had ever engaged in work out of desire, then the sons of Partha could not have met with unhappiness.

sn: तस्मान्न भवता चिन्ता कार्येषा स्यात् कथंचन। दैवेष्वपेक्षका ह्येते शश्वद् भावेषु भारत॥
en: Therefore should anxiety never be indulged in by you, for the gods incline towards objects worthy of them, O Bharata.

sn: अथ चेत् कामसंयोगाद् द्वेषो लोभश्च लक्ष्यते। देवेषु दैवप्रामाण्यान्नैषां तद् विक्रमिष्यति॥
en: If however out of contact with desire, envy or avarice is observed in the action of gods; then owing to their own ruling it cannot prevail.

sn: मयाभिमन्त्रितः शश्वज्जातवेदाः प्रशाम्यति। दिधक्षुः सकलाँल्लोकान् परिक्षिप्य समन्ततः॥
en: Incantations being repeated by me, fire will that moment be extinguished, been if, desirous of burning up the worlds, it blazes occupying all directions.

sn: यद् वा परमकं तेजो येन युक्ता दिवौकसः। ममाप्यनुपमं भूयो देवेभ्यो विद्धि भारत॥
en: The divine energy with which the denizens of haven endued is great; but mine, too, is without parallel and so greater than that of the gods; know this, O Bharata.

sn: विदीर्यमाणां वसुधां गिरीणां शिखराणि च। लोकस्य पश्यतो राजन् स्थापयाम्यभिमन्त्रणात्॥
en: In the very sight of the world can I reunite, Oking by my incantation, the Earth divided into two or the or the peaks of heavens (divided into two).

sn: स्तम्भितास्वप्सु चेतनाचेतनस्यास्य जङ्गमस्थावरस्य च। विनाशाय समुत्पन्नमहं घोरं महास्वनम्॥ अश्मवर्षं च वायुं च शमयामीह नित्यशः। जगतः पश्यतोऽभीक्ष्णं भूतानामनुकम्पया॥
en: I can at any time before the sight of the entire world put down a roaring downfall of stones or a strong gale produced from the destruction of animate and inanimate things and mobile and immobile beings out of compassion for them.

sn: गच्छन्ति मया रथपदातयः। देवासुराणां भावानामहमेकः प्रवर्तिता॥
en: Cars and infantry can go over waters solidified by me. I am the only director of the affairs of the gods and Asuras.

sn: अक्षौहिणीभिर्यान् देशान् यामि कार्येण केनचित्। तत्राश्वा मे प्रवर्तन्ते यत्र यत्राभिकामये॥
en: To whatever country I go with my Akshauhinis on any purpose, there my horses move in whatever directions I desire.

sn: भयानकानि विषये व्यालादीनि न सन्ति मे। मन्त्रगुप्तानि भूतानि न हिंसन्ति भयंकराः॥
en: In my territories there are no terrible snakes and frightful beasts do not injure men who are protected by my incantations.

sn: निकामवर्षी पर्जन्यो राजन् विषयवासिनाम्। धर्मिष्ठाश्च प्रजाः सर्वा ईतयश्च न सन्ति मे॥
en: To the residents in my territories the clouds shower rains at their (the resident') will (i.e. showers rains in quantities and at times desired by them). My subjects are attached to virtue; and in my territories the calamities of cultivation do not exist.

sn: अश्विनावथ वाय्वग्नी मरुद्भिः सह वृत्रहा। धर्मश्चैव मया द्विष्टान् नोत्सहन्तेऽभिरक्षितुम्॥
en: The Asuras, the wind, the fire, the slayer of Vritra with the Marutas and Virtue himself would not dare protect them whom I hate.

sn: यदि ह्येते समर्थाः स्युर्मविषस्त्रातुमञ्जसः। न स्म त्रयोदश समाः पार्था दुःखमवाप्नुयुः॥
en: If these had been capable of rescuing my enemies by their might; then the sons of Pritha would not have met with trouble years.

sn: नैव देवा न गन्धर्वा नासुरा न च राक्षसाः। शक्तास्त्रातुं मया द्विष्टं सत्यमेतद् ब्रवीमि ते॥
en: Neither the gods and Gandharvas, nor the Asuras and the Rakshasas are capable of rescuing my enemies, I am telling the truth.

sn: यदभिध्याम्यहं शश्वच्छुभं वा यद वाऽशुभम्। नैतद् विपन्नपूर्वं मे मित्रेष्वरिषु चोभयोः॥
en: Whatever happiness or misery I chose to assign to my friends or foes, I have never before been disappointed in.

sn: भविष्यतीदमिति वा यद् ब्रवीमि परंतप। नान्यथा भूतपूर्वं च सत्यवागिति मां विदुः॥
en: It will be as I say, O you subduer of enemies, never before have my words been false; and I have been known as the one of truthful speech.

sn: लोकसाक्षिकमेतन्मे महात्म्यं दिक्षु विश्रुतम्। आश्वासनार्थं भक्तः प्रोक्तं न श्लाघया नृप॥
en: The world is a witness to this greatness of mine, the fame of which has been heard by them. All this has been spoken for consoling you and not by way of self praise, Oking.

sn: न ह्यहं श्लाघनो राजन् भूतपूर्वः कदाचन। असदाचरितं ह्येतद् यदात्मान् प्रशंसति॥
en: I have never, I king, praised myself before; for he who praises himself acts meanly.

sn: पाण्डवांश्चैव मत्स्यांश्च पाञ्चालान् केकयैः सह। सात्यकिं वासुदेवं च श्रोतासि विजितान् मया।॥
en: You will be the hearer of the defeat by me of the Pandavas and Matsyas and the Panchalas with the Kaikeyas and Satyaki and the son of Vasudeva.

sn: सरितः सागरं प्राप्य यथा नश्यन्ति सर्वशः। तथैव ते विनक्ष्यन्ति मामासाद्य सहान्वयाः॥
en: I am of superior intelligence, of superior might and of superior prowess. My knowledge is superior and my application and concentration are superior to theirs.

sn: परा बुद्धिः परं तेजो वीर्यं च परमं मम। परा विद्या परो योगो मम तेभ्यो विशिष्यते॥
en: Asuras on falling into the sea annihilated in every way; so will the Pandavas with others be annihilated on meeting. are

sn: पितामहश्च द्रोणश्च कृपः शल्यः शलस्तथा। अस्त्रेषु यत् प्रजानन्ति सर्वं तन्मयि विद्यते॥
en: What is know as to the use of weapons to our grandfather, Drona, Kripa, Shalya and Shala, is all present in me.

sn: इत्युक्ते संजयं भूयः पर्यपृच्छत भारतः। ज्ञात्वा युयुत्सोः कार्याणि प्राप्तकालमरिन्दम॥
en: Saying this that subduer of enemies desirous of war knowing that proper time had come again asked Sanjaya about their doings.

sn: दुर्योधन उवाच सदृशानां मनुष्येषु सर्वेषां तुल्यजन्मनाम्। कथमेकान्ततस्तेषां पार्थानां मन्यसे जयम्॥
en: Dhritarashtra said Why do you consider victory to be the sole monopoly of the sons of Pritha who are similar to those of all men.

sn: वयं च तेऽपि तुल्या वै वीर्येण च पराक्रमैः। समेन वयसा चैव प्रातिभेन श्रुतेन च।॥
en: We and they too are equal in heroism and in prowess, are similar in age, in intelligence and in knowledge of the holy books.

sn: अस्त्रेण योधयुग्या च शीघ्रत्वे कौशले तथा। सर्वे स्म समजातीयाः सर्वे मानुषयोनयः॥
en: In weapons, in the science of fighting, in agility and in skill, all are of the same species; all had our birth in human beings.

sn: पितामह विजानीषे पार्थेषु विजयं कथम्। नाहं भवति न द्रोणे न कृपे न च बाह्निके॥
en: O grandfather, how then do you know victory to go to the son of Pritha? I do not depend on Drona, nor on Kripa, nor on the son of Balhika.

sn: अन्येषु च नरेन्द्रेषु पराक्रम्य समारभे। अहं वैकर्तनः कर्णो भ्राता दुःशासनश्च मे॥
en: Nor on the other kings. Myself, Karna the son of Vikartana and my brother Dushasana by our prowess will win.

sn: पाण्डवान् समरे पञ्च हनिष्यामः शितैः शरैः। ततो राजन् महायज्ञैर्विविधैर्भूरिदक्षिणैः॥
en: We shall kill the five sons Pandu in battle by means of sharp-edged arrows; then, Oking, with a great sacrificial ceremony with large present of many sorts

sn: ब्राह्मणांस्तर्पयिष्यामि गोभिरश्वैर्धनेन च। यदा परिकरिष्यन्ति ऐणेयानिव तन्तुना। अतरित्रानिव जले बाहुभिर्मामका रणे॥ पश्यन्तस्ते परांस्तत्र रथनागसमाकुलान्। तदा दविमोक्ष्यन्ति पाण्डवाः स च केशवः॥
en: Shall we worship the Brahmanas and with cows and heroes and wealth. When like deer dragged by a net or men unable to him by water shall our soldiers by means of their arms in the battle, drag the enemies and when they (the enemies) see the vast crows of chariots and elephants, then will the sons of Pandu leave off their pride and not they alone but Keshava also.

sn: विदुर उवाच इह निःश्रेयसं प्राहुर्वृद्धा निश्चितदर्शिनः। ब्राह्मणस्य विशेषेण दमो धर्मः सनातनः॥
en: Vidura said Old persons who are unfailing in their predictions say that in this world self-control is excellent; especially in a Brahmana is it an eternal and necessary virtue.

sn: तस्य दानं क्षमा सिद्धिर्यथावदुपपद्यते। दमो दानं तपो ज्ञानमधीतं चानुवर्तते॥
en: He gets success, forgiveness and the fruits of his gifts whose self-control pursues the path of gifts, asceticism, knowledge and study.

sn: दमस्तेजो वर्धयति पवित्रं दम उत्तमम्। विपाप्मा वृद्धतेजास्तु पुरुषो विन्दते महत्॥
en: Self-control increases energy; self-control is excellent and holy. Absolved from his sins and having his energy increased (by selfcontrol) a man obtains great results. are

sn: क्रव्याट्य इव भूतानामदान्तेभ्यः सदा भयम्। येषां च प्रतिषेधार्थं क्षत्रं सृष्टं स्वयम्भुवा॥
en: Those who are devoid of self-control are ever feared by creatures as Rakshasas, for whose check Kshatriyas were created by Him who is born of Himself.

sn: आश्रमेषु चतुर्बाहुर्दममेवोत्तमं व्रतम्। तस्य लिङ्गं प्रवक्ष्यामि येषां समुदयो दमः॥
en: For all the four stages of life, self-control is a very good vow; I speak of the characteristics of him whose life is one of self-control.

sn: क्षमा धृतिरहिंसा च समता सत्यमार्जवम्। इन्द्रियाभिजयो धैर्य मार्दवं ह्रीरचापलम्॥ अकार्पण्यमसंरम्भः संतोषः श्रद्दधानता। एतानि यस्य राजेन्द्र स दान्तः पुरुषः स्मृतः॥ कामो लोभश्च दर्पश्च मन्युनिद्रा विकत्थनम्। मान ईर्ष्या च शोकश्च नैतद् दान्तो निषेवते। अजिह्ममशठं शुद्धमेतद् दान्तस्य लक्षणम्॥
en: They forgiveness, wisdom, benevolence, equality, regard for all virtues, truth, guilelessness, subjugation of the senses, patience, mildness, modesty and steadiness, the reverse of miserliness, mildness, contentment and reverence. Desire, avarice, vanity, envy, sleep, fareness of speech, self-love, jealousy and grief-these are not yielded to by those who have self-control. Simplicity, honestly and purity of mind are the characteristics of a man of self-control.

sn: अलोलुपस्तथाऽल्पेप्सुः कामानामविचिन्तिता। समुद्रकल्पः पुरुषः स दान्तः परिकीर्तितः॥
en: One not given to avarice, who is desirous to obtain little, who is indifferent to objects of desire and who is grave as the sea, is known as the man of self-restraint.

sn: सुवृत्तः शीलसम्पन्नः प्रसन्नात्माऽऽत्मविद् बुधः। प्राप्येह लोके सम्मानं सुगति प्रेत्य गच्छति॥
en: That wise man who is of good habits in life of a blameless disposition is satisfied with his soul and knows his own nature and after commanding respect in this world he is well provided for after death.

sn: अभयं यस्य भूतेभ्यः सर्वेषामभयं यतः। स वै परिणतप्रज्ञः प्रख्यातो मनुजोत्तमः॥
en: He that has no fear from other creatures and from whom other creatures have no fear, is a man of ripe wisdom and is knows as the best of human beings.

sn: सर्वभूतहितो मैत्रस्तस्मान्नोद्विजते जनः। समुद्र इव गम्भीरः प्रज्ञातृप्तः प्रशाम्यति॥
en: People are not made unhappy by him who makes all creatures his friends and seeks their good; he is calm and grave as the ocean and is pleased (with everything) owing to his wisdom.

sn: कर्मणाऽऽचरितं पूर्वं सद्भिराचरितं च यत्। तदेवास्थाय मोदन्ते दान्ताः शमपरायणाः॥
en: Those who have self-control are of peaceful habits and rejoice, regulating their life by the example of deeds done in olden times and deeds in the present by the honest.

sn: नैष्कर्म्यं वा समास्थाय ज्ञानतृप्तो जितेन्द्रियः। कालाकाक्षी चरँल्लोके ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते॥
en: Or living in this world and renouncing all work, the man of self-control, pleased with all by his wisdom, roams about in the world, waiting for death and annihilating into Brahma.

sn: शकुनीनामिवाकाशे पदं नैवोपलभ्यते। एवं प्रज्ञानतृप्तस्य मुनेर्वर्त्म न दृश्यते॥
en: As the passage of birds soaring in the sky cannot be observed, so also the path of that sage who is contented in consequence of his wisdom is not observed.

sn: उत्सृज्यैव गृहान् यस्तु मोक्षमेवाभिमन्यते। लोकास्तेजोमयास्तस्य कल्पन्ते शाश्वता दिवि॥
en: He who desirous of emancipation leaves his home has in heaven bright regions assigned to him forever.

sn: विदुर उवाच शकुनीनामिहार्थाय पाशं भूमावयोजयत्। कश्चिच्छाकुनिकस्तात पूर्वेषामिति शुश्रुम॥
en: Vidura said For the capture of birds did a certain fowler set his net in this world. O Sire, so we have heard from old men.

sn: तस्मिन् तौ शकुनौ बद्धौ युगपत् सहचारिणौ। तावुपादाय तं पाशं जग्मतुः खचरावुभौ॥
en: There were two birds, companions to each other, captured in that net and they both went up into the air with that net.

sn: तौ विहायसमाक्रान्तौ दृष्ट्वा शाकुनिकस्तदा। अन्वधावदनिर्विष्णो येन येन स्म गच्छतः॥
en: The fowler seeing them fly up in the air without losing his senses followed them in the direction they took.

sn: तथा तमनुधावन्तं मृगयुं शकुनार्थिनम्। आश्रमस्थो मुनिः कश्चिद् ददर्शाथ कृताह्निकः॥
en: A certain Rishi living in a hermitage, who had finished his daily worship I saw that fowler following the birds, still in the hope of getting hold of the birds.

sn: तावन्तरिक्षगौ शीघ्रमनुयान्तं महीचरम्। श्लोकेनानेन कौरव्य पप्रच्छ स मुनिस्तदा॥
en: Then did the anchoring address, O Kauravya, that denizen of the earth following the wanderers of the sky in this couplet.

sn: विचित्रमिदमाश्चर्यं मृगहन् प्रतिभाति मे। प्लमानौ हि खचरौ पदातिरनुधावसि॥
en: Slayer of animals, it seems to me wonderfully strange that you who move by your feet in this earth are following wanderers of the sky.

sn: शाकुनिक उवाच पाशमेकमुभावेतौ सहितौ हरतो मम। यत्र वै विवदिष्येते तत्र मे वशमेष्यतः॥
en: The fowler said These two united are taking that one net of mine but they will come under my control where they will quarrel.

sn: विदुर उवाच तौ विवादमनुप्राप्तौ शकुनौ मृत्युसंधितौ। विगृह्य च सुदुर्बुद्धी पृथिव्यां संनिपेततुः॥
en: Vidura said The two birds who were doomed to death quarreled; and having quarrelled the two fools fell to the earth.

sn: तौ युध्यमानौ संरब्धौ मृत्युपाशवशानुगौ। उपसृत्यापरिज्ञातो जग्राह मृगहा तदा॥
en: The slayer of animals then approaching those two fighting with each other, subject to the trap of death, without their knowledge caught hold of them.

sn: एवं ये ज्ञातयोऽर्थेषु मिथो गच्छन्ति विग्रहम्। तेऽमित्रवशमायान्ति शकुनाविव विग्रहात्॥
en: In the same way those cousins who quarrel in matters of wealth are brought under the control of enemies like the birds owing to their quarrel.

sn: सम्भोजनं संकथनं सम्प्रश्नोऽथ समागमः। एतानि ज्ञातिकार्याणि न विरोधः कदाचन॥
en: Dining in one another's company and conversing among, one another, inquiring about one another's health and living together, these are the duties of cousins and quarrel is never.

sn: ये स्म काले सुमनसः सर्वे वृद्धानुपासते। सिंहगुप्तमिवारण्यमप्रधृष्या भवन्ति ते॥
en: Those who in proper season serve the old men out of pure motives, become invincible like a forest protected by lions.

sn: येऽर्थं संततमासाद्य दीना इव समासते। श्रियं ते समप्रयच्छन्ति द्विषद्भ्यो भरतर्षभ॥
en: Those, who attaining to prosperity behave like the mean-minded contribute to the prosperity of their despisers, O you bull among the race of Bharata.

sn: धूमायन्ते व्यपेतानि ज्वलन्ति सहितानि च। धृतराष्ट्रोल्मुकानीव ज्ञातयो भरतर्षभ।॥
en: Cousins, O you bull among the race of Bharata, smoke when quarrelling and blaze up when like charcoals.

sn: इदमन्यत् प्रवक्ष्यामि यथा दृष्टं गिरौ मया। श्रुत्वा तदपि कौरव्य यथा श्रेयस्तथा कुरु॥
en: or I shall speak of something else, which was seen by me in a mountain and hearing that too, O son of Kuru, do whatever is good.

sn: वयं किरातैः सहिता गच्छामो गिरिमुत्तरम्। ब्राह्मणैर्देवकल्पैश्च विद्याजम्भकवार्तिकैः॥
en: We want to the Northern mountains accompanied by hunters and godlike Brahmanas fond of conversations incantations and medicines.

sn: कुञ्जभूतं गिरिं सर्वमभितो गन्धमादनम्। दीप्यमानौषधिगणं सिद्धगन्धर्वसेवितम्॥
en: The Gandhamadana mountain was like a grove (owing to tress growing on it) in every way. It was shining, as it were, with cluster of medicinal plants and inhabited by ascetics and the Gandharvas,

sn: तत्रापश्याम वै सर्वे मधु पीतकमाक्षिकम्। मरुप्रपाते विषमे निविष्टं कुम्भसम्मितम्॥
en: There we all saw some honey of a yellow colour inside a pot placed at a very high point of the mountain.

sn: आशीविषै रक्ष्यमाणं कुबैरदयितं भृशम्। यत् प्राप्य पुरुषो मर्योऽप्यमरत्वं नियच्छति॥
en: This was guarded by snakes, the favourite drink of Kubera, as it was drinking which even an earthy man gets immortality.

sn: अचक्षुर्लभते चक्षुर्वृद्धो भवति वै युवा। इति ते कथयन्ति स्म ब्राह्मणा जम्भसाधकाः॥
en: Those without eyes get eyes, and the old become young. There was the honey described by the Brahmanas conversant with incantations.

sn: ततः किरातास्तद् दृष्ट्वा प्रार्थयन्तो महीपते। विनेशुर्विषमे तस्मिन् ससर्प गिरिगह्वरे॥
en: Then did the hunters, seeing that strive to obtain it, О king and were destroyed in thai frightful mountain cavern full of snakes.

sn: तथैव तव पुत्रोऽयं पृथिवीमेक इच्छति। मधु पश्यति सम्मोहात् प्रपातं नानुपश्यति॥
en: Thus does this son of yours desire to be the one supreme individual in this world; out of loss of his senses, does he see only the honey and not the fall.

sn: दुर्योधनो यो मनाः समरे सव्यसाचिना। न च पश्यामि तेजोऽस्य विक्रमं वा तथाविधम्॥
en: Duryodhana is desirous of a fight with Savyasachin; but I do not see in him the strength or energy necessary for that purpose.

sn: एकेन रथमास्थाय पृथिवी येन निर्जिता। भीष्मद्रोणप्रभृतयः संत्रस्ताः साधुयायिनः॥
en: That Savyasachin, who alone in his car has brought the earth under his control and who inspired dared into Bhishma, Drona and others accompanied by their hosts.

sn: विराटनगरे भग्नाः किं तत्र तव दृश्यताम्। प्रतीक्षमाणो यो वीरः क्षमते वीक्षितं तव॥
en: They were routed at the city of Virata-sce what occurred there. That hero looking at your face and waiting to see your movements will forgive you still.

sn: दुपदो मत्स्यराजश्च संक्रुद्धश्च धनंजयः। न शेषयेयुः समरे वायुयुक्ता इवाग्नयः॥
en: Drupada, the king of the Matsyas and Dhananjaya, fired with wrath, will leave no trace (of your army) like a conflagration urged on by the wind.

sn: अङ्के कुरुष्व राजानं धृतराष्ट्र युधिष्ठिरम्। युध्यतोर्हि द्वयोर्युद्धे नैकान्तेन भवेज्जयः॥
en: 0 Dhritarashtra, take the king Yudhishthira on your lap; for by a struggle between you two none can get an absolute victory.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच दुर्योधन विजानीहि यत् त्वां वक्ष्यामि पुत्रका उत्पथं मन्यसे मार्गमनभिज्ञ इवाध्वगः॥
en: Dhritarashtra said O Duryodhana, think well on what I am telling you, my dear son. You think the wrong way to be the right one like an inexperienced wayfarer.

sn: पञ्चानां पाण्डुपुत्राणां यत् तेजः प्रजिहीर्षसि। पञ्चानामिव भूतानां महतां लोकधारिणाम्॥
en: The energy of the five sons of Pandu, which you are desirous of eclipsing, is like the energy of the five elements in their subtle state supporting the universe.

sn: युधिष्ठिरं हि कौन्तेयं परं धर्ममिहास्थितम्। परां गतिमसम्प्रेत्य न त्वं जेतुमिहार्हसि॥
en: Yudhishthira, the son of Kunti, is established on sound and strict virtue in this world. You are not fit to vanquish him without losing your life.

sn: भीमसेनं च कौन्तेयं यस्य नास्ति समो बले। रणान्तकं तर्जयसे महावातमिव दुमः॥
en: Bhimasena too whose equal there it none in strength, you are roaring at this one who is equal to Yama himself in battle.

sn: सर्वशस्त्रभृतां श्रेष्ठं मेरुं शिखरिणमिव। युधि गाण्डीवधन्वानं को नु युध्येत बुद्धिमान्॥
en: The foremost of the wielder of weapons, that Meru among the mountains, what intelligent man would fight with that wielder of the Gandiva bow.

sn: धृष्टद्युम्नश्च पाञ्चाल्यः कमिवाद्य न शातयेत्। शत्रुमध्ये शरान् मुञ्चन् देवराडशनीमिव॥
en: What man is there is this world whom Dhrishtadyumna cannot vanquish, shooting arrows among the enemy like the king of the gods hurling his thunderbolt.

sn: सात्यक्श्चिापि दुर्धर्षः सम्मतोऽन्धकवृष्णिषु। ध्वंसयिष्यत्ति ते सेनां पाण्डवेयहिते रतः॥
en: Satyaki, too, that one hard to be vanquished, who is respected among the Andhakas and the Vrishnis, will destroy your host; for he is ever attached to what is good for the Pandavas.

sn: यः पुनः प्रतिमानेन त्रीनल्लोकानतिरिच्यते। तं कृष्णं पुण्डरीकाक्षं को नु युद्ध्येत बुद्धिमान्॥
en: Then again, he who in measure of strength surpasses the three worlds, what intelligent man would fight with that Krishna, whose eyes are like lotuses.

sn: एकतो ह्यस्य दाराश्च ज्ञातयश्च सबान्धवाः। आत्मा च पृथिवी चेयमेकतश्च धनंजयः॥
en: Krishna considers his wives, cousins and his friends, his soul and the earth on one side equal to Dhananjaya on the other.

sn: वासुदेवोऽपि दुर्धर्षो यतात्मा यत्र पाण्डवः। अविषां पृथिव्यापि तद् बलं यत्र केशवः॥
en: The son of Vasudeva too who is relied on by the son of Pandu, is hard to be vanquished and the army in which Keshava takes part is invincible even by the whole world.

sn: तिष्ठ तात सतां वाक्ये सुहृदामर्थवादिनाम्। वृद्धं शान्तनवं भीष्मं तितिक्षस्व पितामहम्॥
en: Abide then, my dear, by what your friends who tell you to do only what is conducive to your interests say. Accept the old Bhishma, the son of Shantanu and your grandfather as your guides.

sn: मां च ब्रुवाणं शुश्रूष कुरूणामर्थदर्शिनम्। द्रोणं कृपं विकर्णं च महाराजं च बाह्निकम्॥
en: Listen therefore to what these seekers of good to the Kurus-Drona, Kripa, Vikarna and the great king Bahlika, say and to myself as well.

sn: एते ह्यपि यथैवाहं मन्तुमर्हसि तांस्तथा। सर्वे धर्मविदो ह्येते तुल्यस्नेहाश्च भारत॥
en: These stand in the same relation to you as I myself and it is proper that you should regard them in the same light. All of them know what virtue is and have the same degree of affection for you, O Bharata.

sn: यत् तद् विराटनगरे सह भ्रातृभिरग्रतः। उत्सृज्य गाः सुसंत्रस्तं बलं ते समशीर्यत॥
en: Your host headed by your brothers fled from that city of Virata leaving the king to surrender.

sn: यच्चैव नगरे तस्मिञ्छूयते महदद्भुतम्। एकस्य च बहूनां च पर्याप्तं तन्निदर्शनम्॥
en: This tall story that we hear of what occurred in that city-the struggle between one and many is sufficient proof (of what I say regarding their superiority).

sn: अर्जुनस्तत् तथाकार्षीत् किं पुनः सर्व एव ते। स भ्रातृनभिजानीहि वृत्त्या तं प्रतिपादय॥
en: Such was the feat of Arjuna single; what will they all united not do? Treat them as your own brothers and give them their rights.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्त्वा महाप्राज्ञो धृतराष्ट्रः सुयोधनम्। पुनरेव महाभागः संजयं पर्यपृच्छत॥
en: Vaishampayana said The very wise Dhritarashtra of great prosperity having thus addressed Suyodhana again asked of Sanjaya-

sn: ब्रूहि संजय यच्छेषं वासुदेवादनन्तरम्। यदर्जुन उवाच त्वां परं कौतूहलं हि मे॥
en: Tell me, O Sanjaya, the remaining part, after the speech of Vasudeva, viz., what Arjuna said to you. I have great curiosity for it.

sn: संजय उवाच वासुदेववचः श्रुत्वा कुन्तीपुत्रो धनंजयः। उवाच काले दुर्धर्षो वासुदेवस्य शृण्वतः॥
en: Sanjaya said Having heard the speech of Vasudeva, Dhananjaya the son of Kunti and hard to be vanquished said at the proper time within the hearing of Vasudeva.

sn: पितामहं शान्तनवं धृतराष्ट्रं च संजय। द्रोणं कृपं च कर्णं च महाराजं च बाह्निकम्॥ द्रौणिं च सोमदत्तं च शकुनि चापि सौबलम्। दुःशासनं शलं चैव पुरुमित्रं विविंशतिम्॥ विकर्ण चित्रसेनं च जयत्सेनं च पार्थिवम्। विन्दानुविन्दावावन्त्यौ दुर्मुखं चापि कौरवम्॥ सैन्धव दुःसहं चैव भूरिश्रवसमेव च। भगदत्तं च राजानं जलसन्धं च पार्थिवम्॥ ये चाप्यन्ये पार्थिवास्तत्र योद्धं समागताः कौरवाणां प्रियार्थम्। मुमूर्षवः पाण्डवाग्नौ प्रदीप्ते समानीता धार्तराष्ट्रण होतुम्॥
en: Our grand-father, the son of Shantanu and Dhritarashtra too, O Sanjaya and Drona and Kripa and Karna and the Balhika and the son of Drona and Somadatta and Shakuni and the son of Subala and Dushasana and Shala and Purumitra and Vivingshati and Vikarna and Chitrasena and the ruler of the earth Jayatsena and the two chiefs of Avanti, Vindu and Anuvindu and the Kaurava Durmukha and the king of Sindhu and Dusaha and Bhurishravas and the king Bhagadatta and the ruler of the earth Jarasandha and the other rulers of the earth, who have assembled to fight on that side in the interests of the sons of Kuru, are about to die. They have been brought together by the son of Dhritarashtra as offerings for the blazing fire of the sons of Pandu.

sn: यथान्यायं कौशलं वन्दनं च समागता मद्वचनेन वाच्याः। इदं ब्रूयाः संजय राजमध्ये सुयोधनं पापकृतां निधानम्॥
en: The assembled ones are to be asked in my name about their health each in terms suitable to his rank and the proper greetings are to be presented. Tell this, O Sanjaya, in the midst of those kings to the foremost of sinners, Suyodhana.

sn: अमर्षणं दुर्मतिं राजपुत्रं पापात्मानं धार्तराष्ट्र सुलुब्धम्। सर्वं ममैतद् वचनं समग्रं सहामात्यं संजय श्रावयेथाः॥
en: Make that wrathful prince of wicked intellect, that covetous son of Dhritarashtra of vicious soul hear all these words of mine, O Sanjaya, in the midst of all his ministers and parties.

sn: एवं प्रतिष्ठाप्य धनंजयो मां ततोऽर्थवद् धर्मवच्चापि वाक्यम्। प्रोवाचेदं वासुदेवं समीक्ष्य पार्थो धीमाँल्लोहितान्तायताक्षः॥
en: Saying this by way of an introduction, Dhananjaya the wise son of Pritha then looking at the son of Vasudeva with distended eyes with red corners, spoke these words consistent with both righteousness and morality to me.

sn: यथा श्रुतं ते वदतो महात्मनो मधुप्रवीरस्य वचः समाहितम्। तथैव वाच्यं भवता हि मद्वचः समागतेषु क्षितिपेषु सर्वशः॥
en: You have heard the measured speech of the high-souled hero of Madhu's race. You are to say the same thing to all the assembled rulers of the earth as my words.

sn: शराग्निधूमे रथनेमिनादिते धनुःस्रुवेणास्त्रबलप्रसारिणा। यथा न होमः क्रियते महामृधे समेत्य सर्वे प्रयतध्वमादृताः॥
en: Let them act in such a way that offerings may not have to be made to the smoky fire of arrows in the great sacrificial ceremony with the rattles of the car-wheels as substituting for incantations and the bow-string which will neutralize the effects of their arms as that for the ladle.

sn: न चेत् प्रयच्छध्वममित्रघातिनो युधिष्ठिरस्य शममीप्सितं स्वकम्। नयामि वः साश्वपदातिकुञ्जरान् दिशं पितॄणामशिवां शितैः शरैः॥
en: If you do not return to Yudhishthira, the slayer of his enemies, his own share which he desires; then shall I conduct you with your horses, foot soldiers and elephants to the inauspicious regions of departed spirits by my sharp arrows.

sn: ततोऽहमामन्त्र्य तदा धनंजयं चतुर्भुजं चैव नमस्य सत्वरः। जवेन सम्प्राप्त इहामराते तवान्तिकं प्रापयितुं वचो महत्॥
en: Then quickly bidding farewell to Dhananjaya and the One with four arms and bowing down to them, have I come here with speed to tell you this great news, O you of the luster of immortals.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच दुर्योधने धार्तराष्ट्रे तद् वचो नाभिनन्दति। तूष्णीम्भूतेषु सर्वेषु समुत्तस्थुर्नरर्षभाः॥
en: Vaishampayana said On Duryodhana; the son of Dhritarashtra, not minding this speech much and all the others remaining damp those bulls among men rose up (and departed).

sn: उत्थितेषु महाराज पृथिव्यां सर्वराजसु। रहिते संजयं राजा परिप्रष्टुं प्रचक्रमे॥ आशंसमानो विजयं तेषां पुत्रवशानुगः। आत्मनश्च परेषां च पाण्डवानां च निश्चयम्॥
en: After all the kings of the earth have stood up, the great king (Dhritarashtra) began to enquire of Sanjaya in secret, the resolves of his own party and of his enemies and Pandavas, after the one who was subject to wishes of his son had wished them (the kings) success.

sn: गावल्गणे ब्रुहि नः सारफल्गु स्वसेनायां यावदिहास्ति किंचित्। त्वं पाण्डवानां निपुणं वेत्थ सर्वं किमेषां ज्यायः किमु तेषा कनीयः॥
en: Dhritarashtra said O son of Gavalgani, tell one of the little superiority that exists in our own army. You know the affairs of the Pandavas fuliy, in what points they are superior and in what inferior.

sn: त्वमेतयोः सारवित् सर्वदर्शी धर्मार्थयोनिपुणो निश्चयज्ञः। स मे पृष्टः संजय ब्रूहि सर्वं युध्यमानाः कतरेऽस्मिन् न सन्ति॥
en: You know the points of superiority of these two armies. You know everything and can foresee them. You are well conversant with what is conducive to righteousness and worldly profit. You, who are such, O Sanjaya, asked by me, tell me which of the parties, in the event of war between them, will cease to exist.

sn: संजय उवाच दसूया हि त्वां प्रविशेत राजन्। आनयस्व पितरं महाव्रतं गान्धारीं च महिषीमाजमीढ॥
en: Sanjaya said I shall not tell you any thing in secret, for then ill felling against mc may enter within you, O king. Have our sire of great vows and queen Gandhari brought here, O Ajamida.

sn: तौ तेऽसूयां विनयेतां नरेन्द्र धर्मज्ञौ तौ निपुणौ निश्चयज्ञौ। तयोस्तु त्वां संनिधौ तद् वदेयं कृत्स्नं मतं केशवपार्थयोर्यत्॥
en: They will be able to remove any ill feeling, O chief among men, (you may harbour against me), acquainted as they are with virtue and skilled as they are in foresight. In their presence shall I tell you everything about the purposes determined on by Keshava and the son of Pritha.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच इत्युक्तेन च गान्धारी व्यासश्चात्राजगाम ह। आनीतौ विदुरेणेह सभां शीघ्रं प्रवेशितौ॥
en: Vaishampayana said Gandhari and Vyasa were brought there by him, who was then spoken to. Conducted by Vidura, they quickly entered the Council Chamber.

sn: ततस्तन्मतमाज्ञाय संजयस्यात्मजस्य च। अभ्युपेत्य महाप्राज्ञः कृष्णद्वैपायनोऽब्रवीत्॥
en: And knowing that intention of Sanjaya and of his son, the exceedingly wise Krishna Dvaipayana after coming there said-

sn: व्यास उवाच सम्पृच्छते धृतराष्ट्राय संजय आचक्ष्व सर्वं यावदेषोऽनुयुङ्क्ते। सर्वं यावद् वेत्थ तस्मिन् यथावद् द्याथातथ्यं वासुदेवेऽर्जुने च॥
en: Vyasa said To Dhritarashtra, who is asking, 0 Sanjaya, tell everything that he wants to know. Tell everything to him about the son of Vasudeva and Arjuna, as you know them.

description: Sanjay's description of lord Krishna's greatness to Dhritarashtra
sn: संजय उवाच अर्जुनो वासुदेवश्च धन्विनौ परमार्चितौ। कामादन्यत्र सम्भूतौ सर्वभावाय सम्मितौ॥
en: Sanjaya said Arjuna and the son of Vasudeva, the two very adorable wielders of the bow, born in a region other than their own out of their own will are equal to each other in every detail of their nature.

description: Sanjay's description of lord Krishna's greatness to Dhritarashtra
sn: व्यामान्तरं समास्थाय यथामुक्तं मनस्विनः। चक्रं तद् वासुदेवस्य मायया वर्तते विभो॥
en: That disc of the son of Vasudeva exists, as illusion, O lord though five cubits in diameter it can be hurled by that intelligent in any form he likes.

description: Sanjay's description of lord Krishna's greatness to Dhritarashtra
sn: सापह्नवं कौरवेषु पाण्डवानां सुसम्मतम्। सारासारबलं ज्ञातुं तेज:पुञ्जावभासितम्॥
en: (That disc) is the destroyer of the Kurus and therefore dear to the Pandavas. Shining with effulgence, it is the best measure for forming an idea of points of strength and weakness.

description: Sanjay's description of lord Krishna's greatness to Dhritarashtra
sn: नरकं शम्बरं चैव कंसं चैद्यं च माधवः। जितवान् घोरसंकाशान् क्रीडन्निव महाबलः॥
en: That descendant of Madhu, of great strength, as if in play, conquered Naraka, Shambara, Kansa and the king of the Chedis in terrific battle.

description: Sanjay's description of lord Krishna's greatness to Dhritarashtra
sn: पृथिवीं चान्तरिक्षं च द्यां चैव पुरुषोत्तमः। मनसैव विशिष्टात्मा नयत्यात्मवशं वशीः॥
en: That foremost men, of a superior soul, can by mere force of his will bring under control the earth, the sky and the heavens.

description: Sanjay's description of lord Krishna's greatness to Dhritarashtra
sn: भूयो भूयो हि यद् राजन् पृच्छसे पाण्डवान् प्रति। सारासारबलं ज्ञातुं तत् समासेन मे शृणु॥
en: Again and again, have you, O king, asked me about the Pandavas with a view to know their strength and the points of their superiority and inferiority. Listen to that from me in brief:

description: Sanjay's description of lord Krishna's greatness to Dhritarashtra
sn: एकतो वा जगत् कृत्स्नमेकतो वा जनार्दनः। सारतो जगतः कृत्स्नादतिरिक्तो जनार्दनः॥
en: If the entire world be placed on one side and Janardana on the other; then will the entire world be surpassed by Janardana in point of strength.

description: Sanjay's description of lord Krishna's greatness to Dhritarashtra
sn: भस्म कुर्याज्जगदिदं मनसैव जनार्दनः। न तु कृत्स्नं जगच्छक्तं भस्म कर्तुं जनार्दनम्॥
en: The entire world is not able to reduce Janardana to ashes; while Janardana can reduce the world into ashes.

description: Sanjay's description of lord Krishna's greatness to Dhritarashtra
sn: यतः सत्यं यतो धर्मो यतो ह्रीरार्जवं यतः। ततो भवतो गोविन्दो यतः कृष्णस्ततो जयः॥
en: Where there is truth, where there is righteousness, where there is modesty and where there is humanity, there is Govinda. Where there is Krishna; there is victory.

description: Sanjay's description of lord Krishna's greatness to Dhritarashtra
sn: पृथिवीं चान्तरिक्षं च दिवं च पुरुषोत्तमः। विचेष्टयति भूतात्मा क्रीडन्निव जनार्दनः॥
en: The earth, the sky and the heavens are guided by Janardana, that foremost among men, who is as it were, the soul of all creatures, as if in play.

description: Sanjay's description of lord Krishna's greatness to Dhritarashtra
sn: स कृत्वा पाण्डवान् सत्रं लोकं सम्मोहयन्निव। अधर्मनिरतान् मूढान् दग्धुमिच्छति ते सुतान्॥
en: He, making the Pandavas his instruments, desires to consume your foolish sons, who are attached to vice, sleeping the world in illusion.

description: Sanjay's description of lord Krishna's greatness to Dhritarashtra
sn: कालचक्रं जगच्चक्रं युगचक्रं च केशवः। आत्मयोगेन भगवान् परिवर्तयतेऽनिशम्॥
en: The wheel of time, the wheel of the world and the wheel of the Yuga (i.e. the wheel of work leading to births and rebirths) dose that ! prosperous bcing ever cause to revolve by application of his soul.

description: Sanjay's description of lord Krishna's greatness to Dhritarashtra
sn: कालस्य च हि मृत्योश्च जङ्गमस्थावरस्य च। ईशते भगवानेकः सत्यमेतद् ब्रवीमि ते॥
en: That prosperous Being alone is lord over Time, Death and over all mobile and immobile beings. I tell you the truth.

description: Sanjay's description of lord Krishna's greatness to Dhritarashtra
sn: ईशन्नपि महायोगी सर्वस्य जगतो हरिः। कर्माण्यारभते कर्तुं कीनाश इव वर्धनः॥
en: Though larding over the entire world, Hari, that great anchorite, has recourse to work, as a cultivator tills the soil.

description: Sanjay's description of lord Krishna's greatness to Dhritarashtra
sn: तेन वञ्चयते लोकान् मायायोगेन केशवः। ये तमेव प्रपद्यन्ते न ते मुह्यन्ति मानवाः॥
en: By such illusion dose Keshava deceive the world; but those men that have understood him are not deceived.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच कथं त्वं माधवं वेत्थ सर्वलोकमहेश्वरम्। कथमेनं न वेदाहं तन्ममाचक्ष्व संजय॥
en: Dhritarashtra said How have you come to know, Madhava, the great lord of all the worlds; and how is it that I do not know him? Tell me that, O Sanjaya.

sn: संजय उवाच शृणु राजन् न ते विद्या मम विद्या न हीयते। विद्याहीनस्तमोध्वस्तो नाभिजानाति केशवम्॥
en: Sanjaya said Listen, O king; you have no knowledge and my knowledge has diminished (since my last birth). You being without knowiedge and steeped in ignorance, do not know Keshava.

sn: विद्यया तात जानामि त्रियुगं मधुसूदनम्। कर्तारमकृतं देवं भूतानां प्रभवाप्ययम्॥
en: By my knowledge, O dear, I do know the slayer of Madhu to be the combination of the there ( the cause, the subtie and the gross), that he is the creator of all, though himself created by none and that he is the God by Whom all creatures are created and to Whom they are all lost they are lost in the end.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच गावल्गणेऽत्र का भक्तिर्या ते नित्या जनार्दने। यया त्वमभिजानासि त्रियुगं मधुसूदनम्॥
en: Dhritarashtra said O son of Gavalgani, what is the extent of the belief you ever have in Janardana, by which you Janardana, who is the union of the three.

sn: संजय उवाच मायां न सेवे भद्रं ते न वृथा धर्ममाचरे। शुद्धभाव गतो भक्त्या शास्त्राद् वेद्मि जनार्दनम्॥
en: Sanjaya said I do not care much for illusion (worldly matters); nor do I practice useless things (religious ceremonies in form without faith in the Supreme Being). Good betide you! With the aid of faith derived from purity of mind, do I know Janardana from the holy books.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच दुर्योधन हृषीकेशं प्रपद्यस्व जनार्दनम्। आप्तो न: संजयस्तात शरणं गच्छ केशवम्॥
en: Dhritarashtra said O Duryodhana, have recourse to Hrishikesha or Janardana. Sanjaya, my dear, cver seeks our interests; do you therefore seek refuge under Keshava.

sn: दुर्योधन उवाच भगवान् देवकीपुत्रो लोकांचेनिहनिष्यति। प्रवदन्नर्जुने सख्यं नाहं गच्छेऽद्य केशवम्॥
en: Duryodhana said If the son of Devaki, that divine Being, destroys the worlds the worlds, having recourse to the co-operation of Arjuna; even then shall I not seek refuge under Keshava.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच अवाग् गान्धारि पुत्रस्ते गच्छत्येष सुदुर्मतिः। ईधुंदुरात्मा मानी च श्रेयसां वचनातिगः॥
en: Dhritarashtra said O Gandhari, this wicked-minded son of yours would precipitate himself in misery. This evil-souled one, of an envious disposition and vain, he would not listen to the advice of his elders.

sn: गान्धार्युवाच ऐश्वर्यकाम दुष्टात्मन् वृद्धानां शासनातिग। ऐश्वर्यजीविते हित्वा पितरं मां च बालिश॥
en: Gandhari said O you desiring supremacy, O you of wicked soul, who do not listen to the advice of your elders and who do not pay regard to your father and myself, after losing your position during your life time.

sn: वर्धयन् दुहृदां प्रीतिं मां च शोकेन वर्धयन्। निहतो भीमसेनेन स्मर्ताऽसि वचनं पितुः॥
en: And enhancing the Joy of wicked hearted person as also my grief, when you will be slain by Bhimasena, you will remember the words of your father.

sn: व्यास उवाच प्रियोऽसि राजन् कृष्णस्य धृतराष्ट्र निबोध मे। यस्य ते संजयो दूतो यस्त्वां श्रेयसि योक्ष्यते॥
en: Vyasa said You are, O king, dear to Krishna, O Dhritarashtra; listen to me; since Sanjaya has acted as your ambassador, he will do what is conducive to your interests.

sn: जानात्येष हृषीकेशं पुराणं यच्च वै परम्। शुश्रूषमाणमेकाग्रयं मोक्ष्यते महतो भयात्॥
en: This man knows the ancient and blessed Being Hrishikesha. Listening to him with earnestness, you free from even the greatest dangers.

sn: वैचित्रवीर्यं पुरुषाः क्रोधहर्षसमावृताः। सिता बहुविधैः पाशैर्ये न तुष्टाः स्वकैर्धनैः॥ यमस्य वशमायान्ति काममूढाः पुनः पुनः। अन्धनेत्रा यथैवान्धा नीयमानाः स्वकर्मभिः॥
en: O son of Vichitravirya, men are surrounded with joy and wrath and so they are entangled in several sorts of trap. Those, who are not satisfied with their own wealth and those fools who act by desire, again and again come under the influence of the god of death in consequence of their own acts like those of blind eyes (falling again and again into pits) when led by the blind.

sn: एष एकायनः पन्था येन यान्ति मनीषिणः। तं दृष्ट्वा मृत्युमत्येति महांस्तत्र न सज्जति॥
en: That one is the only path by which the wise man goes (with a view to attain Brahma) and by aiming at that path a superior man overcomes death and attains the object of his ambition.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच अङ्ग संजय मे शंस पन्थानमकुतोभयम्। येन गत्वा हृषीकेशं प्राप्नुयां सिद्धिमुत्तमाम्॥
en: Dhritarashtra said Let me know, O Sanjaya, of that path, devoid of fears, going by which I shall obtain Hrishikesha and eternal salvation.

sn: संजय उवाच नाकृतात्मा कृतात्मानं जातु विद्याज्जनार्दनम्। आत्मनस्तु क्रियोपायो नान्यत्रेन्द्रियनिग्रहात्॥
en: Sanjaya said A man who has not his soul under control cannot know Janardana, who has his soul under control. The performance of sacrifices and other ceremonies, without being accompanied by a control of the senses, is not the proper way to go by for a man.

sn: इन्द्रियाणामुदीर्णानां कामत्यागोऽप्रमादतः। अप्रमादोऽविहिंसा च ज्ञानयोनिरसंशयम्॥
en: The renunciation of the objects of our desire, due to an excitement of the senses, arises from true knowledge. True knowledge and benevolence have their origin in wisdom, there is no doubt about it.

sn: इन्द्रियाणां यमे यत्तो भव राजन्नतन्द्रितः। बुद्धिश्च ते मा च्यवतु नियच्छैनां यतस्ततः॥
en: Therefore, O king, employ yourself in the controlling of your senses with wakefulness; and let not your intellect take the wrong course and keep it aloof from everything save the true path.

sn: एतज्ज्ञानं विदुर्विप्रा ध्रुवमिन्द्रियधारणम्। एतज्ज्ञानं च पन्थाश्च येन यान्ति मनीषिणः॥
en: The control of the senses is known by Brahmanas to be certainly the true wisdom; and true wisdom is the path along which an intelligent man goes.

sn: अप्राप्यः केशवो राजनिन्द्रियैरजितैर्नृभिः। आगमाधिगमाद् योगाद् वशी तत्त्वे प्रसीदति॥
en: Keshava is unattainable, o king, by men who have not controlled their senses. One who has his soul under control is pleased with true knowledge, gained by devotion and intimate knowledge of the holy books.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच भूयो मे पुण्डरीकाक्षं संजयाचक्ष्व पृच्छतः। नामकर्मार्थवित् तात प्राप्नुयां पुरुषोत्तमम्॥
en: Dhritarashtra said Repeat to me, who am asking, all that you have said regarding the Lotus-eyed (Krishna), so that by knowing the meaning of his names and his action I may attain to that best among male beings.

sn: संजय उवाच श्रुतं मे वासुदेवस्य नामनिर्वचनं शुभम्। यावत् तत्राभिजानेऽहमप्रमेयो हि केशवः॥
en: Sanjaya said The blessed list of name of the son of Vasudeva has been heard by me, from which it seems, so far as I can judge, that Keshava is immeasurable.

sn: वसनात् सर्वभूतानां वसुत्वाद् देवयोनितः। वासुदेवस्ततो वेद्यो बृहत्त्वाद् विष्णुरुच्यते॥
en: From his covering all creatures with illusion, from his being the support of the world and from his being of divine origin, he is know as Vasudeva. He is called Vishnu, owing to the fact of his pervading everything.

sn: मौनाद् ध्यानाच्च योगाच्च विद्धि भारत माधवम्। सर्वतत्त्वमयत्वाच्च मधुहा मधुसूदनः॥
en: From his practice of asceticism, from the application of his energy to the supreme truth and from his asceticism know him to be Madhava. O Bharata; and from his having within himself the essence of everything and from the fact of his killing Madhu, he is called Madhusudana.

sn: कृषि वाचकः शब्दो च निर्वृतिवाचकः। विष्णुस्तद्भावयोगाच्च कृष्णो भवति सात्वतः॥
en: Krishi is a word denotes existence; and may denotes eternal tranquility. From the combination of these two states is Vishnu, born of the Satvata race, called Krishna.

sn: पुण्डरीकं परं धाम नित्यमक्षयमव्ययम्। तद्वावात् पुण्डरीकाक्षो दस्युत्रासाज्जनार्दनः॥
en: Pundarika means the eternal regions; and Akshya ever means that which has no waste. From a combination of these two states is he called Pundarikaksha; and form his causing fear in wicked beings is he Janardana.

sn: यतः सत्त्वान्न च्यवते यच्च सत्त्वान्न हीयते। सत्त्वतः सात्वतस्तस्मादार्षभाद् वृषभेक्षणः॥
en: Since he is never dissociated from Sattva and since also Sattva is never dissociated from him; therefore is he called Sattavata. Owing to (the knowledge of) the Vedas being the eyes by which he is seen and the Vedas being the eyes through which he sees, he is called Vrishabha (Vedas) and Ikshana (eyes).

sn: न जायते जनित्राऽयमजस्तस्मादनीकजित्। देवानां स्वप्रकाशत्वाद् दमाद् दामोदरो विभुः॥
en: Not being born in the usual way, that conqueror of armies is called Aja; and from his being conspicuous among the gods and from his self-control is the Lord called Damodara.

sn: हर्षात् सुखात् सुखैश्वर्याधृषीकेशत्वमश्नुते। बाहुभ्यां रोदसी बिभ्रन्महाबाहुरिति स्मृतः॥
en: From the combination of the words, eternal happiness (hrishika) and the attributes of divinity (isha) is he called Hrishikesha. He is known as Mahabahu in the Smritis, as by his two arms he supports the earth and the sky.

sn: अधो न क्षीयते जातु यस्मात् तस्मादधोक्षजः। नराणामयनाच्चापि ततो नारायणः स्मृतः॥
en: Since he never falls down; nor he is wasted away; therefore, he is called Adhokshaja; and he is known as Narayana in the Smritis, as he is the refuge of human beings.

sn: पूरणात् सदनाच्चापि ततोऽसौ पुरुषोत्तमः। असतश्च सतश्चैव सर्वस्य प्रभवाप्ययात्॥
en: From his creating and preserving beings (Parva) and from destroying them (Sa) is he called Purushottama, as also from his being the creator of causes and effects which are also lost in him in the end.

sn: सर्वस्य च सदा ज्ञानात् सर्वमेतं प्रचक्षते। सत्ये प्रतिष्ठितः कृष्णः सत्यपत्र प्रतिष्ठितम्॥
en: Owing to his constant knowledge of everything is he called Sarva. Krishna is established on truth and truth is established on him.

sn: सत्यात् सत्यं तु गोविन्दस्तस्मात् सत्योऽपि नामतः। विष्णुर्विक्रमणाद् देवो जयनाज्जिष्णुरुच्यते॥
en: The name of Govinda is truth; because he is Truth of truths. Owing to his strength he is called Vishnu; and owing to his victory over the gods he is called Jishnu.

sn: शाश्वतत्वादनन्तश्च गोविन्दो वेदनाद् गवाम्। अतत्त्वं कुरुते तत्त्वं तेन मोहयते प्रजाः॥
en: Owing to his eternity is he called Ananta; and Govinda, owing to his control over the senses. He can make the unreal appear as the real, by which he deceives all creatures.

sn: एवंविधो धर्मनित्यो भगवान् मधुसूदनः। आगन्ता हि महाबाहुरानृशंस्यार्थमच्युतः॥
en: The divine slayer of Madhu, who has these qualities and who ever is attached to virtue, that being with long arms, who under goes no waste, will come here to see that there is no unnecessary slaughter.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच चक्षुष्मतां वै स्पृहयामि संजय द्रक्ष्यन्ति ये वासुदेव समीपे। विभ्राजमानं वपुषा परेण प्रकाशयन्तं प्रदिशो दिशश्च।।।।
en: Dhritarashtra said I envy those who have eyes, O Sanjaya and who will see before them the son of Vasudeva with his body shining with great lustre in the cardinal points of the earth and in the points between them.

sn: मभ्यर्चनीयां शङ्करीं सृजयानाम्। बुभूषद्भिर्ग्रहणीयामनिन्द्यां परासूनामग्रहणीयरूपाम्॥
en: And uttering blessed words which ought to be listened to with all respect by the Bharatas, words that are for the good of the Sanjayas, unexceptionable words that ought to be accepted by those praying for prosperity and incapable of being acted up to by those who are about to meet their end.

sn: समुद्यन्तं सात्वतमेकवीरं प्रणेतारमृषभं यादवानाम्। निहन्तारं क्षोभणं शात्रवाणां मुञ्चन्तं च द्विषतां वै यशांसि॥
en: Who (Krishna) is ever full of energy, eternal and the one hero in the world, who is the leader of the Yadavas and the bull among them; who is the slayer of his enemies and the cause of terror among them and the destroyer of the fame of his foes.

sn: द्रष्टारो हि कुरवस्तं समेता महात्मानं शत्रुहणं वरेण्यम्। ब्रुवन्तं वाचमनृशंसरूपां वृष्णिश्रेष्ठं मोहयन्तं मदीयान्॥
en: The sons of Kuru, assembled together, will see that worshipful slayer of his foes, of high soul, that foremost among the Vrishnis, speaking words full of benevolence and thus winning over my party.

sn: ऋषि सनातनतमं विपश्चितं वाचः समुद्रं कलशं यतीनाम्। अरिष्टनेमि गरुडं सुपर्ण हरिं प्रजानां भुवनस्य धाम॥ मनादिमध्यान्तमनन्तकीर्तिम्। शुक्रस्य धातारमजं च नित्यं परं परेषां शरणं प्रपद्ये॥
en: With that ascetic who is eternal and who has the knowledge of self, the ocean of words easily obtainable by anchorites, with that Arishta bird with beautiful wings, that destroyer of creatures, that refuge of the universe, that being with a thousand heads, that ancient Being who has neither beginning, nor end, nor middle, whose fame has no end who is the cause of the universal seed, who is without birth, who is eternity itself, shall I take refuge.

sn: त्रेलोक्यनिर्माणकरं जनित्रं देवासुराणामथ नागरक्षसाम्। मिन्द्रानुजं तं शरणं प्रपद्ये॥
en: I shall take refuge under the creator of the three worlds, the creator of the gods, Asuras, Nagas and Rakshasas, the chief among the rulers of men and learned men and that younger brother of Indra. On the return of Sanjaya, Yudhishthira, the king of virtue, said to the scion of the Dhritarashtra race (Krishna), that bull among all the Sattvatas.

sn: अयं स कालः सम्प्राप्तो मित्राणां मित्रवत्सला न च त्वदन्यं पश्यामि यो न आपत्सु तारयेत्॥
en: This is the time arrived for friends (to show that they are so), O you devoted to the interests of your friends. Any other save yourself I do not see, who could get us through this difficulty.

sn: त्वां हि माधवमाश्रित्य निर्भया मोघदर्पितम्। धार्तराष्ट्र सहामात्यं स्वयं समनुयुक्ष्महे॥
en: Depending on you, Madhava, we have without fear asked back our share (of the kingdom) from the son of Dhritarashtra and all his followers, who are filled with vain pride.

sn: यथा हि सर्वास्वापत्सु पासि वृष्णीनरिंदम) तथा ते पाण्डवा रक्ष्या: पाहस्मान् महतो भयात्॥
en: As you get through the Vrishnis out of all difficulties, O chastiser of chastiser of foes; so are the Pandavas, the proper party, to be protected by you. Get them through this great difficulty.

sn: श्रीभगवानुवाच अयमस्मि महाबाहो ब्रूहि यत् ते विवक्षितम्। करिष्यामि हि तत् सर्वं यत् त्वं वक्ष्यसि भारत॥
en: The blessed Krishna of divine attributes said Here am I, O you with long arms. Speak what you want to say. I shall do all that you will ask me to do, O Bharata.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच श्रुतं ते धृतराष्ट्रस्य सपुत्रस्य चिकीर्षितम्। एतद्धि सकलं कृष्ण संजयो मां यदब्रवीत्॥
en: Yudhishthira said You have heard what Dhritarashtra with his son intends to do. It is, O Krishna, exactly as Sanjaya told me.

sn: तन्मतं धृतराष्ट्रस्य सोऽस्यात्मा विवृतान्तरः। यथोक्तं दूत आचष्टे वध्यः स्यादन्यथा ब्रुवन्॥
en: Such are the intentions of Dhritarashtra; for Sanjaya knows the heart and is as his very soul, so to say. As an ambassador is instructed, so dose he speak; and if he speaks otherwise he should be killed.

sn: अप्रदानेन राज्यस्य शान्तिमस्मासु मार्गति। लुब्धः पापेन मनसा चरन्नसममात्मनः॥
en: Without restoring to us our kingdom ho wants peace with us; and the covetous man behaves by his sinful heart without impartiality towards those whose interests should be looked after by him equally.

sn: यत् तद् द्वादश वर्षाणि वनेषु ह्युषिता वयम्। छद्मना शरदं चैकां धृतराष्ट्रस्य शासनात्॥
en: For twelve years have the forests been inhabited by us; and at the command of Dhritarashtra have we lived in disguise for another year.

sn: स्थाता नः समये तस्मिन् धृतराष्ट्र इति प्रभो। नाहास्म समयं कृष्ण तद्धि नो ब्राह्मणा विदुः॥
en: So that Dhritarashtra might abide by those pledges of ours, O lord; the Brahmanas, O Krishna, in our company know that we did not break our pledges.

sn: गृद्धो राजा धृतराष्ट्रः स्वधर्मं नानुपश्यति। वश्यत्वात् पुत्रगृद्धित्वान्मन्दस्यान्वेति शासनम्॥
en: The avaricious king Dhritarashtra dose not follow the path of virtue of his class, and out of affection for his son and with a desire to please him he follows the course marked out by that fool.

sn: सुयोधनमते तिष्ठन् राजाऽस्मासु जनार्दन। मिथ्या चरति लुब्धः सन् चरन् हि प्रियमात्मनः॥
en: The king listening to the advice of Suyodhna, O Janardana, behaves deceitfully towards his own interests.

sn: इतो दुःखतरं किं नु यदहं मातरं ततः। संविधातुं न शक्नोमि मित्राणां वा जनार्दन॥
en: What is more regrettable than this that I am unable to be of any good to my mother or to my friends, O Janardana.

sn: काशिभिश्चेदिपञ्चालैर्मत्स्यैश्च मधुसूदन। भवता चैव नाथेन पञ्च ग्रामा वृता मया।॥
en: Five villages were only asked by me, who have the Kashis, the Chedis, the Panchalas and the Matsyas for my supporters and your exalted self for my lord.

sn: अविस्थलं वृकस्थलं माकन्दी वारणावतम्। अवसानं च गोविन्द कञ्चिदेवात्र पञ्चमम्॥
en: (The villages were) Avisthala, Vrikasthala, Makandi, Varanavata and any other, O Govinda, for the last or the fifth.

sn: पञ्च नस्तात दीयन्तां ग्रामा वा नगराणि वा। वसेम सहिता येषु मा च नो भरता नशन्॥
en: Give as, O Sire, (so we said) five villages or towns where we may reside united together; for we do not desire the destruction of the Bharatas.

sn: न च तानपि दुष्टात्मा धार्तराष्ट्रोऽनुमन्यते। स्वाम्यमात्मनि मत्वाऽसावतो दुःखतरं नु किम्॥
en: Not this even dose the wicked-souled son of Dhritarashtra grant, thinking the proprietary rights of the entire earth to be vested in him. What is there more regrettable than this.

sn: कुले जातस्य वृद्धस्य परवित्तेषु गृद्ध्यतः। लोभ प्रज्ञानमाहन्ति प्रज्ञा हन्ति श्रियम्॥
en: The avarice of man born in a noble family yet desiring to possess himself the wealth of others nullifies his wisdom; and the wisdom being destroyed, the sense of shame dose nowhere exist.

sn: श्रीर्हता बाधते धर्मं धर्मो हन्ति हतः श्रियम्। श्रीर्हता पुरुषं हन्ति पुरुषस्याधनं वधः॥
en: Sense of shame being lost, desire of virtue is weakened; and the destruction of virtue causes the decline of prosperity. Prosperity being lost, the man meets with death; for poverty is death to a man.

sn: अधनाद्धि निवर्तन्ते ज्ञातयः सुहृदो द्विजाः। अपुष्पादफलाद् वृक्षाद् यथा कृष्ण पतत्रिणः॥
en: Form a man stricken with property do cousins, friends and Brahmanas turn away; as from a tree without flowers and fruits the winged creatures turn away.

sn: एतच्च मरणं तात यन्मत्तः पतितादिव। ज्ञातयो विनिवर्तन्ते प्रेतसत्त्वादिवासवः॥
en: This I regard as death to me, O Sire, since from me the cousins away as from a fallen creature or breath forsakes an animal that is dead.

sn: नातः पापीयसी काञ्चिदवस्थां शम्बरोऽब्रवीत्। यत्र नैवाद्य न प्रातर्भोजनं प्रतिदृश्यते॥
en: Shambara was of opinion that there was no condition of life which could be more woeful than that in which a man cannot see what his food is to be tomorrow.

sn: धनमाहुः परं धर्मं धने सर्वं प्रतिष्ठितम्। जीवन्ति धनिनो लोके मृता ये त्वधना नराः॥
en: Wealth is said to be the best virtue. Everything is established on wealth; and wealthy men are living in this world and men without wealth are dead.

sn: ये धनादपकर्षन्ति नरं स्वबलमास्थिताः। ते धर्ममर्थ कामं च प्रमथ्नन्ति नरं च तम्॥
en: Those, who by force of their physical strength, deprived a man of his wealth, destroy the virtue, profit and pleasure of that man.

sn: एतामवस्थां प्राप्यैके मरणं वविरे जनाः। ग्रामायके वनायके नाशायैके प्रवव्रजुः॥
en: Having reached this condition (i.e. poverty) one class of men prefer death; another retire to villages (form cities); a third to the wilderness; while the fourth rove about with a view to meet speedy death.

sn: उन्मादमेके पुष्यन्ति यान्त्यन्ये द्विषतां वशम्। दास्यमेके च गच्छन्ति परेषामर्थहेतुना॥
en: One class of men become insane; another go under the control of their enemies; and a third become slaves for the sake of getting the wealth of others.

sn: आपदेवास्य मरणात् पुरुषस्य गरीयसी। श्रियो विनाशस्तद्ध्यस्य निमित्तं धर्मकामयोः॥
en: Poverty is a more potent evil to a man than death; for it destroys his prosperity. Wealth is the source of a man's virtue well as his pleasure.

sn: यदस्य धर्म्यं मरणं शाश्वतं लोकवर्त्म तत्। समन्तात् सर्वभूतानां न तदत्येति कश्चनः॥
en: The natural death of a man is like the ever recurring point of the wheel of this world. It is the unavoidable path of all creatures and none can avoid it.

sn: न तथा बाध्यते कृष्ण प्रकृत्या निर्धनो जनः। यथा भद्रां श्रियं प्राप्य हीनः सुखैधितः॥
en: A man without wealth from his very birth does not suffer so much, 0 Krishna, as one who after the possession of great prosperity and a life of great happiness is deprived of it.

sn: स तदाऽऽत्मापराधेन सम्प्राप्तोव्यसनं महत्। सेन्द्रान् गर्हयते देवान् नात्मानं च कथञ्चन॥
en: The man steeped in gigantic difficulties by his own short comings blames the gods with Indra and rarely himself.

sn: न चास्य सर्वशास्त्राणि प्रभवन्ति निबर्हणे। सोऽभिक्रुध्यति भृत्यानां सुहृदश्चाभ्यसूयति॥
en: His intimacy with all the holy books cannot procure him a mitigation of his sufferings. Sometimes he feels wrathful towards his servants; and afterwards he envies his friends.

sn: तं तदा मन्युरेवैति स भूयः सम्प्रमुह्यति। स मोहवशमापन्नः क्रूरं कर्म निषेवते॥
en: Ever subject to outbursts of passion, he sometimes loses his senses and getting himself under the control of his folly he attaches himself to the performance of evil deeds.

sn: पापकर्मतया चैव संकरं तेन पुष्यति। संकरो नरकायैव सा काष्ठा पापकर्मणाम्।।३३।
en: From his evil deeds spring confusion of castes; and a mixing up of castes is the way to hell, for it is the very culminating point of sinful deeds.

sn: न चेत् प्रबुध्यते कृष्ण नरकायैव गच्छति। तस्य प्रबोधः प्रज्ञैव प्रज्ञाचक्षुस्तरिष्यति॥
en: If he does not awake, he goes to hell O Krishna, wisdom alone is his awakening; the ey.es of wisdom alone can rescue him.

sn: प्रज्ञालाभे हि पुरुषः शास्त्राण्येवान्ववेक्षते। शास्त्रनिष्ठः पुनर्धर्मं तस्य ह्रीरङ्गमुत्तमम्॥
en: A man on obtaining the gift of wisdom follows the holy books. Observance of what is enjoyed in the holy books is the best virtue and modesty is the beautiful accompaniment of such a life.

sn: ह्रीमान् हि पापं प्रद्वेष्टि तस्य श्रीरभिवर्धते। श्रीमान् स यावद् भवति तावद् भवति पूरुषः॥
en: A man endued with a senses of shame despises sins and his prosperity ever increases. When he becomes endued with prosperity, then he is a man.

sn: धर्मनित्यः प्रशान्तात्मा कार्ययोगवहः सदा। नाधर्मं कुरुते बुद्धिं न च पापे प्रवर्तते॥
en: That clam soul, ever engaged in the practice of virtue and ever attached to action after mature thought, never turns his mind towards vice, nor ever turns to sin.

sn: अह्रीको वा विमूढो वा नैव स्त्री न पुनः पुमान्। नास्याधिकारो धर्मेऽस्ति यथा शूद्रस्तथैव सः॥
en: The one without a sense of shame is neither a woman nor a man. He has no claims upon virtue; he is as a Shudra.

sn: ह्रीमानवति देवांश्च पितॄनात्मानमेव च। तेनामृतत्वं व्रजति सा काष्ठा पुण्यकर्मणाम्॥
en: The man endued with a sense of shame pleases the gods, the Pitris and his own self; and by this does he obtain immortality which is the goal of men attached to virtuous acts.

sn: तदिदं मयि ते दृष्टं प्रत्यक्षं मधुसूदन यथा राज्यात् परिभ्रष्टो वसामि वसतीरिमाः॥
en: All this has been seen by you in me, o slayer of Madhu, namely, how I have lived these years, deprived of our kingdom.

sn: ते वयं न श्रियं हातुमलं न्यायेन केनचित्। अत्र नो यतमानानां वधश्चेदपि साधु तत्॥
en: There is no need for us to abandon that prosperity. In this case the death of ourselves, struggling to obtain back our prosperity, would be better.

sn: तत्र नः प्रथमः कल्पो यद् वयं ते च माधव। प्रशान्ताः समभूताश्च श्रियं तामश्नुवीमहि॥
en: With regard to that our intention the first thing is to enjoy that prosperity, themselves and ourselves united in peace and with the same interests, O Madhava.

sn: तत्रैषा परमा काष्ठा रौद्रकर्मक्षयोदया। यद् वयं कौरवान् हत्वा तानि राष्ट्राण्यवाप्नुमः॥
en: It is the greatest of all vicious deeds for us to prosper after this destruction-that we should obtain the kingdoms after slaying the sons of Kuru.

sn: ये पुनः स्युरसम्बद्धा अनार्याः कृष्ण शत्रवः। तेषामप्यवधः कार्यः किं पुनर्ये स्युरीदृशाः॥
en: Those that are not related to us, O Krishna, those dishonourable foes-the refrainment of slaying them too is our duty. What then is our duty towards those who are so closely related to us.

sn: ज्ञातयश्चैव भूयिष्ठाः सहाया गुरवश्च नः। तेषां वधोऽतिपापीयान् किं नो युद्धेऽस्ति शोभनम्।।४५
en: We have many cousins; and our elders are supporters (on both sides). Their destruction is extremely vicious. What then is the good in engaging in battle?

sn: पापः क्षत्रियधर्मोऽयं वयं च क्षत्रबन्धवः। स नः स्वधर्मोऽधर्मों वा वृत्तिरन्या विगर्हिता।॥
en: These practices of the Kshatriyas are sinful; but, alas, we are born in Kshatriya families and whether such practices are virtuous or the reverse; any other course of life would not be right!

sn: शूद्रः करोति शुश्रूषां वैश्या वै पण्यजीविकाः। वयं वधेन जीवामः कपालं ब्राह्मणैर्वृतम्॥
en: A Shudra serves (the other classes); a Vaishya lives by trade and commerce; we live by massacre; and the wooden plate (profession of begging) has been selected by the Brahmanas.

sn: क्षत्रियः क्षत्रियं हन्ति मत्स्यो मत्स्येन जीवति। श्वा श्वानं हन्ति दाशार्ह पश्य धर्मों यथागतः॥
en: A Kshatriya kills another Kshatriya; a fish lives on another fish; a dog kills another dog. See how each follows his rule of life, O you of the Dasharha race.

sn: युद्धे कृष्ण कलिनित्यं प्राणां सीदन्ति संयुगे। बलं तु नीतिमाधाय युध्ये जयपराजयौ।॥
en: In battle, O Krishna, Kali is ever present; in a battle lives are lost; but, in spite of fixed policy applied to fighting, success and defeat.

sn: नात्मच्छन्देन भूतानां जीवितं मरणं तथा। नाप्यकाले सुखं प्राप्यं दुःखं वापि यदूत्तम॥
en: Are not dependent on the will (of the combatants); as life and death are independent of the will of creatures. Until the right time happiness cannot be attained, nor misery, O you best of the Yadu race.

sn: एको ह्यपि बहून् हन्ति जन्त्येकं बहवोऽष्युत। शूरं कापुरुषो हन्ति अयशस्वी यशस्विनम्॥
en: One man kills many; and many also united kill one. A coward kills a real hero, known to fame, a renowned warrior.

sn: जयो नैवोभयोर्दष्टो नोभयोश्च पराजयः। तथैवापचयो दृष्टो व्यपयाने क्षयव्ययौ।॥
en: Both parties cannot live to behold victory nor can both parties live to see defeat but the waste and the loss may be seen to be on both sides. To a man attempting to fly there come both loss (of life, and expense.

sn: सर्वथा वृजिनं युद्धं को जन् न प्रतिहन्यते। हतस्य च हृषीकेश समौ जयपराजयौ।॥
en: In all cases fight is an evil. Who that strikes is not struck in return? But victory and defeat, O Hrishikesha, are of the same moment to one that is killed.

sn: पराजयश्च मरणान्मन्ये नैव विशिष्यते। यस्य स्याद् विजयः कृष्ण तस्याप्यपचयो ध्रुवम्॥
