en: Defeat is not very much better than death I think; he on whose side victory is declared, O Krishna, also has surely to meet with a loss.

sn: अन्ततो दयितं नन्ति केचिदप्यपरे जनाः। तस्याङ्ग बलहीनस्य पुत्रान् भ्रातृनपश्यतः॥
en: At least the men on the other side kill some one who is dear; and a man, thus rendered weak, O adorable one and not seeing his sons and brothers.

sn: निर्वेदो जीविते कृष्ण सर्वतश्चोपजायते। ये ह्येव धीरा ह्रीमन्त आर्याः करुणवेदिनः॥ त एव युद्धे हन्यन्ते यवीयान् मुच्यते जनः। हत्वाप्यनुशयो नित्यं परानपि जनार्दन॥
en: Lives on, O Krishna, as if in unconsciousness and his purposes are foiled at every step. Those who are modest, prudent, honourable, kind and wise are killed in battle; while a wicked avoids defeat. Even after killing the enemy we become a prey to repentance, OJanardana.

sn: अनुबन्धश्च पापोऽत्र शेषश्चाप्यवशिष्यते। शेषों हि बलमासाद्य न शेषमनुशेषयेत्॥
en: In the end the result is that a surviver gives a lot of troubles and in the end collecting an army puts an end to what remains.

sn: सर्वोच्छेदे च यतते वैरस्यान्तविधित्सया। जयो वैरं प्रसृजति दुःखमास्ते पराजितः॥
en: One makes attempts at putting an end to everything through a desire to settle the dispute. Victory gives birth to enmity; and that which has met with defeat lives in misery.

sn: सुखं प्रशान्तः स्वपिति हित्वा जयपराजयौ। जातवैस्च पुरुषो दुःखं स्वपिति नित्यदा॥
en: A man peacefully enjoys lives in the case of leaving aside all thoughts of victory and defeat; but a man who has created an enemy ever sleeps in misery.

sn: अनिवृत्तेन मनसा ससर्प इव वेश्मनि। उत्सादयति यः सर्वं यशसा स विमुच्यते॥
en: Without calmness in his mind as if he lives in a house infested by snakes. He who puts an end to everything (of the enemy in battle) gets no fame.

sn: अकीर्तिं सर्वभूतेषु शाश्वती सोऽधिगच्छति। न हि वैराणि शाम्यन्ति दीर्घकालधृतान्यपि॥
en: And he gets the reverse of fame from all beings throughout his life. Enmity though kept alive for a long time is never brought to an end.

sn: आख्यातारश्च विद्यन्ते पुमांश्चेद् विद्यते कुले। न चापि वैरं वैरेण केशव व्युपशाम्यति॥
en: There should be no story-teller (to remind him of his wrongs) so long as there is a man alive in the enemy's) family. Enmity, is never turned into peace by enmity, O Keshava.

sn: हविषाग्निर्यथा कृष्ण भूय एवाभिवर्धते। अतोऽन्यथा नास्ति शान्तिनित्यमन्तरमन्ततः॥
en: But it increases as fire fed by clarified butter. There is no exception to this; and peace is ever only obtainable by total annihilation.

sn: अन्तरं लिप्समानानामयं दोषो निरन्तरः। पौरुषे यो हि बलवानाधिर्हदयबाधनः। तस्य त्यागेन वा शान्तिर्मरणेनापि वा भवेत्॥
en: Defects may always be found on either side, by which advantage is sought to be obtained. Manly strength is ever the source of pain in the innermost heart of a man; and peace is attainable only by leaving aside war or by death.

sn: अथवा मूलघातेन द्विषतां मधुसूदन। फलनिवृत्तिरिद्धा स्यात् तन्नृशंसतरं भवेत्॥
en: By putting an end to the enemy to the roots, O slayer of Madhu, we can attain to our object; but it is most cruel.

sn: या तु त्यागेन शान्तिः स्यात् तदृते वध एव सः। संशयाच्च समुच्छेदाद् द्विषतामात्मनस्तथा॥
en: The peace that we can obtain by foregoing our claim to the kingdom is in effect the same thing as the total extinction of ourselves and the enemy or the uncertainly of victory.

sn: न च त्यक्तुं तदिच्छामो न चेच्छामः कुलक्षयम्। अत्र या प्रणिपातेन शान्तिः सैव गरीयसी॥
en: We do not wish to give up that (kingdom); nor do you wish death of our family; and in such a case that peace which we can obtain through bending ourselves to the will of the other side is preferable.

sn: सर्वथा यतमानानामयुद्धमभिकाङ्क्षताम्। सान्त्वे प्रतिहते युद्धं प्रसिद्धं नापराक्रमः॥
en: When all the attempts of those, who are trying to obtain the kingdom by all means without war, fail; then war is proper for them and not a show of weakness.

sn: प्रतिघातेन सान्त्वस्य दारुणं सम्प्रवर्तते। तच्छुनामिव सम्पाते पण्डितैरुपलक्षितम्॥
en: On the event of these (attempts at obtaining the desired object without war), the results that follow are terrible. All these have been observed by wise men in a war between dogs.

sn: लाडूलचालनं क्ष्वेडा प्रतिवाचो विवर्तनम्। दन्तदर्शनमारावस्ततो युद्धं प्रवर्तते॥
en: First there comes the wagging of tails, then the bark, then the replying back, then the turning of one round the other, then the show of teeth, then the roaring and then comes the commencement of the fight.

sn: तत्र यो बलवान् कृष्ण जित्वा सोऽत्ति तदामिषम्। एवमेव मनुष्येषु विशेषो नास्ति कश्चन॥
en: In the fight the one, who is stronger, O Krishna, gains the victory and eats the other's flesh. Such is the case with men; there is no difference whatever.

sn: सर्वथा त्वेतदुचितं दुर्बलेषु बलीयसाम्। अनादरोऽविरोधश्च प्रणिपाती हि दुर्बलः॥
en: It should always be the duty of a strong man not to crush hostility with the weak; and the weak should be deferential to the strong.

sn: पिता राजा च वृद्धश्च सर्वथा मानमर्हति। तस्मान्मान्यश्च पूज्यश्च धृतराष्ट्रो जनार्दन॥
en: It is proper that the father, the king and the aged should be treated always with respect; therefore is Dhritarashtra the object of our worship and respect, O Janardana.

sn: पुत्रस्नेहश्च बलवान् धृतराष्ट्रस्य माधव। स पुत्रवशमापन्नः प्रणिपातं प्रहास्यति॥
en: The feeling of affection for his son is stronger in Dhritarashtra, O Madhava. Subject to the will of his son, he will laugh away our respectful submission.

sn: तत्र किं मन्यसे कृष्ण प्राप्तकालमनन्तरम्। कथमर्थाच्च धर्माच्च न हीयेमहि माधव॥
en: What then do you think, O Krishna, to be suitable to the occasion. By what means shall I not deviate from virtue and from worldly good, O Madhava.

sn: ईदृशेऽत्यर्थकृच्छ्रेऽस्मिन् कमन्यं मधुसूदन। उपसम्प्रष्टुमर्हामि त्वामृते पुरुषोत्तम॥
en: In such a difficulty whom other, 0 slayer of Madhu, but yourself is it proper for us to consult, O best among men.

sn: प्रियश्च प्रियकामश्च गतिज्ञः सर्वकर्मणाम्। को हि कृष्णास्ति नस्त्वादृक् सर्वनिश्चयवित् सुहृत्।।७८
en: Who is there, O Krishna, who is so dear a friend to ourselves, who desires our welfare so much, who knows so well the course of all acts and who is so well acquainted with the results of everything.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्तः प्रत्युवाच धर्मराजं जनार्दनः। उभयोरेव वामर्थं यास्यामि कुरुसंसदम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Thus addressed, Janardana said to the king of virtue in reply. For the good for the good cause of both to you shall I go to the encampment of the Kurus.

sn: शमं तत्र लभेयं चेद् युष्मदर्थमाहापयन्। पुण्यं सुमहद् राजंश्चरितं स्यान्महाफलम्॥
en: If I succeed in ensuring peace there without a sacrifice of our interests, then will an act of great virtue and of large fruits be done by me, O king.

sn: मोचयेयं मृत्युपाशात् संरब्धान् कुरुसुंजयान्। पाण्डवान् धार्तराष्ट्रांश्च सर्वां च पृथिवीमिमाम्॥
en: Then shall I free the band of the fated Kurus and Pandavas from the trap of death, as also this earth and all the sons of Dhritarashtra.

sn: मे युधिष्ठिर उवाच न ममैतन्मतं कृष्णं यत् त्वं यायाः कुरून् प्रति। सुयोधनः सूक्तमपि न करिष्यति ते वचः॥
en: Yudhishthira said It is not my wish, O Krishna, that you should go to the Kurus. For Suyodhana, though spoken in a most friendly manner and for his own good, will not listen to your words.

sn: समेतं पार्थिवं क्षत्रं दुर्योधनवशानुगम्। तेषां मध्यावतरणं तव कृष्ण न रोचये॥
en: It is not proper for you, O Krishna, to go into the midst of that assembly of Kshatriya rulers of the earth, who follow the lead of Duryodhana.

sn: न हि नः प्रीणयेद् द्रव्यं न देवत्वं कुतः सुखम्। न च सर्वामरैश्वर्यं तव द्रोहेण माधव॥
en: The gain of our object will not make us cheerful and what happiness shall we obtain from god-ship or the lordship over the immortals, if any ill happens to you.

sn: श्रीभगवानुवाच जानाम्येतां महाराज धार्तराष्ट्रस्य पापताम्। अवाच्यास्तु भविष्यामः सर्वलोके महीक्षिताम्॥
en: The blessed God said I know the vicious nature, O great king, of that son of Dhritarashtra; but (by doing as I say) shall we not be spoken ill of in all these worlds in the universe.

sn: न चापि मम पर्याप्ताः सहिताः सर्वपार्थिवाः। क्रुद्धस्य संयुगे सिंहस्येवेतरे मृगाः॥
en: All the rulers of the earth united together are not powerful enough to stand before me in battle when I am angry, like all other animals before a lion.

sn: अथ चेत् ते प्रवर्तन्ते मयि किञ्चिदसाम्प्रतम्। निर्दहेयं कुरून् सर्वानिति मे धीयते मतिः॥
en: If they offer insult to me desiring for their good, I shall consume all the Kurus-such is my intention.

sn: न जातु गमनं पार्थ भवेत् तत्र निरर्थकम्। अर्थप्राप्तिः कदाचित् स्यादन्ततो वाप्यवाच्यता॥
en: O son of Pritha, my going there shall not be without results. There will be some gain in going there, at least we shall not be blamed by others.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच यत् तुभ्यं रोचते कृष्ण स्वस्ति प्राप्नुहि कौरवान्। कृतार्थं स्वस्तिमन्तं त्वां द्रक्ष्यामि पुनरागतम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said As you please, O Krishna. May all that is good come out of it. Go to the sons of Kuru. May I see you return with your object gained and in health.

sn: विष्वक्सेन कुरून् गत्वा भरताञ्छमयन् प्रभो। यथा सर्वे सुमनसः सह स्याम सुचेतसः॥
en: Going to the Kurus, establish such peace among the sons of Bharata, O Lord, that we may live with all of them with cheerful minds and in contentment.

sn: भ्राता चासि सखा चासि बीभत्सोर्मम च प्रियः। सौहृदेनाविशयोऽसि स्वस्ति प्राप्नुहि भूतये॥
en: You are my brother and you are my friend dear to me as Vibhatsa. Relying on your friendship we are not at all anxious. May all that is good attend you, who are going for our interests.

sn: अस्मान् वेत्थ परान् वेत्थ वेत्थार्थान् वेस्थ भाषितुम्। यद् यदस्मद्धितं कृष्ण तत्तद् वाच्यः सुयोधनः॥
en: You know us and you know our enemy; you know what is conducive to our interests and you know what to say. Suyodhana should be addressed in such a way as will be for our benefit.

sn: यद्यधर्मेण संयुक्तमुपपद्येद्धितं वचः। तत्तत् केशव भाषेथाः सान्त्वं वा यदि वेतरत्॥
en: Even if words that are beneficial (to both parties) do not strictly conform to virtue (e.g. peace even by our getting only five villages, which is a sin) or whatever they are (e.g. even if I am to play at a game of dice again) should be spoken by you, O Keshava.

sn: श्रीभगवानुवाच संजयस्य श्रुतं वाक्यं भवतश्च श्रुतं मया। सर्वं जानाम्यभिप्रायं तेषां च भवतश्च यः॥
en: The blessed God said The words of Sanjaya have been listened to by me as also your words. I know all their intentions and also those of yours.

sn: तव धर्माश्रिता बुद्धिस्तेषां वैराश्रया मतिः। यदयुद्धेन लभ्येत तत् ते बहुमतं भवेत्॥
en: Your intentions are established on virtue; while their purposes are based on malice. What is gained by not having recourse to war, is much in your estimate.

sn: न चैवं नेष्ठिकं कर्म क्षत्रियस्य विशाम्पते। आहुराश्रमिणः सर्वे न भैक्षं क्षत्रियश्चरेत्॥
en: A life-long practice of Brahmacharya vow is not the proper course of life for a Kshatriya, O lord of the universe. All the householders have said that a Kshatriya should not gain his livelihood by begging.

sn: जयो वधो वा संग्रामे धात्राऽऽदिष्टः सनातनः। स्वधर्मः क्षत्रियस्यैष कार्पण्यं न प्रशस्यते॥
en: Victory or death has been originally fixed by the Father of the universe. The proper course of life for a Kshatriya is this (war) and it is not proper to show a humiliating spirit in this course. son

sn: न हि कार्पण्यमास्थाय शक्या वृत्तियुधिष्ठिर। विक्रमस्व महाबाहो जहि शत्रून् परंतप॥
en: Earning one's livelihood is not possible by a policy based on a humiliating spirit, O Yudhishthira; show your strength, O you with long arms and conquer your enemies, O you chastiser of your enemies.

sn: अतिगृद्धाः कृतस्नेहा दीर्घकालं सहोषिताः। कृतमित्राः कृतबला धार्तराष्ट्राः परंतप॥
en: The exceedingly avaricious of Dhritarashtra, has, O chastiser of your enemies, lived for too long a time united with other, enjoying their affection and their friendship and supported by them.

sn: योऽस्ति यत् साम्यं त्वयि कुर्युर्विशाम्पते। बलवत्तां हि मन्यन्ते भीष्मद्रोणकृपादिभिः॥
en: The peace of the Kurus with you is therefore not expedient or desirable (they think), O lord of the universe. They think themselves strong having on their side Bhishma, Drona, Kripa and others.

sn: यावच्च मार्दवेनैतान् राजन्नुपचरिष्यसि। तावदेते हरिष्यन्ति तव राज्यमरिंदम॥
en: So long as you treat these, O king, with kindness, they will deprive you of your kingdom, O you chastiser of your foes.

sn: नानुक्रोशान्न कार्पण्यान्न च धर्माथकाराणात्। अलं कर्तुं धार्तराष्ट्रास्तव काममरिंदम्॥
en: Not out of kindness, nor out of cowardice and not even from a desire to gain virtue or profit will the son of Dhritarashtra do as you wish, O you chastiser of your foes.

sn: एतदेवं निमित्तं ते पाण्डवास्तु यथा त्वयि। नान्वतप्यन्त कौपीनं तावत् कृत्वापि दुष्करम्॥
en: This is an example of the feeling they bear you, O son of Pandu. They are not even sorry for making you wear the Kaupinas (a strip of cloth-a sign of a mendicant and undergoing all these hardships.

sn: पितामहस्य द्रोणस्य विदुरस्य च धीमतः। ब्राह्मणानां च साधूनां राज्ञश्च नगरस्य च॥ पश्यतां कुरुमुख्यानां सर्वेषामेव तत्त्वतः। दानशीलं मृदुं दान्तं धर्मशीलमनुव्रतम्॥ यत् त्वामुपधिना राजन् द्यूते वञ्चितवांस्तदा। न चापत्रपते तेन नृशंसः स्वेन कर्मणा॥
en: When before the very eyes of the grandfather (Bhishma), Drona, the wise Vidura and the Brahmanas, holy men and the entire city and before all the chiefs among the Kurus, he, O king, by means of deceit, defeated you at a game of dice, you who are attached to the habit of making gifts, who are of virtuous habits and life of austere vows, he was not ashamed of his cruel act.

sn: तथाशीलसमाचारे राजन् मा प्रणयं कृथाः। वध्यास्ते सर्वलोकस्य किं पुनस्तव भारत॥
en: With one who is of such habits of life, do not, O king, contract a friendship; they are fit to be killed by any man; then why not by you, OBharata.

sn: वाग्भिस्त्वप्रतिरूपाभिरतुदत् त्वां सहानुजम्। श्लाघमानः प्रहृष्टः सन् भ्रातृभिः सह भाषते॥
en: With improper speeches against you did they boast rejoicingly with their brothers, at yourself and your younger.

sn: एतावद् पाण्डवानां हि नास्ति किंचिदिह स्वकम्। नामधेयं च गोत्रं च तदप्येषां न शिष्यते॥
en: He said-Now have the sons of Pandu nothing to call their own in this world. Their very names and the name of their family even no longer exist.

sn: चैषां भविष्यति पराभवः। प्रकृति ते भजिष्यन्ति नष्टप्रकृतयो मयि॥
en: As great time rolls on, they will meet with defeat. Your subjects no longer yours will now adhere to me.

sn: कालेन महता दुःशासनेन पापेन तदा द्यूते प्रवर्तिते। अनाथवत् तदा देवी द्रौपदी सुदुरात्मना॥
en: By the vicious and exceedingly wickedsouled Dushasana, while the game of dice was yet going on, was the lady Draupadi like one having none to protect her.

sn: आकृष्य केशे रुदती सभायां राजसंसदि। भीष्मद्रोणप्रमुखतो गौरिति व्याहृता मुहुः॥
en: Dragged by the hair weeping in the assembly of kings in the council; and in the very presence of Bhishma and Drona they called her cow again and again.

sn: भवता वारिताः सर्वे भ्रातरो भीमविक्रमाः। धर्मपाशनिबद्धाश्च न किंचित् प्रतिपेदिरे॥
en: All your brothers of terrible strength dissuaded by you and tied by the trap of virtue did absolutely nothing at this.

sn: एताश्चान्याश्च परुषा वाचः स समुदीरयन्। श्लाघते ज्ञातिमध्ये स्म त्वयि प्रव्रजिते धनम्॥
en: He pronounced these cruel words and others and he expressed plea are among his cousins at your being exiled into the forest.

sn: तत्रासन् समानीतास्ते दृष्ट्वा त्वामनागसम्। अश्रुकण्ठा रुदन्तश्च सभायामासते तदा॥
en: Those who were assembled there, seeing you without any fault at the time sat in the council weeping with choked voices.

sn: न चैनमभ्यनन्दस्ते राजानो ब्राह्मणैः सह। सर्वे दुर्योधनं तत्र निन्दन्ति स्म सभासदः॥
en: Those kings along with the Brahmanas did not praise him for this; and all the courtiers there spoke ill of Duryodhana,

sn: कुलीनस्य च या निन्दा वधो वाऽमित्रकर्शन। महागुणो वधो राजन् न तु निन्दा कुजीविका॥
en: Blame to one born in a high family is death itself, O you chastiser of your foes. Worthless life with blame attached is death many times over, Oking.

sn: तदैव निहतो राजन् यदैव निरपत्रपः। निन्दितश्च महाराज पृथिव्या सर्वराजभिः॥
en: Since that time is he dead, when he was without shame, though blamed by all the kings on earth, O great king.

sn: ये ईषत् कार्यो वधस्तस्य यस्य चारित्रमीदृशम्। प्रस्कन्देन प्रतिस्तधश्छिन्नमूल इव दुमः॥
en: He whose character is of this description can be killed with very little effort like a tree with all its roots cut asunder and standing only on its principal root.

sn: वध्यः सर्प इवानार्यः सर्वलोकस्य दुर्मतिः। जह्येनं त्वममित्रघ्न मा राजन् विचिकित्सिथाः॥
en: Like a serpent is that dishonourable and wicked-souled wretch fit to he slain by everyone. Kill him therefore, O you slayer of your foes; and do not hesitate, Oking.

sn: सर्वथा त्वक्षमं चैतद् रोचते च ममानघ। यत् त्वं पितरि भीष्मे च प्रणिपातं समाचरेः॥
en: It is proper by all means and my wish, too, that you should pay proper respects to him who is like a father to you, as also to Bhishma.

sn: अहं तु सर्वलोकस्य गत्वा छेत्स्यामि संशयम्। येषामस्ति द्विधाभावो राजन् दुर्योधनं प्रति॥
en: I, too, going there, shall remove the doubts of all men, who are of one opinion and now of another regarding Duryodhana, O king.

sn: मध्ये राज्ञामहं तत्र प्रातिपौरुषिकान् गुणान्। तव संकीर्तयिष्यामि ये च तस्य व्यतिक्रमाः॥
en: In the midst of the kings shall I describe all your good qualities among men, as also defects.

sn: ब्रुवतस्तत्र मे वाक्यं धर्मार्थसहितं हितम्। निशम्य पार्थिवाः सर्वे नानाजनपदेश्वराः॥
en: Hearing me, speak beneficial words conducive to both virtue and worldly good. All the rulers of the earth, the lords of the different provinces,

sn: त्वयि सम्प्रतिपत्स्यन्ते धर्मात्मा सत्यवागिति। तस्मिश्चाधिगमिष्यन्ति यथा लोभादवर्तत।॥
en: Will know you to be virtuous shouted and truthful of speech and will know how avariciously inclined he is.

sn: गर्हयिष्यामि चैवैनं पौरजानपदेष्वपि। वृद्धबालानुपादाय चातुर्वर्ये समागते॥
en: I shell speak of his defects before both people of towns and villages, before both old and young and before all the members of the four orders assembled there.

sn: शमं वै याचमानस्त्वं नाधर्मं तत्र लप्स्यसे। कुरून् विगर्हयिष्यन्ति धृतराष्ट्रं च पार्थिवाः॥
en: You will not be called sinful there; for you ask peace and the rulers of the earth will blame the Kurus and Dhritarashtra.

sn: तस्मिँल्लोकपरित्यक्ते किं कार्यमवशिष्यते।। हते दुर्योधने राजन् यदन्यत् क्रियतामिति॥
en: When he is forsaken by men, what shall there be left to be done and Duryodhana is killed; do whatever remains to be accomplished.

sn: यात्वा चाहं कुरून् सर्वान् युष्मदर्थमहापयन्। यतिष्ये प्रशमं कर्तुं लक्षयिष्ये च चेष्टितम्॥
en: Going to all the Kurus, I shall seek to effect peace without any sacrifice of your interests; and shall observe their intentions.

sn: कौरवाणां प्रवृत्तिं च गत्वा युद्धाधिकारिकाम्। निशम्य विनिवर्तिष्ये जयाय तव भारत॥
en: Having observed and made out the intentions of the sons of Kuru and their preparations for war I shall come back to make victory yours, O Bharata.

sn: सर्वथा युद्धमेवाहमाशंसामि परैः सह। निमित्तानि हि सर्वाणि तथा प्रादुर्भवन्ति मे॥
en: I anticipate war with the enemy by all mcans. It seems to me that all the signs indicate the same.

sn: मृगाः शकुन्ताश्च वदन्ति घोरं हस्त्यश्वमुख्येषु निशामुखेषु। वर्णान् बहून् पुष्यति घोररूपान्॥३९।
en: The birds and beasts are making loud sounds; and the best of elephants and horses assume terrible appearances at the approach of night. Fire too assumes many terrific looking colours.

sn: मनुष्यलोकक्षयकृत् सुघोरो नो चेदनुप्राप्त इहान्तकः स्यात्। शस्त्राणि यन्त्रं कवचा रथांश्च नागान् हयांश्च प्रतिपादयित्वा॥ योधाश्च सर्वे कृतनिश्चयास्ते भवन्तु हस्त्यश्वरथेषु यत्ताः। सांग्रामिकं ते यदुपार्जनीयं सर्वं समग्रं कुरु तन्नरेन्द्र॥
en: If the cause of waste among men and the world generally were not near at hand, these omens indicating evils would never have been here. Keeping ready for use their arms, machines, helmets, cars, elephants and horses, let all your soldiers be prepared for battle; and let them be careful about their horses, elephants and chariots. O chief of men, collect together all that ought to be kept ready for the battle.

sn: दुर्योधनो न ह्यलमद्य दातुं जीवंस्तवैतनृपते कथंचित्। यत्ते पुरस्तादभवत् समृद्ध द्यूते हृतं पाण्डवमुख्य राज्यम्॥
en: Duryodhana, O lord of men, will not be able to return you any portion of your prosperous territories which were yours in days of old and which he stole from you at a game of dice.

sn: भीम उवाच यथा यथैव शान्तिः स्यात् कुरूणां मधुसूदन। तथा तथैव भाषेथा मा स्म युद्धेन भीषयेः॥
en: Bhima said In such a way that there may be peace among the Kurus, O slayer of Madhu, should you speak. Do not frighten them with the prospect of war.

sn: अमर्षी जातसंरम्भः श्रेयोद्वेषी महामनाः। नोग्रं दुर्योधनो वाच्यः साम्नैवैनं समाचरेः॥
en: Resentful wrathful, not accepting what is for his good and of a vain disposition, Duryodhana should not be spoken to in harsh terms. He should be treated with courtesy.

sn: प्रकृत्या पापसत्त्वश्च तुल्यचेतास्तु दस्युभिः। ऐश्वर्यमदमत्तश्च कृतवैस्च पाण्डवैः॥
en: He is by nature of a wicked disposition and has a heart equal to that of the robbers; he is vain with the sense of possession of prosperity and an enemy of the Pandavas.

sn: अदीर्घदर्शी निष्ठूरी क्षेप्ता क्रूरपराक्रमः। दीर्घमन्युरनेयश्च पापात्मा निकृतिप्रियः॥
en: He is without foresight and cruel; and he has the habit of finding fault with others; and he is of crooked prowess, of malice which lasts for a long time and does not permit himself to be led by others, of a wicked soul and fond of deceit.

sn: नियेतापि न भज्येत् नैव जह्यात् स्वकं मतम्। तादृशेन शमः कृष्ण मन्ये परमदुष्करः॥
en: Even if he dies he would not tender his submission, nor give up or alter his own opinions. Peace with such an one, O Krishna, I consider to be difficult of effecting.

sn: सुहृदामप्यवाचीनस्त्यक्तधर्मा प्रियानृतः। प्रतिहन्त्येव सुहृदां वाचश्चैव मनांसि च॥
en: He does not listen to even the words of his well-wishers, destitute of virtue, fond of falsehood and always goes against the advice and intentions of his well-wishers.

sn: स मन्युवशमापन्नः स्वभावं दुष्टमास्थितः। स्वभावात् पापमभ्येति तृणैश्छन्न इवोरगः॥
en: Depending on his own natural wickedness and subject to the impulse of wrath, he as if by nature, acts sinfully like a serpent hid among the grass.

sn: दुर्योधनो हि यत्सेनः सर्वथा विदितस्तव। यच्छीलो यत्स्वभावश्च यद्बलो यत्पराक्रमः॥
en: The extent and numbers of the army of Duryodhana are all known to you, as also the nature of his conduct; and his habits of life and the measure of his strength and prowess.

sn: पुरा प्रसन्नाः कुरवः सहपुत्रास्तथा वयम्। इन्द्रज्येष्ठा इवाभूम मोदमानाः सबान्धवाः॥
en: In days of old the Kurus along with their sons were cheerful at heart and so were we, rejoicing with our kinsmen like the younger brothers of Indra himself.

sn: दुर्योधनस्य क्रोधेन भरता मधुसूदन। धक्ष्यन्ते शिशिरापाये वनानीव हुताशनैः॥
en: Owing to the spite of Duryodhana, the Bharatas, O slayer of Madhu, will be burnt up like the forest by fire at the close of winter.

sn: अष्टादशेमे राजानः प्रख्याता मधुसूदन। ये समुच्चिच्छिदुर्शातीन् सुहृदश्च सबान्धवान्॥
en: These eighteen kings are well known, O destroyer of Madhu, who annihilated their cousins, friends all well-wishers.

sn: असुराणां समृद्धानां ज्वलतामिव तेजसा। पर्यायकाले धर्मस्य प्राप्ते कलिरजायत।॥ हैहयानां मुदावर्तो नीपानां जनमेजयः। बहुलस्तालजंघानां कृमीणामुद्धतो वसुः॥ अजबिन्दुः सुवीराणां सुराष्ट्राणां रुषर्द्धिकः। अर्कजश्च बलीहानां चीनानां धौतमूलकः॥ हयग्रीवो विदेहानां वरयुश्च महौजसाम्। बाहुः सुन्दरवंशानां दीप्ताक्षाणां पुरूरवाः॥ सहजश्चेदिमत्स्यानां प्रवीराणां वृषध्वजः। धारणश्चन्द्रवत्सानां मुकुटानां विगाहनः॥ शमश्च नन्दिवेगानामित्येते कुलपांसनाः। युगान्ते कृष्ण सम्भूताः कुले कुपुरुषाधमाः॥
en: As when Dharma reached the end of his time, Kali was born resplendent with energy in the prosperous race of Asuras; so were born Mudavarta among Haihayas, Janamejaya among the Nipas, Bahula among the Talajanghas and the proud Vasu among the Krimis and Ajabindu among the Suviras, Rushardhika among the Surashtras, Arkaja among the Balih, Dhautamulaka among the Chinas, Hayagriva among the Videhas, Varayu among the Mahonjasas, Bahu among the Sundaravansas, Pururava among the Diptakshas, Sahaja among the Chedis and Matsyas, Vrishadhvaja among the Praviras, Dharana among the Chandravatsas, Vigahanu among the Mukutas and Shama among the Nandivegas. These wicked beings in each family were born, O Krishna, at the end of each Yuga for the destruction of their own family.

sn: अप्ययं नः कुरूणां स्याद् युगान्ते कालसम्भृतः। दुर्योधनः कुलाङ्गारो जघन्यः पापपूरुषः॥
en: So has this Duryodhana been born at the end of this Yuga in our family-that of the Kurus-that wicked individual, the vilest and most despicable of his race, for the extinction of his race.

sn: तस्मान्मृदु शनै—या धर्मार्थसहितं हितम्। कामानुबद्धंबहुलं नोग्रमुग्रपराक्रमः॥
en: There should he be spoken slowly and mildly in words conducive to our interests and to virtue and worldly good and going fully into the subject, so as to attract his heart towards us and not in harsh words, O you of terrific strength.

sn: अपि दुर्योधनं कृष्ण सर्वे वयमधश्चराः। नीचैर्भूत्वानुयास्यामो मा स्म नो भरतानशन्॥
en: We would rather, O Krishna, follow the lead of Duryodhana and be under his control; but let not the Bharatas be destroyed.

sn: अप्युदासीनवृत्तिः स्याद् यथा नः कुरुभिः सह। वासुदेव तथा कार्यं न कुरूननयः स्पृशेत्॥
en: O Son of Vasudeva, act in such a way that we may live as strangers to the Kurus; but let not the sin of annihilating men touch the Kurus.

sn: वाच्यः पितामहो वृद्धो ये च कृष्ण सभासदः। भ्रातृणामस्तु सौभ्रात्रं धार्तराष्ट्रः प्रशाम्यताम्॥
en: Our grandfather and those courtiers, who are aged, O Krishna, should be spoken to. Let there be brotherly feeling among the brothers and peace to the son of Dhritarashtra.

sn: अहमेतद् ब्रवीम्येवं राजा चैव प्रशंसति। अर्जुनो नैव युद्धार्थी भूयसी हि दयाऽर्जुने॥
en: I say this; and the king approves of this. Arjuna is never for war; there is great kindness in Arjuna.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एतच्छ्रुत्वा महाबाहुः केशवः प्रहसन्निव। अभूतपूर्वं भीमस्य मार्दवोपहितं वचः॥ गिरेरिव लघुत्वं तच्छीतत्वमिव पावके। मत्वा रामानुजः शौरिः शार्ङ्गधन्वा वृकोदरम्॥ संतेजयंस्तदा वाग्भिर्मातरिश्वेव पावकम्। उवाच भीममासीनं कृपयाऽभिपरिप्लुतम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said The long-armed Keshava heard with a glad heart these words fraught with mildness from Bhima. Being of opinion that such words from Bhima were as unusual as lightness of a mountain or coldness in fire, the younger brother of Rama, born in the race of Shura and wielding the Sharang bow, then encouraged Vrikodara with his words like wind encouraging flames and said to Bhima, who was seated and who was overwhelmed with his kindness.

sn: श्रीभगवानुवाच त्वमन्यदा भीमसेन युद्धमेव प्रशंससि। वधाभिनन्दिनः क्रूरान् धार्तराष्ट्रान् मिमर्दिषुः॥
en: The blessed God said 0 Bhimasena, at other times you approving of war rejoiced at the prospect of killing the crooked minded sons of Dhritarashtra, who oppress others.

sn: न च स्वपिषि जागर्षि न्युब्जः शेषे परंतप। घोरामशान्तां रुषती सदा वाचं प्रभाषसे॥
en: You do not sleep but are awake with your face bent downwards, O you chastiser of your enemies; and you always speak terrible and wrathful words inclined towards war.

sn: निःश्वसनग्निवत् तेन संतप्तः स्वेन मन्युना। अप्रशान्तमना भीम सधूम इव पावकः॥
en: With your own worth, your breath is hot like fire and, O Bhima, your mind is not calm like fire with smoke.

sn: एकान्ते निःश्वसञ्छेषे भारात इव दुर्बलः। अपि त्वां केचिदुन्मत्तं मन्यन्तेऽतद्विदो जनाः॥
en: Alone and by yourself you sign in a corner like one labouring under a load; and those not aware of the cause thereof consider you to be insane.

sn: आरुज्य वृक्षान् निर्मूलान् गजः परिरुजनिव। निघ्नन् पद्भिः क्षिति भीम निष्टनन् परिधावसि॥
en: Like an elephant breaking into pieces the uprooted trees which he has himself felled down and beating the earth with its feet, you too run about drawing sighs.

sn: नास्मिञ्जनेऽभिरमसे रहः क्षिपसि पाण्डव। नान्यं निशि दिवा चापि कदाचिदभिनन्दसि॥
en: Here you are not pleased with the company of men, but spend your time, O son of Pandu, in solitude; and nothing else ever delights you by day and by night.

sn: अकस्मात् स्मयमानश्च रहस्यास्से रुदन्निव। जान्वोर्मूर्धानमाधाय चिरमास्से प्रमीलितः॥
en: Sometimes you laugh aloud all on a sudden; and sometimes you sit weeping in a secluded spot; and sometimes again you are seated for a long time with your head between your two knees and with your eyes closed.

sn: भृकुटिं च पुनः कुर्वन्नोष्ठौ च विदशनिवा अभीक्ष्णं दृश्यसे भीम सर्वं तन्मन्युकारितम्॥
en: Other times with your eye-brows contracted and your lips firmly pressed against each other, you gaze at objects before you for a long time. All this is the work of wrath.

sn: यथा पुरस्तात् सविता दृश्यते शुक्रमुच्चरन्। यथा च पश्चान्निर्मुक्तो ध्रुवं पर्येति रश्मिवान्॥ तथा सत्यं ब्रवीम्येतन्नास्ति तस्य व्यतिक्रमः। हन्ताहं गदयाभ्येत्य दुर्योधनममर्षणम्॥ इति स्म मध्ये भ्रातॄणां सत्येनालभसे गदाम्। तस्य ते प्रशमे बुद्धिर्धियतेऽद्य परंतप॥
en: As surely the sun is seen in the east rising and blazing forth his radiance and as surely that body of light afterwards sets after revolving round Meru; so truly shall I kill wrathful Duryodhana with a blow of this mace. war I speak this truly and there will be no swerving from this oath of mine. With this oath at one time did you handle the mace in the midst of your brothers. At this time however the inclinations of you, O chastiser of your enemies, who are such; point towards peace.

sn: अहो युद्धाभिकाङ्क्षाणां युद्धकाल उपस्थिते। चेतांसि विप्रतीपानि यत् त्वां भीर्भीम विन्दति॥
en: Alas! at the approach of the time for fight the hearts of those who are inclined towards will be swerved away; since fear penetrates you.

sn: अहो पार्थ निमित्तानि विपरीतानि पश्यसि। स्वप्नान्ते जागारान्ते च तस्मात् प्रशममिच्छसि।॥
en: Alas, O son of Pritha, you see in your mind's eye the omens unfavourable to you, whether you are asleep or awake. Therefore do you desire peace!

sn: अहो नाशंससे किञ्चित् पुंस्त्वंक्लीब इवात्मनि। कश्मलेनाभिपन्नोऽसि तेन ते विकृतं मनः॥
en: Alas, you do not evince any manliness in you like an eunuch. You are overpowered by extreme fear; and therefore is your mind swerving from the right path.

sn: उद्वेपते ते हृदयं मनस्ते प्रतिसीदति। ऊरुस्तम्भगृहीतोऽसि तस्मात् प्रशममिच्छसि॥
en: Your heart shakes with fear; your mind is filled with despair; and your thighs tremble; and therefore do you desire peace.

sn: अनित्यं किल मर्त्यस्य पार्थ चित्तं चलाचलम्। वातवेगप्रचलिता अष्ठीला शाल्मलेरिव॥
en: O son of Pritha, the hearts of earthly men are inconstant and susceptible of change like a young Shalmali tree moved by the force of wind.

sn: तवैषा विकृता बुद्धिर्गवां वागिव मानुषी। मनांसि पाण्डुपुत्राणां मज्जयत्यप्लवानिव॥
en: This perverted intention of yours is as unusual as the human faculties in a cow. The minds of the (other) sons of Pandu will sink (in an ocean of despair) like those without a race (and yet struggling in the waters).

sn: इदं मे महादाश्चर्यं पर्वतस्येव सर्पणम्। यदीदृशं प्रभाषेथा भीमसेनासमं वचः॥
en: It is to me as great a wonder as the lifting up of a mountain that you should speak worlds in this strain so unlike Bhimasena.

sn: स दृष्ट्वा स्वानि कर्माणि कुले जन्म च भारत। उत्तिष्ठिस्व विषादं मा कृथा वीर स्थिरो भव॥
en: Looking back on your own deeds and the family in which you are born, O Bharata, rise up and do not yield to grief. O hero, be calm.

sn: न चैतदनुरूपं ते यत् ते ग्लानिररिंदम। यदोजसा न लभते क्षत्रियो न तदश्नुते॥
en: This dullness which you evince is not fit for you; for a Kshatriya does not keep that which he does not win by force of his own might.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तथोक्तो वासुदेवेन नित्यमन्युरमर्षणः। सदश्ववत् समाधावद् बभाषे तदनन्तरम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Thus spoken by the son of Vasudeva, the one who was ever wrathful and who was accustomed to return insults immediately woke up like a good horse and instantly said reply-

sn: भीमसेन उवाच अन्यथा मां चिकीर्षन्तमन्यथा मन्यसेऽच्युत। प्रणीतभावमत्यर्थं युधि सत्यपराक्रमम्॥
en: Bhimasena said You regard me, who desire to act in a certain way, in a different light, O Acchyuta. I am in an exceedingly cheerful state of mind at the prospect of war. I am of true prowess.

sn: वेत्सि दाशार्ह सत्यं मे दीर्घकालं सहोषितः। उत वा मां न जानासि प्लवन् ह्रद इवाप्लवे॥
en: You know the truth of this, you of the Dasharha race, owing to your living for a long time with me; or it is possible that you do not know me like one swimming in a lake not knowing its depth.

sn: तस्मादनभिरूपाभिर्वाग्भिर्मा त्वं समर्छसि। कथं हि भीमसेनं मां जानन् कश्चन माधव॥
en: For this reason you find fault with me in words that I dot deserve. Who, knowing me to be Bhimasena.

sn: ब्रूयादप्रतिरूपाणि यथा मां वक्तुमर्हसि। तस्मादिदं प्रवक्ष्यामि वचनं वृष्णिनन्दन॥
en: Would dare speak in such unbecoming language as you have deemed fit to address me? Therefore, O you delighted of the Vrishni race, I tell you these words.

sn: आत्मनः पौरुषं चैव बलं च न समं परैः। सर्वथानार्यकमैतत् प्रशंसा स्वयमात्मनः॥
en: Regarding the manly strength of myself and the might, which are not equalled by my enemies. At all times this is a dishonourable act for a man to praise himself.

sn: अतिवादापविद्धस्तु वक्ष्यामि बलमात्मनः। पश्यमे रोदसी कृष्ण ययोरासन्निमाः प्रजाः॥
en: Yet being pierced with excessive blame, I speak out of my own strength. Look at these two, O Krishna, the earth and the heaven, from which have proceeded all creatures.

sn: अचले चाप्रतिष्ठे चाप्यनन्ते सर्वमातरौ। यदीमे सहसा क्रुद्ध समेयातां शिले इव॥
en: Which are immovable, immense . and without end and which are, as it were, the mothers of all beings. If these two, out of anger, suddenly come against each other like two mountains,

sn: अहमेते निगृह्णीयां बाहुभ्यां सचराचरे। पश्यैतदन्तरं बाह्वोर्महापरिघयोरिवा॥
en: Then I could by my two arms keep them apart with all their mobile and immobile beings. Behold the distance between the two arms, which coming together are like a great circle.

sn: य एतत् प्राप्य मुच्येत न तं पश्यामि पूरुषम्। हिमवांश्च समुद्रश्च वज्री वा बलभित् स्वयम्॥
en: I do not see the man who can free himself after once getting within them. The Himavat, the ocean and the wielder of the thunder-bolt and the grinder of Bala himself.:

sn: मयाभिपन्नं त्रायेरन् बलमास्थाय न त्रयः। युद्धार्हान् क्षत्रियान् सर्वान् पाण्डवेष्वाततायिनः॥
en: These three together cannot by their joint strength rescue a man in my power. All the Kshatriyas, who are fit for battle and who oppose the Pandavas.

sn: अधः पादतलेनैतानधिष्ठास्यामि भूतले। न हि त्वं नाभिजानासि मम विक्रममच्युत॥
en: I shall fell them down to the earth and trample them with the soles of my feet. You, O Acchyuta, are not unfamiliar with my strength.

sn: यथा मया विनिर्जित्य राजानो वशगाः कृताः। अथ चेन्मा न जानासि सूर्यस्येवोद्यतः प्रभाम्॥ विगाढे युधि सम्बाधे वेत्स्यसे मां जनार्दन। परुपैराक्षिपसि किं व्रणं पूतिमिवोन्नयन्॥
en: And the manner in which after conquering the kings, brought them under subjection. If it is a fact that you do not know my strength, which is like the resplendent sun, you will know then me in the fierce turmoil of battle, O Janardana. You cause me pain by your harsh words like the pain felt in opening a long standing boil.

sn: यथामति ब्रवीम्येतद् विद्धि मामधिकं ततः। द्रष्टासि युधि सम्बाधे प्रवृत्ते वैशसेऽहनि॥
en: Know me to be possessed of greater strength than what I have described of my own will. On the day in which the fierce battle begins, you will see me.

sn: मया प्रणुन्नान् मातङ्गान् रथिनः सादिनस्तथा। तथा नरानभिकुद्धं निघ्नन्तं क्षत्रियर्षभान्॥
en: And you will see the elephants, carwarriors and horse soldiers struck down by me; and you will see me moved by rage killing men, who are as bulls among the Kshatriyas.

sn: द्रष्टा मां त्वं च लोकश्च विकर्षन्तं वरान् वरान्। न मे सीदन्ति मज्जानो न ममोद्वेपते मनः॥
en: You will see and the world will see me cutting down the foremost warriors. The marrow of my bones is not wasted away; nor does my mind shake with fear!

sn: सर्वलोकादभिक्रुद्धान्न भयं विद्यते मम। किं तु सौहृदमेवैतत् कृपया मधुसूदन। सर्वास्तितिक्षे संक्लेशान् मा स्म नो भरता नशन्।।१८
en: I have no fear from all the worlds moved with wrath against me. But I am evincing these good wishes only out of mercy, O destroyer of Madhu. I can bear all sorts of troubles, if the Bharatas are not annihilated.

sn: श्रीभगवानुवाच भावं जिज्ञासमानोऽहं प्रणयादिदमब्रुवम्। न चौक्षेपान्न पाण्डित्यान क्रोधान्न विवक्षया॥
en: The blessed God said Desiring to know your intentions, I said this of affection and out of a desire to find fault with you, nor out of a desire to show my learning, not from anger, nor from a desire of saying something.

sn: वेदाहं तव माहात्म्यमुत ते वेद यद् बलम्। उत ते वेद कर्माणि न त्वां परिभवाम्यहम्॥
en: I know the greatness of your soul; and I know what strength you possess; and I know also your deeds; and I do not find fault with you.

sn: यथा चात्मनि कल्याणं सम्भावयसि पाण्डव। सहस्रगुणमप्येतत् त्वयि सम्भावयाम्यहम्॥
en: What good you yourself consider possible to do to the Pandavas, I consider it possible for you to do a thousand times of that.

sn: यादृशे च कुले जन्म सर्वराजाभिपूजिते। बन्धुमिश्च सुहृद्धिश्च भीम त्वमसि तादृशः॥
en: You along with your friend and wellwishers, are just what you ought to be, being born in such a family worshipped by all the kings.

sn: जिज्ञासन्तो हि धर्मस्य संदिग्धस्य वृकोदर। पर्यायं नाध्यवस्यन्ति देवमानुषयोर्जनाः॥
en: O Vrikodara, those men, who enquire after the certainty of the consequence of virtue and vice in the next world in a spirit of doubt any matter regarding god or man, can never arrive at the right conclusion.

sn: स एव हेतुर्भुत्वा हि पुरुषस्यार्थसिद्धिषु। विनाशेऽपि स एवास्य संदिग्धं कर्म पौरुषम्॥
en: The same thing which is the cause of the attainment of the object of man is (sometimes) also the cause of his ruin. The effect of human acts therefore is doubtful.

sn: अन्यथा परिदृष्टानि कविभिर्दोषदर्शिभिः। अन्यथा परिवर्तन्ते वेगा इव नभस्वतः॥
en: The act recommended to be followed by wise men competent to foresee the evil effects of actions have consequences other than those foreseen, like the winds from heaven (the direction taken by which no one can predict).

sn: सुमन्त्रितं सुनीतं च न्यायतश्चोपपादितम्। कृतं मानुष्यकं कर्भ दैवेनापि विस्थ्यते॥
en: The acts performed by a man well advised, well controlled and done in a way not injurious to any body has contrary effect by the dispensations of Providence.

sn: दैवमप्यकृतं कर्म पौरुषेण विहन्यते। शीतमुष्णं तथा वर्षं क्षुत्पिपासे च भारत॥
en: Then, again, the dispensation of the gods, that are not the results of any particular actions, are neutralized by the actions of men; as for instance cold, heat and rain and hunger and thirst, O Bharata.

sn: यदन्यद् दिष्टभावस्य पुरुषस्य स्वयं कृतम्। तस्मादनुपरोधश्च विद्यते तत्र लक्षणम्॥
en: Over and above the actions that a man is destined to perform, he can do away with others as well at his will; which the Shastras testify.

sn: लोकस्य नान्यतो वृत्तिः पाण्डवान्यत्र कर्मणः। एवंबुद्धिः प्रवर्तेत फलं स्यादुभयान्वये॥
en: Since, O son of Pandu, there is no other way for than action. A man should engage in acts with this knowledge; and the result will be brought about by both preordainment and action.

sn: य एवं कृतबुद्धिः स कर्मस्वेव प्रवर्तते। नासिद्धो व्यथते तस्य न सिद्धौ हर्षमश्नुते॥
en: He who engages in action with this knowledge is not annoyed at failure; nor is he elated with success.

sn: तत्रेयमनुमात्रा मे भीमसेन विवक्षिता। नैकान्तसिद्धिर्वक्तव्या शत्रुभिः सह संयुगे॥
en: In this sense, O Bhimasena, did I speak; and I did not mean that in a battle with the enemy; success would be absolutely theirs.

sn: नातिप्रहीणरश्मिः स्यात् तथा भावविपर्यये। विषादमछेद् ग्लानि वाप्येतमर्थं ब्रवीमि ते॥
en: I am speaking all this to you; as when a man's intellect is confused, he should not be wholly devoid of cheerfulness; nor yield wholly to sadness or dullness.

sn: श्वोभूते धृतराष्ट्रस्य समीपं प्राप्य पाण्डव। यतिष्ये प्रशमं कर्तुं युष्मदर्थमहापयन्॥
en: At the dawn of day, going near Dhritarashtra, O son of Pandu, shall I try to effect peace without a sacrifice of your interests.

sn: शमं चेत् ते करिष्यन्ति ततोऽनन्तं यशोमम। भवतां च कृतः कामस्तेषां च श्रेय उत्तमम्॥
en: If they consent to peace, then unending fame will be mine; while your desires will be fulfilled and advantage will accrue to them.

sn: ते चेदभिनिवेक्ष्यन्ते नाभ्युपैष्यन्ति मे वचः। कुरवो युद्धमेवात्र घोरं कर्म भविष्यति॥
en: If however they stick to their resolve and not listen to my advice, in that case there will be a terrible war among the sons of Kuru.

sn: अस्मिन् युद्धे भीमसेन त्वयि भारः समाहितः। धूरर्जुनेन धार्या स्याद् वोढव्य इतरो जनः॥
en: In this battle, O 0 Bhimasena, the responsibility of guiding the car of war rests on you; while Arjuna will draw the car, on which will be seated other persons.

sn: अहं हि यन्ता बीभत्सोर्भविता संयुगे सति। धनंजयस्यैष कामो न हि युद्धं न कामये॥
en: The war taking place, I shall drive Vibhatsu's car; for such is the desire of Dhananjaya and not because I myself am desirous of fight.

sn: तस्मादाशङ्कमानोऽहं वृकोदर मतिं तवा गदतः क्लीबया वाचा तेजस्ते समदीदिपम्॥
en: Therefore did I, fearful of the direction your inclination might follow from your words which were like those of an eunuch, rekindle your energy, O Vrikodara.

sn: अर्जुन उवाच उक्तं युधिष्ठिरेणैव यावद् वाच्यं जनार्दन। तव वाक्यं तु मे श्रुत्वा प्रतिभाति परंतप॥
en: Arjuna said By Yudhishthira has been uttered all that ought to be spoken, O Janardana; but hearing your words, O chastiser of foes, it seems to me.

sn: नैव प्रशममत्र त्वं मन्यसे सुकरं प्रभो। लोभाद् वा धृतराष्ट्रस्य दैन्याद् वा समुपस्थितात्॥
en: That you do not consider peace to be easily obtainable in this instance, O Lord, owing either to avarice on the part of Dhritarashtra or the weakness of ourselves.

sn: अफलं मन्यसे वाऽपि पुरुषस्य पराक्रमम्। न चान्तरेण कर्माणि पौरुषेण फलोदयः॥
en: You consider, too, that human strength (alone) is without avail and that human desires are fruitless save when attended with action.

sn: तदिदं भाषितं वाक्यं तथा च न तथैव तत्। न चैतदेवं द्रष्टव्यमसाध्यमपि किंचन॥
en: These words spoken by you may or may not be true; but there is nothing which ought to be regarded as incapable of attainment.

sn: किं चैतन्मन्यसे कृच्छ्रमस्माकमवसादकम्। कुर्वन्ति तेषां कर्माणि येषां नास्ति फलोदयः॥
en: You consider peace to be improbable owing to our weakness; but they are doing deeds, which do not seem to bear fruits.

sn: सम्पाद्यमानं सम्यक् च स्यात् कर्म सफलं प्रभो। स तथा कृष्ण वर्तस्व यथा शर्म भवेत् परैः॥
en: Done in a proper way, however, our object may be successful, O lord, therefore, O Krishna, act in such a way that there may be enemy.

sn: पाण्डवानां कुरूणां च भवान् नः प्रथमः सुहृत्। सुराणामसुराणां च यथा वीर प्रजापतिः॥
en: You are the best well-wisher of ourselves, of both the Kurus and the Pandavas; as the hero Prajapati was of the Suras and the Asuras.

sn: कुरूणां पाण्डवानां च प्रतिपत्स्व निरामयम्। अस्मद्धितमनुष्ठानं मन्ये तव न दुष्करम्॥
en: Do, therefore, that which is conducive to the interests of both the Kurus and the Pandavas. I think that the accomplishment of what is for our good is not difficult for you; and this is a work which is the proper thing for you to do, O Janardana.

sn: एवं च कार्यतामेति कार्यं तव जनार्दन। गमनादेवमेव त्वं करिष्यसि जनार्दन।॥
en: You will accomplish this, as soon as you go there, O Janardana; and, O hero, if any other treatment of that evil-souled one is derived by you; it will be as you wish, whether it is to be peace with them or not or whatever is desired by you.

sn: चिकीर्षितमथान्यत् ते तस्मिन् वीर दुरात्मनि। भविष्यति च तत् सर्वं यथा तवचिकीर्षितम्॥
en: O Krishna, whatever you desire after mature deliberation will be accepted by us with due respect. Is not death proper for that evil-minded one, as well as for his friends and sons?

sn: शर्म तैः सह वा नोऽस्तु तव वा यच्चिकीर्षितम्। विचार्यमाणो यः कामस्तव कृष्ण स नो गुरुः। न स नार्हति दुष्टात्मा वधं ससुतबान्धवः॥
en: By whom was seen the beauty of prosperity established on the son of Dharma; and who on seeing that had no righteous means (of wining the kingdom) O slayer of Madhu.

sn: येन धर्मसुते दृष्टा न सा श्रीरुपमर्षिता। यच्चाप्यपश्यतोपायं धर्मिष्ठं मधुसूदन॥
en: They robbed us (of our kingdom) by the cruel and sinful means of a deceitful game at dice. Where is the wielder of the bow, who though born in a Kshatriya family.

sn: उपायेन नृशंसेन हृता दुर्दूतदेविना। कथं हि पुरुषो जातः क्षत्रियेषु धनुर्धरः॥
en: When challenged (for battle) turns back even when death stares on him? Seeing ourselves defeated by deceit and while wandering in the woods.

sn: समाहूतो निवर्तेत प्राणत्यागेऽप्युपस्थिते। अधर्मेण जितान् दृष्ट्वा वने प्रव्रजितांस्तथा॥ वध्यतां मम वार्ष्णेय निर्गतोऽसौ सुयोधनः। न चैतदद्भुतं कृष्ण मित्रार्थं यच्चिकीर्षसि। क्रिया कथं च मुख्या स्यान्मृदुना चेतरेण वा॥
en: Did I think that Suyodhana ought to be slain by me when I came out of the forest, O you of the Vrishini race; but what you desire to do on behalf of your friends is not strange, O Krishna, though how that is capable of accomplishment by mildness or by other means (I do not see).

sn: अथवा मन्यसे ज्यायान् वधस्तेषामनन्तरम्। तदेव क्रियतामाशु न विचार्यमतस्त्वया॥
en: If you consider their immediate destruction better, do that instantly for there is nothing to be considered about in this matter.

sn: जानासि हि यथैतेन द्रौपदी पापबुद्धिना। परिक्लिष्टा सभामध्ये तच्च तस्योपमर्षितम्॥
en: You know, how by that evil-minded one Draupadi was troubled and annoyed in the midst of the Council and that act of his was borne with difficulty.

sn: स नाम सम्यग् वर्तेत पाण्डवेष्विति माधव। न मे संजायते बुद्धिर्बीजमुप्तमिवोषरे॥
en: That he should treat the Pandavas justly, O Madhava, dose not seem possible to me. Good counsel to him will give the same result as seed thrown on barren lands.

sn: तस्माद् यन्मन्यसे युक्तं पाण्डवानां हितं च यत्। तथाऽऽशु कुरु वार्ष्णेय यन्नः कार्यमनन्तरम्॥
en: There for what you consider proper and beneficial for Kurus, What ought to be done next by us, do immediately.

sn: श्रीभगवानुवाच एवमेतन्महाबाहो यथा वदसि पाण्डवा पाण्डवानां कुरूणां च प्रतिपत्स्ये निरामयम्॥
en: The blessed God said O you of long arms, it will be as you say, O Pandava. I shall accomplish what would be for the well being of the Pandavas and for the Kurus.

sn: सर्वं त्विदं ममायत्तं बीभत्सो कर्मणोर्द्वयोः। क्षेत्रं हि रसवच्छुद्धं कर्मणैवोपपादितम्॥
en: Everything about these two acts (peace and war) is within my power. Land is moistened and purified (i.e. all weeds are rooted out of it) by action.

sn: ऋते वर्षान्न कौन्तेय जातु निवर्तयेत् फलम्। तत्र वै पौरुषं ब्रूयुरासेकं यत्र कारितम्॥
en: But without rain, O son of Kunti, it cannot be made to yield crops. In that case ( i.e. if there is no rain) it is said that irrigation, which can be done men, ought to be resorted to.

sn: तत्र चापि ध्रुवं पश्येच्छोषणं दैवकारितम्। तदिदं निश्चितं बुद्ध्या पूर्वैरपि महात्मभिः॥
en: But there even (i.e. even in artificial irrigation) you will surely behold draught brought on by divine agency (if He so will it). Knowing this to be the case, the great-souled ones of old.

sn: दैवे च मानुषे चैव संयुक्तं लोककारणम्। अहं हि तत् करिष्यामि परं पुरुषकारतः॥
en: Have said that human affairs accomplished both by divine providence and by exertion on the part of man. This shall do only that which is capable of being done by human beings.

sn: दैवं तु न मया शक्यं कर्म कर्तुं कथंचन। स हि धर्मं च लोकं च त्यक्त्वा चरति दुर्मतिः॥
en: What can be done only by divine agency can never be done by me. That wicked-minded are one acts without any regard to righteousness or to the world.

sn: न हि संतप्यते तेन तथारूपेण कर्मणा। तथापि बुद्धि पापिष्ठा वर्धयन्त्यस्य मन्त्रिणः॥
en: And he dose not regret for doing that sort of acts; and his inclinations which are so vicious are supported by his advisers.

sn: शकुनिः सूतपुत्रश्च भ्राता दुःशासनस्तथा। स हि त्यागेन राज्यस्य न शमं समुपैष्यति॥
en: (Who are) Shakuni, the son of Suta (Karna) and his brother Dushasana? He will not effect peace by giving up (any portion of) the kingdom.

sn: अन्तरेण वधं पार्थ सानुबन्धः सुयोधनः। न चापि प्रणिपातेन त्यक्तुमिच्छति धर्मराट्। याच्यमानश्च राज्यं स न प्रदास्यति दुर्मतिः॥
en: Without the slaying of Suyodhana and his kinsmen, O son of Pritha, he dose not desire to give up (the kingdom), not even by our surrendering to him, O virtuous king. That evilminded one will not give you the kingdom by your asking for it.

sn: मन्ये वाच्यो यद् युधिष्ठिरशासनम्। धर्मराजेन भारत॥
en: I think that Yudhishthira's message ought to be conveyed to him; what is necessary and proper has already been said by the virtuous king, O Bharata.

sn: तथा पापस्तु तत् सर्वं न करिष्यति कौरवः। तस्मिश्चाक्रियमाणेऽसौ लोके वध्यो भविष्यति॥
en: The one who is such vicious inclinations will not do even that in its entirety, O son of Kuru; and he, refusing compliance with that will deserve death in this world.

sn: मम चापि स वध्यो हि जगतश्चापि भारत। येन कौमारके यूयं सर्वे विप्रकृताः सदा॥
en: (In that case) he would deserve death at my hands and at the hands of the entire world. By him you all in your youth were ever persecuted.

sn: विप्रलुप्तं च वो राज्यं नृशंसेन दुरात्मना। न चोपशाम्यते पापः श्रियं दृष्ट्वा युधिष्ठिरे॥ न तु स तद् उक्तं प्रयोजनं यत् तु
en: (And since) your kingdom has been wrested by means of deceit by that evil-souled one, who would not obtain peace at seeing prosperity in Yudhishthira.

sn: असकृच्चाप्यहं तेन त्वत्कृते पार्थ भेदितः। न मया तद् गृहीत् च पापं तस्य चिकीर्षितम्॥
en: I, too, O son of Pritha, was sought to be withdrawn from four side by that vicious one; but that evil counsel of his was not accepted by me.

sn: जानासि हि महाबाहो त्वमप्यस्य परं मतम्। प्रियं चिकीर्षमाणं च धर्मराजस्य मामपि॥
en: You, too, know, O you of long of arms, his dearly cherished intentions and purposes; and that the good of the king of virtue is ever desired to be accomplished by me.

sn: संजास्तस्य चात्मानं मम चैव परं मतम्। अजानन्निव मां कस्मादर्जुनद्याभिशङ्कसे॥
en: Knowing then his purposes and my dearly cherished intentions, why do you, O Arjuna, seem to be afraid of me, as if you did not know them.

sn: यच्चापि परमं दिव्यं तच्चाप्यनुगतं त्वया। विधानं विहितं पार्थ कथं शर्म भवेत् परैः॥
en: The one prime object, that has been ordained in Heaven, is known to you. How then can your advice of peace with the enemy be followed?

sn: यत् तु वाचा शक्यं कर्मणा वाऽपि पाण्डव। करिष्ये तदहं पार्थ न त्वाशंसे शमं परैः॥
en: Whatever is capable of being done by me, by speech or by deed, O Pandava, shall be done by me, O son of Pritha, but do not expect peace with the enemy;

sn: कथं गोहरणे ह्युक्तो नैतच्छर्म तथा हितम्। याच्यमानो हि भीष्मेण संवत्सरगतेऽध्वनि॥
en: Why was not this very peace, which is so beneficial, proposed by Bhishma and humbly besought by him at the time of attacking the cattle of Virata, which is now a year since, concluded?

sn: तदैव ते पराभूता यदा संकल्पितास्त्वया। लवशः क्षणशश्चापि न च तुष्टः सुयोधनः॥
en: At that moment have they been vanquished, when their defeat has been determined on by you. Suyodhana is not satisfied at the prospect of parting with a small part of his kingdom for even a very brief period.

sn: सर्वथा तु मया कार्यं धर्मराजस्य शासनम्। विभाव्यं तस्य भूयश्च कर्म पापं दुरात्मनः॥
en: The instructions of the king of virtue will always be attended to by me; and the wicked acts of that evil-souled one will have again to be considered by me.

sn: नकुल उवाच उक्तं बहुविधं वाक्यं धर्मराजेन माधव। धर्मज्ञेन वदान्येन श्रुतं चैव हि तत् त्वया॥
en: Nakula said Words of different degrees of worth have been said by the just king, O Madhava, who knows what righteousness is and who is benevolent; and they have all been heard by you.

sn: मतमाज्ञाय राज्ञश्च भीमसेनेन माधव। संशमो बाहुवीर्यं च ख्यापितं माधवात्मनः॥
en: Bhimasena, having ascertained the wishes of the king, has dwelt on peace as well as on his own strength of arms, O Madhava.

sn: तथैव फाल्गुनेनापि यदुक्तं तत् त्वया श्रुतम्। आत्मनश्च मतं वीरं कथितं भवता सकृत्॥
en: In the same way what has been said by Falguna has been heard by you; and your own opinions, O hero have been expressed by you.

sn: सर्वमेतदतिक्रम्य श्रुत्वा परमतं भवान्। यत् प्राप्तकालं मन्येथास्ततं कुर्याः पुरुषोत्तम॥
en: Shutting your mind to all this and hearing what the intentions of the enemy are, do that what you consider to be opportune, O foremost among men.

sn: तस्मिंस्तस्मिन् निमित्तं हि मतं भवति केशव। प्राप्तकाल मनुष्येण क्षमं कार्यमरिन्दम॥
en: Different conclusions are arrived at in different matters, O Keshava, but with a view to success, O chastiser of your enemies, a thing ought to be done by man at the right moment.

sn: अन्यथा चिन्तितो ह्यर्थः पुनर्भवति सोऽन्यथा। अनित्यमतयो लोके नराः पुरुषसत्तम॥
en: An object, settled on in a particular way, again becomes different, when the conditions are changed; therefore man cannot stick to the same opinions in this world, O you foremost among men.

sn: अन्यथा बुद्धया ह्यासन्नस्मासु वनवासिषु। अदृश्येष्वन्यथा कृष्ण दृश्येषु पुनरन्यथा॥
en: While residing in the wood, we were of a different inclination; and while in concealment we came to be of other inclination. But now when we are out of concealment, when we can expose ourselves to the view of others, our inclinations are again changed.

sn: अस्माकमपि वार्ष्णेय वने विचरतां तदा। न तथा प्रणयो राज्ये यथा सम्प्रति वर्तते॥
en: O you of the Vrishni race, the love of kingdom, which now exists among us, did not exist to the same degree when we wandered in the woods.

sn: निवृत्तवनवासान् नः श्रुत्वा वीर समागताः। अक्षौहिण्यो हि सप्तेमास्त्वत्प्रसादाज्जनार्दन॥
en: Hearing that, we are returned from our exile in the woods, O hero. These seven Akshauhinis have gathered round us through your grace, OJanardana.

sn: इमान् हि पुरुषव्याघ्रानचिन्त्यबलपौरुषान्। आत्तशस्त्रान् रणे दृष्ट्वा न व्यथेदिह कः पुमान्॥
en: What man is there who, seeing these tigers among men of inconceivable strength and prowess and ready for battle with all their arms, will not be struck with fear?

sn: स भवान् कुरुमध्ये तं सान्त्वपूर्वं भयोत्तरम्। ब्रूयाद् वाक्यं यथा मन्दो न व्यथेत सुयोधनः॥
en: Therefore do you in the midst of the Kurus speak words fraught with mildness, so that the foolish Suyodhana may not be struck with fear; and then (when these have failed) use threats.

sn: युधिष्ठिरं भीमसेनं बीभत्सुं चापराजितम्। सहदेवं च मां चैव त्वां च रामं च केशव।॥ सात्यकिं च महावीर्यं विराटं च सहात्मजम्। दुपदं च सहामात्यं धृष्टद्युम्नं च माधव॥ काशिराजं च विक्रान्तं धृष्टकेतुं च चेदिपम्। मांसशोणितभृन्मर्त्यः प्रतियुध्येत को युधि॥
en: Yudhishthira, Bhimasena, Vibhatsu, Aparajita, Sahadeva, myself Rama and yourself, O Keshava, Satyaki, Virat of great strength with his son, Drupada with his minister and Dhrishtadyumna, O Madhava, the king of Kashi of great strength and Dhrishtaketu, the lord of the Chedis-what earthly mortal is there of flesh and blood, who fight against these in battle.

sn: स भवान् गमनादेव साधयिष्यत्यसंशयम्। इष्टमर्थं महाबाहो धर्मराजस्य केवलम्॥
en: Therefore you will the moment you go there, accomplish without doubt the only object desired by the virtuous king, O you of long arms. are

sn: विदुरश्चैव भीष्मश्च द्रोणश्च सहबाह्निकः। श्रेयः समर्था विज्ञातुमुच्यमानास्त्वयानघ॥
en: Vidura, Bhishma and Drona with Bahlika are capable of understanding yourself and of speaking words of wisdom of wisdom which beneficial at the same time.

sn: ते चैनमनुनेष्यन्ति धृतराष्ट्रं जनाधिपम्। तं च पापसमाचारं सहामात्यं सुयोधनम्॥
en: And they too will lead Dhritarashtra, the lord of men and that Suyodhana of wicked nature with his ministers to do as you bid.

sn: श्रोता चार्थस्य विदुरस्त्वं च वक्ता जनार्दन। कमिवार्थं निवर्तन्तं स्थापयेतां न वर्मनि॥
en: When you, O Janardana, speak and Vidura hears on subjects conducive to their interests; what subject is there in the world which you cannot turn smooth and clear.

sn: सहदेव उवाच यदेतत् कथितं राज्ञा धर्म एष सनातनः। यथा च युद्धमेव स्यात् तथा कार्यमरिंदम॥
en: Sahadeva said All this which has been said by the king is eternal virtue; but, O chastiser of foes, should act in that way by which there shall be war.

sn: यदि प्रशममिच्छेयुः कुरवः पाण्डवैः सह। तथापि युद्धं दाशाह योजयेथाः सहैव तैः॥
en: If even the sons of Kuru desire peace with the sons of Pandu, still do you provoke war with them, O you of the Dasharha race.

sn: कथं नु दृष्ट्वा पाञ्चालीं तथा कृष्ण सभागताम्। अवधेन प्रशाम्येत मम मन्युः सुयोधनेः॥
en: Having seen the princess of Panchala come in the assembly, O Krishna, annoyed in that fashion, how can my wrath towards Suyodhana be appeased without killing him?

sn: यदि भीमार्जुनौ कृष्ण धर्मराजश्च धार्मिकः। धर्ममुत्सृज्य तेनाहं योद्भुमिच्छामि संयुगे॥
en: If Bhima and Arjuna, O Krishna and the virtuous king are virtuous, then I leading the path of virtue desire to fight with him in battle.

sn: सात्यकिरुवाच सत्यमाह महाबाहो सहदेवो महामतिः। दुर्योधनवधे शान्तिस्तस्य कोपस्य मे भवेत्॥
en: Satyaki said Sahadeva of large mind has spoken the truth, O you of long arms. His wrath and mine will be appeased only by killing Duryodhana.

sn: न जानासि यथा दृष्ट्वा चीराजिनधरान् वने। तवापि मन्युरुद्भूतो दुःखितान् प्रेक्ष्य पाण्डवान्॥
en: Do you not know that you, too seeing the Pandavas clad in rags and deer skin in the forest, felt very sorry and your wrath was kindled

sn: तस्मान्माद्रीसुतः शूरो यदाह रणकर्कशः। वचनं सर्वयोधानां तन्मतं पुरुषोत्तम॥
en: Therefore what the heroic son of Madri terrific in battle has said is the opinion of all the soldiers, O you foremost of men.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवं वदति वाक्यं तु युयुधाने महामतौ। सुभीमः सिंहनादोऽभूद् योधानां तत्र सर्वशः॥
en: Vaishampayana said While Suyodhana of large mind was yet speaking such, a terrible roar like that of a lion came from all the soldiers assembled there.

sn: सर्वे हि सर्वशो वीरास्तद्वचः प्रत्यपूजयन्। साधु सध्विति शैनेयं हर्षयन्तो युयुत्सवः॥
en: And all the heroes accepted and honoured these words of his in every way saying-Well done, well done; and the soldiers desirous of battle expressed their joy.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच राज्ञस्तु वचनं श्रुत्वा धर्मार्थसहितं हितम्। कृष्णा दाशार्हमासीनमब्रवीच्छोककर्शिता॥ सुता दुपदराजस्य स्वसितायतमूर्धजा। सम्पूज्य सहदेवं च सात्यकिं च महारथम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Hearing the king's words which were beneficial as well as conducive to morality and worldly good, Krishna, the daughter of king Drupada, of long and very black tresses, afflicted with grief, said to the scion of the Dasharha race, who was seated there, after having given due respects to Sahadeva and the great car-warrior Satyaki.

sn: भीमसेनं च संशान्तं दृष्ट्वा परमदुर्मनाः। अश्रुपूर्णेक्षणा वाक्यमुवाचेदं मनस्विनी॥
en: Seeing Bhimasena inclined towards peace, that intelligent lady with a sense of her wrongs said these words with tears in her eyes:

sn: विदितं ते महाबाहो धर्मज्ञ मधुसूदन। यथा निकृतिमास्थाय भ्रंशिताः पाण्डवाः सुखात्॥
en: O you of long arms, this is known to you. slayer of Madhu, how the Pandavas were deprived of all happiness through deceit.

sn: धृतराष्ट्रस्य पुत्रेण सामात्येन जनार्दन। यथा च संजयो राज्ञा मन्त्रं रहसि श्रावितः॥
en: By the son of Dhritarashtra within ministers, O Janardana; and what message was covered through Sanjaya in private by the king.

sn: युधिष्ठिरस्य दाशार्ह तच्चापि विदितं तव। यथोक्तः संजयश्चैव तच्च सर्वं श्रुतं त्वया॥
en: Yudhishthira, that too is known to you of the Dasharha race and by you has been heard all what Sanjaya said.

sn: पञ्च नस्तात दीयन्तां ग्रामा इति महाद्युते। अविरथलं वृकस्थलं माकन्दी वारणावतम्॥ अवसानं महाबाहो कञ्चिदेकं च पञ्चमम्। इति दुर्योधनो वाच्यः सुहृदश्चास्य केशव॥
en: O you of great luster, (this was the massage) give us, O sire, five villages namely, Avisthala, Vrikasthala, Makandi, Varanavata and any one for the last or the fifth, O you of long arms. In these terms was Duryodhana to be addressed and his friends too, O Keshava.

sn: न चापि ह्यकरोद् वाक्यं श्रुत्वा कृष्ण सुयोधनः। युधिष्ठिरस्य दाशार्ह श्रीमतः संधिमिच्छतः॥
en: Suyodhana, though he heard these words of Yudhishthira endued with prosperity and desirous if peace, did not act up to them, O you of the Dasharha race.

sn: अप्रदानेन राज्यस्य यदि कृष्ण सुयोधनः। संधिमिच्छेन्न कर्तव्यं तत्र गत्वा कथञ्चन॥
en: If, O Krishna, Suyodhana desires peace without returning the kingdom; then it is by no means proper that you should go there.

sn: शक्ष्यन्ति हि महाबाहो पाण्डवाः संजयैः सह। धार्तराष्ट्रबलं घोरं क्रुद्ध प्रतिसमासितुम्॥
en: O you of long arms, the Pandavas supported by the Srinjayas will be able to fight with the terrible army of Dhritarashtra excited with range.

sn: ते न हि साम्ना न दानेन शक्योऽर्थस्तेषु कश्चर। तस्मात् तेषु न कर्तव्या कृपा मधुसूदन॥
en: Not by peaceful means, nor by surrender can our object be gained from them; therefore, O destroyer of Madhu, mercy ought not to be shown to them by you.

sn: साम्ना दानेन वा कृष्ण ये न शाम्यन्ति शत्रवः। योक्तव्यस्तेषु दण्डः स्याज्जीवितं परिरक्षता॥
en: Those enemies, who do not assume an attitude of peace by words of humility or by surrender, ought to be visited with punishment by him who cares to preserve his life.

sn: तस्मात् तेषु महादण्डः क्षेप्तव्यः क्षिप्रमच्युत। त्वया चैव महाबाहो पाण्डवैः सह संजयैः॥
en: Therefore should heavy punishment fall or them from yourself, O Acchyuta of long arms, supported by the Pandavas and the Srinjayas.

sn: एतत् समर्थं पार्थानां तव चैव यशस्करम्। क्रियमाणं भवेत् कृष्ण क्षत्रस्य च सुखावहम्॥
en: This would be just the thing for the son of Pritha to do; and will also redound to your glory; and the accomplishment will be, O Krishna, the source of happiness to the entire Kshatriya race.

sn: क्षत्रियेण हि हन्तव्यः क्षत्रियो लोभमास्थितः। अक्षत्रियो वा दाशार्ह स्वधर्ममनुतिष्ठता।॥
en: A Kshatriya who is avaricious ought to be killed by a Kshatriya who is desirous of proving true to his our religion; and even if the covetous man is not a Kshatriya he ought to be slain.

sn: अन्यत्र ब्राह्मणात् तात सर्वपापेष्ववस्थितात्। गुरुर्हि सर्ववर्णानां ब्राह्मणः प्रसृताग्रभुक्॥
en: An exception should be made, O Sire, in the case of a Brahmana, though he be addicted to all sorts of vices; for a Brahmana is the preceptor of all the other classes and he is allowed precedence in everything.

sn: यथावध्ये वध्यमाने भवेद् दोषो जनार्दन। स वध्यस्यावधे दृष्ट इति धर्मविदो विदुः॥
en: The sin, that accrues from killing from one that ought but to be killed, is ihe fame as that which accrues him not slaying one that deserves death. Such has been the instructions of those conversant with the rulers of virtue.

sn: यथा त्वां न स्पृशेदेष दोषः कृष्ण तथा कुरु। पाण्डवैः सह दाशार्हः संजयैश्च ससैनिकैः॥
en: Do that, O Krishna, so that this sin may not touch you along with the Pandavas, O you of the Dasharha race and the Srinjayas and their armies.

sn: पुनरुक्तं च वक्ष्यामि विश्रम्मेण जनार्दन। का तु सीमन्तिनी मादृक् पृथिव्यामस्ति केशव॥
en: Out of excessive confidence on you, O Janardana, that I repeat what has been already repeated again and again. What woman is there in this world equal to me?

sn: सुता दुपदराजस्य वेदिमध्यात् समुत्थिता। धृष्टद्युम्नस्य भगिनी तव कृष्ण प्रिया सखी।॥
en: The daughter of king Drupada born of the sacrificial altar, sister of Dhrishtadyumna and your dear friend, O Krishna.

sn: आजमीढकुलं प्राप्ता स्नुषा पाण्डोर्महात्मनः। महिषी पाण्डुपुत्राणां पञ्चेन्द्रसमवर्चसाम्॥
en: I have become a member of the Ajamida race; and the daughter-in-law of the highsouled Pandu and the chief queen of the sons of Pandu, who in splendor are equal to five Indra's.

sn: सुता मे पञ्चभिर्वीरैः पञ्च जाता महारथाः। अभिमन्युर्यथा कृष्ण तथा ते तव धर्मतः॥
en: By the five heroes are born of me five sons, great car-warriors, who morally bear the same relation with you, O Krishna, as Abhimanyu.

sn: साहं केशग्रहं प्राप्ता परिक्लिष्टा सभां गता। पश्यतां पाण्डुपुत्राणां त्वयि जीवति केशव॥
en: When I, who am such, coming to the Council Chamber was caught hold of by the extremity of my hairs and annoyed within the range of vision of the Pandu's sons and during your life time, O Keshava.

sn: जीवत्सु पाण्डुपुत्रेषु पञ्चालेष्वथ वृष्णिषु। दासीभूतास्मि पापानां सभामध्ये व्यवस्थिता।॥
en: During the life time of the Pandu's, the Panchalas and the Vrishnis I was treated like a maid-servant and made to stand in the Council Chamber of those incarnations of vice.

sn: निरमपेष्वचेष्टेषु प्रेक्षमाणेषु पाण्डुषु। पाहि मामिति गोविन्द मनसा चिन्तितोऽसि मे॥
en: The sons of Pandu, gazing at me, without any wrath and without any efforts to extricate me, O Govinda, were thought of by me, saying-"save me."

sn: यत्र मां भगवान् राजा श्वशुरो वाक्यमब्रवीत्। वरं वृणीष्व पाञ्चालि वराहा॑ऽसि मता मम॥
en: On this the prosperous king (Dhritarashtra), my father-in-law, said these words chose a boon, O Princess of Panchala, in my opinion you are the proper recipient of a boon.”

sn: अदासाः पाण्डवाः सन्तु सरथाः सायुधा इति। पयोक्ते यत्र निर्मुक्ता वनवासाय केशव॥
en: "Let the Pandavas be liberated with their chariots and soldiers" was the boon I asked for; and at my solicitation were they liberated and sent to exile in the forest, OKeshava.

sn: एवंविधानां दुःखानापभिज्ञोऽसि जनार्दन। त्रायस्व पुण्डरीकाक्ष सभर्तृज्ञातिबान्धवान्॥
en: You, O Janardana, are very well aware of such-like troubles; and save us, o you with eyes like lotus, along with my husbands, kinsmen and friends.

sn: नन्वहं कृष्ण भीष्मस्य धृतराष्ट्रस्य चोभयोः। स्नुषा भवामि धर्मेण साहं सादीकृता बलात्॥
en: I am, morally speaking, O Krishna, the daughter-in-law of both Bhishma and Dhritarashtra; and yet I, who am such, was made a slave by force.

sn: धिक्पार्थस्य धनुष्यत्तां भीमसेनस्य धिक् बलम्। यत्र दुर्योधनः कृष्ण मुहूर्तमपि जीवति॥
en: Shame to the skill in archery of the son of Pritha and shame to the strength of Bhimasena! that Duryodhana, O Krishna, should be alive for one single moment.

sn: यदि तेऽहमनुग्राह्या यदि तेऽस्ति कृपा मयि। धार्तराष्ट्रेषु वै कोप: सर्वः कृष्ण विधीयताम्॥
en: If I ain fit to be favored by you, if there is mercy in you for me; then direct all your wrath on the sons of Dhritarashtra.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच इत्युक्त्वा मृदुसंहारं वृजिनाग्रं सुदर्शनम्। सुनीलमसितापाङ्गी सर्वगन्धाधिवासितम्॥ सर्वलक्षणसम्पन्नं महाभुजगवर्चसम्। केशपक्षं वरारोहा गृह्य वामेन पाणिना॥ पद्माक्षी पुण्डरीकाक्षमुपेत्य गजगामिनी। अश्रुपूर्णेक्षणा कृष्णा कृष्णं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Saying this, pretty Krishna having lotuslike eyes, of a black colour and the gait of an elephant and possessed of beautiful hips, taking hold of her beautiful ringlets with curls at their ends and of a deep blue colour, perfumed with all sorts of scents, with all the auspicious marks and very soft though bound up in a braid by her left hand, approached the lotus-eyed Krishna; and with eyes full of tears said these words.

sn: अयं ते पुण्डरीकाक्ष दुःशासनकरोद्धृतः। स्मर्तव्यः सर्वकार्येषु परेषां संधिमिच्छता॥
en: O you with lotus-like eyes, desirous of peace with the enemy, you should remember in all your acts that these (tresses) were seized by the hands of Dushasana.

sn: यदि भीमार्जुनौ कृष्ण कृपणौ संधिकामुकौ। पिता मे योत्स्यते वृद्धः सह पुत्रैर्महारथैः॥
en: If Bhima and Arjuna, O Krishna, are so mean as to desire peace, then my old father will fight along with his sons who are great car-warriors.

sn: पञ्च च महावीर्याः पुत्रा मे मधुसूदन। अभिमन्युं पुरस्कृत्य योत्स्यन्ते कुरुभिः सह॥
en: And my five sons, too, O slayer of Madhu, of great heroism, having placed Abhimanyu in the front will fight the Kurus.

sn: दुःशासनभुजं श्यामं संछिन्नं पांसुगुण्ठितम्। यद्यहं तु न पश्यामि का शान्तिर्हदयस्य मे॥
en: If I do not see the dark-coloured hand of Dushasana torn off from his body and reduced to powder, then what peace shall there be in my heart?

sn: त्रयोदश हि वर्षाणि प्रतीक्षन्त्या गतानि मे। विधाय हृदये मन्युं प्रदीप्तमिव पावकम्॥
en: Thirteen years have elapsed, during which I was waiting, entertaining in my heart feelings of revenge which were like blazing fire.

sn: विदीर्यते मे हृदयं भीमवाक्छल्यपीडितम्। योऽयमद्य महाबाहुर्धर्ममेवानुपश्यति॥
en: My heart, O Bhima, is rent asunder, pierced by darts of sharp words, as it were, at the thought that the long-armed one (Bhima) has an eye on morality.

sn: इत्युक्त्वा वाष्परुद्धेन कण्ठेनायतलोचना। सरोद कृष्णा सोत्कम्पं सस्वरं बाष्पगद्गदम्॥
en: Saying this with voice choked with tears, Krishna of distended eyes began to weep aloud in convulsive sobs and with her eyes full of tears.

sn: स्तनौ पीनायतश्रोणी सहिताबभिवर्षती। द्रवीभूतमिवात्युष्णं मुञ्चन्ती वारि नेत्रजम्॥
en: And the lady with beautiful hips began to shower from her eyes extremely hot tears, which flowed down her round bosom.

sn: तामुवाच महाबाहुः केशवः परिसान्त्वयन्। अचिराद् द्रक्ष्यसे कृष्णे रुदतीर्भरतस्त्रियः॥
en: Keshava with long arms then spoke these words with a view to comfort her, before long will you see, O Krishna, the ladies of Bharata's household weeping.

sn: एवं ता भीरु रोत्स्यन्ति निहतज्ञातिबान्धवाः। हतमित्रा हतबला येषां क्रुद्धाऽसि भामिनी॥
en: O timid one, they will weep as you now do, having their kinsmen and friends killed. Alrcady, O lady, are those with whom you are angry deprived of their friends and of their strength.

sn: अहं च तत् करिष्यामि भीमार्जुनयमैः सह। युधिष्ठिरनियोगेन दैवाच्च विधिनिर्मितात्॥
en: I shall accomplish this with Bhima, Arjuna and the twins, supported by Yudhishthira, through the ordainment of the gods.

sn: धार्तराष्ट्राः कालपक्वा न चेच्छृण्वन्ति मे वचः। शेष्यन्ते निहता भूमौ श्वशृगालादनीकृताः॥
en: If the sons of Dhritarashtra, whose time is now arrived, do not hear my advice; then they will sleep dead on the bare earth and be food for dogs and jackals.

sn: चलेद्धि हिमवाञ्छैलो मेदिनी शतधा फलेत्। द्यौः पतेच्च सनक्षत्रान मे मोघं वचो भवेत्॥
en: The Himavat mountains could move; the earth could be split up into a hundred pieces; and the heavenly regions with stars might fall; but my words would not be vain.

sn: सत्यं ते प्रतिजानामि कृष्णे बाष्पो निगृह्यताम्। हतामित्रात्प्रिया युक्तानचिराद् द्रक्ष्यसे पतीन्॥
en: I tell you truly, O Krishna, stop your tears. You will ever (in future) see your husbands endued with prosperity and with all their enemies killed.

sn: अर्जुन उवाच कुरूणामद्य सर्वेषां भवान् सुहृदनुत्तमः। सम्बन्धी दयितो नित्यमुभयोः पक्षयोरपि॥
en: Arjuna said You are now the best friend of the Kurus. Being related to both parties by thick ties, you are now their friend.

sn: पाण्डवैर्धार्तराष्ट्राणां प्रतिपाद्यमनामयम्। समर्थः प्रशमं चैव कर्तुमर्हसि केशव॥
en: O Keshava, you are competent to bring about what is good both for the Pandavas and the son of Dhritarashtra; and therefore it is proper that you should bring about peace between them.

sn: त्वमितः पुण्डरीकाक्ष सुयोधनममर्षणम्। शान्त्यर्थं भ्रातरंब्रूया यत् तद् वाच्यममित्रहन्॥
en: Having set out from here, O you like lotus, being free from wrath to Suyodhana, with the objects of peace, speak to our brothers what should be spoken, O you slayer of enemies.

sn: त्वया धर्मार्थयुक्तं चेदुक्तं शिवमनामयम्। हितं नादास्यते बालो दिष्टस्य वशमेष्यति॥
en: with eyes If the boy does not accept your beneficial words conducive both to morality and worldly good and calculated to assure their weal; then shall he be subject to his fate,

sn: श्रीभगवानुवाच धर्म्यमस्मद्धितं चैव कुरूणां यदनामयम्। एष यास्यामि राजानं धृतराष्ट्रमभीप्सया॥
en: The blessed God said I shall go to king Dhritarashtra with the desire of doing what is righteous and what is our good and the benefit of the Kuru.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततो व्यपेततमसि सूर्ये विमलवद्गते। मैत्रे मुहूर्ते सम्प्राप्ते मृदर्चिषि दिवाकरे॥
en: Vaishampayana said The night passed away and the sun having risen, as it were and on the setting in of the moment, called Maitri, while the rays of the sun were still mild.

sn: कौमुदे मासि रेवत्यां शरदन्ते हिमागमे। स्फीतसस्यसुखे काले कल्पः सत्त्ववतां वरः॥
en: In the month of Kaumuda (Kartika) under the constellation of Revati after the passing away of Autumn and in the dewy season and at time when the earth had an abundance of crops on it, that foremost of men of prowess

sn: मङ्गल्याः पुण्यनिर्घोषा वाचः शृण्वंश्च सूनृताः। ब्राह्मणानां प्रतीतानामृषीणामिव वासवः॥ कृत्वा पौर्वाह्निकं कृत्यं स्नातः शुचिरलंकृतः। उपतस्थे विवस्वन्तं पावकं च जनार्दनः॥ ऋषभं पृष्ठ आलभ्य ब्राह्मणानभिवाद्य च। अग्नि प्रदक्षिणं कृत्वा पश्यन् कल्याणमग्रतः॥ तत् प्रतिज्ञाय वचनं पाण्डवस्य जनार्दनः। शिने प्तारमासीनमभ्यभाषत सात्यकिम्॥
en: (Janardana) listening to auspicious and lily sounding words by the Brahmanas, like Vasava hearing the prayers of the Rishis and having performed the customary rites of the morning and after a bath wearing holy ornaments, worshipped the sun and the fire, having touched the tail of a bull and having paid due respect to the Brahmanas and going round the fire and looking an auspicious object placed before him, Janardana addressed Satyaki, the grandson of Shirii, who was seated near, after knowing the exact wishes of the Pandava (Yudhishthira), sayingरथ आरोप्यतां शङ्खश्चक्रं च गदया सह।

sn: उपासंगाच शक्त्यश्च सर्वप्रहरणानि च॥
en: ‘Make ready my car along with my conch, discus and mace and my arrows and arrowholders all sorts of offensive and defensive weapons;

sn: दुर्योधनश्च दुष्टात्मा कर्णश्च सहसौबलः। न च शत्रुरवज्ञेयो दुर्बलोऽपि बलीयसा॥
en: For Duryodhana is wicked-souled and so are Karna and the son of Subala. Even by a strong man an enemy should not be made light of though be he weak.

sn: ततस्तन्मतमाज्ञाय केशवस्य पुरःसराः। प्रसस्रुर्योजयिष्यन्तो रथं चक्रगदाभृतः॥
en: Knowing his wishes, the attendants of Keshava, the wielder of the mace and the discus, employed themselves in yoking the car.

sn: तं दीप्तमिव कालाग्निमाकाशगमिवाशुगम्। सूर्यचन्द्रप्रकाशाभ्यां चक्राभ्यां समलंकृतम्॥
en: The car was shining and effulgent like the fire appearing before the dissolution of the world and quick of speed like the wind and ornamented with two wheels which were shining like the sun and the moon.

sn: अर्धचन्दैश्च चन्द्रश्च मत्स्यैः समृगपक्षिभिः। पुष्पैश्च विविधैश्चित्रं मणिरत्नैश्च सर्वशः॥
en: (And it was ornamented) with figures of half moons and of fishes, animals and birds with various kinds of flowers and with all sorts of precious stones all over.

sn: तरुणादित्यसंकाशं बृहन्तं चारुदर्शनम्। मणिहेमविचित्राङ्गं सुध्वजं सुपताकिनम्॥
en: It was beautiful to look at, being large and effulgent like the morning sun and having its several parts ornamented with gems and gold and furnished with nice flags and banners. Ornamented with gems and gold and furnished with nice flags and banners.

sn: सूपस्करमनाधृष्यं वैयाघ्रपरिवारणम्। यशोघ्र प्रत्यमित्राणां यदूनां नन्दिवर्धनम्॥
en: Ornamented with beautiful objects and covered over with tiger skins, it was incapable of being opposed, the destroyer of the fame of enemies and the cause of enhancement of the joys of the Yadu race.

sn: वाजिभिः शैब्यसुग्रीवमेघपुष्पबलाहकैः। स्नातैः सम्पादयामासुः सम्पन्नैः सर्वसम्पदा॥
en: They yoked to it the horses Shaivya, Sugriva, Meghapushpa and Balahaka, after they had been bathed and attired in all their harness.

sn: महिमानं तु कृष्णस्य भूय एवाभिवर्धयन्। सुघोषः पतगेन्द्रेण ध्वजेन युयुजे रथः॥
en: And, as if enhancing the glory of Krishna, the chariot with flag was perched on with a loud noise by the chief of the fatherly creation.

sn: तं मेरुशिखरप्रख्यं मेघदुन्दुभिनिस्वनम्। आरुरोह रथं शौरिविमानमिव कामगम्॥
en: Shaurin then ascended the chariot, which moved along at the will of the rider, which was high as the peak of the Meru and which rattled as the roar of the clouds or the sound of the kettle drums.

sn: ततः सात्यकिमारोप्य प्रययौ पुरुषोत्तमः। पृथिवीं चान्तरिक्षं च रथघोषेण नादयन्॥
en: Then having caused Satyaki to mount on it, that best of male beings set out filling the earth and the sky with the rattle of the wheels of the chariot.

sn: व्यपोढाभ्रस्ततः कालः क्षणेन समपद्यत। शिवश्चानुववौ वायुः प्रशान्तमभवद् रजः॥
en: And in a moment the sky became cloudless; and favourable winds blew; and the weather became calm and serene.

sn: प्रदक्षिणानुलोमाश्च मङ्गल्या मृगपक्षिणः। प्रयाणे वासुदेवस्य बभूवुरनुयायिनः॥
en: Auspicious animals and birds going round the car became the followers of Vasudeva in his journey.

sn: मङ्गल्यार्थप्रदैः शब्दैरन्ववर्तन्त सर्वशः। सारसाः शतपत्राश्च हंसाश्च मधुसूदनम्॥
en: The birds of the crane peacock and goose species followed the slayer of Madhu with sounds signifying the attainment of the object for which the journey was undertaken.

sn: मन्त्राहुतिमहाहोमैहूयमानश्च पावकः। प्रदक्षिणमुखो भूत्वा विधूमः समपद्यत॥
en: The fire, too, on which had been offered Homa libations accompanied by incantations, became bright and smokeless inclining towards the right.

sn: वसिष्ठो वामदेवश्च भूरिद्युम्नो गयः क्रथः। शुक्रनारदवाल्मीका मरुत्तः कुशिको भृगुः॥ देवब्रह्मर्षयश्चैव कृष्णं यदुसुखावहम्। प्रदक्षिणमवर्तन्त सहिता वासवानुजम्॥
en: Vasishtha and Vamadeva, Bhuridyumna, Gaya, Kratha, Shukra, Narada and Valmika, Maruta, Kushika and Bhrigu and other Brahmarshis and the gods united together and stood to the right of Krishna, who contributed to the happiness of the Yadus and was ihe younger brother of Vasava.

sn: एवमेतैर्महाभागैर्महर्षिगणसाधुभिः। पूजितः प्रययौ कृष्णः कुरूणां सदनं प्रति॥
en: In this way worshipped by this blessed group of great qualities, Krishna set out for the encampment of the Kurus.

sn: तं प्रयान्तमनुप्रायात् कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः। भीमसेनार्जुनौ चोभो माद्रीपुत्रौ च पाण्डवौ।॥ चेकितानश्च विक्रान्तो धृष्टकेतुश्च चेदिपः। दुपदः काशिराजश्च शिखण्डी च महारथः॥ धृष्टद्युम्नः सपुत्रश्च विराटः केकयैः सह। संसाधनार्थ प्रययुः क्षत्रियाः क्षत्रियर्षभ॥
en: Yudhishthira, the son of Kunti, Bhimasena and Arjuna and the two descendants of Pandu-the two sons of Madri followed him as he proceeded along. The powerful Chekitana and Dhrishtaketu, the lord of the Chedis, Drupada, Kashi and the great car-warrior Shikhandi and Dhrishtadyumna and Virata in company with his sons, the Kaikeya princes, all Kshatriyas followed the bull of the Kshatriya race to attain his object.

sn: ततोऽनुव्रज्य गोविन्दं धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः। राज्ञां सकाशे द्युतिमानुवाचेदं वचस्तदा॥
en: And the just king Yudhishthira, endued with luster, having followed Govinda to some distance, said these words in the midst of those kings.

sn: यो वै न कामान भयान्न लोभान्नार्थकारणात्। अन्यायमनुवर्तेत स्थिरबुद्धिरलोलुपः॥
en: He, who from desire or anger, fear or object of gaining his ends, never does an unjust act; and he who is of a calm intellect and not given to avarice,

sn: धर्मज्ञो धृतिमान् प्राज्ञः सर्वभूतेषु केशवः। ईश्वरः सर्वभूतानां देवदेवः सनातनः॥
en: Who knows what virtue is, who is wise and endued with intelligence, who is cognizant of the inner working of the hearts of all beings, who is the lord of all creatures and the eternal god of the gods.

sn: तं सर्वगुणसम्पन्न श्रीवत्सकृतलक्षणम्। सम्परिष्वज्य कौन्तेयः संदेष्टुमुपचक्रमे॥
en: The son of Kunti embracing this being, endued with all the virtues and having the mark of the auspicious whirl on his person, began to address thus-

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच या सा बाल्यात् प्रभृत्यस्मान् पर्यवर्धयताबला। उपवासतप:शीला सदा स्वस्त्ययने रता॥ देवतातिथिपूजासु गुरुशुश्रूषणे रता। वत्सला प्रियपुत्रा च प्रियास्माकं जनार्दन॥ सुयोधनभयाद् या नोऽत्रायतामित्रकर्शन। महतो मृत्युसम्बाधादुद्धरेनौरिवार्णवात्॥ अस्मत्कृते च सततं यया दुःखानि माधव। अनुभूतान्यदुःखार्हाः तां स्म पृच्छेरनामयम्॥
en: Yudhishthira said The lady, who had reared us from our infancy, with whom fasts and devotion are habits and who is ever attached to propitiatory rites and ceremonics, who is attached to the worship of the Gods and the guest and the due service of her elder, who is fond of her sons and bearing great affection for them and who, OJanardana, are dear to us, who has saved us from the wickedness of Suyodhana, O grinder of enemies, like a boat (saving the ship wracked) from the great and terrific death in the sea and by whom troubles have often been encountered, O Madhava, for our sake, though she herself is not desiring it, should be interrogated regarding her welfare.

sn: भृशमाश्वासयेश्चैनां पुत्रशोकपरिप्लुताम्। अभिवाद्य स्वजेथास्त्वं पाण्डवान् परिकीर्तयन्॥
en: Having saluted her first, embrace this lady and comfort her, who is filled with grief for her sons by talking again and again of the Pandavas.

sn: ऊढात् प्रभृति दुःखानि श्वसुराणामरिंदम। निकारानतदर्हा च पश्यन्ती दुःखमश्नुते॥
en: Ever since her wedding has she, O chastiser of foes, encountered troubles and grief's due to her father-in-law, though she has not deserved these.

sn: अपि जातु स काल: स्यात् कृष्ण दुःखविपर्ययः। यदहं मातरं क्लिष्टा सुखं दद्यामरिंदम॥
