en: Will there ever come a time, O Krishna, when at the end of all my troubles, I shall give my troubled mother happiness, O chastiser of foes.

sn: प्रव्रजन्तोऽनुधावन्तीं कृपणां पुत्रगृद्धिनीम्। रुदतीमुपहायैनामगच्छाम वयं वनम्॥
en: When we were about to go into exile, she followed us in distress out of fondness for her children crying aloud; but we went to the forest leaving her behind.

sn: न नूनं म्रियते दुःखैः सा चेज्जीवति केशव। तथा पुत्रादिभिर्गाढमार्ता ह्यानर्तसत्कृत॥
en: One does not necessarily die of grief and if she is alive, O Keshava, hospitably entertained by the Anartas through in extreme distress on account of her sons and others.

sn: अभिवाद्याथ सा कृष्ण त्वया मद्वचनाद् विभो। धृतराष्ट्रश्च कौरव्यौ राजानश्च वयोऽधिकाः॥ भीष्मं द्रोणं कृपं चैव महाराजं च बाह्निकम्। द्रौणिं च सोमदत्तं च सर्वांश्च भरतान् प्रति॥ विदुरं च महाप्राज्ञं कुरूणां मन्त्रधारिणम्। अगाधबुद्धिं मर्मज्ञं स्वजेथा मधुसूदन॥
en: Then, O Krishna, having greeted her on my behalf, O Lord and also Dhritarashtra and the kings on the side of the Kurus and those who are my seniors in age and Bhishma and Drona and Kripa and the great king Balhika and the son of Drona and Somadatta and all the Bharatas and the exceedingly wise Vidura, the adviser of the Kurus, O slayer of Madhu, that man of illimitable knowledge and conversant with the rulers of morality should be embraced by you.

sn: इत्युक्त्वा केशवं तत्र राजमध्ये युधिष्ठिरः। अनुज्ञातो निववृते कृष्णां कृत्वा प्रदक्षिणम्॥
en: Yudhishthira, having thus addressed Keshava in the midst of those kings, returned at the bidding of Krishna, after going round him.

sn: व्रजन्नेव तु बीभत्सुः सखायं पुरुषर्षभम्। अब्रवीत् परवीरनं दाशार्हमपराजितम्॥
en: Vibhatsu, too, as he proceeded along, said to his friend, that bull among men, that slayer of heroes on the enemy's side, that scion of the Dasharha race who has never been defeated.

sn: यदस्माकं विभो वृत्तं पुरा वै मन्त्रनिश्चये। अर्धराज्यस्य गोविन्द विदितं सर्वराजसु॥
en: O Lord, O Govinda, it is know among all the kings that it has already been decided in our consultation to demand the return of one half of the kingdom.

sn: तच्चेद् दद्यादसंगेन सत्कृत्यानवमन्य च। प्रियं मे स्यान्महाबाहो मुच्येरन् महतो भयात्॥
en: And if they give us that for the sake of honesty without insult to us and with due respect to yourself, then, O you with long arms, they should do what is desired by me and themselves escape a great evil.

sn: अतश्चेदन्यथा कर्ता धार्तराष्ट्रोऽनुपायवित्। अन्तं नूनं करिष्यामि क्षत्रियाणां जनार्दन॥
en: But if the son of Dhritarashtra, who is not cognizant of the proper way of executing acts, does otherwise, I shall surely bring on the annihilation of the Kshatriyas, O Janardana.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्ते पाण्डवेन समहृष्यद् वृकोदरः। मुहुर्मुहुः क्रोधवशात् प्रावेपत च पाण्डवः॥
en: The son of Pandu (Arjuna) having thus addressed, Vrikodara became greatly pleased; and every moment out of rage, the Pandava's frames shook.

sn: वेपमानश्च कौन्तेयः प्राक्रोशन्महतो रवान्। धनंजयवचः श्रुत्वा हर्षोत्सिक्तमना भृशम्॥
en: And while trembling, the son of Kunti sent forth loud shouts hearing the words of Dhananjaya; and his mind was exceedingly filled with delight.

sn: तस्य तं निनदं श्रुत्वा सम्प्रावेपन्त धन्विनः। वाहनानि च सर्वाणि शकृन्मूत्रे प्रसुस्रुवुः॥
en: Hearing that shout of his, the bowmen trembled (with fear); and the animals in the army passed urine and dung.

sn: इत्युक्त्वा केशवं तत्र तथा चोक्त्वा विनिश्चयम्। अनुज्ञातो निववृते परिष्वज्य जनार्दनम्॥
en: Having thus addressed Keshava and thus given out his resolve, he (Arjuna) returned at his bidding after first going round Janardana.

sn: तेषु राजसु सर्वेषु निवृत्तेषु जनार्दनः। तूर्णमभ्यगमद्धृष्टः शैव्यसुग्रीववाहनः॥
en: And all these kings having returned Janardana made good progress in his journey, light of heart, drawn by Saivya and Sugriva.

sn: ते हया वासुदेवस्य दारुकेण दारुकेण प्रचोदिताः। पन्थानमाचेमुरिव ग्रसमाना इवाम्बरम्॥
en: These horses of Vasudeva, led by Daruka, (wenton) as if kissing the roads and swallowing the sky.

sn: अथापश्यन्महावाहुर्ऋषीनध्वनि केशवः। ब्राह्मया श्रिया दीप्यमानान् स्थितानुभयतः पथि॥
en: Keshava of long arms saw on the road, standing on either side, several Rishis effulgent with the Brahmic luster; and Janardana, too, quickly alighting from his chariot paid them due respects.

sn: सोऽवतीर्य स्थात् तूर्णमभिवाद्य जनार्दनः। यथावृत्तानृषीन् सर्वानभ्यभाषत पूजयन्॥
en: Then Janardana quickly step down from his chariot, and said all those Rishis with adoration and respect.

sn: कच्चिल्लोकेषु कुशलं कच्चिद् धर्मः स्वनुष्ठितः। ब्राह्मणानां त्रयो वर्णाः कच्चित् तिष्ठन्ति शासने॥
en: As he worshipped them, he addressed to each in suitable terms, inquiring of them if all went on well in the worlds and if piety was well established there. And also if the three orders acted in obedience to the Brahmanas.

sn: तेभ्यः प्रयुज्य तां पूजां प्रोवाच मधुसूदनः। भगवन्तः क्व संसिद्धाः का वीथी भवतामिह॥ किं वा कार्यं भगवतामहं किं करवाणि वः। केनार्थेनोपसम्प्राप्ता भगवन्तो महीतलम्॥
en: Having paid them due honours, the slayer of Madhu said to them. What is the object of you prosperous ones? Where are you going? What are you, prosperous beings, going to do? What shall I do for you? With what object have you, prosperous ones, come down to the face of the earth?

sn: तमब्रवीज्जामदग्न्य उपेत्य मधुसूदनम्। परिष्वज्य च गोविन्दं सुरासुरपतेः सखा।॥
en: The son of Jamadagni said coming near that slayer of Madhu the friend of the lord of the gods and the Asuras had embraced Govinda and said-

sn: देवर्षयः पुण्यकृतो ब्राह्मणाश्च बहुश्रुताः। राजर्षयश्च दाशार्ह मानयन्तस्तपस्विनः। देवासुरस्य द्रष्टारः पुराणस्य महामते॥ समेतं पार्थिवं क्षत्रं दिदृक्षन्तश्च सर्वतः। सभासदश्च राजानस्त्वां च सत्यं जनार्दनम्॥ एतन्महत् प्रेक्षणीयं द्रष्टुं गच्छाम केशव। धर्मार्थसहिता वाचः श्रोतुमिच्छाम माधव॥
en: The divine Rishis and vastly learned Brahmanas of a pious life. And Rishis of royal descent, O you of the Dasharha race, as also venerable devotees, who were witnesses, O you exceedingly wise Being, to the ancient feats of the gods and the Asuras. Are desirous of seeing all the Kshatriya rulers of the earth and the countries and the kings assembled together from all sides, as also yourself, the true Janardana. We are going, O Keshava, to behold this grand sight worthy of being seen; and we desire to hear, O Madhava, words conducive to morality and worldly profit. Which will be addressed by you to the Kurus in the midst of the kings, O you chastiser of foes.

sn: त्वयोच्यमानाः कुरुषु राजमध्ये परंतप। भीष्मद्रोणादयश्चैव विदुरश्च महामतिः॥
en: Bhishma, Drona and others as also the greatly intelligent Vidura and yourself, O you tiger among the race of the Yadus, will be assembled together in the Council Chamber.

sn: त्वं च यादवशार्दूल सभायां वै समेष्यथ। तव वाक्यानि दिव्यानि तथा तेषां च माधव॥ श्रोतुमिच्छाम गोविन्द सत्यानि च हितानि च।
en: O Govinda, O Madhava, we desire to hear your divine, truth and of benefit words assembled together in the Council Chamber.

sn: आपृष्टोऽसि महाबाहो पुनर्चक्ष्यामहे वयम्॥ याह्यविन्नेन वै वीर द्रक्ष्यामस्त्वां समागतम्। आसीनमासने दिव्ये बलतेज:समाहितम्॥
en: You now know our purpose, O you of long arms; and you will again see us. O hero, we will see you come to the Council safely and sealed on a divine seat, endued with strength and prowess.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच प्रयान्तं देवकीपुत्रं परवीररुजो दश। महारथा महाबाहुमन्वयुः शस्त्रपाणयः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Ten mighty car-warriors capable of vanquishing heroes on the enemy's side with arms in their hands followed the son of Devaki of long arms as he proceeded along.

sn: पदातीनां सहस्रं च सादिनां च परंतप। भोज्यं च विपुलं राजन् प्रेष्याच शतशोऽपरे॥
en: A thousand foot-soldiers and a thousand horsemen too (followed him) O chastiser of foes; as also hurdreds of others carrying sufficient provision and other things. one was

sn: जनमेजय उवाच कथं प्रयातो दाशार्हो महात्मा मधुसूदनः। कानि वा व्रजतस्तस्य निमित्तानि महौजसः॥
en: Jariamejaya said How did the great should scion of the Dasharha race, the slayer of Madhu, go on his journey; and what were the omens observed when that of great prowess journeying?

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तस्य प्रयाणे यान्यासन् निमित्तानि महात्मनः। तानि मे शृणु सर्वाणि दैवान्यौत्यातिकानि च॥
en: Vaishampayana said Listen from me to all these omens that were observed when the large-souled che commenced the journey. Some of them were earthly and heavenly.

sn: अनभ्रेऽशनिनिर्घोषः सविद्युत् समजायत। अन्वगेव च पर्जन्यः प्रावर्षद् विघने भृशम्॥
en: In the cloudless sky lightning were heard with loud roars; while behind him clouds poured down shower of rain.

sn: प्रत्यगूहुर्महानद्यः प्राङ्मुखाः सिन्धुसप्तमाः। विपरीता दिश: सर्वा न प्राज्ञायत किंचन॥
en: The seven large rivers with the Sindhu flowing to go east, turned their courses in the contrary detection. The cardinal points were reversed, as it were; and nothing could be distinguished.

sn: प्राज्वलन्नग्नयो राजन् पृथिवी समकम्पत। उदपानाश्च कुम्भाश्च प्रासिञ्चञ्छतशो जलम्॥
en: The fires were ablaze, o king and the earth shook; and well and water pots shot forth water by hundreds and flowed out.

sn: तमः संवृतमप्यासीत् सर्वं जगदिदं तथा। न दिशो नादिशो राजन् प्रज्ञायन्ते स्म रेणुना॥
en: The whole of this world was enveloped with darkness; and neither the cardinal nor subsidiary points of the earth could be known on account of the dust that was raised.

sn: प्रादुरासीन्महाञ्छब्दः खे शरीरंदृशयते। सर्वेषु राजन् देशेषु तदद्भुतमिवाभवत्॥
en: There were loud roars though no body could be seen in this earth; and in all countries, Oking there occurred the same strange things.

sn: प्रामथ्नाद्धास्तिनपुरं वातो दक्षिणपश्चिमः। आरुजन् गणशो वृक्षान् परुषोऽशनिनिस्वनः॥
en: A gale from the south-west devastated the city of Hastinapura, uprooting clusters of trees; and there were loud sounds in the sky.

sn: यत्र यत्र च वार्ष्णेयो वर्तते पथि भारत। तत्र तत्र सुखो वायुः सर्वं चासीत् प्रदक्षिणम्॥
en: But wherever, O Bharata, the scion of the Vrishni race went on his way; there were favourable winds and everything went right.

sn: ववर्ष पुष्पवर्षं च कमलानि च भूरिशः। समश्च पन्था निर्दुःखो व्यपेतकुशकण्टकः॥
en: There was a down-fall of flowers including large numbers of lotuscs. The roads became plain and divested of prickly grass and thorns.

sn: संस्तुतो ब्राह्मणैर्गीर्भिस्तत्र तत्र सहस्रशः। अर्च्यते मधुपश्च वसुभिश्च वसुप्रदः॥
en: Wherever he went, the giver of wealth was praised by the Brahmanas by thousands by laudatory words; and they served him with curds, honey, clarified butter and riches.

sn: तं किरन्ति महात्मानं वन्यैः पुष्पैः सुगन्धिभिः। स्त्रियः पथि समागम्य सर्वभूतहिते रतम्॥
en: Women coming out on the highways threw on the great-souled one attached to the good of all creatures wild flowers of great fragrance.

sn: स शालिभवनं रम्यं सर्वसस्यसमाचितम्। सुखं परमर्मिष्ठमभ्यगाद् भरतर्षभ॥
en: He then Shalibhavana, enchanting spot filled with all sorts of crops, a place that was at once delicious and sacred, O bull of the Bharata race.

sn: पश्यन् बहुपशून् ग्रामान् रम्यान् हृदयतोषणान्। पुराणि च व्यतिक्रामन् राष्ट्राणि विविधानि च॥
en: After having seen many animals and beautiful villages enchanting the heart and after traversing diverse cities and kingdoms.

sn: नित्यं हृष्टाः सुमनसो भारतैरभिरक्षिताः। नोद्विग्नाः परचक्राणां व्यसनानामकोविदाः॥ उपप्लव्यादथागम्य जनाः पुरनिवासिनः। पथ्यतिष्ठन्त सहिता विष्वक्सेनदिदृक्षया॥
en: Ever of cheerful hearts, of good minds and well protected by the Bharatas and therefore not caring for the designs of the enemies and incognizant of all sorts of calamities, the people and the inhabitants of the city of Upaplavya, coming out of the city, stood on the roads desirous of beholding Vishvaksena.

sn: ते तु सर्वे समायान्तमग्निमिद्धमिव प्रभुम्। अर्चयामासुरर्चाहँ देशातिथिमुपस्थितम्॥
en: And they too worshipped the worshipful guest, who had come to their country-the lord who had arrived there as blazing fire.

sn: वृकस्थलं समासाद्य केशवः परवीरहा। प्रकीर्णरश्मावादित्ये व्योम्नि वै होहितायति॥
en: Keshava, the slayer of heroes on the enemy's side, having come near Vrikasthala, the sky was reddened by the rays shot by the sun.

sn: अवतीर्य रथात् तूर्णं कृत्वा शौचं यथाविधि। रथमोचनमादिश्य संध्यामुपविवेश ह॥
en: Quickly getting down from his chariot and having undergone the purifactory rites according to the usual custom and ordering for his chariot to be unyoked, he sat down for the customary evening duties.

sn: दारुकोऽपि हयान् मुक्त्वा परिचर्य च शास्त्रतः। मुमोच सर्वयोक्त्रादि मुक्त्वा चैतानवासृजत्॥
en: Daruka, too having unyoked the horses and after having tended them according to the science of the management of horses and taking down all the trappings, set them completely free.

sn: अभ्यतीत्य तु तत् सर्वमुवाच मधुसूदनः। युधिष्ठिरस्य कार्यार्थमिह वत्स्यामहे क्षपाम्॥
en: All this being done, the slayer of Madhu said-with view to the attainment of Yudhishthira's object must we pass the night here.

sn: तस्य तन्मतमाज्ञाय चक्रुरावसथं नराः। क्षणेन चान्नपानानि गुणवन्ति समार्जयन्॥
en: The men, knowing that intention of his in a moment, prepared a lodging; and collected together suitable food and drink.

sn: तस्मिन् ग्रामे प्रधानास्तु य आसन् ब्राह्मणा नृप। आर्याः कुलीना ह्रीमन्तो ब्राह्मी वृत्तिमनुष्ठिताः॥
en: The chief Brahmanas, that were in that village, O ruler of men, that were of noble ways of life, of good birth, modest and given to the observance of the Vedic rules and

sn: तेऽभिगम्य महात्मानं हृषीकेशमरिंदमम्। पूजां चक्रुर्यथान्यायमाशीर्मङ्गसंयुताम्॥
en: Having come near the great-souled Hrishikesha, the chastiser the chastiser of foes, honored him with suitable blessings and auspicious speeches.

sn: ते पूजयित्वा दाशार्ह सर्वलोकेषु पूजितम्। न्यवेदयन्त वेश्मानि रनवन्ति महात्मने॥
en: Having done honours to the scion of the Dasharha race, who was honoured in all the worlds, they placed at the disposal of the greatsouled one their houses filled with wealth.

sn: तान् प्रभुः कृतमित्युक्त्वा सत्कृत्य च यथार्हतः। अभ्येत्य चैषां वेश्मानि पुनरायात् सहैव तैः॥
en: The Lord saving to them "you have done your part” and paying then due homage and coming to their houses, again came back to his own encampment with their company,

sn: सुमृष्टं भोजयित्वा च ब्राह्मणांस्तत्र केशवः। भुक्त्वा च सह तैः सर्वैरवसत् तां क्षपां सुखम्॥
en: Keshava, feeding the Brahmanas there to their satisfaction and having himself eaten in company of all of them, spent the night in happiness. Happlicad.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तथा दूतैः समाज्ञाय प्रयान्तं मधुसूदनम्। धृतराष्ट्रोऽब्रवीद् भीष्ममर्चयित्वा महाभुजम्॥ द्रोणं च संजयं चैव विदुरं च महामतिम्। दुर्योधनं सहामात्यं हृष्टरोमाब्रवीदिदम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said In the mean time, having come to know of the departure of the slayer of Madhu (from the Pandava camp) through his spies, Dhritarashtra said to Bhishma of long arms after paying him due honours; and also to Drona and Sanjaya and the greatly intelligent Vidura his hairs standing up and also to Duryodhana and his ministers.

sn: अद्भुतं महदाश्चर्यं श्रूयते कुरुनन्दन। स्त्रियो बालाश्च वृद्धाश्च कथयन्ति गृहे गृहे॥ सत्कृत्याचक्षते चान्ये तथैवान्ये समागताः। पृथग्वादाश्च वर्तन्ते चत्वरेषु सभासु च॥
en: o descendant of Kuru, I hear a strange thing-an exceedingly one. Women and children and old men are talking about it in every household. Some are discussing the subject out of good motives; while others are doing it, united together or separately; and the discussion is going on within the houses, as also in open spots.

sn: उपायास्यति दाशार्हः पाण्डवार्थं पराक्रमी। स नो मान्यश्च पूज्यश्च सर्वथा मधुसूदनः॥
en: The powerful scion of Dasharha race is coming here for the sake of the Pandavas; and that slayer of Madhu is by all means the object of our respect and regard.

sn: तस्मिन् हि यात्रा लोकस्य भूतानामीश्वरो हि सः। तस्मिन् धृतिश्च वीर्यं च प्रज्ञा चौजश्च माधवे॥
en: On him depends the course of the world. He is the lord of all creatures, and in that scion of Madhu's are centered patience, prowess, wisdom and energy.

sn: स मान्यता नरश्रेष्ठः स हि धर्मः सनातनः। पूजितो हि सुखाय स्यादसुखः स्यादपूजितः॥
en: That chief among men ought to be respected by the good; for he is the eternal virtue. For the sake of happiness is he worshipped. If he is not due regard, misery race ensues.

sn: स चेत् तुष्यति दाशार्ह उपचारैररिंदमः। कृष्णात् सर्वानभिप्रायान् प्राप्स्यामः सर्वराजसु॥
en: If that chastiser of foes of the Dasharha race is satisfied with due reception; them shall we obtain the fulfillment of all our wishes from i Krishna in the midst of all the kings.

sn: तस्य पूजार्थमद्यैव संविधत्स्व परंतप। सभाः पथि विधीयन्तां सर्वकामसमन्विताः॥
en: O chastiser of foes, prepare for his worship from this moment and erect pavilions on the way filled with all necessary articles.

sn: यथा प्रीतिर्महाबाहो त्वयि जायेत तस्य वै। तथा कुरुष्व गान्धारे कथं वा भीष्म मन्यसे॥१०
en: So that one of long arins may be gratified with you. Do that, O son of Gandhari. What do you think. O Bhisma?

sn: ततो भीष्मादयः सर्वे धृतराष्ट्र जनाधिपम्। ऊचुः परममित्येवं पूजयन्तोऽस्य तद् वचः॥
en: Then Bhishma and others all approving of those words of his said to Dhritarashtra, the ruler of men-"This excellent."

sn: तेषामनुमतं ज्ञात्वा राजा दुर्योधनस्तदा। सभावास्तूनि रम्याणि प्रदेष्टुमुपचक्रमे॥
en: King Duryodhana, then ascertaining that desire of theirs began to order the selection of sites for the erection of enchanting Pavilions.

sn: ततो देशेषु देशेषु रमणीयेषु भागशः। सर्वरत्नसमाकीर्णा: सभाश्चक्रुरनेकशः॥
en: Then in all places and in the most enchanting sites there were erected many pavilions (at proper intervals) adorned with all sorts of gems and precious stones.

sn: आसनानि विचित्राणि युतानि विविधैर्गुणैः। स्त्रियो गन्धानलंकारान् सूक्ष्माणि वसनानि च॥ गुणवन्त्यन्नपानानि भोज्यानि विविधानि च। माल्यानि च सुगन्धीनि तानि राजा ददौ ततः॥
en: The king then sent there beautiful seats endued with various good qualities, girls, scents ornaments fine cloths, eatables and drinks of excellent qualities, garlands and perfumes of several kinds.

sn: विशेषतश्च वासार्थं सभां ग्रामे वृकस्थले। विदधे कौरवो राजा बहुरत्नां मनोरमाम्॥
en: Especially for his residence in the town of Vrikasthala the Kuru king erected an enchanting palace adorned with many gems and precious stones.

sn: एतद् विधाय वै सर्वं देवाहमतिमानुषम्। आचख्यौ धृतराष्ट्राय राजा दुर्योधनस्तदा।॥
en: Having done all this, which could be done only by gods and men of superhuman qualifications, king Duryodhana informed Dhritarashtra of what he had done.

sn: ता: सभाः केशवः सर्वा रत्नानि विविधानि च। असमीक्ष्यैव दाशार्ह उपायात् कुरुसद्म तत्॥
en: That scion of the Dasharha race, Keshava, however, came to that encampment of the Kurus without even casting his eyes on all those pavilions and diverse sorts of gems and precious stones.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच उपप्लव्यादिह क्षत्तरुपायातो जनार्दनः। वृकस्थले निवसति स च प्रातरिहैष्यति॥
en: Dhritarashtra said O Kshatriya (Vidura), Janardana has set out from Upaplavya. He is now staying at Vrikasthala; and will come here in the morning.

sn: आहुकानामधिपतिः पुरोगः सर्वसात्वताम्। महामना महावीर्यो महासत्त्वो जनार्दनः॥
en: Janardana is the rule of the Ahukas, the foremost of the scions of the Satvata race, is large-minded, of great prowess and great energy.

sn: स्फीतस्य वृष्णिराष्ट्रस्य भर्ता गोप्ता च माधवः। त्रयाणामपि लोकानां भगवान् प्रपितामहः॥
en: Madhava, too, is the lord and protector of the rising and prosperous kingdom of the Vrishnis; and that divine being is the great grandfather of the three worlds.

sn: वृष्ण्यन्धकाः सुमनसो यस्य प्रज्ञामुपासते। आदित्या वसवो रुद्रा यथा बुद्धिं बृहस्पतेः॥
en: The Vrishnis and the Andhakas of honest minds honour his wisdom; as the Adityas, the Vasus and the Rudras do the intelligence of Brihaspati.

sn: तस्मै पूजां प्रयोक्ष्यामि दाशार्हाय महात्मने। प्रत्यक्षं तव धर्मज्ञ तां मे कथयतः शृणु॥
en: That large-souled scion of the Dasharha race shall I worship in your immediate presence. O you conversant with mediate presence. O you conversant with virtue, listen to me speaking of that worship.

sn: एकवर्गः सुक्लृप्तार्बाह्निजातैहयोत्तमैः। चतुर्युक्तान् रथांस्तस्मैरौक्मान् दास्यामिषोडश॥
en: I shall present to him sixteen golden chariots, each drawn by excellent horses of the same colour bred of the Bahlika species and all well equipped.

sn: नित्यप्रभिन्नान् मातङ्गानीषादन्तान् प्रहारिणः। अष्टानुचरमेकैकमष्टौ दास्यामि कौरव॥
en: O son of Kuru, I shall also present him eight elephants capable of working havoc among the enemy, whose juice shall be ever flowing from their temples and whose tusk shall be equal to sloughs, each with eight human attendants.

sn: दासीनामप्रजातानां शुभानां रुक्मवर्चसाम्। शतमस्मै प्रदास्यामि दासानामपि तावताम्॥
en: A hundred of maid servants beautiful and without issue and beauty of gold, shall I give to him; and the same number of man-servants.

sn: आविकं च सुखस्पर्श पार्वतीयैरुपाहृतम्। तदप्यस्मै प्रदास्यामि सहस्राणि दशाष्ट च॥
en: Blankets pleasant to touch and procured from hilly tracts shall I give to him eighteen thousand in number.

sn: अजिनानां सहस्राणि चीनदेशोद्भवानि च। तान्यप्यस्मै प्रदास्यामि यावदर्हति केशवः॥
en: Thousands of deer skins produced in the country of China shall I give to him and whatever else may be fitting gifts to Keshava.

sn: दिवा रात्रौ च भात्येष सुतेजा विमलो मणिः। तमप्यस्मै प्रदास्यामि तमर्हति हि केशवः॥
en: I shall give him this pure and very bright gem that shines day and night; for Keshava is the proper recipient of these.

sn: एकनाभिपतत्यह्रा योजनानि चतुर्दश। यानमश्वतरीयुक्तं दास्ये तस्मै तदप्यहम्॥
en: This chariot drawn by excellent horses that traverses fourtcen yojanas in a single day, that too shall I give him.

sn: यावन्ति वाहनान्यस्य यावन्तः पुरुषाश्च ते। ततोऽष्टगुणमप्यस्मै भोज्यं दास्याम्यहं सदा॥
en: I shall present to him eight times the eatables that all his attendants and animals in the army may consume.

sn: मम पुत्राश्च पौत्राश्च सर्वे दुर्योधनादृते। प्रत्युद्यास्यन्ति दाशार्ह रथैर्पष्टैः स्वलंकृताः॥
en: All my sons and grandsons with the exception of Duryodhana will go forward, mounted on chariots and with ornaments on to receive the scion of the Dasharha race.

sn: स्वलंकृताश्च कल्याण्यः पादैरेव सहस्रशः। वारमुख्या महाभागं प्रत्युद्यास्यन्ति केशवम्॥
en: Blessed damsels, the foremost among dancing girls, by thousands with ornaments on will go out on foot to receive Keshava of large parts.

sn: नगरादपि याः काश्चिद् गमिष्यन्ति जनार्दनम्। द्रष्टुं कन्याश्च कल्याणयस्ताश्च यास्यन्त्यनावृताः॥
en: The beautiful girls, that will go out from this ten to see Janardana, will go with out their veils drawn.

sn: सस्त्रीपुरुषबालं च नगरं मधुसूदनम्। उदीक्षतां महात्मानं भानुमन्तमिव प्रजाः॥
en: Let my subjects in this town, including women, men and children, behold the largesouled slayer of Madhu like the rising sun.

sn: महाध्वजपताकाश्च क्रियन्तां सर्वतो दिशः। जलावसिक्तो विरजाः पन्थास्तस्येति चान्वशात्॥
en: Let the points of the earth be filled with large flags and banners and let the rods through which he will pass be drenched with water so as to remove the dust.

sn: दुःशासनस्य च गृहं दुर्योधनगृहाद् वरम्। तदद्य क्रियतां क्षिप्रं सुसम्पृष्टमलंकृतम्॥
en: The house of Dushasana is better than that of Duryodhana. Let that be now furnished and well cleansed quickly.

sn: एतद्धि रुचिराकारैः प्रासादैरुपशोभितम्। शिवं च रमणीयं च सर्वर्तुसुमहाधनम्॥
en: This one (the abode of Dushasana) is graced with many palaces beautiful to look at; and it is comfortable, enchanting and rich during every season of the year.

sn: सर्वमस्मिन् गृहे रत्नं मम दुर्योधनस्य च। यद् यदर्हति वार्ष्णेयस्तत् तद् देयमसंशयम्॥
en: All my wealth and that of Duryodhana are in this house. Whatever is fitting for the scion of the Vrishni race should be given to him without doubt TARAAVML+V40

sn: विदुर उवाच राजन् बहुतमश्चासि त्रैलोक्यस्यापि सत्तमः। सम्भावितश्च लोकस्य सम्मतश्चासि भारत॥
en: Vidura said O king, you are thought very well of in the there worlds, indeed as, the best of men. You are beloved by the world and respected as well, OBharata.

sn: यत् त्वमेवंगते ब्रूयाः पश्चिमे वयसि स्थितः। शास्त्राद् वा सुप्रतर्काद् वा सुस्थिरः स्थविरोह्यसि॥
en: Having reached the setting part of your life, whatever you say under these circumstances can never be against the holy books, nor against the dictates the dictates of reason; for your mind is clam, as you are aged.

sn: लेखा शशिनि भा: सूर्ये महोर्मिरिव सागरे। धर्मस्त्वयि तथा राजनिति व्यवसिताः प्रजाः॥
en: The subjects are confident that virtue resides in you, O king permanently even as marks on the stone or as rays in the sun and waves in the sea.

sn: सदैव भावितो लोको गुणौघेस्तव पार्थिव। गुणानां रक्षणे नित्यं प्रयतस्व सबान्धवः॥
en: O ruler of the earth one is ever beloved in this world owing to your large number of good qualities. Take pains always, therefore, with your friends in the preservation of your noble traits.

sn: आर्जवं प्रतिपद्यस्व मा बाल्याद् बहु नीनशः। राजन् पुत्रांश्च पौत्राश्च सुहृदश्चैव सुप्रियान्॥
en: Be simple-minded. Do not out of childishness destroy, o king, your sons and grandsons and good and dearly beloved friends.

sn: यत् त्वमिच्छसि कृष्णाय राजन्नतिथये बहु। एतदन्यश्च दाशार्हः पृथिवीमपि चार्हति॥
en: What you desire to present your guest Krishna with is much; but the scion of the Dasharha race deserves all this and much more or indeed the whole earth.

sn: न तु त्वं धर्ममुद्दिश्य तस्य वा प्रियकारणात्। एतद् दित्ससि कृष्णाय सत्येनात्मानमालभे॥
en: For the sake of virtue or for desire of pleasing him however you do not give all this to Krishna; and I speak truly that you do this for the gain of yourself.

sn: मायैषा सत्यमेवैतच्छौतद् भूरिदक्षिण। जानामि त्वन्मतं राजन् गूढं बाह्येन कर्मणा॥
en: It is true that this proceeds out of deception and insincerity and therefore it is cxceedingly improper. I know your secret intentions, O king from your outward acts.

sn: पञ्च पञ्चैव लिप्सन्ति ग्रामकान् पाण्डवा नृप। न च दित्ससि तेभ्यस्तांस्तच्छा न करिष्यसि॥
en: The five Pandavas, O king desire only five villages. If you do not give them those they will not conclude peace.

sn: अर्थेन तु महाबाहुं वार्ष्णेयं त्वं जिहीर्षसि। अनेन चाप्युपायेन पाण्डवेभ्यो विभेत्स्यसि॥
en: You desire to win the son of Vrishnis to your own side by wealth; and by this means you want to create gull between himself and the Pandavas.

sn: न च वित्तेन शक्योऽसौ नोद्यमेन न गर्हया। अन्यो धनंजयात् कर्तुमेतत् तत्त्वं ब्रवीमि ते॥
en: He cannot, however be separated from Dhananjaya by wealth or by exertions, nor by speaking all about the Pandavas. I tell this you in all sincerity.

sn: वेद कृष्णस्य माहात्म्यं वेदास्य दृढभक्तिताम्। अत्याज्ययस्य जानामि प्राणैस्तुल्यं धनंजयम्॥
en: I know the noble-mindedness of Krishna and I know his firm devotion and I know that Dhananjaya is inseparable from him even as life itself.

sn: अन्यत् कुम्भादपां पूर्णादन्यत् पादावसेचनात्। अन्यत् कुशलम्प्रश्नान्नैवेक्ष्यति जनार्दनः॥
en: On anything else besides a pot full water and water for washing his feet and interrogations on his health even cast his eyes.

sn: यत् त्वस्य प्रियमातिथ्यं मानार्हस्य महात्मनः। तदस्मै क्रियतां राजन् मानार्होऽसौ जनार्दनः॥
en: Show him however, that hospitality which is acceptable to that large-souled one deserving of honour. O king, that Janardana is the proper party for showing honour to.

sn: आशंसमानः कल्याणं कुरूनभ्येति केशवः। येनैव राजन्नर्थेन तदेवास्मा उपाकुरु॥
en: Keshava comes here expecting to do good to the Kurus. Do that, О king, by which that object may be gained.

sn: शममिच्छति दाशार्हस्तव दुर्योधनस्य च। पाण्डवानां च राजेन्द्र तदस्य वचनं कुरु॥
en: The scion of the Dasharha race desires peace for yourself and for Duryodhana and for the Pandavas as well, O chief among kings; do you therefore, what he says.

sn: पितासि राजन् पुत्रास्ते वृद्धस्त्वं शिशवः परे। वर्तस्व पितृवत् तेषु वर्तन्ते ते हि पुत्रवत्॥
en: O king you are father and they are your sons. you are aged and others are children. Act therefore as befits a father and let them act as your children.

sn: दुर्योधन उवाच यदाह विदुरः कृष्णे सर्वं तत् सत्यमच्युते। अनुरक्तो ह्यसंहार्यः पार्थान् प्रति जनार्दनः॥
en: Duryodhana said What Vidura has said regarding Krishna has been truly spoken; for Janardana is firmly attached to the son of Pritha and inseparable from them.

sn: यत् तत् सत्कारसंयुक्तं देयं वसु जनार्दने। अनेकरूपं राजेन्द्र न तद् देयं कदाचन॥
en: The diverse kinds of wealth therefore that is proposed to be bestowed on Janardana for his honour, O chief among kings, should on no account be given.

sn: देशः कालस्तथाऽयुक्तो न हि नार्हति केशवः। मंस्यत्यधोक्षजो राजन् भयादर्चति मामिति॥
en: Though Keshava is worthy of all that, yet place and time render it in-expedient; for he will come to think on receiving our worship, O king, that we are honoring him out of fear.

sn: अवमानश्च यत्र स्यात् क्षत्रियस्य विशाम्पते। न तत् कुर्याद् बुधः कार्यमिति मे निश्चिता मतिः॥
en: O Lord of the world, what would conduce to the disgrace of the Kshatriya race should not be done by a wise man. Such is my decided opinion.

sn: स हि पूज्यतमो लोके कृष्णः पृथुललोचनः। त्रयाणामपि लोकानां विदितं मम सर्वथा॥
en: Krishna of big eyes is most worthy of worship in this world by all the three worlds. This fact is always present in my mind.

sn: न तु तस्मै प्रदेयं स्यात् तथा कार्यगतिः प्रभो। विग्रहः समुपारब्धो न हि शाम्यत्यविग्रहात्॥
en: But circumstances are such, my lord, that nothing should be given him. War having been decided on will not turn into peace by delaying the former.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा भीष्मः कुरुपितामहः। वैचित्रवीर्यं राजानमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Bhishma, the grandfather of the Kurus, having heard these words of his said these words to the royal son of Vichitravirya.

sn: सत्कृतोऽसत्कृतो वापि न क्रुद्ध्येत जनार्दनः। नालमेनमवज्ञातुं नावज्ञेयो हि केशवः॥
en: Janardana will not get angry, whether he is properly received or not. He cannot be insulted; for Keshava is not capable of being SO.

sn: यत् तु कारयं महाबाहो मनसा कार्यतां गतम्। सर्वोपायैर्न तच्छक्यं केनचित् कर्तुमन्यथा॥
en: Whatever act, O you with long arms, is fructified in his mind's eye cannot be prevented by any man by every mean in his power.

sn: स यद् ब्रूयान्महाबाहुस्तत कार्यमविशङ्कया। वासुदेवेन तीर्थेन क्षिप्रं संशाम्य पाण्डवैः॥
en: What that being with long arms says, should be done without hesitation. Effect peace quickly with the Pandavas through the instrumentality of Vasudeva.

sn: धर्म्यमर्थ्यं च धर्मात्मा ध्रुवं वक्ता जनार्दनः। तस्मिन् वाच्याः प्रिया वाचो भवता बान्धवैः सह।॥
en: Janardana, inclined to virtue, will surely say what is conducive to morality as well as worldly profit; and he should be spoken to in agreeable words by yourself along with your friends.

sn: दुर्योधन उवाच न पर्यायोऽस्ति यद् राजश्रियं निष्केवलामहम्। तैः सहेमामुपाश्नीयां यावज्जीवं पितामह॥
en: Duryodhana said Since, O king, there is no likelihood of my being the sole enjoy of royalty and since, O grandsire, I cannot share it for life with them.

sn: इदं तु सुमहत् कार्यं शृणु मे यत् समर्थितम्। परायणं पाण्डवानां नियच्छामि जनार्दनम्॥
en: Listen to this great deed which I have fixed in my mind. I shall make Janardana-the refuge of the Pandavas, the captive.

sn: तस्मिन् बद्धे भविष्यन्ति वृष्णयः पृथिवी तथा। पाण्डवाश्च विधेया मे स च प्रातरिहैष्यति॥
en: On his imprisonment, the Vrishnis and the Pandavas, in fact the whole world, will be at my disposal. Krishna, too, will be here tomorrow morning.

sn: अत्रोपायान् यथा सम्यगन बुद्ध्येत जनार्दनः। न चापायो भवेत् कश्चित् तद् भवान् प्रब्रवीतु मे॥
en: Some means for executing this in such a way that Janardana may not at all anticipate it; and so that we way not fall into any danger, should be told me by you.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा घोरं कृष्णाभिसंहितम्। धृतराष्ट्रः सहामात्यो व्यथितो विमनाऽभवत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Hearing these words of terrible import, namely of making of making Krishna a captive, Dhritarashtra with his ministers became oppressed with pain.

sn: ततो दुर्योधनमिदं धृतराष्ट्रोऽब्रवीद् वचः। मैवं वोचः प्रजापाल नैष धर्मः सनातनः॥
en: Dhritarashtra then said these words to Duryodhana, do not say so, O you protector of men. This is against eternal virtue.

sn: दूतश्च हि हृषीकेशः सम्बन्धी च प्रियश्च नः। अपापः कौरवेयेषु स कथं बन्धमर्हति॥
en: Hrishikesha is an ambassador; and in relation he is dear to ourselves. He has done no wrong to the Kurus. How then is it proper that he should be made a captive?

sn: भीष्म उवाच परीतस्तव पुत्रोऽयं धृतराष्ट्र सुमन्दधीः।। वृणोत्यनर्थं नैवार्थं याच्यमानः सुहृज्जनैः॥
en: Bhishma said This wicked son of yours, O Dhritarashtra, is on the verge of eternity. He selects the evil and not what is good, though begged by persons who wish well to him.

sn: इममुत्पथि वर्तन्तं पापं पापानुबन्धिनम्। वाक्यानि सुहृदां हित्वा त्वमप्यस्यानुवर्तसे॥
en: Instead of listening to the advice of your well-wishers, you too follow him, who is established on this unrighteous path and whose surroundings are sinful.

sn: कृष्णमक्लिष्टकर्माणमासाद्यायं सुदुर्मतिः। तव पुत्रः सहामात्यः क्षणेन न भविष्यति॥
en: This son of Dhritarashtra of exceedingly wicked purposes, along with his advisers, will cease to exist in a moment when he comes against Krishna, who can do a work without the least trouble.

sn: पापस्यास्य नृशंसस्य त्यक्तधर्मस्य दुर्मतेः। नोत्सहेऽनर्थसंयुक्ताः श्रोतुं वाचः कथंचन॥
en: I dare not listen to any words of this man of wicked purpose, who has abandoned virtue and who is cruel and sinful.

sn: इत्युक्त्वा भरतश्रेष्ठो वृद्धः परममन्युमान्। उत्थाय तस्मात् प्रातिष्ठद् भीष्मः सत्यपराक्रमः॥
en: Having said this, the foremost of aged men among the Bharata Bhishma of true prowess got up and went away from that place, fired with great rage.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच प्रातरुत्थाय कृष्णस्तु कृतवान् सर्वमाह्निकम्। ब्राह्मणैरभ्यनुज्ञात: प्रययौ नगरं प्रति॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having got up (from the bed) in the morning, Krishna attended to the daily rites; and with the permission of the Brahmanas went towards the city.

sn: तं प्रयान्तं महाबाहुमनुज्ञाप्य महाबलम्। पर्यवर्तन्त ते सर्वे वृकस्थलनिवासिनः॥
en: All those residents of Vrikasthala returned after duly informing the greatly powerful one, who was departing (for the city).

sn: धार्तराष्ट्रास्तमायान्तं प्रत्युज्जग्मुः स्वलंकृताः। दुर्योधनादृते सर्वे भीष्मद्रोणकृपादयः॥
en: The of Dhritarashtra with the exception of Duryodhana, Bhishma, Drona, Kripa and others, beautifully attired went forth to (receive) him who was coming towards them.

sn: पौराश्च बहुला राजन् हृषीकेशं दिदृक्षवः। यानैर्बहुविधैरन्यैः पन्दिरेव तथा परे॥
en: Crowds of the townsmen, o king, desirous of having a look of Hrishikesha, were there in diverse sorts of conveyances, while there were others on foot. son

sn: स वै पथि समागम्य भीष्मेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा। द्रोणेन धार्तराष्ट्रश्च तैर्वृतो नगरं ययौ॥
en: He (Krishna) too having met with Bhishma who does acts without any efforts and Drona and the sons of Dhritarashtra on the way, went to the town surrounded by them.

sn: कृष्णसम्माननार्थं च नगरं समलंकृतम्। बभूव राजमार्गश्च बहुरत्नसमाचितः॥
en: For paying honour to Krishna the city was well ornamented and the public roads were decked with diverse sorts of gems and precious stones.

sn: न च कश्चिद् गृहे राजंस्तदाऽऽसीद् भरतर्षभ। न स्त्री न वृद्धो न शिशुर्वासुदेवदिदृक्षया।॥
en: There was none who stayed within the house, O king, on that occasion. O bull among the race of Bharata-no woman, no aged, no child was indoors out of a desire to have a gaze of Vasudeva.

sn: राजमार्गो नरास्तस्मिन् संस्तुवन्त्यवनिं गताः। तस्मिन् काले महाराज हृषीकेशप्रवेशने॥
en: On the public road the people with their heads bowing down on the earth were praising him in verses at that time, O great king, when Hrishikesha entered the city.

sn: आवृतानि वरस्त्रीभिर्गृहाणि सुमहान्त्यपि। प्रचलन्तीव भारेण दृश्यन्ते स्म महीतले॥
en: The spacious mansions, filled with the ladies of rank, seemed to tremble under their weight to fall over upon the ground.

sn: तथा च गतिमन्तस्ते वासुदेवस्य वाजिनः। राजमार्गे नरैर्वृते॥
en: The steeds of Vasudeva, though swift in speed lost their motion, in the public road covered over by human beings.

sn: स गृहं धृतराष्ट्रस्य प्राविशच्छत्रुकर्शनः। पाण्डुरं पुण्डरीकाक्षः प्रासादैरुपशोभितम्॥
en: That lotus-eyed grinder of foes entered the gray-coloured abode of Dhritarashtra graced with many palaces.

sn: तिस्रः कक्ष्या व्यतिक्रम्य केशवो राजवेश्मनः। वैचित्रवीर्यं राजानमभ्यगच्छदरिंदमः॥ प्रनष्टगतयोऽभूवन्
en: come to After traversing through the apartments of the royal abode, Keshava, the subduer of foes, came to the royal son of Vichitravirya.

sn: अभ्यागच्छति दाशार्हे प्रज्ञाचक्षुर्नराधिपः। सहैव द्रोणभीष्माभ्यामुदतिष्ठन्महायशाः॥
en: On the scion of the Dasharha race approaching towards him, the high-famed ruler of men, who had eyes of wisdom, along with Drona and Bhishma stood up;

sn: कृपश्च सोमदत्तश्च महाराजश्च बाह्निकः। आसनेभ्योऽचलन् सर्वे पूजयन्तो जनार्दनम्॥
en: So also Kripa, Somadatta and the great king Balhika stood up from their respective seats for worshipping Janardana.

sn: ततो राजानमासाद्य धृतराष्ट्रं यशस्विनम्। स भीष्मं पूजयामास वार्ष्णेयो वाग्भिरञ्जसा॥
en: Then having the king Dhritarashtra of renown, the scion of the Vrishni race honoured him along with Bhishma with suitable words and without delay.

sn: तेषु धर्मानुपूर्वी तां प्रयुज्य मधुसूदनः। यथावयः समीयाय राजभिः सह माधवः॥
en: Madhava, the slayer of Madhu, having done honour to them according to the usual custom, exchanged words with other kings according to their age.

sn: अथ द्रोणं सबाह्रीकं सपुत्रं च यशस्विनम्। कृपं च सोमदत्तं च समीयाय जनार्दनः॥
en: Janardana then addressed Balhika and the famous Drona with his son and Kripa and Somadatta.

sn: तत्रासीदूर्जितं मृष्टं काञ्चनं महदासनम्। शासनाद् धृतराष्ट्रस्य तत्रोपाविशदच्युतः॥
en: There in that place was a large wheat made of gold, of beautiful workmanship and ornamented with jewels, on which Achyuta took his seat at the request of Dhritarashtra.

sn: अथ गां मधुपर्कं चाप्युदकं च जनार्दने। उपजह्वर्यथान्यायं धृतराष्ट्रपुरोहिताः॥
en: They, headed by Dhritarashtra, duly offered to Janardana, as was the custom, a cow, honey, curds and water.

sn: कृतातिथ्यस्तु गोविन्दः सर्वान् परिहसन् कुरुन्। आस्ते साम्बन्धिकं कुर्वन् कुरुभिः परिवारितः॥
en: The rites of hospitality being finished, Govinda stayed there (for a short time) surrounded by the Kurus, jesting with them and exchanging words of courtesy according to his relationship.

sn: सोऽचितो धृतराष्ट्रेण पूजितश्च महायशाः। राजानं समनुज्ञाप्य निर्कामदरिंदमः॥
en: He, the subduer of his enemies, being worshipped and honoured by Dhritarashtra of great fame, issued out with the permission of the king.

sn: तैः समेत्य यथान्यायं कुरुभिः कुरुसंसदि। विदुरावसथं रम्यमुपातिष्ठत माधरः॥
en: Madhava, having exchanged greetings with the Kurus suitably in their assembly, went to the enchanting abode of Vidura.

sn: विदुरः सर्वकल्याणैरभिगम्य जनार्दनम्। अर्चयामास दाशार्ह सर्वकामैरुपस्थितम्॥
en: Vidura approached and worshipped Janardana of the Dasharha race and presented him every auspicious and desirable offering.

sn: या मे प्रीतिः पुष्कराक्ष त्वदर्शनसमुद्भवा। सा किमाख्यायते तुभ्यमन्तरात्मासि देहिनाम्॥
en: He said-'The joy I feel at the sight of yourself, who have come here, O you with lotus eyes, what is the use of describing? For, you are the inner soul of all corporeal beings.'

sn: कृतातिथ्यं तु गोविन्दं विदुरः सर्वधर्मवित्। कुशलं पाण्डुपुत्राणामपृच्छन्मधुसूदनम्॥
en: Vidura, conversant with all the virtues, having finished the rites of hospitality to Govinda, asked the slayer of Madhu about the welfare of the sons of Pandu.

sn: प्रीयमाणस्य सुहृदो विदुरो बुद्धिसत्तमः। धर्मार्थनित्यस्य सतो गतरोषस्य धीमतः॥ तस्य सर्वं सविस्तारं पाण्डवानां विचेष्टितम्। क्षत्तुराचष्ट दाशार्हः सर्वं प्रत्यक्षदर्शिवान्॥
en: That scion of the Dasharha race who sees everything as plainly as what he sees before his eyes, told everything in detail about the doings of the Pandavas to Khattva. Vidura was the best among the honest and learned men and he also was the dear friend and well-wisher (of the Pandavas), he was wise, honest and a man of principle, virtuous and learned in worldly profit and he felt no malice (for the Pandavas), Anrn

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच अथोपगम्य विदुरमपराह्ने जनार्दनः। पितृष्वसारं स पृथामभ्यगच्छदरिंदमः॥
en: Vaishampayana said After his visit to Vidura, Janardana, the subduer of enemies, went in the afternoon to Pritha, his mother's sister.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: सा दृष्ट्वा कृष्णमायान्तं प्रसन्नादित्यवर्चसम्। कण्ठे गृहीत्वा प्राक्रोशत् स्मरन्ती तनयान् पृथा॥
en: Seeing Krishna approaching and effulgent like the radiant sun, Pritha clasped his neck with her arms and poured forth her loud lamentations, remembering her sons.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: तेषां सत्त्ववतां मध्ये गोविन्दं सहचारिणम्। चिरस्य दृष्ट्वा वार्ष्णेयं बाष्पमाहारयत् पृथा॥
en: Seeing Govinda after a long time, the action of the Vrishni race, companion of her sons, endued with prowess, Pritha shed tears.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: साब्रवीत् कृष्णमासीनं कृतातिथ्यं युधां पतिम्। बाष्पगद्गदपूर्णेन मुखेन परिशुष्यता॥
en: She said to Krishna, the best of warriors who had seated himself after receiving the rites of hospitality, with her face dried up with woe and in a voice choked up with tears.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: ये ते बाल्यात् प्रभृत्येव गुरुशुश्रूषणे रताः। परस्परस्य सुहृदः सम्मताः समचेतसः। निकृत्या भ्रंशिता राज्याज्जनार्हा निर्जनं गताः॥
en: 'Those, who ever since their childhood are attached to the service of their elders, those who are endued with humility and those who are of similar hearts, were deprived of their kingdom by deceit and sent into exile, through they were desirous of remaining in the society of men.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: विनीतक्रोधहर्षाश्च ब्रह्मण्याः सत्यवादिनः। त्यक्त्वा प्रियसुखे पार्था रुदतीमपहाय माम्॥
en: They, who have brought under control wrath and joy, who are devoted to the Brahmanas, who are speakers of truth, those sons of mine abandoning their dear enjoyments and leaving behind them myself weeping for them.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: अहापुंश्च वनं यान्तः समूलं हृदयं मम। अतदर्हा महात्मानः कथं केशवं पाण्डवाः॥
en: Have gone to the forest, rendering the very bottom of my heart. These large-souled sons of Pandu undeserving of these miserieshow did they, O Keshava.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: ऊषुर्महावने तात सिंहव्याघ्रगजाकुले। बाला विहीनाः पित्रा ते मया सततलालिताः॥
en: Live in that great forest, O child, abandoning, as it was, in lions, tigers and elephants. Losing their father in their boyhood, they were even reared and brought up by myself.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: अपश्यन्तश्च पितरौ कथमूषुर्महावने। शङ्खदुन्दुभिनिर्घोषैर्मृदङ्गैर्वेणुनिःस्वनैः॥
en: Without seeing their parents, how did they live in the great forest? By the sounds of conches and drums and the music of flutes.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: पाण्डवाः समबोध्यन्त बाल्यात् प्रभृति केशव। ये स्म वारणशब्देन हयानां हेषितेन च॥ रथनेमिनिनादैश्च व्यबोध्यन्त तदा गृहे। शङ्खभेरीनिनादेन वेणुवीणानुनादिना॥ पुण्याहघोषमिश्रेण पूज्यमाना द्विजातिभिः। वस्त्रै रत्नैरलंकारैः पूजयन्तो द्विजन्मनः॥ गीर्भिर्मङ्गलयुक्ताभिर्ब्राह्मणानां महात्मनाम्। अर्चितैरर्चनाहश्च स्तुवद्भिरभिनन्दिताः॥ प्रासादाचेष्वबोध्यन्त राङ्कवाजिनशायिनः। क्रूरं च निनदं श्रुत्वा श्वापदानां महावने॥
en: Were the Pandavas awakened from their sleep ever since their infancy, O Keshava; who again, were by the roar of elephants and neighing of horses and by the rattles of the wheels of the chariots awakened from sleep at home-also by the sound of conches and cymbals accompanied with the music of flutes and lyres; and whose praises were sung by the twice-born at the break of day in high sounding songs; and who worshipped the deserving Brahmanas with the raiment's, gems and jewels; who, worthy of respect, themselves were blessed and done homage to by the largesouled Brahmanas by laudatory hymns and worshipped as well. How could they, lying on soft blankets and skin of the Ranku deer in the best parts of the palace, be awakened by hearing the loud roar of animals in the great forest?

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: न स्मोपयान्ति निद्रां ते न तदर्हा जनार्दन। भेरीमृदङ्गनिनदैः शङ्खवैणवनिस्वनैः॥ स्त्रीणां गीतनिनादैश्च मधुरैर्मधुसूदन्। वन्दिमागधसूतैश्च स्तुवद्भिबौधिताः कथम्॥
en: It does not seem possible to me that they obtained sleep, though they did not at all deserve this, O Janardana, those who by the sound of cymbals and drums and the conches and flutes and by the sweet music of songs by woman, O slayer of Madhu, were awakened and praised by the prisoners and professional bards-how could they.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: महावनेष्वबोध्यन्त श्वापदानां रुतेन च। ह्रीमान् सत्यधृतिर्दान्तो भूतानामनुकम्पिता॥ कामद्वेषो वशे कृत्वा सतां वानुवर्तते। अम्बरीषस्य मान्धातुर्ययातेर्नहुषस्य च॥ भरतस्य दिलीपस्य शिबेरौशीनरस्य च। राजर्षीणां पुराणानां धुरं धत्ते दुरुद्वहाम्॥ शीलवृत्तोपसम्पन्नो धर्मज्ञः सत्यसंगरः। राजा सर्वगुणोपेतस्त्रैलोक्यस्यापि यो भवेत्॥ अजातशत्रुर्धर्मात्मा शुद्धजाम्बूनदप्रभः। श्रेष्ठः कुरुषु सर्वेषु धर्मतः श्रुतवृत्ततः। प्रियदशों दीर्घभुजः कथं कृष्ण युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: In the great forest be awakened at the roar of animals? The one endowed with modesty, truth, patience, self-control and kindness to animals and who bringing his desire and malice under control walks on the path followed by the good, he was capable of bearing the heavy burden of the ancient sages of royal descentnamely Amvarisha, Mandhatta, Yayati, Nahusha, Bharata, Dilipa, Shibi, the son of Ushanara; he who followed good habits of life and conversant with virtue, of true prowess, he who endued with all the virtuous uses, the king of all the three worlds, viz., the virtuous-souled Ajatashatru of a pious complexion and having a complexion like that of gold, chief among the Kurus and among all in respect of virtue and those who shape their habits of life to the ways indicated in the holy book, who is of handsome appcarance and of long arms, how is that Yudhishthira, O Krishna?

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: यः स नागायुतप्राणो वातरंहा महाबलः। सामर्षः पाण्डवो नित्यं प्रियो भ्रातुः प्रियंकरः॥ कीचकस्य तु सज्ञातेर्यो हन्ता मधुसूदन। शूरः क्रोधवशानां च हिडिम्बस्य बकस्य च॥ पराक्रमे शक्रसमो मातरिश्वसमो बले। महेश्वरसमः क्रोधे भीमः प्रहरतां वरः॥ क्रोधं बलममर्षं च यो निधाय परंतपः। जितात्मा पाण्डवोऽमर्षी भ्रातुस्तिष्ठति शासने॥ तेजोराशिं महात्मानं वरिष्ठममितौजसम्। भीमं प्रदर्शनेनापि भीमसेन जनार्दनम्॥
en: He who is of as great strength as ten thousand elephants and of speed equal to the wind, that is, one of great prowess and ever wrathful among the sons of Pandu, who ever does good to his dear brothers; who sicw Kichaka with his cousins, 0 slayer of Madhu and Krodhavasha and of Hidimba and of Vaka; who is in strength equal to Shakra and in prowess equal to the god of wind, who is in wrath equal to the great Shiva, namely Bhima, foremost among smiters, that chastiser of foes, that wrathful son of Pandu, who controlling his rage and strength and wrath, stays with his soul under restraint, under the rule of his brother, that great-souled one, that man of energy, that foremost among men, that one of immeasurable prowess, that Bhima in appearance, too, is terrible looking (i.e. justifies his name), O Janardana.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: तं ममाचक्ष्व वार्ष्णेय कथमद्य वृकोदरः। आस्ते परिघबाहुः स मध्यमः पाण्डवो बली॥
en: Tell me, O scion of the Vrishni race, how Vrikodara is doing now, the one having macelike arms, that mighty second son of Pandu.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: अर्जुनेनार्जुनो यः स कृष्ण बाहुसहस्रिणा। द्विबाहुः स्पर्धते नित्यमतीतेनापि केशव॥ क्षिपत्येकेन वेगेन पञ्च बाणशतानि यः। इष्वस्त्रे सदृशो राज्ञः कार्तवीर्यस्य पाण्डवः॥ तेजसाऽऽदित्यसदृशो महर्षिसदृशो दमे। क्षमया पृथिवीतुल्यो महेन्द्रसमविक्रमः॥ आधिराज्यं महद् दीप्तं प्रथितं मधुसूदन। आहृतं येन वीर्येण कुरूणां सर्वराजसु॥ यस्य बाहुबलं सर्वे पाण्डवाः पर्युपासते। स सर्वरथिनां श्रेष्ठः पाण्डवः सत्यविक्रमः॥ यं गत्वाऽभिमुखः संख्ये न जीवन् कश्चिदाव्रजेत्। यो जेता सर्वभूतानामजेयो जिष्णुरच्युत।॥ योऽपाश्रयः पाण्डवानां देवानामिव वासवः। स ते भ्राता सखा चैव कथमद्य धनंजयः॥
en: That two armed Arjuna, O Krishna, who is ever proud of being superior to that Arjuna of ancient days, who had a thousand arms, who with one of his arms darts with violence five hundred arrows, that son of Pandu, who in the use of arrows is equal to the royal son of Kartavirya, equal in energy to Aditya, in selfcontrol equal to a great Rishi, in forbearance equal to the Earth and in prowess equal to the great Indra, that strength by which all kings, the descendants of Kuru, have acquired this large territory of great effulgence; whose strength of arms all the sons of Pandu respect, that son of Pandu, foremost among all the carwarriors, of true prowess; going to whose front no one returns with his life, he, O Achyuta, who is accustomed to victories over all creatures and himself being invincible; who is the refuge of the Pandu's and even of the godsbe your brother and your friend, how is he at present, that Dhananjaya?

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: दयावान् सर्वभूतेषु ह्रीनिषेवो महास्त्रवित्। मृदुश्च सुकुमारश्च धार्मिकश्च प्रियश्च मे॥ सहदेवो महेष्वासः शूरः समिति शोभनः। भ्रातृणां कृष्ण शुश्रूषुधर्मार्थकुशलो युवा॥
en: The one who is kind to all creatures endued with modesty and having a large knowledge of the nature and use of weapons, mild, delicate, virtuous and beloved by me; that great bow-man and hero Sahadeva, that ornament of assemblies, that youth, O Krishna, who is skillful at both religious deeds and profitable from an earthly point of view and properly waiting on his brothers.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: सदैव सहदेवस्य भ्रातरो मधुसूदन। वृत्तं कल्याणवृत्तस्य पूजयन्ति महात्मनः॥ ज्येष्ठोपचायिन वीरं सहदेवं युधां पतिम्। शुश्रूषु मम वार्ष्णेय माद्रीपुत्रं प्रचक्ष्व मे॥
en: Those large-souled brothers of Sahadeva, O Krishna, ever respect the habits of life of Sahadeva, who follows a good course of life-Tell me, O scion of the Vrishni race, of that son of Madri, of that heroic and veteran warrior, Sahadeva, the chief of warriors, who used to wait on me.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: सुकुमारो युवा शूरो दर्शनीयश्च पाण्डवः भ्रातृणां चैव सर्वेषां प्रियः प्राणो बहिश्चरः॥
en: That heroic and delicate youth, that son of Pandu, well worth a gaze, is the life itself to all his brothers, though he has a different body.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: चित्रयोधी च नकुलो महेष्वासो महाबलः। कच्चित् सकुशली कृष्ण वत्सो मम सुखैधितः॥
en: My son, that great bow-man, Nakula of great prowess, that veteran warrior, brought up in luxury, is he well, O Krishna?

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: सुखोचितमदुःखार्ह सुकुमारं महारथम्। अपि जातु महाबाहो पश्येयं नकुलं पुनः॥
en: Shall I behold again this Nakula, O you with long arms, that great car-warrior, brought up in luxury, deserving of every happiness and undeserving of all woe.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: पक्ष्मसम्पातजे काले नकुलेन विनाकृता। न लभामि धृति वीर साद्य जीवामि पश्यमाम्॥
en: Separated from Nakula even for the shortest period of time, taken up by a wink, I obtained no peace of mind, O hero, behold me that I am still alive.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: सर्वैः पुत्रैः प्रियतरा द्रौपदी मे जनार्दन। कुलीना रूपसप्पन्ना सर्वैः समुदिता गुणैः॥
en: O Janardana, Draupadi is dearer to me than all my sons. She comes of a noble family, endued with beauty and endowed with all virtues.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: पुत्रलोकात् पतिलोकं वृण्वानां सत्यवादिनी। प्रियान् पुत्रान् परित्यज्य पाण्डवाननुरुध्यते॥
en: That speaker of truth preferred the company of her husbands to that of her sons and leaving behind her dear sons, she follows the sons of Pandu.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: महाजिनसम्पन्ना सर्वकामैः सुपूजिता। ईश्वरी सर्वकल्याणी द्रौपदी कथमच्युत॥
en: O Achyuta, how is the all blessed queen Draupadi of illustrious birth well gratified with the fulfillment of all her desires?

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: पतिभिः पञ्चभिः शूरैरग्निकल्पैः प्रहारिभिः। उपपन्ना महेष्वासैद्रौपदी दुःखभागिनी॥
en: Draupadi has a bad lot, though she has five husbands, all heroes like the fire, all smiters of foes and all great bowmen.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: चतुर्दशमिदं वर्ष यन्नापश्यमरिंदम। पुत्रादिभिः परियूनां द्रौपदी सत्यवादिनीम्॥
en: O chastiser of foes, the one whom I have not seen for these fourteen years, that Draupadi, truthful of speech, is anxious for her children.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: न नूनं कर्मभिः पुण्यैरश्नुते पुरुषः सुखम्। द्रौपदी चेत् तथावृत्ता नाश्नुते सुखमव्ययम्॥
en: It seems that a man does not surely get happiness as the result of his virtuous acts; for Draupadi, though of virtuous habits of life, does not get unending happiness.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: न प्रियो मम कृष्णाया बीभत्सुर्न युधिष्ठिरः। भीमसेनो यमौ वापि यदपश्यं सभागताम्॥
en: When I remember Krishna dragged to the Assembly-Hall, Vibhatsu, Yudhishthira, Bhimasena and also the twin brothers, Nakula and Sahadeva cease to be dear to me.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: न मे दुःखतरं किंचिद् भूतपूर्वं ततोऽधिकम्। स्त्रीधर्मिणी द्रौपदी यच्छ्वशुराणां समीपगाम्॥
en: Nothing ever before gave me greater pain than the dragging of Draupadi in her season to her father-in-law. was

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: आनायितामनार्येण क्रोधलोभानुवर्तिना। सर्वे प्रेक्षन्त कुरव एकवस्त्रा सभागताम्॥
en: She dragged there by that dishonourable wretch, from motives of wrath and covetousness, and all the Kurus gazed on her brought to the Assembly-Hall in a single raiment.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: तत्रैव धृतराष्ट्रश्च महाराजश्च बाह्निकः। कृपश्च सोमदत्तश्च निर्विण्णाः कुरवस्तथा॥
en: There were at the time Dhritarashtra, the great king Balhika, Kripa, Somadatta and the Kurus who were pained at it.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: तस्यां संसदि सर्वेषां क्षत्तारं पूजयाम्यहम्। वृत्तेन हि भवत्यार्यो न धनेन न विद्यया॥
en: Of all the people present in that assembly I honour that Kshatta (Vidura) most; for a man becomes honourable by his habits and not by his wealth, nor by his knowledge.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: तस्य कृष्ण महाबुद्धेर्गम्भीरस्य महात्मनः। क्षत्तुः शीलमलंकारो लोकान् विष्टभ्य तिष्ठति॥
en: O Krishna, the virtues of that high-souled Kshatta of great and deep wisdom are like an ornament of the whole world.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच सा शोकार्ता च हृष्टा च दृष्ट्वा गोविन्दमागतम्। नानाविधानि दुःखानि सर्वाण्येवान्वकीर्तयत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said That lady oppressed with sorrow and yet cheerful seeing Govinda come, began to describe all the diverse grief's she had suffered.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: पूर्वैराचरितं यत् तत् कुराजभिररिंदमा अक्षयूतं मृगवधः कच्चिदेषां सुखावहम्॥
en: O chastiser of foes, could game at dice and the slaying of deer practised by these bad kings in the days of old be pleasant to them?

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: तन्मां दहति यत् कृष्णा सभायां कुरुसंनिधौ। धाष्ट्रैिः परिक्लिष्टा यथा न कुशलं तथा॥
en: The degree, to which this fact pains me, namely the dragging of Krishna to the Assembly-Hall in the presence of the Kurus and insulted by the sons of Dhritarashtra, is not equalled by death itself.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: निर्वासनं च नगरात् प्रव्रज्या च परंतप। नानाविधानां दुःखानामभिज्ञास्मि जनार्दन॥
en: O chastiser of foes, the exile (of my sons) out of city and their wanderings and several other grief's have l experienced, O Janardana.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: अज्ञातचर्या बालानामवरोधश्च माधवा न मे क्लेशतमं तत् स्यात् पुत्रैः सह परंतप॥
en: O Madhava, O chastiser of foes, living in concealment and the deprivation of my boys, could not be so painful to me in the company of my sons?

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: दुर्योधनेन निकृता वर्षमद्य चतुर्दशम्। दुःखादपि सुखं नः स्याद् यदि पुण्यफलक्षयः॥
en: It is fourteen years now since they were exiled by Duryodhana; and happiness should be ours, if misery puts an end to the fruits of vice.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: न मे विषेषो जात्वासीत् धार्तराष्ट्रेषु पाण्डवैः तेन सत्येन कृष्ण त्वां हतामित्रं श्रिया वृतम्। अस्माद् विमुक्तं संग्रामात् पश्येयं पाण्डवैः सह॥६शा
en: I never treated the sons of Dhritarashtra in a different way from that in which I treated the sons of Pandu; and by virtue of this truth shall I see, O Krishna, yourself along with the Pandavas after you have slain your enemies invested with prosperity, come out safe from this impending war.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: नैव शक्याः पराजेतुं सर्वं ह्येषां तथाविधम्। पितरं त्वेव गर्हेयं नात्मानं न सुयोधनम्॥
en: All of them having such like qualities are incapable of being defeated by the enemies. But my father is to blame ((for all this grief) and not myself, nor Suyodhana.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: येनाहं कुन्तिभोजाय धनं वृत्तैरिवार्पिता। बालां मामार्यकस्तुभ्यं क्रीडन्ती कन्दुहस्तिकाम्॥
en: By him I was given away to Kuntibhoja like wealth given away by a rich man. While yet a girl playing with a ball in my hand, your grand-father.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: अदात् तु कुन्तिभोजाय सखा सख्ये महात्मने। साऽहं पित्रा च निकृता श्वशुरैश्च परंतप। अत्यन्तदुःखिता कृष्ण किं जीवितफलं मम॥
en: Gave me away to his friend, the largesouled Kuntibhoja; such a one was myself and abandoned by my father and my father-in-law. O chastiser of foes, meeting with great troubles, O Krishna, what is the use of my life?

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: यन्मां वागनवीनक्तं सूतके सव्यसाचिनः। पुत्रस्ते पृथिवीं जेता यशश्चास्य दिवं स्पृशेत्॥
en: At the birth of Savyasachi, a voice told me in the room in which I was confined-'Your son will be the conquer of the world and his fame will reach the very heaven.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: हत्वा कुरून् महाजन्ये राज्यं प्राप्य धनंजयः। भ्रातृभिः सह कौन्तेयस्त्रीन् मेधानाहरिष्यति॥
en: Slaughtering the Kurus in a great battle and obtaining the kingdom, Dhananjaya, the son of Kunti, along with his brothers, will perform three grand sacrificial rites.'

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: नाहं तामभ्यसूयामि नमो धर्माय वेधसे। कृष्णाय महते नित्यं धर्मो धारयति प्रजाः॥
en: I do not doubt the eventual justification of that foreboding. I bow to Dharma and to the creator and to Krishna who is ever great. Creatures are supported by Dharma (Virtue).

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: धर्मश्चेदस्ति वार्ष्णेय यथा वागभ्यभाषता त्वं चापि तत् तथा कृष्ण सर्वं सम्पादयिष्यसि॥
en: If Dharma (Virtue) exists in this world, O scion of the Vrishni race, thus you too will be what the voice announced, O Krishna; and you will accomplish all that.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: न मां माधव वैधव्यं नार्थनाशो न वैरता। तथा शोकाय दहति यथा पुत्रैर्विनाभवः॥
en: O Madhava, neither widowhood, nor the loss of wealth, nor even this dispute has pained me so much as my separation from my sons.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: याऽहं गाण्डीवधन्वानं सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वरम्। धनंजयं न पश्यामि का शान्तिर्हदयस्य मे॥
en: I, who do not see the wielder of the Gandiva bow, that foremost of all that wield weapons, Dhananjaya-what peace can I (my heart) know, not having seen Yudhishthira for these fourteen years?

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: इतश्चतुर्दशं वर्ष यन्नापश्यं युधिष्ठिरम्। धनंजयं च गोविन्द यमौ तं च वृकोदरम्॥
en: Nor have I seen Dhananjaya, O Govinda, the twins, Nakula and Sahadeva and also that Vrikodara; people perform the Shradha (obsequies) of absent people under the impression that they are dead.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: जीवनाशं प्रनष्टानां श्राद्धं कुर्वन्ति मानवाः। अर्थतस्ते मम मृतास्तेषां चाहं जनार्दन॥
en: Virtually they are dead to me and I am the same to them, O Janardana, O Madhava, say this to the virtuous-souled king Yudhishthira.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: ब्रूया माधव राजानं धर्मात्मानं युधिष्ठिरम्। भूयास्ते हीयते धर्मो मा पुत्रक वृथा कृथाः॥
en: Your virtue is becoming less and less o son; act in such a way that this may not be; fie to them, O Vasudeva, that live under the protection of others.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: पराश्रया वासुदेव या जीवति धिगस्तु ताम्। वृत्तेः कार्पण्यलध्याया अप्रतिष्ठेव ज्यायसी॥
en: To a mode of life attended with meanness death even is superior. Say also to Dhananjaya and Vrikodara who are constantly on the alert.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: अथो धनंजयं ब्रूया नित्योद्युक्तं वृकोदरम्। यदर्थं क्षत्रिया सूते तस्य कालोऽयमागतः॥
en: This is the time come for the purpose, for which a Kshatriya woman brings forth a son, if you let the occasion, which is now come, slip without doing anything;

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: अस्मिश्चेदागते काले मिथ्या चातिक्रमिष्यति। लोकसम्भाविता: सन्तः सुनृशंसं करिष्यथ॥
en: You will be doing what is cruel and mean, though you are respected by the world; and if you are ever contemptible, I shall abandon and disown you forever.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: नृशंसेन च वो युक्तांस्त्यजेयं शाश्वतीः समाः। काले हि समनुप्राप्ते त्यक्तव्यमपि जीवनम्॥
en: When the suitable moment arrives, life even should be laid down. The two sons of Madri who are ever attached to virtuous deeds should be spoken to.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: पाद्रीपुत्रौ च वक्तव्यौ क्षत्रधर्मरतौ सदा। विक्रमेणार्जितान् भोगान् वृणीतं जीवितादपि॥
en: Chose these comforts and luxuries, which are attainable by a display of your prowess, rather than even life itself, since objects attained by prowess alone are ever pleasing to those who live the life of Kshatriyas.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: विक्रमाधिगता हार्थाः क्षत्रधर्मेण जीवतः। मनो मनुष्यस्य सदा प्रीणन्ति पुरुषोत्तमः॥
en: And ever gladden the hearts of men, O you best among men. Having gone there speak to him who is the foremost among all wielders of weapons,

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: गत्वा ब्रूहि महाबाहो सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वरम्। अर्जुनं पाण्डवं वीरं द्रौपद्याः पदवीं चर॥
en: Namely the hero Arjuna, the son of Pandu. Follow the path pointed out by Draupadi. It is known to you that when they (Bhima and Arjuna) are enraged they are as Death himself.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: विदितौ हि तवात्यन्तं क्रुद्धौ तौ तु यथान्तकौ। भीमार्जुनौ नयेतां हि देवानपि परां गतिम्॥
en: And (when such is the case) Bhima and Arjuna can bring the very gods to the end of their life. This insult, namely that Krishna was dragged to the Assembly-Hall was offered to them;

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: तयोश्चैतदवज्ञानं यत् सा कृष्णा सभां गता। दुःशासनश्च कर्णश्च परुषाण्यभ्यभाषताम्॥
en: And Dushasana and Karna spoke harsh and insulting words. Duryodhana has insulted the spirited Bhimasena.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: दुर्योधनो भीमसेनमभ्यगच्छन्मनस्विनम्। पश्यतां कुरुमुख्यानां तस्य द्रक्ष्यति यत् फलम्॥
en: In the presence of the chiefs among the Kurus he will see what the consequences of that will be. Vrikodara having once been made an enemy cannot make peace.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: न हि वैरं समासाद्य प्रशाम्यति वृकोदरः। सुचिरादपि भीमस्य न हि वैरं प्रशाम्यति। यावदन्तं न नयति शात्रवाञ्छत्रुकर्शनः॥
en: The feelings of revenge in Bhima too will not calm down in a short time until that grinder of enemies does make an end of them.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: न दुःखं राज्यहरणं न च द्यूते पराजयः। प्रव्राजनं तु पुत्राणां न मे तद् दुःखकारणम्॥
en: The loss of kingdom is not a source of trouble, not even the defeat at the game of dice; nor even the exile of my sons was so much the cause of my affliction;

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: यत् तु सा बृहती श्यामा एकवस्त्रा सभां गता। अशृणोत् परुषा वाचः किं न दुःखतरं ततः॥
en: As that youthful Krishna, clothed in a single raiment brought into the Assembly Hall and that she was made to listen to harsh and insulting words, what can be more painful than that.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: स्त्रीधर्मिणी वरारोहा क्षत्रधर्मरता सदा। नाभ्यगच्छत् तदा नाथं कृष्णा नाथवती सती॥
en: Krishna, though her husbands were living, was at that time without the protection of a lord-that lady of beautiful hips with the modesty proper to a lay and ever attached to the virtue of a Kshatriya princess.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: यस्मा मम सपुत्रायास्त्वं नाथो मधुसूदन। रामश्च बलिनां श्रेष्ठः प्रद्युम्नश्च महारथः॥ साऽहमेवंविधं दुःखं सहेऽद्य पुरुषोत्तम। भीमे जीवति दुर्धर्षे विजये चापलायिनि॥
en: Having yourself, O slayer of Madhu, as the protector of myself with my sons and as also that foremost of powerful men, Rama and that great car-warrior Pradyumna; and having the invincible Bhima and Vijaya who never turn back from the field alive, that I should suffer this sort of grief, O best among men!

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तत आश्वासयामास पुत्राधिभिरभिप्लुताम्। पितृष्वसारं शोचन्ती शौरिः पार्थसखः पृथाम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Shauri, the friend of the Partha's, then comforted his paternal aunt Pritha who was lamenting being filled with grief on account of her sons.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: वासुदेव उवाच का तु सीमन्तिनी त्वादृक् लोकेष्वस्ति पितृष्वसः। शूरस्य राज्ञो दुहिता आजमीढकुलं गता।॥
en: Vasudeva said O aunt, what woman is there in this world who is like you? The daughter of king Shura, you now (by marriage) a member of the Ajamida race.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: महाकुलीना भवती ह्रदाद्धदमिवागता। ईश्वरी सर्वकल्याणी भा परमपूजिता॥
en: Born in a noble family (and married to another equally noble family), you are (like a lotus) transplanted from one lake into another; you are the all-auspicious queen and much respected and beloved by your husband.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: वीरसूर्वीरपत्नी त्वं सर्वैः समुदिता गुणैः। सुखदुःखे महाप्राज्ञे त्वादृशी सोढुमर्हति॥
en: Yourself the wife of a hero, you have produced heroes; you are endued with all the virtues; it is fitting, of great wisdom as you are, that you should bear patiently happiness and misery like the Partha's.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: निद्रातन्द्रे क्रोधहर्षों क्षुत्पिपासे हिमातपौ। एतानि पार्था निर्जित्य नित्यं वीरसुखे रताः॥
en: Sleep, laziness, anger, joy hunger and thirst, the Partha's having brought all these under control are ever attached to the enjoyment of happiness attainable by heroes only.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: त्यक्तग्राम्यसुखाः पार्था नित्यं वीरसुखप्रियाः। न तु स्वल्पेन तुष्येयुर्महोत्साहा महाबलाः॥
en: The Partha's ever desirous of enjoyment of heroes' life forego mean happiness; those men of great energy and great prowess were not content with a little.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: अन्तं धीरा निषेवन्ते मध्यं ग्राम्यसुखप्रियाः। उत्तमांश्च परिक्लेशान् भोगांश्चातीव मानुषान्॥ अन्तेषु रेमिरे धीरा न ते मध्येषु रेमिरे। अन्तप्राप्ति सुखामा हुर्दुःखमन्तरमेतयोः॥
en: Those who are wise enjoy or suffer the extremes of whatever is enjoyable or sufferable. But person attached to mean happiness chose indifferent state of dullness; the former delight in the acutest sufferings or highest enjoyments; they do not like a middle course. They consider the extreme to be happiness, while that which lies between, is held by them to be misery.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: अभिवादयन्ति भवर्ती पाण्डवाः सह कृष्णया। आत्मानं च कुशलिनं निवेद्याहुरनामयम्॥
en: The son of Pandu along with Krishna send their greetings to you; and having submitted to your notice that they are in health, asked about welfare.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: अरोगान् सर्वसिद्धार्थान् क्षिप्रं द्रक्ष्यसि पाण्डवान्। ईश्वरान् सर्वलोकस्य हतामित्राश्रिया वृतान्॥
en: You will soon see the sons of Pandu without any illness and all their objects gained, the lords of all the world, with their enemies killed and themselves surrounded by prosperity.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: एवमाश्वासिता कुन्ती प्रत्युवाच जनार्दनम्। पुत्रादिभिरभिध्वस्ता निगृह्याबुद्धिजं तमः॥१००।
en: Kunti who was filled with grief for her sons, thus comforted, said again to Janardana after driving away the gloom of her mind due to ignorance.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: कृन्त्युवाच यद् यत् तेषां महाबाहो पथ्यं स्यान्मधुसूदन। यथा यथा त्वं मन्येथाः कुर्याः कृष्ण तथा तथा॥
en: Kunti said-Whatever, O you with long arms, is beneficial in opinion, O slayer of Madhu and whatever you think right to be done, O Krishna, should be done.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: अविलोपेन धर्मस्य अनिकृत्या परंतप। प्रभावज्ञास्मि ते कृष्ण सत्यस्याभिजनस्य च॥
en: O chastiser of enemies let these be done without transgressing virtue and without the practice of deceit; I know, O Krishna, the power of your truth and your birth.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: व्यवस्थायां च मित्रेषु बुद्धिविक्रमयोस्तथा। त्वमेव नः कुले धर्मस्त्वं सत्यं त्वं तपो महत्॥
en: And I know the wisdom and prowess you apply to the accomplishment of your decisions in any matter regarding your friends. In our family you are virtue, you are truth and you are the great devotee.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: त्वं त्राता त्वं महद् ब्रह्म त्वयि सर्वं प्रतिष्ठितम्। यथैवात्य तथैवैतत् त्वयि सत्यं भविष्यति॥
en: You are the saviour, you are the great Brahma, everything depends on you; what you have must come to pass for truth itself depends on you.

description: The conversation between Kunti and Krishna
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तामामन्त्र्य च गोविन्दः कृत्वा चाभिप्रदक्षिणम्। प्रातिष्ठत महाबाहुर्दुर्योधनगृहान् प्रति॥
en: Vaishampayana said Govinda of long arms bidding adieu to her and also going round her, went towards the residence if Duryodhana.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Duryodhana
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच पृथामामन्त्र्य गोविन्दः कृत्वा चाभिप्रदक्षिणम्। दुर्योधनगृहं शौरिरभ्यगच्छदरिंदमः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Bidding adieu to Pritha and also going round her, Govinda or Shauri, the chastiser of enemies, went the residence of Duryodhana.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Duryodhana
sn: लक्ष्या परमया युक्तं पुरन्दरगृहोपमम्। विचित्रैरासनैर्युक्तं प्रविवेश जनार्दनः॥
en: Janardana entered the house which was furnished very sumptuously and was like the mansion of Purandara, furnished with diverse kinds of seats.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Duryodhana
sn: तस्य कक्ष्या व्यतिक्रम्य तिस्रो द्वा:स्थैरवारितः। ततोऽभ्रघनसंकाशां गिरिकूटमिवोच्छ्रितम्॥ श्रिया ज्वलन्तं प्रासादमारुरोह महायशाः। तत्र राजसहस्त्रैश्च कुरुभिश्चाभिसंवृतम्॥
en: Traversing tree divisions of that mansion, without a word of challenge from the gatekeepers, that one of great fame, came to a palace, effulgent with marks of prosperity and i having the appearance of a mass of clouds, high as the peak of a mountain. There surrounded by a thousand Kuru kings.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Duryodhana
sn: धार्तराष्ट्र महाबाहुं ददर्शासीनमासने। दुःशासनं च कर्णं च शकुनि चापि सौबलम्॥
en: The son of Dhritarashtra of long arms, he saw seated on a seat and he also saw, Dushasana, Karna, Shakuni and the son of Subala.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Duryodhana
sn: दुर्योधनसमीपे तानासनस्थान् ददर्श सः। अभ्यागच्छति दाशार्हे धार्तराष्ट्रो महायशाः॥
en: He saw them on a seat near Duryodhana. The scion of the Dasharha race, having appeared, the son of Dhritarashtra of great fame.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Duryodhana
sn: उदतिष्ठत् सहामात्यः पूजयन् मधुसूदनम्। समेत्य धार्तराष्ट्रेण सहामात्येन केशवः॥ राजभिस्तत्र वार्ष्णेयः समागच्छद् यथावयः। तत्र जाम्बूनदमयं पर्यवं सुपरिष्कृतम्॥
en: Rose up along with his advisers, honouring the slayer of Madhu; Keshava having saluted the son of Dhritarashtra along with his ministers; and having also saluted the kings that were there according to their ages, the scion of the Vrishni race ((Achyuta) seated himself on a seat which was there, made of gold and beautiful looking.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Duryodhana
sn: विविधास्तरणास्तीर्णमभ्युपाविशदच्युतः। तस्मिन् गां मधुपर्कं चाप्युदकं च जनार्दने॥ निवेदयामास तदा गृहान् राज्यं च कौरवः। तत्र गोविन्दमासीनं प्रसन्नादित्यवर्चसम्॥
en: And ornamented with diverse gems and overlaid with a carpet. The Kuru king then presented a cow, honey, curds and water and placed at his disposal his palaces in the kingdom; and then to Govinda seated here like the radiant Sun.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Duryodhana
sn: उपासांचक्रिरे सर्वे कुरवो राजभिः सह। ततो दुर्योधनो राजा वार्ष्णेयं जयतां वरम्॥
en: All the people present including the Kuru kings, made worship. Then the king Duryodhana, that foremost of victors, the scion of Vrishni race.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Duryodhana
sn: न्यमन्त्रयद् भोजनेन नाभ्यनन्दच्च केशवः। ततो दुर्योधनः कृष्णमब्रवीत् कुरुसंसदि॥
en: Invited to dinner; but Keshava did not accept the invitation; then Duryodhana said to Krishna in that assembly of the Kurus.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Duryodhana
sn: मृदुपूर्वं शठोदकं कर्णमाभाष्य कौरवः। कस्मादन्नानि पानानि वासांसि शयनानि च॥
en: In an humble voice but with evil intention concealed in his heart and looking at Karna. 'For what reason the eatables, drinks, garment and beds.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Duryodhana
sn: त्वदर्थमुपनीतानि नागृहीस्त्वं जनार्दन। उभयोश्चाददाः साह्यमुभयोश्च हिते रतः॥ सम्बन्धी दयितश्चासि धृतराष्ट्रस्य माधव। त्वं हि गोविन्द धर्मार्थो वेत्थ तत्त्वेन सर्वशः। तत्र कारणमिच्छामि श्रोतुं चक्रगदाधर॥
en: Which have been provided for you, do you not accept. O Janardana, devoted to the good of both parties in the impending struggle as you are, you ought to keep to both sides; O Madhava, you have besides, closer relationship with Dhritarashtra; you O Govinda, know what is righteous and what is conducive to worldly profit in the true sense and in all their bearings.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Duryodhana
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच स एवमुक्तो गोविन्दः प्रत्युवाच महामनाः! उद्यन्मेघस्वनः काले प्रगृह्य विपुलं भुजम्॥ अलघूकृतमग्रस्तनिरस्तमसंकुलम्। राजीवनेत्रो राजानं हेतुमद् वाक्यमुत्तमम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said O wielder of the discus and the mace, I want to hear the reason of this action of yours). That Govinda of a great mind being then addressed, said in reply, speaking like the roaring of a cloud, at the proper time raising of a cloud, at the proper time raising his long arm. The one with eyes like the leaves of a lotus said to the king these excellent words giving the reasons-words that were not too low, distinct, correctly pronounced and without any confusion.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Duryodhana
sn: कृतार्था भुञ्जते दूताः पूजां गृह्णन्ति चैव ह। कृतार्थं मां सहामात्यं समर्चिष्यसि भारत॥
en: “Those messengers only, who have gained their objects take their food and accept worship; and you, O Bharata, after gratifying me in my wish, may entertain me along with my followers'.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Duryodhana
sn: एवमुक्तः प्रत्युवाच धार्तराष्ट्रो जनार्दनम्। न युक्तं भवताऽस्मासु प्रतिपत्तुमसाम्प्रतम्॥
en: The son of Dhritarashtra, being thus spoken to, said in reply to Janardana-'It is not befitting that your exalted self should behave in this unjust way.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Duryodhana
sn: कृतार्थं वाकृतार्थं च त्वां वयं मधुसूदना यतामहे पूजयितुं दाशार्ह न च शक्नुमः॥
en: Whether your objects are gratified or not gratified, we, O slayer of Madhu, were bent on entertaining you but could not. O you of the Dasharha race.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Duryodhana
sn: न च तत् कारणं विद्यो यस्मिन् नो मधुसूदन। पूजां कृतां प्रीयमाणैर्नामस्थाः पुरुषोत्तम॥
en: We do not however see any reason (for your action) in this matter, O slayer of Madhu, namely your non-acceptance of the entertainment's provided for you, O best among men.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Duryodhana
sn: वैरं नो नास्ति भवता गोविन्द न च विग्रहः। स भवान् प्रसमीक्ष्यैतन्नेदृशं वक्तुमर्हति॥
en: We have no enmity with your exalted self, O Govinda, nor strife; therefore shall it seem to you, on mature thought that it is not proper for you to have spoken thus.'

description: The conversation between Krishna and Duryodhana
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्तः प्रत्युवाच धार्तराष्ट्र जनार्दनः। अभिवीक्ष्य सहामात्यं दाशार्हः प्रहसन्निव॥
en: Vaishampayana said Janardana thus spoken to, said by way of reply to the son of Dhritarashtra, after that scion of the Dasharha race had gazed on him along with his ministers, laughing as it were.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Duryodhana
sn: नाहं कामान संरम्भान द्वेषान्नार्थकारणात्। न हेतुवादाल्लोभाद् वा धर्म जह्यां कथंचन॥
en: 'I never abandon virtue from motives of desire or from wrath or from hate or from the object of gaining my objects or for the sake of argument or from covetousness.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Duryodhana
sn: सम्प्रीतिभोज्यान्यन्नानि आपद्भोज्यानि वा पुनः। न च सम्प्रीयसे राजन् न चैवापद्गता वयम्॥
en: One should eat (others') food when there is love (between them) or again it should be taken when one is in distress; O king, neither do you please me, nor am I in distress.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Duryodhana
sn: अकस्माद् द्वेष्टि वै राजन् जन्मप्रभृति पाण्डवान्। प्रियानुवर्तिनो भ्रातॄन् सर्वैः समुदितान् गुणैः।२६।।
en: For no reason do you, Oking, bear malice, even since their birth, to the Pandavas who are your loving followers and brothers and in whom there are developed all the virtues.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Duryodhana
sn: अकस्माच्चैव पार्थानां द्वेषणं नोपपद्यते। धर्मे स्थिताः पाण्डवेयाः कस्तान् किं वक्तुमर्हति॥
en: This malice towards the sons of Pritha, for no reason, is not fitting. The sons of Pandu stand on virtue and who is there that can blame them and in what way?

description: The conversation between Krishna and Duryodhana
sn: यस्तान् द्वेष्टि स मां द्वेष्टि यस्ताननु स मामनु। ऐकात्म्यं मां गतं विद्धि पाण्डवैर्धर्मचारिभिः॥
en: He who bears them malice, bears me malice; he that follows them, follows me, know that I am merged in the Pandavas.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Duryodhana
sn: कामक्रोधानुवर्ती हि यो मोहाद् विरुरुत्सति। गुणवन्तं च यो द्वेष्टि तमाहुः पुरुषाधमम्॥
en: He who following the dictates of impulse or wrath, owing to a confusion of the intellects, wants to act against the interests of.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Duryodhana
sn: यः कल्याणगुणाज्ञातीन् मोहाल्लोभाद् दिदृक्षते। सोऽजितात्माजितक्रोधो न चिरं तिष्ठति श्रियम्॥
en: A deserving man and bears him malice, has been called the vilest of men, and he who desires to see a cousin endued with blessed virtue with eyes of lost of ignorance.
