description: The conversation between Krishna and Duryodhana
sn: अथ यो गुणसम्पन्नान् हृदयस्याप्रियानपि। प्रियेण कुरुते वश्यांश्चिरं यशसि तिष्ठति।॥
en: Is a slave to his soul and a slave to his wrath; prosperity does not remain with him for any length of time. On the other hand, he, who, by good services, wins over those who are endued with virtues and accomplishments, through they are not dear to his heart ever become renowned.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Duryodhana
sn: सर्वमेतन्न भोक्तव्यमन्नं दुष्टाभिसंहितम्। क्षत्तुरेकस्य भोक्तव्यमिति मे धीयते मतिः॥
en: All these eatables, defiled by wickedness, cannot be taken by me-I am of opinion, that eatables provided to me by Kshatta alone, Vidura should be eaten by me.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Duryodhana
sn: एवमुक्त्वा महाबाहुर्दुर्योधनममर्षणम्। निश्चक्राम ततः शुभ्राद् धार्तराष्ट्रनिवेशनात्॥
en: The one of long arms, thus speaking to the wrathful Duryodhana, then came away from the white mansion of the son of Dhritarashtra.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Duryodhana
sn: निर्याय च महाबाहुर्वासुदेवो महामनाः। निवेशाय ययौ वेश्म विदुरस्य महात्मनः॥
en: And the large minded Vamadeva of long arms, coming out went to the residence of the great-souled Vidura.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Duryodhana
sn: तमभ्यगच्छद् द्रोणश्च कृपो भीष्मोऽथ बाह्निकः। कुरवश्च महाबाहुं विदुरस्य गृहे स्थितम्॥
en: There came to him the Kurus, Drona, Kripa, Bhishma, Bahlika while the house of Vidura.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Duryodhana
sn: त ऊचुर्माधवं वीरं कुरवो मधुसूदनम्। निवेदयामो वार्ष्णेय सरत्नांस्ते गृहान् वयम्॥
en: Those Kurus said to the heroic Madhava, the slayer of Madhu, 'You scion of the Vrishni race, we place at your disposal our abodes ornamented with gems.'

description: The conversation between Krishna and Duryodhana
sn: तानुवाच महातेजाः कौरवान् मधुसूदनः। सर्वे भवन्तो गच्छन्तु सर्वा मेऽपचितिः कृता॥
en: The slayer of Madhu, of great energy said to those descendants of Kuru, 'All of you may go away; by these offers have you honoured me.'

description: The conversation between Krishna and Duryodhana
sn: यातेषु कुरुष क्षत्ता दाशार्हमपराजितम्। अभ्यर्चयामास तदा सर्वकामैः प्रयत्नवान्॥
en: The Kurus having departed, the Khattva Vidura paid due honours to the scion of the Dasharha race who had never met with a defeat and then made special endeavours to meet all his wishes.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Duryodhana
sn: ततः क्षत्तानपानानि शुचीनि गुणवन्ति च। उपाहरदनेकानि केशवाय महात्मने॥
en: Then the Kshatta collected large quantities of clean and delicious foods and drinks for the great-souled Keshava.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Duryodhana
sn: तैस्तर्पयित्वा प्रथमं ब्राह्मणान् मधुसूदनः। वैदविद्भ्यो ददौ कृष्णः परमद्रविणान्यपि॥
en: The slayer of Madhu having gratified the Brahmanas first, he gave first to Brahmanas conversant with the Vedas, some of that food with wealth.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Duryodhana
sn: ततोऽनुयायिभिः सार्धं मरुद्भिरिव वासवः। विदुरान्नानि बुभुजे शुचीनि गुणवन्ति च॥
en: There along with his followers, like Vasava in the midst of the Marutas, he took his clean and delicious eatables provided by Vidura. A

description: The conversation between Krishna and Vidura
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तं भुक्तवन्तमाश्वस्तं निशायां विदुरोऽब्रवीत्। नेदं सम्यग् व्यवसितं केशवागमनं तव॥
en: Vaishampayana said During the night Vidura said to him after he had taken his food and refreshed himself-'O Keshava, this coming of yours is not an act well thought of.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Vidura
sn: अर्थधर्मातिगो मन्दः संरम्भी च जनार्दन। माननो मनकामश्च वृद्धानां शासनातिगः॥
en: Janardana that fool transgresses both worldly profit and virtue, besides he is wrathful, destroyer of other people's honour, though he is himself desirous for obtaining it and is incapable being controlled by aged people.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Vidura
sn: धर्मशास्त्रातिगो मूढो दुरात्मा प्रचग्रहं गतः। अनेयः श्रेयसां मन्दो धार्तराष्ट्रो जनार्दन॥
en: The wicked-souled fool, the son of Dhritarashtra, goes against the rules laid down in our books of religion; being overtaken by fate he is incapable of being led by his superiors and is a fool.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Vidura
sn: कामात्मा प्राज्ञमानी च मित्रध्रुक् सर्वशङ्कितः। अकर्ता चाकृतज्ञश्च त्यक्तधर्मा प्रियानृतः॥
en: His soul follows the beat of his desire and in his own opinion he is a wise man; an enemy to his own friends and suspicious in all matters; doing nothing himself, yet not grateful (for things done for him), he has abandoned virtue and is fond of untruth.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Vidura
sn: मूढचाकृतबुद्धिश्च इन्द्रियाणामनीश्वरः । कामानुसारी कृत्येषु सर्वेष्वकृतनिश्चयः॥
en: He is a fool with his understanding uncultivated, the slave of his senses, following the lead of his desires and hesitates to do a thing which ought to be done.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Vidura
sn: एतैश्चान्यैश्च बहुभिषैिरेव समन्वितः। त्वयोच्यमानः श्रेयोऽपि संरम्भान्न ग्रहीष्यति॥
en: He is possessed with these and many other vices; out of vanity he will not accept your advice though that is distinctly for his good.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Vidura
sn: भीष्मे द्रोणे कृपे कर्णे द्रोणपुत्रे जयद्रथे। भूयसी वर्तते वृत्तिं न शमे कुरुते मनः॥
en: He has too great a confidence on Bhishma, Drona, Kripa, Karna, the son of Drona and Jayadratha and therefore he does not think of peace.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Vidura
sn: निश्चितं धार्तराष्ट्राणां सकर्णानां जनार्दन। भीष्मद्रोणमुखान् पार्था न शक्ताः प्रतिवीक्षितुम्॥
en: It is the conviction of the sons of Dhritarashtra and of Karna, O Janardana, that the sons of Pritha are not capable of even gazing at an army under the leadership of Bhishma and Drona.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Vidura
sn: सेनासमुदयं कृत्वा पार्थिवं मधुसूदन। कृतार्थं मन्यते बाल आत्मानमविचक्षणः॥
en: That boy, who is not shrewd having brought together a large army from this earth, regards himself as having already gained his object,o slayer of Madhu.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Vidura
sn: एकः कर्णः पराञ्जेतुं समर्थं इति निश्चितम्। धार्तराष्ट्रस्य दुर्बुद्धेः स शमं नोपयास्यति॥
en: It is the conviction of the son of Dhritarashtra of mean intelligence, that Karna alone is capable of defeating the enemy and he will not agree to peace.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Vidura
sn: संविच्च धार्तराष्ट्राणं सर्वेषामेव केशव। शमे प्रयतमानस्य तव सौभ्रात्रकाक्षिणः॥
en: Actuated by brotherly feelings as you are attempting to establish peace between the two parties and are seeking the good of the sons of Dhritarashtra, O Keshava.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Vidura
sn: न पाण्डवानामस्माभिः प्रतिदेयं यथोचितम्। इति व्यवसतास्तेषु वचनं स्यान्निरर्थकम्॥
en: It has been decided among themselves that they would not give back their just dues to the sons of Pandu; and advice to them would be useless.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Vidura
sn: यत्र सूक्तं दुरुक्तं च समं स्यान्मधुसूदन। न तत्र प्रलपेत् प्राज्ञो बधिरेष्विव गायनः॥
en: In cases where good and bad advices are of equal effect, O slayer of Madhu, a wise man does not talk like a singer among the deaf.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Vidura
sn: अविजानत्सु मूढेषु निर्मर्यादेषु माधव। न त्वं वाक्यं ब्रुवन् युक्तचाण्डालेषु द्विजो यथा॥
en: Among those fools who do not know anything and who entertain no reverence for others, O Madhava, do not speak any word as a twice-born would do among the Chandalas.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Vidura
sn: सोऽयं बलस्थो मूढच न करिष्यति ते वचः। तस्मिन् निरर्थकं वाक्यमुक्तं सम्पत्स्यते तव॥
en: This child (in wisdom) who is such this fool will not do what you say and your words spoken to him will go in vain.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Vidura
sn: तेषां समुपविष्टानां सर्वेषां पापचेतसाम्। तव मध्यावतरणं मम कृष्ण न रोचते॥
en: The idea does not please me, O Krishna, of your going in the midst of all those of wicked heart seated together.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Vidura
sn: दुर्बुद्धीनामशिष्टानां बहूनां दुष्टचेतसाम्। प्रतीपं वचनं मध्ये तव कृष्ण न रोचते।॥
en: The idea does not please me, O Krishna, that you should utter words among those men, of mean intelligence, vicious and of wicked hearts, of whom there are many.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Vidura
sn: अनुपासितवृद्धत्वाच्छ्रियो दर्पाच्च मोहितः। वयोदर्पादमर्षाच्च न ते श्रोय ग्रहीष्यति॥
en: Owing to their never having respected the aged and to vanity and folly incident to their age and to wrath they will not accept what is। for their good.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Vidura
sn: बलं बलवदप्यस्य यदि वक्ष्यसि माधव। त्वय्यस्य महती शङ्का न करिष्यति ते वचः॥
en: He has at his cominand a strong force and if you speak to him, O Madhava, he will not act according to your advice, for he entertains suspicions against you.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Vidura
sn: नेदमद्य युधा शक्यमिन्द्रेणापि सहामरैः। इति व्यवसिताः सर्वे धार्तराष्ट्रा जनार्दन॥
en: All the sons of Dhritarashtra have come to the conclusion that they are now invincible in battle even with Indra himself along with the gods.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Vidura
sn: तेष्वेवमुपपन्नेषु कामक्रोधानुवर्तिषु। समर्थमपि ते वाक्यमसमर्थं भविष्यति॥
en: Among those who are thus endued and who follow the impulse of desire and anger, your words though able in themselves will be of no use.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Vidura
sn: मध्ये तिष्ठन् हस्त्यनीकस्य मन्दो रथाश्वयुक्तस्य बलस्य मूढः। दुर्योधनो मन्यते वीतभीतिः कृत्स्ना मयेयं पृथिवी जितेति॥
en: Standing in the midst of his ranks of elephants and his army composed of chariots and cavalry, that fool of dull intelligence. Duryodhana, thinks himself past the each of any fear and that he has gained his object having conquered this earth.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Vidura
sn: आशंसते वै धृतराष्ट्रस्य पुत्रो महाराज्यमसपत्नं पृथिव्याम्। तस्मिञ्छमः केवलो नोपलभ्यो बद्धं सन्तं मन्यते लब्धमर्थम्॥
en: The son of Dhritarashtra aspires to an extensive empire in this earth without any rival. Peace with him therefore cannot be obtained. The wealth ((and kingdom) which is now at his command he regards as inalienably his and his alone.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Vidura
sn: पर्यस्तेयं पृथिवी कालपक्वा दुर्योधनार्थं पाण्डवान् योद्धकामाः। समागताः सर्वयोधाः पृथिव्यां राजानश्च क्षितिपालैः समेताः॥
en: This earth, having its allotted time, ever is on the eve of ruin, it seems only for the sake of Duryodhana, for all the Pandavas and all the soldiers including the kings and rulers of the earth have assembled together, desirous of war.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Vidura
sn: सर्वे चैते कृतवैराः पुरस्तात् त्वया राजानो हृतसाराश्च कृष्ण) तवोद्वेगात् संश्रिता धार्तराष्ट्रानं सुसंहताः कर्णेन वीराः॥
en: All these (kings) too have before this been made enemies of by yourself; for you have, O Krishna, dispossessed these kings of their wealth; out of fear of you these heroes have come under the protection of the sons of Dhritarashtra and joined Karna.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Vidura
sn: त्यक्तात्मानः सह दुर्योधनेन हृष्टा योद्धं पाण्डवान् सर्वयोधाः। तेषां मध्ये प्रविशेथा यदि त्वं न तन्मतं मम दाशार्ह वीर॥
en: All those soldiers, united with Duryodhana and regardless of self are delighted at the prospect of) fighting with the Pandavas and, O you heroic scion of the Dasharha race, it is not my opinion that you should enter in their midst.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Vidura
sn: तेषां समुपविष्टानां बहूनां दुष्टचेतसाम्। कथं मध्यं प्रपद्येथाः शत्रूणां शत्रुकर्शन॥
en: Among those men, your enemies any in number, of wicked hearts seated together how will you go, O grinder of your enemies.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Vidura
sn: सर्वथा त्वं महाबाहो देवैरपि दुरुत्सहः। प्रभावं पौरुषं बुद्धिं जानामि तव शत्रुहन्।॥
en: O you of long arms, in every way are you hard to be vanquished even by the gods and, O slayer of your enemies, I know your wisdom, manliness and your importance.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Vidura
sn: या मे प्रीतिः पाण्डवेषु भूयः सा त्वयि माधव। प्रेम्णा च बहुमानाच्च सौहृदाच्च ब्रवीम्यहम्॥
en: What have I to bear to the sons of Pandu, I bear to you in a greater degree, O Madhava and I speak from motives of love, reverence and friendship.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Vidura
sn: या मे प्रीतिः पुष्कराक्ष त्वदर्शनसमुद्भवा। सा किमाख्यायते तुभ्यमन्तरात्माऽसि देहिनाम्॥
en: What is the use of describing the pleasure I feel, owing of my seeing you; for you are the universal soul of all embodies creatures.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Vidura
sn: श्रीभगवानुवाच यथा ब्रूयान्महाप्राज्ञो यथा ब्रूयाद् विचक्षणः। यथा वाच्यस्त्वद्विधेन भवता मद्विधः सुहृत्॥
en: The blessed God said You have spoken as a greatly wise man should-you have spoken as a sharp man should, even as should be spoken by a friend like you to a friend like me.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Vidura
sn: धर्मार्थयुक्तं तथ्यं च यथा त्वय्युपद्यते। तथा वचनमुक्तोऽस्मि त्वयैतत् पितृमातृवत्॥
en: This has the merit of being conversant with morality and worldly good and truth to that degree which proper for you; the words which have been spoken by you are like the advice of a father or a mother.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Vidura
sn: सत्यं प्राप्तं च युक्तं वाप्येवमेव यथाऽऽत्थ माम्। शृणुष्वगमने हेतुं विदुरावहितो भव॥
en: What you have told me is true and worthy of being followed and is even what I have described it to be; listen with attention to the reason of my coming here, O Vidura.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Vidura
sn: दौरात्म्यं धार्तराष्ट्रस्य क्षत्रियाणां च वैरताम्। सर्वमेतदहं जानन् क्षत्तः प्राप्तोऽद्य कौरवान्॥
en: The wickedness of soul of the sons of Dhritarashtra and the hostility of the Kshatriyas, knowing full well, all this, 0 Khattva have I now come to the sons of Kuru.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Vidura
sn: पर्यस्तां पृथिवीं सर्वां साश्वां सरथकुञ्जराम्। यो मोचयेन्मृत्युपाशात् प्राप्नुयाद् धर्ममुत्तमम्॥
en: He that will relive this earth of her burden consisting of horses, chariots, elephants, he that will liberate her from curse of Death will earn great religious merit.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Vidura
sn: धर्मकार्यं यतञ्छक्त्या नो चेत् प्राप्नोति मानवः। प्राप्तो भवति तत् पुण्यमत्र मे नास्ति संशयः॥
en: Attempting with all his might to do a virtuous act, if a man does not accomplish it, he gets the religious merit of having done the act. About that I have no doubt.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Vidura
sn: मनसा चिन्तयन् पापं कर्मणा नातिरोचयन्। न प्राप्नोति फलं तस्येत्येवं धर्मविदो विदुः॥
en: Thinking of a sinful act in his mind, if a man does not accomplish it, he does not get the consequences of that act. Utter those that are conversant with religion.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Vidura
sn: सोऽहं यतिष्ये प्रशमं क्षत्तः कर्तुममायया। कुरूणां सृञ्जयानां च संग्रामे विनशिष्यताम्॥
en: Therefore shall I with all, sincerity try to establish peace, O Khattva among the Kurus and the Srinjayas, for they will meet with ruins in the case of war.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Vidura
sn: सेयमापन्महाघोरा कुरुष्वेव समुत्थिता। कर्णदुर्योधनकृता सर्वे ह्येते तदन्वयाः॥
en: This exceedingly grave calamity has its rise in the Kurus; for it has been brought about by Karna and Duryodhana. All these are but their followers.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Vidura
sn: व्यसने क्लिश्यमानं हि यो मित्रं नाभिपद्यते। अनुनीय यथाशक्ति तं नृशंसं विदुर्बुधाः॥
en: He, who does not seek to serve a friend suffering from a calamity by trying to the best of his abilities, is said to be a cruel man by the wise.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Vidura
sn: आकेशग्रहणान्मित्रमकार्यात् संनिवर्तयन्। अवाच्यः कस्यचिद् भवति कृतयत्नो यथाबलम्॥
en: A friend should be turned back from improper act even by seizing his hair. That being so, how can a man be blamed, if he strives with all his might.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Vidura
sn: तत् समर्थं शुभं वाक्यं धर्मार्थसहितं हितम्। धार्तराष्ट्रः सहामात्यो ग्रहीतुं विदुरार्हति॥
en: It is proper therefore, O Vidura, for the son of Dhritarashtra along with his ministers to accept my blessed advice capable of doing good and consistent with morality and worldly profit.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Vidura
sn: हितं हि धर्तराष्ट्राणां पाण्डवानां तथैव च। पृथिव्यां क्षत्रियाणां च यतिष्येऽहममायया॥
en: With all sincerity shall I strive for the good of the sons of Dhritarashtra and of the Pandavas and indeed of the Kshatriya race of the world.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Vidura
sn: हिते प्रयतमानं मां शङ्केद् दुर्योधनो यदि। हृदयस्य च मे प्रीतिरानृण्यं च भविष्यति॥
en: If Duryodhana suspects me, striving for his good as I do, I shall at least be satisfied with myself in my heart and I shall be discharging the debt (I owe them as a friend).

description: The conversation between Krishna and Vidura
sn: ज्ञातीनां हि मिथो भेदे यन्मित्रं नाभिपद्यते। सर्वयत्नेन माध्यस्थ्यं न तन्मित्रं विदुर्बुधाः॥
en: In a dispute between cousins, the friend who does not serve them as a mediator with all his might, is not said to be a friend at all by wise men.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Vidura
sn: न मां ब्रूयुरधर्मिष्ठा मूढा ह्यसुहृदस्तथा। शक्तो नावारयत् कृष्णः संरब्धान् कुरुपाण्डवान्॥
en: In order that unrighteous, foolish and unfriendly people may not call me that Krishna though competent did not dissuade the Kurus and Pandavas inspired with rage against each other.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Vidura
sn: उभयोः साधयन्नर्थमहमागत इत्युत। तत्र यत्नमहं कृत्वा गच्छेयं नृष्ववाच्यताम्॥
en: And for being of service to both the parties have I come here. And having made attempts in that direction I shall escape blame of men.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Vidura
sn: मम धर्मार्थयुक्तं हि श्रुत्वा वाक्यमनामयम्। न चेदादास्यते बालो दिष्टस्य वशमेष्यति॥
en: If after listening to my beneficial advice, they do not accept it, the fool will feel the consequence of his luck.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Vidura
sn: अहापयन् च्छमं कुरूणां यदि चाचरेयम्। पुण्यं च मे स्याच्चरितं महात्मन् मुच्येरंश्च कुरवो मृत्युपाशात्॥
en: If without sacrificing the interests of the Pandavas I can bring about their peace with the Kurus, then I shall have done a meritorious act, O great-souled one; and the Kurus shall have been liberated from the shackles of death.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Vidura
sn: अपि वाचं भाषमाणस्य काव्यां धर्मारामामर्थवतीमहिंस्राम्। अवेक्षेरन् धार्तराष्ट्राः शमार्थं मां च प्राप्तं कुरवः पूजयेयुः॥
en: If the son of Dhritarashtra think well of the wise words spoken by me-words having their source in virtue and words leading to earthly good and words heading to the reverse of malice, for bringing about peace, then the Kurus too will worship and honour me.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Vidura
sn: न चापि मम पर्याप्ताः सहिताः सर्वपार्थिवाः। क्रुद्धस्य प्रमुख स्थातु सिंहस्येवेतरे मृगाः॥
en: Otherwise I tell you that not even all the rulers of the earth united together are capable of standing in my front like other animals before an enraged lion.

description: The conversation between Krishna and Vidura
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच इत्येवमुक्त्वा वचनं वृष्णीनामृषभस्तदा। शयने सुखसंस्पर्श शिश्ये यदुसुखावहः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having said these words that foremost of the Vrishnis and cause of the happiness of the Yadus, then laid down on his bed pleasant to the touch.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तथा कथयतोरेव तयोर्बुद्धिमतोस्तदा। शिवा नक्षत्रसम्पन्ना सा व्यतीयाय शर्वरी॥शा
en: Vaishampayana said The two wise men talking together in this way spent that night which was beautiful and lit by stars.

sn: धर्मार्थकामयुक्ताश्च विचित्रार्थपदाक्षराः। शृण्वतो विविधा वाचो विदुरस्य महात्मनः॥ कथाभिरनुरूपाभिः कृष्णस्यामिततेजसः। अकामस्येव कृष्णस्य सा व्यतीयाय शर्वरी॥
en: That night passed away against the wishes of Krishna and Vidura, who was listening to the discourses on diverse subjects conducive to religious merit and earthly profit and conveyed in rhythmical language from Krishna and of Krishna of immeasurable prowess listening to similar discourse from high-souled Vidura.

sn: ततस्तु स्वसम्पन्ना बहवः सूतमागधाः। शङ्खदुन्दुभिनिर्घोषैः केशवं प्रत्यबोधयन्॥
en: Then (at the break of day) many professional bards and singers having a good voice awakened Krishna with the sound of conches and cymbals.

sn: तत उत्थाय दाशार्ह ऋषभः सर्वसात्वताम्। सर्वमावश्यकं चक्रे प्रातःकार्यं जनार्दनः॥
en: Janardana, that scion of the Dasharha race, that best among the Satvatas, then performed all the necessary rites of the morning.

sn: कृतोदकानुजप्यः स हुताग्नि: समलंकृतः। ततश्चादित्यमुद्यन्तमुपातिष्ठत माधवः॥
en: Having performed his ablutions, having repeated the usual incantations to the god of fire and having donned his attire and ornaments, Madhava worshipped the rising sun.

sn: अथ दुर्योधनः कृष्ण शकुनिश्चापि सौबलः। संध्यां तिष्ठन्तमभ्येत्य दाशार्हमपराजितम्॥ आचक्षेतां तु कृष्णस्य धृतराष्ट्र सभागतम्। कुरूंश्च भीष्मप्रमुखान् राज्ञः सर्वाश्च पार्थिवान्॥ त्वामर्थयन्ते गोविन्द दिवि शक्रमिवामराः। तावभ्यनन्दद् गोविन्दः साम्ना परमवल्गुना॥
en: Duryodhana and Shakuni the son of Subala coming to Krishna, that scion of the Dasharha race and who had never met with a defeat, while he was yet performing his morning devotions, said to him-"King Dhritarashtra is come to the Assembly-Hall and so have the other Kurus headed by Bhishma and all the rulers of the earth. O Govinda, they are waiting for you like the gods in heaven waiting for Shakra." Govinda welcomed them by courteous words.

sn: ततो विमल आदित्ये ब्राह्मणेभ्यो जनार्दनः। ददौ हिरण्यं वासांसि गाश्चाश्वांश्च परंतपः॥ विसृज्य बहुरत्नानि दाशार्हमपराजितम्। तिष्ठन्तमुपसंगम्य ववन्दे सारथिस्तदा॥
en: When the spotless sun progressed a little further in his diurnal journey, Janardana, the chastiser of foes, gave to the Brahmanas gold, cloths, cattle and horses. Thus Krishna having distributed many gems precious stones, his charioteer approached that unvanquished hero of the Dasharha race, who was seated and paid his respects to him.

sn: ततो रथेन शुभ्रेण महता किङ्किणीकिना। हयोत्तमयुजा शीघ्रमुपातिष्ठत दारुकः॥
en: Then Daruka soon came back with the large and shining car furnished with tinkling bells and yoked to excellent horses.

sn: तमुपस्थितमाज्ञाय रथं दिव्यं महामनाः। महाभ्रघननिर्घोषं सर्वरत्नविभूषितम्॥ अग्नि प्रदक्षिणं कृत्वा ब्राह्मणांश्च जनार्दनः। कौस्तुभं मणिमामुच्य श्रिया परमया ज्वलन्॥ कुरुभिः संवृतः कृष्णो वृष्णिभिश्चाभिरक्षितः। आतिष्ठत रथं शौरिः सर्वयादवनन्दनः॥
en: That one large mind, understanding that the celestial car ornamented with all sorts of gems and precious stones and whose wheels rattled as loudly as masses of thick clouds, had arrived. Made tour round the fire and also round the Brahmanas. And putting on the Kaustubha gem which was shining with excellent beauty and surrounded by the Kurus and protected by the Vrishnis, Krishna or Shauri the center of delight of all the Yadavas mounted on his car.

sn: अन्वारुरोह दाशार्ह विदुरः सर्वधर्मवित्। सर्वप्राणभृतां श्रेष्ठं सर्वबुद्धिमतां वरम्॥
en: After that scion of the Dasharha race had mounted the car, Vidura, conversant with all virtues, superior to all living creatures and foremost among all wise men.

sn: ततो दुर्योधनः कृष्णं शकुनिश्चापि सौबलः। द्वितीयेन रथेनैनमन्वयातां परंतपम्॥
en: Duryodhana and Shakuni the son of Subala on a second car followed this chastiser of enemies, Krishna. as

sn: सात्यकिः कृतवर्मा च वृष्णीनां चापरे स्थाः। पृष्ठतोऽनुययुः कृष्णं गजैरश्वैः रथैरपि॥
en: Satyaki and Kritavarma, as also other warriors of the Vrishni race followed behind, some on elephants, some on horse and others on chariots.

sn: तेषां हेमपरिष्कारैर्युक्ताः परमवाजिभिः। गच्छतां घोषिणश्चित्ररथा राजन् विरेजिरे॥
en: The chariots of these men, O king, adorned with excellent gold and yoked to good horses and producing diverse sounds they proceeded on, looked very beautiful.

sn: सम्मृष्टसंसिक्तरजः प्रतिपेदे महापथम्। राजर्षिचरितं काले कृष्णो धीमाच्छ्रिया ज्वलन्॥
en: The wise Krishna, blazing with beauty, in fit time, came up on a high way well swept and whose dust had been cleared away and which was fit to be used even by the Rishis of royal descent.

sn: ततः प्रयाते दाशार्हे प्रावाद्यन्तैकपुष्कराः। शङ्खाश्च दमिरे तत्र वाद्यान्यन्यानि यानि च॥
en: The scion Dasharha race having set out, there was one continual music of cymbals. The conches began to be played, also all the other instruments that were there.

sn: प्रवीराः सर्वलोकस्य युवानः सिंहविक्रमाः। परिवार्य रथं शौरेरगच्छन्त परंतपाः॥
en: A large number of young men of the strength of lions, heroic chastisers of foes in the world surrounding the car of Shauri, followed him.

sn: ततोऽन्ये बहुसाहस्रा विचित्राद्भुतवाससः। असिप्रासायुधधराः कृष्णस्यासन् पुरःसराः॥
en: And there were others by thousands, who in diverse and strange attires holding swords, lances and axes followed Krishna.

sn: गजाः पञ्चशतातत्र रथाश्चासन् सहस्रशः। प्रयान्तमन्वयुर्वीरं दाशार्हमपराजितम्॥
en: There were five hundred elephants and chariots by thousands, that came up behind the heroic scion of the Dasharha race, who had never sustained a defeat.

sn: पुरं कुरूणां संवृत्तं द्रष्टुकामं जनार्दनम्। सबालवृद्धं सस्त्रीकं रथ्यागतमरिंदम॥
en: chatiser of enemies, the city of the Kurus was filled by old and young men including women, who were desirous of seeing Janardana advancing on a car.

sn: वेदिकालमाश्रिताभिश्च समाकान्तान्यनेकशः। प्रचलन्तीव भारेण योषिद्भिर्भवनान्युत॥
en: Many were the houses that were tottering under the load of women, who were in the terraces and balconies.

sn: स पूज्यमानः कुरुभिः संशृण्वन् मधुराः कथाः। यथार्ह प्रातसत्कुर्वन् प्रेक्षमाणः शनैर्ययौ॥
en: He proceeded slowly along gazing in all directions, worshipped by the Kurus; and listening to sweet speeches and returning suitable greetings.

sn: ततः सभा समासाद्य केशवस्यानुयायिनः। सशङ्खर्वेणुनिघोषैर्दिशः सर्वा व्यनादयन्॥
en: The followers of Keshava having arrived at the Assembly-Hall filled all directions with the sound of conches and cymbals.

sn: ततः सा समितिः सर्वा राज्ञाममिततेजसाम्। सम्प्राकम्पत हर्षेण कृष्णागमनकाझया॥
en: The entire assembly of those kings of immeasurable energy began to shake with delight with the desire of seeing Krishna come.

sn: ततोऽभ्याशगते कृष्णे समहष्यन् नराधिपाः। श्रुत्वा तं रथनिर्घोषं पर्जन्यनिनदोपमम्॥
en: Then those rulers of men became rejoiced at the inference that he was near, which they drew on account of their hearing the rattles of his chariot, which was like the roar of clouds charged with rain.

sn: आसाद्य तु सभाद्वारमृषभः सर्वसात्वताम्। अवतीर्य रथाच्छौरिः कैलासशिखरोपमात्॥
en: Shauri, the best among the entire Satvata race, coming to the gate of the Assembly-Hall, got down from the car which was like the peak of the Kailasa mountain.

sn: नवमेघप्रतीकाशां ज्वलन्तीमिव तेजसा। महेन्द्रसदनप्रख्यां प्रविवेश सभां ततः॥
en: He then entered the Hall, which was like the abode of the great Indra and was blazing as it were with the beauty of energy and which looked like a mass newly formed clouds.

sn: पाणौ गृहीत्वा विदुरं सात्यकिं च महायशाः। ज्योतीष्यादित्यवद् राजन् कुरून् प्राच्छादयच्छ्रिया।।३३।
en: Getting hold of the hand of Vidura and that of Satyaki (on either side) the one of great fame (entered the Assembly-Hall) eclipsing the Kurus (planets) in splendour like the sun.

sn: अग्रतो वासुदेवस्य कर्णदुर्योधनावुभौ। वृष्णयः कृतवर्मा चाप्यासन् कृष्णस्य पृष्ठतः॥
en: I front of Vasudeva were the two, Karna and Duryodhana; while behind him sat the Vrishnis and Kritavarma.

sn: धृतराष्ट्रं पुरुस्कृत्य भीष्मद्रोणादयस्ततः। आसनेभ्योऽचलन् सर्वे पूजयन्तो जनार्दनम्॥
en: Bhishma, Drona and others following the example of Dhritarashtra rose up from their seats with the object of honouring Janardana.

sn: अभ्यागच्छति दाशार्हे प्रज्ञाचक्षुर्नरेश्वरः। सहैव द्रोणभीष्माभ्यामुदतिष्ठन्महायशाः॥
en: That scion of the Dasharha approaching the lord of men having eyes of wisdom along with Drona and Bhishma and others all of great fame rose up from their seats.

sn: उत्तिष्ठति महाराजे धृतराष्ट्र जनेश्वरे। तानि राजसहस्राणि समुत्तस्थुः समन्ततः॥
en: The great king Dhritarashtra, the lord of men, having got up, those thousands of kings all rose up also.

sn: आसनं सर्वतोभद्रं जाम्बूनदपरिष्कृतम्। कृष्णार्थं कल्पितं तत्र धृतराष्ट्रस्य शासनात्॥
en: A seat respectable in every way and adorned with gold was placed there under instructions from Dhritarashtra.

sn: स्मयमानस्तु राजानं भीष्मद्रोणौ च माधवः। अभ्यभाषत धर्मात्मा राज्ञश्चान्यान् यथावयः॥
en: With a smiling face, did the virtuoussouled Madhava great the king, Bhishma and Drona, as also other kings according to their respective age. race

sn: तत्र केशवमानचुः सम्यगभ्यागतं सभाम्। राजानः पार्थिवाः सर्वे कुरवश्च जनार्दनम्॥
en: Then all the kings and rulers of the earth and all the Kurus worshipped Keshava or Janardana who had come into the AssemblyHall..

sn: तत्र तिष्ठन् स दाशार्हो राजमध्ये परंतपः। अपश्यदन्तरिक्षस्थानृषीन् परपुरंजयः। ततस्तानभिसम्प्रेक्ष्य नारदप्रमुखानृषी॥ अभ्यभाषत दाशार्हो भीष्मं शान्तनवं शनैः। पार्थिवीं समितिं द्रष्टुमृषयोऽभ्यागता नृप॥
en: That chastiser of foes, the scion of the Dasharha race, while staying there, beheld in the heaven the Rishis who had attained to the better world. And seeing the Rishis under the leadership of Narada, the scion of the Dasharha race said to Bhishma the son of Shantanu slowly, “To see this earthly assembly have the Rishis come, O ruler of men.

sn: निमन्त्र्यन्तामासनैश्च सत्कारेण च भूयसां। नैतेष्वनुपविष्टेषु शक्यं केनचिदासितुम्॥
en: Invite them with plenty of seats and welcome them; for they remaining unseated, who is capable of taking his seat?

sn: पूजा प्रयुज्यतामाशु मुनीनां भावितात्मनाम्। ऋषीछान्तनवो दृष्ट्वा सभाद्वारमुपस्थितान्॥
en: Arrange therefore immediately for the worship of these Munis who have conquered their souls.” The son of Shantanu seeing the Rishis come at the very gates of the AssemblyHall.

sn: त्वरमाणस्ततो भृत्यानासनानीत्यचोदयत्। आसनान्यथ मृष्टानि महान्ति विपुलानि च॥
en: Quickly commanded the attendants to get seats soon for them and they brought many spacious and beautiful seats.

sn: मणिकाञ्चनचित्राणि समाजह्वस्ततस्ततः। तेषु तत्रोपविष्टेषु गृहीतार्धेषु भारत॥
en: Embroidered with gold and set with gems. After they had accepted due worship and seated themselves, O Bharata.

sn: निषसादासने कृष्णो राजानश्च यथासनम्। दुःशासनः सात्यकये ददावासनमुत्तमम्॥
en: Krishna took his seat; so did all the kings, in their respective seats. Dushasana offered to Satyaki an excellent seat.

sn: विविंशतिर्ददौ पीठं काञ्चनं कृतवर्मणे। अविदूरे तु कृष्णस्य कर्णदुर्योधनावुभौ॥ एकासने महात्मानौ निषीदतुरमर्षणौ। गान्धारराजः शकुनिर्गान्धारैरभिरक्षितः॥
en: Vivingshati gave a beautiful golden seat to Kritavarma and not far from Krishna. Karna and Duryodhana, the two men of large-souled and wrathful sat on one and the same seat. The king of the Gandharas Shakuni, surrounded by the Gandhara chiefs.

sn: निषसादासने राजा सहपुत्रो विशाम्पते। विदुरो मणिपीठे तु शुक्लस्पर्ध्या जिनोत्तरे॥
en: With his son sat on one seat, О lord of the world. The great Vidura sat on a holy seat covered with a white deer skin and decked with gems.

sn: संस्पृशन्नासनं शौरेर्महामतिरूपाविशत्। चिरस्य दृष्ट्वा दाशार्ह राजानः सर्व एव ते॥ अमृतस्येव नातृप्यन् प्रेक्षमाणा जनार्दनम्। अतसीपुष्पसंकाशः पीतवासा जनार्दनः॥
en: That of great intelligence sat contiguous to the seat of Shauri. All those kings, having for a long time looked at the scion of the Dasharha race, were not gratified with gazing on Janardana as if drinking nectar. Janardana was attired in a yellow robe and looked like the Atasi flower.

sn: व्यभ्राजत सभामध्ये हेम्नीवोपहितो मणि॥
en: He sat in the midst of that Assembly like a dark gem placed on gold.

sn: ततस्तूष्णीं सर्वमासीद् गोविन्दगतमानसम्। न तत्र कश्चित् किञ्चिद् वा व्याजहार पुमान् क्वचित्।।
en: They all were silent while Govinda was thinking within himself and no man there mad the slightest utterance. one

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तेष्वासीनेषु सर्वेषु तूष्णीम्भूतेषु राजसु। वाक्यमभ्याददे कृष्णः सुदंष्ट्रो दुन्दुभिस्वनः॥ जीमूत इव धर्मान्ते सर्वां संश्रावयन् सभाम्। धृतराष्ट्रमभिप्रेक्ष्य समभाषत माधवः॥
en: Vaishampayana said All of them having taken their seats and perfect stillness having prevailed among the kings, Krishna who had an excellent set of teeth and had the voice of a drum began to speak like the roar of clouds at the close of summer, Madhava, looking on Dhritarashtra, spoke so that the assembly could hear.

sn: श्रीभगवानुवाच कुरूणां पाण्डवानां च शम: स्यादिति भारत। अप्रणाशेन वीराणामेतद् याचितुमागतः॥
en: "Between the Kurus and Pandavas there may be peace, O Bharata, without the slaying of heroes (on either side) to effect this have I come.

sn: राजन् नान्यत् प्रवक्तव्यं तव नैःश्रेयसं वचः। विदितं ह्येव ते सर्वं वेदितव्यमरिंदम्॥
en: Oking, I have nothing else to say, everything that ought to be known in this world is known to you, O chastiser of foes.

sn: इदं ह्यद्य कुलं श्रेष्ठं सर्वराजसु पार्थिव। श्रुतवृत्तोपसम्पन्नं सर्वैः समुदितं गुणैः॥
en: 0 ruler of the earth, this dynasty (of yours) is the best among these of all kings; it is noted for its knowledge of the scriptures as also for its good ways of life and it is endued with all the virtues.

sn: कृपानुकम्या कारुण्यमानृशंस्यं च भारत। तथाऽऽर्जवं क्षमा सत्यं कुरुष्वेतद् विशिष्यते॥
en: Kindness, pain at the sight of other's pains, desire to remedy evils and humanity, O Bharata, as also sincerity, forgiveness and truth, are specially in the nature of the Kurus.

sn: ते तस्मिन्नेवंविधे राजन् कुले महति तिष्ठति। त्वन्निमित्तं विशेषेण नेह युक्तमसाम्प्रतम्॥
en: Belonging to this noble family which is such, 0 king, no one should do what is improper and especially an improper act is to be deplored when you are the cause of it.

sn: त्वं हि धारयिता श्रेष्ठः कुरूणां कुरुसत्तम। मिथ्या प्रचरतां तात बाह्येष्वाभ्यन्तरेषु च।॥
en: You, O best of Kuru race, being the foremost among them, bear the load of the Kurus when they behave, O Sire, deceitfully towards others or to members of their own family, when the deceit is actually done in act or when it is conceived.

sn: पुत्रास्तव कौरव्य दुर्योधनपुरोगमाः। धर्मार्थौ पृष्ठतः कृत्वा प्रचरन्ति नृशंसवत्॥
en: Those sons of yours, O Kaurava, headed by Duryodhana, are acting impiously setting aside all considerations of morality and earthly good.

sn: अशिष्टा गतमर्यादा लोभेन हृतचेतसः। स्वेषु बन्धुषु मुख्येषु तद् वेत्थ पुरुषर्षभ॥
en: Those wicked ones, whose self-respect is gone and whose hearts have been perverted by avarice (are acting unfairly) towards their own chief friends, O best of men.

sn: सेयमापन्महाघोरा कुरुष्वेव समुत्थिता। उपेक्ष्यमाणा कौरव्य पृथिवीं घातयिष्यति॥
en: This exceedingly grave has its rise among the Kurus and if regarded with indifference, it will destroy the whole earth, O Kaurava.

sn: शक्या चेयं शमयितुं त्वं चेदिच्छसि भारत। न दुष्करो ह्यत्र शमो मतो मे भरतर्षभ॥
en: If you desire so, O Bharata, this can be averted; in this instance peace is not hard to secure; such is my opinion, O best of the Bharatas.

sn: त्वय्यधीनः शमो राजन् मयि चैव विशाम्पते। पुत्रान् स्थापय कौरव्य स्थापयिष्याम्यहं परान्॥
en: Peace depends on you, o king and on myself as well, O lord of the universe. ) Kaurava, set right your sons and I shall the enemies (Pandavas) right.

sn: आज्ञा तव हि राजेन्द्र कार्या पुत्रैः सहान्वयैः। हितं बलवदप्येषां तिष्ठतां तव शासने॥
en: Your commands, O chief among kings, should be followed by your sons with their followers, and it will conduce exceedingly to their own good to act according to your orders.

sn: तव चैव हितं राजन् पाण्डवानामथो हितम्। शमे प्रयतमानस्य तव शासनकाक्षिणः॥
en: It will conduce to your good, O king and also to the good of the Pandavas, for you try to establish peace, desirous of ruling as you are.

sn: स्वयं निष्फलमालक्ष्य संविधत्स्व विशाम्पते। सहायभूता भरतास्तवैव स्युर्जनेश्वरः॥
en: Act for yourself after a consideration of the consequences, O lord of the universe and let the Bharatas be your allies O lord of men.

sn: धर्मार्थयोस्तिष्ठ राजन् पाण्डवैरभिरक्षितः। न हि शक्यास्तथाभूता यत्नादपि नराधिप॥
en: Protected by the Pandavas, Oking, establish morality and earthy good. O lord of men, by every exertion in your power, allies such as they, cannot be secured.

sn: न हि त्वां पाण्डवैर्जेतुं रक्ष्यमाणं महात्मभिः। इन्द्रोऽपि देवैः सहितः प्रसहेत कुतो नृपः॥
en: The great-souled sons of Pandu protecting you, even Indra with the gods cannot withstand you; how can earthy kings do it?

sn: यत्र भीष्मश्च द्रोणश्च कृपः कर्णो विविंशतिः। अश्वत्थामा विकर्णश्च सोमदत्तोऽथ बाह्निकः॥ सैन्धवश्च कलिङ्गश्च काम्बोजश्च सुदक्षिणः। युधिष्ठिरो भीमसेनः सव्यसाची यमौ तथा॥ सात्यकिश्च महातेजा युयुत्सुश्च महारथः। को नु तान् विपरीतात्मा युद्ध्येत भरतर्षभ॥
en: Against the side taken up by Bhishma, Drona, Kripa, Kripa, Vivingshati, Ashvathama, Vikarna, Somadatta, Bahlika the king of the Sindhus and the lord of the Kalingas, the chief of the Kambojas, Sudakshina, Yudhishthira, Bhimasena, Savyasachi and the twins and Satyaki of great energy and the great carwarrior Yuyutsu, who is there of such misdirected energy to fight, O you the best among the Bharatas.

sn: लोकस्येश्वरतां भूयः शत्रुभिश्चाप्यधृष्यताम्। प्राप्स्यसि त्वममित्रघ्न सहितः कुरुपाण्डवैः॥
en: The lordship over the word and the quality of being invincible by your foes, will you attain, O you slayer of enemies, when united with the Kurus and the Pandavas?

sn: तस्य ते पृथिवीपालास्त्वत्समाः पृथिवीपते। श्रेयांसश्चैव राजानः संधास्यन्ते परंतप॥
en: The rulers of the earth, of the same position as yourself, o lord of the earth and kings of better position even will seek to establish peace with you and with one another if you are so united.

sn: स त्वं पुत्रैश्च पौत्रेश्च पितृभिर्धातृभिस्तथा। सुहृद्धिः सर्वतो गुप्तः सुखं शक्ष्यसि जीवितुम्॥
en: You will be able to live in happiness being protected on all sides by your sons and grandsons, your fathers and brothers and friends.

sn: एतानेव पुरोधाय सत्कृत्य च यथा पुरा। अखिला भोक्ष्यसे सर्वां पृथिवीं पृथिवीपते॥
en: Keeping their interests well before you and treating them well, as in days gone by will you enjoy this entire earth, O lord of the earth.

sn: एतैर्हि सहितः सर्वैः पाण्डवैः स्वैश्च भारत। अन्यान् विजेष्यसे शत्रूनेष स्वार्थस्तवाखिलः॥
en: United with these and with all the Pandavas, O Bharata, will you win victories over other enemies; this is all to your own advantage.

sn: तैरेवोपार्जितां भूमि भोक्ष्यसे च परंतप। यदि सम्पत्स्यसे पुत्रैः सहामात्यैर्नराधिप॥
en: Territories acquired by them will you enjoy, O chastiser of enemies if you are allied to your sons, kinsmen and counselors, O lord of men.

sn: संयुगे वै महाराज दृश्यते सुमहान् क्षयः। क्षये चोभयतो राजन् कं धर्ममनुपश्यसि॥
en: In the case of a fight, O great king, you will see a great loss and in loss to both parties what meritorious deed do you see?

sn: पाण्डवैनिहतैः संख्ये पुत्रैर्वाऽपि महाबलैः। यद् विन्देथाः सुखं राजंस्तद् ब्रूहि भरतर्षभ॥
en: The Pandavas being killed in battle or your own sons of great strength, describe O great king the feelings that you will experience, O best of the Bharatas.

sn: शूराश्च हि कृतास्त्राश्च सर्वे युद्धाभिकाक्षिणः। पाण्डवास्तावकाश्चैव तान् रक्ष महतो भयात्॥
en: They are heroes who have mastered the use of weapons and all of them are desirous of war-these sons of Pandu and of yourself; save them from a great calamity,

sn: न पश्येम कुरून् सर्वान् पाण्डवाश्चैव संयुगे। क्षीणानुभयतः शूरान् रथिनो रथिभिर्हतान्॥
en: You will not see all the Kurus, nor all the Pandavas, in the event of a battle, the heroes on both sides being weakened in number and in strength and car-warriors slain by car-warriors.

sn: समवेताः पृथिव्यां हि राजानो राजसत्तम। अमर्षवशमापन्ना नाशयेयुरिमाः प्रजाः॥
en: The kings have assembled here, O best of kings; they will destroy these creatures, being influenced by wrath,

sn: त्राहि राजनिमं लोकं न नश्येयुरिमा: प्रजाः। त्वयि प्रकृतिमापन्ने शेष: स्यात् कुरुनन्दन॥
en: Rescue, O king, the world; do not destroy these creatures; yourself regaining your natural disposition all this will end, O delighted of the Kuru race.

sn: शुक्ला वदान्या ह्रीमन्त आर्याः पुण्याभिजातयः। अन्योन्यसचिवा राजस्तान् पाहि महतो भयात्॥
en: Coming from noble families, liberal and generous, endued with modesty, honourable, picus they are related to one another by blood, O king. Save them from a grave calamity.

sn: शिवेनेमे भूमिपाला: समागम्य परस्परम्। सह भुक्त्वा च पीत्वा च प्रतियान्तु यथागृहम्॥
en: These protectors of the earth meeting one another in a spirit of peace and having dined and drank together, let them return to their respective homes.

sn: सुवाससः स्रग्विणश्च सत्कृता भरतर्षभ। अमर्षं च निराकृत्य वैराणि च परंतप॥
en: With good robes on, with wreaths on and doing courtesies to one another, O best of the Bharata race; and with their wrath and enmity against one another plucked out (from their hearts), O chastiser of your foes.

sn: हार्दै यत् पाण्डवेष्वासीत् प्राप्तेऽस्मिन्नायुषः क्षये। तदेव ते भवत्वद्य संधत्स्व भरतर्षभ॥
en: Let the feelings of affection that you had for the Pandavas, return to you at the expiration of this age; and let them be the same to you; act it this way, O best of the Bharata race.

sn: बाला विहीनाः पित्रा ते त्वयैव परिवर्धिताः। तान् पालय यथान्यायं पुत्रांश्च भरतर्षभ।॥
en: As boys they lost their father and were raced and brought up by you; protect them in a way that would be in accordance with justice as you would do your sons, O best of the Bharata race.

sn: भवतैव हि रक्ष्यास्ते व्यसनेषु विशेषतः। मा ते धर्मस्तथैवार्थो नश्येत भरतर्षभ॥
en: By you they ought to be protected and especially when in distress. Let not your sense of virtue and appreciation of worldly good be lost, O best of the Bharata race.

sn: आहुस्त्वां पाण्डवा राजन्नभिवाद्य प्रसाद्य च। भवत: शासनाद् दुःखमनुभूतं सहानुगैः॥
en: The Pandavas, O king, having saluted and propitiated you, have sent you this message. 'At your command have we with our followers suffered misery.

sn: द्वादशेमानि वर्षाणि वने निर्युषितानि नः। त्रयोदशं तथाऽज्ञातैः सजने परिवत्सरम्॥
en: These twelve years have been spent by us in exile in the forest and the thirteenth year have we spent in each other's company in disguise.

sn: स्थाता नः समये तस्मिन् पितेति कृतनिश्चयाः। नाहास्म समयं तात तच्च नो ब्राह्मणा विदुः॥
en: Truly believing that our father would not break that pledge of his towards us, did we not break, O sire, our own. The Brahmanas who accompanied us know this.

sn: तस्मिन् नः समये तिष्ठ स्थितानां भरतर्षभ। नित्यं संक्लेशिता राजन् स्वराज्यांशं लभेमहि॥
en: Therefore do you abide by your pledge, as we have done ours, O best of the Bharata race; having long suffered grave troubles, O king, we desire to get the share of our own kingdom.

sn: त्वं धर्ममर्थं संजानन् सम्यड्नस्त्रातुमर्हसि। गुरुत्वं भवति प्रेक्ष्य बहून् क्लेशांस्तितिक्ष्महे॥
en: Knowing the principles of virtue and worldly good, it is your duty to save us; seeing that you are our elder, have we patiently suffered troubles.

sn: स भवान् मातृपितृवदस्मासु प्रतिपद्यताम्। गुरोर्गरीयसी वृत्तिर्या च शिष्यस्य भारत॥
en: Therefore do you act towards us as our father and mother; and treat us, O Bharata, according to the excellent principles that ought to be adopted by an elder.

sn: वर्तामहे त्वयि च तां त्वं च वर्तस्व नस्तथा। पित्रा स्थापयितव्या हि वयमुत्पथमास्थिताः॥
en: We act towards you in that way (the way in which younger should behave towards their elders); you also act towards us in the same way (the way in which elders should behave towards their youngers). If we follow the wrong way, then should we be set right by our father.

sn: संस्थापय पथिष्वस्मांस्तिष्ठ धर्मे सुवर्मनि। आहुश्चमां परिषदं पुत्रास्ते भरतर्षभ।॥
en: Set us in the proper path and follow yourself the excellent path of virtue.' And your sons, O best of the Bharata race, have sent this message to this assembly of kings.

sn: धर्मज्ञेषु सभासत्सु नेह युक्तमसाम्प्रतम्। यत्र धर्मो ह्यधर्मेण सत्यं यत्रानृतेन च॥
en: In an assembly conversant with the rules of virtue, nothing improper should happen (but in one) in which vice prevails over virtue or falsehood over truth.

sn: हन्यते प्रेक्षमाणानां हतास्तत्र सभासदः। विद्धो धर्मो ह्यधर्मेण सभां यत्र प्रपद्यते॥ न चास्य शल्यं कृन्तन्ति विद्धास्तत्र सभासदः। धर्म एतानारुजति यथा नद्यनुकूलजान्॥
en: If this happens with the knowledge of the members thereof, they are themselves slain; when virtue, pierced by vice, makes an appeal to an assembly and the shaft (of vice) is not taken out, the members thereof are themselves pierced by it. In fact virtue kills them like a river destroying the trees growing upon its banks.

sn: ये धर्ममनुपश्यन्तस्तूष्णीं ध्यायन्त आसते। ते सत्यमाहुर्धर्म्य च न्याय्यं च भरतर्षभ॥
en: Those, who are adopting a calm attitude and are silently waiting for virtue to assert itself, have said what is righteous, true and just, 0 best of the Bharata race.

sn: शक्यं किमन्यद् वक्तुं ते दानादन्यज्जनेश्वर। ब्रुवन्तु ते महीपालाः सभायां ये समासते॥
en: What else are you capable of saying to them than giving back their kingdom? Let the protectors of the earth who are assembled in this council, speak.

sn: धर्मार्थो सम्प्रधाव यदि सत्यं ब्रवीम्यहम्। प्रमुञ्चैमान् मृत्युपाशात् क्षत्रियान् पुरुषर्षभ॥
en: If I am speaking the truth, keeping in fact virtue and morality, then liberate these Kshatriyas from the shackles of death, O foremost among men.

sn: प्रशाम्य भरतश्रेष्ठ मा मन्युवशमन्वगाः। पित्र्यं तेभ्यः प्रदायांशं पाण्डवेभ्यो यथोचितम्॥
en: Be peaceful, O you foremost of the Bharata race and do not give in to anger. Having given back to those Pandavas, their due shares of the ancestral kingdom.

sn: ततः सपुत्रः सिद्धार्थो भुड्क्ष्व भोगान् परंतप। अजातशत्रु जानीषे स्थितं धर्मं सतां सदा॥
en: Enjoy the blessings of life, O chastiser of foes, along with your sons under the attainment of your objects. You know that Yudhishthira follows the course of virtue always.

sn: सपुत्रे त्वयि वृत्तिं च वर्तते यां नराधिप। दाहितश्च निरस्तश्च त्वामेवोपाश्रितः पुनः॥
en: As aiso (you know) his treatment towards yourself and your sons, O ruler of men. He was brunt and he was exiled but again he has come back to your protection.

sn: इन्द्रप्रस्थं त्वयैवासौ सपुत्रेण विवासितः। स तत्र विवसन् सर्वान् वशमानीय पार्थिवान्॥
en: He was exiled to Indraprastha by yourself with your sons and while staying there be ! brought under his sway all the rulers of the earth.

sn: त्वन्मुखानकरोद् राजन् न च त्वामत्यवर्तत। तस्यैवं वर्तमानस्य सौबलेन जिहीर्षता॥
en: And yet he remained under your protection and never disregarded you; such a man as he, was recently, sought to be robbed by the son of Subala.

sn: राष्ट्राणि धनधान्यं च प्रयुक्तः परमोपधिः। स तामवस्थां सम्प्राप्य कृष्णां प्रेक्ष्य सभागताम्॥
en: Of his kingdom, wealth and coin by means of a great deceit. He, even when he was brought to that condition, namely when Krishna was dragged to the Assembly-Hall.

sn: क्षत्रधर्मादमेयात्मा नाकम्पत युधिष्ठिरः। अहं तु तव तेषां च श्रेय इच्छामि भारत॥
en: Yudhishthira of immeasurable soul did not swerve from Kshatriya's duty. I too desire your good and theirs, OBharata.

sn: धर्मादर्थात् सुखाच्चैव मा राजन् नीनशः प्रजाः। नर्थमर्थं मन्वानोऽप्यर्थं नर्थमात्मनः॥
en: Do not, O king, destroy these beings of the birth for the sake of vice and earthy good for the sake of happiness thinking evil to be good and good to be evil for yourself.

sn: लोभेऽतिप्रसृतान् पुत्रान् निगृह्णीष्व विशाम्पते। स्थिताः शुश्रूषितुं पार्थाः स्थिता योद्धुमरिंदमा:। यत् ते पथ्यतमं राजेस्तस्मिस्तिष्ठ परंतप॥
en: Restrain your sons, O lord of the universe, who are too much attached to avarice. The sons of Pritha live to serve you and to fight for you, O chastiser of foes; whatever course, O king, appears better, follow, O chastiser of foes.”

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तद् वाक्यं पार्थिवाः सर्वे हृदयैः समपूजयन्। न तत्र कश्चिद् वक्तं हि वाचं प्राक्रामदग्रतः॥
en: Vaishampayana said All the rulers of the earth, agreeing as they did in their minds with these words, could not venture to say any thing there in the presence (of Duryodhana).

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तस्मिन्नभिहिते वाक्ये केशवेन महात्मना। स्तिमिता हृष्टरोमाण आसन् सर्वे सभासद ॥
en: Vaishampayana said These words having been uttered by the high-souled, all the courtiers sat stupefied with their hairs standing on their end.

sn: कश्चिदुत्तरमेतेषां वक्तुं नोत्सहते पुमान्। इति सर्वे मनोभिस्ते चिन्तयन्ति स्म पार्थिवाः॥
en: No man ventured to say anything in reply and all the rulers of the earth began to think in own minds.

sn: तथा तेषु च सर्वेषु तूष्णीम्भूतेषु राजसु। जामदग्न्य इदं वाक्यमब्रवीत् कुरूसंसदि॥
en: Silence having thus prevailed in the midst of those kings, the son of Jamadagni, spoke these words in the assembly of the Kurus.

sn: इमां मे सोपमां वाचं शृणु सत्यामशाङ्कितः। तां श्रुत्वा श्रेय आदत्स्व यदि साध्विति मन्यसे॥
en: "To these truthful words of mine, illustrated by an example, listen without entertaining any doubt or suspicion and hearing that accept the moral if you think my story good.

sn: राजा दम्भोद्भवो नाम सार्वभौमः पुराभवत्। अखिला बुभुजे सर्वां पृथिवीमिति नः श्रुतम्॥
en: in days of old, there was a king named Dambhodbhava who had brought under his sway the entire world and enjoyed the fruits of the whole world in their; such has been heard by us.

sn: स स्म नित्यं निशापाये प्रातरुत्थाय वीर्यवान्। ब्राह्मणान् क्षत्रियांश्चैव पृच्छन्नास्ते महारथः॥
en: Every day at the end or night, that great and heroic car-warrior, rising up, used to ask the Brahmanas and Krishna Kshatriyas.

sn: अस्ति कश्चिद् विशिष्टो वा मद्विधो वा भवेद् युधि। शूद्रो वैश्यः क्षत्रियो वा ब्राह्मणो वापि शस्त्रभृत्॥
en: 'Is there anybody who is more accomplished or even equal to myself in battle, be he a Shudra, a Vaishya, a Kshatriyas or a Brahmana?'

sn: इति ब्रुवन्नन्वचरत् स राजा पृथिवीमिमाम्। दर्पण महता मत्तः कंचिदन्यमचिन्तयन्॥
en: Saying thus he would wander over the earth intoxicated with great vanity and without thinking of anything else.

sn: तं च वैद्या अकृपणा ब्राह्मणाः सर्वतोऽभयाः। प्रत्यषेधन्त राजानं श्लाघमानं पुनः पुनः॥
en: Several Brahrnanas, of really noble souls, acquainted with the Vedas and having nothing lo fear, forbade the king who was boasting too often.

sn: निषिध्यमानोऽप्यसकृत् पृच्छत्येव स वै द्विजान्। अतिमानं श्रिया मत्तं तमूचुर्ब्राह्मणास्तदा॥
en: Even when forbidden, that vile man used to ask the same thing to the twice born. Some Brahmanas then thus spoke to him who was too puffed up with vanity and intoxicated with prosperity.

sn: तपस्विनो महात्मानो वेदप्रत्ययदर्शिनः। उदीर्यमाणं राजानं क्रोधदीप्ता द्विजातयः॥
en: Those twice born devotees, of large souls and acquainted with the cases cited in the Vedas, excited by wrath, said to that king.

sn: अनेकजयिनौ संख्यै यौ वै पुरुषसत्तमौ। तयोस्त्वं न समो राजन् भविताऽसि कदाचन।॥
en: There are two persons who are the best among men and who have achieved many victories in battle; you are by no means equal to them, Oking.

sn: एवमुक्तः स राजा तु पुनः पप्रच्छ तान् द्विजान्। क्व तौ वीरौ क्व जन्मानौ किंकर्माणौ च कौ च तौ।
en: The king thus spoken to, asked these Brahmanas again and again, 'Where are these two heroes? Where are they bom? What works have they achieved and who are they?'

sn: ब्राह्मणा ऊचुः नरो नारायणश्चैव तापसाविति नः श्रुतम्। आयातौ मानुषे लोके ताभ्यां युध्यस्व पार्थिव॥
en: The Brahmanas said WE have heard that those two are the devotees Nara and Narayana who have taken their birth in the human world. O ruler of the earth, fight with them.

sn: श्रूयेते तौ महात्मानौ नरनारायणावुभौ। तपो घोरमनिर्देश्य तप्यते गन्धमादने॥
en: We hear that both of them, Nara and Narayana of large souls, are practicing severe austerities in some hidden regions in the Gandhamadana (mountain).

sn: स राजा महतीं सेनां योजयित्वा षडङ्गिनीम्। अमृष्यमाणः सम्प्रायाद् यत्र तावपराजितौ॥
en: The king, having collected a large army consisting of six divisions be took himself to the regions where these two who had never to remain unconcerned at their reputation.

sn: स गत्वा विषमं घोरं पर्वतं गन्धमादनम्। मार्गमाणोऽन्वगच्छत् तौ तापसौ वनमाश्रितौ॥
en: He. going to the rightful and unapproachable Gandhamadana, hunted for the two devotees and at last met them who had taken refuge in the wilderness.

sn: तौ दृष्ट्वा क्षुत्पिपासाभ्यां कृशौ भमनिसन्ततौ। शीतवातातपैश्चैव कर्शितौ पुरुषोत्तमौ॥
en: Seeing them, the best among men, emaciated with hunger and thirst, with their veins visible and afflicted with cold, wind and with the rays of the sun.

sn: अभिगम्यौपसंगृह्य पर्यपृच्छदनामयम्। तमर्चित्वा मूलफलैरासनेनोदकेन च॥ न्यमन्त्रयेतां राजानं किं कार्य क्रियतामिति। ततस्तामानुपूर्वी स पुनरेवान्वकीर्तयत्॥
en: He approached them and touching their feet asked them about their welfare. They received him with roots and fruits and with the offer of a seat and water. They asked the king “What can we do for you?' Then he repeated to them from the very beginning the fact

sn: बाहुभ्यां मे जिता भूमिनिहताः सर्वशत्रवः। भवद्भ्यां युद्धमाकाङ्क्षन्नुपयातोऽस्मि पर्वतम्॥ आतिथ्यं दीयतोमेतत् काक्षितं मे चिरं प्रति।
en: And said-‘The earth has been conquered by my arms and all my enemies have been killed. With the desire of fighting with you, have I come to this mountain; give me this hospitality, the desire which I have entertained for a long time.'

sn: नरनारायणावूचतुः अपेतक्रोधलोभोऽयमाश्रमो राजसत्तम॥ न ह्यस्मिन्नाश्रमे युद्धं कुतः शस्त्रं कुतोऽनृजुः। अन्यत्र युद्धमाकाक्ष बहवः क्षत्रियाः क्षितौ॥
en: Nara and Narayana said This retreat, O best among kings, is beyond the reach of wrath and avarice, there is no warfare in this retreat. Where are weapons to be got from? Desire war elsewhere, there are many Kshatriyas on the face of the earth.

sn: राम उवाच उच्यमानस्तथापि स्म भूय एवाभ्यभाषत्। पुनः पुनः क्षम्यमाणः सान्त्व्यमानश्च भारत॥ दम्भोद्भवो युद्धमिच्छन्नाह्वयत्येव तापसौ।
en: Rama said Though spoken to in this way, he repeated his request and the ascetics, O Bharata, again and again comforted him and pardoned him (for his importunities). Dambhodbhava, desirous of battle, however summoned these two devotees to fight again and again.

sn: ततो नरस्त्विषीकाणां मुष्टिमादाय भारत।॥ अब्रवीदेहि युद्ध्यस्व युद्धकामुक क्षत्रिय। सर्वशस्राणि चादत्स्व योजयस्व च वाहिनीम्॥ अहं हि ते विनेष्यामि युद्धश्रद्धामितः परम्।
en: Then Nara taking up a handful of blades of grass said, 'Come and fight, O you Kshatriya, desirous of fight as you are; take up all your arms and prepare your army. I shall destroy your thirst for war from this moment forward.'

sn: दम्भोद्भव उवाच यद्येतदस्त्रमस्मासु युक्तं तापस मन्यसे॥ एतेनापि त्वया योत्स्ये युद्धार्थी ह्यहमागतः।
en: Dambhodbhava said If, O devotee, you think this weapon fit to be used against me and mine, I shall fight with you though you use that weapon. I am come here for fight.

sn: राम उवाच इत्युक्त्वा शरवर्षेण सर्वतः समवाकिरत्॥ दम्भोद्भवस्तापसं तं जिघांसुः सहसैनिकः।
en: Rama said Saying these Dambhodbhava with his army, desirous of killing that devotee, covered all sides with a downpour of arrows.

sn: तस्य तानस्यतो घोरानिषून परतनुच्छिदः :॥ कदर्थीकृत्य स मुनिरिषीकाभिः समार्पयत्।
en: The Rishi, by means of the same blades of grass, neutralized the terrible arrows capable of rending asunder the body of the enemies.

sn: ततोऽस्मै प्रासृजद् धोरमैषीकमपराजितः॥ अस्त्रमप्रतिसंधेयं तदद्भुतमिवाभवत्।
en: Then the one, who had never sustained a defeat, shot terrible weapons in the shape of blades of grass, which were incapable of being withstood and a strange effect they had.

sn: तेषामक्षीणि कर्णाश्च नासिकाश्चैव मायया॥ निमित्तवेधी स मुनिरिषीकाभिः समार्पयत्।
en: The eyes, ears and noses of his solders were cut off by the Muni who could not possibly miss his aim, by the e blades of grass through his illusive energy.

sn: स दृष्ट्वा श्वेतमाकाशमिषीकाभिः समाचितम्॥ पादयो→पतद् राजा स्वस्ति मेऽस्त्विति चाब्रवीत्।
en: Then seeing the sky rendered white with blades of grass, the king fell at Nara's feet and exclaimed-'May good betide me.'

sn: तमब्रवीनरो राजशरण्यः शरणैषिणाम्॥ ब्रह्मण्यो भव धर्मात्मा मा च स्मैवं पुन: कृथाः।
en: Nara, who is the proper refuge to those that deserve and desire protection, said to him 'O king, be virtuous-souled and act up to the instructions of the Brahmanas and do not again behave in this way.

sn: नैतादृक् पुरुषो राजन् क्षत्रधर्ममनुस्मरन्॥ मनसा नृपशार्दूल भवेत् परपुरंजयः।
en: A conqueror of cities, in the possession of his enemies, performing the duties of Kshatriya should not, Oking, be such even in his intentions, O best of the rulers of men.

sn: मा च दर्पसमाविष्टः क्षेप्सीः कांश्चित् कथंचन॥ अल्पीयांसं विशिष्टं वां तत् ते राजन् समाहितम्।
en: Subject to the influence of vanity never insult any body in any way, who he be, your inferior or your superior; such a conduct, O king, would not be proper for you.

sn: कृतप्रज्ञो वीतलोभो निरहंकार आत्मवान्॥ दान्तः क्षान्तो मृदुः सौम्यः प्रजाः पालय पार्थिवा मा स्म भूयः क्षिपे: कंचिदविदित्वा बलाबलम्॥
en: Acquiring wisdom, being beyond the reach of covetousness, without vanity, acquiring mastery over self, restraining your desires, endued with forgiveness, humility and being peaceful protect your subjects, O ruler of the carth and do not again insult any body with out knowing his strength and weakness.

sn: अनुज्ञातः स्वस्ति गच्छ मैवं भूयः समाचरेः। कुशलं ब्राह्मणान् पृच्छेरावयोर्वचनाद् भृशम्॥
en: May good betide you; with our permission depart and never again act in this way; in obedience to our command, enquire of the Brahmanas about their welfare and what is for your good.'

sn: ततो राजा तयोः पादावभिवाद्य महात्मनोः। प्रत्याजगाम स्वपुरं धर्मं चैवाचरद् भृशम्॥
en: Then the king, bowing to the feet of the two great-souled beings, returned to his own capital and thenceforward acted most righteously.

sn: सुमहच्चापि तत् कर्म यन्नरेण कृतं पुरा। ततो गुणैः सुबहुभिः श्रेष्ठो नारायणोऽभवत्॥
en: The deed, which was achieved by Nara in days of old, was very great indeed. Narayana was still greater in regard to many virtues.

sn: तस्माद् यावद् धनुःश्रेष्ठे गाण्डीवेऽस्त्रं न युज्यते। तावत् त्वं मानमुत्सृज्य गच्छ राजन् धनंजयम्॥
en: For that reason so long as weapons are not joined to that foremost of bows the Gandiva, putting aside your vanity go you, O king, to Dhananjaya.

sn: काकुदीकं शुकं नाकमक्षिसंतर्जनं तथा। संतानं नर्तकं घोरमास्यमोदकमष्टम्॥
en: Kakudika, Shuka, Naka, Akshisantarjana, Santana, Ghora and Asyamodaka-these eight types of weapons.

sn: एतैर्विद्धाः सर्व एव मरणं यान्ति मानवाः। कामक्रोधौ लोभमोहौ मदमानौ तथैव च॥ मात्सर्याहंकृती चैव क्रमादेत उदाहृताः।
en: Pierced by these all men go to the regions of death and the same is the case when they are influenced by desire, wrath, covetousness, vanity, insolence, pride, malice and selfishness. The eight weapons are represented by these vices respectively

sn: उन्मत्ताश्च विचेष्टन्ते नष्टसंज्ञा विचेतसः॥ स्वपन्ति च प्लवन्ते च छर्दयन्ति च मानवाः। मूत्रयन्ते च सततं रुदन्ति च हसन्ति च॥
en: By using these weapons men, struck with them, move about intoxicated, taking leave of their senses and with their minds bewildered. When pierced by them, men sleep, move about here and there, pass excrete and urine and always weep and laugh,

sn: निर्माता सर्वलोकानामीश्वरः सर्वकर्मवित्। यस्य नारायणो बन्धुरर्जुनो दुःसहो युधि॥
en: Arjuna, whose friend is Narayana, the creator of the entire world and its lord and conversant with the nature of all acts, is hard to withstand in battle.

sn: कस्तमुत्सहते जेतुं त्रिषु लोकेषु भारत। वीरं कपिध्वजं जिष्णुं यस्य नास्ति समो युधि॥
en: O Bharata, who can are defeat in the three worlds, the heroic Vishnu, having the emblem of a monkey on his banner and none equal to him in battle?

sn: असंख्येया गुणाः पार्थे तद्विशिष्टो जनार्दनः। त्वमेव भूयो जानासि कुन्तीपुत्र धनंजयम्॥
en: Innumerable are the virtues of the son of Pritha; Janardana excels him however. You know very well Dhananjaya the son of Kunti.

sn: नरनारायणौ यौ तौ तावेवार्जुनकेशवौ। विजानीहि महाराज प्रवीरौ पुरुषोत्तमौ॥
en: Nara and Narayana, as these two were, so are Arjuna and Keshava; know this O great king, that those two best among men are heroes.

sn: यद्येतदेवं जानासि न च मामभिशङ्कसे। आर्यां मतिं समास्थाय शाम्य भारत पाण्डवैः॥
en: If you know it to be so and do not suspect to mistrust me then adopting a virtuous resolution effect peace with the Pandavas.

sn: अथ चेन्मन्यसे श्रेयो न मे भेदो भवेदिति। प्रशाम्य भरतश्रेष्ठ मा च युद्धे मनः कृथाः॥
en: And if you think that a rupture with them is not beneficial to you, be peaceful, O foremost among the race of Bharata and do not set your heart on battle.

sn: भवतां च कुरुश्रेष्ठ कुलं बहुमतं भुवि। तत् तथैवास्तु भद्रं ते स्वार्थमेवोपचिन्तय॥
en: Your family, O foremost of the Kuru race, is well thought of in this world; let it continue to be so, may good betide you, think of what is good for you.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच जामदग्न्य वचः श्रुत्वा कण्वोऽपि भगवानृषिः। दुर्योधनमिदं वाक्यमब्रवीत् कुरुसंसदि॥
en: Vaishampayana said Hearing the words of the son of Jamadagni, the illustrious Rishi Kanva addressed these words to Duryodhana in the assembly of the Kurus.

sn: कण्व उवाच अक्षयश्चाव्ययश्चैव ब्रह्मा लोकपितामहः। तथैव भगवन्तौ तौ नरनारायणावृषी॥
en: Kanva said Brahma, the grand-father of this world, is eternal and undecaying; of the same nature are the two divine Rishis, Nara and Narayana.

sn: आदित्यानां हि सर्वेषां विष्णुरेकः सनातनः। अक्षय्यश्चाव्ययश्चैव शाश्वतः प्रभुरीश्वरः॥
en: Among all sons of Aditi, Vishnu alone is eternal, invincible, undecaying and the divine Lord existing forever.

sn: निमित्तमरणाश्चान्ये चन्द्रसूर्यौ मही जलम्। वायुरग्निस्तथाऽऽकाशं ग्रहास्तारागणास्तथा॥
en: The others namely the moon, the sun, the earth, the water, the air, the fire and also the sky, the planets and the stars have their end in a cause.

sn: ते च क्षयान्ते जगतो हित्वा लोकत्रयं सदा। क्षयं गच्छन्ति वै सरेवे सृज्यन्ते च पुनः पुनः॥
en: They, at the final dissolution of the universe, will themselves cease to exist, leaving behind the three worlds and all will be created again and again.

sn: मुहूर्तमरणास्त्वन्ये मानुषा मृगपक्षिणः। तैर्यग्योन्याश्च ये चान्ये जीवलोकचरास्तथा॥
en: Others there are that die in a short time, namely beings, animals, birds and creatures having their birth among other living beings.

sn: भूयिष्ठेन तु राजानः श्रियं भुक्त्वाऽऽयुषः क्षये। तरुणाः प्रतिपद्यन्ते भोक्तुं सुकृतदुष्कृते॥
en: The kings, enjoying great prosperity up to the end of their lives, are born anew to enjoy the effects of their good and bad deeds.

sn: स भवान् धर्मपुत्रेण शमं कर्तुमिहार्हति। पाण्डवाः कुरवश्चैव पालयन्तु वसुंधराम्॥
en: Therefore it is proper for your exalted self to effect peace with Yudhishthira. Let the Pandavas and the Kurus rule the universe.

sn: बलवानहमित्येव न मन्तव्यं सुयोधन। बलवन्तो बलिभ्यो हि दृश्यन्ते पुरुषर्षभ॥
en: "I am strong", it should not be thought thus, O Suyodhana, for some parties are seen who are stronger than those among men.

sn: न बलं बलिनां मध्ये बलं भवति कौरव। बलवन्तो हि ते सर्वे पाण्डवा देवविक्रमाः॥
en: Among the really strong, physical strength does not count, O son of Kuru and all the sons of Pandu, who are endued with the strength of the gods, are strong.

sn: अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। मातलेर्दातुकामस्य कन्या मृगयतो वरम्॥
en: In this connection is cited the old story of Matali who was desirous of giving away his daughter in marriage and was searching for a bridegroom.

sn: मतस्त्रैलोक्यराजस्य मातलि म सारथिः। तस्यैकैव कुले कन्या रूपतो लोकविश्रुता॥
en: Such is the story-The king of the three worlds had a driver by the name of Matali. In his family there was born only one daughter who had a great reputation for beauty in this world.

sn: गुणकेशीति विख्याता नाम्ना सा देवरूपिणी। श्रिया च वपुषा चैव स्त्रियोऽन्याः साऽतिरिच्यते॥
en: She, having celestial beauty, was well known by the name of Gunakeshi and she greatly excelled all women in beauty, physical development and symmetry.

sn: तस्याः प्रदानसमयं मातलिः सह भार्यया। ज्ञात्वा विममृशे राजंस्तत्परः परिचिन्तयन्॥
en: Matali, along with his wife knowing that the time for giving her away in marriage has arrived, became sorrowful, o king, thinking what to do in the future.

sn: धिकं खल्वलघुशीलानामुच्छ्रितानां यशस्विनाम्। नराणां मृदुसत्त्वानां कुले कन्याप्ररोहणम्॥
en: Alas! the advent of daughters in the family of men who are of good traditions and know for their greatness and are famous and endued with humility, is attended with bad consequences.

sn: मातुः कुलं पितृकुलं यत्र चैव प्रदीयते। कुलत्रयं संशयितं कुरुते कन्यका सताम्॥
en: The family of the mother, the family of the father and the family to which she is given away in marriage-these three families among good people are affected by a daughter.

sn: देवमानुषलोकौ द्वौ मानुषेणैव चक्षुषा। अवगाह्मैव विचितौ न च मे रोचते वरः॥
en: By my human eyes have I searched the two worlds, those of the celestial and human beings and there is no suitable husband for my daughter that pleases me.

sn: कण्व उवाच न देवान् नैव दितिजान् न गन्धर्वान् न मानुषान्। अरोचयद् वरकृते तथैव बहुलानृषीन्॥
en: Kanva said Among the gods, among those born in the Daitya race, among the Gandharvas and among human beings there was none who pleased him enough t be made the husband of his daughter. The same was the case with the numerous Rishis.

sn: भार्ययाऽनु स सम्मन्त्र्य सह रात्रौ सुधर्मया। मातलि गलोकाय चकार गमने मतिम्॥
en: Having consulted with his wife, Sudharma, at night (one day), Matali made up his mind to enter the world of the Nagas.

sn: न मे देवमनुष्येषु गुणकेश्याः समो वरः। रूपतो दृश्यते कश्चिन्नागेषु भविता ध्रुवम्॥
en: Matali said Among gods and men I d not find a suitable husband for Gunakeshi in point of beauty. There must be some one so suitable among the Nagas.

sn: इत्यामन्त्र्य सुधर्मा स कृत्वा चाभिप्रदक्षिणम्। कन्यां शिरस्युपाध्राय प्रविवेश महीतलम्॥
en: Thus thinking he bade adieu to Sudharma; and, going round his superiors and having smelt the head of his daughter entered the nether regions.

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: कण्व उवाच मातलिस्तु व्रजन् मार्गे नारदेन महर्षिणा। वरुणं गच्छता द्रष्टुं समागच्छद् यदृच्छया॥
en: Kanya said While Matali was proceeding on his way he came across the great Rishi Narada who was proceeding, of his own will, to see Varuna.

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: नारद उवाच नारदोऽथाब्रवीदेनं क्व भवान् गन्तुमुद्यतः। स्वेन वा सूत कार्येण शासनाद् वा शतक्रतोः॥
en: Narada said Where are you about to go? Is it, O charioteer, on your own account or by the command of Shatakratu (Indra)?

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: कण्व उवाच मातलिर्नारदेनैव सम्पृष्टः पथि गच्छता। यथावत् सर्वमाचष्ट स्वकार्यं नारदं प्रति॥
en: Kanva said Matali, being thus asked by Narada, who was going on the same road, told Narada all about his business and how it had happened (that he was going there).

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: तमुवाचाथ स मुनिर्गच्छावः सहिताविति। सलिलेशदिदृक्षार्थमहमप्युद्यतो दिवः॥
en: Then the Muni said to him, "We both shall go together." To see the god of the waters I too come down heaven.

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: अहं ते सर्वमाख्यास्ये दर्शयन् वसुधातलम्। दृष्ट्वा तत्र वरं कंचिद् रोचयिष्याव मातले॥
en: While showing you the nether regions of the earth, I shall describe to you everything; and after a search there we shall select some bridegroom, O Matali.

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: अवगाह्य तु तौ भूमिमुभौ मातलिनारदौ। ददृशाते महात्मानौ लोकपालमपां पतिम्॥
en: Then going down to the nether region, the two, Matali and Narada of large souls, paid their respects to the ruler of the word, the lord of the waters.

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: तत्र देवर्षिसदृशीं पूजां स प्राप नारदः। महेन्द्रसदृशीं चैव मातलिः प्रत्यपद्यत॥
en: There that Narada received greetings suitable for a divine Rishi and Matali received what is generally offered to the great Indra.

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: तावुभौ प्रीतमनसौ कार्यवन्ता निवेद्य ह। वरुणेनाभ्यनुज्ञातौ नागलोकं विचेरतुः॥
en: These two, with their minds pleased and having business in hand, submitted everything to their host and with the permission of Varuna roamed about in the world of the Nagas.

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: नारदः सर्वभूतानामन्तभूमिनिवासिनाम्। जानंश्चकार व्याख्यानं यन्तुः सर्वमशेषतः॥
en: Narada, who knew everything about all the creatures living in the nether regions, described them in detail to his companion.

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: नारद उवाच दृष्टस्ते वरुणः सूत पुत्रपौत्रसमावृतः। पश्योदकपते: स्थानं सर्वतोभद्रमृद्धिमत्॥
en: Narada said Varuna, surrounded by his sons and grandsons, has been seen by you o Suta. Behold now the territories of the lord of the waters which are excellent in every respect and full of riches.

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: एष पुत्रो महाप्रज्ञो वरुणस्येह गोपतेः। एष वै शीलवृत्तेन शौचेन च विशिष्यते॥
en: This one is the son, of great wisdom, of Varuna the lord of the seas; he is specially famous for his holiness, his conduct and his ways of life.

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: एषोऽस्य पुत्रोऽभिमतः पुष्करः पुष्करेक्षणः। रुपवान् दर्शनीयश्च सोमपुत्र्या वृतः पतिः॥
en: This is his dear son, Pushkara of eyes like lotus leaves. He is endued with beauty, is worth looking at and has been selected by the daughter of Soma as her husband.

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: ज्योत्स्नाकालीति यामाहुर्द्वितीयां रूपतः श्रियम्। अदित्याश्चैव यः पुत्रो ज्येष्ठः श्रेष्ठः कृतः स्मृतः॥
en: She (the daughter of Soma) is known as Jyotsnakali who has been said to be second Lakshmi or Sri in point of beauty; and she, it is within our recollection, had chosen the eldest son of Aditi as her husband (before this).

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: भवनं वारुणं पश्य यदेतत् सर्वकाञ्चनम्। यत् प्राप्य सुरतां प्राप्ताः सुराः सुरपतेः सखे॥
en: Behold this mansion of Varuna which is inade entirely of gold and attaining to which the gods have obtained their god-ship ( you friend of the lord of the gods.

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: एतानि हृतराज्यानां दैतेयानां स्म मातले। दीप्यमानानि दृश्यन्ते सर्वप्रहरणान्युत॥
en: These weapons of all kinds, which are now visible and which are blazing, were once in the possession of the Daityas, whose territories have been wrested from them (by Varuna), O Matali.

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: अक्षयाणि किलैतानि विवर्ततन्ते स्म मातले। अनुभावप्रयुक्तानि सुरैरवजितानि ह॥
en: These undergo no waste, O Matali and return to the hand of those who hurl them after striking the enemy. Obtained as they are by the gods who have won victories over the Daityas, they can be used only by men of great mental energy.

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: अत्र राक्षसजात्यश्च दैत्यजात्यश्च मातले। दिव्यप्रहरणाश्चासन् पूर्वदैवतनिर्मिताः॥
en: Here many species of Rakshasas and Daityas, O Matali, possessed of celestial weapons lived before, O Matali, which is now inhabited by the gods.

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: अग्निरेष महार्चिष्पाञ्जागर्ति वारुणे ह्रदे। वैष्णवं चक्रमाविद्धं विधूमेन हविष्मता॥
en: There are the fire of blazing flame which is burning in the lake of Varuna and the discus of Vishnu surrounded by the fire and smoke.

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: एष गाण्डीमयश्चापो लोकसंहारसम्भृतः। रक्ष्यते देवतैर्नित्यं यतस्तद गाण्डिवं धनुः॥
en: This is the bow, full of knots, which was created for the destruction of the world; it is ever looked after by the gods and from this the name of the Gandiva bow is derived.

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: एष कृत्ये समुत्पन्ने तत् तद् धारयते बलम्। सहस्रशतसंख्येन प्राणेन सततं ध्रुवः॥
en: This bow, at the approach of the proper time of action, is endued as it is with the strength of a hundred thousand bows, inspired with still greater strength.

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: अशास्यानपि शास्त्येष रक्षोबन्धुषु राजसु। सृष्टः प्रथमतश्चण्डो ब्रह्मणा ब्रह्मवादिना॥
en: It brings under subjugation those kings who are friendly to the Rakshasas, though they are incapable of being reduced to that condition. This terrible weapon was created first by the Brahmana who created in speech the Vedas.

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: एतच्छस्त्रं नरेन्द्राणां महच्चक्रेण भासितम्। पुत्राः सलिलरजास्य धारयन्ति महोदयम्॥
en: This weapon, in its work among the kings, has been pronounced to be the great by Shakra and the son of the lord of the waters hold this weapon of great energy.

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: एतत् सलिलराजस्यच्छत्रं छत्रगृहे स्थितम्। सर्वतः सलिलं शीतं जीमूत इव वर्षति॥
en: This thing, placed in the umbrella room, is the umbrella of the lord of the waters and always showers cold water like the clouds.

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: एतच्छत्रात् परिभ्रष्टं सलिलं सोमनिर्मलम्। तमसा मूर्छितं भाति येन नार्छति दर्शनम्॥
en: The water, falling from this umbrella, is pure as the moon and yet is surrounded by such darkness that it cannot be grasped by the sight.

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: बहून्यद्भुतरूपाणि द्रष्टव्यानीह मातले। तव कार्यावरोधस्तु तस्माद् गच्छाव मा चिरम्॥
en: In these regions, O Matali, there are many things to be seen, but owing to the pressing demands of your business we shall go away from here without delay.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: नारद उवाच एतत् तु नागलोकस्य नाभिस्थाने स्थितं पुरम्। पातालमिति विख्यातं दैत्यदानवसेवितम्॥
en: Narada said This city, situated in the very heart of the region of the Nagas, is known as Patalam, inhabited by the Daityas and Danavas.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: इदमद्भिः समं प्राप्ता ये केचिद् भुवि जङ्गमाः। प्रविशन्तो महानादं नदन्ति भयपीडिताः॥
en: The few creatures of the earth, who are brought here by the current of the water, when entering the region give out loud shrieks being struck with fear.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: अत्रासुरोऽग्निः सततं दीप्यते वारिभोजनः। व्यापारेण धृतात्मानं निबद्धं समबुध्यत॥
en: In these regions, the fire, called Asura fire, which is fed by water, continually blazes forth. Held in great respect, it regards itself as confined (by the gods).

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: अत्रामृतं सुरैः पीत्वा निहितं निहतारिभिः। अतः सोमस्य हानिश्च वृद्धिश्चैव प्रदृश्यते॥
en: Here the gods, who had slain their enemies, having drunk the nectar kept the residue there. It is from here proceed the growth and decline of the moon, which we see.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: अत्रादित्यो हयशिराः काले पर्वणि पर्वणि। उत्तिष्ठति सुवर्णाख्यो वाग्भिरापूरयञ्जगत्॥
en: Here the son of Aditi, with his head like that of the horse, on every festive occasion, rises up, making the world, called Suvarna, filled with the sound of Vedic hymns and mantras.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: यस्मादलं समस्तास्ताः पतन्ति जलमूर्तयः। तस्मात् पातालमित्येव ख्यायते पुरमुत्तमम्॥
en: Since all those objects, having the form of water, fall on it; therefore is this excellent region known by the name of Patalam.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: ऐरावणोऽस्मात् सलिलं गृहीत्वा जगतो हितः। मेघेष्वामुञ्चते शीतं यन्महेन्द्रः प्रवर्षति॥
en: Airavata, taking up cold water from here for the good of the world, gives them to the clouds and the great Indra showers this water as rain.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: अत्र नानाविधाकारास्तिमयो नैकरूपिणः। अप्सु सोमप्रभां पीत्वा वसन्ति जलचारिणः॥
en: Here aquatic animals of many species and shapes and fishes of different sorts, such as Timi and others, live, subsisting on a drink from the water which is like the beams of the moon.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: अत्र सूर्यांशुभिर्भिन्नाः पातालतलमाश्रिताः। मृता हि दिवसे सूत पुनर्जीवन्ति वै निशि॥
en: Some beings, living in this nether world, the Patalam, pierced by the rays of the sun, are dead in the day time, O Suta and are revived again at night.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: उदयन् नित्यशश्चात्र चन्द्रमा रश्मिबाहुभिः। अमृतं स्पृश्य संस्पर्शात् संजीवयति देहिनः॥
en: For the moon, rising in these regions every night, by her beams which are her arms as it were, brings nectar in contact with them; and from that are the creatures revived.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: अन्ने तेऽधर्मनिरता बद्धाः कालेन पीडिताः। दैतेया निवसन्ति स्म वासवेन हतश्रियः॥
en: Here are iroprisoned these wicked and unrighteous sons of Diti afflicted with misfortune. They live here being dispossessed of their prosperity by Vasava.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: अत्र भूतपतिर्नाम सर्वभूतमहेश्वरः। भूतये सर्वभूतानामचरत् तप उत्तमम्॥
en: Here the great Lord of all creatures, by name Bhutpati, practiced austere asceticism for the good of all creatures.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: अत्र गोवतिनो विप्राः स्वाध्यायम्नायकर्शिताः। त्यक्तप्राण जितस्वर्गा निवसन्ति महर्षयः॥
en: Here live the great Rishis those Brahmanas attached to the vow, called go, who have been emaciated with the recitation of the Vedas and who abandoning the pleasures of this life have secured heaven.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: यत्रतत्रशयो नित्यं येन केनचिदाशितः। पेन केनचिदाच्छन्नः स गोव्रत इहोच्यते॥
en: He, who ever sleeps at any place he likes, who lives on with what others place before him, is safe to be attached to the Go vows in this world.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: ऐरावणो नागराजो वामनः कुमुदोञ्जनः। प्रसूताः सुप्रतीकस्य वंशे वारणसत्तमाः॥
en: Here in the race of Supratika are born those best among elephants, namely Airavana, the king among elephants, Kumuda, Vamana and Arjuna.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: पश्य यद्यत्र ते कश्चिद् रोचते गुणतो वरः। वरयिष्यामि तं गत्वा यत्नमास्थाय मातले॥
en: See if in these regions there is any bridegroom who pleases you by his accomplishments. If so, I shall, after respectfully going to him, solicit him to accept your daughter, O Matali.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: अण्डमेतज्जले न्यस्तं दीप्यमानमिव श्रिया। आ प्रजानां निसर्गाद् नै नोद्भिद्यति न सर्पति॥
en: This one, placed here in these waters, is an egg, which is shining as it were with beauty. From the very creation of this universe it is here; and it neither moves away, nor is hatched.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: नास्य जाति निसर्ग वा कथ्यमानं शृणोमि वै। पितरं मातर चापि नास्य जानाति कश्चन॥
en: I have never heard of its species or birth spoken of. No body knows any one as its father or mother.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: अतः किल महानग्निरन्तकाले समुत्थितः। धक्ष्यते मातले सर्वं त्रैलोक्यं सचराचरम्॥
en: From this, at the time of the dissolution of the universe, springs up a fire, which consumes, O Matali, the three entire worlds with all their mobile and immobile creatures.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: मातलिस्त्वब्रवीच्छ्रुत्वा नारदस्याथ भाषितम्। न मेऽत्र रोचते कश्चिदन्यतो व्रज माचिरम्॥
en: Matali too having heard what Narada said, answered-“None in these regions pleases me. Let me go elsewhere without delay.”

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: नारद उवाच हिरण्यपुरमित्येतत् ख्यात् पुरवरं महत्। दैत्यानां दानवानां च मायाशतविचारिणाम्॥
en: Narada said This excellent and spacious city is known by the name of Hiranyapura. It is the city of the Daityas and the Danavas, who practice a hundred different illusions,

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: अनल्पेन प्रयत्नेन निर्मितं विश्वकर्मणा। मयेन मनसा सृष्टं पातालतलमाश्रितम्॥
