en: It having been built with no little care by the divine architect (Vishvakarama) and planned by Maya (Danava) was placed in these nether regions-the Patalam.

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: अत्र मायासहस्राणि विकुर्वाणा महौजसः। दानवा निवसन्ति स्म शूरा दत्तवराः पुरा॥
en: Here the Danavas, endued with great spirit and energy, practicing a thousand kind of different illusions, inhabit. They were, in the days of old, heroes who had received the grant of boons.

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: नैते शक्रेण नान्येन यमेन वरुणेन वा। शक्यन्ते वशमानेतुं तथैव धनदेन च।।४!
en: By Shakra, by Yama or by Varuna or by any body clse they were incapable of being brought inder subjugation; as also by the Lord of wealth (Kubera).

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: असुराः कालखञ्जाश्च तथा विष्णुपदोद्भवाः॥ नैर्ऋता यातुधानाश्च ब्रह्मपादोद्भवाश्च ये॥ दंष्ट्रिणो भीमवेगाश्च वातवेगपराक्रमाः। मायावीर्योपसम्पन्ना निवसन्त्यत्र मातले॥
en: The Asuras, known as Kalakhanjas who have their origin in the feet of Vishnu and the Rakshasas, known as Yatudhanas who have their origin in the feet of Brahma, gifted with teeth and of fearful impetus and endued with strength equal to the force of the wind and with the heroism of illusion, live here, O Matali.

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: निवातकवचा नाम दानवा युद्धदुर्मदाः। जानासि च यथा शक्रो नैताशक्नोति बाधितुम्॥
en: The Danavas named Nivatkavachas, who are hard to be vanquished in battle (also live here.) You know how Shakra is not able to cope with them.

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: बहुशो मातले त्वं च तव पुत्रश्च गोमुखः। निर्भग्नो देवराजश्च सहपुत्रः शचीपतिः॥
en: Yourself and your son Gomukha, O Matali and the king of the gods, the lord of Sachi, with his son, have been repulsed by them.

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: पश्य वेश्मानि रौक्माणि मातले राजतानि च। कर्मणा विधियुक्तेन युक्तान्युपगतानि च॥
en: See these mansions, O Matali, made of gold and silver and embroidered with suitable workmanship filled up according to their scientific principles.

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: वैदूर्यमणिचित्राणि प्रवालरुचिराणि च। अर्कस्फटिकशुभ्राणि वज्रसारोज्ज्वलानि च।॥
en: Decorated with Vaidurya-gems and with corals and with the species of white marble, called Arka and with the shining gems, called Vajrasara,

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: पार्थिवानीव चाभान्ति पद्मरागमयानि च। शैलानीव च दृश्यन्ते दारवाणीव चाप्युत॥
en: They shine as if, made of bricks and set with Padmaraga gems, and they look as if made of stones or of wood.

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: सूर्यरूपाणि चाभान्ति दीप्ताग्निसदृशानि च। मणिजालविचित्राणि प्रांशूनि निबिडानि च॥
en: They are lustrous like the rays of the sun; and are blazing like the fire and set with cluster of gems and precious stones; they are high and stand close to one another.

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: नैतानि शक्यं निर्देष्टुं रूपतो द्रव्यतस्तथा। गुणतश्चैव सिंद्धानि प्रमाणगुणवन्ति च॥
en: All these are incapable of being described with reference to their beauty, to with reference to the materials they are made of. They are erected with many advantages and comforts; and they have answered these objects very well. They are of a large size.

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: आक्रीडान् पश्य दैत्यानां तथैव शयनान्युत। रत्लवन्ति महार्हाणि भाजनान्यासनानि च॥
en: Look at the sporting grounds of the Daityas; and look at the resting places and beds, as also these vessels and seats set with gems and of great value.

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: जलदाभांस्तथा शैलांस्तोयप्रस्रवणानि च। कामपुष्पफलांश्चापि पादपान् कामचारिणः॥
en: Look at these walls which are like masses of clouds; and these fountains of water and also the trees producing flowers and fruits at their will, which can also be removed from one place to another at their pleasure.

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: मातले कश्चिदत्रापि रुचिरस्ते वरो भवेत्। अथवान्यां दिशं भूमेर्गच्छाव यदि मन्यसे॥
en: See, O Matali, in these regions if there is a bridegroom who is to your liking or else we shall go to another direction of this earth.

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: मातलिस्त्वब्रवीदेनं भाषमाणं तथाविधम्। देवर्षे नैव मे कार्य विप्रियं त्रिदिवौकसाम्॥
en: Matali then said to him who spoke thus, "O celestial Rishi, I cannot do what would not be to the liking of the dwellers of the heaven.

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: नित्यानुषक्तवैरा हि भ्रातरो देवदानवाः। परपक्षण सम्बन्धं रोचयिष्याम्यहं कथम्॥
en: The gods and the Danavas, though brothers, are in open enmity with each other and how can I approve of an alliance with the enemies.

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: अन्यत्र साधु गच्छाव द्रष्टुं नार्हामि दानवान्। जानामि तव चात्मानं हिंसात्मकमनं तथा॥
en: It is better that we should go elsewhere. It is not proper that we should seek among the Danavas. I know your nature and know that you desire to sow discord."

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: नारद उवाच अयं लोकः सुपर्णानां पक्षिणां पन्नगाशिनाम्। विक्रमे गमने भारे नैषामस्ति परिश्रमः॥
en: Narada said This region belongs to the birds of excellent feathers which subsist on snakes. They feel no fatigue in showing their strength in traveling or in carrying loads.

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: वैनतेयसुतैः सूत षड्भिस्ततमिदं कुलम्। सुमुखेन सुनाम्ना च सुनेत्रेण सुवर्चसा॥ सुरुचा पक्षिराजेन सुबलेन च मातले। वर्धितानि प्रसृत्या वै विनताकुलकर्तृभिः॥ पक्षिराजाभिजात्यानां सहस्राणि शतानि च। कश्यपस्य ततो वंशे जातैर्भूतिविवर्धनैः॥
en: This species, O Suta, proceed from the six sons of Vainateya (Garuda)-Sumukha, Sunamana, Sunetra, Suvarchas and from the king of birds, Surucha and from Subala; O Matali, they have multiplied from the race of Vinata. Hundreds and thousands of birds, all of noble blood, have founded dynasties by means of begetting children in the race of Kashyapa.

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: सर्वे ह्येते श्रिया युक्ताः सर्वे श्रीवत्सलक्षणाः। सर्वे श्रियमभीप्सन्तो धारयन्ति बलान्युत॥
en: All these are endued with prosperity; and all have the mark of Srivatsa (an auspicious mark); and all of them, desirous of prosperity, are endued with strength.

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: कर्मणा क्षत्रियाश्चैते निघृणा भोगिभोजिनः। ज्ञातिसंक्षयकर्तृत्वाद् ब्राह्मण्यं न लभन्ति वै॥
en: By their habits of life they are Kshatriyas; but as they live on snakes, they are without humanity; and owing to their constant warfare with their kinsmen they never attain to the region of Brahma.

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: नामानि चैषां वक्ष्यामि यथा प्राधान्यतः शृणु। मातले श्लाध्यमेतद्धि कुलं विष्णुपरिग्रहम्॥
en: I shall describe their names according to their rank; hear, O Matali. This race is much thought of in consequence of the favor which Vishnu shows to it.

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: दैवतं विष्णुरेतेषां विष्णुरेव परायणम्। हृदि चैषां सदा विष्णुर्विष्णुरेव सदा गतिः॥
en: Vishnu is their god; and their object of worship, Vishnu, is ever in their heart; and Vishnu is ever their refuge.

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: सुवर्णचूडो नागाशी दारुणश्चण्डतुण्डकः। अनिलश्चानलश्चैव विशालाक्षोऽथ कुण्डली॥ पङ्कजिद् वज्रविष्कम्भो वैनतेयोऽथ वामनः। वातवेगो दिशाचक्षुर्निमेषोऽनिमिषस्तथा॥ त्रिराव: सप्तरावश्च वाल्मीकिर्दीपकस्तथा। दैत्यद्वीपः सरिद्वीपः सारसः पद्मकेतनः॥ सुमुखश्चित्रकेतुश्च चित्रबर्हस्तथाऽनघः। मेषहत् कुमुदो दक्षः सर्पान्तः सहभोजनः॥ गुरुभारः कपोतश्च सूर्यनेत्रश्चिरान्तकः। विष्णुधर्मा कुमारश्च परिबर्हो हरिस्तथा॥ सुस्वरो मधुपर्कञ्च हेमवर्णस्तथैव च। लयो मातरिश्वा च निशाकरदिवाकरौ॥ एते प्रदेशमात्रेण मयोक्ता गरुडात्मजाः। प्राधान्यतस्ते यशसा कीर्तिताः प्राणिनश्च ये॥
en: Suvarnachuda, Nagashi, Daruna, Chandatundaka, Anila, Anala, Vishalaksha and Kundali, Pankajita, Vajravishkambha, Vainateya, Vamanas, Vatavega, Dishachakshu, Nimesha and Animesha, Trirava, Saptarava, Valmiki and Dvipaka, Daityadvipa, Saridvipa, Sarasa and Padmaketana, Sumukha, Chitraketu, Chitrabarha, Anagha, Meshahrita, Kumuda, Daksha, Sarpanta and Sahabhojana, Gurubhara, Kapota, Suryanetra, Chirantaka, Vishnudharma, Kumara, Paribarha and Hari, Susvara, Masduparka, Hemavarna, Malaya, Matarishva, Nishakara and Divakara, these descendants of Garuda, spoken of by me, inhabit a single province; and only these beings are foremost in fame and renown.

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: यद्यत्र न रुचिः काचिदेहि गच्छाव मातले। तं नयिष्यामि देशं त्वां वरं यत्रोपलप्स्यसे।॥
en: If nobody, in these regions, is to your liking, O Matali, then come, we shall go elsewhere and lead you to that country where you will get a bridegroom.

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: नारद उवाच इदं रसातलं नाम सप्तमं पृथिवीतलम्। यत्रास्ते सुरभिर्माता गवाममृतसम्भवा॥
en: Narada said The name of this (region) is Rasatala which is the seventh region in the nether regions of the earth, where lives Surabhi, the mother of cows, who was born out of nectar.

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: क्षरन्ती सततं क्षीरं पृथिवीसारसंभवम्। षण्णां रसानां सारेण रसमेकमनुत्तमम्॥
en: She always distills milk which is produced from the essence of earthly things-which is of the one taste, having nothing superior to it, constituted of the essence of the six different tastes.

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: अमृतेनाभितृप्तस्य सारमुद्रितः पुरा। पितामहस्य वदनादुदतिष्ठदनिन्दिता॥
en: Surabhi, having no defect, herself rose from the mouth of the Grandfather, who satiated with nectar, was in days of old, vomiting the essence of all things.

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: यस्याः क्षीरस्य धाराया निपतन्त्या महीतले। ह्रदः कृतः क्षीरनिधिः पवित्रं परमुच्यते॥
en: One stream, even of whose milk, having fallen on the face of the earth made a lake which is called the excellent and holy sea-milk.

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: पुष्पितस्येव फेनेन पर्यन्तमनुवेष्टितम्। पिबन्तो निवसन्त्यत्र फेनपा मुनिसत्तमाः॥
en: The limit of the sea is surrounded by foam which looks like flowers and here live those best among Munis-the drinkers of foam, drinking it.

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: फेनपा नाम ते ख्याताः फेनाहाराश्च मातले। उचे तपसि वर्तन्ते येषां बिभ्यति देवताः॥
en: They are known as drinkers of foam, O Matali, who practice austere asceticism and of whom the gods are afraid.

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: अस्याश्चतस्रो धेन्वोऽन्या दिक्षु सर्वासु मातले। निवसन्ति दिशां पाल्यो धारयन्त्यो दिशः स्म ताः॥
en: She has got four calves, O Matali which are in the several cardinal points for they bear the load of these points.

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: पूर्वां दिशं धारयते सुरूपा नाम सौरभी। दक्षिणां हंसिका नाम धारयत्यपरां दिशम्॥
en: The child of Surabhi, named Surupa supports the eastern point and the one named Hansika supports another point-the south.

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: पश्चिमा वारुणी दिक् च धार्यते व सुभद्रया। महानुभावया नित्यं मातले विश्वरूपया।॥
en: The western point, under the protection of Varuna, is supported by Subhadra who is ever of a great nature and of a universal foam.

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: सर्वकामदुधा नाम धेनुर्धारयते दिशम्। उत्तरां मातले धा तथैलविसंज्ञिताम्॥
en: The cow, named Sarvakamadugha, supports another point, O Matali, which is the direction in which virtue rules and so named after Kubera the God of wealth.

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: आसां तु पयसा मिश्रं पयो निर्मथ्य सागरे। मन्थानं मन्दरं कृत्वा देवैरसुरसंहितैः॥ उद्धृता वारुणी लक्ष्मीरमृतं चापि मातले। उच्चैःश्रवाश्चाश्वराजो मणिरत्नं च कौस्तुभम्॥
en: The gods united with the Asuras, having churned the water of the ocean, mixed with milk, making the Mandara (mountain) their churning rod, extracted the Varuni wine, Lakshmi (the goddess of beauty and wealth) and nectar, O Matali and also the best of horses, Uchchaishrava and that gem Kaustubha.

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: सुधारहारेषु च सुधां स्वधाभोजिषु च स्वधाम्। अमृतं चामृताशेषु सुरभी क्षरते पयः॥
en: Surabhi yields milk that is Sudha to those that live on Sudha and Svadha to those who subsist on Svadha and Amrita to those who feed on Amrita.

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: अत्र गाथा पुरा गीता रसातलनिवासिभिः। पौराणी श्रूयते लोके गीयते या मनीषिभिः॥
en: The song, that was sung here in days of old by the inhabitants of Rasatala, is still heard to be sung in this world by wise men.

description: The search of bridegroom by Matali
sn: न नागलोके स्वर्गे न विमाने त्रिविष्टपे। परिवासः सुखस्तादृक् रसातलतले यथा॥
en: "Neither in the region of the Nagas, nor in Svarga, nor in Vimana, nor in Trivistapa (all names for heaven) is residence so happy as in the nether regions."

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: नारद उवाच इयं भोगवती नाम पुरी वासुकिपालिता। यादृशी देवराजस्य पुरीवर्याऽमरावती॥
en: Narada said This city is named Bhogavati, ruled by Vasuki, which is similar to the city of the king of the gods-Amaravati.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: एष शेषः स्थितो नागो येनेयं धार्यते सदा। तपसा लोकमुख्येन प्रभावसहिता मही॥
en: This one staying here is Shesha the Naga, by whom is ever upheld the earth with all her greatness by force of his austerities which is the best in this world.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: श्वेताचलनिभाकारो दिव्याभरणभूषितः। सहस्रं धारयन् मूर्धा ज्वालाजिह्वो महाबलः॥
en: His body is of the size of the Shvetachala or white mountain and decked with diverse sorts of ornaments and holding a thousand heads with tongues like blazing fire. His strength and prowess are great.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: इह नानाविधाकारा नानाविधविभूषणाः। सुरसायाः सुता नागा निवसन्ति गतव्यथाः॥
en: Here live, passed the reach of pain, the sons of Surasa, Nagas, of many species and sizes and with diverse sorts of ornaments.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: मणिस्वस्तिकचक्राङ्काः कमण्डलुकलक्षणाः। सहस्रसंख्यां बलिनः सर्वे रौद्रा: स्वभावतः॥
en: And having the mark of gem, Svastika, circles and Kamandulu-all of them, each with the strength of a thousand, are by nature fierce.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: सहस्रशिरसः केचित् केचित् पञ्चशताननाः। शतशीर्षास्तथा केचित् केचित् त्रिशिरसोऽपि च॥
en: Some of them are thousand headed, some have five hundred faces, some, again, have a hundred heads and some three.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: द्विपञ्चशिरसः केचित् केचित् सप्तमुखास्तथा। महाभोगा महाकायाः पर्वताभोगभोगिनः॥
en: Some have twice five heads, some have seven faces and all of them are addicted to great pleasures and have huge bodies resembling the mountains of this earth.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: बहूनीह सहस्राणि प्रयुतान्यर्बुदानि च। नागानामेकवंशानां यथाश्रेष्ठं तु मे शृणु॥
en: There are many thousands and millions and hundreds of millions of unaccountable Nagas, listen to me as I say the few names of the foremost among them of a single race.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: वासुकिस्तक्षकश्चैव कर्कोटकधनंजयौ।। कालियो नहुषश्चैव कम्बलाश्वतरावुभौ॥ बाह्यकुण्डो मणि गस्तथैवापूरणः खगः। वामनश्चैलपत्रश्च कुकुरः कुकुणस्तथा॥ आर्यको नन्दकश्चैव तथा कलशपोतकौ। कैलासकः पिञ्जरको नागश्चैरावतस्तथा॥ सुमनोमुखो दधिमुखः शङ्खो नन्दोपनन्दकौ। आप्तः कोटरकश्चैव शिखी निष्ठुरिकस्तथा॥ तित्तिरिर्हस्तिभद्रश्च कुमुदो माल्यपिण्डकः। द्वौ पद्मौ पुण्डरीकश्च पुष्पो मुद्गरपर्णकः॥ करवीरः पीठरकः संवृत्तो वृत्त एव च। पिण्डारो बिल्वपत्रश्च मूषिकादः शिरीषकः॥ दिलीपः शङ्खशीर्शश्च ज्योतिष्कोऽथापराजितः। कौरव्यो धृतराष्ट्रश्च कुहुरः कृशकस्तथा॥ विरजा धारणश्चैव सुबाहुर्मुखरो जयः। बधिरान्धौ विशुण्डिश्च विरसः सुरसस्तथा॥ एते चान्ये च बहवः कश्यपस्यात्मजाः स्मृताः। मातले पश्य यद्यत्र कश्चित् ते रोचते वरः॥
en: They are Vasuki, Takshaka, Karkotaka, Dhananjaya, Kalia and the two, Kambala and Ashvatara, Bahyakunda, Mani, Apurana, Khaga, Vamana, Elapatra, Kukura, Kukuna, Aryaka, Nandaka, Potaka, Kailasaka, Pinjaraka and the Naga Airavata, Sumanmukha. Dadhimukha, Shankha, Nanda, Upanandaka, Apta, Kotaraka, Shikhi and Nisthuraka, Tittiri, Hastibhadra, Kumuda, Malyapindaka, the two Padmas, Pundarika, Pushpa, Mudgaraparnaka, Karavira, Pitharaka, Samvrita, Virtta, Pindara, Mushikada, Shirishaka, Dilipa, Shankhashirsha, Joytishka, Aparajita, Kauravya, Dhritarashtra, Kuhura Krishna, Virajas, Daharana, Subahu, Mukhara, Jaya, Badhira, Andha, Vishundi, Virasa and Surasa, these and many others are known to the son of Kashyapa, O Matali; see if in the region any bridegroom is to your liking.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: कण्व उवाच मातलिस्त्वेकमव्यग्रः सततं संनिरीक्ष्य वै। पप्रच्छ नारदं तत्र प्रीतिमानिव चाभवत्॥
en: Kanva said While Narada was speaking, Matali had been gazing steadfastly; and he asked Narada being highly pleased.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: स्थितो य एष पुरतः कौरव्यस्यार्यकस्य तु। द्युतिमान् दर्शनीयश्च कस्यैष कुलनन्दनः॥
en: This one standing before Aryaka of the Kauravya race-this effulgent being worthy to look at-whose race dose he delight?

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: कः पिता जननी चास्य कतमस्यैष भोगिनः। वंशस्य कस्यैष महान् केतुभूत इव स्थितः॥
en: Who is his mother and what race dose he come from? Of what race dose he stand like the flagstaff?

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: प्रणिधानेन धैर्येण रूपेण वयसा च मे। मनः प्रविष्टो देवर्षे गुणकेश्याः पतिर्वरः॥
en: By his intelligence, patience, beauty and age is my heart attracted, O divine Rishi. He will make husband for Gunakeshi.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: कण्व उवाच मातलिं प्रीतमनसं दृष्ट्वा सुमुखदर्शनात्। निवेदयामास तदा माहात्म्यं जन्म कर्म च॥
en: Kanya said Seeing Matali, of cheerful mind owing to his seeing Sumukha, Narada informed him the greatness, the birth and the works of that youth.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: नारद उवाच ऐरावतकुले जात: सुमुखो नाम नागराट्। आर्यकस्य मतः पौत्रो दौहित्रो वामनस्य च॥
en: Narad said Born in the race of Airavata, he is the chief of the Nagas, named Sumukha, the grandson of Aryaka and on his mother's side he is the grandson of Vamana.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: एतस्य हि पिता नागश्चिकुरो नाम मातले। नचिराद् वैनतेयेन पञ्चत्वमुपपादितः॥
en: His father is the Naga named Chikura, O Matali and quite recently he was killed by the son of Vinata.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: ततोऽब्रवीत् प्रीतमना मातलि रदं वचः। एष मे रुचितस्तात जामाता भुजगोत्तमः॥
en: Then did Matali, being of heart, speak to Narada these words-'O Sire, this best of the Naga race selected son-in-law.'

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: क्रियतामत्र यत्नो वै प्रीतिमानस्यनेन वै। अस्मै नागाय वै दातुं प्रियां दुहितरं मुने।॥
en: Accomplish; take some pains, for I am pleased with him-O Muni, take some pains to bestow on this Naga my beloved daughter.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: नारद उवाच सुतोऽयं मातलि म शक्रस्य दयितः सुहृत्। शुचिः शीलगुणोपेतस्तेजस्वी वीर्यवान् बली॥
en: Narada said This is the charioteer, named Matali, the dear friend of Shakra, pious, of good behaviour, possessed of good qualities, energetic, mighty and strong, O Aryaka.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: शक्रस्यायं सखा चैव मन्त्री सारथिरेव च। अल्पान्तरप्रभावश्च वासवेन रणे रणे॥
en: He is the friend of Shakra, as also his minister and his charioteer and in successive battles it been found that there is little difference between him and Vasava in point strength.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: अश्यं हरिसहस्रेण युक्तं जैत्रं रथोत्तमम्। देवासुरेषु युद्धेषु मनसैव नियच्छति॥
en: He drives, by his will force alone, the excellent car accustomed to victory in wars between the gods and Asuras, yoked to a thousand steeds.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: अनेन विजितानश्वैर्दो( जयति वासवः। अनेन बलभित् पूर्वं प्रहते प्रहरत्युत॥
en: Vasava gains victories in the sky by means of the horses trained by him and the vanquisher of Bala smotes who had previously been smitten by him,

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: अस्य कन्या वरारोहा रूपेणासदृशी भुवि। सत्यशीलगुणोपेता गुणकेशीति विश्रुता॥
en: He has got a daughter of beautiful hips and unequaled this world in this world for beauty, devoted to truth well-bred and possessed of accomplishments, known by the name of Gunakeshi.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: तस्यास्य यत्नाच्चरतस्त्रैलोक्यममराते। सुमुखो भवत: पौत्रो रोचते दुहितुः पतिः॥
en: For her sake, he is searching carefully in the three worlds including the region of the gods, O illustrious one; and he selects Sumukha, your grandson, as the husband of his daughter.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: यदि ते रोचते सम्यग् भुजगोत्तम मा चिरम्। क्रियतामार्यक क्षिप्रं बुद्धिः कन्यापरिग्रहे॥
en: If this suits you, O best of the serpents, then without delay, O Aryaka, make the necessary arrangement for the acceptance of his daughter.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: यथा विष्णुकुले लक्ष्मीर्यथा स्वाहा विभावसोः। कुले तव तथैवास्तु गुणकेशी सुमध्यमा॥
en: As Lakshmi in the family of Vishnu, Svaha in that of Agni, may the slender-waist Gunakeshi be same to your family.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: पौत्रस्यार्थं भवांस्तस्माद् गुणकेशी प्रतीच्छतु। सदृशी प्रतिरूपस्य वासवस्य शचीमिव॥
en: Therefore do you accept for your grandson Gunakeshi, who equals, in point of beauty, Sachi, the queen of Vasava.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: पितृहीनमपि ह्येनं गुणतो वरयामहे। बहमानाच्च भवतस्तथैवैरावतस्य च॥
en: Though he is without a father, yet for his accomplishment, do we select him and for the great respect in which yourself and the Airavata race generally are held.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: सुमुखस्य गुणैश्चैव शीलशौचदमादिभिः। अभिगम्य स्वं कन्यामयं दातुं समुद्यतः॥
en: Coming here attracted by the accomplishments, good manners, purity of life and self-control of Sumukha, he himself ready to offer his daughter.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: कण्व उवाच मातलिस्तस्य सम्मानं कर्तुमर्हो भवानपि। स तु दीनः प्रहृष्टश्च प्राह नारदमार्यकः॥
en: And it is proper that you should greet Matali with due honors. He (Aryaka) too being sorry and delighted at the same time said to Narada,

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: क्रियमाणे तथा पौत्रे पुत्रे च निधनं गते। कथमिच्छामि देवर्षे गुणकेशी स्नुषां प्रति॥
en: At his grandson being elected (for marriage) and at the death of his son. Aryaka said-"How can I desire, O Rishi, Gunakeshi for my daughter-in-law.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: आर्यक उवाच न मे नमैतद् बहुमतं महर्षे वचनं तव। सखा शक्रस्य संयुक्तः कस्यायं नेप्सितो भवेत्॥
en: These words of yours, O great Rishi, are not approved of by me. The cause is not want of respect for you; foe who would not desire a connection with the friend of Shaka?

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: कारणस्य तु दौर्बल्याच्चिन्तयामि महामुने। अस्य देहकरस्तात मम पुत्रो महाद्युते॥ भक्षितौ वैनतेयेन दुःखार्तास्तेन वै वयम्। पुनरेव च तेनोक्तं वैनतेयेन गच्छता। मासेनान्येन सुमुखं भक्षयिष्य इति प्रभो॥
en: But, O great Muni, we hesitate owing to the unstable character of the cause; the author of his being, my son of great luster, has been enter up by the son of Vinata and for that reason we are struck with grief; and when the son of Vinata was going away he again said-After a month I shall eat the other one of this race) Sumukha.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: ध्रुवं तथा तद् भविता जानीमस्तस्य निश्चयम्। तेन हर्षः प्रणष्टो मे सुपर्णवचनेन वै॥
en: It will surely happen so for I know his determination and for this reason is my cheerfulness lost by the words Suparna (Garuda)."

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: कण्व उवाच मातलिस्त्वब्रवीदेनं बुद्धिरत्र कृता मया। जामातृभावेन वृतः सुमुखस्तव पुत्रजः॥
en: Kanva said Matali then said-"In this connection, a plan has been found by me; Sumukha born of your son is selected as my son-in-law.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: सोऽयं मया च सहितो नारदेन च पन्नगः। त्रिलोकेशं सुरपतिं गत्वा पश्यतु वासवम्॥
en: Let this Naga therefore, accompanied by myself and Narada and going to the lord of the gods, the protector of the three worlds, see Vasava.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: शेषेणैवास्य कार्यण प्रज्ञास्याम्यहमायुषः। सुपर्णस्य विधाते च प्रयतिष्यामि सत्तम॥
en: O best of your race, I shall try to foil the intentions of Suparna and as a last resource shall ascertain Sumukha's length of life.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: सुमुखश्च मया सार्धं देवेशमभिगच्छतु। कार्यसंसाधनार्थाय स्वस्ति तेऽस्तु भुजंगम॥
en: Let Sumukha, along with myself, proceed to the lord of the gods for the attainment of this object and may you fare well, O serpent.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: ततस्ते सुमुखं गृह्य सर्व एव महौजसः। ददृशुः शक्रमासीनं देवराजं महाद्युतिम्॥
en: Then all of them, endued with great energy taking Sumukha along with them, proceeded and saw the king of gods, Shakra of great effulgence seated.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: संगत्या तत्र भगवान् विष्णुरासीच्चतुर्भुजः। ततस्तत् सर्वमाचख्यौ नारदो मातलिं प्रति॥
en: There in his company was the four armed Vishnu and there did Narada tell them all about Matali.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततः पुरंदरं विष्णुरुवाच भुवनेश्वरम्। अमृतं दीयतामस्मै क्रियताममरैः समः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Then did Vishnu thus speak to Purandara, the lord of the universe-Give unto him nectar and make him equal to the immortals.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: मातलि रदश्चैव सुमुखश्चैव वासव। लभन्तां भवतः कामात् काममेतं यथेप्सितम्॥
en: Let Matali Narada and Sumukha 0 Vasava, obtain through your pleasure (the fulfillment of) their desires which they cherish."

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: पुरंदरोऽथ संचिन्त्य वैनतेयपराक्रमम्। विष्णुमेवाब्रवीदेनं भवानेन ददात्विति॥
en: Then Purandara, considering the strength of the son of Vinata, said to Vishnu these words-'Let it be given by your exalted self.'

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: विष्णुरुवाच ईशस्त्वं सर्वलोकानां चराणामचराश्च ये। त्वया दत्तमदत्तं कः कर्तुमुत्सहते विभो॥
en: Vishnu said You are the ruler of all the worlds and of mobile beings as also of those that are immobile; what is given by you, who would dare offend, O lord.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: प्रादाच्छक्रस्ततस्तस्मै पन्नगायायुरुत्तमम्। न त्वेनममृतप्राशं चकार बलवृत्रहा॥
en: Then did Shakra give to the serpent an excellent lease of life, but the slayer of Bala and Vritra did not make him drink nectar.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: लब्ध्वा वरं तु सुमुखः सुमुखः सम्बभूव ह। कृतदारो यथाकामं जगाम च गृहान् प्रति॥
en: Having obtained the (desired) boon Sumukha became possessed of a really pretty face taken wife, went, according to his desire, towards his home.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: नारदस्त्वार्यकश्चैव कृतकार्यों मुदा युतौ। अभिजग्मतुरभ्यर्च्य देवराजं महाद्युतिम्॥
en: Narada and Aryaka being pleased at their success went away after worshipping the king of the gods endued with great luster.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: कण्व उवाच गरुडस्तत्र शुश्राव यथावृत्तं महाबलः। आयुःप्रदानं शक्रेण कृतं नागस्य भारत॥
en: Kanya said In the meantime Garuda endued with great might, heard what had happened, namely the bestowal of a long life on the Naga by Shakra, OBharata.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: पक्षवातेन महता रुद्ध्वा त्रिभुवनं खगः। सुपर्णः परमक्रुद्धो वासवं समुपाद्रवत्॥
en: And Suparna, the wanderer of the sky, obstructing the there worlds as it were by the heavy wind caused by his wings and being very, came to Vasava.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: गरुड उवाच भगवन् किमवज्ञानाद् वृत्तिः प्रतिहता मम। कामकारवरं दत्त्वा पुनश्चलितवानसि॥
en: Garuda said O lord, for what shortcoming on my part have you, forbidden me my subsistence-having granted me a boon of your own accord you have withheld it.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: निसर्गात् सर्वभूतानां सर्वभूतेश्वरेण मे। आहारो विहितो धात्रा किमर्थं वार्यते त्वया॥
en: Since the very creation of all creatures my food has been settled by the Supreme Being, the of all creatures and for what reason have you interfered with it.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: वृतश्चैष महानागः स्थापितः समयश्च अनेन च मया भर्तव्यः प्रसवो महान्॥
en: This great Naga had been chosen by me (for my food) and the limit of his time had been fixed by me and on him was I to have subsisted, 0 lord, as also my numerous progeny.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: एतस्मिंस्तु तथाभूते नान्यं हिंसित्तमुत्सहे। क्रीडसे कामकारेण देवराज यथेच्छकम्॥
en: I dare not now kill another of the species, which is used such (i.e., on whom you have granted a boon); you play as you like, of your own will, O king the gods.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: सोऽहं प्राणान् विमोक्ष्यामि तथा परिजनो मम। ये च भृत्या मम गृहे प्रीतिमान् भव वासव॥
en: Reduced to this I shall lose my life as also will the members of my family and these that are attendants at my house. Be gratified Vasava.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: एतच्चैवाहमर्हामि भूयश्च बलवृत्रहन्। त्रैलोकस्येश्वरो योऽहं परभृत्यत्वमागतः॥
en: O slayer of Bala and Vritra, this indeed do I deserve not; though lord of the three worlds I have been reduced to the state of a servant of another.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: त्वयि तिष्ठति देवेश न विष्णुः कारणं मम। त्रैलोक्यराज राज्यं हि त्वयि वासव शाश्वतम्॥
en: O lord of the celestial whilst you suppress me, I find no cause for going to Vishnu; O Vasava, you are the eternal sovereign of the three worlds.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: जननी कश्यपः पिता। अहमप्युत्सहे लोकान् समन्ताद् वोदुमञ्जसा॥
en: O too have daughter of Daksha for my mother and Kashyapa also for my father and I too can venture to bear easily the weight of the three worlds.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: असह्यं सर्वभूतानां ममापि विपुलं बलम्। मयापि सुमहत् कर्म कृतं दैतेयविग्रहे॥
en: My great strength too is unendurable by all creature and by me too have been done great deeds in the war the sons of Diti.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: श्रुतश्रीः श्रुतसेनश्च विवस्वान् रोचनामुखः। प्रसृतः कालकाक्षश्च मयापि दितिजा हताः॥
en: Shrutashri and Shrutsena, Vivasvata Rochanamukha and Prasrita and Kalka Aksha, these sons of Diti have by me been slain.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: यत् तु ध्वजस्थानगतो यत्नात् परिचराम्यहम्। वहामि चैवानुजं ते तेन मामवमन्यसे॥
en: Stationing myself on the flag I fear your younger and attend on him; Therefore do you disregard me.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: ममापि दक्षस्य सुता कोऽन्यो भारसहो ह्यस्ति कोऽन्योऽस्ति बलवत्तरः। मया योऽहं विशिष्टः सन् वहामीमं सबान्धवम्॥
en: What other being can bear that load? What other being is stronger? Though thus qualified, I yet bear your younger brother with his friends.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: अवज्ञाय तु यत् तेऽहं भोजनाद् व्यपरोपितः। तेन मे गौरवं नष्टं त्वतश्चास्माच्च वासव॥
en: Since however disregarding me, O Vishnu, as for yourself, you have interfered with my subsistence, you have made me lose my respect, as your brother has done.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: अदित्यां य इमे जाता बलविक्रमशालिनः। त्वमेषां किल सर्वेषां बलेन बलवत्तरः॥
en: Among those endued with might and prowess that are begotten in the race of Aditi-you are the strongest in might.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: सोऽहं पक्षैकदेशेन वहामि त्वां गतक्लमः। विमृशं त्वं शनैस्तात को न्वत्र बलवानिति॥
en: I bear you who are such on one portion of my wings without experiencing any fatigue. Think, O dear as to who is the stronger.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: कण्व उवाच स तस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा खगस्योदर्कदारुणम्। अक्षोभ्यं क्षोभयंस्तार्क्ष्यमुवाच रथचक्रभृत्॥
en: Kanva said The wielder of the discus, having heard the words marked with vanity of the wanderer of the sky, which were at the same time indicative of peril, said to Tarkshya, who was annoyed, annoying him the more.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: गरुत्मन् मन्यसेऽऽत्मानं बलवन्तं सुदुर्बलम्। अलमस्मत्समक्षं ते स्तोतुमात्मानमण्डज॥
en: "O Garuda, you consider yourself strong, though you are weak. It is not right that you should thus speak in flattering terms of yourself in presence, O you born of egg.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: त्रैलोक्वमपि मे कृत्स्नमशक्तं देहधारणे। अहमेवात्मनाऽऽत्मानं बहामि त्वां च धारये॥
en: The three worlds, even when united together are incapable are incapable of bearing the load of my body; I myself bear the weight of my-self and also uphold you.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: इमं तावन्ममैकं त्वं बाहुं सव्येतरं वह। यद्येनं धारयस्येकं सफलं ते विकस्थितम्॥
en: To prove your words, bear the weight of my right arm and if you can carry it then what you say will have some reason in it."

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: ततः स भगवांस्तस्य स्कन्धे बाहुं समासजत्। निपपात स भारा” विह्वलो नष्टचेतनः॥
en: Then did that prosperous being place his arm on his shoulder. He fell down struck by the lord stupefied and deprived of his senses.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: यावान् हि भारः कृत्स्नायाः पृथिव्याः पर्वतैः सह। एकस्या देहशाखायास्तावद् भारममन्यत॥
en: The weight, that was in the earth united with the mountains, was in one branch of the body (of Vishnu).

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: न त्वेनं पीडयामास बलेन बलवत्तरः। ततो हि जीवितं तस्य न व्यनीनशदच्युतः॥
en: The one who was by far the stronger did not press him (Garuda) with any force and thus was he alive for Achyuta did not want to kill him.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: व्यात्तास्यः सस्तकायश्च विचेता विह्वलः खगः। मुमोच पत्राणि तदा गुरुभारप्रपीडितः॥
en: Writhing under that heavy load that wanderer of the sky gasped for breath, was stupefied, lost his senses and his energies were all dried up and he was stripped off his feathers.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: स विष्णु शिरसा पक्षी प्रणम्य विनतासुतः। विचेता विह्वलो दीन: किंचिद् वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Then the bird, the son of Vinata, bowed with his head to Vishnu and feebly said to him these words, being stupefied and rendered helpless and regretting his folly.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: भगवल्लोकसारस्य सदृशेन वपुष्मता। भुजेन स्वैरमुक्तेन निष्पिष्टोऽस्मि महीतले॥
en: "O lord, what is the wonder that I should be crushed down to the earth by the arm which belongs to a body which is like the essence of the universe.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: क्षन्तुमर्हसि मे देव विह्वलस्याल्पचेतसः। बलदाहविदग्धस्य पक्षिणो ध्वजवासिनः॥
en: It is proper, O lord, that you should forgiven me am rendered helpless, who am of mean intelligence, intoxicated with the vanity of might and but a bird bearing a flag.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: न हि ज्ञातं बलं देव मया ते परमं विभो। तेन मन्याम्यहं वीर्यमात्मनो न समं परैः॥
en: O god, O lord, your strength was not known to me and for that reason did I think myself possessed of heroism not equaled by others.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: ततश्चक्रे स भगवान् प्रसादं वै गरुत्मतः। मैवं भूय इति स्नेहात् तदा चैनमुवाच ह॥
en: Then was the god pleased with Garuda and he said is the bird out of affection-"'Do not act so again."

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: पादाङ्गुष्ठेन चिक्षेप सुखं गरुडोरसि। ततःप्रभृति राजेन्द्र सह सर्पण वर्तते।॥
en: With the toe of his feet he threw Sumukha on the breast of Garuda and from that time forward O chief of kings, Garuda live (in friendship) with that serpent.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: एवं विष्णुबलाक्रान्तो गर्वनाशमुपागतः। गरुडो बलवान् राजन् वैनतेयो महायशाः॥
en: In this way was the haughty Garuda the son of Vinata and great renown, cured of his vanity, being overpowered by the might of Vishnu.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: कण्व उवाच तथा त्वमपि गान्धारे यावत् पाण्डुसुतान् रणे। नासादयसि तान् वीरांस्तावजीवसि पुत्रक॥
en: Kanva said In the same way, O son of Gandhari, you too, so long as you do not come face to face in battle with those heroes, the sons of Pandu, will be living, O dear, son.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: भीमः प्रहरतां श्रेष्ठो वायुपुत्रो महाबलः। धनंजयश्चेन्द्रसुतो न हन्यातां तु कं रणे॥
en: Who is there whom Bhima the foremost among opponents, the son of Vayu and possessed of great strength and Dhananjaya the son of Shakra cannot kill in battle.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: विष्णुर्वायुश्च शक्रश्च धर्मस्तौ चाश्विनावुभौ। एते देवास्त्वया केन हेतुना वीक्षितुं क्षमाः॥
en: Vishnu, Vayu, Shakra, Dharma and both the Asvinis-all these are gods how are you capable of gazing at?

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: तदलं ते विरोधेन शमं गच्छ नृपात्मज) वासुदेवेन तीर्थेन कुलं रक्षितुमर्हसि॥
en: Fight would therefore be useless; effect peace, O son of a ruler of men, by means of Vasudeva; it is proper that you should save your family.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: प्रत्यक्षदर्शी सर्वस्य नारदोऽयं महातपाः। महात्म्यस्य तदा विष्णोः सोऽयं चक्रगदाधर॥
en: This Narada, of great asceticism, saw all this with his own eyes and this Krishna held the mice and discus of that great souled Vishnu.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच दुर्योधनस्तु तच्छ्रुत्वा निःश्वसन् भृकुटीमुखः। राधेयमभिसम्प्रेक्ष्य जहास स्वनवत् तदा॥
en: Vaishampayana said Duryodhana, having heard all this, breathing herd with his eye-brows contracted and gazing on the son of Radica, laughed aloud at that time.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: कदर्थीकृत्य तद् वाक्यमृषेः कण्वस्य दुर्मतिः। ऊरूं गजकराकारं ताडयन्निदमब्रवीत्॥
en: Without regarding those words of the Rishi Kanva, the one, of evil intellect, said these words slapping his thighs which were of the size of those of an elephant.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: यथैवेश्वरसृष्टोऽस्मि यद् भावि या च मे गतिः। तथा महर्षे वर्तामि किं प्रलापः करिष्यति॥
en: "Since I have been created by god, I am what he has made me; what will happen must happen and so must my course be shaped. O great Rishi, I shall act in that way; what can these useless discussions do?

sn: जनमेजय उवाच अनर्थं जातनिर्बन्धं परार्थं लोभमोहितम्। अनार्यकेष्वभिरतं मरणे कृतनिश्चयम्॥ ज्ञातीनां दुःखकर्तारं बन्धूनां शोकवर्धनम्। सुहृदां क्लेशदातारं द्विषतां हर्षवर्धनम्॥ कथं नैनं विमार्गस्थं वारयन्तीह बान्धवाः। सौहृदाद् वा सुहृत् स्निग्धो भगवान् वा पितामहः॥
en: Janamejaya said Being from his very birth attached to evil and témpted by covetousness for the wealth of others, addicted to wicked habits and bent upon bringing about his own death, the cause of the misery of his kinsmen, the cause of heightening the grief of his friends, the cause of giving pain to his well-wishers and the cause of the increase of the joy of his enemies, for what reason did not his friends dissuade him who was wedding the wrong course and why did not the friend Krishna or the grandfather do it out of friendship or affection?

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच उक्तं भगवता वाक्यमुक्तं भीष्मेण यत् क्षयम्। उक्तं बहुविधं चैव नारदेनापि तच्छृणु॥
en: Vaishampayana said Words were spoken by Krishna and Bhishma, all that could be said and many were the words spoken by Narada. Listen to them.

sn: नारद उवाच दुर्लभो वै सुहच्छ्रोता दुर्लभश्च हितः सुहृत्। तिष्ठते हि सुहृद् यत्र न बन्धुस्तत्र तिष्ठते॥
en: Narada said Race are those persons who listen to the advice of well-wishers and rare are friends who give good counsels, where there is an adviser who could advice well there is no friend standing (in need of it).

sn: श्रोतव्यमपि पश्यामि सुहृदां कुरुनन्दन। न कर्तव्यश्च निर्बन्धो निर्बन्धो हि सुदारुणः॥
en: I see, that the advice of your friends ought to be listened to by you, O you the delighter of the race of Kuru; obstinacy ought not to be persevered in, for it is a great evil.

sn: अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। यथा निर्बन्धतः प्राप्तो गालवेन पराजयः॥
en: In this connection is cited the old story in which out of obstinacy Galava met with defeat.

sn: विश्वामित्रं तपस्यन्तं धर्मो जिज्ञासया पुरा। अभ्यगच्छत् स्वयं भूत्वा वसिष्ठो भगवानृषिः॥
en: In days of old, with a view to try Vishhvamitra who was practicing asceticism, Dharma came to him in person in the disguise of the divinely prosperous Rishi Vasishtha.

sn: सप्तर्षीणामन्यतमं वेषमास्थाय भारत। बुभुक्षुः क्षुभितो राजन्नाश्रमं कौशिकस्य तु॥
en: Having assumed the appearance of one of the seven Rishis, O Bharata, he came to the hermitage of the son of Kushika, as if hungry, with the desire of satisfying his hunger.

sn: विश्वामित्रोऽथ सम्भ्रान्तः श्रपयामास वै चरुम्। परमान्नस्य यत्नेन न च तं प्रत्यपालयत्॥
en: Vishvamitra, with great respect, employed himself in preparing Charu (rice boiled in milk and honey) and in his anxiety to prepare that excellent repast he could not attend to him in other respects.

sn: अन्नं तेन तदा भुक्तमन्यैर्दत्तं तपस्विभिः। अथ गृह्यान्नमत्युष्णं विश्वामित्रोऽप्युपागमत्॥
en: When he had taken the fool offered by other devotees, Vishvamitra too came there taking his food which was very hot.

sn: भुक्तं मे तिष्ठ तावत् त्वमित्युक्त्वा भगवान् ययौ। विश्वामित्रस्ततो राजन् स्थितं एव महाद्युतिः॥
en: I have taken my food; you stay here for the present" saying this the divinely prosperous one went away and then did Vishvamitra, of great effulgence, O king, stand there.

sn: भक्तं प्रगृह्य मूर्धा वै बाहुभ्यां संशितव्रतः। स्थितः स्थाणुरिवाभ्याशे निष्चेष्टो मारुताशनः॥
en: Out of reverence, taking the food on his head and holding the same by his hands the devotee, of austere asceticism, stood there in the hermitage like a post and subsisting on air.

sn: तस्य शुश्रूषणे यलमकरोद् गालवो मुनिः। गौरवाद् बहुमानाच्च हार्देन प्रियकाम्यया॥
en: In attending on him the Muni Galava took pains out of respect, reverence, affection and the desire to do what was pleasing to Vishvamitra.

sn: अथ वर्षशते पूर्णे धर्मः पुनरुपागमत्। वासिष्ठं वेषमास्थाय कौशिकं भोजनेप्सया॥
en: Then on the completion of a hundred years Dharma came there again to the son of Kushika, assuming the appearance of Vasishtha with the desire of eating.

sn: स दृष्ट्वा शिरसा भक्तं ध्रियमाणं महर्षिणा। तिष्ठता वायुभक्षेण विश्वामित्रेण धीमता॥ प्रतिगृह्य ततो धर्मस्तथैवोष्णं तथा नवम्। भुक्त्वाप्रीतोऽस्मि विप्रर्षे तमुक्त्वा स मुनिर्गतः॥
en: He saw his food held on his head by the wise and great Rishi Vishvamitra who stood there subsisting on air and Dharma then accepting the food which was hot and newly cooked and eating it said-“I am pleased, O regenerate Rishi" and went away.

sn: क्षत्रभावादपगतो ब्राह्मणत्वमुपागतः। धर्मस्य वचनात् प्रीतो विश्वामित्रस्तदाभवत्॥
en: He then became divested of the condition of a Kshatriyas and reached that of a Brahmana and Vishvamitra became pleased at those words Dharma.

sn: विश्वामित्रस्तु शिष्यस्य गालवस्य तपस्विनः। शुश्रूषया च भक्त्या च प्रीतिमानित्युवाच ह॥
en: And Vishvamitra, being pleased with the attention and devotion of his disciple the ascetic Galava, said thus:

sn: अनुज्ञातौ मया वत्स यथेष्टं गच्छ गालवा इत्युक्तः प्रत्युवाचेदं गालवो मुनिसत्तमम्॥ प्रीतो मधुरया वाचा विश्वामित्रं महाद्युतिम्। दक्षिणाः काः प्रयच्छामि भवते गुरुकर्मणि॥
en: “With my permission, child, go away wherever you wish, O Galava.” Being thus addressed, Galava, the best of Munis, said this in reply, in words which were sweet and pleasing to Vishvamitra endued with great effulgence-"What gift (Dakshina) shall I give to your exalted self for your favour as my preceptor?

sn: दक्षिणआभिरुपेतं हि कर्म सिद्ध्यति मानद। दक्षिणानां हि दाता वै अपवर्गेण युज्यते॥
en: Every religions act becomes successful only when it is accompanied by a gift, O you the giver of honours and then the giver of those gifts obtains salvation.

sn: स्वर्गे क्रतुफलं तद्धि दक्षिणा शान्तिरुच्यते। किमाहरामि गुर्वर्थं ब्रवीतु भगवानिति॥
en: Gifts are the fruits of acts (enjoyed) in heaven and are therefore said to be the peace. What shall I procure for my spiritual guide let my lord command.”

sn: जानानस्तेन भगवाञ्जितः शुश्रूषणेन वै। विश्वामित्रस्तमसकृद् गच्छ गच्छेत्यचोदयत्॥
en: The Rishi Vishvamitra, divinely prosperous, knowing that he had been conquered by his attentions (and nothing else) said to him-“Go, go" and sought to send his attendant away by that means,

sn: असकृद् गच्छ गच्छेति विश्वामित्रेण भाषितः। किं ददानीति बहुशो गालवः प्रत्यभाषत॥
en: The attendant, being spoken to by Vishvamitra saying again and again 'go, go,' said by way of reply “What shall I give you."

sn: निर्बन्धतस्तु बहुशो गालवस्य तपस्विनः। किंचिदागतसंरम्भो विश्वामित्रऽब्रवीदिदम्॥
en: Vishvamitra, a little angry at the excessive obstinacy of the devotee Galava, said this to him:

sn: एकतः श्यामकर्णानां हयानां चन्द्रवर्चसाम्। अष्टौ शतानि मे देहि गच्छ गालव मा चिरम्॥
en: “Give me eight hundred horses, white as the rays of the moon and each having one ear black. Go,OGalava, without delay."

sn: नारद उवाच एवमुक्तस्तदा तेन विश्वामित्रेण धीमता। नास्ते न शेते नाहारं कुरुते गालवस्तदा॥
en: Narada said Being thus commanded by the intelligent Vishvamitra Galava could not sit, nor sleep nor could he take his meals.

sn: त्वगस्थिभूतो हरिणश्चिन्ताशोकपरायणः। शोचमानोऽतिमात्रं स दह्यमानश्च मन्युना। गालवो दुःखितो दुःखाद् विललाप सुयोधन॥
en: His body was reduced to a skeleton and became pale being subject to grief and a prey to excessive anxiety and burning with dissatisfaction. Galava, being very sorry, thus began to lament, O Suyodhana.

sn: कुतः पुष्टानि मित्राणि कुतोऽर्थाः संचयः कुतः। हयानां चन्द्रशुभ्राणां शतान्यष्टौ कुतो मम॥
en: Where can I get well-to-do friends? Where can I have wealth froin? Where are my saving? Eight hundred horses white as the moon where can I get?

sn: कुतो मे भोजने श्रद्धा सुखश्रद्धा कुतश्च मे। श्रद्धा मे जीवितस्यापि छिन्ना किं जीवितेन मे॥
en: How can I get satisfaction from eating? How can I get satisfaction from happiness? My happiness derived from life itself is broken up. What is the use of my living on?

sn: अहं पारे समुद्रस्य पृथिव्या वा परम्परात्। गत्वाऽऽत्मानं विमुञ्चामि किं फलं जीवितेन मे॥
en: Having gone to the other side of the sea or going to the most distant part of the world, I shall cast off my life. What is the use of my living on?

sn: अधनस्याकृतार्थस्य त्यक्तस्य विविधैः फलैः। ऋणं धारयमाणस्य कुतः सुखमनीहया॥
en: What happiness can there be without hard exertion for him who is poor, unsuccessful, deprived of all the sweets of life and saddled with debts?

sn: सुहृदां हि धनं भुक्त्वा कृत्वा प्रणयमीप्तिसतम्। प्रतिकर्तुमशक्तस्य जीवितान्मरणं वरम्॥
en: Having enjoyed the wealth of my friends having given him to understand that I shall return it to him, I am unable to make a return for his kindness and so death is preferable to life for me.

sn: प्रतिश्रुत्य करिष्येति कर्तव्यं तदकुर्वतः। मिथ्यावचनदग्धस्य इष्टापूर्त प्रणश्यति॥
en: The religious merit of a man bears no fruit, who having promised to do an act fails to perform it and is thus sullied with falsehood.

sn: न रूपमनृतस्यास्ति नानृतस्यास्ति संततिः। नानृतस्याधिपत्यं च कुत एव गतिः शुभा॥
en: A man addicted to false-hood can never get beauty, a man addicted to false-hood can get not get children, a man addicted to falsehood cannot power can he then expect to obtain bliss?

sn: कुतः कृतघ्नस्य यशः कुतः स्थानं कुतः सुखम्। अश्रद्धेयः कृतघ्नो हि कृतघ्ने नास्ति निष्कृतिः॥
en: Where is fame for an ungrateful person? Where is there a proper place for an ungrateful person? An ungrateful person is unworthy of respect and there is no emancipation for an ungrateful person.

sn: न जीवत्यधनः पापः कुतः पापस्य तन्त्रणम्। पापो ध्रुवमवाप्नोति विनाशं नाशयन् कृतम्॥
en: The wretch who is without wealth is dead as it were; and how can such a wretch support his relatives; the wretch certainly meets with ruin for he is unable to return the favours he receives.

sn: सोऽहं पापः कृतघ्नश्च कृपणश्चानृतोऽपि च। गुरोर्यः कृतकार्यः संस्तत् करोमि न भाषितम्॥
en: I am such a wretch, an ungrateful man, without wealth and addicted to false-hood, who, having my wishes gratified by my spiritual guide, am unable to act up to his orders.

sn: सोऽहं प्राणान् विमोक्ष्यामि कृत्वा यलमनुत्तमम्। अर्थिता न मया काचित् कृतपूर्वा दिवौकसाम्। मानयन्ति च मां सर्वे त्रिदशा यज्ञसंस्तरे॥
en: I, who am such, shall cast off this life after having made an attempt which cannot be exceeded (by other attempts in point of earnestness). Never before has anything been asked by me from the gods.

sn: अहं तु विबुधश्रेष्ठं देवं त्रिभुवनेश्वरम्। विष्णुं गच्छाम्यहं कृष्णं गतिं गतिमतां वरम्॥
en: All the gods regard me for this in sacrificial rites; and I shall go to Vishnu the friend of wise men, the god, who is the lord of the three worlds, to Krishna who is the best refuge for those that need refuge.

sn: भोगा यस्मात् प्रतिष्ठन्ते व्याप्य सर्वान् सुरासुरान्। प्रणतो द्रष्टुमिच्छामि कृष्ण योगिनमव्ययम्॥
en: From whom flow all the enjoyments that are enjoyed by the gods and Asuras; with my head bent down I desire to see Krishna, the devotee who is without end.

sn: एवमुक्ते सखा तस्य गरुडो विनतात्मजः। दर्शयामास तं प्राह संहृष्टः प्रियकाम्यया॥
en: He having thus said, his friend Garuda, the son of Vinata, came into his view who being pleased, said to him with a desire to do him good.

sn: सुहृद् भवान् मम मतः सुहृदां च मतः सुहृत्। ईप्सितेनाभिलाषेण योक्तव्यो विभवे सति॥
en: Your exalted self is my friend. A friend is prosperity should try to accomplish the wishes of his friends.

sn: विभवश्वास्ति मे विप्र वासवावरजो द्विजा पूर्वमुक्तस्त्वदर्थं च कृतः कामश्च तेन मे॥
en: O twice-born one, the prosperity I possess has its rise in the younger brother of Vasava; I have already spoken to him about your wishes and he has granted my wishes to do you good).

sn: स भवानेतु गच्छाव नयिष्ये त्वां यथासुखम्। देशं पारं पृथिव्या वा गच्छ गालव मा चिरम्॥
en: Such being the case, wherever you want to go, I will take you without any trouble to yourself, to the countries on the other side of the sea or to the remotest corner of the earth, come, O Galava, without delay.

sn: सुपर्ण उवाच अनुशिष्टोऽस्मि देवेन गालवाज्ञानयोनिना। ब्रूहि कामं तु कां यामि द्रष्टुं प्रथमतो दिशम्॥
en: Suparna said I have been instructed by the god who is the source of all knowledge (to take you where you wish to be taken); tell me-which direction shall I first go, to show you.

sn: पूर्वां वा दक्षिणां वाऽहमथवा पश्चिमां दिशम्। उत्तरां वा द्विजश्रेष्ठं कुतो गच्छामि गालव॥
en: The east or the south or the western point or the northern, O you foremost among the twice-born, where shall I go, OGalava.

sn: यस्यामुदयते पूर्वं सर्वलोकप्रभावनः। सविता यत्र संध्यायां साध्यानां वर्तते तपः॥ यस्यां पूर्वं मतिर्याता यया व्याप्तमिदं जगत्। चक्षुषी यत्र धर्मस्य यत्र चैध सुतिष्ठितेः॥ कृतं यतो हुतं हव्यं सर्पते सर्वतोदिशम्। एतद् द्वारं द्विजश्रेष्ठ दिवसस्य तथाध्वनः॥
en: Where the sun which lights all the worlds first rises and where in the evening the Saddhya practice asceticism, where was first born the intelligence, by which is pervaded this earth and where the two eyes of Dharma are set in order to guide the universe, in which point offers of clarified butter were first made which afterwards flowed in all directions; this, 0 foremost among the twice-born is the gate of day and time.

sn: अत्र पूर्वं प्रसूता वै दाक्षायण्यः प्रजाः स्त्रियः। यस्यां दिशि प्रवृद्धाश्च कश्यपस्यात्मसम्भवाः॥
en: Here in days of old the female children of Daksha brought forth their children-the direction in which those born of Kashyapa grew up.

sn: अदोमूला सुराणां श्रीयंत्र शक्रोऽभ्यषिच्यत। सुरराज्येन विप्रर्षे देवैश्चात्र तपश्चितम्॥
en: Here is the source of the prosperity of the gods, where Shakra was appointed in the kingship of the immortals, where even the gods, O regenerate Rishi, practiced asceticism.

sn: एतस्मात् कारणाद् ब्रह्मन् पूर्वेत्येषा दिगुच्यते। यस्मात् पूर्वतरे काले पूर्वमेवावृता सुरैः॥ अत एव च सर्वेषां पूर्वामाशां प्रचक्षते। पूर्वं सर्वाणि कार्याणि दैवानि सुखमीप्सता॥
en: For this, O Brahmana, this direction is called east (Poorvi) for in the days of yore it was over-spread by the gods. Therefore it is said to be in the possession of the oldest inhabitants; in the east, were done all the acts by the gods who were desirous of obtaining happiness.

sn: अत्र वेदाञ्जगौ पूर्वं भगवाँल्लोकभावनः। अत्रैवोक्ता सवित्राऽऽसीत् सावित्री ब्रह्मवादिषु॥
en: Here were the Vedas chanted first by the prosperous Being, the Creator of the universe; in this direction out of the mouth of the sun is said to be born the goddess Savitri among the chanters of the Vedas.

sn: अत्र दत्तानि सूर्येण यजूंषि द्विजसत्तम। अत्र लब्धवरः सोमः सुरैः क्रतुषु पीयते॥
en: Here were given Surya the hymn of the Yajurveda, O best among the twice-born and here was drunk the Soma juice, previously sacrificial ceremonies.

sn: अत्र तृप्ता हुतवहाः स्वां योनिमुपभुञ्जते। अत्र पातालमाश्रित्य वरुण: श्रियमाप च॥
en: Here were sacrificial fires gratified by offerings of objects of the same origin and class (milk and clarified butter) and here did Varuna attain to his prosperity resorting to the region of the Patala.

sn: अत्र पूर्वं वसिष्ठस्य पौराणस्य द्विजर्षभ। सूतिश्चैव प्रतिष्ठा च निधनं च प्रकाशते॥
en: Here, in days of old, O best among the twice born, took place the birth, attainment to fame and death of the ancient Rishi Vasishtha.

sn: ओङ्कारस्यात्र जायन्ते सुतयो दशतीर्दश। पिबन्ति मुनयो यत्र हविधूमं स्म धूमपाः॥
en: Here was first created the On (the magical beginning of every Mantra) in all its ten times ten branches; and here did the smoke-eating ascetics eat the smoke issuing from sacrificial fire.

sn: प्रोक्षिता यत्र बहवो वराहाद्या मृगा वने। शक्रेण यज्ञभागार्थं दैवतेषु प्रकल्पिताः॥
en: Here were massacred many boars and Other animals by Shakra to be used as offerings for sacrificial ceremonies dedicated to the gods.

sn: अत्राहिताः कृतघ्नाश्च मानुषाश्चासुराश्च ये। उदयंस्तान् हि सर्वान् वै क्रोधाद्धन्ति विभावसुः॥
en: Here does the sun rise and slay in his rage all ungrateful men and Asuras.

sn: एतद् द्वारं त्रिलोकस्य स्वर्गस्य च सुखस्य च। एष पूर्वो दिशां भागो विशावोऽत्र यदीच्छसि॥
en: This is the gate of the three worlds and of heaven and happiness; this direction is the eastern quarter and we shall enter it if you like.

sn: प्रियं कार्यं हि मे तस्य यस्यास्मि वचने स्थितः। ब्रूहि गालव यास्यामि शृणु चाप्यपरां दिशम्॥
en: My duty is to do what you wish, for I am ready to carry out your orders; speaks, O Galava and I shall go; listen to me about another cardinal point.

sn: सुपर्ण उवाच इयं विवस्वता पूर्वं श्रौतेन विधिना किल। गुरवे दक्षिणां दत्ता दक्षिणेत्युच्यते च दिक्॥
en: Suparna said This direction, in days of old, was given away by Vivasvat after the performance of a sacrifice according to the usual custom as a final present (Dakshina) to his spiritual guide; so this direction is called south (Dakshina).

sn: अत्र लोकत्रयस्यास्य पितृपक्षः प्रतिष्ठितः। अत्रोष्मपाणां देवानां निवासः श्रूयते द्विज॥
en: In this direction do the Pitris of the three worlds live and it is said, O twice born one, that this is the residence of those gods that subsist on smoke.

sn: अत्र विश्वे सदा देवाः पितृभिः सार्धमासते। इज्यमानाः स्म लोकेषु सम्प्राप्तास्तुल्यभागताम्॥
en: In this part of the universe the gods along with the Pitris ever reside, who are worshipped in sacrifices in the world and get equal share with the Pitris.

sn: एतद् द्वितीयं देवस्य द्वारमाचक्षते द्विज। त्रुटिशो लवशश्चापि गण्यते कालनिश्चयः॥
en: This direction is said to be the second gate to virtue, O twice born one and here does the king of death, with a sure hand, calculate the life allotted to men, in Trutis and Lavas (periods of time).

sn: अत्र देवर्षयो नित्यं पितृलोकर्षयस्तथा। तथा राजर्षयः सर्वे निवसन्ति गतव्यथा:॥
en: Here do the divine Rishis and the Rishis of the world of the Pitris as also Rishis of royal descent all reside, always being beyond the reach of pain.

sn: अत्र धर्मश्च सत्यं च कर्म चात्र निगद्यते। गतिरेषा द्विजश्रेष्ठ कर्मणामवसायिनाम्॥
en: Here are virtue and truth, here the acts of men bear fruit and this is the refuge, O foremost among the twice born, of the acts of those that are dead.

sn: एषा दिक् सा द्विजश्रेष्ठ यां सर्वः प्रतिपद्यते। वृता त्वनवबोधेन सुखं तेन न गम्यते॥
en: This is that direction, O foremost among the twice born, where every body must go; and as all of them are surrounded by the darkness of ignorance they cannot come here with perfect happiness.

sn: नैर्ऋतानां सहस्राणि बहून्यत्र द्विजर्षभ। सृष्टानि प्रतिकूलानि द्रष्टव्यान्यकृतात्मभिः॥
en: Here are many thousands of Rakshasas, O best among the twice born, who have been created to stand in the way of men coming to these regions and who can be perceived by those who have not brought their souls under control.

sn: अत्र मन्दरकुलेषु विप्रर्षिसदनेषु च। गायन्ति गाथा गन्धर्वाश्चित्तबुद्धिहरा द्विज॥
en: Here in the secluded spots of the Mandara mountains and in the residences of regenerate Rishis the Gandharvas chant songs stealing away the head and the heart, O twice born one.

sn: अत्र सामानि गाथाभिः श्रुत्वा गीतानि रैवतः। गतदारो गतामात्यो गतराज्यो वनं गतः॥
en: The Daityas Raivata, having heard the hymns of the Samaveda chanted here, abandoned wife, friends and kingdoms and went into the forest.

sn: अत्र सावर्णिना चैव यवक्रीतात्मजेन च। मर्यादा स्थापिता ब्रह्मन् यां सूर्यो नातिवर्तते॥
en: Here by the son of Savarni and that of Yavakrita was fixed a limit, O Brahmana, which Surya does not pass beyond.

sn: अत्र राक्षसराजेन पौलस्त्येन महात्मना। रावणेन तपश्चीक़ सुरेभ्योऽमरता वृता॥
en: Here by the great-souled son of Pulastya Ravana, the king of Rakshasas who practiced austerities, was solicited immortality of the gods.

sn: अत्र वृत्तेन वृत्रोऽपि शक्रशत्रुत्यमीयिवान्। अत्र सर्वासवः प्राप्ताः पुनर्गच्छन्ति पञ्चधा॥
en: Here by his habits of life did Vritra (the Asura) incur the hostility of Shankra and here do the lives of all being come and again dissolve into their five elephants.

sn: अत्र दुष्कृतकर्माणो नराः पच्यन्ति गालव। अत्र वैतरणी नाम नदी वितरणैर्वृता।।१४]i
en: Here men, the doers of wicked acts, cannot go, O Galava and here is the river Vaitarani surrounded by people who cannot obtain salvation and cross it.

sn: अत्र गत्वा सुखस्यान्तं दुःखस्यान्तं प्रपद्यते। अत्र वृत्तो दिनकरः सुरसं क्षरते पयः॥
en: Here do men come and attain to a termination of their happiness and misery and coming here does the maker of day (the sun) pour water having a nice taste.

sn: काष्ठां चासाद्य वासिष्ठी हिमपुत्सृजते पुनः। अत्राहं गालव पुरा क्षुधातः परिचिन्तयन्॥
en: And having gone again to the cardinal point, pervaded by Vasishtha he lets fall dew; and here did I, in days of old being hungry and thinking about how to satisfy it.

sn: लब्धवान् युध्यमानौ द्वौ बृहन्तौ गजकच्छपौ। अत्र चक्रधनुर्नाम सूर्याज्जातो महानृषिः॥
en: See fighting with each other, a large elephant and a big tortoise. Here was born from the sun the great Rishi named Chakradhanu,

sn: विदुर्यं कपिलं देवं येनार्ताः सगरात्मजाः। अत्र सिद्धाः शिवा नाम ब्राह्मणा वेदपारगाः॥
en: Who was afterwards known as the god Kapila by whom were afflicted the sons of Sagara; and here did the class of Brahmanas known as Shivas, well versed in the Vedas, meet with success.

sn: अधीत्य सकलान् वेदाँल्लेभिरे मोक्षमक्षयम्। अत्र भोगवती नाम पुरी वासुकिपालिता॥
en: And having studied all the Vedas, they obtained endless salvation; here is the city named Bhogavati ruled by Vasuki.

sn: तक्षकेण च नागेन तथैवैरावतेन च। अत्र निर्याणकालेऽपि तमः सम्प्राप्यते महत्॥
en: And by the Naga, Takshaka and also by Airavala; and here at the time of their journey men meet with a great gloom.

sn: अभेद्यं भास्करेणापि स्वयं वा कृष्णवर्त्मना। एष तस्यापि ते मार्गः परिचार्यस्य गालव। ब्रूहि मे यदि गन्तव्यं प्रतीची शृणु चापराम्॥
en: Which is impregnable even by Bhaskara (the sun himself) or by fire. Even this is your way, O Galava, worthy of attention, tell me if you want to go in this direction; listen now to the description of another direction, the west.

sn: सुपर्ण उवाच इयं दिग् दयिता राज्ञो वरुणस्य तु गोपतेः। सदा सलिलराज्य प्रतिष्ठा चादिरेव च।।।।
en: Suparna said This direction is the favorite one of king Varuna, the lord of the seas. In fact this has been the region of the birth of the king of the waters and even the region of his influence.

sn: अत्र पश्चादहः सूर्यो विसर्जयति गाः स्वयम्। पश्चिमेत्यभिविख्याता दिगियं द्विजसत्तम॥
en: Here does the sun abandon his rays himself last of all ((Paschata) in the day; this is known as the western direction, O best among the twice born.

sn: यादसामत्र राज्येन सलिलस्य च गुप्तये। कश्यपो भगवान् देवो वरुणं स्माभ्यषेचयत्॥
en: For ruling over aquatic animals and for the protection of the waters, the illustrious and divine sage Kashyapa anointed Varuna.

sn: अत्र पीत्वा समस्तान् वै वरुणस्य रसांस्तु षट्। जायते तरुणः सोमः शुक्लस्यादौ तमिस्रहा।॥
en: Here having drunk all the six juices of Varuna, the moon, the destroyer of darkness, becomes new again in the very beginning of the light half of the month.

sn: अत्र पश्चात् कृता दैत्या वायुना संयतास्तदा। निःश्वसन्तो महावातैरर्दिताः सुषुपुर्द्विज॥
en: Here were the Daityas vanquished by Vayu and then confined by him; and O twice born one, they slept here (the sleep that knows no waking) breathing hard and afflicted by a high wind.

sn: अत्र सूर्यं प्रणयिन प्रतिगृह्णाति पर्वतः। अस्तो नाम यतः संध्या पश्चिमा प्रतिसर्पति॥
en: Here does the mountain named Asta receive the sun as if in love owing to which the evening twilight vanishes away in the west.

sn: अतो रात्रिश्च निद्रा च निर्गता दिवसक्षये। जायते जीवलोकस्य हर्तुमर्धमिवायुषः॥
en: From here at the end of the day do the night and sleep come and spread themselves as it were to steal away half the life of living creatures.

sn: अत्र देवीं दितिं सुप्तामात्मप्रसवधारिणीम्। विगर्भामकरोच्छनो यत्र जातो मरुद्गणः॥
en: In this quarter seeing the goddess Diti, who bore a child, asleep, Shakra cut up the focus from which were born the group of Maruts.

sn: अत्र मूलं हिमवतो मन्दरं याति शाश्वतम्। अपि वर्षसहस्रेण न चास्यान्तोऽधिगम्यते॥
en: In this direction the base of the Himavat mountain is extended to the eternal Mandara and no one can reach the end of this mountain even in a thousand years.

sn: अत्र काञ्चनशैलस्य काञ्चनाम्बुरुहस्य च। उदधेस्तीरमासाद्य सुरभिः क्षरते पयः॥
en: In this direction coming to the shore of the sea having golden mountains and golden lotuses, does Suravi yield her milk.

sn: अत्र मध्ये समुद्रस्य कबन्धः प्रतिदृश्यते। स्वर्भानोः सूर्यकल्पस्य सोमसूर्यो जिघांसतः॥
en: Here in the midst of this ocean is seen the hcadless truck of Svarabhanu, (Rahu) who is like the sun himself, lever bent on allowing the sun the moon.

sn: सुवर्णशिरसोऽप्यत्र हरिरोम्णः प्रगायतः। अदृश्यस्याप्रमेयस्य श्रूयते विपुलो ध्वनिः॥
en: Here is heard the loud sound of chanting (the Vedas) by Suvarnashiras who is ever youthful and who is immeasurable and invincible in energy.

sn: अत्र ध्वजवती नाम कुमारी हरिमेधसः। आकाशे तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति तस्थौ सूर्यस्य शासनात्॥
en: Here the daughter of Harimedhas named Dhvajavati remained fixed to the sky by the command of the sun who said-Remain here, remain here.

sn: अत्र वायुस्तथा वह्निरापः खं चापि गालव। आह्निकं चैव नैशं च दुःखं स्पर्श विमुञ्चति॥
en: Here wind and fire and water and earth, O Galava, remain dispossessed of the power of giving pain at their contact, day and night.

sn: अतः प्रभृति सूर्यस्य तिर्यगावर्तते गतिः। अत्र ज्योतींषि सर्वाणि विशन्त्यादित्यमण्डलम्॥
en: From this place forward the sun has recourse to a straight path and here do all the luminous bodies enter the sphere of Aditi (the solar sphere).

sn: अष्टविंशतिरात्रं च चक्रम्य सह भानुना। निष्पतन्ति पुनः सूर्यात् सोमसंयोगयोगतः॥
en: Having journeyed for twenty eight nights in company with the sun they come out again from the solar sphere, being united with the moon.

sn: अत्र नित्यं स्रवन्तीनां प्रभवः सागरोदयः। अत्र लोकत्रयस्यापस्तिष्ठन्ति वरुणालये॥
en: Here in this direction life the sources of rivers from which again rise the seas and here in the region of Varuna are the waters of all the three worlds.

sn: अत्र पन्नगराजस्याप्यनन्तस्य निवेशनम्। अनादिनिधस्यात्र विष्णोः स्थानमनुत्तमम्॥
en: Here is the residence, of Ananta, the king of snakes and here is the place of Vishnu, who has no beginning nor end and than whom nothing is better.

sn: अत्रानलसखस्यापि पवनस्य निवेशनम्। महर्षेः कश्यपस्यात्र मारीचस्य निवेशनम्॥
en: Here is also the residence of Pavana (wind) the friend of Anala (fire) and here is the residence of the great Rishi Kashyapa, the son of Maricha.

sn: एष ते पश्चिमो मार्गो दिग्द्वारेण प्रकीर्तितः। ब्रूहि गालव गच्छावो बुद्धिः का द्विजसत्तम॥
en: This western direction is described to you in the course of my description of the cardinal points; speak, O Galava, ( best among the twice born, in which direction you will go.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: सुपर्ण उवाच यस्मादुत्तार्यते पापाद् यस्मान्निःश्रेयसोऽश्नुते। अस्मादुत्तारणबलादुत्तरेत्युच्यते द्विज॥
en: Suparna said Since a man is absolved from his sins in this quarter and since he attains salvation here, it is called North (Uttara), O twice born one, from its power of absolution (uttarana).

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: उत्तरस्य हिरण्यस्य परिवापश्च गालव। मार्गः पश्चिमपूर्वाभ्यां दिग्भ्यां वै मध्यमः स्मृतः॥
en: And since the north, which is the region of gold (and other treasures) stretches between the west and the east therefore is it called the central region.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: अस्यां दिशि वरिष्ठायामुत्तरायां द्विजर्षभ। नासौम्यो नाविधेयात्मा नाधर्मो वसते जनः॥
en: In this region, the north, which is the best, O best among the twice born, none that is not tranquil, none that has not brought his soul under control and none that is vicious, lives.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: अत्र नारायणः कृष्णो जिष्णुश्चैव नरोत्तमः। बदर्यामाश्रमपदे तथा ब्रह्मा च शाश्वतः॥
en: Here lives Narayana, the ever victorious Krishna, that best among men in the hermitage of Badri and so does Brahma.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: अत्र वै हिमवत्पृष्ठे नित्यमास्ते महेश्वरः। प्रकृत्या पुरुषः सार्धं युगान्ताग्निसमप्रभः॥
en: Here on the breast of the Himayat mountain even lives Maheshvara who is endued with effulgence like that of the fire which blazes at the termination of each Yuga, like Purusha in company with Prakriti.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: न स दृश्यो मुनिगणैस्तथा देवैः सवासवैः। गन्धर्वयक्षसिद्धैर्वा नरनारायणादृते॥
en: He is invisible by the group of Munis as also by the gods along with Vasava and by the Gandharvas and Yakshas who have attained salvation, indeed by all save by Nara and Narayana.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: अत्र विष्णुः सहस्राक्षः सहस्रचरणोऽव्ययः। सहस्रशिरसः श्रीमानेकः पश्यति मायया।॥
en: Here lives the eternal Vishnu of a thousand eye, a thousand feet and a thousand heads who appears one with the aid of illusion.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: अत्र राज्येन विप्राणां चन्द्रमाश्चाभ्यषिच्यत। अत्र गङ्गां महादेवः पतन्तीं गगनाच्च्युताम्॥
en: Here was the moon entrusted with the kingship over regenerate persons and here Mahadeva let fall the Ganga, which descended from the sky,

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: प्रतिगृह्य ददौ लोके मानुषे ब्रह्मवित्तम। अत्र देव्या तपस्तप्तं महेश्वरपरीप्सया॥
en: After receiving her on his head, to the world of men, O you best among those that know Brahma; here was asceticism practiced by the goddess (Uma) with the desire of getting Maheshvara for her husband.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: अत्र कामश्च रोषश्च शैलचोमा च सम्बभुः। अत्र राक्षसयक्षाणां गन्धर्वाणां च गालव॥ आधिपत्येन कैलासे धनदोऽप्यभिषेचितः। अत्र चैत्ररथं रम्यमत्र वैखानसाश्रमः॥
en: Here were born Kama (the god of love) Rosha (the ire of Shiva), the Kailasa mountain as also Uma; and here, O Galava, over the Rakshasas and Yakshas and Gandharvas, was the giver of wealth (Kubera) anointed king in the Kailasa; here is suitable the pleasure garden of Kubera-the enchanting Chaitraratha and here is situate the hermitage of the class of Rishis known as Vaikhanas.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: अत्र मन्दाकिनी चैव मन्दरश्च द्विजर्षभ। अत्र सौगन्धिकवनं नैर्ऋतैरभिरक्ष्यते॥
en: Here are situate the Mandakini (river) and the Mandara (mountain) O best among the twice born and here is the wood named Saugandhanika which is guarded by Rakshasas.

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: शाद्वलं कदलीस्कन्धमत्र संतानका नगाः। अत्र संयमनित्यानां सिद्धानां स्वैरचारिणाम्॥
en: Here are plains covered with green grass and groups of plantain trees and the celestial trees, the Santanakas and in this quarter the Siddhas, who have ever their passions under control and who always roam about at their pleasure,

description: The search of a bridegroom by Matali
sn: विमानान्यनुरूपाणि कामभोग्यानि गालव। अत्र ते ऋषयः सप्त देवी चारुन्धती तथा॥
en: Have their abodes resembling the heaven and replete with all objects of enjoyment; and here live the seven Rishis and also the Goddess Arundhati.

sn: गालव उवाच गरुत्मन् भुजगेन्द्रारे सुपर्ण विनतात्मज। नय मां तार्क्ष्य पूर्वेण यत्र धर्मस्य चक्षुषी॥
en: Galava said O Garuda, O enemy of the chief among serpents, O Suparna, O son of Vinata, 0 Tarkshya, take me to the east, where are pointed the two eyes of Dharma.

sn: पूर्वमेतां दिशं गच्छ या पूर्वं परिकीर्तिता। देवतानां हि सांनिध्यमत्र कीर्तितवानसि॥
en: Go to this eastern quarter which you have described first of all and which you have described as lying in the vicinity of virtue.

sn: अत्र सत्यं च धर्मश्च त्वया सम्यक् प्रकीर्तितः। इच्छेयं तु समागन्तुं समस्तैर्दैवतैरहम्। भूयश्च तान् सुरान् द्रष्टुमिच्छेयमरुणानुज॥
en: Here, you have said, truth and virtue reside. I desire to see those gods, O you the younger brother of Aruna.

sn: नारद उवाच तमाह विनतासूनुरारोह स्वेति वै द्विजम्। आरुरोहाथ स मुनिर्गरुडं गालवस्तदा॥
en: Narada said The son of Vinata said to the twice-born one get you up on me and then the Muni Galava rode on Garuda.

sn: गालव उवाच क्रममाणस्य ते रूपं दृश्यते पन्नगाशन। भास्करस्येव पूर्वाह्ने सहस्रांशोर्विवस्वतः॥
en: Galava said I come to see your beauty, you devourer of snakes, while you are flying along, like at of the sun in the first part of the day, of the sun of a thousand rays.

sn: पक्षवातप्रणुन्नानां वृक्षाणामनुगामिनाम्। प्रस्थितानामिव समं पश्यामीह गतिं खग॥
en: Your course, O wanderer in the sky, I see followed by trees which have been uprooted by the wind caused by the flapping of your wings.

sn: ससागरवनामुर्वी सशैलवनकाननाम्। आकर्षनिव चाभासि पक्षवातेन खेचर॥
en: O you wanderer of sky, you shine as if dragging by the wind, caused by the flapping of wings, the earth bounded by the seas and the forests with its mountains, woods and gardens.

sn: समीननागनक्रं च खमिवारोप्यते जलम्। वायुना चैव महता पक्षवातेन चानिशम्॥
en: The water, along with its fishes, snakes and crocodiles, seems to rise up continually to the sky by the great wind caused by your wings,

sn: तुल्यरूपाननान् मत्स्यांस्तथा तिमितिर्मिगिलान्। नागाश्वनरवक्त्रांश्च पश्याम्युन्मथितानिव॥
en: The fishes, and Timis and Timingalas possessed of similar faces and and snakes possessed of faces like those of human beings are, I see, crushed, as it were, by the wind.

sn: महार्णवस्य च रवैः श्रोत्रे मे बधिरे कृते। न शृणोमि न पश्यामि नात्मनो वेद्मि कारणम्॥
en: I am rendered deaf by hearing the loud roar of the great sea; I cannot see nor can hear; indeed I even forget the object of this journey.

sn: शनैः स तु भवान् यातु ब्रह्मवध्यामनुस्मरन्। न दृश्यते रविस्तात न दिशो न च खं खग॥
en: You please go a little slowly, remembering that you may be responsible for slaying a Brahmana; the sun is invisible, my friend, and cardinal points as also the sky, O you wanderer of heavens.

sn: तम एव तु पश्याम शरीरं ते न लक्षये। मणीव जात्यौ पश्यामि चक्षुषी तेऽहमण्डज॥
en: I see a gloom around me, but your body I cannot see, and you born of an egg, your two eyes appear to me like two bright gems.

sn: शरीरं तु न पश्यामि तव चैवात्मनश्च ह। पदे पदे तु पश्यामि शरीरादग्निमुत्थितम्॥
en: I do not see your body nor mine own and at every step do I see fire coming from your। body.

sn: स मे निर्वाप्य सहसा चक्षुषी शाम्य ते पुनः। तन्नियच्छ महावेगं गमने विनतात्मजः॥
en: Extinguish at once this fire and let your cyes again be brought to their normal state and, O son of Vinata, slacken the great speed you are using in your journey.

sn: न मे प्रयोजनं किंचिद् गमने पन्नगाशन। संनिवर्त महाभाग न वेगं विषहामि ते॥
en: I have no need whatever of this journey, O you who subsist on snakes; return, O you of great attributes, for I can not bear this speed of yours.

sn: गुरवे संश्रुतानीह शतान्यष्टौ हि वाजिनाम्। एकतः श्यामकर्णानां शुभ्राणां चन्द्रवर्चसाम्॥
en: I have promised to present to my preceptor eight hundred horses, white as the rays of moon and having one ear black.

sn: तेषां चैवापवर्गाय मार्ग पश्यामि नाण्डज। ततोऽयं जीवितत्यागे दृष्टो मार्गो मयाऽऽत्मनः॥
en: To redeem my pledge I see no means, O you born of an egg; the only way I can see therefore is to cast off my own life.

sn: नैव मेऽस्ति धनं किंचिन्न धनेनान्वितः सुहृत्। न चार्थेनापि महता शक्यमेतद् व्यपोहितुम्॥
en: I do not possess wealth; nor have I any friend possessed of wealth and even with great wealth this object of mine cannot be gained.

sn: नारद उवाच एवं बहु च दीनं च ब्रुवाणं गालवं तदा। प्रत्युवाच व्रजन्नेव प्रहसन् विनतात्मजः॥
en: Narada said Then to Galava, who was lamenting in this way and uttering many sorrowful things, the son of Vinata, while still proceeding along, said in reply laughing.

sn: नातिप्रज्ञोऽसि विप्रर्षे योऽऽत्मानंत्यक्तुमिच्छसि। न चापि कृत्रिमः कालः कालो हि परमेश्वरः॥
en: You do not seem to be a very wise man, O regenerate Rishi, since you desire to cast off your life; death cannot be met at one's own pleasure for death is God himself.

sn: किमहं पूर्वमेवेह भवता नाभिचोदितः। उपायोऽत्र महानस्ति येनैतदुपपद्यते॥
en: Why have not I been informed (of your purpose) before; there is every good means by which you will gain your object.

sn: तदेष ऋषभो नाम पर्वतः सागरान्तिके। अत्र विश्रम्य भुक्त्वा च निवर्तिष्याव गालव॥
en: This is the mountain named Rishava on the limits of the sea; rest yourself here; after making our repast here we shall return, O Galava.

sn: नारद उवाच ऋषभस्य ततः शृङ्गं निपत्य द्विजपक्षिणौ। शाण्डिली ब्राह्मणी तत्र ददृशाते तपोऽन्विताम्॥
en: Narada said Then having alighted on the peak of the Rishava mountain, the two saw there a Brahmani named Shandili, endued with asceticism.

sn: अभिवाद्य सुपर्णस्तु गालवश्चाभिपूज्य ताम्। तया च स्वागतेनोक्तौ विष्टरे संनिषीदतुः॥
en: Suparna having done her honors, and Galava having worshipped her they were pointed to a seat by her after the usual welcome.

sn: सिद्धमन्नं तया दत्तं बलिमन्त्रोपबृंहितम्। भुक्त्वा तृप्तावुभौ भूमौ सुप्तौ तावनुमोहितौ॥
en: Both, of them, having partaken of the cooked food offered by her after having dedicated the same to the gods with the usual Mantra, were refreshed and both of them slept on the ground and in a moment lost their senses.

sn: मुहूर्तात् प्रतिबुद्धस्तु सुपर्णो गमनेप्सया। अथ भ्रष्टतनूजाङ्गमात्मानं ददृशे खगः॥
en: After a moment Suparna awoke with the desire of departing and the wanderer of the sky saw himself deprived of his wings.

sn: मांसपिण्डोपमोऽभूत् स मुखपादान्वितः खगः। गालवस्तं तथा दृष्ट्वा विमनाः पर्यपृच्छत॥
en: The ranger of the sky became like a lump of flesh with a mouth and feet and Galava seeing him in that condition asked him with a heavy heart.

sn: किमिदं भवता प्राप्तमिहागमनजं फलम्। वासोऽयमिह कालं तु कियन्तं नौ भविष्यति॥
en: "What is this condition you find yourself in, as a result of your doing here, for what length of time shall we have to live here.

sn: किं नु ते मनसा ध्यातमशुभं धर्मदूषणम्। न ह्ययं भवतः स्वल्पो व्यभिचारो भविष्यति॥
en: Is it that in your mind you have entertained a thought which is evil and against the dictates of virtue; this is the result of no small wickedness on your part.

sn: सुपर्णोऽथाब्रवीद् विप्रं प्रध्यातं वै मया द्विज। इमां सिद्धामितो नेतुं तत्र यत्र प्रजापतिः॥
en: Suparna then said to the regenerate one o twice born one, the thought has indeed been entertained by me of carrying away this lady who has been endued with asceticism from this place to where the lord of all creatures is,

sn: यत्र देवो महादेवो यत्र विष्णुः सनातनः। यत्र धर्मश्च यज्ञश्च तत्रेयं निवसेदिति॥
en: Where resides the lord Mahadeva, where resides the eternal Vishnu and where there are virtue and sacrificial ceremonies, so that she might live there.

sn: सोऽहं भगवती याचे प्रणतः प्रियकाम्यया। मयैतन्नाम प्रध्यातं मनसा शोचता किल॥
en: I now pray this goddess for my own good with my head bowed down: I have harbored this thought in my mind and have come to grief consequence thereof.

sn: तदेवं बहुमानात् ते मयेहानीप्सितं कृतम्। सुकृतं दुष्कृतं वात्वं माहात्म्यात् क्षन्तुमर्हसि॥
en: Out of great respect (for you) did I entertain the thought and whether I did right or wrong, it is fitting that out of your own generosity and noble mindedness you should forgive me. in

sn: सा तौ तदाब्रवीत् तुष्टा पतगेन्द्रद्विजर्षभौ। न भेतव्यं सुपर्णोऽसि सुपर्ण त्यज सम्भ्रमम्॥
en: She, thus spoken to, was gratified with the chief of birds and said "Do not fear, O Suparna, become possessed of beautiful wings and leave aside your fears.

sn: निन्दितास्मि त्वया वत्स न च निन्दा क्षमाम्यहम्। लोकेभ्यः सपदि भ्रश्येद् यो मां निन्देत पापकृत्॥
en: I have been insulted by your child and I do not forgive insults; that perpetrator of wicked deeds, who would insult me, would quickly be turned out of all regions of bliss.

sn: हीनयालक्षणैः सर्वैस्तथानिन्दितया मया। आचारं प्रतिगृह्णन्त्या सिद्धिः प्राप्तेयमुत्तमा॥
en: Devoid as I am of all inauspicious signs, and who am blameless, I have obtained excellent asceticism by following the rules of good conduct.

sn: आचारः फलते धर्ममाचारः फलते धनम्। आचाराच्छ्यिमाप्नोति आचारो हन्त्यलक्षणम्॥
en: Good conduct produces virtue, good conduct produces wealth and it is from good conduct that a man attains to prosperity; and good conduct nullifies all inauspicious signs.

sn: तदायुष्मन् खगपते यथेष्टं गम्यतामितः। न च ते गर्हणीयाऽहं गर्हितव्याः स्त्रियः क्वचित्॥
en: Do you now, O lord of the rangers of the firinament, go wherever you like; no woman should henceforth be found fault with by you even when she ought to be blamed.

sn: भवितासि यथापूर्वं बलवीर्यसमन्वितः। बभूवतुस्ततस्तस्य पक्षौ द्रविणवत्तरौ॥
en: You will be endued with strength and prowess as before;" then did his two wings grow up and they were even stronger than before.

sn: अनुज्ञातस्तु शाण्डिल्या यथागतमुपागमत्। नैव चासादयामास तथारूपांस्तुरंगमान्॥
en: Being commanded by Shandili he then went away where he wanted to go (with Galava on his back) but did not come across horses of that description.

sn: विश्वामित्रोऽथ तं दृष्ट्वागालवं चाध्वनि स्थितः। उवाच वदतां श्रेष्ठो वैनतेयस्य संनिधौ॥
en: Vishvamitra, while standing on the path, saw Galava and that foremost among speakers said in the presence of the son of Vinata.

sn: यस्त्वया स्वयमेवार्थः प्रतिज्ञातो मम द्विज। तस्य कालोऽपवर्गस्य यथा वा मन्यते भवान्॥
en: The wealth that you, of your own accord, promised me, O twice-born one, should be given to me; the time to receive the fruit of that promise has come, you can do as you like.

sn: प्रतीक्षिष्याम्यहं कालमेतावन्तं तथा परम्। यथा संसिध्यते विप्र स मार्गस्तु निशाम्यताम्॥
en: As I have waited all this time, so shall I wait for some time more, and Oregenerate being, look out for that means by which you may be successful.
