sn: सुपर्णोऽथाब्रवीद् दीनं गालवं भृशदुःखितम्। प्रत्यक्षं खल्विदानी मे विश्वामित्रो यदुक्तवान्।॥
en: Suparna then said to Galava who was struck with great sorrow, "What Vishvamitra said to you before, he has repeated in my presence.

sn: तदागच्छ द्विजश्रेष्ठ मन्त्रयिष्याव गालव। नादत्त्वा गुरवे शक्यं कृत्स्नमर्थत्वयाऽऽसितुम्॥
en: Therefore do you come, O foremost among the twice-born, we shall consult together ( Galava; without giving to your preceptor the whole of the wealth promised by you, you cannot even sit down."

sn: नारद उवाच अथाह गालवं दीनं सुपर्णः पततां वरः। निर्मितं वाह्निना भूमौ वायुना शोधितं तथा। यस्माद्धिरण्मयं सर्वं हिरण्यं तेन चोच्यते॥
en: Narada said Then did Suparna, the foremost among those possessed of wings, say to the grieving Greeted: "Created by Fire in the Earth and reared up by wind, wealth is called Hiranya for the earth itself named Hiranmaya.

sn: धत्ते धारयते चेदमेतस्मात् कारणाद् धनम्। तदेतत् त्रिषु लोकेषु धनं तिष्ठति शाश्वतम्॥
en: Since it supports and maintains the (creatures of the earth Therefore is it called wealth (Dhana); and the wealth is in the three worlds from time immemorial for meeting this purpose.

sn: नित्यं प्रोष्ठपदाभ्यां च शुक्रे धनपतौ तथा। मनुष्येभ्यः समादत्ते शुक्रश्चित्तार्जितं धनम्॥
en: On a Friday when either of the two constellations is ascendant, Agni, creating wealth by dint of his will, confers it upon mankind for multiplying the possessions of the giver of riches (Kubera).

sn: अजैकपादहिर्बुध्यै रक्ष्यते धनदेन च। एवं न शक्यते लब्धुमलब्धव्यं द्विजर्षभ। ऋते च धनमश्वानां नावाप्तिर्विद्यते तव।॥
en: That wealth is guarded by the Ajaikapada and the Ahibrudhnyas as also by the giver of wealth (Kubera): such being the case, O best among the twice-born, it is very difficult to get that wealth.

sn: स त्वं याचात्र राजानं कंचिद् राजर्षिवंशजम्। अपीड्य राजा पौरान् हि यो नौ कुर्यात् कृतार्थिनौ॥
en: Except by wealth there exists possibility of your getting the horses. Such being the case do you ask some king born in some family of royal Rishi who can make us successful without oppressing his subjects.

sn: अस्ति सोमान्ववाये मे जातः कश्चिन्नृपः सखा। अभिगच्छावहे तं वै तस्यास्ति विभवो भुवि॥
en: There is a king born in the dynasty of the moon, who is my friend and we shall approach him for he has great wealth in this world.

sn: ययाति म राजर्षिर्नाहुषः सत्यविक्रमः। स दास्यति मया चोक्तो भवता चार्थितः स्वयम्॥
en: He is the royal Rishi named Yayati, son of Nahusha, who is of truly great strength, and he will himself give (what we want, when he is asked you and (your suit is) recommended by me. no

sn: विभवश्चास्य सुमहानासीद् धनपतेरिव। एवं गुस्धन विद्वन् दानेनैव विशोधय॥
en: His wealth is as great as that of the lord of riches and O learned man, repay your debt by accepting this large wealth as present.

sn: तथा तौ कथयन्तौ च चिन्तयन्तौ च यत् क्षमम्। प्रतिष्ठाने नरपतिं ययातिं प्रत्युपस्थितौ॥
en: Thus conversing and thus thinking on what could be done they came to the palace of Yayati, the lord of men.

sn: प्रतिगृह्य च सत्कारैरर्घ्यपाद्यादिकं वरम्। पृष्टश्चागमने हेतुमुवाच विनतासुतः॥
en: Having accepted the usual warm welcome and Arghya a and water for washing the feet etc. they were asked the reason of their coming and the son of Vinata thus explained the reasons:

sn: अयं मे नाहुष सखा गालवस्तपसो निधिः। विश्वामित्रस्य शिष्योऽभूत् वर्धाण्ययुतशो नृप॥
en: O you born in the race of Nahusha, this is my friend Galava, the ocean of austerities who became the pupil of Vishvamitra for many tens of thousands years, Oruler of men.

sn: सोऽयं तेनाभ्यनुज्ञात उपकारेप्सया द्विजः। तमाह भगवन् किं ते ददानि गुरुदक्षिणाम्॥
en: This twice born one, then being commanded to go away by Vishvamitra, with a view to give him a present said to him; O lord, the time has come when I should make some final present to my spiritual guide.

sn: असकृत् तेन चोक्तेन किंचिदागतमन्युना। अयमुक्तः प्रयच्छेति जानता विभवं लघु॥
en: Knowing that his means were small he did not ask for anything but being addressed again and again, was thus commanded: You who have said this, make me this present.

sn: एकतः श्यामकर्णानां शुभ्राणां शुद्धजन्मनाम्। अष्टौ शतानि मे देहि हयानां चन्द्रवर्चसाम्॥
en: Give me eight hundred horses white as the rays of the moon, of good birth and black of one ear.

sn: गुर्वर्थो दीयतामेष यदि गालव मन्यसे। इत्येवमाह सक्रोधो विश्वामित्रस्तपोधनः॥
en: Make this present to your spiritual guide if you think fit, O Galava. Thus did the great ascetic Vishvamitra address him in anger.

sn: सोऽयं शोकेन महता तप्यमानो द्विजर्षभः। अशक्तः प्रतिकर्तुं तद् भवन्तं शरणं गतः॥
en: This best among the twice born, is for this reason, being consumed by heavy grief being unable to redeem his pledge and therefore he has come under your protection.

sn: प्रतिगृह्य नरव्याघ्र त्वत्तो भिक्षां गतव्यथः। कृत्वापवर्ग गुरवे चरिष्यति महत् तपः॥
en: Having accepted from you along, O you best among men and thus being beyond the reach of sorrow after fulfilling his pledge to his spiritual guide, he will practice great asceticism.

sn: तपसः संविभागेन भवन्तमपि योक्ष्यते। स्वेन राजर्षितपसा पूर्णं त्वां पूरयिष्यति॥
en: With a portion of the fruit of his austerities will you also be rewarded for with his own devotion will he enrich you, O royal Rishi, who are rich in earthly treasures.

sn: यावन्ति रोमाणि हये भवन्तीह नरेश्वर। तावन्तो वाजिनो लोकान् प्राप्नुवन्ति महीपते॥
en: As many hairs as there are in the bodies of horses, O lord of men, so many horses will you obtain in this world, O lord of the earth.

sn: पात्रं प्रतिग्रहस्यायं दातुं पात्रं तथा भवान्। शो क्षीरमिवासिक्तं भवत्वेतत् तथोपमम्॥
en: He is a fit party to receive gifts and you too are a fit party to make presents, and the present that you now make to him will be like milk kept in deposit in a conch shell (available at any moment).

sn: नारद उवाच एवमुक्तः सुपर्णेन तथ्यं वचनमुत्तमम्। विमृश्यावहितो राजा निश्चित्य च पुनः पुनः॥
en: Narada said Being thus addressed by Suparna in excellent words conducive to his benefit and think calmly on these words and considering them again and again,

sn: यष्टा क्रतुसहस्राणां दाता दानपतिः प्रभुः। ययातिः सर्वकाशीश इदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: The performer of a thousand sacrifices and the lord who, in gifts, was the prince of givers, Yayati, the ruler of all the Kashis said these words,

sn: दृष्ट्वा प्रियसखं टायं गालवं च द्विजर्षभम्। निदर्शनं च तपसा भिक्षा श्लाघ्यां च कीर्तिताम्॥
en: With his eye on his dear friend Tarkshya, as also on the best among the twice-born, Galava, and considering the alms asked for by a devotee as described to him as a highly praiseworthy example,

sn: अतीत्य च नृपानन्यानादित्यकुलसम्भवान्। मत्सकाशमनुप्राप्तावेतां बुद्धिमवेक्ष्य च॥
en: And especial considering that they had come to him passing over the kings born in the solar race.

sn: अद्य मे सफलं जन्म तारितं चाद्य मे कुलम्। अद्यायं तारितो देशो मम तार्क्ष्य त्वयानघ।॥
en: To-day is my birth blessed and my race absolved from sins; to-day is this country, over which I rule, freed from sins by you, O Tarkshya, who are sinless.

sn: वक्तुमिच्छामि तु सखे यथा जानासि मां पुरा। न तथा वित्तवानस्मि क्षीणं वित्तं च मे सखे।॥
en: O friend, I want to tell you however that I am not the same wealthy man that you knew me to be in days of old. O friend, my wealth has been diminished

sn: न च शक्तोऽस्मि ते कर्तुं मोघमागमनं खग। न चाशामस्य विप्रर्षेवितथीकर्तुमुत्सहे॥ तत् तु दास्यामि यत् कार्यमिदं सम्पादयिष्यति। अभिगम्य हताशो हि निवृत्तो दहते कुलम्॥
en: But at the same time I am unable to make your coming here useless, 0 wanderer of the heavens; nor do I dare frustrate the hopes entertained by the regenerate Rishi; I shall therefore give that which will accomplish this purposes of his.

sn: नातः परं वैनतेय किंचित् पापिष्ठमुच्यते। यथाशानाशनाल्लोके देहि नास्तीति वा वचः॥
en: A man, who having come to another with a hope and returns with that hope frustrated, consumes the entire race; and O son of Vinata, it is said that nothing is more

sn: हताशो ह्यकृतार्थः सन् हतः सम्भावितो नरः। हिनस्ति तस्य पुत्रांश्च पौत्रांश्चाकुर्वतो हितम्॥
en: Capable than the saying of a man, in this world "I have not got it" to a man who comes to him entertaining a hope in him. The man, who is unsuccessful in his suit and whose hopes are frustrated,

sn: तस्माच्चतुर्णां वंशानां स्थापयित्री सुता मम। इयं सुरसुतप्रख्या सर्वधर्मोपचायिनी॥
en: Slays the sons and grandsons of the man who dose not do him good. Therefore this daughter of mine, who will be perpetuator of four races,

sn: प्रदास्यन्ति नृपा सदा देवमनुष्याणामसुराणां च गालव। कादिक्षता रूपतो बाला सुता मे प्रतिगृह्यताम्॥
en: This one resembling the daughter of a god and the promoter of every virtue and who is ever solicited by the gods, human beings and Asuras, O Galava,

sn: अस्याः शुल्कं राज्यमपि ध्रुवम्। किं पुनः श्यामकर्णानां हयानां द्वे चतुः शते॥
en: For her beauty do you accept. Rulers of men will surely you even their kingdom as her dowry,

sn: स भवान् प्रतिगृह्णातु ममैतां माधवीं सुताम्। अहं दौहित्रवान् स्यां वै वर एष मम प्रभो॥
en: Not to speak of twice four hundred horses each with a black ear; therefore do you accept this daughter of mine, Madhvi.

sn: प्रतिगृह्य च तां कन्यां गालवः सह पक्षिणा। पुनर्द्रक्ष्याव इत्युक्त्वा प्रतस्थे सह कन्यया॥
en: The only boon that I ask for, O lord, is that I may have a grandson by her.” Having taken that girl with them Galava with the bird,

sn: उपलब्धमिदं द्वारमश्वानामिति चाण्डजः। उक्त्वा गालवमापृच्छ्य जगाम भवनं स्वकम्॥
en: And saying "we see you again” went away. Saying: “The means for obtaining the horses has now been gained," the one born of an egg too

sn: गते पतगराजे तु गालवः सह कन्यया। चिन्तयानः क्षमं दाने राज्ञां वै शुल्कतोऽगमत्॥
en: Went away, after for the permission of Galava, to his own place. And the king of birds having gone away Galava along with that maiden,

sn: सोऽगच्छन्मनसेक्ष्वाकुं हर्यश्वं राजसत्तमम्। अयोध्यायां महावीर्यं चतुरङ्गबलान्वितम्॥
en: Began to think about the king who could offer suitable dowry for her and in his mind decided to go to that best among the kingsHaryashva, of the race of Ikshvaku.

sn: कोशधान्यबलोपेतं प्रियपौरं द्विजप्रियम्। प्रजाभिकामं शाम्यन्तं कुर्वाणं तप उत्तमम्॥
en: He ruled over Ayodhya, was endued with great over Ayodhya, was endued with great prowess and had an army with four divisions and had also in his possession enough of treasures and coins, who was dear to his subject and to whom the twice born were also dear,

sn: तमुवागम्य विप्रः स हर्यश्वं गालवोऽब्रवीत्। कन्येयं मम राजेन्द्र प्रसवैः कुलवर्धिनी॥
en: Who desirous of the peace of his subjects was practicing excellent austerities. The regenerate Rishi Galava, Having approached him, Haryashva, said to him:

sn: इयं शुल्केन भार्यार्थं हर्यश्व प्रतिगृह्यताम्। शुल्कं ते कीर्तयिष्यामि तच्छ्रुत्वा सम्प्रधार्यताम्॥
en: "This girl in my possession, O chief among kings, increases a race by bringing forth children, O Haryashva; accept her by offering a dowry. I shall describe to you what dowry, to offer and hearing that you decide it."

sn: नारद उवाच हर्यश्वस्त्वब्रवीद् राजा विचिन्त्य बहुधा ततः। दीर्घमुष्णं च निःश्वस्य प्रजाहेतोर्नृपोत्तमः॥
en: Narada said The king Haryashva, the best among rulers of men, having thought in his mind for a long time, said having drawn a long and hot sigh about the birth of a son.

sn: उन्नतेषूनता षट्सु सूक्ष्मा सूक्ष्मेषु पञ्चसु। गम्भीरा त्रिषु गम्भीरेष्वियं रक्ता च पञ्चसु॥
en: “Those six limbs that ought to be elevated are elevated (in this girl) and the seven ought to be slender are so; the three that ought to be deep are deep and the five that ought to be red are red.

sn: बहुदेवासुरालोका बहुगन्धर्वदर्शना। बहुलक्षणसम्पन्ना बहुप्रसवधारिणी॥
en: She is fit be looked at by many gods, Asuras and men and by many Gandharvas and she is endued with many auspicious signs and capable of bringing forth many children.

sn: समर्थेयं जनयितुं चक्रवर्तिनमात्मजम्। ब्रूहि शुल्कं द्विजश्रेष्ठ समीक्ष्य विभवं मम॥
en: I am competent to beget on her a son who will be an emperor; speak about the dowry, O foremost the twice born, having paid due regard to the state of my wealth.

sn: गालव उवाच एकतः श्यामकर्णानां शतान्यष्टौ प्रयच्छ मे। हयानां चन्द्रशुभ्राणां देशजानां वपुष्मताम्॥
en: Galava said Give me eight hundred horses, white as the moon, born in this country, and with plump bodies, cach having one ear black.

sn: ततस्तव भवित्रीयं पुत्राणां जननी शुभा। अरणीव हुताशानां योनिरायतलोचना॥
en: Then will this blessed maiden with large eyes, be the mother of your children as the fire stick is mother of fire.

sn: नारद उवाच एतच्छ्रुत्वा वचो राजा हर्यश्वः काममोहितः। उवाच गालव दीनो राजर्षिर्ऋषिसत्तमम्॥
en: Narada said The king Haryashva, that royal sage, hearing these words, senseless with passion, said sorrowfully to that best among the Rishis.

sn: द्वे मे शते संनिहिते हयानां यद्विधास्तव। एष्टव्याः शतशस्त्वन्ये चरन्ति मम वाजिनः॥
en: “The kind of horses that you require, two hundred only I have; got; hundreds of other breeds of horses, all worthy of sacrifice, are roaming about (in my kingdom)

sn: सोऽहमेकमपत्यं वै जनयिष्यामि गालव। अस्यामेतं भवान् काम सम्पादयतु मे वरम्॥
en: Such being the case, I shall beget but one child on this damsel, O Galava; kindly act up to this request of mine."

sn: एतच्छ्रुत्वा तु सा कन्या गालवं वाक्यमब्रवीत्। मम दत्तो वरः कश्चित् केनचिद् ब्रह्मवादिना॥
en: Hearing these words, the damsel said to Galava: “A boon has granted to me by a certain being conversant with Brahma,

sn: प्रसूत्यन्ते प्रसूत्यन्ते कन्यैव त्वं भविष्यसि। स त्वं ददस्व मां राज्ञे प्रतिगृह्य हयोत्तमान्॥
en: That after giving birth to each child I shall again be a virgin; therefore do you offer me to this king accepting these best of horses.

sn: नृपेभ्यो हि चतुर्थ्यस्ते पूर्णान्यष्टौ शतानि मे। भविष्यन्ति तथा पुत्रा मम चत्वार एव च।॥
en: By going to four kings in succession you will get the full complement of eight hundred (horse) and I too shall have four sons.

sn: क्रियतामुपसंहारो गुर्वर्थं द्विजसत्तम। एषा तावन्मम प्रज्ञा यथा वा मन्यसे द्विज॥
en: Give me up therefore in order that you may be able to redeem the pledge made to your spiritual guide; so do I think with my humble wisdom and you can you can as you like.

sn: एवमुक्तस्तु स मुनिः कन्यया गालवस्तदा। हर्यश्वं पृथिवीपालमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: was The Muni Galava, being thus addressed by that said these words to the lord of the earth, Haryashva.

sn: इयं कन्या नरश्रेष्ठ हर्यश्व प्रतिगृह्यताम्। चतुर्भागेन शुल्कस्य जनयस्वैकमात्मजम्॥
en: Accept this maiden, O Haryashva, O foremost among men, by the offer of a fourth part of her dowry and beget on her but one child."

sn: प्रतिगृह्य स तां कन्यां गालवं प्रतिनन्द्य च। समये देशकाले च लब्धवान् सुतमीप्सितम्॥
en: He, having accepted that girl and having pleased Galava, got the wished for son at the proper time and place.

sn: ततो वसुमना नाम वसुभ्यो वसुमत्तरः। वसुप्रख्यो नरपतिः स बभूव वसुप्रदः॥
en: The prince thereafter named Vasumanas who in wealth was richest and lived to be a king as wealthy as one of the Vasus himself and a giver of wealth.

sn: अथ काले पुनर्धीमान् गालवः प्रत्युपस्थितः। उपसंगम्य चोवाच हर्यश्वं प्रीतमानसम्॥
en: In proper time, the wise Galava again presented himself there and having approached Haryashva said to him whose desire had been satisfied.

sn: जातो नृप सुतस्तेऽयं बालो भास्करसंनिभः। कालो गन्तुं नरश्रेष्ठ भिक्षार्थमपरं नृपम्॥
en: "O ruler of men, you have begotten this son, a boy similar to the sun in effulgence and it is time for me to go another ruler of men to ask for alms."

sn: हर्यश्वः सत्यवचने स्थितः स्थित्वा च पौरुषे। दुर्लभत्वाद्धयानां च प्रददौ माधवीं पुनः॥
en: Haryashva, who was ever ready to abide by his words and who made manliness the basis of his action, gave back Madhvi as he could not procure all the horses himself.

sn: माधवी च पुनर्दीप्तां परित्यज्य नृपश्रियम्। कुमारी कामतो भूत्वा गालवं पृष्ठतोऽन्वयात्॥
en: Madhvi, too abandoning that effulgent royal propriety, become a maiden again of her own will and followed Galava.

sn: त्वय्येव तावत् तिष्ठन्तु हया इत्युक्तवान् द्विजः। प्रययौ कन्यया सार्धं दिवोदासं प्रजेश्वरम्॥
en: "Let the horse remain with you for the present, in company with the maiden, to Divodasa, the ruler of men.

sn: गालव उवाच महावीर्यो महीपाल: काशीनामीश्वरः प्रभुः। दिवोदास इति ख्यातो भैमसेनिनराधिपः॥
en: Galava said This lord, the king of the Kashis, is a ruler of the earth endued with great prowess, and this ruler of men is a descendant of Bhimasena and is known as Divodasa.

sn: तत्र गच्छावहे भद्रे शनैरागच्छ मा शुचः। धार्मिकः संयमे युक्तः सत्ये चैव जनेश्वरः॥
en: There shall I go, gentle lady; follow me with show steps and grieve not, for that ruler of men is virtuous, and ever attached to selfcontrol and truth,

sn: नारद उवाच तमुपागम्य स मुनिया॑यतस्तेन सत्कृतः। गालव: प्रसवस्यार्थं तं नृपं प्रत्यचोदयत्॥
en: Narada said The ascetic to him was received with becoming honours and Galava urged that king to beget children.

sn: दिवोदास उवाच श्रुतमेतन्मया पूर्वं किमुक्त्वा विस्तरं द्विज। काक्षितो हि मयैषोऽर्थः श्रुत्वैव द्विजसत्तम॥
en: Divodasa said I have heard of all this already; what is the necessity of repeating all this in detail. As soon as I heard of this, O best among the twice-born, this object (children) was desired for by me.

sn: एतच्च मे बहुमतं यदुत्सृज्य नराधिपान्। मामेवमुपयातोऽसि भावि चैतदसंशयम्॥
en: This too is a mark of great respect for me that passing by many rulers of men you have come to me and without doubt this will be (i.e. your wishes shall be gratified.)

sn: स एव विभवोऽस्माकमश्वानामपि गालव। अहमेप्येकमेवास्यां जनयिष्यामि पार्थिवम्॥
en: But in the matter of horses, my wealth is exactly like his (Haryashva) O Galava; and I too shall beget only one ruler of the earth on this girl.

sn: तथेत्युक्त्वा द्विजश्रेष्ठः प्रादात् कन्यां महीपतेः। विधिपूर्वां च तां राजा कन्यां प्रतिगृहीतवान्॥
en: The foremost among the twice born, saying, be it so, gave that damsel to the ruler of earth and the king too accepted that girl after suitable ceremonies.

sn: रेमे स तस्यां राजर्षिः प्रभावत्यां यथा रविः। स्वाहायां च यथा वह्निर्यथा शच्यां च वासवः॥
en: The royal Rishi than spotted with her as Ravi (the son) with Prabhavati, as Agni (fire) with Svaha, and as Vasava (Indra) with Sachi;

sn: यथा चन्द्रश्च रोहिण्यां यथा धूमोर्णया यमः। वरुणश्च यथा गौर्यां यथा चा धनेश्वरः॥
en: And as Chandra (moon) with Rohini and as Yama (the god of death) with Urmila; as Varuna (the lord of the waters) with Gauri, and as Kubera (the lord of wealth) with Riddhi;

sn: यथा नारायणो लक्ष्यां जाह्रव्यां च यथोदधिः। यथा रुद्रश्च रुद्राण्यां यता वेद्यां पितामहः॥
en: As Narayana with Lakshmi and as Udadhi (the ocean) with Jahnavi, as Rudra with Rudrani and as the grandsire with the goddess (Sarasvati);

sn: अदृश्यन्त्यां च वासिष्ठो वसिष्ठश्चाक्षमालया। च्यवनश्च सुकन्यायां पुलस्त्यः संध्यया यथा॥
en: As the son of Vasishtha with Adrishyanli and Vasishtha with Akshamala; as Chyavana with Sukanya and as Pulastya with Sandhya,

sn: अगस्त्यश्चापि वैद( सावित्र्यां सत्यवान् यथा। यथा भृगुः पुलोमायामदित्यां कश्यपो यथा।॥
en: As Agastya with the princess of Vidarbha, as Satyavana with Savitri, as Bhrigu with Puloma, as Kashyapa with Aditi;

sn: रेणुकायां यथाऽऽर्चीको हैमवत्यां च कौशिकः। बृहस्पतिश्च तारायां शुक्रश्च शतपर्वणा॥
en: As Jamadagni, the son of Richika with Renuka as the son of Kushika (Vishvamitra) with the princess, Hemavati, as Brihaspati with Tara and Shukra with Shataparva;

sn: यथा भूम्यां भूमिपतिसर्वश्यां च पुरूरवाः। ऋचीकः सत्यवत्यां च सरस्वत्यां यथा मनुः॥
en: As Bhumipati with Bhumi, as Pururavas with Urvashi, as Richika with Satyavati, and as Manu with Sarasvati;

sn: शकुन्तलायां दुष्यन्तो धृत्यां धर्मश्च शाश्वतः। दमयन्त्यां नलश्चैव सत्यवत्यां च नारदः॥
en: As Dushyanta with Shakuntala, as the eternal Dharma with Dhirti, as Nala with Damayanti, and as Narada with Satyavati;

sn: जरत्कारुर्जरत्कार्वां पुलस्त्यश्च प्रतीच्यया। मेनकायां यथोर्णायुस्तुम्बुस्श्चैव रम्भया॥
en: As Jaratkaru with Jaratkaru, as Pulastya with Pratichya, as Urnayas with Menaka and as Tambura with Rambha;

sn: वासुकिः शतशीर्षायां कुमार्यां च धनंजयः। वैदेह्यां च यथा रामो रुक्मिण्यां च जनार्दनः॥
en: As Vasuki with Shatashirsha and as Dhananjaya with Kumari,

sn: तथा तु रममाणस्य दिवोदासस्य भूपतेः। माधवी जनयामास पुत्रमेकं प्रतर्दनम्॥
en: As Rama with the princess of Videha and as Janardana with Rukmini. Then to the king of the earth, Divodasa, sporting with her,

sn: अथाजगाम भगवान् दिवोदासं स गालवः। समये समनुप्राप्ते वचनं चेदमब्रवीत्॥
en: Madhvi did bear a son named Pratardana; and then to Divodasa came the great Rishi Galava.

sn: निर्यातयतु मे कन्यां भवांस्तिष्ठन्तु वाजिनः। यावदन्यत्र गच्छामि शुल्कार्थं पृथिवीपते॥
en: When the proper time came, he said these words "Return me my maiden but let the horses remain with you for the present,

sn: दिवोदासोऽथ धर्मात्मा समये गालवस्य ताम्। कन्यां निर्यातयामास स्थितः सत्ये महीपतिः॥
en: As just now I shall go from here to another king of the earth for her dowry;" the virtuoussouled Divodasa in proper time gave back that damsel to Galava for that ruler of the earth was establish in truth.

sn: नारद उवाच तथैव तां श्रियं त्यक्त्वा कन्या भूत्वा यशस्विनी। माधवी गालवं विप्रमभ्ययात् सत्यसंगरा॥
en: Narada said In that way having abandoned that prosperity, the renowned lady Madhvi once more becoming a maiden and according to her promise followed the regenerate Rishi Galava.

sn: गालवो विमृशन्नेव स्वकार्यगतमानसः। जगाम भोजनगरं द्रष्टुमौशीनरं नृपम्॥
en: Galava, whose mind was centered in the accomplishment of his own purpose, after due deliberation, went to the city of the Bhojas to see the ruler of men, the son of Ushinara.

sn: तमुवाचाथ गत्वा स नृपतिं सत्यविक्रमम्। इयं कन्या सुतौ द्वौ ते जनयिष्यति पार्थिवौ॥
en: And going to that ruler of men endued with true prowess he said "This damsel will bear you two sons who will be kings of the earth.

sn: अस्यां भवानवाप्तार्थो भविता प्रेत्य चेह च। सोमार्कप्रतिसंकाशौ जनयित्वा सुतौ नृप॥
en: By this means, you will gain your object after death, as also in this world, having begotten two sons, O ruler of men, equal in effulgence to the moon and the sun.

sn: शुल्कं तु सर्वधर्मज्ञ हयानां चन्द्रवर्चसाम्। एकतः श्यामकर्णानां देयं मह्यं चतुःशतम्॥
en: The dowry is, O you conversant with all virtue, that you should give me four hundred horses like the rays of the moon and having one ear black.

sn: गुर्वर्थोऽयं समारम्भो न हयैः कृत्यमस्ति मे। यदि शक्यं महाराज क्रियतामविचारितम्॥
en: For the sake of my spiritual guide that do I make these efforts for the horses and it is not for myself; if you are prepared to act thus, O great king, do what I have said without any reflection or hesitation.

sn: अनपत्योऽसि राजर्षे पुत्रौ जनय पार्थिव। पितृन् पुत्रप्लवेन त्वमात्मानं चैव तारय॥
en: You are without children, O royal Rishi; beget then two sons, O ruler of the earth, and by means of these rafts in the shape of sons do you obtain salvation for yourself and for your ancestors.

sn: न पुत्रफलभोक्ता हि राजर्षे पात्यते दिवः। न याति नरकं घोरं यथा गच्छन्त्यनात्मजाः॥
en: A man, enjoying the fruit of begetting a son, O royal Rishi, never falls down from heaven and never goes to the terrific hell where goes he who has no child."

sn: एतच्चान्यच्च विविधं श्रुत्वा गालवभाषितम्। उशीनरः प्रतिवचो ददौ तस्य नराधिपः॥
en: Having heard all this and many other things said by Galava the ruler of men Ushinara gave him this answer.

sn: श्रुतवानस्मि ते वाक्यं यथा वदसि गालव। विधिस्तु बलवान् ब्रह्मन् प्रवणं हि मनो मम॥
en: “I have heard what you say and know what you intend to say, O Galava; but O Brahman, the lord has all the power in such matters for my heart inclines to do what you say.

sn: शते द्वे तु ममाश्वानामीदृशानां द्विजोत्तम। इतरेषां सहस्राणि सुबहूनि चरन्ति मे॥
en: But two hundred only of horses of this breed I have; of other sorts thousands are roving about in my territories.

sn: अहमष्येकमेवास्यां जनयिष्यामि गालव। पुत्रं द्विज गतं मागं गमिष्यामि परैरहम्॥
en: I too shall beget only one son on her, O Galava, and, O twice born one I shall go along the course followed by others in this matter.

sn: मूल्येनापि समं कुर्यां तवाहं द्विजसत्तम। पौरजानपदार्थं तु ममार्थो नात्मभोगतः॥
en: In the matter of dowry too, I shall act like them, O best among the twice born; my wealth is the property of my subjects and not for my own enjoyment.

sn: कामतो हि धनं राजा पारक्यं यः प्रयच्छति। न स धर्मेण धर्मात्मन् युज्यते यशसा न च॥
en: The king, who out of desire, spends the wealth of others, is never connected with virtue, o virtuous-souled one, nor with renown.

sn: सोऽहं प्रतिग्रहीष्यामि ददात्वेतां भवान् मम। कुमारी देवग भामेकपुत्रभवाय मे॥
en: Therefore shall I accept (the maiden); you please give her to me so that a son may be born to me in the womb of her who bears god-like children."

sn: तथा तु बहुधा कन्यामुक्तवन्तं नराधिपम्। उशीनरं द्विजश्रेष्ठो गालवः प्रत्यपूजयत्॥
en: The best among the twice-born, Galava then worshipped the king of men, who spoke in that strain many other things by bestowing upon him that maiden.

sn: उशीनरं प्रतिग्राह्य गालवः प्रययौ वनम्। रेमे स तां समासाद्य कृतपुण्य इव श्रियम्॥
en: And having given her to Ushinara, Galava went to the forest and he (Ushinara) spotted in her company like a virtuous man enjoying his prosperity,

sn: कन्दरेषु च शैलानां नदीनां निझरेषु च। उद्योनेषु विचित्रेषु वनेषूपवनेषु च॥
en: In caverns of mountains, and near the sources of rivers, in buildings with windows, and in secluded chambers;

sn: हर्येषु रमणीयेषु प्रासादशिखरेषु च। वातायनविमानेषु तथा गर्भगृहेषु च॥
en: In variegated gardens, and in forests and pleasure gardens, in beautiful palaces and on tops of houses.

sn: ततोऽस्य समये जज्ञे पुत्रो बालरविप्रभः। शिबिर्नाम्नाभिविख्यातो यः स पार्थिवसत्तमः॥
en: Then was born to him in due time a son who was a boy similar in effulgence to the sun; he lived to be an excellent ruler of the earth known by the name Shivi.

sn: उपस्थाय स तं विप्रो गालवः प्रतिगृह्य च। कन्यां प्रयातस्तां राजन् दृष्टवान् विनतात्मजम्॥
en: The twice born Galava having then presented himself to him and having taken back the maiden went away and saw the son of Vinata.

sn: नारद उवाच गालवं वैनतेयोऽथ प्रहसन्निदमब्रवीत्। दिष्ट्या कृतार्थं पश्यामि भवन्तमिह वै द्विज।।।।
en: Narada said The son of Vinata, seeing Galava, said to him thus laughing. “It is by good luck that I see you successful here, O twice-born one".

sn: गालवस्तु वचः श्रुत्वा वैनतेयेन भाषितम्। चतुर्भागावशिष्टं तदाचख्यौ कार्यमस्य हि॥
en: Galava too, hearing those words spoken by the son of Vinata, informed him that a fourth part of the work yet remained to be done.

sn: सुपर्णस्त्वब्रवीदेनं गालवं वदतां वरः। प्रयत्नस्तेन कर्तव्यो नैष सम्पत्स्यते तव॥
en: Suparna, the foremost among speakers then said to Galava. “No pains should be taken by you for this for you will not get it.

sn: पुरा हि कान्यकुब्जे वै गाधेः सत्यवतीं सुताम्। भार्यार्थेऽवरयत् कन्यामृचीकस्तेन भाषितः॥
en: In days of old, in Kanyakubja, Richika chose the damsel Satyavati, the daughter of Gadhi, for his wife and he was thus spoken to by Gadhi.

sn: एकतः श्यामकर्णानां हयानां चन्द्रवर्चसाम्। भगवन् दीयतां मह्यं सहस्रमिति गालव॥
en: You give me a thousand horses white as the moon and black of one ear.

sn: ऋचीकस्तु तथेत्युक्त्वा वरुणस्यालयं गतः। अश्वतीर्थं हयाँल्लब्ध्वा दत्तवान् पार्थिवाय वै॥
en: Richika too saying “very-well” went to the abode of Varuna and from there obtaining the horses from the Ashvatirtha gave them to the ruler of the earth.

sn: इष्ट्वा ते पुण्डरीकेण दत्ता राज्ञा द्विजातिषु। तेभ्यो द्वे द्वे शते क्रीत्वा प्राप्ते तैः पार्थिवैस्तदा॥
en: They were presented to the twice-born one by king Pundarika who performed a sacrificial ceremony; and of them, (the horses) the rulers of the earth (to whom you have applied) obtained two hundred each by purchase from the Brahmanas at the time.

sn: अपराण्यपि चत्वारि शतानि द्विजसत्तम। नीयमानानि संतारे हृतान्यासन् वितस्तया॥
en: The other four hundred, O best among the twice-born while being led across (the Vitasta river) were robbed by the river.

sn: एवं न शक्यमप्राप्यं प्राप्तुं गालव कर्हिचित्। इमामश्वशताभ्यां वै द्वाभ्यां तस्मै निवेदय॥
en: Such being the case, you will not beadle to obtain what is unobtainable by all means; present, therefore, this damsel as a substitute for the two hundred horses to him,

sn: विश्वामित्राय धर्मात्मन् षड्भिरश्वशतैः सह। ततोऽसि गतसम्मोहः कृतकृत्यो द्विजोत्तम॥
en: Namely, Vishvamitra, O virtuous-souled one, along with the six hundred horses; then will you be beyond the reach of grief and your desire will be successful, o best among the twice the twice born."

sn: गालवस्तं तथेत्युक्त्वा सुपर्णसहितस्ततः। आदायाश्वांश्च कन्यां च विश्वामित्रमुपागमत्॥
en: Galava then saying to him “very well” along with Suparna, taking the horses and the maiden with him, went to Vishvamitra and said.

sn: अश्वानां काक्षितार्थानां षडिमानि शतानि वै। शतद्वयेन कन्येय भवता प्रतिगृह्यताम्॥
en: "Of the horses asked for by you there are six hundred here and this damsel is a substitute for the other two hundred. Let these be accepted by you.

sn: अस्यां राजर्षिभिः पुत्रा जाता वै धार्मिकास्त्रयः। चतुर्थं जनयत्वेकं भवानपि नरोत्तमम्॥
en: On her by Rishis of royal descent three virtuous sons have been begotten; you too beget the fourth who will be the best among mankind.

sn: पूर्णान्येवं शतान्यष्टौ तुरगाणां भवन्तु ते। भवतो ह्यनृणो भूत्वा तपः कुर्यां यथासुखम्॥
en: Then will you get the full complement of eight hundred horses asked for by you and I too, after having paid off my debt, shall perform asceticism as I please.

sn: विश्वामित्रस्तु तं दृष्ट्वा गालवं सह पक्षिणा। कन्यां च तां वरारोहामिदमित्यब्रवीद् वचः॥
en: Vishvamitra, seeing Galava along with the bird and also that girl with beautiful hips, said these words.

sn: किमियं पूर्वमेवेह न दत्ता मम गालवा पुत्रा ममैव चत्वारो भवेयुः कुलभावनाः॥
en: "Why was not this girl presented to me beforehand, OGalava? Then would all the four sons have been mine, every one of whom would have perpetuated a dynasty.

sn: प्रतिगृह्णामि ते कन्यामेकपुत्रफलाय वै। अश्वाश्चाश्रममासाद्य चरन्तु मम सर्वशः॥
en: I shall accept this girl from you to beget on her one son and let the horses having been taken to my hermitage roam about at their will in all directions.

sn: स तया रममाणोऽथ विश्वामित्रो महाद्युतिः। आत्मजं जनयामास माधवी पुत्रमष्टकम्॥
en: Vishvamitra, of great effulgence, then roaming and sporting with her, Madhvi brought forth a male child named Ashtaka.

sn: जातमात्रं सुतं तं च विश्वामित्रो महामुनिः। संयोज्यार्थस्तथा धर्मैरश्वैस्तैः समयोजयत्॥
en: At the moment he was born, the great Muni Vishvamitra instructed him in both virtue and worldly good and presented to him those horses.

sn: अथाष्टकः पुरं प्रायात् तदा सोमपुरप्रभम्। निर्यात्य कन्यां शिष्याय कौशिकोऽपि वनं ययौ॥
en: Then did Ashtaka go to the city which was like the city of the moon and the son of Kushika (Vishvamitra) too went to the woods after having returned the damsel to his disciple.

sn: गालवोऽपि सुपर्णेन सह निर्यात्य दक्षिणाम्। मनसाऽतिप्रतीतेन कन्यामिदमुवाच ह॥
en: Galava too, along with Suparna, was light of heart having succeeded in making the final present he had promised, and said this to the girl.

sn: जातो दानपतिः पुत्रस्त्वया शूरस्तथापरः। सत्यधर्मरतश्चान्यो यज्वा चापि तथाऽपरः॥
en: "By you has been brought forth a son who is the foremost among the givers of wealth, a second one who is a great hero, another who is ever attached to virtue and another who is ever attached to virtue and truth and the fourth who is a great performer of sacrificial ceremonies.

sn: तदागच्छ वरारोहे तारितस्ते पिता सुतैः। चत्वारश्चैव राजानस्तथा चाहं सुमध्यमे॥
en: Therefore do you come, O you of beautiful hips, your father has obtained salvation by your sons and also the four kings (their fathers) and so also have been I, O you of slender waist."

sn: गालवस्त्वभ्यनुज्ञाय सुपर्णं पन्नगाशनम्। पितुर्निर्यात्य तां कन्यां प्रययौ वनमेव ह॥
en: Galava, then having permitted Suparna who subsisted on serpents to go away and returning the damsel to his father, went to the forest.

sn: नारद उवाच स तु राजा पुनस्तस्याः कर्तुकामः स्वयंवरम्। उपगम्याश्रमपदं गङ्गायमुनसंगमे॥
en: Narada said The king (Yayati) too, being desirous of giving her (Madhvi) a husband by Svayamvara, went to the hermitage at the confluence of the Ganga and Yamuna,

sn: गृहीतमाल्यदामां तां रथमारोप्य माधवीम्। पूर्यदुश्च भगिनीमाश्रमे पर्यधावताम्॥
en: Making, Madhvi seated on a chariot with garlands and flowers on her person; Puru and Yadu too followed their sister to the hermitage.

sn: नागयक्षमनुष्याणां गन्धर्वमृगपक्षिणाम्। शैलद्रुमवनौकानामासीत् तत्र समागमः॥
en: There, in that hermitage, came together Nagas, Yakshas, and human beings, Gandharvas, animals and birds and dwellers of mountains, woods and forests.

sn: नानापुरुषदेश्यानामीश्वरैश्च समाकुलम्। ऋषिभिर्ब्रह्मकल्पैश्च समन्तादावृतं वनम्॥
en: There was also a concourse of the kings of many countries and the forest, that surrounded the hermitage, was filled with Rishis equal (in asceticism) to Brahma himself.

sn: निर्दिश्यमानेषु तु सा वरेषु वरवर्णिनी। वरानुत्क्रम्य सर्वांस्तान् वरं वृतवती वनम्॥
en: The lady, of good complexion, being directed to choose a husband, passed over all these husbands and selected the forest as her husband.

sn: अवतीर्य रथात् कन्या नमस्कृत्य च बन्धुषु। उपगम्य वनं पुण्यं तपस्तेपे ययातिजा॥
en: Getting down from the chariot, the damsel saluted her friends and having gone to the sacred forest, the lady born of Yayati, practiced austerities,

sn: उपवासैश्च विविधैर्दीक्षाभिर्नियमैस्तथा। आत्मनो लघुतां कृत्वा बभूव मृगचारिणी॥
en: By observing fasts and different sorts of religions rites, as also ceremonies. She reduced her body and adopted the life of a deer.

sn: वैदूर्याङ्कुरकल्पानि मृदूनि हरितानि च। चरन्तीश्लक्ष्णशष्पाणि तिक्तानि मधुराणि च॥
en: Subsisting on sweet and green grass resembling the blades of the Vaidurya gem and which were both sweet and bitter,

sn: स्रवन्तीनां च पुण्यानां सुरसानि शुचीनि च। पिबन्ती वारिमुख्यानि शीतानि विमलानि च॥
en: And drinking the best of holy waters of sacred fountains which was sweet, pure and cool,

sn: वनेषु मृगवासेषु व्याघ्रविप्रोषितेषु च। दावाग्निविप्रयुक्तेषु शून्येषु गहनेषु च॥
en: And roaming in thick forests from which the kings of animals (lions) and tigers had been exiled and in deserts which had no conflagration in them,

sn: चरन्ती हरिणैः सार्धं मृगीव वनचारिणी। चचार विपुलं धर्मं ब्रह्मचर्येण संवृतम्॥
en: In company with deer and adopting their mode of life she earned much religious merit, by practicing Brahmacharya.

sn: ययातिरपि पूर्वेषां राज्ञां वृत्तमनुष्ठितः। बहुवर्षसहस्रायुर्युयुजे कालधर्मणा॥
en: Yayati, too following the mode of life of the kings before him, lived for a thousand years and then paid the debt of nature.

sn: पूर्यदुश्च द्वौ वंशे वर्धमानौ नरोत्तमौ। ताभ्यां प्रतिष्ठितो लोके परलोके च नाहुषः॥
en: The two best among men Puru and Yadu perpetuating the family were established (as king) in this world and the son of Nahusha in the next.

sn: महीपते नरपतिर्ययातिः स्वर्गमास्थितः। महर्षिकल्पो नृपतिः स्वर्गाग्रयफलभुग विभुः॥
en: O monarch, dwelling in heaven Yayati, resembling a great Rishi, enjoyed the choicest blessings of heaven.

sn: बहुवर्षसहस्राख्ये काले बहुगुणे गते। राजर्षिषु निषण्णेषु महीयस्सु महर्धिषु॥
en: After many thousands of years had elapsed in great happiness and while seated among royal Rishis of great luster and renown.

sn: अवमेने नरान् सर्वान् देवानृषिगणांस्तथा। ययातिर्मूढविज्ञानो विस्मयाविष्टचेतनः॥
en: Yayati, with his senses stupefied and his intellect beside himself, insulted all the human beings and the gods and the body of Rishis.

sn: ततस्तं बुबुधे देवः शक्रो बलनिषूदनः। ते च राजर्षयः सर्वे धिग्धिगित्येवमब्रुवन्॥
en: Then did the god Shakra, the slayer of Vala, perceived his folly and all those royal Rishis said-fie, fie.

sn: विचारश्च समुत्पन्नो निरीक्ष्य नहुषात्मजम्। को न्वयं कस्य वा राज्ञः कथं वा स्वर्गमागतः॥
en: And seeing the son of Nahusha, enquiries were made, who is he, what king's son is he, and how did he come to heaven?

sn: कर्मणा केन सिद्धोऽयं क्व वाऽनेन तपश्चितम्। कथं वा ज्ञायते स्वर्गे केन वा ज्ञायतेऽप्युत॥
en: By which deeds did he obtain salvation? In what forest did he practice asceticism? How is he known in heaven and by whom, is he so known?

sn: एवं विचारयन्तस्ते राजानं स्वर्गवासिनः। दृष्ट्वा पप्रच्छुरन्योन्यं ययातिं नृपतिं प्रति॥
en: The dwellers of heaven made such enquiries about the king among themselves pointing to Yayati, the ruler of men.

sn: विमानपालाः शतशः स्वर्गद्वाराभिरक्षिणः। पृष्टा आसनपालाश्च न जानीमेत्यथाब्रुवन्॥
en: The hundreds of the charioteers of heaven and hundreds of the fate keepers of heaven and the persons who had the seats of heaven in their charge being asked about the matter, saidwe do not know.

sn: सर्वे ते दावृतज्ञाना नाभ्यजानन्त तं नृपम्। स मुहूर्तादथ नृपो हतौजाश्चाभवत् तदा॥
en: None of them was then in proper senses and did know that ruler of men, and speedily was that ruler of men shorn of his heavenly effulgence.

description: Turning out from heaven of Yayati
sn: नारद उवाच अथ प्रचलितः स्थानादासनाच्च परिच्युतः। कम्पितेनेव मनसा धर्षितः शोकवह्निना॥
en: Narada said Being thus turned out from his place in heaven) and deprived of his seat there, his heart trembling and consumed by the fire of grief.

description: Turning out from heaven of Yayati
sn: म्लानस्रग्भ्रष्टविज्ञानः प्रभ्रष्टमुकुटाङ्गदः। विघूर्णन् स्रस्तसर्वाङ्गः प्रभ्रष्टाभरणाम्बरः॥
en: With his garlands rendered pale, his senses taking leave of him, deprived of his crown and other ornaments, with his head reeling and his entire body relaxed and robbed of his robes and ornaments,

description: Turning out from heaven of Yayati
sn: अदृश्यमानस्तान् पश्यन्नपश्यंश्च पुनः पुनः। शून्यः शून्येन मनसा प्रपतिष्यन् महीतलम्॥
en: Incapable of being known, and now seeing and again not seeing those gods he fell down to the earth below with his mind in despair and his intellect a blank.

description: Turning out from heaven of Yayati
sn: किं मया मनसा ध्यातमशुभं धर्मदूषणम्। येनाहं चलित: स्थानादिति राजा व्यचिन्तयत्॥
en: "What inauspicious and sinful thought was entertained by me in my mind, in consequence of which I have been turned out from my place in heaven?” Thus did the king think within himself.

description: Turning out from heaven of Yayati
sn: ते तु तत्रैव राजानः सिद्धाश्चाप्सरसस्तथा। अपश्यन्त निरालम्बं तं ययाति परिच्युतम्॥
en: All the kings who were there (in heaven) as also those who had obtained salvation and the Apasaras laughed at Yayati being hurled down from heaven and falling down, having you support to cling to.

description: Turning out from heaven of Yayati
sn: अथैत्य पुरुषः कश्चित् क्षीणपुण्यनिपातकः। ययातिमब्रवीद् राजान् देवराजस्य शासनात्॥
en: Then did some officers whose duty it was to hurl down men, whose religious merit had been rewarded by a sufficiently long term of residence in heaven, coming there said to Yayati, "O king, by command of the king among the gods,

description: Turning out from heaven of Yayati
sn: अतीव मदमत्तस्त्वं न कंचिन्नावमन्यसे। मानेन भ्रष्टः स्वर्गस्ते नाहस्त्वं पार्थिवात्मज॥
en: You are exceedingly intoxicated with vanity and there is no body you have not insulted and owing to this vanity you are no longer fit for heaven, O you born of a king.

description: Turning out from heaven of Yayati
sn: न च प्रज्ञायसे गच्छ पतस्वेति तमब्रवीत्। पतेयं सत्स्विति वचस्त्रिरुक्त्वा नहुषात्मजः॥
en: No one knows you here too, therefore down you and fall down.” “I shall fall among the good” the son of Nahusha said these words three times.

description: Turning out from heaven of Yayati
sn: पतिष्यंश्चिन्तयामास गतिं गतिमतां वरः। एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु नैमिषे पार्थिवर्षभान्॥
en: While falling that foremost of those who had attained salvation thought of the course of his fall (and the place he should fall on in the end.)

description: Turning out from heaven of Yayati
sn: चतुरोऽपश्यत नृपस्तेषां मध्ये पपात ह। प्रतर्दनो वसुमनाः शिबिरौशीनरोऽष्टकः॥
en: At this time he saw four kings and fell among them. They were Pratardana, Vasumanas, Shibi the son of Ushinara and Ashtaka.

description: Turning out from heaven of Yayati
sn: वाजपेयेन यज्ञेन तर्पयन्ति सुरेश्वरम्। तेषामध्वरजं धूमं स्वर्गद्वारमुपस्थितम्॥
en: Who were gratifying the lord of the gods by the performance of the sacrificial ceremony known Vajapeya. And the smoke proceeding from that sacrificial ceremony had gone to the very gates of heaven.

description: Turning out from heaven of Yayati
sn: ययातिरुपजिघ्रन् वै निपपात महीं प्रति। भूमौ स्वर्गे च सम्बद्धां नदी धूममयीमिव। गङ्गां गामिव गच्छन्तीमालम्ब्य जगतीपतिः॥
en: Yayati fell towards the earth smelling that river of smoke which connected as it were the earth with the heaven.

description: Turning out from heaven of Yayati
sn: श्रीमत्स्ववभृथाग्रयेषु चतुर्पु प्रतिबन्धुषु। मध्ये निपतितो राजा लोकपालोपमेषु सः॥
en: The lord, of the earth following the course of that smoke which was moving like the Ganga in heaven, came among those foremost of the performers of sacrifices who were his own relatives;

description: Turning out from heaven of Yayati
sn: चतुषू हुतकल्पेषु राजसिंहमहाग्निषु। पपात मध्ये राजर्षिर्ययाति: पुण्यसंक्षये॥
en: as Among those who were like the supporters of the earth; among those four who were as lions among kings and like the great fire in sacrificial ceremonies the king Yayati fell.

description: Turning out from heaven of Yayati
sn: तमाहुः पार्थिवाः सर्वे दीप्यमानमिव श्रिया। को भवान् कस्य वा बन्धुर्देशस्य नगरस्य वा॥
en: The Royal Rishi Yayati, after all his religious merit had been spent up, fell among them; all the rulers of the earth said to him who was effulgent with beauty. “Who are you? With whom are you related, and from what town and country are you?

description: Turning out from heaven of Yayati
sn: यक्षो वाप्यथवा देवो गन्धर्वो राक्षसोऽपि वा। न हि मानुषरूपोऽसि को वाऽर्थः काइझ्यते त्वया।।१६।
en: Are you a Yakasha or a god, a Gandharva or a Rakshasa, for you have not the appearance of a human being; and what is the object desired for by you?”

description: Turning out from heaven of Yayati
sn: ययातिरुवाच ययातिरस्मि राजर्षिः क्षीणपुण्यश्च्युतो दिवः। पतेयं सत्स्विति ध्यायन् भवत्सु पतितस्ततः॥
en: Yayati said I am the royal Rishi Yayati and the religious merit acquired by me being spent up have been turned out from heaven; and wishing in my mind that I should fall among the good, I have fallen among you.

description: Turning out from heaven of Yayati
sn: राजान ऊचुः सत्यमेतद् भवतु ते काक्षितं पुरुषर्षभ। सर्वेषां नः क्रतुफलं धर्मश्च प्रतिगृह्यताम्॥
en: The king said May what was desired for by you le successful; accept the religious merit of these sacrificial ceremonies performed by all of us.

description: Turning out from heaven of Yayati
sn: ययातिरुवाच नाहं प्रतिग्रहधनो ब्राह्मणः क्षत्रियो ह्यहम्। न च मे प्रवणा बुद्धिः परपुण्यविनाशने॥
en: Yayati said I am not a Brahmana and therefore cannot accept wealth (of any sort) from others, and my I heart is not inclined to destroy the religious merit of others.

description: Turning out from heaven of Yayati
sn: नारद उवाच एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु मृगचर्याक्रमागताम्। माधवीं प्रेक्ष्य राजानस्तेऽभिवाद्येदमब्रुवन्।॥
en: Narada said At this time, seeing Madhvi leading the life of a deer and wandering about, those kings bowing to her said

description: Turning out from heaven of Yayati
sn: किमागमनकृत्यं ते किं कुर्मः शासनं तव। आज्ञाप्या हि वयं सर्वे तव पुत्रास्तपोधने॥
en: “What is the reason of your coming here, what orders of yours shall we obey? Being your sons, O devotee, we are ready to be commanded by you."

description: Turning out from heaven of Yayati
sn: तेषां तद् भाषितं श्रुत्वा माधवी परया मुदा। पितरं समुपागच्छद् ययातिं सा ववन्द च॥
en: Madhvi, hearing that speech of theirs with great delight, came to her father and bowed to Yayati.

description: Turning out from heaven of Yayati
sn: स्पृष्ट्वा मूर्धनि तान् पुत्रांस्तापसी वाक्यमब्रवीत्। दौहित्रास्तव राजेन्द्र मम पुत्रा न ते पराः॥
en: And having touched those sons of hers on their head the anchoring said these words "These are your grandsons, O chief among kings-my sons-they are not unconnected with you.

description: Turning out from heaven of Yayati
sn: इमे त्वां तारयिष्यन्ति दृष्टमेतत् पुरातने। अहं ते दुहिता राजन् माधवी मृगचारिणी॥
en: These will save you-such an example has been seen in days of old-I am your daughter, Madhvi, who, o king, have adopted the life of a deer.

description: Turning out from heaven of Yayati
sn: मयाप्युपचितो धर्मस्ततोऽर्धं प्रतिगृह्यताम्। यस्माद् राजन् नराः सर्वे अपत्यफलभागिनः॥
en: By me too has religious merit been acquired; accept half of that, for, o king, all human beings enjoy the wealth earned by their children.

description: Turning out from heaven of Yayati
sn: तस्मादिच्छन्ति दौहित्रान् यथा त्वं वसुधाधिप। ततस्ते पार्थिवाः सर्वे शिरसा जननीं तदा॥
en: Therefore was it that you, O lord of the earth, wished me to be the mother of son;" then did all those rulers of the earth lowering their heads,

description: Turning out from heaven of Yayati
sn: अभिवाद्य नमस्कृत्य मातामहमथाब्रुवन्। उच्चैरनुपमैः स्निग्धैः स्वरैरापूर्य मेदिनीम्॥
en: Bowed down and said the same thing to their maternal grand father, filling the earth with loud and sweet ponds the like of which there was none.

description: Turning out from heaven of Yayati
sn: मातामहं नृपतयस्तारयन्तो दिवश्च्युतम्। अथ तस्मादुपगतो गालवोऽप्याह पार्थिवम्। तपसो मेऽष्टभागेन स्वर्गमारोहतां भवान्॥
en: The rulers of men thus saved their grandfather who had been turned out from heaven; just then, Galava, coming there said to the ruler of the earth, “A send you heaven by virtue of a eighth part of my austerities.”

description: The getting up to heaven of Yayati
sn: नारद उवाच प्रत्यभिज्ञातमात्रोऽथ सद्भिस्तैर्नरपुङ्गवः। समारोह नृपतिरस्पृशन् वसुधातलम्। ययातिर्दिव्यसंस्थानो बभूव विगतज्वरः॥
en: Narada said The moment he was recognized by those good men, those foremost among human beings, that ruler of men went up again without touching the surface of the earth, and Yayati being freed from all his troubles again got his place in heaven.

description: The getting up to heaven of Yayati
sn: दिव्यमाल्याम्बरधरो दिव्याभरणभूषितः। दिव्यगन्धगुणोपेतो न पृथ्वीमस्पृशत् पदा॥
en: Bedecked with heavenly garlands, clothed in heaven raiment and putting on heavenly ornaments and with heavenly perfumes and endued with heavenly qualities he did not even touch the earth with his feet.

description: The getting up to heaven of Yayati
sn: ततो वसुमनाः पूर्वमुच्चैरुच्चारयन् वचः। ख्यातो दानपतिलेकि व्याजहार नृपं तदा॥
en: Then did Vasumanas, renowned in this world as the foremost among givers, first uttering these words in a loud voice said to the king.

description: The getting up to heaven of Yayati
sn: प्राप्तवानस्मि यल्लोके सर्वर्णेष्वगहया। तदप्यथ च दास्यामि तेन संयुज्यतां भवान्॥
en: "The merit that I have earned in this world by my conduct towards all the castes, which can not be found fault with, that too I give you and may you earn that.

description: The getting up to heaven of Yayati
sn: यत् फलं दानशीलस्य क्षमाशीलस्य यत् फलम्। यच्च मे फलमाधाने तेन संयुज्यतां भवान्॥
en: The merit that is earned by one who is attached to liberality and the merit that is earned by one who exercises forgiveness and the merit that I have by my sacrificial ceremonies-may you earn all that.”

description: The getting up to heaven of Yayati
sn: ततः प्रतर्दनोऽप्याह वाक्यं क्षत्रियपुङ्गवः। यथा धर्मरतिनित्यं नित्यं युद्धपरायणः॥
en: Then did that foremost among the Kshatriyas, Pratardana too, ever attached to virtue and given to war, said:

description: The getting up to heaven of Yayati
sn: प्राप्तवानस्मि यल्लोके क्षत्रवंशोद्भवं यशः। वीरशब्दफलं चैव तेन संयुज्यतां भवान्॥
en: “The farne that I have gained in this world, and which is due to my being born in the Kshatriya order, the merit earned by me for being called a hero-is all yours.”

description: The getting up to heaven of Yayati
sn: शिबिरौशीनरो धीमानुवाच मधुरां गिरम्। यथा बालेषु नारीषु वैहार्येषु तथैव च॥
en: The wise Shibi, the son of Ushinara, then said in a sweet voice Since, to children, or women, as also to those who might be cracked jokes with,

description: The getting up to heaven of Yayati
sn: संगरेषु निपातेषु तथा तद्व्यसनेषु च। अनृतं नोक्तपूर्वं मे तेन सत्येन खं व्रज॥
en: To those who are in danger, to those engaged in a game of dice, as also to those who are suffering from grief and calamities I have never before said a falsehood, by virtue of that truth, wander about in heaven.

description: The getting up to heaven of Yayati
sn: यथा प्राणांश्च राज्यं च राजन् कामसुखानि च। त्यजेयं न पुनः सत्यं तेन सत्येन खं व्रज॥
en: I can abandon my life, my kingdom as also all luxuries and objects of desire but not truth, by that do you wander about in heaven.

description: The getting up to heaven of Yayati
sn: यथा सत्येन मे धर्मो यथा सत्येन पावकः। प्रीत: शतक्रतुश्चैव तेन सत्येन खं व्रज॥
en: The truth by which Dharma, the truth by which Agni and the truth by which the performer of a hundred sacrifices has been gratified by me-by virtue of that truth wander about in heaven.

description: The getting up to heaven of Yayati
sn: अष्टकस्त्वथ राजर्षिः कौशिको माधवीसुतः। अनेकशतयज्वानं नाहुषं प्राप्य धर्मवित्॥
en: And the royal Rishi Ashtaka too, the son of Madhvi, by the son of Kushika, conversant with virtue, addressing the son of Nahusha who had performed many hundreds of sacrifices, said:

description: The getting up to heaven of Yayati
sn: शतशः पुण्डरीका मे गोसवाश्चरिताः प्रभो। क्रतवो वाजपेयाश्च तेषां फलमवाप्नुहि॥
en: "O Lord the sacrificial rites Pundarika, Gosava and Vajapeya have been performed by me by hundreds; get the merits of these.

description: The getting up to heaven of Yayati
sn: न मे रत्नानि न धनं न तथाऽन्ये परिच्छदाः। क्रतुष्वनुपयुक्तानि तेन सत्येन खं व्रज॥
en: I have not considered gems nor wealth, nor sort riches too much for the performance of my sacrifices (that is I have not spared them); by virtue of that truth, do you wander about in heaven."

description: The getting up to heaven of Yayati
sn: यथा यथा हि जल्पन्ति दौहित्रास्तं नराधिपम्। तथा तथा वसुमतीं त्यक्त्वा राजा दिवं ययौ।॥
en: As one by one his grandsons addressed that ruler of men, so by degrees the king went up to the heaven leaving below the earth.

description: The getting up to heaven of Yayati
sn: एवं सर्वे समस्तैस्ते राजानः सुकृतैस्तदा। ययाति स्वर्गतो भ्रष्टं तारयामासुरञ्जसा॥
en: By this means did all those kings by their good deeds easily save Yayati, who had been turned out from heaven, at that time.

description: The getting up to heaven of Yayati
sn: दोहित्राः स्वेन धर्मेण यज्ञदानकृतेन वै। चतुर्षु राजवंशेषु सम्भूताः कुलवर्धनाः। मातामहं महाप्राज्ञं दिवमारोपयन्त ते॥
en: The four grandsons, born in four royal families, and each the perpetuator of a race, sent back by their own virtue, by the sacrificial rites performed by them and gifts made by them, their wise grandfather to heaven.

description: The getting up to heaven of Yayati
sn: राजान ऊचुः राजधर्मगुणोपेताः सर्वधर्मगुणान्विताः। दोहित्रास्ते वयं राजन् दिवमारोह पार्थिव॥
en: The kings said O king, we are your grandsons endued with kingly virtues and with all virtues and accomplishments; ascend heaven, O ruler of men.

description: The ascension to heaven of Yayati
sn: नारद उवाच सद्भिरारोपितः स्वर्ग पार्थिवैर्भूरिदक्षिणैः। अभ्यनुज्ञाय दौहित्रान् ययातिर्दिवमास्थितः।।।।
en: Narada said Being thus made to ascend heaven by those pious rulers of the earth, who were greatly given liberality, Yayati was established in heaven after taking leave of his grandsons.

description: The ascension to heaven of Yayati
sn: अभिवृष्टश्च वर्षेण नानापुष्पसुगन्धिना। परिष्वक्तश्च पुण्येन वायुना पुण्यगन्धिना॥
en: (He went up heaven) amidst the downpour of a shower of sweet scented flow very smell indicated its holiness.

description: The ascension to heaven of Yayati
sn: अचलं स्थानमासाद्य दौहित्रफलनिर्जितम्। कर्मभिः स्वैरुपचितो जज्वाल परया श्रिया॥
en: Reaching then eternal regions earned for him by his grand sons by the fruit of their own deeds, he became effulgent with excellent beauty.

description: The ascension to heaven of Yayati
sn: उपगीतोपनृत्तश्च गन्धर्वाप्सरसां गणैः। प्रीत्या प्रतिगृहीतश्च स्वर्गे दुन्दुभिनिःस्वनैः॥
en: He was gladly received in heaven with songs and dances by groups of Gandharvas and with the sound of cymbals.

description: The ascension to heaven of Yayati
sn: अभिष्टुतश्च विविधैर्देवराजर्षिचारणैः। अर्चितश्चोत्तमायण दैवतैरभिनन्दितः॥
en: He was also duly gratified by various classes of celestial Rishis, royal Rishis, and Charanas and otherwise pleased by the gods.

description: The ascension to heaven of Yayati
sn: प्राप्तः स्वर्गफलं चैव तमुवाच पितामहः। निर्वृतं शान्तमनसं वचोभिस्तर्पयन्निव॥
en: The grandfather then said to him who had earned the merit of ascending heaven as if trying to please him who had obtained gratification and tranquility of mind with his words.

description: The ascension to heaven of Yayati
sn: चतुष्पादस्त्वया धर्मश्चितो लोक्येन कर्मणा। अक्षयस्तव लोकोऽयं कीर्तिश्चैवाक्षया दिवि॥
en: The four Padas (the full amount) of virtue had been earned by you your worldly deeds and these regions were yours for an endless period and your renown in heaven too was eternal.

description: The ascension to heaven of Yayati
sn: पुनस्त्वयैव राजर्षे सुकृतेन विघातितम्। आवृतं तमसा चेतः सर्वेषां स्वर्गवासिनाम्॥
en: But that merit, O royal Rishi, you nullified again, for by your were the minds of all the denizens so clouded.

description: The ascension to heaven of Yayati
sn: येन त्वां नाभिजानन्ति ततोऽज्ञातोऽसि पातितः। प्रीत्यैव चासि दौहित्रैस्तारितस्त्वमिहागतः॥
en: In consequence of this they did not recognize you and being thus rendered unknown (to them) you were hurled down and you have come here again, your grandsons saving you out of affection for you.

description: The ascension to heaven of Yayati
sn: स्थानं च प्रतिपन्नोऽसि कर्मणा स्वेन निर्जितम्। अचलं शाश्वतं पुण्यमुत्तमं ध्रुवमव्ययम्॥
en: Earned by your deeds you have now come to a place which is stable, eternal sacred, excellent and surely indestructible.

description: The ascension to heaven of Yayati
sn: ययातिरुवाच भगवन् संशयो मेऽस्ति कश्चित् ते छेत्तुमर्हसि। न ह्यन्यमहमहमि प्रष्टुं लोकपितामह॥
en: Yayati said O you endued with divine prosperity, I have a certain doubt which it is proper for you to remove; it is not proper that I should ask any body else, O grandfather of the universe.

description: The ascension to heaven of Yayati
sn: बहुवर्षसहस्रान्तं प्रजापालनवर्धितम्। अनेकक्रतुदानौधैरर्जितं मे महत् फलम्॥
en: Great was the merit earned by me by protecting my subjects and increasing the human stock for a great many thousands of years and by many sacrificial rites and pieties.

description: The ascension to heaven of Yayati
sn: कथं तदल्पकालेन क्षीणं येनास्मि पातितः। भगवन् वेत्थ लोकांश्च शाश्वतान् मम निर्मितान्। कथं नु मम तत् सर्वं विप्रनष्टं महाद्युते॥
en: How could that all be spent up in a very short time in consequence of which I was hurled down; O you endued with divine prosperity, you know that the eternal regions were built for me and how and why were all these destroyed, O you of great effulgence?

description: The ascension to heaven of Yayati
sn: पितामह उवाच बहुवर्षसहस्रान्तं प्रजापालनवर्धितम्। अनेकक्रतुदानौधैर्यत् त्वयोपार्जितं फलम्॥
en: The grandsire said The merit, earned by you by protecting your subjects and increasing the human stock for a great many thousands of years and the performance of many sacrificial rites and making many gifts,

description: The ascension to heaven of Yayati
sn: तदनेनैव दोषेण क्षीणं येनासि पातितः। अभिमानेन राजेन्द्र विक्कृतः स्वर्गवासिभिः॥
en: Was destroyed by this defect owing to which you were hurled down: O chief among kings, owing to your vanity you cared very little and held in contempt the denizens of heaven.

description: The ascension to heaven of Yayati
sn: नायं मानेन राजर्षे न बलेन न हिंसया। न शाठ्येन न मायाभिर्लोको भवति शाश्वतः॥
en: In the case of a man affected by vanity, O royal Rishi, or by envy or by force or by wickedness, or by deceit, these regions can not be eternal.

description: The ascension to heaven of Yayati
sn: नावमान्यास्त्वया राजन्नधमोत्कृष्टमध्यमाः। न हि मानप्रदग्धानां कश्चिदस्ति शमः क्वचित्॥
en: By you, a king, are not to be disregarded or insulted those that are superior or those that are inferior or those are indifferent; salvation cannot be attained by one who is consumed by vanity.

description: The ascension to heaven of Yayati
sn: पतनारोहणमिदं कथयिष्यन्ति ये नराः। विषमाण्यपि ते प्राप्तास्तरिष्यन्ति न संशयः॥
en: Those men, who will converse on this story of your fall and recession, will attain salvation though affected by sins; there is no doubt of it.

description: The ascension to heaven of Yayati
sn: नारद उवाच एष दोषोऽभिमानेन पुरा प्राप्तो ययातिना। निर्वघ्नतातिमानं च गालवेन महीपते॥
en: Narada said By Yayati was such a distress met with in days of old of old for his vanity and by Galava owing to an excessive measure of obstinacy, O lord of the world.

description: The ascension to heaven of Yayati
sn: श्रोतव्यं हितकामानां सुहृदां हितमिच्छताम्। न कर्तव्यो हि निर्बन्धो निर्बन्धो हि क्षयोदयः॥
en: The advice of your well wishers should be listened to by you, for your friends wise you well; obstinacy should not be resorted for it gives rise to ruin.

description: The ascension to heaven of Yayati
sn: तस्मात् त्वमपि गान्धारे मानं क्रोधं च वर्जय। संधत्स्व पाण्डवैवीर संरम्भं त्यज पार्थिव॥
en: Therefore, do you also, O son of Gandhari, abandon vanity and with; ( hero make peace with the sons of Pandu and abandon wrath, O ruler of the earth.

description: The ascension to heaven of Yayati
sn: ददाति यत् पार्थिवं यत् करोति यद् वा तपस्तप्यति यज्जुहोति। न तस्य नाशोऽस्ति न चापकर्षो नान्यस्तदश्नाति स एव कर्ता॥
en: O ruler of the earth, that which one gives, or dose, or the asceticism one practices or the sacrifices one makes can never be destroyed nor do they suffer deterioration in quality and the fruits are enjoyed by no body save the doer.

description: The ascension to heaven of Yayati
sn: इदं महाख्यानमनुत्तमं हितं बहुश्रुतानां गतरोषरागिणाम्। समीक्ष्य लोके बहुधा प्रधारितं त्रिवर्गदृष्टिः पृथिवीमुपाश्नुते॥
en: By understanding this great story than which nothing is better, and which is approved of by those who are well read in holy books and those who are past the operations of desire and wrath, a man obtains in this world a knowledge of (virtue, worldly good and desire) and gets the sovereignty of this world.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच भगवन्नेवमेवैतद् यथा वदसि नारद। इच्छामि चाहमप्येवं न त्वीशो भगवन्नहम्॥
en: Dhritarashtra said O you endued with divine prosperity, it is as you say O Narada, and I too wish the same thing, but you endued with heavenly prosperity, I am not the master.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्त्वा ततः कृष्णमभ्यभाषत कौरवः। स्वयं लोक्यं च मामात्य धर्म्यं न्याय्यं च केशव॥
en: Vaishampayana said Saying this the descendant of Kurus said to Krishna "O Keshava, you have said to me what leads to (the attainment of) heaven, to the benefit of the world and which is virtuous and just.

sn: न त्वहं स्ववशस्तात क्रियमाणं न मे प्रियम्। अङ्ग दुर्योधनं कृष्ण मन्दं शास्त्रातिगं मम॥ अनुनेतुं महाबाहो यतस्व पुरुषोत्तम। न शृणोति महाबाहो वचनं साधुभाषितम्॥
en: But I am not my own master, O you of long arms; O best of men, try persuade, O Krishna, my wicked son Duryodhana, who disregards injunctions of the scriptures who never dose what is pleasing to me and never listens to good words.

sn: गान्धार्याश्च हृषीकेश विदुरस्य च धीमतः। अन्येषां चैव सुहृदां भीष्मादीनां हितैषिणाम्॥
en: The son of Gandhari ( does not listen to the advice of) the wise Vidura, O Hrishikesha, as also to that of other friends and of such well wishers as Bhishma and others.

sn: स त्वं पापमति क्रूरं पापचित्तमचेतनम्। अनुशाधि दुरात्मानं स्वयं दुर्योधनं नृपम्॥
en: Therefore do yourself instruct the ruler of men, Duryodhana, of wicked soul crooked of evil intellect, of sinful heart and senseless.

sn: सुहृत्कार्यं तु सुमहत् कृतं ते स्याज्जनार्दन। ततोऽभ्यावृत्य वार्ष्णेयो दुर्योधनममर्षणम्॥
en: Then will a very great duty of a friend have been done by you, O Janardana.” Then did the son of Vrishni addressing the wrathful Duryodhana,

sn: अब्रवीन्मधुरां वाचं सर्वधर्मार्थतत्त्ववित्। दुर्योधन निबोधेदं मद्वाक्यं कुरुसत्तम॥
en: Say these sweet words, conversant as he was with all virtues and worldly profit: “O Duryodhana, listen to this speech of mine, O you best among the Kurus,

sn: शर्मार्थं ते विशेषण सानुबन्धस्य भारत। महाप्राज्ञकुले जातः साध्वेतत् कर्तुमर्हसि॥
en: Especially for the benefit of yourself and of your followers, O Bharata. Born as you are in a family of very wise men. it is indeed proper that you should do this honorable act.

sn: श्रुतवृत्तोपसम्पन्नः सर्वैः समुदितो गुणैः। दौष्कुलेया दुरात्मानो नृशंसा निरपत्रपाः॥
en: You are endue with learning and with good habits of life. Whereas these that are born in low families are wicked souled, Inhuman and shameless.

sn: त एतदीदृशं कुर्युर्यथा त्वं तात मन्यसे। धर्मार्थयुक्ता लोकेऽस्मिन् प्रवृत्तिर्लक्ष्यते सताम्॥
en: These latter alone act in the way that you are contemplating; in this world the inclination of honest men seems to lie towards and virtue and worldly profit.

sn: असतां विपरीता तु लक्ष्यते भरतर्षभ। विपरीता त्वियं वृत्तिरसकृल्लक्ष्यते त्वयि॥
en: And the inclination of bad men seems to lie towards the opposite direction, o best among the Bharatas, this contemplated action of yours seems to lie in this opposite direction.

sn: अधर्मश्चानुबन्धोऽत्र घोरः प्राणहरो महान्। अनिष्टश्चानिमित्तश्च न च शक्यश्च भारत।॥
en: In this case, the obstinacy shown by you is vicious, frightful and greatly destructive of life; it will lead to your harm, it is without reason, and is unworthy of being pursued by you long, OBharata.

sn: तमनर्थं परिहरन्नात्मश्रेयः करिष्यसि। भ्रातॄणामथ भृत्यानां मित्राणां च परंतप॥
en: Abandoning what is injurious to yourself you should do what is for your benefit and that of your brothers, followers and friends, O you chastiser of your foes.

sn: अधादयशस्याच्च कर्मणस्त्वं प्रमोक्ष्यसे। प्राज्ञैः शूरैर्महोत्साहैरात्मवद्भिर्बहुश्रुतैः॥
en: You will escape the blame of an act which is opposed to virtue and which will lead to notoriety. With the sons of Pandu who are wise, heroic, of great energy, of noble souls and very much conversant with our holy books,

sn: संधत्स्व पुरुषव्याघ्र पाण्डवैर्भरतर्षभ। तद्धितं च प्रियं चैव धृतराष्ट्रस्य
en: O foremost among men, make peace-it is beneficial to the wise Dhritarashtra and also pleasing to him,

sn: पितामहस्य द्रोणस्य विदुरस्य महामतेः। कृपस्य सोमदत्तस्य बाह्रीकस्य च धीमतः॥
en: As also to your grandfather and Drona and Vidura of great intelligence and to Kripa and Somadatta and to the wise Balhika,

sn: अश्वत्थाम्नो विकर्णस्य संजस्य विविंशतेः। ज्ञातीनां चैव भूयिष्ठं मित्राणां च परंतप॥
en: And to Ashvathama, and Vikarna, and Sanjaya and Vivingshati and very much so to your cousins and also to your friends, O chastiser of foes.

sn: शमे शर्म भवेत् तात सर्वस्य जगतस्तथा। ह्रीमानसि कुले जातः श्रुतवाननृशंसवान्। धीमतः॥ तिष्ठ तात पितुः शास्त्रे मातुश्च भरतर्षभ॥
en: In peace, there will be your benefit, my dear friend, as also that of the entire world; be endued with modesty, for you are born in a noble family, and be learned and human; therefore, my dear friend, do you follow the commands of your father and mother. O best among the Bharatas.

sn: एतच्छ्रेयो हि मन्यन्ते पिता यच्छास्ति भारत। उत्तमापद्गतः सर्वः पितुः स्मरति शासनम्॥
en: People consider that to be conducive to his good which a father commands, O Bharata, and a good man, when meeting with a danger, remembers all the commands of his father.

sn: रोचते ते पितुस्तात पाण्डवैः सह संगमः। सामात्यस्य कुरुश्रेष्ठ तत् तुभ्यं तात रोचताम्॥
en: Peace, my dear friend, with the sons of Pandu is pleasing to your father and you foremost among the Kurus, may it prove pleasing to yourself along with your advisers.

sn: श्रुत्वा यः सुहृदां शास्त्रं मर्यो न प्रतिपद्यते। विपाकान्ते दहत्येनं किम्पाकमिव भक्षितम्॥
en: That man, who hearing the advice of his friends, does not act according to it, in the end is consumed like one who has eaten the Kimpaka fruit.

sn: यस्तु निःश्रेयसं वाक्यं मोहान्न प्रतिपद्यते। स दीर्घसूत्रो हीनार्थः पश्चात्तापेन युज्यते॥
en: He, who out of folly, does not act according to the advice, than which nothing is more beneficial, is visited by the effects of procrastination, does not gain his object and is afterwards struck with remorse.

sn: यस्तु निःश्रेयसं श्रुत्वा प्राक् तदेवाभिपद्यते। आत्मनो मतमुत्सृज्य स लोके सुखमेधते॥
en: He, who having heard that, than which nothing is more beneficial, acts up to it abandoning his own opinions, gets happiness in this world.

sn: योऽर्थकामस्य वचनं प्रातिकूल्यान मृष्यते। शृणोति प्रतिकूलानि द्विषतां वशमेति सः॥
en: He, who does not act to the advice of one who desires his good thinking it to be against his interests and listens to what is really so (against his interests), comes under the power of his enemies.

sn: सतां मतमतिक्रम्य योऽसतां वर्तते मते। शोचन्ते व्यसने तस्य सुहृदो न चिरादिव॥
en: The friends of him, who disregarding the opinions of the honest, follows that of dishonest men, soon grave at his distress,

sn: मुख्यानमात्यानुत्सृज्य यो निहीनान् निषेवते। स घोरामापदं प्राप्य नोत्तारमधिगच्छति॥
en: He, who abandoning his principal advisers according to the injunctions of inferior ones, meets with grave dangers and does not come out of them safe.

sn: योऽसत्सेवीवृथाचारो न श्रोता सुहृदां सताम्। परान् वृणीते स्वान् द्वेष्टि तं गौस्त्यजति भारत॥
en: He, who acts according to the advice of dishonest men, who behaves falsely and does not listen to the advice of good friends and prefers others to those who are his own, is cast off by the earth, O Bharata.

sn: स त्वं विरुध्य तैवीरैरन्येभ्यस्त्राणमिच्छसि। अशिष्टेभ्योऽसमर्थेभ्यो मूढेभ्यो भरतर्षभ।॥
en: Yourself, being opposed to those heroes, desire to be served by those who are strangers to you, and who are dishonest, incompetent and fools, O best among the Bharatas.

sn: को हि शक्रसमान् ज्ञातीनतिक्रम्य महारथान्। अन्येभ्यस्त्राणमाशंसेत् त्वदन्यो भुवि मानवः॥
en: What man, besides yourself in this world, abandoning kinsmen who are mighty carwarriors and each equal to Shakra himself, expects safely with the help of others.

sn: जन्मप्रभृति कौन्तेया नित्यं विनिकृतास्त्वया। न च ते जातु कुप्यन्ति धर्मात्मानो हि पाण्डवा॥
en: Ever since their birth, have the sons of Kunti been persecuted by you but those virtuous-souled sons of Pandu are not vindictive at your conduct.

sn: मिथ्योपचरितास्तात जन्मप्रभृति बान्धवाः। त्वयि सम्यङ्महाबाहो प्रतिपन्ना यशस्विनः॥
en: O friend, ever since birth the sons of Pandu have been treated with deception but those renowned men, O you of long arms, have treated you generously.

sn: त्वयापि प्रतिपत्तव्यं तथैव भरतर्षभ। स्वेषु बन्धुषु मुख्येषु मा मन्युवशमन्वगाः॥
en: By you too should they be treated in the same way, O you best among the race of Bharata; do not show anger towards your own kinsmen.

sn: त्रिवर्गयुक्तः प्राज्ञानामारम्भो भतर्षभ। धर्मार्थावनुरुध्यन्ते त्रिवर्गासम्भवे नराः॥
en: The energy of wise men follows all the three objects (virtue, profit and desire) O best among the race of Bharata and in the event of it being impossible to follow all the three objects people choose virtue and profit.

sn: पृथक् च विनिविष्टानां धर्मं धीरोऽनुरुध्यते। मध्यमोऽर्थं कलिं बालः काममेवानुरुध्यते॥
en: If these three are to be pursued separately a wise inan chooses virtue; an indifferent man (i.e. neither wise nor a fool) chooses worldly good, while a boy chooses desire.

sn: इन्द्रियैः प्राकृतो लोभाद् धर्मं विप्रजहाति यः। कामार्थावनुपायेन लिप्समानो विनश्यति॥
en: The fool, who out of avarice and desire for sexual pleasure, abandons virtue and desires to gain his desire and profit by improper means, is ruined.

sn: कामार्थों लिप्समानस्तु धर्ममेवादितश्चरेत्। न हि धर्मादपैत्यर्थः कामो वाऽपि कदाचन॥
en: The man, who is desirous of gaining the object of desire or worldly profit, must first of all practice virtue; desire or profit is seldom detached from virtue.

sn: उपायं धर्ममेवाहुस्त्रिवर्गस्य विशाम्पते। लिप्समानो हि तेनाशु कक्षेऽग्निरिव वर्धते॥
en: It is said that virtue is the means of gaining the three objects, O lord of the universe; and he, who is desirous of getting them by this means increases in prosperity as fire in a heap of dry grass.

sn: स त्वं तातानुपायेन लिप्ससे भरतर्षभ। आधिराज्यं महद् दापितं प्रथितं सर्वराजसु॥
en: You however, my dear friend, desire to get by improper means a greatly extensive kingdom well known among all the kings.

sn: आत्मानं तक्षति ह्येष वनं परशुना यथा। यः सम्यग्वर्तमानेषु मिथ्या राजन् प्रवर्तते॥
en: He, who behaves deceitfully towards those following the right path, O king, cuts himself down as the forest by an axe; one does not cut off the intellect of another whose defeat he does not desire.

sn: न तस्य हि मतिं छिन्द्याद् यस्य नेच्छेत् पराभवम्। अविच्छिन्नमतेरस्य कल्याणे धीयते मतिः। आत्मवान् नावमन्येत त्रिषु लोकेषु भारत॥
en: For one, whose intellect has been clouded, cannot direct his attention to what is conducive to his good. One who keeps his soul under proper control does not think lightly of anything in the three worlds, O Bharata,

sn: अप्यन्यं प्राकृतं किंचित् किमु तान् पाण्डवर्षभान्। अमर्षवशमापन्नो न किंचिद् बुध्यते जनः॥
en: Not even an ordinary creature-not to speak to those foremost among men, those sons of Pandu; a man, who is under the influence of wrath, can not discern anything.

sn: छिद्यते ह्याततं सर्वं प्रमाणं पश्य भारत। श्रेयस्ते दुर्जनात् तात पाण्डवैः सह संगतम्॥
en: All the rank growth must be cut off; O Bharata, look at the proofs; peace with the sons of Pandu is more to your interest than union with wicked people.

sn: तैर्हि सम्प्रीयमाणस्त्वं सर्वान् कामानवाप्स्यसि। पाण्डवैनिर्मितां भूमि भुञ्जानो राजसत्तम॥
en: Living in peace with them you will succeed in all your objects enjoying the territories built up by the sons of Pandu, O best among kings,

sn: पाण्डवान् पृष्ठतः कृत्वा त्राणमाशंससेऽन्यतः। दुःशासने दुर्विषहे कर्णे चापि ससौबले॥
en: Keeping the sons of Pandu behind you, you repose your hopes for safety on other sources, namely on Dushasana, Durvisha, Karna and the son of Subala.

sn: एतेष्वैश्वर्यमाधाय भूतिमिच्छसि भारत। न चैते तव पर्याप्ता ज्ञाने धर्मार्थयोस्तथा॥
en: Reposing your kingly prosperity on them you wish for prosperity, O Bharata; but these friends of yours have not sufficient knowledge of virtue of worldly profit.

sn: विक्रमे चाप्यपर्याप्ताः पाण्डवान् प्रति भारत। न हीमे सर्ववराजानः पर्याप्ताः सहितास्त्वया॥
en: They are not competent too in prowess or in strength, to be a match against the sons of Pandu; nor are all these kings united with you competent,

sn: क्रुद्धस्य भीमसेनस्य प्रेक्षितुं मुखमाहवे। इदं संनिहितं तात समग्रं पार्थिवं बलम्॥
en: To look at the face of Bhimasena when exercised by anger in battle field. This entire assembled army of the earth is at your elbow.

sn: अयं भीष्मस्तथा द्रोणः कर्णश्चायं तथा कृपः। भूरिश्रवाः सौमदत्तिरश्वत्थामा जयद्रथः॥
en: This Bhishma, Drona, as also this Karna, Kripa as also Bhurishravas, Ashvathama, the son of Somadatta and Janardana,

sn: अशक्ताः सर्वं एवैते प्रतियोद्धं धनंजयम्। अजेयो ह्यर्जुनः संख्ये सर्वैरपि सुरासुरैः। मानुषैरिप गन्धर्वैर्मा युद्धे चेत आधिथाः॥
en: All these are incapable of fighting against Dhananjaya. This Arjuna is invincible in battle by all the Gods and Asuras and by all human beings and Gandharvas. Do not fix your mind on battle.

sn: दृश्यतां वा पुमान् कश्चितं समग्रे पार्थिवे बले। योऽर्जुनं समरे प्राप्य स्वस्तिमानाव्रजेद् गृहान्॥
en: Do you see any man in this entire army who, having met Arjuna face to face in battle, has returned home safe?

sn: किं ते जनक्षयेणेह कृतेन भरतर्षभ। यस्मिञ्जिते जितं तत् स्यात् पुमानेकः स दृश्यताम्॥५२
en: Of what advantage will a massacre of men be to you, O best among the Bharatas. Show me the man who will defeat the one whose defeat will mean victory to you,

sn: यः स देवान् सगन्धर्वान् सयक्षासुरपन्नगान्। अजयत् खाण्डवप्रस्थे कस्तं युध्येत मानवः॥
en: Him who vanquished the gods along with the Gandharvas and Yakshas, and Asuras and Serpents in Khandava Prastha-who will fight against that son of Pandavas?

sn: तथा विराटनगरे श्रूयते महदद्भुतम्। एकस्य च बहूनां च पर्याप्तं तन्निदर्शनम्॥
en: In the same way in the city of Virata is heard a very strange tale in the fight of one against many; that is a sufficient proof.

sn: युद्धे येन महादेवः साक्षात् संतोषितः शिवः। तमजेयमनाधृष्यं विजेतुं जिष्णुमच्युतम्। आशंससीह समरे वीरमर्जुनमूर्जितम्॥
en: Do you wish to defeat that unconquerable, irrepressible and undetoriating Jishnu, the heroic Arjuna when enraged in battle, by whom in an encounter even Mahadeva was gratified?

sn: मद् द्वितीयं पुनः पार्थं कः प्रार्थयितुमर्हति। युद्धे प्रतीपमायान्तमपि साक्षात् पुरंदरः॥
en: Who can wish to defeat him having me as his help when he goes to the battle field like Indra (himself)?

sn: बाहुभ्यामुद्वहेद् भूमि दहेत् क्रुद्ध इमाः प्रजाः। पातयेत् त्रिदिवाद् देवान् योऽर्जुनं समरे जयेत्॥
en: He, who would defeat Arjuna in battle, could bear the earth with his arms and being excited with wrath could burn up all earthy creatures, and could hurl down the gods from heaven.

sn: पश्य पुत्रांस्तथा भ्रातृज्ञातीन् सम्बन्धिनस्तथा। त्वत्कृते न विनश्येयुरिमे भरतसत्तमाः॥
en: Look at your sons and at your brothers and at your kinsmen and other relations; let them not be destroyed by an act done by you, O you best among the race of Bharata.

sn: अस्तु शेषं कौरवाणां मा पराभूदिदं कुलम्। कुलन इति नोच्येथा नष्टकीर्तिनराधिप॥
en: Let not this race of Kurus be exterminated ard let not yourself be spoken of as the destroyer of the race and be of great notoriety, O lord of men.

sn: त्वामेव स्थापयिष्यन्ति यौवराज्ये महारथाः। महाराज्येऽपि पितरं धृतराष्ट्रं जनेश्वरम्॥
en: Those mighty car warriors will establish yourself as the viceroy and your father Dhritarashtra, the lord of men, as the emperor.

sn: मा तात श्रियमायान्तीमवमंस्थाः समुद्यताम्। अर्धं प्रदाय पार्थेभ्यो महतीं श्रियमाप्नुहि॥
en: Do you not, my dear friend, disregard this prosperity which has appeared in the horizon and is about to come to you; having given half to the sons of Pritha attain to great prosperity.

sn: पाण्डवैः संशमं कृत्वा कृत्वा च सुहृदां वचः। सम्प्रीयमाणोमित्रैश्च चिरं भद्राण्यवाप्सस्यसि॥
en: Having effected peace with the sons of Pandu and listening to the advice to your friends and living in peace with your friends will you ever attain to blessing.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततः शान्तनवो भीष्मो दुर्योधनममर्षणम्। केशवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा प्रोवाच भरतर्षभ॥
en: Vaishampayana said Then did the son of Shantanu, Bhishma, say to the wrathful Duryodhana, hearing the words of Keshava, O you best among the Bharata.

sn: कृष्णेन वाक्यमुक्तोऽसि सुहृदां शममिच्छता। अन्वपद्यस्व तत् तात मा मन्युवशमन्वगाः॥
en: “By Krishna has been spoken the words of a friend wishing for peace; listen to that my dear son, and do not follow the lead if vindictiveness.

sn: अकृत्वा वचनं तात केशवस्य महात्मनः। श्रेयो न जातु न सुखं न कल्याणमवाप्स्यसि॥
en: By not acting up to the words of the great souled Keshava, will you not be able to obtain prosperity nor happiness nor your good.

sn: धर्म्यमर्थ्य महाबाहुराह त्वां तात केशवः। तदर्थमभिपद्यस्व मा राजन् नीनशः प्रजाः॥
en: The one of long arms, Keshava, has told you, my dear son, what will lead to virtue and to the obtainment of earthly good; and may you obtain that object, О king; do not destroy these living creatures.

sn: ज्वलितां त्वमिमां लक्ष्मी भारती सर्वराजसु। जीवतो धृतराष्ट्रस्य दौरात्म्याद् भ्रंशयिष्यसि॥
en: Do not by your wicked deeds cause to break down this blazing prosperity of the Bharatas, among all kings while Dhritarashtra is alive.

sn: आत्मानं च सहामात्यं सपुत्रभ्रातृबान्धवम्। अहमित्यनया बुद्ध्या जीविताद् भ्रंशयिष्यसि॥
en: Yourself with your ministers and with your sons, brothers and friends will be deprived of lives by your way-wardness and obstinacy.

sn: अतिक्रामन् केशवस्य तथ्यं वचनमर्थवत्। पितुश्च भरतश्रेष्ठ विदुरस्य च धीमतः॥
en: By acting against the beneficial advice leading to the obtainment of earthly benefit of Keshava as also of your father and the wise Vidura, O foremost among the Bharatas,

sn: मा कुलघ्नः कुपुरुषो दुर्मतिः कापथं गमः। मातरं पितरं चैव मा मज्जीः शोकसागरे॥
en: Do not bring about the extermination of your race; do not act like a wicked man of evil intellect and do not follow a wrong course. Do not drown your father and your mother in a sea of grief."

sn: अथ द्रोणोऽब्रवीत् तत्र दुर्योधनमिदं वचः। अमर्षवशमापन्नं निःश्वसन्तं पुनः पुनः॥
en: Then did Drona say these words to Duryodhana there who was under the influence of wrath and breathing hard again and again.

sn: धर्मार्थयुक्तं वचनमाह त्वां तात केशवः। तथा भीष्मः शान्तनवस्तज्जुषस्व नराधिप॥
en: “Keshava said words to you which are pregnant with virtue and profit, my dear son,; so did Bhishma, the son of Shantanu, O ruler of men, accept them.

sn: प्राज्ञौ मेधाविनौ दान्तावर्थकामौ बहुश्रुतौ। आहतुस्त्वां हितं वाक्यं तज्जुषस्व नराधिप।॥
en: The two are wise, have intelligence, have their souls under control, know what leads to are, as virtue and to worldly good and they are vastly learned; they have told you beneficial words; O ruler of men, accept them.

sn: अनुतिष्ठ महाप्राज्ञ कृष्णभीष्मौ यदूचतुः। माधवं बुद्धिमोहेन माऽवमंस्थाः परंतप॥
en: Follow, O greatly wise man, what the two, Krishna and Bhishma have said; do not from perverted understanding insult Madhava, O chastiser of foes.

sn: ये त्वां प्रोत्साहयन्त्येते नैते कृत्याय कर्हिचित्। वैरं परेषां ग्रीवायां प्रतिमोक्ष्यन्ति संयुगे।॥
en: Those, who are now encouraging and supporting you, will hardly do any thing when the time comes; and they rather will throw the (act of bearing) hostilities on the shoulders of others.

sn: मा जीधनः प्रजाः सर्वाः पुत्रान् भ्रातृस्तथैव च। वासुदेवार्जुनौ यत्र विद्ध्यजेयानलं हि तान्॥
en: Do not slay all these living creatures as also your sons and brothers; the side on which Vasudeva and Arjuna know unconquerable and invisible.

sn: एतच्चैव मतं सत्यं सुहृदोः कृष्णभीष्मयोः। यदि नादास्यसे तात पश्चात् तप्स्यसि भारत॥
en: This is truly the opinion of your friend Krishna, and if you do not accept that, my dear son, you will grieve for it in the end, O Bharata,

sn: यथोक्तं जामदग्न्येन भूयानेष ततोऽर्जुनः। कृष्णो हि देवकीपुत्रो देवैरपि सुदुःसहः। किं ते सुखप्रियेणेह प्रोक्तेन भरतर्षभ॥
en: Arjuna is still mightier than what the son of Jamadagni has described him to be; Krishna, the son of Devaki, is hard to vanquished even by gods, O best among the Bharatas, what is the use of telling you what is conducive to your happiness and ought therefore to be desired for by you.

sn: एतत् ते सर्वमाख्यातं यथेच्छसि तथा कुरु। न हि त्वामुत्सहे वक्तुं भूयो भरतसत्तम॥
en: All this is described to you; do as you like; I do not wish to address you more, O best among the Bharatas.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तस्मिनं वाक्यान्तरे वाक्यं क्षत्तापि विदुरोऽब्रवीत्। दुर्योधनमभिप्रेक्ष्य धार्तराष्ट्रममर्षणम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said At the end of that speech did Kshattri Vidura also speak words looking at the wrathful son of Dhritarashtra, Duryodhana.

sn: दुर्योधन न शोचामि त्वामहं भरतर्षभ। इमौ तु वृद्धौ शोचामि गान्धारी पितरं च ते॥
en: 'Duryodhana, I do not grieve for you, O best among the Bharatas; I grieve for these two old people namely your father and Gandhari (your mother).

sn: यावनाथौ चरिष्येते त्वया नाथेन दुर्हदा। हतमित्रौ हतामात्यौ लूनपक्षाविवाण्डजौ॥
en: Having yourself of wicked heart as their protector, they will wander about without any one (in a short time) with their friends slain and with ministers killed, like those born of eggs deprived of their wings.

sn: भिक्षुको विचरिष्येते शोचन्तौ पृथिवीमिमाम्। कुलघ्नमीदृशं पापं जनयित्वा कुपूरुषम्॥
en: Grieving, they will wander about as beggars on the earth, having begotten such a wicked and vicious man, the exterminator of his race.

sn: अथ दुर्योधनं राजा धृतराष्ट्रोऽभ्यभाषत। आसीनं भ्रातृभिः सार्धं राजभिः परिवारितम्॥
en: Then the king Dhritarashtra said to Duryodhana who was seated along with his brothers and surrounded by other kings,

sn: दुर्योधन निबोधेदं शौरिणोक्तं महात्मना। आदत्स्व शिवमत्यन्तं योगक्षेमवदव्ययम्॥
en: "O Duryodhana, listen to this alive given by the great-souled Shouri; accept his words which are true, most beneficial, and conducive to our salvation.

sn: अनेन हि सहायेन कृष्णेनाक्लिष्टकर्मणा। इष्टान् सर्वानभिप्रायान् प्राप्स्याम: सर्वराजसु॥
en: By the help of namely of Krishna of unblamable acts, we, of all other kings, shall obtain all desirable

sn: सुसंहतः केशवेन तात गच्छ युधिष्ठिरम्। चर स्वस्त्ययनं कृत्स्नं भरतानामनामयम्॥
