en: being well united with Keshava, my dear son, go to Yudhishthira and make arrangements for a ceremony for the good of the Bharatas (the Pandavas and Kurus united together).

sn: वासुदेवेन तीर्थेन तात गच्छस्व संशमम्। कालप्राप्तमिदं मन्ये मा त्वं दुर्योधनातिगाः॥
en: By the help if Vasudeva, make peace (with the Pandavas); I think the proper time has now arrived; O Dhritarashtra, do not disobey me.

sn: शमं चेद् याचमानं त्वं प्रत्याख्यास्यसि केशवम्। त्वदर्थमभिजल्पन्तं न तवास्त्यपराभवः॥
en: If you abandon peace which is begged from you for the accomplishment of your own good, then will victory never be yours."

description: The speech of Bhishma and Drona
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच धृतराष्ट्रवचः श्रुत्वा भीष्मद्रोणौ समव्यथौ। दुर्योधनमिदं वाक्यमूचतुः शासनातिगम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Hearing the words of Dhritarashtra the two, sympathizing with Dhritarashtra said, word to Duryodhana who did not act according to the instructions of his elders.

description: The speech of Bhishma and Drona
sn: यावत् कृष्णावसंनद्धौ यावत् तिष्ठति गाण्डिवम्। यावद् धौम्यो न मेधाग्नौ जुहोतीह द्विषद्बलम्॥
en: So long as the two Krishna's are not clad in coats of mail, so long as the Gandiva bow is lying still, so long as Dhaumya the priest of the Pandavas does not make offerings to the fire of war, and thereby burns up the strength of their enemy,

description: The speech of Bhishma and Drona
sn: यावन्न प्रेक्षते क्रुद्धः सेनां तव युधिष्ठिरः। ह्रीनिषेवो महेष्वासस्तावच्छाम्यतु वैशसम्॥
en: So long as Yudhishthira who is endued with modesty and a great bow-man does not look on your army with wrath, let hostilities cease.

description: The speech of Bhishma and Drona
sn: यावन्न दृश्यते पार्थः स्वेऽप्यनीके व्यवस्थितः। भीमसेनो महेष्वासस्तावच्छाम्यतु वैशसम्॥
en: So long as the son of Pritha, the great bowman Bhimasena is not seen to take up his position in the division of his own army, let hostilities cease,

description: The speech of Bhishma and Drona
sn: यावन्न चरते मार्गान् पृतनामभिधर्षयन्। भीमसेनो गदापाणिस्तावत् संशाम्य पाण्डवैः॥
en: Let there be peace with Pandavas so long as Bhimasena, with the mace in his hands, does not come this way vanquishing his opponents.

description: The speech of Bhishma and Drona
sn: यावन्न शातयत्याजौ शिरांसि गजयोधिनाम्। गदया वीरघातिन्या फलानीव वनस्पतेः॥
en: So long as he dose not cut off the heads of warriors fighting on elephants and make them by his hero killing mace roll like the fruits of the palmyra,

description: The speech of Bhishma and Drona
sn: कालेन परिपक्वानि तावच्छाम्यतु वैशसम्। नकुलः सहदेवश्च धृष्टद्युम्नश्च पार्षतः॥
en: Which are ripening on their proper time having come, let hostilities cease. So long as Nakula and Sahadeva and Dhrishtadyumna, the son of Prishata,

description: The speech of Bhishma and Drona
sn: विराटश्च शिखण्डी च शैशुपालिश्च दंशिताः। यावन्न प्रविशन्त्येते नक्रा इव महार्णवम्॥
en: And Virata and Sikhandi and the son of Shishupala clad in their coats of mail, do not penetrate into your army like crocodiles in the great sea,

description: The speech of Bhishma and Drona
sn: कृतास्त्राः क्षिप्रमस्यन्तस्तावच्छाम्यतु वैशसम्। यावन्न सुकुमारेषु शरीरेषु महीक्षिताम्॥ गाघ्रपत्राः पतन्त्युचास्तावच्छाम्यतु वैशसम्। चन्दनागुरुदिग्धेषु हारनिष्कघरेषु च। नोर:सु यावद् योधानां महेष्वासैर्महेषवः॥
en: Showering arrows, as they are masters in weapon, let hostilities cease. So long as in the delicate bodies of the rulers of the earth terrible arrows with wings do not fall, let hostilities cease. So long as on the breasts of those warriors smeared with sandal and other sweet scented unguents and bedecked with golden garlands and gems, do not fall the dreadful weapons of iron and steel shot by mighty bowmen,

description: The speech of Bhishma and Drona
sn: कृतास्त्रैः क्षिप्रमस्यद्भिर्दूरपातिभिरायसाः। अभिलक्ष्यैर्निपात्यन्ते तावच्छाम्यतु वैशसम्॥
en: Masters in the use of weapons who can shoot from a long distance and with good aim, let hostilities cease.

description: The speech of Bhishma and Drona
sn: अभिवादयमानं त्वां शिरसा राजकुञ्जरः। पाणिभ्यां प्रतिगृह्णातु धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Let the virtuous king Yudhishthira, that best of kings take you by the hand while you are saluting him with your head bowed down.

description: The speech of Bhishma and Drona
sn: ध्वजाङ्कुशपताकाङ्क दक्षिणं ते सुदक्षिणः। स्कन्धे निक्षिपतां बाहुं शान्तये भरतर्षभ॥
en: Let that one who has performed many sacrifices comfort you, by placing his righi arm, marked with the sign of a banner and hook on you shoulders.

description: The speech of Bhishma and Drona
sn: रत्नौषधिसमेतेन रक्ताङ्गुलितलेन च। उपविष्टस्य पृष्ठं ते पाणिना परिमार्जतु॥
en: Let him put his hands with fingers bedecked with gems and the palm red, on your back while you are seated.

description: The speech of Bhishma and Drona
sn: शालस्कन्धो महाबाहुस्त्वां स्वजानो वृकोदरः। साम्नाभिवदतां चापि शान्तये भरतर्षभ॥
en: Let him, whose shoulders are broad as the trunk of Shala trees, Vrikodara, of long arms, embrace you and with good will greet you for the sake of peace, O best among the Bharatas.

description: The speech of Bhishma and Drona
sn: अर्जुनेन यमाभ्यां च त्रिभिस्तैरभिवादितः। मूर्ध्नि तान् समुपाघ्राय प्रेम्णाभिवद पार्थिव॥
en: Being saluted by the three, Arjuna and the twins, you smell their head and converse in terms of peace, O ruler of the earth.

description: The speech of Bhishma and Drona
sn: दृष्ट्वा त्वां पाण्डवैवीरैर्धातृभिः सह संगतम्। यावदानन्दजाश्रूणि प्रमुञ्चन्तु नराधिपाः॥
en: Let all these rulers of men shed tears of joy at beholding yourself united in peace with your brothers who are heroes.

description: The speech of Bhishma and Drona
sn: घुष्यतां राजधानीषु सर्वसम्पन्महीक्षिताम्। पृथिवी भ्रातृभावेन भुज्यतां विज्वरो भव॥
en: Proclaim it in the several capitals and among all the rulers of the earth; enjoy the sovereignty of the earth like brothers and be freed from all troubles.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच श्रुत्वा दुर्योधनो वाक्यमप्रियं कुरुसंसदि। प्रत्युवाच महाबाहुं वासुदेवं यशस्विनम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Duryodhana, hearing in the assembly of the Kurus those words which he little liked, said in reply to Vasudeva of long arms and of great renown.

sn: प्रसमीक्ष्य भवानेतद् वक्तुमर्हति केशव। मामेव हि विशेषेण विभाष्य परिगर्हसे॥
en: "It is proper, that you should speak to me in this way after due consideration; but you speak, finding fault with me especially.

sn: भक्तिवादेन पार्थानामकस्मान्मधुसूदन। भवान् गर्हयते नित्यं किं समीक्ष्य बलाबलम्॥
en: Why do you, O slayer of Madhu, speak in terms of praise of the sons of Pritha and why are you ever finding fault with me without due consideration of the strength and weakness of our cause?

sn: भवान् क्षत्ता च वाप्याचार्यो वा पितामहः। मामेव परिगर्हन्ते नान्यं कंचन पार्थिवम्॥
en: You and Kshattri and the king, and the preceptor and the grandfather all find fault with me and not with any other king of the earth.

sn: न चाहं लक्षये कंचिद् व्यभिचारमिहात्मनः। अथ सर्वे भवन्तो मां विद्विषन्ति सराजकाः॥
en: But in this matter I do not find any unworthy conduct of myself but still all of you including the king hate me.

sn: न चाहं कंचिदत्यर्थमपराधमरिंदम। विचिन्तयन् प्रपश्यामि सुसूक्ष्ममपि केशव॥
en: I have not committed the slightest fault, O chastiser of foes, nor do I see any after a most minute and searching examination, OKeshava.

sn: प्रियाभ्युपगते द्यूते पाण्डवा मधुसूदन। जिताः शकुनिना राज्यं तत्र किं मम दुष्कृतम्॥
en: O slayer of Madhu, the Pandavas were defeated at a game of dice in which they engaged of their own will and their kingdom was won by Shakuni; what fault is there on my part in this matter?

sn: यत् पुनर्रविणं किंचित् तत्राजीयन्त पाण्डवाः। तेभ्य एवाभ्यनुज्ञातं तत् तदा मधुसूदन॥
en: Indeed, 0 slayer of Madhu, I ordered at the time for the return of the wealth which the Pandavas had lost in that case.

sn: अपराधो न चास्माकं यत् ते द्यूते पराजिताः। अजेया जयतां श्रेष्ठ पार्थाः प्रताजिता वनम्॥
en: It is not our fault that defeated at another game of dice-those invincible sons of Pritha-those foremost among victors were thus exiled into the forest.

sn: केन वाप्यपराधेन विरुद्ध्यन्त्यरिभिः सह। अशक्ताः पाण्डवाः कृष्ण प्रहृष्टाः प्रत्यमित्रवत्॥
en: By the imputation of what fault do they regard ourselves as their enemies-O Krishna? The Pandavas are weak and incapable but they yet cheering treat us as their enemies.

sn: किमस्माभिः कृतं तेषां कस्मिन् वा पुनरागसि। धार्तराष्ट्रान् जिघांसन्ति पाण्डवाः संजयैः सह॥
en: What has been done by us to them and for what injury again do those sons of Pandu united with this Srinjayas, try to slay the sons of Dhritarashtra?

sn: न चापि वयमुग्रेण कर्मणा वचनेन वा। प्रभ्रष्टाः प्रणमामेह भयादपि शतक्रतुम्॥
en: We will not, fearing harsh deeds or words, bow down out of fear even to the performer of a hundred sacrifices (Indra).

sn: न च तं कृष्ण पश्यामि क्षत्रधर्ममनुष्ठितम्। उत्सहेत युधा जेतुं यो नः शत्रुनिबर्हण॥
en: I do not see any body, O Krishna, following the duties of a Kshatriya who would i aspire to defeat us in battle, O chastiser of foes.

sn: न हि भीष्मकृपद्रोणाः सकर्णा मधुसूदन। देवैरपि युधा जेतुं शक्याः किमुत पाण्डवैः॥
en: Bhishma, Kripa and Drona, along with Karna, O slayer of Madhu, are incapable of being vanquished even by the gods, how can they be so by the sons of Pandu?

sn: स्वधर्ममनुपश्यन्तो यदि माधव संयुगे। अस्त्रेण निधनं काले प्राप्स्यामः स्वर्ग्यमेव तत्॥
en: If following the duties laid down by my religion, O Madhava, I fall down dead in the field killed by arms in the proper time, it will lead me to heaven.

sn: मुख्यश्चैवैष नो धर्मः क्षत्रियाणां जनार्दन। यच्छयीमहि संग्रामे शरतल्पगता वयम्॥
en: The principal duty of ours, Kshatriyas, O Janardana, is that we should lie down on a bed of arrows in the battle field.

sn: ते वयं वीरशयनं प्राप्स्यामो यदि संयुगे। अप्रणम्यैव शत्रूणां न नस्तप्स्यन्ति माधव॥
en: If we lie down like heroes in the battle without bowing before the enemies, then it is no matter for regret, O Madhava.

sn: कश्च जातु कुले जातः क्षत्रधर्मेण वर्तयन्। भयाद् वृत्तिं समीक्ष्यैवं प्रणमेदिह कर्हिचित्॥
en: Who is there, who born in a noble family and abiding by the rules of the Kshatriya class, seeing that his life is in danger would bow before any body?

sn: उद्यच्छेदेव न नमेदुद्यमो ह्येव पौरुषम्। अप्यपर्वणि भज्येत न नमेदिह कर्हिचित्॥
en: Keeping one's self erect now should not bow down, for energy or exertion itself is manliness; he may even break at his weak points but on no account should he bow before any body.

sn: इति मातङ्गवचनं परीप्सन्ति हितेप्सवः। धर्माय चैव प्रणमेद् ब्राह्मणेभ्यश्च मद्विधः॥
en: This saying of Matanga is followed by those that desire their own good; men ſike me bow only to Brahmanas for the sake of virtue.

sn: अचिन्तयन् कंचिदन्यं यावज्जीवं तथाऽऽचरेत्। एष धर्मः क्षत्रियाणां मतमेतच्च मे सदा॥
en: Without paying regard to any body else, throughout his life he should act thus, this is the duty of the Kshatriyas in my opinion and such has ever been my conduct.

sn: राज्यांशश्चाभ्यनुज्ञातो यो मे पित्रा पुराभवत्। न स लभ्यः पुनर्जातु मयि जीवति केशव॥
en: The share of the kingdom that was given them in early days will not be regained by them during my life time, O Keshava.

sn: यावच्च राजा ध्रियते धृतराष्ट्रो जनार्दन। न्यस्तशस्त्रा वयं ते वाप्युपजीवाम माधव। अप्रदेयं पुरा दत्तं राज्यं परवतो मम॥
en: O Janardana, so long as the position of a king is held by Dhritarashtra we shall live as his dependents with swords laid aside, O Madhava; this kingdom which ought not to have been given away was given away when I depended on others.

sn: अज्ञानाद् वा भयाद्वापि मयि बाले जनार्दन। न तदद्य पुनर्लभ्यं पाण्डवैर्वृष्णिनन्दन।॥
en: Out of ignorance or fear when I was a child, O Janardana; it is not now to be regained by the sons of Pandu, o delighted of the Vrishinis.

sn: ध्रियमाणे महाबाहौ मयि सम्प्रति केशव। तावदप्यपरित्याज्यं भूमेनः पाण्डवान् प्रति॥
en: So long as this is held by myself of long arms, O Keshava, I shall not leave aside which is pierced by the point of a sharp needle.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततः प्रशम्य दाशार्हः क्रोधपर्याकुलेक्षणः। दुर्योधनमिदं वाक्यमब्रवीत् कुरुसंसदि॥
en: Vaishampayana said Then reflecting, did the scion of the Dasharha race, speak these words to Duryodhana in that assembly of the Kurus.

sn: लप्स्यसे वीरशयनं काममेतदवाप्स्यसि। स्थिरो भव सहामात्यो विमर्दो भविता महान्॥
en: To get the sleep of a hero is your desire and it will be fulfilled; wait for a short time with your ministers and there will be a great massacre.

sn: यच्चैवं मन्यसे मूढ न मे कश्चिद् व्यतिक्रमः। पाण्डवेष्विति तत् सर्वं निबोधत नराधिपाः॥
en: O fool, you think that there is nothing blamable in your conduct towards the Pandavas; all the kings here know this.

sn: श्रिया संतप्यमानेन पाण्डवानां महात्मनाम्। त्वया दुर्मन्त्रितं द्यूतं सौबलेन च भारत॥
en: Being jealous of the prosperity of the great-souled sons of Pandu you arranged for a game at dice consultation with the son of Subala, O Bharata.

sn: कथं च ज्ञातयस्तात श्रेयांसः साधुसम्मताः अथान्याय्यमुपस्थातुं जिह्येनाजिह्मचारिणः॥
en: How could your cousins, my dear fellow, who are worthy in every respect and of honest turns of mind and virtuous, unite themselves with this deceitful one?

sn: अक्षयूतं महाप्राज्ञ सतां मतिविनाशनम्। असतां तत्र जायन्ते भेदाश्च व्यसनानि च॥
en: O greatly wise man, dice destroys the intelligence of the honest and in the dishonest it gives rise to disputes and other troubles.

sn: तदिदं व्यसनं घोरं त्वया द्यूतमुखं कृतम्। असमीक्ष्य सदाचारान् सार्धं पापानुबन्धनैः॥
en: By you and your wicked followers was planned this terrible calamity by means of dice without consulting with those who are of good habits of life.

sn: कश्चान्यो भ्रातृभार्यां वै विप्रकर्तुं तथाऽर्हति। आनीय च सभां व्यक्तं यथोक्ता द्रौपदी त्वया।॥
en: Who else save yourself could treat the wife of your brother in that way and after brining Draupadi to that council hall and using insulting words as you did?

sn: कुलीना शीलसम्पन्ना प्राणेभ्योऽपि गरीयसी। महिषी पाण्डुपुत्राणां तथा विनिकृता त्वया॥
en: She is of noble birth, of good behaviour and dearer to them than even their lives; and that queen of the sons of Pandu was thus insulted by you.

sn: जानन्ति कुरवः सर्वे यथोक्ताः कुरुसंसदि। दुःशासनेन कौन्तेयाः प्रव्रजन्तः परंतपाः॥
en: All the Kurus know how in the assembly those chastisers of foes, the sons of Kunti, were on the eve of their exile, addressed by Dushasana.

sn: सम्यग्वृत्तेष्वलुब्धेषु सततं धर्मचारिषु। स्वेषु बन्धुषु कः साधुश्चरेदेवमसाम्प्रतम्॥
en: What good man would treat in this unbecoming way his own near kinsmen of good habits of life, who are not covetous and who always practice virtues.

sn: नृशंसानामनार्याणां पुरुषाणां च भाषणम्। कर्णदुःशासनाभ्यां च त्वया च बहुशः कृतम्॥
en: Speeches befitting only the cruel and dishonorable men, were used by Karna and Dushasana as also by yourself.

sn: सह मात्रा प्रदग्धुं तान् बालकान् वारणावते। आस्थितः परमं यत्नं न समृद्धं च तत् तव।।१३
en: You took very great pains to burn them up when boys along with their mother at Varanavata but that attempt of yours was not successful.

sn: ऊषुश्च सुचिरं कालं प्रच्छन्नाः पाण्डवास्तदा। मात्रा सहैकचक्रायां ब्राह्मणस्य निवेशने॥
en: At that time did the sons of Pandu live for a long time in disguise in company with their mother in the house of a Brahmana Ekachakra.

sn: विषेण सर्पबन्धैश्च यतिताः पाण्डवास्त्वया। सर्वोपायैर्विनाशाय न समृद्धं च तत् तव॥
en: By poison, by snake, and by rope, in fact by every means was the destruction of the sons of Pandu attempted by you but that attempt of yours was not successful.

sn: एवंबुद्धिः पाण्डवेषु मिथ्यावृत्तिः सदा भवान्। कथं ते नापराधोऽस्ति पाण्डवेषु महात्मसु॥
en: Such was ever your inclination and treacherous treatment towards the sons of Pandu; how have you not then offended the great-souled Pandavas?

sn: यच्चैभ्यो याचमानेभ्यः पित्र्यमंशं न दित्ससि। तच्च पाप प्रदातासि भ्रष्टैश्वर्यो निपातितः॥
en: If you do not give them their paternal share when they ask for it, you shall, O wicked one, have to give it when you will be overthrown, deprived of your prosperity.

sn: कृत्वा बहून्यकार्याणि पाण्डवेषु नृशंसवत्। मिथ्यावृत्तिरनार्यः सन्नद्य विप्रतिपद्यसे॥
en: Having done many wicked deeds like a cruel man towards them and behaved like a dishonorable man, you now try to took different.

sn: मातापितृभ्यां भीष्मेण द्रोणेन विदुरेण च। शाम्येति मुहुरुक्तोऽसि न च शाम्यसि पार्थिव॥
en: By your mother and by your father as also by Bhishma, Drona and Vidura have you been told again and again to make peace but, О ruler of the earth, you do not make peace.

sn: शमे हि सुमहाँल्लाभस्तव पार्थस्य चोभयोः। न च रोचयसे राजन् किमन्यद् बुद्धिलाघवात्॥
en: In peace is your great gain, O ruler of the earth, in fact that of both parties, but it does not seem pleasing to you owing to no other cause save the scarcity of your intelligence.

sn: न शर्म प्राप्स्यसे राजन्नुत्क्रम्य सुहृदां वचः। अधर्म्यमयशस्यं च क्रियते पार्थिव त्वया॥
en: By going against the advice of your wellwishers, will you not attain to your highest good; for what is about to be done by you is not virtuous and will not lead you to fame.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवं ब्रुवति दाशार्हे दुर्योधनममर्षणम्। दुःशासन इदं वाक्यमब्रवीत् कुरुसंसदि॥
en: Vaishampayana said The scion of the Dasharha race having thus spoken to the wrathful Duryodhana, Dushasana said these words in the assembly of the Kurus.

sn: न चेत् संधास्यसे राजन् स्वेन कामेन पाण्डवैः। बद्ध्वा किल त्वां दास्यन्ति कुन्तीपुत्राय कौरवाः॥
en: If you do not make peace, O king, of your own free will with the sons of Pandu, the Kauravas will make you over to the son of Kunti bound hand and foot.

sn: वैकर्तनं त्वां च मां च त्रीनेतान् मनुजर्षभ। पाण्डवेभ्यः प्रदास्यन्ति भीष्मो द्रोण: पिता च ते॥
en: The son of Vikartana, yourself and myself, these three, O best among the sons of Manu, your father and Bhishma and Drona will make over to the sons of Pandu.

sn: भ्रातुरेतद् वचः श्रुत्वा धार्तराष्ट्रः सुयोधनः। क्रुद्धः प्रातिष्ठतोत्थाय महानाग इव श्वसन्॥
en: Suyodhana, the son of Dhritarashtra, hearing those words of his brother was very angry and got up from his seat breathing like a huge serpent.

sn: विदुरं धृतराष्ट्रं च महाराजं च बाह्निकम्। कृपं च सोमदत्तं च भीष्मं द्रोणं जनार्दनम्॥
en: Vidura, Dhritarashtra, the great king Balhika, and Kripa, and Somadatta, Bhishma, Drona and Janardana,

sn: सर्वानेताननादृत्य दुर्मतिर्निरपत्रपः। अशिष्टवदमर्यादो मानी मान्यावमानिता।॥
en: Disregarding all these that shameless one of wicked intellect, like a dishonorable man, vain and yet not commanding respect and given to insulting those who ought to be respected, went out of the court.

sn: तं प्रस्थितमभिप्रेक्ष्य भ्रातरो मनुजर्षभम्। अनुजग्मुः सहामात्या राजानश्चापि सर्वशः॥
en: His brothers, having seen him, that best among those born of Manu, go out, followed him along with the ministers and the entire body to the kings.

sn: सभायामुत्थित क्रुद्धं प्रस्थितं भ्रातृभिः सह। दुर्योधनमभिप्रेक्ष्य भीष्मः शान्तनवोऽब्रवीत्॥
en: Seeing Duryodhana rise up in that council and go away accompanied by his brothers, Bhishma the son of Shantanu said.

sn: धर्मार्थावभिसंत्यज्य संरम्भं योऽनुमन्यते। हसन्ति व्यसने तस्य दुर्लदो न चिरादिव॥
en: He who inclines towards wrath abandoning virtue and worldly profit, is soon rejoiced over by wicked men in his troubles.

sn: दुरात्मा राजपुत्रोऽयं धार्तराष्ट्रोऽनुपायकृत्। मिथ्याभिमानी राज्यस्य क्रोधलोभवशानुगः॥
en: son This wicked prince, the of Dhritarashtra, who does not know the proper means of suitable ends and is vain of the kingdom, is come under the influence of wrath and avarice.

sn: कालपक्वमिदं मन्ये सर्वं क्षत्रं जनार्दन। सर्वे ह्यनुसृता मोहात् पार्थिवाः सह मन्त्रिभिः॥
en: I think that the time for the end of all Kshatriyas is come, O Janardana, for all the rulers of the earth along with the ministers have followed him out of folly."

sn: भीष्मस्याथ वचः श्रुत्वा दाशार्हः पुष्करेक्षणः। भीष्मद्रोणमुखान् सर्वानभ्यभाषत वीर्यवान्॥
en: That heroic scion of the Dasharha race, with eyes like the petals of the lotus, hearing the words of Bhishma, said to all of them headed by Bhishma and Drona.

sn: सर्वेषां कुरुवृद्धानां महानयमतिक्रमः। प्रसह्य मन्दमैश्वर्ये न नियच्छत यन्नृपम्॥
en: "This is the great defeat of all the elders among the Kurus that they do not with force obstruct this wicked king in the enjoyment of prosperity.

sn: तत्र कार्यमहं मन्ये कालप्राप्तमरिंदमाः। क्रियमाणे भवेच्छ्रेयस्तत् सर्वं शृणुतानघाः॥
en: O chastiser of foes, I therefore consider that the time has come for you to act; O sinless men, listen to that by doing which you will obtain benefit.

sn: प्रत्यक्षमेतद् भवतां यद् वक्ष्यामि हितं वचः। भवतामानुकूल्येन यदि रोचेत भारताः॥
en: What I shall tell you is clearly for your benefit, if in consequence of its being favourable to you it is approved by you, o Bharatas.

sn: भोजराजस्य वृद्धस्य दुराचारो ह्यनात्मवान्। जीवतः पितुरैश्वर्यं हृत्वा मृत्युवशं गतः॥
en: During the life time of the old king of Bhoja, his son, of wicked behaviour and a slave to his passions, having usurped the throne of his father subjected himself to death.

sn: उग्रसेनसुतः कंसः परित्यक्तः स बान्धवैः। ज्ञातीनां हितकामेन मया शस्तो महामृधे॥
en: Kansa, the son of Ugrasena, being forsaken by his own friends, was killed by me in a great battle from a desire to do good to my kinsmen.

sn: आहुकः पुनरस्माभिमा॑तिभिश्चापि सत्कृतः। उग्रसेनः कृतो राजा भोजराजन्यवर्धनः॥
en: Ugrasena, the son of Ahuka, being duly honored by ourselves with our kinsmen, was anointed king and he extended the territories of the kingdom of Bhoja.

sn: कंसमेकं परित्यज्य कुलार्थं सर्वयादवाः। सम्भूय सुखमेधन्ते भारतान्धकवृष्णयः॥
en: Abandoning the one, namely Kansa, for the sake of the whole race, did all the Yadavas, Andhakas and Vrishnis attain to happiness, O Bharata.

sn: अपि चाप्यवदद् राजन् परमेष्ठी प्रजापतिः। व्यूढे देवासुरे युद्धेऽब्युद्यतेष्वायुधेषु च॥
en: Paramesthi, the lord of all creatures said, O king, when the gods and the Asuras were prepared for battle and were under arms.

sn: द्वैधीभूतेषु लोकेषु विनश्यत्सु च भारत। अब्रवीत् सृष्टिमान् देवो भगवाँल्लोकभावनः॥
en: When the world was divided into two parties and was about to be ruined, O Bharata-that god endued with divine prosperity, the creator and the protector of the world said

sn: पराभविष्यन्त्यसुरा दैतेया दानवैः सह। आदित्या वसवो रुद्रा भविष्यन्ति दिवौकसः॥
en: In a fight with the Daityas, the Danavas, and the Asuras will be defeated, and the Adityas, the Vasus, the Rudras and the denizens of heaven will be victorious.

sn: देवासुरमनुष्याश्च गन्धर्वोरगराक्षसाः। अस्मिन् युद्धे सुसंक्रुद्धा हनिष्यन्ति परस्परम्॥
en: The gods, the Asuras, the human beings, the Gandharvas and the Rakshasas will, in this battle in their race, kill one another.

sn: इति मत्वाब्रवीद् धर्मं परमेष्ठी प्रजापतिः। वरुणाय प्रयच्छतान् बद्ध्वा दैतेयदानवान्॥
en: Thus thinking Paramesthi, the lord of all creatures, said to Dharma-"Binding these Daityas and Danavas make them over to Varuna."

sn: एवमुक्तस्ततो धर्मो नियोगात् परमेष्ठिनः। वरुणाय ददौ सर्वान् बद्ध्वा दैतेयदानवान्॥
en: Dharma being thus spoken to, by the command of Paramesthi binding the Daityas na.

sn: तान् बद्ध्वा धर्मपाशैश्च स्वैश्च पाशैर्जलेश्वरः। वरुणः सागरे यत्तो नित्यं रक्षति दानवान्॥
en: Having bound them with the aids of Dharma as also by his own power, the lord of the caters, Varuna keeps the Danavas ever in the sea.

sn: तथा दुर्योधनं कर्णं शकुनि चापि सौबलम्। बद्ध्वा दुःशासनं चापि पाण्डवेभ्यः प्रयच्छथ॥
en: In the same way, binding Duryodhana, Karna and Shakuni as also Dushasana make them over to the Pandavas.

sn: त्यजेत् कुलार्थं पुरुष ग्रामस्या) कुलं त्यजेत्। ग्रामं जनपदस्यार्थं आत्मार्थं पृथिवीं त्यजेत्॥
en: One man should be sacrificed for the benefit of a race; a race should be sacrificed for he good a town; a town should be sacrificed for the good of the community, and for the sake of the soul should even the earth be sacrificed.

sn: राजन् दुर्योधनं बद्ध्वा ततः संशाम्य पाण्डवैः। त्वत्कृते न विनश्येयुः क्षत्रियाः क्षत्रियर्षभ।॥
en: O king, having bound Duryodhana make peace with the sons of Pandu. By so doing will the Kshatriyas not be exterminated, O foremost among the Kshatriyas.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच कृष्णस्य तु वचः श्रुत्वा धृतराष्ट्रो जनेश्वरः। विदुरं सर्वधर्मज्ञं त्वरमाणोऽभ्यभाषत॥
en: Vaishampayana said Hearing these words of Krishna Dhritarashtra, the lord of men, said in haste to Vidura conversant with all virtues.

sn: गच्छ तात महाप्राज्ञां गान्धारी दीर्घदर्शिनीम्। आनयेह तया सार्धमनुनेष्यामि दुर्मतिम्॥
en: “Go my dear friend, to the exceedingly wise Gandhari endued with great foresight; get her hare; joining with her shall I persuade that one of evil intellect.

sn: यदि सापि दुरात्मानं शमयेद् दुष्टचेतसम्। अपि कृष्णस्य सुहृदस्तिष्ठेम वचने वयम्॥
en: If she can lead that wicked-souled one of vicious heart, to peace then shall we be able to act up to the words of Krishna, our wellwisher.

sn: अपि लोभाभिभूतस्य पन्थानमनुदर्शयेत्। दुर्बुद्धेर्दुःसहायस्य शमार्थं ब्रुवती वचः॥
en: She might show the right path to him overpowered by avarice, by speaking in favour of that one of wicked intellect and having vicious men for his help, for making peace.

sn: अपि नो व्यसनं घोरं दुर्योधनकृतं महत्। शमयेच्चिररात्राय योगक्षेमवदव्ययम्॥
en: If she can thwart this dire and frightful calamity brought about by Duryodhana then shall we attain happiness and remain happy for ever.

sn: राज्ञस्तु वचनं श्रुत्वा विदरो दीर्घदर्शिनीम्। आनयामास गान्धारी धृतराष्ट्रस्य शासनात्॥
en: Hearing the words of the king Vidura brought, by command of Dhritarashtra, Gandhari endued with great foresight.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच एष गान्धारि पुत्रस्ते दुरात्मा शासनातिगः। ऐश्वर्यलोभादैश्वर्यं जीवितं च प्रहास्यति॥
en: Dhritarashtra said O Gandhari, this is your wicked-souled son who never obeys my commands owing to his avarice for prosperity; he will lose prosperity as also his life,

sn: अशिष्टवदमर्यादः पापैः सह दुरात्मवान्। सभाया निर्गतो मूढो व्यतिक्रम्य सुहृद्वचः॥
en: That wicked-souled like, unmannerly man and without showing any respect for others, accompanied by those one an vicious companions, went out of the council hall and the fool did not pay any attention to the advice of his well-wishers.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच सा भर्तृवचनं श्रुत्वा राजपुत्री यशस्विनी। अन्विच्छन्ती महच्छ्रेयो गान्धारी वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said That princess, of great renown Gandhari having heard the words of her husband, said these words desiring the greatest good of her son.

sn: गान्धार्युवाच आनायय सुतं क्षिप्रं राज्यकामुकमातुरम्। न हि राज्यमशिष्टेन शक्यं धर्मार्थलोपिना॥
en: Gandhari said Quickly summon your son, who is afflicted with a passion for kingdom; a kingdom cannot be maintained by an unrighteous person who seeks neither virtue nor worldly good.

sn: आप्नुमाप्तं तथापीदमविनीतेन सर्वथा। त्वं ह्योवात्र भृशं ग. धृतराष्ट्र सुतप्रियः॥
en: But notwithstanding all this, Duryodhana, having to humility in him, has obtained what is unobtainable by all means and you, O Dhritarashtra, are very much blamable for this, for you are fond of your son.

sn: यो जानन् पापतामस्य तत्प्रज्ञामनुवर्तसे। स एष काममन्युभ्यां प्रलब्धो लोभमास्थितः॥
en: You, who know that he is of a sinful nature, follow his wisdom, and he too supported by you is fully under the influence of desire and wrath and a slave of lust.

sn: अशक्योऽद्य त्वया राजन् विनिवर्तयितुं बलात्। राष्ट्रप्रदाने मूढस्य बालिशस्य दुरात्मनः॥
en: He is now incapable of being swerved from his purpose by force, O king; entrusting the kingdom to that ignorant fool of wicked soul,

sn: दुःसहायस्य लुब्धस्य धृतराष्ट्रोऽश्नुते फलम्। कथं हि स्वजने भेदमुपेक्षेत महीपतिः। भिन्नं हि स्वजनेन त्वां प्रहसिष्यन्ति शत्रवः॥
en: And having wicked ministers and moved by avarice, you are reaping the fruits O Dhritarashtra; why do you, O lord of the earth, look on this dispute with your own kinsmen with indifference? Your enemies will rejoice at this dispute with your own kinsmen.

sn: या हि शक्या महाराज साना भेदेन वा पुनः। निस्तर्तुमापदः स्वेषु दण्डं कस्तत्र पातयेत्॥
en: A difficulty which can be averted, O great king, by means of conciliation in gift, who would care to use violence in?

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच शासनाद् धृतराष्ट्रस्य दुर्योधनममर्षणम्। मातुश्च वचनात् क्षत्ता सभां प्रावेशयत् पुनः॥
en: Vaishampayana said By command of Dhritarashtra as also at the request of the mother the Kshattri again had the wrathful Duryodhana brought there.

sn: स मातुर्वचनाकाङ्क्षी विवेश पुनः सभाम्। अभिताप्रेक्षणः क्रोधान्निःश्वसन्निव पन्नगः॥
en: He, being desirous of hearing what his mother had to say, again entered the council chambers with his eyes red as copper in rage, and breathing ((heavily) like a serpent.

sn: तं प्रविष्टमभिप्रेक्ष्य पुत्रमुत्पथमास्थितम्। विगर्हमाणा गान्धारी शमार्थं वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
en: Seeing her son who was following the wrong course enter, Gandhari with a view to peace, spoke these words finding fault with him.

sn: दुर्योधन निबोधेदं वचनं मम पुत्रक। हितं ते सानुबन्धस्य तथाऽऽयत्यां सुखोदयम्॥
en: O Duryodhana, my dear son, listen to those words of mine which will conduce to the benefit to yourself along with your followers, which will bring on happiness and which is easy for you to listen.

sn: दुर्योधन यदाह त्वां पिता भरतसत्तमा भीष्मो द्रोणः कृपः क्षत्ता सुहृदां कुरु तद् वचः॥
en: Duryodhana, what your father, that best among the Bharatas, as also Bhishma, Drona, Kripa and the Kshatta have told your is the advice of your well wishers; follow that.

sn: विजितात्मा तु भीष्मस्य तु पितुश्चैव मम चापचितिः कृता। भवेद् द्रोणमुखानां च सुहृदां शाम्यता त्वया॥
en: It is my fond and earnest wish as also that of your well wishers Bhishma, your father and others, the chief of whom is Drona, that you should make peace.

sn: न हि राज्यं महाप्राज्ञ स्वेन कामेन शक्यते। अवाप्तुं रक्षितुं वापि भोक्तुं भरतसत्तम॥
en: O you of great wisdom, a kingdom cannot be maintained by following the bent of your desires alone, nor can it be earned, protected or enjoyed (by that means), o best of the Bharatas,

sn: न ह्यवश्येन्द्रियो राज्यमश्नीयाद् दीर्घमन्तरम्। मेधावी स राज्यमभिपालयेत्॥
en: No can one, who has not controlled his senses, enjoy a kingdom for a long while; one, who has controlled his senses and has intelligence, can alone protect a kingdom.

sn: कामक्रोधौ हि पुरुषमर्थेभ्यो व्यपकर्षतः। तौ तु शत्रु विनिर्जित्य राजा विजयते महीम्॥
en: Desire and wrath snatch away a man from earthy good; after subjugating these two enemies does a king conquer the earth.

sn: लोकेश्वर प्रभुत्वं हि महदेतद् दुरात्मभिः। राज्यं नामेप्सितं स्थानं न शक्यमभिरक्षितुम्॥
en: The sovereignty enjoyed by a ruler of men is a great thing; a kingdom can easily be wished for by those that are of wicked souls but it cannot be suitably protected by them.

sn: इन्द्रियाणि महत्प्रेप्सुर्नियच्छेदर्थधर्मयोः। इन्द्रियैर्नियतैर्बुद्धिर्वर्धतेऽन्निरिवेन्धनैः॥
en: One, who aspires to great things, must lead his senses to virtue and profit; by having the senses under control, intelligence increases as fire when it has fuel added on to it.

sn: अविधेयानि हीमानि व्यापादयितुमप्यलम्। अविधेया इवादान्ता हयाः पथि कुसारथिम्॥
en: These, when not kept under proper control, are sufficiently powerful to kill a man like untrained horses not properly managed which can kill an incompetent driver on the road.

sn: अविजित्य य आत्मानममात्यान् विजिगीषते। अमित्रान् वाजितामात्यः सोऽवशः परिहीयते॥
en: He, who without conquering self, wants to conquer his ministers wants to conquer his enemies, is soon brought under subjection by others.

sn: आत्मानमेव प्रथमं द्वेष्यरूपेण योजयेत्। ततोऽमात्यानमित्रांश्च न मोघं विजिगीषते॥
en: He was conquers his own self first, thinking that to be an enemy, and then desires to conquer his ministers and his enemies has his desires fulfilled.

sn: वश्येन्द्रियं जितामात्यं धृतदण्ड विकारिषु। परीक्ष्यकारिणं धीरमत्यर्थं श्रीनिषेवते॥
en: To one who has his senses under control, to one who has gained mastery over his enemies, to one who holds the rod (of punishment) on offenders and to one who does a thing after mature consideration, does prosperity offer great adoration.

sn: क्षुद्राक्षेणेव जालेन झपावपिहितावुभौ। कामक्रोधौ शरीरस्थौ प्रज्ञानं तौ विलुम्पतः॥
en: Like two small fishes, caught in a net with small holes, are desire and wrath which exist in a body, deprived of their existence by wisdom.

sn: याभ्यां हि देवाः स्वर्यातुः स्वर्गस्य पिदधुर्मुखम्। बिभ्यतोऽनुपरागस्य कामक्रोधो स्म वर्धितौ॥
en: Desire and wrath when increased are the things owing to which the gods shut up the doors to heaven to a man who has gained mastery over wordy propensities and otherwise is qualified to enter heaven.

sn: काम क्रोधं च लोभं च दम्भं दर्थं च भूमिपः। सम्यग्विजेतुं यो वेद स महीमभिजायते॥
en: The protector of the earth, who knows how to gain complete ascendancy over desire, wrath, avarice, pride and vanity, subjugates the entire world.

sn: सततं निग्रहे युक्त इन्द्रियाणां भवेन्नृपः। ईष्सन्नर्थं च धर्मं च द्विषतां च पराभवम्॥
en: The rulers of men, desirous of obtaining worldly good, virtue and the defeat of his enemies, should constantly employ them-selves in controlling their senses.

sn: कामाभिभूतः क्रोधाद् वा यो मिथ्या प्रतिपद्यते। स्वेषु चान्येषु वा तस्य न सहाया भवन्त्युत॥
en: He who behaves falsely, being subject to desire or to wrath, towards himself or to others, has got no body to help him.

sn: एकीभूतैर्महाप्राज्ञैः शूरैररिनिवर्हणैः। पाण्डवैः पृथिवीं तात भोक्ष्यसे सहितः सुखी॥
en: Having joined those ones endued with great wisdom, those heroes who are chastisers of their enemies, their enemies, those Pandavas, you will enjoy along with them this earth in happiness, my dear son.

sn: यथा भीष्मः शान्तनवो द्रोणश्चापि महारथः। आहतुस्तात तत् सत्यमजेयौ कृष्णपाण्डवौ॥
en: What Bhishma, the son of Shantanu and the great car-warrior Drona have told you, namely that Krishna and Arjuna are invincible is true indeed.

sn: प्रपद्यस्व महाबाहुं कृष्णमक्लिष्टकारिणम्। प्रसन्नो हि सुखाय स्यादुभयोरेव केशवः॥
en: Seek the refuge of that one of long arms Krishna, who does everything without exertions; if Keshava gratified it will conduce to the happiness of both the sides.

sn: सुहृदामर्थकामानां यो न तिष्ठति शासने। प्राज्ञानां कृतविद्यानां स नरः शत्रुनन्दनः॥
en: That man, who does not follow the instructions of well-wishers who desire his good and who are wise and learned, is the delight of his enemies.

sn: न युद्धे तात कल्याणं न धर्मार्थों कुतः सुखम्। न चापि विजयो नित्यं मा युद्धे चेत आधिथा।॥
en: My dear son, from a fight there will result no good; and how can there be virtue or worldly benefit? and how can there be happiness. Even victory is not stable; do not therefore set your mind on war.

sn: भीष्मेण हि महाप्राज्ञं पित्रा ते बाह्निकेन च। दत्तोंऽशः पाण्डुपुत्राणां भेदाद् भीतैररिंदम॥
en: O you of great wisdom, by Bhishma, by your father and by Balhika were the sons of Pandu given their share of the kingdom out fear for a dispute, O chastiser of foes.

sn: तस्य चैतत्प्रदानस्य फलमद्यानुपश्यसि। यद् भुड्क्षे पृथिवीं कृत्स्ना शूरैर्निहतकण्टकाम्॥
en: The fruits of this bestowal you now seeyou enjoy this entire earth, subjected by those heroes, with all your thorns and barriers removed.

sn: प्रयच्छ पाण्डुपुत्राणां यथोचितमरिंदम। यदीच्छसि सहामात्यो भोक्तुमधु प्रदीयताम्॥
en: Give to the sons of Pandu their due share, O chastiser of foes, if you desire to enjoy earth with your ministers; make over to them one half of kingdom.

sn: अलमर्धं पृथिव्यास्ते सहामात्यस्य जीवितुम्। सुहृदां वचने तिष्ठन् यशः प्राप्स्यसि भारत॥
en: One half of this earth is sufficient for the livelihood of yourself and your ministers; by following the advice of your well-wishers you will earn renown, O Bharata.

sn: श्रीमद्भिरात्मवद्भिस्तैर्बुद्धिमद्भिर्जितेन्द्रियैः। पाण्डवैर्विग्रहस्तात भ्रंशयेन्महतः सुखात्॥
en: By a struggle with the sons of Pandu who are endued are with prosperity, who have intelligence and who have mastered their senses, you will be deprived of great happiness, my dear son.

sn: निगृह्य सुहृदां मन्युं शाधि राज्यं यथोचितम्। स्वमंशं पाण्डुपुत्रेभ्यः प्रदाय भरतर्षभ॥
en: Removing the wrath of your well-wishers, rule over your kingdom duly after having given back to the sons of Pandu their own share, O best among the Bharatas.

sn: अलमङ्ग निकारोऽयं त्रयोदश समाः कृतः। शमयैनं महाप्राज्ञ कामक्रोधसमेधितम्॥
en: The troubles that they have suffered for the last thirteen years are enough; O you of great wisdom, control the feelings you entertain, which are fed by wrath and desire.

sn: न चैष शक्तः पार्थानां यस्त्वमर्थमभीप्ससि। सूतपुत्रो दृढक्रोधो भ्राता दुःशासनश्च ते॥
en: You desire to possess yourself of the wealth of the sons of Pritha but you are not competent to do it, nor is the son of the Suta, nor your brother Dushasana of firm wrath,

sn: भीष्मे द्रोणे कृपे कर्णे भीमसेने धनंजये। धृष्टद्युम्ने च संक्रुद्धे न स्युः सर्वाः प्रजा ध्रुवम्॥
en: Bhishma, Drona, Kripa Karna, Bhimasena, Dhananjaya and Dhrishtadyumna being fired with wrath, all creatures will surely cease to exist.

sn: अमर्षवशमापन्नो मा कुरूंस्तात जीघनः। एषा हि पृथिवी कृत्स्ना मा गमत् त्वत्कृते वधम्॥
en: Being subject to the influence of wrath, do not, my dear son, slay the Kurus; let not this entire earth be massacred on account of your doings.

sn: यच्च त्वं मन्यसे मूढ भीष्मद्रोणकृपादयः। योत्स्यन्ते सर्वशक्त्येति नैतदद्योपपद्यते॥
en: The, thought, that you entertain, o king that Bhishma, Drona, Kripa and others will fight for you, with all their might, will not be realized now.

sn: समं हि राज्यं प्रीतिश्च स्थानं हि विदितात्मनाम्। पाण्डवेष्वथ युष्मासु धर्मस्त्वभ्यधिकस्ततः॥
en: These, who know their own selves, have equal affection for the the Pandavas and yourselves, while virtue is more on their sides; besides whichever side wins, the kingdom will be the same to them.

sn: राजपिण्डभयादेते यदि हास्यन्ति जीवितम्। न हि शक्ष्यन्ति राजानं युधिष्ठिरमुदीक्षितुम्॥
en: If foe the fear of losing the maintenance they get from the king, they can think lightly of their very lives, they will yet not be able to see the king Yudhishthira with (angry) eyes.

sn: न लोभादर्थसम्पत्तिनराणामिह दृस्यते। तदलं तात लोभेन प्रशाम्य भरतर्षभ।॥
en: By avarice men are seen to earn prosperity in this world; therefore do you my dear son, quench this avarice of yours, O best among the Bharatas.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तत् तु वाक्यमनादृत्य सोऽर्थवन्मातृभाषितम्। पुनः प्रतस्थे संरम्भात् सकाशमकृतात्मनाम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Treating with contempt those words spoken by his mother which were pregnant with good sense, the one, of unsubdued soul, again went to his own place fired with wrath.

sn: ततः सभाया निर्गम्य सन्त्रयामास कौरवः। सौबलेन मताक्षेण राज्ञा शकुनिना सह॥
en: Then having issued out of the assemblyhall did that son of Kuru consult with the son of Subala, king Shakuni experienced in the game of dice.

sn: दुर्योधनस्य कर्णस्य शकुनेः सौबलस्य च। दुःशासनचतुर्थानामिदमासीद् विचेष्टितम्॥
en: Such was the resolution of four, namely Duryodhana, Karna, Shakuni, the son of Subala and Dushasana.

sn: पुरायमस्मान् गृह्णाति क्षिप्रकारी जनार्दनः। सहितो धृतराष्ट्रेण राज्ञा शान्तनवेन च॥
en: "Janardana, who does everything speedily, wants to capture us first in consultation with Dhritarashtra and the royal son of Shantanu.

sn: वयमेव हृषीकेशं निगृह्णीन बलादिव। प्रसह्य पुरुषव्याघ्रमिन्द्रो वैरोचनि यथा॥
en: But we shall capture that best among men, Hrishikesha, by force like Indra seizing the son of Virochana (Vali).

sn: श्रुत्वा गृहीतं वार्ष्णेयं पाण्डवा हतचेतसः। निरुत्साहा भविष्यन्ति भग्नदंष्ट्रा इवोरगाः॥
en: Hearing that the scion of the Vrishni race has been captured, the sons of Pandu will lose heart and will became deprived of their energy like serpents whose fangs have been broken.

sn: अयं ह्येषां महाबाहुः सर्वेषां शर्म वर्म च। अस्मिन् गृहीते वरदे ऋषभे सर्वसात्वताम्॥
en: This one of long arms is the refuge and protection of all; and this best among the Satvatas, this giver of boons being captured,

sn: निरुद्यमा भविष्यन्ति पाण्डवाः सोमकैः सह। तस्माद् वयमिहैवैनं केशवं क्षिप्रकारिणम्॥
en: All the son of Pandu, along with the Somakas will be deprived of their energy; therefore now and here should we capture this Keshava of quick action,

sn: क्रोशतो धृतराष्ट्रस्य बद्ध्वा योत्स्यामहे रिपून्। तेषां पापमभिप्रायं पापानां दुष्टचेतसाम्॥
en: In the face of the ravings of Dhritarashtra, and then fight the enemies>” This wicked intention of those wicked-souled wretches,

sn: इङ्गितज्ञः कविः क्षिप्रमन्वबुद्ध्यत सात्यकिः। तदर्थमभिनिष्क्रम्य हार्दिक्येन सहास्थितः॥
en: The wise Satyaki, who could understand the sings, quickly came to Know of; and in consequence of that knowledge he came out with the son of Hridika (Kritavarman).

sn: अब्रवीत् कृतवर्माणं क्षिप्रं योजय वाहिनीम्। व्यूढानीकः सभाद्वारमुपतिष्ठस्व दंशितः॥
en: And he said to Kritavarman "Quickly prepare the army for action and with the division there of ready for action and clad in amours, wait at the gate of the council chamber.

sn: यावदाख्याम्यहं चैतत् कृष्णायाक्लिष्टकारिणे। स प्रविश्य सभां वीरः सिंहो गिरिगुहामिव॥
en: In the meantime, I shall communicate all this to Krishna who performs action without exertion. Then that hero, having entered the council like a lion entering the caverns of a mountain,

sn: आचष्ट तमभिप्रायं केशवाय महात्मने। धृतराष्ट्रं ततश्चैव विदुरं चान्वभाषत॥
en: Communicated that intention (of those Kurus) to the great should Keshava and then to Dhritarashtra and then to Vidura also.

sn: तेषामेतमभिप्रायमाचचक्षे स्मयन्निव। धर्मादर्थाच्च कामाच्च कर्म साधुविगर्हितम्॥
en: They heard this proposal of theirs with laughter and ridicule for this (proposed) deed was against virtue, worldly benefit and desire as also against the principles of an honest man.

sn: मन्दाः कर्तुमिहेच्छन्ति न चावाप्य कथंचन। पुरा विकुर्वते मूढाः पापात्मानः समागताः॥
en: (Satyaki continued). “In this instance the fools seek to do an act which is by no means capable of being performed; these fools of wicked souls are united to gather to pick a quarrel.

sn: धर्षिताः काममन्युभ्यां क्रोधलोभवशानुगाः। इमं हि पुण्डरीकाक्षं जिघृक्षन्त्यल्पचेतसः॥
en: Being overpowered by desire and wrath and being subjected to the influence of anger and avarice, these men, of mean heart, seek to slay the one with lotus eyes,

sn: पटेनाग्नि प्रज्वलितं यथा बाला यथा जडाः। सात्यकेस्तद् वचः श्रुत्वा विदुरोदीर्घदर्शिवान्॥
en: As children and idiots attempt to seize blazing fire by means of their cloths.” Hearing those words of Satyaki Vidura, endued with great foresight,

sn: धृतराष्ट्र महाबाहुमब्रवीत् कुरुसंसदि। राजन् परीतकालास्ते पुत्राः सर्वे परंतप॥
en: Said to Dhritarashtra of long arms in that assembly of the Kurus "O king, the time of all of your sons is come, O chastiser of foes.

sn: अशक्यमयशस्यं च कर्तुं कर्म समुद्यताः। इमं हि पुण्डरीकाक्षमभिभूय प्रसह्य च॥
en: They are prepared to do an act which is incapable of being done and which, if done would be discreditable; having overpowered and vanquished this one with lotus eyes,

sn: निग्रहीतुं किलेच्छन्ति सहिता वासवानुजम्। इमं पुरुषशार्दूलमप्रधृष्यं दुरासदम्॥
en: They desire to capture along with the younger brother of Vasava-this best among men, who is incapable of being vanquished, and in fact hard to stand against.

sn: आसाद्य न भविष्यन्ति पतङ्गा इव पावकम्। अयमिच्छन् हि तान् सर्वान् युध्यमानाञ्जनार्दनः॥
en: Having stood against they will cease to exist as worms in contact with fire. This Janardana, desiring the good of all when lighting, never

sn: सिंहो नागानिव क्रुद्धो गमयेद् यमसादनम्। न त्वयं निन्दितं कर्म कुर्यात् पापं कथंचन॥
en: And rendered angry, will send them to the abode of Yama like a lion routing a heard of elephants; but this mighty blamable act of wickedness will never be perpetrated.

sn: न च धर्मादपक्रामेदच्युतः पुरुषोत्तमः। विदुरेणैवमुक्ते तु केशवो वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
en: Achyuta, the best among men swerves from the Path of rectitude." Vidura having said this, Keshava said these words,

sn: धृतराष्ट्रमभिप्रेक्ष्य सुहृदां शृण्वतां मिथः। राजनेते यदि क्रुद्धा मां निगृह्णीयुरोजसा॥
en: Looking on Dhritarashtra and in the hearing of his well-wishers "O king, if being angry they can by their might capture me,

sn: एते वा मामहं वैनाननुजानीहि पार्थिव। एतान् हि सर्वान् संरब्धान् नियन्तुमहमुत्सहे॥
en: Let them do it, for I know, O ruler of the earth, the might of these and I can venture to cure all of them of their anger.

sn: न त्वहं निन्दितं कर्म कुर्यां पापं कथंचन। पाण्डवार्थं हि लुभ्यन्तः स्वार्थान् हास्यन्ति ते सुताः।।२६
en: But I shall never do an act which is blamable and wicked; these sons of yours will lose their own wealth by coveting the wealth of the Pandavas.

sn: एते चेदेवमिच्छन्ति कृतकार्यो युधिष्ठिरः। अद्यैव ह्यहमेनांश्च ये चैनाननु भारत॥
en: Since they desire to act so wickedly Yudhishthira has all the greater chances of success; for I can at this very moment, capture these and those that follow them,

sn: निगृह्य राजन् पार्थेभ्यो दद्यां किं दुष्कृतं भवेत्। इदं तु न प्रवर्तेयं निन्दितं कर्म भारत॥
en: 0 king, and make ever to the son of Pritha which will not be a hard thing to do; but I am not inched to do such a blamable deed, o Bharata.

sn: संनिधौ ते महाराज क्रोधजं पापबुद्धिजम्। एष दुर्योधनो राजन् यथेच्छति तथाऽस्तु तत्॥
en: What this Duryodhana, O king, wishes to do in your presence, in consequence of wrath and sinful heart, O great king, let him do.

sn: अहं तु सर्वांस्तनयाननुजानामि ते नृप। एतच्छ्रुत्वा तु विदुरं धृतराष्ट्रोऽभ्यभाषत। क्षिप्रमानय तं पापं राज्यलुब्धं सुयोधनम्॥
en: I too allow all your sons, O ruler of men." Hearing this Dhritarashtra said to Vidura “Bring that wicked Suyodhana covetous of the kingdom soon,

sn: सहमित्रं सहामात्यं ससोदर्यं सहानुगम्। शक्नुयां यदि पन्थानमवतारयितुं पुनः॥
en: Along with his friends, with his ministers, with his brothers and with his followers. I shall see again if can get him along the right path."

sn: ततो दुर्योधनं क्षत्ता पुन: प्रावेशयत् सभाम्। अकामं भ्रातृभिः सार्धं राजभिः परिवारितम्॥
en: Then did Kshattri again cause Duryodhana to enter the council chamber, unwilling as he was along with his brothers, and surrounded by the kings.

sn: अथ दुर्योधनं राजा धृतराष्ट्रोऽभ्यभाषत। कर्णदुःशासनाभ्यां च राजभिश्चापि संवृतम्॥
en: Then did the Dhritarashtra to Duryodhana and Karna and Dushasana and the kings who surrounded them.

sn: नृशंस पापभूयिष्ठ क्षुद्रकर्मसहायवान्। पापैः सहायैः संहत्य पापं कर्म चिकीर्षसि॥
en: "O you of inhuman, of exceeding sinfulness, having for your supporters only men of small deeds, united with wicked men, you want to perpetrate a wicked deed.

sn: अशक्यमयशस्यं च सद्धिश्चापि विगर्हितम्। यथा त्वादृशको मूढो व्यवस्येत् कुलपांसनः॥
en: This intended act of yours is incapable of being performed, tending to infamy and disapproved by the honest in fact this is a thing which a fool and the cause of infamy to the race like you would attempt.

sn: त्वमिमं पुण्डरीकाक्षमप्रधृष्यं दुरासदम्। पापैः सहायैः संहत्य निग्रहीतुं किलेच्छसि॥
en: This one with lotus eyes, who can not be vanquished, in fact who is hard to stand save against, you want to capture, being united with your wicked supporters.

sn: यो न शक्यो बलात् कर्तुं देवैरपि सवासवैः। तं त्वं प्रार्थयसे मन्द बालश्चन्द्रमसं यथा।॥
en: Him who cannot be forcibly seized even by the gods under the leadership of Vasava, you want to capture to like a child desiring to grasp the moon.

sn: तेवैर्मनुष्यैर्गन्धर्वैरसुरैरुरगैश्च यः। न सोढुं समरे शक्यस्तं न बुद्ध्यसि केशवम्॥
en: You do not know that Keshava is incapable of being fought with in battle by the gods, the human beings, the Gandharvas, the Asuras and the Nagas.

sn: दुर्गाह्यः पाणिना वायुर्दुस्पर्शः पाणिनाशशी। दुर्धरा पृथिवी मूर्धा दुर्ग्राह्यः केशवोबलात्॥
en: Keshava is hard to capture by force even as air is incapable of being captured by living beings, as moon is incapable of being grasped by living beings and as the earth held on the head."

sn: इत्युक्ते धृतराष्ट्रेण क्षत्तापि विदुरोऽब्रवीत्। दुर्योधनमभिप्रेत्य धार्तराष्ट्रपमर्षणम्॥
en: This being said Dhritarashtra the Kshatta Vidura too said, with his eyes on the wrathful son of Dhritarashtra, Duryodhana.

sn: विदुर उवाच दुर्योधन निबोधेदं वचनं मम साम्प्रतम्। सौभद्वारे वानरेन्द्रो द्विविदो नाम नामतः। शिलावर्षेण महता छादयामास केशवम्॥
en: Vidura said “O Duryodhana, listen now to these words of mine At the gates of Saubha did the chief of monkeys, Dvivida by name, covered Keshava with a heavy down pour of stones.

sn: ग्रहीतुकामो विक्रम्य सर्वयत्नेन माधवम्। ग्रहीतुं नाशकच्चैनं तं त्वं प्रार्थयसे बलात्॥
en: Being desirous of capturing Madhava by force, he made every effort to do it to capture him by force.

sn: प्राग्ज्योतिषगतं शौरि नरकः सह दानवैः। ग्रहीतुं नाशकत् तत्र तं त्वं प्रार्थयसे बलात्॥
en: Naraka, along with all the Danavas, could not capture Shouri who had gone to Pragjyotisha and you want to capture him by force.

sn: अनेकयुगवर्षायुर्निहत्य नरकं मृधे। नीत्वा कन्यासहस्राणि उपयेमे यथाविधि॥
en: Slaying in battle Naraka who had lived for many thousands of years he brought away his thousand daughters and married them with the usual rites.

sn: निर्मोचने षट् सहस्रा: पाशैर्बद्धा महासुराः। चहीतुं नाशकंश्चैनं तं त्वं प्रार्थयसे बलात्॥
en: In the city if Nirmochana sixty thousand great Asuras could not capture him with their nooses and you want to capture him by force.

sn: अनेन हि हता बाल्ये पूतना शकुनी तथा। गोवर्धनो धारितश्च गवार्थं भरतर्षभ।४६॥
en: When he was but a child, Putana and Shakuni were slain by him and the Govardhana mountain was held up by him for the protection of the cows, O best among the Bharatas.

sn: अरिष्टो धेनुकश्चैव चाणूरश्च महाबलः। अश्वराजश्च निहतः कंसश्चारिष्टमाचरन्॥
en: Arishta and Dhenuka as also Chanura of Great; strength and Ashvaraja were slain by him.

sn: जरासंधश्च वक्त्रश्च शिशुपालश्च वीर्यवान्। बाणश्च निहतः संख्ये राजानश्च निषूदिताः॥
en: Jarasandha, and Vakra and Shishupala of great heroism and Vana were slain by him in battle as also several other kings.

sn: वरुणो निर्जितो राजा पावकश्वामितौजसा। पारिजातं च हरता जितः साक्षाच्छचीपतिः॥
en: The Varuna too was defeated as also fire of immeasurable energy and even the lord of Sachi himself was overpowered when robbing the Parijat flower.

sn: एकार्णवे च स्वफता निहतौ मधुकैटभौ। जन्मान्तरमुपागम्य हयग्रीवस्तथा हतः॥
en: White lying asleep on the all spreading ocean by were Madhu and Kaitabha slain and in another birth was Hayagriva slain.

sn: अयं कर्ता न क्रियते कारणं चापि पौरुषे। यद् यदिच्छेदयं शौरिस्तत् तत् कुर्यादयत्नतः॥
en: He is the doer of everything but himself is not created and he is the cause of all power. This Shouri can perform without any effort whatever he wishes

sn: तं न बुद्ध्यसि गोविन्दं घोरविक्रममच्युतम्। आशीविषमिव क्रुद्धं तेजोराशिमनिन्दितम्॥
en: You do not know and fully understand this Achyuta, this Govinda of Fierce prowess; he is endued with unblamable energy like an angry serpent.

sn: प्रधर्षयन् महाबाहुं कृष्णमक्लिष्टकारिणम्। पतङ्गोऽग्निमिवासाद्य सामात्यो न भविष्यसि॥
en: In your a tempt to vanquish Krishna of long arms and of unwearied actions you will with your ministers be reduced to the condition of worms perishing by meeting with fire. A...nrn

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच विदुरेणैवमुक्तस्तु केशवः शत्रुपूगहा। दुर्योधनं धार्तराष्ट्रमभ्यभाषत वीर्यवान्॥
en: Vaishampayana said This being said Vidura, Keshava the killer of his crowds of enemies, endued with prowess, said to Duryodhana, the son of Dhritarashtra.

sn: एकोऽहमिति यन्मोहान्मन्यसे मां सुयोधन। परिभूय सुदुर्बुद्धे ग्रहीतुं मां चिकीर्षसि॥
en: "O Suyodhana, since you think me to be alone out of your folly, you want to effect my capture by overpowering me, O you of very little intellect.

sn: इहैव पाण्डवाः सर्वे तथैवान्धकवृष्णयः। इहादित्याश्च रुद्राश्च वसवश्च महर्षिभिः॥
en: Here are all the Pandavas as also all the Andhakas and the Vrishnis; here are the Adityas, the Rudras and the Vasus along with the great Rishis."

sn: एवमुक्त्वा जहासोच्चैः केसवः परवीरहा। अस्य संस्मयतः शौरेविद्युदूपा महात्मनः॥
en: Saying this Keshava, the slayer of the heroes of his enemies, laughed aloud and at his laughter the body of the great-souled one became like lightning.

sn: अङ्गुष्ठमात्रास्त्रिदशा मुमुचुः पावकार्चिषः। तस्य ब्रह्मा ललाटस्थो रुद्रो वक्षसि चाभवत्॥
en: And from his body issued forth gods of the measures of the thumb but having the rays of fire and Brahma was found to be his brow and Rudra on his breast.

sn: लोकपाला भुजेष्वासन्नग्निरास्यादजायत। आदित्याश्चैव साध्याश्च वसवोऽथाश्विनावपि॥
en: The supporters of the universe were seated on his arms and from his mouth sprang up fire. The Adityas and the Sadhyas, the Vasus and the Ashvinas.

sn: मरुतश्च सहेन्द्रेण विश्वेदेवास्तथैव च। बभूवुश्चैकरूपाणि यक्षगन्धर्वरक्षसाम्॥
en: The Maruts along with Indra as also the gods of the universe of the same form, as also Yakshas, Gandharvas and Rakshasas.

sn: प्रादुरास्तां तथा दो• संकर्षणधनंजयौ। दक्षिणेऽथार्जुनो धन्वी हली रामश्च सव्यतः॥
en: Issued out thence. In the same way from his two eyes sprang up Sankarshana and Dhananjaya. In his right stood Arjuna the bowman and in his left stood Rama with the plough.

sn: भीमो युधिष्ठिरश्चैव माद्रीपुत्रौ च पृष्ठतः। अन्धका वृष्णयश्चैव प्रद्युम्नप्रमुखास्ततः॥
en: Behind him were Bhima and Yudhishthira as also the two sons of Madri and still behind them were the Andhakas and the Vrishnis headed by Pradyumna.

sn: अग्रे बभूवुः कृष्णस्य समुद्यतमहायुधाः। शङ्खचक्रगदाशक्तिशाईलागलनन्दकाः॥
en: In front of Krishna were the order chiefs with their great arms upraised. The conch, the dice, the dice the mace, the Shakti, the bow Sharnga, the plough, the Nandaka.

sn: अदृश्यन्तोद्यतान्येव सर्वप्रहरणानि च। नानाबाहुषु कृष्णस्य दीप्यमानानि सर्वशः॥
en: Were seen upraised and all other arms of offence blazing in all directions in the many hands of Krishna.

sn: नेत्राभ्यां नस्ततश्चैव श्रोत्राभ्यां चसमन्ततः। प्रादुरासन् महारौद्राः सधूमाः पावकार्चिषः॥
en: From his two eyes and from his two ears and his nose issued forth continually the great Rudra himself in the shape of sparks of fires accompanied with smoke.

sn: रोमकूपेषु च तथा सूर्यस्येव मरीचयः। तं दृष्ट्वा घोरमात्मानं केशवस्य महात्मनः॥
en: From the poor of his skin issued in the same way something like the rays of the sun; seeing that frightful appearance of the greatsouled Keshava.

sn: न्यमीलयन्त नेत्राणि राजानस्त्रस्तचेतसः। ऋते द्रोणं च भीष्मं च विदुरं च महामतिम्॥
en: The kings, with their hearts, struck with fear, shut their eyes with the exception of Drona, Bhishma and Vidura of great intelligence.

sn: संजयं च महाभागमृषींश्चैव तपोधनान्। प्रादात् तेषां स भगवान् दिव्यं चक्षुर्जनार्दनः॥
en: And Sanjaya of great power. And those Rishis whose only wealth consisted in devotion for the lord Janardana, gave them celestial sight.

sn: तद् दृष्ट्वा महदाश्चर्य माधवस्य सभातले। देवदुन्दुभयो नेदुः पुष्पवर्षं पपात च॥
en: Seeing that great wonderful appearance of Madhava in the inside of the Assembly-hall celestial drums were sounded and there was a downpour of flowers.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच त्वमेव पुण्डरीकाक्ष सर्वस्य जगतो हितः। तस्मात् त्वं यादवश्रेष्ठ प्रसादं कर्तुमर्हसि॥
en: Dhritarashtra said "You are the doer of good to the entire world, O you of lotus eyes, therefore it is proper that you should bless me, you foremost among the Yadavas.

sn: भगवन् मम नेत्राणामन्तर्धानं वृणे पुनः। भवन्तं द्रष्टुमिच्छामि नान्यं द्रष्टुमिहोत्सहे॥
en: O lord, I again pray for the restoration of my eyes, for I want to see you and I desire not to see anything else."

sn: ततोऽब्रवीन्महाबाहुधृतराष्ट्र जनार्दनः। अदृश्यमाने नेत्रे द्वे भवेतां कुरुनन्दन॥
en: Then did Janardana of long arms say to Dhritarashtra "O delighter of the Kurus, let your eyes, with which you can not see, have sight restored to them.

sn: तत्राद्भुतं महाराज धृतराष्ट्रश्च चक्षुषी। लब्धवान् वासुदेवाच्च विश्वरूपदिदृक्षया॥
en: And wonder it was, Ogreat king that Dhritarashtra got his eyes which he gained in consequence of his desire to behold the universal form of Vasudeva.

sn: लब्धचक्षुषमासीनं धृतराष्ट्र नराधिपाः। विस्मिता ऋषिभिः सार्धं तुष्टुवुर्मधुसूदनम्॥
en: The rulers of men, struck with wonder at the restoration eyesight to the sitting Dhritarashtra propitiated the slayer of Madhu.

sn: चचाल च मही कृत्स्ना सागरचापि चुक्षुभे। विस्मयं परमं जग्मुः पार्थिवा भरतर्षभ॥
en: And the whole earth moved together and the waters of the sea were agitated and the rulers of the earth were struck with great wonder, O best among the Bharatas.

sn: ततः स पुरुषव्याघ्रः संजहार वपुः स्वकम्। तां दिव्यामद्भुतां चित्रामृद्धिमत्तामरिंदमः॥
en: Then did that best among men, that chastiser of foes, cast off that form and wonderful, which was diverse looking and was endued with prosperity.

sn: ततः सात्यकिमादाय पाणौ हार्दिक्यमेव च। ऋषिभिस्तैरनुज्ञातो निर्ययौ मधुसूदनः॥
en: Then taking Satyaki by his hand and also the son of Hridika the slayer of Madhu went out, with the permission of those Rishis.

sn: ऋषयोऽन्तर्हिता जग्मुस्ततस्ते नारदादयः। तस्मिन् कोलाहले वृत्ते तदद्भुतमिवाभवत्॥
en: Then did those Rishis, Narada and others vanished from sight, lost in the confusion, which followed that.

sn: तं प्रस्थितमभिप्रेक्ष्य कौरवाः सह राजभिः। अनुजग्मुर्नरव्याघ्रं देवा इव शतक्रतुम्॥
en: Seeing him go out, the sons of Kuru along with the other kings, followed that best among men like the gods following the performer of a hundred sacrifices.

sn: अचिन्तयन्नमेयात्मा सर्वं तद् राजमण्डलम्। निश्चकाम ततः शौरिः सधूम इव पावकः॥
en: Shouri, of immeasurable soul, however without thinking of that entire assembly of kings (that followed him), went out like fire accompanied with smoke.

sn: ततो रथेन शुभ्रेण महता किङ्किणीकिना। हेमजालविचित्रेण लधुना मेघनादिना॥
en: With his white chariot and large, furnished with tinkling balls and ornamented with gold, with wheels clattering like the roaring of clouds,

sn: सूपस्करेण शुभ्रेण वैयाघेण वरूथिना। शैब्यसुग्रीवयुक्तेन प्रत्यदृश्यत दारुकः॥
en: Which was also covered with white tiger skins, and to which were yoked his excellent horses, among which was Shaivya he saw Daruka.

sn: तथैव रथमास्थाय कृतवर्मा महारथः। वृष्णीनां सम्मतो वीरो हार्दिक्यः समदृश्यत॥
en: He also the great car-warrior Kritavarman, the son of Hridika, the respected hero of the Vrishnis seated on the chariot.

sn: उपस्थितरथं शौरि प्रयास्यन्तमरिंदमम्। धृतराष्ट्रो महाराजः पुनरेवाभ्यभाषत॥
en: The great king Dhritarashtra again said to Shouri, that chastiser of foes, who was about to depart on the chariot which was ready before him.

sn: यावद् बलं मे पुत्रेषु पश्यतस्तेजनार्दन। प्रत्यक्षं ते न ते किंचितं परोक्षं शत्रुकर्शन॥
en: “The influence I wield over my sons you have seen, O Janardana; you have been a saw witness to that; nothing has happened behind your back, O chastiser of foes.

sn: कुरूणां शममिच्छन्तं यतमानं च केशव। विदित्वैतामवस्था मे नाभिशङ्कितुमर्हसि॥
en: Desirous of the peace of Kurus, I have lost my respect; 0 Keshava, knowing these circumstances it is not proper that you should suspect me.

sn: न मे पापोऽस्त्यभिप्रायः पाण्डवान् प्रति केशव। ज्ञातमेव हितं वाक्य यन्मयोक्तः सुयोधनः॥
en: I have no wicked intention against the sons of Pandu, O Keshava; for the words I said to Suyodhana are known to you.

sn: जानन्ति कुरवः सर्वे राजानश्चैव पार्थिवाः। शमे प्रयतमानं मां सर्वयत्नेन माधव॥
en: All the Kurus know, as also these kings, these rulers of the earth, that I have attempted to bring about peace with all earnestness, O Madhava.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततोऽब्रवीन्महाबाहुधृतराष्ट्र जनार्दनः। द्रोणं पितामह भीष्मं क्षत्तारं बाह्निकं कृपम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Then did Janardana of long arms say to Dhritarashtra and to Drona and to Duryodhana's grand-father Bhishma, and to the Kshattri, and to Balhika and to Kripa.

sn: प्रत्यक्षमेतद् भवतां यद् वृत्तं कुरुसंसदि। यथा चाशिष्टवन्मन्दो रोषादद्य समुत्थितः॥
en: "Your exalted selves are witnesses to what transpired in the assembly of the Kurus; how today that fool, like an uneducated and unmannerly fellow, got up from his seat.

sn: वदत्यनीशमात्मानं धृतराष्ट्रो महीपतिः। आपृच्छे भवतः सर्वान् गमिष्यामि युधिष्ठिरम्॥
en: And how the ruler of the of the earth Dhritarashtra says that he is powerless in the matter; with the permission of you all I shall now go to Yudhishthira.

sn: आमन्त्र्य प्रस्थितं शौरिं रथस्थं पुरुषर्षभ। अनुजग्मुर्महेष्वासाः प्रवीरा भरतर्षभाः॥
en: Those mighty bowmen, those heroes, those foremost among the Bharatas followed that best of men, Shouri who was departing in his chariot after taking leave of them.

sn: भीष्मो द्रोणः कृपः क्षत्ता धृतराष्ट्रोऽथ बाह्निकः। अश्वत्थामा विकर्णश्च युयुत्सुश्च महारथः॥
en: Those heroes were Bhishma, Drona, Kripa, Kshattri, Dhritarashtra, Balhika, Ashvathama, Vikarna and the great car-warrior Yuyutsu.

sn: ततो रथेन शुभ्रेण महता किङ्किणीकिना। कुरूणां पश्यतां दुष्टुं स्वसारं स पितुर्ययौ॥
en: Then in that white chariot and large, furnished with thinking bells he went to the sister of his father, the Kurus looking at him. Those mighty bowmen, those heroes, those foremost among the Bharatas followed that best of men, Shouri who was departing in his chariot after taking leave of them.

sn: भीष्मो द्रोणः कृपः क्षत्ता धृतराष्ट्रोऽथ बाह्निकः। अश्वत्थामा विकर्णश्च युयुत्सुश्च महारथः॥
en: Those heroes were Bhishma, Drona, Kripa, Kshattri, Dhritarashtra, Balhika, Ashvathama, Vikarna and the great car-warrior Yuyutsu.

sn: ततो रथेन शुभ्रेण महता किङ्किणीकिना। कुरूणां पश्यतां दुष्टुं स्वसारं स पितुर्ययौ॥
en: Then in that white chariot and large, furnished with thinking bells he went to the sister of his father, the Kurus looking at him.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच प्रविश्याथ गृहं तस्याश्चरणावभिवाद्य च। आचख्यौ तत् समासेन यद् वृत्तं कुरुसंसदि॥
en: Vaishampayana said Then having entered her abode and saluted her feet he described in brief to her what had happened in that assembly of the Kurus.

sn: वासुदेव उवाच उक्तं बहुविधं वाक्यं ग्रहणीयं सहेतुकम्। ऋषिभिश्चैव च मया न चासौ तद् गृहीतवान्।॥
en: Vasudeva said Many sorts of speech were made, all of them being acceptable and consistent with reason, by myself and the Rishis but he did not accept these.

sn: कालपक्वमिदं सर्वं सुयोधनवशानुगम्। आपृच्छे भवतीं शीघ्रं प्रयास्ये पाण्डवान् प्रति॥
en: All these, the followers of Suyodhana, have reached the end of their time and with vas.

sn: किं वाच्याः पाण्डवेयास्ते भवत्या वचनान्मया। तद् ब्रूहि त्वं महाप्राज्ञे शुश्रूषे वचनं तव॥
en: What should be said by me to those sons of Pandu, by your command, tell me, O you of great wisdom; I desire to hear your words.

sn: कुन्त्युवाच ब्रूयाः केशव राजानं धर्मात्मानं युधिष्ठिरम्। भूयास्ते हीयते धर्मो मा पुत्रक वृथा कृथाः॥
en: Kunti said O Keshava, tell that virtuous-souled king Yudhishthira; “Virtue is fast leaving your; do not act vainly, my dear son.

sn: श्रोत्रियस्येव ते राजन् मन्दकस्याविपश्चितः। अनुवाकहता बुद्धिर्धर्ममेवैकमीक्षते॥
en: Like an ignorant student of the Veda, 0 king, understanding the literal meaning but not catching the spirit you have been rendered ignorant of the laws of worldly good and like a fool you have been lost; the literal meaning of the Vedas being too much impressed on you, your intellect follows only virtue.

sn: अङ्गोवेक्षस्व धर्मं त्वं यथा सृष्टः स्वयम्भुवा। बाहुभ्यां क्षत्रियाः सृष्टा बाहुवीर्योपजीविनः॥
en: Consider your own duties for which you were created by him who is born of himself; the Kshatriya has been created from the arms and by the exercise of his arms must he live.

sn: क्रूराय कर्मणे नित्यं प्रजानां परिपालने। शृणु चात्रोपमामेकां या वृद्धेभ्यः श्रुता मया॥
en: For all hard deeds and for the protection of subjects he has been created; hear in this connection an example which has been heard hy me from old people.

sn: मुचुकुन्दस्य राजर्षेरददत् पृथिवीमिमाम्। पुरा वैश्रवणः प्रीतो न चासौ तद् गृहीतवान्॥
en: To Muchukunda, the royal Rishi Vaisravana, being gratified, gave this earth but he did accept it.

sn: बाहुवीर्यार्जितं राज्यमश्नीयामिति कामये। ततो वैश्रवणः प्रीतो विस्मितः समपद्यत॥
en: I desire to get a kingdom, which shall have been earned by the prowess of my arms; then was Vaisravana still more gratified and was struck with wonder.

sn: मुचुकुन्दस्ततो राजा सोऽन्वशासद् वसुन्धराम्। बाहुवीर्यार्जितां सम्यक् क्षत्रधर्ममनुव्रतः॥
en: Then after that did the king Muchukunda rule over this earth which he earned by the prowess of his arms following closely the duties of a Kshatriya.

sn: यं हि धर्म चरन्तीह प्रजा राज्ञा सुरक्षिताः। चतुर्थं तस्य धर्मस्य राजा विन्देत भारत॥
en: The one-fourth of the entire virtue earned by subjects well protected by the king in this world goes to the king, O Bharata.

sn: राजा चरति चेद् धर्मं देवत्वायैव कल्पते। स चेदधर्मं चरति नरकायैव गच्छति॥
en: And if the king practices virtue he resembles the god even and if he practices vice he goes to hell.

sn: दण्डनीतिः स्वधर्मेण चातुर्वर्ण्य नियच्छति। प्रयुक्ता स्वामिना सम्यगधर्मेभ्यश्च यच्छति॥
en: The penal code enforced by Lord in a proper way makes the four orders lead lives in their own proper spheres and makes the king himself earn virtue, desire and salvation.

sn: दण्डनीत्यां यदा राजा सम्यक् कात्स्न्र्येन वर्तते। तदा कृतयुगं नाम कालः श्रेष्ठः प्रवर्तते॥
en: If the king property follows the penal code in its entirety then the best of age called Krita Yuga regions.

sn: कालो वा कारणं राज्ञो राजा वा कालकारणम्। इति ते संशयो मा भूद् राजा कालस्य कारणम्॥
en: Oking, do not linger in doubt as to whether the age that nature of the king or whether it is the king that rules that is the cause of the prevalence of a particular period. The king is the cause of the age.

sn: राजा कृतयुगस्रष्टा त्रेताया द्वापरस्य च। युगस्य च चतुर्थस्य राजा भवति कारणम्॥
en: The king is the creator or maker of the Krita Yuga, as also of the Treta and Dvapara and the king becomes the cause as well of the fourth Yuga.

sn: कृतस्य करणाद् राजा स्वर्गमत्यन्तमश्नुते। त्रेतायाः करणाद् राजा स्वर्ग नात्यन्तमश्नुते॥
en: Owing to causing the Krita Yuga to prevail, a king enjoys exceedingly the fruits of heaven and owing to causing the Treta Yuga he enjoys moderately the fruits of heaven.

sn: प्रवर्तनाद् द्वापरस्य यथाभागमुपाश्नुते। कले प्रवर्तनाद् राजा पापमत्यन्तमजुते॥
en: Owing to causing the Dvapara Yuga to prevail he has also a due share of these fruits but owing to causing the Kali Yuga to prevail, the king attains excessive misery.

sn: ततो वसति दुष्कर्मा नरके शाश्वतीः समाः। राजदोषेण हि जगत् स्पृश्यते जगतः स च॥
en: Then that doer of wicked deeds resides, in hell for eternity; the earth is affected by the sins of the king while he too is affected by the earth's sins.

sn: राजधर्मानवेक्षस्व पितृपैतामहोचितान्। नैतद् राजर्षिवृत्तं हि यत्र त्वं स्थातुमिच्छसि॥
en: Duly following the examples of your father and grandfather, observe the duty or a king-this is not the life of a royal Rishi in which you desire to live.

sn: न कि वैक्लव्यसंसृष्ट आनृशंस्ये व्यवस्थितः। प्रजापालनसम्भूतं फलं किंचन लब्धवान्॥
en: He, that is affected by weakness of mind or heart and follows the Path of compassion, does not gain any portion of the fruits due to the protection of subjects.

sn: न ह्येतामाशिष पाणडुर्न चाहं न पितामहः। प्रयुक्तवन्तः पूर्वं ते यया चरसि मेधया।॥
en: Pandu, nor myself, nor your grandfather blessed you then formerly for that you should follow the course you are adopting.

sn: यज्ञो दानं तपः शौर्यं प्रज्ञा संतानमेव च। माहात्म्यं बलमोजश्च नित्यमाशंसितं मया॥
en: The performance of sacrificial rites, liberality, devotion, heroism, greatness, might and energy, were ever expected of you by me.

sn: नित्यं स्वाहा नित्यं दद्युर्मानुषदेवताः। दीर्घमायुर्धनं पुत्रान् सम्यगाराधिताः शुभाः॥
en: Svadha, and Svaha as also the blessings of a life, wealth, sons are ever given by gods and men, when duly gratified.

sn: पुत्रेष्वाशासते नित्यं पितरो दैवतानि च। दानमध्ययनं यज्ञं प्रजानां परिपालनम्॥
en: The parents, and even the gods always expect liberality, study, sacrificial rites and the protection of subjects, of their sons.

sn: एतद् धर्म्यमधर्म्यं वा जन्मनैवाभ्यजायथाः। ते तु वैद्याः कुले जाता अवृत्त्या तात पीडिताः॥
en: Whether this be virtue or not, you are to practice them in consequence of this your birth; but my children, though wise and born in a high family, are without the means of earning their living and in fact they are persecuted by others.

sn: यत्र दानपतिं शूरं क्षुधिताः पृथिवीचराः। प्राप्य तुष्टाः प्रतिष्ठन्ते धर्मः कोऽभ्यधिकस्ततः॥
en: Who earns greater virtue than he who is a hero and the foremost among the gift makers, coming in contract with whom hungry beings of the earth have their hunger satisfied?

sn: दानेनान्यं बलेनान्यं तथा सूनृतया परम्। सर्वतः प्रतिगृह्णीयाद् राज्यं प्राप्येह धार्मिकः॥
en: Some by means of gifts, others by means of force, a third by means of truth, should be attached to his own side by a virtuous man who has obtained a kingdom.

sn: ब्राह्मणः प्रचरेद् भैक्षं क्षत्रिय: परिपालयेत्। वैश्यो धनार्जनं कुर्याच्छूद्रः परिचरेच्च तान्॥
en: A Brahmana should live on alms, a Kshatriya should protect his subjects, a Vaishya should acquire wealth and a Shudra should serve all these other orders.

sn: भैक्षं विप्रतिषिद्धं ते कृषिःवोपपद्यते। क्षत्रियोऽसि क्षतात् त्राता बाहुवीर्योपजीविता॥
en: The life of a bigger is not suited to you, nor does agriculture seem fit; you are Kshatriya, the Saviour of the oppressed and should live by the prowess of your arms.

sn: पित्र्यमंशं महाबाहो निमग्नं पुनरुद्धर। साम्ना भेदेन दानेन दण्डेनाथ नयेन वा॥ । नु
en: O you of long arms, earn again your paternal wealth which is lost, by means of conciliation, dispute, gifts, punishment, or by diplomacy.

sn: इतो दुःखतरं किं यदहं हीनबान्धवा। परपिण्डमुदीक्षे वै त्वां सूत्वाऽमित्रनन्दन॥
en: What can be more sorrowful than this-that I, deprived of friends and supporters, should live on the food of others, having given birth to you, O delighter of friends.

sn: युद्ध्यस्व राजधर्मेण मा निमज्जी: पितामहान्। मा गमः क्षीणपुण्यस्त्वं सानुजः पापिकां गतिम्॥
en: Fight following the duties of kings and do not sink your grandfathers, in infamy; do not obtain a sinful end along with your younger brothers with the effect of your virtues deeds being wrested away.

description: Injunctions of Vidura to his son
sn: कुन्त्युवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। विदुलायाश्च संवादं पुत्रस्य च परंतप॥
en: Kunti said In this connection is cited the old story of the conversation between Vidula and her son, O chastiser of foes.

description: Injunctions of Vidura to his son
sn: अत्र श्रेयश्च भूयश्च यथावद् वक्तुमर्हसि। यशस्विनी मन्युमती कुले जाता विभावरी॥
en: It is proper that you should tell (Yudhishthira) the words of that story or anything better than that. There was a lady born in a noble family who had great renown and was wrathful.

description: Injunctions of Vidura to his son
sn: क्षत्रधर्मरता दान्ता विदुला दीर्घदर्शिनी। विश्रुता राजसंसत्सु श्रुतवाक्या बहुश्रुता।॥
en: She was attached to the duties of a Kshatriya princess and her name was Vidula, She possessed great foresight and had senses under control; her name was known to all kings and she was very learned for hearing speeches of eminent men.

description: Injunctions of Vidura to his son
sn: विदुला नाम राजन्या जगहें पुत्रमौरसम्। निर्जितं सिन्धुराजेन शयानं दीनचेतसम्॥
en: The princess Vidula thus censured her own son who, being defeated by the king of the Sindhus, was lying down with a sorrowful heart.

description: Injunctions of Vidura to his son
sn: विदुलोवाच अनन्दन मया जात द्विषतां हर्षवर्धन। न मया त्वं न पित्रा च जातः क्वाभ्यागतो ह्यसि॥
en: Vidula said I have begotten a son who does not delight me but on the other hand increases the joys of our enemies. By me nor by your father have you been begotten. Where have you come from?

description: Injunctions of Vidura to his son
sn: निर्मन्युश्चाप्यसंख्येयः पुरुषः क्लीबसाधनः। यावज्जीवं निराशोऽसि कल्याणाय धुरं वह॥
en: Being the reverse of wrathful you cannot be reckoned among men and your features possess no signs of prowess. Throughout your life you are in despair; for your sake, and your welfare, bear the burden of life manfully.

description: Injunctions of Vidura to his son
sn: माऽऽत्मानमवमन्यस्व मैनमल्पेन बीभरः। मनः कृत्वा सुकल्याणं मा भैस्त्वं प्रतिसंहर॥
en: Do not think lightly of your own soul and do not let it be satisfied with a little; having set your mind on very great desirable objects, be not afraid and abandon your misgivings.

description: Injunctions of Vidura to his son
sn: उत्तिष्ठ हे कापुरुष मा शेष्वैवं पराजितः। अमित्रान् नन्दयन् सर्वान् निर्मानो बन्धुशोकदः॥
en: Rise, O coward, do not remain inactive in this way being defeated, thereby increasing the joys of our enemies, affording cause for grief to your friends and regardless of everything.

description: Injunctions of Vidura to his son
sn: सुपूरा वै कुनदिका सुपूरो मूषिकाञ्जलिः। सुसंतोषः कापुरुषः स्वल्पकेनैव तुष्यति॥
en: Bad (small) rivers are filled with a handful water and douses are satisfied with little and a coward is ever well satisfied, for a little satisfies him.

description: Injunctions of Vidura to his son
sn: अप्यहेरारुजन् दंष्ट्रामाश्वेव निधनं व्रजा अपि वा संशयं प्राप्य जीवितेऽपि पराक्रमः॥
en: Rather die in the act of rooting out the fangs of a snake than roam about like a dog and exercise your prowess even at the risk of life.

description: Injunctions of Vidura to his son
sn: अप्यरेः श्येनवच्छिद्रं पश्येस्त्वं विपरिक्रमन्। विवदन् वाथवा तूष्णीं व्योम्नि वापरिशङ्कितः॥
en: Or be on the look out for the holes of your enemies like a hawk roaming about in the sky or you show your prowess and fight without any doubts in your mind.

description: Injunctions of Vidura to his son
sn: त्वमेवं प्रेतवच्छेघे कस्माद् वज्रहतो यथा। उत्तिष्ठ हे कापुरुष मा स्वाप्सीः शत्रुनिर्जितः॥
en: Why are you lying down like a dead body being struck with thunder? Rise, O coward, and do not lie down defeated by your enemies.

description: Injunctions of Vidura to his son
sn: मास्तं गमस्त्वं कृपणो विश्रूयस्व स्वकर्मणा। मा मध्ये मा जघन्ये त्वं माऽधो भूस्तिष्ठ गर्जितः॥
en: Do not vanish away into darkness so miserably; let yourself be heard about by your deeds; do not stand in the second rank, nor in the third nor in the last but stand proudly first.

description: Injunctions of Vidura to his son
sn: अलातं तिन्दुकस्येव मुहूर्तमपि विज्वल। मा तुषाग्निरिवान—िमायस्व जिजीविषुः॥
en: Blaze up even for a moment like a piece of Tindula wood and do not like the fire of husk smoke away fireless out of your desire of life.

description: Injunctions of Vidura to his son
sn: मुहूर्तं ज्वलितं श्रेयो न च धूमायितं चिरम्। मा ह स्म कस्यचिद् गेहे जनि राज्ञः खरो मृदुः॥
en: A momentary blaze is better than smoking for a long time; let not there be born in a royal house a prince who is too harsh or who is too soft-minded.

description: Injunctions of Vidura to his son
sn: कृत्वा मानुष्यकं कर्म सृत्वाजिं यावदुत्तमम्। धर्मस्यानृण्यमाप्नोति न चात्मानं विगर्हते॥
en: Doing the deed of men and achieving every feat that is really great in a field of battle a man satisfied the duties of his order and has no reason to find fault with himself.

description: Injunctions of Vidura to his son
sn: अलब्वा यदि वा लब्ध्वा नानुशोचति पण्डितः। आनन्तर्यं चारभते न प्राणानां धनायते॥
en: A wise man grieves not whether he is successful or not in his object; on the contrary he commences what ought to be done under the altered circumstances without caring for his life.

description: Injunctions of Vidura to his son
sn: उद्भावयस्व वीर्यं वा तां वा गच्छ ध्रुवां गतिम्। धर्म पुत्राग्रतः कृत्वा किंनिमित्तं हि जीवसि॥
en: Show forth your own power or meet with your sure end only playing at your back (making it a secondary consideration) why do you live my son?

description: Injunctions of Vidura to his son
sn: इष्टापूर्तं हि ते क्लीब कीर्तिश्च सकला हता। विच्छिन्नं भोगमूलं ते किंनिमित्तं हि जीवसि॥
en: The fruits of the sacrificial rites performed by you, O coward, and all your renown are all destroyed; the roots of your enjoyment are all cut up; for what reason do you live on?

description: Injunctions of Vidura to his son
sn: शत्रुर्निमज्जता ग्राह्यो जवायां प्रपतिष्यता। विपरिच्छिन्नमूलोऽपि न विषीदेत् कथंचन॥
en: When about to fall down (in wrestling) an enemy should be held by the thing and made to fall down also even when cut up to the roots, one should not grieve.

description: Injunctions of Vidura to his son
sn: उद्यम्य धुरमुत्कर्षेदाजानेयकृतं स्मरन्। कुरु सत्त्वं च मानं च विद्धि पौरुषमात्मनः॥
en: Remembering the exertion made by horses of good breed in moving heavy weight know what in your own manliness lies and bring together all you sense of honour and energy.

description: Injunctions of Vidura to his son
sn: उद्भावय कुलं मग्नं त्वत्कृते स्वयमेव हि। यस्य वृत्तं न जल्पन्ति मानवा महदद्भुतम्॥
en: Raise up the race that has been sunk in infamy by your own doings. The man, whose great and wonderful feats men do not talk about.

description: Injunctions of Vidura to his son
sn: राशिवर्धनमात्रं स नैव स्त्री न पुनः पुमान्। दाने तपसि सत्ये च यस्य नोच्चरितं यशः॥
en: Goes only to increase the common heard; he is neither a woman nor a man; he chose fame is not spoken about in gifts, devolution and truth

description: Injunctions of Vidura to his son
sn: विद्यायामर्थलाभे वा मातुरुच्चार एव सः। श्रुतेन तपसा वापि श्रिया वा विक्रमेण वा॥
en: And in learning and attainment of wealth is but the excretion of his mother. Whereas learning, devotion, in prosperity or prowess.

description: Injunctions of Vidura to his son
sn: जनान् योऽभिभवत्यन्यान् कर्मणा हि स वै पुमान्। न त्वेव जाल्पी कापाली वृत्तिमेषितुमर्हसि॥
en: The man who suppress another or in deeds is a man indeed. It is not proper that you should adopt a life which is idle and wretched,

description: Injunctions of Vidura to his son
sn: नृशंस्यामयशस्यां च दुःखां कापुरुषोचिताम्। यमेनमभिनन्देयुरमित्राः पुरुषं कृशम्॥
en: Compassionate leading to infamy and miserable which is suitable only for a coward; in such a case enemies rejoice over such a weak man.

description: Injunctions of Vidura to his son
sn: लोकस्य समवज्ञातं निहीनासनवाससम्। अहो लाभकर हीनमल्पजीवनमल्पकम्॥
en: Held in contempt and destitute of seats and robes; they express surprise and gratification at small earnings, are means, have no courage and are low.

description: Injunctions of Vidura to his son
sn: नेदृशं बन्धुमासाद्य बान्धवः सुखमेधते। अवृत्त्यैव विपत्स्यामो वयं राष्ट्रात् प्रवासिताः॥
en: Friends derive no happiness from gaining such a friend; being exiled from a kingdom we shall die destitute of the means of earning our livelihood,

description: Injunctions of Vidura to his son
sn: सर्वकामरसैींनाः स्थानभ्रष्टा अकिंचनाः। अवल्गुकारिणं सत्सु कुलवंशस्य नाशनम्॥
en: Deprived of all desires and enjoyments, turned out from our place and having nothing at all. Misbehaving among a race of honest men and the destroyer of the fame of his race and family.

description: Injunctions of Vidura to his son
sn: कलिं पुत्रप्रवादेन संजय त्वामजीजनम्। निरमर्षं निरुत्साहं निर्वीर्यमरिनन्दनम्॥
en: Kali himself in the shape of yourself, my son Sanjaya, has been brought forth, by me who has no wealth in him no energy, no prowess, and is the delighted of his enemies.

description: Injunctions of Vidura to his son
sn: मा स्म सीमन्तिनी काचिज्जनयेत् पुत्रमीदृशम्। मा धूमाय ज्वलात्यन्तमाक्रम्य जहि शात्रवान्॥
en: Let no woman bring forth such a son; do not smoke away but blaze up and exercising your prowess slay your enemies.

description: Injunctions of Vidura to his son
sn: ज्वल मूर्धन्यमित्राणां मुहूर्तमपि वा क्षणम्। एतावानेव पुरुषो यदमर्षी यदक्षमी॥
en: Blaze over the heads of enemies for a moment or even for a small bit of time; those are indeed men who are wrathful and who exercise no forgiveness.

description: Injunctions of Vidura to his son
sn: क्षमावान् निरमर्षश्च नैव स्त्री न पुनः पुमान्। संतोषो वै श्रियं हन्ति तथानुक्रोश एव च॥
en: One, destitute of wrath and given to the exercise of forgiveness, is neither a woman nor a man; satisfaction destroys prosperity so does softness of heart.

description: Injunctions of Vidura to his son
sn: अनुत्थानभये चोभे निरीहो नाश्नुते महत्। एभ्यो निकृतिपापेभ्यः प्रमुञ्चात्मानमात्मना॥
en: And so do these two namely want of exertion and fear; one without exertion never attains to greatness; free your soul, by your own exertions of these defects which lead to ruin.

description: Injunctions of Vidura to his son
sn: आयसं हृदयं कृत्वा मृगयस्व पुनः स्वकम्। परं विषहते यस्मात् तस्मात् पुरुष उच्यते॥
en: Making your heart one of steel, hunt for the recovery of your lost wealth; one is called a man (Purusha) for he vanquishes the enemy (Param).

description: Injunctions of Vidura to his son
sn: तमाहुर्व्यर्थनामानं स्त्रीवद् य इह जीवति। शूरस्योर्जितसत्त्वस्य सिंहविक्रान्तचारिणः॥
en: He is said to bear the false name of Purusha) who leads in this world the life of a woman. A hero of mighty strength and acting like a powerful lion,

description: Injunctions of Vidura to his son
