en: Those delighters of the Pandu race set out with a large army after having made due arrangements for guarding over their wealth and having erected a surrounding wall at a short distance and soldiers being placed at regular intervals.

sn: ददतो गां हिरण्यं च ब्राह्मणैरभिसंवृताः। स्तूयमाना ययू राजन् रथैर्मणिविभूषितैः॥
en: They proceeded distributing cows and gold and surrounded by Brahmanas; O king, they proceeded, hymns being sung in their praise, on chariots ornamented with gems and precious stones.

sn: केकया धृष्टकेतुश्च पुत्रः काश्यस्य चाभिभुः। श्रेणिमान् वसुदानश्च शिखण्डी चापराजितः॥
en: The Kaikeya princes and Dhrishtaketu the son of the prince of the Kashis, Shrenimat, Vasudana, and Shikhandin who had never met with defeat,

sn: हृष्टास्तुष्टाः कवचिन: सशस्त्राः समलंकृताः। राजानमन्ययुः सर्वे परिवार्य युधिष्ठिरम्॥
en: With cheerful hearts, clad in coats of mail, well-armed, and with their persons well ornamented, all followed surrounding the king Yudhishthira.

sn: जघनार्धे विराटश्च याज्ञसेनिश्च सौमकिः। सुधर्मा कुन्तिभोजश्च धृष्टद्युम्नस्य चात्मजाः॥
en: In the rear were, Virata and the son of Yagasena of the Somaka race, Sudharman and Kuntibhoja and the sons of Dhrishtadyumna,

sn: रथायुतानि चत्वारि हयाः पञ्चगुणास्तथा। पत्तिसैन्यं दशगुणं गजानामयुतानि षट्॥
en: Forty thousand chariots, five times that number of horses, ten times that number of foot soldiers, and sixty thousand elephants.

sn: अनाधृष्टिश्चेकितानो धृष्टकेतुश्च सात्यकिः। परिवार्य ययुः सर्वे वासुदेवधनंजयौ॥
en: Anadhristhi and Chekitana, Dhrishtaketu and Satyaki all went surrounding the king as also Vasudeva and Dhananjaya.

sn: आसाद्य तु कुरुक्षेत्रं व्यूढानीकाः प्रहारिणः। पाण्डवाः समदृश्यन्त नर्दन्तो वृषभा इव॥
en: And having racing Kurukshetra with their army ready for action, those smiters, the Pandavas, looked like bulls wandering about with loud roars.

sn: तेऽवगाह्य कुरुक्षेत्रं शङ्खान् दध्मुररिंदमाः। तथैव दध्मतुः शङ्ख वासुदेवधनंजयौ॥
en: And reaching Kurukshetra those chastiser of foes blew their conches and in the same way did Vasudeva and Dhananjaya also blow their conches.

sn: पाञ्चजन्यस्य निर्घोषं विस्फूर्जितमिवाशनेः। निशम्य सर्वसैन्यानि समहृष्यन्त सर्वशः॥
en: All the soldiers of the army became cheerful in every way at hearing the sound of the Panchajanya conch which was similar to the roaring of thunder.

sn: शङ्खदुन्दुभिसंसृष्टः सिंहनादस्तरस्विनाम्। पृथिवीं चान्तरिक्षं च सागरांश्चान्वनादयत्॥
en: Sounds of conches and drums mixed with the leonine roars of those soldiers endued with activity resounded in the earth and the sky and the seas also.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततो देशे समे स्निग्धे प्रभूतयवसेन्धने। निवेशयामास तदा सेनां राजा युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Then in a part of the field which was level, shady and where there was plenty of fodder's and fuel the king Yudhishthira had his army encamped.

sn: परिहत्य श्मशानानि देवतायतनानि च। आश्रमांश्र महर्षीणां तीर्थान्यायतनानि च।॥
en: Avoiding cremation grounds other sacred places and horses consecrated to the gods, and the hermitages of the great Rishis and also other holy places,

sn: मधुरानूषरे देशे शुचो पुण्ये महामतिः। निवेशं कारयामास कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Yudhishthira, the son of Kunti, of great intelligence, ordered his army to be encamped, in a part of the field which was delightful and grassy and which was open.

sn: ततश्च पुनरुत्थाय सुखी विश्रान्तवाहनः। प्रययौ पृथिवीपालैर्वृतः शतसहस्रशः॥
en: Then his army, which was weary and tried, having rested, again set out surrounded by hundred and thousands of rulers of the earth.

sn: विद्राव्य शतशो गुल्मान् धार्तराष्ट्रस्य सैनिकान्। पर्यक्रामत् समन्ताच्च पार्थेन सह केशवः॥
en: Routing hundreds of groups of soldiers of the son of Dhritarashtra Keshava wandered about in company with the son of Pritha.

sn: शिबिरं मापयामास धृष्टद्युम्नश्च पार्षतः। सात्यकिश्च रथोदारो युयुधानश्चः प्रतापवान्॥
en: Dhrishtadyumna, the son of the Prishata race, and the car-warrior Satyaki endued with prowess, otherwise called Yuyudhana, had the land of encampment measured.

sn: आसाद्य सरितं पुण्यां कुरुक्षेत्रे हिरण्वतीम्। सूपतीर्थां शुचिजलां शर्करापङ्कवर्जिताम्॥
en: Reaching, in the field of Kurukshetra the holy lake Hiranvati which was a place of hermitage, the water of which was pure and the bed free from stones and mire,

sn: खानयामास परिखां केशवस्तत्र भारत। गुप्त्यर्थमपि चादिश्य बलं तत्र न्यवेशयत्॥
en: Keshava had a trench dug there, O Bharata and for the protection thereof posted a body of soldiers with instructions to them.

sn: विधिर्यः शिविरस्यासीत् पाण्डवानां महात्मनाम्। तद्विधानि नरेन्द्राणां कारयामास केशवः॥
en: The rulers, that were in force in connection with the encampment of the great souled Pandavas, were ordered also to be followed by Keshava in regard the encampment of other chiefs of men.

sn: प्रभूततरकाष्ठानि दुराधर्षतराणि च। भक्ष्यभोज्यानपानानि शतशोऽथं सहस्रशः॥
en: There were plenty of tents, by hundred and thousands, hard to be captured and provided with abundance of foods, eatables, solid food, drink and fuels.

sn: शिविराणि महामुणि राज्ञां तत्र पृथक् पृथक्। विमानानीव राजेन्द्र निविष्टानि महीतले॥
en: Separate tents of great value were fixed there on the face of the earth, one for each; and they looked like so many palaces, O chief among kings.

sn: तत्रासशिल्पिनः प्राज्ञाः शतशो दत्तवेतनाः। सर्वोपकरणैर्युक्ता वैद्याः शास्त्रविशारदाः॥
en: And there were engaged many skillful workmen and experienced, to whom were given regular salaries, as also physicians, familiar with the science, furnished with all the necessary articles and ingredients of their respective professions.

sn: ज्याधनुर्वर्मशस्त्राणां तथैव मधुसर्पिषोः। ससर्जरसपांसूनां राशयः पर्वतोपमाः॥
en: Bowstrings bows, coats of mail, and weapons as also honey and clarified butter, water, pounded lac, in heaps resembling hills,

sn: बहूदकं सुयवसं तुषाङ्गारसमन्वितम्। शिबिरे शिबिरे राजा संचकारं युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: And plenty of water and fodder for cattle and chaff and fire, the king Yudhishthira placed in each tent.

sn: महायन्त्राणि नाराचास्तोमराणि परश्वधाः। धनूंषि कवचादीनि ऋष्टयस्तूणसंयुताः॥
en: Large machines, long shafts, to maras, and battle-axes, bows, coats of mail, breast-plates and quivers were also there.

sn: गजाः कण्टकसंनाहां लोहवर्मोत्तरच्छदाः। दृश्यन्ते तत्र गिर्याभाः सहस्रशतयोधिनः॥
en: Elephants having coats of steel with prickles thereon and huge as mountain, were seen there, each capable of fighting with a hundred thousand warriors.

sn: निविष्टान् पाण्डवांस्तत्र ज्ञात्वा मित्राणि भारत। अभिससुर्यथादेशं सबलाः सहवाहनाः॥
en: Knowing that the sons of Pandu were encamped there, O Bharata, his friends came from their respective countries along with their own forces and armies.

sn: चरितब्रह्मचर्यास्ते सोमपा भूरिदक्षिणाः। जयाय पाण्डुपुत्राणां समाजाग्मुर्महीक्षितः॥
en: By them had been observed Brahmacharya vows, drunk the Soma juice; and liberal presents had also been made by them to the Brahmanas in sacrifices; these kings came for ensuring victory to the sons of Pandu.

sn: जनमेजय उवाच युधिष्ठिरं सहानीकमुपायान्तं युयुत्सया। संनिविष्टं कुरुक्षेत्रे वासुदेवेन पालितम्॥
en: Janamejaya said Hearing that Yudhishthira with his army was advancing with the desire of fighting and has already reached Kurukshetra and was protected by Vasudeva,

sn: विराटदुपदाभ्यां च सपुत्राभ्यां समन्वितम्। केकयैर्वृष्णिभिश्चैव पार्थिवैः शतशो वृतम्॥
en: And by Virata and Drupada along with their sons, and by the Kaikeyas and Vrishnis and surrounded by the rulers of the earth by hundreds,

sn: महेन्द्रमिव चादित्यैरभिगुप्तं महारथैः। श्रुत्वा दुर्योधनो राजा किं कार्यं प्रत्यपद्यत॥
en: Protected by mighty car-warriors as the great Indra by the Adityas-what did the king Duryodhana do?

sn: एतदिच्छाम्यहं श्रोतुं विस्तरेण महामते। सम्भ्रमे तुमुले तस्मिन् यदासीत् कुरुजाङ्गले॥
en: I desire to hear this in detail, O you of great wisdom-what happened at Kurujangala on that terrible occasion,

sn: व्यथयेयुरिमे देवान् सेन्द्रानपि समागमे। पाण्डवा वासुदेवश्च विराटद्रुपदौ तथा॥
en: These assembled together would strike terror into the hearts of the gods even with Indra-namely the son of Pandu Vasudeva, Virata and Drupada,

sn: धृष्टद्युम्नश्च पाञ्चाल्यः शिखण्डी च महारथः। युधामन्युश्च विक्रान्तो देवैरपि दुरासदः॥
en: Dhrishtadyumna, the princess of Panchala and the great car-warriors Shikhandi and the powerful Yudhamanyu hard to withstand even by the gods.

sn: एतदिच्छाम्यहं श्रोतुं विस्तरेण तपोधन। कुरूणां पाण्डवानां च यद् यदासीद् विचेष्टितम्॥
en: This I desire to hear in detail, O you whose only wealth is devotion, namely the movements respectively of the Kurus and the Pandavas.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच प्रतियाते तु दाशार्हे राजा दुर्योधनस्तदा। कर्णं दुःशासनं चैव शकुनि चाब्रवीदिदम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said The scion of the Dasharha race having gone away, the king Duryodhana then said thus to Karna, Dushasana and Shakuni.

sn: अकृतेनैव कार्येण गतः पार्थानधोक्षजः। स एनान्मन्युनाऽऽविष्टो ध्रुवं धक्ष्यत्यसंशयम्॥
en: “With his object unsuccessful has the one whom the senses cannot know (Krishna) gone back to the son of Pritha and being filled with malice he will surely excite them (against us). there is no doubt of it.

sn: इष्टो हि वासुदेवस्य पाण्डवैर्मम विग्रहः। भीमसेनार्जुनौ चैव दाशार्हस्य मते स्थितौ॥
en: It is the desire of Vasudeva that there should be war between the sons of Pandu and myself; and Bhimasena and Arjuna ever follow the opinions of that scion of the Dasharha race.

sn: अजातशत्रुरत्यर्थं भीमसेनवशानुगः। निकृतश्च मया पूर्वं सह सर्वैः सहोदरैः॥
en: Yudhishthira who has no enemies, too is greatly under the influence of Bhimasena-besides he had been persecuted by me before along with all his brothers.

sn: विराटदुपदौ चैव कृतवैरौ मया सह। तौ च सेनाप्रणेतारौ वासुदेववशानुगौ॥
en: Virata and Drupada too entertain feelings of enmity towards me; and those two leaders of armies too are under the influence of Vasudeva.

sn: भविता विग्रहः सोऽहं तुमुलो लोमहर्षणः। तस्मात् सांग्रामिकं सर्वं कारयध्वमतन्द्रिताः॥
en: Therefore will there be a fierce war which will make one's hair stand on end; therefore do you make all preparations of war very carefully.

sn: शिबिराणि कुरुक्षेत्रे क्रियन्तां वसुधाधिपाः। सुपर्याप्तावकाशानि दुरादेयानि शत्रुभिः॥
en: Let the rulers of the earth fix their tents in Kurukshetra-tents which are spacious and large, and incapable being captured by enemies.

sn: आसन्नजलकाष्ठानि शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः। अच्छेद्याहारमार्गाणि बन्धोच्छ्यचितानि च॥
en: Let them be fixed by hundreds and thousands near a place abounding in water and fuel and in such a place that the way leading to it for supplying rations may not be cut off at the sweet will of the foe.

sn: विविधायुधपूर्णानि पताकाध्वजवन्ति च। समाश्च तेषां पन्थानः क्रियन्तां नगराद् बहिः॥
en: Let them be full of diverse kinds of weapons, flags and banners and let the roads leading to it out of the town be made level and cleared.

sn: प्रयाणं घुष्यतामद्य श्वोभूते इति मा चिरम्। ते तथेति प्रतिज्ञाय श्वोभूते चक्रिरे तथा॥
en: Proclaim without delay that we march forth tomorrow and they too saying "very well” obeyed these instructions on the day after.

sn: हृष्टरूपा महात्मानो निवासाय महीक्षिताम्। ततस्ते पार्थिवाः सर्वे तच्छ्रुत्वा राजशासनम्॥
en: Then did those rulers of the earth hearing those commands of the king become cheerful and made the necessary arrangements for the residence of the allies.

sn: आसनेभ्यो महार्हेभ्य उदतिष्ठन्नमर्षिताः। बाहून् परिघसंकाशान् संस्पृशन्तः शनैः शनैः॥
en: Being excited with wrath (towards the Pandavas) they rose up from their seats of great value and began slowly to rub their arms which had the circumference, of maces.

sn: काञ्चनाङ्गददीप्तांश्च चन्दनागुरुभूषितान्। उष्णीषाणि नियच्छन्तः पुण्डरीकनिभैः करैः। अन्तरीयोत्तरीयाणि भूषणानि च सर्वशः॥
en: And which were blazing with golden ornaments and ornamented with sandal paste; and they began to put on their head gears by the help of their lotus like hands as also their lower and upper garments in all parts body.

sn: ते रथान् रथिनः श्रेष्ठा हयांश्च हयकोविदाः। सज्जयन्ति स्म नागांश्च नागशिक्षास्वनुष्ठिताः॥
en: The foremost among the car-warriors looked to the equipment of the cars, while those who were experts about horses looked to the harnessing of the steeds, and those who knew all about elephants began to get ready the elephants for war.

sn: अथ वर्माणि चित्राणि काञ्चनानि बहूनि च। विविधानि च शस्त्राणि चक्रुः सर्वाणि सर्वशः॥
en: All those warriors then began to take up diverse sorts of coats of mail, many amours which were made of gold and all sorts of weapon in all directions.

sn: पदातयश्च पुरुषा शस्त्राणि विविधानि च। उपाजह्वः शरीरेषु हेमचित्राण्यनेकशः॥
en: The soldiers of the infantry began to take up different sorts of weapons and to protect their bodies by various sorts of amours made of gold.

sn: तदुत्सव इवोदचं सम्प्रहृष्टनरावृतम्। नगरं धार्तराष्ट्रस्य भारतासीत् समाकुलम्॥
en: Then did that army, of the son of Dhritarashtra made up of cheerful men, look like a festive city, O Bharata.

sn: जनौघसलिलावर्तो रथनागाश्वमीनवान्। शङ्खदुन्दुभिनिर्घोषः कोशसंचयरत्नवान्॥
en: The crowd of human beings looked like the water of the sea, the cars, horses, and elephants like the fishes, the sound of conches and the beat of drums were its roar and the collection of treasures was the gems.

sn: चित्राभरणवर्मोर्मिः शस्त्रनिर्मलफेनवान्। प्रासादमालाद्रिवृतो रथ्यापणमहाह्रदः॥
en: The diverse sorts of ornaments were the lesser waves, the bright and spotless weapons the foam, the clusters, of houses in the city were like the mountains on the sea shore and the groups of chariots were the large lakes on the bed of the sea.

sn: योधचन्द्रोदयोद्भूतः कुरुराजमहार्णवः। व्यदृश्यत तदा राजंश्चन्द्रोदय इवोदधिः॥
en: In short, O king, was that great sea of the Kuru king brightened by the moon of warriors and it really then looked like the great sea at the rise of the moon.

sn: ॥इति श्रीमहाभारते उद्योगपर्वणि सैन्यनिर्याणपर्वणि दुर्योधनसैन्यसज्जकरण त्रिपञ्चादधिकशततमोऽध्यायः॥
en: Thus ends the one hundred and fifty third chapter, the in Sainya Niryana of the Udyoga Parva.

description: The conversation between Yudhishthira and Krishna
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच वासुदेवस्य तद् वाक्यमनुस्मृत्य युधिष्ठिरः। पुनः पप्रच्छ वार्ष्णेयं कथं मन्दोऽब्रवीदिदम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Yudhishthira, remembering these words of Vasudeva again asked the scion of the Vrishni race as to how that fool could say it.

description: The conversation between Yudhishthira and Krishna
sn: अस्मिन्नभ्यागते काले किं च नः क्षममच्युत। कथं च वर्तमाना वै स्वधर्मान्न च्यवेमहि॥
en: "Under the present circumstances which have developed before us, what should we do, O you who never go away from the right path; and by shaping our course in what way shall we not fall off from the duties of our class.

description: The conversation between Yudhishthira and Krishna
sn: दुर्योधनस्य कर्णस्य शकुनेः सौबलस्य च। वासुदेव मतक्षोऽसि मम सभ्रातृकस्य च॥
en: O Vasudeva, you know the minds of Duryodhana, Karma, Shakuni and the son of Subala as also of myself along with my brothers.

description: The conversation between Yudhishthira and Krishna
sn: विदुरस्यापि तद् वाक्यं श्रुतं भीष्मस्य चोभयोः। कुन्त्याश्च विपुलप्रज्ञ प्रज्ञा कात्स्न्येन ते श्रुता॥
en: The words of Vidura have been heard by you as also those of Bhishma, as also the entire wisdom of the greatly wise Kunti, as embodied in her words.

description: The conversation between Yudhishthira and Krishna
sn: सर्वमेतदतिक्रम्य विचार्य च पुनः पुनः। क्षमं यन्नो महाबाहो तद् ब्रवीह्यविचारयन्॥
en: Reviewing in your mind all this and reflecting again and again, speak unhesitatingly what our capabilities are, O you of along arms.

description: The conversation between Yudhishthira and Krishna
sn: श्रुत्वैतद् धर्मराजस्य धर्मार्थसहितं वचः। मेघदुन्दुभिनिर्घोषः कृष्णो वाक्यमथाब्रवीत्॥
en: Hearing these words of the virtuous king consistent with both virtue and worldly profit, Krishna said these words with the voice resembling the roar of clouds and beat of drums.

description: The conversation between Yudhishthira and Krishna
sn: कृष्ण उवाच उक्तवानस्मि यद् वाक्यं धर्मार्थसहितं हितम्। न तु तन्निकृतिप्रज्ञे कौरव्ये प्रतितिष्ठति।७॥
en: Krishna said The words that you have said consistent with virtue and profit and are indeed to your benefit but then these do not seem acceptable to the son of Kuru, with whom ignorance has now become wisdom.

description: The conversation between Yudhishthira and Krishna
sn: न च भीष्मस्य दुर्मेधाः शृणोति विदुरस्य वा। मम वा भाषितं किंचित् सर्वमेवातिवर्तते॥
en: That man of bad intellect does not even listen to the words of Bhima nor to those of Vidura nor even the words spoken by me-he disobeys all.

description: The conversation between Yudhishthira and Krishna
sn: नैष कामयते धर्म नैष कामयते यशः। जितं स मन्यते सर्वं दुरात्मा कर्णमाश्रितः॥
en: He does not seek virtue, nor does he see renown, under the protection of Karna, that evil souled one considers everything as conquered.

description: The conversation between Yudhishthira and Krishna
sn: बन्धमाज्ञापयामास मम चापि सुयोधनः। न च तं लब्धवान् कामं दुरात्मा पापनिश्चयः॥
en: Suyodhana even ordered for my capture; but that evil-souled one of sinful determination did not succeed in his desire.

description: The conversation between Yudhishthira and Krishna
sn: न च भीष्मो न च द्रोणो युक्तं तत्राहतुर्वचः। सर्वे तमनुवर्तन्ते ऋते विदुरमच्युत॥
en: In that case neither Bhishma nor Drona said anything-in fact all follow him more or less save Vidura, O you who never swerve from your duties.

description: The conversation between Yudhishthira and Krishna
sn: शकुनिः सौबलश्चैव कर्णदुःशासनावपि। त्यय्युक्तान्यभाषन्त मूढा मूढममर्षणम्॥
en: Shakuni, the son of Subala, Karna and Dushasana-all these fools, spoke of you in a way you did not deserve, to that wrathful one.

description: The conversation between Yudhishthira and Krishna
sn: किं च तेन मयोक्तेन यान्यभाषत कौरवः। संक्षेपेण दुरात्मासौ न युक्तं त्वयि वर्तते॥
en: What is the use of my repeating everything that the son of Kuru said; in brief that evilsouled one does not hold the opinion, you deserve, of yourself.

description: The conversation between Yudhishthira and Krishna
sn: पार्थिवेषु न सर्वेषु य इमे तव सैनिकाः। यत् पापं यन्नकल्याणं सर्वं तस्मिन् प्रतिष्ठितम्॥
en: Not even in all these rulers of the earth who constitute your army combined is there the same wickedness and the want of righteousness as is rooted in him.

description: The conversation between Yudhishthira and Krishna
sn: न चापि वयमत्यर्थं परित्यागेन कहिंचित्। कौरवैः शममिच्छामस्तत्र युद्धमनन्तरम्॥
en: We do not desire peace with the sons of Kuru, at the sacrifice of our own interest and therefore war is what we should follow.

description: The conversation between Yudhishthira and Krishna
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तच्छ्रुत्वा पार्थिवाः सर्वे वासुदेवस्य भाषितम्। अब्रुवन्तो मुखं राज्ञःसमुदैक्षन्त भारत॥
en: Vaishampayana said Hearing those words spoken by Vasudeva all the kings looked on the face of the king Yudhishthira, without saying anything, O Bharata.

description: The conversation between Yudhishthira and Krishna
sn: युधिष्ठिरस्त्वभिप्रायमभिलक्ष्य महीक्षिताम्। योगमाज्ञापयामास भीमार्जुनयमैः सह॥
en: Yudhishthira too having divined the intentions of those kings ordered for the arraying of the troops along with Bhima and Arjuna and the twins.

description: The conversation between Yudhishthira and Krishna
sn: ततः किलकिलाभूतमनीकं पाण्डवस्य ह। आज्ञापिते तदा योगे समहष्यन्त सैनिकाः॥
en: Then was there a din in the army of the Pandavas, and on the order of the arraying troops being given the soldiers became cheerful.

description: The conversation between Yudhishthira and Krishna
sn: अवध्यानां वधं पश्यन् धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः। निःश्वसन भीमसेनं च विजयं चेदमब्रवीत्॥
en: The virtuous king Yudhishthira, now seeing that a slaughter of innocent men was unavoidable, began to sign repeatedly and said these words to Bhimasena and Vijaya.

description: The conversation between Yudhishthira and Krishna
sn: यदर्थं वनवासश्च प्राप्तं दुःखं च यन्मया। सोऽयमस्मानुपैत्येव परोऽनर्थः प्रयत्नतः॥
en: The very thing to avoid which (a war) I went to exile in the forest and experienced other troubles-that Very calamity overtakes us as if with a set purpose.

description: The conversation between Yudhishthira and Krishna
sn: तस्मिन् यत्नः कृतोऽस्माभिः स नो हीनः प्रयत्नतः। अकृते तु प्रयत्नेऽस्मानुपावृत्तः कलिर्महान्॥
en: The object, for which we took so much care, leaves as for our wishing it; and without our wishing for it has the mighty Kali come.

description: The conversation between Yudhishthira and Krishna
sn: कथं ह्यवध्यैः संग्रामः कार्यः सह भविष्यति। कथं हत्वा गुरून् वृद्धान् विजयो नो भविष्यति॥
en: How shall we fight with these who cannot be slain and who lead honorable lives and how now can we expect victory by slaying aged men our elders?

description: The conversation between Yudhishthira and Krishna
sn: तच्छ्रुत्वा धर्मराजस्य सव्यसाची परंतपः। यदुक्तं वासुदेवेन श्रावयामास तद् वचः॥
en: Savyasachin that chastiser of foes, hearing these words of the virtuous king, repeated before him the words said by Vasudeva (in this connection).

description: The conversation between Yudhishthira and Krishna
sn: उक्तवान् देवकीपुत्रः कुन्त्याच विदुरस्य च। वचनं तत् त्वया राजन् निखिलेनावधारितम्॥
en: (He said addressing Yudhishthira), you have, O king, understood the words spoken by Kunti and Vidura in their entirely as repeated before you by the son of Devaki.

description: The conversation between Yudhishthira and Krishna
sn: न च तौ वक्ष्यतोऽधर्ममिति मे नैष्ठिकी मतिः। नापि युक्तं च कौन्तेय निवर्तितुमयुध्यतः॥
en: I firmly adhere to the opinion that they will not say what is unrighteous, not is it proper, O son of Kunti, that we should turn back without enjoying war."

description: The conversation between Yudhishthira and Krishna
sn: तच्छ्रुत्वा वासुदेवोऽपि सव्यसाचिवचस्तदा। स्मयमानोऽब्रवीद् वाक्यं पार्थमेवमिति ब्रुवन्॥
en: Vasudeva too hearing those words of Savyasachin, said laughingly to the son of Pritha (Arjuna) “It is as you have said.”

description: The conversation between Yudhishthira and Krishna
sn: ततस्ते धृतसंकल्पा युद्धाय सहसैनिकाः। पाण्डवेया महाराज तां रात्रिं सुखमावसन्॥
en: Then did those sons of Pandu make up their minds for war, O great king, and passed the night with their soldiers without any mental agitation. um f

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच व्युष्टायां वै रजन्यां हि राजा दुर्योधनस्ततः। व्यभजत् तान्यनीकानि दश चैकं च भारत॥
en: Vaishampayana said The night having passed away, king Duryodhana then made the usual divisions of his army which consisted of ten and one Akshauhinis, O Bharata.

sn: नरहस्तिस्थाश्वानां सारं मध्यं च फल्गु च। सर्वेष्वेतेष्वनीकेषु संदिदेश नराधिपः॥
en: He divided his men, elephants, chariots and horses into superior, inferior inferior and indifferent; and then that ruler of men distributed them in his army.

sn: सानुकर्षाः सतूणीराः सवरूथाः सतोमराः। सोपासङ्गाः सशक्तीकाः सनिषङ्गाः सहर्टयः॥
en: Furnished with all the requirements of a large army, namely with materials for repairs of chariots, with quivers to be carried on chariots, with large sticks fixed to spear blades for throwing with the hand, with quivers suitable to be carried on horses and elephants, with Shaktis, (a sort of long handled weapon) with arrow-holders suitable for the infantry and with heavy sticks,

sn: सध्वजाः सपताकाश्च सशरासनतोमराः। रज्जुभिश्च विचित्राभिः सपाशाः सपरिच्छदाः॥
en: With flags and banners, with huge arrows, and bows and bowstrings and diverse suites of ropes, with nooses and lashes;

sn: सकचग्रहविक्षेपाः सतैलगुडवालुकाः। साशीविषघटाः सर्वे ससर्जरसपांसवः॥
en: With plain pointed sticks, oil, molasses and sand (to be thrown heated at the enemy) pots full of poisonous snakes, with pounded lac and other inflammable articles;

sn: सघण्टफलकाः सर्वे सायोगुडजलोपलाः। सशालभिन्दिपालाश्च समधूच्छिष्टमुद्गराः॥
en: With barbed weapons, with skins furnished with bells and all sorts of weapons and instruments for throwing hot molasses water and sand, with maces making a peculiar sound, with syringes for throwing hot liquids;

sn: सकाण्डदण्डकाः सर्वे ससीरविषतोमराः। सशूर्पपिटकाः सर्वे सदात्राङ्कुशतोमराः॥
en: With staffs having thorns or barbs fixed to them, weapons for thrcwing poison, and sloughs, as also devices for hurling javelins;

sn: सकीलकवचाः सर्वे वासीवृक्षादनान्विताः। व्याघ्रचर्मपरीवारा द्वीपिचर्मावृताश्च ते॥
en: With battle axes, forked lances, sharp spikes, iron gloves with barbs and chariots covered by tiger skins are skins of leopards;

sn: सहर्टयः सशृङ्गाश्च सप्रासविविधायुधाः। सकुठाराः सकुद्दालाः सतैलक्षौमसर्पिषः॥
en: With forbid pieces of wood, with excellent horses, with diverse weapons of offense and defense, with felling axes and spades and with oil-clothes, and clarified butter.

sn: रुक्मजालप्रतिच्छन्ना नानामणिविभूषिताः। चित्रानीका: सुवपुषो ज्वलिता इव पावकाः॥
en: Glittering with robes embroidered with gold and decked with diverse gems and consisting of beautiful warriors, the army of Duryodhana blazed forth like fire.

sn: तथा कवचिनः शूराः शस्त्रेषु कृतनिश्चयाः। कुलीना हययोनिज्ञाः सारथ्ये विनिवेषिताः॥
en: Heroes clad in coats of mail and masters in the use of weapons and of good parentage, competent judges of the breed of horses, were appointed to be charioteers.

sn: बद्धारिष्टा बद्धकक्षा बद्धध्वजपताकिनः। बद्धाभरणनि'हा बद्धचर्मासिपट्टिशाः॥
en: The chariots had on them all sorts of drugs and weapons, were drawn by horses having bells and pearls on their necks and had also flags and standards attached. They had also on their turrets ornaments and shields, swords, Pattishas and cther weapons.

sn: चतुर्युजो रथाः सर्वे सर्वे चोत्तमवाजिनः। सप्रासऋष्टिकाः सर्वे सर्वे शतशरासनाः॥
en: All the chariots were drawn by four horses each, all of whom again were the best of their species; each of them was furnished with a hundred bows and all sorts of defensive weapons.

sn: धुर्ययोर्हययोरेकस्तथाऽन्यौ पार्ष्णसारथी। तौ चापि रथिनां श्रेष्ठो रथी च हयवित् तथा॥
en: Each of them had one driver for the horses in front and one again for each of the horses at the sides and those men were the foremost among car-warriors and also familiar with horse driving.

sn: नगराणीव गुप्तानि दुराधर्षाणि शत्रुभिः। आसन् रथसहस्राणि हेममालीनि सर्वशः॥
en: Each was protected as a city should be and was therefore hard to be captured by the enemies; thousands of those decked with gold were posted in all directions.

sn: यथा रथास्तथा नागा बद्धकक्षाः स्वलंकृताः। बभूवुः सप्तपुरुषा रत्नवन्त इवाद्रयः॥
en: As the chariots had bells and wreaths of pearls and other ornaments so had the elephants and on the back of each were mounted seven men making the animals look like hills decks with jewels.

sn: द्वावङ्कुशधरो तत्र द्वावुत्तमधनुर्धरौ। द्वौ वरासिधरौ राजन्नेकः शक्तिपिनाकधूक्॥
en: These seven were made up of two men holding hooks for driving the elephants, two again who were excellent bowmen, two who could fight well with swords, O king, and one was armed with a lance and a trident.

sn: गजैर्मत्तैः समाकीर्णं सवर्मायुधकोशकैः। तद् बभूव बलं राजन् कौरव्यस्य महात्मनः॥
en: That army of the great-souled Kurus, O king, was full of infuriated animals and was furnished with all necessary weapons and treasuries.

sn: आमुक्तकवचैर्युक्तैः सपताकैः स्वलङ्कतैः। सादिभिश्चोपपन्नास्तु तथा चायुतशो हयाः॥
en: It was also made up of tens of thousands of horse soldiers clad in mail, with ornaments on and holding up flags.

sn: असंग्राहाः सुसम्पन्ना हेमभाण्डपरिच्छदाः। अनेकशतसाहस्राः सर्वे सादिवशे स्थिताः॥
en: All the horses numbering many hundreds and thousands were kept under proper control and were free from the habit of scratching the ground with the fore feet.

sn: नानारूपविकाराश्च नानाकवचशस्त्रिणः। पदातिनो नरास्तत्र बभूवुर्हेममालिनः॥
en: sena There were also in that army, hundreds of thousands of infantry decked with gold, clad in diverse sorts of arms and diverse temper.

sn: रथस्यासन् दश गजा गजस्य दश वाजिनः। नरा दश हयस्यासन् पादरक्षाः समन्ततः।।२२।
en: For every chariot there were ten elephants, for every elephants ten horses, for every horse ten men for the proper protection.

sn: रथस्य नागाः पञ्चाशन्नागस्यासन् शतं हयाः। हयस्य पुरुषाः सप्त भिन्नसंधानकारिणः॥
en: There was also another reserve army in which for every chariot there were five elephants, for every elephant one hundred horses, and for every horse seven men.

sn: सेना पञ्चशतं नागा रथास्तावन्त एव च। दश सेना च पृतना पृतना दशवाहिनी॥
en: A consisted of five hundred elephants, and the same number of elephants (with infantry and cavalry); ten Senas made a Pritana and ten Pritanas a Vahini.

sn: सेना च वाहिनी चैव पृतना ध्वजिनी चमूः। अक्षौहिणीति पर्यायैर्निरुक्ता च वरूथिनी॥
en: Sena, Vahini, Pritana, Dhvajini and Bhuhini, Akshauhini, Chamu, and Varuthini mean however the same thing in common usage.

sn: एवं व्यूढान्यनीकानि कौरवेयेण धीमता। अक्षौहिण्यो दशैका च संख्याताः सप्त चैव ह॥
en: In this way was the army of the intelligent Kaurava arrayed by him; there were seven and eleven Akshauhini of troops altogether.

sn: अक्षौहिण्यस्तु सप्तैव पाण्डवानामभूद् बलम्। अहौहिण्यो दशैका च कौरवाणामभूद् बलम्॥
en: The army of the Pandavas consisted of seven Akshauhini, while that of the Kauravas consisted of ten and one Akshauhini.

sn: नराणां पञ्चपञ्चाशदेषा पत्तिर्विधीयते। सेनामुखं च तिस्रस्ता गुल्म इत्यभिशब्दितम्॥ त्रयो गुल्मा गणस्त्वासीद् गणास्त्वयुतशोऽभवन्। दुर्योधनो सेनासु योत्स्यमानाः प्रहारिणः॥
en: Of men five times fifty constituted a Patti and three Pattis make a Senamukha which is also called a Gulma. Three Gulmas make a Gana, and there were tens thousands of Ganas in the army of Duryodhana, each competent to fight and each a smiter.

sn: तत्र राजा शूरान् बुद्धिमतो नरान्। प्रसमीक्ष्य महाबाहुश्चक्रे सेनापतींस्तदा॥
en: The king Duryodhana, of long arms selecting men who were wise and also heroes, made them leaders of his army.

sn: पृथगक्षौहिणीनां च प्रणेतृन् नरसत्तमान्। विधिवत् पूर्वमानीय पार्थिवानभ्यभाषत॥
en: Having those best among men the leaders of his Akshauhinis brought before them with suitable honour he spoke to them separately.

sn: कृपं द्रोण च शल्यं च सैन्धवं च जयद्रथम्। सुदक्षिणं च काम्बोजं कृतवर्माणमेव च।॥
en: Kripa, Drona, Shalya, Saindhava, Jayadratha, Sudakshina, and Kamboja, and Kritavarman,

sn: द्रोणपुत्रं च कर्णं च भूरिश्रवसमेव च। शकुनि सौबलं चैव बाह्रीकं च महाबलम्॥
en: The son of Drona, Bhurishravas, Shakuni, the son of Subala and Balhika endued with great strength.

sn: दिवसे दिवसे तेषां प्रतिवेलं च भारत। चक्रे स विविधाः पूजाः प्रत्यक्षं च पुनः पुनः॥
en: All of these, O Bharata, he used to bring before him daily for consultation and looked to them himself and offered them due honour.

sn: तथा विनियताः सर्वे ये च तेषां पदानुगाः। बभूवुः सैनिका राज्ञां प्रियं राज्ञश्चिकीर्षवः॥
en: These men being thus treated with respect, and those foot soldiers who constituted the army of the king Duryodhana became desirous of doing what was beneficial to that king.

description: Appointment of Bhishma to the generalship,
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततः शान्तनवं भीष्मं प्राञ्जलिधृतराष्ट्रजः। सह सर्वैर्महीपालैरिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Then did the son of Dhritarashtra, with clasped hands, along with all these rulers of the earth, say these words to Bhishma, the son of Shantanu.

description: Appointment of Bhishma to the generalship,
sn: ऋते सेनाप्रणेतारं पृतना सुमहत्यपि। दीर्यते युद्धमासाद्य पिपीलिकपुटं यथा॥
en: “Without a (suitable) leader of the army even a large army is broken up when engaged in battle like a swarm of ants.

description: Appointment of Bhishma to the generalship,
sn: न हि जातु द्वयोर्बुद्धिः समा भवति कर्हिचित्। शौर्यं च बलनेतृणां स्पर्धते च परस्परम्॥
en: The opinions of two seldom agree besides the leaders of hosts are jealous of one another regarding their own prowess.

description: Appointment of Bhishma to the generalship,
sn: श्रूयते च महाप्राज्ञ हैहयानमितौजसः। अभ्ययुर्ब्राह्मणाः सर्वे समुच्छ्रितकुशध्वजाः॥
en: It is heard, O you of great wisdom, that all the Brahmanas having assembled together, hoisted up their flag of Kusha and proclaimed war with the Haihayas of immeasurable energy.

description: Appointment of Bhishma to the generalship,
sn: तानभ्ययुस्तदा वैश्याः शूद्राश्चैव पितामह। एकतस्तु त्रयो वर्णा एकतः क्षत्रियर्षभाः॥
en: They were joined. O grandfather, by the Vaishyas and Sudras. There were thus on one side three orders and those best among the Kshatriyas on the other.

description: Appointment of Bhishma to the generalship,
sn: ततो युद्धेष्वभज्यन्त त्रयो वर्णाः पुनः पुनः। क्षत्रियाच जयन्त्येव बहुलं चैकतो बलम्॥
en: The three orders broke up again and again in the battle that followed and the Kshatriyas were victorious over that large army though they were alone.

description: Appointment of Bhishma to the generalship,
sn: ततस्ते क्षत्रियानेव पप्रच्छुर्द्विजसत्तमाः। तेभ्यः शशंसुर्धर्मज्ञा याथातथ्यं पितामह॥
en: Then did these best among the twice-born asked the Kshatriya the cause of his and O grandfather, and those men conversant with virtue told them the truth.

description: Appointment of Bhishma to the generalship,
sn: वयमेकस्य शृण्वानां महाबुद्धिमतो रणे। भवन्तस्तु पृथक् सर्वे स्वबुद्धिवशवर्तिनः॥
en: "In battle we listen to the commands of any one person who is the wisest among us, but you are separated and follow your individual whims,

description: Appointment of Bhishma to the generalship,
sn: ततस्ते ब्राह्मणाश्चनुरेकं सेनापतिं द्विजम्। नये सुकुशलं शूरमजयन् क्षत्रियांस्ततः॥
en: Then did those best among the Brahmanas make one among the twice-born the leader of their army, who was skillful in diplomacy and then did they win a victory ever the Kshatriyas

description: Appointment of Bhishma to the generalship,
sn: एवं ये कुशलं शूरं हितेप्सितमकल्मषम्। सेनापतिं प्रकुर्वन्ति ते जयन्ति रणे रिपून्॥
en: In the same way those, who appoint a skillful hero who has the good of his party at heart as the leader of the army, vanquish their enemies in battle.

description: Appointment of Bhishma to the generalship,
sn: भवानुशनसा तुल्यो हितैषी च सदा मम। असंहार्यः स्थितो धर्म स नः सेनापतिर्भव॥
en: You are equal to Ushanas himself and over wish me well and follow a righteous course from which you never fall off. Therefore do you become a general.

description: Appointment of Bhishma to the generalship,
sn: रश्मिवतामिवादित्यो वीस्थामिव चन्द्रमाः। कुबेर इव यक्षाणां देवानामिव वासवः॥
en: You are as the sun is among the luminous bodies, the moon among deciduous herbs, Kubera among the Yakshas, Vasava among the gods,

description: Appointment of Bhishma to the generalship,
sn: पर्वतानां यथा मेरुः सुपर्णः पक्षिणां यथा। कुमार इव देवानां वसूनामिव हव्यवाट्॥
en: Meru among the mountains, Suparna among the birds, Kumara among the gods, Indra among the Vasus.

description: Appointment of Bhishma to the generalship,
sn: भवता हि वयं गुप्ताः शक्रेणेव दिवौकसः। अनाधृष्या भविष्यामस्त्रिदशानामपि ध्रुवम्॥
en: Protected by you we will be as the gods protected by Shakra and we shall surely be invincible even by the denizens of heaven.

description: Appointment of Bhishma to the generalship,
sn: प्रयातु नो भवानग्रे देवानामिव पावकिः। वयं त्वामनुयास्यामः सौरभेया इवर्षभम्॥
en: You march in our front as the son of Agni (Kumara) among the gods and we shall follow you like calves following a cow.

description: Appointment of Bhishma to the generalship,
sn: भीष्म उवाच एवमेतन्महाबाहो यथा वदसि भारत। यथैव हि भवन्तो मे तथैव मम पाण्डवाः॥
en: Bhishma said It is as you say, O Bharata, O you of long arms but as you are to me so are the Pandavas.

description: Appointment of Bhishma to the generalship,
sn: अपि चैव मया श्रेयो वाच्यं तेषां नराधिप। संयोद्धव्यं तवार्थाय यथा मे समयः कृतः॥
en: And it is also my duty to look after their welfare, O ruler of men; but I shall fight on your behalf since I have promised it.

description: Appointment of Bhishma to the generalship,
sn: न तु पश्यामि योद्धारमात्मन: सदृशं भुवि। ऋते तस्मान्नरव्याघ्रात् कुन्तीपुत्राद् धनंजयात्॥
en: I do not see any soldier equal to me in this world save that best among men Dhananjaya, the son of Kunti.

description: Appointment of Bhishma to the generalship,
sn: स हि वेद महाबुद्धिर्दिव्यान्यस्त्राण्यनेकशः। न तु मां विवृतो युद्धे जातु युध्येत पाण्डवः॥
en: He (Arjuna) is a man of great wisdom and knows the use of celestial weapons and many other weapons but that son of Pandu will never encounter me in open fight.

description: Appointment of Bhishma to the generalship,
sn: अहं चैव क्षणेनैव निर्मनुष्यमिदं जगत्। कुर्यां शस्त्रबलेनैव ससुरासुरराक्षसम्॥
en: I, in a moment, shall make this world destitute of men, gods, Asuras and Rakshasas by the strength of my weapons.

description: Appointment of Bhishma to the generalship,
sn: न त्वेवोत्सादनीया मे पाण्डोः पुत्रा जनाधिप। तस्माद् योधान् हनिष्यामि प्रयोगेणायुतं सदा॥
en: But these sons of Pandu ought not to be slain by me, O ruler of men; therefore shall I slay ten thousand warriors every day.

description: Appointment of Bhishma to the generalship,
sn: एवमेषां करिष्यामि निधनं कुरुनन्दन। न चेत् ते मां हनिष्यन्ति पूर्वमेव समागमे॥
en: In this way, shall I bring on their end o delighter of the Kuru race, if indeed they do not kill me before I have time to carry out my desire in the battle.

description: Appointment of Bhishma to the generalship,
sn: सेनापतिस्त्वहं राजन् समये नापरेण ते। भविष्यामि यथाकामं तन्मे श्रोतुमिहार्हसि॥
en: But there is another condition on which I shall be the leader of your army; that desire which I have in my heart it is proper that you should hear of.

description: Appointment of Bhishma to the generalship,
sn: कर्णो वा युध्यतां पूर्वमहं वा पृथिवीपते। स्पर्धते हि सदात्यर्थं सूतपुत्रो मया रणे॥
en: Either let Karna fight first or myself, O lord of the earth. The son of the Suta always compares his prowess in battle with mine,

description: Appointment of Bhishma to the generalship,
sn: कर्ण उवाच नाहं जीवति गाङ्गेये राजन् योत्स्ये कथंचन। हते भीष्मे तु योत्स्यामि सह गाण्डीवधन्वना॥
en: Karria said So long as the son of Ganga is alive I shall never fight, O king; when Bhishma is slain, I shall fight with him who wields the Gandiva bow.

description: Appointment of Bhishma to the generalship,
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततः सेनापतिं चक्रे विधिवद् भूरिदक्षिणम्। धृतराष्ट्रात्मजो भीष्मं सोऽभिषिक्तो व्यरोचत॥
en: Vaishampayana said Then did the son of Dhritarashtra make Bhishma, who had made liberal gifts, the commander of his army, and he too being duly installed blazed forth.

description: Appointment of Bhishma to the generalship,
sn: ततो भेरीश्च शङ्खांश्च शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः। वादयामासुरव्यग्रा वादका राजशासनात्॥
en: Drums and conches were then sounded by hundreds and thousands by eager musicians by command of the king,

description: Appointment of Bhishma to the generalship,
sn: सिंहनादाश्च विविधा वाहनानां च निःस्वनाः। प्रादुरासन्ननभ्रे च वर्षं रुधिरकर्दमम्॥
en: There were also roars like those of lions and several other sorts of roars among the army; and though there were no clouds in the sky there was a down pour of blood which made the ground full of mire.

description: Appointment of Bhishma to the generalship,
sn: निर्घाताः पृथिवीकम्पा कजबंहितनिःस्वनाः। आसंश्च सर्वयोधानां पातयन्तो मनांस्युत॥
en: There were also earthquakes and whirlwinds and roars made by elephants which succeeded in casting a shade on the minds of all warriors.

description: Appointment of Bhishma to the generalship,
sn: वाचश्चाप्यशरीरिण्यो दिवश्चोल्काः प्रपेदिरे। शिवाश्च भयवेदिन्यो नेदुर्दीप्ततरा भृशम्॥
en: There were also incorporeal voices and meteors shot forth the heavens and jackals began to make frightful howls and the cardinal points seemed ablaze.

description: Appointment of Bhishma to the generalship,
sn: सैनापत्ये यदा राजा गाङ्गेयमभिषिक्तवान्। तदैतान्युग्ररूपाणि बभूवुः शतशो नृप।॥
en: When the king installed the son of Ganga in the generalship these frightful sights appeared in hundreds, O ruler of men.

description: Appointment of Bhishma to the generalship,
sn: ततः सेनापति कृत्वा भीष्मं परबलार्दनम्। वाचयित्वा द्विजश्रेष्ठान् गोभिर्निष्कैश्च भूरिश;॥
en: Then having appointed, Bhishma the grinder of the enemies' hosts, as the general and having made liberal presents of cows and gold to the foremost among the twice born.

description: Appointment of Bhishma to the generalship,
sn: वर्धमानो जयाशीभिर्निर्ययौ सैनिकैर्वृतः। आपगेयं पुरस्कृत्य भ्रातृभिः सहितस्तदा।॥
en: He marched forth with the blessings of those Brahmanas glorifying him, surrounded by his army placing Bhishma at the head of his host and accompanied by his brothers.

description: Appointment of Bhishma to the generalship,
sn: स्कन्धावारेण महता कुरुक्षेत्रं जगाम ह॥
en: And with a large army he went to Kurukshetra.

description: Appointment of Bhishma to the generalship,
sn: परिक्रम्य कुरुक्षेत्रं कर्णेन सह कौरवः। शिबिरं मापयामास समे देशे जनाधिप।॥
en: The of Kuru having traversed Kurukshetra in company with Karna placed his camps in a plain, O ruler of men,

description: Appointment of Bhishma to the generalship,
sn: मधुरानूषरे देशे प्रभूतयवसेन्धने। यथैव हास्तिनपुरं तद्वच्छिबिरमाबभौ॥
en: In a part which was also charming and without sands and abounded, fuel and fodder. The encampment then shone forth as the city of Hastina. son

description: Journey of Balarama to the sacred places
sn: जनमेजय उवाच आपगेयं महात्मानं भीष्मं शस्त्रभृतां वरम्। पितामहं भारतानां ध्वजं सर्वमहीक्षिताम्।।।।
en: Janamejaya said The great-souled Bhishma, the foremost among all wielders of weapons, the grandfather of the Bharatas, the flag as it were of all the rulers of the earth,

description: Journey of Balarama to the sacred places
sn: बृहस्पतिसमं बुद्ध्या क्षमया पृथिवीससम्। समुद्रमिव गाम्भीर्ये हिमवन्तमिव स्थिरम्॥
en: In intelligence equal to Brihaspati, in power equal to the earth, in gravity equal to the sea, in calmness equal to the Himavat,

description: Journey of Balarama to the sacred places
sn: प्रजापतिमिवौदार्ये तेजसा भास्करोपमम्। महेन्द्रमिव शत्रूणां ध्वंसनं शरवृष्टिभिः॥
en: In generosity equal to the lord of all creatures, in effulgence equal to the sun, and in destroying the enemies by downpours of arrows equal to great Indra,

description: Journey of Balarama to the sacred places
sn: रणयज्ञे प्रवितते सुभीमे लोमहर्षणे। दीक्षितं चिररात्राय श्रुत्वा तत्र युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Was employed for life as the chief priest of that sacrifice of battle, which was fierce and hair-stirring. Healing this what did Yudhishthira,

description: Journey of Balarama to the sacred places
sn: किमब्रवीन्महाबाहुः सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वरः। भीमसेनार्जुनो वापि कृष्णो वा प्रत्यभाषत॥
en: Of long arms, the foremost among all wielders of weapons, say and what did Bhimasena and Arjuna and what did Krishna say?

description: Journey of Balarama to the sacred places
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच आपद्धर्मार्थकुशलो महाबुद्धियुधिष्ठिरः। सर्वान् भ्रातृन् समानीय वासुदेवं च शाश्वतम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Yudhishthira, who was skillful in virtue and worldly profit especially in seasons of calamities, having summoned together all his brothers as also the eternal Vasudeva,

description: Journey of Balarama to the sacred places
sn: उवाच वदतां श्रेष्ठः सान्त्वपूर्वमिदं वचः। पर्याक्रामत सैन्यानि यत्तास्तिष्ठत दंशिताः॥
en: That foremost of speakers said these words in a calm spirit: “Go round the army and remain watchful being clad in mail.

description: Journey of Balarama to the sacred places
sn: पितामहेन वो युद्धं पूर्वमेव भविष्यति। तस्मात् सप्तसु सेनासु प्रणेतॄन् मम पश्यत॥
en: Our first encounter will be with our grandfather, therefore do you look for the seven leaders of my army.

description: Journey of Balarama to the sacred places
sn: कृष्ण उवाच यथार्हति भवान् वक्तुमस्मिन् काले झुपस्थिते। तथेदमर्थवद् वाक्यमुक्तं ते भरतर्षभ॥
en: Krishna said By you, O best among the race of Bharatas, have these words pregnant with meaning been said, which indeed are proper in these circumstances which have presented themselves.

description: Journey of Balarama to the sacred places
sn: रोचते मे महाबाहो क्रियतां यदनन्तरम्। नायकास्तव सेनायां क्रियन्तामिह सप्त वै॥
en: All this I approve of, O you of long arms, and now do what ought to be done; select seven leaders for your army.

description: Journey of Balarama to the sacred places
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततो दुपदमानाय्य विराटं शिनिपुङ्गवम्। धृष्टद्युम्नं च पाञ्चाल्यं धृष्टकेतुं च पार्थिव॥
en: Vaishampayana said Then summoning before him Drupada, Virata, and that best among the Shini race, and Dhrishtadyumna the prince of Panchala, and the ruler of the earth Dhrishtaketu,

description: Journey of Balarama to the sacred places
sn: शिखण्डिनं च पाञ्चाल्यं सहदेवं च मागधम्। एतान् सप्त महाभागान् वीरान् युद्धाभिकांक्षिणः॥
en: Shikhandin, the prince of Panchala Sahadeva and the king of Magadha summoning these seven heroes of great attributes who were anxious for war,

description: Journey of Balarama to the sacred places
sn: सेनाप्रणेतन् विधिवदभ्यषिञ्चद् युधिष्ठिरः। सर्वेसेनापतिं चात्र धृष्टद्युम्नं चकार ह॥
en: Yudhishthira duly installed them as the leaders of his army and made Dhrishtadyumna the general commander of all.

description: Journey of Balarama to the sacred places
sn: द्रोणान्तहेतोरुत्पन्नो य इद्धाज्जातवेदसः। सर्वेषामेव तेषां तु समस्तानां महात्मनाम्॥
en: This Dhrishtadyumna, who was destined to be the cause of the end of Drona, was born of the blazing sacrificial fire. And over all these great souled men assembled together,

description: Journey of Balarama to the sacred places
sn: सेनापतिपतिं चक्रे गुडाकेशं धनंजयम्। अर्जुनस्यापि नेता च संयन्ता चैव वाजिनाम्॥
en: Dhananjaya of curling hairs was made the general; and the guide of Arjuna and the driver of his horses,

description: Journey of Balarama to the sacred places
sn: संकर्षणानुजः श्रीमान् महाबुद्धिर्जनार्दनः। तद् दृष्ट्वोपस्थितं युद्धं समासन्नं महात्ययम्॥
en: Was the younger brother of Sankarashana, Janardana of great intelligence, endued with great beauty. Then seeing that a great battle : was near at hand,

description: Journey of Balarama to the sacred places
sn: प्राविशद् भवनं राजन् पाण्डवानां हलायुधः। सहाक्रूरप्रभृतिभिर्गदसाम्बोद्धवादिभिः॥
en: The one, who had the slough for his। weapon (elder brother of Krishna), entered the encampment of the Pandavas, o king, in company with Akrura, Akrura, Gadha, Samba, Uddahava,

description: Journey of Balarama to the sacred places
sn: रौक्मिणेयाहुकसुतैश्चारुदेष्णपुरोगमैः। वृष्णिमुख्यैरधिगतैर्व्याधैरिव बलोत्कटैः॥
en: And the son of Rukmini (Pradyumna) and the son of Ahuka and Charudeshna and others, Surrounded and protected by those foremost of the Vrishni race like a hard of powerful tigers,

description: Journey of Balarama to the sacred places
sn: अभिगुप्तो महाबाहुर्मरुद्भिरिव वासवः। नीलकौशेयवसनः कैलासशिखरोपमः॥
en: The one of long arms like Vasava protected by Maruts with blue garments on and looking majestic as the peak of the Kailasa,

description: Journey of Balarama to the sacred places
sn: सिंहखेलगतिः श्रीमान् मदरक्तान्तलोचनः। तं दृष्ट्वा धर्मराजश्च केशवश्च महाद्युतिः॥
en: With the gait of a sporting lion, endued with beauty and with eyes having the ends reddened by drinking wine (entered there. Seeing him, the virtuous king and Keshava of great effulgence,

description: Journey of Balarama to the sacred places
sn: उदतिष्ठत् ततः पार्थो भीमकर्मा वृकोदरः। गाण्डीवधन्वा ये चान्ये राजानस्तत्र केचन॥
en: Rose up from their seats as also did the son of Pritha, and Vrikodara of fierce deeds and the wielder of the Gandiva bow and the other kings that were there.

description: Journey of Balarama to the sacred places
sn: पूजयांचक्रिरे ते वै समायान्तं हलायुधम्। ततस्तं पाण्डवो राजा करे पस्पर्श पाणिना॥
en: And they assembled together did worship the approaching Halayudha. Then did the Pandava king touch him in the hand by his own hands.

description: Journey of Balarama to the sacred places
sn: वासुदेवपुरोगास्तं सर्व एवाभ्यवादयन्। विराटद्रुपदौ वृद्धावभिवाद्य हलायुधः॥
en: And all those kings with Vasudeva at their head greeting him, Halayudha too saluted Virata and Drupada and those who were aged.

description: Journey of Balarama to the sacred places
sn: युधिष्ठिरेण सहित उपाविशदरिंदमः। ततस्तेषुपविष्टेषु पार्थिवेषु समन्ततः। वासुदेवमभिप्रेक्ष्य रौहिणेयोऽभ्यभाषतः॥
en: That chastiser of foes then sat down with Yudhishthira and the son of Rohini then said, with his eyes on Vasudeva, to those rulers of the earth seated together.

description: Journey of Balarama to the sacred places
sn: भविताऽयं महारौद्रो दारुणः पुरुषक्षयः। दिष्टमेतद् ध्रुवं मन्ये न शक्यमतिवर्तितुम्॥
en: There will be a very fierce and harsh massacre of men, it is ordained by the fate surely, I think, and cannot be avoided.

description: Journey of Balarama to the sacred places
sn: तस्माद् युद्धात् समुत्तीर्णानपि वः ससुहृज्जनान्। अरोगानक्षतैर्देष्टाऽस्मीति मतिर्ममा॥
en: And I entertain the hope that I shall see you come out of that battle along with your well wishers without any disease, and without any scars on your persons.

description: Journey of Balarama to the sacred places
sn: समेतं पार्थिवं क्षत्रं कालपक्कमसंशयम्। विमर्दश्च महान् भावी मांसशोणितकर्दमः॥
en: All these Kshatriyas, these rulers of the earth have their hour come and there will be a great massacre which will make the earth one mass of clay of flesh and blood.

description: Journey of Balarama to the sacred places
sn: उक्तो मया वासुदेवः पुनः पुनरुपह्वरे। सम्बन्धिषु समां वृत्तिं वर्तस्व मधुसूदनः॥
en: Vasudeva was thus addressed by me again and again in private: “Behave with impartiality to those who are equally related to you, O slayer of Madhu.

description: Journey of Balarama to the sacred places
sn: पाण्डवा हि यथाऽस्माकं तथा दुर्योधनो नृपः। तस्यापि क्रियतां साह्यं स पर्येति पुनः पुनः॥
en: As the sons of Pandu are to us, so is that ruler of men Duryodhana; and do you therefore help him also for he applied for it again and again.

description: Journey of Balarama to the sacred places
sn: तच मे नाकरोद् वाक्यं त्वदर्थं मधुसूदनः। निर्विष्टः सर्वभावेन धनंजयमवेक्ष्य ह॥
en: For your sake, however, did the slayer of Madhu, not act up to my words. He has with all his heart set himself to your interests, with his eye on the interests of Dhananjaya.

description: Journey of Balarama to the sacred places
sn: ध्रुवो जयः पाण्डवानामिति मे निश्चिता मतिः। तथा ह्यभिनिवेशोऽयं वासुदेवस्य भारत।॥
en: Victory will surely come to the sons of Pandu; such is my opinion, for such is the purpose of Vasudeva.

description: Journey of Balarama to the sacred places
sn: न चाहमुत्सहे कृष्णमृते लोकमुदीक्षितुम्। ततोऽहमनुवामि केशवस्य चिकीर्षितम्॥
en: I do not dare to look on this world separated from Krishna and therefore shall I remain inactive in what Krishna wishes.

description: Journey of Balarama to the sacred places
sn: उभौ शिष्यौ हि मे वीरौ गदायुद्धविशारदौ। दुल्यस्नेहोऽस्म्यतो भीमे तथा दुर्योधने नृपे॥
en: Both of these heroes, well skilled in fighting with maces, are my pupils and I bear the same affection for Duryodhana as for that ruler of men Bhima.

description: Journey of Balarama to the sacred places
sn: तस्माद् यास्यामि तीर्थानि सरस्वत्या निषेवितुम्। न हि शक्ष्यामि कौरव्यान् नश्यमानानुपेक्षितुम्॥
en: Therefore shall I now go to make a pilgrimage to the sacred places on the banks of the Sarasvati for I shall not be able to look on with indifference at this massacre of the Kurus.

description: Journey of Balarama to the sacred places
sn: एवमुक्त्वा महाबाहुरनुज्ञातश्च पाण्डवैः। तीर्थयात्रां ययौ रामो निर्वर्त्य मधुसूदनम्॥
en: The one of long arms, Rama saying this with the leave of the sons of Pandava, went to visit the holy places making the slayer of Madhu return, (he had accompanied him for some distance)

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु भीष्मकस्य महात्मनः। हिरण्यरोम्णो नृपतेः साक्षादीन्द्रसखस्य वै॥ आकृतीनामधिपतिर्भोजस्यातियशस्विनः। दाक्षिणात्यपतेः पुत्रो दिक्षु रुक्मीति विश्रुतः॥
en: Vaishampayana said 1-At this time did there come to the encampment of the Pandavas, the son of the great souled Bhishmaka, otherwise called the king Hiranya Roman, who was the friend of Indra himself, who was the very renowned ruler of the Bhojas, and who was the lord of the entire southern countries. His son was known in all countries by the name of Rukmi, ever devoted to truth,

sn: यः किंपुरुषसिंहस्य गन्धमादनवासिनः। कृत्स्नं शिष्यो धनुर्वेदं चतुष्पादमवाप्तवान्॥
en: Who was a pupil of that lion of the Kimpurushas living on the Gandhamadana mountain and who learnt from him the entire science of handling bows in all its four branches;

sn: यो माहेन्द्रं धनुलेंभे तुल्यं गाण्डीवतेजसा। शाङ्गेण च महाबाहुः सम्मितं दिव्यलक्षणम्॥
en: Who, having long arms, obtained the Vijaya bow of the great Indra himself which was equal in energy to the Gandiva and to the Sharanga which had celestial attributes in it.

sn: त्रीण्येवैतानि दिव्यानि धनूंषि दिविचारिणाम्। वारुणं गाण्डिवं तत्र माहेन्द्रं विजयं धनुः। शाएं तु वैष्णवं प्राहुर्दिव्यं तेजोमयं धनुः॥
en: These were the three celestial bows of the denizens of heaven namely, Gandiva belonging to Varuna, Vijaya belonging to the great Indra and Sharanga the bow of Vishnu, having celestial energy.

sn: धारयामास तत् कृष्णः परसेनाभयावहम्। गाण्डीवं पावकाल्लेभे खाण्डवे पाकशासनिः॥
en: Krishna obtained that bow which struck terror to the soldiers of the enemies. The son of Indra (Arjuna) obtained the Gandiva from the fire on the occasion of burning the Khandava.

sn: द्रुमाद् रुक्मी महातेजा विजयं प्रत्यपद्यत। संछिद्य मौरवान् पाशान् निहत्य मुरमोजसा॥
en: Rukmi of great energy, obtained the Vijaya from Druma after breaking open the knots and nooses of Mura and slaying Asura by his own energy.

sn: निर्जित्य नरकं भौममाहृत्य मणिकुण्डले। षोडश स्त्रीसहस्राणि रत्नानि विविधानि च॥
en: And subjugating Naraka the son of Bhumi (earth) while recovering the jeweled ear-rings and sixteen thousand damsels and diverse sorts of gems,

sn: प्रतिपेदे हृषीकेशः शार्ङ्ग च धनुरुत्तमम्। रुक्मी तु विजयं लब्ध्वा धनुर्मेघनिभस्वनम्॥
en: Hrishikesha obtained that excellent bow the Sharanga. Rukmi, obtaining that bow called Vijaya whose twang was like the roaring of the clouds.

sn: विभीषयन्निव जगत् पाण्डवानभ्यवर्तत। नामृष्यत पुरा योऽसौ स्वबाहुबलगर्वितः॥
en: Came to the Pandavas as if terrifying the earth. The hero, proud of the strength of his own arms, could not pass, in silence before,

sn: रुक्मिण्या हरणं वीरो वासुदेवेन धीमता। कृत्वा प्रतिज्ञा नाहत्वा निवर्तिष्ये जनार्दनम्॥
en: The ravishment of Rukmini (his sister) by the wise Vasudeva; and having resolved "I shall not return without slaying Janardana,"

sn: ततोऽन्वधावद् वार्ष्णेयं सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वरः। सेनया चतुरङ्गिण्या महत्या दूरपातया॥ सैन्येन महता
en: The foremost among wielders of weapons came in pursuit of the scion of Vrishni race, with army having all the four divisions, which occupied a large tract of land as it proceeded,

sn: विचित्रायुधवर्मिण्या गङ्गयेव प्रवृद्धया। स समासाद्य वार्ष्णेयं योगानामीश्वरं प्रभुम्॥
en: And furnished with diverse sorts of amours and weapons resembled the Ganga when full. He, then coming to that scion of the Vrishni race who is the lord, the object of all devotion,

sn: व्यंसितोव्रीडितो राजन् नाजगाम स कुण्डिनम्। यत्रैव कृष्णेन रणे निर्जितः परवीरहा॥
en: Was defeated by him and was thus put to shame. And he returned not, O king, to Kundina, his capital, since that slayer of hostile heroes, Krishna, was not defeated by him in battle.

sn: तत्र भोजकटं नाम कृतं नगरमुत्तमम्। तेनं प्रभूतगजवाजिना॥
en: There he built an excellent city called Bhojakata furnished with a large army and plenty of elephants and horses.

sn: पुरं तद् भुवि विख्यातं नाम्ना भोजकटं नृप। स भोजराजः सैन्येन महता परिवारितः॥
en: That city became famous by the name of Bhojakata, O ruler of men. That king of the Bhojas surrounded by a large army,

sn: अक्षौहिण्या महावीर्यः पाण्डवान् क्षिप्रमागमत्। ततः स कवची धन्वी तली खड़ी शरासनी॥
en: Numbering an Akshauhini and endued with great prowess soon came to the son of Pandu. Then did he, clad in a coat of mail and armed with bow, fencer, sword and quivers,

sn: ध्वजेनादित्यवर्णेन विदितः पाण्डवेयानां वासुदेवप्रियेप्सया॥
en: With a slandered of the hue of the sun, entered into the large army and become known to the sons of Pandu through his desire of doing what was acceptable to Vasudeva.

sn: युधिष्ठिरस्तु तं राजा प्रत्युद्गम्याभायपूजयत्। स पूजितः पाण्डुपुत्रैर्यथान्यायं सुसंस्तुतः॥
en: The king Yudhishthira, too, offered him worship after advancing a little; and he, being

sn: प्रविवेश महाचमूम्। न
en: worshipped and praised by the son of Pandu as became his station and rank,

sn: प्रतिगृह्य तु तान् सर्वान् विश्रान्तः सहसैनिकः। उवाच मध्य वीराणां कुन्तीपुत्रं धनंजयम्॥
en: Saluted those kings in return; and after resting himself with his army he said, in the midst of those heroes, to Dhananjaya the son of Kunti.

sn: सहायोऽस्मि स्थितोयुद्धे यदि भीतोऽसि पाण्डवा करिष्यामि रणे साह्यमसह्यं तव शत्रुभिः॥
en: If, O son of Pandu, you are afraid on the eve of the war I shall afford you assistance. The assistance, I will give, cannot possibly be borne by your enemies.

sn: हि मे विक्रमे तुल्यः पुमानस्तीह कश्चन। हनिष्यामि रणे भागं यन्मे दास्यसि पाण्डवा॥
en: There is no man in this world who is equal to me in prowess. I shall slay in battle that portion of your enemy you will allot to my share,

sn: अपि द्रोणकृपौ वीरौ भीष्मकर्णावथो पुनः। अथवा सर्व एवैते तिष्ठन्तु वसुधाधिपाः॥
en: Even including Drona and Kripa, or the heroes Bhishma or Kuru or all those rulers of the earth assembled together even, if they stand against you.

sn: निहत्य समरे शत्रूस्तव दास्यामि मेदिनीम्। इत्युक्तो धर्मराजस्य केशवस्य च संनिधौ।॥
en: (Even then) having slain in battle your enemies I shall make over the earth to you. Being thus spoken to in the presence of the virtuous king Keshava,

sn: शृण्वतां पार्थिवेन्द्राणामन्येषां चैव सर्वशः। वासुदेवमभिप्रेक्ष्य धर्मराजं च पाण्डवम्॥
en: And in the hearing of those chief among the rulers of the earth, and all others who were there and with his eyes on Vasudeva and on the virtuous king the son of Pandu,

sn: उवाच धीमान् कौन्तेयः प्रहस्य सखिपूर्वकम्। कौरवाणां कुले जातः पाण्डोः पुत्रो विशेषतः॥
en: The son of Kunti said laughingly in a friendly way. “Born in the race of Kurus, especially being the son Pandu,

sn: द्रोणं व्यपदिशशिष्यो वासुदेवसहायवान्। भीतोऽस्मीति कथं ब्रूयां दधानो गाण्डिवं धनुः॥
en: Calling myself the pupil of Drona and getting the help of Vasudeva, how can I say that I am afraid especially as I hold the Gandiva bow?

sn: युध्यमानस्य मे वीर गन्धर्वैः सुमहाबलैः। सहायो घोषयात्रायां कस्तदाऽऽसीत् सखा मम॥
en: O hero, when fighting with the great army of Gandharvas in the battle, who was then my friend?

sn: तथा प्रतिभये तस्मिन् देवदानवसंकुले। खाण्डवे युध्यमानस्य कः सहायस्तदाऽवत्॥
en: Then again in that terrific battle between the gods and the Danavas fighting together at Khandava who was then my friend?

sn: निवातकवचैर्युद्धे कालकेयैश्च दानवैः। तत्र मे युध्यमानस्य कः सहायस्तदाऽवत्॥
en: In my fight with the Nivatakavachas or with the Danavas called Kalakeyais-who was iny friend?

sn: तथा विराटनगरे कुरुभिः सह संगरे। युध्यतो बहुभिस्तत्र कः सहायोऽभवन्मम॥
en: Then again in the battle with Kurus in the city of Virat-who was my friend?

sn: उपजीव्य रणे रुद्रं शक्रं वैश्रवणं यमम्। वरुणं पावकं चैव कृपं द्रोणं च माधवम्॥
en: Having paid homage to Rudra, Shakra, Vaishravana, Yama, Varuna, Agni, Kripa, Drona and Madhava,

sn: धारयन् गाण्डिवं दिव्यं धनुस्तेजोमयं दृढम्। अक्षय्यशरसंयुक्तो दिव्यास्त्रपरिबृहितः॥
en: And holding firmly the celestial bow the Gandiva and furnished with an inexhaustible mass of arrows and protected by celestial weapons,

sn: कथमस्मद्विधो ब्रूयाद् भीतोऽस्मीति यशोहरम्। वचनं नरशार्दूल वज्रायुधमपि स्वयम्॥
en: How can one like myself say 'I am afraid” calculated to cast infamy on my name, to even Indra himself who has the thunderbolt for his weapon, O best among men.

sn: नास्मि भीतो महाबाहो सहायार्थश्च नास्ति मे। यथाकामं यथायोगं गच्छ वाऽन्यत्र तिष्ठ वा॥
en: I am not afraid, O you of long arms and I have no necessity for your assistance. Go elsewhere if you please, or remain here if you like.

sn: विनिवर्त्य ततो रुक्मी सेनां सागरसंनिभाम्। दुर्योधनमुपागच्छत् तथैव भरतर्षभ॥
en: Then Rukmi, returning with that army resembling these came to Duryodhana and spoke in the same strain, O Bharata.

sn: तथैव चाभिगम्यैनमुवाच वसुधाधिपः प्रत्याख्यातश्च तेनापि स तदा शूरमानिना॥
en: Coming to that ruler of the earth did he say the same thing and his help was refused by Duryodhana too who thought himself a hero.

sn: द्वावेव तु महाराज तस्माद् युद्धादपेयतुः। रौहिणेयश्च वार्ष्णेयो रुक्मी च वसुधाधिपः॥
en: Thus two parties, O great king did not take part in that battle, namely the son of Rohini, the scion of the Vrishni race and the ruler of the earth Rukmi.

sn: गते रामे तीर्थयात्रां भीष्मकस्य सुते तथा। उपाविशन् पाण्डवेया मन्त्राय पुनरेव च॥
en: Rama having gone to visit the sacred places and the son of Bhishmaka having returned in the manner just described the sons of Pandu again sat down for consolation.

sn: समितिधर्मराजस्य सा पार्थिवसमाकुला। शुशुभे तारकैश्चित्रा द्यौश्चन्द्रेणेव भारत॥
en: The assembly, of the virtuous king with all the rulers of the earth, shone as the moon in the sky surrounded by diverse stars, O Bharata.

sn: जनमेजय उवाय तथा व्यूढेष्वनीकेषु कुरुक्षेत्रे द्विजर्षभ। किमकुर्वश्च कुरवः कालेनाभिप्रचोदिताः॥
en: Janamejaya said The army having then been prepared in order for battle, O best among the Bharatas, what did the sons of Kuru, urged as they were by destiny itself, do?

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तथा व्यूढेष्वनीकेषु यत्तेषु भरतर्षभ। धृतराष्ट्रो महाराज संजयं वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
en: Vaishampayana said The army having been prepared in order for battle, 0 Bharata, the great king Dhritarashtra said these words to Sanjaya.

sn: एहि संजय सर्वं मे आचक्ष्वानवशेषतः। सेनानिवेशे यद् वृत्तं कुरुपाण्डवसेनयोः॥
en: “Come, O Sanjaya, and tell me everything in detail of the steps taken in the matter of encamping the army of the Kurus and the Pandavas.

sn: दिष्टमेव परं मन्ये पौरुषं चाप्यनर्थकम्। यदहं बुद्ध्यमानोऽपियुद्धदोषान् क्षयोदयान्॥
en: In my opinion luck is the more important factor, manliness and prowess being vain and useless; since I though understanding the disadvantages of war which gives rise only to decay and ruin,

sn: तथापि निकृतिप्रज्ञं पुत्रं दुर्दूतदेविनम्। न शक्नोमि नियन्तुं वा कर्तुं वा हितमात्मनः॥
en: Can not yet retain my son who considers folly to be wisdom and who is addicted to gambling, and cannot thus effect my own good.

sn: भवत्येव हि मे सूत बुद्धिर्दोषानुदर्शिनी। दुर्योधनं समासाद्य पुनः सा परिवर्तते॥
en: My understanding is capable, O Suta, of finding out the disadvantage of a particular act but when I approach Duryodhana my understanding fails me.

sn: एवं गते वै यद् भावि तद् भविष्यति संजय। क्षत्रधर्मः किल रणे तनुत्यागो हि पूजितः॥
en: Such being the case, O Sanjaya, what will happen must happen (in spite of all that I can do to prevent it). Besides it is the honored duty of a Kshatriya to quit this life in battle."

sn: संजय उवाच त्वद्युक्तोऽयमनुप्रश्नो महाराज यथेच्छसि। न तु दुर्योधने दोषमिममाधातुमर्हसि॥
en: Sanjaya said This question, that you desire to put is worthy of you, O great king, but it is not proper that you should lay the fault entirely on Duryodhana.

sn: शृणुष्वानवशेषेण वदतो मम पार्थिवा य आत्मनो दुश्चरितादशुभं प्राप्नुयानरः। न स कालं न वा देवानेनसा गन्तुमर्हति॥
en: Listen to the end of my speech in detail regarding this matter; that man, who meets with disasters owing to his own bad acts, should not, properly speaking, lay the fault on time or luck nor on the gods.

sn: महाराज मनुष्येषु निन्द्यं यः सर्वमाचरेत्। स बध्यः सर्वलोकस्य निन्दितानि समाचरन्॥
en: O great king, he, who behaves sinfully in every thing towards men, ought to be killed by the entire world owing to his sinful behaviour.

sn: निकारा मनुजश्रेष्ठ पाण्डवैस्त्वत्प्रतीक्षया। अनुभूताः सहामात्यैनिकृतैरधिदेवने॥
en: O foremost among the sons of Manu, the Pandavas, defeated at the game dice, were much persecuted but they bore up all that for they had confidence in you.

sn: हयानां च गजानां च राज्ञां चामिततेजसाम्। वैशसं समरे वृत्तं यत् तन्मे शृणु सर्वशः॥
en: Hear from me fully of the slaughter that is about to be perpetrated in the battle, of horses, elephants, and kings of immeasurable prowess.

sn: स्थिरो भूत्वा महाप्राज्ञ सर्वलोकक्षयोदयम्। यथाभूतं महायुद्धे श्रुत्वा चैकमना भव॥
en: Hearing patiently of the massacre of the entire world that is about to take place in the battle, O you of great wisdom, be decided in this point namely.

sn: न ह्येव कर्ता पुरुषः कर्मणोः शुभपापयोः। अस्वतन्त्रो हि पुरुषः कार्यते दारुयन्त्रवत्॥
en: A man is not the doer of his virtuous or impious acts. In fact a man acts under compulsion like a wooden machine.

sn: केचिदीश्वरनिर्दिष्टाः केचिदेव यदृच्छया। पूर्वकर्मभिरष्यन्ये तेरैधमेतत् प्रदृश्यते। तस्मादनर्थमापन्नः स्थिरो भूत्वा निशामय॥
en: Some say that each act is made to be done by god himself; others say that action proceeds from our own free will, while others again say that they are the results three opinions held in this matter. Listen therefore patiently to the disaster that is close on us.

sn: संजय उवाच हिरण्वत्यां निविष्टेषु पाण्डवेषु महात्मसु। न्यविशन्त महाराज कौरवेया यथाविधि।।।।
en: Sanjaya said The great souled sons of Pandu having fixed their encampment at Hiranvati, the sons of Kuru too encamped there as usual, O great king.

sn: तत्र दुर्योधनो राजा निवेश्य बलमोजसा। सम्मानयित्वा नृपतीन् यस्य गुल्मांस्तथैव च॥
en: The king Duryodhana, having encamped his soldiers there strongly, and having paid his respects to the rulers of men on his side and posted guards,

sn: आरक्षस्य विधिं कृत्वा योधानां तत्र भारत। कर्णं दुःशासनं चैव शकुनिं चापि सौबलम्॥
en: And taken other measures for the protection of his soldiers, summoned before him Karna, Dushasana, Shakuni, the son of Subala,

sn: आनाय्य नृपतिस्तत्र मन्त्रयामास भारत। तत्र दुर्योधनो राजा कर्णेन सह भारत॥
en: And consulted with the kings, O Bharata. The king Duryodhana first consulted with Karna, O Bharata.

sn: सम्भाषित्वा च कर्णेन भ्रात्रा दुःशासनेन च। सौबलेन च राजेन्द्र मन्त्रयित्वा नरर्षभ।॥
en: And having consulted with Karna and also with his brother Duhshasana, and that best among men having also consulted with the son of Subala, O chief among kings!

sn: आहूयोपह्वरे राजन्नुलूकमिदमब्रवीत्। उलूक गच्छ कैतव्य पाण्डवान् सहसोमकान्॥
en: And summoning in private Uluka, said these words o king: "O Uluka, O son of one who is skillful at dice, go to the Pandavas united with the Somakas.

sn: गत्वा मम वचो ब्रूहि वासुदेवस्य शृण्वतः। इदं तत् समनुप्राप्तं वर्षपूगाभिचिन्तितम्॥
en: And going there say this on my behalf within the hearing of Vasudeva; "What has been expected for a long series of years has now come.

sn: पाण्डवानां कुरूणां व युद्ध लोकभयंकरम्। यदेतत् कत्थनावाक्यं संजयो महदब्रवीत्॥
en: Namely the war between the Pandavas and the Kurus, frightful to the world. Of the very boastful words Sanjaya told me,

sn: वासुदेवसहायस्य गर्जतः सानुजस्य ते। मध्ये कुरूणां कौन्तेय तस्य कालोऽयमागतः॥
en: Proceeding from yourself and your younger brothers having Vasudeva for your ally, with a roar in the midst of the Kurus. O son of Kunti, the time for that has now come.

sn: यथा वः सम्प्रतिज्ञातं तत् सर्वं क्रियतामिति। ज्येष्ठं तथैव कौन्तेयं ब्रूयास्त्वं वचनान्मम॥
en: What you have resolved to do, do all." Then do you speak to the eldest son of Kunti behalf.

sn: भ्रातृभिः सहितः सर्वैः सोमकैश्च सकेकयैः। कथं वा धार्मिको भूत्वा त्वमधर्मे मनः कृथाः॥
en: He, being a virtuous man, have you set your mind on a wrong course along with your brothers, and all the Somakas and the Kaikeyas.

sn: य इच्छसि जगत् सर्वं नश्यमानं नृशंसवत्। अभयं सर्वभूतेभ्यो दाता त्वमिति मे मतिः॥
en: Do you desire like an inhuman being to destroy the entire world, on the contrary in my opinion you should rather keep all living creatures in safety. on my

sn: श्रूयते हि पुरा गीतः श्लोकोऽयं भरतर्षभ। प्रह्लादेनाथ भद्रं ते हृते राज्ये तु दैवतैः॥
en: It is heard, O best among the Bharatas, that in days of old, Pralhada sang this Sloka on his kingdom being wrested by the gods. May you fare well.

sn: यस्य धर्मध्वजो नित्यं सुरा ध्वज इवोच्छ्रितः। प्रच्छन्नानि च पापानि बैडालं नाम तद् व्रतम्॥
en: He, whose standard of righteousness is ever flying in the air like the standard of the gods and whose wicked deeds are concealed, is said to be of the ways of life adopted by the cat.

sn: अत्र ते वर्तयिष्यामि आख्यानमिदमुत्तमम्। कथितं नारदेनेह पितुर्मम नराधिप॥
en: I shall now tell you in this connection an excellent story repeated to my father by Narada, O ruler of men.

sn: मार्जारः किल दुष्टात्मा निश्चेष्टः सर्वकर्मसु। ऊर्ध्वबाहुः स्थितो राजन् गङ्गातीरे कदाचन॥ कृत्वा मनःशुद्धिं प्रत्ययार्थं शरीरिणाम्। करोमि धर्ममित्याह सर्वानेव शरीरिणः॥
en: A cat, wicked-souled and disinclined to action, once on a time went to the banks of the Ganga and stayed there with his arms upraised. He, having set his heart on holy devotion , to inspire confidence in animals, said to all living beings "I shall practice virtue."

sn: तस्य कालेन महता विश्रम्भं जग्मुरण्डजाः। समेत्य च प्रशंसन्ति मार्जारं तं विशाम्पते॥
en: In course of time birds had much confidence in him and having assembled together they began to praise the cat, O lord of the universe..

sn: पक्षिभिः पक्षिभोजनः। आत्मकार्यं कृतं मेने चर्यायाश्च कृतं फलम्॥
en: That eater of birds, having been thus honored by those feathery creatures, considered his object accomplished and the result of his devotions achieved.

sn: अथ दीर्घस्य कालस्य तं देशं मूषिका ययुः। ददृशुस्तं च ते तत्र धार्मिकं व्रतचारिणम्॥
en: After a long time some mice came there and saw him practicing virtue and ascetic austerities.

sn: पूज्यमानस्तु तैः सर्वैः कार्येण महता युक्तं दम्भयुक्तेन भारत। तेषां मतिरियं राजन्नासीत् तत्र विनिश्चये॥
en: And ever employed in a great deed with pride. Being sure of this fact, they came to cherish this desire, Oking.

sn: बहुमित्रा वयं सर्वे तेषां नो मातुलो ह्ययम्। रक्षां करोतु सततं वृद्धबालस्य सर्वशः॥
en: We have many enemies, therefore let this one be our maternal uncle and let him therefore protect always all of us, old and young.

sn: उपगम्य तु ते सर्वे बिडालमिदमब्रुवन्। भवत्प्रसादादिच्छामश्चर्तं चैव यथासुखम्॥
en: And they having all approached the cat said this. Through your grace we desire to roam about happily.

sn: भवान् नो गतिरव्यग्रा भवान् नः परमः सुहृत्। ते वयं सहिताः सर्वे भवन्तं शरणं गताः॥
en: You are our refuge, you are our best friend; all of us therefore place ourselves under your protection.

sn: भवान् धर्मपरो नित्यं भवान् धर्मे व्यवस्थितः। स नो रक्ष महाप्रज्ञ त्रिदशानिव वज्रभृत्॥
en: You are ever virtuously inclined, you are ever adopting a pious course; therefore do you, O you of great wisdom, protect us as the wielder of the thunder-bolt protects the gods.

sn: एवमुक्तस्तु तैः सर्वैर्मूषिकैः स विशाम्पते। प्रत्युवाच ततः सर्वान् मूषिकान् मूषिकान्तकृत्॥
en: Being thus spoken to by all those mice, O lord of the universe, that destroyer of mice then spoke in reply to those mice.

sn: द्वयोर्योगं न पश्यामि तपसो रक्षणस्य च। अवशयं तु मया कार्यं वचनं भवतां हितम्॥
en: The connection between the two I do not see namely-my austerities and my protecting you, but of course I must act as you ask me for your good.

sn: युष्माभिरपि कर्तव्यं वचनं मम नित्यशः। तपसाऽस्मि परिश्रान्तो दृढं नियममास्थितः॥
en: But my words too ought to be always listened to by you. I am weakened by devolution but yet attached to it by firm resolve.

sn: न चापि गमने शक्ति काश्चित् पश्यामि चिन्तयन्। सोऽस्मि नेयः सदा ताता नदीकूलमितः परम्॥
en: I have not the slightest power to move, I now see on reflection; therefore should I be taken every day hence to the river side by you, my dear friends.

sn: तथेति तं प्रतिज्ञाय मूषिका भरतर्षभ। वृद्धबालमथो सर्वं मार्जाराय न्यवेदयन्॥
en: The mice too saying "very well", O best among the race of Bharatas, placed every one of themselves, old and young, under the protection of the cat.

sn: ततः स पापो दुष्टात्मा मूषिकानथ भक्षयन्। पीवरश्च सुवर्णश्च दृढबन्धश्च जायते॥
en: Then did that wicked-souled wretch began to feed on mice and grow fat and in vigour of body.

sn: मूषिकाणां गणश्चात्र भृशं संक्षीयतेऽथ सः। मार्जारो वर्धते चापि तेजोबलसमन्वितः॥
en: The members of mice began to diminish quickly and the cat too began to grow up endued with strength and energy.

sn: ततस्ते मूषिकाः सर्वे समेत्यान्योऽन्यमब्रुवन्। मातुलो वर्धते नित्यं वयं क्षीयामहे भृशम्॥
en: Then did those rats, meeting together, said to one another 'Our maternal uncle is growing up day by day but we are being speedily reduced in numbers.'

sn: ततः प्राज्ञतमः कश्चिड्डिण्डिको नाम मूषिकः। अब्रवीद् वचनं राजन् मूषिकाणां महागणम्॥
en: Then the wisest among the mice, one named Dindika said these words in the assembly of the rats, Oking.

sn: गच्छतां वो नदीतीरं सहितानां विशेषतः। पृष्ठतोऽहं गमिष्यामि सहैव मातुलेन तु॥
en: You go to the river side together in advance); after you, I shall go in company with our maternal uncle.

sn: साधु साध्वति ते सर्वे पूजयांचक्रिरे तदा। चक्रुश्चैव यथान्यायं डिण्डिकस्य वचोऽर्थवत्॥
en: These words were applauded by them with the exclamation "well said" "well said" and they acted according to the suggestion of Dindika, which was consistent with reason.

sn: अविज्ञानात् ततः सोऽथ डिण्डिकं [पभुक्तवान्। ततस्ते सहिताः सर्वे मन्त्रयामासुरञ्जसा॥
en: Owing to ignorance (of the plan) the cat ate up Dindika that day; then did they united together hold a consultation shortly after. One of the oldest mice named Kolika,

sn: तत्र वृद्धतमः कश्चित् कोलिको नाम मूषिकः। अब्रवीद् वचनं राजन् ज्ञातिमध्ये यथातथम्॥ न मातुलो धर्मकामश्छद्ममात्रं कृता शिखा।
en: Said this words, O king, among the members of his race which was indeed the truth. The desire of our maternal uncle is not to carn virtue, it is only a disguise.

sn: न मूलफलभक्षस्य विष्ठा भवति लोमशा॥ अस्य गात्राणि वर्धन्ते गणश्च परिहीयते।
en: The evacuation of animals eating roots and fruits, cannot have hairs in it; his body is growing fatter while we are decreasing in numbers.

sn: अद्य सप्ताष्टदिवसान् डिण्डिकोऽपि न दृश्यते॥ एतच्छ्रुत्वा वचः सर्वे मूषिका विप्रदुद्रुवुः।
en: For these seven and eight days moreover Dindika too is not seen.' Hearing this all the mice ran away.

sn: बिडालोऽपि स दुष्टात्मा जगामैव यथागतम्॥ तथा त्वमपि दुष्टात्मन् न बैडालं व्रतमास्थितः।
en: The wicked-souled cat too went away where he came from. In the same way are you also, O you of wicked heart, adopting the policy of the cat.

sn: चरसि ज्ञातिषु सदा बिडालो मूषिकेष्विव॥ अन्यथा किल ते वाक्यमन्यथा कर्म दृश्यते।
en: You behave to your kinsmen always as the cat behaved to the mice; your words mean one thing while your acts are seen to be quite different,

sn: दम्भनार्थाय लोकस्य वेदाधोपशमश्च ते॥ त्यक्त्वा छा त्विदं राजन् क्षत्रधर्मं समाश्रितः।
en: For a display before the world your knowledge of the Vedas, and the harmlessness of your nature; leaving aside this disguise and adopting the life of a Kshatriya.

sn: कुरु कार्याणि सर्वाणि धर्मिष्ठोऽसि नरर्षभ॥ बाहुवीर्येण पृथिवीं लब्वा भरतसत्तम।
en: Do all these acts, and then will you be called a righteous man, O best among the men; O best among the Bharatas, having won this earth by the prowess if your arms,

sn: देहि दानं द्विजातिभ्यः पितृभ्यश्च यथोचितम्॥ क्लिष्टाया वर्षपूगांश्च मातुर्मातृहिते स्थितः।
en: Make gifts to the twice-born and due offerings to your forefathers. Seeking the welfare of your mother, that mother who has undergone much trouble for a series of years.

sn: प्रमार्जाश्रु रणे जित्वा सम्मान परमावह॥ पञ्च ग्रामा वृता यत्नान्नास्माभिरपवर्जिताः।
en: Dry up her tears by becoming victories in battle and conferring exalted honours on her. Five villages only were asked for by you humbly and that even was refused by us.

sn: युध्यामहे कथं संख्ये कोपयेव च पाण्डवान्॥ त्वत्कृते दुष्टभावस्य संत्यागो विदुरस्य च।
en: With the thought how can we engage in fight, how can we inspire anger into the sons of Pandu. It was on account of your doing that we cast off the wicked Vidura.

sn: जातुषे च गृहे दाहं स्मर तं पुरुषो भव॥ यच्च कृष्णमवोचस्त्वमायान्तं कुरुसंसदि।
en: Remembering the attempt to burn you up in a house of powered lac be a man (and fight) as you said to Krishna when he was coming to the assembly of the Kurus.

sn: अयमस्मि स्थितो राजन् शमाय समराय च॥ तस्यायमागतः कालः समरस्य नराधिप!
en: I remain here, O king, ready for peace or for war; remember that the time for that fight is now come, O ruler of men.

sn: एतदर्थं मया सर्वं कृतमेतद् युधिष्ठिर॥ किं नु युद्धात् परं लाभं क्षत्रियो बहु मन्यते। किं च त्वं क्षत्रियकुले जातः सम्प्रथितो भुवि॥
en: All this has been made ready by me in view of that, O Yudhishthira. What does a Kshatriya consider to be a greater gain than war? You are born in a Kshatriya race and are known in this world.

sn: द्रोणादस्त्राणि संप्राप्य कृपाच्च भरतर्षभ। तुल्ययोनौ समबले वासुदेवं समाश्रितः॥
en: Having learnt the use of weapons from Drona and from Kripa, O best among Bharatas, you yet seek the protection of Vasudeva, of equal birth and equal strength.

sn: ब्रूयास्त्वं वासुदेवं च पाण्डवानां समीपतः। आत्मार्थं पाण्डवार्थं च यत्ता मां प्रति योधय॥
en: You should also say to Vasudeva in the hearing to the son of Pandu. For your own sake, and for the sake of Pandavas fight with me with all your power.

sn: सभामध्ये च यद् रूपं मायया कृतवानसि। तत् तथैव पुनः कृत्वा सार्जुनो मामभिद्रव॥
en: The form in which you showed yourself in the midst of the assembly by the help of illusion, assuming again, come against me along with Arjuna.

sn: इन्द्रजालं च माया वै कुहका वाऽपि मीषणा। आत्तशस्त्रस्य संग्रामे वहन्ति प्रतिगर्जनाः॥
en: Illusion is sometimes frightful but it only inspires rage in him who has taken up arms and is ready for battle.

sn: वयमप्युत्सहेम द्यां खं च गच्छेम मायया। रसातलं विशामोऽपि ऐन्द्र वा पुरमेव तु॥
en: Who can venture to go to heaven and to the say by the help of illusion and can enter even Rasatala and even the capital of Indra?

sn: दर्शयेम च रूपाणि स्वशरीरे बहून्यपि। न तु पर्यायतः सिद्धिर्बुद्धिमाप्नोति मानुषीम्॥
en: In this body of mine I can show many forms but it is not by inspiring fight that a man becomes successful.

sn: मनसैव हि भूतानि धातैव कुरुते वशे। यद् ब्रवीषि च वार्ष्णेय धार्तराष्ट्रानहं रणे॥
en: By the force of the mind alone, does the Creator bring all creatures under his control. You too, O scion of the Vrishni race, said at the time namely.

sn: घातयित्वा प्रदास्यामि पार्थेभ्यो राज्यमुत्तमम्। आचचक्षे च मे सर्वं संजयस्तव भाषितम्॥
en: That, killing in battle the son of Dhritarashtra I shall bestow an excellent kingdom on the sons of Pritha-Sanjaya informed me of everything that you saidमद्वितीयेन पार्थेन वैरं वः सव्यसाचिना।

sn: स सत्यसंगरो भूत्वा पाण्डवार्थं पराक्रमी॥
en: “You declare war with Savyasachin having me for his second." Now being firmly devoted to truth, and for the sake of the Pandavas,

sn: युध्यस्वाद्य रणे यत्तः पश्यामः पुरुषो भव। यस्तु शत्रुमभिज्ञाय शुद्धं पौरुषमास्थितः॥
en: Fight with all your might and be a manand we shall see. That ma, who knowing the might of his enemy acts, at the dictates of manliness,

sn: करोति द्विषतां शोकं स जीवति सुजीवितम्। अकस्माच्चैव ते कृष्ण ख्यातं लोके महद् यशः॥
en: And brings grief on his enemies, lives indeed a good life. For no reason, O Krishna are you considered to be of great renown in this world and how they will know that many are the oxen who are important though they have horns.

sn: अद्येदानीं विजानीमः सन्ति षण्ढाः सशृङ्गकाः। मद्विधो नापि नृपतिस्त्वयि युक्तः कथञ्चन॥
en: A ruler of man like myself should never you being clad in a coat of mail, you who are the slave of Kansa.

sn: संनाहं संयुगे कर्तुं कंसभृत्ये विशेषतः। तं च तूबरकं बालं बह्वाशिनमविद्यकम्॥
en: To that stupid and dull-headed boy (in wisdom) that voracious eater, that ignorant man,

sn: उलूक मद्वचो ब्रूहि असकृद्भीमसेनकम्। विराटनगरे पार्थ यस्त्वं सूदो ह्यभूः पुरा॥
en: O Uluka, say on my behalf, to that vicious weight Bhimasena: “O son of Pritha, in the city of Virata were you before a cook,"

sn: बल्लवो नाम विख्यातस्तन्ममैव हि पौरुषम्। प्रतिज्ञातं सभामध्ये न तन्मिथ्या त्वया पुरा॥
en: Known by the name of Ballava and that was all on account of my manliness. Be not fight with false to the resolve you made in the midst of the council in olden times.

sn: दुःशासनस्य रुधिरं पीयतां यदि शक्यते। यद् ब्रीवीषि च कौन्तेय धार्तराष्ट्रानहं रणे॥
en: Drink the blood of Dushasana, if you can. O son of Kunti, what you said namely, that in battle, the sons of Dhritarashtra,

sn: निहनिष्यामि तरसा तस्य कालोऽयमागतः। त्वं हि भोज्ये पुरस्कार्यो भक्ष्ये पेये च भारत॥
en: I shall soon slay, the time for that is now come. You can indeed be rewarded in matters of dishes-both meats and drinks.

sn: क्वं युद्धं क्वं च भोक्तव्यं युध्यस्व पुरुषो भव। शयिष्यसे हतो भूमौ गदामालिङ्ग्य भारत॥
