en: Great however is the difference between dishes and war. Come, now, fight and be a man. You will be down on the field killed, embracing your mace, O Bharata.

sn: तद् वृथा च सभामध्ये वल्गितं ते वृकोदर। उलूक नकुलं ब्रूहि वचनान्मम भारत॥
en: The boast you indulged in at that assembly is false, O Vrikodara. O Uluka, on my behalf do you also speak to Nakula.

sn: युद्धयस्वाद्य स्थिरो भूत्वा पश्यामस्तव पौरुषम्। युधिष्ठिरानुरागं च द्वेषं च मयि भारत। कृष्णायाश्च परिक्लेशं स्मरेदानीं यथातथम्॥
en: Fight now with patience and I shall see your manliness. I shall see too how great is your esteem for Yudhishthira and contempt for myself.

sn: ब्रूयास्त्वं सहदेवं च राजमध्ये वचो मम। युद्ध्येदानीं रणे यत्तः क्लेशान् स्मर च पाण्डव॥
en: Remember now the troubles experienced by Krishna. Speak also on my behalf of Sahadeva in the midst of kings these words.

sn: विराटद्रुपदौ चोभौ ब्रूयास्त्वं वचनान्मम। न दृष्टपूर्वा भर्तारो भृत्यैरपि महागुणैः॥ तथाऽर्थपतिभिर्भूत्या यतः सृष्टाः प्रजास्ततः। अश्लाध्योऽयं नरपतिर्युवयोरिति चागतम्॥
en: "War having now been proclaimed, fight with all your might, O son of Pandu, and remember your troubles.” Say also on my behalf to Drupada and Virata: "you are fools for you are not content to have me as your master but on the contrary you have gladly been the slaves of Yudhishthira. This king deserves no praise, probably with this thought do you now come to fight with us.

sn: ते यूयं संहता भूत्वा तद्वधार्थं ममापि च। आत्मार्थं पाण्डवार्थं च प्रयुद्ध्यध्वं मया सह॥
en: Therefore do you, united together, fight with me to gain your own ends and that of the Pandavas and to bring on my death.”

sn: धृष्टद्युम्नं च पाञ्चाल्यं ब्रूयास्त्वं वचनान्मम। एष ते समयः प्राप्तो लब्धव्यश्च त्वयाऽपि सः॥
en: Speak to Dhrishtadyumna, prince of Panchala, on my behalf "now is the time for you and you will now meet with death.

sn: द्रोणमासाद्य समरे ज्ञास्यसे हितमुत्तमम्। युध्यस्व ससुहृत् पापं कुरु कर्म सुदुष्करम्॥
en: Coming face to face with Drona in battle shall you know which is good for you. Do you fight for the sake of your well wishers and accomplish a deed hard to do." O Uluka, speak on my behalf thus Shikhandin; "the son of Kuru having long arms does not slay you for he holds you to be a woman.

sn: शिखण्डिनमथो ब्रूहि उलूक वचनान्मम। स्त्रीति मत्वा महाबाहुर्न हनिष्यति कौरवः॥
en: That son of Ganga, that foremost among bow men, will not kill you therefore, do you fight without fear; fight with all your might, I will see your manliness."

sn: गाङ्गेयो धन्विनां श्रेष्ठो युद्ध्येदानीं सुनिर्भयः। कुरु कर्म रणे यत्तः पश्यामः पौरुषं तव॥
en: Saying this the king laughing aloud said to Uluka:' “Speak again to Dhananjaya in the hearing of Vasudeva.

sn: एवमुक्त्वा ततो राजा प्रहस्योलूकमब्रवीत्। धनंजयं पुनर्बुहि वासुदेवस्य शृण्वतः॥
en: Either having defeated us for you rule over this universe or being yourselves defeated by us steep the sleep of heroes.

sn: अस्मान् वा त्वं पराजित्य प्रशाधि पृथिवीमिमाम्। अथवा निर्जितोऽस्माभी रणे वीर शयिष्यसि॥
en: Remembering, O son of Pandu, the pain of being exiled from your kingdom and of your residence in the forth and the trouble endued by Krishna, be a man.

sn: राष्ट्रनिर्वासनक्लेशं वनवासं च पाण्डव। कृष्णायाश्च परिक्लेशं संस्मरन् पुरुषो भव॥
en: All the objects for which a Kshatriya lady brings forth a son are now come, strength, prowess, heroism and skillfulness in the use of weapon,

sn: यदर्थं क्षत्रिया सूते सर्वं तदिदमागतम्। बलं वीर्यं च शौर्यं च परं चाप्यस्त्रलाघवम्॥
en: And manliness, showing these, in battle, appease your rage. Persecuted, dispirited and exiled for a long time,

sn: पौरुषं दर्शयन् युद्धे कोपस्य कुरु निष्कृतिम्। परिक्लिष्टस्य दीनस्य दीर्घकालोषितस्य च। हृदयं कस्य न स्फोटेदैश्वर्याद् भ्रंशितस्य च॥
en: And deprived of wealth, who is there whose heart would not break. Who is there who being born in a good family, being himself a lord, and not coveting the wealth of others, would not be excited with anger having lost a kingdom which is his by the rights of succession.

sn: कुले जातस्य शूरस्य परवित्तेष्वगृध्यतः। आस्थितं राज्यमाक्रम्य कोपं कस्य न दीपयेत्॥
en: Let the tall talks that you have made be realized in deeds; he is known to be a worthless man who having indulged in boasts does not relies them in deeds.

sn: यत् तदुक्तं महद् वाक्यं कर्मणा तद् विभाव्यताम्। अकर्मणा कत्थितेन सन्तः कुपुरुषं विदुः॥ अमित्राणां वशे स्थानं राज्यं च पुनरुद्धर। द्वावौँ युद्धकामस्य तस्मात् तत् कुरु पौरुषम्॥
en: Recover this kingdom and these territories which are now in the possession of enemies, these are indeed the two objects of war; therefore display your prowess.

sn: पराजितोऽसि द्यूतेन कृष्णा चानायिता सभाम्। शक्योऽमर्षो मनुष्येण कर्तुं पुरुषमानिना॥
en: man In a game at dice have you been defeated and Krishna was dragged into the council. Wrath should therefore be displayed by one who thinks himself a in such circumstances.

sn: द्वादशैव तु वर्षाणि वने धिष्ण्याद् विवासितः। संवत्सरं विराटस्य दास्यमास्थाय चोषितः॥
en: For twelve years have you been exiled from your home into the woods, and for a whole year you lived as a slave under Virata.

sn: राष्ट्रनिर्वासनक्लेशं वनवासं च पाण्डव। कृष्णायाश्च परिक्लेशं संस्मरन् पुरुषो भव॥
en: Remembering therefore the trouble of being exiled from the kingdom, the residence in the forest and the sufferings of Krishna, be a man.

sn: अप्रियाणां च वचनं प्रब्रुवत्सु पुनः पुनः। अमर्ष दर्शयस्व त्वममर्षो ह्येव पौरुषम्॥
en: Show your wrath to them who on the eve of your excite again and again used harsh words to you, for wrath is manliness.

sn: क्रोधो बलं तथा वीर्यं ज्ञानयोगोऽस्त्रलाघवम्। इह ते दृश्यतां पार्थं युद्ध्यस्व पुरुषो भव॥
en: Wrath, strength, prowess, knowledge, application and quickness in the handling of weapons, show these now and fight, O son of Pritha, and act like a man.

sn: लोहाभिसारो निर्वृत्तः कुरुक्षेत्रमकर्दमम्। पुष्टास्तेऽश्वा भृता योधाः श्वो युद्ध्यस्व सकेशवः॥९३।
en: The deities, presiding over each weapon, have now been invoked. Kurukshetra is now free from mud, your horses are fat and sleek, your soldiers have been paid their dues, therefore do you fight, along with Keshava tomorrow.

sn: असमागम्य भीष्मेण संयुगे किं विकत्यसे। आरुरुक्षुर्यथा मन्दः पर्वतं गन्धमादनम्॥
en: Without encountering Bhishma in battle why do you boast? Like that fool who used to boast without ever ascending the Gandhamadana mountain,

sn: एवं कत्थसि कौन्तेय अकत्थन् पुरुषो भव। सूतपुत्रं सुदुर्धर्षं शल्यं च बलिनां वरम्॥
en: You too boast in the same way; O son of Kunti, show forth your manliness without boasting. The son of a Suta, excited with great wrath, and that foremost among persons endued with strength namely Shalya,

sn: द्रोणं च बलिनां श्रेष्ठं शचीपतिसमं युधि। अजित्वा संयुगे पार्थ राज्यं कथमिहेच्छसि॥
en: And Drona that foremost among men gifted with strength, who all in battle are equal to the Lord of Sachi himself, without defeating in battle all these, how do you desire the kingdom, O son of Pritha?

sn: ब्राह्मे धनुषि चाचार्य वेदयोरन्तगं द्वयोः। युधि धुर्यमविक्षोभ्यमनीकचरमच्युतम्॥
en: The one, who is the preceptor in the science of bowmanship as also in the Vedas he who has thoroughly studied these two, he that is foremost in battle and who can never be separated from his army,

sn: द्रोणं महाद्युतिं पार्थं जेतुमिच्छसि तन्मृषा। न हि शुश्रुम वातेन मेरुमुन्मथितं गिरिम्॥
en: O son of Pritha, the desire you entertain of vanquishing in battle that Drona, is vain; I never heard that the Meru mountain was ever moved by the wind.

sn: अनिलो वा वहेन्मेरुं द्यौर्वापि निपतेन्महीम्। युगं वा परिवर्तेन यद्येवं स्याद् यथाऽऽत्य माम्॥
en: But even the wind may move the Meru mountain, the heaven may fall over the earth, the periods now reigning may change, if what you have told me ever happens.

sn: को ह्यस्ति जीविताकाक्षी प्राप्येममरिमर्दनम्। पार्थो वा इतरो वापि कोऽन्यः स्वस्ति गृहान् व्रजेत्॥
en: Who is there, the son of Pritha or any body else, who, having fought with this grinder of foes, would return home with life and in health,

sn: कथमाभ्यामभिध्यातः संस्पृष्टो दारुणेन वा। रणे जीवन् प्रमुच्येत पदा भूमिमुपस्पृशन्॥
en: Who is there touching this earth with his foot who, after an encounter with these two and having his body brought in contract with the fierce arrows, would leave the field of battle alive?

sn: किं दर्दुरः कूपशयो यथेमा न बुध्यसे राजचमूं समेताम्। दुराधर्षां देवचमूप्रकाशां गुप्तां नरेन्द्रस्त्रिदशैरिव द्याम्॥
en: Why do you, like a frog living in a well, not understand the might of this vast army of assembled monarchs which is hard to be vanquished and which, shining as a celestial army, is protected by kings as heaven itself by the gods?

sn: काम्बोजशकैः खशैश्च। शाल्वैः समत्स्यैः कुरुमध्यदेश्यैम्लेंच्छैः पुलिन्दैईविडान्ध्रकाच्यैः॥
en: Protected by the kings of the East, West, South, and North, of the Shalvas along with the Matsya's, the Kurus of the middle countries, the Mlecchas, the Pulindas, the Dravidas, the Andhras, and the Kanchis,

sn: नानाजनौघं युधि सम्प्रवृद्धं गाङ्गं यथा वेगपारणीयम्। मां च स्थितं नागबलस्य मध्ये युयुत्ससे मन्द किमल्पबुद्धे॥
en: Why do you wish to fight, О fool of little understanding, with me in the midst of this army of elephants, this army composed of various races and which in battle is as incapable of being crossed over as the waves of the Ganga.

sn: अक्षय्याविषुधी चैव अग्निदत्तं च ते रथम्। जानीमो हि रणे पार्थं केतुं दिव्यं च भारत॥
en: I know that your quivers are exhausted of their contents. I know your chariot given to you by Agni. I know you, O son of Pritha, in battle and I know your celestial banners, O Bharata.

sn: अकत्थमानो युद्ध्यस्व कत्यसेऽर्जुन किं बहु। पर्यायात् सिद्धिरेतस्य नैतत् सिध्यति कत्थनात्॥
en: Fight and do not boast; why do you; O Arjuna, boast so much? One wins a battle by never his method of fighting and he does not win in consequence of boasts.

sn: यदीदं कत्थनाल्लोके सिध्येत् कर्म धनंजय। सर्वे भवेयुः सिद्धार्थाः कत्थने को हि दुर्गतः॥
en: If, O Dhananjaya, people in the world were to succeed owing to boasting then all would have their objects gained for who would be slow to boast.

sn: जानामि ते वासुदेवं सहायं जानामि ते गाण्डिव तालमात्रम्। जानाम्यहं त्वादृशो नास्ति योद्धा जानानस्ते राज्यमेतद्धरामि॥
en: I know that Vasudeva is your ally, I know your Gandiva bow which is six cubits long. I know that there is no warriors equal to you, and knowing all this I deprive you of your kingdom.

sn: न तु पर्यायधर्मेण सिद्धि प्राप्नोति मानवः। मनसैवानुकूलानि धातैव कुरुते वशे॥
en: Man does not obtain success in his desires simply as a matter of course, By mere will force does the Creator make unfavourable circumstances turn into favourable ones and get them under control.

sn: त्रयोदश समा भुक्तं राज्यं विलपतस्तव। भूयश्चैव प्रशासिष्ये त्वां निहत्य सबान्धवम्॥
en: The kingdom has been enjoyed by me for thirteen years while you were weeping; and again shall I rule over it after slaying yourself along with your friends.

sn: क्वं तदा गाण्डिवं तेऽभूद् यत् त्वं दासपणैर्जितः। क्वं तदा भीमसेनस्य बलमासीच्च फाल्गुन॥
en: Where was your Gandiva bow when you were defeated at a game of dice and made a slave? And where again was the strength of Bhimasena, O Falguna?

sn: सगदाद् भीमसेनाद् वा फाल्गुनाद् वा सगाण्डिवात्। न वै मोक्षस्तदाभूद् वो विना कृष्णमनिन्दृिताम्॥
en: Without the help of that praise worthy Krishna you would not have been liberated at the time, though you had the help of Bhimasena with his mace and Falguna with his Gandiva.

sn: सा वो दास्ये समापन्नान् मोचयामास पार्षती। अमानुष्यं समापन्नान् दासकर्मण्यवस्थितान्॥
en: She, the daughter of Prishata race, liberated you who had come by the condition of a slave, and were engaged in offices becoming only of the low and in working as slaves.

sn: अवोचं यत् षण्ढतिलानहं वस्तथ्यमेव तत्। धृता हि वेणि पार्थेन विराटनगरे तदा॥
en: What, I said then of you, namely, that you were like the seed of the sesame without the kernel, was indeed true for did not the son of Pritha (Arjuna) bear long hair when in the city of Virata?

sn: सूदकर्मणि विश्रान्तं विराटस्य महानसे। भीमसेनेन कौन्तेय यत् तु तन्मम पौरुषम्॥
en: The feelings of weariness, which O son of Kunti, were felt by Bhimasena in the palace of Virata, while engaged in the duties of a cook, are a proof of my manliness.

sn: एवमेव सदा दण्डं क्षत्रियाः क्षत्रिये दधुः। वेणी कृत्वा षण्ढवेषः कन्यां नर्तितवानसि।।११६।'
en: Wearing the disguise of an eunuch, and wearing long hair and with hips and waist bands were you engaged in teaching a girl dancing. Such is the punishment which Kshatriyas award to a Kshatriya who flies from battle.

sn: न भयाद् वासुदेवस्य न चापि तव फाल्गुन। राज्यं प्रतिप्रदास्यामि युद्ध्यस्व सहकेशवः॥
en: Nor from fear of Vasudeva, nor form fear of you, O Falguna, shall I give you back the kingdom therefore do you fight along with Keshava.

sn: न माया हीन्द्रजालं वा कुहका वापि भीषणा। आत्तशस्त्रस्य संग्रामे वहन्ति प्रतिगर्जनाः॥
en: Neither deception, nor illusion, nor the trick of a conjurer is frightful to one who has taken up arms for fight, these only tend to excite his anger.

sn: वासुदेवसहस्रं वा फाल्गुनानां शतानि वा। आसाद्य माममोघेषु द्रविष्यन्ति दिशो दश॥
en: A thousand Vasudevas, a hundred of Falgunas, having confronted me whose arms are never struck in vain, will fly away in all directions.

sn: संयुगं गच्छ भीष्मेण भिन्धि वा शिरसा गिरिम्। तरस्व वा महागाधं बाहुभ्यां पुरुषोदधिम्॥
en: Go to fight with Bhishma, or rend asunder the mountain by your head or with the help only of your two arms cross the sea of vast expanse,

sn: शारद्वतमहामीनं विविंशतिमहोरगम्। बृहद्वलमहोद्वेलं सौमदत्तितिमिङ्गिलम्॥
en: The sea having the son of Sharadvata as the great fish, Vivingshati as the great serpent, Bhishma as current of immeasurable might, Drona as its invincible crocodile,

sn: भीष्मवेगमपर्यन्तं द्रोणग्राहदुरासदम्। कर्णशल्यझषावर्तं काम्बोजवडवामुखम्॥
en: Karna and Shalya as its small fish and whirl pools, Kamboja, throne sending out flames from his mouth Brihadbala, the great waves and the son of Somadatta, the Timi fishes,

sn: दुःशासनौघं शलशल्यमत्स्यं सुषेणचित्रायुधनागनक्रम्। जयद्रथाद्रिं पुरुमित्रगाधं दुर्मर्षणोदं शकुनिप्रपातम्॥
en: Yuyutsu and Bhagadatta as its gale, Shrutayus and the son of Hridika its gulfs and bay, Dushasana its waves, Sushena and Chitrayudha its sea elephants and crocodiles,

sn: शस्त्रौघमक्षय्यमभिप्रवृद्धं यदावगाह्य श्रमनष्टचेताः। भविष्यसि त्वं हतसर्वबान्धवस्तदा मनस्ते परितापमेष्यति॥
en: Jayadratha its hidden rocks, Purumitra its depth, Shakuni its water falls. when descending into the sea having inexhaustible weapons as its waves you will feel weary and be rendered senseless, then will your mind feel repentance.

sn: तदा मन्सते त्रिदिवादिवाशुचे निवर्तिता पार्थ महाप्रशासनात्। प्रशाम्य राज्यं हि सुदुर्लभं त्वया बुभूषितः स्वर्ग इवातपस्विना॥
en: Then, O son of Pritha, will your mind be turned from the thought of ruling over the earth like one who has lived a life of infamy giving up all hopes of heaven. To win a kingdom for you is as difficult as to obtain heaven for a man who has never practiced devotion.

sn: संजय उवाच सेनानिवेशं सम्प्राप्त: कैतव्यः पाण्डवस्य ह। समागत: पाण्डवेयैयुधिष्ठिरमभाषत॥
en: Sanjaya said The son, of the one proficient in the game of dice, having reached the encampment of the Pandavas, said to Yudhishthira who was seated with the other sons of Pandu.

sn: अभिज्ञो दूतवाक्यानां यथोक्तं ब्रूवतो मम। दुर्योधनसमादेशं श्रुत्वा न क्रोद्भुमर्हसि॥
en: You very well know the nature of the words of envoys; therefore it is not proper that you should be angry with me who will only speak what Duryodhana has instructed me.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच उलूकं न भयं तेऽस्ति ब्रूहि त्वं विगतज्वरः। यन्मतं धार्तराष्ट्रस्य लुब्धस्यादीर्घदर्शिनः॥
en: Yudhishthira said O Uluka, you need have no fear; speak out without any fear of trouble, what opinion is held by the son of Dhritarashtra, actuated by avarice and having little foresight."

sn: ततो द्युतिमतां मध्ये पाण्डवानां महात्मनाम्। सृञ्जयानां च मत्स्यानां कृष्णस्य च यशस्विनः॥
en: Then in the midst of those men of effulgence, those great-souled son of Pandu and the Srinjayas and the Matsya's and also the renowned Krishna,

sn: दुपस्य सपुत्रस्य विराटस्य च संनिधौ। भूमिपानां च सर्वेषां मध्ये वाक्यं जगाद ह॥
en: And also of Drupada with his son and in the presence of Virata also and in the midst of those rulers of the earth he uttered these words.

sn: उलूक उवाच इदं त्वामब्रवीद् राजा धार्तराष्ट्रो महामनाः। शृण्वतां कुरुवीराणां तन्निबोध युधिष्ठिर॥
en: Uluka said The royal son of Dhritarashtra, endued with a large mind, said this to you in the hearing, of the Kuru heroes; listen to them O Yudhishthira.

sn: पराजितोऽसि द्यूतेन कृष्णा चानायिता सभाम्। शक्योऽमर्षो मनुष्येण कर्तुं पुरुषमानिना॥
en: You had been defeated at a game of dice, and Krishna had been dragged into the council, a man, who thinks himself to be a male, would be justified under these circumstances to show his wrath.

sn: द्वादशैव तु वर्षाणि वने धिष्ण्याद् विवासितः। संवत्सरं विराटस्य दास्यमास्थाय चोषितः॥
en: For twelve years have you been exiled from your home into the woods, and for a whole year you lived as a slave under Virata.

sn: अमर्षं राज्यहरणं वनवासं च पाण्डव। द्रौपद्याश्च परिक्लेशं संस्मरन् पुरुषो भव॥
en: Remembering, O son of Pandu, the pain of being exiled from your kingdom and of your residence in the forth and the trouble endued by Krishna, be a man.

sn: अशक्तेन च यच्छप्तं भीमसेनेन पाण्डव। दुःशासनस्य रुधिरं पीयतां यदि शक्यते॥
en: O son of Pandu now let what had been said by O Bhimasena namely that he would drink the blood of Dushasana, be made good by him, if he can.

sn: लोहाभिसारो निर्वृत्तः कुरुक्षेत्रमकर्दमम्। समः पन्था भृतास्तेऽश्वाः श्वो युध्यस्व सकेशवः॥
en: The deities, presiding over each weapon, have now been invoked. Kurukshetra is now free from mud, your horses are fat and sleek, your soldiers have been paid their dies, therefore do you fight, along with Keshava tomorrow.

sn: असमागम्य भीष्मेण संयुगे किं विकत्यसे। आरुरुक्षुर्यथा मन्दः पर्वतं गन्धमादनम्॥ एवं कत्थसि कौन्तेय अकत्थन् पुरुषो भव। सूतपुत्रं सुदुर्धर्षं शल्यं च बलिनां वरम्॥ द्रोणं च बलिनां श्रेष्ठं शचीपतिसमं युधि। अजित्वा संयुगे पार्थ राज्यं कथमिहेच्छसि॥
en: Without encountering Bhishma in battle why do you boast? Like that fool who used to boast without ever ascending the Gandhamadana mountain, You too boast in the same way; O son of Kunti, show forth your manliness without boasting. The son of a Suta, excited with great wrath, and that foremost among persons endued with strength namely Shalya and Drona that foremost among men gifted with strength, who all in battle are equal to the Lord of Sachi himself, without defeating in battle all these, how do you desire the kingdom, O son of Pritha?

sn: ब्राह्मे धनुषि चाचार्य वेदयोरन्तगं द्वयोः। युधि धुर्यमविक्षोभ्यमनीकचरमच्युतम्॥ द्रोणं महाद्युति पार्थ जेतुमिच्छसि तन्मृषा। न हि शुश्रुम वातेन मेरुमुन्मथितं गिरिम्॥
en: The one, who is the preceptor in the science of bowmanship as also in the Vedas he who has thoroughly studied these two, he that is foremost in battle and who can never be separated from his army, O son of Pritha, the desire you entertain of vanquishing in battle that Drona, is vain; I never heard that the Meru mountain was ever moved by the wind.

sn: अलिनो वा वहेन्मेरु द्यौर्वापि निपतेन्महीम्। युगं वा परिवर्तेन यद्येवं स्याद् यथाऽऽत्य माम्॥ काक्षी प्राप्येममरिमर्दनम्। गजो वाजी रथो वाऽपि पुनः स्वस्ति गृहान् व्रजेत्॥ कथमाभ्यामभिध्यातः संस्पृष्टो दारुणेन वा। रणेः जीवन् विमुच्येत पदा भूमिमुपस्पृशन्॥
en: But even the wind may move the Meru mountain, the heaven may fall over the earth, the periods now reigning may change, if what you have told me ever happens. Who is there, the son of Pritha or any body else, who, having fought with this grinder of foes, would return home with life and in health, Who is there touching this earth with his foot who, after an encounter with these two and having his body brought in contract with the fierce arrows, would leave the field of battle alive?

sn: किं दर्दुरः कूपशयो यथेमां न बुध्यसे राजचमूं समेताम्। दुराधर्षां देवचमूप्रकाशां गुप्तां नरेन्द्रस्त्रिदशैरिव द्याम्॥ काम्बोजशकैः खशैश्च। म्लेंच्छैः पुलिन्दैईविडान्ध्रकाश्च्यैः॥ नानाजनौघं युधि सम्प्रवृद्धं गाङ्गं यथा वेगमपारणीयम्। मां च स्थितं नागबलस्य मध्ये युयुत्ससे मन्द किमल्पबुद्धे॥
en: Why do you, like a frog living in a well, not understand the might of this vast army of assembled monarchs which is hard to be vanquished and which, shining as a celestial army, is protected by kings as heaven itself by the gods? Protected by the kings of the East, West, South, and North, of the Shalvas along with the Matsya's, the Kurus of the middle countries, the Mlecchas, the Pulindas, the Dravidas, the Andhras, and the Kanchis, Why do you wish to fight, o fool of little understanding, with me in the midst of this army of elephants, this army composed of various races and which in battle is as incapable of being crossed over as the waves of the Ganga.

sn: इत्येवमुक्त्वा राजानं धर्मपुत्रं युधिष्ठिरम्। अभ्यावृत्य पुनर्जिष्णुमुलूकः प्रत्यभाषत॥
en: Saying this to the king Yudhishthira the son of Dharma Uluka again turned to the one accustomed to victories and said to him,

sn: अकत्यमानो युध्यस्व कत्थसेऽर्जुन कि बहु। पर्यायात् सिद्धिरेतस्य नैतत् सिध्यति कत्यनात्॥
en: Fight and do not boast; why do you; O Arjuna, boast so much? One wins a battle by his method of fighting and he does not win in consequence of boats.

sn: यदीदं कत्थनाल्लोके सिध्येत् कर्म धनंजय। सर्वे भवेयुः सिद्धार्थाः कत्थने को हिं दुर्गतः॥
en: If, O Dhananjaya, people in the world were to succeed owing to boasting then all would have their objects gained for who would be slow to boast.

sn: जानामि ते वासुदेवं सहायं जानामि ते गाण्डिवं तालमात्रम्। जानाम्येतत् त्वादृशो नास्ति योद्धा जानानस्ते राज्यमेतद्धरामि॥
en: I know that Vasudeva is your ally, I know your Gandiva bow which is six cubits long. I know that there is no warriors equal to you, and knowing all this I deprive you of your kingdom.

sn: न तु पर्यायधर्मेण राज्यं प्राप्नोति मानुषः। मनसैवानुकूलानि विधाता कुरुते वशे॥
en: Man does not obtain success in his desires simple as a matter of course, By mere will force does the Creator make unfavourable circumstances turn into favourable ones and get them under control.

sn: त्रयोदश समा भुक्तं राज्यं विलपतस्तवा भूयश्चैव प्रशासिष्ये निहत्य त्वां सबान्धवम्॥
en: The kingdom has been enjoyed by me for thirteen years while you were weeping; and again shall I rule over it after slaying yourself along with your friends.

sn: क्व तदा गाण्डिवं तेऽभूद् यत् त्वं दास पणैर्जितः। क्व तदा भीमसेनस्य बलमासीच्च फाल्गुन।॥
en: Where was your Gandiva bow when you were defeated at a game of dice and made a slave? And where again was the strength of Bhimasena, O Falguna?

sn: सगदाद् भीमसेनाद् वा पार्थाद् वापि सगाण्डिवात्। न वै मोक्षस्तदा वोऽभूद् विना कृष्णामनिन्दिताम्॥
en: Without the help of that praise worthy Krishna you would not have been liberated at the time, though you had the help of Bhimasena with his mace and Falguna with his Gandiva.

sn: सा वो दास्ये समापन्नान् मोक्षयामास पार्षती। अमानुष्यं समापन्नान् दासकर्मण्यवस्थितान्॥
en: She, the daughter of Prishata race, liberated you who had come by the condition of a slave, and were engaged in offices becoming only of the low and in working as slaves.

sn: अवोचं यत् षण्ढतिलानहं वस्तथ्यमेव तत्। धृता हि वेणी पार्थेन विराटनगरे तदा।॥
en: What, I said then of you, namely, that you were like the seed of the sesame without the kernel, was indeed true for did not the son of Pritha (Arjuna) bear long hair when in the city of Virata?

sn: सूदकर्मणि च श्रान्तं विराटस्य महानसे। भीमसेनेन कौन्तेय यच्च तन्मम पौरुषम्॥
en: The feelings of weariness, which O son of Kunti, were felt by Bhimasena in the palace of Virata, while engaged in the duties of a cook, are a proof of my manliness.

sn: एवमेतत् सदा दण्डं क्षत्रियाः क्षत्रिये दधुः। वेणीं कृत्वा घण्ढवेषः कन्यां नर्तितवानसि॥
en: Wearing the disguise of an eunuch, and wearing long hair and with hips and waist bands were you engaged in teaching a girl dancing. Such is the punishment which Kshatriyas award to a Kshatriya who flies from battle.

sn: न भयाद् वासुदेवस्य न चापि तव फाल्गुन। राज्यं प्रतिप्रदास्यामि युद्ध्यस्व सहकेशवः॥
en: Nor from fear of Vasudeva, nor form fear of you, O Falguna, shall I give you back the kingdom therefore do you fight along with Keshava.

sn: न माया हीन्द्रजालं वा कुहका वाऽपि भीषणा। आत्तशस्त्रस्य मे युद्ध वहन्ति प्रतिगर्जनाः॥
en: Neither deception, nor illusion, nor the trick of a conjurer is frightful to one who has taken up arms for fight, these only tend to excite his anger.

sn: वासुदेवसहस्रं वा फाल्गुनानां शतानि वा। आसाद्य माममोघेणुं द्रविष्यन्ति दिशो दश॥
en: A thousand Vasudevas, a hundred of Falgunas, having confronted me whose arms are never struck in vain, will fly away in all directions.

sn: संयुगं गच्छ भीष्मेण भिन्धि वा शिरसा गिरिम्। तरेमं वा महागाधं बाहुभ्यां पुरुषोदधिम्॥
en: Go to fight with Bhishma, or rend asunder the mountain by your head or with the help only of your two arms cross the sea of vast expanse,

sn: शारद्वतमहामीनं विविंशतिमहोरगम्। बृहदलमहोद्वेलं सौमदत्तितिमिङ्गिलम्॥
en: With the son of Sharadvata as the great finish, Brihadbala as the great crocodile and the son of Somadatta as the Timi fish.

sn: भीष्मवेगमपर्यन्तं द्रोणग्राहदुरासदम्। कर्णशल्यझषावर्त काम्बोजवडवामुखम्॥
en: With Bhishma as the current which cannot be crossed, with Drona as the alligator which cannot be approached with Karna and Shalya, as a swarm of small fishes, and Kamboja as the mouth giving out flames.

sn: दुःशासनौघं शलशल्यमत्स्यं सुषेणचित्रायुधनागनक्रम् जयद्रथाद्रिं पुरुमित्रगाधं दुर्मर्षणोदं शकुनिप्रपातम्॥
en: Dusshasana is like water-flow in which Shala and Shalya are fishes. Sushena is serpent and Chitrayudha is crocodile, while Jayadratha is mountain, Purumitra is its depth, Durmarshana is water and Shakuni is its falls.

sn: शस्त्रौघमक्षय्यमपिप्रवृद्धं यदावगाह्य श्रमनष्टचेताः। स्तदा मनस्ते परितापमेष्यति॥
en: Many types of weapons are like waterflows of the soldier's sea, which is endless and enlarged. Entering into this, you will grieve, loosing your consciousness on destruction of your relatives.

sn: तदा मनस्ते त्रिदिवादिवाशुचे निवर्तिना पार्थमहीप्रशासनात्। प्रशाम्य राज्यं हि सुदुर्लभ त्वया बुभूषितः स्वर्ग इवातपस्विना॥
en: O Partha! As the mind of an impious man retires from heaven, you will retire from your ruling power. Keep quite, it is very difficult to gain the kingdom for you like a man wants heaven without any penance.

sn: संजय उवाच दुर्योधनस्य तद् वाक्य निशम्य भरतर्षभ। नेत्राभ्यामतिताम्राभ्यां कैतव्य समुदैक्षत॥
en: Sanjaya said That foremost of the Bharata race, hearing those words of Duryodhana, looked on that son of a gambler with eyes excessively red.

sn: स केशवमभिप्रेक्ष्य गुडाकेशो महायशाः। अभ्याभाषत कैतव्यं प्रगृह्य विपुलं भुजम्॥
en: Gudakesha, of great renown, looking on Keshava, said to the gambler's son tossing up his mighty arms.

sn: स्ववीर्यं यः समाश्रित्य समाह्वयति वै परान्। अभीतो युध्यते शत्रून् स वै पुरुष उच्यते॥
en: He, who, relying on his own prowess challenges his enemies to fight and fights with them without being struck with fear, is said to be a man.

sn: परवीर्यं समाश्रित्य यः समाह्वयते परान्। क्षत्रबन्धुरशक्तत्वाल्लोके स पुरुषाधमः॥
en: But he, who challenges his enemies relying on the prowess of others, is the lowest among the Kshatriyas and owing to his weakness he is called the lowest of men.

sn: स त्वं परेषां वीर्येण मन्यसे वीर्यमात्मनः। स्वयं कापुरुषो मूढ परांश्च क्षेप्तुमिच्छसि॥
en: You too think the prowess of others to be your own prowess; being yourself a coward, O fool, you want to have others slain.

sn: यस्त्वं वृद्धं सर्वराज्ञां हितबुद्धिं जितेन्द्रियम्। मरणाय महाप्रज्ञं दीक्षयित्वा विकत्थसे॥
en: You now boast, having installed as your leader the oldest of all kings, whose intelligence is directed to the good of others, who has brought his senses under control and who is endued with great wisdom and has made his death certain.

sn: भावस्ते विदितोऽस्माभिर्दुर्बुद्धे कुलपांसन। न हनिष्यन्ति गाङ्गेयं पाण्डवा घृणयेति हि॥
en: O you of wicked intelligence, O you the stain of your race, your intention is known by us. (You thought) the son of Pandu, would, out of kindness, not slay the son of Ganga,

sn: यस्य वीर्यं समाश्रित्य धार्तराष्ट्र विकत्यसे। हन्तास्मि प्रथमं भीष्मं मिषतां सर्वधन्विनाम्॥
en: Him depending on whose strength you are now boasting. I shall first slay that Bhishma within the sight of all bow men.

sn: कैतव्य गत्वा भरतान् समेत्य सुयोधनं धार्तराष्ट्रं वदस्व। तथेत्युवाचार्जुनः सव्यसाची निशाव्यपाये भविता विमर्दः॥
en: O gambler's son, going to the Bharatas, and going near the son of Dhritarashtra say that Arjuna or Savyasachin has said “Be it so; on the down of the day there will be war.”

sn: यद् वाब्रवीद् वाक्यमदीनसत्त्वं मध्ये कुरून् हर्षयन् सत्यसंघः। अहं हन्ता सृञ्जयानामनीकं शाल्वेयकांचेति ममैष भारः॥
en: The one of unfailing prowess (Bhishma) said among those men leading noble lives and delighting the Kurus namely "that I shall slay the army of the Srinjayas and the army of Shalva; that is my task."

sn: हन्यामहं द्रोणमृतेऽपि लोकं न ते भयं विद्यते पाण्डवेभ्यः। ततो हि ते लब्धतमं च राज्यमापद्गताः पाण्डवाश्चेति भावः॥
en: (Bhishma also said) I shall also slay the entire world except Drona" and therefore do you consider this kingdom already gained and that the sons of Pandu are in a calamity?

sn: मात्मन्यपि वर्तमानम्। तस्मादहं ते प्रथमं समूहे हन्ता समक्षं कुरुवृद्धमेव॥
en: Being filled with that proud thought you will however see ruin overtake yourself and I shall first slay you in the army in the presence of the oldest among the Kurus.

sn: सूर्योदये युक्तसेनः प्रतीक्ष्य द्वजी रथी रक्ष तं सत्यसंधम्। अहं हि वः पश्यतां द्वीपमेनं भीष्मं रथात् पातयिष्यामि बाणैः॥
en: At sun rise, at the head of your army attend with your chariot and your flags on, that one devoted to truth and protect him. I shall within your sight by my arrows fell down from the chariot Bhishma, your refuge,

sn: श्वोभूते कत्थनावाक्यं विज्ञास्यति सुयोधनः। आचितं शरजालेन मया दृष्ट्वा पितामहम्॥
en: When the morrow comes Suyodhana will know what it is to boast of seeing the grandfather felled down by my shower of arrows.

sn: यदुक्तश्च सभामध्ये पुरुषो ह्रस्वदर्शनः। क्रुद्धेन भीमसेनेन भ्राता दुःशासनस्तव॥ अधर्मज्ञो नित्यवैरी पापबुद्धिर्नृशंसवत्। सत्यां प्रतिज्ञामचिराद् द्रक्ष्यसे तां सुयोधन॥
en: What your brother Dushasana, that man of little foresight, who does not know what virtue is, who is ever hostile to me, who is sinful intellect and inhuman, has been told by the angry Bhimasena, you will soon see that resolve fulfilled, O Suyodhana.

sn: अभिमानस्य दर्पस्य क्रोधपारुष्ययोस्तथा। नैष्ठुर्यस्यावलेपस्य आत्मसम्भावनस्य च॥
en: Of too much pride, vanity and of anger and harsh words, of enmity, arrogance and boasts,

sn: नृशंसतायास्तैक्ष्ण्यस्य धर्मविद्वेषणस्य च। अधर्मस्यातिवादस्य वृद्धातिक्रमणस्य च॥
en: Of inhumanity, of cutting speeches, of hating virtue, of vice, of speaking ill of others, and of action against the advice of the old,

sn: दर्शनस्य च चक्रस्य कृत्स्नस्यापनयस्य च। द्रक्ष्यसि त्वं फलं तीव्रमचिरेण सुयोधन॥
en: Of partial opinions and of all vices united together, you shall soon see the sharp effects, O Suyodhana.

sn: वासुदेवद्वितीये हि मयि क्रुद्धे नराधमा आशा ते जीविते मूढ राज्ये वा केन हेतुना।॥
en: Having Vasudeva for my second and myself being angry, O worst of men, who are you that have hopes of life and of getting the kingdom, O fool.

sn: शान्ते भीष्मे तथा द्रोणे सूतपुत्रे च पातिते। निराशो जीविते राज्ये पुत्रेषु च भविष्यसि॥
en: Bhishma, the son of Shantanu, and Drona and the son of a Suta being felled down, you will despair of your life, of the kingdom and of the life of your sons.

sn: भ्रातृणां निधनं श्रुत्वा पुत्राणां च सुयोधन। भीमसेनेन निहतो दुष्कृतानि स्मरिष्यसि॥
en: Hearing of the death of your brother and of your son, O Suyodhana, and being struck by Bhimasena you will remember your vices.

sn: न द्वितीयां प्रतिज्ञां हि प्रतिजानामि कैतव। सत्यं ब्रवीम्यहं ह्येतत् सर्वं सत्यं भविष्यति॥
en: O gambler's son, I do not know how to make a second resolve. I tell you the truth, all this will truly happen."

sn: युधिष्ठिरोऽपि कैतव्यमुलूकमिदमब्रवीत्। उलूक मद्वचो ब्रूहि गत्वा तात सुयोधनम्॥
en: Yudhishthira too said to Uluka the gambler's son, “Uluka, tell my words when you go to Suyodhana.'

sn: स्वेन वृत्तेन मे वृत्तं नाधिगन्तुं त्वमर्हसि। उभयोरन्तरं वेद सूनृतानृतयोरपि॥
en: It is not proper that you should judge of my conduct to you by your own conduct; know that the difference between us two is the same as the difference between truth and falsehood.

sn: न चाहं कामये पापमपि कीटपिपीलयोः। किं पुनर्जातिषु वधं कामयेयं कथंचन॥
en: I do not desire to harm even the worms and ants; how can I then by any means desire the massacre of my kinsmen?

sn: एतदर्थं मया तात पञ्च ग्रामा वृताः पुरा। कथं तव सुदुर्बुद्धे न प्रेक्ष्ये व्यसनं महत्॥
en: It was for this reason, my dear brothers, that I asked for five villages only before; why is it that you do not realize this great calamity, O you of exceedingly sinful understanding?

sn: स त्वं कामपरीतात्मा मूढभावाच्च कत्थसे। तथैव वासुदेवस्य न गृह्णासि हितं वचः॥
en: Having your soul now overpowered by lust and out of folly you are now boasting and for the same reason you do not accept the beneficial words of Vasudeva.

sn: किं चेदानी बहूक्तेन युध्यस्व सह बान्धवैः। मम विप्रियकर्तारं कैतव्य ब्रूहि कौरवम्॥
en: What is the use of much speaking now? Fight with all your friends” O gambler's son, speak this to the Kuru who ever does what I do not like.

sn: श्रुतं वाक्यं गृहीतोऽर्थो मतं यत् ते तथास्तु तत्। भीमसेनस्ततो वाक्यं भूय आह नृपात्मजम्॥ उलूक मद्वचो ब्रूहि दुर्मति पापपूरुषम्।
en: Your words have been heard by us and their sense accepted; let it be as you wish.” Then did Bhimasena, that son of a king, again say O Uluka, tell my words to that wicked man of sinful intellect.

sn: शठं नैकृतिकं पापं दुराचारं सुयोधनम्॥ गृध्रोदरे वा वस्तव्यं पुरे वा नागसाह्वये। प्रतिज्ञातं मया तच्च सभामध्ये नराधम॥
en: To that vicious wretch of sinful habits, Suyodhana; "you will have to remain in the belly of a vulture or in the city called by the name of an elephant. And the resolve made by me in the council,

sn: कर्ताह तद् वचः सत्यं सत्येनैव शपामि ते। दुःशासनस्य रुधिरं हत्वा पास्याम्यहं मृधे॥
en: I shall make true, I swear by truth. Having slain Dushasana, I shall drink his blood in the battle.

sn: सक्थिनी तव भक्त्वैव हत्वा हि तव सोदरान्। सर्वेषां धार्तराष्ट्राणामहं मृत्युः सुयोधन॥ ।
en: I shall break down your thighs after slaying your brothers. I am the death, O Suyodhana, of all the sons of Dhritarashtra.

sn: सर्वेषां राजपुत्राणामभिमन्युरसंशयम्। कर्मणाः तोषयिष्यामि भूयश्चैव वचः शृणु॥
en: And Abhimanyu is without doubt the death of all the princes. I shall satisfy you by my deeds. Hear again my words.

sn: हत्वा सुयोधन त्वां वै सहितं सर्वसोदरैः। आक्रमिष्ये पदा मूर्ध्नि धर्मराजस्य पश्यतः॥
en: Slaying yourself, O Suyodhana, with all your brothers, I shall strike you on the head with my feet in the sight of the virtuous king.”

sn: नकुलस्तु ततो वाक्यमिदमाह महीपते। उलूक ब्रूहि कौरव्यं धार्तराष्ट्र सुयोधनम्॥
en: Nakula also, O lord of the earth, then said these words; "O Uluka, O Kauravya, say to Suyodhana, the son of Dhritarashtra,

sn: श्रुतं ते गदतो वाक्यं सर्वमेव यथातथम्। तथा कर्तास्मि कौरव्य यथा त्वमनुशासि माम्॥
en: The words uttered by you have all been heard by me, let them be so; I shall, O Kauravya, do what you have instructed me to do.

sn: सहदेवोऽपि नृपते इदमाह वचोऽर्थवत्। सुयोधन मतिर्या ते वृथैषा ते भविष्यति॥
en: Sahadeva too, O ruler of men, said these words pregnant with meaning. “O Suyodhana, the hopes entertained by you will be vain.

sn: शोचिष्यसे महाराज सपुत्रज्ञातिबान्धवः। इमं च क्लेशमस्माकं हृष्टो यत् त्वं विकत्थसे॥
en: You will grieve, ogreat king, along with your sons, kinsmen and friends, for this brag of yours at our troubles."

sn: विराटदुपदौ वृद्धावुलूकमिदमूचतुः। दासभावं नियच्छेव साधोरिति मतिः सदा। तौ च दासावदासौ वा पौरुषं यस्य यादृशम्॥
en: The two old kings Virata and Drupada said this to Uluka "We are ever willing to be the slaves of a good man and we shall see who is the slave and who the master and who is now powerful in the battle.”

sn: शिखण्डी तु ततो वाक्यमुलूकमिदमब्रवीत्। वक्तव्यो भवता राजा पापेष्वभिरतः सदा॥
en: Shikhandin then said these words to Uluka “By you should the king ever addicted to vice be thus spoken.

sn: पृश्य त्वं मां राजन् कुर्वाणं कर्म दारुणम्। यस्य वीर्यं समासाद्य मन्यसे विजयं युधि॥
en: Behold me, O king, to be doing hard deeds in the battle. Depending on whose prowess you hope for victory in the battle,

sn: तमहं पातयिष्यामि रथात् तव पितामहम्। अहं भीष्मवधात् सृष्टो नूनं धात्रा महात्मना॥
en: I shall fell down that grand gather of yours from the chariot. I was surely created by the great souled Creator for the slaying of Bhishma.

sn: सोऽहं भीष्मं हनिष्यामि मिषतां सर्वधन्विनाम्। धृष्टद्युम्नोऽपि कैतव्यमुलूकमिदमब्रवीत्॥
en: Therefore shall I slay Bhishma within the sight of all bowmen.” Dhrishtadyumna said this to Uluka, the son of a gambler.

sn: सुयोधनो मम वचो वक्तव्यो नृपतेः सुतः। अहं द्रोणं हनिष्यामि सगणं सहबान्धवम्॥
en: Suyodhana, the son of the king should thus be spoken to, on my behalf. “I shall kill Drona along with his host and his friends.

sn: अवश्यं च मया कार्य पूर्वेषां चरितं महत्। कर्ता चाहं तथा कर्म यथा नान्यः करिष्यति॥
en: The work of which I shall be the doer no one else will do.” Then did the virtuous king say the noble words out of kindness to him.

sn: तमब्रवीद् धर्मराजः कारुण्यार्थं वचो महत्। नाहं ज्ञातिवधं राजन् कामयेयं कथंचन॥
en: “O king, I never desire the massacre of my kinsmen and all this is going to happen owing to your fault.

sn: तवैव दोषाद् दुर्बुद्धे सर्वमेतत् त्वनावृतम्। स गच्छ मा चिरं तात उलूक यदि मन्यसे॥
en: Of course, I shall have to approve of the doings of these followers. There do you go without delay, O Uluka, if you wish it,

sn: इह वा तिष्ठ भद्रं ते वयं हि तव बान्धवाः। उलूकस्तु ततो राजन् धर्मपुत्रं युधिष्ठिरम्॥
en: Or remain here, may you farewell for we are your kinsmen too." Then Uluka taking leave of Yudhishthira, the son of Dharina, O king,

sn: आमन्त्र्य प्रययौ तत्र यत्र राजा सुयोधनः। उलूकस्तत आगम्य दुर्योधनममर्षणम्॥
en: Went where the king Suyodhana was staying. Uluka then coming to the wrathful Duryodhana,

sn: अर्जुनस्य समादेशं यथोक्तं सर्वमब्रवीत्। वासुदेवस्य भीमस्य धर्मराजस्य पौरुषम्॥
en: Told him all he had been instructed to say by Arjuna as also the manly speeches of Vasudeva, of Bhima and of the virtuous king,

sn: नकुलस्य विराटस्य द्रुपदस्य च भारत। सहदेवस्य च वचो धृष्टद्युम्नशिखण्डिनोः।
en: And of Nakula, Virata, and Drupada, 0 Bharata and the speeches of Dhrishtadyumna and Shikhandi,

sn: केशवार्जुनयोर्वाक्यं यथोक्तं सर्वमब्रवीत्॥ कैतव्यस्य तु तद् वाक्यं निशम्य भरतर्षभः।
en: And the speeches of Keshava and Arjuna, all as he had been instructed to say. The foremost of the Bharata race hearing the words of that gambler's son,

sn: दुःशासनं च कर्णं च शकुनि चापि भारत॥ आज्ञापयत राज्ञश्च बलं मित्रबलं तथा।
en: Commanded Dushasana, Karna, Shakuni, O Bharata, and his own army as also those of his allies,

sn: यथा प्रागुदयात् सर्वेयुक्तास्तिष्ठन्त्यनीकिनः॥ ततः कर्णसमादिष्टा दूताः संत्वरिता रथैः।
en: So that all might be at the head of their respective divisions before sun rise. Then did messengers instructed by Karna, mount on cars speedily.

sn: उष्ट्रवामीभिरप्यन्ये सदश्चैश्च महाजवैः॥ तूर्णं परिययुः सेनां कृत्स्ना कर्णस्य शासनात्। आज्ञापयन्तो राज्ञश्च योग: प्रागुदयादिति॥
en: And others on camels, and others again on good horses went out and ordered the united army at Karna's behest to be ready for battle before sunrise.

sn: संजय उवाच उलूकस्यः वचः श्रुत्वा कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः। सेनां निर्यापयामास धृष्टद्युम्नपुरोगमाम्॥
en: Sanjaya said Yudhishthira, the son of Kunti, hearing the words of Uluka, began to move his army at the head of which was Dhrishtadyumna.

sn: पदातिनी नागवती रथिनीमश्ववृन्दिनीम्। चतुर्विधबलां भीमामकम्पां पृथिवीमिव॥
en: That fierce army, immovable as the earth itself, had all the four divisions, namely foot soldiers, elephants, chariots and horses.

sn: भीमसेनादिभिर्गुप्ता सार्जुनैश्च महारथैः। धृष्टद्युम्नवशां दुर्गा सागरस्तिमितोपमाम्॥
en: The army was protected by men of terrific strength and by the great car warriors including Arjuna; and under the leadership of Dhrishtadyumna it was still as the sea.

sn: तस्यास्त्वग्रे महेष्वासः पाञ्चाल्यो युद्धदुर्मदः। द्रोणप्रेप्सुरनीकानि धृष्टद्युम्नो व्यकर्षत॥
en: In the van of it were the great bowman, the prince of Panchala, hard to vanquish in battle and Dhrishtadyumna desirous of an encounter with Drona, attributing particular tasks to each warrior.

sn: यथावलं यथोत्साहं रथिनः समुपादिशत्। अर्जुनं सूतपुत्राय भीमं दुर्योधनाय च॥
en: He gave instructions to car warriors each according to his strength and energy; and he appointed Arjuna to fight with the son of a Suta. Bhima with Duryodhana,

sn: धृष्टकेतुं च शल्याय गौतमायोत्तमौजसम्। अश्वत्थाम्ने च नकुलं शैब्यं च कृतवर्मणे॥
en: Dhrishtaketu with Shalya, Uttamanyus with the son of Gautama, Nakula with Ashvathama, Saivya with Kritavarman,

sn: सैन्धवाय च वार्ष्णेयं युयुधानं समादिशत्। शिखण्डिनं च भीष्माय प्रमुख समकल्पयत्॥
en: And he appointed Yuyudhana of the Vrishini race to fight with the king of the Sindhus and also appointed Shikhandin to be in the front for fighting with Bhishma.

sn: सहदेवं शकुनये चेकितानं शलाय वै। द्रौपदेयांस्तथा पञ्च त्रिगर्तेभ्यः समादिशत्॥
en: He also appointed Sahadeva to fight with Shakuni, Chekitana with Shala, and the five sons of Draupadi with the Trigartas,

sn: वृषसेनाय सौभद्रं शेषाणां च महीक्षिताम्। स समर्थं हि तं मेने पार्थादभ्यधिकं रणे॥
en: The son of Subhadra with Vrishasena and the rest of the rulers of the earth for he regarded him (Abhimanyu) as even superior to Arjuna himself in battle.

sn: एवं विभज्य योधास्तान् पृथक् च सह चैव ह। ज्वालावर्णो महेष्वासो द्रोणमंशमकल्पयत्॥
en: Having thus allotted among those warriors separately and collectively their respective tasks, that warrior, of the hue of fire, kept Drona for his own share,

sn: धृष्टद्युम्नो महेष्वासः सेनापतिपतिस्ततः। विधिवद् व्यूह्य मेधावी युद्धाय धृतमानसः॥
en: The great bowman, Dhrishtadyumna, the general of the commander of the army, endued with intelligence, having prepared his troops, duly waited patiently for the battle.

sn: यथोद्दिष्टानि सैन्यानि पाण्डवानामयोजयत्। जयाय पाण्डुपुत्राणां यत्तस्तस्थौ रणाजिरे॥
en: Having arranged the army of the Pandavas as indicated above, he waited calmly on the field of battle for the sake of victory to the sons of Pandu.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच प्रतिज्ञाते फाल्गुनेन वधे भीष्मस्य संयुगे। किमकुर्वत मे मन्दाः पुत्रा दुर्योधनादयः॥
en: Dhritarashtra said The slaying of Bhishma having been promised by Falguna in battle, what did my foolish sons, Duryodhana and others do?

sn: हतमेव हि पश्यामि गाङ्गेयं पितरं रणे। वासुदेवसहायेन पार्थेन दृढधन्वना॥
en: I already see my father, the son of Ganga, slain in battle by the son of Pritha who has a firm grasp on his bow, having Vasudeva for his help-mate.

sn: स चापरिमितप्रज्ञस्तच्छ्रुत्वा पार्थभाषितम्। किमुक्तवान् महेष्वासो भीष्मः प्रहरतां वरः॥
en: What also did, that great bowman Bhishma, that foremost among strikers, endued with unlimited wisdom, say after he had heard what the son of Pritha had said?

sn: सैनापत्यं च सम्प्राप्य कौरवाणां धुरन्धरः। किमचेष्टत गाङ्गेयो महाबुद्धिपराक्रमः॥
en: What did that oldest and foremost of the Kauravas, the of Ganga, of great intelligence and prowess, do after obtaining the generalship?

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततस्ततं संजयस्तस्मै सर्वमेव न्यवेदयत्। यथोक्तं कुरुवृद्धेन भीष्मेणामिततेजसा॥
en: Vaishampayana said Sanjaya then submitted to him every thing as had happened, what had been said by that oldest among the Kurus, Bhishma of immeasurable energy. son

sn: संजय उवाच सैनापत्यमनुप्राप्य भीष्मः शान्तनवो नृप। दुर्योधनमुवाचेदं वचनं हर्षयन्निव॥
en: Sanjaya said Bhishma, the son of Shantanu, having obtained the generalship, said these words to Duryodhana infusing cheerfulness in him.

sn: नमस्कृत्य कुमाराय सेनान्ये शक्तिपाणये। अहं सेनापतिस्तेऽद्य भविष्यामि न संशयः॥
en: “Having bowed down to Kumara, the god of war, who has a lance in his hand, I shall today be your general, no doubt.

sn: सेनाकर्मण्यभिज्ञोऽस्मि व्यूहेषु विविधेषु च। कर्म कारयितुं चैव भृतानप्यभृतांस्तथा॥
en: I am experienced in all matters relating to the army and in diverse artifices and in making the paid soldiers and unpaid ones (volunteers) do their own work.

sn: यात्रायाने च युद्धे च तथा प्रशमनेषु च। भृशं वेद महाराज यथा वेद बृहस्पतिः॥
en: In the matter of marching out troops in fighting and in declaring war I am as much an adept, O great king, as Brihaspati himself.

sn: व्यूहानां च समारम्भान् दैवगान्धर्वमानुषान्। तैरहं मोहयिष्यामि पाण्डवान् व्येतु ते ज्वरः॥
en: I am also conversant with the plans of attack and and defense, adopted by gods, Gandharvas and human beings, and by means of them I shall deprive the sons of Pandu of their senses. Let your fears be gone.

sn: सोऽहं योत्स्यामि तत्त्वेन पालयंस्तव वाहिनीम्। यथावच्छास्त्रतो राजन् व्येतु ते मानसो ज्वरः॥
en: I, who am so, shall fight observing the usual rules and protecting your army according to plans laid down in the holy books. Let your mind's fear be gone."

sn: दुर्योधन उवाच विद्यते मे न गाङ्गेय भयं देवासुरेष्वपि। समस्तेषु महाबाहो सत्यमेतद् ब्रवीमि ते॥
en: Duryodhana said No fear exists in me, O son of Ganga, froin even the gods and Asuras united together, O you of long arm, I tell you this truly.

sn: किं पुनस्त्वयि दुर्धर्षे सैनापत्ये व्यवस्थिते। द्रोणे च पुरुषव्याने स्थिते युद्धाभिनन्दिनि॥
en: How much less reasons have I for fear when I have you as the commander of my armies and that foremost among men, Drona, who takes delight in war, being on my side.

sn: भवद्भ्यां पुरुषाग्याभ्यां स्थिताभ्यां विजये मम। न दुर्लभं कुरुश्रेष्ठ देवराज्यमपि ध्रुवम्॥
en: You, the best among men, being on my side, victory will be mine and foremost among the Kurus, kingship over the gods is surely not hard to get.

sn: रथसंख्यां तु कात्स्न्येन परेषामात्मनस्तथा। तथैवातिरथानां च वेत्तुमिच्छामि कौरव॥
en: I desire to hear, O Kaurava, of the numbers of Rathis (car) warriors capable of fighting with a certain number of each of the four divisions together) and also the number of Atirathas (greater warrior than a Rathi) in our own army and in that of the enemies.

sn: पितामहो हि कुशलः परेषामात्मनस्तथा। श्रोतुमिच्छाम्यहं सर्वैः सहैभिर्वसुधाधिपैः॥
en: Our grandfather is familiar with ourselves as also with our enemies and I desire to hear all about it, along with these rulers of the earth.

sn: भीष्म उवाच गान्धारे शृणु राजेन्द्र रथसंख्यां स्वके बले। ये रथाः पृथिवीपाल तथैवातिरथाश्च ये॥
en: Bhishma said O son of Gandhari. listen to the numbers of । Rathi, O) chief among kings, in your own army, hcar O ruler of the earth, who are the Rathis and who the Atirathis.

sn: बहूनीह सहस्राणि प्रयुतान्यर्बुदानि च। स्थानां तव सेनायां यथामुख्यं तु मे शृणु॥
en: There are thousands and tens of thousands and millions of Rathis in your army; listen to me, as I speak of them.

sn: भवानग्रे रथोदारः सह सर्वैः सहोदरैः। दुःशासनप्रभृतिभिर्धातृभिः शतसम्मितैः॥
en: You, along with all your brothers Dushasana and others, are the foremost among car-warriors. on are

sn: सर्वे कृतप्रहरणाश्छेदभेदविशारदाः। रथोपस्थे गजस्कन्धे गदाप्रासासिचर्मणि॥
en: All of you are experienced in striking, cutting and piercing, and whether riding on chariots, or the elephants you experienced in the use of the mace, the swords and the shields.

sn: संयन्तारः प्रहर्तारः कृतास्त्रा भारसाधनाः। इष्वस्त्रे द्रोणशिष्याश्च कृपस्य च शरद्वतः॥
en: You are also skillful drivers of elephants and chariots, you have mastered the science of weapons, and in the science of arrows you are the pupils of Drona and Kripa, the son of Sharadvata.

sn: एते हनिष्यन्ति रणे पञ्चालान् युद्धदुर्मदान्। कृतकिल्बिषाः पाण्डवेयैर्धार्तराष्ट्रा मनस्विनः॥
en: These will slay in battle the princes of Panchala, hard to be vanquished in battle, for the sons sons of Dhritarashtra, endued with intelligence, have been wronged by the Pandavas.

sn: तथाहं भरतश्रेष्ठ सर्वसेनापतिस्तव। शत्रून् विध्वंसयिष्यामि कद कृत्य पाण्डवान्॥
en: In the same way, I O foremost among the Bharatas, the commander of all your armies, shall slay your enemies after making the prowess of the Pandavas vain and useless.

sn: न त्वात्मनो गुणान् वक्तुमर्हामि विदितोऽस्मि ते। कृतवर्मा त्वतिरथो भोजः शस्त्रभृतां वरः॥
en: It is not proper for me to describe my own qualifications; it is all known to you. The foremost of wielders of weapons, the king of the Bhojas, Kritavarman is an Atiratha (mightier car warrior).

sn: अर्थसिद्धिं तव रणे करिष्यति न संशयः। शस्त्रविद्भिरनाधृष्यो दूरपाती दृढायुधः॥
en: He will make your object in fighting successful, no doubt for he is invincible among those familiar with the use of weapons and can hurl arms to a long distance and can hold firmly his weapons.

sn: हनिष्यति चमूं तेषां महेन्द्रो दानवानिव। मद्रराजो महेष्वासः शल्यो मेऽतिरथो मतः॥
en: He will slay this army like the great Indra slaying the Danavas. In my opinion, the great bowman Shalya, the king of the Madras, is an Atiratha,

sn: स्पर्धते वासुदेवेन नित्यं यो वै रणे रणे। भागिनेयान् निजांस्त्यक्त्वा शल्यस्तेऽतिरथो मतः।
en: Who ever considers him an equal to Vasudeva in every battle; abandoning his own nephews (sister's sons) Shalya that Atiratha, has came over to your side.

sn: एष योत्स्यति संग्रामे पाण्डवांश्च महारथान्॥ सागरोमिसमैर्बाणैः प्लावयन्निव शात्रवान्। भूरिश्रवाः कृतास्त्रश्च तव चापि हितः सुहृत्॥
en: These will fight in the battle with those great car warriors on the Pandavas side covering the enemies with arrows as ways covering the open. Bhurishravas, that master in the use of weapons, is also your will wisher.

sn: सौमदत्तिर्महेष्वासो रथयूथपयूथपः। बलक्षयममित्राणां सुमहान्तं करिष्यति॥
en: The son of Somadatta, that mighty bowman, is a leader of the commanders of car warriors and he will effect a very great reduction in the strength of the enemy.

sn: सिन्धुराजो महाराज मतो मे द्विगुणो रथः। योत्स्यते समरे राजन् विक्रान्तो रथसत्तमः॥
en: In my opinion, O great king, the king of the Sindhus is twice a car warrior and that powerful and best among the car warriors will fight in the battle, O king.

sn: द्रौपदीहरणे राजन् परिक्लिष्टश्च पाण्डवैः। संस्मरंस्तं परिक्लेशं योत्स्यते परवीरहा।॥
en: Persecuted by the Pandavas, O king, in his attempt to carry away Draupadi, that slayer of hostile heroes will fight remembering that trouble.

sn: एतेन हि तदा रांजस्तप आस्थाय दारुणम्। सुदुर्लभो वरो लब्धः पाण्डवान् योद्धमाहवे।॥
en: After that defeat, severe austerities were practiced by him O king; he has obtained a boon, difficult to get, of fighting with the Pandavas in battle.

sn: स एष रथशार्दूलस्तद् वैरं संस्मरन् रणे। योत्स्यते पाण्डवस्तात प्राणांस्त्यक्त्वा सुदुस्त्यजान्॥३३
en: This foremost among the car warriors, therefore, remembering all this in battle, will fight with the Pandavas, my dear son, even careless of life which is hard to lay down.

sn: भीष्म उवाच सुदक्षिणस्तु काम्बोजो रथ एकगुणो मतः तवार्थसिद्धिमाकाङ्क्षन् योत्स्यते समरे परैः॥
en: Bhishma said In my opinion Sudakshina, of Kamboja, is equal to one Ratha and he will fight in the battle with the enemy desiring the success of your objects.

sn: एतस्य रथसिंहस्य तवार्थं राजसत्तम। पराक्रमं यथेन्द्रस्य द्रक्ष्यन्ति कुरवो युधि॥
en: The prowess of this best among car warriors excited on your behalf, O best among kings, the Kurus in battle with see equal to that of Indra himself.

sn: एतस्य रथवंशे हि तिग्मवेगप्रहारिणः। काम्बोजानां महाराज शलभानामिवायतिः॥
en: The best of car warriors under him are strikers with fierce force. The Kambojas, o great king, will cover like the land like a swarm of locusts.

sn: नीलो माहिष्मतीवासो नीलवर्मा रथस्तव। रथवंशेन कदनं शत्रूणां वै करिष्यति॥
en: Nil of Mahishmati clad in a blue coat of mail is a Ratha of your army and with the car warriors under him he will work havoc among the enemy.

sn: कृतवैरः पुरा चैव सहदेवेन मारिष। योत्स्यते सततं राजंस्तवार्थं कुरुनन्दन॥
en: My child, in former days, he was made an enemy by Sahadeva, and he will ever fight on your behalf, O you delighter of the Kuru race.

sn: विन्दानुविन्दावावन्त्यौ संमतौ रथसत्तमौ। कृतिनौ समरे तात दृढवीर्यपराक्रमौ॥
en: In my opinion Vindu and Anuvindu, the princes of Avanti, accomplished in battle and of firm strength and prowess are two of the best Rathas.

sn: एतौ तौ पुरुषव्याघ्रौ रिपुसैन्यं प्रधक्ष्यतः। गदाप्रासासिनाराचैस्तोमरैश्च करच्युतैः॥
en: These two best among men will consume the army of enemy with maces, bearded darts, swords, muskets and long shafts hurled from their hands.

sn: युद्धाभिकामौ समरे क्रीडन्ताविव यूथपौ। यूथमध्ये महाराज विचरन्तौ कृतान्तवत्॥
en: Desirous of war they will act in battle each like Yama like two sporting elephants moving in the midst of a herd, O king.

sn: त्रिगर्ता भ्रातरः पञ्च रथोदारा मता मम। कृतवैराश्च पार्थस्ते विराटनगरे तदा॥
en: In my opinion, the five Trigarta brothers are Rathas and they were made enemies by the sons of Pritha while in the city of Virata.

sn: मकरा इव राजेन्द्र समुद्धततरङ्गिणीम्। गङ्गा विक्षोभयिष्यन्ति पार्थानां युधि वाहिनीम्॥
en: In the battle, they will agitate the army of the son of Pritha like Makaras agitating the Ganga swollen with its waves.

sn: ते रथाः पञ्च राजेन्द्र येषां सत्यरथो मुखम्। एते योत्स्यन्ति संग्रामे संस्मरन्तः पुराकृतम्॥
en: They are Rathas, O chief among kings, at whose head is Satyaratha and they will fight in the battle remembering the former wrongs.

sn: व्यलीकं पाण्डवेयेन भीमसेनानुजेन ह। दिशो विजयता राजन् श्वेतवाहेन भारत॥
en: They were injured by Bhima's younger brother Arjuna, the son of Pandu, O king, when on a car drawn by white steeds, O Bharata, he went out to conquer all the quarters.

sn: ते हनिष्यन्ति पार्थानां तानासाद्य महारथान्। वरान् वरान् महेष्वासान् क्षत्रियाणां धुरन्धरान्॥
en: Having encountered many car warriors, chiefs of bowmen and leaders of Kshatriyas on the side of Parthas they will forsooth kill them

sn: लक्ष्मणस्तव पुत्रश्च तथा दुःशासनस्य च। उभौ तौ पुरुषव्याघ्रौ संग्रामेष्वपलायिनौ॥
en: Your son Lakshmana and the son of Dushasana, both these foremost among men can never fly back from the battle.

sn: तरुणौ सुकुमारौ च राजपुत्रौ तरस्विनौ। युद्धानां च विशेषज्ञौ प्रणेतारौ च सर्वशः॥
en: The two young and delicate princes are of light hand and know all the details of fighting and are in every way fit to be leaders.

sn: रथौ तौ कुरुशार्दूल मतौ मे रथसत्तमौ। क्षत्रधर्मरतौ वीरौ महत् कर्म करिष्यतः॥
en: These two, O foremost among the Kurus, i am of opinion, are Rathas, and the heroes attached as they are to the duties of the Kshatriya will perform noble deeds.

sn: दण्डधारौ महाराज रथ एको नरर्षभ। योत्स्यते तव संग्रामे स्वेन सैन्येन पालितः॥
en: That foremost among men, Dandadhara, O great king, is a Ratha and he will fight in your battle protected by his own army.

sn: बृहद्बलस्तथा राजा कौसल्यो रथसत्तमः। रथो मम मतस्तात महावेगपराक्रमः॥
en: Brihadbala, too, O king, the prince of the Shalyas, is one of the best among car warriors and is a Ratha, in my opinion, of great impetuosity and prowess.

sn: एष योत्स्यति संग्रामे स्वान् बन्धून् सम्प्रहर्षयन्। उग्रायुधो महेष्वासो धार्तराष्ट्रहिते रतः॥
en: He will fight in the battle delighting his own friends, a wielder of terrible weapons as he is and a mighty bowman devoted to the good of the son of Dhritarashtra.

sn: कृपः शारद्वतो राजन् रथयूथपयूथपः। प्रियान् प्राणान् परित्यज्य प्रधक्ष्यति रिपूंस्तव॥
en: Kripa, the son of Sharadvata, Oking, is the general of the commanders of the Rathas, and careless of his dear life he will consume your enemies.

sn: गौतमस्य महर्षर्य आचार्यस्य शरद्वतः। कार्तिकेय इवाजेयः शरस्तम्बात् सुतोऽभवत्॥
en: The son of the great Rishi Gautama, or the preceptor Sharadvata, born on a clump of health, is invincible as the war god Kartikeya himself.

sn: एष सेना: सुबहुला विविधायुधकार्मुकाः। अग्निवत् समरे तात चरिष्यति विनिर्दहन्॥
en: Destroying this army strong in numbers and furnished with diverse weapons and bows he will roll in the battle like blazing fire.

sn: भीष्म उवाच शकुनिर्मातुलस्तेऽसौ रथ एको नराधिप। प्रयुज्य पाण्डवैर्वैरं योत्स्यते नात्र संशयः॥
en: Bhishma said This Shakuni, your maternal uncle, is equal to a single Ratha, O ruler of men; and having brought about hostility with the Pandavas he will fight, there is no doubt of it.

sn: एतस्य सेना दुर्धर्षा समरे प्रतियायिनः। विकृतायुधभूयिष्ठा वायुवेगसमा जवे॥
en: His army when rushing to battle, is hard to vanquish; and furnished with plenty of weapons of all sorts they are of the velocity of the wind in battle.

sn: द्रोणपुत्रो महेष्वासः सर्वानेवाति धन्विनः। समरे चित्रयोधी च दृढास्त्रश्च महारथः॥
en: That mighty bowman, the son of Drona (Ashvathama) surpasses all bowmen and is familiar with diverse modes of warfare and is of firm weapons; he is a Maharatha.

sn: एतस्य हि महाराज यथा गाण्डीवधन्वनः। शरासनविनिर्मुक्ताः संसक्ता यान्ति सायकाः॥
en: The arrows, shot by him from his bow as by the wielder of the Gandiva bow, proceed touching one another.

sn: नैष शक्यो मया वीरः संख्यातुं रथसत्तमः। निर्दहेदपि लोकांस्त्रीनिच्छन्नेष महारथः॥
en: This best among the Rathas, this hero cannot be described by me; if this Maharatha wishes he can burn up the three worlds.

sn: क्रोधस्तेजश्च तपसा सम्भृतोऽऽश्रमवासिनाम्। द्रोणैनानुगृहीतश्च दिव्यैरस्त्रैरुदारधीः॥
en: He has accumulated wrath and energy by his austerities while living in the hermitage. has been favored by Drona with celestial weapons.

sn: दोषस्त्वस्य महानेको येनैव भरतर्षभ। न मे रथो नातिरथो मतः पार्थिवसत्तमः॥
en: He has however a great draw back owing to which, O foremost of the Bharata race, I do not consider him as a Ratha or an Atiratha, O best among the rulers of the earth.

sn: जीवितं प्रियमत्यर्थमायुष्कामः सदा द्विजः। न ह्यस्य सदृशः कश्चिदुभयोः सेनयोरपि॥
en: He is excessively fond of life and that regenerate young man is always desirous of living but there is no body similar to him in the armies of both the parties.

sn: हन्यादेकरथेनैव देवानामपि वाहिनीम्। वपुष्मांस्तलघोषेण स्फोटयेदपि पर्वतान्॥
en: By means of single of a single chariot can he slay even the army of the gods; and by the flaps of his bowstring striking against the leather fence on his left arm, that one, possessed of a powerful body, can rend asunder the mountains.

sn: असंख्येयगुणो वीरः प्रहर्ता दारुणद्युतिः। दण्डपाणिरिवासह्यः कालवत् प्रचरिष्यति।॥
en: The heroic smiter, of fierce effulgence, has many accomplishments and he will wander about like death himself with rod in hand.

sn: युगान्ताग्निसमः क्रोधात् सिंहग्रीवो महाद्युतिः। एष भारतयुद्धस्य पृष्ठः संशमयिष्यति॥
en: Having the shoulders of a lion and endued with great effulgence he will, like the fire that rages at the end of Yuga, extinguish the embers of this battle between the Bharatas.

sn: पिता त्वस्य महातेजा वृद्धोऽपि युवभिर्वरः। रणे कर्म महत् कर्ता अत्र मे नास्ति संशयः॥
en: His father, endued with great energy, is better then young persons though he is himself old and he will be the doer of great deeds in battle, of this I have no doubt.

sn: अस्त्रवेगानिलोद्भूतः सेनाकक्षेन्धनोत्थितः। पाण्डुपुत्रस्य सैन्यानि प्रधक्ष्यति रणे धृतः॥
en: Resembling the having its source in the dry grass and fuel in the shape of your army and fanned by the force of our weapons, our soldiers will surely consume those on the side of the son of Pandu in battle.

sn: रथयूथपयूथानां यूथपोऽयं नरर्षभः। भारद्वाजात्मजः कर्ता कर्म तीवं हितं तव॥
en: This foremost among men, the son of Bharadvaja, is the leader groups of car-leaders and will be the doer of fierce deeds.

sn: सर्वपूर्धाभिषिक्तानामाचार्य: स्थविरो गुरुः। गच्छेदन्तं संजयानां प्रियस्त्वस्य धनंजयः॥
en: The aged preceptor, the spiritual guide of all those who have undergone the ceremony of investiture on the head, will put an end to all the Srinjayas but Dhananjaya is dear to him.

sn: नैष जातु महेष्वासः पार्थमक्लिष्टकारिणम्। हन्यादाचार्यक दीप्तं संस्मृत्य गुणनिर्जितम्॥
en: The great bowman, remembering the blazing virtues acquired by the son of Pritha and his own relation towards him as a preceptor, will never, be able to kill him who accomplishes things without exertion,

sn: श्लाघतेऽयं सदा वीर पार्थस्य गुणविस्तरैः। पुत्रादभ्यधिकं चैनं भारद्वाजोऽनुपश्यति॥
en: This one (Drona) ever prides himself on the many accomplishments of the son of Pritha, O hero, and the son of Bharadvaja looks on him with greater affection than on his own son.

sn: हन्यादेकरथेनैव देवगन्धर्वमानुषान्। एकीभूतानपि रणे दिव्यैरस्त्रैः प्रजापवान्॥
en: With the assistance of a single car he can slay the gods, the Gandharvas and the human beings united together, with the aid of his heavenly weapons.

sn: पौरवो राजशार्दूलस्तव राजन् महारथः। मतो मम रथोदारः परवीररथारुजः॥
en: That foremost of king, Pauravas, on your side, is a Maharatha, o king; such is my opinion; he is one of the foremost among carwarriors and will work havoc among the heroes on the enemies' side.

sn: स्वेन सैन्येन महता प्रतपन् शत्रुवाहिनीम्। प्रधक्ष्यति स पञ्चालान् कक्षमग्निगतिर्यथा॥
en: With his own large army affecting the army of his enemies he will consume the Panchalas as the course of fire does the dry grass.

sn: सत्यश्रवा रथस्त्वेको राजपुत्रो बृहद्बलः। तव राजन् रिपुबले कालवत् प्रचरिष्यति॥
en: Satyashravas that prince of great strength, is a Ratha on your side, ( king and he will work havoc among the armies of the enemies like Death himself.

sn: एतस्य योधा राजेन्द्र विचित्रकवचायुधाः। विचरिष्यन्ति संग्रामे निघ्नन्तः शात्रवांस्तव॥
en: His soldiers, O chief among kings, clad in diverse kinds of amours and arıncd with diverse weapons, will roam about in the battle killing your enemies.

sn: वृषसेनो रथस्तेऽग्यः कर्णपुत्रो महारथः । प्रधक्ष्यति रिपूणां ते बलं तु बलिनां वरः॥
en: That great car warrior, Vrishasena, the son of Karna is one of the foremost of the carwarriors on your side; and that foremost among mighty persons will consume the army of your enemies.

sn: जलसंधो महातेजो राजन् रथवरस्तव। त्यक्ष्यते समरे प्राणान् माधवः परवीरहा॥
en: Jalasandha, of great energy, is one of the foremost of the Rathas on your side. That scion of the race of Madhu, that slayer of hostile heroes, can even sacrifice his life in battle.

sn: एष योत्स्यति संग्रामे गजस्कन्धविशारदः। रथेन वा महाबाहुः क्षपयन् शत्रुवाहिनीम्॥
en: Conversant with the science of war. that one of long arms having the shoulders of an elephant will fight in battle scattering the hostile army, seated on a chariot.

sn: रथ एष महाराज मतो मे राजसत्तम। त्वदर्थं त्यक्ष्यते प्राणान् सहसैन्यो महारणे॥
en: The best among kings is Ratha in my opinion, O great king, and for your sake he will sacrifice his life a along his army in this greet battle.

sn: एष विक्रान्तयोधी च चित्रयोधी च सङ्गरे। वीतभीश्चापि ते राजन् शत्रुभिः सह योत्स्यते॥
en: This one is a mighty warrior and knows to fight according to diverse methods in battle; and O king, he will fight with your enemies casting fear aside.

sn: बाह्रीकोऽतिरथश्चैव समरे चानिवर्तनः। मम राजन् मतो युद्धे शूरो वैवस्वतोपमः॥
en: Balhika, who never turns his back on the field of battle, is an Atiratha, O great king; such is my opinion and that hero is equal to the sun himself.

sn: न ह्येष समरं प्राप्य निवर्तेत कथञ्चन। यथा सततगो राजन् स हि हन्यात् परान् रणे॥
en: Having once reached the field, he will never turn back and he will slay the enemies in battle as continuously as the wind blows.

sn: सेनापतिर्महाराज सत्यवांस्ते महारथः। रणेष्वद्भुतकर्मा च रथी पररथारुजः॥
en: Satyavana, the leader of your armies, O great king, is Maharatha. A car-warrior himself, he is the doer of wonders in battle and works havoc among the enemies' charioteers.

sn: एतस्य समरं दृष्ट्वा न व्यथास्ति कथञ्चन) उत्स्मयन्नुत्पत्येषु परान् रथप स्थितान्॥
en: He will certainly not be pained at the sight of battle and he will inspire those of the enemy's soldiers who stand in the way of his chariot with wonder,

sn: एष चारिषु विक्रान्तः कर्म सत्पुरुषोचितम्। कर्ता विमर्दै सुमहत् त्वदर्थं पुरुषोतमः॥
en: Showing his strength against his enemies, a thing which is the duty of every good man, this best among men will be the doer of great deeds in your favour,

sn: अलम्बुषो राक्षसेन्द्रः क्रूरकर्मा महारथः। हनिष्यति परान् राजन् पूर्ववैरमनुस्मरन्॥
en: Alambusha, that chief of the Rakshashas of hard deeds, is a Maharatha and O king he will slay the enemies remembering the old enmity.

sn: एष राक्षससैन्यानां सर्वेषां रथसत्तमः। मायावी दृढयैरश्च समरे विचरिष्यति॥
en: He is the best car warrior among all the Rakshasas, and being endued with the powers of illusion he will roam about in the field like an inveterate enemy.

sn: प्राग्ज्योतिषाधिपो वीरो भगदत्तः प्रतापवान्। गजाङ्कुशधरश्रेष्ठी रथे चैव विशारदः॥
en: The hero Bhagadatta, the ruler of the Pragjyotisha, endued with fame, is one of the foremost among the wielders of the hook of the elephant and is also skillful in fighting form the chariot.

sn: एतेन युद्धमभवत् पुरा गाण्डीवधन्वनः। दिवसान् सुबहून् राजन्नुभयोर्जयगृद्धिनोः॥
en: In days of the old there took place a fight between him and the holder of Gandiva, for a number of days, O king, each being desirous of victory over the other.

sn: ततः सखायं गान्धारे मानयन् पाकशासनम्। अकरोत् संविदं तेन पाण्डवेन महात्मना।॥
en: O son of Gandhari, then did he, who thinks Indra to friend, conclude peace with that great souled son of Pandu.

sn: एष योत्स्यति संग्रामे गजस्कन्धविशारदः। ऐरावतगतो राजा देवानामिव वासवः॥
en: This one of shoulders like those of elephants and skillful in battle will fight, O king, like Vasava on the back of the Airavata with the gods.

sn: भीष्म उवाच अचलो वृषकश्चैव सहितौ भ्रातरावुभौ। रथौ तव दुराधर्षी शत्रून् विध्वंसयिष्यतः॥
en: Bhishma said Achala and Vrishaka are two Rathas on your side who are hard to vanquish; both the brothers, united together, will destroy your enemies.

sn: बलवन्तौ नरव्याघ्रौ दृढक्रोधौ प्रहारिणौ। गान्धारमुख्यौ तरुणौ दर्शनीयौ महाबलौ॥
en: These two best among men are mighty, inveterate in their hatred and smiters (of enemies); they are the foremost among the Gandharis, young, handsome and endued with great strength.

sn: सखा ते दयितो नित्यं य एष रणकर्कशः। उत्साहयति राजंस्त्वां विग्रहे पाण्डवैः सह॥
en: But this one who is ever your dear friend, who vaunts of bravery in battle and who encourages you, O king in your dispute with the Pandavas,

sn: परुषः कत्थनो नीचः कर्णो वैकर्तनस्तव। मन्त्री नेता च बन्धुश्च मानी चात्यन्तमुच्छ्रितः॥
en: This man vain and mean, Karna, the son of Vikartana, who is your adviser guide and friend, and who has been placed in too elevated a position by you,

sn: एष कर्णो न चाप्यतिरथो रणे। वियुक्तः कवचेनैष सहजेन विचेतनः॥ कुण्डलाभ्यां च दिव्याभ्यां वियुक्तः सततं घृणी। अभिशापाच्च रामस्य ब्राह्मणस्य च भाषणात्॥
en: This Karna is neither a Rathi nor an Atiratha in battle. Though ever generous he has been deprived of his celestial earrings. All this is owing to the curse of Rama (his preceptor) and the words of a Brahmana.

sn: करणानां वियोगाच्च तेन मेऽर्धरथो मतः। नैष फाल्गुनमासाद्य पुनर्जीवन् विमोक्ष्यसे॥
en: Owing to his being without his natural coat of mail he a Ratha in my opinion; and having once come across Falguna he will not escape him with life.

sn: ततोऽब्रवीत् पुनर्दोणः सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वरः। एवमेतद् यथाऽऽत्य त्वं न मिथ्यास्ति कदाचन॥
en: Then did Drona, the foremost among all wielders, of say as a rejoinder: "It is so; what you say is never false.

sn: नैव रथः रणे रणेऽभिमानी च विमुखश्चापि दृश्यते। घृणी कर्णः प्रमादी च तेन मेऽर्धरथो मतः॥
en: In each battle is he boastful and in each he is seen to be backward. Karna is kind and also becomes confounded; he is therefore in my opinion, to half a Ratha."

sn: एतच्चछ्रुत्वा तु राधेयः क्रोधादुत्फाल्य लोचने। उवाच भीष्मं राधेयस्तुदन् वाग्भिः प्रतोदवत्॥१०
en: Hearing this, the son of Radha, expanding his eyes in wrath, said to Bhishma piercing him with his hook of words.

sn: पितामह यथेष्टं मां वाक्शरैरुपकृन्तसि। अनागसं सदा द्वेषादेवमेव पदे पदे॥
en: "O grandfather, at your pleasure, do you pierce me by your arrows of words; at every step do you thus treat me out of your aversion for me, though I have committed no sin.

sn: मर्षयामि च तत् सर्वं दुर्योधनकृतेन वै। त्वं तु मां मन्यसे मन्दं यथा कापुरुषं तथा॥
en: I tolerate all his however for the sake of Duryodhana,; you deem me to be behind others (in fight) and a coward.

sn: भवानर्धरथो मह्यं मतो वै नात्र संशयः। सर्वस्य जगतश्चैव गाङ्गेयो न मृषा वदेत्॥
en: In my opinion you too are only half a Ratha, there is no doubt about this. O son of Ganga, I do not speak an untruth when I say that you are an enemy of the entire universe.

sn: कुरूणामहितो नित्यं न च राजाऽवबुध्यते। को हि नाम समानेषु राजसूदारकर्मसु॥
en: You are ever devoted to what is to the injury of the Kurus, But the king knows it not. Who else is there who would seek to sap the energy of these kings that are equal and create discord among them,

sn: तेजोवधमिमं कुर्याद् विभेदयिषुराहवे। यथा त्वं गुणविद्वेषादपरागं चिकीर्षसि॥
en: As you desire to do owing to your hatred towards these that endued with accomplishments. Neither age, nor wealth, nor friends,

sn: न हायनैर्न पलितैर्न वित्तैर्न च बन्धुभिः। महारथत्वं संख्यातुं शक्यं क्षत्रस्य कौरव॥
en: are Can entitle a Kshatriya to be included in the category of Maharathas, O Kaurava. It is well-know a Kshatriya is superior by virtue of his strength and that the twice-born are superior by virtue of their learning.

sn: बलज्येष्ठं स्मृतं क्षत्रं मन्त्रज्येष्ठा द्विजातयः। धनज्येष्ठाः स्मृता वैश्याः शूद्रास्तु वयसाधिकाः॥
en: It is also well-known that Vaishyas are superior by virtue of their wealth and that Sudras are superiors by virtue of their years. Speak for yourself then, as you please, your list of Rathas and Atirathas.

sn: यथेच्छकं स्वयं ब्रूया रथानतिरथांस्तथा। कामद्वेषसमायुक्तो मोहात् प्रकुरुते भवान्॥
en: Actuated by desire and hatred and acting from ignorance you have enumerated the heroes. O Duryodhana of long arms, it is for you to judge properly. May you fare well.

sn: दुर्योधन महाबाहो साधु सम्यगवेक्ष्यताम्। त्यज्यतां दुष्टभावोऽयं भीष्मः किल्बिषकृत् तव॥
en: Abandon this wicked Bhishma of unrighteous nature for, O ruler of men, discord once being in your own army it will be difficult to bring union again.

sn: भिन्ना हि सेना नृपते दुःसंधेया भवत्युत। मौला हि पुरुषव्याघ्र किमु नानासमुत्थिताः॥
en: This remark applies to your main army, judge then about the subsidiary forces which have been raised from several sources.

sn: एषां द्वैधं समुत्पन्नं योधानां युधि भारत। तेजोवधो नः क्रियते प्रत्यक्षेण विशेषतः॥
en: This discord has entered among warriors, already, 0 Bharata; in our very presence he saps our energies.

sn: रथानां क्क च विज्ञानं क्व च भीष्मोऽल्पचेतनः। अहमावारयिष्यामि पाण्डवानामनीकिनीम्॥
en: How vast is the difference between the task of estimating the might of Rathas and Bhishma of little intellect. I will meet the armies of the Pandavas.

sn: आसाद्य माममोधेषु गमिष्यन्ति दिशो दश। पाण्डवाः सहपञ्चालाः शार्दूलं वृषभा इव॥
en: Standing against me who are infallible they will be routed in ten directions, the Pandavas with the Panchalas, like bulls meeting with a tiger.

sn: क्व च युद्धं विमर्दो वा मन्त्रे सुव्याहतानि च। क्व च भीष्मो गतवया मन्दात्मा कालचोदितः॥
en: How vast is the difference between real fight, the clash of weapons, good advice, uttered in sweet sounding words on one side and Bhishma who is past the prime of life, of wicked soul and who is urged by fate.

sn: एकाकी स्पर्धते नित्यं सर्वेण जगत सह। न चान्यं पुरुषं कंचिन्मन्यते मोघदर्शनः॥
en: Alone he even boasts to fight with the entire universe, and endued with false vision he does not regard any other man as a human being.

sn: श्रोतव्यं खलु वृद्धानामिति शास्त्रनिदर्शनम्। न त्वेव ह्यतिवृद्धानां पुनर्बाला हि ते मताः॥
en: Certainly, it has been laid down in our holy books that the words of the aged should be listened to, but it does not apply to those who are very old for they are held to be boys.

sn: अहमेको हनिष्यामि पाण्डवानामनीकिनीम्। सुयुद्धे राजशार्दूल यशो भीष्मं गमिष्यति॥
en: Alone I shall slay the army of the sons of Pandu in a fair fight. The fame however of this will go to Bhishma, O best among kings.

sn: कृतः सेनापतिस्त्वेष त्वया भीष्मो नराधिप। सेनापतौ यशो गन्ता न तु योधान् कथंचन॥
en: By you, O ruler of men, has Bhishma been appointed the commander and all fame goes to the leader and never to an individual soldier.

sn: नाहं जीवति गाङ्गेये योत्स्ये राजन् कथंचन। हते भीष्मे तु योद्धास्मि सर्वैरेव महारथैः॥
en: O king, never shall I fight as long as the son of Ganga is alive. When Bhishma is killed I shall fight with all the car-warriors."

sn: भीष्म उवाच समुद्यतोऽयं भारो मे सुमहान् सागरोपमः। धार्तराष्ट्रस्य संग्रामे वर्षपूगाभिचिन्तितः॥
en: Bhishma said The great burden (the impending fight) vast as the ocean is ready to fall on me, a calamity which I had foreseen for a series of years,

sn: तस्मिन्नभ्यागते काले प्रतप्ते लोमहर्षणे। मिथो भेदो न मे कार्यस्तेन जीवसि सूतज॥
en: Now is come that time, that fight the result of which makes our hairs stand on end. It is not my concern to create dispute among ourselves. It is for this that you now live, O you born of a Suta.

sn: न ह्यहं त्वद्य विक्रम्य स्थविरोऽपि शिशोस्तव। युद्धश्रद्धामहं छिन्द्यां जीवितस्य च सूतज॥
en: For though I am now aged and you but young I shall rend asunder your desire for battle and that of your own life, O you born of a Suta.

sn: जामदग्न्येन रामेण महास्त्राणि विमुञ्चता। न मे व्यथा कृता काचित् त्वं तु मे किं करिष्यसि॥३३
en: The weapons hurled at me by Rama the son of Jamadagni did not pain me, What can you do to me then?

sn: कामं नैतत् प्रशंसन्ति सन्तः स्वबलसंस्तवम्। वक्ष्यामि तु त्वां संतप्तो निहीनकुलपांसन।॥
en: Good men do not approve of this praise of one's own might. I speak thus (on this occasion) for I have lost my temper O vile one; the stain of your family.

sn: समेतं पार्थिवं क्षत्रं काशिराजस्वयंवरे। निर्जित्यैकरथेनैव याः कन्यास्तरसा हृताः॥
en: In the election of a bridegroom by the daughters of Kashiraja, I, after defeating all the rulers of the earth united together, took away those girls by force.

sn: ईदृशानां सहस्राणि विशिष्टानामथो पुनः। मयैकेन निरस्तानि ससैन्यानि रणाजिरे॥
en: Thousands of such kings, well known names too, along with their armies, were stopped in the battle by me alone.

sn: त्वां प्राप्य वैरपुरुषं कुरूणामनयो महान्। उपस्थितो विनाशाय यतस्व पुरुषो भव॥
en: Having come across yourself, an illustrated man, the Kurus have come upon a great disaster; try to mete out destruction and be a man.

sn: युद्ध्यस्व समरे पार्थं येन विस्पर्धसे सहा द्रक्ष्यामि त्वां विनिर्मुक्तमस्माद् युद्धात् सुदुर्मते॥
en: In the battle, fight with son of Pritha, whom you are now challenging and I sha'l see how you escape out of that fight, O you of exceedingly wicked intelligence."

sn: तमुवाच ततो राजा धार्तराष्ट्रः प्रतापवान्। मां समीक्षस्व गाङ्गेय कार्यं हि महदुद्यतम्॥
en: Then did the royal son of Dhritarashtra, endued with fame say to him, Look to me, O son of Ganga; the task which has devolved on you is great.

sn: चिन्त्यतामिदमेकाग्रं मम निःश्रेयसं परम्। उभावपि भवन्तौ मे महत् कर्म करिष्यतः॥
en: Think with your entire heart of my interests; both of you will do great deeds for me.

sn: भूयश्च श्रोतुमिच्छामि परेषां रथसत्तमान्। ये चैवातिरथास्तत्र ये चैव रथयूथपाः॥
en: Again do I desire to hear about the best of the car-warriors of the enemy, those who are Atirathas in that side and those that can lead numbers of chariots.

sn: बलाबलममित्राणां श्रोतुमिच्छामि कौरव। प्रभातायां रजन्यां वै इदं युद्धं भविष्यति॥
en: O son of Kuru, I desire to hear of the strength and weakness of the enemies for the fight is to take place at the dawn of night.”

sn: भीष्म उवाच एते रथास्तवाख्यातास्तथैवातिरथा नृप। ये चाप्यर्धरथा राजन् पाण्डवानामत: शृणु।॥
en: Bhishma said These are the notable Rathas and Atirathas on your side, O ruler of men, and these, o king, are semi-Rathas; listen now to those of the Pandavas.

sn: यदि कौतूहलं तेऽद्य पाण्डवानां बले नृप। रथसंख्यां शृणुष्व त्वं सहैभिर्वसुधाधिपः॥
en: If you have now any curiosity to learn of the strength of the Pandavas, O ruler of men, then listen to the list of their Rathas along with these rulers of the earth.

sn: स्वयं राजा रथोदारः पाण्डवः कुन्तिनन्दनः। अग्निवत् समरे तात चरिष्यति न संशयः॥
en: The king, the son of Pandu and the delight of Kunti, is himself a mighty Ratha; and my dear son, he will roam about in the battle like fire itself; there in no doubt.

sn: भीमसेनस्तु राजेन्द्र रथोऽष्टगुणसम्मितः। न तस्यास्ति समो युद्धे गदया सायकैरपि।॥
en: Bhimasena, O chief among kings, is held to be eight times a Ratha and in a fight with the mace or arrows he has no equal.

sn: नागायुतबलो मानी तेजसा न स मानुषः। माद्रीपुत्रौ च रथिनौ द्वावेष पुरुषर्षभौ॥
en: Filled with pride and endued with the strength of ten thousand elephants he is not human is energy; the two foremost among men, the sons of Madri, are two Rathas.

sn: अश्विनाविव रूपेण तेजसा च समन्वितौ। एते चमूमुपगताः स्मरन्तः क्लेशमुत्तमम्॥
en: Like the Ashvins in beauty and endued also with energy these two will fight in the very van on their army remembering their hard sufferings.

sn: रुद्रवत् प्रचरिष्यन्ति तत्र मे नास्ति संशयः। सर्व एव महात्मानः शालस्तम्भा इवोद्गताः॥
en: They will roam about like so many Rudras, of that there is no doubt. All of them are great-souled and tall as the trunks of Shala trees.

sn: प्रादेशेनाधिकाः पुम्भिरन्यैस्ते च प्रमाणतः। सिंहसंहननाः सर्वे पाण्डुपुत्रा महाबलाः॥
en: Measuring a span more than other males, all the sons of Pandu, capable of killing lions, are endued with great strength.

sn: चरितब्रह्मचर्याश्च सर्वे तात तपस्विनः। ह्रीमन्तः पुरुषव्याघ्रा व्याघ्रा इव बलोत्कटाः॥
en: All of them are devotees, my dear son, and Brahmacharyya vows have been practised by all of them; endued with modesty, those foremost among men are of fierce strength as the tigers.

sn: जवे प्रहारे सम्म सर्व एवातिमानुषाः। सर्वैर्जिता महीपाला दिग्जये भरतर्षभ॥
en: In impetuosity, in striking and crushing all of them are superhuman and by them by all the rulers of the earth had been vanquished at the time of the universal conquest.

sn: न चैषां पुरुषाः केचिदायुधानि गदाः शरान्। विषहन्ति सदा कर्तुमधिज्यान्यपि कौरव॥
en: No human being can bear their weapons, maces and arrows, none can even adjust the string at the time of using the bow, O son of Kuru.

sn: उद्यन्तं वा गदा गुर्वीः शरान् वा क्षेप्तुमाहवे। जवे लक्ष्यस्य हरणे भोज्ये पांसुविकर्षणे॥
en: In uplifting maces, in shooting arrows, in hitting the target, in eating and in sporting in the dust,

sn: बालैरपि भवन्तस्तैः सर्व एव विशेषिताः। एतत् सैन्यं समासाद्य सर्व एव बलोत्कटाः॥
en: Even as children there was great difference between yourself and them. They, all of whom are endued with fierce strength, meeting this army,

sn: विध्वंसयिष्यन्ति रणे मा स्म तैः सह सङ्गमः। एकैकशस्ते सम्पर्दे हन्युः सर्वान् महीक्षितः॥
en: Will destroy them in battle; let there therefore be no encounter with them. In the press of battle, each of them can alone slay the entire universe.

sn: प्रत्यक्षं तव राजेन्द्र राजसूये यथाऽभवत्। द्रौपद्याश्च परिक्लेश द्युते च परुषा गिरः॥
en: It was in your presence, O chief among kings, namely what happened in the Rajasuya. The sufferings of Draupadi and the harsh words at the game of vice,

sn: ते स्मरन्तश्च संग्रामे चरिष्यन्ति च रुद्रवत्। लोहिताक्षो गुडाकेशो नारायणसहायवान्॥
en: Remembering these they will wander about in the battle like Rudra. Regarding Gudakesha (curling hair) of copper eyes having Narayana for his ally,

sn: उभयोः सेनयोर्वीरो रथो नास्तीति तादृशः। न हि देवेषु वा पूर्वं मनुष्ये पूरगेषु च॥
en: There is no brave car-warrior who can equal him in both the armies; nor is there any among the gods, human beings or serpents;

sn: राक्षसेष्वथ यक्षेषु नरेषु कुत एव तु। भूतोऽथवा भविष्यो वा रथः कश्चिन्मया श्रुतः॥
en: Nor even among Rakshasas and Yakshas, how can there then be any among men? Nor have I heard of any that has been or that will be.

sn: समायुक्तो महाराज स्थः पार्थस्य धीमतः। वासुदेवश्च संयन्ता योद्धा चैव धनंजयः॥
en: O great king, the wise son of Pritha has a chariot which has Vasudeva for its driver and Dhananjaya as the soldier.

sn: गाण्डीवं च धनुर्दिव्यं ते चाश्वा वातरंहसः। अभेद्यं कवचं दिव्यमक्षय्यौ च महेषुधी॥
en: He has the celestial bow Gandiva and horses that have the speed of wind, celestial coat of mail which is impenetrable and great arrow holders which are inexhaustible;

sn: अस्त्रग्रामश्च माहेन्द्रो रौद्रः कौबेर एव च। याम्यश्च वारुणश्चैव गदाचोग्रप्रदर्शनाः॥
en: Groups of arms presented by the great Indra and Rudra and Kuvera and Yama and Varuna and a mace which is fierce to look at,
