en: (Such as) men equally situated should only fight with one another with all fairness. If having fought with fairness, the combatants withdraw, that would be preferred.

description: JAMBUKHANDA VINIRMANA PARVA Placing of soldiers in the Jambukhanda
sn: यथापरं यथायोगं न च स्यात् कस्यचित् पुनः। वाचा युद्धप्रवृत्तानां वाचैव प्रतियोधनम्। निष्क्रान्ताः पृतनामध्यान्न हन्तव्याः कदाचन॥
en: Those who engaged in a battle of words should be fought against with only words. those that left the fight should never be killed.

description: JAMBUKHANDA VINIRMANA PARVA Placing of soldiers in the Jambukhanda
sn: रथी च रथिना योध्यो गजेन गजधूर्गतः। अश्वेनाश्री पदातिश्च पादातेनैव भारत॥
en: A car-warrior should fight only with a car warrior. He who rode on an elephant should fight only with another such combatant. O descendant of Bharata, a horse man must fight with a horse man and a foot-soldier with a footsoldier.

description: JAMBUKHANDA VINIRMANA PARVA Placing of soldiers in the Jambukhanda
sn: यथायोगं यथाकामं यथोत्साहं यथाबलम्। समाभाष्य प्रहर्तव्यं न विश्वस्ते न विह्वले॥
en: Always being led by consideration of fitness, willingness, bravery and strength, one should strike another after having challenged him. None should strike another who is confiding or who is panic-stricken.

description: JAMBUKHANDA VINIRMANA PARVA Placing of soldiers in the Jambukhanda
sn: एकेन सह संयुक्तः प्रपन्नो विमुखस्तथा। क्षीणशस्त्रो विवर्मा च न हन्तव्यः कदाचन॥
en: One fighting with another, one seeking refuge, one retreating, one whose weapon is broken and one who is not clad in armour should never be struck.

description: JAMBUKHANDA VINIRMANA PARVA Placing of soldiers in the Jambukhanda
sn: न सूतेषु न धुर्येषु न च शस्त्रोपनायिषु। न भेरीशङ्खवादेषु प्रहर्तव्यं कथंचन॥
en: Charioteers, animals, men engaged in carrying weapons, those who play on drums and those who blow conchs should never be smitten.

description: JAMBUKHANDA VINIRMANA PARVA Placing of soldiers in the Jambukhanda
sn: एवं ते समयं कृत्वा कुरुपाण्डवसोमकाः। विस्मयं परमं जग्मुः प्रेक्षमाणाः परस्परम्॥
en: Having made these agreements, the Kurus, the Pandavas and the Somakas, staring at one another were filled with surprise.

description: JAMBUKHANDA VINIRMANA PARVA Placing of soldiers in the Jambukhanda
sn: निविश्य च महात्मानस्ततस्ते पुरुषर्षभाः। हृष्टरूपाः सुमनसो बभूवुः सहसैनिकाः॥
en: Having thus placed their troops those foremost of men, those illustrious heroes were filled with delight, their appearance indicating joy.

description: Meeting with Vyasa in the Jambukhanda
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच ततः पूर्वापरे सैन्ये समीक्ष्य भगवानृषिः। सर्ववेदविदां श्रेष्ठो व्यासः सत्यवतीसुतः॥ भविष्यति रणे घोर भरतानां पितामहः। प्रत्यक्षदर्शी भगवान् भूतभव्यभविष्यवित्॥ वैचित्रवीर्यं राजानं स रहस्यं ब्रवीदिदम्। शोचन्तमार्तं ध्यायन्तं पुत्राणामनयं तदा॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having seen the two armies placed on the east and the west ready for the fearful fight, the holy Rishi Vyasa, the son of Satyavati, that foremost of all men learned in the Vedas, that grandfather of the Pandavas and the Kurus who knew the Past and the Present and the Future thus spoke in private to the king (Dhritarashtra) the son of Vichitravirya who was then distressed and afflicted with sorrow thinking of the evil propensities of his sons.

description: Meeting with Vyasa in the Jambukhanda
sn: व्यास उवाच राजन् परीतकालास्ते पुत्राश्चान्ये च पार्थिवाः। ते हिंसन्तीव संग्रामे समासाद्येतरेतरम्॥
en: Vyasa said O king, the (last) moment of your sons and of other kings has arrived. They have assembled to fight and they will kill one another.

description: Meeting with Vyasa in the Jambukhanda
sn: तेषु कालपरीतेषु विनश्यत्स्वेव भारत। कालपर्यायमाज्ञाय मा स्म शोके मनः कृथाः॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, their (last) moment having arrived, they would now all perish. Reinembering the changes that are brought by Time, do not grieve.

description: Meeting with Vyasa in the Jambukhanda
sn: यदि चेच्छसि संग्रामे द्रष्टुमेतान् विशाम्पते। चक्षुर्ददानि ते पुत्र युद्धं तत्र निशामय॥
en: O king, O child, if you wish to see them in battle, I shall bestow on you sight. Behold the battle.

description: Meeting with Vyasa in the Jambukhanda
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच न रोचये ज्ञातिवधं द्रष्टुं ब्रह्मर्षिसत्तम। युद्धमेतत् त्वशेषेण शृणुयां तव तेजसा॥
en: Dhritarashtra said O foremost of Brahmarshis, I do not desire to see the slaughter of my friends and relatives. I shall, however, through your grace, hear the account of this battle, minutely described to me.

description: Meeting with Vyasa in the Jambukhanda
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एतस्मिन् नेच्छति द्रष्टुं संग्रामं श्रोतुमिच्छति। वराणामीश्वरो व्यासः संजयाय वरं ददौ॥
en: Vaishampayana said On his not wishing to see the battle but to hear of it, that giver of boons Vyasa bestowed a boon on Sanjaya.

description: Meeting with Vyasa in the Jambukhanda
sn: एष ते संजयो राजन् युद्धमेतद् वदिष्यति। एतस्य सर्वसंग्रामे न परोक्षं भविष्यति॥
en: Vyasa said ( king, this Sanjaya will describe to you this great battle. Nothing of the whole battle will remain unseen by him.

description: Meeting with Vyasa in the Jambukhanda
sn: चक्षुषा संजयो राजन् दिव्येनैव समन्वितः। कथयिष्यति ते युद्धं सर्वज्ञश्च भविष्यति॥
en: O king, possessing a possessing a celestial vision Sanjaya will narrate the battle to you. He will possess the knowledge of every thing regarding this battle.

description: Meeting with Vyasa in the Jambukhanda
sn: प्रकाशं वाप्रकाशं वा दिवा वा यदि वा निशि। मनसा चिन्तितमपि सर्वं वेत्स्यति संजयः॥
en: Whether manifest or concealed whether occurring by day or by night, even what will be thought in the mind, will be known to Sanjaya.

description: Meeting with Vyasa in the Jambukhanda
sn: नैनं शस्त्राणि छेत्स्यन्ति नैनं बाधिष्यते श्रमः। गावल्गणिरयं जीवन् युद्धादस्माद् विमोक्ष्यते॥
en: Wcapons will not cut him, exertion will not cxhaust him, this son of Gavalgani will return from battle alive.

description: Meeting with Vyasa in the Jambukhanda
sn: अहं तु कीर्तिपेतेषां कुरूणां भरतर्षभ। पाण्डवानां च सर्वेषां प्रथयिष्यामि मा शुचः॥
en: O foremost of the Bharata race, as for myself, I shall vad the fame of the Kurus and the Pandavas. Do not therefore grieve.

description: Meeting with Vyasa in the Jambukhanda
sn: दिष्टमेतन्नरव्याघ्र नाभिशोचितुमर्हसि। न चैव शक्यं संयन्तुं यतो धर्मस्ततो जयः॥
en: O foremost of men, this is destiny. You should not grieve. It is not to be prevented. As for victory, it would be there where righteousness would be.

description: Meeting with Vyasa in the Jambukhanda
sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्त्वा स भगवान् कुरूणां प्रपितामहः। पुनरेव महाभागो धृतराष्ट्रमुवाच ह॥
en: Vaishampayana said That highly exalted and holy grand father of the Kurus, having said thus, again thus spoke to Dhritarashtra.

description: Meeting with Vyasa in the Jambukhanda
sn: इह युद्धे महाराज भविष्यति महान् क्षयः। तथेह च निमित्तानि भयदान्युपलक्षये॥
en: Vyasa said O king, there will be a great slaughter in this battle. I also see many omens that forebode evil.

description: Meeting with Vyasa in the Jambukhanda
sn: श्येनागृध्राश्च काकाश्च कङ्काश्च सहिता बकैः। सम्पतन्ति नगाग्रेषु समवायांश्च कुर्वते॥
en: Hawks and vultures and crows and herons and cranes are coming down on the top of trees and are assembling in great numbers.

description: Meeting with Vyasa in the Jambukhanda
sn: अभ्यग्रं च प्रपश्यन्ति युद्धमानन्दिनो द्विजाः। क्रव्यादा भक्षयिष्यन्ति मांसानि गजवाजिनाम्॥
en: These birds, becoming exceedingly glad at the prospect of the battle, are loO king down on the field of battle. Carnivorous beasts will feast on the flesh of elephants and horses.

description: Meeting with Vyasa in the Jambukhanda
sn: निर्दयं चाभिवाशन्तो भैरवा भयवेदिनः। कङ्काः प्रयान्ति मध्येन दक्षिणामभितो दिशम्॥
en: Fearful herons, foreboding evil and uttering harsh cries, are going across the centre and are flying towards the south.

description: Meeting with Vyasa in the Jambukhanda
sn: उभे पूर्वापरे संध्ये नित्यं पश्यामि भारत। उदयास्तमने सूर्य कबन्धैः परिवारितम्॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, in both the twilights, morning and evening, I daily see the sun covered by headless trunks when rising or setting.

description: Meeting with Vyasa in the Jambukhanda
sn: श्वेतलोहितपर्यन्ताः कृष्णग्रीवा: सविद्युतः। विवर्णाः परिघाः संधौ भानुमन्तमवारयन्।॥
en: Three coloured clouds with their edges white and red and their middle black, charged with lightning and loO king like bludgeons, cover the sun in both the twilights.

description: Meeting with Vyasa in the Jambukhanda
sn: ज्वलितार्केन्दुनक्षत्रं निर्विशेषदिनक्षयम्। अहोरात्रं मया दृष्टं तद् भयाय भविष्यति॥
en: I have seen the sun, the moon and the stars ablaze. No difference can be found in them in the evening, I have seen this all day and all night. All this forebodes evil.

description: Meeting with Vyasa in the Jambukhanda
sn: अलक्ष्यः प्रभयाहीनः पौर्णमासी च कार्तिकीम्। चन्द्रोऽभूदग्निवर्णश्च पद्मवर्णनभस्तले॥
en: Even in the night of the full moon in the month of Kartikeya the moon, having lost all its splendour, became invisible or looked like fire, the sky loO king like lotus.

description: Meeting with Vyasa in the Jambukhanda
sn: स्वप्स्यन्ति निहता वीरा भूमिमावृत्य पार्थिवाः। राजानो राजपुत्राश्च शूराः परिघबाहवः॥
en: many heroic rulers of earth, many kings and princes, possessing great bravery and weapons loO king like maces will all be killed. They will sleep covering the earth.

description: Meeting with Vyasa in the Jambukhanda
sn: अन्तरिक्षे वराहस्य वृषदंशस्य चोभयोः। प्रणादं युद्ध्यतो रात्रो रौद्रं नित्यं प्रलक्षये॥
en: I during the night daily see in the sky the fearful cries of fighting boars and cats.

description: Meeting with Vyasa in the Jambukhanda
sn: देवताप्रतिमाश्चैव कम्पन्ति च हसन्ति च। वमन्ति रुधिरं चास्यैः खिद्यन्ति प्रपतन्ति च॥
en: The images of gods and goddesses sometime smile, sometime tremble, and again vomit blood, perspire and drop down.

description: Meeting with Vyasa in the Jambukhanda
sn: अनाहता दुन्दुभयः प्रणदन्ति विशाम्पते। अयुक्ताश्च प्रवर्तन्ते क्षत्रियाणां महारथाः॥
en: O king, drums without being beaten give out sounds. The great cars of the Kshatriyas move, though no animals are yoked to them.

description: Meeting with Vyasa in the Jambukhanda
sn: कोकिलाः शतपत्राश्च चाषा भासाः शुकास्तथा। सारसाश्च मयूराश्च वाचो मुञ्चन्ति दारुणाः॥
en: Kokilas, wood packers, jaws, water cocks, parrots, crows, peacocks, all emit fearful cries,

description: Meeting with Vyasa in the Jambukhanda
sn: गृहीतशस्त्राः क्रोशन्ति चर्मिणो वाजिपृष्ठगाः। अरुणोदये प्रदृश्यन्ते शतशः शलभव्रजाः॥
en: Here and there everywhere horse men clad in armours and armed with weapons give out war cries. In the morning when the sun rises, hundreds of fights of insects are seen

description: Meeting with Vyasa in the Jambukhanda
sn: उभे संध्ये प्रकाशन्ते दिशां दाहसमन्विते। पर्जन्यः पांसुवर्षी च मांसवर्षी च भारत॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, in both the twilights, the four quarters appear to be ablaze. The clouds pour down dust and flesh.

description: Meeting with Vyasa in the Jambukhanda
sn: या चैषा विश्रुता राजंस्त्रैलोक्ये साधुसम्मता। अरुन्धती तयाप्येष वसिष्ठः पृष्ठतः कृतः॥
en: O king, she who is celebrated over the three worlds and who is praised by the pious men, en that Arundhati (constellation) keeps Vasishtha on her back.

description: Meeting with Vyasa in the Jambukhanda
sn: रोहिणी पीडयन्नेष स्थितो राजशनैश्चरः। व्यावृत्तं लक्ष्म सोमस्य भविष्यति महद् भयम्॥
en: O king, the planet Shani appears with (the constellation) Rohini. The sign of the dear in the moon has deviated from its original position, a great evil is foreboded by all this.

description: Meeting with Vyasa in the Jambukhanda
sn: अनभ्रे महाघोरः स्तनितः श्रूयते स्वनः। वाहनानां च रुदतां निपतन्त्यश्रुबिन्दवः॥
en: Even when the sky is cloudless, even then fearful roars are heard there. The animals are all weeping and tears are falling fast from their eyes.

sn: व्यास उवाच खरा गोषु प्रजायन्ते रमन्ते मातृभिः सुताः। अनार्तवं पुष्यफलं दर्शयन्ति वनदुमाः॥
en: Vyasa said Asses are being born of cows. Sons hold sexual intercourse with their mothers. The forest trees produce unseasonable flowers and fruits.

sn: गर्भिण्योऽजातपुत्राश्च जनयन्ति विभीषणान्। क्रव्यादाः पक्षिभिश्चापि सहाश्नन्ति परस्परम्॥
en: Women who are pregnant and those that are not, are giving birth to monsters, Carnivorous beasts mingle with birds and are feeding together.

sn: त्रिविषाणाश्चतुर्नेवाः पञ्चपादा द्विमेहनाः। द्विशीर्षाश्च द्विपुच्छाश्च दंष्ट्रिणः पशवोऽशिवाः॥
en: Inauspicious beasts, some having three horns, some having four eyes, some five legs, some two sexual organs, some two heads, some two tails, and some fearful teeth.

sn: जायन्ते विवृतास्याश्च व्याहरन्तोऽशिवा गिरः। त्रिपदाः शिखिनस्तााश्चतुर्दष्ट्रा विषाणिनः॥
en: Are born with mounts wide open : they are emitting fearful cries. Horses with three legs, with crests, with four teeth and with horns are also born.

sn: तथैवान्याश्च दृश्यन्ते स्त्रियो वै ब्रह्मवादिनाम्। वैनतेयान् मयूरांश्च जनयन्ति पुरे तव॥
en: O king, the wives of many Brahmavadins in your city are seen to give birth to Garuda's and pea-cocks.

sn: गोवत्सं वडवा सूते श्वा शृगालं महीपते। कुक्कुरान् करभाश्चैव शुकाश्चाशुभवादिनः॥
en: O king, the mare gives birth to calves the bitch to jackals. Cooks, antelopes and parrots are all sending forth inauspicious notes.

sn: स्त्रियः काश्चित्प्रजायन्ते चतस्रः पञ्चकन्यकाः। जातमात्राश्च नृत्यन्ति गायन्ति च हसन्ति च॥
en: Women give birth to four or five daughters all at a time, and these, as soon as born, dance, sing, and laugh.

sn: पृथग्जनस्य सर्वस्य क्षुद्रकाः प्रहसन्ति च। नृत्यन्ति परिगायन्ति वेदयन्तो महद् भयम्॥
en: The men of the lowest castes laugh, and dance and sign and thus indicate fearful evils.

sn: प्रतिमाश्चालिखन्त्येताः सशस्त्रा: कालचोदिताः। अन्योन्यमभिधावन्ति शिशवो दण्डपाणयः॥
en: Infants as if drawn by death are painting armed images. They are running against one another with maces in their hands.

sn: अन्योन्यमभिमृद्नन्ति नगराणि युयुत्सवः। पद्मोत्पलानि वृक्षेषु जायन्ते कुमुदानि च॥
en: Being desirous of battle, they are breaking down the towns (they have made in sports). Lotuses and lilies are growing on trees.

sn: विष्वग्वाताश्च वान्त्युग्रा रजो नाप्युपशाम्यति। अभीक्ष्णं कम्पते भूमिरर्कं राहुरुपैति च॥
en: Strong winds are fearfully blowing and the dust is unceasingly flying. The earth is often quaking and Rahu advances towards the sun.

sn: श्वेतो ग्रहस्तथा चित्रां समतिक्रम्य तिष्ठति। अभावं हि विशेषेण कुरूणां तत्र पश्यति॥
en: Ketu (the white planet) stops on passing beyond the constellation Chitra. All this forebodes the total destruction of the Kurus.

sn: धूमकेतुर्महाघोरः पुष्यं चाक्रम्य तिष्ठति। सेनयोरशिवं घोरं करिष्यति महाग्रहः॥
en: A fearful comet is rising, and is distressing the constellation Pushya. This great planet will cause terrible harm to both the armies.

sn: मघास्वङ्गारको वक्रः श्रवणे च बृहस्पतिः। भगं नक्षत्रमाक्रम्य सूर्यपुत्रेण पीड्यते॥
en: Mars advances towards Magha and Brihaspati towards Shravana. the sun's offspring (Shani) advances towards Phalguni and afflicts it.

sn: शुक्रः प्रोष्ठपदे पूर्वे समारुह्य विरोचते। उत्तरे तु परिक्रम्य सहितः समुदीक्षते॥
en: The planet Shukra rises towards Purva Bhadra. Shining brilliantly and shooting towards the Uttara Bhadra, it looks towards it.

sn: श्वेतो ग्रहः प्रज्वलित: सधूम इव पावकः। ऐन्द्रं तेजस्वि नक्षत्रं ज्येष्ठामाक्रम्य तिष्ठति॥
en: Ketu, blazing up like smoky fire, stops and afflicts the effulgent constellation of Indra.

sn: ध्रुवं प्रज्वलितो घोरमपसव्यं प्रवर्तते। रोहिणी पीडयत्येवमुभौ च शशिभास्करौ। चित्रास्वात्यन्तरे चैव विष्ठितः परुषग्रहः॥
en: The constellation Dhruva, fearfully blazing, advances towards the right. Both the sun and the moon distress Rohini. The terrible planet Rahu has taken up its position between Chitra and Svati (constellations).

sn: वक्रानुवनं कृत्वा च श्रवणं पावकप्रभः। ब्रह्मराशि समावृत्य लोहिताङ्गो व्यवस्थितः॥
en: Three-bodied planct, effulgent like fire passing in a round and round way stops encircling Shravana over ridden by Brihaspati.

sn: सर्वसस्यपरिच्छन्ना पृथिवी सस्यमालिनी। पञ्चशीर्षा यवाश्चापि शतशीर्षाश्च शालयः॥
en: O great king, the earth that always produce particular crops at particular seasons is simultaneously being overgrown with crops of every season. Every stalk of barely has five years and every stalk of paddy has a hundred.

sn: प्रधानाः सर्वलोकस्य यास्वायत्तमिदं जगत्। ता गाव: प्रस्तुता वत्सैः शोणितं प्रक्षरन्त्युत॥
en: Those animals that are the best of all creatures in the world and upon whom depends the preservation of the whole universe, namely kine, when milked after the calves have sucked them give only blood.

sn: निश्चरुरर्चिषश्चापात् खङ्गाश्च ज्वलिता भृशम्। व्यक्तं पश्यन्ति शस्त्राणि संग्रामं समुपस्थितम्॥
en: Rays of light are coming out from bows and swords produce great luster. It is evident these weapons see before them the battle as if it has already begun.

sn: अग्निवर्णा यथा भासः शस्त्राणामुदकस्य च। कवचानां ध्वजानां च भविष्यति महाक्षयः॥
en: The shine of weapons, of the water, of the armours and of the standards looks like fire. A great slaughter of men and beasts is sure to take place.

sn: पृथिवी शोणितावर्ता ध्वजोडुपसमाकुला। कुरूणां वैशसे राजन् पाण्डवैः सह भारत॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, O king, in this battle of the Kurus and the Pandavas the earth will appear like a river of blood with the standards as so many rafts.

sn: दिक्षु प्रज्वलितास्याश्च व्याहरन्ति मृगद्विजाः। अत्याहितं दर्शयन्तो वेदयन्ति महद् भयम्॥
en: Animals and birds, on all sides, utter harsh cries with their mouths burning like fire. This forebode fearful evils.

sn: एकपक्षाक्षिचरणः शकुनिः खचरो निशि। रौद्रं वदति संरब्धः शोणितं छर्दयनिव॥
en: A bird, with only one wing, one eye and onc leg ranges in the sky in the night. It fearfully screamed in anger, as if it wants every body to vomit blood.

sn: शस्त्राणि चैव राजेन्द्र प्रज्वलन्तीव सम्प्रति। सप्तर्षीणामुदाराणां समवच्छाद्यते प्रभा॥
en: O king of kings, it appears that all weapons are now blazing in great brilliance. But the effulgence of the constellation of the seven Rishis has become dim.

sn: संवत्सरस्थायिनौ च ग्रहौ प्रज्वलितावुभौ। विशाखायाः समीपस्थौ बृहस्पतिशनैश्चरौ॥
en: Those two burning planets namely Brihaspati and Shani have become fixed for a year.

sn: चन्द्रादित्यावुभौ ग्रस्तावेकाह्रा हि त्रयोदशीम्। अपर्वणि ग्रहं यातौ प्रजासंक्षयमिच्छतः॥
en: Three lunation's, meeting twice or thrice in one and the same fortnight and on the thirteenth day, therefore, from the first luxation, according as it is the day of the fullmoon or the new-moon, the moon and the sun are devoured by Rahu. This forebodes a great slaughter (of creatures).

sn: अशोभिता दिशः सर्वाः पांसुवर्षेः समन्ततः। उत्पातमेघा रौद्राश्च रात्रौ वर्षन्ति शोणितम्॥
en: All direction of the earth, covered by showers of dust appears greatly inauspicious. Fearful clouds, foreboding evil, pour showers of blood in the night.

sn: कृत्तिकां पीड़यंस्तीक्ष्णैर्नक्षत्रं पृथिवीपते। अभीक्ष्णवाता वायन्ते धूमकेतुमवस्थिताः॥
en: O king, Rahu of terrible deeds also afflicts Krittika. Rough winds, foreboding terrible danger, are continually blowing.

sn: विषमं जनयन्त्येत आक्रन्दजननं महत्। त्रिषु सर्वेषु नक्षत्रनक्षत्रेषु विशाम्पते। गृध्रः सम्पतते शीर्ष जनयन् भयमुत्तमम्॥
en: All these bring in a war, which is characterised by many weeping. The constellations are divided into three classes. Upon one or the other of each class evil planet has shed its influence. All this forebodes terrible consequences.

sn: चतुर्दशी पञ्चदशी भूतपूर्वां च षोडशीम्। इमां तु नाभिजानेऽहममावास्यां त्रयोदशीम्। चन्द्रसूर्यावुभौ ग्रस्तावेकमासी त्रयोदशीम्॥
en: A lunar fortnight has hither to consisted of fourteen days, or fifteen days or sixteen days. But on the thirteenth day and in the course of the same month two eclipses have taken place.

sn: अपर्वणि ग्रहेणैतौ प्रजाः संक्षपयिष्यतः। मांसवर्ष पुनस्तीव्रमासीत् कृष्णचतुर्दशीम्। शोणितैर्वक्त्रसम्पूर्णा अतृप्तास्तत्र राक्षसाः॥
en: The sun and the moon therefore undergoing eclipses on unusual days willing in a great slaughter of all creatures on earth. Even the Rakshasas drinking mouthful of blood are not satiated.

sn: प्रतिस्रोतो महानद्यः सरितः शोणितोदकाः। फेनायमानाः कूपाश्च कूर्दन्ति वृषभा इव॥
en: The great rivers flow in opposite directions. The waters of rivers have turned into blood,

sn: पतन्त्युल्का सनिर्घाताः शक्राशनिसमप्रभाः। अद्य चैव निशां व्युष्टामनयं समवाप्स्यथ॥
en: Meteors, as effulgent as Indra's thunder, fall on earth with loud sound. When this night passes away, a great danger will fall on you.

sn: विनिःसृत्य महोल्काभिस्तिमिरं सर्वतोदिशम्। अन्योन्यमुपतिष्ठद्भिस्तत्र चोक्तं महर्षिभिः॥
en: Men with lighted torches in their hands will meet great difficulty to meet together, for a thick gloom will cover all space.

sn: भूमिपालसहस्राणां भूमिः पास्यति शोणितम्। कैलासमन्दराभ्यां तु तथा हिमवता विभो॥
en: Great Rishis have said that in such circumstances, the earth drinks the blood of thousands of kings. From the mountains of Kailasa, Mandara and Himalayas.

sn: सहस्रशो महाशब्दः शिखराणि पतन्ति च। महाभूता भूमिकम्पे चत्वारः सागराः पृथक्।
en: Thousands of sounds are heard thousands of mountain-summits are falling down. Earth trembles, and in consequence the four oceans.

sn: वेलामुद्वर्तयन्तीव क्षोभयन्तो वसुंधराम्॥ वृक्षानुन्मथ्य वान्त्युग्रा वाताः शर्करकर्षिणः।
en: Having exceedingly swelled, seem ready to overflow their banks in order to afflict the earth. Fearful winds with stones are blowing crushing all the trees.

sn: आभग्नाः सुमहावातैरशनीभिः समाहताः॥ वृक्षाः पतन्ति चैत्याश्च ग्रामेषु नगरेषु च।
en: Bcing crushed by the high wind and stuck by lightning, sacred and common trees in villages and towns are falling down.

sn: नीललोहितपीतश्च भवत्यग्निर्हतो द्विजैः॥ वामाचिर्दुष्टगन्धश्च मुञ्चन् वै दारुणं स्वनम्।
en: When the Brahmanas pour sacrificial libations on fire, it now becomes blue or red or yellow. Its flame turns towards the left, and produces a bad odor accompanied by loud sounds.

sn: स्पर्शा गन्धा रसाश्चैव विपरीता महीपते॥ धूम ध्वजाः प्रमुञ्चन्ति कम्पमाना मुहुर्मुहुः। मुञ्चन्त्यङ्गारवर्षं च भेर्यश्च पटहास्तथा॥
en: O kings, touch, smell and taste have become quite the contrary. The standards of the warriors often tremble and they send forth smoke. Drums and cymbals cast off showers of coat dust.

sn: शिखराणां समृद्धानामुपरिष्टात् समन्ततः । वायसाश्च रुवन्त्युग्रं वामं मण्डलमाश्रिताः॥ पक्वापक्वेति सुभृशं वावाश्यन्ते वयांसि च।
en: From the top of tall trees crows fly away in circles from the left. They are ultering terrible cries. All of them are sending forth fearful cries of pakka, pakka.

sn: निलीयन्ते ध्वजाग्रेषु क्षयाय पृथिवीक्षिताम्॥ ध्यायन्तः प्रकिरन्तश्च व्याला वेपथुसंयुताः। दीनास्तुरङ्गमा: सर्वे वारणा: सलिलाश्रयाः॥
en: They are sitting on the tops of standards foreboding the destruction of the kings. Poor elephants run hither and thither throwing off urine and excreta. The horses all melancholy, while the elephants are going into the water.

sn: एतच्छ्रुत्वा भवानत्र प्राप्तकालं व्यवस्यताम्। यथा लोकः समुच्छेदं नायं गच्छेत भारत॥
en: Having heard all this, O descendant of Bharata, do what is proper, so that the world may not meet with extermination. are

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच पितुर्वचो निशम्यैतद् धृतराष्ट्रोऽब्रवीदिदम्। दिष्टमेतत् पुरा मन्ये भविष्यति नरक्षयः॥
en: Dhritarashtra said Having heard the words of father Dhritarashtra said: It is my belief that all this has been previously ordained.

sn: राजानः क्षत्रधर्मेण यदि वध्यन्ति संयुगे। वीरलोकं समासाद्य सुखं प्राप्स्यन्ति केवलम्॥
en: If the kings according to the duties of Kshatriyas die in battle, they will then go to the regions reserved for heroes and thus obtain eternal happiness only.

sn: इह कीर्ति परे लोके दीर्घकालं महत् सुखम्। प्राप्स्यन्ति पुरुषव्याघ्राः प्राणांस्त्यक्त्वा महाहवे॥
en: If these foremost of men abandon their lives in a great battle, they will acquire fame in this world and great and eternal happiness in the world ncxi.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्तो मुनिस्तत्त्वं कवीन्द्रो राजसत्तम। धृतराष्ट्रेण पुत्रेण ध्यानमन्वगमत् परम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said O foremost of kings, having been thus addressed by his son Dhritarashtra, that best of poets, that Rishi Vyasa, concentrated his mind in great meditation.

sn: स मुहूर्त तथा ध्यात्वा पुनरेवाब्रवीद् वचः। असंशयं पार्थिवेन्द्र कालः संक्षियते जगत्॥
en: Having meditated for a moment, Vyasa thus again spoke, O king of kings, “there is no doubt that Time destroys the Universe.

sn: सृजते च पुनर्लोकान् नेह विद्यति शाश्वतम्। ज्ञातीनां वै कुरूणां च सम्बन्धिसुहृदां तथा॥ धयं देशय पन्थानं समर्थो ह्यसि वारणे। क्षुद्रं जातिवधं प्राहुर्मा कुरुष्व ममाप्रियम्॥
en: It is Time also which creates the worlds. There is nothing here on earth which is everlasting. Therefore show the path of virtue। to the Kurus, to your relations, your kinsmen and friends. You are the proper person to restrain them. It is said that slaughter of kinsmen is sinful. Do not act in a way which would be disagreeable to me.

sn: कालोऽयं पुत्ररूपेण तव जातो विशाम्पते। न वधः पूज्यते वेदे हितं नैव कथंचन॥
en: O king, Death himself, has taken birth in the form of your son. Slaughter is never spoken high of in the Vedas. It can never produce any good.

sn: हन्यात् स एनं यो हन्यात् कुलधर्मं स्विकां तनुम्। कालेनोत्पथगन्ताऽसि शक्ये सति यथाऽऽपदि॥ कुलस्यास्य विनाशाय तथैव च महीक्षिताम्। अनर्थो राज्यरूपेण तव जातो विशाम्पते॥
en: The custom of a family brings about his own ruin who destroys it resembling his own body. For the destruction of this race as well as that of kings, it is (no doubt). Time that leads you to this wrong path although you are capable to withstand it. O king, in the shape of a kingdom, a great calamity has befallen you.

sn: लुप्तधर्मा परेणासि धर्मं दर्शय वै सुतान्। किं ते राज्येन दुर्धर्ष येन प्राप्तोऽसि किल्बिषम्॥
en: Your virtue suffers a great diminution. Show to your son what is virtuous. O invincible hero, of what value is a kingdom that brings in sin?

sn: यशो धर्मं च कीर्तिं च पालयन् स्वर्गमाप्स्यसि। लभन्तां पाण्डवा राज्यं शमं गच्छन्तु
en: Protect your good name, your virtue and your fame. You will then be able to obtain heaven. Let the Pandavas have their kingdom and let the entire Kuru race have the peace.”

sn: एवं ब्रुवति विप्रेन्द्र धृतराष्ट्रोऽम्बिकासुतः। आक्षिप्य वाक्यं वाक्यज्ञो वाक्यं चैवाब्रवीत् पुनः॥
en: When that foremost of Brahmanas (Vyasa) was thus speaking in a sorrowful tone, the son of Ambika, accomplished in speech, king Dhritarashtra, thus spoke to him.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच यथा भवान् वेत्ति तथैव वेत्ता भावाभावौ विदितौ मे यथार्थो। कौरवाः॥ स्वार्थे हि सम्मुह्यति तात लोको मां चापि लोकात्मकमेव विद्धि॥
en: Dhritarashtra said My knowledge of life and death is the same as yours. The truth of this is well known to me. But men lose (good) judgement in things which concern their interest. O sire, know me to be an ordinary man.

sn: प्रसादये त्वामतुलप्रभावं त्वं नो गतिर्दर्शयिता च धीरः। न चापि ते मद्वशगा महर्षे न चाधर्मं कर्तुमर्हा हि मे मतिः॥ त्वं हि धर्मप्रवृत्तिश्च यशः कीर्तिश्च भारती। कुरूणां पाण्डवानां च मान्यश्चापि पितामहः॥
en: O Rishi of immeasurable power. I pray to you to extend your power towards us. You have your soul under complete control, you are my preceptor and guide. O great Rishi, my sons do not obey me. My mind is not inclined to commit sin. You are the instrument of the fame, the achievements and virtue of the Bharata race. You are the respected grandfather of both the Kurus and the Pandavas.

sn: व्यास उवाच वैचित्रवीर्य नृपते यत् ते मनसि वर्तते। अभिधत्स्व यथाकामं छेत्ताऽस्मि तव संशयम्॥
en: Vyasa said O son of Vichitravirya, tell me openly what is in your mind. I shall remove your doubts.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच यानि लिङ्गानि संग्रामे भवन्ति विजयिष्यताम्। तानि सर्वाणि भगवञ्छ्रोतुमिच्छामि तत्त्वतः॥
en: Dhritarashtra said O reverend sir, I desire to hear from you all those signs that happier before those that become victorious in battle.

sn: व्यास उवाच प्रसन्नभाः पावक ऊर्ध्वरश्मिः प्रदक्षिणावर्तशिखो विधूमः। पुण्या गन्धाश्चाहुतीनां प्रवान्ति जयस्यैतद् भाविनो रूपमाहुः॥
en: Vyasa said The sacred fire assumes a cheerful luster. Its light rises upwards. Its flames bend towards the right. It blazes forth without any smoke. The libations poured in it produce sweet fragrance. These are said to be the indications of future success.

sn: गम्भीरघोषाश्च महास्वनाश्च शङ्खा मृदङ्गाश्च नदन्ति यत्र। विशुद्धरश्मिस्तपनः शशी च जयस्यैतद् भाविनो रूपमाहुः॥
en: The conchs and cymbals produce deep and loud sounds, the sun and the moon give forth pure rays. These are said to be the indications of future success.

sn: इष्टा वाचः प्रसृता वायसानां सम्प्रस्थितानां च गमिष्यतां च। ये पृष्ठतस्ते त्वरयन्ति राजन् ये चाग्रतस्ते प्रतिषेधयन्ति॥
en: Flying or sitting crows utter agreeable cries. Those warriors that are behind urge those that are in front to advance.

sn: कल्याणवाचः शकुना राजहंसाः शुकाः क्रौञ्चा: शतपत्राश्च यत्र। प्रदक्षिणाश्चैव भवन्ति संख्ये ध्रुवं जयस्तत्र वदन्ति विप्राः॥
en: When vultures, swans, parrots, cranes, and woodpeckers utter delightful cries and go towards the right, the Brahmanas say that victory in such cases is certain.

sn: अलङ्कारैः कवचैः केतुभिश्च सुखप्रणादैहेषितैर्वा हयानाम्। भ्राजिष्मती दुष्प्रतिवीक्षणीया येषां चमूस्ते विजयन्ति शत्रून्॥
en: Those, whose ornaments, armours and standards and their bright shields become incapable of being stared at, always conquei their enemies.

sn: हृष्टा वाचस्तथा सत्त्वं योधानां यत्र भारत। न म्लायन्ति सजश्चैव ते तरन्ति रणोदधिम्॥
en: Those, that send forth cheerful shouts, o descendant of Bharata, those warriors, whose courage is not damped and whose garlands do not fade, always cross the ocean of battle.

sn: इष्टा वाचः प्रविष्टस्य दक्षिणाः प्रविविक्षतः। पश्चात् संधारयन्त्यर्थमग्रे च प्रतिषेधिका:॥
en: Those who wishing to enter into the ranks of the foe, utter even kind words and those who warn the foe before striking always obtain victory.

sn: शब्दरूपरसस्पर्शगन्धाश्चाविकृताः शुभाः। सदा हर्षश्च योधानां जयतामिह लक्षणम्॥
en: When the objects of hearing, seeing, tasting, touching and smelling do not undergo any change and become auspicious and if there is joy amongst the warriors at all time, it indicates victory.

sn: अनुगा वायवो वान्ति तथाऽभ्राणि वयांसि च। अनुप्लवन्ति मेघाश्च तथैवेन्द्रधनूंषि च॥
en: O king, these are the indications of victory, namely the winds, the clouds and the birds all become favourable, and the clouds and rainbows that pour beneficial showers.

sn: एतानि जयमानानां लक्षणानि विशाम्पते। भवन्ति विपरीतानि मुमूर्पूणा जनाधिप॥
en: O king, these are the indications that armies would secure success, while, O king, all these become quite the conirary in the case of those that are on the point of death.

sn: अल्पायां वा महत्यां वा सेनायामिति निश्चयः। हर्षो योधगणस्यैको जयलक्षणमुच्यते॥
en: Whether the army be small or large cheerfulness of its soldiers is said to be a certain sign of its winning victory.

sn: एको दीर्णो दारयति सेनां सुमहतीमपि। तां दीर्णामनुदीर्यन्ते योधाः शूरतरा
en: One soldier, struck with panic, can cause a large army to be alarmed and to take to flight, it causes even the bravest of warriors to be frightened.

sn: अपि॥ शक्या समाधातुं संनिपाते दुर्निवा तदा चैव प्रभग्ना महती चमूः। अपामिव महावेगास्त्रस्ता मृगगणा इव॥
en: If a large ariny is once broken up and rouled, it cannot be easily rallied like a herd of deer in a fright or a mighty current of waters (in rains).

sn: नैव महाचमूः। दीर्णामित्येव दीर्यन्ते सुविद्वांसोऽपि भारत॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, if a large army is once routed, it is incapable of being rallied; on the other hand, seeing it dispersed, even wellskilled warriors become confounded.

sn: भीतान् भग्नांश्च सम्प्रेक्ष्य भयं भूयोऽभिवर्धते। प्रभग्ना सहसा राजन् दिशो विद्रवते चमूः॥
en: Secing soldiers struck with panic and flying, the panic spreads also in other directions. O king, in such cases the whole army is soon broken up and all fly in all directions.

sn: नैव स्थापयितुं शक्या शूरैरपि महाचमूः। सत्कृत्य महतीं सेनां चतुरङ्गां महीपतिः।
en: O king, when an army is routed, even brave leaders at the head of large divisions of the army consisting of four kinds of troops can not rally them.

sn: उपायपूर्वं मेधावी यतेत सततोत्थितः॥ उपायविजयं श्रेष्ठमाहुर्भेदन मध्यमम्। जघन्य एष विजयो यो युद्धेन विशाम्पते॥
en: It is said that the success that is obtained by negotiations and other means is the best. That which is secured by creating disunion (amongst the enemy) is but indifferent. O king, the success that is secured by battle is the worst.

sn: महादोष: संनिपातस्तस्याद्यः क्षय उच्यते। परस्परज्ञाः संहृष्टा व्यवधूताः सुनिश्चिताः॥ पञ्चाशदपि ये शूरा मृद्नन्ति महतीं चमूम्। अपि वा पञ्च षट् सप्त विजयन्त्यनिवर्तिनः॥
en: There are many evils in battle; the first and the foremost is slaughter. Even fifty brave men who know one another, who are not dispirited, who are free from family ties and who are firmly resolved can defeat a large ariny. Even fire, six or seven, who do not retreat can obtain victory.

sn: न वैनतेयो गरुडः प्रशंसति महाजनम्। दृष्ट्वा सुपर्णोऽपचितिं महत्या अपि भारत॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, Vinata's son Garuda never asks the assistance of many followers when he sees even a large number of birds.

sn: न बाहुल्येन सेनाया जयो भवति नित्यशः। अध्रुवो हि जयो नाम दैवं चात्र परायणम्। जयवन्तो हि संग्रामे कृतकृत्या भवन्ति हि॥
en: Therefore the strength of number of an army is not always the cause of victory. Victory is always uncertain. It depends on chance. Even those that obtain victory have to suffer loss.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्त्वा ययौ व्यासो धृतराष्ट्राय धीमते। धृतराष्ट्रोऽपि तच्छ्रुत्वा ध्यानमेवान्वपद्यत॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having thus spoken to Dhritarashtra Vyasa went away. Having heard these words, Dhritarashtra also reflected in silence.

sn: स मुहूर्तमिव ध्यात्वा विनिःश्वस्य मुहुर्मुहुः। संजय संशितात्मानमपृच्छद् भरतर्षभ।॥
en: Having reflected for a moment, he sighed again and again. O foremost of the Bharata race, the king then thus spoke to the selfcontrolled Sanjaya.

sn: संजयेमे महीपालाः शूरा युद्धाभिनन्दिनः। अन्योन्यमभिनिघ्नन्ति शस्त्रैरुच्चावचैरिह॥
en: Dhritarashtra said O Sanjaya, these kings, these rulers of carth, so brave and so cheerful in battle, are eager to strike one another with various kinds of weapon.

sn: पार्थिवाः पृथिवीहेतोः समभित्यज्य जीवितम्। न वा शाम्यन्ति निघ्नन्तो वर्धयन्ति यमक्षयम्॥
en: They are not to be restrained. They striking one another and giving up their lives will increase the population of the abode of Yama.

sn: भौममैश्वर्यमिच्छन्तो न मृष्यन्ते परस्परम्। मन्ये बहुगणा भूमिस्तन्ममाचक्ष्व संजय॥
en: Being desirous to obtain prosperity of earth, they cannot bear the sight of one another. I therefore think that the earth must possess many attributes. O Sanjaya, tell me all this.

sn: बहूनि च सहस्राणि प्रयुतान्यर्बुदानि च। कोट्यश्च लोकवीराणां समेताः कुरुजाङ्गले॥
en: Many thousands, many millions, many tens of millions, many hundreds of millions of warriors have assembled at Kurukshetra.

sn: देशानां च परीमाणं नगराणां च संजय। श्रोतुमिच्छामि तत्त्वेन यत एते समागताः॥
en: O Sanjaya, I desire to hear in great detail about the situations and dimensions of those countries and cities from which they have come.

sn: दिव्यबुद्धिप्रदीपेन युक्तस्त्वं ज्ञानचक्षुषा। प्रभावात् तस्य विप्रर्व्यासस्यामिततेजसः॥
en: Through the grace of that immeasurably powerful Rishi Vyasa, you now possess the lamp of celestial vision and the eye of knowledge.

sn: संजय उवाच यथाप्रज्ञं महाप्राज्ञ भौमान् वक्ष्यामि ते गुणान्। शास्त्रचक्षुरवेक्षस्व नमस्ते भरतर्षभ॥
en: Sanjaya said O greatly wise one, I shall narrate to you the merits of the earth according to my knowledge. See them with your eye of scriptural wisdom. O foremost of the Bharata race, I bow to you.

sn: द्विविधानीह भूतानि चराणि स्थावराणि च। त्रसानां त्रिविधा योनिरण्डस्वेदजरायुजाः॥
en: Creatures in this world are of two kinds, namely mobile and immobile. Mobile creatures are three kinds, namely O viperous O viviparous O heat and damp produced.

sn: त्रसानां खलु सर्वेषां श्रेष्ठा राजन् जरायुजाः। जरायुजानां प्रवरा मानवाः पशवश्च ये॥
en: O king, among mobile creatures, those that are viviparous are certainly the foremost. Among viviparous man is certainly the foremost, and next to man is animal.

sn: नानारूपधरा राजेस्तेषां भेदाश्चतुर्दश। वेदोक्ताः पृथिवीपाल येषु यज्ञाः प्रतिष्ठिताः॥
en: O king, animals of various forms are of fourteen kinds. O king, O lord of earth, these fourteen are the domestic and wild animals mentioned in the Vedas and on which the sacrifice rests.

sn: ग्राम्याणां पुरुषाः श्रेष्ठाः सिंहाश्चारण्यवासिनाम्। सर्वेषामेव भूतानामन्योन्येनोपजीवनम्॥
en: Among creatures that are domestic man is the foremost; lions are the foremost of all wild animals. All creatures keep themselves up by living upon one another.

sn: उद्भिज्जाः स्थावराः प्रोक्तास्तेषां पञ्चैव जातयः। वृक्षगुल्मलतावल्लयस्त्वक्सारास्तृणाजातयः॥
en: The immovable are cailed Udbhijas. They have five species (Jati). These are-tree, shrub, creeper, plants (valli) and tvaksara (bamboo etc.). These all species are in the category (class) of straws.

sn: तेषां विंशतिरेकोना महाभूतेषु पञ्चसु। चतुर्विंशतिरुद्दिष्टा गायत्री लोकसम्मता॥
en: Mobile and immobile creatures are thus of nineteen kinds. Their universal constituents are five. Thus they are twenty four in all. They are called Gayatri as is well known to all.

sn: य एतां वेद गायत्री पुण्यां सर्वगुणान्विताम्। तत्त्वेन भरतश्रेष्ठ स लोके न प्रणश्यति॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, he who knows these to be the true sacred Gayatri which possesses every virtue, is not liable to worldly destruction.

sn: अरण्यवासिनः सप्त सप्तैषां ग्रामवासिनः। सिंहा व्याघ्रा वराहाच महिषा वारणास्तथा॥
en: Seven are wild and seven domestic. O king, lions, tigers, boars, buffaloes, elephants, bears, and monkeys are wild.

sn: ऋक्षाश्च वानराश्चैव सप्तारण्याः स्मृता नृप। गौरजाविमनुष्याश्च अश्वाश्वतरगर्दभाः॥ एते ग्राम्या: समाख्याताः पशवः सप्त साधुभिः। एते वै पशवो राजन् ग्राम्यारण्याश्चतुर्दश॥
en: ) Cows, goats, sheep, men, horses, mules and donkey i.e. seven animals are considered to be domestic by the learned men. O king! Thus, the grand total of village dweller and forest dwellers (Vanavasi) is fourteen in number i.e. these are fourteen animals.

sn: भूमौ च जायते सर्वं भूमौ सर्वं विनश्यति। भूमिः प्रतिष्ठा भूतानां भूमिरेव सनातनम्॥
en: Every thing rises from the earth and when destroyed every thing goes into her. The earth is the stay and the refuge of all creatures. The earth is eternal.

sn: यस्य भूमिस्तस्य सर्वं जगत् स्थावरजङ्गमम्। तत्रातिगृद्धा राजानो विनिघ्नन्तीतरेतरम्॥
en: He who possesses the earth possesses the entire universe with its mobile and immobile creatures. It is for this kings long to possess the earth and thus kill one another.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच नदीनां पर्वतानां च नामधेयानि संजय। तथा जनपदानां च ये चान्ये भूमिमाश्रिताः॥ प्रमाणं च प्रमाणज्ञ पृथिव्या मम सर्वतः। निखिलेन समाचक्ष्व काननानि च संजय॥
en: Dhritarashtra said O Sanjaya, O man learned in the measures of all things, tell me in detail the names of rivers and mountains and of provinces and all other things that are on earth and the dimensions of the whole earth and of the forest.

sn: भूमेरेते गुणा: संजय उवाच पञ्चेमानि महाराज महाभूतानि संग्रहात्। जगतीस्थानि सर्वाणि समान्याहुर्मनीषिणः॥
en: Sanjaya said O king of kings, the wise call all things in the universe as equal in consequences of the presence of the five elements (in them).

sn: भूमिरापस्तथा वायुरग्निराकाशमेव च। गुणोत्तराणि सर्वाणि तेषां भूमिः प्रधानतः॥ शब्दः स्पर्शश्च रूपं च रसो गन्धश्च पञ्चमः। प्रोक्ता ऋषिभिस्तत्त्ववेदिभिः॥
en: These elements are the ether, air, fire, water, and earth. Their attributes are sound, touch, vision, taste and smell. Every one of these elements possesses the attributes and the attributes of things that come to it. Therefore the earth is the foremost of all, possessing as it does the attributes of all the other four. Thus say the Rishis who know the truth.

sn: चत्वारोऽप्सु गुणा राजन् गन्धस्तत्र न विद्यते। शब्दः स्पर्शश्च रूपं च तेजसोऽथ गुणास्त्रयः।
en: O king, there are four attributes in water. It has no scent. Fire has three attributes, namely sound, touch and vision.

sn: शब्दः स्पर्शश्च वायोस्तु आकाशे शब्द एव तु॥ एते पञ्च गुणा राजन् महाभूतेषु पञ्चसु! वर्तन्ते सर्वलोकेषु येषु भूताः प्रतिष्ठिताः॥
en: Air has only sound and touch whereas ether has sound alone. O king, these five attributes exist in the five principle elements.

sn: हेमकूटात् परं चैव हरिवर्षं प्रचक्षते। अन्योन्यं नाभिवर्तन्ते साम्यं भवति वै यदा॥
en: On which depend all creatures in the universe for their existence. They do not depend on each other when there is equipoise.

sn: यदा तु विषमीभावमाविशन्ति परस्परम्। तदा देहैर्देहवन्तो व्यतिरोहन्ति नान्यथा॥
en: When these (elements), not existing in the natural state, exist with one another, then all creatures without any deviation spring into life with various sorts of bodies.

sn: अचिन्त्याः खलु ये आनुपूर्व्या विनश्यन्ति जायन्ते चानुपूर्वशः। सर्वाण्यपरिमेयाणि तदेषां रूपमैश्वरम्॥
en: The elements are destroyed in the order of the one succeeding the one that proceeds. They also spring into existence, one arising from one before it. All these are immeasurable, their forms being Brahma himself.

sn: तत्र तत्र हि दृश्यन्ते धातवः पाञ्चभौतिकाः। तेषां मनुष्यास्तर्केण प्रमाणानि प्रचक्षते॥
en: Creatures consisting of the five elements are seen in the universe. Men try to know their proportions by exercising their reason.

sn: भावा न तास्तर्केण साधयेत्। प्रकृतिभ्यः परं यत् तु तदचिन्त्यस्य लक्षणम्॥
en: Those matters that are inconceivable can never be solved by reason. What is above nature is an indication that it is inconceivable.

sn: सुदर्शनं प्रवक्ष्यामि द्वीपं तु कुरुनन्दन। परिमण्डलो महाराज द्वीपोऽसौ चक्रसंस्थितः॥
en: O descendant of Kuru, I shall now describe to you the island called Sudarshana. O king, this island is circular like a wheel.

sn: नदीजलप्रतिच्छन्नः पर्वतैश्चाभ्रसंनिभैः। पुरैश्च विविधाकारै रम्यैर्जनपदैस्तथा॥
en: It abounds in rivers and other waters, in mountains that look like masses of clouds, and in cities and in many charming provinces.

sn: वृक्ष पुष्पफलोपेतैः सम्पन्नधनधान्यवान्। लवणेन समुद्रेण समन्तात् परिवारितः॥
en: It is full of trecs covered with flowers and fruits and with crops of various kinds and with many other rich things. It is surrounded on all sides with the salt sea.

sn: यथा हि पुरुषः पश्येदादर्श मुखमात्मनः। एवं सुदर्शनद्वीपो दृश्यते चन्द्रमण्डले॥
en: As a man can see his face in a mirror, so is the island called Sudarshana seen in the lunar disc.

sn: द्विरंशे पिप्पलस्तत्र द्विरंशे च शशो महान्। सर्वौषधिसमावायः सर्वतः परिवारितः॥
en: Two of its parts appear like a pipal tree, the two others look like a large hare. It is surrounded on all sides with the various kinds of plants.

sn: आपस्ततोऽन्यो विज्ञेयाः शेषः संक्षेप उच्यते। ततोऽन्य उच्यते चायमेनं संक्षेपतः शृणु॥
en: Beside these portions, the rest is all water. I shall describe them to you shortly. Hear what I now describe in brief.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच उक्तो द्वीपस्य संक्षेपो विधिवद् बुद्धिमंस्त्वया। तत्त्वज्ञश्चासि सर्वस्य विस्तरं ब्रूहि संजय॥
en: Dhritarashtra said O Sanjaya, you are intelligent, you know the truth, you have duly given me in brief the description of the island. Tell us now of the island in detail.

sn: यावान् भूम्यवकाशोऽयं दृश्यते शशलक्षणे। तस्य प्रमाणं प्रब्रूहि ततो वक्ष्यसि पिप्पलम्॥
en: Tell us now of the dimension of that portion of the land that looks like a hare. You may then describe the portion that looks like the pipal tree.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवं राज्ञा स पृष्टस्तु संजयो वाक्यमब्रवीत्।
en: Having thus said by the king, Sanjaya spoke these words:

sn: संजय उवाच प्रागायता महाराज षडेते वर्षपर्वताः। अवगाढा [भयतः समुद्रौ पूर्वपश्चिमौ॥
en: Sanjaya said Stretching from east to west, there are six mountains that are all equal and that extend from the eastern to the western sea.

sn: हिमवान् हेमकूटश्च निषधश्च नगोत्तमः। नीलश्च वैदूर्यमयः श्वेतश्च शशिसंनिभः॥
en: They are named Himavat, Hemakut that foremost of mountains Nishadha, Nila that abounds in Vaidurya gems, Shveta, as white as the moon,

sn: सर्वधातुविचित्रश्च शृङ्गवान् नाम पर्वतः। एते वै पर्वता राजन् सिद्धचारणसेविताः॥
en: And Shringavat which is made of all kinds of metals. O king, these are the six mountains ever frequented by the Siddhas and the Charanas.

sn: एषामन्तरविष्कम्भो योजनानि सहस्रशः। तत्र पुण्या जनपदास्तानि वर्षाणि भारत॥
en: The space between them extends cne thousand Yojanas. There are many delightful kingdoms thereon. O descendant of Bharata, these divisions are called Varshas.

sn: वसन्ति तेषु सत्त्वानि नानाजातीनि सर्वशः। इदं तु भारतं वर्षं ततो हैमवतं परम्॥
en: In all these kingdoms live creatures of various kinds. This is the Varsha called after Bharata, Next to it the Varsha called after Himavat.

sn: हेमकूटात् परं चैव हरिवर्षं प्रचक्षते। दक्षिणेन तु नीलस्य निषधस्योत्तरेण तु॥
en: The land that is beyond Hemakuta is called Harivarsha; south of the Nila mountain and the north of the Nishadha.

sn: प्रागायतो महाभाग माल्यवान् नाम पर्वतः। ततः परं माल्यवतः पर्वतो गन्धमादनः॥
en: Is a mountain, O king, called Malyavat that extends from east to west. Beyond Malyavat is the mountain called the Gandhamadana.

sn: परिमण्डलयोर्मध्ये मेरुः कनकपर्वतः। आदित्यतरुणाभासो विधूम इव पावकः॥
en: Between these two (mountains) is a round mountain called Meru which is made of gold. It is as effulgent as the morning sun; it is like fire without smoke.

sn: योजनानां सहस्राणि चतुरशीतिरुच्छ्रितः। अधस्ताच्चतुरशीतिर्योजनानां महीपते॥
en: It is eighty-four thousand Yojanas high. O king, its depth is eighty-four thousand Yojanas.

sn: ऊर्ध्वमधश्च तिर्यक् च लोकानावृत्य तिष्ठति। तस्य पार्श्वेष्वमी द्वीपाश्चत्वारः संस्थिता विभो॥
en: It stands carrying the worlds above, below and transversely. O lord, by the side of Meru are situated four islands.

sn: भद्राश्वः केतुमालश्च जम्बूद्वीपश्च भारत। उत्तराश्चैव कुरवः कृतपुण्यप्रतिश्रयाः॥
en: Namely Bhadrashva, Ketumala, Jambudvipa also called Bharata, and Uttara Kuru which is the abode of the pious.

sn: विहगः सुमुखो यस्तु सुपर्णस्यात्मजः किल। स वै विचिन्तयामास सौवर्णान् वीक्ष्य वायसान्॥
en: The bird Sumukha, the son of Suparna (Garuda), seeing that all the birds on the Meru were of golden plumage, reflected.

sn: मेरुरुत्तममध्यानामधमानां च पक्षिणाम्। अविशेषकरो यस्मात् तस्मादेनं त्यजाम्यहम्॥
en: "I shall go away from this mountain, because there is no difference there between good, indifferent and bad birds".

sn: तमादित्योऽनुपर्येति सततं ज्योतिषां वरः। चन्द्रमाश्च सनक्षत्रो वायुश्चैव प्रदक्षिणः॥
en: That foremost of luminaries, the sun, always goes round the Meru, so does the moon with his attendant constellations so does also Vayu.

sn: स पर्वतो महाराज दिव्यपुष्पफलान्वितः। भवनैरावृतः सर्वैर्जाम्बूनदपरिष्कृतैः॥
en: O king, that mountain possesses celestial fruits and flowers; it is covered all over with houses made of burnished gold.

sn: तत्र देवगणा राजन् गन्धर्वासुरराक्षसाः। अप्सरोगणसंयुक्ताः शैले क्रीडन्ति सर्वदा॥
en: O king, there on that mountain the celestial, the Gandharvas, the Asuras and the Rakshasas with the Apasaras always come to sport.

sn: तत्र ब्रह्मा च रुद्रश्च शक्रश्चापि सुरेश्वरः। समेत्य विविधैर्यज्ञैर्यजन्तेऽनेकदक्षिणैः॥
en: There Brahma, Rudra, and Shakra the lord of the celestial, meet together and perform various kinds of sacrifices with large Dakshinas.

sn: तुम्बुरु रदश्चैव विश्वावसुर्हहा हुहूः। अभिगम्यामरश्रेष्ठांस्तुष्टुवुर्विविधैः स्तवैः॥
en: Tamburu, and Narada, Vishvavasu and the Hahas and the Huhus went there and adored the foremost of the celestial with various hymns.

sn: सप्तर्षयो महात्मानः कश्यपश्च प्रजापतिः। तत्र गच्छन्ति भद्रं ते सदा पर्वणि पर्वणि॥
en: The illustrious seven Rishis and Kashyapa, the lord of creatures, go there on every Parva day.

sn: तस्यैव मूर्धन्युशनाः काव्यो दैत्यैर्महीपते। इमानि तस्य रत्नानि तस्येमे रत्नपर्वताः॥
en: On the summit of that mountain, Ushanas, otherwise called the Poet, sports with the Dailyas. The jewels and gems and all precious stones belong to Meru.

sn: तस्मात् कुबेरो भगवांश्चतुर्थं भागमश्नुते। ततः कलांशं वित्तस्य मनुष्येभ्यः प्रयच्छति॥
en: A fourth part of them is enjoyed by Kubera. Only a sixteenth part he gives away to men to be enjoyed by them.

sn: पार्श्वे तस्योत्तरे दिव्यं सर्वर्तुकुसुमैश्चितम्। कर्णिकारवनं रम्यं शिलाजालसमुद्गतम्॥
en: On the northern side of Meru there is a charming and beautiful forest of Karnikaras. It is ever covered with the flowers of every season. It occupies a range of hills.

sn: तत्र साक्षात् पशुपतिर्दिव्यैर्भूतैः समावृतः। उमासहायो भगवान् रमते भूतभावनः॥
en: There sports the illustrious Pashupati, the creator of all things, surrounded by his celestial attendants and accompanied by Uma.

sn: कर्णिकारमयीं मालां बिभ्रत्पादावलम्बिनीम्। त्रिभित्रैः कृतोद्योतस्त्रिभिः सूर्यैरिवोदितैः॥
en: He wears a garland of Karnikars flowers round his neck which reaches down his feet and which blazes with radiance with his three eyes resembling three suns.

sn: तमुग्रतपसः सिद्धाः सुव्रताः सत्यवादिनः। पश्यन्ति न हि दुर्वृत्तैः शक्यो द्रष्टुं महेश्वरः॥
en: The Siddhas who are truthful, who are of excellent vows and austere asceticism can see him. Maheshvara is incapable of being seen by men of bad conduct.

sn: तस्य शैलस्य शिखरात् क्षीरधारा नरेश्वर। विश्वरूपापरिमिता भीमनिर्घातनि:स्वनः॥ पुण्या पुण्यतमैर्जुष्टा गङ्गा भागीरथी शुभा। प्लवन्तीव प्रवेगेन ह्रदे चन्द्रमसः शुभे॥
en: O king, from the summit of that mountain issues forth like a stream of milk the sacred and immeasurable Ganga of universal form resorted to by the pious. She falls with great force and fearful noise in the charming lake of Chandramas.

sn: तया ह्युत्पादित: पुण्यः स ह्रदः सागरोपमः। तां धारयामास तदा दुर्धरा पर्वतैरपि॥ शतं वर्षसहस्राणां शिरसैव पिनाकधूक्। मरोस्तु पश्चिमे भागे केतुमालो महीपते॥
en: That sacred lake like an ocean has been formed by Ganga herself. Ganga, incapable of being held by even the mountains, was held for one thousand years by the wilder of Pinaka on his head. O king, on the western side of the Meru is Ketumala.

sn: जम्बूखण्डस्तु तत्रैव सुमहान् नन्दनोयमः। आयुर्दश सहस्राणि वर्षाणां तत्र भारत॥
en: Here is also Jambukhanda, O king, which is greatly populated. O descendant of Bharata, the length of human life there is ten thousand years.

sn: सुवर्णवर्णाश्च नराः स्त्रियश्चाप्सरसोपमाः। अनामया वीतशोका नित्यं मुदितमानसाः॥
en: The men are of golden complexion. Women are all like Apsaras. All the persons are without sickness, and grief, and are always cheerful.

sn: जायन्ते मानवास्तत्र निष्टप्तकनकप्रभाः। गन्धमादनशृङ्गेयु कुबेरः सह राक्षसैः॥ संवृतोऽप्सरसा सङ्घर्मोदते गुह्यकाधिपः। गन्धमादनपादेषु परेष्वपरगण्डिकाः॥
en: The men born there possess effulgence like that of the melted gold. On the Gandhamadana the lord of Guhyakas, Kubera, with many Rakshasas and Apsaras passes his time in happiness. By the sides of the Gandhamadana there are many smaller mountains and hills.

sn: तत्र हृष्टा नरा राजंस्तेजोयुक्ता महाबलाः। स्त्रियश्चोत्पलवर्णाभाः सर्वाः सुप्रियदर्शनाः॥
en: The length of human life there is eleven thousand years. O king, the men there are cheerful, and possess great energy and great strength. The women are all of the complexion of the lotus. They are exceedingly beautiful.

sn: नीलात् परतरं श्वेतं श्वेताद्धैरण्यकं परम्। वर्षमैरावतं राजन् नानाजनपदावृतम्॥
en: Beyond the Nila (mountain) is Shveta; beyond Shveta is Hiranyaka, beyond Hiranyaka is Airavata abounding in many countries.

sn: धनु:संस्थे महाराज द्वे वर्षे दक्षिणोत्तरे। इलावृतं मध्यमं तु पञ्च वर्षाणि चैव हि॥
en: O king, the last Varsha in the north and Bharata Varsha in the south are both of the form of a bow. Ilavrita is situated in the very middle of the five Varshas.

sn: उत्तरोत्तरमेतेभ्यो वर्षमुद्रिच्यते गुणैः। आयुःप्रमाणमारोग्यं धर्मतः कामतोऽर्थतः॥
en: Amongst these seven Varshas, the one that is furthest north excels the one immediate south to it as regards its many features such as the length of life, stature, wealth, piety, pleasure and profit.

sn: समन्वितानि भूतानि तेषु वर्षेषु भारत। एवमेषा महाराज पर्वतैः पृथिवी चिता।॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, in these Varshas, creatures all live together. O king, the earth is thus covered with mountains.

sn: हेमकूटस्तु सुमहान् कैलासो नाम पर्वतः। यत्र वैश्रवणो राजन् गुह्यकैः सह मोदते॥
en: The great mountain of Hemakuta is also called Kailasa where, ( king, Vaishravana delightedly sports with his Guhyakas.

sn: अस्त्युत्तरेण कैलासं मैनाकं पर्वतं प्रति। हिरण्यशृङ्गः सुमहान् दिव्यो मणिमयो गिरिः॥
en: Immediately north of Kailasa and near the mountain Mainaka, there is a great and beautiful mountain called Manimeya which possesses golden peaks.

sn: तस्य पार्श्वे महद् दिव्यं शुभं काञ्चनवालुकम्। रम्यं बिन्दुसरो नाम यत्र राजा भगीरथ॥ द्रष्टुं भागीरथीं गङ्गामुवास बहुलाः समाः। यूपा मणिमयास्तत्र चैत्याचापि हिरण्मयाः॥
en: Near this mountain there is a large, celestial and delightful lake called Bindusara with golden sands. There king Bhagiratha, seeing Ganga who is called after his name, lived for many years. There are innumerable sacrificial stakes made of gems and Chaitya trees made of gold.

sn: तत्रेष्ट्वा तु गतः सिद्धिं सहस्राक्षो महायशाः। स्रष्टा भूतपतिर्यत्र सर्वलोकैः सनातनः॥
en: It was there that of greatly renowned Indra obtained success by performing sacrifices. There the lord of all creatures, the eternal creator of all the worlds.

sn: उपास्यते तिग्मतेजा यत्र भूतैः समन्ततः। नरनारायणौ ब्रह्मा मनुः स्थाणुश्च पञ्चमः॥
en: Endued with supreme energy, surrounded by his ghostly attendants, is adored. There Nara and Narayana and Brahma and Manu and Sthanu are ever present.

sn: तत्र दिव्या त्रिपथगा प्रथमं तु प्रतिष्ठिता। ब्रह्मलोकादपक्रान्ता सप्तधा प्रतिपद्यते॥ वस्वोकसारा नलिनी पावनी च सरस्वती। जम्बूनदी च सीता च गङ्गा सिन्धुश्च सप्तमी॥
en: There the celestial river Ganga, of three currents, issues out of the region of Brahima. There she first appeared. Then dividing herself into seven streams she became Vasvokasara, Nalini, the sin-cleansing Sarasvati, Jambunadi, Sita, Ganga and Sindhu.

sn: अचिन्त्या दिव्यसंकाशा प्रभोरेषैव संविधिः। उपासते यत्र सत्रं सहस्रयुगपर्यये।॥
en: The supreme lord has himself made all the arrangements as regards this inconceivable and celestial river. It is there that sacrifices have been performed on thousand of occasions at the revolution of the Yugas.

sn: दृश्यादृश्या च भवति तत्र तत्र सरस्वती। एता दिव्याः सप्तगङ्गास्त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुताः॥
en: As regards the Sarasvati, in some parts she becomes visible and in some parts she disappears. This celestial seven Gangas is known all over the three worlds.

sn: रक्षांसि वै हिमवति हेमकूटे तु गुह्यकाः। सर्प नागाश्च निषधे गोकर्णं च तपोवनम्॥
en: The Rakshasas live on the Himavat, the Guhyakas on Hemakuta and the Nagas on the Nishadha and the ascetics on the Gokarna.

sn: देवासुराणां सर्वेषां श्वेतपर्वत उच्यते। गन्धर्वा निषधे नित्यं नीले ब्रह्मपर्यस्तथा।।
en: The Shveta mountain is said to be the abode of the celestial and celestial and the Asuras. The Gandharvas live on the Nishadha and the Brahmana Rishis on the Nila.

sn: शृङ्गवांस्तु महाराज देवानां प्रतिसंचरः॥ इत्येतानि महाराज सप्त वर्षाणि भागशः।
en: The mountain of Shringavat is considered to be the resort of the celestial. O king of kings, these are the seven Varshas of the world as they are divided.

sn: भूतान्युपनिविष्टानि गतिमन्ति ध्रुवाणि च॥ तेषामृद्धिर्बहुविधा दृश्यते दैवमानुषी।
en: Various mobile and immobile creatures are all placed in them. Various sorts of prosperity, both providential and human are noticeable in them.

sn: अशक्या परिसंख्यातुं श्रद्धेया तु बुभूषता॥ यां तु पृच्छसि मां राजन् दिव्यामेतां शशाकृतिम्।
en: They cannot be counted. Those that are desirous of their own welfare believe in all this. I have now narrated to you the delightful region that is in the form of a hare which you asked me.

sn: पार्श्वे शशस्य द्वे वर्षे उक्ते ये दक्षिणोत्तरे। कर्णौ तु नागद्वीपश्च काश्यपद्वीप एव च।॥ ताम्रपर्णः शिरो राजञ्छीमान् मलयपर्वतः। एतद् द्वितीयं द्वीपस्य दृश्यते शशसंस्थितम्॥
en: At the end of the region are the two Varshas, namely one on the north and the other on the south. Then again the two islands Nagadvipa and Kashyapadvipa are the two cars of this region of the form of a hare. O king, the beautiful mountain of Malaya, with stones like plates of copper, forms the second part of Jambudvipa. This makes it look like a hare.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच मेरोरथोत्तरं पार्श्व पूर्वं चाचक्ष्व संजय। निखिलेन महाबुद्धे माल्यवन्तं च पर्वतम्॥
en: Dhritarashtra said O Sanjaya, O greatly intelligent one, tell me in detail about the country on the north and the east of the Meru and also about the Malyavat mountain.

sn: संजय उवाच दक्षिणेन तु नीलस्य मेरोः पार्श्वे तथोत्तरे। उत्तराः कुरवो राजन् पुण्याः सिद्धनिषेविताः॥
en: Sanjaya said O king, on the south of the Nila mountain and on the north of the Meru are the sacred Northern Kurus where dwell the Siddhas,

sn: तत्र वृक्षा मधुफला नित्यपुष्पफलोपगाः। पुष्पाणि च सुगन्धीनि रसवन्ति फलानि च॥
en: The trees there bear sweet fruits, and are always covered with flowers and fruits. All the flowers are of the sweetest fragrance and all the fruits are of the best taste.

sn: सर्वकामफलास्तत्र केचिद् वृक्षा जनाधिप। अपरे क्षीरिणो नाम वृक्षास्तत्र नराधिप॥
en: O king, some of the trees produce fruits as one desires to cat. There are some trees that are called "Milk-yielding".

sn: ये क्षरन्ति सदा क्षीरं षड्रसं चामृतोपमम्। वस्त्राणि च प्रसूयन्ते फलेष्वाभरणानि च॥
en: They always produce milk and the six different kinds of food with the taste of ambrosia. They also produce cloths, and their fruits are ornaments.

sn: सर्वा मणिमयी भूमिः सूक्ष्मकाञ्चनवालुका। सर्वर्तुसुखसंस्पर्शा निष्पङ्का च जनाधिप।
en: The whole ground is covered with gems and golden sands. A certain part of this region which is extremely delightful is seen to be as radiant as the ruby or the diamond or the Vaidurya gem or other jewels or of the hue of the lotus. O king, all the seasons there are charming, and no part of its ground ever for comes miry.

sn: पुध्यकरिण्यः शुभास्तत्र सुखस्पर्शा मनोरमाः॥ देवलोकच्युताः सर्वे जायन्ते तत्र मानवाः।
en: Its tanks are charming, delicious and full of pure water. The men born there have all come down from the land of the celestial.

sn: शुक्लाभिजनसम्पन्नाः सर्वे सुप्रियदर्शनाः॥ मिथुनानि च जायन्ते स्त्रियश्चाप्सरसोपमाः।
en: All are of pure birth and all are exceedingly handsome. Husband and wife are born there and women there are like the Apsaras in beauty.

sn: तेषां ते क्षीरिणां क्षीरं पिबन्त्यमृतसंनिभम्॥ मिथुनं जायते काले समं तच्च प्रवर्धते।
en: They drink the milk of these “Milkyielding” trees which is as sweet as the ambrosia. The pair grow up there equally.

sn: तुल्यरूपगुणोपेतं समवेषं तथैव च॥ एकैकमनुरक्तं च चक्रवाकसमं विभो।
en: O king, they, both possessing equal beauty, both possessing equal virtues, both wearing equal dresses, grow up in great love like a pair of Chakravakas (birds).

sn: निरामयाश्च ते लोका नित्यं मुदितमानसाः॥ दश वर्षसहस्राणि दश वर्षशतानि च। जीवन्ति ते महाराज न चान्योन्यं जहत्युत॥ भारुण्डा नाम शकुनास्तीक्ष्णतुण्डा महाबलाः। तान् निर्हरन्तीह मृतान् दरीषु प्रक्षिपन्ति च॥ उत्तराः कुरवो राजन् व्याख्यातास्ते समासतः।
en: The dwellers of this region are free from diseases. They are ever happy. O king, they live ten thousand and ten hundred years and they never abandon one another. A kind of birds called Bharunda of sharp beaks and of great strength takes them up when dead and throws them into the mountain caves. O king, I have now described to you the northern Kuru.

sn: मेरोः पार्श्वमहं पूर्वं वक्ष्याम्यथ यथातथम्॥ तस्य मूर्धाभिषेकस्तु भद्राश्वस्य विशाम्पते।
en: I shall now describe to you the eastern side of the mountain Meru. O king, of all the regions there, one called Bhadrashva is the foremost.

sn: भद्रसालवनं यत्र कालाम्रश्च महाद्रुमः॥ कालाम्रस्तु महाराज नित्यपुष्पफलः शुभः।
en: There is a large forest of Bhadrashva and also a very big tree called Kalamra. O king, this Kalamra is always full of fruits and flowers.

sn: दुमश्च योजनोत्सेधः सिद्धचारणसेवितः। तत्र ते पुरुषाः श्वेतास्तेजोयुक्ता महाबलाः।
en: It is a Yojana in height. It is adorned by the Siddhas and the Charanas. The men there are all while. They possess great energy and great strength.

sn: स्त्रियः कुमुदवर्णाश्च सुन्दर्यः प्रियदर्शनाः॥ चन्द्रप्रभाश्चन्द्रवर्णाः पूर्णचन्द्रनिभाननाः।
en: The women possess the complexion like that of lillies. They are very beautiful and charming. They possess the radiance of the morn; they are as white as the morn. Their faces are like full moon.

sn: चन्द्रशीतलगायश्च नृत्यगीतविशारदाः॥ दश वर्षसहस्राणि तत्रायुर्भरतर्षभ।
en: Their bodies are as cool as the rays of the moon, They are all highly accomplished in singing and dancing. O foremost of the Bharata race the length of life here is ten thousand years.

sn: कालाम्ररसपीतास्ते नित्यं संस्थितयौवनाः॥ दक्षिणेन तु नीलस्य निषधस्योत्तरेण तु।
en: They remain young for ever by drinking the juice of the Kalamra tree. On the north of the Nishadha.

sn: सुदर्शनो नाम महाञ्जम्बूवृक्षः सनातनः॥ सर्वकामफलः पुण्यः सिद्धचारणसेवितः।
en: There is a very large Jambu tree by name of Sudarshana which is eternal. When adorned by the Siddhas and Charanas, that sacred tree grants every desire.

sn: तस्य नाम्ना समाख्यातो जम्बूद्वीप: सनातनः॥ योजनानां सहस्रं च शतं च भरतर्षभ। उत्सेधो वृक्षराजस्य दिवस्पृङ्मनुजेश्वरः॥ अरत्नीनां सहस्रं च शतानि दश पञ्च च। परिणाहस्तु वृक्षस्य फलानां रसभेदिनाम्॥ पतमानानि तान्युर्वी कुर्वन्ति विपुलं स्वनम्।
en: This country has been named Jambudvipa after the name of this tree. O best of the Bharata race, O ruler of men, this tree is in height one thousand and one hundred Yojanas. It touches the very heavens. The circumference of a fruit of that free which bursts by itself when ripe is eleven thousand and five hundred cubits. In falling on the ground, they make a very loud noise.

sn: मुञ्चन्ति च रसं राजेस्तस्मिन् रजतसंनिभम्॥ तस्या जम्ब्वाः फलरसो नदी भूत्वा जनाधिप।
en: O king, then they pour out a silvery juice on the ground. O king, that juice of the Jambu, becoming a river.

sn: मेरुं प्रदक्षिणं कृत्वा सम्प्रयात्युत्तरान् कुरून्।॥ तत्र तेषां मन:शान्तिन पिपासा जनाधिप। तस्मिन् फलरसे पीते न जरा बाधते च तान्॥ तत्र जाम्बूनदं नाम कनकं देवभूषणम्। इन्द्रगोपकसंकाशं जायते भास्वरं तु तत्॥ तरुणादित्यवर्णाश्च जायन्ते तत्र मानवाः।
en: Passing round the Meru mountains comes to the country of the northern Kurus. If that juice is drunk, it gives peace of mind. No thirst is ever after felt. O king, old age never comes. A kind of gold called Jambunada is also produced there. They are used in making celestial weapons. They are very shining and look like the Indragopaka insccts. The men born there possess the complexion of the morning sun.

sn: तथा माल्यवतः शृङ्गे दृश्यते हव्यवाट् सदा॥ नाम्ना संवर्तको नाम कालग्निर्भरतर्षभ।
en: O best of the Bharata race on the summit of the Malyavan is always seen the fire called Samvartaka, the fire that blazes forth at the end of a Yoga to destroy the universe.

sn: तथा माल्यवतः शृङ्गे पूर्वपूर्वानुगण्डिका॥ योजनानां सहस्राणि पञ्चषण्माल्यवानथ।
en: o summit of the Malyavat, small mountains. O king, the Malyavat measures eleven thousand Yojanas.

sn: महारजतसंकाशा जायन्ते तत्र मानवाः॥ ब्रह्मलोकच्युताः सर्वे सर्वे सर्वेषु साधवः।
en: The men born there possess complexion like gold. They have all descendent from the abode of Brahma, and thcy are all utterers of the Vedas.

sn: तपस्तप्यन्ति ते तीव्र भवन्ति झूर्ध्वरेतसः। रक्षणार्थं तु भूतानां प्रविशन्ते दिवाकरम्॥
en: The undergo severe asceticism. They have their passions under complete control. They all enter the sun for the protection of creation.

sn: षष्टिस्तानि सहस्राणि षष्टिरेव शतानि च। अरुणस्याग्रतो यान्ति परिवार्य दिवाकरम्॥
en: They are sixty six thousand in number. They proceed in front of Aruna and surrounded the sun.

sn: षष्टि वर्षसहस्राणि षष्टिमेव शतानि च। आदित्यतापतप्तास्ते विशन्ति शशिमण्डलम्॥
en: Having been heated with the sun's rays for sixty six thousand years, they then enter the solar disc.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच वर्षाणां चैव नामानि पर्वतानां च संजय। आचक्ष्व मे यथातत्त्वं ये च पर्वतवासिनः॥
en: Dhritarashtra said O Sanjaya, tell me in detail the names of all the Varshas and of all the mountains and also of all that live on these mountains.

sn: संजय उवाच दक्षिणेन तु श्वेतस्य निषधस्योत्तरेण तु। वर्ष रमणकं नाम जायन्ते तत्र मानवाः॥ शुक्लाभिजनसम्पन्नाः सर्वे सुप्रियदर्शनाः। निःसपत्नाश्च ते सर्वे जायन्ते तत्र मानवाः॥ दश वर्षसहस्राणि शतानि दश पञ्च च। जीवन्ति ते महाराज नित्यं मुदितमानसाः॥
en: Sanjaya said On the south of the Shveta mountains and on the north of the Nishadha is the Varsha called Ramanaka. The men that are born there are all white. They are nobly born, and they are all handsome. They have no enemies.

sn: दक्षिणेन तु नीलस्य निषधस्योत्तरेण तु। वर्ष हिरण्मयं नाम यत्र हैरण्वती नदी॥
en: On the south of the Nishadha is the Varsha called Hiranmaya where flow the river Hiranvati.

sn: यत्र चायं महाराज पक्षिराट् पतगोत्तमः। यक्षानुगा महाराज धनिनः प्रियदर्शनाः॥
en: o king, there lives the king of birds, Garuda. O king, the people there are all handsome and rich, they are all followers of the Yakshas.

sn: महाबलास्तत्र जना राजन् मुदितमानसाः। एकादश सहस्राणि वर्षाणां ते जनाधिप॥ आयुः प्रमाणं जीवन्ति शतानि दश पञ्च च। शृङ्गाणि च विचित्राणि त्रीण्येव मनुजाधिप।॥
en: 0 king, the men there possess great strength, and they are ever cheerful. O king, there length of life is eleven thousand and five hundred years. O lord of men, the Shringavat mountain has there beautiful peaks.

sn: एकं मणिमयं तत्र तथैकं रोक्ममद्भुतम्। सर्वरत्नमयं चैकं भवनैरुपशोभितम्॥
en: One of these (peaks) is made of gold, another is made of jewels and the other is made of all kinds of gems and adorned with large mansions.

sn: तत्र स्वयंप्रभा देवी नित्यं वसति शाण्डिली। उत्तरेण तु शृङ्गस्य समुद्रान्ते जनाधिप॥
en: There always dwells the self luminous lady named Shandili. On the north of Shringavat and as far as the sea, O king,

sn: वर्षमैरावतं नाम तस्माच्छृङ्गमतः परम्। न तत्र सूर्यस्तपति न जीर्यन्ते च मानवाः॥
en: Is the Varsha called Airavat. As there is this jewelled peak, therefore it is superior to all Varshas. The sun does not produce heat there and men are not subject to decay.

sn: चन्द्रमाश्च सनक्षत्रो ज्योतिर्भूत इवावृतः। पद्मप्रभाः पद्मवर्णाः पद्मपत्रनिभेक्षणा:॥ पद्मपत्रसुगन्धाश्च जायन्ते तत्र मानवाः। अनिष्यन्दा इष्टगन्धा निरहारा जितेन्द्रियाः॥
en: The moon with the stars is the only source of light there. Possessing the radiance and complexion of the lotus and eyes that resemble lotus-petals, the men born there have the fragrance of the lotus. With winkless eyes and with charming fragrance, they move about without taking food. They are completely selfcontrolled.

sn: देवलोकच्युताः सर्वे तथा विरजसो नृप। त्रयोदश सहस्राणि वर्षाणां ते जनाधिप॥१४॥ आयुःप्रमाणं जीवन्ति नरा भरतसत्तम। क्षीरोदस्य समुद्रस्य तथैवोत्तरतः प्रभुः।
en: They have all descended from the land of the celestial. O king, they are all without sin of any kind. O best of the Bharata race, the length of their life is thirteen thousand years. On the north of the milky ocean the lord.

sn: हरिर्वसति वैकुण्ठः शकटे कनकामये॥ अष्टचक्रं हि तद् यान् भूतयुक्तं मनोजवम्।
en: The eternal Hari lives on His golden chariot. That chariot is furnished with eight wheels. Innumerable supernatural creatures are placed there each having the fleetness of mind.

sn: अग्निवर्णं महातेजो जाम्बूनदविभूषितम्॥ स प्रभुः सर्वभूतानां विभुश्च भरतर्षभ।
en: Its complexion is like that of the fire. It possesses great velocity and it is adorned with gold. O best of the Bharata race. He is the lord of all creatures and possesses every kind of prosperity.

sn: संक्षेपो विस्तरश्चैव कर्ता कारयिता तथा॥ पृथिव्यापस्तथाऽऽकाशं वायुस्तेजश्च पार्थिव। स यज्ञः सर्वभूतानामास्यं तस्य हुताशनः॥
en: He is finite and He is infinite. He is the doer as well as the instrument of action. O king, He is earth, water, ether air and fire. He is the sacrifice of all creatures and fire is His mouth.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एवमुक्त: संजयेन धृतराष्ट्रो महामनाः। ध्यानमन्वगमद् राजन् पुत्रान् प्रति जनाधिप॥
en: Vaishampayana said O king, having been thus addressed by Sanjaya, the illustrious king Dhritarashtra meditated long about his sons.

sn: स विचिन्त्य महातेजाः पुनरेवाब्रवीद् वचः। असंशयं सूतपुत्र कालः संक्षिपते जगत्।॥
en: endued as he was with great energy he, having thus reflected, said these words to Sanjaya. "O Suta's son, there is no doubt that it is Time that destroys the universe.

sn: सृजते च पुनः सर्वं विद्यति नेह शाश्वतम्। नरो नारायणश्चैव सर्वज्ञः सर्वभूतहत्॥ देवा वैकुण्ठमित्याहुनरा विष्णुमिति प्रभुम्॥
en: It is Time that again creates every thing. Nothing is ever-lasting in this world. It is omniscient Nara and Narayana that destroy all creatures. The celestial call Him Vaikuntha, men call Him the Lord Vishnu.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच यदिदं भारतं वर्षं यत्रेदं मूर्च्छितं बलम्। यत्रातिमात्रलुब्धोऽयं पुत्रो दुर्योधनो मम॥ यत्र गृद्धाः पाण्डुपुत्रा यत्र मे सज्जते मनः। एतन्मे तत्त्वमाचक्ष्व त्वं हि मे बुद्धिमान् मतः॥
en: Dhritarashtra said Tell me about the Varsha called Bharata in which these foolish men have assembled (to fight), for which my son Duryodhana has become so very covetous, which the Pandavas also are desirous of obtaining and in which even my mind sinks. Tell me all this, for you are, in my opinion endued with great intelligence.

sn: संजय उवाच न तत्र पाण्डवा गृद्धाः शृणु राजन् वचो मम। गृद्धो दुर्योधनस्तत्र शकुनिश्चापि सौबलः॥
en: Sanjaya said O king, hear my words. The Pandavas are not covetous about this country. It is Duryodhana who is covetous. It is the son of Subala, Shakuni.

sn: अपरे क्षत्रियाश्चैव नानाजनपदेश्वराः। गृद्धा भारते वर्षे न मृष्यन्ति परस्परम्॥
en: And also many other Kshatriyas who are rulers of countries and who being covetous of this country cannot tolerate one another,

sn: ये अत्र ते कीर्तयिष्यामि वर्ष भारत भारतम्। प्रियमिन्द्रस्य देवस्य मनोवैवस्वतस्य च॥ पृथोस्तु राजन् वैन्यस्य तथेक्ष्वाकोर्महात्मनः। ययातेरम्बरीषस्य मान्धातुर्नहुषस्य च॥ तथैव मुचुकुन्दस्य शिबैरौशीनरस्य च। ऋषभस्य तथैलस्य नृगस्य नृपतेस्तथा॥ कुशिकस्य त दुर्धर्ष गाधेश्चैव महात्मनः। सोमकस्य त दुर्धर्ष दिलीपस्य तथैव च॥ अन्येषां च महाराज क्षत्रियाणां बलीयसाम्। सर्वेषामेव राजेन्द्र प्रियं भारत भारतम्॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, I shall now speak to you about the country named after Bharata, It is the beloved land of Indra. O king, this land called after Bharata, is also the beloved land of Manu, the son of Vivasvat, of Pritha, of Vainya, of the illustrious Ikshvaku, of Yayati, of Ambarisha, of Mandhata, of Nahusha, of Muchukunda, of Shibi, the son of Ushinaras of Rishabha, of Ila, of king Nriga, of Kushika, of the illustrious Gadhi, of Somaka, and of Dilipa and of many other kings. O chastiser of foes, I shall now describe to you the country as I have heard of it.

sn: तत् ते वर्षं प्रवक्ष्यामि यथायथमरिन्दम। शृणु मे गदतो राजन् यन्मां त्वं परिपृच्छसि॥ महेन्द्रो मलयः सह्यः शुक्तिमानृक्षवानपि। विध्यश्च पारियात्रश्च सप्तैते कुलपर्वताः॥ तेषां सहस्रशो राजन् पर्वतास्ते समीपतः। अविज्ञाताः सारवन्तो विपुलाचित्रसानवः॥
en: O king, hear as I speak of what you have asked me. Mahendra, Malaya, Sahya, Shuktimat, Gandhamadana, Vindhya, and Paripatra, these are the seven main mountains forming the boundaries (of Bharata Varsha). Besides these there are 0 king, thousands of other mountains which are hard and huge and which contain many excellent valleys. Besides these (large ones) there are many smaller mountains inhabited by the barbarians.

sn: अन्ये ततोऽपरिज्ञाता ह्रस्वा ह्रस्वोपजीविनः। आर्या म्लेच्छाश्च कौरव्य तैर्मिश्राः पुरुषा विभो॥ नदी पिबन्ति विपुलां गङ्गां सिन्धुं सरस्वतीम्। गोदावरी नर्मदां च बाहुदां च महानदीम्॥ शतदूं चन्द्रभागां च यमुनां च महानदीम्। दृषद्वतीं विपाशां च विपापां स्थूलवालुकाम्॥ नदीं वेत्रवतीं चैव कृष्णवेणां च निम्नगाम्। इरावती वितस्तां च पयोष्णीं देविकामपि॥ वेदस्मृतां वेदवती त्रिदिवामिक्षुलां कृमिम्। करीषिणी चित्रवाहां चित्रसेनां च निम्नगाम्॥ गोमती धूतपापां च वन्दनां च महानदीम्। कौशिकीं त्रिदिवां कृत्या निचितां लोहितारणीम्॥ रहस्यां शतकुम्भां च सरयूं च तथैव च। चर्मण्वतीं वेत्रवती हस्तिसोमां दिशं तथा॥ शरावती पयोष्णीं च वेणां भीमरथीमपि। कावेरी चुलुकां चापि वाणीं शतबलामपि॥ नीवारामहितां चापि सुप्रयोगां जनाधिप। पवित्रां कुण्डली सिन्धुं राजनीं पुरमालिनीम्॥ पूर्वाभिरामां वीरां च भीमामोघवती तथा। पाशाशिनी पापहरां महेन्द्रां पाटलावतीम्॥ करीषिणीमसिक्नी च कुशचीरां महानदीम्। मकरी प्रवरां मेनां हेमां घृतवतीं तथा॥ पुरावतीमनुष्णां च शैब्यां कापी च भारत। सदानीरामधृष्या च कुशधारां महानदीम्॥ सदाकान्तां शिवां चैव तथा वीरमतीमपि। वस्त्रां सुवस्त्रां गौरी च कम्पनां सहिरण्वतीम्॥ वरां वीरकरां चापि पञ्चमी च महानदीम्। रथचित्रां ज्योतिरथां विश्वामित्रां कपिञ्जलाम्॥ उपेन्द्रा बहुलां चैव कुवीरामम्बुवाहिनीम्। विनदी पिञ्जलां वेणा तुङ्गवेणां महानदीम्॥ विदिशां कृष्णवेणां च ताम्रां च कपिलामपि। खलु सुवामां वेदाश्वां हरिश्रावां महापगाम्॥
en: O descendant of Kuru, O lord, the Aryans and the Mlechchhas and many other races drink the waters of the following rivers. The magnificent Ganga, Sindhu, Sarasvati, Godavari, Narmada, the large river called Bahuda, Shatadru, Chandrabhaga, the large river called Yamuna, Drishadvati, Vipasha, Vipapa, Sthulabaluka, Vetravati, Krishnavena, Iravati. Vitasta, Payoshini, Devika, Vedasmrita, Vedavati, Tridiva, Ikshuala, Karishini, Chitravaha, Chitrasena, Gomati, Dhutapapa, Gandaki, Kaushaki, Tridiva, Kritya, Nichita, Lohitarani, Rahasya, Shatakumbha, Sarayu, Charamnvati, Vetravati, Hastisoma, Dika, Sharavati, Payoshini, Vena, Bhimarathi, Kaveri, Chuluka, Vani, Shatabala, Nivara, Ahita, Suprayoga, Pavitra, Kundali, Sindhu, Rajani, Puramalini, Purvabhirama, Vira, Bhima, Oghavati, Pashashini, Papahara, Mahendra, Patalavati, Karishini, Asikni, Kushachira, Makari, Pravara, Mena, Hema, Ghritavati, Puravati, Anushna, Shaivya, Kapi, Sadanira, Adhrishya, The mystery river Kushadhara, Sadakanta, Shiva, Viramati, Vastra, Suvastra, Gouri, Kampana, Hiranvati, Vara, Virakara, Great river Panchami, Rathachitra, Jyotiratha, Vishvamitra, Kapinjala, Upendra, Bahula, Kuvira, Ambuvahini, Vinadi, Pinjala, Vena, the great river Tungavena, Vidisha, Krishnavena, Tamara, Kapila, Khalu, Suvama, Vedashrva, the great river Harishrava.

sn: शीघ्रां च पिच्छिलां चैव भारद्वाजी च निम्नगाम्। कौशिकी निम्नगां शोणां बाहुदामथ चन्द्रमाम्॥ दुर्गा चित्रशिलां चैव ब्रह्मवेध्यां बृहद्वतीम्। यवक्षामथ रोहीं च तथा जाम्बूनदीमपि।॥ सुनसां तमसां दासी वसामन्यां वराणसीम्। नीलां घृतवतीं चैव पर्णाशां च महानदीम्॥
en: Shighra, Pichhala, Bharadvaji, Kaushika, Sona and Chandrama, Durga, Chintrashila, Brahmavaidhya, Brihadvati, Yavaksha, Rohi, Jambunadi, Sunasa, Tamasa, Dasi, Vasa, Varuna and Asi, Nila, Ghritavati, The great river Parnasha, Tamasi, Vrishabha, Brahmamedhya, Brihadhani.

sn: मानवीं वृषभां चैव ब्रह्ममेध्यां बृहनीम्। एताश्चान्याश्च बहुधा महानद्यो जनाधिप॥ सदा निरामयां कृष्णां मन्दगां मदवाहिनीम्। ब्राह्मणी च महागौरी दुर्गामपि च भारत॥ चित्रोपलां चित्ररथां मञ्जुलां वाहिनी तथा। मन्दाकिनी वैतरणी कोषां चापि महानदीम्॥ शुक्तिमतीमनङ्गां च तथैव वृषसाह्वयाम्। लोहित्यां करतोयां च तथैव वृषकाह्वयाम्॥ कुमारीमृषिकुल्यां च मारिषां च सरस्वतीम्। मन्दाकिनीं सुषुण्यां च सर्वां गङ्गां च भारत॥
en: O king, these the many other large rivers such as Sadaniramaya, Krishna, Mandaga, Mandavahini, Brahmini, Mahagouri, Durga, Chitrotpla, Chitraratha, Manjula, Vahini, Mandakani, Vaitarani, Kosha Mahanadi, Shuktimati, Ananga, Pushpavini, Utpalavati, Lohitya, Karatoya, Vrishaka, Kumari, Rishikulya, Marisha, Sarasvati, and Mandakini, Supunya, Sarva and Ganga,

sn: विश्वस्य मातरः सर्वाः सर्वाश्चैव महाफलाः। तथा नद्यस्त्वप्रकाशाः शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः॥ इत्येताः सरितो राजन् समाख्याता यथास्मृति।
en: O descendant of Bharata, all these are the mother of the universe and the produce great merit. Besides these rivers, there are hundreds and thousand of rivers that have no names. O king, I have mentioned to you all the rivers that I remember.

sn: अत उर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध गदतो मम॥ तत्रेमे कुरुपाञ्चाला: शाल्वा माद्रेयजाङ्गलाः। शूरसेनाः पुलिन्दाश्च बोधा मालास्तथैव च॥ मत्स्याः कुशल्या: सौशल्या:कुन्तयः कान्तिकोसलाः। चेदिमत्स्यकरूषाश्च भोजाः सिन्धुपुलिन्दकाः॥ उत्तमाश्वदशार्णाश्च मेकलाश्चोत्कलैः सह। पञ्चाला: कोसलाश्चैव नैकपृष्ठा धुरंधराः॥ गोधा मद्रकलिङ्गाश्च काशयोऽपरकाशयः। जठराः कुक्कुराश्चैव सदशार्णाश्च भारत॥ कुन्तयोऽवन्तयश्चैव तथैवापरकुन्तयः। गोमन्ता मण्डकाः सण्डा विदर्भा रूपवाहिकाः॥ अश्मकाः पाण्डुराष्ट्राश्च गोपराष्ट्राः करीतयः। अधिराज्यकुशाद्याश्च मल्लराष्ट्रं च केवलम्॥ वारवास्यायवाहाश्चचक्राश्चक्रातयः शकाः। विदेहा मगधाः स्वक्षा मलजा विजयास्तथा॥ अङ्गा वङ्गा कलिङ्गाश्च यकृल्लोमान एव च। मल्ला: सुदेष्णाः प्रह्लादामाहिकाः शशिकास्तथा।।४६। बाह्निका वाटधानाश्च आभीराः कालतोयकाः। अपरान्ताः परान्ताश्च पञ्चालाश्चर्ममण्डलाः॥ अटवीशिखराश्चैव मेरुभूताश्च मारिष। उपावृत्तानुपावृत्ताः स्वराष्ट्राः केकयास्तथा॥ कुन्दापरान्ता माहेयाः कक्षा सामुद्रनिष्कुटाः। अन्ध्राश्च बहवो राजन्नन्तगिर्यास्तथैव च॥ बहिगिर्याङ्गमलजा मगधा मानवर्जकाः। समन्तराः प्रावृषेया भार्गवाश्च जनाधिप॥ पुण्ड्रा भर्गाः किराताश्च सुदृष्टा यामुनास्तथा। शका निषादा निषधास्तथैवानर्तनैर्ऋताः॥ दुर्गाला: प्रतिमत्स्याश्च कुन्तलाः कोसलास्तथा। तीरग्रहाः शूरसेना ईजिकाः कन्यकागुणाः॥ तिलभारा मसीराश्च मधुमन्तः सुकन्दकाः। काश्मीराः सिन्धुसौवीरा गान्धारा दर्शकान्तथा॥ अभीसारा उलूताश्च शैवला बालिकास्तथा। दार्वी च वानवा दर्वा वातजामर थोरगाः॥ बहुवाद्याश्च कौरव्य सुदामानः सुमल्लिकाः। वध्राः करीषकाश्चापि कुलिन्दोपत्यकास्तथा॥ वनायवो दशापार्श्वरोमाणः कुशबिन्दवः। कच्छा गोपालकक्षाश्च जाङ्गलाः कुरुवर्णकाः॥ किराता बर्वराः सिद्धा वैदेहास्ताम्रलिप्तकाः। ओण्ड्राम्लेच्छाः सैसिरिध्राः पार्वतीयाश्च मारिष॥ अथापरे जनपदा दक्षिणा भरतर्षभ। द्रविडाः केरलाः प्राच्या भूषिका वनवासिकाः॥ कर्णाटका महिषका विकल्पा मूषकास्तथा। शिल्लिकाः कुन्तलाश्चैव सौहृदा नभकाननाः॥ कौकुट्टकास्तथा चोलाः कोङ्कणा मालवा नराः। समङ्गाः करकाश्चैव कुकुराङ्गारमारिषाः॥ ध्वजिन्युत्सवसंकेतास्त्रिगर्ताः शाल्वसेनयः। व्यूका: कोकबकाः प्रोष्ठाः समवेगवशास्तथा॥ तथैव विन्ध्यचुलिकाः पुलिन्दा वल्कलैः सह। मालवा बल्लवाश्चैव तथैवापरबल्लवाः॥ कुलिन्दाः कालदाश्चैव कुण्डलाः करटास्तथा। मूषकाः स्तनबालाश्च सनीपा घटसुंजयाः॥ अठिदाः पाशिवाटाश्च तनयाः सुनयास्तथा। ऋषिका विदभाः काकास्तङ्गणाः परतङ्गणाः॥ उत्तराश्चापरम्लेच्छा: क्रूरा भरतसत्तम। यवनाचीनकाम्बोजा दारुणा म्लेच्छजातयः॥ सकृद्ग्रहा: कुलत्थाश्च हूणाः पारसिकैः सह। तथैव रमणाश्चीनास्तथैव दशमालिकाः॥

sn: क्षत्रियोपनिवेशाश्च वैश्यशूद्रकुलानि च। शूद्राभीराश्च दरदाः काश्मीराः पशुभिः सह॥ खाशीराश्चान्तचाराश्च पल्हवा गिरिगह्वराः। आत्रेयाः सभरद्वाजास्तथैव स्तनपोषिकाः॥ प्रोषकाश्च कलिङ्गाश्च किरातानां च जातयः। तोमरा हन्यमानाश्च तथैव करभञ्जकाः॥ एते चान्ये जनपदाः प्राच्योदीच्यास्तथैव च।
en: Besides this country is the abode of many Kshatriyas, Vaishyas and Shudra. There are the Shudraviras, the Daradas, the Kashmiras, the Paitis, the Khashiras, the Atreyas, the Bharadvaja, the Stanopi Shikas, the Poshakas, the Kalingas, and many other Kiratas, the Tomaras, the Hansamargas, and Karamanjakas. These and other kingdoms are in the east and in the north.

sn: उद्देशमात्रेण मया देशाः संकीर्तिता विभो॥ यथागुणबलं चापि त्रिवर्गस्य महाफलम्। दुह्येत धेनुः कामधुग् भूमिः सम्यगनुष्ठिताः॥ तस्यां गृद्ध्यन्ति राजानः शूरा धर्मार्थकोविदाः।
en: O lord, I have briefly mentioned them. If the resources of the earth are properly developed, she is then like an all-yielding cow, from which the threefold objects of Dharma, Artha and Kama might be linked. Brave kings learned in Dharma and Artha have become covetous of earth.

sn: ते त्यजन्त्याहवे प्राणान् वसुगृद्धास्तरस्विनः॥ देवमानुषकायानां कामं भूमिः परायणम्।
en: From the thirst of wealth, they would even abandon their lives in battle. Earth is the stay of creatures endued with celestial bodies as well as human bodies.

sn: अन्योन्यस्यावलुम्पन्ति सारमेया यथाऽमिषम्॥ राजानो भरतश्रेष्ठ भोक्तुकामा वसुंधराम्।
en: O foremost of the Bharata race, with the desire of enjoying earth they have become like dogs that snatch meat from one another.

sn: न चापि तृप्ति: कामानां विद्यतेऽद्यापि कस्यचित्।।७४। तस्मात् परिग्रहे भूमेर्यतन्ते कुरुपाण्डवाः। साम्ना भेदेन दानेन दण्डेनैव च भारत॥ पिता भ्राता च पुत्राश्च खं द्योश्च नरपुङ्गव। भूमिर्भवति भूतानां सम्यगच्छिद्रदर्शना॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, their ambition is unlimited; it is for this the Kurus and the Pandavas are trying, to get possession of the earth by negotiations, by disunion, by gift and by battle. O foremost of men, if earth be properly treated, she becomes the father, the mother, the children, the sky and the heaven of all creatures.

description: Description of the duration of life in Bharatavarsha
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच भारतस्यास्य वर्षस्य तथा हैमवतस्य च। प्रमाणमायुषः सूत बलं चापि शुभाशुभम्॥ अनागतमतिक्रान्तं वर्तमानं च संजय। आचक्ष्व मे विस्तरेण हरिवर्षं तथैव च॥
