en: Yudhishthira said Come, come, all of us will fight with your foolish brothers. O Yuyutsu, both Vasudeva and all of us say.

description: Honour of Bhishma and others by Yudhisthira
sn: वृणोमि त्वां महाबाहो युद्ध्यस्व मम कारणात्। त्वयि पिण्डश्च तन्तुश्च धृतराष्ट्रस्य दृश्यते॥
en: I accept you, O mighty-armed hero, fight for my cause. It appears the thread of Dhritarashtra's line, as well as his funeral cake, will rest on you.

description: Honour of Bhishma and others by Yudhisthira
sn: भजस्वास्मान् राजपुत्र भजमानान् महाद्युते। न भविष्यति दुर्बुद्धिर्धार्तराष्ट्रोऽत्यमर्षणः॥
en: O prince, O effulgent one, accept us that accept you; the wrathful and foolish Duryodhana will not live.

description: Honour of Bhishma and others by Yudhisthira
sn: संजय उवाच ततो युयुत्सुः कौरव्यान् परित्यज्यसुतांस्तव। जगाम पाण्डुपुत्राणां सेनां विश्राव्य दुन्दुभिम्॥
en: Sanjaya said Then abandoning the Kurus, your son, Yuyutsu, went over to the army of the Pandavas with the best of drums and cymbals.

description: Honour of Bhishma and others by Yudhisthira
sn: ततो युधिष्ठिरो राजा सम्प्रहृष्टः सहानुजः। जग्राह कवचं भूयो दीप्तिमत् कनकोज्ज्वम्॥ प्रत्यपद्यन्त ते सर्वे स्वस्थान् पुरुषर्षभाः। ततो व्यूहं यथापूर्वं प्रत्यव्यूहन्त ते पुनः॥
en: Those foremost of men then all ascended their respective chariots. They placed their troops in battle-array,

description: Honour of Bhishma and others by Yudhisthira
sn: अवादयन् दुन्दुभीश्च शतशश्चैव पुष्करान्। सिंहनादांश्च विविधान् विनेदुः पुरुषर्षभाः॥
en: They ordered thousands of drums and cymbals to be played. Those foremost of men themselves also sent up lion-like roars.

description: Honour of Bhishma and others by Yudhisthira
sn: रथस्थान् पुरुषव्याघ्रान् पाण्डवान् प्रेक्ष्य पार्थिवाः। धृष्टद्युम्नादयः सर्वे पुनर्जहृषिरे तदा॥
en: ¡Seeing those foremost of men, the Pandavas, seated on their cars, the kings with Dhrishtadyumna and other once more sent up shouts of joy.

description: Honour of Bhishma and others by Yudhisthira
sn: गौरवं पाण्डुपुत्राणां मान्यान् मानयतां च तान्। दृष्ट्वा महीक्षितस्तत्र पूजयाञ्चक्रिरे भृशम्॥
en: Seeing the nobleness of the Pandavas, who had paid due honour to those that deserved it, all the kings highly praised them.

description: Honour of Bhishma and others by Yudhisthira
sn: सौहृदं च कृपां चैव प्राप्तकालं महात्मनाम्। दयां च ज्ञातिषु परां कथयाञ्चक्रिरे नृपाः॥
en: They talked amongst themselves about the friendship, compassion and kindness kinsmen displayed on every occasion by those high-minded men.

description: Honour of Bhishma and others by Yudhisthira
sn: साधु साध्विति सर्वत्र निश्चेरुः स्तुतिसंहिताः। वाचः पुण्याः कीर्तिमतां मनोहृदयहर्षणाः॥
en: "Excellent", Excellent" were the words shouted everywhere. Eulogistic hymns for those illustrious men were chanted by all. The minds and hearts of every one were attracted towards them.

description: Honour of Bhishma and others by Yudhisthira
sn: म्लेच्छाश्चार्याश्च ये तत्र ददृशुः शुश्रुवुस्तथा। वृत्तं तत् पाण्डुपुत्राणां रुरुदुस्ते सगद्गदाः॥
en: Both the Aryas and the Mlecchas that saw or heard of this conduct of the Pandavas all wept with their voice choked with tears.

description: Honour of Bhishma and others by Yudhisthira
sn: ततो जघ्नुर्महाभेरीः शतशश्च सहस्रशः। शङ्खाश्च गोक्षीरनिभान् दध्मुर्हष्टा मनस्विनः॥
en: to Those greatly powerful also ordered hundreds and hundreds of large drums and Pushkaras to be sounded and thousands and thousands of conchs all as white as the milk of the cows to be loudly blown.

parva: BHISHMAVADHA PARVA)-Continued Commencement of the battle (First day
sn: सेनया।॥ धृतराष्ट्र उवाच एवं व्यूढेष्वनीकेषु मामकेष्वितरेषु च। के पूर्वं प्राहरंस्तत्र कुरवः पाण्डवा नु किम्॥
en: Dhritarashtra said When the troops of my side and those of the foe were thus placed in battle-army, who struck first, the Kurus or the Pandavas?

parva: BHISHMAVADHA PARVA)-Continued Commencement of the battle (First day
sn: संजय उवाच भ्रातृभिः सहितो राजन् पुत्रो दुर्योधनस्तव। भीष्म प्रमुखतः कृत्वा प्रययौ सह
en: Sanjaya said Having heard the word of his brother, your son Dushasana advanced with his force with Bhishma at their head.

parva: BHISHMAVADHA PARVA)-Continued Commencement of the battle (First day
sn: तथैव पाण्डवाः सर्वे भीमसेनपुरोगमाः। भीष्मेण युद्धमिच्छन्तः प्रययुर्हष्टमानसाः॥
en: Desiring to fight with Bhishma, the Pandavas cheerfully advanced with Bhimasena at their head.

parva: BHISHMAVADHA PARVA)-Continued Commencement of the battle (First day
sn: क्ष्वेडा: किलकिलाशब्दाः क्रकचा गोविषाणिकाः। भेरीमृदङ्गमुरजा हयकुञ्जरनिःस्वनाः॥ उभयोः सेनयोगसंस्ततस्तेऽस्मान् समाद्रवन्। वयं तान् प्रतिनर्दन्तस्तदासीत् तुमुलं महत्॥
en: Thereupon lion-like roars, clamorous shouts, the noise of Krakachas, the blare of cow-horns and the sounds of drum, cymbals and taboos arose in both the armies. The soldiers of the enemy rushed upon us and we also rushed upon them with loud shouts.

parva: BHISHMAVADHA PARVA)-Continued Commencement of the battle (First day
sn: महान्त्यनीकानि महासमुच्छ्रये समागमे पाण्डवधार्तराष्ट्रयोः। चकम्पिरे शङ्खमृदङ्गनिःस्वनैः प्रकम्पितानीव वनानि वायुना॥
en: The vast arinies of the Kurus and the Pandavas shook in that fearful and body battle by the sounds of conchs and cymbals, as a forest is shaken by the wind.

parva: BHISHMAVADHA PARVA)-Continued Commencement of the battle (First day
sn: मभ्यागतानामशिवे मुहूर्ते। वभूव घोषस्तुमुलश्चमूनां बातोद्भुतानामिव सागराणाम्॥
en: The great nose, made by those troops consisting of kings, elephants and horses, rushing upon one another in an evil hour, was like that of the ocean in a tempest.

parva: BHISHMAVADHA PARVA)-Continued Commencement of the battle (First day
sn: तस्मिन् समुत्थिते शब्दे तुमुले लोमहर्षणे। भीमसेनो महाबाहुः प्राणदद् गोवृषो यथा॥
en: When that loud and hair-stirring noise rose, the mighty Bhimasena roared like a bull.

parva: BHISHMAVADHA PARVA)-Continued Commencement of the battle (First day
sn: शङ्खदुन्दुभिनिर्घोषं वारणानां च बृहितम्। सिंहनादं च सैन्यानां भीमसेनरवोऽभ्यभूत्॥
en: Bhimasena's roars rose above the sounds of conchs, and drums, the roaring of elephants and the lion-like shouts of the warriors.

parva: BHISHMAVADHA PARVA)-Continued Commencement of the battle (First day
sn: हयानां हेषमाणानामनीकेषु सहस्रशः। सर्वानभ्यभवच्छब्दान् भीमस्य नदतः स्वनः॥
en: The shouts of Bhimasena drowned the neighing of thousands of horses in both the armies.

parva: BHISHMAVADHA PARVA)-Continued Commencement of the battle (First day
sn: तं श्रुत्वा निनदं तस्य सैन्यास्तव वितत्रसुः। जीमूतस्येव नदतः शक्राशनिसमस्वनम्॥
en: Hearing those shouts of Bhimnasena whose roaring resembled that of the clouds and the report of the thunder, your soldiers were filled with fear.

parva: BHISHMAVADHA PARVA)-Continued Commencement of the battle (First day
sn: वाहनानि च सर्वाणि शकृन्मूत्रं प्रसुस्रुवुः। शब्देन तस्य वीरस्य सिंहस्येवेतरे मृगाः॥
en: Hearing those roars of that hero (Bhima), the horses and the elephants (of both the armies) ejected urine and excrete, as other animals do at the roars of the lion.

parva: BHISHMAVADHA PARVA)-Continued Commencement of the battle (First day
sn: दर्शयन् घोरमात्मानं महाभ्रमिव नादयन्। विभीषयंस्तव सुतान् भीमसेनः समभ्ययात्॥
en: Roaring like a deep mass of clouds and assuming a fearful appearance, that hero filled your sons with great alarm and then rushed upon them. Sons

parva: BHISHMAVADHA PARVA)-Continued Commencement of the battle (First day
sn: तमायान्तं महेष्वासं सोदर्याः पर्यवारयन्। छादयन्तः शरवातैर्मेघा इव दिवाकरम्॥ दुर्योधनश्च पुत्रस्ते दुर्मुखो दुःशलः शलः। दुःशासनश्चातिरथस्तथा दुर्मर्षणो नृप॥ विविंशतिश्चित्रसेनो विकर्णश्च महारथः। पुरुमित्रो जयो भोजः सौमदत्तिश्च वीर्यवान्।॥ महाचापानि धुन्वन्तो मेघा इव सविद्युतः। आददानाश्च नाराचान् निर्मुक्ताशीविषोपमान्॥
en: Then all the brothers, your Duryodhana, Durmukha, Dushala, that great car-warrior Dushasana, Durmarshana, Vivingshati, Chitrasena, the great car-warrior Vikarna and also Purumitra, Jaya, Bhoja, the brave son of Somadatta, all these heroes, shaking their bows which looked like so many masses of clouds charged with flashes of lightning, and taking out long arrows loO king like so many snakes that have cast off their sloughs, surrounded that great bowman (Bhima) and covered him with a shower of arrows, as clouds cover the sun.

parva: BHISHMAVADHA PARVA)-Continued Commencement of the battle (First day
sn: अथ ते द्रौपदीपुत्राः सौभद्रश्च महारथः। नकुलः सहदेवश्च धृष्टद्युम्नश्च पार्षतः॥ धार्तराष्ट्रान् प्रतिययुरर्दयन्तः शितैः शरैः। वज़ैरिव महावेगैः शिखराणि धराभृताम्॥
en: The sons of Draupadi, the great car-warrior (Abhimanyu) son of Subhadra, Nakula and Sahadeva, Dhrishtadyumna, the of Prishata, all rushed against the warriors of Dhritarashtra's son and tore them asunder with sharp arrows as the summits of mountains are broken down by the thunder-bolt.

parva: BHISHMAVADHA PARVA)-Continued Commencement of the battle (First day
sn: तस्मिन् प्रथमसंग्रामे भीमज्यातलनिःस्वने। तावकानां परेषां च नासीत् कश्चित् पराङ्मुखः॥
en: son In the first encounter that resounded with the terrible twang of the bow and flapping of the leather fences, none of your party or of that of the enemy turned them back.

parva: BHISHMAVADHA PARVA)-Continued Commencement of the battle (First day
sn: लाघवं द्रोणशिष्याणामपश्यं भरतर्षभ। निमित्तवेधिनां चैव शरानुत्सृजतां भृशम्॥
en: 0 best of the Bharata race, O king, I saw the lightness of hands of the disciples of Drona who shot countless arrows and always succeeded in hitting the marks.

parva: BHISHMAVADHA PARVA)-Continued Commencement of the battle (First day
sn: नोपशाम्यति निर्घोषो धनुषां कूजतां तथा। विनिश्चेरुः शरा दीप्ता ज्योतीषीव नभस्तलात्॥
en: The twang of the bows did not stop for a movement and the blazing arrows flashed through the air like meteor falling from the sky.

parva: BHISHMAVADHA PARVA)-Continued Commencement of the battle (First day
sn: सर्वे त्वन्ये महीपालाः प्रेक्षका इव भारत। ददृशुर्दर्शनीयं तं भीमं ज्ञातिसमागमम्॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, all the kings stood like spectators and saw the interesting and awful battle between kinsmen.

parva: BHISHMAVADHA PARVA)-Continued Commencement of the battle (First day
sn: ततस्ते जातसंरम्भाः परस्परकृतागसः। अन्योन्यस्पर्धया राजन् व्यायच्छन्त महारथाः॥
en: O king, then those great car-warriors remembering the great injuries they had suffered, challenged one another in anger and tried their utmost (to win victory).

parva: BHISHMAVADHA PARVA)-Continued Commencement of the battle (First day
sn: कुरुपाण्डवसेने ते हस्त्यश्वरथसंकुले। शुशुभाते रणेऽतीव पटे चित्रार्पिते इव॥
en: The two armies of the Kurus and the Pandavas, full of elephants, horses and cars, looked exceedingly beautiful on the field of battle, like painted figures on canvas. Then all the kings took up their bows. The sun was covered by the dust raised by the combatants.

parva: BHISHMAVADHA PARVA)-Continued Commencement of the battle (First day
sn: ततस्ते पार्थिवाः सर्वे प्रगृहीतशरासनाः। सहसैन्याः समापेतुः पुत्रस्य तव शासनात्॥ युधिष्ठिरेण चादिष्टाः पार्थिवास्ते सहस्रशः। विनदन्तः समापेतुः पुत्रस्य तव वाहिनीम्॥ उभयोः सेनयोस्तीव्रः सैन्यानां स समागमः। अन्तर्धीयत चादित्यः सैन्येन रजसाऽऽवृतः॥
en: Under the command of your son, they rushed upon the enemy at the head of their respective troops. Fearful was the uproar made by the elephants and horses of the kings rushing to the charge, mingled with the lionlike shouts of the warriors and the din made by the sounds of conchs and drums. The uproar of that ocean (the battle field), which had arrows for its crocodiles, bows for its snakes, swords for its tortoises and the toward leaps of the warriors for its tempest, looked like a real ocean agitated by a tempest. Thousands of kings commanded by Yudhishthira attacked the ranks of your son with their respective troops.

parva: BHISHMAVADHA PARVA)-Continued Commencement of the battle (First day
sn: प्रयुद्धानां प्रभग्नानां पुनरावर्तिनामपि। नात्र स्वेषां परेषां वा विशेषः समदृश्यत॥ तस्मिंस्तु तुमुले युद्धे वर्तमाने महाभये। अतिसर्वाण्यनीकानि पिता तेऽभिव्यरोचत।॥
en: While fighting, or retreating, or rallying again, neither the men of our side nor those of the enemy's could be distinguished. But your father (Bhishma) shone transcending all that countless host in that fearful and terrible battle.

sn: संजय उवाच पूर्वाह्ने तस्य रौद्रस्य युद्धमह्नो विशाम्पते। प्रावर्तत महाघोरं राज्ञां देहावकर्तनम्॥
en: Sanjaya said O king, in the morning of that awful day commenced the fearful battle that mangled the bodies of so many kings.

sn: कुरूणां सृञ्जयानां च जिगीषूणां परस्परम्। सिंहानामिव संह्रादो दिवमुर्वी च नादयन्॥
en: Desiring victory in battle, the loud shouts that the Kurus and the Srinjayas made, resembling those of so many lions, caused the earth and the sky to be resounded.

sn: आसीत् किलकिलाशब्दस्तलशङ्खरवैः सह। जज्ञिरे सिंहनादाश्च शूराणां प्रतिगर्जताम्॥
en: A tremendous uproar was heard mingled with the flapping of the leather and the blare of conchs. Lion-like roars rose from men shouting at one another.

sn: तलवाभिहताश्चैव ज्याशब्दा भरतर्षभ। पत्तीनां पादशब्दश्च वाजिनां च महास्वनः॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, the twang of the bow-strings, the heavy feared of infantry, the furious neighing of horses.

sn: तोत्राङ्कुशनिपातश्च आयुधानां च नि:स्वनः। घण्टाशब्दश्च नागानामन्योन्यमभिधावताम्॥
en: The falling of sticks and iron hooks the clash of weapons, the jingle of bells round the necks of elephants rushing upon one another.

sn: तस्मिन् समुदिते शब्दे तुमुले लोमहर्षणे। बभूव रथनिर्घोषः पर्जन्यनिनदोपमः॥
en: The clatter of the wheels of cars that resembled the roars of clouds, all these mingled together, produced a hair-stirring uproar.

sn: ते मनः क्रूरमाधाय समभित्यक्तजीविताः। पाण्डवानभ्यवर्तन्त सर्व एवोच्छ्रितध्वजाः॥
en: All the Kuru warriors, reckless of their lives, with cruel intentions, rushed upon the Pandavas with their standards upraised.

sn: अथ शान्तनवो राजन्नभ्यधावद् धनंजयम्। प्रगृह्य कार्मुकं घोरं कालदण्डोपमं रणे॥
en: O king, taking up a fearful bow that resembled the rod of death himself, the son of Shantanu, Bhishma, rushed upon Dhananjaya (Arjuna) on the field of battle.

sn: अर्जुनोऽपि धनुर्गृह्य गाण्डीवं लोकविश्रुतम्। अभ्यधावत तेजस्वी गाङ्गेयं रणमूर्धनि॥
en: The greatly powerful Arjuna also a king up the bow Gandiva which is celebrated all over the world, rushed upon the son of Ganga (Bhishma) on the field of battle.

sn: तावुभौ कुरुशार्दूलौ परस्परवधैषिणौ। गाङ्गेयस्तु रणे पार्थं विद्ध्वा नाकम्पयत् बली।।१०
en: Both those two foremost heroes of the Kuru race desired to kill each other. Though the mighty son of Ganga pierced Partha with his arrows, yet he could not make him waver.

sn: तथैव पाण्डवो राजन् भीष्मं नाकम्पयद् युधि। सात्यकिस्तु महेष्वासः कृतवर्माणमभ्ययात्॥
en: O king, that son of Pandu (Arjuna) also could not make Bhishma waver in battle. The great bowman Satyaki rushed against Kritavarma.

sn: तयोः समभवद् युद्धं तुमुलं लोमहर्षणम्। सात्यकिः कृतवर्माणं कृतवर्मा च सात्यकिम्॥ आनछुतुः शरैरैस्तक्षमाणौ परस्परम्। तौ शराचितसर्वाङ्गौ शुशुभाते महाबलौ॥ वसन्ते पुष्पशबलौ पुष्पिताविव किंशुकौ। अभिमन्युर्महेष्वासं बृहद्बलमयोधयत्॥
en: The fight between these two(heroes) was extremely fearful and hair-string. Satyaki wounded Kritavarma and Kritavarma wounded Satyaki with loud shouts and thus they weakened each other. Pierced all over the body with arrows, those two great warriors shone like two blossoming Kinshukas, when they are adorned with flowers in spring. The great bowman Abhimanyu fought with Brihadbala.

sn: ततः कोसलराजाऽसावभिमन्योर्विशाम्पते। ध्वजं चिच्छेद समरे सारथिं च न्यपातयत्॥
en: O king, the ruler of Kosala, soon in that battle, cut off the standard and overthrew the charioteer of the son of Subhadra, (Abhimanyu).

sn: सौभद्रस्तु ततः क्रुद्धः पातिते रथसारथौ। बृहद्वलं महाराज विव्याध नवभिः शरैः॥
en: When his charioteer was overthrown, Subhadra's son was filled with wrath. O king, be pierced Brihadbala with nine arrows.

sn: अथापराव्यां भल्लाभ्यां शिताभ्यामरिमर्दनः। ध्वजमेकेन चिच्छेद पार्णिमेकेन सारथिम्॥
en: That chastiser of foes, (Abhimanyu) with a couple of sharp arrows cut off his standard, with one (arrow) he cut down one of the protectors of his car-wheels and with another his charioteer.

sn: अन्योन्यं च शरैः क्रुद्धौ ततक्षाते परस्परम्। मानिनं समरे दृप्तं कृतवैरं महारथम्॥ भीमसेनस्तव सुतं दुर्योधनमयोधयत्। तावुभौ नरशार्दूलौ कुरुमुख्यौ महाबलौ॥
en: Those (two) chastisers of foes fought on and weakened each other with sharp arrows. Bhimasena fought with your son Duryodhana, that great car-warrior who had injured (the Pandavas) in pride. Both of those Kuru chiefs are foremost of men and both of them are great car-warriors.

sn: अन्योन्यं शरवर्षाभ्यां ववृषाते रणाजिरे। तौ वीक्ष्य तु महात्मानौ कृतिनौ चित्रयोधिनौ॥ विस्मयः सर्वभूतानां समपद्यत भारत। दुःशासनस्तु नकुलं प्रत्युद्याय महाबलम्॥ अविध्यन्निशितैर्बाणैहुभिर्मर्मदिभिः। तस्य माद्रीसुतः केतुं सशरं च शरासनम्॥ चिच्छेद निशितैर्बाणैः प्रहसन्निव भारत। अथैनं पञ्चविंशत्या क्षुद्रकाणां समार्पयत्॥
en: They covered each other, on the field of battle, with showers of arrows. O descendant of Bharata, seeing the fight between these two illustrious and accomplished warrior learned in all the modes of warfare all creatures were filled with amazement. Dushasana rushed against the great car warrior Nakula and pierced him with many sharp arrows. The son of Madri laughingly cut off with his sharp arrows the standard and the bow of his adversary. He then wounded him with twenty five small headed arrows.

sn: पुत्रस्तु तव दुर्धर्षो नकुलस्य महाहवे। तुरङ्गांश्चिच्छिदे बाणैर्ध्वजं चैवाभ्यपातयत्॥
en: Your son who is ever difficult to be vanquished then killed in that fearful battle Nakula's horses and then cut down his standard.

sn: दुर्मुखः सहदेवं च प्रत्युद्याय महाबलम्। विव्याध शरवर्षेण यतमानं महाहवे॥
en: Durmukha rushed upon the mighty Sahadeva. He fought with him in that terrible battle and pierced him with a shower of arrows.

sn: सहदेवस्ततो वीरो दुर्मुखस्य महारणे। शरेण भृशतीक्ष्णेन पातयामास सारथिम्॥
en: The heroic Sahadeva soon overthrew in that fearful battle Durmukha's charioteer with a sharp arrow.

sn: तावन्योन्यं समासाद्य समरे युद्धदुर्मदौ। त्रासयेतां शरैोरैः कृतप्रतिकृतैषिणौ।॥
en: Both of them were irresistible in fight. Each attacking the other, and being desirous of warding of each other's attack struck terror into each other with fearful arrows.

sn: युधिष्ठिरः स्वयं राजा मद्रराजानमभ्ययात्। तस्य मद्राधिपश्चापं द्विधा चिच्छेद मारिष॥
en: The king Yudhishthira himself fought with the ruler of the Madra. The Madra king cut off the bow of Yudhishthira.

sn: तदपास्य धनुश्च्छिन्नं कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः। अन्यत् कार्मुकमादाय वेगवद् बलवत्तरम्॥
en: Thereupon, the son of Kunti, took up another bow which was stronger and capable of imparting greater velocity.

sn: ततो मद्रेश्वरं राजा शरैः संनतपर्वभिः। छादयामास संक्रुद्धस्तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति चाब्रवीत्॥
en: The king, then saying in great wrath “Wait" covered the king of Madra with straight arrows.

sn: धृष्टद्युम्नस्ततो द्रोणमभ्यद्रवत भारत। तस्य द्रोणः सुसंक्रुद्धः परासुकरणं दृढम्॥ त्रिधा चिच्छेद समरे पाञ्चाल्यस्य तु कार्मुकम्। शरं चैव महाघोरं कालदण्डमिवापरम्॥ प्रेषयामास समरे सोऽस्य काये न्यमज्जत। अथान्यद् धनुरादाय सायकांश्च चतुर्दश॥ द्रोण द्रुपदपुत्रस्तु प्रतिविव्याध संयुगे। तावन्योन्यं सुसंक्रुद्धौ चक्रतुः सुभृशं रणम्॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, Dhrishtadyumna rushed against Drona. In great anger Drona cut off in that battle the hard bow of the illustrious Panchala prince, the bow which was ever capable of taking the lives of the foes. He shot in that battle a fearful arrow which was like the second rod of Yama. The arrow thus shot son penetrated into the body of the prince. Taking up another bow and fourteen arrows, the son of Drupada pierced Drona with his arrows. Enraged with each other they fought on.

sn: सौमदत्तिं रणे शङ्खो रभसं रभसो युधि। प्रत्युद्ययौ महाराज तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति चाब्रवीत्॥
en: O king, the impetuous Shankha met Somadatta son who was equally impetuous in battle and he shouted out to him "Wait" “Wait".

sn: तस्य वै दक्षिणं वीरो निर्बिभेद रणे भुजम्। सौमदत्तिस्तथा शङ्ख जत्रुदेशे समाहनत्॥
en: That hero then pierced his right arm in that fight. Thereupon the of Somadatta wounded Shankha on the shoulders.

sn: तयोस्तदभवद् युद्धं घोररूपं विशाम्पते। दृप्तयोः समरे पूर्वं वृत्रवासवयोरिव।॥
en: O king, the battle that was fought between these two proud heroes soon became as fearful as the battle between the celestial and the Asuras.

sn: बाह्रीकं तु रणे क्रुद्धं क्रुद्धरूपो विशाम्पते। अभ्यद्रवदमेयात्मा धृष्टकेतुर्महारथः॥
en: O king, that high-souled great car-warrior Dhrishtaketu angrily rushed upon Balhika who was the very embodiment of anger.

sn: बाह्रीकस्तु रणे राजन् धृष्टकेतुममर्षणः। शरैर्बहुभिरानछेत् सिहनादमथानदत्॥
en: O king, great Balhika, sending up a lionlike roar, weakened the wrathful Dhrishtaketu with countless arrows.

sn: चेदिराजस्तु संक्रुद्धो बाह्रीकं नवभिः शरैः। विव्याध समरे तूर्णं मत्तो मत्तमिव द्विपम्॥ तौ तत्र समरे क्रुद्धौ नर्दन्तौ च पुनः पुनः। समीयतुः सुसंक्रुद्धावङ्गारकबुधाविव॥ राक्षसं रौद्रकर्माणं क्रूरकर्मा घटोत्कचः। अलम्बुषं प्रत्युदियाद् बलं शक्र इवाहवे॥
en: The king of the Chedis, then becoming exceedingly, angry, quickly pierced Balhika with nine arrows in that battle. Like an infuriated elephants, attacking another infuriated elephants, they roared against each other in great anger. They fought in great wrath and they looked like the planets Angaraka and Budha. Ghatotkacha the barbarous monster attacked on the monster known as Alambusha, the evildoer. This attack was made same way as Indra invaded on Bala, a dangerous demon.

sn: घटोत्कचस्ततः क्रुद्धो राक्षसं तं महाबलम्। नवत्या सायकैस्तीक्ष्णैर्दारयामास भारत॥
en: The doer of cruel deeds, Ghototkacha, O descendant of Bharata, wounded that mighty and angry Rakshasa (Alambusha with ninety sharp arrows.

sn: अलम्बुषस्तु समरे भैमसेनि महाबलम्। बहुधा दारयामास शरैः संनतपर्वभिः॥
en: Alambusha, in that great battle, wounded the mighty son of Bhimasena (Ghototkacha) in many places with straight arrows.

sn: व्यभ्राजेतां ततस्तौ तु संयुगे शरविक्षतौ। यथा देवासुरे युद्धे बलशक्रौ महाबलौ॥
en: Wounded with arrows they appeared in the battle like the mighty Indra and the powerful Bala in the battle between the celestial and the Danavas.

sn: शिखण्डी समरे राजन् द्रौणिमभ्युद्ययौ बली। अश्वत्थामा ततः क्रुद्धः शिखण्डिनमुपस्थितम्॥
en: O king, the mighty Shikhandin attacked Drona's son. But Ashvatthama severely wounded Shikhandin with a sharp arrows and thus made him tremble.

sn: नाराचेन सुतीक्ष्णेन भृशं विद्ध्वा ह्यकम्पयत्। शिखण्ड्यपि ततो राजन् द्रोणपुत्रमताडयत्॥
en: O king, Shikhandin also wounded the son of Drona (Ashvatthama) with a sharp and excellent weapon.

sn: सायकेन सुपीतेन तीक्ष्णेन निशितेन च। तौ जनतुस्तदाऽन्योन्यं शरैर्बहुविधैर्मधे॥४८॥ भगदत्तं रणे शूरं विराटो वाहिनीपतिः। अभ्ययात् त्वरितो राजंस्ततो युद्धमवर्तत॥ विराटो भगदत्तं तु शरवर्षेण भारत। अभ्यवर्षत् सुसंक्रुद्धो मेघो वृष्ट्या इवाचलम्॥ भगदत्तस्ततस्तूर्णं विराटं पृथिवीपतिम्। छादयामास समरे मेघः सूर्यमिवोदितम्॥
en: They brought on striking cach other with various kinds of arrows. O king, Virata, that commander of an army, against the heroic Bhagadatta in battle. Becoming exceedingly angry, Virata shot at Bhagadatta a shower of arrows, as the clouds shower of arrows, as the clouds shower rain on a mountain. But that ruler of earth, Bhagadatta, soon covered Virata with arrows as clouds cover the sun.

sn: बृहत्क्षत्रं तु कैकेयं कृपः शारद्वतो ययौ। तं कृपः शरवर्षेण च्छादयामास भारत॥
en: The son of Sharadvata, Kripa, attacked the ruler of the Kaikeyas named Brihatkshatra. O descendant of Bharata, Kripa covered him with a shower of arrows.

sn: गौतमं कैकयः क्रुद्धः शरवृष्ययाऽभ्यपूरयत्। तावन्योन्यं हयान् हत्वा धनुश्छित्त्वा च भारत॥ विरथावसियुद्धाय समीयतुरमर्षणौ।
en: Brihatkshatra also cover the angry son of Gautama with a shower of arrows. Having killed each other's steeds and cut off each other's bows, those (two) warriors were both deprived of their cars. Becoming exceedingly angry, they attacked each other with swords.

sn: तयोस्तदभवद् युद्धं घोररूपं सुदारुणम्॥ द्रुपदस्तु अभ्युद्ययौ हृष्टरूपो हृष्टरूपं परंतपः॥ ततः सैन्धवको राजा दुपदं विशिखैस्त्रिभिः। ताडयामास समरे स च तं प्रत्यविध्यत॥
en: The battle they then fought was fearful and unparalleled. That chastiser of foes, king Drupada, angrily rushed on the ruler of Sindhu, Jayadratha. The Sindhu king wounded Drupada in that battle with three arrows, and Drupada too wounded him in return.

sn: तयोस्तदभवद् युद्धं घोररूपं सुदारुणम्। ईक्षणप्रीतिजननं शुक्राङ्गारकयोरिव॥ विकर्णस्तु सुतस्तुभ्यं सुतसोमं महाबलम्। अभ्ययाज्जवनैरश्वैस्ततो युद्धमवर्तत॥ ततो राजन् राजन् सैन्धवं वै सैन्धवं वै जयद्रथम्। विकर्णः सुतसोमं तु विद्ध्वा नाकम्पयच्छरैः।
en: The battle they fought was fearful and terrible. It gave satisfaction to the hearts of all spectators it was like the conflict between the planets Shukra and Angaraka your son Vikarna with fleet steeds attacked the greatly powerful Sutasoma and they began to fight. Though Vikarna wounded Sutasoma with many arrows, yet he failed to make him waver.

sn: सुतसोमो विकर्णं च तदद्भुतविवाभवत्॥ सुशर्माणं नरव्याघ्रश्चेकितानो महारथः। अभ्यद्रवत् सुसंक्रुद्धः पाण्डवार्थे पराक्रमीः॥ सुशर्मा तु महाराज चेकितानं महारथम्। महता शरवर्षेण वारयामास संयुगे॥ चेकितानोऽपि संरब्धः सुशर्माणं महाहवे। प्राच्छादयत् तमिषुभिर्महामेघ इवाचलम्॥
en: Sutasoma also could not make Vikarna waver. It was a wonderful sight. That great carwarrior, that foremost of men, that greatly powerful Chekitan rushed upon Susharma for the sake of the Pandavas. O king of kings, Susharma however cheated the advance of that great car-warrior Chekitana with heavy shower of Chekitana also becoming exceedingly angry showered on Susharma a shower of arrows as a mass of clouds shower rain on a mountain.

sn: शकुनिः प्रतिविन्ध्यं तु पराक्रान्तं पराक्रमी। अभ्यद्रवत राजेन्द्र मत्तः सिंह इव द्विपम्॥
en: 0 king the greatly powerful Shakuni attacked 'the might Prativindhya as a lion attacks an infuriated elephant.

sn: यौधिष्ठिरस्तु संक्रुद्धः सौबलं निशितैः शरैः। व्यदारयत संसंग्रामे मघवानिव दानवम्॥
en: The son of Yudhishthira in great anger wounded Subala's son with many sharp arrows as Maghavat (Indra) mangles a Danava.

sn: शकुनिः प्रतिविन्ध्यं तु प्रतिविध्यन्तमाहवे। व्यदारयन्महाप्राज्ञः शरैः संनतपर्वभिः॥
en: In that terrible, battle, Shakuni also wounded Prativindhya and mangled the body arrows. of that greatly intelligent warrior with sharp arrows.

sn: सुदक्षिणं तु राजेन्द्र काम्बोजानां महारथम्। श्रुतकर्मा पराक्रान्तमभ्यद्रवत संयुगे॥
en: O great king, Shrutakarma attacked in that battle the great car warrior, the mighty Sudakshina, the king of the Kambojas.

sn: सुदक्षिणस्तु समरे साहदेविं महारथम्। विद्ध्वा नाकम्पयत वै मैनाकमिव पर्वतम्॥
en: O king of kings, Sudakshina wounded that great car-warrior the son of Sahadeva, but he could not make him waver; he stood as the Mainaka mountain.

sn: श्रुतकर्मा ततः क्रुद्धः काम्बोजानां महारथम्। शरैर्बहुभिरानछेद् दारयन्निव सर्वशः॥
en: Thereupon Shrutakarma in great anger weakened that great car warrior of the Kambojas with countless arrows and mangled him in many parts of his body.

sn: इरावानथ संक्रुद्धः श्रुतायुषमरिंदमम्। प्रत्युद्ययौ रणे यत्तो यत्तरूपं परंतपः॥
en: That chastiser of foes, Iravan rushed in great anger on the wrathful Shrutayush in that great battle.

sn: आर्जुनिस्तस्य समरे हयान् हत्वा महारथः। ननाद बलवन्नादं तत् सैन्यं प्रत्यपूरयत्॥
en: The mighty son of Arjuna that great carwarrior, then killing the horses of his adversary, sent up a loud roar. O king, all the kings praised him (by his this great fear).

sn: श्रुतायुस्तु ततः क्रुद्धः फाल्गुनेः समरे हयान्। निजघान गदाग्रेण ततो युद्धमवर्तत॥
en: Shruthayusha, in the battle the horses of the son of Arjuna with a great mace and then they fought on.

sn: विन्दानुविन्दावावन्त्यौ कुन्तिभोजं महारथम्। ससेनं ससुतं वीरं संससज्जतुराहवे॥
en: The two princes of Avanti, Vinda and Anuvinda attacked in that battle the great carwarrior the brave Kuntibhoja who was with his son at the head of his troops.

sn: तत्राद्भुतमपश्याम तयो?रं पराक्रमम्। अयुध्येतां स्थिरौ भूत्वा महत्या सेनया सह॥
en: We saw wonderful prowess in those two princes for they fought with great coolness, though they had to fight with a very large number of troops.

sn: अनुविन्दस्तु गदया कुन्तिभोजमताडयत्। कुन्तिभोजश्च तं तूर्णं शरवातैरवाकिरत्॥
en: Anuvinda hurled a mace of Kuntibhoja but he (Kuntibhoja) soon covered him with a shower of arrows.

sn: कुन्तिभोजसुतश्चापि विन्दं विव्याध सायकैः। स च तं प्रतिविव्याध तदद्भुतमिवाभवत्॥
en: The son of Kuntibhoja wounded Vinda with many arrows but he too wounded him in return. The battle they fought was wonderful.

sn: केकया भ्रातरः पञ्च गान्धारान् पञ्च मारिष। ससैन्यास्ते ससैन्यांश्च योधयामासुराहवे॥
en: O respected one, the Kaikeya brothers at the head of their troops attacked in that battle the five Gandharva princes with their troops.

sn: वीरबाहुश्च ते पुत्रो वैराटि रथसत्तमम्। उत्तरं योधयामास विव्याध निशितैः शरैः॥
en: Your son Virabahu fought with that foremost of car-warriors, Uttara, the son of Virata and wounded him with nine arrows.

sn: उत्तस्थापि तं वीरं विव्याध निशितैः शरैः। चेदिराट् समरे राजन्नुलूकं समभिद्रवत्॥
en: Uttara also wounded him with many sharp arrows; O king, the ruler of Chedi attacked in that battle Uluka.

sn: तथैव शरवर्षेण उलूकं समविद्ध्यता उलूकश्चापि तं बाणैर्निशितैर्लोमवाहिभिः॥
en: He wounded Uluka with a shower of arrows and Uluka too wounded him with sharp arrows with excellent wings.

sn: तयोर्युद्धं समभवद् घोररूपं विशाम्पते। दारयेतां सुसंक्रुद्धावन्योन्यमपराजितौ॥
en: O king, the battle they fought was fearful in the extreme, for, being unable to defeat each other, they fearfully mangled each other body.

sn: एवं द्वन्द्वसहस्राणि रथवारणवाजिनाम्। पदातीनं च समरे तव तेषां च संकुले॥
en: Thus in that great battle thousands of single combats were fought between car-warriors, elephants men, horse-men sand foot-soldiers of both the sides.

sn: मुहूर्तमिव तद् युद्धमासीन्मधुरदर्शनम्। तत उन्मत्तवद् राजन् न प्राज्ञायत किंचन॥
en: For a short time the battle looked beautiful, but O king, it soon grew furious and nothing could be seen.

sn: गजो गजेन समरे रथिनं च रथी ययौ। अश्वोऽश्वं समभिप्रायात् पदातिश्च पदातिनम्॥
en: In that battle elephants rushed against elephants, car-warriors against car-warriors, horseman against horseman and foot-soldiers against foot-soldiers.

sn: ततो युद्धं सुदुर्धर्षं व्याकुलं समपद्यत। शूराणां समरे तत्र समासाद्येतरेतरम्॥
en: Thus battle then became confused and fearful in the extreme. The heroes rushed against one another in a great number.

sn: तत्र देवर्षयः सिद्धाश्चारणाश्च समागताः। प्रेक्षन्त तद् रणं घोरं देवासुरसमं भुवि॥
en: The celestial Rishis, the Siddhas and Charanas who were present, saw that battle as if it were the battle between the gods and the demons.

sn: ततो दन्तिसहस्राणि रथानां चापि मारिष। अश्वौघाः पुरुषौघाश्च विपरीतं समाययु॥
en: Thousands of elephants and cars, countless horsemen and foot-soldiers, appeared to have altered their character.

sn: तत्र तत्र प्रदृश्यन्ते रथवारणपत्तयः। सादिनश्च नरव्याघ्र युध्यमाना मुहुर्मुहुः॥
en: O foremost of men, it was seen that carwarriors, elephants, horsemen and foot. soldiers, all fought with one another, again and again , on the same place.

sn: संजय उवाच राजन् शतसहस्राणि तत्र तत्र पदातिनाम्। निर्मर्यादं प्रयुद्धानि तत् ते वक्ष्यामि भारत॥
en: Sanjaya said O king, O descendant of Bharata, I shall now describe to you the fight of hundreds and thousands of foot-soldiers, who were in utter forgetfulness of all considerations for others.

sn: न पुत्रः पितरं जज्ञे पिता वा पुत्रमौरसम्। न भ्राता भ्रातरं तत्र स्वस्रीयं न च मातुलः॥
en: The son did not recognise the father and the father the son. The brother did not recognise his own brother and the sister's son did not recognise his maternal uncle.

sn: न मातुलं च स्वस्रीयो न सखायं सखा तथा। आविष्टा इव युद्धयन्ते पाण्डवाः कुरुभिः सह॥
en: The maternal uncle did not recognise his sister's son, and the friend did not recognise the friend. the Pandava and the Kuru forces fought as if they had been possessed by demons.

sn: स्थानीकं नरव्याघ्राः केचिदभ्यपतन रथैः। अभज्यन्त युगैरेव युगानि भरतर्षभ॥
en: O foremost of men, some warriors attacked with their cars the cars of the enemies, and crushed the yokes of those cars to pieces.

sn: रथेषाश्च रथेषाभिः कूबरा रथकूबरैः। संगतैः सहिताः केचित् परस्परजिघांसवः॥
en: The shafts of cars broke dashing against shafts of other cars, the spikes of car-yokes broke against spikes of car-yokes. Some untidily attacked others that were united but all were eager to take one another's life.

sn: न शेकुश्चलितुं केचित् संनिपत्य स्था रथैः। प्रभिन्नास्तु महाकायः संनिपत्य गजा गजैः॥ बहुधादारयन् क्रुद्धा विषाणैरितरेतरम्। सतोरणपताकैश वारणा वरवारणैः॥ अभिसृत्य महाराज वेगवद्भिर्महागजैः। दन्तैरभिहतास्तत्र चुक्रुशुः परमातुराः॥
en: Some cars were obstructed by other cars and they were unable to move. Huge elephants with rent temples fell upon other huge elephants. They angrily tore one another's body with their tusks. O king, others, again, attacking other impetuous and huge ones with huge standards on their backs, being wounded by tusks, roared in great agony.

sn: अभिनीताश्च शिक्षाभिस्तोत्रांकुशसमाहताः। अप्रभिन्नाः प्रभिन्नानां सम्मुखाभिमुखा ययुः॥
en: Disciplined by training and urged on by pikes and hooks, elephants not in rut attacked those that were in rut.

sn: प्रभिन्नैरपि संसक्ताः केचित् तत्र महागजाः। क्रौञ्चवन्निनदं कृत्वा दुर्दुवुः सर्वतो दिशम्॥
en: Huge elephants, attacked by those that were in rut, ran away in all directions, uttering cries like those of cranes.

sn: सम्यक् प्रणीता नागाश्च प्रभिन्नकरटामुखाः। ऋष्टितोमरनाराचैर्निर्विद्धा वरवारणाः॥ प्रणेदुर्भिन्नमर्माणो निपेतुश्च गतासवः। प्राद्रवन्त दिशः केचिन्नदन्तो भैरवान् रवान्।॥
en: Many huge elephants, well trained and with juice trickling down from their rent temples and moth, having been wounded by swords, lances and arrows, shrieked aloud. Pierced in their vital parts they fell down and expired. Uttering fearful cries, some ran away in all directions.

sn: गजानां पादरक्षास्तु व्यूढोरस्काः प्रहारिणः। ऋष्टिभिश्च धनुर्भिश्च विमलैश्च परश्वधैः॥ गदाभिर्मुसलैश्चैव भिन्दिपालैः सतोमरैः। आयसैः परिपैश्चैव निस्त्रिंशैविमलैः शितैः॥ प्रगृहीतैः सुसंरब्धा द्रवमाणास्ततस्ततः। व्यदृश्यन्त महाराज परस्परजिघांसवः॥
en: O king, the foot-soldiers, that protected the elephants, that possessed broad chests, that were capable of effectually striking the foe, armed with pikes, bows, bright battle-axes, maces, clubs, arrows, lances, shafts and heavy iron-mounted bludgeons and swords of the brightest polish, ran in every direction with the firm resolve of taking one another's life.

sn: राजमानाश्च निस्त्रिंशाः संसिक्ता नरशोणितैः। प्रत्यदृश्यन्त शूराणामन्योन्मभिधावताम्॥
en: The swords of brave combatants who rushed against one another having been steeped in blood shone with great brilliancy.

sn: अवक्षिप्तावधूतानामसीनां वीरबाहुभिः। संजज्ञे तुमुलः शब्दः पततां परमर्मसु॥
en: The whiling noise of the swords made by their whirling and falling by heroic arms became very loud.

sn: गदामुसलरुग्णानां भिन्नानां च वरासिभिः। दन्तिदन्तावभिन्नानां मृदितानां च दन्तिभिः॥ तत्र तत्र नरौघाणां क्रोशतामितरेतरम्। शुश्रुवुर्दारुणा वाचः प्रेतानामिव भारत॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, crushed with maces and clubs, cut off with tempered swords pierced and grinned by the tusks of elephants, the combatants sent forth heart-rending wails as those of men doomed to hell.

sn: हयैरपि हयारोहाश्चामरापीडधारिभिः। हंसैरिव महावेगैरन्योन्यमभिविद्रुताः॥
en: Horsemen on fleet horses with tails like the plumes of swans, rushed upon me another.

sn: तैविमुक्ता महाप्रासा जाम्बूनदविभूषणाः। आशुगा विमलास्तीक्ष्णाः सम्पेतुर्भुजगोपमाः॥
en: Hurled by them, long fleet and polished and sharp-pointed darts, decked with gold, fell (on all sides) like so many snakes.

sn: अश्वैरच्यजवैः केचिदाप्लुत्य महतो स्थान्। शिरांस्याददिरे वीरा रथिनामश्वसादिनः॥
en: Some heroic horsemen on fleet steeds leaped up and cut off the heads of car-warriors who were seated on their cars.

sn: बहूनपि हयारोहान् भल्लैः संनतपर्वभिः। रथी जघान सम्प्राप्य बाणगोचरमागतान्॥
en: A car-warrior, getting a body cavalry within shooting distance, killed many with straight arrows furnished with broad heads.

sn: नवमेघप्रतीकाशाश्चाक्षिप्य तुरगान् गजाः। पादैरेव विमृद्नन्ति मत्ताः कनकभूषणाः॥
en: Many infuriated elephants adorned with gold trappings and loO king like newly-risen clouds threw down the horses and crushed them with their legs.

sn: पाट्यमानेषु कुम्भेषु पार्श्वेष्वपि च वारणाः। प्रासैर्विनिहताः केचिद् विनेदुः परमातुराः॥
en: Being struck on their frontal globes and flanks, and mangled by lances, many elephants roared aloud in great agony.

sn: साश्वारोहान् हयान् कांश्चिदुन्मथ्य वरवारणाः। सहसा चिक्षिपुस्तत्र संकुले भैरवे सति॥
en: In the bewildering confusion of the melee, many elephants threw steeds with their riders and crushed them down.

sn: साश्वारोहान् विषाणाप्रैक्षिप्य तुरगान् गजाः। रथौघानभिमृद्नन्तः सध्वजानभिचक्रमुः॥
en: Overthrowing with their tusks steeds and their riders, some elephants roved about and crushed cars with their standards.

sn: पुंस्त्वादतिमदत्वाच्च केचित् तत्र महागजाः। साश्वारोहान् हयाञ्जघ्नुः करैः सचरणैस्तथा॥ अश्वारोहैश्च समरे हस्तिसादिभिरेव च।
en: Some huge male elephants, from excess of energy and with the temporal juice gushing down from their temples in large quantities, killed horses with their riders by their trunks and legs.

sn: प्रतिमानेषु गात्रेषु पार्श्वेष्वभि च वारणान्। आशुगा विमलास्तीक्ष्णाः सम्पेतुर्भुजगोपमाः॥
en: Polished, sharp-pointed and fleet arrows resembling snakes fell upon the heads, the temples and the flanks and the limbs of elephants.

sn: नराश्वकायान् निर्भिद्य लौहानि कवचानि च। निपेतुर्विमलाः शक्त्यो वीरबाहुभिरर्पिताः॥ महोल्काप्रतिमा घोरास्तत्र तत्र विशाम्पते। द्वीपिचर्मावनद्धैश्च व्याघ्रचर्मच्छदैरपि॥ विकोशैविमलैः खङ्गैरभिजग्मुः परान् रणे।
en: king, icarful, polished javelins resembling large meteoric lashes being hurled by heroic arms fell everywhere piercing through bodies of men and horses and cutting through coats of mail. Taking out their sharp swords from sheathes made of leopard's and tiger's skins, many killed their adversaries in battle.

sn: अभिप्लुतमभिक्रुद्धमेकपाविदारितम्॥ विदर्शयन्तः सम्पेतुः खगचर्मपरश्वधैः।
en: Many warriors, though attacked and their bodies cut open, fell upon their antagonists with swords, shields and battle-axes.

sn: केचिदाक्षिप्य करिणः शाश्वानपि रथान् करैः॥ विकर्षन्तो दिशः सर्वाः सम्पेतुः सर्वशब्दगाः।
en: Dragging down and overthrowing cars with their horses by their trunks, some elephants roved about in all directions, guided by the cries of those behind them.

sn: शङ्कुभिर्दारिताः केचित् सम्भिन्नाश्च परश्वधैः॥ हस्तिभिर्मुदिताः केचित् क्षुण्णाश्चान्ये तुरंगमैः। रथनेमिनिकृत्ताश्च निकृत्ताश्च परश्वधैः॥ व्याक्रोशन्त नरा राजंस्तत्र तत्र स्म बान्धवान्। पुत्रानन्ये पितृनन्ये भ्रातृ॑श्च सह बन्धुभिः॥ मातुलान् भागिनेयांश्च परानपि च संयुगे।
en: Some pierced by javelins, some cut down by battle-axes, some crushed by elephants, some trodden down by horses, some cut by the car-wheels and some by axes, O king, loudly called for their kinsmen. Some called upon their sons, some upon their fathers, some upon their brothers some upon their relatives, some upon their maternal uncles, some upon their sister's sons, and some upon their friends and others.

sn: विकीर्णान्त्राः सुबहवो भग्नसक्थाश्च भारत॥ बाहुभिश्चापरे छिन्नैः पार्थेषु च विदारिताः।
en: O descendant of Bharata, a large number of combatants lost their weapons, many had their thighs broken. Some were seen to cry piteously for their desire for life, with arms torn off or sides pierced or cut open.

sn: क्रन्दन्तः समदृश्यन्त तृषिता जीवितेप्सवः॥ तृषा परिगताः केचिदल्पसत्त्वा विशाम्पते।
en: O king, some having but little strength, and lying on the field of battle asked for water from excessive thirst.

sn: भूमौ निपतिताः संख्ये मृगयांचक्रिरे जलम्॥ रुधिरौघपरिक्लिन्नाः क्लिश्यमानाश्च भारत। व्यनिन्दन भृशमात्मानं तव पुत्रांश्च संगतान्॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, some, sweltering in blood and becoming greatly weakened, ensured themselves and your son assembled (in that battle).

sn: अपरे क्षत्रियाः शूराः कृतवैराः परस्परम्। नैव शस्त्रं विमुञ्चन्ति नैव क्रन्दन्ति मारिष॥
en: O exalted one, but there were others, the brave Kshatriyas, who having wounded one another, did not abandon their weapons nor did they set up any wails,

sn: तर्जयन्ति च संहृष्टास्तत्र तत्र परस्परम्। आदश्य दशनैश्चापि क्रोधात् सरदनच्छदम्॥ भृकुटीकुटिलैर्वक्त्रैः प्रेक्षन्ति च परस्परम्। अपरे क्लिश्यमानास्तु शरार्ता व्रणपीडिताः॥ निष्कूजाः समपद्यन्त दृढसत्त्वा महाबलाः। अन्ये च विस्थाः शूरा स्थमन्यस्य संयुगे।॥ प्रार्थयाना निपतिताः संक्षुण्णा वरवारणैः। अशोभन्त महाराज सपुष्पा इव किंशुकाः॥
en: There were some, who, lying on those places where they lay, roared in joy and bitting from wrath their own lips with their teeth, looked at one another with faces rendered fearful by the contraction of their eye-brows. Others, possessing great strength and tenacity, wounded with arrow, remained perfectly silent smarting under their pains. Other brave carwarriors, deprived of their own cars in battle and thrown down and wounded by huge elephants, asked to be taken up on the cars of others. O king, many looked beautiful like blossoming Kinshukas.

sn: सम्बभूवुरनीकेषु बहवो भैरवस्वनाः। वर्तमाने महाभीमे तस्मिन् वीरवरक्षये।॥ निजघान पिता पुत्रं पुत्रश्च पितरं रणे। स्वस्रीयो मातुलं चापि स्वस्रीयं चापि मातुलः॥
en: In that fearful battle, destructive of heroes, the father killed the son and the son killed the father, the sister's son killed the maternal uncle, the maternal uncle killed the sister's son Friends killed friends and kinsmen killed kinsmen.

sn: सखा सखायं च तथा सम्बन्धी बान्धवं तथा। एवं युयुधिरे तत्र कुरवः पाण्डवैः सह॥
en: Thus took place the great slaughter in that great battle between the Kurus and the Pandavas.

sn: वर्तमाने तथा तस्मिन् निर्मर्यादे भयानके। भीष्ममासाद्य पार्थानां वाहिनी समकम्पत॥
en: In that fearful and terrible battle in which no consideration was shown, the Pandavas (at last) began to waver before Bhishma.

sn: केतुना पञ्चतारेण तालेन भरतर्षभ। राजतेन महाबाहुरुच्छ्रितेन महारथे। बभौ भीष्मस्तदा राजश्चन्द्रमा इव मेरुणा॥
en: 0 best of the Bharata race, O king, the mighty-armed Bhishma, with his great standard made of silver and adorned with the device of a palmyra with five stars sitting upon his excellent car, shone like the moon on the Meru mountain.

sn: संजय उवाच गतपूर्वाह्नभूयिष्ठे तस्मिन्नहनि दारुणे। वर्तमाने तथा रौद्रे महावीरवरक्षये॥ दुर्मुखः कृतवर्मा च कृपः शल्यो विविंशतिः। भीष्मं जुगुपुरासाद्य तव पुत्रेण चोदिताः॥
en: Sanjaya said O king, when the greater part of that fearful day passed away, Durmukha, Kritavarma, Kripa, Shalya and Vivingshati, urged by your son, came to Bhishma and began to protect him in that fearful battle which was so destructive of the foremost of men.

sn: एतैरतिरथैर्गुप्तः पञ्चभिर्भरतर्षभः। पाण्डवानामनीकानि विजगाहे महारथः॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, protected by those five great car-warriors that great hero penetrated the Pandava army.

sn: चेदिकाशिकरूषेषु पञ्चालेषु च भारत। भीष्मस्य बहुधा तालश्चलत्केतुरदृश्यत्॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, the palmyra standard of Bhishma was seen to glide continuously through the Chedis, the Kashis, the Karushas and the Panchalas.

sn: स शिरांसि रणेऽरीणां रथांश्च सयुगध्वजान्। निचकर्त महावेगैर्भल्लैः संनतपर्वभिः॥
en: That hero (Bhishma) cut off the heads (of the foes) and their cars with yokes and standards with broad-headed, swifts and perfectly straight arrows.

sn: नृत्यतो रथमार्गेषु भीष्मस्य भरतर्षभ। भृशमार्तस्वरं चक्रुर्नागा मर्मणि ताडिताः॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, Bhishma seemed to dance on his car as it moved about. Some elephants vitally wounded by him, shrieked in great agony.

sn: अभिमन्युः सुसंक्रुद्धः पिशङ्गैस्तुरगोत्तमैः। संयुक्तं रथमास्थाय प्रायाद् भीष्मरथं प्रति॥
en: Thereupon Abhimanyu angrily rushed towards Bhishma's car on his own car yoked with excellent horses of brown colour.

sn: जाम्भूनदविचित्रेण कर्णिकारेण केतुना। अभ्यवर्तत भीष्म च तांश्चैव रथसत्तमान्॥
en: And adorned with a standard decked with pure gold and resembling a Karnikara tree, he attacked Bhishma and those five foremost of car-warriors.

sn: स तालकेतोस्तीक्ष्णेन केतुमाहत्य पत्रिणा। भीष्मेण युयुधे वीरस्तस्य चानुरथैः सह॥
en: Striking with a sharp arrows the palmyra standard (of Bhishma) that hero fought with Bhishma and those others warriors who were protecting him.

sn: कृतवर्माणमेकेन शल्यं पञ्चभिराशुगैः। विद्ध्वा नवभिरान च्छिताचैः प्रपितामहम्॥
en: Wounding Kritvarma with one arrow and Shalya with five, he weakened his great grandfather with nine arrows.

sn: पूर्णायतविसृष्टेन सम्यक् प्रणिहितेन च। ध्वजमेकेन विव्याध जाम्बूदनपरिष्कृतम्॥
en: With one arrow shot from his bow drawn to its fullest extent, he cut off (Bhishma's) standard adorned with gold,

sn: दुर्मुखस्य तु भल्लेन सर्वावरणभेदिना। जहार सारथेः कायाच्छिरः संनतपर्वणा॥
en: With one broad-headed and straight arrow capable of penetrating every thing, he cut off the head of Durmukha's charioteer.

sn: धनुश्चिच्छेद भल्लेन कार्तस्वरविभूषितम्। कृपस्य निशिताचेण तांश्च तीक्ष्णमुखैः शरैः॥ जघान परमक्रुद्धो नृत्यन्निव महारथः। तस्य लाघवमुद्रीक्ष्य तुतुपुर्देवता अपि॥
en: With another sharp arrow, he cut down the gold-decked bow of Kripa. With many sharp arrows that great car warrior wounded them all. Seeing his lightness of hand, even the celestial were pleased.

sn: लब्धलक्षतया काळूः सर्वे भीष्पमुखा रथाः। सत्त्ववन्तममन्यन्त साक्षादिव धनंजयम्॥
en: Seeing the great exactness of Abhimanyu's aim, all the car-warriors with Bhishma at their head, considered that he possessed the great capacity (of his father) Dhananjaya.

sn: तस्य लाघवमार्गस्थमलातसदृशप्रभम्। दिशः पर्यपतच्चापं गाण्डीवमिव घोषवत्॥
en: His bow, sending forth sound like the twang of Gandiva while stretched and restretched, seemed to revolve like a circle of fire.

sn: तमासाद्य महावेगैर्भीष्मो नवभिराशुगैः। विव्याध समरे तूर्णमा नि परवीरहा॥
en: Then that chastiser of foes, Bhishma rushing on him with great impetuosity, soon, wounded the son of Arjuna with nine arrows.

sn: ध्वजं चास्य त्रिभिर्भल्लैश्चिच्छेद परमौजसः। सारथिं च त्रिभिर्बाणैराजघान यतव्रतः॥
en: He too with three broad-headed arrows cut off the standard of that greatly powerful warrior. Of rigid vows, Bhishma also struck his adversary's charioteer.

sn: तथैव कृतवर्मा च कृपः शल्यश्च मारिष। विद्ध्वा नाकम्पयत् कार्ष्णि मैनाकमिव पर्वतम्॥
en: O sire, Kritavarmana, Kripa and Shalya, piercing Arjuna's son, all failed to make him, waver for he stood firm like the Mainaka mountain.

sn: स तैः परिवृतः शूरो धार्तराष्ट्रमहारथैः। ववर्ष शरवर्षाणि कार्ष्णिः पञ्चरथान् प्रति॥
en: Though surrounded by those greatest carwarriors of Dhritarashtra's army, the heroic son of Arjuna still showered, on those five carwarriors, a down pour of arrows.

sn: ततस्तेषां सहस्राणि संवार्य शरवृष्टिभिः। ननाद बलवान् कार्ष्णिीष्माय विसृजशरान्॥
en: Baffling their great weapons by a shower of arrows and pouring on Bhishma a shower of his arrows, the mighty son of Arjuna sent up a loud roar.

sn: तत्रास्य सुमहद् राजन् बाह्वोर्बलमदृश्यत्। यतमानस्य समरे भीष्ममर्दयतः शरैः॥
en: When he was thus struggling in the battle, and afflicting Bhishma with (his) arrows, the strength of his arms we saw then was very great.

sn: पराक्रान्तस्य तस्यैव भीष्मोऽपि प्राहिणोच्छरान्। स तांश्चिच्छेद समरे भीष्मचापच्युताशरान्॥
en: Possessed of such great power, Bhishma shot his arrows at him. But he (Abhimanyu) cut off in the fight all the arrows shot from Bhishma's bow.

sn: ततो ध्वजममोघेषुर्भीष्मस्य नवभिः शरैः। चिच्छेद समरे वीरस्तत उच्चुक्रुशुर्जनाः॥
en: Then that brave bowman cut off with nine arrows, the standard of Bhishma in the great battle. When this great deed was done, the people sent forth a loud shout.

sn: स राजतो महास्कन्धस्तालो हेमविभूषितः। सौभद्रविशिखैश्छिन्नः पपात भुवि भारत॥
en: Adorned with jewels and made of silver, that tall palmyra-deviced standard. 0 descendant of Bharata, cut off by the arrows of Subhadra's son, fell down on the ground.

sn: तं तु सौभद्रविशिखैः पातितं भरतर्षभ। दृष्ट्वा भीमो ननादोच्चैः सौभद्रमभिहर्षयन्॥
en: 0 best of the Bharata race, seeing that standard cut down by the arrows of Subhadra's son, the proud Bhishma sent up a loud shout to cheer up the son of Subhadra.

sn: अथ भीष्मो महास्त्राणि दिव्यानि सुबहूनि च। प्रादुश्चक्रे महारौद्रे रणे तस्मिन् महाबलः॥
en: Then in that great battle, the mighty Bhimasena caused many powerful celestial weapons to app-ear.

sn: ततः सरसहस्रेण सौभद्रं प्रपितामहः। अवाकिरदमेयात्मा तदद्भुतमिवाभवत्॥
en: The high-souled great grandsire (Bhishma) then covered Subhadra's son with thousands of arrows.

sn: ततो दश महेष्वासाः पाण्डवानां महारथाः। रक्षार्थमभ्यधावन्त सौभद्रं त्वरिता रथैः॥
en: Thereupon ten great bowmen and mighty car-warriors of the Pandava (army) soon rushed on their cars to protect the son of Subhadra.

sn: विराटः सह पुत्रेण धृष्टद्युम्नश्च पार्षतः। भीमश्च केकयाचैव सात्यकिश्च विशाम्पते।॥
en: O king, these were Virata and his son, the descendant of Prishata, Dhrishtadyumna, Bhima, the five Kaikeya brothers, and Satyaki.

sn: तेषां जवेनापततां भीष्मः शान्तनवो रणे। पाञ्चाल्यं त्रिभिरानछेत् सात्यकिं नवभिः शरैः॥
en: As they were rushing upon him with great impetuosity, the son of Shantanu, Bhishma, in that great battle, wounded the Panchala prices with three arrows and Satyaki with nine.

sn: पूर्णायतविसृष्टेन क्षुरेण निशितेन च। ध्वजमेकेन चिच्छेद भीमसेनस्य पत्रिणा॥
en: With one winged arrow as sharp as a razor shot from his bow drawn to its fullest stretch, he cut off the standard of Bhimasena.

sn: जाम्बूनदमय: श्रीमान् केसरी स नरोत्तम। पपात भीमसेनस्य भीष्मेण मथितो रथात्॥
en: O foremost of men, the lion-deviced standard of Bhimasena, made cf gold, being cut off by Bhishma, fell from the car.

sn: ततो भीमस्त्रिभिर्विद्ध्वा भीष्मं शान्तनवं रणे। कृपमेकेन विव्याध कृतवर्माणमष्टभिः॥
en: Thereupon Bhima wounded the son of Shantanu with three arrows, Kripa with one and Kritavarman with eight.

sn: प्रगृहीताग्रहस्तेन वैराटिरपि दन्तिना। अभ्यद्रवत राजानं मद्राधिपतिमुत्तरः॥
en: The son of Virata, Uttara, also riding on an elephant with upraised trunk attacked the king of Madra.

sn: तस्य वारणराजस्य जवेनापततो रथे। शल्यो निवारयामास वेगमप्रतिमं शरैः॥
en: But Shalya checked the great impetuosity of that foremost of elephants rushing towards his car.

sn: तस्य क्रुद्धः स नागेन्द्रो बृहतः साधुवाहिनः। पदा युगमधिष्ठाय जघान चतुरो हयान्॥
en: But that foremost of elephants angrily placed his let on the yoke of (Shalya's) car and killed his four large and swift horses.

sn: स हताश्वे रथे तिष्ठन् मद्राधिपतिरायसीम्। उत्तरान्तकरी शक्तिं चिक्षेप भुजगोपमाम्॥
en: The king of Madra,. staying on the car the horses of which had been killed, hurled an iron dart, which resembled a snake, in order to kill Uttara.

sn: तया भिन्नतनुत्राणः प्रविश्य विपुलं तमः। स पपात गजस्कन्धात् प्रमुक्ताङ्कुशतोमरः॥
en: His armour being cut through by the dart, he lost consciousness and fell from the elephant, the hook and the lance also fell loosened from his grasp.

sn: असिमादाय शल्योऽपि अवप्लुत्य रथोत्तमात्। तस्य वारणराजस्य चिच्छेदाथ महाकरम्॥
en: Shalya then took up his sword and jumping down from his excellent car, he with great force cut off the large trunk of that great elephant.

sn: भिन्नमर्मा शरशतैश्छिन्नहस्तः स वारण:। भीममार्तस्वरं कृत्वा पपात च ममार च॥
en: His armour pierced all over with a shower of arrows and his trunk cut off, that elephant sent forth a loud shriek. He then fell down and expired.

sn: एतदीदृशकं कृत्वा मद्रराजो नराधिप। आरुरोह रथं तूर्णं भास्वरं कृतवर्मणः॥
en: O king, performing this great feat, the Madra king soon got the of Kritavarman.

sn: उत्तरं वै हतं दृष्ट्वा वैराटिर्भ्रातरं तदा। कृतवर्मणा च सहितं दृष्ट्वा शल्यमवस्थितम्॥ श्वेतः क्रोधात् प्रजज्वाल हविषा हव्यवाडिव। स विस्फार्य महच्चापं शक्रचापोपमं बली॥ अभ्यधावज्जिघांसन् वै शल्य मद्राधिपं बली। महता रथवंशेन समन्तात् परिवारितः॥ मुञ्चन् बाणमयं वर्ष प्रायाच्छल्यरधं प्रति। तमापतन्तं सम्प्रेक्ष्य मत्तवारणविक्रमम्॥ तावकानां रथाः सप्त समन्तात् पर्यवारयन्। मद्रराजमभीप्सन्तो मृत्योर्दष्ट्रान्तरं गतम्॥
en: Seeing his brother Uttara killed and seeing Shalya on the Kritavarman's car, Virata's son Shveta blazed up in anger as fire blazed forth with Ghee. That great warrior stretching his large bow that looked like that of Indra, rushed upon Shalya, the king of Madra with the desire of killing him. Surrounded on all sides with innumerable car-warriors, he advanced towards Shalya's chariot and poured upon him a on car shower of arrows. Seeing him rush to the fight with the prowess of an infuriated elephants, seven car-warriors of your side surrounded him on all sides with the desire of protecting the ruler of Madra who seemed to be already within the jaws of death.

sn: बृहद्बलश्च कौसल्यो जयत्सेनश्च मागधः। तथा रुक्मरथो राजन् शल्यपुत्रः प्रतापवान्॥ विन्दानुविन्दावावन्त्यौ काम्बोजश्च सुदक्षिणः। बृहत्क्षत्रस्य दायादः सैन्धवश्च जयद्रथः॥
en: Those seven warriors were Brihadbala, the king of the Kosalas, Jayatsena of Magadha, Rukmaratha, the brave son of Shalya, Vinda and Anuvinda of Avanti, Sudakshina the king of the Kambojas, and Jayadratha, the king of the Sindhus and the kinsman of Brihatkshatra.

sn: नानावर्णविचित्राणि धनूंषि च महात्मनाम्। विस्फारितानि दृश्यन्ते तोयदेष्विव विद्युतः॥
en: The stretched bow of these illustrious warriors, decorated with various colours, looked like the flashes of lightning in the clouds.

sn: ते तु बाणमयं वर्षं श्वेतमूर्धन्यपातयन्। निदाघान्तेऽनिलोद्धृता मेघा इव नगे जलम्॥
en: They all poured on the head of Shveta a continuous shower of arrows as the clouds, tossed by the wind, pure rain on the mountain breast when summer is passed.

sn: ततः क्रुद्धो महेष्वासः सप्तभल्लैः सुतेजनैः। धनूंषि तेषामाच्छिद्य ममर्द पृतनापतिः॥
en: The great bowman, that commander of the force, being greatly enraged at this struck their bows with seven broad-headed arrows of great impetuosity.

sn: निकृत्तान्येव तानि स्म समदृश्यन्त भारत। ततस्ते तु निमेषार्धात् प्रत्यपद्यन् धनूंषि च॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, we saw those bows were cut off. Then within half the time of a wink of the eye they took up other bows.

sn: सप्त चैव पृषत्कांश्च श्वेतस्योपर्यपातयन्। ततः पुनरमेयात्मा भल्लैः सप्तभिराशुगैः। निचकर्त महाबाहुस्तेषां चापानि धन्विनाम्॥
en: That mighty-armed and high-souled warrior then with seven swift arrows again cut off the bows of those bowmen.

sn: ते निकृत्तमहाचापास्त्वरमाणा महारथाः। रथशक्ती: परामृश्य विनेदुभैरवान् रवान्॥
en: Those heroes, those great car-warriors whose large bows had been cut down swelled in wrath, and grasping darts, sent forth a loud shout.

sn: अन्वयुर्भरतश्रेष्ठ सप्त श्वेतरथं प्रति। ततस्ता ज्वलिताः सप्त महेन्द्राशनिनिःस्वनाः॥ अप्राप्ताः सप्तभिर्भल्लैश्चिच्छेद परमास्त्रवित्। ततः समादाय शरं सर्वकायविदारणम्॥ प्राहिणोद् भरतश्रेष्ठ श्वेतो रुक्मरथं प्रति। तस्य देहे निपतितो बाणो वज्रातिगो महान्॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, they hurled these seven darts on Shveta's chariot. Those blazing darts, which flew like large meteors with the sound of thunder, were all cut down by that great warrior with seven broad-headed arrows before they could reach him. O best of the Bharata race, then taking up an arrow which was capable of penetrating into every part of their body, he hurled it on Rukmaratha. That great arrow penetrated into his body.

sn: ततो रुक्मरथो राजन् सायकेन दृढाहतः। निषसाद रथोपस्थे कश्मलं चाविशन्महत्॥
en: Then, O king, being thus struck by the arrow, Rukmaratha sat down on his car and lost all consciousness.

sn: तं विसंज्ञं विमनसं त्वरमाणस्तु सारथिः। अपोवाह न सम्भ्रान्तः सर्वलोकस्य पश्यतः॥
en: His charioteer, however, without betraying any fear, carried him away, senseless and fainted, from the field of battle.

sn: ततोऽन्यान् षट् समादाय श्वेतोहेमविभूषितान्। तेषां षण्णां महाबाहुर्ध्वजशीर्षाण्यपातयत्॥
en: Then taking up six other arrows decked with gold, Shveta cut off the standards of his six adversaries.

sn: हयांश्च तेषां निर्भिद्य सारथींश्च परंतप। शरैश्चैतान् समाकीर्य प्रायाच्छल्यरथं प्रति॥
en: Wounding their horses and charioteers also and covering those six warriors with a continuos shower of arrows, that chastiser of foes, went towards the car of Shalya.

sn: ततो हलहलाशब्दस्तव सैन्येषु भारत। दृष्ट्वा सेनापतिं तूर्णं यान्तं शल्यरथं प्रति॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, when that great general (Shveta) was rushing with great force towards the car of Shalya, loud cries of “Oh" "Alas" rose in your army.

sn: ततो भीष्मं पुरस्कृत्य तव पुत्रो महाबलः। वृतस्तु सर्वसैन्येन प्रायाच्छ्वेतरथं प्रति॥
en: Then your great son, with Bhishma, at the head and with many other heroic warriors and troops, went towards Shveta's car.

sn: मृत्योरास्यमनुप्राप्तं मद्ररोजममोचयत्। ततो युद्ध समभवत् तुमुलं लोमहर्षणम्॥ तावकानां परेषां च व्यतिषक्तरथद्विपम्। सौभद्रे भीमसेने च सात्यकौ च महारथे।॥ कैकेये च विराटे च धृष्टद्युम्ने च पार्षते। एतेषु नरसिंहेषु चेदिमत्स्येषु चैव ह। ववर्ष शरवर्षाणि कुरुवृद्धः पितामहः॥
en: He thus rescued the Madra King who was at the point of death. Then a fearful and hairstring battle was fought between your troops and those of the enemy in which cars and elephants all got mixed up in confusion. The old grandfather of the Kurus poured showers of arrows on Subhadra's son, on Bhimsena and on that great car-warrior Satyaki and also upon the king of the Kaikeyas, on Virata, on the descendant of Prishata, Dhrishtadyumna, and also upon Chedi troops.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच एवं श्वेते महेष्वासे प्राप्ते शल्यरथं प्रति। कुरवः पाण्डवेयाश्च किमकुर्वत संजय॥ भीष्मः शान्तनवः किं वा तन्ममाचक्ष्व पृच्छतः।
en: Dhritarashtra said O Sanjaya when that great bow man Shveta went towards Shalya's chariot, what did the Kurus and the Pandavas do? What did Bhishma the son of Shantanu do? Tell me all this, I ask you

sn: संजय उवाच राजशतसहस्राणि ततः क्षत्रियपुङ्गवाः॥ श्वेतं सेनापतिं शूरं पुरस्कृत्य महारथाः।
en: Sanjaya said O king, hundreds and thousands of the foremost of Kshatriyas, all brave great carwarriors placed their general Shveta in their front.

sn: राज्ञो बलं दर्शयन्तस्तव पुत्रस्य भारत॥ शिखण्डिनं पुरस्कृत्य त्रातुमैच्छन्महारथाः।
en: And displaying their prowess to your royal son, O descendant of Bharata, desired to rescue Shveta, with Shikhandin at their head.

sn: अभ्यवर्तन्त भीष्मस्य रथं हेमपरिष्कृतम्॥ जिघांसन्तं युधां श्रेष्ठं तदाऽऽसीत् तुमुलं महत्।
en: Those great car-warriors rushed towards Bhishma's car decked with gold, with the intention of killing that foremost of warriors. The battle that was then fought was fearful.

sn: तत् तेऽहं सम्प्रवक्ष्यामि महावैशसमच्युत॥ तावकानां परेषा च यथा युद्धमवर्तत।
en: I shall describe to you that wonderful and fearful battle that was fought between your warriors and those of the enemy.

sn: तत्राकरोद् रथोपस्थाशून्याशान्तनवोबहून्॥ तत्राद्भुतं महच्चक्रे शरैराछंद् रथोत्तमान्।
en: The son of Shantanu made many cars empty, for that foremost of all car-warriors cut off many heads by showering his arrows.

sn: समावृणोच्छरैरर्कमर्कतुल्यप्रतापवान्॥ नुदन् समन्तात् समरे रविरुद्यन् यथा तमः।
en: Possessing the prowess of the sun, he covered the very sun with his arrows. As the rising sun dispels the darkness from around him, so did he remove the foe from around him in that great battle.

sn: तेनाजो प्रेषिता राजन् शराः शतसहस्रशः॥ क्षत्रियान्तकराः संख्ये महावेगा महाबलाः।
en: O king, in that great battle, hundreds and thousands of arrows were shot by him. They were very powerful and they possessed great impetuosity. They killed countless Kshatriya in that battle.

sn: शिरांसि पातयामासुर्वीराणां शतशो रणे॥ गजान् कण्टकसन्नाहान् वज्रेणेव शिलोच्चयान्।
en: O king, in that great battle, he cut off the heads of hundreds of heroic warriors and elephants clad in thorny mail as summits of mountains are felled by thunderbolt.

sn: रथा रथेषु संसक्ता व्यदृश्यन्त विशाम्पते॥ एके रथं पर्यवहंस्तुरगाः सुतरङ्गमम्।
en: O king, cars were seen to mingle with cars. One car was seen upon another car and a horse upon another horse.

sn: युवानं निहतं वीरं लम्बमानं सकार्मुकम्॥ उदीर्णाश्च हया राजन् वहन्तस्तत्र तत्र ह।
en: O king, impetuous horses carried here and there the youthful riders killed and hung from their saddle with their bows till in their hands.

sn: बद्धशङ्गनिषङ्गाश्च विध्वस्तशिरसो हताः॥ शतशः पतिता भूमौ वीरशय्यासु शेरते।
en: With swords and quivers, attached to their person and their armours loosened, hundreds of dead warriors lay on the ground sleeping on beds worthy of heroes.

sn: परस्परेण धावन्तः पतिताः पुनरुत्थिताः॥ उत्थाय च प्रधावन्तो द्वन्द्वयुद्धमवाप्नुवन्।
en: Rushing upon one another, falling down and rising up again, and rushing again having risen up the combatants fought hand to hand.

sn: पीडिताः पुनरन्योन्यं लुठन्तो रणमूर्धनि॥ सचापाः सनिषङ्गाश्च जातरूपपरिष्कृताः। विस्रब्धहतवीराश्च शतश: परिपीडिताः॥ तेन तेनाभ्यधावन्त विसृजन्तश्च भारत! मत्तो गजः पर्यवर्तद्धयांश्च हतसादिनः॥
en: Struck by one another, many rolled on the field of battle, O Bharata! several hundred warriors with bow and arrow-stand and gold ornaments on body were destroying the warriors of rival army with all reliance in their might and enduring the blows made by the enemies. They were rushing to and fro through the several routes the found and blowing continuously the arms and weapons on them.

sn: सरथा रथिनश्चापि विमृद्वन्तः समन्ततः। स्यन्दनादपतत् कश्चिन्निहतोऽन्येन सायकैः॥
en: Car-warriors, with their cars, were crushed (by the elephants). Some warrior fell on their cars killed by other warriors with their arrows.

sn: हतसारथिरप्युच्चैः पपात काष्ठवद् रथः। युध्यमानस्य संग्रामे व्यूढे रजसि चोत्थिते॥ धनुः कूजितविज्ञानं तत्रासीत् प्रतियुद्ध्यतः। गात्रस्पर्शेन योधानां व्यज्ञास्त परिपन्थिनम्॥
en: Many great car-warriors were seen to fall down from high, their charioteers being killed. A thick dust covered all sides. Then the warriors knew their adversaries by the twang of the bow. From the pressure also on their bodies the combatants guessed their enemies.

sn: युद्ध्यमानं शरै राजन् सिञ्जिनीध्वजिनीरवात्। अन्योन्यं वीरसंशब्दो नाश्रूयत भटैः कृतः॥
en: O king, the warriors fought on with arrows guided by the twang of the bow strings. Even the very his sing sound of the arrows shot by the combatants at one another could not be heard.

sn: शब्दायमाने संग्रामे पटहे कर्णदारिणि। युद्ध्यमानस्य संग्रामे कुर्वतः पौरुषं स्वकम्॥ नाश्रौषं नामगोत्राणि कीर्तनं च परस्परम्।
en: So loud was the sound of drums that it seemed to pierce the cars. In that tumultuous and hair-string uproar even the names of the combatants could not be heard.

sn: भीष्मचापच्युतैर्बाणैरार्तानां युध्यतां मृधे॥ परस्परेषां वीराणां मनांसि समकम्पयन्। तस्मिन्नत्याकुले युद्धे दारुणे लोमहर्षणे॥ पिता पुत्रं च समरे नाभिजानाति कश्चन।
en: All warriors were bearing the pains sprcaded by the arrows released from Bhishma's bow in battle-field. Those arrows had created fear of death in the mind of all those warriors. That battle was most fierce, thrilling and arousing anxiety in the hearts of all. Any father in that battle was so lost of recognition as his own son was beyond the same.

sn: चक्रे भग्ने युगे छिन्ने एकधुर्ये हये हतः॥ आक्षिप्तः स्यन्दनाद् वीरः ससारथिरजिह्मगैः।
en: One of the wheels being broken, the yoke being torn off, onc of the steeds being killed, the brave car-warrior was overthrown from the car along with his charioteer.

sn: एवं च समरे सर्वे वीराश्च विरथीकृताः॥ तेन तेन स्म दृश्यन्ते धावमानाः समन्ततः।
en: Thus many brave warriors, deprived of their cars, were seen to run (in all directions).

sn: गजो हतः शिरश्छिन्नं मर्म भिन्नं हयो हतः॥ अहतः कोऽपि नैवासीद् भीष्मे निघ्नति शात्रवान्।
en: He, who was killed, had his head cut off, he, who was not killed, was mortally wounded. When Bhishma attacked, there was none who was not wounded.

sn: श्वेतः कुरूणामकरोत् क्षयं तस्मिन् महाहवे॥ राजपुत्रान् रथोदारानधीच्छतसंघशः।
en: In that fearful battle Shveta killed innumerable Kurus. He killed hundreds of noble princes.

sn: चिच्छेद रथिनां बाणैः शिरांसि भरतर्षभ॥ साङ्गदा बाहवश्चैव धनूंषि च समन्ततः।
en: He cut off with his arrows the heads of hundreds of car-warriors and also their arms decked with Angadas, and also their bows.

sn: रथेषां रथचक्राणि तूणीराणि युगानि च॥ छत्राणि च महार्हाणि पताकाश्च विशाम्पते। हयौघाश्च रथौघाश्च नरौघाश्चैव भारत॥ वारणाः शतशश्चैव हताः श्वेतेन भारत।
en: O king, O best of the Bharata race, carwarriors and car-wheels, the cars-themselves, both small and costly standards, many horses and innumerable inen and hundreds of elephants were destroyed by Shveta.

sn: वयं श्वेतभयाद् भीता विहाय रथसत्तमम्॥ अपयातास्तथा पश्चाद् विभुं पश्याम धृष्णवः।
en: From fear of Shveta, we abandoned Bhishma that foremost of warriors; we left the battle and retreated to the rear and therefore, we now see your cxalted self.

sn: शरपातमतिक्रम्य कुरवः कुरुनन्दन॥ भीष्मं शान्तनवं युद्धे स्थिताः पश्याम सर्वशः।
en: O descendant of Kuru, retreating beyond the range of arrows and abandoning the son of Shantanu, Bhishma, in that battle, all the Kurus stood (as spectators), though armed for the battle.

sn: अदीनो दीनसमये भीष्मोऽस्माकं महाहवे॥ एकस्तस्थौ नरव्याघ्रो गिरिर्मेसरिवाचलः।
en: Ever cheerful even in the hour of cheerlessness, that foremost of man, Bhishma, alone, of our army, stood in that fearful battle as immovable as the mountain Meru.

sn: आददान इव प्राणान् सविता शिशिरात्यये॥ गभस्तिभिरिवादित्यस्तस्थौ शरमरीचिमान्।
en: Killing the foes like the sun at the end of the winter, he stood effulgent with the golden rays of his car, as the sun shines with his rays.

sn: स मुमोच महेष्वासः शरसंघाननेकशः॥ निजन्नमित्रान् समरे वज्रपाणिरिवासुरान्।
en: That great bow man shot showers in arrows and struck down his enemies in that battle as Vishnu, arıncd with the discus struck down the Asuras.

sn: ते वध्यमाना भीष्मेण प्रजहुस्तं महाबलम्॥ स्वयूथादिव ते यूथान्मुक्तं भूमिषु दारुणम्।
en: The mighty Bhishma was separated from your army and became ferocious in that battlefield as an elephant becomes dangerous when its caravan missed and he is left alone. (All warriors from rival party, ran away leaving him alone because they could not bear more blows given by Bhishma.)

sn: तमेवमुपलक्ष्यैको हृष्टः पुष्टः परंतप॥ दुर्योधनप्रिये युक्तः पाण्डवान् परिशोचयन्।
en: While fighting with the great warriors (Shveta), that chastiser of foes, Bhishma was the only one who was cheerful. Ever devoted to the welfare of Duryodhana, he began to consume the warriors (Shveta).

sn: जीवितं दुस्त्यजं त्यक्त्वा भयं च सुमहाहवे॥ पातयामास सैन्यानि पाण्डवानां विशाम्पते।
en: O kind, reckless of his own life, abandoning all fear, he slaughtered the Pandava troops in that great battle.

sn: प्रहरन्तमनीकानि पिता देवव्रतस्तव॥ दृष्ट्वा सेनापति भीष्मस्त्वरितः श्वेतमभ्ययात्।
en: Seeing that (Pandava) general striking Duryodhana's troops,, your father Bhishma, also called Devavrata, rushed upon him.

sn: स भीष्मं शरजालेन महता समवाकिरत्॥ श्वेतं चापि तथा भीष्मः शरौघैः समवाकिरत्।
en: Thereupon Shveta covered Bhishma with a great net of arrows, Bhishma also covered Shveta with a shower of arrows.

sn: तौ वृषाविव नर्दन्तौ मत्ताविव महाद्विपौ॥ व्याघ्राविव सुसंरब्धावन्योन्यमभिजघ्नतुः।
en: Roaring like two bulls, they rushed against each other like two gigantic mad elephants or like two angry tigers.

sn: अस्त्रैरस्त्राणि संवार्य ततस्तौ पुरुषर्षभौ॥ भीष्मः श्वेतश्च युयुधे परस्परवधैषिणौ।
en: Baffling each other's weapons by means of their weapons those (two) foremost of men, Bhishma and Shveta fought with each other with the desire of taking each other's life.

sn: एकाछा निर्दहेद् भीष्मः पाण्डवानामनीकिनीम्॥ शरैः परमसंक्रुद्धो यदि श्वेतो न पालयेत्।
en: If Shveta did not protect it, in one single day Bhishma could have in anger consumed the Pandava army with his arrows.

sn: पितामहं ततो दृष्ट्वा श्वेतेन विमुखीकृतम्॥ प्रहर्ष पाण्डवा जग्मुः पुत्रस्ते विमनाऽभवत्।
en: Seeing the grandfather made to retreat by Shveta, the Pandavas grew exceedingly delighted, but your son became very much cheerless.

sn: ततो दुर्योधन: क्रुद्धः पार्थिवैः परिवारितः॥ ससैन्यः पाण्डवानीकमभ्यद्रवत संयुगे।
en: Thereupon Duryodhana surrounded by many kings, rushed in anger against the Pandava troops in that great battle.

sn: दुर्मुखः कृतवर्मा च कृपः शल्यो विशाम्पतिः॥ भीष्मं जुगुपुरासाद्य तव पुत्रेण नोदिताः।
en: Durmukha, Kritavarman, Kripa and Shalya, the lord of men also protected Bhishma inspired by your son.

sn: दृष्ट्वा तु पार्थिवैः सर्वैर्दुर्योधनपुरोगमैः॥ पाण्डवानामनीकानि वध्यमानानि संयुगे। श्वेतो गाङ्गेयमुत्सृज्य तव पुत्रस्य वाहिनीम्॥ नाशयामास वेगेन वायुर्वृक्षानिवौजसा।
en: Seeing the army of Pandavas is being slain in battle by Duryodhana and all other kings, Shveta abandoned the son of Ganga, Bhishma and began to slaughter your son's troops with great iinpetuosity as the wind up-roots trees with great violence.

sn: द्रावयित्वा चमू राजन् वैराटिः क्रोधमूर्च्छितः॥ आपतत् सहसा भूयो यत्र भीष्मो व्यवस्थितः।
en: O king, having routed your army, Virata's son (Shveta) senseless in anger again rushed towards the place where Bhishma stood.

sn: तौ तत्रोपगतौ राजन् शरदीप्तौ महाबलौ।॥ अयुध्येतां महात्मानौ यथोभौ वृत्रवासवौ। अन्योन्यं तु महाराज परस्परवधैषिणौ॥ निगृह्य कार्मुकं श्वेतो भीष्मं विव्याध सप्तभिः।
en: O king! those two mighty and great warriors, both blazing with their arrows, fought with each other like Vritra and Vasava in the days of yore, both eager to kill each other. Having drawn his bow to the fullest stretch, Shveta wounded Bhishma with seven arrows.

sn: पराक्रमं ततस्तस्य पराक्रम्य पराक्रमी॥ तरसा वारयामास मत्तो मत्तमिव द्विपम्।
en: The brave one (Bhishma) then put forth his prowess; he quickly checked his adversary's valour as a mad elephants checks another inad elephant.

sn: श्वेतः शान्तनवं भूयः शरैः संनतपर्वभिः॥ विव्याध पञ्चविंशत्या दद्भुतमिवाभवत्।
en: Shveta again shot twenty five arrows having bent knot cach and penetrated the budy of Bhishma, the son of Shantanu. It was happened as an unprecedented event.

sn: तं प्रत्यविध्यद् दशभिर्भीष्मः शान्तनवस्तदा॥ आजघान ततो भीष्मं श्वेतः क्षत्रियनन्दनः।
en: That delighter of the Kshatriyas, Shveta, then struck Bhishma; and the son of Shantanu pierced him in return with ten arrows.

sn: सम्प्रहस्य ततः श्वेतः सृक्किणी परिसंलिहन्॥ स विद्धस्तेन बलवान् नाकम्पत यथाऽचलः। वैराटिः समरे क्रुद्धो भृशमायम्य कार्मुकम्॥ धनुश्चिच्छेद भीष्मस्य नवभिर्दशधा शरैः। संधाय विशिखं चैव शरं लोमप्रवाहिनम्॥ उन्ममाथ ततस्तालं ध्वजशीर्षं महात्मनः। केतुं निपतितं दृष्ट्वा भीष्मस्य तनयास्तव॥ हतं भीष्ममन्यन्त श्वेतस्य वशमागतम्। पाण्डवाश्चापि संहृष्टादध्मुः शङ्खान् मुदायुताः॥
en: They smiling and licking with his tongue the corners of the mouth, Shveta cut down Bhishma's bow into ten parts with nine arrows. Then taking up a winged arrow made of iron, he crushed the palmyra on the top of the standard of that exalted one (Bhishma). Seeing the standard of Bhishma cut down, your sons thought that Bhishma was killed. The Pandavas in great delight blew their conchs.

sn: भीष्मस्य पतितं केतुं दृष्ट्वा तालं महात्मनः। ततो दुर्योधनः क्रोधात् स्वमनीकमनोदयत्।।६
en: Seeing the palmyra-standard of the illustrious Bhishma cut down, Duryodhana, in great anger, urged his army to the battle.

sn: यत्ता भीष्मं परीप्सध्वं रक्षमाणाः समन्ततः। मा नः प्रपश्यमानानां श्वेतान्मृत्युमवाप्स्यति॥ भीष्मः शान्तनवः शूरस्तथा सत्यं ब्रवीमि वः। राज्ञस्तु वचनं श्रुत्वा त्वरमाणा महारथाः॥ बलेन चतुरङ्गेण गाङ्गेयमन्वपालयन्। बाह्रीकः कृतवर्मा च शलः शल्यश्च भारत॥ जलसंधो विकर्णश्च चित्रसेनो विविंशतिः। त्वरमाणास्त्वराकाले परिवार्य समन्ततः॥ अवारयदमेयात्मा दर्शयन् पाणिलाघवम्। स निवार्य तान् सर्वान् केसरी कुञ्जरानिव॥ महता शरवर्षेण भीष्मस्य धनुराच्छिनत्।
en: They all carefully protected Bhishma who was then in great distress. To them that stood there as spectators, the king (Duryodhana) thus exclaimed. “Either Shveta or Bhishma will die (to day)". Having heard the words of the king, the great car-warriors soon with four kinds of troops advanced to protect the son of Ganga. O descendant of Bharata, Balhika, Kritavarina, Kripa, Shalya, the son of Jarasandha, Vikarna, Chitrasena and Vivingshati, all with great speed, surrounded him on all sides and poured a continuous shower of arrows. That highsouled and mighty warrior then soon checked those wrathful warriors with sharp arrows by displaying his own lightness of hands. Checking them all as a lion checks a herd of elephants, Shveta cut off Bhishma's bow with a thick shower of arrows.

sn: ततोऽन्यद् धनुरादाय भीष्मः शान्तनवो युधि॥ श्वेतं विव्याध राजेन्द्र कङ्कपत्रैः शितैः शरैः। ततः सेनापतिः क्रुद्धो भीष्मं बहुभिरायसैः॥ विव्याध समरे राजन् सर्वलोकस्य पश्यतः। ततः प्रव्यथितो राजा भीष्मं दृष्ट्वा निवारितम्॥ । प्रवीरं सर्वलोकस्य श्वेतेन युधि वै तदा। निष्ठानकश्च सुमहांस्तव सैन्यस्य चाभवत्॥ तं वीरं वारितं दृष्ट्वा श्वेतेन शरविक्षतम्। हतं श्वेतेन मन्यन्ते श्वेतस्य वशमागतम्॥
en: Then the son of Shantanu, Bhishma, took up another bow in that battle and wounded Shveta with arrows, furnished with the feather of Kanka birds. Then that commander (Shveta) in great anger wounded Bhishma in that battle with innumerable arrows in the very sight of all. Seeing Bhishma, that foremost of all the warriors, checked in the battle by Shveta the king (Duryodhana) became exceedingly cheerless, and your whole army felt themselves in great distress. Seeing the heroic Bhislima checked and wounded by Shveta with his arrows, a!' thought that Bhishma had been killed.

sn: ततः क्रोधवशं प्राप्तः पिता देवव्रतस्तव। ध्वजमुन्मथितं दृष्ट्वा तां च सेनां निवारिताम्॥ श्वेतं प्रति महाराज व्यसृजत् सायकान् बहून्। तानावार्य रणे श्वेतो भीष्पस्य रथिनां वरः॥ धनुश्चिच्छेद भल्लेन पुनरेव पितुस्तव। उत्सृज्य कार्मुकं राजन् गाङ्गेयः क्रोधमूर्च्छितः॥ अन्यत् कार्मुकमादाय विपुलं बलवत्तरम्। तत्र संधाय विपुलान् भल्लान् सप्त शिलाशितान्॥ चतुर्भिश्च जघानाश्वाच्छ्वेतस्य पृतनापतेः। ध्वजं द्वाभ्यां तु चिच्छेद सप्तमेन च सारथेः॥ शिरश्चिच्छेद भल्लेन संक्रुद्धो लघुविक्रमः।
en: Thereupon your father Devavrata, seeing his standard cut down and the army checked, grew greatly enraged and shot at Shveta innumerable arrows. O king, that foremost of heroes Shveta however baffled all those arrows of Bhishma and he once more cut off with a broad-headed arrow the bow of your father. O king, throwing aside that bow, the son of Ganga took up in great anger another strong and large bow, and aiming seven large broadheaded arrows, killed the four horses of the general Shveta, then he cut down his standard and then, the head of his charioteer.

sn: हताश्वसूतात् स रथादवप्लुत्य महाबलः॥ अमर्षवशमापन्नो व्याकुलः समपद्यत। विरथं रथिनां श्रेष्ठं श्वेतं दृष्ट्वा पितामहः॥ ताडयामास निशितैः शरसंधैः समन्ततः। स ताड्यमानः समरे भीष्मचापच्युतैः शरैः॥ स्वरथे धनुरुत्सृज्य शक्तिं जग्राह काञ्चनीम्। ततः शक्तिं रणे श्वेतो जग्राहोचां महाभयाम्॥ कालदण्डोपमां घोरां मृत्योर्जिह्वामिव श्वसन्। अब्रवीच्च तदा श्वेतो भीष्मं शान्तनवं रणे॥ तिष्ठेदानीं सुसंरब्धः पश्य मां पुरुषो भव। एवमुक्त्वा महेष्वासो भीष्मं युधि पराक्रमी॥ ततः शक्तिममेयात्मा चिक्षेप भुजगोपमाम्। पाण्डवार्थ पराक्रान्तस्तवानर्थं चिकीर्षुकः॥
en: Thereupon that great car-warrior jumped down from his car the horses and the charioteer of which had been killed. Seeing Shveta, that foremost of car-warriors, deprived of his car, the grandsire began to strike him on all sides with showers of arrows. Wounded in this great battle with arrows shot from Bhishma's bow, leaving his bow on his car, he took up a dart decked with gold, and taking up that terrible and fearful dart which resembled the fatal rod of Death and which was capable of killing even Death himself, Shveta thus spoke in anger to the son of Shantanu, Bhishma. "O foremost of men, wait a little and see my prowess". Having said this to Bhishma that greatly powerful and high-souled bow-man hurled that dart resembling a snake.

sn: हाहाकारो महानासीत् पुत्राणां ते विशाम्पते। दृष्ट्वा शक्तिं महाघोरां मृत्योर्दण्डसमप्रभाम्॥
en: O king, then loud cries of “Oh” and “Alas" rose among your sons when they saw that fearful dart which was as effulgent as the rod of death.

sn: श्वेतस्य करनिर्मुक्तां निर्मुक्तोरगसंनिभाम्। अपतत् सहसा राजन् महोल्केव नभस्तलात्॥ ज्वलन्तीमन्तरिक्षे तां ज्वालाभिरिव संवृताम्।
en: Having been furled from Shveta's handthat dart which resembled a snake that had just cast off its slough, fell with great force like a meteor from the sky.

sn: असम्भ्रान्तस्तदा राजन् पिता देवव्रतस्तव।॥ अष्टभिर्नवभिर्भीष्मः शक्तिं चिच्छेद पत्रिभिः। उत्कृष्टहेमविकृतां निकृतां निशितैः शरैः॥
en: Your father Devavrata, then, without the slightest fcar, with eight sharp and winged arrows, cut down into nine parts that fearful dart which was decked with pure gold and which appeared to be covered with flames of fire.

sn: उच्चुक्रुशुस्ततः सर्वे तावका भरतर्षभ। शक्तिं विनिहतां दृष्ट्वा वैराटिः क्रोधमूर्च्छितः।।८ 1८८॥
en: All your troops, O best of the Bharata race, then sent up a loud shout of joy. Virata's son, however, having seen his dart cut down into fragments, lost all sense in anger.

sn: कालोपहतचेतास्तु कर्तव्यं नाभ्यजानत। क्रोधसम्मूर्च्छितो राजन् वैराटिः प्रहसन्निव॥
en: Like one whose heart was over come by the approaching death, he could not settle what to do. O king, deprived of his senses by anger, Virata's son, with smiles.

sn: गदा जग्राह संहृष्टो भीष्मस्य निधनं प्रति। क्रोधेन रक्तनयनो दण्डपाणिरिवान्तकः॥
en: Took up in great cheerfulness a fearful mace for Bhishma's destruction. With eyes red in anger, and loO king like a second Yama armed with the rod.

sn: भीष्मं समभिदुद्राव जलौघ इव पर्वतम्। तस्य वेगमसंवार्यं मत्वा भीष्मः प्रतापवान्॥
en: He rushed upon Bhishma as a swollen river rushes upon a rock. Considering his great impetuosity as incapable of being checked, the greatly fearful Bhishma.

sn: प्रहारविप्रमोक्षार्थं सहसा धरणीं गतः। श्रेतः क्रोधसमाविष्टो भ्रामयित्वा तु तां गदाम्॥
en: Who is ever skillful in knowing the prowess of other, suddenly jumped down on the ground to avoid that blow. O king, Shveta, however, whirling that heavy mace in anger.

sn: रथे भीष्मस्य चिक्षेप यथा देवो धनेश्वरः। तया भीष्मनिपातिन्या स रथो भस्मसात्कृतः॥ सध्वजः सह सूतेन साश्वः सयुगबन्धुरः। विरथं रथिनां श्रेष्ठं भीष्मं दृष्ट्वा रथोत्तमाः॥ वै॥
en: Hurled it on Bhishma's car like the dcity Maheshvara (Shiva). By the fall of that mace intended for Bhishma's destruction, that car. with its standard, charioteer and horses, was reduced to ashes. Seeing Bhishrma, that foremost of car-warriors fighting on foot.

sn: अभ्यधावन्त सहिताः शल्यप्रभृतयो रथाः। ततोऽन्यं रथमास्थाय धनुर्विस्फार्य दुर्मनाः॥ शनकैरभ्ययाच्छ्वेतं गाङ्गेयः प्रहसन्निव। एतस्मिन्नन्तरे भीष्मः शुश्राव विपुलां गिरम्॥ आकाशादीरितां दिव्यामात्मनो हितसम्भवाम्। भीष्म भीष्म महाबाहो शीघ्रं यत्नं कुरुश्व
en: Many car-warriors, Shalya and others soon came to his help. Getting up on another car and stretching his bow. Bhishma slowly advanced towards Shveta. In the meantime he heard a voice in the sky. It was celestial and fraught with his own good. It said, “O Bhishma, O Bhishma, O mighty armed hero, fight without losing a moment.

sn: एष ह्यस्य जये कालो निर्दिष्टो विश्वयोनिना। एतच्छ्रुत्वा तु वचनं देवदूतेन भाषितम्॥
en: This is the moment fixed by the creator for getting success over this one.” Having heard these words uttered by the celestial messenger.

sn: सम्प्रहृष्टमना भूत्वा वधे तस्य मनो दधे। विरथं रथिनां श्रेष्ठं श्वेतं दृष्ट्वा पदातिनम्॥ सहितास्त्वभ्यवर्तन्त परीप्सन्तो महारथाः। सात्यकिर्भीमसेनश्च धृष्टद्युम्नश्च पार्षतः॥
en: Bhishma carefully determined to kill Shveta. Seeing that foremost of car-warriors fighting on foot, many great car-warriors rushed untidily to his rescue. They were Satyaki, Bhimasena, and that descendant of Prishata, Dhrishtadyumna.

sn: कैकेयो धृष्टकेतुश्च अभिमन्युश्च वीर्यवान्। एतानापततः सर्वान् द्रोणशल्यकृपैः सह॥
en: The Kaikeya brothers, Dhrishtaketu and the greatly powerful Abhimanyu. Seeing them coming to his rescue, with Drona, Shalya, and Kripa.

sn: अवारयदमेयात्मा वारिवेगानिवाचलः। स निरुद्धेषु सर्वेषु पाण्डवेषु महात्मसु॥
en: That high-souled hero (Bhishma) stopped them all as a mountain resists the wind. When the illustrious warriors of the Pandava army were thus checked.

sn: श्वेतः खङ्गमथाकृष्य भीष्मस्य धनुराच्छिनत्। तदपास्य धनुश्छिन्नं त्वरमाणः पितामहः॥ देवदूतवचः श्रुत्वा वधे तस्य मनो दधे। ततः प्रचरमाणस्तु पिता देवव्रतस्तव॥
en: Shveta took up a sword and cut off Bhishma's bow. Throwing off that bow the (Kuru) grandfather having heard the words of the celestial messenger set his heart to destroy Shveta as soon as possible. Though baffled, your father Devavrata.

sn: अन्यत् कार्मुकमादाय त्वरमाणो महारथः। क्षणेन सज्यमकरोच्छक्रचापसमप्रभम्॥
en: That great car-warrior, soon took up another bow as effulgent as the bow of Indra. He stringed it in a moment.

sn: पिता ते भरतश्रेष्ठ श्वेतं दृष्ट्वा महारथैः। वृतं तं मनुजव्यार्भीमसेनपुरोगमैः॥
