en: Bhimsena blazed up in wrath like a fire fed with fuels. Then that best of charioteers, Ashoka, soon brought a car decked with gold, and he caused Bhima to mount upon it. Thereupon that chastiser of foes, the son of Kunti (Bhima) soon mounted on that car.

description: The death of the Kalinga king
sn: कालिङ्गमभिदुद्राव तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति चाब्रवीत्। ततः श्रुतायुर्बलवान् भीमाय निशिताशरान्॥ प्रेषयामास संक्रुद्धो दर्शयन् पाणिलाघवम्। स कार्मुकवरोत्सृष्टैर्नवभिर्निशितैः शरैः॥ समाहतो महाराज कालिङ्गेन महात्मना। संचुक्रुशे भृशं भीमो दण्डाहत इवोरगः॥
en: Then he rushed towards the Kalinga king, shouting “Wait” “Wait”. Then the greatly powerful Shrutayu, in great anger, shot at Bhima many sharp arrows and thus displayed his great lightness of hands. O king, thus wounded by those nine sharp arrows shot by the Kalinga king from his excellent bow, that great warrior Bhima blazed up in anger like a snake struck with a rod.

description: The death of the Kalinga king
sn: क्रुद्धश्च चापमायम्य बलवद् बलिनां वरः। कालिङ्गमवधीत् पार्थो भीमः सप्तभिरायसैः॥
en: Then that foremost of powerful men, that son of Pritha, Bhima in great anger drew his bow to its highest stretch, and killed the Kalinga king with seven iron arrows.

description: The death of the Kalinga king
sn: क्षुराभ्यां चक्ररक्षौ च कालिङ्गस्य महाबलौ। सत्यदेवं च सत्यं च प्राहिणोद् यमसादनम्॥
en: With two arrows he killed the two powerful protectors of his car-wheels; he also killed Satyadeva and Satya.

description: The death of the Kalinga king
sn: ततः पुरमेयात्मा नाराचैर्निशितैस्त्रिभिः। केतुमन्तं रणे भीमोऽगमयद् यमसादनम्॥
en: Thereupon high-souled Bhima then with many sharp arrows caused the destruction of Ketumat.

description: The death of the Kalinga king
sn: ततः कलिङ्गाः संनद्धा भीमसेनममर्षणम्। अनीकैर्बहुसाहस्रैः क्षत्रियाः समवारयन्॥
en: Thereupon the Kalinga warriors in great anger met the angry Bhimasena in battle backed by many thousands of combatants.

description: The death of the Kalinga king
sn: ततः शक्तिगदाखङ्गत्तोमरष्टिंपरश्वधैः। कलिङ्गाश्च ततो राजन् भीमसेनमवाकिरन्॥
en: O king, armed with darts and maces and swords and lances and scimitars and battleaxes, the Kalingas by hundreds and thousands surrounded Bhimasena.

description: The death of the Kalinga king
sn: संनिवार्य स तां घोरां शरवृष्टिं समुत्थिताम्। गदामादाय तरसा संनिपत्य महाबलः॥
en: Resisting that shower of arrows, that great warrior (Bhima) then took up his fearful mace. He then jumped down from his car in great speed.

description: The death of the Kalinga king
sn: भीमः सप्त शतान् वीराननयद् यमसादनम्। पुनश्चैव द्विसाहस्रान् कलिङ्गानरिमर्दनः॥ प्राहिणोन्मृत्युलोकाय तदद्भुतमिवाभवत्। एवं स तान्यनीकानि कलिङ्गानां पुनः पुनः॥ बिभेद समरे तूर्णं प्रेक्ष्य भीष्मं महारथम्। हतारोहाश्च मातङ्गाः पाण्डवेन कृता रणे॥ विप्रजग्मुरनीकेषु मेघा वातहता इव। मृद्गन्तः स्वान्यनीकानि विनदन्तः शरातुराः॥
en: Bhima then killed seven hundred heroes; that chastiser of foes then sent two thousand Kalingas to the region of Death. It was a wonderful feat; it was thus that the heroic and the fearfully strong Bhima again and again killed in that battle a very large number of the Kalingas. Elephants were deprived of their riders by that son of Pandu. Afflicted with arrows they roved about the field, treading down innumerable troops and uttering roars like those of the clouds.

description: The death of the Kalinga king
sn: ततो भीमो महाबाहुः खड्गहस्तो महाभुजः। सम्प्रहृष्टो महाघोषं शङ्ख प्राध्यापयद् बली॥
en: Then the mighty-armed Bhima with his sword in his hand blew in great delight his fearfully roaring conch.

description: The death of the Kalinga king
sn: सर्वकालिङ्गसैन्यानां मनांसि समकम्पयत्। मोहश्चापि कलिङ्गानामाविवेश परंतप॥
en: With that tremendous sound the hearts of the Kalinga troops began to tremble in fear. O chastiser of foes, the Kalingas appeared to have lost all consciousness.

description: The death of the Kalinga king
sn: प्राकम्पन्त च सैन्यानि वाहनानि च सर्वशः। भीमेन समरे राजन् गजेन्द्रेणेव सर्वशः॥ मार्गान् बहून् विचरता धावता च ततस्ततः। मुहुरुत्पतता चैव सम्मोहः समपद्यत॥ भीमसेनभयत्रस्तं सैन्यं च समकम्पत। क्षोभ्यमाणमसम्बाधं ग्राहेणेव महत् सरः॥
en: All the combatants and all the animals trembled in fear. By Bhimasena's roving about over the field of battle like an infuriated elephant, and by his frequent jumping up, a short of trance came over the foe. The whole Kalinga army trembled in fear like a large lake agitated by an alligator.

description: The death of the Kalinga king
sn: त्रासितेषु च सर्वेषु भीमेनाद्भुतकर्मणा। पुनरावर्तमानेषु विद्रवत्सु च सङ्घशः॥ सर्वकालिङ्गयोधेषु पाण्डूनां ध्वजिनीपतिः। अब्रवीत् स्वान्यनीकानि युध्यध्वमिति पार्षतः॥
en: Struck with panic, the Kalingas, fled away in all directions. When they were rallied again, the commander of the Pandava army (Dhrishtadyumna) then ordered his troops, exclaiming “fight”.

description: The death of the Kalinga king
sn: सेनापतिवचः श्रुत्वा शिखण्डिप्रमुखा गणाः। भीममेवाभ्यवर्तन्त रथानीकैः प्रहारिभिः॥
en: Having heard the word of their commander, many heroes headed by Shikhandin came to the help of Bhima, supported by many wellskilled car-warriors.

description: The death of the Kalinga king
sn: धर्मराजश्च तान् सर्वानुपजग्राह पाण्डवः। महता मेघवर्णेन नागानीकेन पृष्ठतः॥
en: The Pandava, king Yudhishthira Dharmaraja followed all of them behind with a large force of elephants, each of the colour of clouds.

description: The death of the Kalinga king
sn: एवं संनोद्य सर्वाणि स्वान्यनीकानि पार्षतः। भीमसेनस्य जग्राह पाणिं सत्पुरुषैर्वृतः ॥
en: Thus urging all his troops, the Prishata prince surrounded by many great warriors went to protect one of the wings of Bhima's troops.

description: The death of the Kalinga king
sn: न हि पञ्चालराजस्य लोके कश्चन विद्यते। भीमसात्यकयोरन्यः प्राणेभ्यः प्रियकृत्तमः॥
en: To the Panchala prince, there was none dearer than life on earth except Satyaki and Bhima.

description: The death of the Kalinga king
sn: सोऽपश्यच्च कलिङ्गेषु चरन्तमरिसूदनः । भीमसेनं महाबाहुं पार्षतः परवीरहा॥
en: That slayer of hostile heroes, the Prishata prince saw that chastiser of foes the mightyarmed Bhimasena fighting among the Kalingas.

description: The death of the Kalinga king
sn: ननर्द बहुधा राजन् हृष्टश्चासीत् परंतपः। शङ्ख दध्मौ च समरे सिंहनादं ननाद च॥
en: O chastiser of foes, O king. He sent forth many loud shouts and filled all his troops with delight. He blew his conch and uttered a lion like roar.

description: The death of the Kalinga king
sn: स च पारावताश्वस्य रथे हेमपरिष्कृते। कोविदारध्वजं दृष्ट्वा भीमसेनः समाश्वसत्॥
en: Seeing the red standard of Dhrishtadyumna's car decked with gold and yoked with milk white steeds, Bhimasena became much encouraged.

description: The death of the Kalinga king
sn: धृष्टद्युम्नस्तु तं दृष्ट्वा कलिङ्गैः समभिद्रुतम्। भीमसेनममेयात्मा त्राणायाजो समभ्ययात्॥
en: The high-souled, Dhrishtadyumna, seeing Bhimasena attacked by the innumerable Kalingas rushed to his rescue.

description: The death of the Kalinga king
sn: तौ दृष्ट्वा दृष्टद्युम्नवृकोदरौ। कलिङ्गान् समरे वीरौ योधयेतां मनस्विनौ॥
en: Seeing Satyaki at a distance, those two greatly powerful heroes Dhrishtadyumna and Vrikodara furiously fell upon the Kalingas.

description: The death of the Kalinga king
sn: स तत्र गत्वा शैनेयो जवेन जयतां वरः। पार्थपार्षतयोः पाणिं जग्राह पुरुषर्षभः॥ दूरात् सात्यकि
en: The foremost of men, the descendant of (Shini), that best of all warriors (Satyaki) also soon came to the spot and defended the wings of both Bhima and the Prishata prince.

description: The death of the Kalinga king
sn: स कृत्वा दारुणं कर्म प्रगृहीतशरासनः। आस्थितो रौद्रमात्मानं कलिङ्गानन्ववैक्षत॥
en: With his big bow in his hand, he created a great havoc. Making himself fierce in the extreme, he began to kill the enemy.

description: The death of the Kalinga king
sn: कलिङ्गप्रभवां चैव मांसशोणितकर्दमाम्। रुधिरस्यन्दिनीं तत्र भीमः प्रावर्तयन्नदीम्॥
en: Bhima caused a river of blood to flow, it was made of the flesh and blood of the Kalingas.

description: The death of the Kalinga king
sn: अन्तरेण कलिङ्गानां पाण्डवानां च वाहिनीम्। तां संततार दुस्तारां भीमसेनो महाबलः॥
en: Bhimasena crossed the inaccessible blood river flowing between Kalinga and arıny of Pandavas by virtue of his unique valour.

description: The death of the Kalinga king
sn: भीमसेनं तथा दृष्ट्वा प्राक्रोशंस्तावका नृप। कालोऽयं भीमरूपेण कलिङ्गैः सह युध्यते॥
en: O king, seeing Bhima in this fearful fight, all the troops exclaimed, “This one who is fighting in Bhima's shape with the Kalingas is Yama himself".

description: The death of the Kalinga king
sn: ततः शान्तनवो भीष्मः श्रुत्वा तं निनदं रणे। अभ्ययात् त्वरितो भीमं व्यूढानीकः समन्ततः॥
en: Having heard their cries, the son of Shantanu, Bhishma, surrounded on all sides by many warriors, soon came to Bhima.

description: The death of the Kalinga king
sn: तं सात्यकिर्भीमसेनो धृष्टद्युम्नश्च पार्षतः। अभ्यद्रवन्त भीष्मस्य रथं हेमपरिष्कृतम्॥
en: Thereupon Satyaki, Bhima, and the Prishata prince Dhrishtadyumna all rushed towards Bhishma's car decked with gold.

description: The death of the Kalinga king
sn: परिवार्य तु ते सर्वे गाडेयं तरसा रणे। त्रिभिस्त्रिभिः शरैोरैर्भीष्ममान रोजसा॥
en: All of them soon surrounded the son of Ganga. Without losing a moment they wounded Bhishma each with three fearful arrows.

description: The death of the Kalinga king
sn: प्रत्यविध्यत तान् सर्वान् पिता देवव्रतस्तव। यतमानान् महेष्वासांस्त्रिभिस्त्रिभिरजिह्मगैः॥
en: Your father Devavrata, wounded each of these mighty bowmen with three straight arrows in return.

description: The death of the Kalinga king
sn: ततः शरसहस्रेण संनिवार्य महारथान्। हयान् काञ्चनसंनाहान् भीमस्य न्यहनच्छरैः॥
en: Having checked those mighty car-warriors with thousands of arrows, he killed with his arrows the horses of Bhima clad in golden armour.

description: The death of the Kalinga king
sn: हताश्वे स रथे तिष्ठन् भीमसेनः प्रतापवान्। शक्तिं चिक्षेप तरसा गाङ्गेयस्य रं प्रति॥
en: The greatly strong Bhima however stood on the car, the horses of which were killed. He then with great force hurled a dart at Bhishma.

description: The death of the Kalinga king
sn: अप्राप्तामथ तां शक्तिं पिता देवव्रतस्तव। त्रिधा चिच्छेद समरे सा पृथिव्यामशीर्यत॥
en: Your father Devavrata cut off in that battle that dart before it could reach his car. It then fell in fragments on the grounds.

description: The death of the Kalinga king
sn: ततः शैक्यायसी गुर्वी प्रगृह्य बलवान् गदाम्। भीमसेनस्ततस्तूर्णं पुप्लुवे मनुजर्षभ॥
en: Then that foremost of men, Bhimasena took up a heavy and might mace made of Saikya iron. He then jumped down from his car.

description: The death of the Kalinga king
sn: सात्यकोऽपि ततस्तूर्णं भीमस्य प्रियकाम्यया। गाङ्गेयसारथिं तूर्णं पातयामास सायकैः॥
en: Satyaki however, in order to do what is agreeable to Bhima, cut down with his arrows the charioteer of the revered Kuru grandfather.

description: The death of the Kalinga king
sn: भीष्मस्तु निहते तस्मिन् सारथौ रथिनां वरः। वातायमानैस्तैरश्वैरपनीतो रणाजिरात्॥
en: When his charioteer was thus killed, that foremost of car-warriors Bhishma was borne away from the battle field by his horses which ran with the speed of wind.

description: The death of the Kalinga king
sn: भीमसेनस्ततो राजन्नपयाते महाव्रते। प्रजज्वाल यथा वह्निर्दहन् कक्षमिवैधित॥
en: O king, when that great car-warrior was thus carried away from the field of battle, Bhima blazed up like a great fire when it consumes dry grass.

description: The death of the Kalinga king
sn: स हत्वा सर्वकालिङ्गान् सेनामध्ये व्यतिष्ठता नैनमभ्युत्सहन् केचित् तावका भरतर्षभ॥
en: Having killed all the Kalingas, O best of the Bharata race, he stood in the midst of the troops, and none dared to withstand him.

description: The death of the Kalinga king
sn: धृष्टद्युम्नस्तमारोप्य स्वरथे रथिनां वरः। पश्यतां सर्वसैन्यानामपोवाह यशस्विनम्॥
en: But Dhrishtadyumna soon took up that foremost of car warriors on his own car. He then took away that illustrious hero in the sight of all the warriors.

description: The death of the Kalinga king
sn: सम्पूज्यमानः पाञ्चाल्यैर्मत्स्यैश्च भरतर्षभ। धृष्टद्युम्नं परिष्वज्य समेयादथ सात्यकिम्॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, praised by the Pandavas and the Matsyas, he embraced Dhrishtadyumna and then went to Satyaki.

description: The death of the Kalinga king
sn: अथाब्रवीद् भीमसेनं सात्यकिः सत्यविक्रमः। प्रहर्षयन् यदुव्याघ्रो धृष्टद्युम्नस्य पश्यतः॥
en: That foremost of the Yadus, that irresistible hero Satyaki then thus spoke to Bhimasena in the presence of Dhrishtadyumna.

description: The death of the Kalinga king
sn: दिष्ट्या कलिङ्गराजश्च राजपुत्रश्च केतुमान्। शक्रदेवश्च कालिङ्गः कलिङ्गाश्च मृधे हताः॥
en: By good luck the Kalinga king, also the Kalinga prince Ketumat and also Shakradeva of that country and also all the Kalingas have been killed, you in this battle.

description: The death of the Kalinga king
sn: स्वबाहुबलवीर्येण नागाश्वरथसंकुलः। महापुरुषभूयिष्ठो धीरयोधनिषेवितः॥ महाव्यूहः कलिङ्गानामेकेन मृदितस्त्वया।
en: The army of the Kalingas, consisting of many thousands of cars, elephants, horses, noble warriors and heroic combatants, has been destroyed by your prowess of arm alone.

description: The death of the Kalinga king
sn: एवमुक्त्वा शिनेर्नप्ता दीर्घबाहुररिंदम्॥ रथाद् रथमभिद्रुत्य पर्यष्वजत पाण्डवम्। ततः स्वरथमास्थाय पुनरेव महारथः। तावकानवधीत् क्रुद्धो भीमस्य बलमादधत्॥
en: Having said this, the mighty-armed grandson of Shini the chastiser of foes embraced the son of Pandu (Bhima). He then quickly got upon his car. Then that great carwarrior began to kill the troops in anger, thus strengthening the hands of Bhima.

sn: संजय उवाच गतपूर्वाह्नभूयिष्ठे तस्मिन्नहनि भारत। रथनागाश्वपत्तीनां सादिनां च महाक्षये॥
en: Sanjaya said O descendant of Bharata when that day passed away, when the destruction of car, elephants, horses, foot-soldiers and horsemen went apace.

sn: द्रोणपुत्रेण शल्येन कृपेण च महात्मना। समसज्जत पाञ्चाल्यस्तरिभिरेतैर्महारथैः॥
en: The Panchala prince fought with Drona's son (Ashvathama), Shalya, and the illustrious Kripa.

sn: स लोकविदितानश्वान् निजघान महाबलः। द्रौणे: पाञ्चालदायादः शितैर्दशभिराशुगैः॥
en: The mighty heir-apparent of the king of Panchala with many sharp arrows killed the horses of Drona's who is celebrated all over the world.

sn: ततः शल्यरथं तूर्णमास्थाय हतवाहनः। द्रौणिः पाञ्चालदायादमभ्यवर्षदथेषुभिः॥
en: Deprived of his horses, Drona's son soon got upon the car of Shalya and showered his arrows on the Panchala prince.

sn: धृष्टद्युम्नं तु संयुक्तं द्रौणिना वीक्ष्य भारत। सौभद्रोऽभ्यपतत् तूर्णं विकिरन् निशिताशरान्॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, seeing Dhrishtadyumna fighting with Drona's son, the son of Subhadra (Abhimanyu) ran up showering his fearful arrows.

sn: स शल्यं पञ्चविंशत्या कृपं च नवभिः शरैः। अश्वत्थामानमष्टाभिर्विव्याध पुरुषर्षभः॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, he wounded Shalya with twenty-five arrows and Kripa with nine arrows and Ashvathama with eight.

sn: आर्जुनि तु ततस्तूर्णं द्रौणिविव्याध पत्रिणा। शल्योऽथ दशभिश्चैव कृपश्च निशितैस्त्रिभिः॥
en: Drona's son also soon wounded Arjuna's son with many winged arrows; Shalya also pierced him with twelve arrows, Kripa shot at him three sharp arrows.

sn: लक्ष्मणस्तव पौत्रस्तु सौभद्रं समवस्थितम्। अभ्यवर्तत संहृष्टस्ततो युद्धमवर्तत॥
en: Your grandson Lakshmana then rushed at Subhadra's son in anger, and a fearful battle began between the two.

sn: दौर्योधनिः सुसंक्रुद्धः सौभद्रं परवीरहा। विव्याध समरे राजस्तदद्भुतमिवाभवत्॥
en: In that fight Duryodhana's son in anger wounded Subhadra's son with many sharp arrows. O king, it was a wonderful feat.

sn: अभिमन्युः सुसंक्रुद्धो भ्रातरं भरतर्षभ। शरैः पञ्चाशतै राजन् क्षिप्रहस्तोऽभ्यविध्यत॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, the light-handed Abhimanyu, also being very much enraged, soon wounded his cousin with five hundred arrows.

sn: लक्ष्मणोऽपि पुनस्तस्य धनुश्चिच्छेद पत्रिणा। मुष्टिदेशे महाराज ततस्ते चुक्रुशुर्जनाः॥
en: O king, Lakshmana also with his arrows cut down (his adversary's) bow staff, on seeing which all the troops sent up a loud shout.

sn: तद् विहाय धनुश्छिन्नं सौभद्रः परवीरहा। अन्यदादत्तवांश्चित्रं कार्मुकं वेगवत्तरम्॥
en: Then that slayer of hostile heroes, Subhadara's son, throwing aside the broken bow, took up another beautiful and tough bow.

sn: तौ तत्र समरे युक्तौ कृतप्रतिकृतैषिणौ। अन्योन्यं विशिखैस्तीक्ष्णैर्जघ्नतुः पुरुषर्षभौ॥
en: Thereupon those two foremost of men, thus fighting together with the desire of counteracting each other's feat, wounded each other with innumerable sharp arrows.

sn: ततो दुर्योधनो राजा दृष्ट्वा पुत्रं महारथम्। पीडितं तव पौत्रेण प्रायात् तत्र प्रजेश्वरः॥
en: O king, Duryodhana on seeing his mighty son thus hard pressed by your grand son ran towards the spot.

sn: संनिवृत्ते तव सुते सर्व एव जनाधिपाः। आणुनि रथवंशेन समन्तात् पर्यवारयन्॥
en: When your son went to the spot, all the kings surrounded Arjuna's son with many thousands of cars.

sn: स तैः परिवृतः शूरैः शूरो युधि सुदुर्जयैः। न स्म प्रव्यथते राजन् कृष्णतुल्यपराक्रमः॥
en: O king, being as invincible and powerful as Krishna himself, that hero, being thus surrounded by those heroes, was not the least agitated.

sn: सौभद्रमथ संसक्तं दृष्ट्वा तत्र धनंजयः। अभिदुद्राव वेगेन त्रातुकामः स्वमात्मजम्॥
en: Seeing Subhadra's fighting, Dhananjaya (Arjuna) hastened to the spot in great anger, with the intention of rescuing his son son.

sn: ततः सरथनागाश्वा भीष्मद्रोणपुरोगमाः। अभ्यवर्तन्त राजानः सहिताः सव्यसाचिनम्॥
en: Thereupon the kings headed by Bhishma and Drona and accompanied by many elephants, horses and cars rushed with great force on Savyasachin (Arjuna).

sn: उद्भूतं सहसा भौमं नागाश्वरथपत्तिभिः। दिवाकररथं प्राप्य रजस्तीव्रमदृश्यत॥
en: Then a thick shower of dust, being raised by foot-soldiers, horses and cars and cavalrymen, covered the sky.

sn: तानि नागसहस्राणि भूमिपालशतानि च। तस्य बाणपथं प्राप्य नाभ्यवर्तन्त सर्वशः॥
en: When those thousands of elephants and hundreds of kings came within the reach of scen Arjuna's arrows, they could not make any further advance.

sn: प्रणेदुः सर्वभूतानि बभूवुस्तिमिरा दिशः। कुरूणां चानयस्तीव्रः समदृश्यत दारुणः॥
en: All the troops sent up loud shouts, and all directions became dark. Then the army of the Kurus assumed a fearful and dreadful aspect.

sn: नाप्यन्तरिक्षं न दिशो न भूमिर्न च भास्करः। प्रजज्ञे भरतश्रेष्ठं शस्त्रसङ्घः किरीटिनः॥
en: Neither the sky, nor the sun, nor the cardinal points, nor the earth, O best of men, could be distinguished, in consequence of the continuous showers of arrows shot by Kiritin (Arjuna).

sn: सादिता रथनागाश्च हताश्वा रथिनो रणे। विप्रदुतरथाः केचिद् दृश्यन्ते रथयूथपाः॥
en: Many clephants were deprived of their standards, and many car-warriors were also deprived of their horses. Having abandoned their cars, many car-warriors were wandering (over the field).

sn: विस्था रथिनश्चान्ये धावमानाः समन्ततः। तत्र तत्रैव दृश्यन्ते सायुधाः साङ्गदैर्भुजैः॥
en: Many other car-warriors, deprived of their cars, were seen to rove about with their weapons in their hands and other arm adorned with Angadas.

sn: हयारोहा हयांस्त्यक्त्वा गजारोहाश्च दन्तिनः। अर्जुनस्य भयाद् राजन् समन्ताद् विप्रदुद्रुवुः॥
en: O king, horsemen, urging their horses and elephant-men urging their elephants fled away in all directions from the fear of Arjuna.

sn: रथे यश्च गजेभ्यश्च हयेभ्यश्च नराधिपाः। पतिताः पात्यमानाश्च दृश्यन्तेऽर्जुनसायकैः॥
en: Kings were seen falling from their cars; elephants and horses were also seen to fall cut down by Arjuna's arrows.

sn: सगदानुद्यतान् बाहून् सखगांश्च विशाम्पते। सप्रासांश्च सतूणीरान् सशरान् शसरासनान्॥ साङ्कुशान् सपताकांश्च तत्र तत्रार्जुनो नृणाम्। निचकर्त शरैरुचै रौद्रं वपुरधारयत्॥
en: Assuming a fierce countenance, Arjuna cut down with fearful arrows the upraised arms of warriors with maces in their hands, also with swords, darts, quivers arrows, bows, hooks and standards.

sn: परिघाणां प्रदीप्तानां मुद्गराणां च मारिष। प्रासानां भिन्दिपालानां निस्त्रिंशानां च संयुगे॥ परश्वधानां तीक्ष्णानां तोमराणां च भारत। वर्मणां चापविद्धानां काञ्चनानां च भूमिप॥ ध्वजानां चर्मणां चैव व्यजनानां च सर्वशः। छत्राणां हेमदण्डानां तोमराणां च भारत॥ प्रतोदानां च योक्त्राणां कशानां चैव मारिष। राशय: स्मात्र दृश्यन्ते विनिकीर्णा रणक्षितौ॥
en: O sire, O descendant of Bharata, spiked mace broken in fragment, mallets, bearded darts, short arrows, swords, sharp edged battle axes, lances, broken shields, armours, standards, every sort of weapons, umbrellas with golden staves, iron-hooks, goads, whips, and traces were all seen strewn over the field of battle in heaps.

sn: नासीत् तत्र पुमान् कश्चित् तव सैन्यस्य भारत। योऽर्जुनं समरे शूरं प्रत्युद्यायात् कथंचन॥
en: O sire, there was none in your army who could advance against Arjuna in battle.

sn: यो यो हि समरे पार्थं प्रत्युद्याति विशाम्पते। स संख्ये विशिखैस्तीक्ष्णैः परलोकाय नीयते॥
en: O king, whoever advanced against the son of Pritha, was immediately shot down and sent to the abode of Yama.

sn: तेषु विद्रवमाणेषु तव योधेषु सर्वशः। अर्जुनो वासुदेवश्च दध्मतुर्वारिजोत्तमौ॥
en: When all your troops broke down and fled away, Arjuna and Vasudeva blew their excellent conchs.

sn: तत् प्रभग्नं बलं दृष्ट्वा पिता देवव्रतस्तव। अब्रवीत् समरे शूरं भारद्वाजं स्मयन्निव॥
en: Your sire Devavrata then, on seeing the Kuru army routed, smilingly thus spoke to the heroic son of Bharadvaja (Drona) on that field of battle.

sn: एष पाण्डुसुतो वीरः कृष्णेन सहितो बली। तथा करोति सैन्यानि यथा कुर्याद् धनंजयः॥
en: “This mighty and heroic son of Pandu Dhananjaya, accompanied as he is by Krishna, is treating our troops as he alone is able to deal with them.

sn: न ह्येष समरे शक्यो विजेतुं हि कथंचन। यथास्य दृश्यते रूपं कालान्तकयमोपमम्॥
en: Seeing him resemble today the destroyer himself as the universal dissolution, we find that he is invincible today.

sn: न निवर्तयितुं चापि शक्येयं महती चमूः। अन्योन्यप्रेक्षया पश्य द्रवतीयं वरूथिनी॥
en: This our vast army is now impossible to be rallied. Behold, loO king at me, they are running away.

sn: एष चास्तं गिरिश्रेष्ठं भानुमान् प्रतिपद्यते। चढूंषि सर्वलोकस्य संहरन्निव सर्वथा॥
en: Sun god here has reached now at the best mountain Astacala as if contracting completely the eye-sight of the entire world,

sn: तत्रावहारं सम्प्राप्तं मन्येऽहं पुरुषर्षभ। श्रान्ता भीताश्च नो योधा न योत्स्यन्ति कंथचन॥
en: O foremost of men, I think, the time has come now to withdraw our army. The troops will never fight, they are tired and struck with panic".

sn: एवमुक्त्वा ततो भीष्मो द्रोणमाचार्यसत्तमम्। अवहारमथो चक्रे तावकानां महारथः॥ ततोऽवहारः सैन्यानां तव तेषां च भारत। अस्तं गच्छति सूर्येऽभूत् संध्याकाले च वर्तति॥
en: Having said this to Drona that foremost of all preceptors, that great car-warriors Bhishma withdrew his army. Then when the sun went down, O sire, both the armies were withdrawn and twilight came in.

sn: संजय उवाच प्रभातायां च शर्वर्या भीष्मः शान्तनवस्तदा। अनीकान्यनुसंयाने व्यादिदेशाथ भारत॥
en: Sanjaya said When night passed away and morning dawned, the son of Shantanu Bhishma, therefore grand-sire of the Kurus gave the order for the Kuru army to be ready for fight.

sn: गारुडं च महाव्यूह चक्रे शान्तनवस्तदा। पुत्राणां ते जयाकाङ्क्षी भीष्मः कुरुपितामहः॥
en: The chastiser of foes, the son of Shantanu, with the desire to win victory for your son then formed that great Vyuha called Garuda.

sn: गरुडस्य स्वयं तुण्डे पिता देवव्रतस्तव। चक्षुषी च भरद्वाजः कृतवर्मा च सात्वतः॥
en: On the back of that Garuda (the king of the bird) your father Devavrata himself stood. Its two eyes were made by the son of Bharadvaja (Drona) and the Satvata Kritvarma.

sn: अश्वत्थामा कृपश्चैव शीर्षमास्तां यशस्विनौ। त्रैगर्तेरथ कैकेयैर्वाटधानैश्च संयुगे॥
en: Those two illustrious heroes, Ashvathama and Kripa, backed by the Trigartas, the Matsyas, the Kaikeyas and the Vatadhanas stood at its head.

sn: भूरिश्वराः शलः शल्यो भगदत्तश्च मारिष। मद्रकाः सिन्धुसौवीरास्तथा पाञ्चनदाश्च ये॥ जयद्रथेन सहिता ग्रीवायां संनिवेशिताः। पृष्ठे दुर्योधनो राजा सोदर्यैः सानुगैर्वृतः॥
en: O sire, Bhurishravas, Shala, Shala, Shalya Bhagadatta, the Madra, the Sindhusauviras, the Panchanadas with Jayadratha stood at its neck. At its back stood king Duryodhana with all his followers.

sn: विन्दानुविन्दावावन्त्यौ काम्बोजाश्च शकैः सह। पुच्छमासन् महाराज शूरसेनाश्च सर्वशः॥
en: O great king, Vinda and Anuvinda of Avanti, the Kambojas with the Shakas and also the Shurasenas formed its tail.

sn: मागधाश्च कलिङ्गाश्च दासेरकगणैः सह। दक्षिणं पक्षमासाद्य स्थिता व्यूहस्य दंशिताः॥
en: The Magadhas the Kalingas with all the Daserakas clad in armour, formed the right wing of that Vyuha.

sn: कारुषाश्च विकुञ्जाश्च मुण्डाः कुण्डीवृषास्तथा। बृहद्बलेन सहिता वाम पार्श्वमवस्थिताः॥
en: The Karushas, the Vikunjas, the Mundas, the Kundivrishas, with Brihadbala formed its left wing.

sn: व्यूढं दृष्ट्वा तु तत् सैन्यं सव्यसाची परंतपः। धृष्टद्युम्नेन सहितः प्रत्यव्यूहत संयुगे॥ अर्धचन्द्रेण व्यूहेन व्यूहं तमतिदारुणम्।
en: That chastiser of foes, Savyasachi (Arjuna) seeing the enemy's troops formed into a Vyuha, with the assistance of Dhrishtadyumna formed his troops into a counter Vyuha. In oppositior of your Vyuha, that son of Pandu formed a Vyuha after the shape of the halfmoon.

sn: दक्षिणं शृङ्गमास्थाय भीमसेनो व्यरोचत॥ नानाशस्त्रौघसम्पन्नै नादेश्यैर्नृपैर्वृतः।
en: On its right side stood stood Bhimasena surrounded by kings of various countries all abundantly provided with arrows.

sn: तदन्वेव विराटश्च द्रुपदश्च महारथः॥ तदनन्तरमेवासीन्नीलो नीलायुधैः सह।
en: Next to him stood those two great carwarriors Virata and Drupada; next to them was Nila armed with poisonous weapons.

sn: नीलादनन्तरश्चैव धृष्टकेतुर्महाबलः॥ चेदिकाशिकरूपैश्च पौरवैरपि संवृतः।
en: Next to Nila stood the great car-warrior Dhrishtakelu backed by the Chedis the Kashis, the Karushas and the Pandavas.

sn: धृष्टद्युम्नः शिखण्डी च पञ्चालाश्च प्रभद्रकाः॥ मध्ये सैन्यस्य महतः स्थिता युद्धाय भारत।
en: Dhrishtadyumna with Shikhandin with the Panchalas and the Prabhadraka and also with other troops stood in the middle.

sn: तत्रैव धर्मराजोऽपि गजानीकेन संवृतः॥ ततस्तु सात्यकी राजन् द्रौपद्याः पञ्चचात्मजाः।
en: Dharmaraja Yudhishthira was also there surrounded by his innumerable elephants. Next to them, O king, stood Satyaki and the five sons of Draupadi.

sn: अभिमन्युस्ततः शूर इरावांश्च ततः परम्॥ भैमसेनिस्ततो राजन् केकयाश्च महारथाः।
en: Next to them was Abhimanyu and then Iravana. Next to Iravana was Bhimasena's son (Ghatotkacha) with the great Kaikeya carwarriors.

sn: ततोऽभूद् द्विपदां श्रेष्ठो वामं पार्श्वमुपाश्रितः॥ सर्वस्य जगतो गोप्ता गोप्ता यस्य जनार्दनः।
en: Next to them, on the left side, was that foremost of men, Arjuna who had as his protector Janardana (Krishna) the protector of the whole universe.

sn: एवमेतं महाव्यूह प्रत्यव्यूहन्त पाण्डवाः॥ वधार्थं तव पुत्राणां तत्पक्षं ये च सङ्गताः।
en: It was thus the Pandavas formed their Vyuha for the destruction of your sons and those who have taken your side.

sn: ततः प्रववृते युद्धं व्यतिपक्तरथद्विपम्॥ तावकानां परेषां च निजतामितरेतरम्।
en: Then commenced the battle between your troops and the foes; all struck at one another; elephants and cars mixed up in one confusion.

sn: हयौघाश्च रथौघाश्च तत्र तत्र विशाम्पते॥ सम्पतन्तो व्यदृश्यन्त निघ्नन्तस्ते परस्परम्।
en: O king, innumerable elephants and cars were seen everywhere. They rushed upon one another for the purpose of slaughter.

sn: धावतां च रथौघानां निघ्नतां च पृथक् पृथक्॥ बभूव तुमुलः शब्दो विमिश्रो दुन्दुभिस्वनैः।
en: The rattle of innumerable car-wheels mingled with the beat of drums created a tremendous din.

sn: दिवस्पृङ् नरवीराणां निघ्नतामितरेतरम्। सम्प्रहारे सुतुमुले तव तेषां च भारत॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, the shouts of the heroic combatants of your army and those of your enemies when killing one another, reached the very heavens.

description: Commencement of the third day's battle
sn: संजय उवाच ततो व्यूढेष्वनीकेषु तावकेषु परेषु च। धनंजयो स्थानीकमवधीत् तव भारत॥ शरैरतिरथो युद्धे दारयन् रथयूथपान्। ते वध्यमानाः पार्थेन कालेनेव युगक्षय॥ धार्तराष्ट्रा रणे यत्नात् पाण्डवान् प्रत्ययोधयन्। प्रार्थयाना यशो दीप्तं मृत्युं कृत्वा निवर्तनम्॥ एकाग्रमनसो भूत्वा पाण्डवानां वरूथिनीम्। बभञ्जुर्बहुशो राजंस्ते चासज्जन्त संयुगे॥
en: Sanjaya said When your troops and those of the Pandavas were placed in battle array, that great car-warrior Dhananjaya made a great slaughter by cutting down with his arrows many leaders of car-warriors; your troops though thus slaughtered in the battle by the son of Pritha who resembled the destroyer himself at the end of a Yuga, yet fought with the Pandavas with perseverance. Desiring to win blazing glory and making death their final goal with minds undirected to anything else, they broke the Pandava ranks in many places, but their ranks also were in many places broken.

description: Commencement of the third day's battle
sn: द्रवद्भिरथ भग्नैश्च परिवर्तद्भिरेव च। पाण्डवैः कौरवेयैश्च न प्राज्ञायत किंचन॥
en: Then both the Kuru and the Pandava army broke and fled away. Nothing could then be distinguished.

description: Commencement of the third day's battle
sn: उदतिष्ठद् रजो भौमं छादयानं दिवाकरम्। न दिशः प्रदिशो वापि तत्र हन्युः कथं नराः॥
en: A thick cloud of dust rose covering the sun. No body could distinguish any of the cardinal points.

description: Commencement of the third day's battle
sn: अनुमानेन संज्ञाभिर्नामगोत्रैश्च संयुगे। वर्तते च तथा युद्धं तत्र तत्र विशाम्पते॥
en: O king, everywhere the battle raged the combatants were guided only by the indications afforded by colours, by watchwords, by names and by tribal distinctions.

description: Commencement of the third day's battle
sn: न व्यूहो भिद्यते तत्र कौरवाणां कथंचन। रक्षितः सत्यसंधेन भारद्वाजेन संयुगे॥
en: O sire, O king, the Vyuha protected as it was by the son of Bharadvaja (Drona) could by no means be broken.

description: Commencement of the third day's battle
sn: तथैव पाण्डवानां च रक्षितः सव्यसाचिना। नाभिद्यत महाव्यूहो भीमेन च सुरक्षितः॥
en: So did the formidable Pandava Vyuha remain unbroken, protected as it was by Savyasachi (Arjuna), and well-guarded by Bhima.

description: Commencement of the third day's battle
sn: सेनाग्रादपि निष्पत्य प्रायुध्यस्तत्र मानवाः। उभयोः सेनयो राजन् व्यतिषक्तरथद्विपाः॥
en: O king, the cars and the elephants of both the armies and other combatants came out of their respective arrays and engaged in the fight.

description: Commencement of the third day's battle
sn: हयारोहैर्हयारोहाः पात्यन्ते स्म महाहवे। ऋष्टिभिविमलाभिश्च प्रासैरपि च संयुगे॥
en: In that fearful battle, horse-men cut down horsemen with sharp and polished swords and long lances.

description: Commencement of the third day's battle
sn: रथी रथिनमासाद्य शरैः कनकभूषणैः। पातयामास समरे तस्मिन्नतिभयङ्करे।।१२
en: Car-warriors getting car-warriors within reach cut them down with their arrows decked with golden wings.

description: Commencement of the third day's battle
sn: गजारोहा गजारोहान् नाराचशरतोमरैः। संसक्तान् पातयामासुस्तव तेषां च सर्वशः॥
en: The elephant riders in your own army and in the army of Pandavas' destroyed the elephant riders of rival party in counter by blowing sharp Naracha, arrows and tomaras from all sides (viz. mutually they killed themselves).

description: Commencement of the third day's battle
sn: पत्तिसङ्घा रणे पत्तीन् भिन्दिपालपरश्वधैः। न्यपातयन्त संहृष्टाः परस्परकृतागसः॥
en: Innumerable foot-soldiers angrily and at the same time cheerfully cut down one another with short arrows and battle axes.

description: Commencement of the third day's battle
sn: रथी च समरे राजन्नासाद्य गजयूथपम्। सगजं पातयामास गजी च रथिनां वरम्॥
en: O king, car-warriors, getting elephants riders within reach cut them down with the elephants. elephants riders also cut down carwarriors.

description: Commencement of the third day's battle
sn: रथिनं च हयारोहः प्रासेन भरतर्षभ। पातयामास समरे रथी च हयसादिनम्॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, horse-men with their lances cut down car-warriors in that battle; car-warriors also cut down horse-men.

description: Commencement of the third day's battle
sn: पदाती रथिनं संख्ये रथी चापि पदातिनम्। न्यपातयच्छितैः शस्त्रैः सेनयोरुभयोरपि॥
en: In both the armies, foot-soldiers cut down many car-warriors, many car-warriors cut down innumcrable foot-soldiers with their sharp weapons.

description: Commencement of the third day's battle
sn: गजारोहा हयारोहान् पातयाञ्चक्रिरे तदा। हयारोहा गजस्थांश्च तदद्भुतमिवाभवत्॥ गजारोहवरैश्चापि तत्र तत्र पदातयः। पातिताः समदृश्यन्त तैश्चापि गजयोधिनः॥
en: Elephant-riders cut down horse-men and horse-men cut down warriors who were on the back of elephants; every thing appeared to be exceedingly wonderful. Foot soldiers were seen to be cut down by the foremost of elephant-riders and the elephant-riders were also to be seen cut down by the foot-soldiers.

description: Commencement of the third day's battle
sn: पत्तिसङ्घा हयारोहैः सादिसङ्घाश्च पत्तिभिः। पात्यमाना व्यदृश्यन्त शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः॥
en: It has been seen there that innumerable foot-soldiers were cut down by horse-riders and horse-riders cut down foot-soldiers,

description: Commencement of the third day's battle
sn: ध्वजैस्तत्रापविद्धैश्च कार्मुकैस्तोमरैस्तथा। प्रासैस्तथा गदाभिश्च परिघैः कम्पनैस्तथा॥ शक्तिभिः कवचैश्चित्रैः कणपैरङ्कुशैरपि। निस्त्रीशैविमलैश्चापि स्वर्णपुङ्खैः शरैस्तथा।॥ परिस्तोमैः कुथाभिश्च कम्बलैश्च महाधनैः। भूति भरतश्रेष्ठ स्रग्दामैरिव चित्रिता॥
en: O best of the Bharata race! the battle field, strewn with broken standards bow, lances, housings of elephants, costly blankets, bearded darts, maces, clubs with iron spikes, Kampanas, various sorts of armours, arrows with golden wings, looked as if it were covered with garlands of flowers.

description: Commencement of the third day's battle
sn: नराश्वकायैः पतितैर्दन्तिभिश्च महाहवे। अगम्यरूपा पृथिवी मांसशोणितकर्दमा॥
en: The ground becoming muddy with flesh and blood, became impassable with the bodies of men, horses and elephants, that were killed in that fearful battle.

description: Commencement of the third day's battle
sn: प्रशशाम रजो भौमं व्युक्षितं रणशोणितैः। दिशश्च विमलाः सर्वाः सम्बभूवुर्जनेश्वर॥
en: O majesty! The dust on the upper surface of earth was stuck to layer on being soaked in blood flown in that battle-field. On being this, all directions became clearly visible.

description: Commencement of the third day's battle
sn: उस्थितान्यगणेयानि कबधानि समन्ततः। चिह्नभूतानि जगतो विनाशार्थाय भारत॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, innumerable headless bodies were seen rising from the ground, an omen to indicate that the destruction of the world is near.

description: Commencement of the third day's battle
sn: तस्मिन् युद्धे महारौद्रे वतमाने सुदारुणे। प्रत्यदृश्यन्त रथिनो धावमानाः समन्ततः॥ ततो भीष्मश्च द्रोणश्च सैन्धवश्च जयद्रथः। पुरुमित्रो जयो भोजः शल्यश्चापि ससौबलः॥ एते समरदुर्धर्षाः सिंहतुल्यपराक्रमाः। पाण्डवानामनीकानि बभञ्जुः स्म पुनः पुनः॥
en: In that fearful and terrible battle, car warriors were to run away in all directions; then Bhishma, Drona, Jayadratha seen the king of the Sindhus, Purumitra, Vikarna, the son of Subala Shakuni, these invincible and lion-like heroes broke the Pandava rank.

description: Commencement of the third day's battle
sn: तथैव भीमसेनोऽपि राक्षसश्च घटोत्कचः। सात्यकिश्चेकितानश्च द्रौपदेयाश्च भारत।॥ तावकांस्तव पुत्रांश्च सहितान् सर्वराजभिः। द्रावयामासुराजौ ते त्रिदशा दानवानिव॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, Bhimasena, the Rakshasa Ghatotkacha, Satyaki, Chekitana, the sons of Draupadi, backed by all the kings, chastised your troops and your sons, as the celestials did the Danavas.

description: Commencement of the third day's battle
sn: तथा ते समरेऽन्योन्यं निघ्नन्तः क्षत्रियर्षभाः। रक्तोक्षिता घोररूपा विरेजुर्दानवा इव॥
en: Those foremost of Kshatriya struck one another in battle. They became terrible to look at. covered with blood, they shone like the Kinshuka flowers.

description: Commencement of the third day's battle
sn: विनिर्जित्य रिपून् वीराः सेनयोरुभयोरपि। व्यदृश्यन्त महामात्रा ग्रहा इव नभस्तले॥
en: O king, vanquishing their adversaries, those foremost of warriors of both the armies looked like the brilliant stars in the sky.

description: Commencement of the third day's battle
sn: ततो रथसहस्रेण पुत्रो दुर्योधनस्तव। अभ्ययात् पाण्डवं युद्धे राक्षसं च घटोत्कचम्॥
en: Then your son Duryodhana supported by one thousand car-warriors rushed to battle with the sons of Pandu and the Rakshasa Ghatotkacha.

description: Commencement of the third day's battle
sn: तथैव पाण्डवाः सर्वे महत्या सेनया सह। द्रोणभीष्मौ रणे यत्तौ प्रत्युद्ययुररिंदमौ॥
en: The Pandava also with many thousand troops rushed in battle against those chastiser of foes, the heroic Bhishma and Drona.

description: Commencement of the third day's battle
sn: किरीटी च ययौ क्रुद्धः समन्तात् पार्थिवोत्तमान्। आर्जुनिः सात्यकिश्चैव ययतुः सौबलं बलम्॥
en: The diadem-decked hero (Arjuna) also rushed in anger against those foremost of kings. then the son of Arjuna, Abhimanyu and Satyaki both rushed against the forces of the son of Subala, Shakuni.

description: Commencement of the third day's battle
sn: ततः प्रववृते भूयः संग्रामो लोमहर्षणः। तावकानां परेषां च समरे विजयैषिणाम्॥
en: Then again commenced a fearful and hairstring battle between the troops and both the sides, both parties being eager to defeat one other.

sn: संजय उवाच ततस्ते पार्थिवाः क्रुद्धाः फाल्गुनं वीक्ष्य संयुगे। रथैरनेकसाहौः समन्तात् पर्यवारयन्॥
en: Sanjaya said Having seen Arjuna in battle, the kings angrily surrounded him on all sides with many thousands of cars.

sn: अथैनं रथवृन्देन कोष्ठकीकृत्य भारत। शरैः सुबहुसाहः समन्तादभ्यवारयन्॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, having surrounded him with many thousand cars, they covered him from all sides with many hundreds of arrows.

sn: शक्तीश्च विमलास्तीक्ष्णा गदाश्च परिघैः सह। प्रासान् परश्वघांश्चैव मुद्गरान् मुसलानपि॥ चिक्षिपुः समरे क्रुद्धाः फाल्गुनस्य रथं प्रति। शस्त्राणामथ तां वृष्टिं शलभानामिवायतिम्॥ रुरोध सर्वतः पार्थः शरैः कनकभूषणैः। तत्र तल्लाघवं दृष्ट्वा बीभत्सोरतिमानुषम्॥ देवदानवगन्धर्वाः पिशाचोरगराक्षसाः। साधु साध्विति राजेन्द्र फाल्गुनं प्रत्यपूजयन्॥
en: They angrily hurled at Falguna's (Arjuna's) car bright and sharp pointed lances, maces, clubs with spikes, bearded darts, battle-axes, mallets, and bludgeons. That. shower of weapons came to him like a flight of locusts. But Pritha's son checked it with his gold decked arrows. Seeing on that occasion the extraordinary lightness of the hands of Vibhatsu (Arjuna), the celestials, in the Danavas, the Gandharvas, the Pishachas the Uragas and the Rakshasas praised Phalguna, exclaiming “Excellent” “Excellent”.

sn: सात्यकिश्चाभिमन्युश्च महत्या सेनया वृतौ। गान्धारान् समरे शूराञ्जग्मतुः सहसौबलान्॥
en: The heroic Gandharvas with Subala's son at their head surrounded Satyaki and Abhimanyu.

sn: तत्र सौबलकाः क्रुद्धा वार्ष्णेयस्य रथोत्तमम्। तिलशश्चिच्छिदुः क्रोधाच्छस्त्रैर्नानाविधैर्युधि॥
en: Then those brave warriors led by Subala's son angrily cut down into fragments the excellent car of the Vrishni hero (Satyaki) with various kinds of weapons.

sn: सात्यकिस्तु रथं त्यक्त्वा वर्तमाने भयावहे। अभिमन्यो रथं तूर्णमासरोह परंतपः॥
en: O chastiser of foes, in that fearful battle, Satyaki abandoned his own car and mounted on that of Abhimanyu.

sn: तावेकरथसंयुक्तौ सौबलेयस्य वाहिनीम्। व्यधमेतां शितैस्तूर्णं शरैः संनतपर्वभिः॥
en: Then those two heroes, mounting on the same car, began to slaughter the army of Subala's son (Shakuni) with innumerable sharp pointed arrows.

sn: द्रोणभीष्मौ रणे यत्तौ धर्मराजस्य वाहिनीम्। नाशयेतां शरैस्तीक्ष्णैः कङ्कपत्रपरिच्छदः॥
en: Drona and Bhishma fighting bravely began to slaughter the troops under Dharmaraja Yudhishthira with sharp arrows furnished with feathers of Kanka bird.

sn: ततो धर्मसुतो राजा माद्रीपुत्रौ च पाण्डवौ। मिषतां सर्वसैन्यानां द्रोणानीकमुपाद्रवन्॥
en: Then the son of Dharma (Yudhishthira) and the two sons of Madri, in the very sight of the whole army, began to chastise the troops of Drona.

sn: तत्रासीत् सुमहद् युद्धं तुमुलं लोमहर्षणम्। यथा देवासुरं युद्धं पूर्वमासीत् सुदारुणम्॥
en: Then the batile that was fought was fearful and terrible, like the one that was fought in the days of yore between the celestials and the Danavas.

sn: कुर्वाणौ सुमहत् कर्म भीमसेनघटोत्कचौ। दुर्योधनस्ततोऽभ्येत्य तावुभावप्यवारयत्॥
en: Bhimasena and Ghatotkacha both performed great feats. Then Duryodhana came and checked them both.

sn: तत्राद्भुतमपश्याम हैडिम्बस्य पराक्रमम्। अतीत्य पितरं युद्धे यदयुध्यत भारत॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, the prowess that we saw displayed by the son of Hidimba was exceedingly wonderful; for he transcended even his father (Bhima).

sn: भीमसेनस्तु संक्रुद्धौ दुर्योधनममर्षणम्। हृद्यविध्यत् पृषत्केन प्रहसन्निव पाण्डवः॥
en: Then the Pandava Bhimasena angrily and smilingly wounded the vindictive Duryodhana in the breast with an arrow.

sn: ततो दुर्योधनो राजा प्रहारवरपीडितः। निषसाद रथोपस्थे कश्मलं च जगाम ह॥
en: Then king Duryodhana, mortally wounded by that arrow, sat dowin on his car and fainted.

sn: तं विसंज्ञं विदित्वा तु त्वरमाणोऽस्य सारथिः। अपोवाह रणाद् राजंस्ततः सैन्यमभज्यत॥
en: O king, seeing him senseless, his charioteer specdily carried him away from the field of battle. Then the the troops that supported Duryodhana broke and fled away.

sn: ततस्तां कौरवीं सेनां द्रवमाणां समन्ततः। निघ्नन् भीमः शरैस्तीक्ष्णैरनुवव्राज पृष्ठतः॥
en: Then striking those flying Kuru troops with his sharp-pointed arrows Bhima pursued them.

sn: पार्षतश्च रथश्रेष्ठो धर्मपुत्रश्च पाण्डवः। द्रोणस्य पश्यत: सैन्यं गाङ्गेयस्य च पश्यतः॥
en: Then that foremost of warriors, the Prishata prince and the Pandava king Dharmaraja Yudhishthira, O descendant of Bharata, in the very sight of Drona and Ganga's son (Bhishma).

sn: जघ्नतुर्विशिखैस्तीक्ष्णैः परानीकविनाशनैः। द्रवमाणं तु तत् सैन्यं तव पुत्रस्य संयुगे॥
en: Slaughtered their troops with sharp arrows, each capable of destroying hostile heroes. Your those troops thus fled from the battle;

sn: नाशक्नुतां वारयितुं भीष्ट्रोणौ महारथौ। वार्यमाणं च भीष्ममेण द्रोणेन च महात्मना॥
en: And those two great car-warriors Bhishma and Drona could not stop them. Though attempted to be stopped by Bhishma and the high souled Drona.

sn: विद्रवत्येव तत् सैन्यं पश्यतोःणभीष्मयोः। ततो रथसहस्रेषु विद्रवत्सु ततस्ततः।२३॥
en: Those troops fled away in the very sight of Drona and Bhishma. When those thousands of car-warriors fled away in all directions.

sn: तावास्थितावेकरथं सौभद्रशिनिपुङ्गवौ। सौबली समरे सेनां शातयेतां समन्ततः॥
en: O chastiser of foes, then Subhadara's son (Abhimanyu) and that best of the Shini's race, both mounting the same car began to slaughter the army of the son of Subala.

sn: शुशुभाते तदा तौ तु शैनेयकुरुपुङ्गवौ। अमावास्यां गतौ यद्वत् सोमसूर्यो नभस्तले॥
en: Shini's grandson and that foremost of Kuru race looked as effulgent as the sun and the moon when they are seen both in the sky after the last lunation of the dark fort-night has passed away.

sn: अर्जुनस्तु ततः क्रुद्धस्तव सैन्यं विशाम्पते। ववर्ष शरवर्षेण धाराभिरिव तोयदः॥
en: O king, then Arjuna angrily poured shower of arrows on your army as clouds pour rain in torrents..

sn: वध्यमानं ततस्तत्र शरैः पार्थस्य संयुगे। दुद्राव कौरवं सैन्यं विषादभयकम्पितम्॥
en: Thus slaughtered in the battle with the arrows of Partha, the Kuru army, trembling in grief and fear fled away.

sn: द्रवतस्तान् समालक्ष्य भीष्मद्रोणौ महारथौ। न्यवारयेतां संरब्यौ दुर्योधनहितैषिणौ॥
en: Seeing the army flying, the mighty Bhishma and Drona both enraged and both eager to do Duryodhana's good tried to stop them.

sn: ततो दुर्योधनो राजा समाश्वस्य विशाम्पते। न्यवर्तयत तत् सैन्यं द्रवमाणं समन्ततः॥
en: Then king Duryodhana himself cheering his troops stopped them from flying away in all directions.

sn: यत्र यत्र सुतस्तुभ्यं यं यं पश्यति भारत। तत्र तत्र न्यवर्तन्त क्षत्रियाणां महारथाः॥
en: Thereupon all the Kshatriya car-warriors stopped, each on the spot from which they saw your son.

sn: तान् निवृत्तान् समीक्ष्यैव ततोऽन्येऽपीतरे जनाः। अन्योन्यस्पर्धया राजल्लँज्जया चावतस्थिरे॥
en: O king, then the common soldiers having seen them stop, stopped of their own accord from shame and from the desire of displaying their prowess.

sn: पुनरावर्ततां तेषां वेग आसीद् विशाम्पते। पूर्यतः सागरस्येव चन्द्रस्योदयनं प्रति॥
en: O king, the army thus rallied appeared then like the surging sea at the time of moon's rising.

sn: संनिवृत्तांस्ततस्तांस्तु दृष्ट्वा राजा सुयोधनः। अब्रवीत् त्वरितो गत्वा भीष्मं शान्तनवं वचः॥
en: Having seen his army relied for fight, king Suyodhana soon went to the son of Shantanu and thus spoke to him.

sn: पितामह निबोधेदं यत् त्वां वक्ष्यामि भारत। नानुरूपमहं मन्ये त्वयि जीवति कौरव॥ द्रोणे चास्त्रविदां श्रेष्ठे सपुत्रे ससुहज्जने। कृपे चैव महेष्वासे द्रवते यद् वरूथिनी॥
en: “O grandfather, hear what I say; O descendant of Bharata, O scion of the Kuru race, when you, and that foremost of men learned in arms, Drona, with his son and with all our other friends, and also the great bowman Kripa are alive. I do not consider it creditable that my troops should run away.

sn: न पाण्डवान् प्रतिबलांस्तव मन्ये कथंचन। तथा द्रोणस्य संग्रामे द्रौणेश्चैव कृपस्य च॥
en: I do not consider the Pandavas a match for you, or for Drona or for Drona's son or for Kripa.

sn: अनुग्राह्याः पाण्डुसुतास्तव नूनं पितामह। यथेमां क्षममे वीर वध्यमानां वरूथिनीम्॥
en: O grandfather, the Pandavas are certainly being favoured by you. O hero, therefore you forgive them this slaughter of my troops.

sn: सोऽस्मि वाच्यस्त्वया राजन् पूर्वमेव समागमे। न योत्स्ये पाण्डवान् संख्ये नापि पार्षतसात्यकी।॥
en: O king, you should have told me, before this battle began, that you would not fight with the Pandavas.

sn: श्रुत्वा तु वचनं तुभ्यमाचार्यस्य कृपस्य च। कर्णेन सहितः कृत्यं चिन्तयानस्तदैव हि॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, hearing such words from you and from the preceptor (Drona), I would have then with Karna reflected what we should have done.

sn: यदि नाहं परित्याज्यो युवाभ्यामिह संयुगे। विक्रमेणानुरूपेण युध्येतां पुरुषर्षभौ॥
en: O foremost of men, if I do not deserve to be abandoned by you two, then fight at the utmost of your power".

sn: एतच्छ्रुत्वा वचो भीष्मः प्रहसन् वै मुहुर्मुहुः। अब्रवीत् तनयं तुभ्यं क्रोधादुद्वृत्य चक्षुषी॥
en: Having heard these words. Bhishma laughed and turned his eyes in anger. He then thus spoke to your son.

sn: बहुशोऽसि मया राजंस्तथ्यमुक्तो हितं वचः। अजेयाः पाण्डवा युद्धे देवैरपि सवासवैः॥
en: "O king, I have innumerable times said to you words worthy of your acceptance and fraught with your good. The Pandavas are invincible even to the celestials with Vasava at their head.

sn: यत् तु शक्यं मया कर्तुं वृद्धेनाद्य नृपोत्तम। करिष्यामि यथाशक्ति प्रेक्षेदानीं सबान्धवः॥
en: O foremost of kings, what I am capable of doing, aged as I am, I shall certainly do in this battle to the utmost of my power. See it now with your kinsmen.

sn: एवमुक्ते तु जनेश्वर। अद्य पाण्डुसुतानेकः ससैन्यान् सह बन्धुभिः। सोऽहं निवारयिष्यामि सर्वलोकस्य पश्यतः॥
en: In the sight of all I shall today alone chastise the Pandavas with their troops and with all their kinsmen".

sn: भीष्मेण पुत्रास्तव दध्मुः शङ्खान् मुदा युक्ता भेरीः संजनिरे भृशम्॥
en: Having been thus addressed by Bhishma, O king, your son was filled with delight. He ordered conchs to be blown and drums to be beat.

sn: पाण्डवा हि ततो राजन्श्रुत्वा तं निनदं महत्। दध्मुः शङ्खांश्च भेरीश्च मुरजांश्चाप्यनादयन्॥
en: O king, having heard the loud uproar, the Pandavas blew their conchs and ordered their drums and cymbals to be sounded.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच प्रतिज्ञाते ततस्तस्मिन् युद्धे भीष्मेण दारुणे। क्रोधितो मम पुत्रेण दुःखितेन विशेषतः॥ भीष्मः किमकरोत् तत्र पाण्डवेयेषु संभारतगे। पितामहे वा पञ्चालास्तन्ममाचक्ष्व संजय॥
en: Dhritarashtra said When enraged by the words of my son, O Sanjaya, Bhishma took thai fearful vow in the battle, what did he do to the Pandavas, and what did the Panchalas do to the grandsire? O Sanjaya, tell me all this.

sn: संजय उवाच गतपूर्वाह्नभूयिष्ठे तस्मिन्नहनि भारत। पश्चिमां दिशमास्थाय स्थिते चापि दिवाकरे॥
en: Sanjaya said O descendant of Bharata, when the morning of that day passed away and when the sun in his westward course had gone some portion of his path.

sn: जयं प्राप्तेषु हृष्टेषु पाण्डवेषु महात्मसु। सर्वधर्मविशेषज्ञः पिता देवव्रतस्तव॥
en: And when the illustrious Pandava had won the victory, your father Devavrata learned in the precepts of morality.

sn: अभ्यायज्जवनैरश्वैः पाण्डवानामनीकिनीम्। महत्या सेनया गुप्तस्तव पुत्रैश्च सर्वशः॥
en: Rushed on the fleetest steed towards the Pandava army, followed by a very large force and by all your sons.

sn: प्रावर्तत ततो युद्धं तुमुलं लोमहर्षणम्। अस्माकं पाण्डवैः सार्धमनयात् तव भारत॥
en: Then O descendant of Bharata, a fearful and hair-stirring battle between ourselves and the Pandavas began in consequences of your sinful policy.

sn: धनुषां कूजतां तत्र तलानां चाभिहन्यताम्। महान् समभवच्छब्दो गिरीणामिव दीर्यताम्॥
en: The twang of bows and the flapping of bowstrings mingling together, made a loud uproar which resembled the noise of splitting hills.

sn: तिष्ठ स्थितोऽस्मि विद्ध्येनं निवर्तस्व स्थिरो भव। स्थिरोऽस्मि प्रहरस्वेति शब्दोऽश्रूयत सर्वशः॥
en: “Stay”, “Hear stand I”, “Turn back” “Stand” "O wait for you” “Strike" these were the words that were heard everywhere.

sn: काञ्चनेषु तनुत्रेषु किरीटेषु ध्वजेषु च। शिलानामिव शैलेषु पतितानामभूद् ध्वनिः॥
en: The sound of the fall of armours, of crowns and diadems and of standards, resembled the sound of falling stones on hard founds.

sn: पतितान्युत्तमाङ्गानि बाहवश्च विभूषिताः। व्यचेष्टन्त महीं प्राप्य शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः॥
en: Hundreds and thousands of heads and arms adorned with ornaments, feil on the ground and moved in convulsions.

sn: हतोत्तमाङ्गाः केचित् तु तथैवोद्यतकार्मुकाः। प्रगृहीतायुधाश्चापि तस्थुः पुरुषसत्तमाः॥
en: Some brave combatants with heads cut off still stood with weapons in their grasp and with bows.

sn: प्रावर्तत महावेगा नदी रुधिरवाहिनी। मातङ्गाङ्गशिला रौद्रा मांसशोणितकर्दमा॥
en: A fearful river of blood began to run there. It was of impetuous current, it was airy with flesh and blood and the dead bodies of elephants appeared in it like (sub-marine) rocks.

sn: वराश्वनरनागानां शरीरप्रभवा तदा। परलोकार्णवमुखी गृध्रगोमायुमोदिनी॥
en: It flowed from the bodies of horses, men and elephants. It was delightful to vultures and jackals. It was delightful to vultures and jackals. It ran towards the ocean of after life.

sn: न दृष्टं न श्रुतं वापि युद्धमेतादृशं नृप। यथा तव सुतानां च पाण्डवानां च भारत॥
en: O king, O descendant of Bharata, a battle like the one that was fought between your sons and the Pandavas was never before seen or heard of.

sn: नासीद् रथपथस्तत्र योधैर्युधि निपातितैः। गजैश्च पतितैर्नीलैर्गिरिशृङ्गैरिवावृतः॥
en: Chariots could not makes their way, for the way was blocked by the bodies of combatants. The field of battle with the bodies of the killed elephants appeared to be strewn over with blew peaks of hills.

sn: विकीर्णैः कवचैश्चित्रैः शिरस्त्राणैश्च मारिष। शुशुभे तद् रणस्थानं शरदीव नभस्तलम्॥
en: O sire, strewn with various coloured armours and turbans the battle field looked beautiful like the autumn sky.

sn: विनिर्भिन्नाः शरैः केचिदन्त्रापीडप्रकर्षिणः। अभीताः समरे शत्रूनभ्यधावन्त
en: Though mortally wounded, some warriors were seen to rush upon the enemy in battle with cheerfulness and pride.

sn: तात भ्रात: सखे बन्धो वयस्य मम मातुल। मा मां परित्यजेत्यन्ये चुक्रुशुः पतिता रणे॥ दर्पिताः॥
en: Many, fallen on the field of battle, cried aloud, “O father, O brother, O friend, O kinsman, O companion, O maternal uncle, do not abandon me".

sn: अथाभ्येहित्वमागच्छ किं भीतोऽसि क्व यास्यसि। स्थितोऽहं समरे मा भैरिति चान्ये विचुक्रुशुः॥
en: Others cried, "Come, come to .his side why are you frightened? Where do you go? I stand in battle. Do not be afraid”.

sn: तत्र भीष्मः शान्तनवो नित्यं मण्डलकार्मुकः। मुमोच बाणान् दीप्ताचानहीनाशीविषानिव॥
en: In that great battle, the son of Shantanu, Bhishma, with his bow drawn to a circle, shot arrows with blazing points which resembled snakes of virulent poison.

sn: शरैरेकायनीकुर्वन् दिशः सर्वा यतव्रतः। जघान पाण्डवरथानादिश्य भरतर्षभ॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, showering continuous arrows in all directions, that hero of rigid vows (Bhishma) struck the Pandava warriors calling each by name.

sn: स नृत्यन् वै रथोपस्थे दर्शयन् पाणिलाघवम्। अलातचक्रवद् राजंस्तत्र तत्र स्म दृश्यते॥
en: O king, displaying his great lightness of hands and dancing as it were along the track of his car, he appeared to be present everywhere like a circle of fire.

sn: तमेकं समरे शूरं पाण्डवाः सुंजयैः सह। अनेकशतसाहस्रं समपश्यन्त लाघवात्॥
en: In consequence of his great lightness of hands, the Pandavas and the Srinjayas saw that hero in that battle multiplied to one thousand fold, though he was really alone.

sn: मायाकृतात्मानमिव भीष्मं तत्र स्म मेनिरे। पूर्वस्यां दिशि तं दृष्ट्वा प्रतीच्यां ददृशुर्जनाः॥
en: Everyone present there considered Bhishma as having multiplied his self by illusion. They now saw him on the cast and on the very next moment, they saw him on the west.

sn: उदीच्यां चैवमालोक्य दक्षिणस्यां पुनः प्रभो। एवं स समरे शूरो गाङ्गेयः प्रत्यदृश्यत॥
en: Now they beheld him on the North, and on the next moment they beheld him on the South. Thus the son of Ganga was seen to fight on all directions (simultaneously).

sn: न चैवं पाण्डवेयानां कश्चिच्छक्नोति वीक्षितुम्। विशिखानेव पश्यन्ति भीष्मचापच्युतान् बहून्॥
en: There was none amongst the Pandavas who was able even to look at him. What they all saw were only innumerable arrows shot from his bow.

sn: कुर्वाणं समरे कर्म सूदयानं च वाहिनीम्। व्याक्रोशन्त रणे तत्र नरा बहुविधा बहु॥
en: Having seen him achieve such great feats and slaughter their ranks, the heroic warriors (of the Pandava side) uttered many lamentations.

sn: अमानुषेण रूपेण चरन्तं पितरं तव। शलभा इव राजानः पतन्ति विधिचोदिताः॥ भीष्माग्निमभिसंक्रुद्धं विनाशाय सहस्रशः। न हि मोघः शरः कश्चिदासीद् भीष्मस्य संयुगे॥ नरनागाश्वकायेषु बहुत्वाल्लघुयोधिनः। भिनत्त्येकेन बाणेन सुमुखेन पतत्त्रिणा॥ गजकण्टकसंनद्धं वज्रेणेव शिलोच्चयम्। द्वौ त्रीनपि गजारोहान् पिण्डितान् वर्मितानपि॥ नाराचेन सुमुक्तेन निजघान पिता तव। यो यो भीष्मं नरव्याघ्रमभ्येति युधि कश्चन॥ मुहूर्तदृष्टः स मया पतितो भुवि दृश्यते। एवं सा धर्मराजस्य वध्यमाना महाचमूः॥ भीष्मेणातुलवीर्येण व्यशीर्यत सहस्रधा। प्राकम्पत महासेना शरवर्षेण तापिता॥ पश्यतो वासुदेवस्य पार्थस्याथ शिखण्डिनः। वर्तमानाऽपि ते वीरा द्रवमाणान् महारथान्॥ नाशक्नुवन् वारयितुं भीष्मबाणप्रपीडितान्। महेन्द्रसमवीर्येण वध्यमाना महाचमूः॥
en: Thousands of kings came in contact with your father who was thus roving over the field in a super-human way. They fell into that fire Bhishma as flights of senseless insects fall on a blazing fire for their own destruction. Not a single arrow of that light-handed hero was futile. They cut down innumerable men, elephants and steeds. With one single straight arrow he felled down one big elephants, as a hill is brought down by the thunder-bolt. Your sire, with sharp arrows, pierced at a time two or three elephant riders clad in armour. Whoever came near that foremost of men Bhishina in that battle, was seen the very next moment to fall down on the ground. The vast army of Dharmaraja Yudhishthira, having been thus slaughtered by the greatly powerful Bhishma, gave way in one thousand directions. Thus afflicted by that shower of arrows, that vast army began to tremble even in the presence of Vasudeva (Krishna) and the illustrious Partha (Arjuna). Though the heroic leaders of the Pandu army tried their utmost, yet they could not prevent the great car-warriors of their side from running away. The prowess with which Bhishma routed that vast army was equal to that of the lord of the celestials himself.

sn: अभज्यत महाराज न च द्वौ सह धावतः। आविद्धनरनागाश्वं पतितध्वजकूबरम्॥
en: O great king, that great army was so completely routed that no two persons were seen together; cars, elephants, and horses were pierced all over their bodies, and the standards and arrows were strewn over the field.

sn: अनीकं पाण्डुपुत्राणां हाहाभूतमचेतनम्। जघानात्र पिता पुत्रं पुत्रश्च पितरं तथा॥ प्रियं सखायं चाक्रन्दे सखा दैवबलात्कृतः। विमुच्य कवचान्यन्ये पाण्डुपुत्रस्य सैनिकाः॥ विमुक्तकेशा धावन्तः प्रत्यदृश्यन्त भारत। तद् गोकुलमिवोद्धान्तमुद्घान्तरथयूथपम्॥ ददृशे पाण्डुपुत्रस्य सैन्यमार्तस्वरं तदा। प्रभज्यमानं सैन्यं तु दृष्ट्वा यादवनन्दनः॥ उवाच पार्थं बीभत्सु निगृह्य रथमुत्तमम्। अयं स कालः सम्प्राप्तः पार्थ यस्तऽभिकाक्षितः॥४२
en: The Pandava army cried “Oh” and “Alas”, and became deprived of its senses. Father struck the son and the son struck the father; friends fought with dearest friends as if all were under the influence of fate. O descendant of Bharata many men of the Pandava army were seen with disheveled hair to run away throwing aside their armours. The Pandava army uttered loud lamentations. Even the very leaders of their car-warriors were seen to be as confounded as a very herd of kinc. Having seen the army thus routed, that delighter of the Yudu race (Krishna) stopped that best of car (belonging to Arjuna) and thus spoke to Partha: "O son of Pritha, the hour has now come which was desired by you.

sn: प्रहरस्व नरव्याघ्र न चेन्मोहाद् विमुह्यसे। यत् त्वया कथितं वीर पुरा राज्ञां समागमे॥ भीष्मद्रोणमुखान् सर्वान् धार्तराष्ट्रस्य सैनिकान्। सानुबन्धान् हनिष्यामि ये मां योत्स्यन्ति संयुगे॥ इति तत् कुरु कौन्तेय सत्यं वाक्यमरिंदम। बीभत्सो पश्य सैन्यं स्वं भज्यमानं ततस्ततः॥
en: O foremost of men, strike Bhishma or else you will lose your senses. O hero, formerly in the assembly of the kings you said," I will kill all the warriors of the sons of Dhritarashtra, headed by Bhishma and Drona, all who will fight me in battle, O Vibhatsu, O son of Kunti, O chastiser of foes, make your words now true. Your army is routed on all sides.

sn: द्रवतश्च महीपालान् पश्य यौधिष्ठिरे बले। दृष्ट्वा हि भीष्मं समरे व्यात्ताननमिवान्तकम्॥
en: Behold, all the kings of Yudhisthira's army are flying away, on seeing Bhishma in battle who looks like the destroyer himself with his wide open mouth.

sn: भयार्ताः प्रपलायन्ते सिंहात् क्षुद्रमृगा इव। एवमुक्तः प्रत्युवाच वासुदेवं धनंजयः॥ नोदयाश्वान् यतो भीष्मो विगाहैतद् बलार्णवम्। पातयिष्यामि दुर्धर्षं वृद्धं कुरुपितामहम्॥
en: Having been afflicted with fear, they are running away, as do the small animals at the sight of the lion". Having been thus addressed, Dhananjaya thus spoke to Vasudeva. "Plunging through this sea of the hostile army, drive the horses to the spot where Bhishma is. I shall fell down (today) that invincible warriors, the revered Kuru grandsire.

sn: संजय उवाच ततोऽश्वान् रजतप्रख्यान् नोदयाभास माधवः। यतो भीष्मरथो राजन् दुष्प्रेक्ष्यो रश्मिमवानिव॥
en: O king, then Madhava drove those silverwhite steeds to the place where the car of Bhishma was, the car which like the very sun was incapable of being gazed at.

sn: ततस्तत् पुनरावृत्तं युधिष्ठिरबलं महत्। दृष्ट्वा पार्थं महाबाहुं भीष्मायोद्यतमाहवे॥
en: Having scen the mighty armed son of Pritha thus rush to fight with Bhishma, the great army of Yudhishthira rallied for battle.

sn: ततो भीष्मः कुरुश्रेष्ठ सिंहवद् विनदन् मुहुः। धनंजयरथं शीघ्रं शरवर्षैरवाकिरत्॥
en: Then that foremost of Kuru warriors Bhishma again and again roared like a lion. He then covered the car of Dhananjaya with a shower of arrows.

sn: क्षणेन स रथस्तस्य सहयः सहसारथिः। शरवर्षेण महता संछन्नो न प्रकाशते॥
en: In a moment (Arjuna's) car with its standard and charioteer became invisible having been covered with that shower of arrows.

sn: वासुदेवस्त्वसम्भ्रान्तो धैर्यमास्थाय सत्त्ववान्। चोदयामास तानश्वान् विचितान् भीष्मसायकैः॥
en: The greatly powerful Vasudeva however, fearlessly and patiently drove the horses now wounded by Bhishma's arrow.

sn: ततः पार्थो धनुर्गृह्य दिव्यं जलदनिःस्वनम्। पातयामास भीष्मस्य धनुश्छित्त्वा त्रिभिः शरैः॥
en: Then Partha took up his celestial bow whose twang resembled the roar of the clouds and cut down Bhishma's bow with his sharp arrows.

sn: स च्छिन्नधन्वा कौरव्यः पुनरन्यन्महद् धनुः। निमिषान्तरमात्रेण सज्यं चक्रे पिता तव।॥
en: Your father, the Kuru hero, took up another bow when he saw the one in his hand cut down. He strung it within the twinkling of an eye.

sn: विचकर्ष ततो दो• धनुर्जलदनि:स्वनम्। अथास्य तदपि क्रुद्धश्चिच्छेद धनुरर्जुनः॥
en: He drew that bow, the twang of which resembled the roar of the clouds, with his two hands. But Arjuna, now excited with anger, again cut down that bow.

sn: तस्य तत् पूजयामास लाघवं शान्तनोः सुतः। साधु पार्थ महाबाहो साधु भोः पाण्डुनन्दन॥
en: Thereupon the son of Shantanu (Bhishma) praised his lightness of hand by saying, “O Partha. O son of Pandu, O mighty-armed hero, 'Excellent, Excellent'.

sn: त्वय्येवैतद् युक्तरूपं महत् कर्म धनंजय। प्रीतोऽस्मि सुभृशं पुत्र कुरु युद्धं मया सह॥
en: O Dhananjaya, such a great feat is indeed worthy of you. I have been pleased with you. O son, fight hard with me”.

sn: इति पार्थं प्रशस्याथ प्रगृह्यान्यन्महद् धनुः। मुमोच समरे वीरः शरान् पार्थरथं प्रति॥
en: Having thus praised Partha, and having taken up a large bow, that great hero hurled his arrows at Partha's car.

sn: अदर्शयद् वासुदेवो हययाने परं बलम्। मोघान् कुर्वशरांस्तस्य मण्डलान्याचरल्लघु॥
en: Vasudeva then displayed his great skill in the guiding the horses. He baffled those arrows by driving the car in quick circles.

sn: तथा भीष्मस्तु सुदृढं वासुदेवधनंजयौ। विव्याध निशितैर्बाणैः सर्वगात्रेषु भारत॥
en: Then, O sire, Bhishma with great force pierced both Vasudeva and Dhananjaya with keen arrows all over their bodies.

sn: शुशुभाते नरव्याघ्रौ तौ भीष्मशरविक्षतौ। गोवृषाविव संरब्धौ विषाणैरिखितङ्कितौ॥
en: Wounded by those arrows of Bhishma those foremost of men looked like two roaring bulls with scratches of horns on their bodies.

sn: पुनश्चापि सुसंरब्धः शरैः शतसहस्रशः। कृष्णयोर्युधि संरब्धो भीष्मोऽथावारयद् दिशः॥
en: Excited with wrath, Bhishma cover the two Krishna's on all sides with hundred and thousands of arrow.

sn: वार्ष्णेयं च शरैस्तीक्ष्णैः कम्पयामास रोषित:। मुहुरभ्यर्दयन् भीष्मः प्रहस्य स्वनवत् तदा॥
en: With his sharp arrows the angry Bhishma made the Vrishni chief (Krishna) to shiver; laughing loudly also he made Krishna very much astonished.

sn: ततस्तु कृष्णः समरे दृष्ट्वा भीष्मपराक्रमम्। सम्प्रेक्ष्य च महाबाहुः पार्थस्य मृदुयुद्धताम्॥ भीष्मं च शरवर्षाणि सृजन्तमनिशं युधि। प्रतपन्तमिवादित्यं मध्यमासाद्य सेनयोः॥
en: Then seeing the great prowess of Bhishma and the mildness with which Arjuna fought, and also seeing that Bhishma was showering a continuous shower of arrows in that battle and that he was appearing like the all consuming sun in the midst of the two arinies.

sn: वरान् वरान् विनिघ्नन्तं पाण्डुपुत्रस्य सैनिकान्। युगान्तमिव कुर्वाणं भीष्मं यौधिष्ठिरे बले॥
en: And marking also that hero (Bhishma) was killing the foremost warriors of Yudhisthira's army and that he was making a great havoc amongst the troops as if the hour of dissolution had come.

sn: अमृष्यमाणो भगवान् केशवः परवीरहा। अचिन्तयदमेयात्मा नास्ति यौधिष्ठिरं बलम्॥
en: The exalted Keshava, that slayer of hostile heroes, that high-souled one became unable to see what he saw. He thought that the army of Yudhishthira could not survive that slaughter.

sn: एकाह्रा हि रणे भीष्मो नाशयेद् देवदानवान्। किं नु पाण्डुसुतान् युद्धे सबलान् सपदानुगान्॥
en: Bhishma was capable of destroying all the Daityas and Danavas in a single day; with how much ease then could he kill the Pandavas with all their soldiers and followers.

sn: द्रवते च महासैन्यं पाण्डवस्य महात्मनः। एते च कौरवास्तूर्णं प्रभग्नान् वीक्ष्य सोमकान्॥ प्राद्रवन्ति रणे दृष्ट्वा हर्षयन्तः पितामहम्। सोऽहं भीष्मं निहन्म्यद्य पाण्डवार्थाय दंशितः॥
en: The vast army of the illustrious Pandava (Yudhishthira) again began to fly away. Having seen the Somakas routed the Kurus gladdening the heart of the grandsire rushed to battle with great cheerfulness. (Seeing) all this, Krishna reflected;-"Clad in armour I will kill Bhishma today for the sake of the Pandavas.

sn: भारमेतं विनेष्यामि पाण्डवानां महात्मनाम्। अर्जुनो हि शरैस्तीक्ष्णैर्वध्यमानोऽपि संयुगे॥ कर्तव्यं नाभिजानाति रणे भीष्मस्य गौरवात्। तथा चिन्तयतस्तस्य भूय एव पितामहः। प्रेषयामास संक्रुद्धः शरान् पार्थरथं प्रति॥
en: I will lighten the burden of the Pandavas. Though struck with keen arrows in the battle, Arjuna does not what he should do, from respect for Bhishma.” While Krishna was thus reflecting the grandsire again hurled his arrows on Partha's car.

sn: तेषां बहुत्वात् तु भृशं शराणां दिशश्च सर्वाः पिहिता बभूवुः। न भास्करोऽदृश्यत रश्ममाली।
en: In consequence of those various arrows flying in all directions, all sides completely enshrouded. Neither the sky, nor the directions, nor the earth, nor the brilliant sun could be seen. were

sn: ववुश्च वात्सतुमुलाः सधूमा दिशश्च सर्वाः क्षुभिता बभूवुः॥ द्रोणो विकर्णोऽथ जयद्रथश्च भूरिश्रवाः कृतवर्मा कृपश्च। श्रुतायुरम्बष्ठपतिश्च राजा विन्दानुविन्दौ च मुदक्षिणश्च॥ प्राच्याश्च सौवीरगणाश्च सर्वे वसातयः क्षुद्रकमालवाश्च। निदेशगाः शान्तनवस्य राज्ञः॥ रनेकसाहस्रशतैर्ददर्श। किरीटिनं सम्परिवार्यमाणं शिनेर्नप्ता वारणयूथपैश्च॥ ततस्तु दृष्ट्वार्जुनवासुदेवौ पदातिनागाश्वरथैः समन्तात्। अभिद्रुतौ शस्त्रभृतां वरिष्ठौ शिनिप्रवीरोऽभिससार तूर्णम्॥ स तान्यनीकानि महाधनुष्माशिनिप्रवीरः सहसाभिपत्य। चकार साहाय्यमथार्जुनस्य विष्णुर्यथा वृत्रनिषूदनस्य॥ विशीर्णनागाश्वरथध्वजौघं भीष्मेण वित्रासितसर्वयोधम्। युधिष्ठिरानीकमभिद्रवन्तं प्रोवाच संदृश्य शिनिप्रवीरः॥ क्व क्षत्रिया यास्यथ नैष धर्मः सतां पुरस्तात् कथितः पुराणैः।
en: The winds that blew appeared to be mixed with smoke; all the directions seemed to be agitated. Drona, Vikarna, Jayadratha, Bhurishrava, Kritvarma, Kripa, Shrutayusha, the ruler of Ambashta, Vinda and Anuvinda, Sudakshina, the people of the western country, the various tribes of Souviras, the Vasatis, the Kshudrakas, and the Malavas, all these at the command of the Gautamas royal son soon came to Kiritin (Arjuna) for battle. The grandson of Shini saw that Kiritin was surrounded by many thousands of horse and foot soldiers and car-warriors and great elephants. Having seen Vasudeva and Arjuna thus surrounded by infantry and elephants and horses and cars on all sides that foremost of all wielders of arms, that chief of the Shini's, soon went to that place. That ioremost of bowmen, the Shini Chief quickly rushed upon those troops and soon came to Arjuna's aid, as cars Vishnu came to the slayer Vritra. That foremost of Shini warriors cheerfully thus addressed the troops of Yudhishthira who were all frightened by Bhishma, and whose elephants, horses and numberless standards had been mangled and broken into pieces and who were all flying away from the battle-field “O Kshatriyas, were do you go? This is not the duty of virtuous men as declared by the ancients.

sn: मा स्वां प्रतिज्ञां त्यजत प्रवीराः स्वं वीरधर्म परिपालयध्वम्॥ तान् वासवानन्तरजो निशाम्य नरेन्द्रमुख्यान् द्रवतः समन्तात्। पार्थस्य दृष्ट्वा मृदुयुद्धतां च भीष्मं च संख्ये समुदीर्यमाणम्।।८२। अमृष्यमाणः स ततो महात्मा यशस्विनं सर्वदशाहभर्ता। उवाच शैनेयमभिप्रशंसन् दृष्ट्वा कुरूनापततः समग्रान्॥ ये यान्ति ते यान्तु शिनिप्रवीर येऽपि स्थिताः सात्वत तेऽपि यान्तु।
en: O foremost of heroes, do not violate your pledges; observe your own duties as heroes." Having seen that the foremost of kings were flying away from the field of battle and having also marked the mildness with which Partha fought and seeing also that Bhishma was exerting himself with all his powers and that the Kurus were rushing from all sides, the younger brother of Vasava, the illustrious protector of all the Dasharnas become unable to bear it all. He thus spoke to the famous grandson of Shini and praised him much; “O hero of the Shini race, those that are retreating are ended retreating. O Satvata chief those that are still staying, let them also go away.

sn: भीष्मं रथात् पश्य निपात्यमानं द्रोणं च संख्ये सगणं मयाद्य॥ न मे रथी सात्वत कौरवाणां क्रुद्धस्य मुच्येत रणेऽद्य कश्चित्।
en: Behold, I shall soon fell Bhishma down from his car and also Drona in this battle with all their followers. O Satvata chief, there is none in the Kuru army who can escape me when I am angry.

sn: तस्मादहं गृह्य रथाङ्गमुग्रं प्राणं हरिष्यामि महाव्रतस्य॥ निहत्य भीष्मं सगणं तथाऽऽजौ द्रोणं च शेनेय रथप्रवीरौ। प्रीतिं करिष्यामि धनंजयस्य राज्ञश्च भीमस्य तथाऽिश्वनोच॥ स्तत्पक्षिणो ये च नरेन्द्रमुख्याः। राज्येन राजानमजातशत्रु सम्पादयिष्याम्यहमद्य हृष्टः॥
en: Therefore taking up my fearful discus I shall (today) kill Bhishma of rigid vows. O grandson of Shini, killing in battle these two foremost of car-warriors, namely Bhishma and Drona with all their followers, I shall gladden the heart of Dhananjaya and the king (Yudhishthira) and also of Bhima and the twin Ashvins. Killing all the sons of Dhritarashtra and all those foremost of kings who have taken their side, I will with great joy secure a kingdom today for Ajatashatru.”

sn: ततः सुनाभं वसुदेवपुत्रः सूर्यप्रभं वज्रसमप्रभावम्। क्षुरान्तमुद्यम्य भुजेन चक्र रथादवप्लुत्य विसृज्य वाहान्॥ संकम्पयन् गां चरणैर्महात्मा वेगेन कृष्णः प्रससार भीष्मम्।
en: Having said this, the son of Vasudeva threw off the reins of the horses and jumped down from the car. Whirling with his right arm his discus with a beautiful shape and with sharpness as that of a razors, which was as effulgent as the sun and possessed the force of one thousand thunderbolts, the high-souled Krishna rushed with great force towards Bhishma making the earth tremble under his feet.

sn: मदान्धमाजौ समुदीर्णदर्प सिंहो जिघांसन्निव वारणेन्द्रम्॥ सोऽभिद्रवन् भीष्ममनीकमध्ये क्रुद्धो महेन्द्रावरजः प्रमाथी।
en: That chastiser of foes, the younger brother of the chief of the celestial, angrily rushed towards Bhishma who stood in the midst of his troops, as a lion, from the desire of killing a large elephant, rushes towards it.

sn: व्यालम्बिपीतान्तपटश्चकाशे घनो यथा खे तडितावनद्धः॥ स्तच्चक्रपद्यं सुभुजोरुनालम्। यथादिपद्मं तरुणार्कवर्ण रराज नारायणनाभिजातम्॥ तत् कृष्णकोपोदयसूर्यबुद्धं क्षुरान्ततीक्ष्णाग्रसुजातपत्रम्। तस्यैव देहोरुसर:प्ररूढं रराज नारायणबाहुनालम्॥ तमात्तचक्रं प्रणदन्तमुच्चैः क्रुद्ध महेन्द्रावरजं समीक्ष्य। सर्वाणि भूतानि भृशं विनेदुः क्षयं कुरूणामिव चिन्तयित्वा॥ स वासुदेवः प्रगृहीतचक्रः संवर्तयिष्यन्निव सर्वलोकम्।
en: The end of his yellow garments waving in the air looked like a cloud charge with lighting. That lotus of a discus, the Sudarshana, having for its stalk the beautiful arms of Shaurin (Krishna) looked as beautiful as the primeval lotus, which was a bright as the morning sun which caused that lotus to bloom. The beautiful leaves of that lotus were as shape as the edge of a razor. Krishna's body was the beautiful lake, his arms where the stalk upon which shone the lotus. Seeing the younger brother of Mahendra excited with anger and hat he was loudly roaring, that he was armed with discus, all creatures uttered loud wails. They thought the destruction of the Kurus was near at hand. Armed with his discus, Vasudeva looked like the Samvarta fire that appears at the end of a Yuga for consuming the world.

sn: ऊभ्युत्पतल्लोकगुरुर्बभासे भूतानि धक्ष्यन्निव धूमकेतुः॥ तमाद्रवन्तं प्रगृहीतचक्रं दृष्ट्वा देवं शान्तनवस्तदानीम्। असम्भ्रमं तद् विचकर्ष दोभ्यां महाधनुर्गाण्डिवतुल्यघोषम्॥ उवाच भीष्मस्तमनन्तपौरुषं गोविन्दमाजावविमूढचेताः। एह्येहि देवेश जगनिवास नमोऽस्तु ते माधव चक्रपाणे॥
en: The preceptor of the universe blazed up like a fearful cometrisen for consuming all creatures. Having seen that foremost of men, that divine personage advancing armed with discus, Shantanu's son (Bhishma) who stood on his car with his bow and arrow in hand thus fearlessly spoke “Come, come, O lord of the gods, O deity that had the universe for your abode, O god armed with mace, sword and Sarnga, I bow to you.

sn: प्रसह्य मां पातय लोकनाथ रथोत्तमात् सर्वशरण्य संख्ये॥ त्वया हतस्यापि ममाघ कृष्ण श्रेयः परस्मिन्निह चैव लोके।
en: O lord of the universe, forcibly fell me dc wn from this excellent car. O refuge of all creates, O Krishna, in this battle, if I be killed by you, great will be my good fortune both in this world and in the next.

sn: सम्भावितोऽस्म्यन्धकवृष्णिनाथ लोकैस्त्रिभिर्वीर तवाभियानात्॥ रथादवप्लुत्य ततस्त्वरावान् पार्थोऽप्यनुदुत्य यदुप्रवीरम्। जग्राह पीनोत्तमलम्बबाहुँ बाह्वोर्हरिं व्यायतपीनबाहुः॥
en: O Vrishni and Andhaka chief, you give me the greatest respect. My dignity will be celebrated all over the three worlds. Meanwhile, jumping from his car, Partha of mighty and long arms himself soon ran after that Yadu chief possessing massive and long arms. He soon came to him and seized him by his two arms.

sn: निगृह्यमाणश्च तदाऽऽदिदेवो भृशं सरोषः किल चात्मयोगी। र्जिष्णु महावात इवैकवृक्षम्।।१००।
en: That first of all gods, Krishna was excited with rage. Therefore, though thus seized, Vishnu (Krishna) forcibly dragged Vishnu (Arjuna) after him, like a tempest carrying away a tree.

sn: पार्थस्तु विष्टभ्य बलेन पादौ भीष्मान्तिकं तूर्णमभिद्रवन्तम्। बलान्निजग्राह हरि किरीटी पदेऽथ राजन् दशमे कथञ्चित्॥
en: The high-souled Partha, however, seized with great force his legs as he was rushing towards Bhishma; O king, he succeeded in stopping him with great difficulty on the tenth step.

sn: अवस्थितं च प्रणिपत्य कृष्णं प्रीतोऽर्जुनः काञ्चनचित्रमाली। उवाच कोपं प्रतिसंहरेति गतिर्भवान् केशव पाण्डवानाम्॥
en: When Krishna stopped, Arjuna, adorned with a beautiful golden garland cheerful, bowed to him and he then thus spoke to him “Quell our wrath o Keshava, you are the refuge of the Pandavas.

sn: ह हास्यते कर्म यथाप्रतिज्ञं पुत्रैः शपे केशव सोदरैश्च। अन्तं करिष्यामि यथा कुरूणां त्वयाऽहमिन्द्रनुज सम्प्रयुक्तः॥ ततः प्रतिज्ञां समयं च तस्य जनार्दनः प्रीतमना निशम्य। स्थित: प्रिये कौरवसत्तमस्य रथं सचक्रः पुनरारुरोह॥
en: O Keshava, I swear by my sons and brothers that I will not withdrawn from the acts to which I have pledged myself. O younger brother of Indra, at your command. I will certainly annihilate the Kurus." Having heard that promise and pledged by Arjuna, Janardana became gratified. He was ever engaged in doing what is agreeable to that foremost of the Kurus, Arjuna. He therefore, discus on arms, once more mounted on the car.

sn: स तानभीषून् पुनराददानः प्रगृह्य शङ्ख द्विषतां निहन्ता। विनादयामास ततो दिशश्च स पाञ्चजन्यस्य रवेण शौरिः॥
en: That chastiser of foes once more took up the reins. Then taking up his couch called Panchajanya, Shaurin (Krishna) filled the sky and all the directions with its sounds.

sn: व्याविद्धनिष्काङ्गदकुण्डलं तं रजोविकीर्णाञ्चितपद्मनेत्रम्। विशुद्धदंष्ट्रं प्रगृहीतशङ्ख विचुक्रुशुः प्रेक्ष्य कुरुप्रवीराः॥
en: Thereupon when the Kuru heroes saw Krishna adorned with necklace and Angada and ear-ring, with carved eye-lashes smeared with dust and with milk white teeth take up his couch, they sent up a loud cry.

sn: मृदङ्गभेरीपणवप्रणादा नेमिस्वना दुन्दुभिनि:स्वनाश्च। ससिंहनादाश्च बभूवुरुचाः सर्वेष्वनीकेषु ततः कुरूणाम्॥
en: The sounds of cymbals, drums and kettledrums and the rattle of car-wheels and also those of smaller drums, mingling with those lion-like shouts sent up by all the Kuru troops became a fearful uproar.

sn: गाण्डीवघोषः स्तनयित्नुकल्पो जगाम पार्थस्य नभो दिशश्च। जग्मुश्च बाणा विमलाः प्रसन्नाः सर्वा दिशः पाण्डवचापमुक्ताः॥
en: The twang of Partha's Gandiva which resembled the roaring of thunder filled the sky and all the directions. Shot from the bow of the Pandava, bright and blazing arrows flew in all directions.

sn: तं कौरवाणामधिपो जवेन भीष्मेण भूरिश्रवसा च सार्धम्। अभ्युद्ययावुद्यतवाणपाणिः कक्षं दिधक्षन्निव धूमकेतुः॥
en: Then the Kuru king with a large force and with Bhishma and Bhurishrava's son with arrows in their hands resembling a comet risen for consuming a constellation rushed again him.

sn: अथार्जुनाय प्रजिघाय भल्लान् भूरिश्रवाः सप्त सुवर्णपुडान्। दुर्योधनस्तोमरमुग्रवेगं शल्यो गदां शान्तनवश्च शक्तिम्॥
en: Bhurishrava hurled at Arjuna seven javelins with wings of gold, Duryodhana hurled a fearful lance, Shalva a mace and Shantanu's son (Bhishma) a dart.

sn: स सप्तभिः सप्त शरप्रवेकान् संवार्य भूरिश्रवसा विसृष्टान्। शितेन दुर्योधनबाहुमुक्तं क्षुरेण तत् तोमरमुन्ममाथ॥
en: Thereupon baffling the seven javelins with seven arrows, which were as fleet as arrows, shot by Bhurishrava, Arjuna cut off with his sharp arrow the lance hurled by Duryodhana.

sn: तत: शुभामापतती स शक्तिं विद्युत्प्रभा शान्तनवेन मुक्ताम्। गदां च मद्राधिपबाहुमुक्तां द्वाभ्यां शराभ्यां निचकर्त वीरः॥
en: That hero cut down with two arrows the blazing dart, as effulgent as lightning that came towards him hurled by Shantanu's son and the mace hurled by the Madra king.

sn: ततो भुजाभ्यां बलवद् विकृष्य चित्रं धनुर्गाण्डिवमप्रमेयम्। माहेन्द्रमस्त्रं विधिवत् सुघोरं प्रादुश्चकाराद्भुतमन्तरिक्षे॥
en: Then drawing with his two hands and with great force his beautiful and irrisisting powerful bow Gandiva he invoked with proper mantras the exceedingly wonderful and fearful weapon named Mahendra. He made it appear in the sky.

sn: तेनोत्तमास्त्रेण ततो महात्मा सर्वाण्यनीकानि महाधनुष्मान्। निवारयामास किरीटमाली॥ शिलीमुखाः पार्थधनुःप्रमुक्ता रथान् ध्वजाग्राणि धनूंषि बाहून्। निकृत्य देहान् विविशुः परेषां नरेन्द्रनागेन्द्रतुरङ्गमाणाम्॥
en: With that great weapon which was as effulgent as the blazing fire, that illustrious great bowmen, adorned with diadem and garland of gold checked the entire Kuru army.

sn: ततो दिशः सोऽनुदिशश्च पार्थः शरैः सुधारैः समरे वितत्य। गाण्डीवशब्देन मनांसि तेषां किरीटमाली व्यथयाञ्चकार॥
en: Those arrows from Partha's bow cut off the arins, bows, standard-tops and cars, penetrated into the ranks of the kings and of the huge elephants and horses of the enemy.

sn: तस्मिंस्तथा घोरतमे प्रवृत्ते शङ्खस्वना दुन्दुभिनिःस्वनाश्चा अन्तर्हिता गाण्डिवनिःस्वनेन बभूवुरुचाश्वरथप्रणादाः॥
en: Having filled all directions with those sharp and terrible arrows Partha adorned with diadem and garland of gold agitated the hearts of his foes by the fearful twang of his Gandiva.

sn: गाण्डीवशब्दं तमथो विदित्वा विराटराजप्रमुखाः प्रवीराः। स्तं देशमाजग्मुरदीनसत्त्वाः॥
en: In that fierce battle, the sounds of conchs and beat of drums and the deep rattle of cars were all silenced by the twang of the Gandiva.

sn: सर्वाणि सैन्यानि त तावकानि यतो यतो गाण्डिवजः प्रणादः। ततस्ततः संनतिमेव जग्मुन तं प्रतीपोऽभिससार कश्चित्॥
en: Having known that twang t have been produced by the Gandiva, king Virata, and the foremost of men, and the brave Panchala king Drupada all went to the place with unrepressed hearts.

sn: तस्मिन् सुघोरे नृपसम्प्रहारे हताः प्रवीराः सरथाश्वसूताः। गजाश्च नाराचनिपाततप्ता महापताकाः शुभरुक्मकक्ष्याः॥
en: All the troops stood struck with fear each at the spot where he heard that twang of the Gandiva. None dared to go to the place whence rose that sound.

sn: परीतसत्त्वाः सहसा निपेतुः किरीटिना भिन्नतनुत्रकायाः। दृढं हताः पत्रिभिरुचवेगैः पार्थेन भल्लैर्विमलैः शिताचैः॥ निकृत्तयन्त्रा निहतेन्द्रकीला ध्वजा महान्तो ध्वजिनीमुखेषु। पदातिसङ्घाश्च रथाश्च संख्ये हयाश्च नागाश्च धनंजयेन॥ बाणाहतास्तूर्णमपेतसत्त्वा विष्टभ्य गात्राणि निपेतुरुक्म्। ऐन्द्रेण तेनास्त्रवरेण राजन् महाहवे भिन्नतनुत्रदेहाः॥
en: In that fearful, slaughter of the kings, heroic warriors as well as car-warriors with their charioteers were killed. elephants with bright golden housings and gorgeous standards wounded with broad headed arrows that fell upon them suddenly fell down dead with their bodies mangled by Kiritin. Forcibly struck by or Partha with his winged arrows and sharp broad headed arrows, the yantras and indragalas of the standards of innumerable kings were cut down. Innumerable foot soldiers, car-warriors, steeds and elephants fell fast on the filed, their limbs paralysed themselves speedily deprived of life afflicted by Dhananjaya with those arrows. O king, many were the warriors who in that terrible fight had their armours and bodies cut through, by that weapon named after Indra.

sn: ततः शरौधैर्निशितैः किरीटिना नृदेहशस्त्रक्षतलोहितोदा। नदी सुघोरा नरमेदफेना प्रवर्तिता तत्र रणाजिरे॥
en: With those fearful and sharp arrows, Kiritin (Arjuna) made a river of blood to flow on the field of battle, its blood was supplied from the mangled bodies of the soldiers. Its forth was made by their feet.

sn: वेगेन साऽतीव पृथुप्रवाहा परेतनागाश्वशरीररोधा। नरेन्द्रमज्जोच्छ्रितमांसपङ्का प्रभूतरक्षोगणभूतसेविता॥
en: Its current was broad and it ran fearfully. The bodies of dead elephants and horses formed its bangs. Its mire consisted of the entail, the marrow and the flesh of human beings and of the huge Rakshasas.

sn: शिरःकपालाकुलकेशशाद्वला शरीरसङ्घातसहस्रवाहिनी। विशीर्णनानाकवचोर्मिसंकुला नराश्वनागास्थिनिकृत्तशर्करा॥
en: Innumerable crowns of human heads covered with hair formed its floating moss, and heaps of human bodies formed its sand banks. They caused that river to flow in one thousand directions, armours strewn all over it formed its waves, and the bones of human beings and elephants and horses formed its stones and pebbles.
