sn: श्वकङ्कशालावृकगृध्रकाकैः क्रव्यादसङ्घश्च तरक्षुभिश्च। उपेतकूलां ददृशुर्मनुष्याः क्रूरां महावैतरणीप्रकाशाम्॥ मैदोवसासृक्प्रवहां सुभीमाम्। हतप्रवीरां च तथैव दृष्ट्वा सेनां कुरूणामथ फाल्गुनेन॥ ते चेदिपाञ्चालकरूषमत्स्याः पार्थाश्च सर्वे सहिताः प्रणेदुः। जयप्रगल्भाः पुरुषप्रवीराः संत्रासयन्तः कुरुवीरयोधान्॥
en: Its banks were infested by large numbers of jackals and wolves and cranes, and vultures and crowds of Rakshasas and herds of hydras. Those that were alive saw that fearful rivers of fat, marrow and blood caused by the showers of arrows shot by Arjuna; it resembled the great Vaitarani (river). Having seen the foremost of warriors thus killed by Phalguna (Arjuna), the Chedis, the Panchalas, the Karushas, the Matsyas, and all the Pandava warriors, those foremost of men, all highly elated with victory sent up loud shouts that frightened the Kuru warriors.

sn: हतप्रवीराणि बलानि दृष्ट्वा किरीटिना शत्रुभयावहेन। वित्रास्य सेनां ध्वजिनीपतीनां सिंहो मृगाणामिव यूथसङ्घान्॥
en: They sent forth that shout indicative of victory on seeing the foremost warriors of the Kuru army, the very combatants who were protected by the (Kuru) leaders thus killed by Kiritin (Arjuna) that terror foes, who frightened them all as a lion frightens a herd of sinall animals.

sn: विनेदतुस्तावतिहर्षयुक्ती गाण्डीवधन्वा च जनार्दनश्च। ततो रविं संवृतरश्मिजालं दृष्ट्वा भृशं शस्त्रपरिक्षताङ्गाः॥ मसह्यमुद्वीक्ष्य युगान्तकल्पम्। अथापयानं कुरवः सभीष्माः सद्रोणदुर्योधनबाह्निकाच॥ चक्रुर्निशां संधिगतां समीक्ष्य विभावसोर्लोहितरागयुक्ताम्। अवाप्य कीर्तिं च यशश्च लोके विजित्य शंत्रूश्च धनंजयोऽपि।।१३३ ययौ नरेन्द्रैः सह सौदरैश्च समाप्तकर्मा शिबिरं निशायाम्। ततः प्रजज्ञे तुमुलः कुरूणां निशामुखे घोरतमः प्रणादः॥
en: Then the wielder of Gandiva and Janardana, with great delight attacked loud shouts. The Kurus with Bhishma and Drona and Duryodhana and Balhịka all mortally wounded by the weapons (of Arjuna) then saw the sun withdraw his rays. Seeing also the Mahendra weapon spread out and causing as it were the end of the Yuga, they withdrew their force for the night's rests. Thus having achieved a great feat and won great renown and having seen the sun assume a red colour and the evening twilight set in and having completed his work (for that day), Arjuna retired with his brothers to the camp for the night's rest. Then when darkness set in, a fearful and great uproar was made by the Kuru troops.

sn: रणे रथानामयुतं निहत्य हता गजा: सप्तशतार्जुनेन। प्राच्याश्च सौवीरगणाश्च सर्वे निपातिताः क्षुद्रकमालवाश्च॥
en: All said: "In today's battle, Arjuna has killed ten thousand car-warriors and seven hundred elephants. All the people of the western country, the various tribes of the Souviras, the Kshudrakas and the Malavas have all been killed.

sn: महत् कृतं कर्म धनंजयेन कर्तुं यथा नार्हति कश्चिदन्यः। श्रुतायुरम्बष्ठपतिश्च राजा तथैव दुर्मर्षणचित्रसेनौ॥ द्रोणः कृपः सैन्धवबाह्निकौ च भूरिश्रवाः शल्यशलौ च राजन्। अन्ये च योधाः शतश: समेताः क्रुद्धेन पार्थेन रणस्य मध्ये॥ स्वबाहुवीर्येण जिताः सभीष्माः किरीटिना लोकमहारथेन। इति ब्रुवन्तः शिबिराणि जग्मुः सर्वे गणा भारत ये त्वदीयाः॥
en: The feat achieved today by Dhananjaya is indeed a very great one! None else is capable of doing it. The king of the Ambashtha, Shrutayu, Durmarshana, Chitrasena, Drona, Kripa, the Sindhu king, Balhika, Bhurishravas, Shalya, Shala, a hundreds of others warriors with Bhishma at their head have today been defeated by the wrathful son of Pritha, Kiritin, the great car-warrior of the world". O descendant of Bharata, talking thus, all the troops of your army went to their tents from the field of battle.

sn: विभ्राजमानैश्च तथा प्रदीपैः। किरीटिवित्रासितसर्वयोधा चक्रे निवेशं ध्वजिनी कुरूणाम्॥
en: All the troops of the Kuru army frightened by Kiritin then went into their tents illuminated by thousands of torches and by innumerable lamps.

sn: संजय उवाच मनीकिनीनां प्रमुखे महात्मा। ययौ सपत्नान् प्रति जातकोपो वृतः समग्रेण बलेन भीष्मः॥
en: Sanjaya said O descendant of Bharata, when the night passed away, the illustrious Bhishma with his wrath excited followed by a very large numbers of troops, going at the head of the Kuru army charged the enemy's troops.

sn: तं द्रोणदुर्योधनबालिकाश्च तथैव दुर्मर्षणचित्रसेनौ। नृपास्तथाऽन्ये प्रययुः समन्तात्॥
en: Drona, and Duryodhana, Balhika, Durmarshans, Chitrasena, the mighty Jayadratha and other royal heroes backed by a large number of troops accompanied him.

sn: स तैर्महद्भिश्च महारथैश्च तेजस्विभिर्वीर्यवद्धिश्च राजन्। वृतः स देवैरिव वज्रपाणिः॥
en: Surrounded by these great and mighty carwarriors all possessing great prowess and energy, O king, he shone in the midst of those foremost of royal heroes like the lord of the celestial in the midst of the celestial.

sn: तस्मिन्ननीकप्रमुखे विषक्ता दोधूयमानाश्च महापताकाः। सुरक्तपीतासितपाण्डुराभा महागजस्कन्धगता विरेजुः॥
en: The magnificent standards on the backs of the elephants stationed in front of the various divisions of the army waved in the air and looked highly beautiful with yellow, black and brown colours.

sn: सा वाहिनी शान्तनवेन गुप्ता महारथैर्वारणवाजिभिश्च। बभौ सविद्युत्स्तनयिलुकल्पा जलागमै द्यौरिव जातमेघा॥
en: That great army with the royal son of Shantanu (Bhishma) at its head and with other great car-warriors and with elephants and horses, looked as resplendent as a mass of clouds charged with lightning or as the sky with gathering clouds in the season of rains.

sn: ततो रणायाभिमुखी प्रयाता प्रत्यर्जुनं शान्तनवाभिगुप्ता। सेना महोग्रा सहसा कुरूणां वेगो यथा भीम इवापगायाः॥
en: Then like the fearful current of the oceangoing Ganga, that great Kuru army, protected by Shantanu's son rushed with great force towards Arjuna.

sn: तं व्यालनानाविधगूढसारं गजाश्वपादातरथौघपक्षम्। व्यूहं महामेघसमं महात्मा ददर्श दूरात् कपिराजकेतुः॥
en: With various kinds of forces possessing great strength and also with innumerable elephants, horses and foot soldiers and carwarriors, the Vyuha invade by the apebannered hero (Arjuna) looked from the distance like a great mass of clouds.

sn: विनिर्ययौ केतुमता रथेन नरर्षभः श्वेतहयेन वीरः। वरूथिना सैन्यमुखे महात्मा वधे धृतः सर्वसपत्नयूनाम्॥
en: That illustrious hero, that foremost of men, standing on his car furnished with his standard and yoked with white steeds went against the enemy's army supported by a large force.

sn: सूपस्करं सोत्तरबन्धुरेषं यत्तं यदूनामृषभेण संख्ये। कपिध्वजं प्रेक्ष्य विषेदुराजौ सहैव पुत्रैस्तव कौरवेयाः॥
en: Seeing that ape-bannered hero accompanied by that foremost of the Yadu race, all the Kurus with your sons were filled with dismay.

sn: प्रकर्षता गुप्तमुदायुधेन किरीटिना लोकमहारथेन। श्चतुश्चतुळलसहस्रकर्णम्॥
en: Your troops saw that best of Vyuhas which was protected by that great car-warriors of the world Kiritin (Arjuna). It had thousands of weapons up-raised and on each of its concerns stood four thousand elephants.

sn: यथा हि पूर्वेऽहनि धर्मराज्ञा व्यूहः कृतः कौरवसत्तमेन। तथा न भूतो भुवि मानुषेषु न दृष्टपूर्वो न च संश्रुतश्च॥
en: This Vyuha of today was like the one which was formed on the day previous by that foremost of Kurus, king Dharamraja Yudhishthira and the like of which had never been seen or heard to before by any man.

sn: ततो यथादेशमुपेत्य तस्थुः पाञ्चालमुख्याः सह चेदिमुख्यैः। ततः समादेशसमाहतानि भेरीसहस्राणि विनेदुराजौ॥
en: Then thousands of drums were loudly beat on the field of battle. There rose from every quareer sounds of conchs and trumpets and lion-like shouts.

sn: शङ्खस्वनास्तूर्यरथस्वनाश्च सर्वेष्वनीकेषु ससिंहनादाः। ततः सबाणानि महास्वनानि विस्फार्यमाणानि धनूंषि वीरैः॥
en: Then bows of loud twang, drawn by heroic warriors, with arrows fixed on the bow brings and the sounds of conchs rose above the uproar made by drums and cymbals.

sn: क्षणेन भेरीपणवप्रणादानन्तर्दधुः शङ्खमहास्वनाश्च। तच्छङ्खशब्दावृतमन्तरिक्षमुद्भूतबीमाद्भुतरेणुजालम्॥
en: The entire sky was filled with the sounds of conchs dust filled every place with that dust the atmosphere appeared as if a canopy had been over-spread. Having seen that canopy, all the brave warriors rushed to the battle.

sn: मालोक्य वीराः सहसाभिपेतुः। रथी रथेनाभिहतः ससूतः पपात साश्वः सरथः सकेतुः॥
en: Car-warriors struck with car-warriors were cut down with their charioteers, horses, car and standards. Elephants struck by elephants and foot soldiers struck by foot soldiers all fell (on the filled of battle).

sn: गजो गजेनाभिहतः पपात पदातिना चाभिहतः पदातिः। ?रीकृतान्यद्भुतदर्शनानि। प्रासैश्च खड्डैश्च समाहतानि सदश्ववृन्दानि सदश्ववृन्दैः॥
en: Impetuous horsemen struck down by impetuous horsemen fell with fearful countenances. All appeared to be exceedingly wonderful.

sn: सुवर्णतारागणभूषितानि सूर्यप्रभाभानि शरावराणि। विदार्यमाणानि परश्वधैश्च प्रासैश्च खड्डैश्च निपेतुरुक्म्॥
en: Excellent shields adorned with golden stars and possessed of the effulgence of the sun, broken by battle axes, lances and swords dropped on the field of battle.

sn: गजैविषाणैर्वरहस्तरुग्णाः केचित् ससूता रथिनः प्रपेतुः। गजर्षभाश्चापि रथर्षभेण निपातिता बाणहताः पृथिव्याम्॥
en: Many car-warriors, mangled and bruised by the tasks and the powerful trunks of elephants fell down with their charioteers, many foremost of car-warriors, struck by the foremost of carwarriors fell on the earth.

sn: गजौघवेगोद्धतसादितानां श्रुत्वा विषेदुः सहसा मनुष्याः। आस्विनं सादिपदातियूनां विषाणगात्रावरताडितानाम्॥
en: Having heard the wails of horsemen and foot soldiers, struck with the tusks and other limbs of elephants or crushed by their huge animals fell down on the field of battle.

sn: सम्भ्रान्तनागाश्वरथे मुहूर्ते महाक्षये सादिपदातियूनाम्। महारथैः सम्परिवार्यमाणो ददर्श भीष्मः कपिराजकेतुम्॥
en: Then when horsemen and foot soldiers were falling fast, and elephants, horses and cars were flying away in fear, Bhishma surrounded by many great car-warriors got a sight of the ape-mannered warrior (Arjuna).

sn: तं पञ्चतालोच्छ्रिततालकेतुः सदश्ववेगाद्भुतवीर्ययानः। महास्त्रबाणाशनिदीप्तिमन्तं किरीटिनं शान्तनवोऽभ्यधावत्॥
en: The plmyra-bannered hero, the son of Shantanu, who had five palmyras on his standard, then rushed upon the diadem decked warrior (Arjuna) whose car was yoked with excellent steeds with possessed wonderful energy and which blazed like the lighting.

sn: मिन्द्रात्मजं द्रोणमुखा विमः। कृपश्च शल्यश्च विविंशतिश्च दुर्योधनः सौमदत्तिश्च राजन्॥
en: O king, thus against that son of Indra who was like Indra himself rushed many warriors headed by Drona, Kripa, Shalya, Vivingshati, Duryodhana and also Somadatta's son.

sn: ततो रथानां प्रमुखादुपेत्य सर्वास्त्रवित् काञ्चनचित्रवर्मा। स्तानर्जुनस्यात्मसुतोऽभिमन्युः॥
en: Then the heroic son of Arjuna Abhimanyu learned in all the weapons and clad in a handsome golden armour, rushed out of the ranks of attacked all your warriors.

sn: मसह्यकर्मा विनिहत्य कार्ष्णिः। बभौ महामन्त्रहुतार्चिमाली भगवानिवाग्निः॥ सदोगतः सन्
en: That son of Arjuna baffled the weapons of all the mighty warriors. He looked effulgent as the exalted Agni on the sacrificial alter when invoked with high Mantras.

sn: ततः स तूर्णं रुधिरोदफेनां कृत्वा नदीमाशु रणे रिपूणाम्। जगाम सौभद्रमतीत्य भीष्मो महारथं पार्थमदीनसत्त्वः॥
en: Then the greatly powerful Bhishma created a river in that field of battle. Its water was made by the blood of foes. But he quickly avoided the son of Subhadra and charged the great car-warrior Pareha.

sn: ततः प्रहस्याद्भुतविक्रमेण गाण्डीवमुक्तेन शिलाशितेना विपाठजालेन महास्त्रजालं विनाशयामास किरीटमाली॥
en: Then Arjuna, adorned with diadem and garlands, with his wonderful Gandiva in his hand, the twang of which resembled the roars of clouds, shot showers of arrows and baffled the showers of arrows (shot by Bhishma).

sn: सक्तकर्मा कपिराजकेतुः। भीष्मं महात्माभिववर्ष तूर्णं शरौघजालैर्विमलैश्च भल्लैः॥
en: That illustrious ape-bannered hero then poured upon Bhishma that foremost of all wielders of arms a shower of sharp arrows and broad-headed polished shafts.

sn: तथैव भीष्माहतमन्तरिक्ष महास्त्रजालं कपिराजकेतोः। विशीर्यमाणं ददृशुस्त्वदीया दिवाकरेणेव तमोऽभिभूतम्॥
en: Your troops then saw that shower of arrow, shot by that great ape-bannered hero, opposed and dispersed by Bhishma, as the sun dispels darkness.

sn: मदीनवत् सत्पुरुषोत्तमाभ्याम्। ददर्श लोकः कुरुसुंजयाच तद् द्वैरथं भीष्मधनंजयाभ्याम्॥
en: Then the Kurus, the Srinjayas, and all other people saw the single combat between those two foremost of men, Bhishma and Arjuna both distinguished by the fearful twang of their bows.

description: Slaughter of the son of Samyamani
sn: संजय उवाच द्रौणिभूरिश्रवाः शल्यश्चित्रसेनश्च मारिष पुत्रः सांयमनेश्चैव सौभद्रं पर्यवारयन्॥
en: Sanjaya said O sire, Drona's son, Bhurishrava, Shalya, Chitrasena, the son of Samyamani all these fought with Subhadra's son.

description: Slaughter of the son of Samyamani
sn: संसक्तमतितेजोभिस्तमेकं ददृशुर्जनाः। पञ्चभिर्मनुजव्यात्रैर्गजैः सिंहशिशुं यथा।॥
en: When he was fighting with these five foremost of men, all saw him endued with great prowess, like a young lion fighting with five elephants.

description: Slaughter of the son of Samyamani
sn: नातिलक्ष्यतया कश्चिन्न शौर्यं न पराक्रमे। बभूव सदृशः काङ्गेर्नास्त्रे नापि च लाघवे॥
en: None among them equaled the son of Arjuna in sureness of aim, in bravery in prowess, in lightness of hands or in the knowledge of weapons.

description: Slaughter of the son of Samyamani
sn: तथा तमात्मजं युद्धे विक्रमन्तमरिंदमम्। दृष्ट्वा पार्थः सुसंयत्तं सिंहनादमथानदत्॥
en: When Partha saw that chastiser of foes, his son thus fighting and displaying his prowess in battle, he sent up a lion-like shout.

description: Slaughter of the son of Samyamani
sn: पीडयानं तु तत् सैन्यं पौत्रं तव विशाम्पते। दृष्ट्वा त्वदीया राजेन्द्र समन्तात् पर्यवारयन्॥
en: O king, having seen your grandson thus afflict your army, your warriors surrounded him from all sides.

description: Slaughter of the son of Samyamani
sn: ध्वजिनीं धार्तराष्ट्राणां दीनशत्रुरदीनवत्। प्रत्युद्ययौ स सौभद्रस्तेजसा च बलेन च॥
en: Then that chastiser of foes, the son of Subhadra, depending on his own prowess and might, advanced with under-pressed heart against the army of the Kurus.

description: Slaughter of the son of Samyamani
sn: तस्य लाघवमार्गस्थमादित्यसदृशप्रभम्। व्यदृश्यत महच्चापं समरे युध्यतः परैः॥
en: When he was thus fighting with the enemy in that battle, his great bow, as effulgent as the sun, was seen by everybody to be incessantly drawn for the purpose of striking at the enemy.

description: Slaughter of the son of Samyamani
sn: स द्रौणिमिषुणैकेन विद्ध्वा शल्यं च पञ्चभिः। ध्वजं सांयमनेश्चैव सोऽष्टाभिश्चिच्छिदे ततः॥
en: Wounding the son of Drona with one arrow and Shalya with five, he cut down the standard of Samyamani's son with eight arrows.

description: Slaughter of the son of Samyamani
sn: रुक्मदण्डां महाशक्तिं प्रेषितां सौमदत्तिना। शितेनोरगसंकाशां पत्रिणापजहार ताम्॥
en: With another sharp arrow, he cut down the great dare with a golden staff which resembled a snake and which was hurled against him by Somadatta's son.

description: Slaughter of the son of Samyamani
sn: शल्यस्य च महावेगानस्यतः समरे शरान्। निवार्यार्जुनदायादो जघान चतुरो हयान्॥
en: Arjuna's son baffled in the very sight of Shalya his hundreds of fearful arrows and killed his four steeds.

description: Slaughter of the son of Samyamani
sn: भूरिश्रवाश्च शल्यश्च द्रौणिः सांयमनि: शलः। नाभ्यवर्तन्त संरलब्धाः काणैर्बाहुबलोदयम्॥
en: Bhurishrava, Shalya, Drona's son, Samyamani and Shala were all seized with panic by seeing the prowess of Arjuna's son. They could not stay before him.

description: Slaughter of the son of Samyamani
sn: ततस्त्रिगर्ता राजेन्द्र मद्राश्च सह केकयैः। पञ्चविंशतिसाहस्रास्तव पुत्रेव चोदिताः॥ धनुर्वेदविदो मुख्या अजेयाः शत्रुभिर्येधि। सहपुत्रं जिघांसन्तं परिवब्रः किरीटिनम्॥
en: O great king, then urged by your son the Trigartas, the Kaikeyas numbering twenty-five thousands, all of whom were foremost of men accomplished in arms and who were incapable of being defeated by any enemy in battle, surrounded Kiritin with his on in order to kill them both.

description: Slaughter of the son of Samyamani
sn: तौ तु तत्र पितापुत्रौ परिक्षिप्तौ महारथौ। । ददर्श ग़जन् पाञ्चाल्यः सेनापतिररिंदम॥
en: O king, that chastiser of foes, the general lissom of the Pandava army, the Panchala prince saw (from a distance) the cars of the father and the son surrounded.

description: Slaughter of the son of Samyamani
sn: स वारणरथौघानां सहस्रैर्बहुभिर्वृतः। वाजिभिः पत्तिभिश्चैव वृतः शतसहस्रशः॥ धनुर्विस्फार्य संक्रुद्धो नोदयित्वा च वाहिनीम्। ययौ तं मद्रकानीकं केकयांश्च परंतप॥
en: Followed by many thousands of horsemen and foot soldiers and many hundreds of elephants and cars and the Madras and the Kaikayas, with his bow drawn in wrath and with all his troops behind him he advanced.

description: Slaughter of the son of Samyamani
sn: तेन कीर्तिमता गुप्तमनीकं दृढधन्वना। संरब्धरथनागाश्वं योत्स्यमानमशोभत॥
en: That division of the Pandava army, protected by that illustrious and firin bow-man and furnished with cars, elephants and horsemen looked exceedingly resplendent as in advanced on battle bent.

description: Slaughter of the son of Samyamani
sn: सोऽर्जुनप्रमुखे यान्तं पाञ्चालकुलवर्धनः। त्रिभिः शारद्वतं बाणैर्जत्रुदेशे समार्पयत्॥
en: When he was thus going to Arjuna's aid, he struck Somadatta's son on his shoulder joint with three arrows.

description: Slaughter of the son of Samyamani
sn: ततः स मद्रकान् हत्वा दशैव दशभिः शरैः। पृष्ठरक्षं जघानाशु भल्लेन कृतवर्मणः॥
en: Wounding the Madrakas with ten sharp arrows, he soon killed the warriors who was protecting the rear of Kritavarma.

description: Slaughter of the son of Samyamani
sn: दमनं चापि दायादं पौरवस्य महात्मनः। जघान विमलाचेण नाराचेन परंतपः॥
en: That O chastiser of foes, then, with a broadheaded arrow killed Damana, the son of Paurava.

description: Slaughter of the son of Samyamani
sn: ततः सांयमनेः पुत्रः पाञ्चाल्यं युद्धदुर्मदम्। अविध्यत् त्रिंशता बाणैर्दशभिश्चास्य सारथिम्॥
en: Then the son of Samyamani wounded the invincible Panchalas prince with ten arrows, and his charioteer with ten more.

description: Slaughter of the son of Samyamani
sn: सोऽतिविद्धो महेष्वासः सृक्किणी परिसंलिहन्। भल्लेन भृशतीक्ष्णेन न चिकर्तास्य कार्मुकम्॥
en: Then that great bowman having been thus wounded, licked with his tongue the corners of his mouth and cut down his enemy's bow with a broad headed and sharp arrow.

description: Slaughter of the son of Samyamani
sn: अथैनं पञ्चविंशत्या क्षिप्रमेव समार्पयत्। अश्वांश्चास्यावधीद् राजन्नुभौ तौ पाjि सारथी॥
en: The Panchala prince soon wounded his foe with twenty five arrows and then O king, the killed his horses and then his two wheel protectors.

description: Slaughter of the son of Samyamani
sn: स हताश्वे रथे तिष्ठन् ददर्श भरतर्षभ। पुत्रः सांयमनेः पुत्रं पाञ्चाल्यस्य महात्मनः॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, Samyamani's son then stood on the car the horses of which were killed, and starred at the illustrious son of the Panchala king.

description: Slaughter of the son of Samyamani
sn: स प्रगृह्य महाघोरं निस्त्रिशवरमायसम्। पदातिस्तूर्णमानछेद् रथस्थं पुरुषर्षभः॥
en: Then taking up a fearful sword made of steel, he walked on foot and came to Drupada's son who was on the car.

description: Slaughter of the son of Samyamani
sn: तं महौघमिवायान्तं खात् पतन्तमिवोरगम्। भ्रान्तावरणनिस्त्रिंशं कालोत्सृष्टमिवान्तकम्॥ दीप्यमानमिवादित्यं मत्तवारणाविक्रमम्। अपश्यनं पाण्डवास्तत्र धृष्टद्युम्नश्च पार्षतः॥
en: The Pandava soldiers as well as the Prishata prince Dhrishtadyumna saw him coming like a surging wave which resembled a snake fallen from the sky. He whirled his sword and looked like the sun. He advanced with the gait of an enraged elephant.

description: Slaughter of the son of Samyamani
sn: तस्य पाञ्चालदायादः प्रतीपमभिधावतः। शितनिस्त्रिशहस्तस्य शरावरणधारिणः॥ बाणवेगमतीतस्य तथाभ्याशमुपेयुषः। त्वरन् सेनापतिः क्रुद्धो बिभेद गदया शिरः॥
en: Thereupon inflamed with rage, the son of the Panchala king, beholding Samyamani's son rush towards him with a sharp sword and buckler in grasp and seeing the other approach his car and beyond the range of arrows crushed his, head with the stroke of his heavy mace.

description: Slaughter of the son of Samyamani
sn: तस्य राजन् स निस्त्रिंशं सुप्रभं च शरावरम्। हतस्य पततो हस्ताद् वेगेन न्यपतद् भुवि॥
en: Then, O monarch, when he was falling down dead, his resplendent sword and shield, loosened from his hands, fell down on th grounds, together with his body.

description: Slaughter of the son of Samyamani
sn: तं निहत्य गदाचेण स लेभे परमां मुदम्। पुत्रः पाञ्चालराजस्य महात्मा भीमविक्रमः॥
en: Thus that high-sculed Panchala prince endued with dreadful might won great fame, by thus having crushed his adversary with his club.

description: Slaughter of the son of Samyamani
sn: तस्मिन् हते महेष्वासे राजपुत्रे महारथे। हाहाकारो महानासीत् तव सैन्यस्य मारिष॥
en: Then, O Sire, when that mighty car-warrior and fierce bowman, that prince, was slain, loud cries of "Oh" and "Alas” war heard in your army.

description: Slaughter of the son of Samyamani
sn: ततः सायंमनिः क्रुद्धौ दृष्ट्वा निहतमात्मजम्। अभिदुद्राव वेगेन पाञ्चाल्यं युद्धदुर्मदम्॥
en: Thereafter, beholding his own son slain, Samyamani inflamed with wrath, impetuously fell upon the Panchala prince, ever invincible in battle.

description: Slaughter of the son of Samyamani
sn: तौ तत्र समरे शूरौ समेतौ युद्धदुर्मदौ। ददृशुः सर्वराजानः कुरवः पाण्डवास्तथा॥
en: Then all the monarchs belonging to the Kuru and the Pandava armies saw those two heroes, those foremost of car-warriors, engaged in battle.

description: Slaughter of the son of Samyamani
sn: ततः सांयमनि: क्रुद्धः पार्षतं परवीरहा। आजघान त्रिभिर्वाणैस्तोत्रैरिव महाद्विपम्॥
en: Then Samyamani, that slayer of hostile heroes, excited with rage, struck the son of Prishata with three arrows, like an elephant rider striking the beast with the hook.

description: Slaughter of the son of Samyamani
sn: तथैव पार्षतं शूरं शल्यः समितिशोभनः। आजधानोरसि क्रुद्धस्ततो युद्धमवर्तत॥
en: Similarly, Shalya also, that beautifier of an assembly, angrily wounded Prishata's heroic son on the breast. Thereupon there commenced another battle.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच दैवमेव परं मन्ये पौरुषादपि संजय। यत् सैन्यं मम पुत्रस्य पाण्डुसैन्येन बाध्यते।।।।
en: Dhritarashtra said I consider, O Sanjaya, destiny to by superior to human endeavor, in as much as, the troops of my son are always being slaughtered by those of the sons of Pandu.

sn: नित्यं हि मामकांस्तात हतानेव हि शंससि। अव्यग्रांश्च प्रहृष्टांश्च नित्यं शंससि पाण्डवान्॥
en: You always, O Suta, tell me, that my troops are slaughtered, whilst on the other hand you say that the Pandava forces are not slaughtered and are all filled with delight.

sn: हीनान् पुरुषकारेण मामकानद्य संजय। पातितान् पात्यमानांश्च हतानेव च शंससि॥
en: You always, O Sanjaya, speak of my troops as being destitute of manliness, as felled and falling and massacred.

sn: युध्यमानान् यथाशक्ति घटमानाञ्जयं प्रति। पाण्डवा हि जयन्त्येव जीयन्ते चैव मामकाः॥
en: Yough they are fighting to the best of their powers, and striving hard to secure victory over them, whilst they are becoming reduced in number.

sn: सोऽहं तीव्राणि दुःखानि दुर्योधनकृतानि च। श्रोष्यामि सततं तात दुःसहानि बहूनि च॥
en: So, O son, I am always hearing of numerous causes of insufferable and poignant grief, engendered by misdeeds of Duryodhana.

sn: तमुपायं न पश्यामि जीयेरन् येन पाण्डवाः न्। मामका विजयं युद्धे प्राप्नुयुर्येन संजय॥
en: I could discover no measure by which the Pandavas could be reduced, also by which, O Sanjaya, my sons would be able to secure victory in this battle.

sn: संजय उवाच शृणु राजन् स्थिरो क्षयं मनुष्यदेहानां गजवाजिरथक्षयम्। भूत्वा तवैवापनयो महान्॥
en: Sanjaya said Listen, O monarch, with patience, to the description of the destruction of human hosts and of the hosts of steeds elephants and cars this mighty evil owes its origin to you.

sn: धृष्टद्युम्नस्तु शल्येन पीडितो नवभिः शरैः। पीडयामास संक्रुद्धो मद्राधिपतिमायसैः॥
en: Dhrishtadyumna, being afflicted by Shalya with nine arrows, was inflamed with wrath; and he afflicted the ruler of the Madras, in return, with dares made of steel.

sn: तत्राद्भुतमपश्याम पार्षतस्य पराक्रमम्। न्यवारयत यस्तूर्णं शल्यं समितिशोभनम्॥
en: Then we saw the highly wonderful prowess of the son of Prishata, as he speedily checked (the career of) Shalya the ornament of assemblies.

sn: नान्तरं दृश्यते तत्र तयोश्च रथिनोस्तदा। मुहूर्तमिव तद् युद्धं तयोः सममिवाभवत्॥
en: No weakness was detected in any one of them, when enraged, they were engaged in the battle. The combat between them seemed to last only for a moment.

sn: ततः शल्यो महाराज धृष्टद्युम्नस्य संयुगे। धनुश्चिच्छेद भल्लेन पीतेन निशितेन च।॥
en: Then, O mighty monarch, in that fight, Shalya cut down the bow of Dhrishtadyumna with a keen pointed yellow dare.

sn: अथैनं शरवर्षेण च्छादयामास संयुगे। गिरिं जलागमे यद्वज्जलदा जलवृष्टिभिः॥
en: Also, Bharata, he covered Dhrishtadyumna with showers of arrows, like clouds, swelling with rain, covering a mountain at the rainy season.

sn: अभिमन्युस्तत: क्रुद्धो धृष्टद्युम्ने च पीडिते। अभिदुद्राव वेगेन मद्रराजरथं प्रति॥
en: When Dhrishtadyumna was being thus fermented, Abhimanyu, inflamed with wrath, rushed with violence against the car of the king of the Madras.

sn: ततो मद्राधिपरथं कार्णः प्राप्यातिकोपनः। आर्तायनिममेयात्मा विव्याध निशितैः शरैः॥
en: Then the highly excited nephew of Krishna, that hero of immeasurable should, having reached near the car of the Madra king, pierced Artayani with three whetted shafts.

sn: ततस्तु तावका राजन् परीप्सन्तोऽर्जुनि रणे। मद्रराजरथं तूर्णं परिवार्यावतस्थिरे॥
en: Thereat, O monarch, your troops desirous of resting the son of Arjuna in battle, speedily formed themselves in a circle around the chariot of the ruler of the Madras.

sn: दुर्योधनो विकर्णश्च दुःशासनविविंशती। दुर्मर्षणो दुःसहश्च चित्रसेनोऽथ दुर्मुखः॥
en: Duryodhana, Vikarna, Dushasana, Vivingshati, Durmarshana Dusaha, Chitrasena, Durmukha.

sn: सत्यव्रतश्च भद्रं ते पुरुमित्रश्च भारत। एते मद्राधिपरथं पालयन्तः स्थिता रणे॥
en: Satyavrata, Purumitra and the mighty carwarrior Vikarna, these stationed themselves in the filed for protecting the chariot of the ruler of the Madras.

sn: तान् भीमसेनः संक्रुद्धो धृष्टद्युम्नश्च पार्षतः। द्रौपदेयाऽभिमन्युश्च माद्रीपुत्रौ च पाण्डवौ॥
en: Threat Bhimsena, excited with rage, and Dhrishtadyumna of Prishata's race, the sons of Draupadi and Abhimanyu, the twin sons of Pandu by Madri.

sn: धार्तराष्ट्रान् दशरथान् दशैव प्रत्यवारयन्। नानारूपाणि शस्त्राणि विसृजन्तो विशाम्पते॥१९॥
en: These ten warriors opposed the ten warriors of Duryodhana's hosts, discharging 0 monarch, weapons of diverse shape.

sn: अभ्यवर्तन्त संहृष्टाः परस्परवधैषिणः। ते वै समेयुः संग्रामे राजन् दुर्मन्त्रिते तव॥
en: It is, O monarch, through the wicked policy of yours that those warriors inflamed with rage then approached and encountered one another in battle, out of a desire for slaying one another.

sn: तस्मिन् दशरथे क्रुद्धे वर्तमाने महाभये। तावकानां परेषां वा प्रेक्षका रथिनोऽभवन॥
en: When those ten warriors, wrought up with wrath, met the other ten in that awful battle, thereat of the car-warriors of your army and of the army of your foes became sight seers.

sn: शस्त्राण्यनेकरूपाणि विसृजन्तो महारथाः। अन्योन्यमभिमर्दन्तः सम्प्रहारं प्रचक्रिरे॥
en: Those mighty car-warriors shooting weapons of diverse shape and roaring at one another began to smite one bother.

sn: ते तदा जातसंरम्भाः सर्वेऽन्योन्यं जिघांसवः। अन्योन्यमभिमर्दन्तः स्पर्धमानाः परस्परम्॥
en: Then in the battle, inflamed with both and desirous of slaying one another, those heroes roared at one another, and boasted of their prowess.

sn: अन्योन्यस्पर्धया राजज्ञातयः सङ्गता मिथः। महास्त्राणि विमुञ्चन्तः समापेतुरमर्षिणः॥
en: Then O monarch, those kinsfolk that had met together, burning with jealousy and challenging one another, fell upon one another, discharging mighty weapons at the same time.

sn: दुर्योधनस्तु संक्रुद्धो धृष्टद्युम्नं महारणे। विव्याध निशितैर्बाणैश्चतुर्भिः समरे द्रुतम्॥
en: Inflamed with wrath, Duryodhana in that fierce battle pierced Dhrishtadyumna with four whetted arrows; and in battle, the feat was wonderful.

sn: दुर्मर्षणश्च विंशत्या चित्रसेनश्च पञ्चभिः। दुर्मुखो नवभिर्बाणैर्दुःसहश्चापि सप्तभिः॥
en: Durmarshana pierced him (Dhrishtadyumna) with twenty shafts, Chitrasena with five, Durmukha with nine, Dusaha with seven.

sn: विविंशतिः पञ्चभिश्च त्रिभिर्दुःशासनस्तथा। तान् प्रत्यविध्यद् राजेन्द्र पार्षतः शत्रुतापनः॥
en: Vivingshati with five, and Dushasana with three. Them, O monarch, the son of Prishata, the slayer of his foes, pierced.

sn: एकैकं पञ्चविंशत्या दर्शयन् पाणिलाघवम्। सत्यव्रतं च समरे पुरुमित्रं च भारत॥ अभिमन्युरविध्यत् तु दशभिर्दशभिः शरैः। माद्रीपुत्रौ तु समरे मातुलं मातृनन्दनौ॥ अविध्येतां शरैस्तीक्ष्णैस्तदद्भुतमिवाभवत्। ततः शल्यो महाराज स्वस्रीयौ रथिनां वरौ॥ शरैर्बहुभिरानछेत् कृतप्रतिकृतैषिणौ। छाद्यमानौ ततस्तौ तु माद्रीपुत्रौ न चेलतुः॥
en: In return, each with twenty shafts displaying great lightness of hands. O Bharata Abhimanyu in that battle pierced Satyavrata and Purumitra each with ten shafts. The sons of Madri, the delighters of their mother, in that battle covered their maternal uncle with a shower of sharp shafts; and that seemed indeed marvelous. Thereupon, O mighty monarch, Shalya covered with innumerable arrows those nephews of his, those two foremost of car warriors, who were desirous of counteracting the stratagems of their uncle (Shalya himself). Yough thus covered over with arrows, the twin sons of Madri flinched not.

sn: अथ दुर्योधनं दृष्ट्वा भीमसेनो महाबलः। विधित्सुः कलहस्यान्तं गदां जग्राह पाण्डव:॥
en: Thereafter the Pandava Bhimasena endued with great might beholding Duryodhana and desirous of putting and end to the strife, grasped his mace.

sn: तमुद्यतगदं दृष्ट्वा कैलासमिव शृङ्गिणम्। भीमसेनं महाबाहुं पुत्रास्ते प्राद्रवन् भयात्॥
en: Seeing that mighty armed Bhimsena with uplifted mace look like the Kailasa mount towering with its peaks your sons fled out of terror.

sn: दुर्योधनस्तु संक्रुद्धो मागधं समचोदयत्। अनीकं दशसाहस्रं कुञ्चराणां तरस्विनाम्॥
en: Duryodhana however wrought up with anger urged against Bhima the Magadha division consisting of ten thousands swiftcoursing elephants.

sn: गजानीकेन सहितस्तेन राजा सुयोधनः। मागधं पुरतः कृत्वा भीमसेनं समभ्ययात्॥
en: King Suyodhana then accompanied by that division of elephants, and placing the ruler of the Maghadas in front of him, advanced towards Bhimasena.

sn: आपतन्तं च तं दृष्ट्वा गजानीकं वृकोदरः। गदापाणिरवारोहद् रथात् सिहं इवोन्नदन्॥
en: Thereat Vrikodara, beholding that division of elephants make towards himself,, descended from his car, holding a mace in his hands and roaring out like a lion.

sn: अद्रिसारमयीं गुर्वी प्रगृह्य महतीं गदाम्। अभ्यधावद् गजानीकं व्यादितास्य इवान्तकः॥
en: Grasping a mighty and heavy mace made of the essence of adamant, Bhimasena charged that division of elephants, like Death himself with his mouth wide open.

sn: स गजान् गदया निघ्नन् व्यचरत् समरे बली। भीमसेनो महाबाहुः सवज्र इव वासवः॥
en: Then like the slayer of Vritra moving amidst the Danava host, the mighty armed Bhimasena, endued with great strength, careered on the filed of battle, slaughtering elephants with his mace.

sn: तस्य नादेन महता मनोहृदयकम्पिना। व्यत्यचेष्टन्त संहत्य गजा भीमस्य गर्जतः॥
en: Then at the defending shouts of the roaring Bhima-shouts that were capable of producing a tremor in the hare and in the mind, the elephants huddling together were deprived of the power of moving.

sn: ततस्तु द्रौपदीपुत्राः सौभद्रश्च महारथः। नकुलः सहदेवश्च धृष्टद्युम्नश्च पार्षतः॥
en: Then the sons of Draupadi, the mighty carwarrior the son of Subhadra, and Nakula, Sahadeva and Dhrishtadyumna the son of Prishata.

sn: पृष्ठं भीमस्य रक्षन्तः शरवर्षेण वारणान्। अभ्यवर्षन्त धावन्तो मेघा इव गिरीन् यथा॥
en: Supporting Bhima's car, proceeded behind him, checking the foe with their shower of arrows, like clouds drenching the mountains with rain.

sn: क्षुरैः क्षुरप्रैर्भल्लैश्च पीतैश्चाञ्जलिकैः शितैः। व्यरत्रुत्तमाङ्गानि पाण्डवा गजयोधिनाम्॥
en: With Kshuras the Kshurapras and Bhallas and Anjalikas, all well-sharpened and tempered, the Pandava warriors cut down the heads of those who were fighting on the backs of elephants.

sn: शिरोभिः प्रपतद्भिश्च बाहुभिश्च विभूषितैः। अश्मवृष्टिरिवाभाति पाणिभिश्च सहाकुशैः॥
en: In consequence of the thick falling of the heads (of elephants-riders), their arms decked with ornaments and their hands grasping the iron hook, a shower of stones appeared to fall.

sn: हृतोत्तमाङ्गाः स्कन्धेषु गजानां गजयोधिनः। अदृश्यन्ताचलाचेषु दुमा भग्नशिखा इव॥
en: And elephants-riders deprived of heads, seated as they were on the necks of those beasts, appeared like ties on a mountain with their heads broken.

sn: धृष्टद्युम्नहतानन्यानपश्याम महागजान्। पतत: पात्यमानांश्च पार्षतेन महात्मना॥
en: We also saw many other mighty elephants, felled and falling, slain by Dhrishtadyumna, the high-souled son of Prishata.

sn: मागधोऽथ महीपालो गजमैरावणोपमम्। प्रेषयामास समरे सौभद्रस्य रथं प्रति॥
en: Thereafter, the ruler of the Magadha territory, goaded in that battle, against the car not of Subhadra's son, an elephants that resembled Airavata itself.

sn: तमापतन्तं सम्प्रेक्ष्य मागधस्य महागजम्। जघानैकेषुणा वीरः सौभद्रः परवीरहा॥
en: Then the heroic son of Subhadra, that slayer of hostile heroes, beholding that mighty elephant of the ruler of the Magadhas make towards himself, killed it with a single shaft.

sn: तस्यावर्जिनागस्य कार्ष्णिः परपुरंजयः। राज्ञो रजतपुखेन भल्लेनापाहरच्छिरः॥
en: Then the nephew of Krishna that conqueror of hostile cities cut down with a Bhalla of silvery wings, the head of the king who could extricate himself from the (falling)elephants.

sn: विगाह्य तद् गजानीकं भीमसेनोऽपि पाण्डवः। व्यचरत् समरे मृद्गन् गजानिन्द्रो गिरीनिव॥
en: Then Bhimasena the son of Pandu, also penetrating that division of elephants, careered in the filed, crushing the elephants, like Indra crushing the mountains.

sn: एकप्रहारनिहतान् भीमसेनेन दन्तिनः। अपश्याम रणे तस्मिन् गिरीन् वज्रहतानिव॥
en: In that battle, we also beheld elephants smashed by Bhimasena, each with a single stoke, like cliffs rent open by the thunder-bolt.

sn: भग्नदन्तान् भग्नकटान् भग्नसक्थांश्च वारणान्। भग्नपृष्ठत्रिकानन्यान् निहतान् पर्वतोपमान्॥ नदतः सीदतश्चान्यान् विमुखान् समरे गतान्। विद्रुतान् भयसंविग्नांस्तथा विशकृतोऽपरान्॥ भीमसेनस्य मार्गेषु पतितान् पर्वतोपमान्।
en: Elephants prodigious like mountains were slain having their tusks broken, their temples, their bones, their backs and their frontal globes smashed.

sn: अपश्यं निहतान् नागान् राजन् निष्ठीवतोऽपरान्॥ वमन्तो रुधिरं चान्ये भिन्नकुम्भा महागजाः।
en: We saw, O monarch, some of those beasts slain and some with mouths foaming (we saw) other mighty elephants with their frontal globes smashed, vomiting blood in profusion.

sn: विह्वलन्तो गता भूमि शैला इव धरातले॥ मेदोरुधिरदिग्धाङ्गो वसामज्जासमुक्षितः।
en: Some fell down on the grounds overwhelmed with terror, and they resembled huge hills and were soiled in every pare of their body with fat and blood, and were almost bathed in marrow and brain matter.

sn: व्यचरत् समरे भीमो दण्डपाणिरिवान्तकः॥ गजानां रुधिरक्लिन्नां गदां बिभ्रद् वृकोदरः।
en: Bhima careered in the filed like the Destroyer himself with his mace in his hand. Vrikodara whirling his mace that was drenched with the blood of the elephants.

sn: घोरः प्रतिभयश्चासीत् पिनाकीव पिनाकधृक्॥ सम्मथ्यमानाः क्रुद्धेन भीमसेनेन दन्तिनः।
en: Appeared dreadful like Pinaki (Shiva) himself wielding the bow Pinaka. Crushed by the wrathful Bhimasena, the elephants.

sn: सहसा प्राद्रवन् क्लिष्टा मृनन्तस्तव वाहिनीम्॥ तं हि वीरं महेष्वासं सौभद्रप्रमुखा रथाः। पर्यरक्षन्त युध्यन्तं वज्रायुधमिवामराः॥ शोणिताक्ता गदां बिभ्रदुक्षितां गजशोणितैः।
en: Sorely afflicted, suddenly fled away, smashing the ranks of your own army. The mighty bowmen and car-warriors headed by the son of Subhadra, protected that hero as he battled, like the immortals protecting the wielder of the thunderbolt. Grasping his bloodstained mace almost bathed in the blood of clephants.

sn: कृतान्त इव रौद्रात्मा भीमसेनो व्यदृश्यत॥ व्यायच्छमानं गदया दिखं सर्वासु भारत। अपश्याम रणे भीमं नृत्यन्तमिव शंकरम्॥ यमदण्डोपमां गुर्वीमिन्द्राशनिसमस्वनाम्। अपश्याम महाराज रौद्रां विशसनी गदाम्॥ विमिश्रां केशमज्जाभिः प्रदिग्धां रुधिरेण च।
en: Bhimasena of fierce should then appeared like the destroyer himself. then O Bharata, we saw Bhimasena whirling his mace in all directions appear like the god Shiva in the course of his wild dance. We beheld, O mighty monarch, his heavy and sounding mace that resembled the club of the destroyer himself, the whiz of which equalled the roar of Indra thunder, which was fierce to look at, and which was stained copiously with blood and smeared with marrow and hair,

sn: पिनाकमिव रुद्रस्य क्रुद्धस्याभिघ्नतः पशून्॥ यथा पशूनां संघातं यष्ट्या पालः प्रकालयेत्।
en: And (lastly) which resembled the Pinaka of the enraged Rudra engaged in slaughtering animals. Just as a herdsman belabours his herd with a cudgel,

sn: तथा भीमो गजानीकं गदया समकालयत्॥ गदया वध्यमानास्ते मार्गणैश्च समन्ततः।
en: So Bhima belaboured the elephants division with his mace. smitten by that mace, as also by means of arrows on all sides,

sn: स्वान्यनीकानि मृनन्तः प्राद्रवन् कुञ्जरास्तव॥ महावात इवाभ्राणि विधमित्वा स वारणान्। अतिष्ठत् तुमुले भीमः श्मशान इव शूलभृत्॥
en: The elephants heavily fled away from the field, smashing the chariots of their own host. Like tempest driving away clouds, Bhimasena driving away from the field those elephants, stood there like the wielder of the trident (Shiva) standing on the cremation grounds.

sn: संजय उवाच हते तस्मिन् गजानीके पुत्रो दुर्योधनस्तव। भीमसेनं नतेत्येवं सर्वसैन्यान्यचोदयत्॥
en: Sanjaya said When that division of elephants had been crushed, your son Duryodhana, commanded his whole force saying, Kill Bhimasena.

sn: ततः सर्वाण्यनीकानि तव पुत्रस्य शासनात्। अभ्यद्रवन् भीमसेनं नदन्तं भैरवान् रवान्॥
en: Thereat, the entire army, at the command of your son, rushed against Bhimasena, setting up at the same time a dreadful uproar.

sn: तं बलौघमपर्यन्तं देवैरपि सुदुःसहम्। आपतन्तं सुदुष्पारं समुद्रमिव पर्वणि॥ रथनागाश्वकलिलं शङ्खदुन्दुभिनादितम्। अनन्तरथपादातं रजसा सर्वतो वृतम्॥ तं भीमसेनः समरे महोदधिमिवापरम्। सेनासागरमक्षोभ्यं वेलेव समवारयत्॥
en: That infinite army, whose impetus it would have been impossible even for the gods to bear, that army which was incapable of being crossed like the sea on a Parva day, that army that swarmed with car-warriors, steeds and elephants and that resounded with the blare of conchs, the rattle of chariots, and the sound drums, that numbered numbered innumerable foot soldiers and car-warriors, that was shrouded in a cloud of dust-that veritable ocean of advancing hostile force that was incapable of being agitated, Bhimasena withstood in battle, like the banks resisting the surging sea.

sn: तदाश्चर्यमपश्याम पाण्डवस्य महात्मनः। भीमसेनस्य समरे राजन् कर्मातिमानुषम्॥
en: The, O monarch, we beheld in that battle, the marvelous and super human feat achieved by the high-souled son of Pandu, namely Bhimasena.

sn: उदीर्णान् पार्थिवान् सर्वान् साश्वान् सरथकुञ्जरान्। असम्भ्रमं भीमसेनो गदया समवारयत्॥
en: Undauntedly did Bhimasena check with his mace, the rulers of men who, excited with wrath, had been advancing towards him, on their steeds, chariots and Bhimasena.

sn: स संवार्य बलौघांस्तानं गदया रथिनां वरः। अतिष्ठत् तुमुले भीमो गिरिर्मेरुरिवाचलः॥
en: Bhima, that foremost of those endued with might, having thus checked with his mace the career of the vast army, stood in that dreadful confusion, immovable as the mount Meru itself.

sn: तस्मिन् सुतुमुले घोरे काले परमदारुणे। भ्रातरश्चैव पुत्राश्च धृष्टद्युम्नश्च पार्षतः॥
en: In that most terrific, fierce and ruthless encounter, his brothers, and and sons, and Dhrishtadyumna the son of Prishata.

sn: द्रौपदेयाऽभिमन्युश्च शिखण्डी चापराजितः। न प्राजहन् भीमसेनं भये जाते महाबलम्॥
en: And the sons of Draupadi, and Abhimanyu and the ever-victorious Shikhandin, these mighty warriors did not forsake Bhimasena, as they all apprehended danger.

sn: ततः शैक्यायसीं गुर्वी प्रगृह्य महतीं गदाम्। अधावत् तावकान् योधान् दण्डपाणिरिवान्तकः॥
en: Thereafter taking up his huge and heavy mace made of Shaikya iron, he (Bhimasena) rushed against your warriors, like the Destroyer himself wielding his club.

sn: पोथयन् स्थवृन्दानि वाजिवृन्दानि चाभिभूः। कर्षयन् स्थवृन्दानि बाहुवेगेन पाण्डवः॥
en: Smashing down hosts of charioteers and also hosts of steeds, that mighty and heroic Bhima careered on the file like fire spreading at the end of a Yuga.

sn: विनिनन् व्यचरत् संख्ये युगान्ते कालवद् विभुः। उरुवेगेन संकर्षन् रथजालानि पाण्डवः॥
en: Slaughtering in that battle numerous warriors, like Death himself destroying animals at the end of a Yuga, smashing with the impetus of his thighs hosts of cars, that son of Pandu,

sn: बलानि सम्पमर्दाशु नड्वलानीव कुञ्जरः। मृनन् रथेभ्यो रथिनो गजेभ्यो गजयोधिनः॥
en: Began to crush your army with the greatest ease, like an elephant crushing a cluster of reeds. Dragging down warriors from the terraces of their respective cars, and felling elephant-riders from the back of the elephants on which they were fighting.

sn: सादिनचाश्वपृष्ठेभ्यो भूमौ चापि पदातिनः। गदया व्यधमत् सर्वान् वातो वृक्षानिवौजसा॥
en: And horse-soldiers from the back of the steeds, and crushing foot-soldiers as they stood on the ground, Bhima killed all with his mace, like a tempest breaking down trees with its violence.

sn: भीमसेनो महाबाहुस्तव पुत्रस्य वै बले। सापि मज्जावसामांसैः प्रदिग्धा रुधिरेण च॥
en: Bhimasena produced a fierce carnage in the force of your son. Smeared with fat, marrow, serum and flesh, and be spattered with blood,

sn: अदृश्यत महारौद्रा गदा नागाश्वपातनी। तत्र तत्र हतैश्चापि मनुष्यगजवाजिभिः॥
en: His mace, that dealt death to steeds and elephants, appeared exceedingly terrible. With corpses and carcasses of steeds, men and elephants and horse-soldiers.

sn: रणाङ्गणं समभवन्मृत्योरावाससंनिभम्। पिनाकमिव रुद्रस्य क्रुद्धस्याभिघ्नतः पशून्॥
en: The field of battle wore the appearance of the (gloomy) abode of Death. Like the Pinaka of the enraged Rudra engaged in slaughtering animals.

sn: यमदण्डोपमामुग्रामिन्द्राशनिसमस्वनाम्। ददृशुर्भीमसेनस्य रौद्रीं विशसनीं गदाम्॥
en: Like the dreadful club of the destroyer himself, and like the effulgent thunderbolt of Indra himself, was seen the terrible-loO king and death-dealing club of Bhimasena.

sn: आविद्ध्यतो गदां तस्य कौन्तेयस्य महात्मनः। बभौ रूपं महाघोरं कालस्येव युगक्षये॥
en: The appearance of that high-souled son of Kunti, as he whirled his mace, became as terrible as that of the Destroyer himself at the time of the universal destruction.

sn: तं तथा महतीं सेनां द्रावयन्तं पुनः पुनः। दृष्ट्वा मृत्युमिवायान्तं सर्वे विमनसोऽभवन्॥
en: Beholding him repeatedly smash that mighty host and advance like Death himself, all the warriors became cheerless.

sn: यतो यतः प्रेक्षते स्म गदामुद्यम्य पाण्डवः। तेन तेन स्म दीर्यन्ते सर्वसैन्यानि भारत॥
en: Uplifting his mace, in whichever direction the son of Pandu turned his eyes 0 Bharata, from that direction, all the soldiers fled (deserting their ranks).

sn: प्रदारयन्तं सैन्यानि बलेनामितविक्रमम्। ग्रसमानमनीकानि व्यादितास्यमिवान्तकम्॥ तं तथा भीमकर्माणं प्रगृहीतमहागदम्। दृष्ट्वा वृकोदरं भीष्मः सहसैव समभ्ययात्॥
en: Beholding Vrikodara of fierce deeds armed with his mace and unconquered by the sea of soldiers and seeing him break the ranks and devour the hostile troops, like Death himself with his gaping mouth, Bhishma rushed at him with great impetuosity,

sn: महता रथघोषेण रथेनादित्यवर्चसा। छादयशरवर्षेण पर्जन्य इव वृष्टिमान्॥
en: Riding on his car of great effulgence and of rattle as loud as the rumble of clouds, and covering the sky with the shower of his arrows, like Parjanya pouring down rain.

sn: तमायान्तं तथा दृष्ट्वा व्यात्ताननमिवान्तकम्। भीष्मं भीमो महाबाहुः प्रत्युदीयादमर्षितः॥
en: Seeing him make towards himself like the Destroyer with wide upon mouth, the mightyarmed Bhimasena inflamed with rage, rushed towards him.

sn: तस्मिन् क्षणे सात्यकिः सत्यसंध: शिनिप्रवीरोऽभ्यपतत्पितामहम्। निघ्नन्नमित्रान् धनुषा दृढेन संकम्पयंस्तव पुत्रस्य सैन्यम्॥
en: That very moment, the heroic grand son of Shini namely Satyaki fell upon the grand-sire (Bhishma), and he began to slay his enemies with his strong bow, agitating the army of your son the while.

sn: तं यान्तमश्चै रजतप्रकाशैः शरान् वपन्तं निशितान् सुपुङ्खान्। नाशक्नुवन् धारयितुं तदानीं सर्वे गणा भारत ये त्वदीयाः॥
en: That at time, O Bharata, all the warriors of your ariny were unable to check him, as he advanced, borne by steeds of Argentine effulgence, discharging (right and left) his shafts well-whetted and furnished with beautiful wings.

sn: रलम्बुषो राक्षसोऽसौ तदानीम्। शरैश्चतुर्भिः प्रतिविद्ध्य तं च नप्ता शिनेरभ्यपतद् रथेन॥
en: Then the Rakshasa Alambhusa pierced him with ten shafts only. Piercing him in return with fine arrows, the grandson of Shini, advanced on his car.

sn: अन्वागतं वृष्णिवरं निशम्य तं शत्रुमध्ये परिवर्तमानम्। प्रद्रावयन्तं कुरुपुङ्गवांश्च पुनः पुनश्च प्रणदन्तमाजौ॥
en: Seeing that heroic warrior of the race of the Vrishnis thus advancing, and whirling in the midst of his enemies, and checking the foremost of the Kurus and uttering repeated war-cries in the battle,

sn: योधास्त्वदीयाः शरवर्षैरवर्षन् मेघा यथा भूधरमम्बुवेगैः। मध्यन्दिने सूर्यमिवातपन्तम्॥
en: your warriors showered their arrow downpour on him, like rain clouds drenching the mountains with torrents of rain. They wear unable to check the carrier of that hero who appeared like the mid-day sun in his full glory.

sn: दृते राजन् सोमदत्तस्य पुत्रात्। स वै समादाय धनुर्महात्मा भूरिश्रवा भारत सौमदत्तिः॥ दृष्ट्वा रथान् स्वान् व्यपनीयमानान् प्रत्युद्ययौ सात्यकिं योद्भुमिच्छन्॥
en: At that time, o king there was none (in your army) who was not cheerless, except the son of Somadatta, by namc Bhurishravas. This one seeing the car warriors of his side routed, Bharata grasping his bow of fierce impetus, rushed at Satyaki desirous of fighting with the latter.

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: संजय उवाच ततो भूरिश्रवा राजन् सात्यकिं नवभिः शरैः। प्राविध्यद् भृशसंक्रुद्धस्तोत्रैरिव महाद्विपम्॥
en: Sanjaya said Then, O monarch, inflamed with wrath he pierced Satyaki with nine arrows, like an elephant-driver piercing the animal with the iron hook.

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: कौरवं सात्यकिश्चैव शरैः संनतपर्वभिः। अवारयदमेयात्मा सर्वलोकस्य पश्यतः॥
en: Thereat, before the very eyes of the spectators, Satyaki of immeasurable soul shrouded with his arrows of straight-joints, him of the Kaurava host.

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: ततो दुर्योधनो राजा सोदर्यैः परिवारितः। सौमदत्तिं रणे यत्तः समन्तात् पर्यवारयत्॥
en: Thereupon king Duryodhana, encircled by his uterine brothers, surrounded (for supporting him) the son of Somadatta, who had been striving hard in the encounter.

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: तं चैव पाण्डवाः सर्वे सात्यकिं रभसं रणे! परिवार्य स्थिताः संख्ये समन्तात् सुमहौजसः॥
en: In the same manner, the Pandavas endued with great might, speedily forming themselves in a circle round Satyaki, stood (ready) in that battle.

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: भीमसेनस्तु संक्रुद्धौ गदामुद्यम्य भारत। दुर्योधनमुखान् सर्वान् पुत्रांस्ते पर्यवारयत्॥
en: Then, O Bharata, Bhimasena wrought up with wrath, with his upraised mace, opposed your sons headed by Duryodnana himself.

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: रथैरनेकसाहौः क्रोधामर्षसमन्वितः नन्दकस्तव पुत्रस्तु भीमसेनं महाबलम्॥ विव्याध विशिखैः षड्भिः कङ्कपत्रैः शिलाशितैः। दुर्योधनश्च समरे भीमसेनं महारथम्॥ आजघानोरसि क्रुद्धो मार्गणैर्नवभिः शितैः। ततो भीमो महाबाहुः स्वरथं सुमहाबलः॥ आरुरोह रथश्रेष्ठं विशोकं चेदमब्रवीत्। एते महारथाः शूरा धार्तराष्ट्राः समागताः॥
en: Supported by many thousand of cars, and excited with rage and fury, your son Nandaka pierced Bhimasena of great might with keenpointed shafts whetted on stone and winged with the feathers of the Kanka bird. Then also, O monarch, Duryodhana excited with rage, in that fierce fight, struck Bhimasena on the breast with nine whetted shafts. Thereafter the mighty-armed Bhimasena endued with superior strength mounted on his own most excellent chariot and thus addressed his charioteer Vishoka. These heroic and mighty carwarriors, these sons of Dhritarashtra endued with prowess.

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: मामेव भृशसंक्रुद्धा हन्तुमभ्युद्यता युधि। मनोरथद्रुमोऽस्माकं चिन्तितो बहुवार्षिकः॥ सफल: सूत चायेह योऽहं पश्यामि सोदरान्। यत्राशोक समुक्षिप्ता रेणवो रथनेमिभिः॥ प्रयास्यन्त्यन्तरिक्षं हि शरवृन्दैदिगन्तरे। तत्र तिष्ठति संनद्धः स्वयं राजा सुयोधनः॥ भ्रातरश्चास्य संनद्धाः कुलपुत्रा मदोत्कटाः। एतानद्य हनिष्यामि पश्यतस्ते न संशयः॥ तस्मान्ममाश्वान् संग्रामे यत्तः संयच्छ सारथे।
en: Excited with anger, are all striving to slay me in battle. Beholding ihose brothers of Duryodhana, I see tree of my desirous so long is now fruitful. O deprived of sorrow, where the dusts of chariots spread with shafts into all directions of the sky, Duryodhana stays for fight. Them will I undoubtedly slay today before your very eyes. Therefore, a charioteer, do you drive iny steeds carefully in this encounter.

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: एवमुक्त्वा ततः पार्थस्तव पुत्रं विशाम्पते।॥ विव्याध दशभिस्तीक्ष्णैः शरैः कनकभूषणैः। नन्दकं च त्रिभिर्बाणैरभ्यविध्यत् स्तनान्तरे॥
en: Having thus spoken, O ruler of men, the pointed shafts ornamented with gold. He also pierced Nandaka in return, in the centre of his breast, with three arrows.

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: तं तु दुर्योधनः षष्ट्या विद्ध्वा भीमं महाबलम्। त्रिभिरन्वैः सुनिशितैर्विशोकं प्रत्यविध्यत॥
en: Thereat Duryodhana, having pierced in return Bhima of superior strength with sin arrows, pierced Vishoka with another three well-sharpened shafts.

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: भीमस्य च रणे राजन् धनुश्चिच्छेद भासुरम्। मुष्टिदेशे भृशं तीक्ष्णैस्त्रिभिर्भल्लैर्हसन्निव॥
en: In that battle, O king, as if smiling, Duryodhana with these arrows cut off the effulgent bow of Bhima near the grasp.

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: समरे प्रेक्ष्य यन्तारं विशोकं तु वृकोदरः। पीडितं विशिखैस्तीक्ष्णैस्तव पुत्रेण धन्विना॥
en: Then in that battle, Bhima, beholding his charioteer Vishoka afflicted with shape shafts discharged by the mighty bowman, namely your son,

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: अमृष्यमाणः संरब्धो धनुर्दिव्यं परामृशत्। पुत्रस्य ते महाराज वधार्थं भरतर्षभ॥
en: And unable to brook it and inflamed with wrath, took up another bow of celestial make, in order, O mighty sovereign, O foremost of men, to encompass the death of your son.

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: समाधत्त सुसंक्रुद्धः क्षुरप्रं लोमवाहिनम्। तेन चिच्छेद नृपतेर्भीमः कार्मुकमुत्तमम्॥
en: Inflamed with wrath, he also took up an arrow with a horse-shoe head, furnished with feathery wings, and with it Bhima severed the excellent bow of the king (Duryodhana).

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: सोऽपविद्ध्य धनुश्छिन्नं पुत्रस्ते क्रोधमूर्छितः। अन्यत् कार्मुकमादत्त सत्वरं वेगवत्तरम्॥
en: Thereat your son overwhelmed with fury, throwing off that severed bow, swiftly took up another bow of tougher make.

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: संदधे विशिखं घोरं कालमृत्युसमप्रभम्। तेनाजघान संक्रुद्धो भीमसेनं स्तनान्तरे॥
en: O monarch placing on his bow-string a fierce Visokha shaft that resembled in effulgence the bludgeon of Death himself, your son excited to the highest pitch of fury struck Bhimasena with it, on the centre of his breast.

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: स गाढविद्धो व्यथितः स्यन्दनोपस्थ आविशत्। स निषण्णो रथोपस्थे मूर्छामभिजगाम ह॥
en: There-with struck home and afflicted sore, he (Bhima) squatted on the terrace of his car; and when he was thus seated, he was overwhelmed with a swoon.

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: तं दृष्ट्वा व्यथितं भीममभिमन्युपुरोगमाः। नामृष्यन्त महेष्वासाः पाण्डवानां महारथाः॥
en: Beholding Bhima thus afflicted, the mighty car-warriors of the Pandava host headed by Abhimanyu, all of excellent parts could not brook it.

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: ततस्तु तुमुलां वृष्टिं शस्त्राणां तिग्मतेजसाम्। पातयामासुरव्यग्राः पुत्रस्य तव मूर्धनि॥
en: Then these warriors, without the least flurry, poured on the head of your son a mighty shower of arrows of fierce velocity.

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: प्रतिलभ्य ततः संज्ञां भीमसेनो महाबलः। दुर्योधनं त्रिभिर्विद्ध्वा पुनर्विव्याध पञ्चभिः॥
en: Meanwhile Bhimasena of mighty prowess having regained consciousness, pierced Duryodhana with three shafts and again with another five.

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: शल्यं च पञ्चविंशत्या शरैर्विव्याध पाण्डवः। रुक्मपुङ्खैर्महेष्वासः सविद्धो व्यपयाद् रणात्॥
en: That fierce bowman, that son of Pandava then pierced Shalya with twenty-five shafts furnished with golden wings. Thus pierced, the latter fled from the field of battle.

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: प्रत्युद्ययुस्ततो भीमं तव पुत्राश्चतुर्दश। सेनापतिः सुषेणश्च जलसंधः सुलोचनः॥ उग्रो भीमरथो भीमो वीरबाहुरलोलुपः। दुर्मुखो दुष्प्रधर्षश्च विवित्सुर्विकटः समः॥
en: Thereat your fourteen sons namely, Senapati, Sushena, Jalasandha, Sulochana, Ugra, Bhimaratha, Bhima, Virabahu, Alolupa, Durmukha, Dushpradharsha, Vivitsu, Vikata and Soma, then encountered Bhima (in that battle).

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: विसृजन्तो बहून् बाणान् क्रोधसंरक्तलोचनाः। भीमसेनमभिद्रुत्य विव्यधुः सहिता भृशम्॥
en: With their eyes coppery in rage, and shooting myriads of shafts, they rushed against Bhimasena, piercing him simultaneously.

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: पुत्रांस्तु तव सम्प्रेक्ष्य भीमसेनो महाबलः। सृक्किणी विलिहन् वीरः पशुमध्ये यथा वृकः॥
en: Then the heroic Bhimasena of superior might, beholding your sons, began to lick the corners of his mouth like a wolf in the midst of inferior beasts.

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: अभिपत्य महाबाहुर्गरुत्मानिव वेगितः। सेनापतेः क्षुरप्रेण शिरश्चिच्छेद पाण्डवः॥
en: Then that mighty-armed son of Pandu, swooping down with great violence like Garuda himself, cut off with a horse shoe headed shaft the head of Senapati.

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: सम्प्रहस्य च हृष्टात्मा त्रिभिर्वाणैर्महाभुजः। जलसंधं विनिर्भिद्य सोऽनयद् यमसादनम्॥
en: Then with a cheerful soul, laughing all the while, that one of strong arms, piercing Jarasandha with three shafts, transported him to the abode of Death.

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: सुषेण च ततो हत्वा प्रेषयामास मृत्यवे। उग्रस्य सशिरस्त्राणं शिरश्चन्द्रोपमं भुवि॥ पातयामास भल्लेन कुण्डलाभ्यां विभूषितम्। वीरबाहुं च सप्तत्याः साश्वकेतुं ससारथिम्॥ निनाये समरे वीरः परलोकाय पाण्डवः। भीमभीमरथौ चोभौ भीमसेनो हसन्निव॥ पुत्रौ ते दुर्मदौ राजन्ननयद् यमसादनम्। ततः सुलोचनं भीमः क्षुरप्रेण महामृधे॥ मिषतां सर्वसैन्यानामनयद् यमसादनम्।
en: Then slaying Sushena also, he dispatched him to Death. With a broad headed arrow he felled on the ground the head of Ugra furnished with a helmet and graced with a couple of Kundalas, and loO king like the (charming) moon itself. Thereafter Bhima the son of Pandu, piercing in that battle Virabahu, along with his steeds, standards and charioteer with seventy arrows, dispatched him to the other world. Then as if smiling, Bhimasena, O monarch, conveyed to the abodes of Death the two brothers Bhima and Bhimaratha. Then in that fierce contest, with an arrow furnished with a horse-shoe head, Bhima, dispatched Sulochana to the regions of Death, before the eyes of all the soldiers.

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: पुत्रास्तु तव तं दृष्ट्वा भीमसेनपराक्रमम्॥ शेषा येऽन्यऽभवंस्तत्र ते भीमस्य भयार्दिताः। विप्रद्रुता दिशो राजन् वध्यमाना महात्मना॥
en: Then the rest of your sons who were there, beholding in the field the prowess of Bhimasena, and while being thus struck by that high-souled warrior, all ran away from the filed of battle afraid of Bhima.

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: ततोऽब्रवीच्छान्तनवः सर्वानेव महारथान्। एष भीमो रणे क्रुद्धो धार्तराष्ट्रान् महारथान्॥ यथा प्राच्यान् यथा ज्येष्ठान् यथा शूरांश्च संगतान्। निपातयत्युग्रधन्वा तं प्रगृह्णीतं माचिरम्॥
en: Thereupon the son of Shantanu thus addressed the mighty car-warriors of his army, This fierce bowman, Bhima, inflamed with wrath, is slaughtering in battle the mighty sons of Dhritarashtra, accomplished in weapons, heroic, courageous and united though they are. Do you all receive that son of Pandu in battle”.

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: एवमुक्तास्तत: सर्वे धार्तराष्ट्रस्य सैनिकाः। अभ्यद्रवन्त संक्रुद्धा भीमसेन महाबलम्॥
en: Thus spoken to, all the warriors belonging to the army of Dhritarashtra's son, furious in at Bhimasena endued with superhuman strength.

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: भगदत्तः प्रभिन्नेन कुञ्जरेण विशाम्पते। अभ्ययात् सहसा तत्र यत्र भीमो व्यवस्थितः॥
en: Suddenly, O ruler of men, Bhagadatta, mounted on an elephants with rent temples, rushed towards the spot where Bhima was stationed.

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: आपतन्नेव च रणे. भीमसेन शिलीमुखैः। अदृष्यं समरे चक्रे जीमूत इव भास्करम्॥
en: rage, rushed Rushing to the encounter, he, in that battle, intercepted Bhimasena from the view, (covering him) with shafts whetted on stone like clouds intercepting the sun from the view.

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: अभिमन्युमुखास्तत् तु नामृष्यन्त महारथाः। भीमस्याच्छादनं संख्ये स्वबाहुबलमाश्रिताः॥
en: Then the mighty car-warriors headed by Abhimanyu, who all relied on the strength of their arms, could not brook this interception of Bhima.

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: त एनं शरवर्षेण समन्तात् पर्यवारयन्। गजं च शरवृष्ट्या तु बिभिदुस्ते समन्ततः॥
en: So, all those heroes opposed Bhagadatta on all sides with a showier of arrows, and they also began to pierce the elephants from all sides with an arrow down pour.

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: स शस्त्रवृष्ट्याऽभिहतः समस्तैस्तैर्महारथैः। प्राग्ज्योतिषगजो राजन् नानालिङ्गैः सुतेजनैः॥
en: That elephants of the ruler of the Pragjyotishas, O king, being struck by all those mighty warriors, with sharers of weapons of diverse description.

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: संजातरुधिरोत्पीडः प्रेक्षणीयोऽभवद् रणे। गभस्तिभिरिवार्कस्य संस्यूतो जलदो महान्॥ संचोदितो मदस्रावी भगदत्तेन वारणः। अभ्यधावत तान् सर्वान् कालोत्सृष्ट इवान्तकः॥
en: And with blood spattered on its body became, in that battle, woryour of being looked at, like masses of rain-clouds tinged with the rays of the sun. That elephant, shedding temporal juice, being goaded by Bhagadatta, rushed against all those (heroes), like Death incarnate urged on by the Destroyer himself.

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: द्विगुणं जवमास्थाय कम्पयंश्चरणैर्महीम्। तस्य तत् सुमहद् रूपं दृष्ट्वा सर्वे महारथाः॥
en: It doubled its speed and shook the earth under death its tread. Then all those mighty car-warriors, seeing that dreadful aspect of the animal,

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: असह्यं मन्यमानाश्च नातिप्रमनसोऽभवन्। ततस्तु नृपतिः क्रुद्धो भीमसेनं स्तनान्तरे॥ आजघान महाराज शरेणानतपर्वणा। सोऽतिविद्धो महेष्वासस्तेन राज्ञा महारथः॥ मूर्च्छयाऽभिपरीतात्मा ध्वजयष्टिं समाश्रयत्। तांस्तु भीतान् समालक्ष्य भीमसेनं च मूर्च्छितम्॥
en: And considering it irresistible, lost their heart. Then that king the foremost of men, excited with wrath, struck Bhimasena on the centre of his chest, with a straight shaft. That mighty car-warrior and bowman, being pierced by that monarch, with his limbs stiffened in consequence of a swoon, caught hold of his flat staff. Beholding them terrified, and seeing Bhima overwhelmed with a swoon.

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: ननाद बलवन्नादं भगदत्तः प्रतापवान्। ततो घटोत्कचो राजन् प्रेक्ष्य भीमं तथागतम्॥ संक्रुद्धो राक्षसो घोरस्तत्रैवान्तरधीयत। स कृत्वा दारुणां मायां भीरूणां भयवर्धिनीम्॥ अदृश्यत निमेषार्धाद् घोररूपं समास्थितः। ऐरावणं समारूढः स वै मायाकृतं स्वयम्॥
en: The powerful Bhagadatta endued with great prowess uttered a loud roar. Then O monarch, the Rakshasa Ghatotkacha of dreadful appearance seeing Bhima ir that plight became inflamed with fury, and even there disappeared from the sight. And spreading a terrible illusion capable of enhancing the apprehension of the cowards, hc reappeared with a moment assuming a dreadful form, and riding on an Airavata the creation of his own illusive powers.

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: तस्य चान्येऽपि दिङ्नागा बभूवुरनुयायिनः। अञ्जनो वामनश्चैव महापद्मश्च सुप्रभः॥
en: Other elephants guarding the points of the compass, namely, Anjana, Vamana Mahapadma, followed it, all effulgence.

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: त्रय एते महानागा राक्षसैः समधिष्ठिताः। महाकायास्त्रिधा राजन् प्रस्रवन्तो मदं बहु॥
en: All these three mighty elephants ridden by Rakshsasa were possessed of prodigious bodies with the temporal juice profusely exuding from their temples. of pure

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: तेजोवीर्यबलोपेता महाबलपराक्रमाः। घटोत्कचस्तु स्वं नागं चोदयामास तं तदा॥
en: And they were endued with prowess strength and might and great fleetness and courage. Then Ghatotkacha goaded his own elephants in battle,

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: सगजं भगदत्तं तु हन्तुकामः परंतपः। ते चान्ये चोदिता नागा राक्षसैस्तैर्महाबलैः॥
en: Being desirous, O afflicter of your foes, of slaying Bhagadatta along with his elephants. Goaded by the Rakshasas, of great strength, the other elephants.

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: परिपेतुः सुसंरब्धाश्चतुर्दष्ट्राश्चतुर्दिशम्। भगदत्तस्य तं नागं विषाणैरभ्यपीडयन्॥
en: Each possessed of four tusks, fell from all sides, with fury, upon the elephants of Bhagadatta, striking the latter at the same time with their tusks.

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: स पीड्यमानस्तै गैर्वेदनातः शराहतः। अनदत् सुमहानादमिन्द्राशनिसमस्वनम्॥
en: Wounded with arrows, and afflicted by those elephants, and smearing with pain, the elephants, of Bhagadatta set up a mighty roar that resembled the rumble of the thunderbolt of Indra.

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: तस्य तं नदतो नादं सुघोरं भीमनिःस्वनम्। श्रुत्वा भीष्मोऽब्रवीद् द्रोणं राजानं च सुयोधनम्॥
en: Hearing those deep and dreadful cries the roaring elephants, Bhishma thus spoke to Drona and king Suyodhana,

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: एष युध्यति संग्रामे हैडिम्बेन दुरात्मना। भगदत्तो महेष्वासः कृच्छ्रे च परिवर्तते॥
en: “This mighty bowman Bhagadatta fighting in his battle with the wicked souled son of Hidimba, is involved in a great peril.

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: राक्षसश्च महाकायः स च राजाऽतिकोपनः। एतौ समेतौ समरे कालमृत्युसमावुभौ॥
en: This Rakshasa is of prodigious stature, and king Bhagadatta also is very wrathful. Surely encountering each other in the fight they both will prove like the Death and the Destroyer.

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: श्रूयते चैव हृष्टानां पाण्डवानां महास्वनः। हस्तिनश्चैव सुमहान् भीतस्य रुदितध्वनिः॥
en: Even now do we hear the mighty uproar of the enraptured Pandavas, as also the distressful and loud cries of the frightened elephants (of Bhagadatta).

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: तत्र गच्छाम भद्रं वो राजानं परिरक्षितुम्। अरक्ष्यमाणः समरे क्षिप्रं प्राणान् विमोक्ष्यति॥
en: Good betide you, we shall now proceed to protect the king; unprotected, in battle, he will soon be deprived of his life.

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: ते त्वरध्वं महावीर्याः किं चिरेण प्रयामहे। महान् हि वर्तते रौद्रः संग्रामो लोमहर्षणः॥
en: Therefore, warriors of extraordinary prowess, make havee; O sinless ones, do not delay. This hair stirring and ruthless combat is deepening more and more.

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: भक्तश्च कुलपुत्रश्च शूरश्च पृतनापतिः। युक्तं तस्य परित्राणं कर्तुमस्माभिरच्युत॥
en: This leader of a division is devoted to us, is the son of an illustrious dynasty and is endued with bravery. O you of unfading renown, it is proper that his rescue should be effected by us."

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: भीष्मस्य तद् वचः श्रुत्वा सर्व एव महारथाः। द्रोणभीष्मौ पुरस्कृत्य भगदत्तपरीप्सया॥
en: Listening to those words of Bhishma all the monarchs forming in serried files and headed by the son Bharadvaja, with a desire for rescuing Bhagadatta.

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: उत्तमं जवमास्थाय प्रययुर्यत्र सोऽभवत्। तान् प्रयातान् समालोक्य युधिष्ठिरपुरोगमाः॥ पञ्चालाः पाण्डवैः सार्धं पृष्ठतोऽनुययुः परान्। तान्यनकान्यथालोक्य राक्षसेन्द्रः प्रतापवान्॥
en: Proceeded in all have to the spot where the later was. Beholding them advance, the Panchalas together with the Pandavas headed by Yudhishthira himself pursued the enemy from behind. Beholding that mighty host, the foremost of the Rakshasa endued with prowess.

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: ननाद सुमहानादं विस्फोटमशनेरिव। तस्य तं निनदं श्रुत्वा दृष्ट्वा नागांश्च युध्यतः॥
en: Uttered a deafening roar, that resembled the roar of thunder. Hearing his roar and seeing those fighting elephants.

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: भीष्मः शान्तनवो भूयो भारद्वाजमभाषत। न रोचते मे संग्रामो हैडिम्बेन दुरात्मना॥
en: The son of Shantanu, namely, Bhishma again addressed the son of Bharadvaja saying:I do not like to fight with the wicked-souled son of Hidimba.

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: बलवीर्यसमाविष्टः ससहायश्च साम्प्रतम्। नैष शक्यो युधा जेतुमपि वज्रभृता स्वयम्॥
en: At present he is surcharged with strength and prowess and is well supported. He is now incapable of being defeated even by the wielder of the thunderbolt himself.

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: लब्धलक्षयः प्रहारी च वयं च श्रान्तवाहनाः। पाञ्चालैः पाण्डवेयैश्च दिवसं क्षतविक्षताः॥
en: He is sure in his aims and can strike home; our vehicles are all fatigued and we have been wounded and lacerated in our fight with the Pandavas and the Panchalas.

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: तन्न मे रोचते युद्धं पाण्डवैर्जितकाशिभिः। घुष्यतामवाहारोऽद्य श्वो योत्स्यामः परैः सह॥
en: Therefore we do not like to fight any longer with the Pandavas. Proclaim there fore, the withdraw of our divisions for this day. Tomorrow shall we again battle with the enemy".

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: पितामहवचः श्रुत्वा तथा चक्रुः स्म कौरवाः। उपायेनापयानं ते घटोत्कचमयार्दिताः॥
en: Hearing these words of the grandsire, and afflicted as they were with the fear of Ghatotkacha, they (the Kauravas) delightedly did what the former said availing themselves of the pretest advent of night.

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: कौरवेषु निवृत्तेषु पाण्डवा जितकाशिनः। सिंहनादान् भृशं चक्रुः शङ्खान् दध्मुश्च भारत॥
en: Upon the withdrawal of the Kurus, the victorious Pandavas sent up their war cries accompanied with the blare of conchs and cornets.

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: एवं तदभवद् युद्ध दिवसं भरतर्षभ। पाण्डवानां कुरूणां च पुरस्कृत्य घटोत्कचम्॥
en: Thus, O foremost of the Bharata race, did the battle rage that day, between the Kurus and the Pandavas headed by Ghatotkacha.

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: कौरवास्तु ततो राजन् प्रययुः शिबिरं स्वकम्। वीडमाना निशाकाले पाण्डवेयैः पराजिताः॥
en: Thereafter, the Kauravas, at night fall haveily repaired to their own encampments, being ashamed and being vanquished by the Pandavas.

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: शरविक्षतगात्रास्तु पाण्डुपुत्रा महारथाः। युद्धे सुमनसो भूत्वा जग्मुः स्वशिबिरं प्रति॥
en: Those mighty car-warriors, the sons of Pandu, with their bodies mangled with shafts in battle. O king retired to their camps with heares over flowing with joy.

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: पुरस्कृत्य महाराज भीमसेनघटोत्कचौ। पूजयन्तस्तदाऽन्योन्यं मुदा परमया युताः॥
en: And, O mighty monarch, they proceeded placing Bhimasena and Ghatotkacha at their van, and 0 mighty sovereign, worshipping them out of great delight.

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: नदन्तो विविधान् नादांस्तूर्यस्वनविमिश्रितान्। सिंहनादांश्च कुर्वन्तो विमिश्रीशङ्खनिःस्वनैः॥
en: They uttered diverse cries that became mingled with sounds of the tabors, and they uttered also their war-cries which again were mingled with the blare of their conchs.

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: विनदन्तो महात्मानः कम्पयन्तश्च मेदिनीम्। घट्टयन्तश्च मर्माणि तव पुत्रस्य मारिष॥
en: Those high-souled warriors, uttering leonine roars and shaking the earth with their tread, O sire, agitated the heares of your sons.

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: प्रयाताः शिबिरायैव निशाकाले परंतप। दुर्योधनस्तु नृपतिर्दीनो भ्रातृवधेन च॥
en: Then those repressors of their foes retired to their camps at the advent of night. King Duryodhana, on the other hand, distressed in consequence of the slaughter of his brothers. some

description: Withdrawal of the troops at the end of the fourth day's combat
sn: मुहूर्तं चिन्तयामास बाष्पशोकसमाकुलः। ततः कृत्वा विधिं सर्वं शिविरस्य यथाविधि। प्रदध्यौ शोकसंतप्तो भ्रातृव्यसनकर्शितः॥
en: Reflected for moments, whelmed with tears and grief. Then making all the necessary arrangements for his camp according to the rules of military sciences he began to mediate, afflicted (as he was with) the death of his brother and overcome with poignant grief on their account.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच भयं मे सुमहज्जातं विस्मयश्चैव संजय। श्रुत्वा पाण्डुकुमाराणां कर्म देवैः सुदुष्करम्॥
en: Dhritarashtra said Hearing of those feats achieved by the sons of Pandu-feats which are difficult of being achieved even by the celestial themselves, O Sanjaya, I have been filled with apprehension and amazement.

sn: पुत्राणां च पराभावं श्रुत्वा संजय सर्वशः। चिन्ता मे महती सूत भविष्यति कथं त्विति॥
en: Hearing also of the humiliation of my sons in every way. O Sanjaya, I have been seized by a burning anxiety as to what the finale (of this war) will be.

sn: ध्रुवं विदुरवाक्यानि धक्ष्यन्ति हृदयं मम। यथा हि दृश्यते सर्वं दैवयोगेन संजय॥
en: The prophecy of Vidura does consume my heart; and, O Sanjaya, I see that through the influence of (adverse) destiny every thing is happening even as he had said.

sn: यत्र भीष्पमुखान् सर्वाञ्छस्त्रज्ञानं योधसत्तमान्। पाण्डवानामनीकेषु योधयन्ति प्रहारिणः॥
en: The smiters of the Pandava hosts are battling with those foremost of warriors headed by Bhishma, who are endued with heroism and accomplished in (the use of) all weapons.

sn: केनावध्या महात्मानः पाण्डुपुत्रा महाबलाः। केन दत्तवरास्तात किं वा ज्ञानं विदन्ति ते॥
en: What asceticism those high-souled and greatly powerful sons of Pandu have observed, what boon, O child, have they secured, what knowledge have they cultivated,

sn: येन क्षयं न गच्छन्ति दिवि तारागणा इव। पुनः पुनर्न मृष्यामि हतं सैन्यं तु पाण्डवैः।
en: In consequences of which they suffer no reduction, like the stars in the firmament? I can not bear the repeated slaughter of my warriors by the sons of Pandu.

sn: मय्येव दण्डः पतति दैवात् परमदारुणः। यथाऽवध्याः पाण्डुसुता यथा वध्याश्च मे सुताः॥ एतन्मे सर्वमाचक्ष्व याथातथ्येन संजय। न हि पारं प्रपश्यामि दुःखस्यास्य कथंचन॥
en: Through the disposal of Destiny, a highly severe chastisement has overtaken me alone. Tell me truly, O Sanjaya, every thing, about why my sons have become liable to slaughter and why the sons of Pandus have been exempted from it. I can not discern, O afflicter of your enemies, the termination of this ocean of distress.

sn: समुद्रस्येव महतो भुजाभ्यां प्रतरन् नरः। पुत्राणां व्यसनं मन्ये ध्रुवं प्राप्तं सुदारुणम्॥
en: Like a man desirous of swimming over the vast sea with his two arms. I now certainly see that a terrible calamity has overtaken my sons.

sn: घातयिष्यति मे सर्वान् पुत्रान् भीमो न संशयः। न हि पश्यामि तं वीरं यो मे रक्षेत् सुतान् रणे॥
en: No doubt, Bhima will slay all my sons. I do not find that hero who can protect my sons in battle.

sn: ध्रुवं विनाशः सम्प्राप्तः पुत्राणां मम संजय। तस्मान्मे कारणं सूत शक्तिं चैव विशेषतः॥ पृच्छतो वै यथातत्त्वं सर्वमाख्यातुमर्हसि। दुर्योधनश्च यच्चक्रे दृष्ट्वा स्वान् विमुखान् रणे॥
en: The destruction of my sons in battle is certain, O Sanjaya. Therefore, O Suta, it behaves you to tell me who am questioning you, in detail and truly, the real cause of these events, as also, what Duryodhana did, seeing his own troops turn their face away from the field of battle.

sn: भीष्मद्रोणौ कृपश्चैव सौबलश्च जयद्रथः। द्रौणिर्वाऽपि महेष्वासो विकर्णो वा महाबलः॥
en: Bhishma, Drona, Kripa and the son of Subala, and Jayadratha, and the mighty bowman the son of Drona, and the mighty Vikarna, what did all these warriors do?

sn: निश्चयो वापि कस्तेषां तदा ह्यासीन्महात्मनाम्। विमुखेषु महाप्राज्ञ मम पुत्रेषु संजय॥
en: What, O highly wise one, the resolution of these high-souled warriors, when, O Sanjaya, my sons turned away their faces from the field? was

sn: संजय उवाच शृणु राजन्नवहितः श्रुत्वा चैवावधारय। नैव मन्त्रकृतं किंचिन्नैव मायां तथाविधाम्॥
en: Sanjaya said Hear, O king, with perfect attention and hearing do you understand what you hear. There was nothing the result of incantation and nothing the production of illusion.

sn: न वै विभीषिकां कांचिद् राजन् कुर्वन्ति पाण्डवाः। युध्यन्ति ते यथान्यायं शक्तिमन्तश्च संयुगे॥
en: Neither, O monarch, did the sons of Pandu create any new source of apprehension. Those warriors endued with strength are fighting their battles according to the rules of fair combat.

sn: धर्मेण सर्वकार्याणि आरभनते सदा पार्थाः जीवितादीनि भारत प्रार्थयाना महद् यशः॥
en: The sons of Pritha, O Bharata, desirous of securing illustrious fame, ever perform all acts, even the maintenance of their lives, in perfect accordance with the rulers of morality.

sn: न ते युद्धान्निवर्तन्ते धर्मोपेता महाबलाः। श्रिया परमया युक्ता यतो धर्मस्ततो जयः॥
en: Attended by excellent prosperity and endued with great strength and conforming to all morality, they never turn back from the fight. Victory ever attends righteousness.

sn: तेनावध्या रणे पार्था जययुक्ताश्च पार्थिव। तव पुत्रा दुरात्मानः पापेष्वभिरताः सदा॥
en: For this reason, O ruler of earth, the sons of Pritha are unslayable in battle and are ever courted by victory. Your sons are of wicked intentions and are intent on perpetrating sin;

sn: निष्ठुरा हीनकर्माणस्तेन हीयन्ति संयुगे। सुबहूनि नृशंसानि पुत्रैस्तव नजनेश्वर॥ निकृतानीह पाण्डूनां नीचैरिव यथा नरैः। सर्वं च तदनादृत्य पुत्राणां तव किल्बिषम्॥
en: And are cruel and of low deeds; therefore are they always worsted in the battle. O ruler of men, various heartless injuries were done to the Pandavas by your sons, like men of low extraction. Disregarding all those offences of your sons.

sn: सापह्नवाः सदैवासन् पाण्डवाः पाण्डुपूर्वज। न चैतान् बहु मन्यन्ते पुत्रास्तव विशाम्पते॥
en: O elder brother of Pandu, the sons of Pandu tried always to keep them 'hidden and unknown. O ruler of men your sons do not pay them proper respect.

sn: तस्य पापस्य सततं क्रियमाणस्य कर्मणः। साम्प्रतं सुमहद् घोरं फलं प्राप्तं जनेश्वर॥
en: Let your sons now reap the fruit that resembles the poisonous fruit of the Kimpaka tree, of that their persistent course of sinful actions.

sn: स त्वं भुक्ष्व महाराज सपुत्रः ससुहृज्जनः। नावबुध्यसि यद् राजन् वार्यमाणः सुहज्जनैः॥
en: Now, O mighty monarch, do you with your sons and relatives, taste that mortal fruit, in as much as, O king, you did not seem to be awakened though always warned by your wellwishers.

sn: विदुरेणाथ भीष्मेण द्रोणेन च महात्मना। तथा मया चाप्यसकृद् वार्यमाणो न बुध्यसे॥
en: Always forbidden by Vidura, Bhishma, Drona of high soul, his son, as also by me, you did not pay any regard.

sn: वाक्यं हितं च पथ्यं च माः पथ्यमिवौषधम्। पुत्राणां मतमाज्ञाय जितान् मन्यसि पाण्डवान्॥
en: To our words, salutary and intended for your good though they were even as a sick man rejects wholesome medicines Accepting the views of your sons, you expected to see the Pandavas vanquished.

sn: शृणु भूयो यथातत्त्वं यन्मां त्वं परिपृच्छसि। कारणं भरतश्रेष्ठ पाण्डवानां जयं प्रति॥
en: Hear again the true reason, about which you had asked me, for the victory of the sons of Pandu, O foremost of the Bharatas.

sn: तत् तेऽहं कथयिष्यामि यथाश्रुतमरिंदम्। दुर्योधनेन सम्पृष्ट एतमर्थं पितामहः॥
en: I shall exactly tell you, O subjugator of your foes, as I myself have heard it. The grandsire himself was questioned, on this point by king Duryodhana.

sn: दृष्ट्वा भ्रातॄन् रणे सर्वान् निर्जितांस्तु महारथान्। शोकमसम्मूढहृदयो निशाकाले स्म कौरवः॥ पितामहं महाप्राज्ञं विनयेनोपगम्य ह। यदब्रवीत् सुतस्तेऽसौ तन्मे शृणु जनेश्वर॥
en: Beholding his brothers, all accomplished car-warriors, worsted in battle, your son Duryodhana, O Kaurava, with his heart overwhelmed with sorrow, asked this question to the grandsire, approaching him with humility, on the advent of night. O ruler of men, hear from me what your son did say at the time.

sn: दुर्योधन उवाच द्रोणश्च त्वं च शल्यश्च कृपो द्रौणिस्तथैव च। कृतवर्मा च हार्दिक्यः काम्बोजश्च सुदक्षिणः॥
en: Duryodhana said Drona, yourself, Shalya, Kripa, the son of Drona, Kritavarma, the son of Hridika, and Sudakshina the ruler of the Kambojas.

sn: भूरिश्रवा विकर्णश्च भगदत्तश्च वीर्यवान्। महारथाः समाख्याताः कुलपुत्रास्तनुत्यजः॥
en: Bhurishravas, Vikarna and Bhagadatta endued with prowess, these heroes are all regarded as mighty car-warriors; all these men are the sons of illustrious dynasties and are ever ready to shuffle off their mortal coil.

sn: त्रयाणामपि लोकानां पर्याप्ता इति मे मतिः। पाण्डवानां समस्ताश्च नातिष्ठन्त पराक्रमे॥
en: I consider these to be a match for the three world united together. The whole Pandava army can not withstand your prowess.

sn: तत्र मे संशयो जातस्तन्ममाचक्ष्व पृच्छतः। यं समाश्रित्य कौन्तेया जयन्त्यस्मान् क्षणे क्षणे॥
en: Regarding these things, a doubt has arisen in my mind. Tell me, who am asking you, of him, relying on whom the sons of Kunti are gaining victory over us at each step.

sn: भीष्म उवाच शृणु राजन् वचो मह्यं यथा वक्ष्यामि कौरव। बहुशश्च मयोक्तोऽसि न च मे तत् त्वया कृतम्॥ क्रियतां पाण्डवैः सार्धं शमो भरतसत्तम। एतत् क्षेममहं मन्ये पृथिव्यास्तव वा विभो॥
