en: Bhishma said Hear, O king, the words that I am going to say to you, O you of the Kuru race. I did frequently address you to the same effect, urging you to conclude peace with the sons of Pandu. I consider this to be profitable both to you and to the earth, O lord.

sn: भुक्ष्वेमां पृथिवीं राजन् भ्रातृभिः सहितः सुखी। दुर्हदस्तापयन् सर्वान् नन्दयंश्चापि बान्धवान्॥
en: Do you, O king, enjoy the blessings of this earth with your brothers, with a contented heart, and enhancing the delight of your relatives and gratifying every one else.

sn: न च मे क्रोशतस्तात श्रुतवानसि वै पुरा। तदितं समनुप्राप्तं यत् पाण्डूनवमन्यसे॥
en: O sire, you paid no heed to my words before, though I cried myself hoarse. Now this evil has overtaken you, in as much as you have ever despised the sons of Pandu.

sn: यश्च हेतुरवध्यत्वे तेषामक्लिष्टकर्मणाम्। तं शृणुष्व महाबाहो मम कीर्तयतः प्रभो॥
en: Hear from me as I speak, O king, O lord, the reason why those sons of Pandu who are never tired in the performance of pious acts, are unslayable.

sn: नास्ति लोकेषु तद् भूतं भविता नो भविष्यति। यो जयेत् पाण्डवान् सर्वान् पालिताञ्छाईधन्वना॥
en: There was not, is not, or will not be a person, who would have been, is or will be able to conquer the Pandavas, protected as they are by the wielder of the Sharnga bow.

sn: यत् तु मे कथितं तात मुनिभिर्भावितात्मभिः। पुराणगीतं धर्मज्ञ तच्छृणुष्व यथातथम्॥
en: Hear from me, you who are versed in morality, the ancient history that was related to me, O sire, by the sages of tranquil souls.

sn: पुरा किल सुराः सर्वे ऋषयश्च समागताः। पितामहमुपासेदुः पर्वते गन्धमादने॥
en: In the days of yore, all the celestial and sages, assembled together, danced attendance upon the grandsire (Brahma) on the mountain Gandhamadana.

sn: तेषां मध्ये समासीनः प्रजापतिरपश्यत। विमान् प्रज्वलद् भासा स्थितं प्रवरमम्बरे॥
en: Seated at his ease in their midst, the lord of people, saw an excellent chariot burning with effulgence, stationed in the firmament.

sn: ध्यानेनावेद्य तद् ब्रह्मा कृत्वा च नियतोऽञ्जलिम्। नमश्चकार हृष्यात्मा पुरुष परमेश्वरम्॥
en: Having ascertained everything about the chariot by means of his contemplation and folding his palms together, Brahma, with his soul filled with delight bowed down his head to the Purusha, the highest of all Divinities.

sn: ऋषयस्त्वथ देवाश्च दृष्ट्वा ब्रह्माणमुत्थितम्। स्थिताः प्राञ्जलयः सर्वे पश्यन्तो महदद्भुतम्॥
en: Also the sages and the celestial beholding the figure thus revealed in the heavens stood with hands folded and with their gaze fixed on the marvel of marvels.

sn: यथावच्च तमभ्यर्च्य ब्रह्मा ब्रह्मविदां वरः। जगाद जगतः स्रष्टा परं परमधर्मवित्॥
en: Then Brahma best conversant with morality, the foremost of those versed in the Vedas and the creator of the worlds, having worshipped that from duly, chanted this hymn of praise.

sn: विश्वावसुर्विश्वमूर्तिर्विश्वेशो विष्वक्सेनो विश्वकर्मा वशी च। विश्वेश्वरो वासुदेवोऽसि तस्माद् योगात्मानं दैवतं त्वामुपैमि॥
en: You are the glory of the universe, and have the universe as your form. You are the lord of the universe; you are the protector of it; you have your senses under your thorough control. You are the lord paramount of this universe, you are the Vasudeva; I seek refuge in your divine self that are the soul of Yoga.

sn: जय विश्व महादेव जय लोकहिते रत। जय योगीश्वर विभो जय योगपरावर॥
en: Victory unto you that are the divine and paramount Lord of this universe; victory unto you, who are ever anxious for the worlds welfare. Victory unto you the lord and the master of the Yogins; victory unto you that are identified with the ocean of yoga energy.

sn: पद्मगर्भ विशालाक्ष जय लोकेश्वरेश्वर। भूतभव्यभवन्नाथ जय सौम्यात्मजात्मज॥
en: Victory unto you the Lord of the lords of the universe, that have the lotus springing from the navel and that have expanded eyes. Victory unto you that are the incarnation of gentleness, you that are the son of sons, O you, the Lord of the past, the present, and the future.

sn: असंख्येयगुणाधार जय सर्वपरायण। नारायण सुदुष्पार जय शार्ङ्गधनुर्धर॥
en: O you, the receptacle of innumerable qualities victory be unto you, the refuge of all things; O you that are Narayana and that are incomprehensible, victory be unto you, the wielder of the Sharnga bow.

sn: जय सर्वगुणोपेत विश्वमूर्ते निरामय। विश्वेश्वर महाबाहो जय लोकार्थतत्पर॥
en: Victory be unto you, O you that have the universe for your from that are free from the influence of all maladies. O Lord of the universe, O you of long arms, victory be unto you who are devoted to further the welfare of the worlds.

sn: महोरग वराहाद्य हरिकेश विभो जय। हरिवास दिशामीश विश्ववासामिताव्यय॥
en: 0 great Serpent, O huge Boar, O Lord, O you possessed of the lion's manes, victory be unto you. O you whose raiment's are yellow, O Lord of the several points of the compass. O you that are like the abode of the universe, O infinite one, O you that dose suffer no deterioration.

sn: व्यक्ताव्यक्तामितस्थान नियतेन्द्रिय सक्रिय। असंख्येयात्मभावज्ञ जय गम्भीर कामद॥
en: O you that are the Manifest, O you that are the Unmanifested. O you of senses thoroughly controlled. O you that are like the infinite space. O you that ever achieve the acts beneficial to the worlds, O you that are beyond all measurement, O you that alone are conversant with your nature, O you that are deep and the fulfiller of desires victory be upto you.

sn: अनन्तविदित ब्रह्मन् नित्य भूतविभावन। कृतकार्य कृतप्रज्ञ धर्मज्ञ विजयावह॥
en: O you that have no end, O you that are known as Brahma, O you that are eternal, and are the protector of all creatures, O you that are ever successful, O you whose understanding is accomplished in all things. O you that are conversant with all righteousness. O you that are ever attended with victory.

sn: गुह्यात्मन् सर्वयोगात्मन् स्फुटं सम्भूतसम्भव। भूताद्य लोकतत्त्वेश जय भूतविभावन॥
en: O you of mysterious self, O you that are the soul of all Yoga, O you that are the origin of every thing that has sprung into existence, O you that are the knowledge of the souls of every being, O master of the universe, victory be unto you that are the creator of all beings.

sn: आत्मयोने महाभाग कल्पसंक्षेप तत्पर। उद्भावनमनोभाव जय ब्रह्म जयप्रिय॥
en: O you that are self-create, O you of eminent parts, O you that are ever active for bringing about the destruction of all beings, O you that are the inspirer of all thoughts in the mind, victory be unto you, the beloved of those that are conversant with Brahma.

sn: निसर्गसर्गनिरत कामेश परमेश्वर। अमृतोद्भव सद्भाव मुक्तात्मन् विजयप्रद॥
en: O you that are ever engaged in the acts of creation and destruction, Orepressor of all desires, O most exalted Divinity, O you the origin of Amrita, O you whose existence only is a reality, O you that are the Fire that do appear at the end of a Yoga, O you that are the bestower of victory.

sn: प्रजापतिपते देव पद्मनाभ महाबला आत्मभूत महाभूत सत्त्वात्मन् जय सर्वदा॥
en: O you that are the Lord of lords of men, O Divine one, O you that have the lotus growing from your navel, O you endued with great might, O you that are self-create, O you that are of elements in their nascent condition, O you that are the soul of all performance, victory be unto you, the giver of all things.

sn: पादौ तव धरा देवी दिशो बाहू दिवं शिरः। मूर्तिस्तेऽहं सुराः कायश्चन्द्रादित्यौ च चक्षुषी॥
en: The goddess of earth constitutes your feet, the cardinal and subsidiary points of the compass represent your arms; the celestial regions constitute your head; your from is composed of myself; the celestials compose your limbs, and the sun and the moon your two eyes.

sn: बलं तपश्च सत्यं च कर्म धर्मात्मकं तव। तेजोऽग्निः पवनः श्वास आपस्ते स्वेदसम्भवाः॥
en: Asceticism and truth born of acts of piety constitute your strength. Your energy is fire, your breath the wind. And waters have been created from your perspiration.

sn: अश्विनौ श्रवणौ नित्यं देवी जिह्वा सरस्वती। वेदाः संस्कारनिष्ठा हि त्वयीदं जगदाश्रितम्॥
en: The twin Ashvins ever constitute your ears, the goddess of leading is your tongue, the Vedas are your knowledge and in you is this world stationed.

sn: न संख्यानं परीमाणं न तेजो न पराक्रमम्। न बलं योगयोगीश जानीमस्ते न सम्भवम्॥
en: O you that are the Lord of Yoga and the Yogins, we know neither your extent nor your measure, neither your energy nor your prowess, nor your strength, nor your origin.

sn: त्वद्भक्तिनिरता देव नियमैस्त्वां समाश्रिताः। अर्चयामः सदा विष्णो परमेशं महेश्वरम्॥
en: O god, cherishing reverence for you and betaking to your ways by the performance of vows and &c., we do ever worship Vishnu, the Supreme Lord, the God of gods.

sn: ऋषयो देवगन्धर्वा यक्षराक्षसपन्नगा:। पिशाचा मानुशाश्चैव मृगपक्षिसरीसृपाः॥
en: The sages, the celestials, the Gandharvas, the Yakshas, the Rakshasas, the Pannagas, the Pishachas, and men, and the animals, and birds and men and reptiles.

sn: एवमादि मया सृष्टं पृथिव्यां त्वत्प्रसादजम्। पद्मनाभ विशालाक्ष कृष्ण दुःखप्रणाशन॥
en: All these have been created by me in the first instance, on earth, through your grace. O you that have the lotus springing from your navel, O you of expanded eyes, O Krishna,O soother of all afflictions.

sn: त्वं गतिः सर्वभूतानां त्वं नेता त्वं जगद्गुरुः। त्वत्प्रसादेन देवेश सुखिनो विबुधाः सदा॥
en: You are the refuge of all created beings and you are their bodies! You have the universe for your mouth; O you that are the Lord of the celestials, the gods are ever happy through your grace only.

sn: पृथिवी निर्भया देव त्वत्प्रसादात् सदाऽभवत्। तस्माद् भव विशालाक्ष यदुवंशविवर्धनः॥
en: O god, through your grace the earth have ever been freed from all her apprehensions. So, O you of expanded eyes, be you the propagator of the Yadu race.

sn: धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय दैत्यानां च वधाय च। जगतो धारणार्थाय विज्ञाप्यं कुरु मे विभो॥
en: Gratify my solicitation O Lord, for the sake of establishing righteousness, for slaying the sons of Diti and for upholding the universe.

sn: यत् तत् परमकं गुह्यं त्वत्प्रसादादिदं विभो। वासुदेव तदेतत् ते मयोद्गीतं यथातथम्॥
en: 0 Vasudeva all that is supremely mysterious regarding you, O Lord, all that have been exactly sung by me, through your grace.

sn: सृष्ट्वा संकर्षणं देवं स्वयमात्मानमात्मना। कृष्ण त्वमात्मनास्राक्षीः प्रद्युम्नं चात्मसम्भवम्॥
en: Having created the divine Sankarshana your self out of your own self, you did then, O Krishna create yourself as Pradyuman, born out of your own self.

sn: प्रद्युम्नादनिरुद्धं त्वं यं विदुर्विष्णुमव्ययम्। अनिरुद्धोऽसृजन्मां वै ब्रह्माणं लोकधारिणम्॥
en: From Pradyumana you did then create Anirudha known as the undetiorating Vishnu. And it was Anirudha who did create me Brahman as the supporter of the universe.

sn: वासुदेवमयः सोऽहं त्वयैवास्मि विनिर्मितः। विभज्य भागशोऽऽत्मानं व्रज मानुषतां विभो॥
en: Thus created by the essence of Vamdeva. I have been created by yourself Dividing yourself into portions, O Lord create yourself among humanity.

sn: तत्रासुरवधं कृत्वा सर्वलोकसुखाय वै। धर्मं प्राप्य यशः प्राप्य योगं प्राप्स्यसि तत्त्वतः॥
en: There, for the well being of the world slaughtering the Asuras, and establishing righteousness and winning glory, you shall again attain to the best Yoga.

sn: त्वां हि ब्रह्मर्षयो लोके देवाश्चामितविक्रम। तैस्तैर्हि नामभिर्युक्ता गायन्ति परमात्मकम्॥
en: O you of immeasurable prowess, the regenerate sages and the celestials sing of your wonderful self out of devotion for you, under those various appellations that are ascribed to you.

sn: स्थिताश्च सर्वे त्वयि भूतसंघाः कृत्वाऽश्रयं त्वां वरदं सुबाहो। अनादिमध्यान्तमपारयोगं लोकस्य सेतुं प्रवदन्ति विप्राः॥
en: O you of excellent arms, all the host of beings find their support in you, having sought shelter in you, the giver of boons. The Vipras eulogise you as the bridge of the universe, having no beginning, middle or end, and as possessed of infinite Yoga prowess.

description: The story of the world's creation,
sn: भीष्म उवाच ततः स भगवान् देवो लोकानामीश्वरेश्वरः। ब्रह्मणं प्रत्युवाचेदं स्निग्धगम्भीरया गिरा॥
en: Bhishma said Thereupon that almighty Divinity the Lord of the lords of people, thus replied to Brahma in a soft and sonorous voice.

description: The story of the world's creation,
sn: विदितं तात योगान्मे सर्वमेतत् तवेप्सितम्। तथा तद् भवितेत्युक्त्वा तत्रैवान्तरधीयत॥
en: “I have come to know, O sire, all that you desire, through my Yoga power. It will be even as you desire”. Saying this he disappeared then and there.

description: The story of the world's creation,
sn: ततो देवर्षिगन्धर्वा विस्मयं परमं गताः। कौतूहलपराः सर्वे पितामहमथाब्रुवन्॥
en: Then the celestials, the sages, and the Gandharvas were all filled with great wonder; and urged by curiosity they then thus spoke to the Grandsire Brahma.

description: The story of the world's creation,
sn: कोन्वयं यो भगवता प्रणम्य विनयाद् विभो। वाग्भिः स्तुतो वरिष्ठाभिः श्रोतुमिच्छाम तं वयम्॥
en: Who indeed is he, O master, that was even now adored by your illustrious self with bows and with humility, and who was eulogised in so high terms? We desire to hear about him.

description: The story of the world's creation,
sn: एवमुक्तस्तु भगवान् प्रत्युवाच पितामहः। देवब्रह्मर्षिगन्धर्वान् सर्वान् मधुरया गिरा॥
en: Thus spoken to, the almighty Grandsire, thus replied to the celestials, the regenerate sages, the Gandharvas and every one else in soft and sweet words.

description: The story of the world's creation,
sn: यत् तत् परं भविष्यं च भवितव्य च यत्परम्। भूतात्मा च प्रभुश्चैव ब्रह्म यच्च परं पदम्॥
en: "O foremost of the celestials he who is designated That, he who is supreme, he who is existent at present, and will be so for all future periods, he who is the highest self, he who is called the soul of beings, and he who is the paramount Lord.

description: The story of the world's creation,
sn: तेनास्मि कृतसंवादः प्रसन्नेन सुरर्षभाः। जगतोऽनुग्रहार्थाय याचितो मे जगत्पतिः॥
en: I was holding conversation even with his ever-contented self; that Lord of the universe has been entreated by me to show his grace on the earth.

description: The story of the world's creation,
sn: मानुषं लोकमातिष्ठ वासुदेव इति श्रुतः। असुराणां वधार्थाय सम्भवस्व महीतले॥
en: To take his birth in the world of men and to be known as the son of Vasudeva (I entreated him saying): "For slaughtering the Asuras, do you take your birth on the face of the earth.

description: The story of the world's creation,
sn: संग्रामे निहता ये ते दैत्यदानवराक्षसाः। त इमे नृषु सम्भूता घोररूपा महाबलाः॥
en: Those Daityas, and Danavas, and Rakshasas of dreadful appearance and of great might who were slain in battle, have been born among men.

description: The story of the world's creation,
sn: तेषां वधार्थं भगवान् नरेण सहितो वशी। मानुषीं योनिमास्थाय चरिष्यति महीतले।॥
en: For slaying them, the almighty Lord of great strength, being accompanied by Nara, shall wonder over the earth assuming a human form.

description: The story of the world's creation,
sn: नरनारायणौ यौ तौ पुराणावृषिसत्तमौ। सहितौ मानुषे लोके सम्भूतावमितद्युती॥
en: Those ancient and illustrious sages namely Nara and Narayana, are incapable of being vanquished in battle by even the gods united together.

description: The story of the world's creation,
sn: अजेयौ समरे यत्तौ सहितैरमरैरपि। मूढास्त्वेतौ न जानन्ति नरनारायणावृषी॥
en: Together, those two sages, Nara and Narayana, of immeasurable effulgence, will be born in the world of men, and they that are fools will not recognise them as such.

description: The story of the world's creation,
sn: तस्याहमग्रजः पुत्रः सर्वस्य जगतः प्रभुः। वासुदेवोऽर्चनीयो वः सर्वलोकमहेश्वरः॥
en: That Lord of the universe, whose son I Brahma am, that Vasudeva, the Paramount Lord of all the worlds should always be worshipped by you.

description: The story of the world's creation,
sn: तथा मनुष्योऽयमिति कदाचित् सुरसत्तमाः। नात्र ज्ञेयो महावीर्यः शङ्खचक्रगदाधरः॥
en: O you foremost of celestials, endued with great prowess and bearing the conch the discus and the mace, he should never be disregarded by you as a man.

description: The story of the world's creation,
sn: एतत् परमकं गुह्यमेतत् परमकं पदम्। एतत् परमकं ब्रह्म एतत् परमकं यशः॥
en: He is the supreme mystery; he is the supreme shelter; he is the supreme Brahma, and he is the supreme glory.

description: The story of the world's creation,
sn: एतदक्षरमव्यक्तमेतद् वै शाश्वतं महः। यत् तत् पुरुषसंज्ञं वै गीयते ज्ञायते न च॥
en: He is undeteriorating, unmanifested and eternal. He is designated the Purusha, he is ever sung but never known by any body.

description: The story of the world's creation,
sn: एतत् परमकं तेज एतत् परमकं सुखम्। एतत् परमकं सत्यं कीर्तितं विश्वकर्मणा॥
en: He is the supreme energy, his is the supreme felicity, he is the supreme truth. Thus has Vishvakarma sung.

description: The story of the world's creation,
sn: तस्मात् सेन्द्रैः सुरैः सर्वैर्लोकैश्चामितविक्रमः। नावज्ञेयो वासुदेवो मानुषोऽयमिति प्रभुः॥
en: Therefore the Lord Vasudeva of infinite prowess should never be disregarded as a man by the celestials and the Asuras headed by Indra himself.

description: The story of the world's creation,
sn: यश्च मानुशमात्रोऽयमिति ब्रूयात् स मन्दधीः। हृषीकेशमवज्ञानात् तमाहुः पुरुषाधमम्॥
en: That one of perverted understanding who, out of contempt, call Hrishikesha a man is said to be the vilest of all creatures.

description: The story of the world's creation,
sn: योगिनं तं महात्मानं प्रविष्टं मानुषीं तनुम्। अवमन्येद् वासुदेवं तमाहुस्तामसं जनाः॥
en: He is spoken of as a great sinner who disregards Vasudeva for his having incarnated himself as a man.

description: The story of the world's creation,
sn: देवं चराचरात्मानं श्रीवत्साङ्कं सुवर्चसम्। पद्मनाभं न जानाति तमाहुस्तामसं बुधाः॥
en: Men speak of him as a great sinner, who does not know that Divine one, that should of the mobile and the immobile, that one of pure effulgence, that one bearing the mark of Srivatsa on his breast, that one from whose navel a lotus has sprung.

description: The story of the world's creation,
sn: किरीटकौस्तुभधरं मित्राणामभयंकरम्। अवजानन महात्मानं घोरे तमसि मज्जति॥
en: Disregarding that wearer of the diadem and the gem Kaustubha, that giver of assurance of safety to his friends and one of illustrious soul, a man becomes sunk in the dreadful mire of sin.

description: The story of the world's creation,
sn: एवं विदित्वा तत्त्वार्थं लोकानामीश्वरेश्वरः। वासुदेवो नमस्कार्यः सर्वलोकैः सुरोत्तमाः॥
en: Every one, having known all these truths, should do obeisance, O best of the celestials, to Vasudeva that Lord of the fords of people”.

description: The story of the world's creation,
sn: भीष्म उवाच एवमुक्त्वा स भगवान् देवान् सर्षिगणान् पुरा। विसृज्य सर्वभूतात्मा जगाम भवनं स्वकम्॥
en: Bhishma said That almighty one (the Grandsire), having thus spoken to the gods and the sages in the days of yore, repaired to his own residence' leaving all creatures behind.

description: The story of the world's creation,
sn: ततो देवाः सगन्धर्वा मुनयोऽप्सरसोऽपि च। कथां तां ब्रह्मणा गीतां श्रुत्वा प्रीता दिवं ययुः॥
en: as Thereafter the celestials, together with the Gandharvas, the sages, and the Apsaras, having listened to that discourse delivered by Brahma, went to Heaven with joyful hearts.

description: The story of the world's creation,
sn: एतच्छ्रुतं मया तात ऋषीणां भावितात्मनाम्। वासुदेवं कथयतां समवाये पुरातनम्॥
en: It was this, O sire, that was heard by me from the sages of accomplished understanding when they were speaking of Vasudeva the ancient one, among their assembly.

description: The story of the world's creation,
sn: रामस्य जामदग्न्यस्य मार्कण्डेयस्य धीमतः। व्यासनारदयोश्चापि सकाशाद् भरतर्षभ।॥
en: O you conversant with the Shastras, I also heard this from Rama the son of Jamnadagni, from the highly intelligent Markandeya and also from Vyasa and Narada.

description: The story of the world's creation,
sn: एतमर्थं च विज्ञाय श्रुत्वा च प्रभुमव्ययम्। वासुदेवं महात्मानं लोकानामीश्वरेश्वरम्॥
en: Having heard the truth about the subject, and having heard of Vasudeva the undeteriorating Lord of illustrious soul, the supreme Master of the Lords of people.

description: The story of the world's creation,
sn: यस्य चैवात्मजो ब्रह्मा सर्वस्य जगत: पिता। कथं न वासुदेवोऽयमय॑श्चेज्यश्च मानवैः॥
en: From whose self has sprung Brahma the father of all the universe, why should not men adore and worship that Vasudeva?

description: The story of the world's creation,
sn: वारितोऽसि मया तात मुनिभिवेदपारगैः। मा गच्छ संयुगं तेन वासुदेवेन धन्विना॥
en: You have been, O sire, forbidden in days past, by the sages of accomplished understandings (who said to you), “Do not risk a battle with Vasudeva the wielder of the bow.

description: The story of the world's creation,
sn: मा पाण्डवैः सार्धमिति तत् त्वं मोहान बुध्यसे। मन्ये त्वां राक्षसं क्रूरं तथा चासि तमोवृतः॥
en: As also with the Pandavas, But out of folly, you could not comprehend my word; I do regard you therefore as a cruel Rakshasa; and you are encompassed in ignorance.

description: The story of the world's creation,
sn: यस्माद् द्विषसि गोविन्दं पाण्डवं तं धनंजयम्। नरनारायणौ देवौ कोऽन्यो द्विष्याद्धि मानवः॥
en: For this reason it is that you despise Govinda and Dhananjaya the son of Pandu; for what other man could despise the divine Nara and Narayana?

description: The story of the world's creation,
sn: तस्माद् ब्रवीमि ते राजन्नेष वै शाश्वतोऽव्ययः। सर्वलोकमयो नित्यः शास्ता धात्रीधरे. ध्रुवः॥
en: I therefore, O monarch, say to you that this one is eternal and undeteriorating pervading the whole universe, immutable, the ruler, the creator, the supporter and the truly existent.

description: The story of the world's creation,
sn: यो धारयति लोकांस्त्रींश्चराचरगुरुः प्रभुः। योद्धा जयश्च जेता च सर्वप्रकृतिरीश्वरः॥
en: That preceptor of the mobile and the immobile creations, that supreme Lord supports the triune world; he is the Warrior the Victory, the Victorious, and the Lord of all nature.

description: The story of the world's creation,
sn: राजन् सर्वमयो ह्येष तमोरागविवर्जितः। यतः कृष्णस्ततो धर्मो यतो धर्मस्ततो जयः॥
en: He is permeated, O king, with the quality of goodness and is free from the slightest tinge of the qualities of passion and dullness. Righteousness is where Krishna is; and victory is where righteousness is.

description: The story of the world's creation,
sn: तस्य माहात्म्ययोगेन योगेनात्ममयेन च। धृताः पाण्डुसुता राजञ्जयश्चैषां भविष्यति॥
en: The sons of Pandu are, O king, supported by the supreme excellence of his Yoga of self; and, with certitude, victory will court them.

description: The story of the world's creation,
sn: श्रेयोयुक्तां सदा बुद्धिं पाण्डवानां दधाति यः। बलं चैव रणे नित्यं भयेभ्यश्चैव रक्षति॥
en: He it is who inspires the sons of Pandu with an intelligence that brings about their prosperity; he it is who charges them with strength in battle; he it is who ever protects them from danger.

description: The story of the world's creation,
sn: स एष शाश्वतो देवः सर्वगुह्यमयः शिवः। वासुदेव इति ज्ञेयो यन्मां पृच्छसि भारत॥
en: This one is that eternal Deity that pervades all creatures, and is ever blessed. He, of whom you have asked me, is celebrated under the name of Vasudeva.

description: The story of the world's creation,
sn: ब्राह्मणैः क्षत्रियैर्वैश्यैः शूदैश्च कृतलक्षणैः। सेव्यतेऽभ्यर्च्यते चैव नित्ययुक्तैः स्वकर्मभिः॥
en: He is adored and served with restrained hearts alike by the Brahmanas, the Kshatriya, the Vaishyas, and the Shudras, each having distinguishing features of their own, and performing their own duties.

description: The story of the world's creation,
sn: द्वापरस्य युगस्यान्ते आदौ कलियुगस्य च। सात्वतं विधिमास्थाय गीत: संकर्षणेन वै॥
en: He it is , whom, at the end of the Dvapara Yuga and in the beginning of the Kali Yuga Samkarshana had eulogised in the manner of devotees.

description: The story of the world's creation,
sn: स एष सर्वं सुरमर्त्यलोकं समुद्रकक्ष्यान्तरितां पुरीं च। युगे युगे मानुषं चैव वासं पुनः पुनः सृजते वासुदेवः॥
en: It is that Vasudeva the creator of the universe who does repeatedly create, Yuga after Yuga, all the regions of the celestials and the mortals, all the sea-girt cities, and also all the regions of human habitation.

sn: दुर्योधन उवाच वासुदेवो महद् भूतं सर्वलोकेषु कथ्यते। तस्यागमं प्रतिष्ठां च ज्ञातुमिच्छे पितामह॥
en: Duryodhana said In all the worlds, Vasudeva is spoken of as the Highest Being; O grandsire, I desire to know all about his nativity and his glory.

sn: भीष्म उवाच वासुदेवो महद् भूतं सर्वदैवतदैवतम्। न परं पुण्डरीकाक्षाद् दृश्यते भरतर्षभ॥
en: Bhishma said Vasudeva is the Supreme Being, the God of all gods. There is to be seen none, O foremost of the Bharata, superior to Him of eyes resembling lotus petals.

sn: मार्कण्डेयश्च गोविन्दे कथयत्यद्भुतं महत्। सर्वभूतानि भूतात्मा महात्मा पुरुषोत्तमः॥
en: Markandeya speaks of Govinda as the great mystery, as all beings, as the Soul of all, as the Highest Soul and as the Foremost of all male beings.

sn: आपो वायुश्च तेजश्च त्रयमेतदकल्पयत्। स सृष्ट्वा पृथिवीं देवीं सर्वलोकेश्वरः प्रभुः॥
en: He created these three things viz., Water, Air, and Fire. Having created this Earth, that Divine Master, the Lord of all the worlds.

sn: अप्सु वै शयनं चक्रे महात्मा पुरुषोत्तमः। सर्वतेजोमयो देवो योगात् सुष्वाप तत्र ह॥
en: That Highest Soul, that Foremost of all Beings, laid himself down on the waters. Therein, that Divine One composed of all energies, was lulled in sleep through his Yoga.

sn: मुखतः सोऽग्निमसृजत् प्राणाद् वायुमथापि च। सरस्वती च वेदांश्च मनसः ससृजेऽच्युतः॥
en: He created Fire from his mouth, and wind from His vital breath. That undeteriorating One created Words and the Vedas from his mind.

sn: एष लोकान् ससर्जादौ देवांश्च ऋषिभिः सह। निधनं चैव मृत्युं च प्राजानां प्रभवाप्ययौ॥
en: At first, He created these worlds as also the celestials along with all the sages, He also created decrepitude and death of all creatures and also their growth and birth.

sn: एष धर्मश्च धर्मज्ञो वरदः सर्वकामदः। एष कर्ता च कार्यं च पूर्वदेवः स्वयम्प्रभुः॥
en: He is righteousness itself and is versed in all duties. He is the giver of boons and the gratifier of all our desires. He is the Actor himself as well as the Act itself, and he is the Divine and the Sole Master.

sn: भूतं भव्यं भविष्यच्च पूर्वमेतदकल्पयत्। उभे संध्ये दिशः खं च नियमांश्च जनार्दनः॥ ऋषींश्चैव हि गोविन्दस्तपश्चैवाभ्यकल्पयत्। स्रष्टारं जगतश्चापि महात्मा प्रभुरव्ययः॥
en: That undeteriorating Lord of illustrious soul, as first created the Past, the Present and the Future and also the creator of the worlds viz., (Brahma).

sn: अग्रजं सर्वभूतानां संकर्षणकल्पयत्। तस्मान्नारायणो जज्ञे देवदेवः सनातनः॥ नाभौ पद्मं बभूवास्य सर्वलोकस्य सम्भवात्। तस्मात् पितामहो जातस्तस्माज्जातास्त्विमाः प्रजाः।१२। शेषं चाकल्पयद् देवमनन्तं विश्वरूपिणम्।
en: That perfect supreme soul Sri Krishna very first originated Samkarsana, the elder to all living beings. Narayana, the everlasting god of gods was then emerged from him. A lotus was appeared from the navel zone of Narayana. Brahma, grandfather to all and sole cause for creation of this entire world, appeared from that lotus flower. All species of the living organisms have originated then from god Brahina. He created the divine Shesha who is otherwise known as Ananta.

sn: यो धारयति भूतानि धरां चेमां सपर्वताम्॥ ध्यानयोगेन विप्राश्च तं विदन्ति महौजसम्।
en: And who supports all creatures and upholds the Earth with all her mountains. Through devout mediation, the Vipras come to know him of supreme energy.

sn: कर्णस्रोतोभवं चापि मधुं नाम महासुरम्॥ तमुग्रमुग्रकर्माणमुग्रां बुद्धिं समास्थितम्। ब्रह्मणोऽपचितिं कुर्वञ् जघान पुरुषोत्तमः॥ तस्य तात वधादेव देवदानवमानवाः।
en: That Foremost of all make beings slew the mighty Asura named Madhu who was born out of the secretion of His ears, who was furious and of fierce actions and fierce intentions, when he was on the point of destroying Brahma. In consequence of His slaying that Asura, the celestials, the Danavas, and the mortals.

sn: मधुसूदनमित्याहुर्ऋषयश्च जनार्दनम्॥ वराहश्चैव सिंहश्च त्रिविक्रमगतिः प्रभुः।
en: And the sages call Janardana by the name of the Slayer of Madhu. The great Boar, the Lion and the three treaded Lord.

sn: एष माता पिता चैव सर्वेषां प्राणिनां हरिः॥ परं हि पुण्डरीकाक्षान्न भूतं न भविष्यति।
en: Hari is the Father, and the Mother of all living creatures. Neither there was nor there will be, any one superior to Him of eyes like lotus petals.

sn: मुखतः सोऽसृजद् विप्रान् बाहुभ्यां क्षत्रियांस्तथा॥ वैश्यांश्चाप्यूस्तो राजशूद्रान् वै पादतस्तथा।
en: From His mouth, O monarch, He created, the Regenerate, from His arms the Kshatriya, from His thighs the Vaishyas and from His legs the Shudras.

sn: तपसा नियतो देवं विधानं सर्वदेहिनाम्॥ ब्रह्मभूतममावास्यां पौर्णमास्यां तथैव च। योगभूतं परिचरन् केशवं महदाप्नुयात्॥ केशवः परमं तेजः सर्वलोकपितामहः।
en: With ascetic austerities devoutly serving in the days of the full moon and the new moon Keshava the Divine, the creator of all corporal creatures, the Essence of Brahma and of Yoga, one surely attains to Him. Keshava has been called the Supreme energy and the Grandsire of the worlds.

sn: एनमाहुर्हषीकेशं मुनयो वै नराधिप॥ एवमेनं विजानीहि आचार्यं पितरं गुरुम्।
en: The sages, O ruler of men, call Him Hrishikesha or the Lord of the senses, Know Him also to be the supreme Teacher, the Father, and the Preceptor.

sn: कृष्णो यस्य प्रसीदेत लोकास्तेनाक्षया जिताः॥ यश्चैवैनं भयस्थाने केशवं शरणं व्रजेत्।
en: Regions of undeteriorating blessedness is secured by him on whom Krishna becomes gracious. He that seeks protection from Keshava in seasons of danger, and

sn: सदा नरः पठंश्चेदं स्वस्तिमान् स सुखी भवेत्॥ ये च कृष्णं प्रपद्यन्ते ते न मुह्यन्ति मानवाः।
en: He that always reads of His themes, becomes happy and attended will all blessings. Those who attain to Krishna are never again befouled.

sn: भये महति मग्नांश्च पाति नित्यं जनार्दनः॥ स तं युधिष्ठिरो ज्ञात्वा याथातथ्येन भारत।
en: That Janardana ever saves those who are overwhelmed with great terror. O descendant of the Bharata race, perfectly aware of this fact, Yudhishthira,

sn: सर्वात्मना महात्मानं केशवं जदीश्वरम्। प्रपन्नः शरणं राजन् योगानां प्रभुमीश्वरम्॥
en: With his whole soul, has sought shelter in Keshava, the Supreme God, the Lord of the worlds, the Master of all Yoga and the Lord of this Earth.

sn: भीष्म उवाच शृणु चेदं महाराज ब्रह्मभूतं स्तवं मम। ब्रह्मर्षिभिश्च देवैश्च यः पुरा कथितो भुवि॥
en: Bhishma said Hear, O monarch, from me this hymn, chanted by Brahma himself, and recounted in the days of yore to men on earth by the Brahmanical sages and the celestial.

sn: साध्यानामपि देवानां देवदेवेश्वरः प्रभुः। लोकभावनभावज्ञ इति त्वां नारदोऽब्रवीत्॥
en: “You are the Master of the Sadhyas and the celestial and are the Lord of the god of gods, the Protector of people and the Knower of all hearts. Thus has the sage Narada sung of you.

sn: भूतं भव्यं भविष्यं च मार्कण्डेयोऽभ्युवाच ह। यज्ञं त्वां चैव यज्ञानां तपश्च तपसामपि॥
en: Markandeya has spoken of you as the Past, the Present, and the Future, the sacrifice of all sacrifices and the Austerity of all austerities.

sn: देवानामपि देवं च त्वामाह भगवान् भृगुः। पुराणं चैव परमं विष्णो रूपं तवेति च॥
en: The almighty Bhrigu has sang of you that you are the God of all gods, and you are the ancient and excellent semblance that is ascribed to Vishnu.

sn: वासुदेवो वसूनां त्वं शक्रं स्थापयिता तथा। देव देवोऽसि देवानामिति द्वैपायनोऽब्रवीत्॥
en: Dvaipayana spoke of you that you are the Vasudeva among the Vasu, the consolidator of the sway of Shakra (Indra) and the God of gods and of all created beings.

sn: पूर्वे प्रजानिसर्गे च दक्षमाहुः प्रजापितम्। स्रष्टारं सर्वलोकानामङ्गिरास्त्वां तथाऽब्रवीत्॥
en: In the days of yore, on the occasion of the creation of creatures, you have been called Daksha, the Lord of creation. Angiras has spoken of you as the creator of all corporeal beings.

sn: अव्यक्तं ते शरीरोत्थं व्यक्तं ते मनसि स्थितम्। देवास्त्वत्सम्भवाश्चैव देवलस्त्वसितोऽब्रवीत्॥
en: Devala has sung of you that the Unmanifest All is in your form and the Manifest is in your mind, and that the celestial have all sprung from your speech (breath).

sn: शिरसा ते दिवं व्याप्तं बाहुभ्यां पृथिवी तथा। जठरं ते त्रयो लोकाः पुरुषोऽसि सनातनः॥
en: The heavens are pervaded with your head; you does sustain the Earth with your two arms the triune world is inside your abdomen you are the Eternal Male being.

sn: एवं त्वामभिजानन्ति तपसा भाविता नराः। आत्मदर्शनतृप्तानामृषीणां चासि सत्तमः॥
en: Persons purified by the performance of austerities, know your divine self even to be such, To the sages gratified with a knowledge of the self, you are the foremost of all true existent entities.

sn: राजर्षीणामुदाराणामाहवेष्वनिवर्तिनाम्। सर्वधर्मप्रधानानां त्वं गतिर्मधुसूदन॥
en: O Slayer of Madhu, you are the sole refuge of the royal sages, who are of illustrious nature, who never turn back from the fight and who are devoted to all their duties.

sn: इति नित्यं योगविद्भिर्भगवान् पुरुषोत्तमः। सनत्कुमारप्रमुखैः स्तूयतेऽभ्यर्च्यते हरिः॥
en: Even thus is that almighty and excellent Being Hari always adored and eulogised by sages conversant with the Yoga who are headed by Sanatkumara".

sn: एष ते विस्तरस्तात संक्षेपश्च प्रकीर्तितः। केशवस्य यथातत्त्वं सुप्रीतो भज केशवम्॥
en: Thus, O Sire, has been described to you, in detail and in brief, the real nature of Keshava. Now turn you heart in love to Keshava.

sn: संजय उवाच पुण्यं श्रुत्वैतदाख्यानं महाराज सुतस्तव। केशवं बहु मेने स पाण्डवांश्च महारथान्॥
en: Sanjaya said Your son, O mighty monarch, listening to this sacred story, began to regard highly Keshava and those mighty car-warriors, the sons Pandu.

sn: तमब्रवीन्महाराज भीष्मः शान्तनवः पुनः। माहात्म्यं ते श्रुतं राजन् केशवस्य महात्मनः॥ नरस्य च यथातत्त्वं यन्मां त्वं पृच्छसे नृप। यदर्थं नृषु सम्भूतौ नरनारायणावृषी॥
en: Thereafter, O monarch, Bhishma, the son of Shantanu, again addressed him saying-"You have now heard, o monarch, the true description of the glory of the high-souled Keshava and of Nara, about which you asked me. You have also heard of the purpose for which both Nara and Narayana have taken their births among men.

sn: अवध्यौ च यथा वीरौ संयुगेष्वपराजितौ। यथा च पाण्डवा राजन्नवध्या युधि कस्यचित्॥
en: You have also learnt why those two heroes are invincible and why they have not been ever vanquished in battle; as also why the sons of Pandu, O king, are unslayable in battle by anybody.

sn: प्रीतिमान् हि दृढं कृष्णः पाण्डवेषु यशस्विषु। तस्माद् ब्रवीमि राजेन्द्र शमो भवतु पाण्डवैः॥
en: Towards the Pandavas endued with fame, Krishna bears an unshaken affection. Therefore it is, O foremost of sovereigns, that I advice that peace be concluded with the Pandavas.

sn: पृथिवीं भुक्ष्व सहितो भ्रातृभिर्बलिभिर्वशी। नरनारायणौ देवाववज्ञाय न शिष्यसि॥
en: Controlling your passions do you rule this earth with your powerful brothers around you. You shall surely reap destruction if you disregard the divine Nara and Narayana”.

sn: एवमुक्त्वा तव पिता तूष्णीमासीद् विशाम्पते। व्यसर्जयच्च राजान शयनं च विवेश ह॥
en: Having spoken thus, O ruler of men, your father became silent; and dismissing the king, he entered his own tent.

sn: राजा च शिबिरं प्रायात् प्रणिपत्य महात्मने। शिश्ये च शयने शुभे रात्रिं तां भरतर्षभ।।२०
en: The king also retired to his own tent having bowed down to that one of illustrious soul. Then, O foremost of the Bharatas, he slept away that night on a (milk) white bed.

description: The commencement of the fifth day's fight
sn: संजय उवाच व्युषितायां तु शर्वर्यामुदिते च दिवाकरे। उभे सेने महाराज युद्धायैव समीयतुः॥
en: Sanjaya said When that night had passed away and when the sun had risen, the two armies O mighty monarch, encountered each other for battle.

description: The commencement of the fifth day's fight
sn: अभ्यधावन्त संक्रुद्धाः परस्परजिगीषवः। ते सर्वे सहिता युद्धे समालोक्य परस्परम्॥
en: LoO king at each other in that battle, they rushed against each other in serried files, inflamed with rage and desirous of slaying and conquering each other.

description: The commencement of the fifth day's fight
sn: पाण्डवा धार्तराष्ट्राश्च राजन् दुर्मन्त्रिते तव। व्यूहौ च व्यूह्य संरब्धाः सम्प्रहृष्टाः प्रहारिणः॥
en: In consequence of your wicked counsel, O king, the Pandavas and the Dhritarashtra, filled with joy, clad in mail and formed in battle array, rushed against one another for striking one another.

description: The commencement of the fifth day's fight
sn: अरक्षन्मकरव्यूह भीष्मो राजन् समन्ततः। तथैव पाण्डवा राजन्नरक्षन् व्यूहमात्मनः॥
en: O monarch, Bhishma protected on all sides the array of his troops that figured the Makara. O king, so also, the sons of Pandu protected the array that they had formed with their troops.

description: The commencement of the fifth day's fight
sn: स निर्ययौ महाराज पिता देवव्रतस्तव। महता रथवंशेन संवृतो रथिनां वरः॥
en: Then, O mighty monarch, your sire Devavrata, that foremost of car-warriors, marched forth surrounded by a mighty host of cars.

description: The commencement of the fifth day's fight
sn: इतरेतरमन्वीयुर्यथाभागमवस्थिताः। रथिनः पत्तयश्चैव दन्तिनः सादिनस्तथा॥
en: And other car-warriors, foot-soldiers tuskers and horse-soldiers, followed him each stationed in his proper rank.

description: The commencement of the fifth day's fight
sn: तान् दृष्ट्वाभ्युद्यतान् संख्ये पाण्डवा हि यशस्विनः। श्येनेन व्यूहराजेन तेनाजव्येन संयुगे॥
en: The sons of Pandu endued with fame, seeing the Kauravas ready for the encounter, formed their troops in that invincible and excellent array that figures a hawk.

description: The commencement of the fifth day's fight
sn: अशोभत मुखे तस्य भीमसेनो महाबलः। नेत्रे शिखण्डी दुर्धर्षो धृष्टद्युम्नश्च पार्षतः॥
en: And in the backs of that hawk-like array shone Bhimasena possessed of great strength. In its eyes Shikhandin and the irrepressible Dhrishtadyumna the of Prishata.

description: The commencement of the fifth day's fight
sn: शीर्षे तस्याभवद् वीरः सात्यकिः सत्यविक्रमः। विधुन्वन् गाण्डिवं पार्थो ग्रीवायामभवत् तदा॥
en: In its head was stationed the heroic Satyaki of invincible prowess; and in its neck was Partha wielding the Gandiva bow.

description: The commencement of the fifth day's fight
sn: अक्षौहिण्या समं तत्र वामपक्षोऽभवत् तदा। महात्मा द्रुपदः श्रीमान् सह पुत्रेण संयुगे।॥
en: The high-souled Drupada ever attended with prosperity, along with his son, and supported by a Akshauhini of troops, formed its left wing. were son

description: The commencement of the fifth day's fight
sn: दक्षिणश्चाभवत् पक्षः कैकेयोऽक्षौहिणीपतिः। पृष्ठतो द्रौपदेयाश्च सौभद्रश्चापि वीर्यवान्॥
en: Its right wing was formed by Kaikeya the commander of a division consisting of a Akshauhini; in its back were the sons of Draupadi and the highly powerful son of Subhadra.

description: The commencement of the fifth day's fight
sn: पृष्ठे समभवच्छ्रीमान् स्वयं राजा युधिष्ठिरः। भ्रातृभ्यां सहितो वीरो यमाभ्यां चारुविक्रमः॥
en: In its tail was the heroic and even prosperous king Yudhishthira himself endued with great prowess, and supported by his twin brothers Nakula and Sahadeva.

description: The commencement of the fifth day's fight
sn: प्रविश्य त रणे भीमो मकरं मुखतस्तदा। भीष्ममासाद्य संग्रामे च्छादयामास सायकैः॥
en: Then in the battle that commenced Bhima, penetrating through the mouth of the Makara like array of the Kauravas, approached Bhishma and covered him over with arrows.

description: The commencement of the fifth day's fight
sn: ततो भीष्मो महास्त्राणि पातयामास भारत। मोहयन् पाण्डुपुत्राणां व्यूढं सैन्यं महाहवे।॥
en: Thereupon Bhishma endued with great prowess, discharged powerful weapons that confounded in that fierce encounter the array of troops belonging to the sons of Pandu.

description: The commencement of the fifth day's fight
sn: सम्मुह्यति तदा सैन्ये त्वरमाणो धनंजयः। भीष्मं शरसहस्रेण विव्याध रणमूर्धनि॥
en: Upon the confusion of the the force, Dhananjaya proceeding heavily, pierced Bhishma with a thousand shafts, at the van of battle.

description: The commencement of the fifth day's fight
sn: प्रतिसंवार्य चास्त्राणि भीष्ममुक्तानि संयुगे। स्वेनानीकेन हृष्टेन युद्धाय समुपस्थितः॥
en: Having baffled in that battle the weapons discharged by Bhishma, Dhananjaya stood ready for the encounter, supported by his own division filled with joy.

description: The commencement of the fifth day's fight
sn: ततो दुर्योधनो राजा भारद्वाजमभाषत। पूर्वं दृष्ट्वा वधं घोरं बलस्य बलिना वरः॥ भ्रातृणां च वधं युद्धे स्मरमाणो महारथः। आचार्य सततं हि त्वं हितकामो ममानघ।॥ वयं हि त्वां समाश्रित्य भीष्मं चैव पितामहम्। देवानपि रणे जेतु प्रार्थयामो न संशयः॥ किमु पाण्डुसुतान् युद्धे हीनवीर्यपराक्रमान्। स तथा कुरु भद्रं ते यथा वध्यन्ति पाण्डवाः॥
en: Thereupon king Duryodhana that foremost of those endued with strength that great carwarrior seeing that terrible slaughter of his army and remembering the death of his brothers, in the battle, speedily approached the son of Bharadvaja, and addressing him said:-0 preceptor, O sinless one, you are my constant well-wisher. Relaying on you as also on the grandsire, we expect without doubt to conquer in battle even the very celestial themselves.

description: The commencement of the fifth day's fight
sn: द्रोण उवाच बालिशस्त्वं न जानीषे पाण्डवानां पराक्रमम्। न शक्या हि यथा जेतुं पाण्डवा हि महाबलाः॥ यथाबलं यथावीर्यं कर्म कुर्यामहं हि ते।
en: It is undoubtedly true that we are ambitious of subjugating the gods too by giving them defeat in battle-field if escorted by you and grandfather Bhishma. Again, it is not anyway a big mission to conquer Pandavas who already are devoid of power and valour both. Be it for all good to you. Do an attempt viable to kill all Pandavas.

description: The commencement of the fifth day's fight
sn: एवमुक्तस्ततो द्रोणस्तव पुत्रेण मारिष। अभिनत् पाण्डवानीकं प्रेक्षमाणस्य सात्यकेः॥
en: Thus spoken to on the field by your son, Drona penetrated the Pandava array even before the very eyes of Satyaki.

description: The commencement of the fifth day's fight
sn: सात्यकिस्तु ततो द्रोणं वारयामास भारत। तयोः प्रववृते युद्धं घोररूपं भयावहम्॥
en: Thereat, O Bharata, Satyaki impeded the progress of Drona. Thereupon ensued an encounter that was fierce and terrible to look at.

description: The commencement of the fifth day's fight
sn: शैनेयं तु रणे क्रुद्धो भारद्वाजः प्रतापवान्। अविध्यन्निशितैर्बाणैर्जत्रुदेशे हसन्निव॥
en: Then in that battle the highly powerful son of Bharadvaja, burning with rage as if smiling, struck the grandson of Shini with ten shafts on his shoulder-joint.

description: The commencement of the fifth day's fight
sn: भीमसेनस्ततः क्रुद्धो भारद्वाजमविध्यत। संरक्षनं सात्यकि राजन् द्रोणाच्छस्त्रभृतां वरात्॥
en: At this, Bhimasena waxing worth, pierced Bharadvaja with arrow, desirous O monarch, of rescuing Satyaki from Drona that foremost of all wielders of weapons.

description: The commencement of the fifth day's fight
sn: ततो द्रोणश्च भीष्मश्च तथा शल्यश्च मारिष। भीमसेनं रणे क्रुद्धाश्छादयांचक्रिरे शरैः॥
en: Thereat Drona and Bhishma and also Shalya, O sire, inflamed with rage, covered Bhimasena in that battle with a thick shower of) arrows.

description: The commencement of the fifth day's fight
sn: तत्राभिमन्युः संक्रुद्धो द्रौपदेयाश्च मारिष। विव्यधुनिशितैर्बाणैः सर्वांस्तानुद्यतायुधान्॥
en: Then, O sire, Abhimanyu waxing worth, and the sons of Draupadi also, pierced with their whetted shafts all those warriors with uplifted weapons.

description: The commencement of the fifth day's fight
sn: द्रोणभीष्मौ तु संक्रुद्धावापतन्तौ महाबलौ। प्रत्युद्ययौ शिखण्डी तु महेष्वासो महाहवे॥
en: Then in that fierce battle, the mighty bowman Shikhandin rushed against Bhishma and Drona, both of great prowess, who inflamed with wrath, had fallen upon his own troops.

description: The commencement of the fifth day's fight
sn: प्रगृह्य बलवद् वीरो धनुर्जलदनिःस्वनम्। अभ्यवर्षच्छरैस्तूर्ण छादयानो दिवाकरम्॥
en: Grasping a every tough bow of which the twang resembled the rumble of the clouds, that hero speedily poured down a shower of arrows, shrouding the sun itself.

description: The commencement of the fifth day's fight
sn: शिखण्डिनं समासाद्य भरतानां पितामहः। अवर्जयत संग्रामं स्त्रीत्वं तस्यानुसंस्मरन्।॥
en: But the grandsire of the Bharatas, meeting with Shikhandin in the battle avoided him, remembering the femininity of his sex.

description: The commencement of the fifth day's fight
sn: ततो द्रोणो महाराज अभ्यद्रवत तं रणे। रक्षमाणस्तदा भीष्मं तव पुत्रेण चोदितः॥
en: Thereat, O mighty monarch, urged by your son, Drona rushed into the encounter, in order to protect Bhishma.

description: The commencement of the fifth day's fight
sn: शिखण्डी तु समासाद्य द्रोणं शस्त्रभृतां वरम्। अवर्जयत संत्रस्तो युगान्ताग्निमिवोल्बणम्॥
en: Shikhandin also encountering Drona the foremost of all wielders of weapons, shunned him out of feat, like one flying from the blazing fire that burns at the end of a Yuga.

description: The commencement of the fifth day's fight
sn: ततो बलेन महता पुत्रस्तव विशाम्पते। जुगोप भीष्मासाद्य प्राथयानो महद् यशः॥
en: Then O ruler of earth, your son, supported by a mighty division, advanced to rescue Bhishma, out of a desire for securing great fame.

description: The commencement of the fifth day's fight
sn: तथैव पाण्डवा राजन् पुरस्कृत्य धनंजयम्। भीष्ममेवाभ्यवर्तन्त जये कृत्वा दृढां मतिम्॥
en: So also, O monarch, the Pandavas firmly setting their heart upon victory rushed at Bhishma, placing Dhananjaya at their head.

description: The commencement of the fifth day's fight
sn: तद् युद्धमभवद् घोरं देवानां दानवैरिव। जयमाकाङ्क्षतां संख्ये यशश्च सुमहाद्भुतम्॥
en: Then a fierce and wonderful encounter, like that between the celestial and the Asuras, ensued between those two hosts each desirous of winning victory and great fame in battle.

sn: संजय उवाच अकरोत् तुमुलं युद्धं भीष्मः शान्तनवस्तदा। भीमसेनभयादिच्छन् पुत्रांस्तारयितुं तव॥ पूर्वाह्ने तन्महारौद्रं राज्ञां युद्धमवर्तत। कुरूणां पाण्डवानां च मुख्यशूरविनाशनम्॥
en: Sanjaya said Then Bhishma, the son of Shantanu, fought a fierce battle, desirous of saving your sons from their fear of Bhimasena. In that morning, a most dreadful battle was fought between the kings of the Kaurava and the Pandava hosts, in which many best warriors were slain.

sn: तस्मिन्नाकुलसंग्रामे वर्तमाने महाभये। अभवत् तुमुलः शब्दः संस्पृशन् गगनं महत्॥
en: When that furious and dreadful engagement raged, a terrible din arose, that touched the very heavens.

sn: नदद्भिश्च महानागैर्हेषमाणैश्च वाजिभिः। भेरीशङ्खनिनादैश्च तुमुलं समपद्यत॥
en: The clangour that was made was deafening in consequence of the roars of stricking elephants and the neighs of steeds and the blare of conchis and the sound of drums.

sn: युयुत्सवस्ते विक्रान्ता विजयाय महाबलाः। अन्योन्यमभिगर्जन्तो गोष्ठेष्विव महर्षभाः॥
en: Those mighty warriors endued with great prowess, fighting with one another out of a desires for victory roared at one another like bulls among a herd of kine.

sn: शिरसां पात्यमानानां समरे निशितैः शरैः। अश्मवृष्टिरिवाकाशे बभूव भरतर्षभ॥
en: O foremost of the Bharatas, heads cut off with keen-edged arrows, falling in that battle, appeared like a shower of stones from the skies.

sn: कुण्डलोष्णीषधारीणि जातरूपोज्ज्वलानि च। पतितानि स्म दृश्यन्ते शिरांसि भरतर्षभ॥
en: Many heads, O foremost of the Bharatas, were seen lying on the field of battle, graced with ear-rings and head-gears, and effulgent like gold itself.

sn: विशिखोन्मथितैर्गात्रैर्बाहुभिश्च सकार्मुकैः। सहस्ताभरणैश्चान्यैरभवच्छादिता मही॥
en: The ground was strewn over with limbs severed by Vishikha, with head graced with ear-rings, and with arms decorated with ornaments &c.

sn: कवचोपहितैर्गात्रैर्हस्तैश्च समलंकृतैः। मुखैश्च चन्द्रसंकाशै रक्तान्तनयनैः शुभैः॥ गजवाजिमनुष्याणां सर्वगात्रैश्च भूपते। आसीत् सर्वा समास्तीर्णा मुहूर्तेन वसुंधरा॥
en: In A moment the earth literally became covered over with bodies cased in arinours, with decorated arms, with faces charming like the moon and beauty fled with eyes with coppery corners, and O monarch, with the of dead bodies of elephants, steeds and men.

sn: रजोमेघैश्च तुमुलैः शस्त्रविद्युत्प्रकाशिभिः। आयुधानां च निर्घोषः स्तनयित्नुसमोऽभवत्।॥
en: Under the thick clouds of dust (raised by the warriors) in which the whistling weapons flashed like lightning, the sound emitted by the various implements of war resembled the roars of thunder.

sn: स सम्प्रहारस्तुमुलः कटुकः शोणितोदकः। प्रावर्तत कुरूणां च पाण्डवानां च भारत॥
en: That dreadful and fierce fight, O Bharata, between the Kurus and the Pandus created a river of blood in the field of battle.

sn: तस्मिन् महाभये घोरे तुमुले लोमहर्षणे। ववृषुः शरवर्षाणि क्षत्रिया युद्धदुर्मदाः॥
en: In that fierce, dreadful terrifying and hairstirring battle, the Kshatriya in capable of being repressed in battle began to shower a veritable down-pour of arrows.

sn: आक्रोशन् कुञ्जरास्तत्र शरवर्षप्रतापिताः। तावकानां परेषां च संयुगे भरतर्षभ॥
en: Afflicted with that shower of arrows, the elephants of your army as well as of the enemy's army, began to shriek aloud and run hither and thither with uplifted trunks.

sn: संरब्धानां च वीराणां धीराणाममितौजसाम्। धनुातलशब्देन न प्राज्ञायत किंचन॥
en: Nothing could be heard in consequence of the flapping produced by bows of great toughness, belonging to cool-headed warriors excited with fury.

sn: उत्थितेषु कबन्धेषु सर्वतः शोणितोदके। समरे पर्यधावन्त नृपा रिपुवधोद्यताः॥
en: As head-less trunks stood up in that sea of blood, other kings rushed into battle endeavoring to slay their enemies.

sn: शरशक्तिगदाभिस्ते खड्नेश्चामिततेजसः। निजघ्नुः समरेऽन्योन्यं शूराः परिघबाहवः॥
en: Heroes of immeasurable prowess possessed of arms resembling bludgeons, slew one another in that battle, with shafts and Shaktis and maces and swords.

sn: बभ्रमुः कुञ्जराश्चात्र शरैर्विद्धा निरङ्कुशाः। अश्वाश्च पर्यधावन्त हतारोहा दिशो दश॥
en: Pierced with shafts and deprived of their riders who used to guide them with hooks, elephants began to course (madly) through the field steeds ran about in all direction having their riders slain.

sn: उत्पत्य निपतन्त्यन्ये शरघातप्रपीडिताः। तावकानां परेषां च योधा भरतसत्तम॥
en: Many warriors of your army and many belonging to the host of enemy afflicted with shafts-wounds, running hither and thither (with pain), (at last) jumped up and fell down.

sn: वाहानामुत्तमाङ्गानां कार्मुकाणां च भारत। गदानां परिघाणां च हस्तानां चोरुभिः सह॥ पादानां भूषणानां च केयूराणां च संघशः। राशयस्तत्र दृश्यन्ते भीष्मभीमसमागमे।॥
en: In that fight between Bhima and Bhishma, heaps of arms, heads, bows maces, legs and ornaments and bracelets were seen rising over the field.

sn: अश्वानां कुञ्जराणां च रथानां चानिवर्तिनाम्। संघाताः स्म प्रदृश्यन्ते तत्र तत्र विशाम्पते॥
en: There was also seen here and there o ruler of men, large number of running steeds and retreating elephants.

sn: गदाभिरसिभिः प्रासैर्बाणैश्च नतपर्वभिः। जघ्नुः परस्परं तत्र क्षत्रियाः काल आगते॥
en: The Kshatriya, urged on by Destiny, began to slay one another in that battle, with maces, swerds, lances and straight-jointed shafts.

sn: अपर गहुभिर्वीरा नियुद्धकुशला युधि। बहुधा सम ज्जन्त आयसैः परिचैरिव॥
en: Other heroes accomplished in battle struck one another in that battle with their bare arms, that resembled bludgeons made wholly of iron.

sn: मुष्टिभिर्जानुभिश्चैव तलैश्चैव विशाम्पते। अन्योन्यं जजिरे वीरास्तावकाः पाण्डवैः सह॥
en: O king, other heroic warriors of your army fought on with those of the Pandava host, and slew one another by striking one another with clenched fists, knees, palms and blows.

sn: पतितैः पात्यमानैश्च विचेष्टद्भिश्च भूतले। घोरमायोधनं जज्ञे तत्र तत्र जनेश्वर॥
en: With the fallen, the falling, and with those rolling on the grounds in agony the battle, O lord of men, became indeed very dreadful.

sn: विरथा रथिनश्चात्र निस्त्रिंशवरधारिणः। अन्योन्यमभिधावन्तः परस्यरवधैषिणः॥
en: Car-warriors deprived of their grasping well tempered swords rushed at one another desirous of slaying one another.

sn: ततो दुर्योधनो राजा कलिङ्गैर्बहुभिर्वृतः। पुरस्कृत्य रणे भीष्मं पाण्डवानभ्यवर्तत॥
en: Thereupon king Duryodhana surrounded by a large number of the Kalingas and placing Bhishma at the head, charged the Pandava host.

sn: तथैव पाण्डवाः सर्वे परिवार्य वृकोदरम्। भीष्ममभ्यद्रवन् क्रुद्धास्ततो युद्धमवर्तत॥
en: So also, the Pandavas, surrounding Vrikodara and riding on fleet animals in that battle, rushed inflamed with wrath against the division led by Bhishma. cars,

sn: संजय उवाच दृष्ट्वा भीष्मेण संसक्तान् भ्रातृनन्यांश्च पार्थिवान्। समभ्यधावद् गाङ्गेयमुद्यतास्त्रो धनंजयः॥
en: Sanjaya said Seeing his brother (Bhima) and other kings (of the Pandava host) engaged with Bhishma with weapons uplifted, Dhananjaya rushed against the son of Ganga.

sn: पाञ्चजन्यस्य निर्घोषं धनुषो गाण्डिवस्य च। ध्वजं च दृष्ट्वा पार्थस्य सर्वान् नो भयमाविशत्॥
en: Hearing the blare of the conch Panchajanya, and the twang of the bow Gandiva, and seeing the standard of the son of Pritha (Arjuna), every one of us was seized with terror.

sn: सिंहलाङ्ग्लमाकाशे ज्वलन्तमिव पर्वतम्। असज्जमानं वृक्षेषु धूमकेतुमिवोत्थितम्॥ बहुवर्णं विचित्रं च दिव्यं वानरलक्षणम्। अपश्याम महाराज ध्वजं गाण्डीवधन्वनः॥
en: O mighty monarch, we then beheld the standard of that wielder of the Gandiva bow, standard that resembled a lion's tail in shape and looked like a blazing mountain in the air; that could not be obstructed by the trees; that appeared like the risen comet; and that was of diverse hue and variegated and of celestial make and bore the device of the monkey.

sn: विद्युतं मेघमध्यस्थां भ्राजमानामिवाम्बरे। ददृशुर्गाण्डिवं योधा रुक्मपृष्ठं महामृधे॥
en: In that terrible encounter, the warriors saw Arjuna's gold mounted Gandiva appear beautiful like flashes of lightning illumining a mass of clouds in the welkin.

sn: अशुश्रुम भृशं चास्य शक्रस्येवाभिगर्जतः। सुघोरं तलयोः शब्दं निघ्नतस्तव वाहिनीम्॥
en: While he was slaying the warriors of your army, we heard shouts that resembled those of Indra himself, uttered by Arjuna, as also the dreadful sounds he produced by striking his palms against his arms.

sn: चण्डवातो यथा मेघः सविद्युत्स्तनयित्नुमान्। दिशः सम्लावयन् सर्वाः शरवर्षैः समन्ततः॥
en: Arjuna poured in for rents his arrow showers in all the directions of the compass like a rain cloud surcharged with lightning and thunder and assisted by violent tempest pouring rain.

sn: समभ्यधावद् गाङ्गेयं भैरवास्त्रो धनंजयः। दिशं प्राची प्रतीची च न जानीमोऽस्त्रमोहिताः॥
en: Then Dhananjaya, possessed of dreadful weapons rushed against the son of Ganga. Confounded with his weapons we then were unable to distinguish between the east and the west.

sn: कांदिग्भूताः श्रान्तपत्रा हताश्वा हतचेतसः। अन्योन्यमभिसंश्लिष्य योधास्ते भरतर्षभ॥
en: Then O foremost of the Bharata, your warriors, not knowing which point of the compass they were in, with their animals exhausted, steeds slain and hearts confounded, and huddling close to one another.

sn: भीष्ममेवाभ्यलीयन्त सह सर्वैस्तवात्मजैः। तेषामार्तायनमभूद् भीष्मः शान्तनवो रणे॥
en: Threw themselves upon the protection of Bhishma, along of with your sons. In that battle Bhishma the son of Shantanu became their refuge.

sn: समुत्पतन्ति वित्रस्ता रथेभ्यो रथिनस्तथा। सादिनश्चाश्वपृष्ठेभ्यो भूमौ चापि पदातयः॥
en: Seized with panic, car warriors jumped down from their cars and cavalry soldiers from the back of their steeds and foot soldiers fell down even on the grounds where they stood.

sn: श्रुत्वा गाण्डीवनिर्घोषं विस्फूर्जितमिवाशनेः। सर्वसैन्यानि भीतानि व्यवालीयन्त भारत॥
en: Hearing the twang of the bow Gandiva, that resembled the rumble of thunder, O Bharata, all your warriors were struck with terror and began to fall off their ranks.

sn: अथ काम्बोजजैरश्वैर्महद्भिः शीघ्रगामिभिः। गोपानां बहुसाहस्रैर्बलैर्गोपायनैर्वृतः॥
en: Then with fleet and mettled chargers of the Kamboja breed, and surrounded by many thousand Gopas and an army of the Gopayanas,

sn: मद्रसौवीरगान्धारैस्त्रैगर्तेश्च विशाम्पते। सर्वकालिङ्गमुख्यैश्च कलिङ्गाधिपतिर्वृतः॥ नानानरगणौघैश्च दुःशासनपुरःसरः। जयद्रथश्च नृपतिः सहितः सर्वराजभिः॥
en: And O ruler of men, supported, by the Madras, the Souviras, the Gandharvas the Trigartas, and the foremost of all Kalinga warriors, the king of the Kalingas, and king Jayadratha accompanied by many kings and followed by a numerous force consisting of various races headed by Dushasana himself.

sn: हयारोहवराश्चैव तव पुत्रेण चोदिताः। चतुर्दश सहस्राणि सौबलं पर्यवारयन्॥
en: And supported by fourteen thousand picked cavalry soldiers urged by your son, encompassed on all sides the king of the Subala's.

sn: ततस्ते सहिताः सर्वे विभक्तरथवाहनाः। अर्जुनं समरे जघ्नुस्तावका भरतर्षभ॥
en: Then in that battle, united together and riding on their respective vehicles, those foremost of Bharata's race, namely the sons of Pandu, began to slaughter the warriors of your army.

sn: रथिभिर्वारणैरश्वैः पादातैश्च समीरितम्। घोरमायोधनं चक्रे महाभ्रसदृशं रजः॥
en: A thick clouds of dust, raised by carwarriors, elephants, steeds and foot soldiers, made the battle that raged all the more terrible.

sn: तोमरप्रासनाराचगजाश्वरथयोधिनाम्। बलेन महता भीष्मः समसज्जत् किरीटिना॥
en: Bhishma then, supported by a mighty force consisting of elephants-warriors, car-warriors and cavalry-soldiers, all armed with Tomaras, Narachas and Prasas fell to fight with the diadem decked Arjuna.

sn: आवन्त्यः काशिराजेन भीमसेनेन सैन्धवः। अजातशत्रुर्मद्राणामृषभेण यशस्विना॥ सहपुत्रः सहामात्यः शल्येन समसज्जत। विकर्णः सहदेवेन चित्रसेनः शिखण्डिना॥
en: The ruler of Avanti encountered the king of the Kashis. Bhimasena engaged the ruler of the Sindhus; and Ajatashatru (Yudhishthira) with his sons and his counsellors, engaged with the renowned Shalya the foremost of the Madras. Vikarna became engaged with Sahadeva, and Chitrasena with Shikhandin.

sn: मत्स्या दुर्योधनं जग्मुःशकुनिं च विशाम्पते। द्रुपदश्चैकितानश्च सात्यकिश्च महारथः॥ द्रोणेन समसज्जन्त सपुत्रेण महात्मना। कृपश्च कृतवर्मा च धृष्टद्युम्नमभिद्रुतौ।२३।।
en: The Matsyas, O ruler of men encountered Duryodhana along with Shakuni. Drupada, Chekitana and the mighty car-warrior Satyaki. Engaged with the illustrious Drona, supported by his son. Kripa and Kritavarma both charged Dhrishtadyumna.

sn: एवं प्रव्रजिताश्वानि भ्रान्तनागरथानि च। सैन्यानि समसज्जन्त प्रयुद्धानि समन्ततः॥ निरभ्रे विद्युतस्तीवा दिशश्च रजसाऽऽवृताः। प्रादुरासन् महोल्काश्च सनिर्घाता विशाम्पते।॥
en: Thus, running steeds and wheeling and whirling cars and elephants, in that battle, engaged with one another, all over the field. Flashes of lightning illumined the welkin although there was no cloud, and the points of the compass were shrouded in thick clouds of dust; and O ruler of men, large meteors were scen falling with terrible sounds.

sn: प्रादुर्भूतो महावातः पांसुवर्षे पपात च। नभस्यन्तर्दधे सूर्यः सैन्येन रजसाऽऽवृतः॥
en: A mighty tempest, raged and a shower of dust began to fall. The sun disappeared in the firmament being shrouded by the dust-clouds raised by the troops.

sn: प्रमोहः सर्वसत्त्वानामतीव समपद्यत। रजसा चाभिभूतानामस्त्रजालैश्च तुद्यताम्॥
en: All the warriors, overwhelmed with that dust and fighting with their various weapons, were greatly confounded.

sn: वीरबाहुविसृष्टानां सर्वावरणभेदिनाम्। संघात: शरजालानां तुमुल: समपद्यत॥
en: The whizzing noise produced by the arrows capable of piercing through every armour and discharged by the arms of heroes, was discharged by the arms of heroes, was indeed deafening.

sn: प्रकाशं चक्रुराकाशमुद्यतानि भुजोत्तमैः। नक्षत्रविमलाभानि शस्त्राणि भरतर्षभ॥
en: O foremost of the Bharatas, weapons endued with the pure effulgence of the stars, illumined the firmament when they were shot by excellent arms.

sn: आर्षभाणि विचित्राणि रुक्मजालावृतानि च। सम्पेतुर्दिक्षु सर्वासु चर्माणि भरतर्षभ॥
en: In all directions were scattered, 0 foremost of the Bharatas, bucklers made of bull's hide, of variegated appearance, and covered with a net work of gold.

sn: सूर्यवर्णैश्च निस्त्रिशैः पात्यमानानि सर्वशः। दिक्षु सर्वास्वदृश्यन्त शरीराणि शिरांसि च॥
en: In all directions were seen heads and limbs falling, being cut off with swords of the effulgence of the sun.

sn: भग्नचक्राक्षनीडाश्च निपातितमहाध्वजाः। हताश्वाः पृथिवी जग्मुस्तत्र तत्र महारथाः॥ परिपेतुर्हयाश्चात्र केचिच्छस्त्रकृतव्रणाः। रथान् विपरिकर्षन्तो हतेषु रथयोधिषु॥
en: Mighty car-warriors, having the wheel, the axle and the terraces of their cars broken, fell down on the grounds, with their steeds slain and their long arms severed. Steeds fell down on the battle-field mangled with the cut of weapons, and car wheeled around deprived of their warriors.

sn: शराहता भिन्नदेहा बद्धयोक्त्रा हयोत्तमाः। युगानि पर्यकर्षन्त तत्र तत्र स्म भारत॥ अदृश्यन्त ससूताश्च साश्वाः सरथयोधिनः। एकेन बलिना राजन् वारणेन विमर्दिताः॥
en: O Bharata, wounded with arrows with their bodies mangled, and their harnesses on, excellent steeds ran there dragging the caryokes after them. Many warriors, O king, with their cars, horses and drivers were seen slain in that battle by a single elephants possessed of great strength.

sn: गन्धहस्तिमदस्रावमाघ्राय बहवो रणे। संनिपाते बलौघानां वीतमाददिरे गजाः॥ सतोमरैर्महामात्रैर्निपतद्भिर्गतासुभिः। बभूवायोधनं छन्नं नाराचाभिहतैर्गजैः॥ संनिपाते बलौघानां प्रेषितैर्वरवारणैः। निपेतुर्यधि सम्भग्नाः सयोधाः सध्वजा गजाः॥
en: In that battle scenting the odour of the temporal juice shed by other compeers many elephants began to snuff the air in the very midst of that slaughter of troops. The field of battle was covered with elephants bearing wooden edifices and guides, as they fell down deprived of live being struck with piked lances. In the midst of large forces, many elephants with the standards and warriors on their back, fell down on the ground being crushed by other huge compeers urged on their guides.

sn: नागराजोपमैर्हस्तै गैराक्षिप्य संयुगे। व्यदृश्यन्त महाराज सम्भग्ना रथकूबराः॥ विशीर्णरथसंघाश्च केशेश्वाक्षिप्य दन्तिभिः। द्रुमशाखा इवाविध्य निष्पिष्टा रथिनो रणे॥
en: In that battle, o king, were seen many chariot-shafts to be broken by elephants using their trunks that resembled the body of the serpent chief. In that battle car-warriors, the yokes of whose cars had been shattered, were seized by the hair by the tuskers and dragged down like branches of trees they were thoroughly crushed.

sn: रथेषु च रथान् युद्धे संसक्तान् वरवारणाः। विकर्षन्तो दिशः सर्वाः सम्पेतुः सर्वशब्दगाः॥ तेषां तथा कर्षतां तु गजानां रूपमावभौ। सरःसु नलिनीजालं विषक्तमिव कर्षताम्॥
en: Other prodigious elephants dragging cars entangled with other cars, ran in all directions uttering loud roars. The appearance of those elephants dragging those chariots looked beautiful like that of others of their species tearing lotus-stems growing in the lakes.

sn: एवं संछादितं तत्र बभूवायोधनं महत्। सादिभिश्च पदातैश्च सध्वजैश्च महारथैः॥
en: Thus then the extensive field of battle was strewn over with cavalry-soldiers, and mighty car-warriors and their tall standards.

sn: संजय उवाच शिखण्डी सह मत्स्येन विराटेन विशाम्पते। भीष्ममाशु महेष्वासमाससाद सुदुर्जयम्॥ द्रोणं कृपं विकर्णं च महेष्वासं महाबलम्। राज्ञश्चान्यान् रणे शूरान् बहूना द् धनंजयः॥
en: Sanjaya said O ruler of men, Shikhandin, with the king of the Matsyas viz., Virata, speedily rushed against Bhishma, that mighty bowman difficult of being defeated in battle. Dhananjaya in that battle rushed against Drona, Kripa, Vikarna, and many kings, all mighty-bowmen, brave,, and endued with great prowess.

sn: सैन्धवं च महेष्वासं सामात्यं सह बन्धुभिः। प्राच्यांश्च दाक्षिणात्यांश्च भूमिपान् भूमिपर्षभ॥ पुत्रं च ते महेष्वासं दुर्योधनममर्षणम्। दुःसहं चैव समरे भीमसेनोऽभ्यवर्तत॥
en: As also, against that great warrior the ruler of the Sindhus supported by his friends and ministers, and, O foremost of the Bharatas, against many other kings from the West and the South. Bhimasena, in that fight, rushed against your vindictive son Duryodhana that mighty bow-men, as also against his brother Dushasana.

sn: सहदेवस्तु शकुनिमुलूकं च महारथम्। पितापुत्रौ महेष्वासावभ्यवर्तत दुर्जयौ॥
en: Sahadeva rushed against the two mighty car-warriors, both skillful bowmen and invincible in battle, namely, Shakuni and Uluka who were father and son.

sn: युधिष्ठिरो महाराज गजानीकं महारथः। समवर्तत संग्रामे पुत्रेण निकृतस्तव॥
en: That mighty car-warriors, O great monarch, namely Yudhishthira, who had been shamefully deceived by yours son, proceeded in that battle against the elephants division of the Kurus. son

sn: माद्रीपुत्रस्तु नकुलः शूरसंक्रन्दनो युधि। त्रिगर्तानां बलैः सार्धं समसज्जत पाण्डवः॥
en: That brave son of Pandu by Madri namely Nakula, who was capable of wringing tears from the foe, encountered in battle that excellent division of car warriors consisting of the Trigartas.

sn: अभ्यवर्तन्त संक्रुद्धाः समरे शाल्वकेकयान्। सात्यकिश्शेकितानश्च सौभद्रश्च महारथः॥
en: Satyaki, Chekitana, and the of Subhadra endued with great prowess, all invincible in battle, rushed against the Shalyas and the Kaikeyas.

sn: धृष्टकेतुश्च समरे राक्षसश्च घटोत्कचः। (नाकुलिश्च शतानीकः समरे रथपुङ्गवः।) पुत्राणां ते रथानीकं प्रत्युद्याताः सुदुर्जयाः॥
en: The Rakshasa Ghatotkacha, and Dhrishtaketu, both incapable of being conquered, charged in that battle the car division of your sons.

sn: सेनापतिरमेयात्मा धृष्टद्युम्नो महाबलः। द्रोणेन समरे राजन् समियायोचकर्मणा॥
en: Then, O king the mighty car-warriors, that generalissimo Dhrishtadyumna of immeasurable soul, engaged with Drona of fierce achievements.

sn: एवमेते महेष्वासास्तावकाः पाण्डवैः सह। समेत्य समरे शूरः सम्प्रहारं प्रचक्रिरे॥
en: Thus the warriors of your army, all heroic and mighty bow-men, encountering the Pandavas in the battle, began to smite one another down.

sn: मध्यंदिनगते सूर्ये नभस्याकुलतां गते। कुरवः पाण्डवेयाश्च निजघ्नुरितरेतरम्॥ ध्वजिनो हेमचित्राङ्गा विचरन्तो रणाजिरे। सपताका रथा रेजुर्वैयाघ्रपरिवारणाः॥
en: When the sun reached the meridian and when the sky burned with his fiery rays, the Kurus and the Pandava began to kill one another. Then chariots, mounted with flagstaffs from the tops of which pennons were fluttering, and variegated with gold and covered with tiger-skins, appeared beautiful as they drove through the scene of battle.

sn: समेतानां च समरे जिगीषूणां परस्परम्। बभूव तुमुलः शब्दः सिंहानामिव नर्दताम्॥
en: A dreadful din was created by those warriors as they engaged in the fight out of a desire for conquering one another, and as they roared like roaring lions themselves.

sn: तत्राद्भुतमपश्याम सम्प्रहारं सुदारुणम्। यदकुर्वन् रणे शूराः संजयाः कुरुभिः सह॥
en: The strokes that the heroic Srinjayas and the Kurus dealt to one another in that conflict and that were terrible and wonderful, were also seen by us.

sn: नैव खं न दिशो राजन् न सूर्यं शत्रुतापन। विदिशो वाऽपि पश्यामः शरैर्मुक्तैः समन्ततः॥
en: Neither, O monarch, O afflicter of your enemies, were we able to see the firmament, the sun or the cardinal and subsidiary quarters, in consequence of their being shrouded on all sides by a thick discharge of arrows.

sn: शक्तीनां विमलाचाणां तोमराणां तथाऽस्यताम्। निस्त्रिंशानां च पीतानां नीलोत्पलनिभाः प्रभाः॥ कवचानां विचित्राणां भूषणानां प्रभास्तथा। खं दिशः प्रदिशश्चैव भासयामासुरोजसा॥
en: The effulgence, like that of blue lotuses, of Shaktis with shinning heads, of hurled lances, of well-tempered swords. As also effulgence of the coats of mail and of diverse and wonderful ornaments, filled the firmament and the cardinal and subsidiary quarters with its flashes.

sn: वपुर्भिश्च नरेन्द्राणां चन्द्रसूर्यसमप्रभैः। विरराज तदा राजंस्तत्र तत्र रणाङ्गणम्॥
en: Then, O monarch, here and there, the field of battle appeared beautiful being strewn over with the bodies of monarchs which were effulgent like the sun or the moon.

sn: रथसङ्घा नरव्याघ्राः समायान्तश्च संयुगे। विरेजुः समरे राजन् ग्रहा इव नभस्तले॥
en: Excellent car-warriors, all foremost of men, encountering one another in battle appear beautiful, O king, like the planets in the heavens.

sn: भीष्मस्तु रथिनां श्रेष्ठो भीमसेन महाबलम्। अवारयत संक्रुद्धः सर्वसैन्यस्य पश्यतः॥
en: Then that foremost of car warriors namely Bhishma, waxing worth opposed Bhimasena of great prowess even before the very eyes of the assembled troops.

sn: ततो भीष्मविनिर्मुक्तारुक्मपुङ्खाः शिलाशिताः। अभ्यघ्नन् समरे भीमं तैलधौताः सुतेजनाः॥
en: Then shafts furnished with golden wings whetted on stone smeared with oil and charged with impetus wounded Bhima in that battle, being shot by Bhishma himself.

sn: तस्य शक्तिं महावेगां भीमसेनो महाबलः। क्रुद्धाशीविषसंकाशां प्रेषयामास भारत॥
en: Thereat the mighty Bhimasena hurled at Bhishma, O Bharata his lance charged with fierce momentum and resembling an enraged snake.

sn: तामापतन्ती सहसा रुक्मदण्डां दुरासदाम्। चिच्छेद समरे भीष्मः शरैः संनतपर्वभिः॥
en: But in that combat Bhishma cut off with his straight arrows that lances furnished with a golden staff as it coursed swiftly towards himself.

sn: ततोऽपरेण भल्लेन पीतेन निशितेन च। कार्मुकं भीमसेनस्य द्विधा चिच्छेद भारत॥
en: Thereafter, O Bharata, with a whetted and well tempered Bhalla Bhishma cut in twin the bow of Bhimasena.

sn: सात्यकिस्तु ततस्तूर्णं भीष्ममासाद्य संयुगे। आकर्णप्रहितैस्तीक्ष्णैनिशितैस्तिग्मतेजनैः।। :॥ शरैर्बहुभिरानछेत् पितरं ते जनेश्वर। ततः संधाय वै तीक्ष्णं शरं परमदारुणम्॥
en: Thereupon, speedily rushing at Bhishma, Satyaki in that encounter, with numerous keen pointed and sharp edged shafts discharged with a bow-string drawn back to the ear, pierced, O ruler of men your own father. Thereat aiming a sharp and very dreadful arrow.

sn: वार्ष्णेयस्य रथाद् भीष्मः पातयामास सारथिम्। तस्याश्वाः प्रद्रुता राजन् निहते रथसारथौ।॥ तेन तेनैव धावन्ति मनोमारुतरंहसः। ततः सर्वस्य सैन्यस्य निस्वनस्तुमुलोऽभवत्॥
en: Bhishma felled the charioteer of that Vrishni hero from his seat on the box of. chariot. Upon the death of the driver the steeds, O king, of that warrior, beheld away. Those steeds wildly careered over the filed of battle endued as they were with the fleetness of the mind or the wind. Thereupon a loud uproar was sent up by all the troops.

sn: हाहाकारश्च संजज्ञे पाण्डवानां महात्मनाम्। अभ्यद्रवत गृह्णीत हयान् यच्छत धावत।॥
en: Exclamations of Oh! and Alas! were uttered by the warriors of the Pandava army. Run, Seize, Hold the steeds, Go in haste,

sn: इत्यासीत् तुमुलः शब्दो युयुधानरथं प्रति। एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु भीष्मः शान्तनवस्तदा॥
en: Such cries followed the chariot of Yudhishthira. During this interval, Bhishma the son of Shantanu.

sn: न्यहनत् पाण्डवीं सेनामासुरीमिव वृत्रहा। ते वध्यमाना भीष्मेण पञ्चाला: सोमकैः : सह॥
en: Began to slay the troops of the Pandavas, like the slayer of Vritra himself slaying the hosts of the Danavas. Thus slaughtered by Bhishma, the Panchalas supported by the Somakas.

sn: स्थिरां युद्धे मतिं कृत्वा भीष्ममेवाभिदुद्रुवुः। धृष्टद्युम्नमुखाश्चापि पार्थाः शान्तनवं रणे॥ अभ्यधावञ्जिगीषन्तस्तव पुत्रस्य वाहिनीम्।
en: Setting their hearts fixed on battle, rushed against Bhishma, Other warriors of the host of the sons of Pritha headed by Dhrishtadyumna himself rushed in battle against the son of Shantanu, inflamed with desire for slaughtering the army of your son. a

sn: तथैव कौरवा राजन् भीष्मद्रोणपुरोगमाः॥ अभ्यधावन्त वेगेन ततो युद्धमवर्तत॥
en: So also, O king, the warriors of your army headed by Bhishma and Drona, rushed with impetuosity against the enemy. Thereupon these raged a second battle.

sn: संजय उवाच विराटोऽथ त्रिभिर्बाणैर्भीष्ममार्छन्महारथम्। विव्याध तुरगांश्चास्य त्रिभिर्बाणैर्महारथः॥
en: Sanjaya said Then the mighty car-warrior Virata pierced with three arrows the mighty car-warrior Bhishma, and the latter's steeds with another three arrows.

sn: तं प्रत्यविध्यद् दशभिर्भीष्मः शान्तनवः शरैः। रुक्मपुजैर्महेष्वासः कृतहस्तो महाबलः॥
en: Thereat Bhishma the son of Shantanu, that mighty bow-man endued with great strength and lightness of hands, pierced him in return with ten shafts furnished with wings of gold.

sn: द्रौणिर्गाण्डीवधन्वानं भीमधन्वा महारथः। अविध्यदिषुभिः षड्भिर्दृढहस्तः स्तनान्तरे॥
en: Then that fierce bow-man and mighty carwarrior of firm hands, namely, the son of Drona pierced with six shafts the wielder of the Gandiva bow between his breasts.

sn: कार्मुकं तस्य चिच्छेद फाल्गुनः परवीरहा। अविध्यच्च भृशं तीक्ष्णैः पत्रिभिः शत्रुकर्शनः॥
en: Thereat the slayer of his foes, that humiliator of his antagonists, namely, Phalguna (Arjuna), cut down the bow of Drona's son and pierced him sore in return with five sharp arrows.

sn: सोऽन्यत् कार्मुकमादाय वेगवान् क्रोधमूर्च्छितः। अमृष्यमाणः पार्थेन कार्मुकच्छेदमाहवे॥
en: Then the latter, endued with great impetuosity, overwhelmed with fury, not broO king the severing of his bow by Partha (Arjuna) in the battle, grasped another bow,

sn: अविध्यत् फाल्गुनं राजन् नवत्या निशितैः शरैः। वासुदेवं च सप्तत्या विव्याध परमेषुभिः॥ ततः क्रोधाभिताम्राक्षः कृष्णेन सह फाल्गुनः। दीर्घमुष्णं च नि:श्वस्य चिन्तयित्वा पुनः पुनः॥
en: And, o king, pierced Phalguna (Arjuna) with ninety keen-pointed shafts then with seventy excellent arrows he pierced the son of Vasudeva. Thereupon with eyes coppery in rage, Phalguna with Krishna breathing long and hot and reflecting again and again,

sn: धनुः प्रपीड्य वामन करेणामित्रकर्शनः। गाण्डीवधन्वा संक्रुद्धः शितान् संनतपर्वणः॥ जीवितान्तकरान् घोरान् समादत्त शिलीमुखान्। तैस्तूर्णं समरेऽविध्यद् द्रौणि बलवतां वरः॥
en: And also that grinder of foes that foremost of mighty heroes pressing his bow with his left arm, and excited with rage, and wielding the Gandiva bow, placed on the bow-string sharp and straight and fierce shafts capable of depriving a foe of his life; and therewith, in that battle, speedily pierced the son of Drona.

sn: तस्य ते कवचं भित्त्वा पपुः शोणितमाहवे। न विव्यथे च निर्भिन्नो द्रोणिर्गाण्डीवधन्वना॥ तथैव च शरान् द्रौणिः प्रविमुञ्चन्नविह्वलः। तस्थौ स समरे राजंस्त्रातुमिच्छन् महाव्रतम्॥
en: Those shafts, in that battle, penetrating through the armour of the son of Drona drank his life-blood. But thus pierced by the wielder of the Gandiva-bow Drona's son did not flinch. Discharging similar arrows at the son of Pritha, O king, he stood unwavering in battle, desirous of protecting Bhishma of illustrious vows.

sn: तस्य तत् सुमहत् कर्म शशंसुः कुरुसत्तमाः। यत् कृष्णाभ्यां समेताभ्यामभ्यापतत संयुगे॥ स हि नित्यमनीकेषु युध्यतेऽभयमास्थितः। अस्त्रग्रामं ससंहारं द्रोणात् प्राप्य सुदुर्लभम्॥
en: That great feat of his which consisted in his encountering the two Krishna's together in battle, was greatly applauded by the foremost among the Kurus. Having obtained from Drona various rare weapons together with the method of their withdrawal, he every day undauntedly fought amidst that host.

sn: ममैष आचार्यसुतो द्रोणस्यापि प्रियः सुतः। ब्राह्मणश्च विशेषेण माननीयो ममेति च॥
en: This is the son of my preceptor; this is the very dear son of Drona; especially he is a Brahmana, and so worthy of my veneration.

sn: समास्थाय मतिं वीरो बीभत्सुः शत्रुतापनः। कृपां चक्रे रथश्रेष्ठो भारद्वाजसुतं प्रति॥
en: Thinking thus, that grinder of enemies the brave Bibhatsu (Arjuna) that foremost of carwarriors, showed mercy towards Bharadvaja's son.

sn: द्रौणिं त्यक्त्वा ततौ युद्धे कौन्तेयः श्वेतवाहनः। युयुधे तावकान् निदर्नस्त्वरमाणः पराक्रमीः॥
en: Thereafter in that encounter leaving alone the son of Drona, Kunti's son (Arjuna) borne by white chargers, endued with great prowess, fought on displaying great lightness of hands and spreading slaughter in the ranks of the enemy.

sn: दुर्योधनस्तु दशभिर्गार्धपत्रैः शिलाशितैः। भीमसेनं महेष्वासं रुक्मपुङ्खः समार्पयत्॥
en: Duryodhana pierced the mighty bow-man Bhimasena with ten shafts furnished with vulture-feathers and whetted on stone and decked with gold.

sn: भीमसेनः सुसंक्रुद्धः परासुकरणं दृढम्। चित्रं कार्मुकमादत्त शरांश्च निशितान् दश॥
en: Excited with wrath, Bhimasena grasped a variegated bow of tough make, capable of depriving the foe of his life, as also ten sharp arrows.

sn: आकर्णप्रहितैस्तीक्ष्णैर्वेगवद्भिरजिह्मगैः। अविध्यत् तूर्णमव्यग्रः कुरुराज महोरसि॥
en: Thereafter taking a steady aim with those keen-pointed shafts charged with great energy and fierce impetus, and drawing the bow-string back to his ears, Bhimasena struck home the ruler of the Kurus on his board chest.

sn: तस्य काञ्चनसूत्रस्थः शरैः संछादितो मणिः। रराजोरसि खे सूर्यो ग्रहैरवि समावृतः॥ पुत्रस्तु तव तेजस्वी भीमसेनेन पाडितः। नामृष्यत यथा नागस्तलशब्दं मदोत्कटः॥
en: Thereupon the gem that was hanging in the breast of Duryodhana by golden threads, being surrounded by those arrows appeared charming like the sun in the heavens surrounded by the planets. But your son endued with great energy, thus pierced by Bhimasena, did not brook it cooly, like a snake not bearing the sound of the tread of man.

sn: ततः शरैर्महाराज रुक्मपुजैः शिलाशितैः। भीमं विव्याध संक्रुद्धस्त्रासयानो वरूथिनीम्॥
en: Thereafter inflamed with rage, O king, he pierced Bhima with numerous shafts furnished with golden wings and whetted on stone, with a view to protect his own soldiers.

sn: तौ युध्यमानौ समरे भृशमन्योन्यविक्षतौ। पुत्रौ ते देवसंकाशौ व्यरोचेतां महाबलौ॥
en: Thus fighting with each other and mangling each other (with shafts) in that battle, those two sons of yours, both endued with great prowess appeared beautiful like two gods.

sn: चित्रसेनं नरव्याघ्रं सौभद्रः परवीरहा। अविध्यद् दशभिर्बाणैः पुरुमित्रं च सप्तभिः॥
en: Then that foremost of men, that slayer of hostile heroes namely the son of Subhadra pierced Chitrasena with innumerable short arrows and also Purumitra with seven shafts.

sn: सत्यव्रतं च सप्तत्या विद्ध्वा शक्रसमो युधि। नृत्यन्निव रणे वीर आर्तिं नः समजीजनत्॥
en: And that heroic one equal to Shakra himself in battle, piercing Satyavrata with seventy shafts, seemed to dance about on the field causing us much pain,

sn: तं प्रत्यविध्यद् दशभिश्चित्रसेन: शिलीमुखैः। सत्यव्रतश्च नवभिः पुरुमित्रश्च सप्तभिः॥ स विद्धो विक्षरन् रक्तं शत्रुसंवारणं महत्। चिच्छेद चित्रसेनस्य चित्रं कार्मुकमार्जुनिः॥
en: Chitrasena pierced him in return with ten shafts, Satyavrata with nine, and Purumitra with seven. Thus pierced the son of Arjuna while still shedding blood, severed the beautiful and mighty bow of Chitrasena that was capable to holding the foe at bay.

sn: भित्त्वा चास्य तनुत्राणं शरैणोरस्यताडयत्। ततस्ते तावका वीरा राजपुत्रा महारथाः॥
en: Penetrating his coat of mail, Arjuna's son, pierced him with a shaft on the breast. Thereat the heroic princes of your army all mighty carwarriors.

sn: समेत्य युधि संरब्धा विव्यधुनिशितैः शरैः। तांश्च सर्वाशरैस्तीक्ष्णैर्जघान परमास्त्रवित्॥
en: Uniting together, and inflamed with rage, pierced Arjuna's son with numerous keen pointed arrows. But the latter, conversant with excellent weapons, wounded all of them with sharp arrows.

sn: तस्य दृष्ट्वा तु तत् कर्म परिवठ्ठः सुतास्तव। दहन्तं समरे सैन्यं वने कक्षं यथोल्बणम्॥
en: Beholding that feat of his, your sons in that battle surrounded him on all sides, who was consuming the warriors of your army.

sn: अपेतशिशिरे काले समिद्धमिव पावकम्। अत्यरोचत सौभद्रस्तव सैन्यानि नाशयन्॥
en: Like a blazing fire consuming a heap of fuel in the summer season. Thus smiting down your soldiers the son of Subhadra appeared highly beautiful.

sn: तत् तस्य चरितं दृष्ट्वा पौत्रस्तव विशाम्पते। लक्ष्मणोऽभ्यपतत् तूर्णं सात्वतीपुत्रमाहवे॥
en: Beholding those feats of Abhimanyu the son of Subhadra, O king, your grandson Lakshmana speedily faced him desirous of battle.

sn: अभिमन्युस्तु संक्रुद्धो लक्ष्मणं शुभलक्षणम्। विव्याध निशितैः षड्भिः सारथिं च त्रिभिः शरैः।।३३।
en: Thereupon waxing worth Abhimanyu that mighty car-warrior pierced Lakshmana of auspicious marks and his charioteer, with six well sharpened arrows.

sn: तथैव लक्ष्मणो राजन् सौभद्रं निशितैः शरैः। अविध्यत महाराज तदद्भुतमिवाभवत्॥
en: So also, O king, Lakshmana pierced the son of Subhadra with sharp arrows; and O mighty sovereign, the feat seemed to be marvelous.

sn: तस्याश्वांश्चतुरो हत्वा सारथिं च महाबलः। अभ्यद्रवत सौभद्रो लक्ष्मणं निशितैः शरैः॥
en: Thereat that mighty car-warrior the son of the Subhadra, slaying the four steeds of Lakshmana, as also his charioteer, rushed at him covering him with sharp shafts.

sn: हताश्वे तु रथे तिष्ठंल्लक्ष्मणः परवीरहा। शक्तिं चिक्षेप संक्रुद्धः सौभद्रस्य रथं प्रति॥
en: Then standing on his chariot of which the steeds were slain, Lakshmana the slayer of inimical heroes, excited with the wrath, hurled a lance aiming at the car of Subhadra's son,

sn: तामापतन्ती सहसा घोररूपां दुरासदाम्। अभिमन्युः शरैस्तीक्ष्णैश्चिच्छेद भुजगोपमाम्॥
en: The Abhimanyu, cut down with his keen pointed arrows, that dreadful and irresistible lances that resembled a snake and that was coursing swiftly toward himself.

sn: ततः स्वरथमारोप्य लक्ष्मणं गौतमस्तदा। अपोवाह रथेनाजौ सर्वसैन्यस्य पश्यतः॥
en: Thereupon Gautama (Kripa) taking Lakshmana upon his chariot carried him away from the field before the very eyes of the troops.

sn: ततः समाकुले तस्मिन् वर्तमाने महाभये। अभ्यद्रवञ्जिघांसन्तः परस्परवधैषिणः॥
