en: Then in that general and dreadful engagement, the fighters rushed, one against another, smiting one another and desirous of depriving one another of his life.

sn: तावकाश्च महेष्वासाः पाण्डवाश्च महारथाः। जुह्वन्तः समरे प्राणान् निजप्नुरितरेतरम्॥
en: The mighty-bowmen of your army and the mighty car-warrior of the Pandava host, all ready to lay down their lives in battle, began to slay one another.

sn: मुक्तकेशा विकवचा विरथाश्छिन्नकार्मुकाः। बाहुभिः समयुध्यन्त संजयाः कुरुभिः सह॥
en: Having disheveled hair, deprived of their armours shorn of their cars, and with their bows served, the Srinjaya fought on with their bare arms.

sn: ततो भीष्मो महाबाहुः पाण्डवानां महात्मनाम्। सेनां जघान संक्रुद्धो दिव्यैरस्त्रैर्महाबलः॥
en: Then the mighty armed Bhishma endued with great strength waxing worth began to slay with weapons of celestial mace, the Pandavas of high-soul.

sn: हतैरश्वैर्गजैस्तत्र नरैरश्चैश्च पातितः। रथिभिः सादिभिश्चैव समास्तीर्यत मेदिनी॥
en: In that battle, the earth was then strewn our with the corpses and falling bodies of carwarriors, cavalry-soldiers, men, and horses and of elephants deprived of their guides.

description: End of the fifth day's fight
sn: संजय उवाच अथ राजन् महाबाहुः सात्यकिर्युद्धदुर्मदः। विकृष्य चापं समरे भारसाहमनुत्तमम्॥ प्रामुञ्चत् पुखसंयुक्ताशरानाशीविषोपमान्। प्रगाढं लघु चित्रं च दर्शयन् हस्तलाघवम्॥
en: Sanjaya said Then O king, the mighty-armed Satyaki, invincible in battle, drawing in that battle, an excellent bow capable of bearing a great strain, Discharged numerous arrows furnished with wings and resembling snakes of virulent venom, displaying at the same time his great and wonderful lightness of hands.

description: End of the fifth day's fight
sn: तस्य विक्षिपतचापं शरानन्यांश्च मुञ्चतः। आददानस्य भूयश्च संदधानस्य चापरान्॥ क्षिपतश्च परांस्तस्य रणे शत्रून् विनिघ्नतः। ददृशे रूपमत्यर्थं मेघस्येव प्रवर्षतः॥
en: While slaying the enemy in that battle so swiftly did he draw his bow take out his arrows (from his quiver), place them on his bowstring, discharge them at the foe, and again take out other arrows and let them off, that he appeared to be highly beautiful like a mass of clouds pouring showers of rain.

description: End of the fifth day's fight
sn: तमुदीर्यन्तमालोक्य राजा दुर्योधनस्ततः। स्थानामयुतं तस्य प्रेषयामास भारत।।५।
en: The king Duryodhana beholding him swell like a raging fire, O Bharata dispatched against him a division consisting of ten thousand cars.

description: End of the fifth day's fight
sn: तांस्तु सर्वान् महेष्वासान् सात्यकिः सत्यविक्रमः। जघान परमेष्वासो दिव्येनास्त्रेण वीर्यवान्।॥
en: Then Satyaki of infallible prowess endued with great strength that mighty bow man slew all those excellent bowmen with weapons of celestial make.

description: End of the fifth day's fight
sn: स कृत्वा दारुणं कर्म प्रगृहीतशरासनः। आससाद ततो वीरो भूरिश्रवसमाहवे॥
en: Having accomplished that fierce feat and grasping his bow, that hero encountered Bhurishravas as in that battle.

description: End of the fifth day's fight
sn: स हि संदृश्य सेनां ते युयुधानेन पातिताम्। अभ्यधावत संक्रुद्धः कुरूणां कीर्तिवर्धनः॥
en: Bhurishravas that enhancer of the glory of the Kurus, seeing that division of his troops felled by Yuyudhana (Satyaki) waiting wroth rushed against Satyaki.

description: End of the fifth day's fight
sn: इन्द्रायुधसवर्णं तु विस्फार्य सुमहद् धनुः। सृष्टवान् वज्रसंकाशाशरानाशीविषोपमान्॥ सहस्रशो महाराज दर्शयन् पाणिलाघवम्। शरांस्तान् मृत्युसंस्पर्शान् सात्यकेश्च पदानुगाः॥ न विषेहुस्तदा राजन् दुद्रुवुस्ते समन्ततः। विहाय सात्यकि राजन् समरे युद्धदुर्मदम्॥
en: Stretching his mighty bow that resembled that of Indra himself (rain-bow) in hue, he, O monarch, discharged thousands of arrows that looked like snakes of virulent poison, that were endued with the energy of the thunderbolt itself displaying in the act his wonderful lightness of hands. Thereupon the followers of Satyaki unable to bear those shafts of fatal touch, O monarch, fled in all directions, abandoning, O king, in battle Satyaki ever invincible in fight.

description: End of the fifth day's fight
sn: तं दृष्ट्वा युयुधानस्य सुता दश महाबलाः। महारथाः सभाख्याताश्चित्रवर्मायुधध्वजाः॥
en: Seeing this, the ten highly powerful sons of Yudhishthira, all mighty car-warriors of great fame, clad in armours of best make possessing various weapons and diverse standards.

description: End of the fifth day's fight
sn: समासाद्य महेष्वासं भूरिश्रवसमाहवे। ऊचुः सर्वे सुसंरब्धा यूपकेतुं महारणे॥
en: Approaching in that fierce conflict that mighty bowmen named Bhurishravas, who bore the device of a sacrificial stake on his standard, thus addressed the latter in wrath in that dreadful fight.

description: End of the fifth day's fight
sn: भो भोः कौरवदायाद सहास्माभिर्महाबल। एहि युध्यस्व संग्रामे समस्तैः पृथगेव वा॥
en: "O kinsman of the Kauravas, O mighty one, come give us battle; fight with us either jointly or separately.

description: End of the fifth day's fight
sn: अस्मान् वा त्वं पराजित्य यशः प्राप्नुहि संयुगे। वयं वा त्वां पराजित्य प्रीतिं धास्यामहे पितुः॥
en: Vanquishing ourselves in battle you may earn great glory, or crushing you in combat we shall attain to great gratification”.

description: End of the fifth day's fight
sn: एवमुक्तस्तदा शूरैस्तानुवाच महाबलः। वीर्यश्लाघी नरश्रेष्ठस्तान् दृष्ट्वा समवस्थितान्॥
en: Thus spoken to, that foremost of men possessed of great strength and heroism and proud of his prowess, seeing them ready for the fight, thus replied to them.

description: End of the fifth day's fight
sn: साध्विदं कथ्यते वीरा यद्येवं पतिरद्य वः। युध्यध्वं सहिता यत्ता निहनिष्यामि वो रणे॥
en: You have spoken well o heroes; if indeed this be your desire, fight with me in a body putting forth all your endeavors. I will slay all of you in battle.

description: End of the fifth day's fight
sn: एवमुक्ता महेष्वासास्ते वीराः क्षिप्रकारिणः। महता शरवर्षेण अभ्यधावन्नरिंदमम्॥
en: Thus spoken to those heroes all mighty bowmen and endued with great lightness of hand, poured a thick shower of arrows on that subduer of his enemies.

description: End of the fifth day's fight
sn: सोऽपराह्ने महाराज संग्रामस्तुमुलोऽभवत्। एकस्य च बहूनां च समेतानां रणाजिरे॥
en: That afternoon, mighty sovereign a dreadful battle was fought on the field between Bhurishravas alone on side and many united together on the other.

description: End of the fifth day's fight
sn: तमेकं रथिनां श्रेष्ठं शरैस्ते समवाकिरन्। प्रावृषीव यथा मेरुं सिषिचुर्जलदा नृप॥
en: O monarch, they then covered that single handed foremost of car-warriors with an arrow downpour, like rain clouds drenching a mighty cliff in the rainy season.

description: End of the fifth day's fight
sn: तैस्तु मुक्ताशरान् घोरान् यमदण्डाशनिप्रभान्। असम्प्राप्तानसम्भ्रान्तश्चिच्छेदाशु महारथः॥
en: But they mighty car-warrior cut down those numerous shafts discharged by them, shafts, which resembled the mace of Death or the thunder-bolt itself in their noise, even before they could reach him.

description: End of the fifth day's fight
sn: तत्राद्भुतमपश्याम सौमदत्तेः पराक्रमम्। यदेको बहुभिर्युद्धे समसज्जदभीतवत्॥
en: There we saw wonderful prowess of Bhurishrava, the son of Somadatti, who was fighting alone with many without fear.

description: End of the fifth day's fight
sn: विसृज्य शरवृष्टिं तां दश राजन् महारथाः। परिवार्य महाबाहुं निहन्तुमुपचक्रमुः॥ सौमदत्तिस्ततः क्रुद्धस्तेषां चापानि भारत। चिच्छेद समरे राजन् युध्यमानो महारथैः॥ अथैषां छिन्नधनुषां शरैः संनतपर्वभिः। चिच्छेद समरे राजशिरांसि भरतर्षभ।॥ ते हता न्यपतन् राजन् वज्रभग्ना इव दुमाः।
en: Those ten warriors then completely surrounding that mighty-armed hero, strove to slay him. But, О Bharata, Somdatta's son, inflamed with wrath, cutting off their bows, served their heads in that conflict with arrows of diverse descriptions. Thus slain, they fell down on the ground like trees crushed by the thunderbolt.

description: End of the fifth day's fight
sn: तान् दृष्ट्वा निहतान् वीरो रणे पुत्रान् महाबलान्।॥ वार्ष्णेयो विनदन् राजन् भूरिश्रवसमभ्ययात्।
en: Beholding those mighty sons of his slain in battle, that hero of the Vrishni race namely Satyaki rushed against Bhurishravas, O king, thundering out of his war cry.

description: End of the fifth day's fight
sn: रथं रथेन समरे पीडयित्वा महाबलौ॥ तावन्योन्यं हि समरे निहत्य रथवाजिनः।
en: Those two heroes both endued with great prowess, then made their cars collide against one another; and in that conflict slaying the steeds of one another's chariot.

description: End of the fifth day's fight
sn: विरथावभिवल्गन्तौ समेयातां महारथौ॥ प्रगृहीतमहाखड्गौ तौ चर्मवरधारिणौ।
en: And thus deprived of the use of their respective chariots those two mighty powerful heroes jumping down on the grounds, rushed against one another, whirling mighty swords and bucklers.

description: End of the fifth day's fight
sn: शुशुभाते नरव्याघ्रौ युद्धाय समवस्थितौ॥ ततः सात्यकिमभ्येत्य निस्त्रिंशवरधारिणम्।
en: Then those two foremost of men thus standing prepared for the encounter, appeared exceedingly beautiful. Thereafter approaching Satyaki who was armed with a sword of best make,

description: End of the fifth day's fight
sn: भीमसेनस्त्वरन् राजन् रथमारोपयत् तदा॥ तवापि तनयो राजन् भूरिश्रवसमाहवे। आरोपयद् रथं तूर्णं पश्यतां सर्वधन्विनाम्॥ तस्मिंस्तथा वर्तमाने रणे भीष्मं महारथम्। अयोधयन्त संरब्धाः पाण्डवा भरतर्षभ॥ लोहितायति चादित्ये त्वरमाणो धनंजयः।
en: Bhimasena, O monarch, hastily took him up on his chariot. Your son also, O king, in that conflict, speedily took up Bhurishravas on his car before the very eyes of all the assembled bowmen. When thus the battle raged, the son of Pandu (Arjuna), inflamed with wrath began to fight with that mighty car-warrior viz., Bhishma, O foremost of the Bharatas. When then the orb of the day assumed a crimson hue, Dhananjaya displaying great activity,

description: End of the fifth day's fight
sn: पञ्चविंशतिसाहस्रान् निजघान महारथान्॥ ते हि दुर्योधनादिष्टास्तदा पार्थनिबर्हणे।
en: Slew twenty five thousand mighty carwarrior of the hostile host. These warriors, being commanded by Duryodhana to slay the son of Pritha,

description: End of the fifth day's fight
sn: सम्प्राप्यैव गता नाशं शलभा इव पारकम्॥ ततो मत्स्याः केकयाश्च धनुर्वेदविशारदाः।
en: Approaching him met with their destruction, like insects burning on fire. Thereupon the Matsyas and the Kaikeyas all accomplished in the science of bowmanship,

description: End of the fifth day's fight
sn: परिवत्रुस्तदा पार्थं सहपुत्रं महारथम्॥ एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु सूर्येऽस्तमुपगच्छति।
en: Surrounded the mighty car-warrior Arjuna along with his son. At that moment the sun having gone down below the horizon.

description: End of the fifth day's fight
sn: सर्वेषां चैव सैन्यानां प्रमोहः समजायत॥ अवहारं ततश्चकेनं पिता देवव्रतस्तव। संध्याकाले महाराज सैन्यानां श्रान्तवाहनः॥ पाण्डवानां कुरूणां च परस्परसमागमे।
en: All the warriors were over whelmed with confusion. Then your Sire Devavrata whose steeds were completely exhausted, O mighty sovereign, caused the withdrawal of the force, After that (fierce) encounter between the Kurus and the Pandavas.

description: End of the fifth day's fight
sn: ते सेने भृशसंविग्ने ययतुः स्वं निवेशनम्॥ ततः स्वशिबिरं गत्वा न्यविशंस्तत्र भारत। पाण्डवाः संजयैः सार्धं कुरवश्च यथाविधि॥
en: The troops, overwhelmed as they were with great apprehension, retired to their respective encampments. There after repairing to their respective camps. O Bharata, the Pandava along with the Srinjayas, as also the Kurus, duly rested (for the night).

description: Commencement of the sixty day's fight
sn: संजय उवाच ते विश्रम्य ततो राजन् सहिताः कुरुपाण्डवाः। व्यतीतायां तु शर्वर्यां पुनर्युद्धाय निर्ययुः॥ तत्र शब्दो महानासीत् तव तेषां च भारत। युज्यतां रथमुख्यानां कल्प्यतां चैव दन्तिनाम्॥
en: Sanjaya said Then O monarch, when the night had worn away, the Kurus and the Pandavas, having duly rested, again marched forth for battle. Then O Bharata, a loud clangour arose there, as mighty car-warrior prepared themselves for battle, as tuskers were equipped for the coming conflict,

description: Commencement of the sixty day's fight
sn: संनह्यतां पदातीनां हयानां चैव भारत। शङ्खदुन्दुभिनादश्च तुमुलः सर्वतोऽभवत्॥ ततो युधिष्ठिरो राजा धृष्टद्युम्नमभाषत। व्यूहं व्यूह महाबाहो मकरं शत्रुनाशनम्॥
en: As the foot-soldiers donned their coats of mail and as steeds were furnished with trappings &c. Then O Bharata, on all sides was heard tremendous sound of drums and blare of conchs. Thereafter king Yudhishthira addressing Dhrishtadyumna said: “Arrange, O mighty-armed hero, the troops in the Makara array that is calculated to extirpate the enemy."

description: Commencement of the sixty day's fight
sn: एवमुक्तस्तु पार्थेन धृष्टद्युम्नो महारथः। व्यादिदेश महाराज रथिनो रथिनां वरः॥ शिरोऽभूद् दुपदस्तस्य पाण्डवश्च धनंजयः। चक्षुषी सहदेवश्च नकुलश्च महारथः॥
en: Thus spoken to by the son of Pritha (Yudhishthira) that mighty car-warrior Dhrishtadyumna, O sovereign, proclaimed that order among the car-warrior (for forming the Makara array). King Drupada and the Pandava Dhananjaya formed its head, Sahadeva along with the mighty car-warriors Nakula constituted its two eyes.

description: Commencement of the sixty day's fight
sn: तुण्डमासीन्महाराज भीमसेनो महाबलः। सौभद्रो द्रौपदेयाश्च राक्षसश्च घटोत्कचः॥ सात्यकिधर्मराजश्च व्यूहग्रीवां समास्थिताः। पृष्ठमासीन्महाराज विराटो वाहिनीपतिः॥
en: Bhimasena endued with great strength, O king, formed its beak. The son of Subhadra, the sons of Draupadi, the Rakshasa Ghatotkacha. Satyaki and the very virtuous king Yudhishthira were stationed on the neck of that array. Virata, the leader of a division, O monarch, formed its back.

description: Commencement of the sixty day's fight
sn: धृष्टद्युम्नेन सहितो महत्या सेनयावृतः। केकया भ्रातरः पञ्च वामपार्श्व समाश्रिताः॥ धृष्टकेतुर्नरव्याघ्रश्चेकितानश्च वीर्यवान्। दक्षिणं पक्षमाश्रित्य स्थितौ व्यूहस्य रक्षणे॥
en: The five Kaikeya brothers, united with Dhrishtadyumna and supported by a mighty division, stationed themselves on its left wing. Dhrishtaketu the foremost of men and Chekitana endued with prowess, stationing themselves on the right wing, prepared themselves for the defence of array.

description: Commencement of the sixty day's fight
sn: पादयोस्तु महाराज स्थितः श्रीमान् महारथः। कुन्तिभोजः शतानीको महत्या सेनया वृतः॥
en: O mighty monarch, at the feet of that array were stationed the ever prosperous and mighty car-warrior namely the Kuntibhoja, and Shatanika supported by a large division.

description: Commencement of the sixty day's fight
sn: शिखण्डी तु महेष्वासः सोमकैः संवृतो बली। इरावांश्च ततः पुच्छे मकरस्य व्यवस्थितौ॥
en: The fierce bowman Shikhandin, of great prowess being surrounded by the Somakas, together with Iravan, was stationed in the tail of that array.

description: Commencement of the sixty day's fight
sn: एवमेतं महाव्यूह व्यूह्य भारत पाण्डवाः। समुच्छ्रितैर्ध्वजैश्छत्रैः शस्त्रैश्च विमलैः शितैः॥
en: Thus 0 Bharata, disposing their troops in this array, the Pandavas, O mighty monarch, donning their mails and desirous of battle at sunrise.

description: Commencement of the sixty day's fight
sn: कौरवानभ्ययुस्तूर्ण हस्त्यश्वरथपत्तिभिः। समुच्छ्रितैर्ध्वजैश्छत्रैः शस्त्रैश्च विमलैः शितैः॥
en: Rushed against the Kauravas with impetuosity, supported by their elephantswarriors, car-warrior, cavalry and infantry as also with their standard, and umbrellas, and effulgent and shinning weapons upraised.

description: Commencement of the sixty day's fight
sn: व्यूढं दृष्ट्वा तु तत् सैन्यं पिता देवव्रतस्तव। क्रौञ्चैन महता राजन् प्रत्यव्यूहत वाहिनीम्॥
en: Beholding the troops of the Pandavas thus disposed of, your sire Devavrata, O king, arranged his troops in a counter-array figuring a huge crane.

description: Commencement of the sixty day's fight
sn: तस्य तुण्डे महेष्वासो भारद्वाजो व्यरोचत। अश्वत्थामा कृपश्चैव चक्षुरासीन्नरेश्वर।॥
en: In its beak was placed that mighty bowman the son of Bharadvaja; and O ruler of man, Ashvatthama and Kripa formed its two eyes.

description: Commencement of the sixty day's fight
sn: कृतवर्मा तु सहितः काम्बोजवरबाह्निकैः। शिरस्यासीन्नरश्रेष्ठः श्रेष्ठः सर्वधनुष्मताम्॥
en: Kritavarma the foremost of all bowman together with the king of the Kambojas and with the Balhikas, was O foremost of men, placed in the head of that array.

description: Commencement of the sixty day's fight
sn: ग्रीवायं शूरसेनश्च तव पुत्रश्च मारिष। दुर्योधनो महाराज राजभिर्बहुभिर्वृतः॥
en: Shurasena and your son Duryodhana, O Bharata, surrounded by numerous kings, was stationed in its neck, O mighty sovereign.

description: Commencement of the sixty day's fight
sn: प्राग्ज्योतिषस्तु सहितो मद्रसौवीरकेकयैः। उरस्यभून्नरश्रेष्ठ महत्या सेनया वृतः॥
en: The ruler of the Pragjyotishas, united with the Madras, the Souviras and the Kaikeyas, and supported by a large division, was, O foremost of men, placed in its breast.

description: Commencement of the sixty day's fight
sn: स्वसेनया च सहितः सुशर्मा प्रस्थलाधिपः। वामपक्षं समाश्रित्य दंशितः समवस्थितः॥
en: Susharma the ruler of Prasthala, clad in mail and supported by his own division stationing himself in its left wing, stood ready for battle.

description: Commencement of the sixty day's fight
sn: तुषारा यवनाश्चैव शकाश्च सह चूचुपैः। दक्षिणं पक्षमाश्रित्य स्थिता व्यूहस्य भारत॥
en: The Tusharas, the Yavanas, the Shakas, together with the Chuchupa, placing themselves in the right wing of that array prepared for battle, O Bharata.

description: Commencement of the sixty day's fight
sn: श्रुतायुश्च शतायुश्च सौमदत्तिश्च मारिष। व्यूहस्य जघने तस्थू रक्षमाणाः परस्परम्॥ ततो युद्धाय संजग्मुः पाण्डवाः कौरवैः सह। सूर्योदये महाराज ततो युद्धमभून्महत्॥
en: Shrutayush and Shatayush and the some of Somadatta, O Sire, supporting one another, stood in the rear of that array. Then the Pandavas rushed to battle with the Kurus. At sun rise, O mighty monarch, the engagement commenced.

description: Commencement of the sixty day's fight
sn: प्रतीयू रथिनो नागा नागांश्च रथिनो ययुः। हयारोहान् रथारोहा रथिनश्चापि सादिनः॥ सादिनश्च हयान् राजन् रथिनश्च महारणे। हस्त्यारोहान् हयारोहा रथिनः सादिनस्तथा॥
en: Elephants rushed against car-warrior and car-warrior proceeded against elephants. Horse-soldiers rushed against horse-soldiers, and car-warrior also advanced towards horsesoldiers. Horse-soldiers, O king, also rushed against horses and elephants in that dreadful fight; also, o king, elephant-riders proceeded against elephant-riders and cavalry.

description: Commencement of the sixty day's fight
sn: रथिनः पत्तिभिः सार्धं सादिनचापि पत्तिभिः। अन्योन्यं समरे राजन् प्रत्यधावन्नमर्षिताः॥
en: Car-warriors encountered foot-soldiers, and cavalry-soldiers also engaged with the infantry. Thus, O king, excited with wrath, they rushed against one another in that battle.

description: Commencement of the sixty day's fight
sn: भीमसेनार्जुनमैगुप्ता चान्यैर्महारथैः। शुशुभे पाण्डवी सेना नक्षत्रैरिव शर्वरी॥
en: The army of the Pandavas, defended by Bhimasena, Arjuna and the twins Nakula and Sahadeva, as also by other mighty car-warrior, appeared beautiful like the sky bespangled with stars in a dark night. as

description: Commencement of the sixty day's fight
sn: तथा भीष्मकृपद्रोणशल्यदुर्योधनादिभि। तवापि च वभौ सेना ग्रहैद्यौरिव संवृता॥
en: So also, your troops, O king, with Bhishma, Drona, Kripa, Shalya, Duryodhana and others, appeared beautiful like the firmament covered with the planets.

description: Commencement of the sixty day's fight
sn: भीमसेनस्तु कौन्तेयो द्रोणं दृष्ट्वा पराक्रमी। अभ्ययाज्जवनैरश्वैर्भारद्वाजस्य वाहिनीम्॥
en: Bhimasena the son of Kunti, endued with great prowess, beholding Drona, rushed against the division of Bharadvaja's son, being borne by fleetest steeds.

description: Commencement of the sixty day's fight
sn: द्रोणस्तु समरे क्रुद्धो भीमं नवभिरायसैः। विव्याध समरश्लाघी मर्माण्युद्दिश्य वीर्यवान्॥
en: The highly powerful Drona, waxing worth, in that battle, O monarch, pierced Bhishma with nine shafts made of iron directing them towards his vital parts.

description: Commencement of the sixty day's fight
sn: दृढाहतस्ततो भीमो भारद्वाजस्य संयुगे। सारथिं प्रेषयामास यमस्य सदनं प्रति॥
en: Thus wounded sore in that battle by the son of Bharadvaja, Bhima dispatched the latter's charioteer to the regions of the of Death.

description: Commencement of the sixty day's fight
sn: स संचह्य स्वयं वाहान् भारद्वाजः प्रतापवान्। व्यधमत् पाण्डवीं सेनां तूलराशिमिवानलः॥
en: Then that son of Bharadvaja endued with prowess, himself holding the reins of his steeds, began to consume the Pandava host like fire consuming a heap of cotton.

description: Commencement of the sixty day's fight
sn: ते वध्यमाना द्रोणेन भीष्मेण च नरोत्तमाः। सृञ्जयाः केकयैः सार्धं पलायनपराऽभवन्।॥
en: Thus slaughtered by Bhishma and Drona, O foremost men, the Srinjayas with the Kaikeyas took to their heels.

description: Commencement of the sixty day's fight
sn: तथैव तावकं सैन्यं भीमार्जुनपरिक्षतम्। मुह्यते तत्र तत्रैव समदेव वराङ्गना॥
en: So also your soldiers, mangled by Bhima and Arjuna, were deprived of their senses even where they stood, like an excellent damsel fainting away in consequence of wounded pride.

description: Commencement of the sixty day's fight
sn: अभिद्येतां ततो व्यूहौ तस्मिन् वीरवरक्षये। आसीद् व्यतिकरो घोरस्तव तेषां च भारत॥
en: In that battle, in which many excellent heroes lost their lives, the array of your soldiers as well as that of the Pandavas was shattered and broken and O Bharata, great distress overwhelmed the two armies.

description: Commencement of the sixty day's fight
sn: तदद्भुतमपश्याम तावकानां परैः सह। एकायनगताः सर्वे यदयुध्यन्त भारत॥
en: Then, O Bharata, we beheld a delightful sight, when your warriors fought with the enemy, both inspired with a singleness of purpose.

description: Commencement of the sixty day's fight
sn: प्रतिसंवार्य चास्त्राणि तेऽन्योन्यस्य विशाम्पते। युयुधुः पाण्डवाश्चैव कौरवाश्च महाबलाः॥
en: In that battle, O lord of men, the Pandavas and the Kauravas, fought with one another hurling weapons at one another.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच एवं बहुगुणं सैन्यमेवं बहुविधं पुरा। व्यूढमेवं यथाशास्त्रममोघं चैव संजय॥
en: Dhritarashtra said Our army is endued with many excellent attributes and composed of various kinds of troops and its efficiency is great. O Sanjaya it is disposed of in perfect accordance to the rules of the military science; so it should to be ever crowned with success.

sn: हृष्टमस्माकमत्यन्तमभिकामं च नः सदा। प्रह्वमव्यसनोपेतं पुरस्ताद् दृष्टविक्रमम्॥
en: The warriors therein are very much devoted to our interest, and are ever attached to us. They are disciplined and free from the vices of lust and anger. Their prowess has been tested before.

sn: नातिवृद्धमबालं च न कृशं न च पीवरम्। लघुवृत्तायतप्रायं सारयोधमनामयम्॥
en: Thus are neither very old nor very young; they are neither lean nor very corpulent. They are of active habits, well-built, strong bodied, and free from any disease.

sn: आत्तसंनाहशस्त्रं च बहुशस्त्रपरिग्रहम्। असियुद्धे नियुद्धे च गदायुद्धे च कोविदम्॥
en: They are clad in coats of mail and well furnished with offensive weapons they are accomplished in the use of all kinds of weapons and are masters in fighting with swords, with maces and even with bare arms.

sn: प्रासर्धितोमरेष्वाजौ परिघेष्वायसेषु च। भिन्दिपालेषु शक्तीषु मुसलेषु च सर्वशः॥ कम्पनेषु च चापेषु कणपेषु च सर्वशः। क्षेपणीयेषु चित्रेषु मुष्टयुद्धेषु च क्षमम्॥
en: They are well practiced in the use of lances, sabers, darts, iron bludgeons, short shafts, javelins and mallets.

sn: अपरोक्षं च विद्यासु व्यायामे च कृतश्रमम्। शस्त्रग्रहणविद्यासु सर्वासु परिनिष्ठितम्॥
en: They are well disciplined in the exercise of all kinds of weapons, and are experts in mounting on and descending from vehicles, in moving forward and in falling back,

sn: आरोहे पर्यवस्कन्दे सरणे सान्तरप्लुते। सम्यक् प्रहरणे याने व्यपयाने च कोविदम्॥ नागाश्वरथयानेषु बहुशः सुपरीक्षितम्।
en: In striking down effectually, in marching forward, and in retreating back; they have been examined in the management of steeds, elephants, and chariots.

sn: परीक्ष्य च यथान्यायं वेतनेनोपपादितम्॥ न गोष्ठ्या नोपकारेण न च बन्धुनिमित्ततः।
en: Being duly tested, they have been employed on pay and not for the sake of fainily relationship.

sn: न सौहृदबलैर्वापि नाकुलीनपरिग्रहै: :॥ समृद्धजनमार्यं च तुष्टसम्बन्धिबान्धवम्। कृतोपकारभूयिष्ठं यशस्वि च मनस्वि च॥ स्वजनैस्तु नरैर्मुख्यैर्बहुशो दृष्टकर्मभिः। लोकपालोपमैस्तात पालितं लोकविश्रुतम्॥ बहुभिः क्षत्रियैर्गुप्तं पृथिव्यां लोकसम्मतैः। अस्मानभिगतैः कामात् सबलैः सपदानुगैः॥ महोदधिमिवापूर्णमापगाभिः समन्ततः।
en: Nor for the sake of friendship, nor for connections through marriage and birth. They are all honorable and prosperous and all their relatives have been honoured and well treated by ourselves. We have done many good services to them; they are also all illustrious men, possessed of great intelligence. They are again defended, O son, by many best of men endued with great lightness, of great achievements, of world-wide renown and resembling the protectors of the worlds themselves they are protected by numerous Kshatriya esteemed throughout the earth who have, out of their own accord, taken our side with their followers and force. Truly our army is like the vast ocean swelling with the waters of various streams flowing into it from all sides.

sn: अपक्षैः पक्षिसंकाशै रथै गैश्च संवृतम्॥ नानायोधजलं भीमं वाहनोर्मितरङ्गिणम्।
en: Our army teems with chariots which though destitute of wings are capable of moving like the winged rangers of the sky; it abounds also in elephants. Myriads of fierce warriors constitute the waters of that ocean and the various vehicles constitute its numerous waves.

sn: क्षेपण्यसिगदाशक्तिशरप्राससमाकुलम्॥ ध्वजभूषणसम्बाधं रत्नपट्टसुसंचितम्।
en: Innumerable maces, dares, arrows and lances form the oars plied on it. It abounds in standards and ornaments and is full of cloths of gold embossed with gems.

sn: परिधावद्भिरश्वैश्च वायुवेगविकम्पितम्॥ अपारमिव गर्जन्तं सागरप्रतिमं महत्।
en: The running vehicles constitute the wind that lashes that ocean into fury. It really resembles the extensive and scoreless sea roaring (in fury).

sn: द्रोणभीष्माभिसंगुप्तं गुप्तं च कृतवर्मणा॥ कृपदुःशासनाभ्यां च जयद्रथमुखैस्तथा।
en: That army of ours is again protected by Drona and Bhishma; so also it is defended by Kritavarma, Kripa and Dushasana and by others headed by Jayadratha.

sn: भगदत्तविकर्णाभ्यां द्रौणिसौबलबाह्निकैः॥ गुप्तं प्रवीरैलॊकैश्च सारवद्भिर्महात्मभिः।
en: By Bhagadatta and Vikarna, by the son of Drona, by Subala and by the ruler of the Balhikas. Thus protected by many foremost of men, all endued with strength and possessed of generous souls.

sn: यदहन्यत संग्रामे दैवमत्र पुरातनम्॥ नैतादृशं समुद्योगं दृष्टवन्तो हि मानुषाः। ऋषयो वा महाभागाः पुराणा भुवि संजय॥ ईदृशोऽपि बलौघस्तु संयुक्तः शस्त्रसम्पदा।
en: If that army be still slaughtered in battle, it is indeed due to predestined Fate. Neither man, nor illustrious and ancient sages, O Sanjaya, ever saw on earth such extensive preparations for battle. That such a large army well-supplied with the implements and sinews of war.

sn: वध्यते यत्र संग्रामे किमन्यद् भागधेयतः॥ विपरीतमिदं सर्वं प्रतिभाति हि संजय।
en: Should be slain in battle, alas, what can it be due to but Destiny? All this appears to be unnatural, O Sanjaya.

sn: यत्रेदृशं बलं घोरं पाण्डवान्नातरद् रणे॥ पाण्डवाार्थाय नियतं देवास्तत्र समागताः। युध्यन्ते मामकं सैन्यं यथाऽध्यत संजय॥
en: This all appears me reverse to listen that so vast army could not face and defeat Pandavas in battle. O Sanjaya! The gods come in support of Pandavas definitely and battle against my army. This is the reason, it is being slaughtered in uncountable numbers day-to-day.

sn: उक्तो हि विदुरेणाहं हितं पथ्यं च नित्यशः। न च जग्राहः तन्मन्दः पुत्रो दुर्योधनो मम॥
en: Vidura had often advised what would have been beneficial and profitable; but my wicked son Duryodhana would not accept his counsel.

sn: तस्य मन्ये मतिः पूर्वं सर्वज्ञस्य महात्मनः। आसीद् यथागतं तात येन दृष्टमिदं पुरा॥
en: I think the prophetic and high-souled Vidura had foreseen all that is happening at present; and hence his thought was so.

sn: अथवा भाव्यमेवं हि संजयैतेन सर्वथा। पुरा धात्रा यथा सृष्टं तत् तथा नैतदन्यथा॥
en: Or it may be, O Sanjaya, that all this had been predestined by the Creator; and what is pre-ordained by him must happen as ordained and can not be other wise.

sn: संजय उवाच आत्मदोषात् राजन् प्राप्तं व्यसनमीदृशम्। न हि दुर्योधनस्तानि पश्यते भरतर्षभ।॥ यानि त्वं दृष्टवान् राजन् धर्मसंकरकारिते। तव दोषात् पुरा वृत्तं द्यूतमेव विशाम्पते॥
en: Sanjaya said Through your won wickedness, O monarch, have you been overwhelmed with this calamity. Those faults, O foremost of the Bharatas, in that sinful conduct towards the Pandavas of which you were cognizant, O king, were not descried by Duryodhana. It was through your fault, O ruler of men, that the game at dice was played in days past.

sn: तव दोषेण युद्धं च प्रवृत्तं सह पाण्डवैः। त्वमेवाद्य फलं भुक्षे कृत्वा किल्बिषमात्मना॥
en: And it is through your fault also that this battle with the Pandavas has been brought about. Do you now reap the fruit of that sin which you have already committed.

sn: आत्मनैव कृतं कर्म आत्मनैवोपभुज्यते। इह च प्रेत्य वा राजंस्त्वया प्राप्तं यथातथम्॥
en: One reaps the fruits of actions done by himself; so, O monarch, do you reap here and hereinafter the fruits of your won actions.

sn: तस्माद् राजन् स्थिरो भूत्वा प्राप्येदं व्यसनं महत्। शृणु युद्धं यथावृत्तं शंसती मे नराधिप।॥
en: O monarch, through overwhelmed with this calamity, be still patient, and listen to the account of the battle as it happened, as I, O sire, go on recounting it.

sn: भीमसेनः सुनिशितैर्वाणैर्भित्त्वा महाचमूम्। आससाद ततो वीरः सर्वान् दुर्योधनानुजान्॥ दुःशासनं दुर्विषहं दुःसहं दुर्मदं जयम्। जयत्सेनं विकर्णं च चित्रसेनं सुदर्शनम्॥ चारुचित्रं सुवर्माणं दुष्कर्णं कर्णमेव च। एतांश्चान्यांश्च सुबहून् समीपस्थान् महारथान्॥ धार्तराष्ट्रान् सुसंक्रुद्धान् दृष्ट्वा भीमो महारथः। भीष्मेण समरे गुप्तां प्रविवेश महाचमूम्॥
en: Having shattered the ranks of your mighty army with his well well sharpened sharpened shafts Bhimasena, endued with heroism, encountered all the younger brothers of Duryodhana. Duryodhana, Durvishaha, Dusaha, Durmada, Jaya, Jayatsena, Vikarna, Chitrasena, Sudarshana, Charuchitra, Suvarma, Dushkarna, and Karna beholding these and many other mighty car-warriors of the Dhritarashtra near enough to himself, all excited with wrath, Bhimasena, endued with great strength, in that battle penetrated into the ranks of your mighty army protected by Bhishma himself.

sn: अथालोक्य प्रविष्टं तमूचुस्ते सर्व एव तु। जीवग्राहं निगृह्णीमो वयमेनं नराधिपाः॥
en: Then seeing him standing amongst them all those kings said; Let us torture this one till he is deprived of his life.

sn: स तैः परिवृतः पार्थो भ्रातृभिः कृतनिश्चयैः। प्रजासंहरणे सूर्यः क्रूरैरिव महाग्रहैः॥
en: Then that of Pritha (Bhima) encompassed by those brothers of his, all resolved (to slay him) appeared like the sun surrounded by the unpropitious planets and the time of the world's annihilation.

sn: सम्प्राप्यमध्यं सैन्यस्य न भीः पाण्डवमाविशत्। यथा देवासुरे युद्धे महेन्द्रं प्राप्य दानवान्॥
en: Though then the son of Pandu (Bhima) was in the very heart of the Kaurava array fear did son not overwhelm him as it did not overwhelm Indra in the midst of the Danava host during the fight, in days of old, between the Asuras and the celestial.

sn: ततः शतसहस्राणि रथिनां सर्वशः प्रभो। उद्यतानि शरैस्तीद्वैस्तमेकं परिवविरे॥
en: Then hundreds and thousands of carwarrior furnished with all kinds of weapons, all ready for the battle, assailed his single self with dreadful arrows.

sn: स तेषां प्रवरान् योधान् हस्त्यश्वरथसादिनः। जघान समरे शूरो धार्तराष्ट्रानचिन्तयन्।॥
en: Thereat the heroic Bhima unmindful of the sons of Dhritarashtra, slow in that battle many foremost (hostile) warriors, including elephantriders, cavalry-soldiers, car-warrior and others.

sn: तेषां व्यवसितं ज्ञात्वा भीमसेनो जिघृक्षताम्। समस्तानां वधे राजन् मतिं चक्रे महामनाः॥
en: And knowing the intention of those cousins of his who were all resolved to slay him, Bhimasena, possessed of great strength determined. O king, to slay them all.

sn: ततो रथं समुत्सृज्य गदामादायें पाण्डवः। जघान धार्तराष्ट्राणां तं बलौघं महार्णवम्॥
en: Thereafter, leaving aside his car and grasping his mace, that son of Pandu (Bhima) began to smite down that ocean like host belonging to the sons of Dhritarashtra.

sn: भीमसेने प्रविष्टे तु धृष्टद्युम्नोऽपि पार्षतः। द्रोणमुत्सृज्य तरसा प्रययौ यत्र सौबलः॥
en: When Bhimasena had thus broken the Kaurava host, Dhrishtadyumna the son of Prishata, abandoning Drona hide there where Subala's son was.

sn: निवार्य महतीं सेनां तावकानां नरर्षभः। आससाद रथं शून्यं भीमसेनस्य संयुगे॥
en: That foremost of men, checking the mighty army of your sons, approached, in that battle, the car of Bhima left empty by himself.

sn: दृष्ट्वा विशोकं समरे भीमसेनस्य सारथिम्। धृष्टद्युम्नो महाराज दुर्मना गतचेतनः॥
en: Seeing, in that conflict, Vishoka the charioteer of Bhimasena, Dhrishtadyumna, O mighty monarch, became depressed in mind and was deprived of his senses.

sn: अपृच्छद् वाष्पसंरुद्धो निःश्वसन वाचमीरयन्। मम प्राणैः प्रियतमः क्व भीम इति दुःखितः॥
en: Overwhelmed with grief, his voice choked up with tears and breathing heavily he questioned Vishoka saying: “Where is Bhimasena, dearer to me than my own life?"

sn: विशोकस्तमुवाचेदं धृष्टद्युम्नं कृताञ्जलिः। संस्थाप्य मामिह बली पाण्डवेयः पराक्रमी॥
en: Thereupon, folding his palm, Vishoka thus replied to Dhrishtadyumna saving: Leaving me here, the mighty son of Pandu (Bhima), possessed of great strength.

sn: प्रविष्टो धार्तराष्ट्राणामेतद् बलमहार्णवम्। मामुक्त्वा पुरुषव्याघ्रः प्रीतियुक्तमिदं वचः॥
en: Has, alone and unsupported entered into the ocean like host of the sons of Dhritarashtra. He said to me, O foremost of men, these cheerful words.

sn: प्रतिपालय मां सूत नियम्याश्वान् मुहूर्तकम्। यावदेतान् निहन्म्यद्य य इमे मद्वधोद्यताः॥
en: Wait for me, O charioteer, restraining the steeds for a moment only, until I slay these that are resolved to destroy me.

sn: ततो दृष्ट्वा प्रधावन्तं गदाहस्तं महाबलम्। सर्वेषामेव सैन्यानां संहर्षः समजायत।॥
en: Beholding then the highly powerful Bhima running mace in hand, all the car-warriors were transported with joy.

sn: तस्मिन् सुतुमुले युद्धे वर्तमाने भयानके। भित्त्वा राजन् महाव्यूहं प्रविवेश वृकोदरः॥
en: And when when that awful and general engagement raged, O monarch, you friend, breaking through the hostile ranks penetrated into it.

sn: विशोकस्य वचः श्रुत्वा धृष्टद्युम्नोऽथ पार्षतः। प्रत्युवाच ततः सूतं रणमध्ये महाबलः॥ न हि मे जीवितेनापि विद्यतेऽद्य प्रयोजनम्। भीमसेनं रणे हित्वा स्नेहमुत्सृज्य पाण्डवैः॥
en: Listening to these words of Vishoka Dhrishtadyumna the son of Prishata, possess of great strength, replied to the charioteer on the filed of battle saying: If today, discarding my affection for the Pandavas, I am to abandon Bhimasena in the fight, what needs have I then of my very life?

sn: यदि यामि विना भीमं किं मां क्षत्रं वदिष्यति। एकायनगते भीमे मयि चावस्थिते युधि॥
en: What will the Kshatriya say of me if I return without Bhima (from the filed of battle)? What will they say of me when they will hear that Bhima alone entered into the hostile ranks though I was there to help him in the conflict?

sn: अस्वस्ति तस्य कुर्वन्ति देवाः शक्रपुरोगमाः। यः सहायान् परित्यज्य स्वस्तिमानाव्रजेद् गृहम्॥
en: The gods headed by Shakra himself visit him with evil who abandoning his supporters in battle, returns home unscathed.

sn: मम भीमः सखा चैव सम्बन्धी च महाबलः। भक्तोऽस्मान् भक्तिमांश्चाहं तमप्यरिनिषूदनम्॥
en: Moreover that highly powerful Bhima is my friend and relative. He is devoted to me, and I cherish a great devotion for that slayer of foes.

sn: सोऽहं तत्र गमिष्यामि यत्र यातो वृकोदरः। निघ्नन्तं मां रिपून् पश्य दानवानिव वासवम्॥
en: I shall therefore penetrate there where Vrikodara has already gone. see me slay the foes like Vasava slaying the Danavas”.

sn: एवमुक्त्वा ततो वीरो ययौ मध्येन भारत। भीमसेनस्य मार्गेषु गदाप्रमथितैर्गजैः॥ स ददर्श तदा भीमं दहन्तं रिपुवाहिनीम्। वातो वृक्षानिव बलात् प्रभञ्जन्तं रणे रिपून्॥
en: Having thus spoken that hero 0 Bharata, advanced through the centre of the hostile ranks following the track (opened and ) marked by Bhima with the elephants crushed by his mace. Then he (Dhrishtadyumna) beheld Bhima consuming the troops of the enemy and crushing in the conflict, many kings, like so many trees.

sn: ते वध्यमानाः समरे रथिनः सादिनस्तथा। पादाता दन्तिनश्चैव चक्रुरार्तस्वरं महत्॥
en: The car-warrior the cavalry-soldiers the foot-soldiers and the tuskers, being thus slaughtered in the fight, began to utter loud distressful cries.

sn: हाहाकारश्च संजयज्ञे तव सैन्यस्य मारिष। वध्यतो भीमसेनेन कृतिना चित्रयोधिना॥
en: Cries of 'Oh and 'Alas'. O sire, arose from the ranks of your soldiers, as they were slaughtered by the accomplished Bhima versed in diverse modes of warfare.

sn: ततः कृतास्त्रास्ते सर्वे परिवार्य वृकोदरम्। अभीताः समवर्तन्त शस्त्रवृष्ट्या परंतप॥
en: Thereafter they (the Kaurava combatants) exercised in all sorts of weapons surrounding, Vrikodara, began fearlessly to pour a shower of weapons on him from all sides.

sn: अभिद्रुतं शस्त्रभृतां वरिष्ठं समन्ततः पाण्डवं लोकवीरः। सैन्येन घोरेण सुसंहितेन दृष्ट्वा बली पार्षतो भीमसेनम्॥
en: Then that highly powerful son of Prishata, beheld that foremost of all wielders of weapons that hero of world-wide fame, that son of Pandu, viz., Bhimasena, charged on all sides by the serried and mighty ranks of the enemy:

sn: अथोपगच्छच्छरविक्षताङ्गं पदातिनं क्रोधविषं वमन्तम्। आश्वासयन् पार्षतो भीमसेनं गदाहस्तं कालमिवान्तकाले॥
en: And approaching Bhimasena, the son of Prishata comforted him whose body was mangled with shaft-cuts, who was treading on foot sand vomiting the poison of his anger and who was wielding his mace like the Destroyer himself as the time of the universal annihilation.

sn: मारोपयच्चात्मरथे महात्मा। माश्वासयामास च शत्रुमध्ये॥
en: That high-souled hero (Dhrishtadyumna) quickly plucked off the arrows from Bhima's body and took him up on his car, and embracing the latter warmly, the former comforted him even in the very midst of the enemy.

sn: स्तस्मिन् विमर्दे महति प्रवृत्ते। अयं दुरात्मा दुपदस्य पुत्रः समागतो भीमसेनेन सार्धम्॥
en: Thereat, in that conflict, your son, approaching his brothers, quickly said to them. "This wicked-souled son of Drupada has now joined Bhimasena.

sn: तं याम सर्वे महता बलेन मा वो रिपुः प्रार्थयतामनीकम्। श्रुत्वा तु वाक्यं तममृष्यमाणा ज्येष्ठाज्ञया नोदिता धार्तराष्ट्राः॥
en: We shall proceed against him in close array in order to slay him, even before he, our enemy, challenges us to fight.” Hearing these words, the sons of Dhritarashtra, urged on by the command of their elder brother and unable to put up with the foe,

sn: वधाय निष्पेतुरुदायुधास्ते युगक्षये केतवो यद्वदुग्राः। प्रगृह्य चास्त्राणि धनूंषि वीरा ज्यां नेमिघोषैः प्रविकम्पयन्तः॥
en: With uplifted weapons fell to slaughter him (Dhrishtadyumna), like so many dreadful comets falling down at the hour of destruction at the end of a Yuga. Grasping beautiful bows and shaking the earth with the twang of their bows and the rattle of their car-wheels, those heroes,

sn: शरैरवर्षन् द्रुपदस्य पुत्रं यथाम्बुदा भूधरं वारिजालैः। न विव्यथे समरे चित्रयोधी॥
en: Showered arrows on the son of Drupada, like the clouds showering rain on mountain breasts. But the latter, accomplished in various modes of warfare, though thus wounded with keen-pointed shafts did not flinch.

sn: समभ्युदीर्णाश्च तवात्मजांस्तथा निशम्य वीरानभितः स्थितान् रणे। जिघांसुरुचं दुपदात्मजो युवा प्रमोहनास्त्रं युयुजे महारथः॥ क्रुद्धो भृशं तव पुत्रेषु राजन् दैत्येषु यद्वत् समरे महेन्द्रः। ततो व्यमुह्यन्त रणे नृवीराः प्रमोहनास्त्राहतबुद्धिसत्त्वाः॥
en: On the other hand, O king, highly inflamed with rage against your sons, like Indra against he Asuras, that mighty car-warrior, the youthful son of Drupada, beholding your heroic sons stay before him in battle and exert their best for slaying him, placed on his bowstring the fierce dart called Pramohana, with a view to slay them all. Then those heroic warriors, having their senses and mind confounded by being struck with the Paramohana weapon lost all consciousness.

sn: प्रदुद्रुवुः कुरवश्चैव सर्वे सवाजिनागाः सरथाः समन्तात्। परीतकालानिव नष्टसंज्ञान् मोहोपेतांस्तव पुत्रान् निशम्य॥
en: Seeing those sons of yours overwhelmed with a swoon and deprived of their senses, like those whose hours has come, thu Kaurava troops fled in all directions, with their steeds, elephants and chariots.

sn: एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु द्रोणः शस्त्रभृतां वरः। दुपदं त्रिभिरासाद्य शरैर्विव्याध दारुणैः॥
en: Meanwhile, Drona that foremost of all wielders of weapons, encountering Drupada, pierced him with there fierce arrows.

sn: सोऽतिविद्धस्ततो राजन् रणे द्रोणेन पार्थिवः। अपायाद् दुपदो राजन् पूर्ववैरमनुस्मरन्।॥
en: Thus, O king, wounded sore by Drona, that ruler of men, Drupada, fled from the field of battle, remembering his former enmity (with Bharadvaja's son).

sn: जित्वा तु दुपदं द्रोण: शङ्ख दध्मौ प्रतापवान्। तस्य शङ्खस्वनं श्रुत्वा वित्रेसुः सर्वसोमकाः॥
en: Thereupon the highly powerful Drona, having vanquished Drupada, sounded his conch. Hearing the blare of his conch, all the Somakas were struck with terror.

sn: अथ शुश्राव तेजस्वी द्रोणः शस्त्रभृतां वरः। प्रमोहनास्त्रेण रणे मोहितानात्मजांस्तव।॥
en: Then Drona, endued with great energy, that foremost of wielders of weapons heard that your sons had been deprived of their senses in battle through the influence of the Pramohana weapon.

sn: ततो द्रोणो महाराज त्वरितोऽभ्याययौ रणात्। तत्रापश्यन्महेष्वासो भारद्वाजः प्रतापवान्॥
en: Thereupon, desirous of rescuing the princes, Drona hastily left that pare of the filed where he was (and went where your sons were); there, that mighty bowman possessed of great prowess namely the son of Bharadvaja beheld.

sn: धृष्टद्युम्नं च भीमं च विचरन्तौ महारणे। मोहाविष्टांश्च ते पुत्रानपश्यत् स महारथः॥ ततः प्रज्ञास्त्रामादाय मोहनास्त्रं व्यनाशयत्। अथ प्रत्यागतप्राणास्तव पुत्रा महारथाः॥
en: Dhrishtadyumna and Bhima career through that dreadful field; and that mighty car-warrior likewise beheld your sons over-whelmed with a swoon. Thereupon, he fixed on his bowstring the weapon known as Pranjana (capable of impairing consciousness) and therewith cut off the Pramohana weapon. Then your sons, those mighty car-warrior, regained their senses.

sn: पुनयुद्धाय समरे प्रययुर्भीमपार्षतौ। ततो युधिष्ठिरः प्राह समाहूय स्वसैनिकान्॥
en: Thereupon, desirous of battle, they again encountered Bhima and the son of Prishata in battle. Then king Yudhishthira summoning his troops addressed them saying:

sn: गच्छन्तु पदवीं शक्त्या भीमपार्षतयोर्युधि। सौभद्रप्रमुखा वीरा रथा द्वादश दंशिताः॥
en: "Let twelve heroic car-warriors headed by Subhadra's son, protected with coats of mail, proceed following, to the best of their abilities, the track of Bhima and the son of Prishata.

sn: प्रवृत्तिमधिगच्छन्तु न हि शुद्ध्यति मे मनः। त एवं समनुज्ञाताः शूरा विक्रान्तयोधिनः॥ बाढमित्येवमुक्त्वा तु सर्वं पुरुषमानिनः। मध्यन्दिनगते सूर्ये प्रययुः सर्व एव हि॥ केकया द्रौपदेयाश्च धृष्टकेतुश्च वीर्यवान्। अभिमन्युं पुरस्कृत्य महत्या सेनया वृताः॥
en: Let intelligence be brought (of those two heroes). My mind is not unmisgiving". Thus commanded, the five Kaikeya princes, the sons of Draupadi, and the highly powerful Dhrishtaketu all powerful warriors, endued with heroism and proud of their manliness, saying 'yea' (to the words of Yudhishthira) marched forward when the sun had reached the meridian, placing Abhimanyu at their head and being supported by a mighty division of troops.

sn: ते कृत्वा समरव्यूहं सूचीमुखमरिंदमाः। बिभिदुर्धार्तराष्ट्राणां तद् स्थानीकमाहवे॥
en: Those grinders of foes forming their troops in the array known as Suchimukha, penetrated, in that battle, into that car-division of the sons of Dhritarashtra.

sn: तान् प्रयातान् महेष्वासानभिमन्युपुरोगमान्। भीमसेनभयाविष्टा धृष्टद्युम्नविमोहिता॥ न संवारयितुं शक्ता तव सेना जनाधिप। मदमूर्छान्वितात्मा वै प्रमदेवाध्वनि स्थिता॥
en: Your troops, O ruler of men struck with the fear of Bhimasena and deprived of their senses by Dhrishtadyumna were not able to bear the charge of those fierce bowmen headed by Abhimanyu as the rushed, like a lady in the streets deprived of her consciousness by a Swoon.

sn: तेऽभिजाता महेष्वासाः सुवर्णविकृतध्वजाः। परीष्सन्तोऽभ्यधावन्त धृष्टद्युम्नवृकोदरौ॥ तौ च दृष्ट्वा महेष्वासावभिमन्युपुरोगमान्। बभूवतुर्मुदा युक्तौ निघ्नन्तौ तव वाहिनीम्॥
en: Desirous of rescuing Dhrishtadyumna and Vrikodara, those fierce bowmen owning and standards decked with gold, approached the former breaking through the hostile ranks. Those two heroes viz., Vrikodara and Dhrishtadyumna himself, became filled with delight, and fell (with increase ardour) to slaughter your troops.

sn: दृष्ट्वा तु सहसाऽऽयान्तं पाञ्चाल्यो गुरुमात्मनः। नाशंसत वधं वीरः पुत्राणां तव भारत॥
en: Then the prince of the Panchalas, the heroic of son of Prishata, beholding his own preceptor suddenly make towards himself, desisted from compassing the death of your sons.

sn: ततो रथं समारोप्य कैकेयस्य वृकोदरम्। अभ्यधावत् सुसंक्रुद्धौ द्रोणमिष्वस्त्रपारगम्॥
en: Then placing Vrikodara on the car of the Kaikeya king he, inflamed with rage, rushed against Drona who was accomplished in the use of arrows and all other kinds of weapons.

sn: तस्याभिपतस्तूर्णं भारद्वाजः प्रतापवान्। क्रुद्धश्चिच्छेद बाणेन धनुः शत्रुनिबर्हणः॥
en: Then the highly-powerful of Bharadvaja, that grinder of foes, excited with wrath severed, with a broad-head shaft, the bow of Dhrishtadyumna as the latter rushed against him with impetuosity.

sn: अन्यांश्च शतशो बाणान् प्रेषयामास पार्षते। दुर्योधनहितार्थाय भर्तृपिण्डमनुस्मरम्॥
en: Bearing in mind the broad he had eaten of his master king Duryodhana and desirous of encompassing his good, he (Drona) directed hundreds of other various shafts towards the son of Prishata.

sn: अथान्यद् धनुरादाय पार्षतः परवीरहा। द्रोणं विव्याध विंशत्या रुक्मपुजैः शिलाशितैः॥
en: Thereafter, grasping another bow that slayer of hostile heroes, namely the son of Prishata, son pierced Drona with seventy shafts all furnished with golden wings and whetted on stone.

sn: तस्य द्रोणः पुनश्चापं चिच्छेदामित्रकर्शनः। हयांश्चचतुरस्तूर्णं चतुर्भिः सायकोत्तमैः॥ वैवस्वतक्षयं घोरं प्रेषयामास भारत। सारथिं चास्य भल्लेन प्रेषयामास मृत्यवे॥
en: Then again Drona, that grinder of foes, cut down Dhrishtadyumna's bow; and his four steeds he dispatched to the dreadful abode of Death with four excellent arrows; and. O Bharata, Drona also dispatched to Death Dhrishtadyumna's charioteer with a broadheaded shaft.

sn: हताश्वात् स रथात् तूर्णमवप्लुत्य महारथः। आरुरोह महाबाहुरभिमन्योर्महारथम्॥
en: Thereupon that mighty car-warrior, Dhrishtadyumna, possessed of long arms, speedily jumping down from his chariot of which the steeds were slain, mounted on the excellent car of Abhimanyu.

sn: ततः सरथनागाश्वा समकम्पत वाहिनी। पश्यतो भीमसेनस्य पार्षतस्य च पश्यतः॥
en: Then the Pandava host, consisting of chariots, elephants and steeds, begin to quake with the fear (of Drona) even before the very eyes of Bhimasena and the intelligent son of Prishata.

sn: तत्प्रभग्नं बलं दृष्ट्वा द्रोणेनामिततेजसा। नाशक्नुवन् वारयितुं समस्तास्ते महारथाः॥
en: Beholding their array thus shattered by Drona of immeasurable prowess, all those mighty car-warrior were not able to check the former.

sn: वध्यमानं तु ततं सैन्यं द्रोणेन निशितैः शरैः। व्यभ्रमतं तत्र तत्रैव क्षोभ्यमाण इवार्णवः॥
en: That army, then thus slaughter by Drona with his keen pointed arrows begin to whirl about,, like the agitated sea, on the filed of battle.

sn: तथा दृष्ट्वा च तत्सैन्यं जहषे तावकं बलम्। दृष्ट्वाऽऽचार्यं सुसंक्रुद्धं पतन्तं रिपुवाहिनीम्। चुक्रुशुः सर्वतो योधाः साधु साध्विति भारत॥
en: Beholding the hostile troops in that plight, your warriors were filled with delight and also beholding the aged preceptor consume the hostile array on all sides, O Bharata, the warriors sent up loud exclamations of “welldone" "well-done".

sn: संजय उवाच ततो दुर्योधनो राजा मोहात् प्रत्यागतस्तदा। शरवर्षेः पुनर्भीमं प्रत्यवारयदच्युतम्॥
en: Sanjaya said Thereafter king king Duryodhana, having regained his senses, once more opposed the invincible Bhima with a shower of arrows.

sn: एकीभूतास्ततश्चैव तव पुत्रा महारथाः। समेत्य समरे भीमं योधयामासुरुद्यताः॥
en: Once more uniting together, your sons, all mighty car-warrior, encountering Bhima in battle, begin to fight with him in all earnestness.

sn: भीमसेनोऽपि समरे सम्प्राप्य स्वरथं पुनः। समारुह्य महाबाहुर्ययौ येन तवात्मजः॥
en: The mighty-armed Bhimasena also approaching his chariot mounted on it, and proceeded to that pare of the filed where your sons were.

sn: प्रगृह्य च महावेगं परासुकरणं दृढम्। सज्जं शरासनं संख्ये शरैर्विव्याध ते सुतम्॥
en: Taking up a wonderfully tough bow endued with great energy, capable of depriving the enemy of his life, and diversely variegated, he (Bhima) began to pierce your sons with innumerable shafts in that battle.

sn: ततो दुर्योधनो राजा भीमसेनं महाबलम्। नाराचेन सुतीक्ष्णेन भृशं मर्मण्यताडयत्॥
en: Then king Duryodhana shortly wounded the mighty Bhima in his very vital parts with a Naracha of exceeding sharpness.

sn: सोऽतिविद्धो महेष्वासस्तव पुत्रेण धन्विना। क्रोधसंरक्तनयनो वेगेनाक्षिप्य कार्मुकम्॥
en: Thus deeply pierced by your son, that fierce bow-man, with eyes red in rage and out of fury drawing his bow-string fiercely.

sn: दुर्योधनं त्रिभिर्वाह्वोरुरसि चार्पयत्। स तत शुशुभे राजा शिखरैगिरिराडिव॥
en: Pierced Duryodhana on this two arms and breast, with three arrows; but O king, thus struck the latter wavered not, like a monarch of mountains.

sn: तौ दृष्ट्वा समरे विनिघ्नन्तौ परस्परम्। दुर्योधनानुजाः सर्वे शूराः संत्यक्तजीविताः॥
en: Beholding those two enraged heroes strike one another in battle, the younger brothers of Duryodhana, all of whom were ready to lay down lives their in battle.

sn: संस्मृत्य मन्त्रितं पूर्वं निग्रहे भीमकर्मणः। निश्चयं परमं कृत्वा निग्रहीतुं प्रचक्रमुः॥
en: Bearing in mind their pre-concerted plan of afflicting Bhima of fierce deeds, began with an earnest determination, to strike him (from all sides).

sn: तानापतत एवाजौ भीमसेनो महाबलः। प्रत्युद्ययौ महाराज गजः प्रतिगजानिव॥
en: Then the highly powerful Bhima beholding them make towards himself in battle, O monarch, rushed against them like an elephants encountering his compeers.

sn: भृशं क्रुद्धश्च तेजस्वी नाराचेन समार्पयत्। चित्रसेनं महाराज तव पुत्रं महायशाः॥
en: Then excited to fury, that hero endued with great fame and energy, afflicted your son Chitrasena, O monarch, with a long shaft.

sn: तथेतरांस्तव सुतांस्तनाडयामास भारत। शरैर्बहुविधैः संख्ये रुक्मपुत्रैः सुतेजनैः॥
en: Then in that conflict, O king, the descendant of the Bharata race smote your other sons with diverse kinds of arrows furnished with golden wings and charged with great impetus.

sn: तत: संस्थाप्य समरे तान्यनीकानि सर्वशः। अभिमन्युप्रभृतयस्ते द्वादश महारथाः॥
en: Then those twelve mighty car-warrior including Abhimanyu and others, arranging their troops in proper order,

sn: प्रेषिता धर्मराजेन भीमसेनपदानुगाः। प्रतिजग्मुर्महाराज तव पुत्रान् महाबलान्॥
en: And being dispatched by the very virtuous king Yudhishthira to follow behind Bhima, encounter, O mighty monarch, your princely sons, all excellent car-warrior.

sn: दृष्ट्वा रथस्थांस्ताशूरान् सूर्याग्निसमतेजसः। सर्वानेव महेष्वासान् भ्राजमानाश्रिया वृतान्॥
en: Beholding those warriors on that chariots resemble the sun or the fire itself in effulgence, beholding all those fierce bow-men of burning effulgence and exceeding beauty,

sn: महाहवे दीप्यमानान् सुवर्णमुकुटोज्ज्वलान्। तत्यजुः समरे भीमं तव पुत्रा महाबलाः॥ तान् नामृष्यत कौन्तेयो जीवमाना गता इति।
en: Shine resplendent in that conflict being decorated with diadems of gold-your sons all endued with great strength abandoned fighting with Bhima. But the son of Kunti was unable to brook the sight of their leaving the combat alive.

sn: संजय उवाच अन्वीय च पुनः सर्वांस्तव पुत्रानपीडयत्॥ अथाभिमन्यु समरे भीमसेनेन संगतम्। पार्षतेन च सम्प्रेक्ष्य तव सैन्ये महारथाः॥ दुर्योधनप्रभृतयः प्रगृहीतशरासनाः। भृशमश्चैः प्रजवितैः प्रययुर्यत्र ते रथाः॥ अपराह्ने महाराज प्रावर्तत महारण:। तावकानां च बलिनां परेषां चैव भारत॥ अभिमन्युविकर्णस्य हयान् हत्वा महाहवे।
en: Sanjaya said Then Abhimanyu accomplished by Bhimasena, once more running after them afflicted your sons in battle. Thereupon the mighty car-warriors of your army including Duryodhana and others seeing Abhimanyu and Bhimasena joined with the son of Prishata in the midst of their own troops grasped their bows and carried along by fleet steeds rushed to the place where those heroes were stationed. Then, in that afternoon O monarch, there ensued a terrible fight between the mighty warriors of your army and those of the enemy, O Bharata. Then Abhimanyu, slaying the steeds of Vikarna in that terrible conflict,

sn: अथैनं पञ्चविंशत्या क्षुद्रकाणां समार्पयत्॥ हताश्वं रथमुत्सृज्य विकर्णस्तु महारथः।
en: Pierced the latter with twenty five short shafts then that mighty car-warrior Vikarna, leaving his chariot of which the steeds were slain,

sn: आरुरोह रथं राजंश्चित्रसेनस्य भारत॥ स्थितावेकरथे तौ तु भ्रातरौ कुलवर्धनौ।
en: Ascended, O king, the resplendent car of Chitrasena; them thus seated on the same chariot, namely those two brothers the perpetuator of Kuru's race.

sn: आर्जुनिः शरजालेन च्छादयामास भारत॥ चित्रसेनो विकर्णश्च कार्ष्णि पञ्चभिरायसैः। विव्याध तेन चाकम्पत् कार्णिमरुरिव स्थितः॥ दुःशासनस्तु समरे केकयान् पञ्च मारिष। योधयामास राजेन्द्र तदद्भुतमिवाभवत्॥ द्रौपदेया रणे क्रुद्धा दुर्योधनमवारयन्।
en: The son of Arjuna, O Bharata covered with a shower of arrows. Then Durjaya and Vikarna pierced the nephew of Krishna with five shafts made entirely of iron. But the nephew of Krishna moved not in the least and remained firm like the immovable Meru. In that conflict, O sire Dushasana fought with the five Kaikeya brothers; O mighty monarch, the battle that raged between them was indeed very wonderful. The sons of Draupadi excited with rage, in that battle, checked Duryodhana.

sn: शरैराशीविषाकारैः पुत्रं तव विशाम्पते॥ पुत्रोऽपि तव दुर्धर्षो द्रौपद्यास्तनयान रणे। सायकैर्निशितै राजन्नाजघान पृथक् पृथक्॥ तैश्चापि विद्धः शुशुभे रुधिरेण समुक्षितः।
en: Your son; and O monarch, every one them pierced him with three shafts each. Your invincible son, O monarch, in that conflict, pierced the sons of Draupadi separately with arrows of exceeding sharpness. Pierced with their arrows in return and bespattered with blood, he (Duryodhana) appeared highly beautiful.

sn: गिरिः प्रस्रवणैर्यद्वद् गैरिकादिविमिश्रितैः॥ भीष्मोऽपि समरे राजन् पाण्डवानामनीकिनीम्। कालयामास बलवान् पालः पशुगणानिव॥ ततो गाण्डीवनिर्घोषः प्रादुरासीद् विशाम्पते। दक्षिणेन वरूथिन्याः पार्थस्यारीन् विनिघ्नतः॥ उत्तस्थुः समरे तत्र कबन्धानि समन्ततः।
en: Like a mountain washed with spring water mixed with red chalk. The highly powerful Bhishma also, O king, in that battle began to afflict the Pandava host like a herdsman belaboring his herd (with his cudgel). Thereupon, O ruler of men, the twang of Partha's Gandiva was heard, when he was engaged in slaughtering the right wing of your arıny. In that battle, headless trunks stood up in all directions.

sn: कुरूणां चैव सैन्येषु पाण्डवानां च भारत॥ शोणितोदं शरावर्तं गजद्वीपं हयोर्मिणम्। रथनौभिर्नरव्याघ्राः प्रतेरुः सैन्यसागरम्॥ छिन्नहस्ता विकवचा विदेहाश्च नरोत्तमाः। दृश्यन्ते पतितास्तत्र शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः॥ निहतैर्मत्तमातङ्गैः शोणितौघपरिप्लुतैः। भूर्भाति भरतश्रेष्ठ पर्वतैराचिता यथा।॥ तत्राद्भुतमपश्याम तव तेषां च भारत।
en: In the host of the Kurus as well as in that of the Pandava. O Bharata that ocean of troops of which blood formed the waters, the arrows the eddies, the elephants the islands, and the steeds the fishes, that ocean was crossed by those foremost of men on their chariots that served the purpose of boats. Many foremost warriors, with arms serve, armours shattered, and bodies mangled were seen lying prostrate there, by hundreds and by thousands. With the car-cases of infuriate elephants slain and bespattered with blood, the filed of battle, O foremost of the Bharatas, appeared beautiful as if strewn with hillocks. The wonderful sight that we beheld, O Bharata, was that among your as well as their army.

sn: न तत्रासीत् पुमान् कश्चिद् यो युद्धं नाभिकाङ्क्षति।।१९। एवं युयुधिरे वीराः प्रार्थयाना महद् यशः। तावकाः पाण्डवैः सार्धमाकाङ्क्षन्तो जयं युधि॥
en: There was no man who was not in flamed with a desire for battle. Thus did those heroic warriors of your army fight on with those of the Pandava, desiring great renown and ardently longing for securing victory in battle.

description: Withdrawal of the force after the Sixth day's fight
sn: संजय उवाच ततो दुर्योधनो राजा लोहितायति भास्करे। संग्रामरभसो भीमं हन्तुकामोऽभ्यधावत॥
en: Sanjaya said Then when the sun assumed a crimsons hue, king Duryodhana, ardently longing for battle, rushed towards Bhima, out of a desire for slaying him.

description: Withdrawal of the force after the Sixth day's fight
sn: तमायान्तमभिप्रेक्ष्य नृवीरं दृढवैरिणम्। भीमसेनः सुसंक्रुद्ध इदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Beholding that best of human heroes, that most implacable enemy of his, make towards himself Bhimasena, excited to the highest pitch of wrath, said these words,

description: Withdrawal of the force after the Sixth day's fight
sn: अयं स कालः सम्प्राप्तो वर्षपूगाभिवाञ्छितः। अद्य त्वां निहनिष्यामि यदि नोत्सृजसे रणम्॥
en: The hour has come that I have been loO king forward to so anxiously for all these years. Today I will slay you, if indeed you, you do not abandon fighting.

description: Withdrawal of the force after the Sixth day's fight
sn: अद्य कुन्त्याः परिक्लेशं वनवासं च कृत्स्नशः। द्रौपद्याश्च परिक्लेशं प्रणेष्यामि हते त्वयि॥
en: Slaying you, I will this day soothe the sorrows of Kunti and also those of Draupadi, today will I avenge the woes that we did suffer during our exile in the woods.

description: Withdrawal of the force after the Sixth day's fight
sn: यत् पुरा मत्सरी भूत्वा पाण्डवानवमन्यसे। तस्य पापस्य गान्धारे पश्य व्यसनमागतम्॥
en: O son of Gandhari, inflated with pride in days past, you disregarded the sons of Pandu, Reap now the dire fruit of that act of yours.

description: Withdrawal of the force after the Sixth day's fight
sn: कर्णस्य मतमास्थाय सौबलस्य च यत् पुरा। अचिन्त्य पाण्डवान् कामाद् यथेष्टं कृतवानसि॥
en: Acting upon the counsel of Karna and the son of Subala, and thoroughly disregarding the Pandavas, you formerly treated the latter as it had pleased you.

description: Withdrawal of the force after the Sixth day's fight
sn: याचमानं च यन्मोहाद् दाशार्हमवमन्यसे। उलूकस्य समादेशं यद् ददासि च हृष्टवत्॥
en: You also despised the descendant of the Dasharnas (Krishna) when be begged you (for peace). Filled with joy, you sent Uluka to us with your messages.

description: Withdrawal of the force after the Sixth day's fight
sn: तेन त्वां निहनिष्यामि सानुबन्धं सबान्धवम्। समीकरिष्ये तत् पापं यत् पुरा कृतवानसि॥
en: For all these act of yours, I will, this day, slay you with all your relations, and will avenge all those wrongs you did formerly inflict on us".

description: Withdrawal of the force after the Sixth day's fight
sn: एवमुक्त्वा धनुर्घोरं विकृष्योभ्राम्य चासकृत्। समाधत्त शरान् घोरान् महाशनिसमप्रभान्॥
en: Having spoken these words, and bending and repeatedly stretching his bow and taking up terrible arrows that resembled the thunder boit itself in effulgence Bhima.

description: Withdrawal of the force after the Sixth day's fight
sn: षड्विंशतिमथ संक्रुद्धो मुमोचाशु सुयोधने। ज्वलिताग्निशिखाकारान् वज्रकल्पानजिह्मगान्॥
en: Excited with rage, quickly shot at Suyodhana thirty six arrows resembling the flames of a blazing fire, loO king like the thunderbolt and coursing straight through the air.

description: Withdrawal of the force after the Sixth day's fight
sn: ततोऽस्य कार्मुकं द्वाभ्यां सूतं द्वाभ्यां च विव्यधे। चतुर्भिरश्वाञ्जवनाननयद् यमसादनम्॥
en: Thereafter he struck Duryodhana's bow with two arrows, his charioteer with another two; and with four others, he dispatched the latter's fleet steeds to the abode of Death.

description: Withdrawal of the force after the Sixth day's fight
sn: द्वाभ्यां च सुविकृष्टाभ्यां शराभ्यामरिमर्दनः। छत्रं चिच्छेद समरे राज्ञस्तस्य नरोत्तम॥
en: Then that grinder of foes, with two other arrows drawn a long way back at the time of being discharged, cut down, in that conflict, the umbrella of the king from his excellent car.

description: Withdrawal of the force after the Sixth day's fight
sn: षड्भिश्च तस्य चिच्छेद ज्वलन्तं ध्वजमुत्तमम्। छित्त्वा तं च ननादोच्चैस्तव पुत्रस्य पश्यतः॥
en: With three more arrows he cut down the excellent standard that was indeed blazing. Having severed it, he uttered a loud roar even before ihe very eyes of your son.

description: Withdrawal of the force after the Sixth day's fight
sn: रथाच्च स ध्वजः श्रीमान् नानारत्नविभूषितात्। पपात सहसा भूमौ विद्युज्जलधरादिव॥
en: And that beautiful standard, decked with diverse kinds of gems, suddenly felt down on the ground from the chariot, like lighting from the clouds shooting down on the earth.

description: Withdrawal of the force after the Sixth day's fight
sn: ज्वलन्तं सूर्यसंकाशं नागं मणिमयं शुभम्। ध्वजं कुरुपतेश्छिन्नं ददृशुः सर्वपार्थिवाः॥
en: And all the rulers of men then beheld that blazing and propitious standard of the Kuru king, effulgent like the sun, bearing the device of an elephants and embossed with gems, fall down, (served by Bhima).

description: Withdrawal of the force after the Sixth day's fight
sn: अथैनं दशभिर्बाणैस्तोत्रैरिव महाद्विपम्। आजघान रणे वीरं स्मयन्निव महारथः॥
en: Then the mighty car-warrior Bhima, as if smiling, struck Duryodhana with ten shafts, in that battle, like and elephants-rider piercing the huge animal with the hook.

description: Withdrawal of the force after the Sixth day's fight
sn: ततः स राजा सिन्धूना रथश्रेष्ठो महारथः। दुर्योधनस्य जग्राह पार्णि सत्पुरुषैर्वृतः॥
en: Thereupon the king of the Sindhus, that foremost of car-warrior, that highly powerful one, stationed himself on the flank of Duryodhana, being supported by many excellent warriors.

description: Withdrawal of the force after the Sixth day's fight
sn: कृपश्च रथिनां श्रेष्ठः कौरममितौजसम्। आरोपयद् रथं राजन् दुर्योधनममर्षणम्॥
en: Then that foremost of car-warrior, namely Kripa took upon his own car, O king, the vindictive Duryodhana, that descendant of the Kuru race, endued with immeasurable energy.

description: Withdrawal of the force after the Sixth day's fight
sn: स गाढविद्धो व्यथितो भीमसेनेन संयुगे। निषसाद रथोपस्थे राजन् दुर्योधनस्तदा॥
en: Then in that conflict, king Duryodhana,, pierced deep and afflicted sore by Bhimasena, squalled down on the terrace of his car.

description: Withdrawal of the force after the Sixth day's fight
sn: परिवार्य ततो भीमं जेतुकामो जयद्रथः। रथैरनेकसाहौर्भीमस्यावारयद् दिशः॥
en: Thereafter king Jayadratha, desirous of slaying Bhima, surrounded him on all sides with thousands of chariots, and warriors, and thus intercepted him.

description: Withdrawal of the force after the Sixth day's fight
sn: धृष्टकेतुस्ततो राजन्नभिमन्युश्च वीर्यवान्। केकया द्रौपदेयाश्च तव पुत्रानयोधयन्॥ चित्रसेनः सुचित्रश्च चित्राङ्गश्चित्रदर्शनः। चारुचित्रः सुचारच तथा नन्दोपनन्दकौः॥
en: Thereupon, O king, Dhrishtaketu and Abhimanyu endued with prowess, the Kaikeyas, and the sons of Draupadi, engaged with your sons.

description: Withdrawal of the force after the Sixth day's fight
sn: अष्टावेते महेष्वासाः सुकुमारा यशस्विनः। अभिमन्युरथं राजन् समन्तात् पर्यवारयन्॥
en: In that battle the eight great archer and chivalrous warriors-Chitrasena, Suchitra, Chitranga, Chitradarshana, Caruchitra, Sucharu, Nanda and Upananda had trapped in a circle the chariot of delicate Abhimanyu.

description: Withdrawal of the force after the Sixth day's fight
sn: आजघान ततस्तूर्णमभिमन्युर्महामनाः। एकैकं पञ्चभिर्वाणैः शितैः संनतपर्वभिः॥ :।
en: The high-souled Abhimanyu quickly struck them all piercing each with five shafts.

description: Withdrawal of the force after the Sixth day's fight
sn: वज्रमृत्युप्रतीकाशैर्विचित्रायुधनिःसृतः। अमृष्यमाणास्ते सर्वे सौभद्रं रथसत्तमम्॥ ववृषुर्मागैस्तीक्ष्णैर्गिरिं मेरुमिवाम्बुदाः। स पीड्यमानः समरे कृतास्त्रो युद्धदुर्मदः॥
en: Resembling the thunder-bolt itself or the mace of Death, shot from his beautiful bow. Thereupon all of them unable to bear it, showered an arrow down pour on that excellent car-warrior namely Subhadra's son, like clouds showering rain on the Meru mountain. Thus afflicted in the battle, that hero, accomplished in the use of weapons, and invincible in fight.

description: Withdrawal of the force after the Sixth day's fight
sn: अभिमन्युर्महाराज तावकान् समकम्पयत्। यथा देवासुरे युद्धे वज्रपाणिर्महासुरान्॥
en: Namely, Abhimanyu, O king, made your warriors tremble, like the wielder of the thunder-bolt making the Asuras tremble in the war between them and the celestial.

description: Withdrawal of the force after the Sixth day's fight
sn: विकर्णस्य ततो भल्लान् प्रेषयामास भारत। चतुर्दश रथश्रेष्ठो घोरानाशीविषोपमान॥
en: Thereafter, O Bharata, that foremost of carwarrior, hurled at Vikarna fourteen mortal broad-headed shafts that looked like snakes of most virulent venom.

description: Withdrawal of the force after the Sixth day's fight
sn: स तैर्विकर्णस्य रथात् पातयामास वीर्यवान्। ध्वजं सूतं हयांश्चैव नृत्यमान इवाहवे॥
en: Possessed of great prowess, and as if dancing in battle, with those shafts he cut down the standard of Vikarna from this car and also slew his charioteer and steeds.

description: Withdrawal of the force after the Sixth day's fight
sn: पुनश्चान्याशरान् पीतानकुण्ठाग्राशिलाशितान्। प्रेषयामास संक्रुद्धो विकर्णाय महाबलः॥
en: Again that mighty car-warrior viz., the son of Subhadra shot at Vikarna other arrows, well tempered, kcen-pointed and straight-coursing.

description: Withdrawal of the force after the Sixth day's fight
sn: ते विकर्णं समासाद्य कङ्कबर्हिणवाससः। भित्तवा देहं गता भूमि ज्वलन्त इव पन्नगाः॥
en: Those arrows decked with the feathers of the Kanka bird, coming upon Vikarna and passing through his body stuck on the ground like so many hissing snakes.

description: Withdrawal of the force after the Sixth day's fight
sn: ते शरा हेमपुङ्खाग्रा व्यदृश्यन्त महीतले। विकर्णरुधिरक्लिन्ना वमन्त इव शोणितम्॥
en: Those arrows, with wings and points decorated with gold and bathed in the blood of Vikarna, and stuck on the earth appeared to the vomit-blood.

description: Withdrawal of the force after the Sixth day's fight
sn: विकर्णं वीक्ष्य निर्भिन्नं तस्यैवान्ये सहोदराः। अभ्यद्रवन्त समरे सौभद्रप्रमुखान् रथान्॥
en: Beholding Vikarna thus penetrated through and through, his other uterine brothers, rushed in that conflict against those warriors who were headed by the son of Subhadra.

description: Withdrawal of the force after the Sixth day's fight
sn: अभियात्वा तथैवान्यान् रथांस्तान् सूर्यवर्चसः। अविध्यन् समरेऽन्योन्यं संरम्भाद् युद्धदुर्मदाः॥
en: When those warriors formidable in battle riding on their own chariots quickly came upon the combatant of the Pandava army seated on their car like so many effulgent suns, they began to pierce one another in that battle.

description: Withdrawal of the force after the Sixth day's fight
sn: दुर्मुखः श्रुतकर्माणं विद्ध्वा सप्तभिराशुगैः। ध्वजमेकेन चिच्छेद सारथिं चास्य सप्तभिः॥
en: Then Durmukha piercing Shrutakarma with five swift-coursing arrows cut down the latter's standard with a single arrow, and pierced his charioteer also with seven others.

description: Withdrawal of the force after the Sixth day's fight
sn: अश्वाञ्जाम्बूनदैर्जालैः प्रच्छन्नान् वातरंहसः। जघान् षड्भिरासाद्य सारथिं चाभ्यपातयत्॥
en: Advancing closer, with six arrows he pierced Shrutakarman's steedscaparisoned with a net work of gold and fleet as the wind itself; he also felled the letters charioteer.

description: Withdrawal of the force after the Sixth day's fight
sn: स हताश्वे रथे तिष्ठश्रुतकर्मा महारथः। शक्तिं चिक्षेप संक्रुद्धो महोल्का ज्वलितामिव॥
en: Thereupon standing on that chariot of his of which the steeds were slain, that mighty carwarrior Shrutakarma, excited to the highest pitch of fury, hurled a great dart blazing like a fierce meteor.

description: Withdrawal of the force after the Sixth day's fight
sn: सा दुर्मुखस्य विमलं वर्म भित्त्वा यशस्विनः। विदार्य प्राविशद् भूमिं दीप्यमाना स्वतेजसा॥
en: That very resplendent dart charge with great energy penetrating through the massive armour of the renowned Durmukha, and shattering it, stuck itself on the ground.

description: Withdrawal of the force after the Sixth day's fight
sn: तं दृष्ट्वा विरथं तत्र सुतसोमो महारथः। पश्यतां सर्वसैन्यानां रथमारोपयत् स्वकम्॥
en: Thereupon Sutosoma, possessed of great prowess beholding Shrutakarma deprived of his chariot, took him up on his car even before the very eyes of the assembled host.

description: Withdrawal of the force after the Sixth day's fight
sn: श्रुतकीर्तिस्तथा वीरो जयत्सेनं सुतं तव। अभ्ययात् समरे राजन् हन्तुकामो यशस्विनम्॥
en: Thereafter, 0 monarch, Shrutakirti possessed of heroism, rushed, in that battle, against your illustrious son Jayatsena, out of a desire for slaying him.

description: Withdrawal of the force after the Sixth day's fight
sn: तस्य विक्षिपतश्चापं श्रुतकीर्तेर्महास्वनम्। चिच्छेद समरे तूर्णं जयत्सेनः सुतस्तव॥ क्षुरप्रेण सुतीक्ष्णेन प्रहसन्निव भारत। तं दृष्ट्वा छिन्नधन्वानं शतानीकः सहोदरम्॥
en: Then in that conflict ( monarch your son Jayatsena with a sharp edged Kshurapra (horse-shoe-headed shaft), as if smiling, cut off the bow of that high-souled warrior, namely Shrutakirti, 0 Bharata, as the latter came repeatedly stretching it. Thereupon Shatanika seeing his uterine brother deprived of his bow.

description: Withdrawal of the force after the Sixth day's fight
sn: अभ्यपद्यत तेजस्वी सिंहवन्निनदन् मुहुः। शतानीकस्तु समरे दृढं विस्फार्य कार्मुकम्॥
en: Endued as he was with great energy, quickly rushed to the shop, every moment uttering roars resembling those of a lion. Then in that conflict stretching his bow with a strong hand, Shatanika.

description: Withdrawal of the force after the Sixth day's fight
sn: विव्याध दशभिस्तूर्णं जयत्सेनं शिलीमुखैः। ननाद सुमहानादं प्रभिन्न इव वारणः॥
en: With great lightness of hands, pierced Jayatsena with ten sharp arrows and then uttered a loud roar like that of an elephants in rut.

description: Withdrawal of the force after the Sixth day's fight
sn: अथान्येन सुतीक्ष्णेन सर्वावरणभेदिना। शतानीको जयत्सेनं विव्याध हृदये भृशम्॥
en: Then again with another sharp arrow capable of penetrating through all kinds of main, Shatanika deeply pierced Jayatsena on the breast.

description: Withdrawal of the force after the Sixth day's fight
sn: तथा तस्मिन् वर्तमाने दुष्कर्णो भ्रातुरन्तिके। चिच्छेद समरे चापं नाकुलेः क्रोधमूर्च्छितः॥
en: At this crisis, Dushkarna, who was near his brother, overwhelmed with wrath cut off the bow and arrows of the son of Nakula (Shatanika).

description: Withdrawal of the force after the Sixth day's fight
sn: अथान्यद् धनुरादाय भारसाहमनुत्तमम्। समादत्त शरान् घोराज्शतानीको महाबलः॥
en: Thereat, grasping another bow of excellent make and capable of bearing great strain the highly powerful Shatanika fixed on the bow string shafts of exceeding sharpness.

description: Withdrawal of the force after the Sixth day's fight
sn: तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति चामन्त्र्य दुष्कर्णं भ्रातुरग्रतः। मुमोचास्मै शितान् बाणाज्वलितान् पन्नगानिव॥
en: Then he (Shatanika) challenged Dushkarna before his brothers, saying "Wait” “Wait", and then he discharged at him those keen pointed arrows that resembled so many blazing snakes.

description: Withdrawal of the force after the Sixth day's fight
sn: ततोऽस्य धनुरेकेन द्वाभ्यां सूतं च मारिष। चिच्छेद समरे तूर्णं तं च विव्याध सप्तभिः॥
en: Then the former cut off the latter's bow with a single shaft; and pierced his charioteer with two shafts; and, O sire, in that conflict the former also quickly pierced the latter with feathered shafts.

description: Withdrawal of the force after the Sixth day's fight
sn: अश्वान् मनोजवांस्तस्य कर्बुरान् वातरंहसः। जघान निशितैस्तूर्णं सर्वान् द्वादशभिः शरैः॥
en: Thereafter that sinless warriors, with twelve shafts of great sharpness, pierced all the steeds of Dushkarna, steeds that we effect as the mind and decked with gold trappings.

description: Withdrawal of the force after the Sixth day's fight
sn: अथापरेण भल्लेन सुयुक्तेनाशुपातिना। दुष्कर्णं सुदृढं क्रुद्धो विव्याध हृदये भृशम्॥
en: Then highly excited with rage, he in that conflict, deeply pierced, Dushkarna on the chest with another broad-headed arrow welldirected and swift coursing.

description: Withdrawal of the force after the Sixth day's fight
sn: स पपात ततो भूमो वज्राहत इव द्रुमः। दुष्कर्णं व्यथितं दृष्ट्वा पञ्च राजन् महारथाः॥
en: There at the latter fell down on the ground like a tree smitten by the thunder bolt. Beholding Dushkarna slain, the five mighty car-warrior, O king.

description: Withdrawal of the force after the Sixth day's fight
sn: जिघांसन्तः शतानीकं सर्वतः पर्यवारयन्। छाद्यमानं शरव्रातैः शतानीकं यशस्विनम्॥
en: encompassed Shatanika on all sides, out of a desire for slaying him; and they began to strike the illustrious Shatanika with a showers of arrows.

description: Withdrawal of the force after the Sixth day's fight
sn: अभ्यधावन्त संक्रुद्धाः केकयाः पञ्च सोदराः। तानभ्यापततः प्रेक्ष्य तव पुत्रा महारथाः॥
en: Thereupon the five Kaikeya princes excited with rage, rushed (to the rescue of Shatanika). Beholding them advance, your sons all mighty car-warriors.

description: Withdrawal of the force after the Sixth day's fight
sn: प्रत्युद्ययुर्महाराज गजानिव महागजाः। दुर्मुखो दुर्जयश्चैव तथा दुर्मर्षणो युवा॥
en: O mighty monarch, encountered them like so many elephants encountering their huge compeers. Durmukha, Durjaya, the youthful Durmarshana.

description: Withdrawal of the force after the Sixth day's fight
sn: शत्रुजयः शत्रुसहः सर्वे क्रुद्धा यशस्विनः। प्रत्युद्याता महाराज केकयान् भ्रातरः समम्॥
en: Shatrunjaya and Shatrusaha, all these illustrious warriors, proceeded, O king, in a body against the Kaikeya brothers.

description: Withdrawal of the force after the Sixth day's fight
sn: रथैर्नगरसंकाशैर्हयैर्युक्तैर्मनोजवैः। नानावर्णविचित्राभिः पताकाभिरलंकृतैः॥
en: Riding their chariots resembling (fortified) cities, to which were steed decked with precious caparisons and which were decorated wonderful streamers of variegated hue.

description: Withdrawal of the force after the Sixth day's fight
sn: वरचापधरा वीरा विचित्रकवचध्वजाः। विविशुस्ते परं सैन्यं सिंहा इव वनाद् वनम्॥
en: on Those heroes, welding excellent bows, owing finest armours and best standards, entered the hostile array like lions going from one forest to another.

description: Withdrawal of the force after the Sixth day's fight
sn: तेषां सुतमुलं युद्धं व्यतिषक्तरथद्विपम्। अवर्तत महारौद्रं निघ्नतामितरेतरम्॥
en: Then between them and the foe, raged a fierce and dreadful combat in which cars and elephants got entangled together and in which the combatants (mercilessly) slew one another,

description: Withdrawal of the force after the Sixth day's fight
sn: अन्योन्यागस्कृतां राजन् यमराष्ट्रविवर्धनम्। मुहूर्तास्तमिते सूर्ये चक्रुर्युद्धं सुदारुणम्॥
en: Out of a feeling of animosity, they fought the dreadful fight that lasted for a few moments only before sun-set, adding to the population of Death's kingdom,

description: Withdrawal of the force after the Sixth day's fight
sn: रथिनः सादिनश्चाथ व्यकीर्यन्त सहस्रशः। ततः शान्तनवः क्रुद्धः शरैः संनतपर्वभिः॥ नाशयामास सेनां तां भीष्मस्तेषां महात्मनाम्। पञ्चालानां च सैन्यानि शरैर्निन्ये यमक्षयम्॥
en: Then car-warriors and cavalry-soldiers were strewn by thousand on the filed of battle. Thereupon excited with wrath, the son of Shantanu namely Bhishma, with straightknotted shafts, began to slay the troops of the high-souled Pandavas. with his arrows he also dispatched to the regions of Death the troops belonging to the Panchala Princes.

description: Withdrawal of the force after the Sixth day's fight
sn: एवं भित्त्वा महेष्वासः पाण्डवानामनीकिनीम्। कृत्वाऽवहारं सैन्यानां ययौ स्वशिबिरं नृप॥
en: Thus, O king, having broken the ranks of the Pandava host, the grandsire, withdrawing his force, retired to his own encampment.

description: Withdrawal of the force after the Sixth day's fight
sn: धर्मराजोऽपि सम्प्रेक्ष्य धृष्टद्युम्नवृकोदरौ। मूर्ध्नि चैतावुपाघ्राय प्रहृष्टः शिबिरं ययौ॥
en: The very virtuous king Yudhishthira also seeing Dhrishtadyumna and Vrikodara, smelt their heads, and with a delighted heart repaired to his camps.

sn: संजय उवाच अथ शूरा महाराज परस्परकृतागसः। जग्मुः स्वशिबिराण्येव रुधिरेण समुक्षिताः॥
en: Sanjaya said Then, O mighty monarch, those heroes literally bespattered with blood, keeping alive their enmity for one another, retired to their respective tents.

sn: विश्रम्य च यथान्यायं पूजयित्वा परस्परम्। संनद्धाः समदृश्यन्त भूयो युद्धचिकीर्षया॥
en: Thereafter having rested awhile, and having duly praised one another (for the feats achieve), they again were seen clad in coats of mail, standing desirous of battle.

sn: ततस्तव सुतो राजंश्चिन्तयाऽभिपरिप्लुतः। विस्रवच्छोणिताक्ताङ्गः पप्रच्छेदं पितामहम्॥
en: Then, O monarch, your son Duryodhana, covered with stains of blood all over the body, and overwhelmed with anxious thought, from confidence, asked the grandsire Bhishma saying;

sn: सैन्यानि रौद्राणि भयानकानि व्यूढानि सम्यग् बहुलध्वजानि। स्ते पाण्डवानां त्वरिता महारथाः॥
en: "Our troops are fierce and formidable and duly arranged; and they carry mighty standards, and yet those heroic and fleet host of car-warrior belonging to the Pandava army, penetrating and slaughtering and crushing.

sn: सम्मोह्य सर्वान् युधि कीर्तिमन्तो व्यूहं च तं मकरं वज्रकल्पम्। प्रविश्य भीमेन रणे हतोऽस्मि घोरैः शरैर्मृत्युदण्डप्रकाशैः॥
en: and confounding us all, has earned great fame in battle. I have also been wounded deeply by those dreadful shafts resembling the club of Death himself, that have been shot by Bhima who broke through our Makara-array that was strong as the thunder bolt itself.

sn: क्रुद्धं तमुवीक्ष्य भयेन राजन् सम्मूर्च्छितो न लभे शान्तिमद्य। इच्छे प्रसादात् तव सत्यसंध प्राप्तुं जयं पाण्डवेयांश्च हन्तुम्॥
en: Beholding Bhima, I have been, O sire, unmanned with fear, even now I can not regain the equilibrium of my mind, O you of neverfalling aim, I desire, through your grace, to obtain victory and to slay the sons of Pandava”.

sn: तेनैवमुक्तः प्रहसन् महात्मा दुर्योधनं मन्युगतं विदित्वा। तं प्रत्युवाचाविमना मनस्वी गङ्गासुतः शस्त्रभृतां वरिष्ठः॥
en: Thus addressed by Duryodhana and knowing him to be possessed by great grief, that high-souled son of Ganga that foremost of all wielders of weapons, endued with intelligence, smiling, replied to the former with a cheerless heart:

sn: परेण यत्नेन विगाह्य सेनां सर्वात्मनाहं तव राजपुत्र। इच्छामि दातुं विजयं सुखं च न चात्मानं छादयेऽहं त्वदर्थे॥
en: "Breaking through the hostile ranks with the greatest exertions and with all my power, O prince, I wish to give you victory and joy. For your sake, I do never dissemble.

sn: एते तु रौद्रा बहवो महारथा यशस्विनः शूरतमाः कृतास्त्राः। ये पाण्डवानां समरे सहाया जितक्लमा रोषविषं वमन्ति॥
en: These mighty car-warrior, who have sided with the Pandavas in this battle, innumerable, formidable, all foremost horses, endued with renown and accomplished in the use of weapons; they are indefatigable and are seem to vomit forth the venom of their wrath in battle.

sn: ते नैव शख्याः सहसा विजेतुं वीर्योद्धताः कृतवैरास्त्वया च। अहं सेनां प्रतियोत्स्यामि राजन् सर्वात्मना जीवितं त्यज्य वीर।।१०
en: These heroes are not to be so easily vanquished; they entertain feelings of the bitterest hostility for you, and are more ever swelling with their powers. Yet O monarch, I will, with all my soul fight these heroes to the bitter end.

sn: रणे तवार्थाय महानुभाव न जीवितं रक्ष्यतमं ममाद्य। सर्वांस्तवार्थाय सदेवदैत्यान् घोरान् दहेयं किमु शत्रुसेनाम्॥
en: For your sake, O generous hero this day will I have no regard for my life in battle. For your sake, will I consume all the regions with their myriad celestial and Daityas, what to speak of your enemies?

sn: तान् पाण्डवान् योधयिष्यामि राजन प्रियं च ते सर्वमहं करिष्ये। श्रुत्यैव चैतद् वचनं तदानीं दुर्योधनः प्रीतमना बभूव॥
en: I will encounter, O king, the Pandavas, and there by encompass all that is agreeable to you”. Hearing these words Duryodhana became inspired with confidence, and his heart swelled in joy.
