sn: सर्वाणि सैन्यानि ततः प्रहृष्टो निर्गच्छतेत्याह नृपांश्च सर्वान्। तदाज्ञया तानि विनिर्ययुद्धेतं गजाश्वपादातरथायुतानि॥
en: Then with a delighted heart, he gave the word of command to the troops and all the assembled kings, saying Proceed. At his command the army consisting of chariots, steeds, foot-soldiers and elephant-riders, began to advance (in battle array).

sn: प्रहर्षयुक्तानि तु तानि राजन् महान्ति नानाविधशस्त्रवन्ति। स्थितानि नागाश्वपदातिमन्ति विरेजुराजौ तव राजन् बलानि॥
en: That extensive army of yours, O king, equipped with various sorts of implements of war, was filled with delight. O king, your army, teeming with elephant-riders, cavalrysoldiers and foot-soldiers arranged in battle order, appeared exceedingly beautiful.

sn: रधिष्ठिताः सैन्यगणास्त्वदीयाः। रथौघपादातगजाश्वसंधैः प्रयाद्भिराजौ विधिवत् प्रणुन्नैः॥
en: The division of tuskers composed of large numbers ad goaded on by skillful riders, appeared charging from all sides of the filed and your troops were also formed into order by many princely warriors, accomplished in the use of offensive and defensive weapons.

sn: समुद्धतं वै तरुणार्कवर्ण रजोबभौच्छादयन् सूर्यरश्मीन्। रेजुः पताका रथदन्तिसंस्था वातेरिता भ्राम्यमाणाः समन्तात्॥
en: A clouds of dust, resembling in hue the rays of the rising sun and intercepting from the view the sun itself-that was raise by the divisions of cars, elephants, infantry and cavalry as they moved over the filed in due order, appeared exceedingly beautiful.

sn: नानारङ्गाः मेधैर्युता विद्युतः खे यथैव। श्चकाशिरे दन्तिगणाः समन्तात्॥
en: Just as lightning, flashing amidst a mass of clouds in the firmament, appears beautiful, so the streamers of variegated hue mounted on cars and the backs of elephants, fluttering in the air and whirling along the welkin, appeared highly effulgent.

sn: समरे तत्र राजन् धनूंषि विस्फारयतां नृपाणां बभूव शब्दस्तुमुलोऽतिघोरः। विमथ्यतो देवमहासुरोधै यथार्णवस्यादियुगे तदानीम्॥
en: A dreadful and deafening din was created by monarchs stretching and twanging their bows-din that resembled the roar of the ocean, when in the Satya era, it was churned by the hosts of celestial and Asuras.

sn: तदुग्रनागं बहुरूपवर्णं तवात्मजानां समुदीर्णमेवम्। बभूव सैन्यं रिपुसैन्यहन्तु युगान्तमेघौघनिभं तदानीम्॥
en: At the moment, that army of your sons, uttering fierce war-cries, comprising in it combatants of divers hues, loO king so resplendent, and capable of slaughtering the enemy's host , appcared like the clan of clouds that are seen at the expiration of a Yuga.

description: Commencement of the seventh day's battle
sn: संजय उवाच अथात्मजं तव पुनर्गाङ्गेयो ध्यानमास्थितम्। अब्रवीद् भरतश्रेष्ठः सम्प्रहर्षकरं वचः॥
en: Sanjaya said Then, O foremost of the Bharatas, the son of Ganga, seeing your son plunged in thought, once more addressed these delightful words to him.

description: Commencement of the seventh day's battle
sn: अहं द्रोणश्च शल्यश्च कृतवर्मा च सात्वतः। अश्वत्थामा विकर्णश्च भगदत्तोऽथ सौबलः॥
en: “Myself, Drona, Shalya, Kritavarma, of the Satvata race, Ashvathama, Vikarna, Somadatta with Shindhus.

description: Commencement of the seventh day's battle
sn: विन्दानुविन्दावावन्त्यौ बाह्रीकः सह बाह्निकैः। त्रिगर्तराजो बलवान् मागधश्च सुदुर्जयः॥
en: And Vinda and Anuvinda of Avanti, and Balhika with the Balhikas, and the mighty king of the Trigartas and the formidable sovereign of the Magadhas,

description: Commencement of the seventh day's battle
sn: बृहद्बलश्च कौसल्यश्चित्रसेनो विविंशतिः। रथाश्च बहुसाहस्राः शोभनाश्च महाध्वजाः॥
en: Brihadabala the ruler of the Kosalas Chitrasena, Vivingshati, with many thousand of car-warriors, decorated with tall standards,

description: Commencement of the seventh day's battle
sn: देशजाश्च हया राजन् स्वारूढा हयसादिभिः। गजेन्द्राश्च मदोवृत्ताः प्रभिन्नकरटामुखाः॥
en: And a large number of country-born steeds, O king, mounted with excellent horse soldiers and innumerable huge elephants infuriate with shedding temporal juice from their temples and mouth.

description: Commencement of the seventh day's battle
sn: पादाताश्च तथा शूरा नानाप्रहरणध्वजाः। नानादेशसमुत्पन्नास्त्वदर्थे योद्धुमुद्यताः॥
en: And many heroic foot-soldiers accomplished in the use of various kinds of weapons, and born in various countries, are all prepared to fight for your sake.

description: Commencement of the seventh day's battle
sn: एते चान्ये च बहवस्त्वदर्थे त्यक्तजीविताः। देवानपि रणे जेतुं समर्था इति मे मतिः॥
en: These and many others, prepared to lay down their very lives for your sake, are I consider, capable of obtaining victory even over the gods in battle.

description: Commencement of the seventh day's battle
sn: अवश्यं हि मया राजंस्तव वाच्य हितं सदा। अशक्याः पाण्डवा जेतुं देवैरपि सवासवैः॥
en: It is my bounded duty, O king, to tell always what will be for your good. The Pandavas are incapable of being vanquished even by the very gods led by Vasava himself.

description: Commencement of the seventh day's battle
sn: वासुदेवसहायाश्च महेन्द्रसमविक्रमाः। सर्वथाऽहं तु राजेन्द्र करिष्ये वचनं तव॥
en: They are supported by the son of Vasudeva himself in battle, and are endued with prowess equal to that of the great Indra himself. But, O foremost of kings, I will ever carry out your commands.

description: Commencement of the seventh day's battle
sn: पाण्डवांश्च रणे जेष्ये मां वा जेष्यन्ति पाण्डवाः। एकमुक्त्वा ददावस्मै विशल्यकरणी शुभाम्॥
en: Either I will conquer the Pandavas in battle, or they will conquer my”. Having thus spoken, Bhishma gave to Duryodhana the excellent herb called Vishalya Karanee, (that which kills all pain).

description: Commencement of the seventh day's battle
sn: ओषधीं वीर्यसम्पन्नां विशल्यश्चाभवत् तदा। ततः प्रभाते विमले स्वेन सैन्येन वीर्यवान्॥ अव्यूहत स्वयं व्यूह भीष्मो व्यूहविशारदः। मण्डलं मनुजश्रेष्ठो नानाशस्त्रसमाकुलम्॥
en: That most efficacious remedy for healing all wounds. Therewith your son cured himself of all his wounds. Then at the fair dawn, the most powerful Bhishma that foremost of men accomplished in the are of arraying troops, formed with his own troops, the array called Mandala, bristling with the glitter of various kings of weapons.

description: Commencement of the seventh day's battle
sn: सम्पूर्णं योधमुख्यैश्च तथा दन्तिपदातिभिः। रथैरनेकसाहौः समन्तात् परिवारितम्॥
en: The array teemed with excellent warriors, as also with tuskers and infantry and it was surrounded on all sides with many thousand cars.

description: Commencement of the seventh day's battle
sn: अश्ववृन्दैर्महद्भिश्च ऋष्टितोमरधारिभिः। नागे नागे रथाः सप्त सप्त चाश्वा रथे रथे॥
en: And with large division of cavalry armed with scimitars and lances. Near every elephants were stationed seven car-warriors, and near every car were placed seven horsemen,

description: Commencement of the seventh day's battle
sn: अन्वश्वं दश धानुष्का धानुष्के दश चर्मिणः। एवं व्यूढं महाराज तव सैन्यं महारथैः॥
en: Behind every horsemen were stationed ten bowmen, and behind each bowman were placed seven foot-soldiers. Thus, O monarch, your troops urged by mighty and great carwarriors.

description: Commencement of the seventh day's battle
sn: स्थितं रणाय महते भीष्मेण युधि पालितम्। दशाश्वानां सहस्राणि दन्तिनां च तथैव च॥
en: Stood ready for the fierce encounter being protected by Bhishma. Then a thousand horseman, and as many tuskers. on

description: Commencement of the seventh day's battle
sn: रथानामयुतं चापि पुत्राश्च तव दंशिताः। चित्रसेनादयः शूरा अभ्यरक्षन् पितामहम्॥
en: And ten thousand chariots, along with your heroic sons, all accounted in mail, headed by Chitrasena, supported the grandsire.

description: Commencement of the seventh day's battle
sn: रक्ष्यमाणः स तैः शूरैर्गोप्यमानाश्च तेन ते। संनद्धाः समदृश्यन्त राजानश्च महाबलाः॥
en: It was seen that as Bhishma was supported by those heroic warriors themselves endued with great strength and clad in mail they were in their turn protect by the grandsire.

description: Commencement of the seventh day's battle
sn: दुर्योधनस्तु समरे दंशितो रथमास्थितः। व्यराजत श्रिया जुष्टो यथा शक्रस्त्रिविष्टपे॥
en: Duryodhana also that battlefield, occupying his car and clad in mail, and endued with all grace, looked beautiful like Indra himself in paradise.

description: Commencement of the seventh day's battle
sn: ततः शब्दो महानासीत् पुत्राणां तव भारत। रथघोषश्च विपुलो वादित्राणां च निस्वनः॥
en: Then, O Bharata, loud were the war cries uttered by your sons, and defending was clatter of chariots and the sound of the musical instruments.

description: Commencement of the seventh day's battle
sn: भीष्मेण धार्तराष्ट्राणां व्यूढः प्रत्युङ्मुखो युधि। मण्डलः स महाव्यूहो दुर्भेद्योऽमित्रघातनः॥
en: Then that mighty and impenetrable Mandala, array of those slayers of enemies viz., the sons of Dhritarashtra, formed by Bhishma himself, began to march forward facing the west.

description: Commencement of the seventh day's battle
sn: सर्वतः शुशुभे राजन् रणेऽरीणां दुरासदः। मण्डलं तु समालोक्य व्यूहं परमदुर्जयम्॥
en: Invulnerable in battle by the enemies, O monarch, that array appeared beautiful in every pare. Then beholding that formidable Mandala, array.

description: Commencement of the seventh day's battle
sn: स्वयं युधिष्ठिरो राजा वज्रं व्यूहमथाकरोत्। तथा व्यूढेष्वनीकेषु यथास्थानमवस्थिताः॥
en: King Yudhishthira himself formed his troops in the array known as Vajra. Thus when the troops were thus formed into battle array, and were stationed in proper ranks.

description: Commencement of the seventh day's battle
sn: रथिनः सादिनः सर्वे सिंहनादमथानदन्। बिभित्सवस्ततो व्यूहं निर्ययुयुद्धकाक्षिणः॥
en: The car-warriors and cavalry soldiers uttered their war-cries (resembling leonine roars). Then, desirous of battle fierce warriors began to leave their ranks.

description: Commencement of the seventh day's battle
sn: इतरेतरतः शूराः सहसैन्याः प्रहारिणः। भारद्वाजो ययौ मत्स्यं द्रौणिश्चापि शिखण्डिनम्॥
en: And those heroes supported by their respective division, began to smite down one another. The son of Bharadvaja encoun the ruler of the Matsyas, and the son of Drona engaged Shikhandin.

description: Commencement of the seventh day's battle
sn: स्वयं दुर्योधनो राजा पार्षतं समुपाद्रवत्। नकुलः सहदेवश्च मद्रराजनमीयतुः॥
en: King Duryodhana, himself rushed against the son of Prishata; the twins Nakula and Sahadeva proceeded against the king of the Madras.

description: Commencement of the seventh day's battle
sn: विन्दानुविन्दावावन्त्याविरावन्तमभिद्रुतौ। सर्वे नृपास्तु समरे धनंजयमयोधयन्॥
en: Vinda and Anuvinda from Avanti went against king Iravat. All the other monarchs engaged Dhananjaya in battle.

description: Commencement of the seventh day's battle
sn: भीमसेनो रणे यान्तं हार्दिक्यं समवारयत्। चित्रसेनं विकर्णं च तथा दुर्मर्षणं विभुः॥ आर्जुनिः समरे राजंस्तव पुत्रानयोधयत्। प्राग्ज्योतिषोमहेष्वासोहैडिम्बं राक्षसोत्तमम्॥
en: Putting forth all his exertions Bhimasena checked the son of Hridika in battle. Endued with great prowess Arjuna's son, O king engaged in battle, your sons viz., Chitrasena Vikarna, and Durmarshana. Against that fierce bow-man, viz., the ruler of the Pragjyotishas, Hidimba, the ruler of the Rakshasas.

description: Commencement of the seventh day's battle
sn: अभिदुद्राव वेगेन मत्तो मत्तमिव द्विपम्। अलम्बुषस्तदा राजन् सात्यकिं युद्धदुर्मदम्॥ ससैन्यं समरे क्रुद्धो राक्षस: समुपाद्रवत्। भूरिश्रवा रणे यत्तो धृष्टकेतुमयोधयत्॥
en: Rushed with impetuosity, like an infuriate elephants mecting a compeer in the same state. Then O monarch, the Rakshasa Alambusha excited with wrath rushed in that battle, against Satyaki invincible in battle surrounded though he was with his own division. Exerting himself well, Bhurishravas engaged in that conflict Dhrishtaketu.

description: Commencement of the seventh day's battle
sn: श्रुतागुषं च राजानं धर्मपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः। चेकितानश्च समरे कृपमेवान्वयोधयत्॥
en: Yudhishthira, the son of Dharma, engaged king Shrutayush; and in that battle Chekitana fought with Kripa.

description: Commencement of the seventh day's battle
sn: शेषाः प्रतियुर्यत्ता भीष्ममेव महारथम्। ततो राजसमूहास्ते परिवQर्धनंजयम्॥
en: The rest putting forth all their endeavors advanced against the mighty car-warrior Bhima. Thereafter thousand of monarchs surrounded Dhananjaya on all sides.

description: Commencement of the seventh day's battle
sn: शक्तितोमरनाराचगदापरिघपाणयः। अर्जुनोऽथ भृशं क्रुद्धो वार्ष्णेयमिदमब्रवीत्॥
en: Wielding in their hands dares, lances arrows, maces, and bludgeons; threat, highly enraged, Arjuna addressed the descendant of the Vrishni race (Krishna) saying:

description: Commencement of the seventh day's battle
sn: पश्य माधव सैन्यानि धार्तराष्ट्रस्य संयुगे। व्यूढानि व्यूहविदुषा गाङ्गेयेन महात्मना॥
en: "Behold, O Madhava, the troops of the sons of Dhritarashtra formed in battle array by the high-souled son of Ganga, who is versed in all the modes of forming soldiers in battle array,

description: Commencement of the seventh day's battle
sn: युद्धाभिकामाशूरांश्च पश्य माधव दंशितान्। त्रिगर्तराजं सहितं भ्रातृभिः पश्य केशव।॥
en: Behold also, O Madhava, innumerable heroes all ardently longing for battle. Behold also, O Keshava, the king of the Trigartas supported by his brothers.

description: Commencement of the seventh day's battle
sn: अद्यैतान् नाशयिष्यामि पश्यतस्ते जनार्दन। य इमे मां यदुश्रेष्ठ योद्धुकामा रणाजिरे॥
en: Today, before your very eyes, I will O Janardana, slay all these, O foremost of the Yadus, who are desirous of fighting with me in the battle".

description: Commencement of the seventh day's battle
sn: एतदुक्त्वा तु कौन्तेयो धनुर्ध्यामवमृज्य च। ववर्ष शरवर्षाणि नराधिपगणान् प्रति॥
en: Having thus spoken, the on of Kunti, rubbing his bow-string poured an arrow downpour on those hosts of kings.

description: Commencement of the seventh day's battle
sn: तेऽपि तं परमेष्वासाः शरवर्षैरपूरयन्। तडागं वारिधाराभिर्यथा प्रावृषि तोयदाः॥
en: Those fierce bowmen also covered him in return with showers of shafts, just as clouds, in the season of rain, fill the tanks with showers of rain.

description: Commencement of the seventh day's battle
sn: हाहाकारो महानासीत् तव सैन्ये विशाम्पते। छाद्यमानौ रणे कृष्णौ शरैर्दृष्ट्वा महारणे॥
en: Then, O ruler of men, when in that great battle the two Krishna's were seen to be covered with fast-falling arrows, loud shouts of "Oh!” “Oh!” were heard in your troops.

description: Commencement of the seventh day's battle
sn: देवा देवर्षयश्चैव गन्धर्वाश्च सहोरगैः। विस्मयं परमं जग्मुर्दृष्ट्वा कृष्णो तथागतौ॥
en: The celestial, the divine divine sages, the Gandharvas, and the mighty reptiles, were all overwhelmed with amazement beholding Krishna and Arjuna thus situated.

description: Commencement of the seventh day's battle
sn: ततः क्रुद्धोऽर्जुनो राजन्नन्द्रमस्त्रमुदैरयत्। तत्राद्भुतमपश्याम विजयस्य पराक्रमम्॥
en: Thereafter waxing worth, Arjuna invoked, O king, the weapon called Indra: then wonderful was the prowess that we beheld of Vijaya.

description: Commencement of the seventh day's battle
sn: शस्त्रवृष्टिं परैर्मुक्ता शरौधैर्यदवारयत्। न च तत्राप्यनिर्भिन्नः कश्चिदासीद् विशाम्पते॥
en: In as much as he baffled the thick shower of arrows discharged by his enemies with myriad of shafts shot by himself. There was none, O ruler of men, that was not wounded.

description: Commencement of the seventh day's battle
sn: तेषां राजसहस्राणां हयानां दन्तिनां तथा। द्वाभ्यां त्रिभिः शरैश्चान्यान् पार्थो विव्याध मारिष॥
en: Among those thousands of kings, steeds and tuskers. The rest, O sire, the son Pritha pierced, each with two or three shafts.

description: Commencement of the seventh day's battle
sn: ते हन्यमानः पार्थेन भीष्मं शान्तनवं ययुः। अगाधे मज्जमानानां भीष्मः पोतोऽभवत् तदा॥
en: While being thus slaughtered by the son of Pritha, they sought protection from the son of Shantanu, and then Bhishma became the rescuer of those warriors who resembled men sinking in the fathomless deep.

description: Commencement of the seventh day's battle
sn: आपतद्भिस्तु तैस्तत्र प्रमग्नं तावकं बलम्। संचुक्षुभे महाराज वातैरिव महार्णवः॥
en: Then those flying and broken ranks of your arniy, moving and falling back upon the division of Bhima, created a great confusion in the latter ranks, like the raging tempest agitating the mighty main.

sn: संजय उवाच तथा प्रवृत्ते संग्रामे निवृत्ते च सुशर्मणि। भग्नेषु चापि वीरेषु पाण्डवेन महात्मना॥
en: Sanjaya said When the battle thus raged, when Susharma had turned away from the battle when the highsouled son of Pandu (Arjuna) had broken your ranks,

sn: क्षुभ्यमाणे बले तूर्णं सागरप्रतिमे तव। प्रत्युद्याते च गाङ्गेये त्वरितं विजयं प्रति॥
en: When your army resembling the mighty main had been greatly agitated, and when the son of Ganga had swiftly advanced towards Vijaya,

sn: दृष्ट्वा दुर्योधनो राजा रणे पार्थस्य विक्रमम्। त्वरमाणः समभ्येत्य सर्वांस्तानब्रवीनृपान्॥
en: King Duryodhana, beholding the prowess of the son of Pritha in that battle hastily approaching all those kings thus addressed them all:

sn: तेषां तु प्रमुखे शूरं सुशर्माणं महाबलम्। मध्ये सर्वस्य सैन्यस्य भृशं संहर्षयन्निव॥
en: Also, addressing the heroic Susharma endued with great strength, and stationed at their head, Duryodhana said these words, amidst all the soldiers, impairing delight to them all.

sn: एष भीष्मः शान्तनवो योद्धुकामो धनंजयम्। सर्वात्मना कुरुश्रेष्ठस्त्यक्त्वा जीवितमात्मनः॥
en: This Bhishma, this son of Shantanu, this foremost of the Kurus, has resolved to fight with Dhananjaya, heedless of his very life and to the best of his abilities,

sn: तं प्रयान्तं रणे वीरं सर्वसैन्येन भारतम्। संयत्ताः समरे सर्वे पालयध्वं पितामहम्॥
en: Do you all, putting forth all your energies in battle, and supported by your respective division, protect the grandsire of the Bharatas, as he rushes against the army of the enemy.

sn: बाढमित्येवमुक्त्वा तु तान्यनीकानि सर्वशः। नरेन्द्राणां महाराज समाजग्मुः पितामहम्॥
en: Saying 'Yea' all those divisions, let by foremost of kings, O mighty monarch moved near the grandsire.

sn: ततः प्रयात: सहसा भीष्मः शान्तनवोऽर्जुनम्। रणे भारतयामायन्तमाससाद महाबलः॥
en: Thereupon the son of Shantanu viz., Bhishma, while thus advancing suddenly encountered the mighty Arjuna of the Bharata race, coming towards himself.

sn: महाश्वेताश्वयुक्तेन भीमवानरकेतुना। महता मेघनादेन रथेनातिविराजता।॥ समरे सर्वसैन्यानामुपयान्तं धनंजयम्। अभवत् तुमुलो नादो भयादृष्ट्वा किरीटिनम्॥
en: Riding on his highly resplendent chariot that bore the standard marked with the emblem of the mighty ape to which were yoked mighty white steeds and that produced a clatter resembling the rumble of clouds. Beholding the diadem-decked Dhananjaya rush to battle, all your troops seized with panic, set up a dreadful uproar.

sn: अभीषुहस्तं कृष्णं च दृष्ट्वाऽऽदित्यमिवापरम्। मध्यंदिनगतं संख्ये न शेकुः प्रतिवीक्षितुम्॥
en: Beholding Krishna resembling another Aditya and holding the reins in his hands, look like the sun in the meridian, your soldiers were unable to fix their eyes on him.

sn: तथा शान्तनवं भीष्मं श्वेताश्वं श्वेतकार्मुकम्। न शेकुः पाण्डवा द्रष्टुं श्वेतं ग्रहमिवोदितम्॥
en: So also the troops of the Pandavas were unable to gaze at Bhishma the son of Shantanu, borne by white steeds, holding a white bow, and loO king like the white planet (Shukra) rising in the skies.

sn: स सर्वतः परिवृतस्त्रिगर्तेः सुमहात्मभिः। भ्रातृभिः सह पुत्रैश्च तथान्यैश्च महारथैः॥
en: He was also surrounded on all sides by the Trigartas of high-soul, along with their brothers, sons, and many other car-warrior.

sn: भारद्वाजस्तु समरे मत्स्यं विव्याध पत्रिणा। ध्वजं चास्य शरेणाजौ धनुश्चैकेन चिच्छिदे॥
en: Meanwhile the son of Bharadvaja in that conflict, pierced the king of the Matsyas with one winged arrow; and he cut down the bow and the standard of the latter with one shaft each.

sn: तदपास्य धनुश्छिन्नं विराटो वाहिनीपतिः। अन्यदादत्त वेगेन धनुर्भारसहं दृढम्॥
en: Thereupon Virata the leader of a division leaving aside his served bow, hastily grasped another of tougher make and capable of bearing great stain.

sn: शरांश्चाशीविषाकाराज्वलितान् पन्नगानिव। द्रोणं त्रिभिश्च विव्याध चतुर्भिश्चास्य वाजिनः॥
en: As also, arrows of the shape of snakes of virulent poison, and resembling blazing serpents. In return, he pierced Drona with three shafts, his steeds with four,

sn: ध्वजमेकेन विव्याध सारथिं चास्य पञ्चभिः। धनुरेकेषुणाविध्यत् तत्राक्रुध्यद् द्विजर्षभः॥
en: His standard with one, and his charioteer with five. Virata also pierced the bow of Drona with one shaft. Thereupon the foremost of the regenerates, Drona, waxed irascible.

sn: तस्य द्रोणोऽवधीदश्वाशरैः संनतपर्वभिः। अष्टाभिर्भरतश्रेष्ठ सूतमेकेन पत्रिणा॥
en: Thereafter with eight straight-knotted shaft, Drona slew Virata's steeds, and, O foremost of the Bharatas, his charioteer also with one shaft furnished with wings.

sn: स हताश्वादवप्लुत्य स्यन्दनाद्धतसारथिः। आरुरोह रथं तूर्णं पुत्रस्य रथिनां वरः॥
en: Thereat that foremost of car-warrior viz., Virata, jumping down from his chariot of which the driver and the steeds had been slain, swiftly ascended the car of Sankha.

sn: ततस्तु तौ पितापुत्रौ भारद्वाजं रथे स्थितौ। महता शरवर्षेण वारयामासतुर्बलात्॥
en: Then, the father and the son (Virata and Sankha) riding on the same car, putting forth all their energies, endeavored to check the son of Bharadvaja with a mighty shower of arrows.

sn: भारद्वाजस्ततः क्रुद्धः शरमाशीविषोपमम्। चिक्षेप समरे तूर्णं शङ्ख प्रति जनेश्वर॥
en: Thereupon that highly-powerful son of Bharadvaja, waxing worth, with great lightness (of hand) hurled, in that battle, a shaft resembling a snake of virulent venom, at Sankha.

sn: स तस्य हृदयं भित्त्वा पीत्वा शोणितमाहवे। जगाम धरणी बाणो लोहितार्द्रवरच्छदः॥
en: That arrow, penetrating through Shankha's heart and drinking his life, blood, struck on the ground with its body rocked in the crimson fluid.

sn: स पपात रणे तूर्णं भारद्वाजशराहतः। धनुस्त्यक्त्वा शरांश्चैव पितुरेव समीपतः॥
en: Pierced by the shaft of Bharadvaja's son, Sankha quickly dropped down from his car, loosing hold of his bow and arrows and before the very presence of his father.

sn: हतं तमात्मजं दृष्ट्वा विराट: प्राद्रवद् भयात्। उत्सृज्य समरे द्रोणं व्यात्ताननमिवान्तकम्॥
en: Beholding his own son slain, Virata, fled out of fear, leaving Drona in battle who then looked like Death himself with yawning jaws.

sn: भारद्वाजस्ततस्तूर्ण पाण्डवानां महाचमूम्। दारयामास समरे शतथोऽथ सहस्रशः॥ शिखण्डी तु महाराज द्रौणिमासाद्य संयुगे। आजधान भ्रुवोर्मध्ये नाराचैस्त्रिभिराशुगैः॥
en: Thereafter in that battle, the son of Bharadvaja resisted, by hundreds and by thousand the mighty army belonging to the sons of Pandu. Shikhandin also, O mighty sovereign encountering the son of Drona in the conflict, wounded him between the brows with three swift coursing long shafts.

sn: स बभौ रथशार्दूलो ललाटे संस्थितैस्त्रिभिः। शिखरैः काञ्चनमयैर्मेरुस्त्रिभिरिवोच्छ्रितैः॥
en: With those three arrows stuck on his forehead, that foremost of men (Drona's son) appeared beautiful like the Meru mountain decked with three golden peaks towering high.

sn: अश्वत्थामा ततः क्रुद्धो निमेषार्धाच्छिखण्डिनः। ध्वजं सूतमथो राजंस्तुरगानायुधानि च॥ शरैर्बहुभिराच्छिद्य पातयामास संयुगे। स हताश्वादवप्लुत्य रथाद् वै रथिनां वरः॥
en: Thereupon waxing worth, within half the lime taken up by the wink, Ashvathama cut off in that combat Shikhandin's Shikhandin's charioteer, standard, horses and weapons covering them, O king, with innumerable arrows, then that foremost of car-warriors jumped down from the car of which, the steeds had been slain.

sn: खङ्गमादाय सुशितं विमलं च शरावरम्। श्येनवद् व्यचरत् क्रुद्धः शिखण्डी शत्रुतापनः॥
en: Grasping a whetted and effulgent sword and buckler. Then that afflicter of foes, namely Shikhandin, waxing wroth began to move about on the field of battle like a hawk.

sn: सखड्गस्य महाराज चरतस्तस्य संयुगे। नान्तरं ददृशे द्रौणिस्तदद्भुतमिवाभवत्॥
en: As he (Shikhandin) whirled about on the field, O mighty monarch, Drona's son could not find any vulnerable point, and this seemed indeed very wonderful.

sn: ततः शरसहस्राणि बहूनि भरतर्षभ। प्रेषयामास समरे द्रौणिः परमकोपनः॥
en: Then, O foremost of the Bharatas, Drona's son inflamed with rage, sped, in that battle many thousands of shafts (against Shikhandin).

sn: तामापतन्ती समरे शरवृष्टिं सुदारुणाम्। असिना तीक्ष्णधारेण चिच्छेद बलिनां वरः॥
en: Then that foremost of those possessed of prowess (Shikhandin) cut off with his sharpedged sword the dreadful shower of arrows that was falling fast upon him.

sn: ततोऽस्य विमलं द्रौणिः शतचन्द्रं मनोरमम्। चर्माच्छिनदसिं चास्य खण्डयामास संयुगे॥
en: Thereafter the son of Drona cut off Shikhandin's glittering shield charming with a hundred moon, then in that battle he also shattered into pieces the latter's sword.

sn: शितैस्तु बहुशो राजंस्तं च विव्याध पत्रिभिः। शिखण्डी तु ततः खङ्गं खण्डितं तेन सायकैः॥ आविध्य व्यसृजत् तूर्णं ज्वलन्तमिव पन्नगम्। तमापतन्तं सहसा कालानलसमप्रभम्॥
en: The O monarch he (Drona's son) pierced Shikhandin with myriad's of shafts furnished with wings. Thereat Shikhandin whirling the fragment of his sword splintered by the arrows (of Drauni), hurled it at the latter, like a blazing serpent. Beholding that fragment of the sword that then resembled the all destructive fire (at the end of a Yuga) come swiftly toward himself.

sn: चिच्छेद समरे द्रौणिर्दर्शयन् पाणिलाघवम्। शिखण्डिनं च विव्याध शरैर्बहुभिरायसैः॥
en: The son of Drona cut in off in the battle, displaying great lightness of hand then also he pierced Shikhandin with many shafts made wholly of iron.

sn: शिखण्डी तु भृशं राजस्ताङ्यमानः शितैः शरैः। आरुरोह रथं तूर्णं माधवस्य महात्मनः॥
en: Thus wounded sore with sharp arrows, Shikhandin quickly ascended, O monarch, the car of the high-souled Satyaki, that scion of the dynasty of Madhu.

sn: सात्यकिश्चापि संक्रुद्धौ राक्षसं क्रूरमाहवे। अलम्बुषं शरैस्तीक्ष्णैर्विव्याध बलिना वरः॥
en: Then Satyaki, inflamed with wrath in that conflict, covered, on all sides, the ruthless Rakshasas Alambusha, with his dreadful arrows.

sn: राक्षसेन्द्रस्ततस्तस्य धनुश्चिच्छेद भारत। अर्धचन्द्रेण समरे तं च विव्याध सायकैः॥
en: Thereat, O Bharata, that foremost of the Rakshasas cut off Satyaki's bow with a crescent-shaped arrow in that combat, and pierced the latter with numerous arrows.

sn: मायां च राक्षसी कृत्वा शरवर्षैरवाकिरत्। तत्राद्भुतमपश्याम शैनेयस्य पराक्रमम्॥
en: Spreading an illusion through his Rakshasas prowess, he covered Satyaki with an arrow downpour. Then we did behold the wonderful prowess of the grandson of Shini.

sn: असम्भ्रमस्तु समरे वध्यमानः शितैः शरैः। ऐन्द्रमस्त्रं च वार्ष्णेयो योजयामास भारत॥
en: In as much as though pierced in that battle, with those sharp arrows, he did not flinch in the least. Then that descendant of the Vrishni race, placed on his bow string the Indra weapon,

sn: विजयाद् यदनुप्राप्तं माधवेन यशस्विना। तदस्त्रं भस्मसात् कृत्वा मायां तां राक्षसीं तदा॥
en: Which that renowned scion of Madhus race had obtained from Vijaya himself. That weapon then reducing into ashes the Rakshasis illusion,

sn: अलम्बुषं शरैरन्यैरभ्याकिरत सर्वतः। पर्वतं वारिधाराभिः प्रावृषीव बलाहकः॥
en: Poured a shower of dreadful shafts of Alambusha from all sides, like clouds in the rainy season covering the mountain top with (thick showers of rain).

sn: तत् तथा पीडितं तेन माधवेन यशस्विना। प्रदुद्राव भयाद् रक्षस्त्यक्त्वा सात्यकिमाहवे॥
en: Thus afflicted sore by that high souled scion of Madhu's race, the Rakshasa fled out of fear, leaving Satyaki (victorious) on the field.

sn: तमजेयं राक्षसेन्द्रं संख्ये मघवता अपि। शैनेयः प्राणदज्जित्वा योधानां तव पश्यताम्॥
en: Then having vanquished that foremost of the Rakshasas who could not be vanquished even by Indra himself the grandson of Shini uttered a loud roar, even before the very eyes of your warriors.

sn: न्यहनत् तावकांश्चापि सात्यकिः सत्यविक्रमः। निशितैर्बहुभिर्बाणैस्तेऽद्रवन्त भयार्दिताः॥
en: Then Satyaki of prowess incapable of being baffled, began to slaughter your warriors with many well-sharpened shafts; and afflicted with fear these latter began to break away.

sn: एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु द्रुपदस्यात्मजो बलि। धृष्टद्युम्नो महाराज पुत्रं तव जनेश्वरम्॥ छादयामास समरे शरैः संनतपर्वभिः। स च्छाद्यमानो विशिखैद्धृष्टद्युम्नेन भारत॥
en: Meanwhile, that mighty son of Drupada, namely, Dhrishtadyumna, O king, in that battle covered your son, the ruler of men, with innumerable straight, knotted shafts. This covered with the shot by Dhrishtadyumna, O Bharata.

sn: विव्यथे न च राजेन्द्र तव पुत्रो जनेश्वर। धृष्टद्युम्नं च समरे तूर्णं विव्याध पत्रिभिः॥ षष्ट्या च त्रिंशता चैव तदद्भुतमिवाभवत्। तस्य सेनापतिः क्रुद्धो धनुश्चिच्छेद मारिष॥
en: Your son, that lord of men, neither wavered nor was agitated with fear, on the other hand, he quickly pierced Dhrishtadyumna with arrows in that conflict. Numbering sixty (first) and thirty (next). all this seemed highly wonderful. Thereupon the generalissimo of the Pandavas, waxing wroth, O Bharata, cut off Duryodhana's bow.

sn: हयांश्च चतुरः शीघ्रं निजघान महाबलः। शरैश्चैनं सुनिशितैः क्षिप्रं विव्याध सप्तभिः॥
en: Also that mighty car-warrior slew the four steeds of the latter in battle, and quickly pierced his person with seven shafts of exceeding sharpness. arrows

sn: स हताश्वान्महाबाहुरवप्लुत्य रथाद् बली। पदातिरसिमुद्यम्य प्राद्रवत् पार्षतं प्रति॥
en: Thereupon that mighty-armed Duryodhana endued with great strength jumping down from his car the steeds of which were slain, rushed on foot towards Prishata's son with sword uplifted.

sn: शकुनिस्तं समभ्येत्य राजगृद्धी महाबलः। राजानं सर्वलोकस्य रथमारोपयत् स्वकम्॥
en: At that moment the highly powerful Shakuni desirous of rescuing the king, approached the spot and placed the monarch on his car before the presence of all warriors.

sn: ततो नृपं पराजित्य पार्षतः परवीरहा। न्यहनत् तावकं सैन्यं वज्रपाणिरिवासुरान्॥
en: Then vanquishing the Kuru king, Prishata's son that slayer of hostile heroes, began to slaughter your troops like the wielder of the thunder-bolt slaying the Asuras.

sn: कृतवर्मा रणे भीमं शरैरार्छन्महारथः। प्रच्छादयामास च तं महामेघो रविं यथा।॥
en: Then in that battle, Kritavarma afflicted the inighty car-warrior Bhima, virtually covering the latter (with arrows), like masses of clouds covering the sun.

sn: ततः प्रहस्य समरे भीमसेनः परंतपः। प्रेषयामास संक्रुद्धः सायकान् कृतवर्मणे॥
en: Thereupon that scorcher of foes Bhimasena, waxing irascible and smiling the while, shot, in that combat, myriad's of shafts towards Kritavarma.

sn: तैरर्चमानोऽतिरथः सात्वतः सत्यकोविदः। नाकम्पत महाराज भीमं चार्मोच्छितैः शरैः॥
en: Wounded with those arrows that Atiratha of the Satvata race swelling with all prowess, quaked not, O mighty monarch but, on the other hand, pierced Bhima with many keen pointed arrows.

sn: तस्याश्वांश्चतुरो हत्वा भीमसेनो महारथः। सारथिं पातयामास सध्वजं सुपरिष्कृतम्॥
en: Thereat the highly powerful Bhimasena slaying Kritavarma's four steeds felled his charioteer and his well cleansed standard.

sn: शरैर्बहुविधैश्चैनमाचिनोत् परवीरहा। शकलीकृतसर्वाङ्गो हताश्वः प्रत्यदृश्यत॥
en: Then that slayer of hostile heroes (Bhima) pierced Kritavarma with arrows of diverse sorts; thus mangled and mutilated with arrows, the latter looked like a porcupine.

sn: हताश्वश्च ततस्तूर्णं वृषकस्य रथं ययौ। श्यालस्य ते महाराज तव पुत्रस्य पश्यतः॥
en: Thereafter leaving his chariot of which the steeds were slain, Kritavarma ascended the car of your brother-in-law Vrishka, O monarch, before the yes of your son.

sn: भीमसेनोऽपि संक्रुद्धस्तव सैन्यमुपाद्रवत्। निजधान च संक्रुद्धो दम्डपाणिरिवान्तकः॥
en: Bhimasena also, inflamed with wrath rushed at your troops; and excited to the highest pitch of fury he began to slaughter them like the god of Death himself wiclding his mace in his hands.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच बहूनि हि विचित्राणि द्वैस्थानि स्म संजय। पाण्डूनां मामकैः सार्धमश्रौषं तव जल्पतः॥
en: Dhritarashtra said I have heard, O Sanjaya as you have discoursed on, of the numerous and wonderful single combats fought between my warriors and those of the sons of Pandu.

sn: न चैव मामकं किंचित् हृष्टं शंससि संजय। नित्यं पाण्डुसुतान् हृष्टानभग्नान् सम्प्रशंससि॥
en: But, O Sanjaya, you never speak of my soldiers being delightful (on such occasion). You always speak of the warriors of the Pandavas as cheerful and never routed.

sn: वै जीयमानान् विमनसो मामकान् विगतौजसः। वदसे संयुगे सूत दिष्टमेतन्न संशयः॥
en: You always speak of my warriors as depressed in mind, vanquished and shorn of energy in battle. O Suta, indubitably all this is brought about by Destiny.

sn: संजय उवाच यथाशक्तिं यथोत्साहं युद्धे चेष्टन्ति तावकाः। दर्शयानाः परं शक्त्या पौरुषं पुरुषर्षभ॥
en: Sanjaya said Your warriors strive in battle to the best of their strength and ardour, displaying, 0 foremost of the Bharatas, their manliness as much as possible.

sn: गङ्गायाः सुरनद्या स्वादु भूत्वा यथोदकम्। महोदधेर्गुणाभ्यासाल्लवणत्वं निगच्छति॥
en: Even as the very tasteful water of the celestial river Ganga flowing into that of the mighty main, aitains saline properties.

sn: तथा तत् पौरुषं राजंस्तावकानां परंतप। प्राप्य पाण्डुसुतान् वीरान् व्यर्थं भवति संयुगे॥
en: So also, O monarch, the mainlines of the illustrious warriors of your army opposed by that of the heroic sons of Pandu becomes baffled in battle.

sn: घटमानान् यथाशक्ति कुर्वाणान् कर्म दुष्करम्। न दोषेण कुरुश्रेष्ठ कौरवान् गन्तुमर्हसि॥
en: It behaves you not, O foremost of the Kurus, to attribute blame to your own warriors, who exert themselves to the best of their inighty and achieve feats that are difficult of being done so.

sn: तवापराधात् सुमहान् सपुत्रस्य विशाम्पते। पृथिव्याः प्रक्षयो घोरो यमराष्ट्रविवर्धनः॥
en: From your own fault, and from that of your son, ruler of men, this great and dreadful destruction ( of the creature of) the earth has come to pass, adding considerably to the population of Death's kingdom.

sn: आत्मदोषात् समुत्पन्नं शोचितुं नार्हसे नृप। न हि रक्षन्ति राजान: सर्वथाऽत्रापि जीवितम्॥
en: It behooves your not. O king, to grieve for what has come to pass in consequence of your own faults. The kings do not pay any the least regard to their lives in this battle.

sn: युद्धे सुकृतिनां लोकानिच्छन्तो वसुधाधिपाः। चमू विगाह्य युध्यन्ते नित्यं स्वर्गपरायणाः॥
en: The rulers of men (assembled on the filed), desire to attain to the regions of those that perform pious acts. always cherishing a desire for attaining paradise, they are fighting agitating the hostile army.

sn: पूर्वाह्ने तु महाराज प्रावर्तत जनक्षयः। तं त्वमेकमना भूत्वा शृणु देवासुरोपमम्॥
en: That afternoon, O mighty monarch a great destruction of creatures took place. Hear of me, with singleness of attention of that battle that ras.

sn: आवन्त्यौ तु महेष्वासौ महासेनौ महाबलौ। इरावन्तमभिप्रेक्ष्य समेयातां रणोत्कटौ॥
en: The two (royal) brothers from Avanti, both mighty bow-men, possessed of great might, and exceeding effulgence, and both formidable in battle, beholding Iravat, rushed at him.

sn: तेषां प्रववृते युद्धं सुमहल्लोमहर्षणम्। इरावांस्तु सुसंक्रुद्धो भ्रातरौ देवरूपिणौ॥ विव्याध निशितैस्तूर्णं शरैःसंनतपर्वभिः। तावेनं प्रत्यविध्येतां समरे चित्रयोधिनौ॥
en: Then the combat that was fought between them was dreadful and horripilating. thereupon Iravat waxing wrath, quickly pierced those two brothers of godly presence, with straight knotted shafts of exceeding sharpness. those two warriors versed in diverse odes of warfare pierced Iravat in return, in that battle,

sn: युध्यतां हि तथा राजन् विशेषो न व्यदृश्यत। यततां शत्रुनाशाय कृतप्रतिकृतैषिणाम्॥
en: As thcy fought on. O king, striking their best to slay their mutual foes and desirous of avenging what is done to one another, there could be found no distinction between them.

sn: इरावांस्तु ततो राजन्ननुविन्दस्य सायकैः। चतुरभिश्चतुरो वाहाननयद् यमसादनम्॥
en: Then in that conflict, Iravat, O king's with four arrows, dispatched the four steeds of Anuvinda to the regions of Death.

sn: भल्लाभ्यां च सुतीक्ष्णाभ्यां धनुः केतुं च मारिष। चिच्छेद समरे राजस्तदद्भुतमिवाभवत्॥
en: Also, O sire, with a couple of keen-aged broad-headed arrows, the former cut off the standard and bow of the latter in that battle. all this, O king, seemed to be wonderful.

sn: त्यक्त्वानुविन्दोऽथ रथं विन्दस्य रथमास्थितः। धनुर्गृहीत्वा परमं भारसाधनमुत्तमम्॥
en: Thereupon Anuvinda leaving his own car, ascended that of Vinda; thereafter he grasped an excellent bow of great toughness and capable of bearing a great strain.

sn: तावेकस्थो रणे वीरावावन्त्यौ रथिनां वरौ। शरान् मुमुग्रतुस्तूर्णमिरावति महात्मनि॥
en: Then those two foremost of car-warriors endued with heroism and riding on one and the same car, both belonging to the country of Avanti, began to shower incessantly arrows on the high-souled Iravat.

sn: ताभ्यां मुक्ता महावेगाः शराः काञ्चनभूषणाः। दिवाकरपथं प्राप्य च्छादयामासुरम्बरम्॥
en: Shot by them both, swift-fiying arrows decked with gold, intercepting the rays of the orb of the day, (literally) covered the sky.

sn: इरावांस्तु रणे क्रुद्धो भ्रातरौ तौ महारथौ। ववर्ष शरवर्षेण सारथिं चाप्यपातयत्॥
en: Thereupon, inflamed with wrath, Iravat poured an arrow downpour on the two brothers both mighty car-warriors; and he felled their charioteer.

sn: तस्मिंस्तु पतिते भूमौ गतसत्त्वे तु सारथौ! रथः प्रदुद्राव दिशः समुद्घान्तहयस्ततः॥
en: When deprived of life, the charioteer fell down on the earth, the chariot was dragged in all directions in consequence of its horses being unrestrained.

sn: तौ स जित्वा महाराज नागराजसुतासुतः। पौरुषं ख्यापयंस्तूर्णं व्यधमत् तव वाहिनीम्॥
en: Obtaining victory, O monarch, over the two brothers, the son of the daughter of the king of the Nagas displaying his inanliness, began speedily to spread havoc among your soldiers.

sn: सा वध्यमाना समरे धार्तराष्ट्री महाचमूः। वेगान् बहुविधांश्चक्रे विषं पीत्वेव मानवः॥
en: This slaughtered in battle, the mighty army of the sons of Dhritarashtra performed various movements like a man reeling through the effects of poisoning.

sn: हैडिम्बो राक्षसेन्द्रस्तु भगदत्तं समाद्रवत्। रथेनादित्यवर्णेन सध्वजेन महाबलः॥
en: Then the on of Hidimba, the foremost of the Rakshasas endued with great strength, riding on his chariot of solar has and furnished with a standard, rushed against Bhagadatta.

sn: ततः प्राग्ज्योतिषो राजा नागराज समास्थितः। यथा वज्रधरः पूर्वं संग्रामे तारकामये॥
en: Thereupon the ruler of the Pragjyotishas mounted on his princes of elephants like the wielder of the thunder bolt mounting on his Airavat in the days of yore at the time of the battle caused by the insult offered by Taraka.

sn: तत्र देवाः सगन्धर्वा ऋषयश्च समागताः। विशेषं न स्म विविदुईडिम्बभगदत्तयोः॥
en: Then there came the celestial along with the Gandharvas and the sages. They were unable to find out any destruction between the son of Hidimba and Bhagadatta.

sn: यथा सुरपतिः शक्रस्त्रासयामास दानवान्। तथैव समरे राजा द्रावयामास पाण्डवान्॥
en: As the lord of the celestial (Indra) waxing worth had struck terror into the hearts of the Danavas, so did also the ruler of the Pragjyotishas, O king, in that battle frighten and crush the Pandava troops.

sn: तेन विद्राव्यमाणास्ते पाण्डवाः सर्वतो दिशम्। त्रातारं नाभ्यगच्छन्तः स्वेष्वनीकेषु भारत॥
en: Thus routed by hiin on all directions, the Pandava troops, O Bharata, did not find, in their whole host, an one competent to save them.

sn: भैमसेनि रथस्थं तु तत्रापश्याम भारत। शेषा विमनसो भूत्वा प्राद्रवन्त महारथाः॥
en: We then only beheld the son of Bhimasena (Ghatotkacha), O Bharata riding on his car the rest of the car-warriors, with minds distracted (with fear) had fled (in all directions.

sn: निवृत्तेषु तु पाण्डूनां पुनः सैन्येषु भारत। आसीनिष्ठानका घोरस्तत सैन्यस्य संयुगे॥
en: Then, O Bharata, when the Pandava forces rallied, a dreadful and fierce roar was sent up by your troops in that battle.

sn: घटोत्कचस्ततो राजन् भगदत्त महारणे। शरैः प्रच्छादयामास मेरुं गिरिमिवाम्बुदः॥
en: Thereupon, O mighty monarch, in the fierce engagement that commenced Ghatotkacha covered Bhagadatta with a shower of arrows, like a rain cloud covering the Meru mountain with a downpour of rain.

sn: निहत्य ताशरान् राजा राक्षसस्य धनुश्च्युतान्। भैमसेनि रणे तूर्णं सर्वमर्मस्वताडयत्॥
en: Then king Bhagadatta, severing those arrows shot from the bow of the Rakshasas, in that combat quickly pierced the son of Bhimasena in all his vital parts.

sn: स ताड्यमानो बहुभिः शरैः संनतपर्वभिः। न विव्यथे राक्षसेन्द्रो भिद्यमान इवाचलः॥
en: Wounded with innumerable this straight jointed shafts, that foremost of the Rakshusas did not fight, (but stood firm) like a mountain though cleft open.

sn: तस्य प्राग्ज्योतिषः क्रुद्धस्तोमरांश्च चतुर्दश। प्रेषयामास समरे ताश्चिच्छेद स राक्षसः॥
en: The ruler of the Pragjyotishas inflamed with rage, in that battle sped fourteen Tomaras against the Rakshasas, who (easily) cut them off.

sn: स तांश्छित्त्वा महाबाहुस्तोमरान् निशितैः शरैः। भगदत्तं च विव्याध सप्तत्या कङ्कपत्रिभिः॥
en: Then that Rakshasa of mighty arms cutting off those Tomaras, pierced Bhagadatta with seventy shafts of exceeding sharpness, all resembling the thunderbolt of Heaven.

sn: ततः प्राग्ज्योतिषो राजा प्रहसन्निव भारत। तस्याश्वांश्चतुरः संख्ये पातयामास सायकैः॥
en: Thereupon the king of the Pragjyotishas, in that combat, as if smiling, dispatched, O Bharata, to death the four horses of the Rakshasas.

sn: स हताश्वे रथे तिष्ठन् राक्षसेन्द्रः प्रतापवान्। शक्तिं चिक्षेप वेगेन प्राग्ज्योतिषगजं प्रति॥
en: Standing on his car of which the steeds were slain, that foremost of the Rakshasas endued with prowess hurled at the elephants of Bhagadatta, s Shakti, with great force.

sn: तामापतन्ती सहसा हेमदण्डां सुवेगिनीम्। त्रिधा चिच्छेद नृपतिः सा व्यकीर्यत मेदिनीम्॥
en: Then the ruler of the Pragjyotishas cut off that Shakti falling with great veheinence and furnished with a golden staff, into three splinters and the Shakti fell shattered on the ground.

sn: शक्तिं विनिहतां दृष्ट्वा हैडिम्बः प्राद्रवद् भयात्। यथेन्द्रस्य रणात् पूर्वं नमुचिर्दैत्यसत्तमः॥
en: seeing his Shakti splintered into pieces, the son of Hidimba fled out of fear like Namuchi the foremost of the Daityas flying, in the days of yore, from the fight with Indra.

sn: तं विजित्य रणे शूरं विक्रान्तं ख्यातपौरुषम्। अजेयं समरे वीरं यमेन वरुणेन च॥
en: Obtaining victory, O king, in battle over that heroic and highly powerful Rakshasa of illustrious renown who is incapable of being vanquished evü by the god of Death and Varuna themselves.

sn: पाण्डवीं समरे सेनां सम्ममर्द स कुञ्जरः। यथा वनगजो राजन् मृनश्चरति पद्मिनीम्॥
en: Bhagadatta riding on his elephants crushed in that battle, the troops of the Pandavas, even like a wild elephants, that roves, O king, trampling lotus stems (underneath its huge feet).

sn: मद्रेश्वरस्तु समरे यमाभ्यां समसज्जत। स्वस्त्रीयौ छादयांचक्रे शरौः पाण्डुनन्दनौ॥
en: The ruler of the Madra encountered in battle the twins (Nakula and Sahadeva. He covered his two nephews, both sons of Pandu, with an arrow down pour.

sn: सहदेवस्तु समरे मातुलं दृश्य संगतम्। अवारयच्छरौघेण मेघो यद्वद् दिवाकरम्॥
en: Sahadeva finding himself encountered by his uncle in battle, shrouded him with a network of arrows, like clouds shrouding the solar orb.

sn: छाद्यमानः शरौघेण हृष्टरूपतरोऽभवत्। तयोश्चाप्यभवत् प्रीतिरतुला मातृकारणात्॥
en: Shrouded by that net-work of shafts the Madra king wore an appearance indicative of joy the twins also were greatly delighted for the sake of their mother.

sn: ततः प्रहस्य समरे नकुलस्य महारथः। अश्वांश्च चतुरो रांजश्चतुर्भिः सायकोत्तमैः॥ प्रेषयामास समरे यमस्य सदनं प्रति। हताश्वात् तु रथात् तूर्णमवप्लुत्य महारथः॥
en: Thereafter in that combat, that mighty carwarriors the Madra king, O king, with four excellent arrows dispatched smilingly Nakula's four steeds to the monsoon of Death. Then that mighty car-warrior Nakula jumping down from his car of which the horses were slain.

sn: आरुरोह ततो यानं भ्रातुरेव यशस्विनः। एकस्थौ तु रणे शूरो दृढे विक्षिप्य कार्मुकौ॥
en: Ascended the vehicle of his illustrious brother. Then in that battle the heroic, mounted on the same car, stretching their touch bows,

sn: मद्रराजरथं तूर्णं छादयामासतुः क्षणात्। स छाद्यमानो बहुभिः शरैः संनतपर्वभिः॥
en: Waxing irascible and becoming formidable in battle, covered the king of the Madras (with shafts). Covered with innumerable straightjointed arrows.

sn: स्वस्त्रीयाभ्यां नरव्याघ्रो नाकम्पत यथाऽचलः। प्रहसन्निव तां चापि शस्त्रवृष्टिं जघान ह॥
en: Shot by his nephews, that foremost of men (the Madra king) moved not, but stood still even like a mountain; then as if smiling, he baffled that shower of arrows.

sn: सहदेवस्ततः क्रुद्धः शरमुद्गृह्य वीर्यवान्। पद्रराजमभिप्रेक्ष्य प्रेषयामास भारत।॥
en: Thereupon the highly powerful Sahadeva, inflamed with wrath, grasping a dare, rushed at the ruler of Madras and then hurled it at him, O Bharata.

sn: स शरः प्रेषितस्तेन गरुडानिलवेगवान्। मद्रराजं विनिर्भिद्य निपपात महीतले॥
en: That dare shot by him and coursing swiftly like the Garuda himself, penetrating through the body of the Madra king, fell down on earth.

sn: स गाढविद्धो व्यथितो रथोपस्थे महारथः। निषसाद महाराज कश्मलं च जगाम ह॥
en: Thus deeply pierced, and smarting with pain, that mighty car-warrior squatted down on the terrace of his car, and O mighty monarch he was overwhelmed with a swoon.

sn: तं विसंज्ञं निपतितं सूतः सम्प्रेक्ष्य संयुगे। अपोवाह रथेनाजौ यमाभ्यामभिपीडितम्॥
en: In that battle, seeing him (the Madra king) i senseless and fallen on the car and afflicted by the twins, his charioteer drove him on his vehicle away from the field of battle.

sn: दृष्ट्वा मद्रेश्वररथं धार्तराष्ट्राः पराङ्मुखम्। सर्वे विमनसो भूत्वा नेदमस्तीत्यचिन्तयन्॥
en: The sons of Dhritarashtra beholding the car of the ruler of the Madras turn away from the field, were all depressed in mind and thought that he was no longer alive.

sn: निर्जित्य मातुलं संख्ये माद्रीपुत्रौ महारथौ। दध्मतुर्मुदितौ शङ्खौ सिंहनादं च नेदतुः॥
en: Obtaining victory in battle, over their uncle, the sons of Madri, greatly delighted blew their conchs and roared out their war cries.

sn: अभिदुद्रुवतुर्हष्टौ तव सैन्यं विशाम्पते। यथा दैत्यचमूं राजन्निन्द्रोपेन्द्राविवामरौ॥
en: Thereafter filled with delight, they rushed against your host, O ruler of men, like the immortals Indra and Upendra, O king, rushing against the host of the Daityas.

sn: संजय उवाच ततो युधिष्ठिरो राजा मध्यं प्राप्ते दिवाकरे। श्रुतायुषमभिप्रेक्ष्य प्रेषयामास वाजिनः॥
en: Sanjaya said Then when the sun shone on the meridian, king Yudhishthira, beholding Shrutayush, urged his own steeds towards him.

sn: अभ्यधावत् ततो राजा श्रुतायुषमरिंदमम्। विनिमन् सायकैस्तीक्ष्णैवभिनतपर्वभिः॥
en: Then the king rushed at Shrutayush, that subduer of foes, wounding the latter at same time with nine straight knotted shafts of exceeding sharpness.

sn: स संवार्य रणे राजा प्रेषितान् धर्मसूनुना। शरान् सप्त महेष्वासः कौन्तेयाय समार्पयत्॥
en: That king, that mighty bowman, (Shrutayush) resisting in battle, the shafts, shot at him by the son of Pandu, sped at Kunti's son a group of seven arrows.

sn: ते तस्य कवचं भित्त्वा पपुः शोणितमाहवे। असूनिव विचिन्वन्तो देहे तस्य महात्मनः॥
en: Those arrows penetrating through Yudhisthira's armour drank, in that battle, his life-blood, as if plucking out all vitality invigorating the frame of that high-souled warrior.

sn: पाण्डवस्तु भृशं क्रुद्धो विद्धस्तेन महात्मना। रणे वराहकर्णेन राजानं हृद्यविध्यत॥
en: Pierced deep by that illustrious sovereign, the son of Pandu, in that combat struck the former on his breast with an arrow resembling in shape the ear of a boar.

sn: अथापरेण भल्लेन केतुं तस्य महात्मनः। रथश्रेष्ठो रथात् तूर्णं भूमौ पार्थो न्यपातयत्॥
en: Then that foremost of car-warriors namely the son of Pritha, with another broad-headed shafts, quickly felled on the illustrious Shrutayush.

sn: केतुं विपतितं दृष्ट्वा श्रुतायुः स तु पार्थिवः। पाण्डवं विशिखैस्तीक्ष्णै राजन् विव्याध सप्तभिः॥
en: Then that ruler of earth Shrutayush, beholding his standard felled, pierced, O king, the son of Pandu with seven arrows of great sharpness.

sn: ततः क्रोधात् प्रजज्वाल धर्मपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः। यथा युगान्ते भूतानि दिधक्षुरिव पावकः॥
en: Then Yudhishthira the son of Dharma burnt with rage, like the fire that burns at the end of a Yuga consuming all creatures.

sn: क्रुद्धं तु पाण्डवं दृष्ट्वा देवगन्धर्वराक्षसाः। प्रविव्यथुमहाराज व्याकुलं चाप्यभूज्जगत्॥
en: Beholding the son of Pandu blaze forth in rage, the celestial, the Gandharvas, and the Rakshasas became afflicted O monarch, and the whole world was seized upon by anxiety.

sn: सर्वेषा चैव भूतानामिदमासीन्मनोगतम्। त्रील्लोकानद्य संक्रुद्धो नृपोऽयं धक्ष्यतीति वै॥
en: Then this thought prevailed in the minds of all beings present, namely 'This king, waxing worth, will today consume the triune world.'

sn: ऋषयश्चैव देवाश्च चक्रुः स्वस्त्ययनं महत्। लोकानां नृप शान्त्यर्थं क्रोधिते पाण्डवे तदा॥
en: Then, O king, when the son of Pandu was thus enraged, the Rishis and the celestial performed many benediction ceremonies for the peace of the worlds.

sn: स च क्रोधसमाविष्टः सृकिणी परिसंलिहन्। दधारात्मवपुर्घोरं युगान्तादित्यसंनिभम्॥
en: Then that king (Yudhishthira) possessed with anger and constantly licking the corners of his mouth, assumed a dreadful appears like that of the sun that rises at the end of a Yuga.

sn: ततः सैन्यानि सर्वाणि तावकानि विशाम्पते। निराशान्यभवंस्तत्र जीवितं प्रति भारत॥
en: one Thereupon, O ruler of men, all the warriors of your army, became despondent of their lives, O Bharata.

sn: स त धैर्मेण तं कोपं संनिवार्य महायशाः। श्रुतायुषः प्रचिच्छेद मुष्टिदेशे महाधनुः॥
en: But that highly-renowned (Yudhishthira) restraining that wrath of his, with patience, served the mighty bow of Shrutayush near the grasp.

sn: अथैनं छिन्नधन्वानं नाराचेन स्तनान्तरे। निर्बिभेद रणे राजा सर्वसैन्यस्य पश्यतः॥
en: Thereafter in that combat the king (Yudhishthira), pierced the latter whose bow had been served, with a long arrow between his breasts, even before the very eyes of all the troops.

sn: सत्वरं च रणे राजन्तस्य वाहान् महात्मनः। निजघान शरैः क्षिप्रं सूतं च सुमहाबलः॥ हताश्वं तु रथं त्यक्त्वा दृष्ट्वा राज्ञोऽस्य पौरुषम्।
en: Then, O monarch, with great quickens, Yudhishthira endued with great prowess, slew the steeds of the illustrious Shrutayush as also his charioteer, with swift-flying arrows.

sn: विप्रदुद्राव वेगेन श्रुतायुः समरे तदा॥
en: Then deserting his car of which the steeds were slain, and beholding the manliness of the monarch (Yudhishthira), Shrutayush fled with all haste from the field of battle.

sn: तस्मिञ्जिते महेष्वासे धर्मपुत्रेण संयुगे। दुर्योधनबलं राजन् सर्वमासीत् पराङ्मुखम्॥
en: When that mighty-bowman Shrutayush was vanquished in battle by the son of Dharma, the troops of Duryodhana, o king, turned their faces away from the field of battle.

sn: एतत् कृत्वा महाराज धर्मपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः। व्यात्ताननो यथा कालस्तव सैन्यं जघान ह॥
en: Achieving this feat, O mighty monarch, Yudhishthira the son of Dharma fell to slaughter your army, like the Destroyer himself with gaping mouth.

sn: चेकितानस्तु वार्ष्णेयो गौतमं रथिनां वरम्। प्रेक्षतां सर्वसैन्यानां छादयामास सायकैः॥
en: Then Chekitana that descendant of the Vrishni race, covered that foremost of carwarriors namely the son of Gautami, with numerous arrows, before the very eyes of all the troops.

sn: संनिवार्य शरांन्तांस्तु कृपः शारद्वतो युधि। चेकितानं रणे यत्तं राजन् विव्याध पत्रिभिः॥
en: Resisting also those arrows, in that combat, Kripa the son of Sharadvata pierced 0 monarch, with winged shafts, Chekitana who had been fighting very heedfully.

sn: अथापरेण भल्लेन धनुश्चिच्छेद मारिष। सारथिं चास्य समरे क्षिप्रहस्तो न्यपातयत्॥
en: Then, O Bharata, with a broad-headed shaft the former severed the latter's bow; as also with great lightness of hand he overthrew with another broad-headed the latter's charioteer.

sn: अश्वांश्चास्यावधीद् राजन्नुभौ तौ पार्णिसारथी। सोऽवप्लुत्य रथात् तूर्णं गदां जग्राह सात्वतः॥
en: Kripa also slew Chekitana's steeds and the charioteers of those who were protecting him in the flank. Then he of the Satvata race quickly jumping down from his car grasped a arrow mace.

sn: स तया वीरघातिन्या गदया गदिनां वरः। गौतमस्य हयान् हत्वा सारथिं च न्यपातयत्॥
en: Then that foremost of all wielders off maces slaying the steeds of the son of Gautami with that mace capable of crushing herces, felled the latter's charioteer.

sn: भूमिष्ठो गौतमस्तस्य शरांश्चिक्षेप षोडश। शरास्ते सात्वतं भित्त्वा प्राविशन् धरणीतलम्॥
en: Then standing on the ground, the son of Gautami shot at him sixteen shafts, and those shafts penetrating through him of the Satvata race, struck on the surface of the earth.

sn: चेकितानस्ततः क्रुद्धं पुनश्चिक्षेप तां गदाम्। गौतमस्य वधाकाक्षी वृत्रस्येव पुरंदरः॥
en: Then Chekitana, inflamed with rage and desirous of slaying the son of Gautami, once more hurled that mace at the latter, like Purandara hurling his thunder-bolt at Vritra.

sn: तामापतन्ती विमलामश्मगर्भा महागदाम्। शरैरनेकसाहस्रर्वारयामास गौतमः॥
en: Thereat the son of Gautami, with many thousands of arrows resisted that mighty and huge mace made entirely of adamant, that was falling swiftly on him.

sn: चेकितानस्ततः खङ्गं क्रोधादुद्धृत्य भारत। लाघवं परमास्थाय गौतमं समुपाद्रवत्॥
en: Thereupon Chekitana, O Bharata, drawing his sword out of its sheath, with admirable activity rushed at the son of Gautami.

sn: गौतमोऽपि धनुस्त्यक्त्वा प्रगृह्यासिं सुसंयतः। वेगेन महता राजंश्चेकितानमुपाद्रवत्॥
en: Thereupon Kripa also having laid aside his bow and grasping his sword highly polished, with great impetuosity rushed at Chekitana.

sn: तावुभौ बलसम्पन्नौ निस्त्रिशवरधारिणौ। निस्त्रिशाभ्यां सुतीक्ष्याभ्यामन्योन्यं संततक्षतुः॥
en: Then those two (heroes) endued with strength and armed with swords of excellent make, began to smite one another with their well-sharpened weapons.

sn: निस्त्रिंशवेगाभिहतौ ततस्तौ पुरुषर्षभौ। धरणीं समनुप्राप्तौ सर्वभूतनिषेविताम्॥
en: Then those two foremost of men, struck with the vehemence of one another's swords (blows) fell down on the earth inhabited by all sorts of creatures.

sn: मूर्छयाऽभिपरीताङ्गौ व्यायामेन तु मोहितौ। ततोऽभ्यधावद् वेगेन करकर्षः सुहृत्तया॥
en: Their limbs were stiffened in a swoon and they lost their consciousness through the fatigue (of their exertions). Thereupon the king of the Kauravas, out of friendship, rushed (to the rescue of Chekitana,

sn: चेकितानं तथाभूतं दृष्ट्वा समरदुर्मदः। रथमारोपयच्चैनं सर्वसैन्यस्य पश्यतः॥
en: And that hero invincible in battle seeing Chekitana in that plight, placed him on his car before the very eyes of all the troops.

sn: तथैव शकुनिः शूरः स्यालस्तव विशाम्पते। आरोपयद् स्थं तूर्णं गौतमं रथिनां वरम्॥
en: So also, O ruler of men, your heroic brother-in-law Shakuni, quickly took up on his chariot that foremost of car-warriors namely the son of Gautami.

sn: सौमदत्तिं तथा क्रुद्धौ धृष्टकेतुर्महाबलः। नवत्या सायकैः क्षिप्रं राजन् विव्याध वक्षसि॥
en: Thereafter Dhrishtaketu endued with great strength, waxing worth, pierced, O king, the son of Somadatta, on the breast, with ninety shafts.

sn: सौमदत्तिरुरःस्थास्तै शं बाणैरशोभत। मध्यंदिने महाराज रश्मिभिस्तपनो यथा॥
en: The son of Somadatta, O mighty monarch, with those arrows struck on his breast, appeared highly beautiful like the midday sun covered with its own rays.

sn: भूरिश्रवास्तु समरे धृष्टकेतुं महारथम्। हतसूतहयं चक्रे विरथं सायकोत्तमैः॥
en: Then in that conflict, Bhurishravas deprived the mighty car-warrior Dhrishtaketu (of the use) of his chariot, having slain its steeds and driver with excellent arrows.

sn: विरथं तं समालोक्य हताश्वं हतसारथिम्। महता शरवर्षेण च्छादयामास संयुगे॥
en: Beholding him deprived of his car in consequence of its driver and steeds being slain, Somadatta's son covered him in the battle with a thick shower of arrows.

sn: स तु तं रथमुत्सृज्य धृष्टकेतुर्महामनाः। आरुरोह ततो यानं शतानीकस्य मारिष॥
en: Then, O sire, deserting that car of his, the high-minded Dhrishtaketu ascended the vehicle belonging to Shatanika.

sn: चित्रसेनो विकर्णश्च राजन् दुर्मर्षणस्तथा। रथिनो हेमसंनाहाः सौभद्रमभिदुद्रुवुः॥
en: Then, O monarch, Chitrasena, Vikarna, and Durmarshana, all good car-warriors, clad in armours of gold, rushed against the son of Subhadra.

sn: अभिमन्योस्ततस्तैस्तु घोरं युद्धमवर्तत। शरीरस्य यथा राजन् वातपित्तकफैस्त्रिभिः॥
en: Then a dreadful combat endued between Abhimanyu and these warriors, that resembled, O king, the fight between the body and its three humours viz., wind bile, and phlegm.

sn: विरथांस्तव पुत्रांस्तु कृत्वा राजन् महाहवे। न जगान नरव्याघ्रः स्मरन् भीमवचस्तदा॥
en: Depriving, O monarch, your sons of their chariot, in that great battle, that foremost of men, Abhimanyu did not slay them recollecting the words of Bhima.

sn: ततो राज्ञां बहुशतैर्गजाश्वरथायायिभिः। संवृतं समरे भीष्मं देवैरपि दुरासदम्॥ प्रयान्तं शीघ्रमुवीक्ष्य परित्रातुं सुतांस्तव। अभिमन्युं समुद्दिश्य बालमेकं महारथम्॥ वासुदेवमुवाचेदं कौन्तेयः श्वेतवाहनः। चोदयाश्वान् हृषीकेश यत्रैते बहुला रथाः॥
en: There after as the battle raged, the son of Kunti (Arjuna) owning white steeds, beholding Bhishma who was unconquerable even by the celestial themselves in battle and who was supported by many thousands king proceed to rescue your sons from Abhimanyu, a mere boy, though a mighty car-warrior still aloneaddressed these words to the son of Vasudeva. “O Hrishikesha, urge the steeds to the spot where those numerous warriors are.

sn: एते हि बहवः शूराः कृतास्त्रा युद्धदुर्मदाः। यथा हन्युर्न नः सेनां तथा माधव चोदया।४६।।
en: O Madhava, so guide the steeds that these numerous heroes irrepressible in battle and all accomplished in the use of weapons, may not slay our troops.

sn: एवमुक्तः स वार्ष्णेयः कौन्तेयनामितौजसा। रथं श्वेतहयैर्युक्तं प्रेषयामास संयुगे॥
en: Thus spoken to by Kunti's son of immeasurable prowess, he of the Vrishni race drove in the thick of the battle that car to which were yoked white steeds.

sn: निष्ठानको महानासीत् तव सैन्यस्य मारिष। यदर्जुनो रणे क्रुद्धः संयातस्तावकान् प्रति॥
en: When wrought up with waist Arjuna rushed against your army O sire a tremendous uproar was set up by your troops.

sn: समासाद्य तु कौन्तेयो राज्ञस्तान् भीष्मरक्षिणः। सुशाण्यथो राजन्निदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: The son of Kunti then having approached those monarchs protected by Bhishma himself, addressing, O king, Susharma spoke these words to him.

sn: जानामि त्वां युधां श्रेष्ठमत्यन्तं पूर्ववैरिणम्। अनयस्याद्य सम्प्राप्तं फलं पश्य सुदारुणम्॥
en: “I know you to be one of the foremost in battle; your enmity for us in days gone by, was also implacable. Today, reap the mortal fruit of that wicked behaviour of yours.

sn: अद्य ते दर्शयिष्यामि पूर्वप्रेतान् पितामहान्। एवं संजल्पतस्तस्य बीभत्सोः शत्रुघातिनः॥ श्रुत्वापि परुषं वाक्य सुशर्मा रथयूथपः। न चैनमब्रवीत् किंचिच्छुभं वा यदि वाऽशुभम्॥
en: Today I shall transport you to your grenadiers who had long being dwelling in the regions of the dead.” Hearing these insulting words spoken by that slayer of foes namely Vibhatsu, Susharma, the commander of a cardivision spoke nothing well or ill in reply.

sn: अभिगम्यार्जुनं वीरं राजभिर्बहुभिर्वृतः। पुरस्तात् पृष्ठतश्चैव पार्श्वतश्चैव सर्वतः॥
en: Surrounded by innumerable monarchs, he attacked the heroic Arjuna from all sides, namely in the front, in the rear and in the two flanks.

sn: परिवार्यार्जुनं संख्ये तव पुत्रैर्महारथः। शरैः संछादयामास मेधैरिव दिवाकरम्॥
en: O sinless one, encircling Arjuna in that battle, Susharma along with your sons covered the former with arrows, like clouds covering the orb of the day.

sn: ततः प्रवृत्तः सुमहान् संग्राम: शोणितोदकः। तावकानां च समरे पाण्डवानां च भारत।॥
en: Then commenced a sanguinary engagement between your warriors and those of the Pandavas, in which blood flowed like streams of water.

sn: संजय उवाच त ताड्यमानस्तु शरैर्धनंजयः पदा हतो नाग इव श्वसन् बली। बाणेन बाणेन महारथानां चिच्छेद चापानि रणे प्रसा॥
en: Sanjaya said Then the highly powerful Dhananjaya wounded with those arrows, breathing like a trodden snake, forcibly cut off, in that battle, the bows bows to those mighty car-warriors, discharging shaft after shaft.

sn: संछिद्य चापानि च तानि राज्ञां तेषां रणे वीर्यवतां क्षणेन। विव्याध बाणैर्युगपन्महात्मा नि:शेषतां तेष्वथ मन्यमानः॥
en: Within a moment having severed the bows of those highly powerful monarchs in the battle, O king, that illustrious hero setting his mind upon their destruction began to pierce them simultaneously with his arrows.

sn: स्ते ताडिताः शक्रसुतेन राजन्। विभिन्नगात्रा: पतितोत्तमाङ्गा गतासवश्छिन्नतनुत्रकायाः॥
en: Wounded by the son of Shakra (Arjuna), O king, they rolled on the field weltering in their blood, with their bodies mutilated, their heads severed their armours shattered and their lives takes out of them.

sn: महीं गताः पार्थबलाभिभूता विचित्ररूपा युगपद् विनेषुः। स्त्रिगर्तराजः प्रययौ रथेन॥
en: Many, of them afflicted with the arrows shot by the son of Pritha (Arjuna), fell down on the earth; and undergoing diverse contortions simultaneously gave up their lives. Beholding those princes slair in battle, the ruler of the Trigartas proceeded (to battle) riding on his own car.

sn: तेषां रथानामथ पृष्ठगोपा द्वात्रिंशदन्येऽभ्यपतन्त पार्थम्। तथैव ते तं परिवार्य पार्थं विकृष्य चापानि महारवाणि॥
en: Then thirty two of those car-warriors, protecting his (Trigarta king's) rear, rushed at the son of Pritha. Thereafter those warriors encircled Pritha's son and drawing their bows emitting fierce twangs,

sn: अवीवृषन् बाणमहौघवृष्ट्या यथा गिरि तोयधरा जलौघैः। सम्पीड्यमानस्तु शरौघवृष्ट्या धनंजयस्तान् युधि जातरोषः॥
en: Covered the latter with a thick shower of arrows, just as clouds charged with rain drench with showers of their contents the mountain breast. Afflicted with that shower of arrows, Dhananjaya inflamed with rage in that battle,

sn: जघान तानप्यथ पृष्ठगोपान्। रथांश्च तांस्तानवजित्य संख्ये धनंजयः प्रीतमना यशस्वी॥
en: With sixty shafts, cleansed with oil, slew all those warriors protecting the rear of the Trigarta king. Vanquishing those sixty carwarriors in battle, filled with delight, the illustrious Dhananjaya,

sn: अथात्वरद् बलानि राजन् समरे निहत्य। त्रिगर्तराजो निहतान् समीक्ष्य महात्मना तानथ बन्धुवर्गान्॥
en: Ever-attended with victory, hide to slay Bhishma, having slain that division of kings. The king of the Trigaretas beholding those mighty car-warriors, his friends slain,

sn: रणे पुरस्कृत्य नराधिपांस्तान् जगाम पार्थं त्वरितो वधाय। अभिद्रुतं चास्त्रभृतां वरिष्ठ धनंजयं वीक्ष्य शिखण्डिमुख्या:॥
en: Speedily advanced towards the son of Pritha in order to slay him, placing in his front large number of kings. Beholding that foremost of those versed in the use of weapons, namely Dhananjaya, thus assailed, the Pandava warriors headed by Shikhandin,

sn: अभ्युद्ययुस्ते शितशस्त्रहस्ता रिरक्षिषन्तो रथमर्जुनस्य। पार्थोऽपि तानापतत: समीक्ष्य त्रिगर्तराज्ञा सहितान् नृवीरान्॥
en: Grasping in their hand well-sharpened weapons, rushed in battle desirous of protecting the car of Arjuna. Beholding those king make towards himself, the son of Pritha,

sn: विध्वंसयित्वा समरे धनुष्मान् गाण्डीवमुक्तैर्निशितैः पृषत्कैः। भीष्मं यियासुर्युधि संददर्श दुर्योधनं सैन्धवादींश्च राज्ञः॥ संवारयिष्णूनभिवारयित्वा मुहूर्तमायोध्य बलेन वीरः।
en: That fierce bowman, destroyed them in battle, with arrows of exceeding sharpness shot from the Gandiva bow. Desirous of encountering Bhishma in battle, Dhananjaya then observed many kings including Duryodhana and the ruler of the Sindhus.

sn: उत्सृज्य राजानमनन्तवीर्यो जयद्रथादींश्च नृपान् महौजाः॥ ययौ ततो भीमबलौ मनस्वी गाङ्गेयमाजौ शरचापपाणिः। युधिष्ठिरश्च प्रबलो महात्मा समाययौ त्वरितो जातकोपः॥
en: Then that highly powerful and wonderfullyintelligent hero of infinite prowess and great energy, fighting with them for a moment only and checking them, and then avoiding the king (Duryodhana) and Jayadratha and others, proceeded towards the son of Ganga, holding in his hands his bow and his arrows. Then the illustrious Yudhishthira of fierce prowess, excited with wrath speedily rushed to the battle.

sn: मद्राधिपं समभित्यज्य संख्ये स्वभागमाप्तं तमनन्तकीर्तिः। भीष्मं ययौ शान्तनवं रणाय॥
en: Avoiding in battle the ruler of the Madras of infinite renown who was allotted to his share and who was his kinsmen, Yudhishthira accompanied by the sons Madri and also by Bhimasena, proceeded, desirous of battle, toward Bhishma the son of Shantanu.

sn: तैः सम्प्रयुक्तैः स महारथाग्न्यै र्गङ्गासुतः समरे चित्रयोधी। न विव्यथे शान्तनवो महात्मा समागतैः पाण्डुसुतैः समस्तैः॥
en: Though assailed in battle by all the sons of Pandu, all mighty car-warriors united in a body, the son of Shantanu begotten upon Ganga, that high-souled warrior versed in all modes of warfare, flinched not in the least.

sn: अथैत्य राजा युधि सत्यसंधो जयद्रथोऽत्युग्रबलो मनस्वी। चिच्छेद चापानि महारथानां प्रसह्य तेषां धनुषा वरेण॥
en: Then king Jayadratha, highly intelligent and endued with great strength, and never failing in his aims in battle, advancing upon those mighty car-warriors forcibly served their bows by means of his own excellent bow.

sn: युधिष्ठिरं भीमसेनं यमौ च पार्थं कृष्णं युधि संजातकोपः। दुर्योधनः क्रोधविषो महात्मा जघान बाणैरनपलप्रकाशैः॥
en: Then the illustrious Duryodhana, having anger for his poison, waxing wrath in battle, wounded Yudhishthira, Bhima, Arjuna, and the twins (Nakula and Sahadeva) with arrows resplendent like fire itself.

sn: कृपेण शल्येन शलेन चैव तथा विभो चित्रसेनेन चाजौ। देवा यथा दैत्यगणैः समेतैः॥
en: Pierced with arrows shot by Kripa, Shalya, Shala and Chitrasena, O master, the Pandava brothers excited to the highest pitch of fury, resembled the celestial wounded with arrows shot by the united hosts of the Daityas.

sn: छिन्नायुधं शान्तनवेन राजा शिखण्डिनं प्रेक्ष्य च जातकोपः। अजातशत्रुः समरे महात्मा शिखण्डिनं क्रुद्ध उवाच वाक्यम्॥
en: Beholding Shikhandin with his bow severed by the royal son of Shantanu, the illustrious Ajatashatru (Yudhishthira) waxing worth, angrily said these words to the foriner.

sn: महं हनिष्यामि महाव्रतं तम्। भीष्मं शरौधैर्विमलार्कवणैः सत्यं वदामीति कृता प्रतिज्ञा॥
en: Having said to me even before your father these words viz., 'I will slay with my showers of arrows of the effulgence of the resplendent sun, Bhishma of great vows. This I say you forsooth, you made a promise.'

sn: त्वया च नैनां सफलां करोषि देवव्रतं यन्न नहंसि युद्धे। मिथ्याप्रतिज्ञो भव माऽत्र वीर रक्ष स्वधर्मं स्वकुलं यशश्च॥
en: You have not redeemed that promise of yours, in as much as you have not yet slain Devavrata in battle. O hero, be not of a man of empty promises. Preserve your virtue, your race and your fame.

sn: प्रेक्षस्व भीष्मं युधि भीमवेगं सर्वांस्तपन्त मम सैन्यसंघान्। शरौघजालैरतितिग्मवेगैः कालं यथा कालकृतं क्षणेन॥
en: Behold Bhishma of tremendous impetuosity falling upon my host of troops destroying it with a shower of arrows of excessive effulgence, like the Destroyer himself destroying everything in a moment,

sn: निकृत्तचापः समरेऽनपेक्षः पराजितः शान्तनवेन चाजौ। विहाय बन्धूनथ सोदरांश्च क्व यास्यसे नानुरूपं तवेदम्॥
en: Having your bow severed, shunning the fight, vanquished by the royal son of Shantanu, whither are you going forsaking your friends and your uterine brothers? this does not befit you.

sn: दृष्ट्वा हि भीष्मं तमनन्तवीर्य भग्नं च सैन्यं द्रवमाणमेवम्। भीतोऽसि नूनं दुपदस्य पुत्र तथा हि ते मुखवर्णोऽप्रहृष्टः॥
en: Beholding Bhishma of infinite prowess and seeing this army broken and routed, O son of Drupada, you are indeed seized with panic, in as much as your countenance has assumed a pallid hue.

sn: अज्ञातमाने च धनंजयेऽपि महाहवे सम्प्रसक्ते नृवीरे। कथं हि भीष्मात् प्रथितः पृथिव्यां भयं त्वमद्य प्रकरोषि वीर॥
en: But, behold, O hero Dhananjaya has engaged in dreadful fight with Bhishma even without your knowledge. Celebrated through out the world, why today, O hero are you afraid to Bhishma?

sn: स धर्मराजस्य वचो निशम्य रुक्षाक्षरं विप्रलापानुबद्धम्। प्रत्यादेशं मन्यमानो महात्मा प्रतत्वरे भीष्मवधाय राजन्।॥
en: Hearing this hard-worded speech full of instructions delivered by the very various king Yudhishthira, that high-souled hero Shikhandin considering it to be good counsel, hastened, O king, to bring about the slaughter of Bhishma.

sn: तमापतन्तं महता जवेन शिखण्डिनं भीष्ममभिद्रवन्तम्। मस्त्रेण घोरेण सुदुर्जयेन॥
en: When Shikhandin had been thus advancing with great momentum to fall upon Bhishma, Shalya checked him with a weapon dreadful and difficult of being baffled.

sn: मस्त्रं युगान्ताग्निसमप्रकाशम्। न सम्मुमोह द्रुपदस्य पुत्रो राजन् महेन्द्रप्रतिमप्रभावः॥
en: Beholding that weapon effulgent like the fire that appears at the Yuga's end (for destroying the world) shot at him, the son of Drupada, of prowess resembling that of the great Indra, was not at all confounded.

sn: शरैस्तदस्त्रं प्रतिबाधमानः। अथाददे वारुणमन्यदस्त्रं शिखण्ड्यथोग्रं प्रतिघातमस्य॥
en: On the other hand, that fierce bowman stood there restating that weapon with numerous arrows. Thereafter Shikhandin fixed on his bow-string the Varuna weapon that was capable of counteracting (the fiery weapon of Shalya).

sn: तदस्त्रमस्त्रेण विदार्यमाणं खस्थाः सुरा ददृशुःपार्थिवाश्च। भीष्मस्तु राजन् समरे महात्मा धनुश्च चित्रं ध्वजमेव चापि॥ छित्त्वाऽनदत् पाण्डुसुतस्य वीरो युधिष्ठिरस्याजमीढस्य राज्ञः। ततः समुत्सृज्य धनुः सबाण युधिष्ठिरं वीक्ष्य भयाभिभूतम्॥
en: The celestial in the heavens and the rulers of the earth, all beheld that weapon (fiery darc of Shalya) baffled by Shikhandin's (Varuna) arrow. In that battle, O king, the high-souled and heroic Bhishma also uttered his war-cry having cut off the bow and wonderfully variegated standard of the royal son of Pandu viz., Yudhishthira of the Ajamida race. Thereupon seeing Yudhishthira overwhelmed with fear, leaving aside his bow and his arrows,

sn: गदां प्रगृह्याभिपपात संख्ये जयद्रथं भीमसेनः पदातिः। तमापतन्तं सहसा जवेन जयद्रथः सगदं भीमसेनम्॥ विव्याध घोरैर्यमदण्डकल्पैः शितैः शरैः पञ्चशतैः समन्तात्। अचिन्तयित्वा स शरांस्तरस्वी वृकोदरः क्रोधपरीतचेताः॥
en: And grasping a mace, Bhimasena rushed on foot against Jayadratha in that battle. Then Jayadratha simultaneously pierced Bhimasena who was thus furiously rushing at him with a mace in hand with five hundred sharp-pointed terrible shafts, each resembling the mace of the Destroyer himself. Without paying the least heed to those arrows, the highly active Vrikodara with heart burning in wrath,

sn: जघान वाहान् समरे समन्तात् पारावतान् सिन्धुराजस्य संख्ये। स्तवात्मजस्त्वरमाणो रथेन॥ अभ्याययौ भीमसेनं निहन्तुं समुद्यतास्त्रोः सुरराजकल्पः। भीमोऽप्यथैनं सहसा विनद्य प्रत्युद्ययौ गदया तर्जयानः॥
en: Slew in that battle all the steeds of the king of the Shindhus, steeds that resembled (in speed) pegions themselves. Then your son Chitrasena of unequaled prowess and resembling the sovereign of the celestial himself, beholding, Bhimasena, rushed to battle with a view to slay the latter, riding swift on his car and with weapons raised over head Bhimasena also, roaring and uttering his warcry, rushed against him mace in hand.

sn: समुद्यतां तां यमदण्डकल्पां दृष्ट्वा गदां ते कुरवः समन्तात्। विहाय सर्वे तव पुत्रमुग्रं पातं गदायाः परिहर्तुकामाः॥
en: Beholding that mace, resembling the mace of Death himself, thus raised overhead (by Bhishma), every one of the Kuru warriors, eager to avoid its fall, deserting the van of your son,

sn: अपक्रान्तास्तुमुले सम्प्रमर्दे सुदारुणे भारत मोहनीये। अमूढचेतास्त्वथ चित्रसेनो महागदामापतन्तीं निरीक्ष्य॥
en: Fled in all directions, in that confounding dreadful and ruthless crush of combatants. O Bharata, your son Chitrasena beholding that mighty mace course towards him, was not confounded at heart.

sn: रथं स्वमुत्सृज्य पदातिराजौ प्रगृह्य खङ्गं विपुलं च चर्म। ज्जगामान्यं भूमिप भूमिदेशम्॥
en: Grasping a resplendent sword and a buckler, Chitrasena leaving his car and jumping down from the crest of a cliff, stood on his legs on the field of the battle.

sn: गदाऽपि सा प्राप्य रथं सुचित्रं सावं ससूतं विनिहत्य संख्ये। जगाम भूमिं ज्वलिता महोल्का भ्रष्टाम्बराद् गामिव सम्पतन्ती॥
en: Meanwhile that mace falling upon that beautiful car with its steeds and elephants, crushed it in battle, and fell on the ground like a blazing and fierce meteor dropping down from the skies.

sn: आश्चर्यभूतं सुमहत् त्वदीया दृष्ट्वैव तद् भारत सम्प्रहृष्टाः। सर्वे विनेदुः सहिताः समन्तात् पुपूजिरे तव पुत्रस्य शौर्यम्॥
en: Seeing that very wonderful feat achieved by your son), your warriors, O Bharata, were filled with delight; and they untidily uttered their war-cries and began to praise your son.

description: Withdrawal of the troops after the seventh day's fight,
sn: संजय उवाच विरथं तं समासाद्य चित्रसेनं यशस्विनम्। रथमारोपयामास विकर्णस्तनयस्तवाशा
en: Sanjaya said Approaching the highly intelligent Chitrasena who had been deprived of his car, your son Vikarna picked him up on his own chariots.

description: Withdrawal of the troops after the seventh day's fight,
sn: तस्मिंस्तथा वर्तमाने तुमुले संकुले भृशम्। भीष्मः शान्तनवस्तूर्णं युधिष्ठिररमुपाद्रवत्॥
en: When that dreadful and confounding battle was thus raging, Shantanu's son Bhishma quickly rushed against Yudhishthira.

description: Withdrawal of the troops after the seventh day's fight,
sn: ततः सरथनागाश्वा: समकम्पन्त सुंजयाः। मृत्योरास्यमनुप्राप्तं मेनिरे च युधिष्ठिरम्॥
en: Then the Srinjayas with their cars, elephants and steeds, began to quake (with inside the jaws of Death.

description: Withdrawal of the troops after the seventh day's fight,
sn: युधिष्ठिरोऽपि कौरव्यो यमाभ्यां सहितः प्रभुः। महेष्वासं नरव्याघ्र भीष्मं शान्तनवं ययौ॥
en: On the other hand that descendant of Kuru's race, that lord Yudhishthira, united with his two twin brothers (Nakula and Sahadeva), encountered that foremost of men, that fierce bowman namely Bhishma, the of Shantanu.

description: Withdrawal of the troops after the seventh day's fight,
sn: ततः शरसहस्राणि प्रमुञ्चन् पाण्डवो युधि। भीष्मं संछादयामास यथा मेघो दिवाकरम्॥
en: Thereafter that son of Pandu shooting in that battle thousands of arrows, covered Bhishma, like clouds covering the orb of the day. son arrows

description: Withdrawal of the troops after the seventh day's fight,
sn: तेन सम्यक् प्रणीतानि शरजालानि मारिष। प्रतिजग्राह गाङ्गेयः शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः॥
en: Those duly discharged by Yudhishthira, the son of Ganga received in distinct sets of hundreds and thousands.

description: Withdrawal of the troops after the seventh day's fight,
sn: तथैव शरजालानि भीष्मेणास्तानि मारिष। आकाशे समदृश्यन्त खगमानां व्रजा इव॥
en: Also, O'sire, a network of arrows woven by Bhima was seen in the heavens resembling fights of insects ranging through the skies.

description: Withdrawal of the troops after the seventh day's fight,
sn: निमेषार्धेन की तेयं भीष्मः शान्तनवो युधि। अदृश्यं समरे चक्रे शरजालेन भागशः॥
en: In half a wink's time, Bhishma the son of Shantanu, in that battle made the son of Kunti disappear in battle, covering him with distinct sets of arrows.

description: Withdrawal of the troops after the seventh day's fight,
sn: ततो युधिष्ठिरो राजा कौरव्यस्य महात्मनः। नाराजं प्रेषयामास क्रुद्ध आशीविषोपमम्॥
en: Thereat king Yudhishthira inflamed with rage, sped at that high-souled grandsire of the Kurus, a Naracha that resembled a snake of virulent venom.

description: Withdrawal of the troops after the seventh day's fight,
sn: असम्प्राप्तं ततस्तं तु क्षुरप्रेण महारथः। चिच्छेद समरे राजन् भीष्मस्तस्य धनुश्च्युतम्॥
en: Then in that battle, O king, the mighty carwarrior Bhishma, with a razor sharp arrow, cut off that Naracha discharged from the bow of Yudhishthira, even before it could reach him.

description: Withdrawal of the troops after the seventh day's fight,
sn: तं तु छित्त्वा रणे भीष्मो नाराचं कालसम्मितम्। निजने कौरवेन्द्रस्य हयान् काञ्चनभूषणान्॥
en: In that battle, Bhishma, having cut off that Naracha that resembled the Destroyer himself, slew the steeds caparisoned with golden ornaments, of that foremost of the Kurus (Yudhishthira).

description: Withdrawal of the troops after the seventh day's fight,
sn: हताश्वं तु रथं त्यक्त्वा धर्मपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः। आरुरोह रथं तूर्णं नकुलस्य महात्मनः॥
en: Leaving his car the steeds of which were slain, Yudhishthira the son of Dharma, quickly ascended the car of the high-souled Nakula.

description: Withdrawal of the troops after the seventh day's fight,
sn: यमावपि हि संक्रुद्धः समासाद्य रणे तदा। शरैः संछादयामास भीष्मः परपुरंजयः॥
en: Thereafter 'Bhishma that conqueror of hostile fortresses, excited with wrath, approaching the twins in battle, covered them with numerous shafts.

description: Withdrawal of the troops after the seventh day's fight,
sn: तौ तु दृष्ट्वा महाराज भीष्मबाणप्रपीडितौ। जगाम परमां चिन्तां भीष्मस्य वधकाझया॥
en: Then O mighty monarch, beholding the twins thus afflicted with the arrows shot by Bhishma, Yudhishthira began to reflect anxiously, desirous of finding out a means for the death of Bhishma.

description: Withdrawal of the troops after the seventh day's fight,
sn: ततो युधिष्ठिरो वश्यान् राज्ञस्तान् समचोदयत्। भीष्मं शान्तनवं सर्वे निहतेति सुहृद्गणान्॥
en: Thereafter, O king, Yudhishthira urged the kings on his side and his relatives, saying "Uniting together do you all slay Bhishma the son of Shantanu."

description: Withdrawal of the troops after the seventh day's fight,
sn: ततस्ते पार्थिवाः सर्वे श्रुत्वा पार्थस्य भाषितम्। महता रथवंशेन परिवत्रुः पितामहम्॥
en: Then bearing the command of Pritha's son, all the rulers of earth surrounded the grandsire with a mighty host of cars.

description: Withdrawal of the troops after the seventh day's fight,
sn: स समन्तात् परिवृतः पिता देवव्रतस्तव। चिक्रीड धनुषा राजन् पातयानो महारथान्॥
en: Thus encircled, your father Devavrata played with his bow and arrows felling, o king, numerous mighty car-warriors.

description: Withdrawal of the troops after the seventh day's fight,
sn: तं चरन्तं रणे पार्था ददृशुः कौरवं युधि। मृगमध्यं प्रविश्येव यथा सिंहशिशुं वने॥
en: The sons of Pritha then beheld that foremost of the Kurus, career on the field of battle, like a lion-cub in the woods amidst a herd of deer.

description: Withdrawal of the troops after the seventh day's fight,
sn: तर्जयानं रणे वीरांस्त्रासयानं च सायकैः। दृष्ट्वा त्रेसुर्महाराज सिंहं मृगगणा इव॥
en: Beholding him utter loud war-cries in battle and frighten heroes with his shafts. O monarch, the Pandava warriors were seized with terror, like a herd of deer at the sight of a lion.

description: Withdrawal of the troops after the seventh day's fight,
sn: रणे भारतसिंहस्य ददृशुः क्षत्रिया गतिम्। अग्नेर्वायुसहायस्य यथा कक्षं दिधक्षतः॥
en: Then the Kshatriyas, in that battle, beheld the movements of that foremost of the Bharatas, resemble the movements of fire aided by a strong wind, when it consumes a heap straw.

description: Withdrawal of the troops after the seventh day's fight,
sn: शिरांसि रथिनां भीष्मः पातयामास संयुगे। तालेभ्यः परिपक्वानि फलानि कुशलो नरः॥
en: Then in that battle Bhishma felled the heads of car-warriors like expert men felling ripe palm-fruits from their trees.

description: Withdrawal of the troops after the seventh day's fight,
sn: पतद्भिश्च महाराज शिरोभिर्धरणीतले। बभूव तुमुलः शब्दः पततामश्मनामिव॥
en: As those heads, O mighty monarch, fell down on the surface of the earth, a great noise was produced like that of a shower of stones.

description: Withdrawal of the troops after the seventh day's fight,
sn: तस्मिन् सुतुमुले युद्धे वर्तमाने भयानके। सर्वेषामेव सैन्यानामासीद् व्यतिकरो महान्॥
en: As that dreadful and fierce battle regard, a great a confusion set in, O king, among all the ranks of the soldiers.

description: Withdrawal of the troops after the seventh day's fight,
sn: भिन्नेषु तेषु व्यूहेषु क्षत्रिया इतरेतरम्। एकमेकं समाहूय युद्धायैवावतस्थिरे॥
en: When the arrays were thus shattered by Bhishma, the Kshatriyas challenging one another encountered one another for battle.

description: Withdrawal of the troops after the seventh day's fight,
sn: शिखण्डी तु समासाद्य भरतानां पितामहम्। अभिदुद्राव वेगेन तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति चाब्रवीत्॥
en: Shikhandin approaching the grandsire of the Bharatas, assailed him with vehemence saying 'stay'.

description: Withdrawal of the troops after the seventh day's fight,
sn: अनादृत्य ततो भीष्मस्तं शिखण्डिनमाहवे। प्रययौ सुंजयान् क्रुद्धः स्त्रीत्वं चिन्त्य शिखण्डिनः॥
en: Then Bhishma remembering the femininity of Shikhandin, and for that reason neglecting him in battle, rushed against the Srinjayas.

description: Withdrawal of the troops after the seventh day's fight,
sn: सुंजयास्तु ततो दृष्ट्वा हृष्टं भीष्मं महारणे। सिंहनादांश्च विविधांश्चक्रुः शङ्खविमिश्रितान्॥
en: Thereupon the Srinjayas, beholding Bhishma in that battle, were filled with delight and they uttered numerous war-cries that became mingled with the blare of the conchs.

description: Withdrawal of the troops after the seventh day's fight,
sn: ततः प्रववृते युद्धं व्यतिषक्तरथद्विपम्। पश्चिमां दिशमासाद्य स्थिते सवितरि प्रभो॥
