en: Then, O lord, when the sun was on the western side of the meridian, there commenced a battle in which car-warriors and elephantriders encountered one another.

description: Withdrawal of the troops after the seventh day's fight,
sn: धृष्टद्युम्नोऽथ पाञ्चाल्यः सात्यकिश्च महारथः। पीडयन्तौ भृशं सैन्यं शक्तितोमरवृष्टिभिः॥
en: Then Dhrishtadyumna the prince of the Pandavas, and also the mighty car-warrior Satyaki, began to torment your troops with showers of Shaktis and Tomaras.

description: Withdrawal of the troops after the seventh day's fight,
sn: शस्त्रैश्च बहुभि राजञ्जनतुस्तावकान् रणे। ते हन्यमानाः समरे तावका भरतर्षभ॥
en: They also, O monarch siew in battle your warriors with innumerable shafts. O foremost of men, your troops, through thus smitten down in battle,

description: Withdrawal of the troops after the seventh day's fight,
sn: आर्यां युद्धे मतिं कृत्वा न त्यजन्ति स्म संयुगम्। यथोत्साहं तु समरे निजघ्नुस्तावका रणे॥
en: Did not desert the fight having formed a laudable determination (to fight to the last); and those foremost of car-warriors began to slay (the hostile troop) to the best o their energies.

description: Withdrawal of the troops after the seventh day's fight,
sn: तत्राक्रन्दो महानासीत् तावकानां महात्मनाम्। वध्यतां समरे राजन् पार्षतेन महात्मना॥
en: Then, O monarch, a loud cry of agony was set up by your high souled warriors as they were slain by the illustrious son of Prishata.

description: Withdrawal of the troops after the seventh day's fight,
sn: तं श्रुत्वा निनदं घोरं तावकानां महारथौ। विन्दानुविन्दावावन्त्यौ पार्षतं प्रत्युपस्थितौ॥
en: Hearing that distressful cry uttered by your troop, Vinda and Anuvinda of the Avanti country, both mighty car-warriors, rushed to cncounter the son of Prishata.

description: Withdrawal of the troops after the seventh day's fight,
sn: तौ तस्य तुरगान् हत्वा त्वरमाणौ महारथौ। छादयामासतुरुभौ शरवाण पार्षतम्॥
en: Then those mighty car-warriors both endued with greu activity, slaying the steeds of Prishata's son, shrouded him with a shower of arrows.

description: Withdrawal of the troops after the seventh day's fight,
sn: अवप्लुत्याथ पाञ्चाल्यो रथात् तूर्णं महाबलः। आरुरोह रथं तूर्णं सात्यकेस्तु महात्मनः॥
en: Thereupon that mighty car-warrior the Panchala prince quickly jumping down his car, ascended with agility the chariot of the highly illustrious Satyaki.

description: Withdrawal of the troops after the seventh day's fight,
sn: ततो युधिष्ठिरो राजा महत्या सेनया वृतः। आवन्त्यौ समरे क्रुद्धावभ्ययात् स परंतपौ॥
en: Thereupon king Yudhishthira surrounded by a mighty division of troops rushed to those two afflicter of foes viz., the princes of Avanti both inflamed with wrath.

description: Withdrawal of the troops after the seventh day's fight,
sn: तथैव तव पुत्रोऽपि सर्वोद्योगेन मारिष। विन्दानुविन्दौ समरे परिवार्यावतस्थिवान्।॥
en: So also, O sire, your sons putting forth all their energies, remained in battle surrounding Vinda and Anuvinda.

description: Withdrawal of the troops after the seventh day's fight,
sn: अर्जुनश्चापि संक्रुद्धः क्षत्रियान् क्षत्रियर्षभः। अयोधयत संग्रामे वज्रपाणिरिवासुरान्॥
en: In that battle Arjuna also inflamed with many wrath fought with many best of Kshatriyas like the wielder of the thunder-bolt fighting against the Asuras.

description: Withdrawal of the troops after the seventh day's fight,
sn: द्रोणस्तु समरे क्रुद्धः पुत्रस्य प्रियकृत् तव। व्यधमत् सर्वपञ्चालास्तूलराशिमिवानलः॥
en: Drona also, that well-wisher of your son, excited with wrath began to consume all the Panchalas like fire consuming a heap of cotton.

description: Withdrawal of the troops after the seventh day's fight,
sn: दुर्योधनपुरोगास्तु पुत्रास्तव विशाम्पते। परिवार्य रणे भीष्मं युयुधुः पाण्डवैः सह॥
en: Your sons, O ruler of men, headed by Duryodhana himself surrounding Bhishma, fought on with the Pandavas.

description: Withdrawal of the troops after the seventh day's fight,
sn: ततो दुर्योधनो राजा लोहितायति भास्करे। अब्रवीत् तावकान् सर्वांस्त्वध्वमिति भारत॥
en: Then, 0 Bharata, when the lustrous orb assume a crimson hue, king Duryodhana addressing all your warriors said, "make hasten".

description: Withdrawal of the troops after the seventh day's fight,
sn: युध्यतां तु तेषां कुर्वतां कर्म दुष्करम्। अस्तं गिरिमथारूढे अप्रकाशति भास्करे॥
en: When they thus fought on achieving feats difficult of being accomplished, the sun being lost to the sight ascended the western hills,

description: Withdrawal of the troops after the seventh day's fight,
sn: प्रावर्तत नदी घोरा शोणितौघतरङ्गिणीः। गोमायुगणसंकीर्णा क्षणेन क्षणदामुखे॥
en: Then in a moment, towards nightfall, a dreadful river surging with billows of flow across the field of battle.

description: Withdrawal of the troops after the seventh day's fight,
sn: शिवाभिरशिवाभिश्च रुवद्भिभैरवं रवम्। धोकमायोधनं जज्ञे भूतसंघैः समाकुलम्॥
en: Then the field of battle assumed a dreadful sight abounding as at did with the spirits of the dead and the ominous jackals howling (tediously).

description: Withdrawal of the troops after the seventh day's fight,
sn: राक्षसाश्च पिशाचाश्च तथान्ये पिशिताशिनः। समन्ततो व्यदृश्यन्त शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः॥
en: Rakshasas, and Pishachas and other feeders on flesh were seen on all sides by hundreds and by thousands.

description: Withdrawal of the troops after the seventh day's fight,
sn: अर्जुनोऽथ सुशर्मादीन् राज्ञस्तान् सपदानुगान्। विजित्य पृतनामध्ये ययौ स्वशिबिरं प्रति॥
en: Arjuna having conquered the kings headed by Susharma along with their followers, proceeded through the divisions towards his own tent.

description: Withdrawal of the troops after the seventh day's fight,
sn: युधिष्ठिरोऽपि कौरव्यौ भ्रातृभ्यां सहितस्तथा। ययौ स्वशिबिरं राजा निशायां सेनया वृतः॥
en: That descendant of the Kuru race, viz., the lord Yudhishthira also proceeded, o king surrounded by his troops and accompanied by his brothers, towards his own tent at the advent of night.

description: Withdrawal of the troops after the seventh day's fight,
sn: भीमसेनोऽपि राजेन्द्र दुर्योधनमुखान् रथान्। अवजित्य ततः संख्ये ययौ स्वशिबिरं प्रति॥
en: Bhimasena also, o foremost of kings having vanquished in battle the kings, all good car-warriors, headed by Duryodhana hiinself, retired to his own camp. slain many

description: Withdrawal of the troops after the seventh day's fight,
sn: दुर्योधनोऽपि नृपतिः परिवार्य महारणे। भीष्मं शान्तनवं तूर्णं प्रयात: शिबिरं प्रति॥
en: In that great battle also, king Duryodhana surrounding Bhishma the son of Shantanu, speedily proceed towards his own tents.

description: Withdrawal of the troops after the seventh day's fight,
sn: द्रोणो द्रौणिः कृपः शल्यः कृतवर्मा च सात्वतः। परिवार्य चमूं सर्वां प्रययुः शिबिरं प्रति॥
en: Drona and his son, Kripa and Shalya and Kritavarma of the Satvata race, bringing up the rear of the hole host of the Kurus, wended towards their respective tents.

description: Withdrawal of the troops after the seventh day's fight,
sn: तथैव सात्यकी राजन् धृष्टद्युम्नश्च पार्षतः। परिवार्य रणे योधान् ययतुः शिबिरं प्रति॥
en: So also, O monarch, Satyaki and Prishata's son Dhrishtadyumna having warriors in the battle proceeded towards their tents.

description: Withdrawal of the troops after the seventh day's fight,
sn: एवमेते महाराज तावकाः पाण्डवैः सह। पर्यवर्तन्त सहिता निशाकाले परंतप॥
en: Thus, O mighty monarch, your warriors as also those of the Pandavas, all chastisers of their enemies, returned to their encampments when the shades of night had fallen on this earth.

description: Withdrawal of the troops after the seventh day's fight,
sn: ततः स्वशिबिरं गत्वा पाण्डवाः कुरवस्तथा। न्यवसन्त महाराज पूजयन्तः परस्परम्॥
en: Then, O mighty monarch, the Pandavas and the Kurus repairing near their respective encampments entered them exchanging greetings with one another.

description: Withdrawal of the troops after the seventh day's fight,
sn: रक्षां कृत्वा ततः शूरा न्यस्य गुल्मान् यथाविधि। अपनीय च शल्यानि स्नात्वा च विविधैर्जलैः॥
en: Then duly arranging for scouts and outposts and for protecting their persons, and drawing out the arrows from their bodies and having bathed in various waters,

description: Withdrawal of the troops after the seventh day's fight,
sn: कृतस्वस्त्ययनाः सर्वे संस्तूयन्तश्च बन्दिभिः। गीतवादित्रशब्देन व्यक्रीडन्त यशस्विनः॥
en: And being praised by the minstrels and bards and arranging for the performance of benedictory rites those illustrious heroes then began to sport accompanied by songs and sounds of musical instruments.

description: Withdrawal of the troops after the seventh day's fight,
sn: मुहूर्तादिव तत् सर्वमभवत् स्वर्गसंनिभम्। न हि युद्धकथां कांचित् तत्राकुर्वन् महारथाः॥
en: For a short while only did that scene resemble paradise itself, and those foremost of mortals for a while desisted from talking of the battle.

description: Withdrawal of the troops after the seventh day's fight,
sn: ते प्रसुप्ते बले तत्र परिश्रान्तजने नृप। हस्त्यश्वबहुले रात्रौ प्रेक्षणीये बभूवतुः॥
en: When those two armies, abounding in elephants and steeds and men exhausted with fatigue, were lulled in the arms of sleep O king, they, indeed presented a charming sight.

description: Commencement of the eighth day's combat
sn: संजय उवाच परिणाम्य निशां तां तु सुखं प्राप्ता जनेश्वराः। कुरवः पाण्डवाश्चैव पुनर्युद्धाय निर्ययुः॥
en: Sanjaya said Having passed that night and having enjoying a peaceful slumber, those rulers of men belonging to the hosts of the Kurus and the Pandavas, again marched out for battle.

description: Commencement of the eighth day's combat
sn: ततः शब्दो महानासीत् सैन्ययोरुभयोर्नृप। निर्गच्छमानयोः संख्ये सागरप्रतिमो महान्॥
en: Then a tremendous din was created by those two hosts when they marched out for battle, did that resembled the uproar of the ocean itself.

description: Commencement of the eighth day's combat
sn: ततो दुर्योधनो राजा चित्रसेनो विविंशतिः। भीष्मश्च रथिनां श्रेष्ठो भारद्वाजश्च वै नृप॥
en: Thereupon king Duryodhana, Chitrasena, Vivingshati, Bhishma the foremost of all carwarriors, the son of Bharadvaja endued with prowess,

description: Commencement of the eighth day's combat
sn: एकीभूताः सुसंयत्ताः कौरवाणां महाचमूम्। व्यूहाय विदधू राजन् पाण्डवान् प्रति दंशिताः॥
en: These mighty car-warriors of the Kaurava host clad in mail and united together and with great care, formed, O king, the battle-array of their troops against those of the Pandavas.

description: Commencement of the eighth day's combat
sn: भीष्मः कृत्वा महाव्यूहं पिता तव विशाम्पते। सागरप्रतिमं घोरं वाहनोर्मितरङ्गिणम्॥
en: Your sire Bhishma, O ruler of men, formed a mighty array resembling the dreadful ocean itself, having for its waves and currents the vehicles (of the warriors).

description: Commencement of the eighth day's combat
sn: अग्रतः सर्वसैन्यानां भीष्मः शान्तनवो ययौ। मालवैर्दाक्षिणात्यैश्च आवन्त्यैश्च समन्वितः॥
en: Then Bhishma the son of Shantanu marched out in the van of all the troops, supported by the Malavas, the Southerners and Avantyas.

description: Commencement of the eighth day's combat
sn: ततोऽनन्तरमेवासीद् भारद्वाजः प्रतापवान्। पुलिन्दैः पारदैश्चैव तथा क्षुद्रकमालवैः॥
en: Behind him came the son of Bharadvaja endued with prowess, being supported by the Pulindas, the Kshudrakas and the Malavas.

description: Commencement of the eighth day's combat
sn: द्रोणादनन्तरं यत्तो भगदत्तः प्रतापवान्। मगधैश्च कलिङ्गैश्च पिशाचैश्च विशाम्पते।॥
en: After Drona marched Bhagadatta endued with great prowess and determined to fight to the last), being supported by the Magadhas, the Kalingas, and the Pisachas, O ruler of men.

description: Commencement of the eighth day's combat
sn: प्राग्ज्योतिषादनु नृपः कौसल्योऽथ बृहद्बलः। मेकलैः कुरुविन्दैश्च त्रैपुरैश्च समन्वितः॥
en: After king of Pragjyotishapur, came Brihadbala the ruler of the Kosalas, being supported by the Mekalas, the Tripuras and the Chichitas.

description: Commencement of the eighth day's combat
sn: बृहद्बलात् ततः शूरस्त्रिगर्तः प्रस्थलाधिपः। काम्बोजैर्बहुभिः सार्धं यवनैश्च सहस्रशः॥
en: After Brihadbala came the heroic Bhagadatta, the ruler of Prasthala, accompanied by numerous Kamboja and thousands of Yavanas.

description: Commencement of the eighth day's combat
sn: द्रौणिस्तु रभसः शूरस्गर्तादनु भारत। प्रययौ सिंहनादेन नादयानो धरातलम्॥
en: After Trigarta, O Bharata, the valiant son of Drona rushed to battle, resounding the earth with his war-cries.

description: Commencement of the eighth day's combat
sn: तथा सर्वेण सैन्येन राजा दुर्योधनस्तदा। द्रौणेरनन्तरं प्रायात् सोदर्यैः परिवारितः॥
en: After the son of Drona proceeded king Duryodhana accompanied by the whole army and surrounded his uterine brothers.

description: Commencement of the eighth day's combat
sn: दुर्योधनादनु ततः कृपः शारद्वतो ययौ। एवमेष महाव्यूहः प्रययौ सागरोपमः॥
en: After Duryodhana marched Kripa, the son of Sharadvata. Thus marched out the mighty array that resembled the ocean itself.

description: Commencement of the eighth day's combat
sn: रेजुस्तत्र पताकाश्च श्वेतच्छत्राणि वा विभो। अङ्गदान्यत्र चित्राणि महार्हाणि धनूंषि च॥
en: In that array, O lord, streamers, white umbrellas, precious armours of wonderful workmanship, and many bows, shone resplendent.

description: Commencement of the eighth day's combat
sn: तं तु दृष्ट्वा महाव्यूहं तावकानां महारथः। युधिष्ठिरोऽब्रवीत् तूर्णं पार्षत पृतनापतिम्॥
en: Seeing that mighty array of your warriors, the mighty car-warrior Yudhishthira speedily addressing Prishata's son, the generalissimo of his army said these words.

description: Commencement of the eighth day's combat
sn: पश्य व्यूहं महेष्वास निर्मितं सागरोपमम्। प्रतिव्यूहं त्वमपि हि कुरु पार्षत सत्वरम्॥
en: Behold, O mighty bowman, this array of troops already formed, resembling the very ocean; O son of Prishata, without loss of time, do you also arrange your troops in counterarray.

description: Commencement of the eighth day's combat
sn: ततः स पार्षतः क्रूरो व्यूह चक्रे सुदारुणम्। शृङ्गाटकं महाराज परव्यूहविनाशनम्॥
en: Thereupon, O mighty monarch, the valiant son of Prishata formed the dreadful array known as Shringataka that is capable of penetrating through the hostile array.

description: Commencement of the eighth day's combat
sn: शृङ्गाभ्यां भीमसेनश्च सात्यकिश्च महारथः। रथैरनेकसाहौस्तथा हयपदातिभिः॥
en: In its two horns was placed Bhimasena and the mighty car-warrior Satyaki, supported by many thousands of car-warriors and cavalry and infantry.

description: Commencement of the eighth day's combat
sn: ताभ्यां बभौ नरश्रेष्ठः श्वेताश्वः कृष्णसारथिः। मध्ये युधिष्ठिरो राजा माद्रीपुत्रौ च पाण्डवौ॥
en: In its navel was the ape-bannered Arjuna owning white steeds; and O foremost of men, in its middle was king Yudhishthira and the sons of Pandu begotten upon Madri.

description: Commencement of the eighth day's combat
sn: अथोत्तरे महेष्वासाः सहसैन्या नराधिपाः। व्यूहं तं पूरयामासुयूंहशास्त्रविशारदाः॥
en: Other mighty bowmen, all rulers of earth, and versed in the are of forming arrays with their troop filled up that array.

description: Commencement of the eighth day's combat
sn: अभिमन्युस्ततः पश्चाद् विराटश्च महारथः। द्रौपदेयाश्च संहृष्टा राक्षसश्च घटोत्कचः॥
en: Abhimanyu and the mighty car-warrior Virata, the sons of Draupadi, and the Rakshasa Ghatotkacha were commanded to bring up the rear.

description: Commencement of the eighth day's combat
sn: एवमेतं महाव्यूहं व्यूह्य भारत पाण्डवाः। अतिष्ठन् समरे शूरा योद्धुकामा जयैषिणः॥
en: Thus, O Bharata, forming this mighty array, the heroic sons of Pandu occupied the fled anxiously longing for battle and for victory.

description: Commencement of the eighth day's combat
sn: भेरीशब्दैश्च विमलैर्विमित्रैः शङ्खनि:स्वनैः। क्ष्वेडितास्फोटितोत्क्रुष्टैर्नादिताः सर्वतो दिशः॥
en: Loud noise of the drums, mingled with the blare of conchs and the slapping of the armpits and the war-cries and shouts of the warriors, became dreadful, and filled all the quarters of heaven.

description: Commencement of the eighth day's combat
sn: ततः शूराः समासाद्य समरे ते परस्परम्। नेत्रेनिमिषै राजन्नवैक्षन्त परस्परम्॥
en: Thus those heroes, O king, encountering one another in battle, gazed at one another with windless eyes.

description: Commencement of the eighth day's combat
sn: नामभिस्ते मनुष्येन्द्र पूर्वं योधाः परस्परम्। युद्धाय समवर्तन्त समाहूयेतरेतरम्॥
en: Then, O foremost of men, challenging one another by their appellation, the warriors became engaged with one another.

description: Commencement of the eighth day's combat
sn: ततः प्रववृते युद्धं घोररूपं भयावहम्। तावकानां परेषां च निघ्नतामितरेतरम्॥
en: There raged a fierce and frightening battle between your warriors and those of the enemy, as they smote down one another.

description: Commencement of the eighth day's combat
sn: नाराचा निशिताः संख्ये सम्पतन्ति स्म भारत। व्यात्तानना भयकरा उरगा इव संघशः॥
en: Whetted long shafts, 0 Bharata, began to rain on all sides of the field of battle, like dreadful reptiles with mouths wide open.

description: Commencement of the eighth day's combat
sn: निष्पेतुर्विमलाः शक्त्यस्तैलधौताः सुतेजनाः। अम्बुदेभ्यो यथा राजन् भ्राजमानाः शतह्रदाः॥
en: Resplendent dares cleansed with oil and shot with great force, began to fall, O king, like flashing forks of lightening from the clouds.

description: Commencement of the eighth day's combat
sn: गदाश्च विमलैः पट्टैः पिनद्धाः स्वर्णभूषितैः। पतन्त्यस्तत्र दृश्यन्ते गिरिशृङ्गोपमाः शुभाः॥
en: Maces, covered with shining pierces of cloth and decked with gold were seen to fall on the field like so many beautiful crests of mountains.

description: Commencement of the eighth day's combat
sn: निस्त्रिंशाश्च व्यदृश्यन्त विमलाम्बरसंनिभाः। आर्षभाणि विचित्राणि शतचन्द्राणि भारत॥
en: Swords resplendent like the clear blue sky, glittered there. Bucklers made of bull's hide and decorated with hundred moons, O Bharata,

description: Commencement of the eighth day's combat
sn: अशोभन्त रणे राजन् पात्यमानानि सर्वशः। तेऽन्योन्यं समरे सेने युध्यमाने नराधिप॥
en: Falling on all sides, appeared beautiful, O king. O ruler of men, when the two armies fought with each other in that battle,

description: Commencement of the eighth day's combat
sn: अशोभेतां यथा देवदैत्यसेने समुद्यते। अभ्यद्रवन्त समरे तेऽन्योन्यं वै समन्ततः॥
en: They appeared beautiful like the hosts of the celestial and the Daityas engaged with one another (in days gone by). From all sides they rushed against one another in that battle.

description: Commencement of the eighth day's combat
sn: रथास्तु रथिभिस्तूर्णं प्रेषिताः परमाहवे। युगैर्युगानि संश्लिष्य युयुधुः पार्थिवर्षभाः॥
en: Excellent royal car-warriors rushing against their antagonist car-warriors fought on in that dreadful battle having the yokes of their chariots entangled with one another.

description: Commencement of the eighth day's combat
sn: दन्तिनां युध्यमानानां संघर्षात् पावकोऽभवत्। दन्तेषु भरतश्रेष्ठ सधूमः सर्वतोदिशम्॥
en: On all sides, O foremost of the Bharatas, were seen scintications of fire mixed with smoke emitted from the tusks of elephants in consequence of friction, as they fought on with one another.

description: Commencement of the eighth day's combat
sn: प्रासैरभिहताः केचिद् गजयोधाः समन्ततः। पतमानाः स्म दृश्यन्ते गिरिशृङ्गान्नगा इव॥
en: Some elephant-warriors struck down with Prasas, falling on the ground appeared like mountain trees overthrown from the peaks.

description: Commencement of the eighth day's combat
sn: पादाताश्चाप्यदृश्यन्त निघ्नन्तोऽथ परस्परम्। चित्ररूपधराः शूरा नखरप्रासयोधिनः॥
en: Heroic foot-soldiers of diverse appearance were seen to slay one another and to battle with lances that looked like their nails.

description: Commencement of the eighth day's combat
sn: अन्योन्यं ते समासाद्य कुरुपाण्डवसैनिकाः। अस्त्रैर्नानाविधैर्घोरै रणे निन्युर्यमक्षयम्॥
en: The combatants of the Kuru and the Pandava troops nearing one another, began to dispatch one another to the regions of death, with arrows of diverse shapes.

description: Commencement of the eighth day's combat
sn: ततः शान्तनवो भीष्मो रथघोषेण नादयन्। अभ्यागमद् रणे पार्थान् धनुः शब्देन महोयन्॥
en: Thereafter Bhishma the son of Shantanu, rushed against the Pandava host, filling the heavens with the clatter of his car and confounding the enemies with the twang of his bow.

description: Commencement of the eighth day's combat
sn: पाण्डवानां रथाश्चापि नदन्तो भैरवं स्वनम्। अभ्यद्रवन्त संयत्ता धृष्टद्युम्नपुरोगमाः॥
en: The car-warriors of the Pandava host also setting up a dreadful noise, rushed towards Bhishma, firmly resolved in fight and headed by Dhrishtadyumna himself.

description: Commencement of the eighth day's combat
sn: ततः प्रववृते युद्धं तव तेषां च भारत। नराश्वरथनागानां व्यतिषक्तं परस्परम्॥
en: Then, O Bharata, raged the battle between your as well as the enemy's troops, consisting of men, steeds, cars and elephants battle in which the combatants became entangled with one another.

sn: संजय उवाच भीष्मं तु समरे क्रुद्धं प्रतपन्तं समन्ततः। न शेकुः पाण्डवा दुष्टुं तपन्तमिव भास्करम्॥
en: Sanjaya said The Pandavas were unable to look at Bhishma burning like the solar disc, when inflamed with wrath he rushed to the thick of the) fight.

sn: ततः सर्वाणि सैन्यानि धर्मपुत्रस्य शासनात्। अभ्यद्रवन्त गाङ्गेयं मर्दयन्तं शितैः शरैः॥
en: Thereafter the whole army, by the order of the son of Dharma, rushed against the son of Ganga when the latter was wounding them with whetted shafts.

sn: स तु भीष्मोरणश्लाघी सोमकान् सहसंजयान्। पञ्चालांश्च महेष्वासान् पातयामास सायकैः॥
en: But Bhishma ever proud in battle, began to fell with his shafts, the Somakas, the Srinjayas and the Panchalas, all mighty wielders of the bow.

sn: ते वध्यमाना भीष्मेण पञ्चाला: भीष्ममेवाभ्ययुस्तूर्णं त्यक्त्वा मृत्युकृतं भयम्॥
en: Through thus slaughtered by Bhishma, the Panchalas with the Somakas impetuously rushed against Bhishma, abandoning all fear of death.

sn: स तेषां रथिनां वीरो भीष्मः शान्तनवो युधि। चिच्छेद सहसा राजन् बाहूनथ शिरांसि च॥
en: Then that foremost of car-warriors namely Bhishma the son of Shantanu, in that battle, O king, cut off the arms and heads of all those combatants.

sn: सोमकैः सह। विरथान् रथिनश्चक्रे पिता देवव्रतस्तव। पतितान्युत्तमाङ्गानि हयेभ्यो हयसादिनाम्॥
en: Your sire Devavrata deprived car-warriors of their car; and the heads of horse-soldiers fell fast as they rode on their chargers.

sn: निर्मनुष्यांश्च मातङ्गाशयानान् पर्वतोपमान्। अपश्याम महाराज भीष्मास्त्रेण प्रमोहितान्॥
en: We also beheld, O mighty monarch elephants deprived of their riders and fallen on the filled like so many hills and also paralyzed by the weapons of Bhishma.

sn: न तत्रासीत् पुमान् कश्चित् पाण्डवानां विशाम्पते। अन्यत्र रथिनां श्रेष्ठाद् भीमसेनान्महाबलात्॥
en: Not a single person of the Pandava host remained there on the field of battle, except, O ruler of men that foremost of car-warriors namely Bhimasena endued with great prowess.

sn: स हि भीष्मं समासाद्य ताडयामास संयुगे। ततो निष्टानको घोरो भीष्मभीमसमागमे॥ बभूव सर्वसैन्यानां घोररूपो भयानकः। तथैव पाण्डवाः हृष्टाः सिंहनादमथानदन्॥
en: Encountering Bhishma in battle, Bhima began to resist the former; a dreadful, fierce and deafening uproar arose among all the troops when Bhima and Bhishma thus encountered each another. Thereupon the Pandavas greatly delighted roared out their war-cries.

sn: ततो दुर्योधनो राजा सोदर्यैः परिवारितः। भीष्मं जुगोप समरे वर्तमाने जनक्षये॥
en: Thereupon king Duryodhana surrounded by his uterine brothers, protected Bhishma when that battle destructive of creatures was raging furiously.

sn: भीमस्तु सारथिं हत्वा भीष्मस्य रथिनां वरः। प्रद्रुताश्वे रथे तस्मिन् द्रवमाणे समन्ततः॥
en: Then that foremost of car-warriors Bhima, slew the charioteer of Bhishma; thereupon the steeds having none to check them ran away dragging the chariot.

sn: सुनाभस्य शरेणाशु शिरश्चिच्छेद भारत। क्षुरप्रेण सुतीक्ष्णेन स हतो न्यपतद् भुवि॥
en: Then that slayer of enemies, Bhima, with an arrow of the shape of horse-shoe and of exceeding sharpness, cut off quickly the head of Sunabha; and the latter fell down on the ground.

sn: हते तस्मिन् महाराज तव पुत्रे महारथे। नामृष्यन्त रणे शूराः सोदराः सप्त संयुगे॥
en: When that mighty car-warrior that fierce bowman namely your son Sunabha was slain in battle, O Sire, his other seven uterine brothers, all brave heroic, could not brook it in battle.

sn: आदित्यकेतुर्बह्वाशी कुण्डधारो महोदरः। अपराजितः पण्डितको विशालाक्षः सुदुर्जयः॥
en: Adityaketu, Bahvashin, Kundadhara, Mahodara, Aparajita, Panditaka, and Vishalaksha, all difficult of being conquered in battle,

sn: पाण्डवं चित्रसंनाहा विचित्रकवचध्वजाः। अभ्यद्रवन्त संग्रामे योद्धकामारिमर्दनाः॥
en: These seven grinders of foes, clad in coats of mail and owning wonderful armours and weapons, rushed to battle against the son of Pandu, desirous of fighting with him.

sn: महोदरस्तु समरे भीमं विव्याध पत्रिभिः। नवभिर्वज्रसंकाशैनमुचिं वृत्रहा यथा॥
en: Then in that battle, Mahendra pierced Bhima with nine winged shafts resembling the thunder bolt itself, like the slayer of Vritra piercing Namuchi (in the days of yore).

sn: आदित्यकेतुः सप्तत्या बह्वाशी चापि पञ्चभिः। नवत्या कुण्डधारच विशालाक्षश्च पञ्चभिः॥
en: Adityaketu pierced Bhima with seventy shafts, Bahvashin with five, Kundadhara with ninety and Vishalaksha with seven.

sn: अपराजितो महाराज पराजिष्णुर्महारथम्। शरैर्बहुभिरान द् भीमसेनं महाबलम्॥
en: That conqueror of foes, namely Aparajita himself, O mighty monarch, that mighty carwarrior, pierced the highly powerful Bhimasena, with innumerable shafts.

sn: रणे पण्डितकश्चैनं त्रिभिर्बाणैः समार्पयत्। स तन्न ममृषे भीमः शत्रुभिर्वधमाहवे॥
en: Panditaka pierced Bhima with three shafts in that battle. But Bhima did not tolerate these wounds inflicted by his enemies in that battle.

sn: धनुः प्रपड्य वामेन करेणामित्रकर्शनः। शिरश्चिच्छेद समरे शरेणानतपर्वणा॥
en: Then that grinder of foes (Bhima) pressing his bow with his left hand, with a straight knotted shaft cut off in that battle, the head of,

sn: अपराजितस्य सुनसं तव पुत्रस्य संयुगे। पराजितस्य भीमेन निपपात शिरो महीम्॥
en: Your son Aparajita, graced with a well formed nose. When he was thus conquered by Bhima, his head fell down on the ground.

sn: अथापरेण भल्लेन कुण्डधारं महारथम्। प्राहिणोन्मृत्युलोकाय सर्वलोकस्य पश्यतः॥
en: Then the former, with another broad headed shaft, dispatched the mighty car-warrior Kundadhara to the region of Dead even before the very eyes of the troops.

sn: ततः पुनरमेयात्मा प्रसंधाय शिलीमुखम्। प्रेषयामास समरे पण्डितं प्रति भारत॥
en: Then that one of immeasurable soul (Bhima), placing on his bow-string another shaft, sped it, O Bharata, against Panditaka in that battle.

sn: स शरः पण्डितं हत्वा विवेश धरणीतलम्। यथा नरं निहत्याशु भुजग: कालचोदितः॥
en: That shaft slaying Panditaka penetrated into the earth, even as a serpent urged by fate, enters the earth having bitten a person whose hour has come.

sn: विशालाक्षशिरश्छित्त्वा पातयामास भूतले। त्रिभिः शरैरदीनात्मा स्मरन् क्लेशं पुरातनम्॥
en: Thereafter that generous-hearted hero, O ruler of earth remembering the woe he (with his brothers) had to undergo, cutting off with three shafts the head of Vishalaksha felled it on the ground.

sn: महोदरं महेष्वासं नाराचेन स्तनान्तरे। विव्याध समरे राजन् स हतो न्यपतद् भुवि॥
en: He also pierced the mighty car-warrior Mahendra with a long shaft between his breasts, and O king, (thus stricken), the latter fell down dead on the ground.

sn: आदित्यकेतोः केतुं च छित्त्वा बाणेन संयुगे। भल्लेन भृशतीक्ष्णेन शिरश्चिच्छेद भारत॥
en: Severing the umbrella of Adityaketu with a shaft, Bhima cut down the former's head, O Bharata, with a broad-headed arrow of exceeding sharpness.

sn: बह्वाशिनं ततो भीमः शरेणानतपर्वणा। प्रेषयामास संक्रुद्धो यमस्य सदनं प्रति॥
en: Thereafter inflamed with rage, with a straight knotted shaft Bhima dispatched Bahvashin to the abode of Death.

sn: प्रदुद्रुवुस्ततस्तेऽन्य पुत्रास्तव विशाम्पते। मन्यमाना हि तत् सत्यं सभायां तस्य भाषितम्॥
en: Then O ruler of men, the rest of your sons fled away in all directions, considering that the words he had uttered in the assembly hall to be true.

sn: ततो दुर्योधनो राजा भ्रातृव्यसनकर्शितः। अब्रवीत् तावकान् योधान् भीमोऽयं युधि वध्यताम्।।३१।
en: Thereupon king Duryodhana, afflicted with the calamity that had befallen hill brothers, commanded his troops saying "Slay this Bhima."

sn: एवमेते महेष्वासाः पुत्रास्तव विशाम्पते। भ्रातृन् संदृश्य निहतान् प्रास्मरंस्ते हि तद् वच॥
en: Thus, O ruler of men, your sons, excellent bowmen, beholding their brothers slain, remembered the words,

sn: यदुक्तवान् महाप्राज्ञः क्षत्ता हितमनामयम्। तदिदं समनुप्राप्तं वचनं दिव्यदर्शिनः॥
en: Salutary and whole some, that the wonderfully wise Kshatriya had said. Those words of that true speaking one has now been realised,

sn: लोभमोहसमाविष्टः पुत्रप्रीत्या जनाधिप। न बुध्यसे पुरा यत् तत् तथ्यमुक्तं वचो महत्॥
en: Words, beneficial and true, to which you paid no heed in past days, being possessed by covetousness and folly, as also, O lord of wealth, by the affection for your sons.

sn: तथैव च वधार्थाय पुत्राणां पाण्डवो बली। नूनं जातो महाबाहुर्यथा हन्ति स्म कौरवान्॥
en: From the in thich that hero (Bhima) of longaiiii, . . .....nungine Kauravas, it may be asserted that mighty son of Pandu has surely taken his birth for the destruction of your sons.

sn: ततो दुर्योधनो राजा भीष्ममासाद्य संयुगे। दुःखेन महताऽऽविष्टो विललाप सुदुःखितः॥
en: Thereafter king Duryodhana possessed with overwhelming grief, approached Bhishma, and O Sire, began to lament before him in great sorrow.

sn: निहता भ्रातरः शूरा भीमसेनेन मे युधि। यतमानास्तथान्येऽपि हन्यन्ते सर्वसैनिकाः॥
en: “My heroic brothers have all been slain in battle by Bhimasena; and other soldiers, through striving their best of resist him, are all being slain and slaughtered.

sn: भवांश्च मध्यस्थतया नित्यमस्मानुपेक्षते। सोऽहं कुपथमारूढः पश्य दैवमिदं मम॥
en: Though you are always in our midst, yet always neglect us. Alas! what a wrong course have I taken! Behold my evil Destiny!”

sn: एतच्छ्रुत्वा वचः क्रूरं पिता देवव्रतस्तव। दुर्योधनमिदं वाक्यमब्रवीत् साश्रुलोचनः॥
en: Sanjaya said Hearing this, your father Devavrata, inflamed with rage, said these words in Suyodhana, with his eyes overflowing with tears.

sn: उक्तमेतन्मया पूर्वं द्रोणेन विदुरेण च। गान्धार्या च यशस्विन्या तत् त्वं तात न बुद्धवान्॥
en: Bhishma said Even this had been said before by myself, by Drona, by Vidura and by the illustrious lady Gandhari. But then, O Sire, you did not pay any heed to it.

sn: समयश्च मया पूर्वं कृतो वै शत्रुकर्शन। नाहं युधि नियोक्तव्यो नाप्याचार्यः कथंचन॥
en: O Grinder of foes, I have made arrangements with you that, neither myself nor the preceptor Drona shall survive this war.

sn: यं यं हि धार्तराष्ट्राणां भीमो द्रक्ष्यति संयुगे। हनिष्यति रणे नित्यं सत्यमेतद् ब्रवीमि ते॥
en: I tell you truly that, every one of ihe host of Dhritarashtra whom Bhima will deer in battle, he will slay in fight.

sn: स त्वं राजन् स्थिरो भूत्वा रणे कृत्वा दृढां मतिम्। योधयस्व रणे पार्थान् स्वर्गं परायणम्॥
en: Therefore, O king, with all your patience, and forming a firm resolution for battle, do you fight with the sons of Pritha, loO king upon paradise as your final goal.

sn: न शक्याः पाण्डवा जेतुं सेन्ट्रैरपि सुरासुरैः। तस्माद् युद्धे स्थिरां कृत्वा मतिं युद्ध्यस्व भारत॥
en: The sons of Pandu cannot be vanquished even by the celestial headed by Indra himself. Therefore, o Bharata, forming a firm determination for fight, do you fight on (with the Pandavas).

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच दृष्ट्वा मे निहतान् पुत्रान् बहूनेकेन संजय। भीष्मो द्रोणः कृपश्चैव किमकुर्वत संयुगे।।।
en: Dhritarashtra said Seeing my sons, so many in number, slain by one, what, O Sanjaya, did, Bhishma, Drona, and Kripa do?

sn: अहन्यहनि मे पुत्राः क्षयं गच्छन्ति संजय। मन्येऽहं सर्वथा सूत दैवेनोपहता भृशम्॥
en: Day by day, O Sanjaya, my sons are being destroyed. Indeed 0 Suta, I consider them to be completely struck down by (Evil) Destiny. are

sn: यत्र मे तनया: जीयन्ते न जयनत्युत। यत्र भीष्मस्य द्रोणस्य कृपस्य च महात्मनः॥ सौमदत्तेश्च वीरस्य भगदत्तस्य चोभयोः। अश्वत्थाम्नस्तथा तात शूराणामनिवर्तिनाम्॥ अन्येषां चैव शूराणां मध्यगास्तनया मम। यदहन्यन्त संग्रामे किमन्यद् भागधेयतः॥
en: In as much as, my sons are never victorious and are ever vanquished in battle, in as much as my sons remaining amidst, Drona, Bhishma, the illustrious Kripa, and the heroic son of Somadatta, and Bhagadatta, and O son, Ashvathama, and many other heroic and valiant warriors of high-soul, still slaughtered in battle, what can it be but (adverse) Fate?

sn: न हि दुर्योधनो मन्दः पुरा प्रोक्तमबुध्यत। वार्यमाणो मया तात भीष्मेण विदुरेण च॥
en: The wicked Duryodhana did not listen to our advise before. Forbidden, O son by myself, by Bhishma, by Vidura,

sn: गान्धार्या चैव दुर्मेधाः सततं हितकाम्यया। नाबुध्यत पुरा मोहात् तस्य प्राप्तमिदं फलम्॥
en: By his mother Gandhari ever anxious to compass his good, that perverse Duryodhana did not comprehend our words before through his folly. Now he reaps the fruits of his own actions,

sn: यद् भीमसेनः समरे पुत्रान् मम विचेतसः। अहन्यहनि संक्रुद्धो नयते यमसादनम्॥
en: In as much as, day by day, waxing worth in battle, Bhimasena is dispatching my sons to the abode of death.

sn: संजय उवाच इदं तत् समनुप्राप्तं क्षत्तुर्वचनमुत्तमम्। न बुद्धवानसि विभो प्रोच्यमानं हितं तदा॥
en: Sanjaya said Those excellent words of Khattva have now been verified, which, O lord, uttered as they were for your good, you did not pay any heed to before.

sn: निवारय सुतान् द्यूतात् पाण्डवान् मा दुहेति च। सुहृदां हितकामानां ब्रुवतां तत् तदेव च॥
en: 'Withhold your sons from the dice, do not persecute the sons of Pandu', these words, spoken by your well-wishing friends,

sn: न शुश्रूषसि तद् वाक्यं मर्त्यः पथ्यमिवौषधम्। तदेव त्वामनुप्राप्तं वचनं साधुभाषितम्॥
en: You did not listen to, like one on death-bed neglecting wholesome medicine. It is now that you relies those words spoken by the righteous.

sn: विदुरद्रोणभीष्माणां तथान्येषां हितैषिणाम्। अकृत्वा वचनं पथ्यं क्षयं गच्छन्ति कौरवाः॥
en: Disregarding the salutary advice offered by well-wishing friends like Bhishma, Drona, Vidura and others, the descendants of the Kuru race are reaping destruction.

sn: तदेतत् समनुप्राप्तं पूर्वमेव विशाम्पते। तस्मात् त्वं शृणु तत्त्वेन यथा युद्धमवर्तत॥
en: Now, O monarch, the inevitable consequence of all that has arrived. Listen now from me as to how the battle was fought.

sn: मध्याह्ने सुमहारौद्रः संग्रामः समपद्यत। लोकक्षयकरो राजस्तन्मे निगदतः शृणु।॥
en: At mid-day, O king, the battle regard fiercely and the carnage that took place was exceedingly terrible. Hear me narrate it.

sn: ततः सर्वाणि सैन्यानि धर्मपुत्रस्य शासनात्। संरब्धान्यभ्यवर्तन्त भीष्ममेव जिघांसया॥
en: Then at the command of the son of Dharma (Yudhishthira), all the troops of the Pandava host inflamed with rage, rushed against Bhishma, out of a desire for slaying him.

sn: धृष्टद्युम्नः शिखण्डी च सात्यकिश्च महारथतः। युक्तानीका महाराज भीष्ममेव समभ्ययुः॥
en: Dhrishtadyumna, Shikhandin and the mighty car-warriors Satyaki, uniting together their divisions, rushed, O mighty monarch, against Bhishma.

sn: विराटो द्रुपदश्चैव सहिताः सर्वसोमकैः। अभ्यद्रवन्त संग्रामे भीष्ममेव महारथम्॥
en: Then the mighty car-warriors Virata and Drupada accompanied by all the Somakas rushed even against Bhishma himself.

sn: केकया धृष्टकेतुश्च कुन्तिभोजश्च दंशितः। युक्तानीका महाराज भीष्ममेव समभ्ययुः॥
en: The Kaikeyas, and Dhrishtaketu, and Kuntibhoja, clad in mail and supported by their armies, rushed, O monarch, against Bhishma himself.

sn: अर्जुनो द्रौपदेयाश्च चेकितानश्च वीर्यवान्। दुर्योधनसमादिष्टान् राज्ञः सर्वान् समभ्ययुः॥
en: Arjuna, the son of Draupadi, and the highly powerful Chekitana, rushed against the kings commanded by Duryodhana himself.

sn: अभिमन्युस्तथा शूरो हैडिम्बश्च महारथः। भीमसेनश्च संक्रुद्धस्तेऽभ्यधावन्त कौरवान्॥
en: Thereafter, the valiant Abhimanyu, that mighty car-warrior, the son of Hidimba, and Bhimasena himself, all wrought up with wrath, assaulted the Kauravas.

sn: त्रिधाभूतैरवध्यन्त पाण्डवैः कौरवा युधि। तथैव कौरवै राजन्नवध्यन्त परे रणे॥
en: Thus were the Kauravas slain in battle by the Pandavas divided in two divisions, so also, O monarch, the Pandavas were slaughtered by the Kauravas in that fight.

sn: द्रोणस्तु रथिनः श्रेष्ठान् सोमकान् संजयैः सह। अभ्यधावत संक्रुद्धः प्रेषयिष्यन् यमक्षयम्॥
en: Then that foremost of car-warriors namely Drona, excited with rage, rushed against the 'Somakas and the Srinjayas, dispatching them to the mansion of death.

sn: तत्राक्रन्दो महानासीत् सुंजयानां महात्मनाम्। वध्यतां समरे राजन् भारद्वाजेन धन्विना॥
en: Then the high-souled Srinjaya, set up a loud and distressful cry when, o king they were thus being slaughtered in battle by that great bowman the son of Bharadvaja.

sn: द्रोणेन निहतास्तत्र क्षत्रिया बहवो रणे। विचेष्टन्तो ह्यदृश्यन्त व्याधिक्लिष्टा नरा इव॥
en: Innumerable Kshatriya warriors, smitten by Drona were seen to conclusive like persons suffering from agonising ailments.

sn: कूजतां क्रन्दतां चैव रस्तनतां चैव भारत। अनिशं शुश्रुवै शब्दः क्षुत्क्लिष्टानां नृणामिव॥
en: They gleaned and moaned and cries and uttered cries of agony in consequence of which a confused noise was heard, resembling that produced by men struck with famine.

sn: तथैव कौरवेयाणां भीमसेनो महाबलः। चकार कदनं घोरं क्रुद्धः काल इवापरः॥
en: On the other hand, the highly puissant Bhimasena, waxing worth, caused a dreadful carnage among the Kaurava ranks like another god of Death himself.

sn: वध्यतां तत्र सैन्यानामन्योन्येन महारणे। प्रावर्तत नदी घोरा रुधिरौघप्रवाहिनी॥
en: In that fierce fight, as the troops slew one another, a terrible river started up into existence on the field of battle, of which the waves and currents were formed of blood.

sn: स संग्रामो महाराज घोररूपोऽभवन्महान्। कुरूणां पाण्डवानां च यमराष्ट्रविवर्धनः॥
en: That great battle, O mighty monarch, between the Kurus and the Pandavas, was indeed very dreadful in its aspect; and it considerably swelled the population of Death's domain.

sn: ततो भीमो रणे क्रुद्धो रभसश्च विशेषतः। गजानीकं समासाद्य प्रेषयामास मृत्यवे॥
en: Thereafter Bhima inflamed with rage, fell with impetuosity upon the elephant-division of the Kurus, and many were the beasts that he sent to the regions of Death.

sn: तत्र भारत भीमेन नाराजाभिहता गजाः। पेतुर्नेदुश्च सेदुश्च दिसश्च परिबभ्रमुः॥
en: There, in that battle, O Bharata, many were the elephants that pierced with Nacharas by Bhima, fell and were confounded and shrieked and careered in all directions.

sn: छिन्नहस्ता महानागाश्छिन्नगात्राश्च मारिष। क्रौञ्चवद् व्यनदन् भीताः पृथिवीमधिशेरते॥
en: Huge elephants, with their trucks cut off, and their bodies mangled, fell down on the earth, O sire, screaming like cranes.

sn: नकुलः सहदेवश्च हयानीकमभिद्रुतौ। ते हयाः काञ्चनापीडा रुक्मभाण्डपरिच्छदाः॥
en: Nakula and Sahadeva, both together, charged the cavalry-division. Those horses decked with golden chains and caparisons of the same metal.

sn: वध्यमाना व्यदृश्यन्त शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः। पतिद्भिस्तुरगै राजन् समास्तीर्यत मेदिनी॥
en: Were scen to be slain by hundreds and by thousands; and O monarch, the earth was strewn over with falling horses.

sn: निर्जिकैश्च श्वसद्धिश्च कूजद्भिश्च गतासुभिः। हयैर्बभौ नरश्रेष्ठ नानारूपधरैर्धरा॥
en: The earth looked awful, O foremost of men, being covered over with horses of diverse appearance, some of which, again were breathing hard, some meaning and some deprived of their lives.

sn: अर्जुनेन हतैः संख्ये तथा भारत राजभिः। प्रबभौ वसुधा घोरा तत्र तत्र विशाम्पते॥
en: The earth also, O Bharata, appeared lawfully beautiful being over strewn with kings slain by Arjuna in the encounter.

sn: स्थैर्भग्नैर्ध्वजैश्छिन्नैनिकृत्तैश्च महायुधैः। चामरैर्व्यजनैश्चैव छत्रैश्च सुमहाप्रभैः॥
en: With shattered chariots, and torn flags and umbrellas of great effulgence, with rent Chamaras and fans, and with mighty weapons splintered into pierces,

sn: हारैर्निष्कैः सकेयूरैः शिरोभिश्च सकुण्डलैः। उष्णीषैरपविद्धैश्च पताकाभिश्च सर्वशः॥
en: With garlands and necklaces of gold, with heads graced with ear-rings, with bracelets, with head-gears fallen off from the heads, and with streamers,

sn: अनुकषैः शुभै राजन् योक्त्रैश्चैव सरश्मिभिः। संकीर्णा वसुधा भाति वसन्ते कुसुमैरिव॥
en: With well-made car-bottoms, and O king, with reins and riggings-covered with all these things, the earth appeared as beautiful as she appears during the spring being strewn over with blossoms.

sn: एवमेष क्षयो वृत्तः पाण्डूनामपि भारत। क्रुद्ध शान्तनवे भीष्मे द्रोणे च रथसत्तमे॥
en: Such also was the carnage caused in the Pandava host, О Bharata, when the son of Shantanu, and Drona that foremost of carwarriors were enraged;

sn: अश्वत्थाम्नि कृपे चैव तथैव कृतवर्मणि। तथेतरेषु क्रुद्धेषु तावकानामपि क्षयः॥
en: As also when Ashvathama, and Kripa and Kritavarma (were wrought up with rage). So also your troops under went destruction when the other side was inflamed with wrath.

sn: संजय उवाच वर्तमाने तथा रौद्रे राजन् वीरवरक्षये। शकुनिः सौबलः श्रीमान् पाण्डवान् समुपाद्रवत्॥
en: Sanjaya said When, o king, that dreadful battle destructive of excellent heroes was thus raging, Subala's prosperous son Shakuni rushed against the Pandava hosts.

sn: तथैव सात्वतो राजन् हार्दिक्यः परवीरहा। अभ्यद्रवत संग्रामे पाण्डवानां वरूथिनीम्॥
en: Also, O king, that slayer of foes, that son of Hridika, of the Satvata race, proceeded in battle against the Pandava divisions.

sn: तत: काम्बोजमुख्यानां नदीजानां च वाजिनाम्। आरट्टानां महीजानां सिन्धुजानां च सर्वशः॥ वनायुजानां शुभ्राणां तथा पर्वतवासिनाम्। वाजिनां बहुभिः संख्ये समन्तात् परिवारयन्॥ ये चापरे तित्तिरिजा जवना वातरंहसः। सुवर्णालंकृतैरेतैर्वर्मवद्भिः सुकल्पितैः॥
en: Several warriors of your army, with a mighty division of horses consisting of best animals of the Kamboja breed, of those born in lands watered by many rivers, of those belonging to Aratta, Mahi, Sindhu, and Vanayu, of those that were white-hued, of those born in mountains tracts, and of those exceedingly swift and endued with the fleetness of wind, and of those of the Tittiri breed, surrounded on all sides the Pandava army. With many steeds duly clad in mail and decked with caparisons of gold,

sn: हयैर्वातजवैर्मुख्यैः पाण्डवस्य सुतो बली। अभ्यवर्तत तत् सैन्यं हृष्टरूपः परंतपः॥
en: All best of their class, and fleet as the wind itself, the highly puissant son of the Pandava (Arjuna), of cheerful appearance and the slayer of his foes, rushed against that division of horses belonging to the enemy.

sn: अर्जुनस्य सुतः श्रीमानिरावान् नाम वीर्यवान्। स्नुषायां नागराजस्य जातः पार्थेन धीमता॥
en: This prosperous son of Arjuna by name Iravat, endued with great prowess was begotten by the highly intelligent Partha (Arjuna) on the daughter of the sovereign of the Nagas.

sn: ऐरावतेन सा दत्ता अनपत्या महात्मना। पतौ हते सुपर्णेन कृपणा दीनचेतना॥
en: Her husband having been slain by Suparna (Garuda), she was helpless and completely depressed in mind; she was then bestowed upon Arjuna by the illustrious Airavata.

sn: भार्यार्थं तां च जग्राह पार्थः कामवशानुगाम्। एवमेष समुत्पन्नः परपक्षेऽर्जुनात्मजः॥
en: As she came to him under the influence of desire, the son of Pritha accepted her as his wife. Thus it was that Arjuna's son was begotten upon another's wife.

sn: स नागलोके संवृद्धो मात्रा च परिरक्षितः। पितृव्येण परित्यक्तः पार्थद्वेषाद् दुरात्मना॥
en: This son of Arjuna was brought up in the regions of the Nagas, and was protected by his mother. He was abandoned by his wickedsouled uncle from his animosity for the son of Pritha.

sn: रूपवान् बलसम्पन्नो गुणवान् सत्यविक्रमः। इन्द्रलोकं जगामाशु श्रुत्वा तत्रार्जुनं गतम्॥
en: Hearing that Arjuna Lad come to the regions of Indra, that handsome, highly puissant and accomplished Iravat of prowess that could not be baffled, hide to those regions.

sn: सोऽभिगम्य महाबाहुः पितरं सत्यविक्रमः। अभ्यवादयदव्यग्रो विनयेन कृताञ्जलिः॥
en: That mighty-armed hero of infallible prowess, approaching his father did obeisance to him, duly folding his palms.

sn: न्यवेदयत चात्मानमर्जुनस्य महात्मनः। इरावानस्मि भद्रं ते पुत्रश्चाहं तव प्रभो॥
en: He introduced himself to the illustrious Arjuna saying-'I am your son Iravat, O lord, may good betide you.'

sn: मातुः समागमो यश्च तत् सर्वं प्रत्यवेदयत्। तच्च सर्वं यथावृत्तमनुसस्मार पाण्डवः॥
en: He also reminded Arjuna of the circumstances under which the latter met his mother. Then the of Pandu also remembered them a right.

sn: परिष्वज्य सुतं चापि आत्मनः सदृशं गुणैः। प्रीतिमाननयत् पार्थो देवराजनिवेशन॥
en: Then in the mansion of the chief of the celestial, the son of Pritha embracing his son equal to him in his acquirements, was highly delighted.

sn: सोऽर्जुनेन समाज्ञप्तो देवलोके तदा नृप। प्रीतिपूर्वं महाबाहुः स्वकार्यं प्रति भारत॥
en: Then that mighty-armed hero (Iravat), O king, was thus cheerfully commanded by Arjuna, in the celestial regions with regard to his own business (namely the impending war with the Kurus).

sn: युद्धकाले त्वयाऽस्माकं साह्यं देयमिति प्रभो। बाढमित्येवमुक्त्वा तु युद्धकाल इहागतः॥
en: 'O son, when the battle would take place, you should render us assistance. He then said 'yea' to the words of his father; and now that the hour has arrived, he also presented himself, Son

sn: कामवर्णजवैरश्चैर्बहुभिः संवृतो नृप। ते हयाः काञ्चनापीडा नानावर्णा मनोजवाः॥
en: 0 king, surrounded by parti-coloured horses, countless in number. Those horses caparisoned with trappings of gold and of diverse hues and great fleetness,

sn: उत्पेतुः सहसा राजन् हंसा इव महोदधौ। ते त्वदीयान् समासाद्य हयसंघान् मनोजवान्॥
en: O king, suddenly appeared on the field like swans on the bosom of the mighty-main. Those horses encountering your division of fleetest steeds,

sn: क्रोडैः क्रोडानभिनन्तो घोणाभिश्च परस्परम्। निपेतुः सहसा राजन् सुवेगाभिहता भुवि॥
en: Struck one another with their chests and noses. Overthrown by their own impetuosity, O king, they began to fall down suddenly on the earth.

sn: निपतद्भिस्तथा तैश्च हयसंधैः परस्परम्। शुश्रुवे दारुणः शब्दः सुपर्णपतने यथा॥
en: When those two horse divisions thus clashed against one another (and some fell down), a terrible sound, resembling that of Suparna's swoop was heard there.

sn: तथैव तावका राजन् समेत्यान्योन्यमाहवे। परस्परवधं घोरं चक्रुस्ते हयसादिनः॥
en: So also, O mighty monarch, those who rode on these steeds nearing one another in that dreadful battle, fell upon slaughtering one another mercilessly.

sn: तस्मिंस्तथा वर्तमाने संकुले तुमुले भृशम्। उभयोरपि संशान्ता हयसङ्घाः समन्ततः॥
en: When that general and dreadful encounter regard fiercely, the chargers of the two hosts, seized with panic, coursed wildly all over the field.

sn: प्रक्षीणसायकाः शूरा निहताश्वाः श्रमातुराः। विलयं समनुप्राप्तास्तक्षमाणाः परस्परम्॥
en: Warriors, mutilated with shafts, with their chargers slain, and themselves exhausted with was fatigue, began to perish, cutting one another with their swords.

sn: ततः क्षीणे हयानीके किंचिच्छेषे च भारत। सौबलस्यानुजाः शूरा निर्गता रणमूर्धनि॥
en: Then when that horse-division considerably thinned and very few survived, O Bharata, the younger brothers of Subala's son (Shakuni), all endued with heroism, rode out in the van (of the hostile ranks).

sn: वायुवेगसमस्पर्शाञ्जवे वायुसमांश्च ते। आरुह्य बलसम्पन्नान् वयःस्थांस्तुगोत्तमान्॥
en: On horses, the contract of whose dash was overthrowing like the vehemence of the wind, which were equal to the wind in fleetness, and which were all excellent chargers, well-broken and youthful.

sn: गजो गवाक्षो वृषभश्चर्मवानार्जवः शुकः। षडेते बलसम्पन्ना निर्ययुर्महतो बलात्॥
en: Gaja, Gavaksha, Vrishabha, Charmavan, Arjava and Shuka, these six highly puissant heroes rode out of the mighty ranks the Kauravas,

sn: वार्यमाणाः शकुनिना तैश्च योधैर्महाबलैः। संनद्धा युद्धकुशला रौद्ररूपा महाबलाः॥
en: Supported by Shakuni and their respective mighty divisions consisting of highly powerful warriors, themselves covered with amours, accomplished in battle, fierce in aspect and possessed of great strength.

sn: तदनीकं महाबाहो भित्तवा परमदुर्जयम्। बलेन महता युक्ताः स्वर्गाय विजयैषिणः॥
en: Breaking through that invincible cavalry division of Iravat, desirous of victory and longing for paradise and endued with great strength,

sn: विविशुस्ते तदा हृष्टा गान्धारा युद्धदुर्मदाः। तान् प्रविष्टांस्तदा दृष्ट्वा इरावानपि वीर्यवान्॥
en: Those Gandhara heroes formidable in battle cheerfully penetrated into it. Thereupon the highly puissant Iravat, beholding them very delightful,

sn: अब्रवीत् समरे योधान् विचित्रान् दारुणायुधान्। यथैते धार्तराष्ट्रस्य योधाः सानुगवाहनाः॥ हन्यन्ते समरे सर्वे तथा नीतिर्विधीयताम्। बाढमित्येवमुक्त्वा ते सर्वे योधा इरावतः॥
en: Thus commanded his own warriors adorned with wonderful ornaments and weapons, saying 'Adopt such measures by which these warriors of Dhritarashtra's son may all be destroyed with their weapons and vehicles. Saying 'Yes,' all those warriors belonging to Iravat,

sn: जह्वस्तेषां बलानीकं दुर्जयं समरे परैः। तदनीकमनीकेन समरे वीक्ष्य पातितम्॥
en: Slew in battle that division of your army difficult of being conquered by the enemy. Beholding their division crushed by the division of Iravat,

sn: अमृष्यमाणास्ते सर्वे सुबलस्यात्मजा रणे। इरावन्तमभिदुत्य सर्वतः पर्यवारयन्॥
en: The sons of Subala not tolerating it is battle, rushing at Iravat, surrounded him on sides.

sn: तादडयन्तः शितैः परासैश्चोदयन्तः परस्परम्। ते शूराः पर्यधावन्त कुर्वन्तो महदाकुलम्॥
en: Piercing Iravat with sharp lances and urging their warriors against him, those heroes careered over the field creating a great confusion.

sn: इरावानथ निर्भिन्नः प्रासैस्तीक्ष्णैर्महात्मभिः। स्रवता रुधिरेणाक्तस्तोत्रैविद्धं इव द्विपः॥
en: Then Iravat pierced with sharp lances by those high-souled warriors and covered with blood that was trickling down from his wounds, appeared like an elephant pierced with the hook.

sn: पुरतोऽपि च पृष्ठे च पार्श्वयोश्च भृशाहतः। एको बहुभिरत्यर्थं धैर्याद् राजन् न विव्यथे॥
en: Single-handed as he was, he was smitten sore by many, on his chest, his back, and his flanks; but o king he flinched not in consequence of his great patience.

sn: इरावानपि संकुद्धः सर्वांस्तान् निशितैः शरैः। मोहयामास समरे विद्ध्वा परपुरंजयः॥
en: Thereupon Iravat, conqueror of hostile cities, waxing worth, piercing all of them with whetted shafts, deprived them of their senses.

sn: प्रासानुत्कृय तरसा स्वशरीरादरिंदमः। तैरेव ताडयमास सुबलस्यात्मजान् रणे॥
en: Then drawing out all those lances from his own body, that subduer of enemies wounded the sons of Subala in battle even with those very lances.

sn: विकृष्य च शितं खङ्गं गृहीत्वा च शरावरम्। पदातिर्दृतमागच्छज्जिघांसुः सौबलान् युधि॥
en: Then drawing his sharp saber and holding his buckler, he (Iravat) quickly ran on foot desirous of slaying the sons of Subala, in that battle.

sn: ततः प्रत्यागतप्राणाः सर्वे ते सुबलात्मजाः। भूयः क्रोधसमाविष्टा इरावन्तमभिद्रुताः॥
en: Then all those sons of Subala regaining consciousness, possessed by rage, once more rushed towards Iravat.

sn: इरावानपि खड्ड्रेन दर्शयन् पाणिलाघवम्। अभ्यवर्तत तान् सर्वान् सौबलान् बलदर्पितः।। :॥
en: Iravat also proud of his strength, and displaying the lightness of his hands by whirling his sword, rushed against all those sons of Subala.

sn: लाघवेनाथ चरतः सर्वे ते सुबलात्मजाः। अन्तरं नाभ्यगच्छन्त चरन्तः शीघ्रगैर्हयैः॥
en: Those sons of Subala, riding on fleet chargers could find no opportunity for striking Iravat moving as he was with great agility.

sn: भूमिष्ठमथ तं संख्ये सम्प्रदृश्य ततः पुनः। परिवार्य भृशं सर्वे ग्रहीतुमुपचक्रमुः:॥
en: Then beholding Iravat standing on foot on the ground, those warriors surrounding him close, endeavored to capture him.

sn: अथाभ्याशगतानां स खड़ेनामित्रकर्शनः। असिहस्तापहस्ताभ्यः तेषां गात्राण्यकृन्तत॥
en: once more Then Iravat, that slayer of foes, beholding them very near to himself, with his sword, cut off their right and left arms (lit: with which they wielded their swords and their bows respectively), and also mutilated their bodies.

sn: आयुधानि च सर्वेषां बाहुनपि विभूषितान्। अपतन्तः निकृत्ताङ्गा मृता भूमौ गतासवः॥
en: Their weapons and their hands furnished with these, fell down on earth, and they themselves deprived of life and with their bodies mangled, fell down dead.

sn: वृषभस्तु महाराज बहुधा विपरिक्षतः। अमुच्यत महारौद्रात् तस्माद् वीरावकर्तनात्॥
en: Only Vrishabha, O mighty monarch, with his body mangled with wounds, escaped, with difficulty, alive from that most terrible combat destructive of heroes.

sn: तान् सर्वान् पतितान् दृष्ट्वा भीतो दुर्योधनस्ततः। अभ्यधावत संक्रुद्धो राक्षसं घोरदर्शनम्॥
en: Then your son Duryodhana beholding all those heroes crushed, waxing worth, said these words unto the Rakshasa of fearful appearance,

sn: आय॑शृङ्गि महेष्वासं मायाविनमरिंदमम्। वैरिणं भीमसेनस्य पूर्वं बकवधेन वै॥
en: That fierce bowman, that subduer of foes, that one of great illusive energies, viz., Alambusha the son of Rishyashringa, who was the enemy of Bhimasena, in consequence of the latter's slaughter of Vaka.

sn: पश्य वीर यथा ह्येष फाल्गुनस्य सुतो बली। मायावी विप्रियं कर्तुमकार्षीन्मे बलक्षयम्॥
en: 'Behold O hero, how this puissant son of Arjuna, versed in illusions, has done me this terrible wrong in the shape of destroying my forces?

sn: त्वं च कामगमस्तात मायास्त्रे च विशारदः। कृतवैरश्च पार्थेन तस्मादेन रणे जहि॥
en: You are also, O sire, capable of going every where at your unrestrained will and are also versed in all weapons of illusion; you are moreover the sworn enemy of Pritha's son; so slay me this one in battle.' Sworn

sn: बाढमित्येवमुक्त्वा तु राक्षसो घोरदर्शनः। प्रययौ सिंहनादेन यत्रार्जुनसुतो युवा॥
en: Saying 'yea' (to Duryodhana's words), that Rakshasas of terrible appearance rushed, uttering his war-cries, to the spot where the youthful son of Arjuna was.

sn: आरूढैयुद्धकुशलैर्विमलप्रासयोधिभिः। वीरैः प्रहारिभिर्युक्तैः स्वैरनीकैः समावृतः॥
en: Alambusha was supported by the heroic lancers of his own division, all accomplished in smiting and well-mounted, skillful in fight, bearing resplendent lances.

sn: हतशेषैर्महाराज द्विसाहौर्हयोत्तमैः। निहन्तुकामः समरे इरावन्तं महाबलम्॥
en: He was desirous, O king, of slaying in battle the highly puissant Iravat, along with the two thousands excellent cavalry that survived the recent conflict.

sn: इरावानपि संक्रुद्धस्त्वरमाणः पराक्रमी। हन्तुकामममित्रघ्नो राक्षसं प्रत्यवारयत्॥
en: The most agile and puissant Iravat also, that slayer of enemies, waxing worth began to resist the Rakshasa who was desirous of slaying him.

sn: तमापतन्तं सम्प्रेक्ष्य राक्षसः सुमहाबलः। त्वरमाणस्ततो मायां प्रयोक्तुमुपचक्रमे॥
en: That Rakshasa (Alambusha) endued with great strength, beholding Iravat make towards himself, speedily began to put forth his illusions.

sn: तेन मायामयाः सृष्टा हयास्तावन्त एव हि। स्वारूढा राक्षसैोरैः शूलपट्टिशधारिभिः॥
en: He then created, as many illusive chargers, all mounted by fierce Rakshasas, bearing in their hands lances and battle axes.

sn: ते संरब्धाः समागम्य द्विसाहस्राः प्रहारिणः। अचिराद् गमयामासुः प्रेतलोकं परस्परम्॥
en: These two thousand well-disciplined smiters, advancing with wrath. and encountering Iravat's division, were both speedily dispatched to the regions of the departed.

sn: तस्मिंस्तु निहते सैन्ये तावुभो युद्धदुर्मदौ। संग्रामे समतिष्ठेतां यथा वै वृत्रवासवौ॥
en: When both the divisions of Iravat and Alambusha were slain in battle, those two heroes, both formidable in battle, encountered each other like Indra and Vritra.

sn: आद्रवन्तमभिप्रेक्ष्य राक्षसं युद्धदुर्मदम्। इरावानथ संरब्धः प्रत्यधावन्महाबलः॥
en: Seeing that Rakshasa invincible in battle make towards himself, the highly puissant Iravat, exited with wrath, began to resist him;

sn: समभ्याशगतस्याजौ तस्य खङ्गेन दुर्मतेः। चिच्छेद कार्मुकं दीप्तं शरावापं च सत्वरम्॥
en: And when the former had come very near to him, with his sword he cut off that wicked one's bow and shafts into five fragments each.

sn: स निकृत्तं धनुर्दृष्ट्वा खं जवेन समाविशत्। इरावन्तमभिक्रुद्धं मोहयन्निव मायया॥
en: Seeing his bow severed, he speedily mounted on the sky, confounding as it were with his illusive powers Iravat who was greatly excited with rage.

sn: ततोऽन्तरिक्षमुत्पत्य इरावानपि राक्षसम्। विमोहयित्वा मायाभिस्तस्य गात्राणि सायकैः॥ चिच्छेद सर्वमर्मज्ञः कामरूपो दुरासदः। तथा स राक्षसश्रेष्ठः शरैः कृत्तः पुनः पुनः॥
en: Thereupon mounting on the sky, that unapproachable hero Iravat, versed in all duty and capable of assuming any from at will, confounding with his illusive powers that Rakshasa, cut off the latter's limbs in that battle. Thus was that foremost of Rakshasas cut into pieces again and again.

sn: सम्बभूव महाराज समवाप च यौवनम्। माया हि सहजा तेषां वयो रूपं च कामजम्॥
en: But, O mighty monarch, Alambusha was again born anew, in the fullness of his youth. Illusion is natural with them (the Rakshasas) and their age and appearance are the result of their will. son

sn: एवं तद् राक्षसस्याङ्गं छिन्नं छिन्नं बभूव ह। इरावानपि संक्रुद्धो राक्षसं तं महाबलम्॥ परश्वधेन तीक्ष्णेन चिच्छेद च पुनः पुनः। स तेन बलिना वीरश्छिद्यमान इरावता॥
en: Thus the limbs of the Rakshasa again and again cut to pieces, appeared very beautiful. Thereupon the enraged Iravat repeatedly cut that Rakshasa endued with great strength with his battle axe of exceeding sharpness. Cut like a tree by that powerful Iravat, that heroic.

sn: राक्षसोऽप्यनदद् घोरं स शब्दस्तुमुलोऽभवत्। परश्वधक्षतं रक्षः सुस्राव बहु शोणितम्॥
en: Rakshasa uttered a dreadful roar; that created a terrible sound. Cut with the strokes of the battle-axes, the Rakshasa shed blood profusely.

sn: ततश्चक्रोध बलवांश्चक्रे वेगं च संयुगे। आर्थ्यशृङ्गिस्तथा दृष्ट्वा समरे शत्रुमूर्जितम्॥
en: Thereafter that of Rishyashringa possessed of great strength, beholding his puissant antagonist blaze forth in that battle, became inflamed with fury and put forth his own powers in that battle.

sn: कृत्वा घोरं महद् रूपं ग्रहीतुमुपचक्रमे। अर्जुनस्य सुतं वीरमिरावन्तं यशस्विनम्॥
en: Assuming a dreadful and prodigious form he tried to capture the son of Arjuna, namely the illustrious Iravat.

sn: संग्रामशिरसो मध्ये सर्वेषां तत्र पश्यताम्। तां दृष्ट्वा तादृशीं मायां राक्षसस्य दुरात्मनः॥
en: In the very thick of the fright, before the very eyes of all the combatants, seeing that; illusion forth by that wicked-souled Rakshasa,

sn: इरावानपि संक्रुद्धो मायां स्रष्टुं प्रचक्रमे। तस्य क्रोधाभिभूतस्य समरेष्वनिवर्तिनः॥
en: Iravat, highly excited with rage, himself began to create great illusions. Then when that unreceding hero was over-whelmed with rage in that battle,

sn: योऽन्वयो मातृकस्तस्य स एनमभिपेदिवान्। स नागैर्बहुभी राजन्निरावान् संवृतो रणे॥
en: A Naga related to him through his mother came to his support; surrounded on all side by numerous Nagas, O king, in that battle,

sn: दधार सुमहद् रूपमनन्त इव भोगवान्। ततो बहुविधैर्नागेश्छादयामास राक्षसम्॥
en: That Naga, assumed a prodigious form mighty like that of Ananta himself. Thereafter with those innumerable and diverse kinds of Nagas, he covered the Rakshasa.

sn: छाद्यमानस्तु नागैः स ध्यात्वा राक्षसपुङ्गवः। सौपर्ण रूपमास्थाय भक्षयामास पन्नगान्॥
en: Thus surrounded by the Nagas, that foremost of the Rakshasas, reflecting for a while, assumed the form of Garuda and devoured all those serpents.

sn: मायया भक्षिते तस्मिन्नन्वये तस्य मातृके। विमोहितमिरावन्तं न्यहनद् राक्षसोऽसिना॥
en: What that Naga, related to him through his mother's side had been thus devoured through the illusive powers of Alambusha, Iravat became confounded and the Rakshasa slew him with his sword.

sn: सकुण्डलं समुकुटं पद्मेन्दुसदृशप्रभम्। इरावत: शिरो रक्षः पातयामास भूतले॥
en: Then that Rakshasa felled on the earth the head of Iravat graced with earrings and a diadem, and effulgent like the moon or the lotus.

sn: तस्मिंस्तु विहते वीरे राक्षसेनार्जुनात्मजे। विशोकाः समपद्यन्त धार्तराष्ट्राः सराजकाः॥
en: When that heroic son of Arjuna had been slain by the Rakshasa, the sons of Dhritarashtra with all their partisan kings, were relieved of their anxiety.

sn: तस्मिन् महति संग्रामे तादृशे भैरवे पुनः। महान् व्यतिकरो घोरः सेनयोः समपद्यत॥
en: In that great and dreadful battle between those two armics, awful was the carnage that then took place.

sn: गजा हयाः पदाताश्च विमिश्रा दन्तिभिर्हताः। रथाश्वाः दन्तिनश्चैव पत्तिभिस्तत्र सूदिताः॥
en: Horses and elephants, and foot-soldiers, mixing with one another, was siain by the tuskers; and car-warriors, and horse-soldiers, and tuskers were also slain in that battle by foot-soldiers.

sn: तथा पत्तिरथौघाश्च हयाश्च बहवो रणे। रथिभिनिहता राजंस्तव तेषां च संकुले॥
en: Then, O king, in that dreadful engagement, divisions of foot-soldiers and car-warriors and numerous horses, belonging to your as well as their (Pandavas) host, were slain by carwarriors.

sn: अजानन्नर्जुनश्चापि निहतं पुत्रमौरसम्। जघान समरे शूरान् राज्ञस्तान् भीष्मरक्षिणः॥
en: Meanwhile Arjuna also unaware the fate of the son of his lions, slew that battle those heroic kings who were engaged in supporting Bhishma.

sn: तथैव तावका राजन् संजयाश्च सहस्रशः। जुह्वतः समरे प्राणान् निजत्रुरितरेतरम्॥
en: Thereafter, O monarch, your warriors and the Srinjayas, by thousands, gave up their lives in battle slaying one another.

sn: मुक्तकेशा विकवचा विस्थाश्छिन्नकार्मुकाः। बाहुभिः समयुध्यन्त समवेताः परस्परम्॥
en: Car-warrior, with disheveled hair, with their arrows, swords, and bows severed, fought on with their naked arms meeting one another.

sn: तथा मर्मातिगैर्भीष्मो निजघान महारथान्। कम्पयन् समरे सेनां पाण्डवानां परंतपः॥
en: The highly powerful Bhishma also show in that battle mighty car-warriors with shafts capable of penetrating into the very vitals, agitating the whole host of the Pandavas.

sn: तेन यौधिष्ठिरे सैन्ये बहवो मानवा हताः। दन्तिनः सादिनश्चैव रथिनोऽथ हयास्तथा॥
en: By him (Bhishma) many warriors and tuskers, and horse-soldiers and car-warriors and steeds of Yudhisthira's army, were slain.

sn: तत्र भारत भीष्मस्य रणे दृष्ट्वा पराक्रमम्। अत्यद्भुतमपश्याम शक्रस्येव पराक्रमम्॥ तथैव भीमसेनस्य पार्षतस्य च भारत। रौद्रमासीद् रणे युद्ध सात्यकस्य च धन्विनः॥
en: In that battle, O Bharata, we beheld the prowess of Bhishma, of Bhimasena and also, O Bharata, of the son of Prishata. The battle that mighty bowmen of the Satvata race namely Satyaki, fought, was indeed very fierce.

sn: दृष्ट्वा द्रोणस्य विक्रान्तं पाण्डवान् भयमाविशत्। एक एव रणे शक्तो निहन्तु सर्वसैनिकान्॥ किं पुनः पृथिवीशूर्योधव्रातः समावृतः।
en: Beholding the prowess of Drona, the Pandavas were seized with terror. Singlehanded can this Drona slay us in battle with all our soldiers; what to speak of him when he is supported by a large body of warriors of worldspread renown.

sn: इत्युब्रुवन् महाराज रणे द्रोणेन पीडिताः॥ वर्तमाने तथा रौद्रे संग्रामे भरतर्षभ।
en: Even these were the words that the sons of Pritha said, O monarch, when o foremost of the Bharatas, they were greatly afflicted by him in that fierce fight.

sn: उभयोः सेनयोः शूरा नामृष्यन्त परस्परम्॥ आविष्टा इव युध्यन्ते रक्षोभूता महाबलाः।
en: All the heroes endued with great strength, of those two armies, did not give or take quarter; they fought on as if possessed by Rakshasas or evil spirits.

sn: तावकाः पाण्डवेयाश्च संरब्धास्तात धन्विनः॥ न स्म पश्यामहे कंचितं प्राणान् यः परिरक्षति। संग्रामे दैत्यसंकाशे तस्मिन् वीरवरक्षये॥
en: And, O sire, the bowmen of your army and those belonging to the army of the Pandavas, were all excited to the highest pitch of fury. We indeed did not then find any one pay the least heed to his life in that battle destructive of heroes, and that resembled the fight of the Daityas themselves.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच इरावन्तं तु निहतं दृष्ट्वा पार्था महारथाः। संग्रामे किमकुर्वन्त तन्ममाचक्ष्व संजय॥
en: Dhritarashtra said Describe to me, O Sanjaya, what the highly puissant sons of Pritha did when they heard that Iravat had been slain in battle,

sn: संजय उवाच इरावन्तं तु निहतं संग्रामे वीक्ष्य राक्षसः। व्यनदत् सुमहानादं भैमसेनिर्घटोत्कचः।। :॥
en: Sanjaya said Beholding Iravat slain in battle, the Rakshasa Ghatotkacha the son of Bhimasena, sent forth a terrible roar.

sn: नदतस्तस्य शब्देन पृथिवी सागराम्बरा। सपर्वतवना राजंश्चचाल सुभृशं तदा॥
en: As he roared, the earth having the oceans for her raiment's, with her mountains and forests, O king, quaked violently with the echo of his roars;

sn: अन्तरिक्षं दिशश्चैव सर्वाश्च प्रदिशस्तथा। तं श्रुत्वा सुमहानादं तव सैन्यस्य भारत॥
en: As also the firmament and all the cardinal and subsidiary quarters. As your soldiers heard, O Bharata, that terrible uproar,

sn: ऊऊस्तम्भः समभवद् वेपथुः स्वेद एव च। सर्व एव महाराज तावका दीनचेतसः॥
en: Their thighs were petrified and they trembled and perspired; and O foremost of kings, all of them became depressed at heart.

sn: सर्वतः समचेष्टन्त सिंहभीता गजा इव। नर्दित्वा सुमहानादं निर्घातमिव राक्षसः॥
en: And they fled on all sides like herds of elephants frightened by a lion. Then the Rakshasa, uttering those loud roars that resembled the rumble of the thunder bolt, a

sn: ज्वलितं शूलमुद्यम्य रूपं कृत्वा विभीषणम्। नानारूपप्रहरणैर्वृतो राक्षसपुङ्गवैः॥
en: Balancing his resplendent trident and assuming dreadful appearance, and surrounded by foremost of Rakshasas of fearful main and armed with diverse weapons,

sn: आजघान सुसंक्रुद्धः कालान्तकयमोपमः। तमापतन्तं सम्प्रेक्ष्य संक्रुद्धं भीमदर्शनम्॥
en: Advanced, greatly excited with rage, like the Destroyer at the time of universal annihilation. Beholding that irate hero of dreadful appearance make towards himself.

sn: स्वबलं च भयात् तस्य प्रायशो विमुखीकृतम्। ततो दुर्योधनो राजा घटोत्कचमुपाद्रवत्॥
en: And seeing also his own troops, one and all, turning their faces away from the field of battle from fear of that Rakshasa, king Duryodhana rushed against Ghatotkacha,

sn: प्रगृह्य विपुलं चापं सिंहवद् विनदन् मुहुः। पृष्ठतोऽनुययौ चैनं स्रवद्भिः पर्वतोपमैः॥ कुञ्जरैर्दशसाहस्रैर्वङ्गानामधिपः स्वयम्। तमापतन्तं सम्प्रेक्ष्य गजानीकेन संवृतम्॥ पुत्रं तव महाराज चुकोप स निशाचरः। ततः प्रववृते युद्धं तुमुलं लोमहर्षणम्॥
en: Grasping a bow with arrows fixed on the string and uttering his war cries incessantly and loud. Behind him followed the ruler of the Bangas himself, supported by ten thousand elephants prodigious like the hills and with the temporal juice flowing down. Beholding your son surrounded by the elephant division rush to battle, O mighty monarch, that night-ranger became inflamed with wrath; then regard a combat, dreadful and hair stirring.

sn: राक्षसानां च राजेन्द्र दुर्योधनबलस्य च। गजानीकं च सम्प्रेक्ष्य मेघवृन्दमिवोदितम्॥
en: Between the Rakshasa, O mighty monarch, and the division of Duryodhana. Beholding that elephant-division like a mass of clouds in the horizon,

sn: अभ्यधावन्त संक्रुद्धा राक्षसाः शस्त्रपाणयः। नदन्तो विविधान् नादान् मेघा इव सविद्युतः॥
en: The Rakshasas, highly enraged, rushed at it, with weapons in their hands, and uttering various war-cries, like clouds charged with lightning.

sn: शरशक्त्यृष्टिनाराचैनिघ्नन्तो गजयोधिनः। भिन्दिपालैस्तथा शूलैर्मुद्गरैः सपरश्वधैः॥
en: With arrows, dares, sabers, shafts, lances, mallets, and battle-axes, they began to slay the warriors fighting from the backs of elephants.

sn: पर्वताग्रैश्च वृक्षैश्च निजघ्नुस्ते सहागजान्। भिन्नकुम्भान् विरुधिरान् भिन्नगात्रांश्च वारणान्॥ अपश्याम महाराज वध्यमानान् निशाचरैः। तेषु प्रक्षीयमाणेषु भग्नेषु गजयोधिषुः॥
en: They slew those huge elephants with blocks of stones and large trees. We beheld, O mighty monarch, elephants with temples rent, and bodies bathed in blood and managed with wounds, slain by those rangers of night. When that division of elephant-riders, was shattered and thinned in number,

sn: दुर्योधनो महाराज राक्षसान् समुपाद्रवत्। अमर्षवशमापन्नस्त्यक्त्वा जीवितमात्मनः॥
en: Duryodhana himself, O mighty monarch, rushed against the Rakshasas, influenced by great animosity and headless of his own life.

sn: मुमोच निशितान् बाणान् राक्षसेषु परंतप। जघान् च महेष्वासः प्रधानांस्तत्र राक्षसान्॥
en: That highly powerful hero sped arrows of exceeding sharpness at those Rakshasas, and that fierce bowman slew many of the Rakshasas that were fighting there.

sn: संक्रुद्धो भरतश्रेष्ठ पुत्रो दुर्योधनस्तव। वेगवन्तं महारौद्रं विद्युज्जिद्वं प्रमाथिनम्॥ शरैश्चतुर्भिश्चतुरो निजघान महाबलः। ततः पुनरमेयात्मा शरवर्षं दुरासदम्॥ मुमोच भतरश्रेष्ठो निशाचरबलं प्रति। तत् तु दृष्टवा महत् कर्म पुत्रस्य तव मारिष।॥
en: Your irate son Duryodhana, O foremost of the Bharatas, that mighty car-warrior slew with four shafts, the four Rakshasas viz., Vegavana, Maharaudra, Vidyutjivha, and Pramathin. Once more, that one of immeasurable soul shot, O foremost of Bharatas, a shower of arrows incapable being ruffled, at the host of the Rakshasas. Beholding, O sire, that marvelous feat achieved by sour son,

sn: क्रोधेनाभिप्रजज्वाल भैमसेनिर्महाबलः। स विस्फार्य महच्चापमिन्द्राशनिसमप्रभम्॥
en: The highly powerful son of Bhimasena blazed forth with rage; then stretching his mighty bow effulgent like the thunder bolt of Indra,

sn: अभिदुद्राव वेगेन दुर्योधनमरिंदमम्। तमापतन्तमुद्वीक्ष्य कालसृष्टमिवान्तकम्॥
en: He rushed against the irate Duryodhana with violence. Beholding him rush forward like death incarnate urged on by the Destroyer himself.

sn: न विव्यथे महाराज पुत्रो दुर्योधनस्तव। अथैनमब्रवीत् क्रुद्धः क्रूरः संरक्तलोचनः॥
en: Your son Duryodhana, O monarch, did not waver at all. Then Ghatotkacha with his eyes coppery in wrath thus addressed Duryodhana angrily saying

sn: अद्यानृण्यं गमिष्यामि पितॄणां मातुरेव च। ये त्वया सुनृशंसेन दीर्घकाल प्रवासिताः॥
en: This day will I liquidate the debt I owe to my fathers and mothers who had so bong been exited by your heartless self.

sn: यच्च ते पाण्डवा राजश्छलछूते पराजिताः। यच्चैव द्रौपदी कृष्णा एकवस्त्रा रजस्वला॥
en: The sons of Pandu, O monarch, were deceitfully defeated by you at a game of dice. The daughter of Drupada by name Krishna, while in her courses and so clad in one garment only,

sn: सभामानीय दुर्बुद्धे बहुधा क्लेशिता त्वया। तव च प्रियकामेन आश्रमस्था दुरात्मना॥
en: O perverse-minded wretch, was brought in the midst of the court-hall and was persecuted by you in various ways. While she was dwelling in her hermitage in the woods, out of a desire for compassing your good, the wickedsouled.

sn: सैन्धवेन परामृष्टा परिभूय पितृन् मम। एतेषामपमानानामन्येषा च कुलाधम॥
en: Ruler of the Sindhus oppressed her disregarding my sires. O you the disgrace to your family, these and many other such insults.

sn: अन्तमद्य गमिष्यामि यदि नोत्सृजसे रणम्। एवमुक्त्वा तु हैडिम्बो महद् विस्फार्य कार्मुकम्॥
en: Will I this avenge, if indeed you do not fly forsaking the field of battle.' Having thus spoken, and stretching his mighty bow Hidimba's son,

sn: संदश्य दशनैरोष्ठं सुक्किणी परिसंलिहन्। शरवर्षेण महता दुर्योधनमवाकिरत्। प्रवतं वारिधाराभिः प्रावृषीव बलाहकः॥
en: Biting his lips with his teeth and licking the corners of his mouth, covered Duryodhana with a mighty shower of arrows, like clouds washing the mountain breast with torrents of rain in the rainy season.

sn: संजय उवाच तु दुःसहं दानवैरपि। ततस्तद् बाणवर्षं दधार युधि राजेन्द्रो यथा वर्ष महाद्विपः॥
en: Sanjaya said Then that shower of arrows, which it was difficult even for the Danavas to withstand, was borne by that foremost of kings Duryodhana, like a mighty elephant bearing a shower of rains.

sn: ततः क्रोधसमाविष्टो निःश्वसत्रिव पन्नगः। संशयं परमं प्राप्तः पुत्रस्ते भरतर्षभ॥
en: Thereafter your son possessed with rage, and breathing like a snake was involved in a very hazardous situation in that battle, O foremost of the Bharatas.

sn: मुमोच निशितांस्तीक्ष्णान् नाराचान् पञ्चविंशतिम्। तेऽपतन् सहसा रांजस्तस्मिन् राक्षसपुङ्गवे॥
en: Then he (Duryodhana) shot (at the Rakshasa), twenty five keep-pointed dares of exceeding sharpness; those dares, O king fell upon that foremost of Rakshasas with great force,

sn: आशीविषा इव क्रुद्धाः पर्वते गन्धमादने। स तैर्विद्धः स्रवन् रक्तं प्रभिन्न इव कुञ्जरः॥
en: Like infuriate snakes falling upon the mountain Gandhamadana. Pierced with those arrows, and shedding blood copiously like an elephant in rut (shedding the temporal juice),

sn: दधे मतिं विनाशाय राज्ञः स पिशिताशनः। जग्राह च महाशक्तिं गिरीणामपि दारिणीम्॥
en: That cannibal formed a fixed resolution for destroying the king. Thereafter the Rakshasa grasped a mighty lance, capable of penetrating even through rocks,

sn: सम्प्रदीप्तां महोल्काभामशनि ज्वलितामिव। समुद्यच्छन् महावाहुर्जिधांसुस्तनयं तव॥
en: Blazing with effulgence, burning like a fierce meteor and resembling the flashes of lightning in radiance. That mighty-armed hero then desirous of slaying your son, raised that lance.

sn: तामुद्यतामभिप्रेक्ष्य वङ्गानामधिपस्त्वरन्। कुञ्जरं गिरिसंकाशं राक्षसं प्रत्यचोदयत्॥
en: Beholding that lance raised, the ruler of the Bangas, speedily urged his elephant of proportions huge like a hill, against the Rakshasa.

sn: स नागप्रवरेणाजौ बलिना शीघ्रगामिना। यतो दुर्योधनरथस्तं मार्ग प्रत्यवर्तत॥
en: This king, in that battle, riding on his excellent elephant ofs, great strength and fleetness, reached the spot where Duryodhana's car was stationed;

sn: रथं च वारयामास कुञ्जरेण सुतस्य मार्गमावारितं दृष्ट्वा राज्ञा वङ्गेन धीमता॥
en: And he covered the car of your son Duryodhana with the body of his elephant. Seeing the way (to Duryodhana's car thus covered by the highly intelligence ruler of the Bangas.

sn: घटोत्कचो महाराज क्रोधसंरक्तलोचनः। उद्यतां तां महाशक्तिं तस्मिश्चिक्षेप वारणे॥
en: Ghatotkacha, O mighty monarch, with eyes coppery in anger, sped that raised dare of great fierceness at the elephant.

sn: स तयाऽभिहतो राजंस्तेन बाहुप्रमुक्तया। संजातरुधिरोत्पीडः पपात च ममार च॥
en: Struck with that dare, O king, hurled by the hand of Ghatotkacha, the elephant bleeding profusely, fell down dead.

sn: पतत्यथ गजे चापि वङ्गानामीश्वरो बली। जवेन समभिदुत्य जगाम धरणीतलम्॥
en: The mighty ruler of the Bangas quickly leaping up from his elephant, jumped down on the surface of the earth.

sn: दुर्योधनोऽपि सम्प्रेक्ष्य पतितं वरवारणम्। प्रभग्नं च बलं दृष्ट्वा जगाम परमां व्यथाम्॥
en: King Duryodhana seeing that excellent elephant felled and his army shattered, was overwhelmed with grief.

sn: क्षत्रधर्मं पुरस्कृत्य आत्मनश्चाभिमानिताम्। प्राप्तेऽपक्रमणे राजा तस्थौ गिरिरिवाचलः॥
en: Holding before his mind's eye the paramount duty of a Kshatriya, and also from his own pride, king Duryodhana, through worsted, stood immovable like the everlasting hills.

sn: संधाय च शितं बाणं कालाग्निसमतेजसम्। मुमोज परमक्रुद्धस्तस्मिन् घोरे निशाचरे॥
en: Then placing on his bow string whetted shafts blazing like the Fire of dissolution, and highly excited with rage, he discharged them at that dreadful ranger of the night.

sn: तमापतन्तं सम्प्रेक्ष्य बाणमिन्द्राशनिप्रभम्। लाघवान्मोचयामास महात्मा वै घटोत्कचः॥
en: Seeing those arrows falling like the thunderbolt of Indra, the high-souled Ghatotkacha foiled their aim by the alacrity of his movements.

sn: भूयश्च विननादोग्रं क्रोधसंरक्तलोचनः। त्रासयामास सैन्यानि युगान्ते जलदो यथा॥
en: Like clouds at the end of a Yuga, once more did he fierce roar out, with eyes coppery in rage, striking terror into the hearts of all soldier.

sn: तं श्रुत्वा निनदं घोरं भीमस्य रक्षसः। आचार्यमुपसङ्गम्य भीष्मः शान्तनवोऽब्रवीत्॥
en: Hearing that deafening roar uttered by the fearful Rakshasa, Bhishma the son of Shantanu, coming to the preceptor Drona addressed him saying.

sn: यथैष निनदो घोरः श्रूयते राक्षसेरितः। हैडिम्बो युध्यते नूनं राज्ञा दुर्योधनेन ह॥
en: As I hear these dreadful roars uttered by the Rakshasa Ghatotkacha, I think it sure that the son of Hidimba is engaged with king Duryodhana himself.

sn: नैष शक्यो हि संग्रामे जेतुं भूतेन केनचित्। तत्र गच्छत भद्रं वो राजानं परिरक्षत॥
en: In battle, this Rakshasa could not be conquered by any creature. So hide yourself to king and rescue him. May good betide you.

sn: अभिद्रुतो महाभागो राक्षसेन महात्मना। एतद्धि वः परं कृत्यं सर्वेषां नः परंतपाः॥
en: That hero of eminent parts viz., Duryodhana has been assaulted by the highsouled Rakshasa. Now, O afflicter of foes, even this (to protect the king) is our incumbent duty.

sn: पितामहवचः श्रुत्वा त्वरमाणा महारथाः। उत्तमं जवमास्थाय प्रययुर्यत्र कौरवः॥
en: Having heard the words of the grandsire, the mighty car-warriors, without delaying and at the top of their speed, rushed where the ruler of the Kurus was.

sn: द्रोणश्च सोमदत्तश्च बाह्रीकोऽथ जयद्रथः। कृपो भूरिश्रवाः शल्य आवन्त्यः सबृहद्बलः॥
en: Drona and Somadatta, and Balhika and Jayadratha and Kripa and Bhurishravas, Shalya and the two princes of Avanti and also Brihadbala,

sn: अश्वत्थामा विकर्णश्च चित्रसेनो विविंशतिः। रथाश्चानेकसाहस्रा ये तेषामनुयायिनः॥
en: And Ashvathama, and and Vikarna, and Chitrasena and Vivinshati, these and thousands of other car-warriors, along with those that followed them.

sn: अभिदुतं परीप्सन्तः पुत्रं दुर्योधनं तव। तदनीकमनाधृष्यं पालितं तु महारथैः॥ आततायिनमायान्तं प्रेक्ष्य राक्षससत्तमः। नाकम्पत महाबाहुर्मैनाक इव पर्वतः॥
en: Proceeded, desirous of rescuing your son Duryodhana who had been hotly pressed. Beholding that invincible division protected by many mighty car-warriors make towards himself with hostile intentions, that foremost of Rakshasas possessed of mighty arms, remained immovable like the Mountain Mainaka,

sn: प्रगृह्य विपुलं चापं ज्ञातिभिः परिवारितः। शूलमुद्गरहस्तैश्च नानाप्रहरणैरपि॥
en: Holding a massive bow and surrounded by his relations armed with bludgeons and mallets, and diverse other kinds of weapons.

sn: ततः समभवद् युद्धं तुमुलं लोमहर्षणम्। राक्षसानां च मुख्यस्य दुर्योधनबलस्य च॥
en: Then commenced a fierce engagement capable of making the hair stand erect, between those foremost among Duryodhana's host and those among the Rakshasa's kinsmen.

sn: धनुषां कूजतां शब्दः सर्वतस्तुमुलो रणे। अश्रूयत महाराज वंशानां दह्यतामिव॥
en: On all sides of the field of battle, the twanging of bows was heard, O mighty monarch, like the crackling of burning bamboo's.

sn: अस्त्राणां पात्यमानानां कवचेषु शरीरिणाम्। शब्दः समभवद् राजन् गिरीणामिव भिद्यताम्॥
en: The din produced by the stroke of weapons against the armours of the combatants, resembled, O king, the sound produced by the rending of mountains.

sn: वीरबाहुविसृष्टानां तोमराणां विशाम्पते। रूपमासीद् वियत्स्थानां सर्पाणामिव सर्पताम्॥
en: The appearance of lances hurled by the arms of heroes was, O ruler of men, like that of serpents coursing swiftly through the welkin.

sn: ततः परमसंक्रुद्धो विस्फार्य सुमहद् धनुः। राक्षसेन्द्रो महाबाहुविनदन् भैरवं रवम्॥
en: Thereafter excited to the highest pitch of fury, that foremost of Rakshasas possessed of mighty arms stretching his mighty bow, uttered a terrible yell.

sn: आचार्यस्यार्धचन्द्रेण क्रुद्धश्चिच्छेद कार्मुकम्। सोमदत्तस्य भल्लेन ध्वजं चोन्मथ्य चानदत्॥
en: He then burst asunder the bow of the preceptor Drona with a crescent shaped arrow. Then with a broad headed arrow, having caused the standard of Somadatta, he broke out into another yell.

sn: बाह्रीकं च त्रिभिर्बाणैः प्रत्यविध्यत् स्तनान्तरे। कृपमेकेन विव्याध चित्रसेनं त्रिभिः शरैः॥
en: He pierced Balhika with three shafts, betwecn his breasts; then he pierced Kripa with one shaft and Mitrasena with three.

sn: पूर्णायतविसृष्टेन सम्यक् प्रणिहितेन च। जत्रुदेशे समासाद्य विकर्णं समताडयत्॥
en: With another well-directed and well-aimed shaft shot by his bow drawn to its fullest stretch, he struck Vikarna on the soldier-joint as the latter neared him;

sn: न्यषीदत् स्वरथोपस्थे शोणितेन परिप्लुतः। ततः पुनरमेयात्मा नाराचान् दश पञ्च च॥ भूरिश्रवसि संक्रुद्धः प्राहिणोद् भरतर्षभ। ते वर्म भित्त्वा तस्याशु विविशुर्धरणीतलम्॥
en: Then Vikarna, bathed in blood, squatted down on the terrace of his car. Thereafter that Rakshasa of infinite soul, excited with wrath, speed, O foremost of the Bharatas, five and ten dares at Bhurishravas; and these dares penetrating through the latter's Armour struck on the surface of the earth.

sn: विविंशतेश्च द्रौणेश्च यन्तारौ समताडयत्। तौ पेततू रथोपस्थे रश्मीनुत्सृज्य वाजिनाम्॥
en: He also wounded the drivers of Vivingshati and the son of Drona; both of them fell down on their seats in the car loosening their grasp of the reins of steeds,

sn: सिंधुराज्ञोऽर्धचन्द्रेण वाराहं स्वर्णभूषितम्। उन्ममाथ महाराज द्वितीयेनाच्छिनद् धनुः॥
en: He cut down, O monarch, the standard of the king of the Sindhus bearing the device of the boar and decked with gold, with a crescentshaped shaft; and with another, he burst the latter's bow asunder.

sn: चतुर्भिरथ नाराचैरावन्त्यस्य महात्मनः। जघान चतुरो वाहान् क्रोधसंरक्तलोचनः॥
en: Then again with eyes red in rage, the Rakshasa slew with four lances the four steeds of the high-souled princes of Avanti.

sn: पूर्णायतविसृष्टेन पीतेन निशितेन च। निर्बिभेद महाराज राजपुत्रं बृहद्बलम्॥
en: Then, O mighty monarch, he pierced prince Brihadbala with another sharp and welltempered arrow, shot from his bow drawn to its fullest stretch.

sn: स गाढविद्धो व्यथितो रथोपस्थ उपाविशत्। भृशं क्रोधेन चाविष्टो रथस्थो राक्षसाधिपः॥
