en: That one (Brihadbala) thus deeply pierced and smarting with pain, sat down on the terrace of his chariot. Then that lord of the Rakshasas possessed with furious wrath, and stationed on his car,

sn: चिक्षेप निशितांस्तीक्ष्णाञ्छरानाशीविषोपमान्। बिभिदुस्ते महाराज शल्यं युद्धविशारदम्॥
en: Shot many keep-pointed shafts of great sharpness that resembled snakes of virulent poison; these shafts, O mighty monarch, penetrated through Shalya accomplished in battle.

sn: संजय उवाच विमुखीकृत्य सर्वांस्तु तावकान् राक्षसः। जिघांसुर्भरतश्रेष्ठ दुर्योधनमुपाद्रवत्॥
en: Sanjaya said Having made all your warriors turn their faces away from field of battle, the Rakshasa, 0 foremost of the Bharatas, assaulted Duryodhana out of a desire for slaying him.

sn: तमापतन्तं सम्प्रेक्ष्य राजानं प्रति वेगितम्। अभ्यधावञ्जिघांसन्तस्तावका युद्धदुर्मदाः॥
en: Beholding him make towards the king with impetuosity, your warriors, all invincible in battle, rushed at him, desirous of doing away with him.

sn: तालमात्राणि चापानि विकर्षन्तो महारथाः। तमेकमभ्यधावन्त नदन्तः सिंहसंघवत्॥
en: Those mighty car-warriors, stretching their bows that looked like large palmyar trees, and uttering their war-cries loud as the roars of the lions, rushed at him shooting weapons at him.

sn: अथैनं शरवर्षेण समन्तात् पर्यवाकिरन्। पर्वतं वारिधाराभिः शरदीव बलाहकाः॥
en: Then they covered him with an arrow downpour, like clouds covering the mountains with a downpour of rain in the rainy season.

sn: स गाढविद्धो व्यथितस्तोत्रादित इव द्विपः। उत्पपात तदाऽऽकाशं समन्ताद् वैनतेयवत्॥
en: Thus pierced sore, and greatly afflicted like an elephant smitten with the hook, the Rakshasa then at once rose to the sky like the son of Vainatay Garuda,

sn: व्यनदत् सुमहानादं जीमूत इव शारदः। दिशः खं विदिशश्चैव नादयन् भैरवस्वनः॥
en: Then he uttered a loud roar that resembled the rumble of autumnal clouds; and that dreadful reverberated through the subsidiary and cardinal points of the compass.

sn: राक्षसस्य तु तं शब्दं श्रुत्वा राजा युधिष्ठिरः। उवाच भरतश्रेष्ठ भीमसेनमरिंदमम्॥
en: King Yudhishthira hearing those war-cries of the Rakshasa, thus spoke, O foremost of the Bharatas, to Bhimasena the subduer of foes.

sn: युध्यते राक्षसो नूनं धार्तराष्ट्रैर्महारथैः। यथाऽस्य श्रूयते शब्दो नदतो भैरवं स्वनम्॥
en: "Surely the Rakshasa is fighting with mighty car-warriors of the host of Dhritarashtra's son, in as much as we can hear, (even at this distance), the noise created by his fierce cries.

sn: अतिभारं च पश्यामि तस्मिन् राक्षसपुङ्गवे। पितामहश्च संक्रुद्धः पञ्चालान् हन्तुमुद्यतः॥
en: I also perceive that foremost of Rakshasas has now to bear a burden unequal to his strength; on the other hand, the grandsire inflamed with rage is exerting for slaughtering the Panchalas.

sn: तेषां च रक्षणार्थाय युध्यते फाल्गुनः परैः। एतज्ञात्वा महाबाहो कार्यद्वयमुपस्थितम्॥
en: For the protection of these latter, Falguna is engaged with the foe. Having heard, O mighty armed hero, of these two tasks both of which demand prompt attention,

sn: गच्छ रक्षस्व हैडिम्बं संशयं परमं गतम्। भ्रातुर्वचनमाज्ञाय त्वरमाणो वृकोदरः॥
en: He yourself for rescuing the son of Hidimba involved in a great predicament.” Accepting the words of his brother, without the least delay, Vrikodara.

sn: प्रययौ सिंहनादेन त्रासयन् सर्वपार्थिवान्। वेगेन महता राजन् पर्वकाले यथोदधिः॥
en: Proceeded to the battle, terrifying all the kings with his fierce war-cries, an, O king, with an impetuosity like that of the ocean in the days of the full moon or the new moon.

sn: तमन्वगात् सत्यधृतिः सौचित्तियुद्धदुर्मदः। श्रेणिमान् वसुदानश्च पुत्रः काश्यस्य चाभिभूः॥
en: Him followed Satyadhriti and Sauchitti ever invincible in battle, and Shrenimat and Vasudhara and the puissant son of the king of the Kashis,

sn: अभिमन्युमुखाश्चैव द्रौपदेया महारथाः। क्षत्रदेवश्च विक्रान्तः क्षत्रधर्मा तथैव च॥
en: The sons of Draupadi, all mighty carwarriors headed by Abhimanyu, and Kshatradeva, the powerful Kshatradharman,

sn: अनूपाधिपतिश्चैव नीलः स्वबलमास्थितः। महता रथवंशेन हैडिम्बं पर्यवारयन्॥
en: And Nila the sovereign of the low countries accompanied by his own divisions. They surrounded the son of Hidimba with a mighty division of cars.

sn: कुञ्जरैश्च सदा मत्तैः षट्सहस्रैः प्रहारिभिः। अभ्यरक्षन्त सहिता राक्षसेन्द्रं घटोत्कचम्॥
en: With six thousand highly infuriated elephants, all potent smiters, those heroes began to protect Ghatotkacha that foremost of the Rakshasas.

sn: सिंहनादेन महता नेमिघोषेण चैव ह। खुरशब्दनिपातैश्च कम्पयन्तो वसुन्धराम्॥
en: These warriors made the very earth quake with their fierce war-cries, the clatter of their car-wheels, the sound produced by the hoofs of their galloping horses.

sn: तेषामापततां श्रुत्वा शब्दं त तावकं बलम्। भीमसेनभयोद्विग्नं विवर्णवदनं तथा॥
en: Hearing that noise of the assaulting army, the warriors of the army of your sons, wore a pallid countenance being agitated with the fear of Bhimasena;

sn: परिवृत्तं महाराज परित्यज्य घटोत्कचम्। ततः प्रववृते युद्धं तत्र तेषां महात्मनाम्॥ तावकानां परेषां च संग्रामेष्वनिवर्तिनाम्। नानारूपाणि शस्त्राणि विसृजन्तो महारथाः॥
en: And leaving Ghatotkacha alone, they turned back from the field of battle. But the combatants of your army and those of the enemy's host were both entreating; so there once more ensured, O mighty monarch, a terrible battle, between these high-souled warriors. Mighty car-warriors hurling weapons of various shapes,

sn: अन्योन्यमभिधावन्तः सम्प्रहारं प्रचक्रिरे। व्यतिषक्तं महारौद्रं युद्धं भीरुभयावहम्॥
en: Rushed at one another and then smote down one another. Thus raged the most dreadful combat capable of inspiring terror into the hearts of the cowards.

sn: हया गजैः समाजग्मुः पादाता रथिभिः सह। अन्योन्यं समरे राजन् प्रार्थयानाः समभ्ययुः॥
en: Horse-soldiers encountered elephant-riders and foot-soldiers fought with the car-warriors; challenging one another in battle they rushed against one another, O king.

sn: सहसा चाभवत् तीव्र संनिपातान्महद् रजः। गजाश्वरथपत्तीनां पदनेमिसमुद्धतम्॥
en: In consequence of this on sleight of cars, horses, elephants, and infantry, a thick and impenetrable cloud of dust appeared being raised by the car-wheels and tread of the footsoldier.

sn: धूम्रारुणं रजस्तीव्र रणभूमि समावृणोत्। नैव स्वेन परे राजन् समजानन् परस्परम्॥
en: Then the field of battle, O king, was shrouded by a thick cloud of dust of the reddish hue of smoke; and none was able to distinguish between his friend and his foe.

sn: पिता पुत्रं न जानीते पुत्रो वा पितरं तथा। निर्मर्यादे तथाभूते वैशसे लोमहर्षणे॥
en: Father could not distinguish his son nor the son his father, in that horripilating, carnage where no consideration was of any evil.

sn: शास्त्राणां भरतश्रेष्ठः मनुष्याणां च गर्जताम्। सुमहानभवच्छब्दः प्रेतानामिव भारत॥
en: The clashing of weapons and the yells of men, O foremost of the Bharatas, created a fierce din, that resembled the roar of demons themselves.

sn: गजवाजिमनुष्याणां शोणितान्त्रतरङ्गिणी। प्रावर्तत नदी तत्र केशशैवलशाद्वला॥
en: On the field of battle a river started up into existence, of which the currents, were constituted by the gore of elephants, horses, and men, and the weeds and moss by the hair (of the warriors).

sn: नराणां चैव कायेभ्यः शिरसां पततां रणे। शुश्रुवे सुमहाञ्छब्दः पततामश्मनामिव॥
en: A defending noise, like that produced by a shower of stones, was heard there, as the heads of the combatants fell on the field severed from their trunks.

sn: विशिरस्कैर्मनुष्यैश्च च्छिन्नगात्रैश्च वारणैः। अश्वैः सम्भिन्नदेहैश्च संकीर्णाभूद् वसुन्धरा॥
en: The earth was covered with headless trucks with mutilated elephants and with horses with limbs mangled and hacked to pieces.

sn: नानाविधानि शस्त्राणि विसृजन्तो महारथाः। अन्योन्यमभिधावन्तः सम्प्रहारार्थमुद्यताः॥
en: Mighty car-warriors, putting forth all their energies rushed to smite down one another, hurling at the same time weapons of various kinds.

sn: हया हयान् समासाद्य प्रेषिता हयसादिभिः। समाहत्य रणेऽन्योन्यं निपेतुर्गतजीविताः॥
en: Urged on by their riders, encountering one another, horses dashed against one another, and fell down on the field deprived of life.

sn: नरा नरान् समासाद्य क्रोधरक्तेक्षणा भृशम्। उरांस्युरोभिरन्योन्यं समाश्लिष्य निजनिरे॥
en: Combatants, with eyes crimsoned in rage, meeting one another, struck one another with their breasts, and thus killed one another.

sn: प्रेषिताश्च ग्रमहामात्रैर्वारणाः परवारणैः। अभ्यघ्नन्त विषाणाग्रैर्वारणानेव संयुगे।॥
en: Goaded on by their riders, elephants slew their hostile compeers with the ends of their tusks, in that battle.

sn: ते जातरुधिरोत्पीडाः पताकाभिरलंकृताः। संसक्ताः प्रत्यदृश्यन्त मेघा इव सविद्युतः॥
en: These elephants decked with fluttering pennons and shedding blood in copious quantities and bespattered with it, appeared like clouds adorned by forks of lightening.

sn: मुमुचुः शोणितं भूरि केचिद् भिन्ना विषाणाचैर्भिन्नकुम्भाश्च तोमरैः। विनदन्तोऽभ्यधावन्त गर्जमाना घना इव॥
en: Some of these with bodies mangled with tusk wounds, others with their temples rent by broad-headed shafts, careered all over the field roaring like roaring clouds.

sn: केचिद्धस्तैर्द्विधा च्छिन्नैश्छिन्नगात्रास्तथाऽपरे। निपेतुस्तुमुले तस्मिंश्छिन्नपक्षा इवाद्रयः॥
en: Some with their trunks cut in twin, others with their bodies mutilated, fell down in that sanguinary battle, like mountains having their wings cut off.

sn: पार्श्वस्तु दारितैरन्ये वारणैर्वरवारणाः। धातूनिव महीधराः॥
en: Other huge elephants having their sides opened by their hostile compeers, copiously shed blood like mountains discharging liquefied red chalk.

sn: नाराचनिहतास्त्वन्ये तथा विद्धाश्च तोमरैः। विनदन्तोऽभ्यधावन्त विशृंगा इव पर्वताः॥
en: Others, slain with lances and pierced with Tomaras, with their riders killed, looked like mountains deprived of their crests.

sn: केचित् क्रोधसमाविष्टा मदान्धा निरवग्रहाः। रथान् हयान् पदातींश्च ममृदुः शतशो रणे॥
en: Others, possessed with fury, and inflamed with shedding the temporal juice, and having none to restrain them, began to crush in that battle, horses and cars and soldiers by hundreds.

sn: तथा हया हयारोहैस्ताडिताः प्रासतोमरैः। तेन तेनाभ्यवर्तन्त कुर्वन्तो व्याकुला दिशः॥
en: So also horses pierced with lances and dares by cavalry-soldiers, dashed against their assailants, as if agitating all the points of the compass.

sn: रथिनो रथिभिः सार्धं कुलपुत्रास्तनुत्यजः। परां शक्तिं समास्थाय चक्रुः कर्माण्यभीतवत्॥
en: Car-warriors born in noble families, and reckless of their lives, meeting their hostile compeers, fought on dauntlessly depending on their own excellent strength.

sn: स्वयंवर इवामर्दे प्रजह्वरितरेतरम्। प्रार्थयाना यशो राजन् स्वर्ग वा युद्धशालिनः॥
en: Those horses accomplished in battle, O king, desirous of securing either fame or paradise, smote down one another in that fierce carnage, as if in a Svayamvara.

sn: तस्मिंस्तथा वर्तमाने संग्रामे लोमहर्षणे। धार्तराष्ट्रं महत् सैन्यं प्रायशो विमुखीकृतम्॥
en: When that hair-string comb was thus raging, the troops belonging to Dhritarashtra's army were generally made to turn back their faces from the field of battle.

description: Display of illusion by Hidimba's son
sn: संजय उवाच स्वसैन्यं निहतं दृष्ट्वा राजा दुर्योधनः स्वयम्। अभ्यधावत संक्रुद्धो भीमसेनमरिंदमम्॥
en: Sanjaya said There upon king Duryodhana, seeing his own troops slain inflamed with wrath, rushed against that subduer of foes namely Bhimasena.

description: Display of illusion by Hidimba's son
sn: प्रगृह्य सुमहच्चापमिन्द्राशनिसमस्वनम्। महता शरवर्षेण पाण्डवं समवाकिरत्॥
en: Grasping a huge bow effulgent like the thunder bolt of Indra himself, he covered the son of Pandu with a thick shower of arrows.

description: Display of illusion by Hidimba's son
sn: अर्धचन्द्रं च संधाय सुतीक्ष्ण लोमवाहिनम्। भीमसेनस्य चिच्छेद चापं क्रोधसमन्वितः॥
en: Fixing on his bow string a crescent shaped and exceedingly sharp arrow furnished with wings of down, and inflamed with rage, he burst asunder the bow of Bhimasena.

description: Display of illusion by Hidimba's son
sn: तदन्तरं च सम्प्रेक्ष्य त्वरमाणो महारथः। प्रसंदधे शितं बाणं गिरीणामपि दारणम्॥
en: At this opportunity, that mighty car-warrior Duryodhana without the least delay placed on his bow string another sharp arrow capable of penetrating even through the very mountains.

description: Display of illusion by Hidimba's son
sn: तेनोरसि महाराज भीमसेनमताडयत्। स गाढविद्धो व्यथितः सृक्किणी परिसंलिहन्॥
en: Then that mighty armed hero, with that arrow struck Bhimasena on the breast. The latter thus pierced deeply, smarting with pain, and licking the corners of his mouth,

description: Display of illusion by Hidimba's son
sn: समाललम्बे तेजस्वी ध्वजं हेमपरिष्कृतम्। तथा विमनसं दृष्ट्वा भीमसेनं घटोत्कचः॥
en: Caught hold of the staff of his standard decked with gold (for support). Thereupon Ghatotkacha seeing Bhimasena thus depressed.

description: Display of illusion by Hidimba's son
sn: क्रोधेनाभिप्रजज्वाल दिघक्षन्निव पावकः। अभिमन्युमुखाश्चापि पाण्डवानां महारथाः॥
en: Blazed up with rage, like a conflagration capable of consuming everything. The mighty car-warriors of the Pandava host headed by Abhimanyu,

description: Display of illusion by Hidimba's son
sn: समभ्यधावन् क्रोशन्तो राजानं जातसम्भ्रमाः। सम्प्रेक्ष्येतान् सम्पतत:संक्रुद्धाञ्जातसम्भ्रमान्॥
en: Now rushed impetuously at the king uttering their fierce war-cries. Beholding those enraged warriors rush with impetuosity.

description: Display of illusion by Hidimba's son
sn: भारद्वाजोऽब्रवीद् वाक्यं तावकानां महारथान्। क्षिप्रं गच्छत भद्रं वो राजानं परिरक्षत॥
en: The son of Bharadvaja spoke these words to the mighty car-warriors of your army "Good betide you all die yourselves and strive to rescue the king.

description: Display of illusion by Hidimba's son
sn: संशयं परमं प्राप्तं मज्जन्तं व्यसनार्णवे। एते क्रुद्धा महेष्वासाः पाण्डवानां महारथाः॥
en: Who is now involved in a great predicament and is being sunk into the sea of danger. These irate car-warriors of the Pandava army, these fierce bow-men,

description: Display of illusion by Hidimba's son
sn: भीमसेनं पुरस्कृत्य दुर्योधनमुपाद्रवन्। नानाविधानि शस्त्राणि विसृजन्तो जये धृताः॥
en: Placing Bhimasena at their head, are rushing at Duryodhana, hurling diverse kinds of weapons, determined to secure success,

description: Display of illusion by Hidimba's son
sn: नदन्तो भैरवान् नादांस्त्रासयन्तश्च भूमिपान्। तदाचार्यवचः श्रुत्वा सौमदत्तिपुरोगमाः॥
en: Roaring out their fierce war-cries and frightening thereby the rulers rulers of earth belonging to our party.” Hearing these words of the preceptor, your warriors headed by Somadatta,

description: Display of illusion by Hidimba's son
sn: तावकाः समवर्तन्त पाण्डवानामनीकिनीम्। कृपो भूरिश्रवाः शल्यो द्रोणपुत्रो विविंशतिः॥
en: Rushed against the ranks of the Pandavas, Kripa, Bhurishravas, Shalya, the son of Drona, Vivingshati,

description: Display of illusion by Hidimba's son
sn: चित्रसेनो विकर्णश्च सैन्धवोऽथ बृहद्बलः। आवन्त्यौ च महेष्वासौ कौरवं पर्यवारयन्॥
en: Chitrasena, Vikarna, the ruler of the Sindhus, Brihadbala and the two Avanti princes, both great bow-men, all in a body surrounded the Kuru ruler (for the aiding him).

description: Display of illusion by Hidimba's son
sn: ते विंशतिपदं गत्वा सम्प्रहारं प्रचक्रिरे। पाण्डवा धार्तराष्ट्राश्च परस्परजिघांसवः॥
en: Proceeding only twenty steps, the Pandavas and the Dhritarashtra's began to strike one another, out of a desire for slaying one another.

description: Display of illusion by Hidimba's son
sn: एवमुक्त्वा महाबाहुर्महद् विस्फार्ये कार्मुकम्। भारद्वाजस्ततो भीमं षड्विंशत्या समार्पयत्॥
en: The mighty-armed son of Bharadvaja also, having spoken the above words, stretched his mighty bow and afflicted Bhima with twenty ! six shafts.

description: Display of illusion by Hidimba's son
sn: भूयश्चैनं महाबाहुः शरैः शीघ्रमवाकिरत्। पर्वतं वारिधाराभिः प्रावृषीव बलाहकः॥
en: Then again that hero of mighty-arms speedily covered him with a shower of arrows, like clouds covering the mountains with rains in the rainy season.

description: Display of illusion by Hidimba's son
sn: तं प्रत्यविध्यद् दशभिर्भीमसेनः शिलीमुखैः। त्वरमाणो महेष्वासः सव्ये पार्श्वे महाबलः॥
en: But the highly puissant Bhimasena, that fierce bow-man, without the least delay, pierced Drona in return in his left side with ten shafts of great sharpness.

description: Display of illusion by Hidimba's son
sn: स गाढविद्धो व्यथितो वयोवृद्धश्च भारत। प्रणष्टसंज्ञः सहसा रथोपस्थ उपाविशत्॥
en: Thus deeply pierced and overwhelmed with pain, the preceptor worn out as he was with age, squatted down on the terrace of his chariot being deprived of his consciousness.

description: Display of illusion by Hidimba's son
sn: गुरुं प्रव्यथितं दृष्ट्वा राजा दुर्योधनः स्वयम्। द्रौणायनिश्च संक्रुद्धौ भीमसेनमभिद्रुतौ॥
en: Beholding him (Drona) highly pained, king Duryodhana himself and the irate son of na.

description: Display of illusion by Hidimba's son
sn: तावापतन्तौ सम्प्रेक्ष्य कालान्तकयमोपमौ। भीमसेनो महाबाहुर्गदामादाय सत्वरम्॥
en: Seeing them both rush against himself like the Destroyer him at the end of a Yuga, the mighty-armed Bhimasena speedily took up a mace;

description: Display of illusion by Hidimba's son
sn: अवप्लुत्य रथात् तूर्णं तस्थौ गिरिरिवाचलः। समुद्यम्य गदां गुर्वी यमदण्डोपमां रणे॥
en: And jumping down from his car he stood fixed like the immovable hills, uplifting his heavy mace that resembled the bludgeon of Death himself.

description: Display of illusion by Hidimba's son
sn: तमुद्यतगदं दृष्ट्वा कैलासमिव शृङ्गिणम्। कौरवो द्रोणपुत्रश्च सहितावभ्यधावताम्॥
en: Beholding him stand with his uplifted mace like the crested Kailasa mountain, the Kuru king and the son of Drona, united together, rushed against him.

description: Display of illusion by Hidimba's son
sn: तावापतन्तौ सहितौ त्वरितौ बलिनां वरौ। अभ्यधावत वेगेन त्वरमाणो वृकोदरः॥
en: Thereupon the highly puissant Bhimasena also rushed with impetuosity against those two foremost of powerful heroes who were rushing united against himself.

description: Display of illusion by Hidimba's son
sn: तमापतन्तं सम्प्रेक्ष्य संक्रुद्धं भीमदर्शनम्। समभ्यधावंस्त्वरिताः कौरवाणां महारथाः॥
en: Beholding the engaged Bhima of terrible expression thus fall upon them, the mighty carwarriors of the Kaurava host proceeded to meet him without delay.

description: Display of illusion by Hidimba's son
sn: भारद्वाजमुखाः सर्वे भीमसेनजिघांसया। नानाविधानि शस्त्राणि भीमस्योरस्यपातयन्॥
en: Headed by the son of Bharadvaja, those heroes, out of a desire for slaying Bhimasena, hurled at the latter's breast weapons of diverse descriptions.

description: Display of illusion by Hidimba's son
sn: सहिताः पाण्डवं सर्वे पीडयन्तः समन्ततः। तं दृष्ट्वा संशयं प्राप्तं पीड्यमानं महारथम्॥
en: Thus united together, they sorely pressed that son of Pandu (Bhima) on all sides. Beholding that mighty car-warrior thus involved in a predicament and thus afflicted,

description: Display of illusion by Hidimba's son
sn: अभिमन्युप्रभृतयः पाण्डवानां महारथाः। अभ्यधावन् परीप्सन्तः प्राणांस्त्यक्त्वा सुदुस्त्यजान्।।२८।
en: The mighty car-warriors of the Pandava host, such as Abhimanyu and others, rushed, forward desirous of rescuing him, setting their own dear lives at naught.

description: Display of illusion by Hidimba's son
sn: अनूपाधिपतिः शूरो भीमस्य दयितः सखा। नालो नीलाम्बुदप्रख्यः संक्रुद्धो द्रौणिमभ्ययात्॥
en: The heroic ruler of the low countries, that dear-loved friend of Bhima, by name Nila, of complexion blue like the clouds, excited with wrath, rushed at the son of Drona.

description: Display of illusion by Hidimba's son
sn: स्पर्धते हि महेष्वासो नित्यं द्रोणसुतेन सः। स विस्फार्य महच्चापं द्रौणिं विव्याध पत्रिणा॥
en: That fierce bowmen (Nila) ever longed for an encounter with the son of Drona. Now stretching his mighty bow he pierced with many a winged shaft the son of Drona,

description: Display of illusion by Hidimba's son
sn: यथा शक्रो महाराज पुरा विप्रचित्तिं दुराधर्षं देवतानां भयंकरम्॥
en: Just as, O mighty monarch, in the days of yore, Shakra pierced the Danava Viprachitti, invincible in battle and the terror of the celestial,

description: Display of illusion by Hidimba's son
sn: येन लोकत्रयं क्रोधात् त्रासितं स्वेन तेजसा। तथा नीलेन निर्भिन्नः सुमुक्तेन पतत्त्रिणा॥
en: Who, possessed by rage, struck terror into the three worlds by the display of his energy. Thus pierced by Nila with well-directed shafts,

description: Display of illusion by Hidimba's son
sn: संजातरुधिरोत्पीडो द्रौणिः क्रोधसमन्वितः। स विस्फार्य धनुश्चित्रमिन्द्राशनिसमस्वनम्॥ विव्याध दानवम्।
en: Drona's son, shedding blood profusely became possessed with wrath; then drawing his wonderful bow whose twang resembled Indra's thunder,

description: Display of illusion by Hidimba's son
sn: दने नीलविनाशाय मति मतिमतां वरः। ततः संधाय विमलान् भल्लान् कर्मारमार्जितान्॥
en: That foremost of intelligent heroes resolved to slay Nila in battle. Thereafter fixing on the bowstring broaded-headed shafts, resplendent and variegated by the forger himself,

description: Display of illusion by Hidimba's son
sn: जधान चतुरो वाहान् सारथिं ध्वजमेव च। सप्तमेन च भल्लेन नीलं विव्याध वक्षसि॥
en: He (Drona's son) slew with these the four horses of Nila and cut down his standard too. With the seventh arrow, he pierced Nila himself on the chest.

description: Display of illusion by Hidimba's son
sn: स गाढविद्धो व्यथितो रथोपस्थ उपाविशत्। मोहितं वीक्ष्य राजानं नीलमध्चयोपमम्॥
en: Thus deeply pierced and sorely pained, Nila squatted down on the terrace of his car. Beholding king Nila, of appearance like a mass of blue clouds, thus confounded,

description: Display of illusion by Hidimba's son
sn: घटोत्कचोऽभिसंक्रुद्धो ज्ञातिभिः परिवारितः। अभिदुद्राव वेगेन द्रौणिमाहवशोभिनम्॥
en: Ghatotkacha excited with wrath and surrounded by his kinsmen, impetuously rushed against Drona's son that ornament of battle.

description: Display of illusion by Hidimba's son
sn: तथेतरे चाभ्यधावन् राक्षसा युद्धदुर्मदाः। तमापतन्तं सम्प्रेक्ष्य राक्षसं घोरदर्शनम्॥
en: Other inferior Rakshasas invincible in battle also rushed to the fight. Seeing that Rakshasa of dreadful aspect make towards himself,

description: Display of illusion by Hidimba's son
sn: अभ्यधावत तेजस्वी भारद्वाजात्मजस्त्वरन्। निजघान च संक्रुद्धो राक्षसान् भीमदर्शनान्॥
en: The highly puissant son of Bharadvaja, without the least delay rushed against the former and excited with wrath he slew many Rakshasas of dreadful visage,

description: Display of illusion by Hidimba's son
sn: येऽभवन्नग्रतः क्रुद्धा राक्षसस्य पुरःसराः। विमुखांश्चैव तान् दृष्ट्वा द्रौणिचापच्युतैः शरैः॥
en: Who were stationed in the front of in Ghatotkacha; beholding his own troops turn faces away from the field of battle, in consequence of the shafts shot from the bow of Drona,

description: Display of illusion by Hidimba's son
sn: अक्रुद्ध्यत महाकायो भीमसेनिर्घटोत्कचः। प्रादुश्चक्रे ततो माया घोररूपां सुदारुणाम्॥
en: The huge-bodied Ghatotkacha, the son of Bhimasena became wrought up with rage, and brought into existence an awful and terrible illusion.

description: Display of illusion by Hidimba's son
sn: मोहयन् समरे द्रौणि मायावी राक्षसाधिपः। ततस्ते तावकाः सर्वे मायया विमुखीकृताः॥
en: Then therewith that ruler of the Rakshasas of potent illusive powers, confounded in battle Drona's son. Then all your warriors were repulsed through the illusion of the Rakshasa.

description: Display of illusion by Hidimba's son
sn: अन्योन्यं समपश्यन्त निकृत्ता मेदिनीतले। विचेष्टमानाः कृपणाः शोणितेन परिप्लुताः॥
en: They (your warriors) saw one another mangled and lying on the surface of the battle field, writhing in convulsions, distressed and weltering their own blood.

description: Display of illusion by Hidimba's son
sn: द्रोणं दुर्योधनं शल्यमश्वत्थामानमेव च। प्रायशश्च महेष्वासा ये प्रधानाः स्म कौरवाः॥
en: Drona, Duryodhana, Shalya Ashvathama, and other foremost bowmen of the Kaurava host were seen to fly away from the field of battle.

description: Display of illusion by Hidimba's son
sn: विध्वस्ता रथिनः सर्वे राजानश्च निपातिताः। हयाश्चैव हयारोहाः संनिकृत्ताः सहस्रशः॥
en: All the car-warriors appeared to be smashed, the kings fells, the horses and cavalry hacked to pieces by thousands.

description: Display of illusion by Hidimba's son
sn: तद् दृष्ट्वा तावकं सैन्यं विद्रुतं शिबिरं प्रति। मम प्राक्रोशतो राजंस्तथा देवव्रतस्य च॥
en: Beholding this (illusive) your warriors, 0 king, ran towards the encampments, although myself and Devavrata cried at the top of our voice saying, O king,

description: Display of illusion by Hidimba's son
sn: युध्यध्वं मा पलायध्वं मायैषा राक्षसी रणे। घटोत्कचप्रमुक्तेति नातिष्ठन्त विमोहिताः॥
en: scene "Go on fighting, fly not, this illusion has been set forth by Ghatotkacha?" But confounded as they were, they did not stop;

description: Display of illusion by Hidimba's son
sn: नैव ते श्रद्दधुर्मीता वदतोरावयोर्वचः। तांश्च प्रद्रवतो दृष्ट्वा जयं प्राप्ताश्च पाण्डवाः॥
en: They also did not believe the words we uttered, as they were inspired with terror. Beholding them fly, the Pandavas winning victory.

description: Display of illusion by Hidimba's son
sn: घटोत्कचेन सहिताः सिंहनादान् प्रचक्रिरे। शङ्खदुन्दुभिनिर्घोषैः समन्तान्नेदिरे भृशम्॥
en: Began to shout their war-cries, being joined by Ghatotkacha himself. They uttered continued yells of triumph, which became mixed with the blare of conchs and sound of drums.

description: Display of illusion by Hidimba's son
sn: एवं तव बलं सर्वं हैडिम्बेन दुरात्मना। सूर्यास्तमनवेलायां प्रभग्नं विद्रुतं दिशः॥
en: Thus it was that your whole army was broken and routed in all directions by the wicked-souled son of Hidimba at the time when the sun set.

sn: संजय उवाच तस्मिन् महति संक्रन्दे राजा दुर्योधनस्तदा। गाङ्गेयमुपसंगम्य विनयेनाभिवाद्य च॥
en: Sanjaya said When that dreadful battle was over, king Duryodhana, approaching the son of Ganga, and saluting him with humility,

sn: तस्य सर्वं यथावृत्तमाख्यातुमुपचक्रमे। घटोत्कचस्य विजयमात्मनश्च पराजयम्॥
en: Began to describe everything that had taken place, namely, victory by Ghatotkacha, and the defeat he himself has suffered.

sn: कथयामास दुर्धर्षो विनिःश्वस्य पुनः पुनः। अब्रवीच्च तदा राजन् भीष्मं कुरुपिताहम्॥
en: the won That invincible warrior, O king, theli spoke these words, sighing repeatedly and addressing the grandsire of the Kurus namely Bhishma.

sn: भवन्तं समुपाश्रित्य वासुदेवं यथा परैः। पाण्डवैर्विग्रहो घोरः समारब्धो मया प्रभो॥
en: "Just as the son of Vasudeva has been relied upon by the foe, so replying upon yourself, I have commenced this dreadful war with the Pandavas, O lord.

sn: एकादश समाख्याता अक्षौहिण्यश्च या मम। निदेशे तव तिष्ठन्ति मया सार्धं परंतप॥
en: My troops counting eleven Akshauhini in number, as also my own self, O grinder of foes, are all under your command.

sn: सोऽहं भरतशार्दूल भीमसेनपुरोगमैः। घटोत्कचं समाश्रित्य पाण्डवैर्युधि निर्जितः॥
en: Though thus supported, yet, О foremost of the Bharatas, I have been worsted in battle by the Pandava combatants headed by Bhimasena and dependent on Ghatotkacha.

sn: तन्मे दहति गात्राणि शुष्कवृक्षमिवानलः। यदिच्छामि महाभाग त्वत्प्रसादात् परंतप॥
en: This it is that is corroding my limbs like fire burning a withered tree. Therefore, O you of eminent parts, O slayer of foes, through your grace, I wish,

sn: राक्षसापसदं हन्तु स्वयमेव पितामह। त्वां समाश्रित्य दुर्धर्षं तन्मे कर्तुं त्वमर्हसि॥
en: O grandsire, to slay that worst of Rakshasas myself, mainly depending upon your invincible self. It behaves you to see that my wish is fulfilled.”

sn: एतच्छ्रुत्वा तु वचनं राज्ञो भरतसत्तम। दुर्योधनमिदं वाक्यं भीष्मः शान्तनवोऽब्रवीत्॥
en: Hearing, O foremost of the Bharatas, these words of the king, Bhishma the son of Shantanu addressed these words to Duryodhana.

sn: शृणु राजन् मम वचो यत् त्वां वक्ष्यामि कौरव। यथा त्वया महाराज वर्तितव्यं परंतप॥
en: "Hear, O king the words that I shall speak to you, O scion of the Kuru race, about how you should conduct yourself, Ogrinder of foes.

sn: आत्मा रक्ष्यो रणे तात सर्वावस्थास्वरिंदम। धर्मराजेन संग्रामस्त्वया कार्यः सदाऽनघ॥
en: O sire, O slayer of foes, you should ever carefully protect yourself in battle, under all circumstances. O sinless one, you should always engage with the very virtuous king Yudhishthira.

sn: अर्जुनेन यमाभ्यां वा भीमसेनेन वा पुनः। राजधर्मं पुरस्कृत्य राजा राजानमार्छति॥
en: Or with Arjuna or with Bhimasena or with the twins Nakula and Sahadeva. Keeping in view the duty of a king, a king strikes another royal compose.

sn: अहं द्रोणः कृपो द्रौणिः कृतवर्मा च सात्वतः। शल्यश्च सौमदत्तिश्च विकर्णश्च महारथः॥
en: Myself, Drona, Kripa, the son of Drona, Kritavarma of the Satvata race, Shalya, Somadatta's son, the might car-warrior Vikarna,

sn: तव च भ्रातरः श्रेष्ठा दुःशासनपुरोगमाः। त्वदर्थे प्रतियोत्स्यामो राक्षसं तं महाबलम्॥
en: Your heroic brothers headed by Dushasana, we shall all right with that highly puissant Rakshasa for your sake.

sn: रौद्रे तस्मिन् राक्षसेन्द्रे यदि तेऽनुशयो महान्। अयं वा गच्छतु रणे तस्य युद्धाय दुर्मतेः॥ भगदत्तो महीपालः पुरन्दरसमो युधि। एतावदुक्त्वा राजानं भगदत्तमथाब्रवीत्॥ समक्षं पार्थिवेन्द्रस्य वाक्यं वाक्यविशारदः। गच्छ शीघ्रं महाराज हैडिम्बं युद्धदुर्मदम्॥
en: Or if you bear implacable hatred for that fierce prince of Rakshasas, let this ruler of earth namely Bhagadatta, who is equal to Indra in battle, encounter in battle that evil-minded one." Having thus addressed the king, Bhishma eloquent in speech thus spoke of Bhagadatta even before that foremost of king “Proceed, O mighty monarch, without delay, against the son of Hidimba, invincible in battle.

sn: वारयस्व रणे यत्तो मिषतां सर्वधन्विनाम्। राक्षसं क्रूरकर्माणं यथेन्द्रस्तारकं पुरा॥
en: Putting forth all your energies do you resist that Rakshasa of cruel deeds before the eyes of these bowmen, even as Indra resisted Taraka in days gone by.

sn: तव दिव्यानि चास्त्राणि विक्रमश्च परंतप। समागमश्च बहुभिः पुराभूदमरैः सह॥
en: Your weapons are of celestial make and o redresser of your foes, your prowess in divine. And before this, you have had encounters with many a host of Asuras.

sn: त्वं तस्य नृपशार्दूल प्रतियोद्धा महाहवे। स्वबलेनोच्छ्रितो राजञ्जहि राक्षसपुङ्गवम्॥
en: O foremost of kings, you are a match for the Rakshasa in this fierce battle; and supported by your own divisions, O king, do you slay that foremost of Rakshasas.”

sn: एतच्छ्रुत्वा तु वचनं भीष्मस्य पृतनापतेः। प्रययौ सिंहनादेन परानभिमुखो द्रुतम्॥
en: Hearing these words of Bhishma the generalissimo of the Kauravas, Bhagadatta rushed towards the enemy uttering his war cries.

sn: तमाद्रवन्तं सम्प्रेक्ष्य गर्जन्तमिव तोयदम्। अभ्यवर्तन्त संक्रुद्धाः पाण्डवानां महारथाः॥
en: Beholding him rush like a mass of roaring clouds, the mighty car-warriors of the Pandava host inflamed with wrath advanced with impetuosity.

sn: भीमसेनोऽभिमन्युश्च राक्षश्च घटोत्कचः। द्रौपदेयाः सत्यधृतिः क्षत्रदेवश्च भारत॥
en: Bhimasena, Abhimanyu, the Rakshasa Ghatotkacha, the son of Draupadi, Satyadhriti, Kshatradeva, and O sire,

sn: चेदिपो वसुदानश्च दशार्णाधिपतिस्तथा। सुप्रतीकेन तांश्चापि भगदत्तोऽप्युपाद्रवत्॥
en: Vasudeva, the ruler of the Chedis, the ruler of the Dasharnas, all these warriors assaulted Bhagadatta. Bhagadatta also mounted on his elephant Supratika, charged these heroes.

sn: ततः समभवद् युद्धं घोररूपं भयानकम्। पाण्डूनां भगदत्तेन यमराष्ट्रविवर्धनम्॥
en: Then ensued a dreadful combat of awful aspect, between the Pandava hosts and Bhagadatta's divisions, increasing the population of Death's domain.

sn: प्रयुक्ता रथिभिर्बाणा भीमवेगाः सुतेजनाः। ते निपेतुर्महाराज नागेषु च रथेषु च॥
en: Fleet arrows charged with energy and shot by car-warriors, O mighty monarch, began to fall on elephants and chariots.

sn: प्रभिन्नाश्च महानागा विनीता हस्तिसादिभिः। परस्परं समासाद्य संनिपेतुरभीतवत्॥
en: Huge-elephants with rent temples and goaded on by their riders, approached and fell upon one another dauntlessly.

sn: मदान्धा रोषसंरब्धा विषाणार्महाहवे। बिभिदुर्दन्तमुसलैः समासाद्य परस्परम्॥
en: Excited to the highest pitch of fury and blind with shedding the temporal juice, those elephants approaching one another ripped one another open with the point of their tusks resembling hard bludgeons.

sn: हयाश्च चामरापीडाः प्रासपाणिभिरास्थिताः। चोदिताः सादिभिः क्षिप्रं निपेतुरितरेतरम्॥
en: Horses, graced with long-flowing tails and mounted by lancers, urged on by their riders, vehemently dashed against one another totally undaunted.

sn: पादाताश्च पदात्यौटुस्ताडिताः शक्तितोमरैः। न्यपतन्त तदा भूमौ शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः॥
en: Foot-soldiers struck by other foot soldiers with lances and dares, fell down on the ground by hundreds and thousands.

sn: रथिनश्च स्थै राजन् कर्णिनालीकसायकैः। निहत्य समरे वीरान् सिंहनादान् विनेदिरे॥
en: Car-warriors riding on their cars, O king, having slain many heroes with Karnis (barbed arrows) Nalikas (fire-arms) and shafts to began to vociferate their war-cries.

sn: तस्मिंस्तथा वर्तमाने संग्रामे लोमहर्षणे। भगदत्तो महेष्वासो भीमसेनमथाद्रवत्॥
en: When that hair string combat was thus raging, the fierce bowmen Bhagadatta assailed Bhimasena,

sn: कुञ्जरेण प्रभिन्नेन सप्तधा स्रवता मदम्। पर्वतेन यथा तोयं स्रवमाणेन सर्वशः॥
en: On his elephant with rent temples and with the temporal juice trickling down in seven distinct lines like so many billets flowing down the mountain barest.

sn: किरछरसहस्राणि सुप्रतीकशिरोगतः। ऐरावतस्थो मघवान् वारिधारा इवानघ॥
en: That sinless one advanced on the neck of Supratika, scattering thousands of arrows like the almighty Purandara riding on the Airavata.

sn: स भीमं शरधाराभिस्ताडयामास पार्थिवः। पर्वतं वारिधारभिस्तापान्ते जलदो यथा॥
en: That ruler of men afflicted Bhima with an arrows down-pour, like clouds afflicting the mountains with a down-pour of rain at the end of the summer.

sn: भीमसेनस्तु संक्रुद्धः पादरक्षान् परःशतान्। निजघान महेष्वासः संरब्धः शरवृष्टिभिः॥
en: Then that fierce that bowman Bhimasena excited with rage, slew his showers of arrows those warriors numbering more than hundred who were engaged in protecting Bhagadatta's feet.

sn: तान् दृष्ट्वा निहतान् क्रुद्धो भगदत्तः प्रतापवान्। चोदयामास नागेन्द्र भीमसेनस्थं प्रति॥
en: Seeing them slain, the highly powerful Bhagadatta, inflamed with wrath, goaded his foremost elephant towards chariot of Bhimasena.

sn: स नागः प्रेषितस्तेन बाणो ज्याचोदितो यथा। अभ्यधावत वेगेन भीमसेनमरिंदमम्॥
en: Like an arrow shot from the bowstring, that elephant, O subduer of foes, directed by Bhagadatta, impetuously rushed against Bhimasena.

sn: तमापतन्तं सम्प्रेक्ष्य पाण्डवानां महारथाः। अभ्यवर्तन्त वेगेन भीमसेनपुरोगमाः॥
en: Beholding that elephant thus advance furiously, the mighty car-warriors of the Pandava host headed by Bhima assaulted it.

sn: केकयाश्चाभिमन्युश्च द्रौपदेयाश्च सर्वशः। दशार्णाधिपतिः शूरः क्षत्रदेवश्च मारिष॥
en: The five Kaikeya brothers, Abhimanyu the sons of Draupadi, the heroic, ruler of the Dasharnas, Kshatra, and O sire,

sn: चेदिपश्चित्रकेतुश्च संरब्धाः सर्व एव ते। उत्तमास्त्राणि दिव्यानि दर्शयन्तो महाबलाः॥
en: The ruler of the Chedis, and Chitraketu, all these powerful warriors wrought up with wrath, displaying their excellent weapons of celestial make,

sn: तमेकं कुञ्जरं क्रुद्धाः समन्तात् पर्यवारयन्। स विद्धो बहुभिर्बाणैर्व्यरोचत महाद्विपः॥ संजातरुधिरोत्पीडो धातुचित्र इवाद्रिराट्। दशार्णाधिपतिश्चापि गजं भूमिधरोपमम्॥ समास्थितोऽभिदुद्राव भगदत्तस्य वारणम्। तमापतन्तं समरे गजं गजपति: स च॥
en: Surrounded that single elephant on all sides. That huge elephant pierced with many shafts and shedding blood profusely, appeared beautiful like the king of mountains decked with red chalk solution. The ruler of the Dasharnas, mounted on an elephant prodigious like a mountain, dashed against the elephant of Bhagadatta. Beholding that elephant rush towards himself that foremost of elephants,

sn: दधार सुप्रतीकोऽपि वेलेव मकरालयम्। वारितं प्रेक्ष्य नागेन्द्रं दशार्णस्य महात्मनः॥
en: Namely Supratika withstood it like the banks of the ocean resisting its surging waves. Beholding the excellent elephant of the highsouled ruler of Dasharna thus checked,

sn: साधु साध्विति सैन्यानि पाण्डवेयान्यपूजयन्। ततः प्राग्ज्योतिषः क्रुद्धस्तोमरान् वै चतुर्दश॥
en: The troops of the Pandavas, all applauded Bhagadatta saying 'excellent' 'excellent'. Thereupon the ruler of the Pragjyotishas waxing wrath, with fourteen lances,

sn: प्राहिणोत् तस्य नागस्य प्रमुखे नृपसत्तम। वर्म मुख्यं तनुत्राणं शातकुम्भपरिष्कृतम्॥ विदार्य प्राविशन् क्षिप्रं वल्मीकमिव पन्नगाः। स गाढविद्धो व्यथितो नागो भरतसत्तम॥
en: Struck, O foremost of men, the elephant of the Dasharna king; these lances penetrating the fine Armour and caparisons of gold covering the elephant's body, entered into it like snakes entering into their holes on ant-hills. That elephant, O foremost of the Bharatas, thus deeply pierced and extremely pained,

sn: उपावृत्तमदः क्षिप्रमभ्यवर्तत वेगितः। स प्रदुद्राव वेगेन प्रणदन् भैरवं रवम्॥
en: With its fury quenched, turned back with great vehemence; then that elephant uttering dreadful roars of agony ran,

sn: सम्मर्दयानः स्वबलं वायुर्वृक्षानिवौजसा। तस्मिन् पराजिते नागे पाण्डवानां महारथाः॥
en: Crushing the army to which it belonged, like the strong wind crushing the trees with its velocity. When that elephant of the Dasharna king was defeated, the mighty car-warriors of the Pandava host,

sn: सिंहनादं विनद्योच्चैयुद्धायैवावतस्थिरे। ततो भीमं पुरस्कृत्य भगदत्तमुपाद्रवन्॥
en: Uttering their war cries aloud, proceeded for battle. Then placing Bhima at their head they assailed Bhagadatta,

sn: किरन्तो विविधान् बाणाशस्त्राणि विविधानि च। तेषामापततां राजन् संकुद्धानाममर्षिणाम्॥ श्रुत्वा स निनदं धोरभमर्षाद् गतसाध्वसः। भगदत्तो महेष्वासः स्वनागं प्रत्यचोदयत्॥
en: Shooting arrows and weapons of various descriptions and shapes. Thereupon hearing the war-cries of those advancing and irate warriors longing for vengeance, that fierce bowman Bhagadatta Dauntless through rage, goaded his own elephant.

sn: अङ्कुशाङ्गुनुदितः स गजप्रवरो युधि। तस्मिन् क्षणे समभवत् सांवर्तक इवानलः ॥
en: That foremost of elephants, thus urged on by the press and stroke of the toe and the hook, in that battle destructive like the fire of dissolution.

sn: रथसंघांस्तथा नागान् हयांश्च हयासादिभिः। पादातांश्च सुसंक्रुद्धः शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः॥
en: Then, O king the elephant careered, hither and thither, and crushed divisions of cars and elephants and horses mounted by cavalrysoldiers.

sn: अमृद्गात् समरे नागः सम्प्रधावंस्ततस्ततः। तेन संलोड्यमानं तु पाण्डवानां बलं महत्॥
en: It also crushed foot-soldiers by hundreds and by thousands. Thus agitated by it, that mighty army of the Pandavas,

sn: संचुकोच महाराज चर्मेवाग्नौ समाहितम्। भग्नं तु स्वबलं दृष्ट्वा भगदत्तेन धीमता॥
en: Contracted, O monarch, like a piece of hide held over a blazing fire. Beholding his own army thus routed by the highly inteiligent Bhagadatta,

sn: घटोत्कचोऽथ संक्रुद्धो भगदत्तमुपाद्रवत्। विकटः परुषो राजन् दीप्तास्यो दीप्तलोचनः॥
en: Ghatotkacha excited to the highest pitch of fury, rushed against the former. That being of fierce aspect, with countenance and eyes flashing fire,

sn: रूपं विभीषणं कृत्वा रोषेण प्रज्वलन्निव। जग्राहं विमलं शूलं गिरीणामपि दारणम्॥
en: Burning with rage, assuming a dreadful form, took up a resplendent trident capable of rending even the mountains.

sn: नागं जिघांसुः सहसा चिक्षेप च महाबलः। स विस्फुलिङ्गमालाभिः समन्तात् परिवेष्टितः॥
en: Then that highly powerful hero desirous of slaying the elephant, hurled the lance, emitting scintillations of fire from all sides.

sn: तमापतन्तं सहसा दृष्ट्वा प्राग्ज्योतिषो नृपः। चिक्षेप रुचिरं तीक्ष्णमर्धचन्द्रं सुदारुणम्॥
en: Beholding that lance swiftly course towards the elephant, the ruler of the Pragjyotishas, sped dreadful crescent-shaped arrow of exceeding sharpness and effulgence.

sn: चिच्छेद तन्महन्छूलं तेन बाणेन वेगवान्। उत्पपात द्विधा च्छिन्नं शूलं हेमपरिष्कृतम्॥
en: Then with that arrow, that hero endued with energy, cut off the fierce trident; and that trident of golden effulgence then fell down on the ground divided in twain,

sn: महाशनिर्यथा भ्रष्टा शक्रुमुक्ता नभोगता। शूलं निपतितं दृष्ट्वा द्विधा कृत्तं च पार्थिवः॥
en: Like the mighty thunder bolt of Indra discharged by him, dropping through the skies. Then beholding that trident fallen and severed in twin, that ruler of the earth Bhagadatta,

sn: रुक्मदण्डां महाशक्ति जग्राहाग्निशिखोपमाम्। चिक्षेप तां राक्षसस्य तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति चाब्रवीत्॥
en: Took up a lance furnished with a golden staff and blazing like the flames of fire, and then hurled it at the Rakshasa saying 'Stay' 'Stay.'

sn: तामापतन्ती सम्प्रेक्ष्य वियत्स्थामशनीमिव। उत्पत्य राक्षसस्तूर्णं जग्राह च ननाद च॥
en: Beholding it course through the air like the thunder bolt itself, the Rakshasa lightly jumped up and caught hold of it uttering fierce warcries.

sn: बभञ्ज चैनां त्वरितो जानुन्यारोप्य भारत। पश्यतः पार्थिवेन्द्रस्य तदद्भुतमिवाभवत्॥
en: Then before before the very eyes eyes of the Pragjyotishas, O Bharata, he broke it into pieces placing it on his things. This feat was indeed wonderful.

sn: तदवेक्ष्य कृतं कर्म राक्षसेन बलीयसा। दिवि देवाः सगन्धर्वा मुनयश्चापि विस्मिताः॥
en: Beholding that mighty feat achieved by the puissant Rakshasa, the celestial in the heavens, along with the Gandharvas and the sages were amazed.

sn: पाण्डवाश्च महाराज भीमसेनपुरोगमाः। साधु साध्विति नादेन पृथिवीमन्वनादयन्॥
en: The Pandavas also, O mighty monarch, headed by Bhimasena filled the earth with their shouts of 'well-done' 'well-done'.

sn: तं तु श्रुत्वा महानादं प्रहृष्टानां महात्मनाम्। नामृष्यत महेष्वासो भगदत्तः प्रतापवान्॥
en: Hearing the roars of the delighted Pandavas of high soul, the highly powerful Bhagadatta that fierce bowman was unable to brook them.

sn: स विस्फार्य महच्चापमिन्द्राशनिसमप्रभम्। तर्जयामास वेगेन पाण्डवानां महारथान्॥
en: Then stretching his mighty bow equal to the thunder bolt of Indra in effulgence, he assailed with vehemence the mighty car-warriors of the Pandavas,

sn: विसृजन् विमलांस्तीक्ष्णान् नाराचाज्वलनप्रभान्। भीममेकेन विव्याध राक्षसं नवभिः शरैः॥
en: Discharging, as he advanced, resplendent dares of exceeding sharpness and of the effulgence of fire. He pierced Bhima with one shaft and the Rakshasas with nine,

sn: अभिमन्यु त्रिभिश्चैव केकयान् पञ्चभिस्तथा। पूर्णायतविसृष्टेन शरेणानतपर्वणा॥
en: Abhimanyu with three, and the Kaikeyas with five. Then with a shaft of straight joints, shot from his bow drawn to its fullest length,

sn: बिभेद दक्षिणं बाहुं क्षत्रदेवस्य चाहवे। पपात सहसा तस्य सशरं धनुरुत्तमम्॥
en: He pierced in that battle the right arm of Kshatradeva, and suddenly the latter's excellent bow with shafts fixed on the string fell down, loosed from the grasp.

sn: द्रौपदेयास्ततः पञ्च पञ्चभिः समताडयत्। भीमसेनस्य च क्रोधान्निजघान तुरङ्गमान्॥
en: Then again he pierced the five sons of Draupadi with five shafts, and inflamed with rage he slew the chargers of Bhimasena.

sn: ध्वजं केसरिणं चास्य चिच्छेद विशिखैस्त्रिभिः। निर्बिभेद त्रिभिश्चान्यैः सारथिं चास्य पत्रिभिः॥
en: Then with three shafts he cut down Bhima's standard bearing the device of the lion, and with another three winged shafts be penetrated the latter's charioteer.

sn: स गाढविद्धो व्यथितो रथोपस्थ उपाविशत्। विशोको भरतश्रेष्ठ भगदत्तेन संयुगे॥
en: The charioteer Vishoka thus deeply pierced and extremely pained by Bhagadatta in the conflict, squatted down on the terrace of the car, O foremost of the Bharatas.

sn: ततो भीमो महावाहुर्विरथो रथिनां वरः। गदां प्रगृह्य वेगेन प्रचस्कन्द रथोत्तमात्॥
en: Then O mighty monarch, that foremost of car-warriors Bhima, thus deprived of the use of his car, quickly leapt off from his excellent chariot with a mace in hand.

sn: तमुद्यतगदं दृष्ट्वा सशृङ्गमिव पर्वतम्। तावकानां भयं घोरं समपद्यत भारत॥
en: Beholding him with the uplifted mace resemble a crested mountain, your troops, O Bharata, were seized with panic.

sn: एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु पाण्डव: कृष्णसारथिः। आजगाम महाराज निनशत्रून् समन्ततः॥
en: At this juncture, O king, that son of Pandu, whose charioteer is Krishna, came destroying his foes right and left,

sn: यत्र तौ पुरुषव्याघ्रौ पितापुत्रौ महाबलौ। प्राग्ज्योतिषेण संयुक्तौ भीमसेनघटोत्कचौ॥
en: To that pare of the field where those two foremost of the men, those two mighty carwarriors, viz., Bhimasena and Ghatotkacha, father and son, were engaged with the ruler of the Pragjyotishas.

sn: दृष्ट्वा च पाण्डवो भ्रातृन् युध्यमानान् महारथान्। त्वरितो भरतश्रेष्ठ तत्रायुध्यत् किरञ्छरान्॥
en: Beholding his brothers, all mighty carwarriors, thus engaged in battle, that son of Pandu (Arjuna), O foremost of the Bharatas, joined the fight scattering his shafts on all sides.

sn: ततो दुर्योधनो राजा त्वरमाणो महारथः। सेनामचोदयत् क्षिप्रं रथनागाश्वसंकुलाम्॥
en: Then that mighty car-warrior namely Duryodhana himself in all haste urged on his army teeming with chariots and elephant.

sn: तामापतन्तीं सहसा कौरवाणां महाचमूम्। अभिदुद्राव वेगेन पाण्डवः श्वेतवाहनः॥
en: Thereupon that son of Pandu owning white steeds, rushed with velocity against the mighty army of the Kauravas that was speedily advancing.

sn: भगदत्तश्च समरे तेन नागेन भारत। विमृद्गन् पाण्डवबलं युधिष्ठिरमुपाद्रवत्॥
en: Then in that combat, O Bharata, Bhagadatta also, crushing the ranks of the Pandavas with that elephant of his, assailed Yudhishthira himself.

sn: तदाऽऽसीत् सुमहद् युद्धं भगदत्तस्य मारिष। पञ्चालैः पाण्डवेयैश्च केकयैश्चोद्यतायुधैः॥
en: Thereat, O sire, a fierce battle commenced between Bhagadatta on one side, and the Panchalas, the Srinjayas, and the Kaikeyas on the other, all with weapons upraised.

sn: भीमसेनोऽपि समरे तावुभौ केशवार्जुनौ। अश्रावयद् यथावृत्तमिरावद्वधमुत्तमम्॥
en: In the course of that combat, Bhimasena apprised Keshava and Arjuna of the slaughter of Iravat as it had happened.

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: संजय उवाच पुत्रं विनिहतं श्रुत्वा इरावन्तं धनंजयः। दुःखेन महताऽऽविष्टो निःश्वसन् पन्नगो यथा।॥
en: Sanjaya said Hearing his son Iravat slain, Dhananjaya, overwhelmed with grief and sighing like a snake.

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: अब्रवीत् समरे राजन् वासुदेवमिदं वचः। इदं नूनं महाप्राज्ञो विदुरो दृष्टवान् पुरा॥ कुरूणा पाण्डवानां च क्षयं घोरं महामतिः। स ततो निवारितवान् धृतराष्ट्र जनेश्ररम्॥
en: Spoke, O king, these words addressing the son of Vasudeva, even on the field of battle. "Surely the high-minded Vidura of great wisdom divined before hand this dreadful destruction of the Kurus and the Pandavas. It he was therefore that forbade king Dhritarashtra.

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: अन्ये च बहवो वीराः संग्रामे मधुसूदन। निहताः कौरवैः संख्ये तथास्माभिश्च कौरवाः॥
en: Innumerable other heroes, Oslayer of Madhu, have been slain by ourselves and the Kauravas in this sanguinary war.

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: अर्थहेतोर्नरश्रेष्ठ क्रियते कर्म कुत्सितम्। धिगर्थान् यत्कृते ह्येव क्रियते ज्ञातिसंक्षयः॥
en: For the sake of wealth, O foremost of men, vile deeds are being perpetrated. Fie on that wealth for the sake of which this destruction of kinsmen is being perpetrated.

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: अधनस्य मृतं श्रेयो न च ज्ञातिवधाद् धनम्। किं न प्राप्स्यामहे कृष्ण हत्वा ज्ञातीन् समागतान्॥
en: Death is preferable, for him who has no wealth, to the acquisition of wealth by the slaughter of his kinsmen. What good 0 Krishna, shall we reap, slaughtering these our kinsmen assembled together.

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: दुर्योधनापराधेन शकुनेः सौबलस्य च। क्षत्रिया निधनं यान्ति कर्णदुर्मन्त्रितेन च॥
en: In consequence of the faults of Duryodhana and those of Shakuni the son of Subala, and in consequence of the wicked counsels of Karna, the Kshatriyas are suffering destruction.

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: इदानीं च विजानामि सुकृतं मधुसूदन। कृतं राज्ञा महाबाहो याचता च सुयोधनम्॥
en: Now, O slayer of Madhu, do I realize what a great act of piety, O mighty-armed, one, did the king (Yudhishthira) do by begging of Suyodhana,

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: राज्याधु पञ्च वा ग्रामान् नाकार्षीत् स च दुर्मतिः। दृष्ट्वा हि क्षत्रियाशूराशयानान् धरणीतले॥
en: Either half of the kingdom or else five villages only. But the pervert Duryodhana turned deaf ears to our solicitations. Beholding these Kshatriyas, all brave warriors, prostrate on the surface of the earth.

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: निन्दामि भृशमात्मानं धिगस्तु क्षत्रजीविकाम्। अशक्तमिति मामेते ज्ञास्यन्ते क्षत्रिया रणे।॥
en: I can not but reproach myself. Fie on the life of a Kshatriya. These Kshatriyas may consider me incapable of batting any longer,

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: युद्धं तु मे न रुचितं ज्ञातिभिर्मधुसूदन। संचोदय हयाशीघ्रं धार्तराष्ट्रचमूं प्रति॥
en: But, O slayer of Madhu, this battle with my kinsmen does not at all please me. However, swiftly drive the horses towards the army of the sons of Dhritarashtra.

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: प्रतरिष्ये महापारं भुजाभ्यां समरोदधिम्। नायं यापयितुं कालो विद्यते माधव क्वचित्॥
en: I shall cross this ocean of battle incapable of being crossed by the strength of my arms. Surely, O Madhava, this is not the time for the display of feminine sentiments."

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: एवमुक्तस्तु पार्थेन केशवः परवीरहा। चोदयामास तानश्वान् पाण्डुरान् वातरंहसः॥
en: Thus spoken to by the son of Pritha that slayer of hostile heroes Keshava, urged on those cream colored steeds endued with the fleetness of the wind.

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: अथ शब्दो महानासीत् तव सैन्यस्य भारत। मारुतोद्धतवेगस्य सागरस्येव पर्वणि॥
en: Thereupon a deafening uproar was set up by your troops. O Bharata, like that of the ocean lashed into fury by the wind in the day of the new moon or the full moon.

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: अपराह्ने महाराज संग्रामः समपद्यत। पर्जन्यसमनिर्घोषो भीष्मस्य सह पाण्डवैः॥
en: Then in the afternoon, O mighty monarch, the battle that was fought between Bhishma and the Pandavas, resembled in its din the rumble of the rain clouds Parjanya.

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: ततो राजंस्तव सुता भीमसेनमुपाद्रवन्। परिवार्य रणे द्रोणं वसवो वासवं यथा॥
en: Then your sons, O king, surrounding Drona like the Vasus encircling Vasava, assailed Bhimasena.

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: ततः शान्तनवो भीष्मः कृपश्च रथिनां वरः। भगदत्तः सुशर्मा च धनंजयमुपाद्रवन्।॥
en: Thereafter Bhishma the son of Shantanu, Kripa the foremost of car-warriors, Bhagadatta and Susharma rushed against Dhananjaya.

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: पुत्रास्तु तव कौन्तेयं हार्दिक्यो बाह्निकश्चैव सात्यकिं समभिद्रुतौ। अम्बष्ठकस्तु नृपतिरभिमन्युमवस्थितः॥
en: The son of Hridika and Balhika both assailed Satyaki. King Ambashtaka encountered Abhimanyu.

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: शेषास्त्वन्ये महाराज शेषानेव महारथान्। ततः प्रववृते युद्धं घोररूपं भयावहम्॥
en: The rest of the warriors, O mighty monarch, engaged with other great car-warriors of the hostile party. Then commenced an awful engagement whose aspect was indeed terrible.

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: भीमसेनस्तु सम्प्रेक्ष्य पुत्रांस्तव जनेश्वर। प्रजज्वाल रणे क्रुद्धो हविषा हव्यवाडिव॥
en: Bhimasena beholding your sons, O ruler of me, in battle, blazed forth in anger like the sacrificial fire blazing forth with clarified butter.

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: छादयाञ्चक्रिरे शरैः। प्रावृषीव महाराज जलदा इव पर्वतम्॥
en: Your sons, o king, covered that son of Kunti with a shower of arrows like clouds covering a mountain with torrents of rain during the rainy season.

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: स च्छाद्यमानो बहुधा पुत्रैस्तव विशाम्पते। क्किणी संलिहन् वीरः शार्दूल इव दर्पितः॥
en: Then, O ruler of men, when thus covered with arrows by your sons, that hero Bhima, agile as a tiger, began to lick the corners of his mouth.

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: व्यूढोरस्कं ततो भीमः पातयामास भारत। क्षुरप्रेण सुतीक्ष्णेन सोऽभवद् गतजीवितः॥
en: Thereafter, 0 Bharata, he felled Vyudoraska with a sharp arrow furnished with a head like that of a horse-shoe; and the letter was deprived of his life.

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: अपरेण तु भल्लेन पीतेन न निशितेन तु। अपातयत् कुण्डलिनं सिंहः क्षुद्रमृगं यथा॥
en: Then again with an well tempered and well sharpened broad-headed shaft, he felled Kundalin, like a lion felling a smell deer.

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: ततः सुनिशितान् पीतान् समादत्त शिलीमुखान्। ससर्ज त्वरया युक्तः पुत्रास्ते प्राप्य मारिष॥
en: Then Bhima fixed on his bow-string arrows well-tempered and of exceeding sharpness. Getting near your sons. O sire, he let these arrows go with great lightness and with good aim.

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: प्रेषिता भीमसेनेन शरास्ते दृढधन्वना। अपातयन्त पुत्रांस्ते रथेभ्यः सुमहारथान्॥
en: These arrows sped by that firm bowman Bhimasena began to overthrow your sons, all mighty car-warriors, from their seats.

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: अनाधृष्टिं कुण्डभेदिं वैराटं दीर्घलोचनम्। दीर्घबाहुं सुबाहुं च तथैव कनकध्वजम्॥
en: Bhima felled Anadhrishti, Kundabheda, Vairata, Deerghalochana, Deerghabhau and Kanakdhvaja.

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: प्रपतन्त स्म वीरास्ते विरेजुर्भरतर्षभ। वसन्ते पुष्पशबलाश्शूताः प्रपतिता इव॥
en: When falling, these heroes, O scion of the Bharata race, appeared beautiful like blossoming mango trees falling down in the spring.

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: ततः प्रदुद्रुवुः शेषास्तव पुत्रा महाहवे। तं कालमिव मन्यन्तो भीमसेनं महाबलम्॥
en: Then considering the highly puissant Bhima to be the Destroyer incarnate, the rest of your sons, O ruler of men fled with haste.

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: द्रोणस्तु समरे वीरं निर्दहन्तं सुतांस्तव। यथाद्रिं वारिधाराभिः समन्ताद् व्यकिरच्छरैः। :॥
en: Then Drona covered that hero (Bhima) who had been consuming your sons, with a shower of shafts, like showers of rain covering the mountain breast.

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: तत्राद्भुतमपश्याम कुन्तीपुत्रस्य पौरुषम्। द्रोणेन वार्यमाणोऽपिनजघ्ने यत् सुतांस्तव॥
en: Then indeed we beheld the wonderful prowess of the son of Kunti, in as much as, though opposed by Drona himself, he succeeded in slaughtering your sons.

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: यथा गोवृषभो वर्ष संधारयति खात् पतत्। भीमस्तथा द्रोणमुक्तं शरवर्षमदीधरत्॥
en: Just as a heifer bears the shower of rain falling from the skies, so did Bhima bear the arrowy downpour discharged by Drona, like one undaunted.

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: अद्भुतं च महाराज तत्र चक्रे वृकोदरः। यत् पुत्रास्तेऽवधीत् संख्ये द्रोणं चैव न्यवारयत्॥
en: Really, O mighty monarch, Vrikodara achieved marvellous feats, in as much as he succeeded in slaying your sons and opposing Drona simultaneously.

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: पुत्रेषु तव वीरेषु चिक्रीडार्जुनपूर्वजः। मृगेष्विव महाराज चरन् व्याघ्रो महाबलः॥
en: Then the elder brother of Arjuna played amidst your heroic sons like, O monarch, a powerful tiger roving amidst a herd of deer.

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: यथा हि पशुमध्यस्थो दारयेत पशून् वृकः। वृकोदरस्तव सुतांस्तथा व्यद्रावयद् रणे॥
en: Just a wolf, remaining inside a herd of cattle, chases and terrifies them, so, in that battle, did Vrikodara crush and frighten your sons.

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: गाङ्गेयो भगदत्तश्च गौतमश्च महारथाः। पाण्डवं रभसं युद्धे वारयामासुरर्जुनम्॥
en: The son of Ganga, Bhagadatta, the mighty car-warrior Gautami's son, all opposed in battle Arjuna himself the son of Pandu.

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: अस्त्रैरस्त्राणि संवार्य तेषां सोऽतिरथो रणे। प्रवीरांस्तव सैन्येषु प्रेषयामास मृत्यवे॥
en: Then that Atiratha checking the enemies weapons with his own weapons, dispatched many mighty heroes of the hostile rank to the regions of Death.

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: अभिमन्युस्तु राजानमम्बष्ठं लोकविश्रुतम्। विरथं रथिनां श्रेष्ठं वारयामास सायकैः॥
en: Then Abhimanyu with his shafts, deprived that foremost of car-warriors, viz., king Ambashta of world-wide fame, of his car.

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: विरथो वध्यमानस्तु सौभद्रेण यशस्विना। अवप्लुत्य रथात् तूर्णमम्बष्ठो वसुधाधिपः॥
en: Deprived of his car and wondered by the illustrious son of Subhadra, he quickly jumped down from his car in shame and O lord of men.

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: असिं चिक्षेप समरे सौभद्रस्य महात्मनः। आरुरोह रथं चैव हार्दिक्यस्य महाबलः॥
en: Hurled his sword at the high-souled son of Subhadra. Thereafter that highly-powerful hero ascended the car of the son of Hridika.

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: आपतन्तं तु निस्त्रिंशं युद्धमार्गविशारदः। लाघवाद् व्यंसयामास सौभद्रः परवीरहा॥
en: Then that slayer of hostile hero, namely Abhimanyu, versed in all the modes, of warfare, beholding the swiftly advancing sword, evaded its strike by the agility of his movements.

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: व्यंसितं वीक्ष्य निस्त्रिंशं सौभद्रेण रणे तदा। साधु साध्विति सैन्यानां प्रणादोऽभूद् विशाम्पते॥
en: Beholding the sword thus baffled by the son of Subhadra, in that battle, the troops, O ruler of men, set up an uproar crying 'well-done' 'well-done'.

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: धृष्टद्युम्नमुखास्त्वन्ये तव सैन्यमयोधयन्। तथैव तावकाः सर्वे पाण्डुसैन्यमयोधयन्॥
en: Other warriors of the Pandava host headed by Dhrishtadyumna himself, engaged with your warriors; so also your warriors fought against the troops of the Pandavas.

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: तत्राक्रन्दो महानासीत् तव तेषां च भारत। निघ्नतां दृढमन्योन्यं कुर्वतां कर्म दुष्करम्॥
en: Then when they were thus slaughtering one another mercilessly and achieving feats difficult of being accomplished, fierce was the battle that raged between your and their warriors.

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: अन्योन्यं हि रणे शूराः केशेष्वाक्षिप्यमानिनः। नखदन्तैरयुध्यन्त मुष्टिभिर्जानुभिस्तथा॥
en: In that battle the warriors, O sire, dragging one another by the hair, fought on striking one another with their finger-nails, their teeth, their blows and thighs,

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: तलैश्चैवाथ निस्त्रिंशैर्बाहुभिश्च सुसंस्थितैः। विवरं प्राप्य चान्योन्यमनयन् यमसादनम्॥
en: Their sabers and palms and sinewy arms. Availing themselves of another's one weaknesses, they dispatched one another to the regions of Death.

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: न्यहनच्च पिता पुत्रं पुत्रश्च पितरं तथा। व्याकुलीकृतसर्वाङ्गा युयुधुस्तत्र मानवा॥
en: Father slew son and son slew father in that battle men fought on making the best use of all limbs.

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: रणे चारूणि चापानि हेमपृष्ठानि मारिष। हतानामपविद्धानि कलापाश्च महाधनाः॥
en: Beautiful bows with their staves decked with gold, O Bharata, loosened from the hold of slain warriors, and precious ornaments,

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: जातरूपमयैः पुखैः राजतैर्निशिताः शराः। तैलधौता व्यराजन्त निर्मुक्तभुजगोपमाः॥
en: And whetted shafts furnished with golden or Argentine wings and cleansed with oil and resembling snakes that have recently cast of their slough, bone on the field (as they lay scattered thereon).

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: हस्तिदन्तत्सरून् खङ्गाञ्जातरूपपरिष्कृतान्। चर्माणि चापविद्धानि रुक्मचित्राणि धन्विनाम्॥
en: Swords with hilts made of ivory and decked with gold, and bucklers, belonging to bowmen, embossed with gold, lay scattered on the field, loosened from the grasp of their wielders.

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: सुवर्णविकृतप्रासान् पट्टिशान् हेमभूषितान्। जातरूपमयाश्च : शक्तीश्च कनकोज्ज्वलाः॥
en: Lances and dares and battle-axes, and javelins, all decked with gold and of golden hue,

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: सुसंनाहाश्च पतिता मुसलानि गुरूणि च। परिधान् पट्टिशांश्चैव भिन्दिपालांश्च मारिष॥
en: And, O sire, beautiful coats of mail, heavy and light bludgeons, inaces, battle-axes and small arrows,

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: पतितान् विविधांश्चापाश्चित्रान् हेमपरिष्कृतान्। कुथा बहुविधाकाराश्चामरान् व्यजनानि च॥
en: And diverse-sharped, capricious for elephants, and chamaras and fans and numerous bows variegated and decorated with gold, lay scattered on the field.

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: नानाविधानि शस्त्राणि प्रगृह्य पतिता नराः। जीवन्त इव दृश्यन्ते गतसत्त्वा महारथाः॥
en: Men lying on the field with diverse weapons in grasp looked as if alive, though those mighty car-warriors were all deprived of the vital breaths.

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: गदाविमथितैर्गात्रैर्मुसलैभिन्नमस्तकाः। गजवाजिरथक्षुण्णाः शेरते स्म नराः क्षितौ॥
en: With their bodies crushed with strokes of maces, their heads smashed with the blows of bludgeons, and thoroughly mangled by the cars and elephants and steed, men lay on the field.

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: तथैवाश्वनृनागानां शरीरैर्विबभौ तदा। संछन्ना वसुधा राजन् पर्वतैरिव सर्वशः॥
en: Then the surface of the earth covered over with carcasses and corpses of men and elephants and steeds, appeared, O king, as if covered with hillocks.

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: समरे पतितैश्चैव शक्त्यष्टिशरतोमरैः। निस्त्रिशैः पट्टिशैः प्रासैरयस्कुन्तैः परश्वधैः॥ परिचैर्भिन्दिपालैश्च शतघ्नीभिश्च मारिष। शरीरैः शस्त्रनिर्भिन्नैः समास्तीर्यत मेदिनी॥
en: The field of battle was strewn over with fallen dares, swords, arrows, lances, sabers, axes, piked stakes, iron crows, battle-axes, clubs and bludgeons, and Shataghnees and bodies mutilated with weapons.

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: विशब्दरल्पशब्दैश्च शोणितौघपरिप्लुतैः। गतासुभिरमित्रघ्न विबभौ निचिता मही॥
en: O slayer of enemies, the earth covered with some warriors silent in death, with others weltering in their blood and with some again moaning feebly, became highly beautiful.

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: सतलत्रैः सकेयूरैर्बाहूभिश्चन्दनोक्षितैः। हस्तिहस्तोपमैश्छिरूरुभिश्च तरस्विनाम्॥ बद्धचूडामणिवरैः शिरोभिश्च सकुण्डलैः। पातितैर्ऋषभाक्षाणां बभौ भारत मेदिनी॥
en: O Bharata, the field of battle assumed a beautiful aspect, being strewn over with arms of mighty warriors smeared with sandal paste and adorned with leather fences and bracelets, as also with well snapped thighs resembling the trunks of elephants, and with severed heads of large-eyed combatants, graced with gems and car-rings.

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: कवचैः शोणितादिग्धैविप्रकीर्णश्च काञ्चनैः। रराज सुभृशं भूमिः शान्तार्चिभिरिवानलैः॥
en: Covered over with blood-soiled amours and golden ornaments, the field of battle appeared most beautiful as of scattered over with fires of mild flames.

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: विप्रविद्धैः कलापैश्च पतितैश्च शरासनैः। विप्रकीर्णैः शरैश्चैव रुक्मपुखैः समन्ततः॥
en: With ornaments of various kinds loosened from their places, with bows fallen about, with shafts of golden wings lying about,

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: रथैश्च सर्वतो भग्नैः किङ्किणीजालभूषितैः। वाजिभिश्च हतैर्बाणैः स्रस्तजिह्वः सशोणितैः॥
en: With many broken cars decked with rows of bells, with numerous slain steeds bespattered with gore and their tongues protruding,

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: अनुकर्णैः पताकाभिरुपासङ्गैर्ध्वजैरपि। प्रवीराणां महाशङ्कुर्विप्रकीर्णैश्च पाण्डुरैः॥
en: With car-bottons, and standards quivers, pennons, huge milk white conchs, belonging to mighty warrior,

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: स्रस्तहस्तैश्च मातङ्गैः शयानैर्विबभौ मही। नानारूपैरलंकारैः प्रमदैवाभ्यलकृता॥
en: With trunkless elephants, scattered on the field, the earth appeared charming like a damsel adorned with various of ornaments.

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: दन्तिभिश्चापरैस्तत्र सप्रसैर्गाढवैदनैः। करैः शब्दं विमुञ्चद्भिः शीकरं च मुमुर्मुहुः॥ विबभौ तद् रणस्थानं स्यन्दमानैरिवाचलैः। नानारागैः कम्बलैश्च परिस्तोमैश्च दन्तिनाम्॥
en: Then also with other elephants pierced with lances and pained to the extreme, and repeatedly uttering shrinks of agony with their trunks, the field of battle appeared beautiful as if covered with moving mountains. With blankets of various colors, and caparisons of elephants, sorts

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: वैदूर्यमणिदण्डैश्च पतितैरङ्कुशैः शुभैः। घण्डाभिश्च गजेन्द्राणां पतिताभिः समन्ततः॥
en: With well-shaped hooks having their handles decked with lapses, with bells of huge elephants scattered here and there.

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: विपाटितविचित्राभिः कुथाभिरङ्कुशैस्तथा। ग्रैवेयश्चित्ररूपैश्च रुक्मकक्ष्याभिरेव च॥
en: With clean housing of wonderful workmanship, with the skins of Ranku deer, with beautiful neck-laces and golden girths,

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: यन्त्रैश्च बहुधाच्छिन्नस्तोमरैश्चापि काञ्चनैः। अश्वानां रेणुकपिलै रुक्मच्छन्नैरुरश्छदैः॥
en: With many broken implements of war, with golden dares, with many gold fringed breast plates of steeds soiled with dust,

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: सादिनां भुजगैश्छिन्नैः पतितैः साङ्गदैस्तथा। प्रासैश्च विमलैस्तीक्ष्णैर्विमलाभिस्तथर्टिभिः॥
en: With served arms of horse soldiers, adorned with bracelets and scattered about, with well polished lances of keep points and with resplendent swords,

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: उष्णीषैश्च तथा चित्रैविप्रविब्रैस्ततस्ततः। विचित्रैर्बाणवर्धेश्च जातरूपपरिष्कृतैः॥
en: With variegated turbans fallen off and lying about, with wonderful crescent shaped arrows of golden effulgence,

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: अश्वास्तरपरिस्तोमै राङ्कवैर्मुदितैस्तथा। नरेन्द्रचूडामणिभिर्विचित्रैश्च महाधनैः॥
en: With housings of steeds with skins of Ranku deer, torn and soiled, with beautiful and precious gems that had graced the turbans of the kings,

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: छत्रैस्तथापविद्धैश्च चामरैर्व्यजनैरपि। पोन्दुद्युतिभिश्चैव वदनैश्चारुकुण्डलैः॥
en: With umbrellas, and chamaras and fans scattered about, with moon-like or lotus-like faces of warriors conspicuous with charming ear-rings,

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: क्लप्तश्मश्रुभिरत्यर्थं वीराणां समलंकृतैः। अपविद्धैर्महाराज सुवर्णोज्ज्वकुण्डलैः॥
en: And graced with well clipped beards and beautified, O king, with Kundalas of golden effulgence,

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: ग्रहनक्षत्रशबला द्यौरिवासीद् वसुन्धरा। एवमेते महासेने मृदृिते तत्र भारत॥
en: The earth looked like the sky be-spangled with the stars and the planets. Thus, O Bharata, the two mighty armies crushed one another,

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: परस्परं समासाद्य तव तेषां च संयुगे। तेषु श्रान्तेषु भग्नेषु मृदितेषु च भारत॥
en: Encountering one another in battle. When, O Bharata, the two armies were crushed and exhausted and completely broken,

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: रात्रिः समभवत् तत्र नापश्याम ततोऽनुगान्। ततोऽवहारं सैन्यानां प्रचक्रुः कुरुपाण्डवाः॥
en: The hideous pall of night fell over the earth and the fight could no longer be discerned. Then the Kurus and the Pandavas withdrew their forces from the field.

description: Withdrawal of the forces in the eighth day's fight
sn: रजनीमुखे सुरौद्रे तु वर्तमाने महाभये। अवहारं ततः कृत्वा सहिताः कुरुपाण्डवाः। न्यविशन्त यथाकालं गत्वा स्वशिबिरं तदा॥
en: When that hideous night, fierce and dreadful, set in, both the Kurus and the Pandavas, having withdrawn their forces, entered their encampments and retired to their respective tents.

sn: संजय उवाच ततो दुर्योधनो राजा शकुनिश्चापि सौबलः। दुःशासनश्च पुत्रस्ते सूतपुत्रश्च दुर्जयः॥
en: Sanjaya said Then king Duryodhana, Shakuni the son of Subala, your son Dushasana and the invincible son of Suta,

sn: समागम्य महाराज मन्त्रं चक्रुर्विवक्षितम्। कथं पाण्डुसुताः संख्ये जेतव्याः सगणा इति॥
en: These assembled together, O monarch, began to consult as to 'how could the sons of Pandu with their partisans be conquered in battle.'

sn: ततो दुर्योधनो राजा सर्वांस्तानाह मन्त्रिणः। सूतपुत्रं समाभाष्य सौबलं च महाबलम्॥
en: Thereafter king Duryodhana, addressing the son of Suta and the highly powerful son of Subala, spoke to all his counselors thus

sn: द्रोणो भीष्मः कृपः शल्यः सौमदत्तिश्च संयुगे। न पार्थान् प्रतिबाधन्ते न जाने तच्च कारणम्॥
en: “Even Drona, Bhishma, Kripa, Shalya, and the son of Somadatta cannot withstand the sons of Pritha in battle. I know not what the cause may be.

sn: अवध्यमानास्ते चापि क्षपयन्ति बलं मम। सोऽस्मि क्षीणबलः कर्ण क्षीणशस्त्रश्च संयुगे॥ निकृतः पाण्डवैः शूरैरवध्यैर्दैवतैरपि।
en: Thus unslain, they (the Pandavas) are every day reducing my troops in great number. Therefore, O Karna, I am becoming weaker in strength, and my store of weapons is also being exhausted.

sn: सोऽहं संशयमापन्नः प्रहरिष्ये कथं रणे॥ तमब्रवीन्महाराजं सूतपुत्रो नराधिपम्।
en: I am deceived by the warlike Pandavas, who cannot even be slain by the celestial themselves. I am doubtful of the means as to how to smile them down in battle.” To these words of the ruler of men, O king, Suta's son replied

sn: कर्ण उवाच मा शोच भरतश्रेष्ठ करिष्येऽहं प्रियं तव।॥ भीष्मः शान्तवस्तूर्णमपयातु महारणात्।
en: Karna said "Grieve not, O foremost of the Bharatas, I will compass your pleasure. Let Bhishma the son of Shantanu be speedily withdrawn from the battle.

sn: निवृत्ते युधि गाङ्गेये न्यस्तशस्त्रे च भारत॥ अहं पार्थान् हनिष्यामि सहितान् सर्वसोमकैः।
en: When, O scion of the Bharata race, the son of Ganga shall cease to fight, and when he shall lay aside his weapons, I will slay the sons of Pritha together with all the Somakas,

sn: पश्यतो युधि भीष्मस्य शपे सत्येन ते नृप॥ पाण्डवेषु दयां नित्यं स हि भीष्मः करोति वै।
en: In the battle even before the eyes of Bhishma himself. O king, I pledge my troth for this. Bhishma always uses the Pandavas leniently.

sn: अशक्तश्च रणे भीष्मो जेतुमेतान् महारथान्।॥ अभिमानी रणे भीष्मो नित्यं चापि रणप्रियः।
en: Bhishma also is incapable of conquering these mighty car-warriors (the Pandavas) in battle. Moreover Bhishma is proud in battle and is very fond of battle.

sn: स कथं पाण्डवान् युद्धे जेष्यते तातं संगतान्॥ स त्वं शीघ्रमितो गत्वा भीष्मस्य शिबिरं प्रति।
en: How could he, O sire, then conquer the Pandavas who have mustered a mighty force. Therefore, without the least delay, haying yourself towards the tent of Bhishma.

sn: अनुमान्य गुरुं वृद्धं शस्त्रं न्यासय भारत॥ न्यस्तशस्त्रे ततो भीष्मे निहतान् पश्य पाण्डवान्।
en: Persuade that venerable and old hero to lay aside weapons. Thus when Bhishma will lay aside his weapons, you shall see the Pandavas slain.

sn: मयैकेन रणे राजन् ससुहृद्गणबान्धवान्॥ एवमुक्तस्तु कर्णेन पुत्रो दुर्योधनस्तव। अब्रवीद् भ्रातरं तत्र दुःशासनमिदं वचः॥
en: With all their kinsmen and allies, by my single self in battle" Sanjaya said Thus spoke spoken to by Karna, your son Duryodhana,

sn: अनुयात्रं यथा सर्वं सज्जीभवति सर्वशः। दुःशासन तथा क्षिप्रं सर्वमेवोपपादय॥ एवमुक्त्वा ततो राजन् कर्णमाह जनेश्वरः। अनुमान्य रणे भीष्ममेषोऽहं द्विपदां वरम्॥
en: Then said these words addressing his brother Dushasana 'Look to it O Dushasana, that all my retinue may without delay be dressed and ready'. Having thus spoken, O king, to Dushasana, that ruler of men addressed Karna saying:

sn: आगमिष्ये ततः क्षिप्रं त्वत्सकाशमरिंदम्। अपक्रान्ते ततो भीष्मे प्रहरिष्यसि संयुगे॥
en: “Having persuaded that foremost of men, Bhishma to withdraw himself from the battle, I shall soon come back to you, O redresser of foes.

sn: निष्पपात ततस्तूर्णं पुत्रस्तव विशाम्पते। सहितो भ्रातृभिस्तैस्तु देवैरिव शतक्रतुः॥
en: When Bhishma will be withdrawn from the fight, you shall slay the Pandavas in battle." Then, O ruler of men your son, without any more loss of time, set out,

sn: ततस्तं नृपशार्दूलं शार्दूलसमविक्रमम्। आरोहयद्धयं तूर्णं भ्राता दुःशासनस्तदा॥ अङ्गदी बद्धमुकुटो हस्ताभरणवान् नृप। धार्तराष्ट्रो महाराज विबभौ स पथि व्रजन्॥
en: Accompanied by his brothers, and loO king like Indra surrounded by the celestial. Thereafter, his brother Dushasana, helped that foremost of kings equal to a tiger in strength, to mount on his steed. Decked with bracelets, with a diadem on his head, and O king, his arms graced with other ornaments,

sn: भण्डीपुष्पनिकाशेन तपनीयनिभेन च। अनुलिप्तः पराद्ध्यन चन्दनेन सुगन्धिना॥ अरजोऽम्बरसंवीतः सिंहखेलगतिर्नृप। शुशुभे विमलार्चिष्मान् नभसीव दिवाकरः॥ तं प्रयान्तं नरव्याघ्रं भीष्मस्य शिबिरं प्रति। अनुजग्मुर्महेष्वासाः सर्वलोकस्य धन्विनः॥
en: That son of yours, O monarch, shone brightly as he went towards Bhishma's tent. Smeared with fragrant sandal paste of the colour of Vandi flowers and of the effulgence of gold, and vested in dirtless raiment's, and proceeding with the playful gait of the lion, O king, Duryodhana appeared beautiful like the bright rayed orb of day in the skies. As that foremost of men (Duryodhana) proceeded towards the tent of Bhishma,

sn: भ्रातरश्च महेष्वासास्त्रिदशा इव वासवम्। हयानन्ये समारुह्य गजानन्ये च भारत॥
en: Numerous fierce bowmen of worldwide fame with bows in hand, as also his brothers all mighty bowmen, followed him like the celestial following Vasava.

sn: रथानन्ये नरश्रेष्ठं परिवः समन्ततः। आत्तशस्त्राश्च सुहृदो रक्षणार्थं महीपतेः॥
en: Mounted on other horses, elephants and chariots, other foremost of men, O Bharata, surrounded him on all sides.

sn: प्रादुर्बभूवुः सहिताः शक्रस्येवामरा दिवि। स पूज्यमानः कुरुभिः कौरवाणां महाबलः॥
en: Many of his friends bearing weapons came there for protecting the king, and accompanying Indra in heaven.

sn: प्रययौ सदनं राजा गाङ्गेयस्य यशस्विनः। अन्वीयमानः सततं सोदरैः परिवारितः॥
en: Thus honored by the Kurus, that highly puissant king of the Kurus repaired to the son of Ganga of illustrious fame.

sn: दक्षिणं दक्षिणं काले सम्भृत्य स्वभुजं तदा। हस्तिहस्तोपमं शैक्षं सर्वशत्रुनिबर्हणम्॥ प्रगृह्णन्नञ्जलीन् नृणामुद्यतान् सर्वतो दिशः। शुश्राव मधुरा वाचो नानादेशनिवासिनाम्॥
en: Followed and surrounded by his uterine brother, he proceeded, raising his right arm sinewy like the trunk of the elephant and capable of crushing all his foes, and therewith accepting the homage's offered by men on all sides with their raised and folder palms.

sn: संस्तूयमानः सूतैश्च मागधैश्च महायशाः। पूजयानश्च तान् सर्वान् सर्वलोकेश्वरेश्वरः॥
en: He heard sweet words uttered by the assembled inhabitants of various countries. moon That illustrious one was applauded and eulogised by the bards and minstrels.

sn: प्रदीपैः काञ्चनैस्त गन्धतैलावसेचितैः। परिवर्महाराज प्रज्वलद्भिः समन्ततः॥ स तैः परिवृतो राजा प्रदीपैः काञ्चनैर्व्वलन्। शुशुभे चन्द्रमा युक्तो दीप्तैरिव महाग्रहैः॥
en: That lord paramount of all men honorea all these men in return. Many high-souled persons then surrounded him on all sides with golden lamps, lighted and fed with fragrant oil. Thus surrounded by those lighted lamps made of gold, king Duryodhana,

sn: काञ्चनोष्णीषिणस्तत्र वेत्रझर्झरपाणयः। प्रोत्सारयन्तः शनकैस्तं जनं सर्वतो दिशम्॥
en: Shone resplendent like the surrounded by blazing mighty planets. Then attendants, graced with golden turbans, and bearing canes and Jharjharas in their hands,

sn: सम्प्राप्य तु ततो राजा भीष्मस्य सदनं शुभम्। अवतीर्य हयाच्चापि भीष्मं प्राप्य जनेश्वरः॥
en: Gradually cleared the crowd that surrounded the king on all sides. Thereafter, the king, reaching the beautiful tent of Bhishma.

sn: अभिवाद्य ततो भीष्मं निषण्णः परमासने। काञ्चने सर्वतोभद्रे स्पास्तरणसंवृते॥
en: And then descending from his horse, that ruler of men approached Bhishma. Thereafter doing obeisance to Bhishma, he seated himself on a beautiful seat,

sn: उवाच प्राञ्जलिर्भीष्मं बाष्पकण्ठोऽश्रुलोचनः। त्वां वयं हि समाश्रित्य संयुगे शत्रुसूदन॥
en: Made of gold, of exquisite workmanship and over-spread with an excellent coverlet. Then he thus spoke to Bhishma, with his palms folded, his voice choked in grief and his eyes bathed in tears.

sn: उत्सहेम रणे जेतुं सेन्द्रानपि सुरासुरान्। किमु पाण्डुसुतान् वीरान् ससुहृद्गणबान्धवान्॥
en: "Reliving upon you, O slayer of foes, we are even capable of vanquishing in battle the celestials and the Asuras united together, with Indra at their head,

sn: तस्मादर्हसि गाङ्गेय कृपां कर्तुं मयि प्रभो। जहि पाण्डुसुतान् वीरान् महेन्द्र इव दानवान्॥
en: What to speak of the sons of Pandu though they may be warlike and supported by their friends, allies and kinsmen. Therefore, O son of Ganga, O lord, it behold you to be merciful on me.

sn: अहं सर्वान् महाराज निहनिष्यामि सोमकान्। पञ्चालान् केकयैः सार्धं करूषांश्चेति भारत॥
en: Do you slay the heroic sons of Pandu like the great Indra slaying the Danavas. 'O monarch, I shall slaughter all the Somakas,

sn: त्वद्वचः सत्यमेवास्तु जहि पार्थान् समागतान्। सोमकांश्च महेष्वासान् सत्यवाग् भव भारत॥
en: The Panchalas, the Kauravas, O Bharata.' These were your words to me, verify them by slaying the assembled sons of Pritha,

sn: दयया यदि वा राजन् द्वेष्यभावान्मम प्रभो। मन्दभाग्यतया वापि मम रक्षसि पाण्डवान्॥
en: As also the Somakas, all fierce bowmen. Prove, O Bharata, the truth of your words. But if out of mercy, or out of your hatred, O lord,

sn: अनुजानीहि समरे कर्णमाहवशोभिनम्। स जेष्यति रणे पार्थान् ससुहृद्गणबान्धवान्॥
en: For my unfortunate self, you are inclined to spare the sons of Pandu, then permit Karna, that ornament of battle, to join the fight.

sn: स एवमुक्त्वा नृपतिः पुत्रो दुर्योधनस्तव। नोवाच वचनं किञ्चिद् भीष्मं सत्यपराक्रमम्॥
en: He will conquer the sons of Pritha together with all their friends, allies and kinsmen." Having thus spoken, your royal son dreadful prowess. airunn

sn: संजय उवाच वाक्शल्यैस्तव पुत्रेण सोऽतिविद्धो महामनाः। दुःखेन महताऽऽविष्टो नोवाचाप्रियमण्वपि॥
en: Sanjaya said Thereupon the high-souled Bhishma, thus deeply pierced by the dagger-like words of your son and overwhelmed with grief, spoke not even a single disagreeable word to your son.

sn: स ध्यात्वा सुचिरं कालं दुःखरोषसमन्वितः। श्वसमानो यथा नागः प्रणुन्नो वाक्शलाकया।॥
en: Thus mutilated with those 'worldly daggers' and sighing like a snake, and meditating for a while, and possessed with rage and sorrow,

sn: उद्धृत्य चक्षुषी कोपानिर्दहन्निव भारत। सदेवासुरगन्धर्व लोकं लोकविदां वरः॥
en: And raising, out of wrath, his two eyes, as if, O Bharata, desirous of consuming the universe with the celestial, the Gandharvas, and the Asuras, that foremost of those learned in the ways of the world (viz., Bhishma),

sn: अब्रवीत् तव पुत्रं स सामपूर्वमिदं वचः। किं त्वं दुर्योधनैवं मां वाक्शल्यैरपकृन्तसि॥
en: Coolly addressed these words to your son "Why, O Duryodhana, are you piercing me with these harrowing words of yours'

sn: घटमानं यथाशक्ति कुर्वाणं च तव प्रियम्। जुह्वानं समरे प्राणांस्तव वै प्रियकाम्यया॥
en: Me who ever endeavoring to the best of my abilities to accomplish what will be for your benefit, me who am ready to lay down my very life in battle, for doing good to you?

sn: यदा तु पाण्डवः शूरः खाण्डवेऽग्निमतर्पयत्। पराजित्य रणे शक्रं पर्याप्तं तन्निदर्शनम्॥
en: Is not this sufficient indication (of his invincibility) that heroic son of Pandavas and (Arjuna), gratified Agni by allowing it to consume the Khandava foremost, after having vanquished his opponents in battle?
