en: Therefore surrounding the grandsire with all our troops, do you protect him as he accomplishes difficult feats in battle.”

sn: स एवमुक्तः समरे पुत्रो दुःशासनस्तव। परिवार्य स्थितो भीष्मं सैन्येन महता वृतः॥
en: Thus spoken to, your son Dushasana stood with his mighty army, surrounding Bhishma in that battle.

sn: ततः शतसहस्राणां हयानां सुबलात्मजः। विमलप्रासहस्तानामृष्टितोमरधारिणाम्॥
en: Then Shakuni the son of Subala with hundred thousands cavalry soldiers, holding resplendent spears, swords and lances,

sn: दर्पितानां सुवेशानां बलस्थानां पताकिनाम्। शिक्षितैयुद्धकुशलैरुपेतानां नरोत्तमैः॥
en: And forming proud and strong detachment of troops, bearing standards, and supported by well-disciplined and wellaccomplished foot-soldiers alll excellent fighters,

sn: नकुलं सहदेवं च धर्मराजं च पाण्डवम्। न्यवारयन्नरश्रेष्ठान् परिवार्य समन्ततः॥
en: Began to oppose Nakula, Sahadeva, and Yudhishthira the son of Pandu, surrounding those foremost of men on all sides.

sn: ततो दुर्योधनो राजा शूराणां हयसादिनाम्। अयुतं प्रेषयामास पाण्डवानां निवारणे॥११॥
en: Then king Duryodhana dispatched a detachment of ten thousand horses all brave warriors, for checking the Pandavas. a

sn: तैः प्रविष्टैर्महावेगैर्गरुत्मद्भिरिवाहवे। खुराहता धरा राजंश्चकम्पे च ननाद च॥
en: As these highly fleet chargers resembling so many Sarudas rushed to battle, the earth, O king, struck with their hoof quaked and produced a loud din.

sn: खुरशब्दश्च सुमहान् वाजिनां शुश्रुवे तदा। महावंशवनस्येव दह्यमानस्य पर्वते॥
en: The dreadful clatter of the hoofs of steeds that was then heard resembled the cracking sound produced by a bamboo forest on the top of a hill, when set on fire.

sn: उत्पतद्भिश्च तैस्तत्र समुद्भूतं महद् रजः। दिवाकररथं प्राप्य छादयामास भास्करम्॥
en: As these rushed to the charge, there arose a thick cloud of dust, that mounting to the solar orbit shrouded the sun itself.

sn: वेगवद्भिर्हयैस्तैस्तु क्षोभिता पाण्डवी चमूः। निपतद्भिर्महावेगैर्हसैरिव महत् सरः॥ (तुरगैर्वायुवेगैश्च तत् सैन्यं व्याकुलीकृतम्।)
en: Then the army of the Pandavas was agitated by the charge of that fleetest horse division, like flight of swans suddenly alighting on its waters.

sn: हेषतां चैव शब्देन न प्राज्ञायत किञ्चन। ततो युधिष्ठिरो राजा माद्रीपुत्रौ च पाण्डवौ।॥
en: Nothing could be heard in consequence of their neighs. Then king Yudhishthira, and the two sons of Pandu begotten upon Madri,

sn: प्रत्यघ्नस्तरसा वेगं समरे हयसादिनाम्। उद्वृत्तस्य महाराज प्रावृट्कालेऽतिपूर्यतः॥ पौर्णमास्यामम्बुवेगं यथा वेला महोदधेः। ततस्ते रथिनो राजञ्छरैः संनतपर्वभिः॥
en: Quickly checked the furious charge of those horsemen in battle, like, O mighty monarch, the banks withstanding the waves of the mighty main swollen with the waters of the rainy season on the day of the full moon. Thereupon, O king, these car-warriors, with their straightknotted shafts,

sn: न्यकृन्तन्नुमाङ्गानि शरेण हयसादिनाम्। ते निपेतुर्महाराज निहता दृढधन्विभिः॥
en: Began to sever the heads of these horsesoldiers from their trunk; then, O mighty monarch, they fell down slain by these firm bowmen,

sn: नागैरिव महानागा यथावद् गिरिहरे। तेऽपि प्रासैः सुनिशितैः शरैः संनतपर्वभिः॥
en: Like huge elephants falling down in mountain caves, slain by their compeers. Those warriors of the Pandava, army also with sharp lances and straight shafts,

sn: न्यकृन्तन्नुत्तमाङ्गानि विचरन्तो दिशो दश। अभ्याहता हयारोहा ऋष्ठियभर्भरतर्षभ॥
en: Cut down the head of those horsemen, coursing all over the field. Then, O foremost of the Bharatas, the horse-riders thus struck with swords,

sn: अत्यजन्नुत्तमाङ्गानि फलानीव महाद्रुमाः। ससादिनो हया राजंस्तत्र तत्र निषूदिताः॥
en: Began to drop their heads like mighty trees dropping the fruits. Slain on all sides, horse with their riders.

sn: पतिताः पात्यमानाश्च प्रत्यदृश्यन्त सर्वशः। वध्यमाना हयाश्चैव प्राद्रवन्तः भयार्दिताः॥
en: Were seen fallen and falling. When being thus slaughtered, the horses began to fly away struck with terror,

sn: यथा सिहं समासाद्य मृगाः प्राणपरायणा:। पाण्डवाश्च महाराज जित्वा शत्रून् महामृधे॥
en: Like so many deer flying for the sake of preserving their lives at the sight of a lion. The Pandavas then, O monarch, confounding their foes in battle,

sn: दध्मुः शङ्खांश्च भेरीश्च ताडयामासुराहवे। ततो दुर्योधनो दीनो दृष्ट्वा सैन्यं पराजितम्॥
en: Blew their conchs and struck up their drums in battle. Then dejected in consequence of the defeat of his troops, Duryodhana.

sn: अब्रवीद् भरतश्रेष्ठ मद्रराजमिदं वचः। एष पाण्डुसुतो ज्येष्ठो यमाभ्यां सहितो रणे॥
en: Said, O foremost of the Bharatas, these words to the king of the Madras: “This eldest son of Pandu, supported by his twin brothers in battle.

sn: पश्यतां वो महाबाहो सेनां द्रावयति प्रभो। तं वारय महाबाहो वेलेव मकरालयम्॥
en: Is routing my army, O mighty-armed king, before your very eyes. Do you check him, O inighty-armed one, like the banks of the sea checking its fury.

sn: त्वं हि संश्रूयसेऽत्यर्थमसाबलविक्रमः। पुत्रस्य तव तद् वाक्यं श्रुत्वा शल्यः प्रतापवान्॥
en: You are well-known for the irresistibleness of your strength and prowess.” Then hearing these words of your son, the highly puissant Shalya,

sn: स ययौ रथवंशेन यत्र राजा युधिष्ठिरः। तदापतद् वै सहसा शल्यस्य समुदहद् बलम्॥ महौघवेगं समरे वारयामास पाण्डवः। मद्रराजं च समरे धर्मराजो महारथः॥ दशभिः सायकैस्तूर्णमाजघान स्तनान्तरे। नकुलः सहदेवश्च तं सप्तभिरजिह्मगैः॥
en: Supported by a division of cars, tied to the spot where king Yudhishthira was. Then the son of Pandu checked in battle that detachment of Shalya falling upon him with great fury. Then that mighty car-warrior the very virtuous king Yudhishthira quickly pierced the king of the Madras with ten shafts between his breasts; and Nakula and Sahadeva pierced him with seven straight wafts.

sn: मद्रराजोऽपि तान् सर्वानाजघान त्रिभिस्त्रिभिः। युधिष्ठिरं पुनः षष्ट्या विव्याध निशितैः शरैः॥
en: The king of the Madras in return pierced them all with three shafts each; then again he pierced Yudhishthira with sixty shafts of exceeding sharpness;

sn: माद्रीपुत्रौ च सम्भ्रान्तौ द्वाभ्यां द्वाभ्यामताडयत्। ततो भीमो महाबाहुर्दृष्ट्वा राजानमाहवे॥
en: He also wounded the two terrified sons of Madri with two shafts cach. Thereupon the mighty armed Bhima, beholding the king,

sn: मद्रराजरथं प्राप्तं मृत्योरास्यगतं यथा। अभ्यपद्यत संग्रामे युधिष्ठिरममित्रजित्॥
en: Staying within the reach of the Madra king's car, as if within the very jaws of death, rushed in that battle to the side of Yudhishthira.

sn: ततो युद्धं महाघोरं प्रावर्तत सुदारुणम्। अपरां दिशमास्थाय पतमाने दिवाकरे॥
en: Then when the sun, rising on the western quarter, was scorching the earth, a fierce and sanguinary engagement commenced.

description: Termination of the ninth day's battle
sn: संजय उवाच ततः पिता तव क्रुद्धो निशितैः सायकोत्तमैः। आजघान रणे पार्थान् सहसेनान् समन्ततः॥ भीमं द्वादशभिर्विद्ध्वा सात्यकिं नवभिः शरैः। नकुलं च त्रिभिर्विद्ध्वा सहदेवं च सप्तभिः॥
en: Sanjaya said Thereupon your father, waxing worth, began to pierce the sons of Pritha and their troops, with excellent shafts of exceeding sharpness. Piercing Bhima with twelve, Satyaki with nine shafts, Nakula with three, Sahadeva with seven, he pierced.

description: Termination of the ninth day's battle
sn: युधिष्ठिरं द्वादशभिर्बाह्वोरुरसि चार्पयत्। धृष्टद्युम्नं ततो विद्ध्वा ननाद सुमहाबलः॥ तं द्वादशाख्यैर्नकुलो माधवश्च त्रिभिः शरैः। धृष्टद्युम्नश्च सप्तत्या भीमसेनश्च सप्तभिः॥
en: Yudhishthira with twelve shafts on the arms and on the breast. Then that highly powerful hero, having pierced Dhrishtadyumna also, uttered a loud roar. Nakula pierced him in return with twelve shafts, the descendant of Madhu's race with three, Sahadeva with seventy, Partha with nine, Dhrishtadyumna with seventy and Bhimasena with seven shafts.

description: Termination of the ninth day's battle
sn: युधिष्ठिरो द्वादशभिः प्रत्यविध्यत् पितामहम्। द्रोणस्तु सात्यकि विद्ध्वा भीमसेनमविध्यत॥
en: Then Yudhishthira pierced the grandsire in return with twelve shafts. Drona having pierced Satyaki began to pierce Bhima,

description: Termination of the ninth day's battle
sn: एकैकं पञ्चभिर्बाणैर्यमदण्डोपमैः शितैः। तौ च तं प्रत्यविध्येतां त्रिभिस्त्रिभिरजिह्मगैः॥
en: Each time with five whetted shafts resembling the rods of Death himself. Those two heroes, each then with three straight shafts, pierced in return,

description: Termination of the ninth day's battle
sn: तोत्रैरिवं महानागं द्रोणं ब्राह्मणपुङ्गवम्। सौवीराः कितवाः प्राच्याः प्रतीच्योदीच्यमालवाः॥
en: That foremost of Brahmanas namely Drona, like a guide piercing a mighty elephant with the hook. The Souviras, the Kitavas, the Easterners, the Westerners, the Northerners, the Malavas,

description: Termination of the ninth day's battle
sn: अभीषाहाः शूरसेनाः शिवयोऽथ वसातयः। संग्रामे नाजहुर्भीष्मं वध्यमानाः शितैः शरैः॥
en: The Abhishahas, the Shurasenas, the Shibi's and the Vasatis, these did not avoid Bhishma through fearfully slaughtered by him in battle with whetted shafts.

description: Termination of the ninth day's battle
sn: तथैवान्ये महीपाला नानादेशसमागताः। पाण्डवानभ्यवर्तन्त विविधायुधपाणयः॥
en: So also many other kings, come from various other realms, rushed at the Pandavas, bearing in their hands weapons of diverse kinds.

description: Termination of the ninth day's battle
sn: तथैव पाण्डवा राजन् परिवब्रुः पितामहम्। स समन्तात् परिवृतो रथौधैरपराजितः॥
en: The Pandavas also surrounded the grandsire on all sides. That invincible one (Bhishma) surrounded by that mighty division of cars,

description: Termination of the ninth day's battle
sn: गहनेऽग्निरिवोत्सृष्टः प्रजज्वाल दहन् परान्। रथाग्न्यगारश्चापार्चिरसिशक्तिगदेन्धनः॥
en: Blazed forth destroying the foe, like a terrible conflagration in a wood. His car was his fire chamber, his bow was his flames, his sword, dares, and maces were his fuels.

description: Termination of the ninth day's battle
sn: शरस्फुलिङ्गो भीष्माग्निर्ददाह क्षत्रियर्षभान्। सुवर्णपुङरिषुभिर्गार्धपक्षौः सुतेजनैः॥
en: His arrows were the scintillation's, and Bhishma himself was the fire that consumed the forest of the Kshatriyas. With arrows furnished with golden wings and the feathers of vultures and charged with great energy,

description: Termination of the ninth day's battle
sn: कर्णिनालीकनाराचैश्छादयामास तद् बलम्। अपातयद् ध्वजांश्चैव रथिनश्च शितैः शरैः॥
en: With barbed arrows, with Nalikas and Narachas, Bhishma covered that army of the Pandavas. He felled with whetted shafts elephants and car-warriors.

description: Termination of the ninth day's battle
sn: मुण्डतालवनानीव चकार स रथव्रजान्। निर्मनुष्यान् रथान् राजन् गजाश्वांश्च संयुगे॥ अकरोत् स महाबाहुः सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वरः। तस्य ज्यातलनिर्घोषं विस्फूर्जितमिवाशनेः॥ निशम्य सर्वभूतानि समकम्पन्त भारत। अमोघा ह्यपतन् बाणाः पितुस्ते भरतर्षभ॥
en: He made the large detachment of carwarriors look like a palmyra-forest with its trees deprived of their tops. In that battle, ) king, that mighty-armed hero, the foremost of all wielders of weapons, made cars, elephants and steeds deprived of their riders. Hearing the twang, that resembled the rumbling of the thunder, of your father's bow, ( Bharata, ali creatures began to tremble, and O foremost of the Bharatas, then the arrows of your father seemed to be incapable of being baffled.

description: Termination of the ninth day's battle
sn: नासज्जन्त तनुत्रेषु भीष्मचापच्युताः शराः। हतवीरान् रथान् राजन् संयुक्ताञ्जवनैर्हयैः॥ अपश्याम महाराज ह्रियमाणान् रणाजिरे। चेदिकाशिकरूषाणं सहस्राणि चतुर्दश॥ महारथाः समाख्याताः कुलपुत्रास्तनुत्यजः। अपरावर्तिनः सर्वे सुवर्णविकृतध्वजाः॥ संग्रामे भीष्ममासाद्य व्यादितास्यमिवान्तकम्। निमग्नाः परलोकाय सवाजिरथकुञ्जराः॥
en: Then the arrows, shot from the bow of Bhishma, did not only strike against the armours of combatants but penetrated through them. We saw, O monarch, many cars dragged over the field, by the fleet steeds that were harnessed to them, in consequence of the death of the heroes that rode them. Four and ten thousand car-warriors belonging to the Chedis, the Kashis and the Karushas, all well-known, and born of illustrious family, never retreating from field and owners of golden standards, prepared to lay down their lives in battle, encountering Bhishma who looked like Death himself with mouth wide open, were all dispatched to the regions of the departed along with their steeds, cars and elephants.

description: Termination of the ninth day's battle
sn: भग्नाक्षोपस्करान् कांश्चिद् भग्नचक्रांश्च भारत। अपश्याम महाराज शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः॥
en: We beheld, O monarch, chariots by hundreds and thousands then, some with their Akihas shattered and bottoms broken, some with their wheels broken.

description: Termination of the ninth day's battle
sn: सवरूथे रथैर्भग्नै रथिभिश्च निपातितः। शरैः सुकवचैश्छिन्नैः पट्टिशैश्च विशाम्पते।॥
en: Then, O monarch, with cars broken along with their wooden fences, with fallen carwarriors, with arrows, with beautiful but broken armours, with battle axes,

description: Termination of the ninth day's battle
sn: गदाभिर्भिन्दिपालैश्च निशितैश्च शिलीमुखैः। अनुकईंपासङ्गैश्चर्भग्नैश्च मारिष॥
en: With maces, with short arrows, and whetted shafts, with car bottoms, with quivers, shattered wheels, O sire,

description: Termination of the ninth day's battle
sn: बाहुभिः कार्मुकैः खङ्गैः शिरोभिश्च सकुण्डलैः। तलत्रैरङ्गुलित्रैश्च ध्वजैश्च विनिपातितैः॥
en: With arms, bows, words, and heads graced with ear-rings, with finger-protectors and gloves, and broken standards,

description: Termination of the ninth day's battle
sn: चापैश्च बहुधा च्छिन्नैः समास्तीर्यत मेदिनी। हतारोहा गजा राजन् हयाश्च हयसादिनः॥
en: With bows splintered into pieces, the earth become strewn over. Then, O king, elephants with their riders slain, and slaughtered horsemen,

description: Termination of the ninth day's battle
sn: न्यपतन्त मतप्राणाः शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः। यतमानाश्च ते वीरा द्रवमाणान् महारथान्॥ नाशक्नुवन् वारयितुं भीष्मबाणप्रपीडितान्। महेन्द्रसमवीर्येण वध्यमाना महाचमूः॥ अभज्यत महाराज न च द्वौ सह धावतः। आविद्धरथनागाश्वं पतितध्वजसंकुलम्॥
en: Began to fall down dead on the field by hundreds and by thousands. Striving their least, the heroic warriors of the Pandava army could not rally the car-warriors who, afflicted by the arrows of Bhishma, were flying then in all directions. That mighty host (of the Pandavas), slaughtered by Bhishma who equaled even Indra in prowess, were so completely broken that no two persons were seen to fly together. With its chariots, elephants and horses laid low and with its standards and flags overthrown in profusion,

description: Termination of the ninth day's battle
sn: अनीकं पाण्डुपुत्राणां हाहाभूतमचेतनम्। जघानात्र पिता पुत्रं पुत्रश्च पितरं तथा।॥ प्रियं सखायं चाक्रन्दे सखा दैवबलात् कृतः। विमुच्य कवचानन्ये पाण्डुपुत्रस्य सैनिकाः॥ प्रकीर्य कैशान् धावन्तः प्रत्यदृश्यन्त सर्वशः। तद् गोकुलमिवोद्भ्रान्तमुद्घान्तरथकूबरम्॥ ददृशे पाण्डुपुत्रस्य सैन्यमार्तस्वरं तदा। प्रभज्यमानं सैन्यं तु दृष्ट्वा यादवनन्दनः॥
en: The army of the sons of Pandu, deprived of its consciousness began to utter cries of “Oh” and "Alas.” In that battle father slew his own son and son slew his own father, and friend slew his dear friend urged on to the deed by Destiny. Many combatants of the Pandava army, doffing their armours, were seen to run away in all directions with their hair disheveled. Then the troops belonging to the son of Pandu were seen to run hurriedly in fear like a herd of bulls throwing aside the yokes of cars, and the cries of distress that these troops then uttered were indeed fearful. Then the descendant of the Yadava race beholding the army thus routed,

description: Termination of the ninth day's battle
sn: उवाच पार्थं बीभत्सुं निगृह्य रथमुत्तमम्। अयं स कालः सम्प्राप्तः पार्थ यः काक्षितस्तव॥
en: Spoke to Vibhatsu the son of Pritha reining in the excellent chariot he drove, "O Partha, the hour which you so ardently looked forward to, has now arrived.

description: Termination of the ninth day's battle
sn: प्रहरास्मिन् नरव्याघ्र न चेन्मोहाद् विमुह्यसे। यत् पुरा कथितं वीर राज्ञां तेषां समागमे॥
en: Now strike, O foremost of men, or you shall be unconscious being overwhelm by a swoon. O hero, the words you uttered before in the assemblage of kings.

description: Termination of the ninth day's battle
sn: विराटनगरे तात संजयस्य समीपतः। भीष्मद्रोणमुखान् सर्वान् धार्तराष्ट्रस्य सैनिकान्॥ सानुबन्धान् हनिष्यामि ये मां योत्स्यन्ति संगरे। इति तत् कुरु कौन्तेय सत्यं वाक्यमरिंदम॥
en: In the city of Virata, before Sanjaya himself. O Pritha's son, those words are 'I will slay all the combatants of Dhritarashtra's son along with their followers, headed by Bhishma and Drona, all who will fight with me.' O son of Kunti, O grinder of foes, do you now verify those words of yours.

description: Termination of the ninth day's battle
sn: क्षत्रधर्ममनुस्मृत्य युध्यस्व विगतज्वरः। इत्युक्तो वासुदेवेन तिर्यग्दृष्टिरधोमुखः॥ अकाम इव बीभत्सुरिदं वचनमब्रवीत्। अवध्यानां वधं कृत्वा राज्यं वा नरकोत्तरम्॥
en: Remembering the duties of a Kshatriya go to fighting without harbouring any anxious feeling.” Thus spoken to, by the son of Vasudeva, with his head hung down and loO king askance, Arjuna as if unwilling said these words to the former. “Either to acquire monarchy with hell at the end by the slighter of those who ought not to be slain,

description: Termination of the ninth day's battle
sn: दुःखानि वनवासे वा किं नु मे सुकृतं भवेत्। चोदयाश्वान् यतो भीष्मः करिष्ये वचनं तव॥
en: Or to suffer the woes of an exiled life, which of these should now be considered as my duty? However, O Hrishikesha, urged the steeds on, I shall do your bidding.

description: Termination of the ninth day's battle
sn: पातयिष्यामि दुर्धर्षं भीष्मं कुरुपितामहम्। स चाश्वान् रजतप्रख्यांश्चोदयामास माधवः॥
en: I will lay low Bhishma the grandsire of the Kurus." Thereupon that descendant of Madhu's race, drove those steeds of Argentine hue,

description: Termination of the ninth day's battle
sn: यतो भीष्मस्ततो राजन् दुष्प्रेक्ष्यो रश्मिवानिव।
en: To the spot, O king, where Bhishma; incapable of being gazed at like the sun himself, was staying. Thereupon the mighty army of king Yudhishthira returned to the charge,

description: Termination of the ninth day's battle
sn: दृष्ट्वा पार्थं महाबाहुं भीष्मायोद्यतमाहवे। ततो भीष्मः कुरुश्रेष्ठः सिंहवद् विनदन् मुहुः॥
en: Beholding the mighty-armed son of Pritha rush for an encounter with Bhishma in that terrible fight. Thereupon, O foremost of the Kurus, Bhishma uttered his war-cry even like a roaring lion,

description: Termination of the ninth day's battle
sn: धनंजयरथं शीघ्रं शरवर्षैरवाकिरत्। क्षणेन स रथस्तस्य सहयः सहसारथिः॥
en: And then quickly covered the car of Dhananjaya with a shower of arrows. Within a moment Arjuna's car with the steeds and charioteer,

description: Termination of the ninth day's battle
sn: शरवर्षेण महता न प्राज्ञायत भारत। वासुदेवस्त्वसम्भ्रान्तो धैर्यमास्थाय सत्वरः॥
en: Were lost to view in consequence of that thick arrows shower. But the son of Vasudeva, with the least delay and with patience, fearlessly,

description: Termination of the ninth day's battle
sn: चोदयामास तानश्वान् विनुन्नान् भीष्मसायकैः। ततः पार्थो धनुर्गृह्य दिव्यं जलदनिःस्वनम्॥
en: Drove forward those steeds mangled with the shafts of Bhishma. Then the son of Pritha taking up his bow of celestial make and of twang as loud as the rumble of clouds,

description: Termination of the ninth day's battle
sn: पातयामास भीष्मस्य धनुश्छित्त्वा शितैः शरैः। सच्छिन्नधन्वा कौरव्यः पुनरन्यन्महद् धनुः॥ निमेषान्तरमात्रेण सज्यं चक्रे पिता तव। चकर्ष च ततो दो• धनुर्जलदनिःस्वनम्॥ अथास्य तदपि क्रुद्धश्चिच्छेद धनुरर्जुनः।
en: Felled the bow of Bhishma having burst it open with whetted shafts. Then deprived of his bow, that foremost of the Kurus, viz., your father, within a moment made another bow ready for use. But Arjuna, waxing worth, cut off even that bow of his.

description: Termination of the ninth day's battle
sn: तस्य तत् पूजयामास लाघवं शान्तनोः सुतः॥ गाङ्गेयस्त्वब्रवीत् पार्थं धन्विश्रेष्ठमरिंदम। साधु साधु महाबाहो साधु कुन्तीसुतेति च॥
en: Then the son of Shantanu highly praised Arjuna's lightness of hand saying "Well-done well-done, O mighty-armed one, well-done, 0 son of Kunti."

description: Termination of the ninth day's battle
sn: समाभाष्यैवमपरं प्रगृह्य रुचिरं धनुः। मुमोच समरे भीष्मः शरान् पार्थरथं प्रति॥
en: Having thus applauded Partha and taking up another bow of great excellence, Bhishma sped, in that battle, arrows against the chariot of the former.

description: Termination of the ninth day's battle
sn: अदर्शयद् वासुदेवो हययाने परं बलम्। मोघान् कुर्वशरांस्तस्य मण्डलानि निदर्शयन्॥
en: Then the son of Vasudeva displayed superior skill in the management of horses in as much as he baffled Bhishma's arrows by a swift whirling of the car in a circular motion.

description: Termination of the ninth day's battle
sn: शुशुभाते नरव्याघ्रौ तौ भीष्मशरविक्षतौ। गोवृषाविव संरब्धौ विषाणोल्लिखिताङ्कितौ॥
en: Mangled with the shafts of Bhishma, those two foremost of men, (Arjuna and Krishna) then appeared beautiful like two heifers, enraged, and mangled with scratches of their horns.

description: Termination of the ninth day's battle
sn: वासुदेवस्तु सम्प्रेक्ष्य पार्थस्य मृदुयुद्धताम्। भीष्मं च शरवर्षाणि सृजनामनिशं युधि॥ प्रतपन्तमिवादित्यं मध्यमासाद्य सेनयोः। वरान् वरान् विनिघ्नन्तं पाण्डुपुत्रस्य सैनिकान्॥ युगान्तमिव कुर्वाणं भीष्मं यौधिष्ठिरे बले। नामृष्यत महाबाहुर्माधवः परवीरहा॥
en: Then that slayer of hostile heroes, that mighty-armed descendant of Madhu's race, viz., the son of Vasudeva, seeing that Arjuna was fighting mildly, and that Bhishma was continually pouring his showers of arrows in battle, also that the latter standing in the centre of the two hosts, was scorching (every thing) like the sun himself and was slaying the foremost combatants of the army of Pandu's son, and was producing in the army of Yudhishthira a total annihilation like that at the end of a Yuga, was unable to bear it any longer.

description: Termination of the ninth day's battle
sn: उत्सृज्य रजतप्रख्यान् हयान् पार्थस्य मारिष। वासुदेवस्ततो योगी प्रचस्कन्द महारथात्॥
en: Then, O sire, throwing away the reins of Partha's steeds of Argentine hue, that illustrious Yogin (Krishna) waxing irascible, jumped down from that huge chariot.

description: Termination of the ninth day's battle
sn: अभिदुद्राव भीष्मं स भुजप्रहरणो बली। प्रतोदपाणिस्तेजस्वी सिंहवद् विनदन् मुहुः॥ दारयन्निव पद्भ्यां स जगतीं जगदीश्वरः। क्रोधताप्रेक्षणः कृष्णो जिघांसुरमितद्युतिः॥
en: Then roaring repeatedly like a lion, Krishna endued with strength and fleetness, and of incomparable effulgence, that lord of the universe, having his bare arms for his weapons and wielding the whip in his hands, and with his eyes coppery in rage, rushed towards Bhishma, splitting the earth with his tread, and desirous of slaying the latter.

description: Termination of the ninth day's battle
sn: ग्रसन्तमिव चेतांसि तावकानां महाहवे। दृष्ट्वा माधवमाक्रन्दे भीष्मायोद्यतमन्तिके॥
en: In that mighty battle, the hearts of your warriors were filled with terror as they beheld him of Madhu's race near Bhishma, ready to fall upon the latter.

description: Termination of the ninth day's battle
sn: हतो भीष्मो हतो भीष्मस्तत्र तत्र वचो महत्। अश्रूयत महाराज वासुदेवभयात् तदा॥
en: Then, O mighty monarch, exclamations of 'Bhishma is slain, Bhishma is slain' were heard there, uttered by your troops inspired with the fear of Vasudeva's son.

description: Termination of the ninth day's battle
sn: पीतकौशेयसंवीतो मणिश्यामो जनार्दनः। शुशुभे विद्रवन् भीष्मं विद्युन्माली यथाम्बुदः॥
en: Then Janardana, vested in yellow silk raiment’s and blue in complexion like the lapis lazuli, rushing towards Bhishma appeared beautiful like a rain cloud charged with lightning.

description: Termination of the ninth day's battle
sn: स सिंह इव मातङ्गं यूथर्षभ इवर्षभम्। अभिदुद्राव वेगेन विनदन् यादवर्षभः॥
en: Just as the king of beasts uttering loud roars rushes towards the leader of an elephant-herd, so then that foremost of Madhu's race rushed impetuously towards Bhishma, uttering loud roars.

description: Termination of the ninth day's battle
sn: तमापतन्तं सम्प्रेक्ष्य पुण्डरीकाक्षमाहवे। असम्भ्रमं रणे भीष्मो विचकर्ष महद् धनुः॥
en: Then beholding in that dreadful battle, Krishna of eyes like lotus petals rush furiously towards him, Bhishma began to stretch his strong and mighty bow.

description: Termination of the ninth day's battle
sn: उवाच चैव गोविन्दमसम्भ्रान्तेन चेतसा। एह्येहि पुण्डरीकाक्ष देवदेव नमोऽस्तु ते॥
en: Then addressing Govinda with a dauntless heart, he said "Come, come, O you of eyes like lotus petals! O god of gods, I do bow down unto you.

description: Termination of the ninth day's battle
sn: मामद्य सात्वतश्रेष्ठ पातयस्व महाहवे। त्वया हि देव संग्रामे हतस्यापि ममानघ॥
en: Lay me low, O foremost of the Satvata race, this day in this dreadful fight! O sinless one, slain by you in this battle, O god,

description: Termination of the ninth day's battle
sn: श्रेय एव परं कृष्ण लोके भवति सर्वतः। सम्भावितोऽस्मि गोविन्द त्रैलोक्येनाद्य संयुगे॥
en: I shall reap great good, O Krishna, in every respect in this world. O Govinda, today, in the three worlds, have I attained great honour in battle.

description: Termination of the ninth day's battle
sn: प्रहरस्व यथेष्टं वै दासौऽस्मि तव चानघ। पार्थः समभिद्रुत्य केशवम्॥ नग्राह महाबाहुर्बाहुभ्यां परिगृह्य वै। निगृह्यमाणः पार्थेन कृष्णो राजीवलोचनः॥ जगामैवैनमादाय वेगेन पुरुषोत्तमः। पार्थस्तु विष्टभ्य बलाच्चरणौ परवीरहा॥ अन्वगेव ततः निजग्राह हृषीकेशं कथंचिदं दशमे पदे।
en: Strike me as it pleases you, O sinless one, as I am merely a slave of yours.” Meanwhile the mighty-armed son of Pritha, running behind Keshava, seized the latter embracing him with his two arms. That foremost of men viz., Krishna of eyes like expanded lotuses, thus held by the son of Pritha proceeded even carrying the latter with him. Then that slayer of hostile heroes, that puissant warrior, the son of Pritha, forcibly encircling (with his two arms) the two legs of Hrishikesha stopped him when he was going to take the tenth step.

description: Termination of the ninth day's battle
sn: तत एवमुवाचार्तः क्रोधपर्याकुलेक्षणम्॥ निःश्वसन्तं यथा नागमर्जुनः प्रणयात् सखा। निवर्तस्व महाबाहो नानृतं कर्तुमर्हसि॥ यत् त्वया कथितं पूर्वं न योत्स्यामिति केशव। मिथ्यावादीति लोकास्त्वां कथयिष्यन्ति माधव॥
en: Then his friend Arjuna, highly distressed, affectionately addressing Keshava, who was then breathing like a snake and whose eyes were rolling in wrath, said 'Stop, O mightyarmed one! It behooves you not to falsify those words of yours viz., 'I will not fight,' that you had spoken before, O Keshava. Then, O descendant of Madhu's race, men will call your a liar.

description: Termination of the ninth day's battle
sn: ममैषः भारः सर्वो हि हनिष्यामि पितामहम्। शपे केशव शस्त्रेण सत्येन सुकृतेन च॥
en: Let all the burden be on me, I will slay the grandsire! Ishvara, O Keshava, o Keshava, by my weapons, by my troth and by iny good achievements,

description: Termination of the ninth day's battle
sn: अन्तं यथा गमिष्यामि शत्रूणां शत्रुसूदन। अद्यैव पश्य दुर्धर्षं पात्यमानं महास्थम्॥
en: That, O destroyer of foes, I will do everything by which the destruction of the enemy may be accomplished. Even this day behold the invincible mighty car-warrior overthrown.

description: Termination of the ninth day's battle
sn: तारापतिमिवापूर्णमन्तकाले यदृच्छया। माधवस्तु वचः श्रुत्वा फाल्गुनस्य महात्मनः॥ (अभवत् परमप्रीतो ज्ञात्वा पार्थस्य विक्रमम्।)
en: By me, with the least difficulty like the crescent moon at the end of a Yuga.” Hearing those words of the high-souled Phalguna, that descendant of Madhu's race, became cheerful knowing the prowess of Partha.

description: Termination of the ninth day's battle
sn: न किंचिदुक्त्वा सक्रोध आरुरोह रथं पुनः। तौ रथस्थौ नरव्याघ्रो भीष्मः शान्तनवः पुनः॥ ववर्ष शरवर्षेण मेघो वृष्ट्या यथाऽचलौ। प्राणानादत्त योधानां पिता देवव्रतस्तव॥
en: Without speaking any thing, again mounted the chariot in rage. Then Bhishma the son of Shantanu, once more covered those two foremost of men on their cars, with an arrows downpour, like clouds drenching the mountain breast with showers of rain. Then your sire Devavrata took the lives of all hostile warriors,

description: Termination of the ninth day's battle
sn: गभस्तिभिरिवादित्यस्तेजांसि शिशिरात्यये। यथा कूरूणां सैन्यानि बभ युधि पाण्डवाः॥
en: Like the sun drawing energies from all things with his rays at the end of the winter season. As the sons of Pandu broke the ranks of the Kuru troops in battle.

description: Termination of the ninth day's battle
sn: तथा पाण्डवसैन्यानि बभञ्ज युधि ते पिता। हतविद्रुतसैन्यास्तु निरुत्साहा विचेतसः॥ निरीक्षितुं न शेकुस्ते भीष्ममप्रतिमं रणे। मध्यंगतमिवादित्यं प्रतपन्तं स्वतेजसा॥ ते वध्यमाना भीष्मेण शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः। कुर्वाणं समरे कर्माण्यतिमानुषविक्रमम्॥ वीक्षांचक्रुर्महाराज पाण्डवा भयपीडिताः। तथा पाण्डवसैन्यानि द्राव्यमाणानि भारत॥ त्रातारं नाध्यगच्छन्त गावः पङ्कगता इव। पिपीलिका इव क्षुण्णा दुर्बला बलिना रणे॥
en: So your father also broke the Pandava ranks in battle. The soldiers thus routed, and despondent and cheerless, slain, by hundreds and thousands, by Bhishma, were unable to gaze at the incomparable Bhishma, who was scorching the foe like the sun in the meridian. The Pandava troops then afflicted with terror, O monarch, (fearfully) looked at Bhishma who was achieving great feats with his superhuman prowess. Then, O Bharata, the Pandava troops thus crushed by Bhishma, could not find a protector, like kine sunk in slough, or like an ephemeral ant afflicted by a powerful creature.

description: Termination of the ninth day's battle
sn: महारथं भारत दुष्प्रकम्पं शरौघिणं प्रतपन्तं नरेन्द्रान्। भीष्मं न शेकुः प्रतिभीक्षितुं ते शरार्चिषं सूर्यमिवातपन्तम्॥
en: The combatants of the Pandava hosts, O Bharata, were unable to look at that mighty car-warrior Bhishma, who was incapable of being shaken, who with his arrow showers was afflicting the hostile kings, and who in consequence of his blazing shafts looked like the shining sun.

description: Termination of the ninth day's battle
sn: मस्तं जगामाथ सहस्ररश्मिः। ततो बलानां श्रमकर्शितानां मनोऽवहारं प्रति सम्बभूव॥
en: While he was thus crushing the Pandava troops, the sun of thousand rays went below the horizon. Then the hearts, of all those warriors exhausted with fatigue, yearned for the order of withdrawal.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: संजय उवाच युध्यतामेव तेषां तु भास्करेऽस्तमुपागते। संध्या समभवद् घोरा नापश्याम ततो रणम्॥
en: Sanjaya said While they were thus fighting and when the sun set, the pall of hideous twilight enveloped the earth, and the battle became lost of view.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: ततो युधिष्ठिरो राजा संध्यां संदृश्य भारत। वध्यमानं च भीष्मेण त्यक्तास्त्रं भयविह्वलम्॥ स्वसैन्यं च परावृत्तं पलायनपरायणम्। भीष्मं च युधि संरब्ध पीडयन्तं महारथम्॥ सोमकांश्च जितान् दृष्ट्वा निरुत्साहान् महारथान्। चिन्तयित्वा ततो राजा अवहारमरोचयत्॥
en: Then o Bharata, king Yudhishthira, beholding that twilight had set in and that his own soldiers, slaughtered by Bhishma, had thrown down their weapons, and that terrorstruck and repulsed from the field of battle, they are flying away in all directions; beholding also the mighty car-warrior Bhishma inflicting everybody, and seeing also the mighty car-warriors if the Somakas defeated and cheerless, pondered a while and then commanded the withdrawal of the forces.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: ततोऽवहारं सैन्यानां चक्रे राजा युधिष्ठिरः। तथैव तव सैन्यानामवहारो ह्यभूत् तदा॥
en: Then king Yudhishthira withdrew his troops; so also the withdrawal of your forces was also done at the same time.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: ततोऽवहारं सैन्यानां कृत्वा तत्र महारथाः। न्यवशिन्त कुरुश्रेष्ठ संग्रामे क्षतविक्षताः॥
en: Then the mighty car-warriors, having withdrawn their forces, foremost of the Kurus, entered their tents, with their bodies mangled with wounds.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: भीष्मस्य समरे कर्म चिन्तयानास्तु पाण्डवाः। नालभन्त तदा शान्ति भीष्मबाणप्रपीडिताः॥
en: The Pandavas, afflicted with the arrows of Bhishma and thinking of the feats achieved in battle, did not obtain any peace.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: भीष्योऽपि समरे जित्वा पाण्डवान् सहसृजयान्। पूज्यमानस्तव सुतैर्वन्द्यमानश्च भारत॥
en: Having vanquished the Pandavas and the Srinjayas in battle and adored and honoured by your sons, Bhishma then, O monarch.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: न्यविशत् कुरुभिः सार्धं हृष्टरूपैः समन्ततः। ततो रात्रिः समभवत् सर्वंभूतप्रमोहिनी॥
en: Accompanied by the delighted Kurus, entered his tent. Then night set in, that renders all creatures unconscious (in sleep).

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: तस्मिन् रात्रिमुखे घोरे पाण्डवा वृष्णिभिः सह। सुंजयाच दुराधर्षा मन्त्राय समुपाविशन्॥
en: In the beginning of that dread time of night, the Pandavas along with the Vrishnis and the invincible Srinjayas, sat together for consultation.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: आत्मनिःश्रेयसं सर्वे प्राप्तकालं महाबलाः। मन्त्रयामासुरव्यग्रा मन्त्रनिश्चयकोविदाः॥
en: The highly powerful heroes, accomplished in drawing conclusion from inferences, coolly consulted about what would be most profitable to them under these circumstances.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: ततो युधिष्ठिरो राजा मन्त्रयित्वा चिरं नृप। वासुदेवं समुद्वीक्ष्य वचनं चेदमाददे॥
en: Thereafter king Yudhishthira, O king, having pondered for a considerable length of time, addressed these words to the son of Vasudeva, casting his eyes on the latter.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: कृष्ण पश्य महात्मानं भीष्मं भीमपराक्रमम्। गजं नलवनानीव विमृद्रन्त बलं मम॥
en: Behold, O Krishna, the high-souled Bhishma of fierce prowess crush my ariny like an elephant crushing a forest of reeds.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: न चैवैनं महात्मानमुत्सहामो निरीक्षितुम्। लेलिह्यमानं सैन्येषु प्रवृद्धमिव पावकम्॥
en: We dare not even look at that illustrious warrior when he licks, like a raging conflagration, all my troops up.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: यथा घोरो महानागस्तक्षको वै विषोल्बणः। तथा भीष्मो रणे क्रुद्धस्तीक्ष्णशस्त्रः प्रतापवान्॥
en: The mighty puissant Bhishma, possessed of sharp weapons and inflamed with rage battle, appears like the mighty snake Takshaka of great ferocity and virulent venom.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: गृहीतचापः समरे प्रमुञ्चन् निशिताञ्छरान्। शक्यो जेतुं यमः क्रुद्धो वज्रपाणिश्च देवराट्॥ वरुणः पाशभृच्चापि सगदो वा धनेश्वरः। न तु भीष्मः सुसंक्रुद्धः शक्यो जेतुं महाहवे॥
en: Indeed the god of Death wrought up with wrath and shooting whetted shafts from his bow, or the king of the celestial armed with the thunder-bolt, or Varuna holding his mighty in noose or the god of wealth wielding his mace, may be vanquished in battle. But Bhishma cnraged in battle could not be vanquished.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: सोऽहमेवंगते. कृष्ण निमग्नः शोकसागरे। आत्मनो बुद्धिदौर्बल्याद् भीष्ममासाद्य संयुगे॥
en: When, O Krishna, such is the state of affairs, I am, in consequence of the weakness of my own understanding, sunk in sorrow, having to fight with Bhishma as an opponent in battle.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: वनं यास्यामि दुर्धर्ष श्रेयो वै तत्र मे गतम्। न युद्धं चोरते कृष्ण हन्ति भीष्मो हि नः सदा॥
en: I will again retire, O invincible one, to the forests, even that is better for me now. Battle I no longer like, O Krishna, as Bhishma always slaughters our troops.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: यथा प्रज्वलितं वह्नि पतङ्गः समभिद्रवन्। एकतो मृत्युमभ्येति तथाऽहं भीष्ममीयिवान्॥
en: Just as an insect rushing at a blazing fire reaps only death, so llave I reaped the same result having dared a combat with Bhishma.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: क्षयं नीतोऽस्मि वार्ष्णेय राज्यहेतोः पराक्रमी। भ्रातरश्चैव मे शूराः सायकै शपीडिताः॥
en: Put as I may, my prowess forth, ) descendant of the Vrishni race, I am being Vriven to destruction for the sake of my kingdom. My brave brothers are all surely afflicted with the shafts of Bhishma.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: मत्कृते भ्रातृसौहार्दाद् राज्यभ्रष्टा वनं गताः। परिक्लिष्टा तथा कृष्णा मत्कृते मधुसूदन॥
en: Through their fraternal affection, they had to go into exile into the woods, for me, deprived of their kingdom. So also, O slayer of Madhu, Krishna had to undergo various troubles for me only.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: जीवितं बहु मन्येऽहं जीवितं ह्यद्य दुर्लभम्। जीवितस्याद्य शेषेण चरिष्ये धर्ममुत्तमम्॥
en: I prize life very much; and it is dear and scare to be obtained. If I can save it now, shall husband out the rest of it in the performance of excellent deeds of piety

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: यदि तेऽहमनुग्राह्यो भ्रातृभिः सह केशव। स्वधर्मस्याविरोधेन हितं व्याहर केशव॥
en: If, indeed, I and my brothers be worthy of your grace, then O Keshava, advice me what will be beneficial to me, without clashing against our prescribed duties.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: एवं श्रुत्वा वचस्तस्य कारुण्याद् बहुविस्तरम्। प्रत्युवाच ततः कृष्णः सान्त्वयानो युधिष्ठिरम्॥
en: Hearing these many words of Yudhishthra describing the state of affairs in details, out of compassion, Krishna spoke these words in reply to console the former.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: धर्मपुत्र विषाद् त्वं मा कृथाः सत्यसङ्गर। यस्य ते भ्रातरः शूरा दुर्जयाः शत्रुसूदनाः॥
en: O son of Dharma, do not indulge so much in grief, O you who are always firin in truth, you who have got, heroic and invincible warriors, all slayers of foes, in your brothers.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: अर्जुनो भीमसेनश्च वाय्वग्निसमतेजसौ। माद्रीपुत्रौ च विक्रान्तौ त्रिदशानामिवेश्वरौ॥
en: Arjuna and Bhimasena are both powerful like the Wind and the Fire respectively. The twin sons of Madri equal in prowess even the Lord of the celestial himself.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: मां वा नियुक्ष्व सौहार्दाद् योत्स्ये भीष्मेण पाण्डव। त्वत्प्रयुक्तो महाराज किं न कुर्यां महाहवे॥
en: Out of the friendship that exists between lis, employ me also (to perforin the task of slaying Bhishma). O son of Pandu, I will fight Bhishma. For you, O mighty monarch, what could I not do in battle.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: हनिष्यामि रणे भीष्ममाहूय पुरुषर्षभम्। पश्यतां धार्तराष्ट्राणां यदि नेच्छति फाल्गुनः॥
en: Summoning that foremost of men Bhishma in battle, I will slay him, even before the very eyes of the Dhritarashtra's troops, if indeed Arjuna desists from slaying the former.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: यदि भीष्मे हते वीरे जयं पश्यसि पाण्डव। हन्तासम्येकरथेनाद्य कुरुवृद्धं पितामहम्॥
en: If, O son of Pandu, by the slaughter of Bhishma you see victory certain to yourself, then even this day riding on a singie car, I will slay the venerable grandsire of the Kurss.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: पश्य मे विक्रमं राजन् महेन्द्रस्येव संयुगे। विमुञ्चन्त महास्त्रागि पातायष्यामि तं रथात ॥
en: Behold, O king, my rowess in battle, o be cqual to that of tl.. great Indra himself. I will overthrow nim (Bhishma) from lus car, in spite of his shooting mighty weapons.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: यः शत्रुः पाण्डुपुत्राणां मच्छत्रुः स न संशयः। मदर्था भवदीया ये ये मदीयास्तवैव ते॥
en: He that is inimical to the sons of Pandu, is surely inim.cal also to myself. Those that are friendly to you are also so to me and those that are friendly to me are also so to you

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: तव भ्राता मम सखा सम्बन्धी शिष्य एव च। मांसान्युत्कृत्य दास्यामि फाल्गुनार्थे महीपते॥
en: Your brother, Arjuna, is my friend, relative and pupil; O ruler of earth, I can cut off and give away my own flesh for Arjuna's sake.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: एष चापि नरव्याघ्रां मत्कृते जीवितं त्यजेत्। एष नः सपयस्तात तारयेम परस्परम्॥
en: This foremost of men also will lay down his own life for my sake. This O sire, is our understanding, that we will protect one another.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: स मां नियुक्ष्व राजेन्द्र यथा योद्धा भवाम्हम्। प्रतिज्ञातमुपप्लव्ये यत् तत् पार्थेन पूर्ततः॥ घातयिष्यामि गाङ्गेयमिति लोकस्य संनिधौ। परिरक्ष्यमिदं तावद् वचः पार्थस्य धीमतः॥
en: So, O most excellent king, command me so that I may fight for you. The vow that formerly Partha took at Upaplavya saying 'I will slay the son of Ganga' before the presence of all creatures, even that vow of intelligent Partha should be kept inviolate.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: अनुज्ञातं तु पार्थेन मया कार्यं न संशयः। अथवा फाल्गुनस्यैष भारः परिमितो रणे॥
en: But if the son of Pritha permits me, I will with certitude do it for him. As it seems to me the task of Phalguna is easy and it is not difficult for him to perform.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: स हनिष्यति संग्रामे ीष्म परपुरञ्जयम्। अशक्यमपि कुमुद्धि रणे पार्थः समुद्यतः॥
en: Arjuna will slay in battle, Bhishma that conqueror of hostile cities. Putting forth his energies in fight, Partha can achieve what is incapable of being achieved.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: त्रिदशान् वा समुधुक्तान् सहितान् दैत्यदानवैः। निहन्यादर्जुनः संख्ये किमु भीष्मं नराधिप।॥
en: Arjuna is capable of slaying in battle, O ruler of men, the very immortals along with the Daityas and Danavas, exerting their best in the fight, what to speak of Bhishma.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: विपरीतो महावीर्यो गतसत्त्वोऽल्पजीवनः। भीष्मः शान्तनवो नूनं कर्तव्यं नावबुध्यते॥
en: The highly puissani Bhishma the son of Shantanu, now perverted in his judgment, decayed in intelligence and in vitality surely knows not what he ought to do."

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच एवमेतन्महाबाहो यथा वदसि माधव। सर्वे होते न पर्याप्तास्तव वेगविधारणे॥
en: Yudhishthira said It is even so as you say, O mightv-armed descendant of Madhu's race. All these (universe) taken together are not capable of bearing your force.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: नियतं समवाप्स्यामि सर्वमेतद् यथेप्सितम्। यस्य मे पुरुषव्याघ्र भवान् पक्षे व्यवस्थितः॥
en: I am sure of obtaining all those things that I may desire, I, O foremost of men, on whose side you are staying.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: सेन्द्रानपि रणे देवाञ्जयेयं जयतां वर। त्वया नाथेन गोविन्द किमु भीष्मं महारथम्॥
en: O foremost of those that are ever victorious, with yourself as our master, we can conquer in battle, even the celestial with Indra at their head, what to speak of Bhishma that mighty car-warrior.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: न तु त्वामनृतुं कर्तुमुत्सहे स्वात्मगौरवात्। अयुध्यमानः साहाय्यं यथोक्तं कुरु माधव॥
en: For my own glorification, I dare not falsify your words; so do you render me assistance, O Madhava, as promised, without fighting on my behalf.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: समयस्तु कृतः कश्चिन्नमम भीष्मेण संयुगे। मन्त्रयिष्ये तवार्थाय न तु योत्स्ये कथञ्चन॥
en: Before this battle there was an understanding between me and Bhishma. He said 'I will give you good counsel, but will not fight for your interests.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: दुर्योधनार्थं योत्स्यामि सत्यमेतदिति प्रभो। स हि राज्यस्य मे दाता मन्त्रस्यैव च माधव॥
en: I shall fight for the interests of Duryodhana; this I speak to you, O lord, for certain.' Therefore, O you of Madhu's race, he may offer us salutary advice which will enable us to obtain the kingdom.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: तस्माद् देवव्रतं भूयो वधोपायार्थमात्मनः। भवता सहिताः सर्वे प्रयाम मधुसूदन॥
en: Therefore once more accompanied by you, Oslayer of Madhu, we shall repair to Bhishma for inquiring of him the means of his own death.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: तद् वयं सहिता गत्वा भीष्ममाशु नरोत्तमम्। नचिरात् सर्वे वार्ष्णेय मन्त्रं पृच्छाम कौरवम्॥
en: So, O descendant of the Vrishni race, repairing speedily with you to that foremost of men Bhishma, we shall seek counsel from that descendant of Kuru's race.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: स वक्ष्यति हितं वाक्यं सत्यमस्माञ्जनार्दन। यथा च वक्ष्यते कृष्णे तथा कर्ताऽस्मि संयुगे॥
en: He, O Janardana, will truly offer us salutary advice; and O Krishna, in battle we will do, what he shall advice.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: स नो जयस्य दाता स्यान्मन्त्रस्य च दृढव्रतः। बालाः पित्रा विहीनाश्च तेन संवर्धिता वयम्॥
en: O you of firm vows, he will give us counsel as well as victory. We became fatherless when we were mere children. It was he who reared us.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: तं चेत् पितामहं वृद्धं हन्तुमिच्छामि माधव। पितुः पितरमिष्टं च धिगस्तु क्षत्रजीविकाम्॥
en: O Madhava, even such an aged grandsire, I want to slay-him who is the father of our dearloved father! Fie on the life of a Kshatriya.”

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: संजय उवाच ततोऽब्रवीन्महाराज वार्ष्णेयः कुरुनन्दनम्। रोचते मे महाप्राज्ञ राजेन्द्र तव भाषितम्॥
en: Sanjaya said Thereupon, O mighty monarch, he of the Vrishni race, said to that delighter of the Kuru race, O highly wise king, your words find an echo in soul.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: देवव्रतः कृती भीष्मः प्रेक्षितेनापि निर्दहेत्। गम्यतां स वधोपायं प्रष्टुं सागरगासुतः॥
en: Devavrata of fierce Vows, is wellaccomplished in weapons. He can consume the foe even by his glances only. Let us go to that son of the ocean-going Ganga for asking the means of his death.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: वक्तुमर्हति सत्यं स त्वया पृष्टो विशेषतः। ते वयं तत्र गच्छामः प्रष्टुं कुरुपितामहम्॥
en: It behooves him to speak the truth, specially when questioned by you. Therefore let us go to the grandşire of the Kurus for asking him about the means of his death.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: गत्वा शान्तनवं वृद्ध मन्त्रं पृच्छाम भारत। स वो दास्यति मन्त्रं यं तेन योत्स्यामहे परान्॥
en: Repairing to that aged son of Shantanu, we shall seek counsel of him. And following the advice he will offer we shall fight with the enemy.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: एवमामत्र्य ते वीराः पाण्डवाः पाण्डुपूर्वजम्। जग्मुस्ते सहितः सर्वे वासुदेवश्च वीर्यवान्॥
en: Having thus consulted, the heroic Pandavas, together with the highly powerful son of Vasudeva, went, O elder brother of Pandu,

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: विमुक्तशस्त्रकवचा भीष्मस्य सदनं प्रति। प्रविश्य च तदा भीष्मं शिरोभिः प्रणिपेदिरे॥
en: Towards the tent of Bhishma, having previously cast off their armours and dresses. Then entering the tent, they all touched his feet with their hands.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: पूजयन्तो महाराज पाण्डवा भरतर्षभम्। प्रणम्य शिरसा चैनं भीष्मं शरणमभ्ययुः॥
en: Then, O mighty monarch, the Pandavas, saluting that foremost of the Bharatas with their bent heads, sought his protection.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: तानुवाच महाबाहुर्भीष्मः कुरुपितामहः। स्वागतं तव वार्ष्णेय स्वागतं ते धनंजय॥
en: Then the mighty-armed Bhishma the grandsire of the Kurus thus addressed them saying “All hail, O you of Vrishni's race, all hail, O Dhananjaya.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: स्वागतं धर्मपुत्राय भीमाय यमयोस्तथा। किं वा कार्यं करोम्यद्य युष्माकं प्रीतिवर्धनम्॥
en: Welcome to the son of Dharma and also to Bhima and the twins. What act enhancing your delight shall I do now?

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: सर्वात्मनापि कर्तास्मि यदपि स्यात् सुदुष्करम्। तथा ब्रुवाणं गाङ्गेयं प्रीतियुक्तं पुनः पुनः॥
en: I shall do it with all iny soul even if it be exceedingly difficult of being accomplished' When the son of Ganga had thus repeate addressed them with afflictio..

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: उवाच राजा दीनात्मा जीतियुक्तमिदं वचः। कथं जयेम सर्वज्ञ कथं राज्यं लभेमहि॥
en: King Y hishthira with a cheerful heart spoke these words to him affectionately. “O you who are acquainted with all these things, how shall we conquer and how shall we acquire our kirgdom?

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: प्रजानां संशयो न स्यात् कथं तन्मे वद प्रभो। भवान् हि नो वधोपायं ब्रवीतु स्वचमात्मनः॥
en: How may stop be put to this destruction of creatures? Say, O lord, all this to me. Tell us yoursell the means of your own death.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: भवन्तं समरे वीर विषहेम कथं वयम्। न हि ते सूक्ष्ममप्यस्ति रन्धं कुरुपितामह॥
en: How, O hero, shall we be competent enough to withstand you in battle? You do not disclose even the slightest weakness to your enemy, O grandsire of the Kurus, whereby to overthrow you.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: भरतर्षभ। मण्डलेनैव धनुषा दृश्यसे संयुगे सदा। आददार संदधानं विकर्षन्तं धनुर्न च॥
en: You are always seen in battle with your bow drawn to a circle. None can mark when you take up your shafts, place them in the bowstring or draw the string for shooting them.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: पश्यामस्त्वां महाबाहो रथे सूर्यमिवापरम्। रथाश्वनरनागानां हन्तारं परवीरहन्॥
en: O slayer of hostile heroes, slaying as you do, car-warriors, horsemen and elephant-riders, we behold you, O mighty-armed one, as a second sun on the chariot.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: कोऽथ वोत्सहते जेतुं त्व पुमान वर्षता शरवर्षा ग संयुगे बैशसं कृतम्॥
en: What person, O foremost of the Bharatas, dared variquish yi" this day, when showering a arrows downpour, you spread havoc among my troops.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: क्षयं नीता हि पृतना संयुगे महती मम। यथा युधि जो चां यथा राज्यं भृशं मम॥
en: My mighty army is every day being reduced by you in battle. How could we vanquish you in battle, hov. could sovereignty be ours?

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: मम सैन्यस्य च क्षेमं तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह। ततोऽब्रवीच्छान्तनवः पाण्डवान् पाण्डुपूर्वजः॥
en: How also could my troops he saved from this destruction? O grandsire, tell me the means for accompiishing all these ends." Thereupon, O elder brother of Pandu, the son of Shantanu said these words to the Pandavas.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: न क चन कौन्तेय मयि जीवति संयुगे। जयो भवति सर्वज्ञ सत्यमेतद् ब्रवीमि ते॥
en: “O son of Kunti, so long as I am alive, you will not be able to obtain victory, O you who know everything. This I tell you truly.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: निर्जिते मयि युद्धेन रणे जेष्यथ पाण्डवाः। क्षिप्रं मयि प्रहरध्वं यदीच्छथ रणे जयम्॥
en: When I shall be slain in battle, the Pandavas will surely win victory, in battle. Smite me down without delay, if you at all long to have victory in this war.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: अनुजानामि वः पार्थाः प्रहरध्वं यथासुखम्। एवं हि सुकृत मन्ये भवतां विदितो ह्यहम्॥ ते मयि हतं सर्वं तस्मादेवं विधीयताम्।
en: I permit you, O sons of Pritha, to strike me as you please. Indeed I consider it to be a favourable circumstance for you that you know me (to te invincible). When i shall be slaughtered, all eise will be slaughtered. So do as I tell you."

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच ब्रूहि तस्मादुपायं नो यथा युद्धे जयेमहि॥ भवन्तं समरे क्रुद्धं दण्डहस्तमिवान्तकम्।
en: Yudhishthira said Tell us the means by which we may be able to vanquish your enraged self in battle-you who resemble the vely god of Death himself wielding the mace.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: शक्यो वज्रधरो जेतुं वरुणोऽथ यमस्या॥ न भवान् समरे शक्य: सेन्ट्रैरपि सुरासुरैः।
en: We can vanquish the wielder the thunder-bolt, or Varuna, or Yama himself, but you are incapable of being defeated by the celestial and Asuras rnited together with Indra at their head.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: भीष्म उवाच सत्यमेतन्महाबाहो यथा वदसि पाण्डव॥ नाहं जेतुं रणे शक्य. सेन्ट्रैरपि सुरासुरैः। आत्तशस्त्रो रणे यत्तो गृहीतवरकार्मुकः ७६।।
en: Bhishma said O son of Pandu, O mighty-armed one, what you have said is indeed true. I am indeed incapable of being vanquished by the celestial and the Asuras united together with Indra at their head,

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: ततो मां न्यस्तशस्त्रं तु एते हन्युर्महारथाः। निक्षिप्तशस्त्रे पतिते विमुक्तकवचध्वजे॥
en: When with my weapons and my excellent bow in hard I engage myself in battle with care. But when I lay aside my weapons, even these mighiy car-warriors may slay me.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: द्रवमाणे च भीते च तवास्मीति च वादिनि' स्त्रियां स्त्रीनामधेये न विवले चैकपरिणे॥
en: One who lays his weapons aside, one who is fallen, one whose armour and standard have been shattered, one who flies away, one who is panic-struck, one who say “I am yours”

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: अप्रशते नरे चैव न युद्धं रोचते मम। इमं में शृणु रजेन्द्र संकल्पं पूर्वचिन्तितम्॥
en: One who is a female, one who bears a feminine designation, one who is disabled, one who has got only one son, and one who is a mean fellow, with these I do not like to fight.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: अमङ्गल्यध्वज दृष्ट्वा न युध्येयं कदाचन' य एप द्रौपदो राजंस्तव सैन्ये महारथः॥
en: Hear also, O foremost of kings, about the vow that I had formerly taken. Beholding any inauspicious sign I would under no circumstance fight.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: शिखण्डी समरामर्षी शूरश्च समितिञ्जयः। यथाभवञ्च स्त्री पूर्वं पश्चात् पुंस्त्वं ममागतः॥
en: That mighty car-warrior, O king, that son of Draupada, who belongs to your army, who is known under the name of Shikhandin, who is wrathful in battle, valiant and ever attended with victory,

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: जानन्ति च भवन्तोऽपि सर्वमेतद् यथातथम्। अर्जुनः समरे शूर पुरस्कृत्य शिखण्डिनम्॥
en: He was female before, but afterwards attained manhood. You all know truly how all this came to pass.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: मामेव विशिस्त्रैस्तीक्ष्णैरभिद्रया, दंशितः। अमङ्गल्यध्वजे तस्मिन् स्त्रीपूर्वं च विशेषतः॥
en: Let the heroic Arjuna clad in mail placing Shikhandin in front of him assail me with exceedingly sharp shafts

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: न प्रहर्तुमीप्सामि गृहीतेषुः कथइन। तदन्तरं समासाद्य पाण्डवो धनंजयः८४॥
en: Beholding them an inauspicious man in the person of him who was female before, I will not strike though I may be armed with arrows.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: शरैर्घातयतु क्षिप्रं समन्ताद् भरतर्षभ। न तं पश्यामि लोकेषु मां हन्याद् यः समुद्यतम्॥
en: Availing himself of that opportunity, let Pandu's son Dhananjaya quickly pierce me, O foremost of the Bharatas, on all sides.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: ऋते कृष्णान्महाभागात् पाण्डवाद् वा धनञ्जयात्। एष तस्मात् पुरोधाय कञ्चिदन्यं ममाग्रतः॥
en: Except the illustrious Krishna or Dhananjaya the son of Pandu, I do not find any one in the three worlds who can slay me in battle.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: आत्तशस्त्रो रणे यत्तो गृहीतवरकार्मुकः। मां पातयतु बीभत्सुरेवं तव जयो ध्रुवम्॥ एतत् कुरुष्व कौन्तेय यथोक्तं मम सुव्रत। संग्रामे धार्तराष्ट्रांश्च हन्याः सर्वान् समागतान्॥
en: Therefore let Vibhatsu armed with weapons and excreting in battle to the best of his abilities and wielding his excellent bow, overthrow me in battle, placing (this Shikhandin or) any one else before him. Thus victory will be yours with certainty. O foremost of kings, O you of chaste vows, do as I tell you. Then you shall be able to slay in battle all the Dhritarashtra assembled together.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: संजय उवाच तु ज्ञात्वा ततः पार्धा जग्मुः स्वशिबिरं प्रति। अभिवाद्य महत्मानं भीष्मं कुरुपितामहम्॥
en: Sanjaya said Then, the sons of Pritha, ascertaining all these things, went back to their own camps, having saluted the high-souled Bhishma the grandsire of the Kurus.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: तथोक्तवति गाङ्गेये परलोकाय दीक्षिते। अर्जुनो दुःखसंतप्तः सर्वीडमिदमब्रवीत्॥
en: When Ganga's son ready to repair to the regions of the departed, had thus spoken, Arjuna, afflicted with grief and with his face covered with blushes of shame, said :Arjuna said

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: गुरुणा कुरुवृद्धेन कृतप्रज्ञेन धीमता। पितामहेन संग्रामे कथं योद्धाऽस्मि माधव॥ ते
en: "How, O Madhava, shall I fight in battle, with the venerable and aged preceptor of the Kurus, the grandsire of accomplished understanding and intelligence.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: क्रीडता हि मया बाल्ये वासुदेव महामनाः । पांसुरूषितगात्रेण महात्मा परुषीकृतः॥
en: O Vasudeva, while playing in the days of childhood, I used to soil the garments of the high-souled and illustrious one by climbing on his lap with my body smeared with dust.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: यस्याहमधिरुह्याङ्कं बालः किल गदाग्रजा तातेत्यवोचं पितरं पितुः पाण्डोर्महात्मनः॥
en: O elder brother of Gada, in my childhood, climbing on the lap of the high-souled father of Pandu (our father), I used to say 'Father';

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: नाहं तातस्तव पितुस्तातोऽस्मि तव भारत। इति मामब्रवीद् बाल्ये य: स वध्यः कथं मया॥
en: I am not your father, but your father's father, O Bharata' even these were the words he used to say in reply to me. Oh he who used to treat me thus how could he be now slain by me!

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: कामं वध्यतु सैन्यं मे नाहं योत्स्ये महात्मना। जयो वाऽस्तु वधो वा मे कथं वा कृष्ण मन्यसे॥
en: Let him slay all my troops. I will not fight with that high-souled one, whether thereby I reap victory or death. What do you, O Krishna, think?

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: प्रतिज्ञाय वधं जिष्णो पुरा भीष्मस्य संयुगे। क्षत्रधर्मे स्थितः पार्थ कथं नैनं हनिष्यसि॥
en: O Vishnu, having promised to slay Bhishma in battle, how can you desist from slaying him without transgressing the duties of a Kshatriya?

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: वासुदेव उवाच पातयैनं रथात् पार्थ क्षत्रियं युद्धदुर्मदम्। नाहत्वा युधि गाङ्गेयं विजयस्ते भविष्यति॥
en: Vasudeva said Overthrow, O son of Pritha, this Kshatriya ever invincible in battle, from his car. Without slaying Ganga's son in battle you can not hope to win victory.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: दृष्टमेतत् पुरा देवैर्गमिष्यति यमक्षयम्। यद् दृष्टं हि पुरा पार्थ तत् तथा न तदन्यथा॥
en: It have been foredoomed, O Partha by the gods that Bhishma shall go to the abode of Death. That must come to pass which has been destined by the gods.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: न हि भीष्मं दुराधर्षं व्यात्ताननमिवान्तकम्। त्वदन्यः शक्नुयाद् योद्धमपि वज्रधरः स्वयम्॥
en: Except yourself, O invincible one, none including the wielder of the thunder bolt himself will be able to fight with Bhishma who resembles Death himself with wide open mouth.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: जहि भीष्मं स्थिरो भूत्वा शृणु चेदं वचो मम। यथोवाच पुरा शक्रं महाबुद्धिवृहस्पतिः॥
en: Do you slay Bhishma, with great coolness. Hear also these words of mine which were said to Shakra formerly by the highly intelligent Brihaspati.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: ज्यायांसमपि चेद् वृद्धं गुणैरपि समन्वितम्। आततायिनमायान्तं हन्याद् घातकमात्मनः॥
en: One ought to slay even an aged man, or a person who is older than himself, or one who may be endowed with all virtues, if he comes as an enemy, or indeed any one else who comes for destroying him.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: शाश्वतोऽयं स्थितो धर्मः क्षत्रियाणां धनंजय। योद्धव्यं रक्षितव्यं च यष्टव्यं चानसूयुभिः॥
en: This, O Dhananjaya, is the eternal duty prescribed for Kshatriyas viz., they should fight, protect their subjects, and perform sacrifices, all without any maliciousness.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: अर्जुन उवाच शिखण्डी निधनं कृष्ण भीष्मस्य भविता पम्। दृष्ट्वैव हि सदा भीष्मः पाञ्चाल्यं विनिवर्तते॥
en: Arjuna said Surely, O Krishna, Shikhandin has been born as the Death of Bhishma; for as soon as Bhishma sees the Panchala prince, he desists from striking.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: ते वयं प्रमुखे तस्य पुरस्कृत्य शिखण्डिनम्। गाङ्गेयं पातयिष्याम उपायेनेति मे मतिः॥
en: Therefore, placing Shikhandin in front of him (Bhishma) and stationing him in our van, we shall, by this means, overthrow the son of Ganga. This is my opinion.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: अहमन्यान् महेष्वासान् वारयिष्यामि सायकैः। शिखण्ड्यपि युधां श्रेष्ठं भीष्ममेवाभियोधयेत्॥
en: I will preclude the attack made by the great archers through arrows I shot on them. Shikhandi too should carry battle against Bhishma, the best warrior.

description: Consultation after the withdrawal of troops from the ninth day's fight
sn: श्रुतं हि कुरुमुख्यस्य नाहं हन्यां शिखण्डिनम्। कन्या ह्येषा पुरा भूत्वा पुरुषः समपद्यत॥ इत्येवं निश्चयं कृत्वा पाण्डवाः सहमाधवाः। अनुमान्य महात्मानं प्रययुर्हष्टमानसाः। शयनानि यथास्वानि भेजिरे पुरुषर्षभाः॥
en: I have heard that foremost of the Kurus viz., Bhishma say, 'I will never strike Shikhandin, in as much as formerly born as a daughter he attained manhood subsequently." Having formed this resolution the Pandavas with him of Madhu's race went back to their tents with cheerful hearts, and with the permission of the illustrious Bhishma.

description: Interchange of words between Bhishma and Shikhandin
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच कथं शिखण्डी गाङ्गेयमभ्यवर्तत संयुगे। पाण्डवांश्च कथं भीष्मस्तन्ममाचक्ष्व संजय॥
en: Dhritarashtra said How did Shikhandin proceed in battle against the son of Ganga? How also Bhishma advance against the Pandavas? Speak to me of all these, O Sanjaya.

description: Interchange of words between Bhishma and Shikhandin
sn: संजय उवाच ततस्ते पाण्डवाः सर्वे सूर्यस्योदयनं प्रति। ताड्यमानासु भेरीषु मृदङ्गेष्वानकेषु च।॥
en: Sanjaya said Then towards the hour of sunrise, all the Pandava warriors, with the sound of drums, cymbals and Anakas,

description: Interchange of words between Bhishma and Shikhandin
sn: ध्मायत्सु दधिवर्णेषु जलजेषु समन्ततः। शिखण्डिनं पुरस्कृत्य निर्याताः पाण्डवा युधि॥
en: And with the blare of conchs of the hue of curds, all around, placing Shikhandin at their van, marched forth in battle array.

description: Interchange of words between Bhishma and Shikhandin
sn: कृत्वा व्यूह महाराज सर्वशत्रुनिबर्हणम्। शिखण्डी सर्वसैन्यानामग्र आसीद् विशाम्पते॥
en: O mighty monarch, they disposed of their troops in an array capable if destroying all the foes; and O ruler of men, Shikhandin then occupied the van of all the troops.

description: Interchange of words between Bhishma and Shikhandin
sn: चक्ररक्षौ ततस्तस्य भीमसेनधनंजयौ। पृष्ठतो द्रौपदेयाश्च सौभद्रश्चैव वीर्यवान्॥
en: Then Bhimasena and Dhananjaya became the protectors of his car-wheels. Behind him were the sons of Draupadi and the highly puissant of Subhadra.

description: Interchange of words between Bhishma and Shikhandin
sn: सात्यकिश्चेकितानश्च तेषां गोप्ता महारथा धृष्टद्युम्नस्ततः पश्चात्यञ्चालैरभिरक्षितः॥
en: Then Satyaki and Chekitana, each a mighty car-warrior, became the protector of these last named. Behind them came Dhrishtadyumna protected by the Panchalas.

description: Interchange of words between Bhishma and Shikhandin
sn: ततो युधिष्ठिरो राजा यमाभ्यां सहितः प्रभुः। प्रययौ सिंहनादेन नादयन् भरतर्षभ॥
en: Then king Yudhishthira that mighty lord, with his twin brothers, Nakula and Sahadeva, proceeded to battle, O foremost of the Bharata, uttering his war-cries aloud.

description: Interchange of words between Bhishma and Shikhandin
sn: विराटस्तु ततः पश्चात् स्वेन सैन्येन संवृतः। दुपदश्च महाबाहो ततः पश्चादुपाद्रवत्॥
en: After him came Virata supported by his own divisions and then came, O mighty armed one, king Draupada.

description: Interchange of words between Bhishma and Shikhandin
sn: केकया भ्रातरः पञ्च धृष्टकेतुश्च वीर्यवान्। जघनं पालयामासुः पाण्डुसैन्यस्य भारत॥
en: The five Kaikeya brothers, and the highly powerful Dhrishtaketu, protected, O Bharata, the rear of the Pandava forces.

description: Interchange of words between Bhishma and Shikhandin
sn: एवं व्यूह्य महासैन्यं पाण्डवास्तव वाहिनीम्। अभ्यद्रवन्त संग्रामे त्यक्त्वा जीवितमात्मनः॥
en: Having thus disposed of their troops in battle-array, the Pandavas, all prepared to lay down their lives in battle, charged your divisions.

description: Interchange of words between Bhishma and Shikhandin
sn: तथैव कुरवी राजन् भीष्मं कृत्वा महारथम्। अग्रतः सर्वसैन्यानां प्रययुः पाण्डवान् प्रति॥
en: The Kauravas also, O king, placing at the van of all their troops the mighty car-warrior Bhishma, advanced against the Pandavas.

description: Interchange of words between Bhishma and Shikhandin
sn: पुत्रैस्तव दुराधर्षो रक्षितः सुमहाबलैः। ततो द्रोणो महेष्वासः पुत्रश्चास्य महाबलः॥
en: That invincible warrior Bhishma, was protected by your sons, all endued with great might. Next behind him came the mighty bowman Drona along with his highly puissant son Ashvathama.

description: Interchange of words between Bhishma and Shikhandin
sn: भगदत्तस्ततः पश्चाद् गजानीकेन सवृतः। कृपश्च कृतवर्मा च भगदत्तमनुव्रतौ॥
en: Next behind came Bhagadatta supported by a division of elephants. Kripa and Kritavarma followed Bhagadatta.

description: Interchange of words between Bhishma and Shikhandin
sn: काम्बोजराजो बलवांस्ततः पश्चात् सुदक्षिणः। मागधच जयत्सेनः सौबलश्च बृहद्बलः॥
en: After them came the powerful Sudakshina, the king of the Kambojas, Jayatsena of the Magadha kingdom, and the son of Subala, and Brihadbala.

description: Interchange of words between Bhishma and Shikhandin
sn: तथैवान्ये महेष्वासाः सुशर्मप्रमुखा नृपाः। जघनं पालयामासुस्तव सैन्यस्य भारत॥
en: Other mighty royal bowmen royal bowmen headed by Susharma protected, O Bharata, the rear of your troops.

description: Interchange of words between Bhishma and Shikhandin
sn: दिवसे दिवसे प्राप्ते भीष्मः शान्तनवो युधि। आसुरानकरोद् व्यूहान् पैशाचानथ राक्षसान्॥
en: Day after day Bhishma the son of Shantanu used to dispose of his troops in battle arrays such as Pisachas, Rakshasas, and Asuras.

description: Interchange of words between Bhishma and Shikhandin
sn: ततः प्रववृते युद्धं तव तेषां च भारत। अन्योन्य निजतां राजन् यमराष्ट्रविवर्धनम्॥
en: Then ensued a fight, as they slew on another, between your troops and theirs, that added considerably to the population of Death's domain.

description: Interchange of words between Bhishma and Shikhandin
sn: अर्जुनप्रमुखाः पार्थाः पुरस्कृत्य शिखण्डिनम्। भीष्मं युद्धेऽभ्यवर्तन्त किरन्तो विविधाञ्छरान्॥
en: The son of Pritha headed by Arjuna, placing Shikhandin in front of them, advanced towards Bhishma in battle, shooting arrows of various descriptions.

description: Interchange of words between Bhishma and Shikhandin
sn: तत्र भारत भीमेन ताडितास्तावकाः शरैः। रुधिरोधपरिक्लिन्ना: परलोकं ययुस्तदा॥
en: Then, O Bharata, your troops wounded with shafts shot by Bhima, exhausted with the loss of blood, repaired to the regions of the departed.

description: Interchange of words between Bhishma and Shikhandin
sn: नकुलः सहदेवश्च सात्यकिश्च महारथः। तव सैन्यं समासाद्य पीडयामासुरोजसा॥
en: Then Nakula, Sahadeva, and the mighty car-warrior Satyaki, all approaching your troops began to afflict them with force.

description: Interchange of words between Bhishma and Shikhandin
sn: ते वध्यमानाः समरे तावका भरतर्षभ। नाशक्नुतन् वारयितुं पाण्डवानां महद् वलम्॥
en: Thus, O foremost of the Bharatas, slaughtered in battle, your troops were unable to resist the mighty army of the Pandavas.

description: Interchange of words between Bhishma and Shikhandin
sn: ततस्तु तावकं सैन्यं वध्यमानं समन्ततः। सुसम्प्राप्तं दश दिशः काल्यमानं महारथैः॥
en: Then your troops, being thus slain, crushed and afflicted by the mighty car-warriors, fled in all directions.

description: Interchange of words between Bhishma and Shikhandin
sn: वातारं नाध्यगच्छन्त तावका भरतर्षभ। वध्यमानाः शितैर्बाणैः पाण्डवैः सहसृञ्जयैः॥
en: Being thus slaughtered, foremost of the Bharatas, by the Pandavas and the Srinjayas, with their sharp arrows your troops could not find a protector

description: Interchange of words between Bhishma and Shikhandin
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच पीड्यमानं बलं दृष्ट्वा पार्थैर्भीष्मः पराक्रमी। यदकार्षीद् रणे क्रुद्धस्तन्ममाचक्ष्व संजय॥
en: Dhritarashtra said Tell me, O Sanjaya, what did the mighty Bhishma wrought up with wrath do, when he saw my troops thus afflicted by the Partha's in battle?

description: Interchange of words between Bhishma and Shikhandin
sn: कथं वा पाण्डवान् युद्धे प्रत्युद्यातः परंतपः। विनिघ्ननं सोमकान् वीरस्तदाचक्ष्व ममानघ॥
en: Tell me also, O sinless one, how that afflicter of foes, that puissant hero comforted the Pandavas and slew the Somakas?

description: Interchange of words between Bhishma and Shikhandin
sn: संजय उवाच आचक्षे ते महाराज यदकार्षीत् पिता तव। पीडिते तव पुत्रस्य सैन्ये पाण्डवसुंजयैः॥
en: Sanjaya said I shall tell you, O monarch, what did your father do, when the troops of your sons were afflicted by the Pandavas and the Srinjayas.

description: Interchange of words between Bhishma and Shikhandin
sn: प्रहृष्टमनसः शूराः पाण्डवाः पाण्डुपूर्वज। अभ्यवर्तन्त निघ्नन्तस्तव पुत्रस्य वाहिनीम्॥
en: The heroic Pandavas, O elder brother of Pandu, with cheerful hearts, advanced slaying the forces of your son,

description: Interchange of words between Bhishma and Shikhandin
sn: तं विनाशं मनुष्येन्द्र गरवारणवाजिनाम्। नामृष्यत तदा भीष्मः सैन्यघातं रणे परैः॥
en: Then, O foremost of men, Bhishma did not tolerate that slaughter of men, elepnants and steeds, of your host, by the enemy.

description: Interchange of words between Bhishma and Shikhandin
sn: स पाण्डवान् महेष्वासः पञ्चामांश्चैव संजरा न्। नाराचैर्वत्सदन्तैश्च शितैरशलिकैस्तथा।॥ अभ्यवर्षत दुर्धर्षस्त्यक्त्वा जीवितमात्मनः। स पाण्डवानां प्रवरान् पञ्च राजन् महारथान्॥ आत्तशत्रो रणे यत्नाद् वारयामास सायकैः। गानाशस्त्रास्त्रवर्षेस्तान् वीर्यामर्षप्रवेरितैः॥
en: Then that fierce bowmen, that invincible hero, ready to lay down his life in battle, showered upon the Pandavas, the Panchalas and the Srinjayas, a downpour of sharp lances, and Vatsadantas and Anjalikas. Then, O king, wielding his weapons Bhishma with his shafts repulsed the five foremost and mighty carwarriors of the Pandava host who had been vigorously exerting theinselves in battle. He held them in check by showering on them many weapons both offensive and defensive, all sped with wrath and force.

description: Interchange of words between Bhishma and Shikhandin
sn: निजघ्ने समरे क्रुन्द्रो हस्त्यश्वं चामितं बहु। र६िनोऽयात बद् राजन् रथेभ्यः पुरुषर्षभः॥
en: Wrought up with rage, he slew in battle countless nuinber: of elephants and stecd:". then, O king, that foremost of me throv, ing many car-warriors from their cars,

description: Interchange of words between Bhishma and Shikhandin
sn: सादिनश्चाश्च पृष्ठे-य: । दातांश्च सम्पगतान्। गजारोहान् गजेभ्यश्च परेषां जयकारिणः॥
en: Many horse-soldiers from the back of horses, and also many foot-seldiers, and elephant-riders from the back of the elephants, inspired terror into the hearts of the foe.

description: Interchange of words between Bhishma and Shikhandin
sn: तमेकं समरे भीष्मं त्वरमाण महारथम्। पाण्डवाः समवर्तन्त वज्रहस्तमिवासुराः॥
en: Then like the Asuras assailing the wielder of the thunder bolt, the Pandavas assailed, in a body, that single-handed mighty car-warrior Bhishma who was moving swiftly up and down the field of battle.

description: Interchange of words between Bhishma and Shikhandin
sn: शक्राशनिसमस्पर्शान् विमुञ्चन् निशिताञ्छरान्। विश्वदृश्यत सर्वासु घोरं संधारयन् वपुः॥
en: Then Bhishma was seen in all directions, with a terrible form and shooting sharp arrows of which the touch was as fatal as that of Indra's thunder bolt.

description: Interchange of words between Bhishma and Shikhandin
sn: मण्डलीभूतवास्य नित्यं धनुरदृश्यत। संग्रामे युद्ध्यमानस्य शक्रचापोपमं महत्॥
en: As Bhishma fought on, his bow that resembled the mighty bow of Indra (Rainbow) was seen to remain continuously in a circular form.

description: Interchange of words between Bhishma and Shikhandin
sn: तद् दृष्ट्वा सम् कर्म पुत्रास्तव विशाम्पते। विस्म परमं गत्वा पितामहमजयन्॥ पार्था विमनसो भूत्वा पैक्षन पितरं तव॥
en: Then, O ruler of men, your sons beholding those mighty feats of Bhishma in battle, were amazed, and highly honoured the grandsire.

description: Interchange of words between Bhishma and Shikhandin
sn: युध्यमानं रणे शूरं विप्रचित्तिमिवामराः। न चैनं वारयामासुक्त्ताननमिवान्तकम्॥
en: Then like the immortals loO king, in the days of yore, at Viprachitti, the Partha's with depressed hearts began to look at your heroic father who was fighting fiercely;

description: Interchange of words between Bhishma and Shikhandin
sn: दशमेऽहनि सम्प्राप्ते रथानीकं शिखण्डिनः। अहदनिशितैर्बाणैः कृष्णवर्मेव काननम्॥ तं शिखण्डी त्रिभिर्बाणैरभ्यविध्यत् स्तनान्तरे। आशीविषमिव क्रुद्धं कालसृष्टमिवान्तकम्॥
en: And they were unable to resist him who then looked like Death's self with wide-open mouth. On the tenth day of the battle, Bhishma began to consume with his sharp arrows the car-host of Shikhandin like fire consuming a forest. Then Shikhandin with three arrows pierced Bhishma between his breasts,

description: Interchange of words between Bhishma and Shikhandin
sn: स तेना तभृशं विद्धः प्रेक्ष्य भीष्मः शिखाण्डनम्। अनिच्छन्निव संक्रुद्धः प्रहसन्निदमब्रवीत्॥
en: Bhishma-who then resembled an enraged snake of virulent venom or the Destroyer himself let loose by time. Thus sorely pierced by Shikhandin Bhishma loO king at him.

description: Interchange of words between Bhishma and Shikhandin
sn: काममभ्यस वा मा वा न त्वां योत्स्ये कथंचन। यैव हि त्वं कृता धात्रा सैव हिच शिखण्डिनी॥
en: And waxing wroth, as if unwillingly said these words with a smile "Whether you strike me (with arrows) or not, I will never fight with you;

description: Interchange of words between Bhishma and Shikhandin
sn: तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा शिखण्डी क्रोधमूर्छितः। उवाचैनं तथ पीष्मं सृक्किणी परिसंलिहन्॥
en: You are even now the same Shikhandin as the creator made you before. Hearing these words of his, Shikhandin overwhelmed with rage,

description: Interchange of words between Bhishma and Shikhandin
sn: जानामि त्वां मह बाहो क्षत्रियाणां क्षयंकर। मया श्रुतं च ते युद्धं जामदग्न्टे. वै सह॥
en: Said these words to Bhishma in battle licking at the same time the corners of his and mouth. “I know you, O mighty-armed hero, to be the destroyer of the Kshatriyas.

description: Interchange of words between Bhishma and Shikhandin
sn: दिव्यश्च ते प्रभावोऽयं मया च बहुशः श्रुतः। जानन्नपि प्रभावंते योत्स्येऽद्याहं त्वया सह॥
en: I have heard of the battle you fought with the son of Jamadagni; I have also heard of your divine prowess.

description: Interchange of words between Bhishma and Shikhandin
sn: पाण्डवानां प्रियं कुर्वन्नात्मनश्च नरोत्तम। अद्य त्वां योधयिष्यामि रणे पुरुषसत्तम॥
en: Knowing your prowess, I will still fight with you this day, desirous of doing a good turn to the Pandavas and to myself, O afflicter of foes.

description: Interchange of words between Bhishma and Shikhandin
sn: ध्रुवं च त्वां हनिष्यामि शपे सत्येन तेऽग्रतः। एतच्छुत्रा च मद्वाक्यं यत् कृत्यं तत् समाचर॥
en: O foremost of men, I will fight with you this day on the field of battle, and will, without doubt, slay you in battle. This I swear by my troth before you.

description: Interchange of words between Bhishma and Shikhandin
sn: काममभ्यस वा मा वा न मे जीवन् प्रमोक्ष्यसे। सुदृष्टः क्रियतां भीष्मं लोकोऽयं समितिंजय॥
en: Having heard these words of mine do what you think to be your duty. Whether you strike me or not, you shall not escape me alive this day. So, O ever-victorious Bhishma, let your eyes take a good view of this world, (as they will no longer see its charms).”

description: Interchange of words between Bhishma and Shikhandin
sn: संजय उवाच एवमुक्त्वा ततो भीष्मं पञ्चभिर्नतपर्वभिः। अविध्यत रणे भीष्मं प्रणुन्नं वाक्यसायकैः॥
en: Sanjaya said Having thus spoken, ne, with five shafts of depressed knots, pierced Bhishma in battle who had already been deeply pierced with the former's wordy arrow.

description: Interchange of words between Bhishma and Shikhandin
sn: तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा सव्यसाची महारथः। कालोऽयमिति संचिन्त्य शिखण्डिनमचोदयत्॥
en: Hearing those words of Shikhandin, the mighty car-warrior Savyasachi (Arjuna) thinking that was the right moment (to strike Bhishma) urged the former on saying

description: Interchange of words between Bhishma and Shikhandin
