sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच अभिद्रवध्वं युध्यध्वं भीष्मं जयत संयुगे। रक्षिताः सत्यसंधेन जिष्णुना रिपुजिष्णुना॥
en: Yudhishthira said Proceed, fight! conquer Bhishma in battle; you will be protected by Jishnu of unerring aim who is ever the conqueror of foes;

sn: अयं चापि महेष्वासः पार्षतो वाहिनीपतिः। भीमसेनश्च समरे पालयिष्यति वो ध्रुवम्॥
en: This fierce bowman the son of Prishata the commander of our hosts and Bhimasena also, will assuredly protect you all in battle.

sn: मा वो भीष्माद् भयं किञ्चिदस्त्वद्य युधि संजयाः। ध्रुवं भीष्मं विजेष्यामः पुरस्कृत्य शिखण्डिनम्॥
en: He Srinjayas, entertain no fear of Bhishma in battle today! Placing Shikhandin in our van we will assuredly conquer Bhishma in battle.”

sn: ते तथा समयं कृत्वा दशमेऽहनि पाण्डवाः। ब्रह्मलोकपरा भूत्वा संजग्मुः क्रोधमूर्छिताः॥
en: Sanjaya said Then on the tenth day, making all these arrangements, the Pandavas determined to conquer or to go to the regions of Brahma; and infuriate with rage, they encountered Bhishma.

sn: शिखण्डिनं पुरस्कृत्य पाण्डवं च धनंजयम्। भीष्मस्य पातने यत्नं परमं ते समास्थिताः॥
en: Placing Shikhandin and Dhananjaya the son of Pandu at their head, they struggled arduously to overthrown Bhishma.

sn: ततस्तव सुतादिष्टा नानाजनपदेश्वराः। द्रोणेन सहपुत्रेण सहसेना महाबलाः॥
en: Then numerous heroic rulers of various countries commanded by your son, accompanied by their sons, and by their own mighty divisions,

sn: दुःशासनश्च बलवान् सह सर्वैः सहोदरैः। भीष्मं समरमध्यस्थं पालयाञ्चक्रिरे तदा॥
en: As also your highly puissant son Dushasana supported by all his uterine brothers, then began to support Bhishma staying in the midst of the troops.

sn: ततस्तु तावकाः शूराः पुरस्कृत्य महाव्रतम्। शिखण्डिप्रमुखान् पार्थान् योधयन्ति स्म संयुगे॥
en: Then all your warriors placing before them Bhishma of regulated vows began to fight with the Partha's having Shikhandin at their van.

sn: चेदिभिस्तु सपञ्चालैः सहितो वानरध्वजः। ययौ शान्तनवं भीष्मं पुरस्कृत्य शिखण्डिनम्॥
en: Then that hero having the ape as the device on his standard, placing Shikhandin before him and accompanied by the Chedis and Panchalas, rushed against Bhishma the son of Shantanu.

sn: द्रोणपुत्रं शिनेर्नप्ता धृष्टकेतुस्तु पौरवम्। अभिमन्युः सहामात्यं दुर्योधनमयोधयत्॥
en: The grandson of Shini fought with Drona's son, Dhrishtaketu with the descendant of Puru and Yudhamanyu with king. Duryodhana and his ministers. son

sn: विराटस्तु सहानीकः सहसेनं जयद्रथम्। वृद्धक्षत्रस्य दायादमाससाद परंतप॥
en: Then, O afflicter of foes, Virata supported by his division confronted Jayadratha with his troops, that heir of Vridhakshatra.

sn: मद्रराजं महेष्वासं सहसैन्यं युधिष्ठिरः। भीमसेनोऽभिगुप्तस्तु नागानीकमुपाद्रवत्॥
en: Yudhishthira encountered the king of Madras supported by his soldiers. Bhimasena also, well protected, assaulted the elephant division of the enemy.

sn: अप्रधृष्यमनावार्यं सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वरम्। द्रौणिं प्रति ययौ यत्तः पाञ्चाल्यः सह सोदरैः॥
en: The prince of the Panchalas wrought up with rage and supported by his uterine brothers rushed against Drona's invincible, irresistible, and foremost of all wielders of weapons.

sn: कर्णिकारध्वजं चैव सिंहकेतुररिंदमः। प्रत्युज्जगाम सौभद्रं राजपुत्रो बृहद्बलः॥
en: That subduer of enemies, viz., prince Brihadbala, confronted Subhadra's son who bore the device of a lion on his standard and whose flag resembled a shaking Karnikara flower.

sn: शिखण्डिनं च पुत्रास्ते पाण्डवं च धनंजयम्। राजभिः समरे पार्थमभिपेतुर्जिघांसवः॥
en: Then your sons accompanied by other monarchs, fell upon Shikhandin and that son of Pandu namely Dhananjaya, desirous of slaying them both.

sn: तस्मिन्नतिमहाभीमे सेनयोर्क पराक्रमे। सम्प्रधावत्स्वनीकेषु मेदिनी समकम्पत।॥
en: Then when the fighters of the two hosts rushed impetuously against one another in thai terrible combat, the earth shook underneath their tread.

sn: तान्यनीकान्यनीकेषु समसज्जन्त भारत। तावकानां परेषां च दृष्ट्वा शान्तनवं रणे॥
en: Beholding Shantanu's son in battle, the divisions of your army and those of the enemy clashed against one another, O Bharata.

sn: ततस्तेषां प्रतप्तानामन्योन्यमभिधावताम्। प्रादुरासीन्महाशब्दो दिक्षु सर्वासु भारत।॥
en: Then when, infuriated, those two hosts rushed against one another, terrible was the din that filled all the different quarters of the earth, OBharata.

sn: शवदुन्दुभिघोषश्च वारणानां च बृहितैः। सिंहनादश्च सैन्यानां दारुणः समपद्यत॥
en: And the din become still more awful being aggravated by the blare of conchs and the sound of drums and the roars of elephants and the war-cries of the troops.

sn: स च सर्वनरेन्द्राणां चन्द्रार्कसदृशी प्रभा। वीराङ्गदकिरीटेषु निष्प्रभा समपद्यत॥
en: Then the radiance emitted from the bracelets and diadems of all the royal warriorsradiance resembling the splendour of the sun or the moon-become bedimmed.

sn: रजोमेघास्तु संजजुः शस्त्रविद्युद्भिरावृताः। धनुषां चापि निर्घोषो दारुणः समपद्यत॥
en: Clouds of dust were raised in which played the lighting consisting of the flashes of weapons. The twang of bows also became tremendous.

sn: बाणशङ्खप्रणादाश्च भेरीणां च महास्वनाः। स्थघोषश्च संजज्ञे सेनयोरुभयोरपि॥
en: The whizzing of arrows, the blare of conchs, the loud sound of the drums, and the clatter of cars of the warriors of both the hosts were indeed awful.

sn: प्रासख्यृष्टिसबैश्च बाणौघश्च समाकुलम्। निष्प्रकाशमिवाकाशं सेनयोः समपद्यत॥
en: The sky over the head of the two armies assumed a lowering aspect in consequence of the numerous dares, javelins, lances and arrows shot and hurled by them.

sn: अन्योन्यं रथिन: पेतुर्वाजिनश्च महाहवे। कुञ्जरान् कुञ्जरा जनुः पादातांश्च पदातयः॥
en: In that dreadful battle car-warriors and horsemen, smote down one another Elephants crushed elephants, and foot-soldiers slew footsoldiers.

sn: तत्रासीत् सुमहद् युद्धं कुरूणां पाण्डवैः सह। भीष्महेतोर्नरव्याघ्र श्येनयोरामिषे यथा।॥
en: Then, O foremost of men, like the fight between two hawks for a piece of meat, the fight, for the sake of Bhishma, between the Pandavas and the Kurus, become very awful.

sn: तेषां समागमो घोरो बभूव युधि संगतः। अन्योन्यस्य वधार्थाय जीगीषूणां महाहवे॥
en: Then dreadful was the encounter in that battle between those two armies, each desirous of slaughtering and gaining victory over its rival.

sn: संजय उवाच अभिमन्युर्महाराज तव पुत्रमयोधयत्। महत्या सेनया युक्तं भीष्महेतोः पराक्रमी॥
en: Sanjaya said Then for the sake of Bhishma's slaughter, the highly powerful Abhimanyu, o mighty monarch, engaged with your son supported by his large division.

sn: दुर्योधनो रणे कार्ष्णि नवभिनतपर्वभिः। आजघानोरसि क्रुद्धः पुनश्चैनं त्रिभिः शरैः॥
en: Thereupon king Duryodhana waxing worth, pierced Krishna's nephew, on the beast first with nine arrows of straight knots, and then again with three shafts.

sn: तस्य शक्तिं रणे कार्णिभृत्यो?रां स्वसामिव। प्रेषयामास संक्रुद्धो दुर्योधनरथं प्रति॥
en: Then in that battle, Krishna's nephew, inflamed with wrath, let go at the car of Duryodhana his lance that looked like the sister of Death himself.

sn: तामापतन्तीं सहसा घोररूपा विशाम्पते। द्विधा चिच्छेद ते पुत्रः क्षुरप्रेण महारथः॥ तां शक्तिं पतितां दृष्ट्वा कार्ष्णिः परमकोपनः। दुर्योधनं त्रिभिर्बाणैर्बाह्वोरुरसि चार्पयत्॥
en: arms O majesty! Your son Duryodhana splitted up in two pieces that pierce Sakti by throwing a Kshurapra in defence when that great chariot holder saw it suddenly approaching very fast towards him. When the son of Arjuna saw that Sakti so splitted, he filled with anger and gave hard blows on the chest and of Duryodhana.

sn: पुनश्चैनं शोरैराजघान स्तनान्तरे। दशभिर्भरतश्रेष्ठ भरतानां महारथः॥
en: Then the battle that raged between the two horses became awful and admirable to look at; and, O Bharata, it was gratifying to the senses and applauded by the rulers of earth.

sn: तद् युद्धमभवद् घोरं चित्ररूपं च भारत। इन्द्रियप्रीतिजननं सर्वपार्थिवपूजितम्॥ भीष्मस्य निधनार्थाय पार्थस्य विजयाय च।
en: The two heroes, viz., the son of Subhadra and the chief of the Kurus, fought fiercely with one another, the former for bringing about the slaughter of Bhishma and the latter for gaining victory over Arjuna.

sn: युयुधाते रणे वीरौ सौभद्रकुरुपुङ्गवौ॥ सात्यकिं रभसं युद्धे द्रौणिर्ब्राह्मणपुङ्गवः। आजघानोरसि क्रुद्धो नाराचेन परंतपः॥
en: Then that afflicter of foes, viz., Drona's son that foremost of Brahmanas encountering Satyaki in battle and waxing worth, pierced the latter on the breast with a long shaft.

sn: शैनेयोऽपि गुरोः पुत्रं सर्वमर्मसु भारत। अताडयदमेयात्मा नवभिः कङ्कवाजितैः॥
en: Then that grandson of Shini also possessed of generous heart, with nine shafts winged with Kanka feathers, pierced the preceptor's son, O Bharata, in all his vital parts.

sn: अश्वत्थामा तु समरे सात्यकि नवभिः शरैः। त्रिंशता च पुनस्तूर्णं बाह्वोरुरसि चार्पयत्॥
en: Thereupon Ashvathama pierced Satyaki in that battle, first with nine shafts, and next with thirty more on the breast and the arms.

sn: सोऽतिविद्धो महेष्वासो द्रोणपुत्रेण सात्वतः। द्रोणपुत्रं त्रिभिर्बाणैराजघान महायशाः॥
en: Then that illustrious descendant of the Satvata race that great bowman thus deeply pierced by the son of Drona struck the latter with three shafts in return.

sn: पौरवो धृष्टकेतुं च शरैराच्छाद्य संयुगे। बहुधा दारयांचने महेष्वासं महारथः॥
en: The mighty car-warrior, the descendant of the Kuru having covered that fierce, bowman, viz., Dhrishtaketu with his shafts, wounded the latter on many parts of his body.

sn: तथैव पौरवं युद्धे धृष्टकेतुर्महारथः। त्रिंशता निशितैर्बाणैर्विव्याधाशु महाभुजः॥
en: Similarly the mighty car-warrior Dhrishtketu endued with great might, pierced in that battle that descendant of Kuru with three hundred shafts of great sharpness.

sn: पौरवस्तु धनुश्छित्त्वा धृष्टकेतोर्महारथः। ननाद बलवन्नादं विव्याध च शितैः शरैः॥
en: Thereupon the descendant of Puru, that mighty car-warrior, having cut off the bow of Dhrishtaketu uttered a loud roar and pierced the latter with many sharp arrows.

sn: सोऽन्यत् कार्मुकमादाय पौरवं निशितैः शरैः। आजघान महाराज त्रिसप्तत्या शिलीमुखैः॥
en: The latter then taking up another bow, wounded, o king, that descendant of Kuru, with seventy three sharp shafts whetted on stone.

sn: तौ तु तत्र महेष्वासो महामात्रौ महारथौ। महता शरवर्षेण परस्परमविध्यताम्॥
en: Then those two fierce bowmen, both mighty car-warriors, and of gigantic proportions pierced each other with their thick arrows showers.

sn: अन्योन्यस्य धनुश्छित्त्वा हयान् हत्वा च भारत। विरथावसियुद्धाय समीयतुरमर्षणौ॥
en: Then, O Bharata, those two heroes waxed up with rage, having cut off one another's bow and slain one another's steeds, and being thus deprived of the use of their cars, rushed against one another for fighting with the sword.

sn: आर्षभे चर्मणी चित्रे शतचन्द्रपुरस्कृते। तारकाशतचित्रे च निस्त्रिंशौ सुमहाप्रभौ॥ प्रगृह्य विमलौ राजस्तावन्योमभिद्रुतौ। वासितासंगमे यत्तौ सिंहाविव महावने।॥
en: Then, O king taking up two resplendent shields, made of bull's hide, and embossed and decked with hundred beautiful stars and moons on the ground, as also taking up two swords of dazzling effulgence, those two warriors assailed one another, like two lions, in deep woods, both striving to consort with the same lioness in her season.

sn: मण्डलानि विचित्राणि गतप्रत्यागतानि च। चेरतुर्दर्शयन्तौ च प्रार्थयन्तौ परस्परम्॥
en: Longing to get near each other, they wheeled and inoved, displaying various charming circles and various forward and backward movements.

sn: पौरवो धृष्टकेतुं तु शङ्खदेशे महासिना। ताडयामास संक्रुद्धस्तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति चाब्रवीत्॥
en: Then the wrathful descendant of Puru, with his huge sword, struck Dhrishtaketu on the frontal bone, saying at the same time 'Stop, stop.'

sn: चेदिराजोऽपि समरे पौरवं पुरुषर्षभम्। आजघान शिताग्रेण जत्रुदेशे महासिना॥
en: The ruler of the Chedis also, with the sharp end of his mighty sword, wounded that descendant of Puru, that foremost of men, on his shoulder joint.

sn: तावन्योन्यं महाराज समासाद्य महाहवे। अन्योन्यवेगाभिहतौ निपेततुररिंदमौ॥ ततः स्वरथमारोप्य पौरवं तनयस्तव। जयत्सेनो रथेनाजावपोवाह रणाजिरात्॥
en: Then, O mighty monarch, those two subduers of foes, rushing against one another in that fierce combat, fell down, overthrown by one another's velocity. Thereupon your son Jayatsena taking up the descendant of Puru carried him away from the field of battle on his own vehicle.

sn: धृष्टकेतुं तु समरे माद्रीपुत्रः प्रतापवान्। अपोवाह रणे क्रुद्धः सहदेवः पराक्रमी॥ चित्रसेनः सुशर्माणं विद्ध्वा बहुभिरायसैः। पुनर्विव्याध तं षष्ट्या पुनश्च नवभिः शरैः॥
en: The highly powerful son of Madri, viz., Sahadeva, possessed of great prowess and heroism bore away Dhrishtaketu from the field on his own car. Chitrasena having pierced Susharma with many iron shafts, again pierced him with sixty and again with nine shafts.

sn: सुशर्मा तु रणे क्रुद्धस्तव पुत्रं विशाम्पते। दशभिर्दशभिश्चैव विव्याध निशितैः शरैः॥
en: Susharma also waxing worth in battle, O ruler of men, pierced your son with sets of ten sharp arrows each time.

sn: चित्रसेनश्च तं राजंस्त्रिंशता नतपर्वभिः। आजधान रणे क्रुद्धः स च तं प्रत्यविध्यत॥
en: He also pierced Chitrasena, O king, with nine shafts of depressed knot; then the latter inflamed with rage in battle pierced the former in return (with many shafts compassing the death).

sn: भीष्मस्य समरे राजन् यशो मानं च वर्धयन्। सौभद्रो राजपुत्रं तु बृहद्बलमयोधयत्॥
en: Then in that conflict for Bhishma 0 king, Subhadra's son, acquiring great fame and honour fought with prince Brihadbala,

sn: पार्थहेतोः पराक्रान्तो भीष्मस्यायोधनं प्रति। आर्जुनि कोसलैन्द्रस्तु विद्ध्वा पञ्चभिरायसैः॥
en: Displaying his prowess, for helping his father Arjuna then rushing at the car of Bhishma. Then the ruler of the Kosalas having pierced Arjuna's son with five dares made of iron,

sn: पुनर्विव्याध विंशत्या शरैः संनतपर्वभिः। सौभद्रः कोसलेन्द्रं तु विव्याधाष्टभिरायसैः॥
en: Once more pierced him with twenty shafts of straight knots. Then Subhadra's son pierced the ruler of the Kosalas with eight iron made dares.

sn: नाकम्पयत संग्रामे विव्याध च पुनः शरैः। कौसल्यस्य धनुश्चापि पुनश्चिच्छेद फाल्गुनिः॥ आजघान शरैश्चापि त्रिंशता कङ्कपत्रिभिः। सोऽन्यत् कार्मुकमादाय राजपुत्रो बृहद्बलः॥ फाल्गुनिं समरे क्रुद्धो विव्याध बहुभिः शरैः। तयोर्युद्धं समभवद् भीष्महेतोः परंतप॥ संरब्धयोर्महाराज समरे चित्रयोधिनोः। यथा देवासुरे युद्धे बलिवासवयोरभूत्॥
en: But he could not make the latter tremble in battle before him, and so again pierced him with many arrows. Then the son of Phalguna cut off the bow of the Kosala king once more; and he struck him with thirty shafts furnished with wings of the Kanka feather. Thereupon that prince Brihadbala taking up another bow, and waxing irascible, pierced with many an arrow the son of Phalguna. Indeed, O afflicter of enemies, the battle, that took place for the sake of Bhishma, between them both, O king, inflamed with anger and both well versed in all manner of warfare, was like that between Bali and Vasava in the days of yore on the occasion of the war between the celestial and the Asuras.

sn: भीमसेनो गजानीकं योधयन् बह्वशोभत। यथा शक्रो वज्रपाणिर्दारयन् पर्वतोत्तमान्॥
en: Bhimasena then fighting with the elephant division looked highly beautiful, like the wielder of the thunder bolt himself running upon the mountains.

sn: ते वध्यमाना भीमेन मातङ्गा गिरिसंनिभाः। निपेतुरुवा॒ सहिता नादयन्तो वसुन्धराम्॥
en: Those elephants, huge bodied like the hills, being thus slaughtered in battle fell down on the earth in large numbers, filling the earth with their roars.

sn: गिरिमात्रा हि ते नागा भिन्नाञ्जनचयोपमाः। विरेजुर्वसुधां प्राप्ता विकीर्णा इव पर्वताः॥
en: Those elephants prodigious like hills and resembling broken heaps of antimony appeared beautiful, as they lay prostrate, like so many mountains covering the earth's surface.

sn: युधिष्ठिरो महेष्वासो मद्रराजानमाहवे। महत्या सेनया गुप्तं पीडयामास संगतम्॥
en: Then king Yudhishthira that great bowman, protected by a mighty division encountering the Madra king in battle began to afflict him sorely.

sn: मद्रेश्वरश्च समरे धर्मपुत्रं महारथम्। पीडयामास संरब्धो भीष्महेतोः पराक्रमी॥
en: The highly powerful ruler of the Madras also, for the sake of rescuing Bhishma began to afflict that mighty car-warrior the son of Dharma in battle.

sn: विराटं सैन्धवो राजा विद्ध्वा संनतपर्वभिः। नवभिः सायकैस्तीक्ष्णैस्त्रिंशता पुनरार्पयत्॥
en: The king of the Sindhus having pierced Virata with nine shafts of straight knots once more pierced him with thirty shafts of keen edges.

sn: विराटश्च महाराज सैन्धवं वाहिनीपतिः। त्रिंशद्भिर्निशितैर्बाणैराजघान स्तनान्तरे॥ चित्रकार्मुकनिस्त्रिंशो चित्रवर्मायुधध्वजौ। रेजतुश्चित्ररूपौ तौ संग्रामे मत्स्यसैन्धवौ॥ द्रोणः पाञ्चालपुत्रेण समागम्य महारणे। महासमुदयं चक्रे शरैः संनतपर्वभिः॥ ततो द्रोणो महाराज पार्षतस्य महद् धनुः। छित्त्वा पञ्चाशतेषूणां पार्षतं समविध्यत॥ सोऽन्यत् कार्मुकमादाय पार्षतः परवीरहा। द्रोणस्य मिषतो युद्धे प्रेषयामास सायकान्॥
en: Then Virata also that leader of a division, O king, in return pierced the ruler of the Sindhus with thirty sharp arrows between his breast. Then those two kings of the Matsyas and the Sindhus, both of charming appearance and both furnished with beautiful armours, weapons and standards, and both wielding excellent bows and swords, appeared highly resplendent. Then Drona being engaged in that dreadful battle with the son of the Panchala king, fought on fiercely with arrows of close knots.

sn: ताज्छराज्छरघातेन चिच्छेद स महारथः। द्रोणो द्रुपदपुत्राय प्राहिणोत् पञ्च सायकान्॥ ततः क्रुद्धो महाराज पार्षतः परवीरहा। द्रोणाय चिक्षेप गदां यमदण्डोपमां रणे॥
en: Then Drona, O mighty monarch, having cut off the mighty bow of Prishata's son pierced latter with a set of five shafts. Then that slayer of hostile heroes namely Prishata's son, took up another bow, and then he hurled at Drona a terrible mace resembling the bludgeon of Death himself.

sn: तामापतन्ती सहसा हेमपट्टविभूषिताम्। शरैः पञ्चाशता द्रोणो वारयामास संयुगे॥ सा छिन्ना बहुधा राजन् द्रोणचापच्युतैः शरैः। चूर्णीकृता विशीर्यन्ती पपात वसुधातले॥ गदां विनिहतां दृष्ट्वा पार्षतः शत्रुतापनः। द्रोणाय शक्तिं चिक्षेप सर्वपारसवीं शुभाम्॥
en: Then Drona with fifty shafts, in that battle repulsed that mace decked with plates of gold as it flew swiftly towards himself. Then, O king, that mace cut into fragments by the arrows shot from Drona's bow, and splintered and shattered into pierces, fell down on the surface of the earth. Beholding his mace thus destroyed that afflicter of foes viz., the son of Prishata hurled at Drona his lance, excellent, and made of iron.

sn: तां द्रोणो नवभिर्बाणैश्चिच्छेद युधि भारत। पार्षतं च महेष्वासं पीडयामास संयुगे॥ एवमेतन्महायुद्धं द्रोणपार्षतयोरभूत्। भीष्मं प्रति महाराज घोररूपं भयानकम्॥ अर्जुन: प्राप्य गाङ्गेयं पीडयन् निशितैः शरैः। अभ्यद्रवत संयत्तो वने मत्तमिव द्विपम्॥ प्रत्युद्ययौ च तं राजा भगदत्तः प्रतापवान्। त्रिधा भिन्नेन नागेन मदान्धेन महाबलः॥ तमापतन्तं सहसा महेन्द्रगजसंनिभम्। परं यत्नं समास्थाय बीभत्सुः प्रत्यपद्यत॥
en: Drona, O Bharata, cut off that lance with nine arrows in the battle; and he then began to afflict the great bowman, viz., Prishata's son on battle. Then, O mighty monarch, for the sake of Bhishma, regard the fierce battle between Drona and Prishata's son, battle that was dreadful to the extreme and terrible in its aspects. Then Arjuna sighting the son of Ganga rushed at him discharging sharp arrows, like an infuriate elephant rushing in the woods at a compeer in the same state.

sn: ततो गजगतो राजा भगदत्तः प्रतापवान्। अर्जुनं शरवर्षेण वारयामास संयुगे॥ अर्जुनस्तु ततो नागमायान्तं रजतोपमैः। विमलैरायसैस्तीक्ष्णैरविध्यत महारणे॥
en: The highly puissant king Bhagadatta confronted Arjuna, and held the latter in check with a thick shower of arrows. Thereupon Arjuna pierced the elephant of Bhagadatta rushing towards himself in battle, with many keep pointed and iron made arrows, all bright as silver.

sn: शिखण्डिनं च कौन्तेयो याहियाहीत्यचोदयत्। भीष्मं प्रति महाराज जोनमिति चाब्रवीत्॥ प्राग्ज्योतिपस्ततो हित्वा पाण्डवं पाण्डुपूर्वज। प्रययौ त्वरितो राजन् दुपदस्य रथं प्रति॥ ततोऽर्जुनो पहाराज भीष्ममभ्यद्रवद् द्रुतम्। शिखण्डिन पुरस्कृत्य ततो युद्धमवर्तत॥ ततस्ते तावकाः शूराः पाण्डवं रभसं युधि। समभ्यधावन् क्रोशनतस्तदद्भुतमिवाभवत्॥ नानाविधान्यननीकानि पुत्राणां ते जनाधिप। अर्जुनो व्यधमत् काले दिवीवाम्राणि मारुतः॥
en: The son of Kunti, O king, urged on Shikhandin, saying “Advance, advance upon Bhishima and slay him.” Thereupon, O elder brother of Pandu the ruler of the Pragjyotishas abandoning Pandu's son in battle, rushed swiftly, o king, towards the chariot of Draupada. Thereat Arjuna, O mighty monarch, quickly advanced towards Bhishma, with Shikhandin in front of him, and then there raged a (dreadful) fight. Thereupon, in that battle your warriors, uttering fierce yells, rushed quickly at the son of Pandu. Then all this appeared marvelous. Then, O ruler of men, the army of your sons consisting of various divisions Arjuna began to scatter away like a strong gale scattering away clouds in the walk in.

sn: शिखण्डी तु समासाद्य भरतानां पितामहम्। इषुभिस्तूर्णमव्यग्रो बहुभिः स समाचिनोत्॥
en: Then Shikhandin confronting the grandsire of the Bharatas, pierced patiently the latter with myriad's of shafts.

sn: रथाग्यगारश्चापार्चिरसिशक्तिगदेन्धनः। शरसंघमहाज्वालः क्षत्रियान् समरेऽदहत्॥ यथाग्निः सुमहानिद्धः कक्षे चरति सानिलः। तथा जज्वाल भीष्मोऽपि दिव्यान्यस्त्राण्युदीरयन्॥
en: Then Bhishma began to consume the Kshatriyas in battle, like a fire, having his chariot for its fire-chambers, his bow for its flames, his swords, lances and maces for its fuel and his numerous shafts for its dreadful scintillation's. Just as a conflagration fed with a constant supply of fuel leaps from house to house being aided by a breeze, so also old displaying his weapons of celestial make.

sn: सोमकांश्च रणे भीष्मो जघ्ने पार्थपदानुगान्। न्यवारयत तत् सैन्यं पाण्डवस्य महारथः॥ सुवर्णपु?रिषुभिः शितैः संनतपर्वभिः। नादयन् स दिशो भीष्मः प्रदिशश्च महाहवे॥
en: Then that mighty car-warrior Bhishma, holding in check the division of the son of Pandu (Arjuna), slew those Somakas in battle who followed Partha, with arrows furnished with golden wings and of great sharpness and depressed knots; and he filled the points cardinal and subsidiary of the compass with the echoes of his war-cries.

sn: पातयन् रथिनो राजन् हयांश्च सहसादिभिः। मुण्डतालवनानीव चकार स रथव्रजान्॥ निर्मनुष्यान् रथान् राजन् गजानश्वांश्च संयुगे। चकार समरे भीष्मः सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वरः॥ तस्य ज्यातलनिर्घोषं विस्फूर्जितमिवाशनेः। निशम्य सर्वतो राजन् समकन्यन्त सैनिकाः॥ अमोघा न्यपतन् बाणाः पितुस्ते मनुजेश्वर। नासज्जन्त शरीरेषु भीष्मचापच्युताः शराः॥
en: He dislodged car-warriors from their cars, and felled, O king, horsemen with their chargers; he also made the mighty car-division look like Palmyra groves, with trees deprived of their leafy heads. Then Bhishma that foremost of all wielders of weapons deprived, 0 king, the cars, the chargers and the elephants, of their respective riders, in that battle. The troops then, O king, began to tremble, hearing the twang of his bow-string and the slap of his palms, that resembled the thunder itself. Indeed, O lord of men, the arrows of Bhishma did never fail to hit their marks. Shot from his bow, the arrows did not stick merely on the skin of warriors and animals.

sn: निर्मनुष्यान् रथान् राजन् सुयुक्चाञ्जवनैर्हयैः। वातायमानानद्राक्षं ह्रियमाणान् विशाम्पते॥
en: Then, O king, O ruler of men, we beheld cars deprived of their riders, dragged on all side, with the velocity of the wind by the fleet steeds that were yoked to them.

sn: चेदिकाशिकरूषाणां सहस्राणि चतुर्दशा महारथाः समाख्याताः कुलपुत्रास्तनुत्यजः॥ अपरावर्तिनः शूराः सुवर्णविकृतध्वजाः। संग्रामे भीष्मपासाद्य सवाजिरथकुञ्जराः॥ जग्मुस्ते परलोकाय व्यादितास्यमिवान्तकम्। न तत्रासीद् रणे राजन् सोमकानां महारथः॥
en: Full fourteen thousand high famed mighty car-warriors of illustrious extraction, ready to sacrifice their lives in battle, and unretreating and heroic, and owner of standards adorned with gold, all belonging to the race of the Chedis, the Kashis and Karushas, confronting the heroic Bhishma who them appeared like Death himself worth mouth wide open, were swiftly dispatched to the other world with all their cars, elephants and chargers. There was not a single mighty car-warrior, O king, among the Somakas,

sn: यः सम्प्राप्य रणे भीष्मं जीविते स्म मनो दधे। तांश्चं सर्वान् रणे योधान् प्रेतराजपुरं प्रति॥ नीतानमन्यन्त जना दृष्ट्वा भीष्मस्य विक्रमम्। न कश्चिदेनं समरे प्रत्युद्याति महारथः॥
en: Who having confronted Bhishma in that battle, was able to return alive from the engagement. Beholding all those warriors dispatched to the domain of the lord of the departed, people then thought high of Bhishma's prowess. No car-warrior then ventured to encounter that hero.

sn: ऋते पाण्डुसुतं वीरं श्वेताश्वं कृष्णसारथिम्। शिखण्डिनं च समरे पाञ्चाल्यममितौजसम्॥
en: Save and except that heroic son of Pandu, owning cream-coloured steeds, and having Krishna for his charioteer, and that prince of the Panchalas, Shikhandin of immeasurable energy.

sn: संजय उवाच शिखण्डी तु रणे भीष्ममासाद्य पुरुषर्षभम्। दशभिर्निशितैर्भल्लैराजघान स्तनान्तरे॥
en: Sanjaya said Then, O foremost of men, Shikhandin having encountered Bhishma in battle, pierced the latter on his breast with ten broad-headed shafts of great sharpness.

sn: शिखण्डिनं तु गाङ्गेयः क्रोधदीप्तेन चक्षुषा। सम्प्रेक्षत कटाक्षेण निर्दहन्निव भारत॥
en: Then the son of Ganga looked at Shikhandin with his eyes blazing in rage, and O Bharata, he seemed to burn the latter by his glance only.

sn: स्त्रीत्वं तस्य स्मरन् राजन् सर्वलोकस्य पश्यतः। नाजधान रणे भीष्मः स च तन्नाववुद्धवान्॥
en: But, O king, remembering his femininity, Bhishma did not wound him before the eyes of all in that battle. The latter however comprehended it not.

sn: अर्जुनस्तु महाराज शिखण्डिनमभाषत। अभिद्रवस्व त्वरितं जहि चैनं पितामहम्॥
en: Therefore, O monarch, Arjuna said to Shikhandin, “swiftly rush at the grandsire and slay him.

sn: किं ते विवक्षया वीर जहि भीष्मं महारथम्। न ह्यन्यमनुपश्यामि कञ्चिद् यौधिष्ठिरे बले॥
en: What is that you want to speak, O hero? Slay the mighty car-warrior Bhishma, I do not see a man in the whole army of Yudhishthira,

sn: यः शक्तः समरे भीष्मं प्रतियोद्भुमिहाहवे। ऋते त्वां पुरुषव्याघ्र सत्यमेतद् ब्रवीमि ते॥
en: Who is able to fight with Bhishma in battle, except yourself, O best of men? This I say to you forsooth."

sn: एवमुक्तस्तु पार्थेन शिखण्डी भरतर्षभ। शरैर्नानाविधैस्तूर्णं पितामहमवाकिरत्॥
en: Thus spoken to by Pritha's son, O foremost of the Bharatas, Shikhandin speedily covered the grandsire with arrows of various description;

sn: अचिन्तयित्वा तान् बाणान् पिता देवव्रतस्तव। अर्जुगं समरे क्रुद्धं वारयामास सायकैः॥
en: But disregarding those arrows, your sire Devavrata, wrought up with wrath engaged to fight with Arjuna by means of his shafts.

sn: तथैव च चमू सर्वां पाण्डवानां महारथः। अप्रैषीत् स शरैस्तीक्ष्णैः परलोकाय मारिष॥
en: That mighty car-warrior also dispatched the forces of the Pandavas to the other world, O sire, with his sharp-pointed shafts.

sn: तथैव पाण्डवा राजन् सैन्येन महता वृताः। भीष्मं संछादयामासुर्मेघा इव दिवाकरम्॥
en: On the other hand, O king, the sons of Pandu, supported by mighty divisions covered Bhishma over, like clouds covering the orb of the day.

sn: स समन्तात् परिवृतो भारतो भरतर्षभ। निर्ददाह रणे शूरान् वने वह्निरिव ज्वलन्॥
en: Then, O foremost of the Bharata, that chief of the Bharatas thus surrounded on all sides, began to consume those heroes in battle like a raging conflagration burning the woods.

sn: तत्राद्भुतमपश्याम तव पुत्रस्य पौरुषम्। अयोधयच्च यत् पार्थं जुगोप च पितामहम्॥
en: Then we beheld the wonderful prowess of your son as much as he simultaneously fought with Arjuna and protected the grandsire.

sn: कर्मणा तेन समरे तव पुत्रस्य धन्विनः। दुःशासनस्य तुतुषुः सर्वे लोका महात्मनः॥
en: Then all people were gratified with the feat achieved by your high-minded son Dushasana wielding his bow;

sn: यदेकः समरे पार्थान् सार्जुनान् समयोधयत्। न चैनं पाण्डवा युद्धे वारयामासुरुल्बणम्॥
en: For then he, single-handed, fought with the Pandavas including Arjuna himself; he then fought so fiercely that the Pandavas were unable to resist him.

sn: दुःशासनेन समरे रथिनो विरथीकृताः। सादिनश्च महेष्वासा हस्तिनश्च महाबलाः॥
en: In that battle car-warriors were deprived of their cars by Dushasana; mighty horse-men and highly powerful elephant-riders,

sn: विनिर्भिन्नाः शरैस्तीक्ष्णैनिपेतुर्वसुधातले। शरातुरास्तथैवान्ये दन्तियो विद्रुता दिशः॥
en: Mangled with his shafts, fell down on the surface of the earth. Huge-tusked elephants afflicted with arrow-wounds in all directions.

sn: यथाग्निरिन्धनं प्राप्य ज्वलेद् दीप्तार्चिरुल्बणम्। तथा जवाल पुत्रस्ते पाण्डुसेनां विनिर्दहन्॥
en: Just as fire fed with fuel fiercely blazes forth with terrible flames, so did your son consume the troops of the Pandavas.

sn: तं भारतमहामात्रं पाण्डवानां महारथः। जेतुं नोत्सहते कश्चिन्नाभ्युद्यातुं कथंचन॥ ऋते महेन्द्रतनयाच्छवेताश्वात् कृष्णसारथेः। स हि तं समरे राजन् निर्जित्य विजयोऽर्जुनः॥ भीष्ममेवाभिदुद्राव सर्वसैन्यस्य पश्यतः। विजितस्तव पुत्रोऽपि भीष्मबाहुव्यपाश्रयः॥
en: ran None of the heroic car-warriors of the Pandava host, O Bharata, was then able to vanquish, nay to encounter, that warrior of gigantic stature, except Arjuna the son of the great Indra, having white steeds and owning Krishna for his charioteer. Then, o king, the ever-victorious Arjuna defeating Dushasana in battle, rushed against Bhishma even before the very eyes of the people assembled there. Though vanquished, your son then depending greatly upon the strength of Bhishma's arms,

sn: पुनः पुनः समाश्वस्य प्रायुध्यत मदोत्कटः। अर्जुनस्तु रणे राजन् योधयन् संव्यराजत॥
en: Furiously fought with the Pandavas comforting his own troops at the same time. Arjuna also, O king, engaged in battle appeared very beautiful.

sn: शिखण्डी तु रणे राजन् विव्याधैव पितामहम्। शरैरशनिसंस्पर्शस्तथा सर्पविषोपमैः॥
en: Shikhandin also, O monarch, pierced the grandsire in battle with sharp arrows, of which the touch resembled that of the bolt of heaven and which were mortal like the virulent venom of snakes.

sn: न च स्म ते रुजं चक्रुः पितुस्तव जनेश्वर। स्मयमानस्तु गाड्नेयस्तान् बाणाञ्जगृहे तदा॥
en: These shafts, O ruler of men, did not cause any the slightest pain to your father, and then the son of Ganga received those arrows with a smile.

sn: उष्णातॊ हि नरो यद्वज्जलधाराः प्रतीच्छति। तथा जग्राह गाङ्गेयः शरधारा: शिखण्डिनः॥
en: Just as a man burning with thirst eagerly welcomes a shower of rain, so did also the son of Ganga receive the shower of arrows discharged by Shikhandin.

sn: तं क्षत्रिया महाराज ददृशुर्घोरमाहवे। भीष्मं दहन्तं सैन्यानि पाण्डवानां महात्मनाम्॥
en: Then, O mighty monarch, the Kshatriyas beheld Bhishma look terrible as he consumed the ranks of the high-souled Pandavas.

sn: ततोऽब्रवीत्तव सुतः सर्वसैन्यानि मारिष। अभिद्रवत संग्रामे फाल्गुनं सर्वतो रणे॥
en: Then your son commanded, O sire, all your troops saying. “Assail from all sides the heroic Phalguna.

sn: भीष्मो वः समरे सर्वान् पालयिष्यति धर्मवित्। ते भयं सुमहत् त्यक्त्वा पाण्डवान् प्रति युध्यत॥
en: The valiant Bhishma conversant with all duties will protect us in battle.” Then those troops of yours dismissing all fears fought on with the Pandavas.

sn: हेमतालेन महता भीष्मस्तिष्ठति पालयन्। सर्वेषां धार्तराष्ट्राणां समरे शर्म वर्म च॥
en: (Again did Duryodhana say) “Yonder is Bhishma, with his tall standard marked with the device of a golden palmyra, striving for saving the honour and armours of all the Dhritarashtra warriors.

sn: त्रिदशाऽपि समुधुक्ता नालं भीष्मं समासितुम्। किमु पार्था महात्मानं मर्त्यभूता महाबलाः॥
en: Even the celestial striving vigorously cannot overcome the mighty and high-souled Bhishma in battle, what to speak of the sons of Pritha who are mere mortals.

sn: तस्माद्रवत मा योधाः फाल्गुनं प्राप्य संयुगे। अहमद्य रणे यत्तो योधयिष्यामि पाण्डवम्॥
en: Therefore, O warriors, do you not run away getting Phalguna as an adversary in battle. I myself, putting forth my best energies, shall day battle against the Pandavas,

sn: सहितः सर्वतो यत्तैर्भवद्भिर्वसुधाधिपः। तच्छ्रुत्वा तु वचो राजंस्तव पुत्रस्य धन्विनः॥
en: United with all these rulers of earth, all exerting their best in battle.” Hearing those words of your son wielding the bow,

sn: सर्वे योधाः सुसंरब्धा बलवन्तो महाबलाः। ते विदेहाः कलिङ्गाश्च दासेरकगणाश्च ह॥
en: All the valiant and highly powerful warriors wrought up with rage, belonging to the clans of the Videhas, the Kalingas, the Daserakas, and many other tribes,

sn: अभिपेतुर्निषादाश्च सौवीराश्च महारणे। बाह्रीका दरदाश्चैव प्रतीच्योदीच्यमालवाः॥ अभीषाहाः शूरसेनाः शिवयोऽथ वसातयः। शाल्वाः शकास्त्रिगाश्च अम्बष्ठाः केकयैः सह॥
en: Fell upon Arjuna in battle. The Nishadas, the Souviras, the Balhika's, the Daradas, the Westerners, the Northerners and the Malavas, Abhishahs, the Shurasenas, the Shibis, the Vasatis, the Shalavas, the Shakas, the Trigartas, the Ambasthas with the Kaikeyas,

sn: अभिपेतू रणे पार्थं पतङ्गा इव पावकम्। शलभा इव राजेन्द्र पार्थमप्रतिमं रणे। एतान् सर्वान् सहानीकान् महाराज महारथान्॥ दिव्यान्यस्त्राणि संचिन्त्य प्रसंधाय धनंजयः। स तैरस्त्रैर्महावेगैर्ददाह सुमहाबलः॥ शरप्रतापैर्बीभत्सुः पतङ्गानिव पावकः। तस्य बाणसहस्राणि सृजतो दृढधन्विनः॥ दीप्यमानमिवाकाशे गाण्डीवं समदृश्यत।
en: Then rushed upon the son of Pritha like a flight of insects rushing at the flames of a fire. Then, O mighty monarch, that highly powerful hero Dhananjaya, always dreaded in battle, invO king celestial weapons, fixed them on his bowstring, and aiming them at those hundreds of enemy's divisions of car-warriors swiftly consumed them all, by means of those powerful dares of great velocity, like fire burning down a fight of insects. Then the bow Gandiva of that resolute bowman appeared resplendent as he shot myriad's upon myriad's of arrows from it.

sn: ते शरार्ता महाराज विप्रकीर्णमहाध्वजाः॥ नाभ्यवर्तन्त राजानः सहिता वानरध्वजम्। सध्वजा रथिन: पेतुर्हयारोहा हयैः सह॥ सगजाश्च गजारोहाः किरीटिशरताडिताः। ततोऽर्जुनभुजोत्सृष्टैरावृताऽऽसीद् वसुन्धरा॥ विद्रवद्भिश्च वहुधा बलैः राज्ञां समन्ततः। अथ पार्थो महाराज द्रावयित्वा वरुथिनीम्॥
en: Then, O mighty monarch, those Kaurava warriors with their tall standards splintered into pieces, ventured nor, even in a body, experienced against Arjuna owning the standard marked with the device of an ape. S011 Afflicted with shafts by the diadem-decked Arjuna, car-warriors fell with their standards, horse-riders with their horses and elephantriders with their elephants. Then the earth become soon covered with divisions of kings flying in all directions in consequence of the shafts shot by the arms of Arjuna. Then having completely crushed the enemy's ranks, the son of Pritha,

sn: दुःशासनाय सुबहून् प्रेषयामास सायकान्। ते तु भित्त्वा तव सुतं दुःशासनमयोमुखाः॥
en: Sped numerous shafts at your Dushasana. Those iron-tipped arrows, having pierced Dushasana.

sn: धरणी विविशुः सर्वे वल्मीकमिव पन्नगाः। हयांश्चास्य ततो जघ्ने सारथिं च न्यपातयत्॥
en: Penetrated the earth like so many snakes entering their holes in ant-bills. Then Arjuna slew the steeds and charioteer of the latter.

sn: विविंशतिं च विंशत्या विरथं कृतवान् प्रभुः। आजघान भृशं चैव पञ्चभिर्नतपर्वभिः॥
en: Then that valiant hero deprived Vivingshati of his car with twenty shafts and wounded the latter with shafts of straight knots.

sn: कृपं विकर्णं शल्यं च विद्ध्वा बहुभिरायसैः। चकार विरथांश्चैव कौन्तेयः श्वेतवाहनः॥
en: Then the son of Kunti, owning white steeds, having pierced Kripa, Vikarna, and Shalya with many iron arrows, deprived them of their cars.

sn: एवं ते विरथाः सर्वे कृपः शल्यश्च मारिष। दुःशासनो विकर्णश्च तथैव च विविंशतिः॥
en: Thus deprived of their chariots, O sire, Kripa, Shalya, Dushasana, Vikarma and Vivingshati,

sn: सम्प्राद्रवन्त समरे निर्जिताः सव्यसाचिना। पूर्वाह्ने भरतश्रेष्ठ पराजित्य महारथान्॥
en: All fled away from the field of battle being completely worsted by Savyasachin. Then, O foremost of the Bharatas, having vanquished the mighty car-warriors at the forenoon,

sn: प्रजज्वाल रणे पार्थो विधूम इव पावकः। तथैव शरवर्षेण भास्करो रश्मिवानिव॥
en: Partha then blazed forth in battle like fire without even one curl of smoke. He then, in consequence of his pouring arrows showers, looked like the sun scattering his myriad rays in all directions.

sn: अन्यानपि महाराज तापयामास पार्थिवान्। पराङ्मुखीकृत्य तथा शरवधर्महारथान्॥
en: He felled also, O mighty monarch, many rulers of the earth all mighty car-warriors, having compelled them to turn their faces away from the field of battle.

sn: प्रावर्तयत संग्रामे शोणितोदां महानदीम्। मध्येन कुरुसैन्यानां पाण्डवानां च भारत॥
en: Then, O Bharata, between the armies of the Kurus and the Pandavas, he crushed a mighty river of bloody current to flow.

sn: गजाश्च रथसङ्घाश्च बहुधा रथिभिर्हताः। स्थाश्च निहता नागैर्हयाश्चैव पदातिभिः॥
en: Large bodies of elephants, steeds and carwarriors were slain by car-warriors; and many were the car-warriors slain by elephants and many the horse-men slain by foot-soldiers.

sn: अन्तराच्छिद्यमानानि शरीराणि शिरांसि च। निपेतुर्दिक्षु सर्वासु गजाश्वरथयोधिनाम्॥
en: In all directions then fell many heads and bodies cut in the middle, of car-warriors, horsemen and elephant-riders.

sn: छन्नमायोधनं राजन् कुण्डलाङ्गदधारिभिः। पतितैः पात्यमानैश्च राजपुत्रैर्महारथैः॥
en: The field of battle, O king, became strewn with fallen and falling bodies of many royal car-warriors even then decked with bracelets and graced with ear-rings.

sn: रथनेमिनिकृत्तैश्च गजैश्चैवावपोथितैः। पादाताश्चाप्यधावन्त साश्वाश्च हययोधिनः॥
en: The field was also covered over with many bodies mangled by car-wheels and trampled upon by by elephants. Foot-soldiers, and horsemen with their chargers fled away in all directions.

sn: गजाश्च रथयोधाश्च परिपेतुः समन्ततः। विकीर्णाश्च रथा भूमौ भग्नचक्रयुगध्वजाः॥ तद् गजाश्वरथौघानां रुधिरेण समुक्षितम्। छन्नमायोधनं रेजे रक्ताभ्रमिव शारदम्॥
en: Elephants and car-warriors left in all directions. Many were the gore of elephants, horses and car-warriors, appeared beautiful like the autumnal sky covered with specks of red cloud.

sn: श्वानः काकाश्च गृध्राश्च वृका गोमायुभिः सह। प्रणेदुर्भक्ष्यमासाद्य विकृताश्च मृगद्विजाः॥
en: Dogs, crows, vultures, wolves, and jackels and other beasts set up loud yields, at the sight of food that was then before them.

sn: बवुर्बहुविधाश्चैव दिक्षु सर्वासु मारुताः। दृश्यमानेषु रक्षःसु भूतेषु च नदत्सु च॥
en: Then, when Rakshasas and evil spirits were seen to roar there, various kinds of winds began to blow in all directions.

sn: काञ्चनानि च दामानि पताकाश्च महाधनाः। धूयमाना व्यदृश्यन्त सहसा मारुतेरिताः॥
en: Strings of gold and precious standards were seen suddenly to be fluttered by the wind, and began to tremble,

sn: श्वेतच्छत्रसहस्राणि सध्वजाश्च महारथाः। विकीर्णाः समदृश्यन्त शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः॥
en: Thousands of white umbrellas and many mighty car-warriors with their standards, were seen strewn on the surface of the earth.

sn: सपताकाश्च मातङ्गा दिशो जग्मुः शरातुराः। क्षत्रियाश्च मनुष्येन्द्र गदाशक्तिधनुर्धराः॥ समन्ततश्च दृश्यन्ते पतिता धरणीतले।
en: Many huge elephants with the flags unfurled on their back started running in all the four directions because of severe pain caused to them by hard blows of arrows. O king! A number of Kshatriyas with gada, sakti and bows in their hands were seen fell down on the earth everywhere.

sn: ततो भीष्मो महाराज दिव्यमस्त्रमुदीरयन्॥ अभ्यधावत कौन्तेयं मिषतां सर्वधन्विनाम्।
en: Thereupon, O mighty monarch, Bhishma having invoked into existence a celestial weapon rushed at the son of Kunti even before the very eyes of all bowmen.

sn: तं शिखण्डी रणे यान्तमभ्यद्रवत दंशितः॥ ततः समाहरद् भीष्मस्तदस्त्रं पावकोपमम्।
en: Then clad in mail Shikhandin confronted him rushing in battle. Whereupon Bhishma withdrew that dare resembling fire itself.

sn: त्वरितः पाण्डवो राजन् मध्यमः श्वेतवाहनः। निजघ्ने तावकं सैन्यं मोहयित्वा पितामहम्॥
en: Meanwhile Kunti's son owning white steeds having confounded the grandsire began to slaughter your forces.

sn: संजय उवाच समं व्यूढेष्वनीकेषु भूयिष्ठेष्वनिवर्तिनः। ब्रह्मलोकपराः सर्वे समपद्यन्त भारत॥ न ह्यनीकमनीकेन समसज्जत संकुले। रथा न रथिभिः सार्ध पादाता न पदातिभिः॥
en: Sanjaya said When the division of the two armies strong in numbers and arranged in order of battle, met one another, all the unretreating heroes, O Bharata, then rushed to battle keeping in view the regions of Brahma. In that pell-mell fight, neither similar divisions fought with their similar, not car-warriors with car-warriors, nor foot-soldier with their foot-soldiers.

sn: अश्वा नाश्वैरयुध्यन्त गजा न गजयोधिभिः। उन्मत्तवन्महाराज युध्यन्ते तत्र भारत॥ महान् व्यतिकरो रौद्रः सेनयोः समपद्यता नरनागगणेष्वेव विकीर्णेषु च सर्वशः॥
en: Horsemen then fought not with horsemen and elephant-riders fought not with other elephant-riders. But like men seized with fury, O Bharata, they indiscriminately slaughtered men one another, O monarch, in that battle. Fierce and great was the carnage that then spread itself among the ranks of the two armies, as and elephants, by hundreds, were scattered slain in all directions.

sn: क्षये तस्मिन् महारौद्रे निर्विशेषमजायत। ततः शल्यः कृपश्चैव चित्रसेनश्च भारत॥ दुःशासनो विकर्णश्च रथानास्थाय भास्वरान्। पाण्डवानां रणे शूरा ध्वजिनीं समकम्पयन्॥
en: In that fierce battle the slaughter was indiscriminate. Then, 0 Bharata, Shalya, Kripa, Chitrasena, Dushasana and Vikarna, all riding on resplendent chariots, and all mighty heroes, made the host of the Pandavas tremble in battle before them.

sn: सा वध्यमाना समरे पाण्डुसेना महात्मभिः। भ्राम्यते बहुधा राजन् मारुतेनेव नौर्जले॥
en: The army of the Pandavas thus slaughtered by those high-souled warriors, was caused to wheels in various motions, like a bark tossed by the wind on the waters (of the sea).

sn: यता हि शैशिरः कालो गवां मर्माणि कृन्तति। तथा पाण्डुसुतानां वै भीष्मो मर्माणि कृन्तति॥ तथैव तव सैन्यस्य पार्थेन च महात्मना। नवमेघप्रतीकाशा: पातिता बहुधा गजाः॥
en: Just as bleak wintry cold penetrates into the very vitals of the kine, so did then Bhishma cut the army of the sons of the Pandu to the very quick. Then many elephants of your army loO king like newly formed clouds, were felled by the high-souled son of Pritha in that battle.

sn: मृद्यमानाश्च दृश्यन्ते पार्थेन नरयूथपाः। इषुभिस्ताङ्यमानाश्च नाराचैश्च सहस्रशः॥
en: The leaders of hosts of combatants were then seen to be crushed and mangled by the son of Pritha with his arrows and lances shot by thousands.

sn: पेतुरार्तस्वरं घोरं कृत्वा तत्र महागजाः। आनद्धाभरणैः कार्येनिहतानां महात्मनाम्॥ छन्नमायोधनं रेजे शिरोभिश्च सकुण्डलैः। तस्मिन्नेव महाराज महावीरवरक्षये॥
en: over Mighty elephants fell there setting up loud yells of agony and distress. The field of battle then looked beautiful being strewn withthe ornament-decked bodies of slain warriors of high soul, as also with their heads glanced with ear-rings. In that conflict, O monarch, so destructive of mighty heroes,

sn: भीष्मे च युधि विक्रान्ते पाण्डवे च धनंजये। ते पराक्रान्तमालोक्य राजन् युधि पितामहम्॥ अभ्यवर्तन्त ते पुत्राः सर्वे सैन्यपुरस्कृताः। इच्छन्तो निधनं युद्धे स्वर्गं कृत्वा परायणम्॥
en: When both Bhishma and Dhananjaya the son of Pandu were displaying their prowess, your sons beholding the grandsire strive vigorously in battle. O king, rushed at the head all of their troops. Desirous of death in battle, and loO king upon heaven as their final goal.

sn: पाण्डवानभ्यवर्तन्त तस्मिन् वीरवरक्षये। पाण्डवाऽपि महाराज स्मरन्तो विविधान् बहून्॥
en: They rushed against the Pandavas in that battle destructive of many heroes. The Pandavas also, O monarch, remembering the diverse woes and hardships.

sn: क्लेशान् कृतान् सपुत्रेण त्वया पूर्वं नराधिप। भय त्यक्त्वा रणे शूरा ब्रह्मलोकाय तत्पराः॥
en: Inflicted, O ruler of men, on them by you and your son and dismissing all fears, and desirous of attaining to the regions of Brahma,

sn: तावकांस्तव पुत्रांश्च योधयन्ति प्रहृष्टवत्। सेनापतिस्तु समरे प्राह सेनां महारथः॥
en: Cheerfully fought on with your troops and your sons. Then that mighty car-warrior the commander of the Pandava host addressing his troops said.

sn: अभिद्रवत गाङ्गेयं सोमकाः सृञ्जयैः सह। सेनापतिवचः श्रुत्वा समोकाः सृञ्जयाश्च ते॥
en: "Rush you, O Somakas, together with the Srinjayas at the son of Ganga.” Hearing those words of their commander-in-chief, the Somakas and the Srinjayas,

sn: अभ्यद्रवन्त गाङ्गेयं शरवृष्ट्या समाहताः। वध्यमानस्ततो राजन् पिता शान्तनवस्तव॥
en: Through afflicted with showers of arrows rushed at the son of Ganga. Thus assailed, O king, your father, the son of Shantanu,

sn: अमर्षवशमापन्नो योधयामास सृञ्जयान्। तस्य कीर्तिमतस्तात पुरा रामेण धीमता॥
en: Influenced by wrath fought with the Srinjayas. To your highly renowned father. O sire, in the days of yore, the intelligent Rama,

sn: सम्प्रदत्तास्त्रशिक्षा वै परानीकविनाशनी। स ता शिक्षामधिष्ठाय कुर्वन् परबलक्षयम्॥
en: Imparted a lesson in the use of weapons that were capable of destroying the hostile ranks. Depending upon that instruction of his and thinning the ranks of the enemy,

sn: अहन्यहनि पार्थानां वृद्धः कुरुपितामहः। भीष्मो दश सहस्राणि जघान परवीरहा।॥
en: The old grandsire of the Kurus, viz., Bhishma that slayer of hostile heroes day after day slaughtered ten thousand warriors belonging to the Pandava host.

sn: तस्मिंस्तु दशमे प्राप्ते दिवसे भरतर्षभ। भीष्मेणैकेन मत्स्येषु पञ्चालेषु च संयुगे॥
en: One that the tenth day of the battle, O foremost of the Bharatas, from among the Matsyas and the Panchalas, Bhishma, single handed,

sn: गजाश्वमिमितं हत्वा हताः सप्त महारथाः। हत्वा पञ्च सहस्राणि रथानां प्रपितामहः॥
en: Having slain ten thousand elephants, slew also seven mighty car-warriors. Then the great grandsire also five thousand car-warriors.

sn: नराणां च महायुद्धे सहस्राणि चतुर्दशः। दन्तिनां च सहस्राणि हयानामयुतं पुनः॥
en: In that fierce battle in addition to all this, fourteen thousand foot-soldiers, one thousand elephants, and ten thousand steeds.

sn: शिक्षाबलेन नहितं पित्रा तव विशाम्पते। ततः सर्वमहीपनां क्षपयित्वा वरूथिनीम्॥
en: Were slain, O ruler of men, by your father through his superior education.

sn: विराटस्य प्रियो भ्राता शतानीको निपातितः। शतानीकं च समरे हत्वा भीष्मः प्रतापवान्॥
en: Then reducing in number all the divisions led by rulers of earth, Bhishma slew Shatanika the dear-loved brother of Virata. Having slain Shatanika in battle, the valiant Bhishma.

sn: सहस्राणि महाराज राज्ञा भल्लैरपातयत्। उद्विग्नाः समरे योधा विक्रोशन्ति धनंजयम्॥
en: Felled thousand royal warriors with broadheaded shafts. All those Kshatriyas of the Pandava host, that followed Dhananjaya,

sn: ये च केचन पार्थानामभियाता धनंजयम्। राजानो भीष्ममासाद्य गतास्ते यमसादनम्॥ एवं दश दिशो भीष्मः शरजालैः समन्ततः। अतीत्य सेनां पार्थानामवतस्थे चमूमुखे॥
en: Approaching Bhishma, were dispatched to the abode of Death. Thus covering the ten points of the compass with the net-work of his arrows, as also the army of the Partha's, Bhishma remained the master of the situation.

sn: स कृत्वा सुमहत् कर्म तस्मिन् वै दशमेऽहनि। सेनयोरन्तरे तिष्ठन् प्रगृहीतशरासनः॥ न चैनं पार्थिवाः केचिच्छक्ता राजन् निरीक्षितुम्।
en: On that the tenth day of the battle, achieving marvelous feats, Bhishma stayed between the two arinies, holding his bow and arrows in his hands. O king, then none of the royal warriors were able to look at him,

sn: मध्यं प्राप्तं यथा ग्रीष्मे तपन्तं भास्करं दिवि॥ यथा दैत्यचमूं शक्तस्तापयामास संयुगे।
en: Who then resembled the summer sun scorching the world from the meridian. Just as in the days of yore, Shakra afflicted the hosts of the Daityas,

sn: तथा भीष्मः पाण्डवेयास्तापयामास भारत॥ तथा चैनं पराक्रान्तमालोक्य मधुसूदनः।
en: So did, O Bharata, Bhishma then afflict the ranks of the Pandavas. Then beholding Bhishma thus display his prowess in battle, the slayer of Madhu,

sn: उवाच देवकीपुत्रः प्रीयमाणो धनंजयम्॥ एष शान्तनवो भीष्मः सेनयोरन्तरे स्थितः।
en: That son of Devaki, joyfully addressed Dhananjaya saying. “Yonder is Bhishma, the son of Shantanu staying between the two armies.

sn: संनिहत्य बलादेन विजयस्ते भविष्यति॥ बलात् संस्तम्भयस्वैनं यत्रैषा भिद्यते चमूः।
en: Slay him by putting forth your prowess, and victory will be yours. Check him through your prowess even there where he is penetrating our ranks.

sn: न हि भीष्मशरानन्यः सोढुमुत्सहते विभो॥ ततस्तस्मिन् क्षणे राजंश्चोदितो वानरध्वजः।
en: None among us, O lord, is capable of bearing the shafts of Bhishma save and except your mighty self."

sn: सध्वजं सरथं साश्वं भीष्ममन्तर्दधे शरैः॥ स चापि कुरुमुख्यानमृषभः पाण्डवेरितान्।। शरव्रातैः शरव्रातान् बहुधा विदुधाव तान्॥ ततः पञ्चालराजश्च धृष्टकेतुश्च वीर्यवान्।
en: Then, O king, thus urged on, Dhananjaya owning a standard bearing the device of an ape, rendered Bhishma with his standard, chariots and horses, invisible by his shafts. Then that foremost of the Kuru chiefs (Bhishma) also, with the shower of his own arrows scattered the arrows discharged by that son of Pandu. Thereupon the king of the Panchalas, and the valiant Dhrishtaketu.

sn: पाण्डवो भीमसेनश्च धृष्टद्युम्नश्च पार्षतः॥ यमौ च चेकितानश्च केकया: पञ्च चैव ह।
en: Pandu's son Bhimasena, Prishata's son Dhrishtadyumna, the twins Nakula and Sahadeva, Chekitana, the five Kaikeya brothers,

sn: सात्यकिश्च महाबाहुः सौभद्रोऽथ घटोत्कचः॥ द्रौपदेयाः शिखण्डी च कुन्तिभोजश्च वीर्यवान्। सुशर्मा च विराटश्च पाण्डवेया महाबलाः॥ एते चान्ये च बहवः पीडिता भीष्मसायकैः।
en: The mighty-armed Satyaki, the son of Subhadra, Ghatotkacha, the sons of Draupada, down pour Shikhandin, the highly powerful Kuntibhoja, Susharma, and Virata, these and many other mighty heroes of the Pandava host were then afflicted by the shafts of Bhishma.

sn: समुद्धृताः फाल्गुनेन निमग्नाः शोकसागरे॥ ततः शिखण्डी वेगेन प्रगृह्य परमायुधम्। भीष्ममेवाभिदुद्राव रक्ष्यमाणः किरीटिना॥
en: Then from the ocean of grief in which they were sunk, they were rescued by Phalguna. Thereupon grasping an excellent weapon Shikhandin. Assailed Bhishma, being protected by the diadem-decked Arjuna.

sn: ततोऽस्यानुचरान् हत्वा सर्वान् रणविभागवित्। भीष्ममेवाभिदुद्राव बीभत्सुम्पराजितः॥ सात्यकिश्चेकितानश्च धृष्टद्युम्नश्च पार्षतः।
en: Then slaying all the followers of Bhishma, and knowing what should be done in battle after what, the unvanquished Vibhatsu rushed even at Bhishma himself. Then Satyaki, Chekitana, Dhrishtadyumna of the Prishata race,

sn: विराटो द्रुपदश्चैव माद्रीपुत्रौ च पाण्डवौ॥ दुद्रुवुर्भीष्ममेवाजौ रक्षिता दृढधन्वना।
en: Virata and Draupada, the two sons of Madri begotten by Pandu, all rushed against Bhishma, their attack being covered by the firm bowman Arjuna.

sn: अभिमन्युश्च समरे द्रौपद्याः पञ्च चात्मजाः॥ दुद्रुवुः समरे भीष्मं समुद्यतमहायुधाः।
en: Then in that battle, Abhimanyu and the five sons of Draupadi all with weapons upraised rushed against Bhishma.

sn: ते सर्वे दृढधन्वानः संयुगेष्वपलायिनः॥ बहुधा भीष्ममानछुर्मार्गणैः क्षतमार्गणैः।
en: All those firm bowmen, never receding from the fight pierced Bhishma on many parts of his body with arrows steadily directed.

sn: विधूय तान् बाणगणान् ये मुक्ताः पार्थिवोत्तमैः॥ पाण्डवानामदीनात्मा व्यगाहत वरूथिनीम्।
en: Then baffling all those arrows shot by those foremost rulers of earth, that warrior of unrepressed soul (Bhishma) penetrated into the ranks of the Pandavas.

sn: चक्रे शरविघातं चक्रीडन्निव पितामहः॥ नाभिसंधत्त पाञ्चाल्ये स्मयमानो मुहुर्मुहः।
en: The grandsire then repulsed all those arrows as if in sport. He did not aim any shafts at the prince of the Panchalas, but laughingly looked at him now and then.

sn: स्त्रीत्वं तस्यानुसंस्मृत्य भीष्मो बाणाशिखण्डिने॥ जगान द्रुपदानीके रथान् सप्त महारथः।
en: Remembering Shikhandin's femininity Bhishma sped not a single arrow at the former. But that mighty car-warrior then slew seven of the best car-warriors of Draupada's division.

sn: तत: किलकिलाशब्दः क्षणेन समभूत् तदा॥ मत्स्यपाञ्चालचेदीनां तमेकमभिधावताम्।
en: Then as the Matsyas, the Panchalas and the Chedis rushed against that single-handed warrior, loud became the din and confusion that then arose.

sn: ते नराश्वरथव्रातैर्मार्गणैश्च परंतप॥ तमेकं छादयामासुर्मेघा इव दिवाकरम्।
en: Then like clouds covering the sun, all those heroes, O afflicter of foes, covered on all sides with foot-soldiers, horse-men and car-warriors and with a network of arrows,

sn: भीष्मं भागीरथीपुत्रं प्रतपन्तं रणे रिपून्॥ ततस्तम्य च तेषां च युद्धे देवासुरोपमे। किरीटीभीष्ममागच्छत् पुरस्कृत्य शिखण्डिनम्॥
en: That single-handed son of Bhagirathi, viz., Bhishma, who was then scorching the foe in battle. Then in that battle between Bhishma on one side and all the Pandava heroes on the other-battle that resembled the one between the gods and the Asuras-Kiritin placing Shikhandin in front of him began to pierce Bhishma,

sn: संजय उवाच एवं ते पाण्डवाः सर्वे पुरस्कृत्य शिखण्डिनम्। विव्यधुः समरे भीष्मं परिवार्य समन्ततः॥
en: Sanjaya said Thus all the Pandavas, placing Shikhandin before them and surrounding Bhishma on all sides began to pierce him in battle.

sn: शतघ्नीभिः सुघोराभिः परिघैश्च परश्वधैः। मुद्गरैर्मुसलैः प्रासैः क्षेपणीयैश्च सर्वशः॥
en: Then with terrible Shataghnis, with bludgeons, battle-axes, maces, mallets, thick short clubs, and lances, and other missiles,

sn: शरैः कनकपुबैश्च शक्तितोमरकम्पनैः। नाराचैर्वत्सदन्तैश्च भुशुण्डीभिश्च सर्वशः॥
en: With arrows furnished with golden wings, with dares, javelins and Kampanas, with Narachas, Vatsadantas, and Bhushundis,

sn: अताडयन् रणे भीष्मं सहिताः सर्वसृञ्जयाः। स विशीर्णतनुत्राणः पीडितो बहुभिस्तदा॥
en: The Srinjayas united together began to wound Bhishma in battle. Then when his shattered and he himself overwhelmed with many arrows.

sn: न विव्यथे तदा भीष्मो भिद्यमानेषु मर्मसु। संदीप्तशरचापाग्निरस्त्रप्रसृतमारुतः॥ नेमिनिदिसंतापो महास्त्रोदयपावकः। चित्रचापमहाज्वालो वीरक्षयमहेन्धनः॥ युगान्ताग्निसमप्रख्यः परेषां समपद्यत। विवृत्य रथसङ्घानामन्तरेण विनिःसृतः॥ दृश्यते स्म नरेन्द्राणां पुनर्मध्यगतश्चरन्। ततः पञ्चालराजं च धृष्टकेतुमचिन्त्य च॥
en: Bhishma experienced no pain pierced though he was to the very vitals. On the other hand Bhishma then appeared fearful to his enemies like the all destructive fire at the expiration of a Yuga, fire, whose flames were armour was constituted by his effulgent arrows and bow, whose (friendly) gale was constituted by the vibrations of air produced by the shafts shot by him, whose heat was constituted by the clatter of his car-wheel, whose splendor was constituted by his mighty weapons, tongues by his variegated bow and fuel by the destruction of heroes. Wheeling in the midst of those car divisions, he sometimes came out of the press, And sometimes again was seen to career rapidly through them. Thereafter without regarding the king of the Panchalas and Dhrishtaketu,

sn: पाण्डवानीकिनीमध्यमाससाद विशाम्पते। ततः सात्यकिभीमौ च पाण्डवं च धनंजयम्॥ दुपदं च विराटं च धृष्टद्युम्नं च पार्षतम्। भीमघोषैर्महावेगैर्मर्मावरणभेदिभिः॥ षडेतान् निशितैर्भीष्मः प्रविव्याधोत्तमैः शरैः। तस्य ते निशितान् बाणान् संनिवार्य महारथाः॥
en: Bhishma, O ruler of men, penetrated into the very heart of the Pandava ranks. Then with arrows of excellent make and great sharpness, all capable of penetrating all kinds of armour and producing great whizz, and charged with great velocity, Bhishma pierced deeply the following six car-warriors, viz., Satyaki, Bhima, Dhananjaya the son of Pandu, Draupada, Virata and Dhrishtadyumna of Prishata's race. These mighty car-warriors also resisting those sharp arrows shot by Bhishma,

sn: दशभिर्दशभिर्भीष्ममर्दयामासुरोजसा। शिखण्डी तु महाबाणान् यान् मुमोच महारथः॥ न चक्रुस्ते रुजं तस्य स्वर्णपङ्खाः शिलाशिताः। ततः किरीटी संरब्धो भीष्ममेवाभ्यधावत॥
en: Pierced him with force, each shooting ten arrows. Those dreadful arrows which that mighty car-warrior Shikhandin shot, and which were furnished with wings of gold and whetted on stone, quickly penetrated the body of Bhishma. Thereupon the diadem-decked Arjuna waxing worth rushed at Bhishma,

sn: शिखण्डिनं पुरस्कृत्य धनुश्चास्य समाच्छिनत्। भीष्मस्य धनुपश्छेदं नामृष्यन्त महारथाः॥
en: And placing Shikhandin before him, he cut off the bow of the latter. Then the following seven mighty car-warriors did not brook that cutting off of Bhishma's bow, warriors namely,

sn: द्रोणश्च कृतवर्मा च सैन्धवश्च जयद्रथः। भूरिश्रवाः शलः शल्यो भगदत्तस्तथैव च॥
en: Drona, Kritavarina, Jayadratha the ruler of the Sindhus, Bhurishravas, Sala, Shalya, and Bhagadatta.

sn: सप्तैते परमक्रुद्धाः किरीटिनमभिद्रुताः। तत्र शस्त्राणि दिव्यानि दर्शयन्तो महारथाः॥
en: These seven car-warriors waxing irascible and displaying weapons of celestial make rushed against the diadem-decked Arjuna.

sn: अभिपेतुर्भृशं क्रुद्धाश्छादयन्तश्च पाण्डवम्। तेषामापततां शब्दः शुश्रुवे फाल्गुनं प्रति॥ उद्वृत्तानां यथा शब्दः समुद्राणां युगक्षये। मतानयत गृह्णीत विद्ध्यध्वमवकर्तत॥ इत्यासीत् तुमुलः शब्दः फाल्गुनस्य रथं प्रति।
en: Indeed excited to the highest pitch of fury they fell upon that son of Pandu shrouding him (with those arrows). Great was the din that as they rushed against Phalguna's chariot. The challenges with loud voice of those warriors who attacked on Arjuna was heard like the roaring seas who violate the limits in devastation (Pralaya kala) and move forward to merge the entire universe with them. The dreadful words started making echo as-"Kill them", "Bring here", "trap soon", "pierce in pieces", "divide in small fractions" near the chariot of Arjuna.

sn: तं शब्दं तुमुलं श्रुत्वा पाण्डवानां महारथाः॥ अभ्यधावन् परीप्सन्तः फाल्गुनं भरतर्षभ।
en: Hearing that dreadful din, the mighty carwarriors of the Pandava host rushed to battle desirous of rescuing that foremost of the Bharatas, viz., Phalguna.

sn: सात्यकिर्भीमसेनश्च धृष्टद्युम्नश्च पार्षतः॥ विराटदुपदौ चोभौ राक्षसश्च घटोत्कचः।
en: arose Then Satyaki, Bhimasena, Prishata's son Dhrishtadyumna, both Virata and Draupada, the Rakshasa Ghatotkacha,

sn: अभिमन्युश्च संक्रुद्धः सप्तैते क्रोधमूर्च्छिताः॥ समभ्यधावंस्त्वरिताश्चित्रकार्मुकधारिणः।
en: The enraged Abhimanyu, all these seven warriors seized with fury and wielding variegated bows rushed to battle, at the top of their speed.

sn: तेषां समभवद् युद्धं तुमुलं लोमहर्षणम्॥ संग्रामे भरतश्रेष्ठ देवानां दानवैरिव।
en: Then, O foremost of the Bharatas, like the battle between the celestial and the Danavas, the battle between those seven car-warriors of each army raged fiercely causing the hair to stand erect.

sn: शिखण्डी त रणे श्रेष्ठो रक्ष्यमाणः किरीटिना॥ अविध्यद् दशभिर्भीष्मं छिन्नधन्वानमाहवे।
en: In that battle, protected as he was by Dhananjaya, that excellent warrior Shikhandin, with ten shafts pierced Bhishma whose bow had been cut off.

sn: सारथिं दशभिश्चास्य ध्वजं चैकेन चिच्छिदे॥ सोऽन्यत् कार्मुकमादाय गाङ्गेयो वेगवत्तरम्।
en: He then pierced the latter's charioteer with ten shafts and with another one shaft cut off his standard. Then Ganga's son took up another bow of superior toughness.

sn: तदप्यस्य शितैर्बाणैस्त्रिभिश्चिच्छेद फाल्गुनः॥ एवं स पाण्डवः क्रुद्ध आत्तमात्तं पुनः पुनः। धनुश्चिच्छेद भीष्मस्य सव्यसाची परंतपः॥ स छिन्नधन्वा संक्रुद्धः सृक्किणी परिसंलिहन्।
en: But that again was cut off with three sharp shafts by Phalguna. 'Thus that scorcher of foes that son of Pandu namely Savyasachin, excited with wrath again and again cut off all the bows that Bhishma took up. Then excited with wrath in consequence of his bows being cut off and licking the corners of his mouth,

sn: शक्ति जग्राह तरसा गिरीणामपि दारणीम्॥ तां च चिक्षेप संक्रुद्धः फाल्गुनस्य रथं प्रति।
en: Bhishma took up a lance with lightness, that was capable of rending even the breasts of mountains, and inflamed with rage he hurled that lance at the car of Phaiguna.

sn: तामापतन्ती सम्प्रेक्ष्य ज्वलन्तीमशनीमिव॥ समादत्त शितान् भल्लान् पञ्च पाण्डवनन्दनः।
en: Beholding that lance course towards himself like the blazing bolt of Heaven, the son of Pandu took up five sharp broad headed arrows,

sn: तस्य चिच्छेद तां शक्तिं पञ्चधा पञ्चभिः शरैः॥ संक्रुद्धो भरतश्रेष्ठ भीष्मबाहुप्रवेरिताम्।
en: Then, O foremost of the Bharatas, inflamed with rage, Arjuna with those five arrows, splintered into five fragments that lance hurled with strength of Bhishma's arms.

sn: सा पपात तथा च्छिन्ना संक्रुद्धेन किरीटिना॥ मेघवृन्दपरिभ्रष्टा विच्छिन्नेव शतह्रदा।
en: Then shattered by the wrathful Arjuna decked with a diadem, that lance fell down like forks of lightning torn away from large masses of clouds.

sn: छिन्नां तां शक्तिमालोक्य भीष्मः क्रोधसमन्वितः॥ अचिन्तयद् रणे वीरो बुद्ध्या परपुरंजयः।
en: Beholding his lance severed, Bhishma became inflamed with rage; and that hero that subduer of hostile cities began to think with the help of his understanding thus.

sn: शक्तोऽहं धनुषैकेन निहन्तुं सर्वपाण्डवान्॥ यद्येषां न भवेद् गोप्ता विष्वक्सेनो महाबलः।
en: “I can slay even with a single bow all these Pandavas, if highly powerful Visaksena (Krishna) be not their protector.

sn: कारणद्वयमास्थाय नाहं योत्स्यामि पाण्डवान्॥ अवध्यत्वाच्च पाण्डूनां स्त्रीभावाच्च शिखण्डिनः।
en: I shall not fight with the Pandavas for two reasons, viz., for the unslayableness of the Pandavas and for the femininity of Shikhandin.

sn: पित्रा तुष्टेन मे पूर्व यदा कालीमुदावहम्॥ स्वच्छन्दमरणं दत्तमवध्यत्वं रणे तथा।
en: Formerly on the occasion of his marrying Kali, my father gratified with me, accorded me two boons, viz., death at my pleasure, and unslayableness in battle.

sn: तस्मान्मृत्युमहं मन्ये प्राप्तकालमिवात्मनः॥ एवं ज्ञात्वा व्यवसितं भीष्मस्यामिततेजसः।
en: I now think that the proper time for my death has arrived." Ascertaining this to be the intention of Bhishma of immeasurable energy,

sn: ऋषयो वसवश्चैव वियत्स्था भीष्ममब्रुवन्॥ यत् ते व्यवसितं तात तदस्माकमपि प्रियम्।
en: The Rishis and Vasus stationed in the firmament then thus addressed Bhishma saying "What you have resolved upon O sire, is also our dear will.

sn: तत् कुरुष्व महाराज युद्धे बुद्धि निवर्तय॥ अस्य वाक्यस्य निधने प्रादुरासीच्छिवोऽनिलः।
en: Therefore, O monarch, follow up in action what you have resolved; and withdraw your heart from fight.” At the conclusion of these words there began to blow an auspicious breeze,

sn: अनुलोमः सुगन्धी च पृषतैश्च समन्वितः॥ देवदुन्दुभयश्चैव सम्प्रणेदुर्महास्वनाः।
en: Fragrant and moistened with sprinkles of water, from all directions. Celestial drums were also sounded emitting great din.

sn: पपात पुष्पवृष्टिश्च भीष्मस्योपरि मारिष॥ न च तच्छुश्रुवे कश्चित् तेषां संवदतां नृप।
en: And, O sire, over Bhishma fell a shower of blossoms. As those Rishis and Vasus spoke, O king, none heard then.

sn: ऋते भीष्मं महाबाहुं मां चापि मुनितेजस॥ सम्भ्रमश्च महानासीत् त्रिदशानां विशाम्पते। पतिष्यति स्थाद् भीष्मे सर्वलोकप्रिये तदा॥ इति देवगणानां च वाक्यं श्रुत्वा महातपाः।
en: Save the mighty armed Bhishma and myself through the prowess of the sage (Vyasa). O ruler of men, great was the flurry that was then found among the Gods, As they thought of the fall of Bhishma, that favorite of all the worlds. Then hearing those words of the celestial, that hero of great ascetic wealth, viz.,

sn: ततः शान्तनवो भीष्मो बीभत्सु नात्यवर्तत॥ भिद्यमानः शितैर्बाणैः सर्वावरणभेदिभिः।
en: Shantanu's son Bhishma assailed not Vibhatsu although he was then being pierced by sharp shafts capable of penetrating through all armours.

sn: शिखण्डी तु महाराज भरताना पितामहम्॥ आजघानोरसि क्रुद्धो नवभिर्निशितैः शरैः।
en: Then, O mighty monarch, Shikhaindin inflamed with wrath struck the grandsire of the Bharatas on the breast with nine shafts of great sharpness.

sn: स तेनाभिहत: संख्ये भीष्मः कुरुपितामहः॥ नाकम्पत महाराज क्षितिकम्पे यथाचलः।
en: Then, O mighty monarch, Shikhandin inflamed with wrath struck the grandsire of the Bharatas on the breast with nine shafts of great sharpness.

sn: ततः प्रहस्य बीभत्सुर्व्याक्षिपन् गाण्डिवं धनुः॥ गाङ्गेयं पञ्चविंशत्या क्षुद्रकाणां समार्पयत्।
en: Then smiling and stretching his bow Gandiva, Vibhatsu wounded Ganga's son with twenty-five short thick shafts.

sn: पुनः पुनः शतैरेनं त्वरमाणो धनंजयः॥ सर्वगात्रेषु शंक्रुद्धः सर्वमर्मस्वताडयत्।
en: Then again under the influence of wrath, Dhananjaya pierced him quick on all parts of his body and to the vitals, with one hundred shafts more.

sn: एवमन्यैरपि भृशं विद्ध्यमानः सहस्रशः॥ तानप्याशु शरैर्भीष्मः प्रविव्याध महारथः।
en: Thus pierced by many other warriors with thousands of arrows, the mighty car-warrior Bhishma pierced them all in return quickly with his own arrows.

sn: तैश्च मुक्ताञ्छरान् भीष्मो युधि सत्यपराक्रमः॥ निवारयामास शरैः समं संनतपर्वभिः।
en: Then Bhishma of prowess unfailing, in battle, with his own shafts of depressed knots simultaneously baffled all these arrows shot by the hostile warriors.

sn: शिखण्डी तु रणे बाणान् यान् मुमोच महारथः॥ न चक्रुस्ते रुजं तस्य रुक्मपुङ्खाः शिलाशिताः।
en: Those arrows furnished with golden wings and whetted on stone that Shikhandin the mighty car-warrior shot at him could not produce any the slightest pain to him.

sn: ततः किरीटी संक्रुद्धो भीष्ममेवाभ्यवर्तत॥ शिखण्डिनं पुरस्कृत्य धनुश्चास्य समाच्छिनत्।
en: Thereupon inflamed with wrath the diademdecked Arjuna placing Shikhandin before him rushed at Bhishma and cut off the latter's bow.

sn: अथैनं नवभिर्विद्ध्वा ध्वजमेकेन चिच्छिदे॥ सारथिं विशिखैश्चास्य दशभिः समकम्पयत्।
en: Then he pierced Bhishma with ten arrows and with another cut down the latter's standard; then with ten other arrows he caused Bhishma's charioteer to tremble.

sn: सोऽन्यत् कार्मुकमादाय गाङ्गेयो बलवत्तरम्॥ तदप्यस्य शितैर्भल्लैस्त्रिधा त्रिभिरघातयत्। निमेषार्धन कौन्तेय आत्तमात्तं महारणे॥ एवमस्य धनूंष्याजौ चिच्छेद सुबहून्यथ।
en: Then that son of Ganga took up another bow of great toughness. Then in that battle, within a twinkling of the eye, Arjuna cut off with three sharp broad-headed arrows that bow as soon as it was taken up. Thus Arjuna cut off successively all the bows that the son of Ganga took up one after another.

sn: ततः शान्तनवो भीष्मो बीभत्सु नात्यवर्तत॥ अथैनं पञ्चविंशत्या क्षुद्रकाणां समाप्रयत्।
en: Thereupon Bhishma the son of Shantanu did no longer assail Vibhatsu; then the latter pierced the former with twenty-five small arrows.

sn: सोऽतिविद्धा महेष्वासो दुःशासनमभाषत॥ एष पार्थो रणे क्रुद्धः पाण्डवानां महारथः।
en: That mighty bowman thus deeply pierced addressing Dushasana said: 'This mighty carwarriot of the Pandava host, viz., Pritha's son Arjuna, inflamed with rage,

sn: शरैरनेकसाहौर्मामेवाभ्यहनन् रणे॥ ३. न चैष समरे शक्यो जेतुं बज्रभृता अपि।
en: Is afflicting me in battle with many thousands of arrows. This one is incapable of being conquered even by the wielder of the thunder bolt.

sn: न चापि सहिता वीरा देवदानवराक्षसाः॥ मां चापि शक्ता निर्जेतुं किमु मर्त्या महारथाः।
en: Regarding me, I may say that all the heroic celestial, Danavas and Rakshasas, united together, can not vanquish me in battle, what to speak of human car-warriors?"

sn: एवं तयोः संवदतोः फाल्गुनो निशितैः शरैः॥ शिखण्डिनं पुरस्कृत्य भीष्मं विव्याध संयुगे।
en: Thus when they were conversing with one another, Arjuna, placing Shikhandin before him, began to pierce Bhishma in battle with shafts of great sharpness.

sn: ततो दुःशासनं भूयः स्मयमान इवाब्रवीत्॥ अतिविद्धः शितैर्बाणैर्भृशं गाण्डीवधन्वना।
en: Thus pierced with sharp arrows by the wielder of the Gandiva, Bhishma once more addressing Dushasana smilingly said:

sn: वज्राशनिसमस्पर्शा अर्जुनेन शरा युधि॥ मुक्ताः सर्वेऽव्यवच्छिन्ना नेमे बाणाः शिखण्डिनः।
en: These arrows of touch resembling that of the thunder bolt, coming in an unbroken line towards me have been discharged by Arjuna. Surely they are not Shikhandin's.

sn: निकृन्तमाना मर्माणि दृढावरणभेदिनः॥ मुसला इव मे नन्ति नेमे बाणाः शिखण्डिनः। वज्रदण्डसमस्पर्शा वज्रवेगदुरासदाः॥ मम प्राणानारुजन्ति नेमे बाणा: शिखण्डिनः।
en: Eating into my very vitals, and penetrating even through my invulnerable armour, these arrows are striking like so many bludgeons. Surely they are not Shikhandin's. Of the touch like that of a Brahmana's rod, of velocity like that of the thunder bolt and incapable of being repulsed, these arrows are sucking out my vital energies. Surely they are not Shikhandin's.

sn: नाशयन्तीव मे प्राणान् यमदूता इवाहिताः॥ गदापरिघसंस्पर्शा नेमे बाणाः शिखण्डिनः।
en: Of touch heavy like that of a mace or a bludgeon these arrows are destroying my vital breaths like so many messengers of Death. Surely they are not Shikhandin's.

sn: भुजगा इव संक्रुद्धा लेलिहाना विषोल्बणाः॥ समाविशन्ति मर्माणि नेमे बाणाः शिखण्डिनः।
en: Like infuriate snakes of virulent venom with their tongues protruding out these arrows are penetrating into my very vitals. Surely these are not Shikhandin's.

sn: अर्जुनस्य इमे बाणा नेमे बाणाः शिखण्डिनः॥ कृन्तन्ति मम गात्राणि माघमां सेगवा इव।
en: These are the arrows of Arjuna and not of Shikhandin, arrows that are cutting me to the quick like the bleakness of winter cutting kine to the quick.

sn: सर्वे ह्यपि न मे दुःखं कुर्युरन्ये नराधिपाः॥ वीरं गाण्डीवधन्वानमृते जिष्णुं कपिध्वजम्।
en: Save and except the heroic wielder of the Gandiva bow, that owner of the standard marked with the device of an ape, viz., the ever victorious Arjuna, all the other monarchs united together can not afflict me."

sn: इति ब्रुवञ्छान्तनवो दिधक्षुरिव पाण्डवान्॥ शक्तिं भीष्मः स पार्थाय ततश्चिक्षेप भारत।
en: Having thus spoken, the highly powerful Bhishma, as if desirous of consuming the Pandavas, hurled at Pritha's son a (terrible) lance.

sn: तामस्य विशिखैश्छित्त्वा त्रिधा त्रिभिरपातयत्॥ पश्यतां कुरुवीराणां सर्वेषां तव भारत।
en: Thereupon with three arrows cutting that lance into three pierces Arjuna felied it down on the ground, O Bharata, even before the very eyes of all the Kurus heroes.

sn: चर्माथादत्त गाड्यो जातरूपपरिष्कृतम्॥ खङ्गं चान्यतप्रेप्सुर्मृत्योरगे जयाय वा।
en: Thereafter Ganga's son grasped a buckler of the polish of gold, as also a resplendent sword, desirous of reaping either victory or death.

sn: तस्य तच्छतधा चर्म व्यधमत् सायकैस्तथा॥ रथादनवरूढस्य तदद्भुतमिवाभवत्।
en: But before he (Bhishma) could descend from his chariot, Arjuna with his shafts splintered that buckler into hundred fragments. Indeed that looked like something marvelous.

sn: ततो युधिष्ठिरो राजा स्वान्यनीकान्यचोदयत्॥ अभिद्रवत गाङ्गेयं मा वोऽस्तु भयमण्वपि।
en: Thereupon, king Yudhishthira urged on his own division saying “Assail the son of Ganga. Entertain not the slightest fear."

sn: अथ ते तोमरैः प्रासैर्वाणौधैश्च समन्ततः॥ पट्टिशैश्च सुनिस्त्रिशैर्नाराचैश्च तथा शितैः।
en: Thereupon from all sides, those troops, with dares, lances, arrows, battle-axes, excellent swords, long shafts of great sharpness,

sn: वत्सदन्तैश्च भल्लैश्च तमेकमभिदुद्रुवुः॥ सिंहनादस्ततो घोरः पाण्डवानामभूत् तदा।
en: With Vatsadantas, and broad-headed arrows, rushed against that single warrior. Then loud was the sin of war-cries that rang through the Pandava ranks.

sn: तथैव तव पुत्राश्च नेदुर्भीष्मजयैषिणः॥ तमेकमभ्यरक्षन्त सिंहनादांश्च चक्रिरे।
en: Similarly, O king, your sons all desirous of seeing Bhishma victorious rushed forward for rescuing that single hero, and they also set up a mighty uproar caused by their yells and warcries.

sn: तत्रासीत् तुमुलं युद्धं तावकानां परैः सह॥ दशमेऽहनि राजेन्द्र भीष्मार्जुनसमागमे।
en: Then on that the tenth day when Bhishma and Arjuna contested with one another, fierce was the fight that regard between your soldiers and those of the enemy.

sn: आसीद् गाङ्ग इवावर्तो मुहूर्तमुदधेरिव॥ सैन्यानां युध्यमानानां निघ्नतामितरेतरम्।
en: Then at the spot where the hostile troops clashed and smote down one another an eddy seemed to stare up into existence like that occurring at the spot where Ganga meets the Ocean.

sn: असौम्यरूपा पृथिवी शोणिताक्ताभवत् तदा॥ समं च विषमं चैव न प्राज्ञायत किंचन।
en: Deluged with blood the earth then assumed a hideous aspect, and her undulations were lost to sight.

sn: योधानामयुतं हत्वा तस्मिन् स दशमेऽहनि॥ अतिष्ठदाहवे भीष्मो भिद्यमानेषु मर्मसु।
en: Having slain ten thousand warriors on that the tenth day of the fight, Bhishma stood on the field while his vitals were being pierced into by Arjuna.

sn: ततः सेनामुखे तस्मिन् स्थितः पार्थो धनुर्धरः॥ मध्येन कुरुसैन्यानां द्रावयामास वाहिनीम्।
en: Then Partha, holding his bow and standing at the head of his divisions broke the Kuru ranks in the very centre of their array.

sn: वयं श्वेतहयाद् भीताः कुन्तीपुत्राद् धनंजयात्॥ पीड्यमानाः शितैः शस्त्रैः प्रद्रवाम रणे तदा।
en: Then afraid of that son of Kunti viz., Dhananjaya the owner of cream-coloured steeds and afflicted with his sharp arrows, we then began to fly away from the field of battle.

sn: सौवीराः कितवाः प्राच्याः प्रतीच्योदीच्यमालवाः॥ अभीषाहाः शूरसेनाः शिवयोऽथ वसातयः।
en: Then the Souviras, the Kitavas, the Westerners, the Northermers and the Malavas, the Abhishahas, the Shurasenas, the Shinis, the Vasatis,

sn: शाल्वाश्रयास्त्रिगर्ताश्च अम्बष्ठाः केकयैः सह॥ सर्व एते महात्मानः शरार्ता व्रणपीडिताः।
en: The Shalvas, Shakas, the Trigartas, the Ambashta, the Kaikeyas, all these illustrious warriors, afflicted with shafts, and pained with thcir cuts,

sn: संग्रामे न जहुर्भीष्मं युध्यमानं किरीटिना॥ ततस्तमेकं बहवः परिवार्य समन्ततः।
en: Did not abandon Bhishma in battle who had been fighting with the diadem-decked Arjuna. Then surrounding the single car-warrior *Bhishma, large numbers of the enemy,

sn: परिकाल्य कुरून् सर्वाशरवर्षैरवाकिरन्॥ निपातयत गृह्णीत युध्यध्वमवकृन्तत।
en: Covered him with arrows showers, having at first defeated the rest of the Kuru warriors. “Slay” “Seize” “Fight” “Cut into pieces,"

sn: इत्यासीत् तुमुल: शब्दो राजन् भीष्मरथं प्रति॥ निहत्य समरे राजशतशोऽथ सहस्रशः।
en: Such were the cries, O king, that were then heard round Bhishma's chariot. Bhishma then slaughtered his foes by hundreds and thousands.

sn: न तस्यासीदनिर्भिन्नं गात्रे व्यङ्गुलमन्तरम्॥ एवंभूतस्तव पिता शरैर्विशकलीकृतः। शिताचैः फाल्गुनेनाजौ प्राक्शिराः प्रापतद् रथात्॥ किंचिच्छेषे दिनकरे पुत्राणां तव पश्यताम्।
en: But then there was not even a space of two fingers in all his body that was not mangled with shafts. Thus then your father, mangled with keep-pointed dares shot by Phalguna, fail down from his car on the field with his head laid towards the East, a little before sunset before the very eyes of your sons.

sn: हाहेति दिवि देवानां पार्थिवानां च भारत॥ पतमाने बभूव सुमहास्वनः।
en: Then at the overthrow of Bhishma loud lamentations of “Alas" and "Oh" were heard,O Bharata, among the kings, and the celestial in the heaven.

sn: सम्पतन्तमभिप्रेक्ष्य महात्मानं पितामहम्॥ सह भीष्मेण सर्वेषां प्रापतन् हृदयानि नः।
en: Beholding the illustrious grandsire fall, we all became dejected and depressed at heart.

sn: स पपात महाबाहुर्वसुधामनुनादयन्॥ इन्द्रध्वज इवोत्सृष्टः केतुः सर्वधनुष्मताम्।
en: That foremost of all bowmen, that mightyarmed hero fell like an uprooted standard in honour of Indra, causing the earth tremble for the while.

sn: धरणी न स पस्पर्श शरसंधैः समावृतः॥ रथाद् भीष्मे शरतल्पे महेष्वासं शयानं पुरुषर्षभम्।
en: Covered closely with arrows he did not then touch the earth's surface. Then as that mighty bowman, that foremost of all male beings lay prostrate on his arrows bed,

sn: रथात् प्रपतितं चैनं दिवियो भावः समाविशत्॥ अभ्यवर्षच्च पर्जन्यः प्राकम्पत च मेदिनी।
en: Being overthrown from his car, a divine inspiration took possession of him. The raincloud Parjanya then poured down its contents and the earth waked.

sn: पतन् स ददृशे चापि दक्षिणेन दिवाकरम्॥ संज्ञां चोपालभद् वीरः कालं संचिन्त्य भारत।
en: When falling Bhishma had marked the sun to be then on the Southern solstice and that hero considering that hour to be inauspicious for paying his debt to nature did not allow his senses to depart.

sn: अन्तरिक्षे च शुश्राव दिव्या वाचः समन्ततः॥ कथं महात्मा गाङ्गेयः सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वरः।
en: He then also heard divine utterance in the heaven, viz., “Why should that foremost of all wielders of weapons, Oh, why should the illustrious son of Ganga,

sn: कालकर्ता नरव्याघ्रः सम्प्राप्ते दक्षिणायने॥ स्थितोऽस्मीति च गाङ्गेयस्तच्छ्रुत्वा वाक्यमब्रवीत्।
en: Why should that foremost of men give up his life when the sun is in the Southern solstice?" Hearing those words Ganga's son said "I am still alive."

sn: धारयामास च प्राणान् पतितोऽपि महीतले॥ उत्तरायणमन्विच्छन् भीष्मः कुरुपितामहः।
en: Then desirous of yielding his life up during the Northern solstice, the grandsire of the Kurus, viz., Bhishma though fallen on earth still retained his vital breaths.

sn: तस्य तन्मतमाज्ञाय गङ्गा हिमवतः सुता॥ महर्षीन् हंसरूपेण प्रेषयामास तत्र वै।
en: Ascertaining that to be his intention, Ganga, the daughter of the Himalayas sent great sages under the disguise of swans then to Bhishma. one,

sn: ततः सम्पातिनो हंसास्त्वरिता मानसौकसः॥ आजग्मुः सहिता द्रष्टुं भीष्मं कुरुपितामहम्।
en: Then those sages disguised under the forms of swans inhabiting the Manasa lake flew to the sky, and in a line came to see Bhishma, the grandsire of the Kurus,

sn: यत्र शेते नरश्रेष्ठः शरतल्पे पितामहः॥ ते तु भीष्मं समासाद्य ऋषयो हंसरूपिणः।
en: At the spot where that foremost of men was lying on his arrowy bed. Then coming to Bhishma those sages under the forms of swans,

sn: अपश्यञ्छरतल्पस्थं भीष्मं कुरुकुलोद्वहम्॥ ते तं दृष्ट्वा महात्मानं कृत्वा चापि प्रदक्षिणम्।
en: Beheld that perpetuator of the Kuru race, viz., Bhishma laid on his bed of arrows. Then beholding that illustrious and circumbulating.

sn: गाङ्गेयं भरतश्रेष्ठं दक्षिणेन च भास्करम्॥ इतरेतरमामन्त्र्य प्राहुस्तत्र मनीषिणः।
en: That foremost of the Bharatas, that son of Ganga, the sages, knowing the sun to be then in the Southern solstice addressing one another said

sn: भीष्मः कथं महात्मा सन् संस्थाता दक्षिणायने॥ इत्युक्त्वा प्रस्थिता हंसा दक्षिणामभितो दिशम्।
en: “Why should the high-souled Bhishma pass away when the sun is in the Southern solstice." Having thus spoken, the swans flew towards the Southern directions.

sn: सम्प्रेक्ष्य वै महाबुद्धिश्चिन्तयित्वा च भारत॥ तानब्रवीच्छान्तनवो नहां गन्ता कथंचन।
en: Then that highly intelligent Bhishma beholding them and reflecting for a while said to them, "I shall not yield up my life,

sn: दक्षिणावर्त आदित्ये एतन्मे मनसि स्थितम्॥ गमिष्यामि स्वकं स्थानमासीद् यन्मे पुरातनम्।
en: As long as the sun will remain in the Southern solstice. This indeed is my determination, I shall repair to my own former abode,

sn: उदगायन आदित्ये हंसाः सत्यं ब्रवीमि वः॥ धारयिष्याम्यहं प्राणानुत्तरायणकाक्षया।
en: When the sun will be in the Northern solstice; this, O Swans. I tell you forsooth. I shall retain my vital breaths loO king anxiously forward for the Northern' solstice.

sn: ऐश्वर्यभूतः प्राणानामुत्सर्गो हि यतो मम॥ तस्मात् प्राणान् धारयिष्ये मुमूर्षुरदगायने।
en: In as much as my giving up of my life is under my thorough control, therefore shall I retain it desirous of dying during the Northern solstice.

sn: यश्च दत्तो वरो मह्यं पित्रा तेन महात्मना॥ छन्दतो मृत्युरित्येवं तस्य चास्तु वरस्तथा।
en: The boon that my illustrious father accorded me. viz.,; that I shall die at my own pleasure, let that boon be true.

sn: धारयिष्ये ततः प्राणानुस्सर्गे नियते सति॥ इत्युक्त्वा तांस्दा हंसान् स शेते शरतल्पगः।
en: As the yielding up of my vital breaths lies entirely with me, I shall retain them.” Having then thus spoken to the swans, he remained (motionless) on his arrowy bed.

sn: एवं कुरूणां पतिते शृङ्गे भीष्मे महौजसि॥ पाण्डवाः सुंजयाश्चैव सिंहनादं प्रचक्रिरे।
en: Thus when the crest of the Kurus, viz., the highly puissant Bhishma was over thrown the Pandavas and the Srinjayas set up a loud warcry.

sn: तस्मिन् हते महासत्त्वे भरतानां पितामहे॥ न किंचित् प्रत्यपद्यन्त पुत्रास्ते भरतर्षभ।
en: When that grandsire of the Bharatas, possessed of great strength was overthrown, O foremost of the Bharatas, your sons knew not what to do.

sn: सम्मोहश्चैव तुमुलः कुरूणामभवत् तदा॥ कृपदुर्योधनमुखा निःश्वस्य रुरुदुस्ततः।
en: Then the Kurus were totally confounded; and Kripa and Duryodhana and others began to wail aloud drawing long and heavy signs.

sn: विषादाच्च चिरं कालमतिष्ठन् विगतेन्द्रियाः॥ दध्युश्चैव महाराज न युद्धे दधिरे मनः।
en: With their senses deprived of their powers in consequence of grief, they remained inert and reflected for long and did not think of fighting.

sn: ऊरुग्राहगृहीताश्च नाभ्यधावन्त पाण्डवान्॥ अवध्ये शन्तनोः पुत्रे हते भीष्मे महौजसि।
en: They could not then rush against the Pandavas as if their thighs were locked and seized in a vice. When that unslayable son of Shantanu. viz., Bhishma endued with great prowess was overthrown,

sn: अभावः सहसा राजन् कुरुराजस्य तर्कितः॥ हतप्रवीरास्तु वयं निकृत्ताश्च शितैः शरैः।
en: O king, the destruction of the Kuru monarch became apparent. Mangled with sharp shafts and with our foremost heroes slain,

sn: कर्तव्यं नाभिजानीमो निर्जिताः सव्यसाचिना॥ पाण्डवाश्च जयं लब्ध्वा परत्र च परां गतिम्।
en: And crushed completely by Savyasachin (Arjuna), we did not then know what to do. Then obtaining victory, and a highly blessed state of existence (hereafter), the Pandavas,

sn: सर्वे दध्मुर्महाशङ्खाशूराः परिघबाहवः॥ सोमकाश्च सपञ्चालाः प्राहृष्यन्त जनेश्वर।
