en: All endued with heroism and possessed of bludgeon-like arms, blew their mighty conchs and, O ruler of men, the Somakas together with the Panchalas then were filled with great delight.

sn: ततस्तूर्यसहस्रेषु नदत्सु स महाबलः॥ आस्फोटयामास भृशं भीमसेनो ननाद च।
en: Then when thousands of drums were struck up, the highly powerful Bhimasena uttered his fierce war-cries and slapped his arms.

sn: सेनयोरुभयोश्चापि गाङ्गेये निहते विभौ॥ संन्यस्य वीराः शस्त्राणि प्राध्यायन्त समन्ततः।
en: On the fall of that illustrious son of Ganga, the heroic combatants of the two armies laying down their weapons, fell to thinking.

sn: प्राक्रोशन् प्राद्रवंश्चान्ये जग्मुर्मोहः तथापरे॥ क्षत्रं चान्येऽभ्यनिन्दन्त भीष्मं चान्येऽभ्यपूजयन्।
en: Some wept aloud, some ran wildly, some were overwhelmed with swoon; some then censured the life of a Kshatriya and some worshipped Bhishma.

sn: ऋषयः पितरश्चैव प्रशशंसुर्महाव्रतम्।१२०॥ भरतानां च ये पूर्वे ते चैनं प्रशशंसिरे।
en: The sages and the Patriarchs all applauded Bhishma. The ancestral manes of the Bharata race also began to praise him.

sn: महोपनिषदं चैव योगमास्थाय वीर्यवान्॥ जपशान्तनवो धीमान् कालाकाक्षी स्थितोऽभवत्।।
en: Then the highly intelligent son of Shantanu, viz., Bhishma endued with great prowess, be taking himself to the Yoga taught in the Upanishadas and reiterating prayers in his mind, remained quite, anxiously loO king forward for his last hour.

description: Giving of a pillow to Bhishma
sn: संजय उवाच समारोप्य महच्चापमभिवाद्य पितामहम्। नेत्राभ्यामश्रुपूर्णाभ्यामिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Sanjaya said Then Arjuna, fixing the string on his mighty bow and saluting the grandsire and with his eyes overflowing with tears thus spoke.

description: Giving of a pillow to Bhishma
sn: आज्ञापय कुरुश्रेष्ठ सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वर। प्रेष्योऽहं तव दुर्धर्ष क्रियतां किं पितामह॥
en: Command me, O foremost of the Kurus, O chief of all wielders of weapons. I am your slave, O invincible one. What, O grandsire, shall I do for you.

description: Giving of a pillow to Bhishma
sn: तमब्रवीच्छान्तनवः शिरो मे तात लम्बते। उपधानं कुरुश्रेष्ठ फाल्गुनोपदधत्स्व मे॥
en: The son of Shantanu then thus replied to him saying "My head, O sire, is hanging down. Fetch me, O foremost of the Kurus, Phalguna, a pillow,

description: Giving of a pillow to Bhishma
sn: शयनस्यानुरूपं वै शीघ्रं वीर प्रयच्छ मे। त्वं हि पार्थ समर्थो वै श्रेष्ठः सर्वधनुष्मताम्॥४।
en: That will be suitable to my bed, and O hero, give that to me soon. You only, O Partha, are equal to the task, you are the foremost of all the bowmen;

description: Giving of a pillow to Bhishma
sn: क्षत्रधर्मस्य वेत्ता च बुद्धिसत्त्वगुणान्वितः। फाल्गुनोऽपि तथेत्युक्त्वा व्यवसायमरोचयत्॥
en: You are conversant with the duties of a Kshatriya and endowed with keep intelligence and modesty and bravery.” Then Phalguna of great might saying yea to his words, prepared to do what Bhishma bade him do.

description: Giving of a pillow to Bhishma
sn: गृह्यानुमन्त्र्य गाण्डीवं शरान् संनतपर्वणः। अनुमान्य महात्मानं भरतानां महारथम्॥
en: Then taking up the Gandiva bow and shafts of close knots, and purifying them with are Mantras and obtaining the permission of that illustrious car-warrior of the Bharatas, Arjuna,

description: Giving of a pillow to Bhishma
sn: त्रिभिस्तीक्ष्णैर्महावेगैरन्वगृह्णच्छिरः शरैः। अभिप्राये तु विदिते धर्मात्मा सव्यसाचिना॥ अतुष्यद् भरतश्रेष्ठो भीष्मो धर्मार्थततत्ववित्। उपधानेन दत्तेन प्रत्यनन्दद् धनंजयम्॥
en: With those sharp arrows charged with great velocity supported Bhishma's head. Then, O foremost of the Bharatas, seeing that Savyasachin had rightly divined his thought, Bhishma of illustrious soul conversant with the essence of all things became gratified with Arjuna; and then greatly praised Dhananjaya for having given him that pillow.

description: Giving of a pillow to Bhishma
sn: प्राह सर्वान् समुद्वीक्ष्य भरतान् भारतं प्रति। कुन्तीपुत्रं युधां श्रेष्ठं सुहृदां प्रीतिवर्धनम्॥
en: Then casting his glances on the Bharatas present there, Bhishma said to that descendant of the Bharatas, namely Kunti's son, that foremost of all warriors, and that enhancer of the delight of his friends.

description: Giving of a pillow to Bhishma
sn: शयनस्यानुरूपं मे पाण्डवोपहितं त्वया। यद्यन्यथा प्रपद्येथाः शपेयं त्वामहं रूषा॥
en: O son of Pandu, you have indeed fetched me a pillow becoming my bed. Had you fetched me something else, I would have cursed you

description: Giving of a pillow to Bhishma
sn: एवमेव महाबाहो धर्मेषु परितिष्ठता। स्वप्तव्यं क्षत्रियेणाजो शरतल्पगतेन वै॥
en: O mighty-armed hero this indeed is the way in which a Kshatriya not transgressing his duties, should sleep on the battle-field lying on an arrowy bed.

description: Giving of a pillow to Bhishma
sn: एवमुक्त्वा तु बीभत्सुं सर्वास्तानब्रवीद् वचः। राज्ञश्च राजपुत्रांश्च पाण्डवानभिसंस्थितान्॥
en: Having thus spoken to Vibhatsu' he said to all the kings and princes present there, the following words. in rage.

description: Giving of a pillow to Bhishma
sn: भीष्म उवाच पश्यध्वमुपधानं मे पाण्डवेनाभिसंधितम्। शिश्येऽहमस्यां शय्यायां यावदावर्तनं रवेः॥
en: Bhishma said Behold you all, the son of Pandu has supplied me with! I shall lie on this bed until the sun rolls back to the Northern solstice.

description: Giving of a pillow to Bhishma
sn: ये तदा मां गमिष्यन्ति ते च प्रेक्ष्यन्ति मां नृपाः। दिशं वैश्रवणाक्रान्तां यदाऽऽगन्ता दिवाकरः॥ नूनं सप्ताश्वयुक्तेन रथेनोत्तमतेजसा। विमोक्ष्येऽहं तदा प्राणान् सुहृदः सुप्रियानिव॥
en: Those kings that will then come to me shall see me (give up my life). When the maker of the day (sun), on his swift moving car yoked with seven horses, will proceed towards the point of the compass occupied by Vaisravana, then shall I yield up my vital breaths, like a friend, bidding adieu to his dear friend.

description: Giving of a pillow to Bhishma
sn: परिखा खन्यतामत्र ममावसदने नृपाः। उपासिष्ये विवस्वन्तमेवं शरशताचितः॥ उपारमध्वं संग्रामाद् वैरमुत्सृज्य पार्थिवाः।
en: O kings, dig up an entrenchment around here; mangled with hundreds of arrows as I am I will offer my homage's to the sun. You, O kings, do desist from the battle, vanquishing all thoughts of hostility.

description: Giving of a pillow to Bhishma
sn: संजय उवाच उपातिष्ठन्नथो वैद्याः शल्योद्धरणकोविदाः॥ सर्वोपरकरणैर्युक्ताः कुशलैः साधु शिक्षिताः।
en: Sanjaya said Thereafter there came several practitioners of the healing are, all well-trained and skillful in drawing out shafts, carrying with them all the necessary balms and appliances.

description: Giving of a pillow to Bhishma
sn: तान् दृष्ट्वा जाछवीपुत्रः प्रोवाच तनयं तव॥ धनं दत्त्वा विसृज्यन्तां पूजयित्वा चिकित्सकाः।
en: Beholding them, Ganga's son said to your son. “Paying proper respect to these physicians, and rewarding them with money, do you dismiss them.

description: Giving of a pillow to Bhishma
sn: एवंगते मयेदानी वैद्यैः कार्यमिहास्ति किम्॥ क्षत्रधर्मे प्रशस्तां हि प्राप्तोऽसस्मि परमां गतिम्।
en: Reduced to this condition, what necessity have I of physicians? I have attained to that blessed existence that is so applauded in those that observe the Kshatriya duties.

description: Giving of a pillow to Bhishma
sn: नैष धर्मो महीपालाः शरतल्पगतस्य मे॥ एभिरेव शरैश्चाहं दग्धव्योऽस्मि नराधिपाः।
en: As I lie on this arrowy bed, it is not indeed my duty to allow myself to be treated by these physicians. I should like, O rulers of earth, to be consumed even by these arrows,

description: Giving of a pillow to Bhishma
sn: तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं तस्य पुत्रो दुर्योधनस्तव॥ वैद्यान् विसर्जयामास पूजयित्वा यथार्हतः।
en: Having heard those words of his, your son Duryodhana dismissed all those physicians, having honoured them duly.

description: Giving of a pillow to Bhishma
sn: ततस्ते विस्मयं जग्मुर्नानाजनपदेश्वराः॥ स्थितिं धर्मे परां दृष्ट्वा भीष्मस्यामिततेजसः।
en: Then the rulers of the various countries, beholding the religious firmness of Bhishma of infinite prowess, were greatly amazed.

description: Giving of a pillow to Bhishma
sn: उपधानं ततो दत्त्वा पितुस्ते मनुजेश्वराः॥ सहिताः पाण्डवाः सर्वे कुरवश्च महारथाः।
en: Then having offered that pillow of your sire, all those kings, together with the mighty car-warriors of the Kurus and the Pandavas,

description: Giving of a pillow to Bhishma
sn: उपगम्य महात्मानं शयानं शयने शुभे॥ तेऽभिवाद्य ततो भीष्मं कृत्वा च त्रिः प्रदक्षिणम्। विधाय रक्षां भीष्मस्य सर्व एव समन्ततः॥ वीराः स्वशिबिराण्येव ध्यायन्तः परमातुराः। निवेशायाभ्युपागच्छन् सायाछे रुधिरोक्षिताः॥ निविष्टान् पाण्डवांश्चैव प्रीयमाणान् महास्थान्। भीष्मस्य पतने हृष्टानुपगम्य महाबलः॥ उवाच माधवः काले धर्मपुत्रं युधिष्ठिरम्।
en: Again approached the illustrious Bhishma prostrate on his excellent bed of arrows. Then having saluted and three times circumbulated that illustrious one viz., Bhishma, and having arranged for his protection, the heroes entered their respective camps, for taking rest, at the hour of sun-set, with their bodies bespattered with blood, and thoughtful and extremely pained. Then approaching, at a suitable season, the Pandavas, those mighty car-warriors cheerfully seated together and rejoicing at the fall of Bhishma, the mighty Madhava said these words to Yudhishthira the son of Dharma.

description: Giving of a pillow to Bhishma
sn: दिष्ट्या जयसि कौरव्य दिष्ट्या भीष्मो निपातितः॥२८ अवध्यो मानुषैरेव सत्यसंधो महारथः।
en: “Through good fortune, O best of the Kurus, have you attained victory; through good fortune has Bhishma, that mighty car-warrior of unerring aim, incapable of being slain by men, been overthrown.

description: Giving of a pillow to Bhishma
sn: अथवा दैवतैः सार्धं सर्वशास्त्रस्य पारगः॥ त्वां तु चक्षुर्हणं प्राप्य दग्धो घोरेण चक्षुषा।
en: Or it may be, that having, through Destiny, obtained you that slay with your very glances for a foe, that one through conversant with the use of all weapons has been destroyed by your angry looks."

description: Giving of a pillow to Bhishma
sn: एवमुक्तो धर्मराजः प्रत्युवाच जनार्दनम्॥ तव प्रसादाद् विजयः क्रोधात् तव पराजयः।
en: Being thus spoken to, the very virtuous king Yudhishthira replied to Janardana saying. “Victory comes to a man through your grace, and defcat overtakes him through your wrath.

description: Giving of a pillow to Bhishma
sn: त्वं हि नः शरणं कृष्ण भक्तानामभयंकरः॥ अनाश्चर्यो जयस्तेषां येषां त्वमसि केशव।
en: You are sole refuge, O Krishna: You give assurances of safety to your devotees. Victory is not a marvel for those whom,OKeshava,

description: Giving of a pillow to Bhishma
sn: रक्षिता समरे नित्यं नित्यं चापि हिते रतः॥ सर्वथा त्वां समासाद्य नाश्चर्यमिति मे मतिः।
en: You always protect in battle, and for whose welfare you always concern yourself. Having yourself for our protector, I do not consider anything wonderful for us."

description: Giving of a pillow to Bhishma
sn: एवमुक्तः प्रत्युवाच स्मयमानो जनार्दनः। तवैवैतद् युक्तरूपं वचनं पार्थिवोत्तम॥
en: Thus spoken to Janardana smilingly replied. “Indeed, O foremost of all the rulers of earth, these are words suited to fall from your lips only."

sn: संजय उवाच व्युष्टायां तु महाराज शर्वर्यां सर्वपार्थिवाः। पाण्डवा धार्तराष्ट्राश्च उपातिष्ठन् पितामहम्॥
en: Sanjaya said O monarch, after the night had passed away, all the kings belonging to the Pandava and Dhritarashtra hosts approached the grandsire.

sn: तं वीरशयने वीरं शयानं कुरुसत्तम। अभिवाद्योपतस्थुर्वै क्षत्रियाः क्षत्रियर्षभम्॥
en: Then all the Kshatriyas, having saluted that foremost of the Kurus, that hero prostrate on a hero's bed, that chief of all; Kshatriyas, stood near him.

sn: कन्याश्चन्दनचूर्णैश्च लाजैर्माल्यैश्च सर्वशः। अवाकिरज्छान्तनवं तत्र गत्वा सहस्रशः॥
en: Repairing there by thousands, maidens covered the son of Shantanu on all parts of his body, with pulverised sandal-wood. fieldpaddy, and garlands of flowers.

sn: स्त्रियो वृद्धास्तथा बालाः प्रेक्षकाच पृथग्जनाः। समभ्ययुः शान्तनवं भूतानीव तमोनुदम्॥
en: Women, old and children, and numerous other, spectators approached the son of Shantanu, like the Bhutas approaching the iising .luminary of the day.

sn: तूर्याणि शतसंख्यानि तथैव नटनर्तकाः। शिल्पिनश्च तथाऽऽजग्मुः कुरुवृद्धं पितामहम्॥
en: Trumpeters, courtesans, mimes, actors and dancers and artisans, in crowds repaired to that venerable grandsire of the Kurus.

sn: उपारण्य च युद्धेभ्यः संनाहान् विप्रमुच्य ते। आयुधानि च निक्षिप्य सहिताः कुरुपाण्डवाः॥
en: Desisting from fight and doffing their armours and laying aside their weapons, the Kurus and the Pandavas together, men

sn: अन्वासन्त दुराधर्षं देवव्रतमरिंदमम्। अन्योन्यं प्रीतिमन्तस्ते यथापूर्वं यथावयः॥
en: Approached the invincible Devavrata that subduer of foes. Then as in former days, they were friendly to one another, and addressed one another in agreeable words.

sn: सा पार्थिवशताकीर्णा समितिर्भीष्मशोभिता। शुशुभे भारती दीप्ता दिवीवादित्यमण्डलम्॥
en: Then that assembly crowded with numerous Bharata kings, and ornamented by the presence of Bhishma, appeared beautiful like a conclave of the gods in the heavens.

sn: विबभो च नृपाणां सा गङ्गासुतमुपासताम्। देवानामिव देवेशं पितामहमुपासताम्॥
en: And that assembly of kings paying their respects of the son of Ganga, appeared beautiful like that of the gods adoring their lord the venerable Grandsire (Brahma).

sn: भीष्मस्तु वेदनां धैर्यानिगृह्य भरतर्षभ। अभितप्तः शरैश्चैव निःश्वसन्नुरगो यथा।॥
en: Then, O foremost of the Bharatas, Bhishma, having overcome his pain by his patience, and afflicted with many dares, breathed like a snake.

sn: शराभितप्तकायोऽपि शस्त्रसम्पातमूर्छितः। पानीयमिति सम्प्रेक्ष्य राज्ञस्तान् प्रत्यभाषत॥
en: His body was burning with the pain caused by the arrow's struck therein, and he was being deprived of his senses in consequence of the weapons-cuts. Beholding those kings, he then said "Bring me water."

sn: ततस्ते क्षत्रिया राजन्नुपुजङ्गः समन्ततः। भक्ष्यानुच्चावचान् राजन् वारिकुम्भांश्च शीतलान्॥
en: Thereat those Kshatriyas, O king, brought many excellent viands, and jars filled with cold water.

sn: उपानीतं तु पानीयं दृष्ट्वा शान्तनवोऽब्रवीत्। नाद्यातीता मया शक्या भोगाः केचन मानुषाः॥
en: Thereupon Shantanu's son beholding water brought for him said "This day forward, O son, I will no longer use articles of human enjoyment.

sn: अपक्रान्तो मनुष्येभ्यः शरशय्यां गतो ह्यहम्। प्रतीक्षमाणस्तिष्ठामि निवृत्तिं शशिसूर्ययोः॥
en: I have passed away from the society of men, and am now lying on this bed of arrows. I am lying here expectant of the change in the sun and moon."

sn: एवमुक्त्वा शान्तनवो निन्दन् वाक्येन पार्थिवान्। अर्जुनं द्रष्टुमिच्छामीत्यभ्यभाषत भारत॥
en: Having thus spoken, and censuring those kings with (cruel) words, Bhishma said, O Bharata I desire to see Arjuna."

sn: अथोपेत्य महाबाहुरभिवाद्य पितामहम्। अतिष्ठत् प्राञ्जलिः प्रह्वः किं करोमीति चाब्रवीत्॥
en: Thereupon that mighty-armed hero Arjuna approaching and saluting the grandsire stood there with palms folded, and said “What shall I do."

sn: तं दृष्ट्वा पाण्डवं राजन्नभिवाद्याग्रतः स्थितम्। अभ्यभाषत धर्मात्मा भीष्मः प्रीतो धनंजयम्॥
en: Beholding that son of Pandu stand before him with folded palms, the virtuous-souled Bhishma highly pleased, said these words of Dhananjaya.

sn: दह्यतीव शरीरं मे संवृतस्य तवेषुभिः। मर्माणि परिदूयन्ते मुखं च परिशुष्यति॥
en: “My body is burning, and I am covered with your sorrows. All the vital parts of my body are suffering extreme pain and my mouth is becoming dry.

sn: वेदनार्तशरीरस्य प्रयच्छापो ममार्जुन। त्वं हि शक्तो महेष्वास दातुमापो यथाविधि॥
en: Afflicted as my body is with extreme pain, give me water, O Arjuna, to drink. It is you alone, O mighty bowman, that are capable of supplying me with proper drink now."

sn: अर्जुनस्तु तथेत्युक्त्वा रथमारुह्य वीयवान्। अधिज्यं बलवत् कृत्वा गाण्डीवं व्याक्षिपद् धनुः॥
en: Thereupon the highly puissant Arjuna saying "yea" to Bhishma's words, mounted on his chariot. Then fixing the string to his mighty bow Gandiva, he began to stretch it.

sn: तस्य ज्यातलनिर्घोषं विस्फूर्जितमिवाशनेः। वित्रेसुः सर्वभूतानि सर्वे श्रुत्वा च पार्थिवाः॥
en: Then hearing the twang of his bow and the slap of his arms that resembled the rumble of thunder, the troops and kings there, were inspired with terror.

sn: ततः प्रदक्षिणं कृत्वा रथेन रथिनां वरः। शयानं भरतश्रेष्ठं सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वरम्॥
en: Thereafter that foremost of car-warriors (Arjuna) circumambulating that prostrate chief of the Bharatas, that foremost of all wielders of weapons, viz., Bhishma,

sn: संधाय च शरं दीप्तमभिमत्र्य स पाण्डवः। पर्जन्यास्त्रेण संजोज्य सर्वलोकस्य पश्यतः॥
en: And fixing on his bowstring an effulgent arrow inspired with aphorisms and identified with the Parjanya weapon, before the very eyes of all the people present,

sn: अविध्यत् पृथिवीं पार्थः पार्श्वे भीष्मस्य दक्षिणे। उत्पपात ततो धारा वारिणो विमला शुभा॥
en: Penetrated the earth a little to the right of the spot where Bhishma lay. Thereupon, there gushed out a jet of water pure and auspicious,

sn: शीतस्यामृतकल्पस्य दिव्यगन्धरसस्य च। अतर्पयत् ततः पार्थः शीतया जलधारया।॥
en: And cool and nectar-like an fraught with celestial fragrance and tastefulness. Then with that cool jet of water did the son of Pritha gratify.

sn: भीष्मं कुरूणामृषभं दिव्यकर्मपराक्रमम्। कर्मणा तेन पार्थस्य शक्रस्येव विकुर्वतः॥
en: That foremost of the Kurus, viz., Bhishma of god-like achievements and prowess. Then seeing that feat of Pritha son, that resembled that of Indra himself,

sn: विस्मयं परमं जग्मुस्ततस्ते वसुधाधिपाः। तत् कर्म प्रेक्ष्य बीभत्सोरतिमानुषविक्रमम्॥
en: All the rulers of the earth present there, were filled with wonder. Then beholding that feat of Vibhatsu that indicated his superhuman prowess,

sn: सम्प्रावेपन्त कुरवो गावः शीतार्दिता इव। विस्मयोच्चोत्तरीयाणि व्याविध्यन् सर्वतो नृपाः॥
en: The Kurus began to shiver like kine afflicted with the chill of winter. Out of amazement the kings then began to waive their garments;

sn: शङ्खदुन्दुभिनिर्घोषस्तुमुल: सर्वतोऽभवत्। तृप्तः शान्तनवश्चापि राजन् बीभत्सुमब्रवीत्॥
en: And the sound of drums and the blare of conchs on all sides became deafening. Then, O king, Shantanu's son, being greatly gratified, thus addressed Vibhatsu,

sn: सर्वपार्थिववीराणां संनिधौ पूजयन्निव। नैतच्चित्रं महाबाहो त्वयि कौरवनन्दन।॥
en: Applauding him before all the heroic rulers of earth. “O mighty-armed hero, this feat is not a marvel in respect to you, O delighter of the Kurus.

sn: कथितो नारदेनासि पूर्वर्षिरमितद्युते। वासुदेवसहायस्त्वं महत् कर्म करिष्यसि॥
en: You have been spoken of by Narada as an ancient sage, O you of dazzling effulgence. Having the son of Vasudeva for your helpmate, you shall achieve great feats,

sn: यन्त्रोत्सहति देवेन्द्रः सह देवैरपि ध्रुवम्। विदुस्त्वां निधनं पार्थं सर्वक्षत्रस्य तद्विदः॥ धनुर्धराणामेकस्त्वं पृथिव्यां प्रवरो नृषु॥
en: That even the lord of the celestial with his heavenly host dare not accomplish. Those that are conversant with the knowledge of every thing, regard you, O Arjuna, to be the foremost bowman among all the Kshatriyas.

sn: मनुष्या जगति श्रेष्ठाः पक्षिणां पतगेश्वरः। सरितां सागरः श्रेष्ठो गौर्वरिष्ठा चतुष्पदाम्॥
en: Among all human wielders of bows, you are unrivaled; you are the foremost of all men. As man is the foremost of all created beings of this world, as Garuda is the chief of all winged creatures,

sn: आदित्यस्तेजसां श्रेष्ठो गिरीणां हिमवान् वरः। जातीनां ब्राह्मणः श्रेष्ठः श्रेष्ठस्त्वमसि धन्विनाम्॥
en: As the Ocean is the chief of all reservoirs of water, as the cow is the best of all quadruped animals, as the Himavat is the chief of all mountains, as the Brahmana is the foremost of all castes, so are you the foremost of all wielders of bows.

sn: न वै श्रुतं धार्तराष्ट्रेण वाक्यं मयोच्यमानं विदुरेण चैव। द्रोणेन रामेण जनार्दनेन मुहुर्मुहुः संजयेनापि चोक्तम्॥
en: The son of Dhritarashtra paid no heed to the (salutary) counsel repeatedly offered by myself, by Vidura, Drona, Rama, Janardana and Sanjaya.

sn: परीतबुद्धिर्हि विसंज्ञकल्पो दुर्योधनो न च तच्छ्रद्दधाति। स शेष्यते वै निहतश्चिराय शास्त्रातिगो भीमवलाभिभूतः॥
en: Raft of his reason, and like one senseless, Duryodhana then disregarded our words. Past all counsel, he shall have soon to lie on the field crushed by the might of Bhishma.”

sn: एतच्छ्रुत्वा तद्वचः कौरवेन्द्रो दुर्योधनो दीनमना बभूव। तमब्रवीच्छान्तनवोऽभिवीक्ष्य निबोध राजन् भव वीतमन्युः॥
en: Hearing these words of Bhishma, Duryodhana, the lord of the Kurus, became depressed at heart. Then the son of Shantanu, casting his eyes on him once more said "Hear me, O king, renounce your wrath.

sn: दृष्टं दुर्योधनैतत् ते यथा पार्थेन धीमता। जलस्य धारा जनिता शीतस्यामृतगन्धिनः॥
en: You have seen, even now, O Duryodhana, how the intelligent Partha created that jet of water, cool and fraught with nectarious fragrance.

sn: एतस्य कर्ता लोकेऽस्मिन् नान्यः कश्चन विद्यते। आग्नेयं वारुणं सौम्यं वायव्यमथ वैष्णवम्॥
en: There is none in the universe who can achieve the self-same feat. The weapons of are which the presiding deities respectively are Agni, Varuna, Soma Vayu, Vishnu,

sn: ऐन्द्रं पाशुपत ब्राह्मं पारमेष्ठ्यं प्रजापतेः। धातुस्त्वष्टुश्च सवितुर्वैवस्वतमथापि वा॥
en: Indra, Pashupati, Paramesthi, Prajapati, Dhata, Tvashtra, Savita, and Vaivasvata,

sn: सर्वस्मिन् मानुषे लोके वेत्त्येको हि धनंजयः। कृष्णो वा देवकीपुत्रो नान्यो वेदेह कश्चन॥
en: Alll these weapons known to Dhananjaya only, as also to Krishna, the son of Devaki, and not to any one else.

sn: अशक्यः पाण्डवस्तात युद्धो जेतुं कथंचन। अमानुषाणि कर्माणि यस्यैतानि महात्मनः॥
en: This son of Pandu, O sire, is incapable of being defeated in battle, by the celestial and the Asuras united together. These are the superhuman feats achieved by this illustrious hero.

sn: तेन सत्त्ववता संख्ये शूरेणाहवशोभिना। कृतिना समरे राजन् संधिर्मवतु मा चिरम्॥
en: Therefore, O monarch, let peace be soon concluded with that truthful hero that ornament of the fled, accomplished in all modes of warfare.

sn: यावत् कृष्णो महाबाहुः स्वाधीनः कुरुसत्तम। तावत् पार्थेन शूरेण संधिस्ते तात युज्यताम्॥
en: As long as the mighty-armed Krishna is under his own control let, O sire, O foremost the Kurus, peace be made with this heroic sons of Pritha.

sn: यावन्न ते चमूः चमूः सर्वाः शरैः संनतपर्वभिः। नाशयत्यर्जुनस्तावत् संधिस्ते तात युज्यताम्॥
en: O son! Your alliance with Arjuna is must to be made unless he destroys your whole army by hitting hard through the arrows having bent knots.

sn: यावत् तिष्ठन्ति समरे हतशेषाः सहोदराः। नृपाश्च बहवो राजस्तावत् संधिः प्रयुज्यताम्॥
en: As still, O king, these your uterine brothers and these myriad kings here survive the battle, let peace be concluded.

sn: न निर्दहति ते यावत् क्रोधदीप्तेक्षणश्चमूम्। युधिष्ठिरो रणे तावत् संधिस्ते तात युज्यताम्॥ नकुलः सहदेवश्च भीमसेनश्च पाण्डवः। यावच्चमू महाराज नाशयन्ति न सर्वशः॥
en: As long as Yudhishthira does not burn down your army with his eyes flashing the fire of wrath, let peace by concluded with him, O sire. As long as Nakula, Sahadeva, and Pandu's son Bhimasena, do not totally crush your army down, let peace be made with them.

sn: तावत् ते पाण्डवैवीरैः सौहार्द मम रोचते। युद्धं मदन्तमेवास्तु तात संशाम्य पाण्डवैः॥
en: It likes me best to see amity established between you and the heroic Pandavas. Let, O sire, peace by concluded with the Pandavas.

sn: एतत् तु रोचतां वाक्यं यदुक्तोऽसि मयानघ। एतत् क्षेममहं मन्ये तव चैव कुलस्य च॥
en: Let these words, O sinless one, uttered by me, be agreeable to you. This conclusion of peace do I consider to be beneficial to you and to your dynasty.

sn: त्यक्त्वा मन्युं व्युपशाम्यस्व पार्थैः पर्याप्तमेतद् यत् कृतं फाल्गुनेन। भीष्मस्यान्तादस्तु वः सौहृदं च जीवन्तु शेषाः साधु राजन् प्रसीद॥
en: Renouncing your wrath, do you conclude peace with the sons of Pritha. Enough has already been accomplished by Phalguna. Let amity be established among you with the death of Bhishma. Let the rest (of the warriors) live! Relent, reient, O monarch!

sn: मिन्द्रप्रस्थं धर्मराजोऽभियातु। मा मित्रचक् पार्थिवानां जघन्यः "पापां कीर्ति प्राप्स्यसे कौरवेन्द्र॥
en: Give half of your kingdom to the Pandavas. Let Yudhishthira repair to Indraprastha. Be not despised by the rulers of the earth for having brewed in testine broils. Do not, O foremost of the Kurus, attain a sinful notoriety.

sn: ममावसानाच्छान्तिरस्तु प्रजानां संगच्छन्तां पार्थिवाः प्रीतिमन्तः। पिता पुत्रं मातुलं भागिनेयो भ्राता चैव भ्रातरं प्रैतु राजन्॥
en: With my passing away, let peace be enjoyed by the people; let these kings embrace one another out of friendship. Let father be reconciled to his son, let nephew be reconciled to his uncle; let brother he reconciled to his brother, O king.

sn: न चेदेवं प्राप्तकालं वचो मे मोहाविष्टः प्रतिपत्स्यस्यबुद्ध्या। तप्स्यन्ते एतदन्ताः स्थ सर्वे सत्यामेतां भारतीमीरयामि॥
en: If through perverted understanding, and possessed by folly, you do not listen to these reasonable words of mine, then-this I tell you for certain-you shall have to rue your folly hereinafter. Therefore let the war end here."

sn: एतद् वाक्यं सौहृदादापगेयो मध्ये राज्ञां भारतं श्रावयित्वा। तूष्णीमासीच्छल्यसंतप्तमर्मा योज्यात्मानं वेदनां संनियम्य॥
en: Having out of affection spoken these words of Duryodhana among all those kings, the son of Ganga remained silent; though his vital parts were then being consumed by those arrowwounds, he, overcoming his agony, kept himself tranquil.

sn: संजय उवाच धर्मार्थसहितं वाक्यं श्रुत्वा हितमनामयम्। नारोचयत् पुत्रस्ते मुमूर्षुरिव भेषजम्॥
en: Sanjaya said Hearing these salutary and peaceful words of counsel, fraught with virtue and worldly profit, your son refused to act up to them, like a dying man refusing to take medicine.

sn: संजय उवाच ततस्ते पार्थिवाः सर्वे जग्मुः स्वानालयान् पुनः। तूष्णीभूते महाराज भीष्मे शान्तनुन्दने॥
en: Sanjaya said After Bhishma the son of Shantanu had ceased speaking, O mighty monarch, all the rulers of earth that had come there, went back to their respective quarters.

sn: श्रुत्वा तु निहतं राधेयः पुरुषर्षभः। ईषदागतसंत्रासस्त्वरयोपजगाम ह॥
en: Hearing of the slaughter of Bhishma, that best of men, Vikarna's terrified to a certain extent, quickly to the spot where Bhishma lay.

sn: स ददर्श महात्मानं शरतल्पगतं तदा। जन्मशय्यागतं वीरं कार्तिकेयमिव प्रभुम्॥
en: There he saw the illustrious hero lying on his arrowy bed, like the heroic lord Kartikeya lying after his birth on his bed of reeds.

sn: निमीलिताक्षं तं वीरं साश्रुकण्ठस्तदा वृषः। भीष्म भीष्म महाबाहो इत्युवाच महाद्युतिः॥
en: Then the highly effulgent Vrisha (Karna), with voice with tears of grief, approaching that hero lying with his eyes shut, fell at his two feet.

sn: राधेयोऽहं कुरुश्रेष्ठ नित्यमक्षिगतस्तव। द्वेष्योऽहं तव सर्वत्र इति चैनमुवाच ह॥
en: "I am Radha's son, O foremost of the Kurus, who whenever he became the object of your sight, looked upon with enmity by ." These were the words he then addressed to Bhishma.

sn: तच्छ्रुत्वा कुरुवृद्धो हि बली संवृतलोचनः। शनैरुद्वीक्ष्य सस्नेहमिदं च रक्षिणः। पितेव पुत्रं गाड्यः परिरभ्यैकपाणिना॥
en: Hearing those words of his, the venerable Kuru grandsire, viz., the son of Ganga, slowly loO king at him with his eyes covered with film, and dismissing his guards and embracing Karna with one arm like a father embracing his son, thus affectionately addressed him saying.

sn: एह्येहि मे विप्रतीप स्पर्धसे त्वं मया सह। यदि मां नाधिगच्छेथा न ते श्रेयो ध्रुवं भवेत्॥
en: Come, come you were ever my opponent, and ever tried to outvote me. Every think would not surely have well with you, had you not come here.

sn: कौन्तेयस्त्वं न राधेयो न तवाधिस्थः पिता। सूर्यजस्त्वं महाबाहो विदितो नारदान्मया॥
en: You are the son of Kunti, and not that of Radha; Adhiratha is not you father; all this, O mighty-armed one, regarding you, I have heard from Narada,

sn: कृष्णद्वैपायनाच्चैव तच्च सत्यं न संशयः। न च द्वेषोऽस्ति मे तात त्वयि सत्यं ब्रवीमि ते॥
en: As also from Vyasa. All this therefore can not but be true. I tell you, O son, forsooth, that I entertain no malice against you.

sn: तेजोवधानिमित्तं तु परुषं त्वाहमब्रुवम्। अक्समात् पाण्डवान् सर्वानवाक्षिपसि सुब्रत।॥
en: I used to apply words to you only for reducing your prowess. O you of excellent vows, you abuse the Pandavas without any reason whatsoever.

sn: येनासि बहुशो राज्ञा चोदितः सूतनन्दन। जातोऽसि धर्मलोपेन ततस्ते बुद्धिरीदृशी॥ नीचाश्रयान्मत्सरेण द्वेषिणी गुणिनामपि।
en: Your very birth attended with transgression of virtue. Therefore is your intellect thus (perverted). In consequence of your arrogance and also association with the mean, your heart harbors malice against even the meritorious.

sn: तेनासि बहुशो रूक्षं श्रावितः कुरुसंसदि॥ जानामि समरे वीर्यं शत्रुभिर्दुःसहं भुवि।
en: For this reason did I use harsh language against you in the assembly of the Kurus. I know your prowess in battle incapable of being borne by the foe, was

sn: ब्रह्मण्यतां शौर्यं च दाने परमां स्थितिम्॥ न त्वया सदृशः कश्चित् पुरुषेष्वमरोपम।
en: Your devotion to the Brahman, your bravery, and your great love for deeds of benevolence. Among men there is none capable of rivaling you, O you resembling an immortal.

sn: कुलभेदभयाच्चाहं सदा परुषमुक्तवान्॥ इष्वस्त्रे चास्त्रसंधाने लाघवेऽस्त्रबले तथा।
en: Apprehending intestine quarrels, I always applied harsh words to you. In archery, in fixing the arrows on the string, in lightness of hands, in the force of your weapons,

sn: सदृशः फाल्गुनेनासि कृष्णेन च महात्मना॥ कर्ण काशिपुरं गत्वा त्वयैकेन धनुष्मता।
en: You are equal to Phalguna or the illustrious Krishna. In the city of the Kashis, O Karna, holding the bow single-headed.

sn: कन्यार्थे कुरुराजस्य राजानो मृदिता युधि॥ तथा च बलवान् राजा जरासंधो दुरासदः।
en: You humiliated in battle all the other kings, for securing the bride for the king of the Kurus. Even the invincible king Jarasandha endued with might,

sn: समरे समरश्लाघिन् न त्वया सदृशोऽभवत्॥ ब्रह्मण्यः सत्त्वयोधी च तेजसा च बलेन च।
en: Ever boastful in battle, could never cope with you in fight. You are devoted to the Brahmanas, you always love fair fight. In prowess and in might,

sn: देवगर्भसमः संख्ये मनुष्यैरधिको युधि॥ व्यपनीतोऽद्य मन्युर्मे यस्त्वा प्रति पुरा कृतः।
en: You certainly are equal to a celestial child, and are far-superior to men. I relinquish today the wrath I formerly harbored against you.

sn: दैवं पुरुषकारेण न शक्यमतिवर्तितुम्॥२० सोदर्याः पाण्डवा वीरा भ्रातरस्तेऽरिसूदन।
en: Human effort can never overcome Destiny. O slayer of your foes, the Pandavas are your uterine brothers.

sn: संगच्छ तैर्महाबाहो मम चेदिच्छसि प्रियम्॥ मया भवतु निर्वृत्तं वैरमादित्यनन्दन। पृथिव्यां सर्वराजानो भवन्त्वद्य निरामयाः॥
en: O mighty-armed hero, if you desire to do what is agreeable to me, then be reconciled to them. O son of the Sun, let hostilities see their end at my fall. Let all kings of the earth be relieved of their burden of anxiety and dangers.

sn: कर्ण उवाच जानाम्येव महाबाहो सर्वमेतन्न संशयः। यथा वदसि मे भीष्म कौन्तेयोऽहं न सूतजः॥
en: Karna said I know all this, O mighty-armed her; there is nothing to be doubted in what you have spoken. You speak truly, O Bhishma. I am Kunti's son, and not that of a charioteer.

sn: अवकीर्णस्त्वहं कुन्त्या सूतेन च विवर्धितः। भुक्त्वा दुर्योधनैश्वर्यं न मिथ्याकर्तुमुत्सहे॥
en: I was however disowned by Kunti, and I have been brought up by a charioteer. Having enjoyed the wealth of Duryodhana so long, I can not venture to disappoint his hopes.

sn: वसुदेवसुतो यद्वत् पाण्डवाय दृढव्रतः। वसु चैव शरीरं च पुत्रदारं तथा यशः॥ सर्वं दुर्योधनस्यार्थे त्यक्त मे भूरिदक्षिण। मा चैतद् व्याधिमरणं क्षत्रं स्यादिति कौरव॥
en: Like the son of Vasudeva who is firmly resolved to do good to the Pandavas, I also, have set at naught, you that bestow profuse gifts to the Brahmanas, my wealth, my sons, my wife and even my own body and honour. Death resulting from disease is not, indeed, a meet end for a Kshatriya, O you of Kuru's race.

sn: कोपिताः पाण्डवा नित्यं समाश्रित्य सुयोधनम्। अवश्यभावी ह्यर्थोऽयं योन शक्यो निवर्तितुम्॥
en: For the interests of Duryodhana, I have hitherto always incited the Pandavas against me; the result is inevitable and none possibly can prevent it.

sn: दैवं पुरुषकारेण को निवर्तितुमुत्सहेत्। पृथिवीक्षयशंसीनि निमित्तानि पितामह॥
en: What person ever ventures to overcome Destiny by human endeavor? Numerous protects, O grandsire, indicating the destruction of the earth,

sn: भवद्भिपलब्धानि कथितानि च संसदि। पाण्डवा वासुदेवश्च विदिता मम सर्वशः॥
en: Were seen and declared in the assembly by you. I perfectly know that the Pandavas and the son of Vasudeva.

sn: अजेयाः पुरुषैरन्यैरिति तांश्चोत्सहामहे। विजयिष्ये रणे पाण्डुनिति मे निश्चितं मनः॥
en: Are invincible by other men. Even with them do I propose to fight. I have firmly set my heart upon vanquishing the sons of Pandu on battle.

sn: न च शक्यमवस्रष्टुं वैरमेतत् सुदारुणम्। धनंजयेन योत्स्येऽहं स्वधर्मप्रीतमानसः॥
en: I can not, on the other hand, renounce this fierce hostility that I cherish for the Pandavas. With a joyful heart performing the duties of my order, I will fight with Dhananjaya.

sn: अनुजानीष्व मां तात युद्धाय कृतनिश्चयम्। अनुज्ञातस्त्वया वीर युद्ध्येयमिति मे मतिः॥
en: Determined as I am to fight, it behaves you, O sire, to accord me your permission. With your permission, O hero, I intend to fight.

sn: दुरुक्तं विप्रतीपं वा रभसाच्चापलात् तथा। यन्मयेह कृतं किंचित् तन्मे त्वं क्षन्तुमर्हसि॥
en: It also befits you, to forgive me any cruel word I might have uttered against you at any time, as also any act injurious to you, that I might have done, through malice or fickleness.

sn: भीष्म उवाच न चेच्छक्यमवस्रष्टुं वैरमेतत् सुदारुणम्। अनुजानामि कर्ण त्वां युद्ध्यस्व स्वर्गकाम्यया॥
en: Bhishma said If indeed you can not cast off the fierce hostility you have imbibed against the Pandavas, then O Karna, I accord you my permission. Fight, actuated by a desire for attaining paradise.

sn: निर्मन्युर्गतसंरम्भः कृतकर्मा रणे स्म ह। यथाशक्ति यथोत्साहं सतां वृत्तेषु वृत्तवान्।॥
en: Free from wrath and malice, do you carry out the commissions of the king, to the best of your abilities and energies, and observant of the conduct of the righteous.

sn: अहं त्वामनुजानामि यदिच्छसि तदाप्नुहि। क्षत्रधर्मजिताल्लोकानवाप्स्यसि धनंजयात्॥
en: I do accord you my unqualified permission; attain what you desire to attain. Through the instrumentality of Dhananjaya, you shall attain to those (posthumous) regions that are secured by the observance of a Kshatriya's duties.

sn: युध्यस्व निरहङ्कारो बलवीर्यव्यपाश्रयः। धाद्धि युद्धाच्छ्रेयोऽन्यत् क्षत्रियस्य न विद्यते॥
en: Casting off arrogance and depending on your own prowess and strength, engage yourself in the fight; for what is there more desirable to a Kshatriya than a righteous battle?

sn: प्रशमे हि कृतो यत्नः सुमहान् सुचिरं मया। न चैव शकितः कर्तुं कर्ण सत्यं ब्रवीमि ते॥
en: For long and strenuously, did I strive to bring about peace. But I failed to accomplish the task; this, O Karna, I tell you forsooth.

sn: संजय उवाच इत्युक्तवति गाङ्गेये अभिवाद्योपमन्त्र्य च। राधेयो रथमारुह्य प्रायात् तव सुतं प्रति॥
en: Sanjaya said When Ganga's son had thus spoken, the son of Radha, having saluted and propitiated the former, mounted his chariot and drove towards the pavilion of your son.

sn: नारायणं नमस्कृत्य नरं चैव नरोत्तमम्। देवी सरस्वतीं व्यासं ततो जयमुदीरयेत्।।
en: Having saluted the Supreme Deity (Narayana) and the highest of all male beings Nara and also the Goddess of Learning (Sarasvati), let us cry "Success"!

sn: तमप्रतिमसत्त्वौजोबलवीर्यसमन्वितम्। हतं देवव्रतं श्रुत्वा पाञ्चाल्येन शिखण्डिना॥ धृतराष्ट्रस्ततो राजा शोकव्याकुललोचनः। किमचेष्टत विप्रर्षे हते पितरि वीर्यवान्॥
en: Janamejaya said Hearing that his sire Devavrata of unequaled might, energy, sturdiness, prowess and vigour, had been slain by Sikhandin the son of Panchala. O Brahmanical sage, what did the very powerful monarch Dhritarashtra with eyes blinded with fast-falling tears, do?

sn: तस्य पुत्रो हि भगवन् भीष्मद्रोणमुखै रथैः। पराजित्य महेष्वासान् पाण्डवान् राज्यमिच्छति॥
en: His son, O worshipful one, desired to obtain monarchy after having defeated the mighty warriors, the sons of Pandu, through the assistance of Bhima, Drona and other such heroes.

sn: तस्मिन् हते तु भगवन् केतौ सर्वधनुष्मताम्। यदचेष्टत कौरव्यस्तन्मे ब्रूहि तपोधन॥
en: O illustrious ascetic, tell me all that the foremost of the Kuru dynasty did, when that chief of all bowmen (Bhima) had been killed.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच निहतं पितरं श्रुत्वा धृतराष्ट्रो जनाधिपः। लेभे न शान्तिं कौरव्यश्चिन्ताशोकपरायणः॥
en: Vaishampayana said Having heard that his sire (Bhishma) had been slain in battle, that ruler of men, Dhritarashtra of the Kuru dynasty knew no rest of mind, being worn out with anxiety and Sorrow.

sn: तस्य चिन्तयतो दुःखमनिशं पार्थिवस्य तत्। आजगाम विशुद्धात्मा पुनर्गावल्गणिस्तदा॥
en: When that foremost of the Kurus had been thus brooding over his grief, there came again to him the pure-souled son of Gavalgani.

sn: शिबिरात् संजयं प्राप्तं निशि नागाह्वयं पुरम्। आम्बिकेयो महाराज धृतराष्ट्रोऽन्वपृच्छत॥
en: O great king, Dhritarashtra, the son of Ambika, then thus questioned Sanjaya who had that night returned from the camp of the city named after the elephant.

sn: श्रुत्वा भीष्मस्य निधनमप्रहृष्टमना भृशम्। पुत्राणां जयमाकाङ्क्षन् विललापातुरो यथा॥
en: Hearing of the death of Bhishma, he became exceedingly cheerless and longing for the victory of his sons, he broke out into lamentations like one sorely distressed.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच संशोच्य तु महात्मानं भीष्मं भीमपराक्रमम्। किमकार्षुः परं तात कुरुः कालचोदिताः॥
en: Dhritarashtra said O son, having bewailed the high-souled Bhima of terrific might, what did the Kurus, goaded by Destiny, do?

sn: तस्मिन् विनिहते शूरे दुराधर्षे महात्मनि। किं नु स्वित् कुरोऽकार्पुर्निमग्नाः शोकसागरे॥
en: When that unconquerable and high-souled hero was slain, what, for sooth, did the Kurus, deep down into the sea of sorrow, do?

sn: तदुदीर्णं महत् सैन्यं त्रैलोक्यस्यापि संजय। भयमुत्पादयेत् तीव्र पाण्डवानां महात्मनाम्॥ को हि दौर्योधने सैन्ये पुमानासीन्महारथः। यं प्राप्य समरे वीरा न त्रस्यन्ति महाभये॥
en: Verily, O Sanjaya, the innumerable and excellent army of the high-souled sons of Pandu, can strike the worlds with keenest apprehension. In this terrific battle, was any great car-warrior in the troop of Duryodhana who was fearless?

sn: संजय उवाच देवव्रते तु निहते कुरूणामृषभे तदा। किमकार्ष पतयस्तन्ममाचक्ष्व संजय॥
en: Sanjaya said Therefore, O Sanjaya, recount to me what the kings did, when Devarata, the foremost of the Kurus, had been slain.

sn: शृणु राजन्नेकमना वचनं ब्रुवतो मम। यत् ते पुत्रास्तदाऽकार्युर्हते देवव्रते मृधे॥
en: Hear, O monarch, with singleness of mind, the words, falling from my lips, regarding what your sons did when Devavrata had fallen.

sn: निहते तु तदा भीष्मे राजन् सत्यपराक्रमे। तावकाः पाण्डवेयाश्च प्राध्यायन्त पृथक् पृथक्॥
en: 0 monarch, when Bhishma of invincible prowess had been slain, your own warriors and also those of the Pandava host, began to think of the duties of the Kshatriya sect; and,

sn: विस्मिताश्च प्रहृष्टाश्च क्षत्रधर्मं निशम्य ते। स्वधर्म निन्दमानास्ते प्रणिपत्य महात्मने॥ शयनं कल्पयामासुर्भीष्मायामितकर्मणे। सोपधानं नरव्याघ्र शरैः संनतपर्वभिः॥
en: o lord of men, at the thought, they wondered and were delighted; and in obedience to their sectarian duties, they bowed down to the illustrious Bhishma. Then those foremost of men prepared for Bhishma of infinite energy a bed furnished with a pillow, made of close-knotted arrows.

sn: विधाय रक्षां भीष्माय समाभाष्य परस्परम्। अनुमान्य च गाङ्गेयं कृत्वा चापि प्रदक्षिणम्॥ क्रोधसंरक्तनयनाः समवेत्य परस्परम्। पुनर्युद्धाय निर्जग्मुः क्षत्रियाः कालचोदिताः॥
en: Having arranged for Bhishma's safety and having greeted one another, and with the permission of the son of Ganga and having circumambulated him and looking at each other with eyes coppery with anger, those Kshatriyas, goaded by Destiny, again issued forth for fighting with one another.

sn: ततस्तूर्यनिनादैश्च भेरीणां निनदेन च। तावकानामनीकानि परेषां च विनिर्ययुः॥
en: Then to the voice of the trumpets and to the roar of the drums, the army of your sons and that of their adversaries, formed in battle-array.

sn: व्यावृत्तेऽर्यम्णि राजेन्द्र पतिते जाह्नवीसुते। अमर्षवशमापन्नाः कालोपहतचेतसः॥ अनादृत्य वचः पथ्यं गाङ्गेयस्य महात्मनः। निर्ययुर्भरतश्रेष्ठाः शस्त्राण्यादाय सत्वराः॥
en: When, O greatest of kings, the son of Janhavi (Bhishma) had fallen and when the greater part of the day had worn out, these foremost of the Bharata race, overpowered by the influence of their wrath, and having their reasons bewildered through fate and neglecting the salutary counsel of the illustrious son of Ganga, came out in haste grasping their weapons.

sn: मोहात् तव सपुत्रस्य वधाच्छान्तनवस्य च। कौरव्या मृत्युसाद्भूताः सहिताः सर्वराजभिः॥
en: Owing to your own foolishness and that of your sons and owing to the death of the son of Shantanu, the descendants of the Kuru race together with all the (assembled) kings, appeared to be summoned by the God of death.

sn: अजावय इवागोपा वने श्वापदसंकुले। भृशमुद्विग्नमनसो हीना देवव्रतेन ते॥
en: Like a herd of goats without a herdsman in wood infested with beasts of prey, they were exceedingly oppressed with fear, being deprived of Devavrata.

sn: पतिते भरतश्रेष्ठे बभूव कुरुवाहिनी। द्यौरिवापेतनक्षत्रा हीनं खमिव वायुना॥ विपन्नसस्येव मही वाक् चैवासंस्कृता तथा। आसुरीव यथा सेना निगृहीते नृपे बलौ॥
en: On the fall of that foremost of the Bharata race, the army of the Kurus resembled the heavenly dome stripped of the stars or the sky deprived of the atmosphere; or the earth with her crops blighted; or a discourse teeming with unrefined expressions; or the army of the Asuras when in the days of yore, Bali had been (thoroughly) humiliated.

sn: विधवेव वरारोहा शुष्कतोयेव निम्नगा। वृकैरिव वने रुद्धा पृषती हतयूथपा॥ शरभाहतसिंहेव महती गिरिकन्दरा। भारती भरतश्रेष्ठे पतिते जाह्नवीसुते॥
en: Or a charming lady deprived of her lord; a stream the waters of which had been dried up; or a doe deprived of her mate, surrounded by wolves in the forest or the wide, extended, mountain-cave having its lion slain by the fabulous Sarabha. Or the slaughter of Janhavi's son, O foremost of the Bharata race, the army of the Bharatas.

sn: विश्वग्वाताहता रुग्णा नौरिवासीन्महार्णवे। बलिभिः पाण्डवैरीरैर्लब्धलक्ष शार्दिता॥
en: Resembled a tiny bark thrown up and down on the bosom of the mighty main, driven by the gale rushing from all sides. It was then greatly harassed by the powerful Pandavas heroes of infallible aims.

sn: सा तदाऽऽसीद् भृशं सेना व्याकुलाश्वरथद्विपा। विपन्नभूयिष्ठनरा कृपणा ध्वस्तमानसा॥
en: Then that host, with its elephants, horses and car-warriors, was much distressed and exceedingly jeopardised and rendered helpless and terror-stricken.

sn: तस्यां त्रस्ता नृपतयः सैनिकाश्च पृथग्विधाः। पाताल इव मज्जन्तो हीना देवव्रतेन ते॥
en: Then, in that army, bereft of Devavrata, the kings and the (common) soldiers, individually struck with panic, seemed to be sinking into the nethermost regions.

sn: कर्णे हि कुरवोऽस्मार्षुः स हि देवव्रतोपमः। सर्वशस्त्रभृतां श्रेष्ठं रोचमानमिवातिथिम्॥ बन्धुमापद्गतस्येव तमेवोपागमन्मनः। चक्रुशुः कर्ण कर्णेति तत्र भारत पार्थिवाः॥
en: Thereafter the Kauravas remembered Karna, who was equal to Devavrata himself and who was the foremost of all wielders of weapons and resplendent like a guest. Then like the heart of a distressed person looking for a friend, their hearts turned towards him (Karna); and, O Bharata, the kings then broke out into exclamations saying, "O Karna, O Karna."

sn: राधेयं हितमस्माकं सूतपुत्रं तनुत्यजम्। स हि नायुध्यत तदा दशाहानि महायशाः॥ सामात्यबन्धुः कर्णो वै तमानयत मा चिरम्। भीष्मेण हि महाबाहुः सर्वक्षत्रस्य पश्यतः॥ रथेषु गण्यमानेषु बलविक्रमशालिषु। संख्यातोऽर्धरथः कर्णोद्विगुणः सन्नरर्षभः॥
en: That son of Radha, that benefactor of ours, that progeny of Suta, he that will sacrifice his life in battle, that one of illustrious renown with his followers and friends, has refrained from fighting these ten days; summon him without delay. That foremost of men, that hero of mighty arms, Karna, had been reckoned by Bhishma as only an Ardharatha, in the presence of all the Kshatriyas, during the tale of car-warriors of valour and prowess, in spite of his being equal to two Maharathas.

sn: स्थातिरथसंख्यायां योऽग्रणीः शूरसम्मतः। सासुरानपि देवेशान् रणे यो योद्धमुत्सहेत्॥
en: Indeed in that enumeration of Rathas and Atirathas, Karna was thus reckoned-Karna who is the foremost (of all fighters), who is held in high respect by the heroes and who would dare give battle even to Yama, Kubera, Varuna and Indra.

sn: स तु तेनैव कोपेन राजन् गाङ्गेयमुक्तवान्। त्वयि जीवति कौरव्य नाहं योत्स्ये कदाचन॥ त्वया तु पाण्डवेयेषु निहतेषु महामृधे। दुर्योधनमनुज्ञाप्य वनं यास्यामि कौरव॥
en: Out of wrath (excited by this classification of himself, he had thus addressed, O king, the son of Ganga-'O Kaurava, I will not fight so long as you live; if you shall slay in battle the Sons of Pandu, O you of Kuru'a race, I will retire into the woods with the permission of Duryodhana.

sn: पाण्डवैर्वा हते भीष्मे त्वयि स्वर्गमुपेयुषि। हन्तास्येकरथेनैव कृत्स्नान् यान् मन्यसे रथान्॥
en: If, O Bhisma, on the contrary, you, being slain by the Pandavas, are transported to heaven, then will I, riding on a single car, slay those whom you consider to be the mightiest of all car-warriors.

sn: एवमुक्त्वा महाबाहुर्दशाहानि महायशाः। नायुध्यत ततः कर्णः पुत्रस्य तव सम्मते॥
en: Having thus spoken, the mighty-armed Karna of illustrious renown, refrained, with the perinission of your son, from taking part in the battle for these ten days.

sn: भीष्मः समरविक्रान्तः पाण्डवेयस्य भारत। जघान समरे योधानसंख्येयपराक्रमः॥
en: 0 Bharata, Bhishma of immeasurable prowess, displaying his might in battle, slew a large number of warriors of the Pandava host in that (sanguinary) engagement.

sn: तस्मिंस्तु निहते शूरे सत्यसंधे महौजसि। त्वत्सुता: कर्णमस्मार्पुस्ततुकामा इव प्लवम्॥
en: On the fall of that most powerful hero of linerring aim, your sons remembered Karna, like persons desirous of crossing the ocean) remembering a raft.

sn: तावकास्तव पुत्राश्च सहिताः सर्वराजभिः। हा कालोऽयमिति चाब्रुवन्॥
en: Your sons and the warriors of your party, together with the (assembled) monarchs then, began to bewail saying 'Karna' they also said 'It is time for you to come.'

sn: एवं ते स्म हि राधेयं सूतपुत्रं तनुत्यजम्। चुक्रुशुः सहिता योधास्तत्र तत्र महाबलाः॥.
en: Thus all the warriors endued with great prowess, bewailed on the dead body of Karna, the son of Suta and Radha.

sn: जामदग्न्याभ्यनुज्ञातमस्त्रे दुर्वारपौरुषम्। आगमन्नो मनः कर्णे बन्धुमात्यमिकेष्विव॥ कर्ण इति चाक्रन्दन्
en: As during emergencies the heart flies to a friend, so our hearts then flew to Karna of irrepressible manhood who had acquired his knowledge of weapons from the son of Jamadagni.

sn: स हि शक्तो रणे राजंस्त्रातुमस्मान् महाभयात्। त्रिदशानिव गोविन्दः सततं सुमहाभयात्॥
en: O monarch, he only was capable of saving us from the great dangers of battle, iike Govinda protecting the celestials from all calamities.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच तथा तु संजयं कर्णे कीर्तयन्तं पुनः पुनः। आशीविषवदुच्छ्वस्य धृतराष्ट्रोऽब्रवीदिदम्॥
en: Vaishampayana said Thereupon breathing (heavily) out like a snake, Dhritarashtra spoke these words to Sanjaya who had been thus repeatedly extolling Karna.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच यत् तद्वैकर्तनं कर्णमगमद् वो मनस्तदा। अप्यपश्यत राधेयं सूतपूत्रं तनुत्धजम्॥
en: Dhritarashtra said As your heart then were drawn to wards Karna, the son of Vikartana, you surely saw that son of Radha, that descendant of Suta, who was ever-ready to lay down his life for you.

sn: अपि तन्न मृषाकार्षीत् कच्चित् सत्यपराक्रमः। सम्भ्रान्तानां तदार्तानां त्रस्तानां त्राणमिच्छताम्॥
en: Did that Karna, of infallible prowess in battle, disappoint Duryodhana and his brothers, who had been all exceedingly distressed, panicstruck and anxious for being extricated from their difficulties?

sn: अपि तत् पूरयांचक्रे धनुर्धरवरो युधि। यत्तद् विनिहते भीष्मे कौरवाणामपाकृतम्॥
en: Was that foremost of bowmen in battle capable of filling up the void created by the fall of Bhishma, the shelter of the Kurus?

sn: तत् खण्डं पूरयन् कर्णः परेषामादधद् भयम्। स हि वै पुरुषव्याघ्रो लोके संजय कथ्यते॥
en: Supplying the gap, was Karna successful in striking terror into the hearts of the enemy? Therefore, it is said, O Sanjaya! he is the lion among the men.

sn: आर्तानां बान्धवानां च क्रन्दतां च विशेषतः। परित्यज्य रणे प्राणांस्तत्त्राणार्थं च शर्म च। कृतवान् मम पुत्राणां जयाशां सफलामपि॥
en: Renouncing his breaths in battle field, for protecting the helpless, distressed and roaring our relatives, did he also succeed in fructifying the hopes of victory cherished by my sons? Supplying the gap, was Karna successful in striking terror into the hearts of the enemy? Therefore, it is said, O Sanjaya! he is the lion among the men.

sn: आर्तानां बान्धवानां च क्रन्दतां च विशेषतः। परित्यज्य रणे प्राणांस्तत्त्राणार्थं च शर्म च। कृतवान् मम पुत्राणां जयाशां सफलामपि॥
en: Renouncing his breaths in battle field, for protecting the helpless, distressed and roaring our relatives, did he also succeed in fructifying the hopes of victory cherished by my sons?

sn: संजय उवाच हतं भीष्मथाधिरथिर्विदित्वा भिन्नां नावमिवात्यगाधे कुरूणाम्। सोदर्यवद् व्यसनात् सूतपुत्रः संतारयिष्यंस्तव पुत्रस्य सेनाम्॥
en: Sanjaya said Then Adhiratha's son of the Suta caste, knowing that Bhisma had fallen, became desirous of saving, like a brother, the army of your son from the calamity it was in, like a boat split in the midst of the unfathomable deep.

sn: श्रुत्वा तु कर्णः पुरुषेन्द्रमच्युतं निपातितं शान्तनवं महारथम्। अथोपयायात् सहसारिकर्षणो धनुर्धराणां प्रवरस्तदा नृप॥
en: Having heard that the son of Shantanu, that foremost of men, the never-dropping one and the best of all car-warriors, had been slain, O king, Karna the repressor of enemies and the foremost of all bowmen, speedily arrived at the field of battle.

sn: निमज्जती नावमिवार्णवे कुरून्। पितेव पुत्रांस्त्वरितोऽभ्ययात् ततः संतारयिष्यंस्तव पुत्रस्य सेनाम्॥
en: When that excellent of car-warriors, Bhishma had been slain by the enemy, Karna soon (came of the battle field), desirous of saving the army of your son resembling a boat sunk in the deep, like a father anxious for rescuing his sons.

sn: कर्ण उवाच यस्मिन् धृतिर्बुद्धिपराक्रमौजः सत्यं स्मृतिर्वीरगुणाश्च सर्वे। अस्त्राणि दिव्यान्यथ संलतिहीं: प्रिया च वागनसूया च भीष्मे॥ सदा कृतज्ञे द्विजशत्रुघातके सनातनं चन्द्रमसीव लक्ष्म। स चेत् प्रशान्तः परवीरहन्ता मन्ये हतानेव च सर्ववीरान्॥
en: Karna said When that Bhishma, who was endued with resoluteness, intelligence, prowess, energy, truthfulness, self-control and with all the other attributes of a hero; who was proficient in the use of celestial weapons; in whom there were humility, bashfulness, sweet speech and harmlessness; who was always grateful, the slayer of the enemies of the twice-borns, in whom there resided all these virtues for ever that Bhishma the destroyer of hostilc heroes had obtained his quietus, I consider the remaining warriors as already slain.

sn: नेह ध्रुवं किंचन जातु विद्यते लोके ह्यस्मिन् कर्मणोऽनित्ययोगात्। सूर्योदये को हि विमुक्तसंशयो भावं कुर्वीतार्य महाव्रते हते॥
en: Owing to the constant connection with action, there is nothing in this world that is eternal. When that one of illustrious vows (Bhishma) has been killed today, what man can say with certitude that today, what man can say with certitude that tomorrow the sun will rise?

sn: वसुप्रभावे वसुवीर्यसम्भवे गते वसूनेव वसुन्धराधिपे। वसूनि पुत्रांश्च वसुन्धरां तथा कुरूंश्च शोचध्वमिनां च वाहिनीम्॥
en: When that one of prowess equal to that of the Vasus, when he that was born of the energy of the Vasus, when that ruler of earth has gone back to the Vasus, do you then lament for your wealth, your sons and this army?

sn: संजय उवाच महाप्रभावे वरदे निपातिते लोकेश्वरे शास्तरि चामितौजसि। पराजितेषु भरतेषु दुर्मनाः कर्णो भृशंन्यश्वसदश्रु वर्तयन्॥
en: Sanjaya said When that giver of boons, that most puicsant hero, that lord of men, that one of great vigour had been slain, that when the Bharatas had been vanquished, Karna, with a sorrowful heart and shedding copious tears, began to comfort (the Kurus).

sn: इदं च राधेयवचो निशम्य सुताश्च राजंस्तव सैनिकाश्च ह। स्तदाश्रु नेत्रैर्मुमुचुश्च शब्दवत्॥ प्रवर्तमाने तु पुनर्महाहवे विगाह्यमानासु चमूषु पार्थिवैः। अथाब्रवीद्धर्षकरं तदा वचो रथर्षभान् सर्वमहारथर्षभः॥
en: Having heard, O monarch, these wordr of the son of Radha, your sons and your soldiers, out of grief, broke out into loud lamentations and shed tears from their eyes, which were as copious as their wails were loud. When the sanguinary engagement waged anew and the Kaurava host led by kings once more roared forth (their battle-cry), then that foremost of all Maharathis (Karna) addressed these words to the mighty car-warriors, that imparted joy to their hearts.

sn: जगत्यनित्ये सततं प्रधावति प्रचिन्तयनस्थिरमद्य लक्षये। भवत्सु तिष्ठत्स्विह पातितो मृधे गिरिप्रकाशः कुरुपुङ्गवः कथम्॥
en: This transient words is ever flying (towards death); considering this I always regard everything as unsteady. When you were all present here, how could that foremost of the Kurus (Bhishma), who resembled a mountain in steadiness, be slain in battle?

sn: निपातिते शान्तनवे महारथे दिवाकरे भूतलमास्थिते यथा। न पार्थिवाः सोढुमलं धनंजयं गिरिप्रवोढारमिवालिनं दुमाः॥
en: When like the sun dropping down on the earth, that foremost of car-warriors, the son of Shantanu has fallen, the monarchs (of the Kuru army) are hardly capable of withstanding Dhananjaya, like trees unable to withstand the hurricane that uproots even the hills.

sn: हतप्रधानं त्विदमार्तरूपं परैर्हतोत्साहमनाथमद्य वै। मया कुरूणां परिपाल्यमाहवे बलं यथा तेन महात्मना तथा॥
en: As that high-minded one did, so today will I protect, in this dreadful battle, this army of the Kurus, whose appearance is cheerless and whose zeal has been destroyed by the enemy, which is helpless and whose best warriors have already been slain.

sn: समाहितं चात्मनि भारमीदृशं जगत् तथानित्यमिदं च लक्षये। निपातितं चाहवशौण्डमाहवे कथं नु कुर्यामहमीदृशे भयम्॥
en: This heavy burden now devolves on myself; I shall that this world is transitory. That most excellent of warriors has also fallen in battle. Why shall I then entertain any apprehension for fighting?

sn: अहं तु तान् कुरुवृषभानजिह्मगैः प्रवेशयन् यमसदनं चरन् रणे। यशः परं जगति विभाव्य वर्तिता परैर्हतो भुवि शयिताऽथवा पुनः॥
en: Coursing (swiftly) in the battle-field, I shall send, by means of my straight-going shafts, to the abode of Death, the foremost descendants of Kuru's race (Pandavas). Considering fame to be the best of all worldly possessions, I shall kill them in the engagement or myself lie on the field being slain by them.

sn: युधिष्ठिरो धृतिमतिसत्यसत्त्ववान् वृकोदरो गजशततुल्यविक्रमः। तथाऽर्जुनस्त्रिदशवरात्मजो युवा न तद्बलं सुजयमिहामरैरपि॥
en: Yudhishthira is endued with resoluteness, intelligence, piety and vigour; Vrikodara equals a hundred elephants in might; Arjuna also is youthful and the begotten son of the foremost of celestials; so the army belonging to them is not to be easily vanquished even by the immortals.

sn: यमौ रणे यत्र यमोपमौ बले ससात्यकिर्यत्र च देवकीसुतः। न तद्बलं कापुरुषोऽभ्युपेयिवान् निवर्तते मृत्युमुखान्न चासुभृत्॥
en: As no one ever returns alive from the jaws of death, so no coward ever returns (alive) after having confronted that hostile army to which belong the twins (Nakula and Sahadeva), each resembling death himself in battle and in which are Satyaki and the son of Devaki.

sn: तपोऽभ्युदीर्णं तपसैव बाध्यते बलं बलेनैव तथा मनस्विभिः। मनश्च मे शत्रुनिवारणे ध्रुवं स्वरक्षणे चाचलवद् व्यवस्थितम्॥
en: Great power, begot of austerities, should be opposed by ascetic wealth. So should the wise oppose might with might. My mind is decided upon withstanding the enemy and it is resolutely fixed upon ensuring the safety (of my own troops).

sn: एवं चैषां वाधमानः प्रभावं गत्वैवाहं ताञ्चयाम्यद्य सूत। मित्रद्रोहो मर्षणीयो न मेऽयं भग्ने सैन्ये यः समेयात् स मित्रम्॥
en: For certain, O charioteer, I shall today oppose their force and shall defeat them by simply going to the field. This conflict of friends (internecine war) ought not to be tolerated by men. He that helps in rallying a routed army is the true friend.

sn: कर्तास्म्येतत् सत्पुरुषार्यकर्म त्यक्त्वा प्राणाननुयास्यामि भीष्मम्। सर्वान् संख्ये शत्रुसंघान् हनिष्ये हतस्तैर्वा वीरलोकं प्रपत्स्ये॥
en: I shall either achieve this pious act of manliness or shall follow Bhishma, renouncing my vital breaths. I shall either slay in battle my myriad enemies or slain by them I shall attain to the posthumous regions of the heroes.

sn: सम्प्राक्रुष्टे रुदितस्त्रीकुमारे पराहते पौरुषे धार्तराष्ट्र। मया कृत्यमिति जानामि सूत तस्माद् राज्ञस्त्वद्य शत्रून् विजेष्ये॥
en: I regard, indeed, this to be my bounden duty, O charioteer, when women and infants wail aloud for assistance and when Dhartarastra's pride has been humiliated. So I shall this day conquer the enemies of the monarch (Duryodhana)

sn: स्त्यक्त्वा प्राणान् घोररूपे रणेऽस्मिन्। सर्वान् संख्ये शत्रुसंघान् निहत्य दास्याम्यहं धार्तराष्ट्राय राज्यम्॥
en: Preserving the Kurus and massacring the sons of Pandu even at the cost of my very life in this dreadful fight and dispatching to Death my myriad enemies in this battle, I shall bestow this monarchy the of Dhritarashtra.

sn: निबध्यतां मे कवचं विचित्रं हैमं शुभं मणिरत्लावभासि। शिरस्त्राणं चार्कसमानभासं धनुः शरांश्चग्निविषाहिकल्पान्॥
en: Fasten on me this magnificent, golden and resplendent armour radiant with gems and jewels. Let also my helmet lustrous like the sun and my bows and arrows resembling fire, poison or serpents, be donned. on son

sn: उपासङ्गान् षोडश योजयन्तु धनूंषि दिव्यानि तथाऽऽहरन्तु। असींश्च शक्तीश्च गदाश्च गुर्वीः शङ्ख च जाम्वूनदचित्रनालम्॥
en: Fasten sixteen quivers (to my chariot); fetch strongest bows and also arrows, spears, heavy maces and my conch with its body variegated with gold.

sn: इमां रौक्मी नागकक्ष्यां विचित्रां ध्वजं चित्रं दिव्यमिन्दीवराङ्कम्। श्लक्ष्णैर्वस्त्रौर्विप्रमृज्यानयन्तु चित्रां मालां चारुबद्धां सलाजाम्॥
en: Procure also my standard, variegated, beautiful, magnificent, made of gold, burning with the luster of a lotus, bearing the emblem of the elephant's girth, after having cleansed it with a fine piece of cloth and having decorated it with festoons of flowers and a net-work of fine wires.

sn: अश्वानग्यान् पाण्डुराभ्रप्रकाशान् पुष्टान् स्नातान् मन्त्रपूताभिरद्भिः। शीघ्राच्छीघ्रं सूतपुत्रानयस्व॥
en: O son a charioteer, bring me also, in all haste, fleetest horses, of the colour of to tawny clouds, stout, washed with water hallowed by mantras and decorated with rich caparisons made of effulgent gold.

sn: रथं चायं हेममालावनद्धं रत्नैचित्रं सूर्यचन्द्रप्रकाशैः। हैर्युक्तं तूर्णमावर्तयस्व॥
en: Procure, in all haste, a chariot, most magnificent, festooned with garlands of gold, adorned with gems resembling the Sun and the Moon, furnished with all necessary objects and offensive weapons and yoked with lusty horses.

sn: चित्राणि चापानि च वेगवन्ति ज्याश्चोत्तमाः संनहनोपपन्नाः। मासाद्य गात्रावरणानि चैव॥ भेरी:॥
en: Bring me also beautiful bows of great toughness and bow-strings of finest make, capable of throwing (arrows at great distances) and some large quivers well-stuffed with shafts and several cuirasses (to cover my person).

sn: प्रायात्रिकं चानयताशु सर्वं दना पूर्ण वीर कांस्यं च हैमम्। आनीय मालामवबध्य चाङ्गे प्रवादयन्त्वाशु जयाय ॥
en: O hero, bring speedily all auspicious articles required at the time of setting ous (for battle) and brass and golden vessel filled with curds. Bring garlands of flowers and decorate my person with them; strike up, also, kettledrums for victory.

sn: प्रयाहि सूताशु यतः किरीटी वृकोदरो धर्मसुतो ममौ च। तान् वा हनिष्यामि समेत्य संख्ये भीष्माय गच्छामि हतो द्विषद्भिः॥
en: Drive, O charioteer, quickly thither where Kiritin (diadem-decked), Vrikodara, the virtuous Yudhishthira and the twins are. Confronting them either I shall slay them or being slain in battle by the foes, I shall follow Bhishma.

sn: यस्मिन् राजा सत्यधृतियुधिष्ठिरः समास्थितो भीमसेनार्जुनौ च। वासुदेवः सात्यकिः सुंजयाश्च मन्ये बलं तदजय्यं महीपैः॥
en: That host to which belongs, Yudhishthira, firm in truth, in which are Bhima and Arjuna and which contains the son of Vasudeva, Satyaki and the Srinjayas, that host I consider to incapable of being vanquished by these monarchs.

sn: तं चेन्मृत्युः सर्वहरोऽभिरक्षेत् सदाप्रमत्तः समरे किरीटिनम्। तथापि हन्ताऽस्मि समेत्य संख्ये यास्यामि वा भीष्मपथा यमाय॥
en: Even if all-devouring Death were to guard Arjuna in the encounter. with the utmost heed, still would I slay him confronting him in battle; or myself hie to the regions of Death following the trail of Bhishma.

sn: न त्वेवाहं न गमिष्यामि तेषां मध्ये शूराणां तत्र चाहं ब्रवीमि। मित्रQहो दुर्बलभक्तयो ये पापात्मानो न ममैते सहायाः॥
en: It is not that, I say, that I shall not go amidst those heroes. Those that sow dissension's among friends, that are of veering devotion and of impious souls those are not my allies.

sn: संजय उवाच समृद्धिमन्तं रथमुत्तमं दृढं सकूबरं हेमपरिष्कृतं शुभम्। र्युक्तं समास्थाय ययौ जयाय॥
en: Sanjaya said Karna then drove out for victory, mounting excellent chariot, most lavishly furnished, invulnerable, with a magnificent pole, adorned with gold, auspicious, with (fluttering) penons and to which harnessed steeds fleet like the wind.

sn: सम्पूज्यमानः कुरुभिर्महात्मा रथर्षभो देवगणैर्यथेन्द्रः। ययौ तदायोधनमुग्रधन्वा यत्रावसानं भरतर्षभस्या।३५।। वरूथिना महता सध्वजेन सुवर्णमुक्तामणिरत्नमालिना। सदश्वयुक्तेन रथेन कर्णो मेघस्वनेनार्क इवामितौजाः॥
en: Worshipped by the best of the car-warriors of the Kuru party, like Indra by the immortals, that high-souled and most terrible of all wielders of bow, endowed with immeasurable vigour like the sun himself,-riding on his chariot decorated with gold, gems and jewels, mounted with a magnificent standard, to which were harnessed finest animals and the rattle of which resembled the rumbling of clouds, went, attended by a mighty host, to the battle-field where that foremost of the Bharata race (Bhishma) had obtained his quietus.

sn: हुताशनाभः स हुताशनप्रभे शुभः शुभे वै स्वरथे धनुर्धरः। स्थितो रराजाधिरथिर्महारथः स्वयं विमाने सुरराडिवास्थितः॥
en: Then that son of Adhiratha, the mighty bowman and warrior Karna, blessed with a handsome appearance and effulgent like fire, riding on his Own auspicious chariot resplendent like fire, shone like the monarch of the celestials himself riding on his own heavenly chariot.

sn: संजय उवाच शरतल्पे महात्मानं शयानममितौजसम्। महावातसमूहेन समुद्रमिव शोषितम्॥ दृष्ट्वा पितामह भीष्मं सर्वक्षत्रान्तकं गुरुम्। दिव्यैरस्त्रैर्महेश्वासं पातितं सव्यसाचिना॥ जयाशा तव पुत्राणां सम्भग्ना शर्म वर्म च। अपाराणामिव द्वीपमगाधे गाधमिच्छताम्॥ स्रोतसा यामुनेनेव शरौघेण परिप्लुतम्। महेन्द्रेणेव मैनाकमसह्यं भुवि पातितम्॥ नभश्च्युतमिवादित्यं पतितं धरणीतले। शतकतुमिवाचिन्त्यं पुरु वृत्रेण निर्जितम्॥ मोहनं सर्वसैन्यस्य युधि भीष्मस्य पातनम्। ककुदं सर्वसैन्यानां लक्ष्म सर्वधनुष्मताम्॥ धनंजयशरैर्व्याप्तं पितरं ते महाव्रतम्। तं वीरशयने वीरं शयानं पुरुषर्षभम्॥ भीष्ममाधिरथिदृष्ट्वा भरतानां महाद्युतिः। अवतीर्य रथादा” वाष्पव्याकुलिताक्षरम्॥
en: Sanjaya said Seeing the most worshipful champion, the high-souled grandsire Bhishma of immeasurable prowess, the death of all Kshatriyas, lie on a bed of arrows and resemble the mighty main dried by violent storms, the seeing that hero dragged down from his car by the celestial weapons of Savysachin, (Arjuna), the hope your sons cherished for victory was gone as also their armours for victory was gone as also their armours and peace of mind. Seeing that one who was always like an island to persons going down into the unfathomable deep in their attempt to cross it; seeing him pierced with shafts that had flown in an uninterrupted stream like that of the Yamuna, hiin who appeared like the unbearable Menaka hurled on the earth by Mahendra; seeing that hero fallen on the surface of the earth like the sun dropped down from the heavens; seeing him who resembled the unconquerable Vritra when he had been vanquished in the days of yore by Vasava; seeing that stupifier of the consciousness of all heroes, that most excellent of champions, that foremost of all bowmen; seeing that hero an foremost of men, your father Bhishma of illustrious vows, that grandsire of the descendant of the Bharatas thrown down and lying prostrate on the field, pierced through and through by the arrows of Arjuna; seeing that hero resting on a couch worthy of a hero-the son of Adhiratha dismounted from his chariot, greatly distressed and overwhelmed with grief and with his consciousness well-nigh clouded.

sn: अभिवाद्याञ्जलिं बद्ध्वा वन्दमानोऽभ्यभाषत। कर्णोऽहमस्मि भद्रं ते वद मामभि भारत॥
en: He (Karna) walked towards him (Bhishma) on foot, distressed and with eyes blinded with fast-falling tears. Then saluting him and folding his palms and having paid his respects, Karna thus spoke. guerent stere are a anchet

sn: न नूनं सुकृतस्येह फलं कश्चित् समश्नुते॥
en: I am Karna; good betide you; speak to me, O Bharata, in auspicious and sweet language; turn your eyes on me.

sn: यत्र धर्मपरो वृद्धः शेते भुवि भवानिह। कोशसंचयने मन्त्रे व्यूहे प्रहरणेषु च॥
en: None can except to reap the fruits of his meritorious deeds here, since you, O venerable pious old man, lie prostrate on the ground being slain (by your enemies).

sn: नाहमन्यं प्रपश्यामि कुरूणां कुरुपुङ्गवा बुद्ध्या विशुद्धया युक्तो यः कुरूंस्तारयेद् भयात्।।१२
en: In replenishing the treasury, in matters of counsel, in arranging troops for battle and in the handling of arms, I do not , Oforemost of the Kurus, find any one else among the Kurus equal to you.

sn: योधांस्तु बहुधा हत्वा पितृलोकं गमिष्यति। अद्यप्रभृति संकुद्धा व्याघ्रा इव मृगक्षयम्॥
en: I do not see any one else that endued with a pure intelligence, will save the Kurus from their terror. Having slain numerous warriors, you are now repairing to the regions of the Pitris.

sn: पाण्डवा भरतश्रेष्ठ करिष्यन्ति कुरुक्षयम्। अद्य गाण्डीवधोषस्य वीर्यज्ञाः सव्यसाचिनः॥
en: O foremost of the Bharatas, from this day forward, the sons of Pandu possessed with ire, will slay the Kurus, as tigers slaughter deer.

sn: कुरुः संत्रसिष्यन्ति वज्रपाणेरिवासुराः। अद्य गाण्डीवमुक्तानामशनीनामिव स्वनः॥
en: Today the Kurus will realise the vigour of Savyasachin, who produces the twang of the Gandiva bow; today they will be frightened by him as the Asuras were frightened by the wielder of the thunderbolt.

sn: त्रासयिष्यति बाणानां कुरुनन्यांश्च पार्थिवान्। समिद्धोऽग्निर्यथा वीर महाज्वालो दुमान् दहेत्॥
en: Today the whizzle, resembling the rumble of thunders, of arrows shot from the Gandiva, will strike terror into the hearts of the Kurus and other rulers of earth.

sn: धार्तराष्ट्रान् प्रधक्ष्यन्ति तथा बाणा: किरीटिनः। येनयेन प्रसरते वाय्वग्नी सहितौ वने।॥
en: O hero, today the shafts of the diademdecked Arjuna, will burn down the sons of Dhritarashtra, just as a swelling forestconflagration of terrible flames burns down the trees.

sn: तेन तेन प्रदहतो भूरिगुल्मतृणदुमान्। यादृशौग्निः समुद्भूतस्तादृक् पार्थो न संशयः॥
en: Fire and wind coursing together, consume numerous copses, creepers and trees in that part of a forest through which they pass.

sn: यथा वायुर्नरव्याघ्र तथा कृष्णो न संशयः। नदतः पाञ्चजन्यस्य रसतो गाण्डिवस्य च॥
en: there can be no doubt that the son of Pritha is like a raging fire; and, O foremost of men, without doubt Krishna resembles the strong wind (that accompanies fire).

sn: श्रुत्वा सर्वाणि सैन्यानि त्रासं यास्यन्ति भारत। कपिध्वजस्तोत्पततो रथस्यामित्रकर्षिणः॥
en: Hearing the sound of the conch Panchajannya and the twang of the bow Gandiva, all the soldiers will be terror-stricken.

sn: शब्दं सोढुं न शक्ष्यन्ति त्वामृते वीर पार्थिवाः। को हर्जुनं योधयितुं त्वदन्यः पार्थिवोऽर्हति॥ यस्य दिव्यानि कर्माणि प्रवदन्ति मनीषिणः। अमानुषेश्च संग्रामस्त्र्यम्बकेण महात्मना॥
en: O hero, bereft of you, the monarchs will not be able to bear the rumble of the advancing chariot mounted with the banner having for its emblem the (terrible) ape, that belong to that repressor of foes (Arjuna). What other monarch, except yourself, is capable of combating with Arjuna, all whose super-human deeds the wise extol. Superhuman was indeed the combat he had with the high-souled Tryambaka (the three-eyed god).

sn: तस्माच्चैव वरं प्राप्तो दुष्प्रापमकृतात्मभिः। कोऽन्यः शक्तो रणे जेतुं पूर्वं यो न जितस्त्वया॥
en: From him did he (Arjuna) secure a boon which is difficult of being obtained by the incan-ininded. That son of Pandu ever boastful of his prowess is protected by Madhava. What other person can overcome him in battle who could not be vanquished even by you before.

sn: जितो येन रणे रामो भवता वीर्यशालिना। क्षत्रियान्तकरो घोरो देवदानवदर्पहा॥
en: You who, endowed with great prowess, had defeated in battle, Rama, that terrible destroyer of the Kshatriya race, held in high honour by the celestials and the Asuras.

sn: ममृष्यमाणो भवता चानुशिष्टः। आशीविषं दृष्टिहरं सुघोरं शूरं शक्ष्याम्यस्त्रबलानिहन्तुम्॥
en: With your permission I as I am unable to tolerate him any longer, can today slay, with the dint of my weapons, that son of Pandu, that foremost of warriors in battle who is like a serpent of virulent venom and is terrible, heroic and capable of slaying his enemies even by his very glances.

sn: संजय उवाच तस्य लालप्यतः श्रुत्वा कुरुवृद्धः पितामहः। देशकालोचितं वाक्यमब्रवीत् प्रीतमानसः॥
en: Sanjaya said When he had been thus speaking, the venerable grandsire of the Kurus, pleased with him, addressed to him these words suitable to season and place.

sn: समुद्र इव सिन्धूनां ज्योतिषामिव भास्करः। सत्यस्य च यथा सन्तो बीजानामिव चोर्वरा॥ पर्जन्य इव भूतानां प्रतिष्ठा सुहृदां भव। बान्धवास्त्वानुजीवन्तु सहस्राक्षमिवामराः॥
en: May you be the refuge of your friends, even as the ocean is the refuge of the rivers, the sun of the other planets, the pious of the truth, fertile soil of the seeds and Parjanya of the created beings. May your relations depend on you even as the immortals depend upon the thousand-eyed Indra.

sn: मानहा भव शत्रूणां मित्राणां नन्दिवर्धनः। कौरवाणां भव गतिर्यथा विष्णुर्दिवौकसाम्॥
en: May you be the humiliator of the pride of your enemies, and may you be the enhancer of the delight of your friends, the Kauravas, as Vishnu is of the denizens of heaven.

sn: स्वबाहुबलवीर्येण धार्तराष्ट्रजयैषिणा। कर्ण राजपुरं गत्वा काम्बोजा निर्जितास्त्वया॥
en: ( Karna, ever anxious to perform the pleasures of the son of Dhritarashtra, you, with the strength and vigour of your arms, did defeat the Kambojas, having goue to their country, namely Rajapura.

sn: गिरिव्रजगताश्चापि नग्नजित्प्रमुखा नृपाः। अम्बष्ठाश्च विदेहाश्च गान्धाराश्च जितास्त्वया॥
en: You also vanquished the monarchs who was stopping at Girivraja and who was headed by Nagnajit, as also the Ambasthas, the Vidchas and the Gandharvas.

sn: हिमवदुर्गनिलयाः किराता रणकर्कशाः। दुर्योधनस्य वशगास्त्वया कर्ण पूरा कृताः॥
en: O Karna, in days gone by, you brought under the authority of Duryodhana the Kiratas obstinate in battle and peopling the strongholds of the Himavat.

sn: उत्कला मेकला: पौण्ड्राः कलिङ्गान्ध्राश्च संयुगे। निषादाश्च त्रिगर्ताश्च बाह्रीकाश्च जितास्त्वया॥
en: The Utkalas, the Mekhalas, the Paundras, the Kalingas, the Nishadhas, the Trigarttas and the Valhikas, were also worsted in battle by you.

sn: तत्र तत्र च संग्रामे दुर्योधनहितैषिणा। बहवश्च जिताः कर्ण त्वया वीरा महौजसा॥
en: O Karna, desirous of doing good to Duryodhana, you defeated in battle in various lands, O hero, numerous highly vigorous clans.

sn: यथा दुर्योधनस्तात सज्ञातिकुलवान्धवः। तथा त्वमपि सर्वेषां कौरवाणां गतिर्भव॥
en: May you, O son, be the shelter of all the Kauravas, even as Duryodhana is, with his friends, relatives and kinsmen.

sn: शिवेनाभिवदामि त्वां गच्छ युध्यस्व शत्रुभिः। अनुशाधि कुरून् संख्ये धत्स्व दुर्योधने जयम्॥
en: I do bid you farewell in benedictory language; go and fight with enemy; command the Kurus in battle and secure victory for Duryodhana.

sn: भवान् पौत्रसमोऽस्माकं यथा दुर्योधनस्तथा। तवापि धर्मतः सर्वे यथा तस्य वयं तथा॥
en: Like Duryodhana, you are to us our grandson. Therefore, by the ordinances, we are the same to you as we are to him.

sn: यौनात् सम्बन्धकाल्लोके विशिष्टं संगतं सताम्। सद्भिः सह नरश्रेष्ठ प्रवदन्ति मनीषिणः॥
en: O foremost of men, the intelligent hold that in this world the connection of the pious with the pious is more closer in respect of relationship than that through the uterus.

sn: स सत्यसंगतो भूत्वा ममेदमिति निश्चितः। कुरूणां पालय बलं यथा दुर्योधनस्तथा॥
en: Therefore being faithfully united with the Kurus and believing their army to be your own, do you, like Duryodhana himself, protect it."

sn: निशम्य वचनं तस्य चरणावभिवाद्य च। ययौ वैकर्तनः कर्णः समीपं सर्वधन्विनाम्॥
en: Having heard these words of him (Bhishma) and having bowed down to his feet, Karna, the son of Vikartana, went to the place where all the bowmen were assembled.

sn: सोऽभिवीक्ष्य नरौघाणां स्थानमप्रतिमं महत्। व्यूढप्रहरणोरस्कं सैन्यं तत् समबृंहयत्॥
en: Beholding that matchless and extensive encampment of the innumerable army, Karna encouraged that host of well-accoutered and broad-chested soldiers.

sn: षिताः कुरवः सर्वे दुर्योधनपुरोगमाः। उपागतं महाबाहुं सर्वानीकपुरःसरम्॥ कर्णे दृष्ट्वा महात्मानं युद्धाय समुपस्थितम्। क्ष्वेडितास्फोटितरवैः सिंहनादरवैरपि। धनुःशब्दैश्च विविधैः कुरुः समपूजयन्॥
en: All the Kurus, having Duryodhana at their head, were greatly delighted; and seeing that mighty-armed and high-souled Karna come with the intent of battle and place himself at the command of the whole host, the Kurus welcomed him, with sounds produced by the striking of the arm-pits, with rending shouts, twang of bow-strings, roars like that of lions and diverse other kinds of sounds.

sn: संजय उवाच रथस्थं पुरुषव्याघ्रं दृष्ट्वा कर्णमवस्थितम्। हृष्टो दुर्योधनो राजन्निदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Sanjaya said O monarch, seeing that foremost of men Karna scated on his car, Duryodhana highly enraptured, spoke these words.

sn: सनाथमिव मन्येऽहं भवता पालितं बलम्। अत्र किं नु समर्थे यद्धितं तत् सम्प्रधार्यताम्॥
en: I consider this army, protected by you, to have found a suitable commander in you. Do you now decide that which will be beneficial (to this army) and which is practicable.

sn: कर्ण उवाच ब्रूहि नः पुरुषव्याघ्र त्वं हि प्राज्ञतमो नृप। यथा चार्थपतिः कृत्यं पश्यते न तथेतरः॥
en: Karna said O foremost of men, yourself speak to us, since you are the wisest of kings. A third person cannot so well descry as to what should be done, as he who is interested in any affair.

sn: ते स्म सर्वे तव वचः श्रोतुकामा नरेश्वर। नान्याय्यं हि भवान् वाक्यं ब्रूयादिति मतिर्मम॥
en: All these rulers of men are desirous of hcaring your words; and I am sure you will never speak unjust words.

sn: दुर्योधन उवाच भीष्मः सेनाप्रणेताऽऽसीद् वयसा विक्रमेण च। श्रुतेन चोपसम्पन्नः सर्वैर्योधगणैस्तथा॥ तेनातियशसा कर्ण जता शत्रुगणान् मम। सुयुद्धेन दशाहानि पालिताः स्मो महात्मना॥
en: Duryodhana said Owing to his prowess, seniority, knowledge of the Srutis and the support he obtained from all the warriors, he (Bhishma) was the leader of our host. In the fair battle of these ten days that highly glorious one of generous soul, O Karna, slew a large number of my foes and protected my own army.

sn: तस्मिन्नसुकरं कर्म कृतवत्यास्थिते दिवम्। कंन सेनाप्रणेतारं मन्यसे तदनन्तरम्॥
en: When that onc, who accomplished many difficult acts, is gone to heaven, ( Karna, whom do you consider capable of leading this host into battle)?

sn: न बिना नायकं सेना मुहूर्तमपि तिष्ठति। आहवेष्वाहवश्रेष्ठ नेतृहीनेव नौ ले॥
en: Like an unmanned boat in waters, the army cannot stand in battle even for a short while without a leader, O Karna, O you who are foremost in battle.

sn: यथा ह्यकर्णधारा नौ रथश्चासारथिर्यथा। द्रवेद् यथेष्टं तद्वत् स्याहते सेनापति बलम्॥
en: An army without a commander is like a boat with none to steer her through or like a chariot without a driver, going any where.

sn: अदेशिको यथा सार्थः सर्वः कृच्छ्रे समृच्छति। अनायका तथा सेना सर्वान् दोषान् समर्छति॥
en: Just as a foreign trader in an unknown country reaps all distress, so an army without a commander is exposed to all dangers.

sn: स भवान् वीक्ष्य सर्वेषु मामकेषु महात्मसु। पश्य सेनापतिं युक्तमनु शान्तनवादिह॥
en: Therefore do you look among all these high-souled warriors of ours and find out a proper person who may, as a commander, fill the place of Shantanu's son.

sn: यं हि सेनाप्रणेतारं भवान् वक्ष्यति संयुगे। तं वयं सहिताः सर्वे करिष्यामो न संशयः॥
en: The person, who you will consider to be fit to lead our army, in battle, will undoubtedly be chosen to be so unanimously.

sn: कर्ण उवाच सर्व एव महात्मान इमे पुरुषसत्तमाः। सेनापतित्वमर्हन्ति नात्र कार्या विचारणा॥
en: Karna said All these foremost of men of high soul are worthy of the leadership (of this host). There is no necessity for making any selection. ever one

sn: कुलसंहननज्ञानैर्बलविक्रमबुद्धिभिः। युक्ताः श्रुतज्ञा धीमन्त आहवेष्वनिवर्तिनः॥
en: All of them are perfectly acquainted with the genelogies (of princes) and with the vital parts of the body; they are possessed of prowess, might and intelligence; they are grateful, highly intelligent and unretreating from battle.

sn: युगपन्न तु ते शक्याः कर्तुं सर्वे पुरःसराः। एक एव तु कर्तव्यो यस्मिन् वैशेषिका गुणाः॥
en: But all of them cannot at the same time assume the leadership; therefore only one among them is to be chosen, in whom there reside superior qualities.

sn: अन्योन्यस्पर्धिनां होषां यद्येकं यं करिष्यसि। शेषा विमनसो व्यक्तं न योत्स्यन्ति हितास्तव॥
en: If you promote among several contending rivals, the rest, it is clear, being depressed, will not fight with a desire for doing your good.

sn: अयं च सर्वयोधानामाचार्यः स्थविरो गुरुः। यक्तः सेनापतिः कर्तुं द्रोणः शस्त्रभृतां वरः॥
en: But this foremost of all the wielders of weapons, this preceptor and teacher, of all the warriors, this Drona who is venerable in years, is worthy of being elected generalissimo.

sn: को हि तिष्ठति दुर्धर्षे द्रोणे शस्त्रभृतां वरे। सेनापतिः स्यादन्योऽस्माच्छुकाङ्गिरसदर्शनात्॥
en: When the indomitable Drona, who is foremost among those conversant with Brahma and is equal to Shuka and Angirasa in learning, is here, who else is worthy of being selected as a leader?

sn: न च सोऽप्यस्ति ते योधः सर्वराजसु भारत। द्रोणं यः समरे यान्तं नानुयास्यति संयुगे॥
en: O Bharata, there is not even a single warrior among this mighty host of kings, who will not follow Drona when he goes to fight.

sn: एष सेनाप्रणेतृणामेष शस्त्रभृतामपि। एष बुद्धिमतां चैव श्रेष्ठो राजन् गुरुस्तव॥
en: O monarch, this one is the foremost of all leaders of warriors; he is the foremost of all wielders of arms, as also of all intelligent persons and he is also your preceptor (in arms).

sn: एवं दुर्योधनाचार्यमाशु सेनापतिं कुरु। जिगीषन्तोऽसुरान् संख्ये कार्तिकेयमिवामराः॥
en: As the immortals desirous of defeating the Asuras in battle made Kartikeya their leader, so, do you, O Duryodhana, soon elect this one (Drona) as the leader of your army.

sn: संजय उवाच कर्णस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा राजा दुर्योधनस्तदा। सेनामध्यगतं द्रोणमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Sanjaya said Thereupon having listened to the words of Karna, king Duryodhana thus addressed Drona who was standing in the midst of the soldiers.

sn: दुर्योधन उवाच वर्णश्रेष्ठ्यात् कुलोत्पत्त्या श्रुतेन वयसा धिया। वीर्याद् दाक्ष्यादधृष्यत्वादर्थज्ञानान्नयाज्जयात्॥ तपसा च कृतज्ञत्वाद् वृद्धः सर्वगुणैरपि। युक्तो भवत्समो गोप्ता राज्ञामन्यो न विद्यते॥ स भवान् पातु नः सर्वान् देवानिव शतक्रतुः। भवन्नेत्राः पराञ्जेतुमिच्छामो द्विजसत्तम॥
en: Duryodhana said Amongst all this numerous host of kings, there is none who can be as good a protector as you, owing to the superiority of the order to which you belong, to the nobility of your birth, to your knowledge of the Shastras, your age, your intelligence, prowess, skillfulness, invincibility, perfect acquaintance with worldly matters, moral purity, self-control, asceticism, seniority and gratefulness, as also owing to your being endued with all desirable qualities. Like Indra protecting the celestials, do you protect ourselves, O foremost of the twice born ones, being led by yourself, we desire to obtain victory over our enemies.

sn: रुद्राणामिव कापाली वसूनामिव पावकः। कुबेर इव यक्षाणां मरुतामिव वासवः॥ वसिष्ठ इव विप्राणां तेजसामिव भास्करः। पितृणामिव धर्मेन्द्रो यादसामिव चाम्बुराट्। ६॥ नक्षत्राणामिव शशी दितिजानामिवोशनाः। श्रेष्ठः सेनाप्रणेतृणां स नः सेनापतिर्भव॥
