en: Like Kapala amongst the Rudras; like Pavaka amongst the Vasus; like Kuvera amongst the Yakshas; like Vasava amongst the Marutas; like Vasistha amongst the Vipras, like Bhaskara (sun) amongst the lustrous bodies, like Yama amongst the Pitris, like Varuna amongst the creatures of the waters; like the moon amongst the stars, like Usanas amongst the sons of Diti, you are the foremost amongst all commanders of armies; therefore be you our leader.

sn: अक्षौहिण्यो दशैका च वशगाः सन्तुतेऽनघ। ताभिः शत्रून् प्रतिव्यूह्य जहीन्द्रो दानवानिव॥
en: Like Indra slaying the Danavas, do you slay our enemies, O sinless one, by arranging in battle-array this eleven Akshauhini of soldiers which will be placed under your complete disposal.

sn: प्रयातु नो भवानग्रे देवानामिव पावकिः। अनुयास्यामहे त्वाजौ सौरभेया इवर्षभम्॥
en: Like the son of Pavaka proceeding before the celestials, do you proceed at the head of this our army; we will follow you in battle like a heard of bulls following the leader.

sn: उग्रधन्वामहेष्वासो दिव्यं विस्फारयन् धनुः। अग्रेभवं त्वां तु दृष्ट्वा नार्जुन: प्रहरिष्यति॥
en: That fierce bowman, that mighty champion, : Arjuna, stretching his celestial bow, will not strike us seeing you go before us.

sn: ध्रुवं युधिष्ठिरं संख्ये सानुबन्धं सबान्धवम्। जेष्यामि पुरुषव्याघ्र भवान् सेनापतिर्यदि॥
en: O foremost of men, if you accept our leadership, then I am sure to conquer in battle Yudhishthira with all his friends and followers.

sn: संजय उवाच एवमुक्ते ततो द्रोर्ण जयेत्यूचुनराधिपाः। सिंहनादेन महता हर्षयन्तस्तवात्मजम्॥
en: Sanjaya said When Duryodhana had finished his address, the kings, imparting great delight to your sons by their loud defiant shouts, exclaimed Victory to Drona.

sn: सैनिकाच मुदा युक्ता वर्धयन्ति द्विजोत्तमम्। दुर्योधनं पुरस्कृत्य प्रार्थयन्तो महद् यशः। दुर्योधनं ततो राजन् द्रोणो वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Then the soldiers also filled with delight and desirous of earning fame, began to extol that foremost of regenerate ones, with Duryodhana at their head. Thereupon, O monarch, Drona spoke these words of Duryodhana.

sn: द्रोण उवाच वेदं षडङ्ग वेदाहमर्थविद्यां च मानवीम्। त्रैय्यम्बकमथेष्वस्त्रं शस्त्राणि विविधानि चाशा
en: Drona said I am versed in the Vedas and in their six auxiliaries; and in the science of practical life concerning itself with men. I know the weapons of Tryambaka and various other weapons and mantras.

sn: ये चाप्युक्ता मयि गुणा भवद्भिर्जयकाक्षिभिः। चिकीर्षुस्तानहं सर्वान् योधयिष्यामि पाण्डवान्॥
en: Those qualities, which, you, desirous of victory, have ascribed to me, bringing them to play, I will offer battle to the sons of Pandu.

sn: पार्षतं तु रणे राजन् न हनिष्ये कथंचन। स हि सृष्टो वधार्थाय ममैव पुरुषर्षभः॥
en: But, O monarch, I shall never slay the son of Prisata in battle; O foremost of men, he has been created to kill me.

sn: योधयिष्यामि सैन्यानि नाशयन् सर्वसोमकान्। न च मां पाण्डवा युद्धे योधयिश्यन्ति हर्षिताः॥
en: I shall encounter the hostile array and kill the Somakas. In battle, the Pandavas will not meet me with delightful hearts.

sn: संजय उवाच स एवमभ्यनुज्ञातश्चक्रे सनापतिं ततः। द्रोणं तव सुतो राजन् विधिदृष्टेन कर्मणा॥
en: Sanjaya said O monarch, then your son, with the perinission of Drona, made him the commander of his troops, with ceremonies enjoined by the ordinances for such occasions.

sn: अथाभिषिषिचुर्दोणं दुर्योधनमुखा नृपाः। सैनापत्ये यथा स्कन्दं पुरा शक्रमुखाः सुराः॥
en: As in days of yore, the gods with Indra at their head, invested Skanda with their leadership, so now did the monarchs headed by Duryodhana, invest Drona with the command of the troops.

sn: ततो वादित्रघोषेण शंखनां च महास्वनैः। प्रादुरासीत् कृते द्रोणे हर्षः सेनापतौ तदा॥
en: thereupon on Drona's investiture with the command, the delight (of troops) was manifest by the sound of musical instruments and the deafening blare of the conchs.

sn: ततः पुण्याहघोषेण स्वस्तिवादस्वनेन च। संस्तवैतिशब्दैश्च सूतमागधबन्दिनाम्॥ जयशब्दैजिएयाणां सुभगानर्तितैस्तथा। सत्कृत्य विधिना द्रोणं मेनिरे पाण्डवाञ्जितान्॥
en: Then honouring Drona with shouts the like of which fill the ear during a holy day, with sounds of benedictory utterances, with eulogies, songs and cries of bards, minstrels and panegyrists, with the cries of victory uttered by the foremost of regenerate ones and with the frolics of mimes, the Kauravas considered the sons of Pandu as already worsted in battle.

sn: सैनापत्यं तु सम्पाष्य भारद्वाजो महारथः। युयुत्सुयूँह्य सैन्यानि प्रायात् तव सुतैः सह॥
en: on Then having been installed the command of the army, that mighty car-warrior, the son of Bharadvaja, arranging the troops in battle-array, marched out, accompanied by your sons, from a desire of giving battle.

sn: सैन्धवश्च कलिङ्गश्च विकर्णश्च तवात्मजः। दक्षिणं पार्श्वमास्थाय समतिष्ठन्त दंशिताः॥
en: Donning their armours, the king of the Sindhus and the Kalingas and Vikarna, your son, stationed themselves in the right wing of Drona.

sn: प्रपक्षः शकुनिस्तेषां प्रवरैर्हयसादिभिः ययौ गान्धारकैः सार्धं विमलप्रासयोधिभिः॥
en: Then accompanied by a numerous and picked cavalry recruited from men belonging to the Gandhara tribe and armed with lustrous lances, Shakuni marched out as their support.

sn: कृपश्च कृतवर्मा च चित्रसेनो विविंशतिः। दुःशासनमुखा यत्ताः सव्यं पक्षमपालयन्॥
en: Then Kripa, Kritavarman, Chitrasena and Vivinsati, having Dushasana at their head, proceeded, covering the left wing.

sn: तेषां प्रपक्षाः काम्बोजा: सुदक्षिणपुरःसराः। ययुरश्वैर्महावेगैः शकाश्च यवनैः सह॥
en: Then riding on horses of great fleetness, the Kamvojas headed by Sudakshina and the Shakas with the Yavanas, marched forth, forming the support of the last mentioned party.

sn: मद्रास्त्रिगर्ताः साम्बष्ठाः प्रतीच्योदीच्यमालवाः। शिवयः शूरसेनाश्च शूद्राश्च मलदैः सह॥ सौवीराः कितवाः प्राच्या दाक्षिणात्याश्च सर्वशः। तवात्मजं पुरस्कृत्य सूतपुत्रस्य पृष्ठतः॥ हर्षयन्तः स्वसैन्यानि ययुस्तव सुतैः सह। प्रवरः सर्वयोधानां बलेषु बलमादधत्॥ ययौ वैकर्तनः कर्णः प्रमुखे सर्वधन्विनाम्।
en: Then the Madras, the Trigartas, the Ambasthas, the warriors from the West and the North, the Malavas, the Shivis, the Surasenas, the Sudras with the Malavas, the Sauviras, the Kitavas, the warriors from the East and the South, all these with your son Duryodhana at son their head and the son of Suta at their rear, cheering the hearts of their own partisans, marched forth and increased the strength of the (advancing) troops. Karna, the of Vikartana, then marched at the head of all bowmen.

sn: तस्य दीप्तो महाकाय: स्वान्यनीकानि हर्षयन्॥ हस्तिकक्ष्यो महाकेतुर्बभौ सूर्यसमद्युतिः।
en: His mighty standard, huge and resplendent and marked with the device of the elephant's girth, imparting delight into the hearts of his own soldiers, burned with effulgence cqual to that of the sun.

sn: न भीष्मव्यसनं कश्चिद् दृष्ट्वा कर्णममन्यत॥ विशोकाश्चाभवन् सर्वे राजानः कुरुभिः सह।
en: All the kings and the Kurus, seeing Karna, did pay no heed to the calamity that had befallen them in the shape of Bhishma's death and they all were shorn of their sorrow.

sn: हृष्टाश्च बहवो योधास्तत्राजल्पन्त वेगतः॥ न हि कर्णे रणे दृष्ट्वा युधि स्थास्यान्ति पाण्डवाः।
en: Numerous warriors, highly delighted, forming into groups, thus began to talk, “Surely the Pandavas, seeing Karna in the field, will not stay a while in battle.

sn: कर्णो हि समरे शक्तो जेतुं देवान् सवासवान्॥ किमु पाण्डुसुतान् युद्धे हीनवीर्यपराक्रमान्।
en: Truly, Karna is powerful enough to gain victory in battle over the celestials led by Vasava himself, not to speak of the sons of Pandu, who are devoid of prowess and energy alike.

sn: भीष्मेण तु रणे पार्थाः पालिता बाहुशालिना॥ तांस्तु कर्णः शरैस्तीक्ष्णैर्नाशयिष्यति संयुगे।
en: The sons of Pritha were tenderly treated by the mighty-armed Bhishma in battle. But Karna shall slay them in the encounter with sharpened arrows.

sn: एवं ब्रुवन्तस्तेऽन्योन्यं हृष्टरूपा विशाम्पते॥ राधेयं पूजयन्तश्च प्रशंसन्तश्च निर्ययुः। अस्माकं शकटव्यूहो द्रोणेन विहितोऽभवत्॥
en: O lord of people, thus talking to one another with joyful looks and honouring and eulogising the son of Radha, they marched along (in battle-array). Our own army, O monarch, was arrayed in the form of a Sakata (or car).

sn: परेषां क्रौञ्च एवासीद् व्यूहो राजन् महात्मनाम्। प्रीयमाणेन विहितो धर्मराजेन भारत॥
en: The army of our high-souled enemies was formed in the shape of a Krauncha (crane). O Bharata, by the very virtuous Yudhishthira with a delighted heart.

sn: व्यूहप्रमुखतस्तेषां तस्थतुः पुरुषर्षभौ। वानरध्वजमुच्छ्रित्य विष्वक्सेनधनंजयौ॥
en: At the head of their array stood the two foremost of men, Vishvaksena (Vishnu) and Dhananjaya, with their banner, bearing the emblem of the ape, uplifted.

sn: ककुदं सर्वसैन्यानां धाम सर्वधनुष्मताम्। आदित्यपथगः केतुः पार्थस्यामिततेजसः॥ दीपयामास तत् सैन्यं पाण्डवस्य महात्मनः।
en: That banner of Partha of immeasurable prowess, the hump of the whole army and the refuge of all wielders of bow, that banner which reached the orbit of the sun, seemed to illumine the whole army of Yudhishthira of high soul.

sn: यथा प्रज्वलितः सूर्यो युगान्ते वै वसुंधराम्॥ दीप्यन् दृश्येत हि तथा केतुः सर्वत्र धीमतः।
en: That banner of the most intelligent Partha appeared like the burning sun when at the end of a Yuga, it rises to consume the earth.

sn: योधानामजुनः श्रेष्ठो गाण्डीवं धनुषां वरम्॥ वासुदेवश्च भूतानां चक्राणां च सुदर्शनम्।
en: Of all the warriors Arjuna is the foremost; of all the bows Gandiva is the best. Vasudeva is the foremost of all created beings and Sudarshana is the best of all kinds of discus.

sn: चत्वार्येतानि तेजांसि वहश्वेतहयो रथः॥ परेषामग्रतस्तस्थौ कालचक्रमिवोद्यतम्। एवं तौ सुमहात्मानौ बलसेनाग्रगावुभौ॥
en: The chariot, to which were harnessed white horses, carrying these four kinds of energy incarnate, stood at the head of the hostile array, like the discus of Kala raised (for being hurled). Thus those two high-souled heroes stood at the head of their armies. Karna stood at the head of your army and Dhananjaya at the head of the hostile troops.

sn: तावकानां मुखे कर्णः परेषां च धनंजयः। ततो जयाभिसंरब्धौ परम्परवधैषिणौ।॥ अवेक्षेतां तदान्योन्यं समरे कर्णपाण्डवौ।
en: Oking! in that battle, the Kauravas and the Pandavas, looked at each other possessed with ire and each desirous of slaying the other.

sn: ततः प्रयाते सहसा भारद्वाजे महारथे॥ आर्तनादेन घोरेण वसुधा समकम्पत।
en: Thereafter when the mighty car-warrior, the son of Bharadvaja, flew suddenly to the fight, the earth began to shake with the sound of terrible wails.

sn: ततस्तुमुलमाकाशमावृणोत् सदिवाकरम्॥ वातोद्भूतं रजस्तीवं कौशेयनिकरोपमम्। ववर्ष द्यौरनभ्रापि मांसास्थिरुधिराण्युत॥
en: Then thick clouds of dust, blown up by the storm and resembling heaps of tawny silk, intercepted from the view the welkin in and the sun. Though the sky was cloudless yet a shower of flesh bones and blood fell on the earth.

sn: गृध्राः श्येना बकाः कङ्का वायसाच सहस्रशः। उपर्युपरि सेनां ते तदा पर्यपतन् नृप॥
en: O king, vultures, hawks, cranes, kanakas and crows, by thousands swooped on your army, over and over again.

sn: गोमायवश्च प्राक्रोशन् भयदान् दारुणान् रवान्। अकार्षुरपसव्यं च बहुशः पृतनां तव॥ चिखादिषन्तो मांसानि पिपासन्तश्च शोणितम्।
en: The jackals yelled forth and many dreadful and fierce rangers of the sky repeatedly placed your army to their right, being desirous of devouring flesh and thirsting for blood.

sn: अवतद् दीप्यमाना च सनिर्घाता सकम्पना॥ उल्का ज्वलन्ती संग्रामे पुच्छेनावृत्य सर्वशः।
en: On the field of battle, illuminating the welkin, dropped many a burning meteor accompanied with thundering sounds and vibrating motions and covering with their tails large areas.

sn: परिवेषो महांश्चापि सविद्युत्स्तनयित्नुमान्॥ भास्करस्याभवद् राजन् प्रयाते वाहिनीपतौ।
en: Then, O monarch, when the commander of the host (Drona) set out for battle, the wide circumference of the lustrous orb of day, emitted flashes of lightving and thundering sounds.

sn: एते चान्ये च बहवः प्रादुरासन् सुदारुणाः॥ उत्पाता युधि वीराणां जीवितक्षयकारिणः।
en: These and many other terrible portents appeared indicating a great loss of life of many heroes in the ensuing encounter.

sn: ततः प्रववृते युद्धं परस्परवधैषिणाम्॥ कुरुपाण्डवसैन्यानां शब्देनापूरूज्जगत्।
en: Thereafter the fight between the Kurus and the Pandus, both desirous of killing one another, commenced; and the terrible din rising therefrom filled the whole world.

sn: तेत्वनयोन्यं सुसंरन्धाः पाण्डवाः कौरवैः सह॥ अभ्यघ्नन् निशितैः शस्त्रैर्जयगृद्धाः प्रहारिणः।
en: Then, burning with wrath, the Pandavas and the Kauravas, all first-class smiters, began to pierce one another with sharpened weapons, ardently longing for victory.

sn: स पाण्डवानां महतीं महेष्वासो महाद्युतिः॥ वेगेनाभ्यद्रवत् सेनां किरञ्छरशतैः शितैः।
en: Then that mighty champion (Drona) of great effulgence, charged, with headlong speed, the army of the sons of Pandu, shooting hundreds of sharpened shafts.

sn: द्रोणमभ्युद्यतं दृष्ट्वा पाण्डवाः सह सृञ्जयैः॥४४॥ प्रत्यगृणंस्तदा राजञ्छरवर्षैः पृथक् पृथक्।
en: Beholding Drona charge, the Pandavas along with the Srinjayas received him, o monarch, with showers of shafts in distinct sets.

sn: विक्षोभ्यमाणा द्रोणेन भिद्यमाना महाचमूः॥ व्यशीर्यत सपाञ्चाला वातेनेव बलाहकाः।
en: That mighty host (of the Pandavas) along with the Panchalas agitated and routed by Drona, was shattered like rows of cranes by the wind.

sn: बहूनीह विकुर्वाणो दिव्यान्यस्त्राणि संयुगे॥ अपीडयत् क्षणेनैव द्रोणः पाण्डवसृञ्जयान्।
en: In the encounter, invoking various celestial weapons Drona, in a moment, sorely oppressed the Pandavas and the Srinjayas.

sn: ते वध्यमाना द्रोणेन वासवेनेव दानवाः॥ पञ्चाला: समकम्पन्त धृष्टद्युम्नपुरोगमाः।
en: The Panchalas having Dhrishtadyumna at their head being slaughtered by Drona, like the Danavas by Vasava, began to quake.

sn: ततो दिव्यास्त्रविच्छूरो याज्ञसेनिर्महारथः॥ अभिनच्छरवर्षेण द्रोणानीकमनेकधा।
en: Thereupon that mighty car-warriors, the heroic Yajnaserma versed in the knowledge of the celestial weapons, produced by his showers of arrows many a breach, in the columns of Drona.

sn: द्रोणस्य शरवर्षाणि शरवर्षेण पार्षतः॥ संनिवार्य ततः सर्वान् कुरूनप्यवधीद् बली।
en: Then that powerful son of Prishata, checking the showers of Drona's arrows with those of his own, slew many a Kuru warrior.

sn: संयम्य तु ततो द्रोणः समवस्थाप्य चाहवे॥ स्वमनीकं महेष्वासः पार्षतं समुपाद्रवत्।
en: Thereupon Drona of mighty arms, again rallying has soldiers and re-arranging them, charged the son of Prishata in battle.

sn: स बाणवर्ष सुमहदसृजत् पार्षतं प्रति॥ मघवान् समभिक्रुद्धः सहसा दानवानिव।
en: Then towards the son of Prishata he directed a close shower of arrows, like Meghavat exceedingly enraged shooting his shafts towards the Danavas.

sn: ते कम्प्यमाना द्रोणेन बाणैः पाण्डवसृञ्जयाः॥ पुनः पुनरभज्यन्त सिंहेनेवेतरे मृगाः।
en: Thus, agitated by Drona with his arrows, the Pandavas and Srinjays, again and again, broke their lines, like a herd of inferior beasts attacked by a lion.

sn: तथा पर्यचरद् द्रोणः पाण्डवानां बले बली। अलातचक्रवद् राजस्तदद्भुतमिवाभवत्॥
en: Then O monarch, like a circle of firebrands, the mighty Drona careered through the army of the Pandavas; and that was a wonderful sight.

sn: खचरनगरकल्पं कल्पितं शास्त्रदृष्ट्या चलदनिलपताकं ह्लादनं वल्पिताश्वम्। स्फटिकविमलकेतुं त्रासन शात्रवाणां रथवरमधिरूढः संजहारारिसेनाम्॥
en: Riding on his own excellent cars, that resembled a city careering through the skies; that was well supplied with the implements of war according to the military science, the banner of which was fluttering on the air, the rattle of which was resounding all round the field, the steeds of which were well-driven and the flagstaff of which was shining like a rod of crystal-riding on such a chariot. Drona inspired the hostile army with terror and massacred (right and left).

description: The audition of the account of Drona's death
sn: संजय उवाच तथा द्रोणमभिनन्तं साश्वसूतरथद्विपान्। व्यथिताः पाण्डवा दृष्ट्वा न चैनं पर्यवारयन्॥
en: Sanjaya said Seeing Drona thus destroy their horses, drivers, cars and elephants the Pandavas were greatly afflicted and could not check his career.

description: The audition of the account of Drona's death
sn: ततो युधिष्ठिरो राजा धृष्टद्युम्नधनंजयौ। अब्रवीत् सर्वतो यत्तैः कुम्भयोनिर्निवार्यताम्॥
en: Thereupon king Yudhishthira said Dhrishtadyumna and Dhananjaya, "Check the carrier of the pot-born Drona by surrounding him with great heed.

description: The audition of the account of Drona's death
sn: तत्रैनमर्जुनश्चैव पार्षतश्च सहानुगः। प्रत्यगृह्णात् ततः सर्वे समापेतुर्महारथाः॥
en: to Thereupon the mighty car-warriors namely Arjuna and the son of Prishata together with their followers, encompassed Drona, as he was rushing at them.

description: The audition of the account of Drona's death
sn: केकया भीमसेनश्च सौभद्रोऽथ घटोत्कचः। युधिष्ठिरो यमौ मत्स्या द्रुपदस्यात्मजास्तथा॥ द्रौपदेयाश्च संहृष्टा धृष्टकेतुः ससात्याकिः। चेकितानश्च संक्रुद्धो युयुत्सुश्च महारथः॥ ये चान्ये पार्थिवा राजन् पाण्डवस्यानुयायिनः। कुलवीर्यानुरूपाणि चक्रुः कर्माण्यनेकशः॥
en: The Kekayas, Bhimasena, the son of Subhadra, Ghatotkacha, Yudhishthira the twins Nakula and Sahadeva, the king of the Matsyas the son of Drupada and the five son of Draupadi greatly delighted and Dhristaketu along with Satyaki, the wrathful Chekitana, the Yuyutsu the mighty car-warrior and, O monarch, all the other rulers of earth who followed the Pandavas in battle, achieved many feats (of valour), in accordance with their prowess and nobility of birth.

description: The audition of the account of Drona's death
sn: संरक्ष्यमाणां तां दृष्ट्वा पाण्डवैर्वाहिनीं रणे। व्यावृत्य चक्षुषी कोपाद् भारद्वाजोऽन्ववैक्षत॥
en: Seeing the Pandavas protect their army in battle, the son of Bharadvaja, rolling his eyes in anger, cast his glances (on the army).

description: The audition of the account of Drona's death
sn: स तीव्र कोपमास्थाय रथे समरदुर्जयः। व्यधमत् पाण्डवानीकमभ्राणीव सदागतिः॥
en: Working himself up with ire, that one (Drona), indomitable in war, seated on his chariot, blew the Pandava host off like the storm blowing thick clouds off.

description: The audition of the account of Drona's death
sn: रथानश्वान् नरान् नागानभिधावन्नितस्ततः। चचारोन्मत्तवद् द्रोणोवृद्धोऽपि तरुणो यथा॥
en: Charging cars, steed, men and elephants on all sides, Drona roamed in the field like one insane and though grown up in years, he resembled one endued with the energy of youth.

description: The audition of the account of Drona's death
sn: तस्य शोणितदिग्धाङ्गा शोणास्ते वातरंहसः। आजानेया हया राजन्नविश्रान्ता ध्रुवं ययुः॥
en: O monarch, his horses, of chestnut colour, of excellent breed, of wind-like speed, and of indefatigable energy, assumed a beautiful appearance being bespattered with blood.

description: The audition of the account of Drona's death
sn: तमन्तकमिव क्रुद्धमापतन्तं यतव्रतम्। दृष्टा सम्प्राद्रवन् योधाः पाण्डवस्य ततस्ततः॥
en: Beholding that one of regulated vows rush at them like the god of Death enraged, all the warriors of the Pandavas sped on all directions.

description: The audition of the account of Drona's death
sn: तेषां प्राद्रवतां भीमः पुनरावर्ततामपि। पश्यतां तिष्ठतां चासीच्छब्दः परमदारुणः॥
en: As some fled and some rallied and some looked at Drona, and some stood on the field, the noise (of the confusion) they caused was dreadful and deafening.

description: The audition of the account of Drona's death
sn: शूराणं हर्षजननो भीरूणां भयवर्धनः। द्यावापृथिव्योर्विवरं पूरयामास सर्वतः॥
en: That noise that imparted delight to the heroes and enhanced the terrors of the cowards, filled the whole interval between the earth and the skies.

description: The audition of the account of Drona's death
sn: ततः पुनरपि द्रोणो नाम विश्रावयन् युधि। अकरोद् रौद्रमात्मानं किरञ्छरशतैः परान्॥
en: And again did Drona, shouting forth his own name, made himself terrible in battle by piercing his enemies with hundreds of arrows.

description: The audition of the account of Drona's death
sn: स तथा तेष्वनीकेषु पाण्डुपुत्रस्य मारिष। कालवद् व्यचरद् द्रोणो युवेव स्थविरो बली॥
en: O sire, then the mighty Drona careered fiercely amid the army of the sons of Pandu, like the god of Death himself; and he appeared like one young, though bearing the weight of years.

description: The audition of the account of Drona's death
sn: उत्कृत्य च शिरांस्युग्रान् बाहूनपि सुभूषणान्। कृत्वा शून्यान् रथोपस्थानुदक्रोशन्महारथान्॥
en: Severing down many heads as well as arms decorated with ornaments and rendering the seats of many a car empty, he sent up terrific roars.

description: The audition of the account of Drona's death
sn: तस्य हर्षप्रणादेन बाणवेगेन वा विभो। प्राकम्पन्त रणे योधा गाव: शीतार्दिता इव॥
en: In consequence of his rapturous roars and of the fleetness of his arrows, O master, the warriors began to shake in battle, like kine shivering with cold.

description: The audition of the account of Drona's death
sn: द्रोणस्य रथघोषेण मौर्वीनिप्पेषणेन च। धनुः शब्देन चाकाशे शब्दः समभवन्महान्॥
en: A terrible sound caused by the rattle of Drona's chariot, by the contraction and stretching of his bow-string and by the twang of his bow, filled the conclave dome.

description: The audition of the account of Drona's death
sn: अथास्य धनुषो बाणा निश्चरन्तः सहस्रशः। व्याप्य सर्वा दिश: पेतुर्नागाश्वरथपत्तिषु ॥
en: Thousands of arrows not shot from his bow fell, covering cardinal points, upon the elephants, steeds, chariots and foot-soldiers (of the hostile array).

description: The audition of the account of Drona's death
sn: तं कार्मुकमहावेगमस्त्रज्वलितपावकम्। द्रोणमासादयांचक्रुः पञ्चालाः पाण्डवैः सह॥
en: Then the Pandavas along with the Panchalas, rushed at Drona wielding a bow of great strength and resembling a blazing fire in consequence of his weapons.

description: The audition of the account of Drona's death
sn: तान् सकुञ्जरपत्त्यश्वान् प्राहिणोद् यमसादनम्। चक्रेऽचिरेण च द्रोणो महीं शोणित कर्दमाम्॥
en: Then he began to dispatch them with their elephants, steeds and foot-soldiers to the regions of Death; and within a short while Drona made the earth muddy with blood.

description: The audition of the account of Drona's death
sn: तन्वता परमास्त्रणि शरान् सततमस्यता। द्रोणेन विहितं दिक्षु शरजालमदृश्यत॥
en: A net-work of arrows, woven by Drona who had been scattering celestial weapons and shooting shafts on all sides, was seen to over shroud the cardinal points.

description: The audition of the account of Drona's death
sn: पदातिषु रथाश्वेषु वारणेषु च सर्वशः। तस्य विद्युदिवाभ्रेषु चरन् केतुरदृश्यत॥
en: Like flashes of lightning amid dense masses of clouds, his standard could be seen whirling amongst foot-soldiers, chariots, horses and carwarriors.

description: The audition of the account of Drona's death
sn: स केकयानां प्रवरांश्च पञ्च पञ्चालराजं च शरैः प्रमथ्य। युधिष्ठिरानीकमदीनसत्त्वो द्रोणोऽभ्ययात् कार्मुकबाणपाणिः॥
en: Afflicting with arrows the five foremost among the Kekayas and the king of the Panchadas,' Drona, of irrepressible vigour, armed with a bow and arrows, charged the division commanded by Yudhishthira.

description: The audition of the account of Drona's death
sn: तं भीमसेनश्च धनंजयश्च शिनेश्च नप्ता द्रुपदात्मजश्चा शैव्यात्मजः काशिपतिः शिबिश्च दृष्ट्वा नदन्तो व्यकिरछरौघैः॥
en: Thereupon, Bhimasena and Dhananjaya and the grandson of sini and the sons of Drupada and the son of Saibya, the ruler of the Kasis and Sibi himself, greatly delighted and sending up loud shouts, covered Drona with a stream of shafts.

description: The audition of the account of Drona's death
sn: तेषामथ द्रोणधनुर्विमुक्ताः पतत्रिणः काञ्चनचित्रपुङ्खाः। भित्त्वा शरीराणि गजाश्वयूनां जग्मुर्महीं शोणितदिग्धवाजाः॥
en: Then numerous arrows shot from the bow of Drona and adorned with golden wings, piercing through the bodies of elephants and young steeds, stuck themselves on the ground, with feathers crimson with blood.

description: The audition of the account of Drona's death
sn: सा योधसंधैश्च रथैश्च भूमिः शरैर्विभिन्नैर्गजवाजिभिश्च। प्रच्छाद्यमाना पतितैर्बभूव समावृता द्यौरिव कालमेघैः॥
en: Then the field of battle, being covered over with fallen bands of warriors, (shattered) chariots and carcasses of elephants and horses mangled with arrows, appeared like the firmament overhung with dense masses of black clouds.

description: The audition of the account of Drona's death
sn: शैनेयभीमार्जुनवाहिनीशं सौभद्रपाञ्चालसकाशिराजम्। अन्यांश्च वीरान् समरे ममर्द द्रोणः सुतानां तव भूतिकामः॥
en: Then Drona desirous of the prosperity of your sons, having in battle trampled down the divisions led by the grandson of Sini, Bhima and Arjuna and having crushed the son of Subhadra and the king of the Panchalas and the ruler of the Kasis and many other warriors.

description: The audition of the account of Drona's death
sn: एतानि चान्यानि च कौरवेन्द्र कर्माणि कृत्वा समरे महात्मा। प्रताप्य लोकानिव कालसूर्यो द्रोणो गतः स्वर्गमितो हि राजन्॥
en: And having achieved these and other wondrous feats in battle, O foremost among the Kurus, that high-souled one, Drona, left this world for heaven, after having consumed this earth like the sun that rises at the time of the world's annihilations, O monarch.

description: The audition of the account of Drona's death
sn: एवं रुक्मरथः शूरो हत्वा शतसहस्रशः। पाण्डवानां रणे योधान् पार्षतेन निपातितः॥ अक्षौहिणीमभ्यधिकां शूराणामनिवर्तिनाम्। निहत्य पश्चाद् धृतिमानगच्छत् परमां गतिम्॥ पाण्डवैः सह पञ्चालैरशिवैः क्रूरकर्मभिः। हतो रुक्मरथो राजन् कत्वा कर्म सुदुष्करम्॥ ततो निनादो भूतानामाकाशे समजायत। सैन्यानां च ततो राजन्नाचार्ये निहते युधि॥ द्यां धरां खं दिशो वापि प्रदिशश्चानुनादयन्। अहोधिगिति भूतानां शब्दः समभवद् भृशम्॥ देवताः पितरश्चैव पूर्वे ये चास्य बान्धवाः। ददृशुनिहतं तत्र भारद्वाजं महारथम्॥ पाण्डवास्तु जयं लब्ध्वा सिंहनादान् प्रचक्रिरे। सिंहनादेन महता समकम्पत मेदिनी॥
en: Having achieved these great feats of valour, that chastiser of hostile armies, that possessor of a golden car, that hero, who had killed in battle hundreds of thousands of the soldiers of the Pandavas, was himself slain by the son of Prishata. Having slain more than Akshauhini of unreturning heroes, that Drona of (unrivaled) intelligence, at last attained to the highest state of existence. O monarch, having achieved these most difficult feats, that one of a golden car was slain by the Pandavas and the Panchalas of inauspicious and heartless of deeds. When the preceptor was slain in battle, o king, a loud roar of all creatures as two also of the warriors filled the sky. The loud cry of 'O fie' uttered by creatures arose in the welkin resounding through the earth, the heavens and the interval between them and the cardinal and the subsidiary quarters. Then all the celestials and the Pitris and the friend of the mighty car-warrior Bharadvaja (Drona), saw him slain in battle. The son of Pandu having obtained victory gave forth roars resembling those of a lion; and the (foundation of) the carth shook with those loud leonine roars of theirs.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच किं कुर्वाणं रणे द्रोणं जनुः पाण्डवसुंजयाः। तथा निपुणमस्त्रेषु सर्वशस्त्रभृतामपि।।।।
en: What was Drona doing when the Pandavas and the Srinjayas slew him in battle,-he who was so skillful in the use of weapons amongst all wielders of arms?

sn: रथभङ्ग बभूवास्य धनुर्वाशीर्यतास्यतः। प्रमत्तो वाभवद् द्रोणस्ततो मृत्युमुपेयिवान्॥
en: Did his chariot give way? Did his bow snap in two in the act of smiting? Did Drona go mad and for the reason met with his death?

sn: कथं नु पार्षतस्तात शत्रुभिर्दुष्प्रधर्षणम्। किरन्तमिषुसंघातान् रुक्मपुङ्खाननेकशः॥ क्षिप्रहस्तं द्विजश्रेष्ठं कृतिनं चित्रयोधिनम्। दूरेषुपातिनं दान्तमस्त्रयुद्धेषु पारगम्॥ पाञ्चालपुत्रो न्यवधीद दिव्यास्त्रधरमच्युतम्। कुर्वाणं दारुणं कर्म रणे यत्तं महारथम्॥
en: O son, how was it that the son of Prishata, the prince of the Panchalas, slew that invincible hero, who scattered thick shower of arrows decked with golden wings, who was : (wonderfully) light-handed; that foremost of the regenerate who proficient in everything, thoroughly familiar with all modes of warfare and capable of shooting his shafts to was over a long distance; who was self-controlled, skilful in the use of weapons and blessed with the possession of celestial weapons, that mighty warrior who performed many dreadful feats and who was ever heedful in fight?

sn: व्यक्तं हि दैवं वलवत् पौरुषादिति मे मतिः। यद् द्रोणो निहतः शूरू पार्षतेन महात्मना॥
en: Since that heroic Drona was slain by Parshata of illustrious soul, it is evident, I think, that Destiny is more powerful than exertion.

sn: अस्त्रं चतुर्विधं वीरे यस्मिन्नासीत् प्रतिष्ठितम्। तमिष्वस्त्रधराचार्ये द्रोणं शंससि मे हतम्॥
en: In that mighty warrior, the knowledge of all the four kinds of wcapons was present. Do you say to me that Drona, that preceptor of all wielders of arrows and weapons is slain?

sn: श्रुत्वा हतं रुक्मरथं वैयाघ्रपरिवारितम्। जातरूपशिरस्त्राणं नाद्य शोकमपानुदे॥
en: Hearing the death that hero of golden car covered with tiger-skins, whose effulgence was like that of gold, I cannot today discard my grief.

sn: न नूनं परदुःखेन म्रियते कोऽपि संजय। यत्र द्रोणमहं श्रुत्वा हतं जीवामि मन्दधीः॥
en: Surely, O Sanjaya, no man ever dies through sorrow caused by another's calamity; since, I, unfortunate as I am, am still alive having heard of Drona's death.

sn: दैवमेव परं मन्ये नन्वनर्थं हि पौरुषम्। अश्मसारमयं नूनं हृदयं सुदृढं मम॥
en: I do consider Destiny to be, by far, the superior; and exertion is of no avail. Surely my heart is so hard as if it were made of adamant.

sn: यच्छुत्वा निहतं द्रोणं शतधा न विदीर्यते। ब्राह्ये दैवे तथेष्वस्त्रे यमुपासन् गुणार्थिनः॥ ब्राह्मणा राजपुत्राश्च स कथं मृत्युना हृतः। शोषणं सागरस्येव मेरोरिव विसर्पणम्॥ पतनं भास्करस्येव न मृष्ये द्रोणपातनम्। दुष्टानां प्रतिषेद्धाऽऽसीद् धार्मिकाणां च रक्षिता॥
en: Since it does not break into hundred pieces, although I have heard of the slaughter of Drona. How could he had bean struck by death, on whom the Brahmanas and the princes danced attendance being desirous of receiving lessons in the Vedas and in divination and in the use of bows. I cannot even conceive the fall of Drona which is like the drying up of the ocean, the removal of the Meru mountain and the dropping of the lustrous orb from the heavens. He was the repressor of the wicked and the protector of the pious.

sn: योऽहासीत् कृपणस्यार्थे प्राणानपि परंतपः। मन्दानां मम पुत्राणां जयाशा यस्य विक्रमे॥ बृहस्पत्युशनस्तुल्यो बुद्ध्या स निहतः कथम्। तेच शोणा बृहन्तोऽश्वाश्छन्ना जालैहिरण्मयैः॥
en: That afflicter of enemies, who has sacrificed his life for the pitiable Duryodhana, on whose prowess rested the hope of victory of my wicked sons, who was equal to Brihaspati and Ushanas in intelligence, how could he have been slain? His stout chestnut-coloured steed, decked with golden trappings.

sn: रथे बातजवा युक्ताः सर्वशास्त्रातिगा रणे। बलिनो हैषिणो दान्ताः सैन्धवाः साधुवाहिनः॥
en: Fleet as the wind, yoked to his car, beyond the reach of all weapons in battle, endued with great strength, emitting neights (in joy), welltrained, of the Sindhu breed, excellently dragging the chariot.

sn: दृढाः संग्राममध्येषु कच्चिदासन्नविह्वलाः। करिणां बृंहतां युद्धे शङ्खदुन्दुभिनि:स्वनैः॥
en: Of great sturdiness, were exhausted in the very midst of the fight? Unmoved in battle by the sight of the elephants as those huge monsters roared out with the sound of conchs and kettledrums.

sn: ज्याक्षेपशरवर्षाणां शस्त्राणां च सहिष्णवः। आशंसन्तः पराञ्जेतुं जितश्वासा जितव्यथा॥
en: By the twangs of bow-strings and showers of arrows and other weapons, foretelling victory over enemies (by their appearance), of inexhaustible breath and indefatigable.

sn: हयाः पराजिताः शीघ्रा भारद्वाजरथोद्वहाः। ते स्म रुक्मरथे युक्ता नरवीरसमास्थिताः॥
en: mere Those fleet horses harnessed to the car of the son of Bharadvaja, were they overpowered? Even such steeds were yoked by that foremost of human heroes to his golden car.

sn: कथं नाभ्यतरंस्तात पाण्डवानामनीकिनीम्। जातरूपपरिष्कारमास्थाय रथमुत्तमम्॥
en: Why could he not cross the ocean of the Pandava army, mounted on his own best of cars effulgent like gold?

sn: भारद्वाजः किमकरोद् युधि सत्यपराक्रमः। विद्यां यस्योपजीवन्ति सर्वलोकधनुर्धराः॥
en: What feats did that son of Bharadvaja achieve in battle, who made all the heroes, cry and on whose knowledge of weapons all the bowmen in the world depend?

sn: स सत्यसंघो बलवान् द्रोणः किमकरोद् युधि। दिवि शक्रमिव श्रेष्ठं महामात्रं धनुर्भृताम्॥ के नु तं रौद्रकर्माणं युद्धे प्रत्युद्ययू रथाः। ननु रुक्मरथं दृष्ट्वा प्राद्रवन्ति स्म पाण्डवाः॥
en: What feats did Drona perform in battle, Drona who was endued with great strength and was ever devoted to truth? What car-warriors felled in battle Drona of fierce deeds, that foremost of bowmen, that foremost commanders who was like Shakra himself in heaven? Did the Pandavas fly on all directions sceing him of the golden car?

sn: दिव्यमस्त्रं विकुर्वाणं रणे तस्मिन् महाबलम्। उताहो सर्वसैन्येन धर्मराज सहानुजः॥ पाञ्चाल्यप्रग्रहो द्रोणं सर्वत: समावारयत्। नूनमावास्यत् पार्थो रथिनोऽन्यानजिह्मगैः॥
en: Him endued with great might who invoked in that batile many celestial weapons? Did the very virtuous king Yudhishthira, with his younger brothers and is army having the prince of the Panchalas for its reins, encompass Drona on all sides? Surely Partha checked the career of other car-warriors with his straight going arrows.

sn: ततो द्रोणं समारोहत् पार्षतः पापकर्मकृत्। न ह्यहं परिपश्यामि वधे कंचन शुष्मिण:॥
en: of
Then, of course, the son of Prishata, that perpetrator of evil deeds, assaulted Drona. Indeed I do not see any one capable of bringing about the death of Drona.

sn: धृष्टद्युम्नाटते रौद्रात् पाल्यमानात् किरीटिना। तैर्वृतः सर्वतः शूरः पाञ्चाल्यापसदस्ततः॥ केकयैश्चेदिकारूषैर्मत्स्यैरन्यैश्च भूमिपैः। व्याकुलीकृतमाचार्यं पिपीलैरुरगं यथा॥ कर्मण्यसुकरे सक्तं जघानेति मतिर्मम। योऽधीत्य चतुरो वेदान् साङ्गानाख्यानपञ्चमान्॥
en: Save the fierce warrior Dhrishtadyumna supported by Arjuna himself. I think that when these heroes namely the Kekayas, the Chedis, the Karushas, the Matsyas and the other rulers of earth, encompassing the preceptor hemmed him in on all sides, like ants pressing upon a serpent and that when he was occupied in the achievement of some difficult feat, then the vilest among the Panchalas must have slain him. He who, having studied the four Vedas along with their auxiliaries and the Histories constituting the fifth Veda.

sn: ब्राह्मणानां प्रतिष्ठाऽऽसीत् स्रोतसामिव सागरः। क्षत्रं च ब्रह्म चैवेह योऽभ्यतिष्ठत् परंतपः॥ स कथं ब्राह्मणो वृद्धः शस्त्रेण वधमाप्तवान्। अमर्षिणा मर्षितवान् क्लिश्यमानान् सदा मया॥
en: Became the refuge of the Brahmanas as the ocean is that of the rivers, that afflicter of eneinies who led the life both of a Brahmana and a Kshatriya, how could that Brahinana, venerable in years meet his death through weapons. Intolerant in spirit, he was ever humiliated and had to undergo troubles for my sake.

sn: अनर्हमाणान् कौन्तेयान् कर्मणस्तस्य तत् फलम्। यस्य कर्मानुजीवन्ति लोके सर्वधनुर्भृतः॥ स सत्यसंधः सुकृती श्रीकामैनिहतः कथम्। दिवि शक्र इव श्रेष्ठो महासत्त्वो महाबलः॥
en: Through the son of Kunti he reaped the fruits of his own actions however undeserving he might have been of them. How could that one, on whose feats of valour depends the world of bowmen, who was cver devoted to truth and of pious deeds, who was foremost like the Shakra in heaven, who was endued with great vigours and strength, how could that one be slain by persons hankering after prosperity?

sn: स कथं निहतः पाथैः क्षुद्रमत्स्यैर्य था तिमिः। क्षिप्रहस्तश्च बलवान् दृढधन्वाऽरिमर्दनः॥
en: How could that one of great lightness of hand, endued with might, a firm wielder of bow and the grinder of his foes, how could that one he slain by the sons of Pritha like a timi slain by the smaller fishes?

sn: न यस्य विजयाकाक्षी विषयं प्राप्य जीवति। यं द्वौ न जहतः शब्दौ जीवमानं कदाचन॥
en: He, meeting whom no person desirous of victory, ever returned with life, he whom when alive the following two sound never left, namely.

sn: ब्राह्मश्च वेदकामानां ज्याघोषश्च धनुष्मताम्। अदीनं पुरुषव्याघ्र द्वीमन्तमपराजितम्॥
en: The sound of the recital of Vedic verses, by those desirous of acquiring Vedic knowledge and the twang of the bowstrings, caused by those wishing to acquire skill in bowmanship; he who was never depressed, who was the foremost among men and was ever attended with prosperity and was invincible.

sn: नाहं मृष्ये हतं द्रोणं सिंहद्विरदविक्रमम्। कथं संजय दुर्धर्षमनाधृष्ययशोबलम्॥ पश्यतां पुरुषेन्द्राणां समरे पार्षतोऽवधीत्। के पुरुतादयुध्यन्त रक्षन्तो द्रोणमन्तिकात्॥
en: He who was equal to the elephant and the lion in prowess, even he has been slain! I cannot even tolerate the thought of Drona's death. How, O Sanjaya, the son of Prishata, slew in battle that most invincible hero whose might was never checked and whose fame was never soiled even before the very eyes of the foremost of men? Who were those persons who fought in Drona's front and protected him from near?

sn: के नु पश्चादवर्तन्त गच्छन्तो दुर्गमां गतिम्। केऽरक्षन् दक्षिणं चक्रं सव्यं के च महात्मनः॥ पुरस्तात् के च वीरस्य
en: Who were they who brought up his rear and obtained that end which is so difficult to being attained? Who were they that covered the right। and the left wings of that high-souled one?

sn: युध्यमानस्य संयुगे। केच तस्मिंस्तनूंस्त्यक्त्वा प्रतीपं मृत्युमाव्रजन्॥
en: Who went before him when that hero fought in the battle? Who were they that courted death stood face to face to them regardless of their body?

sn: द्रोणस्य समरे वीराः केऽकुर्वन्त परां धृतिम्। कञ्चिन्नैनं भयान्मन्दाः क्षत्रिया व्यजहन् रणे॥ रक्षितारस्ततः शूनये कच्चित् तैर्न हतः परैः। न स पृष्ठमरेस्त्रासाद् रणे शौर्यात् प्रदर्शयेत्॥ परामप्यापदं प्राप्य स कथं निहतः परैः। एतदार्येण कर्तव्यं कृच्छ्रास्वापत्सु संजय॥ पराक्रमेद यथाशक्त्या तच्च तस्मिन् प्रतिष्ठितम्। मुह्यते मे मनस्तात कथा तावन्निवार्यताम्। भूयस्तु लब्धसंज्ञस्त्वां परिपृच्छामि संजय॥
en: Who were those heroes that attained the highest state of existence, in the battle with Drona? Did those vile Kshatriyas entrusted with the protection of Drona, out of apprehension, abandon him in (the thick of) the fight? Was he slain by the foe while there helpless? Out of fear Drona would never turn his back on the field of battle, though the danger might be very great. How could he have been slain by the enemy? O Sanjaya, although in a very critical situation, an illustrious person should do this, namely, display his prowess to the best of his might; all this was in Drona. O son, my mind is loosing consciousness; refrain for a while from this discourse. O Sanjaya, regaining my consciousness, I shall again question you.

sn: वैशम्पायन उवाच एतत् पृष्ट्वा सूतपुत्रं हृच्छोकेनार्दितो भृशम्। जये निराशः पुत्राणां धृतराष्ट्रोऽपतत् क्षितौ॥
en: Vaishampayana said Thus having questioned the son of Suta, Dhritarashtra, sorely oppressed with the sorrow of his heart and despondent of the victory of his sons, dropped down on the ground.

sn: तं विसंज्ञं निपतितं सिषिचुः परिचारिकाः। जलेनात्यर्थशीतेन वीजन्त्यः पुण्यगन्धिना॥
en: Seeing him unconscious and fallen down on the ground, the attendants sprinkled him with very cold and holy-scented water, fanning him all the while.

sn: पतितं चैनमालोक्य समन्ताद् भरतस्त्रियः। परिवर्महारुजमस्पृशंश्चैव पाणिभिः॥
en: Beholding that great king fallen down, the Bharata ladies surrounded him on all sides and began to chafe him (gently) with their hands.

sn: उत्थाप्य चैनं शनकै राजानं पृथिवीतलात्। आसनं प्रापयामासुर्वाष्पकण्ठ्यो वराननाः॥
en: Then those beautiful ladies, with their voices choked up with the vapour of grief, gently raised the monarch from the surface of the earth and placed him on his throne.

sn: आसनं प्राप्य राजा तु मूर्छयाभिपरिप्लुतः। निश्चेष्टोऽतिष्ठत तदा वीज्यमानः समन्ततः॥
en: Placed the throne, the monarch overwhelmed by the influence of the swoon, remained motionless, while he was fanned from all sides.

sn: स लब्वा शनकैः संज्ञां वेपमानो महीपतिः। पुनर्गावल्गणिं सूतं पर्यपृच्छद् यथातथम्॥
en: Slowly regaining consciousness, that ruler of carth began to quake and he again questioned the son of Gavalgani, of the Suta tribe, regarding the events of the battle, as they occurred. on

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच यः स उद्यन्निवादित्यो ज्योतिषा प्रणुदंस्तमः। अजातशत्रुमायान्तं कस्तं द्रोणादवारयत्॥ प्रभिन्नमिव मातङ्गं यथा क्रुद्धं तरस्विनम्। प्रसन्नवदनं दृष्ट्वा प्रतिद्विरदगामिनम्॥ वासितासंगमे यद्वदजय्यं प्रति यूथपैः। निजधान रणे वीरान् वीरः पुरुषसत्तमः॥
en: Dhritarashtra said That Ajatasatru (Yudhishthira) who like the rising sun drives awake darkness by his own radiance, who (charges an enemy), like a tremendous and infuriated elephant in rut, incapable of being defeated by a rival leader of herds, charging a rival proceeding with cheerful face towards a female of the species, what great warrior of my host faced that Ajatasatru, as he charged, in order to keep him away from Drona? That foremost of men, that hero, who has slain in battle many brave warriors.

sn: यो होको हि महावीर्यो निर्दहेद् घोरचक्षुषा। कृत्त्रं दुर्योधनबलं धृतिमान् सत्यसंगरः॥
en: That mighty-armed, intelligent and brave hero of invincible might, who, singled-handed, can consume the whole host of Duryodhana by means of his terrible glances.

sn: चक्षुर्हणं जये सक्त मिष्वासधरमच्युतम्। दान्तं बहुमतं लोके के शूराः पर्यवारयन्॥
en: That destroyer by his glances, that one ever inclined to gain victory, that wielder of bow, that hero of eternal renown, that self-controlled warrior held in high respect by the whole world-what warriors of my army did surround that hero?

sn: के दुष्प्रधर्षे राजानमिष्वासधरमच्युतम्। समासेदुनरव्याघ्रं कौन्तेयं तत्र मामकाः॥
en: Who were those warriors of my host that encountered that irrepressible prince, that wielder of bow, that hero of unfading glory, that foremost of men, that son of Kunti?

sn: तरसैवाभिपद्याथ यो वै द्रोणमुपाद्रवत्। यः करोति महत् कर्म शत्रूणां वै महाबलः॥ महाकायो महोत्साहो नागायुतसमो बले। तं भीमसेनमायान्तं के शूराः पर्यवारयन्॥
en: That hero who rushing with headlong speed charged Drona, who achieves grand feats at the expense of the enemy, that most puissant one of gigantic stature and great vigour, who equals ten thousand elephants in strength, what warrior surrounded that Bhimasena as he charged my army?

sn: यदाऽऽयाज्जलदप्रख्यो रथः परमवीर्यवान्। पर्जन्य इव वीभत्सुस्तुमुलामशनीं सृजन्॥
en: As that mighty car-warrior of excessive energy, Vibhatsu, resembling a dense mass of rain-clouds, came, creating terrible sounds like the clappings of the thunder-bolt, like Parjanya itself.

sn: विसृजञ्छरजालानि वर्षाणि मघवानिव। अवस्फूर्जन् दिशः सर्वास्तलनेमिस्वनेन च॥
en: Showering torrents of arrows like Indra showering rain and causing the cardinal quarters to reverberate with the sound of his palms and rattle of his chariot-wheels.

sn: चापविद्युत्प्रभो घोरो रथगुल्मवलाहकः। स नेमिघोषस्तनितः शरशब्दातिबनधुरः॥
en: (When that terrible hero) whose bow was effulgent like a flash of lightning, whose chariot resembled a cloud having for its thunder the rattle of its wheels, (that hero) the whizz of whose arrows made him all the more fierce.

sn: रोषानिलसमुद्भूतो मनोऽभिप्रायशीघ्रगः। मर्मातिगो वाणधरस्तुमुलः शोणितोदकैः॥ सम्लावयन् दिशः सर्वा मानवैरास्तरन् महीम्। भीमनि: स्वनितो रौद्रो दुर्योधनपुरोगमान्॥ युद्धेऽभ्यषिञ्चद् विजयो गापत्रैः शिलाशितैः। गाण्डीवं धारयन् धीमान् कीदृशं वो मनस्तदा।॥
en: Whose ire is like a dreadful cloud, who is fleet like the mind or the wind, who always pierces the enemy to the very core of his heart, who, armed with shafts, is dreadful to gaze at, who profusely fills all the cardinal quarters with human blood like Death himself, who, with a terrific roar and a dreadful countenance, wielding the Gandiva, pours, in one continuous shower, on the head of my warriors led by Duryodhana, shafts whetted on stone and decked with the feathers of vultures, when that intelligent Vijaya came, what became the state of your mind.

sn: इघुसम्बाधमाकाशं कुर्वन् कपिवरध्वजः। यदाऽऽयात् कथमासीत् तु तदा पार्थं समीक्षताम्॥
en: When that son of Pritha bearing the device of the foremost of apes on his banner, came, overspreading the sky with his shower of shafts, what became the state of your mind at the sight of him?

sn: कच्चिद् गाण्डीवशब्देन न प्रणश्यति वैबलम्। यद्वः सभैरवं कुर्वन्नर्जुनो भृशमन्वयात्॥
en: Did Arjuna rush to battle, killing your warriors by the very twang of his bow Gandiva and achieving dreadful feat (as he advanced).

sn: कच्चिन्नापानुदत् प्राणानिषुभिवों धनंजयः। वातो वेगादिवाविध्यन्मेधाशरगणैर्नृपान्॥
en: Did Dhananjaya deprived you of your lives with his arrows, like the hurricane scattering masses of gathering clouds or felling forest of reed by blowing through them?

sn: को हि गाण्डीवधन्वानं रणे सोढुं नरोऽर्हति। यमुपश्रुत्य सेनाग्रे जन: सर्वो विदीर्यते॥
en: What man is powerful enough to encounter the wielder of the Gandiva bow in battle? Even hearing him to be on the head of the (hostile) array, all ranks of soldiers give way.

sn: यत्सेनाः समकम्पन्त यद्वीरानस्पृशद् भयम्। के तत्र नाजहुर्दोणं के क्षुद्राः प्राद्रवन् भयात्॥
en: In that battle, in which soldiers trembled and even heroes were inspired with fear, who were they that did not forsake Drona and who were those mean fellows that fled out terror?

sn: के वा तत्र तनूंस्त्यक्त्वा प्रतीपं मृत्युमाव्रजन्। अमानुषाणां जेतारं युद्धेष्वपि धनंजयम्॥
en: Who were they that battle, shuffling this mortal coil, courted Death standing before them in the shape of Dhananjaya who had obtained victory even over superhuman combatants?

sn: न च वेगं सिताश्वस्य विसहिष्यन्ति मामकाः। गाण्डीवस्य च निर्घोषं प्रावृड्जलदनि:स्वनम्॥
en: My warriors cannot withstand the impetus of that one having white horses harnessed to chariot, nor can they bear to twang of the I Gandiva, that resembles the rumbling of clouds in the rainy season.

sn: विष्वक्सेनो यस्य यन्ता यस्य योद्धा धनंजयः। अशक्यः स रथो जेतुं मन्ये देवासुरैरपि॥
en: consider that chariot which has Vishvaksena for its driver and Dhananjaya for its warrior, to be unconquerable even be the celestials and Asuras united together.

sn: सुकुमारो युवा शूरो दर्शनीयश्च पाण्डवः। मेधावी निपुणो धीमान् युधि सत्यपराक्रमः॥
en: Delicate, youthful, brave, of a handsome appearance, that son of Pandu who is intelligent, skillful, accurate in his memory, of prowess incapable of being thwarted, in battle.

sn: आरावं विपुलं कुर्वन् व्यथयन् सर्वसैनिकान्। यदाऽऽयान्नकुलो द्रोणं के शूराः पर्यवारयन्॥
en: When that Nakula giving forth a loud roar and afflicting the whole army, rushed upon Drona, what warriors tried to check his career?

sn: आशीविष इव क्रुद्धः सहदेवो यदाभ्ययात्। कदनं करिष्यञ्छत्रूणां तेजसा दुर्जयो युधि॥
en: When Sahadeva, resembling an infuriated snake of mortal poison, rushed at Drona, afflicting his enemies, when that one owning white horses and incapable of being conquered in battle.

sn: आर्यव्रतममोधेषु द्वीमन्तमपराजितम्। सहदेवं तमायान्तं के शूराः पर्यवारयन्॥
en: When that one of illustrious vows, of neverfailing aim, of bashful nature and invincible prowess, when that Sahadeva charged, who were those heroes that withstood him?

sn: यस्तु सौवीरराजस्य प्रमथ्य महतीं चमूम्। आदत्त महिषीं भोजां काम्यां सर्वाङ्गशोभनाम्॥
en: That hero who having completely crushed the army of king Sauvira, took for his consort the desirable princess of the Bhojas and graceful in limbs of the body.

sn: सत्यं धृतिश्च शौर्ये च ब्रह्मचर्ये च केवलम्। सर्वाणि युयुधानेऽस्मिन् नित्यानि पुरुषर्षभे॥
en: That foremost of men Yayudhana who is ever endued with truthfulness, resoulteness, bravery and Brahmacharya.

sn: बलिनं सत्यकर्माणमदीनमपराजितम्। वासुदेवसमं युद्धे वासुदेवादनन्तरम्॥
en: That warrior possessed of great physical strength, who always does what is true, who is never depressed and who is invincible and equals Vasudeva in battle and is considered to be a second Vasudeva.

sn: धनंजयोपदेशेन श्रेष्ठमिष्वस्त्रकर्मणि। पार्थेन सममस्त्रेषु कस्तं द्रोणादवारयत्॥
en: Who, by the teachings of Dhananjaya has become foremost in the act of using arrows, who is equal to the son of Pritha in the use of weapon, what warrior of my army kept him away from Drona?

sn: वृष्णीनां प्रवरं वीरं शूरं सर्वधनुष्मताम्। रामेण सममस्त्रेषु यशसा विक्रमेण च॥
en: That foremost hero among the Vrishnis that bravest among all wielders of bow, who is equal to Rama himself in the use of weapons, in glory and in prowess.

sn: सत्यं धृतिर्मतिः शौर्यं ब्राह्मं चास्त्रमनुत्तमम्। सात्वते तानि सर्वाणि त्रैलोक्यमिव केशवे॥
en: That one of the Satvata race in who there are truth, firmness, intelligence, prowess, the knowledge of the Vedas and the most excellent weapons, as the triune world is in Keshava himself.

sn: तमेवंगुणसम्पन्नं दुर्धारमपि दैवतैः। समासाद्य महेष्वासं के शूराः पर्यवारयन्॥
en: That mighty champion who is endued with all virtues and who is incapable of being opposed even by the celestials, what warriors (of my army) approaching him, surrounded him on all sides?

sn: पञ्चालेषूत्तमं वीरमुत्तमाभिजनप्रियम्। नित्यमुत्तमकर्माणमुत्तमौजसमाहवे॥
en: That foremost among the Panchalas, that hero of noble extraction and a favourite of all high-born person, always achieving excellent feats in battle, namely Uttamanjaya.

sn: युक्तं धनंजयहिते ममानार्थमुत्थितम्। यमवैश्रवणादित्यमहेन्द्रवरुणोपमम्॥
en: That one ever intent on doing good to Dhananjaya and born for doing evil only to me, who resembles Yama or Vaishravana or Aditya or Mahendra or Varuna.

sn: महारथं समाख्यातं द्रोणायोद्यतमाहवे। त्यजन्तं तुमुले प्राणान् के शूराः समवारयन्॥
en: That prince renowned as a great car-warrior and ever ready to sacrifice his life in the every think of battle, what heroes of my army surrounded him?

sn: एकोऽपसृत्य चेदिभ्यः पाण्डवान् य: समाश्रितः। धृष्टकेतुं समायान्तं द्रोणं कस्तं न्यवारयत्॥
en: That one who alone descrting the Chedis had sided with the Pandus, namely Dhristaketu, what heroes surrounded him when he advanced towards Drona?

sn: योऽवधीत् केतुमान् वीरो राजपुत्रं दुरासदम्। अपरान्तगिरिद्वारे द्रोणात् कस्तं न्यवारयत्॥
en: Thai heroic Ketumat, who slew the Prince Durjaya when the took sheller in Girivraja, what hero of my army kept him (Ketumat) away from Drona?

sn: स्त्रीपुंसयोर्नरव्याघ्रो यः स वेद गुणागुणान्। शिखण्डिनं याज्ञसेनिमम्लानमनसं युधि॥ देवव्रतस्य समरे हेतुं मृत्योर्महात्मनः। द्रोणायाभिमुखं यान्तं के शूराः पर्यवारयन्॥
en: What warriors of my army encountered Sikhandin when he rushed at Drona-Sikhandin, the foremost of mean, who has relised the pleasures (in himself) of man hood and femininity, that son of Yajnasena, who is ever cheerful in battle and who became the cause of the death of the high souled Devavrata in battle?

sn: यस्मिन्नभ्यधिका वीरे गुणाः सर्वे धनंजयात्। यस्मिन्नस्त्राणि सत्यं च ब्रह्मचर्ये च सर्वदा॥
en: That most excellent hero among the Vrishnis, that foremost of all wielders of bow, that hero, in whom reside all virtues even in a greater degree than in Dhananjaya himself.

sn: वासुदेवसमं वीर्ये धनंजयसमं बले। तेजसाऽऽदित्यसदृशं बृहस्पतिसमं मतौ॥
en: In whom always exist truth, (the knowledge of) the best weapons and Brahmacharya, who is equal to the son of Vasudeva in prowess and to Dhananjaya in strength.

sn: अभिमन्युं महात्मानं व्यात्ताननमिवान्तकम्। द्रोणायाभिमुखं यान्तं के शूराः समवारयन्॥
en: Who resembles Aditya in effulgence, Brihaspati in intelligence-namely, the highsouled Abhimanyu who is like Death himself with a gapping mouth.

sn: तरुणस्तरुणप्रज्ञः सौभद्रः परवीरहा। यदाभ्यधावद्वै द्रोणं तदाऽऽसीद् वो मनः कथम्॥
en: What heroes surrounded him when he advanced towards Drona? That youthful hero of unripe understanding, that slayer of hostile heroes, namely Subhadra's son.

sn: द्रौपदेया नरव्याघ्राः समुद्रमिव सिन्धवः। यद् द्रोणमाद्रवन् संख्ये के शूरास्तान् न्यवारयन्॥५१ एते द्वादश वर्षाणि क्रीडामुत्सृज्य बालकाः। अस्त्रार्थमवसन् भीष्मे विभ्रतो व्रतमुत्तमम्॥
en: When he charged Drona, what became the state of your mind then? When those foremost of princes, the son of Draupadi, in battle rushed at Drona liko streams flowing towards the ocean, what heroes obstructed them? Those boys, who having abandoned all boyish sports, for twelve years. And observing excellent vows danced attendance on Bhima in order to receive lessons in the use of weapons.

sn: क्षत्रंजयः क्षत्रदेवः क्षत्रवर्मा च मानदः। धृष्टद्युम्नात्मजा वीराः के तान् द्रोणादवारयन्॥
en: Those boys, namely Kshatranjaya, Kshatradeva and Kshatravarma and Manada. Those heroic sons of Dhrishtadyumna, what warriors kept them away from Drona?

sn: शताद् विशिष्टं यं युद्धे सममन्यन्त वृष्णयः। चेकितानं महेष्वासं कस्तं द्रोणादवारयत्॥
en: That one whom the Vrishnis consider superior in battle to hundred warriors. That mighty warrior Chekitana, what hero of my army tried to keep him away from Drona?

sn: वार्धक्षेमिः कलिङ्गानां यः कन्यामाहरद् युधि। अनाधृष्टिरदीनात्मा कस्तं द्रोणादवारयत्॥
en: Son

sn: वीराः
en: Anadhrishti, the generous of Vriddhaksema had kidnapped the daughter of Kalingaraja, who had prevented him to make an access to Drona?

sn: भ्रातरः पञ्च कैकेया धार्मिका: सत्यविक्रमाः। इन्द्रगोपकसंकाशा रक्तवर्मायुधध्वजाः॥ मातृष्वसुः सुता पाण्डवानां जयार्थिनः। तान् द्रोणं हन्तुमायातान् के वीराः पर्यवारयन्॥
en: The five Kekaya brothers, virtuous and endued with prowess incapable of being thwarted. Resembling the Indragopakas (in complexion), furnished with red armours and weapons and banners, those heroes who are the sons of the sister of the Pandavas' mother and who ever long for the victory of the Pandavas. What heroes of my army surrounded them when they assaulted Drona with a view to kill hin?

sn: यं योधयन्तो राजानो नाजयन् वारणावते। षण्मासानपि संरब्धा जिघांसन्तो युधाम्पतिम्॥ धनुष्मतां वरं शूरं सत्यसंघ महाबलम्। द्रोणात् कस्तं नरव्याघ्रं युयुत्सुं पर्यवारयत्॥
en: That lord of battles, desirous of slaying whom the enraged Monarchs united together for six months in Varanavata could not defeat, that best of all wielders of bows, that hero of great strength and unerring aim, that foremost of men, Yuyutsu, tried to keep him away from Drona?

sn: यः पुत्रं काशिराजस्य वाराणस्यां महारथम्। समरे स्त्रीषु गृध्यन्तं भल्लेनापाहरद्रथात्॥ धृष्टद्युम्नं महेष्वासं पार्थानां मन्त्रधारिणम्। युक्तं दुर्योधनानथें सृष्टं द्रोणवधाय च॥ निर्दहन्तं रणे योधान् दारयन्तं च सर्वतः। द्रोणाभिमुखमायान्तं के शूराः पर्यवारयन्॥
en: Who in a battle in Varanasi, everthrew from his car with a broad-headed shaft, the great warrior the son of Kashiraja, desirous of scizing a maiden, what hero kept him away from Drona? That mighty warrior Dhrishtadyumna, that principal counsellor of the sons of Pritha. Who is ever engaged in doing harm to Duryodhana, who has been created to slay Drona, what warriors of my side surrounded him, when consuming in battle all warriors and shattering all the ranks of my soldiers, he advanced towards Drona?

sn: उत्सङ्ग इव संवृद्धं द्रुपदस्यास्त्रवित्तमम्। शैखण्डिनं शस्त्रगुप्तं के च द्रोणादवारयन्॥
en: That foremost of all men conversant with the weapons, who has been reared, as it were, on the very lap of Drupada. That Sikhandin, guarded by Arjuna's weapons, what warriors of my army kept him away from Drona?

sn: य इमां पृथिवीं कृत्स्नां चर्मवत् समवेष्टयत्। महता रथघोषेण मुख्यारिनो महारथः॥ दशाश्वमेधानाजहे स्वन्नपानाप्तदक्षिणान्। निरर्गलान् सर्वमेधान् पुत्रवत् पालयन् प्रजाः॥ गङ्गस्रोतसि यावन्यः सिकता अप्यशेषतः। तावतीर्गा ददौ वीर उशीनरसुतोऽध्वरे॥
en: That one who, as if with a leathern belt, encompassed this extensive earth. With the deafening rattle of his chariot, that foremost of warriors, the chief of all slayers of enemies, who in lieu of other sacrifices accomplished ten horse-sacrifices with ample food, drink and Dakshina, that one who ruled his subjects, as if they were his own sons, that son of Ushinara who in his sacrifice gave away kineas numerous as the sand that over-spread the banks of the Ganges-stream, whose this deed no man has been or will be able to imitate.

sn: न पूर्वे नापरे चकुरिदं केचन मानवाः। इतीदं चुकुशुर्देवाः कृते कर्मणि दुष्करे॥
en: After the accomplishment by him of this feat, the very gods had exclaim saying, We do not see in the three worlds with all their mobile and immobile creations,

sn: पश्यामस्त्रिषु लोकेषु न तं संस्थास्नुचारिषु। जातं चापि जनिष्यन्तं द्वितीयं चापि साम्प्रतम्॥ अन्यमौशीनराच्छैव्याद् धुरो वोढारमित्युत। गतिं यस्य न यास्यन्ति मानुषा लोकवासिन.॥
en: A second person save Ushinara's son, who has attained to regions, after death, which are unattainable by human beings'-who amongst my warriors, opposed that Shaivya, that grandson of the Ushinara's son, while he assaulted Drona?

sn: तस्य सप्तारमायान्तं शैब्यं कः समवारयत्। द्रोणायाभिमुखं यत्तं व्यात्ताननमिवान्तकम्॥
en: Shaivya, the grand son of that king was when approaching to Dronacarya with widely opened mouth like the death god (Kala), who had prevented him marching that time?

sn: विराटस्य रथानीकं मत्स्यस्यामित्रघातिनः। प्रेप्सन्तं समरे द्रोणं के वीराः पर्यवारयन्॥
en: What warriors of my host obstructed that squadron of cars, belonging to Virata, the king of the Matsyas, the slayer of his enemies, as it careered towards Drona?

sn: सद्यो वृकोदराज्जातो महाबलपराक्रमः। मायावी राक्षसो वीरो यस्मान्मम महद् भयम्॥ पार्थानां जयकामं तं पुत्राणां मम कण्टकम्। घटोत्कचं महात्मानं कस्तं द्रोणादवारयत्॥
en: That one endued with great strength and prowess, born of Vrikodara in the course of a single day, that heroic Rakshasa of potent illusive powers, of whom I entertain great apprehensions. Who is always desirous of victory for the sons of Pritha, who is a thorn in the sides of my sons, what hero of my army kept that Ghatotkacha of gigantic body away from Drona?

sn: एते चान्ये च बहवो येषामर्थाय संजय। त्यक्तारः संयुगे प्राणान् किं तेषामजितं युधि॥
en: O Sanjaya, what cannot be vanquished by them for whose interests these and other such numerous (heroes) are ever ready to sacrifice their lives in battle?

sn: येषां च पुरुषव्याघ्रः शाईधन्वा व्यपाश्रयः। हितार्थी चापि पार्थानां कथं तेषां पराजयः॥
en: Those sons of Pritha, whose well-wisher and refuge is that wielders of Saranga bow, those sons, how could they suffer defeat in battle?

sn: लोकानां गुरुरत्यर्थं लोकनाथः सनातनः। नारायणो रणे नाथोदिव्यो दिव्यात्मकः प्रभुः॥
en: The son of Vasudeva in the supreme preceptor of the worlds, the Lord of all and the Eternal; that master Narayana, that one of divine soul is the refuge of men in battle.

sn: यस्य दिव्यानि कर्माणि प्रवदन्ति मनीषिणः। तान्यहं कीर्तयिष्यामिभक्त्या स्थैर्यार्थमात्मनः॥
en: His divine achievements are extolled by the wise; I shall also recite them with reverence, regaining my equanimity.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच शृणु दिव्यानि कर्माणि वासुदेवस्य संजया कृतवान् यानि गोविन्दो तथा नान्यः पुमान् क्वचित्॥१
en: Dhritarashtra said Hear, O Sanjaya, of the celestial feats of the son of Vasudeva,-feats which Govinda achieved and which no other person.

sn: संवर्धता गोपकुले बालेनैव महात्मना। विख्यापितं बलं बाहोस्त्रिषु लोकेषु संजय॥
en: While he was being reared in the family of the cowherds, the illustrious one, even in his early years, made the might of his arms, O Sanjaya, known to the three worlds.

sn: उच्चैः श्रवस्तुल्यबलं वायुवेगसमं जवे। जघान हयराजं तं यमुनावनवासिनम्॥
en: (Even then) he slew the Asura Hayaraja (prince of steeds) who was equal to the Uchchaishravas in might and the wind itself in fleetness and who infested the woods on the shores of the Yamuna.

sn: दानवं घोरकर्माणं गवां मृत्युमिवोत्थितम्। वृषरूपधरं बाल्ये भुजाभ्यां निजधान ह॥
en: In his early years, he killed with his two arms only, the Danava in the form of a bull, of terrible deeds and born as Death himself to the COWS.

sn: प्रलम्बं नरकं जम्भं पीठं चापि महासुरम्। मुरं चान्तकसंकाशमवधीत् पुष्करेक्षणः॥
en: He of eyes resembling lotus petals, also slew the great Asuras, named, Pralamba, Naraka, Jamva, Peeta, as also, Mura of godlike nature.

sn: तथा कंसो महातेजा जरासंधेन पालितः। विक्रमेणैव कृष्णेन सगणः पातितो रणे॥
en: Also Kansa of great vigour who was protected by Jarasandha himself, was slain with his followers, in battle, by Krishna with his prowess alone.

sn: सुनामा रणविक्रान्तः समग्राक्षोहिणीपतिः। भोजराजस्य मध्यस्थो भ्राता कंसस्य वीर्यवान्॥ बलदेवद्वितीयेन कृष्णेनामित्रघातिना। तरस्वी समरे दग्धः ससैन्यः शूरसेनराट्॥
en: The mighty sovereign of the Shurasenas, by name Sunamana, of great prowess in battle, the master of a complete Akshauhini, endued with activity and the second brother of Kansa the ruler of the Bhojas, with all his soldiers, was consumed in battle by that slayer of enemies, viz., Krishna with Baladeva as his second.

sn: दुर्वासा नाम विप्रर्षिस्तथा परमकोपनः। आराधितः सदारेण स चास्मै प्रददौ वरान्॥
en: That highly passionate Brahmanical sage, by name Durvasa, was adored by him (Krishna) along with his wives. The sage (pleased with him) accorded boons to him.

sn: तथा गान्धारराजस्य सुतां वीरः स्वयंवरे। निर्जित्य पृथिवीपालानावहत् पुष्करेक्षणः॥ अमृष्यमाणा राजानो यस्य जात्या हया इव। रथे वैवाहिके युक्ताः प्रतोदेन कृतव्रणाः॥
en: That one eyes resembling lotus petals, that most puissant hero, (Krishna), carried away the daughter of the king of the Gandharas, after having defeated, at a Svayamvara (Self-choice) all the rulers of the earth. Like horses, those exasperated kings were harnessed to his bridal chariot and lacerated with the cut of his whip.

sn: जरासंधं महाबाहुमुपायेन जनार्दनः। परेण घातयामास समग्राक्षौहिणीपतिम्॥
en: That Janardana, through the instrumentality of another, slew Jarasandha of mighty arms, the lord of a complete Akshauhini.

sn: चेदिराजं च विक्रान्तं राजसेनापति बली। अर्पा विवदमानं च जघान पशुवत् तदा॥
en: That puissant one, slaughtered, like a beast, the king of the Chedis, that powerful leader of kingly hosts, when the latter disputed with him about the (sacrificial) Arghya.

sn: सौभं दैत्यपुरं खस्थं शाल्वगुप्तं दुरासदम्। समुद्रकुक्षौ विक्रम्य पातयामास माधवः॥
en: Madhava, by his prowess, hurled into the bosomn of the sea, the fortress of the Danavas known as Soubha, situated in heaven, protected by Shalva and considered to be invulnerable.

sn: अङ्गान् वङ्गान् कलिङ्गांश्च मागधान् काशिकोसलान्। वात्स्यगार्यकरूषांश्च पौण्ड्रांश्चाप्यजयद् रणे॥
en: He obtained victory in battle over the Angas, the Bangas, the Kalingas, the Magadhas, the Kasis, the Koshalas, the Vatsyas, the Gargas, the Karushas and the Poundras,

sn: आवन्त्यान् दाक्षिणात्यांश्च पर्वतीयान् दशेरकान्। काश्मीरकानौरसिकान् पिशाचांश्च समुद्गलान्॥ काम्बोजान् वाटधानांश्च चोलान् पाण्ड्यांश्च संजय। त्रिगर्तान् मालवांश्चैव दरदांश्च सुदुर्जयान्॥ नानादिग्भ्यश्च सम्प्राप्तान् खशांश्चैव शकांस्तथा। जितवान् पुण्डरीकाक्षो यवनं च सहानुगम्॥
en: Avantyas, the Southerners, the Mountaineers, the Daserakas, the Kashmirakas, the Auroshikas, the Pishachas, the Samudgalas, the Kambojas, the Vatadhanas, the Cholas, the Pandavas and, O Sanjaya, the Trigarttas, the Malavas, the Daradas incapable of being defeated. The Khasas and the Shakas, comform various directions and the Yavanas with their followers, that one of eyes resembling the petals of a blue lotus, conquered all these tribes in battle.

sn: प्रविश्य मकारावासं यादोगणनिषेवितम्। जिगाय वरुणं संख्ये सलिलान्तर्गतं पुरा॥
en: In days gone by, entering into the abode of the sea-monster Makara, he defeated in battle Varuna, surrounded by all kinds of sea-animals and hidden underneath watery depths.

sn: युधि पञ्चजनं हत्वा दैत्यं पातालवासिनम् पाञ्चजन्यं हृषीकेशो दिव्यं शङ्खमवाप्तवान्॥
en: Hrishikesha obtained the celestial conch called Panchajanya, after having slain in battle Panchajana, who lived in the nether regions.

sn: खाण्डवे पार्थसहितस्तोषयित्वा हुताशनम्। आग्नेयमस्त्रं दुर्धर्षं चक्रं लेभे महाबलः॥
en: That puissant hero, obtained his indomitable weapon of fire, the discus (Sudarshana), by propitiating Hutashana (Fire) by helping it to burn down the Khandava forest, in which act he was assisted by the son of Pritha (Arjuna).

sn: वैनतेयं समारुह्य त्रासयित्वाऽमरावतीम्। महेन्द्रभवनाद् वीरः पारिजातमुपानयत्॥
en: Riding on the son of Vinata and creating quite a panic in the city of the Immortals, that hero carried away the Parijata tree from the abode of the great Indra.

sn: अच्च मर्षितवाशक्रो जानंस्तस्य पराक्रमम्। राज्ञां चाप्यजितं कञ्चित् कृष्णेनेह न शुश्रुम॥
en: That act Shakra submissively brooked, for he was perfectly acquainted with the prowess of Krishna. We have never heard of a king who has not been worsted by Krishna (in battle).

sn: यच्च तन्महदाश्चर्ये सभायां मम संजय। कृतवान् पुण्डरीकाक्षः कस्तदन्य इहार्हति॥
en: That most marvelous act, which he achieved in my assembly hall, O Sanjaya, who else, save that one of eyes resembling lotus petal, is capable of doing?

sn: यच्च भक्त्या प्रसन्नोऽहमद्राक्षं कृष्णमीश्वरम्। तन्मे सुविदितं सर्वे प्रत्यक्षमिव चागमम्॥
en: Since inspired by reverence I have been able to recognise Krishna as the Lord, everything in the Vedas is well-known to me and is before my eyes.

sn: नान्तो विक्रमयुक्तस्य बुद्ध्या युक्तस्य वा पुनः। कर्मणां शक्यते गन्तुं हृषीकेशस्य संजय॥
en: Verily, O Sanjaya, none can reach the end (of the account) of of achievements Hrishikesha who is endued with prowess and intelligence. or

sn: तथा गदश्च साम्बश्च प्रद्युम्नोऽथ विदूरथः। अगावहोऽनिरुद्धश्च चारुदेष्णः ससारणः॥ उल्मुको निशठश्चैव झिल्ली बभ्रुश्च वीर्यवान्। पृथुश्च विपृथुश्चैद शमीकोऽथारिमेजय॥ एतेऽन्ये बलवन्तश्च वृष्णिवीराः प्रहारिणः। कथंचित् पाण्डवानीकं श्रयेयुः समरे स्थिताः॥ आहूता वृष्णिवीरेण केशवेन महात्मना। ततः संशयितं सर्वे भवेदिति मतिर्मम॥
en: Then also Gada, Shamva, Pradyumna, Viduratha, Agaboha Anirudina, Charudeshna along with Sarana, Ulmuka, Nisata, the powerful Jhilhivobhru, Prithu, Viprithu, Somika and Arimejaya. These and other most puissant Vrishni heroes, skilled in the art of smiting, will, standing on the field, betake to the ranks of the Pandava host. Being called to do so by that foremost of Vrishni warriors, viz., Keshava of high soul; then me-seems, everything (on my side) will be in great dangers.

sn: नागायुतबलो वीरः कैलासशिखरोपमः। वनवाली हली रामस्तत्र यत्र जनार्दनः॥
en: The heroic Rama, decked with garlands of wild flowers, equal in strength to two thousand elephants, resembling the peck of the Kailasa mountain and armed with the plough, will be there where Janardana is.

sn: यमाहुः सर्वपितरं वासुदेवं द्विजातयः। अपि वा ह्येष पाण्डूनां योत्स्यतेऽर्थाय संजय॥
en: That son of Vasudeva, whom all the regenerate ones call the Father of all, O Sanjaya, will battle for the interests of the sons of Pandu?

sn: स यदा तात संनोत् पाण्डवार्थाय संजय। न तदा प्रतिसंयोद्धा भविता तत्र कश्चन॥
en: When that one, O son, O Sanjaya, clothes himself in mail for the interests of the Pandavas, none will come forth as his antagonist.

sn: यदि स्म कुरवः सर्वे जयेयुर्नाम पाण्डवान्। वार्ष्णेयोऽर्थाय तेषां वै गृह्णीयाच्छस्त्रमुत्तमम्॥
en: If, per chance, the Kurus obtain victory over the Pandavas then that one of the Vrishni race, for the interests of these latter will take up his excellent weapon (the discus).

sn: ततः सर्वान् नरव्याघ्रो हत्वा नरपतीन् रणे। कौरवांश्च महाबाहुः कुन्त्यैदद्यात् स मेदिनीम्॥
en: Then that foremost of men, that mightyarmed hero, having slain in battle the Kauravas and the (assembled) monarchs will offer the whole earth of Kunti.

sn: यस्य यन्ता हृषीकेशो योद्धा यस्य धनंजयः। रथस्य तस्य का संख्ये प्रत्यनीको भवेद् रथः॥
en: What other car can encounter in battle, that car of which the driver is Hrishikesha and the warrior is Dhananjaya?

sn: न केनचिदुपायेन कुरूणां दृश्यते जयः। तस्मान्मे सर्वमाचक्ष्व यथा युद्धमवर्तत॥
en: In any way, I do not see victory for the Kurus, Recount to me then, all as to how the battle raged.

sn: अर्जुनः केशवस्यात्माकृष्णोऽप्यात्मा किरीटिनः। अर्जुने विजयो नित्यं कृष्णे कीर्तिश्च शाश्वती॥
en: Arjuna is the soul of Keshava and Krishna is the soul of the diadem-decked (Arjuna). In Arjuna victory ever resides and eternal glory is in Krishna.

sn: सर्वेष्वपि च लोकेषु बीभत्सुरपराजितः। प्राधान्येनैव भूयिष्ठममेयाः केशवे गुणा:॥
en: In all the regions, Vibhatsu is unconquerable. All virtues are in Keshava in an extraordinary degree.

sn: मोहाद् दुर्योधनः कृष्णं यो न वेत्तीह केशवम्। मोहितो दैवयोगेन मृत्युपाशपुरस्कृतः॥
en: Duryodhana, through foolishness cannot recognise Krishna or Keshava; he is befooled by Destiny and the noose of Death hangs over him.

sn: न वेद कृष्णं दाशार्हमर्जुनं चैव पाण्डवम्। पूर्वदेवी महात्मानौ नरनारायणावुभौ॥
en: Duryodhana knows not Krishna of the Dasharha race and Arjuna the son of Pandu; they both are supreme divinities, of high soul, know on earth as Nara and Narayana.

sn: नेच्छतः। एकात्मानौ द्विधाभूतौ दृश्येते मानवैर्भुवि। मनसाऽपि हि दुर्धर्षी सेनामेतां यशस्विनौ॥ नाशयेतामिहेच्छन्तौ मानुषत्वाच्च युगस्येव विपर्यासो लोकानामिव मोहनम्॥ भीष्मस्य च वधस्तात द्रोणस्य च महात्मनः। न होव ब्रह्मचर्येण न वेदाध्ययनेन च॥
en: On earth they appear to men as two different persons, though ir reality they are of one and the same soul. That highly-renowned invincible pair, can with the fiat of their will slay this host, if only they wish it. But for humanity's sake, they do not wish it. O son, the slaughter of Bhishma and Drona, of high souls, appears to be like the over-turning of the Yuga and the stupefaction of the senses. In this world neither by Brahmacharya, nor by the study of the Vedas.

sn: न क्रियाभिर्न चास्त्रेण मृत्योः कश्चिनिवार्यते। लोकसम्भावितौ वीरौ कृतास्त्रौ युद्धदुर्मदौ॥
en: Nor by the performance of rites or by the dint of weapons, can any one be saved from Death. Those two heroes, held in high honour by the worlds, accomplished in the use of Weapons and invincible in battle.

sn: भीष्मद्रोणौ हतौ श्रुत्वा किं नु जीवामि संजय। यां तां श्रियमसूयामः पुरा दृष्ट्वा युधिष्ठिरे॥
en: Namely, Bhishma and Drona, hearing of their death, why do I, O Sanjaya, still live? That prosperity, seeing which attend Yudhishthira before, we were so jealous.

sn: अद्य तामनुजानीमो भीष्मद्रोणवधेन ह। मत्कृते चाप्यनुप्राप्तः कुरूणामेष संक्षयः॥
en: Today, deprived of that prosperity, we shall have to live, in consequence of the death of Bhishma and Drona. This complete annihilation of the Kurus has come consequent upon my actions.

sn: पक्वानां हि वधे सूत वज्रायन्ते तृणान्युत। अनन्तमिदमैश्वर्यं लोके प्राप्तो युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: For the destruction of those, O you of the Suta caste, who are ripe for it, even the straw behave like a thunder-bolt. In this world Yudhishthira is going to obtain prosperity which is infinite.

sn: यस्य कोपान्महात्मानौ भीष्मद्रोणौ निपातितौ। प्राप्तः प्रकृतितो धर्मो न धर्मो मामकान् प्रति॥
en: Yudhishthira, through whose wrath Bhisma and Drona have met their ends. Righteousness had naturally attached itself to Yudhishthira, while it is hostile of the cause of my sons.

sn: क्रूरः सर्वविनाशाय कालोऽसौ नातिवर्तते। अन्यथा चिन्तिता ह्या नरैस्तात मनस्विभिः॥
en: Time so cruel, that has come for destroying every one, cannot be overcome! O son, things calculated in one way even by intelligent persons.

sn: अन्यथैव प्रपद्यन्ते दैवादिति मतिर्मम। तस्मादपरिहार्येऽर्थे सम्प्राप्ते कृच्छ्र उत्तमे। अपारणीये दुश्चिन्त्ये यथाभूतं प्रचक्ष्व मे॥
en: Result in an altogether different way, through the agency of Destiny; this is my belief. Therefore relate to me truly all that occurred, on the advent of that dreadful but inevitable calamity (the death Drona, generating most grieving thoughts and incapable of being crossed over by us).

description: The granting of a boon by Drona
sn: संजय उवाच हन्त ते कथयिष्यामि सर्वं प्रत्यक्षदर्शिवान्। यथा स न्यपतद् द्रोणः सूदितः पाण्डुसृञ्जयै :॥
en: Sanjaya said Alas! I shall relate to you everything, as I saw with my own eyes, how Drona fell being slain by the Pandus and the Srinjayas.

description: The granting of a boon by Drona
sn: सेनापतित्वं सम्प्राप्य भारद्वाजो महारथः। मध्ये सर्वस्य सैन्यस्य पुत्रं ते वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
en: The mighty car-warrior, the of Bharadvaja, having been installed as the commander of the army, said these words to your son, in the very midst of the soldiers. son

description: The granting of a boon by Drona
sn: यत् कौरवाणामृषभादापगेयादनन्तरम्। सैनापत्येन यद् राजन् मामद्य कृतवानसि॥
en: “O monarch, in as much as, today you have honoured me with the general-ship of this army, immediately after that foremost of the Kauravas, the son of the river (Ganga).

description: The granting of a boon by Drona
sn: सदृशं कर्मणस्तस्य फलं प्राप्नुहि भारत। करोमि कामं कं तेऽद्य प्रवृणीष्व यमिच्छसि॥
en: O Bharata, reap the adequate fruit of that act of yours. What desire of yours shall I fulfill now? Ask whatever boon you may like?"

description: The granting of a boon by Drona
sn: ततो दुर्योधनो राजा कर्णदुःशासनादिभिः। सम्मत्र्योवाच दुर्धर्षमाचार्य जयतां चार्यं जयतां वरम्॥
en: Thereupon king Duryodhana, accompanied by Karna, Dushasana and others thus spoke to the invincible preceptor, the foremost of all victors.

description: The granting of a boon by Drona
sn: ददासि चेद् वरं मह्यं जीवग्राहं युधिष्ठिरम्। गृहीत्वा रथिनां श्रेष्ठं मत्समीपमिहानय॥
en: If you would at all accord me a boon, then having captured that foremost of car-warriors, Yudhishthira alive, do you bring him to me.

description: The granting of a boon by Drona
sn: ततः कुरूणामाचार्यः श्रुत्वा पुत्रस्य ते वचः। सेनां प्रहर्षयन् सर्वामिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Thereupon the preceptor of the Kurus hearing these words of your son, spoke the following words, thereby imparting great delight to the troops.

description: The granting of a boon by Drona
sn: धन्यः कुन्तीसुतो राजन यस्य ग्रहणमिच्छसि। न वधार्थं सुदुर्धर्षं वरमद्य प्रयाचसे॥
en: Fortunate is the king, the son of Kunti, whose capture only you desire. O invincible one, you do not ask for any other boon, such as his slaughter.

description: The granting of a boon by Drona
sn: किमर्थे च नरव्याघ्र न वधं तस्य काक्षसे। नाशंससि क्रियामेतां मत्तो दुर्योधन ध्रुवम्॥
en: Why, O foremost of men, do you not desire his slaughter? For what reason do you not allude to his death? Surely ODuryodhana, you are not wanting in policy.

description: The granting of a boon by Drona
sn: आहोस्विद् धर्मराजस्य द्वेष्टा तस्य न विद्यते। यदीच्छसि त्वं जीवन्तं कुलं रक्षसि चात्मनः॥
en: It is wonderful that the virtuous king Yudhishthira should have none deadly inimical to him. As you desire him to live, either you intend to preserve your own race.

description: The granting of a boon by Drona
sn: अथवा भरतश्रेष्ठ निर्जित्य युधि पाण्डवान्। राज्यं सम्प्रति दत्त्वा च सौभ्रात्रं कर्तुमिच्छसि॥
en: Or, O foremost of the Bharatas, having defeated the Pandavas in battle, you desire to re-establish brotherly feelings (with them), by giving them back their kingdom.

description: The granting of a boon by Drona
sn: धन्यः कुन्तीसुतो राजा सुजातं चास्य धीमतः। अज्ञातशत्रुता सत्या तस्य यत् स्निह्यते भवान्॥
en: Praised be that king the son of Kunti. The birth of that intelligent one was auspicious. The fact of his being Ajatasatru (having no enemy) is verified today, in as much as even you are affectionate towards him.

description: The granting of a boon by Drona
sn: द्रोणेन चैवमुक्तस्य तव पुत्रस्य भारत। सहसा निःसृतो भावो योऽस्य नित्यं हदि स्थितः।।१३
en: ( Bharata, when your son had been thus addressed by Drona, the feeling that was then present in his heart, suddenly round vent.

description: The granting of a boon by Drona
sn: नाकारो गृहितुं शक्यो बृहस्पतिसमैरपि। तस्मात्तव सुतो राजन् प्रहृष्टो वाक्यमव्रवीत्॥
en: Even beings like Brihaspati himself cannot suppress the outward manifestations of internal feelings. Therefore, O menarch, your son, transported with joy, spoke these words.

description: The granting of a boon by Drona
sn: वधे कुन्तिसुतस्याजौ नाचार्य विजयो मम। हते युधिष्ठिरे पार्था हन्युः सर्वान् हि नो ध्रुवम्॥
en: On the event of the death of the son of Kunti in battle, O preceptor, victory cannot be inine. If Yudhishthira were to be slain, Partha is sure to slay all of us.

description: The granting of a boon by Drona
sn: न च शक्या रणे सर्वे निहन्तुममरैरपि। य एव तेषां शेषः स्यात् स एवास्मान् न शेषयेत्॥१६
en: Even the immortals cannot slay all of them in battle; so he that will survive the rest of them is sure to extirpate us all.

description: The granting of a boon by Drona
sn: सत्यप्रतिज्ञे त्वानीते पुन तेन निर्जिते। पुनर्यास्यन्त्यख्याय पाण्डवास्तमनुव्रताः॥
en: ever to.. his If Yudhishthira, truthful promises, be brought here alive, he being once more defeated at dice, the Pandavas obedient to him, will again repair to the woods.

description: The granting of a boon by Drona
sn: सोऽयं मम जयो व्यक्तं दीर्घकालं भविष्यति। अतो न वधमिच्छामि धर्मराजस्य कर्हिचित्॥
en: In this way, it is obvious, that my victory will endure for a long time. It is for this that I do never desire the death of the virtuous king Yudhishthira.

description: The granting of a boon by Drona
sn: तस्य जिह्ममभिप्रायं ज्ञात्वा द्रोणोऽथतत्त्ववित्। तं वरं सान्तरं तस्मै ददौ संचिन्त्य बुद्धिमान्॥
en: Being apprised of his crooked intentions, Drona of keen intellect and conversant with the science of polity, accorded the boon to him after a little reflection, modifying it thus.

description: The granting of a boon by Drona
sn: द्रोण उवाच न चेद् युधिष्ठिरं वीरः पालयत्यर्जुनो युधि। मन्यस्व पाण्डवश्रेष्ठमानीतं वशमात्मनः॥
en: Drona said "If in battle, the heroic Arjuna does not protect king Yudhishthira, then you may already regard the foremost of the Pandavas, brought under your control.

description: The granting of a boon by Drona
sn: न हि शक्यो रणे पार्थः सैन्ट्रैर्देवासुरैरपि। प्रत्युद्यातुमतस्तात नैतदामर्षयाम्यहम्॥
en: Even the celestials with Indra at their head and united with the Asuras theinselves, cannot cope with Partha in battle; for this reason, O son, I do not venture to advance against him.

description: The granting of a boon by Drona
sn: असंशयं स मे शिष्यो मत्पूर्वश्चास्त्रकर्मणि। तरुणः सुकृतैर्युक्त एकायनगतश्च ह॥
en: No doubt, he is my disciple and I am senior to him in the use of weapons. But he is youthful, blessed with a good fortune and assiduous in (the execution of) his intents.

description: The granting of a boon by Drona
sn: अस्त्राणीन्द्राच्च रुद्राच्च भूयः स समवाप्तवान्। अमर्षितश्च ते राजंस्ततो नामर्षयाम्यहम्॥
en: Moreover, he has obtained weapons from Indra and Rudra; besides he has been, O king, incensed by you. It is for these reasons, that I venture not to perform what you ask me to do.

description: The granting of a boon by Drona
sn: स चापक्रम्यतां युद्धाद् येनोपायेन शक्यते। अपनीते ततः पार्थे धर्मराजो जितस्त्वया॥
en: Withdraw Arjuna from the battle by what means so ever that can be done. On Partha being removed, the righteous Yudhishthira is as good as vanquished by you.

description: The granting of a boon by Drona
sn: ग्रहणे हि जयस्तस्य न वधे पुरुषर्षभ। एतेन चाप्युपायेन ग्रहणं समुपैष्यसि॥
en: O foremost of men, victory depends on his capture and not on the death; and his capture can be brought about by this artifice.

description: The granting of a boon by Drona
sn: अहं गृहीत्वा राजानं सत्यधर्मपरायणम्। आनयिष्यामि ते राजन् वशमद्य न संशयः॥
en: I, having seized that king devoted to truth and righteousness, will, O monarch, no doubt, bring him under your control today.

description: The granting of a boon by Drona
sn: यदि स्थास्यति संग्रामे मुहूर्तमपि मेऽग्रतः। अपनीते नरव्याघ्र कुन्तीपुत्रे धनंजये॥
en: Provided, he remains even for a moment before me in battle of course, if that foremost of men the son of Kunti Dhananjaya be removed from the field of battle.

description: The granting of a boon by Drona
sn: तु न हि शक्यो युधिष्ठिरः। ग्रहीतुं समरे राजन् सेन्ट्रैरपि सुरासुरैः॥
en: But, Oking, before the eyes of Phalguna, Yudhishthira cannot be captured in battle, even by the celestials and the Asuras exerting jointly with Indra at their head.

description: The granting of a boon by Drona
sn: फाल्गुनस्य समीपे संजय उवाच सान्तरं तु प्रतिज्ञाते राज्ञो द्रोणेन निग्रहे। गृहीतं तममन्यन्त तव पुत्राः सुबालिशाः॥
en: Sanjaya said When under these circumscription's, Drona had promised the capture of king Yudhishthira, jour greatly-foolish sons regarded the latter as already scized.

description: The granting of a boon by Drona
sn: पाण्डवेयेषु साक्षेपं द्रोणं जानाति ते सुतः। तत: प्रतिज्ञास्थर्यार्थं स मन्त्रो बहुलीकृतः॥
en: Your son was perfectly aware of the partiality Drona cherished for the Pandavas; so to make Drona strictly redeem his promise, Duryodhana gave publicity to that counsel.

description: The granting of a boon by Drona
sn: ततो दुर्योधनेनापि ग्रहणं पाण्डवस्य तत्। सैन्यस्थानेषु सर्वेषु सुघोषितमरिंदम॥
en: Thereafter, O grinder of your foes, Drona's promise regarding the seizure of amongst the eldest of the Pandavas, was proclaimed all his soldiers by Duryodhana himself.

description: The solemn declaration of Drona to capture Yudhishthira
sn: संजय उवाच सान्तरे तु प्रतिज्ञाते राज्ञो द्रोणेन निग्रहे। ततस्ते सैनिकाः श्रुत्वा तं युधिष्ठिरनिग्रहम्॥
