en: Sanjaya said When Drona had promised the capture of the king under these limitations your soldiers, hearing of the probable capture of Yudhishthira.

description: The solemn declaration of Drona to capture Yudhishthira
sn: सिंहनादरवांश्चक्रुर्बाहुशब्दांश्च कृत्स्नशः। तच्च सर्वं यथान्यायं धर्मराजेन भारत॥ आप्तैराशु परिज्ञातं भारद्वाजचिकीर्षितम्। ततः सर्वान् समानाय्य भ्रातृनन्यांश्च सर्वशः॥
en: Uttered many loud shouts like the roars of lions, accompanying them with the noise of their (flying) shafts and the sound of their conchs. The virtuous king Yudhishthira, O Bharata, was soon apprised, in detail, of everything regarding the purposes of the son of Bharadvaja, by his trusty emissaries. Thereupon having summoned together all his brothers and the other monarchs of his host.

description: The solemn declaration of Drona to capture Yudhishthira
sn: अब्रवीद् धर्मराजस्तु धनंजयमिदं वचः। श्रुतं ते पुरुषव्याघ्र द्रोणस्याद्य चिकीर्षितम्॥
en: The very righteous king addressed these words to Dhananjaya-"O foremost of men today you have heard of the design of Drona.

description: The solemn declaration of Drona to capture Yudhishthira
sn: यथा तन्न भवेत् सत्यं तथा नीतिर्विधीयताम् सान्तरं हि प्रतिज्ञातं द्रोणेनामित्रकर्षिणा॥
en: Adopt such course of action, as will prevent the execution of that design. Truc it is that Drona the destroyer of his foes, has pledged his troth with certain limitations.

description: The solemn declaration of Drona to capture Yudhishthira
sn: तच्चान्तरं महेष्वास त्वयि तेन समाहितम्। स त्वमद्य महाबाहो युध्यस्व मदनन्तरम्॥
en: But those limitations, O mighty warrior, have been all made dependent on you, by him (Drona). Therefore, O mighty-armed one, do you this day fight by my side, so that Duryodhana may not secure the fruition of his desire through the agency of Drona."

description: The solemn declaration of Drona to capture Yudhishthira
sn: अर्जुन उवाच यथा दुर्योधनः कामं नेमं द्रोणादवाप्नुयात्। यथा मे न वधः कार्य आचार्यस्य कदाचन॥
en: Arjuna said As, the slaughter of my own preceptor can never be perpetrated by me, so, also, O monarch, I can never agree to abandon you.

description: The solemn declaration of Drona to capture Yudhishthira
sn: तथा तव परित्यागो न मे राजश्चिकीर्षितः। अप्येवं पाण्डव प्राणानुत्सृजेयमहं युधि॥
en: Rather, O son of Pandu, I would give up my life in battle, than be antagonistic to my preceplor, at any tiine.

description: The solemn declaration of Drona to capture Yudhishthira
sn: प्रतीपो नाहमाचार्ये भवेयं वै कथंचन। तवां निगृह्याहवे राज्यं धार्तराष्ट्रोऽयमिच्छति॥
en: Having captured you in battle, the son of Dhritarashtra, desires to possess the kingdom; but in this world of living beings, he will never obtain the fruition of his desire.

description: The solemn declaration of Drona to capture Yudhishthira
sn: न स तं जीवलोकेऽस्मिन् कामं प्राप्येत् कथंचन। प्रपतेत् द्यौः सनक्षत्रा पृथिवी शकली भवेत्॥
en: The conclave dome with the stars may drop down; the earth itself may be shattered to pieces; yet Drona will never capture you, so long as I live.

description: The solemn declaration of Drona to capture Yudhishthira
sn: न त्वां द्रोणो निगृह्णीया ज्जीवमाने मयि ध्रुवम्। यदि तस्यं रणे साह्यं कुरुते वज्रभृत् स्वयम्॥
en: Even if the wielder of the thunderbolt himself or Vishnu accompanied by the celestials, assists him in battle, still, he shall never capture you in battle.

description: The solemn declaration of Drona to capture Yudhishthira
sn: विष्णुर्वासहितो देवैर्न त्वां प्राप्स्यत्यसौ मृधे। मयि जीवति राजेन्द्र न भयं कर्तुमर्हसि॥
en: O foremost of monarchs, so long as I am alive, you need not entertain any apprehension from Drona the foremost of all wielders of weapon or any body else.

description: The solemn declaration of Drona to capture Yudhishthira
sn: द्रोणादस्त्रभृतां श्रेष्ठात् सर्वशस्त्रभृतामपि। अन्यच्च ब्रूयां राजेन्द्र प्रतिज्ञां मम निश्चलाम्॥
en: Moreover, O foremost of kings, I say that my resolution is decided. I never think of perjuring myself; I never think of my defeat. I never think of keeping the least part, of any vow I may take, unredeemed.

description: The solemn declaration of Drona to capture Yudhishthira
sn: न स्मराम्यनृतं तावन्न स्मरामि पराजयम्। न स्मरामि प्रतिश्रुत्य किंचिदप्यनृतं कृतम्॥
en: Sanjaya said Thereupon, O monarch, in the camp of the Pandavas, chonchs and drums and Mridangas together with the Anakas, were simultaneously sounded.

description: The solemn declaration of Drona to capture Yudhishthira
sn: संजय उवाच ततः शङ्खाश्च भेर्यश्च मृदङ्गाश्चानकैः सह। प्रावाद्यन्त महाराज पाण्डवानां निवेशने॥ सिंहनादश्च संजज्ञे पाण्डवानां महात्मनाम्। धनुातलशब्दश्च गगनस्पृक् सुभैरवः॥
en: There arose also loud shouts, like the roar of lions, uttered by the high-souled Pandavas; and the deafening sound resulting from the twang of their bow-strings and the striking of their palms against their arīns, reached the very skies.

description: The solemn declaration of Drona to capture Yudhishthira
sn: श्रुत्वा शङ्खस्य निर्घोषं पाण्डवस्य महौजसः। त्वदीयेष्वप्यनीकेषु वादित्राण्यभिजजिरे॥
en: Hearing that blare of the conchs sounded by the highly-puissant sons of Pandu, your soldiers in their camp struck up various instruments.

description: The solemn declaration of Drona to capture Yudhishthira
sn: ततो व्यूढान्यनीकानि तव तेषां च भारत। शनैरुपेयुरुयोन्यं योध्यमानानि संयुगे॥
en: Thereafter, O Bharata, your, as well their, divisions were formed into battle-array; and slowly then advanced desirous of encountering one another in battle.

description: The solemn declaration of Drona to capture Yudhishthira
sn: तत: प्रववृते युद्धं तुमुलं लोमहर्षणम्। पाण्डवानां कुरूणां च द्रोणपाञ्चाल्ययोरपि॥
en: Then raged a dreadful and hair-stirring battle, between the Pandavas and the Kurus, as also between Drona and the Panchalas.

description: The solemn declaration of Drona to capture Yudhishthira
sn: यत्नमानाः प्रयत्नेन द्रोणानीकविशातने। न शेकुः सृञ्जया युद्धे तद्धि द्रोणेन पालितम्॥
en: Struggling to the best of their endeavours, to slay the division of Drona, the Srinjayas could not accomplish their purpose, as the divisions were protected by Drona himself.

description: The solemn declaration of Drona to capture Yudhishthira
sn: तथैव तव पुत्रस्य रथोदाराः प्रहारिणः। न शेकुः पाण्डवीं सेनां पाल्यमानां किरीटिना॥
en: So also the car-warriors of your son's host, skillful in smiting down the enemy could not vanguish the Pandava division led by the diadem-decked Arjuna himself.

description: The solemn declaration of Drona to capture Yudhishthira
sn: आस्तां ते स्तिमिते सेने रक्ष्यमाणे परस्परम्। सम्प्रसुप्ते यथा नक्तं वनराज्यौ सुपुष्यिते॥
en: Protected by Drona and Arjuna respectively, the two armies, appeared to stand still like two blossoming forests, in the silence of the night.

description: The solemn declaration of Drona to capture Yudhishthira
sn: ततो रुक्मरथो राजन्नर्केणेव विराजता। वरूथिना विनिष्पत्य व्यचरत् पृतनामुखे॥
en: Then, O monarch, that one (Drona) riding on the golden car like the sun himself in radiance, crushing hosts of the Pandavas, careed at will through its various divisions.

description: The solemn declaration of Drona to capture Yudhishthira
sn: तमुद्यतं रथेनैकमाशुकारिणमाहवे। अनेकमिव संत्रासान्मेनिरे पाण्डुसृञ्जयाः॥
en: Then the Pandavas and the Srinjayas considered, through fright, that single carwarrior mounted on a swift-moving car and of great activity in battle, as multiplied in to many.

description: The solemn declaration of Drona to capture Yudhishthira
sn: तेन मुक्ता: शरा घोरा विचेरुः सर्वतोदिशम्। त्रासयन्तो महाराज पाण्डेयस्य वाहिनीम्॥
en: Dreadful shafts shot by him, whizzed in all directions, terrifying, O monarch, the army belonging to the son of Pandu.

description: The solemn declaration of Drona to capture Yudhishthira
sn: मध्यंदिनमनुप्राप्तो गभस्तिशतसंवृतः। यथा दृश्येत घर्मांशुस्तथा द्रोणोऽप्यदृश्यत॥
en: Drona then appeared like the midday sun burning with a hundred light rays that drew out the perspiration from the body.

description: The solemn declaration of Drona to capture Yudhishthira
sn: न चैनं पाण्डवेयानां कश्चिच्छक्नोति भारत। वीक्षितुं समरे क्रुद्धं महेन्द्रमिव दानवाः॥
en: O Bharata, as the Danavas were unable to look at the great Indra, so none among ti army of the sons of Pandu, was able to look his wrathful self (Drona) in battle.

description: The solemn declaration of Drona to capture Yudhishthira
sn: मोहयित्वा ततः सैन्यं भारद्वाजः प्रतापवान्। धृष्टद्युम्नबलं तूर्णे व्यधमन्निशितैः शरैः॥
en: Then that most puissant son of Bharadvaja, stupefying the whole host, speedily blew of the division of Dhrishtadyumna with his sharpened arrows.

description: The solemn declaration of Drona to capture Yudhishthira
sn: स दिशः सर्वतो रुद्ध्वा संवृत्य खमजिह्मगैः। पार्षतो यत्र तत्रैव ममृदे पाण्डुवाहिनीम्॥
en: Obstructing the points of the compass 2 overspreading the whole welkin with his straight-going shafts, Drona commend crushing the division of the Pandava host, even at the place where the son of Prishata was.

sn: संजय उवाच ततः स पाण्डवानीके जनयन् सुमहद् भयम्। व्यचरत् पृतनां द्रोणो दहन कक्षमिवानलः॥
en: Sanjaya said Then Drona creating great confusion c*! the ranks of the Pandava host, trampled : under foot, like a forest-conflagration burning down trees.

sn: निद्रहन्तमनीकानि साक्षादग्निमिवोत्थितम्। दृष्ट्वा रुक्मरथं क्रुद्धं समकम्पन्त सृञ्जया:॥
en: The Srinjayas began to tremble with fear, seeing that enraged hero of the golden cam (Drona), consume their division like a raging conflagration.

sn: सततं कृष्यतः संख्ये धनुषोऽस्याशुकारिणः। जयाघोषः शुश्रुवेऽत्यर्थं विस्फूर्जितमिवाशनेः॥
en: In that battle, they heard the twang of the constantly stretched bow of that warrior of great activity, twang that resembled the rumbling of the thunder.

sn: रथिनः सादिनश्चैव नागानश्वान् पदातिनः। रौद्रा हस्तवता मुक्ताः सम्मृद्नन्ति स्म सायका॥
en: Terrible shafts shot by that one of great lightness of hands, completely crushed carwarriors and cavalry and clephants horses and infantry.

sn: नानद्यमानः पर्जन्यः प्रवृद्धः शुचिसंक्षये। अश्मवर्षमिवावर्षत् परेषामावहद् भयम्॥
en: At the expiration of the summer, like the rain-cloud, assisted by the strong gale, showering its contents, Drona, pouring streams of iron-tipped arrows, struck terror into the hearts of his enemies.

sn: विचरन् स तदा राजन सेनां संक्षोभयन् प्रभुः। वर्धयामास संत्रासं शात्रवाणाममानुषम्॥
en: Then, O king, that puissant one careering through the troops of the enemy and agitating them, aggravated their fears.

sn: तस्य विद्युदिवाभ्रेषु चापं हेमपरिष्कृतम्। भ्रमद्रथाम्बुदे चास्मिन् दृश्यते स्म पुनः पुनः ॥
en: Like flashes of lightning traversing dense of clouds, his bow of golden effulgence, was repeatedly seen to flash in his whirling car that resembled a mass of cloud itself.

sn: स वीरः सत्यवान् प्राज्ञो धर्मनित्यः सदा पुनः। युगान्तकालवद् घोरां रोद्रां प्रावर्तयनदीम्॥
en: That hero, ever devoted to truth, endued with intelligence and firm righteousness, then caused a dreadful river with swelling currents, to flow there, that appeared like the one seen at the end of a Yuga.

sn: अमर्षवेगप्रभवां क्रव्यादगणसंकुलाम्। बलौघैः सर्वत: पूर्णो ध्वजवृक्षापहारिणीम्॥
en: That had its origin in the flow of Dronas wrath; that was infested with numerous masses ever ill carnivorous animals; that was filled with waves consisting of the troops; the ate away the trees (standing on its banks) consisting of heroic warriors.

sn: शोणितोदां रथावर्ती हस्त्यश्वकृतरोधसम्। कवचोडुपसंयुक्तां मांसपङ्कसमाकुलाम्॥
en: That had blood for its waters, cars, for its eddies, elephants and horses for its banks, armours for its rows of lotuses and flesh for the mire filling its bed.

sn: मेदोमज्जास्थिसिकतामुष्णीषचयफेनिलाम्। संग्रामजलदापूर्णो प्रासमत्स्यसमाकुलाम्॥
en: That had, fat, marrow and bones, for its beaches and excellent head-gears for its froth; that had the raging encounter for the cloudy canopy over its surface and the split lances for the fishes that abounded in it.

sn: नरनागाश्वकलिला शरवेगौधवाहिनीम्। शरीरदारुसंघट्टां रथकच्छपसंकुलाम्॥
en: That was inaccessible in conscquence of the corpses of large number of men, elephants and horses; that flew in strong currents constituted by the impetus of the shafts; that had the slain bodies for logs of timber floating on it; that swarmed with tortoises constituted by cars.

sn: उत्तमाङ्गैः पङ्कजिनी निस्त्रिंशझषसंकुलाम्। रथनागह्रदोपेतां नानाभरणभूषिताम्॥
en: That had heads for pebbles scattered on its banks; that had scimitars for the fishes abounding in it; that had elephants and chariots for its lakes; that was adorned with many ornaments.

sn: महारथशतावर्ती भूमिरेणूर्मिमालिनीम्। महावीर्यवतां संख्ये सुतरूं भीरुदुस्तराम्॥
en: That had mighty car-warriors for its hundred little whirlpools; that was ornamented with little wavelets constituted by the dust of the earth; that was capable of being crossed over in battle by those endued with great prowess and incapable of being crossed by the cowards.

sn: शरीरशतसम्बाधां गृध्रकङ्कनिषेविताम्। महारथसहस्राणि नयन्तीं यमसादनम्॥
en: That had heaps of corpses obstructing its navigation; that was haunted by Kankas, and vultures; that carried, by thousand, mighty carwarriors to the regions of Death.

sn: शूलव्यालसमाकीर्णां प्राणिवाजिनिषेविताम्। छिन्नक्षत्रमहाहंसां मुकुटाण्डजसेविताम्॥
en: That was infested by snakes consisting of the (broken) spears; that abounded in aquatic fowls consisting of living fighters, that had torn umbrellas for its large swans and (fallen) diadems for its smaller birds.

sn: चक्रकूर्मो गदानकां शरक्षुद्रझषाकुलाम् बकगृध्रसृगालानां घोरसंधैर्निषेविताम्॥
en: That had wheels (or discs) for its turtles and maces for its sharks and arrows for its smaller fishes; that was resorted to by fearful swarms of crows, vultures and jackals.

sn: निहतान प्राणिनः संख्ये द्रोणेन बलिना रणे। वहन्ती पितृलोकाय शतशो राजसत्तमम्॥
en: And, O foremost of kings, that bore in hundreds to the regions of the ancestral manes, beings slain by the powerful Drona in that battle.

sn: शरीरशतसम्बाधां केशशैवलशाद्वलाम्। नदी प्रावर्तयद् राजन् भीरूणां भयवर्धिनीम्॥
en: That was choked up with heaps of dead bodies; that had hair for its mosses and weeds. O monarch, such a river Drona caused to flow, that enhanced the apprehension of the cowards.

sn: तर्जयन्तमनीकानि तानि तानि महारथम्। सर्वतोऽभ्यद्रवन द्रोणं युधिष्ठिरपुरोगमाः॥
en: Then all those divisions having Yudhishthira at their head, assaulted on all sides that mighty car-warrior Drona who had been uttering loud shouts.

sn: तानभिद्रवतः शूरांस्तावका दृढ़विक्रमाः। सर्वतः प्रत्यगृह्णन्त तदभूल्लोमहर्षणम्॥
en: Then all your heroic troops endued with steady prowess received (unflinchingly) that rushing army on all sides, the result was horripilating

sn: शतमायस्तु शकुनिः सहदेवं समाद्रवत्। सनियन्तृध्वजरथं विव्याध निशितैः शरैः॥
en: Shakuni conversant with hundred kinds of deceitful practices, encountered Sahadeva, piercing the latters charioteer, chariot and flagstaff with sharpened shafts.

sn: तस्य माद्रीसुतः केतुं धनुः सूतं हयानपि। नातिक्रुद्धः शरैश्छित्त्वा षष्ट्या विव्याध सौबलम्।। २३
en: Thereupon the son of Madri, wrought up with ire, cut down with his arrows, the standard, bow, charioteer and steeds of the son of Subala and then pierced the latter with sixty shafts.

sn: सौबलस्तु गदां गृह्य प्रचस्कन्द रथोत्तमात्। स तस्य गदया राजन् रथात् सूतमपातयत्॥
en: Thereupon the son of Subala, grasping a mace, jumped down from his best of cars; then with the stroke of his mace, he felled, O king, the driver of Sahadeva, from his chariot.

sn: ततस्तौ विरथौ राजन् गदाहस्तौ महाबलौ। चिक्रीडतू रणे शूरौ सशृङ्गाविव पर्वतौ॥
en: Then, O monarch, those two heroic mighty warriors deprived of their cars, armed with their clubs, began to roam in the field of battic like two mountains adorned with peaks,

sn: द्रोणः पाञ्चालराजानं विद्ध्वा दशभिराशुगैः। बहुभिस्तेन चाभ्यस्तस्तं विव्याध ततोऽधिकैः॥
en: Drona, having pierced the king of the Panchalas with ten swift-going (shafts), was in return, pierced by him with many shafts; and he then again pierced the latter with a still larger number of arrows.

sn: विविंशति भीमसेनो विंशत्या निशितैः शरैः। विद्ध्वा नाकम्पयद् वीरस्तदद्भुतमिवाभवत्॥
en: Bhimasena pierced Vivinsati with twenty keen-pointed shafts; but being so pierced, he did not tremble; and that was indeed marvelous.

sn: विविंशतिस्तु सहसा व्यश्वकेतुशरासनम्। भीमं चक्रे महाराज ततः सैनयान्यपूजयन्॥
en: But O mighty sovereign, Vivinsati suddenly deprived Bhimasena of his horses, standard and bow; and then the troops highly applauded him.

sn: स तन्न मसृषे वीरः शत्रोर्विक्रममाहवे। ततोऽस्य गदया दान्तान् हयान् सर्वानपातयत्॥
en: But the latter did not tolerate that act of prowess achieved by his adversary in battle; and then with his mace he felled the excellently trajned horses of Vivinsati.

sn: हताश्वात् सरथाद् राजन् गृह्य चर्म महाबलः। अभ्यायाद् भीमसेनं तु मत्तो मत्तमिव द्विपम्॥
en: Then like an infuriated clephant rushing at an infuriated rival, the puissant Vivinsati, grasping a buckler, jumped down from his car the steeds of which had been slain and assaulted Bhimasena.

sn: शल्यस्तु नकुलं वीर: स्वस्त्रीयं प्रियमात्मनः। विव्याध प्रहसन् बाणैालयन् कोपयन्निव॥
en: The heroic Shalya, pierced, smilingly, his own dear nephew Nakula, as if in dalliance, with arrows, in order to excite the latter's Wrath.

sn: तस्याश्वानातपत्रं च ध्वजं सूतमथो धनुः। निपात्य नकुलः संख्ये शङ्ख दध्मौ प्रतापवान्॥
en: But the mighty Nakula, cutting dowii, in the battle, Shalya's steeds, umbrella, standard, charioteer and bow, blew his conch.

sn: धृष्टकेतुः कृपेणास्तान् छित्त्वा बहुविधाञ्छरान्। कृपं विव्याध सप्तत्या लक्ष्म चास्याहरत् त्रिभिः॥
en: Dhristaketu having sundered in twain various shafts shot by Kripa, pierced the latter with seventy arrows; and then with three more cut-off the device on Kripa's standard.

sn: तं कृपः शरवर्षण महता समवारयत्। विव्याध च रणे विप्रो धृष्टकेतुममर्षणम्॥
en: Thereupon Kripa encompassed him with a unighty shower of arrows; thus holding Dhristaketu in check, the Vipra fought on with him, in battle.

sn: सात्यकिः कृतवर्माणं नाराचेन स्तनान्तरे। विद्ध्वा विव्याध सप्तत्या पुनरन्यैः स्मयन्निव॥
en: Satyaki pierced Kritavarman in the middle of his breast with a Naracha; then again piercing him with seventy arrows, he dove many more inside the latter's body laughing all the while.

sn: तं भोजः सप्तसप्तत्या विद्ध्वाऽऽशु निशितैःशरैः। नाकम्पयत शैनेयं शीघ्रो वायुरिवाचलम्॥
en: The warrior of the Bhoja race, then pierced Satyaki with seven and seventy keen pointed arrows; but he failed to move the latter like the fleet wind failing to move the mountain.

sn: सेनापतिः सुशर्माणं भृशं मर्मस्वताडयत्। स चापि तं तोमरेण जत्रुदेशेऽभ्यताडयत्॥
en: Senapati sorely pierced Susarman to the very quick. The latter also struck the former on the shoulder-joint with a Tomara (or lance).

sn: वैकर्तनं त समरे विराटः प्रत्यवारयत्। सह मत्स्यैर्महावीर्यस्तदद्भुतमिवाभवत्॥
en: King Virata, with the highly puissant Matsyas, opposed in battle the of Vikartana. And there raged a wonderful combat.

sn: तत् पौरुषमभूत् तत्र सूतपुत्रस्य दारुणम्। यत् सैन्यं वारयामास शरैः संनतपर्वभिः॥
en: Then a great feat was achieved by the son of the charioteer, when he held the whole force (of Virata) in check with (a shower ot) his shafts of close-joints.

sn: द्रुपदस्तु स्वयं राजा भगदत्तेन संगतः। तयोर्युद्धं महाराज चित्ररूपमिवाभवत्॥
en: King Drupada himself was engaged with Bhagadatta. O mighty monarch, the combat between them was indeed marvellous.

sn: भगदत्तस्तु राजानं दुपदं नतपर्वभिः। सनियन्तृध्वजरथं विव्याध पुरुषर्षभः॥
en: Bhagadatta, the foremost of men, pierced with close-jointed shafts, king Drupada, his charioteer, flag-staffs and chariot.

sn: द्रुपदस्तु ततः क्रुद्धो भगदत्तं महारथम्। आजधानोरसि क्षिप्रं शरेणानतपर्वणा॥
en: Thereupon, wrought up with ire, king Drupada, swiftly struck the mighty car-warrior Bhagadatta on the chest with a close-jointed Shafi.

sn: युद्धं योधवरौ लोके सौमदत्तिशिखण्डिनौ। भूतानां त्रासजननं चक्रातेऽस्त्रविशारदौ॥
en: Those two foremost of warriors on carth, both conversant with the use of weapons, namely, Sikhandin and the son of Somadatta, fought with one another in a combat that inspired terror into the hearts of all creatures.

sn: भूरिश्रवा रणे राजन् याज्ञसेनं महारथम्। महता सायकौघेन छादयामास वीर्यवान्॥
en: Bhurisrava endued with great prowess, O king, covered in battle with a great stream of arrows, the mighty car-warrior, the son of Yajnasena.

sn: शिखण्डी तु ततः क्रुद्धः सौमदत्तिं विशाम्पते। नवत्या सायकानां तु कम्पयामास भारत॥
en: O ruler of men, Sikhandin, filled with rage, picrced the son of Somadatta with ninety shafts and, O Bharata, caused hinm to tremble.

sn: राक्षसौ रौद्रकर्माणौ हैडिम्बालम्बुषावुभौ। चक्रातेऽत्यद्भुतं युद्धं परस्परजयैषिणौ॥
en: The two Rakshasas of fierce deeds, viz., Hidimba and Alambusha, desirous of vanquishing cach other, were engaged in a terrible combat.

sn: मायाशतसृजौ दृप्तौ मायाभिरितरेतरम्। अन्तर्हितौ चेरतुस्तौ भृशं विस्मयकारिणौ॥
en: Capable of creating a hundred illusions, inflamed with arrogance and each desirous of vanquishing the other, they fought a wonderful battle assailing one another with their power of iilusions.

sn: चेकितानोऽनुविन्देन युयुधे चातिभैरवम्। यथा देवासुरे युद्धे बलशक्रौ महाबलौ॥
en: The dreadful Chekitana fought with Anuvindha; they careered through the field of battle, disappearing at times and exciting great wonder.

sn: लक्ष्मणः क्षत्रदेवेन विमर्दमकरोद् भृशम्। यथा विष्णुः पुरा राजन् हिरण्याक्षेण संयुगे॥
en: Lakshmana was engaged in a terrible combat with Kshatradeva, as, O monarch, Vishnu was, in days of yore, engaged with the Daitya Hiranyakashipu.

sn: ततः प्रचलिताश्वेन विधिवत्कल्पितेन च। रथेनाभ्यपतद् राजन् सौभद्रं पौरवो नदन्॥
en: Then, O king, Paurava, uitering a loud roar and mounting on a car, to which were yoked fleet steeds and which was properly furnished, rushed at the son of Subhadra,

sn: ततोऽभ्ययात् सत्वरितो युद्धाकाक्षी महाबलः। तेन चक्रे महद् युद्धमभिमन्युररिंदमः॥
en: Then desirous of battle, Paurava possessed of great might assaulted Abliimanyu. Then that grinder of focs (Abhimanyu) battled fiercely with his antagonist.

sn: पौरवस्त्वथ सौभद्रं शरव्रतैरवाकिरत्। तस्या निर्ध्वजं छत्रं धनुश्चोक्मपातयत्॥
en: Then the son of Puru covered the son of Subhadra with a thick shower of arrows. Then the son of Arjuna cut down on earth the standard, umbrella and steeds of the former.

sn: सौभद्रः पौरवं त्वन्यैर्विद्ध्वा सप्तभिराशुगैः। पञ्चभिस्तस्य विव्याध हयान् सूतं च सायकैः॥
en: Then the son of Subhadra having pierced Paurava with seven swiftly-flying arrows, pierced with five shafts his charioteer and horses.

sn: ततः प्रहर्षयन् सेनां सिंहवद् विनदन् मुहुः। समादत्तार्जुनिस्तूर्णे पौरवान्तकरं शरम्॥
en: Thus imparting delight to his own troops and repeatedly uttering leonine roars, Arjuna's son quickly took in his hand a shaft that was sure to cause Paurava's death.

sn: तं तु संधितमाज्ञाय सायकं घोरदर्शनम्। द्वाभ्यां शराभ्यां हार्दिक्यश्चिच्छेद सशरं धनुः॥
en: The son of Hridika seeing that shaft of dreadful sight fixed on the bow-string (of Subinadra's son) cut it down, along with the bow, with two arrows.

sn: तदुत्सृज्य धनुश्छिन्नं सौभद्रः परवीरहा। उद्ववर्ह सितं खङ्गमाददानः शरावरम्॥
en: Thereupon throwing aside that severed bow, the son of Subhadra, that slayer of inimical heroes, grasping a sharp sword and a buckler jumped down (from his car).

sn: स तेनानेकतारेण चर्मणा कृतहस्तवत्। भ्रान्तासिनाचरन्मार्गान् दर्शयन् वीर्यमात्मनः॥
en: Then whirling that buckler bearing the devices of many stars which seemed to be identified with his hands as also the sword, he careered through the field of battle displaying his prowess.

sn: भ्रामितं पुनरुद्धान्तमाधूतं पुनरुत्थितम्। चर्मनिस्त्रिंशयो राजन् निर्विशेषमदृश्यत॥
en: O king, whirling the weapons by his sides and whirling them on high and shaking them and himself jumping up he made the distinction between the sword and shield to to be imperceptible.

sn: स पौरवरथस्येषामाप्लुत्य सहसा नदन्। पौरवं रथमास्थाय केशपक्षे परामृशत्॥
en: Then with a loud shout he suddenly leapt upon the shaft of Paurava's car; then ascending the car he dragged Paurava by the hair.

sn: जघानास्य पदा सूतमसिनापातयद् ध्वजम्। विक्षोभ्याम्भोनिधि ताह्मस्तं नागमिव चाक्षिपत्॥
en: Then with a kick of his leg he killed the latter's charioteer and with his sword cut down the standard; then he threw off Paurava, like the son of Tarkhya throwing aside a snake that he had seized having agitated the waters of the ocean.

sn: तमागलितकेशान्तं ददृशुः सर्वपार्थिवाः। उक्षाणमिव सिंहेन पात्यमानमचेतसम्॥
en: Then all the rulers of earth saw Paurava with disheveled hair resembling an ox deprived of his senses, while on the point of being felled by a lion.

sn: तमा निवशं प्राप्तं कृष्यमाणमनाथवत्। पौरवं पातितं दृष्ट्वा नामृष्यत जयद्रथः।६२॥
en: Then beholding Paurava at the mercy of the son of Arjuna and dragged like one helpless and fallen on the ground, Jayadratha did not tolerate it.

sn: स बर्हिबर्हावततं किंकिणीशतजालवत्। चर्म चादाय खङ्गं च नदन् पर्यपतद् रथात्॥
en: Grasping a sword and a shield decorated with the emblem of a peacock and furnished with a row of hundred small tinklers and uttering a loud roar, he jumped down from his chariot.

sn: ततः सैन्धवमालोक्य कार्ष्णिरुत्सृज्य पौरवम्। उत्पपात रथात् तूर्णे श्येनवनिपपात च॥
en: Thereupon the nephew of of Krishna beholding the prince of the Sindhus, left Paurava alone and like a hawk suddenly jumped down from the latter's car.

sn: प्रासपट्टिशनिस्त्रिशाञ्छत्रुभिः सम्प्रचोदितान्। चिच्छेद चासिना कार्ष्णिश्चर्मणा संसरोध च॥
en: The nephew of Krishna, severed down with his sword or warded off with his shield, the Prasas (lances) Pattishas (axes) and scimitars directed to him by his enemies.

sn: स दर्शयित्वा सैन्यानां स्वबाहुबलमात्मनः। तमुद्यम्य महाखङ्गं चर्म चाथ पुनर्बली॥ वृद्धक्षत्रस्य दायादं पितुरत्यन्तवैरिणम्। ससाराभिमुखः शूरः शार्दूल इव कुञ्जरम्॥
en: Then displaying to the troops the might of his own arms, that puissant hero again uplifting his heavy sword and his shield, advanced towards the son of Vriddhakshatra, the eternal enemy of his father, like a tiger rushing at an elephant.

sn: तौ परस्परमासाद्य खड्गदन्तनखायुधौ। हृष्टवत् सम्प्रजह्राते व्याघ्रकेसरिणाविव॥
en: Then having encountered each other as if out of delight, they began to strike each other with their swords, like a tiger and a lion attacking each other with teeth and claws.

sn: सम्पातेष्वभिघातेषु निपातेष्वसिचर्मणोः। न तयोरन्तरं कश्चिद् ददर्श नरसिंहयोः॥
en: Between those two foremost of men no person could notice any distinctiun regarding the whirl, the strokes and the descent of their swords and shields.

sn: अवक्षेपोऽसिनिर्हादः शस्त्रान्तरनिदर्शनम्। बाह्यान्तरनिपातश्च निर्विशेषमदृश्यत॥
en: There seemed no distinction between them as regards the descent and the whirl of their swords and the warding off of each other's blows.

sn: बाह्यमाभ्यन्तरं चैव चरन्तौ मार्गमुत्तमम्। ददृशाते महात्मानौ सपक्षाविव पर्वतौ॥
en: Then those two high-souled ones, careering inward and outward, in most excellent tracks, appeared like two mountains furnished with wings.

sn: ततो विक्षिपतः खङ्गं सौभद्रस्य यशस्विनः। शरावरणपक्षान्ते प्रजहार जयद्रथः॥
en: Then when the high-famed son of Subhadra was on the point of bringing down his sword on the head of Jayadratha, the latter struck him on his shield.

sn: रुक्मपत्रान्तरे सक्तस्तस्मिंश्चर्मणि भास्वरे। सिन्धुराजबलोद्भूतः सोऽभज्यत महानसिः॥
en: Then that mighty sword, struck into the gold plate of Abhimanyu's buckler, O Bharata, broke (in twain) as the king of the Sindhus tried to take it off with force.

sn: भग्नमाज्ञाय निस्त्रिंशमवप्लुत्य पदानि षट्। अदृश्यत निमेषेण स्वरथं पुनरास्थितः॥
en: Beholding his own sword break, Jayadratha receded six steps and within an wink of the eye, was seen to be mounted on his own car.

sn: तं कार्णिं समरान्मुक्तमास्थितं रथमुत्तमम्। सहिताः सर्वराजानः परिवतः सन्ततः॥
en: Then all the kings in a body encompassed on all sides the nephew of Krishna, who had been then disengaged from the combat and had been sitting on his excellent chariot.

sn: ततश्चर्म च खङ्गं च समुत्क्षिप्य महाबलः। ननादार्जुनदायादः प्रेक्षमाणो जयद्रथम्॥
en: Then the highly puissant son of Arjuna looking at Jayadratha, whirled his sword and buckler.

sn: सिन्धुराजं परित्यज्य सौभद्रः परवीरहा। तापयामास तत् सैन्यं भुवनं भास्करो यथा॥
en: Subhadra's son, the slayer of hostile heroes, having vanquished the king of the Sindhus, consumed the troops led by the latter like the Sun scorching the world.

sn: तस्य सर्वायसी शक्तिं शल्यः कनकभूषणाम्। चिक्षेप समरे घोरां दीप्तामग्निशिखामिव॥
en: Thereupon, at him (Abhimanyu) Shalya hurled, in battle, his dreadful dart made of all iron, decked with gold and resembling a flashing flame of fire.

sn: तामवप्लुत्य जग्राह विकोशं चाकरोदसिम्। वैनतेयो यथा कार्ष्णिः पतन्तमुरगोत्तमम्॥
en: Then like the son of Vinata catching hold of a mighty falling snake, the nephew of Krishna, leaping up caught hold of the dart; and having caught it, he drew his sword out of its sheathe.

sn: तस्य लाघवमाज्ञाय सत्त्वं चामिततेजसः। सहिताः सर्वराजानः सिंहनादमथानदन्॥
en: Thereupon all the monarchs in a chorus uttered a shout resembling the roar of a lion, having seen the lightness and prowess of that one of immeasurable energy (Abhimanyu).

sn: ततस्तामेव शल्यस्य सौभद्रः परवीरहा। मुमोच भुजवीर्येण वैदूर्यविकृतां शिताम्॥
en: There after the son of Subhadra, that slayer of hostile heroes, let go, charging with the might of his arms, the self same dart of Shalya of great resplendence and decked with lapises.

sn: सा तस्य रथमासाद्य निर्मुक्तभुजगोपमा। जघान सूतं शल्यस्य रथाच्चैनमपातयत्॥
en: Then that dart, the resembled a snake that had recently cast off its slough, reaching Shalya's chariot, slew its driver and felled him down from the car.

sn: ततो विराटदुपदौ धृष्टकेतुर्युधिष्ठिरः। सात्यकिः केकया भीमो धृष्टद्युम्नशिखण्डिनौ॥ यमो च द्रौपदेयाश्च साधु साध्विति चुकुशुः। बाणशब्दाश्च विविधाः सिंहनादाश्च पुष्कलाः॥
en: Thereupon Virata, Drupada, Dhristaketu and Yudhishthira, Satyaki, Kaikaya, Bhima, Dhrishtadyumna and Sikhandin, the twins Nakula and Sahadeva and the sons of

sn: शरैः।
en: Draupadi, all exclaimed “Well-done" “Welldone." Whizzing sounds produced by the discharge of various arrows and ample leonine roars.

sn: प्रादुरासन् हर्षयन्तः सौभद्रमपलायिनम्। तन्नामृष्यन्त पुत्रास्ते शात्रोविजयलक्षणम्॥
en: Arose there, imparting delight to the unreceding son of Subhadra. But your sons could not tolerate these indications of victory of their adversaries;

sn: अथैनं सहसा सर्वे समन्तानिशितैः अभ्याकिरन् महाराज जलदा इव पर्वतम्॥
en: And so, suddenly there covered him from all sides, with showers of sharpened shafts, O monarch, like the clouds pouring their contents on the mountain.

sn: तेषां च प्रियमन्विच्छन् सूतस्य च पराभवम्। आर्तायनिरमित्रनः क्रुद्धः सौभद्रमभ्ययात्॥ 1८७॥
en: Then Artayani, the slayer of foes, desirous of doing good to your sons and remembering the overthrow of his charioteer, rushed in rage at the son of Subhadra.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच बहूनि सुविचित्राणि द्वन्द्वयुद्धानि संजय। त्वयोक्तानि निशम्याहं स्पृहयामि सचक्षुषाम्॥
en: Dhritarashtra said O Sanjaya, you have described to me various wonderful accounts of single combats; hearing them I envy those who are blessed with eyes.

sn: आश्चर्यभूतं लोकेषु कथयिष्यन्ति मानवाः। कुरूणां पाण्डवानां च युद्धं देवासुरोपमम्॥
en: In this world, all men will speak of this battle between the Kurus and the Pandavas, resembling that between the celestials and the Asuras, as very wonderful.

sn: न हि मे तृप्तिरस्तीह शृण्वतो युद्धमुत्तमम्। तस्मादार्तायनेयुद्धं सौभद्रस्य च शंस मे॥
en: I am never satiated with the audition of this excellent fight; therefore do you recount to me the (details of the combat between Atrayan and the son of Subhadra.

sn: संजय उवाच सादितं प्रेक्ष्य यन्तारं शल्यः सर्वायसीं गदाम्। समुत्क्षिप्य नदन् क्रुद्धः प्रचस्कन्द रथोत्तमात्॥
en: Sanjaya said Seeing his charioteer overthrown, Shalya uplifting a mace wholly made of iron and in rage uttering a loud shout, jumped down from his excellent car.

sn: तं दीप्तमिव कालाग्निं दण्डहस्तमिवान्तकम्। जवेनाभ्यपतद् भीमः प्रगृह्य महतीं गदाम्॥
en: Thereupon Bhima also grasping a mighty mace speedily encountered him (Shalya) who then resembled the all-destroying fire in effulgence and also the God of death wielding his bludgecn.

sn: जवेनाभ्यपतद् भीमः प्रगृह्य महतीं गदाम्। एह्येहीत्यब्रवीच्छल्यं यत्नाद् भीमेन वारितः॥
en: The son of Subhadra also grasping a huge mace that looked like the thunderbolt itself, called out to Shalya saying 'Come, Come'; but Bhima, with great efforts, prevented him (from joining in the fray).

sn: वारयित्वा तु सौभद्रं भीमसेनः प्रतापवान्। शल्यमासाद्य समरे तस्थौ गिरिरिवाचलः॥
en: Then having dissuaded the son of Subhadra, the puissant Bhimasena, meeting Shalya in battle, stood immovable like a mountain.

sn: तथैव मद्रराजोऽपि भीमं दृष्ट्वा महाबलम्। ससाराभिमुखस्तूर्णं शार्दूल इव कुञ्जरम्॥
en: Also the mighty-powerful king of the Madras, beholding Bhima, rushed at him with impetuosity, like a tiger attacking an elephant.

sn: ततस्तूर्यनिनादाश्च शङ्खानां च सहस्रशः। सिंहनादाश्च संजजुर्भेरीणां च महास्वनाः॥
en: Then there arose the blare of trumpets and conchs by thousands, as also leonine roars and deafening sounds of drums.

sn: पश्यता शतशो ह्यासीदन्योन्यमभिधावताम्। पाण्डवानां कुरूणां च साधु साध्विति नि:स्वनः॥
en: Loud shouts of Well-done' “Well-done' were uttered by hundreds of Kuru and Pandava warriors who had been looking on and rushing against one another.

sn: न हि मद्राधिपादन्यः सर्वराजसु भारत। सोढुमुत्सहते वेगं भीमसेनस्य संयुगे॥
en: Bharata, none among host of kings, except the ruler of the Madras, could withstand in battle, the impetuosity of the attack of Bhimasena.

sn: तथा मद्राधिपस्यापि गदावेगं महात्मनः। सोढुमुत्सहते लोके युधि कोऽन्यो वृकोदरात्॥
en: Also, in this earth, none except Vrikodara, could bear the vehemence of the mace wielded by the king of the Madras, of illustrious soul attack of Bhimasena.

sn: पटैर्जाम्बूनदैर्बद्धा बभूव जनहर्षणी। प्रजज्वाल तदाऽऽविद्धा भीमेन महती गदा॥
en: Then that huge mace, covered over with a 11C/-work composed of hempen strings and gold wires, imparted grcal delight into the hearts of the troops and being wielded by Bhima it seemed to blaze forth.

sn: तथैव चरतो मार्गान् मण्डलानि च सर्वशः। महाविद्युत्प्रतीकाशा शल्यस्य शुशुभे गदा॥
en: Similarly, the mace was getting grace like lightening in the hands of king Shalya when it was being played in orbits, circles and several trends as prescribed for truncheon-war.

sn: तौ वृषाविव नर्दन्तौ मण्डलानि विचेरतुः। आवर्तितगदाशृङ्गावुभौ शल्यवृकोदरौ॥
en: The both Shalya and Vrikodara, whirling their maces and moving in various orders, began to course in various circles.

sn: मण्डलावर्तमार्गेषु गदाविहरणेषु च। निर्विशेषमभूद् युद्धं तयोः पुरुषसिंहयोः॥
en: Whether as regards their circular movements and whirling motions or their wielding of the maces, the fight between those two foremost of men as equal in every respect.

sn: ताडिता भीमसेनेन शल्यस्य महती गदा। साग्निज्वाला महारौद्रा तदा तूर्णमशीर्यत॥
en: The prodigious mace of Shalya being struck against that of Bhimasena, emitted dreadful flashes of fire and then quickly fell into fragments.

sn: तथैव भीमसेनस्य द्विषताभिहता गदा। वर्षाप्रदोघे खद्योतैर्वृतो वृक्ष इवाबभौ॥
en: Similarly the mace of Bhimasena being struck against that of his adversary, resembled a tree lighted by fire-flies during the rainy season at night-fall.

sn: गदा क्षिप्ता तु समरे मद्रराजेन भारत। व्योम दीपयमाना सा ससृजे पावकं मुहुः॥
en: The mace hurled by the king of the Madras in battle, O Bharata, illuminating the welkin, frequently emitted flashes of fires.

sn: तथैव भीमसेनेन द्विषते प्रेषिता गदा। तापयामास तत् सैन्यं महोल्का पतती यथा।॥
en: Similarly the mace hurled by Bhimasena at his foe, consumed the latter's troops like a dreadful meteor shooting down.

sn: ते गदे गदिनां श्रेष्ठौ समासाद्य परस्परम्। श्वसन्त्यौनागकन्येव ससृजाते विभावसुम्॥
en: Then those two excellent of maces, clashing against each other, appeared like two fiercely breathing she-snakes and emitted flashes of fire.

sn: नखैरिव महाव्याघ्रौ दन्तैरिव महागजौ। तौ विचेरतुरासाद्य गदाण्याभ्यां परस्परम्॥
en: Then like two mighty tigers attacking one another with their claws or like two infuriated elephants doing the same with their tusks, those two heroes, coursed (in the field), having grasped their two excellent maces.

sn: ततो गदाग्राभिहतौ क्षणेन रुधिरोक्षितौ। ददृशाते महात्मानौ किंशुकाविव पुष्पितौ॥
en: Then both of them being simultaneously struck with those excellent of maces, were soon besmeared with blood and they resembled two Kinshuka trees decked with blossoms.

sn: शुश्रुवे दिक्षु सर्वासु तयोः पुरुषसिंहयोः। गदाभिधातसंहादः शक्राशनिरवोपमः॥२४॥
en: Then in all the points of the compass was heard, like the rumbling of Shakra's thunder, the sound generated by the clash of the maces wielded by those two foremost of men.

sn: गदया मद्रराजेन सब्यदक्षिणमाहतः। नाकम्पत तदा भीमो भिद्यमान इवाचलः॥
en: Struck with the mace of the ruler of the Madras both on the left and on the right side, Bhima did not tremble, even like a mountain cleft open (by the thunder-bolt).

sn: तथा भीमगदावेगैस्ताड्यमानो महाबलः। धैर्यानमद्राधिपस्तस्थौ वचैर्गिरिरिवाहतः॥
en: Also the puissant king of the Madras being struck by impetus of the mace of Bhima, patiently stood immovable like a mountain riven by the thunder-bolt itself.

sn: आपेततुर्महावेगौ समुच्छ्रितगदावुभौ। पुनरन्तरमार्गस्थौ मण्डलानि विचेरतुः॥
en: Upraising their maces, they assaulted one another with great impetus; they then again began to course in shorter circles.

sn: अथाप्लुत्य पदान्यष्टौ संनिपत्य गजाविव। सहसा लोहदण्डाभ्यामन्योन्यमभिजघ्नतुः॥
en: Leaping over space measuring eight steps and falling upon one another like two rival elephants, they began to strike with vehemence, one another, with their iron bludgeons.

sn: तौ परस्परवेगाच्च गदाभ्यां च भृशाहतौ। युगपत् पेततुर्वीरौ क्षिताविन्द्रध्वजाविव॥
en: In consequence of their great impetus and being struck sorely with each other's mace, those two heroes simultaneously fell down on earth like two poles raised in honour of Indra.

sn: ततो विह्वलमानं तं निःश्वसन्तं पुनः पुनः। शल्यमभ्यपतत् तूर्णे कृतवर्मा महारथः॥
en: Thereupon the mighty car-warrior Kritavarman speedily came to Shalya's rescue who was deprived of his senses and was breathing quickly.

sn: दृष्ट्वा चैनं महाराज गदयाभिनिपीडितम्। विचेष्टन्तं यथा नागं मूर्च्छयाभिपरिप्लुतम्॥
en: Seeing Shalya crushed with the stroke of the mace and writhing like a snake and overwhelmed with a swoon, O monarch.

sn: ततः स्वरथमारोष्य मद्राणामधिपं रणे। अपोवाह रणात् तूर्णे कृतवर्मा महारथः॥
en: The mighty car-warrior car-warrior Kritavarman, speedily taking up the ruler of the Madras on his car carried him away from the field of battle.

sn: क्षीबवद् विह्वलो वीरो निमेषात् पुनरुत्थितः। भीमोऽपि सुमहाबाहुर्गदापाणिरदृश्यत॥
en: Though unconscious like one drunk the mighty-armed and heroic Bhima rose up in a twinkling of the eye and was seen standing with his mace in his grost.

sn: ततो मद्राधिपं दृष्ट्वा तव पुत्राः पराङ्मुखम्। सनागपत्त्यश्वरथाः समकम्पन्त मारिष॥
en: Thereupon your sons-seeing the king of the Madras turn back from the field of battle, O Sire, began to tremble supported though they were by elephant, infantry, cavalry and cars.

sn: ते पाण्डवैरर्यमानास्तावका जितकाशिभिः। भीता दिशोऽन्वपद्यन्त वातनुन्ना घना इव।॥
en: The warriors of your army being crushed by the Pandavas desirous of victory and struck with fear, fled in all directions like clouds driven by the storm.

sn: निर्जित्य धार्तराष्ट्रांस्तु पाण्डवेया महारथाः। व्यरोचन्त रणे राजन् दीप्यमाना इवाग्नयः॥
en: The mighty warriors, Oking, of the Pandava host having vanquished, in battle, the army of Dhritarashtra, appeared effulgent like blazing fires.

sn: सिंहनादान् भृशं चक्रुः शङ्खान् दध्मुश्च हर्षिताः। भेरीश्च वादयामासुर्मृदङ्गांश्चानकैः सह॥
en: Transported with joy, they blew their conchs and gave forth roars resembling those of the lions and struck up their drums along with Mridangas and cymbals.

sn: संजय उवाच तद् बलं सुमहद् दीर्णं त्वदीयं प्रेक्ष्य वीर्यवान्। दधारैको रणे राजन् वृषसेनोऽस्त्रमायया॥
en: Sanjaya said Seeing that army of yours thoroughly routed in battle, O monarch, Vrishasena endued with prowess, single-handed, began to protect it by means of the illusion of this weapons.

sn: शरा दश दिशो मुक्ता वृषसेनेन संयुगे। विचेरुस्ते विनिर्भिद्य नरवाजिरथद्विपान्॥
en: In that battle numerous shafts discharged by Vrishasena flew in all the ten directions of the compass, piercing men, horses, cars and elephants.

sn: तस्य दीप्ता महाबाणा विनिश्चेरुः सहस्रशः। भानोरिव महाराज धर्मकाले मरीचयः॥
en: Like the rays of the sun, o king, mighty arrows of blazing effulgence shot by him, began to fly (on all sides).

sn: तेनार्दिता महाराज रथिनः सादिनस्तथा। निपेतुरुवा॒ सहसा वातभग्ना इव द्रुमाः॥
en: O monarch, pierced by him car-warriors and cavalry began to fall down suddenly on the ground, like trees broken by the hurricane.

sn: हयौघांश्च रथौघांश्च गजौघांश्च महारथः। अपातयद् रणे राजशतशोऽथ सहस्रशः॥
en: That mighty car-warrior felled in battle, O monarch, large divisions of steeds, car-warriors and elephants, by hundreds and thousands.

sn: दृष्ट्वा तमेकं समरे विचरन्तमभीतवत्। सहिताः सर्वराजानः परिवठ्ठः समन्ततः॥
en: Seeing him career along through the field of battle, like one fearless, all the monarchs uniting together encompassed him on all sides.

sn: नाकुलिस्तु शतानीको वृषसेनं समभ्ययात्। विव्याध चैनं दशभिनौराचैर्मर्मभेदिभिः॥
en: The son of Nakula by name Shatanika charged Vrishasena and pierced the latter with ten Narachas that could penetrate into the very vitals.

sn: तस्य कर्णात्मजश्चापं छित्त्वा केतुमपातयत्। तं भ्रातरं परीप्सन्तो द्रौपदेयाः समभ्ययुः॥
en: The son of Karna, in return, sundered his bow and cut down his standard. The sons of Draupadi desiring to rescue their brother, rushed towards him.

sn: कर्णात्मजं शरवातैरदृश्यं चक्रुरञ्जसा। तान् नदन्तोऽभ्यधावन्त द्रोणपुत्रमुखा रथाः॥
en: Soon with their arrowy showers they made the son of Karna disappear from the view. Thereupon car-warriors headed by the son of Drona charged them, removing the shower of their arrows.

sn: छादयन्तो महाराज द्रोपदेयान् महारथान्। शरैर्नानाविधै स्तूर्णं पर्वताञ्जलदा इव॥
en: o monarch, these warriors (headed by Drona's son) speedily covered over the mighty car-warriors namely the sons of Draupadi, with arrows of various description like clouds pouring their contents on a mountain.

sn: तान् पाण्डवाः प्रत्यगृहंस्त्वरिताः पुत्रगृद्धिनः। पञ्चाला: केकया मत्स्याः सृञ्जयाचोद्यतायुधाः॥
en: Prompted by their affection for their sons, the Pandavas quickly encountered them (assailants), being followed by the Panchalas, Kaikayas, Matsyas and Srinjayas, with their arms uplifted.

sn: तद् युद्धमभवद् घोरं सुमहल्लोमहर्षणम्। त्वदीयैः पाण्डुपुत्राणां देवानामिव दानवैः॥
en: Then commenced a fierce and sanguinary and hair-stirring engagement between your army and the army of the sons of Pandu like that between the celestials and the Danavas.

sn: एवं युयुधिरे वीराः संरब्धाः कुरुपाण्डवाः। परस्परमुदीक्षन्तः परस्परकृतागसः॥
en: Thus the heroes among the Kuru and the Pandava hosts, wrought up with wrath, fought with one another looking furiously at one another and nourishing (deadly) hatred for one another.

sn: तेषां दशरे कोपाद् वपूंष्यमिततेजसाम्। युयुत्सूनामिवाकाशे पतत्रिवरभोगिनाम्॥
en: The bodies of those warriors of immeasurable prowess in consequence of their being inspired with wrath, appeared like those of the feathered chief (Garuda) and of the mighty serpents fighting in the skies.

sn: भीमकर्णकृपद्रोणद्रोणिपार्षतसात्यकैः। बभासे स रणोद्देश: कालसूर्य इवोदितः॥
en: The scene of action with Bhima. Karna, Kripa, Drona and Drona's son and Parshata and Satyaki, appeared effulgent like the alldestructive sun that rises (at the time of the universal annihilation).

sn: तदाऽऽसीत् तुमुलं युद्धं निघ्नतामितरेतरम्। महाबलानां बलिभिर्दानवानां यथा सुरैः॥
en: Then there ensued a dreadful battle, like that between the celestials and the Danavas, in which mighty warriors engaged with mighty antagonists smote down one another.

sn: ततो युधिष्ठिरानीकमुद्धतार्णवनि:स्वनम्। त्वदीयमवधीत् सैन्यं सम्प्रदुतमहारथम्॥
en: Thereafter the host of Yudhishthira, setting up a noise loud as that of the (agitated) ocean, fell to slaughter your host, of which the mighty car-warriors have fled.

sn: तत् प्रभग्नं बलं दृष्ट्वा शत्रुभि शमर्दितम्। अलं द्रुतेन वः शूरा इति द्रोणोऽभ्यभाषत॥
en: Then seeing the (Kaurava) host thoroughly shattered and excessively mutilated by the enemy, Drona exclaimed-'You need not fly, Oheroes.'

sn: ततः शोणहयः क्रुद्धश्चतुर्दन्त इव द्विपः। प्रविश्य पाण्डवानीकं युधिष्ठिरमुपाद्रवत्॥
en: Thereafter that hero owning chest-nut steeds, inflamed with rage, like an elephant bearing four tusks, penetrated into the Pandava ranks and rushed at Yudhishthira.

sn: तमाविध्यच्छितैर्बाणैः कङ्कपत्रैर्युधिष्ठिरः। तस्य द्रोणो धनुश्छित्त्वा तं द्रुतं समुपाद्रवत्॥
en: Thereupon Yudhishthira pierced him with shafts, keen-pointed and furnished with feathers of the Kanka bird, Drona also cutting his bow in two charged him with great impctus.

sn: चक्ररक्षः कुमारस्तु पञ्चालानां यशस्करः। दधार द्रोणमायान्तं वेलेव सरितां पतिम्॥
en: Thereat the protectors of Yudhishthira's car-wheels namely Kumara, the glory of the Panchala races, resisted the rushing Drona, like the beach opposing the swelling sea.

sn: द्रोणं निवारितं दृष्ट्वा कुमारेण द्विजर्षभम्। सिंहनादरवो ह्यासीत् साधु साध्विति भाषितम्॥
en: When Drona the foremost of the regenerated ones was seen to be held in check by Kumara, there were heard sounds of carcries and exclamations of Excellent, excellent etc.

sn: कुमारस्तु ततो द्रोणं सायकेन महाहवे। विव्याधोरसि संक्रुद्धः सिंहवच्च नदन् मुहुः॥
en: Then in that baitle, fierce Kumara. wrought up with ire, pierced, with a shaft, Drona on the chest; and then repeatedly uttered roars like those of the lion.

sn: संवार्य च रणे द्रोणं कुमारस्तु महाबलः। शरैरनेकसाहौः कृतहस्तो जितश्रमः॥
en: Then that highly puissant and indefatigable Kumara of great lightness of hands, having held Drona at bay in that battle, pierced him with thousands of shafts.

sn: तं शूरमार्यव्रतिनं मन्त्रास्त्रेषु कृतश्रमम्। चक्ररक्षं परामृनात् कुमारं द्विजपुङ्गवः॥
en: Thereafter the foremost of the twice-born one (Drona) slew Kumara that protector of Yudhishthira's car-wheels who was brave, of illustrious vows and well-versed in the use of weapons and mantras.

sn: समध्यं प्राप्य सैन्यानां सर्वा:प्रविचरन् दिशः। तव सैन्यस्य गोप्ताऽऽसीद् भारद्वाजोद्विजर्षभः॥
en: Then that foremost of the regenerate ones, the son of the Bharadvaja, became the protector of your army, having penetrated into the centre of the Pandava host and coursing on all directions. son

sn: शिखण्डिनं द्वादशभिर्विंशत्या चोत्तमौजसम्। नकुलं पञ्चभिर्विद्ध्वा सहदेवं च सप्तभिः॥ युधिष्ठिरं द्वादशभिद्रौपदेयांस्त्रिभिस्त्रिभिः। सात्यकि पञ्चभिर्विद्ध्वा मत्स्यं च दशभिः शरैः॥
en: Piercing Sikhandin with twelve arrows, Uttamaujas with twenty, Nakula with five and Sahadeva with seven. Yudhishthira with twelve and the sons of Draupadi each with three, Satyaki with five and the ruler of the Matsyas with ten arrows.

sn: व्यक्षोभयद् रणे योधान् यथा मुख्यमभिद्रवन्। अभ्यवर्तत सम्प्रेप्सुः कुन्तीपुत्रं युधिष्ठिरम्॥
en: And rushing at the foremost warriors of the Pandavas in due order, he (Drona) agitated the warlike host in that battle. Then desirous of capturing the of Kunti namely Yudhishthira, he (Drona) charged him.

sn: युगन्धरस्ततो राजन् भारद्वाजं महारथम्। वारयामास संक्रुद्धं वातोद्धतमिवार्णवम्॥
en: Thereupon, 0 monarch, Yugandhara opposed the mighty car-warrior, the son of Bharadvaja, who was inflamed with rage like the ocean swelling with the tempest.

sn: युधिष्ठिरं स विद्ध्वा तु शरैः संनतपर्वभिः। युगन्धरं तु भल्लेन रथनीडादपातयत्॥
en: But Drona, having pierced Yudhishthira with close-jointed shafts, overthrew Yugandhara from his niche in the car with a broad-headed arrow.

sn: ततो विराटद्रुपदौ केकया: सात्यकिः शिबिः। व्याघ्रदत्तश्च पाञ्चाल्य: सिंहसेनश्च वीर्यवान्॥ एते चान्ये च बहवः परीप्सन्तो युधिष्ठिरम्। आवब्रुस्तस्य पन्थानं किरन्तः सायकान् बहून्॥
en: Thereupon Virata and Drupada, Kekaya and Satyaki and Shini and Vyaghradatta, the prince of the Panchalas and Sinhasena ondued with prowess. These and many other warriors, desirous of rescuing Yudhishthira, impeded Drona's path by scattering innumerable arrows.

sn: व्याघ्रदत्तस्तुपाञ्चाल्योद्रोणं विव्याघ मार्गणैः। पञ्चाशता शितै राजंस्तत उच्चुक्रुशुर्जनाः॥
en: Vyaghradatta, the prince of the Panchalas, pierced Drona with fifty whetted arrows; as thereupon, O monarch, the Pandava host uttered a loud shout.

sn: त्वरितं सिंहसेनस्तु द्रोण विद्ध्वा महारथम्। प्राहसत् सहसा हृष्टस्त्रासयन् व महारथान्॥
en: Sinhasena also having quickly pierced the mighty car-warrior Drona, suddenly, out of delight, broke out into a laugh, inspiring terror into the hearts of the mighty car-warriors.

sn: ततो विस्फार्य नयने धनुर्ध्यामवमृज्य च। तलशब्दं महत् कृत्वा द्रोणस्तं समुपाद्रवत्॥
en: Thereupon expanding his eyes and twanging his bow-string and making a loud sound by striking his arms with his palms, Drona rushed upon him (Sinhasena).

sn: ततस्तु सिंहसेनस्य शिरः कायात् सकुण्डलम्। व्याघ्रदत्तस्य चाक्रम्य भल्लाभ्यामाहरबली॥
en: Then Drona of great prowess putting forth his energy, severed the head of Sinhasena decked with ear-rings also that of Vyaghradatta, with a pair of broad-headed shafis.

sn: तान् प्रमथ्य शरवातैः पाण्डवानां महारथान्। युधिष्ठिररथाभ्याशे तस्थौ मृत्युरिवान्तकः॥
en: Then with the shower of his arrows having crushed the inighty car-warriors of the Pandava host, he stood near the chariot of Yudhishthira like the all-destroying Death himself.

sn: ततोऽभवन्महाशब्दो राजन् यौधिष्ठिरे बले। हतो राजेति योधानां समीपस्थे यतव्रते॥
en: When Drona of regulated vows reached the vicinity of Yudhishthira, O monarch, loud cries of 'The king is slain' were uttered by the warriors of Yudhishthira's army.

sn: अब्रुवन् सैनिकास्तत्र दृष्ट्वा द्रोणस्य विक्रमम्। अद्य राजा धार्तराष्ट्रः कृतार्थो वै भविष्यति॥
en: Then the soldiers, beholding the prowess of Drona said, "Today the royal son of Dhritarashtra will attain the fruition of his desire.

sn: अस्मिन् मुहूर्ते द्रोणस्तु पाण्डवं गृह्य हर्षितः। आगमिष्यति नो नूनं धार्तराष्ट्रस्य संयुगे॥
en: This very moment Drona, having captured in battle the son of Pandu, will, being transported with joy, surely return to us and to the son of Dhritarashtra.

sn: एवं संजल्पतां तेषां तावकानां महारथः। आयाज्जवेन कौन्तेयो रथघोषेण नादयन्॥
en: When your soldiers had been thus conversing, the mighty car-warrior, the son of Kunti (Arjuna) rushed there with impetuosity, resounding the welkin with the rattle of his car and

sn: शोणितोदां रथावर्ती कृत्वा विशसने नदीम्। शुरास्थिचयसंकीर्णां प्रेतकूलापहारिणीम्॥
en: Creating, by the carnage he caused, a river, of which the water consisted of blood and the eddies of cars; which was stagnant with bones and corpses of brave warriors and which conveyed creatures to the regions of the departed.

sn: तां शरौघमहाफेनां प्रासमत्स्यसमाकुलाम्। नदीमुत्तीर्थ वेगेन कुरून् विद्राव्य पाण्डवः॥
en: Having crossed that river having the myriad shafts for its forth and abounding in fishes consisting of lances the son of Pandu came there crushing the Kurus with his speed.

sn: ततः किरीटी सहसा द्रोणानीकमुपाद्रवत्। छादयन्निषुजालेन महता मोहयन्निव॥ शीघ्रमभ्यस्यतो बाणान् संदधानस्य चानिशम्। नान्तरं ददृशे कश्चित् कौन्तेयस्य यशस्विनः॥
en: Thereafter the diadem-decked Arjuna suddenly charged Drona's division, covering it with net-work of mighty arrows and stupefying therewith the warriors that followed Drona. Nobody was able to perceive any interval between the swift placing of the arrows on the bow-string and their discharge by the wellrenowned son of Kunti.

sn: न दिशो नान्तरिक्षं च न द्यौर्नेव च मेदिनी। अदृश्यन्त महाराज बाणभूता इवाभवन्॥
en: Neither the cardinal quarters, not the welkin, nor the conclave dome, nor the earth, could be seen any longer, O monarch; everything then appeared to be a continuous mass of arrows.

sn: नादृश्यत तदा राजंस्तत्र किंचन संयुगे। बाणान्धकारे महति कृते गाण्डीवधन्वना॥
en: Then when the wielder of the Gandiva had caused a 'palpable darkness' in the field of the battle with his shafts, nothing, O monarch, could be distinguished.

sn: सूर्ये चास्तमनुप्राप्ते तमसा चाभिसंवृते। नाज्ञायत तदा शत्रुर्न सुहन च कश्चन॥
en: At the setting of the sun at that moment, and at the enveloping of the earth with dusk, neither foe nor friend could be distinguished any longer.

sn: ततोऽवहारं चक्रुस्ते द्रोणदुर्योधनादयः। तान् विदित्वा पुनस्त्रस्तानयुद्धमनसः परान्॥
en: Thereupon Drona and Duryodhana and others began to withdraw their forces. Considering his enemies to be inspired with terror and unwilling to carry on the fight.

sn: स्वान्यनीकानि बीभत्सुः शनकैरवहारयत्। ततोऽभितुष्टुवुः पार्थे प्रहृष्टाः पाण्डुसंजयाः॥ पञ्चालाश्च मनोज्ञाभिर्वाग्भिः सूर्यमिवर्षयः। एवं स्वशिबिरं प्रायाज्जित्वा शत्रून् धनंजयः॥ पृष्ठतः सर्वसैन्यानां मुदितो वै सकेशवः॥
en: Vibhatsu also slowly withdrew his own divisions; then the Pandus and the Srinjayas and the Panchalas highly delighted began to praise the son of Pritha (Arjuna), with agreeable words, like the Rishis praising the Sun. Thus having vanquished his foes Dhananjaya, filled with rapture and accompanied by Keshava, retired to his own camp, bringing up the rear of his whole army.

sn: वज्रप्रवालस्फटिकैश्च मुख्यैः। चित्रे रथे पाण्डुसुतो बभासे नक्षत्रचित्रे वियतीव चन्द्रः॥
en: Seated in the terrace of his excellent chariot adorned with emeralds and rubies and diamonds of the first water and with the costliest specimens of gold, silver, corals and crystal, the son of Pandu shone like the moon in the heavens adorned with the stars. costliest specimens of gold, silver, corals and crystal, the son of Pandu shone like the moon in the heavens adorned with the stars.

sn: संजय उवाच ते सेने शिबिरं गत्वा न्यविशेतां विशाम्पते। यथाभागं यथान्यायं यथागुल्मं च सर्वशः॥
en: Sanjaya said O lord of men, the troops having retired to their camps, duly took up their quarters, according to the divisions and ranks to which they belonged.

sn: कृत्वावहारं सैन्यानां द्रोणः परमदुर्मनाः। दुर्योधनमभिप्रेक्ष्य सव्रीडमिदमब्रवीत्॥
en: Having withdrawn his soldiers, Drona, with a dejected heart, seeing Duryodhana, spoke these words in shame.

sn: उक्तमेतन्मया पूर्वं न तिष्ठति धनंजये। शक्यो ग्रहीतुं संग्रामे देवैरपि युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: ‘I have told you before, that when Dhananjaya stays by the side of Yudhishthira, even the celestials will not be able to capture the latter in battle.

sn: इति तद् वः प्रयततां कृतं पार्थेन संयुगे। मा विशङ्कीर्वचो मह्यमजेयौ कृष्णपाण्डवौ॥
en: You all assaulted Partha in battle, but he defeated all of you; do not doubt my words; Krishna and the son of Pandu are incapable of being vanquished in battle.

sn: अपनीते तु योगेन केनचिच्छ्वेतवाहने। तत एष्यति मे राजन् वशमेष युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: If however by any means Arjuna owning white steeds cab be taken away from the side of Yudhishthira , then, O king, even today may Yudhishthira be brought under your sway.

sn: कश्चिदाहूय तं संख्ये देशमन्यं प्रकर्षतु। तमजित्वा न कौन्तेयो निवर्तेत कथंचन॥
en: Let some one challenging him (Arjuna) in battle take him to another part of the field. The son of Kunti will not return without having vanquished him.

sn: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे शून्ये धर्मराजमहं नुप। ग्रहीष्यामि चमूं भित्त्वा धृष्टद्युम्नस्य पश्यतः॥
en: O monarch, during that interval when Yudhishthira will be deprived of the help of Arjuna, I, penetrating through the Pandava hosts, will capture the very virtuous king, even before the very eyes of Dhrishtadyumna.

sn: अर्जुनेन विहीनस्तु यदि नोत्सृजते रणम्। मामुपायान्तमालोक्य गृहीतं विद्धि पाण्डवम्॥
en: Thus, O monarch, I will today with certitude bring under your control Yudhishthira, the son of Dharma, with all his followers.

sn: एवं तेऽहं महाराज धर्मपुत्रं युधिष्ठिरम्। समानेष्यामि सगणं वशमद्य न संशयः॥ यदि तिष्ठति संग्रामे मुहूर्तमपि पाण्डवः। अथापयाति संग्रामाद् विजयात् तद् विशिष्यते॥
en: If, in battle, that son of Pandu stays only for one moment (before me) then I will bring him (a captive) from the field; surely that achievement will be more advantage than victory over the hostile army.'

sn: संजय उवाच द्रोणस्य तद् वचः श्रुत्वा त्रिगर्ताधिपतिस्तदा। भ्रातृभिः सहितो राजन्निदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Sanjaya said Thereat, having listened to these words of Drona, the ruler of the Trigarttas united with his brothers, spoke these words, O monarch.

sn: वयं विनिकृता राजन् तदा गाण्डीवधन्वना। अनाग:स्वपि चागस्तत् कृतमस्मासु तेन वै॥
en: 'O monarch, we have been very often humiliated by the wielder of the Gandiva bow; O foremost of the Bharatas, though we have done him no harm yet he bears malice against us.

sn: ते वयं स्मरमाणास्तान् विनिकारान् पृथग्विधान्। क्रोधाग्निना दह्यमाना न शेमहि सदा निशि॥
en: We, remembering those various occasions of humiliation, are ever consumed with the fire of wrath and at night can never enjoy sleep.

sn: स नो दिष्ट्यास्त्रसमपन्नश्चक्षुर्विषयमागतः। कर्तारः स्म वयं कर्म यच्चिकीर्षाम हृद्गतम्॥
en: By good fortune it is that Arjuna bearing arms, will become the object of our sight; so we will achieve that feat which our hearts long to accomplish.

sn: भवतश्च प्रियं यत् स्यादस्माकं च यशस्करम्। वयमेनं हनिष्यामो निकृश्यायोधनाद् बहिः॥
en: This act will be agreeable to you and shall redound to our renown. Drawing him out of the field of battle we shall slay him.

sn: अद्यास्त्वनर्जुना भूमिरत्रिगर्ताऽथ वा पुनः। सत्यं ते प्रतिजानीमो नैतन्मिथ्या भविष्यति॥
en: Today the earth will be relieved of the burden of Arjuna or that of the Trigarttas. Truly we resolve this before you and this our resolution will never be falsified?

sn: एवं सत्यरथश्चोक्त्वा सत्यवर्मा च भारत। सत्यव्रतश्च सत्येषुः सत्यकर्मा तथैव च॥ सहिता भ्रातरः पञ्च स्थानामयुतेन च। न्यवर्तन्त महाराज कृत्वा शपथमाहवे॥
en: Satyaratha, Satyavarman, Satyavrata, Satyashu and Satyakarman, O Bharata, having spoken in the same manner. Those five brothers, with their ten thousand cars, retired, O monarch, having taken that oath on the field of battle.

sn: मालवास्तुण्डिकेराश्च रथानामयुतैस्त्रिभिः। सुशर्मा च नरव्याघ्रस्त्रिगर्तः प्रस्थलाधिपः॥ मावेल्लकैललित्यैश्च सहितो मद्रकैरपि। रथानामयुतेनैव सोऽगमद् भ्रातृभिः सह॥
en: The Malavas and the Tundikeras, with thirty thousand cars and that foremost of men Susharman of the Trigartta race, the ruler of Prasthala together with the Mavelakas the Lalithyas and the Madrakas and with ten thousand cars and accompanied by his biothers.

sn: नानाजनपदेभ्यश्च स्थानामयुतं पुनः। समुत्थितं विशिष्टानां शपथार्थमुपागमत्॥
en: And with another ten thousand excellent cars come from various kingdoms, came forward to take the oath.

sn: ततो ज्वलनमान→ हुत्वा सर्वे पृथक् पृथक्। जगृहुः कुशचीराणि चित्राणि कवचानि च॥
en: Then bringing fire, and every one having separately kindled one for himself, they took up mats of kusa grass and excellent mail-coats.

sn: ते च बद्धतनुत्राणा धृताक्ताः कुशचीरिणः। मौवींमेखलिनो वीराः सहस्रशतदक्षिणाः॥
en: Then having donned their armours and having smeared themselves with clarified butter and wearing those mattresses of kusa grass and with their bow strings as their belts, those heroes, who had given away hundreds and thousands as Dakshina.

sn: यज्वानः पुत्रिणो लोक्याः कृतकृत्यास्तनुत्यजः। योक्ष्यमाणास्तदाऽऽत्मानं यशसा विजयेन च।॥
en: Who had accomplished many sacrifices, who had been blessed with sons, who deserved regions of bliss hereinafter, who had done what ought to be done, who were ready to lay down their bodies, who had devoted their souls to the acquirement of fame and victory.

sn: ब्रह्मचर्यश्रुतिमुखैः क्रतुभिश्चाप्तदक्षिणैः। प्राप्याँल्लोकान् सुयुद्धेन क्षिप्रमेव यियासवः॥
en: Who were intent speedily on going to the regions, by being killed in a fair fight, that are attained my means of sacrifices attended with profuse Dakshinas, and by means also of many such other rites, the foremost of which are Brahmacharya and the study of the Vedas.

sn: ब्राह्मणांस्तर्पयित्वा च निश्कान् दत्त्वा पृथक् पृथक्। गाश्च वासांसि च पुन: समाभाष्य परस्परम्॥ प्रज्वाल्य कृष्णवनिमुपागम्य रणव्रतम्। तस्मिन्नग्नौ तदा चक्रुः प्रतिज्ञां दृढनिश्चयाः॥
en: Those heroes having gratified the Brahmanas by giving them golden coin separately and also kine and garments and having addressed one another in loving words, and having kindled the fire, took that oath in the field of battle; then in the presence of that fire they took that oath with a great firmness of resolution.

sn: शृण्वतां सर्वभूतानामुच्चैर्वाचो बभाषिरे। सर्वे धनंजयवधे प्रतिज्ञां चापि चक्रिरे॥
en: Having formed that firm resolution for the death of Dhananjaya they said these words aloud in the hearing of all present.

sn: ये वै लोकाश्चावतिनां ये चैव ब्रह्मघातिनाम्। मद्यपस्य च ये लोका गुरुदाररतस्य च॥ ब्रह्मस्वहारिणश्चैव राजपिण्डापहारिणः। शरणागतं च त्यजतो याचमानं तथा मतः॥ अगारदाहिनां चैव ये च गां निजतामपि। अपकारिणां च ये लोका ये च ब्रह्मद्विषामपि॥ स्वभार्यामृतुकालेषु मोहाद् वै नाभिगच्छताम्। श्राद्धमैथुनिकानां च ये चाप्यात्मापहारिणाम्॥ न्यासापहारिणां ये च श्रुतं नाशयतां च ये। क्लीबेन युध्यमानानां ये च नीचानुसारिणाम्॥ नास्तिकानां च ये लोकायेऽग्निमातृपितृत्यजाम्। तानाप्नुयामहे लोकान् ये च पापकृतामपि॥ यद्यहत्वा वयं युद्धे निवर्तेम धनंजयम्। तेन चाभ्यर्दितास्त्रासाद् भवेम हि पराङ्मुखाः॥
en: Thosc regions that are for the liars, those that are for the Brahminicides, those that are for the drunkards, those that are for a person who has illicit intercourse with the wife of his preceptor. Those that are for him who robs a Brahmana of his property or for him who enjoys the king's allowance (without fulfiling the conditions thereof) or for him who forsakes one seeking shelter in him or for him who slays one asking for favours. Those regions that are for the incendiary, or for the slayer of the kine, or for him that does injury to others or for him thai nourishes ill-will against the Brahınanas. Those regions that are for him who, out of foolishness, does not hold sexual intercourse with his wife during her season, those also that are for men who indulge in sexual intercourse on the day they have to perform a Shraddha, those that are for people who injure their own soul; those that are for men who appropriate things deposited with them out of trust or for those who destroy knowledge or for those who fight with the eunuchs or for those that follow thic mean; those regions that are for the atheists or those that arc for people who abandon the Fires and their own mother or those that are for the sinful,-those regions shall be ours. If we return from the field of battle without having slain Dhananjaya or if afflicted by him we, out of terror, turn away our faces from the field.

sn: यदि त्वसुकरं लोके कर्म कुर्याम संयुगे। इष्टॉल्लोकान् प्राप्तुमानो वयमद्य न संशयः॥
en: If, on the other hand, we can accomplish in battle that feat difficult of achieving, then, for certain, today we shall attain to the most desirable regions.

sn: एवमुक्त्वा तदा राजंस्तेऽभ्यवर्तन्त संयुगे। आट्ठयन्तोऽर्जुनं वीराः पितृजुष्टां दिशं प्रति॥
en: O monarch, having thus spoken, they then proceeded to the fight summoning Arjuna to the southern part of the field.

sn: आहूतस्तैर्नरव्याप्रैः पार्थः परपुरंजय। धर्मराजमिदं वाक्यमपदान्तरमब्रवीत्॥
en: That foremost of men, that conqueror of hostile fortresses, namely the son of Pritha, being summoned by them, said these words without delay to the very virtuous king Yudhishthira.

sn: आहूतो न निवर्तेयमिति मे व्रतमाहितम्। संशप्तकाश्च मां राजन्नाह्वयन्ति महामृधे॥
en: 'Challenged, I will never turn back. This is my firm resolution. These Samshaptakas (those who are sworn to die or to conquer) O king, are calling me to meet them in battle.

sn: एष च भ्रातृभिः सार्धं सुशर्माऽऽह्वयते रणे। वधाय सगणस्यास्य मामनुज्ञातुमर्हसि॥
en: This Susarman with his brothers is summoning me to battle. It behoves you to permit me to slay him and his followers.

sn: नैतच्छकोमि संसोढुमाह्वान पुरुषर्षभ। सत्यं ते प्रतिजानामि हतान् विद्धि परान् युधि॥
en: O foremost of men, I cannot brook this challenge; I do tell you truly, know these hostile heroes to be already slain in battle.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच श्रुतं ते तत्त्वतस्तात यद् द्रोणस्य चिकीर्षितम्। यथा तदनृतं तस्य भवेत् तत् त्वं समाचर॥
en: Yudhishthira said O child, you are perfectly aware of what Drona is intent on doing. Act in such a manner so that his intention may be frustrated.

sn: द्रोणो हि बलवाञ्छूरः कृतास्त्रश्च जितश्रमः। प्रतिज्ञातं च तेनैतद् ग्रहणं मे महारथ॥
en: Drona is endued with prowess and he is heroic, accomplished in the use of weapons, and indifatigable (in battle). O mighty carwarrior, even he has resolved to bring about my capture.

sn: अर्जुन उवाच अयं वै सत्यजिद् राजन्नद्य त्वां रक्षिता युधि। ध्रियमाणे च पाञ्चाल्ये नाचार्यः काममाप्स्यति॥
en: Arjuna said This Satyajit, O monarch, will protect you in battle today; and so long as the prince of the Panchalas lives, the preceptor will not attain the fruition of his desires,

sn: हते तु पुरुषव्याघ्ने रणे सत्यजिति प्रभो। सर्वैरपि समेतैर्वा न स्थातव्यं कथंचन॥
en: If, on the other hand, O master, this foremost of men, Satyajit, be slain in battle, then you shall not stay in the field even if surrounded by all (our warriors).

sn: संजय उवाच अनुज्ञातस्ततो राज्ञा परिष्वक्तश्च फाल्गुनः। प्रेम्णा दृष्टश्च बहुधा ह्याशिषश्चास्य योजिताः॥
en: Sanjaya said Then king Yudhishthira gave Phalguna the permission he sought; and embraced him and cast affectionate glances him and pronounced numerous benedictions on him.

sn: विहायैनं ततः पार्थस्त्रिगर्तान् प्रत्ययाद् बली। क्षुधितः क्षुद्विघातार्थं सिंहो मृगगणानिव॥
en: Having made these arrangement, puissant son of Pritha went to meet the Trigarttas, like a hungry lion falling upon a herd of deer, for assuaging its hunger.

sn: ततो दोर्योधनं सैन्यं मुदा परमया युतम्। ऋतेऽर्जुनं भृशं क्रुद्ध धर्मराजस्य निग्रहे॥
en: on Thereafter the army of Duryodhana highly delighted at the absence of Arjuna from Yudhishthira's side, became infuriated at the thought of the capture of the virtuous monarch.

sn: ततोऽन्योन्येन ते सैन्ये समाजग्मतुरोजसा। गङ्गासरय्वौ वेगेन प्रावृषीवोल्वणोदके॥
en: Thereupon both armies clashed against each other with great vehemence, like the conflux of the rivers Ganga and Sarayu in the rainy season, when they are both swollen with water.

sn: संजय उवाच ततः संशप्तका राजन् समे देशे व्यवस्थिताः। व्यूह्यानीकं रथैरेव चन्द्राकारं मुदा युताः॥
en: Sanjaya said Then, O monarch, the Samsaptakas, filled with joy, stood on the level plain, having, with their chariots, formed an array figuring the moon.

sn: ते किरीटिनमायान्तं दृष्ट्वा हर्षेण मारिष। उदक्रोशन् नरव्याघ्राः शब्देन महता तदा॥
en: O Sire, seeing the diadem-decked Arjuna rush at them, those foremost of men, highly delighted, gave out deafening roars.

sn: स शब्दः प्रदिशः सर्वा दिशः खं च समावृणोत् । आवृतत्वाच्चलोकस्य नासीत् तत्र प्रतिस्वनः॥
en: Those roars filled the subsidiary and the cardinal quarters and also the conclave dome. There were produced no reverberations owing to the field being covered over with men.

sn: सोऽतीव सम्प्रहृष्टांस्तानुपलभ्य धनंजयः। किंचिदभ्युत्स्मयन् कृष्णमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Then Dhananjaya, ascertaining them to be excessively delighted, said these words to Krishna, smiling the while.

sn: पश्यैतान् देवकीगतर्मुमूर्पूनद्य संयुगे। भ्रातृस्त्रैगर्तकानेवं रोदितव्ये प्रहर्षितान्॥
en: Behold, you who have Devaki for your mother, these Trigartta brothers, who are about to fall in battle today, are transported with joy at the time when they really ought to weep.

sn: अथवा हर्षकालोऽयं त्रैगर्तानामसंशयम्। कुनरैर्दुरवापान् हि लोकान् प्राप्स्यन्त्यनुत्तमान्॥
en: Or surely, this is the time for joy for the Trigarttas, as they shall, ere long, attain to those excellent regions which cannot be obtained by the cowards.

sn: एवमुक्त्वा महाबाहुर्हषीकेशं ततोऽर्जुनः। आससाद रणे व्यूढां त्रिगर्तानाममनीकिनीम्॥
en: Having thus spoken to the mighty-armed Hrishikesha, Arjuna encountered in battle the ranks of the Trigartta soldiers disposed of in battle-array.

sn: स देवदत्तमादाय शङ्ख हेमपरिष्कृतम्। दध्मौ वेगेन महता घोषेणापूरयन् दिशः॥
en: Thereafter taken up his conch known as Devadatta of the effulgence of gold, he blew it with great force, filling the points of the compass with the blare.

sn: तेन शब्देन विवस्ता संशप्तकवरूथिनी। विचेष्टाऽवस्थिता संख्ये ह्यश्मसारमयी यथा।॥
en: Terrified at that blare, the car-host of the Samshaptakas stood motionless in the field of battle as if turned into adamant.

sn: वाहास्तेषां विवृत्ताक्षाः स्तब्धकर्णशिरोधराः। विष्टब्धचरणा मूत्रं रुधिरं च प्रसुस्रुवुः॥
en: All their steeds stood with their eyes expanded and their ears, necks and lips paralysed and their legs motionless, and they discharged urine and vomited blood.

sn: उपलभ्य ततः सामवस्थाप्य च वाहिनीम्। युगपत् पाण्डुपुत्राय चिक्षिपुः कङ्कपत्रिणः॥
en: However, regaining consciousness and rallying their forces, the Samsaptakas discharged simultaneously, at the son of Pandu, shafts furnished with the feathers of the Kanka bird.

sn: तान्यर्जुनः सहस्राणि दशपञ्चभिराशुगैः। अनागतान्येव शरैश्चिच्छेदाशु पराक्रमी॥
en: Thereupon Arjuna, capable of manifesting with lightness his prowess in battle, severed t'hose thousand arrows before they could reach him, with fifteen swift-coursing shafts of his.

sn: ततोऽर्जुनं शितैर्बाणैर्दशभिर्दशभिः पुनः। प्राविध्यन्त ततः पार्थस्तानविध्यत् स्त्रिभिस्त्रिभिः॥
en: Thereat they pierced Arjuna with ten whetted shafts separately; and the son of Pritha also pierced them separately with three shafts each.

sn: एकैकस्तु ततः पार्थं राजन् विव्याघ पञ्चभिः। स च तान् प्रतिविव्याध द्वाभ्यां द्वाभ्यां पराक्रमी॥
en: Then, O monarch, each of them separately pierced the son of Pritha with five shafts; and the puissant Partha in return pierced them each with a couple of arrows.

sn: भूय एव तु संक्रुद्धास्त्वर्जुनं सह केशवम्। आपूरयशरैस्तीक्ष्णैस्तडागमिव वृष्टिभिः॥
en: Wrought up with ire, they once again quickly filled Arjuna and Keshava with arrows, like the rains filling up a lake.

sn: ततः शरसहस्राणि प्रापतन्नर्जुनं प्रति। भ्रमराणामिव वाताः फुल्लं दुमगणं वने॥
en: Then those thousands of arrows fell upon Arjuna like hosts of bees falling, in a forest, on trees decked with blossoms.

sn: ततः सुबाहुस्त्रिं शद्भिरद्रिसारमयैः शरैः। अविध्यदिषुभिर्गाढं किरीटे सव्यसाचिनम्॥
en: Thereafter Subahu deeply stuck on the diadem of Savyasachi (Arjuna) thirty shafts made of the hardest adamant.

sn: तैः किरीटी किरीटस्थैर्हमपुजैरजिह्मगैः। शातकुम्भमयापीडो बभौ सूर्य इवोत्थितः॥
en: Having those straight-going shafts furnished with wings of gold stuck on his diadem, Arjuna, as if adorned with ornaments of gold, shone like the rising Sun.

sn: हस्तावापं सुबाहोस्तु भल्लेन युधि पाण्डवः। चिच्छेद तं चैव पुनः शरवर्षैरवाकिरत्॥
en: Then in that battle the son of Pandu, with a broad-headed arrow cut-off the finger-guard of Suvahu and also covered him over with arrowy showers.

sn: ततः सुशर्मा दशभिः सुरथस्तु किरीटिनम्। सुधर्मा सुधनुश्चैव सुबाहुश्च समार्पयत्॥
en: Thereafter Susarman, Suratha, Sudhaman and Subahu, pierced the diadem decked Arjuna with ten arrows each.

sn: तांस्तु सर्वान् पृथग्बाणैर्वानरप्रवरध्वजः। प्रत्यविध्यद् ध्वजांश्चैषां.भल्लैश्चिच्छेद सायकान्॥
en: Thereat, that one bearing the foremost of the monkeys as a device on his banner, pierced them all with several arrows in return and he cut down their golden flag-staffs with broadheadedshafts.

sn: सुधन्वनो धनुश्छित्त्वा हयांश्चास्यावधीच्छरैः। अथास्य सशिरस्त्राणं शिरः कायादपातयत्॥
en: Having severed the bow of Sudhaman, Arjuna slew his horses with his shafts. Then Arjuna severed from the trunk, the head of the former furnished with a head-gear.

sn: तस्मिन्निपतिते वीरे त्रस्तास्तस्य पदानुगा:। व्यद्रवन्त भयाद् भीता यत्र दौर्योधनं बलम्॥
en: At the fall of that brave warrior, his followers, were inspired with terror; and seized with panic they ran to where the army of Duryodhana was.

sn: ततो जघान संक्रुद्धो वासविस्तां महाचमूम्। शरजालैरविच्छिन्नस्तमः सूर्य इवांशुभिः॥
en: Then the son of Vasava, (Arjuna) wrought up with rage, began to destroy that mighty host with his continuous network of arrows, like the rays of the sun destroying the darkness (of night).

sn: ततो भग्ने बले तस्मिन् विप्रलीने समन्ततः। सव्यसाचिनि संक्रुद्धे त्रैगर्तान् भयमाविशत्॥
en: When that host was shattered and scattered in all directions and when Savyasachin was inflamed with wrath, panic seized Trigarttas.

sn: ते वध्यमानाः पार्थेन शरैः संनतपर्वभिः। अमुास्तत्र तत्रैव त्रस्ता मृगगणा इव॥
en: the Then they, slaughtered with the close joined shafts of Partha, were over-whelmed with swoons, in that field, like a terrified herd of deer.

sn: ततस्त्रिगर्तराट् क्रुद्धस्तानुवाच महारथान्। अलं द्रुतेन वः शूरा न भयं कर्तुमर्हथ॥
en: Thereupon, excited with rage, the sovereign of the Trigarttas addressing those mighty carwarriors said, 'Fly not, you heroes, it behoves you not to be seized with panic.

sn: शप्त्वाथ शपथान् घोरान् सर्वसैन्यस्य पश्यतः। गत्वा दौर्योधनं सैन्यं किं वै वक्ष्यथ मुख्यशः॥
en: Having taken dreadful oaths before the eyes of the entire troops, what shall you say to the leaders of Duryodhana's army if now you go back to them?

sn: नावहास्याः कथं लोके कर्मणानेन संयुगे। भवेम सहिताः सर्वे निवर्तध्वं यथाबलम्॥
en: Will we not be the objects of derision in this world, for this (cowardly) act of ours in battle? United together, do you again repair to your own divisions?'

sn: एवमुक्तास्तु ते राजन्नुदक्रोशन् मुहुर्मुहुः। शङ्खांश्च दध्मिरे वीरा हर्षयन्तः परस्परम्॥
en: Thus being spoken to, O monarch. they uttered continuous roars and those heroes blew their conchs imparting delight to one another.

sn: ततस्ते सन्यवर्तन्त संशप्तकगणाः पुनः। नारायणाश्च गोपाला मृत्युं कृत्या निवर्तनम्॥
en: Thereafter that Samshaptaka host once more rallied themselves; and with the Narayana cow-herds, they were determined even to encounter Death himself.

sn: संजय उवाच दृष्ट्वा तु संनिवृत्तांस्तान् संशप्तकगणान् पुनः। वासुदेवं महात्मानमर्जुनः समभाषत॥
en: Sanjaya said Beholding the host of the Samsaptakas one more return to battle, Arjuna thus addressed the high-souled son of Vasudeva.

sn: चोदयाश्वान् हृषीकेश संशप्तकगणान् प्रति। नैतै हास्यन्ति संग्रामं जीवन्त इति मे मतिः॥
en: 'O Hrishikesha urge my steeds against this host of the Samshaptakas. I think they will not give up the battle so long life will be extant in them.

sn: पश्यमेऽस्त्रबलं घोरं बाहोरिष्वसनस्य च। अद्यैतान् पातयिष्यामि क्रुद्धो रुद्रः पशूनिव॥
en: Behold, today, the terrible prowess of my two arms as also that of my bow. This day I will slay them, like Rudra slaying creatures (at the time of the universal annihilation).'

sn: ततः कृष्णः स्मितं कृत्वा प्रतिनन्द्य शिवेन तम्। प्रावेशयत दुर्धर्षो यत्र यत्रैच्छदर्जुनः॥
en: Thereupon Krishna smiling and greeting the invincible Arjuna with auspicious words, pushed in the chariot where-so-ever the latter desired it to go.

sn: स रथो भ्राजतेऽत्यर्थमुह्यमानो रणे तदा। उह्यमानमिवाकाशे विमानं पाण्डुरैर्हयैः॥
en: That chariot, borne in that battle by white steeds, appeared excessively effulgent, like a celestial car borne through the firmament.

sn: मण्डलानि ततश्चक्रे गतप्रत्यागतानि च। यथा शक्ररथो राजन् युद्धे देवासुरे पुरा॥
en: O monarch, like the chariot of Shakra in the battle between the gods and the Asuras in the days of yore, that car moved in circular, backward and forward motions.

sn: अथ नारायणाः कुद्धा विविधायुधपाणयः। क्षादयन्तः शरव्रातैः परिववर्धनंजयम्॥
en: Then the Narayana soldiers inflamed with rage and holding various weapons in their hands, encompassing Dhananjaya, covered him with showers of arrows.

sn: अदृश्यं च मुहूर्तेन चकुस्ते भरतर्षभ। कृष्णेन सहितं युद्धे कुन्तीपुत्रं धनंजयम्॥
en: O foremost of the Bharata, in a moment they, in that battle, made the son of Kunti namely Dhananjaya, together with Krishna, disappear from the sight.

sn: क्रुद्धस्तु फाल्गुनः संख्ये द्विगुणीकृतविक्रमः। गाण्डीवं धनुरामृज्य तूर्णं जग्राह संयुगे॥
en: Wrought up with wrath, Phalguna, doubling his energy in that battle, rubbed his bow Gandiva and quickly grasped it.

sn: बद्ध्वा च भ्रुकुटि वक्त्रे क्रोधस्य प्रतिलक्षणम्। देवदत्तं महाशङ्ख पूरयामास पाण्डवः॥
en: Causing a frown indicative of wrath to gather on his brow, the son of Pandu charged his mighty conch called Devadatta with his breath.

sn: अथास्त्रमरिसंघघ्नं त्वाष्ट्रमभ्यस्यदर्जुनः। ततो रूपसहस्राणि प्रादुरासन् पृथक् पृथक्॥
en: Thereafter Arjuna discharged the weapon called Tashtra that is capable of slaying large divisions of the enemy. Thereupon thousands of separate forms (of Arjuna and Vasudeva) started into existence there.

sn: आत्मनः प्रतिरूपैस्तैर्नानारूपैर्विमोहिताः। अन्योन्येनार्जुनं मत्वा स्वमात्मानं च जजिरे॥
en: Confounded by the various images of Arjuna's self, they fell to slay one another each considering the other to be Arjuna himself.

sn: अयमर्जुनोऽयं गोविन्द इमौ पाण्डवयादवौ। इति ब्रुवाणाः सम्मूढा जघ्नुरन्योन्यमाहवे॥
en: 'This is Arjuna, this is Govinda, these two are the son of Pandu and the descendant of Yadu', uttering these exclamations, and stupefied, they slow each other in that fight,

sn: मोहिताः परमास्त्रेण क्षयं जग्मुः परस्परम्। अशोभन्त रणे योधाः पुष्पिता इव किंशुकाः॥
en: Confounded by virtue of that weapon, they courted destruction through one another's agency. In that battle those warriors shone like flowering Kinshuka trees.

sn: ततः शरसहस्राणि तैर्विमुक्तानि भस्मसात्। कृत्वा तदस्त्रं तान् वीराननयद् यमसादनम्॥
en: Then that weapon. consuming the thousands of shafts discharged by the enemy, conveyed those heroes to the regions of Death.

sn: अथ प्रहस्य बीभत्सुर्ललित्थान् मालवानपि। मावेल्लकास्त्रिगतश्चि यौधेयांश्चादयच्छरैः॥
en: Thereafter Vibhatsu, with a smile, crushed with his arrows the war-like Lalithyas, the Malavas, the Mavelakas and the Trigarttas.

sn: ते हन्यमाना वीरेण क्षत्रियाः कालचोदिताः। व्यसृजञ्छरजालानि पार्थे नानाविधानि च॥
en: Those Kshatriyas, doomed by fate to die, being smitten by the heroic son of Pritha, discharged at him a net-work of diverse arrows.

sn: न ध्वजो नार्जुनस्तत्र न रथो न च केशवः। प्रत्यदृश्यत घोरेण शरवर्षेण संवृतः॥
en: Thereupon, neither Arjuna, nor his car, nor Keshava was to be seen on the field, being covered over by that terrible arrowy showers.

sn: ततस्ते लब्धलक्षत्वादन्योन्यमभिचुकुशुः। हतौ कृष्णाविति प्रीत्या वासांस्यादुधुवुस्तदा॥
en: Then finding their arrows strike the aim, they exclaimed to one another saying 'Krishna and Arjuna are both slain’; and out of delight they waived their garments in the air.

sn: भेरीमृदङ्गशङ्खांश्च दध्मुर्वीराः सहस्रशः। सिंहनादरवांश्चोग्रांश्चक्रिरे तत्र मारिष॥
en: Then those heroes sounded, by thousands, drums and Mridangas and conchs; and, O sire, they also gave forth war-cries resembling the roars of lions.

sn: ततः प्रसिष्विदे कृष्णः खिन्नश्चार्जुनमब्रवीत्। क्वासिपार्थन पश्येत्वां कच्चिज्जीवसिशत्रुहन्॥
en: Then Krishna greatly perspiring, addressed Arjuna covered with sweat, saying 'Where are you, O son of Pritha, I do not see you, do you live, O siayer of your foes.'

sn: तस्य तद् भाषितं श्रुत्वा त्वरमाणो धनंजयः। वायव्यास्त्रेण तैरस्तां शरवृष्टिमपाहरत्॥
en: Hearing those words of his (Krishna's), Dhananjaya quickly dispelled that arrowy shower poured by the enemy, by means of the Vavabha weapon.

sn: ततः संशप्तकवातान् साश्वद्विपरथायुधान्। उवाह भगवान् वायुः शुष्कपर्णचयानिव॥
en: Then the almighty Vayu blew away hosts of the Samshaptakas consisting of steeds elephants, chariots and weapons like heaps of dry leafs.

sn: उह्यमानास्तु ते राजन् बह्वशोभन्त वायुना। प्रडीनाः पक्षिण: काले वृक्षेभ्य इव मारिष॥
en: Borne away by the god Vayu, they appeared highly beautiful like flights of birds, O sire, flying up from trees at the hour of dawn.

sn: तांस्तथा व्याकुलीकृत्य त्वरमाणो धनंजयः। जघान निशितैर्बाणैः सहस्राणि शतानि च।॥
en: Thus causing great anxiety in them, Dhananjaya with great lightness of hands slew, with keen pointed shafts, hundreds and thousands of the enemy.

sn: शिरांसि भल्लैरहरद् बाहूनपि च सायुधान्। हस्तिहस्तोपमांश्चोरूशरैरुक्मपातयत्॥
en: He struck their heads and arms hearing weapons, with broad-headed shafts; and with his arrows he cut down on the ground their thighs resembling the trunks of elephants.

sn: पृष्ठच्छिन्नान् विचरणान् बाहुपार्वेक्षणाकुलान्। नानाडावयवैीनांश्चकारारीन् धनंजयः॥
en: Some had their backs lacerated, some were deprived of their legs, some were hit on the arms, backs and eyes; thus Dhananjaya made his enemies deprived of their various limbs.

sn: गन्धर्वनगराकारान् विधिवत्कल्पितान् रथान्। शरैर्विशकलीकुर्वेश्चक्रे व्यश्वरथद्विपान्॥
