en: Thereat the son of Yajnasena covered the former with a net-work of arrows. Your son endued with prowess appeared beautiful by defeating that shower of arrows.

sn: अङ्गदोऽभिमुखं वीरमुत्तमौजसमाहवे। द्रोणायाभिमुखं यान्तं शरौघेण न्यवारयत्॥
en: Angada checked the heroic Uttamaujasa, with a down-pour of arrows, as the latter advanced in that battle against Drona.

sn: स सम्प्रहारस्तुमुलस्तयोः पुरुषसिंहयोः। सैनिकानां च सर्वेषां तयोश्च प्रतीतिवर्धनः॥
en: The awful encounter between those two foremost of men enhanced the delight of all the soldiers as also of them both.

sn: दुर्मुस्वस्तु महेष्वासो वीरं पुरुजितं बली। द्रोणायाभिमुखं यान्तं वत्सदन्तैरवारयत्॥
en: The mighty bowman Durmukha endued with prowess, resisted with shafts called Vatsadantas, the heroic Purujit was rushing at Drona.

sn: स दुर्मुखं भ्रुवोर्मध्ये नाराचेनाभ्यताडयत्। तस्य तद् विबभौ वक्त्रं सनालमिव पङ्कजम्॥
en: As the latter struck Durmukha between his two eye-brows with a Naracha. Thereupon the countenance of Durmukha appeared charming like a lotus with its stem.

sn: कर्णस्तु केकयान् भ्रातॄन् पञ्च लोहितकध्वजान्। द्रोणायाभिमुखं याताशरव(रवारयत्॥
en: Karna checked with an arrowy shower the Kekaya brothers owning crimson standards, as they rushed towards Drona.

sn: ते चैनं भृशसंतप्ताः शरवर्षैरवाकिरन्। स च तांश्छादयामास शरजालैः पुनः पुनः॥
en: Greatly afflicted, they also covered Karna with a down-pour of arrows. Karna also covered them repeatedly with showers of arrows.

sn: नैव कर्णो न ते पञ्च ददृशुर्बाणसंवृताः। साश्वसूतध्वजरथाः परस्परशराचिताः॥
en: Neither they nor Karna was to be seen being covered over with (clouds of) shafts. Their steeds, drivers and standards and cars were all lost to sight being covered with thick arrowy showers.

sn: पुत्रास्ते दुर्जयश्चैव जयश्च विजयश्च ह। नीलकाश्यजयत्सेनांस्त्रयस्त्रीन् प्रत्यवारयन्॥
en: Your three sons, viz., Duryaja, Jaya and Vijaya resisted the three, viz., king Nila, the ruler of Kasis and king Jayatsena.

sn: तद् युद्धमभवद् धारेमीक्षितुप्रीतिवर्धनम्। सिंहव्याघ्रतरक्षूणां यथर्भमहिषर्षभैः॥
en: Then the fierce combat between them afforded delight to the lookers-on like that between a tiger, a lion and a wolf on the one side and a bear, a buffalo and a bull on the other side.

sn: क्षेमधूर्तिबृहन्तौ तु भ्रातरौ सात्वतं युधि। द्रोणायाभिमुखं यान्तं शरैस्तीक्ष्णैस्ततक्षतुः॥
en: Kshemadhuri and Vrihanta, these two brothers together wounded with keen-pointed shafts, him of the Satvata race, as he advanced towards Drona in all battle.

sn: तयोस्तस्य च तद् युद्धमत्यद्भुतमिवाभवत्। सिंहस्य द्विपमुख्याभ्यां प्रभिन्नाभ्यां यथा वने।॥
en: Then the battle between those brothers and Satyaki became exceedingly wonderful. Like that between a lion and a couple of leaderelephants with rent temples in the woods.

sn: राजानं तु तथाम्बष्ठमेकं युद्धाभिनन्दिनम्। चेदिराजः शरानस्यन् क्रुद्धो द्रोणादवारयत्॥
en: Excited with wrath the ruler of the Chedis, kept away, by discharging shafts, from Drona, king Ambastha who always delighted in battle.

sn: ततोऽम्बष्ठोऽस्थिभेदिन्या निरभिद्यच्छलाकया। सत्यक्त्वा सशरं चापं स्थाद् भूमिमुपागमत्॥
en: Then Ambastha pierced him with a long shaft that penetrated into his very bones. Loosing hold of his bow furnished with arrows, he fell down from his chariot.

sn: वार्धक्षेमिं तु वार्ष्णेयं कृपः शारद्वतः शरैः। अक्षुद्रः क्षुद्रकोणात् क्रुद्धरूपमवारयत्॥
en: The generous son of Sharadvata namely Kripa, with arrows called Kshudrakas, resisted Vardhakshemi of the Vrishni race, whose very appearance reflected wrath.

sn: युध्यन्तौ कृपवार्ष्णेयौ येऽपश्यश्चित्रयोधिनौ। ते युद्धासक्तमनसो नान्यां बुबुधिरे क्रियाम्॥
en: Then those that saw Kripa and him of the Vrishni race-the heroes accomplished in various modes of warfare-engaged in battle with each other, became absorbed in that encounter and they could attend to no other action.

sn: सौमदत्तिस्तु राजानं मणिमन्तमतन्द्रितम्। पर्यवारयदायान्तं यशो द्रोणस्य वर्धयन्॥
en: The son of Somadatta for adding to the glory of Drona, opposed the ever vigilant king Manimanta as the latter rushed towards Drona.

sn: स सौमदत्तेस्त्वरितश्चित्रेष्वसनकेतने। पुनः पताकां सूतं च छत्रं चापातयद् रथात्॥
en: The son of Somadatta then with great activity, cut-off the latter's bowstring, banner, charioteer, umbrella and flag-staff and felled him from his car.

sn: अथाप्लुत्य रथात् तूर्णे यूपकेतुरमित्रहा। साश्वसूतध्वजरूां तं चकर्त वरासिना॥
en: Then the slayer of foes, Yupaketu (owning the devise of a sacrificial stake on his standard) jumping down, with lightness, from the car and cut-off with a best-tempered sword king Manimanta with his steeds, charioteer, standard and chariot.

sn: रथं च स्वयं समास्थाय धनुरादाय चापरम्। स्वयं यच्छन् हयान् राजन् व्यधमत् पाण्डवी चमूम्।।
en: Thereafter remounting his own chariot and grasping another bow and himself urging his steeds, he began to consume the host of the Pandavas.

sn: पाण्ड्यमिन्द्रमिवायान्तमसुरान् प्रति दुर्जयम्। समर्थः सायकौधेन वृषसेनो न्यवारयत्॥
en: Vrishasena, a worthy combatant, checked with an arrowy shower, king Pandya who was rushing to battle like Indra rushing after the Asuras for slaying them.

sn: गदापरिघनिस्त्रिंशपट्टिशायोधनोपलैः। कडङ्गरैर्भुशुण्डीभिः प्रासैस्तोमरसायकैः॥ मुसलैमुद्गरैश्चकैर्भिन्दिपालपरश्वधैः। पांसुवाताग्निसलिलैर्भस्मलोष्ठतृणदुमैः॥ आतुदन् प्ररुजन् भञ्जन निघ्नन् विद्रावयन् क्षिपन्। सेनां विभीषयन्नायाद् द्रौणप्रेप्सुर्घटोत्कचः॥
en: With maces, bludgeons, scimitars, axes stones and other weapons and with sort clubs, mallets, discs, Bhindipalas, battle-axes and with dusts, wind, fire, water, ashes, gravel's, straw, trees, afflicting, smiting, breaking, slaying, routing and throwing down and terrifying the hostile troops, came Ghatotkacha, desirous of getting near Drona.

sn: तं तु नानाप्रहरणैर्नानायुद्धविशेषणैः। राक्षसं राक्षसः क्रुद्धः समाजघ्ने ह्यलम्बुषः॥
en: Excited with wrath, Rakshasa Alambusha began to strike that Rakshasa (Ghatotkacha) with various kinds of weapons and various implements of war.

sn: तयोस्तदभवद् युद्धं रक्षोग्रामणिमुख्ययोः। तादृग् यादृक् पुरावृत्तं शम्बरामरराजयोः॥
en: The encounter that then took place between those two foremost of the Rakshasas, resembled that which took place between Sumeru and the king of the immortals, in days gone by.

sn: एवं द्वन्द्वशतान्यासन् रथवारणवाजिनाम्। पदातीनां च भद्रं ते तव तेषां च संकुले॥
en: Good betide you. Thus amidst that dreadful general engagements, hundreds of single combats were fought between the car-warriors, the elephant-warriors, horse-warriors and footsoldiers of your army and theirs.

sn: नैतादृशो दृष्टपूर्वः संग्रामो नैव च श्रुतः। द्रोणस्याभावभावे तु प्रसक्तानां यथाऽभवत्॥
en: Indeed the battle that then raged between the warriors that were intent on destroying and protecting Drona indeed such a battle was never seen or heard of before.

sn: इदं घोरमिदं चित्रमिदं रौद्रमिति प्रभो। तत्र युद्धान्यदृश्यन्त प्रततानि बहूनि च॥
en: Many were the combats that were seen raging on that field; O lord, some of which were dreadful, some wonderful and some exceedingly terrible.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच तेष्वेवं संनिवृत्तेषु प्रत्युद्यातेषु भागशः। कथं युयुधिरे पार्था मामकाश्च तरस्विनः॥
en: Dhritarashtra said When the Pandavas returned and when division clashed against divisions, how did the warriors of my army and those belonging to the sons of Pritha, endued with activity, fight?

sn: किमर्जुनश्चाप्यकरोत् संशप्तकबलं प्रति। संशप्तका पार्थस्य किमकुर्वत संजय॥
en: What also did Arjuna do to the car-warriors of the Samshaptaka host and what, O Sanjaya, did the Samshaptakas do to Arjuna in return?

sn: संजय उवाच तथा तेषु निवृत्तेषु प्रत्युद्यातेषु भागशः। स्वयमभ्यद्रवन् भीमं नागानीकेन ते सुतः॥
en: Sanjaya said When the Pandavas did return to the charge and when divisions clashed against divisions, your son (Duryodhana) himself at the head of the elephant division, rushed at Bhimasena. son

sn: सर्वतो मदम्। स नाग इव नागेन गोवृषेणेव गोवृषः। समाहूतः स्वयं राज्ञा नागानीकमुपाद्रवत्॥
en: Like an elephant challenged by another or like a bovine bull summoned by a rival, Bhimasena, challenged by the king himself, rushed against that elephant division.

sn: स युद्धकुशलः पार्थो बाहुवीर्येण चान्वितः। अभिनत् कुञ्जरानीकमचिरेणैव मारिष॥
en: And, O sire, that of Pritha, accomplished in battle and endued with strength of arms, soon shattered that host of elephants.

sn: ते गजा गिरिसंकाशाः क्षरन्तः भीमसेनस्य नाराचैर्विमुखा विमदीकृताः॥
en: Those elephants, prodigious like mountains and with ichor exuding from all parts of their bodies, were crushed and compelled to turn back by the Narachas of Bhimasena.

sn: विधमेदभ्रजालानि यथा वायुः समुद्धतः। व्यधमत् तान्यनीकानि तथैव पवनात्मजः॥
en: Indeed as a raging tempest tears away a network of clouds, so did the son of the Wind (Bhima) shatter that host (of elephants).

sn: स तेषु विसृजन् बाणान् भीमो नागेष्वशोभत। भुवनेष्विव सर्वेषु गभस्तीनुदितो रविः॥
en: Scattering arrows on that herd of elephants, Bhima appeared beautiful, like the sun scattering his shining rays on all objects of the world.

sn: ते भीमबाणाभिहताः संस्यूता विबभुर्गजाः। गभस्तिभिरिवार्कस्य व्योम्नि नानाबलाहकाः॥
en: Afflicted with the shafts of Bhima and bespattered with biood, those elephants looked beautiful like various masses of clouds in the heavens streaked with the rays of the sun.

sn: तथा गजानां कदनं कुर्वाणमनिलात्मजम्। क्रूद्धोदोधनोऽभ्येत्य प्रत्यविध्यच्छितैः शरैः॥
en: Thereupon Duryodhana excited with wrath, approached and pierced with whetted shafts the son of the Wind who was afflicting his (Duryodhana's) own division of elephants.

sn: ततः क्षणेन क्षितिपं क्षतजप्रतिमेक्षणः। क्षयं निनीषुर्निशितैर्भीमो विव्याध पत्रिभिः॥
en: Thereat, with blood-red eyes, Bhima within a while, desirous of dragging the king to destruction, began to pierce the latter with winged shafts.

sn: स शराचितसर्वाङ्गः क्रुद्धो विव्याध पाण्डवम्। नाराचैरर्करशम्याभैर्भीमसेनं स्मयन्निव॥
en: Then Duryodhana, covered with arrows on all parts of his body and wrought up with rage, began to pierce the son of Pandu, viz., Bhimasena, with Narachas of the effulgence of the rays of the sun, laughing all the while.

sn: तस्य नागं मणिमयं रत्नचित्रध्वजे स्थितम्। भल्लाभ्यां कार्मुकं चैव क्षिप्रं चिच्छेद पाण्डवः॥
en: Duryodhana had an (artificial) elephant embossed with gems and jewels as the device gracing his banner; this elephant together with the former's blow, the son of Pandu severed with two Bhallas in all haste.

sn: दुर्योधनं पीड्यमानं दृष्ट्वा भीमेन मारिष। चक्षोभयिषुरभ्यागादङ्गो मातङ्गमास्थितः॥
en: Beholding Duryodhana afflicted by Bhima, O sire, the sovereign of the Angas, riding on an elephant, came with a view to afflict Bhima,

sn: तमापतन्तं नागेन्द्रमम्बुदप्रतिमस्वनम्। कुम्भान्तरे भीमसेना नाराचैरार्दयद् भृशम्॥
en: Secing that best of elephants make towards himself with a roar resembling the rumble of the clouds, Bhima struck it sore with a Naracha between its two frontal globes.

sn: तस्य कायं विनिर्भिद्य न्यमज्जद् धरणीतले। ततः पपात द्विरदो वजाहत इवाचलः॥
en: That Naracha, penetrating through the body of the elephant at last struck on the ground. Then that elcphant fell like a mountain struck with the thunder-bolt.

sn: तस्यावर्जितनागस्य म्लेच्छस्याधः पतिष्यतः। शिरश्चिच्छेद भल्लेन क्षिप्रकारी वृकोदरः॥
en: The Mlechha king who could not extricate himself from the dropping elephant was also falling with it; with an admirable lightness of hand, Vrikodara cut-off the head of that monarch.

sn: तस्मिन् निपतिते वीरे सम्प्राद्रवत् सा चमूः। सम्भ्रान्ताश्वद्विपरथा पदातानवमृद्नती॥
en: At the fall of the heroic ruler of the Angas, his division fled in all directions. Horses, elephants and car-warrior, seized with panic, began to crush the foot-soldiers in their fight.

sn: तेष्वनीकेषु भग्नेषु विद्रवत्सु समन्ततः । प्राग्ज्योतिषस्ततो भीमं कुञ्जरेण समाद्रवत्॥
en: When that host had been thus broken and rouled in all directions, the sovereign of the Pragjyotisas rushed at Bhima, riding on his elephant.

sn: येन नागेन मघवानजयद् दैत्यदानवान्। तदन्वयेन नागेन भीमसेनमुपाद्रवत्॥
en: Bhagadatta attacked on Bhimasena by riding on the elephant of Airavata breed using which as vehicle, Indra had defeated the demons and monsters.

sn: स नागप्रवरो भीमं सहसा समुपाद्रवत्। चरणाभ्यामथो द्वाभ्यां संहतेन करेण च॥ व्यावृत्तनयनः क्रुद्धः प्रमथनिव पाण्डवम्। वृकोदररथं साश्चमविशेषमचूर्णयत्॥
en: With its two forelegs and its trunk contracted and with its eyes rolling and inflamed with fury, the elephant seemed to consume the son of Pandu. It then shattered to pieces the car of Vrikodara together with the steeds harnessed thereto. Thereat running on his legs Bhima hid himself underneath body of the elephant.

sn: पद्भ्यां भीमोऽप्यथो धावंस्तस्य गात्रेष्वलीयत। जाननञ्जलिकावेधं नापाक्रामत पाण्डवः॥
en: The son of Pandu did not really fly, for he was acquainted with the science called Anjalikavedha. Getting underneath the elephant's body, that elephant that was intent on slaying him; he began to strike it with his bare arms repeatedly.

sn: गात्राभ्यन्तरगो भूत्वा करेणाताडयन्मुहुः। लालयामास तं नागं वधाकाक्षिणमव्ययम्॥ कुलालचक्रवन्नागस्तदा तूर्णमथाभ्रमत्। नागायुतबलःश्रीमान् कालयानो वृकोदरम्॥
en: He began to afflict that elephant that was intent on slaying him; Whereupon the elephant began to whirl round like a potter's wheel in rapid motion. Possessed of the might of ten thousand elephants, the glorious Vrikodara, having struck the elephant. Came out from underneath its body and stood stood before Supratika.

sn: भीमोऽपिनिष्क्रम्य तत: सुप्रतीकाग्रतोऽभवत्। भीमं करेणावनम्य जानुभ्यामभ्यताडयत्॥ ग्रीवायां वेष्टयित्वैनं स गजो हन्तुमैहत। करवेष्टं भीमसेनो भ्रमं दत्त्वा व्यमोचयत्॥
en: Holding down Bhima with its trunk, Supratika then struck him with its knees. And winding its trunk round the neck of Bhima, it really tried to kill him. Whirling round Bhimasena freed himself from the twine of the elephant's trunk.

sn: पुनर्गात्राणि नागस्य प्रविवेश वृकोदरः। यावत् प्रतिगजायातं स्वबले प्रत्यवेक्षत॥
en: Then once more Vrikodara got under the body of that elephant. Then when he saw a rival elephant of his own army make towards the one (underneath which he was standing).

sn: भीमोऽपि नागगात्रेभ्यो विनिःसृत्यापयाज्जवात्। ततः सर्वस्य सैन्यस्य नादः समभवनमहान्॥
en: Bhima issuing out from under the body of the elephant, ran away with speed. Thereupon cry in whole army.

sn: अहो घिङ् निहतो भीमः कुञ्जरेणेति मारिष। तेन नागेन संत्रस्ता पाण्डवानामनीकिनी॥ सहसाभ्यद्रवद् राजन् यत्र तस्थौ वृकोदरः।
en: 'Alas, Bhima is slain by the elephant' was set up by all the troops, O sire. Frightened by that elephant, the Pandava army suddenly fled, O king, there where Vrikodara was standing.

sn: ततो युधिष्ठिरो राजा हतं मत्वा वृकोदरम्॥ भगदत्तं सपाञ्चाल्यः
en: Thereupon, considering Vrikodara to be slain, king Yudhishthira assisted by the Panchalas, environed Bhagadatta on all sides. a loud

sn: सर्वतः समवारयत्। तं रथं रथिनां श्रेष्ठाः परिवार्य परंतपाः॥ अवाकिरशरैस्तीक्ष्णैः शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः।
en: That foremost of car-warriors Yudhishthira, having surrounded Bhagadatta with cars on all sides, covered the latter with keen-pointed shafts by hundreds and thousands.

sn: स विधातं पृषत्कानामङ्कुशेन समाहरन्॥ गजेन पाण्डुपञ्चालान् व्यधमत् पर्वतेश्वरः।
en: Baffling those myriad shafts with his iron hook, the Mountain-king, (Bhagadatta) agitated with his elephant the host of the Pandavas and the Panchalas.

sn: तदद्भुतमपश्याम भगदत्तस्य संयुगे॥ तथा वृद्धस्य चरितं कुञ्जरेण विशाम्पते।
en: Then, O ruler of men, we did indeed behold a wonderful feat achieved in that battle by the old Bhagadatta, through the instrumentality of his elephant.

sn: ततो राजा दशार्णानां प्राग्ज्योतिषमुपाद्रवत्॥ तिर्यग्यातेन नागेन समदेनाशुगामिना।
en: Then the sovereign of the Dasarnas advanced against the ruler of the Pragjyotisas, mounted on a swift-coursing elephant exuding the temporal juice and moving in a tortuous inotion.

sn: तयोर्युद्धं समभवन्नागयोर्भीमरूपयोः॥ सपक्षयोः पर्वतयोर्यथा सदुपयोः पुरा।
en: Then the encounter that ensued between those two elephants of prodigious appearance, resembled the fight, in the days of yore, between winged mountains covered with trees.

sn: प्राग्ज्योतिषपते गः संनिवृत्यापसृत्य च॥ पार्वे दशार्णाधिपतेर्भित्त्वा नागमपातयत्।
en: Thereafter the elephant of the ruler of the Pragjyotisas, turning and wheeling round, slew the elephant of the king of the Dasarnas, by ripping open its flanks.

sn: तोमरैः सूर्यरश्म्याभैर्भगदत्तोऽथ सप्तभिः॥ जघान द्विरदस्थं तं शत्रु प्रचलितासनम्।
en: King Bhagadatta also, with seven Tomaras of the effulgence of the sur's rays, slew his adversary riding on an elephant just when the latter was about to slip down from his seat.

sn: व्यवच्छिद्य तु राजानं भगदत्तं युधिष्ठिरः॥ स्थानीकेन महता सर्वतः पर्यवारयत्।
en: Thereupon Yudhishthira lacerating king Bhagadatta (with many shafts), surrounding him on all sides with a numerous host of carwarriors.

sn: स कुञ्जरस्थोरथिभिः शुशुभे सर्वतो वृतः॥ पर्वत वनमध्यस्थो ज्वलन्निव हुताशनः।
en: Mounted on his elephant and surrounded on all sides by the car-warriors, he (Bhagadatta) appeared beautiful like fire illumining a mountain surrounded by forests.

sn: मण्डलं सर्वतः श्लिष्टं रथिनामुग्रधन्विनाम्॥ किरतां शरवर्षाणि स नागः पर्यवर्तत।
en: Then mounted on his elephant, he remained inside that compact circle of fierce bow-men riding on chariots and pouring showers of arrows. a

sn: ततः प्राग्ज्योतिषो राजा परिगृह्य महागजम्॥ प्रेषयामास सहसा युयुधानस्थं प्रति।
en: Thereafter the king of the Pragjyotisas, poking his prodigious elephant, urged it towards the chariot of Yuyudhana.

sn: शिनेः पौत्रस्य तु रथं परिगृह्य महाद्विपः॥ अभिचिक्षेप वेगेन युयुधानस्त्वपाक्रमत्।
en: Thereat the mighty elephant twining with its trunks the car of Sini's grandson, threw it violently to distance; but Yuyudhana escaped.

sn: बृहत: सैन्धवानश्वान् समुत्थाप्याथ सारथिः॥ तस्थौ सात्यकिमासाद्य सम्प्लुतस्तं रथं प्रति।
en: His charioteer jumping upon the car, urged the mighty steeds of the Shindhu breed yoked thereto and stopped reaching the spot where Satyaki was sianding.

sn: स तु लध्वान्तरं नागस्त्वरितो रथमण्डलात्॥ निश्चकाम ततः सर्वान् परिचिक्षेप पार्थिवान्।
en: Then that elephani, availing itself of that breach in the circle of cars, came speedily out of it and began to overthrow all the rulers of the carth.

sn: ते त्वाशुगतिना तेन त्रास्यमाना नरर्षभाः॥ तमेकं द्विरदं संख्ये मेनिरे शतशो द्विपान्।
en: Those foremost of men being frightened by that swift-coursing elephant, regarded that single one to be multiplied into hundred elephants, in that battle.

sn: ते गजस्थेन काल्यन्ते भगदत्तेन पाण्डवाः॥ ऐरावतस्थेन यथा देवराजेन दानवाः।
en: The Pandavas crushed by Bhagadatta mounted on his elephant, appeared like the Danavas crushed by Indra mounted on his clephant, appeared like the Danavas crushed by Indra mounted on the Airavata.

sn: तेषां प्रद्रवतां भीमः पञ्चालानामितस्ततः॥ गजवाजिकृतः शब्दः सुमहान् समजायत।
en: When the Panchalas were flying on all sides, a defending and dreadful din was created by their elephants and steeds.

sn: भगदत्तेन समरे काल्यमानेषु पाण्डुषु॥ प्राग्ज्योतिषमभिक्रुद्धः पुनर्भीमः समभ्ययात्।
en: Thus when the Pandavas were being afflicted by Bhagadatta in that battle, Bhima wrought up with wrath once more rushed against the ruler of the Pragjyotisas.

sn: तस्याभिद्रवतो वाहान् हस्तमुक्तेन वारिणा॥ सिक्त्वा व्यत्रासयन्नागस्ते पार्थमहरंस्ततः।
en: Then that elephant drenching with the water spouting from its trunk the horses of the advancing Bhima, frightened them and they carried away Bhima from the field.

sn: ततस्तमभ्ययात् तूर्णं रुचिपर्वाऽऽकृतीसुतः॥ समनञ्छरवर्षेण रथस्थोऽन्तकसन्निभः।
en: Thereafter Ruchiparvan the son of Akriti spcedily rushed at him, mounted on his chariot and pouring showers of arrows like Death himself.

sn: ततः स रुचिपर्वाणं शरेणानतपर्वणा॥ सुपर्वा पर्वतपतिर्निन्ये वैवस्वतक्षयम्।
en: Then that ruler of the mountain tracts possessed of shapely limbs, dispatched, with a straight shaft, Ruchiparvan to the regions of the son of Vivasvan (Death).

sn: तस्मिन् निपतिते वीरे सौभद्रो द्रोपदीसुतः॥ चेकितानो धृष्टकेतुर्युयुनसुश्चादयन् द्विपम्। त एनं शरधाराभिर्धाराभिरिव तोयदाः॥ सिषिचुभैरवान् नादान् विनदन्तो जिघांसवः।
en: On the fall of that hero (Ruchiparvan), the son of Subhadra, the sons of Draupadi, Chekitana, Dhristaketu and Yuyutsu, began to afflict that elephant. Desirous of slaying it; and uttering dreadful roars, they began to pour on it their arrows like showers of rain.

sn: ततः पार्यकुशाङ्गुष्ठैः कृतिना चोदितोद्विपः॥ प्रसारितकरः प्रायात् स्तब्धकर्णेक्षणो द्रुतम्। सोऽधिष्ठाय पदा वाहान् युयुत्सोः सूतमारुजत्॥
en: Then that elephant urged with heels toes and the hook, by its skillful rider, rushed (at them) with speed, with its trunk stretched and eyes and ear fixed trampling upon the steeds of Yuyutsu, the animal crushed his charioteer.

sn: युयुत्सुस्तु रथाद् राजन्नपाक्रामत् त्वरान्वितः। ततः पाण्डवयोधास्ते नागराजं शरैर्दुतम्॥ सिषिचुभैरवान् नादान् विनदन्तो जिघांसवः।
en: O monarch, Yuyutsu fled, forsaking his car, in ail haste. Then the warriors of the Pandava host out of a desire for slaying that foremost of elephants, speedily drenched it with the shower of their arrows, uttering loud shouts all the while.

sn: पुत्रस्तु तव सम्भ्रान्तः सौभद्रस्याप्लुतो रथम्॥ स कुञ्जरस्थो विसृजनिषूनरिषु पार्थिवः। बभौ रश्मीनिवादित्यो भुवनेषु समुत्सृजन्॥
en: At this juncture, your son with speed rushed, against the car or Subhadra's son. King Bhagadatta riding on his elephant and discharging arrows at the foc appeared resplendent like the sun scattering his rays on the earth.

sn: तम निदशभिर्युयुन्सुर्दशभिः शरैः। त्रिभिस्त्रिभिौपदेया धृष्टकेतुश्च विव्यधुः॥
en: Then the son of Arjuna pierced him with twelve shafts and Yuyutsu with ten. The sons of Draupadi and Dhrishtaketu also pierced him with ten shafts.

sn: सोऽतियत्नार्पितैर्बाणैराचितो द्विरदा बभौ। संस्यूत इव सूर्यस्य रश्मिभिर्जलदो महान्॥
en: With those arrows shot with great care stuck on its body, the elephant appeared beautiful. Like a mighty rain-cloud struck with the rays of the sun.

sn: नियन्तुः शिल्पयत्नाभ्यां प्रेरितोऽरिशरार्दितः। परिचिक्षेप तान् नागः स रिपून् सव्यदक्षिणम्॥
en: Urged on by the skill and vigour of its rider and smitten with the shafts of the enemy. That clephant began to throw down right and left, the warriors of the hostile host.

sn: गोपाल इव दण्डेन यथा पशुगणान् वने। आवेष्टयत नां सेनां भगदत्तस्तथा मुहुः॥
en: Like a cow-hcard belabouring with his cudgel the herd in the forest. Bhagadatta began to smite the hostile troops repeatedly.

sn: क्षिप्रं श्येनाभिपन्नानां वायसानामिव स्वनः। बभूव पाण्डवेयानां भृशं विद्रवतां स्वनः॥
en: Like the cawing of the crows pounced upon by the hawks. A confused noise was heard among the Pandava hosts, as they fled with speed.

sn: स नागराज: प्रवराड्कुशाहतः पुरा सपक्षोऽद्रिवरो यथा नृप। भयं तदा रिपुषु समादधद् भृशं वणिग्जनानां क्षुभितो यथार्णवः॥
en: O monarch, then that foremost of elephants being struck with the hook resembled with winged mountains of yore. It struck panic into the hearts of the enemy, like to what the merchants (on board) experience when the (tempest-tossed) sea rushes against them.

sn: र्भयाद् द्रवद्भिर्जनितोऽतिभैरवः। क्षितिवियद् द्यां विदिशोदिशस्तथा समावृणोत् पार्थिव संयुगे ततः॥
en: O monarch, then in that battle, a loud din, was raised by the elephants, car-warriors steeds and kings, as they fled in fear; and that din filled the earth, the welkin, the cardinal and subsidiary directions of the compass.

sn: स तेन नागप्रवरेण पार्थिवो भृशं जगाहे द्विषतामनीकिनीम्। पुरा सुगुप्तां विवुधैरिवाहवे विरोचनो देववरूथिनीमिव॥
en: That monarch (Bhagadatta) with that foremost elephant of his, thoroughly agitated the host of the enemy, like Virochana agitating in battle the celestial host well-protected by the immortals in the days of yore.

sn: भृशं ववौ ज्वलनसखो वियद् रजः समावृणोनमुहुरपि चैव सैनिकान्। तमेकनागं गणशो यथा गजान् समन्ततो दुतमथ मेनिरे जनाः॥
en: The friend of fire (tempest) then began to blow violently. A cloud of dust in a moment covered the firmament and the forces. People began to regard that single elephant at multiplied into many and careering in all directions.

sn: संजय उवाच यन्मां पार्थस्य संग्रामे कर्माणि परिपृच्छसि। तच्छृणुष्व महाबाहो पार्थो यदकरोद् रणे॥
en: Sanjaya said As you have enquired of me of the feats of Partha in that battle, hear, O you of mighty arms, what he achieved in that battle.

sn: रजो दृष्ट्वा समुद्भूतं श्रुत्वा च गजनिःस्वनम्। भगदत्ते विकुर्वाणे कौन्तेयः कृष्णमब्रवीत्॥
en: Seeing the cloud of dust and hearing the noise created by the troops when Bhagadatta was achieving feats of valour, the son of Kunti thus addressed Krishna.

sn: यथा प्राग्ज्योतिषो राजा गजेन मधुसूदन। त्वरमाणो विनिष्क्रान्तो ध्रुवं तस्यैष नि:स्वनः॥
en: O slayer of Madhu, as the ruler of the Pragjyotisas has advanced with impetuosity to the battle, riding on his elephant, this loud noise may be attributed to him.

sn: इन्द्रादनवरः संख्ये गजयानविशारदः। प्रथमो गजयोधानां पृथिव्यामिति मे मतिः॥
en: Well-versed in the management of his vehicle the elephant, he is in no way interior to Indra in battle; and I think, he is either the first or the second of all the elephant warriors on the face of this earth.

sn: स चापि द्विरदश्रेष्ठः सदाऽप्रतिगजो युधि। सर्वशस्त्रातिग: संख्ये कृतकर्मा जितक्लमः॥
en: His elephant is also the foremost of the species, whom no rival dares encounter in battle; the animal is well accomplished in all tactics and indefatigable and beyond the reach of all weapons in battle.

sn: सहः शस्त्रनिपातानामग्निस्पर्शस्य चानघ। स पाण्डवबलं सर्वमबैको नाशयिष्यति॥
en: sinless one, that elephant capable of bearing the showers of all kinds of weapon and even the tongues of fire, will alone, this day, destroy all the troops of the Pandavas.

sn: न चावाभ्यामृतेऽनयोऽस्ति शक्तस्तं प्रतिबाधितुम्। त्वरमाणस्ततो याहि यतः प्रज्ज्योतिषाधिपः॥
en: Save and except us two, there is none who is capable of resisting that animal. Therefore with speed do you drive where the ruler of the Pragjyotisas is.

sn: दृप्तं संख्ये द्विपबलाद् वयसा चापि विस्मितम्। अद्यैनं प्रेषयिष्यामि बलहन्तुः प्रियातिथिम्॥
en: I will, this very day, send, as a dear guest to the slayer of Bala (Indra), this my adversary who is proud of the prowess of his elephant and of his venerable age, in battle.

sn: वचनादथ कृष्णस्तु प्रययो सव्यसाचिनः। दीर्यते भगदत्तेन यत्र पाण्डववाहिनी॥
en: No sooner had Arjuna uttered these words than Krishna drove to the spot where Bhagadatta had been crushing and shattering the Pandava ariny. on

sn: तं प्रयान्तं ततः पश्चादाह्वयन्तो महारथाः। संशप्तकाः समारोहन् सहस्राणि चतुर्दश॥
en: As Arjuna winded his way towards Bhagadatta, the fourteen thousand mighty carwarriors, viz., the Samshaptakas summoned him delightfully from behind.

sn: दशैव तु सहस्राणि त्रिगर्तानां महारथाः। चत्वारि च सहस्राणि वासुदेवस्य चानुगाः॥
en: Of these fourteen thousand, ten thousand mighty car-warriors belonged to the Trigartta clan and the remaining) four sand were the followers of the son of Vasudeva.

sn: दीर्यमाणां चमू दृष्ट्वा भगदत्तेन मारिष। आहूयमानस्य च तैरभवद्धृदयं द्विधा॥
en: Beholding then the ranks of his own army broken by Bhagadatta and Osire, being summoned the other-hand by by the Samshaptakas, Arjuna was scen divided in his heart (purpose).

sn: किं नु श्रेयस्करं कर्म भवेदद्येति चिन्तयन्। इह वा विनिवर्तेयं गच्छेयं वा युधिष्ठिरम्॥
en: He began to reflect-‘Which of these two acts will now be beneficial for me viz., to turn back to the Samshaptakas or to repair to Yudhishthira.'

sn: तस्य बुद्ध्या विचार्यैवमर्जुनस्य कुरूद्वह। अभवद् भूयसी बुद्धिः संशप्तकवधे स्थिरा॥
en: Then, ( perpetuator of the race of the Kurus, deciding with the help of his understanding, Arjuna set his heart steadily on the destruction of the Samshaptakas.

sn: स संनिवृत्तः सहसा कपिप्रवरकेतनः। एको रथसहस्राणि निहन्तुं वासवी रणे॥
en: Then that son of Vasava bearing the device of the money-chief on his standard, suddenly wheeled round with the intent of slaughtering, single handed, those thousands of car-warriors in battle.

sn: सा हि दुर्योधनस्यासीन्मतिः कर्णस्य चोभयोः। अर्जुनस्य वधोपाये तेन द्वैधमकल्पयत्॥
en: Even this was what both Karna and Duryodhana had decided to be the means for bringing about the death of Arjuna; and for this they had planned the double encounter.

sn: स तु दोलायमानोऽभूद् द्वैधीभावेन पाण्डवः। वधेन तु नराग्र्याणामकरोत् तां मृषा तदा॥
en: Then the son of Pandu wavered between his two purposes (of slaying the Samslaptakas and of meeting Bhagadatta). But he baffled the purposes of his enemies by slaying then the foremost among the Samshaptakas.

sn: ततः शतसहस्राणि शराणां नतपर्वणाम्। असृजन्नर्जुने राजन् संशप्तकमहारथाः॥
en: Thereat, O monarch, the mighty carwarriors, of the Samshaptaka host showered upon Arjuna hundreds and thousands of straight-jointed shafts.

sn: नैव कुन्तीसुतः पार्थो नैव कृष्णो जनार्दनः। न हया न रथो राजन् दृश्यन्ते स्म शरैश्चिताः॥
en: Covered with those shafts, neither the son of Kunti, namely Partha, nor Krishna the assuager of the grief of men, nor horses nor chariots, O monarch, could be seen.

sn: तदा मोहमनुप्राप्तः सिष्विदे हि जनार्दनः। ततस्तान् प्रायशः पार्थो ब्रह्मास्त्रेण निजघ्निवान्॥
en: Then when Janardana was overwhelmed with a swoon and was covered with drops of perspiration, the son of Pritha tell to slaughter them in large numbers with his Brahma weapon.

sn: शतशः पाणयश्छिन्नाः सेषुज्यातलकार्मुकाः। केतवो वाजिनः सूता रथिनश्चापतन् क्षितौ॥
en: Hundreds of arms with arrows, bow-strings and bows in their grasps, being severed and also, standards, horses, charioteers and carwarriors, all fell down on the earth.

sn: द्रुमाचलाग्राम्बुधरैः समकायाः सुकल्पिता:। हतारोहाः क्षितौ पेतुर्द्विपाः पार्थशराहताः॥
en: Elephants, resembling in stature huge hills covered with trees or masses of rain clouds and furnished with trappings, having their riders slain, fell down on the ground being struck with the arrows of Partha.

sn: ॥ विप्रविद्धकुथा नागाश्छिन्नभाण्डाः परासवः। सारोहास्तु रणे पेतुर्मथिता मार्गणैर्भृशम्॥
en: Greatly afflicted with the shafts of Partha, steeds with riders on their backs, fell down dead on the ground, with their caparisons and reins severed and their Bandha rent.

sn: सर्टिप्रासासिनखराः समुद्गरपरश्वधाः। विच्छिन्ना बाहवः पेतुर्नृणां भल्लैः किरीटिना॥
en: Severed by Kiritin with his board-headed arrows, the arms of men, having swords, lances and rapiers for their nail and grasping bludgeons, mallets and battle-axes, fell down.

sn: बालादित्याम्बुजेन्दूनां तुल्यरूपाणि मारिष। संच्छिन्नान्यर्जुनशरैः शिरांस्युा प्रपेदिरे॥
en: Heads, O sire, resembling the rising sun or the lotus or the moon, being severed by the arrows of Arjuna, fell down on the earth.

sn: जज्वालालंकृता सेना पत्रिभिः प्राणिभोजनैः। नानारूपैस्तदामित्रान् क्रुद्धे निम्नति फाल्गुने॥
en: When the enraged Phalguna had been thus slaying his foes, the forces seemed to be on fire, being struck with beautiful but deadly shafts of various appearances.

sn: क्षोभयन्तं तदा सेनां द्विरदं नलिनीमिव। धनंजयं भूतगणाः साधु साध्वित्यपूजयन्॥
en: Then all beings honoured Dhananjaya, who had been agitating the forces like an elephant crushing the lotus-stalks, by saying 'Well done,' 'Well-done.

sn: दृष्ट्वा तत् कर्म पार्थस्य वासवस्येव माधवः। विस्मयं परमं गत्वा प्राञ्जलिस्तमुवाच ह॥
en: Beholding that feat of the son of Pritha, which was equal to the one achieved by Vasava himself, Madhava, highly amazed thus spoke to the former, with his hands folded.

sn: कर्मैतत् पार्थ शक्रेण यमेन धनदेन च। दुष्करं समरे यत् ते कृमद्येति मे मतिः॥
en: 'I think, O Partha, the feat you have today achieved in battle is difficult of being performed even by Indra or Yama or Kubera himself.

sn: युगपच्चैव संग्रामे शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः। पतिता एव मे दृष्टाः संशप्तकमहारथाः॥
en: I have seen today slay simultaneously in battle, hundreds and thousands of mighty carwarriors of the Samshaptaka host.'

sn: संशप्तकांस्ततो हत्वा भूयिष्ठा ये व्यवस्थिताः। भगदत्ताय याहीति कृष्णं पार्थोऽभ्यनोदयत्॥
en: Then completely slaying those Samshaptakas who stayed in battle, Partha said to Krishna, ‘Now hasten towards Bhagadatta.'

sn: युगपच्चैव संग्रामे शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः। पतिता एव मे दृष्टाः संशप्तकमहारथाः॥
en: I have seen today slay simultaneously in battle, hundreds and thousands of mighty carwarriors of the Samshaptaka host.'

sn: संशप्तकांस्ततो हत्वा भूयिष्ठा ये व्यवस्थिताः। भगदत्ताय याहीति कृष्णं पार्थोऽभ्यनोदयत्॥
en: Then completely slaying those Samshaptakas who stayed in battle, Partha said to Krishna, ‘Now hasten towards Bhagadatta.'

sn: संजय उवाच यियासतस्ततः कृष्णः पार्थस्याश्वान् मनोजवान्। सम्प्रेषीद्धेमसंछन्नान् द्रोणानीकाय संत्वरन्॥
en: Sanjaya said Upon Partha's desire for advancing against the division of Drona, Krishna urged his steeds covered with golden caparisons, fleet as the mind and white in hue.

sn: तं प्रयान्तं कुरुश्रेष्ठं स्वान् भ्रातृन् द्रोणतापितान्। सुशर्मा भ्रातृभिः सार्धं युद्धार्थी पृष्ठतोऽन्वयात्॥
en: Beholding that foremost of the Kurus make towards his brothers afflicted sore by Drona, king Susarman with his brothers followed him, desirous of battle.

sn: ततः श्वेतहयः कृष्णमब्रवीदजितं जयः। एव मां भ्रातृभिः सार्धं सुशर्माऽऽह्वयतेऽच्युत॥
en: The invincible Arjuna owning white steeds then thus addressed Krishna Krishna saying:-'O Achyuta, this Susarman assisted by his brother challenges me (to fight).

sn: दीर्यते चोत्तरेणैव तत् सैन्यं मधुसूदन। द्वैधीभूतं मनो मेऽद्य कृतं संशप्तकैरिदम्॥
en: O slayer of foes, on the other hand, the ranks of my troops are being shattered, (by Drona); today my mind is undecided in its purposes, which is caused by the Samshaptakas.

sn: किं नु संशप्तकान् हन्मि स्वान् रक्षाम्यहितार्दितान्। इति मे त्वं मतं वेत्सि तत्र किं सुकृतं भवेत्॥
en: Shall I slay the Samshaptakas or shall I save my own army afflicted by the foe. Know this to be what I am thinking of; tell me what would be beneficial for me?

sn: एवमुक्तस्तु दाशार्हः स्यन्दनं प्रत्यवर्तयत्। येन त्रिगर्ताधिपतिः पाण्डवं समुपाह्वयत्॥
en: Thus spoken to, the descendant of the Dasharhas (viz., Krishna), turned the car and drove the son of Pandu to the spot whence the ruler of the Trigarttas was summoning Arjuna.

sn: ततोऽर्जुनः सुशर्माणं विद्ध्वा सप्तभिराशुगैः। ध्वजं धनुश्चास्य तथा क्षुराभ्यां समकृन्तत॥
en: Thereat Arjuna piercing Susarman with seven swift-coursing arrows, cut down his standard, bow and chariot with a couple a razor-sharp arrows.

sn: त्रिगर्ताधिपतेश्चापि भ्रातरं षड्भिराशुगैः। साश्वं ससूतं त्वरितः पार्थः प्रैषीद् यमक्षयम्॥
en: Then with six swift-flying arrows Partha speedily dispatched to the mansion of Death the brother of the ruler of the Trigarttas, with his steeds and charioteers.

sn: ततो भुजगसंकाशां सुशर्मा शक्तिमायसीम्। चिक्षेपार्जुनमादिश्य वासुदेवाय तोमरम्॥
en: Thereat Susarman, aiming at Arjuna, hurled an iron dart resembling a snake and he threw a lance at the son of Vasudeva.

sn: शत्ति त्रिभिः शरैश्छित्त्वा तोमरं त्रिभिरर्जुनः। सुशर्माणं शरव्रातैर्मोहयित्वा न्यवर्तयत्॥
en: Having cut down the dart with three shafts and the lance also with another three, Arjuna compelled Susarman to turn back, depriving him of his senses my means of an arrowy down-pour.

sn: तं वासवमिवायान्तं भूरिवर्षं शरौघिणम्। राजस्तावकसैन्यानां नोग्रं कश्चिदवारयत्॥!
en: None among your host ventured to oppose him, O monarch, as he came looking fierce and showering arrows like Vasava pouring rain.

sn: ततो धनंजयो बाणैः सर्वानेव महारथान्। आयाद् विनिघ्नन् कौरव्यान् दहन कक्षमिवानलः।। १२
en: Then Dhananjaya advanced slaying all the mighty car-warriors of the Kauravas, with his arrows, just as fire advances consuming heaps of straw and fuel.

sn: तस्य वेगमसह्यं तं कुन्तीपुत्रस्य धीमतः। नाशक्नुवंस्ते संसोढुं स्पर्शमग्नेरिव प्रजा॥
en: Like the touch of fire, people were unable to bear the unbearablc impetuosity of that intelligent son of Kunti.

sn: संवेष्टयननीकानि शरवर्षेण पाण्डवः। सुपर्णपातवद् राजन्नायात् प्राग्ज्योतिषं प्रति॥
en: The son of Pandu overwhelming with his arrowy showers the hostile host, made, O monarch, towards the rulers of the Pragjyotisas, like Suparna pouncing down (upon his prey).

sn: यत् तदानामयज्जिष्णुर्भरतानामपापिनाम्। धनुः क्षेमकरं संख्ये द्विषतामश्रुवर्धनम्॥ तदेव तव पुत्रस्य राजन् दुर्दूतदेविनः। कृते क्षत्रविनाशाय धनुरायच्छदर्जुनः॥
en: Then the ever-victorious Arjuna held in his grasp the bow, that was prolific of benefit for the sinless Pandavas and that was capable of enhancing the grief of the enemy in battle, for the destruction of the Kshatriyas, brought about, O king, by your son's recourse to the deceitful fame at dice.

sn: तथा विक्षोभ्यमाणा सा पार्थेन तव वाहिनी। व्यशीर्यत महाराज नौरिवासाद्य पर्वतम्॥
en: Then, () monarch, your troops being thus agitated by the son of Pritha, was broken like a frail bark grounded on a rock.

sn: ततो दशसहस्राणि न्यवर्तन्त धनुष्मताम्। मतिं कृत्वा रणे क्रूरां वीरा जयपराजये॥
en: Thereupon, ten thousand bowmen, brave and inflamed with a fierce determination for battle and disregardful of victory or defeat, turned upon (Arjuna).

sn: व्यपेतहृदयत्रासा आवद्रूस्तं महारथाः। आर्छत् पार्थो गुरुं भारं सर्वभारसहो युधि॥
en: With their hearts shorn of fear, those mighty warriors completely encompassed him. Thereat Partha capable of bearing all burdens how heavy sover, took up that burden in that battle.

sn: यथा नलवनं क्रुद्धः प्रभिन्नः षष्टिहायनः। मृद्गीयात् तद्वदायस्तः पार्थोऽमृद्गाच्चमू तव॥
en: Then Partha began to crush your forces just as an infuriatc elephant of six years of age, with rent temples crushes and tears an assemblage of lotus plants.

sn: तस्मिन् प्रमथिते सैन्ये भगदत्तो नराधिपः। तेन नागेन सहसा धनंजयमुपाद्रवत्॥
en: When the troops were being thus crushed, Bhagadatta, the ruler of men, riding on the selfsame elephant, rushed suddenly at Dhananjaya.

sn: तं रथेन नरव्याघ्रः प्रत्यगृह्णाद् धनंजयः। स संनिपातस्तुमुलो बभूव स्थनागयोः॥
en: Thereupon Dhananjaya that foremost of men, received him. (Bhagadatta), opposing him with his car. Then a fierce encounter raged between that car and that elephant.

sn: कल्पिताभ्यां यथाशास्त्रं रथेन च गजेन च। संग्रामे चेरतुर्वीरौ भगदत्तधनञ्जयौ॥
en: Riding their and elephant respectively which were equipped according to the rules of the military science, those two heroes Dhananjaya and Bhagadatta careered through the field of battle.

sn: ततो जीमूतसंकाशान्नागादिन्द्र इव प्रभुः। अभ्यवर्षच्छरौघेण भगदत्तो धनंजयम्॥
en: Then staying on his elephant that resembled a mass of clouds, the mighty down-pour of arrows, like Indra showering rain.

sn: च चापि शरवर्षं तं शरवर्षेण वासविः। अप्राप्तमेव चिच्छेद भगदत्तस्य वीर्यवान्॥
en: Then the son of Vasava (Arjuna) endued with prowess, cut-off with his arrowy showers, the arrows of Bhagadatta, before they could even reach him.

sn: ततः प्राग्ज्योतिषो राजा शरवर्षे निवार्यत्। शरैर्जघ्ने महाबाहुं पार्थे कृष्णं च मारिष॥
en: Oll car Then, O sire, the king of the Pragjyotisas, baffling that shower of arrows, pierced the mighty-armed son of Pritha, as also Krishna, with his arrows.

sn: ततस्तु शरजालेन महताऽभ्यवकीर्य तौ। चोदयामास तं नाग वधायाच्युतपार्थयोः॥
en: Thereafter covering Krishna and Partha with a thick net-work of arrows, Bhagadatta urged his elephant towards them in order to slay them.

sn: तमापतन्तं द्विरदं दृष्ट्वा कुद्धमिवान्तकम्। चक्रेऽपसव्यं त्वरितः स्यन्दनेन जनार्दनः॥
en: Thereat beholding that infuriate elephant make towards themselves like Death himself, Janardana with swiftness moved his car in a manner as to leave the elephant on the left.

sn: तं प्राप्तमपि नेयेष परावृत्तं महाद्वित्तं महाद्विपम्। सारोहं मृत्युसात्कर्तुं स्मरन् धर्म धनंजयः॥
en: Thus Dhananjaya, though he got an opportunity of slaying that mighty elephant and its rider from the right side, yet did not avail himself of it, recollecting the laws of fair combat.

sn: स तु नागो द्विपरथान् हयांश्चामृद्य मारिष। प्राहिणोन्मृत्युलोकाय ततः क्रुद्धो धनंजयः॥
en: The elephant, O sire, trampling down upon other elephants, cars and steeds, sent them all to the regions of Death. Thereat Dhananjaya was inflamed with wrath.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच तथा क्रुद्धः किमकरोद् भगदत्तस्य पाण्डवः। प्राग्ज्योतिषो वा पार्थस्य तन्मे शंस यथातथम्॥
en: Dhritarastra said Wrought up with rage, what did Arjuna the son of Pandu do to Bhagadatta? What did also the ruler of the Pragjyotisas do towards Pritha's son? Tell me all as it happened.

sn: संजय उवाच प्राग्ज्योतिषेण संसक्तावुभौ दाशार्हपाण्डवौ। मृत्युदंष्ट्रान्तिकं प्राप्तौ सर्वभूतानि मेनिरे॥
en: Sanjaya said When Krishna and Arjuna were both thus engaged with the ruler of the Pragjyotisas, all creatures regarded them as placed within the teeth of Death.

sn: तथा तु शरवर्षाणि पातयत्यनिशं प्रभो। गजस्कन्धान्महाराज कृष्णयोः स्यन्दनस्थयोः॥
en: Then, O mighty monarch, froin the back of the elephant he rode, the ruler of the Pragjyotisas poured incessant showers of arrows on the two Krishnas (Arjuna and Krishna) stationed on the same chariot.

sn: अथ कार्णायसैर्वाणैः पूर्णकार्मुकनिःसृतैः। अविध्यद् देवकीपुत्रं हेमपुङ्खः शिलाशितैः॥
en: Thereafter Bhagadatta, with iron shafts furnished with golden wings, whetted on stone and discharged from a full-drawn bow, pierced the illustrious son of Devaki.

sn: अग्निस्पर्शसमास्तीक्ष्णा भगदत्तेन चोदिताः। निर्भिद्य देवकीपुत्रं क्षितिं जग्मुः सुवाससः॥
en: Those superbly ornamented arrows of the touch of fire, shot with force by Bhagadatta, entered the earth, having pierced through the son of Devaki.

sn: तस्य पार्थो धनुश्छित्त्वा परिवारं निहत्य च। लालयन्निव राजानं भगदत्तमयोधयत्॥
en: The son of Pritha then cut-off Bhagadatta's bow and slew that warriors who supporting the latter from his flanks; he then engaged with the Pragjyotisa king as if in sport.

sn: सोऽर्करश्मिनिभांस्तीक्ष्णांस्तोमरान् वै चतुर्दश। अप्रेषयत् सव्यसाची द्विधैकैकमथाच्छिनत्॥
en: Thereat Bhagadatta sped at Arjuna fourteen lances of great sharpness and of the solar effulgence; but Arjuna cut each of thein into two pieces.

sn: ततो नागस्य तद् वर्म व्यधमत् पाकशासनिः। शरजालेन महता तद् वयशीर्यत भूतले॥
en: was numerous Thereafter Arjuna shattered into pieces the armour covering Bhagadatta's elephant, with a mighty shower of arrows, the armour then dropped down on the earth.

sn: शीर्णवर्मा स तु गजः शरैः सुभृशमर्दितः। बभौ धारानिपाताक्तो व्यभ्रः पर्वतराडिव॥
en: With its armour shattered and mangled with arrow-wounds, that elephant appeared like a prince of mountain shorn of its cloudy envelope and with its breast drenched with showers of rain.

sn: ततः प्राग्ज्योतिषः शक्तिं हेमदण्डामयस्मयीम्। व्यसृजद् वासुदेवाय द्विधा तामर्जुनोऽछिनत्॥
en: Thereupon the ruler of the Pragjyotisas hurled at Vasudeva's son a dart having a golden staff and an iron head; but Arjuna cut that dart in two.

sn: ततश्छत्रं ध्वजं चैव छित्त्वा राज्ञोऽर्जुनः शरैः। विव्याध दशभिस्तूर्णमुत्स्मयन् पर्वतेश्वरम्॥
en: Thereafter having severed with arrows the umbrella and the standard of the king, Arjuna quickly pierced the ruler of the mountainprovinces with ten shafts, smiling the while.

sn: सोऽतिविद्धोऽर्जुनशरैः सुपुकैः कङ्कपत्रिभिः। भगदत्तस्ततः क्रुद्धः पाण्डवस्य जनाधिपः॥ व्यसृजत् तोमरान् मूर्ध्नि श्वेताश्वस्योन्ननाद च। तैरर्जुनस्य समरे किरीटं परिवर्तितम्॥
en: Then that ruler of the Pragjyotisas was sorely wounded by Arjuna's arrows furnished with beautiful wings formed of the feathers of the Kanka birds. Thereafter Bhagadatta, O ruler of men, waxing wroth, hurled lances at the head of Pandu's son owning white steeds. And then he uttered a loud war-cry. Then by those lances, the diadem of Arjuna was displaced.

sn: परिवृत्तं किरीटं तद् यमयन्नेव पाण्डवः। सुदृष्टः क्रियतां लोक इति राजानमब्रवीत्॥
en: Then putting his displaced diadem, in its proper place, Phalguna said to king Bhagadatta-"Take you a full view of this world."

sn: एवमुक्तसतु संक्रुद्धः शरवर्षेण पाण्डवम्। अभ्यवर्षत् सगोविन्दं धनुरादाय भास्वरम्॥
en: Thus spoken to, king Bhagadatta, inflamed with rage, took up a lustrous bow and showers of arrow on Pandu's son and Govinda.

sn: तस्य पार्थोधनुश्छित्त्वा तूणीरान् संनिकृत्य च। त्वरमाणो द्विसप्तत्या सर्वमर्मस्वताडयत्॥
en: The son of Pritha then having cut-off Bhagadatta's bow and quivers quickly pierced the latter in all his vital limbs with seventy two arrows.

sn: विद्धस्ततोऽतिव्यथितो वैष्णवास्त्रमुदीरयन्। अभिमन्त्र्याङ्कुशं क्रुद्धो व्यसृजत् पाण्डवोरसि।। १७
en: Thus pierced and pained to the extreme, Bhagadatta invoked the Vaishnava weapon and inspiring its hook with sacred aphorisms, he let to go, in rage, at the breast of Pandu's son.

sn: विसृष्टं भगदत्तेन तदस्त्रं सर्वघाति वै। उरसा प्रतिजग्राह पार्थं संच्छाद्य केशवः॥
en: Thereupon Keshava, covering Pritha's son, received upon his own breast that weapon capable of slaying every being, hurled by Bhagadatta.

sn: वैजयन्त्यभवन्माला तदस्त्रं केशवोरसि। पद्मकोशविचित्राढ्या सर्वर्तुकुसुमोत्कटा॥ ज्वलनार्केन्दुवर्णाभा पावकोज्ज्वलपल्लवा । तया पद्मपलाशिन्या वातकम्पितपत्रया॥ शुशुभेऽभ्यधिकं शौरिरतसीपुष्पसंनिभः।
en: That weapon turned into Vaijayanti garland when it had about to touch the chest of god Sri Krishna. That garland was made of all seasonal flowers and excellently graced with the stamen of lotus flower. It was illuminating like fire, sun and moon. Each petal of flowers intertwined in it was blazing like fire. God Keshava, the killer of Keshi, son of Sureasena, holder of Saranga bow, suppressor of enemy having their dark complexion like the Tisi flowers of that garland looked as if a mountain covered by clouds in one evening of rainy season. That garland was looked fantastic with lotus petals moving with the breeze,

sn: ततोऽर्जुन: क्लान्तमना: केशवं प्रत्यभाषत॥ अयुध्यमानस्तुरगान् संयन्तास्मीति चानघ। इत्युक्त्वा पुण्डरीकाक्ष प्रतिज्ञा स्वां न रक्षसि॥ यद्यहं व्यसनी वा स्यामशक्तो वा निवारणे। ततस्त्वयैवं कार्यं स्यान्न तत्कार्यं मयि स्थिते॥
en: Thereafter with a sorrowful heart Arjuna thus addressed Keshava "O sinless one, without fighting for you, I will drive your steeds, in battle. Even these, O lotus-eyed one, were the words you spoke before. Why then do you not keep your promise inviolate? It is only then when I shall be involved in a calamity or shall be incapable or resisting (my foes and their weapons), it is then only that you shall take it upon yourself to protect me; but not when I am competent and standing thus.

sn: सबाणः सधनुश्चाहं ससुरासुरमानुषान्। शक्तो लोकानिमाजेतुं तच्चापि विदितं तव॥
en: Equipped with my bows and arrows, I am competent enough to conquer the words with all the celestials, Asuras and mortals dwelling in them; this fact indeed you also know."

sn: ततोऽर्जुनं वासुदेवः प्रत्युवाचार्थवद् वचः। शृणु गुह्यमिदं पार्थ पुरा वृत्तं यथानघ॥
en: Thereupon the son of Vasudeva addressing Arjuna spoke these words in reply-"Hear, O sinless one, O son of Pritha, this ancient and mysterious piece of history.

sn: चतुर्मूर्तिरहं शश्वल्लोकत्राणार्थमुद्यतः। आत्मानं प्रविभज्येह लोकानां हितमादधे॥
en: Ever occupied as I am in achieving the welfare of the worlds. I have four semblance's. Dividing myself into parts I do try to bring about the world's benefit.

sn: एका मूर्तिस्तपश्चर्यां कुरुते मे भुवि स्थिता। अपरा पश्यति जगत् कुर्वाणं साध्वसाधुनी॥
en: One of my semblance's, remaining on earth, is even now practising ascetic austerities. Another keeps an eye over the world engaged in good and evil deeds.

sn: अपरा कुरुते कर्म मानुषं लोकमाश्रिता। शेते चतुर्थी त्वपरा निद्रां वर्षसहस्रिकम्॥
en: My third semblance, staying in the world of men, is engaged in the performance of acts and my fourth semblance sleeps a sleep extending over four thousand years.

sn: याऽसौ वर्षसहस्रान्ते मूर्तिरुत्तिष्ठते मम। वराहेभ्यो वराश्रेष्ठांस्तस्मिन् काले ददाति सा॥
en: This last-mentioned semblance of mine that awakes at the end of the every thousand years, accords excellent boons at that time, to those who really deserve them.

sn: तं तु कालमनुप्राप्तं विदित्वा पृथिवी तदा। अयाचत वरं यन्मां नरकार्थाय तच्छृणु॥
en: On one such occasion, the Earth knowing that the boon-giving hour has come, solicited a boon for her son Naraka; hear, I shall tell it to you.

sn: देवानां दानवानां च अवध्यस्तनयोऽस्तु मे। उपेतो वैष्णवास्त्रेण तन्मे त्वं दातुमर्हसि॥
en: Possessed of the Vaishnava weapon let my son be unslayable, both by the gods and the demons. It behoves you to grant me that weapon.

sn: एवं वरमह श्रुत्वा जगत्यास्तनये तदा। अमोघमस्त्रं प्रायच्छं वैष्णवं परमं पुरां॥
en: Listening then to that prayer for the boon that earth wanted me accord to her son, I gave the excellent and irresistible Vaishnava weapon to him.

sn: अवोचं चैतदस्त्रं वै ह्यमोघं भवतु क्षमे। नरकस्याभिरक्षार्थं नैनं कश्चिद् वधिष्यति॥
en: I then said-'O Earth, let this weapon be infallible in protecting Naraka. None, I say, will be able to slay him.

sn: अनेनास्त्रेण ते गुप्तः सुतः परबलार्दनः। भविष्यति दुराधर्षः सर्वलोकेषु सर्वदा॥
en: 'Protected by this weapon, your son, the crusher of hostile hosts, will, in all times and everywhere, be invincible.

sn: तथेत्युक्त्वा गता देवी कृतकामा मनस्विनी। स चाप्यासीद् दुराधर्षो नरकः शत्रुतापनः॥
en: Then saying “Be it so", that intelligent goddess went away, satisfied at the fruition of her desire. Her son Naraka, that afflicter of hostile horses, also accordingly became invincible.

sn: तस्मात् प्राग्ज्योतिषं प्राप्तं तदस्त्रं पार्थ मामकम्। नास्यावध्योऽस्ति लोकेषु सेन्द्ररुद्रेषु मारिष॥
en: Then, O son of Pritha, that weapon of mine was secured by the ruler of the Pragjyotisas from Naraka; and O sire, there, is none unslayable by it in all the worlds, not excluding Indra and Rudra themselves.

sn: तन्मया त्वत्कृते चैतदन्यथा व्यपनामितम्। विमुक्तं परमास्त्रेण जहि पार्थ महासुरम्॥
en: For your sake therefore, O Arjuna, I did baffle the weapon. Now slay the mighty Asura deprived of his excellent weapon.

sn: वैरिणं जहि दुर्धर्षं भगदत्तं सुरद्विषम्। यथाऽहं जनिवान् पूर्वं हितार्थं नरकं तथा॥
en: Now slay in battle your invincible opponent Bhagadatta, that enemy of the gods, like myself slaying, in the days of yore, Naraka, for the worlds' benefit.

sn: एवमुक्तस्तदा पार्थः केशवेन महात्मना। भगदत्तं शितैर्बाणैः सहसा समवाकिरत्॥
en: Thus spoken to by the high-souled Keshava, Pritha's son suddenly covered Bhagadatta with a shower of sharp arrows.

sn: ततः पार्थो महाबाहुरसम्भ्रान्तो महामनाः। कुम्भयोरन्तरे नागं नाराचेन समार्पयत्॥
en: Then the mighty-armed and high-souled Arjuna dauntlessly wounded Bhagadatta's clephant between its frontal globes with a (long) lance.

sn: स समासाद्य तं नागं बाणो वज्र इवाचलम्। अभ्यगात् सह पुढेन वल्मीकमिव पन्नगः॥
en: Then like the thunder-bolt rending a mountain open, that dart flying towards the elephant penetrated into its body to the very wings, like a snake entering into its hole in an ant-hill.

sn: स करी भगदत्तेन प्रेर्यमाणो मुहुर्मुहुः। न करोति वचस्तस्य दरिद्रस्येव योषिता॥
en: Then like the wife of a poor man, refusing to carry out the orders of her husband, that elephant though often urged by Bhagadatta, refused to obey his orders.

sn: स तु विष्टभ्य गात्राणि दन्ताभ्यामवनिं ययौ। नदन्नार्तस्वनं प्राणनुत्ससर्ज महाद्विपः॥
en: With its limbs paralysed it fell down striking the earth with its tusks. Then that huge elephant gave up its breath uttering a yell of distress.

sn: ततो गाण्डीवधन्वानमभ्यभाषत केशवः। अयं महत्तरः पार्थ पालितेन समावृतः॥ वलीसंछन्ननयनः शूरू परमदुर्जयः। अक्ष्णोरुन्मीलनार्थाय बद्धपट्टो ह्यसौ नृपः॥
en: God Sri Krishna then said to Arjuna-O son of Kunti! Bhagadatta is in his old age with all hair lured grey and eyes covered by the forehead flesh due to wrinkles appear as if these are closed. He is great warrior and gallant. It is tough to defeat him in the battle. He has tied the eyelids with a strip of cloth with the forehead so as to keep both eyes opened.

sn: दैववाक्यात् प्रचिच्छेद शरेण भृशमर्जुनः। छिन्नमात्रेऽशुके तस्मिन् रुद्धनेत्रो बभूव सः॥
en: In compliance with the direction, Arjuna took out crescent shaped arrow of straight knots and shot at the eyes of Bhagadatta. He thus, lost his eyes and became blind.

sn: तमोमयं जगन्मेने भगदत्त: प्रतापवान्। ततश्चन्द्रार्धविम्बेन बाणेन तनपर्वणा॥ बिभेद हृदयं राज्ञो भगदत्तस्य पाण्डवः।
en: The mighty Bhagadatta then seemed the whole world sank in darkness a she was blind now. Arjuna, the son of Pandu, in the meantime; pierced the heart of king Bhagadatta by hitting hard an arrow crescent shaped and bent knot at that spot.

sn: स भिन्नहृदयो राजा भगदत्तः किरीटिना॥ शरासनं शरांश्चैव गतासुः प्रमुमोच ह। शिरसस्तस्य विभ्रष्टं पपात च वरांशुकम्। नालताडनविभ्रष्टं पलाशं नलिनादिव॥
en: His bosom being torn open the diademdecked Arjuna. King Bhagadatta lost the grasp of his bow and arrows, being deprived of vitality. The precious cloth that had constituted his turban now fell off from his head like a petal falling off from a lotus when its stem is struck violently.

sn: स हेममाली तपनीयभाण्डात् पपात नागाद् गिरिसंनिकाशात्। सुपुष्पितो मारुतवेगरुग्णो महीधराग्रादिव कर्णिकारः॥
en: He himself decorated with a garland of gold fell down from the back of his mountain-like elephant, decked also with trappings of gold, like a blossoming Karnikara tree falling down from the crest of a hill, being uprooted by the violence of the wind.

sn: निहत्य तं नरपतिमिन्द्रविक्रम सखायमिन्द्रस्य तदैन्द्रिराहवे। ततोऽपरांस्तव जयकाक्षिणो नरान् बभञ्ज वायुर्बलवान् द्रमानिव॥
en: Then in that battle, the son of Indra having slain that monarch equal to Indra in prowess and who was a friend of Indra, began to crush, inspired with the hopes of victory, other warriors of your army, like a violent gust of wind crushing large number to trees.

sn: संजय उवाच प्रियमिन्द्रस्य सततं सखायममितौजसम्। हत्वा प्राग्ज्योतिषं पार्थः प्रदक्षिणमवर्तत॥
en: Sanjaya said Having slain the ruler of the Pragjyotisas who was the friend and favourite of Indra and who was possessed of immeasurable prowess, the son of Pritha circumambulated him.

sn: ततो गान्धारराजस्य सुतौ परपुरंजयौ। अर्देतामर्जुनं संख्ये भ्रातरौ वृषकाचलौ॥
en: Thereafter, Vrisaka and Achala, the two sons of the king of the Gandharas, both competent to subjugate hostile cities, began to afflict the son of Pandu in battle.

sn: तौ समेत्यार्जुनं वीरौ पुरु पश्चाच्च धन्विनौ। अविध्येतां महावेगैर्निशितैराशुगै शम्॥
en: Those two heroic bowmen assailing Arjuna simultaneously from the rear and the van, began to pierce him with swift-flying arrows coursing with vehemence.

sn: वृषकस्य हयान् सूतं धनुश्छत्रं रथं ध्वजम्। तिलशोव्यधमत् पार्थः सौबलस्य शितैः शरैः॥
en: Thereupon with whetted shafts, Pritha's son cut-off into fragments the steeds the charioteer, the bow, the standard, the umbrella and the chariot of Vrishaka the son of Subala.

sn: ततोऽर्जुनः शरवातै नाप्रहरणैरपि। गान्धारानाकुलांश्चक्रे सौबलप्रमुखान् पुनः॥
en: Thereafter Arjuna with showers of arrows and various other weapons, began to afflict the Gandharas headed by Subala and others.

sn: ततः पञ्चशतान् वीरान् गान्धारानुद्यतायुधान्। प्राहिणोन्मृत्युलोकाय क्रुद्धो बाणैर्धनंजयः॥
en: Then wrought up with wrath, Dhananjaya dispatched, by means of his arrows, to the regions of Death, five hundred heroic Gandhara warriors with their weapons held over their heads.

sn: हताश्वात् तु रथात् तूर्णनवतीर्य महाभुजः। आरुरोह रथं भ्रातुरन्यच्च धनुराददे॥
en: Meanwhile the mighty-armed Vrishaka alighting from his chariot of which the horses were slain, ascended the car of his brother with agility and grasped another bow.

sn: तावेकरथमारूढौ भ्रातरौ वृषकाचलौ। शरवर्षेण बीभत्सुमविध्येतां मुहुर्मुहुः॥
en: Then those two heroic brothers Vrishaka and Achala, both riding on the self same car, began incessantly to pierce Pritha's son with their arrowy downpour.

sn: स्यालौ तव महात्मानौ राजानौ वृषकाचलौ। भृशं विजनतुः पार्थमिन्द्रं वृत्रबलाविव॥
en: Then those two kings, your brothers-in-law, viz., Vrishaka and Achala of illustrious souls, began to wound Partha sorely, like Bala or Vritra wounding Indra himself.

sn: लब्धलक्ष्यौ तु गान्धारावहतां पाण्डवं पुनः। निदाघवार्षिकौ मासौ लोकं धर्मोशु भिर्यथा।॥
en: The two Gandhara kings of unerring aims, again and again pierced Pandu's son like the summer and the rainy months of the year piercing the world with heat and rain respectively.

sn: तौ रथस्थौ नरव्याघ्रौ राजानौ वृषकाचलौ। संश्लिष्टाङ्गौ स्थितौ राजञ्जघानेकेषुणाऽर्जुनः॥
en: Thereat, O monarch, Arjuna with a single shaft slew those two foremost of men, those two princes, viz., Vrishaka and Achala who had been riding on the same chariot side by side.

sn: तौ स्थात् सिंहसंकाशौ लोहिताक्षौ महाभुजौ। राजन् सम्पेततुर्वीरौ सोदर्यावेकलक्षणौ॥
en: Thereupon those two heroic brothers with red eyes, possessed on long arms, having similar features and looking like two lions, fell down from their car.

sn: तयोर्भूमिं गतौ देहौ रथाद् बन्धुजनप्रियौ। यशो दश दिशः पुण्यं गमयित्वा व्यवस्थितौ॥
en: Then their bodies, so much tended by their friends and favourities, falling from the car, lay prostrate on the Earth, spreading sacred fame in all the ten points of the compass.

sn: दृष्ट्वा विनिहतौ संख्ये मातुलावपलायिनौ। भृशं मुमुचुरश्रूणि पुत्रास्तव विशाम्पते॥
en: Thereafter, O ruler of men, your sons beholding their two unretreating and heroic maternal uncles slain, began unceasingly to discharge weapons.

sn: निहतौ भ्रातरौ दृष्ट्वा मायाशतविशारदः। कृष्णौ सम्मोहयन् मायां विदधे शकुनिस्ततः॥
en: Then, conversant with hundred kinds of illusion, Shakuni beholding his two brothers slain spread a mighty illusion for confounding the two Krishnas.

sn: लगुडायोगुडाश्मानः शतघ्नयश्च सशक्तयः। गदापरिघनिस्त्रिंशशूलमुद्गरपट्टिशाः॥ सकम्पनर्टिनखरा मुसलानि परश्वधाः। क्षुराः क्षुरप्रनालीका वत्सदन्तास्थिसन्धयः॥ चक्राणि विशिखाः प्रासा विविधान्यायुधानि च। प्रपेतुः शतशो दिग्भ्यः प्रदिग्भ्यश्चार्जुनं प्रति॥
en: Then clubs, iron-balls, Shataghnis, rocks, darts, maces, bludgeons, swords, tridents, mallets, battle-axes, kampanas scimitars, nails, Mushalas, axes, razors, horse-shoe-headed arrows, Nalikas, Vatsadantas and shafts of bony-heads, discuses, Vishikhas, lances and many other kinds of weapons began to fall upon Arjuna from all the cardinal and subsidiary points of the compass.

sn: खरोष्ट्रमहिषा: सिंहा व्याघ्राः सृमरचित्रकाः। ऋक्षाः शालावृका गृध्राः कपयश्च सरीसृपाः॥ विविधानि च रक्षांसि क्षुधितान्यर्जुनं प्रति। संक्रुद्धान्यभ्यधावन्त विविधानि वयांसि च॥
en: Also asses, camels, buffalo's, tigers, lions, deer, leopards, bears, wolves, bears, wolves, vultures, monkeys and various reptiles and diverse kinds of Rakshasas and fights of birds, all burning with hunger and rage, assailed Arjuna from all sides.

sn: ततो दिव्यास्त्रविच्छूरः कुन्तीपुत्रो धनंजयः। विसृजन्निषुजालानि सहसा तान्यताडयत्॥
en: Thereat that heroic son of Kunti, by name Dhananjaya, versed in the use of celestial weapons, discharging a net-work of arrows, simultaneously attacked them all.

sn: ते हन्यमानाः शूरेण प्रवरैः सायकैलैः। विरुवन्तो महारावान् विनेशुः सर्वतो हताः॥
en: Attacked by that hero with excellent and strong airways, those beasts and reptiles and birds, emitting loud yells of agony, began to give the ghost up on the field of battle.

sn: ततस्तमः प्रादुरभूदर्जुनस्य रथं प्रति। तस्माच्च तमसो वाचः क्रूराः पार्थमभर्त्सयन्॥
en: Thereupon Arjuna's chariot was enveloped in a pall of gloom and harsh voices were heard to reproach Arjuna from within that gloom.

sn: भयकर्तृ महाहवे। उत्तमास्त्रेण महता ज्यौतिषेणार्जुनोऽवधीत्॥
en: Then in that fierce battle, Arjuna, with a mighty and lustrous weapon of the finest make

sn: तत् तमो भैरवं घोरं
en: called Gotishka, dispelled that dreadful and palpable darkness capable of inspiring every one with terror.

sn: हते तसिमञ्जलौघास्तु प्रादुरासन् भयानकाः। अम्भसस्तस्य नाशार्थमादित्यास्त्रमथार्जुनः॥ प्रायुक्ताम्भस्ततस्तेन प्रायशोऽस्त्रेण शोषितम्। एवं बहुविधा मायाः सौबलस्य कृताः कृताः॥
en: When that gloom had been dispelled, frightful waves of waters started into existence. Thereupon for destroying these water-waves, Arjuna discharged the Aditya weapon; that weapon then dried up almost all the waterwaves. Thus various kinds of illusions created by Subala's son.

sn: जधानास्त्रबलेनाशु प्रहसनर्जुनस्तदा। तदा हतासु मायासु त्रस्तोऽर्जुनशराहतः॥
en: Arjuna smilingly nullified, by means of the virtue of his weapons. When all his illusions had been nullified, struck with the arrows of Arjuna and seized with terror.

sn: अपाजाज्जवनैरश्वैः शकुनिः प्राकृतो यथा। ततोऽर्जुनोऽस्त्रविच्छैघ्यं दर्शयन्नात्मनोऽरिषु॥
en: Shakuni fled like a mean deserter being borne away by fleet coursers. Then Arjuna conversant with the use of all weapons, displaying to his foes his great lighthandedness.

sn: अभ्यवर्षच्छरौघेण कौरवाणामनीकिनीम्। सा हन्यमाना पार्थेन तव पुत्रस्य वाहिनी॥
en: Poured showers of arrows on the host of the Kauravas. Then that army of your son, thus smashed by Pritha's son.

sn: द्वैधीभूता महाराज गङ्गेवासाद्य पर्वतम्। द्रोणमेवान्वपद्यन्त केचित् तत्र नरर्षभाः॥
en: Became split up in twain, like a current of Ganges water dividing into two streams when it is obstructed by a hillock. Some among those foremost of men, then sought shelter from Drona.

sn: केचिद् दुर्योधनं राजन्नद्यमानाः किरीटिना। नापश्याम ततस्त्वेनं सैन्ये वै रजसावृते॥
en: And others, O king, being afflicted sore by the diadem-decked Arjuna, flew towards Duryodhana's division. Then we could not see Arjuna, as the army was enveloped in a cloud of dust.

sn: गाण्डीवस्य च निर्घोषः श्रुतो दक्षिणतो मया। शङ्खदुन्दुभिनिर्घोषं वादित्राणां च निःस्वनम्॥
en: I could then only hear the twang of the Gandiva-bow on my right side, as also the sound and blare of conch-shells and drums and the din of many other musical instruments.

sn: गाण्डीवस्य तु निर्घोषोव्यतिक्रम्यास्पृशद् दिवम्। ततः पुनर्दक्षिणतः संग्रामश्चित्रयोधिनाम्॥
en: But rising above all those noise and din, the twang of the Gandiva reached the very heavens. Then on the Southern part of the field, again raged a fight between numerous warriors on the one side.

sn: सुयुद्धं चार्जुनस्यासीदहं तु द्रोणमन्वियाम्। यौधिष्ठिराभ्यनीकानि प्रहरन्ति ततस्ततः॥
en: And Arjuna on the other. I, however, followed Drona's division. Then the diverse divisions of Yudhishthira's army began to strike down the eneiny's host on the field.

sn: नानाविधान्यनीकानि पुत्राणां तव भारत। अर्जुनो व्यधमत् काले दिवीवाभ्राणि मारुतः॥
en: Then, O Bharata, like wind scattering masses of clouds in the heavens, Arjuna began to scatter the various divisions composing the army of your son.

sn: तु वासवमिवायान्तं भूरिवर्षं शरौघिणम्। महेष्वासा नरव्याघ्रा नोग्रं केचिदवारयन्॥
en: None could then resist that fierce bowmen, that excellent of all male beings, as he advanced, like Indra, pouring incessantly showers of arrows.

sn: ते हन्यमानाः पार्थेन त्वदीया व्यथिता भृशम्। स्वानेव बहवो जघ्नुर्विद्रवन्तस्ततस्ततः॥
en: Then all those troops of yours, thus slaughtered by Partha and overwhelmed with intense pain, began to fly and in flying crushed many of their own number.

sn: तेऽर्जुनेन शरा मुक्ताः कङ्कपत्रास्तनुच्छिदः। शलभा इव सम्पेतुः संवृण्वाना दिशो दश॥
en: The arrows, sped by Arjuna, furnished with wings of Kanka feather and capable of piercing into every body, began to fall even like flights of locusts covering all the ten points of the compass.

sn: तुरंग रथिनं नागं पदातिमपि मारिष। विनिर्भिद्य क्षिति जग्मुर्वल्मीकमिव पन्नगाः॥
en: Those arrows, O sire, penetrating through horses, car-warriors, elephants and footsoldiers, entered the earth, like snakes entering their holes in ant-hills.

sn: न च द्वितीयं व्यसृजत् कुञ्जराश्वनरेषु सः। पृथगेकशरा रुग्णा निपेतुस्ते गतासवः॥
en: Arjuna did not shoot more than one arrow at any elephant, man or horse. Each of these, afflicted by one shaft only, began to fall down and give up the ghost on the field.

sn: हतैर्मनुष्यैर्द्विरदैश्च सर्वतः शराभिसृष्टैश्च हयैर्निपातितः। तदा श्वगोमायुबलाभिनादितं विचित्रमायोधशिरोबभूव तत्॥
en: Over-strewn with slain men and elephants and horses mangled with arrows and filled with the yells of dogs and jackals, the field of battle assumed an awful appearance.

sn: पिता सुतं त्यजति सुहृद्वरं सुहृत् तथैव पुत्रः पितरं शरातुरः। स्त्यजन्ति वाहानपि पार्थपीडिताः॥
en: Afflicted with arrows, then father deserted his son, friend forsook his friend and son abandoned his father. Then with their hearts intent on saying themselves, men even forsook their very vehicles, being pained by the arrows of Partha.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच तेष्वनीकेषु भग्नेषु पाण्डुपुत्रेण संजय। चलितानां द्रुतानां च कथमासीन्मनो हि चः॥
en: Dhritarashtra said What, O Sanjaya, was the state of your mind when my army was routed and crushed by Pandu's son and when you speedily fled away from the field?

sn: अनीकानां प्रभग्नानामवस्थानमपश्यताम्। दुष्करं प्रतिसंधानं तन्ममाचक्ष्व संजय॥
en: The re-assembling of broken and routed troops is every difficult; tell me all about it, O Sanjaya.

sn: संजय उवाच तथापि तव पुत्रस्य प्रियकामा विशाम्पते। यशः प्रवीरा लोकेषु रक्षन्तो द्रोणमन्वयुः॥
en: Sanjaya said In spite of all these, O ruler of men, many excellent heroes, desirous of doing good to your son and of keeping their reputation unsullied, followed Drona's track.

sn: समुद्यतेषु चास्त्रेषु समप्राप्ते च युधिष्ठिरे। अकुर्वन्नार्यकर्माणि भैरवे सत्यभीतवत्॥
en: During that fierce encounter, they dauntlessly followed their commander, achieving numerous feats of valour, with weapons upraised and with Yudhishthira within accessible distance.

sn: अन्तरं भीमसेनस्य प्रापतन्नमितौजसः। सात्यकेश्चैव वीरस्य धृष्टद्युम्नस्य वा विभो॥
en: Availing themselves of an error of the heroic Bhimasena, of Satyaki of immeasurable prowess and of the mighty Dhrishtadyumna, the Kuru leaders fell upon the Pandava divisions.

sn: द्रोणं द्रोणमिति क्रूराः पञ्चाला: समचोदयन्। मा द्रोणमिति पुत्रास्ते कुरून् सर्वानचोदयन्॥
en: The fierce Panchalas urged on their troops saying, “There is Drona, there is Drona," whilst your sons urged on the Kurus, saying, 'Let not Drona be slain'.

sn: द्रोणं द्रोणमिति ह्येके मा द्रोणमिति चापरे। कुरूणां पाण्डवानां च द्रोणद्यूतमवर्तत॥
en: Then one side saying "Fall upon Drona, fall upon Drona," and the other side saying, "Let not Drona be slain," a game of dice seemed to be played between the Kurus and the Pandavas, in which Drona was the stake.

sn: यं यं प्रमथते द्रोणः पञ्चलानां रथव्रजम्। तत्र तत्र तु पाञ्चाल्यो धृष्टद्युम्नोऽभ्यवर्तत॥
en: Dhrishtadyumna, the Panchala prince, proceeded to those spots where soever Drona sought to assail the car divisions of the Panchalas.

sn: तथा भागविपर्यासौः संग्रामे भैरवे सति। वीराः समासदन् वीरान् कुर्वन्तो भैरवं रवम्॥
en: Thus during that sanguinary engagement in which no rule for selection of antagonists was followed, heroes encountered heroes, uttering aloud their respective war-cries.

sn: अकम्पनीयाः शत्रूणां वभूवुस्तत्र पाण्डवाः। अकम्पयन्ननीकानि स्मरन्तः क्लेशमात्मनः॥
en: The Pandavas then became incapable of being shaken by their enemies, whilst they themselves, keeping alive the memory of all the wrongs they had to suffer, made the ranks of their foes tremble with fear before them.

sn: ते त्वमर्षवशं प्राप्ता ह्रीमन्तः सत्त्वचोदिताः। त्वक्त्वा प्राणान् न्यवर्तन्त घ्नन्तो द्रोणं महाहवे॥
en: Then in that fierce fight, the naturally modest Pandava warriors, under the influence of animosity and urged on by their energy, rushed to battle reckless of their lives and desirous of slaying Drona.

sn: अयसामिव सम्पातः शिलानामिव चाभवत्। दीव्यतां तुमुले युद्धे प्राणैरमिततेजसाम्॥
en: When those heroes of immeasurable energy played in that battle, as if in a game of dice, staking their very lives, there seemed to be a collision of iron against adamant. the army

sn: न तु स्मरन्ति संग्राममपि वृद्धास्तथाविधम्। दृष्टपूर्वे महाराज श्रुतपूर्वमथापि वा॥
en: Even the oldest men could not recollect, O monarch, of having seen or heard of such a battle before.

sn: प्राकम्पतेव पृथिवी तस्मिन् वीरावसादने। निवर्तता बलौघेन महता भारपीडिता॥
en: In that battle distinguished by the slaughter of heroes, the earth seemed to tremble, being oppressed with the burden of the living oceans that rushed against one another.

sn: घूर्णतोऽपि बलौघस्य दिवं स्तब्वेव निःस्वनः। अजातशत्रोस्तत्सैन्यमाविवेश सुभैरवः॥
en: The fierce yells uttered by your troops, tossed and agitated as they had been, filling the very heavens, seemed to penetrate even to the heart of the of the Ajatasatru Yudhishthira.

sn: समासाद्य तु पाण्डुनामनीकानि सहस्रशः। द्रोणेन चरता संख्ये प्रभग्नानि शितैः शरैः।॥
en: Meanwhile the Pandava hosts' having reached by thousands Drona who had been coursing through the field of battle became shattered and broken with the sharp shafts of the latter.

sn: तेषु प्रमथ्यमानेषु द्रोणेनाद्भुतकर्मणा। पयवारयदासाद्य द्रोणं सेनापतिः स्वयम्॥
en: When those troops were thus being crushed by Drona of marvelous achievements, the generalissimo of the Pandava hosts himself encountered Drona.

sn: तदद्भुतमभूद् युद्धं द्रोणपाञ्चालयोस्तथा। नैव तस्योपमा काचिदिति मे निश्चिता मतिः॥
en: Then we beheld the marvelous fight between Drona and the Panchala prince and my firm conviction is that battle had no parallel.

sn: ततो नीलोऽनलप्रख्यो ददाह कुरुवाहिनीम्। शरस्फुलिङ्गश्चापार्चिर्दहन् कक्षमिवानलः॥
en: Then like fire burning down houses, Nila resembling a veritable fire, of which the arrows were the scintillation's, the bow the flames, began to consume the Kuru army.

sn: तं दहन्तमनीकानि द्रोणपुत्रः प्रतापवान्। पूर्वाभिभाषी सुश्लक्ष्णं स्मयमानोऽभ्यभाषत॥
en: Thereat seeing Nila consume the troops, the highly puissant son of Drona, who had long been desirous of fighting with the former, smilingly addressed these smooth words to him (Nila).

sn: नील किं बहुभिर्दग्धैःस्तव योधैः शरार्चिषा। मयैकेन हि युध्यस्व क्रुद्धः प्रहर चाशु माम्॥
en: What do you gain, O Nila, by consuming with your arrowy flame so many of my common soldiers? Fight with me single-handed as I am; and waxing worth, do you strike ma as you can.

sn: तं पद्मनिकराकारं पद्मपत्रनिभेक्षणम्। व्याकोशपद्माभमुखो नीलो विव्याध सायकैः॥
en: Then Nila, possessed of a countenance beautiful like full-blown lotus, began to pierce with his arrows him whose body resembled a cluster of lotuses and whose eyes resembled lotus-petals.

sn: तेनापि विद्धः सहसा द्रौणिर्भल्लैः शितैस्त्रिभिः। धनुर्ध्वजं च छत्रं च द्विषतः स न्यकृन्तत॥
en: Thus pierced deeply by him, Drona's son, with ten whetted and broad-headed arrows, cut-off the bow, the standard and the umbrella of his adversary.

sn: स प्लुतः स्यन्दनात्तस्मान्नीलश्चर्मवरासिभृत्। द्रौणायनेः शिरः कायाद्धर्तुमैच्छत् पतत्रिवत्॥
en: Then jumping down from his car, Nila, armed with an excellent sword and buckler, desired to sever from Ashvatthaman's trunk his head, like a bird (bearing away its prey in its clutches).

sn: तस्तोन्नतांसं सुनसं शिरः कायात् सकुण्डलम्। भल्लेनापाहरद् द्रौणिः स्मयमान इवानघ॥
en: There at, O sinless one, Drona's son with a broad-headed shaft smilingly severed from Nila's trunk his head graced with a fine nose and decked with ear-rings and resting on elevated shoulders.

sn: सम्पूर्णचन्द्राभमुखः पद्मपत्रनिभेक्षणः। प्रांशुरुत्पलपत्राभो निहतो न्यपतद् भुवि॥
en: Then Nila, whose countenance resembled in splendour the full moon, whose eyes were like petals of lotuses, whose stature was tall, whose complexion was like that of the lotus, thus slain, fell down on the earth.

sn: ततः प्रविष्यथे सेना पाण्डवी भृशमाकुला। आचार्यपुत्रेण हते नीले ज्वलिततेजसि॥
en: After Nila of furious energy had been thus slain by the preceptor's son, the host of the Pandavas, was greatly agitated with grief.

sn: अचिन्तयंश्च ते सर्वे पाण्डवानां महारथाः। कथं नो वासविस्त्रायाच्छत्रुभ्य इति मारिष॥
en: Then, O sire, all the mighty car-warriors of the Pandava host began to think, "How indeed, would the son of Vasava (Arjuna) be able to save us from our foes.

sn: दक्षिणेन तु सेनायाः कुरुते कदनं वली। संशप्तकावशेषस्य नारायणबलस्य च॥
en: When that heroic and mighty warrior is engaged in the southern part of the field in crushing the enemies' troops and slaughtering the remnant of the Samshaptaka and the Narayana troops. in

sn: संजय उवाच प्रतिघातं तु सैन्यस्य नामृष्यत वृकोदरः। सोऽभ्याहनद् गुरुं षष्ट्या कर्णे च दशभिः शरैः॥
en: Sanjaya said Vrikodara could not tolerate that slaughter of his own troops. He therefore, wounded Balhika with sixty and Karna with ten shafts.

sn: तस्य द्रोण: शितैर्बाणैस्तीक्ष्णधारैरजिह्मगैः। जीवितान्तमभिप्रेष्सुर्मर्माण्याशु जघान ह॥
en: Thereupon Drona, desirous of taking his life out of him pierced him in all his vital parts, with whetted shafts of exceeding sharpness, all coursing in straight lines.

sn: रणे। आनन्तर्यमभिप्रेप्सुः षड्विंशत्या समार्पयत्। कर्णो द्वादशभिर्बाणैरश्वत्थामा च सप्तभिः॥
en: Once more, desirous of giving Bhima no respite, Drona stuck twenty-six arrows, all resembling fire in touch and venomous serpents in fierceness, on the former. Then again Karna pierced him with twelve and Ashvatthaman with seven arrows.

sn: षड्भिदुर्योधनो राजा तत एनमथाकिरत्। भीमसेनोऽपि तान् सर्वान् प्रत्यविध्यन्महाबलः॥
en: King Duryodhana also covered him with six arrows. The highly puissant Bhimasena also pierced them in return.

sn: द्रोणं पञ्चाशतेषूणां कर्णं च दशभिः शरैः। दुर्योधनं द्वादशभिद्रौणिमष्टाभिराशुगैः॥
en: He pierced Drona with fifty shafts and Karna with ten arrows and Duryodhana with twelve and Drona's son with eight swiftcoursing arrows.

sn: आरावं तुमुलं कुर्वन्नभ्यवर्तत तान् तस्मिन् संत्यजति प्राणान् मृत्युसाधारणीकृते॥ अजातशत्रुस्तान् योधान् भीमं त्रातेत्यचोदयत्। ते ययुर्भीमसेनस्य समीपममितौजसः॥
en: Then uttering a loud war-cry, he engaged himself in battle. In that fight in which the warriors fought heedless of their lives and in which death seemed to be the common lot of all. Ajatasatru (Yudhishthira) urged on his troops to the rescue of Bhima. Those troops then approached Bhimasena of infinite prowess.

sn: युयुधानप्रभृतयो माद्रीपुत्रौ च पाण्डवौ। ते समेत्य सुसंरब्धाः सहिताः पुरुषर्षभाः॥ महेष्वासवरैर्गुप्ता द्रोणानीकं बिभित्सवः। समापेतुर्महावीर्या भीमप्रभृतयो रथाः॥
en: The, Yuyudhana and others, the twin sons of Madri by Pandu and other car-warriors headed by Bhima, assembled and united together and wrought up with rage, all foremost of men, fell upon Drona's division protected by many foremost archers, desirous of breaking and shattering it.

sn: तान् प्रत्यगृह्णादव्यग्रो द्रोणोऽपि रथिनां वरः। महास्थानतिबलान् वीरान् समरयोधिनः॥
en: Then that foremost of car-warriors namely Drona, received unflinchingly those highly puissant heroic car-warriors, all masters in the art of fighting.

sn: बाह्यं मृत्यु भयं कृत्वा तावकान् पाण्डवा ययुः। सादिनः सादिनोऽभ्यघ्नंस्तथैव रथिनो रथान्॥
en: Then your troops, disregarding their kingdoms and the fear of death, encountered those of the Pandavas. Horse soldiers slew horse-soldiers and car-warriors slew warriors.

sn: आसीच्छक्त्यासिसम्पातो युद्धमासीत् परश्वधैः। प्रकृष्टमसियुद्धं च बभूव कटुकोदयम्॥
en: There were then veritable showers of lances and swords; and the battle was fought with battle-axes. Dreadful sword-fights producing great carnage were also fought.

sn: कुञ्जराणां च सम्पाते युद्धमासीत् सुदारुणम्। अपतत् कुञ्जरान्यो हयादन्यस्त्ववाशिराः॥
en: The battle was all the more dreadful in consequence of the tremendous rush of elephants against elephants. Some fell down from the backs of the elephants, some from the backs of the horses, topsy turvy.

sn: नरो बाणविनिर्भिन्नो रथादन्यश्च मारिष। तत्रान्यस्य च सम्म पतितस्य विवर्मणः॥
en: Others fell down, O sire, from their chariots, with hearts torn open with arrows. In that terrible crush as men fell down deprived of their armours.

sn: शिरः प्रध्वंसयामास वक्षस्याक्रम्य कुञ्जरः। अपरांश्चापरेऽमृद्नन् वारणाः पतितान् नरान्॥
en: Elephants crushed their heads having attacked them on the breast. Else-where might be seen elephants crushing other excellent prostrate warriors.

sn: विषाणैश्चावनिं गत्वा व्यभिन्दन् रथनो बहून्। नरान्त्रैः केचिदपरे विषाणालग्नसंश्रयैः॥
en: Many elephants (as they fell down) striking the earth with their tusks, were seen to mangle there with large bodies of car-warriors. With darts sticking to their trunks, many other.

sn: बभ्रमुः समरे नागा मृद्नन्तः शतशो नरान्। कार्णायसतनुत्राणान् नराश्वरथकुञ्जरान्॥ पतितान् पोथयाञ्चकुर्द्विपाः स्थूलनलानिव। गृघ्रपत्राधिवासांसि शयनानि नराधिपाः॥
en: Elephants careered through the field crushing men by hundreds. Some elephants again pressed and squeezed many fallen men, steeds, car-warriors and elephants, all furnished with iron armours, as if they were merely thick stalk or recds. On beds of arrows furnished with vulterine feathers, many rulers of men.

sn: ह्रीमन्तः कालसम्पर्कात् सुदुःखान्यनुशेरते। हन्ति स्मात्र पिता पुत्रं रथेनाभ्येत्य संयुगे॥
en: Endued with modesty, laid themselves down with pain, their hour having come. In that battle father rushing on his car, slew his own son,

sn: पुत्रश्च पितरं मोहान्निमर्यादमवर्तत। रथोभग्नोध्वजश्छिन्नश्छत्रमुर्त्यांनिपातितम्॥
en: Son also, out of confusion and disregardful of anything, fell upon his own father. Axels of cars were shattered, standards were torn to pieces, umbrellas were felled to the earth;

sn: युगाधु छिन्नमादाय प्रदुद्राव तथा हयः। सासिहुर्निपतितः शिरश्छिन्नं सकुण्डलम्॥
en: Dragging halves of broken yokes, horses began to ran away. Arms with swords in their grasps fell, as also heads graced with ear-rings.

sn: गजेनाक्षिप्य बलिना रथः संचूर्णितः क्षितौ। रथिना ताडितो नागो नाराचेनापतत् क्षितौ॥
en: Chariots, dashed against the earth by powerful elephants, became splintered into pieces. Wounded severely by elephants, steeds fell down with their riders.

sn: सारोहश्चापतद् वाजी गजेनाभ्याहतो भृशम्। निर्मर्यादं महद् युद्धमवर्तत सुदारुणम्॥
en: Then there raged a fierce and dreadful fight in which nobody paid any regard to others. "Alas! Oh father" Oh son! Where are you, o friend! stay! Where do you run to!

sn: हा तात हा पुत्र सखे क्वासि तिष्ठ क्व धावसि। प्रहराहर जह्येनं स्मितक्ष्वेडितगर्जितैः॥
en: Smite! Catch! Slay!" These and many other exclamations, mingled with loud laughter's, roars and war-cries, were uttered and heard there.

sn: इत्येवमुच्चरन्ति स्म श्रूयन्ते विविधा गिरः। नरस्याश्वस्य नागस्य समसज्जत शोणितम्॥
en: The blood of men and steeds and elephants mingled together, flowed in one current and caused the Earth's dust to disappear and inspired terror into the hearts of the cowards.

sn: उपाशाम्यद्रजो भौमं भीरून् कश्मलमाविशत्। चक्रेण चक्रमासाद्य वीरो वीरस्य संयुगे॥
en: In that fight one hero having his car-wheel entangled with that of another and being too near to use any other weapon, smashed the other's head with a mace.

sn: अतीतेषु पथे काले जहार गदया शिरः। आसीत् केशपरापर्थी मुष्टियुद्धं च दारुणम्॥
en: In that battle where there was no chance of safety, heroes, desirous of each other's safety, dragged one another by the head and fought with one another with blows, teeth and nails.

sn: नखैर्दन्तैश्च शूराणामद्वीपे द्वीपमिच्छताम्। तत्राच्छिद्यत शूरस्य सखङ्गो बाहुरुद्यतः॥
en: Upraised arms, with swords in grasp, of some heroes, were severed; the arms of others with bows or hook or arrows in grasp, were also lopped off.

sn: सधुनुश्चापरस्यापि सशरः साङ्कुशस्तथा। आक्रोशदन्यमन्योऽत्र तथान्यो विमुखोऽद्रवत्॥
en: Here warrior loudly challenged another, there, another turned away his face from the field. Another lopped off from the trunk the head of another who happened to encounter him.

sn: अन्यः प्राप्तस्य चान्यस्य शिरः कायादयाहरत्। सशब्दमद्रवच्चान्यः शब्दादन्योऽत्रसद् भृशम्॥
en: Some rushed to fight uttering fierce yells. Some became inspired with terror at the sound. Some slew with his sharp arrows a friend or a foe.

sn: स्वानन्योऽथ परानन्यो जघान निशितैः शरैः। गिरिशृङ्गोपमश्चात्र नाराचेन निपातितः॥
en: Here an elephant huge like the summit of a hill, slain by a lance, lay on the field, like a flat island in a river during the summer season.

sn: मातङ्गो न्यपतद् भूमौ नदीरोध इवोष्णगे। तथैव रथिनं नागः क्षरन् गिरिरिवारुजन्॥
en: There like a mountain with rellets flowing down its breasts, stood an elephant exuding the temporal juice, having crushed with its huge legs a car-warrior together with his steeds and charioteer.

sn: अभ्यतिष्ठत् पदा भूमौ सहाश्वं सहसारथिम्। शूरान् प्रहरतो दृष्ट्वा कृतास्त्रान् रुधिरोक्षितान्॥
en: Many weak-hearted cowards overwhelmed with swoons at the sight of heroes accomplished in the use of weapons fighting with one another, literally bathed in blood.

sn: बहूनप्याविशन्मोहो भीरून् हृदयदुर्बलान्। सर्वमाविग्नमभवन प्राज्ञायत किंचन॥
en: Everything rolled in confusion and nothing could be distinguished. Soldiers enveloped in dust fought on regardless of one another.

sn: सैन्येन रजसा ध्वस्तं निर्मर्यादमवर्तत। ततः सेनापतिः शीघ्रमयं काल इति ब्रुवन्॥
en: Then the generalissimo of the Pandava troops saying “This is the opportune moment" quickly led the Pandavas ever endowed with activity, to the battle.

sn: नित्याभित्वरितानेव त्वरयामास पाण्डवान्। कुर्वन्तः शासनं तस्य पाण्डवा बाहुशालिनः॥
