en: Then as they left if, they saw the mighty car-warrior Abhimanyu, who resembled Indra himself, lying on the field of battle, with precious ornaments displaced and falling off and appearing like a sacrificial fire on the alter no longer fed by oblations of clarified butter.

sn: संजय उवाच हते तस्मिन् महावीर्ये सौभद्रे रथयूथपे। विमुक्तस्थसंनाहाः सर्वे निक्षिप्तकार्मुकाः॥ उपोपविष्टा राजानं परिवार्य युधिष्ठिरम्। तदेव युद्धं ध्यायन्तः सौभद्रगतमानसाः॥
en: Sanjaya said When that hero that leader of a car-division viz., Subhadra's son had been slain in battle, leaving their cars and doffing their coats of mail and throwing aside their bows, all the Pandavas sat surrounding king Yudhishthira. They were then brooding upon their grief with their hearts occupied with the thought of the deceased son of Subhadra.

sn: ततो युधिष्ठिरो राजा विललाप सुदुःखितः। अभिमन्यौ हते वीरे भ्रातुः पुत्रेमहारथे॥
en: Then upon the death of the brother's son, the heroic and mighty car-warrior Abhimanyu, king Yudhishthira began to lament totally unmanned by grief.

sn: द्रोणानीकमसम्बाधं मम प्रियचिकीर्षया। भित्त्वा व्यूहं प्रविष्टोऽसौ गोमध्यमिव केसरी॥
en: Desirous of doing an act agreeable to me, he (Abhimanyu) penetrated the array of Drona with the least difficulty, like a lion penetrating into the midst of a herd of kine.

sn: यस्य शूरा महेष्वासाः प्रत्यनीकगता रणे। प्रभग्ना विनिवर्तन्ते कृतास्त्रा युद्धदुर्मदाः॥
en: Meeting with him in battle, fierce bowmen, endowed with heroism, accomplished in the use of weapons and incapable of being easily defeated in battle, were compelled to turn back.

sn: अत्यन्तशत्रुरस्माकं येन दुःशासनः क्षिप्रं ह्यभिमुखः संख्ये विसंज्ञो विमुखीकृतः॥
en: Our implacable enemy Dushasana having encountered him in battle, was quickly compelled by his shafts to retreat, being nearly deprived of his senses.

sn: स तीर्खा दुस्तरं वीरो द्रोणनीकमहार्णवम्। प्राप्य दौःशासनिं कार्णिः प्राप्तो वैवस्वतक्षयम्॥
en: Having crossed the ocean-like host of Drona's troops difficult of being defeated, that nephew of Krishna was despatched to Death's mansion, upon encountering the son of Dushasana.

sn: कथं द्रक्ष्यामि कौन्तेयं सौभद्रे निहतेऽर्जुनम्। सुभद्रां वा महाभागां प्रियं पुत्रमपश्यतीम्॥
en: Oh, now that Abhimanyu is slain, how shall I look upon Kunti's son Arjuna or upon the auspicious Subhadra bereft of her that dearloved son!

sn: किंस्विद् वयमपेतार्थमश्लिष्टमसमञ्जसम्। तावुभौ प्रतिवक्ष्यामो हृषीकेशधनंजयौ॥ शरैः।
en: What meaningless, disjointed and incoherent words shall we have to say today to both Hrishikesha and Dhananjaya!

sn: अहमेव सुभद्रायाः केशवार्जुनयोरपि। प्रियकामो जयाकाक्षी कृतवानिदमप्रियम्॥
en: It is myself, desirous of my own good and intent on victory, that have done this injury to Subhadra, Arjuna and Keshava!

sn: न लुब्धो बुध्यते दोषाँ ल्लोभान्मोहात् प्रवर्तते। मधुलिप्सुर्हि नापश्यं प्रपातमहमीदृशम्॥
en: A covetous man never finds his own shortcomings; and it is from folly, that covetousness proceeds. Desirous of collecting the honey, I could not see that such a fall threatened me.

sn: यो हि भोज्ये पुरुकार्यो यानेषु शयनेषु च। भूषणेषु च सोऽस्माभिर्बालो युधि पुरस्कृतः॥
en: He who was a mere boy and who should have been indulged with good food, conveyance, beds and ornaments, alas, even such a boy was placed by us in the thick of battle!

sn: कथं हि बालस्तरुणो युद्धानामविशारदः। सदश्व इव सम्बाधे विषमे क्षेममर्हति॥
en: Like a steed of spirited mettle that sacrifices itself rather than obey the reins, how could that boy of tender years, unskilled in the modes of warfare reap good in such a perilous situation?

sn: नो चेद्धि वयमप्येनं महीमनु शयीमहि। बीभत्सोः कोपदीप्तस्य दग्धाः कृपणचक्षुषा॥
en: Alas, after him, today we also shall lay ourselves down on the field of battle, being consumed by the glances of grief cast by Vibhatsu inflamed with rage.

sn: अलुब्धो मतिमान् ह्रीमान् क्षमावान् रूपवान् बली। वपुष्मान् मानकृद् वीरः प्रियः सत्यपराक्रमः॥ यस्य श्लाघन्ति विबुधाः कर्माण्यूर्जितकर्मणः। निवातकवचाञ्जने कालकेयांश्च वीर्यवान्॥ महेन्द्रशत्रवो येन हिरण्यपुरवासिनः। अक्ष्णोनिमेषमात्रेण पौलोमाः सगणा हताः॥ परेभ्योऽप्यभयार्थिभ्यो यो ददात्यभयं विभुः। तस्यास्माभिर्न शकितस्त्रातुमप्यात्मजो बली॥
en: Arjuna is free from covetousness, intelligent, bashful, forbearing, handsome, powerful, endowed with well-developed limbs, respectful to the elders, heroic, amiable and devoted to truth; the feats of that one of fierce deeds even the gods applaud; that one of puissant energy slew Nivatakavachas and also the Kalakeyas; by him were the opponents of the great Indra, the dwellers of the golden cities, viz., the Paulamas slain with their followers, within the twinkling of any eye; that lord gives assurance of safety to those who seek to be protected from their enemies. Alas, today, we have not been competent through fear, to save the son even of that one!

sn: तु सुमहत् प्राप्तं धार्तराष्ट्रान् महाबलान्। पार्थः पुत्रवधात् क्रुद्धः कौरवाशोषयिष्यति॥
en: Surely a great fear has overtaken the mighty host of the son of Dhritarashtra. Filled with rage at the slaughter of his son the son of Pritha (Arjuna) without doubt extirpate the Kauravas.

sn: क्षुद्रः क्षुद्रसहायश्च स्वपक्षक्षयमातुरः। व्यक्तं दुर्योधनो दृष्ट्वाशोचन् हास्यति जीवितम्॥
en: It is also evident that the mean-minded Duryodhana, having mean counselors, that destroyer of his own partisans, seeing the destruction of the troops and overtaken by grief, shall give up his life.

sn: न मे जयः प्रीतिकरो न राज्यं न चामरत्वं न सुरैः सलोकता। इमं समीक्ष्याप्रतिवीर्यपौरुषं निपातितं देववरात्मजात्मजम्॥
en: Beholding this son of Indra's son endowed with unequalled energy and prowess fallen on the field of battle, neither victory, nor kingdom, nor immortality, nor equality of rank with the celestials, does afford me the least joy.

sn: संजय उवाच अथैनं विलपन्तं तं कुन्तीपुत्रं युधिष्ठिरम्। कृष्णद्वैपायनस्तत्र आजगाम महानृषिः॥
en: Sanjaya said Thus when the son of Kunti, king Yudhishthira, was indulging in lamentations, there came to him the mighty sage Krishna Dvaipayana.

sn: अर्चयित्वा यथान्यायमुपविष्टं युधिष्ठिरः। अब्रवीच्छोकसंतप्तो भ्रातुः पुत्रवधेन च॥
en: Then having duly worshipped him, Yudhishthira resumed his seat; and afflicted with grief at the death of his brother's son, he then thus addressed the Rishi.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच अधर्मयुक्तैर्बहुभिः परिवार्य महारथैः। युध्यमानो महेष्वासः सौभद्रो निहतो रणे॥
en: Yudhisthira said The son of Subhadra has been slain in battle when fighting with many, by several fierce bowmen of vicious tendencies, who, mighty car-warriors as they were, surrounded him on all sides.

sn: बालश्च बालबुद्धिश्च सौभद्रः परवीरहा। अनुपायेन संग्रामे युध्यमानो विशेषतः॥
en: That layer of hostile heroes that son of Subhadra, was a mere child in years and in understanding. And he fought in battle against overwhelming numbers.

sn: मया प्रोक्तः स संग्रामे द्वारं संजनयस्व नः। प्रविष्टेऽभ्यन्तरे तस्मिन् सैन्धवेन निवारिताः॥
en: During the course of the fight I said to him “Open a passage for us," then he penetrated into the hostile array and then we could not follow him, prevented by the ruler of the Sindhus. an

sn: ननु नाम समं युद्धमेष्टव्यं युद्धजीविभिः। इदं चैवासमं युद्धमीदृशं यत् कृतं परैः॥
en: Those who live by fighting should surely desire equal combats. But his battle that the enemy fought with Abhimanyu was extremely unfair one.

sn: तेनास्मि भृशसंतप्तः शोकबाष्पसमाकुलः। शमं नैवाधिगच्छामि चिन्तयानः पुनः पुनः॥
en: It is this that burns me with the fire of grief and draws tears of sorrow from my eyes. Brooding over this thought I cannot regain the tranquility of my mind.

sn: संजय उवाच तं तथा विलपन्तं वै शोकव्याकुलमानसम्। उवाच भगवान् व्यासो युधिष्ठिरमिदं वचः॥
en: Sanjaya said Then the almighty Vyasa addressing Yudhishthira who was thus bewailing and was unmanned by the force of his grief, spoke the following words.

sn: व्यास उवाच युधिष्ठिर महाप्राज्ञ सर्वशास्त्रविशारद। व्यसनेषु न मुह्यन्ति तवादृशा भरतर्षभ॥
en: Vyasa said O Yudhishthira, O son of superior wisdom, son who are well-learnt in all the branches of knowledge, O foremost of the Bharatas, people of your stamp are never confounded in seasons of calamity.

sn: स्वर्गमेष गतः शूरः शत्रून् हत्वा बहून् रणे। अबालसदृशं कर्म कृत्वा वै पुरुषोत्तमः॥
en: This hero (Abhimanyu), this foremost of all male beings, has attained paradise after having slain numerous enemies in batile and having achieved many feats not at all boy-like.

sn: अनतिक्रमणीयो वै विधिरेष युधिष्ठिर। देवदानवगन्धर्वान् मृत्युर्हरति भारत॥
en: O Yudhishthira, this law (that created being shall die) cannot be violated. O Bharata, Death takes away all Gods, Danavas and Gandharvas, (without exception).

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच इमे वै पृथिवीपाला: शेरते पृथिवीतले। निहताः पृतनामध्ये मृतसंज्ञा महाबलाः॥
en: Yudhishthira said These rulers of earth, all endued with great might, are now lying on the bare ground of the battle-field being slain and deprived of their senses.

sn: नागायुतबलाश्चान्ये वायुवेगबलास्तथा। त एते निहताः संख्ये तुल्यरूपा नरैर्नराः॥
en: Some of them possessed strength equal to that of ten thousand elephants; some, on the other hand, possessed the impetus and force of the very tempest. They have all been slain in battle by beings of their species and are all equal now.

sn: नैषां पश्यामि हन्तारं प्राणिनां संयुगे क्वचित्। विक्रमेणोपसम्पन्नास्तपोबलसमन्विताः॥
en: I do not see the slayer of these created beings in battle, (save one of their own class). They were possessed of prowess and endued with might and energy.

sn: जेतव्यमिति चान्योन्यं येषां नित्यं दि स्थितम्। अथ चेमे हताः प्राज्ञाः शेरते विगतायुषः॥
en: Alas even those who entertained in their heart the hopes of conquering one another in battle, are now lying slain deprived of their senses, in spite of all their wisdom.

sn: मृता इति च शब्दोऽयं वर्तते च ततोऽर्थवत्। इमे मृता महीपाला: प्रायशो भीमविक्रमाः॥
en: The significance of the word 'Death' hastoday been clearly brought home (to our minds), as almost all these rulers of earth possessed of fierce prowess, lie dead on the field of battle.

sn: निश्चेष्टा निरभीमानाः शूराः शत्रुवशंगताः। राजपुत्राश्च संरब्धा वैश्वानरमुखं गताः॥
en: These heroes having succumbed to their foes and now lying motionless and shorn of their pride. Many princes inflamed with wrath have fallen upon the fire of their antagonist's anger.

sn: अत्र मे संशयः प्राप्त: कुत: संज्ञा मृता इति। कस्य मृत्युः कुतो मृत्युः कथं संहरते प्रजाः॥ हरत्यमरसंकाश तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह।
en: On this point a great doubt has taken possession of me, namely, whence has the word "dead" been derived? Whose offspring is Death? Whence does it come and why does it take away creatures? O you equal to a celestial, O grandsire, speak to me about all this.

sn: संजय उवाच तं तथा परिपृच्छन्तं कुन्तीपुत्रं युधिष्ठिरम्। आश्वासनमिदं वाक्यमुवाच भगवानृषिः॥
en: Sanjaya said Then that illustrious sage spoke these comforting words to Yudhishthira, the son of Kunti, who had been questioning him in the above manner.

sn: व्यास उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। अकम्पनस्य कथितं नारदेन पुरा नृप॥
en: Vyasa said On this subject, O monarch, an ancient story is cited as an example, story that was related to Akampana by Narada.

sn: स चापि राजा राजेन्द्र पुत्रव्यसनमुत्तमम अप्रसह्यतमं लोके प्राप्तवानिति मे मतिः॥
en: So far as I know, O king, Akampana, while in this world, was also afflicted with the overwhelming and unbearable grief caused by his son's death.

sn: तदहं सम्प्रवक्ष्यामि मृत्योः प्रभवमुत्तमम्। ततस्त्वं मोक्ष्यसे दुःखात् स्नेहबन्धनसंश्रयात्॥
en: I shall now recount to you the excellent story of the origin of Death. Hearing that story you shall be freed from grief and from the bondage of affection.

sn: समस्तपापराशिघ्नं शृणु कीर्तयतो मम। धन्यमाख्यानमायुष्यं शोकनं पुष्टिवर्धनम्॥
en: Listen to me, O sire, as I go on repeating that ancient story. This story is excellent and enhances the period of life and kills sorrow and bestows health.

sn: पवित्रमरिसंघघ्नं मङ्गलानां च मङ्गलम्। यथैव वेदाध्ययनमुपाख्यानमिदं तथा॥
en: It is holy, capable of destroying large numbers of foes and the most auspicious of all auspicious things. Verily this story is like the study or recital of the Vedas themselves.

sn: श्रवणीयं महाराज प्रातर्नित्यं नृपोत्तमैः। पुत्रानायुष्मतो राज्यमीहमानैः श्रियं तथा॥
en: It should, O king, be every morning listened to be those foremost of the twice-borns, who desire to obtain long-lived sons, sovereignty and their own welfare.

sn: पुरा कृतयुगे तात आसीद् राजा हकम्पनः। स शत्रुवशमापन्नो मध्ये संग्राममूर्धनि॥
en: In the days of yore during the Krita-yuga, O Sire, there lived a certain king by name Akampana. Once on a time, on the field of battle, amongst his foes, he was on the point of succumbing to his enemies.

sn: तस्य पुत्रो हरि म नारायणसमो बले। श्रीमान् कृतास्त्रो मेधावी युधि शक्रोपमो बली॥
en: He had a son by name Hari, who was equal to Narayana himself in might; he was exceedingly handsome, accomplished in the use of weapons, intelligent, powerful and equal to Shakra in battle.

sn: स शत्रुभिः परिवृतो बहुधा रणमूर्धनि। व्यस्यन् बाणसहस्राणि योधेषु च गजेषु च॥
en: Surrounded by countless foes on the field of battle, he shot thousands of shafts at the warriors and elephants that encompassed him.

sn: स कर्म दुष्करं कृत्वा संग्रामे शत्रुतापनः। शत्रुभिर्निहतः संख्ये पृतनायां युधिष्ठिर॥
en: Having achieved many feats difficult of being achieved, that afflicter of foes, 0 Yudhisthira, was slain amidst this troops by his adversaries.

sn: स राजा प्रेतकृत्यानि तस्य कृत्वा शुचान्वितः। शोचनहनि रात्री च नालभत् सुखमात्मनः॥
en: Performing the funeral ceremonies of his son, king Akampana became purified. But bewailing his son, day and night. he could not regain his peace of mind.

sn: तस्य शोकं विदित्वा तु पुत्रव्यसनसम्भवम्। आजगामाथ देवर्षिर्नारदोऽस्य समीपतः॥
en: Then cognisant of his grief caused by the death of his son, there came near him the celestial sage Narada himself.

sn: स तु राजा महाभागो दृष्ट्वा देवर्षिसत्तमम्। पूजयित्वा यथान्यायं कथामकथयत् तदा॥
en: That monarch of illustrious qualities, beholding the sage come, worshipped him duly and then spoke to him these words.

sn: तस्य सर्वे समाचष्ट यथावृत्तं नरेश्वरः। शत्रुभिर्विजयं संख्ये पुत्रस्य च वधं तथा॥
en: And then that ruler of men spoke to the Rishi all that had happened, his defeat by his foes and the slaughter of his son by them.

sn: अकम्पन उवाच मम पुत्रो महावीर्य इन्द्रविष्णुसमद्युतिः। शत्रुभिर्बहुभिः संख्ये पराक्रम्य हतो बली॥
en: Akampana said My son of great energy and mighty equal to Indra or Vishnu himself in effulgence, has been killed in battle by his numerous enemies, when engaged in fighting vigorously with them.

sn: क एष मृत्युभगवन् किंवीर्यबलपौरुषः। एतदिच्छामि तत्त्वेन श्रोतुं मतिमतां वर॥
en: But, O illustrious sage, who is this Death, what is his prowess, might and manliness? O foremost of intelligent beings, I desire to know the real truth about all these questions.

sn: व्यास उवाच तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा नारदो वरदः प्रभुः। आख्यानमिदमाचष्ट पुत्रशोकापहं महत्॥
en: Vyasa said Having heard those words of his, the lord Narada, that bestower of boons, related this story that is capable of destroying the great sorrow caused by the death of one's son.

sn: शृणु राजन् महाबाहो आख्यानं बहुविस्तरम्। यथावृत्तां श्रुतं चैव मयाऽपि वसुधाधिप।॥
en: Hear, O mighty-armed monarch, this long story, exactly, O ruler of earth, as I myself have heard it.

sn: प्रजाः सृष्ट्वा तदा ब्रह्मा आदिसर्गे पितामहः। असंतं महातेजा दृष्ट्वा जगदिदं प्रभुः॥
en: In the beginning of the creations, the Grandsire Brahma created all beings. Then that highly powerful one, seeing that the beings of his creation suffered no decay.

sn: तस्य चिन्ता समुत्पन्ना संहारं प्रति पार्थिव। चिन्तयन्न ह्यसौ वेद संहारं वसुधाधिप॥
en: Fell to thinking, O king, as to how he should cause their destruction. Meditating long over the subject, he then failed to find out any means of destruction, O ruler of earth.

sn: तस्य रोषान्महाराज खेभ्योऽग्निरुदतिष्ठत। तेन सर्वा दिशो व्याप्ताः सान्तर्देशा दिधक्षता॥
en: (Then he waxed wroth) and inconsequence of that wrath then, a fire sprang out from the skies. That fire spread in all the quarters of heaven and it began to consume all the regions of the universe.

sn: ततो दिवं भुवं चैव ज्वालामालासमाकुलम्। चराचरं जगत सर्वे ददाह भगवान् प्रभुः॥
en: Thereat heaven, earth and the welkin, ail became overspread with tongues of flame. And that Almighty lord then burnt down the universe with its mobile and immobile creatures and objects.

sn: ततो हतानि भूतानि चराणि स्थावराणि च। महता क्रोधवेगेन त्रासयन्निव वीर्यवान्॥
en: Then mobile and immobile, all creatures were annihilated. Verily the puissant Brahma did all this, frightening the worlds with the fierceness of his angers.

sn: ततो रुद्रो जटी स्थाणुर्निशाचरपतिहरः। जगाम शरणं देवं ब्रह्मणं परमेष्ठिनम्॥
en: Thereupon Hara, otherwise called Sthanu, wearing matted locks on his head, that Lord of all the night-rangers, sought shelter from the divine Brahma that foremost of all gods.

sn: तस्मिन्नापतिते स्थाणौ प्रजानां हितकाम्यया। अब्रवीत् परमो देवो ज्वलन्निव महामुनिः॥
en: Thus when Sthanu had fallen (at Brahma's feet) desirous of doing good to the creatures, that highest divinity, the foremost of all asceties, burning with effulgence said-

sn: किं कुर्मः कार्म कामाई काकाज्जातोऽसि पुत्रका करिष्यामि प्रियं सर्वे ब्रूहि स्थाणो यदिच्छसि॥
en: What desire of yours shall we fulfill. O you that deserve to have all your wishes gratified! O son, you are born out of our will. We shall accomplish all that is dear unto you. Speak, O Sthanu, what you desire (to have).

description: The story of the origin of Death
sn: स्थाणुरुवाच प्रजासर्गनिमित्तं हि कृतो यत्नस्त्वया विभो। त्वया सृष्टाश्च वृद्धाश्च भूतग्रामाः पृथग्विधाः॥
en: Sthanu said O Lord, you did take great pains for creating various creatures. All these different sorts of beings have been created and reared by you.

description: The story of the origin of Death
sn: तास्तवेह पुनः क्रोधात् प्रजा दह्यन्ति सर्वशः। ता दृष्ट्वा मम कारुण्यं प्रसीद भगवन् प्रभो॥
en: Those very creatures are now being burnt down by the fire of your anger. Seeing their condition, I am filled with compassion; O Lord, O illustrious One, be merciful on them.

description: The story of the origin of Death
sn: ब्रह्मोवाच संहर्तुं न च मे काम एतदेवं भवेदिति। पृथिव्या हितकामं तु ततो मां मन्युराविशत्॥
en: Brahma said I had no desire for destroying the worlds. I wanted to leave them in peace; I always desired the earth's welfare. But then anger took possession of me.

description: The story of the origin of Death
sn: इयं हि मां सहा देवी भारार्ता समचूचुदत्। संहारार्थे महादेव भारेणाभिहता सती॥
en: The goddess of earth, over-burdened with the heavy weight of creatures, always solicited me for destroying the beings on her surface, O mighty God.

description: The story of the origin of Death
sn: ततोऽहं नाधिगच्छामि तथा बहुविधं तदा। संहारमप्रमेयस्य ततो मां मन्युराविशत्॥
en: Then though thinking in many ways, I could not find out the means for destroying the infinite creation. At this, anger entered into me.

description: The story of the origin of Death
sn: रुद्र उवाच संहारार्थे प्रसीदस्व मा रुषो वसुधाधिप। मा प्रजाः स्थावराश्चैव जंगमाश्च व्यनीनशः॥
en: Rudra said Be propitiated, O ruler of the universe and do not cherish wrath for the destruction of creatures. Do you not any longer destroy the mobile and immobile creatures.

description: The story of the origin of Death
sn: तव प्रसादाद् भगवन्निदं वर्तेत् त्रिधा जगत्। अनागतममीनं च यच्च सम्प्रति वर्तते॥
en: Through your grace, O almighty Lord, the universe is divided in three divisions, viz., the Past, the Present and the Future. Let it remain as it is;

description: The story of the origin of Death
sn: भगवन् क्रोधसंदीप्तः क्रोधादग्निमवासृजत्। स दहत्यश्मकूटानि गुमांश्च सरितस्तथा॥
en: You have, O lord, blazed up in anger from anger this fire has proceeded and that fire now consumes rocks, trees and rivers.

description: The story of the origin of Death
sn: पल्वलानि च सर्वाणि सर्वोश्चैव तृणोलपान्। स्थावरं जङ्गमं चैव नि:शेषं कुरुते जगत्॥ तदेतद् भसमसाद्भूतं जगत् स्थावरजङ्गमम्। प्रसीद भगवन् स त्वं रोषो न स्याद् वरो मम॥
en: And all kinds of shrubs and grass. Verily that fire is blasting the mobile and immobile universe. Behold the mobile and immobile universe reduced to ashes. Be propitiated, O almighty God! give not way to wrath. Even this boon do I beg.

description: The story of the origin of Death
sn: सर्वे हि सृष्टा नश्यन्ति तव देव कथंचन। तस्मानिवर्ततां तेजस्त्वय्येवेदं प्रलीयताम्॥
en: All created things, O Divine Being' that belong to you, are being consumed; therefore withdraw your energy, let it be quenched in your ownself.

description: The story of the origin of Death
sn: तत् पश्य देव सुभृशं प्रजानां हितकाम्यया। यथेमे प्राणिनः सर्वे निवर्तेरंस्तथा कुरु॥
en: Look at the creatures of your own creation, filled with a desire for doing good to them all. Do that by which all these beings endued with life, may continue to live.

description: The story of the origin of Death
sn: अभावं नेह गच्छेयुरुत्सन्नजननाः प्रजाः। आदिदेव नियुक्तोऽस्मि त्वया लोकेषु लोककृत्॥
en: Let not these things with their prowess of propagation weakened, be exterminated. O Creator of the world, you have employed me to be their protector.

description: The story of the origin of Death
sn: मा विनश्येज्जगन्नाथ जगत् स्थावरजङ्गमम्। प्रसादाभिमुखं देवं तस्मादेवं ब्रवीम्यहम्॥
en: O Lord of the universe, let not this mobile and immobile universe be destroyed. You are inclined to show mercy and it is for this reason that I now speak thus.

description: The story of the origin of Death
sn: नारद उवाच श्रुत्वाहि वचनं देवः प्रजानां हितकारणे। तेजः संधारयामास पुनरेवानतरात्मनि॥
en: Narada said Hearing these words (of Mahadeva) the Divine Brahma, desirous of accomplishing the good of the created beings, withdrew in his own inner self his anger that had been excited.

description: The story of the origin of Death
sn: ततोऽग्निमुपसंहृत्य भगवाँल्लोकसत्कृतः। प्रवृत्तं च निवृत्तं च कथयामास वै प्रभुः॥
en: Quenching that fire, the illustrious benefactor of the universe, the Supreme Lord, declared the duties of Production and Emancipation.

description: The story of the origin of Death
sn: उपसंहरतस्तस्य तमग्निं रोषजं तथा। प्रादुर्वभूव विश्वेभ्यो गोभ्यो नारी महात्मनः॥ कृष्णरक्ता तथा पिङ्गरक्तजिह्वास्यलोचना। कुण्डलाभ्यां च राजेन्द्र तप्ताभ्यां तप्तभूषणा॥
en: When that high-souled god had thus extinguished that fire of his wrath, there came out from the various outlets of his senseorgans, a female figure. She was dark and red and tawny and her tongue, countenance and eyes were red and she was adorned with two shining ear-rings and various other brilliant ornaments.

description: The story of the origin of Death
sn: सा निःसृत्य तथा खेभ्यो दक्षिणां दिशमाश्रिता। स्मयमाना च सावेक्ष्य देवौ विश्वेश्वरावुभौ॥
en: Coming out of his body, she betook to the southern quarter and she smilingly cast glances at those two lords of the universe.

description: The story of the origin of Death
sn: तामाहूय तदा देवो लोकादिनिधनेश्वरः। मृत्यो इति महीपाल जहि चेमाः प्रजा इति॥
en: Then Brahma, that controller of the creation and destruction of the worlds, called her by the name of "Death." And, Oruler of men, he said to her – "Slay" these beings of my creation.

description: The story of the origin of Death
sn: त्वं हि संहारबुद्धच्याथ प्रादुर्भूता रुषो ममा तस्मात् संहर सर्वांस्त्वं प्रजाः सजड़पण्डिताः॥ मम त्वं हि नियोगेन ततः श्रेयो ह्यवाप्स्यसि।
en: You are the offspring of the wrath I harboured for the destruction of the universe. Therefore kill you all these creations including the learned and the idiot, at my own behest. Thus you shall attain your own good."

description: The story of the origin of Death
sn: एवमुक्ता तु सा तेन मृत्युः कमललोचना॥ दध्यौ चात्यर्थमबला प्ररुरोद च सुस्वरम्।
en: Thus spoken to by him, that lady of lotuslike eyes, called “Death," meditated for a long time and then began to wail aloud helplessly in plaintive voice.

description: The story of the origin of Death
sn: पाणिभ्यां प्रतिजग्राह तान्यश्रूणि पितामहः। सर्वभूहितार्थाय तां चाप्यनुनयत् तदा॥
en: Then the grandsire with two hands caught the tears that flowed from her eyes, for the welfare of all creatures and entreated her in the following words.

description: The colloquy between Death and the Lord of Creation
sn: नारद उवाद विनीय दुःखमबला आत्मन्येव प्रजापतिम्। उवाच प्राञ्जलिर्भूत्वा लतेवावर्जिता पुनः॥
en: Narada said Then that helpless lady restraining her grief within herself, thus addressed the lord of the people, with folded palms and bending like a creeper with humility.

description: The colloquy between Death and the Lord of Creation
sn: मृत्युरुवाच त्वया सृष्टा कथं नारी ईदृशी वदतां वर। क्रूरं कर्माहितं कुर्यां तदेव किमु जानती॥
en: Death said O most eloquent of all speakers, how shall I, created a female by you, do such heartless and mischievous deeds, knowing them at the same time to be so?

description: The colloquy between Death and the Lord of Creation
sn: बिभेम्यहमधर्माद्धि प्रसीद भगवन् प्रभो। प्रियान् पुत्रान् वयस्यांश्च भ्रातॄन् मातृः पितॄन् पतीन्॥३ अपध्यास्यन्ति मे देव मृतेष्वेभ्यो विभेम्यहम्।
en: I fear sin greatly-O illustrious lord, be propitious on me. Sons, friends, brothers, fathers and husbands are always dear to creatures. If they are destroyed by my hands, they that will incur the loss, shall endeavour to avenge themselves on me. It is them that I fear.

description: The colloquy between Death and the Lord of Creation
sn: कृपणानां हि रुदतां ये पतन्त्यश्रुबिन्दवः॥ तेभ्योऽहं भगवन् भीता शरणं त्वाहमागता।
en: The drops of tears that will fall from the eyes of grief-stricken and bewailing persons. Fill me with terror. Thus affrighted, O illustrious Lord, I seek your protection.

description: The colloquy between Death and the Lord of Creation
sn: यमस्य भवनं देव गच्छेयं न सुरोत्तम॥ कायेन विनयोपेता मोदग्रनखेन च। एतदिच्छाम्यहं कामं त्वत्तो लोकपितामह॥
en: O foremost of the celestials, O Divine Being, I will not go to Yama's abode. O you. that bestow boons, I do propitiate you, by bending my head low and by folding my hands, O Grandsire of the worlds, I desire the fulfillment of even this wish of mine at your hands.

description: The colloquy between Death and the Lord of Creation
sn: इच्छेयं त्वत्प्रसादाद्धि तपस्तप्तुं प्रजेश्वर। प्रदिशेमं वरं देव त्वं मह्यं भगवन् प्रभो॥
en: O Lord of the creation, I desire to carry on ascetic austerities through your grace. O great Lord, O divine being, accord me this boon.

description: The colloquy between Death and the Lord of Creation
sn: त्वया झुक्ता गमिष्यामि धेनुकाश्रममुत्तमम्। तत्र तप्स्ये तपस्तीनं तवैवाराधने रता॥
en: Permitted by you, I shall go to the excellent hermitage of Dhenuka and there shall I practice ascetic austerities of the most severe sort, being engaged in worshipping yourself.

description: The colloquy between Death and the Lord of Creation
sn: न हि शक्ष्यामि देवेश प्राणान् प्राणभृतां प्रियान्। हर्तुं विलपमानानामधर्मादभिरक्ष माम्॥
en: O Lord of the celestials, I shall not be able to destroy the dear lives of living creatures, when they will weep in grief. Save me from unrighteousness.

description: The colloquy between Death and the Lord of Creation
sn: ब्रह्मोवाच मृत्यो संकल्पितासि त्वं प्रजासंहारहेतुना। गच्छ संहर सर्वास्त्वं प्रजा मा ते विचारणा॥
en: Brahma said You have been created, O Death, for causing the destruction of creatures; go, destroy all the creatures; entertain no scruples whatsoever.

description: The colloquy between Death and the Lord of Creation
sn: भविता त्वेतदेवं हि नैतज्जात्वन्यथा भवेत्। भव त्वनिन्दिता लोके कुरुष्व वचनं मम॥
en: This must have happened and nothing could have prevented it. Carry out my command; none in the world will find any fault with you.

description: The colloquy between Death and the Lord of Creation
sn: नारद उवाच एवमुक्ताभवत् प्रीता प्राञ्जलिर्भगवन्मुखी। संहारे नाकरोद् बुद्धिं प्रजानां हितकाम्यया॥
en: Narada said Thus spoken to, the lady became pleased and she stood with her face turned towards the illustrious god. And out of desire for doing good to the creatures, she did not set her heart upon the destruction of creature.

description: The colloquy between Death and the Lord of Creation
sn: तूष्णीमासीत् तदा देवः प्रजानामीश्वरेश्वरः। प्रसादं चागमत् क्षिप्रमात्मनैव प्रजापतिः॥
en: Then that Divinity, the Lord of the lords of creatures also remained silent for a while; and the grandsire soon became satisfied with his ownself.

description: The colloquy between Death and the Lord of Creation
sn: स्मयमानश्च देवेशो लोकान् सर्वानवेक्ष्य च। लोकास्त्वासन् यथापूर्वे दृष्टास्तेनापमन्युना॥
en: Then turning his eyes upon the creatures he smiled. Then the creatures lived cheerfully as before, undisturbed by premature death.

description: The colloquy between Death and the Lord of Creation
sn: निवृत्तरोषे तस्मिंस्तु भगवत्यपराजिते। सा कन्यापि जगामाथ समीपात् तस्य धीमतः॥
en: When that invincible and illustrious divinity had cast his wrath off, that lady also went away from the presence of that intelligent being.

description: The colloquy between Death and the Lord of Creation
sn: अपसृत्याप्रतिश्रुत्य प्रजासंहरणं तदा। त्वरमाणा च राजेन्द्र मृत्युर्धेनुकमभ्यगात्॥
en: Then without having promised the destruction of creatures, she went away, O king; and then Death hastily came to Dhenuka.

description: The colloquy between Death and the Lord of Creation
sn: सा तत्र परमं तीव्र चचार व्रतमुत्तमम्। सा तदा ह्येकपादेन तस्थौ पद्मानि षोडश॥ पञ्च चाब्दानि कारुण्यात् प्रजानां तु हितैषिणी। इन्द्रियाणीनिद्रयार्थेभ्यः प्रियेभ्यः संनिवर्त्य सा॥
en: There she practised a vow excellent and greatly severe. There she stood on one leg for sixteen times ten billions of years and five times ten billions also, through compassion for living creatures and through desire for doing them good, all the time withholding her senses from their dear objects.

description: The colloquy between Death and the Lord of Creation
sn: ततस्त्वेकेन पादेन पुनरन्यानि सप्त वै। तस्थौ पद्मानि षट् चैव सप्त चैकं च पार्थिव॥
en: Once more, O monarch, she stood there on one leg for twenty one times ten billions of years.

description: The colloquy between Death and the Lord of Creation
sn: ततः पद्मायुतं तात मृगैः सह चचार सा। पुनर्गत्वा ततो नन्दा पुण्यां शीतामलोदकाम्॥
en: Then she roved for ten times ten thousand billions of years with the animals. Then once again repairing to the holy river Nanda that was full of cool and translucent water.

description: The colloquy between Death and the Lord of Creation
sn: अप्सु वर्षसहस्राणि सप्त चैकं च साऽनयत्। धारयित्वा तु नियमं नन्दायां वीतकल्मषा॥
en: She passed in those waters eight thousand years. Practising austere penances on the banks of the Nanda, she purged herself of all her sins.

description: The colloquy between Death and the Lord of Creation
sn: सा पूर्वे कौशिकी पुण्यां जगाम नियमैघिता। तत्र वायुजलाहारा चचार नियमं पुनः॥
en: Then observant of her vows, she first visited the sacred Kousiki; living upon air and water only, she practised penances there.

description: The colloquy between Death and the Lord of Creation
sn: पञ्चगङ्गसु सा पुण्या कन्या वेतसकेषु च। तपोविशेषैर्बहुभिः कर्षयद् देहमात्मनः॥
en: Going then to Panchaganga and afterwards to Vetasa, that already-purified lady, pulled her own body down by performing various kinds of asceticism.

description: The colloquy between Death and the Lord of Creation
sn: ततो गत्वा तु सा गङ्गां महामेरुं च केवलम्। तस्थौ चाश्मेव निश्चेष्टा प्राणायामपरायणा॥
en: Repairing next to the Ganga and thence to the great Meru, she remained inert like a block of stone, devoting herself in the practice of Pranayama (suspension of breaths).

description: The colloquy between Death and the Lord of Creation
sn: पुनर्हिमवतो मूर्ध्नि यत्र देवाः पुराऽयजन्। तत्राङ्गुष्ठेन सा तस्थौ निखर्वं परमा शुभा॥
en: From that place repairing to the crest of the Himavat mountain, where, in the days of yore, the gods had performed their sacred sacrifices, that excellent and auspicious damsel stood on her tip toe for a billion of years.

description: The colloquy between Death and the Lord of Creation
sn: पुष्करेष्वथ गोकर्णे नैमिषे मलये तथा अपाकर्षत् स्वकं देहं नियमैर्मानसप्रियैः॥
en: Thence going to Puskara and Gokarna and Naimisha and Malaya, she pulled her health down by the practice of penances after her own choice.

description: The colloquy between Death and the Lord of Creation
sn: अनन्यदेवता नित्यं दृढभक्ता पितामहे। तस्थौ पितामहं चैव तोषयामास धर्मतः॥
en: Without worshipping any other god and with firin devotion to the Grandsire, she lived and propitiated him in every way and everywhere.

description: The colloquy between Death and the Lord of Creation
sn: ततस्तामब्रवीत् प्रीतो लोकानां प्रभवोऽव्ययः। सौम्येन मनसा राजन् प्रीत: प्रीतमनास्तदा॥
en: Thereafter the undeteriorating Creator of die universe, thus propitiated, spoke to her with

description: The colloquy between Death and the Lord of Creation
sn: मृत्यो किमिदमत्यन्तं तपांसि चरसीति ह। ततोऽब्रवीत् पुनर्मूतवुर्भगवन्तं पितामहम्॥
en: "O Death, what for are you under-going all these severe ascetic penances?" Thereat Death once more addressed the illustrious divinity, the Grandsire, sayingनाहं हन्यां प्रजा देव स्वस्थाश्चाक्रोशतीस्तथा।

description: The colloquy between Death and the Lord of Creation
sn: एतदिच्छामि सर्वेश त्वत्तो वरमहं प्रभो॥
en: "O God, I shall not be able to destroy of living creatures. They are all in the enjoyment of health and do not envy one another. O Lord, even this is the boon that I want at your hands, Omaster of all.

description: The colloquy between Death and the Lord of Creation
sn: अधर्मभयभीताऽस्मि ततोऽहं तप आस्थिता। भीतायास्तु महाभाग प्रयच्छाभयमव्यय॥
en: I am afraid of sin; and it is for this reason hat I am engaged in the practice of ascetic austerities. 0 blessed Lord! vouchsafe assurances of eternal safety to overwhelmed with terror.

description: The colloquy between Death and the Lord of Creation
sn: आर्ता चानागसी नारी याचामि भव मे गतिः। तामब्रवीत् ततो देवो भूतभव्यभविष्यवित्॥
en: A woman by birth, helpless and sinless, I iimplore your mercy, be you my refuge." Thereupon that Divinity possessed to the knowledge of the past, the present and the future thus spoke to her again.

description: The colloquy between Death and the Lord of Creation
sn: अधर्मोनास्ति ते मृत्योसंहरन्त्या इमाः प्रजाः। मया चोक्तं मृषा भद्रे भविता न कथंचन॥
en: “in destroying all these creatures, O Death, vou shall reap no sin. My words, O handsome dainsel, can never be false. me

description: The colloquy between Death and the Lord of Creation
sn: तस्मात् संहर कल्याणि प्रजाः सर्वाश्चतुर्विधाः। धमः सनातनश्च त्वां सर्वथा पावयिष्यति॥
en: Therefore, O blessed lady, destroy these four kinds of creatures. Eternal virtue shall always be yours.

description: The colloquy between Death and the Lord of Creation
sn: लोकपालो यमश्चैव सहाया व्याधयश्च ते। अहं च विबुधाश्चैव पुनर्दास्याम ते वरम्॥
en: Yama, the Regent of the worlds and the vai tous maladies, shall help you in your work of destruction. Myself and the celestials also will bestow boons on you;

description: The colloquy between Death and the Lord of Creation
sn: यथा त्वमेनसा मुक्ता विरजाः ख्यातिमेष्यसि। सैवमुक्ता महाराज कृताञ्जलिरिदं विभुम्॥ पुनरेवाब्रवीद् वाक्यं प्रसाद्य शिरसा तदा। यद्येवमेतत् कर्तव्यं मया न स्याद् विना प्रभो॥
en: So that purged of all sins and perfectly purified, you shall attain glory. Having been thus spoken to, O mighty monarch, she, with her palms folded, thus addressed the Lord, saluting him by bending her head low. "If, O lord, such be the state of things and if it cannot do without me.

description: The colloquy between Death and the Lord of Creation
sn: तवाज्ञा पूर्ध्निमेन्यस्ता यत् ते वक्ष्यामि तच्छृणु। लोभः क्रोधोऽभ्यसूयेाद्रोहोमोहश्च देहिनाम्॥
en: Then I place your behest upon my own head. However hear what I have to say. Let covetousness, anger, animosity malice, dissensions and folly and shamelessness and other stern passions tear to pieces the frames of corporeal beings.'

description: The colloquy between Death and the Lord of Creation
sn: ब्रह्मोवाच अह्रश्चान्योन्यपरुषा देहं भिन्छुः पृथग्विधाः। तथा भविष्यते मृत्या साधु संहर भोः प्रजाः। अधर्मस्तेन भविता नापध्यास्याम्यहं शुभे॥
en: Brahma said It shall be as you desire, O Death. Do you begin to destroy the creatures. No sin will hang on you; I shall not seek to injure you, O blessed damsel.

description: The colloquy between Death and the Lord of Creation
sn: स्ते व्याधयः प्राणिनामात्मजाताः। ते मारयिष्यन्ति नरान् गतासून् नाधमस्ते भविता मास भैषीः॥
en: There tears of yours which I hold in my hands, even they will become maladies, starting into existence from the creatures themselves. They will destroy men whose lifetime has been exhausted. No sin will hang on you. Do not be frightened.

description: The colloquy between Death and the Lord of Creation
sn: नाधर्मस्ते भविता प्राणिनां वै त्वं वै धर्मस्त्वं हि धर्मस्य चेशा। धा भूत्वा धर्मनित्या धरित्री तस्मात् प्राणान् सर्वथेमान् नियच्छ॥
en: Verily sin shall not be yours. You shall be the righteousness of living creatures, and the presiding deity of that righteousness. Devoted to virtue and observant of your duties, you shall control all creatures. Therefore destroy always the lives of these corporeal creatures.

description: The colloquy between Death and the Lord of Creation
sn: सर्वेषां वै प्राणिनां कामरोषौ संत्यज्य त्वं संहरस्वेह जीवान्। एवं धर्मस्त्वां भविष्यत्यनन्तो मिथ्यावृत्तात् मानयिष्यत्यधर्मः॥
en: Renouncing both desire and anger, snatch out the lives of all living creatures. In this way you shall sccure eternal merit. Sin will destroy those who are vicious in their conduct of life.

description: The colloquy between Death and the Lord of Creation
sn: तेनात्मानं पावयस्वात्मना त्वं पापेऽऽत्मानं मज्जयिष्यन्त्यसत्यात्। तस्मात् कामं रोषमप्यागतं त्वं संत्यज्यान्तः संहरस्वेति जीवान्॥
en: Carrying out my command, purify yourself. The task of plunging those who are wicked, in their own sins, will be left to you. Therefore renounce desire and anger and begin destroying those creatures possessed of life.”

description: The colloquy between Death and the Lord of Creation
sn: नारद उवाच च्छापाद् भीता बाढमित्यब्रवीत् तम्। सा च प्राणं प्राणिनामन्तकाले कामक्रोधौ त्यज्य हरत्यसक्ता॥
en: Narada said Thereafter that lady, seeing that she was persistently called by the name of Death, became afraid of acting otherwise. And in fear of Brahma's malediction, she said Yea.' Unable to set at naught the behests of Brahma, she began, renouncing wrath and desire, 10 deprive living creatures of their lives, when their last days came.

description: The colloquy between Death and the Lord of Creation
sn: मृत्युस्त्वेषां व्याधयस्तत्प्रसूता व्याधी रोगो रुज्यते येन जन्तुः। सर्वेषां च प्राणिनां प्रायणान्ते तस्माच्छोकं मा कृथा निष्फलं त्व त्वम्॥
en: Death is the lot of all living creatures. Maladies originate out of living creatures. Maladies are the abnormal conditions of living beings and they are pained by them. Discase and death fall to the share of all creatures. Therefore do you not indulge in fruitless griet

description: The colloquy between Death and the Lord of Creation
sn: सर्वे देवाः प्राणिभिः प्रायणान्ते गत्वा वृत्त संनिवृत्तास्तथैव। एवं सर्वे प्राणिनस्तत्र गत्वा वृत्ता देवा मर्त्यवद् राजसिंह॥
en: Upon the death of living creatures, their senses go with them; and achieving their respective functions in the other world, they come back with their possessors, (when they are born anew). Thus all creatures including the gods going thither, have to act like mortals, O best of all kings.

description: The colloquy between Death and the Lord of Creation
sn: वायुीमो भीमनादो महौजा भेत्ता देहान् प्राणिनां सर्वगोऽसौ। नो वाऽऽवृत्तिं नैव वृत्तिं कदाचित् प्राप्नोत्युग्रोऽनन्ततेजोविशिष्टः॥
en: The wind that is tremendous. of dreadful roars and great strength, omni-present and endowed with energy infinite, even that wind will tear open the bodies of living creatures. It will, in this action, put forth no active energy. nor will it suspend its workings.

description: The colloquy between Death and the Lord of Creation
sn: स्तस्मात् पुत्रं मा शुचोराजसिंह। स्वर्गे प्राप्तो मोदते ते तनूजो नित्यं रम्यान् वीरलोकानवाप्य॥
en: Even all the gods and qualified with the adjective mortal. Therefore, o foremost of kings, do not bewail you son. Your son having ascended to heaven, is enjoying perpetual happiness, in those delightful regions allotted to the heroes.

description: The colloquy between Death and the Lord of Creation
sn: रेषा मृत्युर्देवदिष्टा प्रजानाम्। प्राप्ते काले संहरन्ती यथावत् स्वयं कृता प्राणहरा प्रजानाम्॥
en: Renouncing all grief, he has obtained the fellowship of the virtuous. Death has been ordained for all corporeal beings by the Creator himself. So when their days are numbered, they suffer destruction. The death of creatures is brought about by their ownselves.

description: The colloquy between Death and the Lord of Creation
sn: आत्मानं वै प्राणिनो मन्ति सर्वे नैतान् मृत्युदण्डपाणिर्हिनस्ति। तस्मान्मृतान् नानुशोचन्ति धीरा मृत्युं ज्ञात्वा निश्चयं ब्रह्मसृष्टम्। इत्थं सृष्टि देवक्लप्तां विदित्वा पुत्रान्नष्टाच्छोकमाशु त्यजस्व॥
en: Creatures destroy themselves. Death does not destroy any one, armed though she is with the mortal dart. Therefore the wise, knowing death to be unavoidable being ordained by Brahma, never lament for those that are dead. Now knowing that death is ordained by the highest divinity, renounce, without delay, your sorrow for you son.

description: The colloquy between Death and the Lord of Creation
sn: व्यास उवाच एतच्छुत्वार्थवद् वाक्यं नारदेन प्रकाशितम्। उवाचाकम्पनो राजा सखायं नारदं तथा॥
en: Vyasa said Having heard these words of grave signification uttered by Narada, Narada, king Akampana, addressing his friend Narada said-

description: The colloquy between Death and the Lord of Creation
sn: व्यपेतशोकः प्रीतोऽस्मि भगवऋषिसत्तम। श्रुत्वेतिहासं त्वत्तस्तु कृतार्थोऽस्म्यभिवादये॥
en: "O illustrious one, O foremost of Rishis, I am gratified an my sorrow has left me. Hearing this story from you, I am contented and I salute you.”

description: The colloquy between Death and the Lord of Creation
sn: तथोक्तो नारदस्तेन राज्ञा ऋषिवरोत्तमः। जगाम नन्दनं शीघ्रं देवर्षिरमितात्मवान्॥
en: Thus spoken to by that monarch, Narada, that excellent of all the foremost sages, that celestial sage of immeasurable soul, speedily went back to the Nandana forest.

description: The colloquy between Death and the Lord of Creation
sn: पुण्यं यशस्यं स्वर्णं च धन्यमायुष्यमेव च। अस्येतिहासस्य सदा श्रवणं श्रावणं तथा॥
en: The frequent audition as well as the recital of this piece of history is held to be purifying, fame-giving leading to paradise, life-giving and fraught with all blessings.

description: The colloquy between Death and the Lord of Creation
sn: एतदर्थपदं श्रुत्वा तदा राजा युधिष्ठिरः। क्षत्रधर्मे च विज्ञाय शूराणां च परां गतिम्॥ सम्प्राप्तोऽसौ महावीर्यः स्वर्गलोकं महारथः।
en: Having heard this instructive story, renounce your sorrow, O king Yudhishthira, you know the duties of a Kshatriya and the region they may attain to after death.

description: The colloquy between Death and the Lord of Creation
sn: युध्यमानो महेष्वासो हतः सोऽभिमुखो रणे। असिना गदया शक्त्या धनुषा च महारथः। विरजाः सोमसूनुः स पुनस्तत्र प्रलीयते॥
en: The mighty car-warrior Abhimanyu endued with great energy has ascended to heaven, having slain his enemies in battle, before the presence of all bowmen. That mighty carwarrior, that fierce bowman, has been slain, when fighting, with swords, lances, maces and bows. He is the sinless son of the moon and is now dissolved in the lunar essence.

description: The colloquy between Death and the Lord of Creation
sn: तस्मात् परां धृति कृत्वा भ्रातृभिः सह पाण्डव। अप्रमत्तः सुसंनद्धः शीघ्रं योद्भुमुपाक्रम॥
en: Therefore, O son of Pandu, mustering all your courage, yourself accompanied by your brothers, speedily march out for battle inflamed with wrath and without allowing your senses to become stupefied.

sn: संजय उवाच श्रुत्वा मृत्युसमुत्पत्तिं कर्माण्यनुपमानि च। धर्मराजः पुनर्वाक्यं प्रसाद्यैनमथाब्रवीत्॥
en: Sanjaya said Having heard of the origin of Death and her strange deeds, the very virtuous king Yudhishthira, once more humbly addressing

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच गुरुः पुण्यकर्माणः शक्रप्रतिमविक्रमाः। स्थाने राजर्षयो ब्रह्मन्ननघाः सत्यवादिनः॥
en: Yudhishthira said In many blessed countries there were many many monarchs, of virtuous deeds and of prowess equal to that of Shakra (Indra) himself. O Brahman, they were royal sages, sinless and lovers of truthful speech.

sn: भूय एव तु मां तथ्यैर्वचोभिरभिबृहय। राजर्षीणां पुराणानां समाश्वासय कर्मभिः॥
en: Once again, do you address me in words of grave signification and comfort me with the story of the feats of those royal sages of ancient days.

sn: कियन्त्यो दक्षिणादत्ताः कैश्च दत्ता महात्मभिः। राजर्षिभिः पुण्यकृद्भिस्तद्भावान् प्रब्रवीतु मे॥
en: What was the amount of the sacrificial gifts made by them? Who were those royal sages of high soul and virtuous practices that made them? Tell me all this, O almighty Rishi!

sn: व्यास उवाच शैब्यस्य नृपतेः पुत्रः सृञ्जया नाम नामतः। सखायौ तस्य चैवोभौ ऋषी पर्वतनारदौ॥
en: There lived in days gone by, a king known by the name of Srinjaya. He had a son who was named Shaivya; the sages Parvata and Narada were his friends.

sn: तौ कदाचिद् गृहं तस्य प्रविष्टौ तद्दिक्षया। विधिवच्चार्चितौ तेन प्रीतौ तत्रौ तत्रोषतुः सुखम्॥
en: Once on a time desirous of an interview with him, the Rishis entered his palace. Being duly adored by him, they continued to live there happily.

sn: तं कदाचित् सुखासीनं ताभ्यां सह शुचिस्मिता। दुहिताभ्यागमत् कन्या सृञ्जयं वरवर्णिनी॥
en: One day when Srinjaya was seated with the sages at his ease, his very beautiful daughter of pure smiles came to him.

sn: तयाभिवादितः कन्यामभ्यनन्दद् यथाविधि। तत्सलिङ्गाभिराशीभिरिष्टाभिरभितः स्थिताम्॥
en: Then saluted by that daughter of his, he greeted her with benedictions after her own desire, when she was standing beside him.

sn: तां नीरीक्ष्याब्रवीद् वाक्यं पर्वतः प्रहसन्निव। कस्येयं चञ्जलापानी सर्वलक्षणसम्मता॥
en: Beholding that girl, Parvata smilingly said these words to Srinjaya-"Whose daughter is this girl of restless glances and auspicious marks?

sn: उताहो भाः स्विदर्कस्य ज्वलनस्य शिखा त्वियम्। श्रीहीः कीर्तिधृतिः पुष्टिः सिद्धिश्चन्द्रमसः प्रभा॥
en: Is she the effulgence of the solar orb or the blazing flame of Fire? Or is she Sri or Hari or Kirti or Dhriti or Pushti or Siddhi or the splendour of the moon?"

sn: एवं ब्रुवाणं देवर्षि नृपतिः सृञ्जयोऽब्रवीत्। ममेयं भगवन् कन्या मत्तो वरमभीप्सति॥
en: Thereupon king Srinjaya replied to the celestial sage who spoke those words, thus-"O almighty Rishis, this damsel is my daughter and she solicits my blessings."

sn: नारदस्त्वप्रवीदेनं देहि मह्यमिमां नृप। भार्यार्थं सुमहच्छ्रेयः प्राप्तुं चेदिच्छसे नृप॥
en: Thereafter Narada addressed the king saying-"O monarch, if you desire to secure great good, give me this your daughter in marriage.”

sn: ददानीत्येव संहृष्टः सृञ्जयः प्राह नारदम्। पर्वतस्तु सुसंकुद्धो नारदं वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
en: Filled with delight (at the Rishi's proposal) Srinjaya said to Narada-"I shall give her in marriage to you." Thercat the other sage Parvata excited with wrath, said these words to Narada.

sn: हृदयेन मया पूर्वे वृतां वै वृतवानसि। यस्माद् वृता त्वया विप्र मागाः स्वर्ग यथेप्सया॥
en: "You have accepted this girl for your wife, whom before you I had chosen in my heart to be my wife; and because you have done this, you shall not, O Brahmana, go to heaven at your will."

sn: एवमुक्तो नारदस्तं प्रत्युवाचोत्तरं वचः। मनोवाग्बुद्धिसम्भाषा दत्ता चोदकपूर्वकम्॥ पाणिग्रहणमन्त्राश्च प्रथितं वरलक्षणम्। न त्वेषा निश्चिता निष्ठा निष्ठा सप्तपदी स्मृता॥
en: Thus spoken to, Narada said to him these words in reply "The husband's heart, his speech, the giver's consent, the speeches of both of them, the actual gift made with the sprinkling of water. The mantras specified for holding the bride's hands, these have been said to be the indications by which one becomes know as the husband of a damsel. But these Ceremonials are not sufficient, the essential one being the walk for seven paces after the marriage.

sn: अनुत्पन्ने च कार्यार्थे मां त्वं व्याहृतवानसि। तस्मात् त्वमपि न स्वर्गे गमिष्यसि मया विना॥
en: "Without any provocation whatever, you have pronounced a curse on me. Therefore you also shall not go to heaven save in my company."

sn: अन्योन्यमेवं शप्त्वा वै तस्थतस्तत्र सौ तदा। अथ सोऽपि नृयो विप्रान् पानाच्छादनभोजनैः॥ पुत्रकामः परं शक्त्या यत्नाच्चोपाचरच्छुचिः। तस्य प्रसन्नाविप्रेन्दाः कदाचित् पुत्रमीप्सवः॥ तपःस्वाध्यायनिरता वेदवेदाङ्गपारगाः। सहिता नारदं प्राहुर्देह्यस्मै पुत्रमीप्सितम्॥
en: Thus having cursed each other those two sages continued to live there. Meanwhile Srinjaya, desirous of obtaining a son and purifying himself, began to gratify the Vipras to the best of his resources, with drinks, garments and foods. After a while, those Brahmanas devoted to the study of the Vedas and acquainted with the contents of the scriptures and their various auxiliaries, being gratified with the king, who desired to have a son, came in a body to Narada and said to him-"Give this king a son of the sort he desires."

sn: तथेत्युक्त्वा द्विजैरुक्तः सृञ्जयनारदोऽब्रवीत्। तुभ्यं प्रसन्ना राजर्षे पुत्रमीप्सन्ति ब्राह्मणाः॥
en: Thus spoken to by the regenerate sages, Narada said Let it be so': and then he addressed Srinjaya saying-'0) royal sage, the Brahmanas have been gratified with you and they desire to bestow a son on you.

sn: वरं वृणीष्व भद्रं ते यादृशं पुत्रमीप्सितम्। तथोक्तः प्राञ्जली राजा पुत्रं वद्रे गुणान्वितम्॥ यशस्विनं कीर्तिमन्तं तेजस्विनमरिंदमम्। यस्य मूत्रं पुरीषं च क्लेदः स्वेदश्च काञ्चनम्॥
en: Good betide you. Ask for the boon about the kind of the son wish to have.' Thus addressed, the king with folded palms, solicited the boon of getting a son endued with all qualities, famous, possessed of glory, highly energetic and subduer of all foes, whose urine, excreta, secretions and perspiration would be gold.”

sn: सुवर्णष्ठीविरित्यवं तस्य नामाभवत् कृतम्। तस्मिन् वरप्रदानेन वर्षयत्यमितं धनम्॥
en: The king then obtained a son in due time who came to be called Suvarnasthivi on earth and through the virtue of that boon the child began to increase the wealth of his father beyond all limit.

sn: कारयामास नृपतिः सौवर्णं सर्वमीप्सितम्। गृहप्राकारदुर्गाणि ब्राह्मणावसथान्यपि॥ शय्यासनानि यानानि स्थाली पिठरभाजनम्। तस्य राज्ञाऽपि यद् वेश्म बाह्याश्चापस्कराश्च ये॥ सर्वे तत् काञ्चनमयं कालेन परिवर्धितम्।
en: King Srinjaya then caused all objects of his desire to be made of gold; and his houses and walls and fortresses and the residencies of the Brahınanas, his beds, conveyances, plates and all kinds of cups, saucers and the mansion he possessed and all implements and utensils, domestic and otherwise. Were caused to be made of gold. In the course of time his treasure went on increasing

sn: अथ दस्युगणाः श्रुत्वा दृष्ट्वा चैनं तथाविधम्॥ सम्भूय तस्य नृपतः समारब्धाश्चिकीर्षितुम्।
en: Then certain robbers hearing of the prince and seeing him to be such banded together and endeavoured to do mischief to the king.

sn: केचित् तत्राब्रुवन् राज्ञः पुत्रं गृह्णीम वै स्वयम्॥ सोऽस्याकरः काञ्चनस्य तस्य यत्तं चरामहे।
en: Some of them said. "We shall seize the son of the king. He is the mine of gold of his father. Let us therefore try to seize him."

sn: ततस्ते दस्यवो लुब्धाः प्रविश्य नृपतेर्गृहम्॥ राजपुत्रं तथा जहुः सुवर्णष्ठीविनं बलात्।
en: Thereafter those robbers, led by covetousness, entered the king's palace; and forcibly look away the young prince Suvarnasthivi.

sn: गृह्येनमनुपायज्ञा नीत्वारण्यमचेतसः॥ हत्वा विशस्य चापश्यन् लुब्धा वसुन किञ्चन। तस्य प्राणैर्विमुक्तस्य नष्टं तद् वरदं वसु॥
en: Seizing him and carrying him to the woods, lose idiots not knowing what to do with him. (Out of avarice slew him and cut him to pieces. But they found not any gold inside his frame. When that child was deprived of his life, all the gold consequent the sages boon, disappeared.

sn: दस्यवश्च तदान्योन्यं जघ्नुर्मूर्खा विचेतसः। हत्वा परस्परं नष्टाः कुमारं चाद्भुतं भुवि॥
en: The robbers then, ignorant and idiotic as they were, slew one another; for having slain that wonderful prince, they also met with their destruction.

sn: असम्भाव्यं गता घोरं नरकं दुष्टकारिणः। तं दृष्ट्वा निहतं पुत्रं वरदत्तं महातपाः॥
en: These robbers of wicked deed were plunged to an awful and unimaginable hell. Then on beholding his son obtained through a boon slain, that one of great asceticism, viz.,

sn: विललाप सुदुःखार्तो बहुधा करुणं नृपः। विलपन्तं निशम्याथ पुत्रशोकहतं नृपम्॥
en: King Srinjaya began to lament plaintively being afflicted with terrible grief. Hearing the king afflicted with grief caused by his son's death thus lament.

sn: प्रत्यदृश्यत देवर्षि रदस्तस्य संनिधौ। उवाच चैनं दुःखार्ते विलपन्तमचेतसम्॥
en: The celestial Rishi Narada revealed himself before the king. And he spoke these words to the bewailing and woc-stricken and senseless.

sn: सृञ्जयं नारदोऽभ्येत्य तन्निबोध युधिष्ठिर। कामानामवितृप्तस्त्वं सृञ्जयेह मरिष्यसि॥
en: King Srinjaya. O Yudhishthira listen on 10 those words. Narada said : You shall have to die, O Srinjaya, with many of your desirc', unfulfiled.

sn: यस्य चैते वयं गेहे उषिता ब्रह्मवादिनः। आविक्षितं मरुत्तं च मृतं सृञ्जय शुश्रुम॥
en: Although we the reciters of the sacre. Veda live under your roof. O Srinjaya, we had ) hear of the death of even Avikshita's son Marutta.

sn: संवर्तो याजयामास स्पर्धया वै बृहस्पतेः। यस्मै राजर्षये प्रादाद् धनं स भगवान् प्रभुः॥ हैमं हिमवतः पादं यियक्षोर्विविधैः स वै। यस्य सेन्द्राऽमरगणा बृहस्पतिपुरोगमाः॥ देवा विश्वसृजः सर्वे यजनान्ते समासते। यज्ञवाटस्य सौवर्णाः सर्वे चासन् परिच्छदाः॥
en: Piqued with Brihaspati, he had compelled even Samvarta himself to be a office-bearer in one of his greal sacrifices. To that royal sage, the illustrious divinity (Mahadeva) had given wealth in the shape of a golden plateau of Himavat. There with Marutta had accomplished numerous sacrifices. After the accomplishment of his sacrifices, various tribes of celestials, the creators of the world, accompanied by Indra and headed by Brihaspati, used to come to him. All the carpets and furniture's of his sacrificial compound were made of gold.

sn: यस्य सर्वं तदा ह्यन्नं मनोऽभिप्रायगं शुचि। कामतो बुभुजुर्विप्राः सर्वे चान्नार्थिनो द्विजाः॥ पयो दधि घृतं क्षौद्रं भक्ष्यं भोज्यं च शोभनम्। यस्य यज्ञेषु सर्वेषु वासांस्याभरणानि च॥ ईप्सितान्युपतिष्ठन्ते प्रहृष्टान् वेदपारगान्। मरुतः परिवेष्टारो मरुत्तास्याभवन् गृहे॥
en: At his sacrifices the twice-born sects desirous of food all ate as it pleased them-food that was purified and suited to their tastes. At all his sacrifices, milk and curds and clarified butter and honey and other kinds of drinks and edibles, all of the finest sort and garments and ornaments precious and desirable, used to be given to Brahmanas thoroughly acquainted with the scriptures. The very gods became the distributors of food in Marutta's palace.

sn: आविक्षितस्य राजर्षेर्विश्वेदेवाः सभासदः। यस्य वीर्यवतो राज्ञः सुवृष्ट्या सस्यसम्पदः॥ हविर्भिस्तर्पिता येन सम्यक् क्लृप्तैर्दिवौकसः। ऋषीणां च पितॄणां च देवानां सुखजीविनाम्॥ ब्रह्मचर्यश्रुतिमुखैः सर्वैर्दानैश्च सर्वदा। शयनासनयानानि स्वर्णराशीश्च दुस्त्यजाः॥ तत् सर्वममितं वित्तं दत्तं विप्रेभ्य इच्छया। सोऽनुध्यातस्तु शक्रेण प्रजाः कृत्वा निरामयाः॥ श्रद्दधानोजिताँल्लोकान् गत: पुण्यदुहोऽक्षयान्।
en: The Visvadevas were the courtiers of that royal sage the son of Avikshita. By him were propitiated the dwellers of heaven with oblations of clarified butter; gratified therewith, the gods, in their turn, increased that sovereign's wealth of corn by profuse showers of rain. He always contributed to the pleasure of the Rishis, the ancestral manes and the celestials and thereby made them propitious, as also by practising Brahmacharya, by the study of the Vedas, by observance of obsequial rites and by offering all kinds of gifts. His beds and carpets and conveyances and his vast treasures of gold difficult to be given away, in reality, all that vast among of wealth of his, were voluntarily distributed among the Brahmanas. Indra himself wished him well. His subjects were made happy by him. Performing all acts through piety, he finally attained to the eternal regions of bliss acquired by his religious merit.

sn: सप्रजः सनृपामात्यः सदारापत्यबान्धवः॥ यौवनेन सहस्राब्दं मरुत्तो राज्यमन्वशात्।
en: With his children, counsellors wives, descendants, relatives, king Marutta, in the days of his youth, ruled his dominions for a thousand years.

sn: स चेन्ममार सृञ्जय चतुर्भद्रतरस्त्वया॥ पुत्रात् पुण्यतरस्तुभ्यं मा पुत्रमनुतप्यथाः। अयज्वानमदाक्षिण्यमभि श्वैत्येव्याहरन्॥
en: When even such a monarch, O Srinjaya, superior to you in respect of the four cardinal virtues and who, superior to you, was much more superior to your son, had to suffer death, do not lament for your son, saying Shvaitya,' who performed no sacrifice and made no sacrificial presents.

sn: नारद उवाच सुहोत्रं नाम राजानं मृतं सृञ्जय शुश्रुम। एकवीरमशक्यं तममरैरभिवीक्षितुम्॥
en: Narada said O Srinjaya, we heard also of the death of king Suhotra, who was the foremost of all heroes, invincible and interviewed by the gods themselves.

sn: यः प्राप्य राज्यं धर्मेण ऋत्विग्ब्रह्मपुरोहितान्। अपृच्छदात्मनः श्रेयः पृष्ट्वा तेषां मते स्थितः॥
en: Having obtained his kingdom by virtue, he used to question his Ritvigas, family priests and Brahmanas about its welfare and then used to live up to their instructions.

sn: प्रजानां पालनं धर्मो दानमिज्या द्विषज्जयः। एतत् सुहोत्रो विज्ञाय धर्मेणैच्छद् धनागमम्॥
en: Knowing virtue to be identified with the protection of his subjects, acts of charity and performance of sacrifices and the subjugation of foes, Suhotra desired the increase of his wealth,

sn: धर्मेणाराधयन् देवान् बाणैः शत्रूञ्जयंस्तथा। सर्वाण्यपि च भूतानि स्वगुणैरण्यरञ्जयत्।॥
en: He worshipped the gods according to the ordinances of the holy texts and conquered his foes by means of his arrows. He pleased all creatures with his own excellent acquirements.

sn: यो भुक्त्वेमां वसुमती म्लेच्छाटविकवर्जिताम्। यस्मै ववर्ष पर्जन्यो हिरण्यं परिवत्सरान्॥
en: During his time of rule, the earth was freed from the depredation of Mlecchas and the forest-thieves and the Parjanya showered gold throughout the whole year.

sn: हैरण्यास्तत्र वाहिन्यः स्वैरिण्यो व्यवहन् पुरा। ग्राहान् कर्कटकांश्चैव मत्स्यांश्च विविधान् बहून्॥ कामान् वर्षति पर्जन्यो रूप्याणि विविधानि च। सौवर्णान्यप्रमेयाणि वाप्यश्च क्रोशसम्मिताः॥
en: In those days of his the rivers ran liquid gold and were open to the use of everybody. Parjanya then poured on his kingdom large numbers of golden alligators, crabs and fishes of various classes and many other objects of desire; the artificial lakes of his dominions were full two miles long.

sn: सहस्रं वामनान् कुब्जान् नक्रान् मकरकच्छपान्। सौवर्णान् विहितान् दृष्ट्वा ततोऽस्मयत वै तदा॥
en: Then king Suhotra beholding thousands of dwarfs hunch-backs, alligators and sharks and tortoises, all made of gold, was greatly amazed.

sn: तत् सुवर्णमपर्यन्तं राजर्षिः कुरुजाङ्गले। ईजानो वितते यज्ञे ब्राह्मणेभ्यो ह्यमन्यत॥
en: That royal sage, having performed a sacrifice in Kurujangala, gave away that unlimited quantity of gold to the Brahmanas, even before the accomplishment of that sacrifice.

sn: सोऽश्वमेधसहस्रेण राजसूयशतेन च। पुण्यैः क्षत्रिययज्ञेश्च प्रभूतवरदक्षिणैः॥
en: Having celebrated thousand horsesacrifices, a hundred Rajasuya sacrifices and, numerous other Kshatriya sacrifices, in all of a which he gave away vast wealth as sacrificial presents.

sn: काम्यनैमित्तिकाजौरिष्टां गतिमवाप्तवान्। स चेन्ममार सृञ्जय चतुर्भद्रतरस्त्वया॥
en: And also having accomplished numerous daily rites from specific wishes, that king ultimately attained to a very desirable end. O Srinjaya, when even such a king suffered death, who was superior to you in all the four virtues.

sn: पुत्रात् पुण्यतरस्तुभ्यं मा पुत्रमनुतप्यथाः। अपज्वानमदाक्षिण्यमभि श्वैत्येत्युदाहरत्॥
en: And so was superior to your son, you should not lament for your son saying 'O Shvaitya' who performed no sacrifice and gave away no sacrificial presents.

sn: नारद उवाच राजानं पौरवं वीरं मृतं सृञ्जय शुश्रुम। सहस्रं यः सहस्राणां श्वेतानश्वानवासृजत्॥
en: Narada said O Srinjaya, we also heard of the death of the heroic king Paurava, who gave away a thousand times thousand horses that were all white in colour.

sn: तस्याश्वमेधे राजधैर्देशाद्देशात् समीयुषाम्। शिक्षाक्षरविधिज्ञानां नासीत् संख्या विपश्चिताम्॥
en: At the celebration of the horse-sacrifice by him, the number of Brahmanas learned in the Shiksha and Aksharas that then presented themselves from different countries, indeed countless.

sn: वेदविद्याव्रतस्नाता वदान्याः प्रियदर्शनाः। सुभिक्षाच्छादनगृहाः सुशय्यासनभोजनाः॥
en: These Brahmanas, purified by the Vedas, by learning, by the observance of vows, all of benevolent dispositions and of amiable features, received from the monarch gifts of such things as garments, horses, precious beeds, carpets and conveyances.

sn: नटनर्तकगन्धर्वैः पूर्णकैवर्धमानकैः। नित्योद्योगैश्च क्रीडद्भिस्तत्र स्म परिहर्षिताः॥
en: They were always entertained by actors, dancers, ministrels perfectly accomplished and well-acquainted with their respective arts and engaged in sports and always striving for pleasing the former.

sn: यज्ञे यज्ञे यथाकालं दक्षिणा: सोऽत्यकालयत्। द्विपा दशसहस्राख्याः प्रमदाः काञ्चनप्रभाः॥
en: Al cach of his sacrifices, in due time, he used to give away as Dakshina, ten thousand elephants of golden cffulgence, with their lemporal juice trickling down.

sn: सध्वजाः सपताकाश्च रथा हेममयास्तथा। यः सहस्रं सहस्राणि कन्या हेमविभूषिताः॥
en: And also golden chariots decked with standards and flags, He also used to give away as Dakshina a thousand times thousand damsels, all adorned with golden ornaments.

sn: धूर्युजाश्वगजारूढाः सगृहक्षेत्रगोशताः। शतं शतसहस्राणि स्वर्णमालिमहात्मनाम्॥ गवां सहस्रानुचरान् दक्षिणामत्यकालयत्।
en: And chariots, elephants and horses for mounting and mansions and fields and luundreds of cows and thousands of high-souled cattle-tenders all decked with chains of gold.

sn: हेमशृङ्ग्यो रौप्यखुराः सवत्सा: कांस्यदोहनाः॥ दासीदासखरोष्ट्राश्च प्रादादाजाविकं बहु।
en: That in that sacrifice king Paurava gave away as gifts kine with calves, having horns of gold, hoofs of silver and udders of brass, as ! also numerous male and female slaves, asses, camels and sheep.

sn: रत्नानां विविधानां च विविधांश्चान्नपर्वतान्॥ तस्मिन् संवितते यज्ञे दक्षिणामत्यकालयत्।
en: He also gave away as presents, diverse kinds of gems and numerous piles of food and cdibles, even before the accomplishment of his sacrifices.

sn: तत्रास्य गाथा गायन्ति ये पुराणविदो जनाः॥
en: People conversant with the history of the past ages sing this songs.

sn: अङ्गस्य यजमानस्य स्वधर्माधिगताः शुभाः। गुणोत्तरास्तु क्रतवस्तस्यासन् सार्वकामिकाः॥
en: That monarch of the Angas, ever devoted to the performance of sacrifice, celebrated many auspicious sacrifices suited to his order, one after another, according to their respective efficacy; and these sacrifices yielded all his objects of desire.

sn: स चेन्ममार सृञ्जय चतुर्भद्रतरस्त्वया। पुत्रा पुण्यतरुतुभ्यं मा पुत्रमनुतप्यथाः। अयज्वानमदाक्षिण्यमभि श्वैत्येत्युदाहरत्॥
en: O Srinjaya, when even such a king suffered destruction, who was superior to you in all his four cardinal virtues and so who was far superior to your son, you should not lament for your son saying, Oh Shvaitya and should not grieve for his having performed no sacrifices and made no sacrificial presents.

sn: नारद उवाच शिबिमौशीनरं चापि मृतं सृञ्जय शुश्रुम। य इमां पृथिवीं सर्वां चर्मवत् पर्यवेष्टयत्॥
en: Narada said We heard, O Srinjaya, that even Sini, the son of Ushinara, had to sutfer death, who had put, as it were, a leathern band round the entire earth.

sn: साद्रिद्वीपार्णववनां रथघोषेण नादयन्। स शिबिर्वैरिपून् नित्यं मुख्यान् निघ्नन् सपत्नजित्॥
en: He made the earth with her mountain and the islands and seas and forests resound with the clatter of his car-whecls. That subduer of foes, viz., Sini himself, every day used to slay the foremost of his opponents.

sn: तेन यज्ञेर्बहुविधैरिष्टं पर्याप्तदक्षिणैः। स राजा वीर्यवान् धीमानवाप्य वसु पुष्कलम्॥
en: He celebrated various sacrifices attended with profuse sacrificial presents; that highly puissant and intelligent monarch acquired enormous quality of wealth.

sn: सर्वमूर्धाभिषिक्तानां सम्मत: सोऽभवद्युधि। अयजच्चाश्वमेधैर्यो विजित्य पृथिवीमिमाम्॥
en: In battle he came to be recognised as the head of all the Kshatriya. Having brought the entire earth under his control, he performed many Horse-sacrifices.

sn: निरर्गलैर्बहुफलैर्निष्ककोटिसहस्रदः। हस्त्यश्वपशुभिर्धान्यैर्मुगैर्गोऽजाविभिस्तथा॥
en: Productive of great merit without any the least obstruction, giving away as sacrificial presents thousands and millions of golden nikshas, numerous elephants, steeds and other kinds of animals, large quantities of grain and countless deer, cows and sheep.

sn: विविधा पृथिवीं पुण्यां शिविर्ब्राह्मणसात्करोत्। यावत्यो वर्षतो धारा यावत्यो दिवि तारकाः॥ यावतयः सिकता गाङ्गेयो यावन्मेरोर्महोपलाः। उदन्वति च यावनित रत्नानि प्राणिनोऽपि च॥ तावतीरददद् गा वै शिविरौशीनरोऽध्वरे। नो यन्तारं धुरस्तस्य कञ्चिदन्यं प्रजापतिः॥ भूतं भव्यं भवन्तं वा नाध्यगच्छन्नरोत्तमम्। तस्यासन् विविधा यज्ञाः सर्वकामैः समन्विताः॥
en: And Sini also offered as a gift to the Brahmanas this earth consisting of various different kinds of soil. Indeed Ushinara's son Sini gave away as presents as many kine as is the number of rain drops showered on the earth or the number of stars in the firmament or the number of sand grains on the bed of the river Ganga, or the number of stones that compose the mount Meru or the number of gems or aquatic animals in the ocean. The Lord of creation has not come across or will not come across, in the past, the present or the future, another king competent to bear the burden that king Sini bore on his shoulders. The sacrifices celebrated by king Sini were numerous and attended with all sorts of rites.

sn: हेमयूपासनगृहा हेमप्राकारतोरणाः। शुचि स्वाद्वन्नपानं च ब्राह्मणाः प्रयुतायुताः॥
en: In his sacrifices, the stakes, the carpets, the horses, the walls and the arches were all made of gold. Edibles and drink suited to the taste and perfectly pure, were used to be supplied in abundance; and the Brahmanas that came there were countless.

sn: नानाभक्ष्यैः प्रियकथाः पयोदधिमहाह्रदाः। तस्यासन् यज्ञवाटेषु नद्यः शुभ्रानपर्वताः॥
en: Viands and edibles of every description were used to be distributed with agreeable words, (such as 'take, accept' etc.). There milk and curds used to be collected in lakes of large dimensions. In his sacrificial compound, flowed rivers of drink and stood hills of white edibles.

sn: पिबत स्नात खादध्वमिति यद् रोचते जनाः। यस्मै प्रादाद् वरं रुद्रस्तुष्टः पुण्येन कर्मणा॥
en: "Drink" "bathe" 'eat' and 'do as like,' these were the words that used to be heard there. Pleased with his deeds of piety, Rudra

sn: अक्षयं ददतो विततं श्रद्धा कीर्तिस्तथा क्रियाः। यथोक्तमेव भूतानां प्रियत्वं स्वर्गमुत्तमम्॥
en: “As you give away numerous presents, let your wealth, your devotion, your renown, your meritorious deeds, the love that people cherish for you and the paradise that you shall attain to, let all these of yours, be inexhaustible.”

sn: एताल्लब्वा वरानिष्टाशिबिः काले दिवं गतः। स चेन्ममार सृञ्जय चतुर्भद्रतरस्त्वया॥
en: Having obtained even such a desirable boon, in due time, Sini had to go to heaven. O Srinjaya, even when such a king had to suffer death who was superior to you in respect of the four virtues.

sn: पुत्रात् पुण्यतरस्तुभ्यं मा पुत्रमनुतप्यथाः। अयज्वानमदाक्षिण्यमभि श्वैत्येत्युदाहरत्॥
en: And consequently who was far more superior to your son, you should not lament for your son saying-O Shvaitya-who performed no sacrifice and made no gifts. your son saying-O Shvaitya-who performed no sacrifice and made no gifts.

sn: नारद उवाच रामं दाशरथिं चैव मृतं सृञ्जय शुश्रुम। यं प्रजा अन्वमोदन्त पिता पुत्रानिवौरसान्॥
en: Narada said O Srinjaya, we heard that even Rama that son of Dasaratha, had to suffer death. His subjects were as much delighted with him a father is pleased with the sons of his own loins.

sn: असंख्येया गुणा यस्मिन्नासन्नमिततेजसि। यश्चतुर्दश वर्षाणि निदेशात् पितुरच्युतः॥ वने वनितया सार्धमवसल्लक्ष्मणाग्रजः।
en: In that one endowed with immeasurable energy, innumerable virtues resided. At the command of his father that undeteriorating one, for fourteen long years lived in the woods with his wife and his younger brother Lakshmana.

sn: जघान च जनस्थाने राक्षसान् मनुजर्षभः॥ तपस्विनां रक्षणार्थे सहस्राणि चतुर्दश।
en: While in the forest of Janasthana, that foremost of men slew Rakshasas, fourteen thousand in number, for the protection of the ascetics.

sn: तत्रैव वसतस्तस्य रावणो नाम राक्षसः॥ जहार भार्यां वैदेहीं सम्मोद्यैनं सहानुजम्।
en: When he was living there, the Rakshasa, by name Ravana stole away his wife, the princess of Videha, having deceived both himself and his follower Lakshmana.

sn: तमागस्कारिणं रामः पौलस्त्यमजितं परैः॥ जघान समरे क्रुद्धः पुरेव त्र्यम्बकोऽन्धकम्।
en: That son of Paulastya invincible by his enemies who had injured him, Rama slew in battle, being excited with rage, like the threeeyed Mahadeva slaying the demon Andhaka.

sn: सुरासुरैरवध्यं तं देवब्राह्मणकण्टकम्॥ जघान स महाबाहुः पौलस्त्यं सगणं रणे।
en: That one (Ravana) incapable of being slain by the celestials and the Asuras, that thorn in the sides of the Gods and Brahmanas, namely that descendant of Paulastya, the mighty-armed Rama slew in battle, with all his followers.

sn: स प्रजानुग्रहं कृत्वा त्रिदशैरभिपूजितः॥
en: In consequence of his showing mercy towards his subjects he used to be honoured by the celestials themselves.

sn: व्याष्य कृत्स्नं जगत् कीर्त्या सुरर्षिगणसेवितः। स प्राप्य विधिवद् राज्यं सर्वभूतानुकम्पकः॥
en: That one (Rama), served even by the Gods and the sages, filled the earth with his fame. Having acquired immeasurable kingdom, he used to treat his subjects with kindness.

sn: आजहार महायज्ञं प्रजा धर्मेण पालयन्। निरर्गलं राजसूयमश्वमेधं च तं विभुः॥
en: Cherishing his subjects virtuously, that lord without any hindrance, accomplished one hundred of that mighty sacrifice Ashvamedha together with the sacrifice called Jaruthya.

sn: आजहार सुरेशस्य हविषा मुदमाहरत्। अन्यैश्च विविधैर्यज्ञैरीजे बहुगुणैर्नृपः॥
en: He created great joy in Indra by pouring libations of clarified butter on the fire. And, O king, he celebrated many other kinds of sacrifice, all productive of great religious merit.

sn: क्षुत्पिपासेऽजयद् रामः सर्वरोगांश्च देहिनाम्। सततं गुणसम्पन्नो दीप्यमानः स्वतेजसा॥
en: Rama conquered hunger and thirst and he was beyond the influence of maladies that trouble the corporeal creation. He was always attended with all kinds of virtues and burnt in his own energy.

sn: अति सर्वाणि भूतानि रामो दाशरथिर्बभौ। ऋषीणां देवतानां च मानुषाणां च सर्वशः॥
en: Indeed Rama, the of Dasaratha surpassed in beauty all other created beings. The Rishis, the celestials and the mortals all together. son

sn: पृथिव्यां सहवासोऽभूद्रामे राज्यं प्रशासति। नाहीयत तदा प्राणः प्राणिनां न तदन्यथा॥
en: Lived on the face of the earth, when Rama ruled over the kingdom. Then the lives of animate beings never terminated untimely.

sn: प्राणोऽपानः समानश्च रामे राज्यं प्रशासति। पर्यदीष्यन्त तेजांसि तदानश्च नाभवन्॥
en: When Rama ruled his dominions, the vital breaths known as Prana and Apana and Samana and others, all duly performed their functions. All splendour appeared to increase and evil portents were never seen.

sn: दीर्घायुषः प्रजाः सर्वा युवा न म्रियते तदा। वेदैश्चतुर्भिः सुप्रीताः प्राप्नुवन्ति दिवौकसः॥
en: All his subjects then enjoyed length of days, men then were not taken away in the prime of their life. The denizens of heaven, highly satisfied, used to obtain, according to the (ordinances of the) four Vedas.

sn: हव्यं कव्यं च विविधं निष्पूर्त हुतमेव च। अदंशमशका देशा नश्टब्यालसरीसृपाः॥
en: Libations of clarified butter and other offerings of edibles presented by men. His dominions were not infested with gnats and flies and they were free from snakes and other reptiles.

sn: नाप्सु प्राणभृतां मृत्यु काले ज्वलनोऽदहत्। अधर्मरुचयो लुब्धा मूर्खा वा नाभवंस्तदा॥
en: Living creatures died not being drowned and prematurely; fire did not consume anything then. Then there were none, of vicious propensities and covetous and ignorant.

sn: शिष्टेष्टयज्ञकर्माणः सर्वे वर्णास्तदाऽभवन्। स्वधां पूजां च रक्षोभिर्जनस्थाने प्रणाशिताम्॥
en: His subjects, belonging to all the four castes, were engaged in the performance of righteous and desirable deeds. The Rakshasas then, used to hinder the adoration of the Pitris in Janasthana.

sn: प्रादान्निहत्य रक्षांसि पितृदेवेभ्य ईश्वरः। सहस्रपुत्राः पुरुषा दशवर्षशतायुषः॥
en: The Lord Rama slaying them, caused the offerings and the adoration to be one more made to the ancestral manes and the gods. Men then became fathers of thousand sons and their duration of life covered a thousand years.

sn: न च ज्येष्ठाः कनिष्ठेभ्यस्तदा श्राद्धान्यकारयन्। श्यामो युवा लोहिताक्षो मत्तमातङ्गविक्रमः॥
en: Then seniors in age had never the misfortunes of performing the obsequies of their juniors. Youthful, of a dark blue complexion, of red eyes, possessing the tread of an infuriate elephant.

sn: आजानुबाहुः सुभुजः सिंहस्कन्धो महाबलः। दशवर्षसहस्राणि दशवर्षशतानि च॥ सर्वभूतमन: कान्तो रामो राज्यमकारयत्। रामो रामो राम इति प्रजानामभवत् कथा॥
en: Having arms hanging down to the knees and of well-shape, of shoulders resembling those of the lion and of great might, that delighter of the hearts of beings, namely Rama, ruled his kingdom for eleven thousand years. His subjects were then always occupied in talking about him.

sn: रामाद् रामं जगदभूद् रामे राज्यं प्रशासति। चतुर्विधाः प्रजा रामः स्वर्गे नीत्वा दिवं गतः॥
en: While Rama ruled his kingdom, the world became most charming and captivating. At last taking his subjects belonging to all the four orders with him, Rama ascended to heaven.

sn: आत्मानं सम्प्रतिष्ठाप्य राजवंशमिहाष्टधा। स चेन्ममार सृञ्जय चतुर्भद्रतरस्त्वया॥
en: Having perpetuated his own, line in eight separate dynasties of kings, When, O Srinjaya, even such a king died who was superior to you in respect of the four cardinal virtues.

sn: पुत्राात् पुण्यतरस्तुभ्यं मा पुत्रमनुतप्यथाः। अयज्वानमदाक्षिण्यमभि श्वैत्येत्युदाहरत्॥
en: Consequently, who was far more superior to your son, you should not lament for your son saying “O Shvaitya" who performed no sacrifice and made no sacrificial presents.

sn: नारद उवाच भगीरथं च राजानं मृतं सृञ्जय शुश्रुम। येन भागीरथी गङ्गा चयनैः काञ्चनैश्चिता॥
en: Narada said () Srinjaya, we also heard that king Bhagiratha, fell a prey to death, Bhagiratha who caused the banks of Ganga-called Bhagirathi after him-to be covered with flights of golden steps.

sn: यः सहस्रं सहस्राणां कन्या हेमविभूषिताः। राज्ञश्च राजपुत्रांश्च ब्राह्मणेभ्यो ह्यमन्यत॥
en: He gave away to Brahmanas, kings and princes, a thousand times thousand damsels, all adorned with ornaments of gold.

sn: सर्वा रथगताः कन्या रथा: सर्वे चतुर्युजः। रथे रथे शतं नागाः सर्वे वै हेममालिनः॥
en: All those damsels were mounted on chariots; and to all the chariots were harnessed four steeds; and again every chariot was attended with a hundred elephants all decked with chains of gold.

sn: सहस्रमश्वाश्चैकैकं गजाना पृष्ठतोऽन्वयुः। अश्वे अश्वे शतं गावो गवां पश्चादजाविकम्॥
en: A thousand horses followed each king and after each horse, came a hundred cows and after the cows came sheep and deer, countless in number.

sn: तेनाक्रान्ता जलौघेन दक्षिणा भूयसीर्ददत्। उपहरेऽतिव्यथिता तस्याङ्के निषसाद ह॥
en: Bhagiratha gave away enormous gifts at his sacrifices in consequence of which, large used to be the concourse of people at them. Afflicted with the heavy burden of men, Ganga saying 'protect me', sat down upon his lap.

sn: तथा भागीरथी गङ्गा उर्वशी चाभवत् पुरा। दुहितृत्वं गता राज्ञः पुत्रत्वमगमत् तदा॥
en: And because in the days of yore Ganga sat on his lap, she, like Urvashi, came to be regarded as his daughter and was named after him. Then having become the kings daughter, she became his son (i.e. she procured, like a son, the salvation of his ancestors).

sn: तां तु गाथां जगुः प्रीता गन्धर्वाः सूर्यवर्चसः। पितृदेवमनुष्याणां शृण्वतां बल्गुवादिनः॥
en: Gandharvas of melodious voice and solar effulgence, greatly pleased, sang this song in the hearing of the anscertral manes, the celestials and the human beings.

sn: भगीरथं यजमानमैक्ष्वाकुं भूरिदक्षिणम्। गङ्गा समुद्रगा देवी वने पितरमीश्वरम्॥
en: Thus, O Srinjaya, that Goddess namely the ocean-going Ganga, chose the Lord Bhagiratha that descendant of Ikshvaku, that performer of sacrifices with profuse gifts, to be her father.

sn: तस्य सेन्द्रैः सुरगणैर्देवैर्यज्ञ: स्वलङ्कृतः। सम्यक्परिगृहीतश्च शान्तविघ्नो निरामयः॥
en: His sacrifices were always honoured by the presence of the celestials with Indra at their head. Removing all obstructions, the Gods used to appropriate their respective shares and to facilitate those sacrifices in every way.

sn: यो य इच्छेत विप्रो वै यत्र यत्रात्मनः प्रियम्। भगीरथस्तदा प्रीतस्तत्र तत्राददद् वशी॥
en: That self-controlled king Bhagiratha highly pleased used to give to the Brahmanas all their objects of desire and all things that any one of the Brahmanas used to set his hcart upon.

sn: नादेयं ब्राह्मणस्यासीद् यस्य यत्स्यात् प्रियं धनम्। सोऽपि विप्रप्रसादेन ब्रह्मलोकं गतो नृपः॥
en: He had nothing that he would have hesitated to give to the Brahmanas. Every one obtained from him everything he wanted; that king also, through the grace of the Brahmanas, ascended to regions of Brahma.

sn: येन यातौ मखमुखौ दिशाशाविह पादपाः। तेनावस्थातुमिच्छन्ति तं गत्वा राजमीश्वरम्॥
en: For the self-same object for which the sages living on the rays of the sun, used to dance attendance upon the Sun, for that very object they used to wait upon the Lord Bhagiratha, that ornament of the three worlds.

sn: स चेन्ममार सृञ्जय चतुर्भद्रतरस्त्वया। पुत्रात् पुण्यतरस्तुभ्यं मा पुत्रामनुतप्यथा:॥ अयज्वानमदाक्षिण्यमभि श्वैत्येत्युदाहरत्।
en: When, O Srinjaya, even such a king had to suffer death, who was superior to you in respect of the four cardinal virtues and consequently far superior to your son you should not lament for your son saying, 'Oh Shvaitya’-who did not perform any sacrifice or make any sacrificial gift.

sn: नारद उवाच दिलीपं चेदैलविलं मृतं सृञ्जय शुश्रुम। यस्य यज्ञशतेष्वासन् प्रयुतायुतशो द्विजाः। तन्त्रज्ञानार्थसम्पन्ना यज्वानः पुत्रपौत्रिणः॥
en: Narada said We also heard, O Srinjaya, that Dilipa the son of Ilavala had to suffer death. In the celebration of his hundred sacrifices were present countless number of the twice-born ones acquainted with the knowledge of the reality about things, devoted to the performance of sacrifices and blessed with sons and grandsons.

sn: य इमां वसुसम्पूर्णो वसुधां वसुधाधिपः। ईजानो वितते यज्ञे ब्राह्मणेभ्यो ह्यमन्यत॥
en: That king of the earth, celebrating various sacrifices, offered this earth replete with treasures, to the Brahmanas as a gift.

sn: दिलीपस्य तु यज्ञेषु कृतः पन्था हिरण्मयः। तं धर्म इव कुर्वाणा: सेन्द्रा देवाः समागमन्॥
en: At all the sacrifices of king Dilipa, the roads used to be constructed of gold. Regarding him equal to Dharma himself, the very Gods and Indra at their head, used to come to him.

sn: सहस्रं यत्र मातङ्गा गच्छन्ति पर्वतोपमाः। सौवर्णं चाभवत् सर्वं सदः परमभास्वरम्॥
en: were here wandering many great clephants like a various hills. The upper and lower rings in his sacrificial stakes were made of gold.

sn: रसानां चाभवन् कुल्या भक्ष्याणां चापि पर्वताः। सहस्रव्यामा नृपते यूपाश्चासन् हिरण्मयाः॥
en: Canals of essence used to flow there and piles of cereal (food-grains) was so collected as that of mountains. Oking! One thousand pandalas (pavilions) made of gold extended each to a vyama were erected with grandeur in the offerings (yajna) arranged by them.

sn: चषालं प्रचषालं च यस्य यूपे हिरण्मये। नृत्यन्तेऽप्सरसस्तस्य षट् सहस्राणि सप्त च॥ यत्र वीणां वादयति प्रीत्या विश्वावसुः स्वयम्। सर्वभूतान्यमन्यन्त राजानं सत्यशीलिनम्॥ रागखाण्डवभोज्यैश्च मत्ताः पतिषु शेरते। तदेतदद्भुतं मन्ये अन्यैर्न सदृशं नृपैः॥ यदप्सु युध्यमानस्य चक्रे न परिपेततुः।
