en: Partaking of his Raga-khandavas, many people at his sacrifices used to lie down on the high-ways. He following thing seemed exceedingly wonderful and never occurred to any other king, viz., that when Dilipa fought on waters, his car-wheels never sank below the surface.

sn: राजानं दृढधन्वानं दिलीपं सत्यवादिनम्॥ येऽपश्यन् भूरिदाक्षिण्यं तेऽपि स्वर्गजितो नराः।
en: Those who saw king Dilipa, that steady bowmen, always truthful and giving away profuse gifts at his sacrifices, succeeded in attaining paradise.

sn: पञ्च शब्दा न जीर्यन्ति खट्वाङ्गस्य स्वाध्यायघोषो ज्याघोषः पिबताश्रीत खादत।
en: In the mansion of Dilipa otherwise called Khattvanga, the following five sorts of sounds were always to be heard, namely, the sound of the recital of the Vedas, the twang of the bow and the sound produced by utterance of the words, 'Drink, Enjoy and Eat.'

sn: निवेशने॥ स चेन्ममार सृञ्जय चतुर्भद्रतरस्त्वया॥ पुत्रात् पुण्यतरस्तुभ्यं मा पुत्रमनुतप्यथाः। अयज्वानमदाक्षिण्यमभि श्वत्येत्युदाहरत्॥
en: When even such a king, O Srinjaya, died, who was superior to you in respect of the four cardinal virtues and consequently far superior to your son, you should not lament for your son saying-'O Shvaitya’, who did perform no sacrifice and make no sacrificial presents.

sn: स चेन्ममार सृञ्जय चतुर्भद्रतरस्त्वया॥ पुत्रात् पुण्यतरस्तुभ्यं मा पुत्रमनुतप्यथाः। अयज्वानमदाक्षिण्यमभि श्वत्येत्युदाहरत्॥
en: When even such a king, O Srinjaya, died, who was superior to you in respect of the four cardinal virtues and consequently far superior to your son, you should not lament for your son saying-'O Shvaitya’, who did perform no sacrifice and make no sacrificial presents.

sn: नारद उवाच मान्धाता चेद्यौवनाश्वो मृतः सृञ्जय शुश्रुम। देवासुरमनुष्याणां त्रैलोक्यविजयी नृपः॥
en: Narada said O Srinjaya, we also heard that Yuvanasva's son, king Mandhata, who vanquished the celestials, the Asuras and the gods and the worlds, had to undergo death.

sn: यं देवावश्विनौ गर्भात् पितुः पूर्वे चकर्षतुः। मृगयां विचरन् राजा तृषितः क्लान्तवाहनः॥
en: The twin Asvinas, (the celestial physicians) drew him out of his fathers womb. Once on a time when out hunting, king Yuvanasva became thirsty and his steed became exhausted.

sn: धूमं दृष्ट्वागमत् सत्रं पृषदाज्यमवाप सः। तं दृष्ट्वा युवनाश्वस्य जठरे सूनुतां गतम्॥
en: Seeing at a distance, a curl of smoke, the monarch (guided by it) reached a sacrificial compound and he drank the sacrificial butter that lay scattered there. (Thereupon the monarch conceived). Then seeing the king quick with child.

sn: गर्भाद्धि जहतुर्देवावश्विनौ भिषजां वरी। तं दृष्ट्वा पितुरुत्सङ्गे शयानं देववर्चसम्॥
en: The two foremost of celestials physicians, the twin Asvins drew out the child from the kings womb. Then beholding the new-born babe of divine radiance lie on the lap of his father. one

sn: अन्योन्यमब्रुवन् देवाः कमयं धास्यतीति वै। मामेवायं धयत्वग्रे इति ह स्माह वासवः॥
en: The gods spoke to another saying-'Whom shall this child suck.' Then Vasava said-"Let this child suck, my finger first.'

sn: ततोऽगुलिभ्यो हीन्द्रस्य प्रादुरासीत् पयोऽमृतम्। मां धास्यतीति कारुण्याद् यदिन्द्रो ह्यन्वकम्पयत्॥
en: Thereupon from the fingers of Indra nectareous milk flowed out. Because Indra had, out of compassion for the child, said “Let him suck me.'

sn: तस्मात्तु मान्धातेत्येवं नाम तस्याद्भुतं कृतम्। ततस्तु धारां पयसो धृतस्य च महात्मनः॥ तस्यास्ये यौवनाश्वस्य पाणिरिन्द्रस्य चास्रवत्। अपिबत् पाणिमिन्द्रस्य स चाप्यहाभ्यवर्धत॥
en: Therefore the celestials designated him as Mandhatri. Then streams of milk and clarified butter flowed into the mouth of Yuvanasva's son from the finger of the high-souled Indra. He then drank the nectar flowing from Indra's hand and thus went on growing.

sn: सोऽभवद् द्वादशसमो द्वादशाहेन वीर्यवान्। इमं च पृथिवीं कृत्स्नामेकाहा स व्यजीजयत्॥
en: In twelve days he became twelve cubits in stature and was also endued with great prowess. And he conquered this extensive earth in the course of a single day.

sn: धर्मात्मा धृतिमान् वीरः सत्यसंधो जितेन्द्रियः। जनमेजयं सुधन्वानं गयं पूरुं बृहद्रथम्॥ असितं च नृगं चैव मान्धाता मनुजोऽजयत्।
en: Of righteous soul, endued with great intelligence and heroic and devoted to truth and of controlled passions, Mandhatri conquered, through the force of his bow, Janarmejaya, Sudhanva, Gaya, Puru, Brihadratha, Asita and king Nriga.

sn: उदेति च यतः सूर्यो यत्र च प्रतितिष्ठति॥ तत् सर्वं योवनाश्वस्य मान्धातुः क्षेत्रमुच्यते।
en: The hill where the sun rises and the hill where it sets, all the land lying between these two hills, is called the dominion of the king Mandhatri, the son of Yuvanasva.

sn: सोऽश्वमेधशतैरिष्ट्वा राजसूयशतेन च॥ अददद् रोहितान् मत्स्यान् ब्राह्मणेभ्यो विशाम्पते। हैरण्यान् यो जनोत्सेधानायताञ्शतयोजनम्॥
en: Having accomplished a hundred horsesacrifices and a hundred Rajasuya sacrifices also. He gave away to the Brahmanas, O ruler of men, some Rohita fish made of gold that were ten yojanas in length and one yojana in breadth.

sn: बहुप्रकारान् सुस्वादून् भक्ष्यभोज्यान्नपर्वतान्। अतिरिक्तं ब्राह्मणेभ्यो भुञ्जानो हीयते जनः॥
en: Piles of delicate and tasteful foods and edibles, after the Brahmanas had been entertained, were partaken of by other people and greatly enhanced their joy.

sn: भक्ष्यान्नपाननिचयाः शुशुभुस्त्वन्नपर्वताः। घृतह्रदाः सूपकूपाः दधिफेना गुडोदकाः॥ रुरुधुः पर्वतान् नद्यो मधुक्षीरवहाः शुभाः।
en: Enormous quantities of food, viands edibles and drinks and potion and piles of cooked rice were there and shone beautiful. Many rivers, having lakes of clarified butter, with various kinds of soup for their mud, curds for their forth and honey for their water, looking charming and flowing in currents of milk and honey, wended round the mountains of solid edibles.

sn: देवासुरा नरा यक्षा गन्धर्वोरगपक्षिणः॥ विप्रास्तत्रागताश्चासन् वेदवेदाङ्गपारगाः। ब्राह्मणा ऋषयश्चापि नासंस्तत्राविपश्चितः॥
en: Gods, Asuras, men, Jakshas, Gandharvas, snakes, birds and many Vipras, learned in the Vedas and their auxiliaries, came at this sacrifices. Among the Brahmanas and the sages who came there, there was none who was not learned.

sn: समुद्रान्तां वसुमती वसुपूर्णां तु सर्वतः। स तां ब्राह्मणसात्कृत्वा जगामास्तं तदा नृपः॥
en: King Mandhatri having given away as gift the earth bounded by the ocean and replete with all sorts of wealth, to the Brahmanas, at last set like the sun itself.

sn: गतः पुण्यकृतां लोकान् व्याप्य स्वयशसा दिशः। स चेन्ममार सृञ्जय चतुर्भद्रतरस्त्वया॥ पुत्रात् पुण्यतरस्तुभ्यं मा पुत्रमनुतप्यथाः। अयज्वानमदाक्षिण्यमभि श्वैत्येत्युदाहरत्॥
en: Then having filled the quarters with his fame, he repaired to the regions of righteous. Even when such a king, O Srinjaya, died, who was superior to you in all the four cardinal qualities and consequently much more superior to your son-you should not lament for your son saying-'Oh Shvaitya'-who performed no sacrifice and made no sacrificial gifts.

sn: नारद उवाच ययातिं नाहुषं चैव मृतं सृञ्जय शुश्रुम। राजसूयशतैरिष्ट्वा सोऽश्वमेधशतेन च॥ पुण्डरीकसहस्रेण वाजपेयशतैस्तथा। अतिरात्रसहस्रेण चातुर्मास्यैश्च कामतः। अग्निष्टोमैश्च विविधैः सत्रैश्च प्राज्यदक्षिणैः॥
en: Narada said O Srinjaya, we heard also that Yayati, the son of Nahusa, was carried away by Death. Having celebrated a hundred Rajasuya sacrifices, a hundred Horse-sacrifices, thousand Pundarikas, a hundred Vajapeya sacrifices, a thousand Atiratra sacrifices, numerous Chaturmasya sacrifices. Many Agnistomas and diverse other kind of sacrifices, all attended with the giving away of profuse Dakshinas.

sn: अब्राह्मणानां यद वित्तं पृथिव्यामस्ति किंचन। तत् सर्वे परिसंख्याय ततो ब्राह्मणसात्करोत्॥
en: He gave unto the Brahmanas all the wealth on the face of Earth, belonging to the nonBrahmana sect, having at first taken an account of them all.

sn: सरस्वती पुण्यतमा नदीनां तथा समुद्राः सरितः साद्रयश्च। इजानाय पुण्यतमाय राज्ञे घृतं पयो दुदुहु हुषाय॥
en: The holiest river Sarasvati, oceans, mountains and rivulets offered ghee and milk for offering arranged by the religious soul, king Yayati.

sn: व्यूढे देवासुरे युद्धे कृत्वा देवसहायताम्। चतुर्धाव्यभजत् सर्वां चतुर्थ्यः पृथिवीमिमाम्॥ यज्ञैर्नानाविधेरिष्ट्वा प्रजामुत्पाद्य चोत्तमाम्। देवयान्यां चौशनस्यां शर्मिष्ठायां च धर्मतः॥ देवारण्येषु सर्वेषु विजहारामरोपमः। आत्मनः कामचारेण द्वितीय इव वासवः।॥
en: He assisted the celestials when they and the Asuras stood ready for fight arraying themselves in battle order. He divided the earth in four parts and gave her away to four persons. Having celebrated diverse sacrifices and virtuously begotten excellent progeny on his wives, viz., Devayani, the daughter of Ushanas and Sharmistha, thai god-like Yayati roamed in the woods of the celestials, at his own unrestrained pleasure, like a second Vasava (or Indra).

sn: यदा नाभ्यगमच्छान्तिं कामानां सर्ववेदवित्। ततो गाथामिमां गीत्वा सदारः प्राविशद् वनम्॥
en: Versed in all the Vedas, when he found that he was not satiated with the indulgence of his desires, he repaired to the forest with his wives, having uttered this saying-

sn: यत् पृथिव्यां व्रीहियवं हिरण्यं पशवः स्त्रियः। नालमेकस्य तत् सर्वमिति मत्वा शमं व्रजेत्॥
en: "Whatever of paddy, wheat, gold, animals and women there are on the face of the earth, are not sufficient for even one single man. Knowing such to be the fact, one should betake to contentment."

sn: एवं कामान् परित्यज्य ययातिकृतिमेत्य च। पूरूं राज्ये प्रतिष्ठाप्य प्रयातो वनमीश्वरः॥
en: Thus having renounced all his desires and cultivating contentment, the Lord Yayati retired into the woods, having installed his son Puru on the throne.

sn: स चेन्ममार सृञ्जय चतुर्भद्रतरस्त्वया। पुत्रात् पुण्यतरस्तुभ्यं मा पुत्रमनुतप्यथाः। अयज्वानमदाक्षिण्यमभि श्वैत्येत्युदाहरत्॥
en: O Srinjaya, when even such a king had to suffer death, who was superior to you in respect of the four cardinal virtues and was consequently much more superior to your son, you should not lament for your son-crying-'O Shvaitya'-who did not perform any sacrifice or offer any sacrificial presents.

sn: नारद उवाच नाभागमम्बरीषं च मृतं सृञ्जय शुश्रुम यः सहस्रं सहस्राणां राज्ञां चैकस्त्वयोधयत्॥
en: Narada said O Srinjaya, we heard that Nabhaga's son Ambarisha, who, single-handed, fought a thousand times against thousand kings, was also carried away by Death.

sn: जिगीषमाणाः संग्रामे समन्ताद् वैरिणोऽभ्ययुः। अस्त्रयुद्धविदो घोराः सृजन्तश्चाशिवा गिरः॥
en: He simultaneously attacked his enemies who desired to obtain victory over him, who were accomplished in fighting with weapons and who had assaulted him with fierce yells.

sn: बललाघवशिक्षाभिस्तेषां सोऽस्त्रबलेन च। छत्रायुधध्वजरथांश्छित्त्वा प्रासान् गतव्यथः॥
en: Subduing them with his prowess and by the strength of his weapons, he cut-off their umbrellas, weapons, standards and chariots and deprived them of their lives. Thus he relieved himself of all his anxieties.

sn: त एनं मुक्तसंनाहाः प्रार्थयन् जीवितैषिणः। शरण्यमीयुः शरणं तवास्म इति वादिनः॥
en: Then desirous of saving their lives, those defeated king, putting off their coats of mail implored the mercy of that compassionate monarch and sought his protection saying, “We surrender ourselves."

sn: स तु तान् वशगान् कृत्वा जित्वा चेमां वसुन्धराम्। ईजे यज्ञशतैरिष्टैर्यथाशास्त्रं तथाऽनध॥
en: Thus having brought them under his control and having conquered this world, he celebrated a hundred desirable sacrifices, in accordance with the ordinances of the Shastras, O sinless one.

sn: बुभुजुः सर्वसम्पन्नमन्नमन्ये जनाः सदा। तस्मिन् यज्ञे तु विप्रेन्द्राः संतृप्ताः परमार्चिताः॥
en: At those sacrifices of his, people partook of edibles possessed of all delicate qualities. Therefore most of the Brahmanas were greatly gratified and were most excellently worshipped.

sn: मोदकान् पूरिकापूपान् स्वादुपूर्णाश्च शष्कुलीः। करम्भान् पृथुमृद्वीका अन्नानि सुकृतानि च॥ सूपान् मैरेयकापूपान् रागखाण्डवपानकान्। मृष्टान्नानि सुयुक्तानि मृदूनि सुरभीणि च॥ घृतं मधु पयस्तोयं दधीनि रसवन्ति च। फलं मूलं च सुस्वादु द्विजास्तत्रोपभुञ्जते॥
en: Sweetmeat, Purikas, Pupas, Saskulis of excellent taste and large size, Karambhas, Prithumridikas and various kinds of wellprepared edibles, various sorts of Supas, Maireyas, Pupas, Ragakhandavas and diverse king of confectionery, well-dressed, delicate and savoury and clarified butter and honey and milk and water and tasteful curds and fruits and esculent roots-these things were there eaten by the regenerate castes.

sn: मादनीयानि पापानि विदित्वा चात्मनः सुखम्। अपिबन्त यथाकामं पानया गीतवादितैः॥
en: And men who were addicted to drink wines, drank, in proper time, various kinds of intoxicating drinks, for the sake of the pleasures they produced and then sang and played upon their musical instruments.

sn: तत्र स्म गाथा गायन्ति क्षीबा हृष्टाः पठन्ति च। नाभागस्तुतिसंयुक्ता ननृतुश्च सहस्रशः॥
en: Some perfectly toxicated sang songs and were greatly delighted; and some reeled on the ground; some applauded the son of Nabhaga in panegyrics and some danced in thousands.

sn: तेषु यज्ञेष्वम्बरीषो दक्षिणामत्यकालयत्। राज्ञां शतसहस्राणि दश प्रयुतयाजिनाम्॥
en: In those sacrifices, Ambarisha gave as gifts the kingdoms of hundreds and thousands of kings to the ten million priests engaged in his sacrifice.

sn: हिरण्यकवचान् सर्वाश्वेतच्छत्रप्रकीर्णकान्। हिरण्यस्यन्दनारूढान् सानुयात्रपरिच्छदान्॥ ईजानो वितते यज्ञे दक्षिणामत्यकालयत्। मूर्धाभिषिक्तांश्च नृपान् राजपुत्रशतानि च॥ सदण्डकोशनिचयान् ब्राह्मणेभ्यो ह्ममन्यत। नैवं पूर्वे जनाचकुर्न करिष्यन्ति चापरे॥
en: Having celebrated diverse sacrifices the king gave unto the Brahmanas as sacrificial presents numerous princes and kings whose coronal locks had been purified by the sacred bath, all furnished with golden armours, all having white umbrellas held over their heads, all mounted on golden chariots, vested in superb garments and having large retinues and all bearing their scepters and possessing their treasuries. 'None amongst the men of olden times did, nor those to come will do.'

sn: यदम्बरीषो नृपतिः करोत्यमितदक्षिणः। इत्येवमनुमोदन्ते प्रीता यस्य महर्षयः॥
en: What king Ambarisha, profuse in his sacrificial present's has done. Even thus did the mighty sages, gratified with him, applauded him.

sn: स चेन्ममार सृञ्जय चतुर्भद्रतरस्त्वया। पुत्रात् पुण्यतरस्तुभ्यं मा पुत्रमनुतप्यथाः। अयजवानमदाक्षिण्यमभि श्वैत्येत्युदाहरत्॥
en: O Srinjaya, when even such a king who was superior in respect of the four cardinal virtues to you and consequently to your son, had to undergo death, you should not lament for your son who performed no sacrifices and made no sacrificial gifts, saying, 'O Shvaitya.'

sn: नारद उवाच ते शशबिन्दुं च राजानं मृतं सृञ्जय शुश्रुमा ईजे स विविधैर्यज्ञैः श्रीमान् सत्यपराक्रमः॥
en: Narada said We also heard, O Srinjaya, that king Shashabindu, who was of great personal beauty and of prowess incapable of being repulsed and who performed numerous and diverse sacrifices, had to undergo death.

sn: तस्य भार्यासहस्राणां शतमासीन्सहात्मनः। एकैकस्यां च भार्यायां सहस्रं तनयाऽभवन्॥
en: That one of illustrious soul had a hundred thousand wives, and each of these wives was blessed with a thousand sons.

sn: कुमाराः पराक्रान्ताः सर्वे नियुतयाजिनः। राजानः क्रतुभिर्मुख्यैरीजाना वेदपारगाः॥
en: All those princes were endowed with prowess; all of them performed ten millions of sacrifices each. Learned in the sacred scriptures, those royal heroes accomplished many excellent sacrifices.

sn: हिरण्यकवचाः सर्वे सर्वे चोत्तमधन्विनः। सर्वेऽश्वमेधैरीजाना: कुमारा: शशबिन्दवः॥
en: All of them, (on occasions of battle) used to don golden coats of mail; and all were excellent bowmen. All those of Shashabindu accomplished the Horse-sacrifice.

sn: तानश्वमेधे राजेन्द्रो ब्राह्मणेभ्योऽददत् पिता। शतं शतं रथगजा एकैकं पृष्ठतोऽन्वयुः॥
en: That foremost of kings, their father gave them away to the Brahmanas as sacrificial peasants, at his own sacrifice. Each of those princes was followed by hundreds upon hundreds of car-warriors and elephants.

sn: राजपुत्रं तदा कन्यास्तपनीयस्वलंकृताः। कन्यां कन्यां शतं नागा नागे नागे शतं रथाः॥
en: And beautiful dansels adorned with ornaments of gold. With each damsel were a sons hundred elephants and with each elephant a hundred chariots.

sn: रथे रथे शतं चाश्वा बलिनो हेममालिनः। अश्वे अश्वे गोसहस्रं गवां पञ्चाशदाविकाः॥
en: With each car were a hundred horses adorned with chains of gold and with each horse a thousand cows. With each cow were fifty goats.

sn: एतद् धनमपर्याप्तमश्वमेधे महामखे। शशबिन्दुमहाभागो ब्राह्मणेभ्यो ह्यमन्यत॥
en: This uncountable wealth was gifted by the prosperous and respected king Sasabindu to Brahmins in the great offering Ashvamedha arranged once by him.

sn: वाश्चि यूपा यावन्त अश्वमेधे महामखे। ते तथैव पुनश्चान्ते तावन्तः काञ्चनाऽभवन्॥
en: In that great Horse-sacrifice of his, he gave away unlimited wealth and in other sacrifices also he gave away equal amount of gold.

sn: भक्ष्यानपाननिचयाः पर्वताः क्रोशमुच्छ्रिताः। तस्याश्वमेधे निर्वृत्ते राज्ञः शिष्टास्त्रयोदश॥
en: There were piles of edibles, foods and confectionery of the height of two full miles. And when the Horse-sacrifices of the king was over thirteen such piles remained (un-used).

sn: तुष्टपुष्टजनाकीर्णा शान्तविघ्नामनामयाम्। शशबिन्दुरिमां भूमिं चिरं भुक्त्वा दिवं गतः॥
en: Having ruled for many years over his kingdom, where the people were well-fed, satisfied and free from diseases and where all kinds of evils rooted out, king Shashabindu ascended to heaven.

sn: स चेन्ममार सृञ्जय चतुर्भद्रतरस्त्वया। पुत्रात् पुण्यतरस्तुभ्यं मा पुत्रमनुतप्यथाः। अयज्वानमदाक्षिण्यमभि श्वैत्येत्युदाहरत्॥
en: O Srinjaya, when even such a sovereign, who was superior in respect of the four cardinal virtues to you and consequently to your son, had to suffer death you should not lament of your son who performed no sacrifices and made no sacrificial gifts, saying 'O Shvaitya'. were

sn: । नारद उवाच गयं चामूर्तरयसं मृतं सृञ्जय शुश्रुम। यो वै वर्षशतं राजा हुतशिष्टाशनोऽभवत्॥
en: Narada said O Srinjaya, we also heard of the death of king Gaya, the son of Amurtarajas, who for hundred years lived only upon remnants of the libations offered on fire.

sn: तस्मै ह्यग्निर्वरं प्रदात् ततो ववे वरं गयः। तपसा ब्रह्मचर्येण व्रतेन नियमेन च॥ गुरूणां च प्रसादेन वेदानिच्छामि वेदितुम्। स्वधर्मेणाविहिंस्यान्यान् धनमिच्छामि चाक्षयम्॥
en: Thereat Agni offered to bestow boon on him; and thereupon Gaya asked for this boon saying, "I desire to acquaint myself with the contents of the Vedas, through ascetic penances, observance of Brahmacharya rites, vows and rules and also through the grace of my preceptors. I also desire to acquire inexhaustible wealth without transgressing the duties of the order which I belong to and without any injury to any one else.

sn: विप्रेषु ददतश्चैव श्रद्धा भवतु नित्यशः। अनन्यासु सवर्णासु पुत्रजन्म च मे भवेत्॥
en: I desire also the boon, that everyday I may give away devoutly my wealth to the Brahmanas. I wish also to beget sons upon females of my own order and not upon others.

sn: अन्नं मे ददतः श्रद्धा धर्मे मे रमतां मनः। अविनं चास्तु मे नित्यं धर्मकार्येषु पावक॥
en: Let devotion be the ruling feeling of my heart when I shall give away edibles; let also my mind delight in the fountain of righteousness. Let, O Agni, no difficulty overtake me when I engage myself in the performance of pious deeds."

sn: तथा भविष्यतीत्युक्त्वा तत्रैवान्तरधीयत। गयो ह्यवाप्य तत् सर्वे धर्मेणारीनजीजयत्॥
en: "It shall be so", saying this, the God of Fire, disappeared even there. Then Gaya realising all those boons sought, began to obtain righteous victories over all his enemies.

sn: स दर्शपौर्णमासाभ्यां कालेष्वाग्रयणेन च। चातुर्मास्यैश्च विविधैर्यज्ञैश्चावाप्तदक्षिणैः॥
en: Then king Gaya celebrated for a full hundred years, various kinds of sacrifices with profuse Dakshinas, as also many other vows as Chaturmasya.

sn: अयजच्छ्रद्धया राजा परिसंवत्सरान् शतम्। गवां शतसहस्राणि शतमश्वशतानि च॥
en: Every year, in a century, the king gave unto the Brahmanas, with due devotion, hundred thousand kine, ten thousand horses.

sn: शतं निष्कसहस्राणि गवां चाप्ययुतानि षट्। उत्थायोत्थाय स प्रादात् परिसंवत्सरान् शतम्॥
en: And for several successive centuries he gave to the Brahmanas hundred thousand Nishkas and sixty-thousand kine, at the time of his rising.

sn: नक्षत्रेषु च सर्वेषु ददनक्षत्रदक्षिणा:। ईजे च विविधैर्यज्ञैर्यथा सोमोऽङ्गिरा यथा॥
en: Under every (auspicious) conjunction of the constellations, he gave away presents specified for those occasions. Verily the monarch performed various sacrifices like another Soma or another Angirasa.

sn: सौवर्णां पृथिवीं कृत्वा य इमां मणिशर्कराम्। विप्रेभ्यः प्राददद् राजा सोऽश्वमेधे महामखे॥
en: Making the earth covered with gold and with pebbles constituted by gems, he gave her away as a present to the Brahmanas during the celebration of his great Horse-sacrifice.

sn: जाम्बूनदमया यूपाः सर्वे रत्नपरिच्छदाः। गयस्यासन् समृद्धास्तु सर्वभूतमनोहराः॥
en: In the sacrifices of Gaya, the stakes were made of gold; and embossed with jewels and precious, they delighted the hearts of all.

sn: सर्वकामसमृद्धं च प्रादादनं गयस्तदा। ब्राह्मणेभ्यः प्रहृष्टेभ्यः सर्वभूतेभ्य एव च॥
en: Then Gaya gave to the delighted Brahmanas and other creatures, those stakes and many other precious objects of desire.

sn: स समुद्रवनद्वीपनदीनदवनेषु च। नगरेषु च राष्ट्रषु दिवि व्योम्नि च येऽवसन्॥ भूतग्रामाश्च विविधाः संतृप्ता यज्ञसम्पदा। गयस्य सदृशो यज्ञो नास्त्यन्य इतितेऽब्रुवन्॥
en: The various species of creatures inhabiting the oceans, the islands, the rivers male and female, the woods, forests, towns, kingdoms, the paradise and the sky and diverse other beings were gratified with the wealth and riches distributed at Gaya's sacrifice. They then said, "There was no sacrifice like that celebrated by Gaya."

sn: षट्त्रिंशद् योजनायामा त्रिंशद् योजनमायता। पश्चात् पुस्चतुर्विशद् वेदी ह्यासीद्धिरण्मयी॥ गयस्य यजमानस्य मुक्तावज्रमणिस्तृता। प्रादात् स ब्राह्मणेभ्योऽथ वासांस्याभरणानि च॥
en: The sacrificial altar of Gaya was thirty yojanas long, twenty-six yojanas high; and it was covered with gold and strewn over with pearls and gems. He gave away this altar and inany garments and ornaments to the Brahmanas.

sn: यथोक्ता दक्षिणाश्चान्या विप्रेभ्यो भूरिदक्षिणः। यत्र भोजनशिष्टस्य पर्वताः पञ्जविंशतिः॥
en: That liberal-handed monarch gave to the Brahmanas other presents specified in the scriptures. When the sacrifice was completed, their remained twenty-five mountains of edibles and foods, (untouched).

sn: कुल्याः कुशलवाहिन्यो रसानामभवंस्तदा। वस्त्राभरणगन्धानां राशयश्च पृथग्विधाः॥
en: And there also remained many lakes of potions and several stream of juicy drinks flowing charmingly and many garments and rnaments, perfumes and many princes (who were intended to be given away as presents).

sn: यस्य प्रभावाच्च गयस्त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतः। वटचाक्षय्यकरणः पुण्यं ब्रह्मसरश्च तत्॥
en: Through that great sacrifice of his, Gaya became well-known in the three worlds; and the eternal Banian tree and the holy Brahmalake, owe their origin to that sacrifice.

sn: स चेन्ममार सृञ्जय चतुर्भद्रतरस्त्वया। पुत्रात् पुण्यतरस्तुभ्यं मा पुत्रमनुतप्यथाः। अयज्वानमदाक्षिण्यमभि श्वैत्येत्युदाहरत्॥
en: O Srinjaya, when even such a king, who was far superior in respect of the four cardinal virtues to you and consequently to your son, had to undergo death, you should not lament for your son who performed no sacrifice and made no sacrificial gifts-saying 'O Shvaitya.'

sn: नारद उवाच सांकृति रन्तिदेवं च मृतं सृञ्जय शुश्रुम। यस्य द्विशतसाहस्रा आसन् सूदा महात्मनः॥
en: Narada said O Srinjaya, we heard also that Sankriti's son Rantideva, who had two hundred-thousand cooks of high-soul, had to undergo death.

sn: गृहानभ्यागतान् विप्रानतिथीन् परिवेषकाः। पक्वापक्वं दिवारानं वरान्नममृतोपमम्॥
en: These cooks of his, used to distribute raw and cooked food and vast amount of wealth, day and night, to the Brahmanas that repaired to Ratindeva's mansion as guests.

sn: न्यायेनाधिगतं वित्तं ब्राह्मणेभ्यो ह्यमन्यत। वेदानधीत्य धर्मेण यश्चके द्विषतो वशे॥
en: He gave away unto the Brahmanas his wealth acquired through fair means. Having studied the Vedas he subdued his foes in fair combats.

sn: ब्राह्मणेभ्योददनिष्कान् सौवर्णान् स प्रभावतः। तुभ्यं निष्कं तुभ्यं निष्कमिति ह स्म प्रभाषते॥
en: He always gave away golden Nishkas to the Brahmanas saying. "I give you Nishkas, I give you Nishkas."

sn: तुभ्यंतुभ्यमिति प्रदानिष्कान् निष्कान् सहस्रशः। ततः पुनः समाश्वास्य निष्कानेव प्रयच्छति॥
en: "To you, to you,” saying these words he gave thousands of Nishkas away to the Brahmanas. Then again, comforting them, he gave them Nishkas.

sn: अल्पं दत्तं मयाद्येति निष्ककोटि सहस्रशः। एकाला दास्यति पुनः कोऽन्यस्तत् सम्प्रदास्यति॥
en: Having given away in the course of a single day, a Koti of Nishkas, he used to say, “I have his day given away a very small number of coins", thus thinking, he would again give away Nishkas. What other person can give away such enormous quantity of wealth?

sn: द्विजपाणिवियोगेन दुःखं मे शाश्वतं महत्। भविष्यति न संदेह एवं राजाददद् वसु॥
en: That king used to give away wealth, thinking-"If I do not give wealth into the hands of the Brahmanas, great and everlasting sorrow will surely fall in my share."

sn: सहस्रशश्च सौवर्णान् वृषभान् गोशतानुगान्। साष्टं शतं सुवर्णानां निष्कमाहुर्धनं तथा॥ अध्यर्धमासमददद् ब्राह्मणेभ्यः शतं समाः। अग्निहोत्रोपकरणं यज्ञोपकरणं च यत्॥
en: For a hundred years, twice a month, he gave away unto thousands of Brahmanas a golden bull each followed by a herd of hundred cows and eight hundred pieces of Nishkas. All the articles necessary for his Agnihotra sacrifice and for his other sacrifices.

sn: ऋषिभ्यः करकान् कुम्भान् स्थालीः पिठरमेव च। शयनासनयानानि प्रासादांश्च गृहाणि च॥ वृक्षांश्च विविधान् दद्यादन्नानि च धनानि च। सर्वे सौवर्णमेवासीद् रन्तिदेवस्य धीमतः॥
en: He gave away to the sages, including karakas and jars for water and plates and dishes and beds, carpets, conveyances, palaces and dwelling houses. And various sorts of trees and diverse kinds of edibles and viands. All the utensils and articles of the intelligent Ratindeva were made of gold.

sn: तत्रास्य गाथा गायन्ति ये पुराणविदो जनाः। रन्तिदेवस्य तां दृष्ट्वा समृद्धिमतिमानुषीम्॥
en: Seeing then the super-human prosperity of king Ratindeva, those that were conversant with the history of past ages sang this song.

sn: नैतादृशं दृष्टपूर्वे कुबेरसदनेष्वपि। धनं च पूर्यमाणं नः किं पुनर्मनुजेष्विति॥
en: We have not seen such vast treasures even in the mansion of Kubera (the Plutus of Hindu mythology), what to speak of the treasures of men?

sn: व्यक्तं वस्वोकसारेयमित्यूचुस्तत्र विस्मिताः।
en: People then wonderingly used to say-"It is evident that the kingdom of Ratindeva, the son of Sankrita, is made of gold.

sn: सांकृते रन्तिदेवस्य यां रात्रिमतिथिर्वसेत्॥ आलभ्यन्त तदा गावः सहस्राण्येकविंशतिः।
en: On such nights when guests used to assemble in the mansion of Ratindeva, twentyone thousand cows used to be sacrificed (for feeding them).

sn: तत्र स्म सूदाः क्रोशन्ति सुपृष्टमणिकुण्डलाः॥ सूपं भूविहमश्नीध्वं नाद्य मासं यथा पुरा।
en: And the cooks of the king, adorned with jewelled ear-rings used to cry out (to the guests) saying-“Drink as much soup as you can, for there is not so much meat today as there was the other day."

sn: रन्तिदेवस्य यत् किंचित् सौवर्णमभवत् तदा॥ तत् सर्वे वितते यज्ञे ब्राह्मणेभ्यो ह्यमन्यत।
en: Whatever of gold Ratindeva possessed, then, was given away to the Brahmanas in the course of one of his sacrifices.

sn: प्रत्यक्षं तस्य हव्यानि प्रतिगृह्णन्ति देवताः॥ कव्यानि पितरः काले सर्वकामान् द्विजोत्तमाः।
en: The gods in person used to accept the libations of butter poured on the fire for them, And the ancestral manes used similarly to accept food that was offered to them in proper time. The Brahmanas, the best of their sects, used to obtain from him all the objects of their desire.

sn: स चेन्ममार सृञ्जय चतुर्भद्रतरस्त्वया॥ पुत्रात् पुण्यतरस्तुभ्यं मा पुत्रमनुतप्यथाः। अयज्वानमदाक्षिण्यमभि श्वैत्येत्युदाहरत्॥
en: When, O Srinjaya, even such a king had to undergo Death, who was superior to you in respect of the four cardinal virtues. And consequently was superior to your son, you should not lament for your son who performed no sacrifice and made no sacrificial gifts, saying-'O Shvaitya'.

sn: स चेन्ममार सृञ्जय चतुर्भद्रतरस्त्वया॥ पुत्रात् पुण्यतरस्तुभ्यं मा पुत्रमनुतप्यथाः। अयज्वानमदाक्षिण्यमभि श्वैत्येत्युदाहरत्॥
en: When, O Srinjaya, even such a king had to undergo Death, who was superior to you in respect of the four cardinal virtues. And consequently was superior to your son, you should not lament for your son who performed no sacrifice and made no sacrificial gifts, saying-'O Shvaitya'.

sn: नारद उवाच दौष्यन्तिं भरतं चापि मृतं सृञ्जय शुश्रुम। कर्माण्यसुकराण्यन्यैः कृतवान् यः शिशुर्वने॥
en: Narada said O Srinjaya, we heard that Dushyanta's son Bharata, who, when a child, performed in the woods many feats difficult of being performed by others, had also to suffer death.

sn: हिमावदातान् यः सिंहान् नखदंष्ट्रायुधान् बली। निर्वीर्यास्तरसा कृत्वा विचकर्ष बबन्ध च॥
en: Possessed of great prowess, he used quickly to deprive the very lions armed with teeth and claws, of all their ferocity and dragged them and bound them at his own pleasure.

sn: क्रूरांश्चोग्रतरान् व्याघ्रान् दमित्वा चाकरोद्वशे। मन:शिला इव शिलाः संयुक्ता जतुराशिभिः॥ व्यालादींश्चातिबलवान् सुप्रतीकान् गजानपि। दंष्ट्रासु गृह्य विमुखाशुष्कासयानकरोद् वशे॥
en: He used to tame down the very tigers, more ferocious and more ruthless than the lions. Seizing various beasts of prey and even prodigious elephants dyed with red chalksolution and bespattered with other liquid minerals, by their teeth and tusks, that highly powerful one used to bring them to his subjection causing their throats to become parched up and compelling them to fly away.

sn: महिषानप्यतिबलो बलिनो विचकर्ष ह। सिंहानां च सुदृप्तानां शतान्याकर्षयद् बलात्॥
en: Endued with great strength he used to drag down the mightiest of buffaloes. Through his prowess, he tamed hundreds of ferocious lions.

sn: बलिनः सृमरान् खड्गान् नानासत्त्वानि चाप्युत। कृच्छ्रप्राणं वने बद्ध्वादमयित्वाप्यवासृजत्॥
en: And powerful tigers and horned rhinoceroses and other animals. Binding them by their necks and twisting the ropes (around their necks) to an inch of their lives, he used to release them.

sn: तं सर्वदमनेत्याहुर्द्विजास्तेनास्य कर्मणा। तं प्रत्यषेधज्जननी मा सत्त्वानि विजीजहि॥
en: For those feats of his, the regenerate sages residing there used to call him Sarvadamana (or the subduer of all). But at last his mother forbade him do so, saying-'Do not torture animals thus.'

sn: सोऽश्वमेधशतेनेष्ट्वा यमुनामनु वीर्यवान्। त्रिशताश्वान् सरस्वत्यां गङ्गामनु चतुःशतान्॥
en: Possessed of great energy, he celebrated a hundred Horse-sacrifices on the banks of the river Yamuna, three hundred such sacrifices on the banks of the Sarasvati and four hundred such on the banks of the Ganges.

sn: सोऽश्वमेधसहस्रेण राजसूयशतेन च। पुनरीजे महायज्ञैः समाप्तवरदक्षिणैः॥
en: Having accomplished all those sacrifices he once more performed a thousand great Horsesacrifices and a hundred such Rajasuya, in which he made profuse gifts to the Brahmanas.

sn: अग्निष्टोमातिरात्राभ्यामिष्ट्वा विश्वजिता अपि। वाजपेयसहस्राणां सहस्रश्च सुसंवृतैः॥
en: He performed also such other sacrifices, as the Agnisthoma, the Atiratra, the Vektha, the Visvajit and thousands of Vajapeyas.

sn: इष्ट्वा शाकुन्तलो राजा तर्पयित्वा द्विजान् घनैः। सहस्रं यत्र पद्यानां कण्वाय भरतो ददौ॥ जाम्बूनदस्य शुद्धस्य कनकस्य महायशाः। यस्य यूपः शतव्यामः परिणाहेन काञ्चनः॥ समागम्य द्विजैः सार्धे सेन्ट्रैर्देवैः समुच्छ्रितः। अलंकृतान् राजमानान् सर्वरत्नैर्मनोहरैः॥ हैरण्यानश्वान् द्विरदान् स्थानुष्ट्रानजाविकम्। दासीदासंघनं धान्यं गाः सवत्साः पयस्विनीः॥ ग्रामान् गृहांश्च क्षेत्राणि विविधांश्च परिच्छदान्। कोटीशतायुतांश्चैव ब्राह्मणेभ्यो ह्यमन्यत॥ चक्रवर्ती ह्यदीनात्मा जितारिॉजितः परैः। स चेन्ममार सृञ्जय चतुर्भद्रतरस्त्वया॥
en: Then the royal son of Sakuntala gratified the Brahmanas with the present of riches; then Bharata of illustrious fame gave ten thousand billions of coins made of the purest gold to Kanwa (who had reared his mother). The gods with Indra at their head, accompanied by the twice-born ones, coming to this sacrifices, set up his sacrificial stake made wholly of gold and measuring hundred vyamas in width. The royal Bharata of magnanimous soul, that conqueror of his foes, that sovereign ever unsubdued by his enemies gave away unto the Brahimanas, charming steeds, elephants and chariots, adorned with gold and embossed with gems of the first water of all sorts and camels and goats and sheep and male and female servants, wealth, grain, milch-cows with calves and villages, houses and fields and garments of various kinds, countless in number. When, O Srinjaya, even such a king had to suffer death who was superior to you in respect to the four cardinal virtues.

sn: पुत्रात् पुण्यतरस्तुभ्यं मा पुत्रमनुतप्यथाः। अयज्वानमदाक्षिण्यमभि श्वैत्येत्युदाहरत्॥
en: And consequently to your son, you should not lament for your son who performed no sacrifice and made no sacrificial gifts saying, 'O Shvaitya.'

sn: नारद उवाच पृथु वैन्यं च राजानं मृतं सृज्जय शुश्रुम। यमभ्यषिञ्चन् साम्राज्ये राजसूये महर्षयः॥
en: Narada said We heard also, O Srinjaya, that Vena's son Prithu, who was installed as the emperor of the world by the mighty sages on the celebration of his Rajasuya-sacrifice, had also to suffer death.

sn: यत्नतः प्रथितेत्यूचुः सर्वानभिभवन् पृथुः। क्षतान्नस्त्रास्यते सर्वानित्येवं क्षत्रियोऽभवत्॥
en: Having vanquished all his foes with great efforts, he consolidated his empire, for which he came to be called Prithu (or the celebrated). He became a true Kshatriya, owing to his protecting his subjects from wounds and injuries.

sn: पृथु वैन्यं प्रजा दृष्ट्वा रक्ताः स्मेति यदब्रुवन्। ततो राजेति नामास्य अनुरागादजायत॥
en: Beholding Vena's son Prithu, his subjects said, “We are delighted and in consequence of the affection of his subjects which he enjoyed, he came to be called Raja.

sn: अकृष्टपच्या पृथिवी आसीद् वैन्यस्य कामधुक्। सर्वाः कामदुघा गावः पुटके पुटके मधु॥
en: The Earth yielded corn without being cultivated and for Vena's son Prithu she fulfilled all his desires. The cows also yielded milk whenever desired and every lotus-bud was filled with honey.

sn: आसन् हिरण्मया दर्भाः सुखस्पर्शाः सुखावहाः। तेषां चौराणि संवीताः प्रजास्तेष्वेव शेरते॥
en: The sacred Kusha grass were all made of gold and were delicate to the touch and otherwise delightful. The people used to wear cloths made of this grass and they used to lie down on beds composed of them.

sn: फलान्यमृतकल्पानि स्वादूनि च मधूनि च। तेषामासीत् तदाहारो निराहाराश्च नाभवन्॥
en: Fruits, nectareous, tasteful and delicate, then became their chief edible; and none went without food.

sn: अरोगाः सर्वसिद्धार्था मनुष्य ह्यकुतोभयाः। न्यवसन्त यथाकामं वृक्षेषु च गुहासु च॥
en: In his kingdom men lived free from all diseases, their desires were all crowned with fruition, they entertained no fear. They lived on trees and in caves, as it pleased them.

sn: प्रविभागो न राष्ट्राणां पुराणां चाभवत् तदा। यथासुखं यथाकामं तथैता मुदिताः प्रजाः॥
en: His dominions and his cities were not divided into smaller sections and countries. There his subjects lived delightedly, as it suited their desire or convenience.

sn: तस्य संस्तम्भिता ह्यापः समुद्रमभियास्यतः। पर्वताश्च ददुर्मार्ग ध्वजभङ्गश्च नाभवत्॥
en: When king Prithu repaired to the sea, its waves become solidified. The very mountains opened a way for him and his standard never broke (being obstructed by any thing).

sn: तं वनस्पतयः शैला देवासुरनरोरगाः। सप्तर्षयः पुण्यजना गन्धवाप्सरसोऽपि च॥ पितरश्च सुखासीनमभिगम्येदमब्रुवन्। सम्राडसि क्षत्रियोऽसि राजा गोप्ता पितासि नः॥ देह्यस्मभ्यं महाराज प्रभुः सन्नीप्सितान् वरान्। यैर्वयं शाश्वतीस्तृप्तीवर्तयिष्यामहे सुखम्॥
en: Him seated at his ease, the mighty trees of the forest, the gods of the mountains, the celestials, the Asuras, the men and the replies the seven sages, sages, the holy ascetics, the Gandharvas, the Apsaras and the ancestral manes, approaching said these words-"You are our Emperor, you protect us from injuries, you are ever our delighter, saviour and father. Give us, O mighty monarch, O Master, the boons we desire to have-boons through whose virtue we may live in happiness and plenty, for eternal years.

sn: तथेत्युक्त्वा पृथुर्वैन्यो गृहीत्वाऽऽजगवं धनुः। शरांश्चाप्रतिमान् घोरांश्चिन्तयित्वाब्रवीन्महीम्॥
en: Then saying yea' to all their prayers, Vena's son Prithu took up his Ajagava bow and several dreadful arrows, whose equals existed not; then thinking for a while, he

sn: एह्येहि वसुधे क्षिप्रं क्षरैभ्यः काक्षितं पयः। ततो दास्यामि भद्रं ते अन्नं यस्य यथेप्सितम्॥
en: "Come, come, O Earth, quickly give these my subjects the milk they desire. Good betide you; from the milk you shall shed, I desire to give my subjects the edibles they wish to have.

sn: वसुधोवाच दुहितृत्वेन मां वीर संकल्पयितुमर्हसि। तथेत्युक्वा पृथुः सर्वे विधानमकरोद् वशी॥
en: The Earth said "O Hero, it behoves you to look upon me as your own daughter." Saying, “So be it” the self-controlled Prithu, then arranged for (milking the Earth).

sn: ततो भूतनिकायास्तां वसुधां दुदुहुस्तदा। तां वनस्पतयः पूर्वं समुत्तस्थधुक्षवः॥
en: Then the whole assemblage of creatures begin to milk the Earth (successively). The mighty trees of the forest then first approached her, desirous of milking her.

sn: साऽतिष्ठद् वत्सला वत्संदोग्धृपात्राणि चेच्छती। वत्सोऽभूत पुष्पितः शालः प्लक्षो दोग्धाऽभवत् तदा।।
en: There then stood the highly affectionate Earth (as a cow), looking for a calf, a milker and a pot wherein to keep the milk. Then the flowering Shala tree became the calf and the Plaksha became the milker.

sn: छिन्नप्ररोहणं दुग्धं पात्रमौदुम्बरं शुभम्। उदयः पर्वतो वत्सो मेरुर्दोगधा महागिरिः॥
en: Torn buds become the milk and the auspicious fig tree became the milk-pot. (Next the mountains appeared to milk her) The Eastern hill then became the calf and the mighty Meru-mountain became the milkman.

sn: रत्नान्योषधयो दुग्धं पात्रमश्ममयं तथा। दोग्धा चासीत् तदा देवो दुग्धमूर्जस्करं प्रियम्॥
en: Jewels and precious stones and the Osadhis became the milk and the stones became the milk-jar. Next the celestials became the milkers and everything capable of imparting energy became the milk.

sn: असुरा दुदुहुर्मायामामपात्रे तु ते तदा। दोग्धा द्विमूधातत्रासीद् वत्सश्चासीद् विरोचनः॥
en: Next the Asuras milked urine from the Earth, in unbaked earthen jars. Dvimurdha (the two-headed) then became the milker and Virochana became the calf.

sn: कृर्षि च सस्यं च नरा दुदुहुः पृथिवीतले। स्वायम्भुवो मनुर्वत्सस्तेषां दोग्धाऽभवत् पृथुः॥
en: Next the men milked her when products of cultivation and crops became the milk; the selfcreate Manu became the calf and Prithu the milker, on this occasion.

sn: अलाबुपात्रे च तथा विषं दुग्धा वसुंधरा। धृतराष्ट्रोऽभवद् दोग्धा तेषां वत्सस्तु तक्षकः॥
en: Next the snakes milked her and they received poison for milk in in gourds. Dhritarashtra became the milker and Takshaka became the calf.

sn: सप्तर्षिभिर्ब्रह्म दुग्धा तथा चाक्लिष्टकर्मभिः। दोग्धा बृहस्पतिः पात्रं छान्दो वत्सश्च सोमराट्॥
en: The seven sages untiring in work, next milked her and obtained the knowledge of the Supreme Brahma for the milk. Then Brihaspati became the milker the Vedas became the milkpot and the Somarat became the calf,

sn: अन्तर्धानं चामपात्रे दुग्धा पुण्यजनैर्विराट्। दोग्धा वैश्रवणस्तेषां वत्सश्चासीद् वृषध्वजः॥
en: The Rakshasas milking her, in a jar of unbaked Earth, obtained the power of disappearing at will. Their milker Vaishravana and Vrishadhvaja was their calf.

sn: पुण्यगन्धान् पद्मपात्रे गन्धर्वाप्सरसोऽदुहन्। वत्सश्चित्ररथस्तेषां दोग्धा विश्वरुचिः प्रभुः॥
en: The Apsaras and the Gandharvas milked her of holy fragrance and received it in lotuspetals. Chitraratha became their calf and the lord Visvaruchi became their milker.

sn: स्वधां रजतपात्रेषु दुदुहुः पितरश्च ताम्। वत्सो वैवस्वतस्तेषां यमो दोग्धाऽन्तकस्तदा॥
en: The ancestral manes milked her of Svadhas in pots of silver. Vaivasvata became their calf and the Destroyer (Yama) himself became their milker.

sn: एवं निकायैस्तैर्दुधा पयोऽभीष्टं हि सा विराट्। यैर्वर्तयन्ति ते ह्यद्य पात्रैर्वत्सैश्च नित्यशः॥
en: Thus was the Earth milked by that entire host of creatures, who obtained for milk all objects of their respective desire. The very was calves and the pots, with whose help they milked could be seen even today.

sn: यज्ञैश्च विविधैरिष्ट्वा पृथुर्वैन्यः प्रतापवान्। संतर्पयित्वा भूतानि सर्वैः कामैर्मनः प्रियैः॥
en: Then Vena's son Prithu, possessed of prowess, celebrated various sacrifices and he gratified the hearts of creature with objects desired by them.

sn: हैरण्यानकरोद् राजा ये केचित् पार्थिवा भुवि। तान् ब्राह्मणेभ्यः प्रायच्छदश्वमेधे महामखे॥
en: The king caused all objects obtaining of the face of the Earth to be made of gold and on the occasion of his great Horse-sacrifice, he gave them away to the Brahmanas.

sn: षष्टिनागसहस्राणि षष्टिनागशतानि च। सौवर्णानकरोद् राजा ब्राह्मणेभ्यश्च तान् ददौ॥
en: The king caused sixty-six thousands images of elephants to be made of gold and he gave them away to the Brahmanas.

sn: इमां च पृथिवीं सर्वां मणिरत्नविभूषिताम्। सौवर्णीमकरोद् राजा ब्राह्मणेभ्यश्च तां ददौ॥
en: The entire Earth adorned with jewels and gems, the king caused to be covered over with gold and he then gave her away to the Brahmanas.

sn: स चेन्ममार सृज्जय चतुर्भद्रतरस्त्वया। पुत्रात् पुण्यतरस्तुभ्यं मा पुत्रमनुतप्यथाः। अयज्वानमदाक्षिण्यमभि श्वैत्येतयुदाहरत्॥
en: When, O Srinjaya, even such a king, who was superior to you in respect of the four virtues and consequently much more superior to your son, you should not lament for your son who performed no sacrifices and made no sacrificial gifts-saying, 'O Shvaitya'.

sn: नारद उवाच रामो महातपाः शूरो वीरलोकनमस्कृतः। जामदग्नयोऽष्यतियशा अवितृप्तो मरिष्यति॥
en: Narada said Even the heroic Rama that illustrious ascetic adored by the heroes of the world, that son of Jamadagni, of great renown, died with his desires unsatiated.

sn: यः स्माद्यमनुपर्येति भूमिं कुर्वन्निमां सुखाम्। न चासीद् विक्रिया यस्यप्राप्य श्रियमनुत्तमाम्॥
en: Making this Earth abound in all kinds of happiness, he caused the primeval Yuga to set in. He was not perverted, having obtained cxcellent affluence.

sn: यः क्षत्रियैः परामृष्टे वत्से पितरि चाब्रुवन्। ततोऽवधीत् कार्तवीर्यमजितं समरे परैः॥
en: When a calf belonging to him when stolen and when his father was slain by the Kshatriyas, he took a vow saying that he would relieve the Earth of her burden of Kshatriyas. Thereafter he slew Kartavirya who was never before defeated in battle by his foes.

sn: क्षत्रियाणां चतुःषष्टिमयुतानि. सहस्रशः। तदा मृत्योः समेतानि एकेन धनुषाऽजयत्॥
en: Single-handed and with a single bow, he vanquished and dispatched to the abode of Death, four and sixty times ten thousand Kshatriyas.

sn: ब्रह्मद्विषां चाथ तस्मिन् सहस्राणि चतुर्दश। पुनरन्यानि जग्राह दन्तक्रूरं जघान ह॥
en: In that slaughter were included fourteen thousand Kshatriyas all contemners of the Brahmanas. Then again he slew slew many Kshatriyas of the Dantakrura country.

sn: सहस्रं मुसलेनाहन् सहस्रमसिनाऽवधीत्। उद्बन्धनात् सहस्रं च सहस्रमुदके धृतम्॥
en: He slew a thousand Kshatriyas with his bludgeon, a thousand with his sword and a thousand of the Kshatriyas also by hanging them.

sn: दन्तान्भक्त्वा सहस्रस्य कर्णान् नासान्यकृन्तत। ततः सप्तसहस्राणां कटुधूपमपाययत्॥
en: He splitted the teeth and cu-off nose and ears of one thousand Kshatriyas and forcibly made seven thousand kings to sip the bitter Dhupa (herb).

sn: शिष्टान् बद्ध्वा च हत्वा वै तेषां मूर्ध्नि विभिद्य च। गुणावतीमुत्तरेण खाण्डवाद् दक्षिणेन च। गिर्यन्ते शतसाहस्रा हैहयाः समरे हताः॥
en: Remaining of them were tied and slain by clashing their heads. At north from Gunavati and at south from Khandava forest, hundreds and thousands of Haihaya kings were slain in the battle field.

sn: सरथाश्वगजा वीरा निहतास्तत्र शेरते। पितुर्वधामर्षितेन जामदग्न्येन धीमता॥
en: Heroes with their chariots, steeds and elephants, lay slain on the field of battle, by the intelligent son of Jamadagni, who had been exasperated by the death of his father.

sn: निजघ्ने दशसाहस्रान् रामः परशुना तदा। न ह्यमृष्यत ता वाचो यास्तै शमुदीरिताः॥ भृगो रामाभिधावेति यदाक्रन्दन् द्विजोत्तमाः।
en: Then Rama slew with his axe ten thousand Kshatriyas. He then could not bear the hot words uttered by his enraged adversaries. When the twice-born sects exclaimed saying, 'O Rama, descendant of Bhrigu's race.

sn: ततः काश्मीरदरदान् कुन्तिक्षुद्रकमालवान्॥ अङ्गवङ्गकलिङ्गांश्च विदेहांस्ताम्रलिप्तकान्। रक्षावाहान् वीतिहोत्रांस्त्रिगर्तान् मार्तिकावतान्॥ शिबीनन्यांश्च राजन्यान् देशान् देशान् सहस्रशः। निजघान शितैर्बाणैर्जामदग्न्यः प्रतापवान्॥
en: Then the puissant son of Jamadgni proceeding against the Kashmiras, the Daradas, the Kuntis, the Kshudrakas, the Malavas, the Angas, the Vangas, the Kalingas, the Videhas, the Tamraliptakas, the Rakshavahan, the Vitihotras, the Trigartas, the Martikavatas the Sini and other kingly races, thousands in number, inhabiting various countries, slew them all with his arrows of exceeding sharpness.

sn: कोटीशतसहस्राणि क्षत्रियाणां सहस्रशः। इन्द्रगोपकवर्णस्य बन्धुजीवनिभस्य च।॥ रुधिरस्य परीवाहैः पूरयित्वा करांसि च। सर्वानष्टादश द्वीपान् वशमानीय भार्गवः॥ ईजे क्रतुशतैः पुण्यैः समाप्तवरदक्षिणैः।
en: Going from country to country, he slew thousands and crores of Kshatriyas creating a deluge of blood and filling many lakes with it, which was as red as Indra Gopakas or the wild fruit known as Bandhu-jiva and also bringing under his sway all the eighteen division of the earth, that descendant of Bhrigu's race. Celebrated a hundred holy sacred sacrifices in which he gave away profuse sacrificial presents.

sn: वेदीमष्टनलोत्सेधां सौवर्णो विधिनिर्मिताम्॥ सर्वरत्नशतैः पूर्णो पताकाशतमालिनीम्। ग्राम्यारण्यैः पशुगणैः सम्पूर्णं च पहीमिमाम्॥ रामस्य जामदग्न्यस्य प्रतिजग्राह कश्यपः।
en: The sacrificial altar, ful} eighteen Nalas high and made entirely of gold and erected duly. And filled with diverse kinds of gems and jewels and adorned with hundreds of pennons, as also this earth abounding in domestic and wild animals were accepted by Kasyapa as sacrificial presents offered to him by Rama.

sn: ततः शतसहस्राणि द्विपेन्द्रान् हेमभूषणान्॥ निर्दस्युं पृथिवीं कृत्वा शिष्टेष्टजनसंकुलाम्। कश्यपाय ददौ रामो हयमेधे महामखे॥
en: The son of Jamadagni, Rama also gave him many thousands of huge elephants adorned with golden ornaments. Freeing the earth from the robbers that infested her and making her full of innocent and amiable people, Rama gave her away to Kasyapa at his great Horsesacrifice.

sn: त्रि:सप्तकृत्वः पृथिवीं कृत्वा निःक्षत्रियां प्रभुः। इष्ट्वा क्रतुशतैर्वीरो ब्राह्मणेभ्यो ह्यमन्यत॥
en: That lord, that hero having relieved the earth, for twenty-one times, of her burdens of the Kshatriya population and having celebrated a hundred sacrifices, gave her away to the Brahmanas.

sn: सप्तद्वीपां वसुमती मारीचोऽगृह्णत द्विजः। रामं प्रोवाच निर्गच्छ वसुधातो ममाज्ञया॥
en: The earth with her seven grand divisions were bestowed by him upon the twice-born son of Maricha (Kasyapa). Then the the latter addressed Rama saying-"Go you out of this Earth, at my command".

sn: स कश्यपस्य वचनात् प्रोत्सार्य सरितां पतिम्। इषुपाते युधां श्रेष्ठः कुर्वन् ब्राह्मणशासनम्॥ अध्यावसद् गिरिश्रेष्ठं महेन्द्रं पर्वतोत्तमम्।
en: At the words of Kasyapa, that best of warriors obedient to the Brahmanas' command, caused, by the fall of his arrows, the very occan to roll back; then going to the foremost of mountains, namely, the Mahendra mountain, he continued to live there.

sn: एवं गुणशतैर्युक्तो भृगूणां कीर्तिवर्धनः॥ जामदग्न्यो ह्यतियशा मरिष्यति महाद्युतिः।
en: Even that enhancer of the glory of the Bhrigu race that one endowed with desirable qualities that son of Jamadagni, of illustrious renown and great effulgence, had to die.

sn: त्वया चतुर्भद्रतरः पुत्रात् पुण्यतरस्तव॥ अयज्वानमदाक्षिण्यं मा पुत्रमनुतप्यथाः।
en: O Srinjaya, Superior to you in respect to the four virtues and also to your son, even that one did die. Therefore you should not weep for your son, who perforined no sacrifice and made no sacrificial gifts.

sn: एते चतुर्भद्रतरास्त्वया भद्रशताधिकाः। मृता नरवरश्रेष्ठ मरिष्यन्ति च सृञ्जय॥
en: These foremost and best of men, all superior to you in respect of the four virtues and in respect of many other meritorious qualities, had to suffer death, O Srinjaya.

description: The conclusion of the story of the sixteen sovereigns
sn: व्यास उवाच पुण्यमाख्यानमायुष्यं श्रुत्वा षोडशराजकम्। अव्याहरन्नरपतिस्तूष्णीमासीत् स सृञ्जयः॥
en: Vyasa said Having heard these holy stories of the sixteen kings, capable of enhancing the duration of the listener's life, king Srinjayas said nothing and remained silent for a while.

description: The conclusion of the story of the sixteen sovereigns
sn: तमब्रवीत् तथाऽऽसीनं नारदो भगवानृषिः। श्रुतं कीर्तयतो मह्यं गृहीतं ते महाद्युते॥
en: Then to him thus sitting silent, the almighty sage Narada said-"O you of great effulgence, you have heard the stories just now related by me and have comprehended their signification.

description: The conclusion of the story of the sixteen sovereigns
sn: आहोस्विदन्ततो नष्टं श्राद्धं शूद्रीपताविव। स एवमुक्तःप्रत्याह प्राञ्जलिः सृञ्जयस्तदा।॥
en: Or are all these lost on you, like a sraddha performed by a twice-born one having a female of the Sudra caste for his wife.” Thus spoken to, Srinjaya replied to him with folded palms, sayingएतच्छ्रुत्वा महाबाहो धन्यमाख्यानमुत्तमम्।

description: The conclusion of the story of the sixteen sovereigns
sn: राजर्षीणां पुराणानां यज्वनां दक्षिणावताम्॥
en: "O you rich in the wealth of asceticism, having heard these best and laudable stories of ancient royal sages, all of whom celebrated great sacrifices with profuse presents unto the Brahmanas.

description: The conclusion of the story of the sixteen sovereigns
sn: विस्मयेन ते शोके तमसीवार्कतेजसा। विपाप्मास्यव्यथोपेतो ब्रूहि किं करवाण्यहम्॥
en: All my sorrow have been driven away by wonder, like darkness being dispelled by the radiance of the sun. I have now been purged of all my sins; and I do not feel any pain now. Tell me what shall I do.

description: The conclusion of the story of the sixteen sovereigns
sn: नारद उवाच दिष्ट्यापहृतशोकस्त्वं वृणीष्वेह यदिच्छसि। तत् तत् प्रपत्स्यसे सर्वं न मृषावादिनो वयम्॥
en: Narada said It is through good luck that your sorrow has been dispelled. Ask you the boon that your heart craves for; you will get whatever you may seek to have. We never speak falsehood.

description: The conclusion of the story of the sixteen sovereigns
sn: संजय उवाच एतेनैव प्रतीतोऽहं प्रसन्नो यद्भवान् ममा प्रसन्नो यस्य भगवान् न तस्यास्तीह दुर्लभम्॥
en: Srinjaya said I am contented even with this, viz., that you, O holy sage, are pleased with me. That person with whom you are pleased, you holy one, has nothing inaccessible to him.

description: The conclusion of the story of the sixteen sovereigns
sn: नारद उवाच मृतं ददानि ते पुत्रं दस्युभिर्निहतं वृथा। उद्धृत्य नरकात् कष्टात् पशुवत् प्रोक्षितं यथा॥
en: Narada said I will once again give you back your son, who was to no purpose slain by the robbers, like an animal immolated in a sacrifice. I shall take him out of the terrible hell.

description: The conclusion of the story of the sixteen sovereigns
sn: व्यास उवाच प्रादुरासीत् ततः पुत्रः सृञ्जयस्याद्भुतप्रभः। प्रसन्नेनर्षिणा दत्तः कुबेरतनयोपमः॥
en: Vyasa said Then the son of Srinjaya of wonderful splendour, resembling the son of Kubera, appeared there, bestowed on his bereaved father, by the qualified sage.

description: The conclusion of the story of the sixteen sovereigns
sn: ततः संगम्य पुत्रेण प्रीतिमानभवनृपः। ईजे च क्रतुभिः पुण्यैः समाप्तवरदक्षिणैः॥
en: Then king Srinjaya once more obtaining the sight of his son became highly delighted. He then gave away numerous merit-giving sacrificial gifts upon their accomplishment of the yajnas.

description: The conclusion of the story of the sixteen sovereigns
sn: अकृतार्थश्च भीतश्च न च सान्नाहिको हतः। अयज्वा त्वनपत्यश्च ततोऽसौ जीवितः पुनः॥
en: The life-mission of Srinjaya's son was not fulfilled. He had performed no sacrifices and had begotten no progeny. Destitute of bravery, he perished miserable and not in battle. For this reason he could be brought back into life.

description: The conclusion of the story of the sixteen sovereigns
sn: शूरो वीरः कृतार्थश्च प्रताप्यारीन् सहस्रशः। अभिमन्युर्गतो वीरः पृतनाभिमुखो हतः॥
en: As regards Abhimanyu, he was courageous and brave. He has fulfilled the mission of his life; for, the brave son of Subhadra having scorched his enemies by thousands, had passed away, falling on the field of battle.

description: The conclusion of the story of the sixteen sovereigns
sn: ब्रह्मचर्येण यान् कांश्चित् प्रज्ञया च श्रुतेन च इष्टैश्च क्रतुभिर्यान्ति तांस्तेपुत्रोऽक्षयान् गतः॥
en: Those eternal regions that are attained through the performance of Brahmacharya vows, through knowledge and acquaintance with the scriptures, through foremost of sacrifices, even those regions have been obtained by your son.

description: The conclusion of the story of the sixteen sovereigns
sn: विद्वांसः कर्मभिः पुण्यैः स्वर्गमीहन्ति नित्यशः। न तु स्वर्गादयं लोकः काम्यते स्वर्गवासिभिः॥
en: Men possessed of knowledge always desire to attain to heaven by their performance of deeds of piety. They who live in heaven do not like this world.

description: The conclusion of the story of the sixteen sovereigns
sn: तस्मात् स्वर्गगतं पुत्रमर्जुनस्य हतं रणे। न चेहानयितुं शक्यं किंचिदप्राप्यमीहितम्॥
en: Therefore it is not easy to find out any desirable thing that might have been unattained by him, that might bring back into this world Arjuna's son slain in battle and now dwelling in heaven.

description: The conclusion of the story of the sixteen sovereigns
sn: यां योगिनो ध्यानविविक्तदर्शनाः प्रयान्ति यां चोत्तमयज्विनो जनाः। तपोभिरिद्धैरनुयान्ति यां तथा तामक्षया ते तनयो गतो गतिम्॥
en: Your son has ascended to those regions, the eternal goal of Yogins who contemplate with their eyes shut or by performers of illustrious sacrifices or by people possessed of great ascetic merit.

description: The conclusion of the story of the sixteen sovereigns
sn: अन्तात् पुनर्भावगतो विराजते राजेव वीरो ह्यमृतात्मरश्मिभिः। तामैन्दवीमात्मतनुं द्विजोचितां गतोऽभिमन्युर्न स शोकमर्हति॥
en: Having attained a new figure after death, that hero is shining like a monarch in his own immortal radiance. Verily Abhimanyu has once more assumed his own body composed of the essence of the moon that is desired by all twice-born ones. Therefore you should not weep for him.

description: The conclusion of the story of the sixteen sovereigns
sn: एवं ज्ञात्वा स्थिरो भूत्वा जहरीन् धैर्यमामुहि। जीवन्त एव नः शोच्या न तु स्वर्गगतोऽनघ॥
en: Acquainted with these facts, compose yourself and slay your enemies. Muster courage, O you sinless one, it is the living beings who want us to grieve for them and not they who have ascended to heaven.

description: The conclusion of the story of the sixteen sovereigns
sn: शोचतो हि महाराज अघमेवाभिवर्धते। तस्माच्छोकं परित्यज्य श्रेयसे प्रयतेद् बुधः॥
en: O king, his sins go on increasing, for whom the living mourn. Fro this reason, the wise, renouncing grief. exert themselves for the benefit of the dead (i.e., their souls).

description: The conclusion of the story of the sixteen sovereigns
sn: प्रहर्षपभिमानं च सुखप्राप्तिं च चिन्तयन्। एतद्बुद्धवा बुधाः शोकं न शोकः शोक उच्यते॥२०
en: The living man should think of the joy, the glory and the happiness of the dead. Acquainted with truth, the wise never harbour grief, for grief is nothing more or less than grief.

description: The conclusion of the story of the sixteen sovereigns
sn: एवं विद्वान् समुत्तिष्ठ प्रयतो भव मा शुचः। श्रुतस्ते सम्भवो मृत्योस्तपांस्यनुपमानि च॥
en: Know this as truth; rise up, grid up your loins; do not lament, you have heard of the origin of the Death and of her unequaled penances.

description: The conclusion of the story of the sixteen sovereigns
sn: सर्वभूतसमत्वं च चञ्चलाश्च विभूतयः। सृञ्जयस्य तु तं पुत्रं मृतं संजीवितं पुनः॥
en: As also of her equality of conduct towards all creatures. You have heard that prosperity is unsteady; you have also heard as how the dead son of Srinjaya was brought back to life.

description: The conclusion of the story of the sixteen sovereigns
sn: एवं विद्वान् महाराज मा शुचः साधयाम्यहम्। एतावदुक्त्वा भगवांस्तत्रैवान्तरधीयत॥
en: O foremost of learned monarchs, do not lament. May you enjoy peace, I depart. Having thus spoken, the sacred Rishi Vyasa disappeared even there.

description: The conclusion of the story of the sixteen sovereigns
sn: वागीशाने भगवति व्यासे व्यभ्रनभःप्रभे। गते मतिमतां श्रेष्ठे समाश्वास्य युधिष्ठिरम्॥
en: Upon the disappearance of that eloquent speaker, that foremost of all intelligent beings, viz., the holy Vyasa whose colour was like that of the sky overspread with clouds, Yudhishthira having obtained consolation.

description: The conclusion of the story of the sixteen sovereigns
sn: पूर्वेषां पार्थिवेन्द्राणां महेन्द्रप्रतिमौजसाम्। न्यायाधिगतवित्तानां तां श्रुत्वा यज्ञसम्पदम्॥
en: In consequence of what he had heard about the sacrificial merit and prosperity, of those great monarchs of ancient times endued with energy equal to that of the great Indra himself and all of whom had acquired wealth by virtuous means.

description: The conclusion of the story of the sixteen sovereigns
sn: सम्पूज्य मनसा विद्वान् विशोकोऽभूद् युधिष्ठिरः। पुनश्चाचिन्तयद् दीनः किंस्विद् वक्ष्ये धनंजयम्॥
en: Applauded them in his mind and then became relieved of his sorrows. But once more, with a sorrowful heart he asked himself saying-"What shall I say to Dhananjaya?'

sn: संजय उवाच तस्मिन्नहनि निर्वृत्ते घोरे प्राणभृतां क्षये। आदित्येऽस्तं गते श्रीमान् संध्याकाल उपस्थिते॥
en: Sanjaya said When that dreadful day so fraught with the slaughter of creatures had passed away and when the sun set, the auspicious shade of twilight began to spread itself.

sn: व्यपयातेषु वासाय सर्वेषु भरतर्षभ। हत्वा संशप्तकवातान् दिव्यैरस्त्रैः कपिध्वजः॥ प्रायात् स शिबिरं जिष्णु जैत्रमास्थाय तं रथम्। गच्छन्नेव च गोविन्दं साश्रुकण्ठोऽभ्यभाषत॥
en: Then, O foremost of the Bharatas, when the troops of both the hosts had retired to their respective quarters, the ape-bannered Jishnu having slain the Samshaptaka hosts with his celestial weapons, proceeded towards his pavilion mounted on that victorious chariot of his. As he went on, he asked Govinda, in a voice choked with tears.

sn: किं नु मे हृदयं त्रस्तं वाक् च सज्जति केशव। स्यन्दन्ति चाप्यनिष्टानिगात्रं सीदति चाप्युत॥
en: “Why, O Keshava, does my mind misgive and why does my speech falter? Evil portents reveal themselves to me and my limbs are becoming weak.

sn: अनिष्टं चैव मे श्लिष्टं हृदयान्नापसर्पति। भुवि ये दिक्षु चात्युग्रा उत्पातास्त्रासयन्ति माम्॥
en: Thoughts, such as a calamity has befallen me, occupying my heart, does not leave it; on earth, in all the directions, various dreadful portents affright me.

sn: बहुप्रकारा दृश्यन्ते सर्व एवाघशंसिनः। अपि स्वस्ति भवेद् राज्ञः सामात्यस्य गुरोर्मम॥
en: Various kinds of omens are being seen by me and they harbinger the happening of a calamity, May all things fare well with the king, my venerable superior and with his followers."

sn: वासुदेव उवाच व्यक्तं शिवं तव भ्रातुः सामात्यस्य भविष्यति। मा शुचः किञ्चदेवान्यत् तत्रानिष्टं भविष्यति॥
en: The son of Vasudeva said It is evident that everything fares well with your brothers and his ministers. Do not give way to evil thoughts; it is probable, that some trivial calamity has taken place.

sn: संजय उवाच ततः संध्यामुपास्यैव वीरौ वीरावसादने। कथयन्तौ रणे वृत्तं प्रयातौ रथमास्थितौ॥
en: Sanjaya said Then those two heroes, having adored the evening twilight, proceeded on their car talking of the incidents of that day's battle so destructive of heroes.

sn: ततः स्वशिबिरं प्राप्तौ हतानन्दं हतत्विषम्। वासुदेवोऽर्जुनश्चैव कृत्वा कर्म सुदुष्करम्॥
en: Thereafter having achieved feats difficult of being achieved, Arjuna and Vasudeva reached the Pandava encampments, joyless joyless and melancholy.

sn: ध्वस्ताकारं समालक्ष्य शिबिरं परवीरहा। बीभत्सुब्रवीत् कृष्णमस्वस्थहृदयस्ततः॥
en: Then that slayer of foes, Vibhatsu, beholding the camp in confusion, said to Krishna with a sorrowful heart-

sn: अर्जुन उवाच नदन्ति नाद्य तूर्योणि मङ्गल्यानि जनार्दन। मिश्रा दुन्दुभिनिर्घोषैः शङ्खाश्चाडम्बरैः सह॥
en: Arjuna said O Jaraddana, the auspicious drums are not best today and their sound does not add to the din created by the trumpet-blasts and conchblares.

sn: वीणा नैवाद्य वाद्यन्ते शम्यातालस्वनैः सह। मङ्गल्यानि च गीतानि च गायन्ति पठन्ति च॥ स्तुतियुक्तानि रम्याणि ममानीकेषु बन्दिनः। योधाश्चापि हि मां दृष्ट्वा निवर्तन्ते ह्यधोमुखाः॥
en: The melodious Venu is not played upon accompanied by claps; auspicious songs, fraught with praises and delightful, are not sung in my troops today, by the minstrels and the bards. All warriors also, beholding me, are turning away.with their faces cast down.

sn: कर्माणि च यथापूर्वं कृत्वा नाभिवदन्ति माम्। अपि स्वस्ति भवेदध भ्रातृभ्यो मम माधव॥
en: Duly performing the ceremonies one after another, they do not come forward to salute me. O Madhava, is everything well with all my brothers?

sn: न हि शुद्ध्यति मे भावो दृष्ट्वा स्वजनमाकुलम्। अपि पाञ्चालराजस्य विराटस्य च मानद॥
en: Seeing my own people distressed with sorrow, my mind does not obtain peace. Does everything fare well, o bestower of honour, with the Panchala king or the ruler of the Viratas.

sn: सर्वेषां चैवयोधानां सामग्यं स्यान्ममाच्युत। न च मामद्य सौभद्रः प्रहृष्टो भ्रातृभिः सह। रणादायान्तुमुचितं प्रत्युद्याति हसन्निव॥
en: Or with all of our warriors, you of undeteriorating glory? Alas, today Subhadra's son accompanied by his brothers, does not come out, smiling and joyful to receive me returning from battle.

sn: संजय उवाच एवं सकथयन्तौ तौ प्रविष्टौ शिबिरं स्वकम्। ददृशाते भृशास्वस्थान् पाण्डवान् नष्टचेतसः॥
en: Sanjaya said Thus talking to one another, they both entered into their encampments and they beheld the Pandavas sit cheerless and with hearts distracted (with grief).

sn: दृष्ट्वा भ्रातूंश्च पुत्रांश्च विमना वानरध्वजः। अपश्यंश्चैव सौभद्रमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Then that hero bearing the ape as a device on his banner, seeing his brother and sons (thus depressed), himself became melancholy. Then not finding Subhadra's son he spoke these

sn: अर्जुन उवाच मुखवर्णोऽप्रसन्नो वः सर्वेषामेव लक्ष्यते। न चाभिमन्यु पश्यामि न च मां प्रतिनन्दथ॥
en: Arjuna said I see that the colour of your countenances has turned pale. I do not also see Abhimanyu here, nor do you welcome me.

sn: मया श्रुतश्च द्रोणेन चक्रव्यूहो विनिर्मितः। न च वस्तस्य भेत्ताऽस्ति विना सौभद्रमर्भकम्॥
en: I have also heard that Drona today arrayed his troops in the circular order. There is also none among you capable of penetrating into that array, save my boy Abhimanyu.

sn: न चोपदिष्टस्तस्यासीन्मयानीकाद् विनिर्गमः। कच्चिन्न बालो युष्माभिः परानीकं प्रवेशितः॥
en: But I did not teach him the means of coming out of that array. Is it that you made the boy enter the array of the enemy?

sn: भित्त्वानीकं महेष्वासः परेषां बहुशो युधि। कच्चिन्न निहतः संख्ये सौभद्रः परवीरहा॥
en: Has that fierce bowman, that slayer of hostile heroes, namely, the son of Subhadra, having penetrated into those numberless divisions of the enemy, been slain in battle.

sn: लोहिताक्षं महाबाहुं जातं सिंहमिवाद्रिषु। उपेन्द्रसदृशं ब्रत कथमायोधने हतः॥
en: Tell me, Oh, how that hero possessed of mighty arms and red eyes, who was born in our race, like a lion on the mountain breast and who resembled Upendra himself, has been slain in battle?

sn: सुकुमारं महेष्वासं वासवस्यात्मजात्मजम्। सदा मम प्रियं ब्रूत कथमायोधने हतः॥
en: Tell me about Abhimanyu, the grandson of Indra, the great archer, delicate body youth and always dear to me. How was he slaughtered in the battle.

sn: सुभद्रायाः प्रियं पुत्रं द्रौपद्याः केशवस्य च। अम्बायाश्च प्रियं नित्यं कोऽवधीत् कालमोहितः॥
en: What warriors, urged on by their evil Destiny, ventured to slay that dear-loved son of Subhadra, that favourite of Draupadi and Keshava, who was always fondly loved by my own mother (Kunti)?

sn: सदृशो वृष्णिवीरस्य केशवस्य महात्मनः। विक्रमश्रुतमाहात्म्यैः कथमायोधने हतः॥
en: How has that hero resembling the highsouled Vrishni hero Keshava himself in prowess, generosity and acquaintance with the Shastras, been slain in battle?

sn: वार्ष्णेयीदयितं शूरं मया सततलालितम्। यदि पुत्रं न पश्यामि यास्यामि यमसादनम्॥
en: If today I do not see that hero dearly loved by that daughter of Vrishni race (Subhadra) and fondly brought up by myself, I shall be a guest of Death's abode.

sn: मृदुकुञ्चितकेशान्तं बालं वालमृगेक्षणम्। मत्तद्विरदविक्रान्तं शालपोतमिवोद्गतम्॥ स्मिताभिभाषिणं दन्तं गुरुवाक्यकरं सदा। बाल्येऽप्यतुलकर्माणं प्रियवाक्यममत्सरम्॥ महोत्साहं महाबाहुं दीर्घराजीवलोचनम्। भक्तानुकम्पिनं दान्तं न च नीचानुसारिणम्॥ कृतज्ञं ज्ञानसम्पन्नं कृतास्त्रमनिवर्तिनम्। युद्धाभिनन्दिनं नित्यं द्विषतां भयवर्धनम्॥ स्वेषां प्रियहिते युक्तं पितॄणां जयगृद्धिनम्। न च पूर्वं प्रहर्तारं संग्रामे नष्टसम्भ्रमम्॥ यदि पुत्रं न पश्यामि यास्मामि यमसादनम्।
en: Possessed of soft and curling hair-ends, of tender years, of eyes like those of a young gazelle graced with the tread of an infuriate elephant, resembling an offshoot of a Shala tree. Of sweet speeches attended with smiles, modest, ever ready to carry out the behests of his venerables, achieving in tender years, feats worthy of mature age, sweet-spoken, free from animosity. Of mighty energy and prowess, of eyes resembling large lotus-petals, ever merciful towards his followers, self-possessed, never pursuing mean objects and men. Ever grateful, endued with the knowledge of all things, unretreating and accomplished in the use of all kinds of weapons, ever delighting in battle and ever enhancing the terror of his adversaries. Always intent on bringing about the welfare of his own party, ever desirous of seeing victory secured by his own sires, never striking first in battle, never daunted in fight. Oh! if, I do not see such a son of mine, I shall carry me to the abode of Death.

sn: रथेषु गण्यमानेषु गणितं तं महारथम्॥ मयाध्यर्धगुणं संख्ये तरुणं बाहुशालिनम्।
en: WEHRI forei fari anae ia 2113811

sn: यदि पुत्रं न पश्यामि यास्यामि यमसादनम्।
en: In the tale of car-warriors, always counted with the mighty car-warriors. Possessed of mighty arins, of tender years, one and a half times superior to me in battle, always a favourite of myself, Pradyumna and Keshava. Oh, if I do not see that son of mine, I shall go to the regions of Death,

sn: सुनसं सुललाटान्तं स्वक्षिभ्रदशनच्छदम्॥ अपश्यतस्तद्वदनं का शान्तिर्हदयस्य मे।
en: Graced with a beautiful nose and fore-head and eyes and eyebrows and teeth and lips. Oh, without seeing that countenance of his, I shall enjoy no peace of mind.

sn: तन्त्रीस्वनमुखं रम्यं पुंस्कोकिलसमध्वनिम्॥ अशृण्वतः स्वनं तस्य का शान्तिर्हृदयस्य मे।
en: Delightful like the warding of a lyre, charming and melodious like the voice of a cuckoo. Oh, without hearing that voice of his what peace can my heart enjoy?

sn: रूपं चाप्रतिमं तस्य त्रिदशेश्चापि दुर्लभम्॥ अपश्यतो हि वीरस्य का शान्तिर्हृदयस्य मे।
en: His beauty that was unequaled and scarce even among the heaven-dwelling gods. Oh, without beholding that beauty of his, what peace can my heart enjoy?

sn: अभिवादनदक्षं तं पितॄणां वचने रतम्॥ नाद्याहं यदि पश्यामि का शान्तिर्हृदयस्य मे।
en: Skillful in congratulating and welcoming others, obedient to the commands of his sires. If I do not see that son of mine, what peace can my heart enjoy?

sn: सुकुमारः सदा वीरो महार्हशयनोचितः॥ भूमावनाथवच्छेते नूनं नाथवतां वरः।
en: Brought up in all luxury, always heroic and accustomed to lie on precious beds. He lies today on the bare earth like one helpless, though he is foremost of all who have others to look after them.

sn: शयानं समुपासन्ति यं पुरा परमस्त्रिय॥ तमद्य विप्रविद्धाङ्गमुपासन्त्यशिवाः शिवाः।
en: He upon whom, when on his bed, the most beautiful women used to attend. Oh! even he, his bodies mutilated with with shafts, has inauspicious jackals prowling over the field to attend upon him today!

sn: यः पुरा बोध्यते सुप्तः सूतमागधबन्दिभिः॥ बोधयन्त्यद्य तं नूनं श्वापदा विकृतैः स्वनैः।
en: He who formerly used to be awakened from his sleep by songsters, ministrels and panegyrists. Oh! even he shall today be roused by the fierce yells of the beasts of prey.

sn: छत्रच्छायासमुचितं तस्य तद् वदनं शुभम्॥ नूनमद्य रजोध्वस्तं रणरेणुः करिष्यति।
en: That auspicious and charming countenances of his, worthy of being shaded by umbrellas. Shall today be soiled with the dust rising from the field of battle.

sn: हा पुत्रकावितृप्तस्य सततं पुत्रदर्शने॥ भाग्यहीनस्य कालेन यथा मे नीयसे बलात्।
en: Oh! my dear child, I, who was never satiated with looking at you. Alas! unfortunate that I am I have been forcibly bereft of you by Death.

sn: सा च संयमनी नूनं सदा सुकृतिनां गतिः॥ स्वभाभि सिता रम्या त्वयात्पर्थं विराजते।
en: Surely the mansion of Death, that goal of persons of pious deeds. That delightful palace, has today been illumined by your splendour and so has been made highly charming by you.

sn: नूनं वैवस्वतश्च त्वां वरुणश्च प्रियातिथिम्॥ शतक्रतुर्धनेशश्च प्राप्तमर्चन्त्यभीरुकम्।
en: "Surely Yama, Varuna, Indra of hundred sacrifices and Kubera, receiving yourself as a welcome guest, are making preparations for worshipping you.”

sn: एवं विलप्य बहुधा भिन्नपोतो वणिग् यथा॥ दुःखेन महताऽऽविष्टो युधिष्ठिरमपृच्छत।
en: Thus copiously lamenting like a trader whose ship has been broken and being possessed by great grief Arjuna thus

sn: कच्चित्स कदनं कृत्वा परेषां कुरुनन्दन॥ स्वर्गतोऽभिमुख: संख्ये युध्यमानो नरर्षभैः।
en: "O delighter of the Kurus, spreading a terrible, slaughter among the enemy's host, did my son ascend to heaven having fought with many foremost of men in battle?

sn: स नूनं बहुभिर्यत्तैर्युध्यमानो नरर्षभैः॥ असहायः सहायार्थी मामनुध्यातवान् ध्रुवम्।
en: "Surely fighting carefully in battle, he, single-handed and needing assistance, repeatedly thought of me!

sn: पीड्यमानः शरैस्तीक्ष्णैः कर्णद्रोणकृपादिभिः॥ नानालिङ्गैः सुधौतागैर्मम पुत्रोऽल्पचेतनः। इह मे स्यात् परित्राणं पितेति स पुनः पुनः॥ इतयेवं विलपन् मन्ये नृशंसैर्भुवि पातितः।
en: Afflicted by Karna and Drona and Kripa and others, with exceedingly sharp shafts of various shape and well-polished tips, my son of smalll strength must have repeatedly thought-"My father will surely rescue me from this difficulty.” I think, when thus thinking of me he was felled to ground by those ruthless warriors.

sn: अथवा मत्प्रसूत: स स्वस्रीयो माधवस्य च॥ सुभद्रायां च सम्भूतो न चैवं वक्तुमर्हति।
en: "Or it may be, that being begotten by myself and being the nephew of Madhava, being born out of Subhadra's womb, he did not utter such exclamations.

sn: वज्रसारमयं नूनं हृदयं सुठलं मम॥ अपश्यतो दीर्घ बाहुं रक्ताक्षं यन्न दीर्यते।
en: Surely my heart is made of the hardest adamant. In as much as, it does not burst open for my not seeing that one of mighty arms and red eyes.

sn: कथं बाले महेष्वासा नृशंसा मर्मभेदिनः॥ स्वस्रीये वासुदेवस्य मम पुत्रेऽक्षिपञ्शरान्।
en: How could the fierce bowmen (of the Kaurava) hosts, ruthless and cruel, have sped their arrows capable of penetrating to the very vitals, at that boy of tender years, that son of mine and the nephew of Madhava?

sn: यो मां नित्यमदीनात्मा प्रत्युद्गम्याभिनन्दति॥ उपायान्तं रिपून हत्वा सोऽद्य मां किं न पश्यति।
en: He of generous soul who everyday used to come out to receive me when I returned after having slain my foes, will he not see me today?

sn: नूनं स पातितः शेते धरण्यां रुधिरोक्षितः॥ शोभयन् मेदिनीं गात्रैरादित्य इव पातितः।
en: Alas, he lies today prostrate on the field of battle weltering in his blood and enhancing the beauty of the earth with the splendour of his limbs and looking like the sun dropped from the firmament.

sn: सुभद्रामनुशोचामि या पुत्रपपलायिनम्॥ रणे विनिहतं श्रुत्वा शोकार्ता वै विनक्ष्यति।
en: I am indeed also destined to grieve for Subhadra who hearing that her unretreating son has been slain in battle, shall be struck with sorrow and shall give up her life?

sn: सुभद्रः वक्ष्यते किं मामभिमन्युमपश्यती॥ द्रौपदी चैव दुःखाते ते च वक्ष्यामि किं त्वहम्।
en: Oh! what will Subhadra say to me when she will not behold Abhimanyu (her son)! Alas, what also shall I tell to Draupadi overwhelmed with great grief?

sn: वज्रसारमयं नूनं हृदयं यन्न यास्यति॥ सहस्रधा वधूं दृष्ट्वा रुदतीं शोककर्शिताम्।
en: Surely my heart is made of the hardest adamant, in as much as it will not be splintered into thousand fragments when I shall behold my daughter-in-law (Abhimanyu's wife), bewail, afflicted with the burden of her grief.

sn: हप्तानां धार्तराष्ट्राणां सिंहनादो मया श्रुतः॥ युयुत्सुश्चापि कृष्णेन श्रुतो वीरानुपालभन्।
en: I heard indeed the war-cries of the Dhritarashtras, elated with pride and Krishna also heard Yuyutsu admonishing the heroes in the following terms.

sn: अशक्रुवन्तो बीभत्सुं बालं हत्वा महारथाः॥ किं मोदध्यवमधर्मज्ञाः पाण्डवं दृश्यतां बलम्।
en: 0 mighty car-warriors, not being able to defeat Vibhatsu and slaying this boy of tender years. What do you rejoice? O inost unrighteous ones, now shall you feel the mighty of the son of Pandu.

sn: किं तयोर्विप्रियं कृत्वा केशवार्जुनयोर्मधे॥ सिंहवन्नदथ प्रीताः शोककाल उपस्थिते। आगमिष्यति वः क्षिप्रं फलं पापस्य कर्मणः॥ अधर्मो हि कृतस्तीव्रः कथं स्यादफलश्चिरम्।
en: Having done an injury to Keshava and Arjuna in battle why do you roar like lions in delight. Verily your hour for grief has come. The fruits of you sinful acts will soon overtake you all. went away, You have committed a heinous crime not long will it delay in bearing the ripe fruit for you!'

sn: इति तान् परिभाषन् वै वैश्यापुत्रो महामतिः॥ अपायाच्छस्त्रमुत्सृज्य कोपदुःखसमन्वितः।
en: Having spoken to them (the enemy) thus, the highly intelligent son of a Vaishya went away, leaving aside his weapons and leaving the Kauravas with wrath and sorrow.

sn: किमर्थमेतन्नाख्यातं त्वया कृष्ण रणे मम॥ अधाक्षं तानहं क्रूरांस्तदा सर्वान् महारथान्।
en: Why, O Krishna, did you not tell me all this in the course of fight? I would then have burnt down all those cruel car-warriors of the enemy's host.

sn: संजय उवाच पुत्रशोकार्दितं पार्थं ध्यायन्तं साश्रुलोचनम्॥ निगृह्य वासुदेवस्तं पुत्राधिभिरभिप्लुतम्। मैवमित्यब्रवीत् कृष्णस्तीव्रशोकसमन्वितम्॥
en: Sanjaya said Thereafter the son of Vasudeva, consoling Pritha's (Arjuna) who overwhelmed with sorrow on account of his son, was exceedingly thoughtful, whose eyes were overflowing with tears and who, indeed, was afflicted by the grief generated by the slaughter of his son, said to him, "Do you not give way to grief."

sn: सर्वेषामेष वै पन्थाः शूराणामनिवर्तिनाम्। क्षत्रियाणां विशेषेण येषां युद्धेन जीविका॥
en: This indeed is the inevitable fate of all those heroes who never think of retreating. Specially of the Kshatriyas who live by war. Of unretreating heroes fighting in battle, this.

sn: एष वै युध्यमानानां शूराणामनिवर्तिनाम्। विहिता सर्वशास्त्रज्ञैर्गतिर्मतिमतां वर॥
en: O foremost of intelligent beings, has been specified to be the finale by those who are conversant with the meanings of our sacred scriptures. Death in battle is the inevitable fate of heroes who do not fly away from the field.

sn: ध्रुवं हि युद्धे मरणं शूराणामनिवर्तिनाम्। गतः पुण्यकृतां लोकानभिमन्यु संशयः॥
en: Undoubtedly Abhimanyu has gone to the regions of those who perform pious deeds; and, O foremost of the Bharatas, even this is coveted by all heroes.

sn: एतच्च सर्ववीराणां काक्षितं भरतर्षभ। संग्रामेऽभिमुखो मृत्युं प्राप्नुयादिति मानद॥
en: O Bharata, you are renowned for honouring others, listen that all chivalrous persons are passionate and consider it their prime objective to die while facing bravely the enemy.

sn: स च वीरान् रणे हत्वा राजपुत्रान् महाबलान्। वीरैराकाइक्षितं मृत्युं सम्प्रापतोऽभिमुखं रणे॥
en: That they may fall in battle facing their enemies. As regards Abhimanyu, he, having slain in battle many heroic and mighty princes.

sn: मा शुचः पुरुषव्याघ्र पूर्वैरेष सनातनः। धर्मकृद्भिः कृतो धर्मः क्षत्रियाणां रणे क्षयः॥
en: Hath reaped that death in battle which is so much desired by the heroes, O foremost of men, do not lament. The ancient sages have specified this to be the enduring merit of the Kshatriyas, viz., their fall in battle.

sn: इमे ते भ्रातरः सर्वे दीना भरतसत्तम। त्वयि शोकसमाविष्टे नृपाश्च सुहृदस्तव॥
en: O foremost of the Bharatas, these your brothers are highly distressed. As also these monarchs and these your relatives, beholding you plunged in sorrow.

sn: एतांश्च वचसा साम्ना समाश्वासय मानद। विदितं वेदितव्यं ते न शोकं कर्तुमर्हसि॥
en: "O bestower of honour, do you console them with comforting speech. Everything worthy of being know is known to you. It behoves you not to indulge in grief.”

sn: एवमाश्वासितः पार्थः कृष्णेनाद्भुतकर्मणा। ततोऽव्रबीत् तदा भ्रातृन् सर्वान् पार्थः सगद्गदान्॥
en: Thus consoled by Krishna of wonderful deeds, the son of Pritha (Arjuna) said to all his brothers these words in a voice choked with griefस दीर्घबाहुः पृथ्वंसो दीर्घराजीवलोचनः।

sn: अभिमन्युर्यथावृत्तः श्रोतुमिच्छाम्यहं तथा॥
en: O lord of Earth, that mighty-armed one, that one possessed of eyes large lake lotus petals namely Abhimanyu, how he fought, I desire to know?

sn: सनागस्यन्दनहयान् द्रक्ष्यध्वं निहतान् मया। संग्रामे सानुबन्धांस्तान् मम पुत्रस्य वैरिणः॥
en: You will see that, I will consume the enemy with their elephants, chariois and steeds in battle all those opponents of my son together with all their blood relations.

sn: कथं च वः कृतास्त्राणां सर्वेषां शस्त्रपाणिनाम्।। सौभद्रो निधनं गच्छेद वर्जिणापि समागतः॥
en: You all are accomplished in the use of weapons and are even now armed with weapons. How then could Subhadra's son be slain in battle, even if it were the wielder of the thunder-bolt whom he might have encountered?

sn: यद्येवमहमज्ञास्यमशक्तान् रक्षणे मम। पुत्रस्य पाण्डुपञ्चालान् मया गुप्तो भवेत् ततः॥
en: Alas, if I had known that the Pandavas and the Panchalas would be incompetent to protect my son in battle, myself would then have protected him.

sn: कथं च वो रथस्थानां शरवर्षाणि मुञ्चताम्। नीतोऽभिमन्युनिधनं कदर्थीकृत्य वः परैः॥
en: You were all then on your chariots and were shooting your arrows; how could then Abhimanyu be slain by the enemy spreading havoc in your troops?

sn: अहो वः पौरुषं नास्ति न च वोऽस्ति पराक्रमः। यत्राभिमन्युः समरे पश्यतां वो निपातितः॥
en: Alas, you possess no manliness! you have no prowess. Inasmuch as even before your very sight Abhimanyu was felled in battle.

sn: आत्मानमेव गहेयं यदहं वै सुदुर्बलान्। युष्मानाज्ञाय निर्यातो भीरूनकृतनिश्चयान्॥
en: It is better I should blame myself, since knowing you all to be cowards, sneaking and irresolute, I went away.

sn: आहोस्विद् भूषणार्थाय वर्म शस्त्रायुधानि वः। वाचस्तु वक्तुं संसत्सु मम पुत्रमरक्षताम्॥
en: Alas! are your armours, weapons, offensive and defensive, mere decorations of your persons? Are your eloquence mere empty words suited to an assembly only? For, you all failed to protect my son.

sn: एवमुक्त्वा ततो वाक्यं तिष्ठंश्चापवरासिमान्। न स्माशक्यत बीभत्सुः केनचित्प्रसमीक्षितुम्॥
en: Having spoken these words, Arjuna sat down armed with his bow and excellent sword. Then none was able to look at Vibhatsu.

sn: तमन्तकमिव क्रुद्धं नि:श्वसन्तं मुहुर्मुहुः। पुत्रशोकाभिसंतप्तमश्रुपूर्णमुखं तदा॥
en: Who then resembled the enraged destroyer, repeatedly drawing long and heavy sighs. Then his friends could not speak to Arjuna or look at him who was burning with the grief on account of his son's death and whose countenance was then over-flooded with tears.

sn: न भाषितुं शक्नुवन्ति द्रष्टुं वा सुहृदोऽर्जुनम्। अन्यत्र वासुदेवाद्वा ज्येष्ठाद्वा पाण्डुनन्दनात्॥
en: Except the son of Vasudeva or the eldest son of Pandu, none then ventured to speak to Arjuna.

sn: सर्वास्ववस्थासु हितावर्जुनस्य मनोनुगौ। बहुमानात् प्रियत्वाच्च तावेनं वक्तुमर्हतः॥
en: These two (Yudhishthira and Krishna) were always agreeable to Arjuna. These two were only competent to address him all occasions, in as much as they were held in great veneration and dear love.

sn: ततस्तं पुत्रशोकेन भृशं पीडितमानसम्। राजीवलोचनं कुद्धं राजा वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Then the king addressed the following words to that one possessed of eyes like lotus petals, whose heart was then aching with the sorrow caused by the (untimely) demise of his son and who was excited to the highest pitch of fury. on

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच त्वयि याते महाबाहो संशप्तकबलं प्रति। प्रयत्नमकरोत् तीव्रमाचार्यो ग्रहणे मम॥
