en: Yudhishthira said When, O mighty-armed one, you had gone against the Samshaptaka hosts, the preceptor Drona exerted himself vigourously for capturing me.

sn: व्यूढानीका वयं द्रोणं वारयामः स्म सर्वशः। प्रतिव्यूह्य स्थानीकं यतमानं तथा रणे॥
en: We then began to resist Drona and his troops arrayed in order on all sides, by dispensing off our troops and car divisions in counter array and striving hard.

sn: स वार्यमाणो रथिभिर्मयि चापि सुरक्षिते। अस्मानभिजगामाशु पीडयन् निशितैः शरैः॥
en: Though he was thus resisted by many and though I was well protected, yet he began to smite us with agility, afflicting us with his sharp shafts.

sn: ते पीड्यमाना द्रोणेन द्रोणानीकं न शक्नुमः। प्रतिवीक्षितुमप्याजौ भेत्तुं तत् कुत एव तु॥
en: My troops then, thus afflicted by Drona, were not even able, in battle, to look at his divisions what to speak of the thought of breaking through them!

sn: वयं त्वप्रतिमं वीर्ये सर्वे सौभद्रमात्मजम्। उक्तवन्तः स्म तं तात भिन्ध्यनीकमिति प्रभो॥
en: Then we all, O sire, spoke to Subhadra's son, who was unequalled in his prowess, saying-'O lord, do you break through these divisions of the enemy.'

sn: स तथा नोदितोऽस्माभिः सदश्व इव वीर्यवान्। असह्यपि तं भारं वोदुमेवोपचक्रमे॥
en: That highly puissant hero then thus urged on by ourselves, like a good horse, prepared himself to take that burden upon himself, however unbearable it might have been for him.

sn: स तवास्त्रोपदेशेन वीर्येण च समन्वितः। प्राविशत् तद्बलं बालः सुपर्ण इव सागरम्॥
en: Then that boy of tender years, endued with energy and possessed of the knowledge of weapons received from you, broke through that array, like Suparna entering into the ocean.

sn: तेऽनुयाता वयं वीरं सात्वतीपुत्रमाहवे। प्रवेष्टकामास्तेनैव येन स प्राविशच्चमूम्॥
en: Then we followed that hero in battle, that son of a daughter of the Satvata race, desirous of entering the hostile ranks even through the path he then opened for us.

sn: ततः सैन्धवको राजा क्षुद्रस्तात जयद्रथः। वरदानेन रुद्रस्य सर्वान् नः समवारयत्॥
en: Then alas, O sire, the puny ruler of the Sindhus, king Jayadratha resisted us all, through the virtue of a boon received from the god Rudra (Mahadeva).

sn: ततो द्रोणः कृपः कर्णो द्रौणिः कौसल्य एव च। कृतवर्मा च सौभद्रं षड् रथाः पर्यवारयन्॥
en: Thereupon Drona, Kripa, Karna, Drona's son, the king of the Kosalas and Kritavarman-these six car-warriors surrounded the son of Subhadra.

sn: परिवार्य तु तैः सर्वैर्युधि वालो महारथैः। यतमानः परं शक्त्या बहुभिर्विरधीकृतः॥
en: Thus surrounded by all those mighty carwarriors in battle, that boy though striking to the best of his abilities, was deprived of the use of his car, by the tremendous odds he was fighting against.

sn: ततो दौःशासनिः क्षिप्रं तथा तैर्विरथीकृतम्। संशयं परमं प्राप्य दिष्टान्तेनाभ्ययोजयत्॥
en: Thus when Abhimanyu was deprived of the use of his car by those warriors, Dushasana's son, who himself was involved in great catastrophe, succeeded, as fate would have it, in making Abhimanyu see his end.

sn: स तु हत्वा सहस्राणि नराश्वरथदन्तिनाम्। अष्टौ रथसहस्राणि नव दन्तिशतानि च॥
en: Having slain thousands of men, steeds, carwarriors and tusked elephants and eight thousands car-warriors and nine hundred elephants.

sn: राजपुत्रसहस्रे द्वे वीरांश्चालक्षितान् बहून्। वृद्धलं च राजानं स्वर्गेणाजौ प्रयोज्य ह॥
en: Two thousand princes and many other unknown heroes and also having dispatched king Brihadbala to Heaven.

sn: ततः परमधर्मात्मा दिष्टान्तमुपजग्मिवान्। एतावदेव निवृत्तमस्माकं शोकवर्धनम्॥
en: That one of highly illustrious soul through Destiny, attained his own end. Thus everything that now burns us with grief, has taken place.

sn: स चैवं पुरुषव्याघ्रः स्वर्गलोकमवाप्तवान्। ततोऽर्जुनो वचः श्रुत्वा धर्मराजेन भाषितम्॥
en: That foremost of men has also in his way, ascended to paradise.” Sanjay Said-Thus Arjuna hearing the word spoken by the virtuous king Yudhishthira.

sn: हा पुत्र इति निःश्वस्य व्यथितोन्यपतद् भुवि। विषण्णवदनाः सर्वे परिवार्य धनंजयम्॥
en: And saying, O my son! and sighing like a furnace, fell down on the earth in great distress. Then every one present, with melancholy countenances sat surrounding Dhananjaya.

sn: नेत्रैरनिमिषैर्दीनाः प्रत्यवेक्षन् परस्परम्। प्रतिलभ्य ततः संज्ञा वासविः क्रोधमूच्छितः॥
en: And highly distressed they began to gaze vacantly at one another with winkless eyes. Then regaining his consciousness and burning with rage, the son of Vasava.

sn: कम्पमानो ज्वरेणेव निःश्वसंश्च मुहुर्मुहुः। पार्णि पाणौविनिष्पिष्य श्वसमानोऽश्रुनेत्रवान्॥
en: Shivering as if with fever and repeatedly sighing and squeezing his hands and drawing deep breaths and with eyes flooded with tears and rolling his eyes like one mad, said these

sn: अर्जुन उवाच उन्मत्त इव विप्रेक्षन्निदं वचनमब्रवीत्। सत्यं वः प्रतिजानामि श्वोऽस्मि हन्ता जयद्रथम्। न चेद् वधभयाद् भीतो धार्तराष्ट्रान् प्रहास्यति॥
en: Arjuna said I tell you this for sooth that, tomorrow I will slay Jayadrath, provided that, afraid of being slain, he does not forsake the sons of Dhritarashtra.

sn: न चास्माशरणं गच्छेत् कृष्णं वा पुरुषोत्तमम्। भवन्तं वा महाराज श्वोऽस्मि हन्ता जयद्रथम्॥
en: Or seek our refuge or that of Krishna the foremost of all male being or that of yourself, O monarch. I will surely slay Jayadratha tomorrow.

sn: धार्तराष्ट्रप्रियकरं मयि विस्मृतसौहृदम्। पापं बालवधे हेतुं श्वोऽस्मि हन्ता जयद्रथम्॥
en: Tomorrow will I slay Jayadratha who forgetting his friendship for me, has been doing good to the sons of Dhritarashtra and who has become instrumental in bringing about the slaughter of my boy.

sn: रक्षमाणाश्च तं संख्ये ये मां योत्स्यन्ति केचन। अपि द्रोणकृपौ राजन् छादयिष्यामि ताञ्छरैः॥
en: Desirous of protecting him in battle whosoever shall fight with me, I will cover him, O king, with my arrows, be he Drona himself or Kripa.

sn: यद्येतदेवं संग्रामे न कुर्यां पुरुषर्षभाः। मा स्म पुण्यकृतां लोकान् प्राप्नुयां शूरसम्मतान्॥
en: O foremost of men, O best of heroes, if I do not do tomorrow in battle what I promise to do, then let me not ever attain to the regions which the righteous attain after death.

sn: ये लोका मातृहतॄणां ये चापि पितृघातिनाम्। गुरुदारगतानां ये पिशुनानां च ये सदा॥ साधूनसूयतां ये च ये चापि परिवादिनाम्। ये च निक्षेपहर्तृणां ये च विश्वासघातिनाम्॥ भुक्तपूर्वां स्त्रियं ये च विन्दतामघशंसिनाम्। ब्रह्मघ्नानां च ये लोका ये च गोघातिनामपि॥ पायसं वा यवान्नं वा शाकं कृसरमेव वा। संयावापूपमांसानि ये च लोका वृथाश्नताम्॥
en: Those regions which are allotted to those who ravish their own mothers, to those who slay their fathers, who violate their preceptor's beds and who are malicious; those regions which are reserved for those who harbour hatred against the righteous, who speak maliciously of others, who appropriate the wealth entrusted with them and who betray their trusts; those regions that are for them who abuse others' wives enjoyed by them before or for them that slay Brahmanas or for them that slaughter the kine or for them that drink payasas or eat food prepared from barley or herbs or articles prepared from milk, sesamum and rice and Pupas and other kinds of cakes or meat, without having first offered them to the gods.

sn: तानन्हायाधिगच्छेयं न चेद्धन्यां जयद्रथम्। वेदाध्यायिनमत्यर्थं संशितं वा द्विजोत्तमम्॥ अवमन्यमानो यान् याति वृद्धान् साधून् गुरुंस्तथा। स्पृशतो ब्राह्मणं गां च पादेनाग्निं च या भवेत्॥ याऽप्सु श्लेष्म पुरीषं च मूत्रं वा मुञ्चतां गतिः। तां गच्छेयं गतिं कष्टां न चेद्धन्यां जयद्रथम्॥
en: Even those regions shall I attain to, if I do not slay Jayadratha. Those regions to which they go who contemn the Brahmanas devoted to the study of the Vedas or otherwise deserving of veneration or those that are senior in years or those that are senior in years or those that are pious or those that are preceptors, (even those region shall mine if I do not slay Jayadratha). That end which becomes theirs who touch the Brahmanas and the fire with their feet, that end which becomes theirs, who throw phlegm or excretions on and discharge urine in water, even that most miserable end shall be mine, if indeed I do not slay Jayadratha tomorrow.

sn: नग्नस्य नायमानस्य या च वन्ध्यातिथेर्गतिः। उत्कोचिनां मृषोक्तीनां वञ्चकानां च या गतिः॥ आत्मापहारिणां या च या च मिथ्याभिशंसिनाम्। भृत्यैः संदिश्यमानानां पुत्रदाराश्रितैस्तथा॥ असंविभज्य क्षुद्राणां या गतिर्मिष्टमश्नताम्। तां गच्छेयं गति घोरां न चेद्धन्यां जयद्रथम्॥
en: That end that overtakes him who bathes naked in water or him who does not hospitably entertain a guest; that and that overtakes them who accept bribes, speak falsehoods and deceive and cheat men; that end that overtakes them who offend against their own souls or who falsely utter praises, that end ihat overtakes low wretches who eat sweetmeats before servants, and wives and dependents without giving them a share of them, may that end also overtake me if I do not slay Jayadratha.

sn: संश्रितं चापि यस्त्यक्त्वा साधुं तद्वचने रतम्। न विभर्ति नृशंसात्मा निन्दते चोपकारिणम्॥ अर्हते प्रातिवेश्याय श्राद्धं यो न ददाति च। अनर्हेभ्यश्च यो दद्याद् वृषलीपतये तथा॥ मद्यपो भिन्नमर्यादः कृतघ्नो भर्तृनिन्दकः। तेषां गतिमियां क्षिप्रं न चेद्धन्यां जयद्रथम्॥
en: That end which overtakes the cruel-hearted wretch who without maintaining a pious and sons obedient protege casts him off or him who without giving a deserving neighbour the offerings in a sraddha, gives them to one undeserving of them; that end that overtakes them who accept in marriage Vrishalis; that end which becomes his who indulges in wine, his who contemns those that are worthy of veneration or his who is ungrateful or his who speaks evil of his brethren, that end shall also soon overtake me if I do not slay Jayadratha.

sn: भुञ्जानानां तु सव्येन उत्सङ्गे चापि खादताम्। पालाशमासनं चैव तिन्दुकैर्दन्तधावनम्॥ ये चावर्जयतां लोकाः स्वपतां च तथोषसि।
en: (If I fail in killing Jayadratha) the hellish living obtained by the people eating meal through left hand, put the food on lap while eating, not abandon the seat of Palasha and brush of Tenduki shall be accepted by me.

sn: शीतभीताश्च ये विप्रा रणभीताश्च क्षत्रियाः॥ एककूपोदकग्रामे वेदध्वनिविवर्जिते। षण्मासं तत्र वसतां तथा शास्त्रं विनिन्दताम्॥ दिवामैथुनिनां चापि दिवसेषु च शेरते। अगारदाहिनां चैव गरदानां च ये मताः॥ अग्न्यातिथ्यविहीनाश्च गोपानेषु च विघ्नदाः। रजस्वला सेवयन्तः कन्यां शुल्केन दायिनः॥ या च वै बहुयाजिनां ब्राह्मणानां श्ववृत्तिनाम्। आस्यमैथुनिकानां च ये दिवा मैथुने रताः॥ ब्राह्मणस्य प्रतिश्रुत्य यो वै लोभाद् ददाति न। तेषां गतिं गमिष्यामि श्वो न हन्यां जयद्रथम्॥
en: If I fail in killing Jayadratha tomorrow, the status of living or the insults as befallen on the persons described hereinafter shall be accepted by me. These persons are-the Brahmins who fear of winter, the Kshatriya who fears of battle, the village where single well is dug for drinking water and where Vedic hymns never chanted-the persons living in such village for six mouths, the people who condemn the scriptures, who cohabit and sleep in the day, who set others' home on fire and poison them, who seldom arrange offering and entertain guests, who disturb cows to drink water, who enjoy intercourse with wife during her marriage by collecting fee, who make numerous clients and live on service even after born in Brahmin family, who enjoy intercourse unnatural way (insertion of penis in mouth) or do intercourse in the day and who promise to give something to any Brahmin but avoid lateron under influence of greed.

sn: धर्मादपेता ये चान्ये मया नात्रानुकीर्तिताः। ये चानुकीर्तितास्तेषां गतिं क्षिप्रमवाप्नुयाम्॥ यदि व्युष्टामिमां रात्रिं श्वो न हन्यां जयद्रथम्।
en: The ends of all those wretched persons whom I have not enumerated, as also of those whom I have here mentioned, shall soon overtake me, if, after this night passing away, I do not slay Jayadratha tomorrow.

sn: इमां चाप्यपरां भूयः प्रतिज्ञां मे निबोधत॥ यद्यस्मिन्त्रहते पापे सूर्योऽस्तमुपयास्यति। इहैव सम्प्रवेष्टाऽहं ज्वलितं जातवेदसम्॥
en: Now listen to another oath of mine. If tomorrow's sun sets before I succeed in slaying this sinful wretch, then even here shall I enter into a blazing fire.

sn: असुरसुरमनुष्या: पक्षिणो वोरगा वा पितृजनिचरा वा ब्रह्मदेवर्षयो वा। चरमचरमपीदं यत्परं चापि तस्मात् तदपि ममरिपुं तं रक्षितुं नैव शक्ताः॥
en: Asuras and the celestials, mortals, winged creatures, reptiles or ancestral manes, rangers of the night, Brahmanical or celestials sages, the mobile and immobile things and beings and what other things there may be on the face of the earth, even all these will not be able to protect that foe of mine.

sn: यदि विशति रसातलं तदग्यं वियदपि देवपुरं दितेः पुरं वा। तदपि शरशतैरहं प्रभाते भृशमभिमन्युरिपोः शिरोऽभिहर्ता॥
en: If he enters the nether regions or ascends to the skies or repairs to the celestial regions or to the dominion of the Daityas, I will still, with a group of hundred, shafts, cut-off the head of Abhimanyu's enemy, when this night passed away."

sn: संजय उवाच एवमुक्त्वा विचिक्षेप गाण्डीवं सव्यदक्षिणम्। तस्य शब्दमतिक्रम्य धनुः शब्दोऽस्पृशद् दिवम्॥
en: Sanjaya Said Having spoken these words, Arjuna began to twang his bow with both his right and left arms. Rising above the voice of Arjuna, the sound of the twanging bow touched even the very heavens.

sn: अर्जुनेन प्रतिज्ञाते पाञ्चजन्यं जनार्दनः। प्रदध्मौ तत्रं संकुद्धो देवदत्तं च फाल्गुनः॥
en: When Arjuna had thus taken that oath Janardana blew the conch Panchajanya and Phalguna also excited with rage blew his conch Devadatta.

sn: स पाञ्चजन्योऽच्युतवक्त्रवायुना भृशं सुपूर्णोदरनिःसृत ध्वनिः। जगत सपाताल वियद्दिगीश्वरं प्रकम्पयामास युगात्यये यथा॥
en: Then that conch Panchajanya being filled with the breath of the undeteriorating Krishna, emitted a loud sound and that sound then caused the universe, the nether regions, the heavens and the quarters O lord, to tremble, as if the end of a Yuga had come.

sn: ततो वादित्रघोषाश्च प्रादुरासन् सहस्रशः। सिंहनादश्च पाण्डूनां प्रतिज्ञाते महात्मना॥
en: Then when the high-souled Arjuna had taken that oath, sounds of thousands of musical instruments and fierce war-cries, arose from the encampment of the Pandavas.

sn: संजय उवाच श्रुत्वा तु तं महाशब्दं पाण्डूनां जयगृद्धिनाम्। चारैः प्रवेदिते तत्र समुत्थाय जयद्रथः॥
en: Sanjaya said Having heard the loud uproar created by the Pandavas desirous of victory and having ascertained through spies the cause thereof, Jayadratha then rose up.

sn: शोकसम्मूढहृदयो दुःखेनाभिपरिप्लुतः। मज्जमान इवागाधे विपुले शोकसागरे॥
en: With a heart confounded with grief and overwhelmed with affliction and like one sinking in an extensive and deep sea of sorrow.

sn: अगाम समिति राज्ञां सैन्धवो विमृशन् बहु। स तेषां नरदेवानां सकाशे पर्यदेवयन्॥
en: Then that ruler of the Sindhus, having reflected for a long while, proceeded to the assembly of the kings; there, before the assemblage of monarchs, expressing his grief.

sn: अभिमन्योः पितुर्भीतः सव्रीडो वाक्यमब्रवीत्। योऽसौ पाण्डो:किल क्षेत्रे जातः शक्रेण कामिना॥
en: And afraid of the father of Abhimanyu and overwhelmed with shame, he spoke these words-"He, who was begotten upon the wife of Pandu by the lustful Indra.

sn: स निनीषति दुर्बुद्धिर्मा किलैकं यमक्षयम्। तत् स्वस्ति वोऽस्तु यास्यामि स्वगृहं जीवितेप्सया।।५
en: That one of perverse intellect is desirous of dispatching me to the abode of Death. Good be tide you all, I shall now go back to my home out of a desire for saving my life.

sn: अथवास्त्रप्रतिबलास्त्रात मां क्षत्रियर्षभाः। पार्थेन प्रार्थिनं वीरास्ते संदत्त ममाभयम्॥
en: Or, O foremost of the Kshatriyas, do you all protect me with the power of your weapons; O heroes, the son of Pritha (Arjuna) seeks to slay me; do you give me assurances of safety.

sn: द्रोणदुर्योधनकृपाः कर्णमद्रेशबाह्निकाः। दुःशासनादयः शक्तास्त्रातुं मामन्तकार्दितम्॥ किमङ्ग पुनरेकेन फाल्गुनेन जिघांसता। न त्रायेयुभवन्तो मां समस्ताः पतयः क्षितेः॥
en: Drona, Duryodhana, Kripa, Karna, the rulers of the Madras and the Balhikas and Dushasana and others, these are competent to save even one who is seized by Death himself. Why then should not all these rulers of earth, united together, be able to protect me, when I are threatened by Phalguna who seeks to slay me?

sn: प्रहर्षे पाण्डवेयानां श्रुत्वा मम महद् भयम्। सीदन्ति मम गात्राणि मुमूर्षोरिव पार्थिवाः॥
en: Having heard the rejoicings of the sons of Pandu, I am struck with fear and O ruler of men, my limbs are loosing strength, like those of one on the verge of death.

sn: वधो नूनं प्रतिज्ञातो मम गाण्डीवधन्वना। तथा हि हृष्टाः क्रोशन्ति शोककाले स्म पाण्डवाः॥
en: Without doubt, the wielder of the bow Gandiva has promised to slay me; therefore it is that, the Pandavas are shouting with delight at a time when they should grieve.

sn: तन्न देवा न गन्धर्वा नासुरोरगराक्षसाः। उत्सहन्तेऽन्यथाकर्तुं कुत एव नराधिपाः॥
en: Even the Gandharavas, the Asuras the reptiles and the Rakshasas, cannot dare baffle a vow of Arjuna, what to speak of the rulers of men?

sn: तस्मानमामनुजानीत भद्रं वोऽस्तु नरर्षभाः। अदर्शनं गमिष्यामि न मां द्रक्ष्यन्ति पाण्डवाः॥
en: Therefore foremost of men, do you all accord me your permission (to go home); may good betide you; I shall go concealed and the Pandavas will not be able to detect me."

sn: एवं विलपमानं तं भयाद् व्याकुलचेतसम्। आत्मकार्यगरीयस्त्वाद् राजा दुर्योधनोऽब्रवीत्॥
en: Him thus lamenting with heart confounded with the burden of fear, king Duryodhana ever devoted to his own personal interests, said these wordsन भेतव्यं नरव्याघ्र को हि त्वां पुरुषर्षभ।

sn: मध्ये क्षत्रियवीराणां तिष्ठन्तं प्रार्थयेद् युधि॥
en: O foremost among men, you should entertain no fear. What person, O beat of men, can seek to slay you, when you stand in the midst of the Kshatriya heroes.

sn: अहं वैकर्तनः कर्णश्चित्रसेनो विविंशतिः। भूरिश्रवाः शल: शल्यो वृषसेनो दुरासदः॥ पुरुमित्रो जयो भोजः काम्बोजश्च सुदक्षिणः। सत्यव्रतो महाबाहुर्विकर्णो दुर्मुखश्च ह॥
en: a from your

sn: दुःशासनः सुबाहुश्च कालिङ्गश्चाप्युदायुधः। विन्दानुविन्दावावन्त्यौ द्रोणो द्रौणिश्च सौबलः॥ एते चान्ये च बहवो नानाजनपदेश्वराः। ससैन्यास्त्वाभियास्यन्ति व्येतु ते मानसो ज्वरः॥
en: Myself, Vikartana's son Karna, Chitrasena, Vivinshati, Bhurishravas, Shala, Shalya, the invincible Vrishasena, Purumitra, Jaya, Bhoja, Sudakshina the ruler of the Kambojas, the mighty armed Satyavrata, Vikarna and Durmukha, Dushasana, Subahu, the ruler of the Kalingas with arms uplifted, Vinda and Anuvinda of Avanti, Drona and the son of Drona, Subala's son, these and many other rulers of various countries, attended with all their troops, shall exert themselves in protecting you. Let the fever of fear be driven away mind.

sn: त्वं चापि रथिनां श्रेष्ठः स्वयं शूरोऽमिताते। स कथं पाण्डवेयेभ्यो भयं पश्यसि सैन्धव॥
en: You also, O you of unrivalled effulgence, are the foremost of all heroes; why then, O ruler of the Sindhus, do you entertain fear from the Pandavas.

sn: अक्षौहिण्यो दशैका च मदीयास्तव रक्षणे। यत्ता योत्स्यन्ति मा भैस्त्वं सैन्धव व्येतु ते भयम्॥
en: These ten and one Akshouhini of my troops shall strive their best for protecting you. Be not afraid, O ruler of the Sindhus. Let fear be driven away from your heart.

sn: संजय उवाच एवमाश्वासितो राजन् पुत्रेण तव सैन्धवः। दुर्योधनेन सहितो द्रोण रात्रावुपागमत्॥
en: Sanjaya said Thus comforted by your son Duryodhana, the ruler of the Sindhus, o king accompanied by the former, went that very night, to the camp of Drona.

sn: उपसंग्रहणं कृत्वा द्रोणाय स विशाम्पते। उपोपविश्य प्रणतः पर्यपृच्छदिदं तदा॥
en: Then saluting Drona by touching his feet and having bowed down to him, Jayadratha, O ruler of men, sat down with humility and then asked the following question.

sn: निमित्ते दूरपातित्वे लघुत्वे दृढवेधने। मम ब्रवीतु भगवान् विशेष फाल्गुनस्य च॥
en: “Tell me, O illustrious one, the difference between myself and Phalguna, as regards hitting the aim, hitting it from a distance, lightness of hands and the force of strokes.

sn: विद्याविशेषमिच्छामि ज्ञातुमाचार्य तत्त्वतः। अर्जुनस्यात्मनश्चैव याथातथ्यं प्रचक्ष्व मे॥
en: O preceptor, I want to know exactly the difference, as regards proficiency in arms between myself and Arjuna. Say it to me truly."

sn: द्रोण उवाच सममाचार्यकं तात तव चैवार्जुनस्य च। योगाद् दुःखोषितत्वाच्च तस्मात्त्वत्तोऽधिकोऽर्जुनः॥२५
en: Drona said As regards teaching you and Arjuna, O sire, have both received an equal share. But through Yoga and through the effects of hardship he had undergone, he has become superior to yourself.

sn: न तु ते युधि संत्रासः कार्यः पार्थात् कथञ्चन। अहं हि रक्षिता तात भयात्त्वां नात्र संशयः॥
en: In battle, you should never entertain any fear from Pritha's son Arjuna, I am surely your protector, O sire, from ali dangers.

sn: न हि माहुगुप्तस्य प्रभवन्त्यमरा अपि। व्यूहयिष्यामि तं व्यूहं यं पार्थो न तरिष्यति॥
en: Even the very gods cannot obtain victory over him who is protected with the strength of my arms. I will (tomorrow) form such an array which Partha will never be able to reach the end of.

sn: तस्माद् युद्ध्यस्वमा भैस्त्वं स्वधर्ममनुपालय। पितृपैतामहं मार्गमनुयाहि महारथ॥
en: Therefore do you fight and be not afraid in the least and observe (scrupulously) the duties of your order. O foremost of car-warriors, do you follow the path chalked out by your fathers and grandfathers.

sn: अधीत्य विधिवद् वेदानग्नयः सुहुतास्त्वया। इष्टं च बहुभिर्यज्ञैर्न ते मृत्युभयङ्करः॥
en: Having studied the various branches of knowledge, you have burnt due offerings on the fire, you have also celebrated various sacrifices; death therefore should not be an object of apprehension to you.

sn: दुर्लभं मानुषैर्मन्दैमहाभाग्यमवाप्यतु। भुजवीर्यार्जिताँल्लोकान् दिव्यान् प्राप्स्यस्यनुत्तमान्।।
en: (On the other hand), if you die you shall attain to that good fortune so difficult of being attained by the vile men, viz., you shall ascend to those excellent regions that are acquired by the strength of our arms.

sn: कुरुः पाण्डवाश्चैव वृष्णयोऽन्ये च मानवाः। अहं च सह पुत्रेण अध्रुवा इति चिन्त्यताम्॥
en: The Kurus, the Pandavas, the Vrishnis and other men and I and my son-think all these to be mortal and uncertain,

sn: पर्यायेण वयं सर्वे कालेन बलिना हताः। परलोकं गमिष्यामः स्वैः स्वैः कर्मभिरन्विताः॥
en: One after another, destroyed by the powerful God of Death, we shall go to the regions of the departed, carrying with us the fruits of our respective actions.

sn: तपस्तप्त्वा तु याँल्लोकान् प्राप्नुवन्ति तपस्विनः। क्षत्रधर्माश्रिता वीराः क्षत्रियाः प्राप्नुवन्ति तान्॥
en: Those regions to which the ascetics repair through their observance of ascetic austerities, even those regions the heroic Kshatriyas attain, by the observance of their own duties.”

sn: एवमाश्वासितो राजा भारद्वाजेन सैन्धवः। अपानुदद् भयं पार्थाद् युद्धाय च मनो दधे॥३४।
en: Thus then was the ruler of the Sindhus comforted by the son of Bharadvaja. He then dismissed (from his heart) all fears of Partha (Arjuna) and set his heart upon battle.

sn: ततः प्रहर्षः सैन्यानां तवाप्यासीद् विशाम्पते। वादित्राणां ध्वनिश्चोग्रः सिंहनादरवै: सह॥
en: Thereupon, O ruler of men, your warriors were filled with delight and the war-cries they then shouted out, became mingled with the terrible din of the musical instruments.

sn: संजय उवाच प्रतिज्ञाते तु पार्थेन सिन्धुराजवधे तदा। वासुदेवो महाबाहुर्धनंजयमभाषत॥
en: Sanjaya said After the son of Pritha (Arjuna) had promised to slay the ruler of the Sindhus, the mighty-armed son of Vasudeva addressed him sayingभ्रातॄणां मतमज्ञाय त्वया वाचा प्रतिश्रुतम्।

sn: सैन्धवं चास्मि हन्तेति तत्साहसमिदं कृतम्॥
en: “Only with the consent of your brothers (and without taking my advice), you have promised to slay the Sindhus king, saying-'I will slay Jayadratha tomorrow. This has been an act of rashness.

sn: असंमन्त्र्य मया सार्धमतिभारोऽयसमुद्यतः। कथं तु सर्वलोकस्य नावहास्या भवेमहि॥
en: Without taking my advice previously, you have drawn down a heavy burden on your shoulders. Alas! how now shall we escape from being the butt of redicule of all men.

sn: धार्तराष्ट्रस्य शिविरे मया प्रणिहिताश्चराः। त इमे शीघ्रमागम्य प्रवृत्तिं वेदयन्ति नः॥
en: I had deputed spies in the encampment of the sons of Dhristarastra. Those spies, returning soon furnished with this information.

sn: त्वया वै सम्प्रतिज्ञाते सिन्धुराजवधे प्रभो। सिंहनादः सवादित्रः सुमहानिह तैः श्रुतः॥
en: 'O Lord, when you had vowed the slaughter of the king of the Sindhus, they (the Kauravas) heard the war-cries mingled with din of musical instruments that then arose from our camp.

sn: तेन शब्देन वित्रस्ता धार्तराष्ट्राः ससैन्धवाः। नाकस्मात् सिंहनादोऽयमिति मत्वा व्यवस्थिताः॥
en: Terrified at that up-roar, the sons of Dhritarashtra together with all their relatives me and kinsmen, thought-these shouts are not without due causes' and they then waited (for what would ensue next).

sn: सुमहाशब्दसम्पात: कौरवाणां महाभुज) आसीन्नागाश्वपत्तीनां रथघोषश्च भैरवः॥
en: Then, O mighty-armed one, a great confused noise was created by the Kauravas and their elephants, steeds, infantry and the rattle of their car-wheels.

sn: अभिमन्योर्वधं श्रुत्वा ध्रुवमार्तो धनंजयः। रात्रौनिर्यास्यति क्रोधादिति मत्वा व्यवस्थिताः॥
en: 'Having been appraised of the slaughter of Abhimanyu, Dhananjaya sorely distressed will surely, in wrath, come out in the night desirous of battle.' Thinking even in the above manner, they stood prepared for battle.

sn: तैर्यतद्भिरियं सत्या श्रुता सत्यवतस्तव। प्रतिज्ञा सिन्धुराजस्य वधे राजीवलोचन॥
en: Thus when those vow-observing heroes were preparing for the battle, O you of eyes like lotus petals, they heard of the true vow you had taken for the slaughter of the Sindhu king.

sn: ततो विमनसः सर्वे त्रस्ताः क्षुद्रमृगा इव। आसन् सुयोधनामात्याः स च राजा जयद्रथः॥
en: Thereat the counsellors of Suyodhana all became depressed at heart and they then resembled weak animals struck with panic. Then king Jayadratha,

sn: अथोत्थाय सहामात्यैर्दीन: शिबिरमात्मनः। आयात् सौवीरसिन्धूनामीश्वरो भृशदुःखितः॥
en: The ruler of the Sindhus and the Sauviras, sorely afflicted with grief and melancholy, rose up and with his ministers retired to his tent.

sn: स मन्त्रकाले सम्मन्त्र्य सर्वां नैःश्रेयसी क्रियाम्। सुयोधनमिदं वाक्यमब्रवीद् राजसंसदि॥
en: Then in that time suitable for consultations, he consulted with them about the best remedial measure (against Arjuna's vow). And then repairing to the assembly of kings he said these words to Suyodhana.

sn: मामसो पुत्रहन्तेति श्वोऽभियाता धनंजयः। प्रतिज्ञातो हि सेनाया मध्ये तेन वधो मम॥
en: "He is the slayer of my son, thinking thus, tomorrow will Dhananjaya assault me. In the very midst of his troops, he has vowed to slay me.

sn: तां न देवा न गन्धर्वा नासुरोरगराक्षसाः। उत्सहन्तेऽन्यथा कर्तुं प्रतिज्ञां सव्यसाचिनः॥
en: Neither the Gods, nor the Gandharvas, nor the Asuras, nor the reptiles nor the Rakshasas would venture to baffle that Vow of Savyasachin (Arjuna).

sn: ते मां रक्षत संग्रामे मा वो मूर्ध्नि धनंजयः। पदं कृत्वाऽऽनुयाल्लक्ष्यं तस्मादत्र विधीयताम्॥
en: Do you all therefore protect me in battle. Let not Dhananjaya, placing his feet on your heads, succeeded in hitting his target. Let suitable arrangements be made.

sn: अथ रक्षा न मे संख्ये क्रियते कुरुनन्दन। अनुजानीहि मां राजन् गमिष्यामि गृहान् प्रति॥
en: On the other hand, O delighter of the Kurus, if you do not undertake to protect me in battle, permit me, O king, to go back to my home.”

sn: एवपुक्तस्त्ववाक्शीर्षो विमनाः स सुयोधनः। श्रुत्वा तं समयं तस्य ध्यानमेवान्वपद्यत॥
en: Thus spoken to, Suyodhana hang down his head and became depressed at heart. And ascertaining Jayadratha to be greatly terrified, he began to meditate (silently).

sn: तमार्तमभिसंप्रेक्ष्य राजा किल स सैन्धवः। मृदु चात्महितं चैव साक्षेपमिदमुक्तवान्॥
en: Then the ruler of the Shindhus seeing Duryodhana sorely afflicted, softly spoke these words, intended to conduce to his own welfare and good.

sn: नेह पश्यामि भवतां तथावीर्यं धनुर्धरम्। योऽर्जुनस्यास्त्रमस्त्रेण प्रतिहन्यान्महाहवे॥
en: "I do not find any bowman among you who is equal to Arjuna in prowess and who is capable of baffling the weapons of Arjuna in battle, with those of his own.

sn: वासुदेवसहायस्य गाण्डीवं धुन्वतो धनुः। कोऽर्जुनस्याग्रतस्तिष्ठेत् साक्षादपि शतक्रतुः॥
en: What person would dare stand before Arjuna who is supported by the son of Vasudeva and who wields the Gandiva bow? Even Indra of hundred sacrifices will not venture to do so!

sn: महेश्वरोऽपि पार्थेन श्रूयते योधितः पुरा। पदातिना महावीर्यो गिरौ हिमवति प्रभुः॥
en: It is said that the son of Pritha (Arjuna), on foot, fought with Almighty Mahesvara himself in days gone by, on the Himavat mountains.

sn: दानवानां सहस्राणि हिरण्यपुरवासिनाम्। जघानैकरथेनैव देवराजप्रचोदितः॥
en: Being commissioned by the lord of the celestials, he slew on a single chariot thousands of Danavas inhabiting the golden city.

sn: समायुक्तो हि कौन्तेयो वासुदेवेन धीमता। सामरानपि लोकांस्त्रींन् हन्यादिति मतिर्मम॥
en: That son of Kunti is now united with the intelligent son of Vasudeva. And I think that he is now competent to destroy the triune, world, with even the immortals therein!

sn: सोऽहमिच्छाम्यनुज्ञातुं रक्षितुं वा महात्मना। द्रोणेन सहपुत्रेण वीरेण यदि मन्यसे॥
en: So, may it please you, I desire to have either your permission to go home or to be protected by the high-souled Drona and his son, both endued with heroism."

sn: स राज्ञा स्वयमाचार्यो भृशमत्रार्थितोऽर्जुन। संविधानं च विहितं रथाश्च किल सज्जिताः॥
en: O Arjuna, thus addressed the king himself entreated the preceptor to undertake to protect Jayadratha. All remedial measures have been adopted; and chariots and steeds have been duly arranged.

sn: कर्णो भूरिश्रवा द्रोणिवृषसेनश्च दुर्जयः। कृपश्च मद्रराजश्च षडेतेऽस्य पुरोगमाः॥
en: Karna, Bhurisravas, the son of Drona, the invincible Vrishasena, Kripa and the ruler of the Madras these six warriors will station themselves in the van of their array.

sn: शकटः पद्मक्श्चा? व्यूहो द्रोणेन निर्मितः। पद्मकर्णिकमध्यस्थः सूचीपार्वे जयद्रथः॥
en: Drona has formed an array, half of which figures a car and half a lotus; inside that array there has been formed a minor array of the shape of an wedge, Jayadratha will stand in the middle of the lotus-like array and by the side of the other array.

sn: स्थास्यते रक्षितो वीरैः सिंधुराट् स सुदुर्मदः। धनुष्यस्त्रे च वीर्ये च प्राणे चैव तथौरसे॥
en: There will the invincible king of the Sindhus stand, being protected by those heroes. In handling the bow and other weapons, in prowess, in might and in their high extraction.

sn: अविषह्यतमा ह्येते निश्चिताः पार्थ षड्रथाः। एतानजित्वा षड् रथान् नैव प्राप्यो जयद्रथः॥
en: These six warriors, O Partha, are surely exceedingly difficult of being borne down, Without first vanquishing these six carwarriors, you cannot hope to reach Jayadratha.

sn: तेषामेकैकशो वीर्यं षण्णां त्वमनुचिन्तय। सहिता हि नरव्याघ्र न शक्या जेतुमञ्जसा॥
en: Think of the respective prowess of these six warriors. O foremost of men, when united together, they cannot be easily defeated.

sn: भूयस्तु मन्त्रयिष्यामि नीतिमात्महिताय वै। मन्त्रज्ञैः सचिवैः सार्धं सुद्भिः कार्यसिद्धये॥
en: Let us once again hold consultation with those versed in the use of weapons and with our own ministers and friends, to settle the course of action that should be adopted for our ! well-being and for the fruition of our aims.

sn: अर्जुन उवाच षड्थान् धार्तराष्ट्रस्य मन्यसे यान् बलाधिकान्। तेषां वीर्ये ममार्धेन न तुल्यमिति मे मतिः॥
en: Arjuna said Those six car-warriors of the Dhartarastra host whom you consider to be superior to me in strength, I think their prowess is not even equal to half that of mine.

sn: अस्त्रमस्त्रेण सर्वेषामेतेषां मधुसूदन। मया द्रक्ष्यसि निर्भिन्नं जयद्रथवधैषिणा॥
en: You will see, O slayer of Madhu, the weapons of all these heroes cut-off by those of mine, when, desirous of slaying Jayadratha, I shall encounter them.

sn: द्रोणस्य मिषतश्चाहं सगणस्य विलप्यतः। मूर्धानं सिन्धुराजस्य पातयिष्यामि भूतले॥
en: Before the eyes of Drona and before his bewailing followers, I will fell down on earth the head of the ruler of the Sindhus.

sn: यदि साध्याश्च रुद्राश्च वसवश्च सहाश्विनः। मरुतश्च सहेन्द्रेण विश्वेदेवाः सहेश्वराः॥
en: Even if the Saddhyas, the Rudras, the Vasus together with the twin Aswins, the Marutas with Indra, the Visvadevas and the mighty gods.

sn: पितरः सहगन्धर्वाः सुपर्णाः सागरादयः। द्यौर्वियत् पृथिवीं चेयं दिशश्च सदिगीश्वराः॥
en: The ancestral manes and the Gandharvas and Suparna and the oceans, the mountains, the firmament, heaven, earth the quarters and their regents.

sn: ग्रामारण्यानि भूतानि स्थावराणि चराणि च। त्रातारः सिन्धुराजस्य भवन्ति मधुसूदन॥
en: The domestic and the wild animals and all the mobile and immobile beings united together-even if all these become the protector of the Sindhu king, O slayer of Madhu.

sn: तथापि बाणैर्निहतं श्वो द्रष्टासि रणे मया। सत्येन च शपे कृष्ण तथैवायुधमालभे॥
en: Still you shall behold him tomorrow slain by my arrows in battle. O Krishna, I swear by my truth and touching my weapons.

sn: यस्तु गोप्ता महेष्वासस्तस्य पापस्य दुर्मतेः। तमेव प्रथमं द्रोणमभियास्यामि केशव॥
en: That, О Keshava, at the very first instance, I shall proceed against that Drona, that fierce bowman who had undertaken to protect the sinful Jayadratha.

sn: तस्मिन् द्यूतमिदं बद्धं मन्यते स सुयोधनः। तस्मात् तस्यैव सेनाग्रं भित्त्वा यास्याभि सैन्धवम्॥
en: King Suyodhana considers this battle as a game depending on the dice identified with Drona himself. Therefore, penetrating through the divisions of Drona himself, I shall reach the king of the Sindhus.

sn: द्रष्टासि श्वो महेष्वासान् नाराचैस्तिग्मतेजितैः। शृङ्गाणीव गिरेर्वत्रैर्दार्यमाणान् मया युधि॥
en: Tomorrow you shall behold the mighty bowmen (of the enemy's host), rent open by me with Narachas of fierce energy, like the crests of the mountains cleft open by the bolt of Heaven.

sn: नरनागाश्वदेहेभ्यो विस्रविष्यति शोणितम्। पतद्भ्यः पतितेभ्यश्च विभिन्नेभ्य: शितैः शरैः॥
en: Blood shall flow out copiously from the bodies of men, elephants and steeds, rent open and fallen on the ground, being struck with my whetted shafts.

sn: गाण्डीवप्रेषिता बाणा मनोऽनिलसमा जवे। नृनागाश्वान् विदेहासून् कर्तारश्च सहस्रशः॥
en: Arrows shot from the bow Gandiva and resembling in speed the speed of mind or the wind itself, shall, by thousands, deprive men, horses and elephants of their lives and limbs.

sn: यमात् कुबेराद् वरुणादिन्द्राद् रुद्राच्च यन्मया। उपात्तमस्त्रं घोरं तद् द्रष्टारोऽत्र नरा युधि॥
en: In tomorrow's battle, men will see those terrible weapons displayed by me which I have secured from Yama, Kubera, Varuna, Indra and Rudra.

sn: ब्राह्मणास्त्रेण चास्त्राणि हन्यमानानि संयुगे। मया द्रष्टासि सर्वेषां सैन्धवस्याभिरक्षिणाम्॥
en: In tomorrow's fight you will see the weapons of those that will come to protect the king of the Sindhus, repulsed by my one Brahma weapon.

sn: शरवेगसमुत्कृत्तै राज्ञां केशव मूर्धभिः। आस्तीर्यमाणां पृथिवीं द्रष्टासि श्वो मया युधि॥
en: Tomorrow you shall see the earth covered by me with the head of princes cut-off their trunks by the force of my arrows, O Keshava.

sn: क्रव्यादास्तर्पयिष्यामि द्रावयिष्यामि शात्रवान्। सुहृदो नन्दयिष्यामि प्रमथिष्यामि सैन्धवम्॥
en: Tomorrow will I afford gratification to the flesh-eaters and will scatter my enemies and delight my friends and completely destroy the ruler of the Sindhus.

sn: बह्वागस्कृत कुसम्बन्धी पापदेशसमुद्भवः। मया सैन्धवको राजा हतः स्वान् शोचयिष्यति॥
en: A greatly sinful wretch, one who had acted not like a kinsman, born in a sinful country, the king of Sindhus slain by me, will, tomorrow, impart sorrow to his followers.

sn: सर्वक्षीरानभोक्तारं पापाचारं रणाजिरे। मया सराजकं बाणैर्भिन्नं द्रक्ष्यसि सैन्धवम्॥
en: Tomorrow you shall see the mean ruler of the Sindus, that one brought up in all luxury and of sinful behaviour, pierced by me in battle with my shafts.

sn: तथा प्रभाते कर्तास्मि यथा कृष्ण सुयोधनः। नान्यं धनुर्धरं लोके मंस्यते मत्समं युधि॥
en: OKrishna, at day-break, I will achieve such feats, that Suyodhana will never think that there is any other bowman equal to me.

sn: गाण्डीवं च धनुर्दिव्यं योद्धा चाहं नरर्षभ। त्वं च यन्ता हृषीकेश किं नु स्यादजितं मया॥
en: This Gandiva bow is of celestial make; I, O foremost of men, am also a warrior; you also, O Hrishikesha, are my driver; what then cannot be conquered by me?

sn: तव प्रसादाद् भगवान् किं नावाप्तं रणे मम। अविषह्यं हृषीकेश किं जानन् मां विगर्हसे॥
en: Through your grace, O almighty one, what is there unacquirable by me in battle? O Hrishikesha, knowing my prowess to be incapable of being baffled, why do you admonish me?

sn: यथा लक्ष्म स्थिरं चन्द्रे समुद्रे च यथा जलम्। एवमेतां प्रतिज्ञां मे सत्यां विद्धि जनार्दन॥
en: As Lakshmi is ever constant in the moon, as water ever remains in the ocean, so, O Janardana, know my vow to be ever incapable of being frustrated.

sn: मावसंस्था ममास्त्राणि मावमंस्था धनुदृढम्। मावमंस्था बलं बाह्वोमावमंस्था धनंजयम्॥
en: Do not hate my weapons, Do not hate my firm and tough bow. Do not despise the prowess of my arms and do not also, O Krishna, despise Dhananjaya.

sn: तथाभियामि संग्रामं न जीयेयं जयामि च। तेन सत्येन संग्रामे हतं विद्धि जयद्रथम्॥
en: I will proceed to battle in such a manner that I will surely win and not lose. When I have taken the oath, count Jayadratha already among those slain in battle.

sn: ध्रुवं वै ब्राह्मणे सत्यं ध्रुवा साधुषु संनतिः। श्रीधुंवापि च यज्ञेषु ध्रुवो नारायणे जयः॥
en: Truth is ever constant in the Brahmana; humility is ever constant in the pious; prosperity ever attends sacrifice and victory ever attends Narayana.

sn: संजय उवाच एवमुक्त्वा हृषीकेशं स्वयमात्मानमात्मना। संदिदेशार्जुनो नर्दन् वासविः केशवं प्रभुम्॥
en: Sanjaya said Having spoken these words to Hrishikesha and having said so to his own self also, Vasava's son (Arjuna) once more addressed

sn: यथा प्रभातं रजनी कल्पितः स्याद् रथो मम। तथा कार्यं त्वया कृष्ण कार्यं हि महदुद्यतम्॥
en: O Krishna, you should so arrange that as soon as the night passes away, my chariot may be ready, well-furnished with the implements of war, inasmuch as the task at hand is very serious.

sn: संजय उवाच तां निशां दुःखशोकातॊ निःश्वसन्ताविवोरगौ। निद्रां नैवोपलेभाते वासुदेवधनंजयौ॥
en: Sanjaya said Then throughout the whole of that night, Vasudeva and Dhananjaya, both afflicted with sorrow and grief and breathing like two serpents, did not enjoy an wink of sleep.

sn: नरनारायणौ क्रुद्धौ ज्ञात्वा देवाः सवासवाः। व्यथिताश्चिन्तयामासुः किंस्विदेतद् भविष्यति॥
en: The gods together with Indra himself, understanding Partha and Narayana to be excited with rage, became anxious and they began to think-what will come of it?

sn: ववुश्च दारुणा वाता रूक्षा घोराभिशंसिनः। सकबन्धस्तथाऽऽदित्ये परिधिः समदृश्यत॥
en: Dry and dreadful winds, portending calamities, began to blow. A headless trunk and a bludgeon became manifest in the solar disc.

sn: शुष्काशन्यश्च निष्पेतुः सनिर्घाताः सविद्युतः। चचाल चापि पृथिवी सशैलवनकानना॥
en: Although the sky cloudless, thunderbolts fell on the earth, accompanied by dreadful rumbling the flashes of lightning; and the Earth with her mountains, hills and forests, began to quake.

sn: चुक्षुभुश्च महाराज सागरा मकरालयाः। प्रतिस्रोतः प्रवृत्ताश्च तथा गन्तुं समुद्रगाः॥
en: 0 mighty monarch, the oceans, the abode of the numerous acquatic creatures, became agitated; and the ocean-going rivers began to flow in directions opposite to their natural was courses.

sn: रथाश्वनरनागानां प्रवृत्तमधरोत्तरम्। क्रव्यादानां प्रमोदार्थं यमराष्ट्रविवृद्धये॥
en: The lower and upper lips of car-warriors, horses, men and elephants began to tremble, indicating, as if, a great festivity for the fleshcaters and an increase of the population of Death's domain.

sn: वाहनानि शकृन्मूत्रे मुमुचू रुरुदुश्च ह। तान् दृष्ट्वादारुणान् सर्वानुत्पाताँल्लोमहर्षणान्॥
en: The animals on the field began to discharge excreta and urine and they began to wail aloud. Beholding all those dreadful portents capable of making the hair stand on end.

sn: सर्वे ते व्यथिताः सैन्यास्त्वदीया भरतर्षभ। श्रुत्वा महाबलस्योग्रां प्रतिज्ञा सव्यसाचिनः॥
en: And having heard of the fierce vow of the mighty Savyasachin, all your troops. O foremost of the Bharatas, became preyed upon by anxious thought.

sn: अथ कृष्णं महाबाहुब्रवीत् णकशासनिः। आश्वासय सुभद्रां त्वं भगिनी स्नुषया सह॥
en: Then the mighty-armed Pakasasaui (Arjuna) addressing Krishna said-"Do you offer consolation to your sister Subhadra and her daughter-in-law.

sn: स्नुषां चास्या वयस्याश्च विशोकाः कुरु माधव। साम्ना सत्येन युक्तेन वचसाऽऽश्वासय प्रभो॥
en: O Madhava, go, assuage the grief of my daughter-in-law and her companions; O lord, console them with your soft words fraught with truth.

sn: ततोऽर्जुनगृहं गत्वा वासुदेवः सुदुर्मनाः। भगिनीं पुत्रशोकार्तामाश्वासयत दुःखिताम्॥
en: Thereat the son of Vasudeva with a depressed heart, going to the pavilion of Arjuna, began to comport his sorrowful sister afflicted with the grief caused by the death of her son.

sn: वासुदेव उवाच कुरु वार्ष्णेयि कुमारं प्रति सस्नुषा। सर्वेषां प्राणिनां भीरु निष्ठैषा कालनिर्मिता॥
en: The son of Vasudeva said O daughter of the Vrishni race, do not grieve, with your daughter-in-law, for your son. O timid lady, the self-same end is ordained by the Destroyer for all created beings.

sn: कुले जातस्य धीरस्य क्षत्रियस्य विशेषतः। सदृशं मरणं ह्येतत् तव पुत्रस्य मा शुचः॥
en: This sort of death is worthy of your son, born in an illustrious family, modest and especially belonging to the Kshatriya order. Do not grieve for him.

sn: मा शोकं दिष्ट्या महारथो धीरः पितुस्तुल्यपराक्रमः। क्षात्रेण विधिना प्राप्तो वीराभिलषितां गतिम्॥
en: Indeed it is through good fortune that mighty car-warrior, modest and equal to his father in prowess, has obtained the goal coveted by the heroes, in consequence of his observance of Kshatriya duties.

sn: जित्वा सुबहुशः शत्रून् प्रेषयित्वा च मृत्यवे। गतः पुण्यकृतां लोकान् सर्वकामदुहोऽक्षयान्॥
en: Vanquishing innumerable foes and dispatching them to the abode of Death, he as attained to the posthumous state of the pious, that is enduring and in which all desires become fruitful.

sn: तपसा ब्रह्मचर्येण श्रुतेन प्रज्ञयाऽपि च। सन्तो यां गतिमिच्छन्ति तां प्राप्तस्तव पुत्रकः॥
en: Your son of tender years has attained to that end which the pious desire to have through the performance ascetic austerities and Brahmacharya and through knowledge of the Shastras and wisdom.

sn: वीरसूर्वीरपत्नी त्वं वीरजा वीरबान्धवा। मा शुचस्तनयं भद्रे गतः स परमां गतिम्॥
en: You are the mother of a hero, the wife of a hero, the daughter of a hero and a kins-woman of the heroes: O amiable one do not bewail your son who has attained an excellent mode of existence.

sn: प्राप्स्यते चाप्यसौ पापः सैन्धवो बालघातकः। अस्यावलेपस्य फलं ससुहृद्गणबान्धवः॥
en: That wretched and sinful ruler of the Sindhus, that murderer of an infant, shall soon reap the fruit of this arrogance, with his relations and kinsmen.

sn: व्युष्टायां तु वरारोहे रजन्यां पापकर्मकृत्। न हि मोक्ष्यति पार्थात स प्रविष्टोऽप्यमरावतीम्॥
en: O beautiful lady, when the day dawns, that perpetrator of sinful acts, shall not escape the son of Pritha, even if he seeks shelter in Heaven itself.

sn: श्वः शिरः श्रोष्यसे तस्य सैन्धवस्य रणे हृतम्। समन्तपञ्चकाद् बाह्यं विशोका भव मा रुंदः॥
en: Tomorrow you shall hear that the head of the Sindhu ruler has been severed from his trunk in battle, to roll on the precincts of the Samantapanchaka. Dismiss your grief and do not weep.

sn: क्षत्रधर्मं पुरस्कृत्य गतः शूरः सतां गतिम्। यां गतिं प्राप्नुयामेह ये चान्ये शस्त्रजीविनः॥
en: Keeping in the view duties of the Kshatriya order, that hero has obtained the end of the pious, end, which we also will meet with, as also many other men who live by their weapons.

sn: व्यूढोरस्को महाबाहुरनिवर्ती स्थप्रणुत्। गतस्तव वरारोहे पुत्रः स्वर्ग ज्वरं जहि॥
en: Of expansive chest and mighty arms, unretreating and slayer of car-warriors, your son, 0 you of dainty waist, has gone to heaven. Renounce yours fever of grief.

sn: अनुयातश्च पितरं मातृपक्षं च वीर्यवान्। सहस्राशो रिपून हत्वा हतः शूरो महारथः॥
en: Obedient to the behests of his sire and his relations through mother's side, that valiant hero and mighty car-warrior that valiant hero and mighty car-warrior of great prowess, has been slain may of his foes.

sn: आश्वासन स्नुषां राज्ञि मा शुचः क्षत्रिये भृशम्। श्वः प्रियं सुमहच्छ्रुत्वा विशोका भव नन्दिनि॥
en: O queen, comfort your daughter-in-law; () daughter of a Kshatriya, do not lament, Dismiss your sorrow, O my beloved sister, as in the morrow you will hear such agreeable news.

sn: यत् पार्थेन प्रतिज्ञातं तत् तथा न तदन्यथा। चिकीर्षितं हि ते भर्तुर्न भवेज्जातु निष्फलम्॥
en: What the son of Pritha has vowed shall be accomplished and cannot be otherwise. What your husband has set his heart upon, cannot remain undone.

sn: यदि च मनुजपन्नगा: पिशाचा रजनिश्चा पतगाः सुरासुराश्च। रणगतमभियान्ति सिन्धुराज नस भविता सह तैरपि प्रभाते॥
en: Even if the descendants of Manu and the Pannagas and Pisachas and night-rangers and winged creatures and Asuras and the celestials come forward to protect in battle the ruler of the Sindhus, yet he, with these, shall cease to exist tomorrow. Even if the descendants of Manu and the Pannagas and Pisachas and night-rangers and winged creatures and Asuras and the celestials come forward to protect in battle the ruler of the Sindhus, yet he, with these, shall cease to exist tomorrow.

sn: संजय उवाच एतच्छ्रुत्वा वचस्तस्य केशवस्य महात्मनः। सुभद्रा पुत्रशोकार्ता विललाप सुदुःखिता॥
en: Sanjaya said Having heard these words of Keshava of high-soul, Subhadra afflicted with grief on account of her son and sorely distressed, began to lament piteously.

sn: हा पुत्र मम मन्दायाः कथमेत्यासि संयुगम्। निधनं प्राप्तवांस्तात पितुस्तुल्यपराक्रमः॥
en: Alas! son of my unfortunate self, why did you go to the battle? Oh son equal in prowess to your father, how could you perish?

sn: कथमिन्दीवरश्यामं सुदंष्ट्रं चारुलोचनम्। मुखं ते दृश्यते वत्स गुण्ठितं रणरेणुना॥
en: Oh my dear child, how shall I see your face dark like the blue lotus and graced with beautiful teeth and charming eyes, soiled with the dust of battle-field!

sn: नूनं शूरं निपतितं त्वां पश्यन्त्यनिवर्तिनम्। सुशिरोग्रीवबाह्वसं व्यूढोरस्कं नतोदरम्॥ चारूपचितसर्वांङ्गं स्वक्षं शस्त्रक्षताचितम्। भूतानि त्वां निरीक्षन्ते नूनं चन्द्रमिवोदितम्॥
en: Surely, heroic and unretreating as you were, you are now being seen by every body. Of graceful head, well-formed neck and arms, of expensive chest, of low belly of limbs, decked with ornaments, of charming eyes and covered with wounds of weapons, surely creatures are now looking at you as if at the rising moon!

sn: शयनीयं पुरा यस्य स्पर्ध्यास्तरणसंवृतम्। भूमावद्य कथं शेषे विप्रविद्धः सुखोचितः॥
en: Alas! you who used to lie down on beds covered with precious coverlets, alas, how could you, ever used to luxuries, now lie down on the bare earth, being pierced with arrows!

sn: योऽन्वास्यत पुरा वीरो वस्त्रीभिर्महाभुजः। कथमन्वास्यते सोऽद्य शिवभिः पतितो मृधे॥
en: That hero of mighty arms who used formerly to be attended upon by most beautiful damsels, Oh, how can he, prostrate on the field of battle, pass his time today in the company of the jackals!

sn: सोऽस्तूयत पुरा हृष्टैः सूतमागधबन्दिभिः। सोऽद्य क्रव्याद्गणैधौरैर्विनदद्भिपास्यते॥
en: He who formerly used to be eulogised by the joyful bards, minstrels and singers alas, he, today, is greeted by the dreadful flesh-eaters with their fierce yells!

sn: पाण्डवेषु च नाथेषु वृष्णिवीरेषु वा विभो। पञ्चालेषु च वीरेषु हतः केनास्यनाथवत्॥
en: O son! having the Pandavas, the Vrishni heroes and the Panchalas for your protector, by whom have you been slain like one helpless?

sn: अतृप्तदर्शना पुत्र दर्शनस्य तवानघ। मन्दभाग्या गमिष्यामि व्यक्तमद्य यमक्षयम्॥
en: O my sinless son! my desire for looking at you is not yet satiated. Unfortunate that I am, I shall surely today go to the regions of Death.

sn: विशालाक्षं सुकेशान्तं चारुवाक्यं सुगन्धि च। तव पुत्र कदा भूयो मुखं द्रक्ष्यामि निव्रणम्॥
en: When again O my son, shall I see that face of yours, graced with expansive eyes, covered with beautiful looks and from which sweet words and fragrant perfume used always to come out?

sn: धिग् बलं भीमसेनस्य धिक् पार्थस्य धनुष्मताम्। धिग् वीर्यं वृष्णिवीराणां पञ्चालानां च धिग्बलम्।।
en: Fie on the strength of Bhima, fie on the 'bowmanship of Arjuna, fie on the prowess of the Vrishni heroes and fie on the mighty of the Panchalas!

sn: धिक्केकयांस्तथा चेदीन् मत्स्यांश्चैवाथ सृञ्जयान्। ये त्वां रणगतं वीरं न शेकुरभिरक्षितुम्॥
en: Fie on the Kaikayas and on the Chedis and the Matsyas and the Srinjayas, who all, united together, could not protect that hero when he went to battle.

sn: अद्य पश्यामि पृथिवीं शून्यामिव हतत्विषम्। अभिमन्युमपश्यन्ती शोकव्याकुललोचना॥
en: Today do I see the earth vacant and destitute of its beauty, inasmuch as I do not see Abhimanyu and my eyes are blinded with grief.

sn: स्वस्रीयं वासुदेवस्य पुत्रं गाण्डीवधन्वनः। कथं त्वातिरथं वीरं द्रक्ष्याम्यद्य निपातितम्॥
en: How shall we see you slain, you who are the son of the wielder of the Gandiva, the son of Vasudeva's sister, you who are a hero and a Atiratha too!

sn: एह्येहि तृषितो वत्स सतनौ पूर्णो पिबाशु मे। अङ्कमारुह्य मन्दाया ह्यतुप्तायाश्च दर्शने॥
en: Dear son! Come to me. You would thirsty. Suck milk from my breast immediately by taking a seat on lap as I am an unfortunate mother who had to live thirsty to see your face.

sn: हा वीर दृष्टो नष्टश्च घनं स्वप्न इवासि मे। अहो ह्यनित्यं मानुष्यं जलबुद्बुदचञ्चलम्॥
en: Alas, O hero, you were like a hoard of treasure to me, seen and lost in dream. Alas! everything human is as transitory as even a bubble of water!

sn: इमां ते तरुणी भार्यां तवाधिभिरभिप्लुताम्। कथं संधारयिष्यामि विवत्सामिव धेनुकाम्॥
en: How shall I comfort your young wife overwhelmed by the grief caused by your death and resembling a cow bereft of its calf.

sn: अहो ाकाले प्रस्थानं कृतवानसि पुत्रका विहाय फलकाले मां सुगृद्धां तव दर्शने॥
en: Alas, Oh my son, you have passed away prematurely at a time when you were on the point of bearing fruit, although I yearn to have a sight of you!

sn: नूनं गतिः कृतान्तस्य प्राज्ञैरपि सुदुर्विदा। यत्र तत्वं केशवे नाथे संग्रामेऽनाथवद्धतः॥
en: Surely the ways of the Destroyer are mysterious even to the wise, inasmuch as, you, having Keshava himself for your protector, have been slain in battle like one perfectly helpless.

sn: यज्वनां दानशीलानां ब्राह्मणानां कृतात्मनाम्। चरितब्रह्मचर्याणां पुण्यतीर्थावगाहिनाम्॥ कृतज्ञानां वदान्यानां गुरुशुश्रूषिणामपि। सहस्रदक्षिणानां च या गतिस्तामवाप्नुहि॥
en: May you, O son, attain that end which is theirs that perform sacrifices, theirs that are Brahmanas of purified soul, theirs that observe the vow Bhramacharya, theirs that have bathed in the sacred waters, theirs that are grateful, theirs that are devoted to the performance of benevolent deeds, theirs that serve their preceptors and theirs that make profuse sacrificial presents!

sn: या गतिर्युध्यमानानां शूराणामनिवर्तिनाम्। हत्वारीन् निहतानां च संग्रामे तां गतिं व्रज॥
en: May that end be yours which they attain who fight and never retreat or who fall in battle after slaying their numerous foes!

sn: गोसहस्रप्रदातॄणां क्रतुदानां च या गतिः। नैवेशिकं चाभिमतं ददतां या गति: शुभा।॥
en: That blessed end which they attain who give away a thousand cows or who perform charitable deeds at a sacrifice or who give away houses and palaces to the liking of the recipients.

sn: ब्राह्मणेभ्यः शरण्येभ्यो निधिं निदधतां च या। या चापि न्यस्तदण्डानां तां गतिं व्रज पुत्रक॥
en: Or who give away gems and jewels to worthy Brahmanas or who mete out just punishments, O son, may that blessed end be yours!

sn: ब्रह्मचर्येण यां यान्ति मुनयः संशितव्रताः। एकपल्यश्च यां यान्ति तां गतिं व्रज पुत्रक॥
en: O son, may you attain to that end which sages of rigid vows attain to, by the performance of Brahmacharya or that end which is attained by the women who marry but once their husbands.

sn: राज्ञां सुचरितैर्या च गतिर्भवति शाश्वती। चतुराश्रमिणां पुण्यैः पावितानां सुरक्षितैः॥ दीनानुकम्पिनां या च सततं संविभागिनाम्। पैशुन्याच्च निवृत्तानां तां गतिं व्रज पुत्रक॥
en: That eternal and which is obtained by monarchs through their good conduct or by those persons who, leading one after another all the four modes of life and through the observance of duties, have purified themselves. That end which they attain who are kind to the poor and the woe-stricken or who equally divide objects of enjoyments amongst themselves and their dependents or who are free from the influence of malice, O son, may that end be yours!

sn: व्रतिनां धर्मशीलानां गुरुशुश्रूषिणामपि। अमोघातिथिनां या च तां गतिं व्रज पुत्रक॥
en: That end which is theirs, who observe their vows, theirs that are devoted to righteous practices, theirs that serve their elders and preceptors, theirs that never drive away guests from their doors, O son, may that end by yours!

sn: कृच्छ्रेषु या धारयतामात्मानं व्यसनेषु च। गतिः शोकाग्निदग्धानां तां गतिं व्रज पुत्रका॥
en: O son, may you attain to that end which they attain who preserve the coolness of their temper in the most difficult circumstances, however much they may be consumed by the fire of sorrow!

sn: मातापित्रोश्च शुश्रूषां कल्पयन्तीह ये सदा। स्वदारनिरतानां च या गतिस्तामवाप्नुहि॥
en: May you attain to the end of those who always take care of their father and mother and who never enjoy the company of women other than their own wives!

sn: ऋतुकाले स्वकां भार्यां गच्छतां या मनीषिणाम्। परस्त्रीभ्यो निवृत्तानां तां गतिं व्रज पुत्रक॥
en: May you attain, O son, to the end of those who hold sexual intercourse with their own wives during their seasons, of those who restrain themselves from enjoying others; wives! even

sn: साम्ना ये सर्वभूतानि पश्यन्ति गतमत्सराः। नारुंतुदानां क्षमिणां या गतिस्तामवाप्नुहि॥
en: May you attain to the end of those, who, free from malice, look upon every one with an eye of peace or who are forgiving and never enflict distress on others!

sn: मधुमांसनिवृत्तानां मदाद् दम्भात् तथानृतात्। परोपतापत्यक्तानां तां गतिं व्रज पुत्रक॥
en: O son, may you attain to the end of those who ever hold themselves aloof from money, meat, intoxicating drinks, pride and falsehood or who never cause pain to any body else!

sn: ह्रीमन्तः सर्वशास्त्रज्ञा ज्ञानतृप्ता जितेन्द्रियाः। यां गतिं साधवो यान्ति तां गति व्रज पुत्रक॥
en: O son, may you attain that end which they attain who are modest, learned in all the Shastras, content in knowledge and hold their passions under check.

sn: एवं विलपती दीनां सुभद्रां शोककर्शिताम्। अन्वपद्यत पाञ्चाली वैराटिसहितां तदा॥
en: While the distressed Subhadra, overwhelmed with grief, had been thus lamenting, Panchali accompanied by Vairata's daughter, came to her.

sn: ताः प्रकामं रुदित्वा च विलय च सुदुःखताः। उन्मत्तवत् तदा राजन् विसंज्ञा न्यपतन् क्षितौ॥
en: Then copiously lamenting and bewailing under the weight of their grief, they fell down, Oking, on the earth, senseless and like so many mad creatures.

sn: सोपचारस्तु कृष्णश्च दुःखितां भृशदुःखितः। सिक्त्वांभसा समाश्वास्य तत्तदुक्त्वा हितं वचः॥ विसंज्ञकल्पां रुदती मर्मविद्धां प्रवेपतीम्। भगिनीं पुण्डरीकाक्ष इदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Then the highly-afflicted Krishna who was there ready with water sprinkled water on the face of them and for comforting them said such salutary words that should be said on such occasions. Then the eyes of resembling lotuspetals said these words to his sister, weeping, insensible, trembling and pierced in her very heart.

sn: सुभद्रे मा शुचः पुत्रं पाञ्चाल्याश्वासयोत्तराम्। गतोऽभिमन्युः प्रथितां गतिं क्षत्रियपुङ्गवः॥
en: 0 Subhadra, bewail not your son; O Panchali, console the sister of Ullara. Abhimany'i, that foremost of Kshatriyas, has atlaired in the most excellent state.

sn: ले सन्ति पुरुषा नो वरानने। *गांत यान्तु ह्यभिमन्योर्यशस्विनः॥
en: you of charming countenance, may all the other people of our race that are yet alive attain to that state which the illustrious Abhimanyu has attained!

sn: कुर्याम तद् वयं कर्म क्रियासु सुहृदश्च नः। कृतवान् यादृगौकस्तव पुत्रोमहारथः॥
en: We, supported by our allies, desire to accomplish that feat in this battle, the like of which, O lady, your son, that mighty carwarrior, achieved single-handed.

sn: एवमाश्वास्य भगिनीं द्रौपदीमपि चोत्तराम्। पार्थस्यैव महाबाहुः पार्श्वमागादरिंदमः॥
en: Thus having consoled his sister and Draupadi and Uttara, that subduer of foes, that mighty-armed one, (viz., Krishna) came back to Partha's side.

sn: ततोऽभ्यनुज्ञाय नृपान् कृष्णा बन्धूंस्तथार्जुनम्। विवेशान्त:पुरे राजस्ते च जग्मुर्यथालयम्॥
en: Then with the permission of his relatives and of the kings and of Arjuna, O monarch, Krishna retired to the inner apartments of the latter's pavilion; the rest of the kings then retired to their respective quarters.

description: The colloquy between Krishna and Daruka
sn: संजय उवाच ततोऽर्जुनस्य भवनं प्रविश्याप्रतिमं विभुः। स्पृष्ट्वाम्भः पुण्डरीकाक्षः स्थण्डिले शुभलक्षणे॥
en: Sanjaya said Then that Lord of eyes like lotus-petals, having entered into the matchless mansion of Arjuna, touched water and on the smooth and auspicious floor.

description: The colloquy between Krishna and Daruka
sn: संतस्तार शुभां शय्यां दभैदूर्यसंनिभैः। ततो माल्येन विधिवल्लजैर्गन्धैः सुमङ्गलैः॥
en: Spread an auspicious bed made of Kushamass of the hue of lapises. Thereafter, with garlands of flowers, fried paddy and perfumes and other auspicious articles.

description: The colloquy between Krishna and Daruka
sn: अलंचकार तां शय्यां परिवार्यायुधोत्तमैः। ततः स्पृष्टोदके पार्थे विनीताः परिचारकाः॥
en: He decorated that bed and then kept around it many excellent weapons. Then when Partha also had touched water, obedient and humble servants.

description: The colloquy between Krishna and Daruka
sn: दर्शयन्तोऽन्तिके चकुर्नैशं त्रैयम्बकं बलिम्। ततः प्रीतमनाः पार्थो गन्धमाल्यैश्च माधवम्॥
en: Performed the usual nightly ceremony of offering victims to the three-eyed Mahadeva. Thereafter with a delighted heart, Pritha's son, with perfumes and garlands.

description: The colloquy between Krishna and Daruka
sn: अलंकृत्योपहारं तं नैशं तस्मै न्यवेदयत्। स्मयमानस्तु गोविन्दः फाल्गुनं प्रत्यभाषत॥
en: Adorned Madhava and then offered him the nightly offering. The Govinda with a smile thus spoke to Phalguna.

description: The colloquy between Krishna and Daruka
sn: सुप्यतां पाथ्र भद्रं ते कल्याणाय व्रजाम्यहम्। स्थापयित्वा ततो द्वा:स्थान् गोप्तुंश्चात्तायुधान् नरान्॥६
en: “O son of Pritha, lay yourself down for sleep; good betide you, I go in search of your welfare.” Then placing at the door well-armed sentinels and door-keepers.

description: The colloquy between Krishna and Daruka
sn: दारुवानुगतः श्रीमान् विवेश शिबिरं स्वकम्। शिश्ये च शयने शुभ्रे बहुकृत्यं विचिन्तयन्॥
en: The auspicious Krishna followed by Daruka, entered his own tent. Then he laid himself down on his milk-white bed and brooded over the diverse measures (to be adopted on the morrow).

description: The colloquy between Krishna and Daruka
sn: पार्थाय सर्वे भगवान् शोकदुःखापहं विधिम्। व्यदधात् पुण्डरीकाक्षस्तेजोद्युतिविवर्धनम्॥
en: Then that illustrious one of eyes resembling lotus-petals, for Partha's sake, began to reflect on various measures that would drive away the one latter's grief and sorrow and increase his energy and effulgence.

description: The colloquy between Krishna and Daruka
sn: योगमास्थाय युक्तात्मा सर्वेषामीश्वरेश्वरः। श्रेयस्कामः पृथुयशा विष्णुर्जिष्णुप्रियंकरः॥
en: Then that of soul engaged in meditation, that foremost lord of all, viz., Vishnu of wide-spread renown, who always performed what was agreeable to Jishnu, had recourse to Yoga-meditation, for benefiting Arjuna.

description: The colloquy between Krishna and Daruka
sn: न पाण्डवानां शिबिरे कश्चित् सुष्वाप तां निशाम्। प्रजागरः सर्वजनं ह्याविवेश विशाम्पते॥
en: During that night none enjoyed sleep in the camp of the Pandavas. During that night, O ruler of men, wakefulness possessed every body.

description: The colloquy between Krishna and Daruka
sn: पुत्रशोकाभितप्तेन प्रतिज्ञातो महात्मना। सहसा सिन्धुराजस्य वधो गाण्डीवधन्वना॥
en: “The wielder of the Gandiva bow, the highsouled Arjuna, being afflicted sore with grief on account of the death of his son, has rashly vowed the slaughter of the king of the Sindhus.

description: The colloquy between Krishna and Daruka
sn: तत् कथं नु महाबाहुर्वासविः परवीरहा। प्रतिज्ञां सफलां कुर्यादिति ते समचिन्तयन्॥
en: How indeed shall the mighty-armed son of Vasava, that slayer of hostile heroes, fulfill his vow?" Even thus did they then think.

description: The colloquy between Krishna and Daruka
sn: कष्टं हीदं व्यवसितं पाण्डवेन महात्मना। पुत्रशोकाभितप्तेन प्रतिज्ञा महती कृता॥
en: "The vow which the high-souled son of Pandu has made, is a very difficult one. King Jayadratha is endued with great energy. may Arjuna successfully observe his vow!

description: The colloquy between Krishna and Daruka
sn: सच राजा महावीर्यः पारयत्वर्जुनः स ताम्। भ्रातरश्चापि विक्रान्ता बहुलानि बलानि च॥
en: Indeed Arjuna has made a tremendous resolve, being highly afflicted with the grief on account of his son's death. The brothers (of Duryodhana) are very powerful and his army is numerous.

description: The colloquy between Krishna and Daruka
sn: धृतराष्ट्रस्य पुत्रेण सर्वे तस्मे निवेदितम्। स हत्वा सैन्धवं संख्ये पुनरेतु धनंजयः॥
en: The son of Dhritarashtra (Duryodhana) has also employed them all in the protection of his (Jayadratha). May Dhananjaya return safe, having slain the ruler of the Sindhus!

description: The colloquy between Krishna and Daruka
sn: जित्वा रिपुगणांश्चैव पारयत्वर्जुनो व्रतम्। श्वोऽहत्वा सिन्धुराजं वै धूमकेतुं प्रवेक्ष्यति॥
en: Let Arjuna fulfill his vow and vanquish his enemies. If tomorrow he fails to slay the Sindhu king, he will enter the blazing fire.

description: The colloquy between Krishna and Daruka
sn: न ह्यसावनृतं कर्तुमलं पार्थो धनंजयः। धर्मपुत्र कथं राजा भविष्यति मृतेऽर्जुने॥
en: Pritha's son Dhananjaya will never venture to falsify his vow. Oh, what will be the condition of king Yudhishthira, the son of Dharma, if Dhananjaya dies!

description: The colloquy between Krishna and Daruka
sn: तस्मिन् हि विजयः कृत्स्नः पाण्डवेन समाहितः। यदि नोऽस्ति कृतं किञ्चिद् यदि दत्तं हुतं यदि॥
en: Indeed Pandu's son (Yudhishthira) has grafted all his hopes of victory on Arjuna. If we have acquired any religious merit, if we have ever given away things in charity, if we have burnt offerings on the fire.

description: The colloquy between Krishna and Daruka
sn: फलेन तस्य सर्वस्य सव्यसाची जयत्वरीन्। एवं कथयतां तेषां जयमाशंसतां प्रभो॥
en: Then through the fruits of all those acts of ours, let Savyasachin (Arjuna) obtain victory." Thus, when they were talking to one another of the victory of Arjuna on the morrow, O lord.

description: The colloquy between Krishna and Daruka
sn: कृच्छ्रेण महता राजन् रजनी व्यत्यवर्तत। तस्यां रजन्यां मध्ये तु प्रतिबुद्धो जनार्दनः॥
en: O monarch, that live-long night at last passed away. During that night Janardana, having awaked.

description: The colloquy between Krishna and Daruka
sn: स्मृत्वा प्रतिज्ञां पार्थस्य दारुकं प्रत्यभाषत।। अर्जुनेन प्रतिज्ञातमार्तेन हतबन्धुना॥
en: And remembering the vow Pritha's son had made, thus addressed Daruka-"Afflicted with sorrow for the death of his dear-loved son, Arjuna has vowed.

description: The colloquy between Krishna and Daruka
sn: जयद्रथं वधिष्यामि श्वोभूत इति दारुक। तत्तु दुर्योधनः श्रुत्वा मन्त्रिभिर्मन्त्रयिष्यति॥
en: O Daruka, saying Before tomorrow's sun sets, I will slay Jayadratha-having heard of this vow, Duryodhana will surely hold counsel with his counsellors.

description: The colloquy between Krishna and Daruka
sn: यथा जयद्रथं पार्थो न हन्यादिति संयुगे। अक्षौहिण्योहिताः सर्वारक्षिष्यन्ति जयद्रथम्॥
en: As to how Partha might be prevented from slaying Jayadratha in battle. His several Akshauhinis will also protect the latter;

description: The colloquy between Krishna and Daruka
sn: द्रोणश्च सह पुत्रेण सर्वास्त्रविधिपारगः। एको वीरः सहस्राक्षो दैत्यदानवदर्पहा॥
en: As also Drona and his son, both accomplished in the use of all sorts of weapons, will protect him. That matchless hero, the thousand-eyed Indra himself, that humiliator of the pride of Daityas and Danavas.

description: The colloquy between Krishna and Daruka
sn: सोऽपि तं नोतसहेताजौ हन्तुं द्रोणेन रक्षितम्। सोऽहं श्वस्तत् करिष्यामि यथा कुन्तीसुतोऽर्जुनः।।२५
en: Even he will not venture to slay Jayadratha, if he is protected by Drona in battle. I, therefore, will do that in the morrow by which Kunti's son Arjuna.

description: The colloquy between Krishna and Daruka
sn: अप्राप्तेऽस्तं दिनकरे हनिष्यति जयद्रथम्। न हि दारा न मित्राणि ज्ञातयो न च बान्धवाः॥
en: May slay Jayadratha before the sun goes down below the horizon. My wives, my friends, my kinsmen, my relatives.

description: The colloquy between Krishna and Daruka
sn: कश्चिदन्यः प्रियतरः कुन्तीपुत्रान्ममार्जुनात्। अनर्जुनमिमं लोकं मुहूर्तमपि दारुक॥
en: None among these is so dear to me as is Kunti's son Arjuna. O Daruka, bereft of Arjuna, for even a moment, this world.

description: The colloquy between Krishna and Daruka
sn: उदीक्षितुं न शक्तोऽहं भविता न च तत् तथा। अहं विजित्य तान् सर्वान् सहसा सहयद्विपान्॥
en: I will not be able to look at. And therefore, it shall not be so. Vanquishing them all, with their horses and elephants.

description: The colloquy between Krishna and Daruka
sn: अर्जुनार्थे हनिष्यामि सकर्णान् ससुयोधनान्। श्वो निरीक्षन्तु मे वीर्ये त्रयो लोका महाहवे॥
en: I will slay them all with Karna and Duryodhana, for the sake of Arjuna. Tomorrow the three worlds will behold my prowess in the dreadful battle.

description: The colloquy between Krishna and Daruka
sn: धनंजयार्थे समरे पराक्रान्तस्य दारुक। श्वो नरेन्द्रसहस्राणि राजपुत्रशतानि च॥
en: When, O Daruka, I shall put forth my prowess for Arjuna's sake. Tomorrow thousands of kings and hundreds of princes.

description: The colloquy between Krishna and Daruka
sn: साश्वद्विपरथान्याजौ विद्रविष्यामि दारुका श्वस्तां चक्रप्रमथितां द्रक्ष्यसे नृपवाहिनीम्॥
en: With their steeds, cars and elephants, will, O Daruka, turn hastily away from the battle. Tomorrow Daruka, you shall see the army of kings crushed with my discus.

description: The colloquy between Krishna and Daruka
sn: मया क्रुद्धेन समरे पाण्डवार्थे निपातिताम्। श्वः सदेवाः सगन्धर्वाः पिशाचोरगराक्षसाः॥
en: And overthrown by my enraged self, for the sake of Arjuna. Tomorrow the celestials, the Gandharvas, the Pisachas, the reptiles and the Rakshasas.

description: The colloquy between Krishna and Daruka
sn: ज्ञास्यन्ति लोकाः सर्वे मां सुहृदं सव्यसाचिनः। यस्तं द्वेष्टि स मां द्वेष्टि यस्तं चानु स मामनु॥
en: Will all know me to be the true friend of Savyasachin. He that injures him (Arjuna) injures me; and he that follows him follows me also.

description: The colloquy between Krishna and Daruka
sn: इति संकल्प्यतां बुद्ध्या शरीरार्द्ध ममार्जुनः। यथा त्वं मे प्रभातायामस्यां निशि रथोत्तमम्॥ कल्पयित्वा यथाशास्त्रमादाय व्रज संयतः। गदा कौमोदकी दिव्यां शक्तिं चक्रं धनुः शरान्॥
en: With the help of your intelligence, do you identify Arjuna to be the half of my ownself. When the day dawns, O Daruka, equipping my best of chariots according to the rules of military science, you must bring it and follow me carefully. My mace Kaumodaki of celestial discus and my bow and arrows.

description: The colloquy between Krishna and Daruka
sn: आरोप्य वै रथे सूत सर्वोपकरणानि च। स्थानं च कल्पयित्वाऽथ रथोपस्थे ध्वजस्य मे॥ वैनतेयस्य वीरस्य समरे रथशोभिनः। छत्रं जाम्बूनदैर्जालैरर्कज्वलनसप्रभैः॥
en: make, my

description: The colloquy between Krishna and Daruka
sn: विश्वकर्मकृतैर्दिव्यैरश्वानपि विभूषितान्। बलाहकं मेघपुष्पं शैव्यं सुग्रीवमेव च॥ युक्तान् वाजिवरान् यत्तः कवचीतिष्ठ दारुका पाञ्चजन्यस्य निर्घोषमार्षभेणैव पूरितम्॥ श्रुत्वा च भैरवं नादमुपेयास्त्वं जवेन माम्। एकाह्राहममर्षं च सर्वदुःखानि चैव ह॥
en: And many other implements of war-placing all these, O Suta, on my chariot and leaving room thereon for my standard and for heroic Garuda that adorns my car and yoking thereto my excellent steeds named Balahaka, Meghapuspa, Shaivya, Sugriva, having incased them in caparisons of gold of the effulgence of the solar orb and the fire and yourself donning your coat of mail, stay on it carefully. Having heard the shrille blast resembling the Rishabha note, of my conch Panchajanya, you will quickly come to me. In the course of a single day, O Daruka, I shall drive away the rage and the various woes of my cousin, the son of my paternal aunt. By every means, I shall so exert in battle, so that Vibhastu in battle.

description: The colloquy between Krishna and Daruka
sn: भ्रातुः पैतृष्वसेयस्य व्यपनेष्यामि दारुक। सर्वोपायैर्यतिष्यामि हनिष्यति बीभत्सुराहवे॥ पश्यतां धार्तराष्ट्राणां हनिष्यति जयद्रथम्। यस्य यस्य च बीभत्सुर्वधे यत्नं करिष्यति। आशंसे सारसे तत्र भविताऽस्य ध्रुवो जयः॥
en: May slay Jayadratha even before the very eyes of the Dhritarastras. All those for whose death Vibhatsu will strive, I tell your truly, will be slain and O charioteer, he will succeed in obtaining victory.

description: The colloquy between Krishna and Daruka
sn: दारुक उवाच जय एव ध्रुवस्तस्य कुत एव पराजयः। यस्य त्वं पुरुषव्याघ्र सारथ्यमुपजग्मिवान्॥
en: Daruka said Victory is sure to him and whence can defeat come to him, whose charioteership you, O foremost men, have accepted.

description: The colloquy between Krishna and Daruka
sn: एवं चैतत् करिष्यामि यथा मामनुशाससि। सुप्रभातामिमां रात्रिं जयाय विजयस्य हि॥
en: I shall do what you will bid me do. This night will end ushering in a morning, that will bring victory for Vijaya.

sn: संजय उवाच कुन्तीपुत्रस्तु तं मन्त्रं स्मरन्नेव धनंजयः। प्रतिज्ञामात्मनो रक्षन् मुमोहाचिन्त्यविक्रमः॥
en: Sanjaya said Then Dhananjaya the son of Kunti, possessed of inconceivable prowess thinking of how to redeem his vow, recollected the mantras (obtained from Vyasa); and soon was he lost of sleep.

sn: तं तु शोकेन संतप्तं स्वप्ने कपिवरध्वजम्। आससाद महातेजा ध्यायन्तं गरुडध्वजः॥
en: Then the highly puissant god having the Garuda as an emblem on his banner, appeared before the ape-bannered Arjuna merged in thought and burning with grief, in his dream.

sn: प्रत्युत्थानं च कृष्णस्य सर्वावस्थो धनंजयः। न लोपयति धर्मात्मा भक्त्या प्रेम्णा च सर्वदा॥
en: The pious-souled Dhananjaya through the love and venevation he bore for Krishna, never failed under any circumstance, to rise up and advance a few steps for welcoming him.

sn: प्रत्युत्थाय च गोविन्दं स तस्मा आसनं ददौ। न चासने स्वयं बुद्धिं बीभत्सुर्व्यदधात् तदा॥
en: Standing up therefore (in his dream), he welcomed Govinda and offered him a seat, He himself however then did not think of resuming his own seat.

sn: ततः कृष्णोमहातेजा जानन् पार्थस्य निश्चयम्। कुन्तीपुत्रमिदं वाक्यमासीनः स्थितमब्रवीत्॥
en: Thus seated, Krishna of mighty energy, knowing what resolution Partha had formed, said these words to the son of Kunti, while the latter was standing before him.

sn: मा विषादे मनः पार्थ कृथाः कालो हि दुर्जयः। कालः सर्वाणि भूतानि नियच्छति परे विधौ॥
en: O Son of Pritha, let not your heart give way to sorrow. Time is invincible. It is time that compels all creatures to take to the inevitable course.

sn: किमर्थे च विषादस्ते तद् ब्रूहि द्विपदां वर। न शोच्यं विदुषां श्रेष्ठ शोकः कार्यविनाशनः॥
en: Tell me, O foremost of men. the cause of this your sorrow? O foremost of the learned, sorrow should not be indulged in, inasmuch as it overthrows the ends of life.

sn: यत् तु कार्यं भवेत् कार्ये कर्मणा तत् समाचर। हीनचेष्टस्य यः शोकः स हि शत्रुर्धनंजय॥
en: What should be done should be done (without hesitation). Do your duty with all endeavours, O Dhananjaya, the grief that deprives one of the power of acting, is indeed his greatest enemy.

sn: शोचन् नन्दयते शत्रून् कर्शयत्यपि बान्धवान्। क्षीयते च नरस्तस्मान्न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि॥
en: A man giving way to grief delights his enemies and saddens his friends and himself becomes reduced in (strength). Therefore you should not grieve.

sn: इत्युक्तो वासुदेवेन बीभत्सुरपराजितः। आबभाषे तदा विद्वानिदं वचनमर्थवत्॥
en: Having been thus spoken to by the son of Vasudeva, the invincible and learned Vibhatsu said these words of (grave) signification to the former

sn: मया प्रतिज्ञा महती जयद्रथवधे कृता। श्वोऽस्मि हन्ता दुरात्मानं पुत्रघ्नमिति केशव॥
en: I have taken a terrible oath in vowing to slaughter Jayadratha. Tomorrow shall I slay, O Keshava that wicked-souled slayer of my son.

sn: मत्प्रतिज्ञाविघातार्थं धार्तराष्ट्रः किलाच्युत। पृष्ठतः सैन्धवः कार्यः सर्वैर्गुप्तो महारथैः ॥
en: Surely, O undeteriorating one, in order to frustrate that resolution of mine, the partisans of Dhritarashtra will place the ruler of the Sindhus in their furthest rear and have him protected by all their mighty car-warriors.

sn: दश चैका चताः कृष्ण अक्षौहिण्यः सुदुर्जयाः। हतावशेषास्तत्रेमा हन्त माधव संख्यया॥
en: Alas! O Mahadeva, their invincible army of one and ten Akshauhini strong, consists of the remnants of their soldiers (slain during the last compaign).

sn: ताभिः परिवृतः संख्ये सर्वेश्चैव महारथैः। कथं शक्येत संद्रष्टुं दुरात्मा कृष्ण सैन्धवः॥
en: Surrounded by all these troops, as also by all their mighty car-warriors, how could that wicked-souled ruler of the Sindhus, O Krishna, be seen (by us)?

sn: प्रतिज्ञापारणं चापि न भविष्यति केशव। प्रतिज्ञायां च हीनायां कथं जीवेत मद्विधः॥
en: Me seems, O Keshava, I shall not be able to fulfill my vow. And why should one like myself who could not redeem his promises, bear the burden of his life?

sn: दुःखोपायस्य मे वीर विकाङ्क्षा परिवर्तते। द्रुतं च याति सविता तत एतद् ब्रवीम्यहम्॥
en: O hero, despondency stares me at the face, me whose only consolation now is in grief. I also tell you this that (during this period of the year) the sun runs his heavenly course swiftly.

sn: पार्थस्य द्विजकेतनः। संस्पृश्याम्भस्ततः कृष्णः प्राङ्मुखः समवस्थितः॥
en: Then Krishna that foremost of the twiceborn ones, having heard of the source of Partha's sorrow, touched water and sat there with his face turned towards the East.

sn: इदं वाक्यं महातेजा बभाषे पुष्करेक्षणः। हितार्थं पाण्डुपुत्रस्य सैन्धवस्य वधे कृती॥
en: Thereafter that highly puissant one of eyes like lotus-petals, said these words, for the welfare of Pandu's son who had resolved upon the slaughter of the Sindhu king.

sn: पार्थ पाशुपतं नाम परमास्त्रं सनातनम्। येन सर्वान् मृधे दैत्याञ्जघ्ने देवो महेश्वरः॥
en: "O Son of Pritha, there is a weapon excellent and eternal known by the name of Pasupata. By means of this weapon the god Mahesvare (in days gone by) slew all the Daityas in battle.

sn: शोकस्थानं तु तच्छ्रुत्वा यदि तद् विदितं तेऽद्यश्वो हन्तासि जयद्रथम्। अथाज्ञातं प्रपद्यस्व मनसा वृषभध्वजम्॥
en: If today it be with your recollection, then tomorrow you will be able to slay Jayadratha. If it is unknown to you now, then do you worship in you mind the god having the bull for his emblein.

sn: तं देवं मनसा ध्यात्वा जोषमास्व धनंजय। ततस्तस्य प्रसादात् त्वं भक्तः प्राप्स्यसि तन्महत्॥
en: Meditating on that god in your mind. do you hold communion with him. You are his devotee and in this way, through his grace only, can you expect to obtain that valuable treasure (Pasupata weapon).”

sn: ततः कृष्णवचः श्रुत्वा संस्पृश्याम्भो धनंजयः। भूमावासीन एकाग्रो जगाम मनसा भवम्॥
en: Thereupon, having heard Krishna's words and having rinsed his mouth with water, Dhananjaya sat down on the ground; and with a singleness of heart, began to adore Siva (in his mind).

sn: ततः प्रणिहितो ब्राह्ये मुहूर्ते शुभलक्षणे। आत्मानमर्जुनोऽपश्यद् गगने सहकेशवम्॥
en: Thus rapt up in meditation, Arjuna saw himself and Keshava roving in the skies, just when the hour Brahma of auspicious indication set in.

sn: पुण्यं हिमवतः पादं मणिमन्तं च पर्वतम्। ज्योतिर्भिश्च समाकीर्णं सिद्धचारणसेवितम्॥ वायुवेगगतिः पार्थः खं भेजे सहकेशवः। केशवेन गृहीत: स दक्षिणे विभुना भुजे॥
en: Then it seemed that Parth held by his right arın by the lord Keshava and endued with the fleetness of the wind, reached the root of the sacred Himavat mountain teeming with gems, abounding in luminous objects and inhabited by Siddhas and Charanas. He was then accompanied by Keshava.

sn: प्रेक्षमाणो बहून् भावाञ्जगामाद्भुतदर्शनान्। उदीच्यां दिशि धर्मात्मासोऽपश्यच्छ्वेतपर्वतम्॥
en: It seemed that he saw, as he went, many wonderful sight and objects; that one of righteous soul then saw on the Northern direction the white mountain.

sn: कुबेरस्य विहारे च नलिनी पद्मभूषिताम्। सरिच्छेष्ट्रां च तां गङ्गां वीक्षमाणो बहूदकाम्॥
en: He beheld in the pleasure-garden of Kubera, the delightful lake adorned with lotuses. He also beheld that most excellent of rivers namely Ganga of copious waters.

sn: सदा पुष्पफलैर्वृक्षरुपेतां स्फटिकोपलाम्। सिंहव्याघ्रसमाकीर्णो नानामृगसमाकुलाम्॥ पुण्याश्रमवती रम्यां मनोज्ञाण्डजसेविताम्। मन्दरस्य प्रदेशांश्च किन्नरोद्गीतनादितान्॥
en: Then he saw the regions about the Mandara mountains, regions that abounded in trees bearing blossoms and fruits; that were covered with pebbles and transparent crystals, that were infested with lions and tigers; that abounded in many other animals, that contained many sacred hermitages; that were charming; that there frequented by beautiful birds and that ever rang with the melodious songs of the Kinnaras.

sn: हेमरूप्यमयैः शृङ्गै नौषधिविदीपितान्। तथा मन्दारवृक्षेश्च पुष्पितैरुपशोभितान्॥
en: The mountain itself was graced with gold and silver peaks blazing with various herbs and Oshadhis; and it was beautiful with numerous Mandara trees decked with blossoms.

sn: ग्निग्धाञ्जनचयाकारं सम्प्राप्तः कालपर्वतम्। ब्रह्मतुङ्गं नदीश्चान्यास्तथा जनपदानपि॥
en: He then arrived at the black mountains that looked like a heap of collyrium and after that, at the Brahmatunga, at many rivers and at many countries.

sn: स तुङ्गं शत शृङ्गं च शर्यातिवनमेव च। पुण्यमश्वशिरःस्थानं स्थानमाथर्वणस्य च।॥
en: He then reached the Sutunga and the Shatashringa hills and the woods known by the name of Sharyati. Then he went to the holy place called Ashvashiras and also to the one known by the name of Artharvana.

sn: वृषदंशं च शैलेन्द्र महामन्दरमेव च। अप्सरोभिः समाकीर्णं किन्नरैचोपशोभितम्॥
en: Then he arrived at that foremost of hills known as Vrisha-Dansha and also the hill called the great Mandara, both of which were thickly peopled by the Apsaras and beautified by the Kinnaras.

sn: तस्मिशैले व्रजन् पार्थः सकृष्णः समवेक्षता शुभैः प्रस्रवणैजुष्टां हेमधातुविभूषिताम्॥ चन्द्ररश्मिप्रकाशाङ्गी पृथिवीं पुरमालिनीम्। समुद्रांश्चाद्भुताकारानपश्यद् बहुलाकरान्॥
en: Then roaming on that hill in the company of Krishna, Pritha's son beheld a plot of earth abounding in soothing springs, teeming with gold and other minerals, burning with the effulgence of the sun or moon and possessing a large number towns and cities. He also beheld various seas and numerous rich mines of wealth.

sn: वियद् द्यां पृथिवीं चैव तथा विष्णुपदं व्रजन्। विस्मितः सह कृष्णोन क्षिप्तो बाण इवाभ्यगात्॥
en: Then wandering through the sky the firmament and the earth, he arrived at Vishnupada; there struck with admiration and like an arrow shot from the bow, he came down with Krishna.

sn: ग्रहनक्षत्रसोमानां सूर्याग्न्योश्च समत्विषम्। अपश्यत तदा पार्थो ज्वलन्तमिव पर्वतम्॥
en: Partha then beheld a mountain blazing as if with the effulgence of the planets, the stars, the moon, the sun and the fire.

sn: स्मासाद्य तु तं शैलं शैलाग्रे समवस्थितम्। तपोनित्यं महात्मानमपश्यद् वृषभध्वजम्॥
en: Having reached that hill he beheld that high-souled Divinity having the bull for his emblem on the banner, seated on its peak and lost in contemplation.

sn: सहस्रमिव सूर्याणां दीप्यमानं स्वतेजसा। शूलिनं जटिलं गौरं वल्कलाजिनवाससम्॥
en: He saw the god burning in his own energy like a thousand suns; holding the trident; with matted locks on his head; of milk-white complexion; and wearing barks and tiger skins.

sn: नयनानां सहस्रश्च विचित्राङ्गं महौजसम्। पार्वत्या सहितं देवं भूतसंधैश्च भास्वरैः॥
en: He was the highly puissant god having his body rendered beautiful with a thousand eyes; and in company with Parvati and numerous other beings of great effulgence.

sn: गीतवादित्रसंनादैर्हास्यलास्यसमन्वितम्। वल्गितास्फोटितोत्क्रुष्टैः पुण्यैर्गन्धैश्च सेवितम्॥
en: The dependents of the god were engaged in singing, in playing upon musical instruments, in dancing, in laughing, in frolicking about and stricking and clapping their palms. The place was also made fragrant with perfumes.

sn: स्तूयमानं स्तवैद्रिव्यैर्ऋषिभिर्ब्रह्मवादिभिः। गोप्तारं सर्वभूतानामिष्वासधरमच्युतम्॥
en: Arjuna then beheld that protector of all creatures, that undeteriorating wielder of the bow (Pinaka), eulogised with beautiful panegyrics by the sages and the reciters of the Vedas.

sn: वासुदेवस्तु तं दृष्ट्वा जगाम शिरसा क्षितिम्। पार्थेन सह धर्मात्मा गृणन् ब्रह्म सनातनम्॥
