en: Beholding the god, the pious-souled son of Vasudeva, together with the son of Pritha, saluted him by touching the earth with his head; and he uttered then the eternal verses from the Vedas.

sn: लोकार्दि विश्वकर्माणमजमीशानमव्ययम्। मनसः परमं योनि खं वायुं ज्योतिषां निधिम्॥ स्रष्टारं वारिधाराणां भुवश्च प्रकृति पराम्। देवदानवयक्षाणां मानवानां च साधनम्॥ योगानां च परं धाम दृष्टं ब्रह्मविदां निधिम्। चराचरस्य स्रष्टारं प्रतिहारमेव च॥ कालकोपं महात्मानं शक्रसूर्यगुणोदयम्। ववन्दे तं तदा कृष्णो वाङ्मनोबुद्धिकर्मभिः॥
en: Then Krishna adored with his speech, his mind, his intellect and his acts that origin of the worlds; that creator of the universe; that unborn divinity; that lord paramount; that undeteriorating che; that primary source from which the mind has sprung; that receptacle of the space, the wind and the luminary bodies; that creator of the rain; that primordial essence of the earth; that one worthy of the reverence of the celestials, the Danavas, the Yakshas and the human beings; that one who is the highest Brahma realised by the Yogins; that protector of those versed in the Vedas; that creator and destroyer of the mobile and immobile creatures, that God whose anger is destruction; that supreme soul; that one who is equal to Shakra or the sun.

sn: यं प्रपद्यन्ति विद्वांसः सूक्ष्माध्यात्मपदैषिणः। तमजं कारणात्मानं जग्मतुः शरणं भवम्॥
en: Then Krishna and Arjuna sought the protection of that Bhava who is uncreate the unmanifest cause and whom sages learned in the Vedas worship when they desire to obtain the subtle and spiritual existence.

sn: अर्जुनश्चापि तं देवं भूयो भूयोऽप्यवन्दता ज्ञात्वा तं सर्वभूतादि भूतभव्यभवोद्भवम्॥
en: Arjuna also worshipped that Deity over and over again, knowing him to be origin of all creatures and the cause of the Past, the Present and the Future.

sn: ततस्तावागतौ दृष्ट्वा नरनारायणावुभौ। सुप्रसन्नमनाः शर्वः प्रोवाच प्रहसन्निव॥
en: Then beholding them two, viz., Nara and Narayana come to him, Sharva with a delightful heart said these words, as if smiling the whileस्वागतं वो नरश्रेष्ठावुत्तिष्ठेतां गतक्लमौ।

sn: किं च वामीप्सितं वीरौ मनसः क्षिप्रमुच्यताम्॥
en: All hail, O you two foremost of men! Arise and let the fatigue of your journey be shaken off. Tell me soon that things your minds earn after, O you heroes!

sn: येन कार्येण सम्प्राप्तौ युवां तत् साधयामि किम्। वियतामात्मनः श्रेयस्तत् सर्वे प्रददानि वाम्॥
en: What business of yours has brought you here? I will perform it. Ask for the boon that will benefit you? I will grant all your desire.

sn: ततस्तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा प्रत्युत्थाय कृताञ्जली। वासुदेवार्जुनौ सर्वं तुष्टुवाते महामती॥ भक्त्या स्तवेन दिव्येन महात्मानाविनिन्दितौ॥
en: Hearing these words of the god, Vasudeva and Arjuna rose up with their palms folded;
and they both endued with great intelligence and of unblamable character, out of reverence, began to eulogise the high-souled Sharva with beautiful panegyrics.

sn: कृष्णार्जुनावूचतुः नमो भवाय शर्वाय रुद्राय वरदाय च। पशूनां पतये नित्यमुग्राय च कपर्दिने॥
en: Krishna and Arjuna said Salutation to Bhava, to Sharva and to Rudra the giver of all boons; to the lord of all animate beings; to him who is known as Kapardin; to the great Divinity.

sn: महादेवाय भीमाय त्र्यम्बकाय च शान्तये। ईशानाय मखघ्नाय नमोऽस्त्वन्धकघातिने॥
en: To Bhima; to the three-eyed god who is identical with peace; to Isha and to him who annihilates all pride engendered by the possession of prosperity. Salutation to the slayer of Andhaka;

sn: कुमारगुरवे तुभ्यं नीलग्रीवाय वेधसे। पिनाकिने हविष्याय सत्याय विभवे सदा॥
en: To the father of the Kumara (Kartikeya); unto him of blue neck and of great intelligence; unto the wielder of the Pinaka bow; unto the !.avisya; unto him who is ever attended with truth and prosperity.

sn: विलोहिताय धूम्राय व्याधायानपराजिते। नित्यनीलशिखण्डाय शूलिने दिव्यचक्षुषे॥ होने पोत्रे त्रिनेत्राय व्याधाय वसुरेतसे। अचिनत्यायाम्बिकाभर्ने सर्वदेवस्तुताय च॥ वृषध्वजाय मुण्डाय जटिने ब्रह्मचारिणे। तप्यमानाय सलिले ब्रह्मण्यायाजिताय च॥ विश्वात्मने विश्वसृजे विश्वमावृत्य तिष्ठते। नमो नमस्ते सेव्याय भूतानां प्रभवे सदा॥
en: To him who is red; who is tawny, who is the hunter in disguise; and who is unvanquished; unto his who possesses blue locks, who wields the trident, who is omniscient; unto him who is the Hotri and the Pitri; unto him of three-eyes, who is disease and whose vital seed is fire itself; unto him who is inconceivable, who is the lord of the goddess Ambika; who receives homage from all creatures; whose emblem is the bull; whose head is shaved and who wears matted locks and who is again a Brahmacharin, unto him who performs ascetic austerities in the waters, who is devote to the study of the Vedas and who is unvanquished. Unto him who is the soul of the universe, its creator and remains pervading it. Salutation unto him worthy of the homage of all creatures and the origin of all creatures; unto the Brahmachakra, the Sharva, the Shankara and Shiva.

sn: ब्रह्मवक्त्राय सर्वाय शङ्कराय शिवाय च। नमोऽस्तु वाचस्पतये प्रजानां पतये नमः॥
en: Salutations be unto him who is the lord of speech and the master of the created beings; salutation unto the lord of the universe and of the great people.

sn: नमो विश्वस्य पतये महतां पतये नमः। नमः सहस्रशिरसे सहस्रभुजमृत्यवे॥
en: Salutations unto him of thousand heads who possesses a thousand arms and who is Death himself. Salutations unto him of thousand eyes and legs, whose deeds are countless.

sn: सहस्रनेत्रपादाय नमोऽसंख्येयकर्मणे। नमो हिरण्यवर्णाय हिरण्यकवचाय च। भक्तानुकम्पिने नित्यं सिध्यतां नो वरः प्रभौ॥
en: Salutations unto him of the complexion of gold, who is clad in a armour of gold; and unto him who is ever gracious upon his devotees. O lord let our desires be fulfilled.

sn: संजय उवाच एवं स्तुत्वा महादेवं वासुदेवः सहार्जुनः। प्रसादयामास भवं तदा शस्त्रोपलब्धये॥
en: Sanjaya said Thus having eulogised the great god, Arjuna and the son of Vasudeva began to propitiate the former for obtaining the weapon (Pasupata) from him.

description: The obtaining of the Pasupata weapon
sn: संजय उवाच ततः पार्थः प्रसन्नात्मा प्राञ्जलिर्वृषभध्वजम्। ददर्शोत्फुल्लनयनः समस्तं तेजसां निधिम्॥
en: Sanjaya said Then the son of Pritha with a delightful soul and joined palms and eyes expanded in amazement, gazed at the god having the bull for his banner-mark and the receptacle of all energies.

description: The obtaining of the Pasupata weapon
sn: तं चोपहारं सुकृतं नैशं नैत्यकमात्मना। ददर्श त्र्यम्बकाभ्याशे वासुदेवनिवेदितम्॥
en: He then beheld by the side of the three-eyed god, the offerings he used to make, every night, to the son of Vasudeva.

description: The obtaining of the Pasupata weapon
sn: ततोऽभिपूज्य मनसा कृष्णं शर्वं च पाण्डवः। इच्छाम्यहं दिव्यमस्त्रमित्यभाषत शङ्करम्॥
en: Thereafter that son of Pandu having worshipped in his mind both Sharva and Krishna, said unto the gold Sankara-'I desire to have the celestial weapon (Pasupata)!'

description: The obtaining of the Pasupata weapon
sn: ततः पार्थस्य विज्ञाय वरार्थे वचनं तदा। वासुदेवार्जुनौ देवः स्मयमानोऽभ्यभाषत॥
en: Then having heard the words of Pritha's son, that disclosed that boon he wanted, the god (Mahadeva) with a smile, thus replied to Vasudeva's son and Arjunaस्वागतं वां नरश्रेष्ठौ विज्ञातं मनसेप्सितम्।

description: The obtaining of the Pasupata weapon
sn: वेन कामेन सम्प्राप्तौ भवद्भ्यां तं ददाम्यहम्॥
en: All hail, O you two foremost of men, I have known the desire of your hearts; I shall grant even that desire of yours which has brought you both here.

description: The obtaining of the Pasupata weapon
sn: सरोऽसृतमयं दिव्यमभ्याशे शत्रुसूदनौ। तत्र मे तद् धनुर्दिव्यं शश्च निहितः पुरा॥
en: You slayers of foes, there is a heavenly lake of nectar not far from this place; in days gone by, I laid down my celestial bow and arrows there.

description: The obtaining of the Pasupata weapon
sn: येन देवारयः सर्वे मया युधि निपातिताः। तत आनीयतां कृष्णौ सशरं धनुरुत्तमम्॥
en: With that bow and arrow, I slew in battle all the enemies of the gods. From that lake bring, O Krishnas, that excellent bow and arrow of mine.

description: The obtaining of the Pasupata weapon
sn: अथेत्युक्त्वा तु तौ वीरौ सर्वपारिषदैः सह। प्रस्थितौ तत्सरो दिव्यं दिव्यैश्वर्यशतैर्युतम्॥
en: Thereupon saying 'year to the words of Siva, the two heroes with all their followers, went to that celestial lake possessed hundreds of celestial wonders.

description: The obtaining of the Pasupata weapon
sn: निर्दिष्टं यद् वृषाङ्केण पुण्यं सर्वार्थसाधकम्। तौ जग्मतुरसम्भ्रान्तौ नरनारायणावृषी॥
en: Then those two sages Nara and Narayana fearlessly went to that holy lake capable of fulfilling all desires, that had been indicated by the god having the bull for his emblem.

description: The obtaining of the Pasupata weapon
sn: ततस्तौ तत् सरो गत्वा सूर्यमण्डलसंनिभम्। नागमन्तर्जले घोरं ददृशातेऽर्जुनाच्युतौ॥
en: Thereafter Arjuna and the undeteriorating Krishna having repaired to that lake of the effulgence of the solar disc, saw in its waters a terrible serpent.

description: The obtaining of the Pasupata weapon
sn: द्वितीयं चापरं नाग सहस्रशिरसं वरम्। मन्तं विपुला ज्वाला ददृशातेऽग्निवर्चसम्॥
en: They also saw there another foremost of snakes possessing a thousands hoods, of the effulgence of fire; it was then vomiting terrible flames.

description: The obtaining of the Pasupata weapon
sn: ततः कृष्णश्च पार्थश्च संस्पृश्याम्भः कृताञ्जली। तौ नागावुपतस्थाते नमस्यन्तौ वृषध्वजम्॥
en: Then Krishna and Partha, having touched water and having folded their palms and saluted the god having the bull of his emblem, approached those snakes.

description: The obtaining of the Pasupata weapon
sn: गृणन्तौ वेदविद्वांसौ तद् ब्रह्म शतरुद्रियम्। अप्रमेयं प्रणमतो गतवा सर्वात्मना भवम्॥
en: As they approached the snakes, learned as they were in the Vedas, they recited the hundred slokas in the Veda to the praise of Rudra, saluting all the time with all their heart, Bhava of infinite might. arrow

description: The obtaining of the Pasupata weapon
sn: ततस्तो रुद्रमाहात्म्याद्धित्वा रूपं महोरगौ। धुनर्बाणश्च शत्रुधं तद् द्वन्द्वंद्व समपद्यत॥
en: Then through the charm of those adorations offered to Rudra, those two snakes forsook their snake forms and assumed the forms of a bow and arrow capable of slaying the enemy.

description: The obtaining of the Pasupata weapon
sn: तौ तज्ज्गृहतुः प्रीतौ धनुर्बाणं च सुप्रभम्। आजह्रतुर्महात्मानौ ददतुश्च महात्मने॥
en: Then highly delighted, they both took up those effulgent weapons, the bow and the arrow. Then those two high-souled ones, gave that bow and to the illustrious Mahadeva.

description: The obtaining of the Pasupata weapon
sn: ततः पार्वाद् वृषाङ्कस्य ब्रह्मचारी न्यवर्तत। पिङ्गाक्षस्तपसः क्षेत्रं बलवान् नीललोहितः॥
en: Thereafter from one of the sides of Siva's body, a Brahmacharin issued forth; his eyes were tawny and he seemed to be the refuge of all asceticism. Having blue throat and red hair, he was possessed of great energy.

description: The obtaining of the Pasupata weapon
sn: स तद् गृह्य धनुःश्रेष्ठं तस्थौ स्थानं समाहितः। विचकर्षाथ विधिवत् सशरं धनुरुत्तमम्॥
en: Then that Brahmacharin taking up that most excellent bow stood in the proper posture. And placing the arrow on the string he began to stretch the latter duly.

description: The obtaining of the Pasupata weapon
sn: तस्य मौर्वी च मुष्टिं च स्थानं चालक्ष्य पाण्डवः। श्रुत्वा मन्त्रं भवप्रोक्तं जग्राहाचिन्त्यविक्रमः॥
en: Thereupon, seeing the mode of his grasping the bow, drawing the string, placing his legs and hearing also the mantras uttered by Bhava, Pandu's son of infinite prowess duly learnt them all.

description: The obtaining of the Pasupata weapon
sn: स सरस्येव तं बाणं मुमोचातिबलः प्रभुः। चकार च पुनर्वीरस्तस्मिन् सरसि तद्धनुः॥
en: When the mighty and powerful Brahmacharin, shot that arrow even to the lake whence it had been brought; he also threw that bow into the self-same lake.

description: The obtaining of the Pasupata weapon
sn: ततः प्रीतं भवं ज्ञात्वा स्मृतिमानर्जुनस्तदा। वरमारण्यके दत्तं दर्शनं शङ्करस्य च॥
en: Thereupon Arjuna gifted with an accurate memory knowing that Bhavas was pleased with him and recollecting the boon the latter had accorded to him in the forest and the sight of his person he had vouchsafed to reveal to him.

description: The obtaining of the Pasupata weapon
sn: मनसा चिन्तयामास तन्मे सम्पद्यतामिति। तस्य तन्मतमाज्ञाय प्रीतः प्रादाद् वरं भवः॥
en: Desired in his mind that all this might be true, thinking-'May all this be productive of fruit.' Knowing this to be his desire, Bhava pleased with him, gave him the boon.

description: The obtaining of the Pasupata weapon
sn: तच्च पाशुपतं घोरं प्रतिज्ञायाश्च पारणम्। ततः पाशुपतं दिव्यमवाप्य पुनरीश्वरात्॥
en: He also granted him the terrible Pasupata weapon and the fulfilment of his vow. Then having obtained the Pasupata weapon of celestial make, once more, from the Lord.

description: The obtaining of the Pasupata weapon
sn: संहष्टरोमा दुर्धर्षः कृतं कार्यममन्यत। ववन्दतुश्च संहृष्टौ शिरोभ्यां तं महेश्वरम्॥
en: The invincible Arjuna, with the down of his body erect, consider his vow already fulfiled. Then with delighted hearts, they (Krishna and Arjuna) saluted the god Maheshvara, by bending their heads low.

description: The obtaining of the Pasupata weapon
sn: अनुज्ञातौ क्षणे तस्मिन् भवेनार्जुनकेशवौ। प्रापतौ स्वशिविरं वीरौ मुदा परमया युतौ॥
en: Even at that moment obtaining the permission of Bhava, the two heroes Arjuna and Krishna, transported with delight came back to their own encampment.

description: The obtaining of the Pasupata weapon
sn: तथा भवेनानुमतौ महासुरनिघातिना। इन्द्राविष्णू यथा प्रीतौजम्भस्य वधकाक्षिणौ॥
en: Indeed their joy was as great as that which filled Indra and Vishnu when those two deities, desirous of slaying Jambha, had secured the permission of Bhava (to do so), the slayer of mighty Asuras.

sn: संजय उवाच तयोः संवदतोरेवं कृष्णदारुकयोस्तथा। सात्यगाद् रजनी राजन्नथ राजाऽनवबुध्यत॥
en: Sanjaya said When Krishna and Daruka were thus talking to one another, O king, the night drew to its close. At day-break, king (Yudhishthira) Rose from his bed.

sn: पठन्ति पाणिस्वनिका मागधा मधुपर्किकाः। वैतालिकाश्च सूताश्च तुष्टुवुः पुरुषर्षभम्॥
en: The Panisvanikas, the Magadhas, the Madhuparkikas began to read verses in his praise; and Vaitalikas and minstrels began to eulogise that foremost of men (Yudhishthira).

sn: नर्तकाश्चाप्यनृत्यन्त जगुर्गीतानि गायकाः। कुरुवंशस्तवार्थानि मधुरं रक्तकण्ठिनः॥
en: The dancers commenced dancing, songsters gifted with melodious voices, began to sing charming songs frought with praises of the Kuru dynasty.

sn: मृदङ्गा झर्झरा भेर्यः एणवानकगोमुखाः। आडम्बराश्च शङ्खाश्च दुन्दुभ्यश्च महास्वनाः॥
en: Mridangas, Jhanjharas, Bheri, Panavas, Anakas, Gomukhas, Adambaras, conchs and Dundubhis of fierce sounds.

sn: एवमेतानि सर्वाणि तथान्यान्यपि भारत। वादयन्ति सुसंहृष्टाः कुशलाः साधुशिक्षिताः॥
en: These and many other such musical instruments, were, O Bharata, played upon by well-trained and expert performers, all of them being transported with joy.

sn: स मेघसमनि?षो महाशब्दोऽस्पृशद् दिवम्। पार्थिवप्रवरं सुप्तं युधिष्ठिरमबोधयत्॥
en: The loud din (thus produced) resembling the rumbling of clouds, reached the very heavens themselves; and it awakened that foremost of all rulers of earth viz., king Yudhishthira, from his sleep.

sn: प्रतिबुद्धः सुखं सुप्तो महार्हे शयनोत्तमे। उत्थायावश्यकार्यार्थं ययौ स्नानगृहं नृपंः॥
en: Having enjoyed an undisturbed sleep on his precious and excellent bed, king Yudhishthira awoke (in the morning). Then rising up, the king retired to the bath-room, for performing acts that must be performed (sandhyas).

sn: ततः शुक्लाम्बराः स्नातास्तरुणाः शतमष्ट च। स्नापकाः काञ्चनैः कुम्भैः पूर्णैः समुएतस्थिरे॥
en: There, a hundred and eight orderlies robed in white garments, all washed and of youthful age, approached the king with many a golden jar filled (with water) to the very brim.

sn: भद्रासने सूपविष्टः परिधायाम्बरं लघु। सस्नौ चन्दनसंयुक्तैः पानीयैरभिमन्त्रितैः॥
en: Seated at his ease on an auspicious seat and vested in a garment of fine texture, the king bathed in waters fragrant with sandal-wood and sanctified with religious aphorisms.

sn: उत्सादितः कषायेण बलवद्भिः सुशिक्षितैः। आप्लुतः साधिवासेन जलेन स सुगन्धिना॥
en: His limbs were shampooed by strong and well-trained servants, with water that had been rendered bitter, with medicinal drugs. He was then washed with holy Adivasa-water fragrant with perfumes.

sn: राजहंसनिभं प्राप्य उष्णीषं शिथिलार्पितम्। जलक्षयनिमित्तं वै वेष्टयामास मूर्धनि॥
en: Then being furnished with a piece of cloth that was as white as the plumage of the swan and that had been lying loose there, the king encircled his head with it in order to rub off the water therefrom.

sn: हरिणा चन्दनेनाङ्गमुपलिप्य महाभुजः। स्रग्वी चाक्लिष्टवसनः प्राङ्मुखः प्राञ्जलिः स्थितः।।
en: Thereafter that mighty-armed one, having smeared his body with the paste of Hari-sandal and decorated his person with garlands and flowers and dressed in stainless garments, sat with his palms folded, facing the east.

sn: जजाप जप्यं कौन्तेय सतां मार्गमनुष्ठितः। तत्राग्निशरणं दीप्तं प्रविवेश विनीतवत्॥
en: Then, ever following in the wake of the righteous, the son of Kunti reiterated the prayers that should be done so; and then with becoming meekness, he entered the chamber where the blazing fire was kept (for adoration).

sn: समिद्भिः सपवित्राभिरग्निमाहुतिभिस्तथा। मन्त्रपूताभिरर्चित्वा निश्चक्राम गृहात् ततः॥
en: Then having worshipped the fire with holy and purified faggots and religious aphorisms, the monarch came out of the fire-chamber.

sn: द्वितीयां पुरुषव्याघ्रः कक्ष्यां निर्गम्य पार्थिवः। ततो वेदविदो वृद्धानपश्यद् ब्राह्मणर्षभान्॥
en: Then entering into a second chamber, that foremost of men king Yudhishthira saw a number of venerable old Brahmanas wellversed in the Vedas and all foremost of their order.

sn: दान्तान् वेदव्रतस्नातान् स्नातानवभृथेषु च। सहस्रानुचरान् सौरान् सहस्रं चाप्ट चापरान्॥
en: They were all self-restrained and had performed ablutions after the accomplishment of sacrifices, vows and recital of the Vedas. Worshippers of the sun, they counted a thousand in number with one thousand and eight followers.

sn: अक्षतैः सुमनोभिश्च वाचयित्वा महाभुजः। तान् द्विजान् मधुसर्पि• फलैः श्रेष्ठैः सुमङ्गलैः॥ प्रादात् काञ्चनमेकैकं निष्कं विप्राय पाण्डवः। अलंकृतं चाश्वशतं वासांसीष्टाश्च दक्षिणाः॥
en: The mighty armed son of Pandu having caused these Brahmanas to pronounce, in clear voices, benedictions on him, by making presents of honey, clarified butter and delicious fruits of the best sort, gave away to every one them a Niksha of gold, a hundred steeds adorned with golden caparisons and precious garments and other presents that were liked by them.

sn: तथा गा: कपिला दोन्ध्री: सवत्साः पाण्डुनन्दनः। हेमशृङ्गा रौप्यखुरा दत्त्वा चक्रे प्रदक्षिणम्॥
en: Then the son of Pandu, giving unto them milch cow, that yielded milk whenever touched, with calves and with their horns and hoofs decked with gold and silver respectively, circumambulated them.

sn: स्वस्तिकान् वर्धमानांश्च नन्द्यावर्ताश्च काञ्चनान्। माल्यं च जलकुम्भांश्च ज्वलितं च हुताशनम्॥
en: Auspicious objects capable of increasing good fortune, golden Nandyavartas, garlands of flowers, jars of water, blazing fire.

sn: पूर्णान्यक्षतपात्राणि रुचकं रोचनास्तथा। स्वलंकृताः शुभाः कन्या दधिसर्पिर्मधूदकम्॥
en: Vessels filled to the brim and containing Askhotas (sun-dried rice) and the yellow pigment prepared from the urine of the cow and also well-decked and beautiful maidens and curds and clarified butter and honey and water.

sn: मङ्गल्यान् पक्षिणश्चैव यच्चान्यदपि पूजितम्। दृष्ट्वास्पृष्ट्वा च कौन्तेयो बाह्यां कक्ष्यां ततोऽगमत्।।
en: And auspicious birds and other things considered to be holy-seeing and touching these things, the son of Kunti proceeded to the outer apartments.

sn: ततस्तस्यां महाबाहोस्तिष्ठतः परिचारकाः। सौवर्णं सर्वतोभद्रं मुक्तावैदूर्यमण्डितम्॥ पराास्तरणास्तीर्णं सोत्तरच्छदमृद्धिमत्। विश्वकर्मकृतं दिव्यसुपजहुर्वरासनम्॥
en: There, O mighty armed one the attendants that were in waiting, brought the monarch an excellent throne (to sit upon)-throne that was wholly made of gold and of auspicious marks and adorned with pearls and lapises; this throne made by the celestial artificer Vishvakarman and was over-spread with a precious carpet which again was covered by a stuff of very fine texture.

sn: तत्र तस्योपविष्टस्य भूषणानि महात्मनः। उपाजहुर्महार्हाणि प्रेष्याः शुभ्राणि सर्वशः॥
en: Then when that high-souled one had seated himself on that throne, his orderlies brought him all his precious and glittering ornaments,

sn: मुक्ताभरणवेषस्य कौन्तेयस्य महात्मनः। रूपमासीन्महाराज द्विषतां शोकवर्धनम्॥
en: Then, O mighty monarch, the appearance of the illustrious son of Kunti who was adorned was with pearls and various ornaments was such as to excite the jealousy of his foes.

sn: चामरैश्चन्द्ररश्म्याभैहेमदण्डैः सुशोभनैः। दोधूयमानैः शुशुभे विद्युद्भिरिव तोयदः॥
en: Then fanned with yak-tails furnished with handles of gold and of white effulgence outvying the charming beams of the moon, the monarch shone like a mass of cloud emitting flashes of lightning.

sn: संस्तूयमानः सूतैश्च वन्द्यमानश्च बन्दिभिः। उपगीयमानो गन्धर्वैरास्ते स्म कुरुनन्दनः॥
en: That delighter of the Kurus then, was praised by all creatures, the minstrels gratified him with panegyrics; and the Gandharvas then began to sing at his hearing.

sn: ततो मुहूर्तादासीत् तु स्यन्दनानां स्वनो महान्। नेमियोपश्च रथिनां सुरघोषश्च वाजिनाम्॥
en: Thereafter within a moment the voices of the bards swelled to a tremendous sound; and instantly were there heard the clatter of the carwheels of car-warriors and the hoof-sounds of the cavalry.

sn: ह्रादेन गजघण्टानां शङ्खानां निनदेन च। नराणां पदशब्दैश्च कम्पतीव स्म मेदिनी॥
en: With the tinkling of bells tied round the necks of the elephants, with the blasts of conchs and with the sound of the measured) foot-fall of the infantry, the earth began to quake.

sn: ततः शुद्धान्तमासाद्य जानुभ्यां भूतले स्थितः। शिरसा वन्दनीयं तमभिवाद्य जनेश्वरम्॥ कुण्डली बद्धनिस्त्रिंशः संनद्धकवचो युवा। अभिप्रणम्य शिरसा द्वा:स्थो धर्मात्मजाय वै॥ न्यवेदयद्धृषीकेशमुपयान्तं महात्मने। सोऽब्रवीत् पुरुषव्याघ्रः स्वागतेनैव माधवम्॥
en: Then one of the attendants guarding the doors, cased in armour, youthful, adorned with ear-rings and having his sword tied to his waist-band, entered the private chamber of the very virtuous king Yudhishthira; then kneeling down before him and doing obeisance to the worshipful and illustrious monarch with his head, he represented that Hrishikesha was waiting to be ushered in. Thereupon that foremost of men (Yudhishthira) welcomed Madhava with inquiries after his health and welfare.

sn: अयं चैवासनं चास्मै दीयतां परमार्चितम्। ततः प्रवेश्य वार्ष्णेयमुपवेश्य वरासने। पूजयामास विधिवद् धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: He also ordered his attendants saying, "Give to this one an excellent seat and offer him a Argha.” Then when he of the Vrishni race was ushered in, the very virtuous king Yudhishthira caused him to be seated on an excellent seat and worshipped him with proper ceremonies.

sn: संजय उवाच ततो युधिष्ठिरो राजा प्रतिनन्द्य जनार्दनम्। उवाच परमप्रीतः कौन्तेयो देवकीसुतम्॥
en: Sanjaya said King Yudhishthira the son of Kunti then welcoming the son of Devaki, that assuager of the grief of men, cheerfully addressed the following words to himसुखेन रजनी व्युष्टा कच्चित् ते मधुसूदन।

sn: कच्चिज्ज्ञानानि सर्वाणि प्रसन्नानि तवाच्युत॥
en: "Having you, O slayer of Madhu, passed the night in happiness? Are all your senseorgans, O undeteriorating one, as keen as ever?"

sn: वासुदेवोऽपि तद्युक्तं पर्यपृच्छद् युधिष्ठिरम्। ततश्च प्रकृतीः क्षत्ता न्यवेदयदुपस्थिताः॥
en: The son of Vasudeva also put similar questions to Yudhishthira. Then an orderly came there and said that other Kshatriya warriors were waiting to be ushered in.

sn: अनुज्ञातश्च राज्ञा स प्रावेशयत तं जनम्। विराटं भीमसेनं च धृष्टद्युम्नं च सात्यकिम्॥ चेदिपं धृष्टकेतुं च द्रुपदं च महारथम्। शिखण्डिनं यमो चैव चेकितानं सकेकयम्॥ युयुत्सुं चैव कौरव्यं पाञ्चाल्यं चोत्तमौजसम्। युधामन्युं सुबाहुं च द्रौपदेयांश्च सर्वशः॥
en: Permitted by the king, the orderly introduced that influx of men, numbering it, Virat, Bhimasena, Dhristadyumna and Satyaki and the ruler of the Chedis, Dhrishtaketu the mighty car-warriors Drupada, Sikhandin, the twins Nakula and Sahadeva, Chekitana with the prince of the Kekayas. As also Yuyutsu of Kuru race and Uttamaujas of the Panchala tribe and Yudhamanyu and Subahu and the five sons of Draupadi.

sn: एते चान्ये च बहवः क्षत्रियाः क्षत्रियर्षभम्। उपतस्थुर्महात्मानं विविशुश्चासने शुभे॥
en: These and many other Kshatriyas approached that best of Kshatriyas of illustrious fame; and they sat down on auspicious seats.

sn: एकस्मिन्नासने वीरावुपविष्टौ महाबलौ। कृष्णश्च युयुधानश्च महात्मानौ महाद्युती॥
en: The two mighty heroes, Krishna and Yuyudhana, of illustrious souls and great effulgence, both sat on a single seat.

sn: ततो युधिष्ठिरस्तेषां श्रृण्वतां मधुसूदनम्। अब्रवीत् पुण्डरीकाक्षमाभाष्य मधुरं वचः॥
en: Thereafter king Yudhishthira, at the hearing of those assembled Kshatriyas, said these sweet words addressing that slayer of Madhu, who

sn: एकं त्वां वयमाश्रित्य सहस्राक्षमिवामराः। प्रार्थमायो जयं युद्धे शाश्वतानि सुखानि च॥
en: Like celestials depending on the strength of the thousand-eyed (Indra), we relying on you alone, seek victory in battle and eternal happiness.

sn: त्वं हि राज्यविनाशं न द्विषद्भिश्चनिराक्रियाम्। क्लेशांश्च विविधान् कृष्ण सर्वांस्तानपि वेद नः॥
en: You, () Krishna, know all about the despoliation of our kingdom, our exile by the that, my enemy and also all the miseries we had to suffer.

sn: त्वयि सर्वेश सर्वेषामस्माकं भक्तवत्सल। सुखमायत्तमत्यर्थे यात्रा च मधुसूदन॥
en: O Lord of everything, O you who are merciful to all devoted to you, upon you rest all our happiness and even our existence, O slayer of Madhu.

sn: स तथा कुरु वार्ष्णेय यथा त्वयि मनो मम। अर्जुनस्य यथा सत्या प्रतिज्ञा स्याच्चिकीर्षिता॥
en: O descendant of the Vrishni race, so do you manage heart may always rely on you and Arjuna's oath may remain inviolate.

sn: स भवांस्तारयत्वस्माद् दुःखामर्षमहार्णवात्। पारं तितीर्षतामद्य प्लवो नो भव माधव॥
en: Help us to cross this veritable ocean of grief and wrath. O Madhava, be you our raft today, as we desire to cross this ocean (of troubles).

sn: न हि तत् कुरुते संख्ये रथी रिपुवधोद्यतः। यथा वै कुरुते कृष्ण सारथिर्यलमास्थितः॥
en: A car-warrior desirous of slaying his adversary cannot, in battle, do that (to achieve his purpose) which, O Krishna, his driver can do, if this latter strides with due caution.

sn: यथैव सर्वास्वापत्सु पासि वृष्णीञ्जनार्दन। तथैवास्मान् महाबाहो वृजिनात् त्रातुमर्हसि॥
en: O mighty-armed Janardana, as you save the Vrishnis from all calamities, so also, it behoves you to save us from this impending ruin.

sn: त्वमगाधेऽप्लवे मग्नान् पाण्डवान् कुरुसागरे। समुद्धर प्लवो भूत्वा शङ्खचक्रगदाधर॥
en: O you the bearer of the conch, the discus and the mace, do you save the sons of Pandu sunk in the deep and boatless Kurn ocean, by becoming even a boat to them.

sn: नमस्ते देवदेवेश सनातन विशातन। विष्णो जिष्णो हरे कृष्ण वैकुण्ठ पुरुषोत्तम॥
en: Salutations unto you, the Lord of the foremost of celestials, the eternal one, the supreme destroyer, O Vishnu, O Jishnu, O Hari, O Krishna, O Vaikuntha and.O foremost of all male beings.

sn: नारदस्त्वां समाचख्यौ पुराणमृषिसत्तमम्। वरदं शाङ्गिणं श्रेष्ठं तत् सत्यं कुरु माधव॥
en: Narada had pronounced you to be that best and most ancient of sages viz., (Narayana), who accord boons, who wields the Sharnga bow and who are the foremost of all. Make, O Madhava, all these words true.

sn: इत्युक्तः पुण्डरीकाक्षो धर्मराजेन संसदि। तोयमेघस्वनो वाग्मी प्रत्युवाच युधिष्ठिरम्॥
en: Thus spoken to in the midst of the assembly by the very virtuous king Yudhishthira, that most fluent speaker Keshava replied to the former, in a voice sonorous like the rumbling of clouds charged with rain.

sn: वासुदेव उवाच सामरेष्वपि लोकेषु सर्वेषु न तथाविधः। शरासनधरः कश्चिद् यथा पार्थो धनजंयः॥
en: Krishna said In all the worlds, including the regions of celestials, there is no such wielder of bow who can equal Dhananjaya the son of Pritha.

sn: वीर्यवानस्त्रसम्पन्नः पराक्रान्तो महाबलः। युद्धशोण्डः सदामर्षी तेजसा परमो नृणाम्॥
en: Endowed with energy, accomplished in the use of weapons, possessed of great prowess and might, ever brave in battle and wrathful and agile, he is the foremost of all men.

sn: स युवा वृषभस्कन्धो दीर्घबाहुर्महाबलः। सिंहर्षभगतिः श्रीमान् द्विषतस्ते हनिष्यति॥
en: Moreover is youthful, of shoulders strong like those of the bull, of long-arms and mighty prowess; his gait resembles that of the lion itself. That handsome hero will slay all your enemies.

sn: अहं च तत् करिष्यामि यथा कुन्तीसुतोऽर्जुनः। धार्तराष्ट्रस्य सैन्यानि धक्ष्यत्यग्निरिवेन्धनम्॥
en: On my part, I shall so act as Kunti's son Arjuna may be able to consume the troops of Dhritarashtra's son, like raging conflagration.

sn: अद्य तं पापकर्माणं क्षुद्रं सौभद्रघातिनम्। अपुनर्दर्शनं मार्गमिषुभिः क्षेप्स्यतेऽर्जुनः॥
en: even Even this very day, with the help of his arrows, Arjuna will compel that one of sinful acts, that mean-minded slayer of Subhadra's son viz., Jayadratha, to travel on a road from which no traveller ever returns.

sn: तस्याद्य गृध्राः श्येनाश्च चण्डगोमायवस्तथा। भक्षयिष्यन्ति मांसानि ये चान्ये पुरुषादकाः॥
en: The vultures, the hawks, the fierce jackals and other carnivorous animals, will today hold a feast on the flesh of that one.

sn: यद्यस्य देवा गोप्तारः सेन्द्राः सर्वे तथाप्यसौ। राजधानी यमस्याद्य हतः प्राप्स्यति संकुले॥
en: O Yudhishthira, even if the Gods with Indra at their head today become the protectors of Jayadratha, yet, slain in the thick of the fight, he shall undoubtedly be borne to the capital of Death's domain.

sn: निहत्य सैन्धवं जिष्णुरद्य त्वामुपयास्यति। विशोको विज्वरो राजन् भव भूतिपुरस्कृतः॥
en: The victorious Arjuna shall this day come to you, having slain in battle the ruler of the Sindhus. Dismiss the grief of your heart and free yourself of the fever of anxiety and O king, be you attended with prosperity!

sn: संजय उवाच तथा तु वदतां तेषां प्रादुरासीद् धनंजयः। दिक्षुर्भरतश्रेष्ठं राजानं ससुहृद्गणम्॥
en: Sanjaya said When they were thus conversing, Dhananjaya appeared there, desirous of seeing that foremnost of Bharatas, viz., king Yudhishthira and his relatives.

sn: तं निविष्टं शुभां कक्ष्यामभिवन्द्याग्रतः स्थितम्। तमुत्थायार्जुनं प्रेम्णा सस्वजे पाण्डवर्षभः॥
en: When he had entered that auspicious chamber and was standing before the king, having saluted him duly, that foremost of the Pandavas (king Yudhishthira) rose from his। seat and out of affection, embraced Arjuna.

sn: मूनि चैनमुपाघ्राय परिष्वज्य च बाहुना। आशिषः परमाः प्रोच्य स्मयमानोऽभ्यभाषत॥
en: Having locked Arjuna in his affectionate embrace and having smelled the crown of his head and pronouncing best benedictions of

sn: व्यक्तमर्जुन संग्रामे ध्रुवस्ते विजयो महान्। याग्रूपा च ते च्छाया प्रसन्नश्च जनार्दनः॥
en: “It is evident, O Arjuna, that in today's fight a great victory is sure to court you, inasmuch as your very appearance indicates it, as also the fact that Janardana is gratified with you.”

sn: तमब्रवीत् ततो जिष्णुर्महदाश्चर्यमुत्तमम्। दृष्टवानस्मि भद्रं ते केशवस्य प्रसादजम्॥
en: Then Jishnu spoke to him of the wonderful incident (he had seen in his dream) in the following terms "May good betide, you, O monarch! Through the mercy of Keshava, I have seen a marvel."

sn: ततस्तत् कथयामास यथा दृष्टं धनंजयः। आश्वासनार्थं सुहृदां त्र्यम्बकेण समागमम्॥
en: Then, for giving very assurance to his partisans, Dhananjaya related everything he had seen in his dream-his meeting with the three eyed god.

sn: ततः शिरोभिरवर्नि स्पृष्टवा सर्वे च विस्मिताः। नमस्कृत्य वृषाङ्काय साधु साध्वित्यथाब्रुवन्॥
en: Thereupon all the hearers filled with wonder, touched the earth with their heads; and thus having bowed down to the god having the bull for his emblem, they said excellent, excellent.

sn: अनुज्ञातास्ततः सर्वे सुहृदो धर्मसूनुना। त्वरमाणा: सुसंनद्धा हृष्टा युद्धाय निर्ययुः॥
en: Then permitted by the son of Dharma, all the friends and partisans of the Pandavas, cheerfully set out for the battle with haste and with hearts swelling with rage.

sn: अभिवाद्य तु राजानं युयुधानाच्युतार्जुनाः। हृष्टा विनिर्ययुस्ते वै युधिष्ठिरनिवेशनात्॥
en: Then having saluted the king, Yuyudhana, Arjuna and Krishna of unfading glory, with cheerful hearts, issued out of the chamber of Yudhishthira.

sn: रथेनैकेन दुर्धर्षों युयुधानजनार्दनौ। जग्मतुः सहितौ वीरावर्जुनस्य निवेशनम्॥
en: Those two indomitable warriors, the heroes Yuyudhana and Janardana, riding on the same car, proceeded towards the abode of Arjuna.

sn: तत्र गत्वा हृषीकेशः कल्पयामास सूतवत्। रथं रथवरस्याजौ वानरर्षभलक्षणम्॥
en: Repairing there, Hrishikesha dressed and equipped the car of the foremost of warriors, like a profession charioteer-car that bore the device of the monkey prince on its standards.

sn: स मेघसमनिर्घोषस्तप्तकाञ्चनसप्रभः। बभौ रथवदः क्लृप्तः शिशुर्दिवसकृद् यथा॥
en: Thereupon that best of chariots of rattle resembling the rumble of clouds and of effulgence like that of heated gold, thus equipped (by Keshava), shone like the maker of day in the morning.

sn: ततः पुरुषशार्दूलः सज्जं सज्जपुरःसरः। कृताह्निकाय पार्थाय न्यवेदत तं रथम्॥
en: Thereafter that foremost of men, namely the son of Vasudeva eased in an armour, told Pritha's son who had completed his morning prayers that his chariot had been made ready.

sn: तं तु लोकवरः पुंसा किरीटी हेमवर्मभृत्। चापबाणधरो वाहं प्रदक्षिणमवर्तत॥
en: Then that foremost of all men of this world, namely, the diadem-decked Arjuna, clad in a golden cost of mail and holding his bow and arrows in his grasp, circumbulated his vehicle.

sn: तपोविद्यावयोवृद्धैः क्रियावद्भिर्जितेन्द्रियैः। स्तूयमानो जयाशीर्भिरारुरोह महारथम्॥
en: Then praised and blessed with benedictions believed to bestow victory in battle, by Brahmanas old in the performance of austerities, in knowledge and in years, ever engaged in the performance of religious rites and sacrifices and holding all their passions in subjugation, Arjuna mounted upon his mighty chariot.

sn: जैत्रैः सांग्रामिकैर्मन्त्रैः पूर्वमेव रथोत्तमम्। अभिमन्त्रितमर्चिष्मानुदयं भास्करो यथा॥
en: That excellent vehicle of his which had been previously purified with victory-giving mantras, like the sun of burning radiance ascending the Eastern mountains.

sn: स रथे रथिनां श्रेष्ठः काञ्चने काञ्चनावृतः। विबभौ विमलोऽर्चिष्मान् मेराविव दिवाकरः॥
en: Then that best of car-warriors adorned with golden ornaments, shone, in consequence of those golden ornaments of his, on his chariot, like the sun of burning radiance on the breast of the Meru mountain.

sn: अन्वारुरुहतुः पार्थे युयुधानजनार्दनौ। शर्यातेर्यज्ञमायान्तं यथेन्द्र देवमश्विनौ॥
en: After Partha, Yuyudhana and Janardana mounted on that car, like the twin Ashvinis riding on the best celestial car when they had come to the sacrifice of Sharyati.

sn: अथ जग्राह गोविन्दो रश्मीन् रश्मिविदां वरः। मातलिसिवस्येव वृत्रं हन्तुं प्रयास्यतः॥
en: The Govinda that best of charioteers took up the reins (of Arjuna's steeds)., like Matali taking up the reins of Indra's horses, when the latter went to fight in order to slay Vritra.

sn: स ताभ्यां सहितः पार्थो रथप्रवरमास्थितः। सहितोबुधशुक्राभ्यां तमोनिघ्नन् यथा शशी॥
en: Mounting on that his best of cars, with those two heroes Yuyudhana and Janardana, Pritha's son appeared like the moon dispelling darkness when rising in conduction with Budha and Shukra.

sn: सैन्धवस्य वधं प्रेप्सुः प्रयातः शत्रुपूगहा। सहाम्बुपतिमित्राभ्यां यथेन्द्रस्तारकामये॥
en: Then that slayer of large bodies of foes (Arjuna), desirous of bringing about the slaughter of the Sindhu ruler, proceeded to battle, like Indra accompanied by Varuna and the sun, proceeding to fight with the Asuras, in the battle caused by the abduction of Taraka.

sn: ततो वादित्रनिर्घोषैर्माङ्गल्यैश्च स्तवैः शुभैः। प्रायान्तमर्जुनं वीरं मागधाश्चैव तुष्टुवुः॥
en: The minstrels and musicians then greeted the heroic Arjuna as he proceeded, with the sounds of musical instruments and eulogies, auspicious and well-worded.

sn: सजयाशीः सपुण्याहः सूतमागधनिःस्वनः। युक्तो वादित्रघोषेण तेषां रतिकरोऽभवत्॥
en: The voice of the bards and the minstrels pronounced benedictions of victory; and goodday greetings became pleasing to the heroes, being mingled with the din of musical instruments.

sn: तमनुप्रयतो वायुः पुण्यगन्धवहः शुभः। ववौ संहर्षयन् पार्थं द्विषतश्चापि शोषयन्॥ ततस्तस्मिन् क्षणे राजन् विविधानि शुभानि च। प्रादुरासन् निमित्तानि विजयाय बहूनि च। पाण्डवानां त्वदीयानां विपरीतानि मारिष॥
en: An auspicious breeze bearing bearing holy fragrance, began to blow from behind Partha and it gladdened him, but sucked up the energies of his adversaries. in that moment, O king, various auspicious signs appeared to view, indicative of the victory of the Pandavas.

sn: दृष्ट्वार्जुनो निमित्तानि विजयाय प्रदक्षिणम्। युयुधानं महेष्वासमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: And, O sire, of the reverses of their enemies seeing those signs indicative of victory Arjuna, addressing the mighty bow-man Yuyudhana who was sitting at his right, said these words"O Yuyudhana, in today's battle, my victory is undoubted."

sn: युयुधानाद्य युद्ध मे दृश्यते विजयो ध्रुवः। यथा होमानि लिङ्गानि दृश्यन्ते शिनिपुङ्गव॥
en: Inasmuch as, O foremost of Sini's race Yuyudhana, these auspicious signs appearing to us.

sn: सोऽहं तत्र गमिष्यामि यत्र सैन्धवको नृपः। यियासुर्यमलोकाय मम वीर्यं प्रतीक्षते॥
en: I shall now penetrate to the spot where the king of the Sindhus remains desirous of seeing a display of my prowess and of going to the domain of Yama. are

sn: यथा परमकं कृत्यं सैन्धवस्य वधो मम। तथैव सुमहत् कृत्यं धर्मराजस्य रक्षणम्॥
en: Indeed, as the slaughter of the Sindhu ruler in one of my foremost duties. So also the protection of the very virtuous king Yudhishthira is another imperative duty of mine.

sn: स त्वमद्य महाबाहो राजानां परिपालय। यथैव हि मया गुप्तस्त्वया गुप्तो भवेत् तथा॥
en: Therefore, O mighty-armed one, do you protect the king this day. So that, protected by you he will be as safe as if he were protected by my own self.

sn: न पश्यामि च तं लोके यस्त्वां युद्धे पराजयेत्। वासुदेवसमं युद्धे स्वयमप्यमरेश्वरः॥
en: Moreover, I do not see any one who can vanquish you in battle. In battle you are equal to Vasudeva himself; even the lord of the celestials cannot vanquish you.

sn: त्वयि चाहं पराश्वस्तः प्रद्युम्ने वा महारथे। शक्नुयां सैन्धवं हन्तुमनपेक्षो नरर्षभ॥
en: Placing the burden of the king's protection you the mighty car-warrior Pradyumna. I can, O foremost of men, without anxiety, exert myself in slaying the Sindhu king.

sn: मय्यपेक्षा न कर्तव्या कथंचिदपि सात्वत। राजन्येव परा गुप्तिः कार्या सर्वात्माना त्वा॥
en: O descendant of the Satvata race, you need not entertain any misgiving about myself. It shall be your first duty to protect the king, with all your heart and soul.

sn: न हि यत्र महाबाहुर्वासुदेवो व्यवस्थितः। किंचिद् व्यापद्यते तत्र यत्राहमपि च ध्रुवम्॥
en: "There where the mighty-armed son of Vasudeva stay or where I myself stay, certainly no calamity can befall there."

sn: एवमुक्तस्तु पार्थेन सात्यकिः परवीरहा। तथेत्युक्त्वागमत् तत्र यत्र राजा युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Thus spoken to by Pritha's son, Satyaki the slayer of hostile heroes, saying 'yea' to the words of the former, returned to that part of the field where Yudhishthira was. on Or on

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच श्वोभूते किमकार्पुस्ते दुःखशोकसमन्विताः। अभिमन्यौ हते तत्र के वायुध्यन्त मामकाः॥
en: Dhritarashtra said When the day after the one in which Abhimanyu had been slain, came, what did the Pandavas, afflicted with grief and sorrow, do? What warriors of my host fought with them?

sn: जानन्तस्तस्य कर्माणि कुरुः सव्यसाचिनः। कथं तत् किल्बिषं कृत्वा निर्भया ब्रूहि मामकाः॥
en: Aware, as they were, of the feats achieved by Savyasachin (Arjuna), tell me, how could the Kauravas and and my warriors, having perpetrated that sinful act. (Abhimanyu's slaughter) remain undaunted?

sn: पुत्रशोकाभिसंतप्तं क्रुद्धं मृत्युमिवान्तकम्। आयान्तं पुरुषव्याघ्रं कथं ददृशुराहवे॥
en: How could they in battle dare look at that foremost of men as he proceeded like the alldestroying Death, burning with fury and distressed with the grief occasioned by the slaughter of his son.

sn: कपिराजध्वजं संख्ये विधुन्वानं महद् धनुः। दृष्टवा पुत्रपरिघुनं किमकुर्वत मामकाः॥
en: What did my warriors do, beholding that warriors having the king of the monkeys for the emblem on his standard, that hero afflicted with the grief caused by the death of his son and shaking his huge bow in battle?

sn: किं नु संजय संग्रामे वृत्तं दुर्योधनं प्रति। परिदेवो महानद्य श्रुतो मे नाभिनन्दनम्॥
en: What, O Sanjaya, has befallen, unto Duryodhana in this day's battle? A great grief stares us in the face. I do not hear any longer, sounds of joy (from my camp).

sn: वभूवुर्ये मनोग्राह्याः शब्दाः श्रुतिसुखावहाः। न श्रूयन्तेऽद्य सर्वे ते सैन्धवस्य निवेशने॥
en: Those inind-captivating sounds, highly pleasing to the sense of hearing that were before heard from the pavilion of the Sindhu king, those sounds are no longer perceived today.

sn: स्तुवतां नाद्य श्रूयन्ते पुत्राणां शिबिरे मम। सूतमागधसंघानां नर्तकानां च सर्वशः॥
en: In the encampment of my sons, the sounds of numerous minstrels and panegyrists singing eulogies and of dancers, are no longer heard.

sn: शब्देन नादिताभीक्ष्णमभवद् यत्र मे श्रुतिः। दीनानामद्य तं शब्दं न शृणोमि समीरितम्॥
en: formerly all these sounds used to strike my ears incessantly. Alas, merged as they are in grief, do not any longer here those sounds from their pavilions

sn: निवेशने सत्यधृतेः सोमदत्तस्य संजय। आसीनोऽहं पुरा तात शब्दमश्रौषमुत्तमम्॥
en: Formerly, O Sanjaya, while sitting in the camp of the truth-loving Somadatta, I used to hear all those charming sounds.

sn: तदद्य पुण्यहीनोऽहमार्तस्वरनिनादितम्। निवेशनं गतोत्साहं पुत्राणां मम लक्षये॥
en: How poor in religious merit I am today, inasmuch as I perceive the pavilion of my sons today to be resounding with sounds of sorrow and lamentations and to be destitute of all sounds of life and energy.

sn: विविंशतेर्तुर्मुखस्य चित्रसेनविकर्णयोः। अन्येषां च सुतानां मे न तथा श्रूयते ध्वनिः॥
en: I do not now hear those sounds I used to hear formerly in the camps of Vivinshati, Durmukha, Chitrasena, Vikarna and other sons of mine.

sn: ब्राह्मणाः क्षत्रिया वैश्या यं शिष्याः पर्युपासते। द्रोणपुत्रं महेष्वासं पुत्राणां मे परायणम्॥
en: That fierce bowman namely the son of Drona, who is the protector of my sons, upon whom Brahmanas, Kshatriyas and Vaishya and a large number of pupils used to wait.

sn: वितण्डालापसंलापैर्दुतवादित्रवादितैः। गीतैश्च विविधैरिष्टै रमते यो दिवानिशम्॥
en: Who delighted in disputations and conversation and in the stirring music of various instruments and in diverse kinds of songs.

sn: उपास्यमानो बहुभिः कुरुपाण्डवसात्वतैः। सूत तस्य गृहे शब्दो नाद्य द्रौणेर्यथा पुरा॥
en: Who was worshipped by many persons among the Kurus, the Pandavas and the Satvatas-you son of Suta, even in the carp of that son of Drona no sound could be heard as before.

sn: द्रोणपुत्रं महेष्वासं गायना नर्तकाश्च ये। अत्यर्थमुपतिष्ठन्ति तेषां न श्रूयते ध्वनिः॥
en: Numerous songsters and dancers used to dance attendance upon that mighty bowman viz., the son of Drona! Now their sounds could no longer be heard in their camp.

sn: विन्दानुविन्दयोः सायं शिबिरे योमहाध्वनिः॥
en: The loud sound that used to be sent up from the pavilion of Vinda and Anuvinda every evening, alas, that sound could no longer be heard there. In the camp of the Kekayas also.

sn: श्रूयते सोऽद्य न तथा केकयानां च वेश्मसु। नित्यं प्रमुदितानां च तालगीतस्वनो महान्॥
en: Could no longer be heard the sound that used to be made by the songs and slappings of palms of soldiers engaged in dance and merrymaking.

sn: नूत्यतां श्रूयते तात गणानां सोऽद्य न स्वनः। सप्त तन्तून् वितन्वाना याजका यमुपासते॥
en: Those Yajaka Brahmanas accomplished in conducting Saptatantu sacrifices, who used to wait upon the son of Somadatta versed in the Vedas, the sound made by those Brahmanas could no longer be heard.

sn: सौमदत्तिं श्रुतनिधि तेषां न श्रूयते ध्वनिः। ज्याघोषो ब्रह्मघोषश्च तोमरासिरथध्वनिः॥
en: The twang of bows, the sound of Vedic recitations, the whistle of shafts, the whiz of swords and the rattle of cars, these sounds were the be heard incessantly in the pavilion of Drona. But I do not hear them now.

sn: द्रोणस्यासीदविरतो गृहे तं न शृणोम्यहम्। नानादेशसमुत्थानां गीतानां योऽभवत् स्वनः॥
en: The melody of songs that used to be sang in the various parts of the field and that used to be mingled with the sound of musical instruments, alas, that sound could not be heard this day.

sn: वादिननादितानां च सोऽद्य न श्रूयते महान्। यदा प्रभृत्युप्लव्याच्छानितमिच्छञ्जनार्दनः॥
en: When Janardana of unfading glory out of the compassion he cherished for every creature, came here with a desire for concluding peace.

sn: आगतः सर्वभूतानामनुकम्पार्थमच्युतः। ततोऽहमब्रुवं सूत मन्दं दुर्योधनं तदा॥
en: Then, O Suta, I said unto the wicked Duryodhana-"With the son of Vasudeva as the mediator, O son, do you conclude peace with the Pandavas.

sn: वासुदेवेन तीर्थेन पुत्र संशाम्य पाण्डवैः। कालप्राप्तमहं मन्ये मा त्वं दुर्योधनातिगाः॥
en: Me seems the time for concluding peace has arrived. O Duryodhana, do not violate my command. If you now disregard the son of Vasudeva who now entreats you for peace.

sn: शमं चेद् याचमानं त्वं प्रत्याख्यास्यसि केशवम्। हिमार्थमभिजल्पन्तं न तवास्ति रणे जयः॥
en: And advises you for your welfare, victory will never fall in your lot in battle." Duryodhana however neglected him of the Dasharha race, that foremost of all bowmen.

sn: प्रत्याचष्ट स दाशार्हमृषभं सर्वधन्विनाम्। अनुनेयानि जल्पन्तमनयान्नान्वपद्यत॥ ततो दुःशासनस्यैव कर्णस्य च मतं द्वयोः। अन्ववर्तत मां हित्वा कृष्टः कालेन दुर्मतिः॥
en: Who then addressed him for his welfare and thus he brought danger on his own head. Then that son of mine, whose intellect was perverted and who was being drawn into the jaws of death, accepted the counsel of Dushasana and Karna and rejected that which I offered him.

sn: न ह्यहं द्यूतमिच्छामि विदुरो न प्रशंसति। सैन्धवो नेच्छति द्यूतं भीष्मो न द्यूतमिच्छति॥
en: I was not in favour of the game at dice, nor was Vidura so. Neither also did the ruler of the Sindhus approve of the game at dice, nor did Bhishma approve of it.

sn: शल्यो भूरिश्रवाश्चैव पुरुमित्रो जयस्तथा। अश्वत्थामा कृपो द्रोणो द्यूतं नेच्छन्ति संजय!॥
en: O Sanjaya, so also, Shalya Bhurishravas, Purumitra. Jaya, Ashvatthaman, Kripa and Drona, none of these approved of that game.

sn: एतेषां मतमादाय यदि वर्तेत पुत्रकः। सज्ञातिमित्रः ससुच्चिरं जीवेदनामयः॥
en: If my unfortunate son had conducted himself according to the counsel of these persons. He with his friends and relatives would then have passed his days in peace and happiness.

sn: श्लक्ष्णा मधुरसम्भाषा ज्ञातिबन्धुप्रियंवदाः। कुलीनाः सम्मताः प्राज्ञाः सुखं प्राप्स्यन्ति पाण्डवाः॥
en: Of sweet and charming speech, always speaking what is agreeable to their relatives. Of noble extraction, esteemed by all, gifted with knowledge, the sons of Pandu are sure to reap happiness.

sn: धर्मापेक्षी नरो नित्यं सर्वत्र लभते सुखम्। प्रेत्यभावे च कल्याणं प्रसादं प्रतिपद्यते॥
en: The man who depends of righteousness, is sure to reap happiness always and everywhere. After death, he obtains bliss and grace (of god).

sn: अर्हास्ते पृथिवीं भोक्तुं समर्थाः साधनेऽपि च। तेषामपि समुद्रान्ता पितृपैतामही मही॥
en: Relying on their own prowess for the achievement of their purposes, the Pandavas deserve to enjoy one half of the Earth itself. The sea-girt earth is as much an inheritance to them as it is to the Kurus.

sn: नियुज्यमानाः स्थास्यन्ति पाण्डवा धर्मवर्मनि। सन्ति मे ज्ञातयस्तात येषां श्रोष्यन्ति पाण्डवाः॥
en: Obtaining sovereignty they will ever remain in the path of virtue. I have kinsmen, O son, to whose words the Pandavas will ever pay attention.

sn: शल्यस्य सोमदत्तस्य भीष्मस्य च महात्मनः। द्रोणस्याथ विकर्णस्य बाह्रीकस्य कृपस्य च॥ अन्येषां चैव वृद्धानां भरतानां महात्मनाम्। त्वदर्थं ब्रुवतां तात करिष्यन्ति वचो हि ते॥
en: O sire, As for instance, Shalya, Somadatta, the high-souled Bhishma, Drona, Vikarna, Balhika, Kripa and numerous other high-souled and venerable in years) members of the Bharata dynasty. If these persons speak for you, the Pandavas will act up to their beneficial words. Who among these do you think would speak otherwise?

sn: कं वा त्वं मन्यसे तेषां यस्तान् ब्रूयादतोऽन्यथा। कृष्णो न धर्म संजह्यात् सर्वे ते हि तदन्वयाः॥
en: Krishna will never abandon righteousness; the Pandavas are ever submissive to him.

sn: पयापि चोक्तास्ते वीरा वचनं धर्मसंहितम्। नान्यथा प्रकरिष्यन्ति धर्मात्मानो हि पाण्डवाः॥
en: Those heroes will not also disregard the righteous words that I shall speak to them for the Pandavas are all of righteous soul.

sn: इत्यहं विलपन् सूत बहुशः पुत्रमुक्तवान्। न च मे श्रुतवान् मूढो मन्ये कालस्य पर्ययम्॥
en: Thus plaintively lamenting, I said these and many other words to my son, O Suta. But that fool did not listen to me, Me seems all this is owing to the evil influence of time.

sn: वृकोदरार्जुनौ यत्र वृष्णिवीरश्च सात्यकिः। उत्तमौजाश्च पाञ्चाल्यो युधामन्युश्च दुर्जयः॥ धृष्टद्युम्नश्च दुर्धर्षः शिखण्डी चापराजितः। अश्मकाः केकयाश्चैव क्षत्रधर्मा च सौमकिः॥ चैद्यश्च चेकितानश्च पुत्रः काश्यस्य चाभिभूः। द्रौपदेया विराटश्च दुपदश्च महारथः॥ यमो च पुरुषव्याघ्रौ मन्त्री च मधुसूदनः। क एताजातु युध्येत लोकेऽस्मिन् वै जिजीविषुः॥४२
en: There where remain Vrikodara and Arjuna and the Vrishni hero Satyaki and Uttamaujas of thie Panchala race and the indomitable Yudhamanyu and the invincible Dhristadyumna and the ever-victorious Sikhandin and the Ashmakas, Kekayas and Kshatradharinan of the Somaka clan, the ruler of the Chedis and Chekitana and Abhibhu the son of the Kasi king, the sons of Draupadi and Virata and the mighty car-warrior Drupada and those foremost of men the twins Nakula and Sahadeva and the slayer of Madhu as the counsellor. What man in this world desirous of living would venture to fight with these?

sn: दिव्यमस्त्रं विकुर्वाणान् प्रसहेद् वा परान् मम। अन्योदुर्योधनात् कर्णाच्छकुनेश्चापि सौबलात्॥ दुःशासनचतुर्थानां नान्यं पश्यामि पञ्चमम्।
en: Who else again will face my enemies when they will display their celestial weapons. Save and except Duryodhana, Karna, Shakuni the son of Subala and Dushasana as their fourth; I do not indeed see a fifth man.

sn: येषामभीषुहस्तः स्याद् विष्वक्सेनो रथे स्थितः॥ संनद्धश्चार्जुनो योद्धा तेषां नास्ति पराजयः।
en: They who have Vishvaksena (Vishnu), clad in armour and reins in hand, on their chariot, they who have Arjuna for their warrior, they can never suffer defeat.

sn: तेषामथ विलापानां नायं दुर्योधनः स्मरेत्॥ हतौ हि पुरुषव्याघ्रौ भीष्मद्रोणौ त्वमात्य वै।
en: Does Duryodhana now remember all those lamentations of mine? You say that Bhishma and Drona, those two foremost of men, have been killed.

sn: तेषां विदुरवाक्यानां मुक्तानां दीर्घदर्शनात्॥ दृष्ट्वेमां फलनिर्वृत्तिं मन्ये शोचन्ति पुत्रकाः। सेनां दृष्ट्वाभिभूतां मे शैनेयेनार्जुनेन च॥
en: I think my foolish sons are now overwhelmed with grief, seeing now the words of the far-sighted Vidura to be true and fruitful. I think my foolish sons are now indulging in lamentations seeing the army sorely distressed by Arjuna and the grand son of Sini.

sn: शून्यान् दृष्ट्वा रथोपस्थान् मन्ये शोचन्ति पुत्रकाः। हिमात्यये यथा कक्षं शुष्कं दातेरितो महान्॥ अग्निहेत् तथा सेनां मामिकां स धनंजयः। आचक्ष्व मम तत् सर्वे कुशलो ह्यसि संजयः॥
en: And seeing also the terraces of their cars empty. Surely Dhananjaya is consuming my stoops like fire assisted by the wind, burning down a heap of straw dried by the heat of the sun that rises at the expiration of the winter season. O Sanjaya, expert as you are in storytelling, relate to me everything that happened.

sn: यदुपायात सायाह्ने कृत्वा पार्थस्य किल्बषम्। अभिमन्यौ हते तात कथमासीन्मनो हि वः॥
en: After that wrong had been inflicted on Arjuna in the evening. What was the state of your mind, O son, when Abhimanyu was slain?

sn: न जातु तस्य कर्माणि युधि गाण्डीवधन्वनः। अपकृत्यमहत् तात सोढुं शक्ष्यन्ति मामकाः॥
en: Surely the feats of valour of the wielder of the Gandiva bow. My warriors were unable to bear, guilty, as they were, of injuring Arjuna (by slaying his son).

sn: किन्नु दुर्योधनः कृत्यं कर्णः कृत्यं किमब्रवीत्। दुःशासनः सौबलश्च तेषामेवं गतेष्वपि॥
en: What measures Duryodhana or Karna direct to be adopted? What also Dushasana or the son of Subala thought fit to do, when they were involved in this predicament.

sn: सर्वेषां समवेतानां पुत्राणां मम संजय। यद् वृत्तं तात संग्रामे मन्दस्यापनयैर्भृशम्॥ लोभानुगस्य दुर्बुद्धेः क्रोधेन विकृतात्मनः। राज्यकामस्य मूढस्य रागोपहतचेतसः। दुर्नीतं वा सुनीतं वा तन्ममाचक्ष्व संजय॥
en: O sire, everything that befell my assembled sons was, O Sanjaya, certainly owing to the misdeeds of my wicked son Duryodhana, who follows in the path of covetousness, whose understanding has been perverted by wrath, whose soul is vitiated, who longs to have sovereignty who is stupid and whose reason is clouded by anger. O Sanjaya, tell me whether the measure adopted by him was agreeable to policy or against it?

sn: संजय उवाच हन्त ते सम्प्रवक्ष्यामि सर्वे प्रत्यक्षदर्शिवान्। शुश्रूषस्व स्थिरो भूत्वा तव ह्यपनयो महान्॥
en: Sanjaya said Alas, as I have seen everything with my own eyes, I shall tell you. Hear me patiently. Great indeed is your fault.

sn: गतोदके सेतुबन्धो याक् तागयं तव। विलापो निष्फलो राजन् मा शुचो भरतर्षभ॥
en: O king, these lamentations of yours are as useless as the construction of embankments when the waters have receeded from a flooded field. O foremost of the Bharatas, do not indulge in grief.

sn: अनतिक्रमणीयोऽयं कृतान्तस्याद्भुतो विधिः। मा शुचो भरतश्रेष्ठ दिष्टमेतत् पुरातनम्॥
en: The decrees of Destiny and wonderful and enevitable. O foremost of the Bharatas, do not give way to grief, for these things are not unique.

sn: यदि त्वं हि पुरा द्यूतात् कुन्तीपुत्रं युधिष्ठिरम्। निवर्तयेथाः पुत्रांश्च न त्वां व्यसनमाव्रजेत्॥
en: If in days gone by, you had prevented Kunti's son Yudhishthira or your own sors, from the tournament at dice, then this calamity would not have overtaken you.

sn: युद्धकाले पुनः प्राप्ते तदैव भवता यदि। निवर्तिताः स्युः संरब्धा न त्वां व्यसनमाव्रजेत्॥
en: If, again, on the eve of the battle, you had prevented the enraged parties from joining in the battle, then this calamity would not have overtaken you.

sn: दुर्योधनं चाविधेयं बनीतेति कुरूनचोदयिष्यस्त्वं न त्वां व्यसनमाव्रजेत्॥
en: If, again, formerly you had incited the other Kurus to put an end to the existence of the refractory Duryodhana, then this calamity would never have overtaken you.

sn: पुरा यदि। तत् ते बुद्धिव्यभीचारमुपलप्स्यन्ति पाण्डवाः। पञ्चाला वृष्णयः सर्वे ये चान्येऽपि नराधिपाः॥
en: If, indeed, you had done one of these alternatives, then the Pandavas, the Panchalas, the Vrishnis and the other rulers of Earth have never had the reason for blaming you for your pervert understanding.

sn: स कृत्वा पितृकर्म त्वं पुत्रं संस्थाप्य सत्पथे। वर्तेथा यदि धर्मेण न त्वां व्यसनमाव्रजेत्॥
en: If, again, doing the duty of a father, you had (by directing Duryodhana on the path of virtue) compelled him to follow in the same path, then this calamity would never have befallen you.

sn: त्वं तु प्राज्ञतमो लोके हित्वा धर्मे सनातनम्। दुर्योधनस्य कर्णस्य शकुनेश्चान्वागा मतम्॥
en: You are the wisest man on the face of the Earth. But inspite of your being so, you accepted the counsel of Karna, Duryodhana and Shakuni, abounding the ways of eternal virtue.

sn: तत् तं विलपितं सर्वं मया राजन् निशामितम्। अर्थे निविशमानस्य विषमिश्रं यथा मधु॥
en: Therefore, O king, all these lamentations of yours that I have heard, you who are absorbed in the enjoyment of worldly objects-appear to me to be like honey-mixed with poison.

sn: नामन्यत तदा कृष्णो राजानं पाण्डवं पुरा। न भीष्मं नैव च द्रोणं यथा त्वां मन्यतेऽच्युतः॥
en: In days gone by, Krishna did not hold king Yudhishthira the son of Pandu or Bhishma or Drona, in so high an estimation as he did hold you, O king.

sn: अजानात् स यदा तु त्वां राजधर्मादधश्च्युतम्। तदाप्रभृति कृष्णस्त्वां न तथा बहु मन्यते॥
en: But when he came to know you fallen from the duties of royalty, that time forward, he did not respect you as before.

sn: परुषाण्युच्यमानांश्च यथा पार्थानुपेक्षसे। तस्यानुबन्धः प्राप्तस्त्वां पुत्राणां राज्यकामुक॥
en: When your sons applied harsh epithets to the sons of Pritha, you assumed an indifferent attitude. The result of that indifference of yours has now overtaken you-you who long to see your sons installed on the throne.

sn: पितृपैतामहं राज्यमपवृत्तं तदानघ। अथ पार्जितां कृत्स्नां पृथिवीं प्रत्यपद्यथाः॥
en: O sinless one, the royalty you inherited from your fore-fathers, is now going to slip off your hands; or on the other hand you will have it, obtaining it from the sons of Pritha (who would certainly snatch it away from your sons after slaying them).

sn: पाण्डुना निर्जितं राज्यं कौरवाणां यशस्तथा। ततश्चाप्यधिक भूयः पाण्डवैर्धर्मचारिभिः॥१५॥
en: The dominions of the Kurus and their fame, had been cquired by Pandu and the rightbehaving sons of Pandu have again added to that fame and those dominions.

sn: तेषां तत् तादृशं कर्म त्वामासाद्य सुनिष्फलम्। यत् पित्र्याद् भ्रंशिता राज्यात् त्वयेहामिषगृद्धिना॥
en: All those endeavours of their became fruitless when indeed their interests clashed with yours, in as much as they were despoiled of their ancestral sovereignty by your very avaricious self.

sn: यत् पुनयुद्धकाले त्वं पुत्रान् गर्हयसे नृप। बहुधा व्याहरन् दोषान् न तदद्योपपद्यते॥
en: So, O king, the fact of your attributing blame to your sons at the time of the actual warfare and the face of your expatiating on their faults, indeed, seem very unbecoming.

sn: न हि रक्षन्ति राजानो युध्यन्तो जीवितं रणे। चमू विगाह्य पार्थानां युध्यन्ते क्षत्रियर्षभाः॥
en: The monarchs, when engaged in battle, do not pay the least regard to their lives. Those foremost of the Kshatriyas fight (to the best of their abilities, having penetrated into the heart of the array of troops belonging to the sons of Pritha.

sn: यांतु कृष्णार्जुनौ सेनां यां सात्यकिवृकोदरौ। रक्षेरन् को नु तां युध्येच्चमूमन्यत्र कौरवैः॥
en: The army which Krishna and Arjuna and Satyaki and Vrikodara protect what persons except the Kauravas would hazard a battle with that army.

sn: येषां योद्धा गुडाकेशो येषां मन्त्री जनार्दनः। येषां च सात्यकिर्योद्धा येषां योद्धा वृकोदरः॥
en: They whose warrior is Gudakesha (Arjuna), they whose counsellor is Krishna, they whose protectors are Vrikodara and Satyaki.

sn: को हि तान् विषहेद् योद्धं मर्त्यधर्मा धनुर्धरः। अन्यत्र कौरवेयेभ्यो ये वा तेषां पदानुगाः॥
en: What human wielder of bow would venture to fight them, save and except the Kauravas and those who follow their lead.

sn: यावत् तु शक्यते कर्तुमन्तरज्ञैर्जनाधिपः। क्षत्रधर्मरतैः शूरैस्तावत् कुर्वन्ति कौरवाः॥
en: Everything that can possibly be done by devoted (tributary) kings endued with heroism and observant of the duties of the Kshatriyas, all that is being done for the Kauravas by their partisans.

sn: यथा तु पुरुषव्या युद्ध परमसंकटम्। कुरूणां पाण्डवैः सार्धं तत् सर्वं शृणु तत्त्वतः॥
en: Hear now from me everything that transpired in that dreadful battle between those foremost of men, viz., the Kauravas and the Pandavas.

description: The arraying of the Kaurava troops
sn: संजय उवाच तस्यां निशायां व्युष्टायं द्रोणः शस्त्रभृतां वरः। स्वान्यनीकानि सर्वाणि प्राक्रामद् व्यूहितुं ततः॥
en: Sanjaya said After the night had passed away, that foremost of all wielders of weapons, viz., Drona began to dispose of his divisions in battle array.

description: The arraying of the Kaurava troops
sn: शूरूणां गर्जतां राजन् संक्रुद्धानाममर्षिणाम्। श्रूयन्ते स्म गिरश्चित्राः परस्परवधैषिणाम्॥
en: Then there were heard the diverse words of challenge uttered by shouting heroes, inflamed with rage and desirous of slaying one another.

description: The arraying of the Kaurava troops
sn: विस्कार्य च धनूंष्यन्ये ज्याः परे परिमृज्य च। विनिःश्वसन्तः प्राक्रोशन् क्वेदानीं सधनंजयः॥
en: Stretching their bows and drawing back the strings of their bow with their hands and breathing (hot), they began to exclaim, 'where now is that Dhananjaya.'

description: The arraying of the Kaurava troops
sn: विकोशान् सुत्सरूनन्ये कृतधारान् समाहितान्। पीतानाकाशसंकाशानसीन् केचिच्च चिक्षिपुः॥
en: Some began to toss their swords in airswords that were naked, non-plant, welltempered, of the hue of the sky, possessed of great sharpness and decorated with ornamental hilts.

description: The arraying of the Kaurava troops
sn: चरन्तस्त्वसिमाश्चि शिक्षया। संग्राममनसः शूरा दृश्यन्ते सम सहस्रशः॥
en: Thousands of heroic warriors longing for battle, were seen to perform various evolutions of swordsmen and bowmen, with dexterity acquired through discipline.

description: The arraying of the Kaurava troops
sn: सघण्टाश्चन्दनादिग्धाः स्वर्णवज्रविभूषिताः। समुत्क्षिप्य गदाश्चान्ये पर्यपृच्छन्त पाण्डवम्॥
en: Others again whirling in the air their maces tied with belts decorated with sandal paste and adorned with gold and diamond, began to enquire after the son of Pandu (Arjuna).

description: The arraying of the Kaurava troops
sn: अन्ये बलमदोन्मत्ताः परिधैर्बाहुशालिनः। चक्रुः सम्बाधमाकाशमुच्छ्रितेन्द्रध्वजोपमैः॥
en: Other warriors, maddened with the pride of their prowess and endued with strong arms, obstructed the sky with their spiked bludgeons that looked like bannered poles raised in honor of Indra.

description: The arraying of the Kaurava troops
sn: नानाप्रहरणैश्चान्ये विचित्रस्रगलकृताः। संग्राममनसः शूरास्तत्र तत्र व्यवस्थिताः॥
en: Other brave warriors again decorated with charming floral garlands and armed with various kinds of weapons, stationed themselves on different parts of the field, burning with a desire for battle.

description: The arraying of the Kaurava troops
sn: क्वार्जुनः क्व सगोविन्दः क्व च मानी वृकोदरः। क्व च ते सुहृदस्तेशामाह्वयन्ते रणे तदा॥
en: 'Where is Arjuna? Where is Govinda? Where is the proud Vrikodara? Where are all their followers and friends? Even thus did they then challenge the Pandavas to battle.

description: The arraying of the Kaurava troops
sn: ततः शङ्खमुपाध्याय त्वरयन् वाजिनः स्वयम्। इतस्ततस्तान् रचयन् द्रोणश्चरति वेगितः॥
en: Then blowing his conch and urging his steeds to full speed, Drona began to move hither and thither with great celerity, arranging his troops in order.

description: The arraying of the Kaurava troops
sn: तेष्वनीकेषु सर्वेषु स्थितेष्वाहवनन्दिषु। भरद्वाजो महाराज जयद्रथमथाब्रवीत्॥
en: When those divisions that ever delighted in fight, were disposed of in order, O mighty monarch, the son of Bharadvaja addressing Jayadratha said these words.

description: The arraying of the Kaurava troops
sn: त्वं चैव सौमदत्तिश्च कर्णश्चैव महारथः। अश्वत्थामा च शल्यश्च वृषसेनः कृपस्तथा॥ शतं चाश्वसहस्राणां रथानामयुतानि षट्। द्विरदानां प्रभिन्नानां सहस्राणि चतुर्दश॥ पदातीनां सहस्राणि दंशितान्येकविंशतिः। गव्यूतिषु त्रिमात्रासु मामनासाद्य तिष्ठत॥
en: "Yourself, the son of Somadatta, the mighty car-warrior Karna, Ashvatthaman, Shalya, Vrishasena and Kripa supported with hundred thousand horses, sixty thousand chariots, fourteen thousand elephants with rent temples, twenty-one thousand foot-soldiers cased in armour, take up your stand behind me at a distance of twelve miles.

description: The arraying of the Kaurava troops
sn: तत्रस्थं तवां न संसोढुं शक्ता देवाः सवासवाः। किं पुनः पाण्डवाः सर्वे सामश्वसिहि सैन्धव॥
en: There even the very gods led by Vasava himself will not be able to assault you what to speak of the sons of Pandu? Take heart, O ruler of the Sindhus."

description: The arraying of the Kaurava troops
sn: एवमुक्तः समाश्वस्त: सिन्धुराजो जयद्रथः। सम्प्रायात् सह गान्धारैर्वृतस्तैश्च महारथैः॥
en: Thus spoken to, Jayadratha the ruler of the Sindhus became comforted. He then set out for the spot indicated by Drona, followed by many Gandhara heroes and surrounded by those great car-warriors.

description: The arraying of the Kaurava troops
sn: वर्मिभिः सादिभिर्यत्तैः प्रासपाणिभिरास्थितैः। चामरापीडिनः सर्वे जाम्बूनदविभूषिताः॥
en: And accompanied by many foot soldiers cased in armours, armed with nooses and prepared to fight to the best of their abilities. Decked with Chamaras and adorned with golden caparisons.

description: The arraying of the Kaurava troops
sn: जयद्रथस्य राजेन्द्र हयाः साधुप्रवाहिनः। ते चैक सप्तसाहस्रास्त्रिसाहस्राश्च सैन्धवाः॥
en: The horses of Jayadratha, O mighty king, were all very good carriers; seven thousand such steeds and three thousands other steeds of the Shindhu breed, were also with him.

description: The arraying of the Kaurava troops
sn: मत्तानां सुविरूढानां हस्त्यारोहैर्विशारदैः। नागानां भीमरूपाणां वर्मिणां रौद्रकर्मिणाम्॥ अध्यर्धेन सहस्रेण पुत्रो दुर्मर्षणस्तव। अग्रतः सर्वसैन्यानां युध्यमानां युध्यमानो व्यवस्थितः।।
en: Your son Durmarshana, desirous of doing battle, was stationed in the van of the rest of the troops being supported by one thousand and five hundred maddened elephants of prodigious size, covered with mail and of dreadful deeds, all mounted by skillful elephant-riders.

description: The arraying of the Kaurava troops
sn: ततो दुःशासनश्चैव विकर्णश्च तवात्मजौ। सिन्धुराजार्थसिद्ध्यर्थमग्रानीके व्यवस्थितौ॥
en: Your other two sons, Dushasana and Vikarna, stationed themselves amidst the advance division of the army, for securing success to the king of the Sindhus.

description: The arraying of the Kaurava troops
sn: दी? द्वादश गव्यूतिः पश्चाः पञ्च विस्तृतः। व्यूहस्तु चक्रशकटो भारद्वाजेन निर्मितः॥
en: The array that the son of Bharadvaja then formed, partly figuring a sakata and partly a circle, was full forty-eight miles in length and its back portion, in width, measured full twenty miles.

description: The arraying of the Kaurava troops
sn: नानानृपतिभिर्वीरैस्तत्र तत्र व्यवस्थितैः। स्थाश्वगजपत्त्योधैर्दोणेन विहितः स्वयम्॥
en: Drona himself formed this array in which were stationed numerous brave kings and innumerable cars, elephants, horses and foot soldiers.

description: The arraying of the Kaurava troops
sn: पश्चार्धे तस्य पद्मस्तु गर्भव्यूहः सुदुर्भिदः। सूची पद्मस्य गर्भस्थो गूढो व्यूहः कृतः पुनः॥
en: In the back portion of that array was formed another impenetrable array figuring a lotus. Within this latter again was constructed another closely formed array, that was designated the needle.

description: The arraying of the Kaurava troops
sn: एवमेतं महाव्यूहं व्यूह्य द्रोणो व्यवस्थितः। सूचीमुखे महेष्वासः कृतवर्मा व्यवस्थितः॥
en: Thus having formed this inighty array Drona waited for the encounter. In the rear of the needle array was placed Kritavarman the fierce bowman.

description: The arraying of the Kaurava troops
sn: अनन्तरं च काम्बोजो जलसंधश्च मारिष। दुर्योधनश्च कर्णश्च तदनन्तरमेव॥
en: After him were stationed the Kamboja Princes and also Jalasandha, O sire, Behind them stood Duryodhana and Karna, in the Sakata.

description: The arraying of the Kaurava troops
sn: ततः शतसहस्राणि योधानामनिवर्तिनाम्। व्यवस्थितानि सर्वाणि शकटे मुखरक्षिणाम्॥
en: Nex, to them were placed hundreds and thousands of unretreating warriors, for protecting the head of that array.

description: The arraying of the Kaurava troops
sn: तेषां च पृष्ठतो राजा बलेन महता वृतः। जयद्रथस्ततो राजा सूचीपार्वे व्यवस्थितः॥
en: Behind their back, was stationed · king Jayadratha by the side of the needle array and surrounded by a mighty division of troops.

description: The arraying of the Kaurava troops
sn: शकटस्य तु राजेन्द्र भारद्वाजो मुखे स्थितः। अनु तस्याभवद् भोजो जुगोपैनं ततः स्वयम्॥
en: The son of Bharadvaja, himself stood at the mouth of the Sakata. Next to him stood the ruler of the Bhojas, who protected the former.

description: The arraying of the Kaurava troops
sn: श्वेतवर्माम्बरोष्णीषो व्यूढोरस्को महाभुजः। धनुर्विस्फारयन् द्रोणस्तस्थौ क्रुद्ध इवान्तकः॥
en: Cased in a white coat of mail, graced with a beautiful turban, of broad chest and of mighty arms, Drona there stood stretching his bow, like the enraged God of Death.

description: The arraying of the Kaurava troops
sn: पताकिनं शोणहयं वेदिकृष्णाजिनध्वजम्। द्रोणस्य रथमालोक्य प्रहृष्टाः कुरवोऽभवन्॥
en: The Kurus then were filled with delight by beholding the chariot of Drona, graced with a banner, having crimson steeds yoked to it and standard that bore the device of the sacrificial altar and a black deer.

description: The arraying of the Kaurava troops
sn: सिद्धचारणसंघानां विस्मयः सुमहानभूत्। द्रोणेन विहितं दृष्ट्वा व्यूहं क्षुब्धार्णवोपमम्॥
en: Beholding that array formed by Drona that resembled the ocean agitated (by the tempest), the Siddhas and the Charanas were filled with great wonder.

description: The arraying of the Kaurava troops
sn: सशैलसागरवनां नानाजनपदाकुलाम्। ग्रसेद् व्यूहः क्षितिं सर्वामिति भूतानि मेनिरे॥
en: The creatures then thought that array would devour the whole Earth with her mountains, oceans, forests and the various rivers flowing on its surface.

description: The arraying of the Kaurava troops
sn: बहुरथमनुजाश्वपत्तिनागं प्रतिभयनिः स्वनमद्भुतानुरूपम्। अतिहहृदयभेदनं महद् वै शकटमवेक्ष्यकृतं ननन्द राजा॥
en: King Duryodhana then beholding that great array figuring a Sakata, teeming with chariots, men, steeds and elephants and roaring fearfully, of wonderful appearance and capable of afflicting the hearts of the enemy, became filled with delight.

description: The appearance of Arjuna on the field of battle
sn: संजय उवाच ततो व्यूढेष्वनीकेषु समुत्कृष्टेषु मारिष। ताड्यमानासु भेरीषु मृदङ्गेषु नदत्सु च॥
en: Sanjaya said Thus when the troops had been excellently disposed of in that array, Osire and when Bheris were sounded and Mridangas struck up.

description: The appearance of Arjuna on the field of battle
sn: अनीकानां च संह्रादे वादित्राणां च निःस्वने। प्रध्यापितेषु शोषु संनादे लोमहर्षणे॥
en: When the soldiers uttered loud war-cries and musical instruments emitted tremendous din, when conchs were blown and horripilating roars were heard.

description: The appearance of Arjuna on the field of battle
sn: अभिहारयत्सु शनकैर्भरतेषु युयुत्सुषु। रौद्रे मुहूर्ते सम्प्राप्ते सव्यसाची व्यदृश्यत॥
en: When the field slowly became over-spread with Bharata heroes desirous of battle and when the hour known as Roudra arrived, Savyasachin (Arjuna) made his appearance on the field of battle.

description: The appearance of Arjuna on the field of battle
sn: बलानां वायसानां च पुरस्तात् सव्यसाचिनः । बहुलानि सहस्रणि प्राक्रीडंस्तत्र भारत॥
en: Then, O Bharata, many thousands of ravens and crows flew sportively in front of Arjuna's car.

description: The appearance of Arjuna on the field of battle
sn: मृगाश्च घोरसंनादः शिवाश्चाशिवदर्शनाः। दक्षिणेन प्रयातानामस्माकं प्राणदंस्तथा॥
en: Various animals of fearful yells and jackals of dreadful appearance, began to how in our right as we proceeded to battle.

description: The appearance of Arjuna on the field of battle
sn: सनिर्घाता ज्वलन्त्यश्च पेतुरुल्काः सहस्रशः। चचाल च मही कृत्स्ना भये घोरे समुत्थिते॥
en: Thousands of meteors, with harsh sounds and blazing tails, began to drop down; on the dreadful occasion, the whole Earth began to quake and tremble.

description: The appearance of Arjuna on the field of battle
sn: विष्वग्वाताः सनिर्घाता रूक्षाः शर्करकर्षिणः। ववुरायाति कौन्तेये संग्रामे समुपस्थिते॥
en: Dry winds accompanied by deep sounds and driving pebbles and gravel, began to blow when Kunti's son made his appearance before the commencement of the battle.

description: The appearance of Arjuna on the field of battle
sn: नाकुलिश्च शतानीको धृष्टद्युम्नश्च पाण्डवानामनीकानि प्राज्ञौ तौ व्यूहतुस्तदा॥
en: Then Shatanika the son of Nakula and Dhristadyumna the son of Prishata, these two warriors endued with great wisdom began to array in order the numerous divisions of the Pandavas.

description: The appearance of Arjuna on the field of battle
sn: ततो रथसहस्रेण द्विरदानां शतेन च। त्रिभिरश्वसहस्त्रैश्च पदातीनां शतैः शतैः॥ पार्षतः। अध्यर्धमात्रे धनुषां सहस्रे तनयस्तव। अग्रतः सर्वसैन्यानां स्थित्वा दुर्मर्षणोऽब्रवीत्॥
en: Supported by a thousand cars, a hundred elephants, three thousand horses and ten thousand foot-soldiers and covering a part of the field measuring fifteen hundred bows, your son Durmarshana stationed himself in the very

description: The appearance of Arjuna on the field of battle
sn: अद्य गाण्डीवधन्वानं तपन्तं युद्धदुर्मदम्। अहमावारयिष्यामि वेलेव मकरालयम्॥
en: Like the banks resisting the waves of the swelling main, even I myself will this day hold in check the wielder of the Gandiva bow, that slayer of foes, that hero who is irrepressible in battle.

description: The appearance of Arjuna on the field of battle
sn: अद्य पश्यन्तु संग्रामे धनंजयममर्षणम्। विषक्तं मयि दुर्धर्षमश्मकूटमिवाश्मनि॥
en: Today let people see the irate and indomitable Dhananjaya collide with me, even like a mass of stone against another story mass.

description: The appearance of Arjuna on the field of battle
sn: तिष्ठध्वं स्थनो यूयं संग्राममभिकाक्षिणः। युध्यामि संहतानेतान् यशो मानं च वर्धयन्॥
en: Stay, O you car-warriors that long to join in the fray! Single-handed, will I fight with the assembled Pandavas, for enhancing my glory and my fame

description: The appearance of Arjuna on the field of battle
sn: एवं ब्रुवन्महाराज महात्मा स महामतिः। महेष्वासैर्वतो राजन् महेष्वासो व्यवस्थितः॥
en: Having thus (spoken, O mighty monarch, that illustrious site of generous intellect, that fierce bowmen, stood, king, being surrounded by many excellent car-warriors.

description: The appearance of Arjuna on the field of battle
sn: ततोऽन्तक इव क्रुद्धः सवज्र इव वासवः। दण्डपाणिगि मह्यो मृत्युः कालेन चोदितः॥
en: Then, ikt, the enraged Destroyer or like Vasata arnted with the thunderbolt or like the unbearate'r god of Death wielding his bludgeon and lét loose by time.

description: The appearance of Arjuna on the field of battle
sn: शूलपाणिरिवाक्षोभ्यो वरुणः पाशवानिव। युगान्कांग्नरिवार्चिष्मान् प्रधक्ष्यन् वै पुनः प्रजाः॥
en: Or like Siva with trident and unruffled or like Varuna armed with the noose or like the blazing fire appearing at the end of a Yuga for consuming the creation.

description: The appearance of Arjuna on the field of battle
sn: क्रोधामर्षबलोद्भूतो निवातकवचान्तकः। जयो जेता स्थितः सत्ये पारयिष्यन् महाव्रतम्॥
en: That slayer of the Nivatakavachas, inflamed with rage and swelling with his energies, the ever victorious Jaya attached to truth and intent on accomplishing his great vow.

description: The appearance of Arjuna on the field of battle
sn: आमुक्तकवचः खड्गी जाम्बूनदकिरीटभृत्। शुभ्रमाल्याम्बरधरः स्वगदश्चारुकुण्डलः॥
en: Cased in mail and armed with a sword, graced with a golden diadem, decorated with garlands of white flowers and attired in white garments, his arms decked with charming Angadas and ears with resplendent ear-rings.

description: The appearance of Arjuna on the field of battle
sn: रथप्रवरमास्थाय नरो नारायणानुगः। विधुन्वन् गाण्डिवं संख्ये बभौ सूर्य इवोदितः॥
en: Riding on his own best of chariots, the embodied Nara accompanied by Narayana, shaking his Gandiva bow in battle appeared shining and dazzling like the risen sun.

description: The appearance of Arjuna on the field of battle
sn: सोऽग्रानीकस्य महत इषुपाते धनंजयः। व्यवस्थाप्य रथं राजशङ्ख दध्मौ प्रतापवान्॥
en: Then Dhananjaya endued with great might, O king, stopping his chariot before the van of his troops where the thickest downpour of arrows was expected blew his conch.

description: The appearance of Arjuna on the field of battle
sn: अथकृष्णोऽप्यसम्भ्रान्तः पार्थेन सह मारिष। प्राध्यापयत् पाञ्चजन्यं शङ्ख प्रवरमोजसा॥
en: Thereupon the undaunted Krishna also, O sire, with Pritha's son, blew with force that most excellent conch of his, known as the Panchajanya.

description: The appearance of Arjuna on the field of battle
sn: तयोः शङ्खपणादेन तव सैन्ये विशाम्पते। आसन् संहृष्टरोमाणः कम्पिता गतचेतसः॥
en: Then at that blare of the conchs, O ruler of men, the soldiers of your army had the hair of their body erect and they trembled and were confounded.

description: The appearance of Arjuna on the field of battle
sn: यथा त्रस्यन्ति भूतानि सर्वाण्यशनिनिः स्वनात्। तथा शङ्खप्रणादेन वित्रेसुस्तव सैनिकाः॥
en: At the blare of their conchs, your troops took right even as creatures become frightened at the rumbling of the thunder.

description: The appearance of Arjuna on the field of battle
sn: प्रसुस्रवुः शकृन्मूत्रं वाहनानि च सर्वशः। एवं सवाहनं सर्वमाविग्नमभवद् बलम्॥
en: All the beasts discharged urine and excreta. Your whole army with its animals seized with anxiety.

description: The appearance of Arjuna on the field of battle
sn: सीदन्ति स्म नरा राजशङ्खशब्देन मारिष। विसंज्ञाश्चाभवन् केचित् केचिद् राजन् वितत्रसु॥
en: O sire, O monarch, in consequence of the blare of those two conchs, all men were deprived of their strength. And some of our array the were filled with fear and some lost their consciousness.

description: The appearance of Arjuna on the field of battle
sn: ततः कपिमहानादं सह भूतैर्ध्वजालयैः। अकरोद्ध व्यादितास्यश्च भीषयंस्तव सैनिकान्॥
en: Then frightening your soldiers, the ape of Arjuna's banner with other creatures thereon, opening its mouth, uttered a terrible roar.

description: The appearance of Arjuna on the field of battle
sn: ततः शङ्खाश्च भेर्यश्च मृदङ्गाश्चानकैः सह। पुनरेवाभ्यहन्यन्त तव सैन्यप्रहर्षणाः॥
en: Then conchs, horns, cymbals and Anakas, were sounded and blown for inspiring energy into your troops.

description: The appearance of Arjuna on the field of battle
sn: नानावादित्रसंहादैः श्वैडितास्फोटिताकुलैः। सिंहनादैः समुत्कुष्टैः समाधूतैर्महारथैः॥
en: Then din thus produced, became mixed up with the din produced by various musical instruments, by the shouts of warriors and by the slappings of their armpits, by the war-cries of the great car-warriors, as they challenged one another.

description: The appearance of Arjuna on the field of battle
sn: तस्मिंस्तु तुमुले शब्दे भीरूणां भयवर्धने। अतीव हृष्टो दाशार्हमब्रवीत् पाकशासनिः॥
en: Thus when that tremendous din arose there din that enhanced the fear of the cowards the son of Pakashasani became filled with joy; and addressing the descendant of the Dasarha race, he then thus spoke.

sn: अर्जुन उवाच चोदयाश्वान् हृषीकेश यत्र दुर्मर्षणः स्थितः। एतद् भित्त्वा गजानीकं प्रवेक्ष्याम्यरिवाहिनीम्॥
en: Arjuna said Drive, O Hrishikesha, the horses to the spot where Durmarsana stands. Penetrating through this division of elephants. I shall enter into the heart of the hostile army.

sn: संजय उवाच एवमुक्तो महाबाहुः केशवः सव्यसाचिना। अचोदयद्धयांस्तत्र यत्र दुर्मर्षणः स्थितः॥
en: Sanjaya said Thus spoken to by Savyasachin, the mighty-armed Keshava drove the steeds to the spot where Durmarsana was standing.

sn: स समप्रहारस्तुमुलः सम्प्रवृत्तः सुदारुणः। एकस्य च बहूनां च रथनागनरक्षयः॥
en: Thereupon, there ensued a fearful and terrible encounter between the many and the one, encounter that was destructive of many cars, elephants and men.

sn: ततः सायकवर्षेण पर्जन्य इव वृष्टिमान्। परानवाकिरत् पार्थः पर्वतानिव नीरदः॥
en: Then, like masses of clouds surcharged with rain drenching the mountain-breast with their contents. Pritha's son covered his enemies with his arrowy downpour.

sn: ते चापि रथिनः सर्वे त्वरिताः कृतहस्तवत्। अवाकिरन् बाणजालैस्तत्र कृष्णधनंजयौ॥
en: The warriors of your army then with great lightness of hands, hastily covered Arjuna and Krishna with a net-work of arrows.

sn: ततः क्रुद्धो महाबाहुर्वार्यमाणः परैयुधि। शिरांसि रथिनां पार्थः कायेभ्योऽपाहरच्छरैः। :॥
en: Then excited to the highest pitch of anger by his enemies, the mighty-armed Partha endued with great prowess, began to rob, with his arrows, the heads of car-warriors, from their trunks.

sn: उद्भान्तनयनैर्वक्त्रैः संदष्टौष्ठपुटैः शुभैः। सकुण्डलशिरस्त्राणैर्वसुधा समकीर्यत॥
en: The Earth became overspread with handsome heads graced with ear-rings and head-gears, the lower lips bit by the upper ones and the faces adorned with eyes inflamed with rage.

sn: पुण्डरीकवनानीव विध्यस्तानि समन्ततः। विनिकर्णानि योधानां वदनानि चकाशिरे॥
en: The countenance of the warriors scattered here and there, looked charming like an assemblage of plucked off lotuses lying crushed and strewn about the field.

sn: तपनीयतनुत्राणाः संसिक्ता रुधिरेण च। संसक्ता इव दृश्यन्ते मेघसंघाः सविद्युतः॥
en: Armours of gold bespattered with blood and lying thick over the field, appeared like masses of clouds fringed with flashes of lightning.

sn: शिरसां पततां राजशब्दोऽभूद् वसुधातले। कालेन परिपक्वानां तालानां पततामिव॥
