en: This golden coat of mail of yours, O king, I shall so tie on you that all weapons discharged by human hands will not be able to pierce you in battle.

description: The donning of the armour on Duryodhana by Drona
sn: यदि त्वां सासुरसुरा: सयक्षोरगराक्षसाः। योधयन्ति त्रयो लोकाः सनरा नास्ति ते भयम्॥
en: Even if the three worlds, with the Asuras, the celestials, the Yakshas, the Reptiles and the Rakshasas, together with all human beings, fight with today, still you need entertain no fear.

description: The donning of the armour on Duryodhana by Drona
sn: न कृष्णो न च कौन्तेयो न चान्यः शस्त्रभृद् रणे। शरानर्पयितुं कश्चित् कवचे तव शक्ष्यति॥
en: Neither Krishna, nor the son of Kunti, nor any other wielder of weapons, will be able to pierce your armour in baitle with his arrows.

description: The donning of the armour on Duryodhana by Drona
sn: स त्वं कवचमास्थाय क्रुद्धपद्य रणेऽर्जुनम्। त्वरमाणः स्वयं यानि न त्वासौ विसहिष्यति॥
en: So, cased in this golden armour, do you hastily advance upon the wrathful Arjuna, yourself; he shall not be able to beat you in battle today.

description: The donning of the armour on Duryodhana by Drona
sn: संजय उवाच एवमुक्त्वा त्वरन् द्रोणः स्पृष्ट्वाम्भो वर्म भास्वरम्। आबबन्धाद्भुततमं जपन् मन्त्रं यथाविधि॥
en: Sanjaya said Having thus spoken, Drona quickly rinced his mouth with water and then bound that lustrous armour on Duryodhana, having duly reiterated most marvellous incantations.

description: The donning of the armour on Duryodhana by Drona
sn: रणे तस्मिन् सुमहति विजयस्य सुतस्य ते। विसिस्मापयिषुर्लोकान् विद्यया ब्रह्मवित्तमः॥
en: In that dreadful battle, that foremost of persons conversant with the knowledge of the Vedas, was desirous of bestowing victory on your son and of exciting the wonder of the worlds with his excellent learning.

description: The donning of the armour on Duryodhana by Drona
sn: द्रोण उवाच करोतु स्वस्ति ते ब्रह्म ब्रह्मा चापि द्विजातयः। सरीसृपाश्च ये श्रेष्ठास्तेभ्यस्ते स्वस्ति भारत॥
en: Drona said May all the Vedas, the Brahmanas and Brahman himself and the Reptiles and other beings of superior order bless you, O Bharata!

description: The donning of the armour on Duryodhana by Drona
sn: ययाति हुषश्चैव धुन्धुमारो भगीरथः। तुभ्यं राजर्षयः सर्वे स्वस्ति सकुर्वन्तु ते सदा॥
en: May Yayati, Nahusha, Dhundhumara and Bhagiratha and other royal sage bless you in all acts!

description: The donning of the armour on Duryodhana by Drona
sn: स्वस्ति तेऽस्त्वेकपादेभ्यो बहुपादेभ्य एव च। स्वस्तयस्त्वपादकेभ्यश्च नित्यं तव महारणे॥
en: May you obtain blessing from creatures having one leg only and creatures having many also! May you also get blessings from those who have no legs at all!

description: The donning of the armour on Duryodhana by Drona
sn: स्वाहा स्वधा शची चैव स्वस्ति कुर्वन्तु ते सदा। लक्ष्मीररुन्धती चैव कुरुतां स्वस्ति तेऽनघ॥
en: May Svaha and Svadha and Sachi all oless you always! O sinless one, may Lakshmi and Arundhati also pronounce benedictions on you!

description: The donning of the armour on Duryodhana by Drona
sn: असितो देवलश्चैव विश्वामित्रस्तथाङ्गिराः। वसिष्ठः कश्यपश्चैव स्वस्ति कुर्वन्तु ते नृप॥
en: May Asita, Devala, Vishvamitra, Angiras, Vasistha and Kashyapa, O monarch, bless you!

description: The donning of the armour on Duryodhana by Drona
sn: धाता विधाता लोकेशो दिशश्च सदिगीश्वराः। स्वस्ति तेऽद्य प्रयच्छन्तु कार्तिकेयश्च षण्मुखः॥
en: May Dhatri and Vidhatri, the quarters of heaven and their regents and the six-headed Kartikeya do all that is beneficial you!

description: The donning of the armour on Duryodhana by Drona
sn: विवस्वान् भगवान् स्वस्ति करोतु तव सर्वशः। दिग्गजाश्चैव चत्वारः क्षितिश्च गगनं ग्रहाः॥
en: May the illustrious Vivasvat bless you today! May the four elephants guarding the cardinal points, the earth, the firmament, the planets.

description: The donning of the armour on Duryodhana by Drona
sn: अधस्ताद् धरणीं योऽसौ सदा धारयते नृप। शेषश्च पनगश्रेष्ठः स्वस्ति तुभ्यं प्रयच्छतु॥
en: And he who is underneath this earth and o king who ever upholds her, viz., Shesha, that foremost of snakes-may all these do what is beneficial to you!

description: The donning of the armour on Duryodhana by Drona
sn: गान्धारे युधि विक्रम्य निर्जिताः सुरसत्तमाः। पुरा वृत्रेण दैत्येन भिन्नदेहाः सहस्रशः॥
en: O Son of Gandhari, in days gone by, the Asura named Vritra, exerting his might in battle, had defeated the foremost of celestials in battle.

description: The donning of the armour on Duryodhana by Drona
sn: हातेजोबलाः सर्वे तदा सेन्द्रा दिवौकसः। ब्रह्माणं शरणं जग्मुर्वत्राद् भीता महासुरात्॥
en: All those dwellers of heaven then with Indra at their head, destitute of their head, destitute of their energy and prowess, sought refuge with Brahman being highly afraid of the mighty Asura Vritra.

description: The donning of the armour on Duryodhana by Drona
sn: देवा ऊचुः प्रमर्दितानां वृत्रेण देवानां देवसत्तम। गतिर्भव सुरश्रेष्ठ त्राहि नो महतो भयात्॥
en: The celestials said O foremost of the celestials, O best of the gods, be you the protector of the gods now, crushed as they are by the Asura Vritra. Save us from this our great fear.

description: The donning of the armour on Duryodhana by Drona
sn: अथ पार्श्वे स्थितं विष्णुं शक्रादींश्च सुरोत्तमान्। प्राह तथ्यमिदं वाक्यं विषण्णान् सुरसत्तमान्॥
en: Drona continued Thereupon Brahman addressing Vishnu standing by his side, as also the other foremost of celestials headed by Indra, spoke to them that were are depressed, these words, all perfectly true.

description: The donning of the armour on Duryodhana by Drona
sn: रक्ष्या मे सततं देवाः सहेन्द्राः सद्विजातयः। त्वष्टः सुदुर्धरं तेजो येन वृत्रो विनिर्मितः॥
en: The celestials with Indra at their head, as also the regenerate order are ever deserving of my protection. But the energy of Tvashtri from which Vritra has been created is indeed irrepressible.

description: The donning of the armour on Duryodhana by Drona
sn: त्वष्ट्रा पुरा तपस्तप्त्वा वर्षायुतशतं तदा। वृत्रो विनिर्मितो देवाः प्राप्यानुज्ञां महेश्वरात्॥
en: In days gone by, observing ascetic austerities for millions of years, Tvashtri created, O Gods, Vritra, having obtained permission thereto from Mahadeva.

description: The donning of the armour on Duryodhana by Drona
sn: स तस्यैव प्रसादाद् वो हन्यादेव रिपुर्बली। नागत्वा शंकरस्थानं भगवान् दृश्यते हरः॥
en: Hence that mighty energy of ours has succeeded in vanquishing you through the grace of that god. Without repairing to the place where Sankara stays, you cannot except to obtain a sight of him.

description: The donning of the armour on Duryodhana by Drona
sn: दृष्ट्वा जेष्यथ वृत्रं तं क्षिप्रं गच्छत मन्दरम्। यत्रास्ते तपसां योनिर्दक्षयज्ञविनाशनः॥
en: After you have seen that god, you will be able to conquer Vritra. Therefore, his yourselves to the Mandara mountain; there dwells that origin of ascetic austerities, that destroyer of Daksha's sacrifice.

description: The donning of the armour on Duryodhana by Drona
sn: पिनाकी सर्वभूतेशो भगनेत्रनिपातनः। ते गत्वा सहिता देवा ब्राह्मणा सह मन्दरम्॥
en: That wielder of the Pinaka, that lord of all creatures, that slayer of the Asura that Bhaganetra. Thereupon all those celestials accompanied by Brahma, proceeded to the Mandara mountain.

description: The donning of the armour on Duryodhana by Drona
sn: अपश्यंस्तेजसां राशिं सूर्यकोटिसमप्रभम्। सोऽब्रवीत् स्वागतं देवा ब्रूत किं करवाण्यहम्॥
en: And there, beheld that heap of energy, who resembled in radiance a million of suns. (Seeing the gods come) Mahadeva said, "All hail O god! speak what am I to do for you!

description: The donning of the armour on Duryodhana by Drona
sn: अमोघं दर्शनं मह्यं कामप्राप्तिरतोऽस्तु वः। एवमुक्तास्तु ते सर्वे प्रत्यूचुस्तं दिवौकसः॥
en: A sight of my self cannot be barren. So let the fruition of your desires proceed from this!” Thus spoken to, all those denizens of heaven

description: The donning of the armour on Duryodhana by Drona
sn: तेजो हृतं नो वृत्रेण गतिर्भव दिवौकसाम्। मूर्तीरीक्षस्व नो देव प्रहारैर्जर्जरीकृताः। शरणं त्वां प्रपन्ना स्म गतिर्भव महेश्वर॥
en: All our energy has been robbed by Vritra. Be you the protector of us the dwellers of heaven. O God, look upon our bodies mangled and mutilated with the wounds inflicted by the Asura. We seek protection from you; O God of gods, be you our refuge.

description: The donning of the armour on Duryodhana by Drona
sn: शर्व उवाच विदितं वो यथा देवाः कृत्येयं सुमहाबला। त्वष्टस्तेजोभवा घोरा दुर्निवार्याकृतात्मभिः॥
en: Sharva said O Gods, it is well-known to all of you, how this Asura, surcharged with strength, dreadful and incapable of being held in check by persons devoid of ascetic merit, came into being, created by the energy of Tvashtri.

description: The donning of the armour on Duryodhana by Drona
sn: अवश्यं तु मया कार्यं साह्यं सर्वदिवौकसाम्। ममेदं गात्रजं शक्र कवचं गृह्य भास्वरम्॥
en: Surely it is my duty to protect the denizens of heaven. O Shakra, take this radiant coat of mail off my body; and O lord of the gods, don it, reiterating these Mantras.

description: The donning of the armour on Duryodhana by Drona
sn: बधानानेन मन्त्रेण मानसेन सुरेश्वर। वधायासुरमुख्यस्य वृत्रस्य सुरघातिनः॥
en: O sovereign gods! Tie this to your body by reciting hymn through mental japa as told by men. Then you will able enough to kill Vritra, the monster king and enemy to the gods.

description: The donning of the armour on Duryodhana by Drona
sn: द्रोण उवाच इत्युक्त्वा वरदः प्रादाद् वर्म तन्मन्त्रमेव च । स तेन वर्मणा गुप्तः प्रायाद् वृत्रचमूं प्रति॥
en: Drona continued Having thus spoken, that giver of boons, gave that armour and the necessary Mantras to Indra. Clad in that coat of mail Indra then assaulted the army of Vritra.

description: The donning of the armour on Duryodhana by Drona
sn: नानाविधैश्च शस्त्रौघैः पात्यमानैर्महारणे। न संधिः शक्यते भेत्तुं वर्मबन्धस्य तस्य तु॥
en: Although then in that dreadful battle myriads of weapons of diverse description were hurled at him, yet they could not slacken or pierce through the joints, of that armour.

description: The donning of the armour on Duryodhana by Drona
sn: ततो जघान समरे वृत्रं देवपतिः स्वयम्। तं च मन्त्रमयं बन्धं वर्म चाङ्गिरसे ददौ॥
en: Then the lord of the celestials slew Vritra in battle and gave afterwards that armour of which the joints were composed of Mantras, unto Angiras.

description: The donning of the armour on Duryodhana by Drona
sn: अङ्गिराः प्राह पुत्रस्य मन्त्रज्ञस्य बृहस्पतेः। बृहस्पतिरथोवाच अग्निवेश्याय धीमते॥
en: Angiras again gave those Mantras to Brihaspati his son conversant with all Mantras. Brihaspati next imparted them to the intelligent Agniveshya.

description: The donning of the armour on Duryodhana by Drona
sn: आग्निवेश्यो मम प्रादात् तेन बघ्नामि वर्म ते। तवाद्य देहरक्षार्थ मन्त्रेण नृपसत्तम॥
en: Agniveshya gave them to me; and now with the help of those mantras I have bound up this armour on you, O foremost of the kings, in order to guard your body from all weaponwounds.

description: The donning of the armour on Duryodhana by Drona
sn: संजय उवाच एवमुक्त्वा ततो द्रोणस्तव पुत्रं महाद्युतिम्। पुनरेव वचः प्राह शनैराचार्यपुङ्गवः॥
en: Sanjaya said Having thus spoken, Drona that foremost of all preceptors, once more addressed your son

description: The donning of the armour on Duryodhana by Drona
sn: ब्रह्मसूत्रेण बध्नामि कवचं तव भारत। हिरण्यगर्भेण यथा बद्धं विष्णोः पुरा रणे॥
en: “O ruler of men, I don this armour on your body joining its parts by means of Brahmathreads. Even thus did Brahman springing from the golden lotus, put it on Vishnu.

description: The donning of the armour on Duryodhana by Drona
sn: यथा च ब्रह्मणा बद्धं संग्रामे तारकामये। शक्रस्य कवचं दिव्यं तथा बधाम्यहं तव।।७शा
en: I do it on you, even in the same manner in which Brahman himself had put this armour of celestial make on Indra, during the battle caused by the abduction of Taraka."

description: The donning of the armour on Duryodhana by Drona
sn: बद्ध्वा तु कवचं तस्य मन्त्रेण विधिपूर्वकम्। प्रेषयामास राजानं युद्धाय महते द्विजः॥
en: Thus having tied that Duryodhana with due mantras, the regenerate Drona dispatched the king to the mighty encounter.

description: The donning of the armour on Duryodhana by Drona
sn: स संनद्धो महाबाहुराचार्येण महात्मना। रथानां च सहस्रेण त्रिगर्तानां प्रहारिणाम्॥
en: Then the mighty-armed king, accoutered by the illustrious preceptor, supported by a thousand car-warriors of the Trigartta country, all accomplished in smiting down.

description: The donning of the armour on Duryodhana by Drona
sn: तथा दन्तिसहस्रेण मत्तानां वीर्यशालिनाम्। अश्वानां नियुतेनैव तथान्यैश्च महारथैः॥
en: As also by a thousand infuriate elephants endued with great mighty and a hundred thousand horses and numerous other mightycar-warriors. armour on

description: The donning of the armour on Duryodhana by Drona
sn: वृतः प्रायान्महाबाहुरर्जुनस्य रथं प्रति। नानावादित्रघोषेण यथा वैराचनिस्तथा॥
en: Advanced against the chariot of Arjuna. He then proceeded accompanied by the sounds of various kinds of musical instruments, even like the son of Virochana (in the days of yore).

description: The donning of the armour on Duryodhana by Drona
sn: ततः शब्दो महानासीत् सैन्यानां तव भारत। अगाधं प्रस्थितं दृष्ट्वा समुद्रमिव कौरवम्॥
en: Thereupon O Bharata, a loud uproar was created by your troops as they beheld the illustrious Kuru king advance like the fathomless deep itself.

sn: संजय उवाच प्रविष्टयोर्महाराज पार्थवार्ष्णेययो रणे। दुर्योधने प्रयाते च पृष्ठतः पुरुषर्षभे॥
en: Sanjaya said When that foremost of men viz., king Duryodhana had started from behind, following Pritha's son and him of the Vrishni race, both of whom, O monarch, had penetrated into the Kaurava ranks.

sn: जवेनाभ्यद्रवद् द्रोणं महता नि:स्वनेन च। पाण्डवाः सोमकैः सार्धं ततो युद्धमवर्तत॥
en: The Pandavas supported by the Somakas furiously assaulted Drona, creating a loud din. Thereupon a fearful battle commenced between them and Drona's troops.

sn: तद् युद्धमभवत् तीव्र तुमुलं लोमहर्षणम्। कुरूणां पाण्डवानां च व्यूहस्य पुरतोऽद्भुतम्॥
en: The battle then that commenced between the Kurus and the Pandavas at the van of their array was terrible, awful and capable of making the hair to stand erect; and it was wonderful to the extreme.

sn: राजन् कदाचिन्नास्माभिईष्टं तादृङ् न च श्रुतम्। यादृङ् मध्यगते सूर्ये युद्धमासीद् विशाम्पते॥
en: O king, that battle that raged when the sun shone on the meridian, was such that we had neither seen nor heard of its like, ever before.

sn: धृष्टाद्युम्नमुखाः पार्था व्यूढानीकाः प्रहारिणः। द्रोणस्य सैन्यं ते सर्वे शरवर्षैरवाकिरन्॥
en: The troops of the sons of Pritha commanded by Dhristadyumna, all accomplished in smiting and arranged in proper order, covered the division of Drona with arrowy showers.

sn: वयं द्रोणं पुरस्कृत्य सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वरम्। पार्षतप्रमुखान् पार्थानभ्यवर्षाम सायकैः॥
en: We also placing that foremost of all wielders of bow namely Drona, at our head, began to pour our showers of arrows on the Parthas headed by the son of Prishata.

sn: महामेघाविवोदीर्णौ मिश्रवातौ हिमात्यये। सेनाग्रे प्रचकाशेते रुचिरे रथभूषिते॥
en: The vanguards of the two hosts, teeming with cars and appearing charming, then looked like two masses of clouds in the summer sky, rushing towards each other, being driven by opposite winds.

sn: समेत्य तु महासेने चक्रतुर्वेगमुत्तमम्। जाह्नवीयमुने नद्यौ प्रावृषीवोल्बणोदके॥
en: Clashing against each other, the two armies put forth their exertions, like the rivers Ganga and Yamuna swelling with water during the rain season.

sn: नानाशस्त्रपुरोवातो द्विपाश्वरथसंवृतः। गदाविद्युन्महारौद्रः संग्रामजलदो महान्॥ भारद्वाजानिलोद्भूतः। शरधारासहस्रवान्। अभ्यवर्षन्महासैन्यः पाण्डुसेनाग्निमुद्धतम्॥
en: Having various kinds of weapons for the wind that preceeded them, abounding in elephants, horses and chariots, surcharged with the lightning formed by the flashing of maces wielded by warriors, the fierce and thick mass of cloud constituted by the army of the Kurus. Driven forward by the tempest constituted by Drona and incessantly pouring its arrowy showers, tried to extinguish the raging fie constituted by the Pandavas.

sn: समुद्रमिव धर्मान्ते विशन् घोरो महानिलः। व्याक्षोभयदनीकानि पाण्डवानां द्विजोत्तमः॥
en: Then that foremost of regenerate heroes, namely Drona, agitated the Pandava hosts like a raging tempest of the summer, agitating the mighty main.

sn: तेऽपि सर्वप्रयत्नेन द्रोणमेव समाद्रवन्। बिभित्सन्तो महासेतुं वार्योधाः प्रबला इव॥
en: They also, putting forth all their endeavours, awaited Drona himself, like a strong current of water striking against an embankment with a view of carry it away.

sn: वारयामास तान् द्रोणो जलौघमचलो यथा। पाण्डवान् समरे क्रुद्धान् पाञ्चालांश्च सकेकयान्॥
en: Then like unto a mountain checking the progress of torrents of water, in that battle, Drona held in check the enraged Pandavas, Parichalas and Kekayas.

sn: अथापरे च राजानः परिवृत्य समन्ततः। महाबला रणे शूराः पञ्चालानन्ववारयन्॥
en: Other kings also endued with great mighty and heroism began to oppose the Panchalas, having surrounded them on all sides.

sn: ततो रणे नरव्याघ्रः पार्षतः पाण्डवैः सह। संजघानासकृद् द्रोणं विभित्सुररिवाहिनीम्॥
en: Thereafter in that battle, that foremost of men, viz., Prishata's son, supported by the Pandavas, repeatedly assailed Drona desirous of breaking through his division.

sn: यथैव शरवर्षाणि द्रोणो वर्षति पार्षते। तथैव शरवर्षाणि धृष्टद्युम्नोऽप्यवर्षत॥
en: Indeed, as as Drona poured his arrowy showers on the son of Prishata, so also, did this latter pour his own on the son of Bharadvaja.

sn: सनिस्त्रिंशपुरोवातः शक्तिप्रासर्टिसंवृतः। ज्याविधुच्चापसंहादो धृष्टद्युम्नबलाहकः॥
en: Then the Dhristadyumna-cloud having rapiers and swords for the winds that preceeded it, well-furnished with darts, lances and scimitar, having the bowstring for its flashes of lightning and the twang of the bow for its rumbling.

sn: शरधाराश्मवर्षाणि व्यसृजत् सर्वतो दिशम्। निनन् रथवराश्वौघान् प्लावयामास वाहिनीम्॥
en: Poured, on all directions, torrents of weapons, for its showers of stones, slaying large bodies of car-warriors, best steed; he seemed to deluge the earth with currents of blood, created by means of his weapon.

sn: यं यमाच्छच्छरैोणः पाण्डवानां रथव्रजम्। ततस्ततः शरैर्दोणमपाकर्षत पार्षतः॥
en: Then with his arrows Prishata's son turned Drona away from all those breaches in the ranks of the car-warriors of the Pandavas, through which the latter tried to pass, striking the men there with his arrows.

sn: तथा तु यतमानस्य द्रोणस्य युधि भारत। धृष्टद्युम्नं समासाद्य त्रिधा सैन्यमभिद्यत॥
en: Then O Bharata, the division of Drona, although he exerted to the best of his mighty, became divided in divided in three parts, having encountered Dhrishtadyumna in battle.

sn: भोजमेकेऽभ्यवर्तन्त जलसन्धं तथापरे। पाण्डवैर्हन्यमानाश्च द्रोणमेवापरे ययुः॥
en: One of these divisions retraced their steps towards Kritavarman the ruler of the Bhojas, the other towards Jalasandha and the other slaughtered by the Pandavas fell back upon Drona himself.

sn: संघट्टयति सैन्यानि द्रोणस्तु रथिनां वरः। व्यधमच्चापि तान्यस्य धृष्टद्युम्नो महारथः॥
en: Then, as many times did that foremost of car-warriors, Drona rally his troops, so many times did that mighty car-warrior Dhrishtadyumna break and route them.

sn: धार्तराष्ट्रास्तथाभूता वध्यन्ते पाण्डुसृञ्जयैः। अगोपाः पशवोऽरण्ये बहुभिः श्वापदैरिव॥
en: Then like herds of cattle destitute of herdsmen slain by the beasts of prey, the troops of the Kurus divided in three divisions, began to be slaughtered by the Pandavas and the Srinjayas.

sn: कालः स्म ग्रसते योधान् धृष्टद्युम्नेन मोहितान्। संग्रामे तुमुले तस्मिन्निति सम्मेनिरे जनाः॥
en: SO People then thought that in that terrible battle Death himself devoured up warriors stupefied by the mighty Dhrishtadyumna.

sn: कुनृपस्य यथा राष्टं दुर्भिक्षव्याधितस्करैः। द्राव्यते तद्वदापन्ना पाण्डवैस्तव वाहिनी॥
en: Just as the dominions of a wicked monarch are devasted by famine, pestilence and marauders, were your Own troops slaughtered and destroyed by the Pandavas.

sn: अर्करश्मिविमिश्रेषु शस्त्रेषु कवचेषु च। चढूंषि प्रत्यहन्यन्त सैन्येन रजसा तथा॥
en: Our eyes were then dazzled and blinded by the weapons and armours on which the sun's rays were reflected, as also by the dust raised by the troops.

sn: त्रिधाभूतेषु सैन्येषु वध्यमानेषु पाण्डवैः। अमर्षितस्ततो द्रोणः पञ्चालान् व्यधमच्छरैः॥
en: Then when his troops had been divided in three bodies and when they were being slaughtered by the Pandavas, Drona inflamed with fury, began to consume the Panchalas with his arrows.

sn: मृद्गतस्तान्यनीकानि निघ्नतश्चापि सायकैः। बभूव रूपं द्रोणस्य कालाग्नेरिव दीप्यतः॥
en: Then as Drona, crushed and slew the hostile host with his arrows, his appearance looked like that of the blazing fire that appears in the time of the universal Dissolution.

sn: रथं नागं हयं चापि पत्तिनश्च विशाम्पते। एकैकेनेषुणा संख्ये निर्बिभेद महारथः॥
en: That mighty car-warrior, o king, then in that battle, began to pierce car-warriors, elephants and steeds and foot-soldiers each with a single arrow only.

sn: पाण्डवानां तु सैन्येषु नास्ति कश्चित् स भारत। दधार योरणे बाणान् द्रोणचापच्युतान् प्रभो॥
en: There was none, O Bharata, in the host of the Pandavas who could bear the arrows in that battle, shot, O lord, from the bow of Drona.

sn: तत् पच्यमानमर्केण द्रोणसायकतापितम्। बभ्राम पार्षतं सैन्यं तत्र तत्रैव भारत॥
en: Scorched by the rays of the sun and felled by the arrows of Drona, the army of the Pandavas, O Bharata, began to reel about on the field.

sn: तथैव पार्षतेनापि काल्यमानं बलं तव। अभवत् सर्वतो दीप्तं शुष्कं वनमिवाग्निना॥
en: So also your troops afflicted by the arrows of Parshata, appeared to blaze up at every place, like a dry forest on fire.

sn: बाध्यमानेषु सैन्येषु द्रोणपार्षतसायकैः। त्यक्त्वा प्राणान् परं शक्त्या युध्यन्ते सर्वतोमुखाः॥३३
en: When the troops were thus being slaughtered by the arrows of Drona and Prishata's son, all warriors, heedless of their lives, fought on putting forth all their best energies.

sn: तावकानां परेषां च युध्यतां भरतर्षभ। नासीत् कश्चिन्महाराज योऽत्याक्षीत् संयुगं भयात्।।३४
en: O foremost of the Bharatas, then there was none among your or the enemy's host, who, O mighty monarch, forsook the fight out of fear.

sn: भीमसेनं तु कौन्तेयं सोदर्याः पर्यवारयन्। विविंशतिचित्रसेनो विकर्णश्च महारथः॥
en: His brothers, Vivinshati, Chitrasena and the mighty car-warrior Vikarna, opposed Kunti's son Bhimasena in the battle.

sn: विन्दानुविन्दावावन्त्यौ क्षेमधूर्तिश्च वीर्यवान्। त्रयाणां तव पुत्राणां त्रय एवानुयायिनः॥
en: The two princes from Avanti, viz., Vinda and Anuvinda and the highly puissant Kshemadhurti were the followers of your three sons,

sn: बाह्लीकराजस्तेजस्वी कुलपुत्रो महारथः। सहसेन; सहामात्यो द्रौपदेयानवारयत्॥
en: That mighty car-warrior, the king of the Balhikas, endued with strength and nobility of birth, assisted by his troops and ministers, began to hold in check the sons of Draupadi.

sn: शैब्यो गोवासनो राजा योधैर्दशशतावरैः। काश्यस्याभिभुवः पुत्रं पराक्रान्तमवारयत्॥
en: Shaivya, the king of the Govasanas supported by a thousand excellent warriors, faced the son of the Kashi king and began to oppose that valorous prince.

sn: अजातशत्रु कौन्तेयं ज्वलन्तमिव पावकम्। मदाणामीश्वरः शल्योराजाराजानमावृणोत्॥
en: King Shalya the ruler of the Madras began to resist king Ajatsatru Yudhishthira that son of Kunti, who resembled a blazing fire.

sn: दुःशासनस्त्ववस्थाप्य स्वमनीकममर्षणः। सात्यकि प्रत्ययौ क्रुद्धः शूरो रथवरं युधि॥
en: The vindictive Dushasana inflamed with rage and inspired with courage and heading his own troops, advanced upon that foremost of car-warriors viz. Satyaki.

sn: स्वकेनाहमनीकेन संनद्धः कवचावृतः। चतुःशतैर्महेष्वासैश्चेकितानमवारयम्॥
en: Myself cased in mail, furnished with arms and supported by my troops, numbering four hundred picked bowmen strong, resisted Chekitana himself.

sn: शकुनिस्तु सहानीको माद्रीपुत्रमवारयत्। गान्धारकैः सप्तशतैश्चापशक्त्यसिपाणिभिः॥
en: Shakuni accompanied by seven hundred Gandhara warriors armed with lances darts and bows, began to oppose the son of Madri.

sn: विन्दानुविन्दावावन्त्यौविराटं मस्यमार्च्छताम्। प्राणांस्त्यक्त्वा महेष्वासौ मित्रार्थेऽभ्युद्यतायुधौ॥
en: The two princes Vinda and Anuvinda, both fierce bowmen, for the sake of their friend Duryodhana, rushed upon Virata the ruler of the Matsyas, heedless of their lives and holding their weapons over head.

sn: शिखण्डिनं याज्ञसेनि रुन्धानमपराजितम्। बाह्रीकः प्रतिसंयत्तः पराक्रान्तमवारयत्॥
en: Exerting his best, Balhika resisted the invincible and puissant Sikhandin the son of Yajnasena, capable resisting all foes.

sn: धृष्टद्युम्नं तु पाञ्चाल्यं क्रूरैः सार्धं प्रभद्रकैः। आवन्त्यः सहसौवीरैः क्रुद्धरूपमवारयत्॥
en: The prince of Avanti supported by the Sauviras and the ruthless ruthless Prabhadrakas opposed Dhristadyumna the Panchala prince whose very appearance reflected wrath.

sn: घटोत्कचं तथा शूरं राक्षसं क्रूरकर्मिणम्। अलायुधोऽद्रवत् क्रुद्धमायान्तमाहवे॥
en: Alayudha quickly rushed upon that various Rakshasa Ghatotkacha of fierce deeds who was proceeding to battle with fury.

sn: अलम्बुषं राक्षसेन्द्रं कुन्तिभोजो महारथः। सैन्येन महता युक्तः क्रुद्धरूपमवारयत्॥
en: The mighty car-warrior Kuntibhoja, supported by large division of troops resisted that wrathful Alambusha that best of the Rakshasas.

sn: सैन्धवः पृष्ठतस्त्वासीत् सर्वसैन्यस्य भारत। रक्षितः परमेष्वासे: कृपप्रभृतिभी रथैः॥
en: Thus in that battle thousands of single combats were fought, O Bharata; and then the ruler of the Sindhus was stationed behind all the troops and he was there protected by Kripa and other such car-warriors and bowmen.

sn: तस्यास्तां चक्ररक्षौ द्वौ सैन्धवस्य बृहत्तमौ। द्रौणिर्दक्षिणतो राजन् सूतपुत्रश्च वामतः॥
en: O King, then the son of Drona on the right and the son of Suta on the left, there, two great warriors were engaged in protecting the carwheels of the ruler of the Sindhus.

sn: पृष्ठगोपास्तु तस्यासन् सौमदत्तिपुरोगमाः। कृपश्च वृषसेनश्च शल: शल्यश्च दुर्जयः॥
en: A number of other warriors headed by Somadattas' son, viz., Kripa,, Vrishasena, Shala and the invincible Shalya were engaged in protecting his rear.

sn: नीतिमन्तो महेष्वासाः सर्वे युद्धविशारदाः। सैन्धवस्य विधायैवं रक्षां युयुधिरे ततः॥
en: Thus many warriors accomplished in the art of fighting and conversant with the rules of policy, having arranged for the safety of the Sindhu king, went on fighting with the Pandavas.

sn: संजय उवाच राजन् संग्राममाश्चर्यं शृणु कीर्तयतो मम। कुरूणां पाण्डवानां च यथा युद्धमवर्तत॥
en: Sanjaya said Hear from me, O king, as I relate to you, the description of the wonderful fight that then took place between the Kuru and the Pandavas.

sn: भारद्वाजं समासाद्य व्यूहस्य प्रमुखे स्थितम्। अयोधयन् रणे पार्था द्रोणानीकं बिभित्सवः॥
en: Then the Parthas desirous of breaking through the Kuru array fought vigorously with Bharadvaja's son Drona, having encountered him at the head of his array.

sn: रक्षमाणः स्वकं व्यूह द्रोणोऽपि सह सैनिकैः। अयोधयद् रणे पार्थान् प्रार्थयानो महद् यशः॥
en: Drona also, desirous of winning great fame, fought on with the Parthas, protecting his array and helped, in the encounter, by his own troops.

sn: विन्दानुविन्दावावन्त्यौ विराटं दशभिः शरैः। आजघ्नतुः सुसंक्रुद्धौ तव पुत्रहितैषिणौ॥
en: Then the two Avanti princes Vinda and Anuvinda, those well-wishers of your son, inflamed with rage, pierced Virata with ten sharp arrows.

sn: विराटश्च महाराज तावुभौ समरे स्थितौ। पराक्रान्तौ पराक्रम्य योधयामास सानुगौ॥
en: Virata mighty monarch, encountering in battle these two puissant heroes together with their followers, fought on cheerfully.

sn: तेषां युद्धं समभवद् दारुणं शोणितोदकम्। सिंहस्य द्विपमुख्याभ्यां प्रभिन्नाभ्यां यथा वने ॥
en: A cruel and sanguinary combat raged between them, like that between a lion and a pair of elephants in rut, in a forest. also,

sn: बाह्रीकं रभसं युद्धे याज्ञसेनिर्महाबलः। आजघ्ने विशिखैस्तीक्ष्णैरैर्मर्माथिभेदिभिः॥
en: The highly powerful son of Yajnasena pierced with force, Balhika, with dreadful and sharp arrows capable of penetrating to the very vitals and the bones.

sn: बाह्नीको याज्ञसेनि तु हेमपुजैः शिलाशितैः। आजघान भूशं क्रुद्धो नवभिनतपर्वभिः॥
en: Thereupon Balhika also inflamed with rage, deeply struck Yajnasena's son with nine shafts of depressed knot, whetted on stone and furnished with golden wings.

sn: तद् युद्धमभवद् घोरं शरशक्तिसमाकुलम्। भीरूणां त्रासजननं शूरूणां हर्षवर्धनम्॥
en: Then that battle raged furiously in which arrows, lances and darts were freely used and that inspired terror into the hearts of the cowards and delight into those of the heroes.

sn: ताभ्यां तत्र शरैर्मुक्तैरन्तरिक्षं दिशस्तथा। अभवत् संवृतं सर्वे न प्राज्ञायत किंचन॥
en: Then with the arrows discharged by them, the welkin and the quarters became completely shrouded and nothing could be distinguished.

sn: शैब्यो गोवासनो युद्धे काश्यपुत्रं महारथम्। ससैन्यो योधयामास गजः प्रतिगजं यथा॥
en: Shaivya the ruler of the Govasanas, with his troops, fought with that mighty car-warrior the son of Kasyapa, even as an elephant fights with its rival.

sn: बाह्रीकराजः संकुद्धो द्रोपदेयान् महारथान्। मनः पञ्चेन्द्रियाणीव शुशुभे योधयन् रणे॥
en: Then the king of the Balhikas excited with wrath, fought with the mighty car-warriors, the sons of Draupadi; and then he shone like the soul fighting with five senses.

sn: अयोधयस्ते सुभृशं तं शरौघैः समन्ततः। इन्द्रियार्था यथा देहं शश्वद् देहवतां वर॥
en: Those five princes, O foremost of embodied beings, fought with his discharging their numerous arrows, like the sense-objects ever fighting with the body.

sn: वार्ष्णेयं सात्यकि युद्धे पुत्रो दुःशासनस्तव। आजघ्ने सायकैस्तीक्ष्णैर्नवभिनतपर्वभिः॥
en: Your son Dushasana struck in that battle Satyaki of the Vrishni race with nine sharp shafts of depressed knots;

sn: सोऽतिविद्धो बलवता महेष्वासेन धन्विना। ईषन्मूर्छा जगामाशु सात्यकिः सत्यविक्रमः॥
en: Thereupon Satyaki of invincible prowess, being thus deeply pierced by that mighty and fierce bowman, was soon partially deprived of his senses.

sn: समाश्वस्तस्तु वार्ष्णेयस्तव पुत्रं महारथम्। विव्याध दशभिस्तूर्णं सायकैः कङ्कपत्रिभिः॥
en: Then regaining his composure, he of the Vrishni race, pierced that mighty car-warrior viz., your son, with ten shafts furnished with wings of the Kanka feathers.

sn: तावन्योन्यं दृढं विद्धावन्योन्यशरपीडितौ। रेजतुः समरे राजन् पुष्पिताविव किंशुकौ॥
en: Then those heroes piercing each other deeply and each afflicted with the shafts of the other, shone, Oking, like two blossoming Kinshuka trees.

sn: अलम्बुषस्तु संक्रुद्धः कुन्तिभोजशरार्दितः। अशोभत भृशं लक्ष्म्या पुष्पाढ्य इव किंशुकः॥
en: Afflicting with the arrows of Kuntibhoja, Alambusha inflamed with wrath, appeared beautiful like a Kinshuka tree rich with the wealth of its flowers.

sn: कुन्तिभोजं ततो रक्षो विद्ध्वा बहुभिरायसैः। अनदद् भैरवं नादं वाहिन्याः प्रमुखे तव॥
en: Then that Rakshasa having pierce Kuntibhoja, with numerous swift, coursing arrows, uttered a terrible war-cry, standing in the van of your troops.

sn: ततस्तौ समरे शूरौ योधयन्तौ परस्परम्। ददृशुः सर्वसैन्यानि शक्रजम्भौ यथा पुरा॥
en: Then all the troops beheld these heroes each fighting with the other, appear like Shakra and Jambha fighting in the days of yore.

sn: शकुनि रभसं युद्धे कृतवैरं च भारत। माद्रीपुत्रौ च संरब्धौ शरैश्चार्दयतां भृशम्॥
en: The twin sons of Madri, Nakula and Sahadeva, inflamed with rage, O Bharata, mangled Shakuni with their shafts, in as much as the latter was their implacable enemy.

sn: तुमुलः स महान् राजन् प्रावर्तत जनक्षयः। त्वया संजनितोऽत्यर्थं कर्णेन च विवर्धितः॥
en: O mighty monarch, the carnage that then spread there was dreadful. Kindled by you, fanned into flames by Karna.

sn: रक्षितस्तव पुत्रैश्च क्रोधमूलो हुताशनः। य इमां पृथिवीं राजन् दग्धुं सर्वां समुद्यतः॥
en: And kept up by your sons, the fire of wrath of the Pandavas, O king, was then in full blaze in order to consume the whole world.

sn: शकुनिः पाण्डुपुत्राभ्यां कृतः सविमुखः शरैः। न स्म जानाति कर्तव्यं युद्धे किंचित् पराक्रमम्॥
en: Shakuni was then compelled to turn his face away from the field, by the arrows shot by the sons of Pandu; and unable to fight any longer, he knew not what to do.

sn: विमुखं चैनमालोक्य माद्रीपुत्रौ महारथौ। ववर्षतुः पुनर्बाणैर्यथा मेघौ महागिरिम्॥
en: Seeing him turn away from the field, those two mighty car-warriors, the sons of Madri, again poured on him their arrowy showers, like two clouds drenching a mighty hill with showers of rain.

sn: स वध्यमानो बहुभिः शरैः संनतपर्वभिः। सम्प्रायाज्जवनैरश्वैोणानीकाय सौबलः॥
en: The son of Subala, struck with numerous arrows of close knots, flew towards the division of Drona, being borne away by fleetest steeds.

sn: घटोत्कचस्तथा शूरं राक्षसं तमलायुधम्। अभ्यवाद् रभसं युद्धे वेगमास्थाय मध्यमम्॥
en: Then with medium impetuosity ihat hero, Ghatotkacha rushed upon the Rakshasa Alayudha, in that battle.

sn: तयोर्युद्धं महाराज चित्ररूपमिवाभवत्। यादृशं हि पुरा वृत्तं रामरावणयोमृधे॥
en: The battle battle between between them was very wonderful, like that which took place between Rama and Ravana in the days of yore.

sn: ततो युधिष्ठिरो राजा मद्रराजानमाहवे। विद्ध्वा पञ्चाशताबाणैः पुनर्विव्याध सप्तभिः॥
en: King Yudhishthira having at first pierced the king of the Madras with five hundred arrows, again pierced him with seven.

sn: ततः प्रववृते युद्धं तयोरत्यद्भुतं नृप। यथा पूर्वे महद् युद्धं शम्बरामरराजयोः॥
en: O king, the battle that was then fought between them, was indeed marvellous and it resembled that fought between Shambara and the chief of the immortals in the days of yore.

sn: विविंशतिश्चित्रसेनो विकर्णश्च तवात्मजः। अयोधयन् भीमसेनं महत्या सेनया वृताः॥
en: Your Vikarna, Vivinshati and Chitrasena, surrounded by their divisions, fought on with Bhimasena. son

sn: संजय उवाच तथा तस्मिन् प्रवृत्ते तु संग्रामे लोमहर्षणे। कौरवेयांस्त्रिधाभूतान् पाण्डवा: समुपाद्रवन्॥
en: Sanjaya said Thus when that horripilating battle was progressing on, the Pandavas rushed against the Kauravas divided into three bodies.

sn: जलसंधं महाबाहुं भीमसेनोऽभ्यवर्तत। युधिष्ठिरः सहानीकः कृतवर्माणमाहवे॥
en: Bhimasena rushed against the mighty armed Jalasandha and king Yudhishthira supported by his divisions assailed Kritavarman in battle.

sn: किरंस्तु शरवर्षाणि रोचमान इवांशुमान्। धृष्टद्युम्नो महाराज द्रोणमभ्यद्रवद् रणे॥
en: Appearing beautiful like the sun and scattering showers of arrows, Dhrishtadyumna, O mighty monarch, rushed upon Drona in that battle.

sn: ततः प्रवृते युद्धं त्वरतां सर्वधन्विनाम्। कुरूणां पाण्डवानां च संक्रुद्धानां परस्परम्॥
en: Then raged the encounter between all the enraged bowmen of the Kurus and the Pandavas, all eater for encountering each other in fight.

sn: संक्षये तु तथा भूते वर्तमाने महाभये। द्वन्द्वीभूतेषु सैन्येषु युध्यमानेष्वभीतवत्॥
en: During the progress of that dreadful carnage when the warriors were undauntedly fighting with one another in single combats.

sn: द्रोणः पाञ्चालपुत्रेण बली बलवता सह। यदक्षिपत् पृषत्कौघांस्तदद्भुतमिवाभवत्॥
en: The mighty Drona fought on with the powerful prince of the Panchalas and the myriads of shafts that he then discharged filled everybody with great wonder.

sn: पुण्डरीकवनानीव विध्वस्तानि समन्ततः। चक्राते द्रोणपाञ्चाल्यौ नृणां शीर्षाण्यनेकशः॥
en: Like a forest of lotuses lying torn hither and hither, the heads of princes were being scattered all over the field by Drona and the prince of the Panchalas.

sn: विनिकीर्णानि वीराणामनीकेषु समन्तताः। वस्त्राभरणशस्त्राणि ध्वजवर्मायुधानि च॥
en: In every division of heroic warriors, garments ornaments standards, armours and weapons were scen scattered in all directions.

sn: तपनीयतनुत्राणाः संसिक्ता रुधिरेण च। संसक्ता इव दृश्यन्ते मेघसंघाः सविद्युतः॥
en: Golden arınours bespattered with blood, looked like masses of clouds illumined with flashes of lightning.

sn: कुञ्जराश्वनरानन्ये पातयन्ति स्म पत्रिभिः। तालमात्राणि चापानि विकर्षन्तो महारथाः॥
en: Other mighty car-warriors, stretching their bows full six cubits long, felled with their winged shafts numerous elephants, steeds and men.

sn: असिचर्माणि चापानि शिरांसि कवचानि च। विप्रकीर्यन्त शूराणां सम्प्रहारे महात्मनाम्॥
en: In that battle between illustrious combatants, many swords, bucklers, bows, heads and armours of heroes, were seen lying scattered all over the field.

sn: उत्थितान्यगणेयानि कबन्धानि समन्ततः। अदृश्यन्त महाराज तस्मिन् परमसंकुले॥
en: In that extremely terrible encounter, () mighty monarch, thousands of headless trunks were seen to rise up from the ground.

sn: गृध्राः कङ्का बकाः श्येना वायसा जम्बुकास्तथा। बहुशः पिशिताशाश्च तत्रादृश्यन्त मारिष॥
en: Vultures and Kankas and crows and jackals and numerous other flesh-eating animals, were seen there, O sire.

sn: भक्षयन्तश्च मांसानि पिबन्तश्चापि शोणितम्। विलुम्पन्तश्च केशांश्च मज्जाश्च बहुधा नृप॥
en: Eating flesh, drinking blood, dragging the hair and pecking the marrow.

sn: आकर्षन्तः शरीराणि शरीरावयवांस्तथा। नराश्वगजसंघानां शिरांसि च ततस्ततः॥
en: And dragging out the bodies and limbs and heads, O king, of slain men, steeds, elephants.

sn: कृतास्त्रा रणदीक्षाभिर्दीक्षिता रणशालिनः। रणे जयं प्रार्थयाना भृशं युयुधिरे तदा॥
en: Accomplished in the use of weapons, skilled in fighting and firmly resolved to fight, warriors exerted themselves vigorously in the battle, desirous of winning fame only.

sn: असिमार्गान् बहुविधान् विचेरुः सैनिकारणे। ऋष्टिभिः शक्तिभिः प्रासैः शूलतोमरपट्टिशैः॥
en: The soldiers then roamed over the field, performing various evolutionary movements performed by swords-men. With darts, lances, javelins, tridents, tomaras and battle axes.

sn: गदाभिः परिर्पश्चान्यैरायुधैश्च भुजैरपि। अन्योन्यं जजिरे क्रुद्धा युद्धरङ्गगता नराः॥
en: With maces, bludgeons and many other kinds of weapons as also with their bare arms, men who careered in that arcna, inflamed with rage, fell to slay one another.

sn: रथिनो रथिभिः सार्धमश्वारोहाश्च सादिभिः। मातङ्गा वरमातङ्गैः पदाताश्च पदातिभिः॥
en: Car-warriors became engaged with carwarriors, cavalry soldiers with cavalry-soldiers, elephants with other excellent elephants and infantry with infantry.

sn: क्षीबा इवान्ये चोन्मत्ता रङ्गेष्विव च वारणाः। उच्चुक्रुशुरथान्योन्यं जघ्नुरन्योन्यमेव च॥
en: Many infuriate elephants as if perfectly mad, uttered loud shrieks and killed one another, after the manner they do so in arenas of sport.

sn: वर्तमाने तथा युद्धे निर्मर्यादे विशाम्पते। धृष्टद्युम्नो हयानश्वैणिस्य व्यत्यमिश्रयत्॥
en: O ruler of men, as that battle, in which none paid any regard to any one, raged, Dhrishtadyumna caused his own horses to be entangled with those of Drona.

sn: ते हयाः साध्वशोभन्त मिश्रिता वातरंहसः। पारावतसवर्णाश्च रक्तशोणाश्च संयुगे॥
en: Those pegion-white and crimson steeds, endued with the fleetness of the wind, appeared extremely beautiful, being mingled together in that battle.

sn: पारावतसवर्णास्ते रक्तशोणविमिश्रिताः। हयाः शुशुभिरे राजन् मेघा इव सविद्युतः॥
en: The horses, O king, then shone like clouds surcharged with lightning. Then Dhrishtadyumna beholding Drona approach him.

sn: धृष्टद्युम्नस्तु सम्प्रेक्ष्य द्रोणमभ्याशमागतम्। असिचर्मादद वीरो धनुरुत्सृज्य भारत॥
en: Grasped his sword and mace and that hero, O Bharata, left aside his bow. Then that slayer of hostile heroes viz., Prishatas son, desirous of achieving a difficult feat.

sn: चिकीर्षुर्दुष्करं कर्म पार्षतः परवीरहा। ईषया समतिक्रम्य द्रोणस्य रथमाविशत्॥
en: Leap over the shafts of Drona's car and entered into it. He then stood sometimes on the yoke and sometimes on its joints.

sn: अतिष्ठ युगमध्ये स युगसनहनेषु च। जधानार्थेषु चाश्वानां तत् सैन्यान्यभ्यपूजयन्॥
en: And sometimes beside the horses. His troops then applauded him highly. When he, armed with the sword, was thus moving quickly on the backs of those crimson steeds.

sn: खङ्गेन चरतस्तस्य शोणाश्वानधितिष्ठतः। न ददर्शान्तरं द्रोणस्तदद्भुतमिवाभवत्॥
en: Drona could find no opportunity for striking him; that indeed seemed extremely marvellous. Indeed like the swoop of a hawk on a piece of meat in a forest.

sn: यथा श्येनस्य पतनं वनेष्वामिषगृद्धिनः। तथैवासीदभीसारस्तस्य द्रोणं जिघांसतः॥ ततः शरशतेनास्य शतचन्द्रं समाक्षिपत्। द्रोणो दुपदपुत्रस्य खङ्गं च दशभिः शरैः॥
en: Looked that sally of Dhrishtadyumna from his own chariot, upon Drona, for his slaughter, Thereafter with a hundred shafts Drona cut-off the shield of Drupada's son, decked with hundred moons and then with another ten he cut-off nis sword.

sn: हयांश्चैव चतुःषष्ट्या शराणां जनिवान् बली। ध्वजं क्षत्रं च भल्लाम्यां तथा तौ पार्ष्णसारथी॥
en: Thereafter that mighty warrior slew the latter's steeds with sixty-four shafts. Then with a couple of broad-head shafts, he cut-off his enemy's standards and umbrella and his two Parshani charioteers.

sn: अथास्मै त्वरितो बाणमपरं जीवितान्तकम्। आकर्णपूर्णं चिक्षेप वज्रं वज्रधरो यथा॥
en: Having at first drawn the bow-string back to the very ears, like Indra hurling the thunderbolt.

sn: तं चतुर्दशभिस्तीक्ष्णैर्बाणैश्चिच्छेद सात्यकिः। ग्रस्तमाचार्यमुख्येन धृष्टद्युम्नं व्यमोचयत्॥
en: Then again with great lightness of hands, he sped at Dhrishtadyumna an arrow capable of destroying his life, but soon Satyaki, with fourteen arrows of great sharpness, cut-off that fatal shaft shot by Drona.

sn: सिंहेनेव मृगं ग्रस्तं नरसिंहेन मारिष। द्रोणेन मोचयामास पाञ्चाल्यं शिनिपुङ्गवः॥
en: Thus, 0 sire, Satyaki rescued Dhrishtadyumna, who had been seized by that foremost of the preceptor, that best of men, like a deer seized by a lion.

sn: सात्यकि प्रेक्ष्य गोप्तारं पाञ्चाल्यं च महाहवे। शराणां त्वरितो द्रोणः षड्विंशत्या समार्पयत्॥
en: That foremost descendant of Sini then rescued the prince of the Panchalas from Drona. Beholding Satyaki save the Panchala prince in that battle. Drona quickly sped at him twenty-six arrows.

sn: ततो द्रोणं शिनेः पौत्रो ग्रसन्तमपि सुंजयान्। प्रत्यविध्यच्छितैर्बाणैः षड्विंशत्या स्तनान्तरे॥
en: Thereupon the grandson of Sini, pierced, with twenty-six arrows of great sharpness, Drona who seemed to swallow up the Srinjayas, on the centre of his breast.

sn: ततः सर्वे रथास्तूर्णं पाञ्चाल्या जयगृद्धिनः। सात्वताभिसृते द्रोणे धृष्टद्युम्नमवाक्षिपन्॥
en: Then, upon the Satvata hero Satyaki advancing upon Drona, all the Panchala carwarriors, desirous of victory, extricated Dhrishtadyumna from that encounter.

description: The battle between Drona and Satyaki
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच बाणे तस्मिन् निकृत्ते तु धृष्टद्युम्ने च मोक्षिते। तेन वृष्णिप्रवीरेण युयुधानेन संजय॥
en: Dhritarashtra said After that arrows shot by Drona had been severed and Dhristadyumna rescued by Yuyudhana that foremost of the Vrishnis, o Sanjaya.

description: The battle between Drona and Satyaki
sn: अमर्षितो महेष्वासः सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वरः। नरव्याघ्रः शिनेः पौत्रे द्रोणः किमकरोद् युधि॥
en: What did the fierce bowman Drona, that foremost of all wielders of weapons, inflamed with wrath, do to the grandson of Sini that foremost of men?

description: The battle between Drona and Satyaki
sn: संजय उवाच सम्प्रद्रुतः क्रोधविषो व्यादितास्यशरासनः। तीक्ष्णधारेषुदशनः शितनाराचदंष्ट्रवान्॥ संरम्भामर्षताम्राक्षो महोरग इव श्वसन्। नरवीरः प्रमुदितः शौणैरश्वैर्महाजवैः॥ उत्पतद्भिरिवाकाशे क्रामद्भिरिव पर्वतम्। रुक्मपुङ्खाञ्छरानस्यन् युयुधानमुपाद्रवत्॥
en: Sanjaya said Then Drona, like a huge snake having wrath for his poison, the stretched bow for his wide open mouth, sharp Narachas for his teeth, whetted arrows for his fangs, with woves coppery in rage and breathing like a furnacethat undaunted warrior, borne by his fleet steeds of crimson hue that appeared to soar high into the heavens or get at the summit of the highest of mountains, advanced against Yuyudhana, scattering right and left his arrows furnished with golden wings.

description: The battle between Drona and Satyaki
sn: शरपातमहावर्षं रथघोषबलाहकम्। कार्मुकाकर्षविक्षेपं नाराचबहुविद्युतम्॥ शक्तिखड्गाशनिधरं क्रोधवेगसमुत्थितम्। द्रोणमेघमनावार्य हयमारुतचोदितम्॥
en: Beholding the irresistible Drona-cloud having showers of arrows for its watery downpour, the rattle of Chariot-wheels for its rumbling noise, the stretched bow for its volume, numerous Narachas for its flashes of lightning, darts and scimitars for its thunder, wrath for the violent wind going before it and steeds for the hurricane driving it forward.

description: The battle between Drona and Satyaki
sn: दृष्ट्वैवाभिपतन्तं तं शूरः परपुरंजयः। उवाज सूतं शैनेयः प्रहसन् युद्धदुर्मदः॥
en: Make towards himself, that subjugator of hostile towns, the invincible and heroic grandson of Sini, smilingly addressing his charioteer said

description: The battle between Drona and Satyaki
sn: एनं वै ब्राह्मणं शूरं स्वकर्मण्यनवस्थितम्। आश्रयं धार्तराष्ट्रस्य राज्ञो दुःखभयापहम्॥
en: Against this heroic Brahmana fallen off from all his duties, who is the refuge of the Dhritarashtras and the despeller of the sorrow and anxiety of their king,

description: The battle between Drona and Satyaki
sn: शीघ्रं प्रजवितैरश्वैः प्रत्युद्याहि प्रहृष्टवत्। आचार्यं राजपुत्राणां सततं शूरमानिनम्॥
en: Who is also he preceptor of all the princes and is ever boastful of his prowess, do rush cheerfully and quickly, being borne by steeds urged to the top of their speed?

description: The battle between Drona and Satyaki
sn: ततो रजतसंकाशा माधवस्य हयोत्तमाः। द्रोणस्याभिमुखाः शीघ्रमगच्छन् वातरंहसः॥
en: Thereupon those best of steeds of argentine hue and of the fleetness of the wind, belonging that descendant of Madhus race, flew in all haste, towards Drona in that battle.

description: The battle between Drona and Satyaki
sn: ततस्तौ द्रोणशैनेयो युयुधाते परंतपौ। शरैरनेकसाहस्रेस्ताडयन्तौ परस्परम्॥
en: Then those two afflicters of foes Drona and Yuyudhana began to fight with each other, striking each other with many a thousand shafts.

description: The battle between Drona and Satyaki
sn: इषुजालावृतं व्योम चक्रतुः पुरुषर्षभौ। पूरयामासतुर्वीरावुभौ दश दिशः शरैः॥
en: Those two foremost of men enshrouded the Welkin in a net-work of arrows and those two heroes filled the ten points of the compass with their arrowy discharges.

description: The battle between Drona and Satyaki
sn: मेघाविवातपायाये धाराभिरितरेतरम्। न स्म सूर्यस्तदा भाति न ववौ च समीरणः॥
en: Like two clouds at the expiration of summer pouring their contents on the Earth, they poured their showers of arrows on each other; the sun did not shine then, nor did the wind bow.

description: The battle between Drona and Satyaki
sn: इषुजालावृतं घोरमन्धकारं समन्ततः। अनाधृष्यमिवान्येषां शूराणामभवत् तदा॥
en: In consequence of these showers of arrows filling the firmament, in impenetrable and deep gloom created there that became unbearable to the other warriors.

description: The battle between Drona and Satyaki
sn: अन्धकारीकृते लोके द्रोणशैनेययोः शरैः। तयोः शीघ्रास्त्रविदुषोोणसात्वतयोस्तदा॥
en: was

description: The battle between Drona and Satyaki
sn: नान्तरं शरवृष्टीनां ददृशे नरसिंहयोः।
en: When the arrows of those two foremost of those accomplished in the use of weapons, viz., Drona and Shini's grandson, had covered the world with that gloom. None could find any interval in the shooting of arrows by those two best of warriors.

description: The battle between Drona and Satyaki
sn: इपूणां संनिपातेन शब्दो धाराभिघातजः॥ शुश्रुवे शक्रमुक्तानामशनीनामिव स्वनः।
en: The sound produced by the clashing of the showers of arrows shot by them, was heard there to resemble the rumble of the thunderbolt hurled by Indra himself,

description: The battle between Drona and Satyaki
sn: नाराचैर्व्यतिविद्धानां शराणां रूपमाबभौ॥ आशीविषविदष्टानां सर्पाणामिव भारत।
en: The appearances of heroic warriors pierced with Narachas looked, O Bharata, like those of snakes of virulent poison, bit by other snakes.

description: The battle between Drona and Satyaki
sn: तयोर्ध्यातलनिर्घोषः शुश्रुवे युद्धशौण्डयोः॥ अजस्रं शैलशृङ्गाणां वज्रेणाहन्यतामिव।
en: The sound produced by the palm-strokes and twanging bows of those two accomplished warriors, was heard there. To resemble the sound that is produced by the incessant striking of the bolt of heaven on mountain summits.

description: The battle between Drona and Satyaki
sn: उभयोस्तौ रथौ राजंस्ते चाश्वास्तौ च सारथी॥ रुक्मपुकैः शरैश्छिन्नाश्चित्ररूपा बभुस्तदा।
en: The chariots of both those heroes, O king and their horses and charioteers being pierced with shafts of golden wings, became beautiful to look at.

description: The battle between Drona and Satyaki
sn: निर्मलानामजिह्यानां नाराचानां विशाम्पते॥ निर्मुक्ताशीविषाभानां सम्पातोभूत् सुदारुणः।
en: O ruler of men, of effulgent and straightgoing Narachas, the down-pour was terrible and it resembled a shower of snakes of virulent poison, that have just cast off their slough.

description: The battle between Drona and Satyaki
sn: उभयोः पतिते छत्रे तथैव पतितो ध्वजौ॥ उभौ रुधिरसिक्ताङ्गावुभौ च विजयैषिणौ।
en: The umbrellas of both those warriors were felled and their standards were also cut down. Both of them were bespattered with blood and both were desirous of obtaining victory.

description: The battle between Drona and Satyaki
sn: नवद्भिः शोणितं गात्रैः प्रस्रुताविव वारणौ॥ अन्योन्यमभ्यविध्येतां जीवितान्तकरैः शरैः।
en: With bodies steeped in blood and looking like two elephants in rut. They began to pierce each other with arrows capable of destroying life.

description: The battle between Drona and Satyaki
sn: गर्जितोत्कृष्टसंनादाः शङ्खदुन्दुभिनिःस्वनाः॥ उपारमन् महाराज व्याजहार न कश्चन।
en: The din of battle caused by war-cries, shouts, roars and the sound of drums and the blare of conchs ceased, O mighty monarch, for none then uttered anything.

description: The battle between Drona and Satyaki
sn: तूष्णीम्भूतान्यनीकानि योधा युद्धादुपारमन्॥ ददर्श द्वैरथं ताभ्यां जातकौतूहलो जनः।
en: The troops became silent and warriors withdrew from the fight, filled with curiosity, men began to behold that single combat between those two heroes.

description: The battle between Drona and Satyaki
sn: रथिनो हस्तियन्तारो हयारोहा: पदातयः॥ अवैक्षन्ताचलैत्रः परिवार्य नरर्षभौ।
en: Car-warriors, elephant-drivers, horsemen and foot-soldiers surrounding those two foremost of men, began to witness that combat with fixed eyes.

description: The battle between Drona and Satyaki
sn: हस्त्यनीकान्यतिष्ठन्त तथानीकानि वाजिनाम्॥ तथैव रथवाहिन्यः प्रतिव्यूह्य व्यवस्थिताः।
en: The elephant-division as also the horse division stood still, so also the car-divisions stood still, arranging themselves in battle array.

description: The battle between Drona and Satyaki
sn: मुक्ताविद्रुमचित्रैश्च मणिकाञ्चनभूषितैः॥ ध्वजैराभरणैश्चित्रैः कवचैश्च हिरण्मयैः। वैजयन्तीपताकाभिः परिस्तोमाङ्गकम्बलैः॥ विमलैर्निशितैः शस्त्रैर्हयानां च प्रकीर्णकैः। जातरूपमयीभिश्च राजनीतिभश्च मूर्धसु॥ गजानां कुम्भमालाभिर्दन्तवेष्टैश्च भारत। सबलाकाः सखद्योताः सैरावतशतह्रदाः॥ अदृश्यन्तोष्णपर्याये मेघानामिव वागुराः।
en: Adorned with diverse kinds of pearls and corals, decked with jewels and gold adorned with standards and ornaments, with armour made of gold, with flags and pennons, with the precious caparisons of elephants, with fine blankets with effulgent and whetted weapons, with Chamaras decked with gold and silver, with warriors on the backs and necks of horse and elephants with garlands round the frontal globes of elephants and with circlets round their tusks, ( Bharata, the Kuru and the Pandava troops then looked like masses of clouds at the close of the summer seasons, decked with rows of cranes and numerous fireflies underneath them and beautified with rainbows and flashes of lightning.

description: The battle between Drona and Satyaki
sn: अपश्यन्नस्मदीयाश्च ते च यौधिष्ठिराः स्थिताः॥ तद् युद्धं युयुधानस्य द्रोणस्य च महात्मनः।
en: O king, Our troops, as also those belonging to Yudhishthira, beheld that combat between Yuyudhana and the illustrious Drona.

description: The battle between Drona and Satyaki
sn: विमानाग्रगता देवा ब्रह्मसोमपुरोगमाः॥ सिद्धचारणसंघाश्च विद्याधरमहोरगाः।
en: Coming there on their sky-ranging cars, the gods headed by Brahma and Soma and hosts of Siddhas and Charanas and Vidyadharas and mighty reptiles, all saw that combat.

description: The battle between Drona and Satyaki
sn: गतप्रत्यागताक्षेपैश्चिौरस्त्रविघातिभिः॥ विविधैर्विस्मयं जग्मुस्तयोः पुरुषसिंहयोः।
en: The backward and forward movements and the modes of fighting, o king, of those two foremost of heroes, filled all of them with wonder.

description: The battle between Drona and Satyaki
sn: हस्तलाघवमस्त्रेषु दर्शयन्तौ महाबलौ॥ अन्योन्यमभिविध्येतां शरैस्तौ द्रोणसात्यकी।
en: Displaying great lightness of hands, those two mighty heroes, namely Drona and Satyaki, pierced each other with each other's arrows.

description: The battle between Drona and Satyaki
sn: ततो द्रोणस्य दाशार्हः शरांश्चिच्छेद संयुगे॥ पत्रिभिः सुदृढराशु धनुश्चैव महाद्युतेः।
en: Thereafter in that battle he of the Dasharha race cut-off the arrows shot by Drona with his strong and winged shafts; as also the bow of that highly effulgent warrior.

description: The battle between Drona and Satyaki
sn: निमेषान्तरमात्रेण भारद्वाजोऽपरं धनुः॥ सज्यं चकार तदपि चिच्छेदास्य च सात्यकिः। ततस्त्वरन् पुनर्दोणो धनुर्हस्तो व्यतिष्ठत॥ सज्यं सज्यं धनुश्चास्य चिच्छेद निशितैः शरैः।
en: But in a wink's time, the son of Bharadvaja fixed the string on another bow; but that also Satyaki cut-off quickly. But again Drona stood ready with a bow in hand. As often however Drona strung his bow so often did Satyaki cut it off and this he did for full sixty-three times.

description: The battle between Drona and Satyaki
sn: एवमेकशतं छिन्नं धनुषां दृढधन्विना॥ न चान्तरं तयोर्दृष्टं संधाने छेदनेऽपि च।
en: Satyaki with his formidable bow cut-off one hundred bows of Acharya. However, it was strange to guess the difference between two functions i.e. when Acharya shoot the arrow and when Satyaki cut-off it.

description: The battle between Drona and Satyaki
sn: ततोऽस्य संयुगे द्रोणो दृष्ट्वा कर्मातिमानुषम्॥ युयुधानस्य राजेन्द्र मनसैतदचिन्तयत्।
en: Thereupon in that battle, Drona beholding that superhuman feat thought in his mind thus.

description: The battle between Drona and Satyaki
sn: एतदस्त्रबलं रामे कार्तवीर्ये धनंजये॥ भीष्मे च पुरुषव्याघ्र यदिदं सात्वतां वरे। तं चास्य मनसा द्रोणः पूजयामास विक्रमम्॥
en: Achieved by Yuyudhana, O king-'This force of weapon that I see in this foremost of the Satvata race is possible only in Rama, in Kartavirya, in Dhananjaya and in Bhishma'. So, Drona praised the prowess of that hero in his mind.

description: The battle between Drona and Satyaki
sn: लाघवं वासवस्येव सम्प्रेक्ष्य द्विजसत्तमः। तुतोषास्त्रविदां श्रेष्ठस्तथा देवाः सवासवाः॥
en: Then that foremost of the regenerate ones, that best of all wielders of weapons, namely Drona, as also the celestials with Indra himself at their head, were highly gratified at seeing the lightness of hands displayed by Satyaki, which resembled that of Vasava himself.

description: The battle between Drona and Satyaki
sn: न तामालक्षयामासुर्लघुतां शीघ्रचारिणः। गन्धर्वाश्च विशाम्पते॥ सिद्धाचारणसंघाश्च विदुयॊणस्य कर्म तत्।
en: O ruler of men neither the gods nor the Gandharvas ever before beheld the like of that lightress of hands now displayed by the swiftly-moving Yuyudhana. Although they, the Siddhas and the Charanas, were cognisant of the feats of which Drona was capable.

description: The battle between Drona and Satyaki
sn: देवाश्च युयुधानस्य ततोऽन्यद् धनुरादाय द्रोणः क्षत्रियमर्दनः॥ अस्त्रैरस्त्रविदां श्रेष्ठो योधयामास भारत।
en: Then taking up another bow, Drona that crusher of Kshatriyas that foremost of those acquainted with the use of weapons, O Bharata, placed some weapons on its string.

description: The battle between Drona and Satyaki
sn: तस्यास्त्राण्यस्त्रमायाभिः प्रतिहत्य स सात्यकिः॥ जघान निशितैर्बाणैस्तदद्भुतमिवाभवत्।
en: But repulsing Drona's weapons with the illusion of his own weapons, Satyaki pierced Drona with exceedingly sharp arrows; that indeed appeared marvellous.

description: The battle between Drona and Satyaki
sn: तस्यातिमानुषं कर्म दृष्ट्वान्यैरसमं रणे॥ युक्तं योगेन योगज्ञास्तावकाः समपूजयन्।
en: Beholding that superhuman feat achieved by him in battle-feat which was incapable of being achieved by others and which displayed great tact, those amongst your warriors who were judges of skill, highly praised it.

description: The battle between Drona and Satyaki
sn: यदस्त्रमस्यति द्रोणस्तदेवास्यति सात्यकिः॥ तमाचार्योऽप्यसम्भ्रान्तोऽयोधयच्छत्रुतापनः
en: Whatsoever weapon Drona discharged, Satyaki also discharged the same. Beholding this, scorcher of foes namely the preceptor fought with Satyaki diffidently.

description: The battle between Drona and Satyaki
sn: ततः क्रुद्धो महाराज धनुर्वेदस्य पारगः॥ वधाय युयुधानस्य दिव्यमस्त्रमुदैरयत्।
en: Thereupon, O mighty monarch, that one who had reached the end of all military sciences, being inflamed with wrath invoked into existence a celestial weapon slaughtering Yuyudhana.

description: The battle between Drona and Satyaki
sn: तदाग्नेयं महाघोरं रिपुघ्नमुपलक्ष्य सः॥ दिव्यमस्त्रं महेष्वासो वारुणं समुदैरयत्।
en: Beholding that dreadful and fiery dart capable of slaying the foe and of celestial make, that fierce bowman Satyaki invoked into existence the Varuna weapon.

description: The battle between Drona and Satyaki
sn: हाहाकारो महानासीद् दृष्ट्वा दिव्यास्त्रधारिणौ॥ न विचेरुस्तदाकाशे भूतान्याकाशगाम्यपि।
en: Beholding them both using celestial weapons, the troops uttered loud cries of Alas weapon for and Oh; then the denizens of the air ceased to range through the sky.

description: The battle between Drona and Satyaki
sn: अस्त्रे ते वारुणाग्नेये ताभ्यां बाणसमाहिते॥ न यावदभ्यपद्येतां व्यावर्तदथ भास्करः।
en: When the Varuna and Agneva weapons were placed on their bow strings just at that moment, the lustrous orb of day went below the horizon.

description: The battle between Drona and Satyaki
sn: ततो युधिष्ठिरो राजा भीमसेनश्च पाण्डवः॥ नकुलः सहदेवश्च पर्यरक्षन्त सात्यकिम्।
en: Thereupon, king Yudhishthira and Bhimasena and the son of Pandu, (Arjuna) and Nakula and Sahadeva, rushed to the rescue of Satyaki.

description: The battle between Drona and Satyaki
sn: धृष्टद्युम्नमुखैः सार्ध विराटश्च सकेकयः॥ मत्स्याः शाल्वेयसेनाश्च द्रोणमाजग्मुरञ्जसा।
en: Other warriors headed by Dhristadyumna and accompanied by Virata and his divisions so also the Matsyas and Shalvas quickly advanced upon Drona.

description: The battle between Drona and Satyaki
sn: द्रोणमभ्युपपद्यन्त दुःशासनं पुरस्कृत्य राजपुत्राः सहस्रशः॥ सपनैः परिवारितम्।
en: Thousands of princes, on the other hand, headed by Dushasana proceeded to help Drona who had been thoroughly encompassed by the foe.

description: The battle between Drona and Satyaki
sn: ततो युद्धमभूद् राजेस्तेषां तव च धन्विनाम्॥ रजसा संवृते लोके शरजालसमावृते।
en: Thereat, O king, the fight between your warriors and those of the Pandava, commenced anew. Then the earth became enveloped in a cloud of dust and in a net-work of arrows.

description: The battle between Drona and Satyaki
sn: सर्वमाविग्नमभवन्न प्राज्ञायत किंचन। सैन्येन रजसा ध्वस्ते निर्मर्यादमवर्तत॥
en: Everything being covered, nothing could any longer be distinguished. Thus when the troops were overwhelmed with dust, the battle raged in utter disregard of all rules of combat.

description: The slaughter of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: संजय उवाच विवर्तमाने त्वादित्ये तत्रास्तशिखरं प्रति। रजसा कीर्यमाणे च मन्दीभूते दिवाकरे॥
en: Sanjaya said When the sun had turned in its downward course towards the summit of the Western hills, when the earth was scattered over the dust and when the effulgence of the solar disc had become lessencd.

description: The slaughter of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: तिष्ठतां युध्यमानानां पुनरावर्ततामपि। अज्यतां जयतां चैव जगाम तदहः शनैः॥
en: And when some of the soldiers were standing aloof, some fighting on, returning to the charge and some winning victory, the day gradually began to wane.

description: The slaughter of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: तथा तेषु विषक्तेषु सैन्येषु जयगृद्धिषु। अर्जुनो वासुदेवश्च सैन्धवायैव जग्मतुः॥
en: Thus when the troops inflamed with the hopes of victory were fighting together, Arjuna and Vasudeva proceeded towards the spot where the ruler of the Sindhus were.

description: The slaughter of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: रथमार्गप्रमाणं कौन्तेयो निशितैः शरैः। चकार यत्र पन्थानं ययौ येन जनार्दनः॥
en: Vibhatsu the son of Kunti, with his sharp shafts went on creating breaches wide enough for his chariot io pass through; and through these breaches, the son of Vasudeva guided the chariot.

description: The slaughter of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: यत्र यत्र रथो याति पाण्डवस्य महात्मनः। तत्र तत्रैव दीर्यन्ते सेनास्तव विशाम्पते॥
en: Wherever the car of the illustrious son of Pandu proceeded, thither O ruler of men your troops began to give way.

description: The slaughter of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: रथशिक्षां तु दाशार्हो दर्शयामास वीर्यवान्। उत्तमाधममध्यानि मण्डलानि विदर्शयन्॥
en: Then he of the Dasharha race endued with great might, displayed his superior skill in driving the car, in as much he performed, with the car, numerous kinds of circular motions.

description: The slaughter of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: तेतु नामाङ्किताः पीता: कालज्वलनसंनिभाः। स्नायुनद्धाः सुपर्वाणः पृथवो दीर्घगामिनः॥ वैणवाश्चायसाश्चोग्रा ग्रसन्तौ विविधानरीन्। रुधिरं पतगैः सार्धे प्राणिनां पपुराहवे॥
en: Then, arrows having their names engraved on them, well-tempered, of the effulgence of the fire of dessolution, tied round with cat-guts, of polished joints, thick, far-reaching, made either of stiff bamboo or of iron, capable of taking the life out of the enemies, drank in that battle the life blood of numerous warriors, together with the birds of prey assembled on the field.

description: The slaughter of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: रथस्थितोऽग्रतः क्रोशं यानस्यत्यर्जुनः शरान्। रथे क्रोशमतिक्रान्ते तस्य ते नन्ति शात्रवान्॥
en: The arrows which Arjuna discharged standing on his car, fell two miles ahead and pierced and mangled the foe, just when that car came up to the spot.

description: The slaughter of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: तार्श्वमारुतरंहोभिर्वाजिभिः साधुवाहिभिः। तदागच्छद्धृषीकेशः कृत्स्नं विस्मापयजगत्॥
en: Borne by those yoke-bearing steeds endued with the fleetness of Garuda or the wind, Hrishikeshas, advanced with such quickness that caused the whole universe to be filled with amazement.

description: The slaughter of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: न तथा गच्छति रथस्तयनस्य विशाम्पते। नेन्द्रस्य न तु रुद्रस्य नापि वैश्रवणस्य च॥
en: O ruler of men, even the chariot of the sun himself or of Indra or of Rudra or of Vaishravana, can never proceed so quickly.

description: The slaughter of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: नान्यस्य समरे राजन् गतपूर्वस्तथा रथः। यथा ययावर्जुनस्य मनोऽभिप्रायशीघ्रगः॥
en: Indeed, no one else's chariot had before moved with such quickness in battle as Arjuna's chariot then moving with the fleetness of a glance of the mind.

description: The slaughter of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: प्रविश्य तु रणे राजन् केशवः परवीरहा। सेनामध्ये हयांस्तूर्णं चोदयामास भारत॥
en: Then having taken the chariot to the thick of the fight, that slayer of hostile heroes, Keshava, O Bharata, quickly drove the steeds of it into the ranks of the soldiers.

description: The slaughter of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: ततस्तस्य रथौघस्य मध्यं प्राप्य हयोत्तमाः। कृच्छ्रेण रथमूहुस्तं क्षुत्पिपासासमन्विताः॥
en: Having penetrated into the rear of the cardivision, these excellent steeds drew the car of Arjuna with great difficulty, suffering as they did from hunger, thirst and fatigue.

description: The slaughter of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: क्षताश्च बहुभिः शस्त्रैर्युद्धशौण्डैरनेकशः। मण्डलानि विचित्राणि विचेरुस्ते मुहुर्मुहुः॥
en: They were also mangled with numerous weapons by many foremost of combatants. Then they began to move in various wonderful circular motions.

description: The slaughter of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: हतानां वाजिनागानां स्थानां च नरैः सह। उपरिष्टादतिक्रान्ताः शैलाभानां सहस्रशः॥
en: Passing over many slain steeds elephants and many men and also over broken cars, like a group of locusts.

description: The slaughter of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे वीरावावन्त्यौ भ्रातरौ नृप। सहसेनो समाच्छेतां पाण्डवं क्लान्तवाहनम्॥
en: During this opportunity, O king, the two heroic brothers, the princes of Avanti supported by their troops, rushed upon of Pandu whose steeds were fatigued and tired.

description: The slaughter of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: तावर्जुनं चतुःषष्ट्यासप्तत्या च जनार्दनम्। शराणां च शतैरश्वानविध्येतां मुदान्वितौ॥
en: Filled with delight they pierced Arjuna with sixty-four, Janardana with seventy and the horses with a hundred shafts.

description: The slaughter of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: तावर्जुनो महाराज नवभिनतपर्वभिः। आजघान रणे क्रुद्धो मर्मज्ञो मर्मभेदिभिः॥
en: Then the enraged Arjuna knowing the vital parts of the body, pierced them both, O king, with nine arrows of depressed knots, all capable of penetrating to the very vitals.

description: The slaughter of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: ततस्तौ तु शरौघेण वीभत्सुं सहकेशवम्। आच्छदयेतां संरब्धौ सिंहनादं च चक्रतुः॥
en: Thereat inflamed with rage, those two warriors covered Vibhatsu and Keshava with the son their arrowy downpour and uttered loud warcries.

description: The slaughter of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: तयोस्तु धनुषी चित्रे भल्लाभ्यां श्वेतवाहनः। चिच्छेद समरे तूर्णं ध्वजौ च कनकोज्ज्वलौ॥
en: Then that hero of white steeds with a pair of broad-headed shafts, quickly cut-off in that battle the two wonderful bows of those princes, as also their standards of golden effulgence.

description: The slaughter of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: अथान्ये धनुषी राजन् प्रगृह्य समरे तदा। पाण्डवं भृशसंक्रुद्धावर्दयामासतुः शरैः॥
en: Thereupon, Oking, taking another two bows and excited to the highest pitch of fury, they began to afflict sorely the son of Pandu, with their arrows.

description: The slaughter of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: तयोस्तु भृशसंक्रुद्धः शराभ्यां पाण्डुनन्दनः। धनुशी चिच्छिदे तूर्णं भूय एव धनंजयः॥
en: Then again, that son of Pandu Dhananjaya, inflamed with rage, quickly cut-off their bows with another pair of arrows.

description: The slaughter of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: तथान्यैर्विशिखैस्तूर्णं रुक्मपुत्रैः शिलाशितैः। जघानाश्वांस्तथा सूतौ पार्णी च सपदानुगौ॥
en: Then with other shafts, furnished with golden wings and whetted on stone, he quickly slew their steeds, charioteers, Parshni-drivers and followers.

description: The slaughter of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: ज्येष्ठस्य च शिरः कायात् क्षुरप्रेण न्यकृन्तत। स पपात हतः पृथ्व्यां वातरुग्ण इव दुमः॥
en: Thereafter with a razor-headed arrow, he cut the head of the elder of the two brothers, off his trunk; thus slain, the latter fell down on the Earth like a tree broken down by the wind.

description: The slaughter of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: विन्दं तु निहतं दृष्ट्वा ह्यनुविन्दः प्रतापवान्। हताश्वं रथमुत्सृज्य गदां गृह्य महाबलः॥
en: The highly puissant Anuvinda, beholding Vinda thus slain, left the car of which the steeds were slain; and that mighty hero, taking up a mace.

description: The slaughter of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: अभ्यवर्तत संगामे भ्रातुर्वधमनुस्मरम्। गदया रथिनां श्रेष्ठो नृत्यन्निव महारथः॥
en: Rushed towards Arjuna's car for avenging the death of his brother. Then that mighty car-warrior, that foremost of all car-warriors armed with his mace, appeared to dance on the field.

description: The slaughter of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: अनुविन्दस्तु गदया ललाटे मधुसूदनम्। स्पृष्ट्वा नाकम्पयत् क्रुद्धो मैनाकमिव पर्वतम्॥
en: Inflamed with rage then Anuvinda struck with that mace of his, the slayer of Madhu on the forehead. But he could not make him tremble who remained immovable like the Mainaka mountain.

description: The slaughter of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: तस्यार्जुनः शरैः षड्भिर्गीवां पादौ भुजौ शिरः। निचकर्त स संछिन्नः पपातादिचयो यथा॥
en: Of him, with six shafts, Arjuna cut-off the neck, the two legs, his arms and his head; and thus cut to pieces, he fell down like fragments of rocks.

description: The slaughter of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: ततस्तौ निहतौ दृष्ट्वा तयो राजन् पदानुगाः। अभ्यद्रवन्त संक्रुद्धाः किरन्तः शतशः शरान्॥
en: Then, O king, beholding those two heroes slain, their followers inflamed with rage, rushed against Arjuna, discharging arrows by thousands.

description: The slaughter of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: तानर्जुनः शरैस्तूर्णं निहत्य भरतर्षभ। व्यरोचत यथा वह्निवं दग्ध्वा हिमात्यये॥
en: Quickly dispatching them with his arrows, O foremost of the Bharata, Arjuna, then appeared beautiful like the fire consuming the forest at the expiration of winter.

description: The slaughter of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: तयोः सेनामतिक्राम्य कृच्छ्रादिव धनंजयः। विबभौ जलदं हित्वा दिवाकर इवोदितः॥
en: Then Dhananjaya, having passed with difficulty, through their (Vinda and Anuvinda's) divisions, appeared beautiful like the lustrous orb of the day emerging out of a cluster of clouds.

description: The slaughter of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: तं दृष्ट्वा कुरवस्त्रस्ताः प्रहृष्टाश्चाभवन् पुनः। अभ्यवर्तन्त पार्थे च समन्ताद् भरतर्षभ॥
en: At first beholding him the Kurus were struck with panic! But in the next moment they were filled with delight; and then, O foremost of the Bharatas, they rushed upon Pritha's son from all sides.

description: The slaughter of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: श्रान्तं चैनं समालक्ष्य ज्ञात्वा दूरे च सैन्धवम्। सिंहनादेन महता सर्वतः पर्यवारयन्॥
en: Beholding them fatigued and knowing the ruler of the Sindhus to be stationed afar, they surrounded Arjuna with a loud roar.

description: The slaughter of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: तांस्तु दृष्ट्वा सुसंरब्धानुत्स्मयन् पुरुषर्षभः। शनकैरिव दाशार्हमर्जुनो वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
en: Beholding them highly excited, that foremost of men Arjuna smilingly addressed these words to that descendant of the Dasharha

description: The slaughter of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: शरार्दिताश्च ग्लानाश्च हया दूरे च सैन्धवः। किमिहानन्तरं कार्यं ज्यायिष्ठं तव रोचते॥
en: "Our steeds are afflicted with arrowwounds; they are exhausted; the ruler of the Sindhus is still far off. What in your opinion is the best course to be adopted now?

description: The slaughter of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: ब्रूहि कृष्ण यथातत्त्वं त्वं हि प्राज्ञतमः सदा। भवन्नेत्रा रणे शत्रून् विजेष्यन्तीह पाण्डवाः॥
en: Speak, O Krishna, truly on this point? You are ever the foremost of the wise. The sons of Pandu, having yourself only for their eyes, can hope to vanquish their enemies in battle.

description: The slaughter of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: मम त्वनन्तरं कृत्यं यद् वै तत् त्वं निबोध मे। हयान् विमुच्य हि सुखं विशल्यान् कुरु माधव॥
en: Hear what seems to me to be our duty next. Unyoking the steeds, leave them to their ease and O Madhava, draw out the arrows from their body."

description: The slaughter of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: एवमुक्तस्तु पार्थेन केशवः प्रत्युवाच तम्। म्माप्येतन्मतं पार्थ यदिदं ते प्रभाषितम्॥
en: Thus spoken to by Pritha's son, Keshava replied to him saying-"O Partha, I am also of the same opinion that you have expressed."

description: The slaughter of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: अर्जुन उवाच अहमावारयिष्यामि सर्वसैन्यानि केशव। त्वमप्यत्र यथान्यायं कुरु कार्यमनन्तरम्॥
en: Arjuna said O Keshava, I shall hold the whole army in check. Do you duly perform whatever should be done now.

description: The slaughter of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: संजय उवाच सोऽवतीर्य रथोपस्थादसम्भ्रान्तो धनंजयः। गाण्डीवं धनुरादाय तस्थो गिरिरिवाचलः॥
en: Sanjaya said Thereupon descending from the terrace of his car, Dhananjaya, with the Gandiva bow in his grasp, stood on the field of battle like an immovable hill.

description: The slaughter of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: तमभ्यधावन् क्रोशन्तः क्षत्रिया जयकाक्षिणः। इदं छिद्रमिति ज्ञात्वा धरणीस्थं धनंजयम्॥
en: Beholding Dhananjaya on the ground and taking this to be a meet opportunity, the Kshatriyas, desirous of obtaining victory and uttering load roars, rushed upon the former.

description: The slaughter of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: तमेकं रथवंशेन महता पर्यवारयन्। विकर्षन्तश्च चापानि विसृजन्तश्च सायकान्॥
en: Then with a mighty host of cars, they surrounded that single-handed hero, stretching their bows and discharging their arrows right and left.

description: The slaughter of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: शस्त्राणि च विचित्राणि क्रुद्धास्तव व्यदर्शयन्। छादयन्तः शरैः पार्थं मेघा इव दिवाकरम्॥
en: Inflamed with rage, they then displayed numerous wonderful weapons; and like the clouds covering the solar disc, they covered Pritha's son with their arrows.

description: The slaughter of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: अभ्यद्रवन्त वेगेन क्षत्रियाः क्षत्रियर्षभम्। नरसिंहं रथोदारा: सिंह मत्ता इव द्विपाः॥
en: Then those Kshatriyas, illustrious carwarriors all, rushed with impetuously upon that foremost of Kshatriyas and that best of men, Arjuna, like infuriate elephant rushing upon a lion.

description: The slaughter of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: तत्र पार्थस्य भुजयोर्महद्बलमदृश्यत। यत् क्रुद्धो बहुलाः सेनाः सर्वतः समवारयत्॥
en: Then we beheld the wonderful might of Partha's arms inasmuch as inflamed with wrath, he held in check, the numerous army of the Kauravas.

description: The slaughter of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: अस्त्रैरस्त्राणि संवार्य द्विषतां सर्वतोविभुः। इषुभिर्बहुभिस्तूर्णं सर्वानेव समावृणोत्॥
en: Resisting with his own weapons those hurled by the foe, that highly puissant hero quickly covered all his adversaries with his myriad shafts.

description: The slaughter of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: तत्रान्तरिक्षे बाणानां प्रगाढानां विशाम्पते। संघर्षण महार्चिष्मान् पावकः समजायत॥
en: The, O ruler of men, generated by the clash of those thick showers of arrows, a mighty fire of blazing flames, burnt on that part of the welkin.

description: The slaughter of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: तत्र तत्र महेष्वासैः श्वसद्भिः शोणितोक्षितैः। हयैर्नागैश्च सम्मिन्नैर्नदद्धिश्चारिकर्षणैः॥ संरब्धैश्चारिभिर्वीरैः प्रार्थयद्भिर्जयं मृधे। एकस्थैर्बहुभिः क्रुद्धैरूष्मेव समजायत॥
en: There, in consequence of countless heroes, all inflamed with wrath and united together for a common cause seeking to obtain victory in battle, supported by steeds bespattered with blood and breathing heavily and by maddened and foe-crushing elephants emitting fierce yells, the weather became excessively hot.

description: The slaughter of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: शरोर्मिणं ध्वजावर्तं नागनकं दुरत्ययम्। पदातिमत्स्यकलिलं शङ्खदुन्दुभिनि:स्वनम्॥ असंख्येयमपारं च रथोर्मिणमतीव च। उष्णीषकमठं छत्रपताकाफेनमालिनम्॥ रणसागरमक्षोभ्यं मातङ्गाङ्गशिलाचितम्। वेलाभूतस्तदा पार्थः पत्रिभिः समवारयत्॥
en: Then with his arrows Pritha's son held in check that uncrossable, wide, fathomless ocean of cars-incapable of being, agitated, having arrows for its waves, flags for its whirl-pools, elephants for its sharks fcot-soldiers for its countless fishes, the blare of conches and the sound of drums for its roar, chariots for its swelling current, turbans of warriors for its tortoises, umbrellas and banners for its foam and the carcasses of elephants for its submarine rocks, which then was appearing like a vast continent.

description: The slaughter of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच अर्जुने धरणी प्राप्ते हयहस्ते च केशवे। एतदन्तरमासाद्य कथं पार्थो न घातितः॥
en: Dhritarashtra said Dhritarashtra asked-Why did my soldiers killed the son of Kunti when Arjuna descended on earth and god Krishna started giving treatment to the horses because it was the good opportunity.

description: The slaughter of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: संजय उवाच सद्यः पार्थिव पार्थेन निरुद्धाः सर्वपार्थिवाः। रथस्था धरणीस्थेन वाक्यमच्छान्दसं यथा॥
en: Sanjaya said Sanjaya said Partha in the meantime resisted all kings seated on chariots suddenly, the same way as the sentence contrary to Vedas is declared unacceptable. This valour he exhibited when merely stood on the earth.

description: The slaughter of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: सपार्थः पार्थिवान् सर्वान् भूमिस्थोऽपिरथस्थितान्। एको निवारयामास लोभः सर्वगुणानिव॥
en: As the greed suppresses all qualities, Arjuna resisted all kings seated on their chariots even when his feet were touching the ground and chariot was wrecked.

description: The slaughter of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: ततो जनार्दनः संख्ये प्रिय पुरुषसत्तमम्। असम्भ्रान्तो महाबाहुरर्जुनं वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
en: Then as the battle progressed, the mighty armed and dauntless Janardana addressing his dear friend, that foremost of men (Arjuna), thus spokeउदपानमिहाश्वानां नालमस्ति रणेऽर्जुन।

description: The slaughter of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: परीप्सन्ते जलं चेमे पेयं न त्ववगाहनम्॥
en: O Arjuna, there is no water here on the field of battle for the forces to drink from. They want water for drinking and not for a bath.

description: The slaughter of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: इदमस्तीत्यसम्भ्रान्तो ब्रुवन्नस्त्रेण मेदिनीम्। अभिहत्यार्जुनश्चक्रे वाजिपानं सरः शुभम्॥
en: Thereupon saying “Here is it" Arjuna fearlessly struck the Earth with a weapon and thus created a beautiful lake there from which the teeds could quench their thirsts.

description: The slaughter of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: हंसकारण्डवाकीर्णं चक्रवाकोपशोभितम्। सुविस्तीर्णं प्रसन्नाम्भः प्रफुल्लवरपङ्कजम्॥
en: That watery expanse abounded in swans and ducks and was beautified with hosts of Chakravakas. Its water was translucent and abounded with full-blown lotuses of the best order.

description: The slaughter of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: कूर्ममत्स्यगणाकीर्णमगाधमृषिसेवितम्। आगच्छन्नारदमुनिदर्शनार्थं कृतं क्षणात्॥
en: It swarmed with tortoises and fishes and was fathomless and frequented by numerous seas. Then there came the sage Narada to have a look at that lake created there in a moment's time.

description: The slaughter of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: शरवंशं शरस्थूणं शराच्छादनमद्भुतम्। शरवेश्माकरोत् पार्थस्त्वष्टेवाद्भुतकर्मकृत्॥
en: Then Partha that performer of wonderful works like Krishna himself, created there an arrowy hall having arrows for its beams and rafts, arrows for its pillars and arrows for its roof.

description: The slaughter of Vinda and Anuvinda
sn: ततः प्रहस्य गोविन्दः साधु साध्वित्यथाब्रवीत्। शरवेश्मनि पार्थेन कृत तस्मिन् महात्मना॥
en: Thereupon Govinda, seeing the illustrious son of Pritha construct that hall there, laughing applauded him saying "Well-done, welldone."

sn: संजय उवाच सलिले जनिते तस्मिन् कौन्तेयेन महात्मना। निस्तारिते द्विषत्सैन्ये कृते च शरवेश्मनि॥
en: Sanjaya said When the illustrious son of Kunti had created that water there and had held in check the troops of the enemies and when he had constructed that arrowy hall.

sn: वासुदेवो रथात् तूर्णमवतीर्य महाद्युतिः। मोचयामास तुरगान् विनुन्नान् कङ्कपत्रिभिः॥
en: The highly effulgent son of Vasudeva descending down quickly from the chariot unharnessed the horses lacerated with arrows furnished with wings of the Kanka feathers.

sn: अदृष्टपूर्वे तद् दृष्ट्वा साधुवादो महानभूत्। सिद्धचारणसंघानां सैनिकानां च सर्वशः॥
en: The Siddhas, the Charanas and the troops present there, beholding that sight unseen before, uttered loud exclamations in praise of Arjuna.

sn: पदातिनं तु कौन्तेयं युध्यमानं महारथाः। नाशक्नुवन् वारयितुं तदद्भुतमिवाभवत्॥
en: That all the mighty car-warriors of your army were unable to resist that son of Kunti who then was fighting standing on his legs, was indeed wonderful.

sn: आपतत्सु रथौधेषु प्रभूतगजवाजिषु। नासम्भ्रमत् तदा पार्थस्तदस्य पुरुषानति॥
en: Though myriads of chariots and thousands upon thousands of elephants and steeds assailed him, yet Partha experienced no fear; but every moment obtained advantages over his enemies.

sn: व्यसृजन्त शरौघांस्ते पाण्डवं प्रति पार्थिवाः। न चाव्यथत धर्मात्मा वासविः परवीरहा॥
en: Showers of arrows were poured upon that son of Pandu by the hostile kings; but that slayer of foes, the illustrious son of Vasava felt no pain.

sn: स तानि शरजालानि गदाः प्रासांश्च वीर्यवान्। आगतानग्रसत् पार्थः सरितः सागरो यथा॥
en: Then the highly puissant son of Pritha received those showers of arrows, lances and maces, like the ocean receiving the numerous rivers flowing into it.

sn: अस्त्रवेगेन महता पार्थो बाहुबलेन च। सर्वेषां पार्थिवेन्द्राणामग्रसत् तान् शरोत्तमान्॥
en: With the tremendous force of his arms, Pritha's son began to swallow up, as it were, all the excellent arrows shot at him by hostile kings.

sn: तत् तु पार्थस्य विक्रान्तं वासुदेवस्य चोभयोः। अपूजयन् महाराज कौरवा महदद्भुतम्॥
en: During that fight, O mighty kings, even the Kurus themselves applauded the prowess displayed by Arjuna and the son of Vasudeva. course

sn: किमद्भुततमं लोके भविताप्यथवा ह्यभूत्। यदश्वान् पार्थगोविन्दौ मोचयामासतू रणे॥
en: “What incident, more wonderful has ever taken place or will ever take place in this world, then this, viz., that Pritha's son and Govinda in of the fight, have unharnessed their steeds?

sn: भयं विपुलमस्मासु तावधत्तां नरोत्तमौ। तेजो विदधतुश्चोग्रं विस्रब्धौ रणमूर्धनि॥
en: Those two foremost of men, displaying fierce energy in battle and confident of their prowess, have filled our hearts with terrors.
