sn: अथ स्मयन् हृषीकेशः स्त्रीमध्य इव भारत। अर्जुनेन कृते संख्ये शरगर्भगृहे तथा॥ उपावर्तयदव्यग्रस्तानश्वान् पुष्करेक्षणः। मिषतां सर्वसैन्यानां त्वदीयानां विशाम्पते॥
en: Thereafter Hrishikesha of eyes resembling lotus petals, smiling with the greatest assurance as if he were in the midst of women, led the steeds in the arrowy hall created on the field of battle by Arjuna, before the very eyes of all your troops, O king.

sn: तेषां श्रमं च ग्लानिं च वमथु वेपथु व्रणान्। सर्वं व्यपानुदत् कृष्णः कुशलो ह्यश्वकर्मणि॥
en: Then Krishna well-skilled in the art of grooming, removed their fatigue, pain, trembling and lacerations.

sn: शल्यानुद्धृत्य पाणिभ्यां परिमृज्य च तान् हयान्। उपावर्त्य यथान्यायं पाययामास वारि सः॥
en: Drawing the arrows out of their bodies and shampooing them with his two hands and walking them duly, he made them drink water.

sn: सताँल्लब्धोदकान् स्नातान् जग्धान्नान् विगतक्लमान्। योजयामास संहृष्टः पुनरेव रथोत्तमे।॥
en: Having then washed them and made them drink and removing their fatigue and pain, he once more harnessed them to that foremost of chariots, with a joyful heart.

sn: स तं रथवरं शौरिः सर्वशस्रभृतां वरः। सामास्थाय महादेवाः सार्जुनः प्रययौ द्रुतम्॥
en: Thereafter that foremost of all wielders of weapons, that one endued with fierce energy viz., Shauri (Krishna), accompanied by Arjuna, mounted on the car and once more drove on quickly.

sn: रथं रथवरस्याजौ युक्तं लब्धोदकैर्हयैः। दृष्ट्वा कुरुबलश्रेष्ठाः पुनर्विमनसोऽभवन्॥
en: Beholding then that car belonging to that foremost of car-warrior, to which were yoked steeds whose thirst had been quenched, the foremost of the Kuru warriors once more became depressed at heart.

sn: विनिःश्वसन्तस्ते राजन् भग्नदंष्ट्रा इवोरगाः। धिगहो धिग्गतः पार्थः कृष्णश्चेत्यब्रुवन् पृथक्॥
en: O king, beating like snakes whose fangs have been broken, they exclaimed, 'Fie fie on us; Oh, Partha and Krishna, have gone.'

sn: त्वत्सेनाः सर्वतो दृष्ट्वा लोमहर्षणमद्भुतम्। त्वरध्वमिति चाक्रन्दन् नैतदस्तीति चाब्रुवन्॥
en: Your armies excited by seeing that excellent and thrilling experience began to cry on their follows-"Bravo! It cannot be so. Pursue them immediately.

sn: सर्वक्षत्रस्य मिषतो रथेनैकेन दंशितौ। बालः क्रीडनकेनेव कद कृत्य नो बलम्॥ क्रोशतां यतमानानामसंसक्तौ परंतपौ। दर्शयित्वाऽऽत्मनो वीर्यं प्रयातौ सर्वराजसु॥
en: Riding on a single car and clad in mail, slaughtering our troops with as much as ease as boys playing with a toy, even before the very eyes of all the Kshatriyas. In spite of all our efforts and endeavours, those two scorchers of foes, have gone way, disregarding all other kings and displaying their superior prowess."

sn: तौ प्रयातौ पुनदृष्ट्वा तदान्ये सैनिकाब्रुवन्। त्वरध्वं कुरवः सर्वे वधे कृष्णकिरीटिनोः॥
en: Beholding them gone away, other soldiers said-"O Kurus, prepare yourselves in all haste for slaughtering Krishna and the diademdecked Arjuna.

sn: रथयुक्तो हि दाशार्हो मिषतां सर्वधन्विनाम्। ज्यद्रथाय यात्येष कद कृत्य नो रणे॥
en: Yoking the steeds to the car, he of the Dasharha is proceeding toward race Jayadratha, crushing us in battle before the very eyes of all our bow-men."

sn: तत्र केचिन्मिथो राजन् समभाषन्त भूमिपाः। अदृष्टपूर्वं संग्रामे तद दृष्ट्वा महदद्भुतम्॥
en: Other rulers of earth, seeing that highly wonderful incident, never seen before, o king, said among themselves-

sn: सर्वसैन्यानि राजा च धृतराष्ट्रोऽत्ययं गतः। दुर्योधनापराधेन क्षत्रं कृत्स्ना च मेदिनी॥
en: "These troops, the king Dhritarashtra himself, the Kshatriyas and the earth herself, are a'l now involved in a great calamity, through the fault of king Duryodhana.

sn: विलयं समनुप्राप्ता च्च राजा न बुध्यते। इत्येवं क्षत्रियास्तत्र ब्रुवन्त्यन्ये च भारत।॥
en: All these are being destroyed; but the king (Duryodhana) heeds it not." Even thus did the Kshatriyas speak there. Others O Bharata, said

sn: सिन्धुराजस्य यत् कृत्यं गतस्य यमसादनम्। तत् करोतु वृथाष्टिर्धार्तराष्ट्रोऽनुपायवित्॥
en: Let the son of Dhritarashtra, of erring sight and meagre knowledge of measures, now perform those rites that are done for the departed, for, the ruler of the Sindhus may already be taken to be dispatched to the abode of Yama.

sn: ततः शीघ्रतरंप्रायात् पाण्डवः सैन्धवं प्रति। विवर्तमाने तिग्मांशौ हृष्टैः पीतोदकैर्हयैः॥
en: Then as the sun perambulated through the concavity of heaven, that son of Pandu proceeded with increased speed towards the ruler of the Sindhus, being borne by refreshed steeds whose thirst had been quenched.

sn: तं प्रयान्तं महाबाहुं सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वरम्। नाशक्नवन् वारयितुं योधाः क्रुद्धमिवान्तकम्॥
en: Then your warriors were unable to check that mighty-armed hero, that foremost of all wielders of weapons, viz., Arjuna, who had been proceeding like the enraged Destroyer himself.

sn: विद्राव्य तु ततः सैन्यं पाण्डवः शत्रुतापनः। यथा मृगगणान् सिंहः सैन्धवार्थे व्यलोडयत्॥
en: Then for getting at the ruler of the Sindhus, that son of Pandu, that afflicter of foes, routing your army, began to agitate it like a lion agitating a herd of deer.

sn: गाहमानस्त्वनीकानि तूर्णमश्वानचोदयत्। बलाकाभं तु दाशार्हः पाञ्चजन्यं व्यनादयत्।॥
en: Plunging into the ranks of your soldiers, he of the Dasharha race, urged the steeds of to the top their speed and blew his conch Panchajanya of the hue of clouds.

sn: कौन्येनाग्रतः सृष्टा न्यपतन् पृष्ठतः शराः। तूर्णात् तूर्णतरं हाश्वाः प्रावहन् वातरंहसः॥
en: The arrows discharged by the son of Kunti began to fall behind him, so quickly did those steeds, endowed with the fleetness of the wind, bear that chariot of his.

sn: ततो नृतपयः क्रुद्धाः परिवQर्धनंजयम्। क्षत्रिया बहवश्चान्ये जयद्रथवधैषिणम्॥
en: Thereafter, inflamed with rage, numerous hostile kings and various other Kshatriyas, surrounded Dhananjaya who was eager for bringing about the slaughter of Jayadratha.

sn: सैन्येषु विप्रयातेषु धिष्ठितं पुरुषर्षभम्। दुर्योधनोऽन्वयात् पार्थं त्वरमाणो महाहवे॥
en: When the Kuru-combatants thus rushed upon that foremost of men who had stopped for moment only, Duryodhana, advancing quickly, followed Partha from behind, in that fierce encounter.

sn: वातोद्धृतपताकं तं रथं जलदनिःस्वनम्। घोरं कपिध्वजं दृष्ट्वा विषण्णा रथिनोऽभवन्॥
en: Many warriors became greatly depressed, beholding that chariot, of which the banner fluttered in the air, the rattle of which resembled the rumble of clouds and which was mounted with that fearful standard having the ape for its device.

sn: दिवाकरेऽथ रजसा सर्वतः संवृते भृशम्। शरार्ताश्च रणे योधाः शेकुः कृष्णौ न वीक्षितुम्॥
en: Thus when the ord of the day had been enshrouded in a cloud of dust and when the a warriors had been afflicted sore with arrows, they could not look at the two Krishnas engaged in that battle. warriors had been afflicted sore with arrows, they could not look at the two Krishnas engaged in that battle.

sn: संजय उवाच संसन्त इव मज्जानस्तावकानां भयानृप। तौ दृष्ट्वा समतिक्रान्तौ वासुदेवधनंजयौ॥
en: Sanjaya said Beholding, king, Vasudeva and Dhananjaya penetrate into their ranks, having already pierced through many divisions, the kings of yours army fled in fear.

sn: सर्वे तु प्रतिसंरब्धा ह्रीमन्तः सत्त्वचोदिताः। स्थिरीभूता महात्मानः प्रत्यगच्छन् धनंजयम्॥
en: After a while, however, those illustrious warriors, overwhelmed with wrath and shame and urged on by their prowess, gathered courage and rushed upon Dhananjaya.

sn: ये गताः पाण्डवं युद्धे रोषामर्षसमन्विताः। तेऽद्यापि न निवर्तन्ते सिन्धवः सागरादिव॥
en: But, O king, those who proceeded to fight against the son of Pandu, being filled even as rivers falling into the sea, never return.

sn: असन्तस्तु न्यवर्तन्त वेदेभ्य इव नास्तिकाः। नरकं भजमानास्ते प्रत्यपद्यन्त किल्बिषम्॥
en: Like atheists turning away from the Vedas, many ignoble warriors turned away from the fight and thus incurred sin and hell.

sn: तावतीत्य रथानीकं विमुक्तौ पुरुषर्षभौ। ददृशाते यथा राहोरास्यान्मुक्ती प्रभाकरौ॥
en: Then those two foremost of men, passing beyond that cluster of cars, appeared like the two effulgent orbs (the sun and the moon) freed from the jaws of Rahu.

sn: मत्स्याविव महाजालं विदार्य विगतक्लमौ। तथा कृष्णावदृश्येतां सेनाजालं विदार्य तत्॥
en: They then with their fatigue completely dispelled and passing beyond that net-work of soldiers, looked like two fishes that had torn away from a strong net.

sn: विमुक्तौ शस्त्रसम्बाधाद् द्रोणानीकात् सुदुर्भिदात्। अदृश्येतां महात्मानौ कालसूर्याविवोदितौ॥
en: Having passed through that impenetrable array of Drona impassable in consequence of showers of weapons, those two illustrious heroes looked like two suns risen at the period of Dissolution.

sn: अस्त्रसम्बाधनिर्मुक्तौ विमुक्तौ शस्त्रसंकटात्। अदृश्येतां महात्मानौ शत्रुसम्बाधकारिणौ॥
en: Penetrating through those showers of weapons and freed from the imminent danger to their lives, those illustrious warriors, themselves obstructing the sky with their weapons.

sn: विमुक्तौ ज्वलनस्पर्शान्मकरास्याज्झषाविव। अक्षोभयेतां सेनां तौ समुद्रं पकराविव॥
en: Appeared like two persons escaped from a raging fire or like two fish from the jaws of a Makara. They then agitated the Kuru ocean like two Makara agitated the mighty deep.

sn: तावकास्तव पुत्राश्च द्रोणानीकस्थयोस्तयोः। नैतौ तरिष्यतो द्रोणमिति चक्रुस्तदा मतिम्॥
en: While Arjuna and Krishna were within Drona's division, your warriors and your sons, had thought that the two heroes would never be able to pass through it.

sn: तौ तु दृष्ट्वा व्यतिक्रान्तौ द्रोणानीकं महायुती। नाशशंसुर्महाराज सिन्धुराजस्य जीवितम्॥
en: But beholding those two highly effulgent warriors now beyond the division of Drona, they became doubtful about the life of the ruler of the Sindhus.

sn: आशा बलवती राजन् सिन्धुराजस्य जीविते। द्रोणहार्दिक्ययोः कृष्णो न मोक्ष्येते इति प्रभो॥
en: Up till then, they cherished strong hopes of Jayadratha's life, for they had thought, O monarch, that the two Krishnas would never be able to escape from Drona and Hridika's son.

sn: तामाशां विफलीकृत्य संतीर्णौ तौ परंतपौ। द्रोणानीकं महाराज भोजानीकं च दुस्तरम्॥
en: Falsifying that hope of theirs, those two scorchers of foes, succeeded in crossing over the uncrossable division of Drona and the Bhojas, O king.

sn: अथ दृष्ट्वा व्यतिक्रान्तौ ज्वलिताविव पावकौ। निराशाः सिन्धुराजस्य जीवितं न शशंसिरे॥
en: Beholding them beyond those divisions and look like two blazing fires, your troops became despondent and they gave up all hopes for the life of the ruler of the Sindhus.

sn: मिथश्च समभाषेतामभीतौ भयवर्धनां। जयद्रथवधे वाचस्तास्ताः कृष्णधनंजयौ॥
en: Then those two dauntless heroes, those enhancers of the fears of their foes, namely Krishna and Dhananjaya, thus began to talk among themselves, regarding the slaughter of Jayadratha.

sn: असौ मध्ये कृतः षड्भिर्धार्तराष्ट्रमहारथैः। चक्षुर्विषयसम्प्राप्तौ न मे मोक्ष्यति सैन्धवः॥
en: “This ruler of the Sindhus has been placed in their midst by six of the foremost carwarriors of Dhritarashtra's army. Still he shall not escape, if we can only have a look of him.

sn: यद्यस्य समरे गोप्ता शक्रो देवगणैः सह। तथाप्येनं निहंस्याव इति कृष्णावभाषताम्॥
en: Even if Indra himself with all the celestials, were to become his protector in battle, yet we shall slay him.” Sanjaya said-Thus did the two Krishna's talk to themselves.

sn: इति कृष्णौ महाबाहू मिथोऽकथयतां तदा। सिन्धुराजमवेक्षन्तौ त्वत्पुत्रा बहु चुकुशुः॥
en: Even so, O mighty-armed one, did the two Krishna's speak amongst themselves while looking for the ruler of the Sindhus. (Hearing what they said) your sons set up a loud wail.

sn: अतीत्य मरुधन्वानं प्रयान्तौ तृषितौ गजौ। पीत्वा वारि समाश्वस्तौ तथैवास्तामरिंदमौ॥
en: Those two subduers of foes then appeared like a pair of elephants of great quickness, whose thirst had been slaked and who had been refreshed with the drinking water, after they had passed through a desert.

sn: व्याघ्रसिंहगजाकीर्णानतिक्रम्य च पर्वतान्। वणिजाविव दृश्येतां हीनमृत्यू जरातिगौ॥
en: Beyond death and above the reach of decay, they then appeared like two tradesmen that have passed over a hilly district infested with tigers, lions and elephants.

sn: तथा हि मुखवर्णोऽयमनयोरिति मेनिरे। तावका वीक्ष्य मुक्तौतौ विक्राशन्ति स्म सर्वशः॥
en: Indeed then your troops considered the hue of their countenances to be incapable of being faded; and beholding them freed, they began to wail aloud.

sn: द्रोणादाशीविषाकाराज्ज्वलितादिव पावकात्। अन्येभ्यः पार्थिवेभ्यश्च भास्वन्ताविव भास्करौ॥
en: Escaping from Drona who resembled a snake of virulent poison or a blazing fire, as also from the other rulers of Earth, Partha and Krishna looked like two burning suns.

sn: विमुक्तौ सागरप्रख्याद् द्रोणानीकादरिंदमौ। अदृश्येतां भुदा युक्तौ समुत्तीर्यार्णवं यथा॥
en: Those two subduers of foes, escaping from Drona's division which resembled the very ocean, seemed to be filled with delight, like persons that have safely crossed the mighty main.

sn: अस्त्रौघान्महतो मुक्तौ द्रोणहार्दिक्यरक्षितात्। राच्मानावदृश्येतामिन्द्राग्न्योः सदृशौ रणे॥
en: Escaping from those thick down-pours of arrows, from those divisions protected by Drona and Hridika's son, Keshava and Arjuna appeared like Indra and Agni of burning radiance.

sn: उद्भिनरुधिरौ कृष्णौ भारद्वाजस्य सायकैः। शितैश्चितौ व्यरोचेतां कर्णिकारैरिवाचलौ॥
en: Pierced with the whetted shafts of Bharadvaja's son and profusely shedding blood, the two Krishnas appeared beautiful, like two mountains adorned with flowering Karnikara trees.

sn: द्रोणग्राहह्रदान्मुक्तौ शक्त्याशीविषसंकटात्। अयःशरोग्रमकरात् क्षत्रियप्रवराम्भसः॥
en: Having passed through that expensive lake, of which Drona formed the shark, darts the fierce snakes, shafts the Makaras and Kshatriyas the fathomless waters.

sn: ज्याघोषतलनिर्हादाद् गदानिस्त्रिंशविद्युतः। द्रोणास्त्रमेघानिर्मुक्तौ सूर्येन्दू तिमिरादिव॥
en: Having emerged out of that cloud formed by Drona's weapons, of which the thunders were the twang of bows and the sound of palmstrokes and the lightning the flashing maces and swords-Partha and Krishna appeared like the sun and the moon emerging out of darkness.

sn: बाहुभ्यामिव संती# सिन्धुषष्ठाः समुद्रगाः। तपान्ते सरितः पूर्णा महाग्राहसमाकुलाः॥
en: In consequence of their crossing the regions obstructed with the weapons of Drona, all creatures regarded those fierce and renowned bowmen viz., Keshava and Dhananjaya to be like two persons who have the strength of their arms, the five rivers having the ocean for their sixth when full of waters during the rainy season and abounding in numerous sharks and alligators.

sn: इति कृष्णौ महेष्वासौ प्रशस्तौ लोकविश्रुतौ। सर्वभूतान्यमन्यनत द्रोणास्त्रबलवारणात्॥
en: All human beings began to assume Sri Krishna and Arjuna, great archer, meritorious and renowned world-wide as they had effaced the destructive power of the weapon shot by Dronacarya.

sn: जयद्रथं समीपस्थमवेक्षन्तौ जिघांसया। रुरुं निपाने लिप्सन्तौ व्याघ्राविव व्यतिष्ठताम्॥
en: From a desire for slaughtering Jayadratha stationed very near to them, looking at him, the two warriors appear like two tigers waiting to fall upon a Ruru deer.

sn: यथा हि मुखवर्णोऽयमनयोरिति मेनिरे। तव योधा महाराज हतमेव जयद्रथम्॥
en: The colour of their faces was such that your warriors, o mighty monarch, considered Jayadratha already to be one among the slain.

sn: लोहिताक्षौ महाबाहू संयुक्तौ कृष्णपाण्डवौ। सिन्धुराजमभिप्रेक्ष्य हृष्टौ व्यनदतां मुहुः॥
en: O mighty-armed one, with red eyes and staying together, the son of Pandu and Krishna then beholding the ruler of the Sindhus, became filled with delight and incessantly uttered loud war-cries.

sn: शौरेरभीषुहस्तस्य पार्थस्य च धनुष्मतः। तयोरासीत् प्रभा राजन् सूर्यपावकयोरिव॥
en: The radiance of Shauri holding the reins and Partha wielding the bow, O king, was like that of the fire and the sun.

sn: हर्ष एव तयोरासीद् द्रोणानीकप्रमुक्तयोः। समीपे सैन्धवं दृष्ट्वा श्येनयोरामिषं यथा।॥
en: Escaping from the division of Drona and beholding the ruler of the Sindhus within reach, they were filled with delight, even as a hawk is filled with delight at the sight of a piece of meat.

sn: तौ तु सैन्धवमालोक्य वर्तमानमिवान्तिके। सहसा पेततुः क्रुद्धौ क्षिप्रं श्येनाविवामिषम्॥
en: Beholding the ruler of the Sindhus stay near them and burning with rage, they pounced down upon him, like a pair of hawks pouncing down upon a piece of meat.

sn: तौ दृष्ट्वा तु व्यतिक्रान्तौ हृषीकेशधनंजयौ। सिन्धुराजस्य रक्षार्थं पराक्रान्तः सुतस्तव॥ द्रोणेनाबद्धकवचो राजा दुर्योधनस्ततः। ययावेकरथेनाजौ हयसंस्कारवित् प्रभो॥
en: Then beholding Hrishikesha and Dhananjaya penetrate through the division of Drona, your highly powerful, son, king Duryodhana, having his armour donned by Drona and knowing how to guide and groom horses, proceeded on a single car against those two warriors, in order to rescue the ruler of the Sindhus.

sn: कृष्णपार्थो महेष्वासौ व्यतिक्रम्याथ ते अग्रतः पुण्डरीकाक्षं प्रतीयाय नराधिप॥
en: Leaving behind him the two mighty carwarriors Krishna and Partha, your son proceeded ahead and then turned back, p king, facing Keshava of lotus-like eyes.

sn: ततः सर्वेषु सैन्येषु वादित्राणि प्रहृष्टवत्। प्रावाद्यन्त व्यतिक्रान्ते तव पुत्रे धनंजयम्॥ सुतः।
en: Then when your son had outrun Dhananjaya, numerous musical instruments were joyfully sounded by all your troops.

sn: सिंहनादरवाश्चासशङ्खशब्दविमिश्रिताः। दृष्ट्वा दुर्योधनं तत्र कृष्णयोः प्रमुखे स्थितम्॥
en: Then beholding Duryodhana stay, facing the two Krishna's, your troops uttered warcries resembling leonine roars that became mingled with the blare of conchs.

sn: ये च ते सिन्धुराजस्य गोप्तारः पावकोपमाः। ते प्राहृष्यन्त समरे दृष्ट्वा पुत्रं तव प्रभो॥
en: Beholding your son rush to fight, they also of blazing effulgence who were engaged in protecting Jayadratha, became filled with joy.

sn: दृष्ट्वा दुर्योधनं कृष्णो व्यतिक्रान्तं सहानुगम्। अब्रवीदर्जुनं राजन् प्राप्तकालमिदं वचः॥
en: Then seeing Duryodhana and his followers outrun Dhananjaya, Krishna, O king addressing Arjuna, said these words suited to the occasion.

sn: वासुदेव उवाच दुर्योधनमतिक्रान्तमेतं पश्य धनंजय। अत्यद्भुतमिमं मन्ये नास्त्यस्य सदृशो रथः॥
en: Vasudeva said O Dhananjaya, behold, Suyodhana has outrun Meseems this to be highly wonderful. There is indeed no car-warrior equal to him.

sn: दूरपाती महेष्वासः कृतास्त्रो युद्धदुर्मदः। दृढास्त्रश्चित्रयोधी च धार्तराष्ट्रो महाबलः॥
en: He is capable of shooting his arrows to a great distance; he is a fierce bowman, accomplished in the use of all weapon and formidable in battle. This son of Dhritarashtra is endued with great prowess and strikes hard and is versed in all modes of warfare.

sn: अत्यन्तसुखसंवृद्धो मानितश्च महारथः। कृती च सततं पार्थ नित्यं द्वेष्टि च बान्धवान्॥
en: Reared in all luxury, he is highly esteemed by all the mighty car-warriors. O Partha, he is accomplished and the constant hater of the Pandavas.

sn: तेन युद्धमहं मन्ये प्राप्तकालं तवानघ। अत्र वो द्यूतमायत्तं विजयायेतराय वा॥
en: O sinless one, for these reasons I think that the time had now arrived, when you shall fight with him. Upon him rests, as upon a stake at dice, victory or the reverse.

sn: अत्र क्रोधविषं पार्थ विमुञ्च चिरसम्भृतम्। एष मूलमनर्थानां पाण्डवानां महारथः॥
en: On him vomit the venom of your wrath that you have cherished so long, O Partha. This mighty car-warrior is the root of all wrongs inflicted on the Pandavas.

sn: सोऽयं प्राप्तस्तवाक्षेपं पश्य साफल्यमात्मनः। कथं हि राजा राज्यार्थी त्वया गच्छेत संयुगम्॥६
en: He is not within your arrow-shot. Be mindful of your success. Why has king Duryodhana, desirous as he is of enjoying the kingdom come to fight with you?

sn: दिष्ट्या त्विदानी सम्प्राप्त एष ते बाणगोचरम्। यथायं जीवितं जह्यात् तथा कुरु धनंजय॥
en: By good fortune it is that he has now come within the reach arrows, 0 Dhananjaya, do you so strive now, that this one may lose his very life in battle.

sn: ऐश्वर्यमदसम्मूढो नैष दुःखमुपेयिवान्। न च ते संयुगे वीर्ये जानाति पुरुषर्षभ॥
en: Elated with the pride engendered by his prosperity, he has never experienced pain. O foremost of men, he knows your prowess in battle.

sn: त्वां हि लोकास्त्रयः पार्थ ससुरासुरमानुषाः। नोत्सहन्ते रणे जेतुं किमुतैकः सुयोधनः॥
en: O Partha, the three worlds and the celestials, the Asuras and the men, cannot bear you in battle, what to speak of this singlehanded Suyodhana? of your

sn: स दिष्ट्या समनुप्राप्तस्तव पार्थ रथान्तिकम्। जह्येनं त्वं महाबाहो यथा वृत्रं पुरंदरः॥
en: By good luck, has he now come near your chariot; O Partha, slay him, O mighty-armed hero, even as Purandara (Indra) slew Vritra (in days gone by).

sn: एष ह्यनर्थे सततं पराक्रान्तस्तवानघ। निकृत्या धर्मराजं च द्यूते वञ्चितवानयम्॥
en: O sinless one, this Duryodhana ever tried to bring down distress on you. Through deceitful measures, he defeated the very virtuous king Yudhishthira at the game of dice.

sn: बहूनि सुनृशंसानि कृतान्येतेन मानद। युष्मासु पापमतिना अपापेष्वेव नित्यदा॥
en: O bestower of honour, sinless though you all are, this one of sinful understanding had always injured you with many cruel wrongs.

sn: तमनार्यं सदा क्रुद्धं पुरुषं कामचारिणम्। आर्यां युद्धे मतिं कृत्वा जहि पार्थाविचारयन्॥
en: Nobly resolving to fight, O you son of Pritha, slay without any hesitation, this perverse wretch who is ever vindictive and cruel and who is avarice incarnate.

sn: निकृत्या राज्यहरणं वनवासं च पाण्डव। परिक्लेशं च कृष्णाया हदि कृत्वा पराक्रमम्॥
en: O son of Pandu, put forth all your prowess, recollecting the despoliation of your kingdom through deceit, your exile in the woods and the woes of Krishna.

sn: दिष्ट्यैष तव बाणानां गोचरे परिवर्तते। प्रतिघाताय कार्यस्य दिष्ट्या च यततेऽग्रतः॥
en: Through good fortune it is, that he now move within the range of your arrows. By good luck it is that, staying before you, he is striving to thwart you in the fulfilment of your purposes.

sn: दिष्ट्या जानाति संग्रामे योद्धव्यं हि त्वया सह। दिष्ट्या च सफलाः पार्थसर्वे कामा ह्यकामिताः॥
en: By good luck it is that he has come to know that he will have to fight with you! By good luck it is that all your desires, though not at present eagerly cherished, will meet with their fruition, O Pritha's son.

sn: तस्माज्जहि रणे पार्थ धार्तराष्ट्र कुलाधमम्। यथेन्द्रेण हतः पूर्वे जम्भो देवासुरे मृधे॥
en: For these reasons, O Partha, slay you this disgrace to the race of Dhritarashtra, even as Indra slew the Asura Jambha in days gone by, in the battle between the celestials and the Asuras.

sn: अस्मिन् हते त्वया सैन्यमनाथं भिद्यतामिदम्। वैरस्यास्यास्त्ववभृथो मूलं छिन्धि दुरात्मनाम्॥
en: If this one be slain by you, you can penetrate through this array that will be then masterless. Let the Avabhritha of these hostilities be performed now, cut the root of these wretches of wicked souls.

sn: संजय उवाच तं तथेत्यब्रवीत् पार्थः कृत्यरूपमिदं मम। सर्वमन्यदनात्य गच्छ यत्र सुयोधनः॥
en: Sanjaya said Thus spoken to, Pritha's son answered him saying-"Let it be so. Even this will I do. Unmindful of anything else, drive where Duryodhana stands.

sn: येनैतद् दीर्घकालं नो भुक्तं राज्यमकण्टकम्। अप्यस्य युधि विक्रम्य छिन्द्यां मूर्धानमाहवे॥
en: Putting forth all my prowess in battle, I will in this day's battle, cut-off the head of this wretch, who had enjoyed our dominions for a long period, without a single thorn in his side.

sn: अपि तस्य शनायाः परिक्लेशस्य माधव। कृष्णायाः शकुयां गन्तुं पदं केशप्रधर्षणे॥
en: O Keshava, shall I not be successful in avenging the wrongs inflicted on Draupadi by her being dragged by the hair, undeserving as she was of such treatment?

sn: इत्येवंवादिनौ कृष्णौ हृष्टौ श्वेतान् हयोत्तमान्। प्रेषयामासतुः संख्ये प्रेप्सन्तौ तं नराधिपम्॥
en: Thus speaking to each other and filled with delight, the two Krishnas urged on their steeds of white hue and best breed, with a view to get at the ruler of the Kurus viz., king Duryodhana.

sn: त्योः समीपं सम्प्राप्य पुत्रस्ते भरतर्षभ। न चकार भयं प्राप्ते भये महति मारिष॥
en: fear, Your son, O foremost of the Bharatas, approaching them entertained no although, O sire, there were reasons enough to fill him with terror.

sn: तदस्य क्षत्रियास्तत्र सर्व एवाभ्यपूजयन्। यदर्जुनहषीकेशौ प्रत्युद्यातौ न्यवारयत्॥
en: Then all the Kshatriyas present there applauded him, inasmuch as he ventured to rush against Arjuna and Hrishikesha with a view to oppose them.

sn: ततः सर्वस्य सैन्यस्य तावकस्य विशाम्पते। महानादो ह्यभूत् तत्र दृष्ट्वा राजानमाहवे॥
en: Then beholding the king proceed to the battle, all your troops, O ruler of men, raised a loud uproar.

sn: तस्मिञ्जनसमुन्नादे प्रवृत्ते भैरवे सति। कदर्थीकृत्य ते पुत्रः प्रत्यमित्रमवारयत्॥
en: When that loud and dreadful uproar was set up by your people, your son pressing his foe hard, began to impede his progress.

sn: आवारितस्तु कौन्तेयस्तव पुत्रेण घन्विना। संरम्भमगमद् भूयः स च तस्मिन् परंतपः॥
en: Opposed by that illustrious bowmen viz., your son, the son of Kunti became excited to the highest pitch of fury; also that afflicter of foes, your son, became highly angry upon Dhananjaya.

sn: तौ दृष्ट्वा प्रतिसंरब्धौ दुर्योधनधनंजयौ। अभ्यवैक्षन्त राजानो भीमरूपाः समन्ततः॥
en: Then beholding Duryodhana and Dhananjaya, both enraged against each other, all the royal warriors of fierce appearance, began to look at them from all sides.

sn: दृष्ट्वा तु पार्थे संरब्धं वासुदेवं च मारिष। प्रसन्नेव पुत्रस्ते योद्धुकामः समाह्वयत्॥
en: Beholding Partha and Vasudeva both filled with wrath, your son desirous of fighting with them, smiling, challenged them to the combat.

sn: ततः प्रहष्टो दाशार्हः पाण्डवश्च धनंजयः। व्यक्रोशेतां महानादं दध्यतुश्चाम्बुजोत्तमौ॥
en: Thereupon he of the Dasharha race and Dhananjaya the son of Pandu filled with delight, uttered loud shouts and blew their best of conchs.

sn: तौ हृष्टरूपौ सम्प्रेक्ष्य कौरवेयास्तु सर्वशः। निराशाः समपद्यन्त पुत्रस्य तव जीविते॥
en: The Kaurava warriors then beholding their appearance reflect joy, became hopeless of the life of your son.

sn: शोकमायुः परे चैव कुरुः सर्व एव ते। अमन्यन्त च पुत्रं ते वैश्वानरमुखे हुतम्॥
en: Then many among the enemies and the Kurus were filled with grief, as they then considered your son to be like a libation poured into the mouth of fire.

sn: तथा तु दृष्ट्वा योधास्ते प्रहृष्टौ कृष्णपाण्डवौ। हतो राजा हतो राजेत्यूचिरे च भयार्दिताः॥
en: Then your warriors beholding Krishna and Pandu's son filled with joy, out of fear, began to exclaim saying "the king is slain, the king is slain."

sn: जनस्य संनिनादं तु श्रुत्वा दुर्योधनोऽब्रवीत्। व्येतु वो भीरहं कृष्णौ प्रेषयिष्यामि मृत्यवे॥
en: But Duryodhana, hearing that confusion created by his own men, said-"Let all your apprehensions be dispelled; I will send the two Krishnas to the abode of Death"

sn: इत्युक्त्वा सैनिकान् सर्वाञ्जयापेक्षी नराधिपः। पार्थमाभाष्य संरम्भादिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: Having thus spoken to the soldiers, the king desirous of victory, addressing Pritha's son, out of anger, said these wordsपार्थ यच्छिक्षितं तेऽस्त्रं दिव्यं पार्थिवमेव च।

sn: तद् दर्शय मयि क्षिप्रं यदि जातोऽसि पाण्डुना॥
en: 'O son of Pritha, if you are begotten by Pandu, then quickly display against me all weapons the use of which you learned from the celestials or on this Earth?

sn: यद् बलं तव वीर्यं च केशवस्य तथैव च। तत् कुरुष्व मयि क्षिप्रं पश्यामस्तव पौरुषम्॥
en: Exert all your might and prowess and let also Keshava do so, against me. I want to see your manliness.

sn: अस्मत्परोक्षं कर्माणि कृतानि प्रवहन्ति ते। स्वामिसत्कारयुक्तानि यानि तानीह दर्शय॥
en: Men speak of many feats achieved by you out of our view. Show all those feats to me that have rendered you worthy of the applause and reverence of others."

sn: अस्मत्परोक्षं कर्माणि कृतानि प्रवहन्ति ते। स्वामिसत्कारयुक्तानि यानि तानीह दर्शय॥
en: Men speak of many feats achieved by you out of our view. Show all those feats to me that have rendered you worthy of the applause and reverence of others."

sn: संजय उवाच एवमुक्त्वार्जुनं राजा त्रिभिर्मर्मातिगैः शरैः। अभ्यविध्यन्महावेगैश्चतुर्भिश्चतुरो हयान्॥
en: Sanjaya said Having thus spoken, the king pierced Arjuna with three shafts capable of penetrating to the very vitals; and then with another four arrows of great velocity, he pierced the latter's four steeds.

sn: वासुदेवं च दशभिः प्रत्यविध्यत् स्तनान्तरे। प्रतोदं चास्य भल्लेन छित्त्वा भूमावपातयत्॥
en: He also pierced the son of Vasudeva with ten arrows between his breasts. The cutting off the whip of the latter, he felled it on the ground.

sn: तं चतुर्दशभिः पार्थश्चित्रपुजैः शिलाशितैः। अविध्यत् तूर्णमव्यग्रस्ते चाभ्रश्यन्त वर्मणि॥
en: Thereupon with perfect coolness, Pritha's son quickly sped at him four shafts of variegated wings and whetted on stone; but all these shafts were baffled by Duryodhana's armour.

sn: तेषां नैष्फल्यमालोक्य पुनर्नव च पञ्च च। प्राहिणोनिशितान् बाणांस्ते चाभ्रश्यन्त वर्मणः॥
en: Beholding those shafts repelled, Partha once more struck Duryodhana with another nine and seven arrows of exceeding sharpness; but these also became baffled by Duryodhana's armour,

sn: अष्टाविंशांस्तु तान् बाणानस्तान् विप्रेक्ष्य निष्फलान्। अब्रवीत् परवीरनः कृष्णोऽर्जुनमिदं वचः॥
en: Then seeing those twenty shafts of Arjuna repelled, that slayer of hostile warriors Krishna,

sn: अदृष्टपूर्वं पश्यामि शिलानामिव सर्पणम्। त्वया सम्प्रेषिताः पार्थ नार्थं कुर्वन्ति पत्रिणः॥
en: O Partha, now I see a sight never before seen by me, which is as wonderful as the moving about of hills. Winged shafts shot by yourself, are becoming abortive!

sn: कच्चिद् गाण्डीवजः प्राणस्तथैव भरतर्षभ। मुष्टिश्च ते यथापूर्वं भुजयोश्च बलं तव॥
en: Is everything right with the toughness of the Gandiva, O foremost of the Bharatas? Are your grasp and the prowess of arms, as firm and strong as before?

sn: न वा कच्चिदयं कालः प्राप्तः स्यादद्य पश्चिमः। तव चैवास्य शत्रौश्च तन्ममाचक्ष्व पृच्छतः॥
en: Is not this to be the last time that you shall meet with Duryodhana your foe? Tell me all this; O son of Pritha, for I ask you.

sn: विस्मयो मे महान् पार्थ तव दृष्ट्वा शरानिमान्। व्यर्थान् निपतितान् संख्ये दुर्योधनरर्थ प्रति॥
en: Seeing all these shafts of yours falling upon Duryodhana's chariots without producing the least effect, o Partha, I have been filled with great surprise.

sn: वज्राशनिसमा घोराः परकायावभेदिनः। शराः कुर्वन्ति ते नार्थं पार्थ काऽद्य विडम्बना॥
en: O son of Pritha what misfortune is this that your arrows, dreadful like the bolt of Heaven and capable of piercing through the body of the enemy, produce no effect today?

sn: अर्जुन उवाच द्रोणेनैषा मतिः कृष्ण धार्तराष्ट्र निवेशिता। अभेद्या हि मास्त्राणामेषा कवचधारणा॥
en: । Arjuna said I think, O Krishna, that Drona has donned this armour on Duryodhana. This armour, tied as it has been, in invulnerable by my weapons.

sn: अस्मिन्नन्तर्हितं कृष्ण त्रैलोक्यमपि वर्मणि। एको द्रोणो हि वैदेतदहं तस्माच्च सत्तमात्॥
en: O Krishna, this armour contains in it the mighty of the three worlds. Drona only knows the mode of donning it and from that foremost of men, I also have learnt it.

sn: न शक्यमेतत् कवचं बाणैर्भेत्तुं कथंचन। अपि वज्रेण गोविन्द स्वयं मघवता युधि॥
en: This armour cannot be penetrated by arrows. Even, O Govinda, Maghavat himself cannot penetrate it in battle with his thunderbolt.

sn: आनंस्त्वमपि वै कृष्ण मां विमोहयसे कथम्। यद् वृत्तं त्रिषु लोकेषु यच्च केशव वर्तते॥
en: Knowing all this, O Krishna, why do you confound me. That which happened in the three world, that which now happens.

sn: तथा भविष्यद् यच्चैव तत् सर्वं विदितं तव। न त्विदं वेद वै कश्चिद् यथा त्वं मधुसूदन॥
en: And that which will happen in the future, are all known to yourself. Indeed O slayer of Madhu, no one knows this better than yourself.

sn: एष दुर्योधनः कृष्ण द्रोणेन विहितामिमाम्। तिष्ठत्यभीतवत् संख्ये बिभ्रत् कवचधारणाम्॥
en: This Duryodhana, O Krishna, accoutered in this armour by Drona, is standing dauntlessly in battle, cased in this coat of mail.

sn: यत्त्वत्र विहितं कार्ये नैष तद् वेत्ति माधव। स्त्रीवदेष बिभ]तां युक्तां कवचधारणाम्॥
en: But he knows not what is to be done with this armour, O Madhava, but wears this coat of mail even like a woman.

sn: पश्य बाह्वोश्च मे वीर्यं धनुषश्च जनार्दन। पराजयिष्ये कौरव्यं कवचेनापि रक्षितम्॥
en: Behold, O Janardana, the prowess of my arms and the strength of my bow, in as much as I will vanquish the Kuru king, protected though he is with this coat of mail.

sn: इदमङ्गिरसे प्रादाद् देवेशो वर्म भास्वरम्। तस्माद् बृहस्पतिः प्राप ततः प्राप पुरंदरः॥
en: The lord of the celestials gave this effulgent armour to Angiras; from him Brihaspati obtained it; and from him again Purandara got it.

sn: पुनर्ददौ सुरपतिर्मह्यं वर्म ससंग्रहम्। दैवं यद्यस्य वर्मैतद् ब्रह्मणा वा स्वयं कृतम्॥ नैनं गोप्स्यति दुर्बुद्धिमद्य बाणहतं मया।
en: The lord of the celestials once more presented it to me with mantras to be uttered in donning it. Even if this armour were of celestial make or were forged by Brahma himself, yet it will not protect this wickedminded wretch from the stroke of my arrows.

sn: संजय उवाच एवमुक्त्वार्जुनो बाणमभिमन्त्र्य व्यकर्षयत्॥ मानवास्त्रेण मानार्हस्तीक्ष्णावरणभेदिना!
en: Sanjaya said Having thus spoken, Arjuna inspired some shafts with mantras and then began to draw them on the bow-string.

sn: विकृष्यमाणांस्तेनैव धनुर्मध्यगताञ्छरान्॥ तानस्यास्त्रेण चिच्छेद द्रौणिः सर्वास्त्रघातिना।
en: But while he was thus drawing those arrows placed on the centre of his bow-string, the son of Drona cut them off with a weapon capable of baffling all other weapons.

sn: तान् निकृत्तानिषून् दृष्ट्वा दूरतो ब्रह्मवादिना॥ न्यवेदयत् केशवाय विस्मितः श्वेतवाहनः।
en: Beholding those shafts severed from a distance by that reciter of the Vedas (Ashvatthaman) the owner of the creamcoloured steeds (Arjuna), filled with surprise, addressing Keshava thus spoke

sn: नैतदस्त्रं मया शक्यं द्विः प्रयोक्तुं जनार्दन॥ अस्त्रं मामेव हन्याद्धि हन्याच्चापि बलं मम।
en: 0 Janardana! these arrows I cannot use twice; then they will slay me and my own troops.

sn: ततो दुर्योधनः कृष्णौ नवभिनवभिः शरैः॥ अविध्यत रणे राजञ्छरैराशीविषोपमैः।
en: O king, thereafter king Duryodhana, pierced the two Krishnas, each with none shafts. Resembling snakes of virulent poison.

sn: भूय एवाभ्यवर्षच्च समरे कृष्णपाण्डवौ॥ शरवर्षेण महता ततोऽहष्यन्त तावकाः। चक्रुर्वादिनिनदान् सिंहनादरवांस्तथा॥
en: Once more he poured upon Krishna and the son of Pandu in that battle a mighty shower of arrows; upon this all your troops became filled with joy and they struck up musical instruments and uttered their war-cries.

sn: ततः क्रुद्धो रणे पार्थः सृक्किणी परिसंलिहन्। नापश्यच्च ततोऽस्याङ्गं यन्न स्याद् वर्मरक्षितम्॥
en: Thereat filled with fury, Pritha's son began to lick the corners of his mouth. He could then find no part of Duryodhana's body that was not covered by that armour.

sn: ततोऽस्य निशितैर्बाणैः सुमुक्तैरन्तकोपमैः। हयांश्चकार निर्देहानुभौ च पार्णिसारथी॥
en: Then with sharp arrows, resembling Death and duly discharged, Arjuna cut to pieces Duryodhana's horses and his two Parshni. drivers.

sn: धनुरुयाच्छिनत् तूर्णं हस्तावापं च वीर्यवान्। रथं च शकलीकर्तुं सव्यसाची प्रचक्रमे।॥
en: Then that highly powerful hero cut-off the latter's bow and the leathern gloves quickly. Savyasachin then began to cut his car into fragments.

sn: दुर्योधनं च बाणाभ्यां तीक्ष्णाभ्यां विरथीकृतम्। आविध्यद्धस्ततलयोरुभ्योरर्जुनस्तदा॥
en: Thereafter Arjuna pierced with two sharp arrows, the two palms of Duryodhana who had been deprived of the use of his car.

sn: प्रयत्नज्ञो हि कौन्तेयो नखमांसान्तरेषुभिः। स वेदनाभिराविग्नः पलायनपरायणः॥
en: Then your warriors, beholding Duryodhana that foremost of bowmen, involved in great danger and afflicted with the arrows of Dhananjaya, rushed to his rescue.

sn: तं कृच्छ्रामापदं प्राप्तं दृष्ट्वा परमधन्विनः। समापेतुः परीप्सन्तो धनंजयशरादितम्॥
en: Then they surrounded Dhananjaya with thousands of duly equipped chariots and elephants and horses and numerous divisions of infantry, all inspired with wrath.

sn: तं रथैर्बहुसाहस्रैः कल्पितैः कुञ्जरैर्हयैः। पदात्योपैश्च संरब्धैः परिबर्धनंजयम्॥
en: Thereupon, neither Govinda nor Arjuna nor their car could be seen; for they were then covered with thick showers of weapons and surrounded with large bodies of troops.

sn: अथ नार्जुनगोविन्दौ न रथो वा व्यदृश्यता अस्त्रवर्षेण महता जनौधैश्चापि संवृतौ॥
en: Arjuna, Sri Krishna and their chariot all had become invisible due to a dense cover from all sides of arrows and the crowd of soldiers.

sn: ततोऽर्जुनोऽस्त्रवीर्येण निजघ्ने तां वरूथिनीम्। तत्र व्यङ्गीकृताः पेतुः शतशोऽथ रथद्विपाः॥
en: Then with the force of his weapons, Arjuna began to slaughter that host of your carwarriors and elephants, by hundreds. With their limbs cut-off, they began to fall fast on the field of battle.

sn: ते हता हन्यमानाश्च न्यगृहंस्तं रथोत्तमम्। स रथस्तम्भितस्तस्थौ क्रोशमात्रे समन्ततः॥
en: Slain or in the act of being stain, they succeeded not in reaching that excellent car of Arjuna, which stood immovable full two miles away from the besieging troops on all sides.

sn: ततोऽर्जुनं वृष्णिवीरस्त्वरितो वाक्यमब्रवीत्। धनुर्विस्फारयात्यर्थमहं ध्यास्यामि चाम्बुजम्॥
en: Thereafter, the Vrishni Vrishni hero quickly addressed Arjuna saying "Do you tremendously stretch your bow for I will blow this conch of mine.

sn: ततो विस्फार्य बलवद् गाण्डीवं जनिवान् रिपून्। महता शरवर्षेण तलशब्देन चार्जुनः॥
en: Then stretching his toughest bow Gandiva, Arjuna went on slaughtering his foes, shooting arrowy showers and producing loud din with his palm-strokes.

sn: पाञ्चजन्यं च बलवान् दध्मौ तारेण केशवः। रजसा ध्वस्तपक्ष्मान्तः प्रस्विन्नवदनो भृशम्॥
en: Then the mighty Keshava loudly blew his conch Panchajanya, with his eye lashes covered with dust and countenance shedding drops of perspiration.

sn: तस्य शङ्खस्य नादेन धनुषो निःस्वनेन च। निःसत्त्वाश्च ससत्त्वाश्च क्षितौ पेतुस्तदा जनाः॥
en: In consequence of that twang of the Gandiva and the blast of that conch, all the Kuru-people, strong or weak, fell down on the Earth.

sn: तैर्विमुक्तो रथो रेजे वाय्वीरित इवाम्बुदः। जयद्रथस्य गोप्तारस्ततः क्षुब्धाः सहानुगाः॥
en: The chariot of Arjuna, thus freed from that press, looked like a cloud driven a head by the wind. Then the protectors of Jayadratha and their followers, beholding Arjuna became filled rage.

sn: ते दृष्ट्वा सहसा पार्थे गोप्तारः सैन्धवस्य तु। चक्रुर्नादान् महेष्वासाः कम्पयन्तो वसुंधराम्॥
en: Then suddenly seeing Partha before them, those guards of Jayadratha the Sindnu-king, all mighty bowmen, uttered a fierce shout, causing the earth to tremble therewith.

sn: बाणशब्दरवांश्चोग्रान् विमिश्राशङ्खनिःस्वनैः। प्रादुश्चक्रुर्महात्मानः सिंहनादरवानपि॥
en: The fierce whizz of arrows became mingled with the blast of conchs and other loud noises; the illustrious soldiers your army then also uttered their war-cries resembling leonine roars.

sn: तं श्रुत्वा निनदं घोरं तावकानां समुत्थितम्। प्रदध्मतुः शङ्खवरौ वासुदेवधनंजयौ॥
en: Hearing that dreadful din raised by your troops, Dhananjaya and the son of Vasudeva blew their two best of conchs.

sn: तेन शब्देन महता पूरितेयं वसुंधरा। सशैला सार्णवद्वीपा सपाताला विशाम्पते॥
en: Then, O ruler of men, with that loud sound, the earth seemed to be filled, with its mountains, seas, islands and the subterranean regions.

sn: स शब्दो भरतश्रेष्ठ व्याप्य सर्वा दिशो दश। प्रतिसस्वान तत्रैव कुरुपाण्डवयोर्बले॥
en: Indeed, O foremost of the Bharatas, that sound filling the ten points of the compass, reverberated through the armies of the Kuru and the Pandavas.

sn: तावका रथिनस्तत्र दृष्ट्वा कृष्णधनंजयौ सम्भ्रमं परमं प्राप्तास्त्वरमाणा महारथाः॥
en: Warriors of your host then, beholding Krishna and Dhananjaya, were very much terrified. Soon however those mighty carwarriors recovered and put forth their activity and prowess.

sn: अथ कृष्णौ महाभागौ तावका वीक्ष्य दंशितौ। अभ्यद्रवन्त संक्रुद्धास्तदद्भुतमिवाभवत्॥
en: Then your warriors beholding the two Krishnas cased in mair became excited with rage; and they rushed upon them both. All this looked wonderful.

sn: संजय उवाच तावका हि समीक्ष्यैवं वृष्ण्यन्धककुरूत्तमौ। प्रागत्वरञ्जिघांसन्तस्तथैव विजयः परान्॥
en: Sanjaya said Your warriors, as soon as they saw those two foremost heroes of the Vrishni-Andhaka and the Kuru races, quickly advanced against them, each striving to be the first. So also, Vijaya rushed against those foe of his.

sn: सुवर्णचित्रैर्वैयाप्रैः स्वनवद्भिर्महारथैः। दीपयन्तो दिशः सर्वा ज्वलद्भिरिव पावकैः॥
en: Mounted on their huge chariots adorned with gold, covered with tiger-skins, producing deep rattle their car-wheels and looking like blazing fires, they advanced, illumining the all points of the compass.

sn: रुक्मपुबैश्च दुष्प्रेक्ष्यैः कार्मुकैः पृथिवीपते। कूजद्भिरतुलानादान् कोपितैस्तुरगैरिव॥
en: Armed, O monarch, with bows whose stave's were decked with gold and which, in consequence of their splendour were incapable of being looked at and settling up loud warcries' and being borne by mettled horses.

sn: भूरिश्रवाः शलः कर्णो वृषसेनो जयद्रथः। कृपश्च मद्रराजश्च द्रौणिश्च रथिनां वरः॥
en: Bhurishravas, Sala, Karna Vrishasena Jayadratha, Kripa, the ruler of the Madras and that foremost of car-warriors viz., Drona's son.

sn: ते पिबन्त इवाकाशमश्वैरष्टौ महारथाः। व्यराजयन् दश दिशो वैयाघेहेमचन्द्रकैः॥
en: These eight great car-warriors, as if devouring up the skies, illumined the ten quarters, with their excellent chariots covered with tiger-skins and decked with golden moons.

sn: ते दंशिताः सुसंरब्धा स्थैर्मेघौघनिःस्वनैः। समावृण्वन् दश दिशः पार्थस्य निशितैः शरैः।।६।
en: Accoutered in coats of mail, inflamed with rage, riding upon those chariots the rattle of whose wheels resembled the rumble of the clouds, they covered Arjuna on every side, with shower of sharps shafts.

sn: कौलूतका हयाचित्रा वहन्तस्तान् महारथान्। व्यशोभन्त तदा शीघ्रा दीपयन्तो दिशो दश॥
en: Steeds of best breed and variegated hue and endued with great fleetness, bearing those mighty car-warriors, appeared beautiful as they illumined the ten quarters of heaven.

sn: आजानेवैर्महावेगैर्नानादेशसमुत्थितैः। पर्वतीयैर्नदीजैश्च सैन्धवैश्च हयोत्तमैः॥
en: Their chariots drawn by excellent horses of great fleetness born in various countries and of diverse species-some bred in hilly tracts, some in river-lands and some in the Sindhu country.

sn: कुरुयोधवरा राजस्तव पुत्रं परीप्सवः। धनंजयरथं शीघ्रं सर्वतः समुपाद्रवन्॥
en: Many foremost of car-warriors among the Kuru, swiftly rushed towards Dhananjaya's car, desirous, Oking, of saving your son.

sn: प्रगृह्य महाशलान् दध्मुः पुरुषसत्तमाः। पूरयन्तो दिवं राजन् पृथिवीं च ससागराम्॥
en: Those foremost of men taking up their huge conchs blew them and with blasts they filled the welkin and the earth with her all oceans.

sn: ते तथैव दध्मतुः शङ्खौ वासुदेवधनंजयौ। प्रवरौ सर्वदेवानां सर्वशङ्खवरौ भुवि॥
en: Thereupon those two foremost of all gods, viz., Vasudeva and Dhananjaya also blew their conchs that were regarded as the best of all the conchs on the face of the earth.

sn: देवदत्तं च कौन्तेयः पाञ्चजन्यं च केशवः। शब्दस्तु देवदत्तस्य धनंजयसमीरितः॥
en: Kunti's son blew his conch Devadatta and Keshava blew Panchajanya. The tremendous blare of the conch Devedatta, produced by Dhananjaya.

sn: पृथिवीं चान्तरिक्षं च दिशश्चैव समावृणोत्। तथैव पाञ्चजन्योऽपि वासुदेवसमीरितः॥
en: Filled the earth, the skies and the ten points of the compass. So also the blast of the Panchajanya, blown by the son of Vasudeva.

sn: सर्वशब्दानतिक्रम्य पूरयामास रोदसी। तस्मिंस्तथा वर्तमाने दारुणे नादसंकुले॥
en: Surpassing all other sounds filled the welkin and the earth. And when the fierce and dreadful sound was still continuing.

sn: भीरूणां त्रासजनने शूराणां हर्षवर्धने। प्रवादितासु भेरीषु झर्झरेष्वानकेषु च॥
en: Sound that struck the hearts of the cowards with terror and enhanced the delight of the brave and while drums, Jarajhwaras and cymbals.

sn: मृदङ्गेष्वपि राजेन्द्र वाद्यमानेष्वनेकशः। महारथाः समाख्याता दुर्योधनहितैषिणः॥
en: And Mridangas, O mighty monarch, were sounded by thousands, great car-warriors, befriending the Kurus and desirous of Duryodhana's good.

sn: अमृष्यमाणास्तं शब्दं क्रुद्धाः परमधन्विनः। नानादेश्या महीपाला: स्वसैन्यपरिरक्षिणः॥
en: All great bow-men, inflamed with anger and unable to bear the loud blasts of Arjuna's and Krishna's conchs, those kings come from diverse countries and accompanied by their troops.

sn: अमर्षिता महाशङ्खान् दध्मुर्वीरा महारथाः। कृते प्रतिकरिष्यन्तः केशवस्यार्जुनस्य च॥
en: Blew their huge conchs, desirous of answering with the blasts thus produced, the blasts produced by Keshava and Arjuna.

sn: बभूव तव तत् सैन्यं शङ्खशब्दसमीरितम्। उद्विग्नथनागाश्वमस्वस्थमिव वा विभो॥
en: Then your army filled with the blasts of the conchs, had its car-warriors, elephants and horses filled with anxiety and O master, all who composed it, seemed to be ill.

sn: तत् प्रविद्धमिवाकाशं शूरैः शङ्खविनादितम्। बभूव भृशमुद्विग्नं निर्घातैरिव नादितम्॥
en: Then that host filled with the blasts of conchs blown by heroic warriors, seemed to be like the welkin echoing with sounds of thunder and fallen down (through some natural cause).

sn: स शब्दः सुमहान् राजन् दिशः सर्वा व्यनादयत्। त्रासयामास तत् सैन्यं युगान्त इव सम्भृतः॥
en: That loud sound, o king, filled all the quarters with its echoes. It frightened the troops as if the end of the Yuga had come.

sn: ततो दुर्योधनोऽष्टौ च राजानस्ते महारथाः। जयद्रथस्य रक्षार्थे पाण्डवं पर्यवारयन्॥
en: Thereafter Duryodhana and the other eight sovereigns, all mighty car-warriors, surrounded Pandu's son for effecting the safety to Jayadratha.

sn: ततो द्रौणिस्त्रिसप्तया वासुदेवमताडयत्। अर्जुनं च त्रिभिर्भल्लैर्ध्वजमश्वांश्च पञ्चभिः॥
en: Then the son of Drona pierced Vasudeva's son with seventy-three arrows and he also pierced Arjuna with three broad-headed shafts and the latter's steeds and standard with five arrows.

sn: तमर्जुनः पृषत्कानां शतैः षड्भिरताडयत्। अत्यर्थमिव संक्रुद्धः प्रतिविद्धे जनार्दने॥
en: Then beholding Janardana pierced and excited to the highest pitch of fury, Arjuna struck his foe with six hundred arrows.

sn: कर्णं च दशभिर्विद्ध्वा वृषसेनं त्रिभिस्तथा। शल्यस्य सशरं चापं मुष्टौ चिच्छेद वीर्यवान्॥
en: Piercing then Karna with ten and Vrishasena with three arrows, that highly puissant hero, cut-off Shalya's bow with arrows fixed on the string, near the grasp.

sn: गृहीत्वा धनुरन्यत्तु शल्यो विव्याध पाण्डवम्। भूरिश्रवास्त्रिभिर्बाणैर्हेमपुङ्खः शिलाशितैः॥
en: Thereupon taking another bow Shalya began to pierce Pandu's son. Then Bhurishrava with three arrows furnished with golden wings and whetted on stone.

sn: कर्णो द्वात्रिंशत चैव वृषसेनश्च सप्तभिः। जयद्रथस्त्रिसप्तत्या कृपश्च दशभिः शरैः॥ मद्रराजश्च दशभिर्विव्यधुः फाल्गुनं रणे।
en: Karna with thirty-two, Vrishasena, with seven, Jayadratha with seventy-three and Kripa with ten shafts and the king of the Madras with ten other shafts, pierced Phalguna in that battle.

sn: ततः शराणां षष्ट्या तु द्रौणिः पार्थमवाकिरत्॥ वासुदेवं च विंशत्या पुनः पार्थं च पञ्चभिः।
en: Thereafter with a group of sixty arrows, Drona's son covered Partha. He then pierced Vasudeva with twenty and Partha again with five arrows.

sn: प्रहसंस्तु नरव्याघ्रः श्वेताश्वः कृष्णसारथिः॥ प्रत्यविध्यत् स तान् सर्वान् दर्शयन् पाणिलाघवम्।
en: Thereupon that foremost of men, that owner of white steed, who had Krishna for his charioteer pierced them all in return displaying great lightness of hand.

sn: कर्णं द्वादशभिर्विद्ध्वा वृषसेनं त्रिसिः शरैः॥ शल्यस्य सशरं चापं मुष्टिदेशे व्यकृन्तत।
en: Piercing Karna with twelve and Vrishasena with three shafts. He cut-off Shalya's bow, once more near the handle.

sn: सौमदत्तिं त्रिभिर्विद्ध्वा शल्यं च दशभिः शरैः॥ शितैरग्निशिखाकारैौणिं विव्याध चाष्टभिः।
en: He piercing Somadatta's son with three and Shalya with ten arrows and pierced Drona's son with eight shafts, well-sharpened and resembling tongues of fire.

sn: गौतमं पञ्चविंशत्या सैन्धवं च शतेन ह॥ पुनद्रौणिं च सप्तत्या शराणां सोऽभ्यताडयत्।
en: He struck the son of Gautama with twenty five and the ruler of the Sindhus with a hundred arrows, once more he pierced Drona's son with seventy shafts.

sn: भूरिश्रवास्तु संक्रुद्धः प्रतोदं चिच्छिदे हरेः॥ अर्जुनं च त्रिसप्तत्या बाणानामाजघान ह॥
en: Bhurishrava then inflamed with rage, cutoff the whip that Hari held and he then pierced Arjuna with a group of seventy-three arrows.

sn: ततः शरशतैस्तीक्ष्णैस्तानरीश्वेतवाहनः। प्रत्यषेधद् द्रुतं क्रुद्धो महावातो घनानिव॥
en: Thereat Dhananjaya owning white seeds and burning with rage, mangled those enemies of his with hundreds of shafts, like a raging tempest tearing away masses of clouds.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच ध्वजान् बहुविधाकारान् भ्राजमानानति श्रिया। पार्थानां मामकानां च तान् ममाचक्ष्व संजय॥
en: Dhritarashtra said O Sanjaya, describe to me the numerous standards, decked beautifully, belonging both to the warriors of the Parthas and to our warriors?

sn: संजय उवाच ध्वजान् बहुविधाकाराशृणु तेषां महात्मनाम्। रूपतो वर्णतश्चैव नामतश्च निबोध मे॥
en: Sanjaya said Hear from me of the diverse kinds of standards belonging to those illustrious warriors. Listen to me, as I go on describing their name, their appearance and their hue.

sn: तेषां तु रथमुख्यानां रथेषु विविधा ध्वजाः। प्रत्यदृश्यन्त राजेन्द्र ज्वलिता इव पावकाः॥
en: O king, on the chariots of those foremost of car-warriors were seen various kinds of standards shining like blazing fire.

sn: काञ्चनाः काञ्चनापीडाः काञ्चनस्रगलंकृताः। काञ्चनानीव शृङ्गाणि काञ्चनस्य महागिरेः॥
en: Made of gold or adorned with gold or decked with garlands of gold, looking like the golden peak of the mighty Meru mountain. The standards of those warriors were of variegated hue and of great beauty.

sn: अनेकवर्णा विविधा ध्वजाः परमशोभनाः। ते ध्वजा: संवृतास्तेषां पताकाभिः समन्ततः॥ नानावर्णविरागाभिः शुशुभुः सर्वतो वृताः।
en: Those standards also were adorned with fluttering flags on all sides. Having steamers of variegated hue tied to them all round, those standards appeared highly charming.

sn: पताकाश्च ततस्तास्तु श्वसनेन समीरिताः॥ नृत्यमाना व्यदृश्यन्त रङ्गमध्ये विलासिकाः।
en: Those streamers also moved by the wind. Looked like beautiful damsels dancing in the midst of arenas erected for sport.

sn: इन्द्रायुधसवर्णाभाः पताका भरतर्षभ॥ दोधूयमाना रथिनां शोभयन्ति महारथान्।
en: Resembling the rainbow in hue, those streamers, 0 best of the Bharata race. Belonging to those car-warriors, fluttering in the air, beautified their cars.

sn: सिंहलाङ्गलमुग्रास्यं ध्वजं वानरलक्षणम्॥ धनञ्जयस्य संग्रामे प्रत्यदृश्यत भैरवम्।
en: The standard, having for its device the ape of fierce face and lion-like tail. Of Dhananjaya, seemed to strike terror into the hearts of his foes. That foremost of apes, O king, adorned as he was with banners.

sn: स वानरवरो राजन् पताकाभिरलंकृतः॥ त्रासयामास तत् सैन्यं ध्वजो गाण्डीवधन्वनः।
en: That device on the standard of the wielder of Gandiva, frightened all your troops, O king.

sn: तथैव सिंहलाङ्गलं द्रोणपुत्रस्य भारत॥ ध्वजाग्रं समपश्याम गलसूर्यसमप्रभम्।
en: We beheld the standard-top of Drona's son, resembling the tail of the lion and effulgent like the newly-risen sun, O Bharata.

sn: काञ्चनं पवनोद्भूतं शक्रध्वजसमप्रभम्॥ नन्दनं कौरवेन्द्राणां द्रौणेर्लक्ष्म समुच्छ्रितम्।
en: Made of gold, fluttering in the air and of the effulgence of the device on the standard of Drona's son like the standard of Shakra floated on highly inspiring the foremost of the Kurus with delight.

sn: हस्तिकक्ष्या पुनहैमी बभूवाधिस्थेर्ध्वजः॥ आहवे खं महाराज ददृशे पूरयन्निव।
en: The standard of Adhiratha's son bore the device of an elephants-girth made of gold. In that battle, it appeared O mighty king, to fire the whole firmament.

sn: पताका काञ्चनी स्रग्वी ध्वजे कर्णस्य संयुगे॥ नृत्यतीव रथोपस्थे श्वसनेन समीरिता।
en: The banners attached to it decked with garlands of flowers and adorned with gold and moved by the wind, seemed to dance on the top of his chariot.

sn: आचार्यस्य तु पाण्डूनां ब्राह्मणस्य तपस्विनः॥ गोवृषो गौतमस्यासीत् कृपस्य सुपरिष्कृतः। स तेन भ्राजते राजन् गोवृषेण महारथः॥ त्रिपुरनरथो यद्वद् गोवृषेण विराजता।
en: The preceptor of the Pandavas, that Brahman devoted to ascetic observances, viz., Kripa the son of Gautama, had for his device an excellent bovine bull. O king, the illustrious Kripa with that bovine bull on his standard, looked as effulgent as the Destroyer of the three-fortresses (Mahadeva) looks with his bull.

sn: मयूरो वृषसेनस्य काञ्चनो मणिरत्नवान्॥ व्याहरिष्यन्निवातिष्ठत् सेनाग्रमुपशोभयन्।
en: Vrishasena had for his device a peacock made of gold and decked with gems and jewels beautifying the van of the army it stood on his standard as if on the point of emitting its notes.

sn: तेन तस्य रथो भाति मयूरेण महात्मनः॥ यथा स्कन्दस्य राजेन्द्र मयूरेण विराजता।
en: With that peacock, the car of that illustrious hero appeared as beautiful as the car of Skanda, O king, appears, being decked by his peacock.

sn: मद्रराजस्य शल्यस्य ध्वजाग्रेऽग्निशिखामिव॥ सौवर्णी प्रतिपश्याम सीतामप्रतिमां शुभाम्।
en: The ruler of the Madras, we beheld, had on his standard-top, the unequalled and charming device of a plough-share, made of gold and looking like a flame of fire.

sn: सा सीता भ्राजते तस्य रथमास्थाय मारिष॥ सर्वबीजविरूढेव यथा सीता श्रिया वृता।
en: O sire, that plough-share mounted on his chariot looked beautiful. Like the Goddess of corn incarnate, endued with all beauty and producing every seed.

sn: वराहः सिन्धुराजस्य राजतोऽभिविराजते॥ ध्वजाग्रेऽलोहितार्काभो हेमजालपरिष्कृतः।
en: The device of a silver boar shone on the standard of the Sindhu king; it was decked with garlands of gold and was of the splendour of the rising sun.

sn: शुशुभे केतुना तेन राजतेन जयद्रथः॥ यथा देवासुरे युद्धे पुरा पूषा स्म शोभते।
en: With that device on his standard, Jayadratha appeared as beautiful. As Pusha in the days of yore, in the battle between the celestials and the Asuras.

sn: सौमदत्तेः पुन पो यज्ञशीलस्य धीमतः॥ ध्वजः सूर्य इवाभाति सोमश्चात्र प्रदृश्यते।
en: The standard of Somadatta's son, ever devoted to the performance of sacrifices was decked with the device of a sacrificial stake. It shone like the sun or the moon.

sn: स यूपः काञ्चनो राजन् सौमदत्तेर्विगजते॥ राजसूये मखश्रेष्ठे यथा यूपः समुच्छ्रितः।
en: o king, that golden sacrificial stake decorating the banner of Somadatta's son, looked effulgent. Like the huge stake erected in that foremost of sacrifices, called the Rajasuya.

sn: शलस्य तु महाराज राजतो द्विरदो महान्॥ केतुः काञ्चनचित्राङ्गैर्मयूरैरुपशोभितः। स केतुः शोभयामास सैन्यं ते भरतर्षभ।॥
en: Shalya's standard bearing the device of a silver-elephant, О king, as adorned on all sides with peacocks made of gold. O foremost of the

sn: स्तदा।
en: Bharatas, that standard enhanced the beauty of your troops.

sn: यथा श्वेतो महानागो देवराजचमूं तथा। नागो मणिमयो राज्ञो ध्वजः कनकसंवृतः॥
en: Like the prodigious white elephant adorning the host of the ruler of the celestials. On the gold-decked standard of king Duryodhana, was the device of an elephant embossed with gems.

sn: किंकिणीशतसंहादो भ्राजंचित्रो रथोत्तमे। व्यभ्राजत भृशं राजन् पुत्रस्तव विशाम्पते॥ ध्वजेन महता संख्ये कुरूणामृषभस्त
en: O king, that standard stood on the chariot of that hero, tinkling with the sound of a hundred bells. Then O monarch, in that battle with that huge standard, that foremost of the Kurus viz., your son appeared highly beautiful.

sn: नवैते तव वाहिन्यामुच्छ्रिताः परमध्वजाः॥ व्यदीपयंस्ते पृतनां युगान्तादित्यसन्निभाः।
en: These nine excellent standards rose high amidst your troops and they lighted up your army, even like the suns that rise at the end of a Yuga.

sn: दशमस्त्वर्जुनस्यासीदेक एव महाकपिः॥ अदीप्यतार्जुनो येन हिमवानिव वह्निना।
en: The tenth standard there, was the mighty ape belonging to Arjuna with that standard Arjuna looked like a mountain lighted up by fire.

sn: ततश्चित्राणि शुभ्राणि सुमहान्ति महारथाः॥ कार्मुकाण्याददुस्तूर्णमर्जुनार्थे परंतपाः।
en: Then many mighty car-warriors all afflicters of their foes, quickly took up, for opposing Arjuna, their huge, white and variegated bows.

sn: तथैव धनुरायच्छत् पार्थः शत्रुविनाशनः॥ गाण्डीवं दिव्यकर्मा तद् राजन् दुर्मन्त्रिते तव।
en: So also Pritha's son of godly achievements took up his bow capable of slaughtering the foe, namely the Gandiva; and all this was owing to your crooked policy.

sn: तवापराधाद् राजानो निहता बहुशो युधि॥ नानादिग्भ्यः समाहूताः सहयाः सरथद्विपाः।
en: Through your fault, in that battle, were slain numerous kings, invited from various countries, with their steeds and elephants and chariots.

sn: तेषामासीद् व्यतिक्षेपौ गर्जतामितरेतरम्॥ दुर्योधनमुखानां च पाण्डूनामृषभस्य च।
en: Then roaring at one another they fall upon one another, headed as they were by Duryodhana on one side and by that foremost of the Pandavas on the other.

sn: तत्राद्भुतं परं चक्रे कौन्तेयः कृष्णसारथिः॥ यदेको बहुभिः सार्धं समागच्छदभीतवत्।
en: Then that son of Kunti having Krishna for his charioteer, inspired his foes with wonder. Inasmuch as he, though single handed, dauntlessly encountered the numerous odds against him;

sn: अशोभत महाबाहुर्गाण्डीवं विक्षिपन् धनुः॥ जिगीषुस्तान् नरव्याघ्रो जिघांसुश्च जयद्रथम्।
en: Then that mighty armed one appeared beautiful stretching his bow Gandiva desirous of defeating those best of men ranged against him and of slaughtering Jayadratha the ruler of the Sindhus.

sn: तत्रार्जुनो नरव्याघ्रः शरैर्मुक्तैः सहस्रशः॥ अदृश्यांस्तावकान् योधान् प्रचक्रे शत्रुतापनः।
en: That foremost of men, that scorcher of his foes, viz., Arjuna discharging his arrows by thousands, made all the soldiers of your army invisible.

sn: ततस्तेऽपि नरव्याघ्राः पार्थं सर्वे महारथाः॥ अदृश्यं समरे चक्रुः सायकौघैः समन्ततः।
en: Thereupon those mighty car-warriors, those best of men, also rendered Pritha's son invisible in that battle, with the shower of their shafts poured from all sides.

sn: संवृते नरसिंहैस्तु कुरूणामृषभेऽर्जुने। महानासीत् समुद्भूतस्तस्य सैन्यस्य नि:स्वनः॥
en: Thus when that foremost of the Kurus Arjuna had been surrounded by those foremost of men, the uproar that was raised in your army was indeed very great and deafening. of men, the uproar that was raised in your army was indeed very great and deafening.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच अर्जुने सैन्धवं प्राप्ते भारद्वाजेन संवृताः। पञ्चाला; कुरुभिः सार्धं किमकुर्वत संजय॥
en: Dhritarashtra said When Arjuna had got the Sindhu king within reach, witat, O Sanjaya, did the Panchalas, assailed by Bharadvaja's son, do, encountering the Kurus?

sn: संजय उवाच अपराह्ने महाराज संग्रामे लोमहर्षणे। पञ्चालानां कुरुणां च द्रोणद्यूतमवर्तत॥
en: Sanjaya said On that afternoon, O mighty monarch, in that hair-stirring battle that then raged between the Panchalas and the Kurus, Drona became as it were, the stake for which they fought.

sn: पञ्चाला हि जिघांसन्तो द्रोणं संहृष्टचेतसः। अभ्यमुञ्चन्त गर्जन्तः शरवर्षाणि मारिष।॥
en: Filled with delight and a desire for slaying Drona, the Panchalas, O sire, poured showers of arrows and uttered loud war-cries.

sn: ततस्तु तुमुलस्तेषां संग्रामोऽवर्तताद्भुतः। पञ्चालानां कुरूणां च घोरो देवासुरोपमः॥
en: That battle between the Kurus and the Panchalas, dreadful, confused and wonderful, was like that which was fought between the Gods and the Asuras in days gone by.

sn: सर्वे द्रोणरथं प्राप्य पञ्चालाः पाण्डवैः सह। तदनीकं बिभित्सन्तो महास्त्राणि व्यदर्शयन्॥
en: Then all the Panchalas accompanied by the Pandavas, reaching Drona's chariot, displayed many mighty weapons, with a view to break through Drona's array.

sn: द्रोणस्य रथपर्यन्तं रथिनो रथमास्थिताः। कम्पयन्तोऽभ्यवर्तन्त वेगमास्थाय मध्यमम्॥
en: Car-warriors mounted on their cars, causing the earth to shake under them and pouring their arrowy showers, proceeded towards Drona's car in a medium speed.

sn: तमभ्ययाद् बृहत्क्षत्रः केकयानां महारथः। प्रवपन् निशितान् बाणान् महेन्द्राशनिसंनिभान्॥
en: Then Vrihatkshatra, that mighty carwarriors among the Kekayas, rushed upon Drona discharging whetted arrows, resembling the thunderbolt of the great Indra.

sn: तं तु प्रत्युद्ययौ शीघ्रं क्षेमधूर्तिर्महायशाः। विमुञ्चद् निशितान् बाणाशतशोऽथ सहस्रशः॥
en: Thereupon Kshemadhurti of illustrious renown quickly rushed against Brihatkshatra, shooting sharp shafts by hundreds and thousands.

sn: धृष्टकेतुश्च चेदीनामृषभोऽतिबलोदितः। त्वरितोऽभ्यद्रवद द्रोणं महेन्द्र इव शम्बरम्॥
en: Then again Dhristaketu that foremost among the Chedis, urged on by his great strength, quickly rushed against Kshemadhurti like the great Indra advancing upon the Asura Shambara.

sn: तमापतन्तं सहसा व्यादितास्यमिवान्तकम्। वीरधन्वा महेष्वासस्त्वरमाणः समभ्ययात्॥
en: Beholding this latter rush with great impetuosity like the Destroyer with mouth wide open, the mighty bowman, Viradhanva proceeded in all haste against him.

sn: युधिष्ठिरं महाराजं जिगीषू समवस्थितम्। सहानीकं ततो द्रोणो न्यवारयत वीर्यवान्॥
en: Then the valorous Drona began to resist king Yudhishthira and his troops, when they were exerting themselves for obtaining victory.

sn: नकुलं कुशलं युद्धे पराक्रान्तं पराक्रमी। अभ्यगच्छत् समायान्तं विकर्णस्ते सुतः
en: O master, your son Vikarna endued with great might assailed Nakula, endued with strength and versed in the art of fighting, who had been proceeding to fight.

sn: प्रभो॥ सहदेवं तथाऽऽयान्तं दुर्मुखः शत्रुकर्षणः। शरैरनेकसाहस्रैः समवाकिरदाशुगैः॥
en: That crusher of foes namely Durmukha, with many thousand swift-coursing arrows, covered Sahadeva who had been making towards himself.

sn: सात्यकि त नरव्याघ्रं व्याघ्रदत्तरत्ववारयत्। शरैः सुनिशितैस्तीक्ष्णैः कम्पयन् वै मुहुर्मुहुः॥
en: Vyaghradatta held in check Satyaki that foremost of men and he caused the latter to tremble incessantly with his sharp shafts properly whetted.

sn: द्रौपदेयान् नरव्याघ्रान् मुञ्चतः सायकोत्तमान्। संरब्धान् रथिनः श्रेष्ठान् सौमदत्तिरवारयत्॥
en: The son of Somadatta resisted those best of men and foremost of car warriors viz., the sons of Draupadi, who filled with rage, had been shooting excellents shafts.

sn: भीमसेनं तदा क्रुद्धं भीमरूपो भयानकः। प्रत्यवारयदायान्तमार्घ्यशृङ्गिर्महारथः॥
en: That mighty car-warrior the son of Rishyashringa, of dreadful appearance and fierce temper, opposed the enraged Bhimasena rushing upon Drona.

sn: तयोः समभवद् युद्धं नरराक्षसयोर्मधे। याहगेव पुरा वृत्तं रामरावणयोर्नृप॥
en: Then between that man and that Rakshasa, raged a fight that resembled, O king, the one that took place between Rama and Ravana in days gone by.

sn: ततो युधिष्ठिरो द्रोणं नवन्या नतपर्वणाम्। अजघ्ने भरतश्रेष्ठः सर्वमर्मसु भारत॥
en: Then, O Bharata, that best of the Bharatas, viz., king Yudhishthira pierced Drona on all his vital limbs with ninety shafts of depressed knots.

sn: तं द्रोणः पञ्चविंशत्या निजघान स्तनान्तरे। रोषितो भरतरेष्ठ कौन्तेयेन यशस्विना॥
en: Thus exasperated by the illustrious son of Kunti, O foremost of the Bharatas, Drona struck him on the chest with twenty-five arrows.

sn: भूय एव तु विंशत्या सायकानां समाचिनोत्। साश्वसूतध्वजं द्रोणः पश्यतां सर्वधन्विनाम्॥
en: Then once more, with twenty shafts, Drona pierced him and his steeds, charioteer and standards, before the very eyes of all the bowmen present.

sn: ताशरान् द्रोणमुक्तांस्तु शरवर्षेण पाण्डवः अवारयत धर्मात्मा दर्शयन् पाणिलाघवम्॥
en: Then that son of Pandu, of virtuous soul, with his own showers of arrows checked those discharged by Drona, displaying great lightness of hands.

sn: ततो द्रोणो भृशं क्रुद्धो धर्मराजस्य संयुगे। चिच्छेद समरे धन्वी धनुस्तस्य महात्मनः॥
en: Then that best of bowman, viz., Drona excited to the highest pitch of fury, in that fight with the very virtuous king Yudhishthira, cutoff the bow of that illustrious warriors.

sn: अथैनं छिन्नधन्वानं त्वरमाणो महारथः। शरैरनेकसाहस्रैः पूरयामास सर्वतः॥
en: Thus depriving Yudhishthira of the use of his bow, that mighty warrior Drona quickly filled the pores of the latter's body with many thousand shafts.

sn: अदृश्यं वीक्ष्य राजानं भारद्वाजस्य सायकैः। सर्वभूतान्यमन्यन्त हतमेव युधिष्ठिरम्॥
en: Then beholding the king rendered invincible by the arrows of Bharadvaja's son, all creatures took him to be slain in battle.

sn: केचिच्चैनममन्यन्त तथैव विमुखीकृतम्। हयो राजेति राजेन्द्र ब्राह्मणेन महात्मना॥
en: Some thought that he had been compelled to turn his face away from the field. Some exclaimed saying-"That foremost of the king has been slain by the illustrious Brahmana.”

sn: स कृच्छू परमं प्राप्तो धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः। त्यक्त्वा तत् कार्मुकं छिन्नं भारद्वाजेन संयुगे॥ आददेऽन्यद् धनुर्दिव्यं भास्वरं वेगवत्तरम्।
en: Thus the very virtuous king Yudhishthira was put in a very dangerous position. Then leaving aside his bow cut-off by Bharadvaja's son in that battle he, took up another effulgent bow of celestial make and endued with greater loughness.

sn: ततस्तान् सायकांस्तत्र द्रोणनुन्नान् सहस्रशः॥ चिच्छेद समरे वीरस्तदद्भुतमिवाभवत्।
en: Then all those arrows shot by thousands by Drona that hero cut-off in battle. Indeed this looked wonderful.

sn: छित्त्वा तु नाशरान् राजन् कोधसरक्तलोचनः॥ शक्तिं जग्राह समरे गिरीणामपि दारिणीम्। स्वर्णदण्डां महाघोरामष्टघण्टा भयावहाम्॥
en: O king, having cut-off all those arrows and with his eyes rendered coppery in rage. He took up a lance capable of penetrating even though the very mountains-lance, of which the stave was of gold, which was terror-inspiring, dreadful and furnished with eight bells.

sn: समुत्क्षिप्य च तां हृष्टो ननाद बलवद् बली। नादेन सर्वभूतानि त्रासयन्निव भारत॥
en: Wielding that lance that mighty warrior became filled with rage and uttered a loud warcry. And O Bharata, with that war-cry of his, he seemed to frighten all creatures.

sn: शक्तिं समुद्यतां दृष्ट्वा धर्मराजेन संयुगे। स्वस्ति द्रोणाय सहसा सर्वभूतान्यथाब्रुवन्॥
en: Beholding that lance raised by the very virtuous king in that battle, all creatures present, pronounced benedictions on Drona.

sn: सा राजभुजनिर्मुक्ता निर्मुक्तोरगसंनिभा। प्रज्वालयन्ती गगनं दिशः सप्रदिशस्तथा॥ द्रोणान्तिकमनुप्राप्ता दीप्तास्या पन्नगी यथा।
en: Then that lance hurled by the arms of the king, resembling a snake that has cast off its slough and illumining the cardinal and subsidiary quarters coursed towards Drona's division like a she-snake of fiery mouth.

sn: तामापतन्ती सहसा दृष्ट्वा द्रोणो विशाम्पते॥ प्रादुश्चक्रे ततो ब्राह्ममस्त्रमस्त्रविदां वरः।
en: Then O ruler off men, beholding that lance coursing towards himself with great force, Drona that foremost of all warrior versed in the use of weapons, invoked into existence the Brahma weapon.

sn: तदस्त्रं भस्मसात्कृत्य तां शक्तिं घोरदर्शनाम्॥ जगाम स्यन्दनं तूर्णं पाण्डवस्य यशस्विनः।
en: That weapon, having burnt into ashes that terrible-looking lance flew quickly towards the chariot of the illustrious son of Pandu.

sn: ततो युधिष्ठिरो राजा द्रोणास्त्रं तत् समुद्यतम्॥ अशामयन्महाप्राज्ञो ब्रह्मास्त्रेणैव मारिष।
en: Thereupon king Yudhishthira endued with great prudence, O sire, baffled that weapon of Drona flying at himself, by invoking the Brahma weapon.

sn: विद्ध्वा तं च रणे द्रोणं पञ्चभिर्नतपर्वभिः॥ क्षुरप्रेण सुतीक्ष्णेन विच्छेदास्य महद् धनुः।
en: Then also piercing Drona with five depressed-knotted razor-headed shafts of great sharpness, he cut-off his mighty bow.

sn: तदपास्य धनुश्छिन्नं द्रोणः क्षत्रियमर्दनः॥ गदां चिक्षेप सहसा धर्मपुत्राय मारिष।
en: Thereupon Drona, that crusher of foes, leaving aside the severed bow hurled, O sire, quickly a mace upon the son of Dharma (Yudhishthira).

sn: तामापतन्ती सहसा गदां दृष्ट्वा युधिष्ठिरः॥ गादामेवाग्रहीत् क्रुद्धश्चिक्षेप च परंतप।
en: Then beholding that mace fall quickly upon himself, king Yudhishthira took up another mace and afflicter of your foes, he also hurled it.

sn: ते गदे सहसा मुक्त समासाद्य परस्परम्॥ संघर्षात् पावकं मुक्त्वा समेयातां महीतले।
en: Those two maces hurled with force, clashing against one another emitted fire in consequence of the dash and then fell on the ground.

sn: ततो द्रोणो भृशं क्रुद्धो धर्मराजस्य मारिष॥ चतुर्भिनिशितैस्तीक्ष्णैर्हयाञ्जने शरोत्तमैः।
en: Then highly enraged, O sire, Drona slew the horses of the very virtuous virtuous king Yudhishthira, with four excellent sharp shafts of keen-points.

sn: चिच्छेदैकेन भल्लेन धनुश्चेन्द्रध्वजोपमम्॥ केतुमेकेन चिच्छेद पाण्डवं चादयत् त्रिभिः।
en: With another broad-headed shaft he cut-off the latter's bow that resembled the rain-bow. He cut down his standard with a single arrow and afflicted Pandu's son with another three.

sn: हताश्वात् तु रथात् तूर्णमवप्लुत्य युधिष्ठिरः॥ तस्थावूलभुजो राजा व्यायुधो भरतर्षभ।
en: Then quickly jumping down from the chariot whose horses had been slain, Yudhishthira stood on the field, weaponless and with his arms upraised, O foremost of the Bharatas.

sn: विरथं तं समालोक्य व्यायुधं च विशेषतः॥ द्रोणो व्यमोहयच्छत्रून् सर्वसैन्यानि वा विभो।
en: Beholding him careless and specially, weaponless Drona of firm vow and great lightness of hands held in bay all the enemy's soldiers, Olord.

sn: मुञ्चश्चेषुगणांस्तीक्ष्णाल्लँघुहस्तो दृढव्रतः॥ अभिदुद्राव राजानं सिंहो मृगमिवोल्बणः।
en: By discharging numerous sharp arrows and like a fierce lion assailing a deer, he then assailed the king.

sn: तमभिद्रुतमालोक्य द्रोणेनामित्रघातिना॥ हाहेति सहसा शब्दः पाण्डूनां समजायत।
en: Beholding the king assailed by Drona that slayer of foes the Pandavas began to exclaim saying, 'Alas'.

sn: हतो राजा हतो राजा भारद्वाजेन मारिष॥ इत्यासीत् सुमहाञ्छब्दः पाण्डुसैन्यस्य भारत।
en: The king is captured, the king is seized by the son of Bharadvaja. Even these were the cries that were then uttered by the Pandava troops, O Bharata.

sn: ततस्त्वरितमारुह्य सहदेवरथं नृपः। अपायाज्जवनैरश्वैः कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Then ascending with quickness on the chariut of Sahadeva, king Yudhishthira the son of Kunti, fled away from the field of battle, being borne away by fleetest steeds.

sn: संजय उवाच बृहत्क्षत्रमथायान्तं कैकेयं दृढविक्रमम्। क्षेमधूतिर्महाराज विव्याधोरसि मार्गणैः॥
en: Sanjaya said Then, O mighty monarch, Kshemadhurti, with numerous shafts pierced the advancing Brihatkshatra, that valorous prince of the Kekayas, on the breast.

sn: बृहत्क्षत्रस्तु तं राजा नवत्या नतपर्वणाम्। अजघ्ने त्वरितो राजन् द्रोणानीकबिभित्सया॥
en: Thereupon king Brihatkshatra, O monarch, desirous of breaking Drona's array, quickly pierced Kshemadhurti with ninety shafts of depressed knots.

sn: क्षेमधूर्तिस्तु संक्रुद्धः कैकेयस्य महात्मनः। धनुचिच्छेद भल्लेन पीतेन निशितेन ह॥
en: Thereat Kshemadhurti excited the highest pitch of fury, cut-off the bow of the illustrious ruler of the Kekayas with a welltempered and well-sharpened arrow.

sn: अथैनं छिन्नधन्वानं शरेणानतपर्वणा। विव्याध समरे तूर्णं प्रवरं सर्वधन्विनाम्॥
en: Then having cut-off his bow, he pierced that foremost wielder of the bow quickly in that battle with shafts of depressed knots.

sn: अथान्यद् धनुरादाय बृहत्क्षत्रो हसन्निव। व्यश्वसूतरथं चक्रे क्षेमधूति महारथम्॥
en: After this Brihatkshatra smilingly taking up another bow deprived the mighty car-warrior Kshemadhurti of the use of his car, steed and charioteer.

sn: ततोऽपरेण भल्लेन पीतेन निशितेन च। जहार नृपतेः कायाच्छिरो ज्वलितकुण्डलम्॥
en: Thereafter with a well-sharpened and welltempered arrow he severed from the trunk of that king his head graced with resplendent earrings. to

sn: तच्छिन्नं सहसा तस्य शिरः कुञ्चितमूर्धजम्। सकिरीटं महीं प्राप्य बभौ ज्योतिरिवाम्बरात्॥
en: That head graced with curling locks and a beautiful diadem, suddenly cut-off, fell on the earth and shone like a meteor dropped down from the heavens.

sn: तं निहत्य रणे हृष्टो बृहत्क्षत्रो महारथः। सहसाभ्यपतत् सैन्यं तावकं पार्थकारणात्॥
en: Thus having slain his adversary, the mighty car-warrior Brihatkshatra became filled with delight; and he rushed quickly upon your troops, desirous of doing good to the Parthas.

sn: धृष्टकेतुं तथाऽऽयान्तं द्रोणहेतोः पराक्रमी। वीरधन्वा महेष्वासो वारयामास भारत॥
en: The fierce bowman, Viradhanvan endued with great prowess, began, O Bharata, to oppose Dhristaketu proceeding against Drona.

sn: तौ परस्परमासाद्य शरदंष्ट्रौ तरस्विनौ। शरैरनेकसाहौरन्योन्यमभिजघ्नतुः॥
en: Those two warriors, having arrows for their teeth and endued with activity, meeting each other began to strike each other with many thousand shafts.

sn: तावुभौ नरशार्दूलौ युयुधाते परस्परम्। महावने तीव्रमदौ वारणाविव यूथयौ॥
en: Then those two foremost of inen fought on with each other like two elephant leaders in rut, in a deep wood.

sn: गिरिगह्वरमासाद्य शार्दूलाविव रोषितौ। युयुधाते महावीर्यो परस्परजिघांसया॥
en: Then those two heroes endued with great prowess fought with each other out of desire for slaying each other, like two ferocious tigers fighting inside a mountain cave.

sn: तद् युद्धमासीत् तुमुलं प्रेक्षणीयं विशाम्पते। सिद्धचारणसंघानां विस्मयाद्भुतदर्शनम्॥
en: That awful fight, O ruler of men, indeed became a sight to look at; and Siddhas and Charanas, by thousands witnessed it with eyes expanded in wonder.

sn: वीरधन्वा ततः क्रुद्धो धृष्टकेतोः शरासनम्। द्विघा चिच्छेद भल्लेन प्रहसनिनव भारत॥
en: Then, O Bharata, Viradhanva excited with rage smilingly cut-off the bow of Dhristaketu in twain with a broad-headed shaft.

sn: तदुत्सृज्य धनुश्छिन्नं चेदिराजो महारथः। शक्ति जग्राह विपुलां हेमदण्डामयस्मयीम्॥
en: Thereupon that mighty car-warrior the ruler of the Chedis, leaving aside the severed bow took up a huge lance of golden staff and iron head.

sn: तां तु शक्तिं महावीर्यां दोामायम्य भारत। चिक्षेप सहसा यत्तो वीरधन्वरथं प्रति॥
en: Then, O Bharata, balancing the lance of fierce energy with both his hands, he hurled it quickly at the car of Viradhanva.

sn: तया तु वीरघातिन्या शक्त्या त्वभिहतो भृशम्। निर्भिन्नहृदयस्तूर्णं निपपात रथान्महीम्॥
en: Wounded sore with that lance capable of killing all creatures, the latter with his heart rent open, quickly fell down on the Earth from his car.

sn: तस्मिन् विनिहते वीरे त्रैगर्तानां महारथे। बलं तेऽभज्यत विभो पाण्डवेयैः समन्ततः॥
en: When that heroic and mighty car-warrior of the Trigarttas had been slain, O master, your army was completely broken and routed by the Pandavas.

sn: सहदेवे ततः षष्टिं सायकान् दुर्मुखोऽक्षिपत्। ननाद च महानादं तर्जयन् पाण्डवं रणे॥
en: Durmukha then hurled sixty shafts at Sahadeva and he uttered a loud war-cry defying in that battle that son of Pandu.

sn: माद्रेयस्तु ततः क्रुद्धो दुर्मुखं च शितैः शरैः। भ्राता भ्रातरमायान्तं विव्याध प्रहसन्निव॥
en: Thereupon the son of Madri excited with rage, smilingly pierced the advancing Durmukha, with many sharp arrows, the brother striking the brother.

sn: तं रणे रभसं दृष्ट्वा सहदेवं महाबलम्। दुर्मुखो नवभिर्बाणैस्ताडयामास भारत॥
en: Then beholding the mighty Durmukha fight with fury, Sahadeva struck him, O Bharata, with nine arrows.

sn: दुर्मुखस्य तु भल्लेन छित्त्वा केतुं महाबलः। जघान चतुरो वाहांश्चतुर्भिनिशितैः शरैः॥
en: Then that mighty hero, cutting off with a broad-headed shaft the standard of Durmukha, slew his four steeds with four arrows of great sharpness.

sn: अथापरेण भल्लेन पीतेन निशितेन हा चिच्छेद सारथेः कायाच्छिरो ज्वलितकुण्डलम्॥
en: Then with another well-tempered and sharpened shaft, he severed the head of his charioteer from his trunk, head that was graced with effulgent ear-rings.

sn: क्षुरप्रेण च तीक्ष्णेन कौरव्यस्य महद् धनुः। सहदेवो रणे छित्त्वा तं च विव्याध पञ्चभिः॥
en: Cutting off with a sharp razor-headed arrow the mighty bow of the Kuru-descendant, Sahadeva pierced him with five arrows.

sn: हताश्वं तु रथं त्यक्त्वा दुर्मुखो विमनास्तदा। आरुरोह रथं राजन् निरमित्रस्य भारत॥
en: Thereupon the cheerless Durmukha leaving that chariot of which the horses had been slain, ascended, O king, upon the car of Niramitra.

sn: सहदेवस्ततः क्रुद्धो निरमित्रं महाहवे। जघान पृतनामध्ये भल्लेन परवीरहा॥
en: Thereat the enraged Sahadeva, that slayer of hostile heroes, in that fierce battle, slew Niramitra with a broad-headed shaft, O prince.

sn: स पपात रथोपस्थानिरमित्रो जनेश्वरः। त्रिगर्तराजस्य सुतो व्यथयंस्तव वाहिनीम्॥
en: Then Niramitra that son of the Trigartta king, fell down from the terrace of his car, afflicting your troops with woe.

sn: तं तु हत्वा महाबाहुः सहदेवो व्यरोचत। यथा दाशरथी रामः खरं हत्वा महाबलम्॥
en: Slaying him, the mighty-armed Sahadeva shone like Dasharatha's son Rama after he had killed the mighty Rakshasas Khara.

sn: हाहाकारो महानासीत् त्रिगर्तानां जनेश्वर। राजपुत्रं हतं दृष्ट्वा निरमित्रं महारथम्॥
en: O ruler of men, beholding the son of their king, the mighty car-warrior Niramitra slain, the Trigarttas uttered loud cries of 'Oh and Alas.'

sn: नकुलस्ते सुतं राजन् विकर्णे पृथुलोचनम्। मुहूर्ताज्जितवाँल्लोके तदद्भुतमिवाभवत्॥
en: O king, Nakula then vanquished in a moment your son Vikarna of expanded eyes; that indeed seemed marvellous, Oking.

sn: सात्यकिं व्याघ्रदत्तस्तु शरैः संनतपर्वभिः। चक्रेऽदृश्यं साश्वसूतं सध्वजं पृतनान्तरे॥
en: Then in the midst of the troops Vyaghradatta rendered Satyaki, his horses, charioteer and and standard, invisible, with numerous shafts of depressed knots.

sn: तान् निवार्य शराशूरः शैनेयः कृतहस्तवत्। साश्वसूतध्वजं बाणैर्व्याघ्रदत्तमपातयत्॥
en: Then the heroic grandson of Sini baffling those arrows like one accomplished in the art of fighting, felled with his arrows Vyaghradatta together with his horses, charioteer and standard.

sn: कुमारे निहते तस्मिन् मागधस्य सुते प्रभो। मागधाः सर्वतो यत्ता युयुधानमुपाद्रवन्॥
en: Upon the fall of their prince the Magadhas, strive their best assailed Yuyudhana, O king.

sn: विसृजन्तः शरांश्चैव तोमरांश्च सहस्रशः। भिन्दिपालांस्तथा प्रासान् मुद्गरान् मुसलानपि॥
en: Discharging arrows and Tomaras by thousands, as also Bhirdipalas, lancesi and mallets and bludgeons.

sn: अयोधयन् रणे शूराः सात्वतं युद्धदुर्मदम्। तांस्तु सर्वान् स बलवान् सात्यकियुद्धदुर्मदः॥ नातिकृच्छ्राद्धसन्नेव विजिग्ये पुरुषर्षभः। मागधान् द्रवतो दृष्ट्वा हतशेषान् समन्ततः॥
en: Those heroes fought on with the invincible Satvata hero, in battle. Then indomitable Satyaki, that foremost of men endued with great strength without the slightest difficulty, smiling the while vanquished the Magadhas and the few that survived, fled in all directions.

sn: बलं तेऽभज्यत विभो युयुधानशरार्दितम्। नाशयित्वा रणे सैन्यं त्वदीयं माधवोत्तमः॥
en: Beholding this, O master, your troops already afflicted with the shafts of Yuyudhana, broke and fled. Then that best of the descendants of Madhu's race, slaughtering in battle your warriors.

sn: विधुन्वानो धनुः श्रेष्ठं व्यभ्राजत महायशाः। भज्यमानं बलं राजन् सात्वतेन महात्मना॥
en: And stretching his mighty bow shone beautiful, endued as he was with great renown. Then, o king, the army routed by the illustrious Satvata hero.

sn: नाभ्यवर्तत युद्धाय त्रासितं दीर्घबाहुना। ततो द्रोणो भृशं क्रुद्धः सहसोवृत्य चक्षुषी। सात्यकिं सत्यकर्माणं स्वयमेवाभिदुद्रुवे॥
en: Refused to return to the fight, frightened as they were by that mighty-armed hero. Thereat Drona, highly enraged, quickly casting his glance on Satyaki, himself rushed upon that hero of wonderful feat, incapable of being defeated.

sn: संजय उवाच द्रौपदेयान् महेष्वासान् सौमदत्तिर्महायशाः। एकैकं पञ्चभिर्विद्ध्वा पुनर्विव्याध सप्तभिः॥
en: Sanjaya said The illustrious son of Somadatta piercing each of those mighty bow men, the sons of Draupadi with five shafts, again pierced them with seven.

sn: ते पीडिता भृशं तेन रौद्रेण सहसा विभो। प्रमूढा नैव विविदुर्मधे कृत्यं स्म किंचन॥
en: Thus deeply afflicted by that fierce warrior, the sons of Draupadi, o king, became confounded and knew not what to do in that fight.

sn: नाकुलिश्च शतानीकः सौमदत्तिं नरर्षभम्। द्वाभ्यां विद्धवानदद्धृष्टः शराभ्यां शत्रुकर्शनः॥
en: Thereafter that crusher of foes, namely Nakula's son Shatanika piercing that best of men viz., Somadatta's son with two arrows, became filled with joy and uttered a loud roar.

sn: तथेतरे रणे यत्तास्त्रिभिस्त्रिभिरजिह्मगैः। विव्यधुः समरे तूर्णं सौमदत्तिममर्षणम्॥
en: The rest of the brothers, then exerting their best in battle, pierced the irate son of Somadatta, each with ten straight-flyings arrows.

sn: स तान् प्रति महाराज पञ्च चिक्षेप सायकान्। एकैकं हृदि चाजघ्ने एकैकेन महायशाः॥
en: Thereupon, O mighty monarch, the illustrious son of Somadatta sped at them five arrows and with each of those struck each of the brothers on the chest.

sn: ततस्ते भ्रातरः पञ्च शरैर्विद्धा महात्मना। परिवार्य रणे वीरं विव्यधुः सायकै शम्॥
en: Thereupon those five brothers pierced by the arrows of that high-souled one, surrounding the hero, wounded him soon with their arrows.

sn: आर्जुनिस्तु हयांस्तस्य चतुर्भिनिशितैः शरैः। प्रेषयामास संक्रुद्धो यमस्य सदनं प्रति॥
en: Then the son of Arjuna filled with rage dispatched the four horses of him to the region of Death with four whetted shafts.

sn: भैमसेनिर्धनुश्छित्त्वा सौमदत्तेर्महात्मनः। ननाद बलवन्नादं विव्याध च शितैः शरैः॥
en: The son of Bhimasena cutting of the bow of the illustrious son of Somadatta, uttered a fierce roar and pierced the latter with numerous sharp arrows.

sn: यौधिष्ठिरिध्वजं तस्य छित्त्वा भूमावपातयत्। नाकुलिश्चाथ यन्तारं रथनीडादपाहरत्॥
en: The son of Yudhishthira felled his standard having at first cut it off, so also Nakula's son felled his charioteer from its place on the chariot.

sn: साहदेविसतु तं ज्ञात्वा भ्रातृभिर्विमुखीकृतम्। क्षुरप्रेण शिरो राजन् निचकर्त महात्मनः॥
