en: Sahadeva's, son, then knowing him to be already vanquished by his brothers, cut-off, ) king, his head with a razor-headed arrow. Once more slaying four hundred warriors, he pierced Bhima with winged shafts. Then thus deepły pierced by that Rakshasa, the highly puissant Bhima.

sn: तच्छिरो न्यपतद् भूमौ तपनीयविभूषितम्। भ्राजयत् तं रणोद्देशं बालसूर्यसमप्रभम्॥
en: Then that head fell down on ground beautifying the field of battle-head that was adorned with gold and that equalled in effulgence the newly-risen sun.

sn: सौमदत्तेः शिरो दृष्ट्वा निहतं तन्महात्मनः। वित्रस्तास्तावका राजन् प्रदुद्रुवुरनेकधा॥
en: Beholding the illustrious son of Somadatta slain and his head roll on the ground, your troops, O king, greatly frightened, began to fly in all directions.

sn: अलम्बुषस्तु समरे भीमसेनं महाबलम्। योधयामास संक्रुद्धो लक्ष्मणं रावणिर्यथा॥
en: Alambusha filled with rage, fought on with the highly powerful Bhimasena, like the son of Ravana fighting with Lakshmana.

sn: सम्प्रयुद्धौ रणे दृष्ट्वा तावुभौ नरराक्षसौ। विस्मयः सर्वभूतानां प्रहर्षः समजायत॥
en: Beholding then that man and that Rakshasa engaged in fighting with each other, all creatures were filled with delight and wonder simultancously.

sn: आर्ण्यशृङ्गिं ततो भीमो नवभिर्निशितैः शरैः। विव्याध प्रहसन राजन् राक्षसेन्द्रममर्षणम्॥
en: Then, O king, with nine shafts of depressed knots, Bhima smilingly pierced, O king, that wrathful son of Rishyshringa, that foremost of Rakshasas.

sn: तद् रक्षः समरे विद्धं कृत्वा नाद भयावहम्। अभ्यद्रवत् ततो भीमं ये च तस्य पदानुगाः॥
en: Thereat the Rakshasa, thus pierced, uttering aloud fierce roars in that battle, rushed, supported by all his followers, upon Bhima.

sn: स भीमं पञ्चभिर्विद्ध्वा शरैः संनतपर्वभिः भैमान् परिजघानाशु रथास्त्रिशतमाहवे॥
en: That Rakshasa then piercing Bhima with five arrows of depressed knots, quickly slew three hundred car-warriors engaged supporting Bhima.

sn: पुनश्चतु:शतान् हत्वा भीमं विव्याध पत्रिणा। सोऽतिविद्धस्तथा भीमो राक्षसेन महाबलः॥
en: Once more slaying four hunderd warriors, he pierced Bhima with winged shafts. Then thus deeply peirced by that Rakshasa, the highly puissant Bhima.

sn: निपयात रथोपस्ये मूर्छयाभिपरिप्लुतः। प्रतिलभ्य ततः संज्ञा मारुतिः क्रोधमूर्छितः॥
en: Squatted down on the terrace of his car, being overwhelmed with a swoon. Regaining his senses, the son of Maruta, overwhelmed with rage.

sn: विकृष्य कार्मुकं घोरं भारसाधनमुत्तमम्। अलम्बुषं शरैस्तीक्ष्णैरर्दयामास सर्वतः॥
en: Stretched his dreadful and excellent bow capable of bearing a great strain and then he wounded Alambusha on all parts of his body with sharp shafts

sn: स विद्धो बहुभिर्वाणैर्नीलाञ्जनचयोपमः। शुशुभे सर्वतो राजन् प्रफुल्ल इव किशुकः॥
en: Thus pierced with many shafts that Rakshasa resembling a heap of antimony looked beautiful, O king like a Kinshuka tree decorated with flowers.

sn: स वध्यमानः समरे भीमचापच्युतैः शरैः। स्मरन् भ्रातृवधं चैव पाण्डवेन महात्मना॥
en: Thus struck in that battle with arrows shot from Bhima's bow and recollecting the slaughter of his brother by that illustrious son of Pandu, the Rakshasa.

sn: घोरं रूपमथो कृत्वा भीमसेनमभाषत। तिष्ठेदानी रणे पार्थ पश्य मेऽद्य पराक्रमम्॥
en: Caused his appearance to be dreadful and addressing Bhimasena spoke these words "Stay, O son of Pritha, on the field of battle and bchold today the prowess I am endued with.

sn: बको नाम सुदुर्बुद्धे राक्षसप्रवरो बली। परोक्षं मम तद् वृत्तं यद् भ्राता मे हतस्त्वया॥
en: O you of perverted understanding, I had a brother by name Baka who was the foremost of the Rakshasas and endued with great prowess. He was slain by you; but that transpired out of my sight.'

sn: एवमुक्त्वा ततो भीममन्तर्धानं गतस्तदा। महता शरवर्षेण भृशं तं समवाकिरत्॥
en: Having thus spoken to Bhima, he became invisible then and there; and then he covered the former with a thick shower of arrows.

sn: भीमस्तु समरे राजन्नदृश्ये राक्षसे तदा। आकाशं पूरयामास शरैः संनतपर्वभिः॥
en: Bhima also O king filled the welkin with arrows of depressed knots, when that Rakshasa became invisible in battle.

sn: स वध्यमानो भीमेन निमेषाद् रथमास्थितः। जगाम धरणीं चैव क्षुद्रः ख सहसागमत्॥
en: Thus wounded by Bhima, the Rakshasa soon got inside his chariot; and soon again he entered into the bowels of the earth and soon again becoming little, flew into the sky.

sn: उच्चावचानि रूपाणि चकार सुबहूनि च। अणुवृहत्पुनः स्थूलोनादान् मुञ्चन्निवाम्बुदः॥
en: He assumed forms countless and large and small. Sometimes assuming subtle, sometimes a gross and sometimes a huge form, he began to roar like the clouds.

sn: उच्चावचास्तथा वाचे व्याजहार समन्ततः। निपेतुर्गगनाच्चैव शरधाराः सहस्रशः॥
en: He spoke diverse kinds of words and uttered speeches everywhere. From the welkin then fell thousands of arrowy showers.

sn: शक्तयः कणपाः प्रासाः शूलपट्टिशतोमराः। शतभ्यः परिघाश्चैव भिन्दिपालाः परश्वधाः॥ शिलाः खड्गा गुडाश्चैव ऋष्टीर्वजाणि चैव ह। सा राक्षसविसृष्टा तु शस्त्रवृष्टिः सुदारुणा॥
en: As also darts, Kunapas lances, pikes axes, spears, rockets, spiked maces, short javelins, battle-axes, rocks, scimitars treacle and swords and thunder bolts. That dreadful shower of weapons created by that Rakshasa.

sn: जघान पाण्डुपुत्रस्य सैनिकान् रणमूर्धनि। तेन पाण्डवसैन्यानां सूदिता युधि वारणाः॥
en: Slaughtered the soldiers of Pandu's son on the field of battle. In consequence of showers of weapons, many elephants of the Pandava host were killed.

sn: हयाश्च बहवो राजन् पत्तयश्च तथा पुनः। रथेभ्यो रथिन: पेतुस्तस्य नुन्नाः स्म सायकैः॥
en: As also numerous steeds and foot-soldiers, O king. Slain by the shafts of the Rakshasa, many car-warriors were dislodged from their seats in the car.

sn: शोणितोदां रथावर्ती हस्तिग्राहसमाकुलाम्। छत्रहंसां कर्दमिनी बाहुपन्नगसंकुलाम्॥ नदी प्रावर्तयामास रक्षोगणसमाकुलाम्। वहन्ती बहुधा राजश्चेदिपाञ्चालसृञ्जयान्॥
en: The Rakshasa then caused a river to flow on the field of battle, the waters of which were constituted by blood and eddies by cars; which abounded in alligators constituted by the elephants, which has the umbrellas of carwarriors for its swans and the flesh and marrow of animals for its mire; which was infested with snakes formed by the severed arms of human beings; which was frequented by many Rakshasas and other cannibals; and O king, which carried with its currents numerous Chedis, Panchalas and Srinjayas.

sn: तं तथा समरे राजन् विचरन्तमभीतवत्। पाण्डवा भृशसंविग्नाः प्रापश्यंस्तस्य विक्रमम्॥
en: 0 monarch, seeing him careering dauntlessly on the field of battle and beholding his prowess, the Pandava became filled with anxious thought.

sn: तावकानां तु सैन्यानां प्रहर्षः समजायत। वादित्रनिनदश्चोग्रः सुमहान् रोमहर्षणः ३७॥
en: The soldiers of your army were then filled with delight; the musical instruments were then struck up emitting fierce and deep sound, making the hair to stand erect.

sn: तं श्रुत्वा निनदं घोरं तव सैन्यस्य पाण्डवः। नामृष्यत यथा नागस्तलशब्दं समीरितम्॥
en: Then hearing that mighty uproar of delight caused by your troops, the son of Pandu (Bhima) did hot tolerate it, even like a snake not tolerating the sound of the palm-stroke.

sn: ततः क्रोधाभिताम्राक्षो निर्दहन्निव पावकः। संदधे त्वाष्ट्रमस्त्रं स स्वयं त्वष्टेव मारुतिः॥
en: Then with his eyes coppery in rage and consuming the foe like fire itself, the son of Maruta invoked the Tvashtra weapon like the god Tvashtri himself.

sn: ततः शरसहस्राणि प्रादुरासन् समन्ततः। तैः शरैस्तव सैन्यस्य विद्रवः सुमहानभूत्॥
en: Thereupon a thousand shafts started into existence from all sides. Great was the carnage that was then created in your troops by those arrows of Bhima.

sn: तदस्त्रं प्रेरितं तेन भीमसेनेन संयुगे। राक्षसस्य महामायां हत्वा राक्षसमार्दयत्॥
en: That weapon discharged by Bhimasena in battle, nullifying the mighty illusion of the Rakshasa, began to afflict the Rakshasa himself.

sn: स वध्यमानो बहुधा भीमसेनेन राक्षसः। संत्यज्य समरे भीमं द्रोणानीकमुपाद्रवत्॥
en: Thus that Rakshasa wounded by Bhimasena in all parts of his body, fled towards Drona's division, abandoning his antagonist.

sn: तस्मिंस्तु निर्जिते राजन् राक्षसेन्द्रे महात्मना। अनादयन् सिंहनादैः पाण्डवाः सर्वतो दिशम्॥
en: Then, O king, when that foremost of the Rakshasas had been worsted by the illustrious Bhimasena, the Pandavas filled the quarters with the echoes of their war-cries.

sn: अपूजयन् मारुतिं च संहृष्टास्ते महाबलम्। प्रह्रादं समरे जित्वा यथा शक्रं मरुद्गणाः॥
en: Then filled with delight, they applauded the mighty son of Maruta the Marutas themselves applauded Shakra after he had vanquished Pralhada in battle. as

sn: संजय उवाच अलम्बुषं तथा युद्धे विचरन्तमभीतवत्। हैडिम्बिः प्रययौ तूर्णे विव्याध निशितैः शरैः॥
en: Sanjaya said Alambusha then began to career dauntlessly on another part of the field. And when he was thus careering, Hidimba's son rushed against and quickly pierced him with whetted shafts.

sn: तयोः प्रतिभयं युद्धमासीद् राक्षससिंहयोः। कुर्वतोर्विविधा मायाः शक्रशम्बरयोरिव॥
en: Then like the battle between Shakra and Shambara in the days of yore, the battle between those two foremost of Rakshasas became terrible, as they invoked into existence many illusions.

sn: अलम्बुषो भृशं क्रुद्धो घटोत्कचमताडयत्। तयोर्युद्धं समभवद् रक्षोग्रामणिमुख्ययोः॥
en: Highly excited, Alambusha began to strike Ghatotkacha. The battle between those two best and foremost of the Rakshasas that then raged.

sn: याहगेव पुरावृत्तं रामरावणयोः प्रभो। घटोत्कचस्तु विंशत्या नाराचानां स्तनान्तरे।४॥ अलम्बुषमथो विद्ध्वा सिंहवद् व्यनदन्मुहुः। तथैवालम्बुषो राजन् हैडिम्बि युद्धदुर्मदम्॥ विद्ध्वा विद्ध्वा नदष्टः पूरयन् खं समनततः। तथा तौ भृशसंक्रुद्धौ राक्षसेन्द्रौ महाबलौ॥
en: O master, resembled that between Rama and Ravana, that took place in days gone. Thereupon Ghatotkacha piercing Alambusha on the breast with a score of Narachas uttered incessantly lion-like roars; so also, o king, piercing the invincible son son of Hidimba repeatedly, Alambusha became filled with। delight and he roared filling the welkin with his roars. Then those two foremost of the Rakshasas, both endued with might and both excited to the highest pitch of fury.

sn: निर्विशेषमयुध्येतां मायाभिरितरेतरम्। मायाशतसृजौ नित्यं मोहयन्तौ परस्परम्॥
en: Fought on with each other, displaying numerous illusions and none getting any advantage over the other. Creating hundreds of illusions and therewith confounding each other.

sn: मायायुद्धेषु कुशलौ मायायुद्धमयुध्यताम्। यां यां घटोत्कचो युद्धे मायां दर्शयते नृप॥
en: Those two Rakshasas, versed in illusive combats, fought on displaying illusions O king; and in in that that battle whatsoever illusions Ghatotkacha created.

sn: तां तामलम्बुषो राजन् माययेव निजनिवान्। तं तथा युध्यमानं तु मायायुद्धविशारदम्॥ अलम्बुषं राक्षसेन्द्रं दृष्ट्वाक्रुध्यन्त पाण्डवाः। त एनं भृशसंविग्नाः सर्वतः प्रवरा रथैः॥ अभ्यद्रवन्त संक्रुद्धा भीमसेनादयो नृप। त एनं कोष्ठकीकृत्य रथवंशेन मारिष॥ सर्वतो व्यकिरन् बाणैरुल्काभिरिव कुञ्जरम्। स तेषामस्त्रेवेगं तं प्रतिहत्यास्त्रमायया॥
en: Alambusha nullified them with those of his own, O ruler of men. Then beholding that foremost of the Rakshasas, that one versed in the illusive mode of warfare, viz., Alambusha fight in that manner, the Pandavas became greatly enraged. Preyed upon by anxiety and excited with rage, Bhimasena and others, supported by many best car-warriors, assailed him with force. ( sire, then they having completely surrounded him with the host of their cars covered him from all sides, with their arrows, like men covering an elephant with blazing brands. Checking the force of their weapons with the illusive weapons of his own.

sn: तस्माद् रथव्रजान्मुक्तो वनदाहादिय द्विपः। स विस्फार्य धनु।रमिन्द्राशनिसमस्वनम्॥
en: Alambusha freed himself from the press of those cars, like an elephant freeing himself from a forest-conflagration. Then stretching his bow the twang of which resembled the roar of Indra's thunder, he

sn: मारुतिं पञ्चविंशत्या भैमसेनि च पञ्चभिः। युधिष्ठिरं त्रिभिर्विध्वा सहदेवं च सप्तभिः॥
en: Pierced Maruta's son (Bhima) with twentyfive, Bhimasena's son with five, Yudhishthira with three and Sahadeva with five arrows.

sn: नकुलं च त्रिसप्तत्या द्रौपदेयांश्च मारिष। पञ्चभिः पञ्चभिर्विद्ध्वा घोरं नादं ननाद ह॥
en: Then again, O sire, piercing Nakula with seventy-three and the sons of Draupadi, each with five arrows, he uttered a loud and dreadful war-cry.

sn: तं भीमसेनो नवभिः सहदेवस्तु पञ्चभिः। युधिष्ठिरः शतेनैव राक्षसं प्रत्यविध्यत॥
en: Thereupon Bhimasena pierced the Rakshasa with nine arrows; Sahadeva pierced him with five and Yudhishthira with a hundred shafts.

sn: नकुलस्तुचतुःषष्ट्या द्रौपदेयास्त्रिभिस्त्रिभिः। हैडिम्बो राक्षसं विद्ध्वा युद्धे पञ्चाशता शरैः॥
en: Nakula pierced him with sixty-four and the sons of Draupadi each with three shafts seperately. The son of Hidimba then piercing the Rakshasa (Alambusha), with five hundred arrows.

sn: पुनर्विव्याध सप्तत्या ननाद च महाबलः। तस्य नादेन महता कम्पितेयं वसुंधरु॥
en: Once more pierced him with seventy arrows; and that highly powerful one sent up a loud roar. In consequence of that roar of his, the earth trembled.

sn: सपर्वतवना राजन् सपादपजलाशया। सोऽतिविद्धो महेष्वासैः सर्वतस्तैर्महारथैः॥
en: With her mountains, forests trees and watery expanses. O king, pierced deeply by those mighty car-warriors, those fierce bowmen from all sides, Alambusha.

sn: प्रतिविव्याध तान् सर्वान् पञ्चभिः पञ्चभिः शरैः। तं क्रुद्धं राक्षसं युद्धे प्रतिक्रुद्धस्तु राक्षसः॥
en: Pierced all of them in return with five shafts each. Then the Rakshasa Ghatotkacha became thoroughly enraged upon the enraged Alambusha.

sn: हैडिम्बो भरतश्रेष्ठ शरैर्विव्याघ सप्तभिः। सोऽतिविद्धो बलवता राक्षसेन्द्रो महाबलः॥
en: And the former (the son of Hidimba) then pierced the latter with seven shafts. O king that foremost of the Rakshasas, endued with might viz., Alambusha, being pierced deeply by his powerful antagonist.

sn: व्यसृजत् सायकांस्तूर्णं रुक्मपुङ्खान् शिलाशितान्। ते शरा नतपर्वाणो विविशू राक्षसं तदा॥
en: Quickly created numerous arrows, furnished with golden wings and whetted on stone. Those shafts of depressed knots then penetrated into the body of the Rakshasa Ghatotkacha.

sn: रुषिताः पन्नगा यद्वद् गिरिशृङ्गं महाबलाः। ततस्ते पाण्डवा राजन् समन्तानिनशिताशरान्॥ प्रेषयामासुरुद्विग्ना हैडिम्बश्च घटोत्कचः। स विध्यमानः समरे पाण्डवैर्जितकाशिभिः॥
en: Like angry snakes of great strength entering into a mountain summit. Thereupon, O king, the Pandavas and Ghatotkacha the son of Hidimba, filled with anxiety, began to sped sharp shafts at Alambusha from all sides. Wounded sore in battle by the Pandavas desirous of securing victory, Alambusha.

sn: मर्त्यधर्ममनुप्राप्तः कर्तव्यं नान्वपद्यत। ततः समरशौण्डो वै भैमसेनिर्महाबलः॥
en: Mortal as he was, knew not what to do. Thereat that foremost combatant, the highly powerful son of Bhimasena.

sn: समीक्ष्य तदवस्थं तं वधायास्य मनो दधे। वेगं चक्रे महान्तं च राक्षसेन्द्ररथं प्रति॥
en: Beholding him in that state, resolved to slay him. Then he rushed with great vehemence upon the car of that foremost of the Rakshasas (Alambusha).

sn: दग्धाद्रिकूटशृङ्गाभं भिन्नाञ्जनचयोपमम्। रथाद् रथमभिदुत्य क्रुद्धो हैडिम्बिराक्षिपत्॥
en: Car that resembled in effulgence the summit of a burning hill or a broken heap of antimony. Burning with rage, Hidimba's son flew for his own chariot to that of his adversary and seized the latter.

sn: उद्वबर्ह रथाच्चापि पन्नगं गरुडो यथा। समुत्क्षिप्य च बाहुभ्यामाविध्य च पुनः पुनः॥
en: He then took the latter up from his chariot like Garuda taking up a snake. Then dragging him up with his arrows and whirling him again and again.

sn: निष्पिपेष क्षितौ क्षिप्रं पूर्णकुम्भमिवाश्मनि। बललाघवसम्पन्नः सम्पन्नो विक्रमेण च॥
en: Ghatotkacha dashed him against the earth like a man dashing a earthen jar full of water against a stone. Endued with mighty and agility and possessed of prowess.

sn: भैमसेनी रणे क्रुद्धः सर्वसैन्यान्यभीषयत्। स विस्फारितसर्वाङ्गश्शूर्णितास्थिर्विभीषणः॥
en: The son of Bhimasena inflamed with rage, began to frighten all your troops. With all his limbs crushed, his bones broken and appearing dreadful.

sn: घटोत्कचेन वीरेण हतः शालकटङ्कटः। ततः सुमनसः पार्था हते तस्मिन् निशाचरे॥ चुक्रुशुः सिंहनादांश्च वासांस्यादुधुवुश्च ह। तावकाश्च हतं दृष्ट्वा राक्षसेन्द्रं महाबलम्॥
en: And slain by the heroic Ghatotkacha the Rakshasa Alambusha looked like a Sala tree broken and uprooted by the wind. Upon the slaughter of that ranger ranger of the night (Alambusha), the Parthas, filled with delight, Uttered loud roars and waived their garments in the air. Beholding that mighty foremost the Rakshasas slain.

sn: अलम्बुषं तथा शूरा विशीर्णमिव पर्वतम्। हाहाकारमकार्षुश्च सैन्यानि भरतर्षभ॥
en: And crushed like a mountain, your heroic warriors, O foremost of the Bharatas, uttered exclamations of Alas and Oh.

sn: जनाश्च तद् ददृशिरे रक्षः कौतूहलान्विताः। यदृच्छया निपतितं भूमावङ्गारकं यथा॥
en: Filled with curiosity, people then came to seen that Rakshasa who was lying on the field like a piece of charcoal (no longer capable of burning).

sn: घटोत्कचस्तु तद्धत्वा रक्षो बलवतां वरम्। मुमोच बलचन्नादं बलं हत्वेव वासवः॥
en: That best of all beings possessed of might viz., the Rakshasa Ghatotkacha, slaying Alambusha like Vasava laying Bala, uttered by loud roars.

sn: घटोत्कचः कर्मणि दुष्करे कृते। रिपुं निहत्याभिननन्द वै तदा ह्यलम्बुषं पक्वमलम्बुषं यथा॥
en: For having achieved that most difficult feat Ghatotkacha was greatly praised by his sires and his other relatives. Indeed having felled his foe Alambusha even like an Alambusha fruit, he became filled with joy.

sn: ततो निनादः सुमहान् समुत्थितः सशङ्खनानाविधबाणघोषवान्। स्ततोध्वनिर्भुवनमथास्पृशद् भृशम्॥
en: Then there arose among the Pandavas a mighty din produced by the blare of conchs and the whizz of various kinds of weapons. Hearing that din the Kauravas uttered equally loud shouts in reply, filling completely the earth with their resonance. For having achieved that most difficult feat Ghatotkacha was greatly praised by his sires and his other relatives. Indeed having felled his foe Alambusha even like an Alambusha fruit, he became filled with joy.

sn: ततो निनादः सुमहान् समुत्थितः सशङ्खनानाविधबाणघोषवान्। स्ततोध्वनिर्भुवनमथास्पृशद् भृशम्॥
en: Then there arose among the Pandavas a mighty din produced by the blare of conchs and the whizz of various kinds of weapons. Hearing that din the Kauravas uttered equally loud shouts in reply, filling completely the earth with their resonance.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच भरद्वाजं कथं युद्धे युयुधानो न्यवारयत्। संजयाचक्ष्व तत्त्वेन परं कौतुहलं हि मे॥
en: Dhritarashtra said Tell me in detail, O Sanjaya, how did Yuyudhana oppose in battle the son of Bharadvaja? I feel a great curiosity for knowing what happened then. Sanjaya said

sn: शृणु राजन् महाप्राज्ञ संग्राम लोमहर्षणम्। द्रोणस्य पाण्डवैः सार्धं युयुधानपुरोगमैः॥
en: Hear, 0 highly intelligent king, the description of that hair-stirring battle that then took place between Drona on the one hand and the Pandavas headed by Yuyudhana on the other.

sn: वध्यमानं बलं दृष्ट्वा युयुधानेन मारिष। अभ्यद्रवत् स्वयं द्रोणः सात्यकिं सत्यविक्रमम्॥
en: Then, O sire, beholding the troops slaughtered by Yuyudhana, Drona himself assailed Satyaki of prowess incapable of being baffled.

sn: तमापतन्तं सहसा भारद्वाजं महारथम्। सात्यकिः पञ्चविंशत्या क्षुद्रकाणां समार्पयत्॥
en: Thereupon Satyaki pierced with five and twenty short arrows that mighty car-warrior the son of Bharadvaja, who had been advancing furiously against him.

sn: द्रोणोऽपि युधि विक्रान्तो युयुधानं समाहितः। अविध्यत् पञ्चभिस्तूर्णं हेमपुङ्खैः शरैः शितैः॥
en: Drona also, fighting heedfully and putting forth his prowess, quickly pierced Yuyudhana, with five sharp arrows furnished with wings of gold.

sn: ते वर्म भित्त्वा सुदृढं द्विषत्पिशितभोजनाः। अभ्ययुर्धरणी राजश्वसन्त इव पन्नगाः॥
en: These arrows piercing through the tough armour of Satyaki, drank the blood of Drona's enemy; and, O king, they then penetrated into the earth like snakes breathing furiously.

sn: दीर्घबाहुरभिक्रुद्धस्तोत्रादित इव द्विपः। द्रोणं पञ्चशताविध्यन्नाराचैरग्निसंनिभैः॥
en: Then the long-armed Satyaki, like an elephant struck with the hook, became filled with fury; and he then pierced Drona with fifty Narachas, all resembling fire itself.

sn: भारद्वाजो रणे विद्धो युयुधानेन सत्वरम्। सात्यकि बहुभिर्बाणैर्यतमानमविध्यत॥
en: Pierced quickly by Yuyudhana in battle, the son of Bharadvaja, pierced Satyaki who had been fighting vigorously, with countless shafts.

sn: ततः क्रुद्धो महेष्वासो भूय एव महाबलः। सात्वतं पीडयामास शरेणानतपर्वणा॥
en: Then again excited to the highest pitch of fury, that fierce bowman endued with great might, once more began to afflict him of the Satvata race, with arrows of depressed knots.

sn: स वध्यमानः समरे भारद्वाजेन सात्यकिः। नान्वपद्यत कर्तव्यं किञ्चदेव विशाम्पते॥
en: Thus repeatedly wounded by Bharadvaja's son in battle, O ruler of men, Satyaki could not decide as to what he should then do.

sn: विषण्णवदनश्चापि युयुधानोऽभवननृप। भारद्वाजं रणे दृष्ट्वा विसृजन्तं शिताशरान्॥
en: Then, O king Yuyudhana's face became cheerless, as he saw Drona discharge numerous sharp arrows in battle.

sn: तं तु सम्प्रेक्ष्य ते पुत्राः सैनिकाश्च विशाम्पते। प्रहृष्टमनसो भूत्वा सिंहवद् व्यनदन् मुहुः॥
en: Beholding Satyaki then in that plight, your sons your troops, O ruler of men, became greatly delighted at heart and they began incessantly to roar like lions.

sn: तं श्रुत्वा निनदं घोरं पीड्यमानं च माधवम्। युधिष्ठिरोऽब्रवीद् राजा सर्वसैन्यानि भारत॥
en: Hearing that dreadful din and seeing that descendant of Madhu's race sorely afflicted, O Bharata, king Yudhishthira addressing his

sn: एष वृष्णिवरो वीरः सात्यकिः सत्यविक्रमः। ग्रस्यते युधि वीरेण भानुमानिव राहुणा॥
en: "This foremost of the Vrishnis this hero Satyaki of indomitable prowess, is about to be destroyed in battle by the heroic Drona, like the sun by Rahu.

sn: अभिद्रवत गच्छध्वं सात्यकिर्यत्र युध्यते। धृष्टद्युम्नं च पाञ्चाल्यमिदमाह जनाधिपः॥
en: Charge and rush to the spot where Satyaki is fighting.” Then that ruler of men, addressing the Panchala prince Dhrishtadyumna said-

sn: अभिद्रव दुतं द्रोणं किमु तिष्ठसि पार्षत। न पश्यसि भयं द्रोणाद् घोरं नः समुपस्थितम्॥
en: "Why do you tarry Oson, of Prisata? Assail Drona quickly? Can you not see the great danger to ourselves that has arisen from Drona?

sn: असौ द्रोणो महेष्वासो युयुधानेन संयुगे। क्रीडते सूत्रवद्धन पक्षिणा बालको यथा॥
en: This fierce bowman Drona is playing with Yuyudhana in battle, like a boy playing with a bird bound with a string.

sn: तत्रैव सर्वे गच्छन्तु भीमसेनपुरोगमाः। तत्रैव सहिताः सर्वे युयुधानरथं प्रति॥
en: Let every one of my troops headed by Bhimasena and others and accompanied by yourself, rush to the spot where Yuyudhana's chariot is stationed.

sn: पृष्ठतोऽनुगमिष्यामि त्वामहं सहसैनिकः। सात्यकिं मोक्षयस्वाद्य यमदंष्ट्रान्तरं गतम्॥
en: Supported by my divisions, I will follow behind you. Do you all rescue Satyaki today who is now within the very teeth of death."

sn: एवमुक्त्वा ततो राजा सर्वसैन्येन भारत। अभ्यद्रवद् रणे द्रोणं युयुधानस्य कारणात्॥
en: Having thus spoken, the king, O Bharata, supported by all his troops, charged Drona in that battle, for the sake of rescuing Yuyudhana.

sn: तत्रारावो महानासीद् द्रोणमेकं युयुत्सताम्। पाण्डवानां च भद्रं ते सृञ्जयानां च सर्वशः॥
en: May good betide you; the din that then arose there, when the Pandavas and the Srinjaya rushed against the single-handed Drona, was indeed very tremendous.

sn: ते समेत्य नरव्याघ्रा भारद्वाजं महारथम्। अभ्यवर्षशरैस्तीक्ष्णैः कङ्कबर्हिणवाजितैः॥
en: Then, O foremost of men, encountering Drona that son of Bharadvaja, that mighty carwarrior, they began to pour upon him showers of sharp arrows furnished with wings of Kanka-feathers and the feathers of peacocks.

sn: स्मयन्नेव तु तान् वीरान् द्रोणः प्रत्यग्रहीत् स्वयम्। अतीथीनागतान् यद्वत् सलिलेनासनेन च॥
en: Then Drona received all those heroes smilingly, even as a host receives his welcome guest with water and the offer of seats.

sn: तर्पितास्ते शरैस्तस्य भारद्वाजस्य धन्विनः। अतिथेयं गृहं प्राप्य नृपतेऽतिथयो यथा॥
en: Then like the guests becoming gratified with hospitality of their hosts, those heroes were gratified with the shafts sped at them by that bowman viz., the son of Bharadvaja.

sn: भारद्वाजं च ते सर्वे न शेकुः प्रतिवीक्षितुम्। मध्यंदिनमनुप्राप्तं सहस्रांशुमिव प्रभो॥
en: They could not then behold the son of Bharadvaja, even as men cannot look at the midday sun of thousand rays, O lord.

sn: तांस्तु सर्वान् महेष्वासान् द्रोणः शस्त्रभृतांवरः। अतापयच्छरव्रातैर्गभस्तिभिरिवांशुमान्॥
en: Then that foremost of all wielders of weapons, viz., Drona afflicted all of them with his myriad shafts, even as the sun afflicts the objects of his earth with his myriad rays.

sn: वध्यमाना महाराज पाण्डवाः सृञ्जयास्तथा। त्रातारं नाध्यगच्छन्त पङ्कमग्ना इव द्विपाः॥
en: Slaughtered (ruthlessly), the Pandava and the Srinjayas, O mighty monarch, could not find a protector, like elephants sunk in mire.

sn: द्रोणस्य च व्यदृश्यन्त विसर्पन्तो महाशराः। गभस्तय इवार्कस्य प्रतपन्तः समन्ततः॥
en: Like the burning rays of the sun scattering in all sides, the mighty arrows of Drona were then seen to scatter on all directions.

sn: तस्मिन् द्रोणेन निहताः पञ्चालाः पञ्चविंशतिः। महारथाः समाख्याता धृष्टद्युम्नस्य सम्मताः॥
en: In that battle were slain twenty-five best Panchala heroes, all reckoned among Maharathas and all enjoying the favour of Dhrishtadyumna.

sn: पाण्डूनां सर्वसैन्येषु पञ्चालानां तथैव च। द्रोणं स्म ददृशुः शूरं विनिघ्नन्तं वरान् वगन्।॥
en: People then beheld the heroic Drona slay in succession the best warriors among the Pandavas and the Panchalas.

sn: केकयानां शतं हत्वा विद्राव्य च समन्ततः। द्रोणस्तस्थौ महाराज व्यादितास्य इवान्तकः॥
en: Slaying a hundred warriors from the Kekaya hosts and routing them completely, Drona stood on the field, O king, like the Destroyer with his mouth wide open.

sn: पञ्चालान् सृञ्जयान् मत्स्यान् केकयांश्च नराधिप। द्रोणोऽजयन्महाबाहुः शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः॥
en: Then, O ruler of men, the mighty-armed Drona vanquished hundreds and thousands of the Panchalas, the Srinjayas, the Matsyas and the Kekayas.

sn: तेषां समभवच्छब्दो विद्धानां द्रोणसायकैः। वनौकसामिवारण्ये व्याप्तानां धूम्रकेतुना॥
en: Pierced by the arrows of Drona, the roar they then uttered, resembled that sent up by the denizen of the woods when the forest is burnt down by a conflagration.

sn: तत्र देवाः सगन्धर्वाः पितरश्चाब्रुवन् नृप। एते द्रवन्ति पञ्चलाः पाण्डवाश्च ससैनिकाः॥
en: Then, o king, all the celestials, the Gandharvas and the ancestral manes said-"Behold the Panchalas and the Pandavas, with their troops, fly away from the field of battle!"

sn: तं तथा समरे द्रोणं निघ्नन्तं सोमकान् रणे। न चाप्यभिययुः केचिदपरे नैव विव्यधुः॥
en: Thus when Drona was slaying the Somakas in battle, none ventured to assail him and none was able to pierce him.

sn: वर्तमाने तथा रौद्रे तस्मिन् वीरवरक्षये। अशृणोत् सहसा पार्थः पाञ्चजन्यस्य निःस्वनम्॥
en: When that fight destructive of best and foremost heroes was thus raging with fury, Pritha's son Yudhishthira, suddenly heard the blast of the conch Panchajanya.

sn: पूरितो वासुदेवेन शङ्खराट् स्वनते भृशम्। युध्यमानेषु वीरेषु सैन्धवस्याभिरक्षिषु॥
en: That prince of conchs viz., the Panchajanya, filled with the breath of Vasudeva's son, yielded loud blasts. When those heroes engaged in protecting the Sindhu ruler were thus fighting.

sn: नदत्सु धार्तराष्ट्रेषु विजयस्य रथं प्रति। गाण्डीवस्य च निषि विप्रणष्टे समन्ततः॥
en: And when the Dharitarashtra warriors were roaring before Vijaya's chariot, the din was so great that the twang of the Gandiva could not be heard.

sn: कश्मलाभिहतो राजा चिन्तयामास पाण्डवः। न नूनं स्वस्ति पार्थाय यथा नदति शङ्खराट्॥
en: Then the royal of Pandu (Yudhishthira); overwhelmed with great anxiety, began to reflect thus-"Surely everything is not well with Arjuna, as this conch-blast indicates. son

sn: कौरवाश्च यथा हृष्टा विनदन्ति मुहुर्मुहुः। एवं स चिन्तयित्वा तु व्याकुलेनान्तरात्मना॥
en: And as the Kurus are roaring out rapturously every moment.” Thus thinking and with a heart filled with anxiety.

sn: अजातशत्रुः कौन्तेयः सात्वतं प्रत्यभाषत। वाष्पगद्गदया वाचा मुह्यमानो मुहुर्मुहुः। कृत्यस्यानन्तरापेक्षी शैनेयं शिनिपुङ्गवम्॥
en: Ajatasatru, the son of Kunti, addressing him of the Satvata race said these words. Though his voice was choked with the vapour of grief and though he was constantly overwhelmed with swoons, yet the king (Yudhishthira) then did not lose sight of what should be done next; and addressing that foremost of the Sinis he then spoke thus

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच यः स धर्मः पुरा दृष्टः सद्भिः शैनेय शाश्वतः। साम्पराये सुहृत्कृत्ये तस्य कालोऽयमागतः॥
en: Yudhishthira said O grandson of Sini, the hour for that duty which sages of the past have enjoined to be done towards a friend by a friend in times of nced, has now arrived.

sn: सर्वेष्वपि च योधेषु चिन्तयशिनिपुङ्गव। त्वत्तः सुहृत्तमं कञ्चिन्नाभिजानामि सात्यके॥
en: O foremost of the Sinis, thinking within inyself, I cannot find out any one, among all my troops, who is a greater well-wisher of ours than yourself, O Satyaki.

sn: यो हि प्रीतमना नित्यं यश्च नित्यमनुव्रतः। स कार्ये साम्पराये तु नियोज्य इति मे मतिः॥
en: He that is always well-affected, ha that is always obedient, in my opinion, only he should be entrusted with the commission of a serious duty.

sn: यथा च केशवो नित्यं पाण्डवानां परायणम्। तथा त्वमपि वार्ष्णेय कृष्णतुल्यपराक्रमः॥
en: Just as Keshava is ever devoted to the interests of the Pandavas, so also are you, O you of the Vrishni race, who are equal to Keshava himself in prowess.

sn: सोऽहं भारं समाधास्ये त्वयि तं वोढुमर्हसि। अभिप्रायं च मे नित्यं न वृथा कर्तुमर्हसि॥
en: I am now going to place a heavy burden on you; and it befits you to bear that burden; it behoves you not to disappoint my hopes.

sn: स त्वं भ्रातुर्वयस्यस्य गुरोरपि च संयुगे। कुरु कृच्छ्रे सहायार्थमर्जुनस्य नरर्षभ॥
en: O foremost of men, do you now assist Arjuna involved in great distress, who is your friend, brother and your preceptor.

sn: त्वं हि सत्यव्रतः शूरो मित्राणामभयङ्करः। लोके विख्यायसे वीर कर्मभिः सत्यवागिति॥
en: You are ever true to your vows and are endued with heroism and the giver of assurances to you friends. In consequence of your feats, you are renowned in the worlds as one devoted to truthful speech.

sn: यो हि शैनेय मित्रार्थे युध्यमानस्त्यजेत् तनुम्। पृथिवीं च द्विजातिभ्यो यो दद्यात् स समा भवेत्।।४९
en: O grandson of Sini, he that casts off this mortal frame in fighting for the cause of friends, becomes equal to him that gives away the earth as a gift to the twice born ones.

sn: श्रुताश्च बहवोऽस्माभी राजानो ये दिवं गताः। दत्त्वेमां पृथिवीं कृत्स्नां ब्राह्मणेभ्यो यथाविधि॥
en: We have heard of numerous monarchs who attained to heaven having duly given away this earth as a gift to the Brahmanas.

sn: एवं त्वामपि धर्मात्मन् प्रयाचेऽहं कृताञ्जलिः। पृथिवीदानतुल्यं स्यादधिकं वा फलं विभो॥
en: O virtuous-souled one, with folded palms, I do beg of you even this, viz., that you attain, O master, the merit of giving away the earth as a gift or of something better than that (by incurring the risk of being killed for the sake of Arjuna, you friend).

sn: एक एव सदा कृष्णो मित्राणामभयङ्करः। रणे संत्यजति प्राणान् द्वितीयस्त्वं च सात्यके॥
en: There is only one person, namely Krishna, that giver of assurances of safety to his friends, who is ever prepared to lay down his life for the sake of his friends. You, O Satyaki, are the second.

sn: विक्रान्तस्य च वीरस्य युद्धे प्रार्थयतो यशः। शूर एव सहाय: स्यान्नेतरः प्रकृतो जनः॥
en: None but a hero volunteers to render help to another hero fighting courageously from a desire of winning fame. An ordinary man cannot do so.

sn: ईदृशे तु परामर्दै वर्तमानस्य माधव। त्वदन्यो हि रणे गोप्ता विजयस्य न विद्यते॥
en: Odescendant of Madhu's race, when this is the course to be followed, I do not find any one else save yourself, who can become a help to Arjuna.

sn: श्लाघन्नेव हि कर्माणि शतशस्तव पाण्डवः। मम संजनयन् हर्षं पुनः पुनरकीर्तयत्॥
en: On one occasion, Arjuna applauding your achievements and repeatedly reciting them afforded me great pleasure.

sn: लघुहस्तश्चित्रयोधी तथा लघुपराक्रमः। प्राज्ञः सर्वास्त्रविच्छूरो मुह्यते न च संयुगे।॥
en: He said-"Satyaki is endued with great lightness of hands; he is versed in all modes of warfare; he is very agile, prudent, acquainted with the use of all weapons and downed with bravery. He is never confounded in the course of a fight.

sn: महास्कन्धो महोरस्को महाबाहुर्महाहनुः। महाबलो महावीर्यः स महात्मा महारथः॥
en: That high-souled and mighty car-warriors possesses broad shoulders, bread chest, long arms, large jaws, great strength and unrivalled prowess.

sn: शिष्यो मम सखा चैव प्रियोऽस्याहं प्रियश्च मे। युयुधानः सहायो मे प्रमथिष्यति कौरवान्॥
en: He is both my pupil and friend. I am dear to him and he is dear to me. And if Yuyudhana renders me help, I can then crush the whole Kuru host completely.

sn: अस्मदर्थं च राजेन्द्र संनह्येद् यदि केशवः। रामो वाप्यनिरुद्धो वा प्रद्युम्नो वा महारथः॥ गदो वा सारणो वापि साम्यो वा सह वृष्णिभिः। सहायार्थं महाराज संग्रामोत्तममूर्धनि॥
en: or

sn: तथाप्यहं नरव्याघ्रं शैनेयं सत्यविक्रमम्। साहाय्ये विनियोक्ष्यामि नास्ति मेऽन्यो हि तत्समः।।६१
en: O foremost of kings, even if Keshava dons the armour for rendering us aid or if Rama, Aniruddha the mighty car-warrior Pradyumna or Gada or Sarana or Samva with the Vrishnis does so, O mighty Inonarch, to assist us in battle. Yet I shall select that foremost of men, that grandson of Sini of unbaffled prowess to assist me, in exclusion of the others, for, there is none equal to him."

sn: इति द्वैतवने तात मामुवाच धनंजयः। परोक्षे त्वद्गुणांस्तथ्यान् कथयन्नार्यसंसदि॥
en: This is what Dhananjaya said to me in your absence in the Dvaita forest while applauding your virtue's truly in an assembly of the righteous.

sn: तस्य त्वमेवं संकल्पं न वृथा कर्तुमर्हसि। धनंजयस्य वार्ष्णेय मम भीमस्य चोभयोः॥
en: O descendant of the Vrishni race, it behoves you not to disappoint Dhananjaya and myself and Bhima.

sn: यच्चापि तीर्थानि चरन्नगच्छं द्वारकां प्रति। तत्राहमपि ते भक्तिमर्जुनं प्रति दृष्टवान्॥
en: When, returning from a sojourn to all the sacred places, I went to Dvaraka, I saw your reverence for Arjuna.

sn: न तत् सोहृदमन्येषु मया शैनेय लक्षितम्। यथा त्वमस्मान् भजसे वर्तमानानुपप्लवे॥
en: When at Upaplava, O grandson of Sini, I did not mark any one else who showed us greater love and affection, than yourself.

sn: सोऽभिजात्या च भक्त्या च सख्यस्याचार्यकस्य च। सौहृदस्य च वीर्यस्य कुलीनत्वस्य माधव॥ सत्यस्य च महाबाहो अनुकम्पार्थमेव च। अनुरूपं महेष्वास कर्म त्वं कर्तुमर्हसि॥
en: For showing kindness, therefore, to one who is your friend and preceptor, O mightyarmed hero, it behoves you, who are of noble lineage and who cherish reverence for us, to act in a way, O great bowman, worthy of your friendship, prowess, nobility of birth and devotion to truth, O descendant of Madhu's race.

sn: सुयोधनो हि सहसा गतो द्रोणेन दंशितः। पूर्वमेवानुयातास्ते कौरवाणां महारथाः॥
en: Accoutered in armour by Drona himself, Suyodhana has suddenly gone behind Arjuna. Ere this, the other mighty car-warriors of the Kauravas have pursued Arjuna.

sn: सुमहान् निनदश्चैव श्रूयते विजयं प्रति। स शैनेय जवेनाशु गन्तुमर्हसि मानद॥
en: We can also hear the defiant roars that the enemy is uttering against Arjuna. Therefore, O honoured hero, O grandson of Sini, it behoves you to hie yourself to Arjuna without delay.

sn: भीमसेनो वयं चैव संयत्ताः सहसैनिकाः। द्रोणमावारयिष्यामो यदि त्वां प्रति यास्यति॥
en: Ourselves and Bhimasena supported by our troops, shall hold Drona in check if he tries to pursue you.

sn: पश्य शैनेय सैन्यानि द्रवमाणानि संयुगे। महान्तं च रणे शब्दं दीर्यमाणां च भारतीम्॥
en: Behold, O grandson of Sini, the Bharata troops are broken and flying away; and as they fly, hear the loud wails they utter.

sn: महामारुतवेगेन समुद्रमिव पर्वसु। धार्तराष्ट्रबलं तात विक्षिप्तं सव्यसाचिना॥
en: Like the very ocean in a Parva day agitated by a mighty tempest, the army of Dhritarashtra, O sire, is being agitated by Savyasachin.

sn: रथैर्विपरिधावद्भिर्मनुष्यैश्च हयैश्च ह। सैन्यं रज:समुद्भूतमेतत् सम्परिवर्तते॥
en: The dust raised by the swiftly moving chariots, horses and foot soldiers, is gradually enveloping the entire army.

sn: संवृतः सिन्धुसौवीरैर्नखरप्रासयोधिभिः। अत्यन्तोपचितैः शूरैः फाल्गुनः परवीरहा॥
en: Behold the mighty Phalguna that destroyer of hostile heroes surrounded by the SindhuSouviras armed with lances and javelins and numbering countless heroes among their ranks.

sn: नैतद् बलमसंवार्य शक्यो जेतुं जयद्रथः। एते हि सैन्धवस्यार्थे सर्वे संत्यक्तजीविताः॥
en: Without defeating this army it will not be possible (for Arjuna) to vanquish the ruler of the Sindhus. All these warriors again are prepared to lay down their lives for the sake of the Sindhu king.

sn: शरशक्तिध्वजवरं हयनागसमाकुलम्। पश्यैतद् धार्तराष्ट्राणामनीकं सुदुरासदम्॥
en: Behold the invincible army of the Dhartarashtras, teeming with lances, arrows, excellent standards, heroes and elephants!

sn: शृणु दुन्दुभिनिर्घोषं शङ्खशब्दांश्च पुष्कलान्। सिंहनादरवांश्चैव रथनेमिस्वनांस्तथा॥
en: Hear the roar of their drums and the full blasts of their conchs, the uproar of war-cries and the rattle of their car-wheels!

sn: नागानां शृणु शब्दं च पत्तीनां च सहस्रशः। सादिनां द्रवतां चैव शृणु कम्पयतां महीम्॥
en: Hear also the roars of elephants the yells of infantry and the cries of hoses-men, as they proceed causing the earth to tremble underneath their tread.

sn: पुरस्तात् सैन्धवानीकं द्रोणानीकं च पृष्ठतः। बहुत्वाद्धि नरव्याघ्र देवेन्द्रमपि पीडयेत्॥
en: In the front of Arjuna is the division of the Sindhus and in his rear is the division of Drona. The foes are so strong in number, O foremost of men, that they can even afflict the lord of the celestials.

sn: अपर्यन्ते बले मग्नो जह्यादपि च जीवितम्। तस्मिंश्च निहते युद्धे कथं जीवेत मादृशः॥
en: Sunk in his fathomless ocean of troops, Arjuna may be deprived of his life. And if he be slain in battle, how can I live?

sn: सर्वथाहमनुप्राप्तः सुकृच्छं त्वयि जीवति। श्यामो युवा गुडाकेशो दर्शनीयश्च पाण्डवः॥
en: Is this great catastrophe, in the shape of Arjuna's death, to overtake me when you are alive? Of blue complexion, youthful in years, of curly locks and exceedingly beautiful is that son of Pandu.

sn: लघ्वस्त्रश्चित्रयोधी च प्रविष्टस्तात भारतीम्। सूर्योदये महाबाहुर्दिवसश्चातिवर्तते॥
en: Light-handed in using the weapons, acquainted with various modes of warfare, that mighty armed hero, O sire, has entered into the ranks of the Bharata troops at the hour of sunrise; and the hour of sun-set is approaching fast.

sn: तन्न जानामि वार्ष्णेय यदि जीवति वा न वा। कुरूणां चापि तत् सैन्यं सागरप्रतिमं महत्॥
en: 0 you of Vrishni's race, I do not know whether he lives or not. The host of the Kurus is like the mighty ocean itself.

sn: एक एव च बीभत्सुः प्रविष्टस्तात भारतीम्। अविषह्यां महाबाहुः सुरैरपि महाहवे॥
en: O sire, single-handed has the mighty-armed Vibhatsu entered into the Bharata army which cannot be encountered even by the celestials themselves in battle.

sn: न हि मे वर्तते बुद्धिरद्य युद्धे कथंचन। द्रोणोऽपि रभसो युद्धे मम पीडयते बलम्॥
en: In this day's battle, my heart misgives me. Yonder also is Drona sorely afflicting my troops in battle.

sn: प्रत्यक्षं ते महाबाहो यथाऽसौ चरति द्विजः। युगपच्च समेतानां कार्याणां त्वं विचक्षणः॥
en: You can see, O mighty-armed hero, how his twice-born one is careering in battle. When several tasks present themselves, you know perfectly which of them should be first attended to.

sn: महार्थं लघुसंयुक्तं कर्तुमर्हसि मानद। तस्य मे सर्वकार्येषु कार्यमेतन्मतं महत्॥
en: O bestower of honour, it behoves you to accomplish first that task which is the most serious, with great activity. Of all these tasks therefore, I do think the task of aiding Arjuna should be accomplished first.

sn: अर्जुनस्य परित्राणं कर्तव्यमिति संयुगे। नाहं शोचामि दाशार्ह गोप्तारं जगतः पतिम्॥
en: The rescue of Arjuna a therefore should be at first effected. I do not grieve for him of the Dasharha race, who is the protector and the Lord of the universe.

sn: स हि शक्तो रणे तात त्रील्लोकानपि संगतान्। विजेतुं पुरुषव्याघ्रः सत्यमेतद् ब्रवीमि ते॥
en: I tell you truly that foremost men, is capable of vanquishing in battle all the three worlds united against him.

sn: किं पुनर्धार्तराष्ट्रस्य बलमेतत् सुदुर्बलम्। अर्जुनस्त्वेष वार्ष्णेय पीडितो बहुभिर्युधि॥
en: What to speak of this weak host of the sons Dhritarashtra? But, O you of Vrishni's race, Arjuna is sorely pressed by numerous odds in battle.

sn: प्रजह्यात् समरे प्राणांस्तस्माद् विन्दामि कश्मलम्। तस्य त्वं पदवीं गच्छ गच्छेयुस्त्वादृशा यथा॥
en: He may lose his life. For this reason it is that I am so cheerless. Therefore do you follow in his track, even as men like you should do.

sn: तादृशस्येदृशे काले कादृशेनाभिनोदितः। रणे वृष्णिप्रवीराणां द्वावेवातिरथौ स्मृतौ॥
en: For men like Arjuna, being urged on by men like myself. Of all the Vrishni heroes, two are reckoned as Atirathas in battle.

sn: प्रद्युम्नश्च महाबाहुस्त्वं च सात्वत विश्रुतः। अस्त्रे नारायणसम: संकर्षणसमो बले॥
en: One among them is the mighty armed Pradyumna and the other is yourself, O Satvata hero, who both are well-known in the world. Equal to Narayana himself in the use of weapons, so Samkarshana in physical strength.

sn: वीरतायां नरव्याघ्र धनंजयसमो ह्यसि। भीष्मद्रोणावतिक्रम्य सर्वयुद्धविशारदम्॥
en: You are equal, O foremost of men, to Dhananjaya in bravery. You surpass Bhishma and Drona and others versed in all modes of warfare.

sn: त्वामेव पुरुषव्याघ्रं लोके सन्तः प्रचक्षते। नाशक्यं विद्यते लोके सात्यकेरिति माधव॥
en: The wise speak of you, O foremost of all male beings, saying-There is nothing unachievable by Satyaki, O descendant of Madhu's race.

sn: तत् त्वां यदभिवक्ष्यामि तत् कुरुष्व महाबल। सम्भावना हि लोकस्य मम पार्थस्य चोभयोः॥
en: Thereupon, O mighty hero, do you perform what I say to you, viz., carry out the wishes of myself and of Arjuna and of all present here.

sn: नान्यथा तां महाबाहो सम्प्रकर्तुमिहार्हसि। परित्यज्य प्रियान् प्राणान् रणे चर विभीतवत्॥
en: O mighty-armed one, it behoves you not to falsify our expectations. Disregardful of your dear life, do you begin to career like a hero in battle.

sn: न हि शैनेय दाशार्हा रणे रक्षन्ति जीवितम्। अयुद्धमनवस्थानं संग्रामे च पलायनम्॥
en: O grandson of Sini, the descendants of the Dasharha race never care for their lives in the course of fight. Avoidance of fight, indecision or hesitation to fight and flying away from fight.

sn: भीरूणामसतां मार्गो नैष दाशार्हसेवितः। तवार्जुनो गुरुस्तात धर्मात्मा शिनिपुङ्गव॥
en: These practices of the coward and the mean, are never resorted to by the scions of the Dasharaha race. O foremost of the Shinis, the illustrious Arjuna is your preceptor, O sire.

sn: वासुदेवो गुस्श्चापि तव पार्थस्य धीमतः। कारणद्वयमेतद्धि जानंस्त्वामहमब्रुवम्॥
en: Vasudeva again is superior both to yourself and to Arjuna of great intelligence. Knowing this, I speak to you these words.

sn: मावमंस्था वचो मह्यं गुरुस्तव गुरोर्बाहम्। वासुदेवमतं चैव मम चैवार्जुनस्य च॥
en: Do not disregard iny words, for I am superior to all your superiors. Whatever I say to you, know that to be approved of by Vasudeva and by Arjuna.

sn: सत्यमेतन्मयोक्तं ते याहि यत्र धनंजयः। एतद् वचनमाज्ञाय मम सत्यपराक्रम॥
en: All this I have spoken to you in right earnestness. Proceed where Dhananjaya is, 0 you of prowess incapable of being baffled, following these words of command uttered by me.

sn: प्रविशैतद् बलं तात धार्तराष्ट्रस्य दुर्मतेः। प्रविश्य च यथान्यायं संगम्य च महारथैः। यथार्हमात्मनः कर्म रणे सात्वत दर्शय॥
en: Do you, O sire, penetrate into this army of the wicked-minded sons of Dhritarashtra. Entering into it and meeting duly with mighty car-warrior in. battle, display ( you of the Satvata race, the feats that you are capable of achieving and that are worthy of yourself.

sn: संजय उवाच प्रीतियुक्तं च हृद्यं च मधुराक्षरमेव च। कालयुक्तं च चित्रं चन्याय्यं यचापि भाषितुम्॥ धर्मराजस्य तद् वाक्यं निशम्य शिनिपुङ्गवः। सात्यकिर्भरतश्रेष्ठ प्रत्युवाच युधिष्ठिरम्॥
en: Sanjaya said Then that foremost of the Sinis viz., Satyaki, hearing those words of the very virtuous king Yudhishthira, words that were agreeable, salutary, fraught with sweet sounds, opportune, delightful and equitable, replied, O

sn: श्रुतं ते गदतो वाक्यं सर्वमेतन्मयाच्युत। न्याययुक्तं च चित्रं च फाल्गुनार्थे यशस्करम्॥
en: “O you of unfading glory, I have heard all the words you have spoken for Arjuna's sake-words that are delightful, equitable and conducive to fame.

sn: एवंविधे तथा काले मादृशं प्रेक्ष्य सम्मतम्। वक्तमर्हसि राजेन्द्र यथा पार्थ तथैव माम्॥
en: At a time like the present, beholding one devoted to you like me, it behoves you, O mighty monarch, to command me as much as you can command Partha himself.

sn: न मे धनंजयस्यार्थे प्राणा रक्ष्याः कथंचन। त्वत्प्रयुक्तः पुनरहं किं न कुर्यो महाहवे॥
en: For the sake of Dhananjaya, I am ever prepared to sacrifice my life. Commanded by you, what is there that I would not do in this great battle.

sn: लोकत्रयं योधयेयं सदेवासुरमानुषम्। त्वत्प्रयुक्तो नरेन्द्रेह किमुतैतत् सुदुर्बलम्॥
en: O ruler of men, commanded by you, I am ready to fight even with the three worlds with the Gods. Asuras and mortals therein, what to speak of this weak host of the Kuru?

sn: सुयोधनबलं त्वद्य योधयिष्ये समन्ततः। विजेष्ये च रणे राजन् सत्यमेतद् ब्रवीमि ते॥
en: I will, this day, fight with the entire army of Suyodhana and vanquish it in battle, Oking. This I tell you for sooth.

sn: कुशल्यहं कुशलिनं समासाद्य धनंजयम्। हते जयद्रथे राजन् पुनरेष्यामि तेऽन्तिकम्॥
en: Safely shall I reach Dhananjaya who is also safe and after the slaughter of Jayadratha, we both shall come back to you, O king.

sn: अवश्यं तु मया सर्व विज्ञाप्यस्त्वं नराधिपा वासुदेवस्य यद् वाक्यं फाल्गुनस्य च धीमतः॥
en: But, O foremost of men, I think it a duty to remind you of the words which were spoken to me by Vasudeva and the highly intelligent Phalguna.

sn: दृढं त्वभिपरीतोऽहमर्जुनेन पुनः पुनः। मध्ये सर्वस्य सैन्यस्य वासुदेवस्य शृण्वतः॥
en: I was repeatedly and strongly solicited by Arjuna in the very midst of all our troops and at the hearing of Vasudeva's son, in these words.

sn: अद्य माधव राजानमप्रमत्तोऽनुपालय। आर्यो युद्धे मतिं कृत्वा यावद्धन्मि जयद्रथम्॥
en: : "O you of Madhu's race, today, with a cool understanding and resolving to fight nobly and resolutely, do you protect the king, till I succeed in slaying Jayadratha.

sn: त्वयि चाहं महाबाहो प्रद्युम्ने वा महारथे। नृपं निक्षिप्य गच्छेयं निरपेक्षो जयद्रथम्॥
en: O nighty-arined hero, making over the inonarch to you or to the mighty car-warriors Pradyumna only, can I I go to slaughter Jayadratha, with an easy heart.

sn: जानीषे हि रणे द्रोणं रभसं श्रे. पम्मतम्। प्रतिज्ञा चापि ते नित्यं श्रुता द्रोणस्य माधव॥
en: You know how formidable Drona is in battle, Drona who is regarded as the foremost of the Kuru warriors. You also know the vow he made before the eyes of all, O master.

sn: ग्रहणे धर्मराजस्य भारद्वाजोऽपि गृध्यति। शक्तश्चापि रणे द्रोणो निग्रहीतुं युधिष्ठिरम्॥
en: The son of Bharadvaja, eagerly longs to capture the very virtuous king Yudhishthira. Drona also is competent enough to afflict Yudhishthira in battle.

sn: एवं त्वयि समाधाय धर्मराजं नरोत्तमम्। अहमद्य गमिष्यामि सैन्धवस्य वधाय हि॥
en: Now, making over the charge of the very virtuous king Yudhishthira, that best of men to you, I am today going to slaughter the ruler of the Sindhus.

sn: जयद्रथं च हत्वाहं द्रुतमेष्यामि माधव। धर्मराजं न चेद् द्रोणो निगृह्णीयाद् रणे बलात्॥
en: Slaying Jayadratha in battle, I will return as soon as possible; O descendant of Madhu's race, meanwhile see that Drona may not capture Yudhishthira.

sn: निगृहीते नरश्रेष्ठे भारद्वाजेन माधव। सैन्धवस्य वधो न स्यान्ममाप्रीतिस्तथा भवेत्॥
en: Oscion of Madhu's race, if that foremost of men Yudhishthira be captured by the son of Bharadvaja, I shall not be able to accomplish the slaughter of the king of the Sindhus and my grief will be great.

sn: एवंगते नरश्रेष्ठे पाण्डवे सत्यवादिनी। अस्माकं गमनं व्यक्तं वनं प्रति भवेत् पुनः॥
en: If the truthful son of Pandu, that foremost of the Pandavas (Yudhishthira) be captured by Drona, it is evident that we shall have to go the forest in exile once more.

sn: सोऽयं मम जयो व्यक्तं व्यर्थ एव भविष्यति। यदि द्रोणो रणे क्रुद्धो निगृह्णीयाद् युधिष्ठिरम्॥
en: If Dróna inflamed with rage succeeds in capturing Yudhishthira, it is evident my victory over Jayadratha will be productive of no good.

sn: स त्वमद्य महाबाहो प्रियार्थे मम माधव। जयार्थं च यशोऽर्थं च रक्ष राजानमाहवे॥
en: Thereupon, O scion of Madhu's race, o mighty-armed one, do you undertake to protect the king in battle, for my sake and for the sake of winning victory and fame.

sn: स भवान् मयि निक्षेपो निक्षिप्तः सव्यसाचिना। भारद्वाजाद् भयं नित्यं मन्यमानेन वै प्रभो॥
en: Thus do you see, O king, that you have been made over to me as sacred trust by Savyasachin, afraid as he ever is of the son of Bharadvaja, on your account.

sn: तस्यापि च महाबाहो नित्यं पश्यामि संयुगे। नान्यं हि प्रतियोद्धारं रौक्मिणेयादृते प्रभो॥
en: I see every day, O mighty-armed one that except Rukmini's son there is no one who can be a match for Drona in battle,Omaster.

sn: मां चापि मन्यते युद्धे भारद्वाजस्य धीमतः। सोऽहं सम्भावनां चैतामाचार्यवचनं च तत्॥ पृष्ठतो नोत्सहे कर्तु त्वां वा त्युक्तं महीपते। आचार्यो लघुहस्तत्वादभेद्यकवचावृतः॥
en: I also am regarded to be a match for the intelligent son of Bharadvaja. So it is evident, I cannot falsify that reputation which I enjoy or disregard the behests of my preceptor Arjuna or leave you, O king, alone. The preceptor Drona, covered with impenetrable armour as he is and endued with great lightness of hands.

sn: उपलभ्य रणे क्रीडेद् यथा शकुनिना शिशुः। यदि काष्णिर्धनुष्पाणिरिह स्यान्मकरध्वजः॥
en: Obtaining you in battle, will sport with you as boy with an innocent bird. If that son of Krishna bearing the Makara as a device on his banner, were here with his bow.

sn: तस्मै त्वं विसृजेयं वै स त्वां रक्षेद् यथार्जुनः। कुरु त्वमात्मनो गुप्ति कस्ते गोप्ता गते मयि॥
en: I could have made you over to his protection and he could have protected, you like Arjuna himself. You should look after your own protection. Who shall protect you when I am gone?

sn: यः प्रतीयाद् रणेद्रोणं यावद् गच्छामि पाण्डवम्। मा च ते भयमद्यास्तु राजन्नर्जुनसम्भवम्॥
en: Who will advance against Drona for protecting you, when I shall proceed towards Arjuna? Let no fear, O king, assail your heart today on Arjuna's account.

sn: न स जातु महाबाहुर्भारमुद्यम्य सीदति। ये च सौवीरका योधास्तथा सैन्धपौरवाः॥
en: That mighty-armed one will never succumb under the heaviest of burdens. Those warriors that are ranged against him viz., the Souvirakas, the Sindhus, the Pauravas.

sn: उदीच्या दाक्षिात्याश्च ये चान्येऽपि महारथाः। ये च कर्णमुखा राजन् रथोदाराः प्रकीर्तिताः॥
en: The Northerners, the Southerners and all cther mighty car-warriors and O king, they that are headed by Karna and are regarded to be most excellent warriors.

sn: एतेऽर्जुनस्य क्रुद्धस्य कलां नार्हन्ति षोडशीम्। उद्युक्ता पृथिवी सर्वा ससुरासुरमानुषा॥
en: All these warriors, taken together, cannot equal the sixteenth part of Arjuna, when he becomes angry. The whole earta rising against him, with her gods, Asuras and men.

sn: सराक्षसगणा राजन् सकिन्नरमहोरगा। जङ्गमाः स्थावराः सर्वे नालं पार्थस्य संयुगे॥
en: And the Rakshasas, the Kinnaras and the reptiles, O king, in fact, with all the mobile and immobile creatures, cannot withstand Pritha's son Arjuna in battle.

sn: एवं ज्ञात्वा महाराज व्येतु ते भीर्धनंजये। यत्र वीरौ महेष्वासौ कृष्णौ सत्यपराक्रमौ॥
en: Knowing this, 0 king, let your apprehension on Dhananjaya's account be discarded, O mighty-monarch. Where the two heroic Krishnas, both fierce bowmen and both of prowess incapable of being baffled are present.

sn: न तत्र कर्मणो व्यापत् कथञ्चिदपि विद्यते। दैवं कृतास्रतां योगममर्षमपि चाहवे॥ कृतज्ञतां दयां चैव भ्रातुस्त्वमनुचिन्तय। मयि चापि सहाये ते गच्छमानेऽर्जुनं प्रति॥
en: There cannot happen slightest impediment to their prowess incapable of being the baffled are present. There cannot happen the slightest impediment to their purpose. Think of the celestial prowess, the accomplishment in the use of weapons, the vast resources, the fierceness, the gratefulness and the kingheartedness of your brother in battle. When I shall leave this place for proceeding towards Arjuna.

sn: द्रोणे चित्रास्रता संख्ये राजंस्तवमनुचिन्तय। आचार्यो हि भृशं राजन् निग्रहे तव गृध्यति॥
en: Think also of Drona, of the wonderful knowledge of weapons he will display in battle; O king, the preceptor earnestly longs to capture you in battle.

sn: प्रतिज्ञामात्मनो रक्षन् सत्यां कर्तु च भारत। कुरुष्वाद्यत्मनो गुप्ति कस्ते गोप्ता गते मयि॥
en: And, O Bharata, he endeavours to keep his vow inviolate and true. Would you be able to protect yourself? Who shall protect you when I am gone?

sn: यस्याहं प्रत्ययात् पार्थ गच्छेयं फाल्गुनं प्रति। न ह्यहं त्वां महाराज अनिक्षिप्य महाहवे॥
en: Who is he, whom I may entrust with your protection and then go towards Arjuna, O king? O mighty monarch, without making over the charge of protecting you in this battle, to somebody else.

sn: क्वचिद् यास्यामि कौरव्य सत्यमेतद् ब्रवीमि ते। एतद्विचार्य बहुशो बुद्ध्या बुद्धिमतां चर॥ दृष्ट्वाश्रेयः परं बुद्ध्या ततो राजन् प्रशाधिमाम्॥
en: I cannot go away, O you of Kuru's race. This I tell you truly; O foremost of persons gifted with intelligence, considering view with the help of your understanding and ascertaining your highest good, do you command me, O king.

sn: युधिष्ठिर उवाच एवमेतन्महाबाहो यथा वदसि माधव। न तु मे शुद्ध्यते भावः श्वेताश्वं प्रति मारिष॥
en: Yudhishthira said O descendant of Madhu's race O mightyarmed one, it is even so as you say. But inspite

sn: रोचय॥
en: of all this, my mind is not very sanguine regarding Arjuna that owner of white horses, O sire.

sn: करिष्ये परमं यत्नमात्मनो रक्षणे ह्यहम्। गच्छ त्वं समनुज्ञातो यत्र यातो धनंजयः॥
en: I shall try my best to protect myself. Do you go, commanded by me, to the spot where : Dhananjaya has gone.

sn: आत्मसंरक्षणं संख्ये गमनं चार्जुनं प्रति। विचार्यैतत् स्वयं बुद्ध्या गमनं तत्र
en: The protection of myself in battle and the necessity of rendering aid to Dhananjaya, weighting these two propositions in the balance of my understanding, I prefer that you should do the latter.

sn: स त्वमातिष्ठ यानाय यत्र यातो धनंजयः। ममापि रक्षणं भीमः करिष्यति महाबलः॥
en: Therefore prepare yourself for proceeding to the spot where Dhananjaya has gone. The highly powerful Bhima will look after my protection.

sn: पार्वतश्च ससोदर्यः पार्थिवाश्च महाबलाः। द्रौपदेयाश्च मां तात रक्षिष्यन्ति न संशयः॥
en: The son of Prisata with his uterine brothers, these mighty kings and the sons of Draupadi, O sire, will certainly, protect me.

sn: केकया भ्रातरः पञ्च राक्षसश्च घटोत्कचः। विराटो दुपदश्चैव शिखण्डी च महारथः॥
en: The five Kekaya brothers, the Rakshasa Ghatotkacha and Virata, Drupada and the mighty car-warrior Sikhandin.

sn: धृष्टकेतुश्च बलवान् कुन्तिभोजश्च मातुलः। नकुल-सहदेवश्च पञ्चालाः सृञ्जयास्तथा॥
en: Dhristaketu, the puissant Kuntibhoja and O sire, Nakula, Sahadeva and the Srinjayas.

sn: एते समाहितास्तात रक्षियन्ति न संशयः। न द्रोणः सह सैन्येन कृतवर्मा च संयुगे॥
en: These warriors all, with great care, will surely exert themselves for protecting me. Neither Drona at the head of his troops, nor Kritavarman.

sn: समासादयितुं शतो न च मां धर्षयिष्यति। धृष्टद्युम्नश्च समरे द्रोणं क्रुद्धं परंतपः॥ वारयिष्यति विक्रम्य वेलेव मकरालयम्। यत्र स्थास्यति संग्रामे पार्षतः परवीरहा॥
en: Will be able to defeat or afflict us. Dhrishtadyumna also that scorcher of foes, putting forth all his prowess in battle will hold the enraged Drona in check like the banks resisting the mighty main. In battle, where that slayer of foes viz., the son of Prisata will present him.

sn: द्रोणो न सैनयं बलवत् कामेत् तत्र कथंचन। एष द्रोणविनाशाय समुत्पन्नो हुताशनात्॥
en: There Drona will not be able to pierce with force, our troops. For the destruction of Drona, Dhrishtadyumna has come out of fire.

sn: कवची स शरी खड्गी धन्वी च वरभूषणः। विश्रब्धं गच्छ शैनेय मा कार्षीर्मयि सम्भ्रमम्। धृष्टद्युम्नो रणे क्रुद्धं द्रोणमावारयिष्यति॥
en: Cased in mail, armed with shafts, swords, bow and decked with many ornaments. Therefore, O grandson of Sini, go with an easy heart and entertain no anxiety on my account. Dhrishtadyumna himself will resist the enraged Drona in battle.

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: संजय उवाच धर्मराजस्य तद् वाक्यं निशम्य शिनिपुङ्गवः। स पार्थाद् भयमाशंसन् परित्यागान्महीपतेः॥
en: Sanjaya said Hearing those words of the very virtuous king Yudhishthira, that foremost of the Sinis, became afraid of the reproach he would incur at Arjuna's hands, it he would leave the king.

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: अपवाद ह्यात्मनश्च लोकात् पश्यन् विशेषतः। ते मां भीतमिति ब्रूयुरायान्तं फाल्गुनं प्रति॥
en: But seeing certainly of an imputation of cowardice by the people (if he were to disobey the words of Yudhishthira), he thus thought within himself. “Let not men say that I am afraid of proceeding to the rescue of Arjuna.

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: निश्चित्य बहुधैवं स सात्यकियुद्धदुर्मदः। धर्मराजमिदं वाक्यमब्रवीत् पुरुषर्षभः॥
en: Thus thinking over the matter in various ways, that foremost of men, the invincible Satyaki, spoke these words to the very virtuous king Yudhishthira.

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: कृतां चेन्मन्यसे रक्षां स्वस्ति तेऽस्तु विशाम्पते। अनुयास्यामि बीभत्सुं करिष्ये वचनं तव॥
en: May good betide you, O king. If you think that these arrangements will be sufficient to ensure your safety, O ruler of men, then I shall go towards Vibhatsu and carry out your command.

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: न हि मे पाण्डवात् कश्चित् त्रिषु लोकेषु विद्यते। यो मे प्रियतरो राजन् सत्यमेतद् ब्रवीमि ते॥
en: There is nothing dearer to my soul in the three worlds, then that son of Pandu (Arjuna). This I tell you in all earnestness.

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: तस्याहं पदवीं यास्ये संदेशात् तव मानद। त्वत्कृते न च मे किंचिदकर्तव्यं कथंचन॥
en: O bestower of honor, with your permission, I will follow his track. There is nothing that I shall not do for your sake.

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: यथा हि मे गुरोर्वाक्यं विशिष्टं द्विपदां वर। तथा तवापि वचनं विशिष्टतरमेव मे॥
en: 0 best of men, the commands of my preceptor are ever worthy of my attention. But your words are all the more so.

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: प्रिये हि तव वर्तते भ्रातरौ कृष्णपाण्डवौ। तयोः प्रिये स्थितं चैव विद्धि मां राजपुङ्गव॥
en: The brothers Krishna and Arjuna are ever engaged in achieving your good; O best of all kings, know me also to be devoted to your welfare.

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: तवाज्ञां शिरसा गृह्य पाण्डवार्थमहं प्रभो। भित्त्वेदं दुर्भिदं सैन्यं प्रयास्ये परपुङ्गव॥
en: Holding your behest on my head, I will, O lord, proceed piercing this impenetrable army, for rendering help, O best of men, to that son of Pandu.

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: द्रोणानीकं विशाम्येष क्रुद्धो झष इवार्णवम्। तत्र यास्यामि यत्रासौ राजन् राजा जयद्रथः॥
en: Here shall, I plunge into the divisions of Drona, excited as I am with rage. I shall then dart through it like a fish through the ocean, O king, to the spot where king Jayadratha.

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: यत्र सेनां समाश्रित्य भीतस्तिष्ठति पाण्डवात् गुप्तो रथवरश्रेष्ठैद्रौणिकर्णकृपादिभिः॥
en: Stays, protected by his troops and trembling in fear of the son of Pandu and depending upon those feremost of car-warriors viz., Drona's son, Karna, Kripa and others.

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: इतस्त्रियोजनं मन्ये तमध्वानं विशाम्पते। यत्र तिष्ठति पार्थोऽसौ जयद्रथवधोद्यतः॥
en: This distance, O king, between this place and the spot where Arjuna is exerting himself for the slaughter of Jayadratha, measures full three Yojanas.

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: त्रियोजनगतस्यापि तस्य यास्याम्यहं पदम्। आसैन्धववधान राजन् सुदृढेनान्तरात्मना॥
en: But through Partha is three Yojanas away from this place, yet I shall pursue his track with a firm heart and support him till the slaughter of Jayadratha in accomplished.

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: अनादिष्टस्तु गुरुणा को नु युध्येत मानवः। आदिष्टस्तु यथा राजन् को न युध्येत मादृशः॥
en: Unless commanded by his preceptors, what man goes to battle with his enemies? When again commanded, O king, like myself, by his preceptors, what man is there that would not fight?

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: अभिजानामि तं देशं यत्र यास्याम्यहं प्रभो। हलशक्तिगदाप्रासचर्मखड्गटितोमरम्॥
en: I know the spot, O king, whither I have to go. Teeming as it does with plough-shares, lances, maces darts, bludgeons.

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: इष्वस्रवरसम्बाधं क्षोभयिष्ये बलार्णवम्। यदेत। कुञ्जरानीकं साहस्रमनुपश्यसि॥
en: Arrows and other weapons, I shall still agitate this ocean-like host. This elephant division, numbering a thousand elephants strong, that you see.

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: कुलमाञ्जनकं नाम यत्रैते वीर्यशलिनः। आस्थिता बहुभिर्लेच्छैर्युद्धशौण्डैः प्रहारिभिः॥
en: All belonging to the breed known as Arjuna and all possessed of great prowess and ridden by numerous Mlechchas delighting in battle and skilled in smiting down.

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: नागा मेघनिभा राजन् क्षरन्त इव तोयदाः। नैते जातु निवर्तेरन् प्रेषिता हस्तिसादिभिः॥
en: These elephants shedding the temporal juice like clouds pouring rain, they never turn back when goaded on by those on their backs.

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: अन्यत्र हि वधादेषां नास्ति राजन् पराजयः। अथ यान् रथिनो राजन् सहस्रमनुपश्यसि॥
en: They cannot be defeated unless they are slaughtered, Oking. Then again you carwarriors thousands strong in number, whom you can see.

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: एते रुक्मरथा नाम राजपुत्रा महारथाः। रथेष्वस्रेषु निपुणा नागेषु च विशाम्पते॥
en: Are of royal extraction and are all recongnised as Maharathas. All of them are of golden chariots. They accomplished in the use of weapons, in fighting upon cars and on the backs of elephants, O king!

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: धनुर्वेद गताः पारं मुष्टियुद्धे च कोविदाः। गदायुद्धविशेषज्ञा नियुद्धकुशलास्तथा॥
en: Masters in the art of bowmanship, they are well-skilled in fighting with their fist also. They are skilled in fighting with maces and also in close quarters.

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: खड्गप्रहरणे युक्ताः सम्पाते चासिचर्मणोः। शूराश्च कृतविद्याश्च स्पर्धन्ते च परस्परम्॥
en: They are equally active in fighting with the sword and falling upon the foe with sword and buckler. They are courageous, learned and inspired with a desire for outvieing one another. Owners are

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: नित्यं हि समरे विजिगीषन्ति मानवान्। कर्णेन विहिता राजन् दुःशासनमनुव्रताः॥
en: O king, they every day conquer countless warriors. They are under Karna's commanded and devotedly follow Dushasana.

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: एतांस्तु वासुदेवोऽपि रथोदारान् प्रशंसति। सततं प्रियकामाश्च कर्णस्यैते वशे स्थिताः॥
en: Even Vasudeva's son praises these men as mighty car-warriors. Always solicitous of doing good to the Kurus, they are obedient to Karna.

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: तस्यैव वचनाद् राजन् निवृत्ताः श्वेतवाहनात्। ते न क्लान्ता न च श्रान्ता दृढावरणकार्मुकाः॥
en: Returning, at Karna's command, from their pursuit of Arjuna of white steeds and so unfatigued and in-exhausted, those brave warriors, accoutered in impenetrable mail and armed with tough bows.

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: मदर्थेऽधिष्ठिता नूनं धार्तराष्ट्रस्य शासनात्। एतान् प्रमथ्य संग्रामे प्रियार्थे तव कौरव॥
en: Are made to wait for me at Duryodhana's command. For your good, O foremost descendant of the Kuru race, crushing these warriors in battle.

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: प्रयास्यामि ततः पश्चात् पदवीं सव्यसाचिनः। यांस्त्वेतानपरान् राजन् नागान् सप्त शतानिमान्॥
en: I will follow from behind the track laid open by Savyasachin. Those other elephants, O monarch, full seven hundred in number.

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: प्रेक्षसे वर्मसंछन्नान् किरातैः समधिष्ठितान्। किरातराजो यान् प्रादाद् द्विरदान् सव्यसाचिनः॥ स्वलंकृतांस्तदा प्रेष्यानिच्छञ्जीवितमात्मनः। आसन्नेते पुरा राजस्व कर्मकरा दृढम्॥
en: That you can see, all covered with armours, ridden by Kiratas and adorned with ornaments, were formerly presented by the king of the Kiratas, together with many servants, to Savyasachin; O King these were at first engaged in doing your good.

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: त्वामेवाद्य युयुत्सन्ते पश्य कालस्य पर्ययम्। एषामेते महामात्राः किराता युद्धदुर्मदाः॥ हस्तिशिक्षाविदश्चैव सर्वे चैवाग्नियोनयः। एते विनिर्जिता: संख्ये संग्रामे सव्यसाचिना॥
en: Behold the changes brought about by time, in as mush as, they are now ranged to fight against you. The Kiratas indomitable, in battle are their guides. Skillful in guiding elephants and all sprung from fire, they were all unitedly defeated in battle by Savyasachin.

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: मदर्थमद्य संयत्ता दुर्योधवशानुगा: एतान् हत्वा शरे राजन् किरातान् युद्धदुर्मदान्॥
en: Obedient to the commands of Duryodhana, they are bow waiting unitedly to receive me, Slaying, O king, these Kiratas indomitable in battle, by means of these shafts.

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: सैन्धवस्य वधे यत्तमनुयास्यामि पाण्डवम्। ये त्वेते सुमहानागा अञ्जनस्य कुलोद्भवाः॥
en: I will follow in the track of Pandu's son intent on the slaughter of the Sindhu king. Those other elephants sprung from the race of the Anjanas.

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: कर्कशाश्च विनीताश्च प्रभिन्नकरटामुखाः। जाम्बूनदमयैः सर्वे वर्मभिः सुविभूषिताः॥
en: Of tough hide, well-trained and shedding secretions from their temples and mouth and covered with armours made entirely of gold.

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: लब्धलक्ष्या रणे राजन्नैरावणासमा युधि। उत्तरात् पर्वतादेते तीक्ष्णैर्दुस्युभिरास्थिताः॥
en: Those elephants are all very useful in battle and equal to Airavat himself. These have come from the northern hills and are mounted by fierce robbers.

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: कर्कशैः प्रवरैर्योधैः कार्णायसतनुच्छैः। सन्ति गोयोनयश्चात्र सन्ति वानरयोनयः॥ अनेकयोनयश्चान्ये तथा मानुषयोनयः। अनीकं समवेतानां धूम्रवर्णमुदीर्यते॥ म्लेच्छाना पापकर्तृणा हिमदुर्गनिवासिनाम्। एतद् दुर्योधनो लब्ध्वा समग्रं राज मण्डलम्॥
en: Possessed of strong limbs, cased in armours and all excellent fighters. There are, amongst them persons born of the cow, of the ape, or of diverse other creatures, including those born of men; that division of the sinful Mlechchas assembled together and come from the strongholds of the Himavat hill, appear to be like volumes of smoke from this distance. Obtaining these and numerous other Kshatriyas.

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: कृपं च सौमदत्तिं च द्रोणं च रथिनां वरम्। सिन्धुराजं तथा कर्णमवमन्यत पाण्डवान्॥
en: As also Kripa and Somadatta's son and that foremost of car-warriors viz., Drona and the ruler of the Sindhus and Karna, as partisans, Duryodhana disregards the Pandavas.

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: कृतार्थमथ चात्मानं मन्यते कालचोदितः। ते तु सर्वेऽद्य सम्प्राप्ता मम नाराचगोचरम्॥
en: He also thinks himself to be already crowned with success, being impelled by Fate. But today, all these warriors, coming within the reach of my Narachas.

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: न विमोक्ष्यन्ति कौन्तेय यद्यपि स्युर्मनोजवाः। तेन सम्भाविता नित्यं परवीर्योपजीविना॥
en: Will not escape alive, O son of Kunti, even if they he gifted with the fleetness of the mind. Always held in honour by king Duryodhana ever-depending on the prowess of others.

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: विनाशुमुपयास्यन्ति मच्छरौघनिपीडिताः। ये त्वेते रथिनो राजन् दृश्यन्ते काञ्चनध्वजाः॥
en: They shall today meet with their destruction, being sorely afflicted by my arrowy showers. O king, those other warrior owning golden standards, whom you can see.

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: एते दुर्वारणा नाम काम्बोजा यदि ते श्रुताः। शूराश्च कृतविद्याश्च धनुर्वेद च निष्ठिताः॥
en: They are known the irresistible Kambojas. They are brave, learned and practised in the use of the bow;

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: संहताश्च भृशं ह्येते अन्योन्यस्य हितैषिणः। अक्षौहिण्यश्च संरब्धा धार्तराष्ट्रस्य भारत॥
en: They are arranged in serried file and are resolved to stand firmly by one another. These Akshauhini of troops belonging to the sons of Dhritarashtra, all inspired with rage. as are

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: यत्ता मदर्थे तिष्ठन्ति कुरुवीराभिरक्षिताः। अप्रमत्ता महाराज मामेव प्रत्युपस्थिताः॥
en: And expectantly looking for me, awaiting my arrival, being supported by numerous Kuru heroes. They are all coolheaded, O monarch and long to receive me.

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: तानहं प्रमथिष्यामि तृणानीव हुताशनः। तस्मात् सर्वानुपासंगान् सर्वोपकरणानि च॥ रथे कुर्वन्त ते राजन् यथावद् रथकल्पकाः। अस्मिस्तु किल सम्म ग्राह्यं विविधमायुधम्॥
en: Them shall I consume, like fire consuming a heap of grass. Let, therefore, o king, those who are versed in equipping chariots, equip my chariot with numerous quivers and all other implements of war and let these weapons be placed in proper places. Weapons of diverse kinds will have to be used in the terrible fight that will commence, ere long.

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: यथोपदिष्टमाचार्यैः कार्यः पञ्चगुणो रथः। काम्बोजैर्हि समेष्यामि तीक्ष्णैराशीविषोपमैः॥
en: Let the chariot be stuffed with necessaries, five times more then what the professors of military science direct, in as much as, I shall have to encounter the united Kambojas resembling fierce snakes of virulent poison.

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: नानाशस्त्रसमावायैर्विविधायुधयोधिभिः। किरातैश्च समेष्यामि विषकल्पैः प्रहारिभिः॥
en: I shall also have to engage with the Kiratas armed with various implements of war, who resemble virulent poison, who accomplished in striking down.

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: लालितैः सततं राज्ञा दुर्योधनहितैषिभिः। शकैश्चापि समेष्यामि शक्रतुल्यपराक्रमैः॥
en: Who have been favoured by the king and who in consequence, ever desire to achieve the good of Duryodhana. I shall also encounter the Shakas who resemble Indra himself in prowess.

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: अग्निकल्पैर्दुराधर्षः प्रदीप्तैरिव पावकैः। तथान्यैर्विविधैर्योधैः कालकल्पैर्दुरासदैः॥
en: Who are fierce as fire and difficult of being repressed like a raging conflagration. I shall have also to meet numerous other warriors, all irresistible and resembling Death himself. are

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: समेष्यामि रणे राजन् बहुभिर्युद्धदुर्मदैः। तस्माद् वैवाजिनो विश्रान्ताः शुभलक्षणाः॥
en: I shall have to encounter, O king, countless indomitable warriors. For these reasons, let excellent steeds of the best breed and graced with auspicious marks be harnessed to my chariot, after they had drank their fill and been groomed properly.

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: संजय उवाच उपावृत्ताश्च पीताश्च पुनर्युज्ययन्तु मे रथे। तस्य सर्वानुपासंगान् सर्वोपकरणानि च॥
en: Sanjaya said Then king Yudhishthira directed quivers full of shafts and various other kinds of weapons and all other necessaries, to be placed in the chariot of Satyaki.

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: रथे चास्थापयद् राजा शस्त्राणि विविधानि च। ततस्तान् सर्वतो युक्तान् सदश्वांश्चतुरो जनाः॥
en: Then people caused the four excellent steed yoked to his car to drink juicy and intoxicating liquors.

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: रसवत् पाययामासुः पानं मदसमीरणम्। पीतोपवृत्तान् स्नातांश्च जग्धान्नान् समलंकृतान्॥
en: Having caused those four steeds to slake their thirsts and walk and bathe and eat and having decked them with garlands of gold, men plucked the arrows out of their bodies;

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: विनीतशल्यांस्तुरगांश्चतुरो हेममालिनः। तान् युक्तान् रुक्मवर्णाभान् विनीत्व्शीघ्रगामिनः॥
en: Those animals that had been unharnessed for these operations, that were of golden hue, well-trained, endued with great fleetness, cheerful and extremely docile, were gain properly yoked to his chariot.

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: संहृष्टमनसोऽव्यग्रान् विधिवत्कल्पितान् रथे। महाध्वजेन सिंहेन हेमकेसरमालिना॥ संवृते केतकैमैर्मणिवद्विमचित्रितैः पाण्डुराभ्रप्रकाशाभिः पताकाभिरलंकृते॥ हेमदण्डोच्छ्रितच्छत्रे बहुशस्त्रपरिच्छदे। योजयामास विधिवद्धेमभाण्डविभूषितान्॥ दारुकस्यानुजो भ्राता सूतस्यस्य प्रियः सस्त्रा। न्यवेदयद् रथं युक्तं वासवस्येव मातलिः॥
en: On the top of that chariot was mounted a tall standard bearing the device of a lion of golden manes. The standard was decked with banners of the hue of white clouds and it was graced with golden circles and pearls and corals. An umbrella with a huge golden staff was also placed upon that car that was groaning under the burden of weapons. When those horses decked with golden caparisons had been yoked to the car, the younger brother of Daruka, who was Satyaki's friend and charioteer came and represented to him that the car was ready, even as Matali informs Indra about the equipment of his car.

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: ततः स्नातः शुचिर्भूत्वा कृतकौतुकमङ्गलः। स्नातकानां सहस्त्रस्य स्वर्णनिष्कानथो ददौ॥
en: Then Satyaki, having taken a bath and having purified himself and having under gone every auspicious ceremony gave away to the Snataka Brahmanas thousand of golden Nikshasas.

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: आशीर्वादैः परिष्वक्तः सात्यकिः श्रीमतांवरः। ततः स मधुपर्कार्हः पीत्वा कैलातकं मधु॥ लोहिताक्षो बभौ तत्र मदविह्वललोचनः। आलभ्य वीरकांस्यं च हर्षेण महतान्वितः॥
en: Then blessed with the benedictions the latter pronounced upon him, that foremost handsome looking men. That hero worthy of adoration, having drunk Kailataka honey, appeared exceedingly beautiful with reddened eyes rolling in intoxication. Having touched a brazen mirror and being highly delighted, he became filled the double his ordinary energy and looked like the blazing fire.

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: द्विगुणीकृततेजा हि प्रज्वलन्निव पावकः। उत्सङ्गे धनुरादाय सशरं रथिनां वरः॥
en: Taking upon his shoulder his bow and arrows that best of car-warriors, covered in mail and adorned with ornaments, made the twice-born perform the rites of propitiation on his behalf. ones

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: कृतस्वस्त्ययनो विप्रैः कवची समलंकृतः। लाजैर्गन्धैस्तथा माल्यैः कन्याभिश्चाभिनन्दितः॥ युधिष्ठिरस्य चरणावभिवाद्य कृताञ्जलिः। तेन मूर्धन्युपाघ्रात आरुरोह महारथम्॥ ततस्ते वाजिनो हृष्टाः सुपुष्टाः वातरंहसः। अजय्या जैत्रमूहुस्तं विकुर्वाणाः स्म सैन्धवाः॥
en: Handsome damsels then adored him by covering him with a shower of fried paddy, perfumes and garlands of flowers. Thereafter that brave warrior with folded palms worshipped Yudhishthira's feet; whereupon the latter smelt his head. Having undergone all these ceremonies he mounted his chariot. Thereafter those horses, cheerful, plump, of the fleetness of the wind. Invincible in battle and of the Sindhu breed, were on the point of dragging that excellent chariot of Satyaki. Bhimasena also similarly, honoured by the very virtuous king Yudhishthira.

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: तथैव भीमसेनोऽपि धर्मराजेन पूजितः। प्रायात् सात्यकिना सार्धभिवाद्य युधिष्ठिरम्॥
en: Set out with Satyaki, after having duly saluted the king (Yudhishthira). Beholding these two scorchers of foes cast their glances on your army.

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: तौ हृष्टवा प्रविविक्षन्तौ तव सेनामरिंदमौ। संयत्तास्तावकाः सर्वे तस्थुट्टैणपुरोगमाः॥
en: All your warriors ranged against them with Drona at their head, stood still and motionless. Then beholding Bhima accoutered in mail follow him from behind.

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: संनद्धमनुगच्छन्तं दृष्टवा भीमं स सात्यकिः। अभिनन्द्याब्रवीद् वीरस्तदा हर्षकरं वचः॥ त्वं भीम रक्ष राजानमेतत् कार्यतमं हि ते। अहं भित्त्वा प्रवक्ष्यामि कालपक्वमिदं बलम्॥
en: The heroic Satyaki saluting him said these delightful words. Then Satyaki with his person filled with delight, spoke these very words addressing Bhima-"O Bhima, do you protect the king, even this is your duty. I will proceed along penetrating through this host whose hour has come;

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: आयत्यां च तदात्वे च श्रेयो राज्ञोऽभिरक्षणम्। जानीषे मम वीर्ये त्वं तव चाहमरिंदम॥
en: At present and in all future periods, it should be your first duty to protect the king. You know my prowess and I all know yours, O Subduer of foe.

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: तस्माद् भीम निवर्तख मम चेदिच्छसि प्रियम्। तथोक्तः सात्यकिं प्राह व्रज त्वं कार्यसिद्धये॥
en: Therefore, O Bhima, turn back, if you, desire to do my good.” Thus spoken to Bhima replied to Satyaki saying “Go you then and be victorious and successful!

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: अहं राज्ञः करिष्यामि रक्षां पुरुषसत्तम। एवमुक्तः प्रत्युवाच भीमेसनं स माधवः॥
en: O foremost of men, I will protect the king to the best of my prowess." "Being thus addressed he of Madhu's race, replied to Bhimasena sayingगच्छ गच्छ ध्रुवं पार्थ ध्रुवो हि विजयो मम।

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: यन्मे गुणानुरक्तश्च त्वमद्य वशमास्थितः॥
en: "Turn back, turn back, O son of Pritha; my victory today is certain in as much as you, won over by my merits, are now intent to carry out my wishes.

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: निमित्तानि च धन्यानि यथा भीम वदन्ति माम्। निहते सैन्धवे पापे पाण्डवेन महात्मना॥
en: These auspicious omens also indicate my victory. When the sinful ruler of the Sindhus will be slain by the high-souled son of Pandu (Arjuna).

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: परिष्वजिष्ये राजानं धर्मात्मानं युधिष्ठिरम्। एतावदुक्त्वा भीमं तु विसृज्य च महायशाः॥ सम्प्रेक्षत् तावकं सैन्यं व्याघ्रो मृगगणानिव।
en: I shall embrace the illustrious king viz., Yudhishthira.” Having thus spoken to Bhima, the high-famed Satyaki left him. He then cast his eyes on your troops like a tiger looking at herds of deer.

description: The penetration of Satyaki into the Kaurava troops
sn: तं दृष्ट्वा प्रविविक्षन्तं सैन्यं तव जनाधिप॥ भूय एवाभवन्मूढं सुभृशं चाप्यकम्पत। ततः प्रयातः सहसा तव सैन्यं स सात्यकिः॥ दिहक्षुरर्जुनं राजन् धर्मराजस्य शासनात्।
en: once more O ruler of men, beholding him look at your army, your soldiers became confounded and they began to tremble. Thereafter Satyaki suddenly assailed your troops, desirous of meeting Arjuna, commanded by the virtuous king Yudhishthira to do so. once more O ruler of men, beholding him look at your army, your soldiers became confounded and they began to tremble. Thereafter Satyaki suddenly assailed your troops, desirous of meeting Arjuna, commanded by the virtuous king Yudhishthira to do so.
