en: Then excited to the highest pitch of fury, Satyaki struck Drona in battle with mine shafts of depressed knots. He also struck with sharp shafts, the standard.

sn: सारथिं च शतेनैव भारद्वाजस्य पश्यतः। लाघवं युयुधानस्य दृष्ट्वा द्रोणो महारथः॥
en: And charioteer of Drona, before his very eyes. Then beholding the lightness of hands displayed by Yuyudhana, the mighty carwarrior Drona.

sn: सप्तत्या सारथिं विद्ध्वा तुरङ्गांश्चत्रिस्त्रिभिः। ध्वजमेकेन चिच्छेद माधवस्य रथे स्थितम्॥
en: Piercing the charioteer of him of Madhu's race with seventy arrows and the horses with three arrows each, cut-off his standard with a single arrows.

sn: अथापरेण भल्लेन हेमपुखेन पत्रिणा। धनुचिच्छेद समरे माधवस्य महात्मनः॥
en: Then with another broad-headed shaft equipped with golden wings, he curt off bow of that illustrious descendant of Madhu's race.

sn: सात्यकिस्तुततःक्रुद्धो धनुस्त्यक्त्वा महारथः। गदां जग्राह महती भारद्वाजाय चाक्षिपत्॥
en: Thereat that mighty car-warrior Satyaki highly excited with rage, laid aside his bow and taking up a mighty mace, hurled it at the son of Bharadvaja.

sn: तामापतन्ती सहसा पट्टबद्धामयस्मयीम्। न्यवारयच्छरैद्रोणो बहुभिर्बहुरूपिभिः॥
en: Then Drona with numerous shafts of various appearance, baffled that mace made of iron and covered with silken cloth, as it coursed vehemently towards him.

sn: अथान्यद् धनुरादाय सात्यकिः सत्यविक्रमः। बिव्याध बहुभिर्वीरं भारद्वाजं शिलाशितैः॥
en: Thereafter Satyaki of prowess incapable of being baffled taking up another bow, pierced the heroic son of Bharadvaja with numerous shafts whetted on stone.

sn: स विद्ध्वा समरे द्रोणं सिंहनादममुञ्चत। तं वै न ममृषे द्रोणः सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वरः॥
en: Thus wounding Drona in battle he sent up his war-cry. But Drona that foremost of all wielders of weapons did not brook that war-cry of his.

sn: ततः शक्तिं गृहीत्वा तु रुक्मदण्डामयस्मयीम्। तरसा प्रेषयामास माधवस्य रथं प्रति॥
en: Then taking up a lance of golden staff and iron-head, Drona hurled it vchemently at the car of that descendant of Madhu's race (Satyaki).

sn: अनासाद्य तु शैनेयं सा शक्तिः कालसंनिभा। भित्त्वा रथं जगामोग्रा धरणी दारुणस्वना॥
en: That lance resembling the Destroyer himself, without reaching the grandson of Sini, penetrated through his chariot and then fell on the ground, looking fierce and emitting a loud noise.

sn: ततोद्रोणं शिने:पौत्रो राजन् विव्याध पत्रिणा। दक्षिणं भुजमासाद्य पीडयन् भरतर्षभ॥
en: Thereafter ( king, Sini's grandson pierced Drona on his right arin with many winged shafts. Thus, O foremost of the Bharatas, Drona was greatly afflicted,

sn: द्रोणोऽपि समरे राजन् माधवस्य महद् धनुः। अर्धचन्द्रेण चिच्छेद रथशक्त्वा च सारथिम्॥
en: In that battle Drona also, O king, with a crescent-shaped arrow cut-off the mighty bow of that descendant of Madhava; and he smote the latter's driver with a lance.

sn: मुमोह सारथिस्तस्य रथशक्त्या समाहतः। स रथोपस्थमासाद्य मुहूर्त संन्यषीदत॥
en: Satyaki's charioteer was then overwhelmed with a swoon in consequent of his being struck with that dart. For a while, he lay senseless on his niche on the car.

sn: चकार सात्यकी राजन् सूतकर्मातिमानुषम्। अयोधयच यद् द्रोणं रश्मीञ्जग्राह च स्वयम्॥
en: Then, o king, Satyaki achieved a superhuman feat, in as much as he fought on with Drona and held the reins of his horse like his driver simultaneously.

sn: ततः शरशतेनैव युयुधानो महारथः। अविध्यद् ब्राह्मणं संख्ये दृष्टरूपो विशाम्पते॥
en: Then, O ruler of men, with a cheerful appearance, the mighty car-warrior Yuyudhana, pierced in that that battle that Brahmana with a set of hundred arrows.

sn: तस्य द्रोणः शरान् पञ्च चप्रेषयामास भारत। ते घोराः कवचं भित्त्वा पपुः शोणितमाहवे॥
en: At him then Drona sped, O Bharata, five shafts and those dreadful shaft penetrating through his armour drank his life-blood.

sn: निर्विद्धस्तु शरैोरैरक्रुद्ध्यत् सात्यकि शम्। सायकान् व्यसृजचापि वीरो रुक्मरथं प्रति॥
en: Pierced deeply with those fierce arrows Satyaki became exited to the highest pitch of Wrath; and then that hero began to shoot numerous arrows at him of the golden car.

sn: ततो द्रोणस्य यन्तारं निपात्यैकेषुणा भुवि। अश्वान् व्यद्रावयद् बाणैर्हतसूतांस्ततस्ततः॥
en: He then felled Drona's driver by striking him with a single arrow; then with other arrows, he compelled his horses to run away from the field.

sn: स रथः प्रद्रुतः संख्ये मण्डलानि सहस्रशः। चकार राजतो राजन् भ्राजमान इवांशुमान्॥
en: That resplendent chariot, Oking, dragged over all parts of the field, began to describe various circles like the Sun in motion.

sn: अभिद्रवत गृह्णीत हयान् द्रोणस्य धावत। इति स्म चुक्रुशुः सर्वे राजपुत्राः सराजकाः॥
en: 'Rush,' 'seize the running steeds of Drona,' these were the words that were then uttered loudly by the kings and princes of the Kaurava host.

sn: ते सात्यकिमपास्याशु राजन् युधि महारथाः। यतो द्रोणस्ततः सर्वे सहसा समुपाद्रवन्॥
en: O king, then all those mighty car-warriors, leaving Satyaki in battle, proceeded to the spot where Drona was carried away by his horses.

sn: तान् दृष्ट्वाप्रदुतान् संख्ये सात्वतेन शरार्दितान्। प्रभग्नं पुनरेवासीत् तव सैन्यं समाकुलम्॥
en: Then once more seeing all those heroes routed and afflicted by the scion of the Satvata race, your troops once more began to give way, being overwhelmed with fear.

sn: व्यूहस्यैव पुनरं गत्वा द्रोणो व्यवस्थितः। वातायमानैस्तैरश्वैर्नीतो वृष्णिशरार्दितैः॥
en: Drona, once more proceeding to the gate of the array of his troops, stationed himself there, borne away, as he was, by those steeds of the fleetness of the wind, that had been afflicted by the shafts of the Vrishni hero.

sn: पाण्डुपाञ्चालसम्भिन्नं व्यूहमालोक्य वीर्यवान्। शैनेये नाकरोद् यत्नं व्यूहमेवाभ्यरक्षत॥
en: Then that highly puissant Drona, seeing his array shattered by the Pandavas and the Panchalas, did not try to check the grandson of Sini, but began to re-arrange his broken array.

sn: निवार्य पाण्डुपञ्चालान् द्रोणाग्निः प्रदहनिव। तस्थौ क्रोधेमसंदीप्तः कालसूर्य इवोद्यतः॥
en: Resisting the Pandavas and the Panchalas, the Drona-fire then, burning in rage, stationed himself there, consuming everything like the Sun that rises at the end of a Yuga.

sn: संजय उवाच स्तथैव हार्दिक्यमुखांस्त्वदीयान्। प्रहस्य सूतं वचनं बभाषे शिनिप्रवीरः कुरुपुङ्गवाय॥
en: Sanjaya said Having defeated in battle Drona and other warriors of your army headed by Hridika's son, that foremost of men, that best scion of the Sini race, addressing smilingly his charioteer, said, O best of the Kurus, these wordsनिमित्तमात्रं वयमद्य सूत दग्धारयः केशवफाल्गुनाभ्याम्

sn: हतान् निहन्मेह नरर्षभेण वयं सुरेशात्मसमुद्भवेन॥
en: O charioteer, our opponents have already heen consumed by Keshava and Phalguna. In defeating them again, we have only been (secondarily) instrumental. Slaying them already slain by that foremost of men, viz., the son of the celestial chief, we have but slain the slain.

sn: तमेवमुक्त्वा शिनिपुङ्गवस्तदा महामृधे सोऽग्र्यधनुर्धरोऽरिहा। किरन् समन्तात् सहसा शरान् बली समापतच्छ्येन इवामिषं यथा।॥
en: Saying these words to his driver, that best of the Sinis, that illustrious bowman, that slayer of hostile heroes, that highly puissant warrior, shooting vehemently his arrows in all directions pounced upon the Kaurava host like a hawk swooping down upon a piece of meat.

sn: विगाह्य सैन्यं पुरुषप्रवीरम्। नाशक्नुवन् वारयितुं समन्ता दादित्यरश्मिप्रतिमं रथाग्र्यम्॥
en: The warriors of the Kaurava army, although they assailed him from all sides, were unable to resist that best of car-warriors resembling the thousand-rayed sun himself, that foremost of men, who having penetrated through the Kaurava array, was advancing, borne by his excellent steeds that were white like the moon or he conch-shell.

sn: असह्यविक्रान्तमदीनसत्त्वं सर्वे गणा भारत ये त्वदीयाः। सहस्रनेत्रप्रतिमप्रभावं दिवीव सूर्यं जलदव्यपाये॥
en: O Bharata, none amongst your warriors was then able to resist Yuyudhana of prowess incapable of being withstood, of unmitigating energy, of heroism equal to that of the thousand-eyed deity, looking like the autumnal sun in the firmament.

sn: अमर्षपूर्णस्त्वतिचित्रयोधी शरासनी काञ्चनवर्मधारी। सुदर्शनः सात्यकिमापतन्तं न्यवारयद् राजवरः प्रसह्य॥
en: Thereupon that foremost of kings, named Sudarsana, versed in all modes of warfare, clad in golden armour, armed with the bow and the arrows and inspired with wrath, proceeded against the dashing Satyaki and strove to check his career.

sn: तयोरभूद् भारत सम्प्रहारः सुदारुणस्तं समतिप्रशंसन्। योधास्त्वदीयाश्च हि सोमकाश्च वृत्रेन्द्रयोयुद्धमिवामरौघाः॥
en: The encounter that then commenced between them was extremely awful. Both your warriors and the Somakas applauded it highly; and the immortals compared it to the one that took place in days gone by between Vritra and Indra.

sn: शरैः सुतीक्ष्णैःशतशोऽभ्यविध्यत् सुदर्शन: सात्वतमुख्यमाजौ। श्चिच्छेद राजशिनिपुङ्गवोऽपि॥
en: Sudarsana striving hard sped at that foremost descendant of the Satvata race, hundreds of sharp arrows, but O king, that illustrious scion of the Sini race, cut down all those arrows, before they could ever reach him.

sn: तथैव शक्रप्रतिमोऽपि सात्यकिः सुदर्शने यान् क्षिपति स्म सायकान्। द्विधा त्रिधा तानकरोत् सुदर्शन: शरोत्तमैः स्यन्दनवर्यमास्थितः॥
en: So also did, Sudarsana, riding on his own chariot of excellent make, severed, by means of his own arrows, in two or three parts, all the arrows sped at him by Satyaki who resembled Indra himself.

sn: तान् वीक्ष्य बाणान् निहतांस्तदानीं सुदर्शन: सात्यकिबाणबेगैः। क्रोधाद् दिधक्षन्निव तिग्मतेजाः शरानमुञ्चत् तपनीयचित्रान्॥
en: Then beholding his own arrows repulsed by the force of those shot by Satyaki, Sudarsana of fierce energy in order to burn down his adversary, angrily shot some beautiful shafts equipped with wings of gold.

sn: राकर्णपूर्णैर्निशितैः सुपुजैः। विव्याध देहावरण विभिद्य ते सात्यकेराविविशुः शरीरम्॥
en: Then he pierced his adversary with three beautiful arrows resembling fire itself and furnished with golden wings, discharged from the bowstring drawn back to the very ear. These arrows penetrating through Satyaki's armour mangled his body.

sn: तथैव तस्यावनिपालपुत्रः संधाय बाणैरपरैवलद्भिः। श्चतुर्भिरश्वांश्चतुरः प्रसह्य॥
en: Once more that prince Sudarsana, fixing on his bowstring another four resplendent shafts, struck therewith the four steeds of Satyaki that were of argentine huc.

sn: तथा तु तेनाभिहतस्तरस्वी नप्ता शिनेरिन्द्रसमानवीर्यः। हयान् निहत्याशु ननाद नादम्॥
en: Thus afflicted by him, Sini's grandson, possessed of great agility and endowed with might equal to that of Indra himself, quickly slew with his own arrows the steeds of Sudarsana and sent up (then) a loud war-cry.

sn: अथास्य सूतस्य शिरो निकृत्य भल्लेन शक्राशनिसंनिभेन। सुदर्शनस्यापि शिनिप्रवीरः क्षुरेण कालानलसंनिभेन॥ सकुण्डलं पूर्णशशिप्रकाशं भ्राजिष्णु वक्त्रं विचकर्त देहात्। यथा पुरा वज्रधरः प्रसह्य बलस्य संख्येऽतिबलस्य राजन्॥
en: Then lopping off with a bhalla charged with the vehemence of Indra's thunder-bolt, the head of Sudarsana's charioteer, that best of the Sinis, with a razor-headed arrow resembling the fire that appears at the end of a Yuga, cutoff from Sudarsana's trunk his head graced with ear-rings, resembling the full moon and decked with an exceedingly charming face, like the wiclder of the thunder-bolt, 0 king, forcibly cutting off in day's gone by, the head of the Asura bala in battle.

sn: निहत्य तं पार्थिवपुत्रपौत्रं रणे यदूनामृषभस्तरस्वी। मुदा समेतः परया महात्मा रराज राजन् सुरराजकल्पः॥
en: Thus having slain that grandson of a prince, that illustrious Scion of the Yadu race became inspired with joy and shone resplendent, O king, like the chief of the celestials himself.

sn: ततो ययावर्जुन एव येन निबार्य सैन्य तव मार्गणौधैः। ल्लोकं विसिस्मापयिषुर्दैवीरः॥
en: Then that best hero among men viz., Yuyudhana proceeded along the track by which Arjuna had gone before him, resisting as he advanced, by means of his myriad shafts, all your warriors and riding on that excellent chariot of his, O king, to which were yoked those best steeds and filling every body with wonder.

sn: तत् तस्य विस्मापयनीयमय मपूजयन् योधबराः समेताः। प्रवर्तमानानिषुगोचरेऽरीन् ददाह बाणैर्तुतभुग् यथैव॥
en: Then all the excellent warriors assembled on the field of battle, applauded that wonderful feat achieved by Satyaki, inasmuch as he consumed all opponents that came within the range of his arrows, like a blazing conflagration burning everything that falls in its way.

sn: संजय उवाच ततः स सात्यकिर्थीमान् महात्मावृष्णिपुङ्गवः। सुदर्शनं निहत्याजौ यन्तारं पुनरब्रवीत्॥
en: Sanjaya said Thereafter that illustrious scion of the Vrishni race, the high-souled and intelligent Satyaki, having slain Sudarsana in battle, addressing charioteer thus spoke.

sn: रथाश्वनागकलिलं शरशक्त्यूमिमालिनम्। खङ्गमत्स्यं गदाग्राहं शूरायुधमहास्वनम्॥ प्राणापहारिणं रौद्रं वादिवोत्क्रुष्टनादितम्। योधानामसुखस्पर्शे दुर्धर्षमजयैषिणाम्॥ तीर्णाः स्म दुस्तरं तात द्रोणानीकमहार्णवम्। जलसंधबलेनाजौ पुरुषादैरिवावृतम्॥ अतोऽन्यत् पृतनाशेषं मन्ये कुनदिकामिव। तर्तव्यामल्पसलिलां चोदयाश्वानसम्भ्रमम्॥
en: Having crossed the almost uncrossable ocean of Drona's division abounding with chariots and steeds and elephants-ocean of which the waves are constituted by arrows and darts, fishes by swords and scimitars and alligators by the maccs; which roars with the whizz of arrows and the clash of diverse weapons, an ocean that is fierce and destructive of life and resounds with the din created by diverse musical instruments; of which the touch is disagreeable and unbearable to warriors longing to have victory and of which the banks infested by flesh-eaters represented by the forces of Jalasandha, I consider that the remaining of the array yet to be crossed, can be crossed with great ease, like a stream-let of shallow water. Therefore do you dauntlessly drive the steeds forwards.

sn: हस्तप्राप्तमहं मन्ये साम्प्रतं सव्यसाचिनम्। निर्जित्य दुर्घरं द्रोणं सपदानुगमाहवे॥
en: I think I am now within a hand's distance from Savyasachin. Having vanquished in are battle, the indomitable Drona together with his followers.

sn: हार्दिक्यं योधवर्ये च मन्ये प्राप्तं धनंजयम्। न हि मे जायते त्रासो दृष्ट्वा सैन्यान्यनेकशः॥
en: As also that best of all warriors namely, the son of Hridika, I think I have already reached Dhananjaya. Though I see these numerous divisions of troops before me, fear does not assail my heart.

sn: वढेरिव प्रदीप्तस्य वने शुष्कतृणोलपे। पश्य पाण्डवमुख्येन यातां भूमि किरीटिना॥
en: For a raging forests conflagration shrinks not at the sight of numerous heaps of dried grass. Behold the ground through which the diadem-decked Arjuna, that best of the Pandavas has passed.

sn: पत्त्यश्वरथनागौघैः पतितैर्विषमीकृताम्। द्रवते तद् यथा सैन्यं तेन भग्नं महात्मना॥
en: Rendered uneven by the slain foot-soldiers, horses, car-warriors and elephants. Yonder the Kaurava array is giving way being routed by that high-souled warrior.

sn: रथैविपरिधावद्भिर्गजैरश्चैश्च सारथे। कौशेयारुणसंकाशमेतदुद्भूयते रजः॥
en: O charioteer, behold a thick tawny cloud of dust raised by the flying cars, elephants and steeds.

sn: अभ्याशस्थमहं मन्ये श्वेताश्वं कृष्णासारथिम्। स एष श्रूयते शब्दो गाण्डीवस्यामितौजसः॥
en: I think myself to be very near to that one of white steeds whose charioteer in Krishna, inasmuch as I hear the twang of the bow Gandiva wielded by that one of infinite prowess.

sn: यादृशानि निमित्तानि मम प्रादुर्भवन्ति वै। अनस्तंगत आदित्ये हन्ता सैन्धवमर्जुनः॥
en: From the omens that are revealing themselves to me, I can judge that Arjuna will slay the ruler of the Sindhus before the sun today goes below the horizon.

sn: शनैर्विश्रम्भयन्नश्वान् याहि यत्रारिवाहिनी। यौते सतलत्राणाः सुयोधनपुरोगमाः॥
en: Without exhausting their strength, drive the steeds slowly to the spot where the hostile ranks are staying, that is, to the spot where yonder warriors headed by Duryodhana, their hands cased in leathern fences

sn: दंशिताः क्रूरकर्माणः काम्बोजा युद्धदुर्मदाः। शरबाणासनधरा यवनाश्च प्रहारिणः॥
en: And yonder Kambojas of dreadful deeds, cased in mail and difficult of defeat in battle and these Yavanas armed with bows and arrows and accomplished in smiting.

sn: शकाः किराता दरदा बर्बरास्ताम्रलिप्तकाः। अन्ये च बहवो म्लेच्छा विविधायुधपामयः॥
en: And yonder Sakas and Kiratas and Daradas and Barbaras and Tamraliptakas and numerous other Mlechchas armed with diverse weapons are staying.

sn: यौते सतलत्राणाः सुयोधनपुरोगमाः। मामेवाभिमुखाः सर्वे तिष्ठन्ति समरार्थिनः॥
en: To the spot (I repeat) where yonder warriors headed by Duryodhana, their hands defended by leathern gloves, are standing with their faces turned towards me and inspired with the resolution of encountering me.

sn: एतान् सरथनागाश्वान् निहत्याजौ सपत्तिनः। इदं दुर्गे महाघोरं तीर्णमेवोपधारय॥
en: Consider me, O charioteer as already passed through this dreadful strong-hold, having slain in battle all these warriors and cars, elephants, horses and foot-soldiers that are among them.

sn: सूत उवाच न सम्भ्रमो मे वार्ष्णेय विद्यते सत्यविक्रम। यद्यपि स्यात् तव क्रुद्धो जामदग्न्योऽग्रतः स्थितः॥
en: The Charioteer said O scion of the Vrishni race, fear I have none, O you of prowess incapable of being withstood! If you had before you the enraged son of Yamadagni.

sn: द्रोणो वा रथिनां श्रेष्ठः कृपो मद्रेश्वरोऽपि वा। तथापि सम्भ्रमो न स्यात् त्वामाश्रित्य महाभुज॥
en: Or Drona that foremost of car-warriors or Kripa or the ruler of the Madras himself, even then fear would not enter my heart, O you of mighty arms, as long as I am under the shadow of your protection.

sn: त्वया सुबहवो युद्धे निर्जिताः शत्रुसूदन। दंशिताः क्रूरकर्माणः काम्बोजा युद्धदुर्मदाः॥
en: O slayer of hostile heroes, numerous Kambojas covered in coats of mail, of dreadful deeds and difficult of defeat in battle, have already been worsted by you;

sn: शरबाणासनधरा यवनाश्च प्रहारिणः। शकाः किराता दरदा बर्बरास्ताम्रलिप्तकाः॥
en: As also numerous Yavanas armed with bow and arrows and accomplished in smiting, including Sakas, Kiratas, Daradas Barbars, Tamraliptakas.

sn: अन्ये च बहवो म्लेच्छा विविधायुधपाणयः। न च मे सम्भ्रमः कश्चिद् भूतपूर्वः कथंचन॥
en: And many other Miechchas, armed with various weapons. Never did I feel fear in any battle.

sn: किमुतैतत् समासाद्य धीरसंयुगगोष्पदम्। आयुष्मन् कतरेण त्वां प्रापयामि धनंजयम्॥
en: O you of great courage, why shall I then experience any fear in this battle, which is like the vestige of a cow's hoof. O long-lived one, by which track shall I carry you to the spot where Dhananjaya is?

sn: केषां क्रुद्धोऽसि वार्ष्णेय केषां मृत्युरुपस्थितः। केषां संयमनीमद्य गन्तुमुत्सहते मनः॥
en: On whom have you been angry, O you of the Vrishni race? Who are they for whom death is waiting? Who are they that are destined to repair to the mansion of death today?

sn: के त्वां युधि पराक्रान्तं कालान्तकयमोपमम्। दृष्ट्वा विक्रमसम्पन्नं विद्रविष्यन्ति संयुगे॥ केषां वैवस्वतो राजा स्मरतेऽद्य महाभुज।
en: Who are they that will fly away from the field of battle beholding you endowed with such prowess, resembling the Destroyer himself as he appears at the end of the Yuga and putting forth that prowess of yours? O you of mighty arms who are they whoin king Vaivasvat, has remembered today?

sn: सात्यकिरुवाच मुण्डानेतान् हनिष्यामि दानवानिव वासवः॥ प्रतिज्ञा पारयिष्यानि काम्बोजानेव मां वह।
en: Satyaki said I will slay these warriors with sharpened shafts like Vasava slaying the Danavas. Slaying the Kambojas, I will fulfill my vow. Carry me thither.

sn: अद्यैषां कदनं कृत्वा प्रियं यास्यामि पाण्डवम्॥ अद्य द्रक्ष्यन्ति मे वीर्ये कौरवाः ससुयोधनाः।
en: Today crushing the foe I shall repair to that son of Pandu who is dearly loved my me. Today the Kurus with Suyodhana at their head, will bchold my prowess in battle.

sn: मुण्डानीके हते सूत सर्वसैन्येषु चासकृत्॥ अद्य कौरवसैन्यस्य दीर्यमाणस्य संयुगे। श्रुत्वा विरावं बहुधा संतप्स्यति सुयोधनः॥ अद्य पाण्डवमुख्यस्य श्वेताश्वस्य महात्मनः। आचार्यस्य कृतं मार्गे दर्शयिष्यामि संयुगे॥ अद्य माणनिहतान् योधमुख्यान् सहस्रशः। दृष्ट्वा दुर्योधनो राजा पश्चात्तापं गमिष्यति॥ अद्य मे क्षिप्रहस्तस्य क्षिपतः सायकोत्तमान्। अलातचक्रप्रतिमं धनुर्द्रक्ष्यन्ति कौरवाः॥ मत्सायकचिताङ्गानां रुधिरं स्रवता मुहुः। सैनिकानां वधं दृष्ट्वा संतप्स्यति सुयोधनः॥
en: When this division of the Mlecnchas of shaved heads will be exterminated and the entire Kaurava army put to great distress. Hearing the loud lamentation of the Kaurava host today lacerated and shattered by me in battle, Suyodhana will be filled with great fcar. Today I shall show to my precep:or. the highsouled Pandava of white horse skill in in use of weapons acquired by fie from him Beholding today thousands of forcnes: warriors slain with Duryodhana will be overwhelmed with 21. The Kauravas will this day bozoid the bow in my hand to resemble a circle of fire whe:1, nav arrows. string for discharging my numerous arrows. Beholding the continuous carnage of his troops bathed in blood and many filled all over with shafts, Suyodhana today will be filled with great grief. When I shall slay the best of the Kuru warriors wrathfully.

sn: अद्य मे क्रुद्धरूपस्य निघ्नतश्च वरान् वरान्। द्विरर्जुनमिमं लोकं मंस्यतेऽद्य सुयोधनः॥ अद्य राजसहस्राणि निहतानि मया रणे। दृष्ट्वा दुर्योधनो राजा संतप्स्यति महामृधे॥ अध स्नेहं च भक्तिं च पाण्डवेषु महात्मसु। हत्त्वा राजसहस्राणि दर्शयिष्यामि राजसु॥ वलं वीर्ये क-तज्ञत्वं मम ज्ञास्यन्ति कौरवाः
en: Suyodhana will today behold the world to contain two Arjunas. Beholding thousands of kings slain by me in battle, king Duryodhana will be overwhelmed with grief in this day's great fight. Slaying thousands of monarchs today, I will show love and devotion to those high-souled ones viz., the sons of Pandu. Today the Kauravas will know the extent of my prowess and energy and my gratefulness to the Pandavas.

sn: संजय उवाच एवमुक्तस्तदा सूत: शिक्षितान् साधुवाहिनः॥ शशाङ्कसंनिकाशान् वै वाजिनो व्यनुदद् भृशम्।
en: Sanjaya continued Thus spoken to, the charioteer quickly drove those well-trained steeds resembling the moon in huc and carrying the warrior Satyaki well.

sn: ते पिवन्त इवाकाशं युयुधानं हयोत्तमाः॥ प्रापयन् यवनाशीघ्रं मन:पवनरंहसः।
en: Those excellent steeds, possessed of the fleetness of the wind or the mind, dashed forward scanning to devour the very skies and bore Yuyudhana to the spot where those Vas were,

sn: त्यांक ते समासाद्य पृतनास्वनिवर्तिनम्॥ वहवो लघुहस्ताश्च शरवधैरवाकिरन्।
en: Then thosc Yavanas endued with great lightness of hunds obtaining in their midst the unretreating Satyaki, began to cover him with mighty showers of arrows.

sn: तेषामिषूनथास्त्राणि वेगवान् नतपर्वभिः॥ अच्छिनत् सात्यकी राजन् नैनं ते प्राप्नुव-शराः।
en: Then Satyaki who was moving with great celerity, cul-off their arrows and weapons with his shafts of depressed knots. Indeed the arrows discharged by them could not then reach him.

sn: रुक्मपुत्रैः सुनिशितैर्गापत्रैरजिह्मगैः॥ उचकर्त शिरांस्युग्रो यवनानां भुजानपि।
en: The fierce Satyaki then began to lop off the heads and arms of the Yavanas, with sharp arrows cquipt with golden wings or wings made of vultering feathers, all-flying straight.

sn: सैक्यायसानि वर्माणि कांस्यानि च समन्ततः॥ भित्त्वा देहांस्तथा तेषां शरा जग्मुर्महीतलम्।
en: Those arrows, penetrating through the iron or brass armours of the Yavanas as also their bodies, then fell down on the earth.

sn: तेहन्यमाना वीरेणम्लेच्छाः सात्यकिना रणे॥ शतशोऽभ्यपतंस्तत्र व्यसवो बसुधातले।
en: Thus slaughtered by the heroic Satyaki in that haitle, the Mlechchas began to fall by inundreds on the ground deprived of their lives.

sn: सुपूर्णायतमुक्तैस्ताव्यवच्छिन्नपिण्डितैः॥ पञ्च षट् सप्त चाष्टौ च बिभेद यवनाशरैः।
en: With his arrows disc!larged from his bow drawn to the fullest exicnt and flying in a continuous line, that brave warrior began to slay, five, six, seven or eight Yavanas at a time.

sn: काम्बोजाना सहस्त्रैश्च शकानां च विशाम्पते॥ शबराणां किरातानां बर्वराणां तथैव च।
en: With the dead bodies of hundreds and thousands of Kambojas, Sakas, Souviras, Trgartas andri ruler of men.

sn: अगम्यरूपा पृधिवा यशाणातकर्दमाम्॥ कृतवांस्तत्र शैनयः क्षपयंस्तावकं बलम्।
en: The carth became impassable; and it was slippery with the flesh and blond that then constitutcoins mire. The grandson of Sini then cabut carnage amous pour troops.

sn: दस्यूना सशिरस्त्राणैः शिरोभिनमूर्धजैः। :।।४ दीर्घकूचैर्मही कीर्णा विबहरण्डजैरिव।
en: The ground was then strewn over with the head-gears of those robbers and the shaved heads that looked like unfledged birds in consequence of their long beards.

sn: रुधिरोक्षितसर्वाङ्गैस्तैस्तदायोधन बभौ॥ कबन्धैः संवृतं सर्वे ताम्राभैः खमिबावृतम्।
en: The field of battle overspread with headless trunks bathed in blood, appeared charming like the firmament overspread with coppery clouds.

sn: बज्राशनिसमस्पर्शः सुपर्वभिरजिह्मगैः॥ ते सात्वतेन निहताः समावबुर्वसुंधराम्।
en: Slain with the shafts of the heroic Satyaki, shafts whose touch resembled the thunderbolt's stroke and whose knots were wellpressed and which were flying in straight lines, the Yavanas covered the field of battle over.

sn: अल्पावशिष्टाः सम्भग्नाः कृच्छ्रप्राणा विचेतसः॥ जिता: संख्ये महाराज युयुधानेन दंशिताः।
en: The handful remnant of those mail-covered soldiers, defeated, O king, by the Satvata hero, became cheerless; and finding their lives on the points of being snatched away from them, they broke.

sn: पाणिभिश्च कशाभिश्च ताडयन्तस्तुरङ्गमान्॥ जवमुत्तममास्थाय सर्वतः प्राद्रवन् भयात्।
en: And fled away, urging, their steeds to the top of their speed, with their whips, goads & c out of great fear that then overwhelmed them.

sn: काम्बोजसैन्यं विद्राव्य दुर्जयं युधि भारत॥ यवनानां च तत् सैन्यं शकानां च महद् बलम्।
en: Routing in battle the invisible Kamboja troops and 0 Bharata, the troops of the Yavanas and the mighty host of the Sakas.

sn: ततः स पुरुषव्याघ्रः सात्यकिः सत्यविक्रमः॥ प्रविष्टस्तावकाञ्जित्वा सूतं याहीत्यचोदयत्।
en: That foremost of men, viz... Satyaki of prowess incapable of being baffled, penetrated into the heart of your troops, vanquishing them and urging his charioteer saying, "Proceed."

sn: तत् तस्य समरे कर्म दृष्ट्वान्यैरकृतं पुरा॥ चारणां सहगन्धर्वाः पूजयाञ्चक्रिरे भृशम्।
en: Beholding that feat achieved in battle by him-fcat that nobody before ever performed, the Charanas and the Gandharvas began to applaud him highly.

sn: तं यान्तं पृष्ठगोप्तारमर्जुनस्य विशाम्पते। चारणा: प्रेक्ष्य संहृष्टास्त्वदीयाश्चाभ्यपूजयन्॥
en: Then, O ruler of men, beholding him proceeding as the rear-guard of Arjuna, the Charanas were filled with delight. Even your troops then began to applaud him.

sn: तत् तस्य समरे कर्म दृष्ट्वान्यैरकृतं पुरा॥ चारणां सहगन्धर्वाः पूजयाञ्चक्रिरे भृशम्।
en: Beholding that feat achieved in battle by him-fcat that nobody before ever performed, the Charanas and the Gandharvas began to applaud him highly.

sn: तं यान्तं पृष्ठगोप्तारमर्जुनस्य विशाम्पते। चारणा: प्रेक्ष्य संहृष्टास्त्वदीयाश्चाभ्यपूजयन्॥
en: Then, O ruler of men, beholding him proceeding as the rear-guard of Arjuna, the Charanas were filled with delight. Even your troops then began to applaud him.

sn: संजय उवाच जित्वा यवन काम्बोजान् युयुधानस्ततोऽर्जुनम्। जगाम तव सैन्यस्य मध्येन रतिनां वरः॥
en: Sanjaya said Having defeated the Yavanas and the Kambojas that foremost of car-warriors Yuyudhana advanced after Arjuna right through the centre of your troops.

sn: चारुदंष्ट्रो नरव्याघ्रो विचित्रकवचध्वजः। मृगं व्याघ्र इवाजिघ्रंस्तव सैन्यमभीषयत्॥
en: Then like a huntsman slaying dcer, that foremost of men, viz., Satyaki, graced with beautiful teeth, cased in exceilent armour and owning a beautiful standard, slew the Kaurava troops and struck terror into their hearts.

sn: स रथेन चरन् मार्गान् धनुरभ्रामयद् भृशम्। रुक्मपृष्ठं महावेगं रुक्मचन्द्रकसंकुलम्॥
en: Advancing on his chariot, he began to shake his bow with force, bow the back of which was decked with gold, the toughness of which as great and which was beautified with golden moons.

sn: रुक्माङ्गदशिस्त्राणो रुक्मवर्मसमावृतः। रुक्मध्वजधनुः शूरो मेरुशृङ्गमिवाबभौ॥
en: His arms adorned with golden Angadas, his turban decked with gold, his body covered with a golden armour, his standard and bow variegated with gold, that hero appeared resplendent like the crest of the Merumountain.

sn: सधनुर्मण्डल: संख्ये तेजोभास्कररश्मिवान्। शरदीवोदितः सूर्यो नृसूर्यो नृसूर्यो विरराज ह॥
en: Himself emitting great effulgence and wielding that bow drawn to a circle in his hands, he appeared like another autumnal sum.

sn: वृषभस्कन्धविक्रान्तो वृषभाक्षो नरर्षभः। तावकानां बभौ मध्ये गवां मध्ये यथा वृषः॥
en: That foremost of men graced with shoulders, tread and eyes, resembling those of the moon, appeared in the centre of your army, like a bull in the midst of a cowpen.

sn: मत्तद्विरदसंकाशं मत्तद्विरदगामिनम्। प्रभिन्नमिव मातङ्गं यूथमदे व्यवशअथितम्॥
en: Him looking like and possessing the graceful tread of, an infuriate elephant and appearing like an elephant leader with open temples, standing in their midst.

sn: व्याघ्रा इव जिघांसन्तस्त्वदीयाः समुपाद्रवन्। द्रोणानीकमतिक्रान्तं भोजानीकं च दुस्तरम्॥
en: Your troops desirous of slaying assailed with fury. After Satyaki had passed through Drona's division and the uncrossable oceanlike division of the Bhojas.

sn: जलसंधार्णवं तीा काम्बोजानां च वाहिनीम्। हार्दिक्यमकरान्मुक्तं तीर्णे वै सैन्यसागरम्॥
en: After he had passed through the son of Jalasandha's troops, as also the host of the Kamboja, after had escaped the alligator constituted by Hridika's son, after he had forded through that ocean like host.

sn: परिवठ्ठः सुसंक्रुद्धास्त्वदीयाः सात्यकिं रथाः। दुर्योधनश्चित्रसेनो दुःशासनविविंशती॥
en: Many car-warriors of your army inflamed with fury encompassed Satyaki on all sides. Duryodhana, Chitrasena, Dushasana, Vivnishati.

sn: शकुनिर्दुःसहश्चैव युवा दुर्धर्षण: ऋथः। अन्ये च बहवः शूराः शस्त्रवन्तो दुरासदाः॥
en: Shakuni, Dussaha, the youthful Durmarsana, Kratha and many other brave warriors, all well-versed in the use of weapons and difficult of being defeated.

sn: पृष्ठतः सात्यकिं यान्तमन्वधावन्नमर्षिणः। अथ शब्दो महानासीत् तव सैन्यस्य मारिष॥
en: Angrily followed Satyaki from behind as he proceeded onwards. Then, O sire, tremendous was the din that arose among your army.

sn: मारुतोद्भूतवेगस्य सागरस्येव पर्वणि। तानभिद्रवतः सर्वान् समीक्ष्य शिनिपुङ्गवः॥
en: Resembling the roar of the ocean in a Parva-day when it is lashed into fury by the wind. Beholding them all rush towards himself, that foremost of then Sinis.

sn: शनैर्याहीति यन्तारमब्रवीत् प्रहसन्निव। इदमेतत् समुद्भूतं धार्तराष्ट्रस्य यद् बलम्॥
en: Addressing his charioteer smilingly said "Proceed slowly" this army of the sons of Dhritarashtra, swelling with fury.

sn: मामेवाभिमुखं तूर्णे गजाश्वरथपन्तिमत्। नादयन् वै दिशः सर्वा रथघोषेण सारथे॥
en: And abounding in elephants, horses, chariots and infantry, is rushing at me with vehemence, O charioteer, filling all the quarters with the clatter of its cars.

sn: पृथवीं चान्तरिक्षं च कम्पयन् सागरानपि। एतद् बलार्णवं सूत वारयिष्ये महारणे॥
en: And causing the earth, the conclave dome and occans to tremble. O Suta, this ocean like host I shall resist in battle.

sn: पौर्णमास्यामिवोद्भूतं वेलेव मकरालयम्। पश्य मे सूत तविक्रान्तमिन्द्रस्येव महामृधे॥
en: Like the banks resisting the mighty main when it swells in the day of the full moon. Behold charioteer, my prowess in battle witch resembles that of Indra himself.

sn: एष सैन्यानि शत्रूणां विधमामि शितैः शरै। निहतानाहवे पश्य पदात्यश्वरथाद्विपान्॥
en: Behold me crush these hostile forces with my own sharp arrows. Behold these footsoldiers, horses, car-warriors and elephants of the hostile force slain.

sn: मच्छरैरग्निसंकाशैविद्धदेहान् सहस्रशः। इत्येवं ब्रुवतस्तस्य सात्यकेरमितौजसः॥
en: And mangled, by my sharp shafts whose touch resemble that of fire itself.” When Satyaki of immeasurable prowess was thus speaking.

sn: समीपे सैनिकास्ते तु शीघ्रमीयुर्युयुत्सवः। जह्याद्रवस्व तिष्ठेति पश्य पस्येति वादिनः॥
en: You warriors quickly approached him desirous of battling with him, saying, 'Slay'. 'Rush,' “Wait" 'Look look'.

sn: तानेवं ब्रुवतो वीरान् सात्यकिनिशितैः शरैः। जधान त्रिशतानश्वान् कुञ्जरांश्च चतुःशतान्॥
en: Satyaki then fell to slaughter those heroes even when they were thus speaking, with his sharp arrows. He slew three hundred steeds and four hundred elephants.

sn: स समप्रहारस्तुमुलस्तस्य तेषां च धन्विनाम्। देवासुररणप्रख्यः प्रावर्तत जनक्षयः॥
en: That battle between Satyaki on the one hand and your warriors of the others, became awful like that between the gods and the Asuras fought in the days of yore. The carnage that attended it, was fierce in the extreme.

sn: मेघजालनिमं सैन्यं तव पुत्रस्य मारिष। प्रत्यगृह्णाच्छिने: पौत्रः शरैराशीविषोपमैः॥
en: O sire, the grandson of Sini received the assault of your son's divisions resembling thick masses of clouds, with his shafts resembling snakes of virulent poison.

sn: प्रच्छाद्यमानः समरे शरजालैः स वीर्यवान्। असम्भ्रमन् महाराज तावकानवधीद् बहून्॥
en: That valorous hero then covered over with net-work of arrows, O king, began to slay your troops by hundreds, nothing daunted.

sn: आश्चर्ये तत्र राजेन्द्र सुमहद् दृष्टवानहम्। न मोघः सायकः कश्चित् सात्यकेरभवत् प्रभो॥
en: 0 king, I then beheld an extremcly wonderful sight there, inasmuch as, O lord, I saw not one shaft of Satyaki fail in striking its aim.

sn: रथनागाश्वकलिल: पदात्यूर्मिसमाकुलः। शैनेयवेलामासाद्य स्थितः सैन्यमहार्णवः॥
en: That ocean constituted by the troops of Duryodhana, teening with cars, elephants and steeds and surging with waves constituted by cars, as soon as it came in contact with the bank formed by Sinis grandson.

sn: सम्भ्रान्तनरनागाश्वमावर्तत मुहुर्मुहुः। तत् सैन्चमिषुभिस्तेन वध्यमानं समन्ततः॥
en: That host consisting of terrified warriors, clephants and horses, carnaged on all sides by the arrows of Satyaki, began to turn round repeatedly.

sn: बभ्राम तत्र तत्रैव गावः शीतार्दिता इव। पदातिनं रथं मागं सादिनं तुरगं तथा॥
en: And wandered hither and thither like kine afflicted with the chill of winter. Among footsoliers, car-warriors, clephants and horsc-men and horses.

sn: अविद्धं तत्र नाद्राक्षं युयुधानस्य सायकः। न तादृक् कदनं राजन् कृतवांस्तत्र फाल्गुनः॥
en: We then beheld none who was not pierced will the arrows of Yuyudhana. Even Phaiguna himselt () king, spread not such carnage in your rooms.

sn: यादृक् क्षयमनीकानामकरोत् सात्यकिर्नृप। अत्यर्जुनं शिनेः पौत्रो युध्यते पुरुषर्षभः॥
en: As was done by Satyaki in your ranks. O foremost of men, Sini's grandson then fought, surpassing even Arjuna himself.

sn: वीतभीाघवोपेतः कृतित्वं सम्प्रदर्शयन्। ततो दुर्योधनो राजा सात्वतस्य त्रिभिः शरैः॥
en: Completely fearless and displaying his Tightness of hands and skill in the use of weapons. Thereafter king Duryodhana, with three arrows.

sn: विव्याध सूतं निशितैश्चतुर्भिश्चतुरो हयान्। मात्यकिं च त्रिभिविद्ध्वा पुनरष्टाभिरेव च॥
en: Pierced the charioteer of that Satvata hero; and then with another four sharp shafts, he pierced the latter's four steeds. Next piercing Satyaki himself with three arrows, he pierced him with a set of another cight shafts.

sn: दुःशासनः षोडशभिर्विव्याध शिनिपुङ्गवम्। शकुनिः पञ्चविंशत्या चित्रसेनश्च पञ्चभिः॥
en: Then Dushasana pierced that foremost scion of the Sini dynasty with sixteen shafts, Shakuni pierced him with twenty-five and Chitrasena with five arrows.

sn: दुःसहः पञ्चदशभिर्विव्याधोरसि सात्यकिम्। उत्स्मयन् वृष्णिशार्दूलस्तथा बाणैः समाहतः॥
en: Dussaha then pierced Satyaki on the centre of his chest with fifteen arrows. Then thus struck with those numerous shafts, that foremosi hero among the Vrishnis, smiled.

sn: तानविध्यन्महाराज सर्वानेव त्रिभिस्त्रिभिः। गाढविद्वानरीन् कृत्वा मार्गणैःसोऽतितेजनैः॥
en: And, O mighty monarch, pierced each of his assailers with three shafts. Thus piercing his foes with darts of fierce energy.

sn: शैनेयः श्येनवत् संख्ये व्यचरल्लघुविक्रमः। सौबलस्य धनुश्छित्त्वाहस्तावापं निकृत्य च॥
en: That grandson of Sini endued with great celerity, began to move about the field of battle, even like a hawk. Cutting off the bow of Suvalas son and severing his gloves.

sn: दुर्योधनं त्रिभिर्बाणैरभ्यविध्यत् स्तनान्तरे। चित्रसेनं शतेनैव दशभिर्दुःसहं तथा॥
en: He pierced Duryodhana on the centre of his chest with three arrows; he pierce Chitrasena with hundred and Dussaha with ten arrows.

sn: दुःशासनं तु विंशत्या विव्याध शिनिपुङ्गवः। अथान्यद् धनुरादाय श्यालस्तव विशाम्पते॥
en: That illustrious grandson of Sini next pierced Dushasana with twenty arrows. Thereafter O ruler of men, your brother-in-law, taking up another bow.

sn: अष्टाभिःसात्यकि विद्ध्वा पुनर्विव्याध पञ्चभिः। दुःशासनश्च दशभिर्दुःसहश्च त्रिभिः शरैः॥ दुर्मुखश्च द्वादशमी राजन् विव्याध सात्यकिम्। दुर्योधनस्त्रिसप्तत्या विद्ध्वा भारत माधवम्॥
en: Pierced Satyaki first with eight and then with another five arrows. Then o king, Dushasana pierced Satyaki with ten, Dussaha with three and Durmukha with twelve shafts. O Bharata, then Duryodhana, pierced that scion of Madhu's race with seventy-three arrows.

sn: ततोऽस्यनिशितैर्वाणैस्त्रिभिर्विव्याध सारथिम्। तान् सर्वान् सहिताशूरान् यतमानान् महारथान्॥
en: Next he pierced the latter's charioteer with three sharp arrows. Then all those mighty carwarriors who were fighting unitedly and heedfully.

sn: पञ्चभिः पञ्चभिर्बाणैः पुनर्विव्याध सात्यकिः। ततः स रथिनां श्रेष्ठस्तव पुत्रस्य सारथिम्॥ आजघानाशु भल्लेन स हतो न्यपतद् भुवि। पतिते सारथौ तस्मिंस्तव पुत्ररथः प्रभो॥
en: Were pierced each with five arrows by Satyaki. Then that foremost of warriors struck the driver of your son with a broad-headed shaft. The latter then fell down on the ground slain. When his charioteer had been laid low, O master, that car-warrior, your son.

sn: वातायमानैस्तैरश्वैरपानीयत संगरात्। ततस्तव सुता राजन् सैनिकाच विशाम्पते॥
en: Was borne away from the field of battle by his steeds of the fleetness of the wind. Thereupon, your other sons and the troops, () king.

sn: राज्ञो रथमभिप्रेक्ष्य विद्रुताः शतशोऽभरन्। विद्रुतं तत्र तत् सैन्यं दृष्ट्वा भारत सात्यकिः॥
en: Looking at the chariot of the king, began to break away by hundreds. Then O Bharata, beholding the divisions routed, Satyaki.

sn: अवाकिरच्छरैस्तीक्ष्णै रुक्मपुङ्खः शिलाशितैः। विद्राव्य सर्वसैन्यानि तावकानि सहस्रशः॥
en: Covered them with keen pointed arrows furnished with golden wings and whetted on stone. Thus, o king, crushing all the warriors of your army by thousands.

sn: तं शरानाददानं च रक्षमाणं च सारथिम्। आत्मानं पालयानं स तावकाः समपूजयन्॥
en: Satyaki flew towards the chariot of Arjuna owning cream-colored steeds. Even your troops then applauded him as they beheld him proceed shooting arrows and protecting himself and his charioteer.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच समप्रमृद्य महत् सैन्यं यान्तं शैनेयमर्जुनम्। निह्रींका मम ते पुत्राः किमकुर्वत संजय॥
en: Dhritarastra said What, O Sanjaya, did my shameless sons do when they beheld the grandson of Sini proceed towards Arjuna, crushing as he advanced my troops?

sn: कथं वेषां तदा युद्धे धृतिरासीन्मुमूर्षताम्। शैनेयचरितं दृष्ट्वा यादृशं सव्यसाचिनः॥
en: How indeed did those dying wretches set their heart on fight, when Sini's grandson who is equal to Savyasachin himself appeared before them?

sn: किं नु वक्ष्यन्ति ते क्षात्रं सैन्यमद्ये पराजिताः। कथं नु सात्यकिर्युद्धे व्यतिक्रान्तो महायशाः॥
en: What indeed, did the Kshatriyas defeated in battle do? How indeed did the illustrious Satyaki penetrate through their ranks?

sn: कथं च मम पुत्राणां जीवतां तत्र संजय। शैनेयोऽभिययौ युद्धे तन्ममाचक्ष्व संजय॥
en: O Sanjaya, tell me also, how could the grandson of Sini proceed to battle when all my sons were alive and fighting?

sn: अत्यद्भुतमिदं तात त्वत्सकाशाच्छ्रणोम्यहम्। एकस्य बहुभिः सार्धे शत्रुबिस्तैर्महारथैः॥
en: What I have heard from you, O son, appears to be exceedingly wonderful viz., the battle between the one and the many the latter counting many mighty car-warrior among them.

sn: विपरीतमहं मन्ये मन्दभाग्यं सुतं प्रति। यत्रावध्यन्त समरे सात्वतेन महारथाः॥
en: O Suta, I think Destiny is adverse to the interests of my sons, in as much as they are now being slaughtered by that mighty carwarrior of the Satvata race.

sn: एकस्य हि न पर्याप्तं यत्सैन्यं तस्य संजय। क्रुद्धस्य ययुधानस्य सर्वे तिष्ठन्तु पाण्डवाः॥
en: Even all my troops united together were not competent enough to withstand the enraged Yuyudhana; not to speak of the sons of Pandu.

sn: निर्जित्य समरे द्रोणं कृतिनं चित्रयोधिनम्। यथा पशुगणान् सिंहस्तद्धद्धन्ता सुतान् मम॥
en: Like a lion slaying other inferior beasts Satyaki is slaughtering my sons, having first vanquished in battle Drona that warrior accomplished in weapons and versed in all modes of warfare.

sn: कृतवर्मादिभिः शूरैर्यत्तैर्बहुभिराहवे। युयुधानो न शकितो हन्तुं यत् पुरुषर्षभः॥
en: Countless heroes headed by Kirtavaiman himself, fighting heedfully, were not able to slay Satyaki in battle; so it is certain that the latter will vanquish my sons single-headed.

sn: नैतदीदृशकं युद्धं कृतवांस्तत्र फाल्गुनः। यादृशं कृतवान् युद्धं शिनेर्नप्ता महायशाः॥
en: Even Phalguna himself did not fight in the manner in which the illustrious grandson of Sini has fought.

sn: संजय उवाच तव दुर्मन्त्रिते राजन् दुर्योधनकृतेन च। शृणुष्वावहितोभूत्वा यत् ते वक्ष्यामि भारत॥
en: Sanjaya said All this has been brought about by your wicked policy and by the vile deeds of Duryodhana o king. O Bharata, now hear attentively what I am going to say to you.

sn: पुनः संन्यवर्तन्त कृत्वा संशप्तकान् मिथः। परां युद्धे मतिं क्रूरां तव पुत्रस्य शासनात्॥
en: At the command of your son, all those warriors then taking tremendous vows to fight

sn: ते
en: to the last, rallied and resolved upon fighting fierce.

sn: त्रीणि सादिसहस्राणि दुर्योधनपुरोगमाः। शककाम्बोजबाह्रीका यवनाः पारदास्तथा॥
en: Three thousand bowmen, commanded by Duryodhana himself and supported by a numerous body of Sakas, Kambojas, Valhikas, Yavanas, Paradas.

sn: कुलिन्दास्तङ्गणाम्बष्ठा पैशाचाश्च सबर्बराः। पर्वतीयाश्च राजेन्द्र क्रुद्धा: पाषाणपाणयः॥
en: Kulindas, Tanganas, Amvartas, Pisachas, Barbaras and mountaineers, Oking, all inspired with rage and armed with stones.

sn: अभ्यद्रवन्त शैनेयं शलभाः पावकं यथा। युक्ताश्च पर्वतीयानां रथाः पाषाणयोधिनाम्॥
en: Rushed against Sini's grandson like flights of insects falling upon a blazing fire. Five hundred other warriors united together, O king, then also assailed Satyaki.

sn: शूराः पञ्चशता राजन् शैनेयं समुपाद्रवन्। ततो रथसहस्रेण महारथशतेन च।॥ द्विरदानां सहस्रेण द्विसाहनैश्च वाजिभिः। शरवर्षाणि मुञ्चन्तो विविधानि महारथाः॥
en: Another large division consisting of a thousand chariots, a hundred mighty carwarriors, a thousand elephants, two thousand horses and innumerable foots soldiers, also assailed the grandson of Sini.

sn: अभ्यद्रवन्त शैनेयमसंख्येयाश्च पत्तगः। तांश्च संचोदयन् सर्वान् नतैनमिति भारत॥
en: Then, O Bharata, Dushasana, urged those troops saying, slay him' and encompassed Satyaki there with.

sn: दुःशासनो महाराज सात्यकिं पर्यवारयत्। तत्राद्भुतमपश्याम शैनेयचरितं महत्॥
en: Then we beheld the marvellous character of the prowess of Sini's grandson, in as much as single handed as he was he fearlessly fought on with the odds against him.

sn: यदेको बहुभिः सार्धमसम्भ्रान्तमयुध्यत। अवधीच रथानीकं द्विरदानां च तद् बलम्॥
en: He then continually went on slaying the divisions of car-warriors elephants and horsemen and the robbers.

sn: सादिनश्चैव तान् सर्वान् दस्यूनपि च सर्वशः। तत्र चक्रैर्विमथितैर्भग्नैश्च परमायुधैः॥ अक्षैश्च बहुधा भग्नैरीषादण्डकबन्धुरैः। कुञ्जरैर्मथितैश्चापि ध्वजैश्च विनिपातितः॥ वर्मभिश्च तथानीकैर्व्यवकीर्णा वसुंधरा। स्रग्भिराभरणैर्वस्त्रैरनुकपैश्च मारिष॥
en: Like the autumnal sky bespangled with stars, the field of battle then became covered with car wheels broken and smashed by means of his mighty weapons with innumerable Akshas and beautiful car-shafts crushed to pieces with mangled elephants and broken standards with coats of mail and bucklers scattered all about and O sire, with garlands and ornaments and attires and Anukarshas.

sn: संछन्ना वसुधा तत्र द्यौर्यहैरिव भारत। गिरिरूपधराश्चापि पतिताः कुञ्जरोत्तमाः॥ अञ्जनस्य कुले जाता वामनस्य च भारत। सुप्रतीककुले ज्ञाता महापद्मकुले तथा॥ एरावतकुले चैव तथान्येषु कुलेषु च। जाता दन्तिवरा राजशेरते बहवो हताः॥ वनाजान् पर्वतीयान् काम्बोजान् बालिकानपि। तथा हयवरान् राजन् निजघ्ने तत्र सात्यकिः॥ नानादेशसमुत्थांश्च नानाजातींश्च दन्तिनः। निजम्ने तत्र शैनेयः शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः॥
en: Many best elephants prodigious mountainous and of the Anjanors, of the Vamana breed, O Bharata or of the Supratika Mahapadmat or Airavata or other breeds, many excellent tuskers, O king, lay prostrate on the ground, deprived of life. Satyaki then slew, O king, many foremost of steeds of the Vanaya, the mountain, the Kamboja and the Valhika breeds. The grandson of Sini also slaughtered foot soldiers there, in hundreds and thousands, born in various realms and belonging to various nationalities. Whilst those troops were being thus carnaged, Dushasana addressing the or

sn: तेषु प्रकाल्यमानेषु दस्यून् दुःशासनोऽब्ररीत्। निवर्तध्वमधर्मज्ञा युध्यध्वं किं सृतेन वः॥
en: 'Ye heroes, ignorant of the rules of fighting, fight on.” Why do you retreat? But seeing them break away in spite of all his commands yo!'r son Dushasana.

sn: तांश्चातिभग्नान् सम्प्रेक्ष्य पुत्रो दुःशासनस्तव। पाषाणयोधिनः शूरान् पर्वतीयानचोदयत्॥
en: Urged on the heroic mountaineers skilled in fighting with stones saying-"You are all skillful in fighting. The Kauravas also are all ignorant of this mode of war-fare.

sn: अश्मयुद्धेषु कुशला नैतजानाति सात्यकिः। अश्मयुद्धमजानन्तं नतैनं युद्धकार्मुकम्॥
en: Do you slay then this hero who, desirous as he is of battle, is unacquainted with your manner of fighting. The Kauravas also are all ignorant of this mode of battle.

sn: तथैव कुरवः सर्वे नाश्मयुद्धविशारदाः। अभिद्रवत माभैष्ट न वः प्राप्स्यति सात्यकिः॥
en: Rush upon Satyaki and fear not for he will not be able to reach you in battle. Thereupon all those mountain kings, all accomplished in fighting with stones.

sn: ते पर्वतीया राजानः सर्वे पाषाणयोधिनः। अभ्यद्रवन्त शैनेयं राजानमिव मन्त्रिणः॥
en: Rushed upon the grandson of Sini like so many counsellors rushing in the train of a king. Then all those denizens of the mountains, armed with hollicks looking like the heads of the elephants.

sn: ततो गजशिरःप्रख्यैरुपलैः शैलवासिनः। उद्यतैर्युयुधानस्य पुरतस्तस्थुराहवे॥
en: Stood before Yuyudhana in that battle ready to strike others desirous of compassing the slaughter of the Satvata hero with their missiles.

sn: क्षेपणीयैस्तथाप्यन्ये सात्वतस्य वधैषिणः। चोदितास्तव पुत्रेण सर्वतो रुरुधुर्दिशः॥
en: They obstructed all the points of the compass, urged as they were by your son. Then as they rushed desirous of fighting with their stones.

sn: तेषामापततामेव शिलायुद्धं चिकीर्षताम्। सात्यकिः प्रतिसंधाय निशितान् प्राहिणोच्छरान्॥
en: Satyaki sped at them sharp arrows fixing them on his bow string. That awful shower of stones then discharged by the Mountaineers.

sn: तामश्मवृष्टिं तुमुलां पर्वतीयैः समीरिताम्। चिच्छेदोरगसंकाशैर्नाराचैः शिनिपुङ्गवः॥
en: The foremost scion of the Sini race baffled with his Narachas resembling venomous reptiles. Then with those lustrous fragments of stones looking like a flight of fire flies.

sn: तैरश्मचूर्णैर्दीप्यद्भिः खद्योतानामिव व्रजैः। प्राय: सैन्यान्यहन्यन्त हाहाभूतानि मारिष॥
en: Many of our soldiers were slaughtered; and O sire, cries of alas and Oh were heard in all directions. Then with heavy stones uplifted, five hundred heroic warriors.

sn: ततः पञ्चशतं शूराः समुद्यतमहाशिलाः। निकृत्तबाहवो राजन् निपेतुर्धरणीतले॥
en: Fell down, O king with their arms severed. Again a thousand warriors and other hundred thousand warriors.

sn: पुनर्दशशताश्चान्ये शतसाहस्त्रिणस्तथा। सोपलैर्बाहुभिश्छिन्नैः पेतुरप्राप्य सात्यकिम्॥
en: Encounterirg Satyaki fell down with their arms bearing stones lopped off. Then many heroic warriors, accomplished in fighting with stones, began to fall down, with their purposes unsettled.

sn: पाषाणयोधिनः शूरान् यतमानावस्थितान्। न्यवधीद् बहुसाहस्त्रांस्तदद्भुतमिवाभवत्॥
en: Stayaki then slew them by thousands and that appeared indeed wonderful. Then again many of them, returning to the charge, hurled at Satyaki showers of stones.

sn: ततः पुनात्तमुखास्तेऽश्मवृष्टीः समन्ततः। अयोहस्ताः शूलहस्ता दरदास्तङ्गणाः खसाः॥
en: With swords and lances in their grasp, many Daradar, Tanjanas, Thasus, Lampakas and Pulindas, hurled their weapons at Satyaki.

sn: लम्पाकाश्च कुलिन्दाश्च चिक्षिपुस्तांश्च सात्यकिः। नाराचैः प्रतिचिच्छेद प्रतिपत्तिविशारदः॥
en: But the latter well accomplished in the use of weapons cut all of them in pieces with his Narachns. Then as the stones were being broken in the air by sharp arrows.

sn: अद्रीणां भिद्यमानानामन्तरिक्षे शितैः शरैः। शब्देन प्राद्वन् संख्ये रक्षाश्वगजपत्तयः॥
en: The sound, that was created, caused many car-warriors, horses, elephants and footsoldiers to fly away. Pelted in all directions by fragments of stones, men, elephants and horses.

sn: अश्मचूर्णैरवाकीर्णा मनुष्यगजवाजिनः। नाशक्नुवन्नस्थातुं भ्रमरैरिव दंशिताः॥
en: Were unable to stand in the field of battle, in as much as they felt as if bit by bees. The survivors, bathed in blood and with their heads and frontal globes shattered.

sn: हतशिष्टाः सरुधिरा भिन्नमस्तकपिण्डिकाः। कुञ्जरा वर्जयामासुसुयुधानरथं तथा॥
en: Of the elephant hosts, then began to break away leaning the car of Yuyudhana. Then the noise that your troops created, O sire.

sn: ततः शब्दः समभवत् तव सैन्यस्य मारिष। माधवेनार्धमानस्य सागरस्येव पर्वणि॥
en: Afflicted as they were with the shafts of that descendent of Madhu's race, was tremendous like that of the Ocean in a Parvadayi. Then hearing the cry and that tremendous din, Drona, addressing his charioteer, said

sn: तं शब्दं तुमुलं श्रुत्वा द्रोणो यन्तारमब्रवीत्। क्रुद्धः सात्वतानां महारथः॥
en: "O charioteer this mighty car-warrior, of the Satvata race inflamed with wrath, has shattered the host in many places and is now careering like the Destroyer in the field of battle.

sn: दारयन् बहुधा सैन्यं रणे चरति कालवत्। यत्रैष शब्दस्तुमुलस्तत्र सूत रथं नय॥
en: O charioteer, drive my car to the spot whence this noise is coming. Surely Yuyudhana has now encountered these heroes that fight with the stones.

sn: एष सूते रणे पाषाणयोधिभिर्नूनं युयुधानः समागतः। तथा हि रथिनः सर्वे ह्रियन्ते विद्रुतैर्हयैः॥
en: Yonder the car-warriors are leaving Satyaki being borne away by their flying steeds. Behold some are falling down on the spot with their bodies mangled.

sn: विशस्त्रकवचा रुग्णास्तत्र तत्र पतन्ति च। न शक्नुवन्ति यन्तारः संयन्तुं तुमुले हयान्॥
en: Their drivers are not able to restrain their wild horses.” The charioteer hearing these words of Bharadvaja's son.

sn: इत्येतद् वचनं श्रुत्वा भारद्वाजस्य सारथिः। प्रत्युवाच ततो द्रोणं सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वरम्॥
en: Replied unto Drona that foremost of all wielders of weapons saying-"O long-lived one, behold the army of the Kauravas routed in all directions.

sn: सैन्यं द्रवति चायुष्मन् कौरवेयं समन्ततः। पश्य रोधान् रणेभग्नान् धावतो वै ततस्ततः॥
en: Behold the warriors rush in all directions deserting their ranks! But in fact you behold those heroic Panchalas and Pandavas.

sn: इमे च संहताः शूराः पञ्चाला: पाण्डवैः सह। त्वामेव हि जिघांसन्त आद्रवन्ति समन्ततः॥
en: Advance desirous of encountering yourself. O subduer of foes, now behave yourself in the manner one should behave on such occasions.

sn: अत्र कार्य समाधत्स्व प्राप्तकालमरिंदम। स्थाने वा गमने वापि दूरं यातश्च सात्यकिः॥
en: Shall we proceed or stay here? Satyaki has gone far ahead of us." While the charioteer was thus speaking to the son of Bharadvaja, O sire.

sn: तथैवं वदतस्तस्य भारद्वाजस्य सारथेः। प्रत्यदृश्यत शैनेयो निघ्नन् बहुविधान् रथान्॥
en: The grandson of Sini suddenly came to view, engaged in siaughtering a large number of car-warriors. Those soldiers of yours while being thus slaughtered by Yuyudhana in battle.

sn: ते वध्यमानाः समरे युयुधानेन तावकाः। युयुधानरथं त्यक्त्वा द्रोणानकाय दुद्रुवुः॥ यैस्तु दुःशासनः सार्ध रथैः पूर्व न्यवर्तत। ते भीतास्त्वभ्यधावन्त सर्वे द्रोणरथं प्रति॥
en: They fled away from Yuyudhana's chariot towards the spot where Drona's division was placed. Those other car-warriors accompanied by Dushasana, all struck with panic, also rushed to the place where Drona's chariot was seen.

sn: संजय उवाच दुःशासनरथं दृष्टवा समीपे पर्यवस्थितम्। भारद्वाजस्ततो वाक्यं दुःशासनमथाब्रवीत्॥
en: Sanjaya said Beholding then the chariot of Dussana stationed near him, the son of Bharadvaja addressing him said these wordsदुःशासन रथाः सर्वे कस्माच्चैते प्रविद्रुताः।

sn: कचित् क्षेनं तु नृपतेः कचिजीवति सैन्धवः॥
en: "O Dussana, why are all these car-warriors, flying away? Is everything right with the king? Does the king of the Sindhus still live?

sn: राजपुत्रो भवानत्र राजभ्राता महारथः। किमर्थ द्रवते युद्धे यौवराज्यमवाप्य हि॥
en: You are the son of a king, the brother of a king and a mighty car-warrior; why then do you fly away? Constitute yourself the Princeregent (by making your brother the king)?

sn: दासी जितासि द्यूते त्वं यथाकामचरी भव। वाससां वाहिका राज्ञो भ्रातुर्येष्ठस्य मे भव॥
en: "You are our slave; you have been won by us as a stake in the game of dice; become you a courtezan; and engaged yourself as a bearer of attires to the king, my elder brother.

sn: न सन्ति पतयः सर्वे तेऽद्य षण्ढतिलैः समा। दुःशासनैवं कस्मात् त्वं पूर्वमुक्त्वा पलायसे॥
en: Your husbands do not live; they are like sesamum seeds without the kernel.” 0 Dushasana, it was you who spoke those words to Draupadi. Why then do you now fly away.

sn: स्वयं वैरं महत् कृत्वा पञ्चालैः पाण्डवैः सह। एकं सात्यकिमासाद्य कथं भीतोऽसि संयुगे॥
en: Having yourself provoked inveterate enmity with the Panchalas and the Pandavas, why do you now fly, out of fear, obtaining Satyaki alone in battle for your opponent?

sn: न जानीषे पुरा पं तु गृह्णन्नक्षान् दुरोदरे। शरा ह्येते भविष्यन्ति दारुणाशीविषोपमाः॥
en: In days gone by, at the game of dice having taken up the dice, you did not divine that they would be changed into dreadful darts resembling snakes of virulent poison.

sn: अप्रियाणां हि वचसां पाण्डवस्य विशेषतः। द्रौपद्याश्च परिक्लेशस्त्वन्मूलो ह्यमवत् पुरा॥
en: It were you who formerly abused the Pandavas in filthy language; you were the cause of all the wocs of Draupadi.

sn: क्व ते मानश्च दर्पश्च व ते वीर्ये क्व गर्जितम्। आशीविषसमान् पार्थान् कोपयित्वा व यास्यसि॥
en: Where your pride, your haughtiness and brag? Having provoked the Parthas who are like so may snakes of virulent poison, where do you intend to fly?

sn: शोच्येयं भारती सेना राज्यं चैव सुयोधनः। यस्य त्व कर्कशो भ्राता पलायनपरायणः॥
en: Both this army of the Bharatas and king Suyodhana are to be pitied, in asmuch as the latter own you who are now flying away as his brave brother.

sn: ननु नाम त्वया वीर दीर्यमाणा भयार्दिता। स्वबाहुबलमास्थाय रक्षितव्य ह्यनीकिनी॥
en: Indeed, O hero, this army, shattered and afflicted with fear as it is, ought to be protected by you, by your own strength of arms.

sn: स त्वमद्य रणं हित्वा भीतो हर्षयसे परान्। विद्रुते त्वयि सैन्यस्य नायके शत्रुसूदन॥
en: But you now, leaving the fight, are affording delight unto your foes. O slayer of foes, when you, the leader of the host are flying away. are 110W

sn: कोऽन्यः स्थास्यति संग्रामे भीतो भीते व्यपाश्रये। एकेन सात्वतेनाद्य युध्यमानस्य तेन वै॥
en: Who, seized with panic as he is, will care to remain, in the field of battle? Encountering that single-handed warriors of the Satvata race.

sn: पलायने तव मतिः संग्रामाद्धि प्रवर्तते। यदा गाण्डीवधन्वानं भीमसेनं च कौरव॥ यमौ वा युधि द्रष्टासि तदा त्वं कि करिष्यसि। युधि फाल्गुनबाणानां सूर्याग्निसमवर्चसाम्॥ न तुल्याः सात्यकिशराः येषां भीतः पलायसे।
en: Your heart is inclined to fly away from battle. What then, O Kaurava, will you do when you will see the wielder of the Gandiva in battle or Bhimasena of the twins, Nakula and Sahadeva. The arrows of Satyaki, afraid of which you are seeking to fly away, are scarcely equal to those of Arjuna, that resemble the sun or the fire in effulgence? If your heart is intent on flying away.

sn: त्वरितो वीर गच्छ त्वं गान्धार्युदरमाविश॥ पृथिव्यां धावमानस्य नान्यत् पश्यामि जीवनम्। यदि तावत् कृता बुद्धिः पलायणपरायणा॥
en: O brave warrior! Go immediately and reenter in the ovary of Gandhari, your mother. Because, there is o other place on this earth capable to defend you if you depart from the battle-field.

sn: पृथिवी धर्मराजाय शमेनैव प्रदीयताम्। यावत् फाल्गुननाराचा निर्मुक्तोरगसंनिभाः॥
en: Then let the sovereignty of the earth be given to king Yudhishthira the virtuous shafts of Phalguna looking like snakes divested of their slough.

sn: नाविशन्ति शरीरं ते तावत् संशाम्य पाण्डवैः। यावन्न क्रुद्धयते राजा धर्मपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: Penetrate into your body, let peace of Pritha slaying your hundred brothers snatch the earth away by force, conclude peace with the Pandavas. Before king Yudhishthira is excited with wrath.

sn: कृष्णश्च समरश्लाघी तावत् संशाम्य पाण्डवैः। यावद् भीमो महाबाहुर्विगाह्य महतीं चमूम्॥ पाण्डवैः।
en: And Krishna also, that giver of joy, conclude peace with the Pandavas. Before the mighty-armed Bhima, piercing through this vast array of yours.

sn: सोदरांस्ते न गृह्णाति तावत् संशाम्य पाण्डवैः। पूर्वमुक्तश्च ते भ्राता भीष्मेणासौ सुयोधनः॥
en: Seizes (and slays) your brothers, conclude peace with the Pandavas. Formerly Bhishma told your brother Suyodhana.

sn: अजेयाः पाण्डवाः संख्ये सौम्य सशाम्य तैः सह। न च तत् कृतवान् मन्दस्त्व भ्राता सुयोधनः॥
en: “The Pandavas are incapable of being vanquished in battle. O Gentle one, make peace with them.” Your perverted brother Suyodhana however did not listen to him.

sn: स युद्धे धृतिमास्थाय यत्तो युध्यस्य तवापि शोणितं भीमः पास्यतीति मया श्रुतम्॥ तच्चप्यवितथं तस्य तत् तथैव भविष्यति। किं भीमस्य न जानासि विक्रमं त्वं सुबालिश॥ यत्त्वया वैरमारब्धं संयुगे प्रपलायिना। गच्छ तूर्णं रथेनैव यत्र तिष्ठति सात्यकिः॥
en: Therefore firmly resolved to fight, battle on heedfully with the Pandavas. I heard that Bhima will drink too your blood. Forsooth, it is true. O fool, do you not aware of the prowess of Bhima. You took the enmity with him, and now escape from the battle field? Proceed quickly on you car, where Satyaki is?

sn: त्वया हीनं बल ह्येतद् विद्रविष्यति भारत। आत्मार्थ योधय रणे सा सात्यकिं सत्यविक्रमम्॥
en: Deprived of your help, this host will fly away. For your own sake, fight with Satyaki of indomitable prowess."

sn: एवमुक्तस्तव सुतो नाब्रवीत् किंचिदप्यसौ। श्रुतं चाश्रुतवत् कृत्वा प्रायाद् येन स सात्यकिः॥
en: Thus spoken to by Drona, your son spoke nothing in reply. Feigning as if he has not heard the words of Drona, Dushasana advanced to the spot where Satyaki was.

sn: सैन्येन महता युक्तो म्लेच्छानामनिवर्तिनाम्। आसाद्य च रणे यत्तो युयुधानमयोधयत्॥
en: Supported by a mighty division of unretreating Mlechchas, Dushasana fell upon Satyaki and fought on vigorously.

sn: द्रोणोऽपि रथिनां श्रेष्ठः पञ्चालान् पाण्डवांस्तथा। अभ्यद्रवत संक्रुद्धो जवमास्थाय मध्यमम्॥
en: Drona also, that best of car-warriors, inflamed with rage, proceeded against the Panchalas and the Pandavas in medium speed.

sn: प्रविश्य च रणे द्रोणः पाण्डवानां वरूथिनीम्। द्रावयामास योधान् वै शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः॥
en: Then Drona, engaging himself in battle, began to crush the Pandava army slaying heroes by hundreds and thousands.

sn: ततो द्रोणो महाराज नाम विश्राव्य संयुगे। पाण्डुपाञ्चालमत्स्यानां प्रचक्रे कदनं महत्॥
en: Thereafter, O mighty monarch, proclaiming his name in battle, he began to spread havoc among the ranks of the Pandavas, Panchalas and the Matsyas.

sn: तं जयन्तमनीकानि भारद्वाजं ततस्ततः। पाञ्चालपुत्रो द्युतिमान् वीरकेतुः समभ्ययात्॥
en: Thereat the effulgent Viraketu, the Panchala prince, encountered Drona the of Bharadvaja who had been vanquishing his troops.

sn: स द्रोणं पञ्चभिर्विद्ध्वा शरैः संनतपर्वभिः। ध्वजमेकेन विव्याध सारथिं चास्य सप्तभिः॥
en: Piercing Drona with five shafts of depressed knots, he cut down his standard with one and wounded his charioteer with seven shafts.

sn: तत्राद्भुतं महाराज दृष्टवानस्मि संयुगे। यद् द्रोणो रभसं युद्धे पाञ्चाल्यं नाभ्यवर्तत॥
en: Then O mighty monarch, we beheld a wonderful sight in that battle, in as much Drona striving hard could not approach the Panchala prince.

sn: संनिरुद्धं रणे द्रोणं पञ्चाला वीक्ष्य मारिष। आवत्रुः सर्वतो राजन् धर्मपुत्रजयैषिणः॥
en: O sire, then beholding Drona held in check, the Panchalas surrounded him O king, on all son sides, desirous as they were of securing victory to the very virtuous king Yudhishthira.

sn: ते शरैरग्निसंकाशैस्तोमरैश्च महाधनैः। शस्त्रैश्च विविधै राजन् द्रोणमेकमवाकिरन्॥
en: They then began to pour upon Drona darts resembling fire, thick showers of Tomaras and numerous other weapons, O king.

sn: निहत्य तान् बाणगणैोणो राजन् समन्ततः। महाजलधरान् व्योम्नि मातरिश्वेव चावभौ॥
en: Then baffling those thick showers of arrows by means of his own, like the wind scattering away mighty rain-clouds on the sky, Drona appeared exceedingly beautiful.

sn: ततः शरं महाघोरं सूर्यपावकसंनिभम्। संदधे परवीरघ्नो वीरकेतो रथं प्रति॥
en: Thereafter that slayer of hostile heroes viz., Drona aimed at the chariot of Viraketu a dreadful shaft, resembling the sun or fire in splendour.

sn: स भित्त्वा तु शरो राजन् पाञ्चालकुलनन्दनम्। अभ्यगाद् धरणीं तूर्णं लोहितार्दो ज्वलन्निव॥
en: O king, then that shaft penetrating through the scion of the Panchala dynasty entered the earth, steeped in blood and burning like a flame of fire.

sn: ततोऽपतद् रथात् तूर्णं पाञ्चालकुलनन्दनः। पर्वताग्रादिव महांश्चम्पको वायुपीडितः॥
en: Thereupon that delighter of the Panchala race, quickly fell down from his chariot like a Champaka falling down from the crest of a mountain, being up-rotted by the force of the wind.

sn: तस्मिन् हते महेष्वासे राजपुत्रे महाबले। पञ्चालास्त्वरिता द्रोणं समन्तात् पर्यवारयन्॥
en: When that highly puissant and fierce bowmen, that prince of the Panchalas, had been slain, the Panchalas, in all haste, surrounded Drona on all sides.

sn: चित्रकेतुः सुधन्वा च चित्रवर्मा च भारत। तथा चित्ररथश्चैव भ्रातृव्यसनकशिंताः॥
en: Chitraketu, Sudhanvan, Chitravarman and O Bharata, also Chitraratha-all afflicted with son grief at the calamity that had befallen their brother.

sn: अभ्यद्रवन्त सहिता भारद्वाजं युयुत्सवः। मुञ्चन्तः शरवर्षाणि तपान्ते जलदा इव॥
en: Unitedly and with a desire for fighting, rushed against the of Bharadvaja, discharging their showers of shafts like so many clouds discharging their contents at the expiration of the summer season.

sn: स वध्यमानो बहुधा राजपुत्रैर्महारथैः। क्रोधमाहारयत् तेषामभावाय द्विजर्षभः॥
en: Thus wounded by those princes, all mighty car-warriors, that foremost of the regenerate wrought himself up with anger, for putting an end to their existence.

sn: ततः शरमयं जालं द्रोणस्तेषामवासृजत्। ते हन्यमाना द्रोणस्य शरैराकर्णचोदितैः॥
en: Thereafter Drona hurled at them a net-work of Arrows. Those princes, then pierced with those shafts of Drona shot from the bow string drawn back to the very ear.

sn: कर्तव्यं नाभ्यजानान् वै कुमारा राजसत्तम। तान् विमूढान् रणे द्रोणः प्रहसन्निव भारत॥
en: Became embarrassed as to what they should do, O foremost of kings. Then when they were thus confounded, Drona with perfect ease.

sn: व्यश्वसूतरथांश्चक्रे कुमारान् कुपितो रणे। अथापरैः सुनिशितैर्भल्लैस्तेषां महायशाः॥
en: Inflamed as he was with rage, deprived those princes of their chariots, charioteers and steeds. Thereafter that hero of world-wide fame, with his sharp arrows and Vallas.

sn: पुष्पाणीव विचिन्वन् हि सोत्तमाङ्गान्यपातयत्। ते रथेभ्यो हताः पेतुः क्षितौ राजन् सुवर्चसः॥
en: Felled their heads, like one culling flowers. O king, those radiant heroes then fell down slain from their respective cars.

sn: देवासुरे पुरा युद्धे यथा दैतेयदानवाः। तान् निहत्य रणे राजन् भारद्वाजः प्रतापवान्॥
en: Even as the Daityas and Danavas fell, in the battle between the gods and the Asuras fought in the days of yore. Slaying them in battle, the valorous son of Bharadvaja.

sn: कार्मुकं भ्रामयामास हेमपृष्ठं दुरासदम्। पञ्चालान् निहतान् दृष्ट्वा देवकल्पान् महारथान्॥
en: Began to shake his excellent bow whose staff was golden and which was incapable of being approached. Then beholding those Panchala princes all mighty car-warrior and resembling the Pandavas themselves, slain.

sn: धृष्टद्युम्नो भृशोद्विग्नो नेत्राभ्यां पातयञ्जलम्। अभ्यवर्तते संग्रामे क्रुद्धो द्रोणरथं प्रति॥
en: Dhrishtadyumna was filled with rage and tears trickled down from his eyes. Then burning with rage, he rushed at the car of Drona.

sn: ततो हाहेति सहसा नादः समभवन्नृप। पाञ्चाल्येन रणे दृष्ट्वा द्रोणमावारितं शरैः॥
en: Thereupon, O king, suddenly cries of Alas and Oh were heard there, for, then Drona was seen covered with the shafts of the Panchala prince Dhrishtadyumna.

sn: बहुधा पार्षतेन महात्मना। न विव्यथे ततो द्रोण: स्मयन्नेवान्वयुध्यत॥
en: Though covered on all sides by the illustrious son of Prisata, yet Drona flinched not, but fought on smilingly.

sn: ततो द्रोणं महाराज पाञ्चाल्यः क्रोधमूर्छितः। आजघानोरसि क्रुद्धो नवत्या नतपर्वणाम्॥
en: Then, O mighty monarch, the Panchala prince, overwhelmed with rage, pierced Drona on the breast with ninety shafts of depressed knots.

sn: स गाढविद्धो बलिना भारद्वाजो महायशाः। निषसाद रथोपस्थे कश्मलं च जगाम ह॥
en: Pierced deeply by that powerful hero, the illustrious son of Bharadvaja, squatted down on the terrace of his chariot and fainted away in a

sn: स च्छाद्यमानो
en: Swoon.

sn: तं वै तथागतं दृष्ट्वा धृष्टद्युम्नः पराक्रमी। चापमुत्सृज्य शीघ्रं तु असिं जग्राह वीर्यवान्॥
en: Then beholding him in that plight, Dhrishtadyumna, of fierce energy and great might, grasped his sword and left aside his bow.

sn: अवप्लुत्य रथाचापि त्वरितः स महारथः। आरुरोह रथं तूर्णं भारद्वाजस्य मारिष॥
en: Then that mighty car-warrior, jumping down from his chariot with quickness, O sire, ascended with agility upon the car of the son of Bharadvaja.

sn: हर्तुमिच्छशिरः कायात् क्रोधसंरक्तलोचनः। प्रत्याश्वस्तस्ततो द्रोणो धनुर्गृह्य महारवम्॥
en: With his eyes rolling in rage and urged on by a desire for cutting off Drona's head from the trunk. Meanwhile the puissant Drona, recovering from the swoon, took up his bow.

sn: आसन्नमागतं दृष्ट्वा धृष्टद्युम्नं जिघांसया। शरैर्वैतस्तिकै राजन् विव्याधासन्नवेधिभिः॥ योधयामास समरे धृष्टद्युम्नं महारथम्। ते हि वैतस्तिका नाम शरा आसन्नयोधिनः॥
en: But beholding Dhristadyumna inflamed with a desire for slaughtering him so near, he began to pierce him with arrows measuring a span only and so fit to be used in close quarter. Those arrows known by the name of Vaitastika and fit to be used in close quarters.

sn: द्रोणस्य विहिता राजन् यैधृष्टद्युम्नमाक्षिणोत्। स वध्यमानो बहुभिः सायकैस्तैर्महाबलः॥
en: Where known to Drona only and by means of them, he succeeded in weakening Dhristadyumna's powers. Then the puissant Dhristadyumna wounded with those arrows,

sn: अवप्लुत्य रथात् तूर्णं भग्नवेगः पराक्रमी। आरुह्य स्वरथं वीरः प्रगृह्य च महद् धनुः॥
en: Swifty came down from Drona's chariot. That hero of fierce energy was then greatly robbed of his strength. Thereafter ascending his car and taking up a mighty bow.

sn: विव्याध समरे द्रोणं धृष्टद्युम्नो महारथः। द्रोणश्चापि महाराज शरैर्विव्याध पार्षतम्॥
en: The mighty car-warrior Dhristadyumna began to pierce Drona in battle; Drona also, O mighty monarch, pierced the son of Prisata with numerous shafts in battle.

sn: तदतद्भुतमभूद् युद्धं द्रोणपाञ्चालयोस्तदः। त्रैलोक्यकाक्षिणोरासीच्छक्रप्रह्लादयोरिव॥
en: Then a wonderful fight was fought between Drona and the Panchala prince, like what was fought between Shakra and the Prahlada, both longing to enjoy the sovereignty of the three worlds.

sn: मण्डलानि विचित्राणि यमकानीतराणि च। चरन्तौ युद्धमार्गशो ततक्षतुरथेषुभिः॥
en: Both versed in various modes of warfare, they careered over the field, displaying various motions with their chariots and mangling one another with their shafts.

sn: मोहयन्तौ मनांस्याजौ योधानां द्रोणपार्षतौ। सृजन्तौ शरवर्षाणि वर्षास्विव बलाहकौ॥
en: Then confounding the minds of the other warriors. Drona and Prisata's son began to pour their arrowy showers like rain-clouds purring their contents in the rainy seasons.

sn: छादयन्तौ महात्मनौ शरैर्योम दिशो महीम्। तदद्भुतं तयोर्युद्धं भूतसङ्घा ह्यपूजयन्॥
en: Those two high-souled warriors then covered the conclave dome, the earth and the quarters with their shafts. The creatures assembled there, then began to applaud that battle that was fought between them.

sn: क्षत्रियाश्च महाराज ये चान्ये तव सैनिकाः। अवश्यं समरे द्रोणो धृष्टद्युम्नेन सङ्गतः॥ वशमेष्यति नो राजन् पञ्चाला इति चुक्रुशः। द्रोणस्तु त्वरितो युद्धे धृष्टद्युम्नस्य सारथेः॥ शिरः प्रच्यावयामास फलं पक्वं तरोरिव। ततस्तु प्रदुता वाहा राजंस्तस्य महात्मनः॥
en: So also, O mighty monarch, the Kshatriyas and other soldiers praised that battle. “Meeting Dhristadyumna in battle Drona will surely succumb to him." The Panchalas exclaimed, O king, speaking thus. Then Drona fighting with great agility cut-off the head of Dhristadyumna's charioteer, like one felling ripe fruits from a tree. Thereupon O king, the steeds of the illustrious Dhristadyumna ran away wildly.

sn: तेषु प्रद्रवमाणेषु पञ्चालान् सृञ्जयांस्तथा। अयोधयद् रणे द्रोणस्तत्र तत्र पराक्रमी॥
en: When those steeds thus ran away bearing Dhristadyumna away, Drona of great might began to crush the Panchalas and Srinjayas (mercilessly).

sn: विजित्य पाण्डुपञ्चालान् भारद्वाजः प्रतापवान्। स्वं व्यूह पुनरास्थाय स्थितोऽभवदरिंदमः। न चैनं पाण्डवा युद्धे जेतुमुत्सेहिरे प्रभो॥
en: Then the highly puissant son of Bharadvaja having vanquished the Pandavas and the Panchalas and having reformed his array of troops, stood at its mouth. O master the Pandavas then ventured not to vanquish him in battle.

sn: संजय उवाच ततो दुःशासनो राजशैनेयं समुपाद्रवत्। किरशतसहस्त्राणि पर्जन्य इव वृष्टिमान्॥
en: Sanjaya said Meanwhile, o king, Dushasana advanced upon the grandson of Sini, shooting thousands of arrows, like a mighty rain-clouds pouring its contents.

sn: स विद्धवा सात्यकिं षष्ट्या तथा षोडशभिः शरैः। नाकम्पय स्थितं युद्धे मैनाकमिव पर्वतम्॥
en: Having pierced Satyaki first with sixty shafts and next with sixteen, he could not make him tremble who was fighting steadily like the immovable Mainaka mountain.

sn: तं तु दुःशासनः शूरः सायकैरावृणोद् भृशम्। रथावातेन महता नानादेशोद्भवेन च॥
en: Then that foremost of the Bharatas surrounded Satyaki with a mighty division of car-warriors born in various realms; he shot numerous arrows.

sn: सर्वतो भरतश्रेष्ठ विसृजन् सायकान् बहून्। पर्जन्य इव घोषेण नादयन् वै दिशो दश॥
en: And filled the ten quarters with the clatter of his car-wheels, that resembled the rumble or rain clouds. Beholding that Kaurava hero advance upon him Satyaki.

sn: तमापतन्तमालोक्य सात्यकिः कौरवं रणे। अभिदुत्य महाबाहुश्छादयामास सायकैः॥
en: Possessed of mighty arms, rushed against him and covered him with his own shafts. Then those warriors headed by Dushasana being thus covered by those arrowy showers.

sn: ते छाद्यमाना बाणौधैर्दुःशासनपुरोगमाः। प्राद्रवन् समरे भीतास्तव सैन्यस्य पश्यतः॥
en: Became seized with panic and began to fly away even before the very eyes of your son. O monarch, when those warriors were thus flying, your son Dushasana.

sn: तेषु द्रवत्सु राजेन्द्र पुत्रो दुःशासनस्तव। तस्थौ व्यपेतभी राजन् सात्यकिं चार्दयच्छरैः॥
en: Stood fearlessly before Satyaki afflicting him with his arrows. He then pierced the latter's charioteer with three and his steeds with four arrows;

sn: चतुर्भिर्वाजिनस्तस्य सारथिं च त्रिभिः शरैः। सात्यकिं च शतेनाजौ विद्ध्वा नादं मुमोच सः॥
en: Then piercing Satyaki himself with a set of hundred arrows, he uttered his war-cry. Thereupon O mighty monarch, that descendant of Madhu's race, being worked up

sn: तत: क्रुद्धो महाराज माधवस्तस्य संयुगे। रथं सूतं ध्वजं तं च चक्रेऽदृश्यमजिह्मगैः॥
en: Rendered Dushasana's car, charioteer and standard invisible with his swift flying arrows. he then entirely shrouded the heroic Dushasana with his shafts.

sn: स तु दुःशासनं शूरं सायकैरावृणोद् भृशम्। सशकं समनुप्राप्तमूर्णनाभिरिवोर्णया॥
en: That subduer of foes then quickly covered Dushasana with his arrows like a spider cntangling a gnat in its web.

sn: त्वरन् समावृणोद् बाणैर्दुःशासनममित्रजित्। दृष्टा दुःशासनं राजा तथा शरशताचितम्॥
en: with rage. Beholding Dushasana thus covered by the shafts of Satyaki, king Duryodhana urged the Trigarttas towards the car of Yuyudhana.

sn: त्रिगर्मीश्चोदयामास युयुधानस्थं प्रति। तेऽगच्छन् युयुधानस्य समीपं क्रूरकर्मणः।
en: Then three thousand warriors of the Trigaratta clan versed in battling and of cruel deeds, reaching the car of Yuyudhana.

sn: त्रिगर्तानां त्रिसाहस्त्रा रथा युद्धविशारदाः। ते तु तं रथवंशेन महता एर्यवारयन्॥
en: Surrounded the latter with the mighty division of their car. They on their hearts firmly on fighting and took terrible oaths.

sn: स्थिरां कृत्वा मतिं युद्धे भूत्वा संशप्तका मिथः। तेषां प्रपततां युद्धे शरवर्षाणि मुञ्चताम्॥
en: As they rushed to battle discharging showers of arrows, Yuyudhana crushed five hundred of their foremost warriors that marched in their front.

sn: योधान् पञ्चशतान् मुख्यानग्रयानीके व्यपोथयत्। तेऽपतन् निहतास्तूर्ण शिनिप्रवरसायकैः॥
en: They then began to fall down slain quickly by the arrows of the foremost of Sinis, like trees broken by the force of the wind falling down from the top of the mountain.

sn: महामारुतवेगेन भग्ना इव नगाद् दुमाः। नागैश्च बहुधा च्छिन्नैर्ध्वजैश्चैव विशाम्पते॥ हयैश्च कनकापीडैः पतितैस्तत्र मेदिनी। शैनेयशरसंकृतैः शोणितौघपरिप्लुतैः॥ अशोभत महाराज किंशुकैरिव पुष्पितैः।
en: The field of battle, overspread with mangled elephants, 0 king and broken standards and fallen bodies of horses furnished with golden traces and wounded and cut by the arrows of Sini's grandson and rolling in their blood, looked beautiful like a plain covered over with Kinsuka trees decked with blossoms.

sn: ते वध्यमानाः समरे युयुधानेन तावकाः॥ त्रातारं नाध्यगच्छन्त पङ्कमग्ना इव द्विपाः।
en: Then all those warriors of yours, slain in battle by Yuyudhana, were unable to find out a protector like elephants sunk in deep mire. was

sn: ततस्ते पर्यवर्तन्त सर्वे द्रोणरथं प्रति॥ भयात् पतगराजस्य गर्तानीव महोरगाः।
en: Thereafter terrified all of them proceeded towards the car of Drona like mighty snakes entering their holes from fear of the king of birds (Garuda).

sn: हत्वा पञ्चशतान् योधाञ्छरैराशिविषोपमैः॥ प्रायात् स शनकैर्वीरो धनंजयरथं प्रति।
en: Slaying five hundred warriors with his arrows resembling snakes of virulent poison, the heroic Satyaki proceeded slowly towards the car of Dhananjaya.

sn: तं प्रयान्तं नरश्रेष्ठं पुत्रो दुःशासनस्त्व॥ विव्याध नवभिस्तूर्ण शरैः संनतपर्वभिः।
en: Then as that foremost of men proceeding your son Dushasana pierced him quickly with nine shafts of depressed knots.

sn: स तु तं प्रतिविव्याध पञ्चभिर्निशितैः शरैः॥ रुक्मपुखैर्महेष्वासो गापत्रैरजिह्मगैः।
en: Him the fierce bowmen Satyaki pierced in return with five sharp shafts, all straight flying and furnished with golden as well as vulterine wings.

sn: सात्यकिं तु महाराज प्रहसन्निव भारत॥ दुःशासनस्त्रिभिर्विद्ध्वा पुनर्विव्याध पञ्चभिः।
en: But O Bharata, Dushasana, smiling a little, pierced Satyaki O king, first with three and then with five shafts,

sn: शैनेयस्तव पुत्रं तु हत्वा पञ्चभिराशुगैः॥ धनुश्चास्य रणे छित्त्वा विस्मयन्नर्जुनं ययौ।
en: Thereupon the grandson of Sini wounding your son with five swift-coursing arrows cutoff the latter's bow and then smiling a little proceeded towards Arjuna.

sn: ततो दुःशासनः क्रुद्धो वृष्णिरवीराय गच्छते॥ सर्वपारशवीं शक्तिं विससर्ज जिघांसया।
en: Thereat Dushasana, highly enraged and desirous of slaying the Vrishni hero as he was proceeding, hurled at him a lance capable of penetrating through all things.

sn: तां तु शक्तिं तदा घोरां तव पुत्रस्य सात्यकिः॥ चिच्छेद शतधा राजन् निशितैः कङ्कपत्रिभिः।
en: But that dreadful lance hurled by your son, Satyaki cut-off, O king, with whetted shafts furnished with wings of the Kanka bird.

sn: अथान्यद् धनुरादाय पुत्रस्तव जनेश्वर॥ सात्यकिं च शरैर्विद्ध्वा सिंहनादं ननर्द ह।
en: O ruler of men, then your son taking up another bow pierced Satyaki with his arrows and then uttered a loud war-cry.

sn: सात्यकिस्तु रणे क्रुद्धो मोहयित्वा सुतं तव॥ शरैरग्निशिखाकारैराजघान स्तनान्तरे। त्रिभिरेव महाभागः शरैः संनतपर्वभि।
en: Thereat Satyaki waxing wroth, stupefied your son and struck him on the centre of his chest with arrows resembling tongues of fire.

sn: सर्वायसैस्तीक्ष्णवक्त्रैः पुनर्विव्याध चाष्टभिः॥ दुःशासनस्तु विंशत्या सात्यकिं प्रत्यविध्यत।
en: He then once more pierced Dushasana with eight arrows made completely of iron and of sharp heads. Dushasana in return pierced Satyaki with twenty shafts of eminents parts.

sn: सात्वतोऽपि महाराज तं विव्याध स्तनान्तरे॥ त्रिभिरेव महाभागः शरैः संनतपर्वभिः।
en: He, of the Satvata race of eminent parts o mighty monarch, again pierced him on the breast with three arrows of straight knots.

sn: सारथिं च सुसंक्रुद्धः शरैः संनतपर्वभिः। ततोऽस्य वाहान निशितैः शरैर्जने महारथः॥
en: Then that mighty car-warrior, highly inflamed with rage, slew Dushasana's steeds with sharp arrows and his charioteer with numerous shafts of depressed knots.

sn: धनुरेकेन भल्लेन हस्तावापं च पञ्चभिः॥ ध्वजं च रथशक्तिं च भल्लाभ्यां परमास्त्रवित्। चिच्च्द विशिखैस्तीक्ष्णैस्तथोभौ पार्णिसारथी॥
en: Versed in the use of many excellent weapons Satyaki then cut-off Dushasana's bow with a single bhalla, his gloves with five and his chariot and chariot shaft, with a couple of broad-headed arrows with sharp shafts he cutoff his two Parshni drivers. Then Dushasana, deprived of his car, with his bow burst open, his charioteer and steeds slain.

sn: स च्छिन्नधन्वा विस्थो हताश्वो हतसारथिः। त्रिगर्तसेनापतिना स्वरथेनापवाहितः॥
en: Was carried away by the commander of the Trigartta divisions on his own chariot. O Bharata, then the grandson of Sini once more assailed him.

sn: तमभिद्रुत्य शैनेया मुहूर्तमिव भारत! न जघान महाबाहुर्भीमसेनवचः स्मरन्॥ भीमसेनेन तु वधः सुतानां तव भारत। प्रतिज्ञातः सभामध्ये सर्वेषामेव संयुगे॥
en: But he refrained from slaying him remembering the words of Bhimasena. O Bharata, amidst the assembly Bhimasena before swore to slay your sons. Then Satyaki, vanquishing Dushasana, quickly proceeded in the track in which Dhananjaya had proceeded, Oking.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच किं तस्यां मम सेनायां नासन् केचिन्महारथाः। ये तथा सात्यकिं यान्तं नैवाघ्नन् नाष्यवारयन्॥
en: Dhritarastra said Was there then, O Sanjaya, no mighty carwarrior in my entire army who could resist or slay Satyaki as he proceeded forward?

sn: एको हि समरे कर्म कृतवान् सत्यविक्रमः। शक्रतुल्यबलो युद्धे महेन्द्रो दानवेष्विव॥
en: Of indomitable prowess and possessed of strength equal to that of Indra himself, singlehanded he achieved feats amidst my troops like Indra achieving feats amidst the Danavas.

sn: अथवा शून्यमासीत् तद्येन यातः स सात्यकिः। हतभूयिष्ठमथवा येन यातः स सात्यकिः॥
en: Perhaps the track through which Satyaki passed was empty. Possessed of prowess in the true sense of the term, he alone has crushed numerous hosts, of mine.

sn: न सन्ति तस्मात् पुत्रा यत् कृतं वृष्णिवीरेण कर्म शंससि मे रणे। नैतदुत्सहते कर्तु कर्म शक्रोऽपि संजय॥
en: Tell me O Sanjaya, how the single-handed grandson Sini passed through that host of mine, which was fighting vigorously against him?

sn: संजय उवाच अश्रद्धेयमचिन्यं च कर्म तस्य महात्मनः। वृष्णयन्धकप्रवीरस्य श्रुत्वा मे व्यथितं मनः॥
en: Sanjaya said O monarch, the exertion and din that were then made by your troops, O king, teeming with cars, elephants, foot-soldiers, resembled that which occurs at the end of a Yuga.

sn: मे यथा संजय भाषसे। एको वै बहुला: सेनाः प्रामृद्गत् सत्यविक्रमः॥
en: 0 bestower of honour, when your assembled host daily increased in numerical strength before, I thought that another muster like that of your army had never been on earth.

sn: कथं च युध्यमानानामपक्रान्तो महात्मनाम्। एको बहूनां शैनेयस्तन्ममाचक्ष्व संजय॥
en: The Gods and the Charanas that then came there said, "this muster will be the last of its kind on the earth."

sn: राजन् सेनासमुद्योगो रथनागाश्वपत्तिमान्। तुमुलस्तव सैन्यानां युगान्तसदृशोऽभवत्॥
en: O king, the array, which was formed by Drona in view of a slaughter of Jayadratha, was such that its equal had never been formed on the face of the earth.

sn: आहूतेषु समूहेषु तव सैन्यस्य मानद। नाभूल्लोके समः कश्चित् समूह इति मे मतिः॥
en: Then the din that was made by the armies as they rushed to battle with one another, was as tremendous as one created by the ocean agitated with the vehemence of a mighty tempest.

sn: तत्र देवास्त्वभाषन्त चारणाश्च समागताः। एतदन्ताः समूहा वै भविष्यन्ति महीतले॥
en: In those two assembled hosts of the Pandavas and the Kurus, O foremost of men,
innumerable rulers of earth, numbering by hundred and thousand, were enrolled.

sn: न च वैतादृशो व्यूह आसीत् कश्चिद् विशाम्पते। यादृग् जयद्रथवधे द्रोणेन विहितोऽभवत्॥
en: Horripilating, dreadful and deafening was the uproar set up by those enraged heroes of resolute deeds, as they proceeded to battle.
