description: Continuous The fight between Bhima and Karna
sn: त्वरध्वं सर्वतो यत्ता राधेयस्य रथं प्रति। ततस्तव सुता राजञ्छ्रुत्वा भ्रातुर्वचो द्रुतम्॥
en: “Hie yourselves quickly near the car of Pandu's son.” Thereupon, o king, your sons hearing those words of your son.

description: Continuous The fight between Bhima and Karna
sn: अभ्ययुः पाण्डवं युद्धे विसृजन्तः शिलीमुखान्। चित्रोपचित्रश्चित्राक्षश्चारुचित्र: शरासनः॥
en: Rushed against Pandu's son in battle shooting numerous sharp arrows. They were Chitra, Upachitra, Chitraksha, Charuchitra, Chitrasana.

description: Continuous The fight between Bhima and Karna
sn: चित्रायुधश्चित्रवर्मा समरे चित्रयोधिनः। तानापतत एवाशु भीमसेनो महारथः॥ एकैकेन शरेणाजौ पातयामास ते सुतान्। ते हता न्यपतन् भूमौ वातरुग्णा इव दुमाः॥
en: Chitrayudha and Chitravarman, all versed in various modes of warfare. Then the mighty car-warrior Bhimasena slew all your sons with a single arrows, as they were quickly proceeding against him. Slain they fell down on the earth like trees broken by the vehemence of the tempest.

description: Continuous The fight between Bhima and Karna
sn: दृष्ट्वा विनिहतान् पुत्रांस्तव राजन् महारथान्। अश्रुपूर्णमुखः कर्णः क्षत्तुः सस्मार तद् वचः॥
en: Beholding your sons all mighty carwarriors slain, o king, Karna with a tearful countenance, began to think of those words of Khatva.

description: Continuous The fight between Bhima and Karna
sn: रथं चान्यं समास्थाय विधिवत् कल्पितं पुनः। अभ्ययात् पाण्डवं युद्धे त्वरमाणः पराक्रमी॥
en: Then that puissant hero, mounting on another duly furnished car, quickly rushed at the son of Pandu.

description: Continuous The fight between Bhima and Karna
sn: तावन्योन्यं शरैर्भित्त्वा स्वर्णपुजैः शिलाशितैः। व्यभ्राजेतां यथा मेघौ संस्यूतौ सूर्यरश्मिभिः॥
en: Piercing each other with arrows furnished with golden wings and whetted on stone, those two heroes appeared beautiful like two clouds fringed with the rays of the sun.

description: Continuous The fight between Bhima and Karna
sn: षट्त्रिंशद्भिस्ततो भल्लैर्निशितैस्तिग्मतेजनैः। व्यधमत् कवचं क्रुद्धः सूतपुत्रस्य पाण्डवः॥
en: Then Pandu's son, excited with rage cut-off the armour of Suta's son with thirty-six Vallas of great sharpness and energy.

description: Continuous The fight between Bhima and Karna
sn: सूतपुत्रोऽपि कौन्तेयं शरैः संनतपर्वभिः। पञ्चाशता महाबाहुर्विव्याध भरतर्षभ॥
en: The son of Suta O foremost of the Bharatas, the mighty-armed hero, pierced Kunti's son with fifty arrows of depressed knots.

description: Continuous The fight between Bhima and Karna
sn: रक्तचन्दनदिग्धाङ्गो शरैः कृतमहाव्रणौ। शोणिताक्तौ व्यराजेतां चन्द्रसूर्याविवोदितौ॥
en: Those two combatants then, smeared with red sandal-paste, covered with many wounds caused by each other's shaft and steeped in blood, appeared charming like the sun or the moon in full splendour.

description: Continuous The fight between Bhima and Karna
sn: तौ शोणितोक्षितैर्गात्रैः शरैश्छिन्नमनुच्छदौ। कर्णभीमौ व्यराजेतां निर्मुक्ताविव पन्नगौ॥
en: Then Karna and Bhima, with their bodies steeped in blood and armour shattered with arrows appeared beautiful like snakes freed from their sloughs.

description: Continuous The fight between Bhima and Karna
sn: व्याघ्राविव नरव्याघ्रौ दंष्ट्राभिरितरेतरम्। शरधारासृजौ वीरौ मेघाविव ववर्षतुः॥
en: Assailing each other like two tigers fighting with their teeth, those two foremost of men poured their showers of arrows on each other like two mighty clouds pouring rain.

description: Continuous The fight between Bhima and Karna
sn: वारणाविव चान्योन्यं विषाणाभ्यामरिंदमौ। निर्भिन्दन्तौ स्वगात्राणि सायकैश्चारु रेजतुः॥
en: Like two elephants goring each other with their tusks, those two subduers of foes mangling each other with their shafts, appeared highly beautiful.

description: Continuous The fight between Bhima and Karna
sn: नादयन्तौ प्रहर्षन्तौ विक्रीडन्तौ परस्परम्। मण्डलानि विकुर्वाणौ रथाभ्यां रथसत्तमौ॥
en: Roaring at each other and covering each other with their arrows, those two foremost of car-warriors seemed to play with each other, causing their chariots to describe various circles.

description: Continuous The fight between Bhima and Karna
sn: वृषाविवाथ नर्दन्तौ बलिनौ वासितान्तरे। सिंहाविव पराक्रान्तौ नरसिंहौ महाबलौ॥
en: Those two powerful heroes then appeared like two heifers roaring at each other for consorting with a cow in her season, those two foremost of men, endued with prowess, then looked like two mighty lions engaged with one another.

description: Continuous The fight between Bhima and Karna
sn: परस्परं वीक्षमाणौ क्रोधसंरक्तलोचनौ। युयुधाते महावी? शक्रवैरोचनी यथा॥
en: Looking at each other with eyes red in rage, those two heroes of mighty energy fought on with each other like Indra and Virochana.

description: Continuous The fight between Bhima and Karna
sn: ततो भीमो महाबाहुर्बाहुभ्यां विक्षिपन् धनुः। व्यराजत रणे राजन्सविद्युदिव तोयदः॥
en: Then the mighty-armed Bhima stretching his bow with both his hands, appeared beautiful like a mass of clouds charged with lightning flashes.

description: Continuous The fight between Bhima and Karna
sn: स नेमिघोषस्तनितश्चापविद्युच्छराम्बुभिः। भीमसेनमहामेघः कर्णपर्वतमावृणोत्॥
en: Then, O mighty monarch, the Bhima-cloud, having ihe twang of the bow for its peal of thunder and the arrows for showers of rain, began to drench the mountain constituted by Karna.

description: Continuous The fight between Bhima and Karna
sn: ततः शरसहस्रेण सम्यगस्तेन भारत। पाण्डवो व्यकिरत् कर्ण भीमो भीमपराक्रमः॥
en: Then that son of Pandu, Bhima of terrible prowess, 0 Bharata, covered Karna with thousands of arrows shot from his own bow.

description: Continuous The fight between Bhima and Karna
sn: तत्रापश्यंस्तव सुता भीमसेनस्य विक्रमम्। सुपुङ्खैः कङ्कवासोभिर्यत् कर्ण छादयच्छरैः॥ स नन्दयन् रणे पार्थ केशवं च यशस्विनम्। सात्यकिं चक्ररक्षौ च भीमः कर्णमयोधयत्॥ विक्रमं भुजयोर्वीर्य धैर्य च विदितात्मनः। पुत्रास्तव महाराज दृष्ट्वा विमनसोऽभवन्॥
en: Then your sons beheld the prowess of Bhimasena, when he covered Karna with arrows decked with beautiful wings made of the feathers of the Kanka bird. Thus then Bhima fought on with Karna, affording delight there by to Arjuna and the illustrious Keshava and Satyaki and his two protectors of carwheels. Then your sons, O mighty monarch, became depressed, seeing the prowess, the strength of arms and the patience of Bhima, who thoroughly knew his self.

description: Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima
sn: संजय उवाच भीमसेनस्य राधेयः श्रुत्वा ज्यातलनि: स्वनम्। नामृष्यत यथा मत्तो गजः प्रतिगजस्वनम्॥
en: Sanjaya said Then the son of Radha hearing the sound of the twanging of Bhima's bow and of the slappings of his palm, did not brook it, like an infuriate elephant not brooking the roar of its rival.

description: Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima
sn: सोऽपक्रम्य मुहूर्त तु भीमसेनस्य गोचरात्। पुत्रांस्तव ददर्शाथ भीमसेनेन पातितान्॥
en: Retiring for a moment only from the presence of Bhimasena, Karna looked at your sons felled by him.

description: Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima
sn: तानवेक्ष्य नरश्रेष्ठ विमना दुःखितस्तदा। निःश्वसन् दीर्घमुष्णं च पुनः पाण्डवमभ्ययात्॥
en: O foremost of men, beholding them he became cheerless and filled with sorrow; then breathing like a snake, he once more assailed Bhima.

description: Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima
sn: स ताम्रनयनः क्रोधाच्छ्वसन्निव महोरगः। बभौ कर्णः शरानस्यन् रश्मीनिव दिवाकरः॥
en: With his eyes coppery in rage and breathing like a fierce snake, Karna then shooting arrows, appeared beautiful like the sun shooting his myriad rays.

description: Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima
sn: किरणैरिव सूर्यस्य महीथ्रो भरतर्षभ। कर्णचापच्युतैर्बाणैः प्राच्छाद्यत वृकोदरः॥
en: Vrikodara then, O foremost of the Bharatas, was covered with those shafts shot from Karna's bow, as if with the scattering rays of the blazing sun.

description: Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima
sn: ते कर्णचापप्रभवाः शरा बर्हिणवाससः। विविशुः सर्वतः पार्थ वासायेवाण्डजा द्रुमम्॥
en: Diverse kinds of arrows furnished with wings of peacock-feathers and shot from the bow of Karna, then penetrated into the body of Pritha's son, like so many birds entering their nests on the tree.

description: Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima
sn: कर्णचापच्युता बाणा: सम्पतन्तस्ततस्ततः। रुक्मपुङ्खा व्यराजन्त हंसाः श्रेणीकृता इव॥
en: Arrows of golden wings shot from the bow of Karna appeared everywhere, like rows of swans (flying through the welkin).

description: Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima
sn: चापध्वजोपस्करेभ्यश्छत्रादीषामुखाद् युगात्। प्रभवन्तो व्यदृश्यन्त राजन्नाधिरथेः शराः॥
en: The arrows of Adhiratha's son were so numerous that they seemed to come out not only from his bow, but also, from his standard, Upaskara, umbrella and the shafts, yoke and bottom of his car.

description: Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima
sn: खं पूरयन् महावेगान् खगमान् गृध्रवाससः। सुवर्णविकृतांश्चित्रान् मुमोचाधिरथिः शरान्॥
en: Filling the sky, the son of Adhiratha showered arrows decked with gold and furnished with vulturine feathers, that ranged variously through the entire welkin.

description: Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima
sn: तमन्तकमिवायस्तमापतन्तं वृकोदरः। त्यक्त्वा प्राणानतिक्रम्य विव्याध निशितैः शरैः॥
en: Then reckless of his very life, Vrikodara got the better of his foe and then pierced the latter with a shaft as he was rushing like Death incarnate at him.

description: Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima
sn: तस्य वेगमसह्य स दृष्ट्वा कर्णस्य पाण्डवः। महतश्च शरौघांस्तान् न्यवारयत वीर्यवान्॥
en: Then beholding the unbearable charge of Karna and the shower of mighty arrows shot by him, Vrikodara flinched not in fear, inasmuch as he was possessed of mighty energy.

description: Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima
sn: ततो विधम्याधिस्थेः शरजालानि पाण्डवः। विव्याध कर्ण विंशत्या पुनरन्यैः शिलाशितैः॥
en: Then that son of Pandu shot net-works of arrows at the son of Adhiratha. He pierced Karna with twenty sharp arrows.

description: Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima
sn: यथैव हि स कर्णेन पार्थः प्रच्छादितः शरैः। तथैव स रणे कर्ण छादयामास पाण्डवः॥
en: As Pritha's son himself had been covered by Suta's son, even in the same manner was the latter now covered by the former with his arrows.

description: Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima
sn: दृष्ट्वा तु भीमसेनस्य विक्रमं युधि भारत। अभ्यनन्दंस्त्वदीयाश्च सम्प्रहृष्टाश्च चारणाः॥
en: Beholding then the prowess of Bhimasena in battle, 0 Bharata, even your troops applauded him and the Charanas were filled with delight.

description: Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima
sn: भूरिश्रवाः कृपो द्रौणिर्मद्रराजो जयद्रथः। उत्तमौजा युधामन्युः सात्यकिः केशवार्जुनौ॥
en: Then Bhurisravas, Kripa, the son of Drona, the ruler of the Madras, Jayadratha, Uttamoujas, Yudhamanyu, Satyaki, Keshava and Arjuna.

description: Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima
sn: कुरुपाण्डवप्रवरा दश राजन् महारथाः। साधु साध्विति वेगेन सिंहनादमथानदन्॥
en: These ten best of mighty car-warriors of the Kuru and the Pandava hosts, applauding Bhima with shouts of 'well-done' 'well-done' uttered their war-cries.

description: Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima
sn: तस्मिन् समुत्थिते शब्दे तुमुले लोमहर्षणे। अभ्यभाषत पुत्रस्ते राजन् दुर्योधनस्त्वरन्॥
en: When that dreadful and hair-stirring sound arose, your son, king Duryodhana, thus spoke.

description: Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima
sn: राज्ञः सराजपुत्रांश्च सोदर्याश्च विशेषतः। कर्ण गच्छत भद्रं वः परीप्सन्तो वृकोदरात्॥
en: Addressing the kings and princes of his army and specially his brothers. "May good betide you. Hie yourselves to the rescue of Karna from Vrikodara.

description: Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima
sn: पुरा निघन्ति राधेयं भीमचापच्युताः शराः। ते यतध्वं महेष्वासाः सूतपुत्रस्य रक्षणे॥
en: Yonder, the shafts shot from Bhima's bow are piercing Karna (to the quick). O mighty bowmen, do you all now exert vigourously for protecting the son of the charioteer."

description: Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima
sn: दुर्योधनसमादिष्टाः सोदर्याः सप्त भारत। भीमसेनमभिद्रुत्य संरब्धाः पर्यवारयन्॥
en: Commanded by Duryodhana, O sire, seven uterine (Kaurava) brothers, rushing with fury at Bhimnasena surrounded him on all sides.

description: Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima
sn: ते समासाद्य कौन्तेयमावृण्वशरवृष्टिभिः। पर्वतं वारिधाराभिः प्रावृषीव वलाहकाः॥
en: Encountering the son of Kunti, they poured their arrowy torrents on him, like clouds pouring rain on the mountain breast during the rainy season.

description: Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima
sn: तेऽपीडयन् भीमसेनं क्रुद्धाः सप्त महारथाः। प्रजासंहरणे राजन् सोमं सप्त ग्रहा इव।॥
en: Then those seven mighty car-warriors inflamed with rage, began to afflict Bhima, like the seven planets afflicting the Sun at the time of the universal annihilation, O king.

description: Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima
sn: ततो वेगेन कौन्तेयः पीडयित्वा शरासनम्। मुष्टिना पाण्डवो राजन् दृढेन सुपरिष्कृतम्॥
en: Thereupon, drawing his effulgent bow with great force and firm grasp, the son of Kunti.

description: Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima
sn: मनुष्यसमतां ज्ञात्वा सप्त संधाय सायकान्। तेभ्यो व्यसृजदायस्तः सूर्यरश्मिनिभान् प्रभुः॥
en: Knowing that his adversaries were nothing but men, fixed seven shafts on his bowstring. And then the mighty Bhima sped those arrows radiant like the solar rays, at them.

description: Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima
sn: निरस्यन्निव देहेभ्यस्तनयानामसूंस्तव। भीमसेनो महाराज पूर्ववैरमनुस्मरन्॥
en: Bhimasena then keep alive the memory of the former wrongs inflicted on them, sped those arrows as if for wrenching out the very lives out of your sons.

description: Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima
sn: ते क्षिप्ता भीमसेनेन शरा भारत भारतान्। विदार्य खं समुत्पेतुः स्वर्णपुङ्खाः शिलाशिताः॥
en: Those shafts furnished with golden wings and whetted on stone shot by Bhimasena, O Bharata, penetrating through the body of the Bharata princes, flew through the sky.

description: Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima
sn: तेषां विदार्य चेतांसि शरा हेमविभूषिताः। व्यराजन्त महाराज सुपर्णा इव खेचराः॥
en: Those gold-decked arrows tearing their hearts, looked beautiful, O mighty monarch, like birds of beautiful plumage.

description: Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima
sn: शोणितादिग्धवाजाग्राः सप्त हेमपरिष्कृताः। पुत्राणां तव राजेन्द्र पीत्वा शोणितमुद्गताः॥
en: Those seven arrows of the effulgence of molten gold, steeped in blood, came out, O king after having drank the life-blood of your sons.

description: Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima
sn: ते शरैर्भिन्नमर्माणो रथेभ्यः प्रापतन् क्षितौ। गिरिसानुरुहा भग्ना द्विपेनेव महाद्रुमाः॥
en: With their armour shattered by those arrows, your sons then fell down from their cars on the earth, like tall trees growing on the slopes of mountains, broken down by elephants.

description: Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima
sn: शत्रुजयः शत्रुसहश्चित्रश्चित्रायुधो दृढः। चित्रसेनो विकर्णश्च सप्तैते विनिपातिताः॥
en: Satrunjaya, Satrusaha, Chitra, Chitrayudha, Dridha, Chitrasena and Vikarna these seven sons of yours were then slain by Bhima.

description: Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima
sn: पुत्राणां तव सर्वेषां निहतानां वृकोदरः। शोचत्यतिभृशं दुःखाद् विकर्ण पाण्डवः प्रियम्॥
en: Of all your sons thus slain, Vrikodara lamented piteously for Vikarna who was very dear to the Pandavas.

description: Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima
sn: प्रतिज्ञेयं मया वृत्ता निहन्तव्यास्तु संयुगे। विकर्ण तेनासि हतः प्रतिज्ञा रक्षिता मया।॥
en: Bhima then said-"I vowed saying, You shall all be slain by me. O Vikarna, for this vow it is that you have been slain. And thus have I kept my bow inviolate.

description: Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima
sn: त्वमागाः समरं वीर क्षात्रधर्ममनुस्मरन्। ततो विनिहत: संख्ये युद्धधर्मो हि निष्ठुरः॥
en: O hero, you proceeded against me with hostile intentions, bearing in mind the duties of a Kshatriya. You were ever engaged in doing our, special the king's (Yudhishthira's) good.

description: Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima
sn: विशेषतो हि नृपतेस्तथास्माकं हिते रतः। न्यायतोऽन्यायतो वापि हतः शेते महाद्युतिः॥
en: It is therefore not fit that I should lament for you, O your of great effulgence.” O mighty monarch then slaying them before the very eyes of Radha's son.

description: Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima
sn: अगाधबुद्धिर्गाङ्गेयः क्षितौ सुरगुरोः समः। त्याजितः समरे प्राणांस्तस्माद् युद्धं हि निष्ठुरम्॥ तान् निहत्य महाबाहू राधेयस्यैव पश्यतः। सिंहनादरवं घोरमसृजत् पाण्डुनन्दनः॥
en: That son of Pandu uttered a dreadful warcry. The shout of that hero, then O Bharata, carried to the very virtuous king Yudhishthira as if the intelligence of his victory. Hearing that loud cry of that fierce bowman Bhimasena.

description: Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima
sn: स रवस्तस्य शूरस्य धर्मराजस्य भारत। आचख्याविव तद् युद्धं विजयं चात्मनो महत्॥ तं श्रुत्वा तु महानादं भीमसेनस्य धन्विनः। बभूव परमा प्रीतिधर्मराजस्य धीमतः॥ ततो दृष्टमना राजन् वादित्राणां महाखनैः। सिंहनादरवं भ्रातुः प्रतिजग्राह पाण्डवः॥ हर्षेण महता युक्तः कृतसंज्ञो वृकोदरे। अभ्ययात् समरे द्रोणं सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वरः॥
en: The very virtuous king Yudhishthira obtained great delight in battle. Then highly delighted, that son of Pandu, O mighty monarch, received the sound of the war-cry of his brother with the beating of drums and other musical instruments. After Vrikodara had given him that intelligence by the hint agreed upon by both, that foremost of persons Yudhishthira versed in the use of all weapons, joyfully rushed against Drona in that battle. On the other hand, O monarch, seeing thirty-one of your son's slain in battle, Duryodhana recalled to mind the words of Vidura thus, "those salutary words spoken by Vidura are now being realised.

description: Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima
sn: एकत्रिंशन्महाराज पुत्रांस्तव निपातितान्। हतान् दुर्योधनो दृष्ट्वा क्षत्तुः सस्मार तद् वचः॥ तदिदं समनुप्राप्तं क्षत्तुनिःश्रेयसं वचः। इति संचिन्त्य ते पुत्रो नोत्तरं प्रत्यपद्यत॥ दुर्बुद्धिरब्रवीत् तनयस्तव। सभामानाय्य पाञ्चाली कर्णेन सहितोऽल्पधीः॥ यच्च कर्णोऽब्रवीत् कृष्णां सभायां परुषं वचः। प्रमुख पाण्डुपुत्राणां तव चैव विशाम्पते॥
en: Thinking thus, king Duryodhana was unable to do what he should do. All those words that your wicked-minded and foolish son, urged on by Karna, said to that princess of the Panchala race, having brought her in the assembly shall; also all those harsh words which Karna himself addressed in the assembly hall to her before yourself and the sons of Pandu, O monarch, at your and the Kauravas' hearing words to this effect, 'O Krishna, the

description: Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima
sn: यद् द्यूतकाले
en: sessamum Pandavas are destroyed and they have fallen into eternal hell; so do you choose a second husband'-the result of all these has now overtaken you.

description: Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima
sn: शृण्वतस्तव राजेन्द्र कौरवाणां च सर्वशः। विनष्टाः पाण्डवाः कृष्णे शाश्वतं नरकं गताः॥ पतिमन्यं वृणीष्वेति तस्येदं फलमागतम्। यच षण्ढतिलादीनि परुषाणि तवात्मजैः। श्रावितास्ते महात्मानः पाण्डवाः कोपयिष्णुभिः॥ तं भीमसेनः क्रोधाग्नि त्रयोदश समाः स्थितम्। उद्गिरंस्तव पुत्राणामन्तं गच्छति पाण्डवः॥
en: Then again, O you of Kuru's race, various abusive language like kernel, without seeds were directed by your enraged sons to these illustrious ones, viz., the sons of Pandu, Bhimasena vomitting forth the fire of wrath held in check for these thirteen years, is now achieving the destruction of your sons.

description: Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima
sn: विलपंश्च बहु क्षत्ता शमं नालभत त्वयि। सपुत्रो भरतश्रेष्ठ तस्य भुटव फलोदयम्॥
en: Entreating you repeatedly, Khattwa failed to bend you towards peace. O foremost of the Bharatas, now do you, together with your son, suffer the consequences (of your folly).

description: Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima
sn: त्वया वृद्धेन धीरेण कार्यतत्त्वार्थदर्शिना। न कृतं सुहृदां वाक्यं दैवमत्र परायणम्॥
en: That you old, patient and capable of foreseeing the consequences of acts as you are, would not accept the well-meaning words of your friends, is due to the influence of (adverse) fate.

description: Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima
sn: तन्मा शुचो नरव्याघ्र तवैवापनयो महान्। विनाशहेतुः पुत्राणां भवानेव मतो मम॥
en: O foremost of men, it therefore behoves you not to weep. Yours is the greatest fault in the matter. In my opinion your are the cause of the ruin of your sons.

description: Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima
sn: हतो विकर्णो राजेन्द्र चित्रसेनश्च वीर्यवान्। प्रवराश्चात्मजानां ते सुताश्चान्ये महारथाः॥
en: O foremost of kings, Vikarna and the puissant Chitrasena, have been slain; as also numerous other mighty car-warriors and your other sons have fallen.

description: Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima
sn: यानन्यान् ददृशे भीमश्चक्षुर्विषयमागतान्। पुत्रांस्तव महाराज त्वरया ताञ्जघान ह॥
en: O mighty-armed one, other sons of yours, who became the objects of Bhima's sight, were slain by him in a moment,

description: Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima
sn: त्वत्कृते ह्यहमद्राक्षं दह्यमानां वरूथिनीम्। सहस्रशः शरैर्मुक्तैः पाण्डवेन वृषेण च॥
en: It was through your fault that I had to see our army consumed in thousands by the shafts discharged by Pandu's son and by Vrisha. numerous other mighty car-warriors and your other sons have fallen.

description: Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima
sn: यानन्यान् ददृशे भीमश्चक्षुर्विषयमागतान्। पुत्रांस्तव महाराज त्वरया ताञ्जघान ह॥
en: O mighty-armed one, other sons of yours, who became the objects of Bhima's sight, were slain by him in a moment,

description: Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima
sn: त्वत्कृते ह्यहमद्राक्षं दह्यमानां वरूथिनीम्। सहस्रशः शरैर्मुक्तैः पाण्डवेन वृषेण च॥
en: It was through your fault that I had to see our army consumed in thousands by the shafts discharged by Pandu's son and by Vrisha.

description: Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच महानपनयः सूत ममैवात्र विशेषतः। स इदानीमनुप्राप्तो मन्ये संजय शोचतः॥
en: Dhritarashtra said I see, O son of a charioteer, that mine has been the greatest fault in this matter; O Sanjaya, the consequences have now overtaken me, grieve though I may!

description: Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima
sn: यद् गतं तद् गतमिति ममासीन्मनसि स्थितम्। इदानीमत्र किं कार्य प्रकरिष्यामि संजय॥
en: Hitherto I thought that what is gone for good. But, O Sanjaya, what measures is gone should now be adopted.

description: Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima
sn: यथा ह्येष क्षयो वृत्तो ममापनयसम्भवः। वीराणां तन्ममाचक्ष्व स्थिरीभूतोऽस्मि संजय॥
en: I have now become calm, O Sanjaya; relate to me how this slaughter of heroes is went onslaughter that owes its origin to my evil policy.

description: Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima
sn: संजय उवाच कर्णभीमौ महाराज पराक्रान्तौ महाबलौ। बाणवर्षाण्यसृजतां वृष्टिमन्ताविवाम्बुदौ॥
en: Sanjaya said O mighty monarch, then the two powerful heroes Karna and Bhima began to pour showers of arrows, like two rain clouds pouring their contents.

description: Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima
sn: भीमनामाङ्किता बाणा: स्वर्णपुलाः शिलाशिताः। विविशुः कर्णमासाद्य च्छिन्दन्त इव जीवितम्॥
en: Then gold-winged arrows, whetted on stone and engraved with the name of Bhima, reaching Karna, penetrated thought him cutting him to the very quick.

description: Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima
sn: तथैव कर्णनिर्मुक्ता:शरा बर्हिणवाससः। छादयाञ्चकिरे वीरं शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः॥
en: Similarly Bhima was pierced hundreds and thousands of times by the arrows shot by Karna, that resembled snakes of virulent poison.

description: Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima
sn: तयोः शरैर्महाराज सम्पतद्भिः समन्ततः। बभूव तत्र सैन्यानां संक्षोभः सागरोत्तरः॥
en: An agitation like that produced in the ocean, was then produced in your troops by the arrows of them both, falling on all sides.

description: Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima
sn: भीमचापच्युतैर्बाणैस्तव सैन्यमरिंदम। अवध्यत चमूमध्ये घोरैराशीविषोपमैः॥
en: O subduer of foes, shot from Bhima's bow, shafts resembling dreadful snakes, began to slay your troops amidst your own army.

description: Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima
sn: वारणैः पतितै राजन् वाजिभिश्च नरैः सह। अदृश्यत मही कार्णा वातभग्नैरिव दुमैः॥
en: With fallen elephants, horses and men, the Earth became covered and looked as if covered with trees broken by the force of the wind.

description: Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima
sn: ते वध्यमानाः समरे भीमचापच्युतैः शरैः। प्राद्रवंस्तावका योधाः किमेतदिति चाब्रुवन्॥
en: Wounded with the arrows shot from Bhima's bow, your troops then began to fly away from the field saying what is it?

description: Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima
sn: ततो व्युदस्तं तत सैन्यंसिन्धुसौवीरकौरवम्। प्रोत्सारितं महावेगैः कर्णपाण्ड्योः शरैः॥
en: That host composed of the Sindhus, the Souviras and the Kauravas, afflicted and wounded with the terrible shafts of Bhima and

description: Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima
sn: ते
en: Karna, was then driven back to a great distance.

description: Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima
sn: शूरा हतभूयिष्ठा हताश्वरथवारणाः। उत्सृज्य भीमकर्णौ च सर्वतो व्यद्रवन् दिशः॥
en: Then those heroes, with their ranks thinned and their horses and elephants slain, fled in all directions, leaving Bhima and Karna on the field.

description: Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima

sn: मूलपुष्पफलाहारो व्रतेषु नियमेषु च। उचितस्त्वं वने भीम न त्वं युद्धविशारदः॥
en: Devouring esculent roots, fruits fruits and flowers, it is proper that you should engage yourself in the observance of vows and rites, in the woods. O Bhima, you know not how to fight!

description: , Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima torrents arrows
sn: क्व युद्धं व मुनित्वं च वनं गच्छ वृकोदर। न त्वं युद्धोचितस्तात वनवासरतिर्भवान्॥
en: Vast is the difference, O Vrikodara, between fighting and the occupation of a hermit. So, do you repair to the forest O master; you are not capable of fighting and have an inclination for dwelling in the wood.

description: , Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima torrents arrows
sn: सूदान् भृत्यजनान् दासांस्त्वं गृहे त्वरयन् भृशम्। योग्यस्ताडयितुं क्रोधाद् भोजनार्थ वृकोदर॥
en: Urging cooks and servants and orderlies to make haste in making your dinner ready, O Vrikodara, you are capable of striking and reproving them.

description: , Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima torrents arrows
sn: मुनिर्भूत्वाथवा भीम फलान्यादत्ख दुर्मते। वनाय व्रज कौन्तेय न त्वं युद्धविशारदः॥
en: Becoming a hermit, O Bhima, do you began eating fruits, O wicked-minded wretch. O son of Kunti, betake to the forest, for you are incapable of fighting.

description: , Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima torrents arrows
sn: फलमूलाशने शक्तस्त्वं तथातिथिपूजने। न त्वां शत्रसमुद्योगे योग्यं मन्ये वृकोदर॥
en: You are fit, O Vrikodara, for eating large quantities of esculent roots and for receiving and welcoming guests, O Vrikodara, I do not consider you fit for wielding weapons.”

description: , Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima torrents arrows
sn: कौमारे यानि वृत्तानि विप्रियाणि विशाम्पते। तानि सर्वाणि चाप्येव रूक्षाण्यश्रावयद् भृशम्॥
en: O monarch, he was also reminded by Karna in harsh language, of all the wrongs done to him in his days of childhood.

description: , Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima torrents arrows
sn: अथैनं तत्र संलीनमस्पृशद् धनुषा पुनः। प्रहसंश्च पुनर्वाक्यं भीममाह वृषस्तदा॥
en: And once more as Bhima greatly weakened stood there, Vrishasena poked him with horn of his bow and smilingly addressed these words to him.

description: , Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima torrents arrows
sn: योद्धव्यं मारिषान्यत्र न योद्धव्यं च मादृशैः। मादृशैर्युध्यमानानामेतचान्यच विद्यते॥
en: O child, you should fight with others and not with men like myself. Those who fight with men like myself, have to undergo this and many things else.

description: , Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima torrents arrows
sn: गच्छ वा यत्र तौ कृष्णौ तौ त्वां रक्षिष्यतो रणे। गृहं वा गच्छ कौन्तेय किं ते युद्धेन बालक॥
en: Hie yourself to the spot where the Krishnas are and they will then protect you in battle. Or, O son of Kunti, return to your home, O child what is the good of fighting?"

description: , Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima torrents arrows
sn: कर्णस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा भीमसेनोऽतिदारुणम्। उवाच कर्ण प्रहसन् सर्वेषां शृण्वतां वचः॥
en: Then hearing those very harsh words of Karna, Bhima smilingly spoke these words to him at the presence of every body.

description: , Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima torrents arrows
sn: जितस्त्वमसकृद् दुष्ट कत्थसे किं वृथाऽऽत्मना। जयाजयौ महेन्द्रस्य लोके दृष्टौ पुरातनैः॥
en: "O wicked fool! Your have been repeatedly defeated by me, how then can you indulge in this vain brag? The ancients have seen the victory and defeat of the mighty Indra himself!

description: , Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima torrents arrows
sn: मल्लयुद्धं मया सार्ध कुरु दुष्कुलसम्भव। महाबलो महाभोगी कीचको निहतो यथा॥
en: O scion of a mean family, come and wrestle with me. Then even as I have slain the mighty and luxurious Kichaka.

description: , Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima torrents arrows
sn: तथा त्वां घातयिष्यामि पश्यत्सु सर्वराजसु। भीमस्य मतमाज्ञाया कर्णो बुद्धिमतां वरः॥
en: I will slay you before the very eyes of all the kings. “But knowing Bhima's intention, that foremost of intelligent beings Karna.

description: , Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima torrents arrows
sn: विररामरणात् तस्मात् पश्यतां सर्वधन्विनाम्। एवं तं विरथं कृत्वा कर्णो राजन् व्यकत्थयत्॥
en: Refrained from that fight before they very eyes of the bowmen present. Thus o king, making Bhima carless, Karna reproved him in such harsh language.

description: , Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima torrents arrows
sn: प्रमुखे वृष्णिसिंहस्य पार्थस्य च महात्मनः। ततो राजशिलाधौताशराशाखामृगध्वजः॥ प्राहिणोत् सूतपुत्राय केशवेन प्रचोदितः। ततः पार्थभुजोत्सृष्टाः शराः कनकभूषणाः॥
en: In the presence of that best of the Vrishnis and the son of Pritha. Then O king, the apebannered Arjuna, being urged on by Keshava, sped a the son of Suta numerous arrows whetted on stone. Then those gold-decked arrows hurled by the force Partha's arm.

description: , Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima torrents arrows
sn: गाण्डीवप्रभवाः कर्ण हंसाः क्रौञ्चमिवाविशन्। स भुजङ्गैरिवाविष्टैर्गाण्डीवप्रेषितैः शरैः॥
en: And issuing out of the Gandiva, penetrated into Karna's body like so many cranes entering into the Krouncha mountains. Wounding Karna with those arrows shot from the Gandiva, that entered his body like so many snakes.

description: , Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima torrents arrows
sn: भीमसेनादपासेधत् सूतपुत्रं धनंजयः। स च्छिन्नधन्वा भीमेन धनंजयशराहतः॥
en: Dhananjaya, drove away the son of Suta from the vicinity of Bhimasena. Then with his bow burst open by Bhima and pierced sore with the arrows of Dhananjaya.

description: , Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima torrents arrows
sn: कर्णो भीमदपासासीद् रथेन महता दुतम्। भीमोऽपि सात्यकेहिं समारुह्य नरर्षभः॥
en: Karna fled away from Bhima being borne hastily on his swift-coursing car. Bhima also, O foremost of men, ascending Satyaki's Vehicle.

description: , Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima torrents arrows
sn: अन्यवयाद् भ्रातरं संख्ये पाण्डवं सव्यसाचिनम्। ततः कर्णे समुद्दिश्य त्वरमाणो धनंजयः॥ नाराचं क्रोधताम्राक्षः प्रैषीन्मृत्युमिवान्तकः। स गरुत्मानिवाकाशे प्रार्थयन् भुजगोत्तमम्॥
en: Followed his brother Savyasachin the son of Pandu in battle. Then Dhananjaya with his eyes red in rage and with great celerity sped at Karna a Naracha like the Destroyer urging death forward. Then like. Garuda ranging through the welkin in quest of a mighty snake.

description: , Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima torrents arrows
sn: नाराचोऽभ्यपतत् कर्ण तूर्ण गाण्डीवचोदितः। तमन्तरिक्षे नाराचं द्रौणिश्चिच्छेद पत्रिणा॥
en: That Naracha shot form the Gandiva, flew through the sky towards Karna in all quickness. Then the son of Drona cut-off that Naracha as it coursed through the sky, with a singed arrows.

description: , Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima torrents arrows
sn: धनंजय भयात् कर्णमुजिहीर्षन् महारथः ततो द्रौणिं चतुःषष्ट्या विव्याध कुपितोऽर्जुनः॥
en: Desirous as he was of freeing Karna from his fear of Dhananjaya. Thereupon Arjuna inflamed with rage, pierced Drona's son with sixty-four arrows.

description: , Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima torrents arrows
sn: शिलीमुखैमहाराज् मा गास्तिष्ठेति चाब्रवीत्। स तु मत्तगजाकीर्णमानकं रथसंकुलम्।। १२० तूर्णमभ्याविशद् द्रौणिर्धनंजयशरादितः। ततः सुवर्णपृष्ठानां चापानां कूजतां रणे॥१२१ शब्दं गाण्डीवघोषेण कौन्तेयोऽभ्यभवद् बली। धनंजयस्तथा यान्तं पृष्ठतौ द्रौणिमभ्यगात्॥ नातिदीर्घमिवाध्वानं शरैः संत्रासयन् बलम्। विदार्य देहान् नाराचैर्नरवारणवाजिनाम्॥१२३
en: Whetted on stone and O monarch addressed the latter saying 'Fly not'. But afflicted with the arrows of Dhananjaya, Drona's son quickly entered into the army teeming with infuriated elephants and numerous chariots. Then the puissant son of Kunti drowned the sound of the other twangs of bows decked with gold, with the tremendous twang of his own bow Gandiva. Then the mighty Dhananjaya pursued Drona's son from behind who was thus flying and who had not then proceeded to a long way, frightening him all the way with his shafts. Tearing open the body of men, elephants and steeds with his Narachas.

description: , Continuous The fight between Karna and Bhima torrents arrows
sn: कङ्कबर्हिणवासोभिर्बलं व्यधमदर्जुनः। तद् बलं भरतश्रेष्ठ सवाजिद्विपमानवम्॥ पाकशासनिरायत्तः पार्थः स निजघान ह॥
en: Furnished with wings made of the feathers of the peacock and the Kanka, Arjuna began to agitate that army of yours. O foremost of the Bharatas, Partha, the son of Pakasasani (Indra) then began to carnage that host of yours, consisting of horses elephants and men.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच अहन्यहनि मे दीप्तं यशः पतति संजय। हता मे बहवो योधा मन्ये कालस्य पर्ययम्॥
en: Dhritarashtra said Day by day, O Sanjaya, by blazing fame is dwindling away. Numerous warriors of my side are being slain. I consider all this to be due to the adverse influence of Fate.

sn: धनंजयः सुसंकुद्धः प्रविष्टो मामकं बलम्। रक्षितं द्रौणिकर्णाभ्यामप्रवेश्यं सुरैरपि॥
en: Inflamed with wrath, Dhananjaya has entered into my host which is protected by Drona's son and Karna and which is therefore incapable of being penetrated into by the very celestials.

sn: ताभ्यामूर्जितवीर्याभ्यामाप्यायितपराक्रमः। सहितः कृष्णभीमाभ्यां शिनीनामृषभेण च॥
en: Dhananjaya's prowess has increased in consequence of his being united with that foremost of the Sinis and those two of burning energy, namely Krishna and Bhima.

sn: तदाप्रभृति मां शोको दहत्यग्निरिवाशयम्। ग्रस्तानिव प्रपश्यामि भूमिपालान् ससैन्धवान्।॥
en: Like fire burning down a heap of dry grass, grief is corroding my heart since I have heard of Dhananjaya's entrance into my army. I see that all the king's of the earth with the ruler of the Sindhus amongst them, are under the influence of adverse Fate.

sn: अप्रियं सुमहत् कृत्वा सिन्धुराजः किरीटिनः। चक्षुर्विषयमा यमापन्नः कथं जीवितमाप्नुयात्॥
en: Having inflicted a terrible injury to the diadem-checked Arjuna, how could the ruler of the Sindhu's escape with his life, when he would become the object of Arjuna's sight?

sn: अनुमानाच पश्यामि नास्ति संजय सैन्धवः। युद्धं तु तद् यथावृत्तं तन्ममाचक्ष्व तत्त्वतः॥
en: O Sanjaya, I can imagine even now that the king of the Sindhus no longer lives. Therefore, tell me how in reality did that battle rage then.

sn: यश्च विक्षोभ्य महतीं सेनामालोड्य चासकृत्। एकः प्रविष्टः संक्रुद्धो नलिनीमिव कुञ्जरः॥
en: He that had single-handed and unsupported entered into and agitated my army, even as an infuriate elephant enters and crushes a group of lotuses.

sn: तस्य मे वृष्णिवीरस्य ब्रूहि युद्धं यथातथम्। धनंजयार्थे यत्तस्य कुशलो ह्यसि संजय॥
en: Tell me of the feats of that Vrishnipero, as he achieved them, struggling to help Dhananjaya in battle. O Sanjaya, you are an expert in narration.

sn: संजय उवाच तथा तु वैकर्तनपीडितं तं भीमं प्रयान्तं पुरुषप्रवीरम् समीक्ष्य राजन् नरवीरमध्ये शिनिप्रवीरोऽनुययौ रथेन।॥
en: Sanjaya said Seeing that foremost of men namely Bhima, proceed, although pierced with the arrows of Vikartana's son in the midst of so many heroes, O monarch, that excellent warrior of the Sini race, followed him on his chariot.

sn: नदन् यथा वज्रधरस्तपान्ते ज्वलन् यथा जलदान्ते च सूर्येः। निघ्नन्नमित्रान् धनुषा दृढेन स कम्पयंस्तव पुत्रस्य सेनाम्॥
en: Uttering thundering roars like the clouds at the expiration of the summer season or burning like the sun at the end of the rainy season, he began to slaughter his foes by means of his tough bow and caused the troops of your son repeatedly to tremble.

sn: तं यान्तमश्वै रजतप्रकाशैरायोधने वीरवरं नदन्तम्। नाशक्नुवन् वारयितुं त्वदीयाः सर्वे तथा भारत माधवाग्रयम्॥
en: When that foremost of Madhu's race careered on the field on his chariot drawn by horses of argentine hue and roared fiercely, O Bharata, there was none amongst your troops who could then check him.

sn: अमर्षपूर्णस्त्वनिवृत्तयोधी शरासनी काञ्चनवर्मधारी। अलम्बुषः मवारयद् राजवरोऽभिपत्य॥
en: Then that foremost of kings namely Alambusha excited with wrath, untreatreating in battle, armed with a bow and covered in a golden coat of mail, advancing against Satyaki checked his carreer in battle.

sn: तयोरभूद् भारत सम्प्रहारो यथाविधो नैव बभूव कश्चित्। प्रेक्षन्त एवाहवशोभिनौ तौ योधास्त्वदीयाश्च परे च सर्वे॥
en: Then encounter that thereupon raged between them was unparalleled. Your soldiers and the enemy's troops, giving up the fight became spectators of that battle.

sn: रलम्बुषो राजवरः प्रसा। अनागतानेव तु तान् पृषत्कां श्चिच्छेद बाणैः शिनिपुङ्गवोऽपि॥
en: The foremost of all kings viz., king Alambusha, then sped at Satyaki ten shafts; but that foremost of scions of the Sini race, cut-off all those shafts, with those of his own, before they could reach him.

sn: राकर्णपूर्णैर्निशितैः सपुकैः। विव्याध देहावरणं विदार्य ते सात्यकेराविविशुः शरीरम्॥
en: Thereupon, Alambusha pierced Satyaki with three sharp arrows furnished with beautiful wings blazing as fire and discharged from the bow drawn back to the very ear. These arrows penetrating through Satyaki's coat of mail mangled his body.

sn: विदार्य बाणैर्निशितैर्व्वलद्भिः। नश्वांश्चतुर्भिश्चतुरः प्रसा॥
en: Then piercing Satyaki's body with those keen pointed and effulgent arrows, poisoned and of the energy of fire or the wind, Alambusha, with four other shafts, struck the four silver-white steeds of Satyaki with great force.

sn: तथा तु तेनाभिहतस्तरस्वी। नप्ता शिनेश्चक्रधरप्रभावः। रश्वांश्चतुर्भिनिजघान बाणैः॥
en: Possessing prowess and activity equal to those of that bearer of the discus (Krishna), the grandson of Sini, thus struck by Alambusha, slew the latter's fours steeds with four keen arrows.

sn: अथास्य सूतस्य शिरो निकृत्य भल्लेन कालानलसंनिभेन। सकुण्डलं पूर्णशशिप्रकाशं भ्राजिष्णु वक्त्रं निचकर्त देहात्॥
en: Then cutting off the head of Alambusha's charioteer, he severed with a broad-headed arrows fierce as the yoga-fire from the former's trunk his head graced with excellent ear-rings and beautiful as the full moon.

sn: निहत्य तं पार्थिवपुत्रपौत्रं संख्ये यदूनामृषभः प्रमाथी। ततोऽन्वयादर्जुनमेव वीरः। सैन्यानि राजंस्तव संनिवार्य॥
en: Having slain that scion of a mace whose descendants are all kings, the illustrious descendant of the Yadu race that hero capable of crushing the hostile army, advanced towards Arjuna, o king, checking in his progress of soldiers of the enemy.

sn: अन्वागतं वृष्णिवीरं समीक्ष्य तथारिमध्ये परिवर्तमानम्। मन्तं कुरूणामिषुभिर्बलानि पुनः पुनर्वायुमिवाभ्रपूगान्॥
en: O monarch, thus careering amongst his enemies, the Vrishni hero, when following in the track of Arjuna, was seen with his shafts to destroy repeadly the Kuru host, like the raging tempest scattering masses of clouds.

sn: ततोऽवहन् सैन्धवाः साधुदान्ता गोक्षीरकुन्देन्दुहिमप्रकाशाः। सुवर्णजालावतताः सदश्वा यतो यतः कामयते नृसिंहः॥
en: Where-ever that foremost of men desired to go, he was borne thither by those best steeds of his that were of Sindhu breed, well-broken, tame, white as milk or the Kunda flower or the moon or the snow and that were decked with housings and traces of gold.

sn: रन्ये च योधास्त्वरितास्त्वदीयाः। कृत्वा मुखं भारत योधमुख्यं दुःशासनं त्वत्सुतमाजमीढ॥
en: Then, O descendant of Ajamidas race, yours sons, united with other soldiers of your army, quickly rushed against Satyaki, making that foremost of warrior's viz., Dushasana their leader.

sn: ते सर्वतः सम्परिवार्य संख्ये शैनेयमाजघ्नुरनीकसाहाः। स चापि तान् प्रवरः सात्वतानां न्यवारयद् बाणजालेन वीरः॥
en: Those commanders of divisions surrounding the grandson of Sini on all sides, began to wound him viz., that foremost of the Satwata's; that hero Satyaki resisted them with showers of his arrows.

sn: निवार्य तांस्तूर्णममित्रघाती नप्ता शिनेः पत्रिभिरग्निकल्पैः। नुद्यम्य बाणासनमाजमीढ॥ ततोऽर्जुनो हर्षमवाप संख्ये कृष्णश्च दृष्ट्वा पुरुषप्रवीरम्॥
en: Resisting them all quickly with his shafts of fiery energy, that slayer of hostile heroes, the grandson of Sini uplifting his bow, slew the horses of Dushasana's chariot; then Arjuna and Krishna seeing that foremost of men Satyaki thus fight in battle became highly delighted.

sn: संजय उवाच तमुद्यतं महाबाहुं दुःशासनरथं प्रति। त्वरितं त्वरणीयेषु धनंजयजयैषिणम्॥ क्रुद्धाःय त्रिगर्तानां महेष्वासाः सुवर्णविकृतध्वजाः। सेनासमुद्रमाविष्टमनन्तं पर्यवारयन्॥
en: Sanjaya said Then the mighty archers of the Trigartta clan, all owning gold-decked standards, surrounded on all sides the mighty-armed Satyaki-that hero who performed with activity everything that demanded promptness and who having penetrated into that host fathomless as the ocean, was advancing against Dushasana's chariot, for giving victory of Dhananjaya.

sn: अथैनं रथवंशेन सर्वतः संनिवार्य ते। अवाकिरज्छरवातैः परमधन्विनः॥
en: Then all those excellent bowmen waxing worth and surrounding him with hosts of cars on all sides, began to pour their arrowy showers on them.

sn: अजयद् राजपुत्रांस्तान् भ्राजमानान् महारणे। एकः पञ्चाशतं शत्रून् सात्यकिः सत्यविक्रमः॥
en: But the unsupported Satyaki of prowess incapable of being baffled, conquered his fifth antagonists, all princes of the Trigartta race looking very beautiful in battle.

sn: सम्प्राप्य भारतीमध्यं तलघोषसमाकुलम्। असिशक्तिगदापूर्णमप्लवं सलिलं यथा॥
en: Then he reached the centre of the Bharata host echoing with the sound of palm-strokes and abounding in swords, lances and maces and looking like the unfordable ocean itself.

sn: तत्राद्भुतमपश्याम शैनेयचरितं रणे। प्रतीच्यां दिशितं दृष्ट्वा प्राच्यां पश्यामि लाघवात्॥
en: We then behold the wonderful conduct of Sini's grandson, for beholding him now in the Western direction, we immediately after beheld him in the Eastern direction, so great indeed was his lightness of movements.

sn: उदीची दक्षिणां प्राची प्रतीची विदिशस्तथा। नृत्यन्त्रिवाचरच्छूरो यथा रथशतं तथा॥
en: Then if dancing and resembling, although alone, a hundred car-warriors, that hero careered in the East, West, North and South and all the subsidiary directions. as

sn: तद् दृष्ट्वा चरितं तस्य सिंहविक्रान्तगामिनः। त्रिगर्ताः संन्यवर्तन्त संतप्ताः स्वजनं प्रति॥
en: Beholding that conduct of that one of lionlike prowess and tread, the Trigartta warriors greatly afflicted, fell back upon the division of their clansmen.

sn: तमन्ये शूरसेनानां शूराः संख्ये न्यवारयन्। नियच्छन्तः शरव्रातैर्मतं द्विपमिवाङ्कुशैः॥
en: Thereafter the brave warriors viz., the Surasenas tried to resist Satyaki wounding him with arrowy showers, like a guide percing his mad elephant with the goad.

sn: तैर्व्यवाहरदार्यात्मा मुहूर्तादेव सात्यकिः। ततः कलिङ्गैर्युयुधे सोऽचिन्त्यबलविक्रमः॥
en: The illustrious Satyaki fought with them only for a while and then that hero of inconceivable prowess commenced his fight with the Kalingas.

sn: तां च सेनामतिक्रम्य कलिङ्गानां दुरत्ययाम्। अथ पार्थ महाबाहुर्धनंजयमुपासदत्॥
en: Passing through the division of the Kalingas that was incapable being passed through, the mighty-armed Satyaki approached Dhananjaya the son of Pritha.

sn: तरन्निव जले श्रान्तो यथा स्थलमुपेयिवान्। तं दृष्ट्वा पुरुषव्याघ्रं युयुधानः समाश्वसत्॥
en: Then like an exhausted swimmer reaching land, the heroic Yuyudhana became comforted on obtaining sight of Dhananjaya that foremost of men.

sn: तमायान्तमभिप्रेक्ष्य केशवः पार्थमब्रवीत्। असावायति शैनेयस्तव पार्थ पदानुगः॥
en: Beholding Satyaki Satyaki come them, Keshava addressing Arjuna said "There comes the grandson of Sini, O son of Pritha, pursuing the track (opened by you).

sn: एष शिष्यः सखा चैव तव सत्यपराक्रमः। सर्वान् योधांस्तृणीकृत्य विजिग्ये पुरुषर्षभः॥
en: O your of true prowess, Satyaki is your friend and pupil. That foremost of men, holding all the warriors of the hostile host a pins fee, has vanquished them all. near

sn: एष कौरवयोधानां कृत्वा घोरमुपद्रवम्। तव प्राणैः प्रियतमः किरीटिन्नेति सात्यकिः॥
en: Inflicting dreadful loss upon the Kauravas, Satyaki dear unto you like your own life, is coming towards you, O diadem-decked one!

sn: एष द्रोणं तथा भोजं कृतवर्माणमेव च। कदर्थीकृत्य विशिखैः फाल्गुनाभ्येति सात्यकिः॥
en: Having worsted with his arrows, Drona and Kritavarman of the Bhoja race, this Satyaki is approaching you, O Phalguna.

sn: धर्मराजप्रियान्वेषी हत्वा योधान् वरान् वरान्। शूरश्चैव कृतास्रश्च फाल्गुनाभ्येति सात्यकिः॥
en: Having slain numerous warriors all best of their class, the valorous Satyaki ever solicitous of the welfare of Yudhishthira and accomplished in the use of weapons, is approaching you, O Arjuna.

sn: कृत्वा सुदुष्करं कर्म सैन्यमध्ये महाबलः। तव दर्शनमन्विच्छन् पाण्डवाभ्येति सात्यकिः॥
en: O son of Pandu, the puissant Satya is coming to you have achieved numerous difficult feats in the midst of the Kaurava host.

sn: बहूनेकरथेनाजौ योधयित्वा महारथान्। आचार्यप्रमुखान् पार्थ प्रयात्येष स सात्यकिः॥
en: Having encountered on a single car many mighty car-warriors having Drona at their head, the heroic Satyaki is approaching you, O Arjuna.

sn: स्वबाहुबलमाश्रित्य विदार्य च वरूथिनीम्। प्रेषितो धर्मराजेन पार्थेषोऽभ्येति सात्यकिः॥
en: Deputed by the very virtuous king Yudhishthira, O Partha, this Satyaki is coming to you, having penetrated through the Kaurava army, depending upon the mighty of his arms.

sn: यस्य नास्ति समो योधः कौरवेषु कथंचन। सोऽयमायाति कौन्तेय सात्यकिर्युद्धदुर्मदः॥
en: Invincible in battle, that Satyaki who has no match for him in the whole Kaurava army, is now coming to you, O son of Kunti!

sn: कुरुसैन्याद् विमुक्तो वै सिंहो मध्याद् गवामिव। निहत्य बहुला: सेनाः पार्थेषोऽभ्येति सात्यकिः॥
en: Freed from the press of the Kaurava troops, like a lion from amidst a herd of kine, Satyaki is not approaching you, after having slain numerous hostile soldiers.

sn: एष राजसहस्राणां वक्त्रैः पङ्कजसंनिभैः। आस्तीर्य वसुधां पार्थ क्षिप्रमायाति सात्यकिः॥
en: O son of Pritha, here comes Satyaki in all quickness, having covered the earth with the heads of thousand's of kings, graced with faces resembling blooming lotuses.

sn: एष दुर्योधनं जित्वा भ्रातृभिः सहितं रणे। निहत्य जलसंधं च क्षिप्रमायासि सात्यकिः॥
en: Yonder comes Satyaki, having conquered Duryodhana with his brothers and having slain Jalasandha in battle.

sn: रुधिरौघवतीं कृत्वा नदीं शोणितकर्दमाम्। तृणवद् व्यस्य कौरव्यानेष ह्यायाति सात्यकिः॥
en: Yonder comes Satyaki, having created a river of blood with clots of blood for its mire and having disregarded the Kauravas like some any straws."

sn: ततः प्रहृष्टः कौन्तेयः केशवं वाक्यमब्रवीत्। न मे प्रियं महाबाहो यन्मामभ्येति सात्यकिः॥
en: Hearing these words of Keshava Kunti's son although filled with delight replied to the former saying-"O mighty-armed one, I am not pleased to find that Satyaki is coming to me.

sn: न हि जानामि वृत्तान्तं धर्मराजस्य केशव। सात्वतेन विहीनः स यदि जीवति वा न वा॥
en: O Keshava, I do not know the where abouts of the very virtuous king Yudhishthira. I am doubtful whether he lives or not, being deprived of the help of this Satvata hero.

sn: एतेन हि महाबाहो रक्षितव्यः स पार्थिवः। तमेष कथमुत्सृज्य मम कृष्ण पदानुगः॥
en: O mighty-armed one, it should have been this one's first duty to protect the king in battle. O Krishna, wherefore has then this one : abandoning him has followed in my wake?

sn: राजा द्रोणाय चोत्सृष्टः सैन्धवश्चानिपातितः। प्रत्युद्याति च शैनेयमेष भूरिश्रवा रणे॥
en: The king has been left to the mercy of Drona; the ruler of the Sindhus is still unslain and yonder does Bhurisravas rush against Satyaki in battle.

sn: सोऽयं गुरुतरो भारः सैन्धवार्थ समाहितः। ज्ञातव्यश्च हि मे राजा रक्षितव्यश्च सात्यकिः॥
en: I have still the heavies burden hanging on me, in the shape of my vow to slay the Sindhu king. It is my duty to inform myself of the where-abouts of the king. It is also my duty to protect Satyaki.

sn: जयद्रथश्च हन्तव्यो लम्बते च दिवाकरः। श्रान्तश्चैष महाबाहुरल्पप्राणश्च साम्प्रतम्॥
en: It is also my (self-imposed) duty to slay Jayadratha. Yonder is the sun going down (the horizon). As regards the mighty-armed Satyaki he is fatigued and his stock of weapons is also exhausted.

sn: परिश्रान्ता हयाश्चास्य हययन्ता च माधव। न च भूरिश्रवाः श्रान्तः ससहायश्च केशव॥
en: His horses are tired and O Madhava his driver is worn out with fatigue. On the other hand, O Keshava, Bhurisrava is not at all fatigued and moreover he is well supported.

sn: अपीदानीं भवेदस्य क्षेममस्मिन् समागमे। कचिन्नं सागरं तीर्वा सात्यकिः सत्यविक्रमः॥
en: Will Satyaki reap victory in this encounter? Having crossed the ocean itself will Satyaki of prowess incapable of being vanquished.

sn: गोष्पदं प्राप्य सीदेत महौजाः शिनिपुङ्गवः। अपि कौरवमुख्येन कृतास्रेण महात्मना॥ समेत्य भूरिश्रवसा स्वस्तिमान् सात्यकिर्भवेत्। व्यतिक्रममिमं मन्ये धर्मराजस्य केशव॥ आचार्याद् भयमृत्सृज्य यः प्रैषयत् सात्यकिम्। ग्रहणं धर्मराजस्य खगः श्येन इवामिषम्॥ नित्यमाशंसते द्रोणः कचित् स्यात् कुशली नृपः॥३७
en: Will that foremost of scion of the Sini race, will that highly energetic one, succumb in crossing the little water contained in the vestige of a cow's hoof? Will Satyaki obtain good fortune having encountered Bhurisravas that foremost of the Kurus, who is high-souled and accomplished in the use of weapons? That he should dispatch Satyaki after me, dismissing all his fears from Drona, O Keshava, I think this to be a mistake committed by the very virtuous king Yudhishthira. Like a hawk when ranging through the skies, ever trying to pounce upon a piece of meat, Drona is ever endeavouring to effect the capture of the very virtuous king. Will the king fare well?" foremost of the Kurus, who is high-souled and accomplished in the use of weapons? Like a hawk when ranging through the skies, ever trying to pounce upon a piece of meat, Drona is ever endeavouring to effect the capture of the very virtuous king. Will the king fare well?"

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: संजय उवाच तमापतन्तं सम्प्रेक्ष्य सात्वकं युद्धदुर्मदम्। क्रोधाद् भूरिश्रवा राजन् सहसा समुपाद्रवत्॥
en: Sanjaya said Beholding that warrior indomitable in battle, that scion of the Sini race rush furiously to battle, o king, Bhurisravas, inflamed with wrath, assailed him.

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: तमब्रवीन्महाराज कौरव्यः शिनिपुङ्गवम्। अद्य प्राप्तोऽसि दिष्ट्या मे चक्षुर्विषयमित्युत॥
en: Then, O mighty monarch, that foremost of the Kurus (Bhurisravas) addressing Sini's grandson thus spoke-"By good luck it is that you have today come within the range of my sight;

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: चिराभिलषितं काममहं प्राप्स्यामि संयुगे। न हि मे मोक्ष्यसे जीवन् यदि नोत्सृजसे रणम्॥
en: Today, I shall realise in battle my longcherish I hope; you shall not escape me alive if indeed you do not fly away from the battle.

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: अद्य त्वां समरे हित्वा नित्यं शूराभिमानिनम्। नन्दयिष्यामि दाशार्ह कुरुराजं सुयोधनम्॥
en: O scion of the Dasarha race, today slaying you who ever boast of your prowess, I shall afford delight to Suyodhana, the king of the Kurus.

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: अद्य मद्वाणनिर्दग्धं पतितं धरणीतले। द्रक्ष्यतस्त्वां रणे वीरौ सहितौ केशवार्जुनौ॥
en: Today the heroes, Keshava and Arjuna, will both behold you prostrate on the field of battle, consumed with the fire of my barrows.

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: अद्य धर्मसुतो राजा श्रुत्वा त्वां निहतं मया। सवीडो भविता सद्यो येनासीह प्रवेशितः॥
en: Today Dharma's son king Yudhishthira hearing you slain by me, would be covered with shame, for it was he who dispatched you on this mission.

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: अद्य मे विक्रम पार्थो विज्ञास्यति धनंजयः। त्वयि भूमौ विनिहते शयाने रुधिरोक्षिते॥
en: Today Pritha's son Dhananjaya will come to know of my prowess when he will see you slain by me and lie weltering in your blood.

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: चिराभिलषितो ह्येष त्वया सह समागमः। पुरा देवासुरे युद्धे शक्रस्य बलिना यथा॥
en: This encounter with you has long been desired by me, like that desired by Shakra with Bali, in the battle between the Gods and the Asuras in days gone by.

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: अद्य युद्धं महाघोरं तव दास्यामि सात्वत। ततो ज्ञास्यसि तत्त्वेन मद्वीर्यबलपौरुषम्॥
en: Today, O descendant of the Satvata race, I shall fight a terrible fight with you, whence you shall know my great mighty and manliness.

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: अद्य संयमनी याता मया त्वं निहतो रणे। यथा रामानुजेनाजौ रावणिर्लक्ष्मणेन ह॥
en: Slain by me in battle, you shall today go to the domains of the Samyamni, like the son of Ravana slain by the younger brother of Rama (Lakshmana.)

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: अद्य कृष्णश्च पार्थश्च धर्मराजश्च माधवा हते त्वयि निरुत्साहा रणं त्यक्ष्यन्त्यसंशयम्॥
en: Today Krishna, Partha and the virtuous king Yudhishthira, O Madhava, will abandon fighting and became despondent, consequence of your slaughter.

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: अद्य तेऽपचितिं कृत्वा शितैमाधव सायकैः। तस्त्रियो नन्दयिष्यामि ये त्वया निहता रणे॥
en: O Madhava, today, slaying you with my sharp arrows, I shall afford delight to the wives of those who have been slain by you. in

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: मचक्षुर्विषयं प्राप्तो न त्वं माधव मोक्ष्यसे। सिंहस्य विषयं प्राप्तो यथा क्षुद्रमृगस्तथा॥
en: Just as a small deer coming within the range of a lion's sight cannot escape, SO O descendant of Madhu's race, you shall not escape me alive, having come within the range of my sight."

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: युयुधानस्तु तं राजन् प्रत्युवाच हसन्निव। कौरवेय न संत्रासो विद्यमे मम संयुगे॥
en: Thereupon, O king, Yuyudhana smilingly replied to him saying,"O illustrious descendant of the Kuru race, I have no fear in fight.

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: नाहं भीषयितुं शक्यो वाङ्मात्रेण तु केवलम्। स मां निहन्यात् संग्रामे यो मां कुर्यान्निरायुधम्॥
en: I am not to be terrified by empty words. He will slay me in battle who will be competent to deprive me of my weapons.

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: समास्तु शाश्वतीर्हन्याद् यो मां हन्याद्वि संयुगे। किं वृथोक्तेन बहुना कर्मणा तत् समाचर॥
en: He that will slay me in battle will ever be victorious. What is the use of vain boasts. Achieve in deeds what you say in words.

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: शारदस्येव मेघस्य गर्जितं निष्फलं हि ते। श्रुत्वा त्वद्गर्जितं वीरं हास्यं हि मम जायते॥
en: Like the rumbled of autumnal clouds, your roars are barren. So hearing your empty roars nothing beast my laughter is being excited.

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: चिरकालेप्सितं लोके युद्धमद्यास्तु कौरव। त्वरते मे मतिस्तात तप युद्धाभिकाङ्क्षिणी॥
en: O Kaurava, let the encounter which you looked so eargrly for, today take place; O sire, my heart that longs for the combat with you, cannot tolerate any more delay.

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: नाहत्वाहं निवर्तिष्ये त्वामद्य पुरुषाधम। अन्योन्यं तौ तथा वाग्भिस्तक्षन्तौ नरपुङ्गवौ।॥
en: O wretch, I shall not abstain from the fight today without having slain you in battle.” Thus those two foremost of men, stirring each other with their biting words.

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: जिघांसू परमक्रुद्धावभिजघ्नतुराहवे। समेतौ तौ महेष्वासौ शुष्मिणो स्पर्धिनो रणे॥
en: And waxing wroth and desirous of slaying each other in battle began to smite each other. Then those two mighty bow-men both boastful of their prowess and both challenging each other.

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: द्विरदाविव संक्रुद्धौ वासितार्थ मदोत्कटौ। भूरिश्रवाः सात्यकिश्च ववर्षतुररिंदमौ॥
en: Appeared like two infuriate elephants encounter each other, with a desire to consort with a she-elephant. Then those two subduers of foes, Bhurisravas and Satyaki began to pour.

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: शरवर्षाणि घोराणि मेघाविव परस्परम्। सौमदत्तिस्तु शैनेयं प्रच्छायेषुभिराशुगैः॥
en: On each other, dreadful showers of arrows like two mighty-clouds. Covering Sini's grandson with swift-coursing arrows, Somadatta's son.

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: जिघांसुर्भरतश्रेष्ठ विव्याध निशितैः शरैः। दशभिः सात्यकि विदध्वा सौमदत्तिरथापरान्॥
en: O foremost of the Bharatas, desirous of slaying the former, pierced him with sharp arrows. Having pierced Satyaki then with ten arrows, Somadatta's son.

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: मुमोच निशितान् बाणान् जिघांसुः शिनिपुङ्गवम्। तानस्य विशिखांस्तीक्ष्णानन्तरिक्षे विशाम्पते।॥ अप्राप्तानसमायाभिरग्रसत् सात्यकिः प्रभो। तौ पृथक् शस्त्रवर्षाभ्यामवर्षतां परस्परम्॥
en: Out of a desire for slaying that illustrious scion of the Sini race, sped other sharp shafts at him. Then, O ruler of men, Satyaki with the illusion of his weapons devoured up all those up all those arrows, O lord, when they were ranging through the skies and before they had even reached him (Satyaki). Then those two heroes began to pour upon one another their showers of weapons.

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: उत्तमाभिजनौ वीरौ कुरुवृष्णियशस्करौ। तौ नखैरिव शार्दूलौ दन्तैरिव महाद्विपौ॥
en: Those two heroes, of noble extraction both enhancers of the fame of the Kurus and the Vrishnis respectively, began to fight with each other like two tigers fighting with claws or two elephants fighting with their tusks.

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: रथशक्तिभिरन्योन्यं विशिग्वैश्चाप्यकृन्तताम्। निर्भिन्दन्तौ हि गात्राणि विक्षरन्तौ च शोणितम्॥
en: With lances and with darts and javelins they inflicted wounds on each other. They mangled their bodies and shed blood profusely.

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: व्यष्टम्भयेतामन्योन्यं प्राणद्यूताभिदेविनौ। एवमुत्तमकर्माणौ कुरुवृष्णियशस्करौ॥
en: Then those two heroes checked each other in that battle which was like a gambling match in which their lives were the stakes. Thus those two enhancers of the glory of the Kuru and the Vrishni races (respectively).

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: परस्परमयुध्येतां वारणाविव यूथपौ। तावदीर्पण कालेन ब्रह्मलोकपुरस्कृतौ॥ यियासन्तौ परं स्थानमन्योन्यं संजगर्जतुः। सात्यकिः सौदत्तिश्च शरवृष्ट्या परस्परम्॥ हृष्टवद् धार्तराष्ट्राणां पश्यतामभ्यवर्षताम्। सम्प्रेक्षन्त जनास्तौ तु युध्यमानौ युधाम्पती॥
en: Fought on with each other like two huge elephants, the leaders of two herds. Those two warriors, both desirous of attaining the highest of regions both longing to attain to the region of Brahma, thus roared at each other. Indeed Satyaki and Somadatta's son continued to cover each with their arrowy downpour in the sight of the delighted Dharatarastras. The people then witnessed that encounter between those two foremost of warriors.

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: यूथपौ वासिताहेतोः प्रयुद्धाविव कुञ्जरौ। अन्योन्यस्य हयान् हत्वा धनुषी विनिकृत्य च॥
en: Who were fighting like two leaders of elephant herds for the sake of consorting with a she-elephant in her season. Then each slaying the other's steeds and cutting off the other's bow.

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: विरथावसियुद्धाय समेयातां महारणे। आर्षभे चर्मणी चित्रे प्रगृह्य विपुले शुभे॥
en: And thus deprived of the use of their cars, encountered each other for sword fighting. Taking up two large and beautiful and variegated shields made of bull's hide.

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: विकोशौ चाप्यसी कृत्वा समरे तौ विचेरतुः। चरन्तौ विविधान् मार्गान् मण्डलानि च भागशः॥
en: And drawing out their swords out of their scabbards, they appeared beautiful on the field of battle. They moved in various motions and described in their montions, various circles.

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: मुहुराजघ्नतुः क्रुद्धावन्योन्यमरिमर्दनौ। सखड्गी चित्रवर्माणौ सनिष्काङ्गदभूषणौ॥
en: Those two subduers of foes incessantly then began to strike one another out of rage. With their swords and covered in variegated coats of mail and adorned with Nikas and Angadas.

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: भ्रान्तमुद्भरान्तमाविद्धमाप्लुतं विप्लुतं सृतम्। सम्पातं समुदीर्ण च दर्शयन्तौ यशस्विनौ॥
en: Those two renowned warriors displayed various kinds of motions. They wheeled about and jumped on high, made side thirsts, leapt forward whirled on high, ran and dashed forward and advanced upwards.

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: असिभ्यां सम्प्रजह्राते परस्परमरिंदमौ। उभौ छिट्टैषिणो वीरावुभौ चित्रं ववल्गतुः॥
en: Those two subduer of foes began to smite each other with their swords and each was on the alert for finding the weakness of other. Both of those two heroes jumped up superbly.

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: दर्शयन्तावुभौ शिक्षा लाघवं सौष्ठवं तथा। रणे रणकृतां श्रेष्ठावन्योन्यं पर्यकर्षताम्॥
en: And both displayed their training agility and skill. Those foremost of warriors in that battle, made many skillful thirst at each other.

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: मुहूर्तमिव राजेन्द्र समाहत्य परस्परम्। पश्यतां सर्वसैन्यानां वीरावाश्वासतां पुनः॥
en: Then, O foremost of men, striking each other, they took respite only for a moment before the presence of all the troop.

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: असिभ्यां चर्मणी चित्रे शतचन्द्रे नराधिप। निकृत्य पुरुषव्याघ्रौ बाहुयुद्धं प्रचक्रतुः॥
en: Having, with their respective swords cut-off the variegated buckler of each other decked with hundred moons, those foremost of men engaged in a wrestling encounter, O ruler of men.

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: व्यूढोरस्कौ दीर्घभुजौ नियुद्धकुशलावुभौ। बाहुभिः समसज्जेतामायसैः परिधैरिव॥
en: Possessed of expanded chests, long arms and both versed in wrestling, they fought on with each other with their arms that resembling iron-piked bludgeons.

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: तयो राजन् भुजाधातनिग्रहप्रग्रहास्तथा। शिक्षाबलसमुद्भूताः सर्वयोधप्रहर्षणाः॥
en: They struck and seized each other with their arms and each seized the others neck with his arms. The skill that hey had acquired by practice, afforded great delight to other warriors who then were turned into mere spectators.

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: तयोर्नृवरयो राजन् समरे युध्यमानयोः। भीमोऽभवन्महाशब्दो वज्रपर्वतयोरिव॥
en: The, O king, as those two foremost of men fought on with each other, the sound that then arose, was the like that caused by the striking of thunder against a mountain.

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: द्विपाविव विषाणाग्रैः शृङ्गैरिव महर्षभौ। भुजयोक्त्रावबन्धैश्च शिरोभ्यां चावघातनैः॥ पादावकर्षसंधानैस्तोमराङ्कुशलासनैः। पादोदरविबन्धैश्च भूतावुभ्रमणैस्तथा॥ गतप्रत्यागताक्षेपैः पातनोत्थानसम्प्लुतैः। युयुधाते महात्मानौ कुरुसात्वतपुङ्गवौ॥
en: Like two elephants fighting with each other with the ends of their tusks, of like two bulls with their horns, those two high-souled and foremost warriors of the Kuru and the Satvata races, fought with each other, sometimes twining each other with their arms, sometimes striking each other with their heads, sometimes binding each other with their legs, sometimes slaping their arm-pits, sometimes scraching each other with their nails, sometimes embracing each other tightly, sometimes twining their legs round each others loins, sometimes rolling on the ground, sometimes going forward and sometime falling back, sometimes challenging each other, sometimes throwing each other down, sometimes rising up and sometimes jumping on high.

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: युध्यमानं द्वात्रिंशत्करणानि स्युर्यानि युद्धानि भारत। तान्यदर्शयतां तत्र युध्यमानौ महाबलौ॥
en: Then those two puissant combatant's displayed in that encounter all the thirty kinds of manoeuvres and acts that are the principal feathers of these kinds of encounters.

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: क्षीणायुधे सात्वते युध्यमाने ततोऽब्रवीदर्जुनं वासुदेवः। पश्यस्वैनं विरथं रणे वरं सर्वधनुर्धराणाम्॥
en: When during that encounter, the lock of Satwata's weapons was exhausted, Vasudeva's son addressing Arjuna said-" Behold this carless hero, viz., Satyaki, this foremost of all wielder of bow, engaged in fight.

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: प्रविष्टो भारती भित्त्वा तव पाण्डव पृष्ठतः। योधितश्च महावीर्यैः सर्वैर्भारत भारतैः॥
en: O son of Pandu, he has followed you having penetrated into the Bharata host. O Bharata, he has fought with many mighty warriors of the Bharata host.

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: परिश्रान्तं युधां श्रेष्ठं सम्प्राप्तो भूरिदक्षिणः। युद्धाकाङ्क्षी समायान्तं नैतत् सममिवार्जुन॥
en: Bhurisravas who has made great sacrificial presents, rushing upon that foremost of warriors viz., Satyaki exhausted with fatigue, has no encountered him. This is indeed very unfair."

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: ततो भूरिश्रवाः क्रुद्धः सात्यकिं युद्धदुर्मदः। उद्यम्याभ्याहनद् राजन् मत्तो मत्तमित द्विपम्॥
en: Then the indomitable Bhurisravas inflamed with rage, uplifting his sword struck Satyaki like a mad elephant striking another in the same state.

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: स्थस्थयोर्द्वयोर्युद्धे क्रुद्धयोर्योधमुख्ययोः। केशवार्जुनयो राजन् समरे प्रेक्षमाणयोः॥
en: Those two foremost of car-warriors, both riding in their cars and both rushing with rage fought on with each other, Arjuna and Krishna being their witness.

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: अथ कृष्णो महाबाहुरर्जुनं प्रत्यभाषत। पश्य वृष्ण्यन्धकव्यानं सौमदत्तिवशं गतम्॥
en: Thereupon the mighty-armed Krishna addressing Arjuna, said. “Behold the foremost of the Vrishni and Andhaka races, viz., Satyaki succumb to the son of Somadatta.

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: परिश्रान्तं गतं भूतौ कृत्वा कर्म सुदुष्करम्। तवान्तेवासिनं वीरं पालयार्जुन सात्यकिम्॥
en: Having achieved many difficult feats he now laid low on the field in consequence of his great exhaustion. O Arjuna protect the heroic Satyaki, your (renowned) pupil.

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: न वशं यज्ञशीलस्य गच्छेदेष वरोऽर्जुन। त्वत्कृते पुरुषव्याघ्र तदाशु क्रियतां विभो॥
en: O foremost of men, O Arjuna, do you soon take that measure by which Satyaki many not succumb to Bhurisravas the performer of numerous sacrifices, O lord.”

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: अथाब्रवीद्धष्टमना वासुदेवं धनंजयः। पश्य वृष्णिप्रवीरेण क्रीडन्तं कुरुपुङ्गवम्॥
en: Then Dhananjaya, with cheerful heart addressing Vasudeva's son said-"Behold that foremost among the Kurus and that best hero among the Vrishni's, sport with each other.

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: महाद्विपेनेव वने मत्तेन हरियूथपम्। इत्येवं भाषमाणे तु पाण्डवे वै धनंजये॥
en: Like a huge and infuriate elephant sporting in the woods with mighty lion.” While Pandu's son Dhananjaya was thus speaking.

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: हाहाकारो महानासीत् सैन्यानां भरतर्षभ। तदुद्यम्य महाबाहुः सात्यकिं न्यहनद् भुवि॥
en: Loud cried of Oh and Alas arose among the troops, foremost of the Bharatas, as the mighty-armed (Bhurisravas) striking vigorously had brought Satyaki down on the earth.

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: स सिंह इव मातङ्गं विकर्षन् भूरिदक्षिणः। व्यरोचत कुरुश्रेष्ठः सात्वतप्रवरं युधि॥
en: Then like a lion dragging an elephant, that foremost of the Kuru race, namely Bhurisravas, that destroyer of darkness, looked beautiful in that battle as he dragged that foremost one of the Satwatas.

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: अथ कोशाद् विनिष्कृष्य खङ्गं भूरिश्रवा रणे। मूर्धजेषु निजग्राह पदा चोरस्यताडयत्॥
en: Then drawing his sword out of the scabbard and holding Satyaki by the hair, Bhurisravas struck the former on the breast with his legs.

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: ततोऽस्य छेत्तुपारब्धः शिरः कायात् सकुण्डलम्। तावत्क्षणात् सात्वतोऽपि शिरः सम्भ्रमयंस्त्वरन्॥
en: Bhurisravas was then about to sever from Satyaki's trunk his head graced with earrings. For sometimes, that hero of the Satvata race rapidly whirling round with the rod.

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: यथा चक्रं तु कौलालो दण्डविद्ध तु भारत। सहैव भूरिश्रवसो बाहुना केशधारिणा॥
en: Together with the arm of Bhurisravas that held it by the hair, like a potters wheel whirling round with the rod.

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: तं तथा परिकृष्यन्तं दृष्ट्वा सात्वतमाहवे। वासुदेवस्ततो राजन् भूयोऽर्जुनमभाषत॥
en: Beholding the Satvata hero thus dragged by Bhurisravas, Vasudeva once more addressing Arjuna said-

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: पश्य वृष्ण्यन्धकव्याघ्रं सौमदत्तिवशं गतम्। तव शिष्यं महाबाहो धनुष्यनवरं त्वया॥
en: Behold O mighty-armed one, that foremost hero among the Vrishnis and Andhakas, that disciple of yours who is not inferior to you in bowmanship, succumb to the son of Somadatta.

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: असत्यो विक्रमः पार्थ यत्र भूरिश्रवा रणे। विशेषयति वार्ष्णेयं सात्यकिं सत्यविक्रमम्॥
en: Behold, O son of Partha, the weak Bhurisravas obtain advantage over the Vrishni hero Satyaki of prowess incapable of being baffled.

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: एवमुक्तो महाबाहुर्वासुदेवेन पाण्डवः। मनसा पूजयामास भूरिश्रवसमाहवे॥
en: The mighty-armed son of Pandu thus spoken to by Vasudeva (Krishna), worshipped Bhurisravas in his minds.

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: विकर्षन् सात्वतश्रेष्ठं क्रांडमान इवाहवे। संहर्षयति मां भूयः कुरूणां कीर्तिवर्धनः॥
en: (He then said to himself). 'Dragging this foremost of the Satvata race as if in sport, the enhancer of the glory of the (Bhurisravas) is filling me with delight.

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: प्रवरं वृष्णिवीराणां यत्र हन्याद्धि सात्यकिम्। महाद्विपमिवारण्ये मृगेन्द्र इव कर्षति॥
en: Without slaying that foremost of the Vrishni heroes viz., Satyaki he is only dragging the former like the king of the beasts dragging a mighty elephant in the woods.'

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: एवं तु मनसा राजन् पार्थः सम्पूज्य कौरवम्। वासुदेवं महाबाहुरर्जुनः प्रत्यभाषत॥
en: Having thus mentally applauded that foremost of the Kauravas, Pritha's son, O king, the mighty Arjuna thus replied to Vasudeva

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: सैन्धवे सक्तदृष्टित्वान्नैनं पश्यामि माधवम्। एतत् त्वसुकरं कर्म यादवार्थे करोम्यहम्॥
en: “O Madhava, my eyes being fixed on the ruler of the Sindhus, I cannot see Bhurisravas; but for the sake of that descendant of Yadu's, race, I shall perform a very difficult feat.”

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: इत्युक्त्वा वचनं कुर्वन् वासुदेवस्य पाण्डवः। ततः क्षुरप्रं निशितं गाण्डीवे समायोजयत्॥
en: Having thus spoken and desirous of carrying out the words of Vasudeva, the son of Pandu placed a sharp razor-headed arrows on the bowstring.

description: Continuous The lopping of Bhurisrava's arm
sn: पार्थबाहुविसृष्टः स महोल्केव नभश्च्युता। सखङ्गं यज्ञशीलस्य साङ्गदं बाहुमच्छिनत्॥
en: That arrow shot by the force of Partha's arms and looking like a meteor dropping from the skies, cut-off the arm of that one devoted to the performance of sacrifice arm that was decked with Angadas and had a sword in its grasp.

sn: संजय उवाच स बाहुय॑पतद् भमौ सखङ्ग सशुभाङ्गदः। आदधजीवलोकस्य दुःखमद्भुतमुत्तमः॥
en: Sanjaya said Then that arm with the sword in grasp and decked with beautiful Angadas, fell down on the earth, thereby inflicting great grief on the living creation.

sn: प्रहरिष्यन् हृतो बाहुरदृश्येन किरीटिना। वेगेन न्यपतद् भूमौ पञ्चास्य इव पन्नगः॥
en: In the act of striking, that arm was lopped off by the diadem-decked Arjuna, who himself remained invisible to Bhruisravas; thus cut-off, it fell down vehemently on the earth, like a five-hooded snake.

sn: स मोघं कृतमात्मानं दृष्ट्वा पार्थेन कौरवः। उत्सृज्य सात्यकि क्रोधाद् गर्हयामास पाण्डवम्॥
en: Then that descendant of the Kuru race, beholding himself incapacitated by Pritha's son, began, out of rage, to reprove the son of Pandu, having abandoned Satyaki.

sn: भूरिश्रवा उवाच नृशंसं बत कौन्तेय कर्मेदं कृतवानसि। अपश्यतो विषक्तस्य यन्मे बाहुमचिच्छिदः॥
en: Bhurisravas said Alas, O son of Kunti, you have committed a cruel and heartless deed, in as much as, not being engaged with me and covertly, you have cut-off my arm.

sn: किं नु वक्ष्यसि राजानं धर्मपुत्रं युधिष्ठिरम्। किं कुर्वाणो मया संख्ये हतो भूरिश्रवा रणे॥
en: Shall you have not to say to king Yudhishthira, the son of Dharma-'Bhurisravas when engaged with another was slain by me in battle?"

sn: इदमिन्द्रेण ते साक्षादुपदिष्टं महात्मना। अस्त्रं रुद्रेण वा पार्थ द्रोणेनाथ कृपेण वा॥
en: Was it for this that you learnt the use of weapons from the illustrious Indra or Rudra or Drona or Kripa. O son of Pritha!

sn: ननु नामास्रधर्मज्ञस्त्वं लोकेऽभ्यधिकः परैः। सोऽयुध्यमानस्य कथं रणे प्रहृतवानसि॥
en: It is said that you are batter acquainted with the rules about the use of weapons then many others. Why then have you lopped off the arm of one who was not fighting with you?

sn: न प्रमत्ताय भीताय विरथाय प्रयाचते। व्यसने वर्तमानाय प्रहरन्ति मनस्विनः॥
en: The righteous never strike him who is careless or who is frightened or who is made carless or who implores mercy or who is involved in a calamity.

sn: इदं तु नीचाचरितमसत्पुरुषसेवितम्। कथमाचरितं पार्थ पापकर्म सुदुष्करम्॥
en: Why then, O son of Pritha, have you perpetrated this vile and difficult deed, that is only worthy of a mean fellow and is practised only by wicked people.

sn: आर्येण सुकरं त्वाहुरार्यकर्म धनंजय। अनार्यकर्म त्वार्येण सुदुष्करतमं भुवि॥
en: O Dhananjaya, respectable people look upon respectable deeds to be very easy of being accomplished. But a disrespectable deed is difficult of being perpetrated by a respectable person.

sn: येषु येषु नरव्याघ्र यत्र यत्र च वर्तते। आशु तच्छीलतामेति तदिदं त्वयि दृश्यते॥
en: Men quickly imbibe the behaviours of those among whom they live, O Bharata, the truth of this proposition is verified in you.

sn: कथं हि राजवंश्यस्त्वं कौरवेया विशेषतः। क्षत्रधर्मादपक्रान्तः सुवृत्तश्चरितव्रतः॥
en: Of royal extraction and specially descendant as you are of the Kuru race, how could you transgress the duties of the Kshatriya race, although you were well-behaved and observant of vows.

sn: इदं तु यदतिक्षुद्रं वार्ष्णेयार्थे कृतं त्वया। वासुदेवमतं नूनं नैतत् त्वय्युपपद्यते॥
en: This vile act that you have today perpetrated for the sake of the Vrishni hero, is surely the result of Vasudeva's instigations. And it cannut possibly be reconciled to your nature.

sn: को हि नाम प्रमत्ताय परेण सह युध्यते। ईदृशं व्यसनं दद्याद् यो न कृष्णसखो भवेत्॥
en: What man, except he that calls himself a friended of Krishna would inflict such an injury on another who is engaged deeply in fighting with his adversary?

sn: व्रात्याः संक्लिष्टकर्माणः प्रकृत्यैव च गर्हिताः। वृष्ण्यन्धकाः कथं पार्थ प्रमाणं भवता कृताः॥
en: The Vrishnis and the Andhakas are vile Kshatriyas, ever engaged in perpetrating low deeds and are by nature wedded to shameful conduct. Why, O Partha, have you chosen them to be your model?” Being thus spoken to Partha then replied to Bhurisravas sayingएवमुक्तो रणे पार्थो भूरिश्रवसमब्रवीत्।

sn: अर्जुन उवाच व्यक्तं हि जीर्यमाणोऽपि बुद्धिं जरयते नरः॥
en: Arjuna said “Now it is clear that with the decay of body, the intellect of men also suffer decay, since, O master, you have uselessly directed all these reproaches to me.

sn: अनर्थकमिदं सर्व यत् त्वया व्याहृतं प्रभो। जानन्नेव हृषीकेशं गर्हसे मां च पाण्डवम्॥
en: Knowing myself and Hrishikesha perfectly well how is it that you reproach us both? I am conversant perfectly with the rules of fair combat and I am acquainted with the meaning of all moral precepts.

sn: संग्रामाणां हि धर्मज्ञः सर्वशास्त्रार्थपारगः। न चाधर्ममहं कुर्या जानंश्चैव हि मुह्यसे॥
en: So, it is impossible that I should commit a sinful act. Knowing this also, fight with their foes, being supported by their own men.

sn: युध्यन्ति क्षत्रियाः शत्रून् स्वैः स्वैः परिवृता नराः। भ्रातृभिः पितृभिः पुत्रैस्तथा सम्बन्धिबान्धवैः॥ वयस्यैरथ मित्रैश्च ते च बाहुं समाश्रिताः।
en: Such as their brothers, their fathers their sons and relatives and friends and kinsmen and companions and also relying on the strength of their arms.

sn: स कथं सात्यकिं शिष्यं सुखसम्बन्धमेव च॥ अस्मदर्थे च युध्यन्तं त्यक्त्वा प्राणान् सुदुस्त्यजान्।
en: men Why then should I not protect, Satyaki my disciple and my dear relative who is fighting in this battle on our behave reckless of the very life that is so difficult of being laid down?

sn: मम बाहुं रणे राजन् दक्षिणं युद्धदुर्मदम्॥ न चात्मा रक्षितव्यो वै राजन् रणगतेन हि।
en: Why should I not protect "Satyaki who is, O king, like my own right arm to me? In battle, one should not look after his own protection only.

sn: यो यस्य युज्यतेऽर्थेषु स वे रक्ष्यो नराधिप॥ तै रक्ष्यमाणैः स नृपो रक्षितव्यो महामृधे।
en: O ruler of men, he that is engaged on behalf of another, should surely be protected by that other. When such are themselves protected they can look after the protection of the king (on whose behalf they fight).

sn: यहहं सात्यकिं पश्ये वध्यमानं महारणे॥ ततस्तस्य वियोगेन पापं मेऽनर्थतो भवेत्।
en: If indeed I had passively beheld Satyaki's slaughter in this great encounter, then, at Satyaki's death, sin would have hanged on me for my negligence.

sn: रक्षितश्च मया यस्मात् तस्मात् क्रुध्यसि किं मयि॥२४ यच्च मे गर्हसे राजन्नन्येन सह संगतम्। अहं त्वया विनिकृतस्तत्र मे बुद्धिविभ्रमः॥ कवचं धुन्वतस्तुभ्यं रथं चारोहतः स्वयम्। धनुर्ध्या कर्पतश्चैव युध्यतः सह शत्रुभिः॥ एवं रथगजाकीर्णे हयपत्तिसमाकुले। सिंहनादोद्धतरवे गम्भीरे सैन्यसागरे॥ स्वैः परैश्च समेतेभ्यः सात्वतेन च संगमे। एकस्यैकेन हि कथं संग्रामः सम्भविष्यति॥ बहुभिः सह संगम्य निर्जित्य च महारथान्।
en: Why do you wax wroth upon me for my having protected him, who is every way deserves my protection? You are reproaching me, O king, saying, 'When engaged with another, I have yet been incapacitated by you.' In respect to this, I submit that I committed an error in my judgment. Satyaki was shaking his armour against you and was riding on his own car, drawing his bow-string he was fighting with the foes, in the midst of his enemies abounding in steeds and foot-soldiers and teeming with cars and elephants and echoing with the war-cries of combatants.
