Amongst friends and foes engaged with one another, how could it be possible that the Satvata hero was engaged with one person only? Having encountered many warriors and vanquished many mighty car-warrior.

sn: श्रान्तश्च श्रान्तवाहश्च विमनाः शस्त्रपीडितः॥ ईदृशं सात्यकि संख्ये निर्जित्य च महारथम्।
en: Satyaki was fatigued and afflicted with weapons-wounds and cheerless in mind; his horses also were exhausted. Having, under these circumstances, defeated the mighty carwarrior Satyaki.

sn: ईदृशं सात्यकिं संख्ये निर्जित्य च महारथम्। अधिकत्वं विजानीषे स्ववीर्यवशमागतम्॥
en: And having thus obtained advantage over him, you seek to establish your superiority. You desired to cut-off with your sword the head of Satyaki.

sn: यदिच्छसि शिरश्चास्य असिना हन्तुमाहवे। तथा कृच्छ्रगतं चैव सात्यकिं कः क्षमिष्यति॥ त्वं वै विगर्हयात्मानमात्मानं यो न रक्षसि। कथं करिष्यसे वीर यो वा त्वां संश्रयेज्जनः॥
en: I could not possibly behold passively Satyaki reduced to that plight. It is proper that you should reproach your own self in as much as you neglected to protect yourself (when trying to injure another). Indeed O hero, how would you yourself have behaved towards one who would be your dependent.

sn: संजय उवाच एवमुक्तो महाबाहुपकेतुर्महायशाः। युयुधानं समुज्सृज्य रणे प्रायमुपाविशत्॥
en: Sanjaya said Thus spoken to (by Arjuna), the illustrious and mighty-armed Bhurisravas bearing the device of a sacrificial stake on his banner, let Yuyudhana go and desired to enter upon the performance of Praya-Yoga.

sn: शरानास्तीर्य सव्येन पाणिना पुण्यलक्षणः। यियासुर्ब्रह्मलोकाय प्राणान् प्राणेष्वथाजुहोत्॥
en: Distinguished by many pious deeds, he then spread with his left hand a bed of arrows and out of a desire for going to the regions of Brahman, he committed his vital breaths to the care of the gods presiding over them.

sn: सूर्ये चक्षुः समाधाय प्रसन्नं सलिले मनः। ध्यायन् महोपनिषदं योगयुक्तोऽभवन्मुनिः॥
en: Steadying his eyes on the sun, setting his mind on the purified water and meditating the Mantras contained in the Upanishads, Bhurisravas betaking himself to yoga, became reticent.

sn: ततः स सर्वसेनायां जनः कृष्णधनंजयौ। गर्हयामास तं चापि शशंस पुरुषर्षभम्॥
en: Then all the men in the army began to rebuke Krishna and Dhananjaya and applaud that foremost of men viz., Bhurisravas.

sn: निन्द्यमानौ तथा कृष्णौ नोचतुः किंचिदप्रियम्। ततः प्रशस्यमानश्च नाहृष्यद् यूपकेतनः॥
en: Though thus reproached by the general voice, the two Krishnas uttered not a single word, nor did the stake-bannered Bhurisravas feel any joy in consequence of those encomiums.

sn: तांस्तथावादिनो राजन् पुत्रांस्तव धनंजयः। अमृष्यमाणो मनसा तेषां तस्य च भाषितम्॥ असंक्रुद्धमना वाचः स्मारयन्निव भारत। उवाच पाण्डुतनयः साक्षेपमिव फाल्गुनः॥
en: Then Dhananjaya otherwise called Phalguna, that son of Pandu unable to tolerate your sons speaking in that strain as also to put up with their words and the words of Bhurisravas, O Bharata, in sorrows and not at all angry, spoke these words, as if for remaining them all.

sn: मम सर्वेऽपि राजानो जानन्त्येव महाव्रतम्। न शक्यो मामको हन्तुं यो मे स्याद् बाणगोचरे॥
en: All kings know of this my great vow, that no one shall slay any body of our party so long as the latter is with in the range of my arrows.

sn: यूपकेतो निरीक्ष्यैतन्न मामर्हसि गर्हितुम्। न हि धर्ममविज्ञाय युक्तं गर्हयितुं परम्॥
en: Knowing this, O stake-bannered, one it befits you not to reproach me; without yourself knowing the rules of morality, you should not censure others.

sn: आत्तशस्त्रस्य हि रणे वृष्णिवीरं जिघांसतः। यदहं बाहुमच्छत्सं न स धर्मो विगर्हितः॥
en: That I have lopped off your arm while you, armed to the teeth, were on the point of slaying the unarmed Satyaki, is not at all against the rules of fair combat.

sn: न्यस्तशस्त्रस्य बालस्य विरथस्य विवर्मणः। अभिमन्योर्वधं तात धार्मिकः को नु पूजयेत्॥
en: But what righteous man is there who will not condemn the slaughter of the body Abhimanyu specially when he was deprived of his weapons, his car and his armour?

sn: एवमुक्तः स पार्थेन शिरसा भूमिमस्पृशत्। पाणिना चैव सव्येन प्राहिणोदस्य दक्षिणम्॥
en: Thus addressed by Pritha's son, Bhurisravas touched the ground with his head and offered with his left arm the right one that had been severed.

sn: एतत् पार्थस्य तु वचस्ततः श्रुत्वा महाद्युतिः। यूपकेतुर्महाराज तूष्णीमासीदवाङ्मुखः॥
en: Then the stake-bannered Bhurisravas of great effulgence O king having heard those words of Partha, become silent with his face turned towards the earth.

sn: या प्रीतिधर्मराजे मे भीमे च बलिनां वरे। नकुले सहदेवे च सा मे त्वयि शलाग्रज॥
en: Arjuna said O eldest brother of Shalya, the love I bear for you is equal even to that I bear for king Yudhishthira the virtuous or Bhima that foremost of all mighty persons or Nakula or Sahadeva.

sn: मया त्वं समनुज्ञातः कृष्णेन च महात्मना। गच्छ पुण्यकृताल्लोकाञ्छिबिरौशीनरो यथा॥
en: With my permission as also with that of the high-souled Krishna do you go to the regions of the righteous where Sivi the son of Usinara is.

sn: वासुदेव उवाच ये लोका मम विमला: सकृद् विभाता ब्रह्माद्यैः सुरवृषभैरपीष्यमाणाः। तान् क्षिप्रं व्रज सतताग्निहोत्रयाजिन् मत्तुल्यो भव गरुडोत्तमाङ्गयानः॥
en: Vasudeva said You are ever devoted to the performance of sacrifices and Agnihotras; therefore repair quickly to those holy regions of mine that constantly burn with effulgence and that are coveted by the foremost of gods withi Brahman as their head and becoming equal to myself by you carried on the back of Garuda.

sn: संजय उवाच उत्थितः स तु शैनेया विमुक्तः सौमदत्तिना। खङ्गमादाय चिच्छित्सुः शिरस्तस्य महात्मनः॥
en: Sanjaya said Liberated from the grasp of Somadatta's son, the grandson of Sini rose and with a view to cut-off the head of that illustrious hero, drew his sword.

sn: निहतं पाण्डुपुत्रेण प्रसक्तं भूरिदक्षिणम्। इयेष सात्यकिर्हन्तुं शलाग्रजमकल्मषम्॥
en: Satyaki then desired to slay the sinless Bhurisravas, the eldest brother of Saila that giver of profuse presents at sacrifices, who was staying with his senses drawn back from the battle and who had already been slain by Arjuna the son of Pandu;

sn: निकृत्तभुजमासीनं छिन्नहस्तमिव द्विपम्। क्रोशतां सर्वसैन्यानां निन्द्यमानः सुदुर्मनाः॥
en: Who was sitting with his arm lopped off, like an elephant with his trunk cut-off. Then all the warriors reproached him loudly for his intention. But destitute of reason.

sn: गीर्यमाणः च कृष्णेन पार्थेन च महात्मना। भीमेन चक्ररक्षाभ्यामश्वत्थाम्ना कृपेण च॥
en: And although forbidden by the high-souled Partha and Krishna and Bhima and the two wheel protectors of of Arjuna's car and Ashvattharnan and Kripa.

sn: कर्णेन वृषसेनेन सैन्धवेन तथैव च। विक्रोशतां च सैन्यानामवधीत् तं धृतव्रतम्॥
en: And Karna and Vrishasena and the king of the Sindhus and while the soldiers were still uttering loud shouts of denunciation, Satyaki flew Bhurisravas while engaged in the observance of the vow.

sn: प्रायोपविष्टाय रणे पार्थेन छिन्नबाहवे। सात्यकिः कौरवेयाय खड्ड्रेनापाहरच्छिरः॥
en: Indeed with his sword Satyaki lopped off the head of the Kuru warrior who had been deprived of his arm by Partha and who was then engaged in the Praya for liberating his soul from the body.

sn: नाभ्यनन्दन्त सैन्यानि सात्यकिं तेन कर्मणा। अर्जुनेन हतं पूर्व यजघान कुरूद्वहम्॥
en: The soldiers then did not praise Satyaki for that act of his, viz., the slaughter of the perpetuator of the Kuru race, who already been slain by Pritha's son.

sn: सहस्राक्षसमं चैव सिद्धचारणमानवाः। भूरिश्रवसमालोक्य युद्धे प्रायगतं हतम्॥ अपूजयन्त तं देवा विस्मितास्तेऽस्य कर्मभिः। पक्षवादांश्च सुबहून् प्रावदंस्तव सैनिकाः॥
en: Then the Siddhas, the Charanas and the men present, as also the celestials, seeing the Indra-like Bhurisravas slain in battle when sitting in the observance of the vow Praya, began to praise him, struck with wonder at the feats achieved by him. Your troops also argued

sn: न वार्ष्णेयस्यापराधो भवितव्यं हि तत् यथा। तस्मान्मन्युर्न वः कार्यः क्रोधो दुःखतरो नृणाम्॥
en: In this matter no blame should be attributed to the Vrishni hero. What has been ordained must happen. Therefore we should not cherish wrath; since again wrath is the cause of a man's grief.

sn: हन्तव्यश्चैव वीरेण नात्र कार्या विचारणा। विहितो ह्यस्य धात्रैव मृत्युः सात्यकिराहवे॥
en: It was doomed that Bhurisravas would be slain by the heroic Satyaki. We need not judge of its propriety or otherwise. Satyaki has been made the instrument of Bhurisrava's death by the Creator himself.

sn: सात्यकिरुवाच न हन्तव्यो न हन्तव्यो इति यन्मां प्रभाषत। धर्मवादैरधर्मिष्ठा धर्मकञ्चकमास्थिताः॥
en: Satyaki said You, sinful Kauravas, vested in outward garments of virtue, you are telling me in words of virtue, that Bhurisravas should not have been slain.

sn: यदा बाल: सुभद्रायाः सुतः शस्त्रविना कृतः। युष्माभिनिहतो युद्धे तदा धर्मः क वो गतः॥
en: Where did this righteousness of yours fly when you ruthlessly slew in battle that child viz., Subhadra's son when he was deprived to the use of his weapons;

sn: मया त्वेतत् प्रतिज्ञातं क्षेपे कस्मिंश्चिदेव हि। यो मां निष्पिष्य संग्रामे जीवन् हन्यात् पदा रुषा॥६२
en: In a certain fit of haughtiness I had vowed that he who would throw me down in battle alive and strike me in wrath with his knees.

sn: स मे वध्यो भवेच्छत्रुर्यद्यपि स्यान्मुनिव्रतः। चेष्टमानं प्रतीघाते सभुजं भां सचक्षुषः॥
en: Would be slain by me even though that antagonist of mine should adopt the vow of asceticism. Though I was fighting in battle with my arins and cyes in tact.

sn: मन्यध्वं मृत इत्येवमेतद् वो बुद्धिलाघवम्। युक्तो ह्यस्य प्रतीघातः कृतो मे कुरुपुङ्गचाः॥
en: Yet you had taken me as already slain. It is indeed a great foolishness on your part. You foremost of the Kurus, the slaughter of Bhurisravas achieved by me, in indeed very proper.

sn: यत् तु पार्थेन मां दृष्ट्वा प्रतिज्ञामभिरक्षता। सखङ्गोऽस्य हृतो बाहुरेतेनैवास्मि वञ्चितः॥
en: Partha by lopping off the arm of this one, with sword in grasp, had fulfiled his vow of protecting his own partisans and has thereby robbed me of my glory!

sn: भवितव्यं हि यद् भावि दैवं चेष्टयतीव च। सोऽयं हतो विमर्देऽस्मिन् किमत्राधर्मचेष्टितम्॥
en: What is ordained must come to pass. It is the hand of fate that works. Bhurisravas has been slain in the course of this battle. What sin have I perpetrated?

sn: अपि चायं पुरा गीतः श्लोको वाल्मीकिना भुवि। न हन्तव्याः स्त्रिय इति यद् ब्रवीषि प्लवङ्गम॥
en: In days gone by, Valmiki sang this verse on earth viz., "You say, Oape, that women should not be slain!

sn: सर्वकालं मनुष्येण व्यवसायवता सदा। पीडाकरममित्राणां यत् स्यात् कर्तव्यमवे तत्॥
en: In all times however men should always with resolute care do that which would give pain to this foes."

sn: संजय उवाच एवमुक्त महाराज सर्वे कौरवपुङ्गवाः। न स्म किंचिदभाषन्त मनसा समपूजयन्॥
en: Sanjaya said After Satyaki had said these words, none amongst the Pandavas and the Kauravas, o king, said anything; on the other hand they praised Bhurisravas in their mind.

sn: मन्त्राभिपूतस्य महाध्वरेषु। यशखिनो भूरिसहस्रदस्य चा मुनेरिवारण्यगतस्य तस्या न तत्र कश्चिद् वधमभ्यनन्दत॥
en: Nobody present there countenanced the slaughter of Somadatta's illustrious son, who resembled an hermit of the woods and who had given away thousands of golden coins.

sn: सुनीलकेशं वरदस्य तस्य शूरस्य पारावतलोहिताक्षम्। अश्वस्य मेध्यस्य शिरो निकृत्तं न्यस्तं हविर्धानमिवान्तरेण॥
en: The head of that brave hero graced with beautiful blue locks and eyes red like those of pegions looked like the head of a horse cut-off in a horse sacrifice and placed on the sacrificial altar.

sn: स तेजसा शस्त्रकृतेन पूतो महाहवे देहवरं विसृज्य। आक्रामदूर्ध्व वरदो वरा) व्यावृत्त्य धर्मेण परेण रोदसी॥
en: Purified through his prowess and death by the edge of weapons and in consequence of the boon accorded to him, Bhurisravas worthy of every boon went to the regions on high, shuffling off his mortal coil and filling the heavens with his illustrious fame.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच अजितो द्रोणराधेयविकर्णकृतवर्मभिः। तीर्णः सैन्यार्णवं वीरः प्रतिश्रुत्य युधिष्ठिरे॥
en: Dhritarashtra said Having promised to Yudhishthira to do so, the heroic Satyaki crossed the ocean of my troops, unvanquished cven by Drona, Radha's son, Vikarna and Kritavarman.

sn: स कथं कौरवेयेण समरेष्वनिवारितः। निगृह्य भूरिश्रवसा बलाद् भुवि निपातितः॥
en: How was it then that Satyaki checked and humiliated by the scion of the Kurus namely Bhurisravas, was brought down on the ground with force.

sn: शृणु राजन्निहोत्पतिं शैनेयस्य यथा पुरा। यथा च भूरिश्रवसो यत्र ते संशयो नृप॥
en: Sanjaya said Hear, O monarch, how the grandson of Sini came to being in days gone by as also how Bhurisravas was descended. O ruler of men, this will explain all your doubts.

sn: अत्रेः पुत्रोऽभवत् सोमः सोमस्य तुबुधः स्मृतः। बुधस्यैको महेन्द्राभः पुत्र आसीत् पुरूरवाः॥
en: Atri had Soma for his son and Soma's son was called Buddha. Buddha's son was Pururava whose effulgence was like that of the great Indra.

sn: पुरूरवस आयुस्तु आयुषो नहुषः सुतः। नहुषस्य ययातिस्तु राजा देवर्षिसम्मतः।
en: Pururava had a son called Ayush; and Ayush's son was Nahusha. Nahusha had Yayati for his son who was a royal sage equal to a celestial.

sn: ययातेर्देवयान्यां तु यदुर्येष्ठोऽभवत् सुतः। यदोरभूदन्ववाये देवमीढ इति स्मृतः॥
en: By his wife Deveyani Yayati had Yadu for his eldest son. In the dynasty of Yadu was born a son called by the name of Devamida.

sn: यादवस्तस्य तु सुतः शूरस्त्रैलोक्यसम्मतः। शूरस्य शौरिवरो वसुदेवो महायशाः॥
en: Devamnida of Yadu's race had Sura for his son, who was highly esteemed in all the three worlds. Sura had for his son that foremost of men namely the illustrious Vasudeva.

sn: धनुध्यनवरः शूरः कार्तवीर्यसमो युधि। तद्वीर्यश्चापि तत्रैव कुले शिनिरभून्नृप॥
en: Foremost of all wielders of bows, Sura was equal to Kartikeya in battle. O king, in his race and equal to him in energy was born Sini, O monarch.

sn: एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु देवकस्य महात्मनः। दुहितु, स्वयंवरे राजन् सर्वक्षत्रसमागमे॥
en: At this time, O monarch the Sayamvara of the daughter of the illustrious Devaka took place in which numerous Kshatriyas were present.

sn: तत्र वै देवकी देवीं वसुदेवार्थमाशु वै। निर्जित्य पार्थिवान् सर्वान् रथमारोपयच्छिनिः॥
en: In that Sayamvara, Sini having vanquished the kings, placed the princess Devaki on his car, with a view to marry her to Vasudeva.

sn: तां दृष्ट्वा देवकी शूरो रथस्थां पुरुषर्षभ। नामृष्यत महातेजाः सोमदत्तः शिने प॥
en: O foremost of men, O king, then beholding the princess Devaki on the car of Sini of Sura's line, the highly puissant Somadatta could not broke it.

sn: तयोर्युद्धमभूद् राजन् दिनार्ध चित्रमद्भुतम्। बाहुयुद्धं सुबलिनोः प्रसक्तं पुरुषर्षभ॥
en: Thereupon, O king, a battle was fought between then, that occupied half a day and was beautiful to look at. O foremost of men, a wrestling encounter then took place between those heroes endued with great heroism.

sn: शिनिना सोमदत्तस्तु प्रसह्य भुवि पातितः। असिमुद्यम्य केशेषु प्रगृह्य च पदा हतः॥
en: Somadatta then was seized upon and felled on the ground by Sini; and the latter raising his sword and holding the former by the hair, struck him with his legs.

sn: मध्ये राजसहस्राणां प्रेक्षकाणां समन्ततः। कृपया च पुनस्तेन स जीवेति विसर्जितः॥
en: In the midst of thousands of kings who were witnessing the combat, from all sides. Then out of mercy; the latter abandoned the former saying go, live.'

sn: तदवस्थः कृतस्तेन सोमदत्तोऽथ मारिष। प्रासादयन्महादेवममर्षवशमास्थितः॥
en: Reduced to that humiliatory condition, O sire, Somadatta, influenced by anger began to offer worship to Mahadeva in order to propitiate him.

sn: तस्य तुष्टो महादेवो वराणां वरदः प्रभुः। वरेण च्छन्दयामास स तु वने वरं नृपः॥
en: That foremost of all boon-giving deities namely Mahadeva became pleased with him and requested him to ask for his desired boon. The royal son of Somadatta then asked for this boon-

sn: पुत्रमिच्छामि भगवन् यो निपात्य शिनेः सुतम्। मध्ये राजसहस्राणां पदा हन्याच संयुगे॥
en: “I wish to have a son, O master, who will strike down Sini's son in the midst of thousands of kings in battle and who will strike the latter with his leg." related to you

sn: तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा सोमदत्तस्य पार्थिव। एवमस्त्विति तत्रोक्त्वा स देवोऽन्तरधीयत॥
en: Hearing these words of Somadatta O king, the god disappeared then and there saying 'so be it.'

sn: स तेन वरदानेन लब्धवान् भूरिदक्षिणम्। अपातयच समरे सौमदत्तिः शिनेः सुतम्॥
en: Through the virtue of that boon Somadatta afterwards got the liberal-minded and munificent Bhurisravas for his son; and it was thus that Somadatta's son succeeded in throwing down the descendant of Sini.

sn: पश्यतां सर्वसैन्यानां पदा चैनमताडयत्। एतत् ते कथितं राजन् यन्मां त्वं परिपृच्छसि।॥
en: And in striking him with his legs in the presence of the whole army. O king now I have what you asked me.

sn: न हि शक्यो रणे जेतुं सात्वतो मनुजर्षौः। लब्धलक्ष्याश्च संग्रामे बहुशश्चित्रयोधिनः॥
en: Indeed that scion of the Satvata race (Satyaki) cannot be worsted in battle by even the foremost of men. The Vrishni heroes are all of sure aim and are acquainted with all modes of warfare.

sn: देवदानवगन्धर्वान् विजेतारो ह्यविस्मिताः। स्ववीर्यविजये युक्ता नैते परपरिग्रह्यः॥
en: They can defeat the very gods the Danavas and the Gandharvas. They confounded; they fight depending totally on their own energy. They never seek other's help.

sn: न तुल्यं वृष्णिभिरिह दृश्यते किंचन प्रभो। भूतं भव्यं भविष्यच बलेन भरतर्षभ।॥
en: O lord, there is none in this world equal to the Vrishnis. O foremost of the Bharata's none, has been, are or will be a match for the Vrishnis in might.

sn: न ज्ञातिमवमन्यन्ते वृद्धानां शासने रताः। न देवासुरगन्धर्वा न यक्षोरगराक्षसाः॥
en: They never condemn their kinsmen and are ever observant of the commands of the elders. are never Neither the gods nor the Asuras, nor the Gandharvas, nor the Yakshas nor the Rakshasas.

sn: जेतारो वृष्णिवीराणां किं पुनर्मानवा रणे। ब्रह्मद्रव्ये गुरुद्रव्ये ज्ञातिस्वे चाप्यहिंसकाः॥
en: Can conquer the Vrishni heroes, what to speak of men! They never cast covetousglances on the things of possessions of their kinsmen, preceptor or those of the Brahmanas.

sn: एतेषां रक्षितारश्च ये स्युः कस्याञ्चिदापदि। अर्थवन्तोन चोत्सित्ता ब्रह्मण्याः सत्यवादिनः॥
en: They never covet also the properties of those that render then help on any time of distress. Devoted to the Brahinanas and truthful in speech, they never show any pride although they are wealthy.

sn: समर्थान् नावमन्यन्ते दीनानभ्युद्धरन्ति च। नित्यं देवपरा दान्तास्त्रातारश्चाविकत्थनाः॥
en: Those who are really strong are regarded as weak by the Vrishnis and are rescued by them when involved in any danger. Ever devoted to the worship of gods, the Vrishnis are selfcontrolled munificent and shorn of pride.

sn: तेन वृष्णिप्रवीराणां चक्रं न प्रतिहन्यते। अपि मेरुं वहेत् कश्चित् तरेद् वा मकरालयम्।
en: For this it is that prowess of the Vrishni heroes are never thwarted. It is possible for one to carry on his shoulders the Meru mountain or the swim across the very ocean.

sn: न तु वृष्णिप्रवीराणां समेत्यान्तं व्रजेन्नृप॥ एतत् ते सर्वमाख्यातं यत्र ते संशयः प्रभो। कुरुराज नरश्रेष्ठ तव व्यपनयो महान्।॥
en: But it is impossible for him to obtain advantage over the Vrishnis in an encounter with them. O lord, I have now explained to you everything in respect of which you entertained doubts. After all, O king of the Kurus, O foremost of men, yours is the great fault (that had bred this war).

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच तदवस्थे हते तस्मिन् भूरिश्रवसि कौरवे। यथा भूयोऽभवद् युद्धं तन्ममाचक्ष्व संजय॥
en: Dhritarashtra said When under these circumstances the Kuru warrior Bhurisravas had been slain, relate to me, O Sanjaya how the battle progressed.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: संजय उवाच भूरिश्रवसि संक्रान्ते परलोकाय भारत। वासुदेव महाबाहुरर्जुनः समचूचुदत्॥
en: Sanjaya said After Bhurisravas had gone to the regions of the departed, O Bharata, that mighty-armed Arjuna urged Vasudeva sayingचोदयाश्वान् भृशं कृष्ण

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: यतो राजा जयद्रथ.i श्रूयते पुण्डरीकाक्ष त्रिषु धर्मेषु वर्तते॥ प्रतिज्ञा सफलां चापि कर्तुमर्हसि मेऽनघ।
en: O Krishna, urge the steeds to the top of their speed, so that they may soon carry me to spot where king Jayadratha is, O sinless one, it behoves you, to help me in the fulfilment of my vow!

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: अस्तमेति महाबाहो त्वरमाणो दिवाकरः॥ एतद्धि पुरुषव्याघ्र महदभ्युद्यतं मया। कार्य संरक्ष्यते चैष कुरुसेनामहारथैः॥ तथा नाभ्येति सूर्योऽस्तं यथा सत्यं भवेद् वचः। चोदयाश्वांस्तथा कृष्ण यथा हन्यां जयद्रथम्॥
en: O mighty-armed one, the orb of the day, is quickly going towards the Western hills. O foremost of men, I have undertaken to achieve a mighty task. But the ruler of the Sindhus on the other hand is protected by many foremnost warriors among the Kurus. O Krishna, do you drive the horses in such a manner that my vow may be fulfilled before sunset and that Jayadratha may be slain. were

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: ततः कृष्णो महाबाहु रजतप्रतिमान् हयान्। हयज्ञश्चोदयामास जयद्रथवधं प्रति॥ तं प्रयान्तममोघेषुमुत्पतद्भिरिवाशुगैः। त्वरमाणा महाराज सेनामुख्या: समाद्रवन्॥ दुर्योधनश्च कर्णश्च वृषसेनोऽथ मद्रराट्।
en: Then the mighty-armed Krishna versed in horse-lore, urged those horses of Argentine hue towards the car of Jayadratha. Then as Arjuna proceeded shooting swift-flying arrows ever hitting their marks. O mighty monarch, the foremost warriors of yours troops quickly proceeded to meet him. They Duryodhana, Karna, Vrishasena, the king of the Madras.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: अश्वत्थामा कृपश्चैव स्वयमेव च सैन्धवः॥ समासाद्य च बीभत्सुः सैन्धवं समुपस्थितम्।
en: Ashvatthaman, Kripa and the ruler of the Sindhus himself; encountering the Sindhu king who was standing before him, Vibhatsu.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: नेत्राभ्यां क्रोधदीप्ताभ्यां सम्प्रेक्षन्निर्दहनिव॥ ततो दुर्योधनो राजा राधेयं त्वरितोऽब्रवीत्। अर्जुनं प्रेक्ष्य संयातं जयद्रथवधं प्रति॥
en: Cast his eyes burning with rage on him and seemed to burn the former there with. Thereupon king Duryodhana addressing Radha's son quickly said. 'Beholding Arjuna exert himself for compassing the slaughter of Jayadratha.” O king, your royal son Suyodhana spoke these very words to Karna.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: अयं स वैकर्तन युद्धकालो विदर्शयस्वात्मबलं महात्मन्। यथा न वध्येत रणेऽर्जुनेन जयद्रथः कर्ण तथा कुरुष्व॥
en: O son of Vikartana, the crisis in the battle has arrived. O high-souled warriors, now show your own strength. O Karna, do you so act as Jayadratha may not be slain in battle by Arjuna.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: अल्पावशेषो दिवसो नृवीर विघातयस्वाद्य रिपुं शरौघैः। दिनक्षयं प्राप्य नरप्रवीर ध्रुवोहि नः कर्ण जयो भविष्यति॥
en: O foremost hero among men, very little remains of the day. Thwart the enemy now with the waves of your arrows. O foremost of men, if we can safely reach the expire of the day, victory will certainly be ours.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: सैन्धवे रक्ष्यमाणे तु सूर्यस्यास्तमनं प्रति। मिथ्याप्रतिज्ञः कौन्तेयः प्रवेक्ष्यति हुताशनम्॥
en: If the ruler of the Sindhus can be saved till the sun sets, then the son of Kunti, in consequence of his vow being baffled will fall upon.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: अनर्जुनायां च भुवि मुहूर्तमपि मानद। जीवितुं नोत्सहरेन् वै भ्रातरोऽस्य सहानुगाः॥
en: O giver of honour, the brothers and the followers of Arjuna will not be able to live for a moment on the face of the earth, when he passes away from it.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: विनष्टैः पाण्डवेयैश्च सशैलवनकाननाम्। वसुंधरामिमां कर्ण भोक्ष्यामो हतकण्टकाम्॥
en: When the Pandavas will be destroyed, O Karna, we shall enjoy this earth with its mountains, gardens and forests, without a thorn in our sides.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: दैवेनोपहतः पार्थो विपरीतश्च मानद। कार्याकार्यमजानानः प्रतिज्ञां कृतवान् रणे॥
en: 0 bestower of honor, confounded by adverse Destiny and through the perversion of his judgment, Arjuna has made this vow without judging what is practicable and what impracticable.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: नूनमात्मविनाशाय पाण्डवेन किरीटिना। कर्ण जयद्रथवधं प्रति॥
en: Surely, O Karna, the diadem-decked son of Pandu had vowed the slaughter of Jayadratha for encompassing his own destruction.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: कथं जीवति दुर्धर्षे त्वयि राधेय फाल्गुनः। अनस्तंगत आदित्ये हन्यात् सैन्धवकं नृपम्॥
en: O son of Radha, how can Phalguna succeed in slaying the ruler of the Sindhus, before

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: प्रतिज्ञेयं कृता
en: sunset, when yourself indomitable in battle, is still alive?

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: रक्षितं मद्रराजेन कृपेण च महात्मना। जयद्रथं रणमुखे कथं हन्याद् धनंजयः॥
en: How can Dhananjaya succeed in slaying in battle Jayadratha who is protected by the king of the Madras and the illustrious Kripa himself?

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: द्रौणिना रक्ष्यमाणं च मया दुःशासनेन च। कथं प्राप्स्यति बीभत्सुः सैन्धवं कालचोदितः॥
en: How can Vibhatsu, who it appears is urged on by Fate, reach the Sindhu-king, who is protected by Drona's son and myself and Dushasana?

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: युध्यन्ते बहवः शूरा लम्बते च दिवाकरः। शङ्के जयद्रथं पार्थो नैव प्राप्स्यति मानद॥
en: Numerous heroic warriors are fighting for the sake of Jayadratha and the sun is also hanging low. O giver of honors, Partha will not be able to reach the ruler of the Sindhus in battle.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: स त्वं कर्ण मया साधु शूरैश्चान्यैर्महारथैः। द्रौणिना त्वं हि सहितो मद्रेशेन कृपेण च॥
en: Now, O Karna, supported by myself, by other heroic mighty car-warriors, by Drona's son, by the king of the Madras and Kripa himself.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: युध्यस्व यत्नमास्थाय परं पार्थेन संयुगे। एवमुक्तस्तु राधेयस्तव पुत्रेण मारिष॥
en: Do you fight with Pritha's son in battle, exerting to the best of your capabilities. Having been thus spoken to by your son, O sire, the son of Radha.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: दुर्योधनमिदं वाक्यं प्रत्युवाच कुरूत्तमम्। दृढलक्ष्येण वीरेण भीमसेनेन धन्विना॥ भृशं भिन्नतनुः संख्ये शरजालैरनेकशः। स्थातव्यमिति तिष्ठामि रणे सम्प्रति मानद॥
en: Replied to Duryodhana that foremost of the Kurus in these words-My body has been mangled with numerous net-works of arrows in the battle by the heroic Bhimasena of resolute aim and of skillful bowmanship. O bestower of honors, I now stay in battle-field, only because it is my duty to do so.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: नाङ्गमिङ्गति किंचिन्मे संतप्तस्य महेषुभिः। योत्स्यामि तु यथाशक्त्यात्वदर्थं जीवितं मम॥
en: Afflicted with mighty shafts there is not a single limb of mine that is not suffering excruciating pain; still I shall fight to the best of my abilities. My very life is for you.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: यथा पाण्डवमुख्योऽसौ न हनिष्यति सैन्धवम्। न हि मे युध्यमानस्य सायकानस्यतः शितान्॥
en: I shall do that by which this foremost of the Pandavas will not succeed in slaying the Sindhu-king. So long as I shall fight discharging sharp arrows.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: सैन्धवं प्राप्स्यते वीरः सव्यसाची धनंजयः। यत्तु भक्तिमता कार्यं सततं हितकाङ्क्षिणा॥
en: The brave Dhananjaya, who can shoot weapons even with his left hand, will not be able to reach the ruler of the Sindhus. Everything that a man bearing love and devotion to you and always anxious for your welfare, ought to do for you.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: तत् करिष्यामि कौरव्य जयो दैवे प्रतिष्ठितः। सैन्धवार्थे परं यत्नं करिष्याम्यद्य संयुगे॥
en: Shall be done by me, O you of Kuru's race. As regards our victory it is under the disposal of Destiny. I shall exert myself in battle today to the best of my abilities, for the sake of the Sindhu king.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: त्वत्प्रियार्थ महाराज जयो दैवे प्रतिष्ठितः। अद्य योत्स्येऽर्जुनमहं पौरुषं स्वं व्यपाश्रितः॥
en: And also for accomplishing what would conduce to your good, O monarch. But, o king, victory depends upon Destiny. Relying on my prowess, I shall today fight with Arjuna.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: त्वदर्थे पुरुषव्याघ्र जयो दैवे प्रतिष्ठितः। अद्य युद्धं कुरुश्रेष्ठ मम पार्थस्य चोभयोः॥ पश्यन्तु सर्वसैन्यानि दारुणं लोमहर्षणम्। कर्णकौरवयोरेवं रणे सम्भाषमाणयोः॥
en: For your sake, O foremost of men, but victory is dependent on Destiny. O foremost of the Kurus, let all the troops today witness the horripilating and fierce encounter that shall take place between myself and Pritha's son." When Karna and the king of the Kurus were thus talking to each other on the field.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: अर्जुनो निशितैर्बाणैर्जघान तव वाहिनीम्। चिच्छेद निशितैर्बाणैः शूराणामनिवर्तिनाम॥ भुजान् परिघसंकाशान् हस्तिहस्तोपमान् रणे। शिरांसि च महाबाहुश्चिच्छेद निशितै शरैः॥
en: Arjuna was engaged in slaughtering your army with his sharp arrows. He then cut-off with sharp Vallas the arms of unretreating heroes, arms that resembled bludgeons or trunks of elephants. That mighty-armed hero also severed many heads from the trunks of men with his arrows.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: हस्तिहस्तान् हयग्रीवान् रथाक्षांश्च समन्ततः। शोणिाक्तान् हयारोहान् गृहीतप्रासतोमरान्॥ क्षुरैश्चिच्छेद बीभत्सुधैिकैकं त्रिधैव च। हया वारणमुख्याश्च प्रापतन्त समन्ततः३७॥
en: Vibhatsu also cut-off the trunks of elephants, the necks of steeds, the axels of cars and also horses and men steeped in blood and armed with lances, in two or three fragments with his Kshurapras. And horses and excellent elephants.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: ध्वजाश्छत्राणि चापानि चामराणि शिरांसि च। कक्षमग्निरिवोद्भूतः प्रदहंस्तव वाहिनीम्॥
en: And standards and umbrellas and bows and chamaras and heads began to fall fast on all sides. The consuming your troops like fire consuming a heap of dry grass.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: अचिरेण महीं पार्थश्चकार रुधिरोत्तराम्। हतभूयिष्ठयोधं तत् कृत्वा तव बलं बली॥ आससाद दुराधर्षः सैन्धवं सत्यविक्रमः। बीभत्सुभीमसेनेन सात्वतेन च रक्षितः॥
en: Partha soon made the earth deluged with blood. The mighty and indomitable son of Pritha of prowess incapable of being baffled, spreading a terrible carnage in that host of yours, soon reached the ruler of the Sindhus. Protected by Bhimasena and by Satvata, Vibhatsu.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: प्रबभौ भरतश्रेष्ठ ज्वलन्निव हुताशनः। तं तथावस्थितं दृष्ट्वा त्वदीया वीर्यसम्पदा॥ नामृष्यन्त महेष्वासाः पाण्डवं पुरुषर्षभाः। दुर्योधनश्च कर्णश्च वृषसेनोऽथ मद्रराट्॥
en: O foremost of the Bharatas, appeared effulgent like a blazing fire. Then seeing Arjuna in that condition, all the fierce bowmen of your army, those foremost of men, possessed of the wealth of energy, could not brook him. Thereupon Duryodhana, Karna, Vrihasena, the ruler of the Madras.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: अश्वत्थाम कृपश्चैव स्वयमेव च सैन्धवः। संनद्धाः सैन्धवस्यार्थे समावृण्वन् किरीटिनम्॥
en: Ashvatthaman, Kripa and the ruler of the Sindhus surrounded the diadem-decked Arjuna on all sides.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: नृत्यन्तं रथमार्गेषु धनुर्ध्यातलनिःस्वनैः। संग्रामकोविदं पार्थ सर्वे युद्धविशारदाः॥ अभीताः पर्यवर्तन्त व्यादितास्यमिवान्तकम्। सैन्धवं पृष्ठतः कृत्वा जिघांसन्तोऽच्युतार्जुनौ॥
en: Then all those combatants skilled in fighting, placing the ruler Sindhus at their back and impelled by a desire for slaying Arjuna and Krishna, dauntlessly surrounded Partha, that hero versed in all modes of warfare., who then appeared to dance in the terrace of this chariot, emitting fierce sounds, with his bow-string and his palms and resembling the Destroyer himself with mouth agape.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: सूर्यास्तमनमिच्छन्तो लोहितायति भास्करे। ते भुजैर्भोगिभोगाभै—yष्यानम्य सायकान्॥
en: Meanwhile the sun and the heavens had assumed a crimson hue. Desirous of the speedy setting of the sun, the Kaurava warriors bending their bows with arms resembling the tapering bodies of serpents.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: मुमुचः सूर्यरश्म्याभाञ्छतशः फाल्गुनं प्रति। ततस्तानस्यमानांश्च किरीटी युद्धदुर्मदः॥ द्विधा त्रिधाष्टधैकैकं छित्त्वा विव्याध तान् रथान्। ॥ सिंहलाडुलकेतुस्तु दर्शयन् वीर्यमात्मनः॥
en: Discharged their arrows by hundreds, towards Phalguna, arrows, that resembled the rays of the sun. Cutting off all those shafts thus sped towards him, into two, three or eight fragments, the diadem-decked Arjuna, indomitable in battle, pierced them all (with his arrows). Then Ashvatthaman owning the device of a lion's tail in his banner, displaying his might.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: शारद्वतीसूतो राजन्नर्जुनं प्रत्यवारयत्। स विदध्वा दशभिः पार्थ वासुदेवं च सप्तभिः॥
en: Began, O monarch, to resist Arjuna. Indeed the son of the daughter of Saradvata, piercing Partha with ten shafts and Krishna with seven.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: अतिष्ठद् रथमार्गेषु सैन्धवं प्रतिपालयन्। अथैनं कौरवश्रेष्ठाः सर्व एव महारथाः॥ महता रथवंशेन सर्वतः प्रत्यवारयन्। विस्फारयन्तश्चापानि विसृजन्तश्च सायकान्॥
en: Impeded the progress of Arjuna's chariot, with a view to protect the ruler of the Sindhus. Then many foremost one among the Kurus all great car-warriors, surrounded Arjuna on all sides with a large number of chariots, stretching their bows and discharging numerous arrows.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: सैन्धवं पर्यरक्षन्त शासनात् तनयस्य ते। ततः पार्थस्य शूरस्य बाह्वोर्बलमदृश्यत॥
en: They began to exert themselves for protecting the ruler of the Sindhus, at the command of your son. We then beheld the strength of the heroic Partha's arms.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: इषूणामक्षयत्वं च धनुषो गाण्डिवस्य च। अस्त्रैरस्त्राणि संवार्य द्रौणेः शारद्वतस्य च॥
en: The inexhaustibility of his shafts and the strength also of his bow Gandiva. Repulsing with his own weapons, those of Drona's son and of Kripa.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: एकैकं दशभिबाणैः सर्वानेव समापर्यत्। तं द्रौणिः पञ्चविंशत्या वृषसेनश्च सप्तभिः॥
en: He pierced every one of your warriors with nine arrows. Thereupon Drona's son pierced him with twenty-five arrows and Vrishasena pierced him with seven.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: दुर्योधनस्तु विंशत्या कर्णशल्यौ त्रिभित्रिभिः। त एनमभिगर्जन्तो विध्यन्तश्च पुनः पुनः॥
en: Duryodhana pierced him with twenty, Karna with three shafts. And all of them roared at him and went on piercing him without remission.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: विधुन्वतश्च चापानि सर्वतः प्रत्यवारयन्। श्लिष्टं च सर्वतश्चक्रू रथमण्डलमाशु ते॥
en: Shaking their bows, they encompassed him on all sides and they also made their chariots to be drawn in a compact circle around him.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: सूर्यास्तमनमिच्छन्तस्त्वरमाणा महारथाः। त एनमभिनर्दन्तो विधुन्वाना धनूंषि च॥
en: Desirous of the speedy setting of the sun, those mighty fighters of the Kuru host possessed of great agility, began to roar at Arjuna and shaking their bows.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: सिषिचुर्मार्गणैस्तीक्ष्णैर्गिरिं मेघा इवाम्बुभिः। ते महास्त्राणि दिव्यानि तत्र राजन् व्यदर्शयन्॥ धनंजयस्य गात्रे तु शूराः परिघबाहवः। हतभूयिष्ठयोधं तत् कृत्वा तव बलं बली॥
en: Covered him with showers of sharp arrows like clouds pouring rain over the mountainbreast; those brave warriors, having arms like heavy bludgeons and showed on that occasion, 0 monarch, on Dhananjaya's body their celestials weapons. Having spread a great carnage in your army, your army, the mighty.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: आससाद दुराधर्षः सैन्धवं सत्यविक्रमः। तं कर्णः संयुगे राजन् प्रत्यवारयदाशुगैः॥
en: And indomitable Dhananjaya, of prowess incapable of being baffled, came upon the ruler of the Sindhus. Karna however, O king, with his arrows, resisted him in that battle.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: मिषतो भीमसेनस्य सात्वतस्य च भारत। तं पार्थो दशभिबाणैः प्रत्यविध्यद् रणाजिरे॥ सूतपुत्रं महाबाहुः सर्वसैन्यस्य पश्यतः। सात्वतश्च त्रिभिर्बाणैः कर्ण विव्याध मारिष॥
en: Before the very eyes, 0 Bharata of Bhimasena and Satvata. The mighty armed son of Pritha in the very sight of all the troops pierced the son of Suta, in return, with ten arrows, on the field of battle. Then Satvata, O sire, pierced Karna with three arrows.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: भीमसेनस्रिभिश्चैव पुनः पार्थश्च सप्तभिः। तान् कर्णः प्रतिविव्याध षष्ट्या षष्ट्या महारथः॥
en: Bhimasena pierced him with three and Partha again with seven arrows. Then Karna that mighty car-warrior pierced each of them with sixty shafts.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: तद् युद्धमभवद् राजन् कर्णस्य बहुभिः सह। तत्राद्भुतमपश्याम सूतपुत्रस्य मारिष॥
en: O king, then a terrible battle raged between Karna on one side and the many on the other, then, O sire, we beheld the wonderful prowess of the son of Suta.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: यदेकः समरे क्रुद्धस्त्रीन् रथान् पर्यवारयत्। फाल्गुनस्तु महाबाहुः कर्ण वैकर्तनं रणे॥ सायकानां शतेनैव सर्वमर्मस्वताडयत्। रुधिरोक्षितसर्वाङ्ग सूतपुत्रः प्रतापवान्॥
en: In asmuchas single-handed, he succeeded in checking the three mighty warriors in battle; then the mighty armed Phalguna struck Karna on the vital limbs with a group of hundred arrows. Thereupon, the puissant son of Suta, steeped all over his body with blood.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: शरैः पञ्चाशता वीरः फाल्गुनं प्रत्यविध्यता तस्य तल्लाघ्वं दृष्ट्वा नामृष्यत रणेऽर्जुनः॥
en: Pierced the heroic Phalguna in return with fifty arrows. Beholding that lightness of hands displayed by him, Arjuna did not throok him.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: ततः पार्थो धनुश्छित्त्वा विव्याधैनं स्तनान्तरे। सायकैनवभिवीरस्त्वरमाणो धनंजयः॥
en: Then Pritha's son busting his bow open, pierced him on his chariot with nine arrows of depressed knots, with great speed.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: अथान्यद् धनुरादाय सूतपुत्रः प्रतापवान्। सायकैरष्टसाहस्रश्छादयामास पाण्डवम्॥
en: Then with great lightness at a time when lightness was necessary, Dhananjaya in order to slay Karna, sped at him an arrows of the effulgence of the solar rays.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: तां बाणवृष्टिमतुला कर्णचापसमुत्थिताम्। व्यधमत् सायकैः पार्थः शलभानिव मारुतः॥
en: As that arrows was coursing with vehemence through the sky, Drona's son with a sharp crescent-shaped arrow cut it off, thus cut down it fell down, on the ground.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: छादयामास च तदा सायकैरर्जुनो रणे। पश्यतां सर्वयोधानां दर्शयन् पाणिलाघवम्॥
en: Then the highly puissant son of Suta taking up another bow, covered Pandu's son with thousands of arrows.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: वधार्थ चास्य समरे सायकं सूर्यवर्चसम्। चिक्षेप त्वरया युक्तस्त्वराकाले धनंजयः॥
en: Then with his arrows, Fritha's son scattered the unrivaled shower of arrows that proceeded from Karna's bow, like the tempest scattering masses of clouds.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: तमापतन्तं वेगेन द्रौणिश्चिच्छेद सायकम्। अर्धचन्द्रेण तीक्ष्णेन स च्छिन्नः प्रापतद् भुवि॥
en: Then again Arjuna covered him with arrows, before the eyes of all warriors, displaying great lightness of hands.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: कर्णोऽपि द्विषतां हन्ता छादयामास फाल्गुनम्। सायकैर्बहुसाहस्रैः कृतप्रतिकृतेप्सया॥
en: Karna also that slayer of foes, desirous of counteracting the feats of his antagonist, covered Phalguna with thousands of arrows.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: तौ वृषाविव नर्दन्तौ नरसिंहौ महारथौ। सायकैस्तु प्रतिच्छन्नं चक्रतुः खमजिह्मगैः॥
en: Roaring at each other like two bulls, those foremost of men, those two mighty carwarriors, covered the welkin with clouds of straight-going shafts.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: अदृश्यौ च शिरोघेस्तो निघ्नन्तावितरेतरम्। कर्ण पार्थोऽस्मि तिष्ठ त्वं कर्णोऽहं तिष्ठ फाल्गुन।।७६ इत्येवं तर्जयन्तौ तौ वाक्शल्यैस्तुदतां तदा। युध्येतां समरे वीरौ चित्रं लघु च सुष्ठु च॥
en: Each made invisible by the other's arrowy downpour, they went on striking each other; they roared at each other and wounded each other with their sharp arrows respectively saying, I am Partha wait or I am Karna, wait, O Phalguna. Indeed those two heroes fought with each wonderfully, displaying great skill and agility.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: प्रेक्षणीयौ चाभवतां सर्वयोधसमागमे। प्रशस्यमानो समरे सिद्धचारपपन्नगैः॥
en: The sight they then presented was such that all the other combatants became spectators of the battle. Then praised by the Siddhas and the Charanas and the Pannagas.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: अयुध्येतां महाराज परस्परवधैषिणौ। ततो दुर्योधनो राजस्तावकानभ्यभाषत॥
en: They fought on with each other desirous of slaying each other. Then Duryodhana addressing your warriors said

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: यत्नाद् रक्षत राधेयं नाहत्वा समरेऽर्जुनम्। निवर्तिष्यति राधेय इति मामुक्तवान् वृषः॥
en: “Heedfully protect the son of Radha. Without slaying Arjuna in battle, he will not abstain. Even these words had Vrisha said to me.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे राजन् दृष्ट्वा कर्णस्य विक्रमम्। आकर्णमुक्तैरिषुभिः कर्णस्य चतुरो हयान्॥ अनयत् प्रेतलोकाय चतुर्भिः श्वेतवाहनः। सारथिं चास्य भल्लेन रथनीडादपातयत्॥
en: In the meantime, o king, beholding the prowess of Karna, Arjuna of white horses, with four shafts shot from the bow-string drawn back to the ear, dispatched the four horses of Karna to the regions of Death. Then with a bhalla he felled Karna's charioteer from his niche in the car.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: छादयामास स शरैस्तव पुत्रस्य पश्यतः। संछाद्यमानः समरे हताश्वो हतसारथिः॥
en: Then he covered Karna himself with a network of arrows, even before the very eyes of your son. Thus covered with arrows, the steedless and driverless Karna.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: मोहितः शरजालेन कर्तव्यं नाभ्यपद्यता तं तथा विस्थं दृष्ट्वा रथमारोप्य तं तदा॥ अश्वत्थामां महाराज भूयोऽर्जुनमयोधयत्। मद्रराजश्च कौन्तेयमविध्यत् त्रिंशता शरैः॥
en: Confounded with arrowy showers was completely embraced. Beholding him made carless, Ashvatthaman, O monarch, caused him to ride on his own chariot and went on fightin with Arjuna. Then the king of the Madras pierced the son of Kunti with thirty arrows.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: शारद्वतस्तु विंशत्या वासुदेवं समार्पयत्। धनंजयं द्वादशभिराजघान शिलीमुखैः॥
en: The son of Saradvata pierced Vasudeva with twenty arrows; he then struck Dhananjaya with twelve arrows.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: चतुर्भिः सिन्धुराजश्च वृषसेनश्च सप्तभिः। पृथक् पृथङ्महाराज विव्यधुः कृष्णपाण्डवौ॥
en: The king of the Sindhus with four. Vrishasena with Karna, separately pierced 0 mighty monarch, Krishna and Pritha's son.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: तथैव तान् प्रत्यविध्यत् कुन्तीपुत्रो धनंजयः। द्रोणपुत्रं चतुःषष्ट्या मद्रराजं शतेन च॥
en: Dhananjaya, the son of Kunti then in return pierced Drona's son with sixty-four and the ling of the Madras while hundred arrows.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: सैन्धवं दशभिर्गाणैर्वृषसेनं त्रिभिः शरैः। शारद्वतं च विंशत्या विद्ध्वा पार्थो ननाद ह॥
en: He pierced the Sindhu ruler with Vallas and Vrishasena with three arrows and then piercing the son of Saradvata, Pritha's son uttered a loud war-cry.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: ते प्रतिज्ञाप्रतीधातमिच्छन्त: सव्यसाचिनः। सहितास्तावकास्तूर्णमभिपेतुर्धनंजयम्॥
en: Then your troops desirous of baffling the fulfillment of Savayasachin's vow, quickly fell upon him, all inflamed with rage.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: अथार्जुनः सर्वतो वारुणास्रं प्रादुश्चके त्रासयन् धार्तराष्ट्रान्। तं प्रत्युदीयुः कुरवः पाण्डुपुत्रं स्थैर्महाहैः शरवर्षाण्यवर्षन्॥
en: Then striking terror into the hearts of the Dhritarastra's troops, Arjuna invoked into existence the Varuna weapon. Then Karna riding on his precious chariot, pouring showers of arrows, proceeded against the son of Pritha.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: ततस्तु तस्मिंस्तुमुले समुत्थिते। सुदारुणे भारत मोहनीये। नोऽमुह्यत प्राप्य स राजपुत्रः। किरीटमालीव्यसृजच्छरौघान्॥
en: But, O Bharata, as that fierce stupefying and terrible battle progressed, the diademdecked Arjuna reaching the Sindhu king did not loose his senses and sped his arrows continuously.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: राज्यप्रेप्सुः सव्यसाची कुरूणां स्मरन् क्लेशान् द्वादशवर्षवृत्तान्। गाण्डीवमुक्तैरिषुभिर्महात्मा। सर्वा दिशो व्यावृणोदप्रमेयः॥
en: Desirous of getting back the kingdom and keeping in mind all the wrongs inflicted by the Kurus on them during twelve years past, the high-souled Savyasachin of immeasurable prowess, shrouded all the points of the compass with shafts shot from the Gandiva.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: प्रदीप्तोल्कमभवचान्तरिक्ष मृतेषु देहेष्वपतन् वयांसि। यत् पिङ्गलज्येन किरीटमाली क्रुद्धो रिपूनाजगवेन हन्ति॥
en: The welkin then seemed to be illumined by blazing neteors; countless crows began to shoot down on the bodies of the troops. Meanwhile the diadem-decked Arjuna continued to slay the foe with his Gandiva of twany string like the wrathful Mahadeva slaying creatures with his Ajagara bow.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: ततः किरीट महता महायशाः शरासनेनास्य शराननीकजित्। हयप्रवेकोत्तमनागधूर्गतान् कुरुप्रवीरानिषुभिर्व्यपातयत्॥
en: Then the highly-renowned Arjuna that subduer of hostile troops, scattering away the arrows of the son Drona by means of those shot from his own bow, slew many foremost warriors of the Kurus. mounted on their excellent steeds and elephants.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: नसींश्च शक्तीश्च नराधिपाः। महान्ति शस्त्राणि च भीमदर्शनाः प्रगृह्य पार्थ सहसाभिदुद्रुवुः॥
en: Then numerous monarchs taking up heavy maces and clubs of iron and swords and darts and many other kinds of strong weapons and assuming frightful appearance, advanced furiously upon Partha in that battle.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: ततो युगान्ताभ्रसमखनं महन्महेन्द्रचापप्रतिमं च गाण्डिवम्। चकर्ष दोर्ध्या विहसन् भृशं ययौ दहंस्त्वदीयान् यमराष्ट्रवर्धनः॥
en: Arjuna bending his with the force of his arms, his terrible bow the Gandiva that resembled the bow of Indra and of which the twang was as loud as roar of clouds at the end of a Yuga, went on carnaging your soldiers and adding to the population of Death's domain.

description: Continuous The fierce fight between Arjuna and Karna
sn: स तानुदीर्णान् सरथान् सवारणान् पदातिसङ्घांश्च महाधनुर्धरः। विपन्नसर्वायुधजीवितान् रणे चकार वीरो यमराष्ट्रवर्धनान्॥
en: Then that brave warrior caused those furious warriors with their cars and elephants and foot soldiers and bowmen supporting them, to be deprived of their arms and lives and thus considerable added to the population of Yama's kingdom.

sn: संजय उवाच श्रुत्वा निनादं धनुषश्च तस्य विस्पष्टमुत्क्रुष्टमिवान्तकस्य। शक्राशनिस्फोटसमं सुधोरं विकृष्यमाणस्य धनंजयेन॥
en: Sanjaya said Hearing the twang of Dhananyaja's bow, that resembled the loud call of Death or the sonorous rumble of the thunder.

sn: त्रासोद्विग्नं तथोद्भान्तं त्वदीयं तद् बलं नृप। युगान्तवातसंक्षुब्धं चलद्वीचितरङ्गितम्॥ प्रलीनमीनमकरं सागराम्भ इवाभवत्। सरणे व्यचरत् पार्थः प्रेक्षमाणो धनंजयः॥
en: Your troops, O monarch, agitated with fear and greatly confounded, became like the waters of the sea, with the fishes and Makaras within them, ruffled into huge waves and lashed to fury by the storm that blows at the end of a Yoga. Then the handsome son of Pritha, by name Dhananjaya began to career on the field of battle.

sn: युगपद् दिक्षु सर्वासु सर्वाण्स्त्राणि दर्शयन्। आददातुं महाराज संदधानं च पाण्डवम्॥ उत्कर्षन्तं सृजन्तं च न स्म पश्याम लाघवात्। ततः क्रुद्धो महाबाहुरैन्द्रमस्रं दुरासदम्॥ प्रादुश्चक्रे महाराज त्रासयन् सर्वभारतान्। ततः शराः प्रादुरासन् दिव्यास्रप्रतिमन्त्रिताः॥ प्रदीप्ताश्च शिखिमुखा: शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः। आकर्णपूर्णनिर्मुक्तैरग्न्याशुनिभैः शरैः॥
en: Displaying inighty weapons and simultaneously showing his presence in all the different directions. O mighty monarch, indeed we could not then discern when the son of Pandu took out his arrows, placed them on the bowstring, drew the string hack and let them off, so great was his lightness of hands. Thereafter the mighty-armed one, excited to the highest pitch of fury, invoked into existence the terrible Indra weapon and mighty monarch thereby inspired the Bharatas with terror. Hundreds and thousands of blazing arrows, of fiery heads and inspired with Mantras then began to start up into existence. Then with those shafts, shot from a string drawn back to the ear the resembling the rays of the sun or the flame of fire.

sn: नभोऽभवत् तद् दुष्प्रेक्ष्यमुल्काभिरिव संवृतम्। ततः शस्रान्धकारं तत् कौरवैः समुदीरितम्॥
en: The sky became incapable of being looked at, as if covered with flashing meteors. Thereupon the darkness that the Kauravas had created with their arrows.

sn: अशक्यं मनसाप्यनयैः पाण्डवः सम्भ्रमनिव। नाशयामास विक्रम्य शरैर्दिव्यास्रमन्त्रितैः॥
en: And that was incapable of being dispersed by other men even in their imagination. The son of Pandu, traversing the field and displaying his energy, dispelled by means of his arrows inspired by Mantras with the energy of celestial weapons.

sn: नैशं तमोऽशुभिः क्षिप्रं दिनादाविव भास्करः। ततस्तु तावकं सैन्यं दीप्तैः शरगभस्तिभिः॥ आक्षिपत् पल्वलाम्बूनि निदाघार्क इव प्रभुः। ततो दिव्यास्रविदुषा प्रहिताः सायकांशवः॥
en: Like the sun dispelling at day-break the darkness of night with his light-rays. The with those blazing arrowy rays of his, the puissant son of Pritha sucked the lives of your warriors, like the summer sun sucking with his scorching rays the waters of tanks and lakes. Then those arrows sped by him conversant in the use of celestial weapons.

sn: समाप्लवन् द्विषत्सैन्यं लोकं मानोरिवांशवः। अथापरे समुत्सृष्टा विशिखास्तिग्मतेजसः॥
en: Covered over the hostile troops, like the rays of the sun covering over the earth. Similarly other arrows of fierce energy shot by Arjuna.

sn: हृदयान्याशु वीराणां विविशुः प्रियबन्धुवत्। य एनमीयुः समरे त्वद्योधाः शूरमानिनः॥
en: Entered into the hearts of heroes, as if they were their intimate friends. Those of then ventured to encounter Arjuna.

sn: शलभा इव ते दीप्तमग्निं प्राप्य ययुः क्षयम्। एवं स मृद्गशत्रूणां जीवितानि यशांसि च॥
en: Were destroyed like so many insects falling upon a blazing lamp flame. Thus crushing the lives and fame of his enemies.

sn: पार्थश्चचार संग्रामे मृत्युर्विग्रहवानिव। सकिरीटानि वक्त्राणि साङ्गदान् विपुलान् भुजान्॥१५
en: Pritha's son careered on the field like Death incarnate. Heads decked with diadems,, huge arms adorned with Angadas.

sn: सकुण्डलयुगान् कर्णान् केषांचिदहरज्छरैः। सतोमरान् गजस्थानां सप्रासान् हयसादिनाम्॥
en: And ears graced with pairs of ear-rings, of his enemies, Pritha's son cut-off with his shafts. The arms of elephant-riders, with Tomaras; those of horsemen, with Prasas;

sn: सचर्मणः पदातीनां रथीनां च सधन्वनः सप्रतोदान् नियन्तॄणां बाहूंश्चिच्छेद पाण्डवः॥
en: Those of foot-soldiers with shields; those of car-warriors with bows; and those drivers, with whips and hooks, the son of Pandu then cut-. off.

sn: प्रदीप्तोग्रशरार्चिष्मान् बभौ तत्र धनंजयः। सविस्फुलिङ्गाग्रशिखो ज्वलन्निव हुताशनः॥
en: Dhananjaya then shone resplendent with his arrows of glittering tips that seemed to constitute his rays, like a blazing fire with incessant scintillations and raging flames.

sn: तं देवराजप्रतिमं सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वरम्। युगपद् दिक्षु सर्वासु रथस्थं पुरुषर्षभम्॥ निक्षिपन्तं महास्त्राणि प्रेक्षणीयं धनंजयम्। नृत्यन्तं रथमार्गेषु धनुातलनादिनम्॥ निरीक्षितुं न शेकुस्ते यत्नवन्तोऽपि पार्थिवाः। मध्यंदिनगतं सूर्य प्रतपन्तमिवाम्बरे॥
en: The hostile kings then inspite of all their endeavours, could not even secure a sight of the handsome Dhananjaya, that foremost of all wielders of weapons, that hero equal to the king of the celestials, that best of men, seen at the same time in all directions on his chariot, shooting his terrible weapons, dancing in the terrace of his car and producing deafening sounds with his bow-string and palms and resembling the mid-day sun of burning rays in the heavens.

sn: दीप्तोग्रसम्भृतशरः किरीट विरराज ह। वर्षास्विवोदीर्णजल: सेन्द्रधन्वाम्बुदो महान्॥
en: The diadem-decked Arjuna, armed with arrows of glittering tips shone resplendent like a mighty mass of cloud swelling with rain and bearing the rainbow on its bosom.

sn: महास्रसम्पल्वे तस्मिञ्जिष्णुना सम्प्रवर्तिते। सुदुस्तरे महाघोरे ममज्युर्योधपुङ्गवाः॥
en: Then when that veritable flood of mighty weapons was created by Jishnu, many foremost warriors sank in that dreadful and uncrossable sea of weapons.

sn: उत्कृत्तवदनैर्दैहैः शरीरैः कृत्तबाहुभिः। भुजैश्च पाणिनिर्मुक्तैः पाणिभिर्व्यङ्गुलीकृतैः॥
en: Strewn over with mangled faces and bodies and limbs, with lacerated arms, with arms deprived of palms and palms deprived of fingers.

sn: कृत्ताग्रहस्तैः करिभिः कृत्तदन्तैर्मदोत्कटैः। हयैश्च विधुरग्रीवै रथैश्च शकलीकृतैः॥
en: With infuriate elephants having trunks and tusks severed and broken respectively, with horses deprived of riders and necks; with shattered chariots.

sn: निकृत्तान्त्रैः कृत्तपादैस्तथान्यैः कृत्तसंधिभिः। निश्चेष्टैर्विस्फुरद्भिश्च शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः॥
en: With bodies having entrails drawn out, legs cut-off and severed remaining still or moving unconsciously and with hundreds and thousands of corpses and car-casses.

sn: मृत्योराघातललितं तत्पार्थायोधानं महत्। अपश्याम महीपाल भीरूणां भयवर्धनम्॥
en: The field where Partha fought was seen by us to resemble an area ravaged by Death and to enhance, O ruler of men, the fears of the cowards.

sn: आक्रीडमिव रुद्रस्य पुराभ्यर्दयतः पशून्। गजानां क्षुरनिर्मुक्तैः करैः सभुजगेव भूः॥
en: Or it then appeared like the sporting ground of Rudra where he slew creatures in days gone by. Portions of the field covered over with trunks of elephants, severed by Kshurapras, appeared as if covered by snakes.

sn: क्वचिद् बभौ स्रग्विणीव वक्त्रपझैः समाचिता। विचित्रोष्णीषमुकुटैः केयूराङ्गदकुण्डलैः॥
en: Portions again strewn over with the heads of warriors graced with lotus like countenances, looked as if covered with garlands of flower. With beautiful head gears and crowns, with Keyuras, Angadas and Kundalas.

sn: स्वर्णचित्रतनुत्रैश्च भाण्डैश्च गजवाजिनाम्। किरीटशतसंकीर्णा तत्र तत्र समाचिता॥
en: With armours decked with gold, with the caparisons and trappings of elephants and horses and with hundreds of diadems, strewn all over with these things.

sn: विरराज भृशं चित्रा मही नववधूरिव। मञ्जामेदःकर्दमिनी शोणितौघतरङ्गिणीम्॥
en: The earth, highly beautified, appeared like a newly married bride. Having the marrow and fat (of slain creatures) for its mire, having blood for its current.

sn: मर्मास्थिभिरगाधां च केशशैवलशाद्वलाम्। शिरोबाहूपलतटां रुग्णक्रोडास्थिसंकटाम्॥
en: Full of limbs and bones and fathomless in death, having the hair of creatures for its moss and weeds and heads and arms for stones on its shore;

sn: चित्रध्वजपताकाढ्यां छत्रचापोर्मिमालिनीम्। विगतासुमहाकायां गजदेहाभिसंकुलाम्॥
en: Decked with variegated standards and banners; having umbrellas and bows for its huge waves; stagnant with the huge carcasses of elephants.

sn: रथोडुपशताकीर्णा हयसंघातरोधसम्। रथचक्रयुगेपाक्षकूबरैरतिदुर्गमाम्॥
en: Having innumerable cars for rafts to cross it; infested with the dead bodies of horses; rendered unfordable with car wheels, yokes, axels and Kuvaras;

sn: प्रासासिशक्तिपरशुविशिखाहिदुरासदाम्। बलकङ्कमहानक्रां गोमायुमकरोत्कटाम्॥
en: Infested with snakes constituted by lances, darts, axes and arrows; having crows and Kankas for its sharks and jackals for its Makaras.

sn: गृध्रोदग्रमहाग्राहां शिवाविरुतभैरवाम्। नृत्यत्प्रेतपिशाचाद्यैर्भूताकीर्णा सहस्रशः॥
en: And vultures for its fierce aquatic animals; echoing with the yells of jackals; infested with dancing ghosts and Pisachas and Pretas, thousands in number.

sn: गतासुयोधनिश्चेष्टशरीरशतवाहिनीम्। महाप्रतिभयां रौद्रां घोरां वैतरणीमिव॥
en: Carrying away many, corpses of slain warriors, highly dreadful and fierce and awful

sn: नदी प्रवर्तयामास भीरूणां भयवर्धिनीम्। तं दृष्ट्वा तस्य विक्रान्तमन्तकस्येव रूपिणः॥
en: Such a river capable of striking terror into the hearts of the cowards, was then caused to flow on the field of battle. Then beholding the prowess of Arjuna, whose appearance then resembled that of the Destroyer.

sn: अभूतपूर्व कुरूषु भयमागाद् रणाजिरे। तत आदाय वीराणामस्त्रैरस्त्राणि पाण्डवः॥
en: A panic, such as had never occurred before, prevailed among the Kuru ranks. Thereupon the son of Pandu, receiving the weapons of heroes, with those of his own.

sn: आत्मानं रौद्रमाचष्ट रौद्रकर्मण्यधिष्ठितः। ततो रथवरान् राजन्नत्यतिक्रामदर्जुनः॥
en: And achieving wonderful feats, proclaimed himself to be a warrior of terrible deeds. Then 0 king, Arjuna passed leaving all those foremost car-warriors of your army behind.

sn: मध्यंदिनगतं सूर्य प्रतपन्तमिवाम्बरे। न शेकुः सर्वभूतानि पाण्डवं प्रतिवीक्षितुम्॥
en: Then all the creatures were unable to look at Pandu's son, who then resembled the sun shining on the meridian,

sn: प्रसृतांस्तस्य गाण्डीवाच्छरवातान् महात्मनः। संग्रामे सम्प्रपश्यामो हंसपङ्क्तिमिवाम्बरे॥
en: Arrows shooting out of the Gandiva bow of that illustrious hero, were then seen by us to resemble rows of cranes ranging through the firmament.

sn: विनिवार्य स वीराणामस्त्रैरस्त्राणि सर्वतः। दर्शयन् रौद्रमात्मानमुने कर्मणि धिष्ठितः॥ स तान् रथवरान् राजन्नत्याक्रामत् तदार्जुनः। मोहयन्निव नाराचैर्जयद्रथवधेप्सया।
en: Repulsing everywhere the weapons of heroes with those of his own and displaying his fierce feats, Arjuna then continued to a achieve terrible deeds. Then impelled by the desire for killing Jayadratha, O king, Arjuna passed through the car-division, compounding your warriors with his Narachas.

sn: विसृजन् दिक्षु सर्वासु शरानसितसारथिः॥ सरथो व्यचरत् तूर्णं प्रेक्षणीयो धनंजयः।
en: Then the handsome Dhananjaya having Krishna for his charioteer, began quickly to career on the field, shooting his shafts in all directions.

sn: भ्रमन्त इव शूरस्य शरव्राता महात्मनः॥ अदृश्यन्तान्तरिक्षस्थाः शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः।
en: Then hundreds and thousands of shafts shot by the heroic Arjuna of illustrious soul, appeared in the sky, flying in all directions and incessantly.

sn: आददानं महेष्वासं संदधानं च सायकम्॥ विसृजन्तं च कौन्तेयं नानुपश्याम वै तदा।
en: We then could not discern when that mighty bowmen, that son of Pandu begotten upon Kunti, took out his shafts, placed them on the bow-string and let them off.

sn: तथा सर्वा दिशो राजन् सर्वाश्च रथिनो रणे॥ कदम्बीकृत्य कौन्तेयो जयद्रथमुपाद्रवत्।
en: Thereafter, O king, covering all the points of the compass with his arrows and afflicting all the car-warriors in battle, the son of Kunti dashed towards Jayadratha.

sn: विव्याध च चतुःषष्ट्या शराणां नतपर्वणाम्॥ सैन्धवाभिमुखं यान्तं योधाः सम्प्रेक्ष्य पाण्डवम्।
en: And pierced him with four and sixty straight-going shafts. The Kuru warriors then seeing Pandu's son rush upon Jayadratha.

sn: न्यवर्तन्त रणाद् वीरा निराशास्तस्य जीविते॥ यो योऽभ्यधावदाक्रन्दे तावकः पाण्डवं रणे।
en: Gave up fighting, becoming hopeless of Jayadratha's life. Whoever amongst your troops then rushed to encounter the son of Pandu in that battle.

sn: तस्य तस्यान्तगा बाणाः शरीरे न्यपतन् प्रभो॥ कबन्धसंकुलं चक्रे तव सैन्यं महारथः। अर्जुनो जयतां श्रेष्ठः शरैरग्न्यंशुसंनिभैः॥ एवं तत् तव राजेन्द्र चतुरङ्गबलं तदा। व्याकुलीकृत्य कौन्तेयो जयद्रथमुपाद्रवत्॥ द्रौणिं पञ्चाशताविध्यद् वृषसेनं त्रिभिः शरैः।
en: Had his body pierced deep with the latter's arrows. Then the mighty car-warriors Arjuna, that foremost of victorious heroes made your ranks headless by means of his arrows resembling the flames of fire. Thus then, O foremost of kings, sorely afflicting your troops consisting of four kinds of forces, the son of Kunti rushed upon Jayadratha. He then pierced Drona's son with five hundred and Vrishasena with three arrows.

sn: कृपायमाणः कौन्तेयः कृपं नवभिरार्दयत्॥ शल्यं षोडशभिर्बाणैः कर्णं द्वात्रिंशता शरैः।
en: Compassionate as the son of Kunti was, he pierced Kripa with nine arrows. He pierce Slay with sixteen and Karna with thirty two arrows.

sn: सैन्धवं तु चतुःषष्ट्या विद्ध्वा सिंह इवानदत्॥ सैन्धवस्तु तथा विद्धः शरैर्गाण्डीवधन्वना।
en: Then piercing the ruler of the Sindhus with sixty-four arrows, he uttered a roar like that of the lion. Then the ruler of the Sindhus, being pierced with the arrows shot from the bow of the wielder of the Gandiva.

sn: न चक्षमे सुसंक्रुद्धस्तोत्रादित इव द्विपः॥ स वराहध्वजस्तूर्णं गार्धपत्रानजिह्मगान्। क्रुद्धाशीविषसंकाशान् कर्मारपरिमार्जितान्॥ आकर्णपूर्णाञ्चिक्षेप फाल्गुनस्य रथं प्रति।
en: And excited to the highest pitch of fury, did not to brook it, even like an elephant struck with the good. Then that one bearing the boar car arrows as a device on his standard quickly shot at the of Phalguna straight-flying furnished with vulturine feathers, rubbed by the smith and looking like so many enraged snakes and hurled from a string dawn back to the very ears.

sn: स विक्षिप्यार्जुनस्तूर्णं सैन्धवप्रहिताशरान्॥ युगपत् तस्य चिच्छेद शराभ्यां सैन्धवस्य ह। सारथेश्च शिरः कायाद् ध्वजं च समलंकृतम्॥ स छिन्नयष्टिः सुमहान् धनंजयशराहतः। वराहः सिन्धुराजस्य पपाताग्निशिखोपमः॥ एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु द्रुतं गच्छति भास्करे।
en: Thereupon Arjuna, repuising the sharp shafts shot by the ruler of the Sindhus, cut-off at the same time, with a couple of arrows, the head of Jayadratha's driver and his welldecked standard. Its stay cut-off and itself shattered and struck with arrows, that boars bearing standard of the Sindhu king fell down like a flash of fire. Meanwhile the sun was rapidly going towards the western hills.

sn: अब्रवीत् पाण्डवं राजंस्त्वरमाणो जनार्दनः॥ एष मध्ये कृतः षड्भिः पार्थ वीरैर्महारथैः।
en: Janardana quickly addressing Pandu's son said-"O son of Pritha, this Jayadratha has been placed in their midst by these heroic and mighty car-warriors.

sn: जीवितेप्सुर्महाबाहो भीतस्तिष्ठति सैन्धवः॥ एताननिर्जित्य रणे षड् स्थान् पुरुषर्षभ।
en: O mighty-armed one, Jayadratha desirous of saving his life, is standing in the rear in their midst. O foremost of men, without vanquishing in battle these six mighty car-warriors.

sn: न शक्यः सैन्धवो हन्तुं यतो निर्व्याजमर्जुन॥ योगमत्र विधास्यामि सूर्यस्यावरणं प्रति।
en: You shall not be able to slay the ruler of the Sindhus, even if you exert yourself to the best of your powers, O Arjuna. Now I shall put forth my Yoga prowess for covering over the Sun.

sn: अस्तंगत इति व्यक्तं द्रक्ष्यत्येकः स सिन्धुराट्। ६४ हर्षेण जीविताकाक्षी विनाशार्थं तव प्रभो।
en: in consequence of which the ruler of the Sindhus only shall behold the sun as already set. Filled with delight and sanguine of his life and desirous of seeing your destruction.

sn: न गोप्स्यति दुराचारः स आत्मानं कथंचन॥ तत्र छिद्रे प्रहर्तव्यं त्वयास्य कुरुसत्तम।
en: That wicked creature will no longer conceal himself. Taking advantage of that opportunity you should, O foremost of the Kurus, strike him.

sn: व्यपेक्षा नैव कर्तव्या गतोऽस्तमिति भास्करः॥ एवमस्त्विति बीभत्सुः केशवं प्रत्यभाषत।
en: You should not then give up the enterprise thinking the sun to have already set. "Then Vibhatsu replied to Keshava saying “let it be so."

sn: ततोऽसृजत् तमः कृष्णः सूर्यस्यावरणं प्रति॥ योगी योगेन संयुक्तो योगिनामीश्वरो. हरिः।
en: Thereafter that lord of the kings viz., Krishna created a veil of darkness for covering the sun, by means of his Yoga prowess.

sn: सृष्टे तमसि कृष्णेन गतोऽस्तमिति भास्करः॥ त्वदीया जहषुर्योधाः पार्थनाशानराधिप।
en: When Krishna had created that veil of darkness, thinking the sun to have set, your troops became delighted, O king, in view of the destruction of Pritha's son Arjuna.

sn: प्रहृष्टा रणे राजन् नापश्यन् सैनिका रविम्॥ उन्नाम्य वक्त्राणि तदा स च राजा जयद्रथः।
en: Highly delighted, O King, your troops and king Jayadratha could not see the sun though they all stood with their heads thrown back.

sn: वीक्षमाणे ततस्तस्मिन् सिन्धुराजे दिवाकरम्॥ पुनरेवाब्रवीत् कृष्णो धनंजयमिदं वचः।
en: When the ruler of the Sindhus was beholding the setting sun, once more did Krishna spoke these words to Arjuna.

sn: पश्य सिन्धुपतिं वीरं प्रेक्षमाणं दिवाकरम्॥ भयं हि विप्रमुच्यैतत् त्वत्तो भरतसत्तम।
en: Beholding, O foremost of the Bharatas, the heroic ruler of the Sindhus looked at the sun, freed from the fear he entertained to you.

sn: ते अयं कालो महाबाहो वधायास्य दुरात्मनः॥ छिन्धि मूर्धानमस्याशु कुरु साफल्यमात्मनः।
en: O mighty-armed one this is the opportune moment to slay the wicked-souled weight. Now quickly lop off the head of this fellow and fulfill your vows.

sn: इत्येवं केशवेनोक्तः पाण्डुपुत्रः प्रतापवान्॥ न्यवधीत् तावकं सैन्यं शरैराग्निसंनिभैः।
en: Thus spoken to by Keshava the puissant son of Pandu, began to carnage your troops with arrows resembling the rays of the sun or the flame of fire.

sn: कृपं विव्याध विंशत्या कर्ण पञ्चाशता शरैः॥ शल्यं दुर्योधनं चैव षभिः षड्भिरताडयत्।
en: He pierced Kripa with twenty and Karna with fifty shafts; he then wounded Shalya and Duryodhana each with six shafts.

sn: वृषसेनं तथाष्टाभिः षष्ट्या सैन्धवमेव च॥ तथैव च महाबाहुस्त्वदीयान् पाण्डुनन्दनः।
en: He pierced Vrishasena with eight and the ruler of the Sindhus with sixty shafts. The mighty-armed son of Pandu.

sn: गाढं विद्ध्वा शरै राजन् जयद्रथमुपाद्रवत्॥ तं समीपस्थितं दृष्ट्वा लेलिहानमिवानलम्।
en: Piercing your troops with his arrows, O king, assailed Jayadratha. Then beholding him within measurable distance like a swelling tongue of fire.

sn: जयद्रथस्य गोप्तारः संशयं परमं गताः॥ ततः सर्वे महाराज तव योधा जयैषिणः।
en: The protectors of Jayadratha became highly anxious (about his life). Then O mighty monarch, all your warriors desirous of victory.

sn: सिषिचुः शरधाराभिः पाकशासनिमाहवे॥ संछाद्यमानः कौन्तेयः शरजालैरनेकशः। अक्रुध्यत् स महाबाहुरजितः कुरुनन्दनः॥ ततः शरमयं जालं तुमुलं पाकशासनिः। व्यसृजत् पुरुषव्याघ्रस्तव सैन्यजिघांसया॥ ते हन्यमाना वीरेण योधा राजन् रणे तव।
en: Began to pour their arrowy showers of Pakasasani in that battle. Then that delight of was over. the Kurus (Arjuna) covered Thereafter, that foremost of men, Pakasasani began to shoot terrible net-works of arrows with a view to slaughter your troops. Then those warriors of yours mangled by that hero in battle.

sn: प्रजहुः सैन्धवं भीता द्वौ समं नाप्यधावताम्॥ तत्राद्भुतमपश्याम कुन्तीपुत्रस्य विक्रमम्।
en: Where greatly frightened frightened and they abandoned the ruler of the Sindhus. They were so much confused that no two persons were seen to fly together. Then we beheld the wonderful prowess of Kunti's son.

sn: तादृड्न भावी भूतो वा यच्चकार महायशाः॥ द्विपान् द्विपगतांश्चैव हयान् हयगतानपि।
en: Inasmuch as that high-souled warrior then achieved feats whose equals had never before becn achieved or will be achieved in future. Elephants and elephant-riders and horses and horsemen.

sn: तथा स रथिनश्चैव न्यहन् रुद्रः पशूनिव॥ न तत्र समरे कश्चिन्मया दृष्टो नराधिप।
en: And car-drivers, these then Arjuna began to slaughter like Rudra slaying the creatures. I could not find in that battle. O king.

sn: गजो वाजी नरो वापि यो न पार्थशराहतः॥ रजसा तमसा चैव योधाः संछन्नचक्षुषः।
en: A single elephant or horses of men that was not struck with the arrows of Partha. The vision of warriors were blinded with dust and darkness.

sn: कश्मलं प्राविशन् घोरं नान्वजानन् परस्परम्॥ ते शरैर्भिन्नमर्माणः सैनिकाः पार्थचोदितैः।
en: They were dreadfully confused and could not recognise one another. Your troops urged on by fate, having their vitals torn open by arrows.

sn: बभ्रमुश्चस्खलुः पेतुः सेदुर्मम्लुश्च भारत॥ तस्मिन् महाभीषण के प्रजानामिव संक्षये।
en: Began to wander or lamp of fall down. Some became paralysed and some became pale. During that terrible carnage of creatures.

sn: रणे महति दुष्पारे वर्तमाने सुदारुणे॥ शोणितस्य प्रसेकेन शीघ्रत्वादनिलस्य च। अशाम्यत् तद् रजो भौममसृक्सिक्ते धरातले॥ आनाभि निरमज्जश्च रथवक्त्राणि शोणिते।
en: In that awful and fierce battle from which few escaped alive, the earth became deluged with blood and the dust that had then arisen disappeared inconsequence of the showers of blood and the gale that blew over the field of battle; so great was the shower of blood that car wheel sank in the mire caused thereby up to their naves.

sn: मत्ता वेगवतो राजस्तावकानां रणाङ्गणे॥ हस्तिनश्च हतारोहा दारिताङ्गा सहस्रशः।
en: Thousands of mad elephants possessed of great energy, O king, of your army, their riders slain the limbs mangled.

sn: स्वान्यनीकानि मृद्गन्त आर्तनादाः प्रदुद्रुवुः॥ हयाच पतितारोहाः पत्तयश्च नराधिप।
en: Began to fly away uttering shrieks of pain and crushing their own ranks under heath their feat. Riderless steeds and foot soldiers also, O monarch.

sn: प्रदुद्रुवुर्भयाद् राजन् धनंजयशराहताः॥ मुक्तकेशा विकवचाः क्षरन्तः क्षतज क्षतैः। प्रापलायन्त संत्रस्तास्त्यक्त्वा रणशिरो जनाः॥ ऊरुग्राहगृहीताश्च केचित् तत्राभवन् भुवि।
en: Fled away in fright, struck with the arrows of Dhananjaya. Indeed your troop with dishevelled hairs and shattered arinours, with blood streaming out of their wounds, fled away from the field of battle, forsaking it out of fear. Some again deprived of the power of moving, remained there as if their lower limbs had been seized by alligators.

sn: हतानां चापरे मध्यं द्विरदानां निलिल्यिरे॥ एवं तव बलं राजन् द्रावयित्वा धनंजयः।
en: Some hid themselves behind and under the carcasses of slain elephants. Thus causing your troop to fly, O monarch, Dhananjaya.

sn: न्यवधीत् सायकै?रैः सिन्धुराजस्य रक्षिणः॥ द्रौणिं कृपं कर्णशल्यौ वृषसेनं सुयोधनम्। छादयामास तीव्रण शरजालेन पाण्डवः॥ न गृह्णन् न क्षिपन् राजन् मुञ्चन्नापि च संदधत्। अदृश्यतार्जुनः संख्ये शीघ्रास्रत्वात् कथंचन॥ धनुर्मण्डलमेवास्य दृश्यते स्मास्यतः सदा। सायकाश्च व्यदृश्यन्त निश्चरन्तः समन्ततः॥ कर्णस्य तु धनुश्छित्त्वा वृषसेनस्य चैव ह।
en: Began to wound with dreadful shafts the protectors of the Sindhu ruler. The son of Pandu then covered with his arrowy showers Karna, Drona's son, Kripa, Shalya, Vrishasena and Duryodhana. Arjuna was quick in the use of weapons that none was able to notice when he took out his arrows, fixed them on the bowstring and stretched the bow and discharged them. Thus when he was engaged in wounding the foe, his bow was seen incessantly drawn to a circle. Thousands of shafts were seen to issue out from his bow and to scatter in all directions. Then severing off Karna's and Vrishasena's bow.

sn: शल्यस्य सूतं भल्लेन रथनीडादपातयत्॥ गाढविद्धावुभौ कृत्वा शरैः स्वस्त्रीयमातुलौ। अर्जुनो जयतां श्रेष्ठो द्रौणिशारद्वतौ रणे॥ एवं तान् व्याकुलीकृत्य त्वदीयानां महारथान्।
en: Arjuna with a broad-headed arrow felled Shalya's charioteer from his niche on the car. Then that foremost of victorious heroes viz. Dhananjaya, pierced with many arrows in that battle Kripa and Ashvatthaman, related to each other as uncle and nephew. Thus sorely afflicting the mighty car-warriors of your army.

sn: उनहार शरं घोरं पाण्डवोऽनलसंनिभम्॥ इन्द्राशनिसमप्रख्यं दिव्यमस्त्राभिमन्त्रितम्।
en: Pandu's son took up a terrible shaft of the splendour of fire. Appearing like the thunderbolt of Indra and inspired with sacred Mantras.

sn: सर्वभारसह शश्वद् गन्धमाल्यार्चितं महत्॥ वज्रेणास्त्रेण संयोज्य विधिवत् कुरुनन्दनः।
en: That dreadful arrow became capable of bearing any strain. It used always to be worshipped with perfumes and garlands of flowers. Duly charging it was the impetuosity of the thunder-bolt, that descendant of Kuru.

sn: समादधन्माहाबाहुर्गाण्डीवे क्षिप्रमर्जुनः॥ तस्मिन् संधीयमाने तु शरे ज्वलनतेजसि।
en: Namely the mighty-armed Arjuna, placed it on the Gandiva's string. When that shaft of fiery effulgence was fixed on the bow string.

sn: अन्तरिक्षे महानादो भूतानामभवन्नृप॥ अब्रवीच पुनस्तत्र त्वरमाणो जनार्दनः।
en: Loud shouts were heard, O king, in the welkin. Then Janardana once more quickly addressing Arjuna said

sn: धनंजय शिरश्छिन्धि सैन्धवस्य दुरात्मनः॥ अस्तं महीधरश्रेष्ठं यियासति दिवाकरः।
en: O Dhananjaya quickly cut-off the head of the wicked-souled ruler of the Sindhus. The sun is on the point of going to the Western hills.

sn: शृणुष्वैतच वाक्यं मे जयद्रथवधं प्रति॥ वृद्धक्षत्रः सैन्धवस्य पिता जगति विश्रुतः।
en: Listen however to the words that I am going to speak about the slaughter of Jayadratha. The father of Jayadratha is Vridhakshatra known all over the world.

sn: स कालेनेह महता सैन्धवं प्राप्तवान् सुतम्॥ जयद्रथममित्रघ्नं वागुवाचाशरीरिणी। नृपमन्तर्हिता वाणी मेघदुन्दुभिनिःस्वना॥ तवात्मजो मनुष्येन्द्र कुलशीलदमादिभिः। गुणैर्भविष्यति विभो सदृशो वंशयोर्द्वयोः॥
en: It was after a long time that he got Jayadratha that slayer of enemies, for his son; on the occasion of his son's birth, a disembodied and unseen voice, deep as the rumble of clouds or the beat of the drums, said unto king Vridhakshatra-'This your son, O master among men, in this world, will become worthy of the two races (the solar and the lunar) in respect of lineage, conduct, selfpossession and such other attributes. He will become one of the foremost of Kshatriyas and will always obtain adoration from the heroes.

sn: क्षत्रियप्रवरो लोके नित्यं शूराभिसत्कृतः। किं त्वस्य युध्यमानस्य संग्रामे क्षत्रियर्षभः॥ शिरश्छेत्स्यति संक्रुद्धः शत्रुरालक्षितो भुवि।
en: But while struggling in battle, some one foremost among the Kshatriyas, some wellknown person in the world, worked up with anger, will cut-off his head.'

sn: एतच्छुत्वा सिन्धुराजो ध्यात्वा चिरमरिंदमः॥ ज्ञातीन् सर्वानुवाचेदं पुत्रस्नेहाभिचोदितः।
en: That subduer of foes, viz., the old ruler of the Sindhus having heard these words became thoughtful for a while; filled with affection for his son, he summoned all his kinsmen and told them so.

sn: संग्रामे युध्यमानस्य वहतो महतीं धुरम्॥ धरण्यां मम पुत्रस्य पातयिष्यति यः शिरः। तस्यापि शतधा मूर्धा फलिष्यति न संशयः॥ एवमुक्त्वा ततो राज्ये स्थापयित्वा जयद्रथम्।
en: That man who will caused the head of my sons to fall on the earth, struggling in battle, will be bearing a great burden. I say that the head of that man will crack into a hundred pieces.' Having spoken these words and having installed Jayadratha on the throne.

sn: वृद्धक्षत्रो वनं यातस्तपश्चोग्रं समास्थितः॥ सोऽयं तप्यति तेजस्वी तपो घोरं दुरासदम्।
en: Vridhakshatra, retired into the woods and devoted himself to ascetic austerities. Possessed of great energy, he is still engaged in the observance of the austerest of penances.

sn: समन्तपञ्चकादस्माद् बहिर्वानरकेतन॥ तस्माजयद्रथस्य त्वं शिरश्छित्त्वा महामृधे।
en: Outside the precincts of the Samantapanchaka, o ape-bononered one. Therefore, severing Jayadratha's head in this terrible fight, you.

sn: दिव्येनास्त्रेण रिपुहन् घोरेणाद्भुतकर्मणा॥ सकुण्डलं सिन्धुपतेः प्रभञ्जनसुतानुजा उत्सङ्गे पातयस्वास्य वृद्धक्षत्रस्य भारत॥ अथ त्वमस्य मूर्धानं पातयिष्यासि भूतले।
en: O slayer of foes, should, O Bharata, by your fierce heaven-made weapons capable of achieving great feats, quickly throw that head adorned with ear-ring upon the lap of Vridhakshatra himself, O younger brother of the son of the wind-god. If you cause Jayadratha's head to fall on the earth.

sn: तवापि शतधा मूर्धा फलिष्यति न संशयः॥ यथा चेदं न जानीयात् स राजा तपसि स्थितः। तथा कुरु कुरुश्रेष्ठ दिव्यमस्रमुपाश्रितः॥ न ह्यसाध्यमकार्य वा विद्यते तव किंचन। समस्तेष्वपि लोकेषु त्रिषु वासवनन्दन॥
en: Then your own head will certainly crack into hundred pieces. By mean of your weapons of celestial make do you accomplish your vow in such a way, that may not know that it is done. O Arjuna, indeed their is nothing which you cannot achieve or perform, Oson of Vasava.

sn: एतच्छ्रुत्वा तु वचनं सृक्किणी परिसंलिहन्। इन्द्राशनिसमस्पर्श दिव्यमन्त्राभिमन्त्रितम्॥ सर्वभारसहं शश्वद् गन्धमाल्यार्चितं शरम्। विससर्जार्जुनस्तूर्णं सैन्धवस्य वधे धृतम्॥ स तु गाण्डीवनिर्मुक्तः शरः श्येन इवाशुगः। छित्त्वा शिरः सिन्धुपतेरुत्पपात विहायसम्॥ तच्छिर: सिन्धुराजस्य शरैरूर्ध्वमवाहयत्।
en: Having heard these words of Krishna, Dhananjaya licking the corners of his mouth. Shot the shaft he had taken up for slaughtering Jayadratha, shaft whose touch resembled that of Indra's thunder which was inspired with mantras, which was of celestial make, which was capable of bearing any strain and which had ever been worshipped with perfumes and garlands. That swift-coursing arrows shot from the Gandiva bow, snatched away the head of the ruler of the Sindhus like a hawk snaluhing away a little bird from the top of a tree. Dhananjaya then discharging other arrows carried that head along in the heavens.

sn: दुर्हदामप्रहर्षाय सुहृदां हर्षणाय च॥ शरैः कदम्बकीकृत्य काले तस्मिश्च पाण्डवः। योधयामास तांश्चैव पाण्डवः षण्महारथान्॥ ततः सुमहदाश्चर्ये तत्रापश्याम भारत। समन्तपञ्चकाद् बाह्यं शिरो यद् व्यहरत् ततः॥ एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु वृद्धक्षत्रो महीपतिः।
en: Then that son of Pandu imparting delight to his friends and grief to his foes, made his head like a Kadamba flower. He fought with those six great car-warriors. O Bharata! There was wonder, he carried that head beyond the precincts of the Samantapanchaka by means of his continuous groups of arrows. Meanwhile king Vridhakshatra.

sn: संध्यामुपास्ते तेजस्वी सम्बन्धी तव मारिष॥ उपासीनस्य तस्याथ कृष्णकेशं सकुण्डलम्। सिन्धुराजस्य मूर्धानमुत्सङ्गे समपातयत्॥ तस्योत्सङ्गे निपतितं शिरस्तचारुकुण्डलम्। वृद्धक्षत्रस्य नृपतेरलक्षितमरिंदम॥ कृतजप्यस्य तस्याथ वृद्धक्षत्रस्य भारत। प्रोत्तिष्ठतस्तत् सहसा शिरोऽगच्छद् धरातलम्॥
en: The father of your son-in-law, possessed of great energy, was engaged in perfuming his evening Sandhya. Adorned with sable locks and graced with ear-rings, that head of Jayadratha was thrown upon his lap as he was uttering his prayers in a sitting posture. () subduer of foes, thus thrown in his lap, that head graced with beautiful ear-rings was not perceived by king Vridhakshatra, so when the intelligent Vridhakshatra, having finished his evening prayers, was rising up, the head fell down on the earth.

sn: ततस्तस्य नरेन्द्रस्य पुत्रमूर्धनि भूतले। गते तस्यापि शतधा मूर्धागच्छदरिंदम॥ ततः सर्वाणि सैन्यानि विस्मयं जग्मुरुत्तमम्।
en: And as the head of that king's son fell down on earth. The head of that king also was cracked into thousand pieces, subduer of foes. Then all creatures were greatly filled with wonder.

sn: वासुदेवं च बीभत्सुं प्रशशंसुर्महारथम्॥ ततो विनिहते राजन् सिन्धुराजे किरीटिना। तमस्तद् वासुदेवेन संहृतं भरतर्षभ॥ पश्चाज्ज्ञातं महीपाल तव पुत्रैः सहानुगैः।
en: They then highly applauded Vasudeva and the mighty son of Pritha. Thus 0 king, when the king of the Sindhus was slain by the diadem-decked Arjuna.
