The darkness that Vasudeva's son had caused was withdrawn, O foremost of the Bharatas. O ruler of carth, thus your sons and their followers, afterwards came to know that.

sn: वासुदेवप्रयुक्तेयं मायेति नृपसत्तम॥ एवं स निहतो राजन् पार्थेनामिततेजसा। अक्षौहिणीरष्ट हत्वा जामाता तव सैन्धवः॥
en: That veil of darkness was only an illusion caused by Vasudeva's son, O foremost of men. Thus, O king, was your son-in-law, the ruler of the Sindhus slain by Arjuna of infinite energy, having caused the slaughter of eight Akshauhini of troops.

sn: हतं जयद्रथं दृष्ट्वा तव पुत्रा नराधिप। दुःखादश्रूणि मुमुचुनिराशाश्चाभवञ्जये॥ ततो जयद्रथे राजन् हते पार्थेन केशवः।
en: Then beholding Jayadratha the ruler of the Sindhus's slain, tearing of sorrow gushed out from the eyes of your sons. Thereafter, O king, when Jayadratha had been slain by Pritha's son, Keshava.

sn: दध्मौ शङ्ख महाबाहुरर्जुनश्च परंतपः॥ भीमश्च वृष्णिसिंहश्च युधामन्युश्च भारत।
en: Blew his conch, as also the mighty Arjuna that afflicter of his foes. Bhimasema also, as if for informing Yudhishthira of that joyful news.

sn: उत्तमौजाश्च विक्रान्तः शङ्खान् दध्मुः पृथक् पृथक्॥ १३७ श्रुत्वा महान्तं तं शब्दं धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः।
en: Filled the welkin with a mighty war-cry. Hearing that formidable war-cry, the very virtuous king Yudhishthira.

sn: सैन्धवं निहतं मेने फाल्गुनेन महात्मना॥ ततो वादित्रघोषेण स्वान् योधान् पर्यहर्षयत्।
en: Considered the ruler of the Sindhus to be slain by the high-souled Phalguna. Then he son imparted delight to his own warriors by means of the sound of his musical instruments.

sn: अभ्यवर्तत संग्रामे भारद्वाजं युयुत्सया॥ ततः प्रववृते राजन्नस्तंगच्छति भास्करे।
en: He then rushed furiously against the son of Bharadvaja for slaying him. Then, O king, as the sun was hanging down the horizon.

sn: द्रोणस्य सोमकैः सार्धं संग्रामो लोमहर्षणः॥ ते तु सर्वे प्रयत्नेन भारद्वाजं जिघांसवः।
en: A fierce battle between Drona and the Somakas commenced, capable making the hair to stand erect. Then putting forth all their energies slaughtering the of Bharadvaja.

sn: सैन्धवे निहते राजन्नयुध्यन्त महारथाः॥ पाण्डवास्तु जयं लब्ध्वा सैन्धवं विनिहत्य च। अयोधयंस्तु ते द्रोणं जयोन्मत्तास्ततस्ततः॥ अर्जुनोऽपि ततो योधांस्तावकान् रथसत्तमान्। अयोधयन्महाबाहुर्हत्वा सैन्धवकं नृपम्॥
en: The mighty car-warriors of the Pandavas fought on, O king, delighted at the slaughter of the Sindhu king. The Pandavas then obtaining victory and having slain the ruler of the Sindhus, fought on with Drona literally intoxicated with their good luck. o king, having slain the ruler of the Sindhus, long armed Arjuna also fought with those carwarriors.

sn: स देवशत्रूनिव देवराजः किरीटमालीव्यधमत्समन्तात्। यथा तमांस्यभ्युदितस्तमोनः पूर्वप्रतिज्ञां समवाप्य वीरः॥
en: Then the heroic Arjuna decked with a diadem and garlands, having fulfilled his principal; vow, began to slaughter your troops, even like the king of the celestials destroying the darkness of night.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच तस्मिन् विनिहते वीरे सैन्धवे सव्यसाचिना। मामका यदकुर्वन्त तन्ममाचक्ष्व संजय॥
en: Dhritarashtra said The heroic king of Sindhu being killed by that one who could draw the bow with his left hand (i.e., Arjuna), relate to me O Sanjaya,

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: संजय उवाच सैन्धवं निहतं दृष्ट्वा रणे पार्थेन भारत। अमर्षवशमापन्न: कृपः शारद्वतस्ततः॥
en: Sanjaya said O king, seeing the king Sindhu slain in battle by Partha, Kripa, the son of Saradvat, waxing wrath.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: महता शरवर्षेण पाण्डवं समवाकिरत्। द्रौणिश्चाभ्यद्रवद् राजन् रथमास्थाय फाल्गुनम्॥
en: Surrounded the son of Pandu by a mighty discharge of arrows. The son of Drona too, seated on his car, rushed against Phalguna, the son of Pritha.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: तावेतौ रथिनां श्रेष्ठौ रथाभ्यां रथसत्तमौ। उभावुभयतस्तीक्ष्णैर्विशिखैरभ्यवर्षताम्॥
en: Those two best and most excellent of carwarriors from two sides, began to shower keen darts, from their cars (upon Arjuna).

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: स तथा शरवर्षाभ्यां सुमहद्भ्यां महाभुजः। पीड्यमानः परामार्तिमगमद् रथिनां वरः॥
en: That mighty-armed one, the best of carwarriors, sore oppressed by those mighty showers of arrows, experienced a great pain.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: सोऽजिघांसुर्मुरं संख्ये गुरोस्तनयमवे च। चकाराचार्यकं तत्र कुन्तीपुत्रो धनंजयः॥
en: Dhananjaya, the son of Kunti, not liking to slay his preceptor (i.e. Kripa) and his (other) preceptor's son (i.e. Ashvatthama) in battle began to act like a preceptor (teaching the science of arms of his pupil).

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: अस्त्रैरस्त्राणि संवार्य द्रौणे: शारद्वतस्य च। मन्दवेगानिपूंस्ताभ्यामजिघांसुरवासृजत्॥
en: And unwillingly warded off the weapons of the sons of Drona and Saradvat, by means of his own weapons and discharged at them arrows of milder speed.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: ते चापि भृशमभ्यघ्नन् विशिखा: पार्थचोदिताः। बहुत्वात् तु परामाति शराणां तावगच्छताम्॥
en: Overcome by the numbers of arrows though discharged mildly by Arjuna, those two (warriors) were greatly afflicted.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: अथ शारद्वतो राजन् कौन्तेयशरपीडितः। अवासीदद् रथोपस्थे मूर्छामभिजगाम ह॥
en: Then, O monarch, the son of Saradvat, painted by the darts of the son of Kunti, lost all strength and fainted away on the terrace of his car.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: विह्वलं तमभिज्ञाय भर्तारं शरपीडितम्। हतोऽयमिति च ज्ञात्वा सारथिस्तमपावहत्॥
en: Seeing his master afflicted with darts and devoid of senses and taking him for dead his charioteer carried him off (from the field of battle).

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: तस्मिन् भग्ने महाराज कृपे शारद्वते युधि। अश्वत्थामाप्यपायासीत् पाण्डवेयाद् स्थान्तरम्॥
en: Then, O great king, Kripa being thus borne away from (the field of battle), Ashvatthaman too fled away in terror from the son of Pandu.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: दृष्ट्वा शारद्वतं पार्थो मूच्छितं शरपीडितम्। रथ एव महेष्वासः सकृपं पर्यदेवयत्॥
en: (Then), seeing the son of Saradvat faint away and afflicted with arrows, the mighty bowman Partha, (seated) on his car, gave way to doleful cries.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: अश्रुपूर्णमुखो दीनो वचनं चेदमब्रवीत्। पश्यन्निदं महाप्राज्ञः क्षत्ता राजानमुक्तवान्॥
en: And with his face full of tears and in "Anticipating all this, the greatly wise Kshatta (Vidura) said to the king (Dhritarashtra).

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: कुलान्तकरणे पापे जातमात्रे सुयोधने। नीयतां परलोकाय साध्वयं कुलपांसनः॥
en: As soon as the destroyer of his race, the vile Suyodhana was born, Make away this destroyer of your race.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: अस्माद्धि कुरुमुख्यानां महदुत्पत्स्यते भयम्। तदिदं समनुप्राप्तं वचनं सत्यवादिनः॥
en: (Or), through him a great disaster will befall the best of the Kuru race. Now the words of that truthful one have proved true.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: तत्कृते ह्यद्य पश्यामि शरतल्पगतं गुरुम्। धिगस्तु क्षात्रमाचारं धिगस्तु बलपौरुषम्॥
en: It is on his account, that I behold today my preceptor lying on an arrowy bed. Curse on the practices of the Kshatriyas and on my strength and manliness!

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: को हि ब्राह्मणमाचार्यमभिदुह्येत मादृशः। ऋषिपुत्रो ममाचार्यो द्रोणस्य परमः सखा।॥
en: (For) is there any body, who is, like me, hostile to a Brahmana who is his preceptor as well? He is (moreover) the son of a sage, my preceptor and the dear friend of Drona.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: एष शेते रथोपस्थे कृपो मद्बाणपीडितः। अकामयानेन मया विशिखैरर्दितो भृशम्॥
en: Such a one lies (insensible) on the terrace of his car smitten with my darts. Although I did not wish it, (still), through me he has been crushed with the arrows.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: अवसीदन् रथोपस्थे प्राणान् पीडयतीव मे। पुत्रशोकाभितप्तेन शरैरभ्यर्दितेन च॥
en: (The sight of his) lying insensible on the terrace of his car greatly afflicts my heart. Though sorely afflicted with his arrows, I should have looked at that one of great splendour (without striking him).

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: अभ्यस्तो बहुभिर्बाणैर्दशधर्मगतेन वै। शोचयत्येष नियत्तं भूयः पुत्रवधाद्धि माम्॥
en: Afflicted with various darts he has gone to the way of all creatures. I grieve more over his than on the slaughter of my son.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: कृपणं स्वरथे सन्नं पश्य कृष्ण यथागतम्। उपाकृत्य तु वै विद्यामाचार्येभ्यो नरर्षभाः॥
en: O Krishna, beholding what a sad plight he is in, lying senseless of his car! Those most excellent of men, who after acquiring knowledge from their preceptors.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: प्रयच्छन्तीह ये कामान् देवत्वमुपयान्ति ते। ये च विद्यामुपादाय गुरुभ्यः पुरुषाधमाः॥
en: Bestow on them what they desire, attain to Godhead. (But) those basest of men who after acquiring knowledge from their preceptors.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: प्रन्ति तानेव दुर्वृत्तास्ते वै निरयगामिनः। तदिदं नरकायाद्य कृतं कर्म मया ध्रुवम्॥
en: Destroy them, are doomed to hell. Surely, what I have done today will lead me to hell.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: आचार्य शरवर्षेण रथे सादयता कृपम्। यत् तत् पूर्वमुपाकुर्वन्नत्रं मामब्रवीत् कृपः॥
en: In as much as I have overpowered my preceptor with showers of arrows. Formerly when teaching me the science of weapons, Kripa said to me.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: न कथंचन कौरव्य प्रहर्तव्यं गुराविति। तदिदं वचनं साधोराचार्यस्य महात्मनः॥
en: "O scion of Kuru's race, on no account strike thy preceptor.” (But, those words of my virtuous and high-souled preceptor).

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: नानुष्ठितं तमेवाजौ विशिखैरभिवर्षता। नमस्तस्मै सुपूज्याय गौतमायापलायिने॥
en: I have disregarded and have struck him with showers of arrows. I bow down to that worshipful son of Goutama, who never flies away (from the field of battle).

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: धिगस्तु मम वार्ष्णेय यदस्मै प्रहराम्यहम्। तथा विलयमाने तु सव्यसाचिनि तं प्रति॥
en: O scion of Vrishni's race, fie on me who have struck him. While that one who could draw his bow as well with the left hand (i.e. Arjuna) was thus grieving for him.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: सैन्धवं निहितं दृष्ट्वा राधेयः समुपाद्रवत्। तमापतन्तं राधेयमर्जुनस्य रथं प्रति॥
en: The son of Radha beholding the king of Sindhu dead rushed against him. (Seeing?) the son of Radha make for the car of Arjuna.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: पाञ्चाल्यौ सात्यकिश्चैव सहसा समुपाद्रवन्। उपायान्तं तु राधेयं दृष्ट्वा पार्थो महारथः॥
en: The two Panchala princes and Satyaki came up to him. Seeing the son of Radha rush (against him), the mighty car-warrior Partha.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: प्रहसन् देवकीपुत्रमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्। एष प्रयात्याधिरथिः सात्यकेः स्यन्दनं प्रति॥
en: Said these words to the son of Devaki with a simile-“(Behold!) the son of Adhiratha is making for the car of Satyaki.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: न मृष्यति हतं नूनं भूरिश्रवसमाहवे। यत्र यात्येष तत्र त्वं चोदयाश्वान् जनार्दन॥
en: Surely, he cannot endure the destruction of Bhurisrava in battle. O Janaradana, drive the horses towards the place whither he goes.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: न सौमदत्तिपदवीं गमयेत् सात्यकिं वृषः। एवमुक्तो महाबाहुः केशवः सव्यसाचिना॥
en: Have a care that Vrisha cannot send the Satvata hero to the path of Somadatta.” Thus addressed by that one who could draw his bow as well with the left hand, Keshava, possessed of mighty arms.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: प्रत्युवाच महातेजाः कालयुक्तमिदं वचः। अलमेष महाबाहुः कर्णायैकोऽपि पाण्डव।॥
en: And great energy, replied (to him) in words suited to the occasion “O Pandava, this mighty arıncd one (Satyaki) is alone capable of fighting with Karna.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: किं पुनद्रौपदेयाभ्यां सहितः सात्वतर्षभः। न च तावत् क्षमः पार्थ तव कर्णेन सङ्गरः॥
en: (And), much more son, since this most exalted of the Satvatas is joined by the two sons of Drupada. O Partha, you need (therefore, not fight with Karna at present.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: प्रज्वलन्ती महोल्केव तिष्ठत्यस्य हि वासवी। त्वदर्थे पूज्यमानैषा रक्ष्यते परवीरहन्॥
en: He has with him the blazing dart, like a terrible meteor, granted to him by Vasava. O destroyer of hostile warriors, he has preserved it (carefully) for (slaying) you and worships it.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: अतः कर्णः प्रयात्वत्र सात्वतस्य यथातथा। अहं ज्ञास्यामि कौन्तेय कालमस्य दुरात्मनः। यत्रैनं विशिखैस्तीक्ष्णैः पातयिष्यसि भूतले॥
en: Let, therefore, Karna march against the scion of Satvatta's race as he wills. I am, O son of Kunti, conscious of the hour when this wicked-souled one will be struck down on the ground from his car (pierced) by keen darts.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच योऽसौ कर्णेन वीरस्य वार्ष्णेयस्य समागमः। हते तु भूरिश्रवसि सैन्धवे च निपातिते॥
en: Dhritarashtra said How, after Bhurisrava and the king of Sindhu being slain, the heroic Karna and the scion of Vrishni's race, came incontact with each other.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: सात्यकिश्चापि विरथः कं समारूढवान् रथम्। चक्ररक्षौ च पाञ्चाल्यौ तन्ममाचक्ष्व संजय॥
en: And on what cars the carless Satyaki and the two Panchala princes, the protectors of (Arjuna's) car-wheels (respectively) mounted, relate to me, O Sanjaya.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: संजय उवाच हन्त ते वर्तयिष्यामि यथा वृत्तं महारणे। शुश्रूषस्व स्थिरो भूत्वा दुराचरितमात्मनः॥
en: Sanjaya said I will relate to you faithfully all that took place in that terrible encounter. Listen calmly to (the consequences of) your own culpable conduct.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: पूर्वमेव हि कृष्णस्य मनोगतमिदं प्रभो। विजेतव्यो यथा वीरः सात्यकिः सौमदत्तिना॥
en: My Lord, Krishna knew it before hand, in his mind that the heroic Satyaki would be defeated by Yupaketu (i.e., Bhurisrava).

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: अतीतानागते राजन् स हि वेत्ति जनार्दनः। ततः सूतं समाहूय दारुकं संदिदेश ह॥ रथो मे युज्यतां कल्यमिति राजन् महाबलः। न हि देवा न गन्धर्वा न यक्षोरगराक्षसाः॥
en: O king, Janaradana is conversant with the past and the future alike. Therefore, O king, that highly-powerful one summoned Daruka and ordered him thus-"Get my car ready tomorrow." Neither the Gods nor the Gandharvas nor the Yakshas, nor the Uragas, nor the Rakshas.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: मानवा वापि जेतारः कृष्णयोः सन्ति केचन। पितामहपुरोगाश्च देवाः सिद्धाश्च तं विदुः॥ तयोः : प्रभावमतुलं शृणु युद्धं तु तत् तथा। सात्यकिं विरथं दृष्ट्वा कर्ण चाभ्युद्यतं रणे॥
en: Nor men can conquer Krishna and Arjuna. Even the celestials with the (original) Grandsire (Brahma) at their head and the Siddhas are aware of the matchless strength of those two. Now hear about the battle as it took place. Seeing Satyaki without a car and Karna prepared for the encounter.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: दध्मौ शङ्ख महानादमाषभेणथ माधवः। दारुकोऽवेत्य सदेशं श्रुत्वा शङ्खस्य च स्वनम्॥
en: Madhava loudly blew his conch in the Rishava note. Hearing the loud sound of the conch, Daruka understood the hint.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: स्थमन्वानयत् तस्मै सुपर्णोच्छ्रितकेतनम्। स केशवस्यानुमते रथं दारुकसंयुतम्॥ आरुरोह शिनेः पौत्रो ज्वलनादित्यसनिभम्। कामगैः शैब्यसुग्रीवमेघपुष्पबलाहकैः॥ हयोदग्रैर्महावेगैर्हेमभाण्डविभूषितैः। युक्तं समारुह्य च तं विमानप्रतिमं रथम्॥
en: And brought to him the car adorned with a lofty golden flag with Keshava's permission. The grandson of Sini ascended that car guided by Daruka and resembling in splendour the son or the fire. (And) mounting on that car, resembling a celestial chariot yoked unto which were the foremost of horses, viz., Savya, Sugriva, Meghapuspa and Balahaka endued with great fleetness and adorned with golden trappings.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: अभ्यद्रवत् राधेयं प्रवपन् सायकान् बहून्। चक्ररक्षावपि तदा युधामन्यूत्तमौजसौ॥
en: (Satyaki) discharging numerous. arrows, rushed upon the son of Radha. Then Yudhamanyu and Uttamouja, the protectors of Arjuna's car-wheels.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: धनंजयरथं हित्वा राधेयं प्रत्युदीयतुः। राधेयोऽपि महाराज शरवर्ष समुत्सृजन्॥
en: Leaving the car of Dhananjaya, advanced against the son of Radha. (There upon) O monarch, the son of Radha too, began to discharge showers of arrows.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: अभ्यद्रवत् सुसंक्रुद्धो रणे शैनेयमच्युतम्। नैव दैवं न गान्धर्व नासुरं न च राक्षसम्॥
en: And wrathfully rushed against the undeteriorating grandson of Sini in that encounter. Neither among the celestials, the Gandharvas, the Asuras, the Uragas, nor among the Rakshas.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: तादृशं भुवि नो युद्धं दिवि वा श्रुतमित्युत। उपारमत तत् सैन्यं सरथाश्वनरद्विपम्॥
en: Was such a battle seen or heard in heaven or on earth as took place (between Karna and Satyaki.) The entire army consisting of cars, horses, men and elephants.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: तयोर्दृष्ट्वा महाराज कर्म सम्पूढचेतसः। सर्वे च समपश्यन्त तद् युद्धमतिमानुषम्॥
en: Beholding their exploits, O monarch lay (as if) entranced. All of them witnessed that superhuman battle.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: तयोर्तृवरयो राजन् सारथ्यं दारुकस्य च। गतप्रत्यागतावृत्तैर्मण्डलैः संनिवर्तनैः॥
en: Between those two best of men and the dexterity of Daruka as a charioteer. And the forward, backward, side long and circular movements (of the car).

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: सारथेस्तु रथस्थस्य काश्यपेयस्य विस्मिताः। नभस्तलगताश्चैव देवगन्धर्वदानवाः॥
en: Caused by the charioteer Daruka the Kasyapa's race, stationed on the car, struck (everybody) with wonder. The celestials, the Gandharvas and the Danavas stationed in the firmament.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: अतीवावहिता द्रष्टुं कर्णशैनेययो रणम्। मित्रार्थे तौ पराक्रान्तौ शुष्मिणो स्पर्घिनौ रणे॥
en: Witnessed with rapt attention that encounter between Karna and the grandson of Sini. and for the sake of their friends those two powerful and highly-energetic ones challenged each other in that battle.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: कर्णश्चामरसंकाशो युयुधानश्च सात्यकिः। अन्योन्यं तौ महाराज शरवर्षैरवर्षताम्॥
en: O mighty monarch, Karna who resembled a god and Yuyudhana Satyaki showered upon each other volleys of arrows.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: प्रममाथ शिनेः पौत्रं कर्णः सायकवृष्टिभिः। अमृष्यमाणो निधनं कौरव्यजलसंधयोः॥
en: First Karna, unable to endure the destruction of Jalasandha of the Kuru party, overpowered the grandson of Sini with downpours of shafts.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: कर्णः शोकसमाविष्टो महोरग इव श्वसन्। स शैनेयं रणे क्रुद्धः प्रदहन्निव चक्षुषा॥
en: And heaving sighs like a mighty serpent smitten with grief and darting wrathful glance upon the grandson of Sini as if to consume him (therewith) in that encounter, Karna.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: अभ्यधावत वेगेन पुनः पुनररिंदम। तं तु सक्रोधमालोक्य सात्यकिः प्रत्युयुध्यत॥
en: Rushed furiously again and again (towards him.) O chastiser of foes, seeing him greatly enraged, Satyaki smote him.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: महता शरवर्षेण गजं प्रति गजो यथा। तौ समेतौ नरव्याघ्रौ व्याघ्राविव तरस्विनौ॥ अन्योन्यं संततक्षाते रणेऽनुपमविक्रमौ। ततः कर्ण शिनेः पौत्रः सर्वपारसवैः शरैः॥ बिभेद सर्वगात्रेषु पुनः पुनररिंदम। सारथिं चास्य भल्लेन रथनीडादपातयत्॥
en: With mighty discharges of arrows as an elephant smites (with his tusks) his rival elephant. Those two most valiant of mortals, as agile as tigers and endued with matchless strength wounded each other in that battle. Then the grandson of Sini by means of shafts made entirely of iron, pierced Karna, the chastiser of his foes, all through his body over and over again and with a broad headed arrows smote his (Karna's) charioteer from his niche in the car.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: अश्वांश्च चतुरः श्वेतान् निजघान शितैः शरैः। छित्त्वा ध्वजं रथं चैव शतधा पुरुषर्षभ॥
en: (And he) killed the white steeds with sharpened darts. (Then) that most exalted of the Bharatas, cutting the standard (of Karna) into a hundred pieces.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: चकार विस्थं कर्ण तव पुत्रस्य पश्यतः। ततो विमनसो राजंस्तावकास्ते महारथाः॥
en: Made him carless in the very presence of your son. Thereupon, O king, O most exalted of the Bharatas, the warriors on your side got dispirited.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: वृषसेनः कर्णसुतः शल्यो मद्राधिपस्तथा। द्रोणपुत्रश्च शैनेयं सर्वतः पर्यवारयन्॥
en: (Then) Vrisasena, the son of Karna and Shalya, the king of Madra and the son of Drona surrounded the grandson of Sini on all sides.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: ततः पर्याकुलं सर्व न प्राज्ञायत किंचन। तथा सात्यकिना वीरे विस्थे सूतजे कृते॥
en: Then such a confusion followed (on the battlefield) that nothing could be seen. The heroic son of charioteer being thus made carless by Satyaki.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: हाहाकारस्ततो राजन् सर्वसैन्येष्वभून्महान्। कर्णोऽपि विरथो राजन् सात्वतेन कृतः शरैः॥
en: The whose army set up a wail, O king. And Karna too, O monarch, greatly weakened by Satvatta's darts.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: दुर्योधनरथं तूर्णंमारुरोह विनिःश्वसन्। मानयंस्तव पुत्रस्य बाल्यात् प्रभृति सौहृदम्॥
en: Got to the car of Duryodhana, heaving deep sighs, remembering his friendship, O king, with your son from his very childhood.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: कृतां राज्यप्रदानेन प्रतिज्ञा परिपालयन्। तथा तु विरथं कर्ण पुत्रांश्च तव पार्थिव॥ दुःशासनमुखान् वीरान् नावधीत् सात्यकिर्वशी। रक्षन् प्रतिज्ञां भीमेन पार्थेन च पुराकृताम्॥
en: And striving to fulfill the promise that he had made on the occasion of the bestowal of the kingdom (of Anga) on him (by Duryodhana). But O lord of the earth, the selfrestrained Satyaki did not slay Karna thus made carless (by him) and your valiant son with Dushasana at their head. Desirous of not falsifying the vow made by Bhima and Partha formerly.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: विरथान् विह्वलांश्चक्रे न तु प्राणैर्व्ययोजयत्। भीमसेनेन तु वधः पुत्राणां ते प्रतिश्रुतः॥
en: He (simply) made them carless and destitute of energy, but did not deprive them of their lives. Bhimasena vowed to slay your sons.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: अनुद्यूते च पार्थेन वध: कर्णस्य संश्रुतः। वधे त्वकुर्वन् यत्नं ते तस्य कर्णमुखास्तदा॥
en: And at the second game of dice Partha swore to do away with Karna. Though the carwarriors with Karna at their head tried (their utmost) to slay.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: नाशकुवंस्ततो हन्तुं सात्यकिं प्रवरा रथाः। द्रौणिश्च कृतवर्मा च तथैवान्ये महारथाः॥
en: Satyaki, yet those foremost of car-warriors were unable to kill him. The son of Drona, Kritavarman and other great car-warriors.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: निर्जिता धनुषैकेन शतशः क्षत्रियर्षभाः। काङ्क्षता परलोकं च धर्मराजस्य च प्रियम्॥
en: And hundreds of the foremost of the Kshatriyas were defeated with only one bow by Satyaki, who was desirous of doing good to Dharmaraja and of attaining heaven.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: कृष्णयोः सदृशो वीर्ये सात्यकिः शत्रुतापनः। जितवान् सर्वसैन्यानि तावकानि हसन्निव॥
en: Satyaki, the grinder of his foes, equal in prowess to either Krishna or Arjuna, defeated all your troops with a smile (i.e., very easily).

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: कृष्णो वापि भवेल्लोके पार्थो वापि धनुर्धरः। शैनेयो वा नरव्याघ्र चतुर्थस्तु न विद्यते॥
en: (To achieve such feats) there is no fourth to be seen, besides Krishna, the bowman Partha and that most exalted of men, the grandson of Sini.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच
en: on car

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: अजय्यं वासुदेवस्य रथमास्थाय सात्यकिः। विरथं कृतवान् कर्ण वासुदेवसमो युधि॥ दारुकेण समायुक्तः स्वबाहुबलदर्पितः। कचिदन्यं समारूढः सात्यकि: शत्रुतापनः॥
en: Dhritarashtra said Mounting the invincible of Vasudeva, guided by Daruka, Satyaki, proud of the prowess of his arms and equal to Vasudeva in battle, made Karna carless. Did Satyaki ascend any other car (after the defeat of Karna)?

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: एतदिच्छाम्यहं श्रोतुं कुशलो ह्यासि भाषितुम्। असा तमहं मन्ये तन्ममाचक्ष्व संजय॥
en: I am desirous of listening to all this. You are a skillful narrator. I regard him invincible. O Sanjaya, relate to me this.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: शृणु राजन् यथावृत्तं रथमन्यं महामतिः। दारुकस्यानुजस्तूर्ण कल्पनाविधिकल्पितम्॥ आयसैः काञ्चनैश्चापि पट्टैः संनद्धकूबरम्। तारासहस्रखचितं सिंहध्वजपताकिनम्॥ अश्वैर्वातजवैर्युक्तं हेमभाण्डपरिच्छदैः। सैन्धवैरिन्दुसंकाशैः सर्वशब्दातिगैइँदैः॥
en: Sanjaya said O king, listen to all this. The high-minded younger brother of Daruka soon brought (for Satyaki) another car duly furnished with all necessaries, having shafts attached to it by golden and iron chains and bands of silk, studded with a thousand stars, graced with a standard having the figure of a lion (painted on it) and to which were yoked horses fleet as the wind adorned with golden trappings and the rattling of which resembled the roar of the clouds.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: चित्रकाञ्चनसंनाहैर्वाजिमुख्यैर्विशाम्पते। घण्टाजालाकुलरवं शक्तितोमरविद्युतम्॥
en: The grandson of Sini, having mounted on it, advanced against your forces. And Daruka also, of his own will, went over to Keshava.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: युक्तं सांग्रामिकैर्द्रव्यैर्वहुशस्त्रपरिच्छदैः। रथं सम्पादयामास मेघगम्भीरनिःस्वनम्॥ तं समारुह्य शैनेयस्तव सैन्यमुपाद्रवत्। दारुकोऽपि यथाकामं प्रययौ केशवान्तिकम्॥ कर्णस्यापि रथं राजशङ्खगोक्षीरपाण्डुरैः। चित्रकाञ्चनसंनाहैः सदश्वर्वेगवत्तरैः॥
en: Then, O great monarch, a goodly car was also brought for Karna, drawn by fleet horses of the best breed, having the colour of the milk of the cow or conch and adorned with golden trappings. (The car was also) furnished with golden maces and standards, machines and flags. It had also an expert driver and was furnished with many weapons and accouterments. Having, O great king, mounted on this car, Karna too rushed upon his enemies. Now I have related to you all that you asked me.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: हेमकक्ष्याध्वजोपेतं क्लृप्तयन्त्रपताकिनम्। अग्यं रथं सुयन्तारं बहुशस्त्रपरिच्छदम्॥
en: Listen again to the (great) destruction (of creatures) brought about by your vile policy. Thirty-one of your sons have been destroyed by Bhimasena.

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: उपाजह्वस्तमास्थाय कर्णोऽप्यभ्यद्रवद् रिपून्। एतत् ते सर्वमाख्यातं यन्ां त्वं परिपृच्छसि॥ भूयश्चापि निबोधेमं तवापनयजं क्षयम्। एकत्रिंशत् तव सुता भीमसेनेन पातिताः॥ दुमुर्ख प्रमुखे कृत्वा सततं चित्रयोधिनम्।
en: They had Durmukha at their head they were good warriors. Saivatta and Arjuna also destroyed hundreds of warriors,

description: The battle between Karna and Satyaki
sn: शतशो निहताः शूराः सात्वतेतार्जुनेन च॥ भीष्मं प्रमुखतः कृत्वा भगदत्तं च भारत। एवमेष क्षयो वृत्तो राजन् दुर्मन्त्रिते तव॥
en: With Bhima at their head and Bhagadatta too (has been slain). This great destruction of creatures O king, has been brought about by your evil counsels.

description: The showing of the field of battle
sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच तथा गतेषु शूरेषु तेषां मम च संजय। किं वै भीमस्तदाकार्षीत् तन्ममाचक्ष्व संजय॥
en: Dhritarashtra said When the warriors on their side and mine remained thus on the field of battle, what did Bhima do? Tell me, this O Sanjaya.

description: The showing of the field of battle
sn: संजय उवाच विरथो भीमसेनो वै कर्णवाक्शल्यपीडितः। अमर्षवशमापन्नः फाल्गुनं वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
en: Sanjaya said When Bhimasena was made carless by Karna, he was tormented with the words poignant as a dart, of the latter. Now under the influence of passion he said these words of Phalguna.

description: The showing of the field of battle
sn: पुनः पुनस्तूबरक मूढ औदरिकेति च। अकृतास्रक मा योत्सीर्बाल संग्रामकातर॥ इति मामब्रवीत् कर्णः पश्यतस्ते धनंजय। एवं वक्ता च मे वध्यस्तेन चोक्तोऽस्मि भारत॥
en: "O Dhananjaya, in your very presence, Karna has repeatedly said to me-(you are) a eunuch, fool, child, glutton, (you are) unable to endure (the fury of) battle. He, that would tell me so, would be my victim. O Bharata, he (Karna) has said to me these words (and therefore, he must be slain by me),

description: The showing of the field of battle
sn: एतद् व्रतं महाबाहो त्वया सह कृतं मया। तथैतन्मम कौन्तेय यथा तव न संशयः॥
en: I have made this vow jointly with you, O mighty armed one. O son of Kunti undoubtedly, as they (these vows) are to you so they are to me.

description: The showing of the field of battle
sn: तद्वधाय नरश्रेष्ठ स्मरैतद् वचनं मम। यथा भवति तत् सत्यं तथा कुरु धनंजय॥
en: Remember, O best of men, my words and fulfill them (i.e., the vows). O Dhananjaya, act in such a way that they may prove true.”

description: The showing of the field of battle
sn: तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं तस्य भीमस्यामितविक्रमः। ततोऽर्जुनोऽब्रवीत् कर्णं किंचिदभ्येत्य संयुगे॥
en: Thus addressed by Bhima, Arjuna of matchless prowess, coming up to Karna in that battle, said to him (thus):

description: The showing of the field of battle
sn: कर्ण कर्ण वृथादृष्टे सूतपुत्रात्मसंस्तुत। अधर्मबुद्धे शृणु मे यत् त्वां वक्ष्यामि साम्प्रतम्॥
en: "O Karna, O son of a charioteer, you are of false sight, you praise your ownself, you are of wicked intelligence. Hear what I tell you now.

description: The showing of the field of battle
sn: द्विविधं कर्म शूराणां युद्धे जयपराजयौ। तौ चाप्यनित्यौ राधेय वासवस्यापि युध्यतः॥
en: Warriors either meet with victory or defeat in battle. O son of Radha, even these two are uncertain. Even when Vasava himself fights, the case is not otherwise.

description: The showing of the field of battle
sn: मुमूर्षर्युयुधानेन विरथो विकलेन्द्रियः। मद्वध्यस्त्वमिति ज्ञात्वा जित्वा जीवन् विसर्जितः॥
en: You where (ere long) made carless and deprived of energy by Yujudhana and were nearly dead. Knowing, however, that I have sworn to slay you he only defeated but spared your life.

description: The showing of the field of battle
sn: यदृच्छया रणे भीमं युध्यमानं महाबलम्। कथंचिद् विरथं कृत्वा यत् त्वं सक्षमभाषथा:॥
en: By freak of fate, you succeeded in making Bhimasena carless. (And) you have committed a sin by abusing Bhima, O son of Radha.

description: The showing of the field of battle
sn: अधर्मस्त्वेष सुमहाननार्चचरितं च तत्। नारिं जित्वातिकत्यन्ते न च जल्पन्ति दुर्वचः॥
en: Men, that are heroic, virtuous and most exalted, having defeated an enemy, neither! boast of themselves with harsh words, nor indulge in abusive language.

description: The showing of the field of battle
sn: न च कञ्चन निन्दन्ति सन्तः शूरा नरर्षभाः। त्वं तु प्राकृतविज्ञानस्तत् तद् वदसि सूतज॥ बह्वबद्धमकर्ण्य च चापलादपरीक्षितम्। युध्यमानं पराक्रान्तं शूरमार्यव्रते रतम्॥ यदवोचेऽप्रियं भीमं नैतत् सत्यं वचस्तव। पश्यतां सर्वसैन्यानां केशवस्य ममैव च।॥
en: O son of a charioteer, weak in intellect as you are, you have made use of these words. Again, the (abusive) epithets that you have hurled against the fighting Bhimasena, endued with prowess, heroic and ever devoted to righteousness, are not true. In the very sight of the whole army of Keshava and myself.

description: The showing of the field of battle
sn: विरथो भीमसेनेन कृतोऽसि बहुशो रणे। न च त्वां परुषं किंचिदुक्तवान् पाण्डुनन्दनः॥
en: You were several times, in battle, deprived of your car by Bhimasena. But the son of Pandu did never utter any harsh words to you.

description: The showing of the field of battle
sn: यस्मात् तु बहु रूक्षं च श्रावितस्ते वृकोदरः। परोक्षं यच सौभद्रो युष्माभिनिहतो मम॥
en: As you have indulged in many harsh words against Vrikodara and as you have jointly with others, killed the son of Subhadra, when I was not present.

description: The showing of the field of battle
sn: तस्मादस्यावलेपस्य सद्यः फलमवाप्नुहि। त्वया तस्य धनुश्छिन्नमात्मनाशाय दुर्मते॥
en: You will, therefore, very soon feel the consequences of your offense. () wicked minded one, it was for your own destruction that you cut-off his bow.

description: The showing of the field of battle
sn: तस्माद् वध्योऽसि मे मूढ सभृत्यसुतबान्धवः। कुरु त्वं सर्वकृत्यानि महत् ते भयमागतम्॥
en: It is for this reason, O fool, that I will slay you together with your attendants, forces and beast of burden. Now (while yet there is time) perform what you ought to do, because a great calamity is hanging over you.

description: The showing of the field of battle
sn: हन्तास्मि वृषसेनं ते प्रेक्षमाणस्य संयुगे। ये चान्येऽप्युपयास्यन्ति बुद्धिमोहेन मां नृपाः॥ तांश्च सर्वान् हनिष्यामि सत्येनायुधमालभे। त्वां च मूढाकृतप्रज्ञमतिमानिनमाहवे॥ दृष्ट्वा दुर्योधनो मन्दो भृशं तप्स्यति पातितम्। अर्जुनेन प्रतिज्ञाते वधे कर्णसुतस्य तु॥
en: I swear truly by my bow that I will slay, in your very sight, Vrishasena and will destroy all those other kings, who through cloudiness of intellect will oppose me in battle. Fool, unwise and self-conceited that you are, the wicked Duryodhana will give way to lamentations seeing you slain on the field of battle. Arjuna having promised to kill the son of Karna.

description: The showing of the field of battle
sn: महान् सुतुमुलः शब्दो बभूव रथिनां तदा। तस्मिन्नाकुलसंग्रामे वर्तमाने महाभये॥
en: There arose a great and tumultuous uproar among the car-warriors. And at the time of that dreadful battle.

description: The showing of the field of battle
sn: मन्दरश्मिः सहस्रांशुरस्तं गिरिमुपाद्रवत्। ततो राजन् हृषीकेशः संग्रामशिरसि स्थितम्॥
en: The thousand-rayed (deity) with his rays dimmed entered into the setting hill. Then stationed at the head of the battle, O king, Hrishikesa.

description: The showing of the field of battle
sn: तीर्णप्रतिज्ञं बीभत्सुं परिष्वज्यैनमब्रवीत्। दिष्ट्या सम्पादिता जिष्णो प्रतिज्ञा महती त्वया॥
en: Embraced Vibhatsu, who had fulfilled his promise and addressed him thus-"O Jishnu, it is by good fortune that you have been able to accomplish your great vow.

description: The showing of the field of battle
sn: दिष्ट्या विनिहतः पापो वृद्धक्षत्र: सहात्मजः। धार्तराष्ट्रबलं प्राप्य देवसेनापि भारत॥
en: It is by good luck, again that you have slain the wretch Vridhakshatra together with his son. O Bharata, even the general of the celestials, if engaged with the force of Dhritarashtra.

description: The showing of the field of battle
sn: सीदेत समरे जिष्णो नात्र कार्या विचारणा। न तं पश्यामि लोकेषु चिन्तयन् पुरुषं क्वचित्॥
en: In battle, would be quite stupefied. O Jishnu, there is no doubt of this. Even on reflection, I do not find any individual in the (three) words.

description: The showing of the field of battle
sn: त्वदृते पुरुषव्याघ्र य एतद् योधयेद् बलम्। महाप्रभावा बहवस्त्वया तुल्याधिकाऽपि वा॥ समेताः पृथिव गला धार्तराष्ट्रस्य कारणात्। ते त्वां प्राप्य रणे क्रुद्धा नाभ्यवर्तन्त दंशिताः॥
en: Capable of encountering these forces, besides you, O most valiant of men. Numerous lords of the earth, endowed with great prowess and either equal or superior to you, have, at the command of Dhritarashtra assembled together. (But) those (warriors). clad in armour, could not withstand your wrathful self in battle.

description: The showing of the field of battle
sn: तव वीर्य बलं चैव रुद्रशक्रान्तकोपमम्। नेदृशं शक्नुयात् कश्चिद् रणे कर्तुं पराक्रमम्॥
en: Your strength and prowess, (therefore), resemble those of Rudra or Shakra. No one is capable of displaying so much prowess in battle.

description: The showing of the field of battle
sn: यादृशं कृतवानद्य त्वमेकः शत्रुतापनः। एवमेव हते कर्णे सानुबन्धे दुरात्मनि॥
en: As you have singly shown this day. O tormentor of foes, when the wicked-souled Karna together with his followers shall be vanquished (by you) I will thus.

description: The showing of the field of battle
sn: वर्धयिष्यामि भूयस्त्वां विजितारिं हतद्विषम्। तमर्जुनः प्रत्युवाच प्रसादात् तव माधव॥ प्रतिज्ञेयं मया तीर्णा विबुधैरपि दुस्तरा। अनाश्चर्यो जयस्तेषां येषां नाथोऽसि केशव॥ त्वत्प्रसादान्महीं कृत्स्नां सम्प्राप्स्यति युधिष्ठिरः। तव प्रभावो वार्ष्णेय तवैव विजयः प्रभो। वर्धनीयास्तव वयं सदैव मधुसूदन॥ एवमुक्तस्ततः कृष्णः शनकैर्वाहयन् हयान्। दर्शयामास पार्थाय क्रूरमायोधनं महत्॥
en: o destroyer of Madhu, you are (ever) concerned in our welfare and we are always) at your enemy." Arjuna then replied to him (thus)-"O Madhava, through your favour, I have fulfilled the vow, which even by the celestials can with difficulty be performed. O Keshava, it is no wonder that they, who have you for their lord, will win the victory. Through your favour Yudhishthira will recover the entire earth. O descendant of Vrishnis, (as) all this is due to your power, (so) O lord, this victory is yours. O destroyer of Madhu, you are (ever) concerned in our welfare wand we are (always) at your service.” Thus spoken to Krishna with a smile, slowly guided the steeds and showed to Partha the greatly cruel field of battle.

description: The showing of the field of battle
sn: श्रीकृष्ण उवाच प्रार्थयन्तो जयं युद्धे प्रथितं च महद् यशः। पृथिव्यां शरेते शूराः पार्थिवास्त्वच्छरैर्हताः :॥
en: Krishna said Longing for either victory or great renown, (many) heroic kings, struck dead by your shafts, are lying on earth.

description: The showing of the field of battle
sn: विकीर्णशस्त्राभरणा विपन्नाश्वरथद्विपाः। संछिन्नभिन्नमर्माणो वैकुव्यं परमं गताः॥
en: Their weapons and ornaments lie scattered (all over the battle-field); their horses, elephants and cars are killed and shattered; and with their armour perforated and cut-off they are reduced to a woeful plight.

description: The showing of the field of battle
sn: ससत्त्वा गतसत्त्वाश्च प्रभया परया युताः। सजीव इव लक्ष्यन्ते गतसत्त्वा नराधिपाः॥
en: Some (of them) are already deal and some are still alive; and those lords of men whose life is extinct look live on account of their great splendour.

description: The showing of the field of battle
sn: तेषां शरैः स्वर्णपुङ्खः शस्त्रैश्च विविधैः शितैः। वाहनैरायुधैश्चैव सम्पूर्णा पश्य मेदिनीम्॥
en: Look! the earth is entirely filled with their gold-winged shafts, their weapons of various kinds, their beasts of burden and with their arims.

description: The showing of the field of battle
sn: वर्मभिश्चर्मभिर्हारैः शिरोभिश्च सकुण्डलैः। उष्णीषैर्मुकुटैः स्रग्भिश्चूडामणिभिरम्बरैः॥ कण्ठसूत्रैरङ्गदैश्च निष्कैरपि च सप्रभैः। अन्यैश्चाभरणैश्चित्रै ति भारत मेदिनी॥
en: (Behold) O Bharata, the earth became with armours, necklaces of gold, heads decked with ear-rings, head-gears and diadems, floral wreaths, gems worn on the crown, Kanthasutras, Angadas, lustrous collars of gold and with various other variegated ornaments;

description: The showing of the field of battle
sn: अनुकरुपासङ्गैः पताकाभिर्ध्वजैस्तथा। उपस्करैरधिष्ठानैरीषादण्डकबन्धुरैः॥
en: (And with) Anukarshas and quivers, standards and flags and Upaskaras and Adhisthanas, shafts and crests of cars.

description: The showing of the field of battle
sn: चक्रैः प्रमथितैश्चिौरक्षश्च बहुधा रणे। युगैर्योक्त्रैः कलापैश्च धनुर्भिः सायकैस्तथा॥
en: With broken wheels and many variegated cars, yokes and trappings of horses, bow and arrows.

description: The showing of the field of battle
sn: परिस्तोमैः कुथाभिश्च परिघैरङ्कुशैस्तथा। शक्तिभिर्भिन्दिपालैश्च तूणैः शूलैः परश्वधैः॥
en: With elephants' trappings, Kudhas, Parighas and Ankushas, maces and Brindipalas, arrow-cases, spiked maces and Parasvadhas.

description: The showing of the field of battle
sn: प्रासैश्च तोमरैश्चैव कुन्तैर्यष्टिभिरेव च। शतघ्नीभिर्भुशुण्डीभिः खङ्गैः परशुभिस्तथा॥
en: With Pashas and Tomaras, Kuntas and clubs, Sataghness and Bhusandees, swords and battle-axes.

description: The showing of the field of battle
sn: मुसलैर्मुद्गरैश्चैव गदाभिः कुणपैस्तथा। सुवर्णविकृताभिश्च कशभिर्भरतर्षभ॥
en: With Musalas and clubs, maces and Kunapas, whips decked with gold, O the most exalted of the Bharatas.

description: The showing of the field of battle
sn: घण्टाभिश्च गजेन्द्राणां भाण्डैश्च विविधैरपि। स्रग्भिश्च नानाभरणैर्वस्त्रैश्चैव महाधनैः॥
en: With the bells and many other ornaments of the best of elephants, garlands, various ornaments and costly dresses.

description: The showing of the field of battle
sn: अपविद्धैर्बभौ भूमिर्ग्रहैद्यौरिव शारदी। पृथिव्यां पृथिवीहेतोः पृथिवीपतयो हताः॥
en: (With all these lying scattered all over the field of battle), the earth looks resplendent like the autumnal sky studded with planets and stars. Those lords of Earth who have sacrificed their live for his sake.

description: The showing of the field of battle
sn: पृथिवीमुपगुह्याङ्गैः सुप्ताः कान्तामिव प्रियाम्। इमांश्च गिरिकूटाभान् नागानैरावतोपमान्॥
en: Lie slumbering on the earth and embracing her like a beloved wife. These elephants resembling mountain-peaks and huge Airavat.

description: The showing of the field of battle
sn: क्षरतः शोणितं भूरि शस्त्रच्छेददरीमुखैः। दरीमुखैरिव गिरीन् गैरिकाम्बुपरिस्रवान्॥
en: Are shedding a profusion of blood through the openings caused by weapons, as mountains discharge through the caves streams of liquid chalk.

description: The showing of the field of battle
sn: तांश्च बाणहतान् वीर पश्य निष्टन्तः क्षितौ। हयांश्च पतितान् पश्य स्वर्ण भाण्डविभूषितान्॥
en: Behold! struck down on the earth by your arrows, these (elephants) are writhing in agonies. Behold! the steeds also, adorned with golden trappings, are lying on the ground.

description: The showing of the field of battle
sn: गन्धर्वनगराकारान् रथांश्च निहतेश्वरान्। छिन्नध्वजपताकाक्षान् विचक्रान् हतसारथीन्॥ निकृत्तकूबरयुगान् भग्नेषाबन्धुरान् प्रभो। पश्य पार्थ हयान् भूमौ विमानोपमदर्शनान्॥
en: Behold, O Partha, O lord, these cars resembling the city of the Gandharvas, with their lords slain and their standards, banners and Akshas cut to pieces, deprived of their wheels and charioteers, with their yokes cut to pieces, with broken shafts and crests and looking (splendid) like the celestial vehicles.

description: The showing of the field of battle
sn: पत्तींश्च निहतान् वीर शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः। धनुर्भृतश्चर्मभृतः शयानान् रुधिरोक्षितान्॥
en: Hundreds and thousands of foot-soldiers, O hero, are lying slain (on the ground) in a pool of blood wielding their bows and shields.

description: The showing of the field of battle
sn: महीमालिङ्गय सर्वाङ्गैः पांसुध्वस्तशिरोरुहान्। पश्य योधान् महाबाहो त्वच्छरैर्भिन्नविग्रहान्॥
en: Clasping the earth with all their limbs and with their hair smeared with dust. Behold, O mighty-armed one, these warriors with their bodies mangled by your arrows.

description: The showing of the field of battle
sn: मसृग्वसापिशितसमृद्धकर्दमम्। निशाचरश्ववृकपिशाचमोदनं महीतलं नरवर पश्य दुर्दशम्॥
en: O best of men, behold also the surface of the earth with dead elephants and horses and (broken) cars, muddy with a profusion of blood, fat and rotten flesh, affording delight to night of blood, fat the rotten flesh, affording delight to night-wanderers, dogs, wolves and Pisachas and dreadful to look at.

description: The showing of the field of battle
sn: इदं महत् त्वय्युपपद्यते प्रभो रणाजिरे कर्म यशोभिवर्धनम्। शतक्रतौ चापि स देवसत्तमे महाहवे जनुषि दैत्यदानवान्॥
en: O lord, that foremost of the celestials, the performer of a hundred sacrifices who slay in great battle the Daytas and the Danavas and yourself only are capable of achieving such a fame-enhancing and glorious feat.

description: The showing of the field of battle
sn: संजय उवाच एवं संदर्शयन् कृष्णो रणभूमिं किरीटिने। स्वैः समेतः समुदितैः पाञ्चजन्यं व्यनादयत्॥
en: Sanjaya said Krishna, thus showing the field of battle to Kiriti (i.e., Arjuna who wore a coronet) blew his conch Panchajanya before the gladdened army (of the Pandavas).

description: The showing of the field of battle
sn: स दर्शयन्नेव किरीटिनेऽरिहा जनार्दनस्तामरिभूमिमञ्जसा। अजातशत्रु समुपेत्य पाण्डवं निवेदयामास हतं जयद्रथम्॥
en: Janardana, the destroyer of foes, having (thus) shown to Kiriti the field of battle, speedily came over to the Pandavas Ajatastru (i.e., Yudhishthira who had no enemy) and informed him of destruction of Jayadratha.

sn: संजय उवाच ततो राजानमभ्येत्य धर्मपुत्रं युधिष्ठिरम्। ववन्दे स प्रहृष्टात्मा हते पार्थेन सैन्धवे॥
en: Sanjaya said The king of Sindhu being slain by Partha, (Krishna) then approached king Yudhishthira, the son of Dharma and worshipped him with a merry heart.

sn: दिष्ट्या वर्धसि राजेन्द्र हतशत्रुर्नरोत्तमा दिष्ट्या निस्तीर्णवांश्चैव प्रतिज्ञामनुजस्तव॥
en: O king of kings, O best of men, by good luck your prosperity increases and your enemy has been slain. It is by good fortune too that your younger brother has fulfilled his promise.

sn: स त्वेवमुक्तः कृष्णेन हृष्टः परपुरंजयः। ततो युधिष्ठिरो राजा रथादाप्लुत्य भारत।॥
en: Thus addressed by Krishna, king Yudhishthira, the conqueror of enemies cities, got down from his car with delight, O Bharata.

sn: पर्यष्वजत् तदा कृष्णावानन्दाश्रुपरिप्लुतः। प्रमृज्य वदनं शुभ्रं पुण्डरीकसमप्रभम्॥
en: And with his eyes full of tears of joy he embraced Krishna and Arjuna; and wiping his white face of lotus-like lustre.

sn: अब्रवीद् वासुदेवं च पाण्डवं च धनंजयम्। प्रियमेतदुपश्रुत्य त्वत्तः पुष्करलोचन॥
en: Said to Vasudeva and the Pandava Dhananjaya (thus)-"0 mighty car-warriors, it is by good fortune that I behold you both after you have performed your heavy task in battle.

sn: नान्तं गच्छामि हर्षस्य तितीर्घरुदधेरिवा अत्यद्भुतमिदं कृष्ण कृतं पार्थेन धीमता॥
en: As good luck would have it, that vilest wretch among men, the king of Sindhus, has been slain. O Krishna and Arjuna, by good luck you have filled me with supreme bliss.

sn: दिष्ट्या पश्यामि संग्रामे तीर्णभारौ महारथौ। दिष्ट्या विनिहतः पाप: सैन्धवः पुरुषाधमः॥
en: (And) it is by good fortune that our enemies are downed in a sea of grief. In the three worlds there is nothing which they cannot perform.

sn: कृष्ण दिष्ट्या मम प्रीतिमहती प्रतिपादिता। त्वया गुप्तेन गोविन्द जता पापं जयद्रथम्॥
en: Who have you, that are the lord of all the words, for their protector, O slayer of Madhu. Govinda, through your favour we will conquer our enemies.

sn: किं तु नात्यद्भुतं तेषां येषां नस्त्वं समाश्रयः। न तेषां दुष्कृतं किंचित् त्रिषु लोकेषु विद्यते॥
en: As in days of yore, through you grace the chastiser of the Asura) Paka (i.e., Indra) did (conquer) the Danavas. Whether it be the supremacy over the three worlds.

sn: स्थितः सर्वात्मना नित्यं प्रियेषु च हितेषु च। त्वां चैवास्माभिराश्रित्य कृतः शस्रसमुद्यमः॥
en: Everything is certain in the case of those who are in your good grace, O bestower of honours. Neither do they incur sin nor meet with reverses.

sn: सर्वलोकगुरुर्येषां त्वं नाथो मधुसूदन। त्वत्प्रसादाद्वि गोविन्द वयं जेष्यामहे रिपून्।॥ सुरैरिवासुरवधे शक्रं शक्रानुजाहवे। असम्भाव्यमिदं कर्म देवैरपि जनार्दन।॥ अमानुषाणि दिव्यानि महान्ति च बहूनि च।
en: With whom, you that are the lord of the celestials, are pleased, O bestower of honours. O Hrishikesha, it is through your favour that Shakra, the lord of all the celestials.

sn: तदैवाज्ञासिषं शत्रून् हतान् प्राप्तां च मेदिनीम्॥ त्वत्प्रसादसमुत्थेन विक्रमेणारिसूदन।
en: Endowed with prosperity, obtained sovereignty over the three world in battle. And O lord of the celestials, it is also through favour that the celestials.

sn: त्वद्बुद्धिबलवीर्येण कृतवानेष फाल्गुनः। बाल्यात् प्रभृति ते कृष्ण कर्माणि श्रुतवानहम्॥
en: Have, O Krishna, obtained immortality and are in enjoyment of eternal regions. O destroyer of foes, it is by means of the prowess obtained through your favour.

sn: सुरेशत्वं गतः शक्रो हत्वा दैत्यान् सहस्रशः॥ त्वत्प्रसादाद्धषीकेश जगत् स्थावरजङ्गमम्।
en: That Shakra having destroyed thousands of Daityas acquired the kingship of the celestials, O Hrishikesha, it is by reason of your grace, the universe, with its mobile and immobile creatures.

sn: स्ववर्त्मनि स्थितं वीर जपहोमेषु वर्तते॥ एकार्णवमिदं पूर्वं सर्वमासीत् तमोमयम्।
en: Remaining in its own course is engaged in (religious) meditation and sacrifices, Originally, buried in darkness and one vast sheet of water.

sn: त्वत्प्रसादान्महाबाहो जगत् प्राप्तं नरोत्तम॥ स्रष्टारं सर्वलोकानां परमात्मानमव्ययम्। ये पश्यन्ति हृषीकेशं न ते मुह्यन्ति कर्हिचित्॥ पुराणं परमं देवं देवदेवं सनातनम्।
en: As the universe was, it has become manifest through your grace, O mighty-armed one, O best of men. Those who look upon Hrishikesha as the creator of all the worlds, the Supreme Soul and as immutable are never subject to illusion. You are the Original Being, you are the Supreme God, you are the God of the gods and you are eternal.

sn: ये प्रपन्ना: सुरगुरुं न ते मुह्यन्ति कर्हिचित्॥ अनादिनिधनं देवं लोककर्तारमव्ययम्।
en: Those that take refuge with you who are the lord of the celestials, are never subject to illusion; without beginning or end, divine, the lord of creation and immutable (as you are).

sn: ये भक्तास्त्वां हृषीकेश दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते॥ परं पुराणं पुरुषं पराणां परमं च यत्।
en: They that are your worshippers, O Hrishikesha (always) get rid of difficulties. Supreme and Ancient male being and the most exalted of the exalted as you are.

sn: प्रपद्यतस्तत् परमं परा भूतिर्विधीयते॥ गायन्ति चतुरो वेदा यश्च वेदेषु गीयते।
en: He that attains to your Supreme self enjoys the highest prosperity. The four Vedas sing of you and you are sung in the four Vedas.

sn: तं प्रपद्य महात्मानं भूतिमश्नाम्यनुत्तमाम्॥ परमेश परेशेश तिर्यगीश नरेश्वर।
en: By taking refuge with you, O high-souled one, I shall enjoy the most excellent prosperity. O Supreme God, O god of the highest gods, O lord of the creation, O lord of men.

sn: सर्वेश्वरेश्वरेशेश नमस्ते पुरुषोत्तम॥ त्वमीशेशेश्वरेशान प्रभो वर्धस्व माधव।
en: O most supreme god of all gods, I bow down to you, that are the best of all male beings. You are the Supreme Being, you are the Lord of Lords, O Lord, O Madhava, may you prosper.

sn: प्रभवाप्यय सर्वस्य सर्वात्मन् पृथुलोचन॥ धनंजयसखा यश्च धनंजयहितश्च यः। धनंजयस्य गोप्ता तं प्रपद्य सुखमेधते॥
en: O Universal Soul, O large-eyed one, you are the origin of all. He that has Dhananjaya for his friend or he who is devoted to the welfare of Dhananjaya. Having attained to the protector of Dhananjaya, enjoys happiness.'

sn: मार्कण्डेयः पुराणर्षिश्चरितज्ञस्तवानघ। माहात्म्यमनुभावं च पुरा कीर्तितवान् मुनिः॥
en: O innocent Sri Krishna! An ancient sage Markandeya knows yours character and that brilliant sage had explained me your impression and magnificence to me at the time of exile.

sn: असितो देवलश्चैव नारदश्च महातपाः। पितामहश्च मे व्यासस्त्वामाहुर्विधिमुत्तमम्॥
en: You are explained as the best creator (Vidhi) by the sages like Asita, Devala, the great austerious Narada and my grand-father Vyasa.

sn: त्वं तेजस्त्वं परं ब्रह्म त्वं सत्यं त्वं महत् तपः। त्वं श्रेयस्त्वं यशश्चायं कारणं जगतस्तथा॥ त्वया सृष्टमिदं सर्वं जगत् स्थावरजङ्गमम्। प्रलये समनुप्राप्ते त्वां वै निविशते पुनः॥
en: You are splendour yourself, you are supreme Brahma, great penance truth, welfare, the best fame and sole cause for universe. You have created this entire movable and immovable world and this world merges again with you at the time of great devastation (Pralaya).

sn: अनादिनिधनं देवं विश्वस्येशं जगत्पते। धातारमजमव्यक्तमाहुर्वेदविदो जनाः॥
en: O lord of this entire world! The people learned to Vedas address you as without birth and death (Ajanama), divine form, lord of the great soul, everlasting and Vishvatomukh.

sn: भूतात्मानं महात्मानमनन्तं विश्वतोमुखम्। अपि देवा न जानन्ति गुह्यमाद्यं जगत्पतिम्॥ नारायणं परं देवं परमात्मानमीश्वरम्। ज्ञानयोनि हरि विष्णुं मुमुक्षूणां परायणम्। परं पुराणं पुरुषं पुराणानां परं च यत्॥
en: Yours is top and undisclosed mystery. You are the foremost cause and supreme lord of this universe. You yourself are supreme god, Narayana, supreme soul (Paramatama) and Ishvara. You yourself are Sri Hari in the form of knowledge, the supreme shelter to the people desirous of emancipation, Vishnu. Gods even are alien to your real form. You yourself are beyond Puranas and supreme Purusha of Purana.

sn: एवमादिगुणानां ते कर्मणां दिवि चेह च। अतीतभूतभव्यानां संख्यातात्र न विद्यते॥ सर्वतो रक्षणीयाः स्म शक्रेणेव दिवौकसः। यैस्त्वं सर्वगुणोपेतः सुहन्न उपपादितः॥
en: Nobody either on this or heaven is capable to make a record of the acts executed in past, present and future and to calculate yours such qualities (gunas). All of us are always defendable by you as lord Indra provides the gods with proper defence. We have got you as a meritorious friend.

sn: इत्येवं धर्मराजेन हरिरुक्तो महायशाः। अनुरूपमिदं वाक्यं प्रत्युवाच जनार्दनः॥
en: The great illustrious god Janardana reciprocated Yudhishthira the Dharmaraja in the following words as per his appreciation made.

sn: भवता तपसोग्रेण धर्मेण परमेण च। साधुत्वादर्जवाच्चैव हतः पापो जयद्रथः॥
en: O Dharmaraja! The evildoer Jayadratha has met to death because of your acute penance, supreme religion, gentleness and simplicity.

sn: अयं च पुरुषव्याघ्र त्वदनुध्यानसंवृतः। हत्वा योधसहस्त्राणि न्यहन् जिष्णुर्जयद्रथम्॥
en: O chivalrous man (Purusha Simha)! your always sacrosanct feelings for all creatures has provided Arjuna with an impenetrable shield and he could kill Jayadratha after beheading several thousand warriors.

sn: कृतित्वे बाहुवीर्य च तथैवासम्भ्रमेऽपि च। शीघ्रतामोधबुद्धित्वे नास्ति पार्थसमः क्वचित्॥
en: Nobody anywhere is comparable to Arjuna, the son of Kunti in respect of his knowledge in weaponry, physical stamina, smartness and target hitting savvy etc. qualities.

sn: तदयं भरतश्रेष्ठ भ्राता तेऽद्य यदर्जुनः। सैन्यक्षयं रणे कृत्वा सिन्धुराजशिरोऽहरत्॥
en: Othe best in Bharata's dynasty! Owing to these qualities, your younger brother Arjuna has today beheaded Sindhuraja and killed the army of enemy in fierce battle.

sn: ततो धर्मसुतो जिष्णुं परिष्वज्य विशाम्पते। प्रसृज्य वदनं तस्य पर्याश्वासयत प्रभुः॥
en: Oking! King Yudhishthira, Dharmaputra (son of Dharma) then embraced in tight grip to Arjuna, wiped his face and told the following worlds in consolation.

sn: अतीव सुमहत् कर्म कृतवानसि फाल्गुन। असह्यं चाविषह्यं च देवैरपि सवासवैः॥
en: O Phalguna! You have executed a rare act today as god Indra including all gods were unable to execute or take-one this anus on their shoulders (viz. it was impossible even for the king of gods).

sn: दिष्ट्या निस्तीर्णभारोऽसि हतारिश्चासि शत्रुहन्। दिष्ट्या सत्या प्रतिज्ञेयं कृता हत्वा जयद्रथम्॥
en: O enemy suppressor! You have discharged today the burden of commitment as you have killed your enemy. It is really a matter of good luck. It is really pleasing to see that you have fulfilled the commitment by killing Jayadratha.

sn: एवमुक्त्वा गुडाकेशं धर्मराजो महायशाः। पस्पर्श पुण्यगन्धेन पृष्ठे हस्तेन पार्थिवः॥
en: The great illustrious king Yudhishthira with these words to Arjuna, the conqueror of sheep, patted on his back with his hand with sheer love.

sn: एवमुक्तौ महात्मानावुभौ केशवपाण्डवौ। तावबूतां तदा कृष्णौ राजानं पृथिवीपतिम्॥
en: On his so delivered statement, Sri Krishna and Arjuna reciprocated the king in following words-

sn: तव कोपाग्निना दग्धः पापो राजा जयद्रथः। उत्तीर्णं चापि सुमहद् धार्तराष्ट्रबलं रणे॥
en: O king! The evildoer king Jayadratha was burnt into ashes in the fire of your fury and it was your grace that enabled us to suppress the huge army of Duryodhana in the battle-field.

sn: हन्यस्ते निहताश्चैव विनश्यन्ति च भारत। तव क्रोधहता ह्येते कौरवाः शत्रुसूदन॥
en: O Bharata! all these Kauravas have been killed owing to your fury, these are killed and will killed in future too as the fire of your fury is blazing in fierce flames.

sn: त्वां हि चक्षुर्हणं वीरं कोपयित्वा सुयोधनः। समित्रबन्धुः समरे प्राणांस्त्यक्ष्यति दुर्मतिः॥
en: Duryodhana, the wicked will finally die in the battle-field with his friends, relatives and siblings as a result of furiating you, the gallant capable to burn in ashes the enemy merely by a furious gaze.

sn: तव क्रोधहतः पूर्वं देवैरपि सुदुर्जयः। शरतल्पगतः शेते भीष्मः कुरुपितामहः॥
en: Bhishma, the grandfather of Kuru family who earlier was tough to win even by gods, is now sleeping on the cot made of arrows owing to your destructive fury.

sn: दुर्लभो विजयस्तेषां संग्रामे रिपुसूदन। याता मृत्युवशं ते वै येषां क्रुद्धोऽसि पाण्डव॥
en: O son of Pandu! You are suppressor of enemy and victory in battle is scarce for those on whom your curse befallen. They have definitely enslaved to the death.

sn: राज्यं प्राणाः श्रियः पुत्राः सौख्यानि विविधानि च। अचिरात् तस्य नश्यन्ति येषां क्रुद्धोऽसि मानद॥
en: O honour giving king! The persons on being victim of your anger shall shortly see their kingdom, life, property, son and a number of luxuries destroyed.

sn: विनष्टान् कौरवान् मन्ये सपुत्रपशुबान्धवान्। राजधर्मपरे नित्यं त्वयि क्रुद्धे परंतप॥
en: O pain giver to enemies! Being yours abiding to Rajadharma (the nationalism), I consider the Kauravas destroyed with sons, animals and siblings automatically in the fire of your anger.

sn: ततो भीमो महाबाहुः सात्यकिश्च महारथः। अभिवाद्य गुरुं ज्येष्ठं मार्गणैः क्षतविक्षतौ॥ क्षितावास्तां महेष्वासौ पाञ्चाल्यैः परिवारितौ। तौ दृष्ट्वा मुदितौ वीरौ प्राञ्जली चाग्रतः स्थितौ॥
en: The long armed Bhimasena and great chariot holder Stayaki with their bodies injured of arrows then bowed their heads on the feet of Yudhishthira and stood on the ground. Having seen those great archers with folded hands and in charms on their faces; Yudhishthira, the son of Kunti greeted them heartily.

sn: अभ्यनन्दत कौन्तेयस्तावुभौ भीमसात्यकी। दिष्ट्या पश्यामि वां शूरौ विमुक्तौ सैन्यसागरात्॥ द्रोणग्राहदुराधर्षाद्धार्दिक्यमकरालयात्।
en: He said-it is very opportuned time to see. both of you duly crossed the ocean of enemy's army. That ocean of army is inaccessible due to presence of the crocodile Dronacarya and the Kritavarma etc. crags are dwelling in that Ocean.

sn: दिष्ट्या विनिर्जिताः संख्ये पृथिव्यां सर्वपार्थिवाः॥५५ युवां विजयिनौ चापि दिष्ट्या पश्यामि संयुगे।
en: It is the time to laugh in exhilaration as all kings defeated in battle and I am seeing both of you as conqueror in this battle-field.

sn: दिष्ट्या द्रोणो जित: संख्ये हार्दिक्यश्च महाबलः॥५६ दिष्ट्या विकर्णिभिः कर्णो रणे नीतः पराभवम्। विमुखश्च कृतः शल्यो युवाभ्यां पुरुषर्षभौ॥
en: It was our destiny that supported and we could defeat Acarya Drona and Kritavarma in the battle. It was another support of destiny that Karna too was defeated in battle-field by virtue of your archery. O best gallants! Both of you have pressed Shalya to leave the battle-field.

sn: दिष्ट्या युवां कुशलिनौ संग्रामात् पुनरागतौ। पश्यामि रथिनां श्रेष्ठावुभौ युद्धविशारदौ॥
en: It is pleasing to see you both warriors, best in chariot holders and efficient in war-craft returned safely from the battle-field.

sn: मम वाक्यकरौ वीरौ मम गौरवयन्त्रितौ। सैन्यार्णवं समुत्तीर्णौ दिष्ट्या पश्यामि वामहम्॥
en: It is high time to feel gaiety when I am seeing you both warriors duly crossed the army ocean. You hold obligation of my dignity and honour the directions issued by me.

sn: समरश्लाघिनौ वीरौ समरेष्वपराजितौ। मम वाक्य समौ चैव दिष्ट्या पश्यामि वामहम्॥
en: You both warriors keep my words while competing with rivals and undefeated in the battle field. It is my high destiny to see you safe here.

sn: इत्युक्त्वा पाण्डवो राजन् युयुधानवृकोदरौ। सखजे पुरुषव्याघ्रौ हर्षाद् वाष्पं मुमोच ह॥
en: Having said these words, these words, o king! Yudhishithira, the son of Pandu embraced Satyaki and Bhimasena both and his eyes started shedding tears of joy.

sn: ततः प्रमुदितं सर्वं बलमासीद् विशाम्पते। पाण्डवानां रणे हृष्टं युद्धाय तु मनो दधे॥
en: O majesty! The whole army of Pandavas then encouraged, gaiety brought new zeal to them and it concentrated whole-hearted on battling.

sn: संजय उवाच सैन्धवे निहते राजन् पुत्रस्तव सुयोधनः। अश्रुपूर्णमुखो दीनो निरुत्साहो द्विषज्जये॥
en: Sanjaya said O monarch, the king of Sindhu being slain, your son Suyodhana, with his eyes full of tears, became (greatly) dejected and despaired of defeating his enemies.

sn: दुर्मना निःश्वसन् दुष्टो भग्नदंष्ट्र इवोरगः। आगस्कृत् सर्वलोकस्य पुत्रस्तेऽऽर्तिं परामगात्॥
en: (And) with his mind weighted down with sorrow and breathing hot sighs like a snake whose (poison) tooth has been broken that offender, against the whole world, felt excruciating agony (if mind).

sn: दृष्ट्वा तत्कदनं घोरं स्वबलस्य कृतं महत्। जिष्णुना भीमसेनेन सात्वतेन च संयुगे।॥
en: Seeing that Jishnu, Bhimasena and Satvatta were making a great and dreadful havoc of his army.

sn: स विवर्णः कृशो दीनो वाष्पविप्लुतलोचनः। अमन्यतार्जुनसमो न योद्धा भुवि विद्यते॥
en: He turned thin and pale and became (greatly) dispirited. And with his eyes filled with tears he began to think that there was no warrior on earth who mighty be match for Arjuna.

sn: न द्रोणो न च राधेयो नाश्वत्थामा कृपो न च। क्रुद्धस्य समरे स्थातुं पर्याप्ता इति मारिष॥
en: Neither Drona, nor the son of Radha, nor Ashvatthama nor Kripa is capable of standing before him (Arjuna) when he is angry, O worshipful one.

sn: निर्जित्य हि रणे पार्थः सर्वान् मम महारथान्। अवधीत् सैन्धवं संख्ये न च कश्चिदवारयत्॥
en: (And Suyodhana, thought within himself.) No was able to resist him when having defeated all the great car-warriors on my side, Partha slew the king of Sindhus.

sn: सर्वथा हतमेवेदं कौरवाणां महद् बलम्। न ह्यस्य विद्यते त्राता साक्षादपि पुरंदरः॥
en: The son of Pandu has totally destroyed my vast army. (I think) even Purandara himself in person cannot protect it.

sn: यमुपाश्रित्य संग्रामे कृतः शस्त्रमुद्यमः। स को निर्जितः संख्ये हतश्चैव जयद्रथः॥
en: Even Karna, depending upon whom, I had engaged in this passage at arms in battle, has been defeated in encounter and Jayadratha slain.

sn: यस्य वीर्यं समाश्रित्य शमं याचन्तमच्युतम्। तृणवत् तमहं मन्ये स कर्णो निर्जितो युधि॥
en: Relying upon whose prowess 1 regarded that undeteriorating one (i.e., Krishna) who sued for peace, (something) like a straw, that Karna has been defeated in battle.

sn: एवं कान्तमना राजन्नुपायाद् द्रोणमीक्षितुम्। आगस्कृत् सर्वलोकस्य पुत्रस्ते भरतर्षभ॥
en: Thus dejected at heart, O king, O the most exalted of the Bharatas, your son, the offender against the whole world, came to seen Drona.

sn: ततस्तत्सर्वमाचख्यौ कुरूणां वैशसं महत्। परान् विजयतश्चापि धार्तराष्ट्रानं निमजतः॥
en: He then told (Drona) all about the great slaughter of the Kurus, the victory of the enemies and the great disaster of the followers of Dhritarashtra.

sn: पश्य मूर्धाभिषिक्तानामाचार्य कदनं महत्। कृत्वा प्रमुखतः शूरं भीष्मं मम पितामहम्॥
en: “O Preceptor," (Duryodhana (continued), "Behold this great carnage of those whose heads have undergone the sacred coronation bath, headed by my heroic grandsire Bhisma,

sn: तं निहत्य प्रलुब्धोऽयं शिखण्डी पूर्णमानसः। पाञ्चाल्यैः सहितः सर्वैः सेनाग्रमभिवर्तते॥
en: The covetous Shiknandi, having killed him, has got his desire fulfilled and is (now) stationed at the head of his troops together with all the Panchalas.

sn: अपरश्चापि दुर्धर्षः शिष्यस्ते सव्यसाचिना। अक्षौहिणी: सप्त हत्वा हतो राजा जयद्रथः॥
en: Having destroyed seven Akshauhinis (of our army), another invincible disciple of yours, viz., Savyasachi has killed king Jayadratha.

sn: अस्मद्विजयकामानां सुहृदामुपकारिणाम्। ॥ गन्तास्मि कथमानृण्यं गतानां यमसादनम्॥
en: Those allies of ours, desirous of our victory and welfare, have gone to the abode of Yama. How can I repay the debt (of obligation) that I owe to them?

sn: ये मदर्थं परीप्सन्ते वसुधां वसुधाधिपाः। ते हित्वा वसुधैश्वर्यं वसुधामधिशेरते॥
en: Those lords of the earth, who desired for me the sovereignty of the earth, having abandoned all earthly prosperity, are lying on the earth.

sn: सोऽहं कापुरुषः कृत्वा मित्राणां क्षयमीदृशम्। अश्वमेधसहस्रेण पावितुं न समुत्सहे॥
en: Coward that I am I have caused this great slaughter of my friends, and (therefore) cannot encourage myself to believe that I shall be able to purify myself by celebrating even a hundred horse-sacrifices.

sn: मम लुब्धस्य पापस्य तथा धर्मापचायिनः। व्यायामेन जिगीषन्तः प्राप्ता वैवस्वतक्षयम्॥
en: Desirous of securing victory (for me who am covetous and sinful and a rebel against virtue, these (kings) have gone to the abode of the sons of Vivasvata.

sn: कथं पतितवृत्तस्य पृथिवी सुहृदां दुहः। विवरं नाशकद् दातुं मम पार्थिवसंसदि।॥
en: I have fallen from virtue; an evil-minded and an enemy to my friends as I am why does not the earth yield me a hole (to bury me in).

sn: योऽहं रुधिरसिक्ताङ्गं राज्ञां मध्ये पितामहम्। किं वक्ष्यत्ति हि दुर्धर्षः समेत्य परलोकजित्॥
en: Among the kings, my grandsire with bloodred eyes (lies on an arrowy bed) what will that invincible hero, who has conquered the next world, say when he will meet me?

sn: जलसंधं महेष्वासं पश्य सात्यकिना हतम्। मदर्थमुद्यतं शूरं प्राणांस्त्यक्त्वा महारथम्॥
en: See that the great bowman Jalasandha has been slain by Satyaki. That hero and mighty car-warrior exerting his utmost for my sake, has (at last) lain down his life.

sn: काम्बोज निहतं दृष्ट्वा तथालम्बुषमेव च। अन्यान् बहूंश्च सुहृदो जीवितार्थोऽद्य को मम॥
en: Beholding the king of Kamboja, Alambusha and many other friends lose their lives, what is the good of preserving my life?

sn: न्यायच्छन्तो हताः शूरो मदर्थे येऽपराङ्मुखाः। यतमानाः परं शक्त्या विजेतुमहितान् मम॥
en: Those unretreating warriors after exerting their utmost to vanquish my enemies and fighting for my sake have (at last) sacrificed their lives.

sn: तेषां गत्वाहमानृण्यमद्य शक्त्या परंतप। तर्पयिष्यामि तानेव जलेन यमुनामनु॥
en: I will today repay the debts I owe them by exerting my utmost in the battle) and will then offer oblation of Jamuna water to them.

sn: सत्यं ते प्रतिजानामि सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वर। इष्टापूर्तेन च शपे वीर्येण च सुतैरपि॥
en: O the foremost of those that wield weapons, I promise truly and swear by my good acts, my prowess and my sons.

sn: निहत्य तान् रणे सर्वान् पञ्चालान् पाण्डवैः सह। शान्ति लब्धास्मि तेषां वा रणे गन्ता सलोकताम्॥
en: That I will either obtain peace of mind by destroying the Panchalas together with the Pandavas or I will depart to the regions where they (i.e., my) friends have gone by being myself slain in battle.

sn: सोऽहं तत्र गमिष्यामि यत्र ते पुरुषर्षभाः। हता मदर्थे संग्रामे युध्यमानाः किरीटिना॥
en: I will go there whither those foremost of men, slain for may sake in battle by the fighting Kiriti, have departed.

sn: न हीदानीं सहाया मे परीप्सन्त्यनुपस्कृताः। श्रेयो हि पाण्डून् मन्यन्ते न तथास्मान् महाभुज॥
en: Seeing they are not well protected our partisans are no longer desirous of supporting use. They deem the sons of Pandu are preferable to us, O mighty armed one.

sn: स्वयं हि मृत्युर्विहितः सत्यसंधेन संयुगे। भवानुपेक्षां कुरुते शिष्यत्वादर्जुनस्य हि॥
en: That truth-abiding one (Bhishma) himself ordained his own death in battle. And your respectable self too does not exert your best because Arjuna is your disciple.

sn: अतो विनिहताः सर्वे येऽस्मजयचिकीर्षवः। कर्णमेव तु पश्यामि सम्प्रत्यस्मजयैषिणम्॥
en: It is, on this account, that all those who were desirous of our victory have been slain. At present I seen that Karna alone is anxious for our success.

sn: यो हि मित्रमविज्ञाय याथातथ्येन मन्दधीः। मित्रार्थे योजयत्येनं तस्य सोऽर्थोऽवसीदति॥
en: That man, of dull understanding who without the exercise of proper discretion, takes one for a friend and employs him in actions which can only be performed by real friends, has his object frustrated.

sn: तादृग् रूपं कृतमिदं मम कार्यं सुहृत्तमैः। मोहाल्लब्धस्य पापस्य जिह्मस्य धनमीहतः॥
en: Covetous, sinful, crooked-minded and greedy of riches that I am, this affair of mine has been managed in this way by (so-called) best friend.

sn: हतो जयद्रथश्चैव सौमदत्तिश्च वीर्यवान्। अभीषाहा शूरसेनाः शिबयोऽथ वसातयः॥
en: King Jayadratha, that powerful monarch, the son of Somadatta, the Ameeshahas, the Surasenas, the Curas and the Vysatis have (all) been slain.

sn: सोऽहमद्य गमिष्यामि यत्र ते पुरुषर्षभाः। हता मदर्थे संग्रामे युध्यमानाः किरीटिना॥
en: I will today go there whither those best of the Bharatas, slain for my sake in battle by the fighting Kiriti, have gone.

sn: न हि मे जीवितेनार्थस्तानृते पुरुषर्षभान्। आचार्यः पाण्डुपुत्राणामनुजानातु नो भवान्॥
en: There is no good of my life without those foremost of men. O preceptor of the sons of Pandu, permit me to do this.

sn: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच सिन्धुराजे हते तात समरे सव्यसाचिना। तथैव भूरिश्रवसि किमासीद् वो मनस्तदा॥
en: Dhritarashtra said What, O Sanjaya, was the state of your mind when the king of Sindhu was slain in battle by Savyasachi and Bhurisrava (by Satyaki)?

sn: दुर्योधनेन च द्रोणस्तथोक्तः कुरुसंसदि। किमुक्तवान् परं तस्मै तन्ममाचक्ष्व संजय॥
en: Relate to me, O Sanjaya, what Drona did say after he had been thus addressed by Duryodhana in the midst of the Kurus.

sn: संजय उवाच निष्टान को महानासीत् सैन्यानां तव भारत। सैन्धवं निहतं दृष्ट्वा भूरिश्रवसमेव च॥
en: Sanjaya said Seeing the king of Sindhu and Bhurisrava slain, there arose a great tumult among your troops, O Bharata.

sn: मन्त्रितं तव पुत्रस्य ते सर्वमवमेनिरे। येन मन्त्रेण निहताः शतशः क्षत्रियर्षभाः॥
en: All of them censured the policy of your son, in virtue of which hundreds of foremost of men were destroyed.

sn: द्रोणस्तु तद् वचः श्रुत्वा पुत्रस्य तव दुर्मनाः। मुहूर्तमिव तद् ध्यात्वा भृशमार्तोऽभ्यभाषत॥
en: Drona too, hearing those words of your son, became sad at heart. Then, O king of kings, reflecting a moment he said very sorrowfully (these words).

sn: द्रोण उवाच दुर्योधन किमेवं मां वाक्शरैरपि कृन्तसि। अजय्यं सततं संख्ये ब्रुवाणं सव्यसाचिनम्॥
en: Drona said O Duryodhana, why are you piercing me with words (keen) as darts? I have told you (repeatedly) that Savyasachi is uncognizable in battle.

sn: एतेनैवार्जुनं ज्ञातुमलं कौरव संयुगे। यच्छिखण्ड्यवधीद् भीष्मं पाल्यमानः किरीटिना॥
en: We have got (sufficient) proofs of what Arjuna is, when protected by Kiriti, Sikhandi slew Bhisma in battle, O Kaurava.

sn: अवध्यं निहतं दृष्ट्वा संयुगे देवदानवैः। तदैवाज्ञासिषमहं नेयमस्तीति भारती॥
en: Seeing that Bhishma, who could not be defeated by the celestials and the Danavas in battle, was slain (by Sikhandi), I understood that the Bharata army was doomed.

sn: यं पुंसां त्रिषु लोकेषु सर्वशूरममंस्महि। तस्मिन् निपतिते शूरं किं शेषं पर्युपास्महे॥
en: That person, whom we looked upon as the foremost of all the heroes in the three worlds, being slain, who else there that can inspire us with confidence?

sn: यान् स्म तान् ग्लहते तात शकुनिः कुरुसंसदि। अक्षान् न तेऽरक्षा निशिता बाणास्ते शत्रुतापनाः॥
en: The dice with which Shakuni played in the assembly-hall of the Kurus, O affecnate one, are not (real) dice but their arrows destructive of foes, has ever been able to achieve.

sn: त एते मन्ति नस्तात विशिखा: पार्थचोदिताः। तांस्तदाऽऽख्यायमानस्त्वं विदुरेण च बुद्धवान्॥
en: Those arrows, O child, now discharged by aya are destroying us; you did not then understand when Vidura told you what those (dice) were.

sn: यास्ता विजयतश्चापि विदुरस्य महात्मनः। धीरस्य वाचो नाश्रौषीः क्षेमाय वदतः शिवाः॥
en: You did not then pay heed to those auspicious words, which the magnanimous wise Vidura with tearful eyes said for your good.

sn: तदिदं वर्तते घोरमागतं वैशसं महत्। तस्यावमानाद् वाक्यस्य दुर्योधन कृते तव॥
en: In consequence of your disregard for those words, O Duryodhana, this dire, terrible and impending disaster has overtaken you.

sn: योऽवमन्य वचः पथ्यं सुहृदामाप्तकारिणाम्। स्वमतं कुरुते मूढः स शोच्यो नचिरादिव॥
en: That stupid person, who disregarding the wholesome advice of his trusted friends, follows his own inclinations, is very soon reduced to a pitiable plight.

sn: यच नः प्रेक्षमाणानां कृष्णामानाय्य तत्सभाम्। अनर्हन्ती कुले जातां सर्वधर्मानुचारिणीम्॥
en: (You) had dragged Krishna to the assembly hall in our very presence who was unworthy of such treatment, was born of a noble line and was devoted to every act of righteousness.

sn: तस्याधर्मस्य गान्धारे फलं प्राप्तमिदं महत्। नो चेत् पापं परे लोके त्वमर्छथास्ततोऽधिकम्॥
en: O son of Gandhari, this (calamity which you are now in) is the bitter fruit of that sinful act on your part. This (punishment) is but insignificant for in the world to come you will be visited with direr calamities.

sn: यच्च तान् पाण्डवान् द्यूते विषमेण विजित्य ह। प्रावाजयस्तदारण्ये रौरवाजिनवाससः॥
en: (This disaster is also the outcome of) your deceit by means of which you defeated the Pandavas at the game of dice and exiled them to the forest clad in deer-skin.

sn: पुत्राणामिव चैतेषां धर्ममाचरतां सदा। दुह्येत् को नु नरो लोके मदन्यो ब्राह्मणब्रुवः॥
en: Is there, in the world, any other Brahmana besides myself that would injure the (Pandavas) who devoted to righteousness and are (as dear) to me as my (own) sons.

sn: पाण्डवानामयं कोपस्त्वया शकुनिना सह। आहृतो धृतराष्ट्रस्य सम्मते कुरुसंसदि॥
en: The wrath that you excited in the Pandavas with the assent of Dhritarashtra and associated with Shakuni in the midst of the Kurus,

sn: दुःशासनेन संयुक्तः कर्णेन परिवर्धितः। क्षत्तुर्वाक्यमनाहृत्य त्वयाभ्यस्तः पुनः पुनः॥
en: are ever Has been fostered by Dushasana together with Karna and had been repeatedly fanned by you who never paid regard to the words of Khattva.

sn: यत्ताः सव्रे पराभूताः पर्यवारयताऽर्जुनम्। सिन्धुराजानमाश्रित्य स वो मध्ये कथं हतः॥
en: How was it that you, who stood by the ruler by the Sindhu and tried your utmost to withstand Arjuna, were all defeated and why was he (Jayadratha) slain in your midst?

sn: कथं त्वयि च कर्णे च कृपे शल्ये च जीवति। अश्वत्थानि च कौरव्य निधनं सैन्धवोऽगमत्॥
en: How is it, O Kaurava prince, that when you, Karna, Kripa, Shalya and Ashvatthama are (all) alive, the king of Sindhu has been slain?

sn: युध्यन्तः सर्वराजानस्तेजस्तिग्ममुपासते। सिन्धुराजं परित्रातुं स वो मध्ये कथं हतः॥
en: How was it that the king of Sindhu was slain in their midst, since for the purpose of rescuing him all the kings fought with fiery energy.

sn: मय्येव हि विशेषेण तथा दुर्योधन त्वयि। आशंसत परित्राणमर्जुनात् स महीपतिः॥
en: That lord of the earth looked especially to yourself and me for his rescue from Arjuna, O Duryodhana.

sn: ततस्तस्मिन् परित्राणमलब्धवति फाल्गुनात्। न किंचिदनुपश्यामि जीवित स्थानमात्मनः॥
en: But he failed to have that rescue from (the clutches of) Arjuna. I too do not find any hope for my own life.

sn: मजन्तमिव चात्मानं धृष्टद्युम्नस्य किल्बिषे। पश्याम्यहत्वा पञ्चालान् सह तेन शिखण्डिना॥
en: I see that I am (fast) sinking into the mire of Dhristadyumna's (cunning) until I can slay the Panchalas together with Sikhandi.

sn: तन्मां किमभितप्यन्तं वाक्शरैरेव कृन्तसि। अशक्तः सिन्धुराजस्य भूत्वा त्राणाय भारत॥
en: Since I myself am tormented with grief, wherefore are you piercing me with words (poignant) as an arrow, you who failed to rescue the king of Sindhu, O Bharata.

sn: सौवर्णं सत्यसंधस्य ध्वजमकिष्टकर्मणः। अपश्यन् युधि भीष्मस्य कथमाशंससे जयम्॥
en: How can you hope for success, since you do not longer seen the golden standard of Bhishma endued with untiring energy and (ever) firm in truth.

sn: मध्ये महारथानां च यत्राहन्यत सैन्धवः। हतो भूरिश्रवाश्चैव किं शेषं तत्र मन्यसे॥
en: Since the ruler of Sindhu and Bhurisrava have been slain from the very midst of the mighty-car-warriors, you can (very well) anticipate what the result will be.

sn: कृप एव च दुर्धर्षा यदि जीवति पार्थिव। यो नागात् सिन्धुराजस्य वर्त्म तं पूजयाम्यहम्॥
en: O lord of the earth, if, without following the path of the king of Sindhu, the irresistible Kripa be still alive, I praise him highly (for his escape with life).

sn: यत्रापश्यं हतं भीष्मं पश्यतस्तेऽनुजस्य वै। दुःशासनस्य कौरव्य कुर्वाणं कर्म दुष्करम्॥ अवध्यकल्पं संग्रामे देवैरपि सवासवैः। न ते वसुन्धरास्तीति तदाहं चिन्तये नृप॥
en: When, O Kaurava king, I behold that Bhishma, capable of achieving the most difficult exploits and unslayable even by the celestials together with Vasava in battle, was slain in your very sight and in that of your younger brother Dusasana, I thought, O king, that the earth no longer belonged to you.

sn: इमानि पाण्डवानां च सृञ्जयानां च भारत। अनीकान्याद्रवन्ते मां सहितान्यद्य भारत॥
en: Behold! O king, O Bharata, the troops of the Pandavas and those of the Srinjayas are jointly advancing against me.

sn: नाहत्वा सर्वपञ्चालान् कवचस्य विमोक्षणम्। कर्तास्मि समरे कर्म धार्तराष्ट्र हितं तव॥
en: I will not lay down my armour without destroying all the Panchalas; (and), O son of Dhritarashtra, I will perform which acts in battle as will benefit you.

sn: राजन् ब्रूयाः सुतं मे त्वमश्वत्थामानमाहवे। न सोमकाः प्रमोक्तव्या जीवितं परिरक्षता॥
en: O king! Go and convey my direction for Ashvatthama that he should battle taking all care of his life and not let go living Somakas at all possible efforts viz. he has to kill them all definitely.

sn: यच्च पित्रानुशिष्टोऽसि तद् वचः परिपालय। आनृशंस्ये दमे सत्ये चार्जवे च स्थिरो भव॥
en: (Tell him also). "Observe the instruction that your father has given you. Be firm in charity, self-restraint, truth and straight forwardness.

sn: धर्मार्थकामकुशलो धर्मार्थावप्यपीडयन्। धर्मप्रधानकार्याणि कुर्याश्चेति पुनः पुनः॥
en: Be diligent in (the exercise) religion, profit and pleasure without despising religion and profit and always perform those acts in which the exercise of religion is mostly required.

sn: चक्षुर्मनोभ्यां संतोष्या विप्राः पूज्याश्च शक्तितः। न चैषां विप्रियं कार्यं ते हि वह्निशिखोपमाः॥
en: You should always propitiate the Brahmanas with presents and worship. Never do anything that will offend them; for, they are flames of fire.

sn: एष त्वहमनीकानि प्रविशाम्यरिसूदन। रणाय महते राजंस्त्वया वाक्शरपीडितः॥
en: O destroyer of foes, afflicted as I am with your words darts I will now penetrate through the enemy's line in order to engage in a furious encounter (for your sake).

sn: त्वं च दुर्योधन बलं यदि शक्तोऽसि पालय। रात्रावपि च योत्स्यन्ते संरब्धाः कुरुसृञ्जयाः॥
en: As for your, O Duryodhana, if you are capable, go and protect your army, for both the Kurus and the Srinjayas, that are furious (with rage) will fight even during the night.

sn: एवमुक्त्वा ततः प्रायाद् द्रोणः पाण्डवसृञ्जयान्। मुष्णन् क्षत्रियतेजांसि नक्षत्राणामिवांशुमान्॥
en: Having said thus, Drona, like the sun drawing out the energy of the stars, advanced against the Pandavas and the Srinjayas in order to destroy the energy of the Kshatriyas.

description: The commencement of a fresh battle
sn: संजय उवाच ततो दुर्योधनो राजा द्रोणेनैवं प्रचोदितः। अमर्षवशमापन्नो युद्धायैव मनो दधे॥
en: Sanjaya said Then king Duryodhana, thus addressed by Drona, directed his mind to battle influenced by rage.

description: The commencement of a fresh battle
sn: अब्रवीच तदा कर्णं पुत्रो दुर्योधनस्तव। पश्य कृष्णसहायेन पाण्डवेन किरीटिना॥
en: Your son Duryodhana, then, spoke to Karna. "See that Kiriti, the son of Pandu with the help of Krishna.

description: The commencement of a fresh battle
sn: आचार्यविहितं व्यूहं भित्त्वा देवैः सुदुर्भिदम्। तव व्यायच्छमानस्य द्रोणस्य च महात्मनः॥
en: Penetrated into the array drawn up by the preceptor, which (array) was difficult of being penetrated through even by the celestials themselves. Moreover, in the very presence of yourself and the high-souled Drona engaged in battle,

description: The commencement of a fresh battle
sn: मिषतां योधमुख्यानां सैन्धवो विनिपातितः। पश्य राधेय पृथ्वीशाः पृथिव्यां प्रवरा युधि॥
en: And that of many other foremost warriors the king of Sindhu was killed. Behold, O son of Radha, many king-excellent warriors on earth.

description: The commencement of a fresh battle
sn: पार्थेनैकेन निहताः सिंहेनेवेतरे मृगाः। मम व्यायच्छमानस्य द्रोणस्य च महात्मनः॥
en: Destroyed by Partha alone like numerous inferior beasts slain by a lion, even when the high-minded Drona and myself were fighting (in order to resist Arjuna).

description: The commencement of a fresh battle
sn: अल्पावशेषं सैन्यं मे कृतं शक्रात्मजनेन ह। कथं नियच्छमानस्य द्रोणस्य युधि फाल्गुनः॥
en: My (once vast) army has been reduced to a handful of men only by the son of Shakra. How, when Drona was trying his utmost (to check him), could the Phalguna.

description: The commencement of a fresh battle
